ashtavakra_gita::1_1.verse_sanskrit:
कथं ज्ञानमवाप्नोति कथं मुक्तिर्भविष्यति ।
वैराग्यं च कथं प्राप्तमेतद् ब्रूहि मम प्रभो ॥
ashtavakra_gita::1_1.verse_hindi: ज्ञान कैसे प्राप्त होता है ? मुक्ति कैसे होती है ? और वैराग्य कैसे प्राप्त होता है ? प्रभु ! यह मुझसे कहिये।
ashtavakra_gita::1_1.english_translation: How does one attain knowledge? How does liberation happen? And how is dispassion achieved? O Lord, please tell me this.
ashtavakra_gita::1_1.translation_literal: katham (how) jnanam (knowledge) avapnoti (is attained) katham (how) muktih (liberation) bhavisyati (will happen) vairagyam (dispassion) ca (and) katham (how) praptam (obtained) etad (this) bruhi (tell) mama (my) prabho (O Lord)
ashtavakra_gita::1_1.speaker: Janaka
ashtavakra_gita::1_1.essence: The seeker's first act is to find the right question.
ashtavakra_gita::1_1.simple_meaning: King Janaka asks his teacher Ashtavakra three essential questions: how to gain true knowledge, how to achieve freedom, and how to cultivate dispassion toward worldly things.
ashtavakra_gita::1_1.simple_insight: The quality of your questions determines the quality of your life. Janaka, a king with everything, asked the one question that matters.
ashtavakra_gita::1_1.detailed_meaning: Janaka's question is the model spiritual inquiry. He doesn't ask for wealth, power, or even peace of mind — he asks how knowledge, liberation, and renunciation are actually achieved. This triple question sets up the entire dialogue: knowledge (jnana), freedom (mukti), and dispassion (vairagya) form a unified path. The question's ordering is also significant: knowledge leads to freedom, and dispassion is the condition that makes both possible.
ashtavakra_gita::1_1.modern_relevance: Most people ask: 'How do I get what I want?' Janaka asked: 'How do I know what is real?' The entire quality of a life pivots on this shift. Stop optimizing answers to the wrong questions. Ask the right ones first.
ashtavakra_gita::1_1.insight: Dispassion is not a side-effect of wisdom — it is listed alongside knowledge and liberation as equally sought. The three arise together or not at all.

ashtavakra_gita::1_2.verse_sanskrit:
मुक्तिमिच्छसि चेत्तात विषयान् विषवत्त्यज ।
क्षमार्जवदयातोषसत्यं पीयूषवद् भज ॥
ashtavakra_gita::1_2.verse_hindi: मुक्ति चाहता है तो विषयों को विष के समान छोड़ दे और क्षमा, दया, सरलता, सन्तोष और सत्य को अमृत के समान सेवन कर।
ashtavakra_gita::1_2.english_translation: If you desire liberation, my child, abandon sense objects as poison, and embrace forgiveness, simplicity, compassion, contentment, and truth as nectar.
ashtavakra_gita::1_2.translation_literal: muktim (liberation) icchasi (you desire) cet (if) tata (dear child) visayan (sense objects) visavat (like poison) tyaja (abandon) ksama (forgiveness) arjava (simplicity) daya (compassion) tosa (contentment) satyam (truth) piyusavat (like nectar) bhaja (embrace/enjoy)
ashtavakra_gita::1_2.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::1_2.essence: Trade the poison of craving for the nectar of simplicity and truth.
ashtavakra_gita::1_2.simple_meaning: Ashtavakra's first answer is simple and direct: if you want liberation, treat sense cravings like poison, and live on the nectar of forgiveness, simplicity, compassion, contentment, and truth.
ashtavakra_gita::1_2.simple_insight: Liberation starts not with grand practice but with this single honest reorientation: what am I feeding?
ashtavakra_gita::1_2.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra doesn't begin with philosophy — he begins with pragmatics. Vishaya (sense objects and their craving) are likened to visha (poison) — the similarity in Sanskrit is deliberate. The antidote is not a complex technique but five qualities: ksama (forgiveness), arjava (straightforwardness), daya (compassion toward all beings), tosa (inner satisfaction), and satya (truthfulness). These are called amrita — the nectar of immortality. This framing suggests that the ethical and the liberative are one.
ashtavakra_gita::1_2.modern_relevance: We scroll, consume, stimulate, and repeat. Ashtavakra says every such loop is a small dose of poison. Not because pleasure is evil, but because chasing it ties us to the wheel of wanting. The cure isn't deprivation — it's a different kind of nourishment.
ashtavakra_gita::1_2.insight: The five qualities listed — forgiveness, simplicity, compassion, contentment, truth — are not practices to achieve liberation. They are themselves the experience of it.

ashtavakra_gita::1_3.verse_sanskrit:
न पृथ्वी न जलं नाग्निर्न वायुर्द्यौर्न वा भवान् ।
एषां साक्षिणमात्मानं चिद्रूपं विद्धि मुक्तये ॥
ashtavakra_gita::1_3.verse_hindi: तू न पृथ्वी है, न जल है, न अग्नि है, न वायु है, न आकाश है । मुक्ति के लिए अपने को इन सबका साक्षी चैतन्यरूप जान।
ashtavakra_gita::1_3.english_translation: You are not earth, not water, not fire, not air, not space. For liberation, know yourself as the witness of all these — as pure awareness, the light of consciousness.
ashtavakra_gita::1_3.translation_literal: na (not) prthvi (earth) na jalam (not water) na agnih (not fire) na vayuh (not air) dyauh (space) na va (nor) bhavan (you are) esam (of all these) saksinam (the witness) atmanam (yourself/the self) cidrupa (consciousness-form) viddhi (know) muktaye (for liberation)
ashtavakra_gita::1_3.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::1_3.essence: You are the witness of all experience, not the experience itself.
ashtavakra_gita::1_3.simple_meaning: Ashtavakra says: you are none of the five elements that make up the body or the world. You are the pure awareness that witnesses them all. This recognition is liberation.
ashtavakra_gita::1_3.simple_insight: Every spiritual tradition eventually arrives here: you are not what you experience. You are what experiences.
ashtavakra_gita::1_3.detailed_meaning: This verse encodes the Samkhya-Vedanta insight of pancha-bhuta (five elements) versus the witnessing consciousness. Earth, water, fire, air, and space constitute all material existence including the physical body. The claim is not that these don't exist, but that 'you' are none of them. The self (atman) is cidrupa — of the nature of pure awareness/consciousness — and it is the saksi, the witness that stands prior to all objects. The path to liberation is not a technique but a recognition: shift identification from object to witness.
ashtavakra_gita::1_3.modern_relevance: Modern psychology confirms: we over-identify with thoughts, emotions, and body-sensations as 'me'. Meditation traditions worldwide exist to cultivate the observer stance. Ashtavakra collapses this to a single pointer: the witness is already free. You are already that.
ashtavakra_gita::1_3.insight: Liberation isn't becoming the witness — it's recognizing you never stopped being it. The practice is seeing through the mistaken identification, not building a new one.

ashtavakra_gita::1_4.verse_sanskrit:
यदि देहं पृथक् कृत्य चिति विश्राम्य तिष्ठसि ।
अधुनैव सुखी शान्तो बन्धमुक्तो भविष्यसि ॥
ashtavakra_gita::1_4.verse_hindi: यदि देह को अपने से अलग कर और चैतन्य में विश्राम कर स्थित है तो अभी ही सुखी, शान्त और बन्ध-मुक्त हो जाएगा।
ashtavakra_gita::1_4.english_translation: If you set the body apart and rest in pure awareness, you will this very moment become happy, peaceful, and free from all bondage.
ashtavakra_gita::1_4.translation_literal: yadi (if) deham (body) prthak (apart/separate) krtva (having set) citi (in pure awareness/consciousness) visramya (resting) tisthasi (you stand/abide) adhunaiva (right now/this very moment) sukhi (happy) santo (peaceful) bandhamukto (free from bondage) bhavisyasi (you will become)
ashtavakra_gita::1_4.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::1_4.essence: Rest in awareness this instant — freedom is not waiting ahead.
ashtavakra_gita::1_4.simple_meaning: If you stop identifying with the body and simply rest in the awareness that you are, you become free, happy, and peaceful — not eventually, but this very instant.
ashtavakra_gita::1_4.simple_insight: Most spiritual traditions say: do this practice for years and eventually you'll be free. Ashtavakra says: recognize what you already are and you're free right now.
ashtavakra_gita::1_4.detailed_meaning: 'Adhunaiva' — right now, this very moment — is the revolutionary word. Ashtavakra refuses to defer liberation to a future state attained through accumulation of practice. The body is not to be rejected or destroyed — it is to be seen through, recognized as not-self. 'Citi' is pure awareness/consciousness. 'Visramya' means resting — not striving, not doing, but simply abiding as what you are. This is the Ashtavakra stance: liberation is recognition, not achievement.
ashtavakra_gita::1_4.modern_relevance: We have a productivity mindset about spirituality too: practice enough and eventually you'll arrive. Ashtavakra dismantles this. The awareness that reads these words right now is already the free awareness. The only thing between you and freedom is misidentification — and misidentification dissolves in the instant it is clearly seen.
ashtavakra_gita::1_4.insight: The phrase 'adhunaiva' — this very moment — is not poetic. It is the central technical claim of the Ashtavakra Gita: liberation is available now, not as a future attainment.

ashtavakra_gita::1_5.verse_sanskrit:
न त्वं विप्रादिको वर्णो नाश्रमी नाक्षगोचरः ।
असङ्गोऽसि निराकारो विश्वसाक्षी सुखी भव ॥
ashtavakra_gita::1_5.verse_hindi: तू ब्राह्मण आदि वर्ण नहीं है और न तू किसी आश्रम वाला है, न आँख आदि इन्द्रियों का विषय है । तू असंग, निराकार और विश्व का साक्षी है, ऐसा जानकर सुखी हो।
ashtavakra_gita::1_5.english_translation: You are not any caste or social stage of life. You are not perceived by the senses. You are unattached, formless, the witness of the universe. Knowing this, be happy.
ashtavakra_gita::1_5.translation_literal: na tvam (not you) vipra-adika (brahmin etc.) varna (caste) na asrami (not belonging to any life stage) na aksa-gocarah (not object of senses) asangah asi (you are unattached) nirakarah (formless) visva-saksi (witness of the universe) sukhi bhava (be happy)
ashtavakra_gita::1_5.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::1_5.essence: You witness the universe. No label can contain the witness.
ashtavakra_gita::1_5.simple_meaning: You are not your social role, your body, or what your senses experience. You are the formless, unattached awareness that witnesses the whole universe. Happiness is the natural result of recognizing this.
ashtavakra_gita::1_5.simple_insight: Every identity label — caste, profession, age, personality — is something you witness. None of it is the witness itself. That witness is you.
ashtavakra_gita::1_5.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra systematically strips away identities: caste (varna), life-stage (ashrama), sensory experience (aksha-gochara). None of these are 'you'. What remains? Asanga — non-attachment; nirakar — without form; visva-saksi — witness of the entire universe. The instruction at the end is striking: sukhi bhava — be happy. Not 'try to be happy' or 'work toward happiness'. Just be it. Because happiness is the natural state of awareness recognized as itself.
ashtavakra_gita::1_5.modern_relevance: We exhaust ourselves building and defending identities — professional, political, cultural. Ashtavakra says all of it is something witnessed by the real you. Not because identity is evil but because you are far larger than any of it. The relief of this recognition is, literally, happiness.
ashtavakra_gita::1_5.insight: The instruction to 'be happy' after the stripping away of identity is not advice — it is a description of what naturally happens when misidentification drops.

ashtavakra_gita::1_6.verse_sanskrit:
धर्माधर्मौ सुखं दुःखं मानसानि न ते विभो ।
न कर्तासि न भोक्तासि मुक्त एवासि सर्वदा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::1_6.verse_hindi: हे विभो ! धर्म और अधर्म, सुख और दुःख मन के हैं । तेरे लिए नहीं । तू न कर्ता है, न भोक्ता है । तू तो सर्वदा मुक्त ही है ।
ashtavakra_gita::1_6.english_translation: O all-pervading one! Virtue and vice, pleasure and pain belong to the mind, not to you. You are neither the doer nor the experiencer. You are eternally free.
ashtavakra_gita::1_6.translation_literal: dharma-adharma (virtue-vice) sukham (pleasure) duhkham (pain) manasani (belonging to the mind) na te (not yours) vibho (O all-pervading one) na karta asi (you are not the doer) na bhokta asi (not the experiencer) mukta eva asi (you are indeed free) sarvada (always/eternally)
ashtavakra_gita::1_6.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::1_6.essence: You are neither doer nor sufferer — eternally free.
ashtavakra_gita::1_6.simple_meaning: Virtue, sin, pleasure, and pain belong to the mind. The real you is neither the one who acts nor the one who suffers the consequences. You have always been free.
ashtavakra_gita::1_6.simple_insight: The most radical form of surrender is releasing not just the outcome, but the idea that you were ever the agent who caused it.
ashtavakra_gita::1_6.detailed_meaning: This verse addresses one of the deepest sources of psychological suffering: the sense of doership (karta-bhava) and experiencership (bhokta-bhava). Dharma and adharma, sukha and duhkha — all these pairs of opposites are dharma of the manas (mind). The true self (called vibhu — all-pervading) has no relationship to them. The declaration 'mukta eva asi sarvada' — you are always already free — is the Ashtavakra view of liberation as recognition rather than achievement.
ashtavakra_gita::1_6.modern_relevance: The crushing weight of guilt, regret, and pride — all rest on the assumption 'I did this'. The Ashtavakra Gita doesn't encourage irresponsibility; it points to something deeper: behind all action is a witnessing awareness that was never implicated in the action. Surrender here is dropping the claim of authorship over your life's story.
ashtavakra_gita::1_6.insight: This verse is not moral nihilism. Dharma still matters — but its weight belongs to the mind, not to the ground of awareness. The distinction between moral mind and free awareness is the whole architecture of the Gita.

ashtavakra_gita::1_7.verse_sanskrit:
एको द्रष्टासि सर्वस्य मुक्तप्रायोऽसि सर्वदा ।
अयमेव हि ते बन्धो द्रष्टारं पश्यसीतरम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::1_7.verse_hindi: तू एक सबका द्रष्टा है और सदा ही मुक्त है । तेरा बन्धन यही है कि तू अपने को छोड़कर दूसरे को द्रष्टा देखता है।
ashtavakra_gita::1_7.english_translation: You are the one seer of all, and ever-free. Your bondage consists only in this: you see the seer as other — as something apart from yourself.
ashtavakra_gita::1_7.translation_literal: ekah (one) drasta asi (you are the seer) sarvasya (of all) mukta-prayah (almost/essentially free) sarvada (always) ayam eva hi (this alone indeed) te bandho (is your bondage) drastaram (the seer) pasyasi (you see) itaram (as other/different)
ashtavakra_gita::1_7.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::1_7.essence: You are the seer. Seeking the seer is the only bondage.
ashtavakra_gita::1_7.simple_meaning: You are the one witnessing awareness of all experience, and you are always free. The only trap is when you treat the seer — awareness itself — as something to be found outside yourself.
ashtavakra_gita::1_7.simple_insight: All spiritual seeking contains this paradox: the seeker is the sought. The eye cannot see itself from the outside.
ashtavakra_gita::1_7.detailed_meaning: This verse identifies the mechanism of bondage with clinical precision. Bondage is not caused by sin, karma, or worldly attachment — it is caused by a single cognitive error: treating the witnessing awareness as an object to be found elsewhere. 'Drstaram pasyasi itaram' — you see the seer as other. This is projection: you place consciousness outside yourself and then seek it. The cure is not more seeking but recognition of the seeker as the sought.
ashtavakra_gita::1_7.modern_relevance: The spiritual marketplace is full of techniques, teachers, and systems for finding yourself. Ashtavakra says: the looking is the problem. Every moment of looking reinforces the illusion that awareness is elsewhere. The moment seeking stops, what you were looking for is obvious — it was looking all along.
ashtavakra_gita::1_7.insight: Bondage has a single cause in this system: mistaken attribution — believing the witness is an object to be found rather than the subject doing all finding.

ashtavakra_gita::1_8.verse_sanskrit:
अहं कर्तेत्यहंमानमहाकृष्णाहिदंशितः ।
नाहं कर्तेति विश्वासामृतं पीत्वा सुखी भव ॥
ashtavakra_gita::1_8.verse_hindi: 'मैं कर्ता हूँ', ऐसा अहंकाररूपी विशाल काले सर्प से दंशित हुआ तू, ' मैं कर्ता नहीं हूँ', ऐसे विश्वास रूपी अमृत को पीकर सुखी हो।
ashtavakra_gita::1_8.english_translation: You have been bitten by the great black serpent of ego — the belief 'I am the doer.' Drink the nectar of the conviction 'I am not the doer' and be happy.
ashtavakra_gita::1_8.translation_literal: aham karta iti (I am the doer — thus) ahammana (ego/self-conceit) maha-krsna-ahi (great black serpent) damsite (bitten) na aham karta iti (I am not the doer — thus) visvasa (conviction/faith) amrtam (nectar) pitva (having drunk) sukhi bhava (be happy)
ashtavakra_gita::1_8.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::1_8.essence: Release the claim of doership — that is the only antidote.
ashtavakra_gita::1_8.simple_meaning: The ego-belief 'I am the one doing everything' is like a venomous snake bite. The antidote is the clear conviction: 'I am not the doer.' This recognition brings happiness.
ashtavakra_gita::1_8.simple_insight: Every anxiety about outcomes is rooted in the belief 'I caused this.' Releasing that claim is not passivity — it is freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::1_8.detailed_meaning: The image is powerful: ahammana (ego-sense) is a maha-krsna-ahi — a great black serpent. Its poison is the 'I am the doer' identification. The antidote is not another technique but a visvasa — a deep conviction or faith — in the truth of non-doership. This is often misread as fatalism or passivity. It is not. Actions still happen. The difference is whether awareness claims to be their source. The one who is not a doer still acts — but without the weight of ownership.
ashtavakra_gita::1_8.modern_relevance: Anxiety, guilt, burnout, and pride all share a common root: the belief that 'I am responsible for all of this.' Surrendering doership isn't resignation — it's what happens when you stop standing in your own way. The energy that went into self-management becomes available for actual living.
ashtavakra_gita::1_8.insight: The serpent metaphor is precise: ego doesn't kill immediately. It poisons slowly — through accumulating self-importance, defensiveness, and the exhaustion of constantly being the author of your life.

ashtavakra_gita::1_12.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मा साक्षी विभुः पूर्ण एको मुक्तश्चिदक्रियः ।
असङ्गो निःस्पृहः शान्तो भ्रमात्संसारवानिव ॥
ashtavakra_gita::1_12.verse_hindi: आत्मा साक्षी है, व्यापक है, पूर्ण है, एक है, मुक्त है, चैतन्यस्वरूप है, क्रियारहित है, असंग है, निस्पृह है, शान्त है । यह भ्रम से संसारी जैसा भासता है।
ashtavakra_gita::1_12.english_translation: The self is witness, all-pervading, whole, one, free, pure awareness, actionless, unattached, desireless, peaceful. It only appears as a worldly being due to illusion.
ashtavakra_gita::1_12.translation_literal: atma (the self) saksi (witness) vibhuh (all-pervading) purna (whole/complete) ekah (one) muktah (free) cid-akriyah (awareness-actionless) asangah (unattached) nihsphrah (desireless) santah (peaceful) bhramat (due to illusion) samsara-van iva (appears like a worldly being)
ashtavakra_gita::1_12.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::1_12.essence: The self is already whole, free, and peaceful — illusion alone obscures it.
ashtavakra_gita::1_12.simple_meaning: The true self is the witness, all-pervading, complete, free, pure awareness — inherently peaceful and desireless. It only seems to be caught in worldly suffering due to illusion.
ashtavakra_gita::1_12.simple_insight: The person you think you are — struggling, seeking, suffering — is the appearance. The reality is equanimous awareness, already whole.
ashtavakra_gita::1_12.detailed_meaning: This verse is one of the most compressed philosophical declarations in the Ashtavakra Gita. Nine qualities of the self are listed in rapid succession: saksi (witness), vibhu (all-pervading), purna (complete/whole), eka (one), mukta (free), cid-akriya (awareness without action), asanga (unattached), nihspha (desireless), santa (peaceful). Then comes the thunderclap: bhramat samsara-van iva — it only appears as a worldly being due to illusion. The entire human drama of suffering and seeking is a misperception of what is actually whole and free.
ashtavakra_gita::1_12.modern_relevance: Equanimity is often taught as a skill to cultivate — breathe deeply, practice acceptance, train your nervous system. Ashtavakra says equanimity is not cultivated, it is recognized. The self is already santa (peaceful) — the apparent turbulence is in the mind, not in awareness itself. The practice is seeing through the illusion, not building a better response to it.
ashtavakra_gita::1_12.insight: Nine attributes, one conclusion: the illusion that you are a suffering worldly being is precisely that — an illusion. What is real is already complete.

ashtavakra_gita::2_7.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मज्ञानाज्जगद् भाति आत्मज्ञानान्न भासते ।
रज्ज्वज्ञानादहिर्भाति तज्ज्ञानाद् भासते न हि ॥
ashtavakra_gita::2_7.verse_hindi: आत्मा के अज्ञान से संसार भासता है, आत्मा के ज्ञान नहीं भासता है । जैसे रस्सी के अज्ञान से सर्प भासता है, उसके अज्ञान से नहीं भासता है।
ashtavakra_gita::2_7.english_translation: From ignorance of the self, the world appears. From knowledge of the self, it ceases to appear. Just as a snake appears from not knowing the rope, and disappears when the rope is recognized.
ashtavakra_gita::2_7.translation_literal: atma-jnanaj (from self-ignorance) jagad (world) bhati (appears) atma-jnanat (from self-knowledge) na bhasate (does not appear) rajju-ajnanat (from rope-ignorance) ahih (snake) bhati (appears) tat-jnanat (from knowing that) bhasate na hi (does not appear)
ashtavakra_gita::2_7.speaker: Janaka
ashtavakra_gita::2_7.essence: Know yourself and the world's bewildering weight dissolves instantly.
ashtavakra_gita::2_7.simple_meaning: When we don't know our true nature, the world seems solid, binding, and real in an overwhelming way. When we know ourselves as awareness, the world continues but no longer binds. Like mistaking a rope for a snake in dim light — the rope was always a rope.
ashtavakra_gita::2_7.simple_insight: This is not saying the world is unreal. It is saying: the world seen through ignorance of self is a different world than the world seen clearly.
ashtavakra_gita::2_7.detailed_meaning: The rope-snake metaphor (rajju-sarpa vivarta) is one of the most celebrated in all of Indian philosophy. The rope is the underlying reality (the self/brahman). The snake is the appearance created by superimposition of error (adhyasa). The snake is not unreal — in the moment of seeing it, it functions as real. But it is wrongly attributed. When the rope is recognized, the snake-appearance ceases — not because the rope destroyed anything but because the error was corrected. Similarly: the world of bondage, suffering, and seeking appears from ignorance of self; with self-knowledge, it resolves back into its actual nature — pure awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::2_7.modern_relevance: We speak of 'perspective shifts' and 'reframes' in therapy and coaching. The Ashtavakra Gita says the deepest shift is not from one perspective to another, but from ignorance of the witness to recognition of it. That shift changes everything without changing anything.
ashtavakra_gita::2_7.insight: The metaphor is not about making the world disappear. It is about the difference between seeing through fearful ignorance versus seeing through the clarity of recognized awareness. The world remains; suffering doesn't.

ashtavakra_gita::1_16.verse_sanskrit:
त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः ।
शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::1_16.verse_hindi: यह संसार तुझमें व्याप्त है, तुझी में पिरोया है । यथार्थतः तू चैतन्यस्वरूप है । अतः क्षुद्रचित्त को मत प्राप्त हो।
ashtavakra_gita::1_16.english_translation: This whole universe is pervaded by you and strung in you. You are pure, awakened awareness in truth. Do not fall into smallness of mind.
ashtavakra_gita::1_16.translation_literal: tvaya (by you) vyaptam (pervaded) idam (this) visvam (universe) tvayi (in you) protam (strung/threaded) yatharthatah (in truth/reality) suddha-buddha-svarupah (pure-awakened-form) tvam (you are) ma gamah (do not go into) ksudra-cittatam (smallness of mind)
ashtavakra_gita::1_16.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::1_16.essence: The universe is within you. Live from that truth, not from smallness.
ashtavakra_gita::1_16.simple_meaning: The entire universe exists within your awareness and is threaded through it. Your true nature is pure, awakened consciousness. Don't fall into small, cramped thinking.
ashtavakra_gita::1_16.simple_insight: Dispassion (vairagya) doesn't come from convincing yourself the world is worthless. It comes from recognizing you are larger than it.
ashtavakra_gita::1_16.detailed_meaning: 'Ksudra-cittatam' — smallness of mind — is what Ashtavakra warns against. This smallness is the contraction into limited self-identity: 'I am just this body, this name, these problems.' The remedy is not positive thinking but an accurate recognition: tvaya vyaptam idam visvam — the universe is pervaded by you. The seeker is told they are not a part of the universe looking up at the stars in awe — they are the awareness in which the universe appears. Dispassion naturally follows from this recognition: you cannot be desperately attached to that which appears within you.
ashtavakra_gita::1_16.modern_relevance: Anxiety contracts. Recognition expands. Most strategies for dealing with anxiety try to manage the contraction. Ashtavakra says the contraction itself is based on error — the error of identifying with the small self. When the error is corrected, the contraction has nowhere to go.
ashtavakra_gita::1_16.insight: This verse connects vairagya (dispassion) to self-knowledge rather than to world-rejection. You become dispassionate not by hating the world but by recognizing you contain it.

ashtavakra_gita::1_17.verse_sanskrit:
निरपेक्षो निर्विकारो निर्भरः शीतलाशयः ।
अगाधबुद्धिरक्षुब्धो भव चिन्मात्रवासनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::1_17.verse_hindi: तू निरपेक्ष, निर्विकार, स्वनिर्भर है । शान्ति और मुक्ति का स्थान है, अगाध बुद्धिरूप है, क्षोभ-शून्य है । अतः चैतन्यमात्र में निष्ठा वाला हो।
ashtavakra_gita::1_17.english_translation: Be without expectation, without modification, self-sufficient, with a cool heart. Be of unfathomable intelligence, undisturbed — established in pure awareness alone.
ashtavakra_gita::1_17.translation_literal: nirapeksah (without expectation) nirvikarah (without modification) nirbharah (self-sufficient) sitala-asayah (cool-hearted) agadha-buddhih (unfathomable intelligence) aksubdhah (undisturbed) bhava (be) cin-matra-vasanah (established in pure awareness alone)
ashtavakra_gita::1_17.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::1_17.essence: Coolness, depth, undisturbed awareness — these are one thing, not many.
ashtavakra_gita::1_17.simple_meaning: Become free of expectations and reactions, self-sufficient and internally cool. Be of unfathomable depth and undisturbed equanimity, grounded entirely in pure awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::1_17.simple_insight: Clarity isn't brightness — it is coolness. Still water is clear. Agitated water reflects nothing truly.
ashtavakra_gita::1_17.detailed_meaning: This verse is a list of qualities of established wisdom (sthitaprajna). Nirapeksha — no expectations from the world. Nirvikara — no internal modifications or reactions. Nirbhara — self-complete, needing nothing from outside. Sitala-asaya — literally 'cool-hearted' — not indifferent but unheated by passion. Agadha-buddhi — intelligence that has no bottom, unfathomable depth. Aksubdha — not disturbed. And the essence: cin-matra-vasana — one whose sole inclination is pure awareness itself. These are not qualities to achieve but qualities of one who has recognized their true nature.
ashtavakra_gita::1_17.modern_relevance: We optimize for peak performance, emotional intelligence, resilience. All of these have their place. But Ashtavakra points to something quieter: the person whose baseline is pure awareness doesn't need to manage their emotions — the emotions arise in a space so large they simply pass through without sticking.
ashtavakra_gita::1_17.insight: 'Cin-matra-vasana' is the key phrase — established in pure awareness alone. Not partly in awareness and partly in distraction. The instruction is total.

ashtavakra_gita::13.verse_sanskrit:
कूटस्थं बोधमद्वैतमात्मानं परिभावय ।
आभासोऽहं भ्रमं मुक्त्वा भावं बाह्यमथान्तरम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::13.verse_hindi: मैं अभासरूप हूँ’ ऐसे भ्रम को एवं बाहर-भीतर के भाव को छोड़कर तू कूटस्थ बोधरूप एवं अद्वैत, आत्मा का विचार कर।
ashtavakra_gita::13.english_translation: Abandon the illusion of 'I am a mere appearance' and the feelings of inside and outside; contemplate the immutable awareness that is non-dual, the true self.
ashtavakra_gita::13.translation_literal: कूटस्थं (immutable) / बोधम् (awareness) / अद्वैतम् (non-dual) / आत्मानं (self) / परिभावय (contemplate) / आभासः (appearance) / अहं (I) / भ्रमं (illusion) / मुक्त्वा (abandoning) / भावं (feeling) / बाह्यम् (outside) / अथ (and) / अन्तरम् (inside)
ashtavakra_gita::13.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::13.essence: The true self is the unchanging awareness beyond all illusions of appearance and inner or outer feelings.
ashtavakra_gita::13.simple_meaning: Stop believing that you are just an appearance and the feelings of inside or outside. Instead, focus on the unchanging, non-dual true self.
ashtavakra_gita::13.simple_insight: You can feel free when you realize you are more than shifting feelings or illusions of self.
ashtavakra_gita::13.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Ashtavakra tells Janaka to give up the mistaken idea that the self is just an appearance or a mix of internal and external feelings. Instead, he must understand himself as the unchanging, non-dual awareness that is the true self beyond all illusions.
ashtavakra_gita::13.modern_relevance: When your identity feels fragmented by your changing moods or roles, this reminds you that your true self is steady beneath all appearances.
ashtavakra_gita::13.insight: It shifts your attention from fleeting feelings and roles to the unchanging awareness that you truly are.

ashtavakra_gita::14.verse_sanskrit:
देहाभिमानपाशेन चिरं बद्धोऽसि पुत्रक ।
बोधोऽहं ज्ञानखड्गेन तन्निकृत्य सुखी भव ॥
ashtavakra_gita::14.verse_hindi: हे पुत्र ! तू बहुत काल से देहाभिमान के पाश से बँधा हुआ है । उसी पाश को ‘मैं बोध हूँ’ इस ज्ञान की तलवार से काटकर तू सुखी हो ।
ashtavakra_gita::14.english_translation: O son, you have long been bound by the chain of attachment to the body. Cut that chain with the sword of 'I am awareness' and be happy.
ashtavakra_gita::14.translation_literal: देहाभिमानपाशेन (by the chain of attachment to the body) / चिरं (for a long time) / बद्धोऽसि (you are bound) / पुत्रक (O son) । / बोधोऽहं (I am awareness) / ज्ञानखड्गेन (with the sword of knowledge) / तन्निकृत्य (cut it off) / सुखी (happy) / भव (be) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::14.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::14.essence: Freedom comes by cutting attachment to the body through recognizing pure awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::14.simple_meaning: You have been trapped by identifying with your body for a long time. Recognize yourself as pure awareness and free yourself to be happy.
ashtavakra_gita::14.simple_insight: There is relief and joy in realizing you are not the body but the awareness behind it.
ashtavakra_gita::14.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka, urging him to see that his suffering comes from identifying with the body. The teaching is that true freedom and happiness arise when you cut that attachment by realizing your true nature as awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::14.modern_relevance: When stress feels like it’s rooted in your physical identity or appearance, this verse reminds you that your true self is beyond the body, offering lasting peace.
ashtavakra_gita::14.insight: It teaches you to shift identity from the changing body to the unchanging awareness beneath it.

ashtavakra_gita::15.verse_sanskrit:
निःसङ्गो निष्क्रियोऽसि त्वं स्वप्रकाशो निरञ्जनः ।
अयमेव हि ते बन्धः समाधिमनुतिष्ठति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::15.verse_hindi: तू असंग है, क्रिया रहित है, स्वयंप्रकाश है और निरञ्जन है । तेरा बन्धन यही है कि तू समाधि के लिए अनुष्ठान करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::15.english_translation: You are detached, inactive, self-illuminating, and stainless; your bondage is that you practice for samadhi.
ashtavakra_gita::15.translation_literal: निःसङ्गो (detached) / निष्क्रियोऽसि (inactive you are) / त्वं (you) / स्वप्रकाशो (self-illuminating) / निरञ्जनः (stainless) । / अयमेव (this indeed) / हि (surely) / ते (your) / बन्धः (bondage) / समाधिमनुतिष्ठति (practicing for samadhi) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::15.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::15.essence: You are already free; your bondage is trying to achieve freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::15.simple_meaning: You are naturally detached and pure, but you bind yourself by trying to practice to reach complete stillness.
ashtavakra_gita::15.simple_insight: Freedom is not about effort; it’s about letting go of trying to be free.
ashtavakra_gita::15.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the true self is already detached, inactive, and pure. The real obstacle is the effort to attain samadhi, which ironically creates bondage by implying freedom is elsewhere.
ashtavakra_gita::15.modern_relevance: You may feel stuck chasing calm or peace, not realizing that your striving itself blocks the natural quiet you seek.
ashtavakra_gita::15.insight: It shifts the mind from striving for freedom to recognizing freedom is already present without effort.

ashtavakra_gita::16.verse_sanskrit:
त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः ।
शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::16.verse_hindi: यह संसार तुझमें व्याप्त है, तुझी में पिरोया है । यथार्थतः तू चैतन्यस्वरूप है । अतः क्षुद्रचित्त को मत प्राप्त हो।
ashtavakra_gita::16.english_translation: This entire world is pervaded by you and woven within you in truth. You are the pure essence of the discerning mind; do not be taken by petty thoughts.
ashtavakra_gita::16.translation_literal: त्वया (by you) / व्याप्तम् (pervaded) / इदम् (this) / विश्वं (world) / त्वयि (in you) / प्रोतं (woven) / यथार्थतः (truly) / शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपः (pure discerning-mind-form) / त्वं (you) / मा (do not) / गमः (go, fall) / क्षुद्रचित्तताम् (to petty minds)
ashtavakra_gita::16.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::16.essence: You are pure clarity pervading all; do not be caught by trivial thoughts.
ashtavakra_gita::16.simple_meaning: You are the pure, clear essence that fills and connects everything; don't get distracted by small, trivial thoughts.
ashtavakra_gita::16.simple_insight: You can feel grounded knowing your true nature is vast and untouched by petty worries.
ashtavakra_gita::16.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Ashtavakra tells Janaka that the whole world exists within the true self, which is pure awareness and clarity. The mind’s small, trivial distractions should not capture your attention because they are not your true nature.
ashtavakra_gita::16.modern_relevance: During moments when your mind is cluttered with minor worries or distractions, this reminds you that your true self is untouched clarity beyond them.
ashtavakra_gita::16.insight: Shift your focus from petty mental clutter to the vast, clear essence that you truly are.

ashtavakra_gita::17.verse_sanskrit:
निरपेक्षो निर्विकारो निर्भरः शीतलाशयः ।
अगाधबुद्धिरक्षुब्धो भव चिन्मात्रवासनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::17.verse_hindi: तू निरपेक्ष, निर्विकार, स्वनिर्भर है । शान्ति और मुक्ति का स्थान है, अगाध बुद्धिरूप है, क्षोभ-शून्य है । अतः चैतन्यमात्र में निष्ठा वाला हो।
ashtavakra_gita::17.english_translation: You are impartial, unchanging, self-reliant, with a calm mind; your wisdom is profound and undisturbed, established solely in pure awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::17.translation_literal: निरपेक्षो (impartial) निर्विकारो (unchanging) निर्भरः (self-reliant) शीतलाशयः (calm-minded) । अगाधबुद्धिः (profound wisdom) अक्षुब्धः (undisturbed) भव (be) चिन्मात्रवासनः (established in pure awareness) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::17.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::17.essence: Your true self is calm, unshaken wisdom resting in pure awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::17.simple_meaning: You are impartial and unchanging with a calm mind. Your wisdom is deep and undisturbed, firmly rooted in pure awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::17.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your true nature is steady and deeply wise beyond disturbance.
ashtavakra_gita::17.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes the true self as free from bias and change, self-sustained and peaceful. This moment, the seeker is called to rest in the profound, undisturbed wisdom that arises from pure awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::17.modern_relevance: When stress makes your thoughts whirl and your emotions sway, remember you can find a calm, steady place deep inside, untouched by turmoil.
ashtavakra_gita::17.insight: It teaches you to identify with the steady, peaceful witness beneath all fluctuations of mind and circumstance.

ashtavakra_gita::18.verse_sanskrit:
साकारमनृतं विद्धि निराकारं तु निश्चलम् ।
एतत्तत्त्वोपदेशेन न पुनर्भवसम्भवः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::18.verse_hindi: साकार को मिथ्या जान, निराकार को निश्चल जान । इस तत्व के उपदेश से संसार में पुनः उत्पत्ति नहीं होती।
ashtavakra_gita::18.english_translation: Know the manifested as false and the unmanifested as steady; through this truth, rebirth ceases.
ashtavakra_gita::18.translation_literal: साकार (manifested) / अमृतं (unreal) / विद्धि (know) / निराकारं (unmanifested) / तु (but) / निश्चलम् (steady) / एतत् (this) / तत्त्वोपदेशेन (by teaching of truth) / न (not) / पुनः (again) / भवसम्भवः (rebirth arises)
ashtavakra_gita::18.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::18.essence: The changing world is false; only the unchanging reality is true and free.
ashtavakra_gita::18.simple_meaning: The visible, changing world is illusory, while the unchanging reality within is steady and true.
ashtavakra_gita::18.simple_insight: You can find freedom by seeing beyond appearances to the unchanging truth inside.
ashtavakra_gita::18.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the world of forms and change is unreal, while the unmanifested, steady reality is the true essence. Recognizing this ends the cycle of rebirth and suffering.
ashtavakra_gita::18.modern_relevance: When your moods and situations keep shifting, remember the steady part of you that remains untouched inside.
ashtavakra_gita::18.insight: This verse shifts your view from trusting outer appearances to recognizing the inner unchanging reality.

ashtavakra_gita::19.verse_sanskrit:
यथैवादर्शमध्यस्थे रूपेऽन्तः परितस्तु सः ।
तथैवाऽस्मिन् शरीरेऽन्तः परितः परमेश्वरः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::19.verse_hindi: जिस तरह दर्पण अपने में प्रतिबिम्बित रूप के भीतर और बाहर स्थित है । उसी प्रकार परमात्मा इस शरीर के भीतर और बाहर स्थित है।
ashtavakra_gita::19.english_translation: Just as a mirror exists both within and around the reflected image, the supreme being exists both inside and outside the body.
ashtavakra_gita::19.translation_literal: यथा (just as) एव (indeed) आदर्शन (mirror) मध्ये (in the middle) स्थे (is) रूपे (in the form) अन्तः (inside) परितः (around) तु (but) सः (that). तथा (likewise) एव (indeed) अस्मिन् (in this) शरीरे (body) अन्तः (inside) परितः (around) परमेश्वरः (supreme being).
ashtavakra_gita::19.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::19.essence: The supreme being exists inseparably both within and around your body, like a mirror with its reflection.
ashtavakra_gita::19.simple_meaning: The supreme being is present inside your body and also all around it, like a mirror and its reflected image.
ashtavakra_gita::19.simple_insight: You are never separate from the supreme being; it is always both within and surrounding you.
ashtavakra_gita::19.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains this to King Janaka by comparing the supreme being’s presence in the body to a mirror's relationship to its reflection, showing the inseparability of the divine from the physical form.
ashtavakra_gita::19.modern_relevance: When you look in the mirror, you see yourself inside the glass and your image around it — your true self is just as near, both inside and all around you.
ashtavakra_gita::19.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as isolated to recognizing the divine as inseparable from your entire being and environment.

ashtavakra_gita::20.verse_sanskrit:
एकं सर्वगतं व्योम बहिरन्तर्यथा घटे ।
नित्यं निरन्तरं ब्रह्म सर्वभूतगणे तथा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::20.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार सर्वव्यापी एक आकाश घट के भीतर और बाहर स्थित है, उसी तरह नित्य और निरन्तर ब्रह्म सब भूतों में स्थित है।
ashtavakra_gita::20.english_translation: Just as the all-pervading one sky exists inside and outside the pot, so the eternal and continuous Brahman exists in all beings.
ashtavakra_gita::20.translation_literal: एकं (one) / सर्वगतं (all-pervading) / व्योम (sky) / बहिरन्तर्यथा (outside and inside as) / घटे (in the pot) / नित्यं (eternal) / निरन्तरं (continuous) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / सर्वभूतगणे (in all beings) / तथा (thus)
ashtavakra_gita::20.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::20.essence: The eternal reality is fully present everywhere, both within and outside all beings.
ashtavakra_gita::20.simple_meaning: The eternal reality is everywhere, both inside and outside all creatures, just like the sky is inside and outside a pot.
ashtavakra_gita::20.simple_insight: You are intimately connected with an unchanging presence that fills everything.
ashtavakra_gita::20.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra uses the image of the sky inside and outside a pot to show that the supreme reality is both immanent and transcendent, present within all beings and beyond them, revealing unity beyond appearances.
ashtavakra_gita::20.modern_relevance: When you feel alone or separated, remember that the same vast presence you sense outside also fills your being completely.
ashtavakra_gita::20.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as separate to recognizing an unbroken, ever-present reality within and beyond all forms.

ashtavakra_gita::21.verse_sanskrit:
अहो निरञ्जनः शान्तो बोधोऽहं प्रकृतेः परः ।
एतावन्तमहं कालं मोहेनैव विडम्बितः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::21.verse_hindi: मैं निरञ्जन हूँ, शान्त हूँ, बोध हूँ, प्रकृति के परे हूँ, आश्चर्य है । किन्तु मैं इतने काल तक मोह के द्वारा ठगा गया हूँ ।
ashtavakra_gita::21.english_translation: I am stainless, peaceful, awareness beyond nature; yet it is astonishing how long I have been deceived by confusion.
ashtavakra_gita::21.translation_literal: अहो (ah) / निरञ्जनः (stainless) / शान्तः (peaceful) / बोधः (awareness) / अहं (I) / प्रकृतेः (of nature) / परः (beyond) / एतावत् (so long) / अहं (I) / कालं (time) / मोहेन (by confusion) / एव (indeed) / विडम्बितः (deceived)
ashtavakra_gita::21.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::21.essence: You are pure awareness beyond nature, despite long deception by confusion.
ashtavakra_gita::21.simple_meaning: You are pure, peaceful awareness beyond the changing world, but you have been misled by confusion for a long time.
ashtavakra_gita::21.simple_insight: There is wonder and relief in realizing your true nature was never lost, only hidden.
ashtavakra_gita::21.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra reveals to Janaka that the true self is untouched by nature and peaceful awareness itself, yet this self has been long deceived by confusion, highlighting the deep veil that hides true freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::21.modern_relevance: After years of self-doubt and mental noise, you suddenly glimpse that your true self was never harmed, only obscured.
ashtavakra_gita::21.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with confusion to recognizing your pure, unchanging awareness.

ashtavakra_gita::22.verse_sanskrit:
यथा प्रकाशयाम्येको देहमेनं तथा जगत् ।
अतो मम जगत्सर्वमथवा न च किञ्चन ॥
ashtavakra_gita::22.verse_hindi: जैसे इस देह को मैं अकेला ही प्रकाशित करता हूँ, वैसे ही संसार को भी प्रकाशित करता हूँ । इसलिए तो मेरा सम्पूर्ण संसार है अथवा कुछ भी नहीं ।
ashtavakra_gita::22.english_translation: Just as I alone illuminate this body, in the same way I illuminate the entire world; therefore, the whole world is mine or nothing at all.
ashtavakra_gita::22.translation_literal: यथा (just as) प्रकाशयामि (I illuminate) एको (alone) देहम् (the body) एतत् (this) तथा (so) जगत् (the world) । अतो (therefore) मम (my) जगत्-सर्वम् (entire world) अथवा (or) न (not) च (also) किञ्चन (anything) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::22.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::22.essence: Your awareness illuminates your body and the entire world as one unified light.
ashtavakra_gita::22.simple_meaning: You shine your own body and the entire world in the same way, so everything is either your world or nothing.
ashtavakra_gita::22.simple_insight: You can feel that the same presence lights your body and everything around you.
ashtavakra_gita::22.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to King Janaka, revealing that the same awareness illuminating his body also illuminates the entire world. This teaches that the self and the world are not separate; they share one light of consciousness.
ashtavakra_gita::22.modern_relevance: When you notice the awareness in your own body, you can realize that same awareness is present everywhere around you.
ashtavakra_gita::22.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as isolated to recognizing your awareness pervades all experience.

ashtavakra_gita::23.verse_sanskrit:
स शरीरमहो विश्वं परित्यज्य मयाधुना ।
कुतश्चित् कौशलाद् एव परमात्मा विलोक्यते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::23.verse_hindi: आश्चर्य है कि शरीर सहित विश्व को त्यागकर किसी कुशलता से ही अब मैं परमात्मा को देखता हूँ ।
ashtavakra_gita::23.english_translation: It is surprising that, having abandoned the body and the world, I now perceive the supreme being only by some skill.
ashtavakra_gita::23.translation_literal: स (this) शरीरम् (body) अहो (indeed) विश्वं (world) परित्यज्य (having abandoned) मया (by me) अधुना (now) कुतश्चित् (somehow) कौशलात् (by skill) एव (only) परमात्मा (supreme being) विलोक्यते (is perceived)
ashtavakra_gita::23.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::23.essence: Leaving behind the body and world alone doesn't show the supreme; refined skill is needed.
ashtavakra_gita::23.simple_meaning: After giving up identification with the body and world, perceiving the supreme requires a special skill or insight.
ashtavakra_gita::23.simple_insight: There is wonder in recognizing that seeing beyond the body takes more than mere effort—it needs skill.
ashtavakra_gita::23.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra reflects on the paradox that abandoning the body and world does not automatically grant perception of the supreme reality; instead, it demands a special skill or clarity to truly perceive it.
ashtavakra_gita::23.modern_relevance: You might step back from distractions and still find it hard to grasp deeper truths without a new way of seeing.
ashtavakra_gita::23.insight: It teaches that renunciation alone isn't enough; cultivating refined perception is essential to recognize the true self.

ashtavakra_gita::24.verse_sanskrit:
यथा न तोयतो भिन्नास्तरङ्गाः फेनबुद्बुदाः ।
आत्मनो न तथा भिन्नं विश्वमात्मविनिर्गतम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::24.verse_hindi: जैसे जल से तरंग, फेन और बुदबुदा भिन्न नहीं है, वैसे ही विश्व आत्मा से भिन्न नहीं है किन्तु आत्मा से ही निकला हुआ है।
ashtavakra_gita::24.english_translation: Just as waves, foam, and bubbles are not separate from water, the world is not separate from the true self but emerges from it.
ashtavakra_gita::24.translation_literal: यथा (just as) न (not) तोयतो (from water) भिन्नाः (separate) तरङ्गाः (waves) फेनबुद्बुदाः (foam and bubbles) आत्मनो (from the true self) न (not) तथा (likewise) भिन्नं (separate) विश्वम् (the world) आत्मविनिर्गतम् (emerged from the true self)
ashtavakra_gita::24.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::24.essence: The world is inseparable from the true self, like waves inseparable from water.
ashtavakra_gita::24.simple_meaning: The world is not different from your true self; it arises from it just like waves come from water.
ashtavakra_gita::24.simple_insight: You can feel connected and whole, knowing you and the world share one essence.
ashtavakra_gita::24.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches Janaka that just as waves, foam, and bubbles cannot be separated from the water they come from, the entire world is not separate from the true self but is its expression.
ashtavakra_gita::24.modern_relevance: When you face challenges or joys, remember they rise from the same source as your true being, never truly apart from you.
ashtavakra_gita::24.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as isolated to seeing yourself as inseparable from everything around you.

ashtavakra_gita::25.verse_sanskrit:
तन्तुमात्रो भवेद् एव पटो यद्वद् विचारितः ।
आत्मतन्मात्रमेवेदं तद्वद् विश्वं विचारितम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::25.verse_hindi: जैसे विचार करने पर वस्त्र तन्तु मात्र ही होता है, वैसे ही विचार करने से यह संसार आत्मसत्ता मात्र ही है।
ashtavakra_gita::25.english_translation: Just as a cloth is only threads when examined, the entire world is only the essence of the true self when contemplated.
ashtavakra_gita::25.translation_literal: तन्तुमात्रो (thread only) भवेद् (becomes) एव (indeed) पटो (cloth) यद्वद् (just as) विचारितः (contemplated) । आत्मतन्मात्रमेवेदं (true self only this) तद्वद् (just as) विश्वं (world) विचारितम् (contemplated) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::25.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::25.essence: Everything you see is woven from the essence of your true self.
ashtavakra_gita::25.simple_meaning: Looking closely at cloth reveals only threads. Similarly, reflecting deeply on the world reveals it as nothing but the essence of your true self.
ashtavakra_gita::25.simple_insight: There is a hidden unity beneath all appearances, waiting to be recognized.
ashtavakra_gita::25.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches King Janaka that the world, like a cloth made of threads, is essentially woven from the true self. This insight invites Janaka to see beyond surface appearances to the underlying reality.
ashtavakra_gita::25.modern_relevance: When you analyze a complex situation or relationship, you often find simpler, fundamental truths beneath the surface that shape everything.
ashtavakra_gita::25.insight: It shifts your view from seeing the world as separate things to recognizing it as expressions of one essence.

ashtavakra_gita::26.verse_sanskrit:
यथैवेक्षुरसे क्लृप्ता तेन व्याप्तैव शर्करा ।
तथा विश्वं मयि क्लृप्तं मया व्याप्तं निरन्तरम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::26.verse_hindi: जैसे ईख के रस से बनी हुई शर्करा ईख के रस में व्याप्त है, वैसे ही मुझसे बना हुआ संसार मुझमें भी व्याप्त है।
ashtavakra_gita::26.english_translation: Just as sugar made from sugarcane is pervaded by the juice of the sugarcane, similarly the world made from me is pervaded by me continuously.
ashtavakra_gita::26.translation_literal: यथा (just as) एवेक्षुः (of the sugarcane) असे (juice) क्लृप्ता (made) तेन (by that) व्याप्तैव (pervaded indeed) शर्करा (sugar) । तथा (similarly) विश्वं (world) मयि (in me) क्लृप्तं (made) मया (by me) व्याप्तं (pervaded) निरन्तरम् (continuously) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::26.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::26.essence: Everything in the world exists within you as an inseparable expression of your true self.
ashtavakra_gita::26.simple_meaning: Everything in the world exists within you just as sugar is fully present in sugarcane juice.
ashtavakra_gita::26.simple_insight: You can feel a deep connection knowing nothing is separate from your true self.
ashtavakra_gita::26.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra uses the example of sugar in sugarcane juice to explain that the world arises from and continuously exists within the true self. This teaching reveals the inseparability of the self from all apparent forms.
ashtavakra_gita::26.modern_relevance: When you realize that people, places, and things are all expressions of your own inner being, feeling disconnected softens.
ashtavakra_gita::26.insight: It shifts your perception from separation to unity, seeing yourself as the container and essence of all experience.

ashtavakra_gita::27.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मज्ञानाज्जगद् भाति आत्मज्ञानान्न भासते ।
रज्ज्वज्ञानादहिर्भाति तज्ज्ञानाद् भासते न हि ॥
ashtavakra_gita::27.verse_hindi: आत्मा के अज्ञान से संसार भासता है, आत्मा के ज्ञान नहीं भासता है । जैसे रस्सी के अज्ञान से सर्प भासता है, उसके अज्ञान से नहीं भासता है।
ashtavakra_gita::27.english_translation: The world appears due to ignorance of the true self; it does not appear due to knowledge of the true self. Just as a snake appears because of ignorance about the rope, it does not appear due to knowledge of the rope.
ashtavakra_gita::27.translation_literal: आत्मज्ञानात् (from knowledge of the true self) जगद् (world) भाति (appears) आत्मज्ञानात् न (not from knowledge of the true self) भासते (appears). रज्ज्वज्ञानात् (from ignorance of the rope) अहिर्भाति (snake appears) तज्ज्ञानात् (from that knowledge) भासते (appears) न (not) हि (indeed).
ashtavakra_gita::27.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::27.essence: Illusions arise from ignorance of the true self, not from its knowledge.
ashtavakra_gita::27.simple_meaning: The world seems real only when you do not truly know yourself. When you have real knowledge of yourself, the world’s illusion disappears, like mistaking a rope for a snake.
ashtavakra_gita::27.simple_insight: There is freedom in realizing illusions come from ignorance, not from your true self.
ashtavakra_gita::27.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains to King Janaka that the entire world appears because of ignorance about the true self. This is like mistaking a rope for a snake in dim light. When true knowledge arises, the illusion vanishes, revealing reality.
ashtavakra_gita::27.modern_relevance: You might panic seeing a shadow or misunderstanding a situation, but when you clearly understand, fear and confusion vanish.
ashtavakra_gita::27.insight: It teaches you to question your perceptions and recognize that confusion comes from misunderstanding your own true nature.

ashtavakra_gita::28.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकाशो मे निजं रूपं नातिरिक्तोऽस्म्यहं ततः ।
यदा प्रकाशते विश्वं तदाहं भास एव हि ॥
ashtavakra_gita::28.verse_hindi: प्रकाश मेरा निजी स्वरूप है । मैं उससे भिन्न नहीं हूँ । जब संसार प्रकाशित होता है तब वह मेरे ही से प्रकाशित होता है ।
ashtavakra_gita::28.english_translation: Light is my own true nature; I am not separate from it. When the world is illuminated, it shines through me.
ashtavakra_gita::28.translation_literal: प्रकाशो (light) / मे (my) / निजं (own) / रूपं (form) / नातिरिक्तः (not separate) / अस्मि (I am) / ततः (therefore) / यदा (when) / प्रकाशते (it shines) / विश्वं (world) / तदा (then) / अहं (I) / भास (light) / एव (indeed) / हि (certainly)
ashtavakra_gita::28.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::28.essence: Your true nature is inseparable light that illuminates the entire world.
ashtavakra_gita::28.simple_meaning: Your essential self is pure light, not separate from it. When the world lights up, it does so through your own shining nature.
ashtavakra_gita::28.simple_insight: You are not apart from the brightness you see; you are its source and expression.
ashtavakra_gita::28.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Ashtavakra explains to Janaka that the true self is pure light, inseparable and foundational to the illumination of the entire world. This insight reveals the unity of self and existence as the source of all radiance.
ashtavakra_gita::28.modern_relevance: When you feel your own clarity or inspiration, recognize it as the same light that brings life and color to everything around you.
ashtavakra_gita::28.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as separate to realizing you are the source of illumination itself.

ashtavakra_gita::29.verse_sanskrit:
अहो विकल्पितं विश्वमज्ञानान्मयि भासते ।
रूप्यं शुक्तौ फणी रज्जौ वारि सूर्यकरे यथा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::29.verse_hindi: आश्चर्य है कि कल्पित संसार अज्ञान से मुझे ऐसा भासता है जैसे सीपी में चाँदी, रस्सी में साँप, सूर्य की किरणों में जल भासता है।
ashtavakra_gita::29.english_translation: How strange that the imagined world appears to me through ignorance, like silver in an oyster, a snake in a rope, or water in sun rays.
ashtavakra_gita::29.translation_literal: अहो (how strange) विकल्पितं (imagined) विश्वम् (world) अज्ञानात् (from ignorance) मयि (in me) भासते (appears) । रूप्यं (silver) शुक्तौ (in oyster) फणी (snake) रज्जौ (in rope) वारि (water) सूर्यकरे (in sun rays) यथा (like) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::29.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::29.essence: The world appears real because of confusion, but it is only a mistaken image.
ashtavakra_gita::29.simple_meaning: The world you experience is a mistaken appearance caused by confusion, like seeing silver in an oyster or a snake in a rope.
ashtavakra_gita::29.simple_insight: You feel surprised that what seems real is actually a false image created by the mind.
ashtavakra_gita::29.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains to King Janaka that the world appears real only because of ignorance, just as illusions like silver in an oyster or snakes in a rope deceive the senses. This shows how perception is distorted by the mind's confusion.
ashtavakra_gita::29.modern_relevance: You glance at a shadow and momentarily mistake it for a person, realizing later it was just a trick of light and mind.
ashtavakra_gita::29.insight: It teaches you to question your perceptions and recognize that appearances can be misleading illusions.

ashtavakra_gita::30.verse_sanskrit:
मत्तो विनिर्गतं विश्वं मय्येव लयमेष्यति ।
मृदि कुम्भो जले वीचिः  कनके कटकं यथा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::30.verse_hindi: मुझसे उत्पन्न यह संसार मुझमें ही लय को प्राप्त होगा जैसे मिट्टी में घड़ा, जल में लहर और सोने में आभूषण लय होते हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::30.english_translation: The universe born from me will dissolve in me, just as a pot merges into clay, a wave into water, and a jewel into gold.
ashtavakra_gita::30.translation_literal: मत्तो (from me) / विनिर्गतं (emerged) / विश्वं (universe) / मयि (in me) / एव (indeed) / लयमेष्यति (will dissolve) / मृदि (in clay) / कुम्भः (pot) / जले (in water) / वीचिः (wave) / कनके (in gold) / कटकं (jewel) / यथा (as)
ashtavakra_gita::30.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::30.essence: All that arises from you will naturally dissolve back into you.
ashtavakra_gita::30.simple_meaning: Everything that appears from you will eventually merge back into you, like a pot into clay or a wave into water.
ashtavakra_gita::30.simple_insight: You can feel grounded knowing all forms arise and dissolve within you.
ashtavakra_gita::30.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the entire universe arises from the true self and will ultimately dissolve back into it, just like everyday objects merge back into their original substance. This reveals the oneness beneath apparent diversity.
ashtavakra_gita::30.modern_relevance: When facing loss or change, remember that all things come from and return to your true essence, easing fear of endings.
ashtavakra_gita::30.insight: It guides you to see all experiences as temporary forms emerging from your core, shifting focus from separation to unity.

ashtavakra_gita::31.verse_sanskrit:
अहो अहं नमो मह्यं विनाशो यस्य नास्ति मे ।
ब्रह्मादिस्तम्बपर्यन्तं जगन्नाशोऽपि तिष्ठतः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::31.verse_hindi: मैं आश्चर्यमय हूँ । मुझको नमस्कार है । ब्रह्मा से लेकर तृणपर्यन्त जगत के नाश होने पर भी मेरा नाश नहीं है।
ashtavakra_gita::31.english_translation: I am wondrous. I bow to myself. From Brahma to the blade of grass, even if the world is destroyed, I am not destroyed.
ashtavakra_gita::31.translation_literal: अहो (oh) अहं (I) नमो (salutation) मह्यं (to myself) विनाशो (destruction) यस्य (whose) नास्ति (is not) मे (for me) । ब्रह्मादि (from Brahma and so on) स्तम्बपर्यन्तं (up to the blade of grass) जगन्नाशोऽपि (even if the world is destroyed) तिष्ठतः (standing/remains) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::31.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::31.essence: You remain untouched and eternal even if the entire world is destroyed.
ashtavakra_gita::31.simple_meaning: You are wondrous and indestructible; even if everything from the greatest to the smallest perishes, you remain unchanged.
ashtavakra_gita::31.simple_insight: There's a deep steadiness in knowing you cannot be destroyed, no matter what happens around you.
ashtavakra_gita::31.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Ashtavakra declares to King Janaka that his true self is beyond all destruction. From the highest deity Brahma to the smallest blade of grass, even if everything is destroyed, the true self remains untouched and eternal.
ashtavakra_gita::31.modern_relevance: When life feels chaotic and everything seems to fall apart, this reminds you of your inner strength that no external event can shake.
ashtavakra_gita::31.insight: It teaches you to recognize your true self as stable and unchanging beneath all external changes and losses.

ashtavakra_gita::32.verse_sanskrit:
अहो अहं नमो मह्यमेकोऽहं देहवानपि ।
क्वचिन्न गन्ता नागन्ता व्याप्य विश्वमवस्थितः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::32.verse_hindi: मैं आश्चर्यमय हूँ । मुझको नमस्कार है । मैं देहधारी होते हुए भी अद्वैत हूँ । न कहीं जाता हूँ, न आता हूँ और विश्व में व्याप्त हुआ स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::32.english_translation: I am wondrous. I bow to myself. Though embodied, I am non-dual. I neither come nor go and pervade the entire world.
ashtavakra_gita::32.translation_literal: अहो (Ah, wondrous) अहं (I) नमो (salutation) मह्यम् (to myself) एकः (alone) अहं (I) देहवानपि (though body-having) क्वचित् (anywhere) न (not) गन्ता (going) न (not) आगन्ता (coming) व्याप्य (pervading) विश्वम् (the world) अवस्थितः (situated)
ashtavakra_gita::32.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::32.essence: You are limitless presence beyond body, neither arriving nor departing.
ashtavakra_gita::32.simple_meaning: You are amazing and complete. Even though you have a body, your true self is not limited by it. You do not come or go but are present everywhere in the world.
ashtavakra_gita::32.simple_insight: You can feel the awe of being more than just a physical form, infinite and ever-present.
ashtavakra_gita::32.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to King Janaka, revealing that despite appearing as a body, the true self is non-dual, neither arriving nor departing, but fully present everywhere in the universe. This teaching uproots ordinary ideas of identity tied to physical form.
ashtavakra_gita::32.modern_relevance: When you catch yourself caught up in your body’s limits, remember you are more than that—already present in all places and moments.
ashtavakra_gita::32.insight: It shifts your view from identifying only as a body to recognizing your limitless, unchanging presence everywhere.

ashtavakra_gita::33.verse_sanskrit:
अहो अहं नमो मह्यं दक्षो नास्तीह मत्समः ।
असंस्पृश्य शरीरेण येन विश्वं चिरं धृतम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::33.verse_hindi: मैं आश्चर्यमय हूँ । मुझको नमस्कार है । इस संसार में मेरे समान निपुण कोई नहीं । क्योंकि शरीर को स्पर्श किये बिना ही इस विश्व को सदा धारण किये रहता हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::33.english_translation: I am wondrous. I bow to myself. No one in this world is as skilled as I am, for without touching the body, I have sustained the universe for a long time.
ashtavakra_gita::33.translation_literal: अहो (Ah) / अहं (I) / नमो (salutation) / मह्यं (to myself) / दक्षो (skilled) / नास्तीह (there is not) / मत्समः (equal to me) / असंस्पृश्य (without touching) / शरीरेण (with the body) / येन (by whom) / विश्वं (universe) / चिरं (long) / धृतम् (sustained)
ashtavakra_gita::33.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::33.essence: Your true self supports all existence beyond any physical limitation.
ashtavakra_gita::33.simple_meaning: You are amazing because your true self supports the entire universe without depending on your physical body.
ashtavakra_gita::33.simple_insight: You can feel awe in knowing your true self is beyond the body yet holds everything.
ashtavakra_gita::33.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra declares his supreme skill and wonder: unlike anyone else, he sustains the universe without relying on his body. This shows the self's power beyond physical limitation in the dialogue with King Janaka.
ashtavakra_gita::33.modern_relevance: When you feel limited by your physical or mental state, remember your deeper self supports much more than you realize.
ashtavakra_gita::33.insight: This verse shifts your view from identifying with your body to recognizing your vast inner presence sustaining all.

ashtavakra_gita::34.verse_sanskrit:
अहो अहं नमो मह्यं यस्य मे नास्ति किञ्चन ।
अथवा यस्य मे सर्वं यद् वाङ्मनसगोचरम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::34.verse_hindi: मैं आश्चर्यमय हूँ । मुझको नमस्कार है । मेरा कुछ भी नहीं है, अथवा मेरा सब कुछ है – जो मन और वाणी का विषय है।
ashtavakra_gita::34.english_translation: I am the wonder. I am worthy of reverence. I have nothing, or I have everything that mind and speech can grasp.
ashtavakra_gita::34.translation_literal: अहो (Ah, wonder) / अहं (I) / नमो (reverence) / मह्यं (to me) / यस्य (whose) / मे (my) / नास्ति (is not) / किञ्चन (anything) / अथवा (or) / यस्य (whose) / मे (my) / सर्वं (everything) / यद् (that) / वाङ्मनसगोचरम् (mind and speech's object)
ashtavakra_gita::34.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::34.essence: You are a wondrous presence beyond all concepts of having or not having.
ashtavakra_gita::34.simple_meaning: You are the miraculous presence that cannot be fully captured by mind or words, both empty and complete.
ashtavakra_gita::34.simple_insight: Feel awe knowing you are beyond both having and not having.
ashtavakra_gita::34.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra proclaims a profound self-recognition that transcends ordinary experience: the true self is astonishing and beyond the grasp of mental concepts or speech, simultaneously empty of possession and full of all.
ashtavakra_gita::34.modern_relevance: In moments when words fail and thoughts fall silent, you glimpse a presence within that is both everything and nothing, beyond explanation.
ashtavakra_gita::34.insight: It shifts your view from limiting identity to an expansive, paradoxical self that defies conceptual boundaries.

ashtavakra_gita::35.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं तथा ज्ञाता त्रितयं नास्ति वास्तवम् ।
अज्ञानाद् भाति यत्रेदं सोऽहमस्मि निरञ्जनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::35.verse_hindi: ज्ञान, ज्ञेय और ज्ञाता ये तीनों यथार्थ नहीं हैं । जहाँ ये तीनों अज्ञान से ही भासते हैं। मैं वही निरञ्जन हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::35.english_translation: Knowledge, the known, and the knower are not real; where these three appear, there is ignorance. I am the stainless one beyond them.
ashtavakra_gita::35.translation_literal: ज्ञानं (knowledge) / ज्ञेयं (the known) / तथा (also) / ज्ञाता (the knower) / त्रितयं (threefold) / नास्ति (is not) / वास्तवम् (real) / अज्ञानाद् (from ignorance) / भाति (shines/appears) / यत्र (where) / एदम् (this) / सोऽहमस्मि (I am that) / निरञ्जनः (stainless).
ashtavakra_gita::35.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::35.essence: The self is beyond the triad of knower, known, and knowledge, which arise from ignorance.
ashtavakra_gita::35.simple_meaning: The ideas of knowledge, the object known, and the knower are not ultimately real. They arise from ignorance. The true self is beyond these and remains pure.
ashtavakra_gita::35.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing your true self is untouched by confusion or knowing.
ashtavakra_gita::35.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the usual division into knower, known, and knowledge is an illusion caused by ignorance. The true self is a pure, spotless awareness beyond this threefold division.
ashtavakra_gita::35.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by thoughts or information, you can find calm by recognizing you are beyond all that restless knowing.
ashtavakra_gita::35.insight: This shifts your mind from identifying with thoughts to realizing your pure awareness beyond all knowledge.

ashtavakra_gita::36.verse_sanskrit:
द्वैतमूलमहो दुःखं नान्यत्तस्याऽस्ति भेषजम् ।
दृश्यमेतन् मृषा सर्वमेकोऽहं चिद्रसोमलः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::36.verse_hindi: अहो ! दुःख का मूल द्वैत है, उसकी औषधि अन्य कोई नहीं । यह सब दृश्य मिथ्या है । मैं एक विशुद्ध चैतन्यरस हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::36.english_translation: The root of all suffering is duality; there is no other remedy. All that appears is false. I am the one pure essence of consciousness.
ashtavakra_gita::36.translation_literal: द्वैतमूलम् (root of duality) / अशो (great) / दुःखम् (suffering) / न (not) / अन्यत् (other) / अस्ति (exists) / भेषजम् (remedy) / दृश्यम् (visible) / एतत् (this) / मृषा (false) / सर्वम् (all) / एकः (one) / अहं (I) / चिद् (consciousness) / रसः (essence) / मलः (pure)
ashtavakra_gita::36.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::36.essence: Suffering arises from seeing separation, but your true self is one pure consciousness.
ashtavakra_gita::36.simple_meaning: Suffering arises from seeing the world as divided and separate. Everything we perceive is an illusion. The true self is pure, unified consciousness.
ashtavakra_gita::36.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing that pain comes from false separation, not from your true self.
ashtavakra_gita::36.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the cause of suffering is the mistaken belief in duality—seeing self and other as separate. He reveals that this visible world is illusory and that your real nature is a single, pure essence of consciousness.
ashtavakra_gita::36.modern_relevance: When you argue with others or feel isolated, remember that this sense of separation causes your distress, not your true nature.
ashtavakra_gita::36.insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with divided appearances to recognizing your oneness as pure awareness.

ashtavakra_gita::37.verse_sanskrit:
बोधमात्रोऽहमज्ञानाद् उपाधिः कल्पितो मया ।
एवं विमृशतो नित्यं निर्विकल्पे स्थितिर्मम ॥
ashtavakra_gita::37.verse_hindi: मैं बोधमात्र हूँ । किन्तु मेरे द्वारा अज्ञान से उपाधि की कल्पना की गई है । इस प्रकार नित्य विचार करते हुए मैं निर्विकल्प में स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::37.english_translation: I am pure awareness, but ignorance has created a false identity around me. Reflecting on this constantly, I remain established in the undifferentiated state.
ashtavakra_gita::37.translation_literal: बोधमात्रः (pure awareness only) / अहम् (I) / अज्ञानात् (from ignorance) / उपाधिः (false identity) / कल्पितः (created) / मया (by me) / एवं (thus) / विमृशतः (reflecting) / नित्यम् (constantly) / निर्विकल्पे (in undifferentiated) / स्थितिः (state) / मम (my)
ashtavakra_gita::37.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::37.essence: Your true self is pure awareness; all separation is imagined by confusion.
ashtavakra_gita::37.simple_meaning: Your true self is pure awareness. The sense of being separate is a false idea created by confusion. By seeing this clearly, you rest in a peaceful undivided state.
ashtavakra_gita::37.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing your true nature is beyond all imagined limits.
ashtavakra_gita::37.detailed_meaning: In a dialogue between King Janaka and sage Ashtavakra, Ashtavakra reveals that the self is pure awareness alone. The sense of separate identity arises from ignorance, but by constant reflection, one can remain established in the undisturbed state beyond thought.
ashtavakra_gita::37.modern_relevance: When your restless mind invents stories about who you are, you can pause and remember you are simply aware, untouched by those stories.
ashtavakra_gita::37.insight: It teaches you to recognize the false labels your mind creates and return to the direct experience of awareness.

ashtavakra_gita::38.verse_sanskrit:
न मे बन्धोऽस्ति मोक्षो वा भ्रान्तिः शान्तो निराश्रया ।
अहो मयि स्थितं विश्वं वस्तुतो न मयि स्थितम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::38.verse_hindi: आश्चर्य है ! मुझमें स्थित हुआ विश्व वास्तव में मुझमें स्थित नहीं है । इसलिए न मेरा बन्ध है, न मोक्ष।
ashtavakra_gita::38.english_translation: Surprisingly, the universe appears to be within me, but in truth, it is not within me; thus, I have neither bondage nor freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::38.translation_literal: न (not) मे (in me) बन्धोऽस्ति (is bondage) मोक्षो (freedom) वा (or) भ्रान्तिः (illusion) शान्तो (peaceful) निराश्रया (without support) । अहो (oh!) मयि (in me) स्थितं (situated) विश्वं (the universe) वस्तुतो (in reality) न (not) मयि (in me) स्थितम् (situated) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::38.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::38.essence: The true self is untouched by the seeming presence of the universe within it.
ashtavakra_gita::38.simple_meaning: Though it seems the universe exists within you, in reality it does not; therefore, you are neither bound nor freed.
ashtavakra_gita::38.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing you're untouched by the world's illusions and limits.
ashtavakra_gita::38.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that although the world appears to be contained within the self, this is a mistaken appearance; the true self is beyond all binding or freeing conditions, peaceful and without support.
ashtavakra_gita::38.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by everything around you, remember that none of it truly confines your true self.
ashtavakra_gita::38.insight: It shifts your view from feeling trapped by appearances to recognizing your inner freedom beyond them.

ashtavakra_gita::39.verse_sanskrit:
सशरीरमिदं विश्वं न किञ्चिदिति निश्चितम् ।
शुद्धचिन्मात्र आत्मा च तत्कस्मिन् कल्पनाधुना ॥
ashtavakra_gita::39.verse_hindi: निश्चय ही शरीरयुक्त यह विश्व कुछ भी नहीं है । यह शुद्ध चैतन्यमात्र आत्मा है तो इसकी कल्पना ही किसमें है।
ashtavakra_gita::39.english_translation: This body-bound universe is certainly nothing; the pure conscious self alone exists, so what is there to imagine?
ashtavakra_gita::39.translation_literal: सशरीरमिदं (this with body) / विश्वं (universe) / न (not) / किञ्चिदिति (anything) / निश्चितम् (certain) / शुद्धचिन्मात्र (pure-consciousness-only) / आत्मा (self) / च (and) / तत्कस्मिन् (in that) / कल्पनाधुना (by imagination)
ashtavakra_gita::39.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::39.essence: The body and universe are imagined; only pure consciousness truly exists.
ashtavakra_gita::39.simple_meaning: The universe tied to the body is ultimately unreal; only the pure conscious self truly exists beyond all imagination.
ashtavakra_gita::39.simple_insight: You can feel a deep relief realizing that what seems solid is just imagined around your true self.
ashtavakra_gita::39.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra tells King Janaka that the entire universe connected to the body is ultimately unreal, and only the pure conscious self truly exists without any imaginary cover.
ashtavakra_gita::39.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your surroundings, remember that what you experience as solid is just imagined by the mind over your pure awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::39.insight: It shifts your perspective from identifying with the body and the world to recognizing the self as pure consciousness alone.

ashtavakra_gita::40.verse_sanskrit:
शरीरं स्वर्गनरकौ बन्धमोक्षौ भयं तथा ।
कल्पनामात्रमेवैतत् किं मे कार्यं चिदात्मनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::40.verse_hindi: यह शरीर, स्वर्ग, नरक, बन्ध, मोक्ष व भय कल्पना मात्र ही हैं । उससे मुझ चैतन्य आत्मा को क्या प्रयोजन ।
ashtavakra_gita::40.english_translation: The body, higher and lower realms, bondage, freedom, and fear are all mere imagination; what purpose do they serve for my conscious self?
ashtavakra_gita::40.translation_literal: शरीरं (body) / स्वर्गनरकौ (heaven and hell) / बन्धमोक्षौ (bondage and freedom) / भयं (fear) / तथा (also) / कल्पनामात्रमेव (only imagination) / एतत् (this) / किं (what) / मे (to me) / कार्यं (purpose) / चिदात्मनः (to the conscious self)
ashtavakra_gita::40.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::40.essence: The true self is untouched by body, fear, or imagined states like bondage or freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::40.simple_meaning: The body, the ideas of higher and lower realms, bondage, freedom, and fear exist only as mental creations. The true self remains unaffected by these.
ashtavakra_gita::40.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing these fears and labels are just mental stories, not your real nature.
ashtavakra_gita::40.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that everything we take seriously—our body, fears, and even concepts like bondage or freedom—are only imagined. The true self, pure consciousness, has no connection or need for these illusions.
ashtavakra_gita::40.modern_relevance: When stress or fear about your body or future overwhelms you, remembering these are just thoughts can bring calm.
ashtavakra_gita::40.insight: It shifts your focus from identifying with physical and emotional fears to recognizing your unchanging conscious self.

ashtavakra_gita::41.verse_sanskrit:
अहो जनसमूहेऽपि न द्वैतं पश्यतो मम ।
अरण्यमिव संवृत्तं क्व रतिं करवाण्यहम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::41.verse_hindi: आश्चर्य है कि जन समूह में भी मुझे द्वैत दिखाई नहीं देता है । यह अरण्यवत् हो गया है तो फिर मैं किससे प्रेम करूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::41.english_translation: I am amazed that even among the crowd, I see no duality; like being in a forest, whom then do I love?
ashtavakra_gita::41.translation_literal: अहो (ah) / जनसमूहेऽपि (among the crowd also) / न (not) / द्वैतं (duality) / पश्यतो (seeing) / मम (to me) / । (।) / अरण्यमिव (like a forest) / संवृत्तं (enclosed, withdrawn) / क्व (where) / रतिं (love) / करवाणि (doing) / अहम् (I) / ॥
ashtavakra_gita::41.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::41.essence: Being among many yet seeing no separation reveals love beyond boundaries.
ashtavakra_gita::41.simple_meaning: Even when surrounded by many people, you perceive no division in reality. Like being deep in a forest, you wonder to whom you should direct your love.
ashtavakra_gita::41.simple_insight: You feel a surprising unity that dissolves usual distinctions and the need to choose whom to love.
ashtavakra_gita::41.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra reflects on the paradox of being among many yet seeing no duality. This moment reveals the depth of non-separation where love is not limited to any particular object or person.
ashtavakra_gita::41.modern_relevance: In a busy room full of faces, you suddenly sense that everyone is connected beyond appearances, making love and separation meaningless.
ashtavakra_gita::41.insight: It teaches you to recognize the oneness beneath apparent diversity, shifting from selective attachment to universal love.

ashtavakra_gita::42.verse_sanskrit:
नाहं देहो न मे देहो जीवो नाहमहं हि चित् ।
अयमेव हि मे बन्ध आसीद्या जीविते स्पृहा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::42.verse_hindi: न मैं शरीर हूँ, न मेरा शरीर है, मैं जीव नहीं हूँ, निश्चय ही मैं चैतन्यमात्र हूँ । मेरा यही बन्ध था कि मेरी जीने की इच्छा थी।
ashtavakra_gita::42.english_translation: I am not the body, nor do I possess a body; I am not the living being, indeed I am pure awareness. My only bondage was the desire to live.
ashtavakra_gita::42.translation_literal: नाहं (not I) देहो (body) न (nor) मे (my) देहो (body) जीवो (living being) नाहम् (not I) हि (indeed) चित् (consciousness) । अयमेव (this alone) हि (indeed) मे (my) बन्ध (bondage) आसीत् (was) या (which) जीविते (in life) स्पृहा (desire) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::42.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::42.essence: You are pure awareness, not the body or life, and desire alone created your bondage.
ashtavakra_gita::42.simple_meaning: You are not your body or your living self; you are pure awareness. The only thing that trapped you was the desire to keep living.
ashtavakra_gita::42.simple_insight: Realizing you are pure awareness frees you from identifying with the body and life’s desires.
ashtavakra_gita::42.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that what you truly are is not the body or the living being but pure consciousness itself. The apparent bondage comes from craving continued existence, which veils your real nature.
