ashtavakra_gita::42.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your body’s needs or fears about survival, remember your true nature is awareness beyond all that.
ashtavakra_gita::42.insight: Shift your identity from physical life and desires to the pure awareness that witnesses all experience.

ashtavakra_gita::43.verse_sanskrit:
अहो भुवनकल्लोलैर्विचित्रैर्द्राक् समुत्थितम् ।
मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ चित्तवाते समुद्यते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::43.verse_hindi: आश्चर्य की अनन्त समुद्ररूप मुझमें चित्तरूपी हवा के उठने पर शीघ्र ही विचित्र जगतरूपी तरंगें पैदा होती हैं ।
ashtavakra_gita::43.english_translation: In me, like an endless ocean, strange waves of the world swiftly arise with the rising of the mind-wind.
ashtavakra_gita::43.translation_literal: अहो (oh) / भुवनकल्लोलैः (world-waves) / विचित्रैः (strange) / द्राक् (quickly) / समुत्थितम् (arisen) / मयि (in me) / अनन्त (endless) / महाम्भोधौ (great ocean) / चित्तवाते (mind-wind) / समुद्यते (rises)
ashtavakra_gita::43.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::43.essence: Restless thoughts arise like waves, but your true self is the vast calm ocean.
ashtavakra_gita::43.simple_meaning: Your restless mind creates many strange waves of thoughts and emotions, but beneath them, you are like a vast, endless ocean.
ashtavakra_gita::43.simple_insight: There is calmness inside you even when your mind feels stormy and restless.
ashtavakra_gita::43.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes the true self as an endless ocean within, while the mind’s restless wind causes waves of changing thoughts and feelings to arise. This moment reveals the contrast between your deep inner stillness and the surface turbulence.
ashtavakra_gita::43.modern_relevance: When your mind races with worry or distraction, remember that your true self remains calm and vast beneath the noise.
ashtavakra_gita::43.insight: It teaches you to see your restless thoughts as temporary waves, not your true nature.

ashtavakra_gita::44.verse_sanskrit:
मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ चित्तवाते प्रशाम्यति ।
अभाग्याज्जीववणिजो जगत्पोतो विनश्वरः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::44.verse_hindi: अनन्त महासागररूप मुझ में चित्तरूप वायु के शान्त होने पर जीवरूप व्यापारी के अभाग्य से जगत रूपी नौका नाश को प्राप्त होती है।
ashtavakra_gita::44.english_translation: In me, the infinite great ocean, the mind calms like the wind; yet, due to misfortune, the living merchant and the world-boat perish.
ashtavakra_gita::44.translation_literal: मयि (in me) अनन्त (infinite) महाम्भोधौ (great ocean) चित्तवाते (mind-wind) प्रशाम्यति (calms) । अभाग्यात् (due to misfortune) जीववणिजः (living merchant) जगत्पतः (world-boat) विनश्वरः (perish) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::44.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::44.essence: The mind can be deeply calm and infinite even while the outer world suffers loss.
ashtavakra_gita::44.simple_meaning: Your mind can become as vast and peaceful as an endless ocean, even while life itself faces destruction and misfortune.
ashtavakra_gita::44.simple_insight: You can feel calm and expansive inside, even when everything outside seems to fall apart.
ashtavakra_gita::44.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that within the infinite self, the restless mind can find deep calm like a vast ocean. Meanwhile, the individual life, compared to a merchant's boat, faces misfortune and eventual destruction. The teaching points to inner equanimity beyond outer loss.
ashtavakra_gita::44.modern_relevance: After a harsh failure or loss, your mind can still find a deep stillness that no external event can shake.
ashtavakra_gita::44.insight: It teaches you that inner calm is separate from outer events and can remain steady despite life's misfortunes.

ashtavakra_gita::45.verse_sanskrit:
मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधावाश्चर्यं जीववीचयः ।
उद्यन्ति घ्नन्ति खेलन्ति प्रविशन्ति स्वभावतः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::45.verse_hindi: आश्चर्य है कि अनन्त महासागररूप मुझ में जीवरूप तरंगें उठती हैं, परस्पर संघर्ष करती हैं, खेलती हैं तथा स्वभाव से ही लय हो जाती हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::45.english_translation: It is astonishing that within me, the infinite great ocean, waves of life rise, clash, play, and naturally dissolve.
ashtavakra_gita::45.translation_literal: मयि (in me) अनन्त (infinite) महाम्भोधौ (great ocean) आश्चर्यं (astonishment) जीव-वीचयः (waves of life) उद्यन्ति (arise) घ्नन्ति (destroy) खेलन्ति (play) प्रविशन्ति (enter) स्वभावतः (by nature)
ashtavakra_gita::45.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::45.essence: Your inner being is an infinite ocean where life’s waves arise and dissolve naturally.
ashtavakra_gita::45.simple_meaning: Within you is an infinite ocean where waves of life appear, interact, and naturally disappear again.
ashtavakra_gita::45.simple_insight: You can feel wonder at how your restless life flows and fades within a vast inner space.
ashtavakra_gita::45.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka about the true self being like an infinite ocean. The waves—our thoughts and experiences—arise, struggle, and vanish naturally within it, showing life’s dynamic yet transient nature.
ashtavakra_gita::45.modern_relevance: You notice your emotions and thoughts rising and falling like waves inside you, sometimes clashing, sometimes playing, always changing.
ashtavakra_gita::45.insight: It teaches you to see your changing thoughts and feelings as natural waves within your vast inner being, not permanent or threatening.

ashtavakra_gita::46.verse_sanskrit:
अविनाशिनमात्मानमेकं विज्ञाय तत्त्वतः ।
तवात्मज्ञानस्य धीरस्य कथमर्थार्जने रतिः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::46.verse_hindi: अष्टावक्र कहते हैं – आत्मा को तत्वतः एक और अविनाशी जानकर भी तुझ आत्मज्ञानी धीर को धन कमाने में आसक्ति क्यों है।
ashtavakra_gita::46.english_translation: Ashtavakra says: Knowing the self as truly one and indestructible, why does your wise and steady self still desire to earn wealth?
ashtavakra_gita::46.translation_literal: अविनाशिनम् (indestructible) आत्मानम् (self) एकम् (one) विज्ञाय (knowing) तत्त्वतः (truly) / तव (your) आत्मज्ञानस्य (self-knowledge) धीरस्य (wise/steady) कथम् (how/why) अर्थार्जने (earning wealth) रतिः (desire/attachment)
ashtavakra_gita::46.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::46.essence: Knowing your self is unchanging, attachment to wealth reveals a hidden inner conflict.
ashtavakra_gita::46.simple_meaning: You understand that your true self is one and indestructible, yet your steady self still craves earning money.
ashtavakra_gita::46.simple_insight: It feels confusing and freeing to realize your deepest self doesn’t need what you chase.
ashtavakra_gita::46.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra confronts a seeker who fully knows the self is eternal and unified but remains attached to material gain, highlighting the tension between true knowledge and worldly desires.
ashtavakra_gita::46.modern_relevance: You’ve grasped your core identity beyond change, yet find yourself anxiously chasing promotions or money that can’t truly satisfy.
ashtavakra_gita::46.insight: It shifts the mind to notice the gap between knowing your true nature and habits of craving external rewards.

ashtavakra_gita::47.verse_sanskrit:
आत्माज्ञानादहो प्रीतिर्विषयभ्रमगोचरे ।
शुक्तेरज्ञानतो लोभो यथा रजतविभ्रमे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::47.verse_hindi: आश्चर्य कि आत्मा के अज्ञान से विषय का भ्रम होने पर वैसी ही प्रीति होती है जैसी सीपी के अज्ञान से चाँदी की भ्रान्ति में लोभ होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::47.english_translation: It is surprising that ignorance of the true self causes attachment to objects, just as a shell's ignorance causes greed for silver.
ashtavakra_gita::47.translation_literal: आत्मा (self) ज्ञान (knowledge) अधः (below/ignorance) प्रीतिः (attachment) विषय (objects) भ्रम (illusion) गोचर (subject to) । शुक्तेः (of the shell) अज्ञानातः (from ignorance) लोभः (greed) यथा (just as) रजत (silver) भ्रमे (illusion) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::47.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::47.essence: Attachment arises from ignorance of your true self, like mistaking a shell for silver.
ashtavakra_gita::47.simple_meaning: Attachment to things happens because you don’t recognize your true self, just like a shell wrongly thinks it holds silver.
ashtavakra_gita::47.simple_insight: You can feel freed when you realize your cravings come from misunderstanding who you truly are.
ashtavakra_gita::47.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra points out a deep error: just as a shell mistakenly believes it contains silver, a person unaware of their true self wrongly clings to external objects, causing attachment and confusion.
ashtavakra_gita::47.modern_relevance: You might find yourself chasing things that seem valuable, only to realize later they aren’t what truly matters because you haven’t connected with your deeper self.
ashtavakra_gita::47.insight: It teaches you to see craving as a mistake born from not knowing your real nature, easing attachment’s hold.

ashtavakra_gita::48.verse_sanskrit:
विश्वं स्फुरति यत्रेदं तरङ्गा इव सागरे ।
सोऽहमस्मीति विज्ञाय किं दीन इव धावसि ॥
ashtavakra_gita::48.verse_hindi: जहाँ यह विश्व आत्मा में समुद्र में तरंग के समान स्फुरित होता है, ‘वही मैं हूँ’, ऐसा जानकर क्यों तू दीन की तरह दौड़ता है।
ashtavakra_gita::48.english_translation: Where the entire universe flickers like waves in the ocean of the self, knowing 'I am that,' why do you run like a helpless one?
ashtavakra_gita::48.translation_literal: विश्वं (universe) स्फुरति (flickers) यत्र (where) एदम् (this) तरङ्गा (waves) इव (like) सागरे (in the ocean) । सोऽहमस्मीति (I am that) विज्ञाय (knowing) किं (why) दीन (helpless) इव (like) धावसि (do you run) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::48.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::48.essence: You are the unchanging ocean in which all waves of the universe appear.
ashtavakra_gita::48.simple_meaning: You are the vast self in which the whole universe appears like waves. Knowing this, you need not run helplessly.
ashtavakra_gita::48.simple_insight: You can feel safe and steady because you are the unchanging ocean beneath all waves.
ashtavakra_gita::48.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the entire universe is like waves on the ocean of the true self. Recognizing 'I am that' means you understand your fundamental unity with everything, so there is no need to run in fear or confusion.
ashtavakra_gita::48.modern_relevance: When anxiety makes you feel small and frantic, remember you are the vast foundation beneath all your worries, steady and unshaken.
ashtavakra_gita::48.insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with fleeting fears to resting as the unchanging self beneath all change.

ashtavakra_gita::49.verse_hindi: आत्मा को शुद्ध चैतन्य व अति सुन्दर सुनकर भी कैसे कोई इन्द्रिय के विषय में अत्यन्त आसक्त होकर मलिनता को प्राप्त होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::49.english_translation: How can the true self, pure consciousness, and supremely beautiful, become tainted by extreme attachment to sense objects despite hearing this?
ashtavakra_gita::49.translation_literal: श्रुत्वा (hearing) अपि (even) शुद्ध (pure) चैतन्य (consciousness) आत्मानम् (self) अति (very) सुन्दरम् (beautiful) / उपस्थे (being present) अत्यन्त (extremely) संसक्तः (attached) मालिन्यम् (taint) अधिगच्छति (attains)
ashtavakra_gita::49.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::49.essence: Pure self remains untainted, but attachment to senses clouds awareness despite knowing this.
ashtavakra_gita::49.simple_meaning: Even when you understand that your true self is pure and beautiful, strong attachment to sensory things can still cloud your inner clarity.
ashtavakra_gita::49.simple_insight: It feels confusing that knowing your true self is pure doesn't stop you from getting caught in distractions.
ashtavakra_gita::49.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra points out the paradox where King Janaka recognizes the true self as pure consciousness and supremely beautiful, yet remains deeply attached to sensory experiences, causing inner confusion and impurity despite this knowledge.
ashtavakra_gita::49.modern_relevance: You know your best self is clear and calm, yet you find yourself stuck in endless distractions and cravings that cloud your peace.
ashtavakra_gita::49.insight: It reveals the gap between intellectual understanding of purity and the habitual emotional attachment that blocks inner clarity.

ashtavakra_gita::50.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि ।
मुनेर्जानत आश्चर्यं ममत्वमनुवर्तते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::50.verse_hindi: सब भूतों में आत्मा को और आत्मा में सब भूतों को जानकर भी मुनि को ममता होती है । यही आश्चर्य है।
ashtavakra_gita::50.english_translation: The sage knows the true self in all beings and all beings in the true self, yet still feels attachment — that is the wonder.
ashtavakra_gita::50.translation_literal: सर्वभूतेषु (in all beings) च (and) आत्मानं (the true self) सर्वभूतानि (all beings) च (and) आत्मनि (in the true self) । मुनेः (of the sage) जानत (knowing) आश्चर्यं (wonder) ममत्वम् (attachment) अनु वर्तते (follows) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::50.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::50.essence: Knowing oneness doesn’t erase the experience of personal identity—it coexists as a mystery.
ashtavakra_gita::50.simple_meaning: Even when a wise person fully understands that their true self is in all beings and all beings are in their true self, they surprisingly still feel a sense of personal identity or attachment.
ashtavakra_gita::50.simple_insight: It’s okay to feel separate even when you know you are connected; that tension is natural.
ashtavakra_gita::50.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra reveals to King Janaka that even the enlightened sage who perceives the true self in all beings and all beings within the true self still experiences a sense of 'me-ness' or attachment. This paradox highlights the complexity of inner realization and human experience.
ashtavakra_gita::50.modern_relevance: You might deeply understand your shared humanity and connection but still feel a strong personal identity or ego that surprises you.
ashtavakra_gita::50.insight: It teaches you to hold the paradox of knowing unity while experiencing individuality without conflict or judgment.

ashtavakra_gita::51.verse_sanskrit:
आस्थितः परमाद्वैतं मोक्षार्थेऽपि व्यवस्थितः ।
आश्चर्यं कामवशगो विकलः केलिशिक्षया ॥
ashtavakra_gita::51.verse_hindi: परम अद्वैत में स्थित हुआ और मोक्ष के लिए भी उद्यत हुआ पुरुष काम के वश होकर क्रीड़ा के अभ्यास से व्याकुल होता है । यही आश्चर्य है।
ashtavakra_gita::51.english_translation: One established in supreme non-duality and striving for freedom yet becomes disturbed by desires through playful habits; this is surprising.
ashtavakra_gita::51.translation_literal: आस्थितः (established) / परमाद्वैतं (supreme non-duality) / मोक्षार्थेऽपि (even for freedom) / व्यवस्थितः (striving) / आश्चर्यं (surprising) / कामवशगो (under desire's control) / विकलः (disturbed) / केलिशिक्षया (by playful practice)
ashtavakra_gita::51.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::51.essence: Knowing freedom doesn’t stop desire’s playful disturbances from affecting you.
ashtavakra_gita::51.simple_meaning: A person may be deeply established in the understanding of oneness and still seek freedom, yet old desires disturb them through habitual play.
ashtavakra_gita::51.simple_insight: You can know the truth but still feel pulled by desires you thought you left behind.
ashtavakra_gita::51.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra points out that even someone firmly rooted in the highest non-dual wisdom and dedicated to liberation can remain unsettled by desires arising from habitual tendencies, showing the subtle power of deep-rooted patterns.
ashtavakra_gita::51.modern_relevance: You might have clarity about your goals and values, yet find yourself distracted by old habits or cravings that disrupt your focus and peace.
ashtavakra_gita::51.insight: Recognize that intellectual understanding alone doesn't dissolve desire; habitual patterns can still disturb the mind.

ashtavakra_gita::52.verse_hindi: काम को उद्भूत ज्ञान का शत्रु जानकर भी अति दुर्बल और अन्तकाल को प्राप्त हुआ पुरुष काम भोग की इच्छा करता है । यही आश्चर्य है।
ashtavakra_gita::52.english_translation: Even knowing desire is the enemy of arising knowledge, the very weak man, nearing death, still longs to satisfy desire. This is truly astonishing.
ashtavakra_gita::52.translation_literal: उद्भूतं (arisen) / ज्ञानदुर्मित्रम् (enemy of knowledge) / अवधार्य (knowing) / अति (very) / दुर्बलः (weak) / आश्चर्यम् (wonder, astonishment) / कामम् (desire) / आकाङ्क्षेत् (wants, longs) / कालम् अन्तम् (end of time, death) / अनुश्रितः (dependent on, nearing)
ashtavakra_gita::52.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::52.essence: Knowing desire harms wisdom doesn’t stop the weak from craving it, even near death.
ashtavakra_gita::52.simple_meaning: Even when a person knows desire harms true understanding and is weak, they still want to satisfy desire near death. This is surprising.
ashtavakra_gita::52.simple_insight: There is a deep human struggle to let go of desire, even when it harms us most.
ashtavakra_gita::52.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra points out the paradox of human weakness: a person aware that desire opposes knowledge still clings to craving, even when death is near, showing how powerful desire is.
ashtavakra_gita::52.modern_relevance: You might recognize this in moments when you know a habit or craving hurts you deeply, yet you keep returning to it despite that awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::52.insight: It teaches you to notice how strong desire’s hold can be, even against your best understanding, inviting honest self-awareness.

ashtavakra_gita::53.verse_sanskrit:
इहामुत्र विरक्तस्य नित्यानित्यविवेकिनः ।
आश्चर्यं मोक्षकामस्य मोक्षाद् एव विभीषिका ॥
ashtavakra_gita::53.verse_hindi: जो इहलोक और परलोक के भोग से विरक्त है और जो नित्य और अनित्य का विवेक रखता है वह भी मोक्ष से भय करता है । यही आश्चर्य है।
ashtavakra_gita::53.english_translation: One who is detached from worldly and otherworldly enjoyments and discerns the eternal from the transient still fears freedom; this is surprising.
ashtavakra_gita::53.translation_literal: इहामुत्र (here and beyond) / विरक्तस्य (of the detached) / नित्य-अनित्य-विवेकिनः (one who discerns eternal and non-eternal) / आश्चर्यं (wonder) / मोक्षकामस्य (of one desiring freedom) / मोक्षाद् (from freedom) / एव (indeed) / विभीषिका (fear)
ashtavakra_gita::53.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::53.essence: Even clear detachment and desire for freedom can hide a subtle fear of freedom itself.
ashtavakra_gita::53.simple_meaning: Even when you let go of desires for this life and the next and see what is permanent and what is not, you can still be afraid of true freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::53.simple_insight: It feels strange but normal to fear the very freedom you seek.
ashtavakra_gita::53.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that even a person who has renounced all pleasures and understands the difference between what lasts and what doesn’t can still be afraid of the freedom they want. This shows how deep and subtle the mind’s conditioning is.
ashtavakra_gita::53.modern_relevance: You’ve worked hard to detach from old habits and understand your true self, yet fear still lingers when facing real change.
ashtavakra_gita::53.insight: It teaches you to recognize that fear can remain even after intellectual understanding and detachment, requiring deeper inner work.

ashtavakra_gita::54.verse_sanskrit:
धीरस्तु भोज्यमानोऽपि पीड्यमानोऽपि सर्वदा ।
आत्मानं केवलं पश्यन् न तुष्यति न कुप्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::54.verse_hindi: धीर पुरुष तो भोगता हुआ भी और पीड़ित होता हुआ भी नित्य केवल आत्मा को देखता हुआ न प्रसन्न होता है, न क्रुद्ध होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::54.english_translation: A steady person, whether enjoying or suffering, always sees only the true self and is neither pleased nor angry.
ashtavakra_gita::54.translation_literal: धीरस्तु (steadfast) भोज्यमानोऽपि (while enjoying) पीड्यमानोऽपि (while suffering) सर्वदा (always) आत्मानं (the true self) केवलं (only) पश्यन् (seeing) न (not) तुष्यति (is pleased) न (nor) कुप्यति (is angry)
ashtavakra_gita::54.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::54.essence: Steady awareness of the true self frees you from emotional swings of pleasure and pain.
ashtavakra_gita::54.simple_meaning: You remain steady and calm whether you enjoy or suffer, because you see only your true self and do not react with pleasure or anger.
ashtavakra_gita::54.simple_insight: You can find calm by focusing on your true self, not on passing feelings.
ashtavakra_gita::54.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a steady person experiences both pleasure and pain but remains unaffected emotionally by seeing only the true self within, beyond external conditions.
ashtavakra_gita::54.modern_relevance: You face constant ups and downs, yet when you focus on who you truly are, emotional storms cannot shake you.
ashtavakra_gita::54.insight: It teaches you to observe your experiences without letting pleasure or pain disturb your inner balance.

ashtavakra_gita::55.verse_sanskrit:
चेष्टमानं शरीरं स्वं पश्यत्यन्यशरीरवत् ।
संस्तवे चापि निन्दायां कथं क्षुभ्येत् महाशयः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::55.verse_hindi: जो अपने चेष्टारत शरीर को दूसरे के शरीर की भाँति देखता है, वह महाशय पुरुष स्तुति और निन्दा में भी कैसे क्षोभ को प्राप्त हो सकता है।
ashtavakra_gita::55.english_translation: One who sees their active body as someone else's body cannot be disturbed by praise or blame.
ashtavakra_gita::55.translation_literal: चेष्टमानं (acting) शरीरं (body) स्वं (own) पश्यति (sees) अन्यशरीरवत् (as another's body) । संस्तवे (in praise) च (and) अपि (also) निन्दायां (in blame) कथं (how) क्षुभ्येत् (would be disturbed) महाशयः (great person) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::55.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::55.essence: Seeing your active body as not truly yours frees you from disturbance by praise or blame.
ashtavakra_gita::55.simple_meaning: If you view your active body as if it belonged to someone else, praise and blame cannot shake you.
ashtavakra_gita::55.simple_insight: You feel peaceful knowing your true self is beyond bodily actions and their judgments.
ashtavakra_gita::55.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the body acts on its own, and when a great person sees it as separate from their true self, they remain calm and unaffected by others’ praise or blame.
ashtavakra_gita::55.modern_relevance: You face criticism or compliments at work, yet when you don't identify completely with your actions, their impact on your mood lessens.
ashtavakra_gita::55.insight: This verse shifts your perspective from identifying with bodily actions to observing them as separate, reducing emotional reactivity.

ashtavakra_gita::56.verse_sanskrit:
मायामात्रमिदं विश्वं पश्यन् विगतकौतुकः ।
अपि सन्निहिते मृत्यौ कथं त्रस्यति धीरधीः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::56.verse_hindi: जो इस विश्व को मायामात्र देखता है, और जो आश्चर्य को पार कर गया है, वह धीर पुरुष मृत्यु के आने पर भी क्यों भयभीत होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::56.english_translation: One who sees this world as mere illusion and has surpassed all wonder, why would such a steady person fear death when it arrives?
ashtavakra_gita::56.translation_literal: मायामात्रम् (mere illusion) / इदं (this) / विश्वं (world) / पश्यन् (seeing) / विगतकौतुकः (having lost wonder) / अपि (even) / सन्निहिते (when present) / मृत्यौ (in death) / कथं (how) / त्रस्यति (fears) / धीरधीः (steady person)
ashtavakra_gita::56.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::56.essence: Seeing the world as illusion removes fear even of death itself.
ashtavakra_gita::56.simple_meaning: If you truly see the world as just an illusion and have moved beyond surprise, then even when death comes close, you remain unshaken and fearless.
ashtavakra_gita::56.simple_insight: There is calm and courage in realizing the world is not ultimately real.
ashtavakra_gita::56.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to the nature of reality and fear. He says that if someone sees the world as nothing but illusion and is no longer caught in amazement or confusion, then facing death does not cause fear. This teaching encourages a deep shift in perspective rooted in wisdom.
ashtavakra_gita::56.modern_relevance: When you face the uncertainty of loss or endings, remembering that appearances are not absolute can help you stay grounded and calm.
ashtavakra_gita::56.insight: It teaches you to steady your mind by recognizing the temporary nature of all things, including death.

ashtavakra_gita::57.verse_sanskrit:
निःस्पृहं मानसं यस्य नैराश्येऽपि महात्मनः ।
तस्यात्मज्ञानतृप्तस्य तुलना केन जायते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::57.verse_hindi: जिस महात्मा का मन नैराश्य में भी स्पृहा नहीं रखता, उस आत्मज्ञान से तृप्त पुरुष की तुलना किससे की जाए।
ashtavakra_gita::57.english_translation: Whose mind is desireless even in despair, who is fulfilled by self-knowledge—how can anyone be compared to such a great being?
ashtavakra_gita::57.translation_literal: निःस्पृहं (without desire) / मानसं (mind's) / यस्य (whose) / नैराश्येऽपि (even in despair) / महात्मनः (of the great soul) । / तस्यात्मज्ञानतृप्तस्य (of that self-knowledge-fulfilled) / तुलना (comparison) / केन (by whom) / जायते (is made) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::57.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::57.essence: True greatness is being desireless and fulfilled within, even in despair.
ashtavakra_gita::57.simple_meaning: A truly great being has a mind free of desire even in despair and is completely satisfied by knowing their true self.
ashtavakra_gita::57.simple_insight: There is a profound peace when your inner being alone satisfies you, no matter how hard life feels.
ashtavakra_gita::57.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra praises the great soul whose mind holds no desires even amid despair, fulfilled fully by self-knowledge. This verse highlights the rare peace that comes from deep inner realization, beyond external circumstances.
ashtavakra_gita::57.modern_relevance: When everything feels lost and your mind craves relief, discovering fulfillment within yourself can steady you completely.
ashtavakra_gita::57.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing fleeting hopes to resting in unshakable self-awareness, even amid hardship.

ashtavakra_gita::58.verse_sanskrit:
स्वभावाद् एव जानानो दृश्यमेतन्न किञ्चन ।
इदं ग्राह्यमिदं त्याज्यं स किं पश्यति धीरधीः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::58.verse_hindi: जो जानता है कि यह दृश्य स्वभाव से ही कुछ नहीं है, वह धीर बुद्धि कैसे देख सकता है कि यह ग्रहण करने योग्य है और यह त्यागने योग्य।
ashtavakra_gita::58.english_translation: The wise know that this appearance is nothing by nature; how can they then see it as something to accept or reject?
ashtavakra_gita::58.translation_literal: स्वभावाद् (by nature) / एव (indeed) / जानानो (knowing) / दृश्यमेतन्न (this visible/appearance) / किञ्चन (anything) / इदं (this) / ग्राह्यम् (to be taken) / इदं (this) / त्याज्यं (to be rejected) / स (he) / किं (how) / पश्यति (sees) / धीरधीः (wise one)
ashtavakra_gita::58.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::58.essence: True wisdom sees that nothing appearing is truly graspable or avoidable.
ashtavakra_gita::58.simple_meaning: The wise understand that what appears to you is not truly real, so it cannot be properly accepted or rejected.
ashtavakra_gita::58.simple_insight: There is peace in seeing that nothing appearing is truly worth clinging to or pushing away.
ashtavakra_gita::58.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the visible world is by nature empty of true substance. A wise person does not treat appearances as real things to grasp or avoid, freeing themselves from reactive attachment or rejection.
ashtavakra_gita::58.modern_relevance: You scroll endlessly through fleeting images and opinions, realizing none fully define you or deserve your full embrace or rejection.
ashtavakra_gita::58.insight: It shifts your mind from reacting to appearances toward seeing them as empty and neutral phenomena.

ashtavakra_gita::59.verse_sanskrit:
अन्तस्त्यक्तकषायस्य निर्द्वन्द्वस्य निराशिषः ।
यदृच्छयागतो भोगो न दुःखाय न तुष्टये ॥
ashtavakra_gita::59.verse_hindi: जिसने अन्तःकरण के कषाय को त्याग दिया है, और जो द्वन्द्वरहित और आशारहित है । ऐसे पुरुष को दैवयोग से प्राप्त भोगों में न दुःख है, न सुख।
ashtavakra_gita::59.english_translation: One who has abandoned inner attachments, is free from duality and desire; whatever pleasures come by chance bring neither pain nor joy.
ashtavakra_gita::59.translation_literal: अन्तस्त्यक्तकषायस्य (inner-attached-abandoned) / निर्द्वन्द्वस्य (without-duality) / निराशिषः (without-desire) / यदृच्छयागतो (by-chance-come) / भोगो (pleasure) / न (not) / दुःखाय (for-pain) / न (not) / तुष्टये (for-joy)
ashtavakra_gita::59.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::59.essence: Without inner craving, chance pleasures bring neither suffering nor delight.
ashtavakra_gita::59.simple_meaning: If you release all inner attachments and desires, then random pleasures won't cause you happiness or suffering.
ashtavakra_gita::59.simple_insight: There is freedom in experiencing life without clinging to any feeling or outcome.
ashtavakra_gita::59.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that when a person abandons all inner cravings and dual feelings, they remain unaffected by whatever pleasures life randomly offers. This frees them from emotional highs and lows.
ashtavakra_gita::59.modern_relevance: You scroll social media and see moments of joy or envy arise suddenly, but your calm comes from not clinging to any feeling.
ashtavakra_gita::59.insight: It shifts your focus from craving experiences to steady inner freedom beyond ups and downs.

ashtavakra_gita::60.verse_sanskrit:
हन्तात्मज्ञानस्य धीरस्य खेलतो भोगलीलया ।
न हि संसारवाहीकैर्मूढैः सह समानता ॥
ashtavakra_gita::60.verse_hindi: भोग-विलास के साथ खेलते हुए आत्मज्ञानी धीर पुरुष की बराबरी संसार को सिर पर ढोने वाले मूढ़ पुरुषों के साथ कैसे की जा सकती है।
ashtavakra_gita::60.english_translation: How can the steady knower of the self, who plays with enjoyment as a sport, be compared to the fools burdened by the world?
ashtavakra_gita::60.translation_literal: हन्त (how) / आत्मज्ञानस्य (of self-knowledge) / धीरस्य (of the steady) / खेलतो (playing) / भोगलीलया (with enjoyment as sport) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / संसारवाहीकैः (those who carry the world) / मूढैः (fools) / सह (with) / समानता (equality/comparison)
ashtavakra_gita::60.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::60.essence: True self-knowledge lets you play freely while others are trapped by their burdens.
ashtavakra_gita::60.simple_meaning: A person who knows their true self lives with calm joy, unlike those blindly burdened by worldly struggles.
ashtavakra_gita::60.simple_insight: There is freedom and lightness in knowing yourself that fools carrying the world cannot understand.
ashtavakra_gita::60.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra contrasts the calm, self-aware person who enjoys life’s play with those foolishly weighed down by worldly concerns, showing the difference between inner wisdom and external struggle.
ashtavakra_gita::60.modern_relevance: You watch others anxiously chase results while you find ease and joy in your steady inner knowing.
ashtavakra_gita::60.insight: It shifts your view from being overwhelmed by life’s burdens to embracing a joyful steadiness rooted in self-knowledge.

ashtavakra_gita::61.verse_sanskrit:
यत् पदं प्रेप्सवो दीनाः शक्राद्याः सर्वदेवताः ।
अहो तत्र स्थितो योगी न हर्षमुपगच्छति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::61.verse_hindi: जिस पद की इच्छा करते हुए इन्द्रादि सम्पूर्ण देवता दीन हो रहे हैं, उस पर स्थित हुआ भी योगी हर्ष को प्राप्त नहीं होता । यही आश्चर्य है ।
ashtavakra_gita::61.english_translation: The place desired by even the great deities like Indra leaves the yogi there without joy; this is the wonder.
ashtavakra_gita::61.translation_literal: यत् (that) / पदं (place) / प्रेप्सवः (desiring) / दीनाः (humble/poor) / शक्राद्याः (like Indra) / सर्वदेवताः (all deities) / aho (ah! / behold) / तत्र (there) / स्थितः (situated) / योगी (the yogi) / न (not) / हर्षम् (joy) / उपगच्छति (attains)
ashtavakra_gita::61.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::61.essence: You can be where others yearn to be and still find no joy inside.
ashtavakra_gita::61.simple_meaning: Even the highest beings long for certain places, but a yogi resting there may still feel no happiness.
ashtavakra_gita::61.simple_insight: Finding what you desire doesn’t guarantee the joy you expect.
ashtavakra_gita::61.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Ashtavakra describes how even the powerful deities like Indra long for a certain state or place. Yet, when the yogi attains that same place, they do not experience joy. It highlights that true contentment is not tied to external attainment.
ashtavakra_gita::61.modern_relevance: You might reach a milestone or a dream job everyone admires, but still feel empty or unsatisfied inside.
ashtavakra_gita::61.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing desires to recognizing that joy is independent of external achievements.

ashtavakra_gita::62.verse_sanskrit:
तज्ज्ञस्य पुण्यपापाभ्यां स्पर्शो ह्यन्तर्न जायते ।
न ह्याकाशस्य धूमेन दृश्यमानापि सङ्गतिः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::62.verse_hindi: उस पद को जानने वाले के अन्तःकरण का स्पर्श वैसे ही पुण्य और पाप के साथ नहीं होता जैसे आकाश का सम्बन्ध भासता हुआ भी धुएँ के साथ नहीं होता।
ashtavakra_gita::62.english_translation: The one who knows that state does not have contact of virtue and sin in their inner being, just as space appears untouched by smoke.
ashtavakra_gita::62.translation_literal: तज्ज्ञस्य (of the knower of that) पुण्यपापाभ्यां (with virtue and sin) स्पर्शो (contact) हि (indeed) अन्तरन् (in the inner being) जायते (arises) । न (not) हि (indeed) आकाशस्य (of space) धूमेन (by smoke) दृश्यमानापि (even visible) सङ्गतिः (connection) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::62.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::62.essence: The true self is untouched by moral dualities, like space is untouched by smoke.
ashtavakra_gita::62.simple_meaning: Knowing your true self means your inner being is not affected by good or bad, just like space is not affected by smoke.
ashtavakra_gita::62.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing your true self is untouched by any moral impressions.
ashtavakra_gita::62.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains to King Janaka that a person who truly knows their real nature experiences no inner taint from virtue or sin, just as space remains unaffected by smoke, showing the pure self is beyond moral dualities.
ashtavakra_gita::62.modern_relevance: When harsh judgments or praise come your way, you can remember your inner self remains untouched, like clear space beyond passing clouds of smoke.
ashtavakra_gita::62.insight: It teaches you to recognize your inner being as inherently pure and unaffected by external moral labels.

ashtavakra_gita::63.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मैवेदं जगत्सर्वं ज्ञातं येन महात्मना ।
यदृच्छया वर्तमानं तं निषेद्धुं क्षमेत कः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::63.verse_hindi: जिस महात्मा ने इस सम्पूर्ण जगत को आत्मा की तरह जान लिया है, उस ज्ञानी को अपनी इच्छा के अनुसार व्यवहार करने से कौन रोक सकता है।
ashtavakra_gita::63.english_translation: Who can prevent the great soul who knows the entire world as the true self from acting according to their own will?
ashtavakra_gita::63.translation_literal: आत्मैवेदं (true self indeed) जगत्सर्वं (entire world) ज्ञातं (known) येन (by whom) महात्मना (great soul) । यदृच्छया (by own will) वर्तमानं (acting) तं (that one) निषेद्धुं (to forbid) क्षमेत (can) कः (who) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::63.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::63.essence: Knowing the world as yourself grants unstoppable freedom to act by your own will.
ashtavakra_gita::63.simple_meaning: A person who truly understands that everything is their own true self cannot be stopped from acting as they wish.
ashtavakra_gita::63.simple_insight: Knowing your unity with all brings a deep sense of freedom to act without hindrance.
ashtavakra_gita::63.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that when someone realizes the entire world is no different from their true self, that person is a great soul. Such a one moves freely and cannot be restrained by others because their actions arise naturally from this understanding.
ashtavakra_gita::63.modern_relevance: You feel the pressure of others trying to control your choices, but when you truly know yourself, that control loses its power.
ashtavakra_gita::63.insight: It shifts your mind from feeling restricted by external forces to embracing your intrinsic freedom to act.

ashtavakra_gita::64.verse_sanskrit:
आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्ते भूतग्रामे चतुर्विधे ।
विज्ञस्यैव हि सामर्थ्यमिच्छानिच्छाविवर्जने ॥
ashtavakra_gita::64.verse_hindi: ब्रह्मा से चींटी पर्यन्त चार प्रकार के जीवों के समूह में ज्ञानी को ही इच्छा और अनिच्छा को रोकने की सामर्थ्य है।
ashtavakra_gita::64.english_translation: Among all groups of beings from Brahma to ants, only the wise have the power to overcome desire and aversion.
ashtavakra_gita::64.translation_literal: आब्रह्म (from Brahma) / स्तम्बपर्यन्ते (up to the ant) / भूतग्रामे (groups of beings) / चतुर्विधे (four types) / विज्ञस्यैव (only the wise) / हि (indeed) / सामर्थ्यम् (power) / इच्छानि (desires) / अनिच्छाविवर्जने (in overcoming aversion)
ashtavakra_gita::64.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::64.essence: Only the wise possess true power to transcend desire and aversion among all beings.
ashtavakra_gita::64.simple_meaning: Among all living beings, only those with wisdom can control their wants and dislikes.
ashtavakra_gita::64.simple_insight: You can feel empowered knowing your true strength lies in mastering desire and aversion.
ashtavakra_gita::64.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra points out that from the greatest beings like Brahma to the smallest like ants, only the wise have the ability to overcome craving and avoidance. This teaching highlights wisdom as the unique power to rise above reactive impulses.
ashtavakra_gita::64.modern_relevance: When emotions pull you between craving and rejection, remember that wisdom gives you the power to remain steady and free.
ashtavakra_gita::64.insight: It teaches you to recognize wisdom as the capacity that stops the mind’s swinging between wanting and rejecting.

ashtavakra_gita::65.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मानमद्वयं कश्चिज्जानाति जगदीश्वरम् ।
यद् वेत्ति तत्स कुरुते न भयं तस्य कुत्रचित् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::65.verse_hindi: कोई विरला ही आत्मा को अद्वय और जगदीश्वर रूप में जानता है। वह जिसे करने योग्य मानता है उसे करता है । उसे किसी प्रकार का भय नहीं।
ashtavakra_gita::65.english_translation: Very few truly know the true self as non-dual and as the supreme lord of the universe. Whoever knows this acts accordingly and fears nothing anywhere.
ashtavakra_gita::65.translation_literal: आत्मानम् (self) अद्वयं (non-dual) कश्चि (someone) जानाति (knows) जगदीश्वरम् (supreme lord of the universe) यद् (that which) वेत्ति (knows) तत् (that) कुरुते (does) न (not) भयं (fear) तस्य (his) कुत्रचित् (anywhere)
ashtavakra_gita::65.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::65.essence: Knowing your true self as undivided power removes all fear and doubt.
ashtavakra_gita::65.simple_meaning: Only a rare person truly knows the self as unified and supreme. Such a person acts rightly and feels no fear anywhere.
ashtavakra_gita::65.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing who you truly are beyond all duality and fear.
ashtavakra_gita::65.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that very few realize the self as both non-dual and the supreme presence behind the world. This deep knowing empowers one to act without fear anywhere, because fear comes from ignorance of this truth.
ashtavakra_gita::65.modern_relevance: When you deeply understand your true nature, you can face any challenge with calm courage and act without hesitation.
ashtavakra_gita::65.insight: This verse invites you to root your actions in the fearless certainty of your true self rather than in shifting appearances.

ashtavakra_gita::66.verse_sanskrit:
न ते सङ्गोऽस्ति केनापि किं शुद्धस्त्यक्तुमिच्छसि ।
सङ्घातविलयं कुर्वन्नेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥
ashtavakra_gita::66.verse_hindi: तेरा किसी से भी संग नहीं है, इसलिए तू शुद्ध है, फिर किसको त्यागना चाहता है। इस प्रकार देहभमान के त्याग की इच्छा करके लय को प्राप्त हो।
ashtavakra_gita::66.english_translation: You have no attachment to anything, so you are already pure; whom do you wish to renounce? By abandoning the false sense of the body, you attain dissolution.
ashtavakra_gita::66.translation_literal: न (not) ते (your) सङ्गः (attachment) अस्ति (exists) केनापि (to anyone) किं (anything) शुद्धः (pure) त्यक्तुम् (to abandon) इच्छसि (you desire) । सङ्घातविलयं (dissolution of the aggregates) कुर्वन् (doing) एवमेव (in this way) लयं (absorption) व्रज (go) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::66.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::66.essence: Purity is your natural state because you have no real attachments to renounce.
ashtavakra_gita::66.simple_meaning: You have no real attachments, so you are already pure; wanting to renounce the body-mind is the way to dissolve false identity.
ashtavakra_gita::66.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing purity is your natural state, not something to achieve by giving up things.
ashtavakra_gita::66.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that because you have no true attachment, you are already pure. The desire to renounce the body and its false identity leads to dissolving the illusion of separation and realizing true self.
ashtavakra_gita::66.modern_relevance: You may feel pressure to give up habits or identities to be 'better,' but this reminds you that your essence was never polluted to begin with.
ashtavakra_gita::66.insight: It shifts your mindset from trying to discard attachments to recognizing your innate freedom beyond all clinging.

ashtavakra_gita::67.verse_sanskrit:
उदेति भवतो विश्वं वारिधेरिव बुद्बुदः ।
इति ज्ञात्वैकमात्मानमेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥
ashtavakra_gita::67.verse_hindi: तुझसे संसार उत्पन्न होता है, जैसे समुद्र से बुलबुला। इस प्रकार आत्मा को एक जानकर मोक्ष को प्राप्त हो।
ashtavakra_gita::67.english_translation: The entire world arises from you like bubbles from the ocean; knowing this, the true self alone attains liberation.
ashtavakra_gita::67.translation_literal: उदेति (arises) भवतो (from you) विश्वं (the world) वारिधेरिव (like ocean) बुद्बुदः (bubbles) । इति (thus) ज्ञात्वा (knowing) एकम् (one) आत्मानम् (self) एव (alone) एव (indeed) लयं (liberation) व्रज (attains) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::67.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::67.essence: The true self is the source of all and alone attains freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::67.simple_meaning: Everything in the world comes from you like bubbles come from the ocean. Realizing this, the true self alone is free.
ashtavakra_gita::67.simple_insight: You can feel the relief of knowing your true self is beyond all appearances.
ashtavakra_gita::67.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains to King Janaka that the entire world arises from the true self just as bubbles arise from the ocean. Recognizing this truth leads to liberation, showing the self is the source and the final freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::67.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by chaos, imagine the world arising from your own being. Knowing your true self is untouched brings calm and freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::67.insight: It teaches you to see yourself as the source of all experience and recognize your freedom beyond appearances.

ashtavakra_gita::68.verse_sanskrit:
प्रत्यक्षमप्यवस्तुत्वाद् विश्वं नास्त्यमले त्वयि ।
रज्जुसर्प इव व्यक्तमेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥
ashtavakra_gita::68.verse_hindi: दृश्यमान जगत प्रत्यक्ष होता हुआ भी रज्जु सर्प की भाँति तुझ शुद्ध के लिए नहीं है। इसलिए तू मोक्ष को प्राप्त हो।
ashtavakra_gita::68.english_translation: The visible world, though appearing real, is like a snake made of rope and is not real for your pure self; therefore, attain freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::68.translation_literal: प्रत्यक्षम् (visible) अपि (even) अवस्तुत्वात् (due to unreality) विश्वं (the world) नास्ति (is not) अमले (for the pure) त्वयि (in you) । रज्जु (rope) सर्प (snake) इव (like) व्यक्तम् (appearing) एव (indeed) एव (certainly) लयं (dissolution) व्रज (goes) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::68.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::68.essence: What appears real is illusion to your pure self; freedom lies beyond appearances.
ashtavakra_gita::68.simple_meaning: The world you see looks real but is like a rope mistaken for a snake; it is not real for your pure self.
ashtavakra_gita::68.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing that the world’s fears and illusions don’t truly bind your inner being.
ashtavakra_gita::68.detailed_meaning: King Janaka is taught by Ashtavakra that the visible world appears real but is like mistaking a rope for a snake. This illusion does not affect the pure self, which is beyond appearance, leading to the call for liberation.
ashtavakra_gita::68.modern_relevance: You panic over imagined threats in your day—like worrying all night over a problem that doesn’t truly exist.
ashtavakra_gita::68.insight: It teaches you to see appearances as illusions and not let imagined fears bind your true self.

ashtavakra_gita::69.verse_sanskrit:
समदुःखसुखः पूर्ण आशानैराश्ययोः समः ।
समजीवितमृत्युः सन्नेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥
ashtavakra_gita::69.verse_hindi: दुःख और सुख जिसके लिए समान है, जो पूर्ण है, जो आशा और निराशा में समान है, जीवन और मृत्यु में समान है। ऐसा होकर तू मोक्ष को प्राप्त हो।
ashtavakra_gita::69.english_translation: One who is equal to pain and pleasure, complete, equal in hope and despair, equal in life and death, attains freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::69.translation_literal: समदुःखसुखः (equal to pain and pleasure) / पूर्ण (complete) / आशानैः (in hopes) / ऐराश्ययोः (and in despairs) / समः (equal) / समजीवितमृत्युः (equal in life and death) / सन्नेवमेव (thus indeed) / लयं (freedom) / व्रज (attain).
ashtavakra_gita::69.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::69.essence: Freedom comes from treating all extremes as equal and staying steady within.
ashtavakra_gita::69.simple_meaning: Being equally steady in pain and pleasure, hope and despair, life and death leads to true freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::69.simple_insight: You feel calm knowing nothing can disturb your inner balance.
ashtavakra_gita::69.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that true freedom comes from equal acceptance of all life's ups and downs—pleasure or pain, hope or despair, life or death. This steady heart is the key to liberation.
ashtavakra_gita::69.modern_relevance: When a sudden failure or success hits you, your peace depends on staying steady, not getting swept away by emotion.
ashtavakra_gita::69.insight: It teaches you to hold your emotional balance regardless of external changes or outcomes.

ashtavakra_gita::70.verse_sanskrit:
आकाशवदनन्तोऽहं घटवत् प्राकृतं जगत् ।
इति ज्ञानं तथैतस्य न त्यागो न ग्रहो लयः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::70.verse_hindi: मैं आकाश की भाँति अनन्त हूँ । यह संसार घड़े की भाँति प्रकृतिजन्य है, ऐसा ज्ञान है । इसलिए न इसका त्याग है, न ग्रहण और न लय है।
ashtavakra_gita::70.english_translation: I am infinite like space; the world is natural like a pot. This knowledge means there is no renunciation, acceptance, or dissolution of it.
ashtavakra_gita::70.translation_literal: आकाशवदनन्तोऽहं (I am infinite like space) / घटवत् (like a pot) / प्राकृतं (natural) / जगत् (world) / । (.) / इति (thus) / ज्ञानं (knowledge) / तथैतस्य (of that) / न (not) / त्यागो (renunciation) / न (not) / ग्रहो (acceptance) / लयः (dissolution) / ॥ (.)
ashtavakra_gita::70.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::70.essence: You are infinite like space, untouched by the natural world's forms or changes.
ashtavakra_gita::70.simple_meaning: You are infinite like space and unchanged by the natural world, which is like a pot. This means you neither reject nor cling to it, nor do you merge with it.
ashtavakra_gita::70.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing you are beyond the changing world, untouched and infinite.
ashtavakra_gita::70.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the true self is limitless like space, while the world is a natural, transient form like a pot. This insight dissolves the need to reject or accept the world or to seek merging with it.
ashtavakra_gita::70.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by change, remember your true self is vast and unchanged, beyond the natural ups and downs.
ashtavakra_gita::70.insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with the world to recognizing your infinite nature beyond appearances.

ashtavakra_gita::71.verse_sanskrit:
महोदधिरिवाहं स प्रपञ्चो वीचिसऽन्निभः ।
इति ज्ञानं तथैतस्य न त्यागो न ग्रहो लयः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::71.verse_hindi: मैं समुद्र के समान हूँ, यह संसार तरंगों के समान है, ऐसा ज्ञान है । इसलिए न इसका त्याग है, न ग्रहण और न इसका लय है।
ashtavakra_gita::71.english_translation: I am like the great ocean; this world is like its waves. Such knowledge means there is no rejection, acceptance, or dissolution of it.
ashtavakra_gita::71.translation_literal: महोदधि (great ocean) इव (like) अहं (I) स (that) प्रपञ्चः (world) वीचिस् (waves) अन्निभः (similar) । इति (thus) ज्ञानं (knowledge) तथैव (such) तस्य (of that) न (not) त्यागः (rejection) न (not) ग्रहो (acceptance) लयः (dissolution) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::71.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::71.essence: Your true self remains steady and untouched despite the world's constant changes.
ashtavakra_gita::71.simple_meaning: You are like the vast ocean and the world is like the waves on it. Knowing this means you neither reject nor cling to the world, and you don’t disappear into it.
ashtavakra_gita::71.simple_insight: You can feel steady and whole even as everything around you changes.
ashtavakra_gita::71.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra compares the self to the vast ocean and the world to its waves. Waves rise and fall but the ocean remains undisturbed. This moment teaches that true knowledge is seeing that the self is untouched by worldly changes, neither rejecting nor absorbing them.
ashtavakra_gita::71.modern_relevance: When life tosses you between ups and downs, you can stay grounded by remembering your deeper steady nature beneath the shifting events.
ashtavakra_gita::71.insight: It teaches you to see yourself as stable and vast, not shaped by passing events or emotions.

ashtavakra_gita::72.verse_sanskrit:
अहं स शुक्तिसङ्काशो रूप्यवद् विश्वकल्पना ।
इति ज्ञानं तथैतस्य न त्यागो न ग्रहो लयः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::72.verse_hindi: मैं सीपी के समान हूँ, विश्व की कल्पना चाँदी के समान है । ऐसा ज्ञान है । अतएव इसका न त्याग है, न ग्रहण है और न लय है।
ashtavakra_gita::72.english_translation: I am like a polished shell, the world's appearance is like silver; such knowledge neither accepts, rejects, nor dissolves.
ashtavakra_gita::72.translation_literal: अहं (I) स (am) शुक्तिसङ्काशो (polished shell-like) रूप्यवद् (like silver) विश्वकल्पना (world's imagination/appearance) । (.) इति (thus) ज्ञानं (knowledge) तथै (such) एतस्य (of this) न (not) त्यागो (rejection) न (not) ग्रहो (acceptance) लयः (dissolution) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::72.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::72.essence: You remain unchanged while the world’s shining appearance neither binds nor alters you.
ashtavakra_gita::72.simple_meaning: You are like a polished shell, solid and unchanged; the world around you is like silver, a shining appearance. This knowledge neither accepts, rejects, nor dissolves the world.
ashtavakra_gita::72.simple_insight: You can feel steady and untouched even as the world appears and changes around you.
ashtavakra_gita::72.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra compares the self to a polished shell—solid, unaffected—and the world to silver—a shining but unreal appearance. He teaches that true knowledge means not clinging to or rejecting this appearance, nor merging into it.
ashtavakra_gita::72.modern_relevance: When everything around you gleams with attraction or distraction, you can hold your calm like a steady shell, not swept away by appearances.
ashtavakra_gita::72.insight: It teaches you to see yourself as unaffected by the world's changing appearances, neither grasping nor rejecting them.

ashtavakra_gita::73.verse_sanskrit:
अहं वा सर्वभूतेषु सर्वभूतान्यथो मयि ।
इति ज्ञानं तथैतस्य न त्यागो न ग्रहो लयः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::73.verse_hindi: मैं निश्चित ही सब भूतों में हूँ और ये सब भूत मुझमें हैं । ऐसा ज्ञान है । इसलिए इसका न त्याग है, न ग्रहण है और न लय है।
ashtavakra_gita::73.english_translation: I am indeed in all beings, and all beings are within me. This is true knowledge. Therefore, it has no abandonment, no acceptance, and no destruction.
ashtavakra_gita::73.translation_literal: अहं (I) / वा (indeed) / सर्वभूतेषु (in all beings) / सर्वभूतानि (all beings) / अथा (also) / मयि (in me) / इति (thus) / ज्ञानं (knowledge) / तथैतस्य (such is that) / न (no) / त्यागो (abandonment) / न (no) / ग्रहो (acceptance) / लयः (destruction)
ashtavakra_gita::73.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::73.essence: You and every being are inseparably present within each other beyond gain or loss.
ashtavakra_gita::73.simple_meaning: You are present in every being, and every being exists within you. This deep knowledge is beyond gaining, losing, or giving up.
ashtavakra_gita::73.simple_insight: You can feel a profound unity that cannot be taken or lost, only realized.
ashtavakra_gita::73.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Ashtavakra reveals to Janaka the non-dual truth that the true self is not separate from all beings. This knowledge has no ownership or loss because it is the essential reality that pervades all existence.
ashtavakra_gita::73.modern_relevance: When you feel alone or isolated, remembering that you are connected deeply to everyone can bring calm and belonging.
ashtavakra_gita::73.insight: It shifts your view from separation to unity, removing attachment to identity as isolated and fixed.

ashtavakra_gita::74.verse_sanskrit:
मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्वपोत इतस्ततः ।
भ्रमति स्वान्तवातेन न ममास्त्यसहिष्णुता ॥
ashtavakra_gita::74.verse_hindi: मुझ अन्तहीन महासमुद्र में विश्वरूपी नाव अपनी ही प्रकृत वायु से इधर-उधर डोलती है । मुझे असहिष्णुता नहीं है।
ashtavakra_gita::74.english_translation: In me, the infinite great ocean, the universal boat drifts here and there by its own natural wind; I have no intolerance.
ashtavakra_gita::74.translation_literal: मयि (in me) अनन्त (infinite) महाम्भोधौ (great ocean) विश्वपोत (universal boat) इतस्ततः (here and there) भ्रमति (drifts) स्वान्तवातेन (by its own natural wind) न (not) मम (my) असहिष्णुता (intolerance) अस्ति (exists)
ashtavakra_gita::74.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::74.essence: Your true self is a vast ocean calmly carried by natural winds, free of resistance.
ashtavakra_gita::74.simple_meaning: Your true self is like an endless ocean where the universal boat floats gently, moved by natural winds, without resistance or intolerance.
ashtavakra_gita::74.simple_insight: Feel the calm acceptance that comes from knowing your true self flows with life without resisting.
ashtavakra_gita::74.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes the true self as an infinite ocean within which the universal boat drifts gently, carried by its own natural winds. This image shows the self’s vastness and unshakable equanimity, untouched by intolerance or resistance.
ashtavakra_gita::74.modern_relevance: You face unexpected changes and pressures, but inside, you can remain vast and calm like an ocean, letting life’s natural flow carry you.
ashtavakra_gita::74.insight: It teaches you to embrace life's natural rhythms without resistance, cultivating deep equanimity.

ashtavakra_gita::75.verse_sanskrit:
मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ जगद्वीचिः स्वभावतः ।
उदेतु वास्तमायातु न मे वृद्धिर्न च क्षतिः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::75.verse_hindi: मुझ अन्तहीन महासमुद्र में जगतरूपी लहर स्वभाव से उदय हो । मेरी न वृद्धि है, न हानि।
ashtavakra_gita::75.english_translation: In me, the infinite great ocean, the waves of the world arise naturally; I have no increase nor loss.
ashtavakra_gita::75.translation_literal: मयि (in me) अनन्त (infinite) महाम्भोधौ (great ocean) जगत् (world) वीचिः (waves) स्वभावतः (by nature) उदेतु (arise) वास्तु (indeed) आयातु (come) न (not) मे (my) वृद्धिः (increase) न (nor) च (and) क्षतिः (loss)
ashtavakra_gita::75.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::75.essence: Your true self remains unchanged as the world’s waves rise and fall within you.
ashtavakra_gita::75.simple_meaning: You are like an infinite ocean where the world’s waves rise naturally, but you yourself don’t grow or shrink.
ashtavakra_gita::75.simple_insight: You can feel steady and untouched even as everything around you changes.
ashtavakra_gita::75.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that the true self is like an endless ocean where the world’s waves arise naturally. Although the waves appear and vanish, the ocean itself neither gains nor loses anything. This teaches that the self remains unchanged amid constant change.
ashtavakra_gita::75.modern_relevance: When your emotions surge like waves, remember your inner core stays calm and unchanged beneath the surface.
ashtavakra_gita::75.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with passing events to recognizing your unchanging awareness as the base of all experience.

ashtavakra_gita::76.verse_sanskrit:
मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्वं नाम विकल्पना ।
अतिशान्तो निराकार एतदेवाहमास्थितः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::76.verse_hindi: मुझ अन्तहीन महासमुद्र में निश्चय ही संसार कल्पनामात्र है । मैं अत्यन्त शान्त हूँ, निराकार हूँ और इसी अवस्था में स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::76.english_translation: In my infinite great ocean, the entire world is just imagination. I am extremely peaceful, formless, and established in this state.
ashtavakra_gita::76.translation_literal: मयि (in me) अनन्त (infinite) महा-अम्भोधौ (great ocean) विश्वं (world) नाम (by name) विकल्पना (imagination) । अतिशान्तः (extremely peaceful) निराकार (formless) एतदेव (this alone) अहम् (I) अस्थितः (established) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::76.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::76.essence: You are an infinite, formless ocean in which the world appears as mere imagination.
ashtavakra_gita::76.simple_meaning: Everything you see as the world is merely imagination inside your infinite being. You are deeply peaceful and formless, resting in that true state.
ashtavakra_gita::76.simple_insight: There is profound calm in realizing your true self is beyond all appearances and forms.
ashtavakra_gita::76.detailed_meaning: The sage Ashtavakra reveals that what we call the world is just imagination within the infinite inner ocean of awareness. He describes himself as formless and utterly peaceful, established in this timeless state beyond all change.
ashtavakra_gita::76.modern_relevance: When distractions flood your mind, remember your true nature is a vast, calm ocean beyond all thoughts and worries.
ashtavakra_gita::76.insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with fleeting forms to resting as the infinite, peaceful ground behind all experience.

ashtavakra_gita::77.verse_sanskrit:
नात्मा भावेषु नो भावस्तत्रानन्ते निरञ्जने ।
इत्यसक्तोऽस्पृहः शान्त एतदेवाहमास्तितः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::77.verse_hindi: आत्मा विषयों में नहीं है और विषय उस अनन्त निरञ्जन आत्मा में नहीं है । इस प्रकार मैं अनासक्त हूँ, स्पृहामुक्त हूँ, और इसी अवस्था में स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::77.english_translation: The true self is not in objects, nor are objects in the infinite pure self; thus, I am unattached, desireless, and established in this state.
ashtavakra_gita::77.translation_literal: नात्मा (not self) / भावेषु (in objects) / नो (nor) / भावः (object) / तत्र (there) / अनन्ते (in infinite) / निरञ्जने (in pure) / इत्यसक्तः (thus unattached) / अस्पृहः (desireless) / शान्तः (peaceful) / एतदेव (this only) / अहम् (I) / आस्तितः (am established)
ashtavakra_gita::77.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::77.essence: You can be free and desireless because your true self is beyond objects.
ashtavakra_gita::77.simple_meaning: You are not part of objects, nor are objects part of your true self. Being free means no attachment or desire.
ashtavakra_gita::77.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing you are beyond wanting and external things.
ashtavakra_gita::77.detailed_meaning: King Janaka learns from Ashtavakra that his true self is beyond all objects and desires. He is taught to rest in a state free of craving and attachment, recognizing his pure nature.
ashtavakra_gita::77.modern_relevance: You notice your mind chasing things around you, but your true being remains untouched, calm, and free from wanting.
ashtavakra_gita::77.insight: It teaches you to see yourself as separate from external things and to release desire for them.

ashtavakra_gita::78.verse_sanskrit:
अहो चिन्मात्रमेवाहमिन्द्रजालोपमं जगत् ।
इति मम कथं कुत्र हेयोपादेयकल्पना ॥
ashtavakra_gita::78.verse_hindi: अहो ! मैं चैतन्यमात्र हूँ । संसार इन्द्रजाल की भाँति है । तब मेरी हेय और उपादेय की कल्पना किसमें हो।
ashtavakra_gita::78.english_translation: Ah! I am pure consciousness alone. The world is like a magic illusion. How can I imagine anything to be worthy or unworthy?
ashtavakra_gita::78.translation_literal: अहो (Ah) / चिन्मात्रम् (pure consciousness alone) / एव (indeed) / अहम् (I) / इन्द्रजालोपमं (like a magic illusion) / जगत् (world) / इति (thus) / मम (my) / कथं (how) / कुत्र (anywhere) / हेयोपादेयकल्पना (worthy-unworthy imagination) ।
ashtavakra_gita::78.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::78.essence: Your true self is pure awareness; the world’s values are illusions.
ashtavakra_gita::78.simple_meaning: You are nothing but pure awareness. The world is like a magical illusion, so ideas of good or bad don’t truly apply.
ashtavakra_gita::78.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing that judgments about worth come from illusion, not your true self.
ashtavakra_gita::78.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to King Janaka, emphasizing that his true nature is pure consciousness alone. The world appears like a magical illusion, so the usual ideas of what is worthy or unworthy do not touch his real self.
ashtavakra_gita::78.modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed by judging situations or people as good or bad. This reminds you that those judgments come from appearances, not from your true self.
ashtavakra_gita::78.insight: It shifts your mind from valuing external things to resting in your nature as pure awareness beyond judgment.

ashtavakra_gita::79.verse_sanskrit:
तदा बन्धो यदा चित्तं किञ्चिद् वाञ्छति शोचति ।
किञ्चिन् मुञ्चति गृण्हाति किञ्चिद् दृष्यति कुप्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::79.verse_hindi: जब चित्त कुछ चाहता है, कुछ सोचता है, कुछ त्याग करता है, कुछ ग्रहण करता है, जब दुःखी और सुखी होता है – तब बन्ध है।
ashtavakra_gita::79.english_translation: When the mind wants something, thinks, lets go, takes, sees, and gets angry, bondage exists.
ashtavakra_gita::79.translation_literal: तदा (then) बन्धो (bondage) यदा (when) चित्तं (mind) किञ्चिद् (something) वाञ्छति (wants) शोचति (grieves) । किञ्चिन् (something) मुञ्चति (lets go) गृण्हाति (takes) किञ्चिद् (something) दृष्यति (sees) कुप्यति (gets angry) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::79.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::79.essence: Bondage exists wherever the mind desires or reacts emotionally.
ashtavakra_gita::79.simple_meaning: Bondage arises whenever your mind desires, feels sorrow, lets go, takes, sees, or gets angry.
ashtavakra_gita::79.simple_insight: You can feel trapped whenever your mind clings or reacts strongly to experience.
ashtavakra_gita::79.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that bondage is not an external force but arises when the mind wants, grieves, releases, grasps, perceives, and becomes angry. This moment of inner unrest is the root of feeling bound.
ashtavakra_gita::79.modern_relevance: When you catch yourself craving, resenting, or reacting strongly to events, you’re experiencing this inner bondage.
ashtavakra_gita::79.insight: It teaches you to watch how your mind’s desires and reactions create your sense of being trapped.

ashtavakra_gita::80.verse_sanskrit:
तदा मुक्तिर्यदा चित्तं न वाञ्छति न शोचति ।
न मुञ्चति न गृण्हाति न हृष्यति न कुप्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::80.verse_hindi: जब मन न चाह करता है, न सोचता है, न त्यागता है, न ग्रहण करता है, जब यह न सुखी होता है, न दुखी होता है – तभी मुक्त है।
ashtavakra_gita::80.english_translation: Freedom arises when the mind neither desires, grieves, lets go, nor clings, neither rejoices nor angers.
ashtavakra_gita::80.translation_literal: तदा (then) मुक्तिः (freedom) यदा (when) चित्तं (mind) न (not) वाञ्छति (desires) न (not) शोचति (grieves) । न (not) मुञ्चति (lets go) न (not) गृण्हाति (clings) न (not) हृष्यति (rejoices) न (not) कुप्यति (angers) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::80.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::80.essence: Freedom is the mind completely free from desire and emotional disturbance.
ashtavakra_gita::80.simple_meaning: Freedom is the state when the mind stops wanting, grieving, letting go, holding on, rejoicing, or getting angry.
ashtavakra_gita::80.simple_insight: You can find freedom by letting your mind rest without craving or aversion.
ashtavakra_gita::80.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that true freedom arises when the mind is completely still and free from desire, sorrow, attachment, joy, or anger. This teaching comes as a radical insight into liberation during his dialogue with King Janaka.
ashtavakra_gita::80.modern_relevance: In a heated argument, your mind can quickly flip between wanting to win and feeling hurt. Freedom is the quiet in between.
ashtavakra_gita::80.insight: It teaches you to observe your mind without reacting to cravings or emotions, revealing true freedom.

ashtavakra_gita::81.verse_sanskrit:
तदा बन्धो यदा चित्तं सक्तं काश्वपि दृष्टिषु ।
तदा मोक्षो यदा चित्तमसक्तं सर्वदृष्टिषु ॥
ashtavakra_gita::81.verse_hindi: जब चित्त किसी दृष्टि अथवा विषय में लगा है तब बन्ध है और चित्त जब सब दृष्टियों से अनासक्त है तब मोक्ष है।
ashtavakra_gita::81.english_translation: When the mind is attached to any perception or object, there is bondage; when the mind is unattached to all perceptions, there is freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::81.translation_literal: तदा (then) बन्धो (bondage) यदा (when) चित्तं (mind) सक्तं (attached) काश्वपि (any) दृष्टिषु (in perceptions) । तदा (then) मोक्षो (freedom) यदा (when) चित्तमसक्तं (mind unattached) सर्वदृष्टिषु (to all perceptions) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::81.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::81.essence: Freedom arises when the mind lets go of attachment to every perception.
ashtavakra_gita::81.simple_meaning: Being mentally attached to any idea or object causes bondage, but when you release attachment to all things, you find freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::81.simple_insight: You can feel the relief that comes when your mind stops clinging to things.
ashtavakra_gita::81.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches King Janaka that bondage is the mind holding on to any perception or object, while true freedom arises when the mind remains unattached to all views and experiences.
ashtavakra_gita::81.modern_relevance: You notice how stress rises when you obsess over one problem, but peace arrives when you let your mind rest without clinging.
ashtavakra_gita::81.insight: It teaches you to observe and release the mind's attachments to perceptions, opening the door to inner freedom.

ashtavakra_gita::82.verse_sanskrit:
यदा नाहं तदा मोक्षो यदाहं बन्धनं तदा ।
मत्वेति हेलया किञ्चिन्मा गृहाण विमुञ्च मा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::82.verse_hindi: जब तक ‘मैं’ है तब तक बन्ध है, जब ‘मैं’ नहीं है तब मोक्ष है । इस प्रकार का विचार कर, न इच्छा कर, न ग्रहण कर, न त्याग कर।
ashtavakra_gita::82.english_translation: As long as there is 'I', there is bondage; when 'I' is not, there is freedom. Consider this and neither desire, accept, nor reject anything.
ashtavakra_gita::82.translation_literal: यदा (when) नाहं (not I) तदा (then) मोक्षो (freedom) यदाहं (when I) बन्धनं (bondage) तदा (then) । मत्वेति (thinking thus) हेलया (easily) किञ्चिन् (anything) मा (do not) गृहाण (accept) विमुञ्च (release) मा (do not) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::82.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::82.essence: True freedom arises only when the sense of 'I' disappears completely.
ashtavakra_gita::82.simple_meaning: The feeling of 'I' creates bondage; when this sense disappears, true freedom arises. So do not cling to desire, acceptance, or rejection.
ashtavakra_gita::82.simple_insight: Freedom feels like the relief when the sense of separate self dissolves completely.
ashtavakra_gita::82.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the sense of 'I'—the ego or separate self—is the root of bondage. Only when this 'I' is absent does freedom naturally arise. He advises to neither crave nor reject but simply rest in this insight.
ashtavakra_gita::82.modern_relevance: You feel trapped by your identity and desires, but true freedom comes when you stop identifying with 'me' and 'mine'.
ashtavakra_gita::82.insight: It shifts attention from attachment to the separate self toward resting in pure awareness beyond 'I'.

ashtavakra_gita::83.verse_sanskrit:
कृताकृते च द्वन्द्वानि कदा शान्तानि कस्य वा ।
एवं ज्ञात्वेह निर्वेदाद् भव त्यागपरोऽव्रती ॥
ashtavakra_gita::83.verse_hindi: कृत्य-अकृत्य और द्वन्द्व किसके कब शान्त हुए हैं । इस प्रकार निश्चिन्त जानकर इस संसार से निर्वेद होकर त्याग और अव्रती हो।
ashtavakra_gita::83.english_translation: When have opposites like action and inaction truly ceased? Knowing this, become free from desire and renunciation in this world.
ashtavakra_gita::83.translation_literal: कृताकृते (done and undone) / च (and) / द्वन्द्वानि (pairs of opposites) / कदा (when) / शान्तानि (have ceased) / कस्य (of whom) / वा (ever) / । / एवं (thus) / ज्ञात्वे (knowing) / ह (indeed) / निर्वेदात् (dispassion) / भव (become) / त्यागपरे (beyond renunciation) / अव्रती (free from vows) / ॥
ashtavakra_gita::83.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::83.essence: True freedom goes beyond the endless cycle of opposites like action and inaction.
ashtavakra_gita::83.simple_meaning: Opposites like action and inaction never fully end. When you truly understand this, you become free from craving and giving up.
ashtavakra_gita::83.simple_insight: Relief comes from knowing you don't need to chase or reject anything to be free.
ashtavakra_gita::83.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Ashtavakra points out that pairs of opposites, like doing and not doing, never really stop. Understanding this deeply helps the seeker move beyond craving and renouncing, finding a freedom that transcends all duality.
ashtavakra_gita::83.modern_relevance: You feel stuck trying to balance doing versus not doing, wanting versus letting go. This teaches that real freedom comes beyond such struggles.
ashtavakra_gita::83.insight: It shifts your view from trying to end opposites to realizing freedom lies beyond desire and renunciation.

ashtavakra_gita::84.verse_sanskrit:
कस्यापि तात धन्यस्य लोकचेष्टावलोकनात् ।
जीवितेच्छा बुभुक्षा च बुभुत्सोपशमः गताः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::84.verse_hindi: हे तात ! लोक की चेष्टा को देखकर किसी भाग्यशाली की ही जीने की कामना, भोगने की वासना और ज्ञान की इच्छा शान्त हुई है।
ashtavakra_gita::84.english_translation: O father, upon seeing the world's ways, even the fortunate lose desire to live, to enjoy, and to seek knowledge.
ashtavakra_gita::84.translation_literal: कस्यापि (of anyone) तात (O father) धन्यस्य (fortunate's) लोकचेष्टावलोकनात् (by observing the world's activity) । जीवितेच्छा (desire to live) बुभुक्षा (desire to enjoy) च (and) बुभुत्सोपशमः (disgust and calming) गताः (have gone) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::84.speaker: Janaka
ashtavakra_gita::84.essence: Observing the world deeply can quiet even the strongest desires in the fortunate.
ashtavakra_gita::84.simple_meaning: Watching how the world acts causes even fortunate people to lose their desire to live, enjoy, or seek more knowledge.
ashtavakra_gita::84.simple_insight: You can feel calm when you see that craving fades naturally, even for those most blessed.
ashtavakra_gita::84.detailed_meaning: King Janaka reflects on how observing the world's restless activity makes even the fortunate lose their desires for life, pleasure, and knowledge. This signals a profound turning point toward detachment and insight.
ashtavakra_gita::84.modern_relevance: You scroll through endless social media, seeing others chase desires, and realize how tiring constant wanting really is.
ashtavakra_gita::84.insight: It shifts your mind from chasing desires to noticing their natural fading when fully witnessed.

ashtavakra_gita::85.verse_sanskrit:
अनित्यं सर्वमेवेदं तापत्रितयदूषितम् ।
असारं निन्दितं हेयमिति निश्चित्य शाम्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::85.verse_hindi: यह सब अनित्य है, तीनों तापों से दूषित है, सारहीन है, निन्दित है, हेय है । ऐसा निश्चित होने पर शान्ति प्राप्त होती है ।
ashtavakra_gita::85.english_translation: Everything that exists is impermanent, tainted by the three sufferings, without essence, blameworthy, and to be rejected; realizing this brings peace.
ashtavakra_gita::85.translation_literal: अनित्यं (impermanent) सर्वमेवेदं (everything that exists) तापत्रितयदूषितम् (tainted by the three sufferings) । असारं (without essence) निन्दितं (blameworthy) हेयमिति (to be rejected) निश्चित्य (realizing) शाम्यति (becomes peaceful) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::85.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::85.essence: Peace arises by clearly seeing all things as impermanent and unworthy of attachment.
ashtavakra_gita::85.simple_meaning: Everything you see changes, causes suffering, lacks true essence, and is not worth holding onto. Understanding this brings calm.
ashtavakra_gita::85.simple_insight: Relief arises from recognizing the impermanence and emptiness of all things.
ashtavakra_gita::85.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that all things are impermanent and flawed by inherent suffering. Realizing their lack of true essence frees the mind and brings peace.
ashtavakra_gita::85.modern_relevance: You watch your favorite things fade or fail, feeling restless—this teaches you to find peace beyond them.
ashtavakra_gita::85.insight: It shifts your attention from clinging to appearances toward embracing their impermanence and emptiness.

ashtavakra_gita::86.verse_sanskrit:
कोऽसौ कालो वयः किं वा यत्र द्वन्द्वानि नो नृणाम् ।
तान्युपेक्ष्य यथाप्राप्तवर्ती सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::86.verse_hindi: वह कौन सा काल है व कौन सी अवस्था है जिसमें मनुष्य को द्वन्द्व न हों । उनकी उपेक्षा कर यथाप्राप्य वस्तुओं में संतोष करने वाला मनुष्य सिद्धि को प्राप्त होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::86.english_translation: What time or stage is there when humans have no conflicts? By ignoring them and being content with what comes, one attains accomplishment.
ashtavakra_gita::86.translation_literal: कोऽसौ (which) कालो (time) वयः (age/stage) किं (what) वा (or) यत्र (where) द्वन्द्वानि (conflicts) नो (not) नृणाम् (of humans) । तान्युपेक्ष्य (ignoring those) यथा (as) प्राप्तवर्ती (received, obtained) सिद्धिम् (accomplishment) अवाप्नुयात् (may attain) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::86.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::86.essence: Conflicts are inevitable; mastery is accepting and being content with what arises.
ashtavakra_gita::86.simple_meaning: Humans always experience conflicts. True success comes when you accept this and find contentment in whatever life gives.
ashtavakra_gita::86.simple_insight: There's relief in accepting that conflicts are natural and peace comes from contentment.
ashtavakra_gita::86.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra tells King Janaka that no moment in life is free of struggles or conflicts. Instead of fighting or denying them, accepting them and being satisfied with what happens leads to true accomplishment.
ashtavakra_gita::86.modern_relevance: You face constant challenges at work or in relationships. Trying to avoid them only adds stress; accepting them lets you focus on what you can handle.
ashtavakra_gita::86.insight: It teaches you to shift focus from eliminating conflicts to accepting them and finding satisfaction in what you have.

ashtavakra_gita::87.verse_sanskrit:
नाना मतं महर्षीणां साधूनां योगिनां तथा ।
दृष्ट्वा निर्वेदमापन्नः को न शाम्यति मानवः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::87.verse_hindi: महर्षियों के, योगियों के एवं साधुओं के अनेक मत हैं । ऐसा देखकर उपेक्षा को प्राप्त हुआ कौन मनुष्य शान्ति को प्राप्त नहीं होता ।
ashtavakra_gita::87.english_translation: Among great sages, yogis, and saints, many opinions exist; seeing this, who does not grow weary? Yet who does not find peace?
ashtavakra_gita::87.translation_literal: नाना (many) मतं (opinions) महर्षीणां (of great sages) साधूनां (of saints) योगिनां (of yogis) तथा (also) । दृष्ट्वा (having seen) निर्वेदमापन्नः (having attained weariness) को (who) न (not) शाम्यति (calms down) मानवः (human) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::87.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::87.essence: Conflicting views tire the mind, but peace remains accessible to every human.
ashtavakra_gita::87.simple_meaning: You encounter many differing opinions from sages and yogis, which can cause weariness, yet everyone can still find peace.
ashtavakra_gita::87.simple_insight: It's natural to feel overwhelmed by conflicting views, but peace is still within reach.
ashtavakra_gita::87.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra points out that great sages, yogis, and saints hold many different opinions. Seeing this variety can cause confusion or weariness in a seeker, but despite this, peace remains accessible to all.
ashtavakra_gita::87.modern_relevance: You scroll through endless advice online, feeling overwhelmed by contradictions—yet a calm center inside you can still be found.
ashtavakra_gita::87.insight: Recognize that conflicting ideas don't prevent your peace; your calm can exist beyond opinions.

ashtavakra_gita::88.verse_sanskrit:
कृत्वा मूर्तिपरिज्ञानं चैतन्यस्य न किं गुरुः ।
निर्वेदसमतायुक्त्या यस्तारयति संसृतेः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::88.verse_hindi: जो उपेक्षा, समता और युक्ति के द्वारा चैतन्य के सच्चे स्वरूप को जानकर संसार में अपने को तारता है, क्या वह गुरु नहीं है ।
ashtavakra_gita::88.english_translation: Who, having realized the true nature of pure awareness through detachment, equanimity, and reasoning, liberates themselves from the cycle of the natural world, is indeed a true teacher.
ashtavakra_gita::88.translation_literal: कृत्वा (having done) / मूर्तिपरिज्ञानं (realization of the form or appearance) / चैतन्यस्य (of pure awareness) / न (not) / किं (what) / गुरुः (teacher) / निर्वेदसमतायुक्त्या (by detachment, equanimity, and reasoning) / यः (who) / तारयति (liberates) / संसृतेः (from the cycle of the natural world)
ashtavakra_gita::88.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::88.essence: Clear, calm understanding of pure awareness liberates you like a true teacher.
ashtavakra_gita::88.simple_meaning: When you understand your true awareness through letting go, balance, and clear thinking, you free yourself from life's endless cycle. Such a person is a real teacher.
ashtavakra_gita::88.simple_insight: There is power in calm, clear knowing that sets you free from repeating patterns.
ashtavakra_gita::88.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that someone who deeply understands pure awareness by practicing detachment, equanimity, and reasoning can free themselves from the endless flow of change and rebirth. This clear realization alone makes one a true teacher.
ashtavakra_gita::88.modern_relevance: You feel stuck in repeating mistakes until you calmly see your true nature with clear reasoning and balanced emotions, freeing yourself from old cycles.
ashtavakra_gita::88.insight: It teaches you to combine detachment, balance, and reasoning to recognize your pure awareness and break free from repetitive patterns.

ashtavakra_gita::89.verse_sanskrit:
पश्य भूतविकारांस्त्वं भूतमात्रान् यथार्थतः ।
तत्क्षणाद् बन्धनिर्मुक्तः स्वरूपस्थो भविष्यसि ॥
ashtavakra_gita::89.verse_hindi: जब भूत-विकारों को तू यथार्थतः भूतमात्र देखेगा – उसी क्षण बन्ध से मुक्त होकर अपने स्वरूप में स्थित हो जाएगा ।
ashtavakra_gita::89.english_translation: When you truly see all changes as nothing but appearances, you become free from bondage and remain established in your true nature.
ashtavakra_gita::89.translation_literal: पश्य (see) / भूतविकारान् (changes of beings) / त्वं (you) / भूतमात्रान् (only appearances) / यथार्थतः (truly) / तत् (that) / क्षणात् (moment) / बन्धनिर्मुक्तः (bondage-free) / स्वरूपस्थो (established in true nature) / भविष्यसि (you will become)
ashtavakra_gita::89.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::89.essence: True freedom arises the moment you see all change as mere appearances.
ashtavakra_gita::89.simple_meaning: When you recognize that all changes you see are just appearances, you instantly become free and rest in your true self.
ashtavakra_gita::89.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing freedom is available the moment you see clearly.
