ashtavakra_gita::89.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the restless changes around you are only appearances. When you see this truth clearly, you instantly release bondage and settle into your unchanging true nature.
ashtavakra_gita::89.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by constant change and inner turmoil; realizing it’s all just surface helps you find calm and freedom now.
ashtavakra_gita::89.insight: It shifts your view from reacting to appearances to resting in your unchanging true self instantly.

ashtavakra_gita::90.verse_sanskrit:
वासना एव संसार इति सर्वा विमुञ्च ताः ।
तत्त्यागो वासनात्यागात्स्थितिरद्य यथा तथा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::90.verse_hindi: वासना ही संसार है इसलिये इन सबका त्याग कर । वासना के त्याग से ही संसार का त्याग है । अब जहाँ चाहे वहाँ रह।
ashtavakra_gita::90.english_translation: Desire alone is the cause of the cycle of reactivity; abandon all desires. By abandoning desires, you abandon the cycle. Now you can remain wherever you wish.
ashtavakra_gita::90.translation_literal: वासना (desire) / एव (alone) / संसार (cycle of reactivity) / इति (thus) / सर्वा (all) / विमुञ्च (abandon) / ताः (them) / । / तत् (that) / त्यागः (abandonment) / वासना (desire) / त्यागात् (from abandonment) / स्थितिः (state) / अद्य (now) / यथा (as) / तथा (so) / ॥
ashtavakra_gita::90.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::90.essence: Abandoning desire breaks the cycle that binds you, granting freedom anywhere.
ashtavakra_gita::90.simple_meaning: All suffering and repeated reactions come from desire. Letting go of desire ends that cycle, letting you exist freely anywhere.
ashtavakra_gita::90.simple_insight: Freedom begins when you drop what pulls you back—your desires.
ashtavakra_gita::90.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Ashtavakra explains to King Janaka that the entire cycle of reactive existence arises from desire. By renouncing desire, one also renounces that cycle, gaining freedom to be at peace anywhere without being bound.
ashtavakra_gita::90.modern_relevance: You feel trapped in patterns driven by what you want but can't have. Letting go of these cravings frees you to find peace wherever you are.
ashtavakra_gita::90.insight: This verse shifts your focus from chasing desires to simply releasing them, breaking habitual patterns.

ashtavakra_gita::91.verse_sanskrit:
विहाय वैरिणं काममर्थं चानर्थसङ्कुलम् ।
धर्ममप्येतयोर्हेतुं सर्वत्रानादरं कुरु ॥
ashtavakra_gita::91.verse_hindi: वैर स्वरूप काम को और अनर्थ से भरे अर्थ को त्याग कर और दोनों के कारण-रूप धर्म को भी छोड़कर तू सबकी उपेक्षा कर।
ashtavakra_gita::91.english_translation: Give up enmity, desire, and goals filled with harm; even abandon the dharma born from these, and everywhere disregard all.
ashtavakra_gita::91.translation_literal: विहाय (giving up) वैरिणं (enmity) काममर्थं (desire and goals) चानर्थसङ्कुलम् (filled with harm) । धर्ममपि (even dharma) एतयोः (of these two) हेतुं (cause) सर्वत्र (everywhere) अनादरं (disrespect) कुरु (do) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::91.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::91.essence: Freedom arises by releasing harm, desire, and even the duties they create.
ashtavakra_gita::91.simple_meaning: Let go of hatred, desire, harmful goals, and even the duties that arise from them. Disregard all such attachments everywhere.
ashtavakra_gita::91.simple_insight: You feel free when you release not only harmful desires but even duties tied to them.
ashtavakra_gita::91.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that true freedom requires abandoning not only hostile feelings and harmful desires but also the sense of duty originating from them. This radical renunciation breaks all attachments, even to what seems righteous.
ashtavakra_gita::91.modern_relevance: You’ve been holding grudges and chasing goals that cause stress; letting go of both the feelings and the obligations tied to them opens space for peace.
ashtavakra_gita::91.insight: This shifts your mind from clinging to any motivation born of harm or desire, freeing you from all binding attachments.

ashtavakra_gita::92.verse_sanskrit:
स्वप्नेन्द्रजालवत् पश्य दिनानि त्रीणि पञ्च वा ।
मित्रक्षेत्रधनागारदारदायादिसम्पदः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::92.verse_hindi: मित्र, खेत, धन, मकान, स्त्री, भाई आदि सम्पदा को तू स्वप्न और इन्द्रजाल के समान देख जो तीन या पाँच दिन ही टिकते हैं ।
ashtavakra_gita::92.english_translation: See friends, fields, wealth, houses, wives, brothers, and such possessions as like a dream or magical illusion that lasts only three or five days.
ashtavakra_gita::92.translation_literal: स्वप्नेन्द्रजालवत् (like dream and magical illusion) / पश्य (see) / दिनानि (days) / त्रीणि (three) / पञ्च (five) / वा (or) / मित्रक्षेत्रधनागारदारदायादि (friend, field, wealth, storehouse, house, wife, gift, wealth etc.) / सम्पदः (possessions)
ashtavakra_gita::92.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::92.essence: All worldly attachments are fleeting illusions that cannot last.
ashtavakra_gita::92.simple_meaning: Everything you consider valuable—friends, land, wealth, and family—is temporary, like a brief dream or illusion.
ashtavakra_gita::92.simple_insight: You feel the freedom that comes from seeing attachments as temporary and insubstantial.
ashtavakra_gita::92.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that what we cling to—friends, property, family—lasts only briefly, like a dream or illusion. This reminder comes early in the dialogue to prompt questioning of worldly attachments.
ashtavakra_gita::92.modern_relevance: You watch a social media highlight fade or a prized possession break, realizing how quickly what you value can change or disappear.
ashtavakra_gita::92.insight: It shifts your mind to see attachments as temporary, reducing clinging and anxiety about loss.

ashtavakra_gita::93.verse_sanskrit:
यत्र यत्र भवेत्तृष्णा संसारं विद्धि तत्र वै ।
प्रौढवैराग्यमाश्रित्य वीततृष्णः सुखी भव ॥
ashtavakra_gita::93.verse_hindi: जहाँ-जहाँ तृष्णा हो वहाँ-वहाँ ही संसार जान । प्रौढ़ वैराग्य को आश्रय करके वीततृष्णा होकर सुखी हो।
ashtavakra_gita::93.english_translation: Wherever craving arises, realize that there is the cycle of reactivity; relying on mature non-attachment, become free of craving and be happy.
ashtavakra_gita::93.translation_literal: यत्र (wherever) यत्र (wherever) भवेत् (arises) तृष्णा (craving) संसारं (the cycle of reactivity) विद्धि (know) तत्र (there) वै (indeed) प्रौढवैराग्यम् (mature non-attachment) आश्रित्य (relying on) वीततृष्णः (free from craving) सुखी (happy) भव (become)
ashtavakra_gita::93.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::93.essence: Craving reveals the cycle of reactivity; mature non-attachment dissolves craving and brings happiness.
ashtavakra_gita::93.simple_meaning: Whenever you notice craving, recognize that it causes continuous reactivity. By embracing mature non-attachment, you can become free of craving and find happiness.
ashtavakra_gita::93.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing craving is the root of your unrest and non-attachment brings peace.
ashtavakra_gita::93.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that wherever craving arises in your mind, that place is where the cycle of reactive suffering exists. He advises to rely on mature non-attachment, which means a deep letting go of desires, so you become free of craving and experience true happiness.
ashtavakra_gita::93.modern_relevance: You scroll social media and feel a sudden urge for more likes or approval. Recognizing that craving fuels your unrest, you choose to let go and find calm instead.
ashtavakra_gita::93.insight: It teaches you to observe craving as the start of reactivity and shift towards mature non-attachment to break free.

ashtavakra_gita::94.verse_sanskrit:
तृष्णामात्रात्मको बन्धस्तन्नाशो मोक्ष उच्यते ।
भवासंसक्तिमात्रेण प्राप्तितुष्टिर्मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::94.verse_hindi: तृष्णामात्र ही आत्मा का बन्ध है और उसका नाश मोक्ष कहा जाता है । संसार मात्र से अनासक्त होने से निरन्तर प्राप्ति और तुष्टि होती है।
ashtavakra_gita::94.english_translation: The only bond is craving; its destruction is freedom. Continuous detachment from the cycle of existence brings repeated fulfillment and contentment.
ashtavakra_gita::94.translation_literal: तृष्णा (craving) / मात्र (only) / आत्मको (of the self) / बन्धः (bond) / तन्नाशः (its destruction) / मोक्षः (freedom) / उच्यते (is called) / भव (world) / आसक्ति (attachment) / मात्रेण (only by) / प्राप्ति (gain) / तुष्टिः (contentment) / मुहूर्मुहुः (again and again)
ashtavakra_gita::94.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::94.essence: Freedom arises not by gaining but by ending craving, the true bond.
ashtavakra_gita::94.simple_meaning: Craving is the only true bond that traps you. When this craving ends, you find freedom and ongoing satisfaction beyond worldly attachments.
ashtavakra_gita::94.simple_insight: Relief arises from seeing craving as the root of all bondage and knowing freedom is its end.
ashtavakra_gita::94.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains to King Janaka that craving alone binds the true self. Liberation is not a distant goal but the simple cessation of craving and attachment to the world, which brings continuous inner fulfillment.
ashtavakra_gita::94.modern_relevance: You notice how wanting more or different things pulls you into stress and restlessness. Letting go of craving reveals a steady satisfaction beneath.
ashtavakra_gita::94.insight: It teaches you to identify craving as your inner bond and to cultivate detachment for lasting contentment.

ashtavakra_gita::95.verse_sanskrit:
त्वमेकश्चेतनः शुद्धो जडं विश्वमसत्तथा ।
अविद्यापि न किञ्चित्सा का बुभुत्सा तथापि ते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::95.verse_hindi: तू एक शुद्ध चैतन्य है, संसार जड़ और असत् है । यह अविद्या भी असत् है । इस पर भी तू क्या जानने की इच्छा रखता है।
ashtavakra_gita::95.english_translation: You are pure consciousness alone; the world is insentient and unreal. Ignorance itself is unreal. Why then do you seek to know it?
ashtavakra_gita::95.translation_literal: त्वम् (you) एकः (one) चेतनः (consciousness) शुद्धः (pure) जडं (insentient) विश्वम् (world) असत् (unreal) तथा (thus) । अविद्या (ignorance) अपि (also) न (not) किञ्चित्सा (anything) का (why) बुभुत्सा (desire to know) तथापि (even so) ते (you) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::95.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::95.essence: Your true nature is pure consciousness; all else, including ignorance, is unreal.
ashtavakra_gita::95.simple_meaning: You are pure awareness alone. The world and ignorance are unreal and insentient. So why desire to know what does not truly exist?
ashtavakra_gita::95.simple_insight: You can feel free from confusion by realizing you are not the unreal world or ignorance.
ashtavakra_gita::95.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that your true nature is pure consciousness, untainted and singular. Everything else, including the world and ignorance, is unreal and insentient. This verse challenges the seeker to stop pursuing false knowledge of what is not real.
ashtavakra_gita::95.modern_relevance: You might catch yourself endlessly chasing worries or false identities, forgetting your true clear awareness beyond all that noise.
ashtavakra_gita::95.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing illusions to recognizing your true, unchanging nature as pure awareness.

ashtavakra_gita::96.verse_sanskrit:
राज्यं सुताः कलत्राणि शरीराणि सुखानि च ।
संसक्तस्यापि नष्टानि तव जन्मनि जन्मनि ॥
ashtavakra_gita::96.verse_hindi: तेरे राज्य, पुत्र, पुत्रियाँ, शरीर और सुख जन्म-जन्म से नष्ट हुए हैं, यद्यपि तू उनमें आसक्त था।
ashtavakra_gita::96.english_translation: Your kingdom, sons, wives, body, and pleasures have been lost again and again in your many births, even though you were attached to them.
ashtavakra_gita::96.translation_literal: राज्यं (kingdom) / सुताः (sons) / कलत्राणि (wives) / शरीराणि (bodies) / सुखानि (pleasures) / च (and) / संसक्तस्यापि (even attached) / नष्टानि (lost) / तव (your) / जन्मनि (in birth) / जन्मनि (birth) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::96.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::96.essence: Clinging to impermanent things only leads to repeated loss over many lives.
ashtavakra_gita::96.simple_meaning: Everything you have clung to—your kingdom, family, body, and pleasures—has been lost repeatedly through many lifetimes.
ashtavakra_gita::96.simple_insight: There's a quiet truth in seeing that holding on causes repeated loss, inviting you to loosen your grip.
ashtavakra_gita::96.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra points out to Janaka that despite his attachments to his kingdom, family, and body, these have disappeared repeatedly across many births, revealing the futility of clinging to impermanent things.
ashtavakra_gita::96.modern_relevance: You might hold tightly to your career, relationships, or health, only to watch them change or disappear over time.
ashtavakra_gita::96.insight: It encourages shifting your focus from clinging to impermanent things toward recognizing what truly endures beyond them.

ashtavakra_gita::97.verse_sanskrit:
अलमर्थेन कामेन सुकृतेनापि कर्मणा ।
एभ्यः संसारकान्तारे न विश्रान्तमभून् मनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::97.verse_hindi: अर्थ, काम और सुकृत कर्म बहुत हो चुके । इनमें भी संसाररूपी जंगल में मन विश्रान्ति को प्राप्त नहीं हुआ।
ashtavakra_gita::97.english_translation: Even after much wealth, desire, and good deeds, the mind found no rest in the forest of the cycle of reactivity.
ashtavakra_gita::97.translation_literal: अलमर्थेन (by much wealth) / कामेन (by desire) / सुकृतेनापि (even by good deeds) / कर्मणा (through action) / एभ्यः (from these) / संसारकान्तारे (in the forest of the cycle of reactivity) / न (not) / विश्रान्तमभून् (became rested) / मनः (the mind)
ashtavakra_gita::97.speaker: Janaka
ashtavakra_gita::97.essence: External gains and good actions alone cannot still a restless mind trapped in reactivity.
ashtavakra_gita::97.simple_meaning: Having wealth, fulfilling desires, and doing good deeds do not guarantee that your mind will be peaceful or free from restlessness.
ashtavakra_gita::97.simple_insight: You feel the gap between external success and inner calm, understanding peace cannot be bought or earned.
ashtavakra_gita::97.detailed_meaning: King Janaka reflects that despite accumulating wealth, satisfying desires, and performing many good actions, his mind remains restless and unsettled, trapped in the endless cycle of reactivity called samsara. He expresses the universal struggle for lasting inner peace beyond external achievements.
ashtavakra_gita::97.modern_relevance: After chasing promotions, buying things, and doing favors, you still lie awake with a busy mind that won’t settle.
ashtavakra_gita::97.insight: Recognize that external achievements and desires don’t quiet the mind; true rest requires inner transformation beyond action.

ashtavakra_gita::98.verse_sanskrit:
कृतं न कति जन्मानि कायेन मनसा गिरा ।
दुःखमायासदं कर्म तदद्याप्युपरम्यताम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::98.verse_hindi: कितने जन्मों तक तूने क्या शरीर, मन और वाणी के दुखपूर्ण और श्रमपूर्ण कर्म नहीं किये हैं । अब तो आराम कर।
ashtavakra_gita::98.english_translation: How many lifetimes have you not performed painful actions with body, mind, and speech? Now, rest at last.
ashtavakra_gita::98.translation_literal: कृतं (done) / न (not) / कति (how many) / जन्मानि (births) / कायेन (by body) / मनसा (by mind) / गिरा (by speech) / दुःखमायासदं (painful and laborious) / कर्म (actions) / तद (that) / अद्यापि (even now) / उपरम्यताम् (let it cease/rest).
ashtavakra_gita::98.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::98.essence: After endless painful effort, the true self can finally rest free of action.
ashtavakra_gita::98.simple_meaning: You have performed many difficult actions over many lives with your body, mind, and speech. Now it is time to stop and rest.
ashtavakra_gita::98.simple_insight: There's relief in realizing you don't have to keep struggling endlessly.
ashtavakra_gita::98.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra reminds that the seeker has carried painful actions through countless births using body, mind, and speech. After this long struggle, the teaching urges to stop striving and rest, hinting at a deeper freedom beyond effort.
ashtavakra_gita::98.modern_relevance: You’ve pushed yourself through endless tasks and worries, caught in constant effort. This moment invites you to pause and just rest.
ashtavakra_gita::98.insight: It shifts the mind from continuous struggle to allowing rest as a form of freedom.

ashtavakra_gita::99.verse_sanskrit:
भावाभावविकारश्च स्वभावादिति निश्चयी ।
निर्विकारो गतक्लेशः सुखेनैवोपशाम्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::99.verse_hindi: और अभाव का विकार स्वभाव से होता है ऐसा जो निश्चयपूर्वक जानता है, वह निर्विकार और क्लेशरहित पुरुष सुखपूर्वक ही शान्ति को उपलब्ध होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::99.english_translation: One who firmly knows that existence and non-existence arise from nature is free from disturbance and pain, and attains peace with joy.
ashtavakra_gita::99.translation_literal: भावाभावविकारश्च (existence-nonexistence-changes) / स्वभावादिति (from nature, thus) / निश्चयी (one who is certain) / निर्विकारो (without disturbance) / गतक्लेशः (gone pain) / सुखेनैवोपशाम्यति (with joy alone attains peace)
ashtavakra_gita::99.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::99.essence: True peace and joy come from knowing change and pain are natural and do not disturb you.
ashtavakra_gita::99.simple_meaning: Understanding that all changes and opposites come from nature helps you become free from disturbance and pain, reaching peaceful joy.
ashtavakra_gita::99.simple_insight: You can feel calm and joyful even when everything changes around you.
ashtavakra_gita::99.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a person who firmly understands that existence and non-existence, and all changes, arise naturally becomes free from emotional disturbance and suffering, naturally resting in joyful peace.
ashtavakra_gita::99.modern_relevance: After losing control or facing constant ups and downs, you realize peace comes when you stop resisting change and pain.
ashtavakra_gita::99.insight: It shifts your mind from reacting to change and pain towards embracing them as natural, bringing steady joy.

ashtavakra_gita::100.verse_sanskrit:
ईश्वरः सर्वनिर्माता नेहान्य इति निश्चयी ।
अन्तर्गलितसर्वाशः शान्तः क्वापि न सज्जते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::100.verse_hindi: सबको बनाने वाले ईश्वर हैं अन्य कोई नहीं है, ऐसा जो निश्चयपूर्वक जानता है वह पुरुष शान्त है । उसकी सब आशाएँ जड़ से नष्ट हो गयी हैं । वह कहीं भी आसक्त नहीं होता।
ashtavakra_gita::100.english_translation: The one who firmly knows that the supreme being alone is the creator of all is peaceful; all their desires are completely dissolved, and they are attached nowhere.
ashtavakra_gita::100.translation_literal: ईश्वरः (supreme being) / सर्वनिर्माता (creator of all) / नेहान्य (none other than this) / इति (thus) / निश्चयी (one who is certain) / अन्तर्गलितसर्वाशः (all desires dissolved within) / शान्तः (peaceful) / क्वापि (anywhere) / न (not) / सज्जते (attached)
ashtavakra_gita::100.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::100.essence: Peace arises when you fully know the supreme alone creates all and all desires vanish.
ashtavakra_gita::100.simple_meaning: Knowing with certainty that the supreme being alone creates everything brings deep peace and frees you from all desires and attachments.
ashtavakra_gita::100.simple_insight: Real peace arises when all your desires vanish in firm knowing of the supreme creation.
ashtavakra_gita::100.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that when someone firmly realizes the supreme being is the sole creator of all, that person's desires dissolve completely. This release from craving brings a state of peace and detachment from all worldly attachments.
ashtavakra_gita::100.modern_relevance: You feel calm when you stop chasing every desire and accept that the source of everything is beyond personal control.
ashtavakra_gita::100.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing desires to resting in the certainty of a single creative source, calming restless seeking.

ashtavakra_gita::101.verse_sanskrit:
आपदः सम्पदः काले दैवादेवेति निश्चयी ।
तृप्तः स्वस्थेन्द्रियो नित्यं न वान्छति न शोचति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::101.verse_hindi: विपत्ति और सम्पत्ति दैवयोग से ही समय पर आती है, ऐसा निश्चय वाला पुरुष सदा सन्तुष्ट हुआ, न कोई कामना करता है, न शोक करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::101.english_translation: Calamity and prosperity come in their own time by the divine's will; a person resolved in this remains always content, desires nothing, and grieves not.
ashtavakra_gita::101.translation_literal: आपदः (calamity) / सम्पदः (prosperity) / काले (in time) / दैवादेवेति (by divine will) / निश्चयी (one who is resolved) । / तृप्तः (content) / स्वस्थेन्द्रियो (with steady senses) / नित्यं (always) / न (not) / वान्छति (desires) / न (nor) / शोचति (grieves) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::101.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::101.essence: Contentment arises by trusting life's timing, freeing you from desire and grief.
ashtavakra_gita::101.simple_meaning: Good or bad events happen according to their own time beyond your control; trusting this, you stay content without craving or sorrow.
ashtavakra_gita::101.simple_insight: Feeling steady through ups and downs frees you from emotional turmoil.
ashtavakra_gita::101.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that calamity and prosperity arrive by divine timing, beyond human control. A person who accepts this remains content, steady of mind, free from desire and grief in life's fluctuations.
ashtavakra_gita::101.modern_relevance: You face sudden news: a lost job or unexpected praise. Trusting that these come and go naturally keeps your mind calm.
ashtavakra_gita::101.insight: It teaches you to anchor your peace in trust of timing, not in external events.

ashtavakra_gita::102.verse_sanskrit:
सुखदुःखे जन्ममृत्यू दैवादेवेति निश्चयी ।
साध्यादर्शी निरायासः कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::102.verse_hindi: सुख-दुःख, जन्म-मृत्यु दैवयोग से ही होती है, ऐसा निश्चय वाला व्यक्ति साध्य कर्मों को देखता हुआ और निरायास कर्मों को करता हुआ भी उनमें लिप्त नहीं होता।
ashtavakra_gita::102.english_translation: A person firmly certain that pleasure, pain, birth, and death happen by the divine order sees actions as unavoidable and performs effortless acts without attachment.
ashtavakra_gita::102.translation_literal: सुखदुःखे (pleasure and pain) जन्ममृत्यू (birth and death) दैवादेवेति (by divine order) निश्चयी (one who is certain) । साध्यादर्शी (seeing actions as unavoidable) निरायासः (effortless) कुर्वन् (doing) अपि (even) न (not) लिप्यते (attached) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::102.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::102.essence: You can act effortlessly without attachment, accepting life’s natural cycles.
ashtavakra_gita::102.simple_meaning: You understand that happiness, suffering, birth, and death happen naturally. Seeing this, you act without effort and without getting caught up in outcomes.
ashtavakra_gita::102.simple_insight: You feel steady and untroubled because you accept life’s natural flow.
ashtavakra_gita::102.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a person who firmly accepts that all experiences arise by natural order can perform necessary actions effortlessly and without emotional attachment, even facing birth, death, joy, and pain.
ashtavakra_gita::102.modern_relevance: You face unexpected setbacks or successes at work but remain calm, knowing these events are part of life’s natural rhythm.
ashtavakra_gita::102.insight: It shifts your focus from resisting life’s ups and downs to embracing your actions without emotional entanglement.

ashtavakra_gita::103.verse_sanskrit:
चिन्तया जायते दुःखं नान्यथेहेति निश्चयी ।
तया हीनः सुखी शान्तः सर्वत्र गलितस्पृहः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::103.verse_hindi: चिन्ता से दुःख उत्पन्न होता है अन्यथा नहीं । ऐसा जो निश्चयपूर्वक जानता है, वह सुखी और शान्त है । सर्वत्र उसकी स्पृहा गलित है और चिन्ता से मुक्त है।
ashtavakra_gita::103.english_translation: Suffering arises only from worry; knowing this with certainty brings peace and joy, dissolving all desire everywhere.
ashtavakra_gita::103.translation_literal: चिन्तया (by worry) / जायते (arises) / दुःखं (suffering) / न (not) / अन्यथे (otherwise) / इति (thus) / निश्चयी (one who is certain) / तया (by that) / हीनः (devoid) / सुखी (happy) / शान्तः (peaceful) / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / गलितस्पृहः (desire dissolved)
ashtavakra_gita::103.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::103.essence: Suffering arises only from worry; knowing this brings lasting peace and ends craving.
ashtavakra_gita::103.simple_meaning: Suffering comes only from worry. When you know this firmly, you become peaceful and joyful, free from all craving.
ashtavakra_gita::103.simple_insight: Relief arises knowing that worry, not events, causes suffering.
ashtavakra_gita::103.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that pain comes solely from the restless mind's worries. Recognising this with certainty calms the spirit. In the midst of life's challenges, this insight lets Janaka become peaceful and desire-free.
ashtavakra_gita::103.modern_relevance: Your mind races with 'what ifs' and fears, making simple moments heavy. Seeing worry as the source frees you to relax.
ashtavakra_gita::103.insight: Shift focus from external troubles to your mental response; calming worry dissolves suffering.

ashtavakra_gita::104.verse_sanskrit:
नाहं देहो न मे देहो बोधोऽहमिति निश्चयी ।
कैवल्यमिव सम्प्राप्तो न स्मरत्यकृतं कृतम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::104.verse_hindi: मैं शरीर नहीं हूँ, देह मेरी नहीं है, मैं तो बोधस्वरूप हूँ, ऐसा जो निश्चयपूर्वक जानता है वह पुरुष कैवल्य को प्राप्त होकर किये और अनकिये कर्म का स्मरण नहीं करता।
ashtavakra_gita::104.english_translation: I am not the body, nor does the body belong to me; I am pure awareness. One who firmly knows this, having attained complete freedom, does not recall actions done or undone.
ashtavakra_gita::104.translation_literal: नाहं (I am not) देहो (body) न (nor) मे (my) देहो (body) बोधोऽहमिति (I am awareness) निश्चयी (firmly knowing) । कैवल्यमिव (as if complete freedom) सम्प्राप्तो (attained) न (not) स्मरत्य (recalls) अकृतं (undone) कृतम् (done) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::104.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::104.essence: Realizing you are pure awareness frees you from attachment to body and actions.
ashtavakra_gita::104.simple_meaning: You are not the body, nor does it belong to you. You are pure awareness. When you truly know this, you no longer remember your past actions or unfinished tasks.
ashtavakra_gita::104.simple_insight: You can feel free by knowing you are beyond your body and actions.
ashtavakra_gita::104.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Ashtavakra tells King Janaka that the true self is pure awareness, separate from the body. When someone firmly realizes this, they reach complete freedom and no longer cling to past or uncompleted actions.
ashtavakra_gita::104.modern_relevance: You finish a task but still feel burdened by what’s done or left undone. Knowing you are beyond these actions lifts that weight.
ashtavakra_gita::104.insight: It shifts your identity from body and deeds to pure awareness, freeing you from attachment to results.

ashtavakra_gita::105.verse_sanskrit:
आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्तमहमेवेति निश्चयी ।
निर्विकल्पः शुचिः शान्तः प्राप्ताप्राप्तविनिर्वृतः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::105.verse_hindi: ब्रह्म से लेकर तृणपर्यन्त ‘मैं ही हूँ’ ऐसा जो निश्चयपूर्वक जानता है, वह निर्विकार, शुद्ध, शान्त और प्राप्त-अप्राप्त से निवृत्त होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::105.english_translation: One who firmly knows 'I am the supreme reality' from Brahman to the blade of grass becomes free from all dualities, pure, peaceful, and beyond gain or loss.
ashtavakra_gita::105.translation_literal: आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्त (from Brahman to the blade) / अहमेवेति (I am indeed) / निश्चयी (firmly knowing) / निर्विकल्पः (without doubt) / शुचिः (pure) / शान्तः (peaceful) / प्राप्ताप्राप्तविनिर्वृतः (free from gain and loss)
ashtavakra_gita::105.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::105.essence: Knowing you are the unchanging reality beneath all things brings lasting peace and freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::105.simple_meaning: Knowing deeply that you are the one reality behind all things, big or small, brings purity, peace, and freedom from all ups and downs.
ashtavakra_gita::105.simple_insight: Feeling that your true self is steady and pure beyond every change brings deep calm and confidence.
ashtavakra_gita::105.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that realizing your identity as the supreme reality—from the greatest to the smallest detail—leads to a state free from confusion, full of purity and peace, and unaffected by gains or losses.
ashtavakra_gita::105.modern_relevance: You realize that beneath every success or failure, you remain untouched and steady, like the quiet truth beneath all your experiences.
ashtavakra_gita::105.insight: It shifts focus from fleeting achievements to the constant, pure presence you already are, freeing you from emotional swings.

ashtavakra_gita::106.verse_sanskrit:
नाश्चर्यमिदं विश्वं न किञ्चिदिति निश्चयी ।
निर्वासनः स्फूर्तिमात्रो न किञ्चिदिव शाम्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::106.verse_hindi: अनेक आश्चर्यों वाला वह विश्व कुछ भी नहीं है अर्थात मिथ्या है ऐसा जो निश्चयपूर्वक जानता है, वह वासनारहित, बोधस्वरूप पुरुष इस प्रकार शान्ति को प्राप्त होता है, मानो कुछ भी नहीं है ।
ashtavakra_gita::106.english_translation: The world full of wonders is ultimately nothing; one who firmly knows this, free from desire, attains a peace as if nothing exists.
ashtavakra_gita::106.translation_literal: नाश्चर्यमिदं (this world full of wonders) / विश्वं (world) / न (not) / किञ्चिदिति (anything) / निश्चयी (one who is certain) / निर्वासनः (free from desire) / स्फूर्तिमात्रो (pure awareness alone) / न (not) / किञ्चिदिव (as if nothing) / शाम्यति (becomes calm).
ashtavakra_gita::106.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::106.essence: True peace comes from fully knowing the world’s wonders are empty appearances.
ashtavakra_gita::106.simple_meaning: The world, though full of wonders, is ultimately empty. One who truly understands this and is free from desire finds deep peace as if nothing disturbs them.
ashtavakra_gita::106.simple_insight: You can feel calm by seeing through the world's illusions and letting go of craving.
ashtavakra_gita::106.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the entire world, despite its many wonders, is ultimately unreal or appearance. A person who is free from desire and rests as pure awareness achieves a profound calm, as if nothing exists to disturb them.
ashtavakra_gita::106.modern_relevance: You pause in a moment of chaos and realize your worries are shadows, not solid threats to your peace.
ashtavakra_gita::106.insight: It shifts your mind from craving and confusion to steady calm by recognizing appearances as empty.

ashtavakra_gita::107.verse_sanskrit:
कायकृत्यासहः पूर्वं ततो वाग्विस्तरासहः ।
अथ चिन्तासहस्तस्माद् एवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::107.verse_hindi: पहले मैं शारीरिक कर्मों का न सराहने वाला हुआ, फिर वाणी के विस्तृत कर्म का न सराहने वाला हुआ । इस प्रकार मैं स्थिर हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::107.english_translation: First, I became indifferent to bodily actions, then to the extensive actions of speech; thus, I have remained steady.
ashtavakra_gita::107.translation_literal: कायकृत्यासहः (to bodily actions indifferent) / पूर्वं (before) / ततो (then) / वाग्विस्तरासहः (to extensive actions of speech indifferent) / अथ (thus) / चिन्तासहः (to mental worries indifferent) / तस्माद् (therefore) / एवमेव (in this way) / अहम् (I) / आस्थितः (have remained steady)
ashtavakra_gita::107.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::107.essence: Steadiness arises when you release attachment to body, speech, and mental worries.
ashtavakra_gita::107.simple_meaning: You find steadiness by no longer clinging to your bodily actions, your words, or your thoughts.
ashtavakra_gita::107.simple_insight: There is calm in releasing the need to control body, speech, and mind.
ashtavakra_gita::107.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains how he achieved true steadiness by first becoming indifferent to physical actions, then to speech, and finally to mental worries, showing a progression of detachment.
ashtavakra_gita::107.modern_relevance: You stop obsessing over what you say, what you do, and what you think, and suddenly your inner calm deepens.
ashtavakra_gita::107.insight: It teaches you to progressively detach from body, speech, and mind to become unshakable.

ashtavakra_gita::108.verse_hindi: शब्द आदि ऐन्द्रिक विषयों के प्रति राग के अभाव से और आत्मा की अदृश्यता से प्राप्त विक्षेपों से जिसका मन मुक्त होकर एकाग्र हो गया – ऐसा ही मैं स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::108.english_translation: I remain established with a heart free from attachment to sensory objects like sounds and free from distractions caused by the invisible nature of the self, fully concentrated on one point.
ashtavakra_gita::108.translation_literal: प्रीत्यभावेन (with feeling of attachment) / शब्दादि (sounds etc.) / इन्द्रिय (sensory) / विषयों (objects) / प्रति (towards) / राग (attachment) / के (of) / अभाव (absence) / से (from) / और (and) / आत्मनः (of the self) / अदृश्यत्वेन (invisibility) / च (and) / विक्षेप (distraction) / एकाग्र (single-pointed) / हृदय (heart) / एवमेव (just so) / अहम् (I) / आस्-स्थितः (established).
ashtavakra_gita::108.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::108.essence: You can remain fully focused and undistracted by sensory attachments or the invisible self.
ashtavakra_gita::108.simple_meaning: You can be free from attachment to sensory things and distractions, keeping your heart focused on one point.
ashtavakra_gita::108.simple_insight: There is peace in a heart that no longer chases senses or distractions.
ashtavakra_gita::108.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes his calm state where he is not drawn by sounds or other sensory objects, nor distracted by the invisible self, but remains deeply focused and undisturbed.
ashtavakra_gita::108.modern_relevance: When your mind wanders amidst constant notifications and noise, knowing how to stay focused and unattached brings clarity and calm.
ashtavakra_gita::108.insight: It teaches you to loosen attachment to sensory distractions and anchor your attention steadily.

ashtavakra_gita::109.verse_sanskrit:
समाध्यासादिविक्षिप्तौ व्यवहारः समाधये ।
एवं विलोक्य नियममेवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::109.verse_hindi: सम्यक् अध्यास आदि के कारण विक्षेप होने पर ही समाधि का व्यवहार होता है । ऐसे नियम को देखकर मैं स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::109.english_translation: Disturbance arises in action due to attachment and other causes; seeing this rule, I remain steady.
ashtavakra_gita::109.translation_literal: समाध्या (by attachment) / आदि (and others) / विक्षिप्तौ (disturbed) / व्यवहारः (action) / समाधये (in absorption) / एवं (thus) / विलोक्य (having seen) / नियममेव (the rule itself) / एव (indeed) / अहम् (I) / अवस्थितः (am situated).
ashtavakra_gita::109.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::109.essence: Seeing attachment's disturbance in action lets you remain steady and present.
ashtavakra_gita::109.simple_meaning: Attachment and similar distractions disturb your actions and presence; recognizing this helps you remain steady.
ashtavakra_gita::109.simple_insight: You can feel calm by noticing what unsettles you instead of being swept away.
ashtavakra_gita::109.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that actions become disturbed due to attachment and related causes. By understanding this pattern, a person can stay steady amidst distractions, which is crucial for inner balance.
ashtavakra_gita::109.modern_relevance: You feel distracted when your mind clings to results or worries, but noticing this pattern helps you stay grounded.
ashtavakra_gita::109.insight: Recognize attachment as the source of disturbance to maintain inner steadiness during action.

ashtavakra_gita::110.verse_sanskrit:
हेयोपादेयविरहाद् एवं हर्षविषादयोः ।
अभावादद्य हे ब्रह्मन्न् एवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::110.verse_hindi: हे ब्रह्मन् ! हेय और उपादेय के वियोग से जो हर्ष और विषाद होता है उसके अभाव में अब मैं जैसा हूँ वैसा ही स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::110.english_translation: O Brahman! Without the separation of what is to be rejected and what is to be embraced, I remain as I am now.
ashtavakra_gita::110.translation_literal: हे (O) / ब्रह्मन् (Brahman) / हेय (to be rejected) / उपादेय (to be embraced) / विरहाद् (separation from) / एवं (thus) / हर्ष (joy) / विषादयोः (and sorrow) / अभावात् (because of absence) / अद्य (now) / हे (O) / ब्रह्मन् (Brahman) / एवमेव (just like this) / अहम् (I) / आसितः (remain/stay)
ashtavakra_gita::110.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::110.essence: True steadiness arises when you stop separating your experience into accepted and rejected parts.
ashtavakra_gita::110.simple_meaning: When you stop dividing your experiences into what you want and what you reject, you remain peaceful and steady as you are.
ashtavakra_gita::110.simple_insight: You can feel steady and whole by letting go of dividing experiences into good and bad.
ashtavakra_gita::110.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Brahman, explaining that by no longer separating experiences into things to accept or reject, like joy or sorrow, one remains steady and unchanged in their true nature.
ashtavakra_gita::110.modern_relevance: You notice your mood swings when you label moments as good or bad; this teaches how to stay unshaken by releasing those judgments.
ashtavakra_gita::110.insight: It shifts your mind from reacting to experiences as good or bad to resting in unshaken presence beyond those labels.

ashtavakra_gita::111.verse_sanskrit:
आश्रमानाश्रमं ध्यानं चित्तस्वीकृतवर्जनम् ।
विकल्पं मम वीक्ष्यैतैरेवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::111.verse_hindi: आश्रम एवं अनाश्रम है, ध्यान है तथा चित्त का स्वीकार और वर्जन है । उन सबसे उत्पन्न हुए अपने विकल्प को देखकर मैं उन तीनों से मुक्त हुआ स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::111.english_translation: The hermitage and non-hermitage, meditation, acceptance and rejection of the mind—seeing these choices arise, I remain free from all three.
ashtavakra_gita::111.translation_literal: आश्रमानाश्रमं (hermitage and non-hermitage) / ध्यानं (meditation) / चित्तस्वीकृतवर्जनम् (mind's acceptance and rejection) / विकल्पं (choices) / मम (my) / वीक्ष्य (seeing) / एतैः (by these) / एवमेव (thus indeed) / अहम् (I) / आस्थितः (established)
ashtavakra_gita::111.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::111.essence: Freedom comes from watching mental choices without identifying with them.
ashtavakra_gita::111.simple_meaning: You can see all mental choices and states arise—like hermitage, meditation, acceptance, and rejection—and remain untouched by them, resting in freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::111.simple_insight: There is peace in realizing you don’t have to be caught by any mental choice.
ashtavakra_gita::111.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes how even concepts like living in hermitage or meditation, or accepting and rejecting thoughts, arise as mental choices. Observing them without attachment lets the true self remain free and unbound.
ashtavakra_gita::111.modern_relevance: When your mind flips between decisions or moods, this teaching invites you to watch without getting caught or overwhelmed.
ashtavakra_gita::111.insight: It shifts your attention from identifying with mental preferences to witnessing them dispassionately, creating inner freedom.

ashtavakra_gita::112.verse_hindi: जैसे कर्म का अनुष्ठान अज्ञान से है, वैसे ही उसके त्याग का अनुष्ठान भी अज्ञान से है । इस तत्व को भली भाँति जानकर मैं कर्म अकर्म से मुक्त हुआ अपने में स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::112.english_translation: Just as performing actions arises from ignorance, so does renouncing actions; knowing this truth well, I remain established beyond action and inaction.
ashtavakra_gita::112.translation_literal: कर्मानुष्ठानमज्ञानाद् (action performance from ignorance) / यथैव (just as) / उपरमस्तथा (renunciation also) / बुध्वा (knowing) / सम्यक् (well) / इदं (this) / तत्त्वम् (truth) / एव (indeed) / एव (only) / अहम् (I) / आस्थितः (established).
ashtavakra_gita::112.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::112.essence: Freedom lies beyond both action and renunciation, both born of ignorance.
ashtavakra_gita::112.simple_meaning: Both doing actions and giving them up come from not knowing. Understanding this, you stand free beyond action and inaction.
ashtavakra_gita::112.simple_insight: You feel relief knowing freedom lies beyond all doing and not doing.
ashtavakra_gita::112.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that both performing actions and renouncing them originate in ignorance. He explains that truly knowing this truth frees you from being caught in either, standing established beyond both.
ashtavakra_gita::112.modern_relevance: You struggle between pushing forward and giving up, not seeing both come from the same confusion. Recognizing this frees your mind.
ashtavakra_gita::112.insight: It shifts your view from opposing action and renunciation to seeing both as rooted in the same confusion, freeing you to rest beyond them.

ashtavakra_gita::113.verse_sanskrit:
अचिन्त्यं चिन्त्यमानोऽपि चिन्तारूपं भजत्यसौ ।
त्यक्त्वा तद्भावनं तस्माद् एवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::113.verse_hindi: अचिन्त्य का चिन्तन करता हुआ भी वह पुरुष चिन्ता को ही भजता है । इसलिए उस भाव को त्यागकर मैं भावनामुक्त हुआ स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::113.english_translation: Even when contemplating the inconceivable, that person worships only the form of thought. Therefore, having abandoned that contemplation, I remain established free from all mental formations.
ashtavakra_gita::113.translation_literal: अचिन्त्यं (inconceivable) चिन्त्यमानोऽपि (even while contemplating) चिन्तारूपं (form of thought) भजत्यसौ (that person worships). त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) तद्भावनं (that contemplation) तस्माद् (therefore) एवमेव (thus indeed) अहम् (I) आस्थितः (established).
ashtavakra_gita::113.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::113.essence: True freedom arises by abandoning even the deepest engagement with thought.
ashtavakra_gita::113.simple_meaning: Even focusing deeply on the unthinkable still ties you to thought. True freedom comes from letting go of even that.
ashtavakra_gita::113.simple_insight: Relief grows when you stop chasing even your highest ideas.
ashtavakra_gita::113.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra reveals that a person who tries to grasp the inconceivable with thought remains caught in mental patterns. He explains that abandoning even this intense focus leads to a state free from all mental formations.
ashtavakra_gita::113.modern_relevance: You might find yourself obsessing over a complex problem or idea, trying to figure it all out. This verse invites you to release that effort and find peace beyond thinking.
ashtavakra_gita::113.insight: It teaches you to recognize when deep contemplation becomes another form of attachment and shift towards release.

ashtavakra_gita::114.verse_sanskrit:
एवमेव कृतं येन स कृतार्थो भवेदसौ ।
एवमेव स्वभावो यः स कृतार्थो भवेदसौ ॥
ashtavakra_gita::114.verse_hindi: जिसने साधनों से क्रियारहित स्वरूप अर्जित किया है – वह पुरुष कृतकृत्य है और जो ऐसा ही स्वभाव वाला है वह तो कृतकृत्य है ही, इसमें कहना ही क्या।
ashtavakra_gita::114.english_translation: One who has attained a natural state beyond action is truly fulfilled; and one whose nature is such is indeed fulfilled, needless to say.
ashtavakra_gita::114.translation_literal: एवमेव (just so) / कृतं (done) / येन (by whom) / स (that one) / कृतार्थो (fulfilled) / भवेदसौ (becomes) । / एवमेव (just so) / स्वभावो (nature) / यः (who) / स (that one) / कृतार्थो (fulfilled) / भवेदसौ (becomes) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::114.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::114.essence: True fulfillment arises when your nature is free from all action.
ashtavakra_gita::114.simple_meaning: You become truly fulfilled when you reach a natural state beyond all actions and effort. When your nature itself is free from doing, you are complete.
ashtavakra_gita::114.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing true fulfillment comes from being, not doing.
ashtavakra_gita::114.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a person who has transcended all effort and action and rests in their natural state is fully accomplished. This is not about what is done, but about who one is at the core — a state beyond doing.
ashtavakra_gita::114.modern_relevance: You feel fulfilled not when checking off tasks, but when you rest as your true self beyond effort and striving.
ashtavakra_gita::114.insight: It shifts focus from actions performed to the natural state of being fulfilled without doing.

ashtavakra_gita::115.verse_sanskrit:
अकिञ्चनभवं स्वास्थं कौपीनत्वेऽपि दुर्लभम् ।
त्यागादाने विहायास्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::115.verse_hindi: है कुछ भी – ऐसे भाव से पैदा हुआ जो स्वास्थ्य है वह कोपीन को धारण करने पर भी दुर्लभ है । इसलिए त्याग और ग्रहण दोनों को छोड़कर मैं सुखपूर्वक स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::115.english_translation: Being without attachment, I remain happily established, even while wearing a loincloth, which is rare to find.
ashtavakra_gita::115.translation_literal: अकिञ्चनभवं (being without attachment) / स्वास्थं (established) / कौपीनत्वेऽपि (even in the state of wearing a loincloth) / दुर्लभम् (rare) / त्यागादाने (from giving up and taking) / विहाय (leaving aside) / अस्मात् (from this) / अहम् (I) / आसे (am) / यथा सुखम् (as comfortably)
ashtavakra_gita::115.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::115.essence: You can be happily settled by giving up both craving and rejection.
ashtavakra_gita::115.simple_meaning: You can stay happily settled without grasping or pushing away anything, even with very little.
ashtavakra_gita::115.simple_insight: Peace grows when you stop clinging or resisting and simply rest in what is.
ashtavakra_gita::115.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that true contentment does not depend on possessions or comfort. Wearing only a loincloth, a symbol of minimalism, he reveals that by abandoning both desire to take and to give, he remains peacefully established.
ashtavakra_gita::115.modern_relevance: When your phone dies and you have no backup, yet you feel calm and okay without needing more.
ashtavakra_gita::115.insight: It shifts your mindset from reacting to circumstances toward resting quietly in acceptance beyond desire and aversion.

ashtavakra_gita::116.verse_sanskrit:
कुत्रापि खेदः कायस्य जिह्वा कुत्रापि खेद्यते ।
मनः कुत्रापि तत्त्यक्त्वा पुरुषार्थे स्थितः सुखम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::116.verse_hindi: कहीं तो शरीर का दुःख है, कहीं वाणी दुःखी है, कहीं मन दुःखी होता है । इसलिए तीनों को त्यागकर मैं पुरुषार्थ में सुखपूर्वक स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::116.english_translation: The body suffers in some place, the speech suffers elsewhere, and the mind suffers somewhere else; abandoning all three, I remain happily established in true purpose.
ashtavakra_gita::116.translation_literal: कुत्रापि (somewhere) खेदः (suffering) कायस्य (of the body) जिह्वा (tongue/speech) कुत्रापि (somewhere) खेद्यते (suffers) मनः (mind) कुत्रापि (somewhere) तत् (that) त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) पुरुषार्थे (in true purpose) स्थितः (established) सुखम् (happiness)
ashtavakra_gita::116.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::116.essence: You find true happiness by letting go of suffering in body, speech, and mind.
ashtavakra_gita::116.simple_meaning: The body, speech, and mind each experience suffering in different ways. By letting go of attachment to all three, you remain happily established in your true purpose.
ashtavakra_gita::116.simple_insight: Freedom arises when you stop identifying with body, speech, and mind, resting in deeper purpose.
ashtavakra_gita::116.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that suffering appears through the body, speech, and mind in different ways. By abandoning attachment to these, one stays happily rooted in the true purpose (Purusha-artha), beyond temporary pains and distractions.
ashtavakra_gita::116.modern_relevance: You feel stress in your body, frustration in your words, and unrest in your mind. Letting go of identifying with all these brings calm and focus.
ashtavakra_gita::116.insight: It teaches you to shift attention from transient pains of body, speech, and mind to abiding in your deeper purpose.

ashtavakra_gita::117.verse_sanskrit:
कृतं किमपि नैव स्याद् इति सञ्चिन्त्य तत्त्वतः ।
यदा यत्कर्तुमायाति तत् कृत्वासे यथासुखम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::117.verse_hindi: किया हुआ कर्म कुछ भी वास्तव में आत्मकृत नहीं होता । ऐसा यथार्थ विचारकर मैं जब जो कुछ कर्म करने को आ पड़ता है उसे करके सुखपूर्वक स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::117.english_translation: No action done is truly your own; understanding this, do whatever must be done with ease and contentment.
ashtavakra_gita::117.translation_literal: कृतं (done) / किमपि (anything) / नैव (not at all) / स्याद् (would be) / इति (thus) / सञ्चिन्त्य (considering) / तत्त्वतः (in truth) / यदा (when) / यत् (whatever) / कर्तुम् (to do) / आयाति (comes) / तत् (that) / कृत्वासे (having done) / यथा (as) / सुखम् (comfortably)
ashtavakra_gita::117.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::117.essence: No action is truly yours; act calmly with that understanding.
ashtavakra_gita::117.simple_meaning: No action you do is truly owned by you; when you understand this, you can act with comfort and ease.
ashtavakra_gita::117.simple_insight: You can feel peaceful doing what comes without clinging to ownership of results.
ashtavakra_gita::117.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that although actions arise, none are truly 'yours' in essence. Understanding this frees King Janaka to act without tension or attachment, embracing whatever life requires with ease.
ashtavakra_gita::117.modern_relevance: You face unexpected tasks today. Realizing none belong fully to you lets you meet them calmly and without stress.
ashtavakra_gita::117.insight: This verse shifts focus from ownership of results to peaceful acceptance of necessary action.

ashtavakra_gita::118.verse_hindi: कर्म और निष्कर्म के बन्धन से संयुक्त भाव वाले शरीर में आसक्त जो योगी है मैं इस देह के संयोग वियोग से सर्वदा पृथक होने के कारण सुखपूर्वक स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::118.english_translation: I am free from attachment to action or inaction in this embodied state; unlike yogis attached to union or separation, I remain happily detached from both.
ashtavakra_gita::118.translation_literal: कर्मनैष्कर्म्यनिर्बन्धभावा (attachment to action or inaction, free from bondage) / देहस्थयोगिनः (yogis in the body) / संयोगायोगविरहादहमासे (I am apart from union and separation) / यथासुखम् (as happily as possible)
ashtavakra_gita::118.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::118.essence: True freedom comes from detaching equally from action and inaction.
ashtavakra_gita::118.simple_meaning: You can remain happily free by not being attached to doing or not doing, unlike those who cling to action or its opposite.
ashtavakra_gita::118.simple_insight: There is freedom and joy when you stop clinging to effort or its absence.
ashtavakra_gita::118.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that while many yogis get caught up in doing or avoiding actions, the true yogi stays detached from both, resting peacefully in the self beyond all attachments to the body or activity.
ashtavakra_gita::118.modern_relevance: You feel pressure to always be either productive or resting perfectly, but real ease comes when you release attachment to both states.
ashtavakra_gita::118.insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with action or inaction to abiding freely beyond both.

ashtavakra_gita::119.verse_sanskrit:
अर्थानर्थौ न मे स्थित्या गत्या न शयनेन वा ।
तिष्ठन् गच्छन् स्वपन् तस्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::119.verse_hindi: मुझको ठहरने से, चलने से या सोने से अर्थ या अनर्थ कुछ भी नहीं है । इस कारण ‘मैं’ ठहरता हुआ, जाता हुआ और सोता हुआ भी सुखपूर्वक स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::119.english_translation: Staying, moving, or sleeping brings me no gain or loss; therefore, I remain happy whether still, moving, or sleeping.
ashtavakra_gita::119.translation_literal: अर्थानर्थौ (gain or loss) / न (not) / मे (to me) / स्थित्या (by staying) / गत्या (by moving) / न (nor) / शयनेन (by sleeping) / वा (or) । तिष्ठन् (remaining) / गच्छन् (going) / स्वपन् (sleeping) / तस्मादहमासे (therefore I am) / यथासुखम् (as happy as possible) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::119.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::119.essence: True happiness remains steady regardless of activity or rest.
ashtavakra_gita::119.simple_meaning: You don’t gain or lose anything by staying still, moving, or sleeping. That’s why you can remain happy in all these states.
ashtavakra_gita::119.simple_insight: There’s comfort in knowing your peace doesn’t depend on activity or rest.
ashtavakra_gita::119.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains to King Janaka that his true happiness is unaffected by physical actions like standing, walking, or sleeping. This teaching reveals a deep equanimity beyond ordinary ups and downs.
ashtavakra_gita::119.modern_relevance: You feel restless switching between busy work and rest, but this teaches peace can remain unchanged through all your daily shifts.
ashtavakra_gita::119.insight: It shifts your focus from external activity to an inner steadiness that remains unshaken by changing states.

ashtavakra_gita::120.verse_sanskrit:
स्वपतो नास्ति मे हानिः सिद्धिर्यत्नवतो न वा ।
नाशोल्लासौ विहायास्मदहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::120.verse_hindi: सोते हुए मुझे हानि नहीं है, न यत्न करते हुए मुझे सिद्धि है । इसलिए मैं हानि-लाभ दोनों को छोड़कर सुखपूर्वक स्थित हूँ ।
ashtavakra_gita::120.english_translation: Sleeping does not harm me; striving does not grant me success. So I have abandoned both loss and gain and remain happily as I am.
ashtavakra_gita::120.translation_literal: स्वपतो (while sleeping) नास्ति (is not) मे (to me) हानिः (harm) सिद्धिर्यत्नवतो (success by effort) न (not) वा (either) । न (not) आश (loss) उल्लासौ (gain) विहाय (abandoning) अस्मदहमासे (I remain) यथा (just like) सुखम् (comfortable/happy) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::120.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::120.essence: True peace comes from releasing attachment to both effort and its results.
ashtavakra_gita::120.simple_meaning: Neither resting nor striving changes your true state. You can let go of both and be peacefully content.
ashtavakra_gita::120.simple_insight: You can feel peace by releasing the need for success or fearing loss.
ashtavakra_gita::120.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains to Janaka that neither sleep nor effort affects his true self. He has moved beyond concern for loss or gain and lives happily without attachment to results.
ashtavakra_gita::120.modern_relevance: After a long day of pushing yourself, you realize neither rest nor frantic effort truly changes your inner peace.
ashtavakra_gita::120.insight: It teaches you to stop equating your value with achievements or setbacks and to rest in contentment.

ashtavakra_gita::121.verse_sanskrit:
सुखादिरूपा नियमं भावेष्वालोक्य भूरिशः ।
शुभाशुभे विहायास्मादहमासे यथासुखम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::121.verse_hindi: इसलिए अनेक परिस्थितियों में सुखादि की अनित्यता को बारम्बार देखकर और शुभ और अशुभ दोनों को छोड़कर मैं सुखपूर्वक स्थित हूँ।
ashtavakra_gita::121.english_translation: Having repeatedly seen the impermanence of pleasure and pain in many states, I let go of good and bad and remain happily established.
ashtavakra_gita::121.translation_literal: सुखादि (pleasure and such) रूपा (formed as) नियमं (law/sequence) भावेषु (in feelings) आलोक्य (having observed) भूरिशः (repeatedly) । शुभाशुभे (good and bad) विहाय (having abandoned) अस्मात् (from this) अहम् (I) आसे (am) यथा (just as) सुखम् (happily) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::121.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::121.essence: True peace comes from releasing attachment to both pleasure and pain.
ashtavakra_gita::121.simple_meaning: When you notice how pleasure and pain always change, you can stop chasing good or avoiding bad and simply be peaceful.
ashtavakra_gita::121.simple_insight: There’s relief in not clinging to either pleasure or pain, allowing calm happiness to settle in.
ashtavakra_gita::121.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that after witnessing many cycles of pleasure and pain, and seeing they don’t last, one can let go of labeling experiences as good or bad and rest in a natural peaceful state.
ashtavakra_gita::121.modern_relevance: You’ve felt excitement fade or discomfort pass, and finally stop reacting, just resting calmly without chasing highs or fearing lows.
ashtavakra_gita::121.insight: It teaches you to stop judging your experiences as good or bad and to stay peacefully aware instead.

ashtavakra_gita::122.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकृत्या शून्यचित्तो यः प्रमादाद् भावभावनः ।
निद्रितो बोधित इव क्षीणसंस्मरणो हि सः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::122.verse_hindi: स्वभाव से ही शून्य चित्त है पर प्रमाद से विषयों की भावना करता है और सोता हुआ भी जागने के समान है – वह पुरुष संसार से मुक्त है।
ashtavakra_gita::122.english_translation: By nature, the mind is empty, but through carelessness, it creates feelings about objects; even in sleep, if one remains aware, they are free from the cycle of reactivity.
ashtavakra_gita::122.translation_literal: प्रकृत्या (by nature) शून्यचित्तो (empty-minded) यः (who) प्रमादाद् (due to carelessness) भावभावनः (feeling sensations) । निद्रितो (sleeping) बोधित (awake) इव (like) क्षीणसंस्मरणो (diminished memory) हि (indeed) सः (he) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::122.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::122.essence: The mind is naturally empty; carelessness fills it with restless feelings.
ashtavakra_gita::122.simple_meaning: Your natural mind is empty and calm. Carelessness causes it to create feelings and distractions, but even in sleep, awareness means freedom from reactivity.
ashtavakra_gita::122.simple_insight: You can rest in your natural emptiness instead of getting caught in restless feelings.
ashtavakra_gita::122.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the true nature of the mind is emptiness, free from thoughts and feelings. Carelessness causes the mind to latch onto objects and create emotional reactions. Yet even while physically asleep, if awareness remains, one is free from the cycle of reactive suffering.
ashtavakra_gita::122.modern_relevance: When your mind drifts into worry or distraction, remember its true nature is empty and calm—staying aware is freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::122.insight: It teaches you to recognize carelessness as the cause of mental agitation and to nurture awareness even in passive states.

ashtavakra_gita::123.verse_sanskrit:
क्व धनानि क्व मित्राणि क्व मे विषयदस्यवः ।
क्व शास्त्रं क्व च विज्ञानं यदा मे गलिता स्पृहा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::123.verse_hindi: जब मेरी स्पृहा नष्ट हो गयी तब मेरे लिए कहाँ धन, कहाँ मित्र, कहाँ विषयीरूप चोर, कहाँ शास्त्र और कहाँ ज्ञान है।
ashtavakra_gita::123.english_translation: When my desire was destroyed, then where were wealth, friends, sensual thieves, scriptures, and knowledge for me?
ashtavakra_gita::123.translation_literal: क्व (where) धनानि (wealth) क्व (where) मित्राणि (friends) क्व (where) मे (my) विषयदस्यवः (thieves of senses) । क्व (where) शास्त्रं (scripture) क्व (where) च (and) विज्ञानं (knowledge) यदा (when) मे (my) गलिता (destroyed) स्पृहा (desire) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::123.speaker: Janaka
ashtavakra_gita::123.essence: Without desire, all attachments including wealth and knowledge lose their grip.
ashtavakra_gita::123.simple_meaning: When your craving or desire disappears, things like money, friends, sensual distractions, scriptures, and knowledge lose their importance to you.
ashtavakra_gita::123.simple_insight: There is freedom in letting go of craving; then nothing outside can control you.
ashtavakra_gita::123.detailed_meaning: King Janaka reflects on how when his desires were extinguished, worldly things such as wealth, friends, sensual temptations, scriptures, and knowledge lost their significance for him, revealing a deep detachment.
ashtavakra_gita::123.modern_relevance: You finally stop chasing likes, money, or approval—suddenly, all those things feel empty and irrelevant.
ashtavakra_gita::123.insight: It teaches you to see desire as the root of attachment, so letting it go frees you from external dependencies.

ashtavakra_gita::124.verse_sanskrit:
विज्ञाते साक्षिपुरुषे परमात्मनि चेश्वरे ।
नैराश्ये बन्धमोक्षे च न चिन्ता मुक्तये मम ॥
ashtavakra_gita::124.verse_hindi: साक्षी पुरुष, परमात्मा, ईश्वर, आशा-मुक्ति तथा बन्ध-मुक्ति के जान लेने पर मुझे मुक्ति के लिए चिन्ता नहीं है।
ashtavakra_gita::124.english_translation: Knowing the witness, the pure awareness, the supreme being, and the lord, I have no worry about liberation or bondage.
ashtavakra_gita::124.translation_literal: विज्ञाते (knowing) साक्षिपुरुषे (the witness-person) परमात्मनि (the supreme being) चेश्वरे (and the lord) । नैराश्ये (no despair) बन्धमोक्षे (bondage and liberation) च (and) न (no) चिन्ता (worry) मुक्तये (for liberation) मम (my) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::124.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::124.essence: Knowing your true self as witness ends all worry about bondage and freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::124.simple_meaning: When you understand your true self as the witness and the supreme being, you stop worrying about being bound or free.
ashtavakra_gita::124.simple_insight: You feel calm and unshaken because the fear of being trapped or needing freedom fades away.
ashtavakra_gita::124.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that recognizing yourself as the pure witness and the supreme reality removes all anxiety about being stuck in bondage or seeking liberation. This deep insight comes in a moment of clarity about the nature of the self and the divine.
ashtavakra_gita::124.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by endless worries about success or failure, but realizing your deeper awareness dissolves all that anxiety.
ashtavakra_gita::124.insight: It shifts your focus from fearing entrapment or chasing freedom to simply knowing your true self beyond those states.

ashtavakra_gita::125.verse_sanskrit:
अन्तर्विकल्पशून्यस्य बहिः स्वच्छन्दचारिणः ।
भ्रान्तस्येव दशास्तास्तास्तादृशा एव जानते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::125.verse_hindi: जो भीतर विकल्प से शून्य है और बाहर भ्रान्त हुए पुरुष की भाँति स्वछन्दचारी है । ऐसे पुरुष की भिन्न-भिन्न दशाओं को वैसी ही दशा वाले पुरुष जानते हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::125.english_translation: The one who is free of inner doubt and moves freely outside is known by others who share the same state.
ashtavakra_gita::125.translation_literal: अन्तर्विकल्पशून्यस्य (inside without doubt) बहिः (outside) स्वच्छन्दचारिणः (free-moving) । भ्रान्तस्येव (of the deluded only) दशास्तास्तास्तादृशा (the states like these) एव (indeed) जानते (know) ।
ashtavakra_gita::125.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::125.essence: Only those free inside can truly recognize freedom in others.
ashtavakra_gita::125.simple_meaning: A person whose mind is free of inner doubts moves freely in the world and is recognized by others who share that same freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::125.simple_insight: Knowing yourself clearly lets you connect deeply with those who are like you.
ashtavakra_gita::125.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes a person free from inner confusion who acts spontaneously in the world. Such a person’s state is only truly known by others who have reached the same clarity and freedom, highlighting shared direct experience beyond words.
ashtavakra_gita::125.modern_relevance: You feel completely calm inside and act without hesitation, and others who have found that same calm recognize you instantly.
ashtavakra_gita::125.insight: It teaches you to see that authentic freedom is recognized only by those who have experienced it themselves.

ashtavakra_gita::126.verse_sanskrit:
यथातथोपदेशेन कृतार्थः सत्त्वबुद्धिमान् ।
आजीवमपि जिज्ञासुः परस्तत्र विमुह्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::126.verse_hindi: सत्व बुद्धि वाला पुरुष थोड़े से उपदेश से ही कृतार्थ होता है । असत् बुद्धि वाला पुरुष आजीवन जिज्ञासा करके उसमें मोह को ही प्राप्त होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::126.english_translation: A person with pure wisdom is fulfilled by little teaching; one with impure wisdom remains confused, endlessly seeking elsewhere.
ashtavakra_gita::126.translation_literal: यथा (as) / तथा (so) / उपदेशेन (by teaching) / कृतार्थः (fulfilled) / सत्त्वबुद्धिमान् (one with pure wisdom) / आजीवमपि (even lifelong) / जिज्ञासुः (one who inquires) / परस्तत्र (elsewhere) / विमुह्यति (becomes confused)
ashtavakra_gita::126.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::126.essence: Clear wisdom quickly fulfills; confusion endlessly chases more and more.
ashtavakra_gita::126.simple_meaning: Some people grasp wisdom quickly from few teachings, but others stay confused, searching endlessly for answers.
ashtavakra_gita::126.simple_insight: You can feel peaceful when your wisdom settles, not restless chasing more knowledge.
ashtavakra_gita::126.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that a person with steady, clear understanding feels fulfilled with even small guidance. Another, with unclear mind, keeps searching for truth elsewhere but remains confused and unsettled.
ashtavakra_gita::126.modern_relevance: You’ve sat through many talks and read many books but still feel lost; sometimes clarity arrives simply, not from endless searching.
ashtavakra_gita::126.insight: It shifts your effort from gathering more information to trusting simple, clear insights that satisfy your mind.

ashtavakra_gita::127.verse_sanskrit:
मोक्षो विषयवैरस्यं बन्धो वैषयिको रसः ।
एतावदेव विज्ञानं यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
ashtavakra_gita::127.verse_hindi: विषयों में विरसता मोक्ष है, विषयों में रस बन्ध है । इतना ही विज्ञान है । तू जैसा चाहे वैसा कर।
ashtavakra_gita::127.english_translation: Freedom is finding disinterest in pleasures; attachment to them is bondage. This much is true knowledge. Do as you wish.
ashtavakra_gita::127.translation_literal: मोक्षो (freedom) विषयवैरस्यं (disinterest in pleasures) बन्धो (bondage) वैषयिको (sensory) रसः (attachment). एतावदेव (this much only) विज्ञानं (knowledge) यथेच्छसि (as you wish) तथा (so) कुरु (do).
ashtavakra_gita::127.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::127.essence: Freedom is the disinterest in sensory pleasures; attachment creates bondage.
ashtavakra_gita::127.simple_meaning: True freedom comes when you stop craving pleasures; being attached to them keeps you bound. Understand this and act as you wish.
ashtavakra_gita::127.simple_insight: You feel relief knowing freedom is within your choice to care or not.
ashtavakra_gita::127.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains to King Janaka that freedom arises from losing interest in sensory pleasures, while attachment to them causes bondage. This simple knowledge is enough; Janaka is free to act as he wishes.
ashtavakra_gita::127.modern_relevance: You scroll endlessly for likes or feel restless chasing pleasures, yet peace comes when these cravings lose their grip.
ashtavakra_gita::127.insight: It shifts your mindset from chasing pleasure to choosing freedom by releasing interest in outcomes.

ashtavakra_gita::128.verse_sanskrit:
वाग्मिप्राज्ञामहोद्योगं जनं मूकजडालसम् ।
करोति तत्त्वबोधोऽयमतस्त्यक्तो बुभुक्षभिः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::128.verse_hindi: यह तत्व बोध वाचाल, बुद्धिमान और महाउद्योगी पुरुष को गूँगा, जड़ और आलसी कर जाता है । इसलिए भोग की अभिलाषा रखने वालों के द्वारा तत्व-बोध त्यक्त है।
ashtavakra_gita::128.english_translation: This knowledge of truth makes the eloquent, wise, and diligent man mute, inert, and lazy; therefore, those craving sensory pleasures abandon this knowledge.
ashtavakra_gita::128.translation_literal: वाग्मि (eloquent) / प्राज्ञ (wise) / अमहोद्योगं (greatly diligent) / जनं (person) / मूक (mute) / जड (inert) / आलसम् (lazy) / करोति (makes) / तत्त्वबोधः (knowledge of truth) / अयम् (this) / तस्मात् (therefore) / त्यक्तः (abandoned) / बुभुक्षभिः (by those craving pleasures)
ashtavakra_gita::128.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::128.essence: Profound truth silences the restless mind and dims craving for sensory pleasures.
ashtavakra_gita::128.simple_meaning: Deep understanding of truth can make even the most active and clever person quiet and inactive because it lessens desire for pleasures.
ashtavakra_gita::128.simple_insight: There is calm in letting go of cravings, even if it feels like losing your drive.
ashtavakra_gita::128.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that true knowledge of reality quiets the mind and reduces the urge to chase pleasures. Even those known for their eloquence and energy become still, as desire loses its power.
ashtavakra_gita::128.modern_relevance: You push yourself hard chasing success and distractions, but true insight can make you pause, slowing your restless striving for fleeting rewards.
ashtavakra_gita::128.insight: Shift your focus from constant doing and craving to deep knowing that naturally reduces restless activity.

ashtavakra_gita::129.verse_sanskrit:
न त्वं देहो न ते देहो भोक्ता कर्ता न वा भवान् ।
चिद्रूपोऽसि सदा साक्षी निरपेक्षः सुखं चर ॥
ashtavakra_gita::129.verse_hindi: तू शरीर नहीं है, न तेरा शरीर है, तू भोक्ता और कर्ता भी नहीं है । तू वो चैतन्यरूप है, नित्य है, साक्षी है, निरपेक्ष है । तू सुखपूर्वक विचर।
ashtavakra_gita::129.english_translation: You are not the body, nor is the body yours; you are neither the experiencer nor the doer. You are the consciousness itself, always the witness, impartial, and moving in bliss.
ashtavakra_gita::129.translation_literal: न (not) / त्वं (you) / देहो (body) / न (not) / ते (your) / देहो (body) / भोक्ता (experiencer) / कर्ता (doer) / न (not) / वा (also) / भवान् (you) । / चिद्रूपोऽसि (are consciousness-form) / सदा (always) / साक्षी (witness) / निरपेक्षः (impartial) / सुखं (blissful) / चर (move) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::129.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::129.essence: You are pure awareness, never the body or its doer, always peacefully witnessing.
ashtavakra_gita::129.simple_meaning: You are not your body, nor the one who acts or experiences. You are pure consciousness, always watching calmly and enjoying peace.
ashtavakra_gita::129.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing your true self is untouched by pain or action.
ashtavakra_gita::129.detailed_meaning: At this moment, Ashtavakra teaches King Janaka that the true self is not the physical body or the doer of actions, but eternal consciousness that witnesses all without attachment or bias, living in bliss.
ashtavakra_gita::129.modern_relevance: When stress hits, notice how the restless mind is not really you but just passing. Your true self stays calm beyond all that.
ashtavakra_gita::129.insight: It shifts your focus from identifying with body and roles to recognizing yourself as the impartial observer beneath all experiences.

ashtavakra_gita::130.verse_sanskrit:
रागद्वेषौ मनोधर्मौ न मनस्ते कदाचन ।
निर्विकल्पोऽसि बोधात्मा निर्विकारः सुखं चर ॥
ashtavakra_gita::130.verse_hindi: राग और द्वेष मन के धर्म हैं । तू कभी मन नहीं है । तू निर्विकल्प, निर्विकार, बोध-स्वरूप आत्मा है । तू सुखपूर्वक विचर।
ashtavakra_gita::130.english_translation: Attachment and aversion are qualities of the mind. You are never the mind. You are the awareness beyond distinctions and changes, dwelling in peaceful bliss.
ashtavakra_gita::130.translation_literal: राग (attachment) / द्वेष (aversion) / मन (mind) / धर्मौ (qualities) / न (not) / मनस् (mind) / ते (your) / कदाचन (ever) / निर्विकल्पः (without distinctions) / असि (are) / बोधात्मा (awareness-self) / निर्विकारः (unchanging) / सुखं (blissful) / चर (dwell)
ashtavakra_gita::130.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::130.essence: You are unchanging awareness, not the ever-changing mind with its likes and dislikes.
ashtavakra_gita::130.simple_meaning: Attachment and aversion arise in the mind, but you are not the mind. You are the unchanging awareness that experiences peaceful happiness.
ashtavakra_gita::130.simple_insight: You can find peace by recognizing you are not the restless mind but the calm awareness behind it.
ashtavakra_gita::130.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra tells Janaka that feelings like attachment and aversion belong to the restless mind, which is always changing. The true self is pure awareness, unchanged and peaceful, not caught up in these mental fluctuations.
ashtavakra_gita::130.modern_relevance: When your emotions swing between liking and disliking, remember you are the calm that notices these shifts, not the shifts themselves.
ashtavakra_gita::130.insight: It teaches you to separate your sense of self from the mind’s emotional ups and downs, resting as the witness instead.

ashtavakra_gita::131.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि ।
विज्ञाय निरहङ्कारो निर्ममस्त्वं सुखी भव ॥
ashtavakra_gita::131.verse_hindi: सब भूतों में आत्म को तथा सब भूतों में आत्मा को जानकर तू अहँकाररहित और ममता रहित है । तू सुखी हो।
ashtavakra_gita::131.english_translation: Knowing the true self in all beings and all beings in the true self, be free from ego and possessiveness; be happy.
ashtavakra_gita::131.translation_literal: सर्वभूतेषु (in all beings) / चात्मानं (the true self) / सर्वभूतानि (all beings) / चात्मनि (in the true self) / । (.) / विज्ञाय (knowing) / निरहङ्कारो (ego-free) / निर्ममः (without possessiveness) / त्वं (you) / सुखी (happy) / भव (be)
ashtavakra_gita::131.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::131.essence: True happiness arises when you know yourself as one with all, free from ego and possessiveness.
ashtavakra_gita::131.simple_meaning: Recognize that your true self is present in all beings and all beings exist in your true self. This understanding frees you from ego and possessiveness and brings happiness.
ashtavakra_gita::131.simple_insight: Knowing your unity with all beings brings freedom from ego and a peaceful happiness.
ashtavakra_gita::131.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that realization of the true self's presence in every being and the presence of all beings in that self dissolves ego and attachment. This insight comes as a key turning point to lasting happiness beyond personal identity.
ashtavakra_gita::131.modern_relevance: When you stop seeing others as separate and stop clinging to your identity, you find relief from jealousy, competition, and loneliness.
ashtavakra_gita::131.insight: Shift from seeing yourself as isolated to recognizing your shared true self with all beings, dissolving ego and possessiveness.

ashtavakra_gita::132.verse_sanskrit:
विश्वं स्फुरति यत्रेदं तरङ्गा इव सागरे ।
तत्त्वमेव न सन्देहश्चिन्मूर्ते विज्वरो भव ॥
ashtavakra_gita::132.verse_hindi: जिसमें यह संसार तरंगों की भाँति स्फुरित होता है वह तू ही है, इसमें सन्देह नहीं है । हे चैतन्य स्वरूप ! तू सन्ताप रहित हो।
ashtavakra_gita::132.english_translation: You are the one in whom this entire world shines like waves in the ocean; there is no doubt about this. O embodiment of pure awareness, you are beyond suffering.
ashtavakra_gita::132.translation_literal: विश्वं (world) स्फुरति (shines) यत्रेतं (where this) तरङ्गा (waves) इव (like) सागरे (in the ocean) । तत्त्वमेव (the essence alone) न (not) सन्देहश्च (doubt also) चिन्मूर्ते (O consciousness-embodiment) विज्वरो (free from suffering) भव (be) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::132.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::132.essence: You are the unchanging ocean in which the world’s waves rise and fall without disturbing you.
ashtavakra_gita::132.simple_meaning: The entire world appears like waves on the ocean, but you are the ocean itself—pure awareness without suffering.
ashtavakra_gita::132.simple_insight: You can feel deep peace knowing your true nature is calm and untouched by pain.
ashtavakra_gita::132.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the world is like waves arising on the vast ocean of consciousness. The true self is that ocean—unchanged and free from suffering—while waves are temporary appearances.
ashtavakra_gita::132.modern_relevance: When stress and change feel overwhelming, remember you are the calm, vast presence beneath the shifting surface.
ashtavakra_gita::132.insight: Shift your focus from fleeting experiences to your unchanging awareness, finding freedom from emotional turmoil.

ashtavakra_gita::133.verse_sanskrit:
श्रद्धस्व तात श्रद्धस्व नात्र मोऽहं कुरुष्व भोः ।
ज्ञानस्वरूपो भगवानात्मा त्वं प्रकृतेः परः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::133.verse_hindi: हे तात ! श्रद्धा कर, श्रद्धा कर । इसमें मोह मत कर । तू ज्ञानस्वरूप, भगवान्-स्वरूप आत्मा है तथा प्रकृति से परे है।
ashtavakra_gita::133.english_translation: Have faith, son, have faith; do not be confused. You are the true self, embodying wisdom and beyond the natural world.
ashtavakra_gita::133.translation_literal: श्रद्धस्व (have faith) तात (son) श्रद्धस्व (have faith) नात्र (here not) मोऽहं (confusion) कुरुष्व (do) भोः (oh) । ज्ञानस्वरूपो (embodiment of knowledge) भगवानात्मा (divine true self) त्वं (you) प्रकृतेः (of nature) परः (beyond) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::133.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::133.essence: You are pure wisdom beyond nature; trust removes all confusion.
ashtavakra_gita::133.simple_meaning: You are urged to have faith without confusion because your true nature is wisdom itself and beyond the changing natural world.
ashtavakra_gita::133.simple_insight: There is calm in trusting your deeper self beyond the doubts and illusions.
ashtavakra_gita::133.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra instructs King Janaka to cultivate faith and avoid confusion, reminding him that his true nature is pure wisdom and beyond the limits of the natural world, pointing to a profound spiritual identity.
ashtavakra_gita::133.modern_relevance: When your mind is restless and confused, trust the deeper wisdom within you that is untouched by everyday worries.
ashtavakra_gita::133.insight: It teaches you to replace doubt with trust in the true self beyond appearances and distractions.

ashtavakra_gita::134.verse_sanskrit:
गुणैः संवेष्टितो देहस्तिष्ठत्यायाति याति च ।
आत्मा न गन्ता नागन्ता किमेनमनुशोचसि ॥
ashtavakra_gita::134.verse_hindi: गुणों से लिप्त यह शरीर रहता है, आता है और जाता है । किन्तु आत्मा न जाने वाला है, न आने वाला । इसके लिए क्यों सोच करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::134.english_translation: The body, covered by qualities, stays, comes, and goes; the true self neither comes nor goes. Why do you grieve over this?
ashtavakra_gita::134.translation_literal: गुणैः (by qualities) संवेष्टितो (covered) देहः (body) तिष्ठति (remains) आयाति (comes) याति (goes) च (and) । आत्मा (the true self) न (not) गन्ता (going) न (not) अगन्ता (coming) किम् (why) एतत् (this) मनः (mind) अशोचसि (do you grieve) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::134.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::134.essence: Your true self remains unchanged while the body moves and changes; grief is unnecessary.
ashtavakra_gita::134.simple_meaning: Your body changes and moves, but your true self remains unchanged and does not come or go. There is no need to grieve over what is always steady.
ashtavakra_gita::134.simple_insight: You can find peace knowing your true self is eternal beyond the body’s changes.
ashtavakra_gita::134.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches King Janaka that although the body is subject to qualities and constantly changes, the true self remains untouched and unmoving. This verse highlights the difference between the temporary body and the eternal self, inviting release from unnecessary sorrow.
ashtavakra_gita::134.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by life's ups and downs, remember your core self remains steady beyond all changes.
ashtavakra_gita::134.insight: Shift your focus from the changing body to the unchanging true self to reduce grief and attachment.

ashtavakra_gita::135.verse_sanskrit:
देहस्तिष्ठतु कल्पान्तं गच्छत्वद्यैव वा पुनः ।
क्व वृद्धिः क्व च वा हानिस्तव चिन्मात्ररूपिणः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::135.verse_hindi: देह चाहे अन्त तक रहे, चाहे वह अभी चली जाए, तुम चैतन्य-रूप वालों की कहाँ वृद्धि है, कहाँ नाश है।
ashtavakra_gita::135.english_translation: Whether the body remains until the end of an age or leaves now, where is increase or decrease for you, the one who is pure consciousness?
ashtavakra_gita::135.translation_literal: देहस्तिष्ठतु (body remains) / कल्पान्तं (until the end of an age) / गच्छत्वदि (goes now) / ऐव (indeed) / वा (or) / पुनः (again) / क्व (where) / वृद्धिः (increase) / क्व (where) / च (and) / वा (or) / हानिः (decrease) / तव (your) / चिन्मात्ररूपिणः (of pure consciousness form)
ashtavakra_gita::135.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::135.essence: Pure consciousness remains unchanged regardless of the body's coming and going.
ashtavakra_gita::135.simple_meaning: Your true nature as pure consciousness does not grow or diminish, even if your body changes or disappears.
