ashtavakra_gita::135.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing your true self is constant beyond physical change.
ashtavakra_gita::135.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra tells King Janaka that regardless of whether the body lasts a long time or leaves immediately, the true self—pure consciousness—is untouched by any increase or loss. This moment in their dialogue highlights the unchanging nature of awareness amid bodily change.
ashtavakra_gita::135.modern_relevance: You watch your body age or face illness, yet your inner awareness remains untouched and whole, beyond these shifts.
ashtavakra_gita::135.insight: It shifts your focus from physical identity to recognizing your unchanging inner being beyond appearances.

ashtavakra_gita::136.verse_sanskrit:
त्वय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्ववीचिः स्वभावतः ।
उदेतु वास्तमायातु न ते वृद्धिर्न वा क्षतिः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::136.verse_hindi: तुझ अनन्त महासमुद्र में विश्वरूप तरंग अपने स्वभाव से उदय और अस्त को प्राप्त होती है, किन्तु न तेरी वृद्धि है, न नाश है।
ashtavakra_gita::136.english_translation: In your infinite great ocean, the universal wave naturally rises and sets, yet it is neither your growth nor your decay.
ashtavakra_gita::136.translation_literal: त्वयि (in you) अनन्त (infinite) महाम्भोधौ (great ocean) विश्ववीचिः (universal wave) स्वभावतः (by nature) उदेतु (rises) वास्तु (exists) अयातु (sets) न (not) ते (your) वृद्धिः (growth) न (nor) वा (or) क्षतिः (decay)
ashtavakra_gita::136.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::136.essence: Your true self remains unchanged amid all natural changes around it.
ashtavakra_gita::136.simple_meaning: You are like an endless ocean where waves rise and fall naturally, but these changes do not affect your true nature.
ashtavakra_gita::136.simple_insight: There is calm in knowing your true self is untouched by life's ups and downs.
ashtavakra_gita::136.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains to King Janaka that the true self is like an infinite ocean. Though waves rise and fall on its surface, these movements do not alter the ocean itself. This shows the distinction between the changing world and the unchanging true self.
ashtavakra_gita::136.modern_relevance: When emotions or events surge and fade around you, your core remains steady beyond their ebb and flow.
ashtavakra_gita::136.insight: It teaches you to see yourself as the unchanging presence beneath all fluctuations and experiences.

ashtavakra_gita::137.verse_sanskrit:
तात चिन्मात्ररूपोऽसि न ते भिन्नमिदं जगत् ।
अतः कस्य कथं कुत्र हेयोपादेयकल्पना ॥
ashtavakra_gita::137.verse_hindi: हे तात ! तू चैतन्यरूप है, तेरा यह जगत तुझसे भिन्न नहीं है । इसलिये हेय और उपादेय की कल्पना किसकी, क्योंकर और कहाँ हो सकती है।
ashtavakra_gita::137.english_translation: Dear one, you are pure consciousness; this world is not separate from you. So who can be despised or praised, and where or why could such ideas arise?
ashtavakra_gita::137.translation_literal: तात (dear one) / चिन्मात्ररूपोऽसि (you are pure consciousness form) / न (not) / ते (your) / भिन्नम् (separate) / इदम् (this) / जगत् (world) / । / अतः (therefore) / कस्य (whose) / कथं (how) / कुत्र (where) / हेयः (despised) / उपादेयः (praised) / कल्पना (imagination) / ॥
ashtavakra_gita::137.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::137.essence: You are pure awareness; ideas of blame or praise arise only from false separation.
ashtavakra_gita::137.simple_meaning: You are pure awareness, and the world around you is not truly separate from your true self. Therefore, ideas of someone being worthy of blame or praise do not truly apply.
ashtavakra_gita::137.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing that separation and judgment are illusions born from misunderstanding your true nature.
ashtavakra_gita::137.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka, revealing that Janaka's true nature is pure consciousness. Since this true self and the world are not separate, the usual distinctions of blame or praise have no real basis. This challenges Janaka's assumptions and invites him to see beyond dualities.
ashtavakra_gita::137.modern_relevance: You might notice how quickly your mind judges others or situations as good or bad. This verse invites you to see that at the core, you and everything else share the same essence beyond those judgments.
ashtavakra_gita::137.insight: It teaches you to question the reality of separation and judgment, shifting your view to see unity beneath appearances.

ashtavakra_gita::138.verse_sanskrit:
एकस्मिन्नव्यये शान्ते चिदाकाशेऽमले त्वयि ।
कुतो जन्म कुतो कर्म कुतोऽहङ्कार एव च ॥
ashtavakra_gita::138.verse_hindi: तुझ एक निर्मल, अविनाशी, शान्त और चैतन्यरूप आकाश में कहाँ जन्म है, कहाँ कर्म है और कहाँ अहंकार।
ashtavakra_gita::138.english_translation: In you, the pure, unchanging, peaceful, and conscious sky, where is birth, where is action, and where is ego?
ashtavakra_gita::138.translation_literal: एकस्मिन् (in one) अव्यये (imperishable) शान्ते (peaceful) चिदाकाशे (conscious sky) अमले (pure) त्वयि (in you) कुतो (where) जन्म (birth) कुतो (where) कर्म (action) कुतो (where) अहङ्कार (ego) एव (indeed) च (also)
ashtavakra_gita::138.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::138.essence: Your true self is pure and peaceful, beyond birth, action, and ego.
ashtavakra_gita::138.simple_meaning: You are like a pure, peaceful, unchanging sky beyond birth, action, and ego.
ashtavakra_gita::138.simple_insight: You can feel freedom knowing your true self is untouched by life’s events or identity.
ashtavakra_gita::138.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the true self is like a pure, peaceful sky—unchanging and conscious—where birth, actions, and ego have no place. This insight challenges the common belief that these define who we are.
ashtavakra_gita::138.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your mistakes or identity, remember your deeper self is untouched and free like a clear sky.
ashtavakra_gita::138.insight: Recognize that your true self is distinct from birth, actions, and ego, freeing you from identification with them.

ashtavakra_gita::139.verse_sanskrit:
यत्त्वं पश्यसि तत्रैकस्त्वमेव प्रतिभाससे ।
किं पृथक् भासते स्वर्णात् कटकाङ्गदनूपुरम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::139.verse_hindi: जिसको तू देखता है, उसमें एक तू ही भासता है । क्या कंगन, बाजूबन्द और नूपुर सोने से भिन्न भासते है।
ashtavakra_gita::139.english_translation: What you see is only you shining there; do the golden bracelet, armlet, and anklet shine differently from gold?
ashtavakra_gita::139.translation_literal: यत् (that which) त्वं (you) पश्यसि (see) तत्र (there) एक (one) त्वम् (you) एव (indeed) प्रतिभाससे (shine) । किं (does) पृथक् (separately) भासते (shine) स्वर्णात् (from gold) कटकाङ्गदनूपुरम् (bracelet-armlet-anklet) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::139.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::139.essence: The same light shines through you and all you perceive; there is no real difference.
ashtavakra_gita::139.simple_meaning: Everything you see shines with the same light—you and all objects share that one radiance.
ashtavakra_gita::139.simple_insight: You feel the unity beneath many forms, a shared brightness connecting all you perceive.
ashtavakra_gita::139.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra tells Janaka that the self and all objects are not separate in their radiance; just as gold shines identically through jewelry, the true self shines through all appearances.
ashtavakra_gita::139.modern_relevance: When you look around, notice how the same awareness lights up your thoughts, feelings, and the world outside alike.
ashtavakra_gita::139.insight: It shifts your view from seeing things as separate to recognizing a single light animating all appearances.

ashtavakra_gita::140.verse_sanskrit:
अयं सोऽहमयं नाहं विभागमिति सन्त्यज ।
सर्वमात्मेति निश्चित्य निःसङ्कल्पः सुखी भव ॥
ashtavakra_gita::140.verse_hindi: ‘यह मैं हूँ’, ‘यह मैं नहीं हूँ’ ऐसे विभाग को छोड़ दे । ‘सब आत्मा है’ ऐसा निश्चय करके तू संकल्परहित हो, सुखी हो।
ashtavakra_gita::140.english_translation: Let go of the division 'This is me' and 'This is not me.' Be certain that everything is the true self, be without doubt, and be happy.
ashtavakra_gita::140.translation_literal: अयं (this) / सः (that) / अहमयं (I am) / न (not) / अहं (I) / विभागमिति (division) / सन्त्यज (abandon) / सर्वम् (all) / आत्मेति (is true self) / निश्चित्य (being certain) / निःसङ्कल्पः (without doubt) / सुखी (happy) / भव (be)
ashtavakra_gita::140.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::140.essence: Happiness arises when you drop the division between self and other completely.
ashtavakra_gita::140.simple_meaning: You should stop dividing experience into 'this is me' and 'this is not me.' Instead, be sure that all is the true self and live without conflicting thoughts to be happy.
ashtavakra_gita::140.simple_insight: Freedom comes from letting go of separation and embracing unity without hesitation.
ashtavakra_gita::140.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches to abandon the mental habit of dividing existence into 'I am' and 'I am not.' He urges King Janaka to recognize all as the true self, removing doubt and conflict, which brings happiness and peace.
ashtavakra_gita::140.modern_relevance: When you stop labeling experiences as 'mine' or 'not mine,' you ease mental tension and find calm amid daily chaos.
ashtavakra_gita::140.insight: It shifts your mind from clinging to separateness toward embracing wholeness without hesitation.

ashtavakra_gita::141.verse_sanskrit:
तवैवाज्ञानतो विश्वं त्वमेकः परमार्थतः ।
त्वत्तोऽन्यो नास्ति संसारी नासंसारी च कश्चन ॥
ashtavakra_gita::141.verse_hindi: तेरे ही अज्ञान से विश्व है । परमार्थतः तू एक है । तेरे अतिरिक्त कोई दूसरा नहीं है । न संसारी है, न असंसारी है।
ashtavakra_gita::141.english_translation: The entire universe exists due to your ignorance. In ultimate reality, you alone are one. There is no other besides you, neither bound nor free.
ashtavakra_gita::141.translation_literal: तवैव (because of you alone) अज्ञानतः (due to ignorance) विश्वं (the universe) त्वम् (you) एकः (one) परमार्थतः (in ultimate reality) । त्वत्तः (besides you) अन्यो (other) नास्ति (does not exist) संसारी (the bound) न (nor) असंसारी (the free) च (also) कश्चन (anyone) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::141.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::141.essence: You alone are the singular ultimate reality beyond all illusion and duality.
ashtavakra_gita::141.simple_meaning: All that seems to exist comes from your own ignorance. In truth, you alone are the singular reality, beyond being bound or free.
ashtavakra_gita::141.simple_insight: You can feel the relief of being the one true reality beyond all confusion and duality.
ashtavakra_gita::141.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches King Janaka that the entire universe is a product of ignorance, and at the deepest level, only the true self exists. There is no other being, no bound or free entity—just the singular reality that you are.
ashtavakra_gita::141.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by the chaos around you, remember that beneath it all, your true self remains untouched and singular.
ashtavakra_gita::141.insight: It invites you to see beyond appearances and recognize that your true nature is the sole reality, free from all dualities.

ashtavakra_gita::142.verse_sanskrit:
भ्रान्तिमात्रमिदं विश्वं न किञ्चिदिति निश्चयी ।
निर्वासनः स्फूर्तिमात्रो न किञ्चिदिव शाम्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::142.verse_hindi: यह विश्व भ्रान्तिमात्र है और कुछ नहीं है । ऐसा निश्चयपूर्वक जानने वाला वासनारहित और चैतन्यमात्र है । वह ऐसी शान्ति को प्राप्त है मानो कुछ नहीं है।
ashtavakra_gita::142.english_translation: This entire world is merely an illusion; one who is certain of this, free from desire and full of pure consciousness, attains a peace as if nothing exists.
ashtavakra_gita::142.translation_literal: भ्रान्तिमात्रमिदं (illusion only this) / विश्वं (world) / न (not) / किञ्चिदिति (anything that) / निश्चयी (one who is certain) । / निर्वासनः (desireless) / स्फूर्तिमात्रो (pure consciousness only) / न (not) / किञ्चिदिव (like anything) / शाम्यति (becomes peaceful) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::142.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::142.essence: True peace arises from seeing the world as illusion and resting in pure awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::142.simple_meaning: The world you see is just an illusion. When you fully realize this without desire and rest in pure consciousness, you experience a deep peace as if nothing disturbs you.
ashtavakra_gita::142.simple_insight: You can feel calm and free when you accept the world as not truly real.
ashtavakra_gita::142.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the entire world is just a mistaken appearance. A person who fully understands this, letting go of desires and resting in pure awareness, attains a profound peace as if nothing affects them. This is a turning point in his teaching.
ashtavakra_gita::142.modern_relevance: When everything feels overwhelming or uncertain, realizing that much of what disturbs you is illusion can bring surprising calm and clarity.
ashtavakra_gita::142.insight: It shifts your mind from clinging to appearances toward resting in pure awareness without disturbance.

ashtavakra_gita::143.verse_sanskrit:
एक एव भवाम्भोधावासीदस्ति भविष्यति ।
न ते बन्धोऽस्ति मोक्षो वा कृत्यकृत्यः सुखं चर ॥
ashtavakra_gita::143.verse_hindi: संसाररूपी समुद्र में तू एक ही था और होगा । तेरा बन्ध और मोक्ष नहीं है । तू कृतकृत्य होकर सुखपूर्वक विचर।
ashtavakra_gita::143.english_translation: In the ocean of existence, you alone have always been and will always be. You have neither bondage nor freedom. Be fulfilled and move joyfully.
ashtavakra_gita::143.translation_literal: एक (one) एव (only) भवाम्भोध (ocean of becoming) आवासीद् (resided) अस्ति (is) भविष्यति (will be) । न (not) ते (your) बन्धः (bondage) अस्ति (is) मोक्षः (freedom) वा (or) कृत्यकृत्यः (done and undone) सुखं (joyful) चर (move/live) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::143.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::143.essence: You have always been complete beyond bondage or freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::143.simple_meaning: You have always existed as the one unchanging presence in the ocean of existence. You are not trapped or free because those ideas do not apply. Live fulfilled and joyful as you are.
ashtavakra_gita::143.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing you were never limited or confined, only ever complete.
ashtavakra_gita::143.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra tells King Janaka that in the vast ocean of existence, the true self is eternally present, untouched by bondage or freedom. This moment reveals the ultimate truth: you are already complete and need no change to be joyful.
ashtavakra_gita::143.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by endless pressure to fix or improve yourself. This reminds you that you are already whole and free beneath it all.
ashtavakra_gita::143.insight: It shifts your view from striving for freedom to recognizing your already complete nature, freeing energy for joyful living.

ashtavakra_gita::144.verse_sanskrit:
मा सङ्कल्पविकल्पाभ्यां चित्तं क्षोभय चिन्मय ।
उपशाम्य सुखं तिष्ठ स्वात्मन्यानन्दविग्रहे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::144.verse_hindi: हे चिन्मय ! तू चित्त को संकल्प और विकल्पों से क्षोभित मत कर । शान्त होकर आनन्दपूरित अपने स्वरूप में सुखपूर्वक स्थित हो ।
ashtavakra_gita::144.english_translation: O Conscious Being, do not disturb your mind with decisions and doubts. Calmly stay happily established in your blissful true nature.
ashtavakra_gita::144.translation_literal: मा (do not) सङ्कल्पविकल्पाभ्यां (by decisions and doubts) चित्तं (mind) क्षोभय (disturb) चिन्मय (O conscious being) । उपशाम्य (calmly) सुखं (happily) तिष्ठ (stay) स्वात्मन्यानन्दविग्रहे (in the form of bliss of own true self) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::144.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::144.essence: Calm your restless mind and rest happily in your true blissful nature.
ashtavakra_gita::144.simple_meaning: You should not disturb your mind with constant thinking and doubts. Instead, calmly remain happily rooted in your true self and its bliss.
ashtavakra_gita::144.simple_insight: Peace comes when you stop overthinking and rest in your natural joy.
ashtavakra_gita::144.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra instructs the conscious being not to let the restless mind be agitated by mental choices and doubts. Instead, the teaching is to calm the mind and settle happily in the blissful nature of the true self, pointing to inner peace beyond mental turmoil.
ashtavakra_gita::144.modern_relevance: Your mind races with endless questions and options. This verse invites you to pause, stop the noise, and rest in your natural happiness beneath the chaos.
ashtavakra_gita::144.insight: It shifts your attention from mental agitation to peaceful presence by calming your restless mind and resting in your true nature.

ashtavakra_gita::145.verse_sanskrit:
त्यजैव ध्यानं सर्वत्र मा किञ्चिद् हृदि धारय ।
आत्मा त्वं मुक्त एवासि किं विमृश्य करिष्यसि ॥
ashtavakra_gita::145.verse_hindi: सर्वत्र ध्यान को त्यागकर हृदय में कुछ भी धारण मत कर । तू आत्मा मुक्त ही है । तू विमर्श करके क्या करेगा।
ashtavakra_gita::145.english_translation: Abandon meditation everywhere; do not hold anything in your heart. You are the true self, already free. What will you gain by questioning?
ashtavakra_gita::145.translation_literal: त्यजैव (abandon indeed) / ध्यानं (meditation) / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / मा (do not) / किञ्चिद् (anything) / हृदि (in the heart) / धारय (hold) / आत्मा (the true self) / त्वं (you) / मुक्त (free) / एव (indeed) / असि (are) / किं (what) / विमृश्य (reflecting) / करिष्यसि (will do)
ashtavakra_gita::145.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::145.essence: You are already free; holding on or questioning only blocks that truth.
ashtavakra_gita::145.simple_meaning: Let go of all meditation and mental holding; you are already free as the true self, so questioning is unnecessary.
ashtavakra_gita::145.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing that freedom is your natural state without extra effort.
ashtavakra_gita::145.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra tells Janaka to abandon all meditation and mental grasping. Janaka, a king, is urged to recognize his true self as already free, making further questioning or striving pointless.
ashtavakra_gita::145.modern_relevance: When you obsess over self-improvement or spiritual practices, this reminds you that your true freedom is already present beneath it all.
ashtavakra_gita::145.insight: This shifts your focus from trying to attain freedom to simply resting in the freedom you already have.

ashtavakra_gita::146.verse_sanskrit:
आचक्ष्व श‍ृणु वा तात नानाशास्त्राण्यनेकशः ।
तथापि न तव स्वास्थ्यं सर्वविस्मरणाद् ऋते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::146.verse_hindi: तात ! अनेक शास्त्रों को अनेक प्रकार से तू कह अथवा सुन लेकिन सब के विस्मरण के बिना तुझे स्वास्थ्य नहीं मिलेगी।
ashtavakra_gita::146.english_translation: Listen well, son; you may speak or hear many scriptures in many ways, but without forgetting all of them, you will not find health.
ashtavakra_gita::146.translation_literal: आचक्ष्व (Speak) / शृणु (Listen) / वा (or) / तात (son) / नानाशास्त्राणि (many scriptures) / अनेकशः (in many ways) / तथापि (yet) / न (not) / तव (your) / स्वास्थ्यं (health) / सर्वविस्मरणाद् (without forgetting all) / ऋते (without) ।
ashtavakra_gita::146.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::146.essence: True well-being requires forgetting all teachings, not accumulating them.
ashtavakra_gita::146.simple_meaning: You can hear or speak many teachings, but true well-being comes only when you forget them all.
ashtavakra_gita::146.simple_insight: Relief comes from releasing the need to hold onto every teaching or idea.
ashtavakra_gita::146.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra tells Janaka that despite hearing many scriptures, true health or well-being cannot be attained without forgetting or letting go of all rigid attachments to teachings. This moment points to the paradox that wisdom arises through non-clinging.
ashtavakra_gita::146.modern_relevance: You scroll endlessly through advice and ideas online but feel overwhelmed until you stop trying to retain every opinion.
ashtavakra_gita::146.insight: It teaches you to release rigid attachment to knowledge, allowing natural peace to arise.

ashtavakra_gita::147.verse_sanskrit:
भोगं कर्म समाधिं वा कुरु विज्ञ तथापि ते ।
चित्तं निरस्तसर्वाशमत्यर्थं रोचयिष्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::147.verse_hindi: हे विज्ञ ! भोग, कर्म अथवा समाधि को तू चाहे साधे, तो भी तेरा चित्त स्वभाव से सभी आशयों से रहित होने पर भी अत्यधिक लोभायमान रहेगा।
ashtavakra_gita::147.english_translation: O wise one, whether you seek pleasure, action, or absorbed presence, your mind will still crave intensely even when free from all desires by nature.
ashtavakra_gita::147.translation_literal: भोगं (pleasure) / कर्म (action) / समाधिं (absorbed presence) / वा (or) / कुरु (do/seek) / विज्ञ (O wise one) / तथापि (even then) / ते (your) / चित्तं (mind) / निरस्तसर्वाशम् (free from all desires) / अत्यर्थं (excessively) / रोचयिष्यति (will crave).
ashtavakra_gita::147.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::147.essence: The mind craves intensely even when free from all desires by nature.
ashtavakra_gita::147.simple_meaning: Even if you pursue pleasure, action, or deep stillness, your mind naturally continues to crave strongly despite seeming free of all desires.
ashtavakra_gita::147.simple_insight: It feels unsettling to realize your mind’s craving can persist beyond what you achieve or renounce.
ashtavakra_gita::147.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to the wise seeker who tries to master pleasure, action, or even profound stillness, yet finds the restless mind clinging intensely. This reveals how deeply ingrained craving is, not erased by external achievements or inner renunciation.
ashtavakra_gita::147.modern_relevance: You finish a project, meditate deeply, or enjoy a moment of joy — but still your mind pulls you toward wanting more, restless as ever.
ashtavakra_gita::147.insight: It shifts your understanding from expecting craving to end with success or stillness, to seeing craving as a persistent nature of the mind itself.

ashtavakra_gita::148.verse_sanskrit:
आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन ।
अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::148.verse_hindi: प्रयास से सब लोग दुःखी हैं, इसको कोई नहीं जानता है । इसी उपदेश से भाग्यवान लोग निर्वाण को प्राप्त होते हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::148.english_translation: Effort causes all suffering; no one truly knows this. By this teaching alone, the fortunate attain freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::148.translation_literal: आयासात् (from effort) सकलो (all) दुःखी (suffering) नैनं (this) जानाति (knows) कश्चन (anyone) । अनेनैव (by this alone) उपदेशेन (teaching) धन्यः (fortunate) प्राप्नोति (attains) निर्वृतिम् (freedom) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::148.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::148.essence: Suffering comes from effort; true freedom arises from seeing this clearly.
ashtavakra_gita::148.simple_meaning: Trying too hard causes suffering, but understanding this leads to true freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::148.simple_insight: Relief comes when you see effort itself can cause pain and freedom lies beyond it.
ashtavakra_gita::148.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Ashtavakra reveals to King Janaka that all suffering arises from effort and striving. Few recognize this root cause. The fortunate gain freedom by grasping this truth and letting go.
ashtavakra_gita::148.modern_relevance: You push yourself relentlessly, chasing success or control, unaware that the very effort fuels your stress and exhaustion.
ashtavakra_gita::148.insight: It teaches you to notice how effort can create resistance and suffering, shifting your approach toward letting be.

ashtavakra_gita::149.verse_sanskrit:
व्यापारे खिद्यते यस्तु निमेषोन्मेषयोरपि ।
तस्यालस्य धुरीणस्य सुखं नन्यस्य कस्यचित् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::149.verse_hindi: जो आँख के खोलने और ढकने के व्यापार से दुःखी होता है, वह आलसी-शिरोमणि का ही सुख है । दूसरे किसी का नहीं।
ashtavakra_gita::149.english_translation: The one who suffers from the opening and closing of the eyes is the master of laziness's own pleasure, not anyone else's.
ashtavakra_gita::149.translation_literal: व्यापारे (in the business) / खिद्यते (is distressed) / यः (who) / तु (indeed) / निमेष (blink) / उन्मेषयोः (opening and closing) / अपि (even) / तस्य (of that one) / आलस्य (of laziness) / धुरीणस्य (master's) / सुखं (pleasure) / नन्यस्य (not of another) / कस्यचित् (anyone).
ashtavakra_gita::149.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::149.essence: Suffering from fleeting distractions is the product of your own restless habit.
ashtavakra_gita::149.simple_meaning: If you feel troubled by every little change or distraction, that restlessness is your own habit causing suffering.
ashtavakra_gita::149.simple_insight: You realize your discomfort comes from your own restless mind, not outside events.
ashtavakra_gita::149.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that those who suffer from even the smallest fluctuations, like the blinking of the eyes, are enslaved by their own inner laziness and restlessness, not by external factors.
ashtavakra_gita::149.modern_relevance: When a tiny annoyance like a phone notification unsettles you, it's your restless habit causing your suffering, not the event itself.
ashtavakra_gita::149.insight: It teaches you to notice how clinging to every distraction creates your own suffering and to loosen that grip.

ashtavakra_gita::150.verse_sanskrit:
इदं कृतमिदं नेति द्वन्द्वैर्मुक्तं यदा मनः ।
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षेषु निरपेक्षं तदा भवेत् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::150.verse_hindi: यह किया गया है और यह नहीं किया गया, ऐसे द्वन्द्व से जब मन मुक्त हो तब वह धर्म, अर्थ, काम और मोक्ष के प्रति उदासीन हो जाता है।
ashtavakra_gita::150.english_translation: When the mind is free from the pairs of opposites 'this is done' and 'this is not done,' it becomes indifferent to dharma, wealth, desire, and freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::150.translation_literal: इदं (this) / कृतमिदं (done this) / नेति (not this) / द्वन्द्वैः (by pairs of opposites) / मुक्तं (free) / यदा (when) / मनः (mind) / धर्मार्थकाममोक्षेषु (towards dharma, wealth, desire, and freedom) / निरपेक्षं (indifferent) / तदा (then) / भवेत् (becomes).
ashtavakra_gita::150.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::150.essence: True freedom arises when the mind transcends all judgments of action and inaction.
ashtavakra_gita::150.simple_meaning: The mind becomes free when it stops seeing actions as done or not done and no longer clings to duty, wealth, desire, or freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::150.simple_insight: You feel peace when your mind no longer swings between opposites or tries to control outcomes.
ashtavakra_gita::150.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that true freedom arises when the mind is no longer caught in dualities like 'done' and 'not done.' At this moment, the mind also becomes detached from goals like dharma (duty), artha (wealth), kama (desire), and moksha (freedom).
ashtavakra_gita::150.modern_relevance: You finish a big task and stop obsessing over whether it was perfect or not; your mind rests beyond judgment.
ashtavakra_gita::150.insight: It teaches you to let go of judging actions as success or failure and to rest in impartial awareness.

ashtavakra_gita::151.verse_sanskrit:
विरक्तो विषयद्वेष्टा रागी विषयलोलुपः ।
ग्रहमोक्षविहीनस्तु न विरक्तो न रागवान् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::151.verse_hindi: विषय का दोषी विरक्त है । विषयलोलुप रागी है । जो ग्रहण और त्याग दोनों से रहित है वह न विरक्त है, न रागवान है।
ashtavakra_gita::151.english_translation: The one free from attachment is averse to sense objects; the one attached is desirous of them. One who is neither taking nor renouncing is neither detached nor attached.
ashtavakra_gita::151.translation_literal: विरक्तो (detached) विषयद्वेष्टा (averse to sense objects) रागी (attached) विषयलोलुपः (desirous of sense objects) । ग्रहम् (taking) मोक्षविहीनः (without renunciation) तु (but) न (not) विरक्तो (detached) न (nor) रागवान् (attached) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::151.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::151.essence: You cannot be truly detached without rejecting desire, nor truly attached without embracing it.
ashtavakra_gita::151.simple_meaning: You are either attached to things or truly detached. Being stuck between wanting and rejecting means you are neither.
ashtavakra_gita::151.simple_insight: There is relief in choosing a clear stance rather than being caught in indecision.
ashtavakra_gita::151.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that true detachment means actively rejecting desire for sense objects, while attachment means craving them. Those who neither accept nor reject are caught in confusion and have neither quality truly.
ashtavakra_gita::151.modern_relevance: You feel uneasy when you’re indecisive—neither fully embracing nor letting go of a situation or desire.
ashtavakra_gita::151.insight: This verse teaches you to recognize that hesitation between wanting and rejecting causes inner turmoil.

ashtavakra_gita::152.verse_sanskrit:
हेयोपादेयता तावत्संसारविटपाङ्कुरः ।
स्पृहा जीवति यावद् वै निर्विचारदशास्पदम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::152.verse_hindi: जब तक स्पृहा जीवित है – जो कि अविवेक की दशा है – तब तक हेय और उपादेय भी जीवित है – जो कि संसाररूपी वृक्ष का अंकुर है।
ashtavakra_gita::152.english_translation: As long as craving lives—the state of confusion—both what should be avoided and what should be attained continue to live, like sprouts on the tree of worldly existence.
ashtavakra_gita::152.translation_literal: हेय (to be avoided) / उपादेयता (to be attained) / तावत् (as long as) / संसार (worldly existence) / विटप (tree) / अंकुरः (sprout) / स्पृहा (craving) / जीवति (lives) / यावत् (until) / वै (indeed) / निर्विचार (without clear thought) / दशा (state) / अस्पदम् (unstable)
ashtavakra_gita::152.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::152.essence: Craving sustains the endless cycle of desire and aversion in the restless mind.
ashtavakra_gita::152.simple_meaning: As long as you have craving, the cycle of wanting and avoiding continues like new sprouts on a tree of suffering.
ashtavakra_gita::152.simple_insight: There’s freedom waiting beyond craving’s endless push and pull.
ashtavakra_gita::152.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that craving (spṛhā) sustains the continuous cycles of attraction and aversion, which are like new sprouts growing on the tree of worldly existence (saṃsāra). This confusion keeps the restless mind entangled.
ashtavakra_gita::152.modern_relevance: When you feel caught between wanting something and fearing its opposite, that restless craving is what keeps your stress alive.
ashtavakra_gita::152.insight: It shifts your view from chasing and avoiding to seeing craving itself as the root of unrest.

ashtavakra_gita::153.verse_sanskrit:
प्रवृत्तौ जायते रागो निर्वृत्तौ द्वेष एव हि ।
निर्द्वन्द्वो बालवद् धीमान् एवमेव व्यवस्थितः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::153.verse_hindi: प्रवृत्ति से राग, व निवृत्ति से द्वेष पैदा होता है । इसलिए बुद्धिमान पुरुष द्वन्द्वमुक्त बालक के समान जैसा है, वैसा ही रहता है।
ashtavakra_gita::153.english_translation: Attachment arises in engagement, aversion arises in withdrawal; the wise remain free of duality like a child.
ashtavakra_gita::153.translation_literal: प्रवृत्तौ (in engagement) / जायते (arises) / रागो (attachment) / निर्वृत्तौ (in withdrawal) / द्वेष (aversion) / एव (indeed) / हि (certainly) / । / निर्द्वन्द्वो (free of duality) / बालवद् (like a child) / धीमान् (the wise) / एवमेव (thus exactly) / व्यवस्थितः (established) / ॥
ashtavakra_gita::153.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::153.essence: Freedom arises by transcending attachment and aversion, staying peacefully beyond conflict.
ashtavakra_gita::153.simple_meaning: When you act, attachment to things arises; when you withdraw, aversion arises. The wise stay free from these opposites, like a peaceful child.
ashtavakra_gita::153.simple_insight: Peace comes when you stop swinging between wanting and rejecting.
ashtavakra_gita::153.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Ashtavakra explains that acting in the world causes attachment, and withdrawing causes aversion. A wise person transcends these dual feelings, remaining peacefully established like a child who does not judge or struggle.
ashtavakra_gita::153.modern_relevance: You feel torn between chasing what you want and pushing away what you dislike. True calm comes when you stop reacting both ways.
ashtavakra_gita::153.insight: You learn to observe your impulses without getting caught in attraction or rejection, stabilizing your mind like a child’s openness.

ashtavakra_gita::154.verse_sanskrit:
हातुमिच्छति संसारं रागी दुःखजिहासया ।
वीतरागो हि निर्दुःखस्तस्मिन्नपि न खिद्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::154.verse_hindi: रागी पुरुष दुःख से बचने के लिए संसार को त्यागना चाहता है लेकिन वीतरागी दुःखमुक्त होकर संसार के बीच भी खेद को प्राप्त नहीं होता।
ashtavakra_gita::154.english_translation: A person attached to desire wants to leave the world to avoid suffering, but one free from desire is without suffering and feels no regret even within the world.
ashtavakra_gita::154.translation_literal: हातुमिच्छति (wants to leave) संसारं (the world) रागी (one attached to desire) दुःखजिहासया (to avoid suffering) । वीतरागो (one free from desire) हि (indeed) निर्दुःखः (without suffering) तस्मिन्नपि (even in that) न (not) खिद्यति (feels regret) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::154.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::154.essence: Freedom from desire ends suffering and regret even while engaged in the world.
ashtavakra_gita::154.simple_meaning: Desire makes you want to avoid suffering by leaving the world. Without desire, you no longer suffer or regret even when in the world.
ashtavakra_gita::154.simple_insight: There is peace in being free from desire, even amid life's challenges.
ashtavakra_gita::154.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains to King Janaka that a person attached to desire tries to escape the world to avoid suffering. But one who is free from desire experiences no suffering or regret, even while living within the world’s conditions.
ashtavakra_gita::154.modern_relevance: You may feel like quitting when problems arise, but real freedom lets you face life without pain or regret.
ashtavakra_gita::154.insight: It shifts your view from avoiding pain by escape to embracing presence without regret.

ashtavakra_gita::155.verse_sanskrit:
यस्याभिमानो मोक्षेऽपि देहेऽपि ममता तथा ।
न च ज्ञानी न वा योगी केवलं दुःखभागसौ ॥
ashtavakra_gita::155.verse_hindi: जिसका मोक्ष के प्रति अहंकार है और वैसी ही शरीर के प्रति ममता है, वह न तो योगी है, न ज्ञानी है । वह केवल दुःख का भागी है।
ashtavakra_gita::155.english_translation: One who clings with ego to freedom and attachment to the body is neither yogi nor knower, only a partaker in suffering.
ashtavakra_gita::155.translation_literal: यस्याभिमानो (whose ego) / मोक्षेऽपि (even in freedom) / देहेऽपि (in the body also) / ममता (attachment) / तथा (same) / न (not) / च (and) / ज्ञानी (knower) / न (not) / वा (or) / योगी (yogi) / केवलं (only) / दुःखभागसौ (partaker of suffering)
ashtavakra_gita::155.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::155.essence: Ego attachment to freedom or body keeps you trapped in suffering, not truly free.
ashtavakra_gita::155.simple_meaning: Holding pride about being free or attachment to your body means you aren’t truly wise or free but caught in suffering.
ashtavakra_gita::155.simple_insight: True freedom requires letting go of ego’s hold on both liberation and the body.
ashtavakra_gita::155.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a person who claims freedom but still clings with ego to that freedom and to their body is not truly liberated. Such a person, neither a yogi nor a knower, remains bound to suffering because ego clouds true understanding.
ashtavakra_gita::155.modern_relevance: You may chase personal growth or health, but pride in these achievements can secretly keep you restless and unhappy.
ashtavakra_gita::155.insight: It teaches to examine how ego clings even to positive states, and to release that grip for genuine peace.

ashtavakra_gita::156.verse_sanskrit:
हरो यद्युपदेष्टा ते हरिः कमलजोऽपि वा ।
तथापि न तव स्वाथ्यं सर्वविस्मरणादृते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::156.verse_hindi: यदि तेरा उपदेशक शिव है, विष्णु है अथवा ब्रह्मा है तो भी सबके विस्मरण के बिना तुझे स्वास्थ्य नहीं होगी ।
ashtavakra_gita::156.english_translation: Even if your teacher is Shiva, Vishnu, or Brahma, you will not find health without forgetting all else.
ashtavakra_gita::156.translation_literal: हरो (Shiva) / यद्युपदेष्टा (if teacher) / ते (your) / हरिः (Vishnu) / कमलजोऽपि (even lotus-born [Brahma]) / वा (or) / तथापि (still) / न (not) / तव (your) / स्वाथ्यं (health) / सर्वविस्मरणादृते (without forgetting all)
ashtavakra_gita::156.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::156.essence: True well-being requires forgetting all else, regardless of who teaches you.
ashtavakra_gita::156.simple_meaning: No matter who teaches you—even the greatest teachers—true health or well-being comes only when you forget all distractions and attachments.
ashtavakra_gita::156.simple_insight: There is freedom in releasing all attachments, even to revered guides.
ashtavakra_gita::156.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra tells Janaka that even if the highest divine teachers instruct you, you cannot gain true health or well-being unless you forget all other distractions and attachments. This teaching points to the need for deep renunciation beyond respect for any teacher.
ashtavakra_gita::156.modern_relevance: You might admire many experts or mentors, but true growth happens only when you stop clinging to all distractions and fully commit.
ashtavakra_gita::156.insight: It shifts focus from relying on external authorities to internal freedom through letting go of all attachments.

ashtavakra_gita::157.verse_sanskrit:
तेन ज्ञानफलं प्राप्तं योगाभ्यासफलं तथा ।
तृप्तः स्वच्छेन्द्रियो नित्यमेकाकी रमते तु यः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::157.verse_hindi: जो पुरुष तृप्त है, शुद्ध इन्द्रियों वाला है और सदा एकाकी रमण करता है उसी को ज्ञान और योगाभ्यास का फल प्राप्त होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::157.english_translation: The person who is content, pure in senses, and constantly delights in solitude attains the fruit of knowledge and yoga practice.
ashtavakra_gita::157.translation_literal: तेन (by that) / ज्ञानफलं (fruit of knowledge) / प्राप्तं (attained) / योगाभ्यासफलं (fruit of yoga practice) / तथा (also) / तृप्तः (content) / स्वच्छेन्द्रियो (pure in senses) / नित्यम् (always) / एकाकी (alone) / रमते (delights) / तु (but) / यः (who)
ashtavakra_gita::157.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::157.essence: Contentment, pure senses, and solitude unlock the real fruits of knowledge and yoga.
ashtavakra_gita::157.simple_meaning: You gain the full benefit of knowledge and yoga when you are satisfied, your senses are clear, and you enjoy solitude.
ashtavakra_gita::157.simple_insight: Peace and purity within open the door to deeper understanding and practice results.
ashtavakra_gita::157.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the true fruits of studying knowledge and practicing yoga come to the person who is inwardly satisfied, has purified senses, and finds joy in being alone. This shows the importance of inner state over external effort.
ashtavakra_gita::157.modern_relevance: When you stop chasing distractions, feel satisfied with yourself, and find calm in solitude, your efforts in growth and learning genuinely deepen.
ashtavakra_gita::157.insight: It shifts your focus from external achievements to cultivating inner contentment and sensory clarity as the foundation for progress.

ashtavakra_gita::158.verse_sanskrit:
न कदाचिज्जगत्यस्मिन् तत्त्वज्ञो हन्त खिद्यति ।
यत एकेन तेनेदं पूर्णं ब्रह्माण्डमण्डलम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::158.verse_hindi: हन्त ! तत्त्वज्ञानी इस जगत में कभी खेद को प्राप्त नहीं होता है क्योंकि उसी एक से यह ब्रह्माण्ड मण्डल पूर्ण है।
ashtavakra_gita::158.english_translation: The true knower of reality never experiences regret because the entire universe is complete in that one.
ashtavakra_gita::158.translation_literal: न (never) / कदाचि (at any time) / जगति (in the world) / अस्मिन् (in this) / तत्त्वज्ञः (knower of reality) / हन्त (indeed) / खिद्यति (feels regret) / यत् (because) / एकेन (by one) / तेने (by that) / इदं (this) / पूर्णं (complete) / ब्रह्माण्डमण्डलम् (the universe)
ashtavakra_gita::158.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::158.essence: Regret cannot arise when you recognize the universe is fully complete in oneness.
ashtavakra_gita::158.simple_meaning: Someone who truly understands reality never feels regret because they see the whole universe as complete in one.
ashtavakra_gita::158.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing that nothing is lacking or incomplete in what is.
ashtavakra_gita::158.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the knower of the ultimate reality perceives the entire universe as whole and complete, so regret or sorrow never arises for them.
ashtavakra_gita::158.modern_relevance: You look back at a decision and realize everything unfolded as it should — no room for regret.
ashtavakra_gita::158.insight: It shifts your mind from scarcity and loss to completeness and acceptance in all experience.

ashtavakra_gita::159.verse_sanskrit:
न जातु विषयाः केऽपि स्वारामं हर्षयन्त्यमी ।
सल्लकीपल्लवप्रीतमिवेभं निम्बपल्लवाः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::159.verse_hindi: जैसे सल्लकी के पत्तों से प्रसन्न हुए हाथी को नीम के पत्ते हर्षित नहीं करते हैं, वैसे ही ये विषय आत्मा में रमण करने वाले को कभी नहीं हर्षित करते हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::159.english_translation: Just as a neem leaf never delights an elephant pleased by sal tree leaves, worldly objects never delight the self immersed in itself.
ashtavakra_gita::159.translation_literal: न (never) जातु (ever) विषयाः (objects) केऽपि (any) स्वारामं (own abode) हर्षयन्ति (delight) अमी (me). सल्लकीपल्लवप्रीतमिवेभं (like elephant pleased by sal tree leaves) निम्बपल्लवाः (neem leaves).
ashtavakra_gita::159.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::159.essence: True happiness arises only when the self is established, untouched by worldly things.
ashtavakra_gita::159.simple_meaning: If you are truly settled in your own self, external things cannot make you happy or disturb you.
ashtavakra_gita::159.simple_insight: You feel steady and unshaken because fleeting things lose their power to affect you.
ashtavakra_gita::159.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Ashtavakra explains to King Janaka that just as an elephant pleased by sal tree leaves does not delight in bitter neem leaves, a person who is established in the true self is not moved by worldly objects or desires.
ashtavakra_gita::159.modern_relevance: You get excited about some new gadget or trend but soon it loses charm—your deeper self stays calm amid such changes.
ashtavakra_gita::159.insight: It teaches you to root your happiness inside yourself, so outer changes don’t disturb your peace.

ashtavakra_gita::160.verse_sanskrit:
यस्तु भोगेषु भुक्तेषु न भवत्यधिवासितः ।
अभुक्तेषु निराकाङ्क्षी तदृशो भवदुर्लभः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::160.verse_hindi: जो भोगे हुए भोगों में वासना नहीं रखता तथा भोगे हुए विषयों के प्रति आकांक्षा नहीं रखता, ऐसा मनुष्य संसार में दुर्लभ है।
ashtavakra_gita::160.english_translation: A person who does not cling to pleasures already enjoyed and does not desire those unexperienced is rare in this world.
ashtavakra_gita::160.translation_literal: यस्तु (whoever) / भोगेषु (in pleasures) / भुक्तेषु (already enjoyed) / न (not) / भवत्यधिवासितः (dwells) / अभुक्तेषु (in unexperienced) / निराकाङ्क्षी (without desire) / तदृशो (such a one) / भवदुर्लभः (is rare)
ashtavakra_gita::160.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::160.essence: True rarity lies in neither clinging to past nor craving future pleasures.
ashtavakra_gita::160.simple_meaning: Someone who neither holds onto past pleasures nor desires new ones is very rare in the world.
ashtavakra_gita::160.simple_insight: There's a unique peace in not chasing or clinging to pleasures, found in very few.
ashtavakra_gita::160.detailed_meaning: In a teaching moment, Ashtavakra points out how uncommon it is to find a person who neither dwells on past enjoyments nor longs for future pleasures, highlighting the rarity of true detachment in human nature.
ashtavakra_gita::160.modern_relevance: You notice how most people replay past moments or chase new experiences, yet true ease comes when you stop holding on or wanting more.
ashtavakra_gita::160.insight: It shifts your mind from clinging to pleasures toward accepting experience without desire or attachment.

ashtavakra_gita::161.verse_sanskrit:
बुभुक्षुरिह संसारे मुमुक्षुरपि दृश्यते ।
भोगमोक्षनिराकाङ्क्षी विरलो हि महाशयः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::161.verse_hindi: इस संसार में भोग की इच्छा रखने वाले और मोक्ष की इच्छा रखने वाले दोनों देखे जाते हैं, लेकिन भोग और मोक्ष दोनों के प्रति निरकांक्षी विरल महाशय ही मिलेगा।
ashtavakra_gita::161.english_translation: In this world, both those who desire pleasure and those who seek freedom are seen, but rare indeed is the noble one who desires neither pleasure nor freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::161.translation_literal: बुभुक्षु (desiring pleasure) इह (here/in this) संसारे (world) मुमुक्षु (seeking freedom) अपि (also) दृश्यते (are seen) । भोग (pleasure) मोक्ष (freedom) निराकाङ्क्षी (desireless) विरलो (rare) हि (indeed) महाशयः (noble person) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::161.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::161.essence: True nobility lies in freeing yourself from every desire, pleasure or freedom alike.
ashtavakra_gita::161.simple_meaning: In life, some chase pleasure, others seek freedom, but very few release all desires completely.
ashtavakra_gita::161.simple_insight: There is a quiet strength in wanting nothing, beyond pleasure or freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::161.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra points out a simple truth: the world has many craving pleasures or liberation, but only a rare noble person frees themselves from all wants, embodying true detachment.
ashtavakra_gita::161.modern_relevance: You scroll social media, see people chasing happiness or escape, but feel drawn to simply rest beyond all craving.
ashtavakra_gita::161.insight: It invites you to notice desire itself as a barrier and consider stepping beyond all wanting.

ashtavakra_gita::162.verse_sanskrit:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षेषु जीविते मरणे तथा ।
कस्याप्युदारचित्तस्य हेयोपादेयता न हि ॥
ashtavakra_gita::162.verse_hindi: कोई उदारचित्त ही धर्म, अर्थ, काम, मोक्ष, जीवन और मृत्यु के प्रति हेय-उपादेय का भाव नहीं रखता।
ashtavakra_gita::162.english_translation: No generous-hearted person regards duty, wealth, desire, freedom, life, or death as contemptible or to be rejected.
ashtavakra_gita::162.translation_literal: धर्मार्थकाममोक्षेषु (in duty, wealth, desire, and freedom) जीविते (in life) मरणे (in death) तथा (also) कस्यापि (anyone's) उदारचित्तस्य (of generous-hearted) हेयोपादेयता (contemptible or to be rejected) न (not) हि (indeed)
ashtavakra_gita::162.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::162.essence: A generous heart accepts all experiences—duty, desire, life, and death—as worthy.
ashtavakra_gita::162.simple_meaning: A truly generous heart does not reject or look down on any aspect of life or death, nor on duty, desire, or freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::162.simple_insight: You can meet all parts of life with respect and openness, feeling no need to reject or despise them.
ashtavakra_gita::162.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a person with a generous mind holds no contempt for any major aspect of existence—whether duty, wealth, desire, freedom, life, or death. This balanced acceptance reflects true inner freedom and equanimity.
ashtavakra_gita::162.modern_relevance: When faced with challenges like career pressure, personal desires, or fears about mortality, you can choose to hold all experiences without rejection or fear.
ashtavakra_gita::162.insight: It teaches you to embrace life's full spectrum without judgment, dissolving resistance and inner conflict.

ashtavakra_gita::163.verse_sanskrit:
वाञ्छा न विश्वविलये न द्वेषस्तस्य च स्थितौ ।
यथा जीविकया तस्माद् धन्य आस्ते यथा सुखम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::163.verse_hindi: जिसमें विश्व के विलय की इच्छा नहीं है और न उसकी स्थिति के प्रति द्वेष है, इसलिए वह धन्य पुरुष यथाप्राप्य आजीविका से सुखपूर्वक जीता है।
ashtavakra_gita::163.english_translation: One who has neither desire for the world's destruction nor hatred toward its state lives blessed, content with what sustains life.
ashtavakra_gita::163.translation_literal: वाञ्छा (desire) / न (not) / विश्वविलये (world’s destruction) / न (nor) / द्वेषः (hatred) / तस्य (toward it) / च (and) / स्थितौ (state) / यथा (just as) / जीविकया (by livelihood) / तस्मात् (therefore) / धन्यः (blessed) / आस्ते (is) / यथा (as) / सुखम् (happiness)
ashtavakra_gita::163.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::163.essence: Blessed living comes from neither craving the world’s end nor hating its state.
ashtavakra_gita::163.simple_meaning: You live a happy, blessed life when you neither desire the world to end nor hate how it is, accepting what supports your living.
ashtavakra_gita::163.simple_insight: Peace arises when you stop wanting the world to change and stop hating its current state.
ashtavakra_gita::163.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a person free from the desire to destroy the world or hate its present condition is truly fortunate. This teaching arises in the context of the seeker learning to accept reality without resistance, finding contentment in whatever sustains life.
ashtavakra_gita::163.modern_relevance: You’ve stopped wishing your situation was different and stopped resenting what you can’t control, feeling a quiet ease with life as it is.
ashtavakra_gita::163.insight: It teaches you to release both craving for radical change and aversion toward current conditions to find contentment.

ashtavakra_gita::164.verse_sanskrit:
कृतार्थोऽनेन ज्ञानेनेत्येवं गलितधीः कृती ।
पश्यन् श‍ृण्वन् स्पृशन् जिघ्रन्न् अश्नन्नास्ते यथा सुखम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::164.verse_hindi: इस ज्ञान से कृतार्थ अनुभव कर, गलित हो गयी बुद्धि जिसकी, ऐसा कृतकार्य पुरुष देखता हुआ, स्पर्श करता हुआ, सूँघता हुआ, खाता हुआ सुखपूर्वक रहता है।
ashtavakra_gita::164.english_translation: With this knowledge, the wise feel fulfilled; their confused mind dissolves. Such a fulfilled person experiences joy while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, and eating.
ashtavakra_gita::164.translation_literal: कृतार्थोऽनेन (fulfilled by this) ज्ञानेन (by knowledge) एति (goes) एवं (thus) गलितधीः (confused mind dissolved) कृती (one who has done) पश्यन् (seeing) शृण्वन् (hearing) स्पृशन् (touching) जिघ्रन् (smelling) अश्नन् (eating) आसते (resides) यथा (just as) सुखम् (joy).
ashtavakra_gita::164.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::164.essence: Fulfillment comes when the confused mind dissolves and joy naturally arises in all experiences.
ashtavakra_gita::164.simple_meaning: When your confusion dissolves through true knowledge, you feel fulfilled and enjoy life fully through all your senses.
ashtavakra_gita::164.simple_insight: There's peace in knowing that clarity brings joy to all your experiences.
ashtavakra_gita::164.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that when deep knowledge dissolves the confused mind, the person becomes fulfilled and naturally enjoys life through all senses without disturbance. This moment marks the transformation from confusion to peaceful awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::164.modern_relevance: You notice how overwhelming thoughts vanish sometimes, letting you fully enjoy a meal or a walk without distraction.
ashtavakra_gita::164.insight: It teaches you to recognize that true fulfillment comes from clarity that frees the mind, not from external pleasures alone.

ashtavakra_gita::165.verse_sanskrit:
शून्या दृष्टिर्वृथा चेष्टा विकलानीन्द्रियाणि च ।
न स्पृहा न विरक्तिर्वा क्षीणसंसारसागरे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::165.verse_hindi: जिसका संसार सागर क्षीण हो गया है, ऐसे पुरुष में न तृष्णा है, न विरक्ति है । उसकी दृष्टि शून्य हो गयी है, चेष्टा व्यर्थ हो गयी है और इन्द्रियाँ विफल हो गयी हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::165.english_translation: A person whose ocean of worldly existence has been exhausted has no thirst, no detachment; their vision is empty, efforts are futile, and senses ineffective.
ashtavakra_gita::165.translation_literal: शून्या (empty) दृष्टिः (vision) वृथा (futile) चेष्टा (effort) विकलानि (ineffective) इन्द्रियाणि (senses) च (also) । न (not) स्पृहा (thirst) न (not) विरक्ति (detachment) वा (or) क्षीण (exhausted) संसारसागर (worldly ocean) इ (in) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::165.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::165.essence: When worldly craving ends, both desire and detachment disappear into emptiness.
ashtavakra_gita::165.simple_meaning: When a person’s engagement with the world is completely exhausted, they no longer crave or reject anything. Their vision feels empty, efforts seem pointless, and the senses lose their power.
ashtavakra_gita::165.simple_insight: There is a calm that arises when both wanting and not-wanting dissolve within you.
ashtavakra_gita::165.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes a person who has fully experienced and moved beyond worldly attachments. Their 'ocean of existence' is dry, meaning they no longer crave or reject. Their senses and efforts fail to stir them because their perspective has emptied of all desire and aversion.
ashtavakra_gita::165.modern_relevance: You’ve worn yourself out trying to control outcomes, pushing and pulling, until nothing excites or repels you anymore—and in that quiet, a new kind of freedom begins.
ashtavakra_gita::165.insight: It teaches you to recognize when desire and aversion both lose their hold, revealing a deeper stillness beneath restless effort.

ashtavakra_gita::166.verse_sanskrit:
न जागर्ति न निद्राति नोन्मीलति न मीलति ।
अहो परदशा क्वापि वर्तते मुक्तचेतसः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::166.verse_hindi: वह न जागता है, न मरता है, न पलक खोलता है, न पलक बन्द करता है । अहो ! मुक्तचेतस् की कैसी परम दशा होती है।
ashtavakra_gita::166.english_translation: The liberated mind neither wakes nor sleeps, neither opens nor closes the eyelids; such is the supreme state of the free mind.
ashtavakra_gita::166.translation_literal: न (not) जागर्ति (wakes) न (not) निद्राति (sleeps) नोन्मीलति (does not open) न (not) मीलति (closes) । अहो (ah!) परदशा (supreme state) क्वापि (anywhere) वर्तते (exists) मुक्तचेतसः (of the free mind) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::166.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::166.essence: Freedom is the unchanging state beyond waking, sleeping, and all dualities.
ashtavakra_gita::166.simple_meaning: The truly free mind is beyond waking, sleeping, or any change in awareness. It remains in an unchanging supreme state.
ashtavakra_gita::166.simple_insight: There is a deep freedom in being beyond all changing states of consciousness.
ashtavakra_gita::166.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes the state of a liberated mind that transcends normal cycles of waking, sleeping, and blinking. This supreme condition is unchanging and beyond the restless fluctuations of ordinary life.
ashtavakra_gita::166.modern_relevance: When your mind feels restless and distracted, imagine a state beyond all shifting moods and thoughts—pure, steady, and free.
ashtavakra_gita::166.insight: It teaches you to recognize freedom as the unchanging awareness beyond all mental fluctuations.

ashtavakra_gita::167.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वत्र दृश्यते स्वस्थः सर्वत्र विमलाशयः ।
समस्तवासना मुक्तो मुक्तः सर्वत्र राजते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::167.verse_hindi: मुक्त पुरुष सर्वत्र स्वस्थ, सर्वत्र विमल आशय वाला दिखाई देता है और सब वासनाओं से रहित सर्वत्र सुशोभित होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::167.english_translation: The liberated person appears established everywhere, with a pure heart everywhere, free from all desires, shining everywhere.
ashtavakra_gita::167.translation_literal: सर्वत्र (everywhere) दृश्यते (is seen) स्वस्थः (established) सर्वत्र (everywhere) विमलाशयः (pure-hearted) समस्तवासना (all-desires) मुक्तो (free) मुक्तः (liberated) सर्वत्र (everywhere) राजते (shines)
ashtavakra_gita::167.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::167.essence: Freedom shines as steady purity and desirelessness everywhere you go.
ashtavakra_gita::167.simple_meaning: A truly free person is steady and pure in every place, free from all desires, and naturally radiant.
ashtavakra_gita::167.simple_insight: You can feel steady and radiant no matter where you are or what surrounds you.
ashtavakra_gita::167.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes the liberated person who is firmly established in freedom, with a clear and pure mind everywhere, free from all cravings, and shining with that inner freedom in every circumstance.
ashtavakra_gita::167.modern_relevance: You walk into any room and feel calm, clear, and unaffected by distractions or cravings around you.
ashtavakra_gita::167.insight: It teaches you to recognize your freedom and purity as constant, not tied to location or situations.

ashtavakra_gita::168.verse_sanskrit:
पश्यन् श‍ृण्वन् स्पृशन् जिघ्रन्न् अश्नन् गृण्हन् वदन् व्रजन् ।
ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो मुक्त एव महाशयः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::168.verse_hindi: देखता हुआ, सुनता हुआ, स्पर्श करता हुआ, सूँघता हुआ, खाता हुआ, ग्रहण करता हुआ, बोलता हुआ, चलता हुआ, हित और अहित से मुक्त महाशय निश्चय ही जीवन मुक्त है।
ashtavakra_gita::168.english_translation: Seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, taking, speaking, walking—free from benefit and harm, the great being is truly free in life.
ashtavakra_gita::168.translation_literal: पश्यन् (seeing) शृण्वन् (hearing) स्पृशन् (touching) जिघ्रन् (smelling) अश्नन् (eating) गृण्हन् (taking) वदन् (speaking) व्रजन् (walking) । ईहितानि (beneficial) अहितैः (harmful) मुक्तो (free) मुक्त (free) एव (indeed) महाशयः (great being) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::168.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::168.essence: True freedom means engaging with life without being bound by gain or loss.
ashtavakra_gita::168.simple_meaning: You can experience the world through all senses and actions without becoming attached to benefits or harms, remaining free within life.
ashtavakra_gita::168.simple_insight: Freedom comes from not letting what helps or harms define your inner state.
ashtavakra_gita::168.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes a great being who fully engages with the world—seeing, hearing, touching, and acting—yet remains free from being affected by what is beneficial or harmful. This shows true inner freedom despite external activity.
ashtavakra_gita::168.modern_relevance: You attend a lively gathering, fully present and engaged, yet your peace stays unshaken by praise or criticism.
ashtavakra_gita::168.insight: It teaches you to remain centered and unattached while fully participating in life's sensory and social experiences.

ashtavakra_gita::169.verse_sanskrit:
न निन्दति न च स्तौति न हृष्यति न कुप्यति ।
न ददाति न गृण्हाति मुक्तः सर्वत्र नीरसः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::169.verse_hindi: मुक्तपुरुष सर्वत्र रसरहित है । वह न निन्दा करता है, न स्तुति करता है, न हर्षित होता है, न क्रुद्ध होता है, न लेता है, न देता है।
ashtavakra_gita::169.english_translation: The liberated person is free from all emotions everywhere; they neither blame nor praise, neither rejoice nor get angry, neither give nor take.
ashtavakra_gita::169.translation_literal: न (not) निन्दति (blames) न (not) च (and) स्तौति (praises) न (not) हृष्यति (rejoices) न (not) कुप्यति (gets angry) । न (not) ददाति (gives) न (not) गृण्हाति (takes) मुक्तः (liberated) सर्वत्र (everywhere) नीरसः (without emotion) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::169.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::169.essence: True freedom is steady presence beyond all emotional reactions.
ashtavakra_gita::169.simple_meaning: A truly free person is emotionally steady everywhere, not moved by praise, blame, joy, anger, giving, or taking.
ashtavakra_gita::169.simple_insight: You can feel calm and steady no matter what others say or do.
ashtavakra_gita::169.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a liberated person is completely unaffected by emotional ups and downs. They neither praise nor blame others, nor do they feel joy or anger. This shows the deep inner freedom beyond all reactions.
ashtavakra_gita::169.modern_relevance: In moments when social media praise or criticism flood your mind, you can stay calm and not get swept away.
ashtavakra_gita::169.insight: It teaches you to observe emotions without getting pulled into them or reacting impulsively.

ashtavakra_gita::170.verse_sanskrit:
सानुरागां स्त्रियं दृष्ट्वा मृत्युं वा समुपस्थितम् ।
अविह्वलमनाः स्वस्थो मुक्त एव महाशयः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::170.verse_hindi: प्रीतियुक्त स्त्री और समीप में उपस्थित मृत्यु को देखकर जो महाशय अविचलमना और स्वस्थ रहता है, वह निश्चय ही मुक्त है।
ashtavakra_gita::170.english_translation: A great person who remains steady and healthy in mind upon seeing a beloved woman or the approaching death is surely free.
ashtavakra_gita::170.translation_literal: सानुरागां (beloved woman) / स्त्रियं (woman) / दृष्ट्वा (seeing) / मृत्युं (death) / वा (or) / समुपस्थितम् (present) / अविह्वलमनाः (unshaken mind) / स्वस्थो (steady/healthy) / मुक्त (free) / एव (indeed) / महाशयः (great person)
ashtavakra_gita::170.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::170.essence: True freedom is unshaken calm when facing both love and death.
ashtavakra_gita::170.simple_meaning: You are free when your mind remains calm and steady even when facing someone you love or death itself.
ashtavakra_gita::170.simple_insight: You feel unshaken and whole, no matter what life or loss comes near you.
ashtavakra_gita::170.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a person who does not lose inner balance when seeing a beloved woman or facing imminent death has truly attained freedom. This shows the depth of equanimity beyond attachment or fear.
ashtavakra_gita::170.modern_relevance: You stay composed when a loved one leaves or when you confront your own limits, revealing your deepest freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::170.insight: It teaches you to steady your mind so external joys or fears no longer control your inner peace.

ashtavakra_gita::171.verse_sanskrit:
सुखे दुःखे नरे नार्यां सम्पत्सु च विपत्सु च ।
विशेषो नैव धीरस्य सर्वत्र समदर्शिनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::171.verse_hindi: समदर्शी धीर के लिए सुख और दुःख में, नर और नारी में, सम्पत्ति और विपत्ति में कहीं भेद नहीं है।
ashtavakra_gita::171.english_translation: For the steady-minded seer, there is no difference in pleasure or pain, man or woman, wealth or loss.
ashtavakra_gita::171.translation_literal: सुखे (in pleasure) दुःखे (in pain) नरे (man) नार्यां (woman) सम्पत्सु (in wealth) च (and) विपत्सु (in loss) च (and) । विशेषो (difference) नैव (not at all) धीरस्य (of the steady-minded) सर्वत्र (everywhere) समदर्शिनः (equal-seeing) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::171.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::171.essence: A steady mind sees no difference in apparent opposites like pain and pleasure or wealth and loss.
ashtavakra_gita::171.simple_meaning: A person with steady wisdom sees no difference between pleasure and pain, men and women, or wealth and loss.
ashtavakra_gita::171.simple_insight: You can feel calm knowing that the world’s ups and downs don’t change your true view.
ashtavakra_gita::171.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a wise and steady person remains unaffected by external differences like joy or sorrow, gender, or fortune and misfortune, seeing everything with equal vision.
ashtavakra_gita::171.modern_relevance: You face the flood of news, social differences, and life’s ups and downs without losing your calm or judging.
ashtavakra_gita::171.insight: It trains you to stop reacting to external labels and see events and people without bias or preference.

ashtavakra_gita::172.verse_sanskrit:
न हिंसा नैव कारुण्यं नौद्धत्यं न च दीनता ।
नाश्चर्यं नैव च क्षोभः क्षीणसंसरणे नरे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::172.verse_hindi: क्षीण हो गया है संसार जिसका, ऐसे मनुष्य में न हिंसा है, न करुणा है, न उद्दण्डता है, न दीनता, न आश्चर्य है, न क्षोभ।
ashtavakra_gita::172.english_translation: A person whose cycle of reactivity has ended shows no violence, no pity, no arrogance, no helplessness, no surprise, and no disturbance.
ashtavakra_gita::172.translation_literal: न (not) हिंसा (violence) नैव (also not) कारुण्यं (pity) नौद्धत्यं (arrogance) न (not) च (and) दीनता (helplessness) । नाश्चर्यं (no surprise) नैव (also not) च (and) क्षोभः (disturbance) क्षीणसंसरणे (in the ended cycle of reactivity) नरे (in a person) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::172.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::172.essence: True freedom means no emotional disturbance or reactive impulses remain.
ashtavakra_gita::172.simple_meaning: A person free from the cycle of reactive emotions no longer feels violence, pity, arrogance, helplessness, surprise, or inner disturbance.
ashtavakra_gita::172.simple_insight: There is peace in ending reactive habits; nothing shakes or disturbs you anymore.
ashtavakra_gita::172.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that when a person transcends the restless cycle of emotional reactivity (samsara), they become free from violence, pity, arrogance, helplessness, surprise, and inner turmoil. This marks a state of profound equanimity and freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::172.modern_relevance: You notice how frustration or anger no longer grips you during a stressful conversation or unexpected event; your mind stays steady and undisturbed.
ashtavakra_gita::172.insight: It teaches you to recognize and transcend emotional triggers, cultivating a steady and peaceful inner state.

ashtavakra_gita::173.verse_sanskrit:
न मुक्तो विषयद्वेष्टा न वा विषयलोलुपः ।
असंसक्तमना नित्यं प्राप्ताप्राप्तमुपाश्नुते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::173.verse_hindi: मुक्त पुरुष न विषयों से द्वेष करने वाला है, न विषयलोलुप है । सदा आसक्तिरहित मन वाला होकर प्राप्त और अप्राप्त वस्तु का उपभोग करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::173.english_translation: The liberated person neither hates nor craves objects; with a mind free from attachment, they constantly experience what comes and goes.
ashtavakra_gita::173.translation_literal: न (not) मुक्तो (liberated) विषयद्वेष्टा (object-hater) न (nor) वा (also) विषयलोलुपः (object-craver) । असंसक्तमना (non-attached mind) नित्यं (constantly) प्राप्ताप्राप्तम् (obtained-unobtained) उपाश्नुते (experiences) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::173.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::173.essence: Freedom means experiencing life without craving or aversion, with a mind untethered to outcomes.
ashtavakra_gita::173.simple_meaning: You don't need to hate or crave things. Staying free from attachment lets you accept whatever happens, good or bad.
ashtavakra_gita::173.simple_insight: There’s peace in not clinging or rejecting what life brings your way.
ashtavakra_gita::173.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a truly free person does not react with dislike or desire toward objects. Their mind remains unattached, calmly experiencing whatever comes and goes without disturbance.
ashtavakra_gita::173.modern_relevance: You scroll through social media, sometimes thrilled, sometimes frustrated, yet your peace stays when you don’t cling or push away those feelings.
ashtavakra_gita::173.insight: It teaches you to maintain inner balance by neither chasing after nor resisting experiences.

ashtavakra_gita::174.verse_sanskrit:
समाधानसमाधानहिताहितविकल्पनाः ।
शून्यचित्तो न जानाति कैवल्यमिव संस्थितः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::174.verse_hindi: शून्यचित्त पुरुष समाधान और असमाधान के, हित और अहित के विकल्प को नहीं जानता है । वह तो कैवल्य जैसा स्थित है।
ashtavakra_gita::174.english_translation: The one whose mind is empty does not know alternatives of satisfaction or dissatisfaction, benefit or harm; they are established as if in perfect freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::174.translation_literal: समाधानसमाधानहिताहितविकल्पनाः (alternatives of satisfaction and dissatisfaction, benefit and harm) / शून्यचित्तो (one with empty mind) / न (not) / जानाति (knows) / कैवल्यमिव (as if perfect freedom) / संस्थितः (established).
ashtavakra_gita::174.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::174.essence: An empty mind no longer sees gain or loss and rests in perfect freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::174.simple_meaning: When your mind is empty and free of thoughts, you no longer see options like gain or loss, satisfaction or dissatisfaction. You rest in a state like perfect freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::174.simple_insight: There’s peace in not needing to judge or pick sides in experience.
ashtavakra_gita::174.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a mind emptied of distractions and judgments no longer distinguishes between opposing experiences such as benefit or harm. Freed from these dualities, a person abides in a state like complete freedom, untouched by the usual fluctuations of the mind.
ashtavakra_gita::174.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by choices or worries about outcomes, you can find calm by stepping back and letting go of judgments about what is good or bad.
ashtavakra_gita::174.insight: It shifts your mind from grasping at outcomes to resting in acceptance beyond duality.

ashtavakra_gita::175.verse_sanskrit:
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारो न किञ्चिदिति निश्चितः ।
अन्तर्गलितसर्वाशः कुर्वन्नपि करोति न ॥
ashtavakra_gita::175.verse_hindi: भीतर से गलित हो गयी हैं आशाएँ जिसकी, और जो निश्चयपूर्वक जानता है कि कुछ भी नहीं है – ऐसा ममतारहित, अहंकारशून्य पुरुष कर्म करता हुआ भी उनमें लिप्त नहीं होता ।
ashtavakra_gita::175.english_translation: One who is free of attachment and ego, firmly knowing there is nothing, acts without being entangled in any desire.
ashtavakra_gita::175.translation_literal: निर्ममो (without attachment) / निरहङ्कारो (without ego) / न (not) / किञ्चिदिति (anything) / निश्चितः (certainly) / अन्तर्गलितसर्वाशः (all hopes dissolved inside) / कुर्वन् (doing) / अपि (even) / करोति (acts) / न (not)
ashtavakra_gita::175.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::175.essence: You can act without ego or desire while remaining fully present and free.
ashtavakra_gita::175.simple_meaning: If you let go of ego and attachments, knowing nothing truly belongs to you, you can act without being caught in desires.
ashtavakra_gita::175.simple_insight: There's freedom in acting fully without being pulled by craving or the sense of self.
ashtavakra_gita::175.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that someone whose hopes and attachments have dissolved, who has no ego or personal clinging, can still act in the world without being entangled by desires. This teaching shows how inner freedom coexists with external action.
ashtavakra_gita::175.modern_relevance: You complete a task without over-identifying or craving the outcome, staying calm even when faced with pressure or uncertainty.
ashtavakra_gita::175.insight: It teaches you to perform actions while witnessing your mind's urges without becoming involved in them.

ashtavakra_gita::176.verse_sanskrit:
मनःप्रकाशसंमोहस्वप्नजाड्यविवर्जितः ।
दशां कामपि सम्प्राप्तो भवेद् गलितमानसः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::176.verse_hindi: जिसका मन गलित हो गया है और जिसके मन में कर्म, मोह, स्वप्न और जड़ता सब समाप्त हो गए हैं, वह पुरुष कैसी अनिर्वचनीय अवस्था को प्राप्त होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::176.english_translation: When the mind is purified, free from action, confusion, sleep, and dullness, it attains an indescribable state.
ashtavakra_gita::176.translation_literal: मनः (mind) / प्रकाश (light) / संमोह (confusion) / स्वप्न (sleep) / जाड्य (dullness) / विवर्जितः (free from) । / दशां (of ten) / कामपि (actions also) / सम्प्राप्तो (attained) / भवेत् (becomes) / गलितमानसः (purified mind) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::176.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::176.essence: A mind free from confusion and dullness attains an indescribable clarity.
ashtavakra_gita::176.simple_meaning: A mind that is clear and free from confusion, sleepiness, and inactivity reaches a special, indescribable state.
ashtavakra_gita::176.simple_insight: There is peace and wonder in a mind fully clear and awake, beyond usual experience.
ashtavakra_gita::176.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes a state where the mind loses all dullness, confusion, dreams, and restless activity. This purified mind then reaches a unique, ineffable experience beyond ordinary understanding.
ashtavakra_gita::176.modern_relevance: When your mind is free from distraction, tiredness, and confusion, you glimpse a clarity that words cannot capture.
ashtavakra_gita::176.insight: It teaches you to recognize clarity as freedom from mental fog and rest, opening a gateway to deeper awareness.

ashtavakra_gita::177.verse_sanskrit:
यस्य बोधोदये तावत्स्वप्नवद् भवति भ्रमः ।
तस्मै सुखैकरूपाय नमः शान्ताय तेजसे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::177.verse_hindi: जिसके उदय होने पर समस्त भ्रान्ति स्वप्न के समान तिरोहित हो जाती है, उस एकमात्र आनन्दस्वरूप, शान्त और तेजोमय को नमस्कार है।
ashtavakra_gita::177.english_translation: Salutations to that one blissful, peaceful, and radiant being whose arising dispels all illusion like a dream.
ashtavakra_gita::177.translation_literal: यस्य (whose) बोधोदये (upon arising of knowledge) तावत् (so much) स्वप्नवत् (like a dream) भवति (becomes) भ्रमः (illusion) । तस्मै (to that) सुखैक-रूपाय (one-form bliss) नमः (salutations) शान्ताय (peaceful) तेजसे (radiant) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::177.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::177.essence: True knowing dissolves all illusion as completely as waking ends a dream.
ashtavakra_gita::177.simple_meaning: When you truly awaken to your inner being, all confusion disappears like a fading dream, revealing peace and joy.
ashtavakra_gita::177.simple_insight: There is deep relief in realizing confusion is as unreal as a dream fading away.
ashtavakra_gita::177.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that when true knowledge arises, all misconceptions vanish as if they were mere dreams. This awakening reveals a peaceful, radiant bliss that is the true nature beyond illusion.
ashtavakra_gita::177.modern_relevance: You’ve had moments when worries suddenly seem unreal, like a bad dream fading upon waking — that’s the power of true awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::177.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with confusion to resting in peaceful clarity as your natural state.

ashtavakra_gita::178.verse_sanskrit:
अर्जयित्वाखिलान् अर्थान् भोगानाप्नोति पुष्कलान् ।
न हि सर्वपरित्यागमन्तरेण सुखी भवेत् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::178.verse_hindi: सारे धन कमाकर मनुष्य अतिशय भोगों को पाता है । लेकिन सबके त्याग के बिना सुखी नहीं होता।
ashtavakra_gita::178.english_translation: By earning all wealth, one gains abundant pleasures. But without completely giving up everything, one cannot be truly happy.
ashtavakra_gita::178.translation_literal: अर्जयित्वा (having earned) अखिलान् (all) अर्थान् (wealth) भोगान् (pleasures) आप्नोति (obtains) पुष्कलान् (abundant) । न (not) हि (indeed) सर्वपरित्यागम् (complete renunciation) अन्तरेण (without) सुखी (happy) भवेत् (becomes) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::178.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::178.essence: True happiness requires completely letting go, not just gaining pleasures.
ashtavakra_gita::178.simple_meaning: Having many pleasures from wealth is possible, but true happiness requires giving up attachment to everything.
ashtavakra_gita::178.simple_insight: You realize that no amount of gain alone can bring lasting happiness without letting go.
ashtavakra_gita::178.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that even if a person acquires all wealth and pleasures, lasting happiness cannot arise without fully renouncing attachment to them. The deeper freedom comes only with total letting go.
ashtavakra_gita::178.modern_relevance: You might chase every comfort and pleasure, yet feel unrest until you let go fully of craving for them.
ashtavakra_gita::178.insight: It shifts your view from accumulating possessions to releasing attachment as the key to happiness.

ashtavakra_gita::179.verse_hindi: कर्तव्य से पैदा हुए दुःखरूप सूर्य के ताप से जला अन्तर्मन जिसका, ऐसे पुरुष को शान्तिरूपी अमृतधारा की वर्षा के बिना सुख कहाँ है।
ashtavakra_gita::179.english_translation: A person whose inner being is burned by the fiery sun of duty-born suffering finds no happiness without the shower of peace-like nectar.
ashtavakra_gita::179.translation_literal: कर्तव्य (duty) दुःख (suffering) अमर्तण्ड (fiery sun) ज्वालाद (by flames) अग्ध (burned) अन्तरात्मनः (inner being) । कुतः (where) प्रशम (peace) पीयूष (nectar) धारासार (shower essence) अमृत (immortal) सुखम् (happiness) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::179.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::179.essence: True happiness comes only when peace soothes the suffering caused by fulfilling duty.
ashtavakra_gita::179.simple_meaning: Suffering caused by fulfilling duty can feel like burning inside; only a peaceful, soothing experience can bring true happiness.
ashtavakra_gita::179.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing peace can heal the deepest burdens duty creates.
ashtavakra_gita::179.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes how the inner self can feel scorched by the intense suffering that arises from fulfilling one's duty. Without the refreshing experience of peace like nectar, lasting happiness is impossible for such a person.
ashtavakra_gita::179.modern_relevance: You’ve pushed yourself through a difficult obligation that left you drained; only moments of genuine calm can restore your joy.
ashtavakra_gita::179.insight: This verse teaches you to seek inner peace as the essential remedy when duty causes emotional pain.

ashtavakra_gita::180.verse_sanskrit:
भवोऽयं भावनामात्रो न किञ्चित् परमर्थतः ।
नास्त्यभावः स्वभावानां भावाभावविभाविनाम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::180.verse_hindi: यह संसार भावनामात्र है, परमार्थतः कुछ भी नहीं है । भावरूप और अभावरूप पदार्थों में स्थित स्वभाव का अभाव नहीं है।
ashtavakra_gita::180.english_translation: This world is only appearance; ultimately, it is nothing real. The true nature of things is the presence of both existence and non-existence aspects inseparable in the nature of all that appears.
ashtavakra_gita::180.translation_literal: भवोऽयं (this existence) / भावना (appearance) / मात्रः (only) / न (not) / किञ्चित् (anything) / परमर्थतः (ultimately) । नास्ति (is not) / अभावः (non-existence) / स्वभावानां (of natures) / भाव-अभाव-विभाविनाम् (of those distinguishing existence and non-existence) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::180.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::180.essence: Everything appears but nothing exists separately; existence and non-existence are inseparable.
ashtavakra_gita::180.simple_meaning: The world you experience is only appearance; in truth, nothing exists independently. Existence and non-existence coexist inseparably in all things.
ashtavakra_gita::180.simple_insight: You can feel the relief of knowing the world is not as separate or solid as it seems.
ashtavakra_gita::180.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains to King Janaka that the entire manifest world is just a play of appearances. There is no absolute existence or non-existence alone; both aspects coexist in the nature of everything perceived.
ashtavakra_gita::180.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by change or loss, remember that what you grasp as solid is just appearance, not fixed reality.
ashtavakra_gita::180.insight: It shifts your view from seeing things as fixed entities to recognizing their inseparable unity of existence and non-existence.

ashtavakra_gita::181.verse_sanskrit:
न दूरं न च सङ्कोचाल्लब्धमेवात्मनः पदम् ।
निर्विकल्पं निरायासं निर्विकारं निरञ्जनम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::181.verse_hindi: यह आत्मपद न तो दूर है, न संकोच से ही प्राप्त होता है । यह निर्विकल्प, निरायास, निर्विकार और निरञ्जन है।
ashtavakra_gita::181.english_translation: The state of the true self is neither distant nor attained by effort; it is without alternatives, effortless, unchanging, and spotless.
ashtavakra_gita::181.translation_literal: न (not) दूरं (distant) न (nor) च (also) सङ्कोचात् (by effort) लब्धम् (attained) एव (indeed) आत्मनः (of self) पदम् (state) । निर्विकल्पं (without alternatives) निरायासं (effortless) निर्विकारं (unchanging) निरञ्जनम् (spotless) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::181.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::181.essence: The true self is always present, effortless, unchanging, and pure.
ashtavakra_gita::181.simple_meaning: The true self is always present and cannot be reached by struggle or effort. It is steady, effortless, and pure.
ashtavakra_gita::181.simple_insight: You can feel peace knowing your true self needs no effort or distance to be found.
ashtavakra_gita::181.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the true self is not something far away or something you acquire by hard effort. It is naturally present, without change or impurity, beyond mental alternatives or struggles.
ashtavakra_gita::181.modern_relevance: You pause, anxious about achieving peace, then realize it’s always been inside you—no effort or distance needed.
