ashtavakra_gita::181.insight: It shifts your view from striving to recognize the true self as already here, beyond all effort or change.

ashtavakra_gita::182.verse_hindi: मोहमात्र से निवृत्त होने पर और अपने स्वरूप के ग्रहण मात्र से वीतशोक और निरावरण दृष्टि वाले पुरुष शोभायमान होते हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::182.english_translation: By renouncing only delusion and simply embracing your true nature, you become free of sorrow and shine with unobstructed vision.
ashtavakra_gita::182.translation_literal: मोहमात्र (only delusion) / विरतौ (renouncing) / स्वरूपादानमात्रतः (simply by embracing true nature) / वीतशोका (free of sorrow) / विराजन्ते (shine) / निरावरणदृष्टयः (with unobstructed vision)
ashtavakra_gita::182.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::182.essence: Renouncing delusion and embracing your true self dissolves sorrow and reveals clear vision.
ashtavakra_gita::182.simple_meaning: When you stop believing in false illusions and simply accept who you truly are, sorrow disappears and your vision becomes clear and unobstructed.
ashtavakra_gita::182.simple_insight: There is deep relief in knowing that dropping confusion reveals your natural brightness and peace.
ashtavakra_gita::182.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that by releasing all false beliefs (delusions) and fully accepting your true self, you naturally become free from sorrow and gain a clear, unobstructed perception of reality.
ashtavakra_gita::182.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed when caught in self-doubt or confusion, but simply accepting who you are can clear your mind and ease your heart.
ashtavakra_gita::182.insight: Shift focus from chasing illusions to resting in your true nature, which dissolves sorrow and reveals clarity.

ashtavakra_gita::183.verse_sanskrit:
समस्तं कल्पनामात्रमात्मा मुक्तः सनातनः ।
इति विज्ञाय धीरो हि किमभ्यस्यति बालवत् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::183.verse_hindi: समस्त जगत कल्पना मात्र है और आत्मा मुक्त और सनातन है । ऐसा जानकर धीर पुरुष बालक के समान क्या चेष्टा करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::183.english_translation: Everything is merely an imagination, the true self is free and eternal; knowing this, what effort can a steady person make like a child?
ashtavakra_gita::183.translation_literal: समस्तं (all) कल्पनामात्रमात्मा (imagination only / self) मुक्तः (free) सनातनः (eternal) । इति (thus) विज्ञाय (knowing) धीरो (steady one) हि (indeed) किम् (what) अभ्यस्यति (makes effort) बालवत् (like a child) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::183.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::183.essence: Your true self is eternally free beyond all imagined effort.
ashtavakra_gita::183.simple_meaning: Everything you see and think is just imagination; your true self is free and eternal. When you realize this, striving like a child makes no sense.
ashtavakra_gita::183.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing your true self is already beyond effort or change.
ashtavakra_gita::183.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the entire world is just imagined, while your true self is eternally free. Understanding this, a wise person ceases futile effort, like a child unaware of struggle.
ashtavakra_gita::183.modern_relevance: You stress over things that feel urgent, but knowing your true self is free can ease your constant striving.
ashtavakra_gita::183.insight: It shifts your mind from trying to control imagined realities to resting in the freedom of your true self.

ashtavakra_gita::184.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मा ब्रह्मेति निश्चित्य भावाभावौ च कल्पितौ ।
निष्कामः किं विजानाति किं ब्रूते च करोति किम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::184.verse_hindi: आत्मा ब्रह्म है और भाव एवं अभाव कल्पित हैं । यह निश्चयपूर्वक जानकर निष्काम पुरुष क्या जानता है, क्या कहता है और क्या करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::184.english_translation: Knowing for certain that the true self is the supreme reality and that existence and non-existence are imagined, a desireless person neither knows nor speaks nor acts.
ashtavakra_gita::184.translation_literal: आत्मा (the true self) / ब्रह्मेति (is the supreme reality) / निश्चित्य (knowing for certain) / भावाभावौ (existence and non-existence) / च (and) / कल्पितौ (are imagined) / । (.) / निष्कामः (desireless person) / किं (what) / विजानाति (knows) / किं (what) / ब्रूते (speaks) / च (and) / करोति (does) / किम् (what) / ॥ (.)
ashtavakra_gita::184.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::184.essence: Fully knowing the true self dissolves all desire, knowledge, speech, and action.
ashtavakra_gita::184.simple_meaning: When you fully understand that your true self is the supreme reality and that existence and non-existence are just imagined, a desireless person no longer knows, speaks, or acts.
ashtavakra_gita::184.simple_insight: You feel the relief of wanting nothing and doing nothing because you recognize your true self.
ashtavakra_gita::184.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the true self is the supreme reality beyond imagined existence and non-existence. Once this is known without doubt, a desireless person transcends knowledge, speech, and action, embodying complete freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::184.modern_relevance: You stop obsessing over choices and outcomes when you deeply realize your essential nature beyond all appearances.
ashtavakra_gita::184.insight: It shifts your mind from reacting and doing to resting in the truth beyond all imagined dualities.

ashtavakra_gita::185.verse_sanskrit:
अयं सोऽहमयं नाहमिति क्षीणा विकल्पना ।
सर्वमात्मेति निश्चित्य तूष्णीम्भूतस्य  योगिनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::185.verse_hindi: सब आत्मा है । ऐसा निश्चयपूर्वक जानकर शान्त हुए योगी की ऐसी कल्पनाएँ कि ‘वह मैं हूँ’ और ‘वह मैं नहीं हूँ’ क्षीण हो जाती हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::185.english_translation: Knowing firmly that everything is the true self, the yogi becomes peaceful as the notions ‘I am this’ and ‘I am not this’ fade away.
ashtavakra_gita::185.translation_literal: अयं (this) / सः (he) / अहम् (I) / अयम् (this) / न (not) / अहम् (I) / इति (thus) / क्षीणा (faded) / विकल्पना (thoughts) / सर्वम् (all) / आत्मेति (is the self) / निश्चित्य (having known firmly) / तूष्णीम्भूतस्य (become peaceful) / योगिनः (of the yogi)
ashtavakra_gita::185.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::185.essence: True peace arises when all conflicting thoughts of self vanish into one knowing.
ashtavakra_gita::185.simple_meaning: When you firmly realize that everything is your true self, conflicting thoughts about being or not being something disappear, bringing deep peace.
ashtavakra_gita::185.simple_insight: You can feel calm by letting go of all self-contradicting thoughts about who you are.
ashtavakra_gita::185.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Ashtavakra explains that the yogi who firmly understands that all is the true self transcends dual ideas like 'I am this' or 'I am not this.' This realization dissolves mental conflict and brings profound stillness.
ashtavakra_gita::185.modern_relevance: After a long day of conflicting feelings about your identity or choices, a quiet certainty about your true nature can calm your restless mind.
ashtavakra_gita::185.insight: It teaches you to release mental divisions of self versus other and rest in the unified true self.

ashtavakra_gita::186.verse_sanskrit:
न विक्षेपो न चैकाग्र्यं नातिबोधो न मूढता ।
न सुखं न च वा दुःखमुपशान्तस्य योगिनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::186.verse_hindi: अपशान्त हुए योगी के लिए न विक्षेप है और न एकाग्रता है, न अतिबोध है और न मूढ़ता है, न सुख है और न दुःख है।
ashtavakra_gita::186.english_translation: For the tranquil yogi, there is no distraction, no concentration, no excessive awareness, no confusion, no pleasure, and no pain.
ashtavakra_gita::186.translation_literal: न (not) विक्षेपो (distraction) न (not) च (and) ऐकाग्र्यं (concentration) न (not) अतिबोधो (excessive awareness) न (not) मूढता (confusion) । न (not) सुखं (pleasure) न (not) च (and) वा (or) दुःखम् (pain) उपशान्तस्य (of the tranquil) योगिनः (yogi) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::186.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::186.essence: True calm is beyond distraction, focus, pleasure, pain, and confusion.
ashtavakra_gita::186.simple_meaning: A truly peaceful yogi experiences no distractions, no focused effort, no confusion, and no feelings of pleasure or pain.
ashtavakra_gita::186.simple_insight: You can rest in a calm beyond all highs and lows, free from inner turmoil.
ashtavakra_gita::186.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes a yogi who has reached deep tranquility—completely free from mental distractions, intense focus, overthinking, confusion, pleasure, or pain. This state marks profound inner equanimity beyond ordinary experience.
ashtavakra_gita::186.modern_relevance: When your mind stops chasing every emotion or thought, you find a calm that no success or failure can shake.
ashtavakra_gita::186.insight: It teaches you to let go of both craving and aversion, resting in neutral awareness beyond all feelings.

ashtavakra_gita::187.verse_sanskrit:
स्वाराज्ये भैक्षवृत्तौ च लाभालाभे जने वने ।
निर्विकल्पस्वभावस्य न विशेषोऽस्ति योगिनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::187.verse_hindi: निर्विकल्प स्वभाव वाले योगी के लिए राज्य और भिक्षावृत्ति में, लाभ और हानि में, समाज और वन में फर्क नहीं है।
ashtavakra_gita::187.english_translation: For a yogi of unwavering nature, there is no difference between rulership and mendicancy, gain and loss, society and solitude.
ashtavakra_gita::187.translation_literal: स्वाराज्ये (in rulership) / भैक्षवृत्तौ (in mendicant life) / च (and) / लाभालाभे (in gain and loss) / जने (in society) / वने (in forest) / निर्विकल्पस्वभावस्य (of the yogi with unwavering nature) / न (no) / विशेषोऽस्ति (there is difference) / योगिनः (of the yogi)
ashtavakra_gita::187.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::187.essence: The steady self is unaffected by external roles, outcomes, or surroundings.
ashtavakra_gita::187.simple_meaning: A yogi who has an unshakable inner nature sees no difference between wealth or poverty, company or loneliness.
ashtavakra_gita::187.simple_insight: You can feel steady and whole regardless of life's ups and downs around you.
ashtavakra_gita::187.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a yogi with unwavering inner nature is unaffected by external conditions like ruling or begging, gaining or losing, being among people or alone in the forest. This moment shows true equanimity beyond worldly dualities.
ashtavakra_gita::187.modern_relevance: You face chaos at work, social events, or quiet moments alone — but your inner peace remains unshaken.
ashtavakra_gita::187.insight: This shifts your focus from external situations to the steady self beneath changing circumstances.

ashtavakra_gita::188.verse_sanskrit:
क्व धर्मः क्व च वा कामः क्व चार्थः क्व विवेकिता ।
इदं कृतमिदं नेति द्वन्द्वैर्मुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::188.verse_hindi: यह किया है और यह अनकिया है इस प्रकार के द्वन्द्व से मुक्त योगी के लिए कहाँ धर्म है, कहाँ काम है, कहाँ अर्थ है, कहाँ विवेक है।
ashtavakra_gita::188.english_translation: For the yogi free from dualities, where is duty, where desire, where wealth, where discrimination in what is done and what is not?
ashtavakra_gita::188.translation_literal: क्व (where) धर्मः (duty) क्व (where) च (and) वा (or) कामः (desire) क्व (where) चार्थः (wealth) क्व (where) विवेकिता (discrimination) । इदं (this) कृतमिदं (done and not done) नेति (this or that) द्वन्द्वैः (duality/opposites) मुक्तस्य (free) योगिनः (yogi) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::188.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::188.essence: Beyond dualities, concepts like duty, desire, and discrimination lose meaning.
ashtavakra_gita::188.simple_meaning: When you are free from seeing things as opposites, concepts like duty, desire, wealth, and even discrimination lose their meaning.
ashtavakra_gita::188.simple_insight: Freedom from opposites brings peace beyond everyday roles and wants.
ashtavakra_gita::188.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a yogi who transcends all dualities—such as duty versus desire or wealth versus poverty—no longer experiences these divisions; the usual distinctions in life dissolve into unity.
ashtavakra_gita::188.modern_relevance: In moments when your mind stops labeling actions as right or wrong, you feel a rare calm beyond stress and ambition.
ashtavakra_gita::188.insight: It shifts your mind from clinging to labels and judgments toward experiencing life as seamless and whole.

ashtavakra_gita::189.verse_sanskrit:
कृत्यं किमपि नैवास्ति न कापि हृदि रञ्जना ।
यथा जीवनमेवेह जीवन्मुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::189.verse_hindi: जीवनमुक्त योगी के लिए कर्तव्यकर्म कुछ भी नहीं है और न हृदय में कोई अनुराग है । वह संसार में यथाप्राप्त जीवन जीता है।
ashtavakra_gita::189.english_translation: For the life-liberated yogi, no duty exists and no attachment stains the heart; they live in the world just as life itself.
ashtavakra_gita::189.translation_literal: कृत्यं (duty/action) किमपि (anything) नैवास्ति (does not exist) न (nor) कापि (any) हृदि (in the heart) रञ्जना (staining/attachment) । यथा (just as) जीवनम् (life) एव (indeed) एह (here) जीवन्मुक्तस्य (life-liberated) योगिनः (yogi) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::189.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::189.essence: Complete freedom means no inner obligations or cravings, just living naturally here and now.
ashtavakra_gita::189.simple_meaning: A fully liberated yogi feels no obligation or desire and lives naturally in the world without attachment.
ashtavakra_gita::189.simple_insight: You can be free inside while still living fully in the world around you.
ashtavakra_gita::189.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the yogi who has attained inner freedom no longer experiences binding duties or emotional cravings; instead, they move through life effortlessly, untouched by attachment, embodying liberation while alive.
ashtavakra_gita::189.modern_relevance: You finish your tasks without clinging to outcomes or stress, simply being present with whatever life brings.
ashtavakra_gita::189.insight: It shifts your mind from feeling bound by roles or desires to embracing life without internal resistance.

ashtavakra_gita::190.verse_sanskrit:
क्व मोहः क्व च वा विश्वं क्व तद् ध्यानं क्व मुक्तता ।
सर्वसङ्कल्पसीमायां विश्रान्तस्य महात्मनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::190.verse_hindi: सम्पूर्ण संकल्पों के अन्त होने पर विश्रान्त हुए महात्मा के लिए कहाँ मोह और कहाँ संसार है, कहाँ वह ध्यान है, कहाँ मुक्ति है।
ashtavakra_gita::190.english_translation: For the great soul who is at rest beyond all intentions, where is delusion, where is the world, where is meditation, where is liberation?
ashtavakra_gita::190.translation_literal: क्व (where) / मोहः (delusion) / क्व (where) / च (and) / वा (or) / विश्वं (world) / क्व (where) / तद् (that) / ध्यानं (meditation) / क्व (where) / मुक्तता (liberation) / सर्वसङ्कल्पसीमायां (at the boundary/end of all intentions) / विश्रान्तस्य (of the one at rest) / महात्मनः (great soul)
ashtavakra_gita::190.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::190.essence: Complete rest beyond all desires ends delusion, the world, and the need for liberation.
ashtavakra_gita::190.simple_meaning: When a great soul stops all mental intentions and desires, there is no delusion, no world, no meditation, and no separate liberation.
ashtavakra_gita::190.simple_insight: True rest beyond craving frees you from confusion and the sense of separation.
ashtavakra_gita::190.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra challenges the seeker to see that when all desires and intentions end, the great soul rests beyond illusion, beyond the world, beyond meditation itself, and beyond the idea of liberation as separate.
ashtavakra_gita::190.modern_relevance: You lie awake, your mind finally quiet after endless striving. In that calm, all worries about progress and escape dissolve naturally.
ashtavakra_gita::190.insight: It shifts your view from seeking something outside to recognizing resting as the true freedom.

ashtavakra_gita::191.verse_sanskrit:
येन विश्वमिदं दृष्टं स नास्तीति करोतु वै ।
निर्वासनः किं कुरुते पश्यन्नपि न पश्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::191.verse_hindi: जिसने जगत को देखा है वह भला उसे इनकार भी करे, लेकिन वासनारहित पुरुष को क्या करना है । वह देखता हुआ भी नहीं देखता है।
ashtavakra_gita::191.english_translation: He who has truly seen this entire world can even deny it; but what can a desireless man do? Though he sees, he does not really see.
ashtavakra_gita::191.translation_literal: येन (by whom) विश्वमिदं (this entire world) दृष्टं (seen) स (he) नास्तीति (it is not) करोतु (may do) वै (indeed) । निर्वासनः (desireless) किं (what) कुरुते (does) पश्यन्नपि (though seeing) न (not) पश्यति (sees) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::191.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::191.essence: True seeing recognizes the world as unreal, though it still appears to the senses.
ashtavakra_gita::191.simple_meaning: A person who has truly understood the nature of the world can deny its reality. A desireless person may look but does not actually perceive the world as real.
ashtavakra_gita::191.simple_insight: You can look at the world without being caught by its illusions or attachments.
ashtavakra_gita::191.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that one who has realized the true nature of the world sees it as illusory. Even a desireless person who looks at the world does not see it as real. This challenges ordinary perception, pointing to deeper wisdom.
ashtavakra_gita::191.modern_relevance: You might scroll endlessly through images and news, but true understanding means seeing beyond appearances, not just looking.
ashtavakra_gita::191.insight: It teaches to distinguish between mere sensory perception and true understanding beyond appearances.

ashtavakra_gita::192.verse_sanskrit:
येन दृष्टं परं ब्रह्म सोऽहं ब्रह्मेति चिन्तयेत् ।
किं चिन्तयति निश्चिन्तो द्वितीयं यो न पश्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::192.verse_hindi: जिसने पर-ब्रह्म को देखा है वह भला ‘मैं ब्रह्म हूँ’ का चिन्तन भी करे, लेकिन जो निश्चिन्त होकर दूसरा कोई नहीं देखता वह क्या चिन्तन करे।
ashtavakra_gita::192.english_translation: One who has seen the supreme reality thinks 'I am that supreme reality'; but one who is without thought and sees no other, what contemplation remains for them?
ashtavakra_gita::192.translation_literal: येन (by whom) दृष्टं (seen) परं (supreme) ब्रह्म (reality) सः (that one) अहं (I) ब्रह्मेति (am supreme reality) चिन्तयेत् (thinks) । किं (what) चिन्तयति (thinks) निश्चिन्तः (without thought) द्वितीयं (second/other) यो (who) न (not) पश्यति (sees) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::192.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::192.essence: True realization ends all dual thoughts and leaves nothing left to contemplate.
ashtavakra_gita::192.simple_meaning: If you have truly realized the supreme reality as yourself, then the usual thinking about separation fades and no other thoughts remain.
ashtavakra_gita::192.simple_insight: There is peace in recognizing that beyond realization, mental effort and duality disappear.
ashtavakra_gita::192.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that once you have directly experienced the supreme reality as your true self, you naturally think 'I am that supreme reality.' But when the mind is fully settled and no duality is perceived, no further thinking or contemplation is necessary.
ashtavakra_gita::192.modern_relevance: After a breakthrough moment where you deeply understand yourself, your restless mind quiets and you don't need to analyze or overthink anymore.
ashtavakra_gita::192.insight: It shifts your mind from constant mental analysis to resting in direct knowing beyond thought.

ashtavakra_gita::193.verse_sanskrit:
दृष्टो येनात्मविक्षेपो निरोधं कुरुते त्वसौ ।
उदारस्तु न विक्षिप्तः साध्याभावात्करोति किम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::193.verse_hindi: जो आत्मा में विक्षेप देखता है वह भला चित्त का निरोध करे, लेकिन विक्षेपमुक्त उदारपुरुष साध्य के अभाव में क्या करे।
ashtavakra_gita::193.english_translation: The one who sees distraction in the self rightly restrains the mind, but what can the noble man who is free from distraction do without a goal?
ashtavakra_gita::193.translation_literal: दृष्टो (seen) येन (by whom) आत्म (self) विक्षेपो (distraction) निरोधं (restraint) कुरुते (does) त्वसौ (that) उदारः (noble) न (not) विक्षिप्तः (distracted) साध्याभावात् (due to lack of goal) करोति (does) किम् (what)
ashtavakra_gita::193.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::193.essence: Calming distraction is not enough; purpose is necessary for meaningful freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::193.simple_meaning: When you notice distraction in yourself, you can calm your mind. But if someone is free from distraction and has no purpose, what can they do?
ashtavakra_gita::193.simple_insight: Calming the mind is vital, but having a clear goal gives meaning to freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::193.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that recognizing distraction in the self allows you to control the restless mind. Yet, a noble person free from distraction but lacking a goal faces a dilemma: freedom alone without purpose feels incomplete.
ashtavakra_gita::193.modern_relevance: You might meditate to quiet your busy thoughts, but without a clear aim, that stillness can feel like emptiness rather than peace.
ashtavakra_gita::193.insight: It teaches you to balance inner calm with a guiding purpose to avoid feeling aimless.

ashtavakra_gita::194.verse_sanskrit:
धीरो लोकविपर्यस्तो वर्तमानोऽपि लोकवत् ।
न समाधिं न विक्षेपं न लोपं स्वस्य पश्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::194.verse_hindi: जो संसार की तरह बरतता हुआ भी संसार से भिन्न है । वह धीर पुरुष न अपनी समाधि को और न बन्धन को ही देखता है।
ashtavakra_gita::194.english_translation: The wise one behaves like the world but remains distinct; they neither see their stillness nor their bondage.
ashtavakra_gita::194.translation_literal: धीरो (wise one) / लोकविपर्यस्तो (behaving like the world) / वर्तमानोऽपि (even while present) / लोकवत् (like the world) / न (not) / समाधिं (stillness) / न (nor) / विक्षेपं (disturbance) / न (nor) / लोपं (loss) / स्वस्य (of oneself) / पश्यति (sees)
ashtavakra_gita::194.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::194.essence: You can live fully yet remain untouched by both stillness and bondage.
ashtavakra_gita::194.simple_meaning: You can live in the world without being caught by either your inner calm or your attachments.
ashtavakra_gita::194.simple_insight: There's freedom in acting fully while staying apart from inner calm and bondage alike.
ashtavakra_gita::194.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a wise person lives in the world yet does not identify with their inner peace or their bindings. This shows a state beyond duality, where external life and internal freedom coexist without conflict.
ashtavakra_gita::194.modern_relevance: You navigate daily challenges like everyone else but no longer get swept away by your emotions or limiting beliefs.
ashtavakra_gita::194.insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with your states to seeing yourself as the presence beyond both calm and disturbance.

ashtavakra_gita::195.verse_sanskrit:
भावाभावविहीनो यस्तृप्तो निर्वासनो बुधः ।
नैव किञ्चित्कृतं तेन लोकदृष्ट्या विकुर्वता ॥
ashtavakra_gita::195.verse_hindi: जो ज्ञानी पुरुष तृप्त है, भाव-अभाव से रहित है, वासना-रहित है वह लोक-दृष्टि से कर्म करता हुआ भी कुछ नहीं करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::195.english_translation: A wise person who is satisfied, free from desire and aversion, acts in the world yet does nothing.
ashtavakra_gita::195.translation_literal: भावाभावविहीनो (free from desire and aversion) / यः (who) / तृप्तो (satisfied) / निर्वासनो (free from longing) / बुधः (wise person) / नैव (indeed not) / किञ्चित्कृतं (anything done) / तेन (by him) / लोकदृष्ट्या (from worldly view) / विकुर्वता (acting)
ashtavakra_gita::195.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::195.essence: Acting without desire or aversion means doing yet not truly doing anything at all.
ashtavakra_gita::195.simple_meaning: A wise person who is satisfied and free from desire acts in the world but is not attached to the results or affected by actions.
ashtavakra_gita::195.simple_insight: You can engage in life fully without being weighed down by craving or aversion.
ashtavakra_gita::195.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that a truly wise person is free from desire and aversion, acting in the world without attachment. Even though they appear to do things, from the worldly perspective, they are untouched by action's binding effects.
ashtavakra_gita::195.modern_relevance: You finish a demanding project without craving praise or fearing failure—your peace stays intact regardless of outcome.
ashtavakra_gita::195.insight: It teaches you to act without attachment, seeing action as a natural flow, not a binding obligation.

ashtavakra_gita::196.verse_sanskrit:
प्रवृत्तौ वा निवृत्तौ वा नैव धीरस्य दुर्ग्रहः ।
यदा यत्कर्तुमायाति तत्कृत्वा तिष्ठतः सुखम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::196.verse_hindi: धीर पुरुष प्रवृत्ति अथवा निवृत्ति में दुराग्रह नहीं रखता । वह जब कभी भी कुछ करने को आ पड़ता है, उसको करके सुखपूर्वक रहता है ।
ashtavakra_gita::196.english_translation: The steady person holds no stubborn attachment in action or rest; whenever something calls, they do it and remain at ease.
ashtavakra_gita::196.translation_literal: प्रवृत्तौ (in activity) / वा (or) / निवृत्तौ (in rest) / वा (or) / नैव (not) / धीरस्य (of the steady person) / दुर्ग्रहः (stubborn attachment) / यदा (when) / यत्कर्तुम् (to do what) / आयाति (comes) / तत्कृत्वा (having done that) / तिष्ठतः (remaining) / सुखम् (at ease).
ashtavakra_gita::196.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::196.essence: True steadiness means no stubborn grip in doing or not doing, with ease throughout.
ashtavakra_gita::196.simple_meaning: You can be steady and peaceful whether you are doing something or resting, without clinging or resisting what happens.
ashtavakra_gita::196.simple_insight: There is freedom in flowing with what comes, without stubbornly holding on or pushing away.
ashtavakra_gita::196.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a wise person remains free from stubborn attachment both in action and in rest. Whether engaged or withdrawn, they respond naturally without inner resistance, maintaining ease and steadiness regardless of circumstance.
ashtavakra_gita::196.modern_relevance: You finish a task or take a break, without obsessing or resisting. That calm steadiness keeps stress away and lets you rest or act fully.
ashtavakra_gita::196.insight: It encourages shifting from pushing or resisting experiences to accepting and engaging with them naturally, fostering inner balance.

ashtavakra_gita::197.verse_sanskrit:
निर्वासनो निरालम्बः स्वच्छन्दो मुक्तबन्धनः ।
क्षिप्तः संस्कारवातेन चेष्टते शुष्कपर्णवत् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::197.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी पुरुष वासना-रहित, आलम्बन-रहित, स्वच्छन्द और बन्धन-रहित संसाररूपी वायु से प्रेरित होकर शुष्क पत्ते की भाँति व्यवहार करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::197.english_translation: The wise person is free from desires and attachments, acting spontaneously, moved by the wind of worldly impressions like a dry leaf.
ashtavakra_gita::197.translation_literal: निर्वासनो (desireless) निरालम्बः (without support) स्वच्छन्दो (free-willed) मुक्तबन्धनः (free from bonds) क्षिप्तः (driven) संस्कारवातेन (by the wind of impressions) चेष्टते (acts) शुष्कपर्णवत् (like a dry leaf)
ashtavakra_gita::197.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::197.essence: True freedom means acting spontaneously without craving or attachment, like a dry leaf in the wind.
ashtavakra_gita::197.simple_meaning: A wise person acts without craving or dependence, spontaneously moving like a dry leaf blown by the wind of impressions.
ashtavakra_gita::197.simple_insight: There's peace in acting freely, without clinging to desires or supports.
ashtavakra_gita::197.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes the wise person whose mind is free from desires and attachments. Like a dry leaf blown by the wind, such a person acts spontaneously, without clinging or support, unaffected by the impressions of the changing world.
ashtavakra_gita::197.modern_relevance: You notice how sometimes you're pushed by moods or expectations, yet the freer you are from clinging, the more naturally you respond without stress.
ashtavakra_gita::197.insight: It teaches you to let go of craving and support, acting with freedom instead of resistance.

ashtavakra_gita::198.verse_sanskrit:
असंसारस्य तु क्वापि न हर्षो न विषादता ।
स शीतलमना नित्यं विदेह इव राजये ॥
ashtavakra_gita::198.verse_hindi: संसारमुक्त पुरुष को न तो कभी हर्ष होता है, न विषाद । वह शान्तमना सदा विदेह की भाँति शोभता है।
ashtavakra_gita::198.english_translation: The one free from worldly existence neither feels joy nor sorrow; always calm, they shine like the bodiless.
ashtavakra_gita::198.translation_literal: असंसारस्य (of the one free from worldly existence) / तु (but) / क्वापि (anywhere) / न (not) / हर्षो (joy) / न (nor) / विषादता (sorrow) / । (.) / स (that one) / शीतलमना (cool-minded) / नित्यं (always) / विदेह (bodiless) / इव (like) / राजये (shines) / ॥
ashtavakra_gita::198.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::198.essence: True freedom means being steady and calm beyond all joy and sorrow.
ashtavakra_gita::198.simple_meaning: A person free from worldly bonds does not experience joy or sorrow and remains calm like one without a body.
ashtavakra_gita::198.simple_insight: There is peace in being steady beyond emotional highs and lows.
ashtavakra_gita::198.detailed_meaning: In the dialogue, Ashtavakra describes the liberated one who no longer reacts emotionally to the changing world. This person remains serene and shines with a calmness like a being beyond physical form.
ashtavakra_gita::198.modern_relevance: You’ve faced moments when success or failure no longer disturb your inner calm but you remain steady and clear within.
ashtavakra_gita::198.insight: It teaches you to hold steady and shine with calmness regardless of emotional swings.

ashtavakra_gita::199.verse_sanskrit:
कुत्रापि न जिहासास्ति नाशो वापि न कुत्रचित् ।
आत्मारामस्य धीरस्य शीतलाच्छतरात्मनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::199.verse_hindi: आत्मा में रमण करने वाले और शीतल तथा निर्मल चित्त वाले धीर पुरुष की न कहीं त्याग की इच्छा है, न कहीं ग्रहण की आशा है।
ashtavakra_gita::199.english_translation: The steady one who delights in the true self and has a calm, clear mind neither desires to give up nor hopes to acquire anything.
ashtavakra_gita::199.translation_literal: कुत्रापि (anywhere) / न (not) / जिहासास्ति (desire to give up) / नाशो (destruction) / वापि (nor) / न (not) / कुत्रचित् (anywhere) / आत्मारामस्य (of the one delighted in self) / धीरस्य (of the steady) / शीतलाच्छतरात्मनः (of the one with a cool and clear mind)
ashtavakra_gita::199.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::199.essence: True steadiness comes from neither wanting to lose nor hoping to gain anything.
ashtavakra_gita::199.simple_meaning: A person who enjoys their true self and has a calm, pure mind does not desire to give up or to acquire anything.
ashtavakra_gita::199.simple_insight: You feel peaceful when you stop wanting to lose or gain anything.
ashtavakra_gita::199.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes a wise person who dwells joyfully in their true self and whose mind remains cool and clear; such a person neither craves loss nor seeks gain, embodying complete inner steadiness.
ashtavakra_gita::199.modern_relevance: After a tough day, you sit quietly and realize you don’t need to push for more or fear losing what you have to feel calm.
ashtavakra_gita::199.insight: It teaches you to rest fully in yourself without chasing or rejecting experiences, freeing your mind from craving.

ashtavakra_gita::200.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकृत्या शून्यचित्तस्य कुर्वतोऽस्य यदृच्छया ।
प्राकृतस्येव धीरस्य न मानो नावमानता ॥
ashtavakra_gita::200.verse_hindi: स्वाभाविक रूप से जो शून्यचित्त है और सहजरूप से जो कर्म करता है, उस धीर पुरुष को सामान्यजन की तरह, न मान है और न अपमान है।
ashtavakra_gita::200.english_translation: A steady person whose mind is naturally empty and who acts spontaneously is neither honored nor dishonored like ordinary people.
ashtavakra_gita::200.translation_literal: प्रकृत्या (by nature) शून्यचित्तस्य (of empty-minded) कुर्वतोऽस्य (who acts) यदृच्छया (spontaneously) । प्राकृतस्येव (just like natural) धीरस्य (of the steady one) न (not) मानो (honor) न (nor) आवमानता (dishonor) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::200.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::200.essence: Natural action from an empty mind leaves you untouched by praise or blame.
ashtavakra_gita::200.simple_meaning: You act naturally with an empty mind and stay steady without caring about praise or insult.
ashtavakra_gita::200.simple_insight: There's freedom in acting without needing approval or fearing blame.
ashtavakra_gita::200.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a steady person with an empty mind acts spontaneously without attachment to others’ opinions, remaining unaffected by honor or dishonor.
ashtavakra_gita::200.modern_relevance: You completed your task honestly and naturally. Whether others applaud or criticize, you remain steady and unshaken.
ashtavakra_gita::200.insight: It guides you to act from your true nature without craving recognition or fearing judgment.

ashtavakra_gita::201.verse_sanskrit:
कृतं देहेन कर्मेदं न मया शुद्धरूपिणा ।
इति चिन्तानुरोधी यः कुर्वन्नपि करोति न ॥
ashtavakra_gita::201.verse_hindi: यह कर्म शरीर से किया गया है, मुझ शुद्ध स्वरूप द्वारा नहीं । ऐसी चिन्तना का जो अनुगमन करता है, वह कर्म करता हुआ भी नहीं करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::201.english_translation: The actions are done by the body, not by my pure true self. One who follows this understanding acts but is not truly acting.
ashtavakra_gita::201.translation_literal: कृतं (done) / देहेन (by the body) / कर्मे (action) / एदं (this) / न (not) / मया (by me) / शुद्धरूपिणा (pure-formed) / इति (thus) / चिन्ता (thought) / अनुरोधी (following) / यः (who) / कुर्वन् (doing) / अपि (even) / करोति (acts) / न (not)
ashtavakra_gita::201.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::201.essence: Your pure true self is always separate and untouched by bodily actions.
ashtavakra_gita::201.simple_meaning: The body performs actions, but your pure true self does not. If you understand this, you act without being truly bound by the actions.
ashtavakra_gita::201.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing your true self is untouched by what your body does.
ashtavakra_gita::201.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains to King Janaka that all actions happen through the body, never through the pure true self. This insight frees the mind from identifying with bodily deeds, showing that even while acting, the true self remains uninvolved.
ashtavakra_gita::201.modern_relevance: When you face pressure to perform or succeed, remember that your deepest self is not responsible for the outcomes, only your body and mind are.
ashtavakra_gita::201.insight: It shifts your perspective from identifying with your actions to witnessing them as separate from your true self.

ashtavakra_gita::202.verse_sanskrit:
अतद्वादीव कुरुते न भवेदपि बालिशः ।
जीवन्मुक्तः सुखी श्रीमान् संसरन्नपि शोभते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::202.verse_hindi: जीवन्मुक्त, उस सामान्यजन की तरह कर्म करता है, जो कहता कुछ और है और करता कुछ और है, तो वह मूढ़ नहीं होता है और वह सुखी श्रीमान् संसार में रहकर भी शोभायमान होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::202.english_translation: One liberated while living acts like an ordinary person, not foolish, and shines happily even within the world.
ashtavakra_gita::202.translation_literal: अतद्वादीव (like one who speaks thus) / कुरुते (does) / न (not) / भवेदपि (although) / बालिशः (foolish) / जीवन्मुक्तः (liberated while living) / सुखी (happy) / श्रीमान् (respected, glorious) / संसरन् (dwelling in the world) / अपि (also) / शोभते (shines)
ashtavakra_gita::202.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::202.essence: True freedom lets you live fully and shine happily within the world.
ashtavakra_gita::202.simple_meaning: A person who is free inside can act like any normal person without confusion and live happily within the world.
ashtavakra_gita::202.simple_insight: You can be free and joyful without withdrawing from life or pretending to be someone else.
ashtavakra_gita::202.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra tells Janaka that a truly liberated person acts in the world like anyone else but without foolishness or confusion. This person enjoys life, shines with dignity, and is not bound by external circumstances.
ashtavakra_gita::202.modern_relevance: You might feel pressured to hide your true freedom or joy to fit in, but real freedom means shining authentically wherever you are.
ashtavakra_gita::202.insight: It teaches you that inner freedom does not require withdrawing or acting differently; you can engage fully and still be free.

ashtavakra_gita::203.verse_sanskrit:
नानाविचारसुश्रान्तो धीरो विश्रान्तिमागतः ।
न कल्पते न जाति न श‍ृणोति न पश्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::203.verse_hindi: जो धीर पुरुष अनेक प्रकार के विचारों से थककर शान्ति को उपलब्ध होता है वह न कल्पना करता है, न जानता है, न सुनता है, न देखता है।
ashtavakra_gita::203.english_translation: The wise man, exhausted by many kinds of thoughts and having attained peace, neither imagines, knows, hears, nor sees.
ashtavakra_gita::203.translation_literal: नानाविचारसुश्रान्तो (exhausted by many thoughts) / धीरो (wise man) / विश्रान्तिमागतः (having attained rest) / न (not) / कल्पते (imagines) / न (not) / जाति (knows) / न (not) / शृणोति (hears) / न (not) / पश्यति (sees)
ashtavakra_gita::203.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::203.essence: Deep peace arises when the mind ceases all mental and sensory activity.
ashtavakra_gita::203.simple_meaning: When your mind tires of endless thoughts and reaches peace, it stops imagining, knowing, hearing, and seeing.
ashtavakra_gita::203.simple_insight: There is calm in ceasing to chase every thought and sense impression.
ashtavakra_gita::203.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes the wise person who, exhausted by many thoughts, attains a state of deep peace where the usual mental activities—imagining, knowing, hearing, and seeing—no longer occur, illustrating complete inner stillness.
ashtavakra_gita::203.modern_relevance: After a day overwhelmed by nonstop mental chatter and distractions, you finally feel a deep calm when your mind stops reacting to it all.
ashtavakra_gita::203.insight: It teaches you to rest beyond active mind and senses, opening space for true peace.

ashtavakra_gita::204.verse_sanskrit:
असमाधेरविक्षेपान् न मुमुक्षुर्न चेतरः ।
निश्चित्य कल्पितं पश्यन् ब्रह्मैवास्ते महाशयः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::204.verse_hindi: महाशय पुरुष विक्षेप-रहित और समाधि-रहित होने के कारण न मुमुक्षु है, न गैर-मुमुक्षु होता है । वह निश्चयपूर्वक संसार को कल्पित देखकर ब्रह्मवत् रहता है।
ashtavakra_gita::204.english_translation: A great being, free from distraction and without attachment to stillness, is neither seeker nor non-seeker; firmly seeing the world as imagined, they remain like the supreme reality.
ashtavakra_gita::204.translation_literal: असमाधेर (without stillness) / अविक्षेपान् (free from distraction) / न (not) / मुमुक्षुर्न (neither seeker) / चेतरः (nor non-seeker) / निश्चित्य (firmly seeing) / कल्पितं (imagined) / पश्यन् (seeing) / ब्रह्मैवास्ते (like the supreme reality there) / महाशयः (great being)
ashtavakra_gita::204.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::204.essence: Freedom comes when seeking and rejecting both fall away by clearly seeing the world as imagined.
ashtavakra_gita::204.simple_meaning: A truly free person neither desires liberation nor rejects it; they see the world as a creation of the mind and remain steady like the supreme reality.
ashtavakra_gita::204.simple_insight: You can feel free by letting go of the need to seek or avoid, simply by seeing clearly.
ashtavakra_gita::204.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that a great being neither chases freedom nor denies it because they recognize the world as an imagined appearance, resting in the unchanging supreme reality beyond distractions and attachment.
ashtavakra_gita::204.modern_relevance: When you stop chasing every desire or pushing away what comes, and simply observe your thoughts as passing images, you find calm that isn’t shaken by craving.
ashtavakra_gita::204.insight: It shifts your mind from restless wanting or rejecting to steady clear seeing without distraction or attachment.

ashtavakra_gita::205.verse_sanskrit:
यस्यान्तः स्यादहङ्कारो न करोति करोति सः ।
निरहङ्कारधीरेण न किञ्चिदकृतं कृतम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::205.verse_hindi: जिसके अन्तःकरण में अहंकार है, वह कर्म नहीं करते हुए भी कर्म करता है और अहंकार-रहित धीर पुरुष कर्म करते हुए भी नहीं करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::205.english_translation: One with ego inside acts without acting; one free of ego acts without acting.
ashtavakra_gita::205.translation_literal: यस्यान्तः (inside whose) स्यादहङ्कारो (ego is) न (not) करोति (acts) करोति (acts) सः (he). निरहङ्कारधीरेण (by the one steady without ego) न (not) किञ्चिदकृतं (anything done) कृतम् (done).
ashtavakra_gita::205.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::205.essence: Ego causes you to act compulsively; freedom lets you act without attachment.
ashtavakra_gita::205.simple_meaning: If your mind is filled with ego, you act even when you don’t intend to. If you are free from ego, you may act but remain untouched by it.
ashtavakra_gita::205.simple_insight: There is freedom in acting without ego and illusion in acting through ego.
ashtavakra_gita::205.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that a person dominated by ego acts compulsively, unaware of true action. The wise who have no ego act consciously but are not bound by their actions. This reveals the inner paradox of action and ego.
ashtavakra_gita::205.modern_relevance: You may feel trapped by your own pride or self-importance, causing restless doing. Yet when you let go of ego, your actions flow freely without inner conflict.
ashtavakra_gita::205.insight: It teaches you to distinguish ego-driven reactions from conscious, detached action, freeing your experience of doing.

ashtavakra_gita::206.verse_sanskrit:
नोद्विग्नं न च सन्तुष्टमकर्तृ स्पन्दवर्जितम् ।
निराशं गतसन्देहं चित्तं मुक्तस्य राजते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::206.verse_hindi: मुक्तपुरुष का उद्वेग-रहित, संतोष-रहित, कर्तव्य-रहित, स्पन्द-रहित, आशा-रहित, सन्देह-रहित चित्त ही शोभायमान है।
ashtavakra_gita::206.english_translation: The mind of a liberated person shines, free from agitation, contentment, doership, movement, hope, and doubt.
ashtavakra_gita::206.translation_literal: नोद्विग्नं (not agitated) / न (and not) / च (also) / सन्तुष्टम (content) / अकर्तृ (without doer) / स्पन्दवर्जितम् (devoid of movement) / निराशं (without hope) / गतसन्देहं (free from doubt) / चित्तं (mind) / मुक्तस्य (of the liberated) / राजते (shines)
ashtavakra_gita::206.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::206.essence: A liberated mind shines by being free from agitation, hope, and doubt.
ashtavakra_gita::206.simple_meaning: A truly free person’s mind is calm and steady, without restlessness, desires, or doubts.
ashtavakra_gita::206.simple_insight: You can feel peaceful and radiant when your mind lets go of agitation and hope.
ashtavakra_gita::206.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes the mind of one who is liberated from all emotional and mental disturbances. This mind is free from agitation, desire for results, the sense of doership, restlessness, hope, and doubt. It shines with natural peace and clarity.
ashtavakra_gita::206.modern_relevance: When your thoughts race and doubts cloud your mind, imagine the calm brightness of a mind free from all that.
ashtavakra_gita::206.insight: This verse teaches you to recognize the natural peace and clarity that arises when you release restless wanting and uncertainty.

ashtavakra_gita::207.verse_sanskrit:
निर्ध्यातुं चेष्टितुं वापि यच्चित्तं न प्रवर्तते ।
निर्निमित्तमिदं किन्तु निर्ध्यायेति विचेष्टते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::207.verse_hindi: मुक्तपुरुष का चित्त ध्यान या चेष्टा में प्रवृत्त नहीं होता है । लेकिन वह निमित्त या हेतु के बिना ध्यान करता है और कर्म करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::207.english_translation: The mind of the liberated person neither dwells on meditation nor on effort; yet it meditates and acts without any cause.
ashtavakra_gita::207.translation_literal: निर्ध्यातुं (to meditate) / चेष्टितुं (to act) / वापि (also) / यत् (that which) / चित्तं (mind) / न (not) / प्रवर्तते (moves) / । / निर्-निमित्तम् (without cause) / इदं (this) / किन्तु (but) / निर्ध्यायेति (it meditates) / विचेष्टते (it acts) / ॥
ashtavakra_gita::207.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::207.essence: True freedom means acting and meditating naturally without effort or cause.
ashtavakra_gita::207.simple_meaning: The liberated mind does not get caught in trying to meditate or act, yet it naturally does both without needing a reason.
ashtavakra_gita::207.simple_insight: There is freedom in acting and being without forcing or expecting anything.
ashtavakra_gita::207.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that the mind of the free person neither struggles to meditate nor pushes to act. Instead, it flows naturally, acting and resting without being driven by causes or desires, showing freedom beyond effort.
ashtavakra_gita::207.modern_relevance: You sit quietly, not forcing calm or productivity, yet your focus and actions arise naturally without strain or pressure.
ashtavakra_gita::207.insight: It teaches you to release the need to force meditation or action and trust natural flow without cause or effort.

ashtavakra_gita::208.verse_sanskrit:
तत्त्वं यथार्थमाकर्ण्य मन्दः प्राप्नोति मूढताम् ।
अथवा याति सङ्कोचममूढः कोऽपि मूढवत् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::208.verse_hindi: मन्दबुद्धि यथार्थत्व को सुनकर मूढ़ता को ही प्राप्त होता है । लेकिन कोई ज्ञानी मूढ़वत् होकर संकोच या समाधि को प्राप्त होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::208.english_translation: A dull mind perceives truth and only attains confusion; a wise person may also appear foolish by entering hesitation or absorption.
ashtavakra_gita::208.translation_literal: तत्त्वं (truth) यथार्थम् (real/actual) आकर्ण्य (not hearing) मन्दः (dull) प्राप्नोति (attains) मूढताम् (foolishness) । अथवा (or) याति (goes) सङ्कोचम् (hesitation) अमूढः (not foolish) कोऽपि (anyone) मूढवत् (like a fool) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::208.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::208.essence: Not hearing truth clearly causes confusion; wisdom may appear foolish in deep hesitation.
ashtavakra_gita::208.simple_meaning: Ignoring or not truly understanding truth leads to confusion; even a wise person can seem foolish when deeply hesitant or absorbed.
ashtavakra_gita::208.simple_insight: It’s okay if you feel confused or look foolish while deeply trying to understand truth.
ashtavakra_gita::208.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra points out that a dull mind that does not grasp truth clearly only gains confusion, but even a wise person may seem foolish when entering deep hesitation or absorption, showing that appearances can mislead.
ashtavakra_gita::208.modern_relevance: You may feel stuck or foolish when wrestling with complex ideas, but hesitation is part of deep understanding.
ashtavakra_gita::208.insight: This verse shifts your view of hesitation from weakness to a phase of deep inquiry and growth.

ashtavakra_gita::209.verse_sanskrit:
एकाग्रता निरोधो वा मूढैरभ्यस्यते भृशम् ।
धीराः कृत्यं न पश्यन्ति सुप्तवत्स्वपदे स्थिताः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::209.verse_hindi: अज्ञानी चित्त की एकाग्रता अथवा निरोध का बहुत अभ्यास करता है लेकिन धीर पुरुष सोये हुए व्यक्ति की तरह अपने स्वभाव में स्थिर रहकर कुछ करने योग्य नहीं देखता है।
ashtavakra_gita::209.english_translation: The ignorant intensely practice concentration or restraint of the mind, but the wise, like one asleep, remain steady in their nature and see no need for action.
ashtavakra_gita::209.translation_literal: एकाग्रता (concentration) / निरोधः (restraint) / वा (or) / मूढैः (by the ignorant) / अभ्यस्यते (is practiced) / भृशम् (intensely) / धीराः (the wise) / कृत्यम् (action) / न (not) / पश्यन्ति (see) / सुप्तवत् (like asleep) / स्वपदे (in their nature) / स्थिताः (standing/remaining).
ashtavakra_gita::209.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::209.essence: True wisdom is steady and effortless; forced concentration is the ignorant's struggle.
ashtavakra_gita::209.simple_meaning: Trying hard to force your mind to focus is a struggle of the ignorant. The wise remain naturally steady and do not feel the need to force anything.
ashtavakra_gita::209.simple_insight: There is calm confidence in resting in your nature instead of straining your mind.
ashtavakra_gita::209.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra contrasts those who forcefully try to control their restless mind with the wise who remain effortlessly steady in their true nature, like someone deeply asleep and undisturbed. This teaching comes as a challenge to overexertion in spiritual practice.
ashtavakra_gita::209.modern_relevance: You find yourself exhausting endless efforts to quiet your racing thoughts, but lasting peace comes when you stop forcing control and simply rest in your true nature.
ashtavakra_gita::209.insight: It teaches you to stop pushing your mind and instead gently rest in natural steadiness, seeing no need for forced effort.

ashtavakra_gita::210.verse_sanskrit:
अप्रयत्नात् प्रयत्नाद् वा मूढो नाप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ।
तत्त्वनिश्चयमात्रेण प्राज्ञो भवति निर्वृतः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::210.verse_hindi: अज्ञानी पुरुष प्रयत्न अथवा अप्रयत्न से निवृत्ति को प्राप्त नहीं होता है जबकि ज्ञानी पुरुष केवल तत्त्व को निश्चयपूर्वक जानकर ही निवृत्त हो जाता है।
ashtavakra_gita::210.english_translation: A fool does not attain freedom by effort or non-effort; the wise become free only by firm certainty in truth.
ashtavakra_gita::210.translation_literal: अप्रयत्नात् (not by non-effort) / प्रयत्नाद् (nor by effort) / वा (either) / मूढो (a fool) / नाप्नोति (does not attain) / निर्वृतिम् (freedom) / तत्त्वनिश्चयमात्रेण (by mere firm certainty in truth) / प्राज्ञो (the wise) / भवति (becomes) / निर्वृतः (free)
ashtavakra_gita::210.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::210.essence: Freedom arises from firm certainty in truth, not from effort or non-effort.
ashtavakra_gita::210.simple_meaning: Trying hard or not trying at all does not bring freedom; only firm understanding of truth frees you.
ashtavakra_gita::210.simple_insight: You feel relief knowing freedom is about clarity, not endless struggle.
ashtavakra_gita::210.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Ashtavakra tells that a confused person cannot find freedom by mere effort or avoidance. Only a wise person who firmly knows the truth becomes truly free, showing freedom arises from clear understanding, not from trying harder or giving up.
ashtavakra_gita::210.modern_relevance: You’ve pushed yourself to the limit or tried to quit, yet freedom still feels distant. This shows freedom is about clear inner certainty, not effort alone.
ashtavakra_gita::210.insight: It shifts your focus from action or inaction to cultivating clear inner certainty as the path to freedom.

ashtavakra_gita::211.verse_sanskrit:
शुद्धं बुद्धं प्रियं पूर्णं निष्प्रपञ्चं निरामयम् ।
आत्मानं तं न जानन्ति तत्राभ्यासपरा जनाः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::211.verse_hindi: इस संसार में अभ्यास परायण पुरुष उस आत्मा को नहीं जान पाते जो शुद्ध, बुद्ध, प्रिय, पूर्ण, प्रपञ्च-रहित और दुःख-रहित है।
ashtavakra_gita::211.english_translation: In this world, those devoted to practice do not know the true self that is pure, wise, beloved, complete, free from appearance, and free from suffering.
ashtavakra_gita::211.translation_literal: शुद्धं (pure) बुद्धं (wise) प्रियं (beloved) पूर्णं (complete) निष्प्रपञ्चं (free of appearance) निरामयम् (free of suffering) आत्मानं (true self) तं (that) न (not) जानन्ति (know) तत्र (there) अभ्यासपरा (devoted to practice) जनाः (people)
ashtavakra_gita::211.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::211.essence: Devoted effort alone cannot reveal the pure and complete true self.
ashtavakra_gita::211.simple_meaning: Many who focus deeply on practice fail to recognize their true self, which is pure, wise, and free from suffering and illusion.
ashtavakra_gita::211.simple_insight: There is a quiet sadness in not realizing what you truly are despite dedicated effort.
ashtavakra_gita::211.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra tells that even those who dedicate themselves fully to spiritual practice often miss recognizing the true self. This self is described as pure, wise, beloved, complete, without illusion or suffering. The moment highlights the paradox of spiritual effort and the elusive nature of true self-knowledge.
ashtavakra_gita::211.modern_relevance: You might spend hours on self-improvement routines yet still feel disconnected from your true essence hidden beneath the surface.
ashtavakra_gita::211.insight: It teaches that effort alone doesn’t guarantee self-knowledge; recognition of the true self requires a shift beyond practice.

ashtavakra_gita::212.verse_sanskrit:
नाप्नोति कर्मणा मोक्षं विमूढोऽभ्यासरूपिणा ।
धन्यो विज्ञानमात्रेण मुक्तस्तिष्ठत्यविक्रियः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::212.verse_hindi: अज्ञानी पुरुष अभ्यासरूपी कर्म से मोक्ष को प्राप्त नहीं होता है । जबकि क्रिया-रहित ज्ञानी पुरुष केवल ज्ञान के द्वारा मुक्त हुआ स्थिर रहता है।
ashtavakra_gita::212.english_translation: A confused person does not attain freedom through habitual action; instead, the wise, free and unmoved, remains established by knowledge alone.
ashtavakra_gita::212.translation_literal: नाप्नोति (does not attain) / कर्मणा (by action) / मोक्षं (freedom) / विमूढः (confused) / अभ्यासरूपिणा (by habitual practice) / धन्यो (fortunate/well-off) / विज्ञानमात्रेण (by knowledge alone) / मुक्तः (free) / तिष्ठत्य (remains) / अविक्रियः (unmoved).
ashtavakra_gita::212.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::212.essence: Freedom is not earned by busy action but by steady, unmoved knowledge.
ashtavakra_gita::212.simple_meaning: Freedom cannot be gained through repeated actions done in confusion. Only steady knowledge brings true freedom and stillness.
ashtavakra_gita::212.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing that freedom comes from clear understanding, not endless doing.
ashtavakra_gita::212.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra addresses the confused seeker who relies on habitual rituals and actions to gain freedom. He contrasts this with the wise person who is free because of deep knowledge and remains steady without needing constant activity.
ashtavakra_gita::212.modern_relevance: You might push yourself through endless routines, hoping for peace, but real freedom arrives when you understand and stop the restless cycle.
ashtavakra_gita::212.insight: Shift from relying on repeated effort to trusting clear understanding as the source of freedom.

ashtavakra_gita::213.verse_sanskrit:
मूढो नाप्नोति तद् ब्रह्म यतो भवितुमिच्छति ।
अनिच्छन्नपि धीरो हि परब्रह्मस्वरूपभाक् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::213.verse_hindi: अज्ञानी जैसे ब्रह्म होने की इच्छा करता है वैसे ही ब्रह्म नहीं हो पाता है और धीर पुरुष नहीं चाहता हुआ भी निश्चित ही परब्रह्म स्वरूप को भजने वाला होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::213.english_translation: The ignorant who desires to become the supreme reality does not attain it; the wise, even without desire, naturally reflect the supreme reality's nature.
ashtavakra_gita::213.translation_literal: मूढः (foolish/ignorant) न (not) आप्नोति (attains) तत् (that) ब्रह्म (supreme reality) यतः (because) भवितुम् (to become) इच्छति (desires) । अनिच्छन्नपि (even without desire) धीः (wise one) हि (indeed) परब्रह्म (supreme reality) स्वरूप (nature) भाक् (reflects) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::213.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::213.essence: Desiring to become the true self blocks you; wisdom embodies it effortlessly.
ashtavakra_gita::213.simple_meaning: Trying to become the true self by desire keeps you from it, but a wise person naturally embodies it without wanting.
ashtavakra_gita::213.simple_insight: There is freedom in letting go of craving and allowing your true nature to shine through.
ashtavakra_gita::213.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that an ignorant person who desires to become the supreme reality fails, while a wise person, even without desire, naturally reflects that supreme nature. This teaching shows the paradox of effort and surrender at the start of Janaka's spiritual inquiry.
ashtavakra_gita::213.modern_relevance: You may struggle to become who you truly are by forcing change, but real transformation happens when you stop pushing and simply let your true self emerge.
ashtavakra_gita::213.insight: It teaches you to release your craving for transformation and trust in the natural expression of your true nature.

ashtavakra_gita::214.verse_sanskrit:
निराधारा ग्रहव्यग्रा मूढाः संसारपोषकाः ।
एतस्यानर्थमूलस्य मूलच्छेदः कृतो बुधैः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::214.verse_hindi: इस आधार-रहित, दुराग्रह-युक्त संसार का पोषक अज्ञानी पुरुष ही है । इस अनर्थ के मूल संसार का मूलाच्छेद ज्ञानियों द्वारा किया गया है।
ashtavakra_gita::214.english_translation: The ignorant person who clings to this unsupported, grasping world is its sustainer; the root of this harm, the root of the world, has been cut by the wise.
ashtavakra_gita::214.translation_literal: निराधारा (unsupported) / ग्रहव्यग्रा (possessive, grasping) / मूढाः (ignorant) / संसारपोषकाः (sustainer of the world) । एतस्यानर्थमूलस्य (of this harm's root) / मूलच्छेदः (root cutting) / कृतो (done) / बुधैः (by the wise) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::214.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::214.essence: Clinging ignorance sustains the world; wisdom ends it by cutting grasping’s root.
ashtavakra_gita::214.simple_meaning: People who ignorantly cling to the unstable world keep it alive; the wise remove this root cause by cutting attachment.
ashtavakra_gita::214.simple_insight: You can find freedom by seeing and releasing the grasping that keeps you stuck.
ashtavakra_gita::214.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that ignorant people sustain the world by clinging to it without true support. The wise end suffering by cutting the root, which is this grasping attachment that creates the world’s illusion.
ashtavakra_gita::214.modern_relevance: You hold tightly to worries and desires that lack stable ground, feeding your own stress; true relief comes when you stop supporting these harmful patterns.
ashtavakra_gita::214.insight: It teaches you to recognize clinging as the source of suffering and to let go with wisdom.

ashtavakra_gita::215.verse_sanskrit:
न शान्तिं लभते मूढो यतः शमितुमिच्छति ।
धीरस्तत्त्वं विनिश्चित्य सर्वदा शान्तमानसः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::215.verse_hindi: अज्ञानी जैसे शान्त होने की इच्छा करता है, वैसे ही वह शान्ति को नहीं प्राप्त होता है किन्तु धीर पुरुष तत्त्व को जानकर सदैव शान्त मन वाला है।
ashtavakra_gita::215.english_translation: The foolish never find peace because they try to force it; the wise, knowing the truth, remain always calm.
ashtavakra_gita::215.translation_literal: न (not) शान्तिं (peace) लभते (obtains) मूढो (foolish person) यतः (because) शमितुम् (to calm) इच्छति (wants) । धीरः (wise one) तत्त्वं (truth) विनिश्चित्य (having known) सर्वदा (always) शान्तमानसः (peaceful minded) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::215.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::215.essence: Peace cannot be forced; it arises naturally from deep knowing and steady mind.
ashtavakra_gita::215.simple_meaning: Trying to force peace never works. True calm comes when you understand reality deeply and accept it.
ashtavakra_gita::215.simple_insight: Peace feels natural and steady when you stop pushing for it and simply know what is.
ashtavakra_gita::215.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Ashtavakra contrasts the restless fool who chases peace with the wise person who, having grasped the truth of existence, maintains steady calm regardless of external turmoil.
ashtavakra_gita::215.modern_relevance: After a hectic day, trying hard to relax only makes you more restless. Real calm begins when you stop forcing it and accept things as they are.
ashtavakra_gita::215.insight: It shifts the mind from pushing for peace to resting in clear understanding and acceptance.

ashtavakra_gita::216.verse_sanskrit:
क्वात्मनो दर्शनं तस्य यद् दृष्टमवलम्बते ।
धीरास्तं तं न पश्यन्ति पश्यन्त्यात्मानमव्ययम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::216.verse_hindi: उसको आत्मा का दर्शन कहाँ जो दृश्य का अवलम्बन करता है । धीर पुरुष दृश्य को नहीं देखते हैं । वे अविनाशी आत्मा को देखते हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::216.english_translation: Those who depend on what is seen do not perceive the true self; the wise see the imperishable true self.
ashtavakra_gita::216.translation_literal: क्व (where) / आत्मन (of the self) / दर्शनं (vision) / तस्य (of that) / यद् (what) / दृष्टम् (seen) / अवलम्बते (depends) / धीराः (wise) / तं (that) / न (not) / पश्यन्ति (see) / पश्यन्ति (see) / आत्मानम् (true self) / अव्ययम् (imperishable)
ashtavakra_gita::216.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::216.essence: Your true self cannot be found by relying on what is seen.
ashtavakra_gita::216.simple_meaning: You cannot truly know your inner self by relying on external appearances; the wise perceive the unchanging true self beyond what is seen.
ashtavakra_gita::216.simple_insight: There's freedom in realizing your real self is beyond fleeting appearances.
ashtavakra_gita::216.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that those who base their understanding on the visible world miss the true self, which is imperishable and beyond appearances. The wise perceive this deeper reality beyond the senses.
ashtavakra_gita::216.modern_relevance: When you judge yourself or others by surface impressions, you miss their deeper value and your own inner truth.
ashtavakra_gita::216.insight: Shift focus from external appearances to the unchanging true self for deeper clarity.

ashtavakra_gita::217.verse_sanskrit:
क्व निरोधो विमूढस्य यो निर्बन्धं करोति वै ।
स्वारामस्यैव धीरस्य सर्वदासावकृत्रिमः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::217.verse_hindi: जो हठपूर्वक चित्त का निरोध करता है, उस अज्ञानी को कहाँ चित्त का निरोध है । स्वयं में रमण करने वाले धीर पुरुष के लिए यह चित्त का निरोध स्वाभाविक है।
ashtavakra_gita::217.english_translation: Where is the restraint of the mind for one who forcibly tries to control it? For the steady person absorbed in the self, that restraint is natural.
ashtavakra_gita::217.translation_literal: क्व (where) / निरोधो (restraint) / विमूढस्य (of the deluded one) / यो (who) / निर्बन्धं (forcibly) / करोति (does) / वै (indeed) । स्वारामस्यैव (of the self-controlled) / धीरस्य (of the steady one) / सर्वदासावकृत्रिमः (natural / without artificiality) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::217.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::217.essence: True mental calm cannot be forced; it arises naturally from steady self-absorption.
ashtavakra_gita::217.simple_meaning: Trying to forcibly control the restless mind shows confusion. Real calm happens naturally when you are steady and absorbed in your true self.
ashtavakra_gita::217.simple_insight: True calm isn't forced; it arises effortlessly when you are steady within.
ashtavakra_gita::217.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that someone who tries to control the mind by force is confused and fails. Instead, the wise and steady person who dwells in their true self experiences natural mental calm without struggle.
ashtavakra_gita::217.modern_relevance: You try to quiet your racing thoughts by sheer willpower, but peace only comes when you stop forcing it and relax into yourself.
ashtavakra_gita::217.insight: It shifts the mind from pushing to letting be, revealing that calmness is a natural state, not a forced achievement.

ashtavakra_gita::218.verse_sanskrit:
भावस्य भावकः कश्चिन् न किञ्चिद् भावकोपरः ।
उभयाभावकः कश्चिद् एवमेव निराकुलः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::218.verse_hindi: कोई भाव को मानने वाला है और कोई ‘कुछ भी नहीं है’ ऐसा मानने वाला है । वैसे ही कोई दोनों को मानने वाला है । वैसे ही कोई दोनों को नहीं मानने वाला है और वही स्वस्थचित्त है।
ashtavakra_gita::218.english_translation: Some identify with feelings, some deny them; one who is free from both is truly steady.
ashtavakra_gita::218.translation_literal: भावस्य (of feeling) भावकः (the one who accepts) कश्चिन् (some) न (not) किञ्चिद् (anything) भावकोपरः (one who denies feeling) । उभयाभावकः (one who accepts both) कश्चिद् (some) एवमेव (indeed) निराकुलः (untroubled) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::218.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::218.essence: True steadiness arises by neither accepting nor rejecting feelings.
ashtavakra_gita::218.simple_meaning: You may accept your feelings or deny them, but true peace comes when you neither cling nor reject them.
ashtavakra_gita::218.simple_insight: Peace is found in not being swayed either by embracing or rejecting feelings.
ashtavakra_gita::218.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that some people identify strongly with their feelings, while others deny them completely. But true steadiness of mind arises when one neither clings to feelings nor rejects them, remaining untroubled by either approach.
ashtavakra_gita::218.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed when you try to control emotions or pretend they don’t exist; peace grows by simply resting beyond that struggle.
ashtavakra_gita::218.insight: Shift your attention away from reacting to feelings and towards simply witnessing them without judgment.

ashtavakra_gita::219.verse_sanskrit:
शुद्धमद्वयमात्मानं भावयन्ति कुबुद्धयः ।
न तु जानन्ति संमोहाद्यावज्जीवमनिर्वृताः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::219.verse_hindi: कुबुद्धि पुरुष शुद्ध अद्वैत आत्मा की भावना करते हैं लेकिन मोहवश उसे नहीं जानते हैं इसलिए जीवन भर सुखरहित रहते हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::219.english_translation: Fools imagine the true self is pure non-duality but, lost in confusion, never truly know it and remain unhappy all their lives.
ashtavakra_gita::219.translation_literal: शुद्धम (pure) अद्वयम् (non-duality) आत्मानं (self) भावयन्ति (imagine) कुबुद्धयः (fools). न (not) तु (but) जानन्ति (know) संमोहात् (from confusion) यावत् (until) जीवः (living being) अनिर्वृताः (unfulfilled).
ashtavakra_gita::219.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::219.essence: Imagining the true self is not the same as knowing it, and confusion causes lifelong unrest.
ashtavakra_gita::219.simple_meaning: People confused by their mind imagine the true self as pure non-duality but never realize it due to their delusion, remaining unhappy their whole life.
ashtavakra_gita::219.simple_insight: There is sadness in realizing that imagining truth is not the same as knowing it.
ashtavakra_gita::219.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that those lacking clear understanding mistake the true self for an intellectual idea of pure non-duality. Because they remain trapped in confusion, they never experience the true self, resulting in lifelong dissatisfaction.
ashtavakra_gita::219.modern_relevance: You might think you understand yourself fully, but hidden confusion keeps you restless and unfulfilled despite your efforts.
ashtavakra_gita::219.insight: It teaches you to distinguish between intellectual ideas of truth and direct knowing, shifting focus from concepts to experience.

ashtavakra_gita::220.verse_sanskrit:
मुमुक्षोर्बुद्धिरालम्बमन्तरेण न विद्यते ।
निरालम्बैव निष्कामा बुद्धिर्मुक्तस्य सर्वदा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::220.verse_hindi: मुमुक्षु पुरुष की बुद्धि आलम्बन के बिना नहीं रहती । मुक्तपुरुष की बुद्धि सदा निष्काम और निरालम्ब रहती है।
ashtavakra_gita::220.english_translation: The seeker’s mind cannot stay without support; the liberated one’s mind is always desireless and unsupported.
ashtavakra_gita::220.translation_literal: मुमुक्षोर्बुद्धिर् (seeker's mind) आलम्बमन्तरेण (without support) न (not) विद्यते (exists) । निरालम्बैव (unsupported) निष्कामा (desireless) बुद्धिर्मुक्तस्य (mind of the liberated) सर्वदा (always) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::220.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::220.essence: True freedom is a mind free from craving and dependence on anything.
ashtavakra_gita::220.simple_meaning: A person seeking freedom depends on something to hold their mind. A truly free mind is always without craving or support.
ashtavakra_gita::220.simple_insight: You can feel peace when your mind stops needing something to hold onto.
ashtavakra_gita::220.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a seeker’s mind is unstable because it relies on external things. Only when the mind becomes desireless and unsupported does true freedom arise.
ashtavakra_gita::220.modern_relevance: You notice how often your mind clings to ideas or things to feel steady, and how tiring that is.
ashtavakra_gita::220.insight: It teaches you to notice your mind’s dependence and gently let go of needing support.

ashtavakra_gita::221.verse_sanskrit:
विषयद्वीपिनो वीक्ष्य चकिताः शरणार्थिनः ।
विशन्ति झटिति क्रोडं निरोधैकाग्रसिद्धये ॥
ashtavakra_gita::221.verse_hindi: विषयरूपी बाघ को देखकर भयभीत हुआ मनुष्य शरण की खोज में शीघ्र ही चित्त के निरोध और एकाग्रता की सिद्धि के लिए पहाड़ की गुफा में प्रवेश करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::221.english_translation: Seeing the tiger of desires, the fearful person quickly seeks refuge in a mountain cave to achieve control of mind and single-pointed concentration.
ashtavakra_gita::221.translation_literal: विषयद्वीपिनो (desire-island-dweller) / वीक्ष्य (seeing) / चकिताः (astonished/fearful) / शरणार्थिनः (seeking refuge) / विशन्ति (enter) / झटिति (quickly) / क्रोडं (mountain) / निरोधैकाग्रसिद्धये (for mind-control-and-concentration-attainment)
ashtavakra_gita::221.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::221.essence: Fear of desires drives you to find calm through focused mind control.
ashtavakra_gita::221.simple_meaning: When overwhelmed by desires, a fearful mind seeks refuge by calming and focusing itself deeply.
ashtavakra_gita::221.simple_insight: You feel relief when your restless mind finds a secure place of calm focus.
ashtavakra_gita::221.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra illustrates how a person frightened by the powerful pull of desires seeks shelter like entering a mountain cave, symbolizing the practice of calming and concentrating the mind to overcome distraction.
ashtavakra_gita::221.modern_relevance: When your cravings flood your thoughts, you might retreat to a quiet room to regain control and focus your attention.
ashtavakra_gita::221.insight: It teaches you to respond to emotional overwhelm by withdrawing inward and sharpening your mental focus.

ashtavakra_gita::222.verse_sanskrit:
निर्वासनं हरिं दृष्ट्वा तूष्णीं विषयदन्तिनः ।
पलायन्ते न शक्तास्ते सेवन्ते कृतचाटवः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::222.verse_hindi: वासना-रहित पुरुष-सिंह को देखकर विषयरूपी हाथी चुपचाप भाग जाते हैं या वे असमर्थ होकर चाटुकार की तरह उसकी सेवा करने लगते हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::222.english_translation: Seeing the desireless lion-like man, the elephant of senses silently flees or, powerless, serves him like a flatterer.
ashtavakra_gita::222.translation_literal: निर्वासनं (desireless) हरिं (lion-like man) दृष्ट्वा (seeing) तूष्णीं (silently) विषयदन्तिनः (the elephant of senses) पलायन्ते (flee) न (not) शक्तास्ते (powerful) सेवन्ते (serve) कृतचाटवः (like flatterers)
ashtavakra_gita::222.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::222.essence: Calm, desireless strength makes restless urges either flee or obey without resistance.
ashtavakra_gita::222.simple_meaning: When you become free from desire and remain calm like a lion, your restless senses either quietly leave or become powerless and serve you obediently.
ashtavakra_gita::222.simple_insight: You can feel strong and undisturbed when your cravings lose their power over you.
ashtavakra_gita::222.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra compares a desireless person to a lion and the restless senses to an elephant. When the senses see calm strength, they either run away silently or lose their strength and serve obediently. This shows how inner calm controls the restless mind.
ashtavakra_gita::222.modern_relevance: You’re sitting quietly amid distractions, and the usual impulses to react or crave either fade away or lose control, letting you stay steady.
ashtavakra_gita::222.insight: It teaches you to embody calmness so impulses lose their grip and either disappear or yield to your presence.

ashtavakra_gita::223.verse_sanskrit:
न मुक्तिकारिकां धत्ते निःशङ्को युक्तमानसः ।
पश्यन् श‍ृण्वन् स्पृशन् जिघ्रन्नश्नन्नास्ते यथासुखम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::223.verse_hindi: शंकारहित और मुक्त मन वाला पुरुष मुक्तिकारी योग को आग्रह के साथ नहीं ग्रहण करता है लेकिन वह देखता हुआ, सुनता हुआ, स्पर्श करता हुआ, सूँघता हुआ, खाता हुआ सुखपूर्वक रहता है।
ashtavakra_gita::223.english_translation: The one free of doubt and with a liberated mind does not cling to liberation practices but lives joyfully while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, and eating.
ashtavakra_gita::223.translation_literal: न (not) मुक्तिकारिकां (liberation-practice) धत्ते (accepts) निःशङ्को (without doubt) युक्तमानसः (with united mind) । पश्यन् (seeing) शृण्वन् (hearing) स्पृशन् (touching) जिघ्रन् (smelling) अश्नन् (eating) आस्ते (he dwells) यथा (just as) सुखम् (joyfully) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::223.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::223.essence: True freedom is joyful presence without clinging to liberation efforts.
ashtavakra_gita::223.simple_meaning: A mind free from doubt and craving does not cling to practices for liberation but enjoys life fully through all senses.
ashtavakra_gita::223.simple_insight: There is peace in letting go of trying to force freedom and just living fully as you are.
ashtavakra_gita::223.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a person with a calm and free mind does not desperately hold onto methods for liberation. Instead, they experience life openly and joyfully through seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, and eating—without attachment or fear.
ashtavakra_gita::223.modern_relevance: You stop obsessing over achieving an ideal state and instead savor the simple moments of life with calm and joy.
ashtavakra_gita::223.insight: It shifts focus from grasping freedom as a goal to embracing joyful, unattached experience in everyday life.

ashtavakra_gita::224.verse_hindi: यथार्थ ज्ञान के सुनने मात्र से शुद्ध बुद्धि और स्वस्थ चित्त हुआ पुरुष न आचार को, न अनाचार को, न उदासीन को देखता है ।
ashtavakra_gita::224.english_translation: By merely hearing true knowledge, the intellect becomes pure and the mind serene; the person no longer sees right or wrong, or indifference.
ashtavakra_gita::224.translation_literal: वस्तुश्रवणमात्रेण (by mere hearing of truth) / शुद्धबुद्धिः (pure intellect) / निराकुलः (untroubled) / नैव (not) / आचरम् (right conduct) / अनाचारम् (wrong conduct) / औदास्यं (indifference) / वा (or) / प्रपश्यति (sees)
ashtavakra_gita::224.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::224.essence: Pure knowledge alone calms the intellect, ending judgment of right, wrong, or apathy.
ashtavakra_gita::224.simple_meaning: Listening to genuine knowledge purifies your intellect and calms your mind, so you stop labeling things as right or wrong or feeling indifferent.
ashtavakra_gita::224.simple_insight: You feel free when your mind stops dividing experience into good, bad, or uncaring.
ashtavakra_gita::224.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that simply hearing true knowledge purifies the intellect and steadies the mind. At this moment, the person stops seeing actions or states as right, wrong, or indifferent, signaling a shift beyond dualistic judgment.
ashtavakra_gita::224.modern_relevance: You listen to a truth that quiets your restless mind, so you stop reacting with approval, disapproval, or detachment to every situation.
ashtavakra_gita::224.insight: It shifts your mind from reactive judgment to stable, clear awareness beyond dualities.

ashtavakra_gita::225.verse_sanskrit:
यदा यत्कर्तुमायाति तदा तत्कुरुते ऋजुः ।
शुभं वाप्यशुभं वापि तस्य चेष्टा हि बालवत् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::225.verse_hindi: धीर पुरुष जब कुछ शुभ या अशुभ करने को आ पड़ता है तो उसे सहजता के साथ करता है, क्योंकि उसका व्यवहार बालवत् होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::225.english_translation: When a steady person has to do something, whether good or bad, they do it simply, for their action is like that of a child.
ashtavakra_gita::225.translation_literal: यदा (when) यत् (whatever) कर्तुम् (to do) आयाति (comes) तदा (then) तत् (that) कुरुते (does) ऋजुः (straight/simply) । शुभं (auspicious/good) वा (or) अपि (also) अशुभं (inauspicious/bad) वा (or) इ (that) तस्य (his) चेष्टा (action/effort) हि (indeed) बालवत् (like a child) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::225.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::225.essence: Act simply and naturally without judging your actions as good or bad.
ashtavakra_gita::225.simple_meaning: You do what needs to be done straightforwardly, without hesitation, whether it seems good or bad.
ashtavakra_gita::225.simple_insight: There's freedom in acting naturally, without weighing outcomes or moralizing.
ashtavakra_gita::225.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a steady person acts with ease and simplicity, unaffected by judging actions as good or bad. Like a child who acts naturally without doubt, this steadiness frees from hesitation and confusion.
ashtavakra_gita::225.modern_relevance: You face a necessary task you dislike but still do it clearly and simply, without getting stuck in judgment.
ashtavakra_gita::225.insight: It shifts your mind from moral hesitation to straightforward action without inner conflict.

ashtavakra_gita::226.verse_sanskrit:
स्वातन्त्र्यात्सुखमाप्नोति स्वातन्त्र्याल्लभते परम् ।
स्वातन्त्र्यान्निर्वृतिं गच्छेत्स्वातन्त्र्यात् परमं पदम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::226.verse_hindi: धीर पुरुष स्वतंत्रता से सुख को प्राप्त होता है, स्वतंत्रता से परम को प्राप्त होता है, स्वतंत्रता से नित्यसुख को प्राप्त होता है और स्वतंत्रता से परमपद को प्राप्त होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::226.english_translation: The steady person attains happiness through freedom, attains the supreme through freedom, attains eternal bliss through freedom, and attains the highest state through freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::226.translation_literal: स्वातन्त्र्यात् (through freedom) सुखम् (happiness) आप्नोति (attains) स्वातन्त्र्यत् (through freedom) अल्लभते (attains) परम् (the supreme) । स्वातन्त्र्यान् (through freedom) निर्वृतिं (liberation) गच्छेत् (goes) स्वातन्त्र्यात् (through freedom) परमं (the highest) पदम् (state) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::226.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::226.essence: Complete inner freedom is the source of all joy, liberation, and highest fulfillment.
ashtavakra_gita::226.simple_meaning: You find happiness, eternal bliss, and the highest state through your own inner freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::226.simple_insight: Knowing that freedom itself brings complete joy creates a deep sense of peace inside you.
ashtavakra_gita::226.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a steady, wise person gains happiness, liberation, and the supreme state by realizing and living in inner freedom. This verse highlights freedom as the source of all fulfillment in life and beyond.
ashtavakra_gita::226.modern_relevance: You feel joy and relief when you stop being controlled by fears or expectations and live with true personal freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::226.insight: It teaches you to recognize freedom as the foundation for all lasting happiness and the ultimate state of being.

ashtavakra_gita::227.verse_sanskrit:
अकर्तृत्वमभोक्तृत्वं स्वात्मनो मन्यते यदा ।
तदा क्षीणा भवन्त्येव समस्ताश्चित्तवृत्तयः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::227.verse_hindi: जब मनुष्य अपनी आत्मा के अकर्त्तापन और अभोक्तापन को मानता है तब उसकी सम्पूर्ण चित्तवृत्तियों का नाश हो जाता है।
ashtavakra_gita::227.english_translation: When a person realizes their true self is neither the doer nor the enjoyer, all mental fluctuations cease.
ashtavakra_gita::227.translation_literal: अकर्तृत्वम् (non-doing) अभोक्तृत्वं (non-enjoying) स्वात्मनो (of the true self) मन्यते (is considered) यदा (when) तदा (then) क्षीणा (exhausted) भवन्ति (become) एव (indeed) समस्ताः (all) चित्तवृत्तयः (mental fluctuations)
ashtavakra_gita::227.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::227.essence: Recognizing you are neither doer nor enjoyer dissolves all mental fluctuations.
ashtavakra_gita::227.simple_meaning: You are not the one who acts or the one who experiences results; recognizing this stops all mental turmoil.
ashtavakra_gita::227.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing you are beyond action and experience.
ashtavakra_gita::227.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that when a person understands the true self is neither the agent nor the experiencer of life’s events, all distractions and mental disturbances dissolve, revealing the self’s pure nature.
ashtavakra_gita::227.modern_relevance: When you stop blaming yourself or taking credit for every outcome, your mind stops spinning in worry and doubt.
ashtavakra_gita::227.insight: Shift your identity from the doer/enjoyer to the silent observer; this calms mental turbulence.

ashtavakra_gita::228.verse_sanskrit:
उच्छृङ्खलाप्यकृतिका स्थितिर्धीरस्य राजते ।
न तु सस्पृहचित्तस्य शान्तिर्मूढस्य कृत्रिमा ॥
