ashtavakra_gita::228.verse_hindi: धीर पुरुष की स्वाभाविक उच्छ्रंखल स्थिति भी शोभती है लेकिन स्पृहायुक्त चित्त वाले मूढ़ की बनावटी शान्ति भी नहीं शोभती।
ashtavakra_gita::228.english_translation: The natural restless state suits the steady person, but the artificial peace of a covetous mind does not.
ashtavakra_gita::228.translation_literal: उच्छृङ्खलाप्यकृतिका (though restless) स्थितिः (state) धीः (of the steady) राजते (shines) । न (not) तु (but) सस्पृहचित्तस्य (of the covetous mind) शान्तिः (peace) मूढस्य (of the deluded) कृत्रिमा (artificial) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::228.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::228.essence: Natural restlessness reflects steady wisdom; artificial calm hides a restless, covetous mind.
ashtavakra_gita::228.simple_meaning: A steady person’s natural restless energy looks good, but a restless mind’s fake calm never does.
ashtavakra_gita::228.simple_insight: You can feel alive and unsettled without losing your inner steadiness and dignity.
ashtavakra_gita::228.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a truly wise and steady person can carry natural restlessness gracefully, unlike a deluded person whose forced calmness hides inner turmoil.
ashtavakra_gita::228.modern_relevance: You feel anxious and unsettled, but when your core steadiness holds, your energy is genuine — unlike pretending to be calm when inside you’re stormy.
ashtavakra_gita::228.insight: It shifts how you see restlessness — not as a flaw but as a sign of authentic inner steadiness.

ashtavakra_gita::229.verse_sanskrit:
विलसन्ति महाभोगैर्विशन्ति गिरिगह्वरान् ।
निरस्तकल्पना धीरा अबद्धा मुक्तबुद्धयः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::229.verse_hindi: कल्पना-रहित, बन्धन-रहित और मुक्त बुद्धि वाले धीर पुरुष कभी बड़े-बड़े भोगों के साथ क्रीड़ा करते हैं और कभी पहाड़ की कन्दराओं में प्रवेश करते हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::229.english_translation: The wise, free from imagination and bondage, sometimes delight in great pleasures and sometimes enter mountain caves.
ashtavakra_gita::229.translation_literal: विलसन्ति (shine/delight) महाभोगैः (with great pleasures) विशन्ति (enter) गिरिगह्वरान् (mountain caves) । निरस्तकल्पना (imagination removed) धीरा (wise men) अबद्धा (unbound) मुक्तबुद्धयः (liberated intellect) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::229.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::229.essence: True freedom lets you move freely between joy and solitude without attachment.
ashtavakra_gita::229.simple_meaning: A wise person with a free and clear mind can enjoy both great pleasures and peaceful solitude without losing inner freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::229.simple_insight: Freedom isn’t about rejecting life’s experiences but embracing them without attachment.
ashtavakra_gita::229.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes the wise person who has let go of mental constructs and attachments. Such a person freely moves between joyful engagement and quiet retreat, never bound by either.
ashtavakra_gita::229.modern_relevance: You might find yourself celebrating loud moments with friends or seeking quiet alone time—and both can coexist without disturbing your inner freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::229.insight: It teaches you to hold experiences lightly, allowing full enjoyment without losing your sense of freedom.

ashtavakra_gita::230.verse_sanskrit:
श्रोत्रियं देवतां तीर्थमङ्गनां भूपतिं प्रियम् ।
दृष्ट्वा सम्पूज्य धीरस्य न कापि हृदि वासना ॥
ashtavakra_gita::230.verse_hindi: धीर पुरुष के हृदय में पण्डित, देवता और तीर्थ का पूजन करके तथा स्त्री, राजा और प्रियजन को देखकर कोई भी वासना नहीं होती।
ashtavakra_gita::230.english_translation: A steady person feels no desire in the heart after worshipping scholars, deities, shrines, women, kings, or loved ones.
ashtavakra_gita::230.translation_literal: श्रोत्रियं (scholar) / देवतां (deity) / तीर्थमङ्गनां (shrines and women) / भूपतिं (king) / प्रियम् (loved one) / दृष्ट्वा (seeing) / सम्पूज्य (having worshipped) / धीरस्य (of the steady person) / न (not) / कापि (any) / हृदि (in the heart) / वासना (desire)
ashtavakra_gita::230.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::230.essence: True steadiness lets you honor all without stirring desire inside.
ashtavakra_gita::230.simple_meaning: A steady person can see and honor respected people and places without feeling desire inside.
ashtavakra_gita::230.simple_insight: You can engage fully with the world without being pulled by craving.
ashtavakra_gita::230.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that a person steady in awareness does not develop desire even after honoring respected scholars, divine beings, sacred places, women, kings, or loved ones, showing freedom from inner craving despite outer engagement.
ashtavakra_gita::230.modern_relevance: You attend a gathering full of admired people and places but remain calm, without craving or distraction pulling your heart.
ashtavakra_gita::230.insight: It teaches you to honor and respect without letting your heart be swayed by desire or attachment.

ashtavakra_gita::231.verse_sanskrit:
भृत्यैः पुत्रैः कलत्रैश्च दौहित्रैश्चापि गोत्रजैः ।
विहस्य धिक्कृतो योगी न याति विकृतिं मनाक् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::231.verse_hindi: योगी नौकरों से, पुत्रों से, पत्नियों से, दोहित्रों और बान्धवों द्वारा हँसकर धिक्कारे जाने पर भी विकार को प्राप्त नहीं होता है ।
ashtavakra_gita::231.english_translation: A yogi does not undergo disturbance of mind even when servants, sons, wives, daughters-in-law, and relatives mock and insult him.
ashtavakra_gita::231.translation_literal: भृत्यैः (by servants) / पुत्रैः (by sons) / कलत्रैः (by wives) / च (and) / दौहित्रैः (by daughters-in-law) / च (and) / अपि (also) / गोत्रजैः (by relatives) / विहस्य (laughing) / धिक्कृतो (insulted) / योगी (the yogi) / न (not) / याति (undergoes) / विकृतिं (disturbance) / मनाक् (of the mind)
ashtavakra_gita::231.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::231.essence: A steady mind stays undisturbed despite mockery from even close relations.
ashtavakra_gita::231.simple_meaning: You can stay calm and undisturbed in your mind even if close people insult or mock you.
ashtavakra_gita::231.simple_insight: You gain freedom by not letting others' mockery shake your inner peace.
ashtavakra_gita::231.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a true yogi remains mentally steady and undisturbed even when servants, family members, and relatives mock or insult him. This highlights the yogi's deep inner stability despite external negativity.
ashtavakra_gita::231.modern_relevance: When someone close ridicules you in front of others, you can keep your mind steady without reacting or losing peace.
ashtavakra_gita::231.insight: It teaches you to build inner resilience so others' words cannot disrupt your mental balance.

ashtavakra_gita::232.verse_sanskrit:
सन्तुष्टोऽपि न सन्तुष्टः खिन्नोऽपि न च खिद्यते ।
तस्याश्चर्यदशां तां तां तादृशा एव जानते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::232.verse_hindi: धीर पुरुष सन्तुष्ट होकर भी सन्तुष्ट नहीं होता है और दुःखी होकर भी दुःखी नहीं होता है । उसकी इस आश्चर्यमय दशा को वैसे ही ज्ञानी जानते हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::232.english_translation: The steady person is not truly pleased even when content, nor truly distressed even when upset; the wise recognize this wondrous state as it is.
ashtavakra_gita::232.translation_literal: सन्तुष्टः (content) अपि (even) न (not) सन्तुष्टः (content) खिन्नः (distressed) अपि (even) न (not) च (and) खिद्यते (is disturbed) तस्य (his) आश्चर्यदशां (wondrous state) तां (that) तां (that) तादृशा (such) एव (indeed) जानते (know)
ashtavakra_gita::232.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::232.essence: True steadiness means not being defined by feeling content or distressed.
ashtavakra_gita::232.simple_meaning: A truly steady person does not get caught up in feeling happy or upset. Their inner state remains unchanged, and wise people understand this surprising quality.
ashtavakra_gita::232.simple_insight: There is freedom in not being swayed by feelings of happiness or sorrow.
ashtavakra_gita::232.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a steady person—like a sage—does not fully belong to emotions of pleasure or pain. Even when content or distressed, their true self remains untouched. Wise people recognize this remarkable balance as a sign of deep inner mastery.
ashtavakra_gita::232.modern_relevance: You might smile after good news yet still feel a calm inside, or face hardship without being overwhelmed. This verse explains that true steadiness doesn’t depend on outer feelings.
ashtavakra_gita::232.insight: It shifts your understanding from identifying with emotions to seeing them as passing states that don’t define your true self.

ashtavakra_gita::233.verse_sanskrit:
कर्तव्यतैव संसारो न तां पश्यन्ति सूरयः ।
शून्याकारा निराकारा निर्विकारा निरामयाः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::233.verse_hindi: कर्तव्य ही संसार है, उसे शून्याकार, निराकार, निर्विकार और निरामय ज्ञानी नहीं देखते हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::233.english_translation: Those who act see the world; the wise see it as empty, formless, changeless, and free from disease.
ashtavakra_gita::233.translation_literal: कर्तव्यतैव (only by action) संसारो (world) न (not) तां (that) पश्यन्ति (see) सूरयः (the wise) । शून्याकारा (empty-shaped) निराकारा (formless) निर्विकारा (changeless) निरामयाः (disease-free) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::233.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::233.essence: The world appears real to those acting, but the wise see it as empty and unchanging.
ashtavakra_gita::233.simple_meaning: People who focus on doing see the world as real and active. The wise understand it as empty, without form or change.
ashtavakra_gita::233.simple_insight: There's freedom in seeing beyond appearances to the unchanging reality beneath.
ashtavakra_gita::233.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that those caught in action perceive the world as real and full of forms. But the enlightened see beyond this illusion, recognizing the world as empty, without shape, change, or disease, revealing its true nature.
ashtavakra_gita::233.modern_relevance: You rush through your day reacting to tasks and problems, but deeper insight comes when you step back and see situations as temporary shapes in a vast silent space.
ashtavakra_gita::233.insight: This verse shifts your view from identifying with actions to recognizing the world as a passing appearance without lasting reality.

ashtavakra_gita::234.verse_sanskrit:
अकुर्वन्नपि सङ्क्षोभाद् व्यग्रः सर्वत्र मूढधीः ।
कुर्वन्नपि तु कृत्यानि कुशलो हि निराकुलः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::234.verse_hindi: अज्ञानी कर्मों को नहीं करता हुआ भी सर्वत्र विक्षोभ के कारण व्याकुल रहता है और ज्ञानी सब कर्मो को करता हुआ भी शान्तचित्त वाला ही होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::234.english_translation: The ignorant remains restless everywhere, even without acting, disturbed by turmoil; the wise performs all actions yet remains calm and untroubled.
ashtavakra_gita::234.translation_literal: अकुर्वन्नपि (not acting yet) सङ्क्षोभाद् (because of disturbance) व्यग्रः (restless) सर्वत्र (everywhere) मूढधीः (ignorant one) / कुर्वन्नपि (acting yet) तु (but) कृत्यानि (actions) कुशलो (skilled) हि (indeed) निराकुलः (untroubled)
ashtavakra_gita::234.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::234.essence: Peace of mind doesn’t depend on doing or not doing—it comes from clear wisdom.
ashtavakra_gita::234.simple_meaning: Restlessness comes from confusion, even when not acting. Wisdom is acting while staying calm and clear.
ashtavakra_gita::234.simple_insight: You can move through life doing what’s needed without losing your inner peace.
ashtavakra_gita::234.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that ignorance causes mental turmoil even in inactivity, while wisdom allows one to engage in all actions with a steady, peaceful mind.
ashtavakra_gita::234.modern_relevance: When your phone won’t stop buzzing but you stay calm, you show the wisdom of this teaching.
ashtavakra_gita::234.insight: It teaches you to separate your sense of peace from your outer activity or lack of it.

ashtavakra_gita::235.verse_sanskrit:
सुखमास्ते सुखं शेते सुखमायाति याति च ।
सुखं वक्ति सुखं भुङ्क्ते व्यवहारेऽपि शान्तधीः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::235.verse_hindi: शान्त बुद्धि वाला ज्ञानी व्यवहार में भी सुखपूर्वक बैठता है, सुखपूर्वक आता है और मर जाता है, सुखपूर्वक बोलता है और सुखपूर्वक भोजन करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::235.english_translation: The calm-minded wise one lives with ease, comes and goes in peace, speaks and eats joyfully.
ashtavakra_gita::235.translation_literal: सुखमास्ते (with happiness sits) सुखं (happiness) शेते (lies down) सुखमायाति (happiness comes) याति (goes) च (and) । सुखं (happiness) वक्ति (speaks) सुखं (happiness) भुङ्क्ते (enjoys) व्यवहारेऽपि (even in conduct) शान्तधीः (calm-minded one) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::235.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::235.essence: A calm mind brings peace and joy to all daily actions and moments.
ashtavakra_gita::235.simple_meaning: A wise person with a calm mind lives peacefully in all actions—sitting, speaking, eating, arriving, and leaving with joy.
ashtavakra_gita::235.simple_insight: You can carry a peaceful joy through every part of your daily life.
ashtavakra_gita::235.detailed_meaning: In this teaching from Ashtavakra, a calm and wise person is described living effortlessly and happily in all ordinary activities. The verse shows how true wisdom brings peace not just in thought but in every moment of daily life.
ashtavakra_gita::235.modern_relevance: You come home tired but find stillness in your voice and meals, living calmly despite the day's chaos.
ashtavakra_gita::235.insight: It teaches you to maintain inner calm so your actions embody peaceful joy, regardless of circumstances.

ashtavakra_gita::236.verse_sanskrit:
स्वभावाद्यस्य नैवार्तिर्लोकवद् व्यवहारिणः ।
महाहृद इवाक्षोभ्यो गतक्लेशः सुशोभते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::236.verse_hindi: जो ज्ञानी स्वभाव से व्यवहार में भी सामान्यजन की तरह नहीं व्यवहार करता है और महासरोवर की तरह क्लेशरहित है, वही शोभता है।
ashtavakra_gita::236.english_translation: A true knower naturally behaves beyond the common world and shines free of suffering like a great lake.
ashtavakra_gita::236.translation_literal: स्वभावाद्यस्य (by nature) नै (not) एवार्तिः (bound) लोकवद् (like the world) व्यवहारिणः (one who acts) । महाहृद (great lake) इवाक्षोभ्यो (like waves) गतक्लेशः (free of pain) सुशोभते (shines) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::236.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::236.essence: True wisdom shines through natural calmness untouched by worldly suffering.
ashtavakra_gita::236.simple_meaning: A true knower lives naturally and calmly, unaffected by common worldly troubles, shining like a peaceful vast lake.
ashtavakra_gita::236.simple_insight: There's peace in being naturally untouched by life's usual struggles and still shining from within.
ashtavakra_gita::236.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a wise person’s natural way of being does not follow common worldly reactions. Like a great lake untouched by waves, such a person remains free of suffering and shines with calm radiance.
ashtavakra_gita::236.modern_relevance: When others around you get caught in stress and reactions, you feel steady and clear, untouched by the chaos.
ashtavakra_gita::236.insight: It teaches you to embody calmness so deeply that external troubles no longer disturb your inner peace.

ashtavakra_gita::237.verse_sanskrit:
निवृत्तिरपि मूढस्य प्रवृत्ति रुपजायते ।
प्रवृत्तिरपि धीरस्य निवृत्तिफलभागिनी ॥
ashtavakra_gita::237.verse_hindi: मूर्ख मनुष्य की निवृत्ति भी प्रवृत्तिरूप हो जाती है । किन्तु धीर पुरुष की प्रवृत्ति भी निवृत्ति के समान फल देती है।
ashtavakra_gita::237.english_translation: A fool's renunciation becomes a form of desire, but a wise person's desire yields the fruit of renunciation.
ashtavakra_gita::237.translation_literal: निवृत्तिः (renunciation) अपि (also) मूढस्य (of the fool) प्रवृत्ति (desire) रुपजायते (takes form). प्रवृत्तिः (desire) अपि (also) धीरस्य (of the wise) निवृत्तिफलभागिनी (bearing fruit of renunciation).
ashtavakra_gita::237.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::237.essence: Letting go can still be craving, and craving can sometimes lead to letting go.
ashtavakra_gita::237.simple_meaning: Sometimes, what looks like giving up is actually still wanting, and what looks like desire can bring true freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::237.simple_insight: You might feel stuck even when you think you've let go—true freedom requires deeper clarity.
ashtavakra_gita::237.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that a fool's attempt to renounce can still be driven by hidden desire, while a wise person's desires can lead to genuine detachment, showing how appearances can mislead us about freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::237.modern_relevance: You might quit a habit but secretly cling to it, or pursue goals that actually bring peace—recognizing this helps you see your true motives.
ashtavakra_gita::237.insight: It teaches you to examine your inner motives honestly, distinguishing true freedom from disguised craving.

ashtavakra_gita::238.verse_sanskrit:
परिग्रहेषु वैराग्यं प्रायो मूढस्य दृश्यते ।
देहे विगलिताशस्य क्व रागः क्व विरागता ॥
ashtavakra_gita::238.verse_hindi: मूढ़ पुरुष का वैराग्य परिग्रह से देखा जाता है । लेकिन देह में गलित हो गयी है आशा जिसकी, ऐसे ज्ञानी को कहाँ राग है, कहाँ वैराग्य।
ashtavakra_gita::238.english_translation: A foolish person shows detachment by giving up possessions, but a wise one whose desires have dissolved in the body has neither attachment nor detachment.
ashtavakra_gita::238.translation_literal: परिग्रहेषु (in possessions) वैराग्यं (detachment) प्रायो (mostly) मूढस्य (of the foolish) दृश्यते (is seen) । देहे (in the body) विगलिताशस्य (of the dissolved desires) क्व (where) रागः (attachment) क्व (where) विरागता (detachment) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::238.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::238.essence: True detachment is the absence of both desire and resistance, not just renouncing possessions.
ashtavakra_gita::238.simple_meaning: Detachment shown by giving up possessions is shallow and belongs to the confused. True detachment means desires have dissolved completely, so no attachment or aversion remains.
ashtavakra_gita::238.simple_insight: You can feel free when you stop clinging and also stop resisting, not just by giving things up.
ashtavakra_gita::238.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains to Janaka that many confuse detachment with simply letting go of possessions. But true detachment is deeper: it arises when desires themselves dissolve within the body-mind, leaving no trace of craving or rejection.
ashtavakra_gita::238.modern_relevance: You might quit a habit or stop chasing things, but real freedom comes when you no longer feel pulled or pushed by desires inside you.
ashtavakra_gita::238.insight: It shifts your understanding from outer actions of renouncing to inner dissolution of desire and aversion.

ashtavakra_gita::239.verse_sanskrit:
भावनाभावनासक्ता दृष्टिर्मूढस्य सर्वदा ।
भाव्यभावनया सा तु स्वस्थस्यादृष्टिरूपिणी ॥
ashtavakra_gita::239.verse_hindi: मूर्ख पुरुष की दृष्टि सदा भावना और अभावना में लगी रहती है । जबकि स्वस्थित पुरुष की दृष्टि भावना-अभावना से युक्त रहकर भी उनके प्रति अदृष्टि रूप ही रहती है।
ashtavakra_gita::239.english_translation: The foolish mind is always caught up in thoughts and their absence, but the steady mind remains as the unseen watcher, even amidst thoughts and their absence.
ashtavakra_gita::239.translation_literal: भावना (thought) / अभावना (absence of thought) / आसक्ता (attached) / दृष्टि (vision) / मूढस्य (of the foolish) / सर्वदा (always) । भावना (thought) / अभावना (absence) / या (which) / सा (that) / तु (but) / स्वस्थस्य (of the steady) / अदृष्टि (unseen) / रूपिणी (form) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::239.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::239.essence: True awareness stays steady as the silent watcher beyond all thoughts and their absence.
ashtavakra_gita::239.simple_meaning: A confused mind is always stuck in thinking or not thinking, but a steady mind observes both without getting involved.
ashtavakra_gita::239.simple_insight: There is calm in knowing you can be aware without being swept away by your thoughts.
ashtavakra_gita::239.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that a fool's mind is always entangled with thoughts and their absence, unable to rest. In contrast, the steady person’s mind remains as a silent witness, seeing thoughts and no-thought alike without being disturbed.
ashtavakra_gita::239.modern_relevance: When your mind races between worries and blankness, this teaches you to stand apart as the calm observer inside.
ashtavakra_gita::239.insight: It shifts your mind from being lost in thoughts to becoming the clear observer of them.

ashtavakra_gita::240.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वारम्भेषु निष्कामो यश्चरेद् बालवन् मुनिः ।
न लेपस्तस्य शुद्धस्य क्रियमाणेऽपि कर्मणि ॥
ashtavakra_gita::240.verse_hindi: जो मुनि बालक के समान व्यवहार करता है एवं कामना-रहित रूप से सभी कर्मों का आरम्भ करता है, उस शुद्ध स्वरूप को क्रियमाण कर्म भी लिप्त नहीं करते हैं।
ashtavakra_gita::240.english_translation: One who acts without desire like an innocent child remains untouched by any action, even while performing duties.
ashtavakra_gita::240.translation_literal: सर्वारम्भेषु (in all beginnings) / निष्कामो (without desire) / यश्चरेद् (who acts) / बालवन् (like a child) / मुनिः (the sage) / न (not) / लेपस्तस्य (attachment of that) / शुद्धस्य (pure) / क्रियमाणेऽपि (even in actions being done) / कर्मणि (in actions)
ashtavakra_gita::240.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::240.essence: You can act with pure innocence and desireless intent, staying untouched by your actions.
ashtavakra_gita::240.simple_meaning: You can start all your actions without craving or expectation, like a child, and remain pure and unaffected by them.
ashtavakra_gita::240.simple_insight: There is freedom in acting without desire, just like the innocent play of a child.
ashtavakra_gita::240.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a sage who begins every action without desire, like the innocent behavior of a child, remains pure and unaffected by the consequences of those actions.
ashtavakra_gita::240.modern_relevance: You begin a project or task with curiosity and no pressure, staying light-hearted and unaffected by the outcome.
ashtavakra_gita::240.insight: It shifts your mindset to act from innocence and detachment, dissolving the sense of binding results.

ashtavakra_gita::241.verse_sanskrit:
स एव धन्य आत्मज्ञः सर्वभावेषु यः समः ।
पश्यन् श‍ृण्वन् स्पृशन् जिघ्रन्न् अश्नन्निस्तर्षमानसः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::241.verse_hindi: वही आत्मज्ञानी धन्य है जो मन का निस्तरण कर गया है और जो देखता हुआ, सुनता हुआ, स्पर्श करता हुआ, सूँघता हुआ, खाता हुआ सब भावों में एकरस है।
ashtavakra_gita::241.english_translation: That self-knower is truly blessed who, having transcended the mind, remains equal while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, and eating all feelings.
ashtavakra_gita::241.translation_literal: स (that) / एव (indeed) / धन्य (blessed) / आत्मज्ञः (self-knower) / सर्वभावेषु (in all feelings) / यः (who) / समः (equal) / पश्यन् (seeing) / शृण्वन् (hearing) / स्पृशन् (touching) / जिघ्रन् (smelling) / अश्नन् (eating) / इस्तर्षमानसः (mind freed from suffering/longing)
ashtavakra_gita::241.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::241.essence: Freedom comes from a mind that stays equal amid all sensory experiences.
ashtavakra_gita::241.simple_meaning: You are blessed when your mind is free from craving and remains steady while experiencing all sensations equally.
ashtavakra_gita::241.simple_insight: There is peace in meeting life’s sensations without disturbance or craving.
ashtavakra_gita::241.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that one who knows their true self is blessed because they have freed their mind from desire and react with equal calm to all sensory experiences.
ashtavakra_gita::241.modern_relevance: You face a flood of emotions and sensations daily. Remaining steady and unaffected brings relief and freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::241.insight: It teaches you to witness sensations without getting caught in desire or aversion, maintaining steady awareness.

ashtavakra_gita::242.verse_sanskrit:
क्व संसारः क्व चाभासः क्व साध्यं क्व च साधनम् ।
आकाशस्येव धीरस्य निर्विकल्पस्य सर्वदा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::242.verse_hindi: सदैव आकाश के समान निर्विकल्प ज्ञानी को कहाँ संसार है, कहाँ आभास है, कहाँ साध्य है, कहाँ साधन है।
ashtavakra_gita::242.english_translation: A steady knower, like the sky, has no world, no appearance, no goal, and no means.
ashtavakra_gita::242.translation_literal: क्व (where) संसारः (world) क्व (where) चाभासः (and appearance) क्व (where) साध्यं (goal) क्व (where) च (and) साधनम् (means) । आकाशस्येव (like the sky) धीरस्य (of the steady one) निर्विकल्पस्य (without distinctions) सर्वदा (always) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::242.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::242.essence: A steady mind transcends all worldly forms, goals, and illusions like the vast sky.
ashtavakra_gita::242.simple_meaning: A truly steady mind is like the sky—unchanged by the world, without any appearance, goal, or method.
ashtavakra_gita::242.simple_insight: You can feel the peace of being untouched by fleeting appearances and desires.
ashtavakra_gita::242.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes the wise person whose mind is like the sky—vast and steady—unmoved by the world, illusions, goals, or ways to achieve them. This teaching comes as Janaka seeks clarity on true inner steadiness.
ashtavakra_gita::242.modern_relevance: When chaos swirls around you, like a noisy room or social media storm, you can remain steady and untouched, just like the open sky.
ashtavakra_gita::242.insight: It teaches you to hold your awareness steady beyond all shifting images and goals, resting in pure presence.

ashtavakra_gita::243.verse_sanskrit:
स जयत्यर्थसंन्यासी पूर्णस्वरसविग्रहः ।
अकृत्रिमोऽनवच्छिन्ने समाधिर्यस्य वर्तते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::243.verse_hindi: वही सन्यासी जय को प्राप्त होता है जो पूर्णानन्दस्वरूप है तथा जिसकी समाधि अविच्छिन्न रूप से विद्यमान रहती है।
ashtavakra_gita::243.english_translation: The true renunciant who attains victory is the one who embodies complete bliss and whose absorbed presence remains unbroken.
ashtavakra_gita::243.translation_literal: स (that) / जयति (wins) / अर्थ (goal) / सन्यासी (renunciant) / पूर्ण (complete) / स्वर (bliss) / अविग्रहः (embodiment) / अकृत्रिमः (natural) / अनवच्छिन्न (uninterrupted) / समाधिः (absorbed presence) / यस्य (whose) / वर्तते (exists)
ashtavakra_gita::243.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::243.essence: True victory comes through natural, unbroken blissful presence.
ashtavakra_gita::243.simple_meaning: Victory belongs to the renunciant who naturally embodies complete bliss and whose deep absorption never breaks.
ashtavakra_gita::243.simple_insight: You can find strength in steady, natural presence without struggle or interruption.
ashtavakra_gita::243.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that true renunciation is not about external acts but about being naturally established in complete bliss and uninterrupted absorbed presence, which leads to real victory in life and inner freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::243.modern_relevance: When your focus stays steady and joyful despite distractions, you succeed beyond external achievements.
ashtavakra_gita::243.insight: It invites you to cultivate effortless, continuous presence as the real source of victory, not external conquest.

ashtavakra_gita::244.verse_sanskrit:
बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन ज्ञाततत्त्वो महाशयः ।
भोगमोक्षनिराकाङ्क्षी सदा सर्वत्र नीरसः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::244.verse_hindi: यहाँ बहुत कहने से क्या प्रयोजन है ? तत्त्व-ज्ञानी महाशय भोग और मोक्ष दोनों में निरकांक्षी, सदा और सर्वत्र रागरहित रहता है।
ashtavakra_gita::244.english_translation: What is the use of saying much here? The great knower of truth desires neither pleasure nor freedom and remains always detached everywhere.
ashtavakra_gita::244.translation_literal: बहुनात्र (much here) / किमुक्तेन (what use) / ज्ञाततत्त्वो (knower of truth) / महाशयः (great person) / भोगमोक्षनिराकाङ्क्षी (desiring neither pleasure nor freedom) / सदा (always) / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / नीरसः (detached)
ashtavakra_gita::244.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::244.essence: True wisdom means desiring nothing and staying detached everywhere always.
ashtavakra_gita::244.simple_meaning: A true knower does not seek pleasure or freedom but stays detached from all desires everywhere at all times.
ashtavakra_gita::244.simple_insight: There is peace in wanting nothing and staying detached wherever you are.
ashtavakra_gita::244.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the great sage who truly understands reality does not cling to pleasures or even freedom and remains without desire and detached in every circumstance.
ashtavakra_gita::244.modern_relevance: You find yourself restless chasing goals or escapes, yet peace comes only when desire fades and detachment grows.
ashtavakra_gita::244.insight: It shifts your view from craving outcomes to simply being detached and steady everywhere.

ashtavakra_gita::245.verse_sanskrit:
महदादि जगद्द्वैतं नाममात्रविजृम्भितम् ।
विहाय शुद्धबोधस्य किं कृत्यमवशिष्यते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::245.verse_hindi: महत्तत्व आदि जो द्वैत-जगत है वह नाम मात्र को ही भिन्न है । उसका त्याग कर देने के बाद शुद्ध बोध वाले का कौन सा कार्य शेष रह जाता है।
ashtavakra_gita::245.english_translation: The great primordial universe of duality is only a name and sound; once pure awareness is realized, no action remains to be done.
ashtavakra_gita::245.translation_literal: महदादि (great primordial) / जगत् (universe) / द्वैतम् (duality) / नाममात्रविजृम्भितम् (only name and sound) / विहाय (leaving aside) / शुद्धबोधस्य (of pure awareness) / किं (what) / कृत्यम् (action) / अवशिष्यते (remains)
ashtavakra_gita::245.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::245.essence: Pure awareness transcends all duality and leaves no action behind.
ashtavakra_gita::245.simple_meaning: The world of separation and names is only an appearance; once you realize pure awareness, no further action is needed.
ashtavakra_gita::245.simple_insight: You can feel complete and free when you rest in pure awareness beyond labels.
ashtavakra_gita::245.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the manifest world of duality is merely a name and sound. Once the seeker attains pure awareness, the sense of obligation or action disappears, revealing the freedom beyond all doing.
ashtavakra_gita::245.modern_relevance: After intense effort to control and understand everything, you realize some things simply need no action—they are already whole as they are.
ashtavakra_gita::245.insight: It shifts your mind from doing to simply being, recognizing that pure awareness requires no further effort or change.

ashtavakra_gita::246.verse_sanskrit:
भ्रमभूतमिदं सर्वं किञ्चिन्नास्तीति निश्चयी ।
अलक्ष्यस्फुरणः शुद्धः स्वभावेनैव शाम्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::246.verse_hindi: यह समस्त जगत-प्रपञ्च कुछ नहीं है, ऐसा निश्चयपूर्वक जानकर अलक्ष्य की स्फुरण वाला शुद्ध पुरुष स्वभाव से ही शान्त होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::246.english_translation: Knowing with certainty that this entire world of illusion is nothing, the pure being, subtle yet perceptible, naturally rests in peace.
ashtavakra_gita::246.translation_literal: भ्रमभूतमिदं (this, being illusion) / सर्वं (all) / किञ्चिन्नास्तीति (is nothing, certainly) / निश्चयी (knowing firmly) / अलक्ष्य (imperceptible) / स्फुरणः (subtle motion) / शुद्धः (pure) / स्वभावेनैव (by nature itself) / शाम्यति (becomes peaceful).
ashtavakra_gita::246.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::246.essence: Knowing the world is mere illusion lets your pure self rest naturally in peace.
ashtavakra_gita::246.simple_meaning: Everything you see as the world is an illusion, and the pure true self naturally remains calm once this is understood.
ashtavakra_gita::246.simple_insight: You can feel a deep peace when you know the world’s appearances are empty.
ashtavakra_gita::246.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the entire manifest world is illusion. Recognizing this without doubt, the pure self, which is subtle yet present, naturally settles into calmness without effort.
ashtavakra_gita::246.modern_relevance: When overwhelming chaos surrounds you, realizing it is just appearance helps you find natural calm within yourself.
ashtavakra_gita::246.insight: It teaches you to identify the subtle pure self behind illusions and let that awareness bring calm.

ashtavakra_gita::247.verse_sanskrit:
शुद्धस्फुरणरूपस्य दृश्यभावमपश्यतः ।
क्व विधिः क्व च वैराग्यं क्व त्यागः क्व शमोऽपि वा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::247.verse_hindi: दृश्यभाव को नहीं देखते हुए शुद्ध स्फुरणरूप का अनुभव करने वाले को कहाँ विधि है और कहाँ वैराग्य है । कहाँ त्याग है और कहाँ शान्ति है।
ashtavakra_gita::247.english_translation: One who experiences the pure shining form without seeing the appearance of forms, where is the rule, where is detachment, where is renunciation, where is peace?
ashtavakra_gita::247.translation_literal: शुद्धस्फुरणरूपस्य (of pure shining form) / दृश्यभावमपश्यतः (not seeing the appearance of forms) / क्व (where) / विधिः (rule) / क्व (where) / च (and) / वैराग्यं (detachment) / क्व (where) / त्यागः (renunciation) / क्व (where) / शमोऽपि (even peace) / वा (or)
ashtavakra_gita::247.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::247.essence: Pure awareness beyond appearances makes rules, detachment, and renunciation unnecessary.
ashtavakra_gita::247.simple_meaning: If you directly experience the pure shining reality beyond appearances, ideas like rules, detachment, renunciation, and peace become irrelevant.
ashtavakra_gita::247.simple_insight: True clarity frees you from needing any external rules or efforts to find peace.
ashtavakra_gita::247.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that when you perceive the pure, radiant essence beyond all forms and appearances, conventional concepts like detachment and renunciation lose their meaning. This moment reveals that peace and freedom are not achieved through effort but are already present.
ashtavakra_gita::247.modern_relevance: When you deeply see the truth beneath surface distractions, you stop chasing rules or methods to feel calm and free.
ashtavakra_gita::247.insight: It shifts the mind from relying on external disciplines to recognizing peace already inherent in pure awareness.

ashtavakra_gita::248.verse_sanskrit:
स्फुरतोऽनन्तरूपेण प्रकृतिं च न पश्यतः ।
क्व बन्धः क्व च वा मोक्षः क्व हर्षः क्व विषादिता ॥
ashtavakra_gita::248.verse_hindi: और अनन्त रूपों में स्फुरित प्रकृति को नहीं देखते हुए ज्ञानी को कहाँ बन्ध है और कहाँ मोक्ष है । कहाँ हर्ष है और कहाँ शोक है।
ashtavakra_gita::248.english_translation: The wise one who does not see the natural world manifesting in infinite forms is free from bondage, freedom, joy, and sorrow alike.
ashtavakra_gita::248.translation_literal: स्फुरतोऽनन्तरूपेण (manifesting in infinite forms) / प्रकृतिं (natural world) / च (and) / न (not) / पश्यतः (seeing) / क्व (where) / बन्धः (bondage) / क्व (where) / च (and) / वा (or) / मोक्षः (freedom) / क्व (where) / हर्षः (joy) / क्व (where) / विषादिता (sorrow)
ashtavakra_gita::248.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::248.essence: Seeing the infinite unity of nature dissolves all distinctions of bondage, freedom, joy, and sorrow.
ashtavakra_gita::248.simple_meaning: When you truly see the infinite forms of nature as one, you no longer experience bondage or freedom, joy or sorrow.
ashtavakra_gita::248.simple_insight: You can feel peace by recognizing that all opposites dissolve in true understanding.
ashtavakra_gita::248.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the wise person perceives the natural world as infinite forms without separation. Because of this clear vision, the distinctions of bondage, freedom, joy, and sorrow lose their grip and meaning.
ashtavakra_gita::248.modern_relevance: When you stop dividing your experiences into success or failure, pleasure or pain, life feels less chaotic and more peaceful.
ashtavakra_gita::248.insight: It shifts your view from seeing life as a series of opposites to recognizing their shared essence, freeing you from emotional extremes.

ashtavakra_gita::249.verse_sanskrit:
बुद्धिपर्यन्तसंसारे मायामात्रं विवर्तते ।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारो निष्कामः शोभते बुधः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::249.verse_hindi: बुद्धिपर्यन्त संसार में जहाँ माया ही माया भासती है वहाँ ममतारहित, अहंकार-रहित और कामनारहित ज्ञानी ही शोभता है।
ashtavakra_gita::249.english_translation: In the world limited by the discerning mind, where only illusion appears, the wise one shines without attachment, ego, or desire.
ashtavakra_gita::249.translation_literal: बुद्धि (discerning mind) / पर्यन्त (limited) / संसार (world) / में (in) / माया (illusion) / मात्रं (only) / विवर्तते (appears) / । / निर्मम (without attachment) / निरहङ्कार (without ego) / निष्काम (without desire) / शोभते (shines) / बुधः (wise one) / ॥
ashtavakra_gita::249.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::249.essence: True wisdom shines when you release ego, desire, and attachment in an illusory world.
ashtavakra_gita::249.simple_meaning: Where the mind sees only illusion, the wise one stands out by being free from ego, attachment, and desire.
ashtavakra_gita::249.simple_insight: There is a calm strength in not clinging to self or wants amid life's illusions.
ashtavakra_gita::249.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the world perceived through the discerning mind is filled with illusion. The truly wise person is free from attachment, ego, and desire, which allows their true nature to shine clearly.
ashtavakra_gita::249.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by endless distractions and false appearances around you. Freedom comes when you stop identifying with your desires and ego.
ashtavakra_gita::249.insight: It teaches you to recognize the illusory nature of appearances and to let go of ego and craving to reveal your true clarity.

ashtavakra_gita::250.verse_sanskrit:
अक्षयं गतसन्तापमात्मानं पश्यतो मुनेः ।
क्व विद्या च क्व वा विश्वं क्व देहोऽहं ममेति वा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::250.verse_hindi: अविनाशी और सन्तापरहित आत्मा को देखने वाले मुनि को कहाँ विद्या है और कहाँ विश्व । कहाँ देह है और कहाँ अहंता-ममता है।
ashtavakra_gita::250.english_translation: Where is knowledge or the world for the sage who sees the true self as imperishable and free of suffering? Where is body, ego, or possession?
ashtavakra_gita::250.translation_literal: अक्षयं (imperishable) गतसन्तापम् (gone-suffering) आत्मानं (self) पश्यतो (seeing) मुनेः (of the sage) । क्व (where) विद्या (knowledge) च (and) क्व (where) वा (or) विश्वं (world) क्व (where) देहोऽहम् (body-I) मम (my) एति (is) वा (or) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::250.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::250.essence: Seeing yourself as beyond suffering reveals that knowledge, world, and ego are illusions.
ashtavakra_gita::250.simple_meaning: A sage who perceives the true self as eternal and free from suffering sees no need for knowledge, the world, body, or ego.
ashtavakra_gita::250.simple_insight: There is freedom in realizing your true self is untouched by suffering or identity.
ashtavakra_gita::250.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra challenges the notion of self as body or ego. He asks where knowledge, world, body, or possession exist for one who sees the self as imperishable and free from suffering, pointing to the ultimate freedom beyond all appearances.
ashtavakra_gita::250.modern_relevance: When you stop identifying with your struggles or roles, you find a space beyond stress and self-doubt.
ashtavakra_gita::250.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with transient things to resting in the unchanging true self.

ashtavakra_gita::251.verse_sanskrit:
निरोधादीनि कर्माणि जहाति जडधीर्यदि ।
मनोरथान् प्रलापांश्च कर्तुमाप्नोत्यतत्क्षणात् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::251.verse_hindi: यदि जड़ बुद्धि मनुष्य निरोध आदि कर्मों को छोड़ता भी है तो वह तत्क्षण मनोरथों और प्रलापों को पूरा करने में प्रवृत्त हो जाता है।
ashtavakra_gita::251.english_translation: Even if a person of dull understanding abandons actions like restraint, they immediately become engaged in fulfilling desires and idle talk.
ashtavakra_gita::251.translation_literal: यदि (if) जड़ (dull) बुद्धि (intellect) मनुष्य (person) निरोधादीनि (restraint and such) कर्माणि (actions) जहाति (abandons) ति (then) मनःरथान् (desires) प्रलापांश्च (idle talks) कर्तुम् (to do) आप्नोति (obtains) तत्क्षणात् (immediately).
ashtavakra_gita::251.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::251.essence: Stopping action doesn’t free you if the mind still pursues desires and chatter.
ashtavakra_gita::251.simple_meaning: Stopping physical actions alone does not free you if your mind still pursues desires and meaningless chatter.
ashtavakra_gita::251.simple_insight: You feel restless when the mind keeps chasing wants, even if you stop doing things.
ashtavakra_gita::251.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a dull mind abandoning physical restraint and actions is still caught immediately by desires and pointless talk, showing that true freedom requires more than just stopping outward acts.
ashtavakra_gita::251.modern_relevance: You might quit a bad habit but still replay cravings and chatter inside your head, trapping you in restlessness.
ashtavakra_gita::251.insight: It shows that true freedom needs calming the mind’s desires, not just stopping outward doing.

ashtavakra_gita::252.verse_sanskrit:
मन्दः श्रुत्वापि तद्वस्तु न जहाति विमूढताम् ।
निर्विकल्पो बहिर्यत्नादन्तर्विषयलालसः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::252.verse_hindi: मन्द बुद्धि उस तत्त्व को सुनकर भी मूढ़ता को नहीं छोड़ता है । वह बाह्य प्रयत्न में निर्विकल्प होकर मन में विषयों की लालसा वाला होता है।
ashtavakra_gita::252.english_translation: Even after hearing that truth, the slow-witted one does not abandon delusion; externally still without thought, yet inwardly craving objects.
ashtavakra_gita::252.translation_literal: मन्दः (slow-witted) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / अपि (even) / तद् (that) / वस्तु (truth) / न (not) / जहाति (abandons) / विमूढताम् (delusion) । / निर्विकल्पः (without thought) / बहिर्यत्नात् (by external effort) / अन्तर्विषयलालसः (inwardly craving objects) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::252.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::252.essence: External calm without inner freedom is still entangled in desire and delusion.
ashtavakra_gita::252.simple_meaning: Even if you hear a truth, you might not let go of your confusion. You can seem calm outside but still crave things inside.
ashtavakra_gita::252.simple_insight: It feels unsettling to realize that calmness alone does not free you from inner longing.
ashtavakra_gita::252.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that some hear the highest truth but remain stuck in delusion because they only quiet the outside without uprooting inner desires. This shows the gap between external calm and inward restlessness.
ashtavakra_gita::252.modern_relevance: You might look composed in meetings but feel restless craving likes or approval deep inside.
ashtavakra_gita::252.insight: It teaches you to watch not just your outer stillness but also your hidden cravings to truly see delusion.

ashtavakra_gita::253.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानाद् गलितकर्मा यो लोकदृष्ट्यापि कर्मकृत् ।
नाप्नोत्यवसरं कर्त्रुं वक्तुमेव न किञ्चन ॥
ashtavakra_gita::253.verse_hindi: ज्ञान से नष्ट हुआ है कर्म जिसका, ऐसा ज्ञानी लोक-दृष्टि में कर्म करने वाला भी है लेकिन वह न कुछ करने का अवसर पाता है, न कुछ कहने का ही।
ashtavakra_gita::253.english_translation: The one whose actions have dissolved through wisdom still acts in the world but has neither the opportunity to act nor to speak.
ashtavakra_gita::253.translation_literal: ज्ञानाद् (through wisdom) गलितकर्मा (dissolved action) यो (who) लोकदृष्ट्यापि (even in the world's view) कर्मकृत् (acts). नाप्नोति (does not obtain) अवसरं (opportunity) कर्त्रुं (to act) वक्तुम् (to speak) एव (even) न (not) किञ्चन (anything).
ashtavakra_gita::253.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::253.essence: You can act without being a doer or having control over actions or speech.
ashtavakra_gita::253.simple_meaning: Even though a wise person appears to act, they no longer truly have the chance to act or speak because their sense of doer has dissolved.
ashtavakra_gita::253.simple_insight: You can be present in action without the pressure or claim of doing anything.
ashtavakra_gita::253.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains that a person who has dissolved their sense of individual doer through wisdom still participates in worldly actions. However, from their inner state, they neither grasp the chance to act nor to speak as a separate agent.
ashtavakra_gita::253.modern_relevance: You might keep performing tasks at work or home, yet inside, you feel detached, as if the need to push or claim anything has vanished.
ashtavakra_gita::253.insight: This verse shifts your view from being the doer to witnessing action without ownership or urgency.

ashtavakra_gita::254.verse_sanskrit:
क्व तमः क्व प्रकाशो वा हानं क्व च न किञ्चन ।
निर्विकारस्य धीरस्य निरातङ्कस्य सर्वदा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::254.verse_hindi: सर्वदा निर्भय और निर्विकार धीर पुरुष को कहाँ अन्धकार है, कहाँ प्रकाश है और कहाँ त्याग है । कहीं कुछ भी नहीं है।
ashtavakra_gita::254.english_translation: A fearless, steady person beyond change has no darkness, no light, and no loss at any time.
ashtavakra_gita::254.translation_literal: क्व (where) तमः (darkness) क्व (where) प्रकाशो (light) वा (or) हानं (loss) क्व (where) च (and) न (not) किञ्चन (anything) । (.) निर्विकारस्य (of the unchanging) धीरस्य (of the steady) निरातङ्कस्य (of the fearless) सर्वदा (always) ॥ (॥)
ashtavakra_gita::254.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::254.essence: A fearless steady mind is beyond all opposites like darkness, light, or loss.
ashtavakra_gita::254.simple_meaning: A person who is fearless and steady, not affected by change, experiences no darkness, no light, and no loss ever.
ashtavakra_gita::254.simple_insight: You can feel completely steady and safe, beyond fears or gains and losses.
ashtavakra_gita::254.detailed_meaning: The sage Ashtavakra speaks to King Janaka, pointing out that a person fully established in pure awareness and without fear never experiences darkness, light, or loss—these dualities have no hold on such a steady mind.
ashtavakra_gita::254.modern_relevance: In moments of stress or uncertainty, you can find a place inside where fear and confusion vanish, leaving calm steadiness.
ashtavakra_gita::254.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing outcomes to resting in unshakable inner steadiness.

ashtavakra_gita::255.verse_sanskrit:
क्व धैर्यं क्व विवेकित्वं क्व निरातङ्कतापि वा ।
अनिर्वाच्यस्वभावस्य निःस्वभावस्य योगिनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::255.verse_hindi: अनिर्वचनीय स्वभाव वाले स्वभावरहित योगी को कहाँ धीरता है, कहाँ विवेकिता अथवा कहाँ निर्भयता है।
ashtavakra_gita::255.english_translation: Where is patience, where is discernment, where is fearlessness for the yogi whose nature is indescribable and without qualities?
ashtavakra_gita::255.translation_literal: क्व (where) / धैर्यं (patience) / क्व (where) / विवेकित्वं (discernment) / क्व (where) / निरातङ्कतापि (fearlessness) / वा (or) / अनिर्वाच्यस्वभावस्य (of indescribable nature) / निःस्वभावस्य (without qualities) / योगिनः (of the yogi)
ashtavakra_gita::255.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::255.essence: The true self is beyond all qualities like patience, discernment, and fearlessness.
ashtavakra_gita::255.simple_meaning: The yogi whose true self is beyond description has no fixed qualities like patience, discernment, or fearlessness.
ashtavakra_gita::255.simple_insight: You find freedom in being beyond all labels and qualities.
ashtavakra_gita::255.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra highlights the yogi whose true nature transcends all qualities. This yogi no longer depends on traits like patience or discernment because they have gone beyond all dualities and definitions.
ashtavakra_gita::255.modern_relevance: When you feel pressured to always stay patient or brave, this reminds you that your deepest self is beyond such demands.
ashtavakra_gita::255.insight: It shifts your view from trying to cultivate traits to recognizing your true self as free from all qualities.

ashtavakra_gita::256.verse_sanskrit:
न स्वर्गो नैव नरको जीवन्मुक्तिर्न चैव हि ।
बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन योगदृष्ट्या न किञ्चन ॥
ashtavakra_gita::256.verse_hindi: योगी को न स्वर्ग है, न नरक है, न जीवनमुक्ति ही है । इसमें बहुत कहने से क्या प्रयोजन, योग की दृष्टि से कुछ भी नहीं है।
ashtavakra_gita::256.english_translation: The yogi has neither higher realm nor lower realm, nor is there any inner freedom; from the yoga perspective, none of these exist.
ashtavakra_gita::256.translation_literal: न (not) स्वर्गो (higher realm) नैव (also not) नरको (lower realm) जीवन्मुक्ति (inner freedom)ः (nor) नै (not) चैव (indeed) हि (certainly) । बहुनात्र (in many places) किमुक्तेन (what freedom) योगदृष्ट्या (from yoga perspective) न (not) किञ्चन (anything) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::256.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::256.essence: Yoga reveals that realms and freedom are illusions, not realities.
ashtavakra_gita::256.simple_meaning: From the perspective of yoga, the ideas of higher realm, lower realm, and inner freedom do not exist for the yogi.
ashtavakra_gita::256.simple_insight: You can feel free by seeing that these divisions are illusions from yoga’s perspective.
ashtavakra_gita::256.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the yogi transcends common concepts like heaven, hell, and liberation. These categories are irrelevant because yoga reveals their emptiness. This challenges conventional beliefs about spiritual progress and freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::256.modern_relevance: When you face life’s highs and lows, yoga invites you to see beyond those labels and find peace in what simply is.
ashtavakra_gita::256.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing states or labels to resting in the direct experience yoga reveals.

ashtavakra_gita::257.verse_sanskrit:
नैव प्रार्थयते लाभं नालाभेनानुशोचति ।
धीरस्य शीतलं चित्तममृतेनैव पूरितम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::257.verse_hindi: धीर पुरुष का चित्त अमृत से पूरित हुआ शीतल है । इसलिए न वह लाभ के लिए प्रार्थना करता है और न ही हानि के लिए कभी चिन्ता करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::257.english_translation: The steady mind is filled with immortality and coolness, so it neither prays for gain nor grieves for loss.
ashtavakra_gita::257.translation_literal: नैव (not) / प्रार्थयते (prays) / लाभं (gain) / न (nor) / अलाभेन (loss) / अनुशोचति (grieves) / धीरस्य (of the steady one) / शीतलं (cool) / चित्तम (mind) / अमृतेनैव (by immortality alone) / पूरितम् (filled)
ashtavakra_gita::257.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::257.essence: A steady mind filled with timeless calm neither desires gain nor fears loss.
ashtavakra_gita::257.simple_meaning: A person with a steady mind is filled with timeless calm and does not seek gain or fear loss.
ashtavakra_gita::257.simple_insight: You can feel peaceful and complete without wanting or fearing anything.
ashtavakra_gita::257.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes a person whose mind is steady and filled with the immortal essence, making them cool and unaffected by desires or fears of gain and loss.
ashtavakra_gita::257.modern_relevance: When your mind stays calm and full inside, you stop chasing results or worrying about setbacks, even during stressful days.
ashtavakra_gita::257.insight: It teaches you to rest your mind in its natural fullness, releasing all craving and aversion.

ashtavakra_gita::258.verse_sanskrit:
न शान्तं स्तौति निष्कामो न दुष्टमपि निन्दति ।
समदुःखसुखस्तृप्तः किञ्चित् कृत्यं न पश्यति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::258.verse_hindi: निष्काम पुरुष न तो शान्त पुरुष की प्रशंसा करता है, न दुष्ट को देखकर निन्दा करता है । वह सुख-दुःख को समान समझता हुआ तृप्त है।
ashtavakra_gita::258.english_translation: A person without desire neither praises the peaceful nor blames the wicked; content, they see no task in anything.
ashtavakra_gita::258.translation_literal: न (not) शान्तं (peaceful) स्तौति (praises) निष्कामो (desireless) न (not) दुष्टमपि (even the wicked) निन्दति (blames) । समदुःखसुखः (equal in sorrow and joy) तृप्तः (content) किञ्चित् (any) कृत्यं (duty/task) न (not) पश्यति (sees) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::258.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::258.essence: True calm means no need to praise or blame; contentment sees no separate tasks.
ashtavakra_gita::258.simple_meaning: You don’t praise good people or blame bad ones. You stay content and see no action as necessary.
ashtavakra_gita::258.simple_insight: You can feel steady and satisfied no matter what others do or say.
ashtavakra_gita::258.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches how a desireless person, neither praising the peaceful nor blaming the wicked, remains content and indifferent to all actions, embodying true equanimity in a world of opposites.
ashtavakra_gita::258.modern_relevance: You scroll through social media, reading praise and criticism, yet you remain unmoved, steady in your own calm.
ashtavakra_gita::258.insight: It shifts your mind from reacting emotionally to others’ behavior toward steady inner contentment.

ashtavakra_gita::259.verse_sanskrit:
धीरो न द्वेष्टि संसारमात्मानं न दिदृक्षति ।
हर्षामर्षविनिर्मुक्तो न मृतो न च जीवति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::259.verse_hindi: धीर पुरुष न संसार के प्रति द्वेष करता है और न आत्मा को देखने की इच्छा करता है । हर्ष और शोक से मुक्त वह, न मरे हुए जैसा है और न जीवित जैसा
ashtavakra_gita::259.english_translation: The steady one neither hates the cycle of change nor seeks the true self; free from joy and sorrow, they are neither dead nor alive.
ashtavakra_gita::259.translation_literal: धीरो (the steady one) न (not) द्वेष्टि (hates) संसारम् (the cycle of change) आत्मानं (the true self) न (not) दिदृक्षति (seeks) । हर्षा (joy) अमर्ष (sorrow) विनिर्मुक्तो (free) न (not) मृतो (dead) न (not) च (and) जीवति (alive) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::259.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::259.essence: Steadiness is freedom from hating change or craving the true self, beyond life and death.
ashtavakra_gita::259.simple_meaning: A steady person neither hates the world nor craves to find the true self; free from highs and lows, they exist beyond life and death.
ashtavakra_gita::259.simple_insight: There is peace in not pushing away or grasping for anything, resting steady beyond extremes.
ashtavakra_gita::259.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a person with steady awareness does not reject the endless changes of the world nor desperately seeks the true self. Such a person remains free from emotional highs and lows, existing beyond ordinary life and death distinctions.
ashtavakra_gita::259.modern_relevance: You pause in the middle of a chaotic day, neither rejecting the noise nor chasing elusive answers, simply steady and calm.
ashtavakra_gita::259.insight: It shifts your mind from reacting to the world or self-searching, to resting in balanced awareness beyond dualities.

ashtavakra_gita::260.verse_sanskrit:
निःस्नेहः पुत्रदारादौ निष्कामो विषयेषु च ।
निश्चिन्तः स्वशरीरेऽपि निराशः शोभते बुधः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::260.verse_hindi: पुत्र, स्त्री आदि के प्रति स्नेह न रखता हुआ और विषयों में कामनारहित हुआ, अपने शरीर की भी चिन्ता नहीं करता हुआ ज्ञानी पुरुष सभी आशाओं से मुक्त शोभा देता है।
ashtavakra_gita::260.english_translation: The wise person who holds no attachment to children, spouse, or desires, who is without craving even for the body, and is free from all hopes shines brightly.
ashtavakra_gita::260.translation_literal: निःस्नेहः (without attachment) पुत्रदारादौ (to children and spouse) निष्कामो (without desire) विषयेषु (in pleasures) च (and) । निश्चिन्तः (without worry) स्वशरीरेऽपि (even about own body) निराशः (hope-free) शोभते (shines) बुधः (the wise)
ashtavakra_gita::260.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::260.essence: True brightness comes from complete freedom from attachment and desire, even toward your own body.
ashtavakra_gita::260.simple_meaning: You become radiant when you let go of attachments to people, desires, and even your own body, living without hope or worry.
ashtavakra_gita::260.simple_insight: Relief and lightness come when you stop clinging to others and your own physical self.
ashtavakra_gita::260.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a wise person who is free from attachments to family and desires, who does not cling even to their own body, and who has no anxious hopes, appears radiant and dignified.
ashtavakra_gita::260.modern_relevance: You notice how much effort you spend worrying about loved ones, desires, or your health—and how much lighter you feel when you stop.
ashtavakra_gita::260.insight: It shifts your focus from clinging to release, showing that true dignity arises from freedom from attachments and hopes.

ashtavakra_gita::261.verse_sanskrit:
तुष्टिः सर्वत्र धीरस्य यथापतितवर्तिनः ।
स्वच्छन्दं चरतो देशान् यत्रस्तमितशायिनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::261.verse_hindi: यथाप्राप्य से जीविका चलाने वाला, देशों में स्वच्छन्दता से विचरण करने वाला, जहाँ सूर्यास्त हो वहाँ शयन करने वाला धीर पुरुष सर्वत्र सन्तुष्ट है।
ashtavakra_gita::261.english_translation: The steady person who earns a living suitably, wanders freely across lands, and rests wherever the sun sets, is content everywhere.
ashtavakra_gita::261.translation_literal: तुष्टिः (contentment) सर्वत्र (everywhere) धीरस्य (of the steady one) यथापतितवर्तिनः (who acts suitably) । स्वच्छन्दं (freely) चरतो (wandering) देशान् (lands) यत्र (where) अस्तमित् (sunset) अशायिनः (resting) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::261.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::261.essence: Steady freedom creates contentment everywhere, independent of place or circumstance.
ashtavakra_gita::261.simple_meaning: A steady person who lives appropriately, travels freely, and rests wherever needed feels content everywhere.
ashtavakra_gita::261.simple_insight: You can carry contentment inside you, no matter where life takes you.
ashtavakra_gita::261.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes a calm and wise person who earns their living properly, wanders without restriction across places, and rests wherever night falls, showing that true contentment is not tied to location or circumstance.
ashtavakra_gita::261.modern_relevance: You move from city to city for work or life changes, yet feel grounded and at peace wherever you arrive.
ashtavakra_gita::261.insight: It teaches you to find inner steadiness and freedom, making external conditions irrelevant to your satisfaction.

ashtavakra_gita::262.verse_sanskrit:
पततूदेतु वा देहो नास्य चिन्ता महात्मनः ।
स्वभावभूमिविश्रान्तिविस्मृताशेषसंसृतेः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::262.verse_hindi: जो निज स्वभाव रूपी भूमि में विश्राम करता है और जिसे संसार विस्मृत हो गया है, उस महात्मा को इस बात की चिन्ता नहीं है कि देह रहे या जाए ।
ashtavakra_gita::262.english_translation: One who rests in the nature of their own true self and has forgotten the entire world has no concern whether the body remains or departs.
ashtavakra_gita::262.translation_literal: पततूदेतु (fall or depart) / वा (or) / देहो (body) / नास्य (there is not) / चिन्ता (worry) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one) / स्वभावभूमिविश्रान्ति (rest in the nature-ground) / विस्मृताः (forgotten) / अेष (entire) / संसृतेः (of the world)
ashtavakra_gita::262.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::262.essence: Resting in your true self dissolves all worry about the body's impermanence.
ashtavakra_gita::262.simple_meaning: When you rest in your true self and forget the world, you no longer worry if your body lives or dies.
ashtavakra_gita::262.simple_insight: Freedom comes when your identity is beyond the body and worldly concerns.
ashtavakra_gita::262.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a great soul who abides in their true self, detached from worldly distractions, faces no fear or anxiety about the body’s mortality.
ashtavakra_gita::262.modern_relevance: You feel calm when you stop obsessing over aging or health and instead connect with your deeper self.
ashtavakra_gita::262.insight: It shifts your focus from bodily survival to abiding as the unchanging true self beneath all change.

ashtavakra_gita::263.verse_sanskrit:
अकिञ्चनः कामचारो निर्द्वन्द्वश्छिन्नसंशयः ।
असक्तः सर्वभावेषु केवलो रमते बुधः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::263.verse_hindi: अकिञ्चन, स्वच्छन्द विचरण करने वाला, द्वन्द्वरहित, संशयरहित, आसक्तिरहित और अकेला बुद्ध पुरुष ही सब भावों में रमण करता है ।
ashtavakra_gita::263.english_translation: The wise person who has nothing, wanders freely, is free of duality and doubt, unattached, and alone, delights in all feelings.
ashtavakra_gita::263.translation_literal: अकिञ्चनः (without possessions) / कामचारो (freely wandering) / निर्द्वन्द्वः (without duality) / छिन्नसंशयः (without doubt) / असक्तः (unattached) / सर्वभावेषु (in all states) / केवलः (alone) / रमते (delights) / बुधः (the wise one)
ashtavakra_gita::263.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::263.essence: True wisdom is freedom from attachments and doubt while delighting in all feelings.
ashtavakra_gita::263.simple_meaning: A wise person who owns nothing, moves freely without confusion or attachments, and enjoys all feelings equally.
ashtavakra_gita::263.simple_insight: There's freedom in letting go and still finding joy in every experience.
ashtavakra_gita::263.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes the wise person who has abandoned all possessions and attachments, walks freely without inner conflict or doubt, and yet finds joy within all emotional states, embodying perfect balance and freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::263.modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed by choices and attachments, but true peace comes when you let go and accept all feelings without clinging.
ashtavakra_gita::263.insight: It teaches you to release attachments and doubts so you can fully engage with life without inner conflict.

ashtavakra_gita::264.verse_hindi: जो ममता रहित है उसके लिए मिट्टी, पत्थर और सोना समान है । जिसके हृदय की ग्रन्थि टूट गयी है और जिसका रज-तम धुल गया है वह धीर पुरुष ही शोभता है।
ashtavakra_gita::264.english_translation: One who is free from attachment sees clay, stone, and gold as the same; whose heart’s knot is undone and whose impurities are removed is the truly steady person.
ashtavakra_gita::264.translation_literal: निर्ममः (without attachment) / शोभते (shines) / धीरः (steady person) / समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः (clay, stone, gold alike) / सुभिन्नहृदयग्रन्थिः (whose heart's knot is undone) / विनिर्धूतरजस्तमः (whose impurities and darkness are removed)
ashtavakra_gita::264.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::264.essence: Freedom from attachment makes all things appear equally radiant and steady.
ashtavakra_gita::264.simple_meaning: A person free from attachment sees all things the same, whether valuable or not, because their heart’s confusion is cleared.
ashtavakra_gita::264.simple_insight: You can feel steady and peaceful when you release your grip on what matters and what doesn’t.
ashtavakra_gita::264.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that when a person’s heart is free from emotional knots and impurities, they no longer differentiate between objects by value. Whether clay, stone, or gold, all appear equal, revealing a deep steadiness in character.
ashtavakra_gita::264.modern_relevance: You notice how you react differently to praise or criticism, success or failure—this verse invites you to find the calm beyond those swings.
ashtavakra_gita::264.insight: It teaches you to clear emotional confusion so external labels lose their power over your peace.

ashtavakra_gita::265.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वत्रानवधानस्य न किञ्चिद् वासना हृदि ।
मुक्तात्मनो वितृप्तस्य तुलना केन जायते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::265.verse_hindi: जो सर्वत्र व्यवधान से मुक्त उदासीन है और जिसके हृदय में कुछ भी वासना नहीं है । ऐसे तृप्त हुए मुक्तात्मा की किसके साथ तुलना हो सकती है।
ashtavakra_gita::265.english_translation: Someone who is free from all distraction and desire, whose heart holds no cravings, cannot be compared to anyone else.
ashtavakra_gita::265.translation_literal: सर्वत्रानवधानस्य (from all-direction inattention) / न (not) / किञ्चिद् (anything) / वासना (craving) / हृदि (in the heart) / मुक्तात्मनो (of the liberated self) / वितृप्तस्य (fully satisfied) / तुलना (comparison) / केन (by whom) / जायते (arises)
ashtavakra_gita::265.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::265.essence: A heart free from desire and distraction is uniquely fulfilled and beyond comparison.
ashtavakra_gita::265.simple_meaning: A person who has no distractions or desires and whose heart is free from cravings is fully satisfied and incomparable.
ashtavakra_gita::265.simple_insight: There is deep peace and unmatched fulfillment in a heart free of desire and distraction.
ashtavakra_gita::265.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains the state of a liberated person whose mind is free from all distractions and whose heart holds no desires. Such a person, fully satisfied and detached, stands beyond any comparison.
ashtavakra_gita::265.modern_relevance: When your mind is not pulled in every direction and your heart holds no craving, you experience a calm no one else can match.
ashtavakra_gita::265.insight: It teaches you to recognize that freedom from distraction and craving creates an incomparable inner satisfaction.

ashtavakra_gita::266.verse_sanskrit:
जानन्नपि न जानाति पश्यन्नपि न पश्यति ।
ब्रुवन्न् अपि न च ब्रूते कोऽन्यो निर्वासनादृते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::266.verse_hindi: वासनारहित पुरुष के अतिरिक्त दूसरा कौन है जो जानता हुआ भी नहीं जानता है, देखता हुआ भी नहीं देखता है, बोलता हुआ भी नहीं बोलता है।
ashtavakra_gita::266.english_translation: Who else exists without desire who neither knows, nor sees, nor speaks despite appearing to do so?
ashtavakra_gita::266.translation_literal: जानन्नपि (knowing also) / न (not) / जानाति (knows) / पश्यन्नपि (seeing also) / न (not) / पश्यति (sees) / ब्रुवन्न् (speaking) / अपि (also) / न (not) / च (and) / ब्रूते (speaks) / कोऽन्यो (who else) / निर्वासनादृते (except the desireless one)
ashtavakra_gita::266.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::266.essence: The desireless self neither knows, sees, nor speaks, yet is the true witness.
ashtavakra_gita::266.simple_meaning: The true self is beyond desire and appears to know, see, and speak, yet actually does not act or perceive in the usual way.
ashtavakra_gita::266.simple_insight: There is freedom in recognizing that your true nature transcends ordinary knowing and speaking.
ashtavakra_gita::266.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra points out that the true self, free from desire, neither truly knows, sees, nor speaks, despite appearing to do so. This teaches that the highest awareness transcends all action and perception.
ashtavakra_gita::266.modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed by endless thoughts and words, yet your true self remains untouched, watching silently beyond all noise.
ashtavakra_gita::266.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with active knowing to recognizing silent, desireless presence.

ashtavakra_gita::267.verse_sanskrit:
भिक्षुर्वा भूपतिर्वापि यो निष्कामः स शोभते ।
भावेषु गलिता यस्य शोभनाशोभना मतिः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::267.verse_hindi: जिसकी सब भावों में शोभन, अशोभन बुद्धि गलित हो गयी है और जो निष्काम है, वही शोभायमान है, चाहे वह भिखारी हो या भूपति।
ashtavakra_gita::267.english_translation: One whose mind is free of conflicting thoughts and who acts without craving shines brightly, whether a beggar or a king.
ashtavakra_gita::267.translation_literal: भिक्षुर्वा (beggar or) / भूपतिर्वापि (king also) / यो (who) / निष्कामः (without desire) / स (that one) / शोभते (shines) / भावेषु (in feelings) / गलिता (dissolved) / यस्य (whose) / शोभना (beautiful) / अशोभना (unbeautiful) / मतिः (mind)
ashtavakra_gita::267.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::267.essence: You shine by dissolving mental conflict and acting without desire, regardless of status.
ashtavakra_gita::267.simple_meaning: You shine when your mind is free of confusing thoughts and you act without wanting anything in return.
ashtavakra_gita::267.simple_insight: You can feel radiant and peaceful simply by letting go of craving and mental confusion.
ashtavakra_gita::267.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that whether someone is poor or powerful, what truly makes them shine is a clear mind free of conflicting thoughts and acting without desire for results. This wisdom comes early in the text to guide Janaka toward freedom.
ashtavakra_gita::267.modern_relevance: You feel calm and confident when your thoughts stop racing and you focus on doing your work without obsessing over rewards.
ashtavakra_gita::267.insight: It teaches you to clear mental clutter and release craving to reveal your natural brightness.

ashtavakra_gita::268.verse_sanskrit:
क्व स्वाच्छन्द्यं क्व सङ्कोचः क्व वा तत्त्वविनिश्चयः ।
निर्व्याजार्जवभूतस्य चरितार्थस्य योगिनः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::268.verse_hindi: निष्कपट, सरल और यथार्थ चरित्र वाले योगी को कहाँ स्वच्छन्दता है, कहाँ संकोच है और कहाँ तत्त्व का निश्चय है।
ashtavakra_gita::268.english_translation: Where is freedom, where hesitation, and where is certainty of truth for the sincere, simple, and genuine yogi?
ashtavakra_gita::268.translation_literal: क्व (where) / स्वाच्छन्द्यं (freedom) / क्व (where) / सङ्कोचः (hesitation) / क्व (where) / वा (or) / तत्त्वविनिश्चयः (certainty of truth) / निर्व्याजार्जवभूतस्य (of the sincere, genuine) / चरितार्थस्य (whose conduct is true) / योगिनः (yogi)
ashtavakra_gita::268.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::268.essence: Sincere, genuine character leaves no room for hesitation or doubt about truth.
ashtavakra_gita::268.simple_meaning: A yogi whose character is sincere, simple, and genuine does not experience hesitation, doubt, or even the need for certainty about truth.
ashtavakra_gita::268.simple_insight: When you live with true sincerity, hesitation and doubt naturally disappear.
ashtavakra_gita::268.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Ashtavakra points out that a yogi who embodies sincerity, simplicity, and truthfulness is beyond hesitation, doubt, or the need to prove ultimate reality. This moment reveals the yogi’s stable and clear state.
ashtavakra_gita::268.modern_relevance: When you act with honest intentions and integrity, you stop second-guessing yourself and find natural clarity in your choices.
ashtavakra_gita::268.insight: It shifts your focus from needing external proof to trusting your sincere inner conduct as enough.

ashtavakra_gita::269.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मविश्रान्तितृप्तेन निराशेन गतार्तिना ।
अन्तर्यदनुभूयेत तत् कथं कस्य कथ्यते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::269.verse_hindi: आत्मा में विश्राम कर तृप्त हुए आशारहित और शोकरहित ज्ञानी के अन्तस् में जो अनुभव होता है उसे कैसे और किसको कहा जाए।
ashtavakra_gita::269.english_translation: When the wise one rests satisfied in the true self, without hope or sorrow, who and how can describe the inner experience?
ashtavakra_gita::269.translation_literal: आत्मविश्रान्तितृप्तेन (in self-rested satisfied) / निराशेन (without hope) / गतार्तिना (without sorrow) / अन्तर्यदनुभूयेत (inner-experience) / तत् (that) / कथं (how) / कस्य (of whom) / कथ्यते (is told)
ashtavakra_gita::269.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::269.essence: The deepest inner peace is beyond words and cannot be described.
ashtavakra_gita::269.simple_meaning: When you are fully at peace within yourself without expecting or grieving, the inner experience is beyond words or explanation.
ashtavakra_gita::269.simple_insight: There is a deep calm that cannot be captured by any description or shared with others.
ashtavakra_gita::269.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra describes the state of a wise person who has settled completely into the true self, free from hope or sorrow. This inner peace is so profound that it defies explanation or naming, revealing the ineffable nature of pure awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::269.modern_relevance: You have moments of quiet peace inside when nothing troubles or excites you, and you realize some experiences simply cannot be put into words.
ashtavakra_gita::269.insight: It teaches you to accept that some inner states transcend language and cannot be communicated fully.

ashtavakra_gita::270.verse_sanskrit:
सुप्तोऽपि न सुषुप्तौ च स्वप्नेऽपि शयितो न च ।
जागरेऽपि न जागर्ति धीरस्तृप्तः पदे पदे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::270.verse_hindi: जो सोया हुआ भी सुषुप्त नहीं है, और न स्वप्न में भी सोया हुआ है, जाग्रत में भी नहीं जागा हुआ है, वही धीर पुरुष क्षण-क्षण तृप्त है।
ashtavakra_gita::270.english_translation: Even when asleep, one is not in deep sleep; even in dreams, not truly asleep; and even awake, one is not truly awake — the wise are satisfied moment to moment.
ashtavakra_gita::270.translation_literal: सुप्तः (asleep) अपि (even) न (not) सुषुप्तौ (in deep sleep) च (and) स्वप्नेऽपि (in dream even) शयितः (lying down) न (not) च (and) जागरेऽपि (in waking even) न (not) जागर्ति (awake) धीरः (wise person) तृप्तः (satisfied) पदे (moment) पदे (moment) ।
ashtavakra_gita::270.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::270.essence: Wisdom is steady satisfaction beyond waking, dreaming, or sleeping states.
ashtavakra_gita::270.simple_meaning: A truly wise person is never fully lost in sleep, dreams, or waking restlessness but remains satisfied and steady at every moment.
ashtavakra_gita::270.simple_insight: You can feel steady and content no matter your state of mind or body.
ashtavakra_gita::270.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra explains to King Janaka that the truly wise do not fully identify with sleep, dreams, or waking states, but maintain a steady, satisfied presence through all phases of consciousness.
ashtavakra_gita::270.modern_relevance: When stress pulls you between restless worry and tired distraction, the wise presence is calm and content through it all.
ashtavakra_gita::270.insight: It teaches you to remain inwardly centered and content regardless of external or mental conditions.

ashtavakra_gita::271.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञः सचिन्तोऽपि निश्चिन्तः सेन्द्रियोऽपि निरिन्द्रियः ।
सुबुद्धिरपि निर्बुद्धिः साहङ्कारोऽनहङ्कृतिः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::271.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी चिन्तायुक्त भी चिन्तारहित है, इन्द्रियों सहित भी इन्द्रियों रहित है, बुद्धिसहित भी बुद्धिरहित है तथा अहंकारयुक्त भी अहंकाररहित है।
ashtavakra_gita::271.english_translation: The wise one, though engaged in thought, is without anxious thought; though with senses, is without being bound by them; though possessing intellect, is without intellect; though with ego, is without ego.
ashtavakra_gita::271.translation_literal: ज्ञः (wise one) / सचिन्तः (with thought) / अपि (also) / निश्चिन्तः (without anxious thought) / सेन्द्रियोऽपि (even with senses) / निरिन्द्रियः (without being bound by senses) / सुबुद्धिः (possessing intellect) / अपि (also) / निर्बुधिः (without intellect) / साहङ्कारः (with ego) / अनहङ्कृतिः (without ego)
ashtavakra_gita::271.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::271.essence: You can fully engage with mind and senses yet remain untouched by them.
ashtavakra_gita::271.simple_meaning: You can think and sense without being controlled by thoughts, senses, intellect, or ego.
ashtavakra_gita::271.simple_insight: You can feel calm and free even while your mind and senses are active.
ashtavakra_gita::271.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a truly wise person can engage with thoughts, senses, and ego without being limited or troubled by them, showing mastery over inner states during deep dialogue with King Janaka.
ashtavakra_gita::271.modern_relevance: You sit through a busy day, your mind active but not overwhelmed, fully present without stress controlling you.
ashtavakra_gita::271.insight: It shifts your view from being captive to your mind and senses to being their calm observer.

ashtavakra_gita::272.verse_sanskrit:
न सुखी न च वा दुःखी न विरक्तो न सङ्गवान् ।
न मुमुक्षुर्न वा मुक्ता न किञ्चिन्न्न च किञ्चन ॥
ashtavakra_gita::272.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी न सुखी है, न दुःखी है, न विरक्त है, न संगयुक्त है, न मुमुक्षु है, न मुक्त है, न किञ्चन है, न अकिञ्चन।
ashtavakra_gita::272.english_translation: The knower is neither happy nor unhappy, neither detached nor attached, neither seeker nor liberated, neither anything nor nothing.
ashtavakra_gita::272.translation_literal: न (not) सुखी (happy) न (nor) च (also) वा (or) दुःखी (unhappy) न (not) विरक्तो (detached) न (not) सङ्गवान् (attached) । न (not) मुमुक्षुः (seeker) न (not) वा (or) मुक्ता (liberated) न (not) किञ्चित् (anything) न (not) च (also) किञ्चन (nothing) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::272.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::272.essence: True knowing is beyond all opposites and identities.
ashtavakra_gita::272.simple_meaning: You are not limited to feelings like joy or sadness, nor to desires or freedom. You simply are beyond all these states.
ashtavakra_gita::272.simple_insight: There’s peace in knowing you aren’t defined by any condition or label.
ashtavakra_gita::272.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that the true knower transcends all dualities—happiness and sadness, attachment and detachment, seeking and liberation. This insight arises as a radical understanding beyond typical human emotions and roles.
ashtavakra_gita::272.modern_relevance: When moods swing or identities feel confining, this reminds you that your true self is untouched by changing feelings or roles.
ashtavakra_gita::272.insight: It shifts your sense of self from identification with emotions or desires to awareness beyond all contrasts.

ashtavakra_gita::273.verse_sanskrit:
विक्षेपेऽपि न विक्षिप्तः समाधौ न समाधिमान् ।
जाड्येऽपि न जडो धन्यः पाण्डित्येऽपि न पण्डितः ॥
ashtavakra_gita::273.verse_hindi: धन्य पुरुष विक्षेप में भी विक्षिप्त नहीं होता, समाधि में भी समाधि वाला नहीं है, जड़ता में भी जड़ नहीं है, पाण्डित्य में भी पण्डित नहीं है।
ashtavakra_gita::273.english_translation: A blessed person is not disturbed even when distractions arise, nor does one possess absorption; not dull in dullness, nor wise in wisdom.
ashtavakra_gita::273.translation_literal: विक्षेपेऽपि (even in distraction) न (not) विक्षिप्तः (disturbed) समाधौ (in absorption) न (not) समाधिमान् (absorbed) जाड्येऽपि (even in dullness) न (not) जडो (dull) धन्यः (blessed) पाण्डित्येऽपि (even in wisdom) न (not) पण्डितः (wise)
ashtavakra_gita::273.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::273.essence: True steadiness lies beyond all mental states, whether distraction, absorption, dullness, or wisdom.
ashtavakra_gita::273.simple_meaning: A truly blessed person stays calm and unchanged whether distracted, absorbed, dull, or wise.
ashtavakra_gita::273.simple_insight: You can be peaceful without being defined by your mental states or knowledge.
ashtavakra_gita::273.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a blessed person remains unaffected by mental disturbances or absorption, dullness or wisdom. This shows freedom from identification with any changing state, marking true equanimity.
ashtavakra_gita::273.modern_relevance: You face moments of distraction, deep focus, confusion, or clarity; yet your inner balance need not shift with them.
ashtavakra_gita::273.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with fluctuating states to recognizing your unchanging steadiness beyond them.

ashtavakra_gita::274.verse_sanskrit:
मुक्तो यथास्थितिस्वस्थः कृतकर्तव्यनिर्वृतः ।
समः सर्वत्र वैतृष्ण्यान्न स्मरत्यकृतं कृतम् ॥
ashtavakra_gita::274.verse_hindi: मुक्त पुरुष सब स्थितियों में स्वस्थ है, किये हुए और करने योग्य कर्म में तृप्त है, सर्वत्र समान है, तृष्णा के अभाव में किये और अनकिये कर्म को स्मरण नहीं करता है।
ashtavakra_gita::274.english_translation: The liberated person remains steady and healthy in all conditions, content with done and to-do actions, equal everywhere, without craving, and does not recall what is done or undone.
ashtavakra_gita::274.translation_literal: मुक्तो (liberated) यथा (as) स्थिति (condition) स्वस्थः (healthy) कृत (done) कर्तव्य (to-do) निर्वृतः (free) । समः (equal) सर्वत्र (everywhere) वैतृष्ण्य (without craving) अन्न (not) स्मरति (remembers) अकृतं (undone) कृतम् (done) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::274.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::274.essence: True freedom is steady contentment, free from craving and memory of actions.
ashtavakra_gita::274.simple_meaning: You can be steady and healthy in every situation, satisfied with what you have done and what remains, without craving or remembering past or future actions.
ashtavakra_gita::274.simple_insight: Freedom feels like steady contentment that doesn’t cling to past or future.
ashtavakra_gita::274.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a liberated person remains balanced and well in any situation. They are satisfied with their past actions and duties yet not attached to them. This equanimity arises from freedom from craving and forgetting both done and undone deeds.
