ashtavakra_gita::274.modern_relevance: When you stop obsessing over past mistakes or future plans, you find peace and steady well-being in any circumstance.
ashtavakra_gita::274.insight: It shifts your mind from regret or anticipation to steady acceptance and freedom in the present.

ashtavakra_gita::275.verse_sanskrit:
न प्रीयते वन्द्यमानो निन्द्यमानो न कुप्यति ।
नैवोद्विजति मरणे जीवने नाभिनन्दति ॥
ashtavakra_gita::275.verse_hindi: मुक्तपुरुष न स्तुति किये जाने पर प्रसन्न होता है, न निन्दित होने पर क्रुद्ध होता है । न मृत्यु में उद्विग्न होता है, न जीवन में हर्षित होता।
ashtavakra_gita::275.english_translation: The liberated person neither feels pleased when praised, nor angry when blamed; neither disturbed by death nor joyful in life.
ashtavakra_gita::275.translation_literal: न (not) प्रीयते (is pleased) वन्द्यमानो (when praised) निन्द्यमानो (when blamed) न (not) कुप्यति (gets angry) । नैव (not at all) उद्द्विजति (is disturbed) मरणे (at death) जीवने (in life) नाभिनन्दति (nor rejoices) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::275.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::275.essence: True freedom means remaining steady and unaffected by praise, blame, life, or death.
ashtavakra_gita::275.simple_meaning: A truly free person does not get happy from praise or angry from blame; they stay calm through life and death.
ashtavakra_gita::275.simple_insight: You can find peace by not letting others' opinions control your feelings.
ashtavakra_gita::275.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Ashtavakra describes a liberated person who is not affected by external judgments or life’s changes. Whether praised or blamed, alive or facing death, their inner state remains steady and undisturbed.
ashtavakra_gita::275.modern_relevance: You receive a compliment or criticism on social media but inside, your mood stays calm and steady, unaffected by others' opinions.
ashtavakra_gita::275.insight: It teaches you to observe others' opinions without letting them sway your emotions or disturb your inner balance.

ashtavakra_gita::276.verse_sanskrit:
न धावति जनाकीर्णं नारण्यमुपशान्तधीः ।
यथातथा यत्रतत्र सम एवावतिष्ठते ॥
ashtavakra_gita::276.verse_hindi: शान्त बुद्धि वाला पुरुष न लोगों से भरे नगर की ओर भागता है, न वन की ओर ही । वह सभी स्थिति और सभी स्थान में समभाव से ही स्थित रहता है।
ashtavakra_gita::276.english_translation: A calm mind does not flee crowded cities nor retreat to forests; it remains equally steady everywhere.
ashtavakra_gita::276.translation_literal: न (not) धावति (runs/flees) जनाकीर्णं (crowded with people) नारण्यम् (to the forest) उपशान्तधीः (calm-minded one) यथा तथा (as it is) यत्र तत्र (here and there) सम एव (equally) अवतिष्ठते (stands/remains)
ashtavakra_gita::276.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::276.essence: Calmness means being equally steady everywhere, not escaping from what surrounds you.
ashtavakra_gita::276.simple_meaning: A peaceful mind does not run away from busy places or hide in solitude; it remains balanced everywhere.
ashtavakra_gita::276.simple_insight: You can feel steady and calm no matter where you are.
ashtavakra_gita::276.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that a truly calm mind neither flees the noise of a crowded city nor seeks refuge in the forest. Instead, such a mind remains balanced and steady in all places and situations, showing true equanimity.
ashtavakra_gita::276.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed in a noisy café or restless in an empty room, but peace comes when your mind stays steady regardless of place.
ashtavakra_gita::276.insight: It teaches you to cultivate inner steadiness that does not depend on external surroundings.

ashtavakra_gita::277.verse_hindi: राजा जनक बोले – “मैंने आपके तत्त्वज्ञानरूपी संसी को लेकर हृदय और उदर से अनेक प्रकार के विचाररूपी बाणों को निकाल दिया है”।
ashtavakra_gita::277.english_translation: King Janaka said: "I have removed the arrows of many kinds of thoughts from my heart and belly, which were wounds caused by your teaching of the true nature."
ashtavakra_gita::277.translation_literal: राजा (king) / जनक (Janaka) / बोले (said) – / मैंने (I have) / आपके (your) / तत्त्वज्ञानरूपी (of true knowledge) / संसी (arrow) / को (object marker) / लेकर (taking) / हृदय (heart) / और (and) / उदर (belly) / से (from) / अनेक (many) / प्रकार (types) / के (of) / विचाररूपी (thought-like) / बाणों (arrows) / को (object marker) / निकाल (removed) / दिया (gave) / है (have) /।
ashtavakra_gita::277.speaker: Janaka
ashtavakra_gita::277.essence: Deep teaching can remove the painful arrows of confusing thoughts lodged inside you.
ashtavakra_gita::277.simple_meaning: King Janaka says that Ashtavakra's teaching has helped him remove many painful, confusing thoughts from deep inside.
ashtavakra_gita::277.simple_insight: There's relief in clearing painful thoughts that once felt like wounds.
ashtavakra_gita::277.detailed_meaning: King Janaka expresses how Ashtavakra's teaching has pierced and cleared many disturbing thoughts and doubts lodged deeply within him, freeing him from mental suffering and confusion.
ashtavakra_gita::277.modern_relevance: You feel the relief after a tough conversation that finally clears confusing doubts weighing on your mind.
ashtavakra_gita::277.insight: It shows how deep understanding can release the mind from painful, stuck thinking.

ashtavakra_gita::278.verse_sanskrit:
क्व धर्मः क्व च वा कामः क्व चार्थः क्व विवेकिता ।
क्व द्वैतं क्व च वाऽद्वैतं स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::278.verse_hindi: अपनी महिमा में स्थित मुझको कहाँ धर्म है, कहाँ काम है, कहाँ अर्थ है, कहाँ विवेकिता है, कहाँ द्वैत है और कहाँ अद्वैत है।
ashtavakra_gita::278.english_translation: In my own greatness, where is duty, where desire, where wealth, where discernment, where duality, and where non-duality?
ashtavakra_gita::278.translation_literal: क्व (where) धर्मः (duty) क्व (where) च (and) वा (or) कामः (desire) क्व (where) चार्थः (wealth) क्व (where) विवेकिता (discernment) । क्व (where) द्वैतं (duality) क्व (where) च (and) वाऽद्वैतं (non-duality) स्वमहिम्नि (in own greatness) स्थितस्य (situated) मे (of me) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::278.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::278.essence: True greatness transcends all distinctions like duty, desire, and duality.
ashtavakra_gita::278.simple_meaning: When you realize your true greatness, concepts like duty, desire, wealth, discernment, and even duality or non-duality lose their meaning.
ashtavakra_gita::278.simple_insight: You feel free from all categories that usually define and limit you.
ashtavakra_gita::278.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra declares that when one abides in their own supreme greatness, all common distinctions such as duty, desire, wealth, wisdom, and philosophical opposites like duality and non-duality collapse into insignificance.
ashtavakra_gita::278.modern_relevance: When you're deeply confident in who you are, societal labels and expectations around roles, wants, and beliefs lose their hold on you.
ashtavakra_gita::278.insight: It shifts your perspective from identifying with roles and concepts to resting in your unchanging essence.

ashtavakra_gita::279.verse_sanskrit:
क्व भूतं क्व भविष्यद् वा वर्तमानमपि क्व वा ।
क्व देशः क्व च वा नित्यं स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::279.verse_hindi: नित्य अपनी महिमा में स्थित हुए मुझको कहाँ भूत है, कहाँ भविष्य है, कहाँ वर्तमान है अथवा देश भी कहाँ है।
ashtavakra_gita::279.english_translation: Where was I in the past, where will I be in the future, and where am I now? Where is the place for the one who abides eternally in my own majesty?
ashtavakra_gita::279.translation_literal: क्व (where) / भूतं (past) / क्व (where) / भविष्यद् (future) / वा (or) / वर्तमानम् (present) / अपि (also) / क्व (where) / वा (or) / देशः (place) / क्व (where) / च (and) / वा (or) / नित्यम् (eternal) / स्वमहिम्नि (in own majesty) / स्थितस्य (abiding) / मे (my)
ashtavakra_gita::279.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::279.essence: Your true self is never confined to time or place but exists eternally.
ashtavakra_gita::279.simple_meaning: You who remain eternally within your own greatness are not limited by past, present, future, or any place.
ashtavakra_gita::279.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing you are not bound by time or location.
ashtavakra_gita::279.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra challenges the idea of self limited by time or space, showing the true self stands eternally beyond all temporal and spatial boundaries.
ashtavakra_gita::279.modern_relevance: When life feels overwhelmed by past regrets or future worries, this reminds you that your true self is beyond these moments.
ashtavakra_gita::279.insight: Shift your view from being a time-bound self to an eternal presence beyond change.

ashtavakra_gita::280.verse_sanskrit:
क्व चात्मा क्व च वानात्मा क्व शुभं क्वाशुभं यथा ।
क्व चिन्ता क्व च वाचिन्ता स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::280.verse_hindi: अपनी महिमा में स्थित हुए मुझको कहाँ आत्मा है और कहाँ अनात्मा अथवा कहाँ शुभ है, कहाँ अशुभ है, कहाँ चिन्ता है अथवा कहाँ अचिन्ता है।
ashtavakra_gita::280.english_translation: Established in my own greatness, where is the self or non-self? Where is good or bad? Where is worry or its absence?
ashtavakra_gita::280.translation_literal: क्व (where) चात्मा (self) क्व (where) च (and) वानात्मा (non-self) क्व (where) शुभं (good) क्वाशुभं (where bad) यथा (just as) । क्व (where) चिन्ता (worry) क्व (where) च (and) वाचिन्ता (no worry) स्वमहिम्नि (in own greatness) स्थितस्य (being) मे (my) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::280.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::280.essence: Resting in your true greatness dissolves all distinctions and worries.
ashtavakra_gita::280.simple_meaning: When you rest in your true greatness, distinctions like self or non-self, good or bad, and worry disappear.
ashtavakra_gita::280.simple_insight: You feel free knowing all dualities and worries fade when you recognize your true nature.
ashtavakra_gita::280.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra teaches that when one abides in their own innate greatness, all dualities—self and non-self, good and bad, worry and peace—lose their meaning and presence, revealing the undivided nature of existence.
ashtavakra_gita::280.modern_relevance: After a stressful day, you finally sit quietly and realize your anxieties and judgments lose their grip when you connect with your inner strength.
ashtavakra_gita::280.insight: It shifts your mind from reacting to dualities toward resting in undivided presence beyond judgments and worries.

ashtavakra_gita::281.verse_sanskrit:
क्व स्वप्नः क्व सुषुप्तिर्वा क्व च जागरणं तथा ।
क्व तुरीयं भयं वापि स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::281.verse_hindi: अपनी महिमा में स्थित हुए मुझको कहाँ स्वप्न, कहाँ सुषुप्ति, कहाँ जाग्रत और कहाँ तुरीय अवस्था का भय है।
ashtavakra_gita::281.english_translation: Being established in my own greatness, where is the fear of dream, deep sleep, waking, or the fourth state for me?
ashtavakra_gita::281.translation_literal: क्व (where) स्वप्नः (dream) क्व (where) सुषुप्तिः (deep sleep) वा (or) क्व (where) च (and) जागरणं (waking) तथा (also) । क्व (where) तुरीयं (the fourth state) भयः (fear) वा (or) अपि (also) स्वमहिम्नि (in own greatness) स्थितस्य (being established) मे (my) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::281.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::281.essence: True self-awareness removes all fear of changing states or experiences.
ashtavakra_gita::281.simple_meaning: When you recognize your true self, you no longer fear dreams, deep sleep, waking, or the fourth state.
ashtavakra_gita::281.simple_insight: You can feel totally safe and fearless by resting in your real, unchanging self.
ashtavakra_gita::281.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra declares that once you are firmly established in your true greatness—the real self—there is no fear of any states of consciousness like dreaming, deep sleep, waking, or the mystical fourth state. This verse reveals the fearless stability of true self-awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::281.modern_relevance: In moments of anxiety or uncertainty, remembering your inner strength makes fears about changing states of mind or life situations disappear.
ashtavakra_gita::281.insight: It teaches you to root your awareness in your true self, beyond all changing mental states, dissolving fear.

ashtavakra_gita::282.verse_sanskrit:
क्व दूरं क्व समीपं वा बाह्यं क्वाभ्यन्तरं क्व वा ।
क्व स्थूलं क्व च वा सूक्ष्मं स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::282.verse_hindi: अपनी महिमा में स्थित मुझको कहाँ दूर है, कहाँ समीप है, कहाँ बाह्य है, कहाँ अभ्यन्तर है, स्थूल कहाँ है और सूक्ष्म कहाँ है।
ashtavakra_gita::282.english_translation: Where is the self established in its own greatness—far or near, outside or inside, gross or subtle?
ashtavakra_gita::282.translation_literal: क्व (where) / दूरं (far) / क्व (where) / समीपं (near) / वा (or) / बाह्यं (outside) / क्वाभ्यन्तरं (where inside) / क्व (where) / वा (or) / स्थूलं (gross) / क्व (where) / च (and) / वा (or) / सूक्ष्मं (subtle) / स्वमहिम्नि (in own greatness) / स्थितस्य (established) / मे (of me)
ashtavakra_gita::282.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::282.essence: The true self transcends all notions of distance, location, and form.
ashtavakra_gita::282.simple_meaning: The true self is not limited by distance, location, or form; it is beyond near, far, inside, outside, gross, or subtle.
ashtavakra_gita::282.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing your true self is everywhere and not confined by any boundary.
ashtavakra_gita::282.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra questions the nature of the self beyond all physical or mental divisions. He points out that the self, established in its own greatness, is beyond concepts of distance, space, and subtlety. This teaching invites Janaka to see beyond appearances to pure awareness.
ashtavakra_gita::282.modern_relevance: When you feel confined by your circumstances or identity, remember your true nature is beyond all limits and labels.
ashtavakra_gita::282.insight: It shifts your perspective from identifying with outer or inner limits to recognizing your boundless true self.

ashtavakra_gita::283.verse_sanskrit:
क्व मृत्युर्जीवितं वा क्व लोकाः क्वास्य क्व लौकिकम् ।
क्व लयः क्व समाधिर्वा स्वमहिम्नि स्थितस्य मे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::283.verse_hindi: अपनी महिमा में स्थित हुए मुझको कहाँ मृत्यु है अथवा कहाँ जीवन है । कहाँ लोक है व कहाँ इसका लौकिक व्यवहार है । कहाँ लय है और कहाँ समाधि।
ashtavakra_gita::283.english_translation: Where is death or life for me who is established in my own greatness? Where are worlds or worldly affairs? Where is dissolution or absorbed presence?
ashtavakra_gita::283.translation_literal: क्व (where) मृत्यु (death) जीवितं (life) वा (or) क्व (where) लोकाः (worlds) क्वास्य (where of that) क्व (where) लौकिकम् (worldly) । क्व (where) लयः (dissolution) क्व (where) समाधिः (absorbed presence) वा (or) स्वमहिम्नि (in own greatness) स्थितस्य (established) मे (of me) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::283.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::283.essence: Your true self is untouched by life, death, worlds, or absorbed states.
ashtavakra_gita::283.simple_meaning: When you rest in your true greatness, life, death, and worldly states lose their hold on you.
ashtavakra_gita::283.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing these changes don't touch your real self.
ashtavakra_gita::283.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to King Janaka, declaring that the true self, rooted in its own greatness, is untouched by death, life, or worldly phenomena. This shifts perspective from identification with change to abiding in unchanging being.
ashtavakra_gita::283.modern_relevance: When stress makes you feel trapped by life’s ups and downs, remember your deepest self is beyond all that.
ashtavakra_gita::283.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as caught in change to realizing your stable, untouchable core.

ashtavakra_gita::284.verse_sanskrit:
अलं त्रिवर्गकथया योगस्य कथयाप्यलम् ।
अलं विज्ञानकथया विश्रान्तस्य ममात्मनि ॥
ashtavakra_gita::284.verse_hindi: अपनी आत्मा में विश्रान्त हुए मुझको त्रिवर्ग की कथा पर्याप्त है, योग की कथा भी पर्याप्त है, विज्ञान की कथा भी पर्याप्त है।
ashtavakra_gita::284.english_translation: For my soul at rest, the stories of the three worlds, of yoga, and of wisdom are all enough.
ashtavakra_gita::284.translation_literal: अलं (enough) / त्रिवर्गकथया (by the story of the three worlds) / योगस्य (of yoga) / कथयाप्यलम् (also enough) / अलं (enough) / विज्ञानकथया (by the story of wisdom) / विश्रान्तस्य (of the one at rest) / ममात्मनि (in my soul)
ashtavakra_gita::284.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::284.essence: When your soul rests deeply, all teachings become naturally sufficient and satisfying.
ashtavakra_gita::284.simple_meaning: When your soul is truly at peace, stories about the universe, yoga, or wisdom all feel fully sufficient.
ashtavakra_gita::284.simple_insight: You can feel complete and content without seeking more knowledge or teachings.
ashtavakra_gita::284.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks from deep inner calm, saying that once the soul rests fully, teachings about the three worlds, yoga, or wisdom no longer pull or push; they are simply enough.
ashtavakra_gita::284.modern_relevance: After restless searching, you finally feel settled and realize you don’t need more advice or concepts to find peace.
ashtavakra_gita::284.insight: It shifts your mind from seeking external teachings to recognizing inner peace as the true fulfillment.

ashtavakra_gita::285.verse_sanskrit:
क्व भूतानि क्व देहो वा क्वेन्द्रियाणि क्व वा मनः ।
क्व शून्यं क्व च नैराश्यं मत्स्वरूपे निरञ्जने ॥
ashtavakra_gita::285.verse_hindi: मेरे निरञ्जन स्वरूप में कहाँ पंचभूत हैं, कहाँ देह है, कहाँ इन्द्रियाँ हैं अथवा कहाँ मन है, कहाँ शून्य है और कहाँ नैराश्य है।
ashtavakra_gita::285.english_translation: In my pure, untouched nature, where are the five elements, the body, the senses, the mind, emptiness, or despair?
ashtavakra_gita::285.translation_literal: क्व (where) / भूतानि (elements) / क्व (where) / देहो (body) / वा (or) / क्वेन्द्रियाणि (senses) / क्व (where) / वा (or) / मनः (mind) / क्व (where) / शून्यं (emptiness) / क्व (where) / च (and) / नैराश्यं (despair) / मत्स्वरूपे (in my nature) / निरञ्जने (untouched/pure)
ashtavakra_gita::285.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::285.essence: Your true self is untouched by body, mind, or any limitation.
ashtavakra_gita::285.simple_meaning: Your true nature is pure and untouched by physical elements, senses, mind, emptiness, or despair.
ashtavakra_gita::285.simple_insight: You are more than your body or mind; your essence is untouched and whole.
ashtavakra_gita::285.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra challenges the idea that the true self is tied to the body, senses, or mind by asking where these exist in his pure, untouched nature. He reveals the self as beyond all change and suffering.
ashtavakra_gita::285.modern_relevance: When stress or despair overwhelm you, remember your true nature remains untouched beneath all mental and physical turmoil.
ashtavakra_gita::285.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing body and mind to recognizing the unchanging true self.

ashtavakra_gita::286.verse_sanskrit:
क्व शास्त्रं क्वात्मविज्ञानं क्व वा निर्विषयं मनः ।
क्व तृप्तिः क्व वितृष्णात्वं गतद्वन्द्वस्य मे सदा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::286.verse_hindi: सदा द्वन्द्वरहित मुझको कहाँ शास्त्र, कहाँ आत्मविज्ञान है, कहाँ विषयरहित मन है, कहाँ तृप्ति है, कहाँ तृष्णा का अभाव है।
ashtavakra_gita::286.english_translation: I am always free from duality; where is scripture, where is knowledge of the true self, where is a mind without desire, where is satisfaction, where is absence of craving?
ashtavakra_gita::286.translation_literal: क्व (where) शास्त्रं (scripture) क्व (where) आत्मविज्ञानं (true-self knowledge) क्व (where) वा (or) निर्विषयं (objectless) मनः (mind) । क्व (where) तृप्तिः (satisfaction) क्व (where) वितृष्णात्वं (absence-of-craving) गतद्वन्द्वस्य (gone-duality) मे (my) सदा (always) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::286.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::286.essence: True self is beyond craving, conflict, and all distinctions.
ashtavakra_gita::286.simple_meaning: You have always been free from duality, craving, and desire; your true self knows no conflict or dissatisfaction.
ashtavakra_gita::286.simple_insight: You can feel peaceful knowing your true self is untouched by cravings or conflict.
ashtavakra_gita::286.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks from the perspective of one who dwells beyond all dualities. He questions the existence of scriptures, self-knowledge, desireless mind, satisfaction, and freedom from craving, revealing he has transcended all these distinctions completely.
ashtavakra_gita::286.modern_relevance: In moments when your mind races with wants and restlessness, you can remember your essential freedom beyond those urges and conflicts.
ashtavakra_gita::286.insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with restless desires to recognizing the unchanging peace beyond all duality.

ashtavakra_gita::287.verse_sanskrit:
क्व विद्या क्व च वाविद्या क्वाहं क्वेदं मम क्व वा ।
क्व बन्ध क्व च वा मोक्षः स्वरूपस्य क्व रूपिता ॥
ashtavakra_gita::287.verse_hindi: स्व स्वरूप की कहाँ रूपिता है, कहाँ विद्या है और कहाँ अविद्या है, कहाँ ‘मैं’ है अथवा कहाँ ‘यह’ है, कहाँ ‘मेरा’ है, कहाँ बन्ध है अथवा कहाँ मोक्ष है।
ashtavakra_gita::287.english_translation: Where is knowledge? Where is ignorance? Where am I? Where is this? Where is mine? Where is bondage? Where is freedom? Where is the form of the true self?
ashtavakra_gita::287.translation_literal: क्व (where) / विद्या (knowledge) / क्व (where) / च (and) / वा (or) / अविद्या (ignorance) / क्वाहं (where am I) / क्वेदं (where is this) / मम (mine) / क्व (where) / वा (or) / क्व (where) / बन्ध (bondage) / क्व (where) / च (and) / वा (or) / मोक्षः (freedom) / स्वरूपस्य (of true self) / क्व (where) / रूपिता (is formed)
ashtavakra_gita::287.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::287.essence: The self and its qualities have no fixed location or form to be found or lost.
ashtavakra_gita::287.simple_meaning: Questions about where knowledge, ignorance, self, and freedom exist show that these ideas have no fixed place or form in reality.
ashtavakra_gita::287.simple_insight: You feel relief realizing these concepts are not separate things to be found or lost.
ashtavakra_gita::287.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra questions the very existence of knowledge, ignorance, self, and freedom as distinct entities. This challenges King Janaka’s assumptions, setting the stage for radical non-dual insight that the true self is beyond all such distinctions.
ashtavakra_gita::287.modern_relevance: You wonder where your true self or clarity lives amid swirling doubts and shifting identities, but the real you has no fixed address.
ashtavakra_gita::287.insight: It shifts your thinking from searching for fixed states to recognizing the emptiness of such concepts as separate realities.

ashtavakra_gita::288.verse_sanskrit:
क्व प्रारब्धानि कर्माणि जीवन्मुक्तिरपि क्व वा ।
क्व तद् विदेहकैवल्यं निर्विशेषस्य सर्वदा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::288.verse_hindi: मुझ सदैव निर्विशेष को प्रारब्ध कर्म कहाँ अथवा कहाँ जीवन्मुक्ति है और कहाँ यह विदेह कैवल्य ही है।
ashtavakra_gita::288.english_translation: Where are the consequences of past actions, where is liberation, and where is the formless isolation that is always present?
ashtavakra_gita::288.translation_literal: क्व (where) / प्रारब्धानि (consequences of past actions) / कर्माणि (actions) / जीवन्मुक्तिरपि (even liberation while living) / क्व (where) / वा (or) / क्व (where) / तद् (that) / विदेहकैवल्यं (formless isolation) / निर्विशेषस्य (without distinction) / सर्वदा (always)
ashtavakra_gita::288.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::288.essence: True freedom is always present and never limited by past actions.
ashtavakra_gita::288.simple_meaning: There is no real place where past actions limit you, no separate liberation needed because the formless freedom is always present.
ashtavakra_gita::288.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing freedom is not somewhere to reach—it is your ever-present reality.
ashtavakra_gita::288.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra questions where past actions truly affect the liberated being, suggesting that ultimate freedom and the formless state are always present beyond action and consequence.
ashtavakra_gita::288.modern_relevance: When regrets or past mistakes weigh on you, this reminds you that your true self remains untouched and free now.
ashtavakra_gita::288.insight: It shifts your view from being trapped by history to recognizing your constant freedom beyond it.

ashtavakra_gita::289.verse_sanskrit:
क्व कर्ता क्व च वा भोक्ता निष्क्रियं स्फुरणं क्व वा ।
क्वापरोक्षं फलं वा क्व निःस्वभावस्य मे सदा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::289.verse_hindi: सदा स्वभावरहित मुझको कहाँ कर्त्तापन है और कहाँ भोक्तापन । कहाँ निष्क्रियता है और कहाँ स्फुरण है । कहाँ अपरोक्ष ज्ञान है अथवा कहाँ फल है।
ashtavakra_gita::289.english_translation: I am always free of doer-ness and experiencer-ness; where is action or reaction? Where is direct result or effect for my true nature?
ashtavakra_gita::289.translation_literal: क्व (where) / कर्ता (doer) / क्व (where) / च (and) / वा (or) / भोक्ता (experiencer) / निष्क्रियं (inactive) / स्फुरणं (activity) / क्व (where) / वा (or) । / क्वापरोक्षं (where direct/unmediated) / फलं (result) / वा (or) / क्व (where) / निःस्वभावस्य (of true nature) / मे (my) / सदा (always) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::289.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::289.essence: Your true self is never the doer or experiencer and remains untouched by action or result.
ashtavakra_gita::289.simple_meaning: You are never truly the one who acts or the one who experiences results. Your true nature is untouched by action, reaction, or outcomes.
ashtavakra_gita::289.simple_insight: There is freedom in realizing you are not the doer or the receiver of consequences.
ashtavakra_gita::289.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra challenges the sense of being a doer or experiencer. He points out that the true self is always beyond action, reaction, and results, untouched by the usual flow of cause and effect.
ashtavakra_gita::289.modern_relevance: When stress hits after a tough conversation, you can remember you are not the doer of all effects, freeing you from unnecessary guilt and anxiety.
ashtavakra_gita::289.insight: It shifts your view from identifying as the actor or sufferer to seeing yourself as the unmoved witness beyond all action.

ashtavakra_gita::290.verse_sanskrit:
क्व लोकं क्व मुमुक्षुर्वा क्व योगी ज्ञानवान् क्व वा ।
क्व बद्धः क्व च वा मुक्तः स्वस्वरूपेऽहमद्वये ॥
ashtavakra_gita::290.verse_hindi: मुझ अद्वय स्वरूप को कहाँ लोक है अथवा कहाँ मुमुक्षु है । कहाँ योगी है, कहाँ ज्ञानवान है अथवा कहाँ बद्ध है और कहाँ मुक्त।
ashtavakra_gita::290.english_translation: Where is the world, where the seeker, where the yogi, the wise one? Where is the bound, and where the free? I am my own non-dual nature.
ashtavakra_gita::290.translation_literal: क्व (where) / लोकं (world) / क्व (where) / मुमुक्षुर्वा (seeker or) / क्व (where) / योगी (yogi) / ज्ञानवान् (wise one) / क्व (where) / वा (or) / क्व (where) / बद्धः (bound) / क्व (where) / च (and) / वा (or) / मुक्तः (free) / स्वस्वरूपेऽहम् (in my own nature I am) / अद्वये (non-dual)
ashtavakra_gita::290.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::290.essence: Your true self is beyond all divided identities and roles.
ashtavakra_gita::290.simple_meaning: You are not the world, the seeker, the yogi, or the bound and free states. You are your own undivided true nature.
ashtavakra_gita::290.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing you are beyond all labels and roles.
ashtavakra_gita::290.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra challenges the idea of separate identities—world, seeker, yogi, bound or free. He reveals that all these distinctions vanish, exposing the self as pure non-dual awareness without divisions.
ashtavakra_gita::290.modern_relevance: When you feel torn by roles or expectations, remember your true self is beyond all these shifting identities.
ashtavakra_gita::290.insight: It shifts your understanding from identifying with roles to recognizing your unchanging true nature.

ashtavakra_gita::291.verse_sanskrit:
क्व सृष्टिः क्व च संहारः क्व साध्यं क्व च साधनम् ।
क्व साधकः क्व सिद्धिर्वा स्वस्वरूपेऽहमद्वये ॥
ashtavakra_gita::291.verse_hindi: मुझ अद्वय स्वरूप को कहाँ सृष्टि और कहाँ संहार । कहाँ साध्य है और कहाँ साधन है । कहाँ साधक है अथवा कहाँ सिद्धि है।
ashtavakra_gita::291.english_translation: Where is creation, where destruction? Where is the to-be-achieved, where the means? Where is the doer, and where is the achievement? I am my nondual nature.
ashtavakra_gita::291.translation_literal: क्व (where) सृष्टिः (creation) क्व (where) च (and) संहारः (destruction) क्व (where) साध्यं (to-be-achieved) क्व (where) च (and) साधनम् (means) । क्व (where) साधकः (doer) क्व (where) सिद्धिर्वा (or achievement) स्वस्वरूपेऽहम् (in my own nature I am) अद्वये (nondual) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::291.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::291.essence: Your true self is beyond doer, deed, and duality—it is pure nondual nature.
ashtavakra_gita::291.simple_meaning: Everything like creation, destruction, doer, and achievement does not apply to your true self, which is nondual and unchanged.
ashtavakra_gita::291.simple_insight: You can feel free from the pressure of being a doer or a result because your true nature is pure and beyond all change.
ashtavakra_gita::291.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to King Janaka, pointing beyond the usual distinctions of life—creation and destruction, doer and deed, goal and means. He reveals that the true self is untouched by these opposites, existing as pure nonduality beyond all dual concepts.
ashtavakra_gita::291.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by roles or achievements, knowing your true self is beyond these brings deep relief and clarity.
ashtavakra_gita::291.insight: It shifts your focus from identifying as a doer or a goal to recognizing your unchanging, nondual essence.

ashtavakra_gita::292.verse_sanskrit:
क्व प्रमाता प्रमाणं वा क्व प्रमेयं क्व च प्रमा ।
क्व किञ्चित् क्व न किञ्चिद् वा सर्वदा विमलस्य मे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::292.verse_hindi: सर्वदा विमालरूप मुझको कहाँ प्रमाता, कहाँ प्रमाण, कहाँ प्रमेय और कहाँ प्रमा है । कहाँ किंचित् है और कहाँ अकिंचित् है।
ashtavakra_gita::292.english_translation: Where is the doer, the object of knowledge, the means of knowledge, or the knowledge itself? Where is anything or nothing for the ever-pure self?
ashtavakra_gita::292.translation_literal: क्व (where) प्रमाता (doer) प्रमाणं (means of knowledge) वा (or) क्व (where) प्रमेयं (object of knowledge) क्व (where) च (and) प्रमा (knowledge) । (.) क्व (where) किञ्चित् (anything) क्व (where) न (not) किञ्चिद् (anything) वा (or) सर्वदा (always) विमलस्य (of the pure) मे (my) ॥ (।)
ashtavakra_gita::292.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::292.essence: The true self transcends all roles of doer, known, and knowledge simultaneously.
ashtavakra_gita::292.simple_meaning: The true self is beyond being a doer, the known, the means of knowing, or knowledge itself; it is always pure and untouched by any object or concept.
ashtavakra_gita::292.simple_insight: You are not the actor or the objects you perceive; you are pure, unchanged presence.
ashtavakra_gita::292.detailed_meaning: In a profound moment of teaching, Ashtavakra questions the very categories of action and knowledge. He challenges King Janaka to see that the true self transcends all roles of doer, means, or object, revealing a reality untouched by any duality or limitation.
ashtavakra_gita::292.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by choices or roles, remember you are not defined by what you do or know but by your pure existence beyond it all.
ashtavakra_gita::292.insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with actions and perceptions to recognizing your nature as pure awareness beyond all distinctions.

ashtavakra_gita::293.verse_sanskrit:
क्व विक्षेपः क्व चैकाग्र्यं क्व निर्बोधः क्व मूढता ।
क्व हर्षः क्व विषादो वा सर्वदा निष्क्रियस्य मे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::293.verse_hindi: सर्वदा क्रियारहित मुझको कहाँ एकाग्रता, कहाँ ज्ञान, कहाँ मूढ़ता, कहाँ हर्ष और कहाँ विषाद है।
ashtavakra_gita::293.english_translation: Where is distraction, where is focus, where is knowledge, where is confusion? Where is joy, where is sorrow, for me who is always inactive?
ashtavakra_gita::293.translation_literal: क्व (where) / विक्षेपः (distraction) / क्व (where) / चैकाग्र्यं (single-pointedness) / क्व (where) / निर्बोधः (knowledge) / क्व (where) / मूढता (confusion) / क्व (where) / हर्षः (joy) / क्व (where) / विषादो (sorrow) / वा (or) / सर्वदा (always) / निष्क्रियस्य (inactive) / मे (of me)
ashtavakra_gita::293.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::293.essence: The true self remains unaffected and inactive beyond all emotions and mental activity.
ashtavakra_gita::293.simple_meaning: There is no distraction, focus, knowledge, confusion, joy, or sorrow in the self that remains always still and inactive.
ashtavakra_gita::293.simple_insight: You can feel peaceful knowing your true self is untouched by emotions or restlessness.
ashtavakra_gita::293.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks about the state of pure awareness free from all mental disturbances. He declares that for the one who is always inactive—beyond action and reaction—there is no mental disturbance or emotion to affect them.
ashtavakra_gita::293.modern_relevance: When your mind feels overwhelmed with emotions or scattered thoughts, this reminds you that your true self remains calm and unaffected beneath it all.
ashtavakra_gita::293.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with fluctuating emotions to resting in the steady awareness beyond them.

ashtavakra_gita::294.verse_sanskrit:
क्व चैष व्यवहारो वा क्व च सा परमार्थता ।
क्व सुखं क्व च वा दुखं निर्विमर्शस्य मे सदा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::294.verse_hindi: सदा निर्विकाररूप मुझको कहाँ यह व्यवहार है और कहाँ वह परमार्थता है । कहाँ सुख है अथवा कहाँ दुःख है।
ashtavakra_gita::294.english_translation: I am always the changeless reality; where is this worldly life, or that supreme truth? Where is happiness or sorrow for one who sees clearly?
ashtavakra_gita::294.translation_literal: क्व (where) चैष (this) व्यवहारो (worldly life) वा (or) क्व (where) च (also) सा (that) परमार्थता (highest truth) । क्व (where) सुखं (happiness) क्व (where) च (also) वा (or) दुखं (sorrow) निर्विमर्शस्य (of the one who sees clearly) मे (my) सदा (always) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::294.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::294.essence: The true self never changes and remains untouched by happiness or sorrow.
ashtavakra_gita::294.simple_meaning: You are always the unchanging reality; worldly life, supreme truth, happiness, and sorrow do not touch your true nature.
ashtavakra_gita::294.simple_insight: There is calm in knowing your true self remains untouched by life's changes.
ashtavakra_gita::294.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra points out that the true self is always changeless and beyond worldly fluctuations. He questions where ordinary life, ultimate reality, happiness, or sorrow truly exist for someone who perceives clearly.
ashtavakra_gita::294.modern_relevance: When stress and emotions overwhelm you, remembering your core remains steady brings relief and perspective.
ashtavakra_gita::294.insight: It teaches you to shift focus from external ups and downs to the inner unchanging awareness.

ashtavakra_gita::295.verse_sanskrit:
क्व माया क्व च संसारः क्व प्रीतिर्विरतिः क्व वा ।
क्व जीवः क्व च तद्ब्रह्म सर्वदा विमलस्य मे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::295.verse_hindi: मुझ सदा विमलस्वरूप को कहाँ माया और कहाँ संसार है । कहाँ प्रीति है अथवा कहाँ विरति है । कहाँ जीव है और कहाँ ब्रह्म है।
ashtavakra_gita::295.english_translation: For my always pure self, where is illusion, where is the cycle of change? Where is attachment or detachment? Where is the individual self, and where is the supreme reality?
ashtavakra_gita::295.translation_literal: क्व (where) / माया (illusion) / क्व (where) / च (and) / संसारः (cycle of change) / क्व (where) / प्रीति (attachment) / विरतिः (detachment) / क्व (where) / वा (or) / क्व (where) / जीवः (individual self) / क्व (where) / च (and) / तद् (that) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / सर्वदा (always) / विमलस्य (pure) / मे (my)
ashtavakra_gita::295.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::295.essence: Your true self is always pure and beyond all illusion and division.
ashtavakra_gita::295.simple_meaning: The pure true self is untouched by illusion, change, attachment, or any division between self and supreme reality.
ashtavakra_gita::295.simple_insight: You can feel the relief of knowing your true self is always clear and free from confusion.
ashtavakra_gita::295.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra questions where illusion, the cycle of change, attachment, or even the separate self truly exist for the always pure self, highlighting the unity of the true self and supreme reality beyond all dualities.
ashtavakra_gita::295.modern_relevance: When your mind is restless with confusion or attachment, this reminds you that your true self remains untouched and pure beneath all that noise.
ashtavakra_gita::295.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with change and confusion to recognizing your unchanging pure nature.

ashtavakra_gita::296.verse_sanskrit:
क्व प्रवृत्तिर्निर्वृत्तिर्वा क्व मुक्तिः क्व च बन्धनम् ।
कूटस्थनिर्विभागस्य स्वस्थस्य मम सर्वदा ॥
ashtavakra_gita::296.verse_hindi: सर्वदा कूटस्थ, अखण्डरूप और स्वस्थ मुझको कहाँ निवृत्ति है, कहाँ मुक्ति है और कहाँ बन्ध है।
ashtavakra_gita::296.english_translation: I am always steady, undivided, and healthy; where is activity, release, or bondage for me?
ashtavakra_gita::296.translation_literal: क्व (where) / प्रवृत्तिः (activity) / निर्वृत्तिः (release) / वा (or) / क्व (where) / मुक्तिः (freedom) / क्व (where) / च (and) / बन्धनम् (bondage) / कूटस्थ (steady) / निर्विभागस्य (undivided) / स्वस्थस्य (healthy) / मम (my) / सर्वदा (always)
ashtavakra_gita::296.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::296.essence: Your true self is always steady and untouched by activity, freedom, or bondage.
ashtavakra_gita::296.simple_meaning: Your true self is always steady, whole, and healthy; it never truly experiences activity, freedom, or bondage.
ashtavakra_gita::296.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing your true self is untouched by change or limitation.
ashtavakra_gita::296.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra challenges the idea that the true self undergoes change or bondage. He says the self is always steady and undivided, so concepts like activity, release, or being bound do not apply.
ashtavakra_gita::296.modern_relevance: When life feels chaotic or you feel trapped by circumstances, this reminds you that your core is untouched and steady beneath it all.
ashtavakra_gita::296.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as a changing doer to recognizing an ever-unchanging presence.

ashtavakra_gita::297.verse_sanskrit:
क्वोपदेशः क्व वा शास्त्रं क्व शिष्यः क्व च वा गुरुः ।
क्व चास्ति पुरुषार्थो वा निरुपाधेः शिवस्य मे ॥
ashtavakra_gita::297.verse_hindi: उपाधिरहित शिवरूप मुझको कहाँ उपदेश है, कहाँ शास्त्र है, कहाँ शिष्य है, कहाँ गुरु है और कहाँ पुरुषार्थ है।
ashtavakra_gita::297.english_translation: To the limitless form of the auspicious, there is no teaching, no scripture, no student, no teacher, and no effort.
ashtavakra_gita::297.translation_literal: क्वोपदेशः (where instruction) / क्व (where) / वा (or) / शास्त्रं (scripture) / क्व (where) / शिष्यः (student) / क्व (where) / च (and) / वा (or) / गुरुः (teacher) / क्व (where) / च (and) / वा (or) / पुरुषार्थो (effort) / वा (or) / निरुपाधेः (without limitation) / शिवस्य (of the auspicious/auspicious one) / मे (to me)
ashtavakra_gita::297.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::297.essence: The limitless true self transcends teaching, scripture, effort, and all dualities.
ashtavakra_gita::297.simple_meaning: The true self is unlimited and free of all conditions—there is no need for teachings, scriptures, students, teachers, or effort to reach it.
ashtavakra_gita::297.simple_insight: You can feel free from the pressure to learn or strive; what you seek is already present.
ashtavakra_gita::297.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to King Janaka, explaining that the supreme reality beyond all limitations needs no formal teaching, scripture, student, teacher, or effort to be realized, highlighting the nature of the true self as already perfect and complete.
ashtavakra_gita::297.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by instructions or efforts to improve, remember that your true nature is beyond all those demands and already whole.
ashtavakra_gita::297.insight: It shifts your focus from external authorities and effort to recognizing your innate completeness beyond conditions.

ashtavakra_gita::298.verse_sanskrit:
क्व चास्ति क्व च वा नास्ति क्वास्ति चैकं क्व च द्वयम् ।
बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन किञ्चिन्नोत्तिष्ठते मम ॥
ashtavakra_gita::298.verse_hindi: कहाँ अस्ति है और कहाँ नास्ति । कहाँ एक है अथवा कहाँ दो है । इसमें बहुत कहने से क्या प्रयोजन, मुझको तो कुछ भी नहीं उठ रहा है।
ashtavakra_gita::298.english_translation: Where is existence, and where is non-existence? Where is the one, and where is the two? There is no point in saying much; nothing arises for me.
ashtavakra_gita::298.translation_literal: क्व (where) चास्ति (is) क्व (where) च (and) वा (or) नास्ति (is not) क्वास्ति (where is) चैकं (one) क्व (where) च (and) द्वयम् (two) । बहुनात्र (much here) किमुक्तेन (by saying) किञ्चिन्नोत्तिष्ठते (nothing arises) मम (to me) ॥
ashtavakra_gita::298.speaker: Ashtavakra
ashtavakra_gita::298.essence: Nothing truly arises or disappears; existence and non-existence are illusions to the true self.
ashtavakra_gita::298.simple_meaning: You cannot locate where things truly exist or don’t exist; for your true self, nothing really appears or disappears.
ashtavakra_gita::298.simple_insight: You feel a quiet peace knowing that nothing truly happens to your true self.
ashtavakra_gita::298.detailed_meaning: Ashtavakra questions the common ideas of existence and non-existence, pointing out that these dualities do not affect the true self. This teaching unfolds as a challenge to ordinary perception during his dialogue with Janaka.
ashtavakra_gita::298.modern_relevance: You stare at problems that seem real but suddenly realize they don’t truly affect who you are at your core.
ashtavakra_gita::298.insight: It shifts your mind from searching for external truths to recognizing the unchanging nature within yourself.

avadhuta_gita::1.verse_hindi: महान भय से रक्षा करने वाली अद्वैत की वासना मनुष्यों में, विप्रों में, ईश्वर के अनुग्रह (कृपा) से ही उत्पन्न होती है।
avadhuta_gita::1.english_translation: The desire for non-duality that frees from great fear arises in humans, especially sages, only by the divine's grace.
avadhuta_gita::1.translation_literal: ईश्वरानुग्रहादेव (by the divine's grace only) / पुंसाम् (in humans) / अद्वैतवासना (desire for non-duality) / महद्भयपरित्राणात् (from great fear's protection) / विप्राणाम् (in sages) / उपजायते (arises)
avadhuta_gita::1.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::1.essence: The desire to transcend fear and grasp non-duality emerges only by divine kindness.
avadhuta_gita::1.simple_meaning: The wish to realize oneness and escape great fear arises in people only through the divine's kindness.
avadhuta_gita::1.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing your deepest spiritual longing is a gift, not just effort.
avadhuta_gita::1.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the powerful craving for non-duality, which protects one from deep fear, arises in humans—especially the wise—only because the divine shows kindness, not by their own doing.
avadhuta_gita::1.modern_relevance: When fear grips you at night, the sudden hope or yearning to find peace often feels like a gift beyond your control.
avadhuta_gita::1.insight: It teaches you to recognize that your deepest spiritual yearnings are not just personal efforts but arise through grace.

avadhuta_gita::2.verse_sanskrit:
येनेदं पूरितं सर्वमात्मनैवात्मनात्मनि ।
निराकारं कथं वन्दे ह्यभिन्नं शिवमव्ययम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::2.verse_hindi: यह दृश्यमान सम्पूर्ण जगत जिस आत्मा द्वारा आत्मा से आत्मा में ही पूर्ण हो रहा है उस निराकार (ब्रह्म) का मैं किस प्रकार वन्दन करूँ क्योंकि वह (जीव से) अभिन्न है, कल्याण स्वरूप है, (तथा) अव्यय है।
avadhuta_gita::2.english_translation: I worship that formless, eternal supreme reality that fills all and is inseparable from the true self.
avadhuta_gita::2.translation_literal: येनेदं (by which this) / पूरितं (is filled) / सर्वम् (all) / आत्मनैव (by the self itself) / आत्मनात्मनि (in the self, by the self) / निराकारं (formless) / कथं (how) / वन्दे (do I worship) / हि (indeed) / अभिन्नं (inseparable) / शिवम् (auspicious, welfare-bestowing) / अव्ययम् (imperishable)
avadhuta_gita::2.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::2.essence: The true self and the formless eternal whole are inseparable and already complete within you.
avadhuta_gita::2.simple_meaning: Everything visible is completely filled by the true self, which is formless, eternal, and inseparable from you.
avadhuta_gita::2.simple_insight: You are not separate from the eternal, formless presence that fills all things.
avadhuta_gita::2.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points to the supreme reality that fills all existence and yet is without form. He reflects on its inseparability from the true self and wonders how to worship what is already fully present and eternal.
avadhuta_gita::2.modern_relevance: When you realize you are deeply connected to the unchanging presence around you, worship becomes a heartfelt recognition, not a distant ritual.
avadhuta_gita::2.insight: It shifts your view from seeking outside to recognizing your own inseparable unity with the eternal presence.

avadhuta_gita::3.verse_sanskrit:
पञ्चभूतात्मकं विश्वं मरीचिजलसन्निभम् ।
कस्याप्यहो नमस्कुर्यामहमेको निरञ्जनः ॥
avadhuta_gita::3.verse_hindi: यह विश्व पाँच भूतों का समुदाय हैं जो मृगतृष्णा के जल के समान मिथ्या भी है। मैं एक ही निरन्जन (निर्दोष) हूँ। फिर मैं किसको नमस्कार करूँ।
avadhuta_gita::3.english_translation: The world is made of five elements, like a mirage or water illusion. I alone am pure and spotless; to whom should I bow?
avadhuta_gita::3.translation_literal: पञ्चभूतात्मकं (composed of five elements) विश्वं (the world) मरीचिजलसन्निभम् (like mirage-water) । कस्यापि (to anyone) अहो (oh) नमस्कुर्याम् (should I bow) अहम् (I) एको (alone) निरञ्जनः (spotless) ॥
avadhuta_gita::3.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::3.essence: You alone are pure; the world is a fleeting illusion of elements.
avadhuta_gita::3.simple_meaning: The entire world is made of changing elements and illusions like a mirage. Only your true self is pure and untainted.
avadhuta_gita::3.simple_insight: There is a deep peace in knowing your true self is untouched by the world's illusions.
avadhuta_gita::3.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the world as composed of five elements, an illusion like a mirage. He declares only the true self is spotless and questions to whom he should pay respect, highlighting the singular purity of the self beyond the transient world.
avadhuta_gita::3.modern_relevance: When everything around you feels uncertain and unstable, remember that your true essence remains pure and steady beneath all appearances.
avadhuta_gita::3.insight: This verse shifts your focus from outer appearances to recognizing your inner purity beyond all change.

avadhuta_gita::4.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मैव केवलं सर्वं भेदाभेदो न विद्यते ।
अस्ति नास्ति कथं ब्रूयां विस्मयः प्रतिभाति मे ॥
avadhuta_gita::4.verse_hindi: यह आत्मा ही सर्वरूप है तथा केवल है जिसमें भेद और अभेद विद्यमान नहीं है- इसे मैं ‘है’ अथवा ‘नहीं है’ किस प्रकार कहूँ। मुझे यह आश्चर्य रूप प्रतीत होता है।
avadhuta_gita::4.english_translation: The true self alone is everything; there is no difference or non-difference in it. How can I say it 'exists' or 'does not exist'? This amazes me.
avadhuta_gita::4.translation_literal: आत्मैव (true self alone) केवलं (only) सर्वं (everything) भेदाभेदो (difference-non-difference) न (not) विद्यते (is present) । अस्ति (exists) नास्ति (does not exist) कथं (how) ब्रूयां (should I say) विस्मयः (wonder) प्रतिभाति (appears) मे (to me) ॥
avadhuta_gita::4.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::4.essence: Your true self is the undivided whole beyond existence and non-existence.
avadhuta_gita::4.simple_meaning: The true self is everything and cannot be split into parts or opposites. It cannot be described as simply existing or not existing.
avadhuta_gita::4.simple_insight: There is wonder in realizing your true nature is beyond all labels and categories.
avadhuta_gita::4.detailed_meaning: The sage speaks from the experience of unity where the self is the totality without any division. This amazes him because usual concepts like existence and non-existence do not apply to this reality.
avadhuta_gita::4.modern_relevance: When you try to define yourself strictly by what you are or are not, you feel stuck—this verse points to a freedom beyond such limits.
avadhuta_gita::4.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as a limited thing to recognizing you are the indivisible whole beyond all distinctions.

avadhuta_gita::5.verse_sanskrit:
वेदान्तसारसर्वस्वं ज्ञानं विज्ञानमेव च ।
अहमात्मा निराकारः सर्वव्यापी स्वभावतः ॥
avadhuta_gita::5.verse_hindi: वेदान्त का सार ही हमारा सर्वस्व है और वही ज्ञान एवं विज्ञान है। मैं आत्मा हूँ, निराकार हूँ तथा स्वभाव से ही सर्वव्यापी हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::5.english_translation: The essence of Vedanta is our all; it is knowledge and wisdom. I am the true self, formless, and naturally all-pervading.
avadhuta_gita::5.translation_literal: वेदान्त (Vedanta) / सार (essence) / सर्वस्वं (all) / ज्ञानं (knowledge) / विज्ञानमेव (and wisdom indeed) / च (also) / अहम् (I) / आत्मा (true self) / निराकारः (formless) / सर्वव्यापी (all-pervading) / स्वभावतः (by nature)
avadhuta_gita::5.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::5.essence: You are the formless true self, knowledge, and presence naturally all around.
avadhuta_gita::5.simple_meaning: You are the essence of the highest teaching, pure knowledge and wisdom, without form and present everywhere naturally.
avadhuta_gita::5.simple_insight: You already are the vast, formless presence beyond shapes and limits.
avadhuta_gita::5.detailed_meaning: The Avadhuta declares that the core of Vedanta teaching is the true self itself, which is formless and pervades everything by its own nature. This identifies the speaker as completely free and united with all existence.
avadhuta_gita::5.modern_relevance: In moments when you feel limited by your body or thoughts, recall that your true self is vast, formless, and everywhere beyond those limits.
avadhuta_gita::5.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with form-bound identity to recognizing your boundless, formless presence.

avadhuta_gita::6.verse_sanskrit:
यो वै सर्वात्मको देवो निष्कलो गगनोपमः ।
स्वभावनिर्मलः शुद्धः स एवायं न संशयः ॥
avadhuta_gita::6.verse_hindi: जो सर्वस्वरूप देव ( ब्रह्म) है वह अवयव रहित,आकाश के सदृश, स्वभाव से निर्मल एवं शुद्ध है। वही मैं हूँ, इसमें संशय नहीं है।
avadhuta_gita::6.english_translation: The divine that is the essence of all is without parts, like the sky, pure by nature, and spotless; that is exactly who I am, without doubt.
avadhuta_gita::6.translation_literal: यो (who) / वै (indeed) / सर्वात्मको (all-self, essence of all) / देवो (divine) / निष्कलो (without parts) / गगनोपमः (like the sky) / स्वभावनिर्मलः (by nature pure) / शुद्धः (spotless) / स (that) / एव (indeed) / अयं (this) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
avadhuta_gita::6.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::6.essence: Your true self is pure, whole, and limitless like the sky, beyond all division.
avadhuta_gita::6.simple_meaning: You are the pure and indivisible essence of everything, like the vast sky, without any flaw or division.
avadhuta_gita::6.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your true nature is whole and untouched by any imperfection.
avadhuta_gita::6.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the supreme reality, which is the essence behind all existence, is completely pure, indivisible, and vast like the sky. He asserts this is his own nature with absolute certainty.
avadhuta_gita::6.modern_relevance: When you feel fragmented or flawed, remember your true self is whole and pure, like the endless sky above.
avadhuta_gita::6.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as broken or limited to recognizing your complete and flawless nature.

avadhuta_gita::7.verse_sanskrit:
अहमेवाव्ययोऽनन्तः शुद्धविज्ञानविग्रहः ।
सुखं दुःखं न जानामि कथं कस्यापि वर्तते ॥
avadhuta_gita::7.verse_hindi: मैं निश्चय ही नाश रहित, अनन्त एवं शुद्ध विज्ञान स्वरूप हूँ। मैं सुख-दु:ख को नहीं जानता हूँ कि ये किसको व किस प्रकार होते हैं।
avadhuta_gita::7.english_translation: I am certainly imperishable, infinite, and pure consciousness itself. I do not know pleasure or pain, nor how they affect anyone.
avadhuta_gita::7.translation_literal: अहम् (I) एव (indeed) अव्ययः (imperishable) अनन्तः (infinite) शुद्ध (pure) विज्ञान (consciousness) विग्रहः (form) । सुखं (pleasure) दुःखं (pain) न (not) जानामि (know) कथं (how) कस्य (to whom) अपि (at all) वर्तते (exists) ॥
avadhuta_gita::7.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::7.essence: You are infinite pure awareness beyond all pleasure and pain.
avadhuta_gita::7.simple_meaning: You are the eternal and infinite pure consciousness that does not experience pleasure or pain.
avadhuta_gita::7.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing your true self is untouched by suffering or joy.
avadhuta_gita::7.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares himself as the imperishable, infinite pure consciousness. He emphasizes that pleasure and pain are unknown to this true self, which stands beyond all dual experiences.
avadhuta_gita::7.modern_relevance: When stress or joy overwhelms you, remember your core self remains untouched and infinite beyond these feelings.
avadhuta_gita::7.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with fleeting feelings to recognizing your unchanging true nature.

avadhuta_gita::8.verse_sanskrit:
न मानसं कर्म शुभाशुभं मे न कायिकं कर्म शुभाशुभं मे ।
न वाचिकं कर्म शुभाशुभं मे ज्ञानामृतं शुद्धमतीन्द्रियोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::8.verse_hindi: मन के द्वारा किये गये शुभ व अशुभ कर्म मेरे नहीं हैं, न शरीर द्वारा किये गये शुभ अशुभ कर्म मेरे हैं, वाणी द्वारा किये गये शुभ अशुभ कर्म भी मेरे नहीं हैं। मैं शुद्ध, ज्ञानामृत एवं इन्द्रियों का अविषय हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::8.english_translation: Neither the good nor the bad actions of the mind, body, or speech belong to me; I am pure, the nectar of knowledge, and beyond the senses.
avadhuta_gita::8.translation_literal: न (not) मानसं (mental) कर्म (action) शुभाशुभं (good and bad) मे (my) न (not) कायिकं (bodily) कर्म (action) शुभाशुभं (good and bad) मे (my) । न (not) वाचिकं (verbal) कर्म (action) शुभाशुभं (good and bad) मे (my) ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) शुद्धमतीन्द्रियोऽहम् (pure, beyond senses, I am) ॥
avadhuta_gita::8.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::8.essence: Your true self is pure and untouched by mind, body, or speech actions.
avadhuta_gita::8.simple_meaning: You are not the good or bad actions done by your mind, body, or speech. Your true self is pure, full of knowledge, and beyond the senses.
avadhuta_gita::8.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing your true self is untouched by any action or its results.
avadhuta_gita::8.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that none of the actions performed by mind, body, or speech truly belong to the self. Instead, the self is pure, beyond sensory experience, and embodies the nectar of knowledge. This teaching unfolds the deep non-dual nature of the true self.
avadhuta_gita::8.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your thoughts, words, or deeds, remember your true self remains untouched and pure beneath it all.
avadhuta_gita::8.insight: It shifts your identity from the doer of actions to the pure awareness beyond all activity and sensory involvement.

avadhuta_gita::9.verse_sanskrit:
मनो वै गगनाकारं मनो वै सर्वतोमुखम् ।
मनोऽतीतं मनः सर्वं न मनः परमार्थतः ॥
avadhuta_gita::9.verse_hindi: निश्चय ही यह मन गगन के आकार वाला है तथा इसके सभी ओर मुख हैं, मन से पार कुछ भी नहीं है, मन ही सब कुछ है किन्तु यह मन भी परमार्थ से सत्य नहीं है।
avadhuta_gita::9.english_translation: The mind is like the sky in shape and faces all directions; beyond mind there is nothing, mind is everything, yet even mind is not the ultimate truth.
avadhuta_gita::9.translation_literal: मनो (mind) / वै (indeed) / गगनाकारं (sky-shaped) / मनो (mind) / वै (indeed) / सर्वतोमुखम् (facing all directions) / मनोऽतीतं (beyond mind) / मनः (mind) / सर्वं (all) / न (not) / मनः (mind) / परमार्थतः (ultimately, in the highest truth)
avadhuta_gita::9.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::9.essence: The mind includes everything but is not the ultimate truth beyond it.
avadhuta_gita::9.simple_meaning: The mind appears limitless and contains everything, but even it is not the highest reality or true self.
avadhuta_gita::9.simple_insight: You can feel the vastness of your mind but also sense it’s not the whole of who you are.
avadhuta_gita::9.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the mind as vast like the sky and facing all directions, implying its reach is everywhere. Yet he points out that beyond this mind, which seems all-encompassing, lies a higher truth it cannot capture.
avadhuta_gita::9.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by countless thoughts and emotions swirling around, you sense your mind is vast but still feel something deeper beyond it.
avadhuta_gita::9.insight: It shifts your view from identifying fully with your thoughts to recognizing the true self beyond the mind’s reach.

avadhuta_gita::10.verse_sanskrit:
अहमेकमिदं सर्वं व्योमातीतं निरन्तरम् ।
पश्यामि कथमात्मानं प्रत्यक्षं वा तिरोहितम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::10.verse_hindi: मैं आत्मा को प्रत्यक्ष अथवा तिरोहित किस प्रकार देखूँ क्योंकि मैं आत्मा स्वरूप होने के कारण एक तथा सर्वरूप हूँ तथा आकाश से भी परे निरन्तर हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::10.english_translation: I am the one and all, beyond space and endless; how can I see the true self as visible or hidden?
avadhuta_gita::10.translation_literal: अहम् (I) एकम् (one) इदम् (this) सर्वं (all) व्योमातीतं (beyond space) निरन्तरम् (endless) । पश्यामि (I see) कथम् (how) आत्मानं (the true self) प्रत्यक्षं (visible) वा (or) तिरोहितम् (hidden) ॥
avadhuta_gita::10.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::10.essence: The true self transcends all forms of visibility and invisibility as the one endless reality.
avadhuta_gita::10.simple_meaning: You are the single reality beyond everything, endless like space. The true self cannot be simply seen or hidden because it is your own nature.
avadhuta_gita::10.simple_insight: You feel the vastness and mystery of your true self beyond ordinary seeing.
avadhuta_gita::10.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he is the one reality that is both the entire universe and beyond it, like limitless space. He reflects on how the true self cannot be seen or hidden because it is his own nature, beyond ordinary perception.
avadhuta_gita::10.modern_relevance: You stare into the mirror of your mind, realizing your true nature cannot be captured by simple seeing or hiding.
avadhuta_gita::10.insight: It shifts your view from trying to observe the self as an object to recognizing it as the boundless presence you already are.

avadhuta_gita::11.verse_sanskrit:
त्वमेवमेकं हि कथं न बुध्यसे 
समं हि सर्वेषु विमृष्टमव्ययम् ।
सदोदितोऽसि त्वमखण्डितः प्रभो
दिवा च नक्तं च कथं हि मन्यसे ॥
avadhuta_gita::11.verse_hindi: ‘हे प्रभो ! तू क्यों नहीं जानता कि तू एक ही है, सभी में समान है, नाश रहित है’ ऐसा विचार किया गया है। तू सदा ही प्रकाशमान है तथा अखण्ड है (भेद रहित है) फिर तू दिन और रात्रि को किस प्रकार मानता है।
avadhuta_gita::11.english_translation: You are indeed the one alone, unchanging and the same in all; always radiant and undivided, so how can you perceive day and night as real?
avadhuta_gita::11.translation_literal: त्वमेवमेकं (You alone one) / हि (indeed) / कथं (how) / न (not) / बुध्यसे (do you understand) / समं (equal/same) / हि (indeed) / सर्वेषु (in all) / विमृष्टम् (unmixed) / अव्ययम् (imperishable) / सदोदितः (always shining) / असि (are) / त्वमखण्डितः (you undivided) / प्रभो (O lord) / दिवा (day) / च (and) / नक्तं (night) / च (and) / कथं (how) / हि (indeed) / मन्यसे (do you consider)
avadhuta_gita::11.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::11.essence: Your true self is one, unchanging, and beyond all dualities like day and night.
avadhuta_gita::11.simple_meaning: You are the same unchanging presence in everyone, always shining and whole. Day and night are just appearances you mistakenly believe in.
avadhuta_gita::11.simple_insight: You can feel the relief of knowing your true nature never changes despite all appearances.
avadhuta_gita::11.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that the true self is one and unchanging, shining equally in all beings. The belief in distinctions like day and night arises from illusion, not reality.
avadhuta_gita::11.modern_relevance: When your mood shifts and you feel scattered, remember your true self remains steady beneath all change.
avadhuta_gita::11.insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with fleeting appearances to recognizing your constant, undivided nature.

avadhuta_gita::12.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मानं सततं विद्धि सर्वत्रैकं निरन्तरम् ।
अहं ध्याता परं ध्येयमखण्डं खण्ड्यते कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::12.verse_hindi: आत्मा को तुम सदा सर्वत्र, एक एवं अविचल जानो। फिर ‘मैं ध्याता ( ध्यान करने वाला) हूँ तथा आत्मा ध्येय’ (जिसका ध्यान किया जाता है) का भेद किस प्रकार करते हो। जो अखण्ड है उसका खण्डन कैसे करते हो।
avadhuta_gita::12.english_translation: Always know the true self as one, unchanging everywhere. How do you separate the meditator 'I' from the meditation object, the self, which is indivisible?
avadhuta_gita::12.translation_literal: आत्मानं (self) सततं (always) विद्धि (know) सर्वत्रैकं (everywhere one) निरन्तरम् (unchanging) । अहं (I) ध्याता (the meditator) परं (other) ध्येयम् (meditation object) अखण्डं (undivided) खण्ड्यते (is separated) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::12.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::12.essence: The true self is indivisible; the watcher and the watched are one.
avadhuta_gita::12.simple_meaning: You are always the one true self everywhere, unchanging. The sense of separating the observer from the observed self is mistaken.
avadhuta_gita::12.simple_insight: There's freedom in seeing that your true self is never divided or separate from your awareness.
avadhuta_gita::12.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out the fundamental non-duality of self: the meditator ('I') and the meditation object (the self) are not two. This teaching challenges the common experience of feeling separate from our own awareness.
avadhuta_gita::12.modern_relevance: When you try to watch your thoughts or feelings as if they are separate, notice how that separation itself cannot hold; you are always the same unchanging self.
avadhuta_gita::12.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as split between watcher and what is watched, to recognizing a seamless unity.

avadhuta_gita::13.verse_sanskrit:
न जातो न मृतोऽसि त्वं न ते देहः कदाचन ।
सर्वं ब्रह्मेति विख्यातं ब्रवीति बहुधा श्रुतिः ॥
avadhuta_gita::13.verse_hindi: न तो तेरा कभी जन्म हुआ है न कभी मरता ही है, न कभी तेरा शरीर ही है। यह सब ब्रह्म ही है ऐसा प्रसिद्ध है तथा अनेक श्रुतियाँ ऐसा ही कहती हैं।
avadhuta_gita::13.english_translation: You were never born, nor do you ever die; your body is never truly yours. Everything is known as Brahman, as many scriptures repeatedly declare.
avadhuta_gita::13.translation_literal: न (not) जातः (born) न (nor) मृतः (dead) असि (are) त्वं (you) न (not) ते (your) देहः (body) कदाचन (ever) । सर्वं (all) ब्रह्मेति (as Brahman) विख्यातं (known) ब्रवीति (says) बहुधा (many times) श्रुतिः (scripture) ॥
avadhuta_gita::13.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::13.essence: You are never born or dead; your true nature is beyond the body.
avadhuta_gita::13.simple_meaning: You have never been born and will never die. Your body is not your true self. Everything is ultimately the supreme reality called Brahman.
avadhuta_gita::13.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing you are beyond birth, death, and the physical body.
avadhuta_gita::13.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the true self is beyond birth and death and is not limited to the physical body. This teaching arises in a text emphasizing the unchanging supreme reality, Brahman, confirmed by many scriptures.
avadhuta_gita::13.modern_relevance: When you face fear of change or loss, remembering you are beyond your body and life’s cycles can bring deep peace.
avadhuta_gita::13.insight: It shifts your identity from the physical and mortal to the timeless and unchanging reality.

avadhuta_gita::14.verse_sanskrit:
स बाह्याभ्यन्तरोऽसि त्वं शिवः सर्वत्र सर्वदा ।
इतस्ततः कथं भ्रान्तः प्रधावसि पिशाचवत् ॥
avadhuta_gita::14.verse_hindi: जो आत्मा (ब्रह्म) बाहर और भीतर सर्वत्र एवं सदा से ही विद्यमान है तथा कल्याण रूप है, वह तू ही है। फिर तू भ्रान्त होकर इधर-उधर पिशाच की तरह क्यों दौड़ता फिरता है।
avadhuta_gita::14.english_translation: You are the true self, the auspicious one, present everywhere always; why then do you wander confused like a ghost?
avadhuta_gita::14.translation_literal: स (You) बाह्याभ्यन्तरोऽसि (are outside and inside) त्वं (you) शिवः (auspicious) सर्वत्र (everywhere) सर्वदा (always) । इतस्ततः (here and there) कथं (how) भ्रान्तः (confused) प्रधावसि (do you run) पिशाचवत् (like a ghost) ॥
avadhuta_gita::14.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::14.essence: You are always fully present and auspicious; confusion is your own making.
avadhuta_gita::14.simple_meaning: You are the ever-present true self, complete and auspicious everywhere, so why are you confused and restless like a lost spirit?
avadhuta_gita::14.simple_insight: There is peace in recognizing your true nature instead of chasing illusions in confusion.
avadhuta_gita::14.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reminds that the true self is always present, auspicious, and complete both inside and outside. Yet the mind often wanders confused, like a ghost, forgetting this reality and causing unnecessary restlessness.
avadhuta_gita::14.modern_relevance: You feel scattered, chasing distractions and doubts, forgetting that your essential self is always calm and complete.
avadhuta_gita::14.insight: It teaches shifting from restless confusion to recognizing your constant, unchanging presence everywhere.

avadhuta_gita::15.verse_sanskrit:
संयोगश्च वियोगश्च वर्तते न च ते न मे ।
न त्वं नाहं जगन्नेदं सर्वमात्मैव केवलम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::15.verse_hindi: तुझमें और मुझमें कोई संयोग और विभाग नहीं है। न तू है, न मैं हूँ और न यह जगत ही है बल्कि यह सब केवल आत्मा ही है।
avadhuta_gita::15.english_translation: There is no union or separation between you and me. Neither you, nor I, nor this world exists; all is only the true self.
avadhuta_gita::15.translation_literal: संयोगश्च (union and) / वियोगश्च (separation and) / वर्तते (exists) / न (not) / च (and) / ते (you) / न (not) / मे (me) / । (.) / न (not) / त्वं (you) / नाहं (nor I) / जगन् (world) / नेदं (this) / सर्वम् (all) / आत्मैव (only the true self) / केवलम् (alone) / ॥ (.)
avadhuta_gita::15.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::15.essence: You, me, and the world are not separate; all is only the true self.
avadhuta_gita::15.simple_meaning: There is no real difference or separation between you, me, or the world. Everything is only the true self.
avadhuta_gita::15.simple_insight: You can feel peaceful knowing separation is an illusion and unity is the truth.
avadhuta_gita::15.detailed_meaning: The Avadhuta reveals that the apparent differences—between you, me, and the world—are illusions. All distinctions dissolve because everything is fundamentally the true self, inviting a radical shift in perspective beyond duality.
avadhuta_gita::15.modern_relevance: You notice how often you feel divided from others or your environment, but this teaches that all separation is imagined.
avadhuta_gita::15.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as separate to recognizing unbroken oneness with all existence.

avadhuta_gita::16.verse_sanskrit:
शब्दादिपञ्चकस्यास्य नैवासि त्वं न ते पुनः ।
त्वमेव परमं तत्त्वमतः किं परितप्यसे ॥
avadhuta_gita::16.verse_hindi: फिर ये शब्दादि पंचक (शब्द, स्पर्श, रूप, रस, गंध) न तो तुम हो न ये तुम्हारे हैं। तुम एक ही परम तत्व ( ब्रह्म) हो इसलिए क्यों संतप्त होते हो।
avadhuta_gita::16.english_translation: You are neither the five elements of sound and so on, nor are they yours; you alone are the supreme reality, so why do you suffer?
avadhuta_gita::16.translation_literal: शब्दादि-पञ्चकस्य (of the group of five elements: sound etc.) अस्य (of this) नै (not) आसि (you are) त्वं (you) न (nor) ते (they) पुनः (again). त्वमेव (you alone) परमं (supreme) तत्त्वम् (reality) अतः (therefore) किं (why) परितप्यसे (do you suffer).
avadhuta_gita::16.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::16.essence: You are the supreme reality, not the senses or their experiences; suffering is needless.
avadhuta_gita::16.simple_meaning: You are not the five senses or their experiences. You alone are the supreme reality, so there is no reason to suffer.
avadhuta_gita::16.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing you are beyond all sensory experiences and their troubles.
avadhuta_gita::16.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the self is not the five sensory elements—sound, touch, form, taste, smell—nor are they possessions of yours. Instead, you are the supreme reality itself, so suffering due to identification with these transient things is needless.
avadhuta_gita::16.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by what you see, hear, or touch, remember you are more than these passing sensations.
avadhuta_gita::16.insight: This verse shifts your view from identifying with fleeting sensations to recognizing your true, unchanging nature.

avadhuta_gita::17.verse_sanskrit:
जन्म मृत्युर्न ते चित्तं बन्धमोक्षौ शुभाशुभौ ।
कथं रोदिषि रे वत्स नामरूपं न ते न मे ॥
avadhuta_gita::17.verse_hindi: जन्म और मृत्यु, बन्धन और मोक्ष तथा शुभ-अशुभ सब मन के धर्म हैं, तेरे नहीं हैं, ये नाम और रूप भी न तेरे हैं न मेरे। फिर हे वत्स! तू क्यों रूदन करता है।
avadhuta_gita::17.english_translation: Birth and death, bondage and freedom, good and bad are all functions of the mind; they belong neither to you nor to me. So why do you cry, dear one?
avadhuta_gita::17.translation_literal: जन्म (birth) / मृत्युर्न (and death) / ते (to you) / चित्तं (mind) / बन्धमोक्षौ (bondage and freedom) / शुभाशुभौ (good and bad) / कथं (how) / रोदिषि (do you cry) / रे (O) / वत्स (dear one) / नामरूपं (name and form) / न (not) / ते (yours) / न (nor) / मे (mine)
avadhuta_gita::17.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::17.essence: Your true self is untouched by birth, death, and mental distinctions; sorrow is needless.
avadhuta_gita::17.simple_meaning: Birth, death, bondage, freedom, good, and bad exist only in the mind, not in your true self or mine. So there is no reason to cry.
avadhuta_gita::17.simple_insight: You can feel peace knowing these fears and joys are not truly yours.
avadhuta_gita::17.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that birth, death, bondage, liberation, and moral qualities belong to the restless mind, not the true self. Addressing the listener as 'dear one,' he points to the futility of sorrow over things that are not real or permanent.
avadhuta_gita::17.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by worries and hopes that seem personal but are just mental patterns you don’t truly own.
avadhuta_gita::17.insight: This verse shifts your perspective from identifying with changing experiences to recognizing your unchanging true self beyond them.

avadhuta_gita::18.verse_sanskrit:
अहो चित्त कथं भ्रान्तः प्रधावसि पिशाचवत् ।
अभिन्नं पश्य चात्मानं रागत्यागात्सुखी भव ॥
avadhuta_gita::18.verse_hindi: खेद है कि यह चित्त किस प्रकार भ्रान्त होकर पिशाच की भाँति दौड़ता-फिरता है। तू अपनी आत्मा को अभिन्न देख तथा राग का त्याग करके सुखी हो।
avadhuta_gita::18.english_translation: Alas, how the restless mind wanders like a ghost. See your true self as one and be happy by abandoning craving.
avadhuta_gita::18.translation_literal: अहो (alas) / चित्त (mind) / कथं (how) / भ्रान्तः (confused) / प्रधावसि (do you run) / पिशाचवत् (like a ghost) । / अभिन्नं (undivided) / पश्य (see) / चात्मानं (your own self) / रागत्यागात् (from abandoning craving) / सुखी (happy) / भव (be) ॥
avadhuta_gita::18.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::18.essence: Your mind wanders in confusion, but your true self is always whole and free from craving.
avadhuta_gita::18.simple_meaning: Your restless mind confuses you like a ghost chasing illusions. Recognize your true self as whole and let go of craving to find happiness.
avadhuta_gita::18.simple_insight: Letting go of craving brings relief from a restless, confused mind.
avadhuta_gita::18.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Dattatreya laments how the restless mind runs wildly like a ghost, lost in confusion. He advises seeing the self as undivided and whole, and by abandoning craving, you can find lasting happiness.
avadhuta_gita::18.modern_relevance: Your mind jumps anxiously from thought to thought, restless and never settled. Seeing yourself beyond this helps you relax and feel content.
avadhuta_gita::18.insight: This verse shifts attention from chasing desires to recognizing your undivided self, calming mental restlessness.

avadhuta_gita::19.verse_sanskrit:
त्वमेव तत्त्वं हि विकारवर्जितं
निष्कम्पमेकं हि विमोक्षविग्रहम् ।
न ते च रागो ह्यथवा विरागः
कथं हि सन्तप्यसि कामकामतः ॥
avadhuta_gita::19.verse_hindi: तू निश्चय ही आत्म तत्व है जो विकार रहित है, निष्काम है, एक ही है तथा मोक्ष स्वरूप है। ये राग और विराग भी तेरे नहीं हैं फिर कामों की कामना से क्यों संतप्त है।
avadhuta_gita::19.english_translation: You are the true essence, free from change, desireless, one, and the form of freedom. Attachment and detachment are not yours; so why do you suffer from desires?
avadhuta_gita::19.translation_literal: त्वमेव (you alone) तत्त्वं (essence) हि (indeed) विकारवर्जितं (free from change) निष्कम्पमेकं (desireless and one) हि (indeed) विमोक्षविग्रहम् (form of freedom)। न (not) ते (yours) च (and) रागो (attachment) ह्यथवा (or) विरागः (detachment) कथं (how) हि (indeed) सन्तप्यसि (do you suffer) कामकामतः (from desires)
avadhuta_gita::19.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::19.essence: Your true self is beyond desire and free from suffering caused by craving.
avadhuta_gita::19.simple_meaning: You are the unchanging true essence, free from desires and attachments. Those feelings are not truly yours, so there is no reason to suffer from wanting.
avadhuta_gita::19.simple_insight: It feels freeing to realize that your deepest self is untouched by desires that trouble you.
avadhuta_gita::19.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that your true self is the changeless essence, free from all attachments and aversions, embodying freedom itself. Since attachment and detachment do not belong to this true self, suffering from desire is a misunderstanding of your real nature.
avadhuta_gita::19.modern_relevance: You feel restless chasing what you want, yet deep inside, you’re untouched by those cravings. Recognizing this can ease your inner struggle.
avadhuta_gita::19.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with desire to recognizing your essence beyond craving and suffering.

avadhuta_gita::20.verse_sanskrit:
वदन्ति श्रुतयः सर्वाः निर्गुणं शुद्धमव्ययम् ।
अशरीरं समं तत्त्वं तन्मां विद्धि न संशयः ॥
avadhuta_gita::20.verse_hindi: सम्पूर्ण श्रुतियाँ आत्म तत्व को निर्गुण, शुद्ध, नाश रहित, शरीर से रहित, समरूप ही कहती हैं वही तुम मुझे जानो इसमें संशय नहीं है।
avadhuta_gita::20.english_translation: All scriptures declare the true self as formless, pure, imperishable, bodiless, and equal; know that as me without doubt.
avadhuta_gita::20.translation_literal: वदन्ति (declare) श्रुतयः (scriptures) सर्वाः (all) निर्गुणं (without qualities) शुद्धम् (pure) अव्ययम् (imperishable) । अशरीरं (bodiless) समं (equal) तत्त्वं (truth) तन्मां (me that) विद्धि (know) न (not) संशयः (doubt) ॥
avadhuta_gita::20.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::20.essence: Your true self is pure, formless, eternal, and beyond any doubt.
avadhuta_gita::20.simple_meaning: The true self is described by all scriptures as pure, without form, never perishing, and beyond the body. You should recognize this without any doubt.
avadhuta_gita::20.simple_insight: There is certainty and peace in knowing your true nature is beyond all change and form.
avadhuta_gita::20.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya states that all sacred teachings agree the true self is without qualities, pure, eternal, and beyond the physical body. There is no need to doubt this identity that transcends appearances.
avadhuta_gita::20.modern_relevance: When your body ages or your feelings shift, remember your true nature remains pure, unchanged, and beyond all forms.
avadhuta_gita::20.insight: It teaches you to identify beyond your body and mind as the unchanging, pure essence.

avadhuta_gita::21.verse_sanskrit:
साकारमनृतं विद्धि निराकारं निरन्तरम् ।
एतत्तत्त्वोपदेशेन न पुनर्भवसम्भवः ॥
avadhuta_gita::21.verse_hindi: साकार को मिथ्या जाने, निराकार को निरन्तर (नित्य) जाने। इस तत्व के उपदेश से संसार में पुन: उत्पत्ति नहीं होती।
avadhuta_gita::21.english_translation: Know the form-based as false, the formless as eternal; this teaching ends rebirth.
avadhuta_gita::21.translation_literal: साकार (with form) / अनृतं (false) / विद्धि (know) / निराकारं (formless) / निरन्तरम् (eternal) / एतत् (this) / तत्त्वोपदेशेन (by this teaching of truth) / न (not) / पुनः (again) / भवसम्भवः (rebirth/origination)
avadhuta_gita::21.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::21.essence: Form is false; the formless eternal truth frees from rebirth.
avadhuta_gita::21.simple_meaning: The appearance of form is an illusion, but the formless reality is eternal. Understanding this ends the cycle of rebirth.
avadhuta_gita::21.simple_insight: There's freedom in seeing that what appears is false, and what truly is never changes.
avadhuta_gita::21.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that the visible, shaped world is an illusion, while the invisible, formless essence is eternal. This knowledge dissolves the cycle of rebirth and suffering.
avadhuta_gita::21.modern_relevance: When distractions and appearances overwhelm you, remembering that the unchanging truth lies beyond form can bring lasting peace.
avadhuta_gita::21.insight: It shifts your mind from attachment to appearances toward abiding in unchanging reality.

avadhuta_gita::22.verse_sanskrit:
एकमेव समं तत्त्वं वदन्ति हि विपश्चितः ।
रागत्यागात्पुनश्चित्तमेकानेकं न विद्यते ॥
avadhuta_gita::22.verse_hindi: विद्वान् जन कहते हैं कि एक ही तत्व समान रूप से व्याप्त है। राग के त्याग देने से यह चित्त फिर एक और अनेक को नहीं जानता।
avadhuta_gita::22.english_translation: The wise say that the one truth pervades all equally; when attachment is renounced, the mind no longer perceives multiplicity.
avadhuta_gita::22.translation_literal: एकमेव (one only) समं (equal) तत्त्वं (truth) वदन्ति (say) हि (indeed) विपश्चितः (the wise) । रागत्यागात् (from renunciation of attachment) पुनः (again) चित्तम् (mind) एकानेकं (one and many) न (not) विद्यते (is known) ॥
avadhuta_gita::22.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::22.essence: Letting go of attachment reveals the mind’s true vision of oneness.
avadhuta_gita::22.simple_meaning: The one true reality is the same everywhere. When you give up attachment, your mind stops seeing many separate things.
avadhuta_gita::22.simple_insight: There is peace in seeing everything as one, freed from craving many things.
avadhuta_gita::22.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that all is pervaded by one truth. The wise recognize this unity. When attachment disappears, the mind no longer perceives the world as fragmented but as a seamless whole.
avadhuta_gita::22.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by choices and desires pulling you in every direction, but letting go of craving brings calm and clarity.
avadhuta_gita::22.insight: It teaches you to release attachment so your mind naturally perceives unity instead of division.

avadhuta_gita::23.verse_sanskrit:
अनात्मरूपं च कथं समाधि-
रात्मस्वरूपं च कथं समाधिः ।
