अस्तीति नास्तीति कथं समाधि-
र्मोक्षस्वरूपं यदि सर्वमेकम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::23.verse_hindi: अनात्म रूप को समाधि कैसे हो सकती है, तथा आत्म स्वरूप को समाधि कैसे हो सकती है। इसी प्रकार ‘है’ और ‘नहीं है’ को भी समाधि कैसे हो सकती है और जो मोक्ष स्वरूप एक ही ब्रह्म है तो भी समाधि कैसे हो सकती है।
avadhuta_gita::23.english_translation: How can there be samadhi of what is not the true self, or samadhi of the true self's form? How can 'exists' and 'does not exist' be samadhi? If the supreme freedom is all one, how can samadhi be?
avadhuta_gita::23.translation_literal: अनात्मरूपं (not-self form) / च (and) / कथं (how) / समाधि- (samadhi) / आत्मस्वरूपं (self-form) / च (and) / कथं (how) / समाधिः (samadhi) । अस्तीति (exists) / नास्तीति (does not exist) / कथं (how) / समाधि- (samadhi) / मोक्षस्वरूपं (freedom-form) / यदि (if) / सर्वमेकम् (all one) ॥
avadhuta_gita::23.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::23.essence: True freedom transcends all forms, existence, and non-existence; samadhi is beyond definition.
avadhuta_gita::23.simple_meaning: Samadhi cannot be about something that is not the true self or even the true self's form. It cannot depend on existence or non-existence. Since freedom is all one, samadhi transcends such distinctions.
avadhuta_gita::23.simple_insight: You feel that true inner freedom is beyond all dual ideas and forms.
avadhuta_gita::23.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya questions how samadhi, a state of complete absorption, can be about something that is not the true self or even about the true self’s form. He challenges the notion that existence or non-existence can define samadhi, pointing to the absolute oneness of supreme freedom beyond all dualities.
avadhuta_gita::23.modern_relevance: When you search for peace, you may try to grasp or define it, but true freedom is beyond all labels and opposites you hold in your mind.
avadhuta_gita::23.insight: It shifts your understanding from trying to fix samadhi as an object to seeing it as the absence of all dual distinctions.

avadhuta_gita::24.verse_sanskrit:
विशुद्धोऽसि समं तत्त्वं विदेहस्त्वमजोऽव्ययः ।
जानामीह न जानामीत्यात्मानं मन्यसे कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::24.verse_hindi: तू (आत्मा स्वरूप होने से) विशुद्ध, समरस, देह रहित, जन्म से रहित तथा नाश से रहित है। फिर तू यह कैसे मानता है कि मैं आत्मा को जानता हूँ मैं आत्मा को नहीं जानता।
avadhuta_gita::24.english_translation: You are pure, equal to all, bodiless, unborn, and imperishable. How then do you think 'I know the self' or 'I do not know the self'?
avadhuta_gita::24.translation_literal: विशुद्धोऽसि (You are pure) / समं (equal) / तत्त्वं (principle/reality) / विदेहः (bodiless) / त्वम् (you) / अजोऽव्ययः (unborn and imperishable) / जानामि (I know) / ही (indeed) / न (not) / जानामि (I know) / इति (thus) / आत्मानं (the self) / मन्यसे (you think) / कथम् (how)
avadhuta_gita::24.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::24.essence: You are pure and unchanging; knowing or not knowing your true self is just a mental illusion.
avadhuta_gita::24.simple_meaning: You are fundamentally pure, equal everywhere, without a body, unborn, and never destroyed. So how can you truly say you know or don't know your true self?
avadhuta_gita::24.simple_insight: There is freedom in realizing that knowing or not knowing your true self is just a mental idea.
avadhuta_gita::24.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that the true self is pure, equal in all things, without body, unborn, and imperishable. Since the self is beyond all change, the concepts of knowing or not knowing it are illusions created by the mind.
avadhuta_gita::24.modern_relevance: When you doubt your own nature or feel confused about who you truly are, remember that your essence is beyond all such thoughts.
avadhuta_gita::24.insight: It shifts you from identifying with mental labels of knowing or ignorance to recognizing your unchanging nature beyond thought.

avadhuta_gita::25.verse_sanskrit:
तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्येन स्वात्मा हि प्रतिपादितः ।
नेति नेति श्रुतिर्ब्रूयादनृतं पाञ्चभौतिकम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::25.verse_hindi: और ‘तत्वमसि’ (यह तू ही है) आदि वाक्यों से अपने आत्मा का ही प्रतिपादन किया गया है और श्रुति ‘नेति नेति’ कहती है। यह पंचभौतिक मिथ्या है।
avadhuta_gita::25.english_translation: The true self is revealed by sayings like 'You are that'; the scriptures negate the false five-element world.
avadhuta_gita::25.translation_literal: तत्त्वमसि (that you are) आदि (and others) वाक्येन (by the words) स्वात्मा (own self) हि (indeed) प्रतिपादितः (established) । नेति नेति (not this, not this) श्रुतिर्ब्रूयात् (scripture says) अनृतं (false) पाञ्चभौतिकम् (five-elemental) ॥
avadhuta_gita::25.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::25.essence: The true self is revealed by negating the false five-element world through scripture.
avadhuta_gita::25.simple_meaning: The true self is described by phrases like 'You are that'. The scriptures teach to reject the false physical world made of five elements.
avadhuta_gita::25.simple_insight: You can let go of identifying with the changing physical world and rest in your true self.
avadhuta_gita::25.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points to the teaching that the true self is revealed in statements like 'You are that'. The scriptures also instruct rejection of the false five-element world, emphasizing that what appears physical is not the ultimate reality.
avadhuta_gita::25.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by your changing body and environment, remember these are not your true self but passing forms to see through.
avadhuta_gita::25.insight: It shifts your attention from identifying with your physical body to recognizing your unchanging true self.

avadhuta_gita::26.verse_sanskrit:
आत्मन्येवात्मना सर्वं त्वया पूर्णं निरन्तरम् ।
ध्याता ध्यानं न ते चित्तं निर्लज्जं ध्यायते कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::26.verse_hindi: तेरी आत्मा ही सभी आत्म रूप से पूर्ण एवं निरन्तर है। इसलिए ध्याता और ध्यान तुम्हारे नहीं हैं फिर यह निर्लज्ज मन कैसे ध्यान करता है।
avadhuta_gita::26.english_translation: Your inner being itself is complete and continuous; the meditator and meditation are not truly yours, so how can a shameless mind meditate?
avadhuta_gita::26.translation_literal: आत्मन्येवात्मना (by the self itself) / सर्वं (all) / त्वया (by you) / पूर्णं (complete) / निरन्तरम् (continuous) । / ध्याता (the meditator) / ध्यानं (meditation) / न (not) / ते (your) / चित्तं (mind) / निर्लज्जं (shameless) / ध्यायते (meditates) / कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::26.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::26.essence: Your true self is always complete; restless mind cannot genuinely meditate.
avadhuta_gita::26.simple_meaning: Your inner being is already complete and continuous. Since the meditator and meditation are not truly separate from you, how can a restless, shameless mind meditate?
avadhuta_gita::26.simple_insight: You feel the tension between your complete self and your restless, unsettled mind.
avadhuta_gita::26.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals that the inner self is already full and uninterrupted. The idea of a separate meditator and meditation is an illusion, so the restless, shameless mind cannot truly focus on meditation.
avadhuta_gita::26.modern_relevance: You try to quiet your mind during meditation, but it keeps wandering, reminding you that your true self is already complete beyond this restlessness.
avadhuta_gita::26.insight: It shifts attention from trying to control the mind to recognizing your already complete true self beyond mental distractions.

avadhuta_gita::27.verse_sanskrit:
शिवं न जानामि कथं वदामि
शिवं न जानामि कथं भजामि ।
अहं शिवश्चेत्परमार्थतत्त्वं
समस्वरूपं गगनोपमं च ॥
avadhuta_gita::27.verse_hindi: मैं शिव को नहीं जानता तो कैसे उसका वर्णन करूँ मैं शिव को नहीं जानता तो कैसे उसे भजूँ, मैं ही शिव स्वरूप एवं परमार्थ तत्व हूँ जो गगन के तुल्य और सम स्वरूप है।
avadhuta_gita::27.english_translation: I do not know Shiva, so how can I describe or worship him? I am Shiva's form and the supreme reality, identical and like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::27.translation_literal: शिवं (Shiva) / न (not) / जानामि (know) / कथं (how) / वदामि (speak) / शिवं (Shiva) / न (not) / जानामि (know) / कथं (how) / भजामि (worship) / अहं (I) / शिवः (Shiva) / चेत् (if) / परम (supreme) / अर्थ (meaning) / तत्त्वं (principle) / सम (equal) / स्वरूपं (form) / गगन (sky) / उपमं (like) / च (and)
avadhuta_gita::27.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::27.essence: You cannot know or worship what you already are, the infinite supreme reality.
avadhuta_gita::27.simple_meaning: You cannot truly know or describe the divine because you already are that supreme reality, vast and unchanging like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::27.simple_insight: You can feel complete knowing you already are the highest truth, beyond needing to seek it.
avadhuta_gita::27.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he does not know Shiva as a separate being and questions how he could praise or describe him. Instead, he reveals that he himself is the supreme reality, equal in essence and vast like the sky, dissolving all separation.
avadhuta_gita::27.modern_relevance: When you stop chasing ideals or descriptions of yourself, you realize you already embody what you sought—vast, unchanging, and whole.
avadhuta_gita::27.insight: It teaches you to stop searching outside and recognize your identity with the supreme reality right now.

avadhuta_gita::28.verse_sanskrit:
नाहं तत्त्वं समं तत्त्वं कल्पनाहेतुवर्जितम् ।
ग्राह्यग्राहकनिर्मुक्तं स्वसंवेद्यं कथं भवेत् ॥
avadhuta_gita::28.verse_hindi: न मैं तत्व हूँ न किसी के समान तत्व हूँ, कल्पना तथा उसके हेतु से भी रहित हूँ, ग्राह्य तथा ग्राहक के व्यवहार से भी रहित हूँ, स्वयंवेद्य भी कैसे हो।
avadhuta_gita::28.english_translation: I am neither a principle nor like any principle, beyond imagination and its cause, free from the relation of subject and object, and how can I be self-known?
avadhuta_gita::28.translation_literal: नाहं (not I) / तत्त्वं (principle) / समं (equal, same) / तत्त्वं (principle) / कल्पना (imagination) / हेतुवर्जितम् (free from cause) / ग्राह्य (object to be grasped) / ग्राहकम् (grasper, subject) / निर्मुक्तं (freed) / स्वसंवेद्यं (self-known) / कथं (how) / भवेत् (can be)
avadhuta_gita::28.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::28.essence: You are beyond all concepts, including knowing and being known.
avadhuta_gita::28.simple_meaning: You are not a principle or like any principle. You are beyond imagination, beyond subject and object, and cannot be grasped or even known by yourself.
avadhuta_gita::28.simple_insight: There is a relief in realizing you are beyond all dualities and cannot be confined by thought or perception.
avadhuta_gita::28.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points inward beyond all concepts. He denies being any principle or equal to any principle, denying all mental constructs like imagination and the duality of subject-object, showing the true self is beyond knowledge or being an object of knowledge.
avadhuta_gita::28.modern_relevance: When you struggle to label or understand yourself, this reminds you that your true nature cannot be boxed by any idea or self-image.
avadhuta_gita::28.insight: It teaches you to release all mental categories of self and stop trying to grasp your identity as an object or subject.

avadhuta_gita::29.verse_sanskrit:
अनन्तरूपं न हि वस्तु किंचि-
त्तत्त्वस्वरूपं न हि वस्तु किंचित् ।
आत्मैकरूपं परमार्थतत्त्वं
न हिंसको वापि न चाप्यहिंसा ॥
avadhuta_gita::29.verse_hindi: यह आत्मा (ब्रह्म) अनन्त रूप है ऐसी अन्य कोई वस्तु नहीं है। यह ब्रह्म ही तत्व स्वरूप है, ऐसी कोई अन्य वस्तु नहीं है। यह आत्मा एक रूप ही है तथा परमार्थ तत्व है इसलिए न तो कोई हिंसक है न अहिंसा ही है।
avadhuta_gita::29.english_translation: The true self is infinite in form; no other object exists. It alone is the supreme reality, neither harmful nor harmless.
avadhuta_gita::29.translation_literal: अनन्तरूपं (infinite form) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / वस्तु (object) / किंचि (anything) - / तत्त्वस्वरूपं (essence form) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / वस्तु (object) / किंचित् (anything) / आत्मैकरूपं (self-one-form) / परमार्थतत्त्वं (supreme reality) / न (not) / हिंसको (harmful) / वापि (nor) / न (not) / च (also) / अप्यहिंसा (harmless)
avadhuta_gita::29.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::29.essence: Your true self is infinite and beyond all opposites like harm and harmlessness.
avadhuta_gita::29.simple_meaning: Your true self has infinite form and is the supreme reality beyond harm or kindness.
avadhuta_gita::29.simple_insight: You carry the freedom of being beyond all dualities, including harm and harmlessness.
avadhuta_gita::29.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares the self as infinite and the supreme essence. There is no separate object or quality like harm or harmlessness attached to it, revealing the self's pure, undivided nature.
avadhuta_gita::29.modern_relevance: In moments of judgment or fear, realize you are beyond simple labels like harm or safety, limitless in your true nature.
avadhuta_gita::29.insight: Recognize the true self as beyond dual qualities, freeing your mind from fear and attachment.

avadhuta_gita::30.verse_sanskrit:
विशुद्धोऽसि समं तत्त्वं विदेहमजमव्ययम् ।
विभ्रमं कथमात्मार्थे विभ्रान्तोऽहं कथं पुनः ॥
avadhuta_gita::30.verse_hindi: तुम विशुद्ध हो, देह रहित, जन्म रहित, अव्यय तथा समरस तत्व हो। आत्मा के विषय में तुम्हे भ्रांति क्यों है ? तुम कैसे कह सकते हो कि मैं भ्रान्ति युक्त हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::30.english_translation: You are pure, without body, unborn, imperishable, and the same essence. Why is there confusion about the true self? How can you claim to be deluded?
avadhuta_gita::30.translation_literal: विशुद्धोऽसि (You are pure) / समं (equal/the same) / तत्त्वं (essence) / विदेहमजमव्ययम् (without body, unborn, imperishable) / विभ्रमं (confusion) / कथमात्मार्थे (how about the self) / विभ्रान्तोऽहं (I am deluded) / कथं (how) / पुनः (again)
avadhuta_gita::30.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::30.essence: Your true self is pure and unchanging; confusion about it is impossible.
avadhuta_gita::30.simple_meaning: You are the pure, unchanging essence beyond body and birth. Confusion about your true self cannot be real.
avadhuta_gita::30.simple_insight: There is relief in realizing your true self is beyond all doubts and illusions.
avadhuta_gita::30.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares you are pure consciousness, beyond physical form or birth. He questions how confusion about your own true nature could exist, challenging the illusion of being deluded.
avadhuta_gita::30.modern_relevance: When self-doubt clouds your mind, remember you are the unchanged essence beyond any confusion.
avadhuta_gita::30.insight: It teaches you to reject self-doubt and recognize your unchanging true nature beyond appearances.

avadhuta_gita::31.verse_sanskrit:
घटे भिन्ने घटाकाशं सुलीनं भेदवर्जितम् ।
शिवेन मनसा शुद्धो न भेदः प्रतिभाति मे ॥
avadhuta_gita::31.verse_hindi: घट के नाश होने पर घटाकाश महाकाश में लीन होकर भेद रहित हो जाता है (इसी प्रकार) शुद्ध मन से शुद्ध ही प्रतीत होता है। मुझे आत्मा का भेद प्रतीत नहीं होता है।
avadhuta_gita::31.english_translation: When the pot breaks, the space within it merges with the vast space, becoming undivided; likewise, a pure mind perceives no division in the true self.
avadhuta_gita::31.translation_literal: घटे (when the pot) / भिन्ने (breaks) / घटाकाशं (the pot-space) / सुलीनं (merged) / भेदवर्जितम् (without division) / शिवेन (by the pure) / मनसा (mind) / शुद्धो (being pure) / न (not) / भेदः (division) / प्रतिभाति (appears) / मे (to me)
avadhuta_gita::31.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::31.essence: Pure awareness reveals that apparent divisions vanish like space freed from a broken pot.
avadhuta_gita::31.simple_meaning: When the pot breaks, the space inside merges with the open sky without divisions. Similarly, a pure mind sees the true self as undivided and whole.
avadhuta_gita::31.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your true self is beyond all separation and division.
avadhuta_gita::31.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya compares the breaking of a pot, where the enclosed space merges with vast space, to the pure mind realizing the true self as indivisible, revealing the non-dual nature of reality.
avadhuta_gita::31.modern_relevance: When you let go of mental barriers, your sense of separation fades and you feel connected with everything around you.
avadhuta_gita::31.insight: It teaches you to recognize that divisions are mental constructs and your true self is seamless and whole.

avadhuta_gita::32.verse_sanskrit:
न घटो न घटाकाशो न जीवो जीवविग्रहः ।
केवलं ब्रह्म संविद्धि वेद्यवेदकवर्जितम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::32.verse_hindi: न घट है, न घटाकाश है, न जीव हैं न उसका कोई विग्रह है। केवल ब्रह्म को ही सम्यक् जान जो ज्ञान तथा ज्ञाता से रहित है।
avadhuta_gita::32.english_translation: There is no pot, no pot-space, no living being, no form; only Brahman is truly known, free from knowledge and knower.
avadhuta_gita::32.translation_literal: न (not) घटो (pot) न (not) घटाकाशो (pot-space) न (not) जीवो (living being) जीवविग्रहः (living form) । केवलं (only) ब्रह्म (Brahman) संविद्धि (is known truly) वेद्यवेदकवर्जितम् (free from knowledge and knower) ॥
avadhuta_gita::32.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::32.essence: You are not any form or identity; only the supreme reality truly exists.
avadhuta_gita::32.simple_meaning: There are no separate things like pot, space, living being, or form ultimately; only the supreme reality exists, beyond any knowledge or knower.
avadhuta_gita::32.simple_insight: You can feel the relief of realizing you are not limited to any shape or identity, but are pure existence itself.
avadhuta_gita::32.detailed_meaning: The sage Dattatreya declares that nothing that appears as separate or with form truly exists. There is only the supreme reality, beyond any duality of knowing or being known.
avadhuta_gita::32.modern_relevance: When you feel boxed in by your roles and identities, remember you are more than those labels—pure and unlimited at core.
avadhuta_gita::32.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing forms to recognizing yourself as the unchanging supreme reality.

avadhuta_gita::33.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वत्र सर्वदा सर्वमात्मानं सततं ध्रुवम् ।
सर्वं शून्यमशून्यं च तन्मां विद्धि न संशयः ॥
avadhuta_gita::33.verse_hindi: तू आत्मा को सर्वत्र, सदा, सर्वरूप (सब कुछ), सतत एवं नित्य जान तथा इस समस्त जगत को शून्य जान और आत्मा को ही अशून्य जान। वह आत्मा मुझे ही जान इसमें संशय नहीं है।
avadhuta_gita::33.english_translation: Know that the true self is everywhere, always, and is all that exists; the entire world is void, and the true self alone is real without doubt.
avadhuta_gita::33.translation_literal: सर्वत्र (everywhere) सर्वदा (always) सर्वम् (all) आत्मानं (true self) सततं (constant) ध्रुवम् (immutable) । सर्वं (all) शून्यम् (void) अशून्यं (non-void) च (and) तत् (that) मां (me) विद्धि (know) न (not) संशयः (doubt) ॥
avadhuta_gita::33.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::33.essence: You are the unchanging reality beyond all empty appearances everywhere and always.
avadhuta_gita::33.simple_meaning: The true self is constant, everywhere present, and is all that truly exists; the world appears empty, but the true self alone is real without doubt.
avadhuta_gita::33.simple_insight: You can rest in the certainty that your true self is unchanging and beyond all appearances.
avadhuta_gita::33.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the true self pervades all places and times, is the essence of all forms, and is unchanging. Everything else—the world and its forms—is empty or void. This verse affirms non-duality and the certainty of the true self's reality.
avadhuta_gita::33.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by endless distractions and shifting situations, you can remember that your true self remains constant and whole beneath it all.
avadhuta_gita::33.insight: It shifts your understanding from seeing separations to recognizing your unchanging presence as the reality behind all change.

avadhuta_gita::34.verse_sanskrit:
वेदा न लोका न सुरा न यज्ञा
वर्णाश्रमो नैव कुलं न जातिः ।
न धूममार्गो न च दीप्तिमार्गो
ब्रह्मैकरूपं परमार्थतत्त्वम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::34.verse_hindi: वेद भी नहीं हैं, लोक भी नहीं है, देवता भी नहीं है, यज्ञ भी नहीं हैं, वर्ण और आश्रम भी नहीं है, न कुल है, न जाति हैं, धूतमार्ग भी नहीं है और न अग्निमार्ग ही है। केवल एकरूप ब्रह्म ही परमार्थ तत्व है।
avadhuta_gita::34.english_translation: There are no Vedas, no worlds, no deities, no sacrifices, no social classes or lineages, no smoke path nor fire path; only the one-form supreme reality exists.
avadhuta_gita::34.translation_literal: वेद (Vedas) / न (not) / लोका (worlds) / न (not) / सुरा (deities) / न (not) / यज्ञा (sacrifices) / वर्णाश्रमो (social classes and stages) / नैव (also not) / कुलं (lineage) / न (not) / जातिः (caste) / न (not) / धूममार्गो (smoke path) / न (not) / च (and) / दीप्तिमार्गो (fire path) / ब्रह्मैकरूपं (one-form supreme reality) / परमार्थतत्त्वम् (ultimate truth)
avadhuta_gita::34.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::34.essence: All divisions vanish; only the one undivided supreme reality exists.
avadhuta_gita::34.simple_meaning: All external divisions like scriptures, social groups, and rituals do not define reality; only the undivided supreme reality truly exists.
avadhuta_gita::34.simple_insight: You are not confined by social or religious labels; your true nature is whole and undivided.
avadhuta_gita::34.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya rejects all customary markers of identity — scriptures, worlds, deities, rituals, social classes, and lineages — declaring that none of these separate or define the ultimate truth, which is the one undivided supreme reality itself.
avadhuta_gita::34.modern_relevance: When you feel boxed in by labels or roles others impose, remember your true nature is beyond all divisions and identities.
avadhuta_gita::34.insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with social or religious categories to recognizing the undivided essence beneath all appearances.

avadhuta_gita::35.verse_sanskrit:
व्याप्यव्यापकनिर्मुक्तः त्वमेकः सफलं यदि ।
प्रत्यक्षं चापरोक्षं च ह्यात्मानं मन्यसे कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::35.verse_hindi: यदि तू एक ही, फल के सहित है और व्याप्त-व्यापक भाव से रहित है तू प्रत्यक्ष और अपरोक्ष आत्मा को कैसे मानता है।
avadhuta_gita::35.english_translation: If you are the one, complete and free from the pervader and the pervaded, how do you consider the self as both direct and indirect?
avadhuta_gita::35.translation_literal: व्याप्यव्यापकनिर्मुक्तः (free from pervader and pervaded) / त्वम् (you) / एकः (one) / सफलं (complete) / यदि (if) / प्रत्यक्षं (direct) / च (and) / अपरोक्षं (indirect) / च (and) / हि (indeed) / आत्मानं (the self) / मन्यसे (you consider) / कथम् (how)
avadhuta_gita::35.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::35.essence: True self is never partly hidden or divided; it is always fully present.
avadhuta_gita::35.simple_meaning: You are whole and free from all divisions; it makes no sense to think of the self as sometimes seen and sometimes hidden.
avadhuta_gita::35.simple_insight: There is relief in realizing your true self is never divided or partial.
avadhuta_gita::35.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya challenges the idea that the true self is partly visible or hidden. He points out that if you are truly one and completely free, then the self cannot be considered both direct and indirect.
avadhuta_gita::35.modern_relevance: When you feel fragmented or unsure of yourself, remember that your true nature is always whole and present, not partly hidden.
avadhuta_gita::35.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as divided to recognizing your constant wholeness.

avadhuta_gita::36.verse_sanskrit:
अद्वैतं केचिदिच्छन्ति द्वैतमिच्छन्ति चापरे ।
समं तत्त्वं न विन्दन्ति द्वैताद्वैतविवर्जितम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::36.verse_hindi: कुछ अद्वैत की इच्छा करते हैं और कुछ द्वैत की इच्छा करते हैं किन्तु वे समतत्व को नहीं जानते जो द्वैत और अद्वैत से रहित है।
avadhuta_gita::36.english_translation: Some desire non-duality, others desire duality, but neither knows the same essence beyond both.
avadhuta_gita::36.translation_literal: अद्वैतं (non-duality) केचिदिच्छन्ति (some desire) द्वैतमिच्छन्ति (duality desire) चापरे (and others) । समं (same) तत्त्वं (essence) न (not) विन्दन्ति (find) द्वैताद्वैतविवर्जितम् (free from duality and non-duality) ॥
avadhuta_gita::36.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::36.essence: The true essence is beyond wanting duality or non-duality; it transcends both.
avadhuta_gita::36.simple_meaning: People either want unity without difference or separation between things, but neither understands the essence that goes beyond both ideas.
avadhuta_gita::36.simple_insight: There's freedom in realizing the true self is beyond all divides you imagine.
avadhuta_gita::36.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that some people seek only unity (non-duality) while others seek separation (duality), yet both fail to grasp that the true essence transcends these categories altogether.
avadhuta_gita::36.modern_relevance: When you argue over extremes or labels, you miss the deeper reality that holds everything together beyond those differences.
avadhuta_gita::36.insight: It shifts your mind from choosing sides to recognizing a single reality beyond all distinctions.

avadhuta_gita::37.verse_sanskrit:
श्वेतादिवर्णरहितं शब्दादिगुणवर्जितम् ।
कथयन्ति कथं तत्त्वं मनोवाचामगोचरम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::37.verse_hindi: जो सफेद आदि वर्गों से रहित है, शब्दादि गुणों से भी रहित है, जो मन और वाणी का विषय ही नहीं है उसे तत्व किस प्रकार कहा जा सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::37.english_translation: How can that principle be described which is free from whiteness and other qualities, beyond words, and not subject to mind or speech?
avadhuta_gita::37.translation_literal: श्वेतादि (whiteness and so on) वर्णरहितं (free from color) शब्दादि (words and so on) गुणवर्जितम् (free from qualities) कथयन्ति (do they describe) कथं (how) तत्त्वं (principle) मनोवाचामगोचरम् (not subject to mind and speech)
avadhuta_gita::37.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::37.essence: The true principle cannot be captured by words, qualities, or mental concepts.
avadhuta_gita::37.simple_meaning: The true principle cannot be described by words, thoughts, or qualities because it is beyond all of these.
avadhuta_gita::37.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing your true nature cannot be pinned down by language or concepts.
avadhuta_gita::37.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya questions how the ultimate principle, which has no qualities like color or sound and is beyond mind and speech, can be described, pointing to the limits of language and thought in capturing reality.
avadhuta_gita::37.modern_relevance: When you try to explain your deepest feelings or experiences, you find words fall short—this shows some truths are beyond description.
avadhuta_gita::37.insight: It shifts your mind away from trying to define the true self and towards simply recognizing its indefinable presence.

avadhuta_gita::38.verse_sanskrit:
यदाऽनृतमिदं सर्वं देहादिगगनोपमम् ।
तदा हि ब्रह्म संवेत्ति न ते द्वैतपरम्परा ॥
avadhuta_gita::38.verse_hindi: जिस समय यह सम्पूर्ण दृश्य जगत मिथ्या ज्ञात होने लगे तथा ये शरीर आदि आकाश के समान शून्य जान पड़े तभी ब्रह्म को ठीक प्रकार से जाना जाता है। उस समय तुझे द्वैत परम्परा का भान नहीं होगा।
avadhuta_gita::38.english_translation: When all this apparent world is known to be false and the body and such are understood as empty like space, then the supreme reality is truly realized, and you no longer perceive duality.
avadhuta_gita::38.translation_literal: यदा (when) अनृतम् (false) इदं (this) सर्वं (all) देहादि (body and others) गगन (sky) उपमम् (like) / तदा (then) हि (indeed) ब्रह्म (supreme reality) संवेत्ति (knows) न (not) ते (you) द्वैत (duality) परम्परा (tradition)
avadhuta_gita::38.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::38.essence: Knowing the world as empty like space reveals the supreme reality beyond duality.
avadhuta_gita::38.simple_meaning: You truly know the supreme reality when you see the world and body as empty like space, and duality disappears.
avadhuta_gita::38.simple_insight: There is freedom in realizing the world is not as solid as it seems.
avadhuta_gita::38.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that recognizing the entire visible world, including the body, as unreal like empty space reveals the supreme reality, dissolving all sense of duality and separation.
avadhuta_gita::38.modern_relevance: In moments when you see your worries and identity as fleeting and empty, you glimpse beyond the usual divisions and fears.
avadhuta_gita::38.insight: It shifts your perception from seeing yourself as separate to recognizing oneness beyond appearances.

avadhuta_gita::39.verse_sanskrit:
परेण सहजात्मापि ह्यभिन्नः प्रतिभाति मे ।
व्योमाकारं तथैवैकं ध्याता ध्यानं कथं भवेत् ॥
avadhuta_gita::39.verse_hindi: मुझे यह भान हो रहा है कि यह अनादि आत्मा परब्रह्म से भिन्न नहीं है जो आकाश के समान व्यापक एवं एक ही है तो फिर ध्याता और ध्यान कैसे हो सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::39.english_translation: I realize that my natural self is not different from the supreme reality, which is vast like the sky and one; so how can there be a meditator and meditation?
avadhuta_gita::39.translation_literal: परेण (by the supreme) सहजात्मा-अपि (natural self also) हि (indeed) अभिन्नः (not different) प्रतिभाति (appears) मे (to me) । व्योमाकारं (like the sky) तथैवैकं (and just one) ध्याता (the meditator) ध्यानं (meditation) कथं (how) भवेत् (can be) ॥
avadhuta_gita::39.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::39.essence: The natural self and supreme reality are one; separation between observer and observed is impossible.
avadhuta_gita::39.simple_meaning: You realize your natural self is not separate from the supreme reality, so there is no true division between meditator and meditation.
avadhuta_gita::39.simple_insight: You can feel the relief of knowing that the sense of separation is just a mental construct.
avadhuta_gita::39.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reflects that his natural self is inseparable from the supreme reality, like the vast sky that is one. This realization dissolves the idea of a separate meditator and meditation, revealing non-duality.
avadhuta_gita::39.modern_relevance: You catch a quiet moment seeing that the 'you' trying to control things is actually part of everything, not apart from it.
avadhuta_gita::39.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing itself as a separate doer to recognizing unity with all experience.

avadhuta_gita::40.verse_sanskrit:
यत्करोमि यदश्नामि यज्जुहोमि ददामि यत् ।
एतत्सर्वं न मे किंचिद्विशुद्धोऽहमजोऽव्ययः ॥
avadhuta_gita::40.verse_hindi: जो मैं करता हूँ, जो मैं भक्षण करता हूँ, जो मैं हवन करता हूँ, जो मैं देता हूँ वह सब किंचिद् भी मेरा नहीं है। मैं विशुद्ध, जन्म रहित एवं नाश रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::40.english_translation: Whatever I do, eat, offer, or give—all of this is not mine. I am pure, unborn, and indestructible.
avadhuta_gita::40.translation_literal: यत्करोमि (whatever I do) / यदश्नामि (whatever I eat) / यज्जुहोमि (whatever I offer in sacrifice) / ददामि (whatever I give) / यत् (that) / एतत्सर्वं (all this) / न (not) / मे (mine) / किंचिद् (anything) / विशुद्धः (pure) / अहम् (I am) / अजो (unborn) / अव्ययः (indestructible)
avadhuta_gita::40.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::40.essence: Your true self transcends all actions, possessions, and changes.
avadhuta_gita::40.simple_meaning: Your actions, meals, offerings, and gifts don’t belong to you. Your true self is pure, eternal, and beyond birth or death.
avadhuta_gita::40.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing your true self is untouched by what you do or own.
avadhuta_gita::40.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that all external actions and possessions are not truly 'his.' As the Avadhuta, he reveals his identity as pure awareness, beyond birth and decay, untouched by worldly acts.
avadhuta_gita::40.modern_relevance: You may feel overwhelmed by roles and responsibilities, but your true self remains untouched by all you do or give.
avadhuta_gita::40.insight: It shifts your focus from identifying with actions or possessions to recognizing your unchanging, pure nature.

avadhuta_gita::41.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वं जगद्विद्धि निराकृतीदं
सर्वं जगद्विद्धि विकारहीनम् ।
सर्वं जगद्विद्धि विशुद्धदेहं
सर्वं जगद्विद्धि शिवैकरूपम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::41.verse_hindi: इस सम्पूर्ण जगत को तू आकार रहित जान, इस सम्पूर्ण जगत को तू विकार रहित जान, इस सम्पूर्ण जगत को तू विशुद्ध ब्रह्म का शरीर जान, इस सम्पूर्ण जगत को तू कल्याण स्वरूप जान।
avadhuta_gita::41.english_translation: Know the entire world as formless, free from change, the pure body of the supreme reality, and the embodiment of auspiciousness.
avadhuta_gita::41.translation_literal: सर्वं (all) जगत् (world) विद्धि (know) निराकृतीदं (formless) / सर्वं (all) जगत् (world) विद्धि (know) विकारहीनम् (free from change) / सर्वं (all) जगत् (world) विद्धि (know) विशुद्धदेहं (pure body) / सर्वं (all) जगत् (world) विद्धि (know) शिवैकरूपम् (auspicious one form)
avadhuta_gita::41.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::41.essence: All appearances are the formless, pure, and auspicious true self at their core.
avadhuta_gita::41.simple_meaning: The whole world is not made of shapes or changes but is the pure, unchanging true self and the source of all goodness.
avadhuta_gita::41.simple_insight: You feel a deep calm knowing the world is not as unstable as it seems but a pure presence.
avadhuta_gita::41.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that everything you see as the world is not limited by form or change. Instead, it is the pure and auspicious reality itself, free from distortions or imperfections, revealing the ultimate truth beyond appearances.
avadhuta_gita::41.modern_relevance: When everything around you feels unstable or confusing, remembering that the world’s true nature is pure and unchanging can bring peace amid chaos.
avadhuta_gita::41.insight: Shift your view from seeing only physical change to recognizing the underlying unchanging essence in all things.

avadhuta_gita::42.verse_sanskrit:
तत्त्वं त्वं न हि सन्देहः किं जानाम्यथवा पुनः ।
असंवेद्यं स्वसंवेद्यमात्मानं मन्यसे कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::42.verse_hindi: वह तू ही है तथा तू वही है इसमें कोई सन्देह नहीं है फिर और मैं क्या जानूँ। फिर आत्मा को असंवेद्य ‘किसी से भी जानने योग्य नहीं’ तथा स्वसंवेद्य ‘अपने से ही जानने योग्य’ कैसे माना जाए।
avadhuta_gita::42.english_translation: You are the essence, there is no doubt in this; what else do I need to know? How can the true self be both unknowable by others and known only by itself?
avadhuta_gita::42.translation_literal: तत्त्वं (essence) त्वं (you) न (not) हि (indeed) सन्देहः (doubt) किं (what) जानामि (do I know) अथवा (or) पुनः (again) । असंवेद्यं (unknowable) स्वसंवेद्यम् (self-known) आत्मानं (true self) मन्यसे (do you consider) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::42.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::42.essence: You are the undeniable essence; no contradiction or doubt can exist about this.
avadhuta_gita::42.simple_meaning: You are the fundamental reality without any doubt. The true self cannot be both unknown to others and known only to itself.
avadhuta_gita::42.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing you are the undeniable essence, beyond confusion or contradiction.
avadhuta_gita::42.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya proclaims that the self is the ultimate reality without any doubt. He challenges the idea that the true self can be unknowable to others yet known only to itself, pointing to the unity and clarity of this truth.
avadhuta_gita::42.modern_relevance: When you feel unsure about who you really are, remember that your true nature is clear and undeniable.
avadhuta_gita::42.insight: It shifts the mind from confusion to certainty about your inner identity and unity with reality.

avadhuta_gita::43.verse_sanskrit:
मायाऽमाया कथं तात छायाऽछाया न विद्यते ।
तत्त्वमेकमिदं सर्वं व्योमाकारं निरञ्जनम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::43.verse_hindi: हे तात! माया और अमाया कैसे है, छाया और अछाया भी विद्यमान नहीं है। यह तू एक ही है तथा यह सम्पूर्ण जगत आकाश के समान व्यापक एवं निर्दोष है।
avadhuta_gita::43.english_translation: O father! How can there be illusion and non-illusion, shadow and no shadow? This is all one truth, vast like space and pure.
avadhuta_gita::43.translation_literal: मायाऽमाया (illusion and non-illusion) / कथं (how) / तात (O father) / छायाऽछाया (shadow and no shadow) / न (not) / विद्यते (exists) / तत्त्वमेकम् (one truth) / इदं (this) / सर्वं (all) / व्योमाकारं (like space) / निरञ्जनम् (pure)
avadhuta_gita::43.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::43.essence: Opposites like illusion and reality dissolve into one pure, limitless truth.
avadhuta_gita::43.simple_meaning: Illusion and its opposite do not truly exist; everything is one pure, boundless reality like space.
avadhuta_gita::43.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing all opposites merge into one pure reality beyond illusion.
avadhuta_gita::43.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares to his father that dualities like illusion and non-illusion, shadow and no shadow, do not exist separately. Instead, everything is one vast, spotless reality comparable to the infinite sky.
avadhuta_gita::43.modern_relevance: When confusion about right and wrong, real and fake overwhelms you, remember that beyond these opposites lies a single pure reality.
avadhuta_gita::43.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing dualities to embracing undivided unity beyond appearances.

avadhuta_gita::44.verse_sanskrit:
आदिमध्यान्तमुक्तोऽहं न बद्धोऽहं कदाचन ।
स्वभावनिर्मलः शुद्ध इति मे निश्चिता मतिः ॥
avadhuta_gita::44.verse_hindi: मैं आदि, मध्य और अन्त से रहित हूँ, न मैं कभी बद्ध ही हूँ। मेरी यह निश्चित मति है कि मैं स्वभाव से ही निर्मल और शुद्ध हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::44.english_translation: I am free from beginning, middle, and end; never bound. I am naturally pure and spotless, this is my firm conviction.
avadhuta_gita::44.translation_literal: आदि (beginning) / मध्य (middle) / अन्त (end) / मुक्तः (free) / अहं (I) / न (not) / बद्धः (bound) / अहं (I) / कदाचन (ever) / स्वभाव (by nature) / निर्मलः (pure) / शुद्ध (spotless) / इति (thus) / मे (my) / निश्चिता (firm) / मतिः (conviction)
avadhuta_gita::44.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::44.essence: Your true self is timeless, always free, and naturally pure.
avadhuta_gita::44.simple_meaning: You are beyond time and never truly limited. Your true nature is pure and unchanging.
avadhuta_gita::44.simple_insight: You can rest in the freedom that was never lost and the purity that was never stained.
avadhuta_gita::44.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares here that he is untouched by the flow of time—no beginning, middle, or end confines him. He knows deeply that his nature is always pure, beyond any limitation or binding.
avadhuta_gita::44.modern_relevance: When life feels like a timeline of stress and obligations, this reminds you that your true self is beyond all that pressure and naturally clear.
avadhuta_gita::44.insight: Recognize your identity beyond all phases and limits, resting in innate purity and freedom.

avadhuta_gita::45.verse_sanskrit:
महदादि जगत्सर्वं न किंचित्प्रतिभाति मे ।
ब्रह्मैव केवलं सर्वं कथं वर्णाश्रमस्थितिः ॥
avadhuta_gita::45.verse_hindi: महतत्व आदि से इस सम्पूर्ण जगत का मुझे थोड़ा सा भी ज्ञान नहीं होता। केवल ब्रह्म ही सब कुछ है फिर वर्णाश्रम की स्थिति किस प्रकार हो सकती है।
avadhuta_gita::45.english_translation: I perceive nothing of the vast universe; only Brahman is all that exists. How then can the distinctions of caste and stages of life be true?
avadhuta_gita::45.translation_literal: महदादि (great origin) / जगत्सर्वं (entire world) / न (not) / किंचित् (anything) / प्रतिभाति (appears) / मे (to me) / ब्रह्मैव (only Brahman) / केवलं (alone) / सर्वं (all) / कथं (how) / वर्णाश्रमस्थितिः (caste and life stages system)
avadhuta_gita::45.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::45.essence: Only the supreme reality truly exists; social distinctions are unreal.
avadhuta_gita::45.simple_meaning: You recognize that the entire universe is just the supreme reality; social categories like caste and life stages are unreal.
avadhuta_gita::45.simple_insight: You feel freed from social labels, sensing the unity beyond all divisions.
avadhuta_gita::45.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he perceives no separate world beyond the supreme reality. He questions how social divisions like caste and life stages can be true if only Brahman truly exists.
avadhuta_gita::45.modern_relevance: You notice how social roles and labels often limit you, but deep down, you are beyond all such divisions.
avadhuta_gita::45.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with social roles to recognizing the unity underlying all distinctions.

avadhuta_gita::46.verse_sanskrit:
जानामि सर्वथा सर्वमहमेको निरन्तरम् ।
निरालम्बमशून्यं च शून्यं व्योमादिपञ्चकम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::46.verse_hindi: मैं जानता हूँ कि ये आकाशादि पंचक (पृथ्वी, जल, अग्नि, वायु और आकाश) शून्य है तथा मैं सब प्रकार से सर्वरूप एक ही निरन्तर, आलम्बन रहित एवं अशून्य हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::46.english_translation: I know completely that the five elements—earth, water, fire, air, and space—are empty, and I alone am the continuous, independent, and unchanging reality, one in all forms.
avadhuta_gita::46.translation_literal: जानामि (I know) / सर्वथा (completely) / सर्वम् (everything) / अहमेव (I alone) / एको (one) / निरन्तरम् (continuous) / निरालम्बम् (without support) / अशून्यम् (unchanging) / च (and) / शून्यम् (empty) / व्योमात् (from space) / आदि (and others) / पञ्चकम् (the five [elements])
avadhuta_gita::46.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::46.essence: You alone are the continuous, unchanging reality beyond all empty forms.
avadhuta_gita::46.simple_meaning: You are the single unchanging reality, independent and continuous, beyond the empty five elements of the world.
avadhuta_gita::46.simple_insight: Feel the relief of knowing your true self is constant beyond all changing things.
avadhuta_gita::46.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the five elements—earth, water, fire, air, and space—are empty and impermanent, while the true self is alone, continuous, independent, and unchanging, revealing the core teaching of non-duality.
avadhuta_gita::46.modern_relevance: When everything around you feels unstable or empty, remember your true self remains steady and whole beneath it all.
avadhuta_gita::46.insight: It teaches you to see beyond appearances to the eternal continuity that you are.

avadhuta_gita::47.verse_sanskrit:
न षण्ढो न पुमान्न स्त्री न बोधो नैव कल्पना ।
सानन्दो वा निरानन्दमात्मानं मन्यसे कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::47.verse_hindi: आत्मा न नपुन्सक है, न पुरुष है, न स्त्री है, न ज्ञान है, न कल्पना ही है। यह आनन्दमय एवं निरानन्द भी नहीं है। फिर तुम आत्मा को किस प्रकार का मानते हो।
avadhuta_gita::47.english_translation: The true self is neither male nor female, neither knowledge nor imagination. It is neither joyful nor sorrowful. How then do you conceive of the true self?
avadhuta_gita::47.translation_literal: न (not) षण्ढो (impotent) न (not) पुमान्न (male) स्त्री (female) न (not) बोधो (knowledge) नैव (not even) कल्पना (imagination) । सानन्दो (joyful) वा (or) निरानन्दम् (without joy) आत्मानं (true self) मन्यसे (do you consider) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::47.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::47.essence: The true self cannot be defined by any identity, feeling, or thought.
avadhuta_gita::47.simple_meaning: The true self transcends all identities like male, female, knowledge, or imagination. It is beyond joy and sorrow. It cannot be limited by any concept.
avadhuta_gita::47.simple_insight: There is freedom in realizing you are not confined to any identity or feeling.
avadhuta_gita::47.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya challenges the common ways we define ourselves—by gender, knowledge, or emotions. He reveals that the true self is beyond all these categories, inviting a deeper questioning of who you really are beyond appearances.
avadhuta_gita::47.modern_relevance: When you feel boxed in by roles or emotions—male, female, happy, sad—this verse reminds you that your true essence is beyond those limits.
avadhuta_gita::47.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing traits to recognizing a limitless, unconditioned self.

avadhuta_gita::48.verse_sanskrit:
षडङ्गयोगान्न तु नैव शुद्धं
मनोविनाशान्न तु नैव शुद्धम् ।
गुरूपदेशान्न तु नैव शुद्धं
स्वयं च तत्त्वं स्वयमेव बुद्धम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::48.verse_hindi: आत्मा षडंग योग से शुद्ध नहीं होता, मन के नाश होने से भी शुद्ध नहीं होता, गुरु के उपदेश से भी शुद्ध नहीं होता। वह स्वयं ही सार तत्व है और स्वयं ही शुद्ध है।
avadhuta_gita::48.english_translation: The true self is not purified by the sixfold yoga, nor by the destruction of the mind, nor by the guru's teachings; it is itself the essence and inherently pure.
avadhuta_gita::48.translation_literal: षडङ्गयोगान्न (sixfold-yogas not) / तु (but) / नैव (not at all) / शुद्धं (pure) / मनोविनाशान्न (mind-destruction not) / तु (but) / नैव (not at all) / शुद्धम् (pure) / गुरूपदेशान्न (guru-instructions not) / तु (but) / नैव (not at all) / शुद्धं (pure) / स्वयं (self) / च (also) / तत्त्वं (essence) / स्वयमेव (indeed itself) / बुद्धम् (pure).
avadhuta_gita::48.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::48.essence: The true self transcends all purification efforts because it is inherently pure essence.
avadhuta_gita::48.simple_meaning: Your true self is never something to be purified by practices, mind changes, or teachings; it is already pure and is the essence itself.
avadhuta_gita::48.simple_insight: There is deep relief in knowing your true self is always inherently pure and complete.
avadhuta_gita::48.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that no external practice, mental transformation, or even guru instruction can purify the true self because it is already the pure essence itself, beyond all method or change.
avadhuta_gita::48.modern_relevance: When you struggle to ‘fix’ or ‘improve’ yourself, this verse reminds you that your true nature is already pure and complete, beyond effort.
avadhuta_gita::48.insight: It shifts your view from trying to purify yourself to recognizing your innate purity as the true self.

avadhuta_gita::49.verse_sanskrit:
न हि पञ्चात्मको देहो विदेहो वर्तते न हि ।
आत्मैव केवलं सर्वं तुरीयं च त्रयं कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::49.verse_hindi: आत्मा पंचभौतिक शरीर भी नहीं है तथा देह से रहित भी नहीं वर्तता है। आत्मा ही केवल और सर्व रूप है फिर इसकी तुरीय और तीन अवस्थाएँ कैसे हैं।
avadhuta_gita::49.english_translation: The true self is neither the five-element body nor without a body; it alone is everything. How then can it have the three states and the fourth beyond them?
avadhuta_gita::49.translation_literal: न (not) हि (indeed) पञ्चात्मको (five-element-body) देहो (body) विदेहो (without-body) वर्तते (exists) न (not) हि (indeed) । आत्मैव (self-alone) केवलं (only) सर्वं (everything) तुरीयं (fourth state) च (and) त्रयं (three states) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::49.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::49.essence: You are the whole reality beyond body and all states of consciousness.
avadhuta_gita::49.simple_meaning: You are not simply your physical body nor completely without one. You alone are the complete reality beyond all states of being.
avadhuta_gita::49.simple_insight: You can feel your true self as neither limited nor absent, but as everything present.
avadhuta_gita::49.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the true self is neither confined to the physical body made of five elements nor completely without a body. It is the sole reality, beyond the three waking, dreaming, and deep sleep states plus the fourth transcendent state.
avadhuta_gita::49.modern_relevance: You might feel stuck identifying only with your body or mind, but this invites you to sense yourself as unlimited—beyond all labels and states.
avadhuta_gita::49.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as limited to recognizing yourself as the unchanging whole beyond all conditions.

avadhuta_gita::50.verse_sanskrit:
न बद्धो नैव मुक्तोऽहं न चाहं ब्रह्मणः पृथक् ।
न कर्ता न च भोक्ताहं व्याप्यव्यापकवर्जितः ॥
avadhuta_gita::50.verse_hindi: मैं बद्ध भी नहीं हूँ, न मुक्त ही हूँ मैं ब्रह्म से भिन्न भी नहीं हूँ, न मैं कर्ता हूँ और न भोक्ता हूँ। मैं व्याप्य और व्यापक भाव से भी रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::50.english_translation: I am neither bound nor free, nor separate from the supreme reality. I am neither the doer nor the experiencer. I am beyond both the pervading and the pervaded.
avadhuta_gita::50.translation_literal: न (not) बद्धो (bound) नैव (nor indeed) मुक्तः (free) अहं (I) न (not) चाहं (am) ब्रह्मणः (of Brahman) पृथक् (separate) । न (not) कर्ता (doer) न (nor) च (also) भोक्ता (experiencer) अहं (I) व्याप्य (pervading) व्यापक (pervaded) वर्जितः (free from) ॥
avadhuta_gita::50.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::50.essence: You are beyond being bound, free, doer, or experiencer—beyond all dual roles.
avadhuta_gita::50.simple_meaning: You are not truly bound or free, not separate from the supreme reality, and not the doer or experiencer of actions.
avadhuta_gita::50.simple_insight: You can feel free from the struggle of doing or suffering because your true nature is beyond both.
avadhuta_gita::50.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he is not bound by limitations nor liberated as something separate. He transcends the roles of doer and experiencer, and even the ideas of pervading or being pervaded, pointing to the ultimate non-dual reality.
avadhuta_gita::50.modern_relevance: When you feel trapped by your choices or outcomes, remember you are not the doer or the one who truly experiences limits—you are beyond those roles.
avadhuta_gita::50.insight: It shifts your self-understanding from identifying as a separate agent or sufferer to recognizing your limitless essence beyond all dualities.

avadhuta_gita::51.verse_sanskrit:
यथा जलं जले न्यस्तं सलिलं भेदवर्जितम् ।
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं तद्वदभिन्नं प्रतिभाति मे ॥
avadhuta_gita::51.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार जल में फेंका हुआ जल जलरूप ही भेद रहित हो जाता है वैसे ही प्रकृति और पुरुष मुझे अभिन्न प्रतीत होते हैं।
avadhuta_gita::51.english_translation: Just as water poured into water becomes indistinguishable from water, so too do nature and pure awareness appear to me as one without difference.
avadhuta_gita::51.translation_literal: यथा (just as) जलं (water) जले (in water) न्यस्तं (placed) सलिलं (water) भेदवर्जितम् (without difference) । प्रकृतिं (nature) पुरुषं (pure awareness) तद्वदभिन्नं (just like that inseparable) प्रतिभाति (appears) मे (to me) ॥
avadhuta_gita::51.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::51.essence: Separation between nature and pure awareness is only an illusion, like water mixing with water.
avadhuta_gita::51.simple_meaning: Nature and pure awareness are not two separate things but one, just like water poured into water becomes inseparable.
avadhuta_gita::51.simple_insight: There is peace in seeing everything as one, without division or separation.
avadhuta_gita::51.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that just as water loses its boundaries when mixed with more water, so too the apparent difference between nature and pure awareness dissolves in true understanding, revealing their essential unity.
avadhuta_gita::51.modern_relevance: When you feel divided or disconnected, remember how water loses all borders when it joins more water—your true self is never apart from the world.
avadhuta_gita::51.insight: It teaches you to see apparent separations as illusions and recognize underlying unity.

avadhuta_gita::52.verse_sanskrit:
यदि नाम न मुक्तोऽसि न बद्धोऽसि कदाचन ।
साकारं च निराकारमात्मानं मन्यसे कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::52.verse_hindi: यदि ऐसा प्रसिद्ध है कि तू मुक्त भी नहीं है और बद्ध भी नहीं है तो फिर आत्मा को साकार और निराकार किस प्रकार मानता है।
avadhuta_gita::52.english_translation: If you are neither free nor bound at any time, then how do you consider the true self both with form and formless?
avadhuta_gita::52.translation_literal: यदि (if) नाम (indeed) न (not) मुक्तः (free) असि (you are) न (not) बद्धः (bound) असि (you are) कदाचन (at any time) । साकारं (with form) च (and) निराकारं (formless) आत्मानं (the true self) मन्यसे (do you consider) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::52.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::52.essence: The true self cannot be limited by opposing ideas of freedom and form.
avadhuta_gita::52.simple_meaning: If you claim to be neither free nor bound, then how can you think of the true self as having form and also being formless?
avadhuta_gita::52.simple_insight: It feels unsettling to hold contradicting ideas about freedom and the nature of the self.
avadhuta_gita::52.detailed_meaning: The Avadhuta challenges the idea of being simultaneously free and bound, questioning how the true self can be understood as both with and without form. This probes the confusion in dualistic thinking about the self's nature.
avadhuta_gita::52.modern_relevance: You feel stuck between feeling restricted and free — and wonder how you can be both at once in your own identity.
avadhuta_gita::52.insight: It shifts your view from accepting contradictory self-images to recognizing the limits of dualistic labels on the true self.

avadhuta_gita::53.verse_sanskrit:
जानामि ते परं रूपं प्रत्यक्षं गगनोपमम् ।
यथा परं हि रूपं यन्मरीचिजलसन्निभम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::53.verse_hindi: मैं तेरे परम रूप को जानता हूँ जो प्रत्यक्ष और आकाश के सदृश है। जिस प्रकार जगत का रूप मृगतृष्णा के जल की तरह है वैसा तुम्हारा नहीं है।
avadhuta_gita::53.english_translation: I know your supreme form, visible and like the sky; unlike the world's form, which is like a mirage's water.
avadhuta_gita::53.translation_literal: जानामि (I know) / ते (your) / परं (supreme) / रूपं (form) / प्रत्यक्षं (visible) / गगनोपमम् (like the sky) / यथा (just as) / परं (supreme) / हि (indeed) / रूपं (form) / यन्मरीचिजलसन्निभम् (like mirage-water)
avadhuta_gita::53.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::53.essence: The true self is visible and vast like the sky, unlike the world's shifting illusions.
avadhuta_gita::53.simple_meaning: The true self is clear and visible like the sky, unlike the world that appears like an illusion or mirage.
avadhuta_gita::53.simple_insight: You are more real and vast than the shifting illusions you see around you.
avadhuta_gita::53.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares knowing the supreme form, which is directly visible and vast like the sky, contrasting it with the world's illusory and fleeting nature, like mirage-water. This highlights the difference between the eternal true self and the deceptive appearances of the natural world.
avadhuta_gita::53.modern_relevance: When everything around you feels uncertain or deceptive, remembering your true self is steady, clear, and vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::53.insight: Recognize that your true nature is unchanging and clearly visible beneath all illusions and appearances.

avadhuta_gita::54.verse_sanskrit:
न गुरुर्नोपदेशश्च न चोपाधिर्न मे क्रिया ।
विदेहं गगनं विद्धि विशुद्धोऽहं स्वभावतः ॥
avadhuta_gita::54.verse_hindi: न तो मेरा कोई गुरु है, न उपदेश ही हैं, न उपाधि है, न क्रिया है। मुझे तू देह से रहित आकाशवत् जान । मैं स्वभाव से ही शुद्ध हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::54.english_translation: I have no guru, no teachings, no title, no action. Know me as the bodyless sky, pure by nature.
avadhuta_gita::54.translation_literal:
न (not) गुरुर्न (guru - not) उपदेशश्च (teaching - and) न (not) च (also) उपाधिर्न (title - not) मे (my) क्रिया (action)।
विदेहं (bodiless) गगनं (sky) विद्धि (know) विशुद्धः (pure) अहं (I) स्वभावतः (by nature)।
avadhuta_gita::54.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::54.essence: Your true nature is pure and limitless, beyond all teachers and actions.
avadhuta_gita::54.simple_meaning: You have no teacher, no instruction, no label, and no required action. You are naturally pure and limitless like the sky without a body.
avadhuta_gita::54.simple_insight: You can feel free from dependence on external authority because your true nature is already pure and complete.
avadhuta_gita::54.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares he has no guru, no teachings, no titles, and no prescribed actions. He reveals his true self as pure and formless like the limitless sky, untouched by any label or condition, emphasizing absolute freedom.
avadhuta_gita::54.modern_relevance: When you feel pressured to seek guidance or prove yourself, remember your true nature is already whole and pure, needing no external validation.
avadhuta_gita::54.insight: It shifts your mind from seeking external approval to recognizing your innate, limitless purity and freedom.

avadhuta_gita::55.verse_sanskrit:
विशुद्धोऽस्य शरीरोऽसि न ते चित्तं परात्परम् ।
अहं चात्मा परं तत्त्वमिति वक्तुं न लज्जसे ॥
avadhuta_gita::55.verse_hindi: तू विशुद्ध है शरीर से रहित है, तू चित्त भी नहीं है। परात्पर है (प्रकृति से भी परे है)। मैं आत्मा हूँ, परम तत्व हूँ, इस प्रकार कहने में तुझे लज्जा नहीं आती है।
avadhuta_gita::55.english_translation: You are pure, beyond the body and the restless mind; you are the supreme reality. You are the true self; never feel shame in declaring this truth.
avadhuta_gita::55.translation_literal: विशुद्धः (pure) अस्य (of this) शरीरः (body) असि (are) न (not) ते (your) चित्तं (mind) परात्परम् (the supreme beyond) । अहं (I) चात्मा (true self) परं (supreme) तत्त्वम् (reality) इति (thus) वक्तुम् (to speak) न (not) लज्जसे (feel shame) ॥
avadhuta_gita::55.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::55.essence: You are pure and supreme beyond body and mind; never feel shame in this truth.
avadhuta_gita::55.simple_meaning: You are not just your body or mind; you are the pure, supreme reality. There is no need to feel ashamed in recognizing this truth about yourself.
avadhuta_gita::55.simple_insight: You can feel proud and free by fully accepting your pure true nature beyond mind and body.
avadhuta_gita::55.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the Avadhuta declares that the true self is pure and transcends both the physical body and the restless mind. The speaker encourages fearless acknowledgment of this supreme reality, affirming one's identity as the highest truth.
avadhuta_gita::55.modern_relevance: When self-doubt or embarrassment about your deepest nature arises, remember that your true self is beyond body and mind and deserves fearless acceptance.
avadhuta_gita::55.insight: It invites you to release identification with body and mind and confidently own your pure, unchanging true self.

avadhuta_gita::56.verse_sanskrit:
कथं रोदिषि रे चित्त ह्यात्मैवात्मात्मना भव ।
पिब वत्स कलातीतमद्वैतं परमामृतम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::56.verse_hindi: हे चित्त ! तू क्यों रूदन करता हैं। निश्चय ही तू आत्म रूप है। यह मानकर स्वयं आत्म-स्वरूप हो जा तथा हे वत्स ! तू कला से अतीत अद्वैत रूपी परम अमृत का पान कर।
avadhuta_gita::56.english_translation: Why do you weep, mind? You are the self itself. Realize your true self and drink the supreme immortal non-duality beyond time.
avadhuta_gita::56.translation_literal: कथं (why) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / रे (O) / चित्त (mind) / हि (indeed) / आत्मैव (self itself) / आत्मा (self) / त्मना (by yourself) / भव (become) / पिब (drink) / वत्स (O dear) / कलातीतम् (beyond time) / अद्वैतं (non-dual) / परमामृतम् (supreme immortal).
avadhuta_gita::56.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::56.essence: Your mind is already the timeless true self; there is no need to weep.
avadhuta_gita::56.simple_meaning: Your restless mind is already your true self. Recognize this and embrace the timeless, undivided reality beyond all change.
avadhuta_gita::56.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing your true self is beyond all pain and confusion.
avadhuta_gita::56.detailed_meaning: The sage addresses the mind, urging it to stop sorrow because it is not separate but the true self itself. This moment invites the mind to recognize its identity with the eternal, non-dual reality beyond time and distinctions.
avadhuta_gita::56.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by worry or sadness, realize that your true self is untouched by these feelings and beyond all time.
avadhuta_gita::56.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with restless emotions to recognizing your unchanging true self.

avadhuta_gita::57.verse_sanskrit:
नैव बोधो न चाबोधो न बोधाबोध एव च ।
यस्येदृशः सदा बोधः स बोधो नान्यथा भवेत् ॥
avadhuta_gita::57.verse_hindi: न तो तू ज्ञान है और न अज्ञान ही है, न ज्ञान एवं अज्ञान का संयुक्त रूप ही है। जिसे इस प्रकार का सदा ज्ञान है वह ज्ञान स्वरूप ही है। वह हमसे भिन्न नहीं होता।
avadhuta_gita::57.english_translation: It is neither knowledge nor ignorance, nor a combination of both; what is always that kind of knowledge is pure knowledge itself.
avadhuta_gita::57.translation_literal: नैव (not at all) बोधो (knowledge) न (nor) चाबोधो (ignorance) न (nor) बोधाबोध (knowledge-ignorance) एव (indeed) च (also) । यस्येतृशः (whose such) सदा (always) बोधः (knowledge) स (that) बोधो (knowledge) नान्यथा (not otherwise) भवेत् (exists) ॥
avadhuta_gita::57.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::57.essence: True knowledge is beyond all opposites and is always present as itself.
avadhuta_gita::57.simple_meaning: True knowledge is not just knowing or not knowing, nor a mix of both. It is always pure and unchanged.
avadhuta_gita::57.simple_insight: You can feel steady knowing your true self is beyond confusion or certainty.
avadhuta_gita::57.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the ultimate truth is not about having or lacking knowledge, nor their combination. Instead, pure knowledge exists always and is inseparable from your true nature.
avadhuta_gita::57.modern_relevance: When you struggle between what you know and what you don’t, this verse reminds you that your deepest self is beyond all that confusion.
avadhuta_gita::57.insight: It teaches you to stop identifying with mental labels and rest as the unchanging essence of knowing itself.

avadhuta_gita::58.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानं न तर्को न समाधियोगो
न देशकालौ न गुरूपदेशः ।
स्वभावसंवित्तरहं च तत्त्व-
माकाशकल्पं सहजं ध्रुवं च ॥
avadhuta_gita::58.verse_hindi: मैं ज्ञान नहीं हूँ, तर्क नहीं हूँ, समाधि योग भी नहीं हूँ, न देश, काल और गुरु का उपदेश ही हूँ। मैं स्वभाव से ही ज्ञान स्वरूप, यथार्थ वस्तु, आकाश के समान व्यापक और स्वभाव से ही नित्य भी हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::58.english_translation: I am not knowledge, nor logic, nor meditation or yoga; not teaching of place, time, or teacher. I am naturally knowledge itself, the true essence, as vast as space, and eternally so by nature.
avadhuta_gita::58.translation_literal: ज्ञानं (knowledge) / न (not) / तर्को (logic) / न (not) / समाधियोगो (meditation-yoga) / न (not) / देशकालौ (place and time) / न (not) / गुरूपदेशः (teacher's instruction) / स्वभावसंवित्तरहं (I am by nature consciousness) / च (and) / तत्त्वमाकाशकल्पं (true essence like space) / सहजं (natural) / ध्रुवं (unchanging) / च (and)
avadhuta_gita::58.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::58.essence: You are naturally the vast, unchanging essence beyond all teachings and concepts.
avadhuta_gita::58.simple_meaning: You are not limited to knowledge, logic, meditation, or any teaching bound by place, time, or teacher. You are naturally the true, vast, and eternal essence like space itself.
avadhuta_gita::58.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing your true self is beyond all concepts and instructions.
avadhuta_gita::58.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that his true self is not confined to knowledge, reasoning, meditation, or any specific teaching bound by place, time, or guru. Instead, he is the natural, infinite essence that is unchanging like space itself, beyond all conditions.
avadhuta_gita::58.modern_relevance: When you feel trapped by endless advice or confusing thoughts, recognize your true self is beyond all these limits—vast and unchanging.
avadhuta_gita::58.insight: It shifts your understanding from identifying with passing ideas or instructions to resting in your boundless, eternal nature.

avadhuta_gita::59.verse_sanskrit:
न जातोऽहं मृतो वापि न मे कर्म शुभाशुभम् ।
विशुद्धं निर्गुणं ब्रह्म बन्धो मुक्तिः कथं मम ॥
avadhuta_gita::59.verse_hindi: न मैं उत्पन्न हुआ हूँ, न मेरी मृत्यु ही है। ये शुभ एवं अशुभ कर्म भी मेरे नहीं हैं। मैं शुद्ध निर्गुण ब्रह्म हूँ। मेरे बन्धन और मुक्ति कैसे कैसे हो सकती है।
avadhuta_gita::59.english_translation: I was never born, nor will I ever die. These good and bad actions are not mine. I am pure, without qualities, the supreme reality; how can bondage or freedom affect me?
avadhuta_gita::59.translation_literal: न (not) जातः (born) अहं (I) मृतः (dead) वा (or) अपि (also) न (not) मे (my) कर्म (actions) शुभाशुभम् (good and bad) । विशुद्धं (pure) निर्गुणं (without qualities) ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) बन्धः (bondage) मुक्तिः (freedom) कथं (how) मम (my) ॥
avadhuta_gita::59.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::59.essence: Your true self is beyond birth, death, and all actions; it is pure and free.
avadhuta_gita::59.simple_meaning: You are not born or dead and are untouched by good or bad actions. You are the pure reality beyond all qualities, unaffected by bondage or freedom.
avadhuta_gita::59.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing your true self never changes or gets trapped.
avadhuta_gita::59.detailed_meaning: The sage Dattatreya declares that the true self is beyond birth and death. He explains that good or bad actions do not affect this pure, qualityless supreme reality, so bondage and freedom are illusions for the true self.
avadhuta_gita::59.modern_relevance: When your mistakes or successes feel overwhelming, remember your true self is untouched by these results and remains pure beyond all change.
avadhuta_gita::59.insight: It teaches you to stop identifying with your actions and realize your true self is always free and unchanged.

avadhuta_gita::60.verse_sanskrit:
यदि सर्वगतो देवः स्थिरः पूर्णो निरन्तरः ।
अन्तरं हि न पश्यामि स बाह्याभ्यन्तरः कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::60.verse_hindi: जब यह आत्मा सर्वत्र व्याप्त है, कभी चलायमान नहीं होता, पूर्ण है, एकरस है तो मैं इसे शरीर के भीतर ही नहीं देखता बल्कि वह बाहर और भीतर सर्वत्र है, उसे कैसे न देखें।
avadhuta_gita::60.english_translation: When the inner being pervades everywhere, is steady, complete, and unchanging, I do not see it only within the body but everywhere, inside and outside; how could it be unseen?
avadhuta_gita::60.translation_literal: यदि (if) सर्वगतो (everywhere-pervading) देवः (divine) स्थिरः (steady) पूर्णो (complete) निरन्तरः (unceasing) । अन्तरं (inside) हि (indeed) न (not) पश्यामि (I see) स (that) बाह्याभ्यन्तरः (outside-inside) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::60.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::60.essence: The true self is steady, complete, and present everywhere, not confined inside the body.
avadhuta_gita::60.simple_meaning: The true self is unchanging, complete, and present everywhere, not limited to inside your body but all around you.
avadhuta_gita::60.simple_insight: You can feel the relief of knowing your true self is never confined or lost anywhere.
avadhuta_gita::60.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya speaks from the experience of the self that is steady and complete everywhere. He explains that this inner reality is not confined to the body but pervades all space, so it cannot be hidden or unseen.
avadhuta_gita::60.modern_relevance: You notice how your awareness flows beyond your body — present in every room, every moment, always steady even when things change.
avadhuta_gita::60.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as limited inside the body to recognizing the constant, all-pervading nature of your true self.

avadhuta_gita::61.verse_hindi: निश्चय ही इस सम्पूर्ण जगत का अखण्डित एवं निरन्तर रूप में स्फुरण हो रहा है। खेद है कि माया और महामोह द्वैत और अद्वैत की कल्पना का भी स्फुरण होता है।
avadhuta_gita::61.english_translation: The entire world continuously shines as an unbroken whole, yet illusion and great delusion also arise as notions of duality and non-duality.
avadhuta_gita::61.translation_literal: स्फुरत्येव (shines certainly) जगत्कृत्स्नम् (the entire world) अखण्डित (unbroken) निरन्तरम् (continuous) । अहो (ah) मायामहामोहो (illusion and great delusion) द्वैताद्वैतविकल्पना (duality and non-duality notions) ॥
avadhuta_gita::61.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::61.essence: The world is an unbroken radiance; all dualities are illusions of the mind.
avadhuta_gita::61.simple_meaning: The whole world is always shining as one continuous reality. Illusion causes us to imagine divisions like duality and non-duality.
avadhuta_gita::61.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that separation is only a mental illusion over an unbroken reality.
avadhuta_gita::61.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals that the world is a continuous, indivisible radiance. Yet, the mind creates confusion by imagining duality and non-duality as separate realities, which are actually illusions.
avadhuta_gita::61.modern_relevance: When you face conflicts or divisions in relationships, remember that these separations arise from your mind, not from the true unity beneath.
avadhuta_gita::61.insight: Recognize that the divisions you perceive are mental constructs; reality itself is seamless and continuous.

avadhuta_gita::62.verse_sanskrit:
साकारं च निराकारं नेति नेतीति सर्वदा ।
भेदाभेदविनिर्मुक्तो वर्तते केवलः शिवः ॥
avadhuta_gita::62.verse_hindi: श्रुति सर्वदा ही साकार और निराकार को ‘नेति-नेति’ (यह सब नहीं हैं, यह सब नहीं है) कहती है। यह ब्रह्म भेद और अभेद से रहित केवल शिव (कल्याण रूप) ही वर्तता है।
avadhuta_gita::62.english_translation: The revealed truth always denies both form and formlessness. Only Shiva exists beyond difference and non-difference.
avadhuta_gita::62.translation_literal: साकारं (with form) / च (and) / निराकारं (formless) / नेति (not this) / नेतीति (not this) / सर्वदा (always) / भेदाभेदविनिर्मुक्तो (free from difference and non-difference) / वर्तते (exists) / केवलः (only) / शिवः (Shiva)
avadhuta_gita::62.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::62.essence: True reality cannot be captured as form or formlessness; it simply is beyond both.
avadhuta_gita::62.simple_meaning: Everything with or without form is denied; only the true self beyond differences truly exists.
avadhuta_gita::62.simple_insight: You can find freedom by realizing you are beyond all labels and opposites.
avadhuta_gita::62.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that the revealed truth always denies describing the divine as either having form or lacking it. The pure reality, called Shiva here, exists free from any distinctions or contradictions.
avadhuta_gita::62.modern_relevance: When you feel pulled between opposing ideas or identities, this reminds you that your true nature is beyond all such limits.
avadhuta_gita::62.insight: It shifts your view from trying to define yourself by any category to simply resting as the undivided reality.

avadhuta_gita::63.verse_sanskrit:
न ते च माता च पिता च बन्धुः न ते च पत्नी न सुतश्च मित्रम् ।
न पक्षपाती न विपक्षपातः कथं हि संतप्तिरियं हि चित्ते ॥
avadhuta_gita::63.verse_hindi: न तो तेरी माता है, न पिता है, न बन्धु है और न पत्नी है, न पुत्र है, न मित्र है, न पक्षपाती है न विपक्षी है। फिर चित्त में यह सन्ताप कैसे करते हो।
avadhuta_gita::63.english_translation: You have no mother, no father, no kin, no wife, no son, no friend, no supporter, no opponent; then why does your mind suffer?
avadhuta_gita::63.translation_literal: न (not) ते (your) च (and) माता (mother) च (and) पिता (father) च (and) बन्धुः (relative) न (not) ते (your) च (and) पत्नी (wife) न (not) सुतः (son) च (and) मित्रम् (friend) । न (not) पक्षपाती (partisan) न (not) विपक्षपातः (opponent) कथं (how) हि (indeed) संतप्तिः (distress) इयं (this) हि (indeed) चित्ते (in the mind) ॥
avadhuta_gita::63.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::63.essence: Without real attachments, your mind’s suffering is a needless illusion.
avadhuta_gita::63.simple_meaning: You have no real relationships or enemies in your true self; so why does your mind feel troubled?
avadhuta_gita::63.simple_insight: Knowing you are beyond all relationships can ease the suffering in your mind.
avadhuta_gita::63.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that in your true nature, you have no family, friends, or foes. Recognizing this absence of real attachments shows that the mind’s suffering comes from false identification, not reality.
avadhuta_gita::63.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by conflicts and relationships, but beneath it all, your true self is untouched by these roles and pains.
avadhuta_gita::63.insight: It teaches you to question the reality of your attachments and see suffering as rooted in false identification.

avadhuta_gita::64.verse_sanskrit:
दिवा नक्तं न ते चित्तं उदयास्तमयौ न हि ।
विदेहस्य शरीरत्वं कल्पयन्ति कथं बुधाः ॥
avadhuta_gita::64.verse_hindi: तेरे चेतन में दिन और रात्रि नहीं है न उदय और अस्त ही है। जो विदेह है (जिसका कोई शरीर नहीं है) उसमें बुद्धिमान लोग शरीर की कैसे कल्पना करते हैं।
avadhuta_gita::64.english_translation: In your consciousness there is no day or night, no sunrise or sunset; how do the wise imagine a body in the bodiless?
avadhuta_gita::64.translation_literal: दिवा (day) / न (not) / न (not) / ते (your) / चित्तं (consciousness) / उदय (rise) / अस्तमयौ (set) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / विदेहस्य (of the bodiless) / शरीरत्वं (bodily-ness) / कल्पयन्ति (imagine) / कथं (how) / बुधाः (wise ones)
avadhuta_gita::64.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::64.essence: Your true self is timeless and formless beyond all cycles of time and body.
avadhuta_gita::64.simple_meaning: Your true awareness is beyond day and night, beyond rising and setting. The wise understand that the true self has no body.
avadhuta_gita::64.simple_insight: You are not limited by time or form, even when appearances suggest otherwise.
avadhuta_gita::64.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that true consciousness transcends all dualities like day and night or sunrise and sunset. Wise people see that the true self is beyond any body, which is only an appearance.
avadhuta_gita::64.modern_relevance: When you feel trapped by the passing hours or your physical limits, remember your core awareness is timeless and bodiless.
avadhuta_gita::64.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with physical form and time to recognizing your timeless, formless nature.

avadhuta_gita::65.verse_sanskrit:
नाविभक्तं विभक्तं च न हि दुःखसुखादि च ।
न हि सर्वमसर्वं च विद्धि चात्मानमव्ययम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::65.verse_hindi: आत्मा न तो विभाग वाला है न विभाग रहित हैं। और न सुख-दु:ख आदि वाला ही है, न यह सर्व है और न असर्व है और आत्मा को तू नाश रहित जान।
avadhuta_gita::65.english_translation: The true self is neither divided nor undivided; it is neither pleasure nor pain, neither all nor none, and is indestructible.
avadhuta_gita::65.translation_literal: नाविभक्तं (not divided) / विभक्तं (divided) / च (and) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / दुःखसुखादि (pain-pleasure etc.) / च (and) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / सर्वमसर्वं (all-none) / च (and) / विद्धि (know) / चात्मानम् (the self) / अव्ययम् (indestructible)
avadhuta_gita::65.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::65.essence: The true self is indivisible, beyond all dualities, and indestructible.
avadhuta_gita::65.simple_meaning: Your true self cannot be split into parts or limited by feelings like pain or pleasure. It is always complete and cannot be destroyed.
avadhuta_gita::65.simple_insight: There’s peace in knowing your true self remains unchanged beyond all experiences.
avadhuta_gita::65.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals that the true self is beyond all dualities like division and unity, pleasure and pain, existence and non-existence. It is eternal and unbreakable, untouched by the changing world around it.
avadhuta_gita::65.modern_relevance: When your feelings shift wildly between joy and pain, remember your core remains undivided and steady beneath it all.
avadhuta_gita::65.insight: It shifts your perspective from identifying with temporary states to recognizing your unchanging essence.

avadhuta_gita::66.verse_sanskrit:
नाहं कर्ता न भोक्ता च न मे कर्म पुराऽधुना ।
न मे देहो विदेहो वा निर्ममेति ममेति किम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::66.verse_hindi: मैं कर्ता नहीं हूँ और भोक्ता भी नहीं हूँ, मेरे पूर्व और वर्तमान के कर्म भी नहीं हैं। मेरा शरीर नहीं है अथवा बिना शरीर के भी नहीं हूँ। मैं ममता से रहित और ममता वाला कैसे हो सकता हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::66.english_translation: I am neither the doer nor the enjoyer; I have no past or present actions. I am neither embodied nor disembodied. How can I both lack attachment and possess it?
avadhuta_gita::66.translation_literal: नाहं (I am not) कर्ता (doer) न (nor) भोक्ता (enjoyer) च (also) न (not) मे (my) कर्म (actions) पुरा- (past) अधुना (present). न (not) मे (my) देहो (body) विदेहो (without body) वा (or) निर्ममेति (without attachment) ममेति (with attachment) किम् (how).
avadhuta_gita::66.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::66.essence: You are beyond doing, enjoying, body, and attachment simultaneously.
avadhuta_gita::66.simple_meaning: You are not the person who acts or who enjoys the outcomes. You transcend body and attachment.
avadhuta_gita::66.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing you are not limited by actions, body, or desires.
avadhuta_gita::66.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the true self is neither the agent of action nor the recipient of its fruits. He transcends physical form and the duality of attachment and non-attachment, revealing the nature of ultimate freedom.
avadhuta_gita::66.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your roles and desires, remember you are more than what you do or feel.
avadhuta_gita::66.insight: It shifts your identity from the restless doer and sufferer to the unchanging true self beyond all actions and attachments.

avadhuta_gita::67.verse_sanskrit:
न मे रागादिको दोषो दुःखं देहादिकं न मे ।
आत्मानं विद्धि मामेकं विशालं गगनोपमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::67.verse_hindi: ये रागादिक दोष मेरे नहीं हैं, शरीर के दु:ख आदि भी मेरे नहीं हैं। मुझे एक ही आत्म रूप एवं विशाल आकाश के समान तू जान।
avadhuta_gita::67.english_translation: I have no faults like attachment; pain and body are not mine. Know me as the one self, vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::67.translation_literal:
न (not) मे (my) रागादि (attachment and others) दोषो (fault) दुःखं (pain) देहादिकं (body etc.) न (not) मे (my) ।
आत्मानं (self) विद्धि (know) मामेकं (me one) विशालं (vast) गगनोपमम् (like sky) ॥
avadhuta_gita::67.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::67.essence: You are vast, one true self beyond fault, attachment, and pain.
avadhuta_gita::67.simple_meaning: You are not your attachments, faults, pain, or body. Your true nature is one and vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::67.simple_insight: You can feel free from blame and suffering by recognizing your vast true self.
avadhuta_gita::67.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares freedom from faults like attachment and pain that belong to the body. He invites you to recognize your one true self, immense and boundless like the sky, beyond all limitations.
avadhuta_gita::67.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by pain or blame yourself for faults, remember you are more than these passing experiences—vast and free.
avadhuta_gita::67.insight: Shift your identity from temporary flaws and pain to recognizing your boundless true self.

avadhuta_gita::68.verse_sanskrit:
सखे मनः किं बहुजल्पितेन
सखे मनः सर्वमिदं वितर्क्यम् ।
यत्सारभूतं कथितं मया ते
त्वमेव तत्त्वं गगनोपमोऽसि ॥
avadhuta_gita::68.verse_hindi: हे सखे मन ! बहुत कहने से क्या प्रयोजन है, हे सखे मन! यह सम्पूर्ण जगत तर्क करने योग्य है। जो सारभूत था उसे मैंने तुझे कह दिया कि तू ही एक तत्त्व ब्रह्म है जो आकाश के समान निर्लेप, असंग व व्यापक है।
avadhuta_gita::68.english_translation: Friend mind, what is the use of much talk? This whole world is subject to reasoning. I have told you the essence: you alone are the truth, like the sky—detached, uninvolved, and vast.
avadhuta_gita::68.translation_literal: सखे (friend) मनः (mind) किं (what) बहुजल्पितेन (by much talking) सखे (friend) मनः (mind) सर्वमिदं (all this) वितर्क्यम् (subject to reasoning) यत्सारभूतं (what is essence) कथितं (told) मया (by me) ते (to you) त्वमेव (you alone) तत्त्वं (truth) गगनोपमोऽसि (are like the sky)
avadhuta_gita::68.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::68.essence: You are the vast, detached truth beyond all mental chatter and reasoning.
avadhuta_gita::68.simple_meaning: The restless mind is told that the entire world can be reasoned about, but at its core, you are the true reality—vast, detached, and all-encompassing like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::68.simple_insight: You can rest knowing your true self is vast, free, and beyond endless talk.
