avadhuta_gita::68.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya addresses the restless mind as a friend, pointing out that endless chatter has no real value. He reveals that beneath all reasoning and appearances lies the true self, vast and detached like the sky, free from involvement and limitation.
avadhuta_gita::68.modern_relevance: When your mind floods with endless thoughts and worries, remember your true nature is vast and unaffected, like the open sky beyond all noise.
avadhuta_gita::68.insight: It teaches you to see beyond mental chatter and recognize your true self as vast, free, and uninvolved.

avadhuta_gita::69.verse_sanskrit:
येन केनापि भावेन यत्र कुत्र मृता अपि ।
योगिनस्तत्र लीयन्ते घटाकाशमिवाम्बरे ॥
avadhuta_gita::69.verse_hindi: जिस किसी भी भाव से योगी (ज्ञानी) को जहाँ कहीं भी मरण होता है वह वहीं ब्रह्म में उसी प्रकार लीन हो जाता है जैसे घटाकाश महाकाश में लीन होता है।
avadhuta_gita::69.english_translation: Whatever the state, wherever a yogi dies, they merge into the supreme reality like a pot dissolves into space.
avadhuta_gita::69.translation_literal: येन (by which) केनापि (any) भावेन (state) यत्र (where) कुत्र (wherever) मृता (dies) अपि (also) । योगिनः (yogis) तत्र (there) लीयन्ते (are dissolved) घटा-काशम् (pot-space) इव (like) अम्बरे (in the sky) ॥
avadhuta_gita::69.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::69.essence: A realized being’s death is a seamless merging into infinite reality, beyond form and place.
avadhuta_gita::69.simple_meaning: No matter the state or place of passing, a realized person merges into the supreme reality just as a pot dissolves into the sky.
avadhuta_gita::69.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing that your true nature remains untouched and unseparated beyond death.
avadhuta_gita::69.detailed_meaning: The sage Dattatreya teaches that when a yogi dies, their individual existence dissolves completely into the supreme reality, just as a pot loses its form when merged into the sky. This verse shows the ultimate unity beyond form and place.
avadhuta_gita::69.modern_relevance: When facing loss or change, you can find comfort knowing your essence is always part of something vast and unchanging.
avadhuta_gita::69.insight: It shifts your view from fearing death to seeing it as a natural return to boundless reality.

avadhuta_gita::70.verse_sanskrit:
तीर्थे चान्त्यजगेहे वा नष्टस्मृतिरपि त्यजन् ।
समकाले तनुं मुक्तः कैवल्यव्यापको भवेत् ॥
avadhuta_gita::70.verse_hindi: ज्ञानवान पुरुष (जीवन्मुक्त) तीर्थ में अथवा चाण्डाल के घर में बेहोश हुआ भी, समकाल में शरीर को त्याग कर भी मुक्त हुआ व्यापक ब्रह्मरूप हो जाता है।
avadhuta_gita::70.english_translation: A wise person who loses memory, even if unconscious in a holy place or a lowly home, becomes liberated at once by leaving the body and is pervaded by the supreme reality.
avadhuta_gita::70.translation_literal: तीर्थे (in a holy place) / च (or) / अन्त्यजगेहे (in a lowly home) / वा (also) / नष्टस्मृतिः (lost memory) / अपि (even) / त्यजन् (leaving) / समकाले (at the same time) / तनुं (the body) / मुक्तः (liberated) / कैवल्यव्यापको (pervaded by supreme freedom) / भवेत् (becomes).
avadhuta_gita::70.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::70.essence: True freedom arises instantly beyond mind, memory, or place upon leaving the body.
avadhuta_gita::70.simple_meaning: Even if your mind forgets everything or you are unconscious anywhere, leaving the body frees you instantly and reveals your true nature.
avadhuta_gita::70.simple_insight: Freedom is not limited by your memory or surroundings—it is immediate and all-pervading.
avadhuta_gita::70.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that a wise liberated being loses all mental limitations like memory, and even if unconscious in a sacred or lowly place, upon leaving the body instantly merges with the all-pervading supreme reality.
avadhuta_gita::70.modern_relevance: You might feel lost or disconnected in unfamiliar places or during moments of confusion, yet your essential freedom and true self remain untouched and always accessible.
avadhuta_gita::70.insight: It shifts your view from needing mental clarity or ideal conditions to recognizing freedom as an ever-present state beyond circumstances.

avadhuta_gita::71.verse_sanskrit:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षांश्च द्विपदादिचराचरम् ।
मन्यन्ते योगिनः सर्वं मरीचिजलसन्निभम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::71.verse_hindi: धर्म, अर्थ, काम और मोक्ष तथा द्विपद आदि जितने स्थावर एवं जंगम जीव हैं, ज्ञानी लोग इन्हें मृगतृष्णा के जल के समान मानते हैं।
avadhuta_gita::71.english_translation: The wise see all things—dharma, wealth, desire, freedom, and all beings, moving or still—as like a mirage's water.
avadhuta_gita::71.translation_literal: धर्म (dharma) / अर्थ (wealth) / काम (desire) / मोक्षांश्च (and freedom) / द्विपदादि (two-footed and so on) / चराचरम् (moving and still) / मन्यन्ते (consider) / योगिनः (the wise) / सर्वं (all) / मरीचिजलसन्निभम् (like mirage-water)
avadhuta_gita::71.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::71.essence: All pursuits and beings appear real but are ultimately illusory like mirage water.
avadhuta_gita::71.simple_meaning: Everything people seek—duty, money, desires, freedom, and all living beings—is like a mirage, an illusion that seems real but isn't.
avadhuta_gita::71.simple_insight: Recognizing life’s goals as illusions lightens your grip and frees your heart.
avadhuta_gita::71.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that all pursuits and beings, whether moving or still, are like mirage water—appearing real but ultimately empty. This teaching invites letting go of clinging to appearances.
avadhuta_gita::71.modern_relevance: You chase success, relationships, and comfort, but sometimes they feel elusive, like something you see but can't grasp.
avadhuta_gita::71.insight: It shifts your view from treating all goals as solid realities to seeing them as illusions not worth clinging to.

avadhuta_gita::72.verse_sanskrit:
अतीतानागतं कर्म वर्तमानं तथैव च ।
न करोमि न भुञ्जामि इति मे निश्चला मतिः ॥
avadhuta_gita::72.verse_hindi: भूत, भविष्यत् तथा वर्तमान कर्मों को भी मैं नहीं करता हूँ न इनके फलों को ही भोगता हूँ। इस प्रकार मेरी स्थिर बुद्धि है।
avadhuta_gita::72.english_translation: I neither perform past, future, nor present actions, nor do I enjoy their results; such is my steady mind.
avadhuta_gita::72.translation_literal: अतीतानागतं (past and future) / कर्म (actions) / वर्तमानं (present) / तथैव (also) / च (and) / न (not) / करोमि (I do) / न (nor) / भुञ्जामि (I enjoy) / इति (thus) / मे (my) / निश्चला (steady) / मतिः (mind)
avadhuta_gita::72.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::72.essence: A steady mind neither acts nor enjoys any actions from past, present, or future.
avadhuta_gita::72.simple_meaning: You neither do nor enjoy any actions from past, present, or future because your mind remains steady and unmoved.
avadhuta_gita::72.simple_insight: There is peace in not being pulled by any action or its results across time.
avadhuta_gita::72.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he does not engage in any actions from past, present, or future, nor does he experience their results because his mind is unwavering. This reflects a state beyond the usual cycles of doing and reaping.
avadhuta_gita::72.modern_relevance: You notice how your mind clings to past mistakes or future worries; this steadiness frees you from those chains.
avadhuta_gita::72.insight: It teaches you to hold your attention steady, detaching from the cycle of acting and expecting results across time.

avadhuta_gita::73.verse_sanskrit:
शून्यागारे समरसपूत-
स्तिष्ठन्नेकः सुखमवधूतः ।
चरति हि नग्नस्त्यक्त्वा गर्वं
विन्दति केवलमात्मनि सर्वम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::73.verse_hindi: शून्य मन्दिर में समता रूपी रस से पवित्र हुआ अवधूत (संन्यासी) अकेला ही सुखपूर्वक रहता है। अहंकार का त्याग करके नग्न ही विचरण करता है तथा केवल आत्मा में ही सबको जानता है।
avadhuta_gita::73.english_translation: The Avadhuta, purified by the essence of equanimity, dwells alone in the empty temple; having abandoned pride, he wanders naked, knowing everything only in the true self.
avadhuta_gita::73.translation_literal: शून्यागारे (in the empty temple) / समरसपूत- (purified by the essence of equanimity) / तिष्ठन्नेकः (dwelling alone) / सुखमवधूतः (the blissful Avadhuta) / चरति (wanders) / हि (indeed) / नग्नः (naked) / त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) / गर्वं (pride) / विन्दति (knows) / केवलम् (only) / आत्मनि (in the true self) / सर्वम् (all).
avadhuta_gita::73.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::73.essence: Abandoning pride and solitude reveal complete knowing in the true self alone.
avadhuta_gita::73.simple_meaning: Living alone in emptiness, free of pride, you find joy by knowing only your true self.
avadhuta_gita::73.simple_insight: Freedom grows when you let go of pride and rest in your true self alone.
avadhuta_gita::73.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the Avadhuta as one who dwells alone in an empty, silent place, purified by equanimity. He has shed pride and social masks, wandering naked and knowing all through the awareness of the true self.
avadhuta_gita::73.modern_relevance: You walk through life stripped of ego and pretense, feeling peaceful and self-knowing even in solitude.
avadhuta_gita::73.insight: It teaches you to release pride and social identity to rest fully in your true self's knowing.

avadhuta_gita::74.verse_sanskrit:
त्रितयतुरीयं नहि नहि यत्र
विन्दति केवलमात्मनि तत्र ।
धर्माधर्मौ नहि नहि यत्र
बद्धो मुक्तः कथमिह तत्र ॥
avadhuta_gita::74.verse_hindi: जहाँ तुरीय आदि तीनों अवस्थाएँ नहीं हैं, वहाँ केवल आत्मा को ही जानता है। जहाँ धर्म और अधर्म भी नहीं है। वहाँ बद्ध और मुक्त का व्यवहार भी कैसे हो सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::74.english_translation: Where the three states, including the fourth, do not exist, only the true self is found; where right and wrong do not exist, bondage and freedom cannot occur there.
avadhuta_gita::74.translation_literal: त्रितयतुरीयं (three states including the fourth) / नहि (not) / नहि (not) / यत्र (where) / विंदति (finds) / केवलम् (only) / आत्मनि (in the true self) / तत्र (there) / धर्माधर्मौ (right and wrong) / नहि (not) / नहि (not) / यत्र (where) / बद्धो (bound) / मुक्तः (free) / कथमिह (how here) / तत्र (there)
avadhuta_gita::74.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::74.essence: True self is beyond all states, judgments, and the duality of bondage and freedom.
avadhuta_gita::74.simple_meaning: You exist beyond all mental and worldly states like waking, dreaming, or deep sleep. Beyond right and wrong, there is only the true self where no bondage or freedom applies.
avadhuta_gita::74.simple_insight: You are not limited by any condition or judgment; your true self is free and untouched.
avadhuta_gita::74.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes a reality beyond all three common states of consciousness and the fourth state (turiya). In that place, distinctions like right and wrong disappear, and the ideas of being bound or free have no meaning, revealing the true self alone remains.
avadhuta_gita::74.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by decisions or labels, you can find peace by remembering your true self is beyond all categories and judgments.
avadhuta_gita::74.insight: It teaches you to see yourself beyond mental states and moral labels, recognizing your essential freedom.

avadhuta_gita::75.verse_sanskrit:
विन्दति विन्दति नहि नहि मन्त्रं
छन्दोलक्षणं नहि नहि तन्त्रम् ।
समरसमग्नो भावितपूतः
प्रलपितमेतत्परमवधूतः ॥
avadhuta_gita::75.verse_hindi: चित्त से शुद्ध हुआ आत्मरस में मग्न अवधूत किसी मन्त्र को नहीं जानता है, न किसी छन्द के रूप व तन्त्र को ही जानता है। यह केवल परब्रह्म का ही कथन करता है।
avadhuta_gita::75.english_translation: The purified Avadhuta immersed in the essence of the true self knows no mantra, no meter, no sacred text; he only speaks of the supreme reality.
avadhuta_gita::75.translation_literal: विन्दति (finds) / विन्दति (finds) / नहि (not) / नहि (not) / मन्त्रं (mantra) / छन्दोलक्षणं (metrical form) / नहि (not) / नहि (not) / तन्त्रम् (sacred text) / समरसमग्नो (immersed in the essence) / भावितपूतः (pure in inner state) / प्रलपितमेतत्परमवधूतः (speaks this supreme Avadhuta)
avadhuta_gita::75.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::75.essence: True knowing transcends all mantras, meters, and sacred texts.
avadhuta_gita::75.simple_meaning: When you are fully pure and immersed in your true self, you don’t rely on mantras, rhythms, or scriptures; you speak only the supreme truth.
avadhuta_gita::75.simple_insight: There’s freedom in realizing that the deepest knowing doesn’t depend on words or rituals.
avadhuta_gita::75.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the Avadhuta who is purified in mind and immersed in the essence of the true self transcends all external practices like mantras, poetic meters, or sacred texts, focusing solely on the ultimate reality.
avadhuta_gita::75.modern_relevance: You’ve tried following all the rules, formulas, and instructions, but real clarity comes when you drop all that and just connect with your own pure being.
avadhuta_gita::75.insight: It shifts focus from external methods to direct experience of the supreme reality within you.

avadhuta_gita::76.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वशून्यमशून्यं च सत्यासत्यं न विद्यते ।
स्वभावभावतः प्रोक्तं शास्त्रसंवित्तिपूर्वकम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::76.verse_hindi: शास्त्रों ने ज्ञानपूर्वक कहा है कि यह सम्पूर्ण जगत शून्यरूप है और ब्रह्म ही अशून्य है। वह स्वभाव से ही भावरूप है। उसमें सत्य और असत्य भी नहीं है।
avadhuta_gita::76.english_translation: The scriptures wisely say that the entire world is void, and the supreme reality is beyond void; by nature, it is pure existence without truth or falsehood.
avadhuta_gita::76.translation_literal: सर्वशून्यमशून्यं (all void - not void) / च (and) / सत्यासत्यं (true-false) / न (not) / विद्यते (exists) / स्वभावभावतः (by nature, by essence) / प्रोक्तं (spoken) / शास्त्रसंवित्तिपूर्वकम् (by scriptures with knowledge)
avadhuta_gita::76.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::76.essence: The true self transcends emptiness and the distinction between truth and falsehood.
avadhuta_gita::76.simple_meaning: All that appears is empty and without true existence; the true self is naturally beyond all opposites like truth and falsehood.
avadhuta_gita::76.simple_insight: You can rest knowing your true self is untouched by what seems real or unreal.
avadhuta_gita::76.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals that according to the scriptures, the whole universe is empty of lasting reality, while the true self is by nature beyond emptiness, beyond the categories of true or false, untouched by appearances.
avadhuta_gita::76.modern_relevance: When your mind wavers between what’s right or wrong, remember your core is beyond these judgments and remains unchanged.
avadhuta_gita::76.insight: It shifts your view from clinging to appearances as real to recognizing your true nature beyond all dualities.

avadhuta_gita::77.verse_sanskrit:
बालस्य वा विषयभोगरतस्य वापि
मूर्खस्य सेवकजनस्य गृहस्थितस्य ।
एतद्गुरोः किमपि नैव न चिन्तनीयं
रत्नं कथं त्यजति कोऽप्यशुचौ प्रविष्टम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::77.verse_hindi: इन गुरुओं को बालक का अथवा विषयभोग में रहकर मूर्ख का, सेवक जन का, गृहस्थी का चिन्तन नहीं करना चाहिए (क्योंकि) अपवित्र वस्तु में गिरे हुए रत्न को कोई भी किस प्रकार छोड़ देता है।
avadhuta_gita::77.english_translation: A true teacher should not be concerned with the childlike, pleasure-seeking, foolish, servant, or household-bound states, just as no one abandons a gem fallen into impurity.
avadhuta_gita::77.translation_literal: बालस्य (of a child) / वा (or) / विषयभोगरतस्य (engaged in sensual pleasures) / वापि (also) मूर्खस्य (of a fool) / सेवकजनस्य (of a servant) / गृहस्थितस्य (of one settled in household) । एतद्गुरोः (of this teacher) / किमपि (anything) / नैव (never) / न (not) / चिन्तनीयं (to be considered) / रत्नं (a jewel) / कथं (how) / त्यजति (abandons) / कोऽपि (anyone) / अशुचौ (impure) / प्रविष्टम् (fallen into) ॥
avadhuta_gita::77.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::77.essence: The true self remains priceless despite appearing caught in foolish or distracted states.
avadhuta_gita::77.simple_meaning: A real teacher does not worry about childish or foolish states because the true self is like a jewel that remains valuable even if surrounded by impurity.
avadhuta_gita::77.simple_insight: You are precious and unchanged, no matter how distracted or confused you feel.
avadhuta_gita::77.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that a true teacher does not fixate on the temporary, childish, or limited states of mind. Like a jewel that remains precious even if covered in dirt, the true self is never devalued by external distractions or impurity.
avadhuta_gita::77.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by distractions or confusion, remember your core worth is untarnished, just like a gem remains valuable despite dirt around it.
avadhuta_gita::77.insight: It teaches you to look past surface confusion and recognize the enduring value of your true self.

avadhuta_gita::78.verse_sanskrit:
नैवात्र काव्यगुण एव तु चिन्तनीयो
ग्राह्यः परं गुणवता खलु सार एव ।
सिन्दूरचित्ररहिता भुवि रूपशून्या
पारं न किं नयति नौरिह गन्तुकामान् ॥
avadhuta_gita::78.verse_hindi: यहाँ (ज्ञान प्राप्ति में) काव्य गुण (विद्वता) का ही चिन्तन नहीं करना चाहिए, निश्चय ही गुणगान से परम सार वस्तु ही ग्रहण करनी चाहिए। इस संसार में नदी पार जाने की कामना वालों को क्या सिन्दूर की चित्रकारी से रहित रूप से शून्य नाव पार नहीं लगाती है।
avadhuta_gita::78.english_translation: Here, one should not contemplate just poetic qualities but grasp the ultimate essence; a boatless crossing cannot be aided by mere painted colors.
avadhuta_gita::78.translation_literal: नैवात्र (here not) काव्यगुण (poetic qualities) एव (only) तु (but) चिन्तनीयो (to be contemplated) ग्राह्यः (to be grasped) परं (ultimate) गुणवता (by qualities) खलु (indeed) सार (essence) एव (only) । सिन्दूरचित्ररहिता (without vermilion painting) भुवि (on earth) रूपशून्या (formless) पारं (to the beyond) न (not) किं (what) नयति (leads) नौरिह (without a boat) गन्तुकामान् (those desiring to cross) ॥
avadhuta_gita::78.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::78.essence: Surface beauty cannot replace the real means to cross beyond illusions.
avadhuta_gita::78.simple_meaning: Don’t get caught up admiring poetic qualities; focus on understanding the ultimate truth that truly helps you cross beyond illusions.
avadhuta_gita::78.simple_insight: You feel the need to seek what truly helps, not just pretty distractions.
avadhuta_gita::78.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya advises that during the quest for knowledge, admiring mere poetic skill or surface qualities won’t help; only the real essence guides those seeking to cross worldly illusions.
avadhuta_gita::78.modern_relevance: You scroll through inspiring quotes but realize only genuine insight helps you move forward, not just beautiful words.
avadhuta_gita::78.insight: It teaches you to distinguish between surface charm and deep substance in your search for understanding.

avadhuta_gita::79.verse_sanskrit:
प्रयत्नेन विना येन निश्चलेन चलाचलम् ।
ग्रस्तं स्वभावतः शान्तं चैतन्यं गगनोपमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::79.verse_hindi: जिस निश्चल (ब्रह्म) से बिना ही प्रयत्न के यह चल एवं अचल ग्रस्त है वह (ब्रह्म) स्वभाव से ही शान्त एवं गगन के सदृश है।
avadhuta_gita::79.english_translation: The supreme reality, naturally still and like the sky, is effortlessly present in both the moving and unmoving.
avadhuta_gita::79.translation_literal: प्रयत्नेन (by effort) विना (without) येन (by which) निश्चलेन (immovable) चलाचलम् (moving and unmoving) । ग्रस्तं (pervading) स्वभावतः (by nature) शान्तं (peaceful) चैतन्यं (consciousness) गगनोपमम् (like the sky) ॥
avadhuta_gita::79.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::79.essence: Effortless stillness underlies and embraces all movement and change.
avadhuta_gita::79.simple_meaning: The true self is naturally peaceful and steady, effortlessly present in everything that moves and doesn't move.
avadhuta_gita::79.simple_insight: You can feel calm knowing your deepest nature does not struggle but holds all experiences peacefully.
avadhuta_gita::79.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals that the supreme reality is like the vast sky—calm and stable by nature—and it pervades all things, moving or still, without effort or disturbance.
avadhuta_gita::79.modern_relevance: When your mind races or feels stuck, remember your natural state is calm and steady, holding all changes without strain.
avadhuta_gita::79.insight: Recognize that your true nature is effortless steadiness beneath all mental activity and life’s flux.

avadhuta_gita::80.verse_sanskrit:
अयत्नाछालयेद्यस्तु एकमेव चराचरम् ।
सर्वगं तत्कथं भिन्नमद्वैतं वर्तते मम ॥
avadhuta_gita::80.verse_hindi: फिर जो एक ही (ब्रह्म) समस्त चर एवं अचर जगत को बिना ही प्रयत्न के चलायमान करता है। वह सर्वगत है। फिर मझसे भिन्न अद्वैत रूप होकर कैसे वर्तता है।
avadhuta_gita::80.english_translation: The one who effortlessly moves the entire moving and unmoving world is all-pervading; how then can non-duality be separate from me?
avadhuta_gita::80.translation_literal: अयत्नाच (without effort) आलयेत् (moves) यः (who) तु (indeed) एकमेव (only one) चराचरम् (moving and unmoving) सर्वगं (all-pervading) तत् (that) कथं (how) भिन्नम् (separate) अद्वैतं (non-duality) वर्तते (exists) मम (in me)
avadhuta_gita::80.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::80.essence: You and all that moves are one effortless, all-pervading presence.
avadhuta_gita::80.simple_meaning: Everything moving and still flows effortlessly through one presence that fills all; separation from this oneness cannot truly exist.
avadhuta_gita::80.simple_insight: You feel the relief of knowing you are inseparably connected to all that moves and rests.
avadhuta_gita::80.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals that the supreme presence moves both the moving and unmoving without any effort. Since this presence is everywhere, the idea that non-duality could be separate from the self is impossible.
avadhuta_gita::80.modern_relevance: When you pause and notice, you see how effortlessly life flows through you and everything around, dissolving the sense of separation.
avadhuta_gita::80.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as separate to recognizing the seamless oneness moving all things effortlessly.

avadhuta_gita::81.verse_sanskrit:
अहमेव परं यस्मात्सारात्सारतरं शिवम् ।
गमागमविनिर्मुक्तं निर्विकल्पं निराकुलम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::81.verse_hindi: मैं ही जिससे सूक्ष्म हूँ, सार असार से रहित कल्याण स्वरूप हूँ, गमन आगमन से रहित हूँ, निर्विकल्प तथा कुल से रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::81.english_translation: I am the supreme beyond the subtle, the essence beyond all essence, pure welfare; free from coming and going, beyond all distinctions and agitation.
avadhuta_gita::81.translation_literal: अहमेव (I myself) / परं (supreme) / यस्मात् (because) / सारात् (than essence) / सारतरं (more than the most subtle essence) / शिवम् (auspicious, welfare) / गमागमविनिर्मुक्तं (free from coming and going) / निर्विकल्पं (without distinctions) / निराकुलम् (without agitation)
avadhuta_gita::81.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::81.essence: You are the changeless essence beyond all movement and disturbance.
avadhuta_gita::81.simple_meaning: You are the highest reality beyond all subtle forms and changes, free from any disturbance or movement.
avadhuta_gita::81.simple_insight: Recognizing your unchanging essence brings deep calm and freedom from life’s ups and downs.
avadhuta_gita::81.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the true self is beyond the finest distinctions and changes, untouched by movement or mental agitation, embodying pure welfare and stability beyond all dualities.
avadhuta_gita::81.modern_relevance: When your thoughts race or life feels chaotic, remember your true self remains peaceful and steady beyond all fluctuations.
avadhuta_gita::81.insight: It teaches you to identify with the unchanging, silent essence beyond all mental and physical movement.

avadhuta_gita::82.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वावयवनिर्मुक्तं तथाहं त्रिदशार्चितम् ।
सम्पूर्णत्वान्न गृह्णामि विभागं त्रिदशादिकम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::82.verse_hindi: सो मैं सम्पूर्ण अवयवों से रहित हूँ, देवताओं द्वारा भी पूजित हूँ। सम्पूर्ण होने से देवताओं के विभाग को भी ग्रहण नहीं करता हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::82.english_translation: I am free from all parts, worshipped by the three realms; being complete, I do not accept division into any realms.
avadhuta_gita::82.translation_literal: सर्वा (all) अवयव (parts) निर्मुक्तं (free) तथा (thus) अहं (I) त्रिदश (three realms) अर्चितम् (worshipped) । सम्पूर्णत्वात् (because of completeness) न (not) गृह्णामि (accept) विभागं (division) त्रिदशादिकम् (of three realms etc.) ॥
avadhuta_gita::82.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::82.essence: You are whole and beyond any division into parts or realms.
avadhuta_gita::82.simple_meaning: You are not made up of separate parts or divisions. You are complete and beyond all separate realms or categories.
avadhuta_gita::82.simple_insight: There is freedom and peace in seeing yourself as whole, not fragmented or limited.
avadhuta_gita::82.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he is beyond all physical and subtle parts and even revered by the three realms of divine beings. Yet, because he is completely whole, he does not identify with any division or category, transcending all distinctions.
avadhuta_gita::82.modern_relevance: When you feel fragmented by roles, labels, or expectations, remembering your completeness beyond parts brings calm and clarity.
avadhuta_gita::82.insight: This verse shifts your view from seeing yourself as fragmented to recognizing your essential unity and completeness.

avadhuta_gita::83.verse_sanskrit:
प्रमादेन न सन्देहः किं करिष्यामि वृत्तिमान् ।
उत्पद्यन्ते विलीयन्ते बुद्बुदाश्च यथा जले ॥
avadhuta_gita::83.verse_hindi: अन्त:करण की वृत्तियों को क्या प्रमादवश मैं उत्पन्न करता हूँ? ये जल में बुदबुदे के समान अपने आप ही उत्पन्न होती हैं तथा विलीन हो जाती हैं इसमें सन्देह नहीं है।
avadhuta_gita::83.english_translation: There is no doubt that I do not cause the inner fluctuations by carelessness; like bubbles in water, they arise and dissolve on their own.
avadhuta_gita::83.translation_literal: प्रमादेन (by carelessness) / न (not) / सन्देहः (doubt) / किं (what) / करिष्यामि (would I do) / वृत्तिमान् (fluctuations) / उत्पद्यन्ते (arise) / विलीयन्ते (dissolve) / बुद्बुदाः (bubbles) / यथा (like) / जले (in water)
avadhuta_gita::83.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::83.essence: Inner mental movements arise and dissolve naturally without your causing them.
avadhuta_gita::83.simple_meaning: Your inner mental movements are not caused by your carelessness. They arise and disappear naturally like bubbles in water.
avadhuta_gita::83.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing your restless thoughts are natural and not your fault.
avadhuta_gita::83.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that the restless waves of the inner mind are not caused by careless mistakes. Like bubbles that appear and vanish in water without effort, these mental fluctuations arise and dissolve on their own, beyond personal control.
avadhuta_gita::83.modern_relevance: Your mind jumps from one thought to another like bubbles in a stream. You don’t cause this; it happens naturally.
avadhuta_gita::83.insight: Recognize that mental restlessness is spontaneous, helping you stop blaming yourself for every thought.

avadhuta_gita::84.verse_sanskrit:
महदादीनि भूतानि समाप्यैवं सदैव हि ।
मृदुद्रव्येषु तीक्ष्णेषु गुडेषु कटुकेषु च ॥
avadhuta_gita::84.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार मृदु पदार्थों में मृदुता, तीक्ष्ण पदार्थों में तीक्ष्णता, गुड़ में मिठास एवं कटु पदार्थों में कटुता भिन्न नहीं है उसी प्रकार महतत्त्व आदि भूत पदार्थों की भिन्नता सदा से समाप्त करे।
avadhuta_gita::84.english_translation: Just as softness is never absent in soft substances, sharpness in sharp ones, sweetness in jaggery, and bitterness in bitter things, similarly the distinctions among the great elements and beings have always ceased.
avadhuta_gita::84.translation_literal: महदादीनि (great-elements and others) / भूतानि (beings) / समाप्यैवं (similarly ended) / सदैव (always) / हि (indeed) / मृदुद्रव्येषु (in soft substances) / तीक्ष्णेषु (in sharp ones) / गुडेषु (in jaggery) / कटुकेषु (in bitter things) / च (and)
avadhuta_gita::84.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::84.essence: Apparent differences among things are always resolved in their true unity.
avadhuta_gita::84.simple_meaning: Just as softness is always present in soft things, and bitterness always in bitter things, the apparent differences among great elements and beings have always ended.
avadhuta_gita::84.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that all apparent differences dissolve into one truth.
avadhuta_gita::84.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that qualities like softness or bitterness never change in their respective substances. Likewise, the seeming differences among fundamental elements and beings are ultimately unreal and have always ceased to exist.
avadhuta_gita::84.modern_relevance: When you notice how you label people or things as different, you can remember that beneath appearances, unity remains constant.
avadhuta_gita::84.insight: It teaches you to see beyond appearances and recognize the timeless unity behind diversity.

avadhuta_gita::85.verse_sanskrit:
कटुत्वं चैव शैत्यत्वं मृदुत्वं च यथा जले ।
प्रकृतिः पुरुषस्तद्वदभिन्नं प्रतिभाति मे ॥
avadhuta_gita::85.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार जल से उसकी शीतलता एवं कोमलता भिन्न नहीं हैं, मृदु पदार्थों में मृदुता, तीक्ष्ण पदार्थों में तीक्ष्णता, गुड़ में मिठास एवं कटु पदार्थों में कटुता भिन्न नहीं है वैसे ही मुझे तो प्रकृति और पुरुष भी अभिन्न ज्ञात होते हैं।
avadhuta_gita::85.english_translation: Just as water's coolness and softness are inseparable from itself, similarly, I perceive nature and pure awareness as inseparable.
avadhuta_gita::85.translation_literal: कटुत्वं (bitterness) चैव (also) शैत्यत्वं (coldness) मृदुत्वं (softness) च (and) यथा (just as) जले (in water) । प्रकृतिः (nature) पुरुषः (pure awareness) तद्वत् (like that) अभिन्नं (inseparable) प्रतिभाति (appears) मे (to me) ॥
avadhuta_gita::85.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::85.essence: The true self and nature are inseparably united like water and its qualities.
avadhuta_gita::85.simple_meaning: You see the true self and the natural world as inseparable, just like water's qualities cannot be separated from water itself.
avadhuta_gita::85.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing your true self is never separate from the world you live in.
avadhuta_gita::85.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that just as water cannot be separated from its coolness and softness, the true self (pure awareness) and nature are not two separate realities but one inseparable whole.
avadhuta_gita::85.modern_relevance: When you touch water and feel its coolness, you experience a unity that mirrors your own inseparability from the world around you.
avadhuta_gita::85.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as separate to recognizing the unity behind all appearances.

avadhuta_gita::86.verse_hindi: जो आत्मा सम्पूर्ण संज्ञा से रहित है, सूक्ष्म से भी अतिसूक्ष्म, श्रेष्ठ है, मन, बुद्धि तथा इन्द्रियों का विषय नहीं हैं, कलंक से रहित है, जगत का स्वामी है।
avadhuta_gita::86.english_translation: The true self is beyond all names, subtler than the subtlest, superior, beyond mind, intellect, and senses, free from all stains, and the master of the world.
avadhuta_gita::86.translation_literal: सर्वाख्यारहितं (beyond all names) यद्यत् (whatever) सूक्ष्मात् (than subtle) सूक्ष्मतरं (more subtle) परम् (supreme) मनोबुद्धीन्द्रियातीतम् (beyond mind, intellect, senses) अकलङ्कं (unstained) जगत्पतिम् (lord of the world)
avadhuta_gita::86.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::86.essence: The true self is beyond mind, senses, names, and is perfectly pure and sovereign.
avadhuta_gita::86.simple_meaning: You are the true self that no name can capture, finer than anything subtle, beyond mind, intellect, or senses, free from any flaw, and the ruler of all existence.
avadhuta_gita::86.simple_insight: There is a part of you untouched by thought or sense, perfectly pure and sovereign.
avadhuta_gita::86.detailed_meaning: The sage declares the true self beyond all labels and concepts. It is subtler than the subtlest things, beyond mental and sensory experience, without any impurity, and the ultimate controller of the universe, revealing the supreme nature of self beyond all appearances.
avadhuta_gita::86.modern_relevance: When thoughts overwhelm and senses pull you in all directions, remember the part of you that remains pure, untouched, and in control beneath it all.
avadhuta_gita::86.insight: Shift your attention from fluctuating mind and senses to the unchanging, pure self beneath them.

avadhuta_gita::87.verse_sanskrit:
ईदृशं सहजं यत्र अहं तत्र कथं भवेत् ।
त्वमेव हि कथं तत्र कथं तत्र चराचरम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::87.verse_hindi: इसी प्रकार के गुण जिसमें स्वभाव से विद्यमान हैं उसमें ‘मैं’ का कथन किस प्रकार बनता है, ‘तू’ का कथन भी कैसे बनता है, चर एवं अचर का कथन भी कैसे बनता है।
avadhuta_gita::87.english_translation: Where qualities are naturally present like this, how can there be saying 'I' there, how can there be saying 'you', how can there be saying 'moving and unmoving'?
avadhuta_gita::87.translation_literal: ईदृशं (such) सहजं (natural/spontaneous) यत्र (where) अहं (I) तत्र (there) कथं (how) भवेत् (can be) । त्वमेव (you indeed) हि (surely) कथं (how) तत्र (there) कथं (how) तत्र (there) चराचरम् (moving and unmoving) ॥
avadhuta_gita::87.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::87.essence: Without mental division, the separate self and other cannot exist.
avadhuta_gita::87.simple_meaning: When qualities and things exist naturally without separation, there is no real 'I' or 'you' or distinction of moving and unmoving.
avadhuta_gita::87.simple_insight: You feel the relief of no separation, no separate self or other, only one seamless reality.
avadhuta_gita::87.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points to a state where natural presence of qualities means no division into 'I' or 'you', or even between moving and unmoving things. The usual sense of separate identities dissolves into pure being.
avadhuta_gita::87.modern_relevance: In moments when you stop labeling yourself and others or things around you, you experience a natural flow without boundaries or conflict.
avadhuta_gita::87.insight: It teaches you to question the reality of separation and see that distinctions like 'I' and 'you' arise only from mental labels.

avadhuta_gita::88.verse_sanskrit:
गगनोपमं तु यत्प्रोक्तं तदेव गगनोपमम् ।
चैतन्यं दोषहीनं च सर्वज्ञं पूर्णमेव च ॥
avadhuta_gita::88.verse_hindi: जिसे आकाश से सदृश कहा गया है वह आकाश के सदृश ही है। वह चैतन्य, दोष से रहित, सर्वज्ञ और पूर्ण भी है।
avadhuta_gita::88.english_translation: What is described as like the sky is indeed like the sky—conscious, free of faults, all-knowing, and complete.
avadhuta_gita::88.translation_literal: गगनोपमं (like the sky) / तु (but) / यत्प्रोक्तं (that which is said) / तदेव (that indeed) / गगनोपमम् (like the sky) / चैतन्यं (consciousness) / दोषहीनं (without fault) / च (and) / सर्वज्ञं (all-knowing) / पूर्णमेव (indeed complete) / च (and)
avadhuta_gita::88.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::88.essence: Your true self is vast, flawless consciousness, fully complete like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::88.simple_meaning: Your true self is like the sky—vast, pure, fully aware, without faults, and completely whole.
avadhuta_gita::88.simple_insight: There is freedom and completeness in recognizing your true self as vast and flawless.
avadhuta_gita::88.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the true self is exactly like the sky—limitless, free of defects, fully conscious, all-knowing, and complete—revealing the non-dual essence beyond every limitation.
avadhuta_gita::88.modern_relevance: In moments when you feel small or flawed, remember your true nature is vast, clear, and untouched by mistakes.
avadhuta_gita::88.insight: It changes how you see yourself—from limited and flawed to expansive, pure, and fully aware.

avadhuta_gita::89.verse_sanskrit:
पृथिव्यां चरितं नैव मारुतेन च वाहितम् ।
वरिणा पिहितं नैव तेजोमध्ये व्यवस्थितम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::89.verse_hindi: वह पृथ्वी में गमन नहीं करता, हवा उसको ले नहीं जा सकती, जल उसको आच्छादित नहीं कर सकता, वह तेज के मध्य स्थित रहता है।
avadhuta_gita::89.english_translation: It does not move in the earth, nor is it carried by the wind, not covered by water; it abides in the midst of fire.
avadhuta_gita::89.translation_literal: पृथिव्यां (on the earth) / चरितं (moving) / नैव (not) / मारुतेन (by wind) / च (and) / वाहितम् (carried) / वरिणा (by water) / पिहितं (covered) / नैव (not) / तेजोमध्ये (in the midst of fire) / व्यवस्थितम् (situated)
avadhuta_gita::89.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::89.essence: Your true self remains steady and radiant, untouched by changing elements.
avadhuta_gita::89.simple_meaning: Your true self does not move or get carried away by earth, wind, or water; it stays steady in the midst of radiant fire.
avadhuta_gita::89.simple_insight: You can feel steady and untouched despite the forces around you.
avadhuta_gita::89.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the true self as unaffected by the elements—earth, wind, and water—emphasizing that it remains steady and radiant like fire at the core of existence.
avadhuta_gita::89.modern_relevance: When everything around you seems chaotic or changing, you can recognize a calm, unshakable center inside yourself that stays steady and bright.
avadhuta_gita::89.insight: This verse shifts your view from identifying with changing surroundings to recognizing your unchanging radiant core.

avadhuta_gita::90.verse_sanskrit:
आकाशं तेन संव्याप्तं न तद्व्याप्तं च केनचित् ।
स बाह्याभ्यन्तरं तिष्ठत्यवच्छिन्नं निरन्तरम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::90.verse_hindi: उस (ब्रह्म) से आकाश भी संव्याप्त है, वह किसी से व्याप्त नहीं है, वह बाहर और भीतर एकरस अनिच्छिन्न रूप से सर्वत्र स्थित है।
avadhuta_gita::90.english_translation: The supreme reality pervades the space yet is not limited by it; it exists everywhere, inside and outside, uninterrupted and uniform.
avadhuta_gita::90.translation_literal: आकाशं (space) तेन (by that) संव्याप्तं (pervaded) न (not) तद्व्याप्तं (limited by that) च (and) केनचित् (by anyone); स (he/it) बाह्याभ्यन्तरं (outside and inside) तिष्ठति (stands) अवच्छिन्नं (unbroken) निरन्तरम् (continuous).
avadhuta_gita::90.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::90.essence: The true self fills all space yet is beyond all confinement.
avadhuta_gita::90.simple_meaning: The true reality fills all space but is not limited by it; it is everywhere continuously, inside and outside.
avadhuta_gita::90.simple_insight: You are not confined by any boundary; you are always present and unbroken.
avadhuta_gita::90.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the supreme reality as pervading the entire space without being limited to it. It exists everywhere at once, inside and outside, continuously without break, revealing the non-dual nature of existence.
avadhuta_gita::90.modern_relevance: When you feel boxed in by your circumstances, remember your true nature is unlimited and present beyond all boundaries.
avadhuta_gita::90.insight: Recognize that your true self transcends all external and internal limits, revealing continuous presence everywhere.

avadhuta_gita::91.verse_sanskrit:
सूक्ष्मत्वात्तददृश्यत्वान्निर्गुणत्वाच्च योगिभिः ।
आलम्बनादि यत्प्रोक्तं क्रमादालम्बनं भवेत् ॥
avadhuta_gita::91.verse_hindi: योगियों ने जिसके आलम्बन आदि की बात कही है, वह आलम्बन क्रम से ही होता है क्योंकि वह ब्रह्म सूक्ष्म, अदृश्य एवं निर्गुण हैं।
avadhuta_gita::91.english_translation: The support spoken of by yogis arises sequentially because Brahman is subtle, invisible, and without qualities.
avadhuta_gita::91.translation_literal: सूक्ष्मत्वात्तत् (because of subtlety that) / अदृश्यत्वात् (because of invisibility) / निर्गुणत्वाच्च (and because of being without qualities) / योगिभिः (by yogis) / आलम्बनादि (support and so on) / यत् (that which) / प्रोक्तं (has been spoken) / क्रमात् (in sequence) / आलम्बनं (support) / भवेत् (arises).
avadhuta_gita::91.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::91.essence: Support from the supreme unfolds gradually because it is subtle and beyond senses.
avadhuta_gita::91.simple_meaning: Support or foundation described by yogis appears gradually because the supreme reality is subtle, invisible, and without qualities.
avadhuta_gita::91.simple_insight: There is a gentle unfolding in how deep support reveals itself beyond what we see.
avadhuta_gita::91.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the 'support' or foundation yogis talk about is not immediate or obvious. Because the supreme reality (Brahman) is subtle, invisible, and without qualities, the experience or realization of support happens in a gradual, ordered way.
avadhuta_gita::91.modern_relevance: Sometimes you expect quick answers or clear support, but deeper help arrives slowly, unfolding beyond what you can immediately see or name.
avadhuta_gita::91.insight: It teaches you to trust a gradual, often invisible process of support instead of demanding instant clarity or proof.

avadhuta_gita::92.verse_sanskrit:
सतताऽभ्यासयुक्तस्तु निरालम्बो यदा भवेत् ।
तल्लयाल्लीयते नान्तर्गुणदोषविवर्जितः ॥
avadhuta_gita::92.verse_hindi: जिस समय सतत अभ्यास से युक्त होकर जब चित्त निरालम्ब हो जाता है जब वह गुण दोष से रहित होता है उसी समय चित्त के लय होने से उसका ब्रह्म में लय हो जाता है। इसके बिना नहीं होता।
avadhuta_gita::92.english_translation: When the mind is constantly practiced and becomes unattached, free from qualities and faults, it dissolves into the supreme reality; nothing else enables this merging.
avadhuta_gita::92.translation_literal: सतताऽभ्यासयुक्तस्तु (constantly-practiced) / निरालम्बो (unattached) / यदा (when) / भवेत् (becomes) / तल्लयाल्लीयते (by its dissolution merges) / नान्तर्गुणदोषविवर्जितः (free from qualities and faults)
avadhuta_gita::92.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::92.essence: Steady practice frees the mind to dissolve and merge into the supreme reality.
avadhuta_gita::92.simple_meaning: When your mind is steady through practice and becomes free of attachments and faults, it naturally merges into the supreme reality.
avadhuta_gita::92.simple_insight: There is peace in steady practice that frees the mind to merge beyond its defects.
avadhuta_gita::92.detailed_meaning: The Avadhuta teaches that with constant disciplined practice, the mind becomes unattached and free of all qualities and faults. At that moment, the mind dissolves and merges completely into the supreme reality, a state that cannot be achieved otherwise.
avadhuta_gita::92.modern_relevance: After persistent effort to calm your restless thoughts, you find a moment when your mind stops clinging and merges into deep stillness.
avadhuta_gita::92.insight: It teaches you that consistent practice leads the mind to release all faults and merge with true stillness.

avadhuta_gita::93.verse_sanskrit:
विषविश्वस्य रौद्रस्य मोहमूर्च्छाप्रदस्य च ।
एकमेव विनाशाय ह्यमोघं सहजामृतम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::93.verse_hindi: यह विश्व रूपी विष बड़ा भयानक और मोह एवं मूर्छा को देने वाला है। इसके विनाश का एक ही अमोघ सहज अमृत (आत्म-ज्ञान) है।
avadhuta_gita::93.english_translation: The world, like a fierce poison, causes delusion and unconsciousness; its only destruction is the unfailing, innate nectar of self-knowledge.
avadhuta_gita::93.translation_literal: विषविश्वस्य (of the poison-world) रौद्रस्य (fierce) मोहमूर्छाप्रदस्य (causing delusion and unconsciousness) च (and) । एकमेव (the one alone) विनाशाय (for destruction) ह्यमोघं (unfailing) सहजामृतम् (innate nectar) ॥
avadhuta_gita::93.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::93.essence: The fierce poison of the world is undone only by innate self-knowledge.
avadhuta_gita::93.simple_meaning: The world acts like a dangerous poison that blinds and confuses you. Only the natural, unfailing knowledge of your true self can destroy this harmful effect.
avadhuta_gita::93.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that your inner true self is the lasting antidote to confusion.
avadhuta_gita::93.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares the world is like a fierce poison causing delusion and unconsciousness. This moment points to self-knowledge—the innate nectar that alone can destroy this confusion and reveal freedom.
avadhuta_gita::93.modern_relevance: When distractions and illusions overwhelm you, remember that clear self-knowledge is the steady remedy that never fails.
avadhuta_gita::93.insight: This verse shifts your focus from outer confusion to recognizing the natural, unfailing clarity within.

avadhuta_gita::94.verse_sanskrit:
भावगम्यं निराकारं साकारं दृष्टिगोचरम् ।
भावाभावविनिर्मुक्तमन्तरालं तदुच्यते ॥
avadhuta_gita::94.verse_hindi: निराकार ( ब्रह्म) को भाव (चित्त) से ही जाना जाता है तथा साकार दृष्टि का विषय है। जो भाव और अभाव से ही रहित है उसे अन्तराल कहा जाता है।
avadhuta_gita::94.english_translation: The formless (Brahman) is known through feeling (mind), and the form is perceived by sight. That which is free from both presence and absence is called the interval.
avadhuta_gita::94.translation_literal: भावगम्यं (felt/known through feeling) / निराकारं (formless) / साकारं (with form) / दृष्टिगोचरम् (visible to sight) / भावाभावविनिर्मुक्तम् (free from presence and absence) / अन्तरालं (interval) / तदुच्यते (that is called)
avadhuta_gita::94.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::94.essence: True reality transcends both sensory presence and absence, existing as a silent interval.
avadhuta_gita::94.simple_meaning: The supreme reality is sometimes formless and known through feeling, sometimes with form and seen by sight. Beyond both presence and absence lies a deeper state called the interval.
avadhuta_gita::94.simple_insight: You can sense a deeper reality that is neither here nor not here, beyond all senses.
avadhuta_gita::94.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains how the supreme reality is both formless, known by inner feeling, and with form, visible to the eyes. Yet, beyond these dualities of presence and absence, there is a deeper dimension called the interval, pointing to a reality beyond all appearances.
avadhuta_gita::94.modern_relevance: When you cannot find words or images to describe your experience, you are touching what is beyond both presence and absence.
avadhuta_gita::94.insight: It shifts your focus from what can be sensed to what lies beyond all sensory perception, opening a wider understanding.

avadhuta_gita::95.verse_sanskrit:
बाह्यभावं भवेद्विश्वमन्तः प्रकृतिरुच्यते ।
अन्तरादन्तरं ज्ञेयं नारिकेलफलाम्बुवत् ॥
avadhuta_gita::95.verse_hindi: बाहर जितना भी भाव पदार्थ है वह विश्व होता है। इसके भीतर को प्रकृति कहते हैं। इस अन्तर प्रकृति के भी भीतर (ब्रह्म) जानने योग्य हैं जैसे नारियल के फल के भीतर जल होता है।
avadhuta_gita::95.english_translation: Everything external is called the world; within it is nature, and within nature is the true self, like water inside a coconut.
avadhuta_gita::95.translation_literal: बाह्यभावं (external feeling) भवेद् (is) विश्वम् (the universe) अन्तः (inside) प्रकृति (nature) उच्यते (is called) । अन्तरादन्तरं (inside that inside) ज्ञेयं (to be known) नारिकेलफलाम्बुवत् (like coconut fruit water) ॥
avadhuta_gita::95.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::95.essence: The true self lies hidden within nature inside the external world.
avadhuta_gita::95.simple_meaning: The world is everything external. Inside it is nature, and inside nature is the true self, like water inside a coconut.
avadhuta_gita::95.simple_insight: There is a deep essence within all appearances, quietly waiting to be recognized.
avadhuta_gita::95.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that all the outer world is just surface. Inside that surface is nature, and deeper within nature is the true self, hidden but knowable, just like water inside a coconut fruit.
avadhuta_gita::95.modern_relevance: Like peeling a fruit to find juice inside, you can look beyond surface appearances to find your deeper true self.
avadhuta_gita::95.insight: It teaches you to look beyond visible reality to recognize the true self within nature and the world.

avadhuta_gita::96.verse_sanskrit:
भ्रान्तिज्ञानं स्थितं बाह्यं सम्यग्ज्ञानं च मध्यगम् ।
मध्यान्मध्यतरं ज्ञेयं नारिकेलफलाम्बुवत् ॥
avadhuta_gita::96.verse_hindi: बाहर स्थित ज्ञान भ्रान्ति रूप हैं, मध्य का ज्ञान यथार्थ ज्ञान है, मध्य के भी मध्य नारियल के फल के भीतर के जल के समान जानने योग्य है।
avadhuta_gita::96.english_translation: Ignorant knowledge exists outside; true knowledge is the middle; deeper still is what is known, like the water inside a coconut fruit.
avadhuta_gita::96.translation_literal: भ्रान्तिज्ञानं (ignorant knowledge) / स्थितं (situated) / बाह्यं (outside) / सम्यग्ज्ञानं (true knowledge) / च (and) / मध्यगम् (middle going) / मध्यान्मध्यतरं (middle of the middle) / ज्ञेयं (to be known) / नारिकेलफलाम्बुवत् (like the water of a coconut fruit)
avadhuta_gita::96.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::96.essence: True knowledge is layered; the deepest reality lies beneath surface appearances.
avadhuta_gita::96.simple_meaning: Surface-level understanding is confused; true understanding lies deeper, like water inside a coconut fruit, hidden beneath layers.
avadhuta_gita::96.simple_insight: There is calm in knowing the deepest truth is always beneath appearances.
avadhuta_gita::96.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes three levels of knowing: confused knowledge on the outside, real knowledge in the middle, and the deepest truth inside, like the hidden water inside a coconut fruit.
avadhuta_gita::96.modern_relevance: When you think you understand something, often you're only seeing the surface. Real insight requires looking deeper, beneath distractions and assumptions.
avadhuta_gita::96.insight: It teaches you to look beyond surface impressions and value the hidden, deeper truth beneath.

avadhuta_gita::97.verse_sanskrit:
पौर्णमास्यां यथा चन्द्र एक एवातिनिर्मलः ।
तेन तत्सदृशं पश्येद्द्विधादृष्टिर्विपर्ययः ॥
avadhuta_gita::97.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार पूर्णमासी में एक ही चन्द्रमा अति निर्मल होता है उसी प्रकार आत्मा को भी उसी के समान देखें। दृष्टि दोष से ही वह दो प्रकार का दिखाई देता है। यह दृष्टि भ्रम है।
avadhuta_gita::97.english_translation: Just as the full moon is one and perfectly pure, see the true self as the same; the mind's error makes it appear divided.
avadhuta_gita::97.translation_literal: पौर्णमास्यां (At full moon) / यथा (just as) / चन्द्र (moon) / एक (one) / एव (indeed) / अतिनिर्मलः (extremely pure) / तेन (by that) / तत्सदृशं (like that) / पश्येद् (see) / द्विधा (twofold) / दृष्टिः (vision) / विपर्ययः (error)
avadhuta_gita::97.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::97.essence: The true self is always whole; division arises only from mistaken perception.
avadhuta_gita::97.simple_meaning: Your true self is completely pure and one, but the restless mind creates the illusion of separation.
avadhuta_gita::97.simple_insight: There's relief in knowing the sense of being split is just a trick of the mind.
avadhuta_gita::97.detailed_meaning: The sage Dattatreya compares the full moon's pure oneness to the true self, explaining how the mind’s confusion causes it to seem divided when it is not.
avadhuta_gita::97.modern_relevance: You look in the mirror and see many flaws, but beneath it all your true nature is whole and untouched.
avadhuta_gita::97.insight: It teaches you to question how your mind divides and labels what is actually unified and pure.

avadhuta_gita::98.verse_sanskrit:
अनेनैव प्रकारेण बुद्धिभेदो न सर्वगः ।
दाता च धीरतामेति गीयते नामकोटिभिः ॥
avadhuta_gita::98.verse_hindi: इसी पूर्वोक्त प्रकार से सर्वगत चैतन्य में ज्ञान का भेद नहीं होता है और इस ज्ञान को देने वाला धीरता को प्राप्त होता है और करोड़ों नामों से उस का गुणगान होता है।
avadhuta_gita::98.english_translation: In this same way, the supreme consciousness has no distinction of knowledge, and the giver of this knowledge attains steadiness; countless names praise this truth.
avadhuta_gita::98.translation_literal: अनेनैव (by this very) प्रकारेण (method) बुद्धिभेदो (difference of knowledge) न (not) सर्वगः (all-pervading) । दाता (giver) च (and) धीरताम् (steadiness) एति (attains) गीयते (is praised) नामकोटिभिः (by millions of names) ॥
avadhuta_gita::98.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::98.essence: True knowledge is unified and steady, praised by countless names.
avadhuta_gita::98.simple_meaning: The supreme consciousness is without any division in knowledge. Those who give this knowledge become steady and are praised in many ways.
avadhuta_gita::98.simple_insight: You feel calm knowing true knowledge is unified and steady within you.
avadhuta_gita::98.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the all-pervading consciousness holds a knowledge without divisions. A person who shares this truth gains steadiness, and countless praises arise for this steadfast knowledge.
avadhuta_gita::98.modern_relevance: You’ve seen how confusing knowledge can be when divided; this verse invites you to find steadiness in unified understanding beyond scattered facts.
avadhuta_gita::98.insight: It shifts your focus from fragmented information to embracing one steady, undivided awareness.

avadhuta_gita::99.verse_sanskrit:
गुरुप्रज्ञाप्रसादेन मूर्खो वा यदि पण्डितः ।
यस्तु सम्बुध्यते तत्त्वं विरक्तो भवसागरात् ॥
avadhuta_gita::99.verse_hindi: मूर्ख हो अथवा पंडित (शास्त्रज्ञ) हो, जो गुरु के ज्ञान रूपी प्रसाद से आत्म तत्व को ठीक प्रकार से जान लेता है वह संसार रूपी भवसागर से विरक्त हो जाता है (जन्म-मरण से छूट जाता है)॥
avadhuta_gita::99.english_translation: Whether foolish or learned, one who truly understands the self through the guru's grace becomes detached from the ocean of worldly existence.
avadhuta_gita::99.translation_literal: गुरुप्रज्ञाप्रसादेन (by guru's wisdom grace) / मूर्खो (fool) / वा (or) / यदि (if) / पण्डितः (learned) / यस्तु (who indeed) / सम्बुध्यते (understands well) / तत्त्वं (the self) / विरक्तो (detached) / भवसागरात् (from the ocean of worldly existence)
avadhuta_gita::99.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::99.essence: True self-knowledge through a teacher’s grace frees anyone, wise or foolish, from worldly attachment.
avadhuta_gita::99.simple_meaning: Regardless of intelligence, anyone who gains true understanding of the self through a teacher’s grace becomes free from attachment to worldly life.
avadhuta_gita::99.simple_insight: Realizing your true nature brings freedom beyond knowledge or ignorance.
avadhuta_gita::99.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that whether a person is wise or foolish, when the guru’s grace reveals the true self, that person becomes detached from the endless cycle of worldly existence, symbolized as an ocean of suffering.
avadhuta_gita::99.modern_relevance: You might doubt your worth or knowledge, yet a genuine insight into who you truly are can liberate you from stress and endless struggles.
avadhuta_gita::99.insight: It shifts focus from intellectual status to experiential understanding as the key to freedom.

avadhuta_gita::100.verse_sanskrit:
रागद्वेषविनिर्मुक्तः सर्वभूतहिते रतः ।
दृढबोधश्च धीरश्च स गच्छेत्परमं पदम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::100.verse_hindi: जो राग द्वेष से रहित है, सम्पूर्ण भूतों के हित में रत है और दृढ़ बोध वाला है, धीर है वह परमपद को गमन करता है।
avadhuta_gita::100.english_translation: One who is free from attachment and aversion, devoted to the welfare of all beings, firmly aware and steady, attains the supreme state.
avadhuta_gita::100.translation_literal: रागद्वेषविनिर्मुक्तः (attachment-aversion-free) / सर्वभूतहिते (for the welfare of all beings) / रतः (devoted) / दृढबोधश्च (firm in awareness) / धीरश्च (steady) / स (he) / गच्छेत् (goes) / परमं पदम् (to the supreme state)
avadhuta_gita::100.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::100.essence: Freedom from craving and hatred, combined with steady care for all, leads to the highest freedom.
avadhuta_gita::100.simple_meaning: Being free from attachment and hatred, caring for all beings, and having firm awareness leads you to the highest state.
avadhuta_gita::100.simple_insight: You feel steady and open when love is free from craving or rejection.
avadhuta_gita::100.detailed_meaning: The Avadhuta teaches that a person who releases attachment and aversion, dedicates themselves to the well-being of every being, and holds firm, clear awareness naturally attains the supreme state of liberation.
avadhuta_gita::100.modern_relevance: When you stop clinging to likes and dislikes and care for others without selfishness, your mind settles, guiding you beyond restless struggle.
avadhuta_gita::100.insight: It shifts your focus from reactive emotions to steady, compassionate awareness that moves beyond dualities.

avadhuta_gita::101.verse_sanskrit:
घटे भिन्ने घटाकाश आकाशे लीयते यथा ।
देहाभावे तथा योगी स्वरूपे परमात्मनि ॥
avadhuta_gita::101.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार घड़े के फूटने पर घड़े का आकाश महाकाश में लय हो जाता है उसी प्रकार देह के नाश होने पर योगी परमात्म स्वरूप में लीन हो जाता है।
avadhuta_gita::101.english_translation: Just as the space inside a broken pot merges into the vast sky, the yogi merges into the supreme self when the body dissolves.
avadhuta_gita::101.translation_literal: घटे (pot) / भिन्ने (broken) / घटाकाश (space inside the pot) / आकाशे (in the sky) / लीयते (merges) / यथा (just as) / देहाभावे (in the absence of the body) / तथा (so) / योगी (the yogi) / स्वरूपे (in the nature) / परमात्मनि (in the supreme self)
avadhuta_gita::101.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::101.essence: The true self transcends the body and merges with the supreme reality without loss.
avadhuta_gita::101.simple_meaning: When the body dies, the yogi's true self merges back into the supreme reality, like space inside a broken pot joining the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::101.simple_insight: You are not limited by your body; your true self is boundless and eternal.
avadhuta_gita::101.detailed_meaning: This verse uses the image of a broken pot to show how the space inside it is not lost but merges with the vast sky. Similarly, when a yogi's body ends, their true self dissolves into the supreme reality without loss.
avadhuta_gita::101.modern_relevance: When a person you love passes away, remember their true self is not gone but merges with something vast and unchanging.
avadhuta_gita::101.insight: It teaches you to see your self beyond physical limits, recognizing your identity with the infinite.

avadhuta_gita::102.verse_sanskrit:
उक्तेयं कर्मयुक्तानां मतिर्यान्तेऽपि सा गतिः ।
न चोक्ता योगयुक्तानां मतिर्यान्तेऽपि सा गतिः ॥
avadhuta_gita::102.verse_hindi: ‘अन्त मति सो गति’ अन्त में जैसी मति (बुद्धि) होती है वैसी ही उसकी गति होती है-यह कर्मयुक्त मनुष्यों (अज्ञानियों) के लिए ही कहा गया है। योगयुक्त मनुष्यों के लिए नहीं कहा गया है कि अन्त में जैसी मति होती है वैसी ही उसकी गति होती है।
avadhuta_gita::102.english_translation: The belief that the end state is determined by the final mindset applies only to those attached to action, not to those united with yoga.
avadhuta_gita::102.translation_literal: उक्तेयं (said) कर्मयुक्तानां (to those attached to action) मति़ (mindset) यानि (which) अन्तेऽपि (even at the end) सा (that) गतिः (state) न (not) च (and) ओक्ता (said) योगयुक्तानां (to those united with yoga) मति़ (mindset) यानि (which) अन्तेऽपि (even at the end) सा (that) गतिः (state)
avadhuta_gita::102.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::102.essence: Attachment to action makes final mindset seem decisive; yoga reveals it is not.
avadhuta_gita::102.simple_meaning: Only those who are attached to their actions believe their final mindset decides their fate; those united with deeper yoga see beyond this.
avadhuta_gita::102.simple_insight: You can free yourself from being limited by how you think at the end.
avadhuta_gita::102.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that people attached to their actions believe their last thoughts determine their final state. But those who have united with yoga transcend this belief, recognizing that the final mindset does not dictate their true outcome.
avadhuta_gita::102.modern_relevance: You might worry that your last decisions or thoughts define your future, but this teaching reminds you that deeper awareness frees you from that fear.
avadhuta_gita::102.insight: It shifts your view from believing outcomes depend on your last mental state to seeing beyond reactive attachments.

avadhuta_gita::103.verse_sanskrit:
या गतिः कर्मयुक्तानां सा च वागिन्द्रियाद्वदेत् ।
योगिनां या गतिः क्वापि ह्यकथ्या भवतोर्जिता ॥
avadhuta_gita::103.verse_hindi: कर्मयुक्त अज्ञानियों की जो गति शास्त्रों में कही गई है वह वाणी तथा इन्द्रियों से कही जाती है और योगियों की गति जो तुमने संग्रह की है वह कहीं भी कथन करने योग्य नहीं है।
avadhuta_gita::103.english_translation: The state attained by those attached to action is described through speech and senses, but the state of yogis you have collected cannot be expressed anywhere.
avadhuta_gita::103.translation_literal: या (which) गतिः (state) कर्मयुक्तानां (of those attached to action) सा (that) च (also) वाग् (speech) इन्द्रियाद्वत् (like senses) एत् (is said) । योगिनां (of yogis) या (which) गतिः (state) क्वापि (anywhere) हि (indeed) अकथ्या (unutterable) भवतोर्जिता (you have collected) ॥
avadhuta_gita::103.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::103.essence: The yogi's supreme state cannot be expressed through words or senses.
avadhuta_gita::103.simple_meaning: The state reached by people focused on action can be described by words and senses, but the yogi's state is beyond any description.
avadhuta_gita::103.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing some experiences can't be captured by language or senses.
avadhuta_gita::103.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya contrasts the common understanding of states achieved by people caught in action, which can be described through speech and senses, with the yogi's supreme state that transcends all descriptions and cannot be expressed anywhere.
avadhuta_gita::103.modern_relevance: You might try to explain your deepest feelings or insights but find words fail to capture their true depth.
avadhuta_gita::103.insight: It teaches you to accept that some experiences are beyond explanation and must be directly known.

avadhuta_gita::104.verse_sanskrit:
एवं ज्ञात्वा त्वमुं मार्गं योगिनां नैव कल्पितम् ।
विकल्पवर्जनं तेषां स्वयं सिद्धिः प्रवर्तते ॥
avadhuta_gita::104.verse_hindi: जो मार्ग कर्मियों के मार्ग की भाँति कल्पित नहीं है। उस विकल्प रहित मार्ग को जानकर योगी उससे अपने आप सिद्धि में प्रवृत्त होता है।
avadhuta_gita::104.english_translation: Knowing this, you realize that path is not imagined like that of actors; without alternatives, yogis naturally attain perfection.
avadhuta_gita::104.translation_literal: एवं (thus) ज्ञात्वा (knowing) त्वम् (you) उं (that) मार्गं (path) योगिनां (of yogis) नैव (not at all) कल्पितम् (imagined) । विकल्पवर्जनं (free from alternatives) तेषां (their) स्वयं (by themselves) सिद्धिः (perfection) प्रवर्तते (arises) ॥
avadhuta_gita::104.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::104.essence: The true path is not a choice but a self-realizing journey without alternatives.
avadhuta_gita::104.simple_meaning: You understand that the true spiritual path is not made up like worldly roles; it has no alternatives and leads yogis naturally to perfection.
avadhuta_gita::104.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing your path is real, not a choice to be made.
avadhuta_gita::104.detailed_meaning: The Avadhuta explains that the spiritual path is not like acting or pretending. Yogis who realize this path has no alternatives naturally progress to perfection without effort or confusion.
avadhuta_gita::104.modern_relevance: When you stop doubting your direction and trust the path itself, progress happens without forcing or second-guessing.
avadhuta_gita::104.insight: This verse shifts your view from seeing the path as a choice to recognizing it as a natural, self-arising process.

avadhuta_gita::105.verse_sanskrit:
तीर्थे वान्त्यजगेहे वा यत्र कुत्र मृतोऽपि वा ।
न योगी पश्यते गर्भं परे ब्रह्मणि लीयते ॥
avadhuta_gita::105.verse_hindi: योगी (ब्रह्मज्ञानी) तीर्थ में अथवा अन्त्यज (चांडाल) के घर में अथवा जहाँ कहीं भी मरे वह गर्भ को नहीं देखता है। वह परब्रह्म में लय हो जाता है।
avadhuta_gita::105.english_translation: A realized yogi does not see the womb whether dying in a holy place, a lowly home, or anywhere; they dissolve into the supreme reality.
avadhuta_gita::105.translation_literal: तीर्थे (in holy place) / वान्त्यजगेहे (in low-caste person's house) / वा (or) / यत्र (where) / कुत्र (where) / मृतोऽपि (even dying) / वा (or) / न (not) / योगी (the yogi) / पश्यते (sees) / गर्भं (the womb) / परे (in supreme) / ब्रह्मणि (reality) / लीयते (is dissolved)
avadhuta_gita::105.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::105.essence: True realization dissolves all distinctions of place and birth into the supreme reality.
avadhuta_gita::105.simple_meaning: A yogi who knows the supreme reality does not see differences in place or birth at death; they merge into the supreme reality beyond all forms.
avadhuta_gita::105.simple_insight: You can be free from all social divisions and limitations, fully merging with what is beyond.
avadhuta_gita::105.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that a yogi who has realized the supreme reality is unaffected by external conditions like where or how they die. Whether in a sacred place or a lowly home, the yogi does not see these distinctions but merges into the supreme reality completely.
avadhuta_gita::105.modern_relevance: When facing judgment or exclusion, you can remember your essence does not depend on where you are or who you are with — you remain whole beyond labels.
avadhuta_gita::105.insight: It teaches you to see beyond external identities and environments, recognizing your unchanging true self everywhere.

avadhuta_gita::106.verse_sanskrit:
सहजमजमचिन्त्यं यस्तु पश्येत्स्वरूपं 
घटति यदि यथेष्टं लिप्यते नैव दोषैः ।
सकृदपि तदभावात्कर्म किंचिन्नकुर्यात्
तदपि न च विबद्धः संयमी वा तपस्वी ॥
avadhuta_gita::106.verse_hindi: फिर जो (ज्ञानी) एक बार भी स्वाभाविक जन्म से रहित, मन एवं वाणी द्वारा उस अचिन्त्य ( ब्रह्म) स्वरूप को देख लेता है यदि वह यथेष्ट कर्म को करता है तो वह दोषों में लिप्त नहीं होता। दोषों का अभाव हो जाने से किंचित् कर्म को न भी करे तो भी संयमी अथवा तपस्वी बद्ध नहीं होता।
avadhuta_gita::106.english_translation: If someone naturally, without mental effort, perceives the inconceivable true self even once, and acts according to their will, they are not tainted by faults. Even if they do no action after that, they are not bound, restrained, or ascetic.
avadhuta_gita::106.translation_literal: सहजम् (naturally) अजम् (without birth) अचिन्त्यं (inconceivable) यः (who) तु (indeed) पश्येत् (sees) स्वरूपं (true form) घटति (acts) यदि (if) यथेष्टं (according to will) लिप्यते (is tainted) नैव (not) दोषैः (by faults) । सकृदपि (even once) तदभावात् (due to absence of that) कर्म (action) किंचिन् (any) न (not) अकुर्यात् (does) तदपि (even then) न (not) च (and) विबद्धः (bound) संयमी (restrainer) वा (or) तपस्वी (ascetic) ॥
avadhuta_gita::106.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::106.essence: A natural glimpse of your true self frees you from faults and binding action.
avadhuta_gita::106.simple_meaning: If you naturally glimpse your true self even once and act freely, you are not stained by faults. After that, even doing no action does not bind you.
avadhuta_gita::106.simple_insight: There is deep freedom in recognizing your true self once—nothing binds you after.
avadhuta_gita::106.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that if a person naturally perceives the inconceivable true self once, their actions, even if done freely, do not cause faults. Even if they stop acting, they are not bound by restraint or asceticism, showing true freedom beyond action.
avadhuta_gita::106.modern_relevance: You might suddenly understand your worth and purpose clearly, and realize past mistakes no longer define or bind you.
avadhuta_gita::106.insight: It shifts your mindset from fearing consequences to embracing freedom from binding faults through clear recognition.

avadhuta_gita::107.verse_sanskrit:
निरामयं निष्प्रतिमं निराकृतिं
निराश्रयं निर्वपुषं निराशिषम् ।
निर्द्वन्द्वनिर्मोहमलुप्तशक्तिकं
तमीशमात्मानमुपैति शाश्वतम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::107.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी जगत के स्वामी उस शाश्वत आत्मा को प्राप्त होता है जो रोग रहित, आकार रहित, प्रतिमा रहित, निराश्रय, शरीर से रहित, इच्छा से रहित, द्वन्द्व रहित, मोह रहित तथा अलुप्त शक्ति (विद्यमान शक्ति ) वाला है।
avadhuta_gita::107.english_translation: The wise attain the eternal true self who is free from disease, form, image, shelter, body, desire, duality, delusion, and whose power is never diminished.
avadhuta_gita::107.translation_literal: निरामयं (disease-free) / निष्प्रतिमं (without form) / निराकृतिं (without image) / निराश्रयं (without shelter) / निर्वपुषं (without body) / निराशिषम् (without desire) / निर्द्वन्द्व (without duality) / निर्मोह (without delusion) / अलुप्तशक्तिकं (power never diminished) / तमीशमात्मानमुपैति (attains the supreme self) / शाश्वतम् (eternal)
avadhuta_gita::107.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::107.essence: Your true self is eternally free and beyond all limitation or desire.
avadhuta_gita::107.simple_meaning: You are the eternal true self, free from disease, form, desire, duality, and delusion, with unending power.
avadhuta_gita::107.simple_insight: You can feel complete beyond all limitations and attachments.
avadhuta_gita::107.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals the nature of the wise one's true self as eternal and untouched by any physical or mental flaws, desires, or illusions. This moment unfolds as a declaration of ultimate freedom beyond the world's changing forms.
avadhuta_gita::107.modern_relevance: Even when your body or mind feels weak or confused, your true self remains untouched and powerful beyond measure.
avadhuta_gita::107.insight: Recognize that your essence is beyond physical or mental conditions and cannot be diminished by circumstance.

avadhuta_gita::108.verse_sanskrit:
वेदो न दीक्षा न च मुण्डनक्रिया गुरुर्न शिष्यो न च यन्त्रसम्पदः ।
मुद्रादिकं चापि न यत्र भासते तमीशमात्मानमुपैति शाश्वतम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::108.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी उस ईश्वर स्वरूप शाश्वत आत्मा को प्राप्त होता है जिसमें वेद और दीक्षा नहीं हैं, न मुण्डन क्रिया ही हैं, गुरु और शिष्य भी नहीं है और यन्त्रों की सम्पदा भी नहीं हैं, और मुद्रा आदि भी जिसमें नहीं प्रतीत होते हैं।
avadhuta_gita::108.english_translation: The knower attains the eternal true self, beyond Vedas, initiation, tonsure, guru, disciple, and ritual objects like seals.
avadhuta_gita::108.translation_literal: वेदो (Vedas) / न (not) / दीक्षा (initiation) / न (not) / च (and) / मुण्डनक्रिया (tonsure ritual) / गुरुर्न (guru) / शिष्यो (disciple) / न (not) / च (and) / यन्त्रसम्पदः (wealth of ritual objects) / मुद्रादिकं (seals and such) / चापि (also) / न (not) / यत्र (where) / भासते (appear) / तमीशमात्मानमुपैति (attains the supreme true self) / शाश्वतम् (eternal)
avadhuta_gita::108.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::108.essence: The eternal true self transcends all rituals, teachers, and symbols.
avadhuta_gita::108.simple_meaning: The eternal true self is beyond scriptures, initiation ceremonies, teachers, disciples, and ritual objects.
avadhuta_gita::108.simple_insight: You are already complete and free beyond all external forms and symbols.
avadhuta_gita::108.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that the highest reality, the true self, is beyond all external rites like Vedas, initiation, tonsure, and the roles of guru and disciple, as well as ritual seals. This reveals ultimate freedom beyond formal religious structures.
avadhuta_gita::108.modern_relevance: You might feel pressured to prove your spirituality by rituals or titles, but your true nature transcends all external symbols.
avadhuta_gita::108.insight: It shifts your focus from external practices to recognizing your inherent, unchanging essence.

avadhuta_gita::109.verse_sanskrit:
न शाम्भवं शाक्तिकमानवं न वा 
पिण्डं च रूपं च पदादिकं न वा ।
आरम्भनिष्पत्तिघटादिकं च नो
तमीशमात्मानमुपैति शाश्वतम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::109.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी उस ईश्वर स्वरूप शाश्वत आत्मा को प्राप्त होता है जिसमें न शाम्भवी, न ही शक्तिचालिनी आदि है, न उसमें पिण्डभाव है, न रूप है, न पाँव आदि ही हैं। न घट के समान आदि व अन्त ही है।
avadhuta_gita::109.english_translation: The knower attains the eternal true self, which is neither Shambhavi nor Shaktichalini, neither embodied nor having form or feet, neither beginning nor end like a pot.
avadhuta_gita::109.translation_literal: न (not) शाम्भवं (Shambhavi) शाक्तिकमानवं (Shaktichalini) न (not) वा (also) पिण्डं (embodied form) च (and) रूपं (form) च (and) पदादिकं (feet and so on) न (not) वा (also) । आरम्भनिष्पत्तिघटादिकं (beginning and ending like a pot) च (and) नो (not) तमीशमात्मानमुपैति (attains the eternal true self) शाश्वतम् (eternal) ॥
avadhuta_gita::109.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::109.essence: You are the eternal true self beyond all form, name, and limits.
avadhuta_gita::109.simple_meaning: The true self you are is eternal and beyond all names, forms, or physical traits. It has no beginning or end.
avadhuta_gita::109.simple_insight: There is freedom in recognizing yourself as limitless and timeless, beyond any shape or label.
avadhuta_gita::109.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares the knower attains the eternal true self that transcends all known deities, physical bodies, forms, and temporal limits. This self is infinite and unchanging, beyond any container or attribute.
avadhuta_gita::109.modern_relevance: When you feel limited by your body, role, or identity, remember your true nature is vast and beyond those boundaries.
avadhuta_gita::109.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with temporary forms to knowing yourself as the timeless essence.

avadhuta_gita::110.verse_sanskrit:
यस्य स्वरूपात्सचराचरं जगदुत्पद्यते तिष्ठति लीयतेऽपि वा ।
पयोविकारादिव फेनबुद्बुदास्तमीशमात्मानमुपैति शाश्वतम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::110.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी उस ईश्वर स्वरूप शाश्वत आत्मा को प्राप्त होता है जिसके स्वरूप से समस्त चर अचर ( स्थावर, जंगम) जगत उत्पन्न होता हैं, स्थित रहता है तथा उसी में विलीन होता है जैसे जल के विकार से फेन और बुदबुदे उत्पन्न होते हैं व उसी में विलीन हो जाते हैं।
avadhuta_gita::110.english_translation: The knower attains the eternal true self from whose nature the entire moving and unmoving world arises, exists, and dissolves, like foam and bubbles arise and vanish from water.
avadhuta_gita::110.translation_literal: यस्य (whose) स्वरूपात् (from the nature) सचराचरं (moving and unmoving) जगत् (world) उत्पद्यते (is born) तिष्ठति (exists) लीयतेऽपि (and dissolves also) वा (or) । पयोविकारादिव (like water's transformations) फेनबुद्बुदाः (foam and bubbles) अस्मीशम् (true self) आत्मानम् (self) उपैति (attains) शाश्वतम् (eternal) ॥
avadhuta_gita::110.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::110.essence: The eternal true self is the source where all things arise and dissolve like bubbles in water.
avadhuta_gita::110.simple_meaning: You are the eternal true self from which everything in the world comes, stays, and eventually disappears like bubbles on water.
avadhuta_gita::110.simple_insight: You can feel steady knowing that all temporary things arise and vanish within your lasting nature.
avadhuta_gita::110.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that the true self is eternal and the source of everything that moves and does not move. Like bubbles forming and dissolving in water, all appearances come from and return to this one reality.
avadhuta_gita::110.modern_relevance: When life feels chaotic and ever-changing, remember you are the steady presence from which all experiences arise and fade.
avadhuta_gita::110.insight: Recognize that what you truly are never changes, even as all forms come and go around you.

avadhuta_gita::111.verse_sanskrit:
नासानिरोधो न च दृष्टिरासनं बोधोऽप्यबोधोऽपि न यत्र भासते ।
नाडीप्रचारोऽपि न यत्र किञ्चित्तमीशमात्मानमुपैति शाश्वतम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::111.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी उस ईश्वर स्वरूप शाश्वत आत्मा को प्राप्त होता है जिसमें नासाग्र भाग में दृष्टि निरोध नहीं है, न आसन ही है, जिसमें ज्ञान और अज्ञान भी नहीं भासता है जिसमें नाड़ी का विस्तार भी नहीं हैं।
avadhuta_gita::111.english_translation: The knower attains the eternal true self where there is no restraint of the nose-tip, no posture, no knowledge or ignorance shining, and no movement through the channels.
avadhuta_gita::111.translation_literal: नासानिरोधो (no restraint of the nose-tip) / न (nor) / च (and) / दृष्टिरासनं (vision/posture) / बोधोऽपि (even knowledge) / अप्यबोधोऽपि (nor ignorance) / न (not) / यत्र (where) / भासते (shines) / नाडीप्रचारोऽपि (nor movement through the channels) / न (not) / यत्र (where) / किञ्चित्त (anything) / अमीशम् (lord/master) / आत्मानम् (self) / उपैति (attains) / शाश्वतम् (eternal)
avadhuta_gita::111.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::111.essence: The eternal true self transcends all physical and mental limitations.
avadhuta_gita::111.simple_meaning: You realize the eternal true self where no physical or mental limitation exists—no posture, no seeing, no knowledge or ignorance, and no subtle movements.
avadhuta_gita::111.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing you are beyond all body and mind restrictions.
avadhuta_gita::111.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the state of the knower who has attained the eternal true self, a reality beyond all bodily constraints and mental dualities. Here, even the subtle breath movements and mental activities cease, revealing pure being beyond all appearances.
avadhuta_gita::111.modern_relevance: When your mind and body feel restless or limited, remember your true self is beyond all these boundaries and remains unchanged.
avadhuta_gita::111.insight: It shifts your experience from identification with body and mind to recognition of timeless awareness.

avadhuta_gita::112.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी उस ईश्वर स्वरूप शाश्वत आत्मा को प्राप्त होता है जिसमें नानात्व, एकत्व अथवा दोनों नहीं हैं, जो अणुत्व, दीर्घत्व, महत्व एवं शून्यता से रहित हैं तथा मानत्व, मेयत्व एवं समच से रहित है।
avadhuta_gita::112.english_translation: The wise attain the eternal true self, beyond diversity or unity, free from smallness, vastness, importance, and emptiness, untouched by ownership, possession, or equality.
avadhuta_gita::112.translation_literal: नानात्वम् (diversity) / एकत्वम् (unity) / अभुत्वम् (non-being) / अन्यता (otherness) / अणुत्व (smallness) / दीर्घत्व (vastness) / महत्त्व (importance) / शून्यता (emptiness) / मानत्वम् (ownership) / मेयत्व (possession) / समत्ववर्जितम् (devoid of equality) / तमीशम् (darkness/ignorance) / आत्मानम् (self) / उपैति (attains) / शाश्वतम् (eternal)
avadhuta_gita::112.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::112.essence: The true self is beyond all distinctions, ownership, and relative qualities.
avadhuta_gita::112.simple_meaning: You reach the eternal true self by transcending all differences, ownership, and notions of smallness or greatness.
avadhuta_gita::112.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing you are beyond all labels and claims.
avadhuta_gita::112.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the wise transcend all dualities—neither diverse nor one, beyond size, importance, or ownership—and realize the eternal true self beyond all changing states.
avadhuta_gita::112.modern_relevance: When you stop defining yourself by what you have or what you are not, you touch a freedom beyond all comparisons and possessions.
avadhuta_gita::112.insight: It teaches you to release all identities and claims to find your unchanging true self.

avadhuta_gita::113.verse_sanskrit:
सुसंयमी वा यदि वा न संयमी सुसंग्रही वा यदि वा न संग्रही ।
निष्कर्मको वा यदि वा सकर्मकस्तमीशमात्मानमुपैति शाश्वतम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::113.verse_hindi: जो ज्ञानी उस ईश्वर स्वरूप आत्मा को प्राप्त हो जाता है वह सुसंयमी हो अथवा असंयमी, संग्रही हो अथवा असंग्रही, निष्कर्मी हो अथवा सकर्मी कोई अन्तर नहीं पड़ता।
avadhuta_gita::113.english_translation: A true knower who has attained the true self remains the same whether self-controlled or not, attached or not, inactive or active.
avadhuta_gita::113.translation_literal: सुसंयमी (self-controlled) / वा (or) यदि (if) / वा न (not) / संयमी (self-controlled) / सुसंग्रही (attached) / वा (or) यदि (if) / वा न (not) / संग्रही (attached) / निष्कर्मको (inactive) / वा (or) यदि (if) / वा (or) सकर्मकः (active) / तमीशम् (the supreme self) / आत्मानम् (self) / उपैति (attains) / शाश्वतम् (eternal)
avadhuta_gita::113.speaker: Dattatreya
