avadhuta_gita::113.essence: The true self remains unchanged by control, attachment, or action.
avadhuta_gita::113.simple_meaning: You have reached the true self when nothing about your control, attachment, or activity changes your inner being.
avadhuta_gita::113.simple_insight: You can feel steady and whole no matter what you do or don’t do.
avadhuta_gita::113.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that once the true self is attained, external behaviors like self-control, attachment, or action no longer define or alter you. Whether you act or stay still, are attached or detached, your essence remains unshaken.
avadhuta_gita::113.modern_relevance: You might feel pressured to always be in control or productive, but your deepest self stays steady even when you let go or rest.
avadhuta_gita::113.insight: It teaches you to see beyond your habits and actions to the steady self beneath all change.

avadhuta_gita::114.verse_sanskrit:
मनो न बुद्धिर्न शरीरमिन्द्रियं तन्मात्रभूतानि न भूतपञ्चकम् ।
अहंकृतिश्चापि वियत्स्वरूपकं तमीशमात्मानमुपैति शाश्वतम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::114.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी उस ईश्वर स्वरूप शाश्वत आत्मा को प्राप्त होता है जो न मन है, न बुद्धि हैं, न शरीर है, न इन्द्रिय ही है, न तन्मात्रा है, न पंच महाभूत है, न अहंकार ही है। वह आकाश तुल्य व्यापक है।
avadhuta_gita::114.english_translation: The knower attains the supreme self who is neither mind nor intellect, nor body, nor senses, nor subtle elements, nor the five great elements, nor ego; that self is vast like space and eternal.
avadhuta_gita::114.translation_literal: मनः (mind) न (not) बुद्धिः (intellect) न (not) शरीरम् (body) इन्द्रियम् (senses) तन्मात्रभूतानि (subtle elements) न (not) भूतपञ्चकम् (five great elements) अहंकृतिः (ego) च (also) अपि (even) विहित् (separated) स्वरूपकम् (true nature) तम् (that) ईशम् (supreme) आत्मानम् (self) उपैति (attains) शाश्वतम् (eternal)
avadhuta_gita::114.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::114.essence: You are the eternal, boundless self beyond mind, body, and ego.
avadhuta_gita::114.simple_meaning: You are not your mind, body, senses, or ego. Your true self is eternal and as vast as space.
avadhuta_gita::114.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing you are limitless and not confined by your thoughts or body.
avadhuta_gita::114.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that the true self surpasses all physical and mental elements, including mind, intellect, body, subtle energies, and ego. This self is infinite and eternal, like space, beyond all changing forms.
avadhuta_gita::114.modern_relevance: When anxiety or self-doubt arises, remember you are more than your fleeting thoughts, feelings, or physical form — you are vast and unchanging.
avadhuta_gita::114.insight: It shifts your sense of identity from limited mental and physical boundaries to the boundless, eternal self.

avadhuta_gita::115.verse_sanskrit:
विधौ निरोधे परमात्मतां गते न योगिनश्चेतसि भेदवर्जिते ।
शौचं न वाशौचमलिङ्गभावना सर्वं विधेयं यदि वा निषिध्यते ॥
avadhuta_gita::115.verse_hindi: भेद से रहित परम आत्मता ( ब्रह्म) को प्राप्त योगी के चित्त में विधि और निरोध नहीं होते, पवित्रता, अपवित्रता तथा लिंग भावना (चिह्न भावना) भी नहीं होती तथा सम्पूर्ण विषयों का ही निषेध हो जाता हैं।
avadhuta_gita::115.english_translation: In the mind of a yogi who has attained the supreme reality free from distinctions, there is no sense of method or restraint; purity, impurity, and the sense of distinction also vanish, and all objects are rejected.
avadhuta_gita::115.translation_literal: विधौ (in method) / निरोधे (in restraint) / परमात्मतां (supreme reality) / गते (having reached) / न (not) / योगिनश्चेतसि (in the mind of the yogi) / भेदवर्जिते (free from distinctions) । शौचं (purity) / न (not) / वाशौचमलिङ्गभावना (impurity and sense of marks) / सर्वं (all) / विधेयं (to be prohibited) / यदि (if) / वा (or) / निषिध्यते (is rejected) ॥
avadhuta_gita::115.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::115.essence: Reaching supreme reality dissolves all methods, rules, and distinctions in the mind.
avadhuta_gita::115.simple_meaning: When you realize the supreme reality without distinctions, your mind no longer follows methods or restrictions, nor judges purity or impurity.
avadhuta_gita::115.simple_insight: You feel freedom when your mind stops dividing experience into pure or impure and lets go of all rules.
avadhuta_gita::115.detailed_meaning: The sage Dattatreya describes a yogi who has reached the supreme reality beyond all dualities and distinctions. At this stage, the mind no longer clings to methods or controls, nor does it hold ideas of purity, impurity, or any symbolic marks. Everything is naturally surrendered.
avadhuta_gita::115.modern_relevance: You know that moment when rules, labels, and judgments feel irrelevant because you simply see things clearly and without separation?
avadhuta_gita::115.insight: It teaches you to release the need for control and categories, resting in a mind beyond distinctions.

avadhuta_gita::116.verse_sanskrit:
मनो वचो यत्र न शक्तमीरितुं नूनं कथं तत्र गुरूपदेशता ।
इमां कथामुक्तवतो गुरोस्तद्युक्तस्य तत्त्वं हि समं प्रकाशते ॥
avadhuta_gita::116.verse_hindi: जिस आत्मा में मन और वाणी द्वारा कथन करने की सामर्थ्य नहीं है वहाँ गुरु का उपदेश कैसे हो सकता है। इस कथन को कहने वाले उस आत्मा से जुड़े हुए गुरु को निश्चय ही एकरस आत्म तत्व प्रकाशमान होता है।
avadhuta_gita::116.english_translation: Where the mind and speech have no power to speak, how can the teacher's instruction occur? The teacher who utters this is surely established in the same essence of the true self.
avadhuta_gita::116.translation_literal: मनो (mind) / वचो (speech) / यत्र (where) / न (not) / शक्तमीरितुं (power to speak) / नूनं (indeed) / कथं (how) / तत्र (there) / गुरूपदेशता (teacher's instruction) । इमां (this) / कथामुक्तवतो (uttered by) / गुरोः (teacher's) / तद्युक्तस्य (of that one spoken) / हि (indeed) / समं (same) / प्रकाशते (is revealed) ॥
avadhuta_gita::116.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::116.essence: True teaching happens only where mind and speech are fully silent.
avadhuta_gita::116.simple_meaning: When the mind and speech cannot express anything, the true teaching cannot happen. The teacher who speaks from that silent place is aligned with the true self.
avadhuta_gita::116.simple_insight: There is a deep stillness behind true guidance that you can feel beyond words.
avadhuta_gita::116.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that true teaching cannot occur where the restless mind and speech are active. Only a teacher rooted in the silent essence of the true self can convey genuine wisdom beyond words.
avadhuta_gita::116.modern_relevance: When your mind is racing and your words feel empty, real guidance comes only when you find quiet inside.
avadhuta_gita::116.insight: It shifts your understanding from relying on external instruction to recognizing the silent source of true wisdom within.

avadhuta_gita::117.verse_sanskrit:
गुणविगुणविभागो वर्तते नैव किञ्चित् 
रतिविरतिविहीनं निर्मलं निष्प्रपञ्चम् ।
गुणविगुणविहीनं व्यापकं विश्वरूपं
कथमहमिह वन्दे व्योमरूपं शिवं वै ॥
avadhuta_gita::117.verse_hindi: जिस ( आत्मा, ब्रह्म) में किंचित भी गुण एवं निर्गुण का विभाग नहीं हैं, जो रति और विरति से रहित निर्मल एवं प्रपंच से रहित है, उस सगुण निर्गुण से रहित, व्यापक, विश्व रूप की मैं कैसे वन्दना करूँ जो आकाश स्वरूप व कल्याण स्वरूप है।
avadhuta_gita::117.english_translation: I cannot worship the true self that has no division of qualities or lack of qualities, is free from attachment and aversion, pure and beyond all appearance, all-pervading, cosmic in form, like the sky and the source of all goodness.
avadhuta_gita::117.translation_literal: गुणविगुणविभागो (qualities-unqualities division) / वर्तते (exists) / नैव (not at all) / किञ्चित् (anything) / रति-विरति-विहीनं (attachment-aversion-free) / निर्मलं (pure) / निष्प्रपञ्चम् (appearance-less) / गुणविगुणविहीनं (qualities-unqualities-free) / व्यापकं (all-pervading) / विश्वरूपं (cosmic form) / कथम (how) / अहम् (I) / इह (here) / वन्दे (worship) / व्योमरूपं (sky-like form) / शिवं (auspicious) / वै (indeed)
avadhuta_gita::117.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::117.essence: The true self is beyond all qualities, vast, pure, and cannot be worshiped as a separate form.
avadhuta_gita::117.simple_meaning: The true self is beyond all qualities, free from attachment and aversion, pure, and all-pervading like the sky; it cannot be worshiped as a separate object.
avadhuta_gita::117.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing the true self is beyond all distinctions and cannot be grasped or worshiped.
avadhuta_gita::117.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the true self transcends all dualities of qualities and lacks, attachment and aversion. It is pure and universal, like the vast sky, making it impossible to approach as a separate entity for worship.
avadhuta_gita::117.modern_relevance: When you try to label or control your inner self, you find it resists all categories and definitions, vast and free beyond your grasp.
avadhuta_gita::117.insight: It teaches you to release all attempts to fix or worship the self as an object, recognizing its boundless nature.

avadhuta_gita::118.verse_sanskrit:
श्वेतादिवर्णरहितो नियतं शिवश्च
कार्यं हि कारणमिदं हि परं शिवश्च ।
एवं विकल्परहितोऽहमलं शिवश्च
स्वात्मानमात्मनि सुमित्र कथं नमामि ॥
avadhuta_gita::118.verse_hindi: जो श्वेत आदि वर्गों से रहित नित्य एवं शिव रूप (कल्याण स्वरूप) है, यही कारण एवं कार्य हैं, श्रेष्ठ व शिव ही हैं। तथा विकल्प रहित, परिपूर्ण शिव रूप ही है। हे सुमित्र! फिर मैं अपनी आत्मा को आत्मा में किस प्रकार नमस्कार करूँ।
avadhuta_gita::118.english_translation: The supreme auspicious reality is beyond all categories like white or others; it is both the cause and the effect, perfectly free from alternatives. How then, friend Sumitra, can I bow to the true self within the true self?
avadhuta_gita::118.translation_literal: श्वेतादि (white and others) वर्णरहितो (without category) नियतं (eternal) शिवश्च (auspicious reality) कार्यं (effect) हि (indeed) कारणमिदं (this cause) हि (indeed) परं (supreme) शिवश्च (auspicious reality) । एवं (thus) विकल्परहितोऽहमलं (free of alternatives and pure) शिवश्च (auspicious reality) आत्मानमात्मनि (self in self) सुमित्र (Sumitra) कथं (how) नमामि (do I bow) ॥
avadhuta_gita::118.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::118.essence: The true self is perfectly complete beyond all forms, needing no separate reverence.
avadhuta_gita::118.simple_meaning: The true self is beyond all categories and dualities; it is both the source and the result, complete and without alternatives. It cannot be separately saluted because it is perfectly whole within itself.
avadhuta_gita::118.simple_insight: You are already perfectly complete beyond all labels; no separate worship is needed for what you truly are.
avadhuta_gita::118.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the supreme reality is beyond all categories like color or class. It is the eternal cause and effect, flawless and without alternatives. He questions how he could bow to the true self when that self is already whole and self-contained.
avadhuta_gita::118.modern_relevance: When you face your reflection, you realize there is nothing separate to admire or bow to; your true essence is already perfect and complete.
avadhuta_gita::118.insight: It shifts attention from seeking an external ideal to recognizing the unchanging completeness within yourself.

avadhuta_gita::119.verse_sanskrit:
निर्मूलमूलरहितो हि सदोदितोऽहं
निर्धूमधूमरहितो हि सदोदितोऽहम् ।
निर्दीपदीपरहितो हि सदोदितोऽहं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::119.verse_hindi: मैं निर्मूल और मूल से रहित हूँ, निधूम और धूम से रहित हूँ, निर्दीप और दीप से रहित हूँ। मैं सदा ही उदित हूँ, ज्ञानामृत, समरस तथा आकाश की उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::119.english_translation: I am without root or origin, without smoke or mist, without lamp or light; I am always radiant, the nectar of wisdom, pure and boundless like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::119.translation_literal: निर्मूलमूलरहितो (without root or origin) / हि (indeed) / सदोदितोऽहं (I am always risen/radiant) / निर्धूमधूमरहितो (without smoke or mist) / हि (indeed) / सदोदितोऽहम् (I am always risen) / निर्दीपदीपरहितो (without lamp or light) / हि (indeed) / सदोदितोऽहं (I am always risen) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of wisdom) / समरसं (of pure essence) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (I am like the sky)
avadhuta_gita::119.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::119.essence: You are eternally radiant and free, beyond all roots, veils, and light.
avadhuta_gita::119.simple_meaning: You are not limited by origins, illusions, or appearances. You are always radiant, embodying pure wisdom like the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::119.simple_insight: You can feel limitless and naturally bright, beyond all conditions or beginnings.
avadhuta_gita::119.detailed_meaning: The Avadhuta declares his true nature as beyond all origins, smoke, or light—symbols of illusion and limitation. He is always radiant, the pure essence of wisdom, vast and unbounded like the sky, expressing freedom from all dualities.
avadhuta_gita::119.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck in your history, doubts, or confusion, remember your true self is free and radiant beyond all those limits.
avadhuta_gita::119.insight: It teaches you to recognize your true self as limitless and unaffected by any passing condition or identity.

avadhuta_gita::120.verse_sanskrit:
निष्कामकाममिह नाम कथं वदामि
निःसङ्गसङ्गमिह नाम कथं वदामि ।
निःसारसाररहितं च कथं वदामि
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::120.verse_hindi: मैं आत्म स्वरूप होने से ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश तुल्य हूँ फिर अपने को निकास एवं कामना नाम वाला किस प्रकार कहूँ, निसंग एवं संग वाला भी किस प्रकार कहूँ, और निसार और सार रहित भी किस प्रकार कहूँ।
avadhuta_gita::120.english_translation: Being the true self, I am the nectar of knowledge, of equal essence, like the sky; how could I be called desireless or attached, or devoid and not devoid?
avadhuta_gita::120.translation_literal: निष्कामकाममिह (desireless here) / नाम (name) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I say) / निःसङ्गसङ्गमिह (detached-attached here) / नाम (name) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I say) / निःसारसाररहितं (devoid and not devoid) / च (and) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I say) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) / समरसं (of equal essence) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (like the sky I am)
avadhuta_gita::120.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::120.essence: You are limitless wisdom beyond all opposing qualities like desire and attachment.
avadhuta_gita::120.simple_meaning: You, as your true self, are pure wisdom like endless sky, beyond desire or attachment or emptiness.
avadhuta_gita::120.simple_insight: Feel your nature as complete and undivided, untouched by wanting or not wanting.
avadhuta_gita::120.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya proclaims that as the true self, he is like the sky—limitless and equal in essence—beyond all dualities like desire and attachment or emptiness and fullness.
avadhuta_gita::120.modern_relevance: In moments when wants pull you every which way, remember your true nature is vast and steady like the open sky.
avadhuta_gita::120.insight: Shift your view from fluctuating desires and aversions to recognizing your unchanging, balanced nature.

avadhuta_gita::121.verse_sanskrit:
अद्वैतरूपमखिलं हि कथं वदामि
द्वैतस्वरूपमखिलं हि कथं वदामि ।
नित्यं त्वनित्यमखिलं हि कथं वदामि
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::121.verse_hindi: इस सम्पूर्ण जगत को मैं अद्वैत रूप कैसे कहूँ, इस सम्पूर्ण जगत को में द्वैत स्वरूप कैसे कहूँ, इस सम्पूर्ण जगत को नित्य अथवा अनित्य कैसे कहूँ। मैं ज्ञानामृत समरस एवं आकाश तुल्य हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::121.english_translation: How can I call the whole world non-dual or dual? How can I say it is eternal or not? I am like the nectar of knowledge, pure and vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::121.translation_literal: अद्वैतरूपमखिलं (non-dual form whole) / हि (indeed) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I speak) / द्वैतस्वरूपमखिलं (dual form whole) / हि (indeed) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I speak) / नित्यं (eternal) / त्वनित्यमखिलं (or non-eternal whole) / हि (indeed) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I speak) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) / समरसं (of equal essence) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (like the sky I am)
avadhuta_gita::121.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::121.essence: Your true nature cannot be confined by any dual or fixed description.
avadhuta_gita::121.simple_meaning: You are not limited by ideas of duality, non-duality, eternal, or temporary. You are like the vast sky—pure and unchanging.
avadhuta_gita::121.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing you are beyond all fixed categories or labels.
avadhuta_gita::121.detailed_meaning: The Avadhuta speaks from complete freedom, declaring that the entire world cannot be truly called dual or non-dual, eternal or temporary. He identifies with the limitless, unchanging essence like the sky, beyond all conceptual divisions.
avadhuta_gita::121.modern_relevance: You find yourself caught in black-and-white thinking, but this invites you to rest in the freedom beyond all fixed categories about who or what you are.
avadhuta_gita::121.insight: It teaches you to release all rigid identities and see your true nature as boundless and ungraspable by labels.

avadhuta_gita::122.verse_sanskrit:
स्थूलं हि नो नहि कृशं न गतागतं हि
आद्यन्तमध्यरहितं न परापरं हि ।
सत्यं वदामि खलु वै परमार्थतत्त्वं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::122.verse_hindi: हमारी आत्मा स्थूल भी नहीं है, न सूक्ष्म है, न गमन आनगमन वाला ही है, यह आदि, अन्त और मध्य से रहित है, पर अपर से भी रहित है। मैं निश्चय ही सत्य कहता हूँ कि मैं परमार्थ तत्व, ज्ञानामृत, एकरस एवं आकाश की उपमा हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::122.english_translation: Our true self is neither gross nor subtle, neither moving nor stationary; it is beyond beginning, middle, and end, beyond higher and lower. I speak the absolute truth: I am the supreme reality, the nectar of knowledge, one with the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::122.translation_literal: स्थूलं (gross) हि (indeed) नो (not) नहि (not) कृशं (subtle) न (nor) गतागतं (moving and gone) हि (indeed) आद्यन्तमध्यरहितं (without beginning, middle, and end) न (not) परापरं (beyond higher and lower) हि (indeed) । सत्यं (truth) वदामि (I speak) खलु (surely) वै (indeed) परमार्थतत्त्वं (supreme reality) ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) समरसं (one-flavored) गगनोपमोऽहम् (like the sky I am) ॥
avadhuta_gita::122.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::122.essence: Your true self is beyond all limits and is as vast and unchanging as the sky.
avadhuta_gita::122.simple_meaning: Your true self is beyond physical form, beyond time, beyond movement, and beyond any duality. It is like the vast sky—unchanging and one.
avadhuta_gita::122.simple_insight: You can feel freedom in knowing you are limitless and not defined by change or form.
avadhuta_gita::122.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares the true self transcends all categories: not gross or subtle, not moving or still, beyond time and dualities. This is the moment of absolute self-recognition, where the self is realized as vast and unbounded like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::122.modern_relevance: When you feel trapped by your changing thoughts or circumstances, this reminds you that your true self is untouched—vast and unchanging beneath it all.
avadhuta_gita::122.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with transient states to recognizing your boundless, unchanging nature.

avadhuta_gita::123.verse_sanskrit:
संविद्धि सर्वकरणानि नभोनिभानि
संविद्धि सर्वविषयांश्च नभोनिभांश्च ।
संविद्धि चैकममलं न हि बन्धमुक्तं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::123.verse_hindi: सम्पूर्ण करणों को (इन्द्रियों को) तू आकाश की भाँति शुन्य जान और सम्पूर्ण विषयों को तू आकाश के तुल्य शून्य जान, एक आत्मा को ही मायामल से रहित तू जान जो बन्धन और मुक्ति से रहित है वही मैं हूँ जो ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश की उपमा वाला है।
avadhuta_gita::123.english_translation: Know all senses as empty like space, and all objects like space; know the one self, free of illusion, beyond bondage and freedom — I am that, pure knowledge, the essence, like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::123.translation_literal: संविद्धि (know) / सर्वकरणानि (all senses) / नभोनिभानि (like space) / संविद्धि (know) / सर्वविषयांश्च (all objects) / नभोनिभांश्च (like space) / संविद्धि (know) / चैकममलं (the one pure) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / बन्धमुक्तं (bondage-free) / ज्ञानामृतं (knowledge-nectar) / समरसं (essence) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (like the sky I am)
avadhuta_gita::123.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::123.essence: Your true self is like the vast sky—pure, free, and beyond all illusions.
avadhuta_gita::123.simple_meaning: Everything your senses perceive and all objects are like empty space. Your true self is pure, free of illusion, beyond bondage or freedom, like the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::123.simple_insight: You can feel free and untouched, like the limitless sky beyond all appearances.
avadhuta_gita::123.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that just as space is unaffected by what it contains, the true self remains pure and free beyond all senses and objects. This moment reveals the self as limitless knowledge and essence, untouched by any duality.
avadhuta_gita::123.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by constant input and distractions, remember your true self is like the open sky—vast, pure, and untouched by noise.
avadhuta_gita::123.insight: It teaches you to see your true nature as beyond all sensory experience and mental labels, untouched and free like space.

avadhuta_gita::124.verse_sanskrit:
दुर्बोधबोधगहनो न भवामि तात
दुर्लक्ष्यलक्ष्यगहनो न भवामि तात ।
आसन्नरूपगहनो न भवामि तात
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::124.verse_hindi: हे तात ! बोध स्वरूप आत्मा का ज्ञान बड़ा दुर्बोध है तथा गम्भीर है, वह मैं नहीं हूं। वह दुर्लक्ष्य है, इन्द्रियों से दिखाई नहीं देता उसे जानना भी गम्भीर है, सो मैं नहीं हूं। वह अति समीप है फिर भी उसको जानना गम्भीर है, वह मैं नहीं हूं। मैं समरस, ज्ञानामृत एवं आकाश को उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::124.english_translation: I am not the deep, obscure knowledge of the true self, nor the elusive perception of it; I am like the sky, the nectar of wisdom in harmony.
avadhuta_gita::124.translation_literal: दुर्बोधबोधगहनो (difficult-to-understand knowledge profound) / न (not) / भवामि (am) / तात (O son) / दुर्लक्ष्यलक्ष्यगहनो (hard-to-perceive, perception profound) / न (not) / भवामि (am) / तात (O son) / आसन्नरूपगहनो (near-form profound) / न (not) / भवामि (am) / तात (O son) / ज्ञानामृतं (wisdom nectar) / समरसं (in harmony) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (like sky I am)
avadhuta_gita::124.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::124.essence: You are not the confusing hidden knowledge but the clear, harmonious essence like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::124.simple_meaning: You are not the confusing, hidden knowledge of the true self. Instead, you are like the open sky—clear, harmonious, and full of the nectar of wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::124.simple_insight: You can feel peace knowing you are not the confusing mystery but the clear, open essence itself.
avadhuta_gita::124.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya speaks to his son, explaining that the true self's knowledge is deep, hidden, and difficult to perceive. Yet, he clarifies he is not that confusing mystery but the vast, clear sky—symbolizing harmony and pure wisdom beyond complexity.
avadhuta_gita::124.modern_relevance: When your thoughts feel tangled and confusing, remember you are not that mess but the clear space that holds it all.
avadhuta_gita::124.insight: It teaches you to let go of trying to grasp confusing knowledge and instead rest in the clear awareness that you truly are.

avadhuta_gita::125.verse_sanskrit:
निष्कर्मकर्मदहनो ज्वलनो भवामि
निर्दुःखदुःखदहनो ज्वलनो भवामि ।
निर्देहदेहदहनो ज्वलनो भवामि
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::125.verse_hindi: मैं कर्म से रहित हूं फिर भी मैं कर्मों का दाहक अग्नि हूँ, मैं दु:खों से रहित हूँ फिर भी दु:खों का दाहक अग्नि हूँ मैं देह से रहित हूँ फिर भी देह का दाहक अग्नि हूँ। मैं ज्ञानामृत समरस एवं आकाश की उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::125.english_translation: I am free from action, yet I burn the fire of actions; free from suffering, yet I burn the fire of sufferings; free from the body, yet I burn the fire of the body. I am the nectar of knowledge, the infinite sky's likeness.
avadhuta_gita::125.translation_literal: निष्कर्मकर्मदहनो (free from action, burning action) ज्वलनो (burning) भवामि (I am) / निर्दुःखदुःखदहनो (free from suffering, burning suffering) ज्वलनो (burning) भवामि (I am) / निर्देहदेहदहनो (free from body, burning body) ज्वलनो (burning) भवामि (I am) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) समरस (of same essence) गगन (sky) उपम (likeness) अहम् (I am)
avadhuta_gita::125.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::125.essence: You appear affected by life but remain untouched, vast like the sky of wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::125.simple_meaning: You are not bound by actions, suffering, or the body, yet you appear to burn through them. Your true nature is like the infinite sky, filled with the nectar of knowledge.
avadhuta_gita::125.simple_insight: You can feel life’s challenges without being truly harmed or defined by them.
avadhuta_gita::125.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that although he appears to engage with actions, sufferings, and the physical body, he remains untouched by them. Like the sky that contains everything without being affected, his true self is pure knowledge and freedom beyond all appearances.
avadhuta_gita::125.modern_relevance: When you face stress or pain, you can remember that beneath all reactions, your true self remains vast and untouched.
avadhuta_gita::125.insight: It teaches you to recognize the difference between your true self and the temporary struggles you experience.

avadhuta_gita::126.verse_sanskrit:
निष्पापपापदहनो हि हुताशनोऽहं
निर्धर्मधर्मदहनो हि हुताशनोऽहम् ।
निर्बन्धबन्धदहनो हि हुताशनोऽहं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::126.verse_hindi: मैं निष्पाप हूँ, फिर भी पापों को नष्ट करने में मैं अग्नि रूप हूँ, मैं निधर्म हूँ फिर भी धर्म और अधर्म को जलाने में मैं अग्नि रूप हूँ, मैं निर्बन्ध होते हुए भी बन्धनों को जलाने में अग्नि रूप हूँ। मैं एक ही ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश के समान हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::126.english_translation: I am without fault, yet I am the fire that burns away sins; I am beyond law, yet I burn both right and wrong; I am without bonds, yet I burn all attachments. I am the nectar of wisdom, pure and boundless like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::126.translation_literal: निष्पापपापदहनो (without-fault / sins-burning) हि (indeed) हुताशनोऽहं (fire-that-destroys-I-am) निर्धर्मधर्मदहनो (lawless / law-burning) हि (indeed) हुताशनोऽहम् (fire-that-destroys-I-am) । निर्बन्धबन्धदहनो (without-bond / bonds-burning) हि (indeed) हुताशनोऽहं (fire-that-destroys-I-am) ज्ञानामृतं (wisdom-nectar) समरसं (purely-blended) गगनोपमोऽहम् (sky-like-I-am) ॥
avadhuta_gita::126.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::126.essence: You are pure and free, yet the fire that burns all faults and bonds.
avadhuta_gita::126.simple_meaning: You are naturally free and pure, yet you have the power to burn away faults, rules, and attachments like a fire. Your true nature is pure wisdom and vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::126.simple_insight: Feel the relief of being naturally free while holding the power to transform what binds you.
avadhuta_gita::126.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that although the true self is without fault and beyond moral rules, it acts like fire that consumes sin, law, and bondage. This verse reveals the paradox of being untouched yet transformative, embodying pure wisdom vast as the sky.
avadhuta_gita::126.modern_relevance: When you feel weighed down by guilt, rules, or attachments, remember your true nature burns these away effortlessly—like a fire within you.
avadhuta_gita::126.insight: Recognize your dual nature as untouched purity and active force dissolving limits and illusions.

avadhuta_gita::127.verse_sanskrit:
निर्भावभावरहितो न भवामि वत्स
निर्योगयोगरहितो न भवामि वत्स ।
निश्चित्तचित्तरहितो न भवामि वत्स
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::127.verse_hindi: हे वत्स! मैं निर्भाव होते हुए भी भाव से रहित हूँ, मैं निर्योग होकर भी योग से रहित नहीं हूँ, मैं बिना चित्त वाला होकर भी चित्त से रहित नहीं हूँ। मैं ज्ञानामृत, एकरस तथा आकाश की उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::127.english_translation: I am free from all states yet not without feeling; without effort yet not without union; without mind yet not without consciousness. I am the nectar of knowledge, one taste, like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::127.translation_literal: निर्भावभावरहितो (free-from-emotion-feeling) / न (not) / भवामि (I am) / वत्स (child/dear one) / निर्योगयोगरहितो (without-effort-yet-not-without-union) / न (not) / भवामि (I am) / वत्स (child/dear one) / निश्चित्तचित्तरहितो (without-mind-yet-not-without-consciousness) / न (not) / भवामि (I am) / वत्स (child/dear one) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar-of-knowledge) / समरसं (one-taste) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (like-the-sky-I-am)
avadhuta_gita::127.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::127.essence: You transcend all states yet remain fully aware and unified like the infinite sky.
avadhuta_gita::127.simple_meaning: You are beyond all changing states but still fully aware and connected. Like the sky, you are steady and one with knowledge.
avadhuta_gita::127.simple_insight: You can be free from fluctuations yet deeply alive and unified.
avadhuta_gita::127.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares his true self transcends all dualities—no separate emotions, effort, or mind limit him. Yet he remains fully aware and unified, like the limitless sky tasting all as one.
avadhuta_gita::127.modern_relevance: When your feelings or thoughts feel overwhelming or absent, remember you can be steady and aware beyond all shifting states.
avadhuta_gita::127.insight: Shift from identifying with passing feelings or efforts to recognizing your unchanging, unified awareness.

avadhuta_gita::128.verse_sanskrit:
निर्मोहमोहपदवीति न मे विकल्पो
निःशोकशोकपदवीति न मे विकल्पः ।
निर्लोभलोभपदवीति न मे विकल्पो
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::128.verse_hindi: मुझमें निर्मोह अथवा मोह वाला विकल्प नहीं है, शोक रहित अथवा शोक वाला विकल्प भी मेरे में नहीं हैं, निर्लोभ अथवा लोभ वाला विकल्प भी मुझमें नहीं है। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश को उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::128.english_translation: In me, there is no choice between delusion and clarity, nor between sorrow and sorrowless; no choice between greed and greedlessness. I am the nectar of knowledge, perfectly balanced and like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::128.translation_literal: निर्मोह (without delusion) / मोह (delusion) / पदवीति (a state/status) / न (not) / मे (in me) / विकल्पो (alternative/choice) / निःशोक (without sorrow) / शोक (sorrow) / पदवीति (state) / न (not) / मे (in me) / विकल्पः (choice) / निर्लोभ (without greed) / लोभ (greed) / पदवीति (state) / न (not) / मे (in me) / विकल्पो (alternative) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) / समरसं (perfectly balanced) / गगनोपम (like the sky) / अहम् (I am)
avadhuta_gita::128.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::128.essence: True self is beyond all opposing inner states and perfectly balanced like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::128.simple_meaning: You are free from all inner conflicts like confusion, sorrow, and greed. You embody balanced knowledge and vastness like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::128.simple_insight: You can feel deep peace knowing your true nature is beyond all opposing struggles.
avadhuta_gita::128.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes his state beyond all dualities: no confusion or clarity, no sorrow or joy, no greed or lack. He is the pure essence of wisdom, steady and vast like the sky itself.
avadhuta_gita::128.modern_relevance: You notice how your mind flips between wanting and not wanting, sadness and calm. Recognizing your true self is beyond these swings brings deep relief.
avadhuta_gita::128.insight: It teaches you to see beyond all inner conflicts as illusions, resting instead in unshakable balance.

avadhuta_gita::129.verse_sanskrit:
संसारसन्ततिलता न च मे कदाचित्
सन्तोषसन्ततिसुखो न च मे कदाचित् ।
अज्ञानबन्धनमिदं न च मे कदाचित्
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::129.verse_hindi: संसार की संतति रूपी लता मेरे में नहीं है, सन्तोष रूपी संतति का सुख भी मेरे में नहीं है, ये अज्ञान के बन्धन भी मेरे में नहीं है। मैं एकरस, ज्ञानामृत एवं आकाश की उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::129.english_translation: I have never been bound by the vine of worldly existence, nor by the happiness of continual satisfaction; ignorance's bonds never held me. I am like the sky—one-tasting, the nectar of knowledge.
avadhuta_gita::129.translation_literal: संसारसन्ततिलता (worldly existence vine) / न (not) / च (and) / मे (in me) / कदाचित् (ever) / सन्तोषसन्ततिसुखो (happiness of continuous satisfaction) / न (not) / च (and) / मे (in me) / कदाचित् (ever) / अज्ञानबन्धनमिदं (these bonds of ignorance) / न (not) / च (and) / मे (in me) / कदाचित् (ever) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) / समरसं (one-tasting) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (I am like the sky)
avadhuta_gita::129.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::129.essence: You are never bound by worldly cravings or ignorance but are pure, infinite awareness.
avadhuta_gita::129.simple_meaning: You are never caught in the endless cycle of worldly attachments or ignorance. Instead, you exist as pure, limitless awareness like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::129.simple_insight: You can feel free and vast inside, beyond any grasping or bonds.
avadhuta_gita::129.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares freedom from all worldly ties and ignorance that bind common beings. Unlike those entangled in endless cravings and confusion, he remains as vast and unified as the sky, tasting only the nectar of true knowledge.
avadhuta_gita::129.modern_relevance: When life feels overwhelming with endless wants or disappointments, remember your true nature is free and expansive like open sky beyond those chains.
avadhuta_gita::129.insight: It shifts your identity from a bound, craving self to one of vast, unconditioned awareness beyond all limitations.

avadhuta_gita::130.verse_sanskrit:
संसारसन्ततिरजो न च मे विकारः
सन्तापसन्ततितमो न च मे विकारः ।
सत्त्वं स्वधर्मजनकं न च मे विकारो
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::130.verse_hindi: संसार को संतति रज (रजोगुण) हैं यह विकार मेरे में नहीं है, सन्ताप को संतति तम (तमोगुण) हैं वह भी विकार मेरे में नहीं है, स्वधर्म का जनक सत्त्व (सतोगुण) है वह विकार भी मेरे में नहीं है। में ज्ञानामृत, एकरस तथा आकाश की उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::130.english_translation: The lineage of the natural world is passion; that flaw is not in me. The lineage of suffering is darkness; that flaw is not in me. The essence of true nature is goodness; that flaw is not in me. I am the nectar of wisdom, of one taste, like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::130.translation_literal: संसारसन्ततिरजो (lineage of natural world is passion) / न (not) / च (also) / मे (in me) / विकारः (flaw) / सन्तापसन्ततितमो (lineage of suffering is darkness) / न (not) / च (also) / मे (in me) / विकारः (flaw) / सत्त्वं (goodness) / स्वधर्मजनकं (creator of true nature) / न (not) / च (also) / मे (in me) / विकारो (flaw) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of wisdom) / समरसं (of one taste) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (like the sky I am)
avadhuta_gita::130.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::130.essence: You are pure wisdom beyond all qualities and flaws of the natural world.
avadhuta_gita::130.simple_meaning: You are not affected by the flaws of passion, suffering, or confusion. You are pure wisdom, steady and vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::130.simple_insight: You can feel steady and untouched despite chaos and pain around you.
avadhuta_gita::130.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he is untouched by the faults of the natural world — passion (rajas), suffering (tamas), and goodness (sattva) when seen as flaws. Instead, he is pure wisdom, unified and vast like the sky, beyond all disturbance.
avadhuta_gita::130.modern_relevance: Even when everything around you feels chaotic or painful, you can remember that your true nature remains steady, clear, and unaffected.
avadhuta_gita::130.insight: It teaches you to recognize your true self as beyond all emotional and mental fluctuations, steady like the sky.

avadhuta_gita::131.verse_sanskrit:
सन्तापदुःखजनको न विधिः कदाचित्
सन्तापयोगजनितं न मनः कदाचित् ।
यस्मादहङ्कृतिरियं न च मे कदाचित्
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::131.verse_hindi: सन्ताप रूपी दु:ख की जनक जो विधि है वह मैं नहीं हूँ सन्ताप के योग से उत्पन्न हुआ मन भी मैं नहीं हूँ, जिससे यह अहंकार भी मेरा नहीं है। मैं ज्ञानामृत, एकरस तथा आकाश की उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::131.english_translation: I am not fate that causes suffering, nor the mind born from suffering; this ego is not mine. I am the nectar of wisdom, steady and like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::131.translation_literal: सन्तापदुःखजनको (suffering-pain-causing) / न (not) / विधिः (fate) / कदाचित् (ever) / सन्तापयोगजनितं (suffering-born) / न (not) / मनः (mind) / कदाचित् (ever) / यस्मात् (since) / अहङ्कृतिः (ego) / इयं (this) / न (not) / च (and) / मे (mine) / कदाचित् (ever) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) / समरसं (one-flavor/unified) / गगन उपम (like the sky) / अहम् (I)
avadhuta_gita::131.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::131.essence: You are the steady, unifying wisdom beyond pain, mind, and ego.
avadhuta_gita::131.simple_meaning: You are not the suffering or the mind created by suffering, nor the ego that appears. You are steady, like the sky, the pure nectar of wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::131.simple_insight: You can feel free from pain and ego because your true nature is steady and wise.
avadhuta_gita::131.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals that he is not the fate causing pain, nor the mind born from that pain, nor the ego that seems to arise. Instead, he is the unchanging, unified essence of wisdom, like the vast and steady sky.
avadhuta_gita::131.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by painful thoughts or a restless ego, remember you are not those feelings but the calm, vast wisdom beyond them.
avadhuta_gita::131.insight: It shifts your sense of identity away from suffering and ego toward a stable, unifying wisdom within.

avadhuta_gita::132.verse_sanskrit:
निष्कम्पकम्पनिधनं न विकल्पकल्पं
स्वप्नप्रबोधनिधनं न हिताहितं हि ।
निःसारसारनिधनं न चराचरं हि
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::132.verse_hindi: मैं कम्पन रहित और कम्पन का नाश करने वाला नहीं हूँ, न संकल्प और विकल्प ही हूँ, स्वप्न और जाग्रत का नाश करने वाला भी नहीं हूँ, न हित और अहित ही हूँ, में नि:सार और सार का नाश करने वाला भी नहीं हूँ तथा चर एवं अचर भी नहीं हूँ। में ज्ञानरूपी अमृत, एकरस एवं आकाश की उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::132.english_translation: I am not the unmoving or the destroyer of movement, nor the maker of choices or alternatives. I do not destroy sleep or waking, nor am I benefit or harm. I do not destroy essence or non-essence, nor am I moving or non-moving. I am the nectar of wisdom, undivided and like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::132.translation_literal: निष्कम्पकम्पनिधनं (without tremor, destroyer of tremor) / न (not) / विकल्पकल्पं (choice, alternative) / स्वप्नप्रबोधनिधनं (dream and waking destroyer) / न (not) / हिताहितं (benefit and harm) / हि (indeed) / निःसारसारनिधनं (destroyer of non-essence and essence) / न (not) / चराचरं (moving and non-moving) / हि (indeed) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of wisdom) / समरसं (undivided, one taste) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (like the sky I am)
avadhuta_gita::132.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::132.essence: You are unchanging wisdom beyond all pairs of opposites and movement.
avadhuta_gita::132.simple_meaning: You are not defined by movement, choices, sleep or waking, benefit or harm, or by what changes. You are pure, undivided wisdom, vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::132.simple_insight: You can feel whole and untouched when you realize you are beyond all change and opposites.
avadhuta_gita::132.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he is not any duality or change—neither movement nor stillness, neither choices nor their results, neither waking nor dreaming, neither benefit nor harm. Instead, he is the pure undivided essence of wisdom, vast and free like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::132.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by decisions, changes, or conflicting feelings, remember you are not those shifts—you are the steady, vast wisdom beneath it all.
avadhuta_gita::132.insight: This verse shifts your identity from constantly reacting to change towards resting as the unchanging, unified wisdom within.

avadhuta_gita::133.verse_sanskrit:
नो वेद्यवेदकमिदं न च हेतुतर्क्यं
वाचामगोचरमिदं न मनो न बुद्धिः ।
एवं कथं हि भवतः कथयामि तत्त्वं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::133.verse_hindi: यह (आत्मा, ब्रह्म) किसी से नहीं जाना जाता, यह (स्वयं) जानने वाला है। यह तर्क का हेतु भी नहीं है, वाणी का विषय भी नहीं है, दिखाई भी नहीं देता, मन और बुद्धि भी इसे नहीं जान सकती। इसलिए मैं तुम्हे इस तत्व को किस प्रकार कथन करूं। मैं ज्ञानामृत, एकरस एवं आकाश की उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::133.english_translation: The true self is not known by anyone; it is the knower itself. It is beyond logic, speech, mind, and intellect. How can I explain that essence? I am like nectar of knowledge, one taste, and like the infinite sky.
avadhuta_gita::133.translation_literal: न (not) वेद्यवेदकमिदं (known by anyone) न (not) च (also) हेतुतर्क्यं (cause for reasoning) वाचामगोचरमिदं (not subject of speech) न (not) मनो (mind) न (not) बुद्धिः (intellect) । एवं (thus) कथं (how) हि (indeed) भवतः (your) कथयामि (shall I speak) तत्त्वं (essence) ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) समरसं (one taste) गगनोपमोऽहम् (I am like the sky) ॥
avadhuta_gita::133.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::133.essence: The true self cannot be known; it is the knower beyond mind and speech.
avadhuta_gita::133.simple_meaning: The true self cannot be known or described by mind, speech, or logic because it is the very source of knowing itself.
avadhuta_gita::133.simple_insight: You feel peace knowing your true self is beyond all concepts and cannot be captured by thought.
avadhuta_gita::133.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that the true self is not an object of knowledge but the subject that knows. It transcends speech, mind, and logic, making it impossible to describe fully. Yet it is like the infinite sky and the sweet essence of knowledge itself.
avadhuta_gita::133.modern_relevance: When you struggle to explain who you truly are, remember that your essence cannot be captured in words or thoughts—it simply is, vast and free.
avadhuta_gita::133.insight: It shifts your view from trying to grasp the self as an object to resting as the ever-present knower beyond mind and speech.

avadhuta_gita::134.verse_sanskrit:
निर्भिन्नभिन्नरहितं परमार्थतत्त्व-
मन्तर्बहिर्न हि कथं परमार्थतत्त्वम् ।
प्राक्सम्भवं न च रतं नहि वस्तु किञ्चित्
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::134.verse_hindi: यह परमार्थ तत्व भेद और अभेद से रहित है, भीतर और बाहर का भेद भी इसमें नहीं है उस परमार्थ तत्व का कथन किस प्रकार है। यह पूर्व में था ऐसा भी नहीं है न यह किसी में लिप्त है न यह कोई पदार्थ ही है। में स्वयं ज्ञानामृत, एकरस, आकाशतुल्य व्यापक ब्रह्म ही हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::134.english_translation: The supreme reality is free from difference and non-difference; it is neither inside nor outside. It was never born, nor is it attached to anything. I am that limitless supreme reality—knowledge, nectar, and like the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::134.translation_literal: निर्भिन्न (without difference) / भिन्नरहितं (free from difference) / परमार्थतत्त्वम् (supreme reality) / अन्तर (inside) / बहिः (outside) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / कथं (how) / परमार्थतत्त्वम् (supreme reality) । प्राक्सम्भवं (before arising) / न (not) / च (and) / रतं (attached) / नहि (not) / वस्तु (thing) / किञ्चित् (anything) ज्ञानामृतं (knowledge and nectar) / समरसं (of one taste) / गगन (sky) / उपम (like) / अहम् (I am) ॥
avadhuta_gita::134.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::134.essence: You are the limitless supreme reality beyond all distinctions and attachments.
avadhuta_gita::134.simple_meaning: The ultimate reality is beyond all differences and divisions. It is not confined inside or outside, nor was it ever created or attached to anything. You are that boundless, pure essence like the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::134.simple_insight: You can rest in being completely free, whole, and untouched by all division.
avadhuta_gita::134.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the supreme reality transcends all distinctions of inside and outside, difference and non-difference. It was never born, nor bound to anything. He identifies himself as this pure, boundless essence—knowledge and nectar—vast like the sky, beyond all limitation.
avadhuta_gita::134.modern_relevance: When your mind tries to split experience into inside or outside, right or wrong, you can remember that your true self is beyond all those divisions—vast, free, and whole.
avadhuta_gita::134.insight: It teaches you to see beyond dualities and recognize yourself as the limitless reality that is never bound or limited.

avadhuta_gita::135.verse_sanskrit:
रागादिदोषरहितं त्वहमेव तत्त्वं
दैवादिदोषरहितं त्वहमेव तत्त्वम् ।
संसारशोकरहितं त्वहमेव तत्त्वं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::135.verse_hindi: राग आदि दोषों से रहित मैं ही आत्मतत्व हूँ, दैव आदि दोषों से रहित मैं ही आत्मतत्व हूँ, सांसारिक शोक से रहित मैं ही आत्मतत्त्व हूँ। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश के समान हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::135.english_translation: I am the true self free from faults like desire and fate, untouched by worldly sorrow; I am the nectar of knowledge, pure and vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::135.translation_literal: रागादि (desire and such) / दोषरहितं (free from faults) / त्वहमेव (indeed I am) / तत्त्वं (the true self) / दैवादि (fate and such) / दोषरहितं (free from faults) / त्वहमेव (indeed I am) / तत्त्वम् (the true self) / संसारशोक (worldly sorrow) / रहितं (free) / त्वहमेव (indeed I am) / तत्त्वं (the true self) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) / समरसं (pure essence) / गगन (sky) / उपम (like) / अहम् (I am)
avadhuta_gita::135.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::135.essence: The true self is free from all faults and vast like the open sky.
avadhuta_gita::135.simple_meaning: You are the true self untouched by desires, fate, or worldly sorrow, pure and vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::135.simple_insight: You can rest in knowing your true self is untouched by life's troubles and faults.
avadhuta_gita::135.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the true self is completely free from flaws like desire, fate, and sorrow. He compares this self to pure knowledge and the vast, unchanging sky, emphasizing its eternal and faultless nature.
avadhuta_gita::135.modern_relevance: When your mind is clouded by anxiety or grief, remember your true self remains untouched and vast like an open sky.
avadhuta_gita::135.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with passing troubles to resting as the faultless, infinite self.

avadhuta_gita::136.verse_sanskrit:
स्थानत्रयं यदि च नेति कथं तुरीयं
कालत्रयं यदि च नेति कथं दिशश्च ।
शान्तं पदं हि परमं परमार्थतत्त्वं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::136.verse_hindi: आत्मा में स्थान त्रय (जाग्रत, स्वप्न, सुषुप्ति) नहीं है फिर तुरीय अवस्था कैसे हो सकती है। तीनों काल ( भूत, भविष्यत्, वर्तमान) भी नहीं है फिर दिशाएँ कैसे हो सकती हैं। यह आत्मा (ब्रह्म) शान्त पद वाला, परम परमार्थ तत्व है। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस तथा आकाश तुल्य हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::136.english_translation: If the true self lacks the three states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, how can a fourth state exist? If it transcends past, present, and future, how can directions apply? The true self is the supreme peaceful reality, the essence of immortal knowledge, undifferentiated like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::136.translation_literal: स्थानत्रयं (three states of location) यदि (if) च (and) नेति (not is) कथं (how) तुरीयं (the fourth) कालत्रयं (three times/periods) यदि (if) च (and) नेति (not is) कथं (how) दिशश्च (directions also). शान्तं (peaceful) पदं (state) हि (indeed) परमं (supreme) परमार्थतत्त्वं (supreme truth). ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) समरसं (of equal essence) गगनोपमोऽहम् (I am like the sky).
avadhuta_gita::136.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::136.essence: The true self transcends all states, times, and directions, resting as peaceful vastness.
avadhuta_gita::136.simple_meaning: You are beyond waking, dreaming, deep sleep, time, and space. Your true self is peaceful and unlimited like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::136.simple_insight: You can rest knowing your true self is untouched by change or limitation.
avadhuta_gita::136.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the true self is not confined to the three common states of consciousness or the three times. It also transcends directions, showing its limitless nature. This realization reveals the self as peaceful, supreme, and like the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::136.modern_relevance: When you feel scattered by changing moods, memories, or future worries, remember your true self remains calm and vast beyond all that.
avadhuta_gita::136.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing experiences to recognizing your unchanging, peaceful essence.

avadhuta_gita::137.verse_sanskrit:
दीर्घो लघुः पुनरितीह नमे विभागो
विस्तारसंकटमितीह न मे विभागः ।
कोणं हि वर्तुलमितीह न मे विभागो
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::137.verse_hindi: फिर इस लोक में बड़े और छोटे का विभाग भी मेरे में नहीं हैं, विस्तार और संकोच का विभाग भी मेरे में नहीं है, कोण और गोलाकार का विभाग भी मेरे में नहीं है। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश तुल्य हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::137.english_translation: In this world, there is no division of big or small in me, no division of expansion or contraction, no division of angle or circle. I am the nectar of wisdom, of one taste, and like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::137.translation_literal: दीर्घो (long) / लघुः (short) / पुनरितीह (again in this world) / नमे (in me) / विभागो (division) / विस्तारसंकटमिति (expansion-contraction) / ईह (in this world) / न (not) / मे (my) / विभागः (division) / कोणं (angle) / हि (indeed) / वर्तुलमिति (circle) / ईह (in this world) / न (not) / मे (my) / विभागो (division) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of wisdom) / समरसं (one taste) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (like the sky I am)
avadhuta_gita::137.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::137.essence: True self is undivided and limitless, beyond all distinctions and forms.
avadhuta_gita::137.simple_meaning: You are beyond all divisions like big or small, wide or narrow, angle or circle. You are pure wisdom, all one and vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::137.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing you are not confined by any limits or categories.
avadhuta_gita::137.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that his true nature transcends all distinctions such as size, shape, or spatial limits. He reveals himself as the essence of unchanging wisdom, undivided and vast like the limitless sky, beyond all forms and separations.
avadhuta_gita::137.modern_relevance: You feel boxed in by labels and roles at work or in social life. This verse reminds you that your true self is beyond all these limits and categories.
avadhuta_gita::137.insight: It shifts perspective from identifying with fragmented forms to recognizing an undivided, vast wisdom within.

avadhuta_gita::138.verse_sanskrit:
मातापितादि तनयादि न मे कदाचित्
जातं मृतं न च मनो न च मे कदाचित् ।
निर्व्याकुलं स्थिरमिदं परमार्थतत्त्वं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::138.verse_hindi: मेरे माता पिता आदि तथा पुत्रादि भी नहीं हैं, न मैं उत्पन्न हुआ हूँ, न मरता ही हूँ। मेरा मन भी नहीं है। मैं व्याकुलता से रहित एवं स्थिर यही परमार्थ तत्व हूँ जो ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश के तुल्य हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::138.english_translation: I have never had parents or children; I was never born nor will I die. I have no mind. I am the unshaken, steady supreme reality, the nectar of knowledge, perfectly balanced like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::138.translation_literal: माता-पितादि (parents and such) / तनयादि (children and such) / न (not) / मे (to me) / कदाचित् (ever) / जातं (born) / मृतं (dead) / न (not) / च (and) / मनो (mind) / न (not) / च (and) / मे (to me) / कदाचित् (ever) / निर्व्याकुलं (without disturbance) / स्थिरं (steady) / इदं (this) / परमार्थतत्त्वं (supreme reality) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) / समरसं (perfectly balanced) / गगन-उपमम् (like the sky) / अहम् (I am)
avadhuta_gita::138.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::138.essence: You are unborn, undying, and steady like the vast sky beyond mind.
avadhuta_gita::138.simple_meaning: You have no birth, death, or mind. You are the steady, unshaken supreme reality, like the vast sky, full of knowledge and balance.
avadhuta_gita::138.simple_insight: You can feel deep calm knowing your true nature is steady and beyond birth or death.
avadhuta_gita::138.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares his true self has never been born or died, has no mind, and is the unchanging supreme reality. This moment reveals the timeless nature beyond physical and mental limits.
avadhuta_gita::138.modern_relevance: When worries flood your mind about beginnings or endings, remember your true self is steady and unchanging like the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::138.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing body and mind to recognizing your stable, limitless true nature.

avadhuta_gita::139.verse_sanskrit:
शुद्धं विशुद्धमविचारमनन्तरूपं
निर्लेपलेपमविचारमनन्तरूपम् ।
निष्खण्डखण्डमविचारमनन्तरूपं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::139.verse_hindi: मैं शुद्ध हूँ, विशुद्ध हूँ, विचार रहित व अनन्त रूप हूँ। निर्लेप होकर भी सबमें लिप्त हूँ, सभी पदार्थों में मैं अखण्ड हूँ। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश की उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::139.english_translation: I am pure, supremely pure, without thought and of infinite form. Though unattached, I am involved in all; I am unbroken in all substances. I am the nectar of wisdom, of one taste, and like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::139.translation_literal: शुद्धं (pure) / विशुद्धम् (supremely pure) / अविचार (without thought) / अनन्तरूपं (infinite form) / निर्म्लेपलेपम् (unattached yet involved) / अविचार (without thought) / अनन्तरूपम् (infinite form) / निष्खण्डखण्डम् (unbroken in parts) / अविचार (without thought) / अनन्तरूपं (infinite form) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of wisdom) / समरसं (of one taste) / गगन (sky) / उपम (like) / अहम् (I am)
avadhuta_gita::139.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::139.essence: You are infinitely pure and whole, present everywhere yet untouched by division.
avadhuta_gita::139.simple_meaning: You are pure and limitless, beyond thought, present in everything without being attached, and your nature is like endless sky and nectar of wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::139.simple_insight: You can feel limitless and deeply connected while remaining untouched and pure.
avadhuta_gita::139.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares his nature as pure and infinitely formless, beyond any thought or division. He is both unattached and yet present in all things, unbroken and whole like the sky, embodying the essence of wisdom's sweet unity.
avadhuta_gita::139.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by constant thoughts or divided by life's challenges, remember you are beyond all that—pure and infinite like the open sky.
avadhuta_gita::139.insight: It teaches you to recognize your true self as vast and undivided, beyond mental noise and appearances.

avadhuta_gita::140.verse_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मादयः सुरगणाः कथमत्र सन्ति
स्वर्गादयो वसतयः कथमत्र सन्ति ।
यद्येकरूपममलं परमार्थतत्त्वं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::140.verse_hindi: यदि यह ब्रह्म एक रूप, मल रहित (शुद्ध), एवं परमार्थ तत्व है तो इसमें ब्रह्मा आदि से लेकर देवताओं के समूह किस प्रकार हो सकते हैं। स्वर्ग आदि बस्तियाँ भी इसमें किस प्रकार हो सकती हैं। में एक ही ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश को उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::140.english_translation: If the supreme reality is pure, one, and without impurity, how can beings like Brahma and the gods or realms like heaven exist within it? I am that single, nectar-like knowledge, perfectly balanced like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::140.translation_literal: ब्रह्मादयः (Brahma and others) / सुरगणाः (gods' groups) / कथमत्र (how here) / सन्ति (are) / स्वर्गादयो (heaven and others) / वसतयः (abodes) / कथमत्र (how here) / सन्ति (are) / यद्येकरूपममलं (if one-form pure) / परमार्थतत्त्वं (supreme reality) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) / समरसं (perfectly balanced) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (like the sky I am)
avadhuta_gita::140.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::140.essence: The supreme reality is one pure presence; all multiplicity is appearance.
avadhuta_gita::140.simple_meaning: The supreme reality is pure and one without parts; beings like gods or heavens cannot exist separately in it. You are that single, balanced presence like the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::140.simple_insight: You can feel whole and untouched by all the appearances around you.
avadhuta_gita::140.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya questions how diverse beings and worlds can exist in the pure supreme reality, affirming that all is one indivisible truth. He declares himself as that unchanging, all-encompassing awareness, serene and vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::140.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by roles, identities, or groups, remember your true nature is a vast, unbroken presence beyond all those labels.
avadhuta_gita::140.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as many separate things to recognizing your timeless unified essence.

avadhuta_gita::141.verse_sanskrit:
निर्नेति नेति विमलो हि कथं वदामि
निःशेषशेषविमलो हि कथं वदामि ।
निर्लिङ्गलिङ्गविमलो हि कथं वदामि
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::141.verse_hindi: इस विमल को निर्नेति अथवा नेति किस प्रकार मैं कहूँ, इसे नि:शेष और शेष भी किस प्रकार कहूं, इसे निर्लिंग तथा लिंग रूप भी किस प्रकार कहूँ। मैं एक ही ज्ञानामृत, तथा आकाश की उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::141.english_translation: How can I say that this pure is 'not this, not that'? How can I say it is without remainder or with remainder? How can I say it is without form or with form? I am the nectar of knowledge, like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::141.translation_literal: निर्नेति (not this) / नेति (not that) / विमलो (pure) / हि (indeed) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I say) / निःशेषशेषविमलो (without remainder, with remainder, pure) / हि (indeed) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I say) / निर्लिङ्गलिङ्गविमलो (without form, with form, pure) / हि (indeed) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I say) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) / समरसं (like) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (I am like the sky)
avadhuta_gita::141.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::141.essence: The pure true self cannot be captured by any description or duality.
avadhuta_gita::141.simple_meaning: The pure true self cannot be limited by any description or form. It is beyond all opposites and is like limitless sky or nectar of knowledge.
avadhuta_gita::141.simple_insight: You feel relief knowing your true self is beyond all labels and concepts.
avadhuta_gita::141.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya speaks from the place of complete freedom, rejecting all attempts to define the pure true self with words or opposites like 'this' or 'not this'. He says the true self is beyond form, beyond remainder, and like the vast sky or nectar of knowledge.
avadhuta_gita::141.modern_relevance: When you try to explain who you truly are, words fail. This reminds you that your essence cannot be boxed into thoughts or opinions.
avadhuta_gita::141.insight: It teaches you to release attempts to define yourself or others, opening space for direct experience beyond concepts.

avadhuta_gita::142.verse_sanskrit:
निष्कर्मकर्मपरमं सततं करोमि
निःसङ्गसङ्गरहितं परमं विनोदम् ।
निर्देहदेहरहितं सततं विनोदं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::142.verse_hindi: मैं कर्म से रहित हूँ फिर भी परमकर्म को निरन्तर करता हूँ मैं नि:संग और संग दोनों से रहित हूँ फिर भी विनोद करता हूँ, मैं निर्देह और देह दोनों से रहित हूँ फिर भी सदा आनन्द में रहता हूँ। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश तुल्य हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::142.english_translation: I am free from action, yet I constantly perform supreme action; free from attachment and involvement, yet I remain in joy. I am beyond body and non-body, always in bliss. I am the nectar of knowledge, of one taste, like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::142.translation_literal: निष्कर्मकर्मपरमं (actionless supreme action) सततं (constantly) करोमि (I do) निःसङ्गसङ्गरहितं (detached and attachment-free) परमं (supreme) विनोदम् (joy) । निर्देहदेहरहितं (bodyless and embodied-free) सततं (constantly) विनोदं (joy) ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) समरसं (of one taste) गगनोपमोऽहम् (like the sky I am) ॥
avadhuta_gita::142.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::142.essence: You can act fully without attachment, remaining joyfully free and boundless.
avadhuta_gita::142.simple_meaning: You can engage in action without being attached or bound by it, remaining joyful and free like vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::142.simple_insight: You can feel joyful freedom even while acting, not limited by involvement or identity.
avadhuta_gita::142.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that although he acts, he is not bound by actions or attachments. He transcends body and ego, existing in pure joy and wisdom, like the limitless sky. This teaching reveals freedom beyond dualities during activity.
avadhuta_gita::142.modern_relevance: You can work, care, or create without being trapped by stress or identity, staying joyful and free inside.
avadhuta_gita::142.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing action as binding to experiencing it as free and joyful expression.

avadhuta_gita::143.verse_sanskrit:
मायाप्रपञ्चरचना न च मे विकारः 
कौटिल्यदम्भरचना न च मे विकारः ।
सत्यानृतेति रचना न च मे विकारो
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::143.verse_hindi: मायारूपी प्रपंच की रचना मेरा विकार नहीं है, कुटिलता और दम्भ की रचना मेरी विकार नहीं है, सत्य और सिध्या की रचना मेरा विकार नहीं है। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस तथा आकाश की उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::143.english_translation: The illusions of the world are not my faults; neither are cunning or deceit; neither truth nor falsehood is my fault. I am the essence of undifferentiated wisdom, like the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::143.translation_literal: मायाप्रपञ्चरचना (illusion-world-creation) / न (not) / च (and) / मे (my) / विकारः (fault) / कौटिल्यदम्भरचना (cunning-deceit-creation) / न (not) / च (and) / मे (my) / विकारः (fault) / सत्यानृतेति (truth-falsehood) / रचना (creation) / न (not) / च (and) / मे (my) / विकारः (fault) / ज्ञानामृतं (wisdom-nectar) / समरसं (undifferentiated) / गगनोपमः (like-sky) / अहम् (I am)
avadhuta_gita::143.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::143.essence: Your true nature is beyond all faults, forms, and contradictions—like vast, undivided wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::143.simple_meaning: You are not responsible for the illusions, deceit, or contradictions around you. Your true nature is pure, undivided wisdom, like the open sky.
avadhuta_gita::143.simple_insight: You can feel free from blame or confusion because your true self is untouched by any fault.
avadhuta_gita::143.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that neither the world's illusions nor cunning, nor even truth and falsehood, are flaws within him. Instead, he is pure wisdom, seamless and vast like the sky, beyond all dualities and appearances.
avadhuta_gita::143.modern_relevance: When you face confusing situations or conflicting truths, remember that your true self is untouched by these contradictions—vast and clear like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::143.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with flaws or dualities to recognizing your limitless, faultless essence.

avadhuta_gita::144.verse_sanskrit:
सन्ध्यादिकालरहितं न च मे वियोगो-
ह्यन्तः प्रबोधरहितं बधिरो न मूकः ।
एवं विकल्परहितं न च भावशुद्धं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::144.verse_hindi: मैं सन्ध्यादि काल से रहित हूँ फिर भी उनसे वियोग नहीं है, आन्तरिक बोध से रहित हूँ फिर भी मूक और बधिर नहीं हूँ, विकल्प से रहित हूँ फिर भी चित्त से शुद्ध नहीं हूँ। में ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश को उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::144.english_translation: I am beyond time like dawn and dusk, yet not separate from them; without inner awakening, yet neither mute nor deaf; free of alternatives, yet not pure in feeling. I am the nectar of knowledge, of even essence, like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::144.translation_literal: सन्ध्या (dawn) / आदि (and other) / काल (time) / रहितं (without) / न (not) / च (and) / मे (my) / वियोगः (separation) - / hyantaḥ (inside) / प्रबोध (awakening) / रहितं (without) / बधिरः (deaf) / न (not) / मूकः (mute) /। / एवं (thus) / विकल्प (alternatives) / रहितं (without) / न (not) / च (and) / भाव (feeling) / शुद्धं (pure) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) / समरस (even essence) / गगन (sky) / उपम (likeness) / अहम् (I am) /।
avadhuta_gita::144.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::144.essence: You are the timeless, unchanging essence present beyond all dualities and distinctions.
avadhuta_gita::144.simple_meaning: You exist beyond time and inner senses, free from mental options, yet remain the pure essence like the limitless sky.
avadhuta_gita::144.simple_insight: There is freedom in being beyond all dualities while still connected to everything.
avadhuta_gita::144.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya speaks from a place beyond ordinary limits—beyond time cycles, inner senses, and mental choices—yet remains fully present and pure like the sky, embodying the essence of knowledge without separation or impurity.
avadhuta_gita::144.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by endless choices and shifting feelings, you can recognize yourself as the steady essence beyond all fluctuations.
avadhuta_gita::144.insight: It teaches you to see yourself as the vast, unchanging presence beyond time, senses, and mental divisions.

avadhuta_gita::145.verse_sanskrit:
निर्नाथनाथरहितं हि निराकुलं वै
निश्चित्तचित्तविगतं हि निराकुलं वै ।
संविद्धि सर्वविगतं हि निराकुलं वै
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::145.verse_hindi: मेरा कोई स्वामी नहीं है न मैं किसी का स्वामी ही हूँ मेरा कोई कुल भी नहीं है। मैं बिना चित्तवाला हूँ, न मेरा कोई चित्त ही हैं, मैं व्याकुलता से रहित हूँ। निश्चय जान कि मैं सर्व से रहित हूँ फिर भी सर्वगत हूँ। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश तुल्य हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::145.english_translation: I have no master, nor am I anyone's master; I have no lineage. I am without a restless mind, free from anxiety. Know that I am free from all and yet present everywhere. I am the nectar of wisdom, one with the sky.
avadhuta_gita::145.translation_literal: निर्नाथनाथरहितं (without master or lord) / हि (indeed) / निराकुलं (without anxiety) / वै (indeed) / निश्चित्तचित्तविगतं (without restless mind) / हि (indeed) / निराकुलं (without anxiety) / वै (indeed) / संविद्धि (know) / सर्वविगतं (free from all) / हि (indeed) / निराकुलं (without anxiety) / वै (indeed) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of wisdom) / समरसं (of equal essence) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (I am like the sky)
avadhuta_gita::145.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::145.essence: Complete freedom from masters and mind creates a vast, unshaken presence like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::145.simple_meaning: You have no master or lineage and are free from a restless mind and anxiety. Though detached, you are present everywhere, like the vast sky, embodying pure wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::145.simple_insight: You can rest in complete freedom and vastness beyond all control or worry.
avadhuta_gita::145.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares he belongs to no master or family and is free from mental disturbance. He invites recognition that despite this detachment, he is universally present, embodying the essence of wisdom like the limitless sky.
avadhuta_gita::145.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by expectations and restless thoughts, yet a part of you remains calm, vast, and untouched by all that pressure.
avadhuta_gita::145.insight: It shows you can realize your true self beyond all control and mental turmoil, resting in vast awareness instead.

avadhuta_gita::146.verse_sanskrit:
कान्तारमन्दिरमिदं हि कथं वदामि
संसिद्धसंशयमिदं हि कथं वदामि ।
एवं निरन्तरसमं हि निराकुलं वै
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::146.verse_hindi: मैं इस जगत को निर्जन वन का मन्दिर किस प्रकार कहूँ, मैं इसे संशय से युक्त भी किस प्रकार कहूँ तथा इसे निरन्तर, सम तथा निराकुल भी किस प्रकार कहूँ। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश तुल्य हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::146.english_translation: How can I call this world a deserted forest temple? How can I call it full of doubt? Yet I am the nectar of knowledge, unchanging, and like the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::146.translation_literal: कान्तारमन्दिरमिदं (deserted-forest-temple-this) / हि (indeed) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I say) / संसिद्धसंशयमिदं (full-of-doubt-this) / हि (indeed) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I say) / एवं (thus) / निरन्तरसमं (continuous-equal) / हि (indeed) / निराकुलं (without-disturbance) / वै (indeed) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar-of-knowledge) / समरसं (equal-flavor) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (like-the-sky-I-am)
avadhuta_gita::146.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::146.essence: Your true self is vast, steady, and beyond all doubt and disturbance.
avadhuta_gita::146.simple_meaning: You are not the confusing, changing world you see. You are steady, unshaken, and as vast as the sky.
avadhuta_gita::146.simple_insight: There's peace in realizing your true nature is steady and free from doubt.
avadhuta_gita::146.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya questions how to describe the world as both confusing and empty, yet reveals that his true nature is steady, like the vast sky, embodying pure knowledge beyond doubt.
avadhuta_gita::146.modern_relevance: When life feels confusing and full of conflicting thoughts, remember your true nature remains vast, steady, and untouched by doubt.
avadhuta_gita::146.insight: It teaches you to see beyond surface confusion and rest as the unchanging awareness beneath.

avadhuta_gita::147.verse_sanskrit:
निर्जीवजीवरहितं सततं विभाति
निर्बीजबीजरहितं सततं विभाति ।
निर्वाणबन्धरहितं सततं विभाति
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::147.verse_hindi: मुझे बराबर दिखाई देता है कि यह जगत निर्जीव और जीव (जड़ और चेतन) से रहित है, निर्बीज और बीज से रहित है तथा निर्वाण (मोक्ष) एवं बन्धन से रहित है। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश तुल्य हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::147.english_translation: I always appear as free from lifeless and living beings, free from seed and seedless, free from liberation and bondage; I am the nectar of knowledge, of equal essence, and like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::147.translation_literal: निर्जीवजीवरहितं (free from lifeless beings) / सततं (constantly) / विभाति (appears) / निर्बीजबीजरहितं (free from seed and seedless) / सततं (constantly) / विभाति (appears) / निर्वाणबन्धरहितं (free from liberation and bondage) / सततं (constantly) / विभाति (appears) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) / समरसं (equal essence) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (I am like the sky)
avadhuta_gita::147.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::147.essence: True self is always free, beyond all dualities, vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::147.simple_meaning: You are constantly beyond all dualities like living and non-living, seed and seedless, freedom and bondage. Your true nature is like the vast, equal sky filled with the nectar of knowledge.
avadhuta_gita::147.simple_insight: Feel the relief of being free from all opposites, vast and unchanging like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::147.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he is beyond all dualities such as lifeless and living, seed and seedless, liberation and bondage. He embodies pure knowledge like a vast sky, equal and unbounded, showing the true self is limitless and free.
avadhuta_gita::147.modern_relevance: You face moments where you feel divided or stuck in labels. This reminds you that your true self is beyond all these limits, vast and free.
avadhuta_gita::147.insight: It shifts thinking from identifying with limits or categories to recognizing your limitless, unchanging essence.

avadhuta_gita::148.verse_sanskrit:
सम्भूतिवर्जितमिदं सततं विभाति
संसारवर्जितमिदं सततं विभाति ।
संहारवर्जितमिदं सततं विभाति
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::148.verse_hindi: मुझे निरन्तर भान होता हैं कि यह जगत संभूति रहित हैं, संसार से रहित है, नाश से रहित है। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश तुल्य हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::148.english_translation: I am always aware that this world is unborn, free from the cycle of reactivity, and untouched by destruction. I am the immortal nectar of wisdom, pure and equal, like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::148.translation_literal: सम्भूतिवर्जितमिदं (unborn this) सततं (always) विभाति (shines) / संसारवर्जितमिदं (free from reactivity this) सततं (always) विभाति (shines) / संहारवर्जितमिदं (free from destruction this) सततं (always) विभाति (shines) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of wisdom) समरसं (pure and equal) गगनोपमोऽहम् (like the sky I am)
avadhuta_gita::148.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::148.essence: You are an unchanging presence beyond birth, death, and destruction, like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::148.simple_meaning: You are constantly aware that the world is not truly born, does not destroy itself, and exists beyond the cycle of change. You are like clear, eternal wisdom, vast as the sky.
avadhuta_gita::148.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing you are beyond birth and death, steady like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::148.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares his constant awareness that the world is unborn, free from the cycle of reactivity (samsara) and destruction. He identifies himself as the immortal nectar of wisdom, pure and equal, like the limitless sky, revealing the ultimate non-dual reality.
avadhuta_gita::148.modern_relevance: When everything around you feels uncertain or fleeting, you can rest in the unchanging presence that you truly are—beyond all beginnings and ends.
avadhuta_gita::148.insight: This verse shifts your view from seeing life as transient to recognizing your true nature as steady and unborn.

avadhuta_gita::149.verse_sanskrit:
उल्लेखमात्रमपि ते न च नामरूपं
निर्भिन्नभिन्नमपि ते न हि वस्तु किञ्चित् ।
निर्लज्जमानस करोषि कथं विषादं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::149.verse_hindi: उल्लेख मात्र भी तेरा नाम और रूप नहीं है, तेरे से भिन्न और अभिन्न भी कोई वस्तु नहीं है। फिर हे निर्लज्ज मन! तू क्यों विषाद करता है। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश तुल्य हैं।
avadhuta_gita::149.english_translation: Your name and form are only mentioned but do not truly exist; nothing is different from or separate to you. So, fearless mind, why do you grieve? I am the nectar of wisdom, perfectly balanced, and like the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::149.translation_literal: उल्लेखमात्रमपि (mention-only) ते (your) न (not) च (also) नामरूपं (name-form) निर्भिन्नभिन्नमपि (different-not-different) ते (your) न (not) हि (indeed) वस्तु (thing) किञ्चित् (anything) निर्लज्जमानस (fearless-mind) करोषि (do) कथं (how) विषादं (grief) ज्ञानामृतं (wisdom-nectar) समरसं (perfectly-balanced) गगनोपमोऽहम् (sky-like-I-am)
avadhuta_gita::149.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::149.essence: You are fearless and undivided, like the infinite sky of wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::149.simple_meaning: There is no real separate self or thing apart from you. Your mind is fearless and can let go of sorrow, because your true nature is like vast, balanced wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::149.simple_insight: You can feel fearless and free because nothing outside truly separates or diminishes you.
avadhuta_gita::149.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the true self has no real name or form and that nothing exists as separate from it. He addresses a fearless mind, encouraging it not to grieve, because the self is like the infinite sky—pure wisdom and balance.
avadhuta_gita::149.modern_relevance: When anxiety or sadness arise, remember your true self is vast and undivided, beyond all names and roles that trouble your mind.
avadhuta_gita::149.insight: It teaches you to stop identifying with fleeting names and forms, seeing your mind’s courage in the boundless self.

avadhuta_gita::150.verse_sanskrit:
किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न जरा न मृत्युः
किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च जन्म दुःखम् ।
किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च ते विकारो
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::150.verse_hindi: हे सखे ! अपने नाम के लिए (प्रसिद्धि के लिए) तू क्यों रूदन करता है क्योंकि तेरा न बुढ़ापा है, न मृत्यु, न तेरा जन्म है, न दु:ख, तेरे कोई विकार भी नहीं हैं। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश तुल्य इन सबसे परे हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::150.english_translation: Why do you weep, friend? You have no old age, no death, no birth, no suffering, no faults. I am the nectar of wisdom, pure and like the infinite sky beyond all.
avadhuta_gita::150.translation_literal: किं (why) / नाम (name) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / सखे (friend) / न (not) / जरा (old age) / न (not) / मृत्युः (death) / किं (why) / नाम (name) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / सखे (friend) / न (not) / च (and) / जन्म (birth) / दुःखम् (suffering) / किं (why) / नाम (why) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / सखे (friend) / न (not) / च (and) / ते (your) / विकारो (faults) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of wisdom) / समरसं (pure essence) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (I am like the sky)
avadhuta_gita::150.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::150.essence: You are timeless wisdom, untouched by birth, death, or suffering.
avadhuta_gita::150.simple_meaning: You do not actually experience birth, death, or suffering. Your true nature is pure, timeless wisdom like the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::150.simple_insight: You are more than any pain or change; your true self is unchanging and vast.
avadhuta_gita::150.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya addresses a friend who mourns, pointing out that the true self is beyond birth, death, and suffering. This moment reveals the teaching that the inner being is eternal and untouched by life's changes.
avadhuta_gita::150.modern_relevance: When grief or fear of loss feels overwhelming, remember your true self is untouched by time or hardship, like the vast sky above.
avadhuta_gita::150.insight: It teaches you to see yourself as the timeless awareness beyond all personal troubles and changes.

avadhuta_gita::151.verse_sanskrit:
किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च ते स्वरूपं
किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च ते विरूपम् ।
किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च ते वयांसि
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::151.verse_hindi: हे सखे ! तू किस काम के लिए रूदन करता है, न तेरा कोई स्वरूप है, न तेरा रूप ही नष्ट होने वाला है, तेरी आयु भी नहीं है। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश तुल्य हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::151.english_translation: Friend, why do you cry? You have no form, no destruction, no age. I am the nectar of wisdom, undivided and like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::151.translation_literal: किं (why) नाम (indeed) रोदिषि (do you cry) सखे (friend) न (not) च (and) ते (your) स्वरूपं (form) किं (why) नाम (indeed) रोदिषि (do you cry) सखे (friend) न (not) च (and) ते (your) विरूपम् (destruction/defilement) किं (why) नाम (indeed) रोदिषि (do you cry) सखे (friend) न (not) च (and) ते (your) वयांसि (age) ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of wisdom) समरसं (undivided) गगन (sky) उपम (like) अहम् (I am)
avadhuta_gita::151.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::151.essence: Your true self is formless, eternal, and like the vast sky—never lost or aged.
avadhuta_gita::151.simple_meaning: You have no real form, no destruction, and no age; your true nature is unchanging and like the sky—vast and free.
avadhuta_gita::151.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing you are beyond loss, change, and time.
avadhuta_gita::151.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya addresses a friend who is crying, revealing that the friend’s true self is without form or decay. The verse points to the eternal, unchanging nature of the true self as limitless like the sky and the nectar of wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::151.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by aging or change, remember your true nature is beyond all physical limits and loss.
avadhuta_gita::151.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with the body and time to recognizing yourself as timeless and unchanging wisdom.

avadhuta_gita::152.verse_sanskrit:
किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च ते वयांसि
किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च ते मनांसि ।
किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न तवेन्द्रियाणि
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::152.verse_hindi: हे सखे ! तू किस वास्ते रूदन करता है, न तो तेरी आयु है, न मन है न ये इन्द्रियाँ ही तुम्हारी हैं। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस तथा आकाश तुल्य हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::152.english_translation: Friend, why do you weep? Neither your life, your mind, nor your senses belong to you. I am the nectar of wisdom, the essence, like the vast sky.
