avadhuta_gita::152.translation_literal: किं (why) नाम (indeed) रोदिषि (you weep) सखे (friend) न (not) च (and) ते (your) वयांसि (lifespans) किं (why) नाम (indeed) रोदिषि (you weep) सखे (friend) न (not) च (and) ते (your) मनांसि (minds) किं (why) नाम (indeed) रोदिषि (you weep) सखे (friend) न (not) तवेन्द्रियाणि (your senses) ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of wisdom) समरसं (essence) गगनोपमोऽहम् (like the sky I am)
avadhuta_gita::152.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::152.essence: You are not your mind, senses, or lifespan but the limitless essence of wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::152.simple_meaning: You do not truly own your lifespan, mind, or senses. Your true nature is like the vast sky — the pure essence of wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::152.simple_insight: There's peace in knowing your true self is beyond the mind and body.
avadhuta_gita::152.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya addresses a friend grieving, pointing out that neither lifespan, mind, nor senses belong ultimately to anyone. Instead, the true self is the unchanging essence of wisdom, vast and like the sky, untouched by grief.
avadhuta_gita::152.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by emotions or loss, remember your true self is larger than these passing experiences.
avadhuta_gita::152.insight: This verse shifts your view from attachment to transient things toward recognizing your boundless, unchanging self.

avadhuta_gita::153.verse_sanskrit:
किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च तेऽस्ति कामः
किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च ते प्रलोभः ।
किं नाम रोदिषि सखे न च ते विमोहो
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::153.verse_hindi: हे सखे! तू किसलिए रूदन करता है, तू काम (कामना) भी नहीं है, न तेरा लोभ ही हैं, विमोह भी तेरा नहीं है। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश तुल्य हूँ ऐसा जान।
avadhuta_gita::153.english_translation: Why do you weep, friend? You have no desire, no greed, no confusion. Know that I am the nectar of wisdom, pure and like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::153.translation_literal: किं (why) / नाम (indeed) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / सखे (friend) / न (not) / च (and) / तेऽस्ति (you have) / कामः (desire) । किम् (why) / नाम (indeed) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / सखे (friend) / न (not) / च (and) / ते (your) / प्रलोभः (greed) । किम् (why) / नाम (indeed) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / सखे (friend) / न (not) / च (and) / ते (your) / विमोहो (confusion) । ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of wisdom) / समरसं (pure essence) / गगनोपमः (like the sky) / अहम् (I am) ॥
avadhuta_gita::153.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::153.essence: You are not your desires or confusion; you are the limitless nectar of wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::153.simple_meaning: You are not bound by desire, greed, or confusion. Your true nature is pure wisdom, vast and clear like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::153.simple_insight: There is freedom in seeing yourself beyond craving and confusion, as boundless wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::153.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya addresses a friend who weeps despite lacking desire, greed, or confusion. He reveals their true self as the pure, vast essence of wisdom—like the sky and the nectar of knowledge—pointing to their innate freedom.
avadhuta_gita::153.modern_relevance: You catch yourself overwhelmed by worries or cravings, yet realize none truly define you. Your true self is calm and vast beyond them.
avadhuta_gita::153.insight: It teaches you to recognize that your true nature is untouched by fleeting emotions or desires, revealing your limitless essence.

avadhuta_gita::154.verse_sanskrit:
ऐश्वर्यमिच्छसि कथं न च ते धनानि
ऐश्वर्यमिच्छसि कथं न च ते हि पत्नी ।
ऐश्वर्यमिच्छसि कथं न च ते ममेति
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::154.verse_hindi: तू ऐश्वर्य की किस प्रकार इच्छा करता हैं। ये धन तेरा नहीं है, पलि भी तेरी नहीं है, तेरा मेरा ऐसा कहना भी नहीं है। तू ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश को उपमा वाला आत्मा है वही में हूँ ऐसा जान।
avadhuta_gita::154.english_translation: You desire wealth, but the riches are not truly yours; you desire a wife, but she is not yours; you claim 'mine,' but even that is not yours. Know that I am the immortal essence of knowledge, like the sky, unchanging and pure.
avadhuta_gita::154.translation_literal: ऐश्वर्यमिच्छसि (you desire wealth) कथं (how) न (not) च (also) ते (your) धनानि (riches) / ऐश्वर्यमिच्छसि (you desire wealth) कथं (how) न (not) च (also) ते (your) हि (indeed) पत्नी (wife) / ऐश्वर्यमिच्छसि (you desire wealth) कथं (how) न (not) च (also) ते (your) ममेति (mine-saying) / ज्ञानामृतं (immortal essence of knowledge) समरसं (of equal taste or essence) गगनोपमोऽहम् (I am like the sky)
avadhuta_gita::154.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::154.essence: You cannot truly own anything; your true self is the limitless, eternal essence.
avadhuta_gita::154.simple_meaning: You might want wealth or relationships, but nothing truly belongs to you. Your real self is the eternal, pure essence like the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::154.simple_insight: There is peace in seeing yourself as beyond possession and personal claims.
avadhuta_gita::154.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya speaks to the illusion of ownership in human desires. Though you want wealth and relationships, none truly belong to you. He reveals that the true self is the unchanging, immortal essence, like the sky, beyond all attachments.
avadhuta_gita::154.modern_relevance: When you stress over keeping things—money, partnerships, status—you forget that your true being is untouched by all that comes and goes.
avadhuta_gita::154.insight: It shifts your view from clinging to ownership toward recognizing your self as the vast, unchanging essence.

avadhuta_gita::155.verse_sanskrit:
लिङ्गप्रपञ्चजनुषी न च ते न मे च
निर्लज्जमानसमिदं च विभाति भिन्नम् ।
निर्भेदभेदरहितं न च ते न मे च
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::155.verse_hindi: इस चिह्न रूपी जगत प्रपंच की उत्पत्ति न तुझसे हुई है न मुझसे, किन्तु इस लज्जा रहित मन को यह भिन्न प्रतीत होती है। यह निर्भेद और भेद रहित जगत भी न तेरा है, न मेरा। मैं एक ही ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश को उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::155.english_translation: This world of forms and appearances is born neither from you nor from me; yet the shameless mind perceives it as different. This world, without distinction or separation, is neither yours nor mine. I am the undivided nectar of wisdom, homogeneous and like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::155.translation_literal: लिङ्गप्रपञ्चजनुषी (form-appearance-origin) न (not) च (and) ते (your) न (not) मे (my) च (and) निर्लज्जमानसमिदं (shameless-mind-this) च (and) विभाति (appears) भिन्नम् (different)। निर्भेदभेदरहितं (without-difference-and-non-difference) न (not) च (and) ते (your) न (not) मे (my) च (and) ज्ञानामृतं (wisdom-nectar) समरसं (homogeneous) गगनोपमोऽहम् (like-sky-I-am) ॥
avadhuta_gita::155.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::155.essence: Separation is an illusion; your true nature is the undivided infinite essence.
avadhuta_gita::155.simple_meaning: The world of forms does not belong to you or me. The mind wrongly sees separation, but the true essence is one, undivided, and like the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::155.simple_insight: You can feel divided, yet your true self is whole and boundless like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::155.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that the visible world of forms and differences is not truly created by 'you' or 'me.' The restless mind wrongly sees separation, but in reality, the world is without division, and the true self is like the limitless sky, unified and pure wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::155.modern_relevance: When you face conflict or division, remember that beneath appearances, the true reality is unified and beyond separation.
avadhuta_gita::155.insight: It teaches you to see past mental divisions and recognize your identity as the undivided essence beyond form.

avadhuta_gita::156.verse_sanskrit:
नो वाणुमात्रमपि ते हि विरागरूपं
नो वाणुमात्रमपि ते हि सरागरूपम् ।
नो वाणुमात्रमपि ते हि सकामरूपं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::156.verse_hindi: तेरा अणु मात्र भी विराग रूप नहीं है, तुम्हारा अणु मात्र भी राग रूप नहीं है, तेरा अणु मात्र भी सकाम रूप नहीं है। मैं एक ही ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश तुल्य हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::156.english_translation: Not even your smallest particle is of detachment, attachment, or desire; I am the undifferentiated nectar of wisdom, like the vast sky.
avadhuta_gita::156.translation_literal: नो (not) / वाणुमात्रमपि (even the smallest particle) / ते (of you) / हि (indeed) / विरागरूपं (form of detachment) / नो (not) / वाणुमात्रमपि (even the smallest particle) / ते (of you) / हि (indeed) / सरागरूपम् (form of attachment) / नो (not) / वाणुमात्रमपि (even the smallest particle) / ते (of you) / हि (indeed) / सकामरूपं (form of desire) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) / समरसं (undifferentiated essence) / गगनोपम (like the sky) / अहम् (I am)
avadhuta_gita::156.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::156.essence: Your true nature is pure, desireless wisdom as vast as the sky.
avadhuta_gita::156.simple_meaning: Nothing in you, not even the tiniest part, is truly attachment, detachment, or desire. You are the pure, undivided essence of wisdom, like the limitless sky.
avadhuta_gita::156.simple_insight: You can feel vast and free because your true nature is beyond all craving or rejection.
avadhuta_gita::156.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that no part of your being is defined by wanting, not wanting, or desire. Instead, your essence is the pure nectar of knowledge, boundless and unchanging like the sky. This verse points to the complete unity and freedom of the true self.
avadhuta_gita::156.modern_relevance: When you feel restless with wanting or trying to avoid things, remember you are deeper than all that—a vast, unchanging presence within.
avadhuta_gita::156.insight: This verse shifts your view from identifying with fleeting feelings to recognizing your timeless, desire-free essence.

avadhuta_gita::157.verse_sanskrit:
ध्याता न ते हि हृदये न च ते समाधि-
र्ध्यानं न ते हि हृदये न बहिः प्रदेशः ।
ध्येयं न चेति हृदये न हि वस्तु कालो
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::157.verse_hindi: तेरे हृदय में न कोई ध्याता है, न समाधि और ध्यान ही है। तेरे हृदय में बाह्य प्रदेश भी नहीं है, तेरे हृदय में न ध्येय ही है। न काल जैसी कोई वस्तु ही है। मैं ज्ञानामृत, समरस एवं आकाश की उपमा वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::157.english_translation: In your heart there is neither meditator nor meditation; no external region exists within it. There is no object of meditation or time there. I am the nectar of knowledge, the essence, and like the infinite sky.
avadhuta_gita::157.translation_literal: ध्याता (meditator) / न (not) / ते (your) / हृदये (in the heart) / न (not) / च (and) / ते (your) / समाधि- (meditation) / ध्यानं (meditation) / न (not) / ते (your) / हृदये (in the heart) / न (not) / बहिः (external) / प्रदेशः (region) / ध्येयं (object of meditation) / न (not) / चेति (also) / हृदये (in the heart) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / वस्तु (thing) / कालो (time) / ज्ञानामृतं (nectar of knowledge) / समरसं (essence) / गगनोपमोऽहम् (I am like the sky)
avadhuta_gita::157.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::157.essence: Your heart contains no doer, object, or time—only infinite, unified presence.
avadhuta_gita::157.simple_meaning: There is no separate meditator or meditation inside your heart. No outer space, object, or time exists there. The true self is like the limitless sky, pure and unified.
avadhuta_gita::157.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing your true self is limitless, with no inner divisions or limits.
avadhuta_gita::157.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that within your own heart, there is no separate person meditating or any meditation happening. Neither is there an external space or object inside you, nor the concept of time. This reveals the true self as the infinite sky, unchanging and unified.
avadhuta_gita::157.modern_relevance: You notice moments when your mind stops labeling you a doer or thinker, and you feel a vast openness inside.
avadhuta_gita::157.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing yourself as a separate actor to recognizing the emptiness where all roles dissolve.

avadhuta_gita::158.verse_sanskrit:
यत्सारभूतमखिलं कथितं मया ते
न त्वं न मे न महतो न गुरुर्न न शिष्यः ।
स्वच्छन्दरूपसहजं परमार्थतत्त्वं
ज्ञानामृतं समरसं गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::158.verse_hindi: मैंने जो सम्पूर्ण सारभूत था वह तुझे कह दिया है। किन्तु यह सब न तेरा है, न मेरा है, महतत्व भी नहीं है न गुरु शिष्य ही है। यह सहज स्वच्छन्द रूप परमार्थ तत्व स्वरूप ज्ञानामृत, समरस तथा आकाश तुल्य है। वह मैं हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::158.english_translation: I have told you the entire essence; yet it is neither yours nor mine, nor of greatness, nor of teacher or student. It is the natural, free, pure reality, the nectar of wisdom, perfectly balanced like the sky — that is what I am.
avadhuta_gita::158.translation_literal: यत् (that) सारभूतम् (essence-contained) अखिलं (whole) कथितं (spoken) मया (by me) ते (to you) न (not) त्वं (you) न (not) मे (me) न (not) महतः (greatness) न (not) गुरुः (teacher) न (not) न (not) शिष्यः (student) स्वच्छन्द (free) रूप (form) सहजं (natural) परमार्थ (supreme reality) तत्त्वं (truth) ज्ञानामृतं (wisdom nectar) समरसं (perfectly balanced) गगन (sky) उपमः (like) अहम् (I)
avadhuta_gita::158.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::158.essence: The true nature is free, beyond all roles and distinctions, naturally pure wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::158.simple_meaning: The true self is beyond all identities, roles, and distinctions; it is natural, free, and the pure essence of wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::158.simple_insight: You can feel the freedom in knowing your true self is beyond all labels and roles.
avadhuta_gita::158.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the essence he shares is not owned by anyone—not by you or me, nor tied to any hierarchy like teacher or student. This essence is natural, free, pure wisdom, balanced like the vast sky, and it is his true nature.
avadhuta_gita::158.modern_relevance: You realize your true worth is not bound by your job title, roles, or achievements—it is simply your natural, free essence.
avadhuta_gita::158.insight: It shifts your perspective from identifying with roles to recognizing your pure, unchanging nature beyond all labels.

avadhuta_gita::159.verse_sanskrit:
कथमिह परमार्थं तत्त्वमानन्दरूपं
कथमिह परमार्थं नैवमानन्दरूपम् ।
कथमिह परमार्थं ज्ञानविज्ञानरूपं
यदि परमहमेकं वर्तते व्योमरूपम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::159.verse_hindi: यदि मैं एक ही परम आकाश रूप हूँ तो उसमें परमार्थ, तत्व एवं आनन्दरूपता कैसे रहती है तथा उसमें परमार्थ एवं आनन्दरूप भी कैसे नहीं रहता है, उसमें ज्ञान-विज्ञान रूप भी कैसे रह सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::159.english_translation: If I am the one supreme sky form, how can ultimate reality, essence, and bliss exist in it, and yet not exist; how can knowledge and wisdom also be present?
avadhuta_gita::159.translation_literal: यदि (if) मैं (I) एक (one) ही (only) परम (supreme) आकाश (sky) रूप (form) हूँ (am) तो (then) उसमें (in it) परमार्थ (ultimate reality), तत्व (essence) एवं (and) आनन्दरूपता (bliss-form) कैसे (how) रहती (exists) है (is) तथा (and) उसमें (in it) परमार्थ (ultimate reality) एवं (and) आनन्दरूप (bliss-form) भी (also) कैसे (how) नहीं (not) रहता (exists) है (is) उसमें (in it) ज्ञान-विज्ञान (knowledge-wisdom) रूप (form) भी (also) कैसे (how) रह सकता (can exist) है (is)
avadhuta_gita::159.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::159.essence: You are the unchanging sky where all truth and its absence coexist.
avadhuta_gita::159.simple_meaning: You are like the single sky that holds all things and yet remains unchanged. Ultimate reality, bliss, and knowledge appear and disappear but you remain one and whole.
avadhuta_gita::159.simple_insight: There is freedom in being the unchanging space where all opposites arise and dissolve.
avadhuta_gita::159.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya questions how he can be the single supreme sky yet contain ultimate truth, bliss, and knowledge, while also seeming that these qualities do not exist separately. This points to non-dual reality where opposites coexist in one essence.
avadhuta_gita::159.modern_relevance: When life feels full of contradictions, you can remember you are the open space holding all experiences without being defined by any.
avadhuta_gita::159.insight: It shifts your view from needing to fix contradictions to embracing the whole paradox as your true nature.

avadhuta_gita::160.verse_sanskrit:
दहनपवनहीनं विद्धि विज्ञानमेक-
मवनिजलविहीनं विद्धि विज्ञानरूपम् ।
समगमनविहीनं विद्धि विज्ञानमेकं
गगनमिव विशालं विद्धि विज्ञानमेकम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::160.verse_hindi: यह आत्मा एक ही विज्ञान रूप है ऐसा तू जान; जो अग्नि और वायु से रहित, पृथ्वी और जल से रहित, आवागमन से रहित है। यह आकाश के समान विशाल है।
avadhuta_gita::160.english_translation: Know that the true self is the sole form of pure awareness—free from fire and wind, free from earth and water, and free from movement. It is vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::160.translation_literal: दहनपवनहीनं (free from fire and wind) / विद्धि (know) / विज्ञानमेक- (the one pure awareness) / अवनिजलविहीनं (free from earth and water) / विद्धि (know) / विज्ञानरूपम् (form of pure awareness) / समगमनविहीनं (free from movement) / विद्धि (know) / विज्ञानमेकं (the one pure awareness) / गगनमिव (like the sky) / विशालं (vast) / विद्धि (know) / विज्ञानमेकम् (the one pure awareness)
avadhuta_gita::160.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::160.essence: Your true self is boundless, motionless pure awareness beyond all elements.
avadhuta_gita::160.simple_meaning: You are pure awareness, untouched by fire, wind, earth, water, or movement. Your true self is vast and limitless like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::160.simple_insight: There is freedom and vastness in realizing you are not tied to any physical or changing element.
avadhuta_gita::160.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that the true self is pure awareness without any physical qualities or movement. It transcends the elements and is as vast and limitless as the sky, revealing the infinite nature of the inner being.
avadhuta_gita::160.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by constant change or pressure, remember your true self is vast and unaffected, like the open sky beyond the storm.
avadhuta_gita::160.insight: Recognize your inner being as unchanging awareness beyond physical and mental fluctuations.

avadhuta_gita::161.verse_sanskrit:
न शून्यरूपं न विशून्यरूपं
न शुद्धरूपं न विशुद्धरूपम् ।
रूपं विरूपं न भवामि किञ्चित्
स्वरूपरूपं परमार्थतत्त्वम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::161.verse_hindi: मैं न शून्य रूप हूँ, न शून्य रहित रूप ही हूँ, न शुद्ध रूप हूँ, न विशुद्ध रूप हूँ, मैं किंचित् मात्र भी रूप और विरूप नहीं हूँ। मैं एक ही परमार्थ तत्व अपने ही रूप वाला हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::161.english_translation: I am neither empty nor non-empty form, neither pure nor impure form; I am not any form or distorted form. I am the supreme reality itself in my own form.
avadhuta_gita::161.translation_literal: न (not) शून्यरूपं (empty form) न (not) विशून्यरूपं (non-empty form) न (not) शुद्धरूपं (pure form) न (not) विशुद्धरूपम् (impure form) । रूपं (form) विरूपं (distorted form) न (not) भवामि (I become) किञ्चित् (any) स्वरूपरूपं (own form) परमार्थतत्त्वम् (supreme reality) ॥
avadhuta_gita::161.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::161.essence: You are not any form but the supreme reality itself beyond all dualities.
avadhuta_gita::161.simple_meaning: You are not limited to any form—neither empty nor full, pure nor impure. You are the supreme reality itself, beyond all appearances.
avadhuta_gita::161.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing you are not confined by any label or form.
avadhuta_gita::161.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he transcends all categories of form—empty, full, pure, impure, or distorted. He is the supreme reality itself, unbound by any shape or definition, revealing the essence of non-duality.
avadhuta_gita::161.modern_relevance: You might feel boxed in by roles or identities, but this teaches you that your true self is beyond all labels and appearances.
avadhuta_gita::161.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with transient forms to recognizing your unchanging true nature.

avadhuta_gita::162.verse_sanskrit:
मुञ्च मुञ्च हि संसारं त्यागं मुञ्च हि सर्वथा ।
त्यागात्यागविषं शुद्धममृतं सहजं ध्रुवम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::162.verse_hindi: तू स्वभाव से ही शुद्ध, अमृतरूप एवं नित्य है। इसलिए तू संसार का त्याग कर दे तथा त्याग को भी सर्वदा छोड़ दे तथा त्याग और अत्याग की भावना विष के समान है उसे भी छोड़ दे।
avadhuta_gita::162.english_translation: You are inherently pure, immortal, and eternal. Therefore, renounce the world, then even renunciation itself, for the feeling of renunciation and non-renunciation is like poison—let it go too.
avadhuta_gita::162.translation_literal: मुञ्च (let go) मुञ्च (let go) हि (indeed) संसारं (world) त्यागं (renunciation) मुञ्च (let go) हि (indeed) सर्वथा (completely) । त्यागात्यागविषं (renunciation-non-renunciation poison) शुद्धम् (pure) अमृतं (immortal) सहजं (natural) ध्रुवम् (eternal) ॥
avadhuta_gita::162.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::162.essence: True self is naturally pure; even renunciation must be released to be free.
avadhuta_gita::162.simple_meaning: You are naturally pure, immortal, and constant. So first renounce the world, then even the idea of renouncing itself, because holding onto renunciation is like poison.
avadhuta_gita::162.simple_insight: There is freedom in dropping not only the world but also the urge to detach from it.
avadhuta_gita::162.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that the true self is naturally pure and immortal. He advises first to renounce the world, but then warns that clinging even to renunciation is harmful, like poison, urging complete freedom from all attachments.
avadhuta_gita::162.modern_relevance: You might try to let go of stress or distractions, but sometimes even holding onto the idea of letting go keeps you stuck. True freedom is beyond all that.
avadhuta_gita::162.insight: This verse shifts your focus from renouncing external things to releasing any attachment to the act of renunciation itself.

avadhuta_gita::163.verse_sanskrit:
नावाहनं नैव विसर्जनं वा पुष्पाणि पत्राणि कथं भवन्ति ।
ध्यानानि मन्त्राणि कथं भवन्ति समासमं चैव शिवार्चनं च ॥
avadhuta_gita::163.verse_hindi: सर्व व्यापक चेतन आत्मा का न आवाहन है, न विसर्जन, इस पर पुष्प एवं पत्र भी कैसे समर्पित हो सकते हैं, इसके लिए ध्यान और मन्त्र भी किस प्रकार हो सकता है। सर्वत्र समान दृष्टि रखना ही इस शिव रूप चेतन आत्मा का पूजन है।
avadhuta_gita::163.english_translation: The all-pervading conscious self cannot be called or dismissed; how then can flowers or leaves be offered, or meditation and mantras performed? Seeing everything equally is the true worship of this Shiva-like conscious self.
avadhuta_gita::163.translation_literal: नावाहनं (no calling) नैव (nor) विसर्जनं (no dismissal) वा (also) पुष्पाणि (flowers) पत्राणि (leaves) कथं (how) भवन्ति (can be) । ध्यानानि (meditations) मन्त्राणि (mantras) कथं (how) भवन्ति (can be) समासमं (equal) चैव (and) शिवार्चनं (Shiva worship) च (also) ॥
avadhuta_gita::163.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::163.essence: True worship transcends rituals; it is equal seeing of all as divine.
avadhuta_gita::163.simple_meaning: The infinite conscious self cannot be called or dismissed like objects; true worship is to see everything equally without rituals.
avadhuta_gita::163.simple_insight: You feel relief knowing devotion is about equal respect, not external acts.
avadhuta_gita::163.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that the supreme conscious self cannot be approached by ordinary rituals like offering flowers or chanting mantras. Instead, true devotion is recognizing the same divine presence in all things with equal vision, transcending all external forms of worship.
avadhuta_gita::163.modern_relevance: When you stop trying to perform perfect rituals or prove your devotion, you begin to see the sacred equally in everyone and everything around you.
avadhuta_gita::163.insight: It shifts your devotion from external acts to a steady inner attitude of equal respect and recognition.

avadhuta_gita::164.verse_sanskrit:
न केवलं बन्धविबन्धमुक्तो न केवलं शुद्धविशुद्धमुक्तः ।
न केवलं योगवियोगमुक्तः स वै विमुक्तो गगनोपमोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::164.verse_hindi: मैं केवल बन्ध और विबन्ध से ही युक्त नहीं हूँ, न शुद्ध विशुद्ध से ही मुक्त हूँ, न योग और वियोग से ही मुक्त हूँ। बल्कि मैं आकाश तुल्य होने से मैं मुक्त ही हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::164.english_translation: I am not merely free from bondage and separation, nor only from purity and impurity, nor just from union and separation; I am truly free like the sky itself.
avadhuta_gita::164.translation_literal: न (not) केवलं (only) बन्धविबन्धमुक्तो (bondage and separation free) न (not) केवलं (only) शुद्धविशुद्धमुक्तः (purity and impurity free) । न (not) केवलं (only) योगवियोगमुक्तः (union and separation free) स (he) वै (indeed) विमुक्तो (liberated) गगनोपमोऽहम् (like the sky I am) ॥
avadhuta_gita::164.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::164.essence: True freedom transcends all opposites, like the sky that embraces everything without attachment.
avadhuta_gita::164.simple_meaning: True freedom is not just escaping opposites like bondage or purity, but being vast and unbounded like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::164.simple_insight: You can feel limitless when you stop defining yourself by opposites and see yourself as vast and free.
avadhuta_gita::164.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that his freedom isn't limited to escaping contrasts like bondage or purity. Instead, he is free in the way the sky is free—unbounded and unaffected by any condition.
avadhuta_gita::164.modern_relevance: When you stop labeling yourself by success or failure, right or wrong, you feel a freedom as wide and open as the sky itself.
avadhuta_gita::164.insight: It shifts your view from escaping conditions to embodying vast, unaffected presence beyond all opposites.

avadhuta_gita::165.verse_sanskrit:
सञ्जायते सर्वमिदं हि तथ्यं सञ्जायते सर्वमिदं वितथ्यम् ।
एवं विकल्पो मम नैव जातः स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::165.verse_hindi: यह सम्पूर्ण जगत सत्य ही उत्पन्न होता है अथवा मिथ्या ही उत्पन्न होता है इस प्रकार का विकल्प मेरे में कभी उत्पन्न ही नहीं हुआ। मैं स्वरूप से ही मुक्त हूँ तथा जन्म मरण के रोग से भी मुक्त हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::165.english_translation: This entire world either truly arises or falsely arises; such a choice never arose in me. I am free in my nature and free from the disease of birth and death.
avadhuta_gita::165.translation_literal: सञ्जायते (arises) / सर्वम् (all) / इदं (this) / हि (indeed) / तथ्यं (true) / सञ्जायते (arises) / सर्वम् (all) / इदं (this) / वितथ्यम् (falsehood) / एवं (thus) / विकल्पः (alternative/choice) / मम (in me) / नैव (never) / जातः (arose) / स्वरूपनिर्वाणम् (nature-liberation) / अनामयः (disease-free) / अहम् (I)
avadhuta_gita::165.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::165.essence: You never face doubt about reality because you are inherently free and unchanging.
avadhuta_gita::165.simple_meaning: Everything either truly exists or does not, but this question never disturbed me. I am naturally free and untouched by birth or death.
avadhuta_gita::165.simple_insight: You can rest in knowing no confusion or doubt touches your true nature.
avadhuta_gita::165.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that unlike others who question reality’s truth or falsity, he never experienced such confusion. He stands firm as the ever-free self, untouched by cycles of birth and death.
avadhuta_gita::165.modern_relevance: When faced with endless doubts about what is real, you can find peace in knowing your true self never wavers or suffers.
avadhuta_gita::165.insight: It teaches you to let go of dualistic doubts and rest in the certainty of your timeless freedom.

avadhuta_gita::166.verse_sanskrit:
न साञ्जनं चैव निरञ्जनं वा न चान्तरं वापि निरन्तरं वा ।
अन्तर्विभन्नं न हि मे विभाति स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::166.verse_hindi: मैं न तो दोष युक्त हूँ न दोष रहित हूँ, मैं व्यवधान सहित एवं व्यवधान रहित भी नहीं हूँ। मेरे में व्यवधान और भेद भी ज्ञात नहीं होते। मैं स्वरूप से ही मुक्त एवं रोग रहित आकाश तुल्य हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::166.english_translation: I am neither tainted nor spotless; neither fragmented nor continuous. In me, no divisions or disturbances appear. I am essentially free, like the sky, without disease or limitation.
avadhuta_gita::166.translation_literal: न (not) साञ्जनं (tainted) चैव (also) निरञ्जनं (spotless) वा (or) न (not) चान्तरं (fragmented) वापि (also) निरन्तरं (continuous) वा (or) । अन्तर्विभन्नं (internally divided) न (not) हि (indeed) मे (in me) विभाति (appears) स्वरूपनिर्वाणम् (essence-free) अनामयः (disease-free) अहम् (I am) ॥
avadhuta_gita::166.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::166.essence: You are fundamentally whole and undivided, free from all faults or fragmentation.
avadhuta_gita::166.simple_meaning: You are not flawed or flawless, divided or whole. You are free and undisturbed, like the limitless sky.
avadhuta_gita::166.simple_insight: Feel the relief of being whole beyond all faults and divisions.
avadhuta_gita::166.detailed_meaning: The Avadhuta declares that the true self is beyond all dualities like fault and purity or fragmentation and continuity. It is free, undivided, and untouched by disturbance, like an infinite sky free from disease.
avadhuta_gita::166.modern_relevance: In moments of self-doubt or inner conflict, remember you are not broken or incomplete — you are vast and whole beyond appearances.
avadhuta_gita::166.insight: Shift your view from seeing yourself as flawed or fragmented to recognizing your inherent wholeness and freedom.

avadhuta_gita::167.verse_sanskrit:
अबोधबोधो मम नैव जातो बोधस्वरूपं मम नैव जातम् ।
निर्बोधबोधं च कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::167.verse_hindi: अबोध ( अज्ञान) का बोध (ज्ञान) भी मेरे में नहीं हुआ है, मैं बोध स्वरूप (ज्ञान स्वरूप) हूँ ऐसा ज्ञान भी मुझे नहीं हुआ है। फिर मैं अपने को निबध (अज्ञानी) अथवा बोध वाला (ज्ञानी) किस प्रकार कहूँ। मैं स्वरूप से ही मुक्त एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::167.english_translation: Ignorance's knowledge has never arisen in me, nor has knowledge of knowledge; I am the embodiment of knowledge itself. How then can I call myself ignorant or knowledgeable? I am inherently free and without disease.
avadhuta_gita::167.translation_literal: अबोध (ignorance) / बोधो (knowledge) / मम (in me) / नैव (not at all) / जातः (arisen) / बोधस्वरूपं (embodiment of knowledge) / मम (in me) / नैव (not at all) / जातम् (arisen) / निर्बोधबोधं (ignorance-knowledge) / च (and) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I say) / स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् (I am the essence, liberation, and without disease)
avadhuta_gita::167.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::167.essence: You are beyond both ignorance and knowledge; your true nature is freedom itself.
avadhuta_gita::167.simple_meaning: You have never experienced ignorance or even the knowledge of it because you are the very essence of knowledge itself, free and untouched by any limitation.
avadhuta_gita::167.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing you are beyond all labels of ignorance and knowledge.
avadhuta_gita::167.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he has never been caught in ignorance or even the awareness of ignorance. He is pure awareness itself, beyond all dualities of learned and unlearned, inherently free and untouched by any flaw or limitation.
avadhuta_gita::167.modern_relevance: When confusion or self-doubt cloud your mind, remember your true self is untouched by these labels and remains whole and free.
avadhuta_gita::167.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing knowledge states to resting in unchanging awareness.

avadhuta_gita::168.verse_sanskrit:
न धर्मयुक्तो न च पापयुक्तो न बन्धयुक्तो न च मोक्षयुक्तः ।
युक्तं त्वयुक्तं न च मे विभाति स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::168.verse_hindi: मैं न धर्म से युक्त हूँ, न पाप से युक्त हूँ, न बन्ध से युक्त हूँ और न मोक्ष से ही युक्त हूँ, युक्त और अयुक्त का भान भी मेरे में नहीं होता है। मैं स्वरूप से ही मोक्ष युक्त एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::168.english_translation: I am not bound by duty, sin, bondage, or freedom; I perceive neither attachment nor detachment. By my true nature, I am free and untouched by illness.
avadhuta_gita::168.translation_literal: न (not) धर्मयुक्तो (joined with duty) न (nor) च (also) पापयुक्तो (joined with sin) न (not) बन्धयुक्तो (joined with bondage) न (nor) च (also) मोक्षयुक्तः (joined with freedom); युक्तं (attached) त्वयुक्तं (and detached) न (not) च (also) मे (in me) विभाति (appears) स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् (true-nature-liberation-illnessless-I am).
avadhuta_gita::168.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::168.essence: Your true self transcends all attachments, bonds, and freedoms—it simply is.
avadhuta_gita::168.simple_meaning: You are neither attached to duty, wrongdoing, bondage, nor freedom. Your true self remains free, pure, and untouched by any condition.
avadhuta_gita::168.simple_insight: There is deep relief in knowing your true self is beyond all dualities and limitations.
avadhuta_gita::168.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he is not confined by social duties, moral labels, bondage, or even liberation. He transcends all dualities of attachment and detachment, existing in his pure true nature, free and without illness.
avadhuta_gita::168.modern_relevance: When life pulls you between obligations and desires for freedom, you can find calm knowing your true self remains untouched by these struggles.
avadhuta_gita::168.insight: Shift your mindset from identifying with roles and conditions toward recognizing your unchanged true nature beyond them.

avadhuta_gita::169.verse_sanskrit:
परापरं वा न च मे कदाचित् मध्यस्थभावो हि न चारिमित्रम् ।
हिताहितं चापि कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::169.verse_hindi: मुझमें पर एवं अपर भाव भी नहीं है, न मध्यस्थ भाव ही है, शत्रु और मित्र भाव भी मेरे में नहीं हैं, फिर मैं हित और अहित किस प्रकार कहूँ। मैं स्वरूप से ही मोक्ष स्वरूप एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::169.english_translation: In me, there is neither the supreme nor the inferior; no middle state, no enemy or friend. How then can I speak of benefit or harm? I am by nature free and untouched by suffering.
avadhuta_gita::169.translation_literal: परापरं (supreme and inferior) / वा (or) / न (not) / च (also) / मे (in me) / कदाचित् (ever) / मध्यस्थभावो (middle state) / हि (indeed) / न (not) / च (also) / अरिमित्रम् (enemy or friend) / हिताहितं (benefit and harm) / चापि (also) / कथं (how) / वदामि (I speak) / स्वरूपनिर्वाणम् (nature as freedom) / अनामयः (without disease) / अहम् (I am)
avadhuta_gita::169.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::169.essence: You are naturally free, beyond all dualities of friend, foe, benefit, or harm.
avadhuta_gita::169.simple_meaning: You are not divided by opposites like friend or enemy, benefit or harm. Your true nature is freedom and health beyond all duality.
avadhuta_gita::169.simple_insight: Knowing you are beyond all conflict brings deep peace and clarity.
avadhuta_gita::169.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that his true self transcends all dualities—no supreme or inferior, no friend or foe, no benefit or harm touches him. This reveals his complete freedom and unchanging nature beyond worldly distinctions.
avadhuta_gita::169.modern_relevance: In moments of conflict or stress, remembering you are beyond friend or enemy can calm your mind and stop endless inner struggle.
avadhuta_gita::169.insight: It shifts your view from seeing life in opposites to recognizing your unchanging, free nature beyond all labels.

avadhuta_gita::170.verse_sanskrit:
नोपासको नैवमुपास्यरूपं न चोपदेशो न च मे क्रिया च । 
संवित्स्वरूपं च कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::170.verse_hindi: न तो मैं उपासक हूँ, न ही उपास्य रूप हूँ न मेरा उपदेश है और न मेरे में क्रिया ही है फिर मैं अपने को ज्ञान स्वरूप भी किस प्रकार कहूँ। मैं स्वरूप से ही मुक्त एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::170.english_translation: I am neither a worshipper nor an object of worship; I have no teachings and no actions. How then can I say I am the form of knowledge? I am free from form, free from disease.
avadhuta_gita::170.translation_literal: नो (not) अपासको (worshipper) नै (also not) एव (indeed) उपास्य (object of worship) रूपं (form) न (not) च (and) उपदेशो (teaching) न (not) च (and) मे (my) क्रिया (action) च (also). संवित् (knowledge) स्वरूपं (form) च (and) कथं (how) वदामि (do I say) स्वरूप (form) निर्वाण (freedom) अमाय (free from disease) अहम् (I).
avadhuta_gita::170.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::170.essence: You are beyond all roles, actions, and forms; you are pure freedom.
avadhuta_gita::170.simple_meaning: You are not a worshipper or an object to be worshipped. You have no teachings or actions. You are pure freedom, free from any form or disease.
avadhuta_gita::170.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing you are not bound by roles or actions, but simply free.
avadhuta_gita::170.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he is beyond all dual roles—neither the worshipper nor the worshipped. He claims no teachings or actions belong to him, emphasizing that his true nature is beyond form, free and untouched by any flaws or limitations.
avadhuta_gita::170.modern_relevance: You feel pressured to fit roles—teacher, doer, or follower—but realizing you are beyond these brings a deep sense of freedom.
avadhuta_gita::170.insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with roles or actions to recognizing pure freedom beyond all labels.

avadhuta_gita::171.verse_sanskrit:
नो व्यापकं व्याप्यमिहास्ति किञ्चित् न चालयं वापि निरालयं वा ।
अशून्यशून्यं च कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::171.verse_hindi: इस आत्मा (ब्रह्म) में व्यापक व्याप्य भाव किंचित भी नहीं हैं, न आश्रय एवं निराश्रय भाव ही है। मैं इसे शून्य तथा अशून्य भी किस प्रकार कहूँ। यह स्वरूप से ही मुक्त एवं रोग रहित है। वही में हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::171.english_translation: This true self is neither pervasive nor moving, neither dependent nor independent; it cannot be called empty or not empty. By nature, it is free and without flaw—I am that.
avadhuta_gita::171.translation_literal:
नो (not) व्यापकं (pervasive) व्याप्यम् (pervading) इह (here) अस्ति (exists) किञ्चित् (anything) न (nor) चालयं (moving) वा (or) अपि (also) निरालयं (without support) वा (or) ।
अशून्यशून्यं (non-empty empty) च (also) कथं (how) वदामि (shall I say) स्वरूप (own form) निर्वाणम् (freedom) अनामयः (without disease) अहम् (I) ॥
avadhuta_gita::171.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::171.essence: The true self is beyond all dualities and completely free by nature.
avadhuta_gita::171.simple_meaning: The true self is beyond any description: it is not limited, not moving, not dependent, and cannot be called empty or full. It is naturally free and without any flaw.
avadhuta_gita::171.simple_insight: You can feel complete knowing your true self is beyond all contradictions and perfectly free.
avadhuta_gita::171.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals the nature of the true self as beyond all ordinary qualities—neither pervasive nor confined, neither dependent nor independent, neither empty nor full. This self is inherently free and without any imperfection, expressing ultimate freedom.
avadhuta_gita::171.modern_relevance: When you face confusion about your identity or feel torn between extremes, remember that your true nature is beyond such limits and completely free.
avadhuta_gita::171.insight: It shifts your mind from trying to define yourself by conditions to recognizing your flawless, free nature beyond all labels.

avadhuta_gita::172.verse_sanskrit:
न ग्राहको ग्राह्यकमेव किञ्चित् न कारणं वा मम नैव कार्यम् ।
अचिन्त्यचिन्त्यं च कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::172.verse_hindi: आत्मा में ग्राहक (ग्रहण करने वाला) एवं ग्राह्य (जिसे ग्रहण किया जाता है) का थोड़ा सा भी भेद नहीं है, मेरा न तो कोई कारण है और न ही कोई कार्य है। इस अचिन्त्य आत्मा का मन से चिन्तन भी नहीं किया जा सकता उसका मैं कथन कैसे करूँ। मैं स्वरूप से ही मुक्त और रोग से रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::172.english_translation: In the true self, there is no distinction between the taker and the taken; I have no cause and no action. How can I speak of the inconceivable self, free from form and disease?
avadhuta_gita::172.translation_literal: न (not) ग्राहको (taker) ग्राह्यकमेव (and taken indeed) किञ्चित् (any) न (not) कारणं (cause) वा (also) मम (my) नैव (not at all) कार्यम् (action) । अचिन्त्यचिन्त्यं (inconceivable and conceivable) च (and) कथं (how) वदामि (can I speak) स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् (formless, free from disease, I am) ॥
avadhuta_gita::172.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::172.essence: The true self is beyond all dualities of taker, taken, cause, and action.
avadhuta_gita::172.simple_meaning: There is no difference between the one who takes and what is taken in your true nature. You have no cause and no action. This self is beyond thought, free from form and disease.
avadhuta_gita::172.simple_insight: You can feel a deep freedom knowing you are beyond cause, effect, and all distinctions.
avadhuta_gita::172.detailed_meaning: The sage Dattatreya declares that the true self is beyond all dualities like taker and taken. It has no cause or action. This self cannot be grasped by thought and is free from all limitations, revealing ultimate freedom.
avadhuta_gita::172.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by choices or blame, remember your true self is beyond these conflicts and completely free.
avadhuta_gita::172.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as a doer caught in cause and effect to recognizing you are pure awareness beyond all distinctions.

avadhuta_gita::173.verse_sanskrit:
न भेदकं वापि न चैव भेद्यं न वेदकं वा मम नैव वेद्यम् ।
गतागतं तात कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::173.verse_hindi: न तो कोई भेद करने वाला है और न भेद करने योग्य ही है, न कोई जानने वाला है, न मेरे में कोई जानने योग्य ही है। होने से मेरा कारण एवं कार्य भी नहीं है। हे तात ! न कोई व्यतीत हुआ है, न आने वाला है फिर उसका कथन कैसे करूँ। मैं स्वरूप से ही मुक्त एवं रोग रहित हूँ ।
avadhuta_gita::173.english_translation: There is neither anything that divides nor anything to be divided, nor any knower or known in me. I have no cause or effect; neither coming nor going exists. I am by nature free and without disease.
avadhuta_gita::173.translation_literal: न (not) भेदकं (divider) वापि (also) न (not) चैव (also) भेद्यं (dividable) न (not) वेदकं (knower) वा (or) मम (my) नैव (also not) वेद्यम् (known) । गतागतं (gone and come) तात (dear one) कथं (how) वदामि (should I speak) स्वरूपनिर्वाणम् (my nature is liberation) अनामयः (disease-free) अहम् (I) ॥
avadhuta_gita::173.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::173.essence: You are perfectly whole, beyond division, time, and knowing.
avadhuta_gita::173.simple_meaning: You are not divided or separate in any way. There is no separate knower or known inside you. You have no cause or effect; you simply are free and whole by nature.
avadhuta_gita::173.simple_insight: You can rest knowing you are already complete, not affected by coming or going.
avadhuta_gita::173.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares the supreme reality has no division, no subject-object split, no past or future. There is no separate self to know or be known. This moment reveals the true self as eternally free and pure.
avadhuta_gita::173.modern_relevance: In moments when you feel fractured or uncertain, recognize that your true nature is whole, beyond all separation and change.
avadhuta_gita::173.insight: It shifts your understanding from a fragmented self to seeing yourself as an undivided presence beyond time and change.

avadhuta_gita::174.verse_sanskrit:
न चास्ति देहो न च मे विदेहो बुद्धिर्मनो मे न हि चेन्द्रियाणि ।
रागो विरागश्च कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::174.verse_hindi: मेरा शरीर भी नहीं है, न मैं देह रहित ही हूँ, मेरी बुद्धि, मन तथा इन्द्रियाँ भी नहीं हैं इसलिए मैं राग और विराग का किस प्रकार कथन करूं। मैं मुक्तरूप रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::174.english_translation: I have no body, nor am I bodiless; I have no intellect, mind, or senses. Therefore, how can I speak of desire and non-desire? I am the free form, free of disease.
avadhuta_gita::174.translation_literal: न (not) चास्ति (exists) देहो (body) न (nor) च (and) मे (my) विदेहो (bodiless) बुद्धिः (intellect) मनो (mind) मे (my) न (not) हि (indeed) चेन्द्रियाणि (senses) । रागः (desire) विरागश्च (and non-desire) कथं (how) वदामि (speak) स्वरूपनिर्वाणम् (own form liberation) आनामयः (disease-free) अहम् (I) ॥
avadhuta_gita::174.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::174.essence: You are neither body nor mind but the free and whole true self beyond all dualities.
avadhuta_gita::174.simple_meaning: You are not your body, mind, intellect, or senses; you are beyond desire and non-desire, naturally free and whole.
avadhuta_gita::174.simple_insight: There's peace in knowing you are untouched by cravings or limitations of the body and mind.
avadhuta_gita::174.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares he is neither body nor without body, nor mind, intellect, or senses. This means he transcends all dualities, including desire and aversion. He exists as pure freedom and health beyond all conditions.
avadhuta_gita::174.modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed by your thoughts, emotions, or physical limits—but your true self is untouched by all these.
avadhuta_gita::174.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with body and mind to recognizing your limitless, unconditioned true nature.

avadhuta_gita::175.verse_sanskrit:
उल्लेखमात्रं न हि भिन्नमुच्चैरुल्लेखमात्रं न तिरोहितं वै ।
समासमं मित्र कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::175.verse_hindi: वह (आत्मा) थोड़ा सा भी (ब्रह्म से) भिन्न नहीं है वह उच्च प्रकार के लेखन में भी नहीं है, उससे भी वह छिपा हुआ है। हे मित्र! उसे मैं सम अथवा असम किस प्रकार कहूँ। मैं आत्म रूप युक्त एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::175.english_translation: The true self is not even slightly different from the supreme reality; it is not present in exalted writings, nor hidden by them. Friend, how can I call it whole or partial? I am the self's form, free from disease.
avadhuta_gita::175.translation_literal: उल्लेखमात्रं (mention only) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / भिन्नम् (different) / उच्चैर् (exalted) / उल्लेखमात्रं (mention only) / न (not) / तिरोहितं (hidden) / वै (indeed) / समासमं (whole or partial) / मित्र (friend) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I speak) / स्वरूपनिर्वाणम् (true self's liberation) / अनामयः (without disease) / अहम् (I)
avadhuta_gita::175.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::175.essence: The true self is entirely one with supreme reality, beyond all division or concealment.
avadhuta_gita::175.simple_meaning: The true self is entirely the supreme reality, not different or hidden anywhere; it cannot be called partial or whole because it simply is.
avadhuta_gita::175.simple_insight: You can feel complete and untouched because your true self is never divided or impaired.
avadhuta_gita::175.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the true self is utterly unified with the supreme reality. It does not appear even in exalted scriptures nor is it concealed by them. He rejects any division or imperfection, affirming his identity as pure and free from all afflictions.
avadhuta_gita::175.modern_relevance: When you feel fragmented or lost, remember that your true being is whole and untouched, beyond any label or limitation.
avadhuta_gita::175.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as divided or flawed to recognizing your complete and pure nature as the true self.

avadhuta_gita::176.verse_sanskrit:
जितेन्द्रियोऽहं त्वजितेन्द्रियो वा न संयमो मे नियमो न जातः ।
जयाजयौ मित्र कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::176.verse_hindi: मैं जितेन्द्रिय भी नहीं हैं, न अजितेन्द्रिय ही हूँ मेरे में संयम नियम भी उत्पन्न नहीं हुए हैं। हे मित्र! मैं जय और अजय का किस प्रकार कथन करूं। मैं स्वरूप से ही मुक्त एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::176.english_translation: I am neither one who has conquered the senses nor one who has not; no control or rules arise in me. Friend, how can I speak of victory and defeat? I am by nature free and without disease.
avadhuta_gita::176.translation_literal: जितेन्द्रियोऽहं (I am one who has conquered senses) / त्वजितेन्द्रियो (nor one who has not conquered senses) / वा (or) / न (not) / संयमो (control) / मे (in me) / नियमो (rules) / न (not) / जातः (arisen) / जयाजयौ (victory and defeat) / मित्र (friend) / कथं (how) / वदामि (can I speak) / स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् (by nature free, liberated, and without disease, I am)
avadhuta_gita::176.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::176.essence: True freedom transcends all control, victory, and defeat—it simply is.
avadhuta_gita::176.simple_meaning: You are neither controlled by your senses nor free because of effort; your true nature is already free beyond victory and defeat.
avadhuta_gita::176.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing freedom isn't earned or lost—it's your natural state.
avadhuta_gita::176.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares he is beyond the duality of senses controlled or uncontrolled. He explains no discipline or rules govern him because his true being is already free and untouched by victory or defeat, revealing absolute freedom.
avadhuta_gita::176.modern_relevance: You feel caught between impulses and control, yet your true self is beyond this struggle, naturally free even if your mind tries to fight or win.
avadhuta_gita::176.insight: It shifts your view from battling impulses to recognizing freedom as your unchanging essence beyond all duality.

avadhuta_gita::177.verse_sanskrit:
अमूर्तमूर्तिर्न च मे कदाचि दाद्यन्तमध्यं न च मे कदाचित् ।
बलाबलं मित्र कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::177.verse_hindi: मैं न कभी मूर्त हूँ, न अमूर्त ही हूँ, मेरा आदि, मध्य और अन्त भी नहीं है। हे मित्र! मैं बलशाली हूँ अथवा निर्बल हूँ। इसका भी किस प्रकार कथन करूं। मैं तो एक ही स्वरूप से ही मुक्त एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::177.english_translation: I am neither form nor formless, without beginning, middle, or end. Friend, how can I be strong or weak? I am free and untouched in my true nature.
avadhuta_gita::177.translation_literal: अमूर्तम् (formless) अमूर्तिः (form) न (not) च (and) मे (my) कदाचि (ever) दाद्यन्तम् (given) अध्यं (beginning) न (not) च (and) मे (my) कदाचित् (ever) बलाबलं (strong or weak) मित्र (friend) कथं (how) वदामि (can I say) स्वरूपनिर्वाणम् (true nature free) अनामयः (disease-free) अहम् (I)
avadhuta_gita::177.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::177.essence: Your true nature is beyond form, time, and all dualities; it is free and whole.
avadhuta_gita::177.simple_meaning: You are not limited by any shape or form, nor by time or strength; your true self is free and untouched by weakness or disease.
avadhuta_gita::177.simple_insight: You can feel a deep freedom knowing you are beyond all limits and conditions.
avadhuta_gita::177.detailed_meaning: The sage Dattatreya declares his identity beyond physical form, time, and dualities like strength or weakness. He reveals the self as eternally free, whole, and unaffected by change or illness.
avadhuta_gita::177.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your changing moods or circumstances, remember you are not defined by them but by a deeper freedom within.
avadhuta_gita::177.insight: It teaches you to recognize your true self as beyond all change, beyond strength or weakness, freeing you from self-judgment.

avadhuta_gita::178.verse_sanskrit:
मृतामृतं वापि विषाविषं च सञ्जायते तात न मे कदाचित् ।
अशुद्धशुद्धं च कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::178.verse_hindi: मेरा न मरना है, न जीना ही है, मैं विष और अमृत भी नहीं हूँ न मेरे से ये कभी उत्पन्न ही हुए हैं। हे तात! मैं अपने को शुद्ध एवं अशुद्ध भी किस प्रकार कहूँ। मैं मोक्ष स्वरूप एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::178.english_translation: I am neither born nor do I die; neither poison nor nectar arises from me. How can I be called pure or impure? I am the embodiment of liberation, free from disease.
avadhuta_gita::178.translation_literal: मृतम् (dead) अमृतम् (immortal) वा (or) अपि (also) विषम् (poison) अशिषम् (nectar) च (and) सञ्जायते (arises) तात (O son) न (not) मे (from me) कदाचित् (ever) । अशुद्ध (impure) शुद्ध (pure) च (and) कथं (how) वदामि (can say) स्वरूप (own form) निर्वाण (liberation) अमय (disease-free) अहम् (I) ॥
avadhuta_gita::178.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::178.essence: Your true nature is beyond birth, death, purity, and impurity—always free and whole.
avadhuta_gita::178.simple_meaning: You are not born and do not die; you are beyond poison or nectar, beyond pure or impure. You are the timeless, disease-free essence of liberation.
avadhuta_gita::178.simple_insight: You can feel unshaken by life’s dualities, resting in your true, unchanged nature.
avadhuta_gita::178.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares here that the true self is beyond birth and death, beyond all opposites like poison and nectar or pure and impure. This moment unfolds the insight that the true self is the embodiment of liberation, untouched by change or disease.
avadhuta_gita::178.modern_relevance: When you face confusing highs and lows or feel labeled by success or failure, remember your true self is beyond those ups and downs.
avadhuta_gita::178.insight: It teaches you to recognize that your essence is untouched by life's opposites, freeing your mind from dualistic judgments.

avadhuta_gita::179.verse_sanskrit:
स्वप्नः प्रबोधो न च योगमुद्रा नक्तं दिवा वापि न मे कदाचित् ।
अतुर्यतुर्यं च कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::179.verse_hindi: मेरे में न स्वप्न है न जाग्रत अवस्था हैं, योग मुद्रा भी नहीं है। मेरे में रात्रि और दिन भी नहीं है फिर मैं तुरीयावस्था अथवा अतुरीया अवस्था का किस प्रकार कथन करूं। मैं स्वरूप से ही मुक्त एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::179.english_translation: In me there is neither dream nor waking state, nor yoga posture; neither night nor day. How then can I speak of the fourth or beyond states? I am by nature free and free of ailments.
avadhuta_gita::179.translation_literal: स्वप्नः (dream) / प्रबोधः (waking state) / न (not) / च (and) / योगमुद्रा (yoga posture) / नक्तं (night) / दिवा (day) / वापि (also) / न (not) / मे (in me) / कदाचित् (ever) / अतुर्यतुर्यं (beyond the fourth) / च (and) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I speak) / स्वरूपनिर्वाणम् (nature's liberation) / अनामयः (free of disease) / अहम् (I am)
avadhuta_gita::179.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::179.essence: Your true self is beyond all changing states and naturally free.
avadhuta_gita::179.simple_meaning: You are not limited by dream, waking, or any yoga posture. You are beyond day and night, naturally free and without sickness.
avadhuta_gita::179.simple_insight: You can feel the relief of knowing your true self is always free and untouched by changing states.
avadhuta_gita::179.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he transcends all common states of consciousness—dreaming, waking, yoga postures, day and night. He points out that the true self is beyond all these and is naturally free and free of all faults.
avadhuta_gita::179.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by shifting moods or roles, remember your true self is untouched by these changes and always free.
avadhuta_gita::179.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with passing states to recognizing your constant, free nature beneath them.

avadhuta_gita::180.verse_sanskrit:
संविद्धि मां सर्वविसर्वमुक्तं माया विमाया न च मे कदाचित् ।
सन्ध्यादिकं कर्म कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::180.verse_hindi: मैं सर्व एवं सर्व रहित से मुक्त हूँ ऐसा तू जान। मेरे में माया एवं विमाया भी नहीं है। फिर मैं संध्या आदि कर्मों का किस प्रकार कथन करूं। मैं मुक्त स्वरूप एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::180.english_translation: Know that I am free from everything and nothingness; neither illusion nor its negation is in me. How then can I speak of duties like evening rituals? I am the free, disease-free true nature.
avadhuta_gita::180.translation_literal: संविद्धि (know) / मां (me) / सर्वविसर्वमुक्तं (free from all and nothing) / माया (illusion) / विमाया (non-illusion) / न (not) / च (and) / मे (in me) / कदाचित् (ever) । / सन्ध्यादिकं (evening and other) / कर्म (duties) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I speak) / स्वरूपनिर्वाणम् (true nature freedom) / अनामयः (disease-free) / अहम् (I am) ॥
avadhuta_gita::180.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::180.essence: Your true self is beyond all rituals, illusions, and limitations.
avadhuta_gita::180.simple_meaning: You are completely free from all illusions and rituals. Your true self is pure, free, and untouched by any duties or ceremonies.
avadhuta_gita::180.simple_insight: There is freedom in realizing you are beyond all rituals and illusions, untouched and whole.
avadhuta_gita::180.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that his essence is beyond all dualities like illusion and its negation. He is not bound by any rituals or duties such as evening prayers. His nature is pure freedom, without disease or limitation.
avadhuta_gita::180.modern_relevance: You might feel pressured by routines or expectations, yet deep inside, you are free of all that and untouched by external demands.
avadhuta_gita::180.insight: It teaches you to see beyond external roles and rituals, recognizing your unchanging, free true nature.

avadhuta_gita::181.verse_sanskrit:
संविद्धि मां सर्वसमाधियुक्तं संविद्धि मां लक्ष्यविलक्ष्यमुक्तम् ।
योगं वियोगं च कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::181.verse_hindi: तू मुझे सर्व समाधि से युक्त जान, मैं लक्ष्य एवं लक्ष्य रहित से मुक्त हूँ ऐसा तू जान । मैं योग और वियोग को किस प्रकार कहूँ मैं स्वरूप से मुक्त एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::181.english_translation: Know me as united with all absorption; free from both target and targetless. How can I call it yoga or separation? I am free in my own nature, without disease.
avadhuta_gita::181.translation_literal: संविद्धि (know as united) / मां (me) / सर्वसमाधियुक्तं (with all absorption) / संविद्धि (know) / मां (me) / लक्ष्यविलक्ष्यमुक्तम् (free from target and targetless) / योगं (yoga) / वियोगं (separation) / च (and) / कथं (how) / वदामि (do I say) / स्वरूपनिर्वाणम् (nature's liberation) / अनामयः (disease-free) / अहम् (I)
avadhuta_gita::181.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::181.essence: True freedom is beyond all goals, efforts, and separations — it simply is.
avadhuta_gita::181.simple_meaning: You are fully absorbed and free of any goal or separation. You cannot call this yoga or separation because your true nature is already free and healthy.
avadhuta_gita::181.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing you are already whole and beyond all striving.
avadhuta_gita::181.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he is completely united with all states of absorption, beyond any duality of having a goal or being without one. He transcends the ideas of yoga (union) and separation, resting in a nature free of all afflictions.
avadhuta_gita::181.modern_relevance: When you stop chasing goals or fearing being lost, you realize you are already whole and free just as you are.
avadhuta_gita::181.insight: It shifts your mind from pursuing goals or fearing separation to resting in the natural completeness of your being.

avadhuta_gita::182.verse_sanskrit:
मूर्खोऽपि नाहं न च पण्डितोऽहंमौनं विमौनं न च मे कदाचित् ।
तर्कं वितर्कं च कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::182.verse_hindi: मैं मूर्ख नहीं हूँ, न पण्डित ही हूँ, मौन एवं बोलना भी मेरे में नहीं है। मैं तर्क और वितर्क को भी किस प्रकार कथन करूं। मैं मोक्ष स्वरूप रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::182.english_translation: I am neither a fool nor a scholar; I am neither silent nor speaking. How could I speak of argument or counter-argument? I am the disease-free nature of freedom.
avadhuta_gita::182.translation_literal: मूर्खोऽपि (fool even) नाहं (not I) न (nor) च (and) पण्डितोऽहं (scholar I am) मौनं (silence) विमौनं (speechlessness) न (not) च (and) मे (in me) कदाचित् (ever) । तर्कं (argument) वितर्कं (counter-argument) च (and) कथं (how) वदामि (do I speak) स्वरूपनिर्वाणम् (nature of liberation) अनामयः (disease-free) अहम् (I am) ॥
avadhuta_gita::182.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::182.essence: You are beyond all dualities and untouched by any condition or argument.
avadhuta_gita::182.simple_meaning: You are neither foolish nor wise, neither silent nor speaking. You cannot be defined by arguments because your true self is free and untouched by suffering.
avadhuta_gita::182.simple_insight: There is freedom in realizing you are beyond all labels and debates.
avadhuta_gita::182.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that he is beyond common dualities like foolishness and wisdom, speech and silence. He cannot engage in arguments because his true nature is already free and without suffering, representing the essence of liberation.
avadhuta_gita::182.modern_relevance: You’ve felt the pressure to fit into roles like smart or ignorant, speaking or silent, but your real self is beyond those boxes, quietly whole inside.
avadhuta_gita::182.insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with roles or debates to recognizing the self as untouched and free.

avadhuta_gita::183.verse_sanskrit:
पिता च माता च कुलं न जाति र्जन्मादि मृत्युर्न च मे कदाचित् ।
स्नेहं विमोहं च कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::183.verse_hindi: मेरे पिता, माता, कुल और जाति नहीं है, मेरे जन्म और मृत्यु आदि भी नहीं है। मैं स्नेह और विमोह का किस प्रकार कथन करूं। मैं स्वरूप से ही मुक्त एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::183.english_translation: I have no father, mother, family, caste, birth, or death. How could I speak of attachment or delusion? I am by nature free and without disease.
avadhuta_gita::183.translation_literal: पिता (father) / च (and) / माता (mother) / च (and) / कुलं (family) / न (not) / जाति (caste) / र्जन्मादि (birth and so on) / मृत्युर्न (death) / च (and) / मे (my) / कदाचित् (ever) । स्नेहं (attachment) / विमोहं (delusion) / च (and) / कथं (how) / वदामि (should I speak) / स्वरूपनिर्वाणम् (nature free-state) / अनामयः (without disease) / अहम् (I) ॥
avadhuta_gita::183.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::183.essence: You are not defined by birth, death, or social ties but are naturally free and whole.
avadhuta_gita::183.simple_meaning: You are not limited by family, birth, or death. You are naturally free and untouched by attachment or confusion.
avadhuta_gita::183.simple_insight: You can feel the relief of knowing you are not bound by any worldly identity or condition.
avadhuta_gita::183.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya proclaims that he transcends all social and biological identities—father, mother, family, caste, birth, and death. Because of this transcendence, attachment and delusion have no hold on him. His true nature is pure freedom and health, untouched by any limitation.
avadhuta_gita::183.modern_relevance: When you feel trapped by your roles or the expectations of family and society, remember your true self is beyond all these labels and limits.
avadhuta_gita::183.insight: It teaches you to recognize yourself beyond all personal and social identities, freeing your mind from attachment and confusion.

avadhuta_gita::184.verse_sanskrit:
अस्तं गतो नैव सदोदितोऽहं तेजोवितेजो न च मे कदाचित् ।
सन्ध्यादिकं कर्म कथं वदामि स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::184.verse_hindi: मैं कभी अस्त नहीं होता ( लय को प्राप्त नहीं होता)। मैं सर्वकाल में उदित ही हूँ। मेरे में तेज और वितेज भी नहीं है फिर सन्ध्यादि कर्म का मैं किस प्रकार कथन करूं। मैं स्वरूप से मुक्त एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::184.english_translation: I never set nor rise; I am beyond light and brilliance. How can I speak of twilight duties? I am inherently free and without affliction.
avadhuta_gita::184.translation_literal: अस्तं (setting) गतो (gone) नैव (never) सदोदितः (always risen) अहं (I) तेजोवितेजो (light and brilliance) न (not) च (and) मे (in me) कदाचित् (ever) । सन्ध्यादिकं (twilight and such) कर्म (duties) कथं (how) वदामि (do I speak) स्वरूपनिर्वाण (nature liberation) अनामयः (without disease) अहम् (I am) ॥
avadhuta_gita::184.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::184.essence: Your true self is eternal, beyond all changes and daily rituals.
avadhuta_gita::184.simple_meaning: You are always present, never changing like sunrise or sunset. You are beyond light and darkness, free from all limitations.
avadhuta_gita::184.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing your true self never fades or changes.
avadhuta_gita::184.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals that his true self is eternal and unchanging, never subject to the cycle of daily light or duties like twilight rituals. This declaration emphasizes his freedom from all temporal roles and afflictions.
avadhuta_gita::184.modern_relevance: When your mood shifts like the day’s light, remember your true self remains steady and untouched.
avadhuta_gita::184.insight: It teaches you to see yourself as beyond changing states, steady and whole no matter external shifts.

avadhuta_gita::185.verse_sanskrit:
असंशयं विद्धि निराकुलं मां असंशयं विद्धि निरन्तरं माम् ।
असंशयं विद्धि निरञ्जनं मां स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::185.verse_hindi: मुझे संशय रहित तथा मूल कारण से रहित तू जान, मुझे संशय से रहित नित्य तू जान, मुझे संशय से रहित निर्दोष तू जान। मैं स्वरूप से ही मुक्त एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::185.english_translation: Know me doubtless as free from confusion and cause, always without doubt; know me as spotless and inherently free and without disease.
avadhuta_gita::185.translation_literal: असंशयं (without doubt) विद्धि (know) निराकुलं (untroubled) मां (me) असंशयं (without doubt) विद्धि (know) निरन्तरं (always) माम् (me) । असंशयं (without doubt) विद्धि (know) निरञ्जनं (spotless) मां (me) स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् (I am by nature free and without disease) ॥
avadhuta_gita::185.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::185.essence: Your true self is always pure, free, and beyond all confusion without exception.
avadhuta_gita::185.simple_meaning: You are inherently without confusion, always pure and free from any flaw or disease. This is your true nature beyond doubt.
avadhuta_gita::185.simple_insight: You can feel peace knowing your true self is always pure and untouched by any problem.
avadhuta_gita::185.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that his true self is forever free from doubt, confusion, and imperfection. This verse reveals the unchanging, pure state beyond any disturbance or cause.
avadhuta_gita::185.modern_relevance: When stress clouds your mind, remember your true self is untouched and free beyond all worries and confusion.
avadhuta_gita::185.insight: This verse shifts your view from seeing yourself as affected by problems to recognizing your essence as eternally pure and free.

avadhuta_gita::186.verse_sanskrit:
ध्यानानि सर्वाणि परित्यजन्ति शुभाशुभं कर्म परित्यजन्ति ।
त्यागामृतं तात पिबन्ति धीराः स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::186.verse_hindi: धीर पुरुष सम्पूर्ण ध्यानों का परित्याग कर देते हैं, शुभ एवं अशुभ सभी प्रकार के कर्मों का त्याग कर देते हैं। वे केवल त्याग रूपी अमृत का ही पान करते हैं। मैं स्वरूप से ही मुक्त एवं रोग रहित हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::186.english_translation: Wise beings abandon all meditations and all good and bad actions; they partake only in the nectar of renunciation. I am inherently free and free from disease.
avadhuta_gita::186.translation_literal: ध्यानानि (meditations) सर्वाणि (all) परित्यजन्ति (abandon) शुभाशुभं (good and bad) कर्म (actions) परित्यजन्ति (abandon) । त्यागामृतं (nectar of renunciation) तात (dear one) पिबन्ति (drink) धीराः (wise beings) स्वरूपनिर्वाणमनामयोऽहम् (I am by nature free, liberated, and free from disease) ॥
avadhuta_gita::186.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::186.essence: True wisdom is complete renunciation, revealing your natural, effortless freedom.
avadhuta_gita::186.simple_meaning: Wise people let go of all meditation techniques and all kinds of actions, good or bad. They simply embrace the sweetness of complete renunciation and recognize their natural freedom.
avadhuta_gita::186.simple_insight: There is peace in realizing that freedom comes not from doing more, but from releasing all doing.
avadhuta_gita::186.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya speaks to those seeking liberation, teaching that true wisdom means abandoning all structured spiritual practices and all actions bound by good and bad. Instead, one embraces renunciation itself as the ultimate nectar, recognizing the self as already free and untouched by suffering.
avadhuta_gita::186.modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed by endless self-improvement techniques and moral choices. This verse reminds you that true peace arises when you stop clinging to all efforts and simply rest in your natural freedom.
avadhuta_gita::186.insight: It teaches you to release all effortful practices and moral judgments, shifting your focus to the effortless state of innate freedom.

avadhuta_gita::187.verse_sanskrit:
विन्दति विन्दति न हि न हि यत्र छन्दोलक्षणं न हि न हि तत्र ।
समरसमग्नो भावितपूतः प्रलपति तत्त्वं परमवधूतः ॥
avadhuta_gita::187.verse_hindi: परम अवधूत ( श्रेष्ठ संन्यासी) एकरस आत्मा में ही मग्न रहता है तथा पवित्र हुआ आत्म तत्व का ही कथन करता है। जिस चेतन ब्रह्म में छन्द और लक्षण नहीं है उसमें प्राप्त होता है।
avadhuta_gita::187.english_translation: The supreme Avadhuta remains absorbed in the singular true self and speaks only of the pure essence, which is beyond all forms and qualities.
avadhuta_gita::187.translation_literal: विन्दति (finds) / विन्दति (finds) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / यत्र (where) / छन्द (rhythm) / लक्षणं (qualities) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / तत्र (there) / समरसमग्नः (deeply absorbed in the one essence) / भावितपूतः (pure in nature) / प्रलपति (speaks) / तत्त्वं (truth) / परमवधूतः (supreme Avadhuta)
avadhuta_gita::187.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::187.essence: The true self is pure, formless, and always present within you.
avadhuta_gita::187.simple_meaning: The highest sage stays fully immersed in the one true self and speaks only about this pure, formless reality.
avadhuta_gita::187.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing you rest in a pure, unchanging essence beyond appearances.
avadhuta_gita::187.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Dattatreya describes the supreme Avadhuta, who is completely absorbed in the undivided true self. This self is beyond any qualities like rhythm or signs. The Avadhuta speaks only of this pure essence, free from all duality or form.
avadhuta_gita::187.modern_relevance: When your mind quiets, you realize your core is untouched by labels or moods—it’s a steady, pure presence.
avadhuta_gita::187.insight: It teaches you to recognize your identity beyond all changing qualities, resting in pure awareness alone.

avadhuta_gita::188.verse_sanskrit:
ॐ इति गदितं गगनसमं तत् न परापरसारविचार इति ।
अविलासविलासनिराकरणं कथमक्षरबिन्दुसमुच्चरणम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::188.verse_hindi: ‘ॐ’ इस प्रकार जो उच्चारण किया जाता है वह आकाश तुल्य (व्यापक) है। वह पर और अपर (ब्रह्म) के सार का विचार नहीं है। उसमें जगत के विलास एवं अविलास का अभाव है। फिर अक्षर एवं बिन्दु रूप ‘ॐ’ शब्द का उच्चारण किस प्रकार हो सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::188.english_translation: 'Om' as pronounced is vast like the sky; it is not a concept of the supreme reality beyond or within. It lacks all play and display of the world. How then can the sound 'Om' be formed from the imperishable point and letters?
avadhuta_gita::188.translation_literal: ॐ (Om) / इति (thus) / गदितं (pronounced) / गगनसमं (like the sky) / तत् (that) / न (not) / परापर (beyond and within) / सारविचार (essence-concept) / इति (thus) / अविलास (absence-of-play) / विलासनिराकरणं (display-negation) / कथम् (how) / अक्षरबिन्दु (imperishable-point) / समुच्चरणम् (combination)
avadhuta_gita::188.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::188.essence: The ultimate reality is beyond all sounds, words, and concepts, including 'Om'.
avadhuta_gita::188.simple_meaning: The true self is vast and beyond all forms, sounds, or concepts. The sacred sound 'Om' cannot fully express this limitless reality.
avadhuta_gita::188.simple_insight: You feel the freedom in knowing the deepest truth cannot be confined to words or sounds.
avadhuta_gita::188.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that the sacred sound 'Om', though revered, is limited compared to the infinite true self that is boundless and beyond all worldly attributes or concepts.
avadhuta_gita::188.modern_relevance: When you try to describe your deepest self in words, you find language falls short—this reveals how vast you truly are.
avadhuta_gita::188.insight: It teaches you to release any attempt to define the ultimate through concepts or sounds, freeing your mind from limits.

avadhuta_gita::189.verse_sanskrit:
इति तत्त्वमसिप्रभृतिश्रुतिभिः प्रतिपादितमात्मनि तत्त्वमसि ।
त्वमुपाधिविवर्जितसर्वसमं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::189.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार श्रुतियों ने जिस आत्मा को ‘तत्वमसि’ (यह तू ही हैं) कहकर प्रतिपादित किया है वह आत्मा तू ही हैं। इसलिए तू उपाधि से रहित सर्वत्र समरूप है। हे मन! तू सर्व में समान रूप है फिर किस वास्ते रूदन करता है।
avadhuta_gita::189.english_translation: The self proclaimed as 'You are that' by scriptures is indeed you; free of all limiting conditions and equal everywhere. So why does your mind weep, when you are the same in all?
avadhuta_gita::189.translation_literal: इति (thus) तत्त्वमसि (you are that) प्रभृतिश्रुतिभिः (by scriptures and others) प्रतिपादितम् (declared) आत्मनि (in the self) तत्त्वमसि (you are that) । त्वम् (you) उपाधि-विवर्जित-सर्वसमम् (free from limiting conditions, equal in all) किमु (then why) रोदिषि (do you weep) मानसि (mind) सर्वसमम् (equal in all) ॥
avadhuta_gita::189.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::189.essence: Your true self is unlimited and equal everywhere; your mind’s sorrow is unfounded.
avadhuta_gita::189.simple_meaning: You are the true self described as 'You are that' by scriptures, free from all limiting identities and equal everywhere. So your mind should not sorrow.
avadhuta_gita::189.simple_insight: There is peace in realizing your mind’s sadness doesn’t reflect your true nature.
avadhuta_gita::189.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that the self declared by sacred teachings as 'You are that' is truly you—free from all conditions and equally present everywhere. He asks the restless mind why it mourns when it is one with all.
avadhuta_gita::189.modern_relevance: When your mind feels overwhelmed or sorrowful, remember that your true self is untouched by those feelings and is the same everywhere.
avadhuta_gita::189.insight: It shifts your perspective from identifying with the restless mind to recognizing your limitless self beyond sorrow.

avadhuta_gita::190.verse_sanskrit:
अध ऊर्ध्वविवर्जितसर्वसमं बहिरन्तरवर्जितसर्वसमम् ।
यदि चैकविवर्जितसर्वसमं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::190.verse_hindi: हे मन! तू ऊपर और नीचे से रहित सब में सम है, बाहर और भीतर से रहित सबमें सम है और यदि एक से रहित सब में सम है तो तू किस वास्ते रूदन करता है।
avadhuta_gita::190.english_translation: O mind! You are equal in all, free from up and down, free from inside and outside, and if you are equal in all without even one, then why do you weep?
avadhuta_gita::190.translation_literal: अध (down) / ऊर्ध्व (up) / विवर्जित (without) / सर्वसमं (equal in all) / बहिरन्तरवर्जित (without outside and inside) / सर्वसमम् (equal in all) / यदि (if) / चैक (one) / विवर्जित (without) / सर्वसमं (equal in all) / किमु (why) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / मानसि (mind) / सर्वसमम् (equal in all)
avadhuta_gita::190.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::190.essence: The mind is already balanced beyond all opposites; sorrow lacks foundation.
avadhuta_gita::190.simple_meaning: Your mind is naturally equal everywhere, above and below, inside and outside. If this is true, then why do you feel sorrow?
avadhuta_gita::190.simple_insight: Realizing your equal nature can soften sorrow and bring peace to your heart.
avadhuta_gita::190.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya addresses the restless mind, showing it is naturally free from all dualities like up/down and inside/outside. If the mind is already equal in all respects, then sorrow has no true basis to arise.
avadhuta_gita::190.modern_relevance: When emotions overwhelm you, remembering your natural balance can quiet your inner storms and reduce needless suffering.
avadhuta_gita::190.insight: It shifts your awareness to see that sorrow arises from false separations, helping you embrace your inherent wholeness.

avadhuta_gita::191.verse_sanskrit:
न हि कल्पितकल्पविचार इति न हि कारणकार्यविचार इति ।
पदसन्धिविवर्जितसर्वसमं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::191.verse_hindi: हे मन! तू न तो कल्पित है, न कल्प आदि विचार ही है, न तु कारण एवं कार्यरूपी विचार ही है। तेरे में पद एवं सन्धि भी नहीं है बल्कि सबमें सम ही है। फिर किस वास्ते रूदन करता है।
avadhuta_gita::191.english_translation: O mind, you are neither imagined nor a product of imagination, nor a cause or effect; you are beyond all divisions and equal in everything. Why then do you weep?
avadhuta_gita::191.translation_literal: न (not) हि (indeed) कल्पित (imagined) कल्प (imagination) विचार (thought) इति (is) न (not) हि (indeed) कारण (cause) कारण (cause) कार्य (effect) विचार (thought) इति (is) । पदसन्धि (word+junction) विवर्जित (without) सर्व (all) समम् (equal) किमु (then what) रोदिषि (do you cry) मानसि (mind) सर्वसमम् (equal in all) ॥
avadhuta_gita::191.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::191.essence: The mind is not fractured or caused; it is fundamentally whole and equal everywhere.
avadhuta_gita::191.simple_meaning: Your mind is not a mere thought or cause-effect chain. It is undivided and equal everywhere. So why are you upset?
avadhuta_gita::191.simple_insight: You might see yourself as broken, but your mind is already whole and undivided.
avadhuta_gita::191.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya addresses the restless mind, rejecting all notions that it is a mere idea or a chain of causes and effects. He points out the mind's true nature as undivided and equal in all things, questioning why it suffers if it is whole.
avadhuta_gita::191.modern_relevance: When your thoughts spiral and you feel fragmented, remember your mind is whole beneath the chaos. There's no need to suffer over illusions.
avadhuta_gita::191.insight: It shifts your view from seeing the mind as fractured to recognizing its fundamental unity, calming inner conflict.

avadhuta_gita::192.verse_sanskrit:
न हि बोधविबोधसमाधिरिति न हि देशविदेशसमाधिरिति ।
न हि कालविकालसमाधिरिति किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::192.verse_hindi: हे मन! तू ज्ञान एवं अज्ञान रूपी समाधि नहीं है, न देश, विदेश एवं काल विकाल रूपी समाधि ही है। तू सर्वत्र समरूप है फिर किस वास्ते रूदन करता है।
avadhuta_gita::192.english_translation: O mind! You are neither the state of knowledge nor ignorance, nor the union of place and time. You are the same everywhere; why then do you weep?
avadhuta_gita::192.translation_literal: न (not) हि (indeed) बोध-विबोध-समाधि-इति (knowledge-ignorance-union thus) न (not) हि (indeed) देश-विदेश-समाधि-इति (place-foreign-union thus) न (not) हि (indeed) काल-विकाल-समाधि-इति (time-change-union thus) किमु (why) रोदिषि (do you weep) मानसि (mind) सर्व-समम् (all-equal)
avadhuta_gita::192.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::192.essence: Your true self is always equal and unchanged; the mind’s suffering is unnecessary.
avadhuta_gita::192.simple_meaning: Your mind is neither knowledge nor ignorance, neither bound by place nor time. It is always the same everywhere, so there’s no reason to suffer or cry.
avadhuta_gita::192.simple_insight: You can feel calm knowing your true self is constant beyond all changes and troubles.
avadhuta_gita::192.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Dattatreya addresses the restless mind that confuses itself with knowledge, ignorance, or changes of time and place. He reminds that the true self remains unchanged, whole, and equal everywhere, so the mind’s sorrow has no basis.
avadhuta_gita::192.modern_relevance: When your thoughts swirl anxiously over changing situations or past mistakes, this verse reminds you that your true being is untouched by these shifts—and you can choose peace instead of pain.
avadhuta_gita::192.insight: It shifts your awareness from identifying with fluctuating thoughts and feelings to recognizing your unchanging true nature.

avadhuta_gita::193.verse_sanskrit:
न हि कुम्भनभो न हि कुम्भ इति न हि जीववपुर्न हि जीव इति ।
