न हि कारणकार्यविभाग इति किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::193.verse_hindi: हे मन! न तो तू घटाकाश है न घट ही हैं, न तू जीव का शरीर है न जीव ही है, तेरे में कारण एवं कार्य का विभाग भी नहीं है फिर तू किस वास्ते रूदन करता है। तू सर्वत्र सम रूप है।
avadhuta_gita::193.english_translation: O mind! You are neither the pot's space nor the pot; neither the living body nor the living being; there is no division of cause and effect in you. So why do you cry? You are equal everywhere.
avadhuta_gita::193.translation_literal: न (not) हि (indeed) कुम्भनभो (pot's space) न (not) हि (indeed) कुम्भ (pot) इति (thus) न (not) हि (indeed) जीववपुर्न (living body) न (not) हि (indeed) जीव (living being) इति (thus) । न (not) हि (indeed) कारणकार्यविभाग (cause-effect division) इति (thus) किमु (why) रोदिषि (do you cry) मानसि (mind) सर्वसमम् (equal everywhere) ॥
avadhuta_gita::193.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::193.essence: You are not divided parts but an equal, undivided whole beyond cause and effect.
avadhuta_gita::193.simple_meaning: You are not the body or the mind, nor divided into cause and effect. You are equally whole everywhere. So, why do you suffer?
avadhuta_gita::193.simple_insight: You can feel peace knowing you aren't fragmented but complete as you are.
avadhuta_gita::193.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya speaks to the restless mind, explaining it is neither the body nor the life within it, nor divided into cause and effect. This insight challenges the mind’s suffering by revealing its essential wholeness and equality everywhere.
avadhuta_gita::193.modern_relevance: When your thoughts spiral in blame or fear, remember you are not broken parts but a complete whole beyond cause and effect.
avadhuta_gita::193.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with limited parts to recognizing your undivided, whole nature.

avadhuta_gita::194.verse_sanskrit:
इह सर्वनिरन्तरमोक्षपदं लघुदीर्घविचारविहीन इति ।
न हि वर्तुलकोणविभाग इति किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::194.verse_hindi: यह आत्मा सर्व, एकरस एवं मोक्ष पद वाला है। यह लघु, दीर्घ आदि विचार से रहित है। इसमें गोल एवं कोण का विभाग भी नहीं है। फिर हे मन तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू सर्वत्र समरूप हैं।
avadhuta_gita::194.english_translation: This true self is all, uniform, and the state of freedom; it is beyond short or long thoughts. It has no divisions like circle or angle. So, mind, why do you weep? You are the same everywhere.
avadhuta_gita::194.translation_literal: इह (here) सर्व (all) निरन्तर (continuous) मोक्षपदं (state of freedom) लघु (short) दीर्घ (long) विचारविहीन (without thought) इति (thus) । न (not) हि (indeed) वर्तुल (circle) कोण (angle) विभाग (division) इति (thus) किमु (why) रोदिषि (do you weep) मानसि (mind) सर्वसमम् (entirely uniform) ॥
avadhuta_gita::194.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::194.essence: The true self is completely uniform and free beyond all distinctions and thoughts.
avadhuta_gita::194.simple_meaning: The true self is complete, unchanging, and beyond concepts like length or shape. It has no divisions or differences inside it. So the restless mind should not grieve.
avadhuta_gita::194.simple_insight: You can feel peace knowing your true self is uniform and free of all limits.
avadhuta_gita::194.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares the true self to be beyond all dualities—no divisions like short or long, circle or angle exist in it. The restless mind cries in ignorance, forgetting it is always whole and the state of freedom itself.
avadhuta_gita::194.modern_relevance: When you feel fragmented or overwhelmed by worries and comparisons, this reminds you that your true self is uniform and unbroken beneath all thoughts.
avadhuta_gita::194.insight: It shifts your perspective from seeing yourself as divided or limited to recognizing your essential wholeness without distinctions.

avadhuta_gita::195.verse_sanskrit:
इह शून्यविशून्यविहीन इति इह शुद्धविशुद्धविहीन इति ।
इह सर्वविसर्वविहीन इति किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::195.verse_hindi: इस (आत्मा) में शून्य एवं विशून्य विहीन, शुद्ध एवं विशुद्ध विहीन, सर्व एवं विसर्व विहीन आदि का व्यवहार नहीं होता है। हे मन! तू सर्व में सम है फिर किस वास्ते रूदन करता है।
avadhuta_gita::195.english_translation: The true self is free from emptiness and fullness, purity and impurity, existence and non-existence; your mind is equal in all, so why do you weep?
avadhuta_gita::195.translation_literal: इह (here/in this) / शून्यविशून्यविहीन (free from emptiness and non-emptiness) / इति (thus) / इह (here/in this) / शुद्धविशुद्धविहीन (free from purity and impurity) / इति (thus) / इह (here/in this) / सर्वविसर्वविहीन (free from existence and non-existence) / इति (thus) / किमु (why) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / मानसि (mind) / सर्वसमम् (equal in all)
avadhuta_gita::195.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::195.essence: The true self is beyond all pairs of opposites, so the mind has no reason to suffer.
avadhuta_gita::195.simple_meaning: The true self is beyond all dualities like empty or full, pure or impure, existent or nonexistent. Your mind is equal in everything, so it has no reason to cry.
avadhuta_gita::195.simple_insight: You can find peace knowing your true self is untouched by life's opposing forces.
avadhuta_gita::195.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals that the true self is beyond all dual concepts such as emptiness and fullness, purity and impurity, existence and non-existence. The restless mind, caught in these opposites, is asked why it continues to suffer when the true self remains untouched and equal in all.
avadhuta_gita::195.modern_relevance: When your thoughts swing between highs and lows, remember your true self is constant and untouched by these ups and downs.
avadhuta_gita::195.insight: It teaches you to see your mind's fluctuations as separate from your true self, which stays steady beyond all dualities.

avadhuta_gita::196.verse_sanskrit:
न हि भिन्नविभिन्नविचार इति बहिरन्तरसन्धिविचार इति ।
अरिमित्रविवर्जितसर्वसमं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::196.verse_hindi: इस (आत्मा) में भिन्न एवं विभिन्न का विचार भी नहीं हो सकता, बाहर, भीतर और सन्धि का विचार भी इसमें नहीं हो सकता। शुद्ध एवं मित्र से रहित यह सर्व में सम है। फिर हे मन! तू किस वास्ते रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::196.english_translation: The true self has no distinctions or divisions, no inner or outer separations. It is pure, free from friends or enemies, and equal in all. So why does your mind weep? You are equal in everything.
avadhuta_gita::196.translation_literal: न (not) / हि (indeed) / भिन्नविभिन्नविचार (divided and diverse thoughts) / इति (thus) / बहिरन्तरसन्धिविचार (outer, inner, and junction thoughts) / इति (thus) / अरिमित्रविवर्जितसर्वसमं (free from enemies and friends, equal in all) / किमु (then why) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / मानसि (mind) / सर्वसमम् (equal in all)
avadhuta_gita::196.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::196.essence: Your true self is undivided, equal everywhere, beyond all inner conflicts.
avadhuta_gita::196.simple_meaning: Your true self is not split or divided; it has no inner or outer boundaries. It is pure and equal everywhere. So your mind need not suffer or cry.
avadhuta_gita::196.simple_insight: You can feel calm knowing your true self is whole and free from conflict.
avadhuta_gita::196.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that the true self is beyond all mental divisions—no inner or outer distinctions exist. It is pure and unaffected by friends or enemies. Even when the restless mind feels sorrow, the self remains unbroken and equal in all.
avadhuta_gita::196.modern_relevance: When your mind feels overwhelmed by conflicts and divisions, this reminds you that your true self is whole and equal beyond all that turmoil.
avadhuta_gita::196.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with the restless mind's divisions to recognizing your unchanging, equal true self.

avadhuta_gita::197.verse_sanskrit:
न हि शिष्यविशिष्यस्वरूप इति न चराचरभेदविचार इति ।
इह सर्वनिरन्तरमोक्षपदं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::197.verse_hindi: यह आत्मा शिष्य एवं अशिष्य स्वरूप भी नहीं है, न इसमें चर एवं अचर जगत के भेद का विचार ही है। यह सर्वरूप, निरन्तर एवं मोक्ष पद वाला है. इसलिए हे मन! तू किस वास्ते रूदन करता है तू सर्व में सम आत्मा है।
avadhuta_gita::197.english_translation: The true self is neither teacher nor student, nor is there a distinction between moving and non-moving; it is all-pervading, eternal, and the state of freedom. So why do you weep, mind? You are the self that is one with all.
avadhuta_gita::197.translation_literal: न (not) हि (indeed) शिष्य (student) विशिष्य (teacher) स्वरूप (form) इति (thus) न (not) चराचर (moving and non-moving) भेद (difference) विचार (thought) इति (thus) । इह (here) सर्व (all) निरन्तर (continuous) मोक्षपदं (state of freedom) किमु (why indeed) रोदिषि (do you weep) मानसि (mind) सर्वसमम् (all-pervading) ॥
avadhuta_gita::197.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::197.essence: You are the undivided, eternal self in which all distinctions dissolve.
avadhuta_gita::197.simple_meaning: You are not a separate learner or teacher, nor divided into moving or still; you are the unchanging freedom present everywhere. So do not grieve, because you are one with everything.
avadhuta_gita::197.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing you are never truly alone or divided from anything.
avadhuta_gita::197.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals that the true self transcends all dualities like student and teacher or moving and still. This self is continuous, all-encompassing, and free. The verse encourages the restless mind to stop suffering, recognizing it is already whole.
avadhuta_gita::197.modern_relevance: When anxiety overwhelms you, remember you are not separate or fragmented but completely whole and free within.
avadhuta_gita::197.insight: It shifts the mind from feeling isolated to recognizing unity with all existence.

avadhuta_gita::198.verse_sanskrit:
ननु रूपविरूपविहीन इति ननु भिन्नविभिन्नविहीन इति ।
ननु सर्गविसर्गविहीन इति किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::198.verse_hindi: निश्चय ही यह (आत्मा) रूप एवं विरूप से विहीन हैं, निश्चय ही यह भिन्न एवं विभिन्न रूपों से विहीन है, निश्चय ही यह उत्पत्ति एवं प्रलय से भी रहित है फिर हे मन! तू किस वास्ते रूदन करता है। तू आत्मरूप होने से सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::198.english_translation: The true self is certainly free from form and formlessness, free from difference and diversity, free from creation and dissolution—why then does the mind cry? It is the same in all.
avadhuta_gita::198.translation_literal: ननु (surely) रूपविरूपविहीन (form-and-formless-free) इति (thus) ननु (surely) भिन्नविभिन्नविहीन (difference-and-diverse-free) इति (thus) । ननु (surely) सर्गविसर्गविहीन (creation-and-destruction-free) इति (thus) किमु (why) रोदिषि (do you cry) मानसि (mind) सर्वसमम् (same-in-all) ॥
avadhuta_gita::198.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::198.essence: You are the unchanging self, present equally in all, beyond all forms and changes.
avadhuta_gita::198.simple_meaning: You are the true self that never changes, is beyond all forms, differences, creation, or destruction. So your mind need not suffer or cry.
avadhuta_gita::198.simple_insight: You can feel peace knowing your essential nature is unchanging and universal.
avadhuta_gita::198.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the true self is beyond all appearances, distinctions, and cycles of creation and destruction. Despite this, the restless mind cries and suffers, unaware that the essence is always the same everywhere.
avadhuta_gita::198.modern_relevance: When your worries and fears overwhelm you, remember that your true being is unchanging and present everywhere, untouched by shifting life circumstances.
avadhuta_gita::198.insight: It teaches you to recognize that your essential nature remains steady despite mental turmoil, reducing suffering.

avadhuta_gita::199.verse_sanskrit:
न गुणागुणपाशनिबन्ध इति मृतजीवनकर्म करोमि कथम् ।
इति शुद्धनिरञ्जनसर्वसमं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::199.verse_hindi: गुण एवं निर्गुण के पाश का बन्धन उसमें ( आत्मा से) नहीं है इसलिए वह मृत एवं जीवन के कर्म किस प्रकार करता है। वह शुद्ध, निर्दोष, सर्वरूप एवं सम है फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू वही आत्मा है जो सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::199.english_translation: The true self is not bound by qualities or their absence, so how can it perform the deeds of death and life? It is pure, spotless, and equal in all forms; why then does your mind weep? You are that self, present in all.
avadhuta_gita::199.translation_literal: न (not) गुणागुणपाशनिबन्ध (bondage of qualities and non-qualities) इति (thus) मृतजीवनकर्म (dead and living actions) करोमि (do) कथम् (how) । इति (thus) शुद्धनिरञ्जनसर्वसमं (pure, spotless, equal in all) किमु (why then) रोदिषि (you weep) मानसि (mind) सर्वसमम् (equal in all) ॥
avadhuta_gita::199.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::199.essence: The true self is untouched by qualities and beyond all sorrow.
avadhuta_gita::199.simple_meaning: You are not tied to qualities or their opposites, so you don't truly act in life or death. You are pure and equal in everything. Your mind’s sorrow is unnecessary.
avadhuta_gita::199.simple_insight: You can feel peace knowing your true self is beyond all suffering and change.
avadhuta_gita::199.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the true self is beyond all dualities like good and bad qualities, so it cannot perform actions that bind it to life or death. The mind, which feels sorrow, is mistaken because the self is pure and present everywhere, unchanging.
avadhuta_gita::199.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by ups and downs or personal failures, remember your true self is untouched and equal in all situations.
avadhuta_gita::199.insight: It teaches you to see sorrow as a product of the restless mind, not the pure self, helping you detach from emotional pain.

avadhuta_gita::200.verse_sanskrit:
इह भावविभावविहीन इति इह कामविकामविहीन इति ।
इह बोधतमं खलु मोक्षसमं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::200.verse_hindi: यह आत्मा भाव एवं विभाव से रहित हैं, यह काम एवं विकाम से रहित है। यह ज्ञान स्वरूप एवं निश्चय ही मोक्ष स्वरूप हैं इसलिए हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है, तू सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::200.english_translation: The true self is without emotions or their opposites, without desire or aversion. It is knowledge itself and truly the state of freedom. So, O mind, why do you cry? You are one with everything.
avadhuta_gita::200.translation_literal: इह (here) भावविभावविहीन (without emotions and their opposites) इति (thus) इह (here) कामविकामविहीन (without desire and aversion) इति (thus) । इह (here) बोधतमं (the highest knowledge) खलु (indeed) मोक्षसमं (equal to liberation) किमु (then why) रोदिषि (do you cry) मानसि (O mind) सर्वसमम् (one with all) ॥
avadhuta_gita::200.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::200.essence: Your true self is untouched by emotions and desires and is one with all.
avadhuta_gita::200.simple_meaning: Your true self is beyond all emotions, desires, and opposites. It is pure knowledge and true freedom. So your mind need not suffer or cry.
avadhuta_gita::200.simple_insight: Knowing your true self is untouched by feelings brings peace amid inner turmoil.
avadhuta_gita::200.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals that the true self is free from all emotional swings and desires. This self is pure knowledge and identical to liberation. The mind’s suffering is unnecessary because the self is always whole and one with everything.
avadhuta_gita::200.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by mood swings or cravings, remember your deeper self is steady and beyond these changes.
avadhuta_gita::200.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with transient emotions to recognizing your unchanging true nature.

avadhuta_gita::201.verse_sanskrit:
इह तत्त्वनिरन्तरतत्त्वमिति न हि सन्धिविसन्धिविहीन इति ।
यदि सर्वविवर्जितसर्वसमं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::201.verse_hindi: इसमें (आत्मा में) तत्व अथवा नित्य तत्व का व्यवहार नहीं हैं, न ही इसमें सन्धि और विसन्धि विहीन का विचार ही है। यदि यह सर्व से रहित सर्व में सम है तो फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू आत्मा होने से सर्व में सम हैं।
avadhuta_gita::201.english_translation: The true self has no constant or changing parts, no junctions or separations; if it is complete beyond all, why does your mind weep?
avadhuta_gita::201.translation_literal: इह (here/in this) तत्त्वनिरन्तर-तत्त्वम् (constant principle) इति (thus) न (not) हि (indeed) सन्धि-विसन्धि-विहीन (without junctions and separations) इति (thus). यदि (if) सर्व-विवर्जित-सर्व-समम् (all removed, all equal) किमु (then why) रोदिषि (do you weep) मानसि (mind) सर्व-समम् (all equal).
avadhuta_gita::201.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::201.essence: Your true self is whole and unchanged; your mind’s sorrow is unfounded.
avadhuta_gita::201.simple_meaning: The true self is unchanging and undivided; if you are complete, your restless mind should not grieve.
avadhuta_gita::201.simple_insight: You can feel calm knowing your true self is whole beyond all change.
avadhuta_gita::201.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the true self has no parts or divisions, no changes or breaks. It is complete and beyond all duality. He challenges the mind that still suffers, asking why it cries if it truly belongs to this whole.
avadhuta_gita::201.modern_relevance: After a long day filled with stress and conflict, the restless mind still feels upset, yet deep down, your essential self remains whole and untouched.
avadhuta_gita::201.insight: It teaches you to notice the contrast between the mind’s sorrow and the unbroken completeness of your true self, encouraging detachment from mental suffering.

avadhuta_gita::202.verse_sanskrit:
अनिकेतकुटी परिवारसमं इहसङ्गविसङ्गविहीनपरम् ।
इह बोधविबोधविहीनपरं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::202.verse_hindi: एकान्त कुटी में रहे अथवा परिवार में रहे सब समान है क्योंकि वह (आत्मा) संग एवं विसंग से रहित है। वह ज्ञान एवं अज्ञान से भी रहित है तथा वही श्रेष्ठ है फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण रूदन करता है। तू वही आत्मा है जो सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::202.english_translation: Whether living alone in a hut or within a family, all is the same because the inner being is free from attachment and aversion. It is beyond knowledge and ignorance and is supreme; so why do you grieve, mind? You are the true self present in all.
avadhuta_gita::202.translation_literal: अनिकेतकुटी (homeless hut) / परिवारसमं (equal to family) / इहसङ्गविसङ्गविहीनपरम् (here attachment-aversion free supreme) / इह (here) / बोधविबोधविहीनपरं (knowledge-ignorance free supreme) / किमु (why) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / मानसि (mind) / सर्वसमम् (equal to all)
avadhuta_gita::202.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::202.essence: Your true self is beyond all attachments and is equally present everywhere.
avadhuta_gita::202.simple_meaning: Your true self does not depend on being alone or with others; it is beyond attachments, knowledge, and ignorance. So, your mind need not grieve.
avadhuta_gita::202.simple_insight: You can find peace knowing your true self is the same everywhere and beyond all pains.
avadhuta_gita::202.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that whether a person lives in solitude or family life, the true self remains unchanged and unaffected by attachments or opposites like knowledge and ignorance. The restless mind’s grief is unnecessary because the true self pervades all.
avadhuta_gita::202.modern_relevance: When you feel restless or overwhelmed by relationships or isolation, remember your true self remains steady and whole beyond these feelings.
avadhuta_gita::202.insight: This verse shifts your perspective from outer conditions to the unchanging self, easing emotional turmoil caused by attachments or aversions.

avadhuta_gita::203.verse_sanskrit:
अविकारविकारमसत्यमिति अविलक्षविलक्षमसत्यमिति ।
यदि केवलमात्मनि सत्यमिति किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::203.verse_hindi: अविकार आत्मा का यह विकार युक्त जगत है यह असत्य है। जो अदृश्य है उसका यह दृश्य जगत असत्य है। जबकि केवल आत्मा ही सत्य रूप है इस लिये हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू आत्मा होने से सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::203.english_translation: The world of change is false; the changeless self is real. The visible is untrue; only the true self is real. So, mind, why do you grieve? You are equal with all as the true self.
avadhuta_gita::203.translation_literal: अविकारविकारमसत्यमिति (the changeless and the changing are untrue) / अविलक्षविलक्षमसत्यमिति (the unseen and the seen are untrue) / यदि (if) केवलमात्मनि (only in the self) सत्यमिति (is true) / किमु (then why) रोदिषि (do you cry) मानसि (mind) सर्वसमम् (equal in all)
avadhuta_gita::203.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::203.essence: You are the unchanging true self beyond the false world of change and sorrow.
avadhuta_gita::203.simple_meaning: The changing world around you is not real; only the unchanging true self is real. Your mind is equal with all through this true self, so there is no need to grieve.
avadhuta_gita::203.simple_insight: You can feel peace knowing your true self is beyond all change and sorrow.
avadhuta_gita::203.detailed_meaning: The sage Dattatreya teaches that the world of appearances, which changes and is visible, is false. Only the changeless true self is real. The restless mind, which grieves, is reminded it is equal with all because it is the true self.
avadhuta_gita::203.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by constant change and loss, remembering your true self is unchanging can bring calm and relief.
avadhuta_gita::203.insight: Shift your perspective from identifying with change to recognizing your unchanging true self beyond appearances.

avadhuta_gita::204.verse_sanskrit:
इह सर्वसमं खलु जीव इति इह सर्वनिरन्तरजीव इति ।
इह केवलनिश्चलजीव इति किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::204.verse_hindi: इस संसार में निश्चय करके जीव ही सर्व एवं सम हैं, इस संसार में निश्चल केवल जीव ही है। हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम हैं।
avadhuta_gita::204.english_translation: In this world, certainly, the living being is the same in all; in this world, the living being alone is unchanging. O mind, why do you weep? You are the same in all.
avadhuta_gita::204.translation_literal: इह (in this) / सर्वसमं (all-equal) / खलु (indeed) / जीव (living being) / इति (is) / इह (in this) / सर्वनिरन्तरजीव (all-continuous-living being) / इति (is) / इह (in this) / केवलनिश्चलजीव (only-unchanging-living being) / इति (is) / किमु (why) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / मानसि (O mind) / सर्वसमम् (all-equal)
avadhuta_gita::204.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::204.essence: You are the same unchanging being present equally in all things.
avadhuta_gita::204.simple_meaning: Your true self is the same unchanging presence in everyone and everything; the mind’s sorrow is unfounded.
avadhuta_gita::204.simple_insight: Realizing your unity with all brings peace and ends inner sorrow.
avadhuta_gita::204.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that beneath all appearances, the living being is one and unchanging. The restless mind grieves, but it forgets that this essence is shared by all and never truly changes.
avadhuta_gita::204.modern_relevance: When you feel isolated or upset, remember your true nature is the same as everyone else’s—unchanging and whole.
avadhuta_gita::204.insight: It shifts your view from separation and suffering to recognizing your shared, constant essence.

avadhuta_gita::205.verse_sanskrit:
अविवेकविवेकमबोध इति अविकल्पविकल्पमबोध इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरबोध इति किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::205.verse_hindi: अविवेक और विवेक दोनों अज्ञान है, अविकल्प और विकल्प भी अज्ञान हैं यदि वही एक नित्य बोध है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::205.english_translation: Both ignorance and discernment are ignorance; both choice and non-choice are ignorance. If constant oneness-awareness is present, then why does your mind weep? It is equal in everything.
avadhuta_gita::205.translation_literal: अविवेक (ignorance) / विवेक (discernment) / अमबोध (non-awareness) / इति (thus) / अविकल्प (non-choice) / विकल्प (choice) / अमबोध (non-awareness) / इति (thus) / यदि (if) / च (also) / एक (one) / निरन्तर (continuous) / बोध (awareness) / इति (thus) / किमु (why) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / मानसि (mind) / सर्वसमम् (equal in all)
avadhuta_gita::205.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::205.essence: True awareness is beyond all choices and confusions; your mind is already whole in everything.
avadhuta_gita::205.simple_meaning: Both lack of discernment and discernment itself are forms of confusion. True constant awareness is beyond all choices. Your mind is already equal in everything, so there is no need to weep.
avadhuta_gita::205.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing your mind's struggles arise from confusion, not reality.
avadhuta_gita::205.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that neither ignorance nor wisdom in the usual sense reflects true knowing. Both choice and non-choice are part of illusion. If the mind truly recognized its continuous oneness-awareness, it would stop suffering and see itself as equal in all.
avadhuta_gita::205.modern_relevance: When your mind is overwhelmed by indecision or doubt, remember that these are just mental states, not your true self.
avadhuta_gita::205.insight: This shifts your view from valuing mental distinctions to recognizing underlying unity beyond all dualities.

avadhuta_gita::206.verse_sanskrit:
न हि मोक्षपदं न हि बन्धपदं न हि पुण्यपदं न हि पापपदम् ।
न हि पूर्णपदं न हि रिक्तपदं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::206.verse_hindi: न मोक्ष पद, न बन्ध पद है, न पुण्य पद है, न पाप पद है, न पूर्ण पद है, न रिक्त पद है। हे मन! तू सर्व में सम है फिर किस कारण से रूदन करता है।
avadhuta_gita::206.english_translation: There is no state of liberation, no state of bondage, no state of merit, no state of fault, no state of fullness, no state of emptiness. O mind, you are equal in all; why then do you weep?
avadhuta_gita::206.translation_literal: न (no) हि (indeed) मोक्षपदं (liberation state) न (no) हि (indeed) बन्धपदं (bondage state) न (no) हि (indeed) पुण्यपदं (merit state) न (no) हि (indeed) पापपदम् (fault state) । न (no) हि (indeed) पूर्णपदं (fullness state) न (no) हि (indeed) रिक्तपदं (emptiness state) किमु (then why) रोदिषि (do you weep) मानसि (O mind) सर्वसमम् (equal in all) ॥
avadhuta_gita::206.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::206.essence: All states are illusions; your true self remains equal and untouched.
avadhuta_gita::206.simple_meaning: There is no real difference between liberation, bondage, merit, fault, fullness, or emptiness. Your mind is always the same everywhere, so there is no reason to suffer or cry.
avadhuta_gita::206.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing that all states are equal, and your pain is a false impression.
avadhuta_gita::206.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya addresses the restless mind caught in dualities like liberation and bondage, merit and fault. He reveals these states as illusions, showing the mind's true nature is always equal and unchanging, questioning why it suffers.
avadhuta_gita::206.modern_relevance: When your emotions swing wildly between success and failure, this verse reminds you that your true self is untouched by those ups and downs.
avadhuta_gita::206.insight: It shifts your awareness from identifying with changing conditions to recognizing your unchanging, equal nature beyond them.

avadhuta_gita::207.verse_sanskrit:
यदि वर्णविवर्णविहीनसमं यदि कारणकार्यविहीनसमम् ।
यदिभेदविभेदविहीनसमं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::207.verse_hindi: यदि यह आत्मा वर्ण एवं विवर्ण से रहित और सम है, यदि यह कारण एवं कार्य से रहित और सम है, यदि यह भेद और विभेद से रहित और सम है तो हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू आत्मा होने से सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::207.english_translation: If the true self is without color or colorlessness, without cause or effect, without difference or distinction, then why do you, mind, weep? The true self is equal in all.
avadhuta_gita::207.translation_literal: यदि (if) वर्ण (color) विवर्ण (colorlessness) विहीन (without) समं (equal) यदि (if) कारण (cause) कार्य (effect) विहीन (without) समम् (equal) यदिभेद (difference) विभेद (distinction) विहीन (without) समं (equal) किमु (why) रोदिषि (you weep) मानसि (mind) सर्वसमम् (equal in all)
avadhuta_gita::207.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::207.essence: The true self is equal in all; the mind’s sorrow is without cause.
avadhuta_gita::207.simple_meaning: Your true self is beyond all distinctions like color, cause, and effect. It is equal and whole everywhere, so your mind has no reason to suffer.
avadhuta_gita::207.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your essential nature is equal and undivided everywhere.
avadhuta_gita::207.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that the true self is beyond all external and internal differences — such as color, cause, or effect. Despite this, the restless mind cries, forgetting this unity. Recognizing this equal nature frees the mind from sorrow.
avadhuta_gita::207.modern_relevance: When you feel upset about differences or causes beyond your control, remember your true self is unchanged and equal everywhere.
avadhuta_gita::207.insight: This verse shifts your attention from the mind’s divisions to the equal, undivided nature of your true self.

avadhuta_gita::208.verse_sanskrit:
इह सर्वनिरन्तरसर्वचिते इह केवलनिश्चलसर्वचिते ।
द्विपदादिविवर्जितसर्वचिते किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::208.verse_hindi: यह आत्मा सर्वरूप, नित्य एवं सबके चित्तों में रहता है। इस संसार में यही केवल निश्चल भाव से सब चित्तों में रहता है। यह दो पाँव से रहित सबके चित्त में रहता है। हे मन! तू वही आत्मा होने से सर्व में सम है फिर किस कारण से रूदन करता है।
avadhuta_gita::208.english_translation: This true self is all forms, always present in every mind. It is the only unchanging presence in all minds, beyond feet or limbs. O mind, since you are that true self present in all, why do you weep?
avadhuta_gita::208.translation_literal: इह (here) सर्वनिरन्तरसर्वचिते (always continuous in all minds) इह (here) केवलनिश्चलसर्वचिते (only unchanging in all minds) । द्विपदादिविवर्जितसर्वचिते (feet-less in all minds) किमु (why indeed) रोदिषि (you weep) मानसि (O mind) सर्वसमम् (equal in all)
avadhuta_gita::208.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::208.essence: You are the unchanging presence in every mind; sorrow is unnecessary.
avadhuta_gita::208.simple_meaning: The true self is present in every mind, always unchanging and whole. Since you are this true self everywhere, there is no reason to suffer or weep.
avadhuta_gita::208.simple_insight: You can feel peace by knowing you are the same unchanging presence in all things.
avadhuta_gita::208.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that the true self pervades every mind without change or limitation. Addressing the restless mind, he asks why it feels sorrow when it is inseparably whole and present everywhere.
avadhuta_gita::208.modern_relevance: When you feel isolated or upset, remembering you are the same unchanging self in all can bring calm and lessen your pain.
avadhuta_gita::208.insight: It shifts your perspective from seeing yourself as separate and vulnerable to recognizing your constant, unchanging nature everywhere.

avadhuta_gita::209.verse_sanskrit:
अतिसर्वनिरन्तरसर्वगतं अतिनिर्मलनिश्चलसर्वगतम् ।
दिनरात्रिविवर्जितसर्वगतं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::209.verse_hindi: यह आत्मा श्रेष्ठ, सर्वरूप, नित्य एवं सभी में व्याप्त है, यह अति निर्मल, निश्चल एवं सबमें व्याप्त है, फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम वही आत्मा है।
avadhuta_gita::209.english_translation: The true self is supreme, present in all forms, eternally pure and unmoving everywhere. So, mind, why do you weep? The true self is the same in all.
avadhuta_gita::209.translation_literal: अतिसर्वनिरन्तरसर्वगतं (supremely all-continuous, all-pervading) अतिनिर्मलनिश्चलसर्वगतम् (supremely pure, unmoving, all-pervading) । दिनरात्रिविवर्जितसर्वगतं (day-night devoid, all-pervading) किमु (then why) रोदिषि (do you weep) मानसि (mind) सर्वसमम् (all-equal) ॥
avadhuta_gita::209.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::209.essence: The pure, unchanging true self pervades all — there is no reason to grieve.
avadhuta_gita::209.simple_meaning: Your true self is pure, steady, and present in everything at all times. The restless mind has no reason to grieve.
avadhuta_gita::209.simple_insight: You can find peace knowing the same pure self pervades all, beyond sorrow.
avadhuta_gita::209.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that the true self is beyond all change and present everywhere at once. Despite appearances, the restless mind’s sorrow is misplaced because the true self remains pure and equal in all things.
avadhuta_gita::209.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by a difficult situation, but this reminds you that your core remains unchanged, steady, and present regardless of external troubles.
avadhuta_gita::209.insight: It shifts your focus from transient emotions to the ever-present, unchanging true self within and around you.

avadhuta_gita::210.verse_sanskrit:
न हि बन्धविबन्धसमागमनं न हि योगवियोगसमागमनम् ।
न हि तर्कवितर्कसमागमनं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::210.verse_hindi: आत्मा में बन्ध और विबन्ध का समागम नहीं है, न योग और वियोग का समागम है, न तर्क और वितर्क का समागम हैं। हे मन! फिर तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::210.english_translation: The true self does not unite with bondage or liberation, nor with joining or separation, nor with reasoning or non-reasoning. O mind, why do you weep? You are equal in all.
avadhuta_gita::210.translation_literal: न (not) हि (indeed) बन्ध (bondage) विबन्ध (liberation) समागमनं (union) न (not) हि (indeed) योग (joining) वियोग (separation) समागमनम् (union) न (not) हि (indeed) तर्क (reason) वितर्क (non-reason) समागमनं (union) किमु (then) रोदिषि (you weep) मानसि (mind) सर्वसमम् (equal in all)
avadhuta_gita::210.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::210.essence: Your true self remains equal and untouched by all opposites the mind experiences.
avadhuta_gita::210.simple_meaning: Your true self is untouched by bonds, freedom, joining, separation, or reasoning. It remains equally present in everything, so your mind’s sorrow is unfounded.
avadhuta_gita::210.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your true self never changes or suffers division.
avadhuta_gita::210.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the true self is beyond all opposites like bondage and freedom or union and separation. The restless mind is weeping unnecessarily because it forgets this essential equality.
avadhuta_gita::210.modern_relevance: When your mind feels torn by conflict or confusion, remember your true self is untouched and equal in all situations.
avadhuta_gita::210.insight: It teaches you to stop identifying with mental conflicts and see yourself as steady and undivided.

avadhuta_gita::211.verse_sanskrit:
इह कालविकालनिराकरणं अणुमात्रकृशानुनिराकरणम् ।
न हि केवलसत्यनिराकरणं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::211.verse_hindi: आत्मा में काल एवं विकाल का निराकरण है, इसमें अणु मात्र भी अग्नि का निराकरण है, केवल सत्य का निराकरण इसमें नहीं है। क्योंकि यह स्वयं सत्य है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::211.english_translation: In the true self, both time and its decay are negated, even the tiniest spark of fire is negated; only the truth itself is never negated. So, mind, why do you weep? You are equal in all.
avadhuta_gita::211.translation_literal: इह (here/in this) काल (time) विकालनिराकरणं (negation of decay) अणुमात्रकृशानुनिराकरणम् (negation even of a tiny particle's fire) । न (not) हि (indeed) केवलसत्यनिराकरणं (only truth's negation) किमु (then why) रोदिषि (do you weep) मानसि (mind) सर्वसमम् (equal in all) ॥
avadhuta_gita::211.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::211.essence: Your true self transcends time and decay; grief arises only in the restless mind.
avadhuta_gita::211.simple_meaning: Your true self is beyond time and decay; nothing in you truly diminishes. So, your mind, there is no reason to grieve because you are equal in all things.
avadhuta_gita::211.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your true self is untouched by change or loss.
avadhuta_gita::211.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that the true self is beyond the effects of time and decay, rejecting even the smallest disturbance. The restless mind, which feels loss or sorrow, is reminded that it is fundamentally equal and steady in everything.
avadhuta_gita::211.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by loss or aging, remember your true self is untouched by time’s changes and remains whole.
avadhuta_gita::211.insight: This verse shifts your perspective from identifying with fleeting loss to recognizing your timeless, unchanging nature.

avadhuta_gita::212.verse_sanskrit:
इह देहविदेहविहीन इति ननु स्वप्नसुषुप्तिविहीनपरम् ।
अभिधानविधानविहीनपरं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::212.verse_hindi: यह आत्मा देह और विदेह से रहित हैं, स्वप्न और सुषुप्ति से भी रहित हैं, विधि एवं निषेध से भी रहित है। फिर हे मन ! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू वही आत्मा है जो सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::212.english_translation: This self is without body or disembodied, beyond dream and deep sleep, beyond rules and prohibitions. So why do you weep, mind? You are the same self present in all.
avadhuta_gita::212.translation_literal: इह (here) देह (body) विदेह (disembodied) विहीन (without) इति (thus) ननु (surely) स्वप्न (dream) सुषुप्ति (deep sleep) विहीन (without) परम् (beyond) अभिधान (rules) विधान (prohibitions) विहीन (without) परं (beyond) किमु (why) रोदिषि (do you weep) मानसि (mind) सर्व (all) समम् (same)
avadhuta_gita::212.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::212.essence: You are the same limitless self beyond body, mind, and rules.
avadhuta_gita::212.simple_meaning: You are not limited by body, mind, or any rules. You are the same self everywhere. So why does your mind grieve?
avadhuta_gita::212.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing you are beyond all limits and present everywhere.
avadhuta_gita::212.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals that the true self is beyond physical form, dreaming, deep sleep, and all rules. Addressing the restless mind, he points out the futility of sorrow since you are the universal self present in all things.
avadhuta_gita::212.modern_relevance: When your thoughts spiral in anxiety, remember you are not your body or mind. This awareness can calm your restless emotions.
avadhuta_gita::212.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with limited experiences to recognizing your boundless, unchanging nature.

avadhuta_gita::213.verse_sanskrit:
गगनोपमशुद्धविशालसमं अतिसर्वविवर्जितसर्वसमम् ।
गतसारविसारविकारसमं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::213.verse_hindi: यह आत्मा आकाश के समान व्यापक, शुद्ध, विशाल एवं सम हैं, यह सर्व से रहित नहीं है किन्तु सर्व में सम हैं, यह सार, विसार एवं विकार से रहित है तथा सम है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::213.english_translation: The true self is like the sky—pure, vast, and equal; it is not separate but present in all. It is free from essence, change, and corruption. So mind, why do you grieve? You are present in everything.
avadhuta_gita::213.translation_literal: गगन (sky) / उपम (like) / अशुद्ध (impure) / विशाल (vast) / समं (equal) / अतिसर्व (beyond all) / विवर्जित (free) / सर्वसमम् (all-pervading) / गत (gone) / सार (essence) / विसार (loss) / विकार (change) / समं (equal) / किमु (why) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / मानसि (mind) / सर्वसमम् (all-pervading)
avadhuta_gita::213.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::213.essence: Your true self is vast, pure, unchanging, and present in everything — so grief is needless.
avadhuta_gita::213.simple_meaning: Your true self is like the vast sky—pure, equal, and present in everything. It does not change or suffer loss. So your mind need not grieve.
avadhuta_gita::213.simple_insight: There is relief knowing your inner being is unchanging and fully present everywhere.
avadhuta_gita::213.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the true self as vast and pure like the sky, present in all things without being touched by change or impurity. He asks the restless mind why it cries when it is itself equal to and part of everything.
avadhuta_gita::213.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by loss or change, remember your true self remains vast, untouched, and present everywhere—beyond all turmoil.
avadhuta_gita::213.insight: It teaches you to see beyond mental grief by recognising your true self as vast and unchanging within all experiences.

avadhuta_gita::214.verse_sanskrit:
इह धर्मविधर्मविरागतरमिह वस्तुविवस्तुविरागतरम् ।
इह कामविकामविरागतरं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::214.verse_hindi: इस संसार में धर्म और विधर्म से वैराग्य ही श्रेष्ठ हैं, काम और विकाम से वैराग्य ही श्रेष्ठ है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::214.english_translation: In this world, dispassion toward what is right and wrong is supreme; dispassion toward desire and aversion is supreme. So, mind, why do you weep? You are equal in everything.
avadhuta_gita::214.translation_literal: इह (here/in this world) / धर्मविधर्मविरागतरम् (dispassion beyond right and wrong) / इह (here) / वस्तुविवस्तुविरागतरम् (dispassion beyond existence and non-existence) / इह (here) / कामविकामविरागतरं (dispassion beyond desire and aversion) / किमु (then why) / रोदिषि (do you weep) / मानसि (O mind) / सर्वसमम् (equal in all)
avadhuta_gita::214.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::214.essence: True peace arises when your mind becomes equally free from desire and judgment.
avadhuta_gita::214.simple_meaning: True freedom comes from letting go of judgments about right and wrong and from releasing desire and dislike. When your mind is equal to all things, there is no need to suffer.
avadhuta_gita::214.simple_insight: You can feel calm knowing your mind is naturally balanced and free of conflict.
avadhuta_gita::214.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya teaches that in the world, the highest state is dispassion—not just indifference to good and bad, but also release from desire and aversion. The mind, which suffers, is reminded it is already equal to all things, so there is no real cause to weep.
avadhuta_gita::214.modern_relevance: When your thoughts swirl between what’s right or wrong, what you want or don’t want, you feel stuck. Recognizing your mind’s natural balance can stop that endless stress.
avadhuta_gita::214.insight: It shifts your focus from reacting to opposites toward resting in your mind’s inherent balance and equality.

avadhuta_gita::215.verse_sanskrit:
सुखदुःखविवर्जितसर्वसममिह शोकविशोकविहीनपरम् ।
गुरुशिष्यविवर्जिततत्त्वपरं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::215.verse_hindi: यह आत्मा सुख और दुःख से रहित सर्व एवं सम है, यह शोक और विशोक से रहित परम है, यह गुरु एवं शिष्य से रहित परम सत्व है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::215.english_translation: The true self is free from pleasure and pain, equal in all, beyond sorrow and distress, beyond teacher and student. So why does your mind weep? You are equal in everything.
avadhuta_gita::215.translation_literal: सुखदुःखविवर्जितसर्वसममिह (pleasure-pain-free, equal-in-all, here) / शोकविशोकविहीनपरम् (sorrow-distress-absent, supreme) / गुरुशिष्यविवर्जिततत्त्वपरं (teacher-student-free, essence-supreme) / किमु (why) / रोदिषि (do-you-weep) / मानसि (mind) / सर्वसमम् (equal-in-all)
avadhuta_gita::215.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::215.essence: The true self is beyond all dualities, so your mind need not suffer.
avadhuta_gita::215.simple_meaning: Your true self is untouched by pleasure or pain, sorrow or joy, teacher or student. So your mind need not cry, because you are equal in all.
avadhuta_gita::215.simple_insight: You can feel calm knowing your true self is beyond all ups and downs.
avadhuta_gita::215.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the true self is beyond all dualities like pleasure and pain or teacher and student. Despite this, the restless mind cries. This verse confronts that inner conflict, inviting recognition of the true self's unchanging nature.
avadhuta_gita::215.modern_relevance: When your emotions overwhelm you, remember that your deeper being is untouched by highs and lows, beyond any role or relationship.
avadhuta_gita::215.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with fluctuating feelings to resting in the unchanging true self beneath them.

avadhuta_gita::216.verse_sanskrit:
न किलाङ्कुरसारविसार इति न चलाचलसाम्यविसाम्यमिति ।
अविचारविचारविहीनमिति किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::216.verse_hindi: आत्मा में निश्चय ही सार एवं विसार का अंकुर भी नहीं है, चल, अचल, साम्य एवं वैषाम्य भी इसमें नहीं है, यह विचार एवं अविचार से भी रहित है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम आत्मा है।
avadhuta_gita::216.english_translation: The true self has no trace of arising or ceasing, no change or unchange, equality or difference; it is beyond thought and beyond non-thought. So why does your restless mind cry? The true self is the same in all.
avadhuta_gita::216.translation_literal: न (not) / किलाङ्क (any mark) / उरसार (arising) / विसार (ceasing) / इति (thus) / न (not) / चल (moving) / अचल (immovable) / साम्य (equality) / विसाम्यम् (inequality) / इति (thus) / अविचार (unthought) / विचार (thought) / विहीनम् (without) / इति (thus) / किमु (why) / रोदिषि (do you cry) / मानसि (mind) / सर्वसमम् (all-equal)
avadhuta_gita::216.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::216.essence: The true self is always unchanging and equal in all; the mind’s suffering is needless.
avadhuta_gita::216.simple_meaning: Your true self does not change or move; it is beyond all thoughts and differences. So your restless mind has no reason to suffer.
avadhuta_gita::216.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your true self never changes or separates you from anything.
avadhuta_gita::216.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the true self is untouched by any arising or ceasing, any change or stability, equality or difference. It transcends both thought and its absence. Yet the restless mind still cries, unaware it is one with this unchanging self.
avadhuta_gita::216.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by shifting feelings and thoughts, yet your core remains steady and untouched beneath the noise.
avadhuta_gita::216.insight: It teaches you to recognize the stable, changeless self beneath all mental fluctuations and to stop identifying with restless thoughts.

avadhuta_gita::217.verse_sanskrit:
इह सारसमुच्चयसारमिति कथितं निजभावविभेद इति ।
विषये करणत्वमसत्यमिति किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::217.verse_hindi: यह आत्मा सार समुच्चय (सभी प्रकार के सारों का) का भी सार हैं। ऐसा कहा गया है। अपने भाव से भी इसका विभेद है (यह भाव रूप नहीं है), विषयों का करणत्व (कार्य) यही है ऐसा असत्य ही कहा गया है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण रूदन करता है। तू सर्व में सम है।
avadhuta_gita::217.english_translation: The self is said to be the essence of all essences. It is distinct from feelings and not the cause of objects. So why does your mind weep? You are equal in all.
avadhuta_gita::217.translation_literal: इह (here) सारसमुच्चय (essence-of-essences) सारमिति (is called essence) कथितं (said) निजभावविभेद (own-feeling-distinction) इति (thus) । विषये (in-objects) करणत्वम् (causality) असत्यमिति (is not true) किमु (then why) रोदिषि (you cry) मानसि (in the mind) सर्वसमम् (equal-in-all) ॥
avadhuta_gita::217.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::217.essence: You are the universal essence, not the cause or the feelings you experience.
avadhuta_gita::217.simple_meaning: You are the core essence behind all things, not the feelings you have or the cause of objects. So your mind’s sorrow is unnecessary because you are present equally everywhere.
avadhuta_gita::217.simple_insight: You can feel sorrow, yet your true self remains unchanged and equal in everything.
avadhuta_gita::217.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya clarifies that the true self is the ultimate essence behind all essences, distinct from emotions and not the cause behind worldly objects. The restless mind cries, but it overlooks the unchanging equality of the self in all.
avadhuta_gita::217.modern_relevance: When your emotions overwhelm you, remember you are more than your feelings or the things happening around you. Your true self remains steady and equal in all situations.
avadhuta_gita::217.insight: It teaches you to separate your true self from the mind’s emotional reactions and the mistaken belief that you cause everything.

avadhuta_gita::218.verse_sanskrit:
बहुधा श्रुतयः प्रवदन्ति यतो वियदादिरिदं मृगतोयसमम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वसमं किमु रोदिषि मानसि सर्वसमम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::218.verse_hindi: अनेक श्रुतियाँ कथन करती हैं कि जितना भी यह आकाशादि प्रपंच है वह मृगतृष्णा के जल के समान है। और यह एक चेतन ही नित्य एवं सर्व में सम है। फिर हे मन! तू किस कारण से रूदन करता है। तू वही आत्म है जो सभी में समान रूप से है।
avadhuta_gita::218.english_translation: Many scriptures say the cosmic play is like mirage water, but the one true self is constant and present in all; why then does your mind grieve?
avadhuta_gita::218.translation_literal: बहुधा (many) / श्रुतयः (scriptures) / प्रवदन्ति (say) / यतो (that) / वियदादि (the cosmic play) / इदम् (this) / मृगतोयसमम् (like mirage water) / यदि (if) / चैक (one) / निरन्तर (constant) / सर्वसमं (present in all) / किमु (then why) / रोदिषि (do you grieve) / मानसि (mind) / सर्वसमम् (present in all)
avadhuta_gita::218.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::218.essence: The true self is one and unchanging; the mind’s grief is needless illusion.
avadhuta_gita::218.simple_meaning: The world is often compared to a mirage, but your true self is constant and present everywhere. Your mind should not suffer grief.
avadhuta_gita::218.simple_insight: You can feel peace knowing your true self is unchanging and everywhere.
avadhuta_gita::218.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya contrasts the fleeting, illusory nature of the cosmic world with the eternal, unchanging true self present in all. Despite this, the restless mind grieves, unaware of its own true nature.
avadhuta_gita::218.modern_relevance: You struggle with sadness over events that seem real but are like illusions; knowing your true self is steady can ease that pain.
avadhuta_gita::218.insight: It teaches you to recognize the mind’s grief as misunderstanding your constant, universal true self.

avadhuta_gita::219.verse_sanskrit:
विन्दति विन्दति न हि न हि यत्र छन्दोलक्षणं न हि न हि तत्र ।
समरसमग्नो भावितपूतः प्रलपति तत्त्वं परमवधूतः ॥
avadhuta_gita::219.verse_hindi: परम अवधूत ( श्रेष्ठ ज्ञानी) जिसका अन्त:करण पवित्र है उस एकरस आत्मा में ही मग्न रहता है तथा उस आत्मतत्व का ही कथन करता है। जिसमें छन्द और लक्षण नहीं हैं उसी आत्मा को प्राप्त होता है।
avadhuta_gita::219.english_translation: The supreme Avadhuta, whose inner being is pure, remains absorbed in that unified true self and speaks only of that ultimate reality, which has no form or qualities.
avadhuta_gita::219.translation_literal: विन्दति (finds) / विन्दति (finds) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / यत्र (where) / छन्दोलक्षणं (form and qualities) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / तत्र (there) । / समरसमग्नो (completely absorbed in the unified) / भावितपूतः (pure in heart) / प्रलपति (speaks) / तत्त्वं (the truth) / परमवधूतः (the supreme Avadhuta) ॥
avadhuta_gita::219.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::219.essence: The supreme being is absorbed in the pure, formless true self and speaks only that truth.
avadhuta_gita::219.simple_meaning: The highest wise one, pure inside, remains fully absorbed in the formless true self and speaks only of that ultimate reality.
avadhuta_gita::219.simple_insight: You are deeply connected to a pure and formless essence beyond appearances.
avadhuta_gita::219.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the supreme Avadhuta as one whose heart is purified and who remains absorbed in the undivided true self, speaking only of that ultimate reality which has no attributes or form.
avadhuta_gita::219.modern_relevance: In moments of quiet, you find yourself connected to something pure and beyond all labels or roles you play.
avadhuta_gita::219.insight: It teaches you to rest in the pure essence within, beyond all forms and mental qualities.

avadhuta_gita::220.verse_sanskrit:
बहुधा श्रुतयः प्रवदन्ति वयं वियदादिरिदं मृगतोयसमम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवमुपमेयमथोह्युपमा च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::220.verse_hindi: अनेक श्रुतियाँ हमें कहती हैं कि यह आकाश आदि प्रपंच मृगतृष्णा के जल के समान है। यदि यह एक ही चेतन नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव स्वरूप है तो यह उपमेय और उपमा किस प्रकार हो सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::220.english_translation: Many scriptures say this world is like a mirage, yet if it is one eternal, all-pervading, auspicious consciousness, how can it be both the object and the comparison?
avadhuta_gita::220.translation_literal: बहुधा (many) श्रुतयः (scriptures) प्रवदन्ति (say) वयं (we) वियदादि (sky and so on) इदं (this) मृगतोयसमम् (like mirage water) । यदि (if) चैक (one) निरन्तर (eternal) सर्वशिवम् (all-auspicious) उपमेयम् (object of comparison) अथ (then) ओह्युपमा (mirage comparison) च (and) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::220.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::220.essence: One eternal reality cannot simultaneously be an illusory object and its own comparison.
avadhuta_gita::220.simple_meaning: If the entire world is one eternal, all-good consciousness, it cannot also be an illusion or separate object.
avadhuta_gita::220.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing reality is not fragmented or deceptive but wholly unified.
avadhuta_gita::220.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya challenges the common teaching that the world is a mere illusion like a mirage. He questions how the same reality can be both the eternal true consciousness and also an illusory object of comparison.
avadhuta_gita::220.modern_relevance: You’ve heard people call life an illusion, but deep down you sense reality is more unified than that.
avadhuta_gita::220.insight: It shifts your view from seeing the world as fragmented to recognizing one unchanging reality beyond all appearances.

avadhuta_gita::221.verse_sanskrit:
अविभक्तिविभक्तिविहीनपरं ननु कार्यविकार्यविहीनपरम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं यजनं च कथं तपनं च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::221.verse_hindi: यह चेतन तत्व अविभक्ति एवं विभक्ति से रहित परम तत्व है, निश्चय ही यह कार्य विकार्य से भी रहित है। यदि यह एक ही नित्य, सर्व रूप एवं शिव है तो फिर यजन और तप कैसे हो सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::221.english_translation: The conscious principle is without division or separation, beyond all change or effect; if it is one, eternal, and all-blissful, then how could worship or austerity apply to it?
avadhuta_gita::221.translation_literal: अविभक्तिविभक्तिविहीनपरं (without division or separation, supreme) ननु (indeed) कार्यविकार्यविहीनपरम् (free from action and effect, supreme) । यदि (if) चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं (one, continuous, all-blissful) यजनं (worship) च (and) कथं (how) तपनं (austerity) च (and) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::221.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::221.essence: The true self is always whole and unaffected by any practice or change.
avadhuta_gita::221.simple_meaning: The true self is beyond division, change, or action; since it is always whole and blissful, practices like worship and austerity do not apply to it.
avadhuta_gita::221.simple_insight: You can rest knowing your true self is already complete and untouched by effort.
avadhuta_gita::221.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the true self is indivisible and beyond cause and effect. If it is eternally one and entirely blissful, then practices like worship or austerity are irrelevant to it.
avadhuta_gita::221.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed trying to fix yourself with constant effort or rituals, but your core being is already whole and unchanged beneath it all.
avadhuta_gita::221.insight: It shifts your mind from trying to change your essence to recognizing the unchanging nature beneath all effort.

avadhuta_gita::222.verse_sanskrit:
मन एव निरन्तरसर्वगतं ह्यविशालविशालविहीनपरम् ।
मन एव निरन्तरसर्वशिवं मनसापि कथं वचसा च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::222.verse_hindi: मन ही निरन्तर एवं सर्वगत है, निश्चय ही यह अविशाल और विशाल से रहित है, मन ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिवरूप, है। इसलिये उस आत्मा को मन और वाणी से कैसे जाना जाये।
avadhuta_gita::222.english_translation: The mind alone is continuously all-pervading, beyond vastness and limitation; it is eternal, all, and the embodiment of the supreme reality. Therefore, how can that true self be known by mind or speech?
avadhuta_gita::222.translation_literal: मन (mind) एव (alone) निरन्तर (continuously) सर्वगतं (all-pervading) हि (indeed) अविशाल (without vastness) विशाल (vast) विहीन (without) परम (supreme) । मन (mind) एव (alone) निरन्तर (eternal) सर्व (all) शिवं (supreme reality) मनसा (by mind) अपि (also) कथं (how) वचसा (by speech) च (and) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::222.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::222.essence: The mind is vast yet cannot know the true self beyond mind and words.
avadhuta_gita::222.simple_meaning: The mind is always present everywhere but is not capable of fully knowing the true self, which is beyond mind and words.
avadhuta_gita::222.simple_insight: There’s freedom in knowing the mind’s limits—it can’t contain your true self.
avadhuta_gita::222.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the mind pervades all but is paradoxically beyond size or limitation. The true self is eternal and embodies the supreme reality. Because the true self transcends mind and speech, it cannot be fully known through them.
avadhuta_gita::222.modern_relevance: You struggle to understand yourself through thoughts or words, but this shows why that effort can never fully succeed.
avadhuta_gita::222.insight: It teaches you to stop relying on mind or language to capture your true self and open to direct experience instead.

avadhuta_gita::223.verse_sanskrit:
दिनरात्रिविभेदनिराकरणमुदितानुदितस्य निराकरणम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं रविचन्द्रमसौ ज्वलनश्च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::223.verse_hindi: दिन और रात्रि का भेद भी उसमें नहीं है। उदय और अस्त का भेद भी उसमें नहीं है। यदि वह एक ही नित्य और सर्वरूप शिव है तो फिर सूर्य, चन्द्रमा और अग्नि उसमें कैसे हो सकती है।
avadhuta_gita::223.english_translation: There is no distinction of day and night in that. No difference between rising and setting. If it is one eternal and all-pervading true self, then how can sun, moon, and fire exist within it?
avadhuta_gita::223.translation_literal: दिनरात्रिविभेदनिराकरणम् (day-night distinction not) / उदितानुदितस्य (rising-setting's) / निराकरणम् (negation) / यदि (if) / चैक (one) / निरन्तर (eternal) / सर्वशिवं (all-pervading true self) / रवि (sun) / चन्द्रमसः (moon) / औ (and) / ज्वलनः (fire) / च (also) / कथम् (how)
avadhuta_gita::223.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::223.essence: The true self is beyond all dualities and natural cycles of change.
avadhuta_gita::223.simple_meaning: The true self is timeless and unchanging, beyond all dualities like day and night or rising and setting.
avadhuta_gita::223.simple_insight: You feel the relief of realizing your true self is untouched by all passing changes.
avadhuta_gita::223.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the true self transcends all opposites such as day and night or sunrise and sunset. If the true self is eternal and all-pervading, then natural phenomena like sun and moon cannot limit or define it.
avadhuta_gita::223.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by constant change and cycles, remember your core remains untouched by time or events.
avadhuta_gita::223.insight: It shifts your perspective from identifying with changing appearances to recognizing your timeless essence.

avadhuta_gita::224.verse_sanskrit:
गतकामविकामविभेद इति गतचेष्टविचेष्टविभेद इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं बहिरन्तरभिन्नमतिश्च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::224.verse_hindi: काम एवं विकाम का भेद उसमें नहीं है, चेष्टा और विचेष्टा का भेद भी उसमें नहीं है। यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्वरूप एवं शिव है तो फिर वह बाहर और भीतर भिन्न है ऐसी बुद्धि कैसे हो सकती है।
avadhuta_gita::224.english_translation: There is no difference in desire or its absence, no difference in action or inaction; if the true self is one, eternal, and blissful, how can the mind perceive a difference between inside and outside?
avadhuta_gita::224.translation_literal: गतकामविकामविभेद (difference of past-desire and absence of desire) / इति (thus) / गतचेष्टविचेष्टविभेद (difference of past-action and inaction) / इति (thus) / यदि (if) / ऐक (one) / निरन्तर (continuous) / सर्वशिवं (all-blissful) / बहिरन्तरभिन्नमतिश्च (outside-inside different mind also) / कथम् (how)
avadhuta_gita::224.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::224.essence: Your true self is beyond all differences like desire, action, inside, and outside.
avadhuta_gita::224.simple_meaning: Desire and its absence, action and inaction, are not different for the true self, which is always whole and blissful; so the mind's idea of inside versus outside is mistaken.
avadhuta_gita::224.simple_insight: You can feel the freedom of being whole, undivided by desires or actions.
avadhuta_gita::224.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that the true self is beyond all distinctions like desire or action. When you realize your true self is one and blissful, the usual mental separations of inside and outside lose their meaning.
avadhuta_gita::224.modern_relevance: When you notice your thoughts and urges rise and fall, you sense how they don’t truly define who you are inside.
avadhuta_gita::224.insight: It teaches you to stop dividing experience into inner and outer; all is one in your true self.

avadhuta_gita::225.verse_sanskrit:
यदि सारविसारविहीन इति यदि शून्यविशून्यविहीन इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं प्रथमं च कथं चरमं च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::225.verse_hindi: यदि वह ब्रह्म सार एवं असार से रहित है, यदि वह शून्य और अशून्य से भी रहित है ऐसा कहा जाता है। यदि वह नित्य, सर्वरूप एवं शिव है तो फिर उसे आदि व अन्त वाला कैसे कहा जा सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::225.english_translation: If the supreme reality is beyond existence and non-existence, beyond emptiness and fullness, and is eternal, all-pervading, and auspicious, then how can it be called the beginning or the end?
avadhuta_gita::225.translation_literal: यदि (if) सारविसारविहीन (essence and non-essence without) इति (thus) यदि (if) शून्यविशून्यविहीन (empty and non-empty without) इति (thus) । यदि (if) चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं (one, eternal, all, auspicious) प्रथमं (first) च (and) कथं (how) चरमं (last) च (and) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::225.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::225.essence: The true self beyond all dualities has no beginning and no end.
avadhuta_gita::225.simple_meaning: The supreme reality is beyond all dualities like existence and non-existence, so it cannot be called having a beginning or an end.
avadhuta_gita::225.simple_insight: You feel the vastness of what cannot be limited by time or categories.
avadhuta_gita::225.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya questions how the supreme reality, which is beyond all opposites and is eternal and all-pervading, can be defined as having a start or an end. This challenges our usual way of seeing beginnings and endings.
avadhuta_gita::225.modern_relevance: When you think about your own nature beyond labels, you realize it doesn't fit into any timeline or category.
avadhuta_gita::225.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing things as limited by time to recognizing the boundless nature of the true self.

avadhuta_gita::226.verse_sanskrit:
यदिभेदविभेदनिराकरणं यदि वेदकवेद्यनिराकरणम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं तृतीयं च कथं तुरीयं च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::226.verse_hindi: यदि वह ब्रह्म भेद और विभेद से रहित है यदि उसमें ज्ञाता और ज्ञेय का भेद नहीं हैं, यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्वरूप एवं शिव है तो फिर उसमें तृतीय अवस्था (सुषुप्ति) एवं तुरीय अवस्था का भेद कैसे हो सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::226.english_translation: If the supreme reality is free from difference and division, beyond knower and known, and is one eternal, all-pervading, and auspicious essence, then how can there be a distinction between the third (deep sleep) and the fourth (transcendent) states?
avadhuta_gita::226.translation_literal: यदि (if) वह (that) ब्रह्म (supreme reality) भेद (difference) और (and) विभेदनिराकरणं (without division) यदि (if) वेदक (knower) वेद्य (known) निराकरणम् (without distinction) यदि (if) च (and) एक (one) निरन्तर (continuous) सर्वशिवं (all-auspicious) तृतीयं (third) च (and) कथं (how) तुरीयं (fourth) च (and) कथम् (how)
avadhuta_gita::226.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::226.essence: True reality has no divisions; states of consciousness are illusions of separation.
avadhuta_gita::226.simple_meaning: If the supreme reality is truly one and beyond all distinctions, then the usual separations between states of consciousness don't actually exist.
avadhuta_gita::226.simple_insight: You feel the unity beneath all apparent separations, freeing you from confusion.
avadhuta_gita::226.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya questions how the supreme reality, which is beyond all dualities like knower and known, can be divided into different states such as deep sleep and the transcendent state, highlighting the non-dual nature of ultimate reality.
avadhuta_gita::226.modern_relevance: When your mind tries to separate your experiences into strict categories, this reminds you that deeper reality is whole and indivisible.
avadhuta_gita::226.insight: It teaches you to stop seeing your experiences as fundamentally separate and instead recognize their underlying unity.

avadhuta_gita::227.verse_sanskrit:
गदिताविदितं न हि सत्यमिति विदिताविदितं नहि सत्यमिति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं विषयेन्द्रियबुद्धिमनांसि कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::227.verse_hindi: ब्रह्म के बारे में जो कहा गया है और जो नहीं कहा गया है दोनों सत्य नहीं हैं। जो विदित है और अविदित है दोनों सत्य नहीं है। यदि वह चेतन नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव रूप एक ही है तो ये विषय, इन्द्रियाँ, बुद्धि और मन कैसे हो सकते हैं।
avadhuta_gita::227.english_translation: What is spoken and unspoken about the supreme reality are both not true; if the supreme is conscious, eternal, all, and benevolent, how can there be senses, intellect, and mind?
avadhuta_gita::227.translation_literal: गदिताविदितं (spoken and known) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / सत्यमिति (truth) / विदिताविदितं (known and unknown) / नहि (not) / सत्यमिति (truth) / यदि (if) / च (also) / एक (one) / निरन्तर (continuous) / सर्वशिवं (all-benevolent) / विषयेन्द्रियबुद्धिमनांसि (objects, senses, intellect, mind) / कथम् (how)
avadhuta_gita::227.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::227.essence: Truth about the supreme is beyond everything said or unsaid and cannot coexist with separate faculties.
avadhuta_gita::227.simple_meaning: Neither what is said nor what is unsaid about the supreme reality fully captures the truth. If the supreme is one, eternal, conscious, and benevolent, then how can separate senses, mind, and intellect exist?
avadhuta_gita::227.simple_insight: You feel the limits of words and concepts when facing the deepest truth.
avadhuta_gita::227.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya challenges the idea that spoken or unspoken descriptions can capture the supreme reality. If the supreme is eternally conscious and all-encompassing, the separate faculties like senses and mind must be illusory or secondary. This verse invites questioning how duality arises if oneness is true.
avadhuta_gita::227.modern_relevance: When you try to explain your deepest experience, words fall short and feel disconnected from what you truly know inside.
avadhuta_gita::227.insight: It shifts your mind from relying on conceptual knowledge to embracing the mystery beyond all categories.

avadhuta_gita::228.verse_sanskrit:
गगनं पवनो न हि सत्यमिति धरणी दहनो न हि सत्यमिति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं जलदश्च कथं सलिलं च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::228.verse_hindi: आकाश और वायु सत्य नहीं है, पृथ्वी और अग्नि भी सत्य नहीं हैं। यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो यह बादल और जल किस प्रकार सत्य हो सकते हैं।
avadhuta_gita::228.english_translation: The sky and wind are not the true self, nor are earth and fire; if the one eternal supreme reality is all, how can clouds and water be true?
avadhuta_gita::228.translation_literal: गगनं (sky) / पवनो (wind) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / सत्यमिति (true-is) / धरणी (earth) / दहनो (fire) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / सत्यमिति (true-is) / । / यदि (if) / चैक (one) / निरन्तर (eternal) / सर्व (all) / शिवं (auspicious/supreme reality) / जलदश्च (clouds and) / कथं (how) / सलिलं (water) / च (also) / कथम् (how) / ॥
avadhuta_gita::228.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::228.essence: Only the one eternal reality is truly real; all else is impermanent.
avadhuta_gita::228.simple_meaning: Everything that changes like sky, wind, earth, fire, clouds, and water is not the true self; only the one eternal supreme reality is real.
avadhuta_gita::228.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing that what constantly changes is not your true self.
avadhuta_gita::228.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that commonly perceived elements—sky, wind, earth, fire, clouds, and water—are not the true self because they change. Only the single eternal supreme reality is truly real, challenging assumptions about the world’s permanence.
avadhuta_gita::228.modern_relevance: You watch the weather shift outside your window, realizing that nothing permanent appears in the changing sky or wind, just like your thoughts and feelings.
avadhuta_gita::228.insight: This verse shifts your view from identifying with ever-changing things to recognizing the unchanging reality behind them.

avadhuta_gita::229.verse_sanskrit:
यदि कल्पितलोकनिराकरणं यदि कल्पितदेवनिराकरणम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं गुणदोषविचारमतिश्च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::229.verse_hindi: शास्त्रों में इसका निराकरण किया गया है कि ये सभी लोक कल्पित हैं, ये सभी देवता कल्पित हैं। केवल एक ब्रह्म ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर गुण दोष विचार वाली बुद्धि कैसे सत्य हो सकती है।
avadhuta_gita::229.english_translation: The scriptures reject the world and gods as imagined; only the supreme reality is eternal, universal, and auspicious—so how can the mind that judges qualities and faults be true?
avadhuta_gita::229.translation_literal: यदि (if) कल्पितलोकनिराकरणं (rejection of imagined worlds) यदि (if) कल्पितदेवनिराकरणम् (rejection of imagined gods) यदि (if) च (and) एैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं (only one eternal universal auspicious) गुणदोषविचारमतिश्च (mind judging qualities and faults) कथम् (how)
avadhuta_gita::229.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::229.essence: The ultimate reality is beyond all mental judgments of qualities and faults.
avadhuta_gita::229.simple_meaning: Only the supreme reality is truly real and eternal; the world, gods, and the mind that judges qualities are all imagined and not ultimately true.
avadhuta_gita::229.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing your judgments about good and bad don’t define the ultimate reality.
avadhuta_gita::229.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya challenges the trust in worldly appearances and gods, emphasizing that only the supreme, eternal reality exists. The mind’s evaluations of qualities and faults are unreliable illusions in this ultimate truth.
avadhuta_gita::229.modern_relevance: When your mind categorizes people or situations as good or bad, remember this division is a mental construct, not the whole truth.
avadhuta_gita::229.insight: Stop trusting your mind’s constant judgment as a reflection of true reality; it shifts your perspective beyond duality.

avadhuta_gita::230.verse_sanskrit:
मरणामरणं हि निराकरणं करणाकरणं हि निराकरणम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं गमनागमनं हि कथं वदति ॥
avadhuta_gita::230.verse_hindi: वेद ग्रन्थों में जन्म एवं मृत्यु का निराकरण किया गया है, कर्तव्य एवं अकर्तव्य का भी निराकरण किया गया है। यदि वह ब्रह्म एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर गमन आगमन किस प्रकार कहा जा सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::230.english_translation: The Vedas negate birth and death, action and inaction; if the supreme is one, eternal, and all-good, how can movement and change be spoken of?
avadhuta_gita::230.translation_literal: मरण (death) / अमरणं (undying) / हि (indeed) / निराकरणं (negation) / करणाकरणं (action and inaction) / हि (indeed) / निराकरणम् (negation) / यदि (if) / चैक (one) / निरन्तर (eternal) / सर्वशिवं (all-good) / गमनागमनं (coming and going) / हि (indeed) / कथं (how) / वदति (can it be said)
avadhuta_gita::230.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::230.essence: The supreme reality is beyond birth, death, and any change, so movement is an illusion.
avadhuta_gita::230.simple_meaning: Birth, death, doing, and not doing are negated by the supreme reality, which is one and eternal. Movement and change cannot truly happen to it.
avadhuta_gita::230.simple_insight: You can feel secure knowing the deepest reality is beyond all change and cycles of life and death.
avadhuta_gita::230.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that according to the highest teachings, birth and death, action and inaction, do not affect the supreme reality. Since it is one, eternal, and wholly benevolent, the usual ideas of coming and going do not apply to it.
avadhuta_gita::230.modern_relevance: When life's ups and downs feel overwhelming, remember the deepest part of you is beyond all change and cycles of loss and gain.
avadhuta_gita::230.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as caught in change to recognizing your unchanging essence beyond all movement.

avadhuta_gita::231.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकृतिः पुरुषो न हि भेद इति न हि कारणकार्यविभेद इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं पुरुषापुरुषं च कथं वदति ॥
avadhuta_gita::231.verse_hindi: इसमें प्रकृति और पुरुष का भेद नहीं हैं, न ही कारण एवं कार्य का विभेद ही है। यदि सर्वत्र एक ही नित्य सर्वरूप एवं शिव आत्मा ही है तो फिर पुरुष और अपुरुष (प्रकृति) किस प्रकार कहा जाता हैं।
avadhuta_gita::231.english_translation: There is no difference between the natural world and pure awareness, nor between cause and effect. If everything is eternally one and wholly auspicious, how can we speak of awareness and the non-awareness as separate?
avadhuta_gita::231.translation_literal: प्रकृतिः (natural world) / पुरुषः (pure awareness) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / भेद (difference) / इति (thus) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / कारण (cause) / कार्य (effect) / विभेद (difference) / इति (thus) / । (punctuation) / यदि (if) / च (also) / एक (one) / निरन्तर (continuous) / सर्व (all) / शिवं (auspicious) / पुरुष (pure awareness) / अपुरुषं (non-awareness) / च (and) / कथं (how) / वदति (speaks) / ॥ (punctuation)
avadhuta_gita::231.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::231.essence: All appearances of duality between awareness and nature are ultimately false.
avadhuta_gita::231.simple_meaning: There is no real difference between pure awareness and the natural world, or between cause and effect. Everything is eternally one and auspicious.
avadhuta_gita::231.simple_insight: You can feel the relief of knowing all separation is only appearance, not reality.
avadhuta_gita::231.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals a radical teaching: the usual distinctions—between pure awareness and the natural world, or between cause and effect—do not truly exist. Everything is one eternal, auspicious reality, challenging how we normally perceive separation.
avadhuta_gita::231.modern_relevance: You catch yourself dividing experience into self and other, cause and result, only to see how everything flows as one seamless reality beneath.
avadhuta_gita::231.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing separate things to recognizing underlying unity in all experience.

avadhuta_gita::232.verse_sanskrit:
तृतीयं न हि दुःखसमागमनं न गुणाद्द्वितीयस्य समागमनम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं स्थविरश्च युवा च शिशुश्च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::232.verse_hindi: ब्रह्म में तीन प्रकार के दु:खों का समागम नहीं है, न ही दोनों गुणों का समागम है। यदि सर्वत्र एक ही नित्य शिव रूप ब्रह्म है तो फिर बुढ़ापा, युवावस्था एवं शिशु अवस्था किस प्रकार कही जा सकती है।
avadhuta_gita::232.english_translation: In the supreme reality, there is no coming together of three types of suffering, nor the union of two qualities. If the supreme reality is eternally one and unchanging, then how can old age, youth, and childhood be said to exist?
avadhuta_gita::232.translation_literal: तृतीयं (third) न (not) हि (indeed) दुःखसमागमनं (meeting/union of suffering) न (nor) गुणाद्द्वितीयस्य (of the second quality) समागमनम् (union) । यदि (if) चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं (one continuous all-auspicious) स्थविरश्च (old) युवा (young) च (and) शिशुश्च (child) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::232.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::232.essence: The true self is timeless and beyond all changes like age or suffering.
avadhuta_gita::232.simple_meaning: The true self is one and unchanging, so suffering and different life stages like youth or old age do not truly belong to it.
avadhuta_gita::232.simple_insight: You can feel free from limits of age and suffering because your true self is beyond them.
avadhuta_gita::232.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that in the supreme reality—pure and eternal—there is no mixing of suffering or qualities like age. If the true self is always the same, then the changes we see in life are not real in that ultimate sense.
avadhuta_gita::232.modern_relevance: When you worry about growing older or facing hardship, this verse reminds you that your essence is untouched by time or pain.
avadhuta_gita::232.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing life stages to recognizing your unchanging true self.

avadhuta_gita::233.verse_sanskrit:
ननु आश्रमवर्णविहीनपरं ननु कारणकर्तृविहीनपरम् ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवमविनष्टविनष्टमतिश्च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::233.verse_hindi: निश्चय ही आत्मा आश्रम और वर्ण से रहित श्रेष्ठ हैं, निश्चय ही यह कारण एवं कार्य से रहित श्रेष्ठ है। यदि यह एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो इसमें नाश होने वाली एवं नाश रहित बुद्धि कैसे हो सकती है।
avadhuta_gita::233.english_translation: The true self is indeed beyond ashramas and social classes, beyond cause and effect. If it is the one eternal, all-pervading, and auspicious reality, how can it have a nature that is both perishable and imperishable?
avadhuta_gita::233.translation_literal: ननु (surely) आश्रमवर्णविहीनपरं (beyond ashramas and social classes, supreme) ननु (surely) कारणकर्तृविहीनपरम् (beyond cause and doer, supreme) । यदि (if) चैक (one) निरन्तर (continuous) सर्वशिवम् (all-auspicious) अविनष्टविनष्टमतिः (perishable and imperishable nature) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::233.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::233.essence: Your true self transcends all social divisions, causes, and contradictory natures.
avadhuta_gita::233.simple_meaning: Your true self is beyond social roles, causes, and effects. It is one eternal reality that cannot be both destructible and indestructible.
avadhuta_gita::233.simple_insight: There's freedom in seeing yourself as beyond all labels and change—not caught between opposites.
avadhuta_gita::233.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that the true self is beyond social systems like ashramas and varnas, and beyond cause and doer. If this self is truly one eternal, all-pervading reality, it cannot have conflicting qualities like being both perishable and imperishable.
avadhuta_gita::233.modern_relevance: You may feel trapped by roles, causes, or outcomes—this reminds you that your true self is beyond all these shifting conditions.
avadhuta_gita::233.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing roles and causes to recognizing your unchanging essence beyond opposites.

avadhuta_gita::234.verse_sanskrit:
ग्रसिताग्रसितं च वितथ्यमिति जनिताजनितं च वितथ्यमिति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवमविनाशि विनाशि कथं हि भवेत् ॥
avadhuta_gita::234.verse_hindi: ग्रसने वाला और ग्रसित दोनों ही मिथ्या हैं। उत्पन्न करने वाला और उत्पन्न हुआ दोनों ही मिथ्या हैं। यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर वह अविनाशी एवं नाश होने वाला कैसे हो सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::234.english_translation: The devourer and the devoured are both false. The creator and the created are both false. If the one is eternal, all, and auspicious, how can it be both destructible and indestructible?
