avadhuta_gita::234.translation_literal: ग्रसिताग्रसितं (devourer-devoured) / च (and) / वितथ्यमिति (falsehood-is) / जनिताजनितं (creator-created) / च (and) / वितथ्यमिति (falsehood-is) / यदि (if) / च (also) / एकनिरन्तर (one-eternal) / सर्वशिवम् (all-auspicious-being) / अविनाशि (indestructible) / विनाशि (destructible) / कथं (how) / हि (indeed) / भवेत् (can be)
avadhuta_gita::234.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::234.essence: The eternal self transcends all dualities of creator and creation, devourer and devoured.
avadhuta_gita::234.simple_meaning: Both the roles of eater and eaten, and creator and created, are illusions. The one true self is eternal and cannot be both destructible and indestructible.
avadhuta_gita::234.simple_insight: You are free from all opposing roles, resting as the eternal reality beyond all illusions.
avadhuta_gita::234.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the dualities of devourer/devoured and creator/created are false appearances. If the true self is one, eternal, and auspicious, it cannot be both destructible and indestructible. This rejects all dualistic notions of separate entities.
avadhuta_gita::234.modern_relevance: When you feel torn between roles—maker and made, winner and loser—remember your true nature is beyond these opposites.
avadhuta_gita::234.insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with changing roles to recognizing the unchanging eternal self beyond all dualities.

avadhuta_gita::235.verse_sanskrit:
पुरुषापुरुषस्य विनष्टमिति वनितावनितस्य विनष्टमिति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवमविनोदविनोदमतिश्च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::235.verse_hindi: आत्मा में पुरुष एवं अपुरुष का भाव नहीं हैं, उस में स्त्री एवं अस्त्री का भाव भी नहीं हैं। यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर उसमें अविनोद और विनोद की बुद्धि किस प्रकार हो सकती है।
avadhuta_gita::235.english_translation: The true self contains no sense of person or non-person, no sense of woman or non-woman; if it is the one eternal, all-pervading, and auspicious reality, how can the mind of pleasure and displeasure arise in it?
avadhuta_gita::235.translation_literal: पुरुष (person) / अपुरुषस्य (non-person's) / विनष्टमिति (nonexistent) / वनितावनितस्य (woman and non-woman's) / विनष्टमिति (nonexistent) / यदि (if) / चैक (one) / निरन्तर (eternal) / सर्वशिव (all-auspicious) / अविनोद (without displeasure) / विनोद (pleasure) / मति (mind/thought) / इति (thus) / कथम् (how)
avadhuta_gita::235.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::235.essence: Your true self is beyond all opposites, untouched by pleasure or pain.
avadhuta_gita::235.simple_meaning: The true self is beyond all distinctions of person, gender, or emotions like pleasure and pain. It is one eternal reality without duality.
avadhuta_gita::235.simple_insight: You can rest knowing your deepest self is free from all conflicting feelings and identities.
avadhuta_gita::235.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the true self transcends all categories like personhood and gender. Because it is the one eternal and all-good reality, it cannot hold the mind's fluctuations between pleasure and displeasure.
avadhuta_gita::235.modern_relevance: When your mood swings between joy and frustration, this reminds you that your core being remains steady beyond those changes.
avadhuta_gita::235.insight: It teaches you to see beyond shifting identities and emotions to the unchanging reality within.

avadhuta_gita::236.verse_sanskrit:
यदि मोहविषादविहीनपरो यदि संशयशोकविहीनपरः ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवमहमत्र ममेति कथं च पुनः ॥
avadhuta_gita::236.verse_hindi: जब वह आत्मा मोह एवं विषाद से रहित इनसे परे है, यदि वह संशय और शोक से रहित और इनसे परे है, यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर ‘मैं’ और ‘मेरा’ इस प्रकार का कथन कैसे हो सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::236.english_translation: If the true self is beyond attachment and despair, beyond doubt and sorrow, if it is one, eternal, all, and auspicious, then how can 'I' and 'mine' arise here again?
avadhuta_gita::236.translation_literal: यदि (if) मोह (attachment) विषाद (despair) विहीन (without) परः (beyond) यदि (if) संशय (doubt) शोक (sorrow) विहीन (without) परः (beyond) यदि (if) च (and) एक (one) निरन्तर (constant) सर्व (all) शिव (auspicious) अहम् (I) अत्र (here) मम (mine) एति (is said) कथं (how) च (also) पुनः (again)
avadhuta_gita::236.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::236.essence: 'I' and 'mine' cannot belong to the true self that is beyond all attachment and sorrow.
avadhuta_gita::236.simple_meaning: Your true self is beyond attachment, sorrow, doubt, and separation; it is one and eternal, so ideas of 'I' and 'mine' cannot apply.
avadhuta_gita::236.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing your core is untouched by personal claims or doubts.
avadhuta_gita::236.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that the true self is beyond all emotional disturbances like attachment, despair, doubt, and sorrow. Since it is constant, all-encompassing, and auspicious, the personal labels 'I' and 'mine' do not truly belong to it. This challenges the usual sense of separateness.
avadhuta_gita::236.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by doubt or sorrow, remember your deepest self remains untouched and beyond such feelings.
avadhuta_gita::236.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing emotions to recognizing your unchanging true self beyond personal claims.

avadhuta_gita::237.verse_sanskrit:
महमेति ननु धर्मविधर्मविनाश इति ननु बन्धविबन्धविनाश इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवंमिहदुःखविदुःखमतिश्च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::237.verse_hindi: निश्चय ही आत्मा धर्म एवं विधर्म से रहित है। निश्चय ही वह बन्ध और मुक्ति से भी रहित है। यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर उसमें सुख एवं दु:ख की बुद्धि किस प्रकार हो सकती है।
avadhuta_gita::237.english_translation: The true self is certainly free from right and wrong, free from bondage and liberation; if it is one, eternal, all, and auspicious, how can it have the mind of pleasure and pain?
avadhuta_gita::237.translation_literal: महमेति (certainly the self) / ननु (is not) / धर्मविधर्मविनाश (destruction of right and wrong) / इति (thus) / ननु (not) / बन्धविबन्धविनाश (destruction of bondage and liberation) / इति (thus) / यदि (if) / चैक (one) / निरन्तर (eternal) / सर्वशिवं (all and auspicious) / मिह (here) / दुःखविदुःखमतिश्च (mind of pleasure and pain) / कथम् (how)
avadhuta_gita::237.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::237.essence: The true self transcends all pairs of opposites including pleasure and pain.
avadhuta_gita::237.simple_meaning: The true self is beyond concepts like right and wrong, bondage and freedom, pleasure and pain. It is unchanging, all-encompassing, and auspicious.
avadhuta_gita::237.simple_insight: Knowing your true self is free from all conflict brings deep inner peace.
avadhuta_gita::237.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the true self is untouched by moral dualities or conditions like bondage or liberation. If it is truly one, eternal, and auspicious, it cannot experience pleasure or pain, highlighting its transcendence.
avadhuta_gita::237.modern_relevance: When you face conflicting feelings or moral dilemmas, remember your deeper self remains untouched and peaceful beyond them.
avadhuta_gita::237.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with changing feelings to recognizing your unchanging true self beyond them.

avadhuta_gita::238.verse_sanskrit:
न हि याज्ञिकयज्ञविभाग इति न हुताशनवस्तुविभाग इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं वद कर्मफलानि भवन्ति कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::238.verse_hindi: आत्मा में याज्ञिक और यज्ञ का विभाग नहीं है, न हवन सामग्री एवं अग्नि का विभाग ही है। यदि वह एक ही निरन्तर, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर कहो उसमें कर्मों का फल किस प्रकार होता है।
avadhuta_gita::238.english_translation: The true self has no division of priest or ritual, no separate fire or offerings; if it is one, continuous, all-pervading, and auspicious, then how can actions bear fruit in it?
avadhuta_gita::238.translation_literal: न (not) / हि (indeed) / याज्ञिकयज्ञविभाग (priest and ritual division) / इति (thus) / न (not) / हुताशनवस्तुविभाग (fire and offering division) / इति (thus) / यदि (if) / च (also) / एकनिरन्तर (one continuous) / सर्वशिवं (all auspicious) / वद (say) / कर्मफलानि (fruits of actions) / भवन्ति (are) / कथम् (how)
avadhuta_gita::238.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::238.essence: The true self is one and undivided; it cannot be affected by action’s results.
avadhuta_gita::238.simple_meaning: The true self is undivided and beyond ritual roles or objects. If it is always one and auspicious, then actions cannot produce results in it.
avadhuta_gita::238.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing your true nature isn’t affected by what you do or what happens.
avadhuta_gita::238.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya challenges the idea that the true self is split by priests, rituals, or offerings. He points out that since the self is one, continuous, and completely auspicious, it cannot be subject to the fruits of any action. This questions the basis of karma and ritual division.
avadhuta_gita::238.modern_relevance: You might feel pressured to fit roles or outcomes at work, but your core self remains untouched by those divisions or results.
avadhuta_gita::238.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as fragmented by roles and actions to recognizing your unchanging unity beyond them.

avadhuta_gita::239.verse_sanskrit:
ननु शोकविशोकविमुक्त इति ननु दर्पविदर्पविमुक्त इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं ननु रागविरागमतिश्च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::239.verse_hindi: निश्चय ही आत्मा शोक-विशोक से मुक्त है, निश्चय ही वह अहंकार एवं निरहंकार से भी मुक्त है। यदि वह एक ही नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर उसमें राग एवं विराग की बुद्धि किस प्रकार हो सकती है।
avadhuta_gita::239.english_translation: The true self is certainly free from sorrow and joy, and also free from pride and humility; if it is one, eternal, all-pervading, and auspicious, then how can it have the intellect of attachment and detachment?
avadhuta_gita::239.translation_literal: ननु (surely) शोकविशोकविमुक्त (free from sorrow and joy) इति (thus) ननु (surely) दर्पविदर्पविमुक्त (free from pride and humility) इति (thus) । यदि (if) च (also) एकनिरन्तर (one and eternal) सर्वशिवं (all and auspicious) ननु (surely) रागविरागमतिश्च (attachment and detachment intellect) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::239.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::239.essence: The true self is beyond all pairs of opposites like sorrow and joy or attachment and detachment.
avadhuta_gita::239.simple_meaning: You are naturally free from sorrow, pride, attachment, and detachment because your true self is one, eternal, and complete.
avadhuta_gita::239.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your true self never experiences conflicting emotions or ego states.
avadhuta_gita::239.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the true self is untouched by sorrow, joy, pride, or humility. Since it is one, eternal, and all-pervading, it cannot hold any dualities like attachment or aversion in its intellect.
avadhuta_gita::239.modern_relevance: When your mood swings between pride and shame or attachment and rejection, remember your true self remains untouched and whole beyond these feelings.
avadhuta_gita::239.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing yourself as caught in emotional ups and downs to recognizing your constant, unchanging nature.

avadhuta_gita::240.verse_sanskrit:
न हि मोहविमोहविकार इति न हि लोभविलोभविकार इति ।
यदि चैकनिरन्तरसर्वशिवं ह्यविवेकविवेकमतिश्च कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::240.verse_hindi: आत्मा में मोह विमोह का विकार नहीं हैं, न ही लोभ और अलोभ का विकार ही है। यदि यह आत्मा एक ही, नित्य, सर्व एवं शिव है तो फिर उसमें अविवेक और विवेक बुद्धि किस प्रकार हो सकती है।
avadhuta_gita::240.english_translation: The true self has no defects of attachment or detachment, no faults of greed or lack of greed; if the self is one, eternal, all-pervading, and benevolent, how can it possess ignorance or wisdom?
avadhuta_gita::240.translation_literal: न (no) हि (indeed) मोहविमोहविकार (attachment-detachment defects) इति (thus) न (no) हि (indeed) लोभविलोभविकार (greed-nongreed defects) इति (thus) । यदि (if) च (also) एक (one) निरन्तर (continuous) सर्व (all) शिवं (benevolent) हि (indeed) अविवेकविवेकमतिश्च (ignorance-wisdom mind) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::240.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::240.essence: The true self is beyond all dualities like attachment, greed, ignorance, and wisdom.
avadhuta_gita::240.simple_meaning: The true self is free from any faults like attachment, greed, or their opposites. Being eternal and all-pervading, it cannot have ignorance or wisdom as qualities.
avadhuta_gita::240.simple_insight: Feel the relief that your true self is pure and untouched by inner conflicts or desires.
avadhuta_gita::240.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that the true self is beyond all changes like attachment, greed, or their opposites. Since it is one, eternal, and all-pervading, it cannot be touched by ignorance or wisdom, showing its absolute nature.
avadhuta_gita::240.modern_relevance: When emotions like craving or aversion arise, remember your true self remains untouched, offering a steady refuge in any turmoil.
avadhuta_gita::240.insight: This verse shifts your view from identifying with fluctuating desires and judgments to recognizing your unchanging, faultless essence.

avadhuta_gita::241.verse_sanskrit:
त्वमहं न हि हन्त कदाचिदपि कुलजातिविचारमसत्यमिति ।
अहमेव शिवः परमार्थ इति अभिवादनमत्र करोमि कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::241.verse_hindi: खेद है कि आत्मा में तू और मैं का भेद कदापि नहीं है तथा उसमें कुल एवं जाति का विचार भी असत्य ही है। परमार्थ रूप में में ही कल्याणकारी आत्मा हूँ फिर में किस प्रकार यहाँ अभिवादन करूँ।
avadhuta_gita::241.english_translation: I regret that in the true self there is never a distinction of you and me, nor of family or caste; in ultimate reality, I am the benevolent true self, so how can I offer respect here?
avadhuta_gita::241.translation_literal: त्वम् (you) अहम् (I) न (not) हि (indeed) हन्त (kill) कदाचिदपि (ever) कुलजातिविचारम् (family-caste distinction) असत्यमिति (is false) । अहम् (I) एव (indeed) शिवः (benevolent) परमार्थ (ultimate reality) इति (thus) अभिवादनम् (greeting/respect) अत्र (here) करोमि (do) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::241.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::241.essence: All divisions vanish in the true self where only unity remains.
avadhuta_gita::241.simple_meaning: There is never any real difference between you and me or among social groups in the true self; in ultimate reality, I am the benevolent true self, so offering respect here seems unnecessary.
avadhuta_gita::241.simple_insight: You can feel the relief of knowing all divisions are illusions in the deepest self.
avadhuta_gita::241.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya reveals that distinctions like you and me or family and caste do not exist in the true self. Since he is that benevolent true self, the idea of greeting or respecting another is meaningless here.
avadhuta_gita::241.modern_relevance: When you realize the divisions between people are mental, it frees you from judgment and separation in daily life.
avadhuta_gita::241.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing others as separate to recognizing fundamental oneness beyond social labels.

avadhuta_gita::242.verse_sanskrit:
गुरुशिष्यविचारविशीर्ण इति उपदेशविचारविशीर्ण इति ।
अहमेव शिवः परमार्थ इति अभिवादनमत्र करोमि कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::242.verse_hindi: आत्मा में गुरु शिष्य का विचार भी नहीं है जिससे उपदेश का विचार भी नहीं हैं। में ही परमार्थ में शिव रूप हूँ। फिर मैं यहाँ किस प्रकार अभिवादन करूँ।
avadhuta_gita::242.english_translation: In the true self, there is no thought of teacher or student, nor of instruction. I alone am the supreme reality as Shiva. How then can I offer salutations here?
avadhuta_gita::242.translation_literal: गुरुशिष्यविचारविशीर्ण (teacher-student-thoughts-absent) इति (thus) उपदेशविचारविशीर्ण (instruction-thoughts-absent) इति (thus) । अहमेव (I-alone) शिवः (Shiva) परमार्थ (supreme-reality) इति (thus) अभिवादनमत्र (salutation-here) करोमि (do) कथम् (how) ॥
avadhuta_gita::242.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::242.essence: The true self transcends all dualities including teacher and student; it alone is supreme.
avadhuta_gita::242.simple_meaning: The true self has no separation of teacher and student or any instruction. It alone is the ultimate reality as Shiva, making formal salutations unnecessary.
avadhuta_gita::242.simple_insight: You can rest in the truth that all roles and teachings dissolve into your true nature.
avadhuta_gita::242.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that in the deepest self there is no distinction between teacher and student or any teachings. He identifies himself as Shiva, the supreme reality, questioning how he could pay respects where there is no duality.
avadhuta_gita::242.modern_relevance: When you realize your true nature, the need for external authorities or roles fades, freeing you from dependency on others for guidance.
avadhuta_gita::242.insight: It shifts your perspective from relying on external roles to recognizing your own inherent completeness as the supreme reality.

avadhuta_gita::243.verse_sanskrit:
न हि कल्पितदेहविभाग इति न हि कल्पितलोकविभाग इति ।
अहमेव शिवः परमार्थ इति अभिवादनमत्र करोमि कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::243.verse_hindi: कल्पित देह से भी आत्मा का भेद सिद्ध नहीं होता, कल्पित लोकों से भी इसका भेद सिद्ध नहीं होता। मैं ही परमार्थ में शिव रूप आत्मा हूँ फिर मैं किस प्रकार अभिवादन करूं।
avadhuta_gita::243.english_translation: The true self does not differ from the imagined body or the imagined worlds. I am the supreme being in reality; how then could I offer reverence?
avadhuta_gita::243.translation_literal: न (not) / हि (indeed) / कल्पितदेहविभाग (imagined-body-difference) / इति (thus) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / कल्पितलोकविभाग (imagined-world-difference) / इति (thus) / अहमेव (I-only) / शिवः (auspicious/ supreme being) / परमार्थ (supreme reality) / इति (thus) / अभिवादनमत्र (reverence here) / करोमि (do) / कथम् (how)
avadhuta_gita::243.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::243.essence: You are the supreme reality beyond all imagined division, so reverence to the self is needless.
avadhuta_gita::243.simple_meaning: The true self is not different from the body or the worlds we imagine. The self is the supreme reality, so offering reverence to it is unnecessary.
avadhuta_gita::243.simple_insight: You can feel complete knowing you are not divided from anything imagined around you.
avadhuta_gita::243.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the distinctions we make between the self, body, and worlds are imagined. He affirms his identity as the supreme reality itself, making any act of reverence toward that reality meaningless.
avadhuta_gita::243.modern_relevance: When you see yourself as separate from your body or surroundings, you might feel small or limited, but recognizing your true nature as whole frees you from that division.
avadhuta_gita::243.insight: It shifts thinking from seeing yourself as a fragmented being to recognizing your oneness with all appearances.

avadhuta_gita::244.verse_sanskrit:
सरजो विरजो न कदाचिदपि ननु निर्मलनिश्चलशुद्ध इति ।
अहमेव शिवः परमार्थ इति अभिवादनमत्र करोमि कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::244.verse_hindi: वह आत्मा कभी भी राग एवं विराग वाली नहीं है, निश्चय ही यह निर्मल, निश्चल एवं शुद्ध है। मैं परमार्थ रूप में वही शिवरूप आत्मा हूँ फिर में किस प्रकार अभिवादन करूँ।
avadhuta_gita::244.english_translation: The true self is never attached or detached; it is pure, steady, and immaculate. I am that self as the supreme reality, so how could I offer salutations to myself?
avadhuta_gita::244.translation_literal: सरजो (attached) / विरजो (detached) / न (not) / कदाचिदपि (ever) / ननु (indeed) / निर्मलनिश्चलशुद्ध (pure-steady-immaculate) / इति (thus) / अहमेव (I alone) / शिवः (Shiva) / परमार्थ (supreme reality) / इति (thus) / अभिवादनमत्र (salutation here) / करोमि (do) / कथम् (how)
avadhuta_gita::244.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::244.essence: The true self is eternally pure and steady; it needs no salutation.
avadhuta_gita::244.simple_meaning: The true self never experiences attachment or detachment. It is always pure, steady, and immaculate. Realizing this, there is no need to offer respect to something that you already are.
avadhuta_gita::244.simple_insight: You can feel complete knowing your true self is already pure and unchanging.
avadhuta_gita::244.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the true self is never caught in attachment or aversion. It remains pure and steady beyond all change. Since he is that self in its supreme reality, he finds no reason to offer any gesture of respect to himself.
avadhuta_gita::244.modern_relevance: When you struggle with self-doubt or feel the need to prove your worth, this reminds you that your true nature is already pure and complete.
avadhuta_gita::244.insight: It shifts your perspective from seeking approval to owning your unchanging true self as whole.

avadhuta_gita::245.verse_sanskrit:
न हि देहविदेहविकल्प इति अनृतं चरितं न हि सत्यमिति ।
अहमेव शिवः परमार्थ इति अभिवादनमत्र करोमि कथम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::245.verse_hindi: उस आत्मा में देह और विदेह का विकल्प भी नहीं है, उसमें मिथ्या चरित्र भी सत्य नहीं हैं। मैं ही परमार्थ रूप में वही शिव रूप आत्मा हूँ। फिर मैं किस प्रकार अभिवादन करूं।
avadhuta_gita::245.english_translation: In that true self, there is no distinction of embodied or disembodied, no false or true character. I am the true self, the supreme reality, the auspicious being. How then should I offer respect?
avadhuta_gita::245.translation_literal: न (not) हि (indeed) देहविदेहविकल्प (embodied-or-disembodied-alternative) इति (thus) अनृतं (false) चरितं (character) न (not) हि (indeed) सत्यमिति (true thus). अहमेव (I alone) शिवः (auspicious one) परमार्थ (supreme reality) इति (thus) अभिवादनमत्र (offering respect here) करोमि (do) कथम् (how).
avadhuta_gita::245.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::245.essence: No duality exists in your true self, so honoring another separate self is unnecessary.
avadhuta_gita::245.simple_meaning: There is no real difference between having a body or not, or between truth and falsehood in the true self. The true self is the supreme reality. So, there is no one else to honor.
avadhuta_gita::245.simple_insight: You can feel complete and whole because no separation or duality truly exists within you.
avadhuta_gita::245.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the true self transcends the usual distinctions like embodied or disembodied states, and false or true traits. Recognizing oneself as the supreme reality removes the need to perform acts of respect or greeting, since there is no separate other.
avadhuta_gita::245.modern_relevance: You realize that all the roles and labels you juggle don't define your true self, so you stop feeling the pressure to perform or please others.
avadhuta_gita::245.insight: It shifts your understanding from seeing yourself as a separate entity to recognizing your unity with all existence, dissolving the need for external validation.

avadhuta_gita::246.verse_sanskrit:
विन्दति विन्दति न हि न हि यत्र छन्दोलक्षणं न हि न हि तत्र ।
समरसमग्नो भावितपूतः प्रलपति तत्त्वं परमवधूतः ॥
avadhuta_gita::246.verse_hindi: परम अवधूत ( श्रेष्ठ ज्ञानी) जिसका अन्त:करण पवित्र है वह उस एकरस आत्मा में ही मग्न रहता है तथा उसी का कथन करता है जिसमें छन्द और लक्षण नहीं है उसी आत्मा को प्राप्त होता है।
avadhuta_gita::246.english_translation: The supreme Avadhuta, whose inner being is pure, remains immersed in the one undifferentiated self beyond form and qualities, and speaks only that ultimate truth.
avadhuta_gita::246.translation_literal: विन्दति (finds) / विन्दति (finds) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / यत्र (where) / छन्दोलक्षणं (meter and qualities) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / तत्र (there) / समरसमग्नः (immersed in the undifferentiated) / भावितपूतः (whose inner being is pure) / प्रलपति (speaks) / तत्त्वं (truth) / परमवधूतः (supreme Avadhuta)
avadhuta_gita::246.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::246.essence: The highest self is pure, undivided, and beyond all forms and qualities.
avadhuta_gita::246.simple_meaning: A fully realized person stays absorbed in the pure self beyond all appearances and speaks only that ultimate reality.
avadhuta_gita::246.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your true self is beyond all labels and forms.
avadhuta_gita::246.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the supreme Avadhuta who, having purified his inner being, dwells fully in the unchanging self beyond poetic meter or qualities, expressing only that ultimate essence.
avadhuta_gita::246.modern_relevance: When distractions and labels overwhelm you, remember your true self is untouched and pure beneath all noise.
avadhuta_gita::246.insight: Shift your focus from external forms to the unchanging pure awareness within you.

avadhuta_gita::247.verse_sanskrit:
रथ्याकर्पटविरचितकन्थः पुण्यापुण्यविवर्जितपन्थः ।
शून्यागारे तिष्ठति नग्नो शुद्धनिरञ्जनसमरसमग्नः ॥
avadhuta_gita::247.verse_hindi: जीवन्मुक्त अवधूत गलियों में पड़े चिथड़ों की झोली बनाकर, पाप और पुण्य रहित मार्ग पर चलता हुआ नग्न होकर शून्य मन्दिर में स्थित होकर शुद्ध, निर्दोष एवं समरस आत्मा में ही लीन रहता है।
avadhuta_gita::247.english_translation: The liberated Avadhuta walks the path free of good and bad, naked, dwelling in the empty temple, immersed in the pure, spotless, and undivided self.
avadhuta_gita::247.translation_literal: रथ्याकर्पटविरचितकन्थः (wrapped in a raggy cloth like a chariot) पुण्यापुण्यविवर्जितपन्थः (path free from merit and demerit) शून्यागारे (in the empty temple) तिष्ठति (stands/dwells) नग्नो (naked) शुद्धनिरञ्जनसमरसमग्नः (pure, spotless, and immersed in sameness)
avadhuta_gita::247.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::247.essence: Freedom arises when you shed all dualities and rest naked in pure awareness.
avadhuta_gita::247.simple_meaning: You live beyond good and bad, stripped of all pretenses, resting in pure and undivided being.
avadhuta_gita::247.simple_insight: There is freedom in shedding all labels and simply being as you are.
avadhuta_gita::247.detailed_meaning: The Avadhuta, fully liberated, wears only ragged cloth, walks a path free of good and bad, and dwells naked in an empty temple, symbolizing complete immersion in pure, spotless, and undivided awareness.
avadhuta_gita::247.modern_relevance: You let go of all judgments about yourself and others, standing vulnerable yet whole, beyond any moral labels or societal masks.
avadhuta_gita::247.insight: It invites you to stop defining yourself by external values and rest in your pure, undivided nature instead.

avadhuta_gita::248.verse_hindi: लक्ष्य और अलक्ष्य से रहित ही जिसका लक्ष्य है, युक्त और अयुक्त से रहित जो दक्ष है, केवल उस निरंजन आत्मतत्व में मग्न अवधूत वाद-विवाद कैसे करे।
avadhuta_gita::248.english_translation: The Avadhuta, immersed in the pure essence beyond visible and invisible, capable beyond the attached and unattached, how could he engage in argument or dispute?
avadhuta_gita::248.translation_literal: लक्ष्यालक्ष्यविवर्जितलक्ष्यो (goal-and-nongoal rejecting is the goal) / युक्तायुक्तविवर्जितदक्षः (attached-and-unattached rejecting is capable) / केवलतत्त्वनिरञ्जनपूतो (only essence pure cleansed) / वादविवादः (argument debate) / कथमवधूतः (how Avadhuta)
avadhuta_gita::248.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::248.essence: True mastery is living beyond all dualities where argument no longer arises.
avadhuta_gita::248.simple_meaning: When you are fully absorbed in the pure true self beyond all opposites, arguing or debating has no place.
avadhuta_gita::248.simple_insight: You can feel free from all conflicts when you realize your nature is beyond division.
avadhuta_gita::248.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the Avadhuta who is established beyond all visible and invisible distinctions, beyond attachment or detachment, fully immersed in the pure true self. At this stage, arguing or disputing is meaningless because there is no duality left to argue about.
avadhuta_gita::248.modern_relevance: You’ve stopped fighting with yourself or others because you see beyond right or wrong, beyond winning or losing.
avadhuta_gita::248.insight: It teaches you to recognize when conflict is unnecessary because your awareness transcends all opposites.

avadhuta_gita::249.verse_hindi: आशा रूपी पाश के बन्धन से मुक्त हैं, बाहर के शौच आचार से रहित आत्मा से युक्त सन्त सभी प्रकार के तत्वों से रहित शुद्ध एवं निर्दोष है।
avadhuta_gita::249.english_translation: Those freed from the bonds of desire, untouched by external rites, are pure, spotless, and free from all elements.
avadhuta_gita::249.translation_literal: आशापाशविबन्धनमुक्ताः (freed from the bonds of desire) / शौचाचारविवर्जितयुक्ताः (joined with absence of external purity and conduct) / एवं (thus) / सर्वविवर्जितशान्ताः (completely free and peaceful) / तत्त्वं (essence) / शुद्धनिरञ्जनवन्तः (pure and spotless, possessing)
avadhuta_gita::249.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::249.essence: True purity arises when desire and external rituals no longer bind you.
avadhuta_gita::249.simple_meaning: Freedom from desire and external rituals reveals your pure, peaceful true nature beyond all elements.
avadhuta_gita::249.simple_insight: There is freedom and peace in letting go of inner craving and outer formality.
avadhuta_gita::249.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes a state where one is no longer tied by desire or by external rules of purity and conduct. This freedom brings a pure and spotless essence, beyond all material elements and appearances.
avadhuta_gita::249.modern_relevance: You feel peace when you stop chasing wants and relax your need to follow every rule or expectation around you.
avadhuta_gita::249.insight: It shifts your focus from outer forms and desires to the pure essence that is naturally free and peaceful.

avadhuta_gita::250.verse_sanskrit:
कथमिह देहविदेहविचारः कथमिह रागविरागविचारः ।
निर्मलनिश्चलगगनाकारं स्वयमिह तत्त्वं सहजाकारम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::250.verse_hindi: जीवन्मुक्त ज्ञानी में देह और विदेह का विचार किस प्रकार हो सकता है, उसमें राग एवं विराग का विचार भी कैसे हो सकता है। वह स्वयं ही स्वभाव से ही आत्म तत्व हैं जो निर्मल, निश्चल एवं आकाश के समान व्यापक है।
avadhuta_gita::250.english_translation: How can a liberated knower think of body and beyond-body, or feel attachment and detachment? They are naturally the pure, steady essence, vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::250.translation_literal: कथमिह (how here) / देहविदेहविचारः (body and beyond-body thought) / कथमिह (how here) / रागविरागविचारः (attachment and detachment thought) / निर्मलनिश्चलगगनाकारं (pure-steady-sky-like) / स्वयमिह (by itself here) / तत्त्वं (essence) / सहजाकारम् (natural form)
avadhuta_gita::250.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::250.essence: True freedom means being steady and pure beyond body and desire.
avadhuta_gita::250.simple_meaning: A truly liberated person does not think in terms of body or outside body, attachment or detachment. Their true nature is pure, steady, and vast like the sky.
avadhuta_gita::250.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing you are naturally steady and untouched by desires or limits.
avadhuta_gita::250.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya points out that for someone fully free, the distinctions of physical body and non-body, or of attachment and detachment, do not arise. Such a person naturally embodies the pure and unshakable essence that is vast like the sky itself.
avadhuta_gita::250.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by your body’s needs and emotional swings. Yet your true self remains calm and vast beneath those waves.
avadhuta_gita::250.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with fleeting states to recognizing your natural, unchanging essence.

avadhuta_gita::251.verse_sanskrit:
कथमिह तत्त्वं विन्दति यत्र रूपमरूपं कथमिह तत्र ।
गगनाकारः परमो यत्र विषयीकरणं कथमिह तत्र ॥
avadhuta_gita::251.verse_hindi: जीवन्मुक्त ज्ञानी जहाँ इस अवस्था में तत्व को किस प्रकार जान सकता है वहाँ रूप एवं अरूप को भी किस प्रकार जान सकता है क्योंकि वह जहाँ आकाश स्वरूप परमतत्व आत्मा ही है फिर वहाँ विषयों का व्यवहार भी नहीं हो सकता।
avadhuta_gita::251.english_translation: How can the liberated knower find the essence where form and formlessness exist? How can there be distinctions where the supreme reality is like space, free of qualities?
avadhuta_gita::251.translation_literal: कथमिह (how here) / तत्त्वं (essence) / विन्दति (finds) / यत्र (where) / रूपमरूपं (form and formlessness) / कथमिह (how here) / तत्र (there) । / गगनाकारः (like sky/space) / परमो (supreme) / यत्र (where) / विषयीकरणं (distinction/particularization) / कथमिह (how here) / तत्र (there) ॥
avadhuta_gita::251.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::251.essence: The supreme reality is beyond all form and distinctions, like infinite space.
avadhuta_gita::251.simple_meaning: You cannot understand essence where form and formlessness both exist, because the supreme reality is like space without distinctions.
avadhuta_gita::251.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing that the highest reality has no divisions or forms to grasp.
avadhuta_gita::251.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya questions how a liberated being can recognize essence where form and formlessness both appear, since the supreme reality is like infinite space without any distinctions or objects.
avadhuta_gita::251.modern_relevance: When you try to define your true nature, you realize it cannot be pinned down by any shape or category—it's boundless and free.
avadhuta_gita::251.insight: It shifts your mind from looking for defined forms to recognizing the limitless, undifferentiated reality beneath appearances.

avadhuta_gita::252.verse_hindi: यह आत्मतत्व आकाश तुल्य व्यापक, नित्य, विशुद्ध, निर्दोष एवं हंस तुल्य है। यह एक ही है इसलिए इसमें भिन्नता एवं समानता का कथन कैसे हो सकता है। इसमें बन्धन, बन्धन रहित एवं विकार का भेद भी नहीं हो सकता।
avadhuta_gita::252.english_translation: The true self is vast like the sky, eternal, pure, and spotless like a swan; therefore, how can it have differences, bonds, or faults?
avadhuta_gita::252.translation_literal: गगनाकारनिरन्तरहंसस्तत्त्वविशुद्धनिरञ्जनहंसः (sky-shaped, continuous, swan, essence, pure, spotless, swan) / एवं (thus) / कथमिह (how here) / भिन्नविभिन्नं (different, various) / बन्धविबन्धविकारविभिन्नम् (bond, bondless, fault, different)
avadhuta_gita::252.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::252.essence: The true self is eternally pure and one without distinction or defect.
avadhuta_gita::252.simple_meaning: The true self is vast and pure, like the sky and an untouched swan. It cannot have differences, bonds, or faults.
avadhuta_gita::252.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing your true self is untouched and unchanged by any flaw or attachment.
avadhuta_gita::252.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that the true self is like the vast sky and a pure swan—continuous and spotless. It is beyond any distinctions of bondage, freedom, or faults, affirming its absolute purity and unity.
avadhuta_gita::252.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your flaws or mistakes, remember your true self is vast and pure, unaffected by those changes.
avadhuta_gita::252.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as limited and flawed to recognizing your essential boundless purity.

avadhuta_gita::253.verse_sanskrit:
केवलतत्त्वनिरन्तरसर्वंयोगवियोगौ कथमिह गर्वम् ।
एवं परमनिरन्तरसर्व मेवं कथमिह सारविसारम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::253.verse_hindi: केवल आत्मतत्व ही नित्य एवं सर्व है, इसमें अहंकारवश योग और वियोग को कथन किस प्रकार हो सकता है। तथा यह आत्मा परम, नित्य एवं सर्व है तो इसमें सार एवं असार भी कैसे हो सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::253.english_translation: The true self alone is eternal and all-pervading; how can pride arise from union and separation? Since the self is supreme, eternal, and all, how can there be essence and non-essence?
avadhuta_gita::253.translation_literal: केवल (only) आत्मतत्त्व (true self principle) निरन्तर (continuous) सर्वं (all) योग (union) वियोग (separation) कथम् (how) इह (here) गर्वम् (pride) । एवं (thus) परम (supreme) निरन्तर (eternal) सर्व (all) मेवं (thus) कथम् (how) इह (here) सार (essence) विसारम् (non-essence) ॥
avadhuta_gita::253.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::253.essence: The eternal true self cannot be divided by union, separation, or value judgments.
avadhuta_gita::253.simple_meaning: The true self is always whole and eternal. It cannot be divided by ideas of coming together or falling apart, nor by what is important or not.
avadhuta_gita::253.simple_insight: You can feel steady knowing your true self is beyond all change and comparison.
avadhuta_gita::253.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares the true self as unchanging and all-encompassing. He challenges the idea that pride or meaning can come from temporary unions or separations since the self transcends all dualities and distinctions.
avadhuta_gita::253.modern_relevance: When relationships or situations shift, you might feel pride or loss. Recognizing your inner self is beyond these ups and downs steadies your sense of self.
avadhuta_gita::253.insight: It shifts your mind from identifying with fluctuating events to resting in the unchanging self.

avadhuta_gita::254.verse_sanskrit:
केवलतत्त्वनिरञ्जनसर्वं गगनाकारनिरन्तरशुद्धम् ।
एवं कथमिह सङ्गविसङ्गं सत्यं कथमिह रङ्गविरङ्गम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::254.verse_hindi: केवल यह आत्मा ही निर्दोष, सवरूप, आकाश, तुल्य व्यापक, नित्य एवं शुद्ध है इसलिए इसमें संग और विसंग कैसे हो सकता है। इसमें सत्य, रंग और विरंग कैसे हो सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::254.english_translation: The true self alone is pure, formless like space, endlessly pure and pervasive; how then can it have attachment or detachment, truth or falsehood?
avadhuta_gita::254.translation_literal: केवलतत्त्वनिरञ्जनसर्वं (only the principle pure-all) / गगनाकारनिरन्तरशुद्धम् (like-sky form continuous-pure) / एवं (thus) / कथमिह (how here) / सङ्गविसङ्गं (attachment-detachment) / सत्यं (truth) / कथमिह (how here) / रङ्गविरङ्गम् (color-no color)
avadhuta_gita::254.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::254.essence: The true self is endlessly pure and cannot hold division or contradiction.
avadhuta_gita::254.simple_meaning: The true self is like pure space—always spotless and unlimited. It cannot have attachments, separations, or contradictions like truth and falsehood.
avadhuta_gita::254.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing your nature cannot be divided or stained.
avadhuta_gita::254.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the true self as utterly pure and formless, like the vast sky. Because it is infinite and spotless, it cannot hold attachments or opposites such as truth and falsehood, revealing the self beyond all duality.
avadhuta_gita::254.modern_relevance: When you feel torn by conflicting desires or judgments, remember your true nature is beyond all these divisions and remains pure.
avadhuta_gita::254.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as fragmented to recognizing your unbroken, pure essence.

avadhuta_gita::255.verse_sanskrit:
योगवियोगै रहितो योगी भोगविभोगै रहितो भोगी ।
एवं चरति हि मन्दं मन्दं मनसा कल्पितसहजानन्दम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::255.verse_hindi: आत्मज्ञानी योगी योग एवं वैराग्य से रहित हो जाता है, भोगी होकर भी भोग और त्याग से रहित हो जाता है। वह अपने मन द्वारा कल्पित स्वाभाविक आनन्द में मन्द-मन्द गति से ( अपनी ही मस्ती में) विचरण करता है।
avadhuta_gita::255.english_translation: The true knower moves beyond yoga and renunciation, enjoying natural bliss in gentle ease.
avadhuta_gita::255.translation_literal: योगवियोगै (by union and separation) / रहितो (free) / योगी (the yogi) / भोगविभोगै (by enjoyment and renunciation) / रहितो (free) / भोगी (the enjoyer) / एवं (thus) / चरति (moves) / हि (indeed) / मन्दं मन्दं (slowly, gently) / मनसा (by the mind) / कल्पितसहजानन्दम् (imagined natural bliss)
avadhuta_gita::255.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::255.essence: You can be free from effort and craving while gently living in imagined natural bliss.
avadhuta_gita::255.simple_meaning: You become free from the need for spiritual striving and from craving or rejecting pleasures. You gently live in your mind’s natural joy.
avadhuta_gita::255.simple_insight: There is peace in gently resting within natural joy without forcing or avoiding anything.
avadhuta_gita::255.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the true knower is free from both the effort of yoga and the rejection of pleasures. Even as an enjoyer, the sage moves slowly and calmly in a bliss imagined by the mind yet naturally arising.
avadhuta_gita::255.modern_relevance: You stop wrestling with every urge or discipline and instead find calm joy simply by letting things be, moving gently through life.
avadhuta_gita::255.insight: It shifts your focus from forcing spiritual effort to allowing natural joy to unfold quietly within.

avadhuta_gita::256.verse_sanskrit:
बोधविबोधैः सततं युक्तो द्वैताद्वैतैः कथमिह मुक्तः ।
सहजो विरजः कथमिह योगी शुद्धनिरञ्जनसमरसभोगी ॥
avadhuta_gita::256.verse_hindi: जो व्यक्ति ज्ञान एवं अज्ञान से निरन्तर युक्त हैं, तथा जो द्वैत और अद्वैत से भी युक्त है वह कैसे मुक्त हो सकता है। इस संसार में योगी सहज ही राग रहित किस प्रकार हो सकता है। आत्मानन्द का भोक्ता ही शुद्ध, निर्दोष एवं समरस होता है।
avadhuta_gita::256.english_translation: How can one be free who is constantly attached to both knowledge and ignorance, duality and non-duality? How can a yogi be naturally without desire? Only the one who enjoys the bliss of the true self is pure, spotless, and fully harmonious.
avadhuta_gita::256.translation_literal: बोधविबोधैः (with knowledge and ignorance) सततं (constantly) युक्तो (attached) द्वैताद्वैतैः (to duality and non-duality) कथमिह (how here) मुक्तः (free) । सहजो (naturally) विरजः (desireless) कथमिह (how here) योगी (the yogi) शुद्धनिरञ्जनसमरसभोगी (pure, spotless, and fully harmonious) ॥
avadhuta_gita::256.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::256.essence: True freedom arises only when you are naturally free from all attachments, including to knowledge and ignorance.
avadhuta_gita::256.simple_meaning: You cannot be truly free if you remain attached to knowledge or ignorance, or to any duality. True purity and harmony come from being naturally free of desire and fully immersed in the bliss of your true self.
avadhuta_gita::256.simple_insight: Freedom comes from releasing all attachments, even to ideas of knowledge or ignorance.
avadhuta_gita::256.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya challenges the idea that holding onto any fixed view—whether knowledge, ignorance, duality, or non-duality—can lead to freedom. The yogi who truly enjoys the bliss of the true self is naturally desireless, pure, and harmoniously united.
avadhuta_gita::256.modern_relevance: You feel stuck toggling between what you think you know and what you doubt, unable to find peace or freedom in your mind.
avadhuta_gita::256.insight: It teaches you to drop all mental attachments, including to the concepts of knowledge and ignorance, to experience true freedom.

avadhuta_gita::257.verse_sanskrit:
भग्नाभग्नविवर्जितभग्नो लग्नालग्नविवर्जितलग्नः ।
एवं कथमिह सारविसारः समरसतत्त्वं गगनाकारः ॥
avadhuta_gita::257.verse_hindi: यह आत्मा समरस तत्व एवं आकाश तुल्य व्यापक हैं जो खण्ड-अखण्ड एवं खण्ड से रहित हैं, यह किसी में लगा हुआ, नहीं लगा हुआ एवं लगे हुए से रहित है। इसे सार एवं असार भी किस प्रकार कहा जा सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::257.english_translation: The true self is like vast sky—both fragmented and unfragmented, attached and unattached simultaneously; how can it be called real or unreal?
avadhuta_gita::257.translation_literal: भग्नाभग्नविवर्जितभग्नः (broken-unbroken-excluded broken) / लग्नालग्नविवर्जितलग्नः (attached-unattached-excluded attached) / एवं (thus) / कथमिह (how here) / सारविसारः (real unreal) / समरसतत्त्वं (of homogeneous essence) / गगनाकारः (like the sky)
avadhuta_gita::257.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::257.essence: You are vast and free beyond all opposites, both attached and unattached at once.
avadhuta_gita::257.simple_meaning: The true self is vast and all-pervading like the sky. It is beyond being fragmented or whole, attached or detached. It cannot be labeled as real or unreal.
avadhuta_gita::257.simple_insight: You can rest in your true nature that is beyond all contradictions and limitations.
avadhuta_gita::257.detailed_meaning: The Avadhuta describes the true self as infinite like the sky, transcending all dualities such as fragment and whole or attached and unattached. This teaching invites seeing beyond all labels of reality or unreality.
avadhuta_gita::257.modern_relevance: When your mind tries to pin you down as this or that, remember you are vast and free, beyond any label or limitation.
avadhuta_gita::257.insight: It shifts your view from defining yourself by conditions to recognizing your unbounded, paradox-embracing nature.

avadhuta_gita::258.verse_sanskrit:
सततं सर्वविवर्जितयुक्तः सर्वं तत्त्वविवर्जितमुक्तः ।
एवं कथमिह जीवितमरणं ध्यानाध्यानैः कथमिह करणम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::258.verse_hindi: योगी निरन्तर उस सर्व रहित आत्मा से मुक्त रहता है तथा सम्पूर्ण तत्वों से रहित होकर मुक्त रहता है। इस प्रकार उसका जीना और मरना किस प्रकार होता है। फिर उसका ध्यान करना और न करना कैसे हो सकता है।
avadhuta_gita::258.english_translation: The yogi remains constantly free, detached from everything and all elements; thus, how can living and dying, or meditating and not meditating, happen to them?
avadhuta_gita::258.translation_literal: सततं (constantly) सर्व (all) विवर्जितयुक्तः (with detachment) सर्वं (everything) तत्त्वविवर्जितम् (elements-detached) मुक्तः (free) । एवं (thus) कथमिह (how here) जीवितम् (living) मरणं (dying) ध्यानाध्यानैः (meditating and not meditating) कथमिह (how here) करणम् (action) ॥
avadhuta_gita::258.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::258.essence: Complete freedom dissolves all distinctions of action, life, and death.
avadhuta_gita::258.simple_meaning: A yogi who is fully free and detached from everything does not truly experience living or dying, nor the act of meditating or not meditating.
avadhuta_gita::258.simple_insight: You can be completely free, untouched by change or effort, beyond all opposites.
avadhuta_gita::258.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya speaks of a yogi who is wholly free from attachment to all things and elements. In this state, the usual distinctions between living and dying, or practicing meditation and not, vanish completely.
avadhuta_gita::258.modern_relevance: You’ve felt overwhelmed by endless choices and worries about success or failure—this frees you from all that pressure entirely.
avadhuta_gita::258.insight: It shifts your view from identifying with life’s changes to recognizing your unchanging freedom beyond them.

avadhuta_gita::259.verse_sanskrit:
इन्द्रजालमिदं सर्वं यथा मरुमरीचिका ।
अखण्डितमनाकारो वर्तते केवलः शिवः ॥
avadhuta_gita::259.verse_hindi: यह सम्पूर्ण जगत इन्द्रजाल के समान हैं अथवा मरुस्थल की मरीचिका के समान है। इनमें केवल घनाकार के रूप में अखण्डित कल्याण स्वरूप आत्मा ही वर्तता है।
avadhuta_gita::259.english_translation: This entire world is like a magic illusion or a mirage in the desert; only the undivided, radiant true self exists.
avadhuta_gita::259.translation_literal: इन्द्रजालमिदं (this magic illusion) / सर्वं (all) / यथा (like) / मरुमरीचिका (desert mirage) / अखण्डित (undivided) / अमनाकारो (imperishable form) / वर्तते (exists) / केवलः (only) / शिवः (auspicious one/true self)
avadhuta_gita::259.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::259.essence: Only the undivided, radiant true self truly exists beyond all illusions.
avadhuta_gita::259.simple_meaning: The world you perceive is like a magic illusion or desert mirage. Only the whole, radiant true self truly exists.
avadhuta_gita::259.simple_insight: There is peace in realizing that the changing world is not ultimately real, only your true self is.
avadhuta_gita::259.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya declares that all of existence is like a magical illusion or a desert mirage—something that appears but is not truly real. Only the undivided, radiant true self remains constant and real behind all appearances.
avadhuta_gita::259.modern_relevance: When life feels confusing and unstable, like things are slipping away, remember that your true self remains unshaken, like a steady light behind all illusions.
avadhuta_gita::259.insight: It shifts your mind from clinging to appearances toward recognizing the unchanging true self behind all change.

avadhuta_gita::260.verse_sanskrit:
धर्मादौ मोक्षपर्यन्तं निरीहाः सर्वथा वयम् ।
कथं रागविरागैश्च कल्पयन्ति विपश्चितः ॥
avadhuta_gita::260.verse_hindi: हम धर्म आदि को लेकर मोक्ष पर्यन्त इच्छा रहित हैं। फिर पण्डित लोग किस प्रकार हम में राग और विराग की कल्पना करते हैं।
avadhuta_gita::260.english_translation: From duty to liberation, we remain without desire in every way; how then do the wise imagine attachment and detachment in us?
avadhuta_gita::260.translation_literal: धर्मादौ (from duty) / मोक्षपर्यन्तं (up to liberation) / निरीहाः (without desire) / सर्वथा (in every way) / वयम् (we) / कथं (how) / रागविरागैः (by attachment and detachment) / च (and) / कल्पयन्ति (imagine) / विपश्चितः (the wise)
avadhuta_gita::260.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::260.essence: You are untouched by desire or aversion through every stage of existence.
avadhuta_gita::260.simple_meaning: You remain completely free of desire through all stages, from duty to liberation. Wise people mistakenly imagine you have attachment or detachment.
avadhuta_gita::260.simple_insight: There's peace in knowing your true nature is beyond all desires and aversions.
avadhuta_gita::260.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya speaks from the perspective of one who is utterly free, unaffected by attachment or aversion from the start of duty through liberation, challenging the wise who falsely attribute such states to him.
avadhuta_gita::260.modern_relevance: When you feel pressured to want or reject things to grow, remember that your true self is already beyond these swings.
avadhuta_gita::260.insight: It shifts your view from seeing desire and aversion as real states to understanding them as mental projections.

avadhuta_gita::261.verse_sanskrit:
विन्दति विन्दति न हि न हि यत्र छन्दोलक्षणं न हि न हि तत्र ।
समरसमग्नो भावितपूतः प्रलपति तत्त्वं परमवधूतः ॥
avadhuta_gita::261.verse_hindi: परम अवधूत ( श्रेष्ठ ज्ञानी) जिसका अन्त:करण पवित्र है उस एकरस आत्मा में ही मग्न रहता है तथा उस आत्मतत्व का ही कथन करता है। जिसमें छन्द और लक्षण नहीं हैं उसी आत्मा को प्राप्त होता है।
avadhuta_gita::261.english_translation: The supreme wise one, whose inner being is pure, remains absorbed in the unified true self and speaks only of that essence where there are no divisions or qualities.
avadhuta_gita::261.translation_literal: विन्दति (finds) / विन्दति (finds) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / यत्र (where) / छन्दः (metrical pattern) / लक्षणं (characteristic) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / तत्र (there) / समरसमग्नः (immersed in the unified essence) / भावितपूतः (pure in feeling) / प्रलपति (speaks) / तत्त्वं (the essence) / परमवधूतः (the supreme free one)
avadhuta_gita::261.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::261.essence: True wisdom is immersion in the pure self beyond all qualities and divisions.
avadhuta_gita::261.simple_meaning: The highest wise one stays absorbed in the pure true self, which has no divisions or qualities, and speaks only of that essence.
avadhuta_gita::261.simple_insight: You can rest in your pure inner being beyond all distinctions and mental labels.
avadhuta_gita::261.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the supreme liberated being who remains deeply immersed in the undivided true self. This self has no defining qualities or divisions such as meter or signs, and the liberated one only speaks of this pure essence.
avadhuta_gita::261.modern_relevance: When all external labels and judgments fall away, you can find calm and deep connection to your true nature beneath the noise.
avadhuta_gita::261.insight: Recognize your identity beyond all mental categories and descriptions, resting in pure awareness itself.

avadhuta_gita::262.verse_sanskrit:
त्वद्यात्रया व्यापकता हता ते
ध्यानेन चेतःपरता हता ते ।
स्तुत्या मया वाक्परता हता ते
क्षमस्व नित्यं त्रिविधापराधान् ॥
avadhuta_gita::262.verse_hindi: तुम्हारी यात्रा से व्यापकता नष्ट हुई, तुम्हारे ध्यान से चित्त की विषयपरता नष्ट हुई, तुम्हारी स्तुति से मेरी वाणी की विषयपरता नष्ट हुई अब मैं नित्य तीन प्रकार के अपराधों से क्षमा माँगता हूँ।
avadhuta_gita::262.english_translation: Your journey ended my expansion, your meditation ended my mind's restlessness, your praise ended my speech's distractions; now I eternally seek forgiveness for these three offenses.
avadhuta_gita::262.translation_literal: त्वद्यात्रया (by your journey) / व्यापकता (expansion) / हता (killed) / ते (your) / ध्यानेन (by meditation) / चेतःपरता (mind's distraction) / हता (killed) / ते (your) / स्तुत्या (by praise) / मया (by me) / वाक्परता (speech's distraction) / हता (killed) / ते (your) / क्षमस्व (forgive) / नित्यं (eternally) / त्रिविधापराधान् (threefold offenses)
avadhuta_gita::262.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::262.essence: Focused presence dissolves restless distractions and opens the way to lasting forgiveness.
avadhuta_gita::262.simple_meaning: Your journey stopped my restless expansion, your meditation calmed my distracted mind, and your praise quieted my distracted speech; now I ask forgiveness for these faults forever.
avadhuta_gita::262.simple_insight: There's relief in surrendering restlessness and seeking forgiveness for mistakes.
avadhuta_gita::262.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya expresses how the divine's journey, meditation, and praise dissolve his mental distractions and speech faults. This moment shows his deep humility and readiness to seek forgiveness for three ongoing faults.
avadhuta_gita::262.modern_relevance: After a long day overwhelmed by scattered thoughts and restless speech, you finally find calm and feel ready to forgive yourself for the slip-ups.
avadhuta_gita::262.insight: It teaches you to recognize how presence and focused attention can dissolve mental chaos and open the heart to forgiveness.

avadhuta_gita::263.verse_sanskrit:
कामैरहतधीर्दान्तो मृदुः शुचिरकिञ्चनः ।
अनीहो मितभुक् शान्तः स्थिरो मच्छरणो मुनिः ॥
avadhuta_gita::263.verse_hindi: जिसकी बुद्धि कामना रहित है (निष्काम है), जिसने बाह्य इन्द्रियों को वश में कर लिया है, जो कोमल स्वभाव वाला है, पवित्र रहता हो, थोड़े में गुजारा करता हो, इच्छा रहित हो, थोड़ा भोजन करता हो, शान्त हो, स्थिर बुद्धि वाला हो तथा आत्मा की शरण हो वही मुनि है।
avadhuta_gita::263.english_translation: One whose mind is free of desire, who controls the senses, is gentle, pure, content with little, desireless, calm, steady-minded, and refuge of the self—that one is a sage.
avadhuta_gita::263.translation_literal: कामैरहतधीर्दान्तो (desire-free, wise, controlled) / मृदुः (gentle) / शुचिरकिञ्चनः (pure, content with little) / अनीहो (desireless) / मितभुक् (moderate eater) / शान्तः (calm) / स्थिरः (steady) / मच्छरणः (refuge of the self) / मुनिः (sage)
avadhuta_gita::263.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::263.essence: A sage is calm, desireless, gentle, and steady, offering refuge to the true self.
avadhuta_gita::263.simple_meaning: A sage is someone who is free from craving, controls their senses, stays gentle and pure, lives simply, and remains calm and steady as a refuge for their true self.
avadhuta_gita::263.simple_insight: There is peace in living simply with a calm, desire-free mind that becomes a true refuge.
avadhuta_gita::263.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the qualities of a sage: free from desires, mastering external senses, gentle by nature, pure, content with little food, calm, steady in mind, and a refuge for their true self. This moment captures the essence of spiritual maturity.
avadhuta_gita::263.modern_relevance: You find peace when you stop chasing wants, control impulses, stay gentle with yourself, and live simply without needless desires.
avadhuta_gita::263.insight: It teaches you to cultivate calmness and simplicity by releasing desire and mastering your senses to become steady and centered.

avadhuta_gita::264.verse_sanskrit:
अप्रमत्तो गभीरात्मा धृतिमान् जितषड्गुणः ।
अमानी मानदः कल्पो मैत्रः कारुणिकः कविः ॥
avadhuta_gita::264.verse_hindi: जो प्रमाद से रहित, गम्भीर स्वभाव वाला, धैर्य युक्त, छ: विकारों को जिसने जीत लिया है, अभिमान रहित, दूसरों को मान देने वाला, मित्रतापूर्वक व्यवहार करने वाला, करुणावान, दयाशील है वही आत्मज्ञानी है।
avadhuta_gita::264.english_translation: The self-knower is vigilant, profound, steady, has conquered the six faults, is free of pride, honors others, is friendly and compassionate.
avadhuta_gita::264.translation_literal: अप्रमत्तो (vigilant) / गभीरात्मा (profound self) / धृतिमान् (steady) / जितषड्गुणः (conqueror of six faults) / अमानी (without pride) / मानदः (one who honors) / कल्पो (friend) / मैत्रः (friendly) / कारुणिकः (compassionate) / कविः (wise one)
avadhuta_gita::264.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::264.essence: True wisdom is shown by steady calmness and kindness after mastering inner faults.
avadhuta_gita::264.simple_meaning: A person who is always alert, deeply calm, patient, free of six inner faults, humble, respectful, friendly, and compassionate is truly wise.
avadhuta_gita::264.simple_insight: You feel peaceful and connected when you overcome your inner flaws with kindness.
avadhuta_gita::264.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the qualities of a realized person: one who is attentive and steady, has mastered six inner faults (desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride, envy), shows humility, respects others, and acts with friendly compassion.
avadhuta_gita::264.modern_relevance: When you stay calm under pressure, avoid negative reactions, and treat others with kindness, you become a source of steady wisdom in any situation.
avadhuta_gita::264.insight: This verse shifts your focus from external achievement to mastering inner qualities like humility and compassion.

avadhuta_gita::265.verse_hindi: जो सम्पूर्ण देहधारियों के प्रति कृपालु, द्रोह ने करने वाला, सहनशील, सत्य का सार, जन्म-मरण से रहित, सम तथा सबका उपकार करने वाला है वही आत्मज्ञानी है।
avadhuta_gita::265.english_translation: The true knower of the self is compassionate to all beings, free from hostility, patient, the essence of truth, beyond birth and death, equal to all, and a benefactor to everyone.
avadhuta_gita::265.translation_literal: कृपालु (compassionate) / अकृतद्रोहः (free from hostility) / तितिक्षुः (patient) / सर्वदेहिनाम् (to all embodied beings) / सत्यसारः (essence of truth) / अनवद्यात्मा (unborn self) / समः (equal) / सर्वोपकारकः (benefactor to all)
avadhuta_gita::265.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::265.essence: Your true self is patient, kind, equal, and beyond all conflict or change.
avadhuta_gita::265.simple_meaning: Your true self is kind to all, patient, free from hostility, beyond birth and death, equal to everyone, and always helpful.
avadhuta_gita::265.simple_insight: You can feel steady kindness inside, untouched by conflict or change.
avadhuta_gita::265.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the self that truly knows itself as compassionate and patient with all beings, free from hostility, beyond the cycle of birth and death, and equal to all, embodying the essence of truth and universal kindness.
avadhuta_gita::265.modern_relevance: When tensions rise around you, remember your inner self can remain calm, kind, and unaffected by conflict.
avadhuta_gita::265.insight: It teaches you to embody patience and compassion beyond personal grievances, seeing all as equal and worthy of kindness.

avadhuta_gita::266.verse_hindi: अवधूत (जीवन्मुक्त ज्ञानी) के ये लक्षण सभी वर्ण वालों को, भक्तों को, वेद वर्ण के तत्वज्ञ पण्डितों को, वेद-वेदान्त के ज्ञाता को जानना चाहिए।
avadhuta_gita::266.english_translation: The characteristics of the Avadhuta (one liberated in life) must be known by all classes, devotees, scholars of Vedic knowledge, and teachers of Vedanta.
avadhuta_gita::266.translation_literal: अवधूतलक्षणं (Avadhuta-characteristics) / वर्णैः (by classes) / ज्ञातव्यं (must be known) / भगवत्तमैः (by devotees of the divine) / वेदवर्णार्थतत्त्वज्ञैः (by scholars knowing Vedic meanings) / वेदवेदान्तवादिभिः (by Vedic and Vedantic teachers)
avadhuta_gita::266.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::266.essence: The Avadhuta's qualities are essential knowledge for all sincere seekers.
avadhuta_gita::266.simple_meaning: The qualities of the Avadhuta should be understood by all social groups, devotees, and learned Vedic and Vedanta scholars.
avadhuta_gita::266.simple_insight: True freedom is a universal reality every sincere seeker should recognize.
avadhuta_gita::266.detailed_meaning: The Avadhuta, a liberated sage, is described here as having traits that all societal groups, devotees, and scholars of sacred texts should recognize. This verse sets the stage for understanding true liberation beyond social or intellectual boundaries.
avadhuta_gita::266.insight: It invites you to see spiritual freedom as accessible and relevant beyond any social or intellectual category.

avadhuta_gita::267.verse_sanskrit:
आशापाशविनिर्मुक्त आदिमध्यान्तनिर्मलः ।
आनन्दे वर्तते नित्यमकारं तस्य लक्षणम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::267.verse_hindi: अवधूत शब्द चार अक्षरों से मिलकर बना है। अ+व+ धू+त। इसमें दत्तात्रेय जी अकार (अ) का लक्षण बताते हुए कहते हैं कि जो ‘आशा’ रूपी पाश से मुक्त है, ‘आदि’ मध्य और अन्त से निर्मल है, ‘आनन्द’ में ही नित्य मग्न रहता है ये तीनों अकार (अ) की अवधूत के लक्षण हैं।
avadhuta_gita::267.english_translation: The liberated one is free from the bond of desire, pure in beginning, middle, and end, and always immersed in bliss; this is the mark of the Avadhuta.
avadhuta_gita::267.translation_literal: आशापाशविनिर्मुक्त (desire-bond-free) आदिमध्यान्तनिर्मलः (beginning-middle-end-pure) । आनंदे (in bliss) वर्तते (dwells) नित्यमकारं (always 'a'-marked) तस्य (his) लक्षणम् (characteristic) ॥
avadhuta_gita::267.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::267.essence: True freedom is being desireless, pure at every moment, and naturally immersed in bliss.
avadhuta_gita::267.simple_meaning: You are completely free from desire and remain pure throughout, always living in bliss; this defines the liberated state.
avadhuta_gita::267.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing you are naturally free and joy-filled beyond desire.
avadhuta_gita::267.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the Avadhuta as someone who has shaken off all bonds of desire, remaining pure in every aspect of existence and continuously absorbed in bliss, revealing the essence of complete liberation.
avadhuta_gita::267.modern_relevance: You notice how craving or longing no longer weighs you down, and joy flows naturally without effort, freeing you from restless wants.
avadhuta_gita::267.insight: It teaches you to recognize that freedom and bliss arise when you release all desires and remain pure in your being.

avadhuta_gita::268.verse_sanskrit:
वासना वर्जिता येन वक्तव्यं च निरामयम् ।
वर्तमानेषु वर्तेत वकारं तस्य लक्षणम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::268.verse_hindi: इसमें अ+व+धू+त शब्द में ‘व’ अक्षर का लक्षण बताते हुए दत्तात्रेय जी कहते हैं कि ‘वासना’ का जिसने त्याग कर दिया है और ‘वक्तव्य’ जिसका राग-रहित है, जो ‘वर्तमान’ में ही रहता है। ‘व’ (वकार) ही अवधूत के लक्षण हैं।
avadhuta_gita::268.english_translation: The sign of the Avadhuta is one who has renounced desire, speaks without attachment, and lives fully in the present.
avadhuta_gita::268.translation_literal: वासना (desire) / वर्जिता (renounced) / येन (by whom) / वक्तव्यं (speech) / च (and) / निरामयम् (without attachment) / वर्तमानेषु (in the present) / वर्तेत (lives) / वकारं (letter 'va' / symbol) / तस्य (his) / लक्षणम् (sign)
avadhuta_gita::268.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::268.essence: Freedom is living desire-free, speaking without attachment, fully present now.
avadhuta_gita::268.simple_meaning: The Avadhuta lives without desire, speaks without attachment, and stays fully present in the moment.
avadhuta_gita::268.simple_insight: You feel the lightness when desire no longer pulls your words or actions.
avadhuta_gita::268.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains the core sign of an Avadhuta: someone who has let go of craving, speaks without bias, and remains grounded in the present moment, showing true freedom beyond mental grasping.
avadhuta_gita::268.modern_relevance: You notice how your mood shifts when you stop chasing wants and just say what is true now.
avadhuta_gita::268.insight: This verse shifts your focus from clinging desires to clear, present living, freeing your speech and actions.

avadhuta_gita::269.verse_sanskrit:
धूलिधूसरगात्राणि धूतचित्तो निरामयः ।
धारणाध्याननिर्मुक्तो धूकारस्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::269.verse_hindi: दत्तात्रेय जी इसमें अ+व+ धू+त शब्द में ‘धू’ अक्षर का लक्षण बताते हुए कहते हैं कि ‘धूलिधूसर’ जिसके अंग हैं, ‘धूत चित्त’ (पापों से धोया गया चित्त) जिसका है, रोग रहित है, ‘धारणा ध्यान’ से जो मुक्त हो गया है ये तीन ‘धूकार’ ही अवधूत के लक्षण हैं।
avadhuta_gita::269.english_translation: The Avadhuta’s marks are a body cleansed of dust and dirt, a mind washed free of faults, and liberation from attachment to meditation and concentration.
avadhuta_gita::269.translation_literal: धूलिधूसरगात्राणि (dust-and-dirt-cleansed-body) / धूतचित्तो (washed-mind) / निरामयः (disease-free) / धारणा-ध्यान-निर्मुक्तो (liberated-from-meditation-and-concentration) / धूकारः (signs) / तस्य (of-that) / लक्षणम् (characteristic)
avadhuta_gita::269.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::269.essence: Freedom is shown by a clean body, pure mind, and release from mental grasping.
avadhuta_gita::269.simple_meaning: You are marked by a body free of dirt, a mind cleansed of faults, and freedom from attachment to mental focus.
avadhuta_gita::269.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your true self is untouched by impurities or fixations.
avadhuta_gita::269.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya describes the Avadhuta as one whose body is free from dust and dirt, whose mind is washed clean of faults, and who is liberated from attachment to meditation and concentration. These qualities define the liberated state beyond physical and mental constraints.
avadhuta_gita::269.modern_relevance: You wipe away all distractions and judgments, carrying a clear mind and body that no longer cling to habits or thoughts.
avadhuta_gita::269.insight: It teaches you to recognize freedom as a state beyond physical cleanliness and mental fixation.

avadhuta_gita::270.verse_sanskrit:
तत्त्वचिन्ता धृता येन चिन्ताचेष्टाविवर्जितः ।
तमोऽहंकारनिर्मुक्तस्तकारस्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥
avadhuta_gita::270.verse_hindi: दत्तात्रेय जी इसमें अ+व+ धू+त शब्द में तकार (त) का अर्थ बताते हुए कहते हैं कि जिसने ‘तत्व चिन्ता’ को ही धारण किया है, जो ‘चिन्ता और चेष्टा’ से रहित है, ‘तम रूपी अहंकार’ से जो रहित है ये तीनों ‘तकार’ अवधूत के लक्षण हैं।
avadhuta_gita::270.english_translation: The one who holds only true reality in mind, free from restless thought and action, and released from the ego of darkness, these three qualities define the free one.
avadhuta_gita::270.translation_literal: तत्त्वचिन्ता (true reality contemplation) / धृता (held) / येन (by whom) / चिन्ताचेष्टाविवर्जितः (free from thought and effort) / तमोऽहंकारनिर्मुक्तः (released from ego of darkness) / तकारस्तस्य (the 'ta' letter of) / लक्षणम् (characteristic)
avadhuta_gita::270.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::270.essence: Freedom is holding only true reality, free from restless mind and ego darkness.
avadhuta_gita::270.simple_meaning: You are defined by focusing only on true reality, without restless mental activity or ego’s darkness.
avadhuta_gita::270.simple_insight: There is freedom in holding only what truly is, letting go of worry and ego.
avadhuta_gita::270.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya explains that the free one (Avadhuta) is marked by holding only the true essence, without mental agitation or egoic darkness, revealing the deepest nature of liberation.
avadhuta_gita::270.modern_relevance: When your mind stops chasing endless worries and self-doubt, you experience true clarity and freedom.
avadhuta_gita::270.insight: It teaches you to rest your mind solely on what is real, dropping all restless efforts and egoic attachments.

avadhuta_gita::271.verse_sanskrit:
दत्तात्रेयावधूतेन निर्मितानन्दरूपिणा ।
ये पठन्ति च श‍ृण्वन्ति तेषां नैव पुनर्भवः ॥
avadhuta_gita::271.verse_hindi: आनन्द मूर्ति दत्तात्रेय जी अवधूत ने इसका निर्माण किया है जो इसको पढ़ते हैं और सुनते हैं उनका पुनर्जन्म कभी नहीं होता।
avadhuta_gita::271.english_translation: The blissful Avadhuta Dattatreya created this; those who read or hear it never take rebirth.
avadhuta_gita::271.translation_literal: दत्तात्रेयावधूतेन (by Avadhuta Dattatreya) निर्मितानन्दरूपिणा (created by the blissful one) । (.) ये (those who) पठन्ति (read) च (and) शृण्वन्ति (hear) तेषां (for them) नैव (certainly not) पुनर्भवः (rebirth) ॥ (.)
avadhuta_gita::271.speaker: Dattatreya
avadhuta_gita::271.essence: Engaging with this teaching ends the cycle of rebirth.
avadhuta_gita::271.simple_meaning: This text was created by the blissful Avadhuta Dattatreya. Those who read or listen to it will not be reborn again.
avadhuta_gita::271.simple_insight: There is reassurance in knowing that engaging deeply with this teaching ends the cycle of rebirth.
avadhuta_gita::271.detailed_meaning: Dattatreya, the blissful Avadhuta, declares that this scripture is his creation. He assures that anyone who reads or hears it will transcend the cycle of rebirth, highlighting the text's spiritual power.
avadhuta_gita::271.insight: It shifts the focus from endless seeking to the power of deep understanding through the text.

bhagwad_gita::1.verse_sanskrit: धृतराष्ट्र उवाचधर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः । मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥
bhagwad_gita::1.verse_hindi: धृतराष्ट्र बोले   हे संजय  धर्मभूमि कुरुक्षेत्र में युद्ध की इच्छा से इकट्ठे हुए मेरेे और पाण्डु के पुत्रों ने भी क्या किया ॥
bhagwad_gita::1.english_translation: Dhritarashtra said: O Sanjaya, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do, assembled on the holy field of Kurukshetra and eager for battle?
bhagwad_gita::1.translation_literal: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच (Dhritarashtra said) / धर्मक्षेत्रे (on the field of duty) / कुरुक्षेत्रे (at Kurukshetra) / समवेता (assembled) / युयुत्सवः (desiring to fight) / मामकाः (my people) / पाण्डवाः (the sons of Pandu) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / किम् (what) / अकुर्वत (did they do) / सञ्जय (O Sanjaya)
bhagwad_gita::1.speaker: Dhritarashtra
bhagwad_gita::1.essence: The war begins in a question, not a sword strike.
bhagwad_gita::1.simple_meaning: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what happened when both sides gathered on the battlefield, ready to fight.
bhagwad_gita::1.simple_insight: Before any action begins, uncertainty can feel heavier than the battle itself.
bhagwad_gita::1.detailed_meaning: Dhritarashtra, blind and anxious, asks Sanjaya about the moment before war begins on Kurukshetra. His own sons and the Pandavas have assembled, but the outcome is still hidden. This opening question sets the whole Gita in motion.
bhagwad_gita::1.modern_relevance: You sit outside a hospital room, waiting for news after a family conflict has finally exploded. Nothing has been said yet, but everything has already changed.
bhagwad_gita::1.insight: It frames the entire Gita as a witness account of a crisis already in motion.

bhagwad_gita::2.verse_sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाचदृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा । आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::2.verse_hindi: संजय बोले  उस समय वज्रव्यूहसे खड़ी हुई पाण्डवसेना को देखकर राजा दुर्योधन द्रोणाचार्य के पास जाकर यह वचन बोला ॥
bhagwad_gita::2.english_translation: Sanjaya said: Seeing the Pandava army arranged in battle formation, King Duryodhana went to Dronacharya and spoke these words.
bhagwad_gita::2.translation_literal: सञ्जय उवाच (Sanjaya said) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / तु (indeed) / पाण्डवानीकं (the Pandava army) / व्यूढं (arrayed in formation) / दुर्योधनः (Duryodhana) / तदा (then) / आचार्यम् (to the teacher) / उपसङ्गम्य (having approached) / राजा (the king) / वचनम् (words) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
bhagwad_gita::2.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::2.essence: War becomes real the moment the enemy is seen clearly.
bhagwad_gita::2.simple_meaning: Duryodhana sees the Pandava army in battle formation and goes to Drona to speak.
bhagwad_gita::2.simple_insight: The scene tightens before the war begins.
bhagwad_gita::2.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Duryodhana sees the Pandava army drawn up in disciplined formation. He immediately approaches Drona, his teacher, and begins speaking. This is the moment just before fear, pride, and strategy spill into words.
bhagwad_gita::2.modern_relevance: You spot the other side is ready, organized, and serious. Before you can hide behind confidence, you walk straight to the person who taught you and admit the pressure.
bhagwad_gita::2.insight: It sets up the first crack in Duryodhana’s certainty and moves the scene into open confrontation.

bhagwad_gita::3.verse_sanskrit: पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम् । व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता ॥
bhagwad_gita::3.verse_hindi: हे आचार्य आपके बुद्धिमान् शिष्य द्रुपदपुत्र धृष्टद्युम्न के द्वारा व्यूहरचना से खड़ी की हुई पाण्डवों की इस बड़ी भारी सेना को देखिये ॥
bhagwad_gita::3.english_translation: O teacher, look at this great army of the sons of Pandu, arranged in battle formation by your wise disciple, the son of Drupada.
bhagwad_gita::3.translation_literal: पश्य (look) / एताम् (this) / पाण्डुपुत्राणाम् (of the sons of Pandu) / आचार्य (O teacher) / महतीम् (great) / चमूम् (army) / व्यूढाम् (arrayed in formation) / द्रुपदपुत्रेण (by the son of Drupada) / तव (your) / शिष्येण (by the disciple) / धीमता (wise)
bhagwad_gita::3.speaker: Duryodhana
bhagwad_gita::3.essence: A battlefield can be won first by how it is described.
bhagwad_gita::3.simple_meaning: Duryodhana points out the Pandava army to Drona and reminds him that the commander is Drona's own clever student.
bhagwad_gita::3.simple_insight: Comparison and pressure can be used to shake another person's resolve.
bhagwad_gita::3.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Duryodhana sees the Pandava forces drawn up against him. He turns to Drona and highlights the army's size and the skill of Dhृष्टद्युम्न, Drona's former student, to stir urgency before battle begins.
bhagwad_gita::3.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting and someone names the room's strongest rival first. The point is not just information; it is pressure, meant to unsettle the person across the table.
bhagwad_gita::3.insight: It shows how speech can frame a situation to influence another person's response before action begins.

bhagwad_gita::4.verse_sanskrit: अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि । युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः ॥
bhagwad_gita::4.verse_hindi: यहाँ पाण्डवों की सेना में बड़ेबड़े शूरवीर हैं, जिनके बहुत बड़ेबड़े धनुष हैं तथा जो युद्ध में भीम और अर्जुनके समान हैं ।  उनमें युयुधान सात्यकि, राजा विराट और महारथी द्रुपद भी हैं ।  धृष्टकेतु और चेकितान तथा पराक्रमी काशिराज भी हैं ।  पुरुजित् और कुन्तिभोजये दोनों भाई तथा मनुष्योंमें श्रेष्ठ शैब्य भी हैं ।  पराक्रमी युधामन्यु और पराक्रमी उत्तमौजा भी हैं ।  सुभद्रापुत्र अभिमन्यु और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र भी हैं ।  ये सबकेसब महारथी हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::4.english_translation: Here in the Pandava army are mighty warriors, great archers, equal to Bhima and Arjuna in battle: Satyaki, Virata, and the great chariot-warrior Drupada.
bhagwad_gita::4.translation_literal: अत्र (here) / शूराः (heroes, brave ones) / महेष्वासाः (great bowmen) / भीमार्जुनसमा (equal to Bhima and Arjuna) / युधि (in battle) / युयुधानः (Yuyudhana) / विराटः (Virata) / च (and) / द्रुपदः (Drupada) / च (and) / महारथः (great chariot-warrior)
bhagwad_gita::4.speaker: Duryodhana
bhagwad_gita::4.essence: The other side is strong, and pretending otherwise changes nothing.
bhagwad_gita::4.simple_meaning: Duryodhana points out the Pandava army's strongest warriors and praises their battle skill.
bhagwad_gita::4.simple_insight: The verse builds tension by showing that the other side is formidable, not weak.
bhagwad_gita::4.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Duryodhana stands before Drona and keeps listing the Pandava forces. He names their finest warriors to impress the scale of the threat and prepare the battlefield mood before the war begins.
bhagwad_gita::4.modern_relevance: You walk into a meeting already knowing the other team is stronger, sharper, and better prepared. Naming the challenge clearly is the first step before any real response.
bhagwad_gita::4.insight: It shifts attention from denial to clear-eyed assessment of what you are facing.

bhagwad_gita::5.verse_sanskrit: धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् । पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः ॥
bhagwad_gita::5.verse_hindi: यहाँ पाण्डवों की सेना में बड़ेबड़े शूरवीर हैं, जिनके बहुत बड़ेबड़े धनुष हैं तथा जो युद्ध में भीम और अर्जुनके समान हैं ।  उनमें युयुधान सात्यकि, राजा विराट और महारथी द्रुपद भी हैं ।  धृष्टकेतु और चेकितान तथा पराक्रमी काशिराज भी हैं ।  पुरुजित् और कुन्तिभोजये दोनों भाई तथा मनुष्योंमें श्रेष्ठ शैब्य भी हैं ।  पराक्रमी युधामन्यु और पराक्रमी उत्तमौजा भी हैं ।  सुभद्रापुत्र अभिमन्यु और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र भी हैं ।  ये सबकेसब महारथी हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::5.english_translation: Dhृष्टकेतु, Chekitana, and the valiant king of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the best among men.
bhagwad_gita::5.translation_literal: धृष्टकेतुः (Dhṛṣṭaketu) / चेकितानः (Chekitana) / काशिराजः (king of Kashi) / वीर्यवान् (valiant) / पुरुजित् (Purujit) / कुन्तिभोजः (Kuntibhoja) / शैब्यः (Shaibya) / नरपुङ्गवः (best among men)
bhagwad_gita::5.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::5.essence: The battlefield is already full of power and named allies.
bhagwad_gita::5.simple_meaning: Sanjaya continues listing the mighty warriors in the Pandava army.
bhagwad_gita::5.simple_insight: The battlefield is crowded with strength on both sides, and the conflict is real.
bhagwad_gita::5.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Sanjaya keeps naming the warriors standing with the Pandavas. This is not teaching yet; it is the buildup that shows Arjuna facing a vast, disciplined force before Krishna begins to answer his collapse.
bhagwad_gita::5.modern_relevance: You walk into a room knowing the decision ahead will affect everyone there. The names, the faces, the stakes keep piling up before you can even speak.
bhagwad_gita::5.insight: It frames the scene as overwhelming reality, not abstract debate.

bhagwad_gita::6.verse_sanskrit: युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान् । सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::6.verse_hindi: यहाँ पाण्डवों की सेना में बड़ेबड़े शूरवीर हैं, जिनके बहुत बड़ेबड़े धनुष हैं तथा जो युद्ध में भीम और अर्जुनके समान हैं ।  उनमें युयुधान सात्यकि, राजा विराट और महारथी द्रुपद भी हैं ।  धृष्टकेतु और चेकितान तथा पराक्रमी काशिराज भी हैं ।  पुरुजित् और कुन्तिभोजये दोनों भाई तथा मनुष्योंमें श्रेष्ठ शैब्य भी हैं ।  पराक्रमी युधामन्यु और पराक्रमी उत्तमौजा भी हैं ।  सुभद्रापुत्र अभिमन्यु और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र भी हैं ।  ये सबकेसब महारथी हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::6.english_translation: Yudhamanyu, brave and powerful, Uttamaujas, brave and powerful, Subhadra's son, and the sons of Draupadi — all of them are great warriors.
bhagwad_gita::6.translation_literal: युधामन्युः (Yudhamanyu) / च (and) / विक्रान्तः (brave, powerful) / उत्तमौजाः (Uttamaujas) / च (and) / वीर्यवान् (valiant) / सौभद्रः (Subhadra's son) / द्रौपदेयाः (the sons of Draupadi) / च (and) / सर्वे (all) / एव (indeed) / महारथाः (great warriors)
bhagwad_gita::6.speaker: Duryodhana
bhagwad_gita::6.essence: The enemy line is full of elite fighters.
bhagwad_gita::6.simple_meaning: Duryodhana keeps listing the Pandava side's strongest fighters, showing how formidable Arjuna's army is.
bhagwad_gita::6.simple_insight: The scale of the coming battle becomes clear: this is not a small clash, but a war between equals.
bhagwad_gita::6.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Duryodhana is still sizing up the enemy lines for Drona. After naming several champions, he adds Yudhamanyu, Uttamaujas, Abhimanyu, and Draupadi's sons. The point is not teaching, but building the picture of a packed battlefield.
bhagwad_gita::6.modern_relevance: You enter a room knowing the other side is stronger than you expected. Before the first word is spoken, the tension already tells you this will be a real fight.
