bhagwad_gita::6.insight: It sharpens the scene by showing the Pandavas are backed by many elite warriors, not just Arjuna.

bhagwad_gita::7.verse_sanskrit: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम । नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते ॥
bhagwad_gita::7.verse_hindi: हे द्विजोत्तम हमारे पक्ष में भी जो मुख्य हैं, उनपर भी आप ध्यान दीजिये ।  आपको याद दिलाने के लिये मेरी सेना के जो नायक हैं, उनको मैं कहता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::7.english_translation: O best of the twice-born, note also our own chief warriors. I name them to remind you of our army.
bhagwad_gita::7.translation_literal: अस्माकं (our) / तु (but/also) / विशिष्टाः (distinguished, chief) / ये (who) / तान् (them) / निबोध (know, note) / द्विजोत्तम (O best of the twice-born) / नायकाः (leaders, chiefs) / मम (of my) / सैन्यस्य (of the army) / संज्ञार्थं (for the sake of recognition, to remind) / तान् (them) / ब्रवीमि (I speak, I name) / ते (to you)
bhagwad_gita::7.speaker: Duryodhana
bhagwad_gita::7.essence: Pride counts its own strength when fear is near.
bhagwad_gita::7.simple_meaning: Duryodhana tells Drona to notice the main warriors on his own side too. He is naming them so they can be recognised before the battle.
bhagwad_gita::7.simple_insight: Even pride wants an audience. He is not just listing names; he is trying to steady his side.
bhagwad_gita::7.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, the armies stand ready and Duryodhana keeps speaking to Drona. After naming the Pandava heroes, he now turns to his own commanders and begins listing them so the teacher sees the strength of his side.
bhagwad_gita::7.modern_relevance: Before a tense meeting, someone starts reciting names, titles, and achievements to prove the team is strong. The real feeling underneath is fear of being outmatched.
bhagwad_gita::7.insight: It shows how anxiety hides inside boasting and turns into a need to count allies.

bhagwad_gita::8.verse_sanskrit: भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः । अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च ॥
bhagwad_gita::8.verse_hindi: आप द्रोणाचार्य और पितामह भीष्म तथा कर्ण और संग्रामविजयी कृपाचार्य तथा वैसे ही अश्वत्थामा, विकर्ण और सोमदत्त का पुत्र भूरिश्रवा ॥
bhagwad_gita::8.english_translation: Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and the son of Somadatta are also there.
bhagwad_gita::8.translation_literal: भवान् (you) / भीष्मः (Bhishma) / च (and) / कर्णः (Karna) / च (and) / कृपः (Kripa) / च (and) / समितिञ्जयः (victorious in battle) / अश्वत्थामा (Ashvatthama) / विकर्णः (Vikarna) / च (and) / सौमदत्तिः (the son of Somadatta) / तथा एव च (and likewise)
bhagwad_gita::8.speaker: Duryodhana
bhagwad_gita::8.essence: Fear clings to strength by naming it aloud.
bhagwad_gita::8.simple_meaning: Duryodhana keeps listing the strongest warriors on his side, naming more of the commanders gathered for battle.
bhagwad_gita::8.simple_insight: Sometimes fear speaks as inventory: count your allies before the fight begins.
bhagwad_gita::8.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Duryodhana is still speaking to Drona, trying to steady the moment by naming his champions. He adds Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and Somadatta's son to the list, building the case that his army is formidable.
bhagwad_gita::8.modern_relevance: Before a tense meeting, someone starts reciting credentials, titles, and backup plans just to feel less exposed. The list itself becomes a shield against fear.
bhagwad_gita::8.insight: It shows how the mind tries to control uncertainty by assembling names, numbers, and status.

bhagwad_gita::9.verse_sanskrit: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः । नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::9.verse_hindi: इनके अतिरिक्त बहुतसे शूरवीर हैं, जिन्होंने मेरे लिये अपने जीने की इच्छा का भी त्याग कर दिया है और जो अनेक प्रकार के शस्त्रअस्त्रों को चलानेवाले हैं तथा जो सबकेसब युद्धकला में अत्यन्त चतुर हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::9.english_translation: Besides these, many heroes have given up their lives for my sake. They wield many kinds of weapons and are all skilled in warfare.
bhagwad_gita::9.translation_literal: अन्ये (others) / च (and) / बहवः (many) / शूराः (heroes) / मदर्थे (for my sake) / त्यक्तजीविताः (having given up life) / नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः (wielding various weapons) / सर्वे (all) / युद्धविशारदाः (expert in warfare)
bhagwad_gita::9.speaker: Duryodhana
bhagwad_gita::9.essence: Confidence built on numbers still trembles before battle.
bhagwad_gita::9.simple_meaning: More warriors stand on Duryodhana's side too. They are fearless, heavily armed, and experienced in battle.
bhagwad_gita::9.simple_insight: Pride can inflate strength into certainty, even before the first blow lands.
bhagwad_gita::9.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Duryodhana keeps listing his side’s champions to Drona. After naming Bhishma, Karna, and others, he adds more fearless fighters who are ready to die for him. The speech builds his confidence before the war begins.
bhagwad_gita::9.modern_relevance: Before a high-stakes confrontation, someone rattles off every ally, every backup, every advantage, trying to silence doubt with a show of force.
bhagwad_gita::9.insight: It shows how fear can be masked by tallying strength instead of facing reality.

bhagwad_gita::10.verse_sanskrit: अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम् । पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::10.verse_hindi: वह हमारी सेना पाण्डवों पर विजय करने में अपर्याप्त है, असमर्थ है क्योंकि उसके संरक्षक उभयपक्षपाती भीष्म हैं ।  परन्तु इन पाण्डवों की सेना हमारे पर विजय करने में पर्याप्त है, समर्थ है क्योंकि इसके संरक्षक निजसेनापक्षपाती भीमसेन हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::10.english_translation: Our force, guarded by Bhishma, is insufficient; their force, guarded by Bhima, is sufficient.
bhagwad_gita::10.translation_literal: अपर्याप्तम् (insufficient) / तत् (that) / अस्माकम् (of us) / बलम् (force) / भीष्म-अभिरक्षितम् (protected by Bhishma) / पर्याप्तम् (sufficient) / तु (but) / इदम् (this) / एतेषाम् (of these) / बलम् (force) / भीम-अभिरक्षितम् (protected by Bhima)
bhagwad_gita::10.speaker: Duryodhana
bhagwad_gita::10.essence: Fear can declare defeat before the battle starts.
bhagwad_gita::10.simple_meaning: Duryodhana judges his own army as weaker and the Pandavas' army as stronger, based on who protects each side.
bhagwad_gita::10.simple_insight: Panic makes the mind measure strength badly and speak from fear.
bhagwad_gita::10.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, before the first arrow is fired, Duryodhana surveys both armies and speaks to Drona. He claims the Kaurava force is not enough and that the Pandava force is stronger, setting the tone for the coming war.
bhagwad_gita::10.modern_relevance: You walk into a meeting already expecting defeat, and every face seems to confirm it. Fear can make one side look larger before a single word is spoken.
bhagwad_gita::10.insight: It shows how fear distorts judgment before action begins.

bhagwad_gita::11.verse_sanskrit: अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः । भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि ॥
bhagwad_gita::11.verse_hindi: आप सबकेसब लोग सभी मोर्चों पर अपनीअपनी जगह दृढ़ता से स्थित रहते हुए ही पितामह भीष्म की चारों ओर से रक्षा करें ॥
bhagwad_gita::11.english_translation: Remain at your stations on every front and protect Bhishma from all sides.
bhagwad_gita::11.translation_literal: अयनेषु (on the battlefronts) / च (and) / सर्वेषु (all) / यथाभागम् (according to each one's place) / अवस्थिताः (standing positioned) / भीष्मम् (Bhishma) / एव (only) / अभिरक्षन्तु (let them protect) / भवन्तः (you all) / सर्वे (all) / हि (indeed)
bhagwad_gita::11.speaker: Duryodhana
bhagwad_gita::11.essence: Victory begins with disciplined formation, not scattered strength.
bhagwad_gita::11.simple_meaning: Duryodhana orders all his warriors to hold their positions and guard Bhishma from every side.
bhagwad_gita::11.simple_insight: The army's first move is pure coordination: hold the line, protect the key commander, do not break formation.
bhagwad_gita::11.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Duryodhana is rallying his side before the first clash. After praising his warriors and measuring the two armies, he gives a tactical command: every fighter must stay in position and shield Bhishma, the main pillar of their force.
bhagwad_gita::11.modern_relevance: Before a tense group presentation, everyone starts drifting into their own panic. One person has to call the room back into formation: stay in your place, cover the weak spot, don't let the center collapse.
bhagwad_gita::11.insight: It shifts attention from individual impulse to coordinated support around the most vulnerable point.

bhagwad_gita::12.verse_sanskrit: तस्य संजनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः । सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् ॥
bhagwad_gita::12.verse_hindi: दुर्योधन के हृदय में हर्ष उत्पन्न करते हुए कुरुवृद्ध प्रभावशाली पितामह भीष्म ने सिंह के समान गरज कर जोर से शंख बजाया ॥
bhagwad_gita::12.english_translation: The elder of the Kuru clan, the powerful grandfather Bhishma, roared like a lion and blew his conch loudly, filling Duryodhana with joy.
bhagwad_gita::12.translation_literal: तस्य (his) / संजनयन् (generating) / हर्षम् (joy) / कुरुवृद्धः (the elder of the Kuru clan) / पितामहः (grandfather) / सिंहनादम् (lion-roar) / विनद्य (having roared) / उच्चैः (loudly) / शङ्खम् (conch) / दध्मौ (blew) / प्रतापवान् (the powerful one)
bhagwad_gita::12.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::12.essence: A single battle cry can turn fear into momentum.
bhagwad_gita::12.simple_meaning: Bhishma blows his conch loudly, and Duryodhana feels encouraged. It is a battle signal, not a teaching verse.
bhagwad_gita::12.simple_insight: The moment before conflict can electrify a whole side.
bhagwad_gita::12.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, the two armies are already formed. Duryodhana has just ordered Bhishma to protect the Kaurava lines. Now Bhishma answers with a lion-like conch blast, lifting Kaurava morale and signaling that battle is about to begin.
bhagwad_gita::12.modern_relevance: A room goes silent before the announcement everyone has been dreading. One decisive sound, one firm gesture, and the whole atmosphere changes.
bhagwad_gita::12.insight: It sets the scene for war and shows how leadership can stir collective emotion before action begins.

bhagwad_gita::13.verse_sanskrit: ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः । सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::13.verse_hindi: उसके बाद शंख, भेरी नगाड़े, ढोल, मृदङ्ग और नरसिंघे बाजे एक साथ बज उठे ।  उनका वह शब्द बड़ा भयंकर हुआ ॥
bhagwad_gita::13.english_translation: Then conches, kettledrums, drums, and trumpets burst forth at once. Their sound became thunderous.
bhagwad_gita::13.translation_literal: ततः (then) / शङ्खाः (conches) / च (and) / भेर्यः (kettledrums) / च (and) / पणवानकगोमुखाः (small drums and trumpets) / सहसा एव (all at once) / अभ्यहन्यन्त (were struck) / सः (that) / शब्दः (sound) / तुमुलः (tumultuous) / अभवत् (became)
bhagwad_gita::13.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::13.essence: The war announces itself before the first blow.
bhagwad_gita::13.simple_meaning: Conches, drums, and trumpets all sounded together, and the noise became overwhelming.
bhagwad_gita::13.simple_insight: The battlefield is no longer quiet. The clash of war has begun to announce itself.
bhagwad_gita::13.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, after Bhishma's conch, the Kaurava side answers with a sudden roar of instruments. The battlefield fills with noise before the first arrows fly, building the tension that leads into Krishna and Arjuna sounding their own conches.
bhagwad_gita::13.modern_relevance: A room goes silent before a hard meeting starts, then every phone buzzes at once. The moment of pressure arrives before a single word is spoken.
bhagwad_gita::13.insight: It turns the scene from preparation into full confrontation.

bhagwad_gita::14.verse_sanskrit: ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ । माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः ॥
bhagwad_gita::14.verse_hindi: उसके बाद सफेद घोड़ों से युक्त महान् रथ पर बैठे हुए लक्ष्मीपति भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण और पाण्डुपुत्र अर्जुन ने दिव्य शंखों को बड़े जोर से बजाया ॥
bhagwad_gita::14.english_translation: Then, seated on the great chariot yoked with white horses, Madhava and Pandava blew their divine conches.
bhagwad_gita::14.translation_literal: ततः (then) / श्वेतैः (with white) / हयैः (horses) / युक्ते (yoked) / महति (great) / स्यन्दने (on the chariot) / स्थितौ (seated) / माधवः (Madhava) / पाण्डवः (the Pandava) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / दिव्यौ (divine) / शङ्खौ (conches) / प्रदध्मतुः (blew)
bhagwad_gita::14.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::14.essence: Resolve answers chaos before words begin.
bhagwad_gita::14.simple_meaning: Krishna and Arjuna stand together on their great chariot and sound their conches. It marks their answer to the Kaurava war cries.
bhagwad_gita::14.simple_insight: A calm, powerful response can change the whole feel of a moment.
bhagwad_gita::14.detailed_meaning: The battlefield is already roaring with enemy conches and drums. On the opposite side, Krishna and Arjuna stand together on their white-horsed chariot and answer with their own conches. The moment turns from threat to resolve.
bhagwad_gita::14.modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with bad news, and everyone around you is already panicking. You take one breath, steady yourself, and answer with clarity instead of fear.
bhagwad_gita::14.insight: It shifts attention from noise around you to the steadiness of your own response.

bhagwad_gita::15.verse_sanskrit: पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनंजयः । पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ॥
bhagwad_gita::15.verse_hindi: अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण ने पाञ्चजन्य नामक तथा धनञ्जय अर्जुन ने देवदत्त नामक शंख बजाया और भयानक कर्म करनेवाले वृकोदर भीम ने पौण्ड्र नामक महाशंख बजाया ॥
bhagwad_gita::15.english_translation: Hrisikesha Krishna blew the Panchajanya, Dhananjaya Arjuna blew the Devadatta, and Bhima of mighty deeds blew the great conch Paundra.
bhagwad_gita::15.translation_literal: पाञ्चजन्यं (Panchajanya) / हृषीकेशः (Hrisikesha) / देवदत्तं (Devadatta) / धनंजयः (Dhananjaya) / पौण्ड्रं (Paundra) / दध्मौ (blew) / महाशङ्खम् (great conch) / भीमकर्मा (one of mighty deeds) / वृकोदरः (Bhimasena)
bhagwad_gita::15.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::15.essence: The war begins in sound before a single strike.
bhagwad_gita::15.simple_meaning: Krishna, Arjuna, and Bhima each blew their own conches as the battle began.
bhagwad_gita::15.simple_insight: The moment is set by sound before the fighting starts.
bhagwad_gita::15.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, the two armies are already formed and the first conches have sounded. Sanjaya names the three great warriors on the Pandava side as their conches answer the call, marking the point where words end and battle begins.
bhagwad_gita::15.modern_relevance: The room goes quiet before the hard announcement. Then one clear voice speaks, and everyone knows the moment has crossed into action.
bhagwad_gita::15.insight: It shifts attention from the names and symbols to the irreversible step of commitment.

bhagwad_gita::16.verse_sanskrit: अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः । नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ॥
bhagwad_gita::16.verse_hindi: कुन्तीपुत्र राजा युधिष्ठिर ने अनन्तविजय नामक शंख बजाया तथा नकुल और सहदेव ने सुघोष और मणिपुष्पक नामक शंख बजाये ॥
bhagwad_gita::16.english_translation: King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughosha and Manipushpaka.
bhagwad_gita::16.translation_literal: अनन्तविजयं (Anantavijaya) / राजा (king) / कुन्तीपुत्रः (son of Kunti) / युधिष्ठिरः (Yudhishthira) / नकुलः (Nakula) / सहदेवः (Sahadeva) / च (and) / सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ (Sughosha and Manipushpaka)
bhagwad_gita::16.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::16.essence: The war begins to answer back in sound.
bhagwad_gita::16.simple_meaning: Yudhishthira, Nakula, and Sahadeva blow their conches. The verse adds to the battle scene and names their sacred war horns.
bhagwad_gita::16.simple_insight: The battlefield is filling with sound, and both sides are being drawn into the moment.
bhagwad_gita::16.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, the Pāṇḍava brothers stand ready beside Krishna and Arjuna. After Krishna and Arjuna sound their conches, Yudhishthira, Nakula, and Sahadeva answer with their own. The verse keeps building the charged scene before the fighting begins.
bhagwad_gita::16.modern_relevance: The room goes quiet before the announcement. One voice follows another, and everyone feels the pressure rise before a hard beginning.
bhagwad_gita::16.insight: It shifts attention from individual heroes to the full force gathering on one side.

bhagwad_gita::17.verse_sanskrit: काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः । धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ॥
bhagwad_gita::17.verse_hindi: हे राजन् श्रेष्ठ धनुषवाले काशिराज और महारथी शिखण्डी तथा धृष्टद्युम्न एवं राजा विराट और अजेय सात्यकि, राजा द्रुपद और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र तथा लम्बीलम्बी भुजाओंवाले सुभद्रापुत्र अभिमन्यु  इन सभी ने सब ओर से अलगअलग अपनेअपने शंख बजाये ॥
bhagwad_gita::17.english_translation: The great archer from Kashi, Shikhandi the great warrior, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and invincible Satyaki.
bhagwad_gita::17.translation_literal: काशीः (the king of Kashi) / च (and) / परमेष्वासः (supreme archer) / शिखण्डी (Shikhandi) / च (and) / महारथः (great warrior) / धृष्टद्युम्नः (Dhrishtadyumna) / विराटः (Virata) / च (and) / सात्यकिः (Satyaki) / च (and) / अपराजितः (invincible)
bhagwad_gita::17.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::17.essence: Names and conches turn hesitation into commitment.
bhagwad_gita::17.simple_meaning: This is a battlefield roll call. More warriors on the Pandava side blow their conches before the war begins.
bhagwad_gita::17.simple_insight: The scene builds tension: the war is no longer abstract; every name makes the confrontation real.
bhagwad_gita::17.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, the Pandava allies answer the Kaurava conches with their own. Sanjaya lists more warriors as each one blows a conch, sharpening the moment before battle into a final, audible commitment.
bhagwad_gita::17.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet before the announcement. One by one, the people who will stand with you are named, and the moment stops being theoretical.
bhagwad_gita::17.insight: It shifts attention from strategy to resolve: the side has chosen itself, and action is about to begin.

bhagwad_gita::18.verse_sanskrit: द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते । सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् ॥
bhagwad_gita::18.verse_hindi: हे राजन् श्रेष्ठ धनुषवाले काशिराज और महारथी शिखण्डी तथा धृष्टद्युम्न एवं राजा विराट और अजेय सात्यकि, राजा द्रुपद और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र तथा लम्बीलम्बी भुजाओंवाले सुभद्रापुत्र अभिमन्यु  इन सभी ने सब ओर से अलगअलग अपनेअपने शंख बजाये ॥
bhagwad_gita::18.english_translation: Drupada, Draupadi's sons, and mighty Abhimanyu each blew their conches separately, O lord of the earth.
bhagwad_gita::18.translation_literal: द्रुपदः (Drupada) / द्रौपदेयाः (Draupadi's sons) / च (and) / सर्वशः (all together) / पृथिवीपते (O lord of the earth) / सौभद्रः (Abhimanyu, son of Subhadra) / च (and) / महाबाहुः (mighty-armed) / शङ्खान् (conches) / दध्मुः (blew) / पृथक् पृथक् (separately each)
bhagwad_gita::18.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::18.essence: Allied resolve announces itself before the battle starts.
bhagwad_gita::18.simple_meaning: Drupada, Draupadi's sons, and Abhimanyu each blew their conches. The Pandava side answers the Kaurava side with a full display of strength.
bhagwad_gita::18.simple_insight: Strength can be announced before a single blow is struck.
bhagwad_gita::18.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, the Pandava allies answer the enemy's gathering with their own conches. Drupada, Draupadi's sons, and Abhimanyu sound their horns one by one, showing that Arjuna is not alone before the war begins.
bhagwad_gita::18.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet before you speak up against something wrong. Your voice may tremble, but the moment you join in, everyone knows you are not backing down.
bhagwad_gita::18.insight: It shifts attention from silent fear to visible resolve before action begins.

bhagwad_gita::19.verse_sanskrit: स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत् । नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन् ॥
bhagwad_gita::19.verse_hindi: पाण्डवसेना के शंखों के उस भयंकर शब्द ने आकाश और पृथ्वी को भी गुँजाते हुए अन्यायपूर्वक राज्य हड़पनेवाले दुर्योधन आदि के हृदय विदीर्ण कर दिये ॥
bhagwad_gita::19.english_translation: That terrible sound split the hearts of Dhritarashtra's side, echoing through sky and earth.
bhagwad_gita::19.translation_literal: सः (that) / घोषः (sound) / धार्तराष्ट्राणाम् (of Dhritarashtra's sons) / हृदयानि (hearts) / व्यदारयत् (split) / नभः (sky) / च (and) / पृथिवीम् (earth) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / तुमुलः (terrible, loud) / व्यनुनादयन् (resounding)
bhagwad_gita::19.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::19.essence: A single sound can break resolve before battle begins.
bhagwad_gita::19.simple_meaning: The loud blast from the Pandava army shook the Kaurava side so deeply that it felt like the sky and earth were trembling too.
bhagwad_gita::19.simple_insight: Some moments hit before any sword is raised. The body knows the battle has already begun.
bhagwad_gita::19.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, just after the Pandava horns sound, Sanjaya describes the effect on Duryodhana's side. The blast is so overwhelming that it seems to split their hearts and fill the whole field with dread before the fighting starts.
bhagwad_gita::19.modern_relevance: You hear the notification, read the message, and know everything has changed before you even reply. Some sounds announce a decision no one can undo.
bhagwad_gita::19.insight: It shifts attention from the action itself to its psychological impact on those who resist it.

bhagwad_gita::20.verse_sanskrit: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः । प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसंपाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः ॥
bhagwad_gita::20.verse_hindi: हे महीपते धृतराष्ट्र अब शस्त्रों के चलने की तैयारी हो ही रही थी कि उस समय अन्यायपूर्वक राज्य को धारण करनेवाले राजाओं और उनके साथियों को व्यवस्थितरूप से सामने खड़े हुए देखकर कपिध्वज पाण्डुपुत्र अर्जुन ने अपना गाण्डीव धनुष उठा लिया और अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण से ये वचन बोले ॥
bhagwad_gita::20.english_translation: Then, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra standing in battle order while the weapons were about to begin, Arjuna lifted his bow.
bhagwad_gita::20.translation_literal: अथ (then) / व्यवस्थितान् (arrayed, standing in order) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / धार्तराष्ट्रान् (the sons of Dhritarashtra) / कपिध्वजः (he whose banner bears Hanuman) / प्रवृत्ते (when begun) / शस्त्रसंपाते (the clash of weapons) / धनुः (bow) / उद्यम्य (lifting) / पाण्डवः (the son of Pandu)
bhagwad_gita::20.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::20.essence: The battle reaches its threshold, and action begins before words do.
bhagwad_gita::20.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees the opposing army ready for battle and raises his bow.
bhagwad_gita::20.simple_insight: The body moves toward action even when the mind is about to hesitate.
bhagwad_gita::20.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, the two armies stand ready. Sanjaya describes the exact instant before violence begins: Arjuna sees the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed before him and lifts Gandiva. This is the moment just before his inner collapse turns into speech.
bhagwad_gita::20.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that changes everything. Your hand is on the phone, your chest tight, and you know there is no taking it back.
bhagwad_gita::20.insight: It shows the threshold before decisive speech or action, when seeing clearly forces a response.

bhagwad_gita::21.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचहृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत ॥
bhagwad_gita::21.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे अच्युत दोनों सेनाओं के मध्य में मेरे रथ को आप तब तक खड़ा कीजिये, जब तक मैं युद्धक्षेत्र में खड़े हुए इन युद्ध की इच्छावालों को देख न लूँ कि इस युद्धरूप उद्योग में मुझे किनकिन के साथ युद्ध करना योग्य है ॥
bhagwad_gita::21.english_translation: Arjuna said: O Hrishikesha, place my chariot between the two armies, O Achyuta, until I can look at these men who wish to fight and see with whom I must battle in this war.
bhagwad_gita::21.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / हृषीकेशं (to Hrishikesha) / तदा (then) / वाक्यम् (words) / इदम् (this) / आह (said) / महीपते (O king) / सेनयोः (of the two armies) / उभयोः (both) / मध्ये (in the middle) / रथम् (chariot) / स्थापय (place) / मे (my) / अच्युत (O Achyuta)
bhagwad_gita::21.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::21.essence: Clear sight comes before decisive action.
bhagwad_gita::21.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to stop his chariot between the two armies so he can see who he must fight.
bhagwad_gita::21.simple_insight: Before a hard act, he chooses to look clearly instead of rushing forward.
bhagwad_gita::21.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, the battle is about to begin and Arjuna has already raised his bow. Then he asks Krishna to place the chariot between the armies, because he wants one clear look at the people he is expected to fight before the first strike.
bhagwad_gita::21.modern_relevance: You are one step from sending the message, signing the form, or walking away. Before the point of no return, Arjuna’s pause asks for one honest look.
bhagwad_gita::21.insight: It teaches you to pause before irreversible action and face the human reality of what you are about to do.

bhagwad_gita::22.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे अच्युत दोनों सेनाओं के मध्य में मेरे रथ को आप तब तक खड़ा कीजिये, जब तक मैं युद्धक्षेत्र में खड़े हुए इन युद्ध की इच्छावालों को देख न लूँ कि इस युद्धरूप उद्योग में मुझे किनकिनके साथ युद्ध करना योग्य है ॥
bhagwad_gita::22.english_translation: Arjuna said: O Achyuta, keep my chariot between the two armies until I can inspect these men standing here, eager for battle, and see with whom I must fight in this great struggle.
bhagwad_gita::22.translation_literal: यावत् (until) / एतान् (these) / निरीक्षे (I may inspect) / अहम् (I) / योद्धुकामान् (those desirous of fighting) / अवस्थितान् (standing) / कैः (with whom) / मया (by me) / सह (together with) / योद्धव्यम् (must be fought) / अस्मिन् (in this) / रणसमुद्यमे (war undertaking)
bhagwad_gita::22.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::22.essence: Clear seeing comes before irreversible action.
bhagwad_gita::22.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to hold the chariot still so he can look at the warriors and understand whom he must face.
bhagwad_gita::22.simple_insight: Before a hard fight, he wants to see clearly instead of rushing blindly.
bhagwad_gita::22.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, the two armies are lined up and Arjuna is still asking Krishna to place the chariot between them. He is not ready to strike yet; he wants one careful look at the people he may have to fight before the battle truly begins.
bhagwad_gita::22.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that will end a friendship, and your hand freezes over the button. Before acting, you need one clear look at what is really in front of you.
bhagwad_gita::22.insight: It shifts the mind from automatic action to deliberate seeing before commitment.

bhagwad_gita::23.verse_sanskrit: योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः । धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः ॥
bhagwad_gita::23.verse_hindi: दुष्टबुद्धि दुर्योधन का युद्ध में प्रिय करने की इच्छावाले जो ये राजालोग इस सेना में आये हुए हैं, युद्ध करने को उतावले हुए इन सबको मैं देख लूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::23.english_translation: I want to see those who have gathered here, eager to fight and wishing to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra.
bhagwad_gita::23.translation_literal: योत्स्यमानान् (those eager to fight) / अवेक्षे (I want to see) / अहम् (I) / ये (who) / एते (these) / अत्र (here) / समागताः (assembled) / धार्तराष्ट्रस्य (of Dhritarashtra’s son) / दुर्बुद्धेः (of the evil-minded) / युद्धे (in battle) / प्रियचिकीर्षवः (wishing to please)
bhagwad_gita::23.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::23.essence: Conflict becomes real when you look at the people involved.
bhagwad_gita::23.simple_meaning: Arjuna wants to inspect the warriors gathered on the opposite side, especially those fighting for Duryodhana.
bhagwad_gita::23.simple_insight: Before a hard choice, he looks directly at the people involved instead of hiding from the reality.
bhagwad_gita::23.detailed_meaning: Arjuna has asked Krishna to place the chariot between the armies. Now, in the charged silence before the battle, he wants to see the warriors who have come to support Duryodhana. This is the moment his hesitation turns into a direct look at the cost of war.
bhagwad_gita::23.modern_relevance: You pause before sending the message that will end a friendship. First you read the names again, face the people involved, and feel the weight of what is about to happen.
bhagwad_gita::23.insight: It shifts the mind from abstract conflict to the real human faces inside it.

bhagwad_gita::24.verse_sanskrit: संजय उवाचएवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::24.verse_hindi: संजय बोले  हे भरतवंशी राजन् निद्राविजयी अर्जुन के द्वारा इस तरह कहने पर अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण ने दोनों सेनाओं के मध्यभाग में पितामह भीष्म और आचार्य द्रोण के सामने तथा सम्पूर्ण राजाओं के सामने श्रेष्ठ रथ को खड़ा करके इस तरह कहा कि हे पार्थ इन इकट्ठे हुए कुरुवंशियोंको देख ॥
bhagwad_gita::24.english_translation: Sanjaya said: Spoken to thus by Gudakesha, Hrishikesha stationed the finest chariot between the two armies, in front of Bhishma, Drona, and all the kings.
bhagwad_gita::24.translation_literal: संजय उवाच (Sanjaya said) / एवम् (thus) / उक्तः (spoken to) / हृषीकेशः (Hrishikesha) / गुडाकेशेन (by Gudakesha) / भारत (O Bharata) / सेनयोः (of the armies) / उभयोः (of both) / मध्ये (in the middle) / स्थापयित्वा (having placed) / रथोत्तमम् (the finest chariot)
bhagwad_gita::24.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::24.essence: The chariot is placed where choice becomes unavoidable.
bhagwad_gita::24.simple_meaning: Krishna places Arjuna’s chariot between the two armies, right where the decision must happen.
bhagwad_gita::24.simple_insight: The pause before action matters. Clarity begins when you face the real center of the conflict.
bhagwad_gita::24.detailed_meaning: Sanjaya describes the battlefield moment after Arjuna asks Krishna to place the chariot between the armies. Krishna drives it into the space before Bhishma, Drona, and the gathered kings, setting up the crisis that will force Arjuna’s deepest choice.
bhagwad_gita::24.modern_relevance: You walk into the meeting, sit between two sides, and everyone waits for your answer. The real pressure begins only when the conflict is no longer abstract.
bhagwad_gita::24.insight: It shifts attention from the setup to the moment of direct confrontation.

bhagwad_gita::25.verse_sanskrit: भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम् । उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति ॥
bhagwad_gita::25.verse_hindi: संजय बोले  हे भरतवंशी राजन् निद्राविजयी अर्जुन के द्वारा इस तरह कहने पर अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण ने दोनों सेनाओं के मध्यभाग में पितामह भीष्म और आचार्य द्रोण के सामने तथा सम्पूर्ण राजाओं के सामने श्रेष्ठ रथको खड़ा करके इस तरह कहा कि हे पार्थ इन इकट्ठे हुए कुरुवंशियोंको देख ॥
bhagwad_gita::25.english_translation: Standing before Bhishma, Drona, and all the rulers, Krishna said, "O Partha, behold these assembled Kurus."
bhagwad_gita::25.translation_literal: भीष्म-द्रोण-प्रमुखतः (in front of Bhishma and Drona) / सर्वेषाम् (of all) / च (and) / महीक्षिताम् (of kings) / उवाच (said) / पार्थ (O Partha) / पश्य (behold) / एतान् (these) / समवेतान् (assembled) / कुरून् (Kurus) / इति (thus)
bhagwad_gita::25.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::25.essence: Seeing the people involved makes denial impossible.
bhagwad_gita::25.simple_meaning: Krishna positions Arjuna’s chariot between the armies and asks him to look at the gathered Kurus, including Bhishma, Drona, and the kings.
bhagwad_gita::25.simple_insight: Before the conflict becomes action, Arjuna is made to face the people he must fight.
bhagwad_gita::25.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna drives Arjuna’s chariot into the space between both armies. He stops before Bhishma, Drona, and the gathered kings, and tells Arjuna to look closely. This moment forces the warrior to see the human cost before the battle begins.
bhagwad_gita::25.modern_relevance: You stand at the edge of a hard message, and the people it will hurt are all in front of you. Before you speak or act, you have to look directly.
bhagwad_gita::25.insight: It shifts the mind from abstract conflict to direct seeing of real people and real stakes.

bhagwad_gita::26.verse_hindi: उसके बाद पृथानन्दन अर्जुनने उन दोनों ही सेनाओंमें स्थित पिताओंको, पितामहोंको, आचार्योंको, मामाओंको, भाइयोंको, पुत्रोंको, पौत्रोंको तथा मित्रोंको, ससुरोंको और सुहृदोंको भी देखा ॥
bhagwad_gita::26.english_translation: Then Arjuna, son of Pritha, saw fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, friends, fathers-in-law, and well-wishers standing there.
bhagwad_gita::26.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / अपश्यत् (saw) / स्थितान् (standing) / पार्थः (Arjuna, son of Pritha) / पितृ़न् (fathers) / अथ (also) / पितामहान् (grandfathers) / आचार्यान् (teachers) / मातुलान् (maternal uncles) / भ्रातृ़न् (brothers) / पुत्रान् (sons) / पौत्रान् (grandsons) / सखीन् (friends) / तथा (and so on)
bhagwad_gita::26.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::26.simple_meaning: Arjuna looks across the battlefield and recognizes his own relatives and teachers among the enemy ranks.
bhagwad_gita::26.simple_insight: The enemy is no longer abstract. The sight of familiar faces turns battle into grief.
bhagwad_gita::26.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna has placed Arjuna between the armies. As Arjuna looks, he sees fathers, grandfathers, teachers, cousins, sons, and friends on both sides. The war becomes personal in a single glance.
bhagwad_gita::26.modern_relevance: You open a group chat before a painful family decision and see every name tied to memory. The choice is no longer theoretical; it cuts through your own relationships.
bhagwad_gita::26.insight: It shifts the mind from strategy to human cost.

bhagwad_gita::27.verse_sanskrit: श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि । तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान् ॥
bhagwad_gita::27.verse_hindi: अपनीअपनी जगह पर स्थित उन सम्पूर्ण बान्धवों को देखकर वे कुन्तीनन्दन अर्जुन अत्यन्त कायरता से युक्त होकर विषाद करते हुए ये वचन बोले ॥
bhagwad_gita::27.english_translation: Seeing all his relatives standing there, Arjuna sank into grief and spoke in fear.
bhagwad_gita::27.translation_literal: श्वशुरान् (fathers-in-law) / सुहृदः (well-wishers) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / सेनयोः (of the armies) / उभयोः (of both) / अपि (also) / तान् (those) / समीक्ष्य (having seen) / सः (he) / कौन्तेयः (son of Kunti) / सर्वान् (all) / बन्धून् (relatives) / अवस्थितान् (standing)
bhagwad_gita::27.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::27.essence: The battle becomes unbearable when every side is family.
bhagwad_gita::27.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees every kind of relative on both sides of the battlefield and is overwhelmed with grief.
bhagwad_gita::27.simple_insight: Seeing familiar faces can make a fight feel unbearable.
bhagwad_gita::27.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna looks again and sees not strangers, but fathers-in-law, friends, and relatives standing in both armies. That sight deepens his collapse and prepares the words of despair that follow.
bhagwad_gita::27.modern_relevance: You open a family group chat and realize the conflict has names and faces. The issue is no longer abstract, and your stomach drops.
bhagwad_gita::27.insight: It turns a distant conflict into a personal wound, making action emotionally impossible.

bhagwad_gita::28.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचकृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::28.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे कृष्ण युद्ध की इच्छावाले इस कुटुम्बसमुदाय को अपने सामने उपस्थित देखकर मेरे अङ्ग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुख सूख रहा है तथा मेरे शरीर में कँपकँपी आ रही है एवं रोंगटे खड़े हो रहे हैं ।  हाथ से गाण्डीव धनुष गिर रहा है और त्वचा भी जल रही है ।  मेरा मन भ्रमितसा हो रहा है और मैं खड़े रहने में भी असमर्थ हो रहा हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::28.english_translation: Arjuna said: Seeing my own people gathered here, eager for battle, I am overcome with pity and grief, O Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::28.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / कृपया (by compassion or pity) / परया (supreme) / आविष्टः (overcome) / विषीदन् (grieving) / इदम् (this) / अब्रवीत् (spoke) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / इमम् (this) / स्वजनम् (my own people) / कृष्ण (O Krishna) / युयुत्सुम् (desiring to fight) / समुपस्थितम् (assembled before me)
bhagwad_gita::28.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::28.essence: Compassion can stop the warrior before the first arrow flies.
bhagwad_gita::28.simple_meaning: Arjuna tells Krishna that seeing his own relatives gathered for battle has overwhelmed him with grief and pity.
bhagwad_gita::28.simple_insight: Love can make violence feel unbearable, even when duty is waiting.
bhagwad_gita::28.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has already recognized fathers, teachers, cousins, and friends on both sides. Now, seeing his own people ready to fight, he collapses into grief. This verse marks the moment his inner conflict becomes impossible to hide.
bhagwad_gita::28.modern_relevance: You open a message thread and realize the argument will wound people you love. Your body tightens before your mind can defend the choice.
bhagwad_gita::28.insight: It shifts the reader from abstract conflict to the human cost hidden inside it.

bhagwad_gita::29.verse_sanskrit: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥
bhagwad_gita::29.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे कृष्ण युद्ध की इच्छावाले इस कुटुम्बसमुदाय को अपने सामने उपस्थित देखकर मेरे अङ्ग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुख सूख रहा है तथा मेरे शरीर में कँपकँपी आ रही है एवं रोंगटे खड़े हो रहे हैं ।  हाथ से गाण्डीव धनुष गिर रहा है और त्वचा भी जल रही है ।  मेरा मन भ्रमितसा हो रहा है और मैं खड़े रहने में भी असमर्थ हो रहा हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::29.english_translation: My limbs are failing, my mouth is drying up, my body trembles, and my hair stands on end.
bhagwad_gita::29.translation_literal: सीदन्ति (are failing) / मम (my) / गात्राणि (limbs) / मुखं (mouth) / च (and) / परिशुष्यति (dries up) / वेपथुः (trembling) / च (and) / शरीरे (in the body) / मे (my) / रोम-हर्षः (standing of hair) / च (and) / जायते (arises)
bhagwad_gita::29.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::29.essence: The body reveals fear before the mind can explain it.
bhagwad_gita::29.simple_meaning: Arjuna's body is breaking under the pressure of what he sees. His strength, speech, and composure are all slipping away at once.
bhagwad_gita::29.simple_insight: Overwhelm shows up in the body before it becomes a decision.
bhagwad_gita::29.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands before his own relatives and teachers. Seeing them in the opposing army, his body begins to fail: his limbs weaken, his mouth dries, and fear shakes him. This verse deepens his collapse before Krishna answers.
bhagwad_gita::29.modern_relevance: You open the message you were dreading, and your hands go cold before you even reply. The body often knows the cost of a hard truth first.
bhagwad_gita::29.insight: It teaches you to notice distress as a physical signal, not just a mental opinion.

bhagwad_gita::30.verse_sanskrit: गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::30.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे कृष्ण युद्ध की इच्छावाले इस कुटुम्बसमुदाय को अपने सामने उपस्थित देखकर मेरे अङ्ग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुख सूख रहा है तथा मेरे शरीर में कँपकँपी आ रही है एवं रोंगटे खड़े हो रहे हैं ।  हाथ से गाण्डीव धनुष गिर रहा है और त्वचा भी जल रही है ।  मेरा मन भ्रमितसा हो रहा है और मैं खड़े रहने में भी असमर्थ हो रहा हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::30.english_translation: My bow slips from my hand. My skin burns. I cannot stand steady, and my mind reels.
bhagwad_gita::30.translation_literal: गाण्डीवम् (the Gandiva bow) / स्रंसते (slips) / हस्तात् (from the hand) / त्वक् (skin) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / परिदह्यते (burns) / न (not) / च (and) / शक्नोमि (I am able) / अवस्थातुम् (to stand) / भ्रमति (reels) / इव (like) / च (and) / मे (my) / मनः (mind)
bhagwad_gita::30.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::30.essence: Fear strips away control before a single arrow is released.
bhagwad_gita::30.simple_meaning: Arjuna is overwhelmed by fear and grief. His body shakes, his bow slips, and he cannot steady his mind or even stand.
bhagwad_gita::30.simple_insight: Overwhelm can make even strength feel useless. The body and mind collapse together when fear takes over.
bhagwad_gita::30.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands before the armies and begins to break down. His bow, Gandiva, slips from his hand, his skin burns, and his mind spins. This is the moment his crisis becomes physical.
bhagwad_gita::30.modern_relevance: You are about to speak in a meeting, but your throat tightens and your hands shake. The body knows before the mind admits it: this is too much right now.
bhagwad_gita::30.insight: It shows how inner collapse first appears as bodily instability, not just thought.

bhagwad_gita::31.verse_sanskrit: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव । न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ॥
bhagwad_gita::31.verse_hindi: हे केशव मैं लक्षणों  शकुनों को भी विपरीत देख रहा हूँ और युद्ध में स्वजनोंको मारकर श्रेय लाभ भी नहीं देख रहा हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::31.english_translation: O Keshava, I see only inauspicious signs, and I see no good in killing my own people in battle.
bhagwad_gita::31.translation_literal: निमित्तानि (signs) / च (and) / पश्यामि (I see) / विपरीतानि (opposite, inauspicious) / केशव (O Keshava) / न (not) / च (and) / श्रेयः (good, welfare) / अनुपश्यामि (I see) / हत्वा (having killed) / स्वजनम् (my own people) / आहवे (in battle)
bhagwad_gita::31.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::31.essence: A victory that destroys your own people is not worth having.
bhagwad_gita::31.simple_meaning: Arjuna says he sees bad signs and no real good in killing his own relatives in battle.
bhagwad_gita::31.simple_insight: When the heart is already broken, even victory can look empty.
bhagwad_gita::31.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen before the two armies. After feeling his body fail and his mind shake, he tells Krishna that the signs around him feel wrong and that killing his own kin cannot lead to anything good.
bhagwad_gita::31.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that will end a friendship, and every detail feels wrong. The mind keeps warning: forcing this will not make life better.
bhagwad_gita::31.insight: It shifts attention from winning to the moral cost of winning.

bhagwad_gita::32.verse_sanskrit: न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च । किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ॥
bhagwad_gita::32.verse_hindi: हे कृष्ण मैं न तो विजय चाहता हूँ, न राज्य चाहता हूँ और न सुखों को ही चाहता हूँ ।  हे गोविन्द हमलोगों को राज्य से क्या लाभ भोगों से क्या लाभ अथवा जीने से भी क्या लाभ ॥
bhagwad_gita::32.english_translation: I do not desire victory, Krishna, nor kingdom, nor pleasures. What use is kingdom to us, Govinda? What use are pleasures or even life?
bhagwad_gita::32.translation_literal: न काङ्क्षे (I do not desire) / विजयम् (victory) / कृष्ण (Krishna) / न (nor) / च (and) / राज्यम् (kingdom) / सुखानि (pleasures) / च (and) / किम् (what) / नः (to us) / राज्येन (with kingdom) / गोविन्द (Govinda) / किम् (what) / भोगैः (with pleasures) / जीवितेन (with life) / वा (or)
bhagwad_gita::32.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::32.essence: Victory means nothing when the price is the destruction of what you love.
bhagwad_gita::32.simple_meaning: Arjuna says he no longer wants victory, a kingdom, pleasure, or even life itself. The fight has lost its meaning for him.
bhagwad_gita::32.simple_insight: When the goal feels hollow, even success stops mattering.
bhagwad_gita::32.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna stands collapsed before Krishna. After seeing his own relatives as enemies, he rejects victory, rule, pleasure, and even survival itself. This verse deepens his crisis and shows how completely his desire to fight has broken.
bhagwad_gita::32.modern_relevance: You are staring at the email that could save your career, but it asks you to betray yourself. Suddenly the promotion, the applause, even the job feel empty.
bhagwad_gita::32.insight: It exposes the moment when outer success can no longer justify inner collapse.

bhagwad_gita::33.verse_sanskrit: येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च । त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ॥
bhagwad_gita::33.verse_hindi: जिनके लिये हमारी राज्य, भोग और सुखकी इच्छा है, वे ही ये सब अपने प्राणों की और धन की आशा का त्याग करके युद्ध में खड़े हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::33.english_translation: Those for whom we wanted kingdom, pleasures, and comfort stand here in battle, ready to give up life and wealth.
bhagwad_gita::33.translation_literal: येषाम् (for whom) / अर्थे (for the sake) / काङ्क्षितम् (desired) / नः (by us) / राज्यम् (kingdom) / भोगाः (pleasures) / सुखानि (comforts) / च (and) / ते (they) / इमे (these) / अवस्थिताḥ (standing) / युद्धे (in battle) / प्राणान् (lives) / त्यक्त्वा (giving up) / धनानि (wealth) / च (and)
bhagwad_gita::33.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::33.essence: The prize is empty when the people attached to it stand in the line of fire.
bhagwad_gita::33.simple_meaning: The people Arjuna hoped to protect and enjoy life with are standing on the battlefield, willing to risk everything. That makes his refusal to fight even heavier.
bhagwad_gita::33.simple_insight: Grief deepens when the people you would fight for are the same people you might have to fight.
bhagwad_gita::33.detailed_meaning: Arjuna is still frozen between the two armies on Kurukshetra. He looks at the relatives, teachers, and elders on the opposite side and realizes that the kingdom he once wanted is tied to their lives. That recognition sharpens his collapse.
bhagwad_gita::33.modern_relevance: You open a family group chat and see the people you love lined up on opposite sides of a painful inheritance dispute. The choice is no longer abstract; every option cuts into someone familiar.
bhagwad_gita::33.insight: It turns the battle from a political contest into a personal wound, making action feel unbearable.

bhagwad_gita::34.verse_sanskrit: आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः । मातुलाः श्चशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा ॥
bhagwad_gita::34.verse_hindi: आचार्य, पिता, पुत्र और उसी प्रकार पितामह, मामा, ससुर, पौत्र, साले तथा अन्य जितने भी सम्बन्धी हैं, मुझ पर प्रहार करने पर भी मैं इनको मारना नहीं चाहता, और हे मधुसूदन मुझे त्रिलोकी का राज्य मिलता हो, तो भी मैं इनको मारना नहीं चाहता, फिर पृथ्वी के लिये तो मैं इनको मारूँ ही क्या ॥
bhagwad_gita::34.english_translation: Teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other relatives.
bhagwad_gita::34.translation_literal: आचार्याः (teachers) / पितरः (fathers) / पुत्राः (sons) / तथा एव च (and likewise) / पितामहाः (grandfathers) / मातुलाः (maternal uncles) / श्चशुराः (fathers-in-law) / पौत्राः (grandsons) / श्यालाः (brothers-in-law) / सम्बन्धिनः (relatives) / तथा (and so on)
bhagwad_gita::34.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::34.essence: Blood ties make victory feel like loss.
bhagwad_gita::34.simple_meaning: Arjuna lists the family members and relatives on both sides of the battlefield. He is overwhelmed because the people he would have to fight are his own kin.
bhagwad_gita::34.simple_insight: The conflict feels unbearable because the enemy is not abstract — it is family.
bhagwad_gita::34.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna looks across the battlefield and sees not strangers but teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, uncles, in-laws, and cousins. The war has become a family catastrophe, and his refusal to strike is growing sharper.
bhagwad_gita::34.modern_relevance: You open a message thread and realize the argument is no longer about the issue. It is about people you love, and hurting them now feels impossible.
bhagwad_gita::34.insight: It shifts the mind from winning a conflict to facing the human cost of victory.

bhagwad_gita::35.verse_sanskrit: एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन । अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ॥
bhagwad_gita::35.verse_hindi: आचार्य, पिता, पुत्र और उसी प्रकार पितामह, मामा, ससुर, पौत्र, साले तथा अन्य जितने भी सम्बन्धी हैं, मुझपर प्रहार करने पर भी मैं इनको मारना नहीं चाहता, और हे मधुसूदन मुझे त्रिलोकी का राज्य मिलता हो, तो भी मैं इनको मारना नहीं चाहता, फिर पृथ्वीके लिये तो मैं इनको मारूँ ही क्या ॥
bhagwad_gita::35.english_translation: I do not want to kill these people, even if they kill me, O Madhusudana. Not even for the rule of the three worlds, much less for the earth.
bhagwad_gita::35.translation_literal: एतान् (these) / न (not) / हन्तुम् (to kill) / इच्छामि (I want) / घ्नतः (of the one killing) / अपि (even) / मधुसूदन (O Madhusudana) / अपि (even) / त्रैलोक्य-राज्यस्य (of the rule of the three worlds) / हेतोः (for the sake) / किं (what) / नु (indeed) / मही-कृते (for the earth)
bhagwad_gita::35.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::35.essence: No prize can justify killing what is sacred to you.
bhagwad_gita::35.simple_meaning: Arjuna says he cannot bring himself to kill his own relatives, even for power over all three worlds, let alone for a kingdom on earth.
bhagwad_gita::35.simple_insight: Some choices feel wrong even when they promise everything. The heart can refuse what ambition wants.
bhagwad_gita::35.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna sees teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, and in-laws standing opposite him. His bow has not yet fallen completely, but his resolve is breaking. He tells Krishna that no kingdom could justify killing them.
bhagwad_gita::35.modern_relevance: You are one signature away from harming a family member's future, and the reward is huge. Something in you knows the price is too high.
bhagwad_gita::35.insight: It shifts the mind from winning at any cost to measuring the moral cost of victory.

bhagwad_gita::36.verse_sanskrit: निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन । पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::36.verse_hindi: हे जनार्दन इन धृतराष्ट्रसम्बन्धियों को मारकर हमलोगों को क्या प्रसन्नता होगी इन आततायियों को मारने से तो हमें पाप ही लगेगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::36.english_translation: O Janardana, what joy would come to us by killing these sons of Dhritarashtra? Killing these aggressors would only bring us sin.
bhagwad_gita::36.translation_literal: निहत्य (by killing) / धार्तराष्ट्रान् (the sons of Dhritarashtra) / नः (to us) / का (what) / प्रीतिः (joy) / स्यात् (would be) / जनार्दन (O Janardana) / पापम् (sin) / एव (only) / आश्रयेत् (would come upon) / अस्मान् (us) / हत्वा (having killed) / एतान् (these) / आततायिनः (aggressors)
bhagwad_gita::36.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::36.essence: Violence against kin brings no joy; it only deepens the wound.
bhagwad_gita::36.simple_meaning: Arjuna says that killing his own relatives will bring no happiness and will only stain the killers with wrongdoing.
bhagwad_gita::36.simple_insight: Moral clarity can feel painful, but it keeps you from confusing victory with peace.
bhagwad_gita::36.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna sees the war’s real cost: teachers, relatives, and family on both sides. Faced with the sons of Dhritarashtra, he says killing them would bring no joy and would burden the killers with wrongdoing.
bhagwad_gita::36.modern_relevance: You are about to expose a lie that will break a family dinner open. The room goes silent, and you realize winning the argument would cost something deeper than being right.
bhagwad_gita::36.insight: It shifts the mind from triumph to moral consequence before taking irreversible action.

bhagwad_gita::37.verse_sanskrit: तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान् । स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥
bhagwad_gita::37.verse_hindi: इसलिये अपने बान्धव इन धृतराष्ट्रसम्बन्धियों को मारने के लिये हम योग्य नहीं हैं क्योंकि हे माधव अपने कुटुम्बियों को मारकर हम कैसे सुखी होंगे ॥
bhagwad_gita::37.english_translation: Therefore, we are not fit to kill our own kinsmen, the sons of Dhritarashtra. How could we be happy after killing our relatives, O Madhava?
bhagwad_gita::37.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) / न अर्हाः (not fit) / वयम् (we) / हन्तुम् (to kill) / धार्तराष्ट्रान् (the sons of Dhritarashtra) / स्व-बान्धवान् (our own relatives) / स्व-जनम् (our own people) / हि (indeed) / कथम् (how) / हत्वा (having killed) / सुखिनः (happy) / स्याम (we would be) / माधव (O Madhava)
bhagwad_gita::37.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::37.simple_meaning: Arjuna says the Kaurava side are his own relatives, so killing them would not bring happiness.
bhagwad_gita::37.simple_insight: You can feel the cost of violence before you act, and that honesty matters.
bhagwad_gita::37.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna looks at the men he is meant to fight and sees family, not enemies. Krishna is pressing him toward action, but Arjuna's heart is breaking under the thought of killing his own kin.
bhagwad_gita::37.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that will end a friendship. Before you hit send, you feel the weight of what cannot be undone.
bhagwad_gita::37.insight: It shifts the mind from winning to seeing the human cost of action.

bhagwad_gita::38.verse_sanskrit: यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः । कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::38.verse_hindi: यद्यपि लोभ के कारण जिनका विवेकविचार लुप्त हो गया है, ऐसे ये दुर्योधन आदि कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को और मित्रों के साथ द्वेष करने से होनेवाले पाप को नहीं देखते, तो भी हे जनार्दन कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को ठीकठीक जाननेवाले हमलोग इस पाप से निवृत्त होने का विचार क्यों न करें ॥
bhagwad_gita::38.english_translation: Though greed has blinded them, they do not see the fault in destroying a family or the wrong in betraying friends.
bhagwad_gita::38.translation_literal: यद्यपि (though) / एते (these) / न पश्यन्ति (do not see) / लोभोपहतचेतसः (those whose minds are overcome by greed) / कुलक्षयकृतं (caused by destruction of the family) / दोषम् (fault) / मित्रद्रोहे (in betrayal of friends) / च (and) / पातकम् (wrongdoing)
bhagwad_gita::38.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::38.essence: Greed blinds people to the damage they are causing.
bhagwad_gita::38.simple_meaning: Greed has made these people blind. They cannot see the harm in destroying their own family or betraying friends.
bhagwad_gita::38.simple_insight: Clear seeing can survive even in a room full of pressure and blindness.
bhagwad_gita::38.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna keeps arguing against war while the armies wait. He points out that Duryodhana and his side are blinded by greed and cannot see the ruin they are causing, which deepens Arjuna’s refusal to fight his own kin.
bhagwad_gita::38.modern_relevance: You’re in a family meeting where money has turned relatives against each other. Everyone speaks loudly, but no one sees the damage being done until it is too late.
bhagwad_gita::38.insight: It shifts attention from winning the argument to seeing the moral cost of greed-driven action.

bhagwad_gita::39.verse_sanskrit: कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम् । कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन ॥
bhagwad_gita::39.verse_hindi: यद्यपि लोभ के कारण जिनका विवेकविचार लुप्त हो गया है, ऐसे ये दुर्योधन आदि कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को और मित्रों के साथ द्वेष करने से होनेवाले पाप को नहीं देखते, तो भी हे जनार्दन कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को ठीकठीक जाननेवाले हमलोग इस पाप से निवृत्त होनेका विचार क्यों न करें ॥
bhagwad_gita::39.english_translation: Why should we not turn away from this sin, when we clearly see the fault in destroying the family, O Janardana?
bhagwad_gita::39.translation_literal: कथं (how) / न (not) / ज्ञेयम् (to be known) / अस्माभिः (by us) / पापात् (from sin) / अस्मात् (from this) / निवर्तितुम् (to turn back) / कुलक्षयकृतम् (caused by family-destruction) / दोषम् (fault) / प्रपश्यद्भिः (by those clearly seeing) / जनार्दन (O Janardana)
bhagwad_gita::39.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::39.essence: Clear sight makes withdrawal from harm the only sane choice.
bhagwad_gita::39.simple_meaning: Arjuna says that because he can see the harm caused by destroying the family, he and his side should turn away from this wrong action.
bhagwad_gita::39.simple_insight: Seeing the damage clearly makes hesitation feel responsible, not weak.
bhagwad_gita::39.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is no longer thinking like a warrior eager for victory. He sees that killing relatives will destroy the family itself, and he asks Krishna why they should not step back from such wrongdoing.
bhagwad_gita::39.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that will break a family apart. The facts are clear, and so is the damage. This verse is the moment you ask whether continuing is worth becoming the person who did it.
bhagwad_gita::39.insight: It shifts the mind from winning to refusing harm once the cost is understood.

bhagwad_gita::40.verse_sanskrit: कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः । धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत ॥
bhagwad_gita::40.verse_hindi: कुल का क्षय होने पर सदा से चलते आये कुलधर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं और धर्म का नाश होनेपर बचे हुए सम्पूर्ण कुल को अधर्म दबा लेता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::40.english_translation: When a family falls apart, its ancient duties disappear. When duty is lost, wrongdoing overtakes the whole family.
bhagwad_gita::40.translation_literal: कुलक्षये (on the destruction of the family) / प्रणश्यन्ति (are destroyed) / कुलधर्माः (family duties) / सनातनाः (ancient, eternal) । / धर्मे (when duty) / नष्टे (is destroyed) / कुलम् (the family) / कृत्स्नम् (entire) / अधर्मः (wrongdoing) / अभिभवति (overpowers) / उत (indeed)
bhagwad_gita::40.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::40.essence: Destroy the family, and the moral order inside it collapses.
bhagwad_gita::40.simple_meaning: When a family is broken, its long-standing duties disappear. Once duty is gone, wrongdoing spreads through the whole family.
bhagwad_gita::40.simple_insight: A broken structure does not stay neutral for long; it quickly trains people toward harm.
bhagwad_gita::40.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna looks beyond the fight and sees a larger collapse. If the Kuru family is destroyed, its old duties will vanish, and the disorder of war will spread through everything that remains.
bhagwad_gita::40.modern_relevance: A household where promises keep getting broken does not stay stable for long. Soon the children learn the chaos as normal, and everyone starts living by damage control instead of responsibility.
bhagwad_gita::40.insight: It shifts attention from immediate victory to the long-term moral cost of breaking inherited obligations.

bhagwad_gita::41.verse_sanskrit: अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः । स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः ॥
bhagwad_gita::41.verse_hindi: हे कृष्ण अधर्म के अधिक बढ़ जाने से कुल की स्त्रियाँ दूषित हो जाती हैं और हे वार्ष्णेय स्त्रियों के दूषित होने पर वर्णसंकर पैदा हो जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::41.english_translation: When lawlessness grows, the women of the family are corrupted. When women are corrupted, mixed social disorder is born.
bhagwad_gita::41.translation_literal: अधर्माभिभवात् (from the dominance of lawlessness) / कृष्ण (O Krishna) / प्रदुष्यन्ति (become corrupted) / कुलस्त्रियः (family women) / स्त्रीषु (when women) / दुष्टासु (are corrupted) / वार्ष्णेय (O descendant of Vrishni) / जायते (is born) / वर्णसङ्करः (mixed disorder of social order)
bhagwad_gita::41.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::41.essence: When order breaks, the damage spreads into future generations.
bhagwad_gita::41.simple_meaning: Arjuna fears that when lawlessness takes over a family, women are harmed and social order breaks down further.
bhagwad_gita::41.simple_insight: Moral collapse feels frightening because it spreads beyond one person and damages the whole community.
bhagwad_gita::41.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is no longer thinking like a warrior. He is imagining the collapse of family order, the loss of restraint, and the damage that war may bring to future generations. This verse continues his fearful argument against fighting.
bhagwad_gita::41.modern_relevance: A family argument turns ugly, and suddenly everyone is carrying the damage. One harsh decision can echo into children, trust, and the whole home.
bhagwad_gita::41.insight: It shifts attention from personal victory to the wider social cost of destructive action.

bhagwad_gita::42.verse_sanskrit: सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च । पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::42.verse_hindi: वर्णसंकर कुलघातियों को और कुल को नरक में ले जानेवाला ही होता है ।  श्राद्ध और तर्पण न मिलने से इन कुलघातियों के पितर भी अपने स्थान से गिर जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::42.english_translation: Mixed lineage leads the destroyers of family to ruin, and their ancestors fall because offerings of food and water stop.
bhagwad_gita::42.translation_literal: सङ्करः (mixed lineage) / नरकाय (for ruin) / एव (indeed) / कुलघ्नानाम् (of family-destroyers) / कुलस्य (of the family) / च (and) / पतन्ति (fall) / पितरः (ancestors) / हि (indeed) / एषाम् (of these) / लुप्त (stopped) / पिण्ड (food offering) / उदक (water offering) / क्रियाः (rites)
bhagwad_gita::42.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::42.essence: Breaking family order is imagined as ruin that reaches even the dead.
bhagwad_gita::42.simple_meaning: Arjuna says that destroying family order creates ruin for the family and even harms the ancestors, because the rites that support them stop.
bhagwad_gita::42.simple_insight: Fear of collapse can make a person see one violent choice as a disaster for generations.
bhagwad_gita::42.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still listing the consequences of civil war. He argues that when family lines are broken, traditional rites stop, social order collapses, and even the dead are thought to suffer. The verse deepens his refusal to fight.
bhagwad_gita::42.modern_relevance: You are about to cut off a relationship, and the mind races ahead to every harm it might cause. In that panic, one decision starts to feel like it will damage an entire family line.
bhagwad_gita::42.insight: It shows how moral panic turns consequences into a chain of fear, making action feel spiritually catastrophic.

bhagwad_gita::43.verse_sanskrit: दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः । उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::43.verse_hindi: इन वर्णसंकर पैदा करनेवाले दोषोंसे कुलघातियों के सदा से चलते आये कुलधर्म और जातिधर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::43.english_translation: Because of these faults that create mixed social order, the eternal duties of family and community are destroyed.
bhagwad_gita::43.translation_literal: दोषैः (by faults) / एतैः (these) / कुलघ्नानाम् (of family-destroyers) / वर्णसङ्करकारकैः (causing mixed social order) / उत्साद्यन्ते (are destroyed) / जातिधर्माः (community duties) / कुलधर्माः (family duties) / च (and) / शाश्वताः (eternal)
bhagwad_gita::43.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::43.essence: When conduct breaks, the inherited order that protects everyone breaks too.
bhagwad_gita::43.simple_meaning: Arjuna says that when family lines break down, long-standing duties within the family and society are destroyed.
bhagwad_gita::43.simple_insight: A collapse in conduct spreads outward, erasing the habits that hold a community together.
bhagwad_gita::43.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna keeps listing the damage he fears from war. After warning about mixed social order and the fall of ancestors, he says these faults destroy the ancient duties that families and communities have preserved for generations.
bhagwad_gita::43.modern_relevance: A household that normalises cruelty or secrecy does not stay contained. The habits spread, and soon even the basic rules that kept everyone steady start disappearing.
bhagwad_gita::43.insight: It shifts attention from one wrong act to the wider damage it can do to shared responsibility.

bhagwad_gita::44.verse_sanskrit: उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन । नरकेऽनियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम ॥
bhagwad_gita::44.verse_hindi: हे जनार्दन जिनके कुलधर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं, उन मनुष्यों का बहुत काल तक नरकों में वापस होता है, ऐसा हम सुनते आये हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::44.english_translation: O Janardana, we have always heard that those whose family duties are destroyed dwell long in a lower realm.
bhagwad_gita::44.translation_literal: उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणाम् (of those whose family duties are destroyed) / मनुष्याणाम् (of people) / जनार्दन (O Janardana) / नरके (in a lower realm) / अनियतं (for an indefinite time) / वासः (dwelling) / भवति (there is) / इति (thus) / अनुशुश्रुम (we have heard)
bhagwad_gita::44.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::44.essence: Breaking family duty brings suffering that lasts beyond one lifetime.
bhagwad_gita::44.simple_meaning: Arjuna says he has heard that people who destroy family duties end up suffering for a long time in a lower realm.
bhagwad_gita::44.simple_insight: The fear is not abstract anymore. He feels the cost of war reaching into the family line.
bhagwad_gita::44.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna keeps listing the consequences of fighting his own kin. After warning that family order will collapse, he recalls a grim teaching: when family duties are destroyed, people suffer in a lower realm for a long time. This deepens his refusal to fight.
bhagwad_gita::44.modern_relevance: You are about to sign something that will hurt your own family later. The short-term win looks smaller when you can already see the damage spreading.
bhagwad_gita::44.insight: It shifts the mind from immediate gain to the long shadow of broken obligations.

bhagwad_gita::45.verse_sanskrit: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम् । यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::45.verse_hindi: यह बड़े आश्चर्य और खेद की बात है कि हमलोग बड़ा भारी पाप करने का निश्चय कर बैठे हैं, जो कि राज्य और सुख के लोभ से अपने स्वजनों को मारने के लिये तैयार हो गये हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::45.english_translation: Alas, we have resolved to commit a grave wrong—driven by greed for kingdom and pleasure, we are ready to kill our own kin.
bhagwad_gita::45.translation_literal: अहो बत (alas indeed) / महत्पापं (great sin / grave wrong) / कर्तुं (to do) / व्यवसिता (resolved) / वयम् (we) / यत् (that) / राज्यसुखलोभेन (by greed for kingdom-pleasure) / हन्तुं (to kill) / स्वजनम् (one's own people / kin) / उद्यताः (prepared / ready)
bhagwad_gita::45.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::45.essence: Greed can make even victory feel like a crime.
bhagwad_gita::45.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees the war as a terrible wrong. He feels they are driven by greed for power and pleasure, and ready to kill their own relatives.
bhagwad_gita::45.simple_insight: A clear conscience can appear even in the middle of confusion.
bhagwad_gita::45.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna looks at the armies and recoils. The fight is no longer about victory; it feels like kin-killing for power and comfort. This verse captures the moment his moral horror becomes explicit.
bhagwad_gita::45.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that will break a family apart, and you can feel the wrongness before your finger moves. That hesitation is not weakness.
bhagwad_gita::45.insight: It shifts the mind from winning at any cost to noticing the moral price of winning.

bhagwad_gita::46.verse_sanskrit: यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः । धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::46.verse_hindi: अगर ये हाथों में शस्त्रअस्त्र लिये हुए धृतराष्ट्र के पक्षपाती लोग युद्धभूमि में सामना न करनेवाले तथा शस्त्ररहित मुझ को मार भी दें, तो वह मेरे लिये बड़ा ही हितकारक होगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::46.english_translation: If the armed sons of Dhritarashtra were to kill me in battle while I stood unresisting and without weapons, that would be far better for me.
bhagwad_gita::46.translation_literal: यदि (if) / माम् (me) / अप्रतीकारम् (unresisting, not striking back) / अशस्त्रम् (without weapons) / शस्त्रपाणयः (those holding weapons) / धार्तराष्ट्राः (the sons of Dhritarashtra) / रणे (in battle) / हन्युः (might kill) / तत् (that) / मे (for me) / क्षेमतरम् (more beneficial, better) / भवेत् (would be)
bhagwad_gita::46.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::46.essence: Harming loved ones feels worse than losing your own life.
bhagwad_gita::46.simple_meaning: Arjuna says that even dying unarmed in battle would be better than fighting his own relatives.
bhagwad_gita::46.simple_insight: The heart can feel so burdened that even defeat seems kinder than harming loved ones.
bhagwad_gita::46.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has already rejected the war’s moral cost. Surrounded by Krishna and the opposing army, he says that if the armed sons of Dhritarashtra killed him while he stayed unarmed, that would be better than fighting kin.
bhagwad_gita::46.modern_relevance: You are standing in a doorway, keys in hand, about to leave a relationship or job that once felt safe. Part of you would rather be hurt than become the one who causes harm.
bhagwad_gita::46.insight: It shifts the mind from winning at any cost to seeing the cost of violence itself.

bhagwad_gita::47.verse_sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् । विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥
bhagwad_gita::47.verse_hindi: संजय बोले  ऐसा कहकर शोकाकुल मनवाले अर्जुन बाणसहित धनुष का त्याग करके युद्धभूमि में रथके मध्यभाग में बैठ गये ॥
bhagwad_gita::47.english_translation: Sanjaya said: Saying this, Arjuna sat down on the chariot seat in the midst of the battlefield, casting aside his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief.
bhagwad_gita::47.translation_literal: सञ्जय उवाच (Sanjaya said) / एवम् (thus) / उक्त्वा (having spoken) / अर्जुनः (Arjuna) / संख्ये (in battle) / रथोपस्थे (on the chariot seat) / उपाविशत् (sat down) / विसृज्य (casting aside) / सशरम् (with arrows) / चापम् (bow) / शोकसंविग्नमानसः (mind agitated by grief)
bhagwad_gita::47.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::47.essence: Grief can make even a warrior lay down his weapons.
bhagwad_gita::47.simple_meaning: Arjuna gives up his bow and sits down in the chariot, overwhelmed by grief.
bhagwad_gita::47.simple_insight: Sometimes the body stops before the heart can bear one more step.
bhagwad_gita::47.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has just voiced his despair. Sanjaya watches him drop his bow and arrows and sink down on the chariot seat. The war is about to begin, but Arjuna is already broken.
bhagwad_gita::47.modern_relevance: You open the message, stare at it, and set the phone down. The decision is still there, but your hands have gone still because the weight of it has landed.
bhagwad_gita::47.insight: It shows the exact moment paralysis takes over, before Krishna begins to answer it.

bhagwad_gita::48.verse_sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाचतं तथा कृपयाऽविष्टमश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम् । विषीदन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::48.verse_hindi: संजय बोले  वैसी कायरता से आविष्ट उन अर्जुन के प्रति, जो कि विषाद कर रहे हैं और आँसुओं के कारण जिनके नेत्रों की देखने की शक्ति अवरुद्ध हो रही है, भगवान् मधुसूदन ये आगे कहे जानेवाले वचन बोले ॥
bhagwad_gita::48.english_translation: Sanjaya said: To Arjuna, overcome by pity, his eyes full of tears and clouded with grief, Madhusudana spoke these words.
bhagwad_gita::48.translation_literal: सञ्जय उवाच (Sanjaya said) / तम् (to him) / तथा (thus) / कृपया (by pity) / आविष्टम् (overcome) / अश्रु-पूर्ण-आकुल-ईक्षणम् (with eyes full of tears and troubled) / विषीदन्तम् (grieving) / इदम् (this) / वाक्यम् (speech) / उवाच (spoke) / मधुसूदनः (Madhusudana)
bhagwad_gita::48.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::48.essence: Grief opens the door for instruction.
bhagwad_gita::48.simple_meaning: Sanjaya describes Arjuna in tears and grief as Krishna begins to speak to him.
bhagwad_gita::48.simple_insight: Even the deepest collapse can become the starting point of guidance.
bhagwad_gita::48.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has broken down before the fight begins. Sanjaya describes his tear-filled, confused state just before Krishna answers him. This verse sets the emotional scene for the teaching that follows.
bhagwad_gita::48.modern_relevance: You sit in your car after a brutal phone call, unable to start the engine. Before any advice can help, the mind first has to be seen in its breaking point.
bhagwad_gita::48.insight: It frames the teaching as a response to collapse, not abstract theory.

bhagwad_gita::49.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचकुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् । अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन ॥
bhagwad_gita::49.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले   हे अर्जुन इस विषम अवसरपर तुम्हें यह कायरता कहाँसे प्राप्त हुई, जिसका कि श्रेष्ठ पुरुष सेवन नहीं करते, जो स्वर्गको देनेवाली नहीं है और कीर्ति करनेवाली भी नहीं है ॥
bhagwad_gita::49.english_translation: Krishna said: Arjuna, where has this delusion come from in this crisis? Noble people do not follow it. It does not lead upward, and it brings disgrace.
bhagwad_gita::49.translation_literal: श्री भगवान् उवाच (the divine said) / कुतः (from where) / त्वा (to you) / कश्मलम् (delusion) / इदम् (this) / विषमे (in this crisis) / समुपस्थितम् (has arisen) / अनार्य-जुष्टम् (not followed by noble people) / अस्वर्ग्यम् (not leading upward) / अकीर्ति-करम् (bringing disgrace) / अर्जुन (Arjuna)
bhagwad_gita::49.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::49.essence: Delusion has no place in a decisive moment.
bhagwad_gita::49.simple_meaning: Arjuna's collapse is called out as misplaced weakness. It is not the response of a noble person, and it only lowers him.
bhagwad_gita::49.simple_insight: A hard moment does not excuse surrendering to confusion. You can notice weakness without obeying it.
bhagwad_gita::49.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Arjuna has dropped into grief and hesitation while the armies wait. Krishna answers sharply, naming the paralysis as out of place in this decisive moment. This verse begins the push to restore action.
bhagwad_gita::49.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that changes everything, and your hand freezes above the screen. The mind calls it caution; Krishna calls it collapse.
bhagwad_gita::49.insight: It teaches you to interrupt panic before it becomes your identity.

bhagwad_gita::50.verse_sanskrit: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते । क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥
bhagwad_gita::50.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन अर्जुन  इस नपुंसकताको मत प्राप्त हो क्योंकि तुम्हारेमें यह उचित नहीं है ।  हे परंतप  हृदयकी इस तुच्छ दुर्बलताका त्याग करके युद्धके लिये खड़े हो जाओ ॥
bhagwad_gita::50.english_translation: Do not yield to weakness, Partha. It does not suit you. Cast off this petty weakness of heart and rise, scorcher of foes.
bhagwad_gita::50.translation_literal: क्लैब्यम् (weakness / impotence) / मा स्म (do not) / गमः (go / fall into) / पार्थ (O Partha) / न (not) / एतत् (this) / त्वयि (in you) / उपपद्यते (is fitting) / क्षुद्रम् (petty) / हृदयदौर्बल्यम् (weakness of heart) / त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) / उत्तिष्ठ (rise) / परन्तप (O scorcher of foes)
bhagwad_gita::50.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::50.essence: Weakness is optional; the call to act remains.
bhagwad_gita::50.simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna not to sink into weakness. He must drop this small-hearted fear and stand up to fight.
bhagwad_gita::50.simple_insight: There is strength in refusing to stay collapsed when duty calls.
bhagwad_gita::50.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has frozen in grief and doubt. Krishna answers sharply, telling him this collapse does not belong to him. The moment demands courage, not self-pity.
bhagwad_gita::50.modern_relevance: You are halfway through a hard conversation, your voice starts shaking, and you want to back out. This verse says the collapse is temporary — stand back up and finish what must be done.
bhagwad_gita::50.insight: It shifts the mind from self-doubt to immediate responsibility.

bhagwad_gita::51.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचकथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन । इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन ॥
bhagwad_gita::51.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे मधुसूदन मैं रणभूमिमें भीष्म और द्रोणके साथ बाणोंसे युद्ध कैसे करूँ क्योंकि हे अरिसूदन ये दोनों ही पूजाके योग्य हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::51.english_translation: Arjuna said: How can I fight Bhishma and Drona with arrows in battle, O Madhusudana? They are worthy of worship, O destroyer of enemies.
bhagwad_gita::51.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / कथम् (how) / भीष्मम् (Bhishma) / अहम् (I) / संख्ये (in battle) / द्रोणम् (Drona) / च (and) / मधुसूदन (O Madhusudana) / इषुभिः (with arrows) / प्रतियोत्स्यामि (shall fight) / पूजार्हौ (worthy of worship) / अरिसूदन (O destroyer of enemies)
bhagwad_gita::51.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::51.essence: Respect can make necessary action feel unbearable.
bhagwad_gita::51.simple_meaning: Arjuna cannot imagine fighting his own respected teachers and elders. His hesitation is not tactical; it is moral and emotional.
bhagwad_gita::51.simple_insight: Some conflicts hurt because the people involved still matter to you.
bhagwad_gita::51.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Krishna has just challenged Arjuna’s collapse. Arjuna answers with a deeper wound: Bhishma and Drona are not enemies in his heart, but revered teachers. His refusal to shoot reveals the conflict tearing him apart.
bhagwad_gita::51.modern_relevance: You have to speak against a mentor who shaped you. Your hand freezes because the person in front of you is not just wrong — they are beloved.
bhagwad_gita::51.insight: It names the paralysis that comes when duty collides with reverence.

bhagwad_gita::52.verse_sanskrit: गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान्श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके । हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैवभुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥
bhagwad_gita::52.verse_hindi: महानुभाव गुरुजनोंको न मारकर इस लोकमें मैं भिक्षाका अन्न खाना भी श्रेष्ठ समझता हूँ ।  क्योंकि गुरुजनोंको मारकर यहाँ रक्तसे सने हुए तथा धनकी कामनाकी मुख्यतावाले भोगोंको ही तो भोगूँगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::52.english_translation: It is better to live on alms in this world than to kill these great teachers. If I kill them, the pleasures I enjoy here will be stained with blood and bound to greed.
bhagwad_gita::52.translation_literal: गुरून् (teachers) / अहत्वा (without killing) / हि (indeed) / महानुभावान् (great-souled, noble) / श्रेयः (better) / भोक्तुम् (to eat/enjoy) / भैक्ष्यम् (alms) / अपि (even) / इह (here) / लोके (in the world) / हत्वा (having killed) / अर्थकामान् (those driven by wealth and desire) / तु (but) / गुरून् (teachers) / इह (here) / एव (indeed) / भुञ्जीय (I would enjoy) / भोगान् (pleasures) / रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् (stained with blood)
bhagwad_gita::52.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::52.essence: A victory that destroys reverence is already a loss.
bhagwad_gita::52.simple_meaning: Arjuna says it would be better to live on alms than kill his respected teachers. He sees any victory gained that way as tainted by blood and greed.
bhagwad_gita::52.simple_insight: Some gains cost too much. Clear conscience matters more than winning.
bhagwad_gita::52.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen between two armies. Krishna has urged him to act, but Arjuna now names the moral cost: these are not enemies only, but revered teachers. His refusal deepens the crisis and shows how tangled duty has become.
bhagwad_gita::52.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that will end a friendship, or take the promotion that depends on someone else being pushed out. The win feels dirty before you even touch it.
bhagwad_gita::52.insight: It shifts the question from can I win to can I live with the cost.
