bhagwad_gita::53.verse_sanskrit: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयोयद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः । यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥
bhagwad_gita::53.verse_hindi: हम यह भी नहीं जानते कि हमलोगोंके लिये युद्ध करना और न करना  इन दोनोंमेंसे कौनसा अत्यन्त श्रेष्ठ है और हमें इसका भी पता नहीं है कि हम उन्हें जीतेंगे अथवा वे हमें जीतेंगे ।  जिनको मारकर हम जीना भी नहीं चाहते, वे ही धृतराष्ट्रके सम्बन्धी हमारे सामने खड़े हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::53.english_translation: We do not know which is better for us: to fight or not to fight. We do not even know whether we will conquer them or they us. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us, and we do not wish to live after killing them.
bhagwad_gita::53.translation_literal: न (not) / च (and) / एतत् (this) / विद्मः (we know) / कतरत् (which of the two) / नः (for us) / गरीयः (better) / यत् वा (or which) / जयेम (we would conquer) / यदि वा (or whether) / नः (us) / जयेयुः (they would conquer) / यान् (those whom) / एव (indeed) / हत्वा (having killed) / न (not) / जिजीविषामः (we wish to live) / ते (they) / अवस्थिताः (standing) / प्रमुखे (in front) / धार्तराष्ट्राः (sons of Dhritarashtra)
bhagwad_gita::53.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::53.essence: Honest uncertainty is the first crack in moral paralysis.
bhagwad_gita::53.simple_meaning: Arjuna admits complete uncertainty. He cannot tell whether fighting or not fighting is the better choice, and he cannot bear the thought of killing relatives who stand before him.
bhagwad_gita::53.simple_insight: It is a relief to name confusion honestly before forcing a choice.
bhagwad_gita::53.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands between two armies with his bow lowered. After seeing teachers, elders, and kin on both sides, he no longer knows what is right. This verse deepens his breakdown before he asks Krishna for clear guidance.
bhagwad_gita::53.modern_relevance: You are holding your phone after a message that could end a relationship, and your thumb freezes. One choice may hurt either way, and you finally admit you cannot sort it alone.
bhagwad_gita::53.insight: It shifts the mind from false certainty to honest doubt, making room for guidance instead of panic.

bhagwad_gita::54.verse_sanskrit: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्िचतं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::54.verse_hindi: कायरतारूपदोषसे तिरस्कृत स्वभाववाला और धर्मके विषयमें मोहित अन्तःकरणवाला मैं आपसे पूछता हूँ कि जो निश्चित कल्याण करनेवाली हो, वह मेरे लिये कहिये ।  मैं आपका शिष्य हूँ ।  आपके शरण हुए मुझे शिक्षा दीजिये ॥
bhagwad_gita::54.english_translation: My nature is overwhelmed by weakness, and my mind is confused about duty. I ask you: tell me with certainty what is best for me. I am your student; instruct me, for I have taken refuge in you.
bhagwad_gita::54.translation_literal: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः (nature overcome by weakness) / पृच्छामि (I ask) / त्वाम् (you) / धर्मसंमूढचेताः (mind confused about duty) / यत् (which) / श्रेयः (the highest good) / स्यात् (may be) / निश्चितम् (certainly) / ब्रूहि (tell) / तत् (that) / मे (to me) / शिष्यः (student) / ते (your) / अहम् (I) / शाधि (instruct) / माम् (me) / त्वाम् (you) / प्रपन्नम् (one who has taken refuge)
bhagwad_gita::54.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::54.essence: Clarity begins when you admit you cannot see the right action alone.
bhagwad_gita::54.simple_meaning: Arjuna admits he is overwhelmed and confused about what is truly right. He asks Krishna to clearly tell him the best course, as a student seeking guidance.
bhagwad_gita::54.simple_insight: It is a relief to admit confusion and ask for guidance instead of pretending to know.
bhagwad_gita::54.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna's bow has fallen and his certainty has collapsed. Surrounded by the armies of his own kin, he stops arguing with himself and turns to Krishna, asking for clear instruction because he can no longer tell what is right.
bhagwad_gita::54.modern_relevance: You are staring at a message you do not want to send, knowing it will change everything. Instead of forcing confidence, you finally admit: I need the clearest counsel I can find.
bhagwad_gita::54.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliant confusion to disciplined seeking of guidance.

bhagwad_gita::55.verse_sanskrit: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::55.verse_hindi: पृथ्वीपर धनधान्यसमृद्ध और शत्रुरहितराज्य तथा स्वर्गमें देवताओंका आधिपत्य मिल जाय तो भी इन्द्रियोंको सुखानेवाला मेरा जो शोक है, वह दूर हो जाय  ऐसा मैं नहीं देखता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::55.english_translation: Even if I gained an unrivaled, prosperous kingdom on earth or lordship over the gods, I see nothing that could remove this grief that dries up my senses.
bhagwad_gita::55.translation_literal: न हि (for not) / प्रपश्यामि (I see) / मम (my) / अपनुद्यात् (could remove) / यत् (that which) / शोकम् (grief) / उच्छोषणम् (drying up) / इन्द्रियाणाम् (of the senses) / अवाप्य (having obtained) / भूमौ (on earth) / असपत्नम् (unrivaled, without enemies) / ऋद्धम् (prosperous) / राज्यम् (kingdom) / सुराणाम् (of the gods) / अपि (even) / च (and) / आधिपत्यम् (lordship)
bhagwad_gita::55.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::55.essence: No outer victory can cure an inner collapse.
bhagwad_gita::55.simple_meaning: Arjuna says that even the greatest possible power and wealth would not remove his grief. His mind is so overwhelmed that nothing outside can fix it.
bhagwad_gita::55.simple_insight: When grief takes over, even the biggest prizes stop looking valuable.
bhagwad_gita::55.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has already admitted confusion and weakness. Now he tells Krishna that even a rich, enemy-free kingdom on earth or rule over the gods would not dry up his sorrow. This is the depth of his collapse before Krishna begins to answer.
bhagwad_gita::55.modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the apartment, the applause — and still feel hollow on the ride home. Some pain is too deep to be solved by winning more.
bhagwad_gita::55.insight: It shifts attention from external gains to the inner wound that must be faced directly.

bhagwad_gita::56.verse_sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप । न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥
bhagwad_gita::56.verse_hindi: संजय बोले  हे शत्रुतापन धृतराष्ट्र ऐसा कहकर निद्राको जीतनेवाले अर्जुन अन्तर्यामी भगवान् गोविन्दसे मैं युद्ध नहीं करूँगा ऐसा साफसाफ कहकर चुप हो गये ॥
bhagwad_gita::56.english_translation: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha, Gudakesha, the scorcher of foes, said to Govinda, “I will not fight,” and fell silent.
bhagwad_gita::56.translation_literal: सञ्जय उवाच (Sanjaya said) / एवम् (thus) / उक्त्वा (having spoken) / हृषीकेशम् (to Hrishikesha) / गुडाकेशः (Gudakesha) / परन्तप (scorcher of foes) / न (not) / योत्स्ये (I will fight) / इति (thus) / गोविन्दम् (to Govinda) / उक्त्वा (having said) / तूष्णीं (silent) / बभूव (became) / ह (indeed)
bhagwad_gita::56.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::56.essence: Refusal has stopped the war inside him.
bhagwad_gita::56.simple_meaning: Arjuna tells Krishna he will not fight, then falls silent. The argument pauses in complete refusal.
bhagwad_gita::56.simple_insight: Sometimes the hardest moment is not action, but the silence after refusing it.
bhagwad_gita::56.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield between two armies, Arjuna has just confessed his despair. Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra that, after speaking to Krishna, Arjuna declared he would not fight and then went silent. The crisis is now fully exposed.
bhagwad_gita::56.modern_relevance: You finally say the thing you’ve been avoiding: “I can’t do this.” Then the room goes quiet, and everyone feels the weight of your choice.
bhagwad_gita::56.insight: It marks the collapse of will before Krishna begins to answer it.

bhagwad_gita::57.verse_sanskrit: तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः ॥
bhagwad_gita::57.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशोद्भव धृतराष्ट्र दोनों सेनाओंके मध्यभागमें विषाद करते हुए उस अर्जुनके प्रति हँसते हुएसे भगवान् हृषीकेश यह आगे कहे जानेवाले वचन बोले ॥
bhagwad_gita::57.english_translation: Hṛṣīkeśa spoke to the grieving Arjuna, smiling slightly, in the midst of the two armies.
bhagwad_gita::57.translation_literal: तम् (to him) / उवाच (spoke) / हृषीकेशः (Hṛṣīkeśa) / प्रहसन्निव (as if smiling) / भारत (O descendant of Bharata) / सेनयोः (of the two armies) / उभयोः (of both) / मध्ये (in the middle) / विषीदन्तम् (to the grieving one) / इदम् (these) / वचः (words)
bhagwad_gita::57.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::57.essence: Guidance begins when grief is met without rejection.
bhagwad_gita::57.simple_meaning: Krishna begins speaking to Arjuna, who is overwhelmed with grief between the two armies.
bhagwad_gita::57.simple_insight: Even in collapse, the teaching begins with presence, not panic.
bhagwad_gita::57.detailed_meaning: Arjuna stands between the two armies, unable to fight. Krishna, seeing his collapse, begins the conversation with a calm, almost gentle smile. This verse marks the turning point from silence and grief to guidance.
bhagwad_gita::57.modern_relevance: You are frozen in the middle of a hard decision, and everything in you wants to shut down. The first real help often arrives not as pressure, but as a steady voice that can hold your fear.
bhagwad_gita::57.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional paralysis to receiving guidance.

bhagwad_gita::58.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचअशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे । गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::58.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  तुमने शोक न करनेयोग्यका शोक किया है और पण्डिताईकी बातें कह रहे हो परन्तु जिनके प्राण चले गये हैं, उनके लिये और जिनके प्राण नहीं गये हैं, उनके लिये पण्डितलोग शोक नहीं करते ॥
bhagwad_gita::58.english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: You grieve for what should not be grieved for, yet speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the dead or the living.
bhagwad_gita::58.translation_literal: श्री भगवानुवाच (the Blessed Lord said) / अशोच्यान् (for the ungrievable) / अन्वशोचः (you have grieved) / त्वम् (you) / प्रज्ञावादान् (words of wisdom) / च (and) / भाषसे (you speak) / गतासून् (the departed breath) / अगतासून् (the not-departed breath) / च (and) / न (not) / अनुशोचन्ति (grieve) / पण्डिताः (the wise)
bhagwad_gita::58.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::58.essence: Clear seeing ends grief where the wise know none is needed.
bhagwad_gita::58.simple_meaning: Arjuna is mourning people who should not be mourned, while speaking as if he understands wisdom. Krishna says the wise do not grieve for either the dead or the living.
bhagwad_gita::58.simple_insight: It brings relief by showing that clear seeing can hold loss without collapsing into sorrow.
bhagwad_gita::58.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield between two armies, Arjuna has frozen. His bow has fallen, and Krishna begins by correcting the confusion itself: Arjuna is speaking like a wise man while reacting like someone lost in grief. This verse starts the teaching that follows.
bhagwad_gita::58.modern_relevance: You stand beside a hospital bed, rehearsing the perfect words while your chest tightens. The mind reaches for philosophy, but the heart is still caught in fear and loss.
bhagwad_gita::58.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional confusion to clear discrimination about what truly deserves grief.

bhagwad_gita::59.verse_sanskrit: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः । न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::59.verse_hindi: किसी कालमें मैं नहीं था और तू नहीं था तथा ये राजालोग नहीं थे, यह बात भी नहीं है और इसके बाद भविष्य में मैं, तू और राजलोग  हम सभी नहीं रहेंगे, यह बात भी नहीं है ॥
bhagwad_gita::59.english_translation: I was never absent, nor were you, nor these kings. Nor will any of us cease to be in the future.
bhagwad_gita::59.translation_literal: न (not) / तु (indeed) / एव (only) / अहम् (I) / जातु (at any time) / न (not) / आसम् (was) / न (not) / त्वम् (you) / नेमे (nor these) / जनाधिपाः (kings) / न (not) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / न (not) / भविष्यामः (will be) / सर्वे (all) / वयम् (we) / अतः परम् (after this)
bhagwad_gita::59.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::59.essence: What truly exists was never born and never lost.
bhagwad_gita::59.simple_meaning: Krishna says that he, Arjuna, and the kings have always existed in some form, and none of them will simply vanish after death.
bhagwad_gita::59.simple_insight: Fear softens when you stop treating the body as the whole story.
bhagwad_gita::59.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has collapsed under grief and doubt. Krishna begins by correcting his view of death: the living presence behind these bodies has not suddenly come into existence, and it will not simply end here.
bhagwad_gita::59.modern_relevance: You are standing at a hospital bed, hearing that a loved one may not recover. Panic narrows everything to the body in front of you. This verse opens a larger horizon.
bhagwad_gita::59.insight: It shifts attention from the body’s ending to the continuity of the true self.

bhagwad_gita::60.verse_sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा । तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥
bhagwad_gita::60.verse_hindi: देहधारीके इस मनुष्यशरीरमें जैसे बालकपन, जवानी और वृद्धावस्था होती है, ऐसे ही देहान्तरकी प्राप्ति होती है ।  उस विषयमें धीर मनुष्य मोहित नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::60.english_translation: Just as the embodied one passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too it passes into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
bhagwad_gita::60.translation_literal: देहिनः (the embodied one) / अस्मिन् (in this) / यथा (just as) / देहे (in the body) / कौमारम् (childhood) / यौवनम् (youth) / जरा (old age) / तथा (so) / देहान्तरप्राप्तिः (attaining another body) / धीरः (the wise) / तत्र (there) / न (not) / मुह्यति (is deluded)
bhagwad_gita::60.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::60.essence: What changes form is not what you truly are.
bhagwad_gita::60.simple_meaning: The body changes through stages, and the one living in it moves on to another body. A steady person does not get confused by this.
bhagwad_gita::60.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing change as natural, not tragic.
bhagwad_gita::60.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen by grief. Krishna first reminds him that no one was truly born or lost, then gives a human example: the body moves from childhood to youth to old age, and the embodied one moves on as well.
bhagwad_gita::60.modern_relevance: You watch an old photo and barely recognise yourself. The face, voice, and fears have changed — yet something in you has kept witnessing all of it.
bhagwad_gita::60.insight: It shifts attention from the body’s changing stages to the steady awareness that outlives them.

bhagwad_gita::61.verse_hindi: हे कुन्तीनन्दन इन्द्रियोंके जो विषय जड पदार्थ हैं, वो तो शीत अनुकूलता और उष्ण प्रतिकूलता  के द्वारा सुख और दुःख देनेवाले हैं तथा आनेजानेवाले और अनित्य हैं ।  हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन उनको तुम सहन करो ॥
bhagwad_gita::61.english_translation: Contacts with the senses, O son of Kunti, bring heat and cold, pleasure and pain. They come and go; they are impermanent. Endure them, O Bharata.
bhagwad_gita::61.translation_literal: मात्रास्पर्शाः (sense-contacts) / तु (indeed) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः (giving cold-heat, pleasure-pain) / आगमापायिनः (coming and going) / अनित्याः (impermanent) / तान् (them) / तितिक्षस्व (endure) / भारत (O Bharata)
bhagwad_gita::61.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::61.essence: Passing sensations lose power when you stop treating them as permanent.
bhagwad_gita::61.simple_meaning: Pleasure and pain from the senses are temporary. They come and go, so you should learn to bear them without being shaken.
bhagwad_gita::61.simple_insight: You do not have to be ruled by every sensation. Calm endurance gives you room to choose wisely.
bhagwad_gita::61.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna answers his collapse. After teaching that the self does not die, Krishna turns to the body’s changing experiences and says they are temporary, so Arjuna must endure them.
bhagwad_gita::61.modern_relevance: You get a sharp message, feel your stomach drop, and want to react instantly. The feeling is real, but it does not deserve the steering wheel.
bhagwad_gita::61.insight: It trains you to notice discomfort without obeying it, so reaction does not become action.

bhagwad_gita::62.verse_sanskrit: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ । समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
bhagwad_gita::62.verse_hindi: कारण कि हे पुरुषोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन सुखदुःखमें सम रहनेवाले जिस धीर मनुष्यको ये मात्रास्पर्श पदार्थ व्यथित सुखीदुःखी नहीं कर पाते, वह अमर होनेमें समर्थ हो जाता है अर्थात् वह अमर हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::62.english_translation: The wise person who is not shaken by these, and remains equal in pain and pleasure, becomes fit for freedom.
bhagwad_gita::62.translation_literal: यम् (whom) / हि (indeed) / न (not) / व्यथयन्ति (disturb) / एते (these) / पुरुषम् (person) / पुरुषर्षभ (best among men) / समदुःखसुखम् (equal in pain and pleasure) / धीरम् (steadfast one) / सः (that one) / अमृतत्वाय (for immortality) / कल्पते (is fit)
bhagwad_gita::62.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::62.essence: Freedom begins where pain and pleasure stop controlling you.
bhagwad_gita::62.simple_meaning: A steady person who stays even through pleasure and pain is not thrown off by changing experiences and becomes ready for inner freedom.
bhagwad_gita::62.simple_insight: You do not need to be ruled by every high and low. Steadiness itself becomes strength.
bhagwad_gita::62.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still reeling from grief and confusion. Krishna has already said the body changes and sensations pass. Now he shows the next step: the person who stays even through pleasure and pain is the one ready for freedom.
bhagwad_gita::62.modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with bad news, then a compliment, then another crisis. The mind jerks in every direction. This verse asks for a steadier center that does not collapse with each swing.
bhagwad_gita::62.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing comfort and avoiding pain to holding both with equal steadiness.

bhagwad_gita::63.verse_sanskrit: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः । उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
bhagwad_gita::63.verse_hindi: टिप्पणी प0 55 असत् का तो भाव सत्ता विद्यमान नहीं है और सत् का अभाव विद्यमान नहीं है, तत्त्वदर्शी महापुरुषोंने इन दोनोंका ही अन्त अर्थात् तत्त्व देखा है ॥
bhagwad_gita::63.english_translation: The unreal has no being; the real has no nonbeing. Seers have understood the boundary of both.
bhagwad_gita::63.translation_literal: नासतः (of the unreal) / विद्यते (exists) / भावः (being) / न (not) / अभावः (nonbeing) / विद्यते (exists) / सतः (of the real) / उभयोः (of both) / अपि (also) / दृष्टः (seen) / अन्तः (limit) / तु (indeed) / अनयोः (of these) / तत्त्वदर्शिभिः (by seers of reality)
bhagwad_gita::63.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::63.essence: What passes away was never ultimate; what is real cannot vanish.
bhagwad_gita::63.simple_meaning: What is temporary does not truly exist, and what is real cannot be destroyed. Those who see clearly understand the difference between the two.
bhagwad_gita::63.simple_insight: You can stop treating every passing fear or loss as ultimate. Some things vanish; what is real stays.
bhagwad_gita::63.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen before the battle. Krishna has already told him to endure changing sensations; now he goes deeper, showing that the wise see through appearance itself. This verse defines what can truly be lost and what cannot.
bhagwad_gita::63.modern_relevance: You reread a message that stung, then imagine the whole relationship collapsing. Krishna’s point cuts through that spiral: not every passing state deserves the weight you give it.
bhagwad_gita::63.insight: It shifts attention from appearances to what remains unchanged beneath them.

bhagwad_gita::64.verse_sanskrit: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित् कर्तुमर्हति ॥
bhagwad_gita::64.verse_hindi: अविनाशी तो उसको जान, जिससे यह सम्पूर्ण संसार व्याप्त है ।  इस अविनाशीका विनाश कोई भी नहीं कर सकता ॥
bhagwad_gita::64.english_translation: Know that to be imperishable by which this entire world is pervaded. No one can destroy this imperishable reality.
bhagwad_gita::64.translation_literal: अविनाशि (imperishable) / तु (indeed) / तत् (that) / विद्धि (know) / येन (by which) / सर्वम् इदम् (all this) / ततम् (pervaded) / विनाशम् (destruction) / अव्ययस्य अस्य (of this imperishable) / न कश्चित् (no one) / कर्तुम् (to do) / अर्हति (is able)
bhagwad_gita::64.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::64.essence: What truly pervades everything cannot be destroyed.
bhagwad_gita::64.simple_meaning: Know that the reality behind everything is imperishable. No force can destroy what pervades the whole world.
bhagwad_gita::64.simple_insight: Fear loosens when you realize what is deepest in you cannot be harmed.
bhagwad_gita::64.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has dropped into despair and Krishna begins rebuilding his understanding from the ground up. After saying the unreal has no lasting existence, Krishna now points to what cannot be destroyed at all.
bhagwad_gita::64.modern_relevance: A diagnosis, a breakup, a public failure — everything seems to collapse at once. This verse reminds you that the deepest reality in you is not fragile, even when your situation is.
bhagwad_gita::64.insight: It shifts attention from what changes to what remains untouched beneath change.

bhagwad_gita::65.verse_sanskrit: अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः । अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत ॥
bhagwad_gita::65.verse_hindi: अविनाशी, अप्रमेय और नित्य रहनेवाले इस शरीरी के ये देह अन्तवाले कहे गये हैं ।  इसलिये हे अर्जुन तुम युद्ध करो ॥
bhagwad_gita::65.english_translation: These bodies are said to be finite, but the embodied being is eternal, indestructible, and immeasurable. Therefore, fight, Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::65.translation_literal: अन्तवन्तः (ending / finite) / इमे (these) / देहाः (bodies) / नित्यस्य (of the eternal) / उक्ताः (are said to be) / शरीरिणः (of the embodied being) / अनाशिनः (of the indestructible) / अप्रमेयस्य (of the immeasurable) / तस्मात् (therefore) / युध्यस्व (fight) / भारत (Arjuna)
bhagwad_gita::65.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::65.essence: What is truly you cannot be destroyed, so duty remains.
bhagwad_gita::65.simple_meaning: Bodies are temporary, but the inner being is eternal and cannot be measured or destroyed. Arjuna is told to fight because of that truth.
bhagwad_gita::65.simple_insight: Fear loosens when you stop treating the body as the whole story.
bhagwad_gita::65.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before the war. Krishna answers his grief by separating the temporary body from the enduring embodied being. Because life is not destroyed by bodily change, Arjuna is told to do his duty and fight.
bhagwad_gita::65.modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, about to make a hard decision for someone you love. The body can change, weaken, and end, but your duty does not vanish with your fear.
bhagwad_gita::65.insight: It shifts the mind from bodily loss to rightful action.

bhagwad_gita::66.verse_sanskrit: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् । उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::66.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य इस अविनाशी शरीरीको मारनेवाला मानता है और जो मनुष्य इसको मरा मानता है, वे दोनों ही इसको नहीं जानते क्योंकि यह न मारता है और न मारा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::66.english_translation: Whoever thinks this imperishable being is the killer, and whoever thinks it is killed, both do not understand. It neither kills nor is killed.
bhagwad_gita::66.translation_literal: यः (who) / एनम् (this) / वेत्ति (knows) / हन्तारम् (as killer) / यः (and who) / च (also) / एनम् (this) / मन्यते (thinks) / हतम् (killed) / उभौ (both) / तौ (those two) / न (not) / विजानीतः (understand) / न (not) / अयम् (this) / हन्ति (kills) / न (not) / हन्यते (is killed)
bhagwad_gita::66.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::66.essence: What you are cannot be reduced to killer or victim.
bhagwad_gita::66.simple_meaning: The true self cannot be killed, and it does not kill. Seeing it as either one is ignorance.
bhagwad_gita::66.simple_insight: Fear loosens when you stop identifying life with what can be destroyed.
bhagwad_gita::66.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen before battle. Krishna has just said the body ends, but the inner being does not. Now he sharpens the point: neither murder nor death touches that reality, so Arjuna’s terror is built on a false identification.
bhagwad_gita::66.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that ends a friendship, or walk away from a role that once defined you. The mind says, 'I am ruining everything.' This verse says the deepest part of you is untouched by such labels.
bhagwad_gita::66.insight: It shifts the mind from personal guilt and fear to clear seeing of what can and cannot be harmed.

bhagwad_gita::67.verse_sanskrit: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः । अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणोन हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥
bhagwad_gita::67.verse_hindi: यह शरीरी न कभी जन्मता है और न मरता है तथा यह उत्पन्न होकर फिर होनेवाला नहीं है ।  यह जन्मरहित, नित्यनिरन्तर रहनेवाला, शाश्वत और पुराण अनादि है ।  शरीरके मारे जानेपर भी यह नहीं मारा जाता ॥
bhagwad_gita::67.english_translation: It is never born and never dies. It did not come into being, and it will not cease. Unborn, eternal, everlasting, ancient, it is not destroyed when the body is destroyed.
bhagwad_gita::67.translation_literal: न जायते (is not born) / म्रियते (dies) वा (or) कदाचित् (at any time) / नायम् (this one not) / भूत्वा (having become) / भविता (will become) वा (or) न भूयः (not again) / अजः (unborn) / नित्यः (eternal) / शाश्वतः (everlasting) / अयम् (this) / पुराणः (ancient) / न हन्यते (is not slain) / हन्यमाने (being slain) शरीरे (in the body)
bhagwad_gita::67.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::67.essence: What you are cannot be touched by birth or death.
bhagwad_gita::67.simple_meaning: The true self is never born and never dies. It does not begin with the body, and it is not destroyed when the body ends.
bhagwad_gita::67.simple_insight: Fear softens when you stop treating your deepest identity as fragile.
bhagwad_gita::67.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen by grief at the thought of killing relatives. Krishna deepens the teaching: the true self does not enter birth or death. The body can be struck; what lives within it cannot be ended.
bhagwad_gita::67.modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed or a graveside and feel everything collapsing. This verse asks you to see that the person you love, and the deepest part of yourself, are not limited to the body alone.
bhagwad_gita::67.insight: It shifts attention from bodily loss to the unbroken reality that witnesses change.

bhagwad_gita::68.verse_sanskrit: वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम् । कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::68.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन जो मनुष्य इस शरीरीको अविनाशी, नित्य, जन्मरहित और अव्यय जानता है, वह कैसे किसको मारे और कैसे किसको मरवाये ॥
bhagwad_gita::68.english_translation: One who knows the imperishable, eternal, unborn, and unchanging cannot think of killing or causing death.
bhagwad_gita::68.translation_literal: वेद (knows) / अविनाशिनम् (the imperishable) / नित्यम् (the eternal) / यः (who) / एनम् (this one) / अजम् (unborn) / अव्ययम् (unchanging) / कथम् (how) / सः (that) / पुरुषः (person) / पार्थ (Arjuna) / कम् (whom) / घातयति (causes to be killed) / हन्ति (kills) / कम् (whom)
bhagwad_gita::68.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::68.essence: Clear seeing makes violence look absurd.
bhagwad_gita::68.simple_meaning: Anyone who truly sees the inner being as unborn and unchanging cannot think in terms of killing or being killed.
bhagwad_gita::68.simple_insight: The fear around death loosens when you see what cannot be destroyed.
bhagwad_gita::68.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before battle. Krishna deepens the teaching: the true inner being is not touched by birth or death. From that vision, the idea of killing becomes confused, because the real person was never perishable.
bhagwad_gita::68.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that ends a relationship, or stay silent and let harm continue. This verse asks you to see deeper than the body of the moment and act from clear seeing, not panic.
bhagwad_gita::68.insight: It shifts the mind from physical appearance to what remains unchanged beneath change.

bhagwad_gita::69.verse_sanskrit: वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहायनवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि । तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥
bhagwad_gita::69.verse_hindi: मनुष्य जैसे पुराने कपड़ोंको छोड़कर दूसरे नये कपड़े धारण कर लेता है, ऐसे ही देही पुराने शरीरोंको छोड़कर दूसरे नये शरीरोंमें चला जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::69.english_translation: As a person discards worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the embodied being discards worn-out bodies and enters new ones.
bhagwad_gita::69.translation_literal: वासांसि (clothes) / जीर्णानि (worn-out) / यथा (as) / विहाय (having discarded) / नवानि (new) / गृह्णाति (takes) / नरः (a person) / अपराणि (other) / तथा (so) / शरीराणि (bodies) / विहाय (having discarded) / जीर्णानि (worn-out) / अन्यानि (other) / संयाति (goes to) / नवानि (new) / देही (the embodied one)
bhagwad_gita::69.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::69.essence: What you are does not end when one body is left behind.
bhagwad_gita::69.simple_meaning: The true self passes from one body to another the way a person changes clothes.
bhagwad_gita::69.simple_insight: A fear of bodily loss softens when you see change as a transition, not an ending.
bhagwad_gita::69.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen by grief and fear. Krishna has just said the true self is unborn and indestructible. Now he gives a simple image: bodies are like clothes, and the embodied one moves on.
bhagwad_gita::69.modern_relevance: Standing beside a hospital bed, you watch a loved one weaken and feel helpless. This image does not erase grief, but it reminds you that change touches the body, not the deepest reality.
bhagwad_gita::69.insight: It shifts attention from identifying with the body to seeing the body as a temporary covering.

bhagwad_gita::70.verse_sanskrit: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः । न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥
bhagwad_gita::70.verse_hindi: शस्त्र इस शरीरीको काट नहीं सकते, अग्नि इसको जला नहीं सकती, जल इसको गीला नहीं कर सकता और वायु इसको सुखा नहीं सकती ॥
bhagwad_gita::70.english_translation: Weapons cannot cut it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, and wind cannot dry it.
bhagwad_gita::70.translation_literal: नैनं (not this) / छिन्दन्ति (cut) / शस्त्राणि (weapons) / नैनं (not this) / दहति (burns) / पावकः (fire) / न (not) / च (and) / एनं (this) / क्लेदयन्ति (wet) / आपो (waters) / न (not) / शोषयति (dries) / मारुतः (wind)
bhagwad_gita::70.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::70.essence: Your deepest reality is beyond every physical force.
bhagwad_gita::70.simple_meaning: The true self cannot be harmed by weapons, fire, water, or wind. It is beyond physical destruction.
bhagwad_gita::70.simple_insight: Fear loosens when you stop treating the deepest part of you as fragile.
bhagwad_gita::70.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before the war begins. Krishna answers his fear by explaining that the inner being is not made of matter at all, so no physical force can destroy it.
bhagwad_gita::70.modern_relevance: You read the message that changes everything after a breakup, a diagnosis, or a dismissal. The body may be shaken, but the deepest part of you is not at the mercy of events.
bhagwad_gita::70.insight: It shifts attention from protecting the body to recognising the untouched witness within.

bhagwad_gita::71.verse_sanskrit: अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च । नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::71.verse_hindi: यह शरीरी काटा नहीं जा सकता, यह जलाया नहीं जा सकता, यह गीला नहीं किया जा सकता और यह सुखाया भी नहीं जा सकता ।  कारण कि यह नित्य रहनेवाला सबमें परिपूर्ण, अचल, स्थिर स्वभाववाला और अनादि है ॥
bhagwad_gita::71.english_translation: This embodied self cannot be cut, burned, wetted, or dried. It is eternal, all-pervading, unmoving, fixed, and timeless.
bhagwad_gita::71.translation_literal: अच्छेद्यः (uncuttable) / अयम् (this) / अदाह्यः (unburnable) / अयम् (this) / अक्लेद्यः (unwettable) / अशोष्यः (undryable) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / नित्यः (eternal) / सर्वगतः (all-pervading) / स्थाणुः (fixed) / अचलः (unmoving) / अयम् (this) / सनातनः (timeless)
bhagwad_gita::71.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::71.essence: What you are cannot be harmed by anything that changes.
bhagwad_gita::71.simple_meaning: The true self cannot be destroyed by any physical force. It is permanent, present everywhere, unmoving, and beyond time.
bhagwad_gita::71.simple_insight: What you truly are is untouched by change, so fear loses its grip.
bhagwad_gita::71.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen before the war. Krishna deepens his teaching: the inner being is not a body and cannot be harmed like a body. This verse strengthens the case for acting without grief.
bhagwad_gita::71.modern_relevance: You are staring at a medical report, a breakup message, or a sudden layoff notice. Everything feels fragile. This verse reminds you that the deepest part of you is not made of what can be broken.
bhagwad_gita::71.insight: It shifts attention from the body’s vulnerability to the true self’s permanence.

bhagwad_gita::72.verse_hindi: यह देही प्रत्यक्ष नहीं दीखता, यह चिन्तनका विषय नहीं है और यह निर्विकार कहा जाता है ।  अतः इस देहीको ऐसा जानकर शोक नहीं करना चाहिये ॥
bhagwad_gita::72.english_translation: It is unseen, beyond thought, and said to be unchanged. Therefore, knowing it this way, you should not grieve.
bhagwad_gita::72.translation_literal: अव्यक्तः (unseen) / अयम् (this) / अचिन्त्यः (unthinkable) / अयम् (this) / अविकार्यः (unchanging) / अयम् (this) / उच्यते (is said to be) / तस्मात् (therefore) / एवम् (thus) / विदित्वा (having known) / एनम् (this) / न (not) / अनुशोचितुम् (to grieve) / अर्हसि (you should)
bhagwad_gita::72.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::72.essence: What is deepest in you was never available for loss.
bhagwad_gita::72.simple_meaning: The true self is not something you can see, think through, or alter. Knowing that, Arjuna should stop grieving.
bhagwad_gita::72.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that what matters most was never fragile.
bhagwad_gita::72.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna answers his grief with a deeper view of the person within the body. The body changes and dies, but the inner reality is beyond sight, thought, and change, so mourning it makes no sense.
bhagwad_gita::72.modern_relevance: You reread the message three times after the breakup, trying to make the loss feel logical. Some things cannot be held, explained, or broken in the first place.
bhagwad_gita::72.insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with what changes to resting in what does not.

bhagwad_gita::73.verse_sanskrit: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् । तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::73.verse_hindi: हे महाबाहो  अगर तुम इस देहीको नित्य पैदा होनेवाला अथवा नित्य मरनेवाला भी मानो, तो भी तुम्हें इस प्रकार शोक नहीं करना चाहिये ॥
bhagwad_gita::73.english_translation: O mighty-armed one, even if you think this embodied being is always born and always dies, you still should not grieve like this.
bhagwad_gita::73.translation_literal: अथ (even then) / च (also) / एनम् (this) / नित्यजातम् (always born) / नित्यम् (always) / वा (or) / मन्यसे (you think) / मृतम् (dead) / तथापि (even so) / त्वम् (you) / महाबाहो (mighty-armed one) / नैवम् (not like this) / शोचितुम् (to grieve) / अर्हसि (you should)
bhagwad_gita::73.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::73.essence: Even the plain fact of change is no reason to drown in sorrow.
bhagwad_gita::73.simple_meaning: Even if you see this embodied being as something that keeps being born and dying, grief is still not fitting. Krishna is pushing Arjuna beyond sorrow itself.
bhagwad_gita::73.simple_insight: You do not need to collapse into grief just because change is happening.
bhagwad_gita::73.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen by sorrow while Krishna keeps dismantling his fear. After explaining the imperishable nature of the embodied being, Krishna adds one more step: even under a simpler view of life and death, grief is still not the right response.
bhagwad_gita::73.modern_relevance: You are sitting beside a hospital bed, bracing for news you cannot control. Even if you think only in terms of birth and death, panic does not help you meet the moment.
bhagwad_gita::73.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional collapse to steady seeing, even before deeper understanding arrives.

bhagwad_gita::74.verse_sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च । तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::74.verse_hindi: क्योंकि पैदा हुएकी जरूर मृत्यु होगी और मरे हुएका जरूर जन्म होगा ।  इस जन्ममरणरूप परिवर्तन के प्रवाह का परिहार अर्थात् निवारण नहीं हो सकता ।  अतः इस विषयमें तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिये ॥
bhagwad_gita::74.english_translation: For what is born, death is certain; for what dies, birth is certain. What cannot be avoided should not be grieved over.
bhagwad_gita::74.translation_literal: जातस्य (of the born) / हि (indeed) / ध्रुवः (certain) / मृत्युः (death) / ध्रुवम् (certain) / जन्म (birth) / मृतस्य (of the dead) / च (and) / तस्मात् (therefore) / अपरिहार्ये (in the unavoidable) / अर्थे (matter) / न (not) / त्वम् (you) / शोचितुम् (to grieve) / अर्हसि (should)
bhagwad_gita::74.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::74.essence: What must change is not a reason for grief.
bhagwad_gita::74.simple_meaning: Anything that is born will die, and anything that dies will be born again. Since this cycle cannot be stopped, there is no reason to grieve over it.
bhagwad_gita::74.simple_insight: Some things are not yours to control, and peace begins where resistance ends.
bhagwad_gita::74.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen as Krishna keeps answering his grief. After saying the true self is beyond change, Krishna now grounds the lesson in the body’s cycle: birth, death, and return. The point is to stop mourning what nature itself keeps moving.
bhagwad_gita::74.modern_relevance: You are sitting beside a hospital bed, watching a monitor you cannot negotiate with. The fear is real, but the fact is plain: some changes cannot be prevented, only met with steadiness.
bhagwad_gita::74.insight: It shifts the mind from resisting inevitability to meeting it without panic.

bhagwad_gita::75.verse_sanskrit: अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत । अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥
bhagwad_gita::75.verse_hindi: हे भारत  सभी प्राणी जन्मसे पहले अप्रकट थे और मरनेके बाद अप्रकट हो जायँगे, केवल बीचमें ही प्रकट दीखते हैं ।  अतः इसमें शोक करनेकी बात ही क्या है ॥
bhagwad_gita::75.english_translation: All beings are unmanifest before birth and unmanifest after death; they are manifest only in between. Why grieve over that?
bhagwad_gita::75.translation_literal: अव्यक्तादीनि (unmanifest at the beginning) / भूतानि (beings) / व्यक्तमध्यानि (manifest in the middle) / भारत (O Bharata) / अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव (unmanifest at the end also) / तत्र (there) / का (what) / परिदेवना (lamentation)
bhagwad_gita::75.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::75.essence: What appears briefly was never meant to be clung to.
bhagwad_gita::75.simple_meaning: All beings are hidden before birth and hidden again after death. Since life is only a brief visible interval, there is no reason for grief.
bhagwad_gita::75.simple_insight: Sorrow loosens when you stop treating a passing form as permanent.
bhagwad_gita::75.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen by grief. Krishna continues his teaching about the body and the true self, saying that all beings are unmanifest before birth and after death, and only briefly visible in between. That makes lamentation over loss misplaced.
bhagwad_gita::75.modern_relevance: You are staring at a hospital monitor, waiting for news you cannot control. The shape of a life is changing in front of you. This verse steadies the heart by showing that appearance and disappearance are not the whole story.
bhagwad_gita::75.insight: It shifts attention from the temporary display to the larger continuity beneath it.

bhagwad_gita::76.verse_sanskrit: आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेनमाश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः । आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः श्रृणोतिश्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित् ॥
bhagwad_gita::76.verse_hindi: कोई इस शरीरीको आश्चर्यकी तरह देखता है और वैसे ही अन्य कोई इसका आश्चर्यकी तरह वर्णन करता है तथा अन्य कोई इसको आश्चर्यकी तरह सुनता है और इसको सुनकर भी कोई नहीं जानता ।  अर्थात यह शरीरी दुर्विज्ञेय है ॥
bhagwad_gita::76.english_translation: Some behold the inner being as wondrous; some speak of it as wondrous; some hear of it as wondrous; and even after hearing, no one truly knows it.
bhagwad_gita::76.translation_literal: आश्चर्यवत् (as wondrous) / पश्यति (beholds) / कश्चित् (someone) / एनम् (this one) / आश्चर्यवत् (as wondrous) / वदति (speaks) / तथा (thus) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / अन्यः (another) / आश्चर्यवत् (as wondrous) / च (and) / एनम् (this one) / अन्यः (another) / श्रृणोति (hears) / श्रुत्वा अपि (even after hearing) / एनम् (this one) / वेद (knows) / न (not) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / कश्चित् (anyone)
bhagwad_gita::76.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::76.essence: The true self remains mysterious even after endless hearing.
bhagwad_gita::76.simple_meaning: The true self is astonishing to behold, describe, and hear about, yet almost no one truly understands it.
bhagwad_gita::76.simple_insight: Curiosity is not enough; real understanding requires a deeper kind of seeing.
bhagwad_gita::76.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen by grief. Krishna deepens the teaching: the inner being is not an ordinary object of thought. People marvel at it, talk about it, listen to it, and still fail to grasp it fully.
bhagwad_gita::76.modern_relevance: You can read three books, hear five opinions, and still miss what matters. Some truths stay hidden until your attention becomes quieter than your analysis.
bhagwad_gita::76.insight: It shifts the mind from collecting descriptions to seeking direct understanding.

bhagwad_gita::77.verse_sanskrit: देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत । तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::77.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन सबके देहमें यह देही नित्य ही अवध्य है ।  इसलिये सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके लिये अर्थात् किसी भी प्राणीके लिये तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिये ॥
bhagwad_gita::77.english_translation: O descendant of Bharata, the embodied one in every body is eternal and cannot be slain. Therefore you should not grieve for any being.
bhagwad_gita::77.translation_literal: देही (the embodied one) / नित्यम् (always, eternally) / अवध्यः (not to be slain) / अयम् (this) / देहे (in the body) / सर्वस्य (of all) / भारत (O Bharata) / तस्मात् (therefore) / सर्वाणि (all) / भूतानि (beings) / न (not) / त्वम् (you) / शोचितुम् (to grieve) / अर्हसि (you should)
bhagwad_gita::77.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::77.essence: What is most real in a person cannot be killed, so grief loses its ground.
bhagwad_gita::77.simple_meaning: The true self in every body cannot be destroyed, so there is no reason to grieve for anyone.
bhagwad_gita::77.simple_insight: Loss feels different when you remember that what is deepest in a person cannot be cut off.
bhagwad_gita::77.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is frozen by grief and fear. Krishna answers by pointing to the deepest reality: the embodied one in every body is not destroyed. That truth undercuts Arjuna’s sorrow and prepares him for duty.
bhagwad_gita::77.modern_relevance: You stand beside a hospital bed, hearing a diagnosis you cannot fix. Panic says everything is ending; this verse says what is deepest in a person is beyond harm.
bhagwad_gita::77.insight: It shifts the mind from mourning the body alone to seeing the enduring presence within it.

bhagwad_gita::78.verse_sanskrit: स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि । धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाछ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::78.verse_hindi: अपने स्वधर्म क्षात्रधर्म को देखकर भी तुम्हें विकम्पित अर्थात् कर्तव्यकर्मसे विचलित नहीं होना चाहिये क्योंकि धर्ममय युद्धसे बढ़कर क्षत्रियके लिये दूसरा कोई कल्याणकारक कर्म नहीं है ॥
bhagwad_gita::78.english_translation: Considering your own duty, you should not waver. For a warrior, no action is more beneficial than a righteous battle.
bhagwad_gita::78.translation_literal: स्वधर्मम् (one's own duty) / अपि (even) / च (and) / अवेक्ष्य (considering) / न (not) / विकम्पितुम् (to waver) / अर्हसि (you should) / धर्म्यात् (from righteous) / हि (indeed) / युद्धात् (from battle) / श्रेयः (more beneficial) / अन्यत् (other) / क्षत्रियस्य (for a warrior) / न (not) / विद्यते (there is)
bhagwad_gita::78.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::78.essence: Right action can feel hard and still be the best choice.
bhagwad_gita::78.simple_meaning: Arjuna is told not to hesitate once he sees his own duty clearly. For a warrior, fighting for what is right is the best course.
bhagwad_gita::78.simple_insight: Clarity can end inner conflict. Once duty is seen, wavering becomes unnecessary.
bhagwad_gita::78.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has dropped into doubt while the armies wait. Krishna answers the paralysis directly: for a warrior, righteous battle is not a failure of morality but the clearest expression of it.
bhagwad_gita::78.modern_relevance: You are standing at the door, phone in hand, about to send the message you have delayed for weeks. The discomfort is real, but the right action does not disappear because it feels hard.
bhagwad_gita::78.insight: It shifts you from hesitation to committed action when your role and responsibility are already clear.

bhagwad_gita::79.verse_sanskrit: यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम् । सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::79.verse_hindi: अपनेआप प्राप्त हुआ युद्ध खुला हुआ स्वर्गका दरवाजा भी है ।  हे पृथानन्दन  वे क्षत्रिय बड़े सुखी भाग्यशाली हैं, जिनको ऐसा युद्ध प्राप्त होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::79.english_translation: An unbidden battle is an open gate to higher realms. O Partha, fortunate are the warriors who receive such a war.
bhagwad_gita::79.translation_literal: यदृच्छया (by chance / unbidden) / च (and) / उपपन्नम् (obtained / come upon) / स्वर्गद्वारम् (gate to higher realms) / अपावृतम् (opened) / सुखिनः (fortunate) / क्षत्रियाः (warriors) / पार्थ (O Partha) / लभन्ते (receive / obtain) / युद्धम् (battle) / ईदृशम् (such)
bhagwad_gita::79.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::79.essence: A righteous burden can become the highest opening.
bhagwad_gita::79.simple_meaning: A warrior who is given a righteous battle has a rare chance to act with honor and courage. Krishna calls such an opportunity a doorway to a higher realm.
bhagwad_gita::79.simple_insight: Hard duty can be a privilege, not a burden.
bhagwad_gita::79.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is frozen by grief. Krishna answers by reframing the war: for a warrior, this is not random violence but a rare righteous duty. Such a battle is presented as a doorway to a higher realm.
bhagwad_gita::79.modern_relevance: You are handed the hard conversation you hoped would disappear: telling the truth, ending the false peace, or standing up when silence would be easier. The moment is costly, but it is also clean.
bhagwad_gita::79.insight: It shifts the mind from avoiding difficulty to recognizing honorable obligation when it appears.

bhagwad_gita::80.verse_sanskrit: अथ चैत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि । ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::80.verse_hindi: अब अगर तू यह धर्ममय युद्ध नहीं करेगा, तो अपने धर्म और कीर्तिका त्याग करके पापको प्राप्त होगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::80.english_translation: If you do not fight this righteous war, you will abandon your duty and honor and incur blame.
bhagwad_gita::80.translation_literal: अथ (then) / च (and) / एत् (this) / त्वम् (you) / इमम् (this) / धर्म्यम् (righteous) / संग्रामम् (war) / न (not) / करिष्यसि (will do) / ततः (then) / स्वधर्मम् (one's own duty) / कीर्तिम् (honor) / च (and) / हित्वा (having abandoned) / पापम् (blame / wrongdoing) / अवाप्स्यसि (you will obtain)
bhagwad_gita::80.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::80.essence: Avoiding the right duty does not protect you; it stains you.
bhagwad_gita::80.simple_meaning: Refusing a just battle would mean abandoning your duty and honor, and that choice would bring blame.
bhagwad_gita::80.simple_insight: Avoiding the hard right thing can feel safer, but it leaves a heavier mark than action.
bhagwad_gita::80.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna answers his collapse with hard clarity. After saying this battle is righteous, Krishna warns that refusing it would mean abandoning the role Arjuna was born to carry.
bhagwad_gita::80.modern_relevance: You’re staring at a message you know you must send, because staying silent will hurt more. The fear of discomfort is real, but so is the cost of walking away from what you know is right.
bhagwad_gita::80.insight: It shifts the mind from fear-based avoidance to responsibility for the action that preserves integrity.

bhagwad_gita::81.verse_sanskrit: अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम् । संभावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::81.verse_hindi: और सब प्राणी भी तेरी सदा रहनेवाली अपकीर्तिका कथन अर्थात निंदा करेंगे ।  वह अपकीर्ति सम्मानित मनुष्यके लिये मृत्युसे भी बढ़कर दुःखदायी होती है ॥
bhagwad_gita::81.english_translation: And all beings will speak of your everlasting disgrace. For an honored person, disgrace is worse than death.
bhagwad_gita::81.translation_literal: अकीर्तिम् (disgrace) / च (and) / अपि (also) / भूतानि (beings) / कथयिष्यन्ति (will speak) / ते (of you) / अव्ययाम् (everlasting) / संभावितस्य (of one who has been honored) / च (and) / अकीर्तिः (disgrace) / मरणात् (than death) / अतिरिच्यते (is greater)
bhagwad_gita::81.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::81.essence: A honored life can be wounded more by shame than by death.
bhagwad_gita::81.simple_meaning: People will keep speaking of your disgrace, and for someone who has been honored, that shame feels worse than death.
bhagwad_gita::81.simple_insight: Honor can feel more fragile than life itself, and avoiding your duty can wound it deeply.
bhagwad_gita::81.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has lowered his bow and is wavering. Krishna warns him that if he turns away now, the world will remember not his greatness but his disgrace. For a warrior known for honor, that loss cuts deeper than death.
bhagwad_gita::81.modern_relevance: You walk out of a room knowing the hard truth but choosing silence. The image that follows you is not comfort — it is the version of yourself that backed away.
bhagwad_gita::81.insight: It shifts the mind from fearing pain to fearing the loss of integrity.

bhagwad_gita::82.verse_sanskrit: भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः । येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::82.verse_hindi: महारथीलोग तुझे भयके कारण युद्धसे उपरत हटा हुआ मानेंगे ।  जिनकी धारणामें तू बहुमान्य हो चुका है, उनकी दृष्टिमें तू लघुताको प्राप्त हो जायगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::82.english_translation: The great warriors will think you withdrew from battle out of fear. Those who once held you in high regard will see you as small.
bhagwad_gita::82.translation_literal: भयात् (from fear) / रणात् (from battle) / उपरतम् (withdrawn) / मंस्यन्ते (they will think) / त्वाम् (you) / महारथाः (great warriors) / येषाम् (of whom) / च (and) / त्वम् (you) / बहुमतः (highly regarded) / भूत्वा (having become) / यास्यसि (you will go) / लाघवम् (to smallness / low status)
bhagwad_gita::82.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::82.essence: Retreat from duty, and respect turns to shrinkage.
bhagwad_gita::82.simple_meaning: If Arjuna stops fighting, the great warriors will assume he fled from fear. People who respected him will now look down on him.
bhagwad_gita::82.simple_insight: Avoiding the hard act can cost you the respect you already earned.
bhagwad_gita::82.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna presses him to act. Krishna warns that if Arjuna steps back now, the strongest warriors will read it as fear, and the honour he once held will shrink before their eyes.
bhagwad_gita::82.modern_relevance: You back out of the difficult conversation at the last minute, and everyone notices. The silence protects you for a moment, then quietly rewrites how people see you.
bhagwad_gita::82.insight: It shifts the mind from protecting comfort to protecting integrity under pressure.

bhagwad_gita::83.verse_sanskrit: अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून् वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः । निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::83.verse_hindi: तेरे शत्रुलोग तेरी सार्मथ्यकी निन्दा करते हुए न कहनेयोग्य बहुतसे वचन भी कहेंगे ।  उससे बढ़कर और दुःखकी बात क्या होगी ॥
bhagwad_gita::83.english_translation: Your enemies will speak many unworthy words, mocking your strength. What could be more painful than that?
bhagwad_gita::83.translation_literal: अवाच्यवादान् (unworthy words) / च (and) / बहून् (many) / वदिष्यन्ति (they will speak) / तव (your) / अहिताः (enemies) / निन्दन्तः (mocking) / तव (your) / सामर्थ्यम् (strength) / ततः (than that) / दुःखतरम् (more painful) / नु (indeed) / किम् (what)
bhagwad_gita::83.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::83.essence: Public shame can hurt more than physical danger.
bhagwad_gita::83.simple_meaning: Your enemies will mock your ability and say cruel things about you. For a respected person, that kind of public shame can feel worse than death.
bhagwad_gita::83.simple_insight: Shame can sting harder than pain when your identity is on the line.
bhagwad_gita::83.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna presses him to act. After warning him about disgrace, Krishna adds that enemies will ridicule his strength itself. The verse deepens Arjuna's fear of public humiliation.
bhagwad_gita::83.modern_relevance: You back out of the hard conversation, and later people call you weak behind your back. The wound is not the criticism itself — it is watching your own courage get rewritten.
bhagwad_gita::83.insight: It exposes how fear of ridicule can paralyze action, and pushes the mind back toward duty.

bhagwad_gita::84.verse_sanskrit: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् । तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥
bhagwad_gita::84.verse_hindi: अगर युद्धमें तू मारा जायगा तो तुझे स्वर्गकी प्राप्ति होगी और अगर युद्धमें तू जीत जायगा तो पृथ्वीका राज्य भोगेगा ।  अतः हे कुन्तीनन्दन तू युद्धके लिये निश्चय करके खड़ा हो जा ॥
bhagwad_gita::84.english_translation: If you are killed, you will attain heaven; if you win, you will enjoy the kingdom. Therefore, rise, Kaunteya, and fight with resolve.
bhagwad_gita::84.translation_literal: हतो (killed) / वा (or) / प्राप्स्यसि (you will attain) / स्वर्गं (heaven) / जित्वा (having won) / वा (or) / भोक्ष्यसे (you will enjoy) / महीम् (the earth) / तस्मात् (therefore) / उत्तिष्ठ (rise) / कौन्तेय (Kaunteya) / युद्धाय (for battle) / कृतनिश्चयः (with firm resolve)
bhagwad_gita::84.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::84.essence: Act now; the result does not cancel the duty.
bhagwad_gita::84.simple_meaning: Arjuna is told to stand up and fight without wavering. Whether he wins or dies, he must do what stands before him now.
bhagwad_gita::84.simple_insight: Courage grows when the outcome stops being the reason to act.
bhagwad_gita::84.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen while two armies wait. Krishna answers his fear by framing battle as unavoidable duty: death brings one result, victory another, but action itself must still happen.
bhagwad_gita::84.modern_relevance: You are staring at the message that could end a relationship or save one. Either way, the longer you delay, the heavier it becomes. Krishna’s answer is simple: decide, then stand up.
bhagwad_gita::84.insight: It shifts the mind from outcome anxiety to firm action in the present.

bhagwad_gita::85.verse_sanskrit: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ । ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::85.verse_hindi: जयपराजय, लाभहानि और सुखदुःखको समान करके फिर युद्धमें लग जा ।  इस प्रकार युद्ध करनेसे तू पापको प्राप्त नहीं होगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::85.english_translation: Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike. Then enter the battle; you will not incur wrongdoing.
bhagwad_gita::85.translation_literal: सुखदुःखे (pleasure and pain) / समे (equal) / कृत्वा (having made) / लाभालाभौ (gain and loss) / जयाजयौ (victory and defeat) / ततः (then) / युद्धाय (for battle) / युज्यस्व (be engaged) / न (not) / एवम् (thus) / पापम् (wrongdoing) / अवाप्स्यसि (you will obtain)
bhagwad_gita::85.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::85.essence: Equanimity frees action from the stain of panic and craving.
bhagwad_gita::85.simple_meaning: Stay steady through pleasure and pain, success and failure. Act from that balance, and your action will not bind you.
bhagwad_gita::85.simple_insight: Inner steadiness makes hard action possible without guilt or panic.
bhagwad_gita::85.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen. Krishna pushes him one step further: do not let pleasure, pain, victory, or defeat shake your mind. From that steadiness, fight without staining yourself.
bhagwad_gita::85.modern_relevance: You open the email that could end a friendship or save one. Your hands shake, but the decision still has to be made. This verse asks for balance before the next move.
bhagwad_gita::85.insight: It shifts attention from emotional reaction to even-minded action under pressure.

bhagwad_gita::86.verse_sanskrit: एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां श्रृणु । बुद्ध्यायुक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::86.verse_hindi: हे पार्थ यह समबुद्धि तेरे लिए पहले सांख्ययोगमें कही गयी, अब तू इसको कर्मयोगके विषयमें सुन जिस समबुद्धिसे युक्त हुआ तू कर्मबन्धनका त्याग कर देगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::86.english_translation: This wisdom has been taught to you in Sankhya. Now hear it in yoga. Equipped with this understanding, Arjuna, you will cast off the bondage of action.
bhagwad_gita::86.translation_literal: एषा (this) / ते (to you) / अभिहिता (has been taught) / सांख्ये (in Sankhya) / बुद्धिः (wisdom) / योगे (in yoga) / तु (now) / इमाम् (this) / श्रृणु (hear) / बुद्ध्या (with understanding) / युक्तः (equipped) / यया (by which) / पार्थ (Arjuna) / कर्मबन्धम् (bondage of action) / प्रहास्यसि (you will cast off)
bhagwad_gita::86.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::86.essence: Clear understanding frees action from bondage.
bhagwad_gita::86.simple_meaning: Krishna says the same wisdom has already been explained as knowledge, and now he will explain it as action. With this clear understanding, Arjuna can break free from the bondage created by action.
bhagwad_gita::86.simple_insight: The same truth can free you both in thought and in action.
bhagwad_gita::86.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before battle. Krishna has already spoken of the self through wisdom, and now he turns to action. He says this same understanding will free Arjuna from being trapped by what he does.
bhagwad_gita::86.modern_relevance: You understand the principle in a quiet room, then face the hard conversation. The real test is whether that clarity still holds when action begins.
bhagwad_gita::86.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing knowledge and action as separate to seeing action as the expression of clear understanding.

bhagwad_gita::87.verse_sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
bhagwad_gita::87.verse_hindi: मनुष्यलोकमें इस समबुद्धिरूप धर्मके आरम्भका नाश नहीं होता, इसके अनुष्ठानका उलटा फल भी नहीं होता और इसका थोड़ासा भी अनुष्ठान जन्ममरणरूप महान् भयसे रक्षा कर लेता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::87.english_translation: In this human world, no effort toward this steady wisdom is ever lost. No harmful result comes from it. Even a little practice of this dharma protects one from great fear.
bhagwad_gita::87.translation_literal: न इह (not here/in this world) / अभिक्रम-नाशः (loss of beginning effort) / अस्ति (there is) / प्रत्यवायः (reverse result or harmful consequence) / न (not) / विद्यते (is found) / स्वल्पम् (a little) / अपि (even) / अस्य (of this) / धर्मस्य (of dharma) / त्रायते (protects) / महतः (from great) / भयात् (fear)
bhagwad_gita::87.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::87.essence: Even a tiny start on the right path protects you from fear.
bhagwad_gita::87.simple_meaning: Even a small beginning in this discipline is never wasted, never backfires, and can protect you from deep fear.
bhagwad_gita::87.simple_insight: You can begin imperfectly without dread. Small practice still counts and still changes you.
bhagwad_gita::87.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield as the war waits. After teaching steady action, he reassures him that even a small step in this path is never wasted, never harmful, and can free a person from the fear that keeps them stuck.
bhagwad_gita::87.modern_relevance: You finally open the meditation app after weeks of avoidance, sit for three minutes, and wonder whether it matters. It matters more than you think.
bhagwad_gita::87.insight: It shifts the mind from all-or-nothing thinking to trusting small, sincere practice.

bhagwad_gita::88.verse_sanskrit: व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन । बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::88.verse_hindi: हे कुरुनन्दन इस समबुद्धिकी प्राप्तिके विषयमें व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धि एक ही होती है ।  अव्यवसायी मनुष्योंकी बुद्धियाँ अनन्त और बहुशाखाओंवाली ही होती हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::88.english_translation: O son of the Kurus, the resolute intellect is one-pointed here. The intellect of the irresolute is many-branched and endless.
bhagwad_gita::88.translation_literal: व्यवसायात्मिका (resolute) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / एका (one) / इह (here) / कुरुनन्दन (O son of the Kurus) / बहुशाखाः (many-branched) / हि (indeed) / अनन्ताः (endless) / च (and) / बुद्धयः (intellects) / अव्यवसायिनाम् (of the irresolute)
bhagwad_gita::88.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::88.essence: Resolute seeing unifies the mind; hesitation multiplies it.
bhagwad_gita::88.simple_meaning: A focused mind has one clear direction, while an unfocused mind keeps branching into endless doubts and options.
bhagwad_gita::88.simple_insight: Clarity feels lighter than indecision. One firm choice calms the whole mind.
bhagwad_gita::88.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen between duty and grief. Krishna explains that the mind seeking freedom needs one steady resolve, not a dozen wavering arguments. This verse names the difference between clarity and inner fragmentation.
bhagwad_gita::88.modern_relevance: You have three tabs open, four messages unanswered, and one hard decision you keep postponing. The problem is not too little information — it is a mind that refuses one clear direction.
bhagwad_gita::88.insight: It shifts attention from scattered possibilities to a single settled intention.

bhagwad_gita::89.verse_sanskrit: यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः । वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::89.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन  जो कामनाओंमें तन्मय हो रहे हैं, स्वर्गको ही श्रेष्ठ माननेवाले हैं, वेदोंमें कहे हुए सकाम कर्मोंमें प्रीति रखनेवाले हैं, भोगोंके सिवाय और कुछ है ही नहीं  ऐसा कहनेवाले हैं, वे अविवेकी मनुष्य इस प्रकारकी जिस पुष्पित दिखाऊ शोभायुक्त वाणीको कहा करते हैं, जो कि जन्मरूपी कर्मफलको देनेवाली है तथा भोग और ऐश्वर्यकी प्राप्तिके लिये बहुतसी क्रियाओंका वर्णन करनेवाली है ॥
bhagwad_gita::89.english_translation: The unwise speak flowery words. They delight in the ritual sections of the Vedas and say nothing else exists.
bhagwad_gita::89.translation_literal: याम् (which) / इमाम् (this) / पुष्पिताम् (flowery, ornamented) / वाचम् (speech) / प्रवदन्ति (they speak) / अविपश्चितः (the unwise) / वेदवादरताः (delighting in Vedic discourse) / पार्थ (O Partha) / न (not) / अन्यत् (anything else) / अस्ति (there is) / इति (thus) / वादिनः (those who say)
bhagwad_gita::89.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::89.essence: Beautiful words can hide a mind trapped by desire.
bhagwad_gita::89.simple_meaning: Ignorant people speak in attractive, polished language that promises pleasure and reward. They get stuck in ritual talk and claim there is nothing beyond it.
bhagwad_gita::89.simple_insight: Not every beautiful promise is wisdom; some words are designed to seduce, not free you.
bhagwad_gita::89.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has lowered his bow and Krishna begins stripping away confusion. After warning him about shallow understanding, Krishna points to people who dress desire in sacred language and treat reward-seeking as the whole of life.
bhagwad_gita::89.modern_relevance: A polished video ad tells you that one purchase will fix your emptiness. Krishna would call that flowered speech: attractive, persuasive, and built to keep desire spinning.
bhagwad_gita::89.insight: It teaches you to distrust language that flatters craving and narrows reality to immediate reward.

bhagwad_gita::90.verse_sanskrit: कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम् । क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति ॥
bhagwad_gita::90.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन  जो कामनाओंमें तन्मय हो रहे हैं, स्वर्गको ही श्रेष्ठ माननेवाले हैं, वेदोंमें कहे हुए सकाम कर्मोंमें प्रीति रखनेवाले हैं, भोगोंके सिवाय और कुछ है ही नहीं  ऐसा कहनेवाले हैं, वे अविवेकी मनुष्य इस प्रकारकी जिस पुष्पित दिखाऊ शोभायुक्त वाणीको कहा करते हैं, जो कि जन्मरूपी कर्मफलको देनेवाली है तथा भोग और ऐश्वर्यकी प्राप्तिके लिये बहुतसी क्रियाओंका वर्णन करनेवाली है ॥
bhagwad_gita::90.english_translation: Those without clear seeing speak flowery words that promise birth and action-fruit, and describe many rites for enjoyment and power.
bhagwad_gita::90.translation_literal: कामात्मानः (those whose minds are full of desire) / स्वर्गपरा (with heaven as their highest aim) / जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम् (giving the fruits of birth and action) / क्रियाविशेषबहुलाम् (full of many special rites) / भोगैश्वर्यगतिम् (a path to enjoyment and power) / प्रति (toward)
bhagwad_gita::90.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::90.essence: Flowery promises can keep desire alive while pretending to guide you.
bhagwad_gita::90.simple_meaning: People driven by desire praise rituals that promise pleasure, status, and future rewards. Their words sound attractive, but they keep the mind chasing more rewards.
bhagwad_gita::90.simple_insight: Not every impressive teaching frees you. Some teachings only dress up craving.
bhagwad_gita::90.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna begins separating clear seeing from desire-driven speech. After warning about flowery promises, he points to teachings that lure people toward enjoyment, status, and future reward instead of freedom.
bhagwad_gita::90.modern_relevance: A polished ad, a glossy seminar, a mentor promising status if you just follow the system — it all sounds convincing until you notice it is feeding craving, not clearing it.
bhagwad_gita::90.insight: It trains you to spot teachings that increase wanting instead of reducing it.

bhagwad_gita::91.verse_sanskrit: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम् । व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥
bhagwad_gita::91.verse_hindi: उस पुष्पित वाणीसे जिसका अन्तःकरण हर लिया गया है अर्थात् भोगोंकी तरफ खिंच गया है और जो भोग तथा ऐश्वर्यमें अत्यन्त आसक्त हैं, उन मनुष्योंकी परमात्मामें निश्चयात्मिका बुद्धि नहीं होती ॥
bhagwad_gita::91.english_translation: For those whose minds are carried away by pleasure and power, steadfast determination in meditation does not arise.
bhagwad_gita::91.translation_literal: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानाम् (of those attached to enjoyment and power) / तया (by that) / अपहृतचेतसाम् (whose minds have been stolen) / व्यवसायात्मिका (one-pointed, resolute) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / समाधौ (in meditation / absorbed stillness) / न (not) / विधीयते (arises / is established)
bhagwad_gita::91.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::91.essence: Craving scatters the mind before wisdom can settle.
bhagwad_gita::91.simple_meaning: People who are pulled toward pleasure and power lose clear judgment. Their mind cannot settle into steady focus on the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::91.simple_insight: Clarity returns when craving stops steering the mind.
bhagwad_gita::91.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen before war. Krishna explains why some people never reach firm understanding: their minds are stolen by pleasure and power, so they cannot rest in steady insight. This verse names the inner obstruction before the next instruction.
bhagwad_gita::91.modern_relevance: You open your phone for one quick check, and an hour disappears into wanting more. The mind that keeps chasing reward cannot hold a steady line.
bhagwad_gita::91.insight: It shifts attention from external reward to inner steadiness as the basis of right understanding.

bhagwad_gita::92.verse_sanskrit: त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन । निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥
bhagwad_gita::92.verse_hindi: वेद तीनों गुणोंके कार्यका ही वर्णन करनेवाले हैं हे अर्जुन तू तीनों गुणोंसे रहित हो जा, निर्द्वन्द्व हो जा, निरन्तर नित्य वस्तु परमात्मा में स्थित हो जा, योगक्षेमकी चाहना भी मत रख और परमात्मपरायण हो जा ॥
bhagwad_gita::92.english_translation: The Vedas deal with the three qualities. Arjuna, rise beyond the three qualities, beyond opposites, fixed in lasting reality, free from concern for gain and security, and established in the true self.
bhagwad_gita::92.translation_literal: त्रैगुण्यविषया (concerned with the three qualities) / वेदा (the Vedas) / निस्त्रैगुण्यो (one beyond the three qualities) / भव (be) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / निर्द्वन्द्वो (free from opposites) / नित्यसत्त्वस्थो (steadfast in the ever-real) / निर्योगक्षेमः (free from concern for acquisition and preservation) / आत्मवान् (established in the true self)
bhagwad_gita::92.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::92.essence: Freedom begins when gain and loss stop defining you.
bhagwad_gita::92.simple_meaning: The sacred texts describe the world of changing forces, but Krishna tells Arjuna to rise above them. He should stop chasing comfort and security, and stay rooted in what is unchanging.
bhagwad_gita::92.simple_insight: There is relief in not being ruled by constant wanting, fear, or comparison.
bhagwad_gita::92.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before the war. Krishna now moves from duty to inner freedom: the Vedas describe worldly patterns, but Arjuna must stand beyond them, unshaken by gain, loss, or duality.
bhagwad_gita::92.modern_relevance: You are refreshing your bank app for the tenth time, waiting for reassurance. The verse says the deeper life begins when you stop living by gain, fear, and the next update.
bhagwad_gita::92.insight: It shifts attention from managing outcomes to resting in what does not change.

bhagwad_gita::93.verse_sanskrit: यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः संप्लुतोदके । तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः ॥
bhagwad_gita::93.verse_hindi: सब तरफसे परिपूर्ण महान् जलाशयके प्राप्त होनेपर छोटे गड्ढों में भरे जल में मनुष्यका जितना प्रयोजन रहता है अर्थात् कुछ भी प्रयोजन नहीं रहता, वेदों और शास्त्रोंको तत्त्वसे जाननेवाले ब्रह्मज्ञानीका सम्पूर्ण वेदोंमें उतना ही प्रयोजन रहता है अर्थात् कुछ भी प्रयोजन नहीं रहता ॥
bhagwad_gita::93.english_translation: For one who understands, all the Vedas are as useful as a small puddle when a great reservoir of water is at hand.
bhagwad_gita::93.translation_literal: यावान् (as much) / अर्थः (use, purpose) / उदपाने (in a small water-source) / सर्वतः (from all sides) / संप्लुतोदके (in a fully flooded reservoir) / तावान् (that much) / सर्वेषु (in all) / वेदेषु (in the Vedas) / ब्राह्मणस्य (for the knower of Brahman) / विजानतः (for one who truly knows)
bhagwad_gita::93.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::93.essence: Complete understanding makes lesser sources unnecessary.
bhagwad_gita::93.simple_meaning: A person who truly understands the supreme reality needs the Vedas no more than a person beside a full reservoir needs a tiny puddle.
bhagwad_gita::93.simple_insight: There is relief in not needing endless guidance once the deeper truth is seen.
bhagwad_gita::93.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is overwhelmed by duty, grief, and contradiction. Krishna answers by showing that real understanding is not scattered across many rules and rituals. For the one who truly knows, the whole point has been grasped.
bhagwad_gita::93.modern_relevance: You have read every article, saved every thread, and still feel unsure before making the hard call. At some point, more input stops helping; clear seeing does.
bhagwad_gita::93.insight: It shifts the mind from collecting information to recognizing the decisive truth that makes excess instruction unnecessary.

bhagwad_gita::94.verse_sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
bhagwad_gita::94.verse_hindi: कर्तव्यकर्म करनेमें ही तेरा अधिकार है, फलोंमें कभी नहीं ।  अतः तू कर्मफलका हेतु भी मत बन और तेरी अकर्मण्यतामें भी आसक्ति न हो ॥
bhagwad_gita::94.english_translation: You have a right to action alone, never to its fruits. Do not become the cause of the result, and do not cling to inaction.
bhagwad_gita::94.translation_literal: कर्मणि (in action) / एव (only) / अधिकारः (right) / ते (your) / मा (not) / फलेषु (in fruits) / कदाचन (at any time) / मा (not) / कर्मफलहेतुः (cause of the fruit of action) / भूः (become) / मा (not) / ते (your) / सङ्गः (attachment) / अस्तु (let there be) / अकर्मणि (in inaction)
bhagwad_gita::94.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::94.essence: Action belongs to you; the result does not.
bhagwad_gita::94.simple_meaning: You control your action, not what it produces. Do your duty without chasing the reward or getting attached to doing nothing.
bhagwad_gita::94.simple_insight: There is relief in giving your full effort without carrying the burden of the result.
bhagwad_gita::94.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is frozen and Krishna begins rebuilding his sense of duty. Here Krishna draws the first hard line: act because it is yours to do, not because you can own what comes after.
bhagwad_gita::94.modern_relevance: You send the apology text after midnight, then keep rereading it for the perfect reply. This verse cuts that loop: speak, act, and stop trying to control the response.
bhagwad_gita::94.insight: It shifts attention from controlling outcomes to carrying out the action cleanly.

bhagwad_gita::95.verse_sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::95.verse_hindi: हे धनञ्जय  तू आसक्तिका त्याग करके सिद्धिअसिद्धिमें सम होकर योगमें स्थित हुआ कर्मोंको कर क्योंकि समत्व ही योग कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::95.english_translation: O Dhananjaya, perform actions while established in yoga, abandoning attachment. Remain equal in success and failure, for equanimity is called yoga.
bhagwad_gita::95.translation_literal: योगस्थः (established in yoga) / कुरु (do) / कर्माणि (actions) / सङ्गं (attachment) / त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) / धनञ्जय (O Dhananjaya) / सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः (in success and failure) / समः (equal) / भूत्वा (having become) / समत्वं (equanimity) / योगः (yoga) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::95.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::95.simple_meaning: Keep doing your duty without clinging to results. Stay steady whether things work out or not; that steady balance is yoga.
bhagwad_gita::95.simple_insight: You can stay calm without stopping action. Inner balance makes effort cleaner and less painful.
bhagwad_gita::95.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before the war. Krishna has already told him to act without craving results; now he sharpens that teaching: stay balanced in victory and defeat, because that inner evenness is the heart of yoga.
bhagwad_gita::95.modern_relevance: You send the message, then stare at the screen waiting for a reply. The mind rises and falls with every notification; this verse teaches you to keep your centre anyway.
bhagwad_gita::95.insight: It shifts attention from outcome-chasing to steady action, so success and failure stop controlling the mind.

bhagwad_gita::96.verse_sanskrit: दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय । बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥
bhagwad_gita::96.verse_hindi: बुद्धियोगसमता की अपेक्षा सकामकर्म दूरसे अत्यन्त ही निकृष्ट है ।  अतः हे धनञ्जय  तू बुद्धि समता का आश्रय ले क्योंकि फलके हेतु बननेवाले अत्यन्त दीन हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::96.english_translation: Action driven by craving is far below the steadiness of clear discernment. Seek refuge in clear discernment, for those who chase results are pitiable.
bhagwad_gita::96.translation_literal: दूरेण (far) / हि (indeed) / अवरम् (inferior) / कर्म (action) / बुद्धियोगात् (to the yoga of discernment) / धनञ्जय (O Dhananjaya) / बुद्धौ (in discernment) / शरणम् (refuge) / अन्विच्छ (seek) / कृपणाः (pitiable ones) / फलहेतवः (those who are motivated by results)
bhagwad_gita::96.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::96.essence: Clear discernment is richer than reward-chasing.
bhagwad_gita::96.simple_meaning: Action done for rewards is lower than action guided by clear discernment. Krishna tells Arjuna to rely on that steadiness instead of craving outcomes.
bhagwad_gita::96.simple_insight: You can stop measuring your worth by what you get back.
bhagwad_gita::96.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Arjuna is still frozen between battle and conscience. Krishna sharpens the teaching: action ruled by reward is inferior to action guided by steady discernment, and the wise refuge is the clear mind.
bhagwad_gita::96.modern_relevance: You send the message, then keep checking for the reply every two minutes. The mind that needs a payoff has already lost its steadiness.
bhagwad_gita::96.insight: It shifts attention from outcome-chasing to the stability of right seeing.

bhagwad_gita::97.verse_sanskrit: बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते । तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::97.verse_hindi: बुद्धिसमता से युक्त मनुष्य यहाँ जीवित अवस्थामें ही पुण्य और पाप दोनोंका त्याग कर देता है ।  अतः तू योगसमता में लग जा, क्योंकि योग ही कर्मोंमें कुशलता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::97.english_translation: One who is united with clear discernment casts off both good and bad deeds in this life. Therefore, devote yourself to yoga, for yoga is skill in action.
bhagwad_gita::97.translation_literal: बुद्धियुक्तः (one united with discerning mind) / जहाति (casts off) / इह (here, in this life) / उभे (both) / सुकृतदुष्कृते (good deed and bad deed) / तस्मात् (therefore) / योगाय (for yoga) / युज्यस्व (be devoted) / योगः (yoga) / कर्मसु (in actions) / कौशलम् (skill, dexterity)
bhagwad_gita::97.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::97.essence: Clear action frees you from the weight of both success and failure.
bhagwad_gita::97.simple_meaning: Clear discernment lets a person rise above both merit and fault. Krishna tells Arjuna to take up yoga, because true yoga is skill in action.
bhagwad_gita::97.simple_insight: You do not have to be trapped by the moral weight of every result.
