bhagwad_gita::97.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen between action and fear. Krishna deepens his teaching: when the mind is steady, a person is no longer bound by the usual grip of merit and fault. That is why he urges Arjuna toward yoga.
bhagwad_gita::97.modern_relevance: You send the message, then keep rereading it for hours, trying to judge whether it was right or wrong. This verse says the steady mind stops living inside that loop and simply acts cleanly.
bhagwad_gita::97.insight: It shifts attention from moral self-judgment to disciplined action with clarity.

bhagwad_gita::98.verse_sanskrit: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः । जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::98.verse_hindi: समतायुक्त मनीषी साधक कर्मजन्य फलका त्याग करके जन्मरूप बन्धनसे मुक्त होकर निर्विकार पदको प्राप्त हो जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::98.english_translation: Wise people, united in clarity, abandon the fruit born of action and reach the flawless state, free from the bondage of birth.
bhagwad_gita::98.translation_literal: कर्मजं (born of action) / बुद्धियुक्ताः (those united with discerning clarity) / हि (indeed) / फलम् (fruit) / त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) / मनीषिणः (wise people) / जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः (freed from the bondage of birth) / पदम् (state) / गच्छन्ति (they go) / अनामयम् (flawless, free from affliction)
bhagwad_gita::98.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::98.essence: Freedom comes when action is done without clutching its reward.
bhagwad_gita::98.simple_meaning: Wise people let go of the results of their actions. That freedom breaks the chain that keeps them bound to repeated birth and suffering.
bhagwad_gita::98.simple_insight: You can do the work and stop clutching the reward. That loosening brings real relief.
bhagwad_gita::98.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna keeps teaching the same turning point: act with clear understanding, but do not cling to what the action produces. That release leads beyond bondage.
bhagwad_gita::98.modern_relevance: You send the hard email, then keep checking for a reply every five minutes. The action is complete, but your mind keeps demanding ownership of the result. This verse cuts that cord.
bhagwad_gita::98.insight: It shifts attention from owning outcomes to doing the work cleanly, so action no longer tightens the mind.

bhagwad_gita::99.verse_sanskrit: यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति । तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥
bhagwad_gita::99.verse_hindi: जिस समय तेरी बुद्धि मोहरूपी दलदलको तर जायगी, उसी समय तू सुने हुए और सुननेमें आनेवाले भोगोंसे वैराग्यको प्राप्त हो जायगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::99.english_translation: When your intellect crosses the swamp of delusion, you will grow dispassionate toward what has been heard and what remains to be heard.
bhagwad_gita::99.translation_literal: यदा (when) / ते (your) / मोहकलिलं (the swamp of delusion) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / व्यतितरिष्यति (will cross over) / तदा (then) / गन्तासि (you will go) / निर्वेदं (to dispassion) / श्रोतव्यस्य (of what is to be heard) / श्रुतस्य (of what has been heard) / च (and)
bhagwad_gita::99.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::99.essence: Clear seeing ends the pull of future pleasures.
bhagwad_gita::99.simple_meaning: When clear understanding rises above confusion, attachment to pleasures you have heard of or are still chasing naturally fades.
bhagwad_gita::99.simple_insight: Clarity itself loosens craving. You do not have to force detachment when confusion ends.
bhagwad_gita::99.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands shaken while Krishna keeps teaching him how to see. After explaining steady action, Krishna says that when the mind crosses the mud of delusion, craving for promised pleasures drops away on its own.
bhagwad_gita::99.modern_relevance: You finally read the message, and the fantasy collapses. The relationship, the job, the purchase, the applause — all of it looks smaller once the fog clears.
bhagwad_gita::99.insight: It shifts you from chasing experiences to seeing through their lure.

bhagwad_gita::100.verse_sanskrit: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला । समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::100.verse_hindi: जिस कालमें शास्त्रीय मतभेदोंसे विचलित हुई तेरी बुद्धि निश्चल हो जायगी और परमात्मामें अचल हो जायगी, उस कालमें तू योगको प्राप्त हो जायगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::100.english_translation: When your intellect, unmoved by conflicting teachings, becomes steady in complete stillness, you will attain yoga.
bhagwad_gita::100.translation_literal: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना (confused by conflicting teachings) / ते (your) / यदा (when) / स्थास्यति (will remain) / निश्चला (steady, unmoving) / समाधौ (in complete stillness) / अचला (unmoving) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / तदा (then) / योगम् (yoga) / अवाप्स्यसि (you will attain)
bhagwad_gita::100.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::100.essence: Yoga begins when the mind stops being pulled in every direction.
bhagwad_gita::100.simple_meaning: When your mind is no longer shaken by conflicting ideas and becomes completely steady, you reach yoga.
bhagwad_gita::100.simple_insight: Relief comes from knowing clarity is not forced; it settles when the mind stops being pulled around.
bhagwad_gita::100.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is trapped between arguments, duties, and fear. Krishna says that when the mind stops wavering under competing teachings and becomes steady in deep stillness, the state of yoga finally opens.
bhagwad_gita::100.modern_relevance: You have three tabs open, ten opinions in your head, and one hard choice in front of you. The answer does not come by adding more noise — it comes when the mind settles enough to see.
bhagwad_gita::100.insight: It shifts attention from intellectual churn to inner steadiness as the condition for clear action.

bhagwad_gita::101.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचस्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव । स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::101.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे केशव  परमात्मामें स्थित स्थिर बुद्धिवाले मनुष्यके क्या लक्षण होते हैं वह स्थिर बुद्धिवाला मनुष्य कैसे बोलता है, कैसे बैठता है और कैसे चलता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::101.english_translation: Arjuna said: O Kesava, what are the marks of one whose wisdom is steady and who is absorbed in stillness? How does a person of steady understanding speak, sit, and walk?
bhagwad_gita::101.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / स्थितप्रज्ञस्य (of one whose wisdom is steady) / का (what) / भाषा (mark or description) / समाधिस्थस्य (of one established in complete stillness) / केशव (O Kesava) / स्थितधीः (one of steady understanding) / किम् (how) / प्रभाषेत (would speak) / किम् (how) / आसीत (would sit) / व्रजेत (would walk) / किम् (what)
bhagwad_gita::101.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::101.essence: Steady wisdom must be recognizable in ordinary movement.
bhagwad_gita::101.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks how a person with steady wisdom behaves in daily life — how they speak, sit, and move.
bhagwad_gita::101.simple_insight: Real wisdom should show up in ordinary behavior, not just in ideas.
bhagwad_gita::101.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has just heard Krishna describe the mind that has crossed confusion. Before the war can begin, he asks for a practical sign: what does a person of steady wisdom actually look like in speech, posture, and movement?
bhagwad_gita::101.modern_relevance: You meet someone who stays calm under pressure and wonder, what makes them different? Arjuna asks the same thing before the hardest decision of his life.
bhagwad_gita::101.insight: It shifts attention from abstract understanding to visible conduct under pressure.

bhagwad_gita::102.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान् । आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::102.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे पृथानन्दन  जिस कालमें साधक मनोगत सम्पूर्ण कामनाओंका अच्छी तरह त्याग कर देता है और अपनेआपसे अपनेआपमें ही सन्तुष्ट रहता है, उस कालमें वह स्थितप्रज्ञ कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::102.english_translation: The divine said: When a person gives up all desires that arise in the mind, and is satisfied in the true self by the true self alone, that person is called steady in wisdom.
bhagwad_gita::102.translation_literal: श्री भगवानुवाच (the divine said) / प्रजहाति (gives up) / यदा (when) / कामान् (desires) / सर्वान् (all) / पार्थ (O Partha) / मनोगतान् (arising in the mind) / आत्मनि (in the true self) / एव (indeed) / आत्मना (by the true self) / तुष्टः (satisfied) / स्थितप्रज्ञः (steady in wisdom) / तदा (then) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::102.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::102.essence: Steadiness begins when desire no longer defines your sense of enough.
bhagwad_gita::102.simple_meaning: A person becomes steady in wisdom when all mental desires are released and contentment comes from within, not from outside things.
bhagwad_gita::102.simple_insight: There is relief in not needing anything extra to feel complete.
bhagwad_gita::102.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has asked what a truly steady person looks like. Krishna answers by describing the inner turning point: desire no longer rules the mind, and contentment comes from the true self itself.
bhagwad_gita::102.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the message, the praise — and still feel restless. This verse points to the deeper shift: stop waiting for outside approval to settle you.
bhagwad_gita::102.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing satisfaction to recognising contentment as inward and already available.

bhagwad_gita::103.verse_hindi: दुःखोंकी प्राप्ति होनेपर जिसके मनमें उद्वेग नहीं होता और सुखोंकी प्राप्ति होनेपर जिसके मनमें स्पृहा नहीं होती तथा जो राग, भय और क्रोधसे सर्वथा रहित हो गया है, वह मननशील मनुष्य स्थिरबुद्धि कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::103.english_translation: The steady-minded sage is unshaken by sorrow, free from craving in joy, and beyond attachment, fear, and anger.
bhagwad_gita::103.translation_literal: दुःखेषु (in sorrows) / अनुद्विग्न-मनाः (mind not agitated) / सुखेषु (in pleasures) / विगत-स्पृहः (free from craving) / वीत-राग-भय-क्रोधः (gone beyond attachment, fear, and anger) / स्थित-धीः (steady-minded) / मुनिः (sage) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::103.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::103.essence: Steadiness remains when pleasure and pain lose their grip.
bhagwad_gita::103.simple_meaning: A truly steady person stays calm in hardship, does not chase pleasure, and is free from attachment, fear, and anger.
bhagwad_gita::103.simple_insight: You do not have to be ruled by every rise and fall. Calm can remain while life changes.
bhagwad_gita::103.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna has asked what a person of steady understanding looks like. Krishna answers with a portrait of inner balance: the sage is not shaken by pain, does not chase pleasure, and is no longer driven by attachment, fear, or anger.
bhagwad_gita::103.modern_relevance: You get a painful message, then a flattering one, then another setback. Your mood whiplashes with each ping. This verse points to a steadier way: let events pass through without letting them seize the mind.
bhagwad_gita::103.insight: It shifts attention from chasing comfort to building inner steadiness that stays intact under praise, loss, and pressure.

bhagwad_gita::104.verse_sanskrit: यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम् । नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
bhagwad_gita::104.verse_hindi: सब जगह आसक्तिरहित हुआ जो मनुष्य उसउस शुभअशुभको प्राप्त करके न तो अभिनन्दित होता है और न द्वेष करता है, उसकी बुद्धि प्रतिष्ठित है ॥
bhagwad_gita::104.english_translation: One who feels no clinging anywhere, and neither rejoices nor hates when good or bad comes, has steady wisdom.
bhagwad_gita::104.translation_literal: यः (who) / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / अनभिस्नेहः (without clinging) / तत्-तत् (that-that) / प्राप्य (having obtained) / शुभ-अशुभम् (good and bad) / न (not) / अभिनन्दति (rejoices) / न (not) / द्वेष्टि (hates) / तस्य (of that one) / प्रज्ञा (wisdom) / प्रतिष्ठिता (firmly established)
bhagwad_gita::104.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::104.essence: Steady wisdom does not need life to feel favorable.
bhagwad_gita::104.simple_meaning: A person with steady wisdom does not cling to anything. When good or bad events happen, they neither get thrilled nor upset.
bhagwad_gita::104.simple_insight: You can meet life fully without being pulled around by every result.
bhagwad_gita::104.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna keeps describing the person whose mind no longer lurches with gain and loss. This verse sharpens that state: neither praise nor pain can disturb settled understanding.
bhagwad_gita::104.modern_relevance: You get the message that changed the plan is bad news, then the next hour brings unexpected praise. Both can hit the same inbox. This verse teaches you not to build your identity from either one.
bhagwad_gita::104.insight: It shifts attention from reacting to events toward remaining inwardly even as events change.

bhagwad_gita::105.verse_sanskrit: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
bhagwad_gita::105.verse_hindi: जिस तरह कछुआ अपने अङ्गोंको सब ओरसे समेट लेता है, ऐसे ही जिस कालमें यह कर्मयोगी इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंसे इन्द्रियोंको सब प्रकारसे समेट लेता हटा लेता है, तब उसकी बुद्धि प्रतिष्ठित हो जाती है ॥
bhagwad_gita::105.english_translation: When this one draws the senses fully back from sense-objects, like a tortoise withdrawing its limbs, wisdom is steady.
bhagwad_gita::105.translation_literal: यदा (when) / संहरते (withdraws) / च (and) / अयम् (this one) / कूर्मः (tortoise) / अङ्गानि (limbs) / इव (like) / सर्वशः (from all sides) / इन्द्रियाणि (the senses) / इन्द्रियार्थेभ्यः (from sense-objects) / तस्य (of that one) / प्रज्ञा (wisdom) / प्रतिष्ठिता (steadfast)
bhagwad_gita::105.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::105.essence: Steadiness begins when the senses stop running outward.
bhagwad_gita::105.simple_meaning: Wisdom becomes stable when the senses are pulled back from the things they chase, just as a tortoise draws in its limbs.
bhagwad_gita::105.simple_insight: You do not need to chase every attraction. Real steadiness begins when attention comes home.
bhagwad_gita::105.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna has been describing the person whose understanding no longer wavers. Here he gives the image: like a tortoise, the wise one draws the senses away from their objects, and the mind becomes steady.
bhagwad_gita::105.modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message, then three more tabs, then a video you did not mean to watch. The day starts leaking away the moment your attention keeps reaching outward.
bhagwad_gita::105.insight: It shifts the mind from constant reaching to deliberate withdrawal from distraction.

bhagwad_gita::106.verse_sanskrit: विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः । रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥
bhagwad_gita::106.verse_hindi: निराहारी इन्द्रियोंको विषयोंसे हटानेवाले मनुष्यके भी विषय तो निवृत्त हो जाते हैं, पर रस निवृत्त नहीं होता ।  परन्तु इस स्थितप्रज्ञ मनुष्यका तो रस भी परमात्मतत्त्वका अनुभव होनेसे निवृत्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::106.english_translation: Objects fall away from the self-denying person, but the taste for them remains. For the one who has seen the supreme reality, even that taste falls away.
bhagwad_gita::106.translation_literal: विषयाः (objects of the senses) / विनिवर्तन्ते (turn away) / निराहारस्य (of the one without intake) / देहिनः (of the embodied one) / रसवर्जम् (except for taste) / रसः (taste) / अपि (even) / अस्य (of this one) / परम् (the supreme) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / निवर्तते (turns away)
bhagwad_gita::106.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::106.essence: Craving ends only when a higher reality becomes more compelling.
bhagwad_gita::106.simple_meaning: Stopping the senses is not enough. The outer attraction may fade, but the inner taste remains until a higher reality is directly seen.
bhagwad_gita::106.simple_insight: Real freedom comes from seeing more clearly, not just forcing restraint.
bhagwad_gita::106.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna is explaining why mere suppression cannot solve inner bondage. Even if the senses are pulled back, the craving remains until a deeper vision replaces it.
bhagwad_gita::106.modern_relevance: You delete the app, mute the chat, and swear off the habit — yet the urge returns at midnight. The surface trigger is gone, but the deeper appetite still needs to be seen through.
bhagwad_gita::106.insight: It shifts the mind from suppression to transformation: remove the craving by changing what you truly value.

bhagwad_gita::107.verse_sanskrit: यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः । इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::107.verse_hindi: हे कुन्तीनन्दन रसबुद्धि रहनेसे यत्न करते हुए विद्वान् मनुष्यकी भी प्रमथनशील इन्द्रियाँ उसके मनको बलपूर्वक हर लेती हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::107.english_translation: Even for a wise person who strives, the turbulent senses can forcibly carry away the mind.
bhagwad_gita::107.translation_literal: यततः (for one striving) / हि (indeed) / अपि (even) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / पुरुषस्य (of a person) / विपश्चितः (of the wise) / इन्द्रियाणि (the senses) / प्रमाथीनि (restless, turbulent) / हरन्ति (carry away) / प्रसभं (forcibly) / मनः (the mind)
bhagwad_gita::107.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::107.simple_meaning: Even a thoughtful person who is trying hard can lose control when the senses become restless and drag the mind away.
bhagwad_gita::107.simple_insight: Willpower alone is not enough; the senses need training too.
bhagwad_gita::107.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has begun learning self-mastery from Krishna. After warning that desire remains even when objects are withdrawn, Krishna adds the harder truth: even a wise person can be overpowered by restless senses. The mind needs disciplined protection, not confidence alone.
bhagwad_gita::107.modern_relevance: You delete the app, silence the phone, and still reach for it. The urge returns from inside, and it can pull even a careful mind off course.
bhagwad_gita::107.insight: It shifts the focus from occasional restraint to steady discipline of the senses and mind.

bhagwad_gita::108.verse_sanskrit: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः । वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
bhagwad_gita::108.verse_hindi: कर्मयोगी साधक उन सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियोंको वशमें करके मेरे परायण होकर बैठे क्योंकि जिसकी इन्द्रियाँ वशमें हैं, उसकी बुद्धि प्रतिष्ठित है ॥
bhagwad_gita::108.english_translation: Having restrained all the senses, the disciplined one should sit devoted to Me. For one whose senses are under control, wisdom is firmly established.
bhagwad_gita::108.translation_literal: तानि (those) / सर्वाणि (all) / संयम्य (having restrained) / युक्तः (disciplined, aligned) / आसीत (should sit) / मत्परः (devoted to Me) / वशे (under control) / हि (indeed) / यस्य (whose) / इन्द्रियाणि (senses) / तस्य (of that one) / प्रज्ञा (wisdom) / प्रतिष्ठिता (firmly established)
bhagwad_gita::108.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::108.essence: Wisdom becomes steady only when the senses are no longer in charge.
bhagwad_gita::108.simple_meaning: Hold the senses in check and stay focused on the divine. When the senses are controlled, clear wisdom becomes steady.
bhagwad_gita::108.simple_insight: Self-control is not repression; it creates the inner steadiness needed for clear judgment.
bhagwad_gita::108.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is overwhelmed before the fight even begins. Krishna answers his confusion by pointing to inner discipline: control the senses, turn the mind toward the divine, and wisdom will stop wavering.
bhagwad_gita::108.modern_relevance: You open your phone to avoid one hard message and lose ten minutes. The real issue is not the screen — it is whether your senses are steering you or you are steering them.
bhagwad_gita::108.insight: It shifts attention from reacting to every impulse toward holding the senses steady so judgment can stay clear.

bhagwad_gita::109.verse_sanskrit: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते । सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥
bhagwad_gita::109.verse_hindi: विषयोंका चिन्तन करनेवाले मनुष्यकी उन विषयोंमें आसक्ति पैदा हो जाती है ।  आसक्तिसे कामना पैदा होती है ।  कामनासे क्रोध पैदा होता है ।  क्रोध होनेपर सम्मोह मूढ़भाव हो जाता है ।  सम्मोहसे स्मृति भ्रष्ट हो जाती है ।  स्मृति भ्रष्ट होनेपर बुद्धिका नाश हो जाता है ।  बुद्धिका नाश होनेपर मनुष्यका पतन हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::109.english_translation: Thinking about sense objects creates attachment to them. Attachment gives rise to desire; desire gives rise to anger.
bhagwad_gita::109.translation_literal: ध्यायतः (while thinking of) / विषयान् (sense objects) / पुंसः (for a person) / सङ्गः (attachment) / तेषु (to them) / उपजायते (arises) / सङ्गात् (from attachment) / संजायते (is born) / कामः (desire) / कामात् (from desire) / क्रोधः (anger) / अभिजायते (arises strongly)
bhagwad_gita::109.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::109.essence: What you dwell on becomes what you cling to, then what burns you.
bhagwad_gita::109.simple_meaning: Fixating on pleasures or objects creates attachment. Attachment turns into wanting, and wanting turns into anger when blocked.
bhagwad_gita::109.simple_insight: There is relief in catching the chain early, before a small craving hardens into a reaction you regret.
bhagwad_gita::109.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen and Krishna is tracing the inner mechanics of collapse. He shows how the mind falls step by step: thought, attachment, desire, anger, confusion, ruin. This verse explains why self-mastery matters.
bhagwad_gita::109.modern_relevance: You keep checking a message thread, then the silence starts to sting, then irritation takes over. The verse names that slide from fixation to fury before it owns you.
bhagwad_gita::109.insight: It teaches you to interrupt the chain at the first attachment, not after the anger has already taken root.

bhagwad_gita::110.verse_sanskrit: क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥
bhagwad_gita::110.verse_hindi: विषयोंका चिन्तन करनेवाले मनुष्यकी उन विषयोंमें आसक्ति पैदा हो जाती है ।  आसक्तिसे कामना पैदा होती है ।  कामनासे क्रोध पैदा होता है ।  क्रोध होनेपर सम्मोह मूढ़भाव हो जाता है ।  सम्मोहसे स्मृति भ्रष्ट हो जाती है ।  स्मृति भ्रष्ट होनेपर बुद्धिका नाश हो जाता है ।  बुद्धिका नाश होनेपर मनुष्यका पतन हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::110.english_translation: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, loss of discernment; from loss of discernment, ruin.
bhagwad_gita::110.translation_literal: क्रोधात् (from anger) / भवति (arises) / संमोहः (delusion) / संमोहात् (from delusion) / स्मृतिविभ्रमः (confusion of memory) / स्मृतिभ्रंशात् (from loss of memory) / बुद्धिनाशः (destruction of discernment) / बुद्धिनाशात् (from destruction of discernment) / प्रणश्यति (one is ruined)
bhagwad_gita::110.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::110.essence: Anger first distorts seeing, then destroys the mind that should guide action.
bhagwad_gita::110.simple_meaning: Anger starts a chain reaction: confusion, broken memory, lost judgment, and finally self-destruction.
bhagwad_gita::110.simple_insight: You can feel the warning inside anger before it turns into damage.
bhagwad_gita::110.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna’s crisis is not only about battle but about what happens inside a mind under pressure. Krishna traces the inner collapse: anger leads to confusion, confusion erases memory, memory loss destroys discernment, and then a person falls.
bhagwad_gita::110.modern_relevance: You read one hostile message and your chest tightens. Within minutes, you forget what mattered, misread everything, and say the thing you’ll regret later.
bhagwad_gita::110.insight: It teaches you to interrupt anger early, before it hijacks memory and judgment.

bhagwad_gita::111.verse_hindi: वशीभूत अन्तःकरणवाला कर्मयोगी साधक रागद्वेषसे रहित अपने वशमें की हुई इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा विषयोंका सेवन करता हुआ अन्तःकरणकी निर्मलता को प्राप्त हो जाता है ।  निर्मलता प्राप्त होनेपर साधकके सम्पूर्ण दुःखोंका नाश हो जाता है और ऐसे शुद्ध चित्तवाले साधककी बुद्धि निःसन्देह बहुत जल्दी परमात्मामें स्थिर हो जाती है ॥
bhagwad_gita::111.english_translation: The disciplined person, moving among objects with senses under control and free from attraction and aversion, attains serenity.
bhagwad_gita::111.translation_literal: राग-द्वेष-वियुक्तैः (free from attraction and aversion) / तु (but) / विषयान् (objects) / इन्द्रियैः (with the senses) / चरन् (moving about) / आत्म-वश्यैः (under the control of the inner self) / विधेय-आत्मा (disciplined person) / प्रसादम् (serenity) / अधिगच्छति (attains)
bhagwad_gita::111.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::111.essence: Freedom comes from meeting experience without attraction or aversion.
bhagwad_gita::111.simple_meaning: A person with controlled senses can engage with the world without craving or rejecting it, and that steadiness brings inner clarity.
bhagwad_gita::111.simple_insight: You do not have to flee life to stay clear inside.
bhagwad_gita::111.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen by grief and conflict. Krishna explains that the one who keeps the senses under inner control, without clinging or rejecting, can move through experience and still become serene.
bhagwad_gita::111.modern_relevance: You open a message from someone you both miss and resent. The old reaction wants to pull you in or push you away. This verse points to a third way: stay steady, respond cleanly.
bhagwad_gita::111.insight: It shifts the mind from reaction to regulated contact with experience.

bhagwad_gita::112.verse_sanskrit: प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते । प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥
bhagwad_gita::112.verse_hindi: वशीभूत अन्तःकरणवाला कर्मयोगी साधक रागद्वेषसे रहित अपने वशमें की हुई इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा विषयोंका सेवन करता हुआ अन्तःकरणकी निर्मलता को प्राप्त हो जाता है ।  निर्मलता प्राप्त होनेपर साधकके सम्पूर्ण दुःखोंका नाश हो जाता है और ऐसे शुद्ध चित्तवाले साधककी बुद्धि निःसन्देह बहुत जल्दी परमात्मामें स्थिर हो जाती है ॥
bhagwad_gita::112.english_translation: In inner clarity, all suffering falls away. For one whose mind is clear, understanding settles quickly.
bhagwad_gita::112.translation_literal: प्रसादे (in clarity/serenity) / सर्वदुःखानाम् (of all sorrows) / हानिः (ending) / अस्य (of this one) / उपजायते (arises) । / प्रसन्नचेतसः (of one with a clear mind) / हि (indeed) / आशु (quickly) / बुद्धिः (understanding) / पर्यवतिष्ठते (becomes firmly established)
bhagwad_gita::112.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::112.essence: Clear seeing ends suffering and lets understanding settle at once.
bhagwad_gita::112.simple_meaning: When the mind becomes calm and clear, suffering drops away and understanding becomes steady very quickly.
bhagwad_gita::112.simple_insight: There is relief in realizing that peace of mind is not a luxury; it is the doorway out of suffering.
bhagwad_gita::112.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between grief and duty. Krishna keeps tracing the chain backward: craving, anger, confusion. Here he shows the other direction too — when the mind becomes clear, suffering falls away and the mind can settle in truth.
bhagwad_gita::112.modern_relevance: You finally stop arguing with a message you already know is true. The tightness in your chest loosens, and the next right thought arrives without force.
bhagwad_gita::112.insight: It shifts attention from emotional turbulence to the clarity that dissolves it.

bhagwad_gita::113.verse_sanskrit: नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना । न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::113.verse_hindi: जिसके मनइन्द्रियाँ संयमित नहीं हैं, ऐसे मनुष्यकी व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धि नहीं होती और व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धि न होनेसे उसमें कर्तव्यपरायणताकी भावना नहीं होती ।  ऐसी भावना न होनेसे उसको शान्ति नहीं मिलती ।  फिर शान्तिरहित मनुष्यको सुख कैसे मिल सकता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::113.english_translation: A restless mind has no steady discernment, no steady purpose, no peace, and without peace, no happiness.
bhagwad_gita::113.translation_literal: नास्ति (there is not) / बुद्धिः (steady discernment) / अयुक्तस्य (of one who is unrestrained) / न (not) / च (and) / अयुक्तस्य (of one who is unrestrained) / भावना (steady purpose) / न (not) / च (and) / अभावयतः (of one who lacks inner cultivation) / शान्तिः (peace) / अशान्तस्य (of one without peace) / कुतः (how can there be) / सुखम् (happiness)
bhagwad_gita::113.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::113.essence: Without inner discipline, even happiness has no place to stand.
bhagwad_gita::113.simple_meaning: A person who cannot control the mind and senses lacks clear judgment, steady purpose, peace, and therefore real happiness.
bhagwad_gita::113.simple_insight: Peace is not accidental; it grows from inner discipline.
bhagwad_gita::113.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna explains that a mind ruled by the senses cannot hold steady judgment or purpose. Without that inner order, peace cannot arise, and without peace, happiness slips away.
bhagwad_gita::113.modern_relevance: You open your phone to calm down, then ten minutes later you are more scattered than before. Krishna points to the real problem: a mind that cannot hold itself together cannot produce peace on demand.
bhagwad_gita::113.insight: It shifts attention from chasing comfort to building inner steadiness first.

bhagwad_gita::114.verse_sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते । तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::114.verse_hindi: अपनेअपने विषयोंमें विचरती हुई इन्द्रियोंमेंसे एक ही इन्द्रिय जिस मनको अपना अनुगामी बना लेती है, वह अकेला मन जलमें नौकाको वायुकी तरह इसकी बुद्धिको हर लेता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::114.english_translation: As the winds carry a boat on water, even one roaming sense can sweep away the mind's discernment.
bhagwad_gita::114.translation_literal: इन्द्रियाणाम् (of the senses) / हि (indeed) / चरताम् (roaming) / यत् (which) / मनः (the mind) / अनुविधीयते (follows after) / तत् (that) / अस्य (of this one) / हरति (takes away) / प्रज्ञाम् (discernment) / वायुः (the wind) / नावम् इव (like a boat) / अम्भसि (on water)
bhagwad_gita::114.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::114.essence: One uncontrolled sense can carry the mind away.
bhagwad_gita::114.simple_meaning: If even one sense runs after its objects, it can pull the mind along and destroy clear judgment, like wind pushing a boat off course.
bhagwad_gita::114.simple_insight: A small lapse of attention can undo a lot of inner steadiness.
bhagwad_gita::114.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen, and Krishna is showing why inner control matters before action begins. Even one sense chasing its object can drag the mind away and sink discernment, just as wind overturns a boat.
bhagwad_gita::114.modern_relevance: You open one app “for a minute,” then your focus is gone. A single unchecked pull can scatter the whole mind before you notice.
bhagwad_gita::114.insight: It teaches you to treat attention as fragile: one unchecked sense can derail judgment.

bhagwad_gita::115.verse_sanskrit: तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
bhagwad_gita::115.verse_hindi: इसलिये हे महाबाहो  जिस मनुष्यकी इन्द्रियाँ इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंसे सर्वथा निगृहीत वशमें की हुई हैं, उसकी बुद्धि स्थिर है ॥
bhagwad_gita::115.english_translation: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, the wisdom of one whose senses are fully restrained from sense-objects is steady.
bhagwad_gita::115.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) / यस्य (whose) / महाबाहो (O mighty-armed one) / निगृहीतानि (restrained) / सर्वशः (in every way) / इन्द्रियाणि (the senses) / इन्द्रियार्थेभ्यः (from sense-objects) / तस्य (of that one) / प्रज्ञा (wisdom) / प्रतिष्ठिता (is established)
bhagwad_gita::115.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::115.essence: Steady wisdom begins when the senses stop ruling your attention.
bhagwad_gita::115.simple_meaning: A person who fully controls the senses and keeps them away from objects of desire develops steady understanding.
bhagwad_gita::115.simple_insight: You feel less pulled around when attention stops chasing every temptation.
bhagwad_gita::115.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna keeps building the ladder of inner mastery: first the senses must no longer drag the mind outward. Only then can clear judgment stand firm.
bhagwad_gita::115.modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message and lose twenty minutes. The problem is not the message — it's the senses running outward before your mind can choose.
bhagwad_gita::115.insight: It shifts attention from impulse control in the moment to a stable pattern of restraint.

bhagwad_gita::116.verse_sanskrit: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी । यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥
bhagwad_gita::116.verse_hindi: सम्पूर्ण प्राणियों की जो रात परमात्मासे विमुखता है, उसमें संयमी मनुष्य जागता है, और जिसमें सब प्राणी जागते हैं भोग और संग्रहमें लगे रहते हैं, वह तत्त्वको जाननेवाले मुनिकी दृष्टिमें रात है ॥
bhagwad_gita::116.english_translation: What is night for all beings is wakefulness for the self-controlled one. What all beings wake toward is night for the seer who knows the real.
bhagwad_gita::116.translation_literal: या (that) / निशा (night) / सर्वभूतानां (of all beings) / तस्याम् (in that) / जागर्ति (is awake) / संयमी (the self-controlled one) / यस्याम् (in which) / जाग्रति (are awake) / भूतानि (beings) / सा (that) / निशा (night) / पश्यतः (of the seer) / मुनेः (of the sage)
bhagwad_gita::116.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::116.essence: What the many pursue in sleep, the wise leave behind awake.
bhagwad_gita::116.simple_meaning: Ordinary people chase pleasure and possessions, but the disciplined seeker sees through that pull. What seems valuable to most becomes empty to the one who knows the real.
bhagwad_gita::116.simple_insight: You can stop measuring life by what the crowd wants and begin seeing what actually matters.
bhagwad_gita::116.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between action and collapse. Krishna explains that the wise do not move by the same cravings that drive everyone else. The world’s obsession is their darkness; inner clarity is their wakefulness.
bhagwad_gita::116.modern_relevance: Everyone around you is refreshing, comparing, buying, and chasing the next hit of approval. You pause, and the whole game looks strangely dim. That pause is not weakness; it is seeing.
bhagwad_gita::116.insight: It shifts attention from shared craving to clear seeing, so desire no longer defines what feels real.

bhagwad_gita::117.verse_sanskrit: आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठंसमुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् । तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वेस शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥
bhagwad_gita::117.verse_hindi: जैसे सम्पूर्ण नदियोंका जल चारों ओरसे जलद्वारा परिपूर्ण समुद्रमें आकर मिलता है, पर समुद्र अपनी मर्यादामें अचल प्रतिष्ठित रहता है ऐसे ही सम्पूर्ण भोगपदार्थ जिस संयमी मनुष्य को विकार उत्पन्न किये बिना ही उसको प्राप्त होते हैं, वही मनुष्य परमशान्तिको प्राप्त होता है, भोगोंकी कामनावाला नहीं ॥
bhagwad_gita::117.english_translation: As rivers flow into the sea and the sea remains steady, so desires may enter a disciplined person without disturbing inner peace. The person who wants pleasures does not find peace.
bhagwad_gita::117.translation_literal: आपूर्यमाणम् (being filled) / अचल-प्रतिष्ठम् (firmly established, unmoving) / समुद्रम् (the sea) / आपः (waters) / प्रविशन्ति (enter) / यद्वत् (just as) / तद्वत् (so) / कामाः (desires) / यम् (whom) / प्रविशन्ति (enter) / सर्वे (all) / सः (that one) / शान्तिम् (peace) / आप्नोति (attains) / न (not) / काम-कामी (one who desires pleasures)
bhagwad_gita::117.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::117.essence: Peace belongs to the one who stays steady while desire moves.
bhagwad_gita::117.simple_meaning: A person can meet desire without being shaken by it. Peace belongs to the one who stays steady, not to the one chasing pleasure.
bhagwad_gita::117.simple_insight: You do not have to fight every desire; you can let it move through without letting it steer you.
bhagwad_gita::117.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is being taught how a human being can remain steady under pressure. Krishna compares the disciplined person to the sea: all rivers enter it, yet it does not lose its depth. That inner steadiness is what makes peace possible.
bhagwad_gita::117.modern_relevance: You open your phone and a hundred wants rush in — one more message, one more purchase, one more distraction. You do not need to obey the wave. You can stay larger than it.
bhagwad_gita::117.insight: It trains the mind to receive experience without becoming dependent on it.

bhagwad_gita::118.verse_sanskrit: विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः । निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति ॥
bhagwad_gita::118.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण कामनाओंका त्याग करके स्पृहारहित, ममतारहित और अहंकाररहित होकर आचरण करता है, वह शान्तिको प्राप्त होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::118.english_translation: One who gives up all desires, moves without craving, without possessiveness, and without ego, attains peace.
bhagwad_gita::118.translation_literal: विहाय (giving up) / कामान् (desires) / यः (who) / सर्वान् (all) / पुमान् (person) / चरति (moves, acts) / निःस्पृहः (without craving) / निर्ममः (without possessiveness) / निरहंकारः (without ego) / सः (that one) / शांतिम् (peace) / अधिगच्छति (attains)
bhagwad_gita::118.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::118.essence: Peace begins when wanting, owning, and self-importance fall away.
bhagwad_gita::118.simple_meaning: A person who acts after releasing desire, possessiveness, and ego finds peace.
bhagwad_gita::118.simple_insight: There is relief in moving through life without needing to own, control, or prove anything.
bhagwad_gita::118.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna keeps refining the way to inner freedom: not by escaping action, but by acting after dropping craving, possessiveness, and ego. That is the doorway to peace.
bhagwad_gita::118.modern_relevance: You send the message, then keep checking for a reply. You finish the work, then want credit. This verse points to the calm that comes when action is no longer chained to grasping.
bhagwad_gita::118.insight: It shifts the mind from needing validation to moving cleanly through action.

bhagwad_gita::119.verse_sanskrit: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति । स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥
bhagwad_gita::119.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन  यह ब्राह्मी स्थिति है ।  इसको प्राप्त होकर कभी कोई मोहित नहीं होता ।  इस स्थितिमें यदि अन्तकालमें भी स्थित हो जाय, तो निर्वाण शान्त ब्रह्मकी प्राप्ति हो जाती है ॥
bhagwad_gita::119.english_translation: Arjuna, this is the Brahmic state. Having reached it, one is never deluded. Remaining established in it even at the end of life, one attains freedom in the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::119.translation_literal: एषा (this) / ब्राह्मी (of Brahman) / स्थितिः (state) / पार्थ (Arjuna) / न (not) / एनाम् (this) / प्राप्य (having attained) / विमुह्यति (is deluded) / स्थित्वा (having remained established) / अस्याम् (in this) / अन्तकाले (at the end of life) / अपि (even) / ब्रह्मनिर्वाणम् (freedom in Brahman) / ऋच्छति (attains)
bhagwad_gita::119.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::119.essence: Steadiness in the supreme reality ends confusion, even at life’s edge.
bhagwad_gita::119.simple_meaning: A person who reaches this steady inner state is no longer confused. Even at life’s end, that steadiness leads to freedom in the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::119.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that clarity can become so deep it cannot be shaken, even at the end.
bhagwad_gita::119.detailed_meaning: After Krishna describes the still mind that no longer chases desire, he names the result for Arjuna on the battlefield: this is the Brahmic state. A person established in it is not confused, and even death cannot undo it.
bhagwad_gita::119.modern_relevance: You are sitting in a hospital corridor after a hard diagnosis, and panic keeps trying to take over. This verse points to a steadiness that does not collapse, even there.
bhagwad_gita::119.insight: It shifts the goal from temporary calm to an unbroken inner steadiness that survives the hardest moment.

bhagwad_gita::120.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन । तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥
bhagwad_gita::120.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे जनार्दन अगर आप कर्मसे बुद्धि ज्ञान को श्रेष्ठ मानते हैं, तो फिर हे केशव  मुझे घोर कर्ममें क्यों लगाते हैं  आप अपने मिले हुएसे वचनोंसे मेरी बुद्धिको मोहितसी कर रहे हैं ।  अतः आप निश्चय करके उस एक बात को कहिये, जिससे मैं कल्याणको प्राप्त हो जाऊँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::120.english_translation: Arjuna said: O Janardana, if you consider understanding superior to action, then why do you urge me to this terrible action, O Keshava? Your mixed words confuse my mind; tell me one clear thing by which I may attain what is good.
bhagwad_gita::120.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / ज्यायसी (better, superior) / चेत् (if) / कर्मणः (than action) / ते (by you) / मता (considered) / बुद्धिः (understanding) / जनार्दन (O Janardana) / तत् (then) / किम् (why) / कर्मणि (in action) / घोरे (terrible, dreadful) / माम् (me) / नियोजयसि (you engage, you urge) / केशव (O Keshava)
bhagwad_gita::120.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::120.essence: Mixed guidance deepens paralysis; clarity must come before action.
bhagwad_gita::120.simple_meaning: Arjuna is confused. Krishna seems to praise understanding over action, yet still asks him to fight. He asks for one clear instruction that will lead him toward what is good.
bhagwad_gita::120.simple_insight: It is honest to ask for clarity when guidance feels split in two.
bhagwad_gita::120.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has not yet moved his bow. Krishna has begun teaching, but Arjuna hears a tension: wisdom sounds higher than action, yet battle still stands before him. This verse is Arjuna’s demand for one clear path.
bhagwad_gita::120.modern_relevance: You get two confident answers from two people you trust, and both cannot be followed at once. Instead of pretending to understand, you ask for the single clear step that matters.
bhagwad_gita::120.insight: It teaches you to name confusion directly and ask for one decisive principle.

bhagwad_gita::121.verse_sanskrit: व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे । तदेकं वद निश्िचत्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::121.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे जनार्दन अगर आप कर्मसे बुद्धि ज्ञान को श्रेष्ठ मानते हैं, तो फिर हे केशव मुझे घोर कर्ममें क्यों लगाते हैं  आप अपने मिले हुएसे वचनोंसे मेरी बुद्धिको मोहितसी कर रहे हैं ।  अतः आप निश्चय करके एक बात को कहिये, जिससे मैं कल्याणको प्राप्त हो जाऊँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::121.english_translation: Arjuna said: Your words seem mixed and confusing to me. Tell me one thing clearly, so I may find the highest good.
bhagwad_gita::121.translation_literal: व्यामिश्रेण (mixed) / इव (as if) / वाक्येन (by words) / बुद्धिम् (understanding) / मोहयसि (you confuse) / इव (as if) / मे (my) / तत् (that) / एकम् (one) / वद (speak) / निश्िचत्य (after deciding) / येन (by which) / श्रेयः (highest good) / अहम् (I) / आप्नुयाम् (may attain)
bhagwad_gita::121.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::121.essence: Confusion ends when the mind asks for one clear direction.
bhagwad_gita::121.simple_meaning: Arjuna says Krishna's advice feels mixed and confusing. He asks for one clear teaching that will lead him to the highest good.
bhagwad_gita::121.simple_insight: Clarity matters when your life is at a crossroads. Mixed guidance only deepens fear.
bhagwad_gita::121.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has already admitted his collapse. Now he pushes Krishna harder: if knowledge is higher, why is he being urged toward terrible action? This verse is Arjuna asking for one decisive teaching before he can move.
bhagwad_gita::121.modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, phone in hand, unable to decide whether to tell the hard truth. Half-answers only stretch the dread. This verse names the need for one clear direction.
bhagwad_gita::121.insight: It shifts the mind from juggling options to demanding a single, workable truth.

bhagwad_gita::122.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचलोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ । ज्ञानयोगेन सांख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::122.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे निष्पाप अर्जुन इस मनुष्यलोकमें दो प्रकारसे होनेवाली निष्ठा मेरे द्वारा पहले कही गयी है ।  उनमें ज्ञानियोंकी निष्ठा ज्ञानयोगसे और योगियोंकी निष्ठा कर्मयोगसे होती है ॥
bhagwad_gita::122.english_translation: The divine said: In this world, I have already taught two kinds of steadfast practice: the path of knowledge for the contemplative, and the path of action for the active.
bhagwad_gita::122.translation_literal: श्रीभगवान् (the divine) / उवाच (said) / लोकेऽस्मिन् (in this world) / द्विविधा (twofold) / निष्ठा (steadfast practice) / पुरा (formerly) / प्रोक्ता (taught) / मया (by me) / अनघ (sinless one) / ज्ञानयोगेन (through the yoga of knowledge) / सांख्यानाम् (of the contemplative knowers) / कर्मयोगेन (through the yoga of action) / योगिनाम् (of the yogis)
bhagwad_gita::122.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::122.essence: Different natures are steadied by different disciplines.
bhagwad_gita::122.simple_meaning: There are two valid ways to live steadily: one through understanding, one through action. Different temperaments need different disciplines.
bhagwad_gita::122.simple_insight: You do not have to force one spiritual style. Your nature can guide the way that steadies you.
bhagwad_gita::122.detailed_meaning: Arjuna has just confessed confusion on the battlefield and asked for one clear answer. Krishna begins by saying that human beings are not all built the same: some are fit for knowledge, others for action. This opens the whole teaching on Karma Yoga.
bhagwad_gita::122.modern_relevance: You are staring at a life decision and want one perfect rule to settle everything. Instead, the answer may be simpler: some people need study and reflection, others need disciplined action.
bhagwad_gita::122.insight: It shifts the mind from searching for one universal method to recognizing the right path for one’s temperament.

bhagwad_gita::123.verse_sanskrit: न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते । न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥
bhagwad_gita::123.verse_hindi: मनुष्य न तो कर्मोंका आरम्भ किये बिना निष्कर्मताको प्राप्त होता है और न कर्मोंके त्यागमात्रसे सिद्धिको ही प्राप्त होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::123.english_translation: A person does not reach actionless freedom by avoiding action, nor by renouncing action alone does one reach perfection.
bhagwad_gita::123.translation_literal: न (not) / कर्मणाम् (of actions) / अनारम्भात् (from non-beginning) / नैष्कर्म्यम् (actionlessness) / पुरुषः (a person) / अश्नुते (attains) । न (not) / च (and) / संन्यसनात् (by renunciation) / एव (alone) / सिद्धिम् (perfection) / समधिगच्छति (reaches)
bhagwad_gita::123.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::123.essence: Freedom is not found by escaping action, but by changing your relation to it.
bhagwad_gita::123.simple_meaning: Freedom does not come from simply stopping action, and perfection does not come from merely giving things up. Real growth requires a deeper way of acting.
bhagwad_gita::123.simple_insight: You can stop running without becoming free. What matters is the inner way you act, not just whether you act at all.
bhagwad_gita::123.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has asked for one clear answer. Krishna now corrects a false choice: neither doing nothing nor merely dropping responsibilities brings the highest state. The teaching must now move toward disciplined action without inner bondage.
bhagwad_gita::123.modern_relevance: You quit the project, mute every notification, and hope the pressure disappears. It doesn’t. Relief comes when your relationship to action changes, not when action vanishes.
bhagwad_gita::123.insight: It shifts the mind from escape to right engagement: freedom is found in how you act, not in avoiding action itself.

bhagwad_gita::124.verse_sanskrit: न हि कश्िचत्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् । कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥
bhagwad_gita::124.verse_hindi: कोई भी मनुष्य किसी भी अवस्थामें क्षणमात्र भी कर्म किये बिना नहीं रह सकता क्योंकि प्रकृतिके परवश हुए सब प्राणियोंसे प्रकृतिजन्य गुण कर्म कराते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::124.english_translation: No one can remain without action even for a moment. Everyone is driven to act by the qualities born of nature.
bhagwad_gita::124.translation_literal: न हि (indeed not) / कश्चित् (anyone) / क्षणम् अपि (even for a moment) / जातु (ever) / तिष्ठति (remains) / अकर्मकृत् (one who does no action) / कार्यते (is made to act) / हि (indeed) / अवशः (helplessly) / कर्म (action) / सर्वः (everyone) / प्रकृतिजैः (born of nature) / गुणैः (by the qualities)
bhagwad_gita::124.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::124.essence: Inaction is an illusion; nature is already moving you.
bhagwad_gita::124.simple_meaning: No one can stay inactive forever. The qualities of nature keep pushing every person into action.
bhagwad_gita::124.simple_insight: You are not failing by acting; action is part of being human.
bhagwad_gita::124.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna wants to withdraw from the war. Krishna answers by showing that complete inaction is impossible: even hesitation, avoidance, and refusal are also movements shaped by nature. This verse deepens the case for right action.
bhagwad_gita::124.modern_relevance: You sit frozen with your phone in hand, avoiding the email that could change everything. Even that delay is a kind of action. The question is not whether you act, but what is steering you.
bhagwad_gita::124.insight: It shifts the mind from pretending neutrality to seeing what force is already moving you.

bhagwad_gita::125.verse_sanskrit: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् । इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::125.verse_hindi: जो कर्मेन्द्रियों सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियों को हठपूर्वक रोककर मनसे इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंका चिन्तन करता रहता है, वह मूढ़ बुद्धिवाला मनुष्य मिथ्याचारी मिथ्या आचरण करनेवाला कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::125.english_translation: One who restrains the organs of action but keeps thinking of sense objects in the mind is deluded and called a hypocrite.
bhagwad_gita::125.translation_literal: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि (organs of action) / संयम्य (having restrained) / यः (who) / आस्ते (sits) / मनसा (with the mind) / स्मरन् (remembering, thinking of) / इन्द्रियार्थान् (sense objects) / विमूढात्मा (deluded one) / मिथ्याचारः (false actor, hypocrite) / सः (he) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::125.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::125.essence: Outer restraint means nothing if the mind still feeds desire.
bhagwad_gita::125.simple_meaning: Holding back your actions while the mind still chases desire is self-deception. Outer restraint means little without inner discipline.
bhagwad_gita::125.simple_insight: It removes the comfort of pretending. Real restraint must include the mind, not just visible behavior.
bhagwad_gita::125.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna sharpens the teaching: merely stopping the body while the mind clings to desire is not true renunciation. This verse exposes false restraint before showing the right way forward.
bhagwad_gita::125.modern_relevance: You delete the app, but keep checking the craving in your head. You cancel the habit, yet rehearse it all day. The form changed; the attachment did not.
bhagwad_gita::125.insight: It shifts attention from outward control to inner honesty. The real task is to align thought and action together.

bhagwad_gita::126.verse_sanskrit: यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन । कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::126.verse_hindi: हे अर्जुन जो मनुष्य मनसे इन्द्रियोंपर नियन्त्रण करके आसक्तिरहित होकर निष्काम भावसे समस्त इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा कर्मयोगका आचरण करता है, वही श्रेष्ठ है ॥
bhagwad_gita::126.english_translation: Arjuna, the one who restrains the senses with the mind and begins karma yoga without attachment is श्रेष्ठ.
bhagwad_gita::126.translation_literal: यः (who) / तु (indeed) / इन्द्रियाणि (the senses) / मनसा (with the mind) / नियम्य (having restrained) / आरभते (begins) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / कर्मेन्द्रियैः (with the organs of action) / कर्मयोगम् (karma yoga) / असक्तः (unattached) / सः (he) / विशिष्यते (is श्रेष्ठ, excels)
bhagwad_gita::126.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::126.essence: Self-mastery makes action noble, not the outer task alone.
bhagwad_gita::126.simple_meaning: The best way to act is to keep the senses under the mind's control and do your work without attachment.
bhagwad_gita::126.simple_insight: You do not need to be dragged around by impulse to be effective.
bhagwad_gita::126.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between two armies. Krishna has already shown that action cannot be avoided and hypocrisy is useless. Now he gives the better method: control the senses, act through the body, and stay free of craving.
bhagwad_gita::126.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, make the apology, or walk out of the room. The pull to react is strong, but the cleaner move is to steady the mind first and act without grabbing for the result.
bhagwad_gita::126.insight: It shifts action from impulse-led reaction to deliberate, disciplined doing.

bhagwad_gita::127.verse_sanskrit: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
bhagwad_gita::127.verse_hindi: तू शास्त्रविधिसे नियत किये हुए कर्तव्यकर्म कर क्योंकि कर्म न करनेकी अपेक्षा कर्म करना श्रेष्ठ है तथा कर्म न करनेसे तेरा शरीरनिर्वाह भी सिद्ध नहीं होगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::127.english_translation: Do the duty prescribed for you. Action is better than inaction, and even your body cannot be sustained by inaction.
bhagwad_gita::127.translation_literal: नियतं (prescribed) / कुरु (do) / कर्म (action, duty) / त्वं (you) / कर्म (action) / ज्यायः (better) / हि (indeed) / अकर्मणः (than inaction) / शरीरयात्रा (bodily maintenance, livelihood) / अपि (also, even) / च (and) / ते (your) / न (not) / प्रसिद्ध्येत् (would be accomplished) / अकर्मणः (by inaction)
bhagwad_gita::127.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::127.essence: Right action is unavoidable; even survival depends on it.
bhagwad_gita::127.simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna to do the duty assigned to him. Action is better than sitting idle, and even basic life cannot continue through inaction.
bhagwad_gita::127.simple_insight: There is relief in moving forward: doing the needed thing is cleaner than freezing in fear.
bhagwad_gita::127.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is paralysed with doubt. Krishna answers the paralysis directly: do the duty that is already yours. This verse turns the argument from fear into action.
bhagwad_gita::127.modern_relevance: You are staring at the unanswered message, the apology, the hard resignation email. Waiting for perfect certainty only deepens the knot; action is what loosens it.
bhagwad_gita::127.insight: It shifts the mind from avoiding discomfort to fulfilling the task already in front of you.

bhagwad_gita::128.verse_sanskrit: यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः । तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसंगः समाचर ॥
bhagwad_gita::128.verse_hindi: यज्ञ कर्तव्यपालन के लिये किये जानेवाले कर्मोंसे अन्यत्र अपने लिये किये जानेवाले कर्मोंमें लगा हुआ यह मनुष्यसमुदाय कर्मोंसे बँधता है, इसलिये हे कुन्तीनन्दन  तू आसक्तिरहित होकर उस यज्ञके लिये ही कर्तव्यकर्म कर ॥
bhagwad_gita::128.english_translation: Actions done for sacrifice free a person; actions done for personal gain bind. Therefore, Arjuna, do your duty without attachment for that purpose alone.
bhagwad_gita::128.translation_literal: यज्ञार्थात् (for the purpose of sacrifice) / कर्मणः (from action) / अन्यत्र (other than) / लोकः अयम् (this world) / कर्मबन्धनः (bound by action) / तत्-अर्थम् (for that purpose) / कर्म (action) / कौन्तेय (son of Kunti) / मुक्तसंगः (free from attachment) / समाचर (perform)
bhagwad_gita::128.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::128.essence: Work becomes bondage when it is done for yourself.
bhagwad_gita::128.simple_meaning: Work done only for personal gain creates bondage. Work done as an offering, without attachment, should be done instead.
bhagwad_gita::128.simple_insight: There is relief in serving something larger than your own gain.
bhagwad_gita::128.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before battle. Krishna sharpens the lesson: action itself is not the problem. Action done for selfish gain binds; action offered without grasping becomes the right way to move.
bhagwad_gita::128.modern_relevance: You send the email, then keep checking for praise. The knot tightens when the action is for your ego; it loosens when the action is for what needs doing.
bhagwad_gita::128.insight: It shifts effort from personal payoff to clean participation in duty.

bhagwad_gita::129.verse_sanskrit: सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः । अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक् ॥
bhagwad_gita::129.verse_hindi: प्रजापति ब्रह्माजीने सृष्टिके आदिकालमें कर्तव्यकर्मोंके विधानसहित प्रजामनुष्य आदि की रचना करके उनसे प्रधानतया मनुष्योंसे कहा कि तुमलोग इस कर्तव्यके द्वारा सबकी वृद्धि करो और वह कर्तव्यकर्मरूप यज्ञ तुमलोगोंको कर्तव्यपालनकी आवश्यक सामग्री प्रदान करनेवाला हो ।  अपने कर्तव्यकर्मके द्वारा तुमलोग देवताओंको उन्नत करो और वे देवतालोग अपने कर्तव्यके द्वारा तुमलोगोंको उन्नत करें ।  इस प्रकार एकदूसरेको उन्नत करते हुए तुमलोग परम कल्याणको प्राप्त हो जाओगे ॥
bhagwad_gita::129.english_translation: In the beginning, Prajapati created beings together with sacrifice and said: “By this, you shall prosper. May this sacrifice be the wish-fulfilling cow for you.”
bhagwad_gita::129.translation_literal: सहयज्ञाः (together with sacrifice) / प्रजाः (beings) / सृष्ट्वा (having created) / पुरा (in the beginning) / उवाच (said) / प्रजापतिः (Prajapati) / अनेन (by this) / प्रसविष्यध्वम् (you shall prosper) / एषः (this) / वः (for you) / अस्तु (may be) / इष्टकामधुक् (the wish-fulfilling cow)
bhagwad_gita::129.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::129.essence: Life flourishes when duty becomes mutual support.
bhagwad_gita::129.simple_meaning: At the start of creation, Prajapati set up a way of living where sacrifice and duty help all beings flourish. The message is to support life through shared responsibility.
bhagwad_gita::129.simple_insight: Your work is not isolated; it feeds a larger exchange that keeps life going.
bhagwad_gita::129.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has frozen before battle, and Krishna is tracing action back to the order of creation itself. He says Prajapati made beings with sacrifice built in, so human life is meant to nourish and be nourished through duty.
bhagwad_gita::129.modern_relevance: You are stocking shelves before dawn, or caring for a parent no one sees. The task feels small, but it belongs to a larger web that lets everyone else keep moving.
bhagwad_gita::129.insight: It shifts action from private gain to participation in a shared order.

bhagwad_gita::130.verse_sanskrit: देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः । परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥
bhagwad_gita::130.verse_hindi: प्रजापति ब्रह्माजीने सृष्टिके आदिकालमें कर्तव्यकर्मोंके विधानसहित प्रजामनुष्य आदि की रचना करके उनसे, प्रधानतया मनुष्योंसे कहा कि तुमलोग इस कर्तव्यके द्वारा सबकी वृद्धि करो और वह कर्तव्यकर्मरूप यज्ञ तुमलोगोंको कर्तव्यपालनकी आवश्यक सामग्री प्रदान करनेवाला हो ।  अपने कर्तव्यकर्मके द्वारा तुमलोग देवताओंको उन्नत करो और वे देवतालोग अपने कर्तव्यके द्वारा तुमलोगोंको उन्नत करें ।  इस प्रकार एकदूसरेको उन्नत करते हुए तुमलोग परम कल्याणको प्राप्त हो जाओगे ॥
bhagwad_gita::130.english_translation: By nurturing the radiant beings through this duty, let them nurture you. Nurturing one another, you will attain the highest good.
bhagwad_gita::130.translation_literal: देवान् (the radiant beings) / भावयत (nurture, support) / अनेन (through this) / ते (those) / देवा (the radiant beings) / भावयन्तु (may nurture, support) / वः (you) / परस्परम् (mutually, one another) / भावयन्तः (nurturing, supporting) / श्रेयः (the highest good) / परम् (supreme) / अवाप्स्यथ (you will attain)
bhagwad_gita::130.speaker: Unknown
bhagwad_gita::130.essence: Your duty nourishes the whole, and the whole nourishes you back.
bhagwad_gita::130.simple_meaning: Support the larger order through your actions, and that order will support you in return. Mutual support leads to the highest good.
bhagwad_gita::130.simple_insight: You are not isolated. What you give to the whole comes back as support for your own life.
bhagwad_gita::130.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still explaining sacrifice as a social and cosmic exchange. After showing that action should be offered rather than hoarded, he says that humans and the radiant beings sustain each other through duty. This is the bridge between private effort and shared order.
bhagwad_gita::130.modern_relevance: You keep the neighborhood garden alive, and it keeps feeding everyone. The effort feels one-sided until you see how much your own life depends on what you sustain.
bhagwad_gita::130.insight: It shifts action from self-protection to participation in a mutual system of giving and receiving.

bhagwad_gita::131.verse_sanskrit: इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः । तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥
bhagwad_gita::131.verse_hindi: यज्ञसे भावित पुष्ट हुए देवता भी तुमलोगोंको बिना माँगे ही कर्तव्यपालनकी आवश्यक सामग्री देते रहेंगे ।  इस प्रकार उन देवताओंसे प्राप्त हुई सामग्रीको दूसरोंकी सेवामें लगाये बिना जो मनुष्य स्वयं ही उसका उपभोग करता है, वह चोर ही है ॥
bhagwad_gita::131.english_translation: The radiant beings, nourished by sacrifice, will give you the enjoyments you need. One who enjoys their gifts without offering back is a thief.
bhagwad_gita::131.translation_literal: इष्टान् (desired) / भोगान् (enjoyments) / हि (indeed) / वः (to you) / देवाः (radiant beings) / दास्यन्ते (will give) / यज्ञभाविताः (nourished by sacrifice) / तैः (by those) / दत्तान् (given) / अप्रदाय (without giving back) / एभ्यः (to these) / यः (who) / भुङ्क्ते (enjoys) / स्तेनः (thief) / एव (indeed) / सः (he)
bhagwad_gita::131.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::131.essence: What is received must be offered back, or it becomes theft.
bhagwad_gita::131.simple_meaning: The world keeps giving when you participate in shared responsibility. Taking benefits without giving back is treated as theft.
bhagwad_gita::131.simple_insight: Generosity feels cleaner than ownership. You are meant to circulate what arrives, not hoard it.
bhagwad_gita::131.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna is teaching Arjuna that life runs on exchange, not extraction. The earlier verses describe sacrifice as the basis of social order; this verse warns that taking without returning breaks that order.
bhagwad_gita::131.modern_relevance: You use the last of the office printer paper, ignore the shared supply closet, and walk away. The verse lands there: what you consume without replenishing was never truly yours.
bhagwad_gita::131.insight: It shifts action from taking to participating in a cycle of return.

bhagwad_gita::132.verse_sanskrit: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः । भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥
bhagwad_gita::132.verse_hindi: यज्ञशेष योग का अनुभव करनेवाले श्रेष्ठ मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण पापोंसे मुक्त हो जाते हैं ।  परन्तु जो केवल अपने लिये ही पकाते अर्थात् सब कर्म करते हैं, वे पापीलोग तो पापका ही भक्षण करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::132.english_translation: Those who eat the leftovers of sacrifice are freed from all faults. Those who cook only for themselves eat only wrongdoing.
bhagwad_gita::132.translation_literal: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः (eating what remains after sacrifice) / सन्तः (the good, the noble) / मुच्यन्ते (are freed) / सर्वकिल्बिषैः (from all faults) / भुञ्जते (they eat/enjoy) / ते (they) / तु (but) / अघं (wrongdoing) / पापाः (the sinful) / ये (those who) / पचन्ति (cook) / आत्मकारणात् (for their own sake)
bhagwad_gita::132.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::132.essence: What is offered purifies; what is hoarded for the self corrupts.
bhagwad_gita::132.simple_meaning: People who take only what remains after offering their work for the larger order are cleansed. People who act only for themselves end up consuming their own wrongdoing.
bhagwad_gita::132.simple_insight: Generosity purifies effort; selfishness poisons it.
bhagwad_gita::132.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen and Krishna is rebuilding the meaning of action. After explaining sacrifice and mutual support, Krishna says that the noble live on what is left after offering first; self-centered action only deepens impurity.
bhagwad_gita::132.modern_relevance: You finish dinner and notice you grabbed the best piece before anyone else. That tiny reflex is the same one that makes larger acts feel hollow.
bhagwad_gita::132.insight: It shifts action from self-collection to offering, so work becomes clean instead of contaminated by greed.

bhagwad_gita::133.verse_sanskrit: अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः । यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥
bhagwad_gita::133.verse_hindi: सम्पूर्ण प्राणी अन्नसे उत्पन्न होते हैं ।  अन्न वर्षासे होती है ।  वर्षा यज्ञसे होती है ।  यज्ञ कर्मोंसे निष्पन्न होता है ।  कर्मोंको तू वेदसे उत्पन्न जान और वेदको अक्षरब्रह्मसे प्रकट हुआ जान ।  इसलिये वह सर्वव्यापी परमात्मा यज्ञ कर्तव्यकर्म में नित्य प्रतिष्ठित है ॥
bhagwad_gita::133.english_translation: All beings arise from food. Food comes from rain. Rain comes from sacrifice. Sacrifice arises from action.
bhagwad_gita::133.translation_literal: अन्नात् (from food) / भवन्ति (come into being) / भूतानि (beings) / पर्जन्यात् (from rain) / अन्नसम्भवः (food-born) / यज्ञात् (from sacrifice) / भवति (comes) / पर्जन्यः (rain) / यज्ञः (sacrifice) / कर्मसमुद्भवः (action-born)
bhagwad_gita::133.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::133.essence: Action sustains the cycle that makes life possible.
bhagwad_gita::133.simple_meaning: Life depends on a chain: food comes from rain, rain comes from sacrifice, and sacrifice comes from action.
bhagwad_gita::133.simple_insight: Your actions are not isolated; they feed the whole web that sustains life.
bhagwad_gita::133.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen while Krishna explains how human life is held together. This verse begins the chain linking food, rain, sacrifice, and action, showing that personal conduct affects the whole order.
bhagwad_gita::133.modern_relevance: You open the fridge after a long week and forget the path behind that meal: weather, work, trade, care. One careless act can still belong to a larger system.
bhagwad_gita::133.insight: It shifts attention from private consumption to the shared systems your actions sustain.

bhagwad_gita::134.verse_sanskrit: कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् । तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::134.verse_hindi: सम्पूर्ण प्राणी अन्नसे उत्पन्न होते हैं ।  अन्न वर्षासे होती है ।  वर्षा यज्ञसे होती है ।  यज्ञ कर्मोंसे निष्पन्न होता है ।  कर्मोंको तू वेदसे उत्पन्न जान और वेदको अक्षरब्रह्मसे प्रकट हुआ जान ।  इसलिये वह सर्वव्यापी परमात्मा यज्ञ कर्तव्यकर्म में नित्य प्रतिष्ठित है ॥
bhagwad_gita::134.english_translation: Know that action comes from the Vedas, and the Vedas come from the imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervading supreme reality is always established in sacrifice.
bhagwad_gita::134.translation_literal: कर्म (action) / ब्रह्मोद्भवं (born from Brahman) / विद्धि (know) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / अक्षरसमुद्भवम् (arising from the imperishable) / तस्मात् (therefore) / सर्वगतम् (all-pervading) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / नित्यम् (always) / यज्ञे (in sacrifice) / प्रतिष्ठितम् (established)
bhagwad_gita::134.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::134.essence: Right action is not random; it rests in a deeper, sustaining order.
bhagwad_gita::134.simple_meaning: Action arises from sacred order, that order arises from the imperishable, and the all-pervading supreme reality is rooted in selfless offering.
bhagwad_gita::134.simple_insight: Work feels lighter when you see it as part of a larger order, not a personal burden.
bhagwad_gita::134.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna explains the hidden structure behind right action. After showing how sacrifice sustains life, Krishna now traces action back to the Vedas and beyond them to the imperishable source, grounding karma yoga in cosmic order.
bhagwad_gita::134.modern_relevance: You are about to make a hard call that affects other people, and the choice feels bigger than your mood. This verse reminds you that right action belongs to a larger order than personal preference.
bhagwad_gita::134.insight: It shifts action from private ambition to participation in a sacred pattern.

bhagwad_gita::135.verse_sanskrit: एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः । अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ॥
bhagwad_gita::135.verse_hindi: हे पार्थ जो मनुष्य इस लोकमें इस प्रकार परम्परासे प्रचलित सृष्टिचक्रके अनुसार नहीं चलता, वह इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा भोगोंमें रमण करनेवाला अघायु पापमय जीवन बितानेवाला मनुष्य संसारमें व्यर्थ ही जीता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::135.english_translation: O Partha, the one who does not follow this cycle set in motion here lives in vain, delighting only in the senses and living a life of wrongdoing.
bhagwad_gita::135.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / प्रवर्तितम् (set in motion) / चक्रम् (cycle) / न (not) / अनुवर्तयति (follows) / इह (here) / यः (who) / अघायुः (one whose life is tainted by wrongdoing) / इन्द्रियारामः (delighting in the senses) / मोघम् (in vain) / पार्थ (O Partha) / सः (he) / जीवति (lives)
bhagwad_gita::135.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::135.essence: A life detached from duty empties itself from within.
bhagwad_gita::135.simple_meaning: A person who ignores the world’s proper cycle of action and only chases pleasure ends up living a wasted life.
bhagwad_gita::135.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that a meaningful life is not random pleasure-seeking.
bhagwad_gita::135.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna explains how life itself depends on a shared cycle of action, sacrifice, and responsibility. This verse warns that refusing that order for private pleasure makes a person’s life hollow.
bhagwad_gita::135.modern_relevance: You keep scrolling, snacking, and numbing out after a hard day, but something inside feels dead. Krishna names that drift: a life cut off from responsibility begins to waste itself.
bhagwad_gita::135.insight: It shifts the mind from appetite as freedom to responsibility as the condition for a meaningful life.

bhagwad_gita::136.verse_sanskrit: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः । आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::136.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य अपनेआपमें ही रमण करनेवाला और अपनेआपमें ही तृप्त तथा अपनेआपमें ही संतुष्ट है, उसके लिये कोई कर्तव्य नहीं है ॥
bhagwad_gita::136.english_translation: The person who delights in the true self, is satisfied in the true self, and is content in the true self has no duty left.
bhagwad_gita::136.translation_literal: यः (who) / तु (indeed) / आत्म-रतिḥ (one who delights in the self) / एव (alone) / स्यात् (may be) / आत्म-तृप्तः (satisfied in the self) / च (and) / मानवः (person) / आत्मनि (in the self) / एव (alone) / च (and) / सन्तुष्टः (content) / तस्य (for that one) / कार्यम् (duty, task) / न (not) / विद्यते (exists)
bhagwad_gita::136.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::136.essence: Fulfillment in the true self ends the need for striving.
bhagwad_gita::136.simple_meaning: A person who finds complete fulfillment in the true self does not act from inner lack. Nothing remains to be gained through duty or effort.
bhagwad_gita::136.simple_insight: There is relief in not needing the world to complete you.
bhagwad_gita::136.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna teaches the deeper aim of action. After showing how the world’s order moves through work, Krishna points to the one who has already found fullness within and no longer needs action for completion.
bhagwad_gita::136.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the praise, the relationship milestone — and still feel restless. The verse points to a deeper fullness that does not depend on the next achievement.
bhagwad_gita::136.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing completion through action to resting in inner fullness before acting.

bhagwad_gita::137.verse_sanskrit: नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन । न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्िचदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥
bhagwad_gita::137.verse_hindi: उस कर्मयोगसे सिद्ध हुए महापुरुषका इस संसारमें न तो कर्म करनेसे कोई प्रयोजन रहता है, और न कर्म न करनेसे ही कोई प्रयोजन रहता है, तथा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें किसी भी प्राणीके साथ इसका किञ्चिन्मात्र भी स्वार्थका सम्बन्ध नहीं रहता ॥
bhagwad_gita::137.english_translation: For the perfected person, no purpose remains in doing, and no purpose remains in not doing. No being in the world is a source of personal gain.
bhagwad_gita::137.translation_literal: नैव (not at all) / तस्य (for that one) / कृतेन (by doing) / अर्थः (purpose, gain) / न (not) / अकृतेन (by not doing) / इह (here) / कश्चन (any) / न (not) / च (and) / अस्य (for this one) / सर्वभूतेषु (among all beings) / कश्चित् (any) / अर्थव्यपाश्रयः (basis for personal gain)
bhagwad_gita::137.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::137.essence: Freedom ends the need to profit from action.
bhagwad_gita::137.simple_meaning: A person who has reached inner completeness no longer acts for personal gain. Neither action nor inaction adds anything to that person.
bhagwad_gita::137.simple_insight: There is relief in not needing life to pay you back.
bhagwad_gita::137.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and fear. Krishna explains the mature state of action: a person established in inner completeness does not act for reward, nor avoid action for reward. Nothing in the world becomes a bargaining chip.
bhagwad_gita::137.modern_relevance: You send the message, make the apology, or walk away from the deal without calculating how it will benefit you. The action stands on its own, even when nothing comes back.
bhagwad_gita::137.insight: It shifts the mind from transaction to freedom: action is no longer a bargain with the world.

bhagwad_gita::138.verse_sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर । असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
bhagwad_gita::138.verse_hindi: इसलिये तू निरन्तर आसक्तिरहित होकर कर्तव्यकर्मका भलीभाँति आचरण कर क्योंकि आसक्तिरहित होकर कर्म करता हुआ मनुष्य परमात्माको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::138.english_translation: Therefore, always perform your duty without attachment; by acting without attachment, a person reaches the supreme.
bhagwad_gita::138.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) / असक्तः (without attachment) / सततम् (always) / कार्यम् (duty) / कर्म (action) / समाचर (perform fully) / असक्तः (without attachment) / हि (indeed) / आचरन् (acting) / कर्म (action) / परमम् (the supreme) / आप्नोति (reaches) / पूरुषः (a person)
bhagwad_gita::138.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::138.essence: Freedom comes when action is done without grasping at its reward.
bhagwad_gita::138.simple_meaning: Keep doing what must be done, but do it without clinging to results. That kind of action leads you to the highest good.
bhagwad_gita::138.simple_insight: There is relief in giving your full effort without carrying the weight of outcomes.
bhagwad_gita::138.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and fear. Krishna has just described the person who needs nothing from action. Now he turns that insight into practice: act steadily, but do not cling. That freedom itself becomes the way forward.
bhagwad_gita::138.modern_relevance: You send the message, make the hard apology, or submit the work knowing it may not land how you hope. The act is complete even before the response arrives.
bhagwad_gita::138.insight: It shifts attention from owning the result to offering the action cleanly.

bhagwad_gita::139.verse_sanskrit: कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः । लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::139.verse_hindi: राजा जनकजैसे अनेक महापुरुष भी कर्मके द्वारा ही परमसिद्धिको प्राप्त हुए हैं ।  इसलिये लोकसंग्रहको देखते हुए भी तू निष्कामभावसे कर्म करनेके योग्य है ॥
bhagwad_gita::139.english_translation: Janaka and others attained perfection through action itself. You should act too, while keeping the welfare of the world in view.
bhagwad_gita::139.translation_literal: कर्मणा (through action) / एव (indeed) / हि (for) / संसिद्धिम् (perfection) / आस्थिता (having attained) / जनकादयः (Janaka and others) / लोकसंग्रहम् (the holding-together of the world) / एव (indeed) / अपि (also) / संपश्यन् (seeing) / कर्तुम् (to do) / अर्हसि (you are fit)
bhagwad_gita::139.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::139.essence: Perfection comes through action that serves more than the self.
bhagwad_gita::139.simple_meaning: Great people like Janaka reached perfection by acting, not by withdrawing. You should also act for the good of the world.
bhagwad_gita::139.simple_insight: It can feel steadying to know that full engagement, not escape, is the mature path.
bhagwad_gita::139.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen. Krishna points to King Janaka and other great figures as proof that spiritual fulfilment did not come from inaction. The teaching now turns from private hesitation to public responsibility.
bhagwad_gita::139.modern_relevance: You are tempted to step back because your decision affects others and you want to stay clean. Krishna says the cleaner move is to act well, because someone else is counting on your example.
bhagwad_gita::139.insight: It shifts the mind from personal withdrawal to responsible participation in shared life.

bhagwad_gita::140.verse_sanskrit: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः । स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥
bhagwad_gita::140.verse_hindi: श्रेष्ठ मनुष्य जोजो आचरण करता है, दूसरे मनुष्य वैसावैसा ही आचरण करते हैं ।  वह जो कुछ प्रमाण देता है, दूसरे मनुष्य उसीके अनुसार आचरण करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::140.english_translation: Whatever the best person does, others follow. Whatever standard they set, the world copies.
bhagwad_gita::140.translation_literal: यद्यत् (whatever) / आचरति (does, practices) / श्रेष्ठः (the best person) / तत् तत् एव (that very same) / इतरः (other) / जनः (people) / सः (that person) / यत् (whatever) / प्रमाणं (standard, authority) / कुरुते (sets, makes) / लोकः (the world, people) / तत् (that) / अनुवर्तते (follows)
bhagwad_gita::140.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::140.essence: The highest standard is not spoken; it is copied.
bhagwad_gita::140.simple_meaning: People copy the conduct of those they admire. A respected person's actions become the standard others imitate.
bhagwad_gita::140.simple_insight: Your choices matter beyond you. Example quietly teaches more than instruction.
bhagwad_gita::140.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna is still teaching Arjuna how to act when the battle has not yet begun. He shows that leaders shape the behavior of everyone watching them, so Arjuna's conduct will matter far beyond his own life.
bhagwad_gita::140.modern_relevance: A parent answers a rude message with calm. A child sees it, and that response becomes normal. People learn more from what you repeatedly do than from what you say.
bhagwad_gita::140.insight: It shifts attention from private morality to public influence: your conduct becomes a template for others.

bhagwad_gita::141.verse_sanskrit: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन । नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ॥
