bhagwad_gita::141.verse_hindi: हे पार्थ मुझे तीनों लोकोंमें न तो कुछ कर्तव्य है और न कोई प्राप्त करनेयोग्य वस्तु अप्राप्त है, फिर भी मैं कर्तव्यकर्ममें ही लगा रहता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::141.english_translation: O Partha, there is nothing in the three worlds that I must do, and nothing I have not yet gained that must be gained. Yet I remain engaged in action.
bhagwad_gita::141.translation_literal: न (not) / मे (for me) / पार्थ (O Partha) / अस्ति (there is) / कर्तव्यम् (to be done / duty) / त्रिषु (in the three) / लोकेषु (worlds) / किञ्चन (anything) / न (not) / अनवाप्तम् (not attained) / अवाप्तव्यम् (to be attained) / वर्ते (I remain / I engage) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / कर्मणि (in action)
bhagwad_gita::141.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::141.essence: Even the fulfilled keep working, because action need not come from lack.
bhagwad_gita::141.simple_meaning: Krishna says he has no unfinished duty and nothing left to gain, yet he still stays active.
bhagwad_gita::141.simple_insight: Real freedom is not doing less; it is acting without inner lack.
bhagwad_gita::141.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before battle. Krishna explains why he himself still acts: not from need, but to guide the world. This verse turns Krishna into the model for action without craving.
bhagwad_gita::141.modern_relevance: You’ve already won the argument in your head, but you still show up for the hard conversation. You do it not to get something, but because the action itself matters.
bhagwad_gita::141.insight: It shifts action from personal gain to steady example and responsibility.

bhagwad_gita::142.verse_sanskrit: यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः । मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥
bhagwad_gita::142.verse_hindi: हे पार्थ अगर मैं किसी समय सावधान होकर कर्तव्यकर्म न करूँ तो बड़ी हानि हो जाय क्योंकि मनुष्य सब प्रकारसे मेरे ही मार्गका अनुसरण करते हैं ।  यदि मैं कर्म न करूँ, तो ये सब मनुष्य नष्टभ्रष्ट हो जायँ और मैं वर्णसंकरताको करनेवाला होऊँ तथा इस समस्त प्रजाको नष्ट करनेवाला बनूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::142.english_translation: For if I ever stopped acting with care, people would follow my path in every way, Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::142.translation_literal: यदि (if) / हि (indeed) / अहं (I) / न (not) / वर्तेयं (were to act) / जातु (ever) / कर्मणि (in action) / अतन्द्रितः (without negligence) / मम (my) / वर्त्मन् (path) / अनुवर्तन्ते (follow) / मनुष्याः (people) / पार्थ (Arjuna) / सर्वशः (in every way)
bhagwad_gita::142.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::142.essence: Careless withdrawal by the highest would unravel everyone below.
bhagwad_gita::142.simple_meaning: Krishna says that if he stopped doing his duty carefully, people would copy that neglect and society would suffer.
bhagwad_gita::142.simple_insight: Your example teaches more loudly than your advice.
bhagwad_gita::142.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Krishna is explaining to Arjuna why even the highest being keeps acting. If he became careless and stopped fulfilling duty, ordinary people would imitate that failure, and the social order would collapse.
bhagwad_gita::142.modern_relevance: A parent says, “Do your homework,” while scrolling on a phone all evening. The child learns the real lesson from the behavior, not the lecture.
bhagwad_gita::142.insight: It shifts attention from private freedom to public responsibility: your conduct becomes a model others unconsciously follow.

bhagwad_gita::143.verse_sanskrit: उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् । सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::143.verse_hindi: हे पार्थ  अगर मैं किसी समय सावधान होकर कर्तव्यकर्म न करूँ तो बड़ी हानि हो जाय क्योंकि मनुष्य सब प्रकारसे मेरे ही मार्गका अनुसरण करते हैं ।  यदि मैं कर्म न करूँ, तो ये सब मनुष्य नष्टभ्रष्ट हो जायँ और मैं वर्णसंकरताको करनेवाला तथा इस समस्त प्रजाको नष्ट करनेवाला बनूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::143.english_translation: If I did not act, these worlds would fall into ruin. I would create disorder and destroy these people.
bhagwad_gita::143.translation_literal: उत्सीदेयुः (would fall into ruin) / इमे (these) / लोकाः (worlds) / न (not) / कुर्याम् (I would do) / कर्म (action) / चेत् (if) / अहम् (I) / सङ्करस्य (of disorder / mixed confusion) / च (and) / कर्ता (maker) / स्याम् (I would become) / उपहन्याम् (I would destroy) / इमाः (these) / प्रजाः (people)
bhagwad_gita::143.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::143.essence: Even the highest must act to prevent disorder.
bhagwad_gita::143.simple_meaning: Krishna says that even he must keep acting, because if he stopped, society would fall into disorder and people would be harmed.
bhagwad_gita::143.simple_insight: Your actions matter beyond you. Neglecting what you must do can unsettle many lives.
bhagwad_gita::143.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen. Krishna explains that duty is not optional even for the highest being: if he stopped acting, the social order would break and people would suffer. This verse strengthens the case for steady action.
bhagwad_gita::143.modern_relevance: You skip the hard conversation, hoping the problem will wait. It doesn't. Silence spreads confusion, and everyone around you ends up paying for your avoidance.
bhagwad_gita::143.insight: It shifts duty from personal preference to responsibility for the wider order.

bhagwad_gita::144.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन कर्ममें आसक्त हुए अज्ञानीजन जिस प्रकार कर्म करते हैं, आसक्तिरहित विद्वान भी लोकसंग्रह करना चाहता हुआ उसी प्रकार कर्म करे ।  तत्त्वज्ञ महापुरुष कर्मोंमें आसक्तिवाले अज्ञानी मनुष्योंकी बुद्धिमें भ्रम उत्पन्न न करे, प्रत्युत स्वयं समस्त कर्मोंको अच्छी तरहसे करता हुआ उनसे भी वैसे ही करवाये ॥
bhagwad_gita::144.english_translation: As the ignorant act with attachment to action, so should the wise act without attachment, seeking the welfare of the world.
bhagwad_gita::144.translation_literal: सक्ताः (attached) / कर्मणि (in action) / अविद्वांसः (the ignorant) / यथा (as) / कुर्वन्ति (perform) / भारत (O Bharata) / कुर्यात् (should perform) / विद्वान् (the wise) / तथा (likewise) / असक्तः (without attachment) / चिकीर्षुः (desiring to do) / लोकसंग्रहम् (the welfare/order of the world)
bhagwad_gita::144.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::144.essence: Wisdom keeps acting, but never for personal gain.
bhagwad_gita::144.simple_meaning: A wise person should keep acting, but without clinging to the results. The point is to support the world, not feed ego.
bhagwad_gita::144.simple_insight: You can stay fully engaged without getting trapped by craving recognition or payoff.
bhagwad_gita::144.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen while Krishna explains how action should continue. Even the wise must work, not for personal gain, but to keep the world in order and guide others by example.
bhagwad_gita::144.modern_relevance: You’re the senior person in a room full of anxious newcomers, and everyone is watching how you handle the pressure. Stay active, stay steady, and let your example carry the room.
bhagwad_gita::144.insight: It shifts action from self-serving ambition to responsible participation for the good of others.

bhagwad_gita::145.verse_sanskrit: न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् । जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान् युक्तः समाचरन् ॥
bhagwad_gita::145.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन कर्ममें आसक्त हुए अज्ञानीजन जिस प्रकार कर्म करते हैं आसक्तिरहित विद्वान भी लोकसंग्रह करना चाहता हुआ उसी प्रकार कर्म करे ।  सावधान तत्त्वज्ञ महापुरुष कर्मोंमें आसक्तिवाले अज्ञानी मनुष्योंकी बुद्धिमें भ्रम उत्पन्न न करे, प्रत्युत स्वयं समस्त कर्मोंको अच्छी तरहसे करता हुआ उनसे भी वैसे ही करवाये ॥
bhagwad_gita::145.english_translation: An awakened person should not unsettle the minds of those attached to action. Instead, acting skillfully, such a person should engage them in all work.
bhagwad_gita::145.translation_literal: न (not) / बुद्धिभेदं (confusion of understanding) / जनयेत् (should generate) / अज्ञानां (of the ignorant) / कर्मसङ्गिनाम् (of those attached to action) / जोषयेत् (should encourage) / सर्वकर्माणि (all actions) / विद्वान् (the wise one) / युक्तः (steadfast, disciplined) / समाचरन् (while acting properly)
bhagwad_gita::145.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::145.essence: Wisdom should steady people, not shake their footing.
bhagwad_gita::145.simple_meaning: A wise person should not confuse people who are still attached to action. Instead, by acting well, they should guide others into right action.
bhagwad_gita::145.simple_insight: Lead by example, not by shaking people’s confidence before they are ready.
bhagwad_gita::145.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna is teaching Arjuna how a wise person should behave in society. Even while remaining free from attachment, the wise must keep others steady, not create confusion in minds still tied to action.
bhagwad_gita::145.modern_relevance: You’ve finally learned a hard lesson, and someone around you is still clinging to the old pattern. Blasting them with your clarity may only make them resist harder.
bhagwad_gita::145.insight: It shifts the aim from proving insight to preserving others’ ability to act well.

bhagwad_gita::146.verse_sanskrit: प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः । अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::146.verse_hindi: सम्पूर्ण कर्म सब प्रकारसे प्रकृतिके गुणोंद्वारा किये जाते हैं परन्तु अहंकारसे मोहित अन्तःकरणवाला अज्ञानी मनुष्य मैं कर्ता हूँ  ऐसा मानता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::146.english_translation: All actions are carried out in every way by the qualities of nature. Deluded by ego, a person thinks, 'I am the doer.'
bhagwad_gita::146.translation_literal: प्रकृतेः (of nature) / क्रियमाणानि (being done) / गुणैः (by the qualities) / कर्माणि (actions) / सर्वशः (in every way) / अहङ्कार-विमूढ-आत्मा (the inner being deluded by ego) / कर्ता (doer) / अहम् (I) / इति (thus) / मन्यते (thinks)
bhagwad_gita::146.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::146.essence: The doer is imagined; action belongs to nature's forces.
bhagwad_gita::146.simple_meaning: Actions happen through the forces of nature, not through the false sense of 'I am the doer.' Ego creates the illusion of authorship.
bhagwad_gita::146.simple_insight: You can loosen the grip of self-importance and let action become cleaner, lighter, and truer.
bhagwad_gita::146.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Krishna is dismantling Arjuna's panic about action itself. After urging him to act, he now explains why the ego's ownership of action is false: nature's forces move everything, while confusion makes the person say, 'I am doing this.'
bhagwad_gita::146.modern_relevance: You replay a painful conversation in your head and keep editing your part in it. Krishna cuts through that loop: the event unfolded through many causes, not one heroic or guilty self.
bhagwad_gita::146.insight: It shifts responsibility from ego-ownership to clear participation in what is already unfolding.

bhagwad_gita::147.verse_sanskrit: तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः । गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ॥
bhagwad_gita::147.verse_hindi: हे महाबाहो गुणविभाग और कर्मविभागको तत्त्वसे जाननेवाला महापुरुष सम्पूर्ण गुण ही गुणोंमें बरत रहे हैं  ऐसा मानकर उनमें आसक्त नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::147.english_translation: The one who truly understands the division of qualities and actions does not cling, seeing that qualities act upon qualities.
bhagwad_gita::147.translation_literal: तत्त्ववित् (one who knows the truth) / तु (indeed) / महाबाहो (mighty-armed one) / गुणकर्मविभागयोः (of the division of qualities and actions) / गुणाः (the qualities) / गुणेषु (among the qualities) / वर्तन्ते (move/operate) / इति (thus) / मत्वा (having understood) / न (not) / सज्जते (becomes attached)
bhagwad_gita::147.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::147.essence: Seeing action as nature's movement ends attachment.
bhagwad_gita::147.simple_meaning: A person who understands how qualities and actions work sees that nature is doing the acting, not the separate ego. That understanding removes attachment.
bhagwad_gita::147.simple_insight: You can stay involved without getting entangled. Clear seeing creates freedom.
bhagwad_gita::147.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna deepens the lesson: the wise person sees that the forces of nature are moving through action, not a separate doer. That vision ends clinging.
bhagwad_gita::147.modern_relevance: You watch yourself getting pulled into a family argument, then catch the pattern before speaking. The pause changes everything: you stop defending a self-image and start seeing the forces at work.
bhagwad_gita::147.insight: It shifts attention from personal ownership of action to clear observation of how nature operates.

bhagwad_gita::148.verse_sanskrit: प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु । तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::148.verse_hindi: प्रकृतिजन्य गुणोंसे अत्यन्त मोहित हुए अज्ञानी मनुष्य गुणों और कर्मोंमें आसक्त रहते हैं ।  उन पूर्णतया न समझनेवाले मन्दबुद्धि अज्ञानियोंको पूर्णतया जाननेवाला ज्ञानी मनुष्य विचलित न करे ॥
bhagwad_gita::148.english_translation: The ignorant, deluded by the qualities of nature, cling to actions born of those qualities. The wise should not unsettle those who do not yet understand fully.
bhagwad_gita::148.translation_literal: प्रकृतेः (of nature) / गुणसम्मूढाः (deluded by the qualities) / सज्जन्ते (they cling) / गुणकर्मसु (to actions of the qualities) / तान् (those) / अकृत्स्नविदः (those who do not know fully) / मन्दान् (the dull-minded) / कृत्स्नवित् (the one who knows fully) / न (not) / विचालयेत् (should unsettle)
bhagwad_gita::148.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::148.essence: Clarity should guide confusion, not crush it.
bhagwad_gita::148.simple_meaning: People lost in the forces of nature become attached to action and its results. A person who understands more deeply should not shake them up unnecessarily.
bhagwad_gita::148.simple_insight: Wisdom does not need to humiliate confusion; it can guide without force.
bhagwad_gita::148.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna explains that most people are driven by nature’s forces and cling to action blindly. The truly wise should not disturb them harshly, but lead them gently toward clarity.
bhagwad_gita::148.modern_relevance: You finally understand a hard truth, but the person beside you is still reacting from fear. Pushing too fast can break trust before understanding has a chance to grow.
bhagwad_gita::148.insight: It teaches restraint in teaching: see confusion clearly, but do not weaponize your clarity.

bhagwad_gita::149.verse_sanskrit: मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा । निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥
bhagwad_gita::149.verse_hindi: तू विवेकवती बुद्धिके द्वारा सम्पूर्ण कर्तव्यकर्मोंको मेरे अर्पण करके कामना, ममता और संतापरहित होकर युद्धरूप कर्तव्यकर्मको कर ॥
bhagwad_gita::149.english_translation: Surrender all actions to me with the disciplined mind. Free from desire, possessiveness, and sorrow, fight.
bhagwad_gita::149.translation_literal: मयि (to me) / सर्वाणि (all) / कर्माणि (actions) / संन्यस्य (having renounced, having surrendered) / अध्यात्मचेतसा (with the inwardly aware mind) / निराशीः (without desire) / निर्ममः (without possessiveness) / भूत्वा (having become) / युध्यस्व (fight) / विगतज्वरः (free from fever, free from distress)
bhagwad_gita::149.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::149.essence: Action becomes free when you stop claiming its results.
bhagwad_gita::149.simple_meaning: Give every action inwardly to the divine, then do your duty without craving results, without clinging, and without inner distress.
bhagwad_gita::149.simple_insight: There is relief in acting cleanly when you stop carrying the outcome as personal property.
bhagwad_gita::149.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while two armies wait. Krishna gives him a way to act without inner collapse: place every deed inwardly before the divine, drop desire and possessiveness, and fight without feverish anxiety.
bhagwad_gita::149.modern_relevance: You send the message, make the hard call, or walk into the tense room knowing the outcome is not yours to own. What remains is clean action.
bhagwad_gita::149.insight: It shifts action from self-protection to offering, so duty can be done without mental strain.

bhagwad_gita::150.verse_sanskrit: ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः । श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः ॥
bhagwad_gita::150.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य दोषदृष्टिसे रहित होकर श्रद्धापूर्वक मेरे इस पूर्वश्लोकमें वर्णित मतका सदा अनुसरण करते हैं, वे भी कर्मोंके बन्धनसे मुक्त हो जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::150.english_translation: Those who always follow this teaching of Mine with trust and without fault-finding are freed from the bonds of action.
bhagwad_gita::150.translation_literal: ये (those) / मे (My) / मतम् (teaching) / इदम् (this) / नित्यम् (always) / अनुतिष्ठन्ति (follow) / मानवाः (people) / श्रद्धावन्तः (full of trust) / अनसूयन्तः (without fault-finding) / मुच्यन्ते (are freed) / ते (they) / अपि (also) / कर्मभिः (from actions)
bhagwad_gita::150.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::150.essence: Trusting the teaching frees action from its binding force.
bhagwad_gita::150.simple_meaning: People who follow Krishna's teaching with trust and without resentment or criticism are freed from the binding effects of action.
bhagwad_gita::150.simple_insight: You do not need perfect understanding to move forward. Trust itself can loosen what keeps you stuck.
bhagwad_gita::150.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna has just explained action without attachment, and now adds the human condition: those who accept this teaching with trust and no bitterness can break free from karma's binding force.
bhagwad_gita::150.modern_relevance: You hear advice that could change your life, but your first reflex is to pick it apart. This verse says the door opens when you stop resisting long enough to try.
bhagwad_gita::150.insight: It shifts the mind from skeptical paralysis to trustful practice.

bhagwad_gita::151.verse_sanskrit: ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् । सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ॥
bhagwad_gita::151.verse_hindi: परन्तु जो मनुष्य मेरे इस मतमें दोषदृष्टि करते हुए इसका अनुष्ठान नहीं करते, उन सम्पूर्ण ज्ञानोंमें मोहित और अविवेकी मनुष्योंको नष्ट हुए ही समझो ॥
bhagwad_gita::151.english_translation: But those who, finding fault with this teaching, do not follow it—know them to be deluded in all knowledge and ruined in understanding.
bhagwad_gita::151.translation_literal: ये (those) / तु (but) / एतत् (this) / अभ्यसूयन्तः (finding fault with) / न (not) / अनुतिष्ठन्ति (follow) / मे (my) / मतम् (teaching) / सर्वज्ञानविमूढान् (deluded in all knowledge) / तान् (them) / विद्धि (know) / नष्टान् (ruined) / अचेतसः (without understanding)
bhagwad_gita::151.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::151.essence: Rejecting clear guidance leaves the mind stranded.
bhagwad_gita::151.simple_meaning: People who reject this teaching out of fault-finding lose clear understanding and become confused. The problem is not the teaching; it is the closed mind that refuses to practise it.
bhagwad_gita::151.simple_insight: Resistance can feel clever, but it quietly cuts you off from clarity.
bhagwad_gita::151.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna still hesitates, and Krishna keeps pressing the case for action without attachment. After promising freedom to those who follow this discipline, Krishna warns that scoffing at it leaves a person mentally lost and unable to see clearly.
bhagwad_gita::151.modern_relevance: You hear advice that could help, but your first reaction is, “That won’t work.” The real trap is not the advice itself — it is the reflex to dismiss what might free you.
bhagwad_gita::151.insight: It shifts the mind from cynical refusal to disciplined practice.

bhagwad_gita::152.verse_sanskrit: सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि । प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥
bhagwad_gita::152.verse_hindi: सम्पूर्ण प्राणी प्रकृतिको प्राप्त होते हैं ।  ज्ञानी महापुरुष भी अपनी प्रकृतिके अनुसार चेष्टा करता है ।  फिर इसमें किसीका हठ क्या करेगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::152.english_translation: Even the wise act according to their own nature. All beings follow nature; what can restraint do?
bhagwad_gita::152.translation_literal: सदृशं (according to) / चेष्टते (acts) / स्वस्याः (of one's own) / प्रकृतेः (nature) / ज्ञानवान् अपि (even the wise) / प्रकृतिम् (nature) / यान्ति (go to) / भूतानि (all beings) / निग्रहः (restraint) / किम् (what) / करिष्यति (will do)
bhagwad_gita::152.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::152.essence: Nature drives behavior; force alone cannot overrule it.
bhagwad_gita::152.simple_meaning: Even a wise person acts according to their own nature. Every living being follows its nature, so force alone cannot change that.
bhagwad_gita::152.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that not everything yields to willpower.
bhagwad_gita::152.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna explains that deep tendencies shape behavior: even the wise act from their nature. This verse prepares Arjuna to understand why mere force cannot solve inner conflict.
bhagwad_gita::152.modern_relevance: You promise yourself you will not check the phone again, then your hand reaches for it before you notice. Krishna points to the harder truth: habits run deep, and brute force alone rarely wins.
bhagwad_gita::152.insight: It shifts attention from moral self-blame to honest observation of ingrained tendencies.

bhagwad_gita::153.verse_sanskrit: इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ । तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥
bhagwad_gita::153.verse_hindi: इन्द्रियइन्द्रियके अर्थमें प्रत्येक इन्द्रियके प्रत्येक विषयमें मनुष्यके राग और द्वेष व्यवस्थासे अनुकूलता और प्रतिकूलताको लेकर स्थित हैं ।  मनुष्यको उन दोनोंके वशमें नहीं होना चाहिये क्योंकि वे दोनों ही इसके पारमार्थिक मार्गमें विघ्न डालनेवाले शत्रु हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::153.english_translation: Attachment and aversion sit in every sense-object. Do not come under their power, for they are your enemies on the path.
bhagwad_gita::153.translation_literal: इन्द्रियस्य-इन्द्रियस्य-अर्थे (in each sense's object) / राग-द्वेषौ (attachment and aversion) / व्यवस्थितौ (are established) / तयोः (of those two) / न (not) / वशम् (under the power) / आगच्छेत् (one should come) / तौ (those two) / हि (indeed) / अस्य (for this one) / परिपन्थिनौ (the two enemies on the path)
bhagwad_gita::153.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::153.essence: Freedom begins when attraction and aversion stop steering action.
bhagwad_gita::153.simple_meaning: Craving and dislike appear in every sense experience. Do not let either one control your choices, because both block the path forward.
bhagwad_gita::153.simple_insight: You are not required to obey every pull and push inside you.
bhagwad_gita::153.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is being taught how to act without being dragged around by inner reactions. Krishna names the two forces that distort judgment: attraction and aversion. Both can sabotage duty before a weapon is even lifted.
bhagwad_gita::153.modern_relevance: You open a message and feel the instant urge to defend yourself, or to ignore it completely. That split-second pull is exactly what this verse warns against.
bhagwad_gita::153.insight: It shifts attention from impulse-driven reaction to conscious choice before action.

bhagwad_gita::154.verse_sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
bhagwad_gita::154.verse_hindi: अच्छी तरह आचरणमें लाये हुए दूसरेके धर्मसे गुणोंकी कमीवाला अपना धर्म श्रेष्ठ है ।  अपने धर्ममें तो मरना भी कल्याणकारक है और दूसरेका धर्म भयको देनेवाला है ॥
bhagwad_gita::154.english_translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than another's duty well performed. Better death in one's own duty; another's duty is dangerous.
bhagwad_gita::154.translation_literal: श्रेयान् (better) / स्वधर्मः (one's own duty) / विगुणः (imperfect, lacking qualities) / परधर्मात् (than another's duty) / स्वनुष्ठितात् (well performed) / स्वधर्मे (in one's own duty) / निधनम् (death) / श्रेयः (better, more auspicious) / परधर्मः (another's duty) / भयावहः (fearful, dangerous)
bhagwad_gita::154.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::154.essence: Imperfect right action is safer than perfect imitation.
bhagwad_gita::154.simple_meaning: Your own responsibility matters more than copying someone else's path. Even if you do it imperfectly, it is better than doing another person's role well.
bhagwad_gita::154.simple_insight: You can stop measuring yourself against others and return to the work that is actually yours.
bhagwad_gita::154.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between his warrior duty and his fear of killing relatives. Krishna answers by grounding him in his own role: the right action is not the one that looks easiest or most polished, but the one that belongs to him.
bhagwad_gita::154.modern_relevance: You are in a room full of people telling you what you should be: the calmer sibling, the louder leader, the easier partner. The verse cuts through the comparison and asks what is actually yours to do.
bhagwad_gita::154.insight: It shifts attention from imitation to rightful action. The measure is not polish, but fidelity to one's own role.

bhagwad_gita::155.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचअथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः । अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥
bhagwad_gita::155.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे वार्ष्णेय  फिर यह मनुष्य न चाहता हुआ भी जबर्दस्ती लगाये हुएकी तरह किससे प्रेरित होकर पापका आचरण करता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::155.english_translation: Arjuna said: O descendant of the Vrishni clan, what drives a person to commit wrongdoing, even unwillingly, as if forced?
bhagwad_gita::155.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / अथ (then) / केन (by what) / प्रयुक्तः (impelled) / अयम् (this) / पापम् (wrongdoing) / चरति (does) / पूरुषः (person) / अनिच्छन् (not desiring) / अपि (even) / वार्ष्णेय (O descendant of the Vrishni clan) / बलात् (by force) / इव (as if) / नियोजितः (appointed / driven) ॥
bhagwad_gita::155.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::155.essence: Compulsion has a cause, and Arjuna wants to name it.
bhagwad_gita::155.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks what makes a person do wrong even when they do not want to, as if some force is pushing them.
bhagwad_gita::155.simple_insight: It gives language to the strange moment when you feel split between intention and action.
bhagwad_gita::155.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has already been told to rise above attachment and follow his duty. Instead of accepting the teaching, he turns to Krishna with a deeper question: what power makes people act against their own will?
bhagwad_gita::155.modern_relevance: You promise yourself you will not send that text, open that tab, or say that cutting remark. Then you do it anyway. The question is no longer moral blame — it is: what is driving me?
bhagwad_gita::155.insight: It shifts attention from self-blame to investigating the hidden force behind compulsive action.

bhagwad_gita::156.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचकाम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः । महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::156.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  रजोगुणसे उत्पन्न हुआ यह काम ही क्रोध है ।  यह बहुत खानेवाला और महापापी है ।  इस विषयमें तू इसको ही वैरी जान ॥
bhagwad_gita::156.english_translation: Krishna said: Desire, born of rajas, turns into anger. It is all-consuming and deeply destructive. Know it as your enemy here.
bhagwad_gita::156.translation_literal: श्रीभगवानुवाच (the Lord said) / कामः (desire) / एषः (this) / क्रोधः (anger) / एषः (this) / रजोगुणसमुद्भवः (born from the quality of passion) / महाशनः (all-devouring) / महापाप्मा (greatly destructive) / विद्धि (know) / एनम् (this) / इह (here) / वैरिणम् (as an enemy)
bhagwad_gita::156.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::156.essence: Desire is not harmless; it mutates into the force that ruins judgment.
bhagwad_gita::156.simple_meaning: Desire, born from restlessness, turns into anger and destroys clarity. Krishna says to recognize it as an enemy before it takes over.
bhagwad_gita::156.simple_insight: You can catch the fire early, before it becomes a blaze that controls your choices.
bhagwad_gita::156.detailed_meaning: Arjuna has asked why people act against their own judgment. Krishna answers on the battlefield: the real enemy is not outside, but the force of desire rising into anger and blinding discernment. This verse names it so Arjuna can fight it first.
bhagwad_gita::156.modern_relevance: You open a message, feel ignored, and the irritation hardens into a cutting reply. The first spark looked harmless; the full fire changes everything.
bhagwad_gita::156.insight: It shifts the mind from blaming others to spotting the inner impulse that distorts action.

bhagwad_gita::157.verse_sanskrit: धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च । यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::157.verse_hindi: जैसे धुएँसे अग्नि और मैलसे दर्पण ढक जाता है तथा जैसे जेरसे गर्भ ढका रहता है, ऐसे ही उस कामके द्वारा यह ज्ञान  विवेक ढका हुआ है ॥
bhagwad_gita::157.english_translation: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and a womb by a membrane, so clear seeing is covered by desire.
bhagwad_gita::157.translation_literal: धूमेन (by smoke) / आव्रियते (is covered) / वह्निः (fire) / यथा (as) / आदर्शः (mirror) / मलेन (by dust) / च (and) / यथा (as) / उल्बेन (by a membrane/womb-covering) / आवृतः (covered) / गर्भः (womb/embryo) / तथा (so) / तेन (by that) / इदम् (this) / आवृतम् (is covered)
bhagwad_gita::157.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::157.essence: Clear seeing is not destroyed; it is simply covered.
bhagwad_gita::157.simple_meaning: Desire hides clear seeing just as smoke hides fire, dust hides a mirror, and a womb-covering hides an embryo.
bhagwad_gita::157.simple_insight: The problem is not lack of intelligence. Something deeper is veiling what you already know.
bhagwad_gita::157.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has asked why people do wrong even against their will. Krishna has named desire as the enemy, and now he shows how it works: it does not erase wisdom, it covers it, just as smoke, dust, and a womb-covering hide what is already there.
bhagwad_gita::157.modern_relevance: You know the right thing to say, but the message sits unopened while anger blurs your judgment. The clarity is still there; something is clouding it.
bhagwad_gita::157.insight: It shifts attention from searching for new answers to removing the obstruction already blocking clear judgment.

bhagwad_gita::158.verse_sanskrit: आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा । कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥
bhagwad_gita::158.verse_hindi: और हे कुन्तीनन्दन  इस अग्निके समान कभी तृप्त न होनेवाले और विवेकियोंके नित्य वैरी इस कामके द्वारा मनुष्यका विवेक ढका हुआ है ॥
bhagwad_gita::158.english_translation: O son of Kunti, wisdom is covered by this desire, the eternal enemy of the wise, as fire is never satisfied.
bhagwad_gita::158.translation_literal: आवृतम् (covered) / ज्ञानम् (wisdom) / एतेन (by this) / ज्ञानिनः (of the wise) / नित्य-वैरिणा (by the eternal enemy) / काम-रूपेण (in the form of desire) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / दुष्पूरेण (by the hard-to-satisfy) / अनलेन (by fire)
bhagwad_gita::158.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::158.essence: Desire does not just tempt; it hides wisdom itself.
bhagwad_gita::158.simple_meaning: Desire hides clear understanding. It never feels satisfied, and it keeps working against the wise like an unquenchable fire.
bhagwad_gita::158.simple_insight: You can see how craving does not just tempt you; it blinds you.
bhagwad_gita::158.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen while Krishna explains the real enemy behind confusion. Desire does not merely distract; it covers wisdom itself, like a fire that never says enough.
bhagwad_gita::158.modern_relevance: You open one more tab, then another, then another, hoping the urge will settle. It does not. It keeps your judgment fogged until you notice what is driving you.
bhagwad_gita::158.insight: It shifts attention from fighting symptoms to seeing desire as the force that clouds judgment.

bhagwad_gita::159.verse_sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते । एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::159.verse_hindi: इन्द्रियाँ, मन और बुद्धि इस कामके वासस्थान कहे गये हैं ।  यह काम इन इन्द्रियाँ, मन और बुद्धि के द्वारा ज्ञानको ढककर देहाभिमानी मनुष्यको मोहित करता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::159.english_translation: The senses, the mind, and the discerning mind are said to be its seat. Through them, it deludes the embodied person by veiling understanding.
bhagwad_gita::159.translation_literal: इन्द्रियाणि (the senses) / मनः (the mind) / बुद्धिः (the discerning mind) / अस्य (of this) / अधिष्ठानम् (seat, basis) / उच्यते (is said to be) । / एतैः (through these) / विमोहयति (deludes) / एषः (this) / ज्ञानम् (understanding) / आवृत्य (covering) / देहिनम् (the embodied one)
bhagwad_gita::159.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::159.essence: Desire conquers by hijacking the mind's own instruments.
bhagwad_gita::159.simple_meaning: Desire works through the senses, the restless mind, and the discerning mind. It clouds understanding and makes a person act blindly.
bhagwad_gita::159.simple_insight: You are less helpless when you can see how desire takes over your mind.
bhagwad_gita::159.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Arjuna is still frozen, and Krishna is tracing the enemy inside the human system. Desire does not attack from outside; it uses the senses, the restless mind, and even the discerning mind to cloud judgment.
bhagwad_gita::159.modern_relevance: You open a message you knew would pull you off course, and suddenly the whole evening is gone. The pull did not begin in the app; it began in the chain of attention.
bhagwad_gita::159.insight: It teaches you to watch where desire enters so you can interrupt the slide before judgment is lost.

bhagwad_gita::160.verse_sanskrit: तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ । पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::160.verse_hindi: इसलिये हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  तू सबसे पहले इन्द्रियोंको वशमें करके इस ज्ञान और विज्ञानका नाश करनेवाले महान् पापी कामको अवश्य ही बलपूर्वक मार डाल ॥
bhagwad_gita::160.english_translation: Therefore, O best of the Bharatas, first control the senses, and then destroy this great sinner, the destroyer of knowledge and wisdom.
bhagwad_gita::160.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) / त्वम् (you) / इन्द्रियाणि (the senses) / आदौ (first) / नियम्य (having restrained) / भरतर्षभ (O best of the Bharatas) / पाप्मानम् (the sinful one) / प्रजहि (strike down) / हि (indeed) / एनम् (this) / ज्ञान-विज्ञान-नाशनम् (the destroyer of knowledge and wisdom)
bhagwad_gita::160.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::160.simple_meaning: Control the senses first, because unchecked craving destroys clear understanding. The real enemy is not outside you but the force that clouds judgment from within.
bhagwad_gita::160.simple_insight: There is relief in naming the real battle: not the world around you, but the impulse that hijacks your mind.
bhagwad_gita::160.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while two armies wait. Krishna has already named desire as the force that blinds judgment. Now he gives the first practical step: restrain the senses, because only then can Arjuna act without being ruled from within.
bhagwad_gita::160.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that could end the relationship, or keep the promise that costs you comfort. Your hands shake over the phone. Krishna's advice is simple: stop the rush of impulse first, then choose.
bhagwad_gita::160.insight: It shifts action from reactive impulse to deliberate restraint, so judgment can return before choice.

bhagwad_gita::161.verse_sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः । मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥
bhagwad_gita::161.verse_hindi: इन्द्रियोंको स्थूलशरीरसे पर श्रेष्ठ, सबल, प्रकाशक, व्यापक तथा सूक्ष्म कहते हैं ।  इन्द्रियोंसे पर मन है, मनसे भी पर बुद्धि है औऱ जो बुद्धिसे भी पर है, वह काम है ।  इस तरह बुद्धिसे पर  काम को जानकर अपने द्वारा अपनेआपको वशमें करके हे महाबाहो  तू इस कामरूप दुर्जय शत्रुको मार डाल ॥
bhagwad_gita::161.english_translation: The senses are higher than the body; the mind is higher than the senses; the discerning mind is higher than the mind. What is beyond the discerning mind, however, is desire.
bhagwad_gita::161.translation_literal: इन्द्रियाणि (the senses) / पराणि (higher) / आहुः (they say) / इन्द्रियेभ्यः (than the senses) / परम् (higher) / मनः (the mind) / मनसः (than the mind) / तु (but) / परा (higher) / बुद्धिः (the discerning mind) / यः (which) / बुद्धेः (than the discerning mind) / परतः (higher) / तु (but) / सः (that)
bhagwad_gita::161.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::161.essence: Desire sits above reason, so mastery must begin earlier.
bhagwad_gita::161.simple_meaning: The senses are above the body, the mind is above the senses, and the discerning mind is above the mind. Beyond even the discerning mind stands desire, which must be mastered.
bhagwad_gita::161.simple_insight: You are not helpless before impulse. There is a level in you that can overrule it.
bhagwad_gita::161.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna traces the chain that drives collapse: body, senses, mind, discerning mind, and then desire. This verse shows where control must begin, so Arjuna can fight the inner enemy before facing the outer one.
bhagwad_gita::161.modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message and lose twenty minutes. The pull did not start in your hands; it rose from deeper layers. You can catch it earlier.
bhagwad_gita::161.insight: It teaches you to locate impulse before it becomes action, and to use discernment before desire takes over.

bhagwad_gita::162.verse_sanskrit: एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना । जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::162.verse_hindi: इन्द्रियोंको स्थूलशरीरसे पर श्रेष्ठ, सबल, प्रकाशक, व्यापक तथा सूक्ष्म कहते हैं ।  इन्द्रियोंसे पर मन है, मनसे भी पर बुद्धि है औऱ जो बुद्धिसे भी पर है वह काम है ।  इस तरह बुद्धिसे पर  काम को जानकर अपने द्वारा अपनेआपको वशमें करके हे महाबाहो  तू इस कामरूप दुर्जय शत्रुको मार डाल ॥
bhagwad_gita::162.english_translation: Thus, knowing the higher beyond the intellect, steady the lower self by the higher self, and destroy that enemy in the form of desire, which is hard to conquer.
bhagwad_gita::162.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / बुद्धेः (of the intellect) / परम् (higher) / बुद्ध्वा (knowing) / संस्तभ्य (steadying) / आत्मानम् (the lower self) / आत्मना (by the higher self) / जहि (destroy) / शत्रुम् (enemy) / महाबाहो (mighty-armed one) / कामरूपम् (in the form of desire) / दुरासदम् (hard to conquer)
bhagwad_gita::162.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::162.essence: Desire loses power when the higher mind takes command.
bhagwad_gita::162.simple_meaning: Recognize that desire is not the highest force in you. Use your deeper discernment to steady yourself and overcome it.
bhagwad_gita::162.simple_insight: You are not helpless before desire; a steadier part of you can lead.
bhagwad_gita::162.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen. Krishna has just mapped the chain from senses to mind to intellect, and now names the real enemy: desire. The teaching turns inward because the war begins inside.
bhagwad_gita::162.modern_relevance: You open the app to check one message and end up scrolling for an hour. The urge feels automatic, but another part of you can still take the wheel.
bhagwad_gita::162.insight: It shifts the response from suppressing desire to leading with discernment.

bhagwad_gita::163.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचइमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम् । विवस्वान् मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::163.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  मैंने इस अविनाशी योगको सूर्यसे कहा था ।  फिर सूर्यने अपने पुत्र वैवस्वत मनुसे कहा और मनुने अपने पुत्र राजा इक्ष्वाकुसे कहा ॥
bhagwad_gita::163.english_translation: The Lord said: I taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvan. Vivasvan taught it to Manu, and Manu taught it to Ikshvaku.
bhagwad_gita::163.translation_literal: श्रीभगवानुवाच (the Lord said) / इमम् (this) / विवस्वते (to Vivasvan) / योगम् (yoga) / प्रोक्तवान् (taught) / अहम् (I) / अव्ययम् (imperishable) / विवस्वान् (Vivasvan) / मनवे (to Manu) / प्राह (said) / मनुः (Manu) / इक्ष्वाकवे (to Ikshvaku) / अब्रवीत् (spoke)
bhagwad_gita::163.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::163.essence: Timeless wisdom survives by being passed on, not newly invented.
bhagwad_gita::163.simple_meaning: Krishna says he taught this timeless yoga to the sun-god, who passed it to Manu, then to Ikshvaku. The teaching is ancient and preserved through a lineage.
bhagwad_gita::163.simple_insight: Some truths are not invented in a moment; they are handed down carefully across generations.
bhagwad_gita::163.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna shaken and unable to fight, Krishna begins by tracing the teaching back through an ancient lineage: from himself to Vivasvan, then to Manu, then to Ikshvaku. He is showing that this is not a new opinion, but a lost inheritance now being restored.
bhagwad_gita::163.modern_relevance: You inherit a practice from a teacher who learned it from someone before them, and they from someone before them. What feels new to you may be older than your doubts.
bhagwad_gita::163.insight: It shifts the mind from treating wisdom as personal invention to seeing it as a preserved lineage of understanding.

bhagwad_gita::164.verse_sanskrit: एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः । स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप ॥
bhagwad_gita::164.verse_hindi: हे परंतप  इस तरह परम्परासे प्राप्त इस कर्मयोग को राजर्षियोंने जाना ।  परन्तु बहुत समय बीत जानेके कारण वह योग इस मनुष्यलोकमें लुप्तप्राय हो गया ॥
bhagwad_gita::164.english_translation: O scorcher of foes, this yoga was known by the royal sages through an unbroken lineage. In the course of great time, this yoga was lost in this world.
bhagwad_gita::164.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / परम्परा-प्राप्तम् (received through succession) / इमम् (this) / राजर्षयः (royal sages) / विदुः (knew) / सः (that) / कालेन (by time) / इह (here) / महता (great) / योगः (yoga) / नष्टः (lost) / परन्तप (O scorcher of foes)
bhagwad_gita::164.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::164.essence: Even timeless wisdom disappears when no one keeps receiving it.
bhagwad_gita::164.simple_meaning: This ancient yoga was passed down from teacher to student and known by wise rulers, but over time it faded from the world.
bhagwad_gita::164.simple_insight: What is deepest can still be forgotten; it must be handed on, not merely admired.
bhagwad_gita::164.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands shaken while Krishna begins a teaching about an ancient yoga. Krishna says it once moved through an unbroken line of wise rulers, but over long ages it has nearly disappeared from human life.
bhagwad_gita::164.modern_relevance: A skill your grandfather knew may survive only as a half-remembered family story. Without living transmission, even the most valuable wisdom can vanish between generations.
bhagwad_gita::164.insight: It shifts attention from private belief to living lineage, showing that wisdom survives only when it is carried forward.

bhagwad_gita::165.verse_sanskrit: स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः । भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::165.verse_hindi: तू मेरा भक्त और प्रिय सखा है, इसलिये वही यह पुरातन योग आज मैंने तुझसे कहा है क्योंकि यह बड़ा उत्तम रहस्य है ॥
bhagwad_gita::165.english_translation: Because you are my devotee and my friend, I have taught you today this ancient yoga. It is a supreme secret.
bhagwad_gita::165.translation_literal: सः (that) / एव (indeed) / अयम् (this) / मया (by me) / ते (to you) / अद्य (today) / योगः (yoga) / प्रोक्तः (spoken) / पुरातनः (ancient) / भक्तः (devotee) / असि (you are) / मे (my) / सखा (friend) / च (and) / इति (thus) / रहस्यम् (secret) / हि (indeed) / एतत् (this) / उत्तमम् (supreme)
bhagwad_gita::165.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::165.essence: The deepest teaching opens only to devotion and trust.
bhagwad_gita::165.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is teaching Arjuna an ancient teaching because Arjuna is both devoted and close to him. This teaching is a rare and highest secret.
bhagwad_gita::165.simple_insight: Closeness opens what argument cannot. Trust makes room for the deepest teaching.
bhagwad_gita::165.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still stunned by Krishna's earlier claim that this teaching began long ago. Krishna now explains why it is being given here: not to everyone, but to Arjuna, who is both devoted and a trusted friend. That relationship makes the hidden teaching possible.
bhagwad_gita::165.modern_relevance: A mentor finally tells you the hard truth after years of trust, not because you asked perfectly, but because you are ready to hear it.
bhagwad_gita::165.insight: It shifts the mind from demanding proof to recognising that deep understanding ripens through trust and relationship.

bhagwad_gita::166.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचअपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः । कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति ॥
bhagwad_gita::166.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  आपका जन्म तो अभीका है और सूर्यका जन्म बहुत पुराना है अतः आपने ही सृष्टिके आदिमें सूर्यसे यह योग कहा था  यह बात मैं कैसे समझूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::166.english_translation: Arjuna said: Your birth is recent, while the birth of the Sun is ancient. How am I to understand that you taught this yoga at the beginning of creation?
bhagwad_gita::166.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / अपरम् (later/recent) / भवतः (your) / जन्म (birth) / परम् (earlier/ancient) / जन्म (birth) / विवस्वतः (of the Sun) / कथम् (how) / एतत् (this) / विजानीयाम् (may I understand) / त्वम् (you) / आदौ (at the beginning) / प्रोक्तवान् (had spoken) / इति (thus)
bhagwad_gita::166.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::166.essence: Doubt becomes the doorway to deeper seeing.
bhagwad_gita::166.simple_meaning: Arjuna doubts Krishna's claim. Krishna is younger than the Sun, so Arjuna cannot see how Krishna could have taught this yoga at the beginning of creation.
bhagwad_gita::166.simple_insight: Honest doubt can open the door to deeper understanding.
bhagwad_gita::166.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has just heard Krishna say this ancient yoga was first taught at the start of creation. That claim collides with ordinary time: Krishna stands before him as a living charioteer, while the Sun is unimaginably ancient. Arjuna asks how both can be true.
bhagwad_gita::166.modern_relevance: You hear a claim that sounds impossible from someone standing right in front of you. Instead of pretending you understand, you ask the hard question that exposes the gap.
bhagwad_gita::166.insight: It shifts the mind from passive acceptance to careful inquiry before belief.

bhagwad_gita::167.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचबहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन । तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप ॥
bhagwad_gita::167.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे परन्तप अर्जुन  मेरे और तेरे बहुतसे जन्म हो चुके हैं ।  उन सबको मैं जानता हूँ, पर तू नहीं जानता ॥
bhagwad_gita::167.english_translation: Krishna said: Many births of yours and mine have passed, Arjuna. I know them all, but you do not, enemy-burner.
bhagwad_gita::167.translation_literal: श्री भगवानुवाच (the Blessed Lord said) / बहूनि (many) / मे (my) / व्यतीतानि (passed) / जन्मानि (births) / तव (your) / च (and) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / तानि (those) / अहं (I) / वेद (know) / सर्वाणि (all) / न (not) / त्वं (you) / वेत्थ (know) / परन्तप (enemy-burner)
bhagwad_gita::167.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::167.essence: Your memory is partial; the divine awareness is not.
bhagwad_gita::167.simple_meaning: Krishna says that both of them have passed through many births, but only Krishna remembers them all. Arjuna does not remember his own past births.
bhagwad_gita::167.simple_insight: It softens pride and confusion: your present view is limited, but reality is larger than what you can recall.
bhagwad_gita::167.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna questions how Krishna could have taught the ancient sun-god long ago. Krishna answers by shifting the frame: both of them have crossed many births, but only Krishna remembers them fully. The teaching prepares Arjuna for a deeper truth about Krishna's timeless nature.
bhagwad_gita::167.modern_relevance: You argue from memory, but the other person sees the whole pattern. In a family conflict, you remember only the last hurt; the deeper story stretches far beyond what you can hold.
bhagwad_gita::167.insight: It shifts the mind from assuming its own memory is complete to recognising a wider continuity of existence.

bhagwad_gita::168.verse_sanskrit: अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन् । प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय संभवाम्यात्ममायया ॥
bhagwad_gita::168.verse_hindi: मैं अजन्मा और अविनाशीस्वरूप होते हुए भी तथा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंका ईश्वर होते हुए भी अपनी प्रकृतिको अधीन करके अपनी योगमायासे प्रकट होता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::168.english_translation: Though unborn and imperishable, and though I am the lord of all beings, I manifest myself by controlling my own nature through my own power of appearance.
bhagwad_gita::168.translation_literal: अजः (unborn) / अपि (even though) / सन् (being) / अव्ययात्मा (of imperishable nature) / भूतानाम् (of beings) / ईश्वरः (lord) / अपि (even though) / सन् (being) / प्रकृतिम् (nature) / स्वाम् (own) / अधिष्ठाय (having taken control of) / संभवामि (I manifest) / आत्ममायया (by my own power of appearance)
bhagwad_gita::168.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::168.essence: The unborn can still appear without ceasing to be free.
bhagwad_gita::168.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is unborn and imperishable, yet still appears in the world by using his own power over nature.
bhagwad_gita::168.simple_insight: What seems like a birth is really a chosen appearance, not a limitation.
bhagwad_gita::168.detailed_meaning: Arjuna has asked how Krishna could have taught the sun at the beginning of time. Krishna answers that he is not bound by ordinary birth at all. On this battlefield, with Arjuna confused about time, divinity, and incarnation, Krishna reveals that his appearance is a deliberate manifestation.
bhagwad_gita::168.modern_relevance: Someone you trust suddenly acts in a way you never expected, and you wonder what is real. This verse says appearance can hide power: not everything that shows up is bound the way it seems.
bhagwad_gita::168.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Krishna as a historical figure to seeing incarnation as conscious manifestation.

bhagwad_gita::169.verse_sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत । अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::169.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशी अर्जुन जबजब धर्मकी हानि और अधर्मकी वृद्धि होती है, तबतब ही मैं अपनेआपको साकाररूपसे प्रकट करता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::169.english_translation: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and a rise of adharma, I manifest myself.
bhagwad_gita::169.translation_literal: यदा यदा (whenever) / हि (indeed) / धर्मस्य (of dharma) / ग्लानिः (decline) / भवति (becomes) / भारत (O Bharata) / अभ्युत्थानम् (rise) / अधर्मस्य (of adharma) / तदा (then) / आत्मानम् (myself) / सृजामि (I create/manifest) / अहम् (I)
bhagwad_gita::169.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::169.essence: When dharma collapses, the divine steps into history.
bhagwad_gita::169.simple_meaning: Whenever righteous order declines and wrongdoing rises, Krishna says he manifests in the world to restore balance.
bhagwad_gita::169.simple_insight: Even in chaos, the world is not abandoned. Help arrives when the balance is most strained.
bhagwad_gita::169.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before the war. Krishna has already said he knows all births and is unborn. Now he explains why divine presence enters history: to answer the collapse of dharma and the rise of adharma.
bhagwad_gita::169.modern_relevance: A family, company, or community starts normalizing what once felt unacceptable. The slide feels slow, then sudden. This verse says the turning point is not invisible — the force that restores order is already at work.
bhagwad_gita::169.insight: It shifts the mind from helplessness to confidence that disorder is not the final word.

bhagwad_gita::170.verse_sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् । धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे ॥
bhagwad_gita::170.verse_hindi: साधुओंभक्तों की रक्षा करनेके लिये, पापकर्म करनेवालोंका विनाश करनेके लिये और धर्मकी भलीभाँति स्थापना करनेके लिये मैं युगयुगमें प्रकट हुआ करता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::170.english_translation: For the protection of the righteous, for the destruction of wrongdoers, and for the establishment of dharma, I appear age after age.
bhagwad_gita::170.translation_literal: परित्राणाय (for protection) / साधूनाम् (of the righteous) / विनाशाय (for destruction) / च (and) / दुष्कृताम् (of wrongdoers) / धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय (for the purpose of establishing dharma) / संभवामि (I appear) / युगे युगे (age after age)
bhagwad_gita::170.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::170.essence: The divine returns whenever order must be restored.
bhagwad_gita::170.simple_meaning: Krishna says he appears again and again to protect the good, stop wrongdoing, and restore dharma.
bhagwad_gita::170.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing order is not abandoned. What is worth protecting is protected.
bhagwad_gita::170.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen and Krishna is revealing why divine presence enters the world. After saying he appears whenever dharma declines, Krishna adds the purpose of that appearance: to protect the righteous, remove destructive forces, and restore right order.
bhagwad_gita::170.modern_relevance: When a family system is poisoned by one cruel person, or a workplace has become toxic, you want to believe repair is still possible. This verse insists that protection and restoration are not fantasies.
bhagwad_gita::170.insight: It shifts the mind from passive despair to trust in restorative action.

bhagwad_gita::171.verse_sanskrit: जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः । त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन ॥
bhagwad_gita::171.verse_hindi: हे अर्जुन  मेरे जन्म और कर्म दिव्य हैं ।  इस प्रकार मेरे जन्म और कर्मको जो मनुष्य तत्त्वसे जान लेता अर्थात् दृढ़तापूर्वक मान लेता है, वह शरीरका त्याग करके पुनर्जन्मको प्राप्त नहीं होता, प्रत्युत मुझे प्राप्त होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::171.english_translation: Arjuna, my birth and action are divine. One who truly understands this does not take birth again after leaving the body, but comes to me.
bhagwad_gita::171.translation_literal: जन्म (birth) / कर्म (action) / च (and) / मे (my) / दिव्यम् (divine) / एवम् (thus) / यः (who) / वेत्ति (knows) / तत्त्वतः (in truth) / त्यक्त्वा (having given up) / देहम् (the body) / पुनर्जन्म (rebirth) / न (not) / एति (goes) / माम् (to me) / एति (goes) / सः (that one) / अर्जुन (Arjuna)
bhagwad_gita::171.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::171.essence: Seeing Krishna truly ends the cycle of return.
bhagwad_gita::171.simple_meaning: Krishna says his birth and actions are not ordinary. Whoever understands their divine nature reaches him and is not born again.
bhagwad_gita::171.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that the deepest reality is already working through what looks human.
bhagwad_gita::171.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen, and Krishna is explaining who he really is. After describing why he appears in the world, Krishna says that his birth and action are divine. Understanding that truth changes a person’s fate beyond bodily death.
bhagwad_gita::171.modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary, yet their presence changes everything. The mind that sees only the surface misses the deeper reality already shaping the moment.
bhagwad_gita::171.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Krishna as a person to recognising divine action in human form.

bhagwad_gita::172.verse_sanskrit: वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः । बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::172.verse_hindi: राग, भय और क्रोधसे सर्वथा रहित, मेरेमें ही तल्लीन, मेरे ही आश्रित तथा ज्ञानरूप तपसे पवित्र हुए बहुतसे भक्त मेरे भाव स्वरूप को प्राप्त हो चुके हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::172.english_translation: Many, purified by the austerity of knowledge, free from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in Me and taking refuge in Me, have attained My being.
bhagwad_gita::172.translation_literal: वीतरागभयक्रोधाः (free from attachment, fear, and anger) / मन्मयाः (mind fixed in Me) / मामुपाश्रिताः (taking refuge in Me) / बहवः (many) / ज्ञानतपसा (by the austerity of knowledge) / पूताः (purified) / मद्भावम् (My being/state) / आगताः (have attained)
bhagwad_gita::172.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::172.essence: Purified minds reach what fear and craving cannot.
bhagwad_gita::172.simple_meaning: People who shed attachment, fear, and anger, and stay centered in the divine, become purified through knowledge and reach that divine state.
bhagwad_gita::172.simple_insight: Inner freedom feels possible when the mind is no longer ruled by fear or reaction.
bhagwad_gita::172.detailed_meaning: Krishna has just explained that understanding his divine nature leads beyond rebirth. He now adds that many have reached him by becoming free of attachment, fear, and anger, and by purifying themselves through knowledge. The teaching is no longer abstract; it shows the inner condition that makes realization possible.
bhagwad_gita::172.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, make the apology, or walk away from what is familiar. The shaking in your chest matters less than whether fear, anger, and clinging are still steering.
bhagwad_gita::172.insight: It shifts attention from outer achievement to inner purification as the condition for transformation.

bhagwad_gita::173.verse_sanskrit: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् । मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥
bhagwad_gita::173.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन  जो भक्त जिस प्रकार मेरी शरण लेते हैं, मैं उन्हें उसी प्रकार आश्रय देता हूँ क्योंकि सभी मनुष्य सब प्रकारसे मेरे मार्गका अनुकरण करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::173.english_translation: As people approach Me, so I respond to them. All people follow My path in every way, O Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::173.translation_literal: ये (who) / यथा (in whatever way) / माम् (Me) / प्रपद्यन्ते (take refuge) / तान् (them) / तथा (in that way) / एव (indeed) / भजामि (I favor/respond to) / अहम् (I) / मम (My) / वर्त्म (path) / अनुवर्तन्ते (follow) / मनुष्याः (people) / पार्थ (O Arjuna) / सर्वशः (in every way)
bhagwad_gita::173.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::173.essence: The divine response matches the way you come forward.
bhagwad_gita::173.simple_meaning: People meet the divine according to their own approach, and the divine responds accordingly. Everyone ultimately follows that same higher path, even if they do it unconsciously.
bhagwad_gita::173.simple_insight: You do not have to begin perfectly. Honest reaching is already a real meeting.
bhagwad_gita::173.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna has begun explaining how action and understanding work together. After describing pure seekers, Krishna adds that every person meets the divine according to their own attitude, and that all lives are already moving within that larger order.
bhagwad_gita::173.modern_relevance: You finally admit you need help, but you do it half-defensively, expecting rejection. The response you receive often mirrors the honesty, openness, or resistance you bring.
bhagwad_gita::173.insight: It shifts the mind from demanding one correct approach to recognizing that sincerity itself shapes the encounter.

bhagwad_gita::174.verse_sanskrit: काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः । क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा ॥
bhagwad_gita::174.verse_hindi: कर्मोंकी सिद्धि फल चाहनेवाले मनुष्य देवताओंकी उपासना किया करते हैं क्योंकि इस मनुष्यलोकमें कर्मोंसे उत्पन्न होनेवाली सिद्धि जल्दी मिल जाती है ॥
bhagwad_gita::174.english_translation: People who want quick success worship radiant beings, because results from action come quickly in the human world.
bhagwad_gita::174.translation_literal: काङ्क्षन्तः (desiring) / कर्मणाम् (of actions) / सिद्धिम् (success, accomplishment) / यजन्ते (worship) / इह (here) / देवताः (radiant beings) / क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / हि (indeed) / मानुषे (in human) / लोके (world) / सिद्धिः (success, accomplishment) / भवति (becomes) / कर्मजा (born of action)
bhagwad_gita::174.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::174.essence: Desire for quick success makes people chase fast-acting powers.
bhagwad_gita::174.simple_meaning: People who want immediate success often turn to lesser powers for help, because in the human world action can produce quick results.
bhagwad_gita::174.simple_insight: The urge for speed can make you chase shortcuts instead of understanding what truly works.
bhagwad_gita::174.detailed_meaning: Krishna is explaining why people seek quick gains through ritual power rather than steady inner understanding. On the battlefield, Arjuna wants a way out of crisis now, and Krishna shows how the mind reaches for fast results.
bhagwad_gita::174.modern_relevance: You refresh the app after sending the message, hoping for an instant reply. That hunger for speed can push you toward shortcuts, hacks, and quick fixes that never last.
bhagwad_gita::174.insight: It shifts attention from craving immediate payoff to seeing why the mind reaches for shortcuts.

bhagwad_gita::175.verse_sanskrit: चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः । तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::175.verse_hindi: मेरे द्वारा गुणों और कर्मोंके विभागपूर्वक चारों वर्णोंकी रचना की गयी है ।  उससृष्टिरचना आदि का कर्ता होनेपर भी मुझ अव्यय रमेश्वरको तू अकर्ता जान ।  कारण कि कर्मोंके फलमें मेरी स्पृहा नहीं है, इसलिये मुझे कर्म लिप्त नहीं करते ।  इस प्रकार जो मुझे तत्त्वसे जान लेता है, वह भी कर्मोंसे नहीं बँधता ॥
bhagwad_gita::175.english_translation: The four social orders were created by Me according to qualities and actions. Though I am their maker, know Me as the unchanging non-doer.
bhagwad_gita::175.translation_literal: चातुर्वर्ण्यम् (the four social orders) / मया (by Me) / सृष्टम् (created) / गुणकर्मविभागशः (according to division of qualities and actions) / तस्य (of that) / कर्तारम् (maker) / अपि (even) / माम् (Me) / विद्धि (know) / अकर्तारम् (as non-doer) / अव्ययम् (unchanging)
bhagwad_gita::175.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::175.essence: The source of order stands outside the order it creates.
bhagwad_gita::175.simple_meaning: The four social orders arise from qualities and actions, but Krishna says he remains the unchanging one who is not bound by creation.
bhagwad_gita::175.simple_insight: You can participate in structure without being trapped by it.
bhagwad_gita::175.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen by conflict and confusion. Krishna now explains that even the world's order comes from him, yet he is not bound by what he sets in motion. The teaching points beyond social roles to the unchanging source behind them.
bhagwad_gita::175.modern_relevance: You are handed a role, a label, a family pattern, a job title, and everyone acts as if that is all you are. This verse says the structure may shape action, but it does not imprison the one who sees clearly.
bhagwad_gita::175.insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with social form to seeing the unchanging awareness behind all roles.

bhagwad_gita::176.verse_sanskrit: न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा । इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::176.verse_hindi: मेरे द्वारा गुणों और कर्मोंके विभागपूर्वक चारों वर्णोंकी रचना की गयी है ।  उससृष्टिरचना आदि का कर्ता होनेपर भी मुझ अव्यय परमेश्वरको तू अकर्ता जान ।  कारण कि कर्मोंके फलमें मेरी स्पृहा नहीं है, इसलिये मुझे कर्म लिप्त नहीं करते ।  इस प्रकार जो मुझे तत्त्वसे जान लेता है, वह भी कर्मोंसे नहीं बँधता ॥
bhagwad_gita::176.english_translation: Actions do not stain me, and I do not crave their fruits. One who knows me this way is not bound by actions.
bhagwad_gita::176.translation_literal: न मां (not me) / कर्माणि (actions) / लिम्पन्ति (stain) / न (not) / मे (my) / कर्मफले (in the fruit of action) / स्पृहा (desire) । इति (thus) / माम् (me) / यः (who) / अभिजानाति (knows truly) / कर्मभिः (by actions) / न (not) / सः (he) / बध्यते (is bound)
bhagwad_gita::176.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::176.essence: Knowing the action is not yours to possess breaks its grip.
bhagwad_gita::176.simple_meaning: Actions do not affect Krishna, because he has no desire for their results. Anyone who understands this deeply is also freed from being bound by action.
bhagwad_gita::176.simple_insight: There is relief in acting fully without being trapped by what comes back.
bhagwad_gita::176.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna explains why he is untouched by action even while shaping the world. He has no hunger for results, and that same understanding can free Arjuna from fear of being bound by duty.
bhagwad_gita::176.modern_relevance: You send the message, make the hard call, or finish the surgery, then wait for the reaction. The verse says your hands can stay clean even when the outcome is beyond you.
bhagwad_gita::176.insight: It shifts the mind from ownership of results to freedom in action.

bhagwad_gita::177.verse_sanskrit: एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः । कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::177.verse_hindi: पूर्वकालके मुमुक्षुओंने भी इस प्रकार जानकर कर्म किये हैं, इसलिये तू भी पूर्वजोंके द्वारा सदासे किये जानेवाले कर्मोंको ही उन्हींकी तरह कर ॥
bhagwad_gita::177.english_translation: Even seekers of freedom acted after knowing this. Therefore, do the work that your ancestors always did.
bhagwad_gita::177.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / कृतम् (done) / कर्म (action) / पूर्वैः (by the earlier ones) / अपि (also) / मुमुक्षुभिः (by seekers of freedom) / कुरु (do) / कर्म (action) / एव (indeed) / तस्मात् (therefore) / त्वम् (you) / पूर्वैः (by the earlier ones) / पूर्वतरम् (from ancient times) / कृतम् (done) /
bhagwad_gita::177.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::177.essence: Right action is the path even for those seeking freedom.
bhagwad_gita::177.simple_meaning: People seeking freedom acted in this way before you. So you should do the same rightful work that has long been done.
bhagwad_gita::177.simple_insight: You are not inventing the path alone. Steady action has always been the way through.
bhagwad_gita::177.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before the war. Krishna reminds him that earlier seekers of freedom also understood this and still acted. The teaching pushes Arjuna back into his rightful duty.
bhagwad_gita::177.modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, phone in hand, about to tell the truth no one wants. The path is not to escape the hard duty, but to do it cleanly.
bhagwad_gita::177.insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to inherited responsibility: act because the work is right, not because it feels easy.

bhagwad_gita::178.verse_sanskrit: किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः । तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥
bhagwad_gita::178.verse_hindi: कर्म क्या है और अकर्म क्या है  इस प्रकार इस विषयमें विद्वान् भी मोहित हो जाते हैं ।  अतः वह कर्मतत्त्व मैं तुम्हें भलीभाँति कहूँगा, जिसको जानकर तू अशुभ संसारबन्धन से मुक्त हो जायगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::178.english_translation: What is action, and what is inaction? Even the wise are confused here. I will explain that action to you, knowing which you will be freed from what is harmful.
bhagwad_gita::178.translation_literal: किम् (what) / कर्म (action) / किम्-अकर्म (what [is] inaction) / इति (thus) / कवयः (the wise) / अपि (even) / अत्र (here) / मोहिताः (deluded) / तत् (that) / ते (to you) / कर्म (action) / प्रवक्ष्यामि (I will explain fully) / यत् (which) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / मोक्ष्यसे (you will be freed) / अशुभात् (from the harmful)
bhagwad_gita::178.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::178.essence: Clear seeing about action is what breaks bondage.
bhagwad_gita::178.simple_meaning: Even intelligent people get confused about what action and inaction really mean. Krishna says he will explain it clearly so Arjuna can be freed from harmful bondage.
bhagwad_gita::178.simple_insight: Clarity can break confusion that effort alone cannot.
bhagwad_gita::178.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna has begun untangling the deepest question behind duty. After saying that wise people are confused about action, he promises to explain the real nature of action so Arjuna can move without bondage.
bhagwad_gita::178.modern_relevance: You stand at the edge of a hard choice and realize you do not even know what the right kind of action looks like. Before moving, you need clarity, not more noise.
bhagwad_gita::178.insight: It shifts the mind from guessing about action to learning its true structure.

bhagwad_gita::179.verse_sanskrit: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः । अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः ॥
bhagwad_gita::179.verse_hindi: कर्मका तत्त्व भी जानना चाहिये और अकर्मका तत्त्व भी जानना चाहिये तथा विकर्मका तत्त्व भी जानना चाहिये क्योंकि कर्मकी गति गहन है ॥
bhagwad_gita::179.english_translation: Action, forbidden action, and inaction must all be understood, because the movement of action is hard to grasp.
bhagwad_gita::179.translation_literal: कर्मणः (of action) / हि (indeed) / अपि (also) / बोद्धव्यम् (must be understood) / बोद्धव्यम् (must be understood) / च (and) / विकर्मणः (of forbidden action) / अकर्मणः (of inaction) / च (and) / बोद्धव्यम् (must be understood) / गहना (deep, hard to grasp) / कर्मणः (of action) / गतिः (movement, course)
bhagwad_gita::179.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::179.essence: Action cannot be judged quickly; its true pattern is subtle.
bhagwad_gita::179.simple_meaning: You must understand action, wrong action, and inaction, because the way action works is subtle and difficult to see.
bhagwad_gita::179.simple_insight: Not every doing is obvious. Clear seeing helps you avoid confusion and act wisely.
bhagwad_gita::179.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen, and Krishna is explaining why moral action is not simple. After saying even wise people are confused about action and inaction, Krishna adds that all three must be understood before Arjuna can move rightly.
bhagwad_gita::179.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, sign the form, or walk away — and every option feels morally tangled. This verse says the first task is to see clearly, not rush blindly.
bhagwad_gita::179.insight: It shifts the mind from automatic reaction to careful discrimination before acting.

bhagwad_gita::180.verse_sanskrit: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः । स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::180.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य कर्ममें अकर्म देखता है और जो अकर्ममें कर्म देखता है, वह मनुष्योंमें बुद्धिमान् है, योगी है और सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंको करनेवाला है ॥
bhagwad_gita::180.english_translation: One who sees action in inaction, and inaction in action, is wise among people; that person is disciplined and complete in action.
bhagwad_gita::180.translation_literal: कर्मणि (in action) / अकर्म (inaction) / यः (who) / पश्येत् (sees) / अकर्मणि (in inaction) / च (and) / कर्म (action) / यः (who) / सः (that one) / बुद्धिमान् (wise) / मनुष्येषु (among people) / सः (that one) / युक्तः (disciplined, united) / कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् (one who does all action completely)
bhagwad_gita::180.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::180.essence: Freedom can live inside action, and bondage can hide inside stillness.
bhagwad_gita::180.simple_meaning: A truly wise person sees that outward action can be inwardly free, and apparent inaction can still hide attachment or effort.
bhagwad_gita::180.simple_insight: You can stop measuring worth by visible busyness and trust a deeper kind of effectiveness.
bhagwad_gita::180.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before battle, and Krishna is explaining the strange nature of action itself. After saying action is hard to understand, he points to a person who acts without inner bondage and sees that real freedom can exist inside movement.
bhagwad_gita::180.modern_relevance: You sit in a silent room after sending the message that may end a relationship. Nothing looks dramatic from outside, yet everything has changed. This verse names that hidden kind of action.
bhagwad_gita::180.insight: It shifts attention from outward motion to the inner state from which action arises.

bhagwad_gita::181.verse_sanskrit: यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः । ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::181.verse_hindi: जिसके सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंके आरम्भ संकल्प और कामनासे रहित हैं तथा जिसके सम्पूर्ण कर्म ज्ञानरूपी अग्निसे जल गये हैं, उसको ज्ञानिजन भी पण्डित बुद्धिमान् कहते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::181.english_translation: The wise call that person learned whose actions begin without desire or personal planning, and whose deeds are burned by the fire of knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::181.translation_literal: यस्य (whose) / सर्वे (all) / समारम्भाः (undertakings, beginnings of action) / कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः (free from desire and intention) / ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं (whose actions are burnt by the fire of knowledge) / तम् (that person) / आहुः (they call) / पण्डितं (learned, wise) / बुधाः (the wise)
bhagwad_gita::181.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::181.essence: Knowledge frees action from craving and leaves no binding trace.
bhagwad_gita::181.simple_meaning: A truly wise person starts actions without craving or mental scheming, and knowledge has already burned up the binding force of those actions.
bhagwad_gita::181.simple_insight: You can act in the world without being driven by wanting or trapped by your own deeds.
bhagwad_gita::181.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen, and Krishna keeps refining the meaning of right action. After showing that true wisdom sees beyond action and inaction, he now defines the person whom the wise respect: one whose beginnings are free from craving and whose karmic burden has been consumed by knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::181.modern_relevance: You send the difficult message after checking your motives one last time. Not to win, not to be praised, not to control the result — only because it is the clean thing to do.
bhagwad_gita::181.insight: It shifts action from desire-driven effort to intention-free clarity, where knowledge dissolves the binding residue of doing.

bhagwad_gita::182.verse_sanskrit: त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः । कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥
bhagwad_gita::182.verse_hindi: जो कर्म और फलकी आसक्तिका त्याग करके आश्रयसे रहित और सदा तृप्त है, वह कर्मोंमें अच्छी तरह लगा हुआ भी वास्तवमें कुछ भी नहीं करता ॥
bhagwad_gita::182.english_translation: One who has abandoned attachment to the fruits of action, remains ever content, and depends on nothing, does nothing at all even while fully engaged in action.
bhagwad_gita::182.translation_literal: त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) / कर्मफलासङ्गम् (attachment to the fruit of action) / नित्यतृप्तः (ever content) / निराश्रयः (without dependence) / कर्मणि (in action) / अभिप्रवृत्तः अपि (even while fully engaged) / न एव (indeed not) / किञ्चित् (anything) / करोति (does) / सः (he)
bhagwad_gita::182.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::182.essence: Action loses its grip when nothing in you waits to possess its fruit.
bhagwad_gita::182.simple_meaning: A person can stay fully active and still be inwardly free by dropping attachment to results and resting in inner contentment.
bhagwad_gita::182.simple_insight: You can give yourself completely without being owned by the outcome.
bhagwad_gita::182.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna now explains the hidden freedom of action: the wise person acts, yet inwardly clings to nothing, so the action leaves no binding trace.
bhagwad_gita::182.modern_relevance: You send the message, make the call, or resign from the safe job — and then you stop chasing the reaction. The clean act is enough.
bhagwad_gita::182.insight: It shifts attention from ownership of results to freedom within action.

bhagwad_gita::183.verse_sanskrit: निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः । शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::183.verse_hindi: जिसका शरीर और अन्तःकरण अच्छी तरहसे वशमें किया हुआ है, जिसने सब प्रकारके संग्रहका परित्याग कर दिया है, ऐसा आशारहित कर्मयोगी केवल शरीरसम्बन्धी कर्म करता हुआ भी पापको प्राप्त नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::183.english_translation: One who has no hope, who has controlled the body and mind, and who has given up all possessions, does only bodily action and incurs no fault.
bhagwad_gita::183.translation_literal: निराशीर् (without hope) / यतचित्तात्मा (one whose mind and inner being are controlled) / त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः (one who has abandoned all possessions) / शारीरम् (bodily) / केवलम् (only) / कर्म (action) / कुर्वन् (doing) / न (not) / आप्नोति (attains) / किल्बिषम् (fault)
bhagwad_gita::183.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::183.essence: Freedom from clinging keeps action untouched.
bhagwad_gita::183.simple_meaning: A person who has no craving, controls the body and mind, and lets go of possessions can act without being stained by wrongdoing.
bhagwad_gita::183.simple_insight: There is relief in acting cleanly without carrying greed, clinging, or inner noise.
bhagwad_gita::183.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen by grief and duty. Krishna keeps refining karma yoga: act without craving, without possession, without inner entanglement. Even bodily action stays clean when the mind is mastered.
bhagwad_gita::183.modern_relevance: You sign the resignation letter, delete the backup plan, and still keep your hands steady. The fear is there, but it no longer owns the action.
bhagwad_gita::183.insight: It shifts action from possession and anxiety to clean, necessary doing.

bhagwad_gita::184.verse_sanskrit: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::184.verse_hindi: जो कर्मयोगी फल की इच्छा के बिना, अपनेआप जो कुछ मिल जाय, उसमें सन्तुष्ट रहता है और जो ईर्ष्यासे रहित, द्वन्द्वोंसे अतीत तथा सिद्धि और असिद्धिमें सम है, वह कर्म करते हुए भी उससे नहीं बँधता ॥
bhagwad_gita::184.english_translation: Content with whatever comes by itself, beyond opposites, free from envy, equal in success and failure, such a person is not bound even while acting.
bhagwad_gita::184.translation_literal: यदृच्छा-लाभ-सन्तुष्टः (content with spontaneous gain) / द्वन्द्व-अतीतः (beyond pairs of opposites) / विमत्सरः (free from envy) / समः (equal) / सिद्धि-असिद्धौ (in success and failure) / च (and) / कृत्वा अपि (even while doing) / न (not) / निबध्यते (is bound)
bhagwad_gita::184.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::184.essence: Equal-minded action leaves no hook for bondage.
bhagwad_gita::184.simple_meaning: A person who is satisfied with whatever comes naturally, stays calm through ups and downs, and does not envy others remains free even while working.
bhagwad_gita::184.simple_insight: Freedom grows when success and failure stop controlling your mood.
bhagwad_gita::184.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen by the weight of consequences. Krishna keeps refining karma yoga: act, but do not let gain, loss, praise, or envy chain the mind. This verse names the inner freedom that makes action clean.
bhagwad_gita::184.modern_relevance: You sent the message, waited, and saw the outcome go sideways. The old urge is to compare, resent, or replay everything. This verse says the work can stay yours without the emotional leash.
