bhagwad_gita::184.insight: It shifts attention from chasing results to staying even-minded while acting.

bhagwad_gita::185.verse_sanskrit: गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः । यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते ॥
bhagwad_gita::185.verse_hindi: जिसकी आसक्ति सर्वथा मिट गयी है, जो मुक्त हो गया है, जिसकी बुद्धि स्वरूपके ज्ञानमें स्थित है, ऐसे केवल यज्ञके लिये कर्म करनेवाले मनुष्यके सम्पूर्ण कर्म विलीन हो जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::185.english_translation: For one who has given up attachment, is freed, and whose mind rests in knowledge, all action melts away when done only for sacrifice.
bhagwad_gita::185.translation_literal: गतसङ्गस्य (of one gone beyond attachment) / मुक्तस्य (of one freed) / ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः (of one whose mind is established in knowledge) / यज्ञाय (for sacrifice) / आचरतः (practising) / कर्म (action) / समग्रम् (entire) / प्रविलीयते (melts away)
bhagwad_gita::185.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::185.essence: Action loses its grip when it becomes offering, not possession.
bhagwad_gita::185.simple_meaning: When attachment is gone and the mind rests in clear understanding, work done as an offering no longer binds a person.
bhagwad_gita::185.simple_insight: There is relief in acting without clinging; the work can be complete without leaving a burden behind.
bhagwad_gita::185.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before the war. Krishna keeps teaching how action can be purified. Here he says that when a person is free of attachment and grounded in knowledge, even action disappears as bondage if it is done only as sacrifice.
bhagwad_gita::185.modern_relevance: You send the message, make the apology, or sign the resignation with a steady hand. The act is finished; the mental grip on it does not have to continue.
bhagwad_gita::185.insight: It shifts action from self-protection to offering, so effort no longer leaves a chain of consequences in the mind.

bhagwad_gita::186.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् । ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥
bhagwad_gita::186.verse_hindi: जिस यज्ञमें अर्पण भी ब्रह्म है, हवी भी ब्रह्म है और ब्रह्मरूप कर्ताके द्वारा ब्रह्मरूप अग्निमें आहुति देनारूप क्रिया भी ब्रह्म है, ऐसे यज्ञको करनेवाले जिस मनुष्यकी ब्रह्ममें ही कर्मसमाधि हो गयी है, उसके द्वारा प्राप्त करनेयोग्य फल भी ब्रह्म ही है ॥
bhagwad_gita::186.english_translation: In such sacrifice, the offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, and the act of offering into the fire of Brahman is Brahman. One whose action is absorbed in Brahman reaches Brahman alone.
bhagwad_gita::186.translation_literal: ब्रह्मार्पणं (Brahman as the offering) / ब्रह्महविः (Brahman as the oblation) / ब्रह्माग्नौ (in the fire of Brahman) / ब्रह्मणा (by Brahman) / हुतम् (offered) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / एव (indeed) / तेन (by that one) / गन्तव्यम् (to be reached) / ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना (by one whose action is absorbed in Brahman)
bhagwad_gita::186.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::186.essence: When action is fully absorbed, even the result is not separate from Brahman.
bhagwad_gita::186.simple_meaning: When action is fully understood, the giver, the offering, the fire, and the result all belong to the same ultimate reality.
bhagwad_gita::186.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that nothing is wasted when action is rooted in the highest truth.
bhagwad_gita::186.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still speaking on the battlefield to Arjuna, who has frozen before the war. After explaining action without attachment, he now shows the deepest form of sacrifice: even the offering, the fire, and the one who acts are all rooted in Brahman.
bhagwad_gita::186.modern_relevance: You are standing before a hard apology, a resignation, or a truth that will change everything. The verse says the whole act can be sacred when your attention is fully aligned.
bhagwad_gita::186.insight: It shifts action from personal striving to complete alignment with the supreme reality.

bhagwad_gita::187.verse_sanskrit: दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते । ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति ॥
bhagwad_gita::187.verse_hindi: अन्य योगीलोग भगवदर्पणरूप यज्ञका ही अनुष्ठान करते हैं और दूसरे योगीलोग ब्रह्मरूप अग्निमें विचाररूप यज्ञके द्वारा ही जीवात्मारूप यज्ञका हवन करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::187.english_translation: Some yogis offer sacrifice to the divine alone. Others offer the self into the fire of Brahman through sacrifice itself.
bhagwad_gita::187.translation_literal: दैवमेव (to the divine alone) / अपरे (others) / यज्ञम् (sacrifice) / योगिनः (yogis) / पर्युपासते (worship) / ब्रह्माग्नौ (in the fire of Brahman) / अपरे (others) / यज्ञम् (sacrifice) / यज्ञेन (by sacrifice) / एव (indeed) / उपजुह्वति (offer)
bhagwad_gita::187.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::187.essence: Sacrifice changes shape, but its aim remains surrender into the absolute.
bhagwad_gita::187.simple_meaning: Different yogis practice sacrifice in different ways. Some dedicate worship to the divine, while others make the act of sacrifice itself into an offering within Brahman.
bhagwad_gita::187.simple_insight: There are many forms of sincere practice, but all can become a way of offering the whole self.
bhagwad_gita::187.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna keeps unfolding the inner logic of action. After describing sacrifice as purified knowledge, Krishna now shows that yogic practice can take different forms, all aimed at offering action back into the absolute.
bhagwad_gita::187.modern_relevance: You sit in a quiet room before a hard decision, trying to get the wording right before you speak. The form may differ, but the real task is the same: let the act become an offering, not a performance.
bhagwad_gita::187.insight: It shifts attention from the outer form of practice to the inward quality of offering.

bhagwad_gita::188.verse_sanskrit: श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति । शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति ॥
bhagwad_gita::188.verse_hindi: अन्य योगीलोग श्रोत्रादि समस्त इन्द्रियोंका संयमरूप अग्नियोंमें हवन किया करते हैं और दूसरे योगीलोग शब्दादि विषयोंका इन्द्रियरूप अग्नियोंमें हवन किया करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::188.english_translation: Some yogis offer the senses into the fires of restraint. Others offer sound and the other sense-objects into the fires of the senses.
bhagwad_gita::188.translation_literal: श्रोत्रादीनि (hearing and the other senses) / इन्द्रियाणि (the senses) / अन्ये (some others) / संयमाग्निषु (into the fires of restraint) / जुह्वति (they offer) / शब्दादीन् (sound and the other objects) / विषयान् (sense-objects) / अन्ये (others) / इन्द्रियाग्निषु (into the fires of the senses) / जुह्वति (they offer)
bhagwad_gita::188.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::188.essence: Restraint can consume desire before desire consumes you.
bhagwad_gita::188.simple_meaning: Some seekers restrain the senses like a fire sacrifice. Others use the senses themselves to consume sense-objects, turning experience into a disciplined offering.
bhagwad_gita::188.simple_insight: Control is not repression; it is a deliberate redirection of appetite.
bhagwad_gita::188.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between action and collapse. Krishna explains inner discipline through sacrifice imagery: one seeker restrains the senses, another lets the senses burn away their own cravings. Both are part of the same training.
bhagwad_gita::188.modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message and lose twenty minutes to noise. The real practice is not pretending desire is absent, but training attention before it carries you away.
bhagwad_gita::188.insight: It shifts discipline from moral guilt to conscious redirection of sensory energy.

bhagwad_gita::189.verse_sanskrit: सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे । आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते ॥
bhagwad_gita::189.verse_hindi: अन्य योगीलोग सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियोंकी क्रियाओंको और प्राणोंकी क्रियाओंको ज्ञानसे प्रकाशित आत्मसंयमयोगरूप अग्निमें हवन किया करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::189.english_translation: Others offer all the activities of the senses and the life-force into the fire of self-control, lit by knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::189.translation_literal: सर्वाणि (all) / इन्द्रियकर्माणि (activities of the senses) / प्राणकर्माणि (activities of the life-force) / च (and) / अपरे (others) / आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ (in the fire of the yoga of self-control) / जुह्वति (offer as an oblation) / ज्ञानदीपिते (kindled by knowledge)
bhagwad_gita::189.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::189.essence: Knowledge turns self-control into a fire that consumes every impulse.
bhagwad_gita::189.simple_meaning: Some seekers train themselves so deeply that every sense activity and every life-force activity is offered into the fire of self-control, which is lit by knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::189.simple_insight: Real mastery begins when even your impulses no longer run the show.
bhagwad_gita::189.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna keeps unfolding the many forms of disciplined offering. After sense-restraint and mental sacrifice, he describes a subtler practice: turning all sensory and vital activity into self-mastery, with knowledge as the fire.
bhagwad_gita::189.modern_relevance: Your hand reaches for the phone before you notice. Your breath shortens, your jaw tightens, your attention scatters. This verse points to a deeper training: not just stopping action, but mastering the energies that drive it.
bhagwad_gita::189.insight: It shifts practice from suppressing behavior to governing the forces beneath behavior.

bhagwad_gita::190.verse_hindi: दूसरे कितने ही तीक्ष्ण व्रत करनेवाले प्रयत्नशील साधक द्रव्यसम्बन्धी यज्ञ करनेवाले हैं, और कितने ही तपोयज्ञ करनेवाले हैं, और दूसरे कितने ही योगयज्ञ करनेवाले हैं, तथा कितने ही स्वाध्यायरूप ज्ञानयज्ञ करनेवाले हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::190.english_translation: Others offer wealth, austerity, yoga, and the study of sacred texts as sacrifice, while disciplined seekers make these offerings with firm vows.
bhagwad_gita::190.translation_literal: द्रव्ययज्ञाः (wealth-offering sacrificers) / तपोयज्ञाः (austerity-offering sacrificers) / योगयज्ञाः (yoga-offering sacrificers) / तथा (likewise) / अपरे (others) / स्वाध्याय-ज्ञान-यज्ञाः (self-study and knowledge sacrificers) / च (and) / यतयः (disciplined seekers) / संशित-व्रताः (those with firm vows)
bhagwad_gita::190.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::190.essence: Sacrifice can be wealth, effort, austerity, or study.
bhagwad_gita::190.simple_meaning: Different seekers turn different things into an offering: wealth, austerity, yoga practice, and study. All of them are disciplined forms of sacrifice.
bhagwad_gita::190.simple_insight: There is more than one way to live with devotion to practice. Even study and restraint can become an offering.
bhagwad_gita::190.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna keeps widening his view of action. After describing sensory restraint and inner discipline, Krishna now names other seekers who turn wealth, austerity, yoga practice, and self-study into offerings.
bhagwad_gita::190.modern_relevance: You are up before dawn, opening a book instead of your phone, or skipping comfort to keep a vow. The sacrifice is not only dramatic; it can be quiet, disciplined, and mental.
bhagwad_gita::190.insight: It expands sacrifice beyond ritual into daily disciplines like study, restraint, and practice.

bhagwad_gita::191.verse_sanskrit: अपाने जुह्वति प्राण प्राणेऽपानं तथाऽपरे । प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::191.verse_hindi: दूसरे कितने ही प्राणायामके परायण हुए योगीलोग अपानमें प्राणका पूरक करके, प्राण और अपानकी गति रोककर फिर प्राणमें अपानका हवन करते हैं तथा अन्य कितने ही नियमित आहार करनेवाले प्राणोंका प्राणोंमें हवन किया करते हैं ।  ये सभी साधक यज्ञोंद्वारा पापोंका नाश करनेवाले और यज्ञोंको जाननेवाले हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::191.english_translation: Some offer the outgoing breath into the incoming breath, and the incoming breath into the outgoing breath, restraining the movement of both through breath-control as their aim. Others, with regulated food, offer the breaths into the breaths. All of them know sacrifice and are cleansed by sacrifice.
bhagwad_gita::191.translation_literal: अपाने (into the outgoing breath) / जुह्वति (offer) / प्राणम् (the incoming breath) / प्राणे (into the incoming breath) / अपानम् (the outgoing breath) / तथाऽपरे (and others likewise) / प्राणापानगती (the movements of incoming and outgoing breaths) / रुद्ध्वा (having restrained) / प्राणायामपरायणाः (devoted to breath-control)
bhagwad_gita::191.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::191.essence: Breath itself can become disciplined offering.
bhagwad_gita::191.simple_meaning: Some practitioners use breath-control as a kind of sacrifice. They regulate inhalation and exhalation, and others do the same with disciplined eating.
bhagwad_gita::191.simple_insight: Even breathing can become a disciplined offering, not a restless habit.
bhagwad_gita::191.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna keeps unfolding the many forms of disciplined action. After speaking of offerings, austerity, and study, he adds breath-control and regulated eating as living sacrifices done by serious practitioners.
bhagwad_gita::191.modern_relevance: You catch yourself holding your breath before sending the message. Instead of letting anxiety drive the body, you slow the breath and regain command of yourself.
bhagwad_gita::191.insight: It turns ordinary bodily regulation into a conscious practice that steadies the mind and weakens impulsive reactivity.

bhagwad_gita::192.verse_sanskrit: अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति । सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::192.verse_hindi: दूसरे कितने ही प्राणायामके परायण हुए योगीलोग अपानमें प्राणका पूरक करके, प्राण और अपानकी गति रोककर फिर प्राणमें अपानका हवन करते हैं तथा अन्य कितने ही नियमित आहार करनेवाले प्राणोंका प्राणोंमें हवन किया करते हैं ।  ये सभी साधक यज्ञोंद्वारा पापोंका नाश करनेवाले और यज्ञोंको जाननेवाले हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::192.english_translation: Some offer the breath into the breath through regulated breathing; some, with regulated food, offer the life-forces into the life-forces. All of them know sacrifice, and sacrifice has washed away their impurities.
bhagwad_gita::192.translation_literal: अपरे (others) / नियताहाराः (regulated in food) / प्राणान् (breaths) / प्राणेषु (into breaths) / जुह्वति (offer) / सर्वे (all) / अपि (indeed) / एते (these) / यज्ञविदः (knowers of sacrifice) / यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः (whose impurities are destroyed by sacrifice)
bhagwad_gita::192.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::192.essence: Discipline itself becomes offering, and offering burns away inner stain.
bhagwad_gita::192.simple_meaning: Some people discipline their breathing, and some control their eating and life-energy. All of them are sincere practitioners of sacrifice, and that practice cleanses them.
bhagwad_gita::192.simple_insight: There is dignity in disciplined practice. Even hidden, inward effort can purify a person.
bhagwad_gita::192.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen while Krishna explains many forms of disciplined offering. After describing different sacrifices, Krishna adds this verse to show that even breath-control and regulated eating are valid offerings that purify the practitioner.
bhagwad_gita::192.modern_relevance: You skip the second coffee, keep your breathing steady, and stop feeding your nerves with more noise. Quiet discipline can be its own offering.
bhagwad_gita::192.insight: It broadens sacrifice beyond ritual into disciplined self-regulation that steadily clears the mind.

bhagwad_gita::193.verse_sanskrit: यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् । नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतो़ऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम ॥
bhagwad_gita::193.verse_hindi: हे कुरुवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  यज्ञसे बचे हुए अमृतका अनुभव करनेवाले सनातन परब्रह्म परमात्माको प्राप्त होते हैं ।  यज्ञ न करनेवाले मनुष्यके लिये यह मनुष्यलोक भी सुखदायक नहीं है, फिर परलोक कैसे सुखदायक होगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::193.english_translation: Those who partake of the nectar left over from sacrifice attain the eternal supreme reality. This world is not for the one who does not perform sacrifice; how then the next world?
bhagwad_gita::193.translation_literal: यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो (those who eat the nectar left over from sacrifice) / यान्ति (go) / ब्रह्म (to the supreme reality) / सनातनम् (eternal) । / न (not) / अयम् (this) / लोकः (world) / अस्ति (is) / अयज्ञस्य (for one without sacrifice) / कुतः (how) / अन्यः (the other) / कुरुसत्तम (O best among the Kurus)
bhagwad_gita::193.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::193.essence: A life without offering cannot even support itself.
bhagwad_gita::193.simple_meaning: People who live by sacrifice and accept its blessed remainder move toward the eternal supreme reality. Without sacrifice, even this life loses its value, so the next one cannot be better.
bhagwad_gita::193.simple_insight: There is relief in giving before taking. Life feels fuller when you live as a participant, not a consumer.
bhagwad_gita::193.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen while Krishna explains how action can become sacred. After describing many forms of sacrifice, Krishna says that those who receive the blessed remainder of sacrifice move toward the eternal supreme reality, while a life without sacrifice cannot even sustain this world.
bhagwad_gita::193.modern_relevance: You keep taking from a relationship, a team, or a family without giving anything back. Eventually the whole thing feels lifeless. The verse says participation is what keeps life alive.
bhagwad_gita::193.insight: It shifts the mind from passive consumption to reciprocal offering, showing that meaningful living depends on contribution.

bhagwad_gita::194.verse_sanskrit: एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे । कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे ॥
bhagwad_gita::194.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार और भी बहुत तरहके यज्ञ वेदकी वाणीमें विस्तारसे कहे गये हैं ।  उन सब यज्ञोंको तू कर्मजन्य जान ।  इस प्रकार जानकर यज्ञ करनेसे तू कर्मबन्धनसे मुक्त हो जायगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::194.english_translation: In this way, many kinds of sacrifice are described in the sacred teaching. Know them all as born of action; knowing this, you will be freed from the bondage of action.
bhagwad_gita::194.translation_literal: एवम् (in this way) / बहुविधाः (many kinds) / यज्ञाः (sacrifices) / वितताः (are विस्तृत / described at length) / ब्रह्मणः (of the sacred teaching) / मुखे (in the mouth) / कर्मजान् (born of action) / विद्धि (know) / तान् (them) / सर्वान् (all) / एवम् (thus) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / विमोक्ष्यसे (you will be freed)
bhagwad_gita::194.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::194.essence: Seeing every offering as action frees you from action’s binding force.
bhagwad_gita::194.simple_meaning: Many kinds of sacrifice are laid out in the sacred teaching. Understand that all of them arise from action, and that understanding frees you from action’s binding force.
bhagwad_gita::194.simple_insight: Clarity itself becomes release when you see action without confusion.
bhagwad_gita::194.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains the many forms of sacrifice already taught in the tradition. Krishna gathers them into one insight: all these acts belong to the realm of action, and seeing that clearly loosens their grip.
bhagwad_gita::194.modern_relevance: You keep replaying a mistake, thinking one more ritual, apology, or correction will make you clean. Seeing the pattern clearly breaks the spell and lets you move on.
bhagwad_gita::194.insight: It shifts the mind from scattered ritual thinking to seeing the common principle behind every act.

bhagwad_gita::195.verse_sanskrit: श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप । सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::195.verse_hindi: हे परन्तप अर्जुन  द्रव्यमय यज्ञसे ज्ञानयज्ञ श्रेष्ठ है ।  सम्पूर्ण कर्म और पदार्थ ज्ञानतत्त्वज्ञान में समाप्त हो जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::195.english_translation: O Arjuna, knowledge-sacrifice is better than sacrifice made of material things. All action and all matter end in knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::195.translation_literal: श्रेयान् (better) / द्रव्यमयात् (than material) / यज्ञात् (than sacrifice) / ज्ञानयज्ञः (knowledge-sacrifice) / परन्तप (O scorcher of foes) / सर्वम् (all) / कर्म (action) / अखिलम् (entire) / पार्थ (O Partha) / ज्ञाने (in knowledge) / परिसमाप्यते (is completed / ends)
bhagwad_gita::195.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::195.essence: Knowledge is the point where every action finally comes to rest.
bhagwad_gita::195.simple_meaning: Inner understanding is higher than outer offerings. Every action and every material effort finally leads toward knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::195.simple_insight: It brings relief: what you do is not wasted, because action can mature into understanding.
bhagwad_gita::195.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before the war. Krishna explains that rituals with material offerings are not the highest form of worship. Deeper than all outward action is knowledge, because every deed finally finds its completion there.
bhagwad_gita::195.modern_relevance: You keep trying to fix a painful situation with more effort, more advice, more buying, more doing. Then one honest insight changes everything. Some problems end not in force, but in understanding.
bhagwad_gita::195.insight: It shifts attention from accumulating outer acts to seeking the understanding that completes them.

bhagwad_gita::196.verse_sanskrit: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::196.verse_hindi: उस तत्त्वज्ञान को तत्त्वदर्शी ज्ञानी महापुरुषोंके पास जाकर समझ ।  उनको साष्टाङ्ग दण्डवत् प्रणाम करनेसे, उनकी सेवा करनेसे और सरलतापूर्वक प्रश्न करनेसे वे तत्त्वदर्शी ज्ञानी महापुरुष तुझे उस तत्त्वज्ञानका उपदेश देंगे ॥
bhagwad_gita::196.english_translation: Know that by prostration, by sincere questioning, and by service. The wise who see reality will teach you that knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::196.translation_literal: तत् (that) / विद्धि (know) / प्रणिपातेन (by prostration) / परिप्रश्नेन (by sincere questioning) / सेवया (by service) / उपदेक्ष्यन्ति (will teach) / ते (to you) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / ज्ञानिनः (the knowers) / तत्त्वदर्शिनः (who see reality)
bhagwad_gita::196.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::196.essence: Humility opens the door to knowledge that pride cannot reach.
bhagwad_gita::196.simple_meaning: Real understanding comes from approaching wise people with humility, honest questions, and service. Those who truly see reality can teach knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::196.simple_insight: You do not have to figure everything out alone. Humility opens the door to understanding.
bhagwad_gita::196.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is paralyzed by confusion. Krishna now shifts from explaining knowledge to showing how it is received: not through pride, but by humble approach, sincere questioning, and service to those who see clearly.
bhagwad_gita::196.modern_relevance: You are stuck on a hard decision and keep re-reading articles, still confused. Then one honest conversation with someone wiser cuts through the noise because you finally ask cleanly and listen fully.
bhagwad_gita::196.insight: It teaches you to seek truth through humility, not ego-driven certainty.

bhagwad_gita::197.verse_sanskrit: यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव । येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि ॥
bhagwad_gita::197.verse_hindi: जिस तत्त्वज्ञान का अनुभव करनेके बाद तू फिर इस प्रकार मोहको नहीं प्राप्त होगा, और हे अर्जुन  जिस तत्त्वज्ञान से तू सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंको निःशेषभावसे पहले अपनेमें और उसके बाद मुझ सच्चिदानन्दघन परमात्मामें देखेगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::197.english_translation: Knowing which, you will not fall into confusion again. Through which, you will see all beings without remainder first in yourself, and then in me.
bhagwad_gita::197.translation_literal: यत् (which) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / न (not) / पुनः (again) / मोहम् (delusion, confusion) / एवम् (thus) / यास्यसि (you will go into) / पाण्डव (O Pandava) / येन (by which) / भूतानि (beings) / अशेषेण (without remainder) / द्रक्ष्यसि (you will see) / आत्मनि (in the self) / अथो (then) / मयि (in me)
bhagwad_gita::197.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::197.essence: Knowing deeply ends confusion by revealing one reality in all beings.
bhagwad_gita::197.simple_meaning: True understanding ends confusion. It lets you see every being as part of one reality, first within yourself and then in the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::197.simple_insight: Clarity feels like relief: the world stops looking scattered and starts making sense as one whole.
bhagwad_gita::197.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna explains the knowledge that dissolves his confusion. This verse says that real understanding changes perception itself: the many beings are seen without separation, first in the true self and then in Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::197.modern_relevance: You stare at a message before sending it, knowing it will change everything. Clear seeing cuts through the fear of fragments and lets you act from wholeness instead of panic.
bhagwad_gita::197.insight: It shifts perception from isolated pieces to a single connected reality, reducing confusion at the root.

bhagwad_gita::198.verse_sanskrit: अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः । सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::198.verse_hindi: अगर तू सब पापियोंसे भी अधिक पापी है, तो भी तू ज्ञानरूपी नौकाके द्वारा निःसन्देह सम्पूर्ण पापसमुद्रसे अच्छी तरह तर जायगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::198.english_translation: Even if you are the worst of wrongdoers, you will cross all wrongdoing by the raft of knowledge alone.
bhagwad_gita::198.translation_literal: अपि (even) / चेदसि (even if you are) / पापेभ्यः (than wrongdoers) / सर्वेभ्यः (all) / पापकृत्तमः (most sinful) / सर्वम् (all) / ज्ञानप्लवेन (by the raft of knowledge) / एव (alone) / वृजिनम् (wrongdoing / trouble) / सन्तरिष्यसि (you will cross over)
bhagwad_gita::198.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::198.essence: Clear understanding can carry even the heaviest past across.
bhagwad_gita::198.simple_meaning: Even if someone has done terrible things, clear understanding can still carry them beyond the whole burden of wrongdoing.
bhagwad_gita::198.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing your worst history does not have the final word.
bhagwad_gita::198.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen by guilt and confusion. Krishna keeps teaching him that knowledge changes everything: even someone burdened by the worst wrongdoing can cross over it. The next verse shows that this knowledge burns action itself.
bhagwad_gita::198.modern_relevance: You replay the mistake in your head after the argument, the lie, the betrayal. Krishna says the mind can stop circling the wound: clear understanding can still carry you through.
bhagwad_gita::198.insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to transformation through clear seeing.

bhagwad_gita::199.verse_sanskrit: यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन । ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥
bhagwad_gita::199.verse_hindi: हे अर्जुन  जैसे प्रज्वलित अग्नि ईंधनोंको सर्वथा भस्म कर देती है, ऐसे ही ज्ञानरूपी अग्नि सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंको सर्वथा भस्म कर देती है ॥
bhagwad_gita::199.english_translation: As a blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, so the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes, Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::199.translation_literal: यथा (just as) / एधांसि (fuel) / समिद्धः (blazing) / अग्निः (fire) / भस्मसात् (to ashes) / कुरुते (makes) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / ज्ञान-अग्निः (fire of knowledge) / सर्व-कर्माणि (all actions) / भस्मसात् (to ashes) / कुरुते (makes) / तथा (so)
bhagwad_gita::199.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::199.essence: Real understanding burns the binding power of every action.
bhagwad_gita::199.simple_meaning: Clear understanding destroys the binding force of past actions, just as fire destroys fuel.
bhagwad_gita::199.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that insight can end what effort alone cannot.
bhagwad_gita::199.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna still stands frozen while Krishna keeps teaching him how action can be transcended. After saying knowledge carries a person across all wrongdoing, Krishna now gives the image: true understanding burns the force of karma completely.
bhagwad_gita::199.modern_relevance: You replay a mistake at 2 a.m., convinced it has branded you forever. Then one honest insight breaks the spell and the story stops running you.
bhagwad_gita::199.insight: It shifts the mind from managing consequences to seeing through the mechanism that creates them.

bhagwad_gita::200.verse_sanskrit: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते । तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥
bhagwad_gita::200.verse_hindi: इस मनुष्यलोकमें ज्ञानके समान पवित्र करनेवाला निःसन्देह दूसरा कोई साधन नहीं है ।  जिसका योग भलीभाँति सिद्ध हो गया है, वह कर्मयोगी उस तत्त्वज्ञानको अवश्य ही स्वयं अपनेआपमें पा लेता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::200.english_translation: No purifier compares to knowledge in this world. The one perfected in yoga finds that knowledge within the self in time.
bhagwad_gita::200.translation_literal: न (not) / हि (indeed) / ज्ञानेन (by knowledge) / सदृशं (equal) / पवित्रम्इह (purifying here) / विद्यते (exists) / तत् (that) / स्वयम् (by oneself) / योगसंसिद्धः (one perfected in yoga) / कालेन (in time) / आत्मनि (in the self) / विन्दति (finds)
bhagwad_gita::200.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::200.essence: Nothing purifies like knowledge, and yoga ripens it from within.
bhagwad_gita::200.simple_meaning: Clear understanding is the highest purifier. A person who has matured through yoga eventually discovers that truth within themselves.
bhagwad_gita::200.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing the deepest clarity is not borrowed from outside; it can ripen inside you.
bhagwad_gita::200.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna keeps turning action into understanding. After saying knowledge burns karma, Krishna adds that no purifier equals knowledge, and that a person perfected through yoga will eventually realize it within.
bhagwad_gita::200.modern_relevance: You’ve tried advice, self-help, and endless opinions, but the knot remains. Then one quiet realization changes everything — not because someone handed it to you, but because it finally became yours.
bhagwad_gita::200.insight: It shifts the seeker from collecting answers to becoming fit for direct realization.

bhagwad_gita::201.verse_sanskrit: श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः । ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥
bhagwad_gita::201.verse_hindi: जो जितेन्द्रिय तथा साधनपरायण है, ऐसा श्रद्धावान् मनुष्य ज्ञानको प्राप्त होता है और ज्ञानको प्राप्त होकर वह तत्काल परम शान्तिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::201.english_translation: The person with trust, discipline, and controlled senses gains knowledge. Having gained knowledge, that person quickly reaches supreme peace.
bhagwad_gita::201.translation_literal: श्रद्धावान् (full of trust) / लभते (attains) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / तत्परः (devoted, intent) / संयतेन्द्रियः (with controlled senses) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / लब्ध्वा (having attained) / पराम् (supreme) / शान्तिम् (peace) / अचिरेण (quickly) / अधिगच्छति (reaches)
bhagwad_gita::201.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::201.essence: Trust, discipline, and restraint make room for peace.
bhagwad_gita::201.simple_meaning: Trust, steady effort, and sense control bring knowledge. Once knowledge arrives, deep peace comes quickly.
bhagwad_gita::201.simple_insight: You do not force clarity. You prepare yourself, and peace arrives with understanding.
bhagwad_gita::201.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, where hesitation has frozen action. After saying knowledge burns karma, he now explains who actually receives that knowledge: the one who trusts, stays focused, and masters the senses.
bhagwad_gita::201.modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, phone in hand, about to hear bad news. Panic will not help. Trust, steadiness, and self-control create the inner space where clear understanding can land.
bhagwad_gita::201.insight: It shifts the mind from demanding certainty first to cultivating the conditions that let clarity arrive.

bhagwad_gita::202.verse_sanskrit: अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति । नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::202.verse_hindi: विवेकहीन और श्रद्धारहित संशयात्मा मनुष्यका पतन हो जाता है ।  ऐसे संशयात्मा मनुष्यके लिये न यह लोक है न परलोक है और न सुख ही है ॥
bhagwad_gita::202.english_translation: The ignorant and faithless person who doubts is ruined. For the doubter, there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.
bhagwad_gita::202.translation_literal: अज्ञः (ignorant) / च (and) / अश्रद्दधानः (without trust) / च (and) / संशयात्मा (a doubting inner being) / विनश्यति (is ruined) / न (not) / अयम् (this) / लोकः (world) / अस्ति (exists) / न (not) / परः (other) / न (not) / सुखम् (happiness) / संशयात्मनः (of the doubting inner being)
bhagwad_gita::202.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::202.essence: A divided mind loses both peace and direction.
bhagwad_gita::202.simple_meaning: A person who lacks clear understanding and trust, and keeps doubting, falls apart. Such a divided mind finds no real happiness here or beyond.
bhagwad_gita::202.simple_insight: You feel the cost of indecision: a mind that won't commit cannot settle anywhere.
bhagwad_gita::202.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield, where hesitation can decide everything. After saying knowledge comes through trust and discipline, he warns that a doubting, faithless mind collapses and cannot find peace in any world.
bhagwad_gita::202.modern_relevance: You keep reopening the same message before sending it, afraid of being wrong. The delay is not caution anymore — it is the split mind making you smaller.
bhagwad_gita::202.insight: It pushes the mind toward commitment: clear seeing and trust are necessary before action can become steady.

bhagwad_gita::203.verse_sanskrit: योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम् । आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥
bhagwad_gita::203.verse_hindi: हे धनञ्जय  योग समता के द्वारा जिसका सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंसे सम्बन्धविच्छेद हो गया है और ज्ञानके द्वारा जिसके सम्पूर्ण संशयोंका नाश हो गया है, ऐसे स्वरूपपरायण मनुष्यको कर्म नहीं बाँधते ॥
bhagwad_gita::203.english_translation: O Dhananjaya, actions do not bind the one who has renounced action through yoga, whose doubts have been cut away by knowledge, and who abides in the true self.
bhagwad_gita::203.translation_literal: योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणम् (one whose actions are renounced through yoga) / ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम् (one whose doubts are cut away by knowledge) / आत्मवन्तम् (the one established in the true self) / न (not) / कर्माणि (actions) / निबध्नन्ति (bind) / धनञ्जय (O Dhananjaya)
bhagwad_gita::203.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::203.essence: Freedom begins when action no longer leaves a hook.
bhagwad_gita::203.simple_meaning: A person rooted in yoga, free of doubt, and established in the true self is not trapped by actions. Action still happens, but it no longer leaves a binding mark.
bhagwad_gita::203.simple_insight: You can stay active without becoming trapped by what you do.
bhagwad_gita::203.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen between armies. Krishna has been dismantling his confusion verse by verse. Here he gives the turning point: when knowledge cuts doubt and yoga loosens attachment, action no longer binds.
bhagwad_gita::203.modern_relevance: You send the message, sign the papers, or walk away from the room knowing the choice is clean. The body acts, but the mind no longer clings to the residue.
bhagwad_gita::203.insight: It shifts attention from the action itself to the state of inner freedom in which action happens.

bhagwad_gita::204.verse_sanskrit: तस्मादज्ञानसंभूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः । छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥
bhagwad_gita::204.verse_hindi: इसलिये हे भरतवंशी अर्जुन  हृदयमें स्थित इस अज्ञानसे उत्पन्न अपने संशयका ज्ञानरूप तलवारसे छेदन करके योग समता में स्थित हो जा, और युद्धके लिये खड़ा हो जा ॥
bhagwad_gita::204.english_translation: Therefore, O Bharata, cut away this doubt in your heart, born of ignorance, with the sword of knowledge. Stand in yoga and rise up for battle.
bhagwad_gita::204.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) / अज्ञानसंभूतम् (born of ignorance) / हृत्स्थम् (situated in the heart) / ज्ञानासिना (with the sword of knowledge) / आत्मनः (of the self) / छित्त्वा (having cut) / एनम् (this) / संशयम् (doubt) / योगम् (in yoga) / आतिष्ठ (stand in) / उत्तिष्ठ (rise up) / भारत (O Bharata)
bhagwad_gita::204.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::204.essence: Knowledge cuts doubt, and then action becomes possible again.
bhagwad_gita::204.simple_meaning: Knowledge should cut through inner doubt, and then you should stand steady and act. Krishna is telling Arjuna to stop wavering and rise for battle.
bhagwad_gita::204.simple_insight: Doubt loses power when you face it directly instead of obeying it.
bhagwad_gita::204.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen while the war waits. Krishna ends his teaching with one final command: use clear understanding to cut away the doubt born of ignorance, then stand up and fight.
bhagwad_gita::204.modern_relevance: You have the message typed out, but your finger hovers over send because you fear the fallout. The mind wants another delay; clarity asks for one clean decision.
bhagwad_gita::204.insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to decisive action after understanding is clear.

bhagwad_gita::205.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचसंन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि । यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्िचतम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::205.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे कृष्ण  आप कर्मोंका स्वरूपसे त्याग करनेकी और फिर कर्मयोगकी प्रशंसा करते हैं ।  अतः इन दोनों साधनोंमें जो एक निश्चितरूपसे कल्याणकारक हो, उसको मेरे लिये कहिये ॥
bhagwad_gita::205.english_translation: Arjuna said: Krishna, you praise both renunciation of action and yoga of action. Tell me clearly which one is definitely better for my welfare.
bhagwad_gita::205.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / संन्यासम् (renunciation) / कर्मणाम् (of actions) / कृष्ण (Krishna) / पुनः (again) / योगम् (yoga) / च (and) / शंससि (you praise) / यत् (which) / श्रेयः (better for welfare) / एतयोः (of these two) / एकम् (one) / तत् (that) / मे (to me) / ब्रूहि (tell) / सुनिश्चितम् (definitely)
bhagwad_gita::205.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::205.essence: Choose the path that truly serves your welfare.
bhagwad_gita::205.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to choose between renouncing action and acting with discipline, and wants the one path that is clearly best.
bhagwad_gita::205.simple_insight: It is honest to ask for clarity when two noble paths seem to pull in different directions.
bhagwad_gita::205.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still shaken and unsure. Krishna has spoken of both renunciation and action, and Arjuna now asks which path truly leads to lasting good. This verse opens the chapter’s central question.
bhagwad_gita::205.modern_relevance: You are torn between quitting a draining commitment and staying to do it well. The mind wants a clean answer, not more philosophy.
bhagwad_gita::205.insight: It shifts the reader from vague spiritual confusion to a direct search for the more beneficial way to live.

bhagwad_gita::206.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचसंन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ । तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::206.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  संन्यास सांख्ययोग और कर्मयोग दोनों ही कल्याण करनेवाले हैं ।  परन्तु उन दोनोंमें भी कर्मसंन्यास सांख्ययोग से कर्मयोग श्रेष्ठ है ॥
bhagwad_gita::206.english_translation: Renunciation and karma yoga both lead to the highest good, but karma yoga is better than renouncing action.
bhagwad_gita::206.translation_literal: संन्यासः (renunciation) / कर्मयोगः (karma yoga) / च (and) / निःश्रेयसकरौ (bringing the highest good) / उभौ (both) / तयोः (of the two) / तु (but) / कर्मसंन्यासात् (than renunciation of action) / कर्मयोगः (karma yoga) / विशिष्यते (is superior)
bhagwad_gita::206.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::206.essence: Renunciation matures when action continues without grasping.
bhagwad_gita::206.simple_meaning: Both renunciation and karma yoga lead to the highest good, but Krishna says karma yoga is better than simply giving up action.
bhagwad_gita::206.simple_insight: You do not have to escape life to grow. Doing your duty cleanly can be the higher way.
bhagwad_gita::206.detailed_meaning: Arjuna has asked which path is better: giving up action or acting rightly. Krishna answers in the middle of the battlefield, where the war has not yet begun, and says both help, but disciplined action without clinging is superior.
bhagwad_gita::206.modern_relevance: You are tempted to quit the conversation, the project, or the relationship just to avoid the mess. Krishna says the cleaner move is not always to withdraw; sometimes it is to stay and act without grasping.
bhagwad_gita::206.insight: It shifts the mind from escape to engaged renunciation: keep acting, but drop possessiveness over the result.

bhagwad_gita::207.verse_sanskrit: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति । निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::207.verse_hindi: हे महाबाहो  जो मनुष्य न किसीसे द्वेष करता है और न किसीकी आकाङ्क्षा करता है वह कर्मयोगी सदा संन्यासी समझनेयोग्य है क्योंकि द्वन्द्वोंसे रहित मनुष्य सुखपूर्वक संसारबन्धनसे मुक्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::207.english_translation: One who neither hates nor desires is always a renunciant. Free from opposites, such a person is easily released from bondage, O mighty-armed one.
bhagwad_gita::207.translation_literal: ज्ञेयः (to be understood) / सः (that one) / नित्यसंन्यासी (always-renunciant) / यः (who) / न (not) / द्वेष्टि (hates) / न (not) / काङ्क्षति (desires) / निर्द्वन्द्वः (free from opposites) / हि (indeed) / महाबाहो (O mighty-armed one) / सुखम् (easily) / बन्धात् (from bondage) / प्रमुच्यते (is released)
bhagwad_gita::207.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::207.essence: Freedom comes when craving and resistance no longer steer the mind.
bhagwad_gita::207.simple_meaning: A true renunciant is not someone who abandons action, but someone who drops hatred and craving. Freedom comes when inner opposites no longer pull the mind.
bhagwad_gita::207.simple_insight: There is relief in not being dragged by what you want or reject.
bhagwad_gita::207.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is torn between two paths: renunciation and action. Krishna now sharpens the teaching. Real renunciation is not escape; it is inner freedom from hatred, craving, and the tug of opposites.
bhagwad_gita::207.modern_relevance: You open a message from someone you resent, then feel the old heat rise. Or you keep refreshing for praise that never arrives. The grip is not the event — it is the wanting and resisting.
bhagwad_gita::207.insight: It shifts renunciation from outward withdrawal to inward non-reactivity.

bhagwad_gita::208.verse_sanskrit: सांख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः । एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::208.verse_hindi: बेसमझ लोग सांख्ययोग और कर्मयोगको अलगअलग फलवाले कहते हैं, न कि पण्डितजन क्योंकि इन दोनोंमेंसे एक साधनमें भी अच्छी तरहसे स्थित मनुष्य दोनोंके फलरूप परमात्माको प्राप्त कर लेता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::208.english_translation: The unwise say that renunciation and yoga lead to different results. The wise see that one who is firmly established in either reaches the same fruit.
bhagwad_gita::208.translation_literal: सांख्ययोगौ (renunciation and yoga) / पृथक् (separate) / बालाः (the unwise) / प्रवदन्ति (declare) / न (not) / पण्डिताः (the wise) / एकम् अपि (even one) / आस्थितः (established) / सम्यक् (properly) / उभयोः (of both) / विन्दते (attains) / फलम् (the fruit)
bhagwad_gita::208.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::208.essence: Different methods can reach the same fulfillment when practiced wholeheartedly.
bhagwad_gita::208.simple_meaning: People who do not understand think renunciation and disciplined action give different results. A wise person sees that either one, practiced well, leads to the same highest fulfillment.
bhagwad_gita::208.simple_insight: You can stop arguing about the “better” path and focus on practicing one sincerely.
bhagwad_gita::208.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna is clarifying the path forward. After saying both renunciation and action can lead to welfare, he now removes the false split between them: a person established in either path reaches the same goal.
bhagwad_gita::208.modern_relevance: You’re torn between quitting everything for a quieter life or staying and doing the hard work where you are. The verse says the split is false — depth matters more than the label on the path.
bhagwad_gita::208.insight: It shifts the mind from comparing spiritual methods to committing fully to one practice.

bhagwad_gita::209.verse_sanskrit: यत्सांख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते । एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
bhagwad_gita::209.verse_hindi: सांख्ययोगियोंके द्वारा जो तत्त्व प्राप्त किया जाता है, कर्मयोगियोंके द्वारा भी वही प्राप्त किया जाता है ।  अतः जो मनुष्य सांख्ययोग और कर्मयोगको फलरूपमें एक देखता है, वही ठीक देखता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::209.english_translation: The state reached by the wise is also reached through yoga. One who sees wisdom and yoga as one sees rightly.
bhagwad_gita::209.translation_literal: यत् (that which) / सांख्यैः (by the wise of analysis) / प्राप्यते (is attained) / स्थानं (state) / तत् (that) / योगैः (by yogis) / अपि (also) / गम्यते (is reached) / एकं (one) / सांख्यं (analysis) / च (and) / योगं (yoga) / च (and) / यः (who) / पश्यति (sees) / सः (that one) / पश्यति (sees rightly)
bhagwad_gita::209.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::209.essence: Different paths can lead to the same freedom.
bhagwad_gita::209.simple_meaning: The wise path of understanding and the path of disciplined action lead to the same realization. Seeing them as separate is the mistake.
bhagwad_gita::209.simple_insight: You can stop ranking paths and relax into what they both accomplish.
bhagwad_gita::209.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen, and Krishna is untangling a false split. He says the state reached by clear understanding is also reached through disciplined action, so the two are not rivals.
bhagwad_gita::209.modern_relevance: You are stuck between quitting and pushing harder, as if only one choice can be right. This verse cuts through that panic: different methods can lead to the same settled place.
bhagwad_gita::209.insight: It shifts the mind from arguing over methods to recognizing the shared result beneath them.

bhagwad_gita::210.verse_sanskrit: संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः । योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म नचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥
bhagwad_gita::210.verse_hindi: परन्तु हे महाबाहो  कर्मयोगके बिना संन्यास सिद्ध होना कठिन है ।  मननशील कर्मयोगी शीघ्र ही ब्रह्मको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::210.english_translation: But, mighty-armed one, renunciation without yoga is hard to attain. The disciplined seeker in yoga quickly reaches the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::210.translation_literal: संन्यासः (renunciation) / तु (but) / महाबाहो (mighty-armed one) / दुःखम् (with difficulty) / आप्तुम् (to attain) / अयोगतः (without yoga) / योगयुक्तः (joined with yoga) / मुनिः (the contemplative sage) / ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / नचिरेण (without delay) / अधिगच्छति (attains)
bhagwad_gita::210.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::210.essence: Real renunciation grows through practice, not withdrawal.
bhagwad_gita::210.simple_meaning: Letting go is not achieved by avoiding action. A steady, disciplined path of yoga leads the thoughtful seeker to the supreme reality quickly.
bhagwad_gita::210.simple_insight: Relief comes from knowing that real renunciation is built through practice, not by forcing yourself to withdraw.
bhagwad_gita::210.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between battle and moral collapse. Krishna continues dismantling the false split between renunciation and action, saying that mere withdrawal is hard, but a disciplined seeker can reach Brahman swiftly.
bhagwad_gita::210.modern_relevance: You quit the argument, delete the app, and still feel the same pull inside. The outer move did nothing because the habit was never uprooted.
bhagwad_gita::210.insight: It shifts renunciation from escape to transformation: act rightly until inner freedom becomes natural.

bhagwad_gita::211.verse_sanskrit: योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः । सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::211.verse_hindi: जिसकी इन्द्रियाँ अपने वशमें हैं, जिसका अन्तःकरण निर्मल है, जिसका शरीर अपने वशमें है और सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंकी आत्मा ही जिसकी आत्मा है, ऐसा कर्मयोगी कर्म करते हुए भी लिप्त नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::211.english_translation: A disciplined yogi, pure in mind, self-mastered, and senses conquered, sees the same self in all beings and is not tainted by action while acting.
bhagwad_gita::211.translation_literal: योगयुक्तः (joined in yoga) / विशुद्धात्मा (pure inner being) / विजितात्मा (self-mastered) / जितेन्द्रियः (senses conquered) / सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा (whose self has become the self of all beings) / कुर्वन् अपि (even while acting) / न (not) / लिप्यते (is stained, clings)
bhagwad_gita::211.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::211.essence: Inner freedom lets action happen without leaving a trace.
bhagwad_gita::211.simple_meaning: A person grounded in yoga, with a pure mind and mastered senses, acts without being stained by action because they see the same self in all beings.
bhagwad_gita::211.simple_insight: You can stay fully active without getting spiritually or emotionally contaminated by what you do.
bhagwad_gita::211.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen between action and renunciation. Krishna explains that true renunciation is not escape, but inner mastery: a person who has purified the mind, controlled the senses, and sees one self in all beings can act without being bound.
bhagwad_gita::211.modern_relevance: You answer the message, attend the meeting, and still feel the pull to perform, impress, or defend yourself. This verse says the work can happen without the inner stain of grasping.
bhagwad_gita::211.insight: It shifts action from self-protection to clear participation, so work happens without leaving a residue of clinging.

bhagwad_gita::212.verse_sanskrit: नैव किंचित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित् । पश्यन् श्रृणवन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपन् श्वसन् ॥
bhagwad_gita::212.verse_hindi: तत्त्वको जाननेवाला सांख्ययोगी देखता, सुनता, छूता, सूँघता, खाता, चलता, ग्रहण करता, बोलता, मलमूत्र का त्याग करता, सोता, श्वास लेता तथा आँखें खोलता और मूँदता भी सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियाँ इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंमें बरत रही हैं  ऐसा समझकर मैं स्वयं कुछ भी नहीं करता हूँ  ऐसा माने ॥
bhagwad_gita::212.english_translation: The knower of reality should think, "I do nothing at all," while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, taking, speaking, discarding, sleeping, breathing, and opening and closing the eyes.
bhagwad_gita::212.translation_literal: नैव (not at all) / किंचित् (anything) / करोमि (I do) / इति (thus) / युक्तः (the disciplined one) / मन्येत (should think) / तत्त्ववित् (the knower of reality) / पश्यन् (seeing) / श्रृणवन् (hearing) / स्पृशन् (touching) / जिघ्रन् (smelling) / अश्नन् (eating) / गच्छन् (walking) / स्वपन् (sleeping) / श्वसन् (breathing)
bhagwad_gita::212.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::212.essence: Seeing life happen is not the same as claiming it.
bhagwad_gita::212.simple_meaning: A person who knows reality sees the senses doing all the work and no longer claims personal doership.
bhagwad_gita::212.simple_insight: There is relief in stepping out of the pressure to own every action.
bhagwad_gita::212.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between action and collapse. Krishna is explaining the inner vision of the wise: even while the body sees, hears, eats, moves, and breathes, the true knower does not mistake these movements for personal doership.
bhagwad_gita::212.modern_relevance: You replay every word after a tense conversation and think, "I ruined it." This verse interrupts that habit: actions happen through the senses, but the self does not need to clutch them as "mine."
bhagwad_gita::212.insight: It shifts attention from personal ownership to clear witnessing of bodily and mental activity.

bhagwad_gita::213.verse_hindi: तत्त्वको जाननेवाला सांख्ययोगी देखता, सुनता, छूता, सूँघता, खाता, चलता, ग्रहण करता, बोलता, मलमूत्र का त्याग करता, सोता हुआ, श्वास लेता तथा आँखें खोलता और मूँदता हुआ भी सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियाँ इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंमें बरत रही हैं  ऐसा समझकर मैं स्वयं कुछ भी नहीं करता हूँ  ऐसा माने ॥
bhagwad_gita::213.english_translation: Even while speaking, releasing, taking, opening, and closing the eyes, the wise know: the senses move among their objects.
bhagwad_gita::213.translation_literal: प्रलपन् (speaking) / विसृजन् (releasing) / गृह्णन् (taking) / उन्मिषन् (opening the eyes) / निमिषन् (closing the eyes) / अपि (even) / इन्द्रियाणि (the senses) / इन्द्रियार्थेषु (among sense-objects) / वर्तन्ते (move) / इति (thus) / धारयन् (holding in mind)
bhagwad_gita::213.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::213.essence: Action happens; ownership is the illusion.
bhagwad_gita::213.simple_meaning: A person who knows the truth understands that actions are happening through the senses, not through a separate doer.
bhagwad_gita::213.simple_insight: You can stay unentangled even while life keeps moving through you.
bhagwad_gita::213.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna is teaching Arjuna how a wise person acts without inner bondage. After saying the self is not the doer, he adds that speaking, taking, blinking, and every bodily act belong to the senses moving among their objects.
bhagwad_gita::213.modern_relevance: Your phone lights up, your mouth answers, your hand reaches for the message. This verse asks you to notice the movement before you call it 'me.'
bhagwad_gita::213.insight: It shifts attention from personal ownership of action to clear witnessing of bodily processes.

bhagwad_gita::214.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः । लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥
bhagwad_gita::214.verse_hindi: जो भक्तियोगी सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंको भगवान् में अर्पण करके और आसक्तिका त्याग करके कर्म करता है, वह जलसे कमलके पत्तेकी तरह पापसे लिप्त नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::214.english_translation: One who offers actions to Brahman, renounces attachment, and acts is not stained by wrongdoing, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
bhagwad_gita::214.translation_literal: ब्रह्मणि (in Brahman) / आधाय (having placed) / कर्माणि (actions) / सङ्गम् (attachment) / त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) / करोति (does) / यः (who) / लिप्यते (is stained) / न (not) / सः (he) / पापेन (by wrongdoing) / पद्मपत्रम् (lotus leaf) / इव (like) / अम्भसा (by water)
bhagwad_gita::214.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::214.essence: Action without attachment leaves no stain.
bhagwad_gita::214.simple_meaning: Do your actions without clinging to them, and they do not bind you. Like a lotus leaf in water, you remain untouched.
bhagwad_gita::214.simple_insight: There is relief in acting fully without carrying the weight of ownership.
bhagwad_gita::214.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna explains that action itself is not the trap; attachment is. If work is offered beyond the ego, it leaves no stain.
bhagwad_gita::214.modern_relevance: You send the message, make the hard apology, or sign the document that changes everything. What matters is not whether the moment feels clean, but whether you acted without clinging to the result.
bhagwad_gita::214.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to clean action: do the work, release the grip, and let consequences unfold.

bhagwad_gita::215.verse_sanskrit: कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि । योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये ॥
bhagwad_gita::215.verse_hindi: कर्मयोगी आसक्तिका त्याग करके केवल ममतारहित इन्द्रियाँशरीरमनबुद्धि के द्वारा केवल अन्तःकरणकी शुद्धिके लिये ही कर्म करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::215.english_translation: Yogis perform action with body, mind, intellect, and the senses, giving up attachment, only for inner purification.
bhagwad_gita::215.translation_literal: कायेन (by the body) / मनसा (by the mind) / बुद्ध्या (by the intellect) / केवलैः (by the merely) / इन्द्रियैः (by the senses) / अपि (also) / योगिनः (yogis) / कर्म (action) / कुर्वन्ति (perform) / सङ्गम् (attachment) / त्यक्त्वा (having given up) / आत्मशुद्धये (for inner purification)
bhagwad_gita::215.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::215.essence: Action becomes cleansing when attachment is removed.
bhagwad_gita::215.simple_meaning: A true practitioner acts with the body, mind, intellect, and senses, but without clinging to results. The purpose is inner cleansing, not possession.
bhagwad_gita::215.simple_insight: You can do the work without being owned by it.
bhagwad_gita::215.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains how action can continue without bondage. The yogi uses body, mind, intellect, and senses, but drops attachment so the action itself becomes purification.
bhagwad_gita::215.modern_relevance: You send the difficult message, close the laptop, and still feel the knot in your stomach. The verse says the act can be clean even when the outcome is uncertain.
bhagwad_gita::215.insight: It shifts action from self-protection to purification, so effort becomes a practice instead of a grab for results.

bhagwad_gita::216.verse_sanskrit: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् । अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::216.verse_hindi: कर्मयोगी कर्मफलका त्याग करके नैष्ठिकी शान्तिको प्राप्त होता है ।  परन्तु सकाम मनुष्य कामनाके कारण फलमें आसक्त होकर बँध जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::216.english_translation: The disciplined one gives up the fruit of action and attains steady peace. The undisciplined one, clinging to results through desire, becomes bound.
bhagwad_gita::216.translation_literal: युक्तः (disciplined one) / कर्मफलम् (fruit of action) / त्यक्त्वा (having given up) / शान्तिम् (peace) / आप्नोति (attains) / नैष्ठिकीम् (steady, abiding) । / अयुक्तः (undisciplined one) / कामकारेण (through desire) / फले (in the fruit) / सक्तः (attached) / निबध्यते (is bound)
bhagwad_gita::216.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::216.essence: Peace comes when action is no longer chained to reward.
bhagwad_gita::216.simple_meaning: Letting go of results brings steady peace. Wanting a specific reward keeps you trapped.
bhagwad_gita::216.simple_insight: There is relief in doing your part without carrying the weight of the result.
bhagwad_gita::216.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen between duty and fear. Krishna explains that action itself does not bind; craving the reward does. The one who gives up attachment to results finds steady peace.
bhagwad_gita::216.modern_relevance: You send the message, then keep checking for the reply. The knot in your chest is not from the action — it is from needing a certain outcome.
bhagwad_gita::216.insight: Shift attention from getting to giving; that loosens the mind’s grip.

bhagwad_gita::217.verse_sanskrit: सर्वकर्माणि मनसा संन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी । नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन् ॥
bhagwad_gita::217.verse_hindi: जिसकी इन्द्रियाँ और मन वशमें हैं, ऐसा देहधारी पुरुष नौ द्वारोंवाले शरीररूपी पुरमें सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंका विवेकपूर्वक मनसे त्याग करके निःसन्देह न करता हुआ और न करवाता हुआ सुखपूर्वक अपने स्वरूपमें स्थित रहता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::217.english_translation: The embodied one, who has mastered the senses and mind, dwells happily in the city of nine gates, mentally renouncing all actions, neither doing nor causing action.
bhagwad_gita::217.translation_literal: सर्वकर्माणि (all actions) / मनसा (with the mind) / संन्यस्य (having renounced) / आस्ते (dwells) / सुखं (happily) / वशी (self-mastered) / नवद्वारे (with nine gates) / पुरे (in the city) / देही (the embodied one) / न (not) / एव (indeed) / कुर्वन् (doing) / न (not) / कारयन् (causing to do)
bhagwad_gita::217.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::217.essence: Freedom begins when action no longer feels personally owned.
bhagwad_gita::217.simple_meaning: A self-mastered person can live peacefully in the body while inwardly letting go of all action. Such a person does not feel like the doer or the one making others act.
bhagwad_gita::217.simple_insight: You can stay fully present in life without carrying the burden of authorship.
bhagwad_gita::217.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield, where action feels impossible and unavoidable at once. After teaching action without attachment, he now shows the deeper freedom: a disciplined person can live in the body, act outwardly, and yet inwardly rest beyond doership.
bhagwad_gita::217.modern_relevance: You sent the message, made the call, and still feel responsible for every reaction. This verse reminds you that peace comes when you stop claiming ownership over everything that follows.
bhagwad_gita::217.insight: It shifts the mind from personal authorship to quiet participation in action.

bhagwad_gita::218.verse_sanskrit: न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः । न कर्मफलसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्तते ॥
bhagwad_gita::218.verse_hindi: परमेश्वर मनुष्योंके न कर्तापनकी, न कर्मोंकी और न कर्मफलके साथ संयोगकी रचना करते हैं किन्तु स्वभाव ही बरत रहा है ॥
bhagwad_gita::218.english_translation: The supreme being creates neither doership nor actions nor the link between action and result for people. Nature alone keeps moving.
bhagwad_gita::218.translation_literal: न (not) / कर्तृत्वं (doership) / न (not) / कर्माणि (actions) / लोकस्य (of the world / for people) / सृजति (creates) / प्रभुः (the supreme being) / न (not) / कर्मफलसंयोगं (connection with action-result) / स्वभावः (nature) / तु (but) / प्रवर्तते (moves onward / operates)
bhagwad_gita::218.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::218.essence: What looks like personal control is nature moving through form.
bhagwad_gita::218.simple_meaning: The supreme being does not manufacture a separate doer, the actions, or the binding link between action and result. What actually operates is nature.
bhagwad_gita::218.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that the ego is not the center of everything.
bhagwad_gita::218.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen, unable to act without guilt. Krishna goes deeper than duty and explains that the sense of personal doership is not the ultimate reality. Actions unfold through nature, not through a separate self.
bhagwad_gita::218.modern_relevance: You replay a painful conversation at 2 a.m. and blame yourself for everything. This verse cuts through that loop: the ego claims ownership, but many forces move through a person.
bhagwad_gita::218.insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame to clear seeing of how action actually happens.

bhagwad_gita::219.verse_sanskrit: नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः । अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः ॥
bhagwad_gita::219.verse_hindi: सर्वव्यापी परमात्मा न किसीके पापकर्मको और न शुभकर्मको ही ग्रहण करता है किन्तु अज्ञानसे ज्ञान ढका हुआ है, उसीसे सब जीव मोहित हो रहे हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::219.english_translation: The all-pervading one takes neither anyone's wrongdoing nor anyone's good deed. Knowledge is covered by ignorance, and that is why living beings are deluded.
bhagwad_gita::219.translation_literal: नादत्ते (does not take) / कस्यचित् (of anyone) / पापम् (wrongdoing) / न (not) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / सुकृतम् (good deed) / विभुः (the all-pervading one) / अज्ञानेन (by ignorance) / आवृतम् (covered) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / तेन (by that) / मुह्यन्ति (are deluded) / जन्तवः (living beings)
bhagwad_gita::219.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::219.essence: Ignorance, not action, is what keeps beings confused.
bhagwad_gita::219.simple_meaning: The divine does not collect anyone's good or bad actions. People get confused because ignorance covers their understanding.
bhagwad_gita::219.simple_insight: You are not trapped by what you did, but by what you fail to see.
bhagwad_gita::219.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield, where duty feels impossible and every choice seems stained. He shifts the focus from action itself to the ignorance that distorts understanding, showing why people stay confused about responsibility.
bhagwad_gita::219.modern_relevance: You replay one mistake at 2 a.m. and treat it like your identity. This verse cuts deeper: the real problem is not the act alone, but the ignorance that keeps repeating it.
bhagwad_gita::219.insight: It shifts attention from moral bookkeeping to clear seeing. When ignorance lifts, the mind stops being ruled by confusion.

bhagwad_gita::220.verse_sanskrit: ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः । तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::220.verse_hindi: परन्तु जिन्होंने अपने जिस ज्ञानविवक के द्वारा उस अज्ञानका नाश कर दिया है, उनका वह ज्ञान सूर्यकी तरह परमतत्त्व परमात्माको प्रकाशित कर देता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::220.english_translation: But for those whose ignorance has been destroyed by knowledge of the true self, that knowledge reveals the supreme reality like the sun.
bhagwad_gita::220.translation_literal: ज्ञानेन (by knowledge) / तु (but) / तत्-अज्ञानम् (that ignorance) / येषाम् (of those whose) / नाशितम् (destroyed) / आत्मनः (of the true self) / तेषाम् (for them) / आदित्य-वत् (like the sun) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / प्रकाशयति (reveals) / तत्-परम् (the supreme reality)
bhagwad_gita::220.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::220.essence: Clear seeing does not create reality; it uncovers what was always there.
bhagwad_gita::220.simple_meaning: When ignorance is removed by true understanding, that understanding itself reveals the highest reality, just as the sun reveals everything in daylight.
bhagwad_gita::220.simple_insight: Clarity is not added from outside; once confusion falls away, what is real becomes obvious.
bhagwad_gita::220.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains why people act blindly. Here Krishna says that when a person’s ignorance is destroyed by insight, the highest reality becomes visible at once, like sunlight after darkness.
bhagwad_gita::220.modern_relevance: You reread the same message ten times, then suddenly understand the room was never the problem. The facts were there; confusion was filtering them. Clear seeing changes everything.
bhagwad_gita::220.insight: It shifts the mind from collecting more data to removing the confusion that hides what is already true.

bhagwad_gita::221.verse_hindi: जिनकी बुद्धि तदाकार हो रही है, जिनका मन तदाकार हो रहा है, जिनकी स्थिति परमात्मतत्वमें है, ऐसे परमात्मपरायण साधक ज्ञानके द्वारा पापरहित होकर अपुनरावृत्ति परमगति को प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::221.english_translation: Those whose intellect is fixed in That, whose mind is That, who are established in That, and who are devoted to That, go to the state of no return, their impurities washed away by knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::221.translation_literal: तद्बुद्धयः (whose intellect is That) / तदात्मानः (whose mind is That) / तन्निष्ठाः (steadfast in That) / तत्परायणाः (devoted to That as the supreme goal) / गच्छन्ति (they go) / अपुनरावृत्तिम् (to no return) / ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः (their impurities washed away by knowledge)
bhagwad_gita::221.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::221.essence: Complete alignment with the supreme reality ends the cycle of return.
bhagwad_gita::221.simple_meaning: When a person's mind, intellect, and whole focus are fully aligned with the supreme reality, knowledge clears away impurity and they reach a state beyond coming back.
bhagwad_gita::221.simple_insight: There is relief in total alignment: the mind stops scattering, and the deepest burden finally drops away.
bhagwad_gita::221.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains the path beyond action and error. After saying knowledge burns away ignorance, Krishna adds that the fully aligned seeker reaches a state beyond return.
bhagwad_gita::221.modern_relevance: You sit in the car after the hardest conversation of your life, hands still shaking. Something in you has already chosen, and the old version of you cannot drive home with you.
bhagwad_gita::221.insight: It shifts the goal from partial improvement to complete inward alignment with what is real.

bhagwad_gita::222.verse_sanskrit: विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि । शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::222.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी महापुरुष विद्याविनययुक्त ब्राह्मणमें और चाण्डालमें तथा गाय, हाथी एवं कुत्तेमें भी समरूप परमात्माको देखनेवाले होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::222.english_translation: The wise see the same reality in a learned, humble brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and an outcaste.
bhagwad_gita::222.translation_literal: विद्याविनयसंपन्ने (endowed with learning and humility) / ब्राह्मणे (in a brahmin) / गवि (in a cow) / हस्तिनि (in an elephant) / शुनि (in a dog) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / श्वपाके (in an outcaste) / च (and) / पण्डिताः (the wise) / समदर्शिनः (equal-seeing)
bhagwad_gita::222.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::222.essence: Real wisdom erases rank and reveals sameness.
bhagwad_gita::222.simple_meaning: A truly wise person does not rank living beings by status, species, or social position. The same reality is seen in all of them.
bhagwad_gita::222.simple_insight: Respect becomes effortless when you stop sorting beings into higher and lower.
bhagwad_gita::222.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna is still answering Arjuna's collapse. After teaching the clear vision of the true self, he shows what that vision looks like in daily perception: a wise person sees the same reality in a learned brahmin, an animal, and someone society rejects.
bhagwad_gita::222.modern_relevance: You walk past a hospital corridor, a luxury lobby, and a street corner in the same hour. The outer labels change fast; this verse asks whether your seeing changes at all.
bhagwad_gita::222.insight: It shifts the mind from status-based judgment to equal vision across all forms of life.

bhagwad_gita::223.verse_sanskrit: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः । निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::223.verse_hindi: जिनका अन्तःकरण समतामें स्थित है, उन्होंने इस जीवितअवस्थामें ही सम्पूर्ण संसारको जीत लिया है ब्रह्म निर्दोष और सम है, इसलिये वे ब्रह्ममें ही स्थित हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::223.english_translation: Those whose mind rests in sameness conquer rebirth here itself. The supreme reality is flawless and equal, so they are established in it.
bhagwad_gita::223.translation_literal: इहैव (here itself) / तैः (by them) / जितः (conquered) / सर्गः (the created world / rebirth) / येषाम् (of whom) / साम्ये (in sameness) / स्थितम् (स्थित) / मनः (mind) / निर्दोषम् (flawless) / हि (indeed) / समम् (equal) / ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / तस्मात् (therefore) / ब्रह्मणि (in the supreme reality) / ते (they) / स्थिताः (established)
bhagwad_gita::223.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::223.essence: Sameness of mind is the real conquest; everything else is aftermath.
bhagwad_gita::223.simple_meaning: A mind that stays even and unshaken has already overcome the cycle of reactivity. Because the supreme reality is free of flaw and division, such a person is established in it.
bhagwad_gita::223.simple_insight: You can stop fighting reality and feel the quiet strength of being rooted beyond change.
bhagwad_gita::223.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna answers with a higher standard: the person whose mind rests in sameness has already conquered the cycle of rebirth while still alive. That steadiness is not escape; it is true establishment.
bhagwad_gita::223.modern_relevance: You read a painful message, feel the surge of anger, and want to fire back. The verse asks for a different victory: let the mind stay even first, and the situation stops owning you.
bhagwad_gita::223.insight: It shifts the goal from winning events to stabilizing the mind that meets them.

bhagwad_gita::224.verse_sanskrit: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् । स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥
bhagwad_gita::224.verse_hindi: जो प्रियको प्राप्त होकर हर्षित न हो और अप्रियको प्राप्त होकर उद्विग्न न हो, वह स्थिर बुद्धिवाला, मूढ़तारहित तथा ब्रह्मको जाननेवाला मनुष्य ब्रह्ममें स्थित है ॥
bhagwad_gita::224.english_translation: One who does not rejoice at the pleasant, and does not shrink from the unpleasant, is steady in understanding, free from delusion, and established in the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::224.translation_literal: न (not) / प्रहृष्येत् (should rejoice) / प्रियं (the pleasant) / प्राप्य (having obtained) / न (not) / उद्विजेत् (should be disturbed) / प्राप्य (having obtained) / च (and) / अप्रियम् (the unpleasant) / स्थिरबुद्धिः (steady in understanding) / असम्मूढः (undeluded) / ब्रह्मविद् (knower of the supreme reality) / ब्रह्मणि (in the supreme reality) / स्थितः (established)
bhagwad_gita::224.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::224.essence: Steadiness begins when pleasure and pain lose their power over you.
bhagwad_gita::224.simple_meaning: A person who stays calm in both good and bad situations has clear understanding and lives in the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::224.simple_insight: You do not have to be pushed around by every gain or loss.
bhagwad_gita::224.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna frozen between duty and grief, Krishna deepens his teaching on inner balance. He says the one who is not tossed by gain or loss, pleasure or pain, has clear understanding and stands firm in the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::224.modern_relevance: You open the message and see praise, then an hour later a harsh reply. If your mood rises and falls with every notification, this verse calls you back to center.
bhagwad_gita::224.insight: It trains the mind to stop using external events as the measure of your stability.

bhagwad_gita::225.verse_sanskrit: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम् । स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते ॥
bhagwad_gita::225.verse_hindi: बाह्यस्पर्शमें आसक्तिरहित अन्तःकरणवाला साधक आत्मामें जो सुख है, उसको प्राप्त होता है ।  फिर वह ब्रह्ममें अभिन्नभावसे स्थित मनुष्य अक्षय सुखका अनुभव करता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::225.english_translation: One who is not attached to outer contacts finds the joy within the true self. Unified with the supreme reality, that person enjoys unending happiness.
bhagwad_gita::225.translation_literal: बाह्यस्पर्शेषु (in outer contacts) / असक्त-आत्मा (one whose inner being is not attached) / विन्दति (finds) / आत्मनि (in the true self) / यत् (which) / सुखम् (happiness) / सः (that one) / ब्रह्म-योग-युक्त-आत्मा (one whose inner being is joined in union with the supreme reality) / सुखम् (happiness) / अक्षयम् (imperishable) / अश्नुते (enjoys, attains)
bhagwad_gita::225.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::225.essence: Freedom begins when outer contact stops controlling inner joy.
bhagwad_gita::225.simple_meaning: Real happiness is found by turning away from outside pleasures and resting in the true self. That inner joy does not wear out.
bhagwad_gita::225.simple_insight: Relief comes from knowing lasting contentment is not dependent on changing circumstances.
bhagwad_gita::225.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna teaches the way beyond restless desire. After describing steadiness and equanimity, Krishna says the one who is no longer hooked by outer contact discovers joy within and enters an unending peace.
bhagwad_gita::225.modern_relevance: You close the app, the room goes quiet, and the buzz is still there in your chest. No amount of scrolling, praise, or distraction reaches the place that actually needs rest.
bhagwad_gita::225.insight: It shifts attention from chasing stimulation to recognising a deeper source of contentment already present.

bhagwad_gita::226.verse_sanskrit: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते । आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः ॥
bhagwad_gita::226.verse_hindi: क्योंकि हे कुन्तीनन्दन  जो इन्द्रियों और विषयोंके संयोगसे पैदा होनेवाले भोग सुख हैं, वे आदिअन्तवाले और दुःखके ही कारण हैं ।  अतः विवेकशील मनुष्य उनमें रमण नहीं करता ॥
bhagwad_gita::226.english_translation: The pleasures born from contact with the senses are only sources of suffering. They have a beginning and an end, O Arjuna, and the wise do not delight in them.
bhagwad_gita::226.translation_literal: ये (these) / हि (indeed) / संस्पर्शजा (born from contact) / भोगाः (pleasures) / दुःखयोनयः (sources of suffering) / एव (only) / ते (they) । / आद्यन्तवन्तः (having beginning and end) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / न (not) / तेषु (in them) / रमते (delights) / बुधः (the wise person)
bhagwad_gita::226.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::226.essence: Passing pleasure loses its power when its ending is seen.
bhagwad_gita::226.simple_meaning: Pleasures that come from the senses do not last and often lead to suffering. A clear-minded person does not get absorbed in them.
bhagwad_gita::226.simple_insight: You can enjoy life without being pulled around by every passing pleasure.
bhagwad_gita::226.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before the war. Krishna continues teaching him how to see clearly: sense-based pleasures are temporary, and their sweetness hides the suffering they bring. A steady mind stops chasing them.
bhagwad_gita::226.modern_relevance: You open your phone for one quick check and lose twenty minutes, then feel worse. The pull was brief; the aftertaste was not. Clear seeing breaks that loop.
bhagwad_gita::226.insight: It shifts attention from chasing stimulation to seeing its cost before you reach for it.

bhagwad_gita::227.verse_sanskrit: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥
bhagwad_gita::227.verse_hindi: इस मनुष्यशरीरमें जो कोई मनुष्य शरीर छूटनेसे पहले ही कामक्रोधसे उत्पन्न होनेवाले वेगको सहन करनेमें समर्थ होता है, वह नर योगी है और वही सुखी है ॥
bhagwad_gita::227.english_translation: Whoever can withstand the surge of desire and anger here before the body falls, is a disciplined person and is truly happy.
bhagwad_gita::227.translation_literal: शक्नोति (is able) / इह एव (here itself) / यः (who) / सोढुम् (to endure) / प्राक्-शरीर-विमोक्षणात् (before the body’s release) / काम-क्रोध-उद्भवम् (born from desire and anger) / वेगम् (impulse/surge) / सः (that one) / युक्तः (disciplined, integrated) / सः (that one) / सुखी (happy) / नरः (person)
bhagwad_gita::227.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::227.essence: Master the surge before it masters you.
bhagwad_gita::227.simple_meaning: A person who can endure the rush of desire and anger before death is truly disciplined and truly happy.
bhagwad_gita::227.simple_insight: Real strength is not suppressing feeling, but not letting it drive your next move.
bhagwad_gita::227.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is being taught how to live without being ruled by inner storms. Krishna says the person who can bear the surge of desire and anger before death arrives has found real steadiness.
bhagwad_gita::227.modern_relevance: A sharp message lands in your inbox, and your chest tightens before you reply. The verse asks for that one breath of restraint where reaction is still optional.
bhagwad_gita::227.insight: It trains you to notice the impulse, hold it, and act from steadiness instead of heat.

bhagwad_gita::228.verse_sanskrit: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः । स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति ॥
