bhagwad_gita::228.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य केवल परमात्मामें सुखवाला है और केवल परमात्मामें रमण करनेवाला है तथा जो केवल परमात्मामें ज्ञानवाला है, वह ब्रह्ममें अपनी स्थितिका अनुभव करनेवाला सांख्ययोगी निर्वाण ब्रह्मको प्राप्त होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::228.english_translation: One who finds happiness within, delights within, and has inner light alone, becomes one with the supreme reality and reaches freedom in the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::228.translation_literal: यः (who) / अन्तःसुखः (one whose happiness is भीतर / within) / अन्तरारामः (one whose delight is within) / तथा (and) / अन्तर्ज्योतिः (inner light) / एव (alone) / यः (who) / सः (that one) / योगी (yogi) / ब्रह्मनिर्वाणम् (freedom in the supreme reality) / ब्रह्मभूतः (become the supreme reality) / अधिगच्छति (attains)
bhagwad_gita::228.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::228.essence: Inner fulfillment makes freedom possible right now.
bhagwad_gita::228.simple_meaning: Real freedom comes to the person who finds joy, delight, and clear awareness within, rather than depending on outside things.
bhagwad_gita::228.simple_insight: You can stop bargaining with the world when inner contentment becomes enough.
bhagwad_gita::228.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, as Arjuna is being taught how to act without being ruled by craving, Krishna describes the person who no longer depends on outer pleasures. Such a person rests in inner joy and reaches freedom in the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::228.modern_relevance: You close the app, silence the room, and still feel the pull to check one more message. This verse points to the rare relief of not needing the next hit of approval or distraction.
bhagwad_gita::228.insight: It shifts attention from chasing stimulation to resting in inner fullness.

bhagwad_gita::229.verse_sanskrit: लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः । छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::229.verse_hindi: जिनका शरीर मनबुद्धिइन्द्रियोंसहित वशमें है, जो सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके हितमें रत हैं, जिनके सम्पूर्ण संशय मिट गये हैं, जिनके सम्पूर्ण कल्मष दोष नष्ट हो गये हैं, वे विवेकी साधक निर्वाण ब्रह्मको प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::229.english_translation: Sages who are free of impurity, free of doubt, self-controlled, and devoted to the welfare of all beings attain freedom in the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::229.translation_literal: लभन्ते (attain) / ब्रह्मनिर्वाणम् (freedom in the supreme reality) / ऋषयः (sages) / क्षीणकल्मषाः (whose impurities are diminished) / छिन्नद्वैधाः (whose doubts are cut away) / यतात्मानः (self-controlled) / सर्वभूतहिते (in the welfare of all beings) / रताः (delighting, devoted)
bhagwad_gita::229.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::229.essence: Freedom arrives when doubt ends and life turns toward all beings.
bhagwad_gita::229.simple_meaning: People who have cleansed themselves, ended doubt, controlled their minds and senses, and care for the good of all beings reach freedom in the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::229.simple_insight: Inner freedom feels possible when self-control and care for others become one practice.
bhagwad_gita::229.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra, where the warrior has collapsed under doubt. After describing the calm, inwardly rooted sage, he adds the outward sign: such a person lives for the welfare of all beings and reaches freedom in the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::229.modern_relevance: You’re standing outside a hospital room after a hard diagnosis, holding back panic so you can help your family. Clear action begins when doubt settles and concern widens beyond yourself.
bhagwad_gita::229.insight: It shifts the goal from private purity to a life that benefits every being.

bhagwad_gita::230.verse_sanskrit: कामक्रोधवियुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाम् । अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::230.verse_hindi: कामक्रोधसे सर्वथा रहित, जीते हुए मनवाले और स्वरूपका साक्षात्कार किये हुए सांख्ययोगियोंके लिये दोनों ओरसेशरीरके रहते हुए अथवा शरीर छूटनेके बाद निर्वाण ब्रह्म परिपूर्ण है ॥
bhagwad_gita::230.english_translation: For those free from desire and anger, with disciplined minds and self-knowledge, freedom in the supreme reality is near on both sides.
bhagwad_gita::230.translation_literal: काम-क्रोध-वियुक्तानाम् (for those free from desire and anger) / यतीनाम् (for disciplined renouncers) / यत-चेतसाम् (for those with controlled minds) / अभितः (on both sides) / ब्रह्म-निर्वाणम् (freedom in the supreme reality) / वर्तते (is present) / विदित-आत्मनाम् (for those who know the true self)
bhagwad_gita::230.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::230.essence: Freedom comes when desire and anger no longer govern the mind.
bhagwad_gita::230.simple_meaning: When desire and anger no longer control the mind, and a person knows the true self, inner freedom is close whether alive or after death.
bhagwad_gita::230.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that freedom begins with inner mastery, not with changing the world.
bhagwad_gita::230.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna explains the state of one who has gone beyond craving and rage. This verse continues the teaching on inner release: the person who knows the true self can rest in freedom even before the body falls.
bhagwad_gita::230.modern_relevance: You read the message that set you off, and the reply is already forming. This verse asks you to notice the heat before it becomes action, because freedom starts there.
bhagwad_gita::230.insight: It shifts attention from managing events to mastering the reactions that bind them.

bhagwad_gita::231.verse_sanskrit: स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यांश्चक्षुश्चैवान्तरे भ्रुवोः । प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ ॥
bhagwad_gita::231.verse_hindi: बाह्य पदार्थोंको बाहर ही छोड़कर और नेत्रोंकी दृष्टिको भौंहोंके बीचमें स्थित करके तथा नासिकामें विचरनेवाले प्राण और अपान वायुको सम करके जिसकी इन्द्रियाँ, मन और बुद्धि अपने वशमें हैं, जो मोक्षपरायण है तथा जो इच्छा, भय और क्रोधसे सर्वथा रहित है, वह मुनि सदा मुक्त ही है ॥
bhagwad_gita::231.english_translation: Leaving outer objects outside, fixing the gaze between the eyebrows, and balancing the inward and outward breaths moving through the nose.
bhagwad_gita::231.translation_literal: स्पर्शान् (outer contacts) / कृत्वा (having made) / बहिः (outside) / बाह्यान् (outer) / चक्षुः (the eyes) / च एव (and indeed) / अन्तरे (between) / भ्रुवोः (the eyebrows) / प्राणापानौ (the inward and outward breaths) / समौ (equal) / कृत्वा (having made) / नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ (moving within the nose)
bhagwad_gita::231.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::231.essence: Outer restraint and balanced breath prepare the mind for freedom.
bhagwad_gita::231.simple_meaning: Withdraw the senses from outer objects, steady the gaze, and balance the breath. This prepares the mind for deep inward focus.
bhagwad_gita::231.simple_insight: Stillness begins with deliberate restraint, not with forcing the mind to obey.
bhagwad_gita::231.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is being taught how to recover inner mastery. After describing the liberated one, Krishna gives the practical method: withdraw the senses, steady the eyes, and regulate the breath. It is a supporting step in a larger discipline.
bhagwad_gita::231.modern_relevance: You sit in the car before walking into a room where one conversation could change everything. Before the door opens, you breathe, settle your eyes, and stop feeding the noise.
bhagwad_gita::231.insight: It shifts attention from outer stimulation to bodily regulation, creating the conditions for a steadier mind.

bhagwad_gita::232.verse_sanskrit: यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः । विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः ॥
bhagwad_gita::232.verse_hindi: बाह्य पदार्थोंको बाहर ही छोड़कर और नेत्रोंकी दृष्टिको भौंहोंके बीचमें स्थित करके तथा नासिकामें विचरनेवाले प्राण और अपान वायुको सम करके जिसकी इन्द्रियाँ, मन और बुद्धि अपने वशमें हैं, जो मोक्षपरायण है तथा जो इच्छा, भय और क्रोधसे सर्वथा रहित है, वह मुनि सदा मुक्त ही है ॥
bhagwad_gita::232.english_translation: One who has controlled the senses, mind, and intellect, who seeks freedom as the highest aim, and who is free from desire, fear, and anger is forever free.
bhagwad_gita::232.translation_literal: यतेन्द्रियमनःबुद्धिः (with senses, mind, and intellect controlled) / मुनिः (the sage) / मोक्षपरायणः (having freedom as the highest aim) / विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधः (free from desire, fear, and anger) / यः (who) / सदा (always) / मुक्तः (free) / एव (indeed) / सः (that one)
bhagwad_gita::232.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::232.essence: Freedom begins where desire, fear, and anger lose authority.
bhagwad_gita::232.simple_meaning: A person who has mastered the senses, mind, and intellect, and has let go of desire, fear, and anger, lives in freedom already.
bhagwad_gita::232.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that freedom is not far away; it begins the moment inner agitation loosens its grip.
bhagwad_gita::232.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still trapped in confusion while Krishna keeps pointing toward inner release. After describing disciplined meditation, Krishna says the person who has mastered the senses, mind, and intellect is already free, even before the body falls.
bhagwad_gita::232.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that could end a relationship, and your chest is tight with fear. This verse points to the steadiness that lets you act without being ruled by panic.
bhagwad_gita::232.insight: It shifts attention from outer circumstances to inner mastery as the sign of freedom.

bhagwad_gita::233.verse_sanskrit: भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् । सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति ॥
bhagwad_gita::233.verse_hindi: भक्त मुझे सब यज्ञों और तपोंका भोक्ता, सम्पूर्ण लोकोंका महान् ईश्वर तथा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंका सुहृद् स्वार्थरहित दयालु और प्रेमी जानकर शान्तिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::233.english_translation: Knowing me as the enjoyer of all sacrifice and austerity, the great lord of all worlds, and the friend of all beings, one attains peace.
bhagwad_gita::233.translation_literal: भोक्तारम् (enjoyer) / यज्ञ-तपसाम् (of sacrifices and austerities) / सर्व-लोक-महेश्वरम् (great lord of all worlds) / सुहृदम् (friend) / सर्व-भूतानाम् (of all beings) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / माम् (me) / शान्तिम् (peace) / ऋच्छति (attains)
bhagwad_gita::233.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::233.essence: Peace comes from knowing the divine receives all effort and cares for all beings.
bhagwad_gita::233.simple_meaning: Peace comes from knowing Krishna as the true receiver of sacrifice and effort, the ruler of all worlds, and the friend of every being.
bhagwad_gita::233.simple_insight: You can stop bracing yourself when the deepest reality is friendly.
bhagwad_gita::233.detailed_meaning: After teaching renunciation through action, Krishna ends this chapter on Kurukshetra with a final reassurance. Arjuna stands between war and collapse, and Krishna says that peace comes when he knows who receives all offering, governs all worlds, and cares for every being.
bhagwad_gita::233.modern_relevance: You finish the hard conversation, heart racing, and still wonder whether it meant anything. This verse says peace comes when you trust that your effort was received by something larger and kinder.
bhagwad_gita::233.insight: It shifts effort from anxious self-ownership to trust in a benevolent order.

bhagwad_gita::234.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचअनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः । स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥
bhagwad_gita::234.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  कर्मफलका आश्रय न लेकर जो कर्तव्यकर्म करता है, वही संन्यासी तथा योगी है और केवल अग्निका त्याग करनेवाला संन्यासी नहीं होता तथा केवल क्रियाओंका त्याग करनेवाला योगी नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::234.english_translation: One who performs the required action without taking shelter in the fruit of action is a renunciate and a yogi. Not one who merely gives up fire, and not one who merely stops acting.
bhagwad_gita::234.translation_literal: श्रीभगवानुवाच (the divine said) / अनाश्रितः (not taking refuge) / कर्मफलम् (fruit of action) / कार्यम् (what must be done) / कर्म (action) / करोति (does) / यः (who) / सः (that one) / संन्यासी (renunciate) / च (and) / योगी (yogi) / च (and) / न (not) / निरग्निः (without fire) / न (not) / च (and) / अक्रियः (one without action)
bhagwad_gita::234.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::234.essence: Renunciation means acting without needing to own the result.
bhagwad_gita::234.simple_meaning: Real renunciation is not escaping action. It is doing what must be done without clinging to the result.
bhagwad_gita::234.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that sincerity matters more than control.
bhagwad_gita::234.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Arjuna is frozen before battle. Krishna begins by redefining renunciation: not as abandoning action, but as acting without dependence on results. This verse sets the tone for the whole teaching on self-mastery.
bhagwad_gita::234.modern_relevance: You send the message, make the hard call, or finish the task late at night. The cleanest act is the one you can stand behind even if nobody rewards it.
bhagwad_gita::234.insight: It shifts attention from outcome-hunting to clean, necessary action.

bhagwad_gita::235.verse_sanskrit: यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव । न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन ॥
bhagwad_gita::235.verse_hindi: हे अर्जुन  लोग जिसको संन्यास कहते हैं, उसीको तुम योग समझो क्योंकि संकल्पोंका त्याग किये बिना मनुष्य कोईसा भी योगी नहीं हो सकता ॥
bhagwad_gita::235.english_translation: Arjuna, what people call renunciation is yoga. No one becomes a yogi without giving up intentions.
bhagwad_gita::235.translation_literal: यं (what) / संन्यासम् (renunciation) / इति (thus) / प्राहुः (they call) / योगम् (yoga) / तम् (that) / विद्धि (know) / पाण्डव (Arjuna) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / असंन्यस्त (not given up) / सङ्कल्पः (intention) / योगी (yogi) / भवति (becomes) / कश्चन (anyone)
bhagwad_gita::235.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::235.essence: Yoga begins when the mind stops clutching its own agenda.
bhagwad_gita::235.simple_meaning: Real renunciation is not outer withdrawal. It is letting go of inner plans and fixed desires so the mind can truly enter yoga.
bhagwad_gita::235.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that inner freedom matters more than outward form.
bhagwad_gita::235.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen while two armies wait. Krishna clarifies that true renunciation is not merely leaving action behind; it is dropping mental intentions. Without that inner release, no one can truly live yoga.
bhagwad_gita::235.modern_relevance: You close the laptop, but your mind keeps rehearsing the outcome of the conversation. The real letting go is not in your hands or schedule — it is in the plans you keep gripping.
bhagwad_gita::235.insight: It shifts practice from external gestures to the inner release of wanting and planning.

bhagwad_gita::236.verse_sanskrit: आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते । योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::236.verse_hindi: जो योगसमता में आरूढ़ होना चाहता है, ऐसे मननशील योगीके लिये कर्तव्यकर्म करना कारण कहा गया है और उसी योगारूढ़ मनुष्यका शम शान्ति परमात्मप्राप्तिमें कारण कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::236.english_translation: For the sage who seeks to rise into yoga, action is the means. For the one who has risen in yoga, stillness is the means.
bhagwad_gita::236.translation_literal: आरुरुक्षोः (of one seeking to ascend) / मुनेः (of the sage) / योगम् (to yoga) / कर्म (action) / कारणम् (means/cause) / उच्यते (is said) / योगारूढस्य (of one established in yoga) / तस्य (of that one) / एव (indeed) / शमः (stillness) / कारणम् (means/cause) / उच्यते (is said)
bhagwad_gita::236.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::236.essence: You reach steadiness through action, then preserve it through stillness.
bhagwad_gita::236.simple_meaning: Action helps a seeker rise into yoga. Once that steadiness is reached, calm stillness becomes the support.
bhagwad_gita::236.simple_insight: Progress is not forced by pressure alone; there is a time for effort and a time for quiet.
bhagwad_gita::236.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna begins mapping the path back to steadiness. He explains that a seeker first uses right action to climb toward inner discipline, and then uses calm stillness to remain established there.
bhagwad_gita::236.modern_relevance: You are learning to meditate, but your mind keeps darting to messages, chores, and unfinished conversations. First you need disciplined practice; later, the deeper work is learning to stay quiet without effort.
bhagwad_gita::236.insight: It shifts the mind from forcing stillness to building the conditions for it.

bhagwad_gita::237.verse_sanskrit: यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते । सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::237.verse_hindi: जिस समय न इन्द्रियोंके भोगोंमें तथा न कर्मोंमें ही आसक्त होता है, उस समय वह सम्पूर्ण संकल्पोंका त्यागी मनुष्य योगारूढ़ कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::237.english_translation: When one no longer clings to sense pleasures or to actions, that person is called established in yoga, having renounced all intentions.
bhagwad_gita::237.translation_literal: यदा (when) हि (indeed) न (not) इन्द्रियार्थेषु (in sense objects) न (not) कर्मसु (in actions) अनुषज्जते (clings) / सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी (renouncer of all intentions) / योगारूढः (established in yoga) तदा (then) उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::237.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::237.essence: Yoga begins when neither pleasure nor action can hook you.
bhagwad_gita::237.simple_meaning: A person is truly steady in yoga when neither pleasures nor actions hook the mind, and all intentions have been let go.
bhagwad_gita::237.simple_insight: There is relief in not being owned by wanting or doing.
bhagwad_gita::237.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna is teaching him how to become inwardly steady. After saying that practice leads toward stillness, Krishna now names the state: a person who no longer clings to pleasures or actions is established in yoga.
bhagwad_gita::237.modern_relevance: You finish the presentation, then keep refreshing the email thread for praise. Or you stop chasing the praise and feel your shoulders drop. This verse names that release.
bhagwad_gita::237.insight: It shifts attention from achievement and stimulation to non-clinging presence.

bhagwad_gita::238.verse_sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::238.verse_hindi: अपने द्वारा अपना उद्धार करे, अपना पतन न करे क्योंकि आप ही अपना मित्र है और आप ही अपना शत्रु है ॥
bhagwad_gita::238.english_translation: Lift yourself by yourself; do not let yourself fall. The true self is its own friend, and the true self is its own enemy.
bhagwad_gita::238.translation_literal: उद्धरेत् (should lift up) / आत्मना (by the self) / आत्मानम् (the self) / न (not) / आत्मानम् (the self) / अवसादयेत् (should let fall) / आत्मा (the self) / एव (indeed) / हि (for) / आत्मनः (of the self) / बन्धुः (friend) / आत्मा (the self) / एव (indeed) / रिपुः (enemy) / आत्मनः (of the self)
bhagwad_gita::238.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::238.essence: Your own inner handling makes you rise or collapse.
bhagwad_gita::238.simple_meaning: Your own effort can raise you or ruin you. The same mind that helps you grow can also drag you down.
bhagwad_gita::238.simple_insight: You are not helpless in your own life; the way you handle yourself changes everything.
bhagwad_gita::238.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen. Krishna begins to show him that the greatest struggle is not outside, but within. Before victory or defeat in war, a person must learn whether the self supports or sabotages itself.
bhagwad_gita::238.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, quit the habit, or tell the truth—and the old voice says to delay again. In that moment, your own inner handling decides whether you rise or shrink.
bhagwad_gita::238.insight: It shifts responsibility inward: stop waiting for rescue and start becoming the force that steadies you.

bhagwad_gita::239.verse_sanskrit: बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः । अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::239.verse_hindi: जिसने अपनेआपसे अपनेआपको जीत लिया है, उसके लिये आप ही अपना बन्धु है और जिसने अपनेआपको नहीं जीता है, ऐसे अनात्माका आत्मा ही शत्रुतामें शत्रुकी तरह बर्ताव करता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::239.english_translation: For one who has conquered the lower self by the true self, the true self is a friend. For one who has not conquered the lower self, the true self behaves like an enemy.
bhagwad_gita::239.translation_literal: बन्धुः (friend) / आत्मा (the true self) / आत्मनः (of the self) / तस्य (of that one) / येन (by whom) / आत्मा (the true self) / एव (indeed) / आत्मना (by the true self) / जितः (conquered) / अनात्मनः (of one not mastered) / तु (but) / शत्रुत्वे (in hostility) / वर्तेत (acts) / आत्मा (the true self) / एव (indeed) / शत्रुवत् (like an enemy)
bhagwad_gita::239.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::239.essence: The same inner nature that frees you can also fight you.
bhagwad_gita::239.simple_meaning: When you master your restless impulses, your deepest nature supports you. If you do not, your own mind and habits work against you.
bhagwad_gita::239.simple_insight: Self-mastery feels like relief because the part of you that fought you starts helping.
bhagwad_gita::239.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen, and Krishna keeps turning the lesson inward. After saying the self can be friend or enemy, Krishna now sharpens it: victory over the lower self changes everything. The real battle is inside.
bhagwad_gita::239.modern_relevance: You sit alone after sending the message you were afraid to send. If you acted from clarity, something in you steadies. If you acted from fear, the same mind turns harsh and restless.
bhagwad_gita::239.insight: It shifts the struggle from controlling the world to mastering the impulses that distort your own judgment.

bhagwad_gita::240.verse_sanskrit: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥
bhagwad_gita::240.verse_hindi: जिसने अपनेआपपर अपनी विजय कर ली है, उस शीतउष्ण अनुकूलताप्रतिकूलता सुखदुःख तथा मानअपमानमें निर्विकार मनुष्यको परमात्मा नित्यप्राप्त हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::240.english_translation: For one who has conquered the self and is serene, the supreme reality is ever present in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, honor and dishonor.
bhagwad_gita::240.translation_literal: जितात्मनः (of one who has conquered the self) / प्रशान्तस्य (of the serene) / परमात्मा (the supreme reality) / समाहितः (is present, absorbed) / शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु (in cold and heat, pleasure and pain) / तथा (and also) / मानापमानयोः (in honor and dishonor)
bhagwad_gita::240.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::240.essence: Steadiness makes the highest reality feel near in every opposite.
bhagwad_gita::240.simple_meaning: A person who has mastered the restless mind stays steady through comfort and discomfort, praise and insult. In that steadiness, the supreme reality is immediately present.
bhagwad_gita::240.simple_insight: You do not need life to become gentle before you can be at ease.
bhagwad_gita::240.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen, and Krishna keeps teaching the inner discipline needed to act rightly. After saying the self can be either friend or enemy, Krishna adds that the conquered, peaceful person remains unchanged through heat, cold, pleasure, pain, praise, and insult.
bhagwad_gita::240.modern_relevance: You get praised in the meeting, then criticized in the hallway, and your mood swings with both. This verse asks for a steadier center that no comment can shake.
bhagwad_gita::240.insight: It shifts attention from outer conditions to inner steadiness, showing that true presence is possible amid opposites.

bhagwad_gita::241.verse_sanskrit: ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः । युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::241.verse_hindi: जिसका अन्तःकरण ज्ञानविज्ञानसे तृप्त है, जो कूटकी तरह निर्विकार है, जितेन्द्रिय है और मिट्टीके ढेले, पत्थर तथा स्वर्णमें समबुद्धिवाला है  ऐसा योगी युक्त योगारूढ़ कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::241.english_translation: One whose mind is satisfied by knowledge and realization, who remains steady, who has conquered the senses, and who sees clay, stone, and gold alike is called a yogi in union.
bhagwad_gita::241.translation_literal: ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा (one whose inner being is satisfied by knowledge and realization) / कूटस्थः (steady like a mountain; unchanging) / विजितेन्द्रियः (one whose senses are conquered) / युक्तः (joined; in union) / इति (thus) / उच्यते (is called) / योगी (the yogi) / समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः (equal-minded toward clay, stone, and gold)
bhagwad_gita::241.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::241.essence: True mastery makes gold and dust feel identical.
bhagwad_gita::241.simple_meaning: A person who is fulfilled by clear understanding, steady in mind, and in control of the senses sees wealth and ordinary matter with the same calmness.
bhagwad_gita::241.simple_insight: Real freedom feels unshaken by what others call valuable.
bhagwad_gita::241.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still learning how to stand without being pulled by fear or desire. Krishna describes the yogi whose mind is full, senses mastered, and judgment even. Such a person no longer ranks the world by greed.
bhagwad_gita::241.modern_relevance: You open a message that could change your salary, your status, or your plans. The mind that has settled itself does not flinch at gain or loss; it stays even.
bhagwad_gita::241.insight: It shifts attention from chasing value to recognizing sameness beneath appearances.

bhagwad_gita::242.verse_hindi: सुहृद्, मित्र, वैरी, उदासीन, मध्यस्थ, द्वेष्य और सम्बन्धियोंमें तथा साधुआचरण करनेवालोंमें और पापआचरण करनेवालोंमें भी समबुद्धिवाला मनुष्य श्रेष्ठ है ॥
bhagwad_gita::242.english_translation: The one whose understanding is equal toward friend, enemy, neutral person, mediator, hateful person, relative, the virtuous, and the sinful is श्रेष्ठ.
bhagwad_gita::242.translation_literal: सुहृद् (well-wisher) / मित्र (friend) / अरि (enemy) / उदासीन (indifferent) / मध्यस्थ (mediator) / द्वेष्य (hateful) / बन्धुषु (among relatives) / साधुषु (among the virtuous) / अपि (also) / च (and) / पापेषु (among the sinful) / समबुद्धिः (equal understanding) / विशिष्यते (is श्रेष्ठ)
bhagwad_gita::242.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::242.essence: Equal vision toward all people marks the highest steadiness.
bhagwad_gita::242.simple_meaning: A calm, even-minded person does not get pulled by labels like friend, enemy, good, or bad. That balanced understanding is considered best.
bhagwad_gita::242.simple_insight: You stop being manipulated by preference and aversion, and that gives real inner freedom.
bhagwad_gita::242.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna keeps teaching Arjuna how a steady meditator sees the world. After describing mastery over the mind and senses, he says the highest balance is to look on all people without bias.
bhagwad_gita::242.modern_relevance: A group chat splits into camps and everyone wants your reaction. You feel the pull to defend one side and condemn the other. This verse asks for a steadier mind that does not get recruited by emotion.
bhagwad_gita::242.insight: It trains you to respond from clear seeing, not from liking and disliking.

bhagwad_gita::243.verse_sanskrit: योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः । एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः ॥
bhagwad_gita::243.verse_hindi: भोगबुद्धिसे संग्रह न करनेवाला, इच्छारहित और अन्तःकरण तथा शरीरको वशमें रखनेवाला योगी अकेला एकान्तमें स्थित होकर मनको निरन्तर परमात्मामें लगाये ॥
bhagwad_gita::243.english_translation: The disciplined yogi, dwelling alone in seclusion, should constantly unite the mind with the supreme being, free from desire and possessiveness, with body and mind under control.
bhagwad_gita::243.translation_literal: योगी (the yogi) / युञ्जीत (should unite) / सततम् (constantly) / आत्मानम् (the self/mind) / रहसि (in seclusion) / स्थितः (स्थित, established) / एकाकी (alone) / यतचित्तात्मा (one whose mind and inner being are restrained) / निराशीः (without desire) / अपरिग्रहः (without possessiveness)
bhagwad_gita::243.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::243.essence: Steady inward practice begins when desire and possessiveness end.
bhagwad_gita::243.simple_meaning: A yogi should sit alone, keep the mind steadily focused on the divine, and let go of desire and possessiveness.
bhagwad_gita::243.simple_insight: There is relief in not needing to grasp anything before you can be steady.
bhagwad_gita::243.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still teaching Arjuna on the battlefield, where fear and attachment have frozen action. After describing the settled yogi, he now gives the practice itself: withdraw, control the mind, and turn inward until desire and grasping fall away.
bhagwad_gita::243.modern_relevance: You close the bedroom door after a draining day, but your mind keeps reaching for messages, praise, and proof. This verse asks you to sit down, stop grasping, and return inward.
bhagwad_gita::243.insight: It shifts practice from chasing stimulation to steady inward attention.

bhagwad_gita::244.verse_sanskrit: शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः । नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::244.verse_hindi: शुद्ध भूमिपर, जिसपर क्रमशः कुश, मृगछाला और वस्त्र बिछे हैं, जो न अत्यन्त ऊँचा है और न अत्यन्त नीचा, ऐसे अपने आसनको स्थिरस्थापन करके ॥
bhagwad_gita::244.english_translation: Having placed a firm seat for himself on a clean spot, neither too high nor too low, with cloth, deerskin, and kusha grass laid in layers.
bhagwad_gita::244.translation_literal: शुचौ (on a clean) / देशे (place) / प्रतिष्ठाप्य (having placed) / स्थिरम् (firm) / आसनम् (seat) / आत्मनः (for oneself) / न (not) / अत्युच्छ्रितम् (too high) / न (not) / अति-नीचम् (too low) / चैल-आजिन-कुश-उत्तरम् (with cloth, deerskin, and kusha grass laid above)
bhagwad_gita::244.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::244.essence: A steady mind begins with a steady seat.
bhagwad_gita::244.simple_meaning: Choose a clean, steady seat that is neither too high nor too low, and prepare it with cloth, deerskin, and kusha grass.
bhagwad_gita::244.simple_insight: Inner training begins with a stable place. Even the body must be settled before the mind can quiet down.
bhagwad_gita::244.detailed_meaning: Krishna is teaching Arjuna how to meditate after the war has frozen in his heart. Before the mind can be gathered, the body needs a clean, steady seat in a quiet place. This verse prepares the ground for practice.
bhagwad_gita::244.modern_relevance: You sit on the edge of the bed after midnight, phone face down, trying to calm a racing mind. The first step is not insight — it is creating a steady place to begin.
bhagwad_gita::244.insight: It shifts attention from abstract intention to physical preparation, showing that practice starts by setting conditions well.

bhagwad_gita::245.verse_sanskrit: तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः । उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये ॥
bhagwad_gita::245.verse_hindi: उस आसनपर बैठकर चित्त और इन्द्रियोंकी क्रियाओंको वशमें रखते हुए मनको एकाग्र करके अन्तःकरणकी शुद्धिके लिये योगका अभ्यास करे ॥
bhagwad_gita::245.english_translation: Sitting on that seat, with the mind made one-pointed and the movements of mind and senses restrained, one should practice yoga for inner purification.
bhagwad_gita::245.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / एकाग्रम् (one-pointed) / मनः (mind) / कृत्वा (having made) / यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः (with mind-and-sense activity restrained) / उपविश्य (having sat down) / आसने (on the seat) / युञ्ज्यात् (should practice) / योगम् (yoga) / आत्मविशुद्धये (for inner purification)
bhagwad_gita::245.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::245.essence: Meditation begins by gathering the mind and training the senses.
bhagwad_gita::245.simple_meaning: Sit steadily, gather the mind, restrain the senses, and practice yoga to purify the inner state.
bhagwad_gita::245.simple_insight: Small discipline creates a cleaner mind than force ever could.
bhagwad_gita::245.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still teaching Arjuna how to meditate. After choosing a clean place and a steady seat, the next step is to gather the mind and restrain the senses. This verse turns preparation into practice, aiming at inner purification.
bhagwad_gita::245.modern_relevance: You sit down to meditate, but the phone buzzes, your body fidgets, and your thoughts scatter. The practice begins by gathering yourself before anything deeper can happen.
bhagwad_gita::245.insight: It shifts meditation from a vague wish into a disciplined act of collecting attention.

bhagwad_gita::246.verse_sanskrit: समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः । संप्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन् ॥
bhagwad_gita::246.verse_hindi: काया, शिर और ग्रीवाको सीधे अचल धारण करके तथा दिशाओंको न देखकर केवल अपनी नासिकाके अग्रभागको देखते हुए स्थिर होकर बैठे ॥
bhagwad_gita::246.english_translation: Holding the body, head, and neck straight and still, and gazing only at the tip of the nose without looking around.
bhagwad_gita::246.translation_literal: समम् (straight/even) / काय-शिरो-ग्रीवम् (body-head-neck) / धारयन् (holding) / अचलम् (motionless) / स्थिरः (steady) / संप्रेक्ष्य (gazing) / नासिका-अग्रम् (tip of the nose) / स्वम् (own) / दिशः (directions) / च (and) / अनवलोकयन् (not looking)
bhagwad_gita::246.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::246.essence: Steady posture is the first gate to a steady mind.
bhagwad_gita::246.simple_meaning: Sit with your body straight and still. Keep your gaze fixed and do not let the eyes wander.
bhagwad_gita::246.simple_insight: Stillness begins with the body. A steady posture helps the mind stop scattering.
bhagwad_gita::246.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is being taught how to meditate after the basic setup has been given. Krishna now moves from the seat and the breath of practice to the body's alignment, showing that inner training begins with disciplined stillness.
bhagwad_gita::246.modern_relevance: You sit down to breathe for five minutes, but your eyes keep jumping to the phone, the door, the clock. The practice starts when the body stops asking to escape.
bhagwad_gita::246.insight: It shifts meditation from a vague idea to a concrete bodily discipline.

bhagwad_gita::247.verse_sanskrit: प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः । मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः ॥
bhagwad_gita::247.verse_hindi: जिसका अन्तःकरण शान्त है, जो भयरहित है और जो ब्रह्मचारिव्रतमें स्थित है, ऐसा सावधान योगी मनका संयम करके मेरेमें चित्त लगाता हुआ मेरे परायण होकर बैठे ॥
bhagwad_gita::247.english_translation: The yogi, with a peaceful mind, free of fear, and firm in celibate discipline, restrains the mind, fixes awareness on Me, and sits devoted to Me as the supreme aim.
bhagwad_gita::247.translation_literal: प्रशान्तात्मा (one whose inner state is peaceful) / विगतभीः (free from fear) / ब्रह्मचारिव्रते (in the vow of celibacy) / स्थितः (established) / मनः (mind) / संयम्य (having restrained) / मच्चित्तः (with mind on Me) / युक्तः (yoked in yoga) / आसीत (should sit) / मत्परः (for whom I am the supreme aim)
bhagwad_gita::247.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::247.essence: A disciplined mind can rest in devotion without fear.
bhagwad_gita::247.simple_meaning: A steady yogi keeps the mind under control, stays free from fear, and turns awareness toward Krishna while sitting in disciplined practice.
bhagwad_gita::247.simple_insight: Inner steadiness makes devotion possible; fear and distraction fall away together.
bhagwad_gita::247.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna keeps guiding Arjuna through meditation. After teaching posture and concentration, he adds the inner conditions: calmness, fearlessness, restraint, and single-pointed devotion. This verse prepares the mind for the deeper peace named in the next one.
bhagwad_gita::247.modern_relevance: You sit alone before sending the message that could change a relationship. Your chest is tight, your thoughts are racing, and you choose calm restraint before you speak.
bhagwad_gita::247.insight: It shifts practice from technique alone to the inner conditions that make practice hold.

bhagwad_gita::248.verse_sanskrit: युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी नियतमानसः । शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति ॥
bhagwad_gita::248.verse_hindi: नियत मनवाला योगी मनको इस तरहसे सदा परमात्मामें लगाता हुआ मेरेमें सम्यक् स्थितिवाली जो निर्वाणपरमा शान्ति है, उसको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::248.english_translation: The disciplined yogi, always uniting the mind in this way, attains the supreme peace of freedom rooted in Me.
bhagwad_gita::248.translation_literal: युञ्जन् (uniting) / एवम् (thus) / सदा (always) / आत्मानम् (the inner self) / योगी (the yogi) / नियत-मानसः (with a disciplined mind) / शान्तिम् (peace) / निर्वाण-परमाम् (supreme freedom) / मत्-संस्थाम् (rooted in Me) / अधिगच्छति (attains)
bhagwad_gita::248.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::248.essence: A steady mind reaches the peace that restlessness can never touch.
bhagwad_gita::248.simple_meaning: A steady yogi keeps the mind gathered and focused, and reaches the highest peace rooted in the divine presence.
bhagwad_gita::248.simple_insight: Stillness is not found by escaping life, but by training the mind to rest in one place.
bhagwad_gita::248.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is being taught how to sit, breathe, and gather the mind without wavering. Krishna now names the result of that practice: a mind held steadily in yoga reaches the highest peace, the calm that ends inner disturbance.
bhagwad_gita::248.modern_relevance: You close the laptop after an argument and your mind keeps replaying every line. The body is still, but the mind keeps running. This verse points to the deeper quiet that comes only when attention is trained.
bhagwad_gita::248.insight: It shifts attention from chasing relief to building a mind that can actually hold peace.

bhagwad_gita::249.verse_sanskrit: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः । न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन ॥
bhagwad_gita::249.verse_hindi: हे अर्जुन  यह योग न तो अधिक खानेवालेका और न बिलकुल न खानेवालेका तथा न अधिक सोनेवालेका और न बिलकुल न सोनेवालेका ही सिद्ध होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::249.english_translation: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who eats nothing at all. It is not for one who sleeps too much, nor for one who stays awake too long, Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::249.translation_literal: न अति-अश्नतः (for one who eats too much) / तु (indeed) / योगः (yoga) / अस्ति (is) / न (not) / च (and) / एकान्तम् (entirely) / अनश्नतः (for one who does not eat) / न (not) / च (and) / अति-स्वप्न-शीलस्य (for one who sleeps too much) / जाग्रतः (for one who stays awake) / न (not) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / अर्जुन (Arjuna)
bhagwad_gita::249.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::249.essence: Balance makes meditation possible; extremes break it.
bhagwad_gita::249.simple_meaning: Meditation does not work with extremes. Too much food, no food, too much sleep, or no sleep all disturb the practice.
bhagwad_gita::249.simple_insight: Steady practice needs a steady body and a steady routine.
bhagwad_gita::249.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is being taught how to train the mind for meditation. Krishna says the practice fails if life swings into extremes of indulgence or deprivation, because the body and mind must be kept in balance.
bhagwad_gita::249.modern_relevance: You skip meals, then overeat at night. You sleep badly, then try to meditate anyway. The mind cannot settle when the body is being pushed into extremes.
bhagwad_gita::249.insight: It shifts discipline from heroic intensity to balanced repetition.

bhagwad_gita::250.verse_sanskrit: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु । युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥
bhagwad_gita::250.verse_hindi: दुःखोंका नाश करनेवाला योग तो यथायोग्य आहार और विहार करनेवालेका, कर्मोंमें यथायोग्य चेष्टा करनेवालेका तथा यथायोग्य सोने और जागनेवालेका ही सिद्ध होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::250.english_translation: Yoga that destroys suffering comes from balanced eating, balanced activity, balanced work, and balanced sleep and waking.
bhagwad_gita::250.translation_literal: युक्ताहारविहारस्य (of one with balanced eating and movement) / युक्तचेष्टस्य (of one with balanced effort) / कर्मसु (in actions) / युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य (of one with balanced sleep and waking) / योगः (yoga) / भवति (becomes) / दुःखहा (destroyer of suffering)
bhagwad_gita::250.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::250.essence: Balanced living makes inner practice possible.
bhagwad_gita::250.simple_meaning: A steady practice works when daily life is balanced: eating, moving, working, sleeping, and waking all in proper measure.
bhagwad_gita::250.simple_insight: Inner steadiness starts with ordinary habits, not with forcing the mind.
bhagwad_gita::250.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still teaching Arjuna how to steady himself after the battlefield collapse. He says meditation will not hold if the body and daily routine are extreme. The practice becomes possible only when life itself is kept in balance.
bhagwad_gita::250.modern_relevance: You skip meals, scroll past midnight, then wonder why your mind feels broken during the hard conversation at 9 a.m. Balance in the body gives the mind a place to stand.
bhagwad_gita::250.insight: It shifts discipline from heroic intensity to sustainable rhythm.

bhagwad_gita::251.verse_sanskrit: यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते । निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा ॥
bhagwad_gita::251.verse_hindi: वशमें किया हुआ चित्त जिस कालमें अपने स्वरूपमें ही स्थित हो जाता है और स्वयं सम्पूर्ण पदार्थोंसे निःस्पृह हो जाता है, उस कालमें वह योगी है  ऐसा कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::251.english_translation: When the controlled mind rests in the true self alone and is free from craving for all pleasures, that person is called united in yoga.
bhagwad_gita::251.translation_literal: यदा (when) / विनियतं (well-controlled) / चित्तम् (mind) / आत्मनि (in the true self) / एव (alone) / अवतिष्ठते (rests) / निःस्पृहः (free from craving) / सर्वकामेभ्यः (from all desires) / युक्तः (united, disciplined) / इति (thus) / उच्यते (is called) / तदा (then)
bhagwad_gita::251.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::251.essence: Yoga begins when craving loses its grip and the mind comes home.
bhagwad_gita::251.simple_meaning: A person is truly steady in yoga when the mind settles into the true self and no longer chases every desire.
bhagwad_gita::251.simple_insight: There is relief in not needing every craving to be answered.
bhagwad_gita::251.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna is teaching the method of inner mastery. After describing balanced habits, Krishna names the real sign of yoga: a mind that has come home to the true self and no longer runs after desire.
bhagwad_gita::251.modern_relevance: You finally close the laptop after midnight, but your mind keeps reaching for one more reply, one more check, one more fix. Peace begins when the chasing stops.
bhagwad_gita::251.insight: It shifts attention from managing impulses to recognizing the mind’s settled state.

bhagwad_gita::252.verse_sanskrit: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता । योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::252.verse_hindi: जैसे स्पन्दनरहित वायुके स्थानमें स्थित दीपककी लौ चेष्टारहित हो जाती है, योगका अभ्यास करते हुए वश में किए हुए चित्तवाले योगीके चित्तकी वैसी ही उपमा कही गयी है ॥
bhagwad_gita::252.english_translation: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker, so the disciplined mind of a yogi does not waver while practicing yoga of the true self.
bhagwad_gita::252.translation_literal: यथा (as) / दीपः (lamp) / निवातस्थः (placed in a windless place) / नेङ्गते (does not flicker) / सा (that) / उपमा (comparison) / स्मृता (is remembered) / योगिनः (of the yogi) / यतचित्तस्य (of the controlled mind) / युञ्जतः (practicing) / योगम् (yoga) / आत्मनः (of the true self)
bhagwad_gita::252.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::252.essence: A trained mind becomes steady enough to stop flickering.
bhagwad_gita::252.simple_meaning: A trained mind becomes steady and unmoving, like a lamp that does not flicker when there is no wind.
bhagwad_gita::252.simple_insight: Stillness is not emptiness; it is a mind no longer pulled around by every disturbance.
bhagwad_gita::252.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna keeps teaching Arjuna how meditation changes a person from the inside. After describing the controlled mind, he gives a vivid image: a lamp in a windless place. That is the calm he wants Arjuna to recognize.
bhagwad_gita::252.modern_relevance: You finally sit down after a fight, but your thoughts keep replaying every word. This verse points to a steadiness that no argument, memory, or fear can shake.
bhagwad_gita::252.insight: It shifts attention from managing thoughts to stabilizing the mind that holds them.

bhagwad_gita::253.verse_sanskrit: यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया । यत्र चैवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति ॥
bhagwad_gita::253.verse_hindi: योगका सेवन करनेसे जिस अवस्थामें निरुद्ध चित्त उपराम हो जाता है तथा जिस अवस्थामें स्वयं अपनेआप से अपनेआपको देखता हुआ अपनेआपमें ही सन्तुष्ट हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::253.english_translation: When the restrained mind becomes still through yoga practice, and the person sees the true self by the true self, one is content in the true self alone.
bhagwad_gita::253.translation_literal: यत्र (where/in which state) / उपरमते (comes to rest) / चित्तम् (the mind) / निरुद्धम् (restrained) / योगसेवया (through the practice of yoga) / यत्र (where/in which state) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / आत्मना (by the true self) / आत्मानम् (the true self) / पश्यन् (seeing) / आत्मनि (in the true self) / तुष्यति (is content)
bhagwad_gita::253.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::253.essence: Stillness reveals a completeness that no outside thing can improve.
bhagwad_gita::253.simple_meaning: Through steady yoga practice, the mind becomes quiet. In that quiet, a person directly sees the true self and feels complete within it.
bhagwad_gita::253.simple_insight: Stillness is not emptiness; it is the relief of no longer needing anything outside yourself.
bhagwad_gita::253.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still trapped in inner conflict. Krishna describes the state meditation can reach: the mind settles, the true self is directly seen, and contentment no longer depends on outside things.
bhagwad_gita::253.modern_relevance: You finally put the phone down after an hour of scrolling and sit in silence. The noise thins, and the craving for one more distraction loses its grip.
bhagwad_gita::253.insight: It shifts attention from chasing stimulation to resting in direct awareness.

bhagwad_gita::254.verse_sanskrit: सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद्बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् । वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः ॥
bhagwad_gita::254.verse_hindi: जो सुख आत्यन्तिक, अतीन्द्रिय और बुद्धिग्राह्य है, उस सुखका जिस अवस्थामें अनुभव करता है और जिस सुखमें स्थित हुआ यह ध्यानयोगी फिर कभी तत्त्वसे विचलित नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::254.english_translation: One knows the boundless joy beyond the senses and grasped by the discerning mind; established in it, one never truly falls away.
bhagwad_gita::254.translation_literal: सुखम् (joy) / अत्यन्तिकम् (boundless, ultimate) / यत् (which) / तत् (that) / बुद्धिग्राह्यम् (grasped by the discerning mind) / अतीन्द्रियम् (beyond the senses) / वेत्ति (knows) / यत्र (in which) / न (not) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / अयम् (this one) / स्थितः (established) / चलति (falls away, wavers) / तत्त्वतः (in truth)
bhagwad_gita::254.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::254.essence: True joy is deeper than sensation and keeps you from wavering.
bhagwad_gita::254.simple_meaning: Meditation reveals a deep joy that the senses cannot reach. Once someone is grounded in it, that person no longer wavers in truth.
bhagwad_gita::254.simple_insight: There is relief in discovering a steadiness that does not depend on outer conditions.
bhagwad_gita::254.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has stopped fighting and Krishna is teaching him how the mind can become unshaken. After describing inner stillness, Krishna names the reward: a joy deeper than the senses, known only by the discerning mind, from which the meditator does not fall away.
bhagwad_gita::254.modern_relevance: You sit alone after a hard decision, phone face down, heart still racing. Then something quieter arrives — not excitement, not escape, but a steadiness that does not need applause to remain.
bhagwad_gita::254.insight: It shifts attention from chasing stimulation to recognising a joy that stabilises the mind.

bhagwad_gita::255.verse_sanskrit: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः । यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::255.verse_hindi: जिस लाभकी प्राप्ति होनेपर उससे अधिक कोई दूसरा लाभ उसके माननेमें भी नहीं आता और जिसमें स्थित होनेपर वह बड़े भारी दुःखसे भी विचलित नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
bhagwad_gita::255.english_translation: Having attained it, one thinks no greater gain exists. Established in it, one is not shaken even by great sorrow.
bhagwad_gita::255.translation_literal: यम् (which) / लब्ध्वा (having attained) / च (and) / अपरम् (another) / लाभम् (gain) / मन्यते (one considers) / न (not) / अधिकम् (greater) / ततः (than that) / यस्मिन् (in which) / स्थितः (established) / न (not) / दुःखेन (by sorrow) / गुरुणा (heavy) / अपि (even) / विचाल्यते (is shaken)
bhagwad_gita::255.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::255.essence: True fulfillment leaves nothing more to chase and nothing strong enough to unsettle you.
bhagwad_gita::255.simple_meaning: A person who reaches this state sees nothing greater to attain and cannot be shaken even by severe suffering.
bhagwad_gita::255.simple_insight: There is calm in no longer needing life to be different.
bhagwad_gita::255.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna’s mind is being trained to settle beyond fear and restlessness. Krishna describes a state so complete that no other gain seems higher, and even heavy sorrow cannot disturb it.
bhagwad_gita::255.modern_relevance: You get the message that would normally wreck your day, and your chest stays open anyway. Nothing inside you begs for a different reality.
bhagwad_gita::255.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing improvement to resting in unshakable steadiness.

bhagwad_gita::256.verse_sanskrit: तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् । स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥
bhagwad_gita::256.verse_hindi: जिसमें दुःखोंके संयोगका ही वियोग है, उसीको योग नामसे जानना चाहिये ।  वह योग जिस ध्यानयोगका लक्ष्य है, उस ध्यानयोगका अभ्यास न उकताये हुए चित्तसे निश्चयपूर्वक करना चाहिये ॥
bhagwad_gita::256.english_translation: Know that as yoga: the severance of union with suffering. Practice that yoga with certainty, with an undiscouraged mind.
bhagwad_gita::256.translation_literal: तम् (that) / विद्यात् (one should know) / दुःखसंयोगवियोगम् (the separation from union with suffering) / योगसंज्ञितम् (called yoga) / सः (that) / निश्चयेन (with certainty) / योक्तव्यः (should be practiced) / योगः (yoga) / अनिर्विण्णचेतसा (with an undiscouraged mind)
bhagwad_gita::256.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::256.essence: Yoga is the breaking of suffering’s grip, practiced steadily.
bhagwad_gita::256.simple_meaning: True meditation is the ending of the mind’s bond with suffering. That practice should be continued steadily, without losing heart.
bhagwad_gita::256.simple_insight: You can keep going without expecting every session to feel good. The practice itself is already the release.
bhagwad_gita::256.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen by grief and confusion. Krishna has already described the calm that meditation can bring, and now he names it plainly: real yoga is freedom from suffering’s grip. This verse urges steady practice without discouragement.
bhagwad_gita::256.modern_relevance: You sit in a parked car after a hard conversation, replaying every word and wanting to avoid the next one. This verse says the way out is not escape, but steady practice without losing heart.
bhagwad_gita::256.insight: It shifts meditation from a mood you wait for to a discipline you keep practicing until suffering loosens.

bhagwad_gita::257.verse_hindi: संकल्पसे उत्पन्न होनेवाली सम्पूर्ण कामनाओंका सर्वथा त्याग करके और मनसे ही इन्द्रियसमूहको सभी ओरसे हटाकर ॥
bhagwad_gita::257.english_translation: Abandon every desire born of resolve, and restrain the whole field of the senses on all sides with the mind alone.
bhagwad_gita::257.translation_literal: सङ्कल्पप्रभवान् (born from resolve) / कामान् (desires) / त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) / सर्वान् (all) / अशेषतः (completely) / मनसा (by the mind) / एव (alone) / इन्द्रियग्रामम् (the group of senses) / विनियम्य (restraining) / समन्ततः (on all sides)
bhagwad_gita::257.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::257.essence: Desire loses power when the mind stops feeding it.
bhagwad_gita::257.simple_meaning: Let go of every desire that rises from planning and craving. Use the mind to pull the senses back from every direction.
bhagwad_gita::257.simple_insight: Freedom starts when wanting stops dragging the senses outward.
bhagwad_gita::257.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is being taught how to steady the mind. Krishna now gives the practical method: drop desires born from thought, and gather the senses back before they scatter the inner life.
bhagwad_gita::257.modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one thing, and twenty minutes vanish. The mind has to pull the senses back before they pull you apart.
bhagwad_gita::257.insight: It shifts attention from chasing impulses to actively gathering the senses under one steady mind.

bhagwad_gita::258.verse_sanskrit: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया । आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::258.verse_hindi: धैर्ययुक्त बुद्धिके द्वारा संसारसे धीरेधीरे उपराम हो जाय और परमात्मस्वरूपमें मनबुद्धि को सम्यक् प्रकारसे स्थापन करके फिर कुछ भी चिन्तन न करे ॥
bhagwad_gita::258.english_translation: Little by little, the mind should be quieted by steady discernment. Fix the mind in the true self and think of nothing else.
bhagwad_gita::258.translation_literal: शनैः शनैः (little by little) / उपरमेत् (should become quiet) / बुद्ध्या (by the discerning mind) / धृतिगृहीतया (held by firmness) / आत्मसंस्थम् (established in the true self) / मनः (the mind) / कृत्वा (having made) / न (not) / किञ्चित् अपि (anything at all) / चिन्तयेत् (should think)
bhagwad_gita::258.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::258.essence: Stillness comes by degrees when the mind stops feeding itself.
bhagwad_gita::258.simple_meaning: The mind should be calmed gradually with firm understanding. Once it rests in the true self, it should stop chasing thoughts.
bhagwad_gita::258.simple_insight: Progress can be gentle. You do not have to win against the mind in one struggle.
bhagwad_gita::258.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna needs more than advice about battle — he needs a mind that can hold still. Krishna now gives the method: steady the mind gradually, place it in the true self, and stop feeding it new thoughts.
bhagwad_gita::258.modern_relevance: You sit in a parked car after a hard conversation, replaying every sentence. The answer is not to wrestle the mind harder, but to bring it back, gently, until the loop loosens.
bhagwad_gita::258.insight: It teaches you to calm thought through gradual restraint, not sudden suppression.

bhagwad_gita::259.verse_sanskrit: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::259.verse_hindi: यह अस्थिर और चञ्चल मन जहाँजहाँ विचरण करता है, वहाँवहाँसे हटाकर इसको एक परमात्मामें ही लगाये ॥
bhagwad_gita::259.english_translation: Whenever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, bring it back under the control of the true self.
bhagwad_gita::259.translation_literal: यतो यतः (wherever) / निश्चरति (wanders out) / मनः (the mind) / चञ्चलम् (restless) / अस्थिरम् (unsteady) / ततस्ततः (from there, from there) / नियम्य (restraining) / एतत् (this) / आत्मनि (in the true self) / एव (only) / वशम् (under control) / नयेत् (should bring)
bhagwad_gita::259.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::259.essence: The mind is mastered by repeated return, not by force.
bhagwad_gita::259.simple_meaning: Each time the mind runs off, bring it back again and again to the true self.
bhagwad_gita::259.simple_insight: Progress comes from returning, not from never drifting.
bhagwad_gita::259.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still teaching Arjuna on the battlefield at Kurukshetra, where the warrior’s mind must be trained like a wild horse. After telling him to withdraw the mind from distraction, Krishna gives the practical method: every time it escapes, bring it back.
bhagwad_gita::259.modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message and lose twenty minutes. The practice is not to shame the drift — it is to notice it, and return.
bhagwad_gita::259.insight: It trains the mind to recover quickly from distraction instead of obeying every impulse.

bhagwad_gita::260.verse_sanskrit: प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम् । उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::260.verse_hindi: जिसके सब पाप नष्ट हो गये हैं, जिसका रजोगुण तथा मन सर्वथा शान्तनिर्मल हो गया है, ऐसे इस ब्रह्मस्वरूप योगीको निश्चित ही उत्तम सात्त्विक सुख प्राप्त होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::260.english_translation: The yogi whose mind is peaceful, whose passion is stilled, and who is free from impurity attains the highest joy.
bhagwad_gita::260.translation_literal: प्रशान्तमनसम् (with a fully peaceful mind) / हि (indeed) / एनम् (this) / योगिनम् (the yogi) / सुखम् (joy) / उत्तमम् (highest) / उपैति (attains) / शान्तरजसम् (with passion stilled) / ब्रह्मभूतम् (become Brahman) / अकल्मषम् (spotless, free from impurity)
bhagwad_gita::260.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::260.essence: Joy comes when the restless mind finally becomes still.
bhagwad_gita::260.simple_meaning: A person who has calmed the mind, quieted passion, and become free of inner impurity reaches the highest kind of joy.
bhagwad_gita::260.simple_insight: Stillness is not emptiness; it is where a deeper happiness becomes available.
bhagwad_gita::260.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is being taught how to master the mind that keeps dragging him into fear and confusion. Krishna says that when the mind becomes peaceful and passion settles, the yogi reaches a higher joy.
bhagwad_gita::260.modern_relevance: After the argument ends and your phone stops buzzing, you finally sit in silence and notice how noisy your own mind has been. Relief begins there, not in the next distraction.
bhagwad_gita::260.insight: It shifts the goal from chasing stimulation to cultivating inner quiet that can actually receive joy.

bhagwad_gita::261.verse_sanskrit: युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः । सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते ॥
bhagwad_gita::261.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार अपनेआपको सदा परमात्मामें लगाता हुआ पापरहित योगी सुखपूर्वक ब्रह्मप्राप्तिरूप अत्यन्त सुखको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::261.english_translation: Thus, the disciplined yogi, free from impurity, always unites the self with the supreme reality and attains limitless joy through that contact.
bhagwad_gita::261.translation_literal: युञ्जन् (uniting) / एवम् (thus) / सदा (always) / आत्मानम् (the self) / योगी (the yogi) / विगतकल्मषः (free from impurity) / सुखेन (with ease) / ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शम् (contact with Brahman) / अत्यन्तम् (limitless) / सुखम् (joy) / अश्नुते (attains)
bhagwad_gita::261.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::261.essence: Repeated union with the supreme reality yields effortless, lasting joy.
bhagwad_gita::261.simple_meaning: A purified yogi keeps the mind steadily joined to the supreme reality and experiences deep, lasting joy.
bhagwad_gita::261.simple_insight: Steady practice can become a quiet joy, not a struggle.
bhagwad_gita::261.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still teaching Arjuna on the battlefield after the mind has been trained to settle down. He says that when a yogi keeps returning the self to the supreme reality, impurity falls away and a deep joy arises from that contact.
bhagwad_gita::261.modern_relevance: You sit in a silent room after a brutal week, and the mind finally stops bargaining. The relief is not dramatic; it is clean, steady, and strangely enough, enough.
bhagwad_gita::261.insight: It shifts meditation from effortful forcing to a settled intimacy with what is real.

bhagwad_gita::262.verse_sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::262.verse_hindi: सब जगह अपने स्वरूपको देखनेवाला और ध्यानयोगसे युक्त अन्तःकरणवाला योगा अपने स्वरूपको सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें स्थित देखता है और सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंको अपने स्वरूपमें देखता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::262.english_translation: The one united in yoga sees the true self in all beings and all beings in the true self, seeing everything with equal vision.
bhagwad_gita::262.translation_literal: सर्वभूतस्थम् (situated in all beings) / आत्मानम् (the true self) / सर्वभूतानि (all beings) / च (and) / आत्मनि (in the true self) / ईक्षते (sees) / योगयुक्तात्मा (the inner being united in yoga) / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / समदर्शनः (one of equal vision)
bhagwad_gita::262.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::262.essence: Equal vision dissolves the illusion of separation.
bhagwad_gita::262.simple_meaning: A person steady in meditation sees the same inner self present in every living being, and sees every living being within that same self.
bhagwad_gita::262.simple_insight: Separation softens. What remains is a quiet sense of shared belonging.
bhagwad_gita::262.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still teaching Arjuna on the battlefield, where fear and division are everywhere. After describing the settled meditator, he now shows the deeper vision that meditation reveals: one who is united in yoga sees the same self in every being and every being in that same self.
bhagwad_gita::262.modern_relevance: You are in a tense room where everyone feels like an opponent. This verse shifts the room: the person across from you is no longer a threat to manage, but a life sharing the same ground.
bhagwad_gita::262.insight: It trains the mind to move from separation to shared essence, changing how you look at people before you act toward them.

bhagwad_gita::263.verse_sanskrit: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति । तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥
bhagwad_gita::263.verse_hindi: जो सबमें मुझे देखता है और सबको मुझमें देखता है, उसके लिये मैं अदृश्य नहीं होता और वह मेरे लिये अदृश्य नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::263.english_translation: Who sees Me in all beings and sees all beings in Me, I am never lost to that person, and that person is never lost to Me.
bhagwad_gita::263.translation_literal: यो (who) / माम् (Me) / पश्यति (sees) / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / सर्वम् (all) / च (and) / मयि (in Me) / पश्यति (sees) / तस्य (to that one) / अहम् (I) / न (not) / प्रणश्यामि (am lost) / सः (that one) / च (and) / मे (to Me) / न (not) / प्रणश्यति (is lost)
bhagwad_gita::263.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::263.essence: Seeing the divine everywhere ends separation.
bhagwad_gita::263.simple_meaning: Seeing the divine in every being creates a living connection that cannot be broken. The one who sees this way is never separated from Krishna, and Krishna is never separated from that person.
bhagwad_gita::263.simple_insight: You do not have to force closeness when you learn to recognize the same presence everywhere.
bhagwad_gita::263.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, after teaching steady meditation, Krishna shows Arjuna the fruit of true vision: a mind that no longer divides the world into separate pieces. The yogi who sees Krishna in all beings and all beings in Krishna lives in unbroken nearness.
bhagwad_gita::263.modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room and see the same fear in the patient, the nurse, and yourself. In that moment, the wall between 'me' and 'them' softens, and compassion becomes natural.
bhagwad_gita::263.insight: It shifts perception from separation to shared presence, making devotion feel immediate rather than abstract.

bhagwad_gita::264.verse_sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः । सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते ॥
bhagwad_gita::264.verse_hindi: मेरेमें एकीभावसे स्थित हुआ जो योगी सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें स्थित मेरा भजन करता है, वह सब कुछ बर्ताव करता हुआ भी मेरेमें ही बर्ताव कर रहा है अर्थात् वह सर्वथा मेरेमें ही स्थित है ॥
bhagwad_gita::264.english_translation: The yogi who abides in unity and worships Me in all beings lives in Me, even while acting in every way.
bhagwad_gita::264.translation_literal: सर्वभूतस्थितम् (situated in all beings) / यः (who) / माम् (Me) / भजति (worships) / एकत्वम् (oneness) / आस्थितः (established) / सर्वथा (in every way) / वर्तमानः अपि (even while acting) / सः (that) / योगी (yogi) / मयि (in Me) / वर्तते (abides)
bhagwad_gita::264.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::264.essence: Unity turns every action into abiding presence.
bhagwad_gita::264.simple_meaning: A person who sees the divine in every being and lives in that oneness remains rooted in the divine, even while going through ordinary activity.
bhagwad_gita::264.simple_insight: You do not have to leave the world to stay connected. Ordinary action can become sacred when your vision changes.
bhagwad_gita::264.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna keeps unfolding the deeper vision. After teaching him to see the same presence in all beings, Krishna says that the one who lives in that unity is never truly separate from Him, even while acting in the world.
bhagwad_gita::264.modern_relevance: You are in a crowded train, answering messages, half-distracted, and still something in you is steady. The verse points to that steadiness: outward motion does not have to break inward communion.
bhagwad_gita::264.insight: It shifts devotion from a separate ritual into a continuous way of seeing and acting.

bhagwad_gita::265.verse_sanskrit: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन । सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः ॥
bhagwad_gita::265.verse_hindi: हे अर्जुन  जो ध्यानयुक्त ज्ञानी महापुरुष अपने शरीरकी उपमासे सब जगह अपनेको समान देखता है और सुख अथवा दुःखको भी समान देखता है, वह परम योगी माना गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::265.english_translation: O Arjuna, the yogi who sees all beings as equal through the measure of the true self, and sees pleasure and pain alike, is considered the highest yogi.
bhagwad_gita::265.translation_literal: आत्मौपम्येन (by comparison with the self) / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / समम् (equally) / पश्यति (sees) / यः (who) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / सुखम् (pleasure) / वा (or) / यदि (if) / वा (or) / दुःखम् (pain) / सः (that) / योगी (yogi) / परमः (highest) / मतः (is considered)
bhagwad_gita::265.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::265.essence: Equal vision makes you unshaken by pleasure or pain.
bhagwad_gita::265.simple_meaning: A true meditator sees every being with equal regard and does not get thrown off by pleasure or pain.
bhagwad_gita::265.simple_insight: There is freedom in meeting life without flinching or favoring one side.
bhagwad_gita::265.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna teaches the discipline of meditation. After showing that the divine is present in all beings, Krishna now gives the inner test: the highest yogi sees every being and every feeling with the same steady mind.
bhagwad_gita::265.modern_relevance: You get praised in the morning and criticized by evening. If your whole mood rises and falls with each message, this verse asks for a steadier center.
bhagwad_gita::265.insight: It shifts the mind from personal reaction to even-minded seeing.

bhagwad_gita::266.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचयोऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::266.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे मधुसूदन  आपने समतापूर्वक जो यह योग कहा है, मनकी चञ्चलताके कारण मैं इस योगकी स्थिर स्थिति नहीं देखता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::266.english_translation: Arjuna said: Krishna, you have described this yoga as balanced, but I do not see its steady practice, because the mind is restless.
bhagwad_gita::266.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / यः (which) / अयम् (this) / योगः (yoga) / त्वया (by you) / प्रोक्तः (spoken) / साम्येन (with balance) / मधुसूदन (O Madhusudana) / एतस्य (of this) / अहम् (I) / न (not) / पश्यामि (see) / चञ्चलत्वात् (because of restlessness) / स्थितिम् (steady state) / स्थिराम् (firm)
bhagwad_gita::266.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::266.essence: Restlessness makes even clear teaching feel unreachable.
bhagwad_gita::266.simple_meaning: Arjuna says the balanced state Krishna described sounds clear, but his restless mind cannot hold it steadily.
bhagwad_gita::266.simple_insight: It is honest to admit when the mind is too unsettled to stay still.
bhagwad_gita::266.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has heard Krishna describe the calm, even-minded yogi. But the pressure of war and his own agitation make that ideal feel unreachable, so he admits the problem directly.
bhagwad_gita::266.modern_relevance: You sit in the car before walking into a hard conversation, heart racing, rehearsing every possible outcome. Part of you knows the right thing; another part cannot settle long enough to do it.
bhagwad_gita::266.insight: It names mental restlessness as the first obstacle, so the response becomes steadiness rather than self-blame.

bhagwad_gita::267.verse_sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::267.verse_hindi: क्योंकि हे कृष्ण  मन बड़ा ही चञ्चल, प्रमथनशील, दृढ़ जिद्दी और बलवान् है ।  उसका निग्रह करना मैं वायुकी तरह अत्यन्त कठिन मानता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::267.english_translation: The mind is restless, turbulent, stubborn, and strong. I think controlling it is as hard as controlling the wind.
bhagwad_gita::267.translation_literal: चञ्चलम् (restless) / हि (indeed) / मनः (mind) / कृष्ण (O Krishna) / प्रमाथि (turbulent) / बलवत् (strong) / दृढम् (stubborn, firm) । / तस्य (of that) / अहम् (I) / निग्रहम् (control, restraint) / मन्ये (consider) / वायोः (of wind) / इव (like) / सुदुष्करम् (very difficult)
bhagwad_gita::267.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::267.essence: The mind resists control like wind resists the hand.
bhagwad_gita::267.simple_meaning: Arjuna admits that the mind is wild, forceful, and hard to restrain, almost like trying to catch the wind.
bhagwad_gita::267.simple_insight: It feels honest to admit how hard inner control can be.
bhagwad_gita::267.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has just asked Krishna about the steady state of meditation. He now confesses the real obstacle: the mind itself. This verse deepens the problem before Krishna answers with a practical method.
bhagwad_gita::267.modern_relevance: You sit down to pray, meditate, or even make one clean decision, and your thoughts scatter in every direction. The struggle is real before the discipline even begins.
bhagwad_gita::267.insight: It names the first obstacle clearly: the mind is not naturally obedient, so practice must begin with that fact.

bhagwad_gita::268.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचअसंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::268.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे महाबाहो  यह मन बड़ा चञ्चल है और इसका निग्रह करना भी बड़ा कठिन है  यह तुम्हारा कहना बिलकुल ठीक है ।  परन्तु हे कुन्तीनन्दन  अभ्यास और वैराग्यके द्वारा इसका निग्रह किया जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::268.english_translation: The mind is hard to control, but it is mastered through practice and detachment.
bhagwad_gita::268.translation_literal: असंशयम् (without doubt) / महाबाहो (mighty-armed one) / मनः (mind) / दुर्निग्रहम् (hard to restrain) / चलम् (restless) / अभ्यासेन (through practice) / तु (but) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / वैराग्येण (through detachment) / च (and) / गृह्यते (is mastered)
bhagwad_gita::268.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::268.essence: A restless mind is not a verdict; it is a training ground.
bhagwad_gita::268.simple_meaning: The mind really is restless and difficult to control, but steady practice and letting go of cravings can bring it under control.
bhagwad_gita::268.simple_insight: You are not stuck with a chaotic mind forever. Repeated practice can change what once felt impossible.
bhagwad_gita::268.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has admitted that his mind feels wild and ungovernable. Krishna answers with reassurance: Arjuna is right, but the mind can still be trained through steady practice and non-attachment.
bhagwad_gita::268.modern_relevance: You sit down to meditate, and the same ten thoughts return before the timer ends. Instead of treating that as failure, you keep returning — again and again — until the mind learns a new habit.
bhagwad_gita::268.insight: It shifts the mind from self-criticism to patient training: repetition and release are the method.

bhagwad_gita::269.verse_sanskrit: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः । वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः ॥
bhagwad_gita::269.verse_hindi: जिसका मन पूरा वशमें नहीं है, उसके द्वारा योग प्राप्त होना कठिन है ।  परन्तु उपायपूर्वक यत्न करनेवाले वश्यात्माको योग प्राप्त हो सकता है, ऐसा मेरा मत है ॥
bhagwad_gita::269.english_translation: Yoga is hard to attain for one whose mind is not fully controlled. But for one who controls the mind and strives with the right method, it can be reached.
bhagwad_gita::269.translation_literal: असंयतात्मना (by one whose self is not controlled) / योगः (yoga) / दुष्प्रापः (hard to attain) / इति (thus) / मे (my) / मतिः (view) । / वश्यात्मना (by one whose self is under control) / तु (but) / यतता (by one striving) / शक्यः (possible) / अवाप्तुम् (to attain) / उपायतः (by right means)
bhagwad_gita::269.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::269.essence: Yoga becomes reachable when the mind is trained, not merely hoped for.
bhagwad_gita::269.simple_meaning: A person ruled by an uncontrolled mind struggles to reach yoga. With self-control, steady effort, and the right method, yoga becomes possible.
bhagwad_gita::269.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing the path is blocked by chaos, not by your worth.
bhagwad_gita::269.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has already admitted that the mind is hard to control. Krishna answers with a practical promise: yoga is difficult for the undisciplined, but possible for the one who steadies the mind and keeps practicing.
bhagwad_gita::269.modern_relevance: You sit at the edge of a hard conversation, rehearsing and retreating at once. The problem is not the conversation itself; it is the mind that keeps slipping away from your intention.
bhagwad_gita::269.insight: It shifts the focus from wishing for calm to building the control and method that make calm possible.

bhagwad_gita::270.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचअयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥
bhagwad_gita::270.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे कृष्ण  जिसकी साधनमें श्रद्धा है, पर जिसका प्रयत्न शिथिल है, वह अन्तसमयमें अगर योगसे विचलितमना हो जाय, तो वह योगसिद्धिको प्राप्त न करके किस गतिको चला जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::270.english_translation: Arjuna said: What happens to a person who has faith but lacks steady effort, whose mind turns away from yoga before full success is reached, O Krishna?
bhagwad_gita::270.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / अयतिः (one without steady effort) / श्रद्धयोपेतः (endowed with faith) / योगात् (from yoga) / चलितमानसः (with a mind turned away) / अप्राप्य (without attaining) / योगसंसिद्धिम् (perfection in yoga) / कां गतिम् (what state) / कृष्ण (O Krishna) / गच्छति (does he go)
bhagwad_gita::270.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::270.essence: Faith without completion still deserves a clear answer.
bhagwad_gita::270.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who begins with faith but loses steadiness before reaching full yogic success.
bhagwad_gita::270.simple_insight: It speaks to the fear of starting well and not finishing cleanly.
bhagwad_gita::270.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has moved from panic to a deeper question about the path itself. After Krishna explains meditation and self-mastery, Arjuna asks about the sincere seeker who slips before completion. The issue is not battle now, but whether unfinished effort is lost.
bhagwad_gita::270.modern_relevance: You start therapy, prayer, or a hard habit change with real hope, then life knocks you sideways. The question is whether a falter erases the sincerity that began the effort.
bhagwad_gita::270.insight: It shifts the mind from judging failure to asking what remains of sincere effort.

bhagwad_gita::271.verse_sanskrit: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति । अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥
bhagwad_gita::271.verse_hindi: हे महाबाहो  संसारके आश्रयसे रहित और परमात्मप्राप्तिके मार्गमें मोहित अर्थात् विचलित  इस तरह दोनों ओरसे भ्रष्ट हुआ साधक क्या छिन्नभिन्न बादलकी तरह नष्ट तो नहीं हो जाता ॥
bhagwad_gita::271.english_translation: O mighty-armed one, does a person who has fallen from both sides, like a torn cloud, perish without support, deluded on the path of the supreme reality?
bhagwad_gita::271.translation_literal: कच्चित् (whether?) / नोभयविभ्रष्टः (fallen from both sides) / छिन्नाभ्रम् (torn cloud) / इव (like) / नश्यति (perishes) / अप्रतिष्ठः (without support) / महाबाहो (O mighty-armed one) / विमूढः (deluded) / ब्रह्मणः (of the supreme reality) / पथि (on the path)
bhagwad_gita::271.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::271.essence: Half-finished striving can feel like total ruin.
bhagwad_gita::271.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks whether a person who fails in both worldly life and spiritual practice is lost completely, like a torn cloud blown apart.
bhagwad_gita::271.simple_insight: It is the fear of trying and still losing everything that makes the mind tremble.
bhagwad_gita::271.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is already shaken by the thought of meditation and duty pulling in opposite directions. He asks Krishna whether someone who slips from both worldly support and the path to liberation simply disappears like a broken cloud. This keeps the question open for Krishna's answer.
bhagwad_gita::271.modern_relevance: You quit the job, leave the relationship, or walk away from the old identity — and then fear hits: what if the new path fails and the old one is already gone?
bhagwad_gita::271.insight: It names the terror of spiritual failure and prepares the mind to seek reassurance beyond success or loss.

bhagwad_gita::272.verse_sanskrit: एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः । त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::272.verse_hindi: हे कृष्ण मेरे इस सन्देहका सर्वथा छेदन करनेके लिये आप ही योग्य हैं क्योंकि इस संशयका छेदन करनेवाला आपके सिवाय दूसरा कोई हो नहीं सकता ॥
bhagwad_gita::272.english_translation: O Krishna, only you can fully cut away this doubt. No one else is able to remove it.
bhagwad_gita::272.translation_literal: एतत् (this) / मे (my) / संशयम् (doubt) / कृष्ण (O Krishna) / छेत्तुम् (to cut) / अर्हसि (you are able) / अशेषतः (completely) / त्वदन्यः (other than you) / संशयस्य (of the doubt) / अस्य (of this) / छेत्ता (cutter) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / उपपद्यते (is possible)
bhagwad_gita::272.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::272.essence: Only clear seeing can end confusion completely.
bhagwad_gita::272.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to remove his doubt completely, saying no one else can resolve it.
bhagwad_gita::272.simple_insight: Some questions need a teacher who can see the whole path, not just one answer.
