bhagwad_gita::272.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is shaken by a deeper fear than war itself: what happens to sincere practice that falters? After asking Krishna about the fate of such a person, he now admits that only Krishna can end this doubt fully.
bhagwad_gita::272.modern_relevance: You keep circling the same decision at 1 a.m., reading opinions, still unsure. At some point, you need someone who can see the whole pattern and name the real issue.
bhagwad_gita::272.insight: It shifts the mind from self-argument to seeking clear guidance from someone who sees beyond confusion.

bhagwad_gita::273.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचपार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते । नहि कल्याणकृत्कश्िचद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥
bhagwad_gita::273.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे पृथानन्दन  उसका न तो इस लोकमें और न परलोकमें ही विनाश होता है क्योंकि हे प्यारे  कल्याणकारी काम करनेवाला कोई भी मनुष्य दुर्गतिको प्राप्त नहीं जाता ॥
bhagwad_gita::273.english_translation: Krishna said: O Partha, there is no destruction for him either here or hereafter. No one who does good ever comes to a bad end, my dear.
bhagwad_gita::273.translation_literal: श्री भगवानुवाच (the Blessed One said) / पार्थ (O Partha) / नैव (not at all) / इह (here) / न (not) / अमुत्र (in the other world) / विनाशः (destruction) / तस्य (of him) / विद्यते (there is) / नहि (indeed not) / कल्याणकृत् (one who does good) / कश्चित् (anyone) / दुर्गतिम् (bad end) / तात (my dear) / गच्छति (goes)
bhagwad_gita::273.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::273.essence: Sincere effort toward the good cannot end in ruin.
bhagwad_gita::273.simple_meaning: A person who does good practice does not lose everything. Even if progress feels interrupted, that effort is never destroyed and never leads to a bad end.
bhagwad_gita::273.simple_insight: You can keep going without fear that honest effort will be wasted.
bhagwad_gita::273.detailed_meaning: Arjuna has asked what happens to someone who starts yoga but falls short. Krishna answers on the battlefield of Kurukshetra: even a failed seeker is not destroyed. A sincere step toward the good cannot end in loss.
bhagwad_gita::273.modern_relevance: You finally start therapy, meditation, or a hard apology, then stumble and feel you ruined everything. This verse says the effort still counts; one setback does not erase sincere movement.
bhagwad_gita::273.insight: It shifts the mind from fear of failure to trust in continued effort.

bhagwad_gita::274.verse_sanskrit: प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः । शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ॥
bhagwad_gita::274.verse_hindi: वह योगभ्रष्ट पुण्यकर्म करनेवालोंके लोकोंको प्राप्त होकर और वहाँ बहुत वर्षोंतक रहकर फिर यहाँ शुद्ध श्रीमानोंके घरमें जन्म लेता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::274.english_translation: The one who falls from yoga reaches the worlds earned by good deeds, dwells there for many long years, and is then born again in the house of the pure and prosperous.
bhagwad_gita::274.translation_literal: प्राप्य (having attained) / पुण्यकृताम् (of those who have done good deeds) / लोकान् (worlds) / उषित्वा (having dwelt) / शाश्वतीः (lasting, long) / समाः (years) / शुचीनाम् (of the pure) / श्रीमताम् (of the prosperous) / गेहे (in the house) / योगभ्रष्टः (one fallen from yoga) / अभिजायते (is born again)
bhagwad_gita::274.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::274.essence: A fall from yoga still carries you forward.
bhagwad_gita::274.simple_meaning: A person who slips from yoga does not lose everything. After enjoying the results of good deeds for a long time, that person is born again in a pure, prosperous family.
bhagwad_gita::274.simple_insight: A setback on the path is not the end. Even a fall can become a new starting point.
bhagwad_gita::274.detailed_meaning: Arjuna has asked what happens if someone begins the path of yoga but fails before completion. Krishna answers with reassurance: the effort is not wasted. A fallen yogi rises again into favorable conditions, carrying the momentum of past practice.
bhagwad_gita::274.modern_relevance: You meditated for months, then life derailed you. The verse says the effort did not vanish; it can return as a better beginning, not a failure.
bhagwad_gita::274.insight: It shifts the mind from shame about interruption to trust in the continuity of practice.

bhagwad_gita::275.verse_sanskrit: अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम् । एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::275.verse_hindi: अथवा वैराग्यवान् योगभ्रष्ट ज्ञानवान् योगियोंके कुलमें ही जन्म लेता है ।  इस प्रकारका जो यह जन्म है, यह संसारमें बहुत ही दुर्लभ है ॥
bhagwad_gita::275.english_translation: Or he is born into the family of wise yogis. Such a birth is very rare in this world.
bhagwad_gita::275.translation_literal: अथवा (or) / योगिनाम् (of yogis) / एव (indeed) / कुले (in the family) / भवति (is born) / धीमताम् (of the wise) । / एतत् (this) / हि (indeed) / दुर्लभतरम् (more rare) / लोके (in the world) / जन्म (birth) / यत् (which) / ईदृशम् (of this kind)
bhagwad_gita::275.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::275.essence: A fallen practitioner is not lost; the next birth can restart the work.
bhagwad_gita::275.simple_meaning: A person who falls from yoga may be born into a family of wise practitioners. That kind of birth is very rare.
bhagwad_gita::275.simple_insight: Even a setback can place you closer to renewal than you think.
bhagwad_gita::275.detailed_meaning: Krishna is reassuring Arjuna after describing the yogi who slips from practice. The one who has not finished the path does not vanish; that person may return in a family shaped by wisdom and discipline, where practice can continue.
bhagwad_gita::275.modern_relevance: You feel like you wasted years after a relapse, a failed attempt, or a broken routine. The path is not erased; the next good environment can carry you forward again.
bhagwad_gita::275.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing failure as loss to seeing it as a delayed continuation of practice.

bhagwad_gita::276.verse_sanskrit: तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम् । यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन ॥
bhagwad_gita::276.verse_hindi: हे कुरुनन्दन  वहाँपर उसको पूर्वजन्मकृत साधनसम्पत्ति अनायास ही प्राप्त हो जाती है ।  फिर उससे वह साधनकी सिद्धिके विषयमें पुनः विशेषतासे यत्न करता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::276.english_translation: O son of Kuru, there he effortlessly regains the spiritual understanding from his previous life. Then he strives again, with greater force, toward complete success.
bhagwad_gita::276.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / तम् (that) / बुद्धिसंयोगम् (union with discernment) / लभते (he attains) / पौर्वदेहिकम् (belonging to the former body) / यतते (he strives) / च (and) / ततः (then) / भूयः (again) / संसिद्धौ (toward complete success) / कुरुनन्दन (O son of Kuru)
bhagwad_gita::276.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::276.essence: Nothing gained in sincere practice is ever truly lost.
bhagwad_gita::276.simple_meaning: A person who falls from yoga does not lose everything. He regains the insight and practice from a former life and continues striving toward full success.
bhagwad_gita::276.simple_insight: Progress is not erased by failure. What you have truly practiced comes back and keeps working for you.
bhagwad_gita::276.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna fears that a failed spiritual effort is wasted. Krishna answers by describing the yogi who falls short: even after death, the person regains past discernment and resumes the path with renewed strength.
bhagwad_gita::276.modern_relevance: You return to a practice after months away and expect to start from zero. Something in you remembers. The old discipline is not gone; it waits to be reawakened.
bhagwad_gita::276.insight: It shifts the mind from fear of wasted effort to trust in accumulated practice.

bhagwad_gita::277.verse_sanskrit: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः । जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥
bhagwad_gita::277.verse_hindi: वह श्रीमानोंके घरमें जन्म लेनेवाला योगभ्रष्ट मनुष्य भोगोंके परवश होता हुआ भी पूर्वजन्ममें किये हुए अभ्याससाधन के कारण ही परमात्माकी तरफ खिंच जाता है क्योंकि योगसमता का जिज्ञासु भी वेदोंमें कहे हुए सकाम कर्मोंका अतिक्रमण कर जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::277.english_translation: Even against his will, he is drawn onward by that earlier practice. Even the seeker of yoga goes beyond the sound of ritual words.
bhagwad_gita::277.translation_literal: पूर्वाभ्यासेन (by earlier practice) / तेन (by that) / एव (indeed) / ह्रियते (is drawn away) / हि (certainly) / अवशः (against his will) / अपि (even) / सः (he) । / जिज्ञासुः (seeker) / अपि (even) / योगस्य (of yoga) / शब्दब्रह्म (sound-Brahman / ritual words) / अति-वर्तते (goes beyond) ॥
bhagwad_gita::277.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::277.essence: Earlier practice keeps pulling you forward, even against resistance.
bhagwad_gita::277.simple_meaning: Past practice pulls a person toward yoga even when the person is not fully in control. A sincere seeker also rises beyond ritual words and outer religious forms.
bhagwad_gita::277.simple_insight: Your deepest practice keeps working even when willpower fades.
bhagwad_gita::277.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Arjuna is being taught why no sincere effort is ever wasted. Krishna explains that past practice keeps drawing a fallen yogi back, and even the mere seeker of yoga moves beyond ritual-minded action.
bhagwad_gita::277.modern_relevance: You open your meditation app after weeks of skipping it, and something in you still remembers the way. That quiet pull is not random — practice leaves a trail.
bhagwad_gita::277.insight: It reframes spiritual effort as cumulative: even broken practice keeps carrying you forward.

bhagwad_gita::278.verse_sanskrit: प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः । अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::278.verse_hindi: परन्तु जो योगी प्रयत्नपूर्वक यत्न करता है और जिसके पाप नष्ट हो गये हैं तथा जो अनेक जन्मोंसे सिद्ध हुआ है, वह योगी फिर परमगतिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::278.english_translation: But the yogi who keeps striving with effort, whose impurities have been cleared, and who has been perfected through many births, reaches the highest goal.
bhagwad_gita::278.translation_literal: प्रयत्नात् (by effort) / यतमानः (striving) / तु (but) / योगी (yogi) / संशुद्धकिल्बिषः (with impurities fully cleansed) / अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धः (perfected through many births) / ततः (then) / याति (goes) / पराम् (highest) / गतिम् (goal)
bhagwad_gita::278.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::278.essence: Persistent striving eventually ripens into the highest fulfillment.
bhagwad_gita::278.simple_meaning: Persistent effort clears inner impurities, and over many lives of practice, the yogi reaches the highest goal.
bhagwad_gita::278.simple_insight: Progress is not wasted. Every sincere attempt adds up, even when results feel far away.
bhagwad_gita::278.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna is answering Arjuna’s fear that spiritual effort can be lost. After describing how practice carries forward across births, he says that the one who keeps striving, becomes purified, and matures through many lives finally reaches the highest state.
bhagwad_gita::278.modern_relevance: You return to the mat after months away, stiff and distracted, wondering whether any of it still counts. It does. The effort itself keeps shaping you, even when progress feels invisible.
bhagwad_gita::278.insight: It shifts the mind from judging practice by speed to trusting cumulative transformation.

bhagwad_gita::279.verse_sanskrit: तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः । कर्मिभ्यश्चाधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन ॥
bhagwad_gita::279.verse_hindi: सकामभाववाले तपस्वियोंसे भी योगी श्रेष्ठ है, ज्ञानियोंसे भी योगी श्रेष्ठ है और कर्मियोंसे भी योगी श्रेष्ठ है  ऐसा मेरा मत है ।  अतः हे अर्जुन  तू योगी हो जा ॥
bhagwad_gita::279.english_translation: The yogi is greater than ascetics, greater than scholars, and greater than workers. Therefore, Arjuna, become a yogi.
bhagwad_gita::279.translation_literal: तपस्विभ्योऽधिकः (greater than ascetics) / योगी (the yogi) / ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि (even than the wise) / मतोऽधिकः (is considered greater) / कर्मिभ्यः (than workers) / च (and) / अधिकः (greater) / योगी (the yogi) / तस्मात् (therefore) / योगी (a yogi) / भव (become) / अर्जुन (Arjuna)
bhagwad_gita::279.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::279.essence: Inner mastery outranks every outer path.
bhagwad_gita::279.simple_meaning: Meditation and inner mastery are higher than harsh austerity, intellectual learning, or mere action. Krishna urges Arjuna to become a true yogi.
bhagwad_gita::279.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that inner steadiness matters more than any single method or achievement.
bhagwad_gita::279.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen, and Krishna is closing his teaching on meditation. After showing that practice can survive failure and carry across lives, he now ranks the yogi above austerity, knowledge, and action, then directly tells Arjuna to become one.
bhagwad_gita::279.modern_relevance: You can meditate for years, read every book, and still feel split when the hard choice arrives at midnight. The real test is whether your mind can stay centered when action is unavoidable.
bhagwad_gita::279.insight: It shifts the goal from collecting spiritual methods to becoming inwardly integrated.

bhagwad_gita::280.verse_sanskrit: योगिनामपि सर्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना । श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः ॥
bhagwad_gita::280.verse_hindi: सम्पूर्ण योगियोंमें भी जो श्रद्धावान् भक्त मुझमें तल्लीन हुए मनसे मेरा भजन करता है, वह मेरे मतमें सर्वश्रेष्ठ योगी है ॥
bhagwad_gita::280.english_translation: Among all yogis, the one who worships me with trust, with the inner self absorbed in me, is considered the most fully united.
bhagwad_gita::280.translation_literal: योगिनाम् (of yogis) / अपि (even) / सर्वेषाम् (of all) / मद्गतेन (with set in me) / अन्तरात्मना (with the inner self) / श्रद्धावान् (trustful) / भजते (worships) / यः (who) / माम् (me) / सः (that one) / युक्ततमः (most united) / मतः (is considered)
bhagwad_gita::280.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::280.essence: Trusting devotion is the highest integration of yoga.
bhagwad_gita::280.simple_meaning: Among all kinds of yogis, the one whose inner being is fixed on Krishna and who worships him with trust is the highest.
bhagwad_gita::280.simple_insight: Devotion is not lesser than discipline; it can be the fullest form of union.
bhagwad_gita::280.detailed_meaning: After teaching meditation, Krishna reaches the climax of Chapter 6. Arjuna has been shown practice, restraint, and steady mind, but Krishna now crowns the path: the most complete yogi is the one whose inner self rests in him and who worships with trust.
bhagwad_gita::280.modern_relevance: You can master breathing exercises, routines, and self-control, yet still feel divided. The deepest integration comes when attention, trust, and love all point in one direction.
bhagwad_gita::280.insight: It shifts the goal from technical mastery to wholehearted devotion, where inner attention and worship become one.

bhagwad_gita::281.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः । असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥
bhagwad_gita::281.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे पृथानन्दन  मुझमें आसक्त मनवाला, मेरे आश्रित होकर योगका अभ्यास करता हुआ तू मेरे समग्ररूपको निःसन्देह जैसा जानेगा, उसको सुन ॥
bhagwad_gita::281.english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: Arjuna, fix your mind on Me, take refuge in Me, and practice yoga. Hear how you will know Me fully, without doubt.
bhagwad_gita::281.translation_literal: श्रीभगवान् (the Blessed Lord) / उवाच (said) / मयि (in Me) / आसक्त-मनाः (mind attached) / पार्थ (Arjuna) / योगम् (yoga) / युञ्जन् (practicing) / मद्-आश्रयः (taking refuge in Me) / असंशयम् (without doubt) / समग्रम् (completely) / माम् (Me) / यथा (how) / ज्ञास्यसि (you will know) / तत् (that) / शृणु (hear)
bhagwad_gita::281.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::281.essence: Refuge and practice open the way to complete knowing.
bhagwad_gita::281.simple_meaning: Keep your mind focused on Krishna, rely on him, and practice yoga. Then you will come to know him fully and without doubt.
bhagwad_gita::281.simple_insight: Trust grows before certainty. The heart learns first, and understanding follows.
bhagwad_gita::281.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna begins the teaching of Chapter 7. This opening verse prepares him to understand Krishna’s full nature by turning attention, practice, and refuge toward the divine.
bhagwad_gita::281.modern_relevance: You are about to make a choice that will change a relationship, a career, or a life direction. Before the noise of opinions takes over, you steady the mind, lean on what is higher, and listen for what is true.
bhagwad_gita::281.insight: It shifts the mind from scattered doubt to devoted attention, making full understanding possible.

bhagwad_gita::282.verse_sanskrit: ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः । यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::282.verse_hindi: तेरे लिये मैं विज्ञानसहित ज्ञान सम्पूर्णतासे कहूँगा, जिसको जाननेके बाद फिर यहाँ कुछ भी जानना बाकी नहीं रहेगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::282.english_translation: I will reveal to you knowledge together with direct realization in full. Knowing that, nothing more remains to be known here.
bhagwad_gita::282.translation_literal: ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / ते (to you) / अहम् (I) / सविज्ञानम् (with realization) / इदम् (this) / वक्ष्यामि (will speak) / अशेषतः (completely) / यत् (which) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / न (not) / इह (here) / भूयः (again) / अन्यत् (other) / ज्ञातव्यम् (to be known) / अवशिष्यते (remains)
bhagwad_gita::282.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::282.essence: Real knowing leaves no unfinished hunger for more.
bhagwad_gita::282.simple_meaning: Krishna promises to explain both understanding and direct realization completely, so that after grasping it, nothing else needs to be learned about the matter.
bhagwad_gita::282.simple_insight: There is relief in a truth that ends restless searching.
bhagwad_gita::282.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna has lowered his bow and Krishna begins the deepest teaching of Chapter 7. After saying he will reveal himself fully, Krishna promises a knowledge so complete that it leaves no remainder for doubt.
bhagwad_gita::282.modern_relevance: You finally ask the question you have avoided for years: whether to stay in the safe job, leave the relationship, or tell the truth. A real answer ends the spinning.
bhagwad_gita::282.insight: It shifts the mind from endless partial answers to a truth that settles the whole search.

bhagwad_gita::283.verse_sanskrit: मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्िचद्यतति सिद्धये । यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्िचन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ॥
bhagwad_gita::283.verse_hindi: हजारों मनुष्योंमें कोई एक वास्तविक सिद्धिके लिये यत्न करता है और उन यत्न करनेवाले सिद्धोंमें कोई एक ही मुझे तत्त्वसे जानता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::283.english_translation: Among thousands of people, one may strive for perfection; among those striving, one may know Me in truth.
bhagwad_gita::283.translation_literal: मनुष्याणाम् (of people) / सहस्रेषु (among thousands) / कश्चित् (some one) / यतति (strives) / सिद्धये (for perfection) / यतताम् अपि (even among those striving) / सिद्धानाम् (of the perfected) / कश्चित् (some one) / माम् (Me) / वेत्ति (knows) / तत्त्वतः (in truth)
bhagwad_gita::283.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::283.essence: True knowing is rarer than striving, even among the successful.
bhagwad_gita::283.simple_meaning: Many people try to reach perfection, but very few reach true understanding of Krishna. Effort is common; real realization is rare.
bhagwad_gita::283.simple_insight: It leaves you humble: sincere effort matters, but deep understanding asks for more than effort alone.
bhagwad_gita::283.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has already been told that Krishna can be known fully. Krishna now makes the point sharper: countless people seek achievement, but only a rare few come to know him as he truly is. This prepares Arjuna for a deeper teaching.
bhagwad_gita::283.modern_relevance: You read a dozen books, follow every step, and still feel something missing. The gap is not more information — it is the rare shift into direct understanding.
bhagwad_gita::283.insight: It shifts the mind from collecting effort to seeking direct realization.

bhagwad_gita::284.verse_sanskrit: भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च । अहङ्कार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा ॥
bhagwad_gita::284.verse_hindi: पृथ्वी, जल, तेज, वायु, आकाश  ये पञ्चमहाभूत और मन, बुद्धि तथा अहंकार  यह आठ प्रकारके भेदोंवाली मेरी अपरा प्रकृति है ।  हे महाबाहो  इस अपरा प्रकृतिसे भिन्न जीवरूप बनी हुई मेरी परा प्रकृतिको जान, जिसके द्वारा यह जगत् धारण किया जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::284.english_translation: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and ego: this is My eightfold lower nature.
bhagwad_gita::284.translation_literal: भूमिः (earth) / आपः (water) / अनलः (fire) / वायुः (air) / खम् (ether) / मनः (mind) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / अहङ्कारः (ego) / इति (thus) / इयम् (this) / मे (my) / भिन्ना (separate) / प्रकृतिः (nature) / अष्टधा (eightfold)
bhagwad_gita::284.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::284.essence: What changes is not the whole of what you are.
bhagwad_gita::284.simple_meaning: Krishna names eight parts of his lower nature: the five elements, mind, intellect, and ego. This is the material side of existence, not the highest reality.
bhagwad_gita::284.simple_insight: You can stop mistaking the changing layers of life for what is ultimate.
bhagwad_gita::284.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna begins to explain the structure of reality. After promising full knowledge, Krishna first separates the changing world into eight parts: the elements, mind, intellect, and ego. This verse sets up the contrast with the higher nature that follows.
bhagwad_gita::284.modern_relevance: You are overwhelmed by your own reactions, your thoughts, and the noise around you. This verse helps you see those layers as parts of life, not the deepest truth about you.
bhagwad_gita::284.insight: It shifts attention from identifying with the changing mind-body complex to seeing it as only the lower field.

bhagwad_gita::285.verse_sanskrit: अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम् । जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::285.verse_hindi: पृथ्वी, जल, तेज, वायु, आकाश  ये पञ्चमहाभूत और मन, बुद्धि तथा अहंकार  यह आठ प्रकारके भेदोंवाली मेरी अपरा प्रकृति है ।  हे महाबाहो  इस अपरा प्रकृतिसे भिन्न मेरी जीवरूपा बनी हुुई मेरी परा प्रकृतिको जान, जिसके द्वारा यह जगत् धारण किया जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::285.english_translation: Know My higher nature, which is different from this lower nature, O mighty-armed one. By that living nature, this world is sustained.
bhagwad_gita::285.translation_literal: अपरा (lower) / इयम् (this) / इतः (from this) / तु (but) / अन्याम् (another) / प्रकृतिम् (nature) / विद्धि (know) / मे (My) / पराम् (higher) / जीवभूताम् (become living) / महाबाहो (O mighty-armed one) / यया (by which) / इदम् (this) / धार्यते (is sustained) / जगत् (world)
bhagwad_gita::285.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::285.essence: What sustains the world is subtler than what the senses first show.
bhagwad_gita::285.simple_meaning: There is a higher nature beyond matter and mind. That living power holds up the whole world.
bhagwad_gita::285.simple_insight: Reality is not just what changes. Something living and subtler is what keeps everything going.
bhagwad_gita::285.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen while Krishna begins explaining what lies behind the visible world. After naming the lower nature, Krishna points to a higher living nature that sustains everything. The teaching prepares Arjuna to see reality beyond what the senses can grasp.
bhagwad_gita::285.modern_relevance: You look at a room full of charts, deadlines, and noise, and still feel something essential is missing. Krishna points to the deeper force that makes the whole system hold together.
bhagwad_gita::285.insight: It shifts attention from surface appearances to the sustaining principle underneath them.

bhagwad_gita::286.verse_sanskrit: एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय । अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा ॥
bhagwad_gita::286.verse_hindi: अपरा और परा  इन दोनों प्रकृतियोंके संयोगसे ही सम्पूर्ण प्राणी उत्पन्न होते हैं, ऐसा तुम समझो ।  मैं सम्पूर्ण जगत् का प्रभव तथा प्रलय हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::286.english_translation: Know that all beings are born from these two natures. I am the source and the dissolution of the entire universe.
bhagwad_gita::286.translation_literal: एतद्योनीनि (having these as their womb/source) / भूतानि (beings) / सर्वाणि (all) / इति (thus) / उपधारय (understand) / अहम् (I) / कृत्स्नस्य (of the entire) / जगतः (universe) / प्रभवः (source/origin) / प्रलयः (dissolution) / तथा (also)
bhagwad_gita::286.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::286.essence: Everything that appears rises from one source and returns there.
bhagwad_gita::286.simple_meaning: All beings arise from these two natures. Krishna says he is the source and end of the whole universe.
bhagwad_gita::286.simple_insight: The world is not random or separate from its source; it rests in a living divine presence.
bhagwad_gita::286.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna unfolds the hidden structure of reality. After naming lower and higher nature, Krishna says every being comes from their union and that he is both the origin and the end of everything.
bhagwad_gita::286.modern_relevance: You watch a child, a career, or a relationship begin and end, and it feels fragile. This verse asks you to see the larger ground beneath every rise and collapse.
bhagwad_gita::286.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing life as isolated events to seeing one source behind all change.

bhagwad_gita::287.verse_sanskrit: मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय । मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥
bhagwad_gita::287.verse_hindi: हे धनञ्जय  मेरे बढ़कर इस जगत् का दूसरा कोई किञ्चिन्मात्र भी कारण नहीं है ।  जैसे सूतकी मणियाँ सूतके धागेमें पिरोयी हुई होती हैं, ऐसे ही यह सम्पूर्ण जगत् मेरेमें ही ओतप्रोत है ॥
bhagwad_gita::287.english_translation: O Dhananjaya, nothing exists higher than Me. All this world is strung on Me like pearls on a thread.
bhagwad_gita::287.translation_literal: मत्तः (than Me) / परतरं (higher) / न (not) / अन्यत् (other) / किञ्चिद् (anything) / अस्ति (exists) / धनञ्जय (O Dhananjaya) / मयि (in Me) / सर्वम् (all) / इदम् (this) / प्रोतम् (strung) / सूत्रे (on a thread) / मणिगणाः (clusters of gems) / इव (like)
bhagwad_gita::287.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::287.essence: Everything is held in one sustaining reality.
bhagwad_gita::287.simple_meaning: Krishna says nothing is greater than him, and the whole world is held together within him like beads on a string.
bhagwad_gita::287.simple_insight: You can stop feeling cut off from life. What holds everything also holds you.
bhagwad_gita::287.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen and overwhelmed. Krishna has already explained the two levels of nature and now reveals the deepest claim: nothing is beyond him, and the entire world is woven through him. This shifts Arjuna from fear to a larger vision of reality.
bhagwad_gita::287.modern_relevance: You are staring at a hospital corridor, waiting for news that could change everything. The room feels isolated, but this verse says nothing is truly separate from the ground that holds it all.
bhagwad_gita::287.insight: It shifts the mind from scattered fragments to a single sustaining presence beneath all experience.

bhagwad_gita::288.verse_sanskrit: रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभास्मि शशिसूर्ययोः । प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु ॥
bhagwad_gita::288.verse_hindi: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  जलोंमें रस मैं हूँ, चन्द्रमा और सूर्यमें प्रभा प्रकाश मैं हूँ, सम्पूर्ण वेदोंमें प्रणव ओंकार मैं हूँ, आकाशमें शब्द और मनुष्योंमें पुरुषार्थ मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::288.english_translation: O son of Kunti, I am the taste in water, the light in the moon and sun, the syllable Om in all the Vedas, the sound in space, and the valor in human beings.
bhagwad_gita::288.translation_literal: रसः (taste) / अहम् (I am) / अप्सु (in waters) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / प्रभा (light) / अस्मि (am) / शशि-सूर्ययोः (of moon and sun) / प्रणवः (the sacred syllable Om) / सर्व-वेदेषु (in all the Vedas) / शब्दः (sound) / खे (in space) / पौरुषम् (valor / human strength) / नृषु (in human beings)
bhagwad_gita::288.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::288.essence: The sacred is already inside ordinary experience.
bhagwad_gita::288.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the life and meaning present in ordinary things: taste in water, light in the sun and moon, Om in the Vedas, sound in space, and strength in people.
bhagwad_gita::288.simple_insight: The world feels less ordinary when you notice the divine presence already filling it.
bhagwad_gita::288.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna still needing certainty, Krishna begins showing how his presence runs through the world. He does not stay distant; he names himself in the taste, light, sound, and strength that sustain life.
bhagwad_gita::288.modern_relevance: You sip water after a long, anxious day and suddenly notice how simple relief can feel sacred. The same presence shows up in sunlight, music, breath, and the courage to keep going.
bhagwad_gita::288.insight: It shifts attention from searching for the divine elsewhere to recognising it in lived experience.

bhagwad_gita::289.verse_sanskrit: पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ । जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु ॥
bhagwad_gita::289.verse_hindi: पृथ्वीमें पवित्र गन्ध मैं हूँ, और अग्निमें तेज मैं हूँ, तथा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें जीवनीशक्ति मैं हूँ और तपस्वियोंमें तपस्या मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::289.english_translation: I am the pure fragrance in the earth, the radiance in fire, the life in all beings, and the austerity in ascetics.
bhagwad_gita::289.translation_literal: पुण्यो (pure) / गन्धः (fragrance) / पृथिव्याम् (in the earth) / च (and) / तेजः (radiance) / च (and) / अस्मि (I am) / विभावसौ (in fire) / जीवनम् (life) / सर्वभूतेषु (in all beings) / तपः (austerity) / च (and) / अस्मि (I am) / तपस्विषु (in ascetics)
bhagwad_gita::289.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::289.essence: The sacred is already inside nature, vitality, and discipline.
bhagwad_gita::289.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is present as the earth’s fragrance, fire’s brilliance, the life in every creature, and the discipline of seekers.
bhagwad_gita::289.simple_insight: The divine is not far away; it already moves through ordinary experience.
bhagwad_gita::289.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna frozen and Krishna teaching the larger vision, this verse continues a list of Krishna’s living presence in the world. He shows that the sacred is woven into nature, vitality, and disciplined striving.
bhagwad_gita::289.modern_relevance: You catch the smell of rain on dry soil, feel heat from a stove, or notice someone’s steady self-control. The sacred is not separate from these moments; it is already there.
bhagwad_gita::289.insight: It shifts attention from seeking the divine elsewhere to recognising it in ordinary life and disciplined effort.

bhagwad_gita::290.verse_sanskrit: बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम् । बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::290.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन  सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंका अनादि बीज मुझे जान ।  बुद्धिमानोंमें बुद्धि और तेजस्वियोंमें तेज मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::290.english_translation: Know Me, O Partha, as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the intelligence of the intelligent and the brilliance of the brilliant.
bhagwad_gita::290.translation_literal: बीजम् (seed) / माम् (Me) / सर्वभूतानाम् (of all beings) / विद्धि (know) / पार्थ (O Partha) / सनातनम् (eternal) / बुद्धिः (intelligence) / बुद्धिमताम् (of the intelligent) / अस्मि (I am) / तेजः (brilliance) / तेजस्विनाम् (of the brilliant) / अहम् (I am)
bhagwad_gita::290.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::290.essence: All brilliance is borrowed from the same source.
bhagwad_gita::290.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the original source of every living being, and that intelligence and brilliance in people come from him.
bhagwad_gita::290.simple_insight: You can stop treating brilliance as personal ownership and start seeing it as something received.
bhagwad_gita::290.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is frozen before the war. Krishna shifts the vision from fear to origin: every being comes from him, and every clear mind and radiant strength is his presence shining through.
bhagwad_gita::290.modern_relevance: You watch someone speak with rare clarity in a tense room and feel small beside them. The verse says that clarity itself is not privately owned; it flows from a deeper source.
bhagwad_gita::290.insight: It shifts attention from personal pride to the shared source behind intelligence, vitality, and presence.

bhagwad_gita::291.verse_sanskrit: बलं बलवतामस्मि कामरागविवर्जितम् । धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥
bhagwad_gita::291.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  बलवालोंमें काम और रागसे रहित बल मैं हूँ ।  मनुषयोंमें धर्मसे अविरुद्ध धर्मयुक्त काम मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::291.english_translation: Among the strong, I am strength free from desire and attachment. In beings, I am desire that does not oppose dharma, O best of the Bharatas.
bhagwad_gita::291.translation_literal: बलं (strength) / बलवताम् (of the strong) / अस्मि (I am) / कामरागविवर्जितम् (free from desire and attachment) । / धर्माविरुद्धः (not opposed to dharma) / भूतेषु (in beings) / कामः (desire) / अस्मि (I am) / भरतर्षभ (O best of the Bharatas)
bhagwad_gita::291.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::291.essence: Strength becomes clean when desire no longer fights dharma.
bhagwad_gita::291.simple_meaning: True strength is free from craving, and desire is right only when it does not fight against dharma.
bhagwad_gita::291.simple_insight: You can feel energy and wanting without being ruled by them.
bhagwad_gita::291.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield, where every impulse could become violence or collapse. He says the power in strength is not blind appetite, and desire itself is not the problem when it stays aligned with dharma.
bhagwad_gita::291.modern_relevance: You feel a surge of anger before sending the text. The force is real, but it does not have to become harm. Some wanting can move you forward without breaking your values.
bhagwad_gita::291.insight: It teaches you to separate raw impulse from rightful desire and to use energy without inner conflict.

bhagwad_gita::292.verse_sanskrit: ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये । मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि नत्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥
bhagwad_gita::292.verse_hindi: और तो क्या कहूँ जितने भी सात्त्विक, राजस और तामस भाव हैं, वे सब मुझ से ही होते हैं  ऐसा समझो ।  पर मैं उनमें और वे मेरेमें नहीं हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::292.english_translation: Know that all states of being—sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic—arise from Me. I am not in them; they are in Me.
bhagwad_gita::292.translation_literal: ये (which) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / सात्त्विकाः (sattvic) / भावाḥ (states of being) / राजसाः (rajasic) / तामसाः (tamasic) / च (and) / ये (which) / मत्तः (from Me) / एव (indeed) / इति (thus) / तान् (them) / विद्धि (know) / न (not) / तु (but) / अहम् (I) / तेषु (in them) / ते (they) / मयि (in Me)
bhagwad_gita::292.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::292.essence: All qualities arise in the divine, yet the divine is not bound by any of them.
bhagwad_gita::292.simple_meaning: Every mode of nature—clear, restless, or dull—comes from Krishna. But Krishna is beyond all of them and is not confined by any one quality.
bhagwad_gita::292.simple_insight: You can notice your moods without believing they define the deepest reality.
bhagwad_gita::292.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still shaken while Krishna keeps unfolding the truth behind all experience. After naming his powers in the world, Krishna now says that every quality of mind and nature comes from him, yet he remains beyond those qualities.
bhagwad_gita::292.modern_relevance: You feel calm in the morning, driven by noon, numb by night, and then call one of those states “me.” This verse reminds you that moods pass through you; they are not your deepest identity.
bhagwad_gita::292.insight: It shifts attention from identifying with changing states to recognising the source behind them.

bhagwad_gita::293.verse_sanskrit: त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत् । मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::293.verse_hindi: किन्तु  इन तीनों गुणरूप भावोंसे मोहित यह सब जगत् इन गुणोंसे अतीत अविनाशी मुझे नहीं जानता ॥
bhagwad_gita::293.english_translation: Deluded by these three qualities, the whole world does not know me, who am beyond them and imperishable.
bhagwad_gita::293.translation_literal: त्रिभिः (by three) / गुणमयैः (made of qualities) / भावैः (states) / एभिः (by these) / सर्वम् (all) / इदम् (this) / जगत् (world) / मोहितम् (deluded) / न (not) / अभिजानाति (knows) / माम् (me) / एभ्यः (from these) / परम् (beyond) / अव्ययम् (imperishable)
bhagwad_gita::293.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::293.essence: Three qualities can hide the imperishable reality from plain sight.
bhagwad_gita::293.simple_meaning: The whole world gets confused by the three qualities of nature and fails to recognize Krishna as the imperishable reality beyond them.
bhagwad_gita::293.simple_insight: It feels freeing to know confusion is not failure; it is a veil that can be lifted.
bhagwad_gita::293.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, where fear and doubt have frozen action. After explaining that all moods and qualities arise from him, he now says the world stays trapped inside them and cannot recognize what is beyond change.
bhagwad_gita::293.modern_relevance: You are certain a person is being difficult, but your own anger is coloring every word they say. This verse points to the hidden filter that keeps reality from being seen clearly.
bhagwad_gita::293.insight: It shifts the mind from reacting inside appearances to asking what lies beyond them.

bhagwad_gita::294.verse_sanskrit: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया । मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥
bhagwad_gita::294.verse_hindi: क्योंकि मेरी यह गुणमयी दैवी माया बड़ी दुरत्यय है अर्थात् इससे पार पाना बड़ा कठिन है ।  जो केवल मेरे ही शरण होते हैं, वे इस मायाको तर जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::294.english_translation: My divine illusion, made of the three qualities, is hard to cross. Only those who take refuge in Me go beyond it.
bhagwad_gita::294.translation_literal: दैवी (divine) / हि (indeed) / एषा (this) / गुणमयी (made of the three qualities) / मम (my) / माया (illusion) / दुरत्यया (hard to cross) / माम् (Me) / एव (alone) / ये (those who) / प्रपद्यन्ते (take refuge) / मायाम् (this illusion) / एताम् (this) / तरन्ति (cross beyond) / ते (they)
bhagwad_gita::294.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::294.essence: The way beyond the veil is not force, but refuge.
bhagwad_gita::294.simple_meaning: The forces that shape ordinary life are hard to overcome on your own. Surrendering to Krishna is what carries a person beyond them.
bhagwad_gita::294.simple_insight: You do not have to outmuscle confusion. There is relief in letting guidance do what force cannot.
bhagwad_gita::294.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen, and Krishna is explaining why ordinary effort cannot by itself break the hold of the three qualities. This verse names the obstacle and the way through it: surrender.
bhagwad_gita::294.modern_relevance: You keep trying to think your way out of the same loop at 1:40 a.m., replaying the conversation, the mistake, the fear. The verse says the exit is not more strain, but a deeper refuge.
bhagwad_gita::294.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance against confusion to surrender as the way through confusion.

bhagwad_gita::295.verse_sanskrit: न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः । माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::295.verse_hindi: मायाके द्वारा अपहृत ज्ञानवाले, आसुर भावका आश्रय लेनेवाले और मनुष्योंमें महान् नीच तथा पापकर्म करनेवाले मूढ़ मनुष्य मेरे शरण नहीं होते । ९ ॥
bhagwad_gita::295.english_translation: The deluded, the lowest among people, the wrongdoers, and those whose understanding has been stolen by the veil do not turn to me. They take refuge in a shadowed nature instead.
bhagwad_gita::295.translation_literal: न (not) / मां (to me) / दुष्कृतिनः (wrongdoers) / मूढाः (deluded) / प्रपद्यन्ते (take refuge) / नराधमाः (lowest among people) / मायया (by the veil) / अपहृत-ज्ञानाः (whose understanding has been stolen) / आसुरम् (shadowed) / भावम् (nature) / आश्रिताः (having taken refuge in)
bhagwad_gita::295.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::295.essence: A corrupted mind cannot recognise what would free it.
bhagwad_gita::295.simple_meaning: People who are deeply confused, morally corrupt, and trapped by the veil do not turn toward the divine. They lean into a destructive nature instead.
bhagwad_gita::295.simple_insight: It is sobering to see how confusion can harden into character, not just opinion.
bhagwad_gita::295.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna explains why some people never seek him even when truth is near. After describing the veil of appearance, he names the kinds of minds that stay trapped in it: confused, harmful, and pulled toward a destructive nature.
bhagwad_gita::295.modern_relevance: Someone hears the truth twice, then laughs it off a third time. The issue is no longer lack of information; the refusal has become a habit of character.
bhagwad_gita::295.insight: It shifts attention from asking why truth is absent to seeing how inner resistance blocks it.

bhagwad_gita::296.verse_sanskrit: चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन । आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ ॥
bhagwad_gita::296.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुनव  पवित्र कर्म करनेवाले अर्थार्थी, आर्त, जिज्ञासु और ज्ञानी अर्थात् प्रेमी  ये चार प्रकारके मनुष्य मेरा भजन करते हैं अर्थात् मेरे शरण होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::296.english_translation: Four kinds of virtuous people worship Me, Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise one, O best of the Bharatas.
bhagwad_gita::296.translation_literal: चतुर्विधा (four kinds) / भजन्ते (worship) / माम् (Me) / जनाः (people) / सुकृतिनः (those with good deeds) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / आर्तः (the distressed) / जिज्ञासुः (the seeker of knowledge) / अर्थार्थी (the seeker of wealth) / ज्ञानी (the wise one) / च (and) / भरतर्षभ (O best of the Bharatas)
bhagwad_gita::296.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::296.essence: Different needs can still lead to one real turning toward the divine.
bhagwad_gita::296.simple_meaning: People come to Krishna for different reasons: pain, curiosity, gain, or wisdom. All four are counted among the virtuous.
bhagwad_gita::296.simple_insight: Even imperfect motives can begin a real relationship with the divine.
bhagwad_gita::296.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen and Krishna begins explaining why people turn toward him. After warning that illusion blocks many, Krishna names four kinds of seekers who still come forward. This verse sets up the next one, which crowns the wise devotee as the highest.
bhagwad_gita::296.modern_relevance: A person opens a prayer app after a panic attack, another after reading a hard question, another because life feels empty, another because they finally want what is true. The door is open to all of them.
bhagwad_gita::296.insight: It expands the idea of devotion beyond purity tests and shows that sincere seeking matters more than perfect motives.

bhagwad_gita::297.verse_sanskrit: तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्ितर्विशिष्यते । प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः ॥
bhagwad_gita::297.verse_hindi: उन चार भक्तोंमें मेरेमें निरन्तर लगा हुआ, अनन्यभक्तिवाला ज्ञानी अर्थात् प्रेमी भक्त श्रेष्ठ है क्योंकि ज्ञानी भक्तको मैं अत्यन्त प्रिय हूँ और वह भी मेरेको अत्यन्त प्रिय है ॥
bhagwad_gita::297.english_translation: Among those four, the wise devotee who is ever united and one-pointed is श्रेष्ठ. For I am exceedingly dear to the wise one, and the wise one is dear to me.
bhagwad_gita::297.translation_literal: तेषाम् (among them) / ज्ञानी (the wise one) / नित्ययुक्तः (ever united) / एकभक्तिः (one-pointed in devotion) / विशिष्यते (is distinguished, is श्रेष्ठ) । / प्रियः (dear) / हि (indeed) / ज्ञानिनः (of the wise one) / अत्यर्थम् (greatly, exceedingly) / अहम् (I) / सः (that one) / च (and) / मम (to me) / प्रियः (dear)
bhagwad_gita::297.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::297.essence: Deep knowing and devoted love become a mutual bond.
bhagwad_gita::297.simple_meaning: Among the four kinds of devotees, the wise one who is constantly devoted and single-minded stands highest. Krishna says this devotee is very dear to him, and he is very dear to that devotee.
bhagwad_gita::297.simple_insight: Love deepens when understanding and devotion become one.
bhagwad_gita::297.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, with Arjuna still shaken, Krishna has just described four kinds of people who turn to him. Now he crowns the wise devotee as the highest: the one whose devotion is steady, exclusive, and intimate. This verse sets up the deeper claim that follows.
bhagwad_gita::297.modern_relevance: You finally understand someone you once only admired from a distance. The relationship changes when attention, trust, and knowledge stop competing and start reinforcing each other.
bhagwad_gita::297.insight: It shifts devotion from neediness to intimate understanding.

bhagwad_gita::298.verse_sanskrit: उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् । आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::298.verse_hindi: पहले कहे हुए सबकेसब भक्त बड़े उदार श्रेष्ठ भाववाले हैं ।  परन्तु ज्ञानी प्रेमी तो मेरा स्वरूप ही है  ऐसा मेरा मत है ।  कारण कि वह युक्तात्मा है और जिससे श्रेष्ठ दूसरी कोई गति नहीं है, ऐसे मेरेमें ही दृढ़ आस्थावाला है ॥
bhagwad_gita::298.english_translation: All these are noble indeed, but the wise devotee is My very self. Established in yoga, that person is steadfast in Me as the unsurpassed goal.
bhagwad_gita::298.translation_literal: उदाराः (noble) / सर्वे (all) / एव (indeed) / एते (these) / ज्ञानी (the wise one) / तु (but) / आत्मा (self) / एव (indeed) / मे (of Me) / मतम् (opinion) / आस्थितः (established) / सः (that one) / हि (indeed) / युक्तात्मा (one whose inner being is united) / माम् (Me) / एव (only) / अनुत्तमाम् (unsurpassed) / गतिम् (goal)
bhagwad_gita::298.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::298.essence: Deep knowing turns devotion into identity.
bhagwad_gita::298.simple_meaning: All four kinds of devotees are good, but the wise devotee is the closest to Krishna. Such a person is firmly united with him and sees him as the highest goal.
bhagwad_gita::298.simple_insight: There is no shame in devotion. Deep understanding turns love into closeness, not distance.
bhagwad_gita::298.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna has just praised four kinds of seekers. Now he raises the highest one: the devotee who truly knows him. In Arjuna’s frozen crisis, Krishna says that real understanding ends in intimate union, not mere admiration.
bhagwad_gita::298.modern_relevance: You have read every argument, sat through every doubt, and still feel pulled toward the same calling. At that point, knowing stops being abstract and becomes a bond that changes who you are.
bhagwad_gita::298.insight: It shifts devotion from asking for help to recognising intimate union with the divine.

bhagwad_gita::299.verse_sanskrit: बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते । वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः ॥
bhagwad_gita::299.verse_hindi: बहुत जन्मोंके अन्तमें अर्थात् मनुष्यजन्ममें सब कुछ परमात्मा ही है, ऐसा जो ज्ञानवान् मेरे शरण होता है, वह महात्मा अत्यन्त दुर्लभ है ॥
bhagwad_gita::299.english_translation: After many births, the wise one surrenders to Me, knowing that Vasudeva is everything. Such a great soul is very rare.
bhagwad_gita::299.translation_literal: बहूनाम् (of many) / जन्मनाम् (births) / अन्ते (at the end) / ज्ञानवान् (the wise one) / माम् (to Me) / प्रपद्यते (surrenders) / वासुदेवः (Vasudeva) / सर्वम् (everything) / इति (thus) / सः (that) / महात्मा (great soul) / सुदुर्लभः (very rare)
bhagwad_gita::299.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::299.essence: Deep seeing ends in surrender to the one reality in all things.
bhagwad_gita::299.simple_meaning: Real understanding ripens over many lives. At its peak, a person sees that everything is the divine and naturally turns in surrender.
bhagwad_gita::299.simple_insight: There is relief in not forcing faith; deep seeing itself becomes surrender.
bhagwad_gita::299.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna explains why some people truly know Him. After many births, rare wisdom matures into surrender: the person sees Vasudeva in all things and comes home to Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::299.modern_relevance: You keep searching for one more fix, one more answer, one more sign. Then a quiet certainty lands: nothing is separate, and the need to grasp begins to loosen.
bhagwad_gita::299.insight: It shifts the mind from fragmented seeking to whole-hearted surrender.

bhagwad_gita::300.verse_sanskrit: कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः । तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया ॥
bhagwad_gita::300.verse_hindi: उनउन कामनाओंसे जिनका ज्ञान अपहृत हो गया है, ऐसे वे मनुष्य अपनीअपनी प्रकृतिसे नियन्त्रित होकर देवताओंके उनउन नियमोंको धारण करते हुए उनउन देवताओंके शरण हो जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::300.english_translation: Driven by desire, people whose understanding has been taken away turn to other radiant beings. They follow the rules of each, shaped by their own nature.
bhagwad_gita::300.translation_literal: कामैः (by desires) / तैः तैः (by those various) / हृत-ज्ञानाः (whose understanding is taken away) / प्रपद्यन्ते (they take refuge) / अन्य-देवताः (other radiant beings) / तम् तम् (that each) / नियमम् (rule / discipline) / आस्थाय (having taken up) / प्रकृत्या (by nature) / नियताः (governed) / स्वया (by their own)
bhagwad_gita::300.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::300.essence: Desire clouds judgment and sends the mind toward smaller refuges.
bhagwad_gita::300.simple_meaning: When desire overwhelms clear thinking, people begin seeking help from other powers and follow whatever practices fit their own nature.
bhagwad_gita::300.simple_insight: It warns that craving can quietly redirect your faith before you notice.
bhagwad_gita::300.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen and Krishna is tracing the roots of human confusion. After praising the rare knower who sees the supreme reality, Krishna explains the opposite case: minds captured by desire turn away and seek smaller forms of support.
bhagwad_gita::300.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone, hoping one more answer will calm you. In that restless state, you start handing your attention to whatever promises relief, even if it never frees you.
bhagwad_gita::300.insight: It shifts attention from impulse-driven seeking to the need for clear seeing before commitment.

bhagwad_gita::301.verse_sanskrit: यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति । तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::301.verse_hindi: जोजो भक्त जिसजिस देवताका श्रद्धापूर्वक पूजन करना चाहता है, उसउस देवताके प्रति मैं उसकी श्रद्धाको दृढ़ कर देता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::301.english_translation: Whatever form a devotee wants to worship with faith, I make that faith firm in that very form.
bhagwad_gita::301.translation_literal: यो यो (whatever) / यां यां (whatever) / तनुं (form) / भक्तः (devotee) / श्रद्धया (with faith) / अर्चितुम् (to worship) / इच्छति (wants) / तस्य तस्य (for that very one) / अचलाम् (unshaken) / श्रद्धाम् (faith) / ताम् एव (that itself) / विदधामि (I make firm) / अहम् (I)
bhagwad_gita::301.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::301.essence: Faith becomes firm where the devotee turns.
bhagwad_gita::301.simple_meaning: Krishna says he strengthens a devotee's faith in whatever form that devotee wishes to worship.
bhagwad_gita::301.simple_insight: Faith is not random here; it is being shaped and steadied from within.
bhagwad_gita::301.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna hears Krishna explain why different worshippers turn toward different forms. Krishna says the inner steadiness behind that devotion is also supported by him, which prepares the next verse about how such worship bears fruit.
bhagwad_gita::301.modern_relevance: You keep returning to the same prayer, the same image, the same practice, even when your mind wanders. What feels like your own devotion is being quietly strengthened.
bhagwad_gita::301.insight: It shifts attention from judging other forms of devotion to seeing faith itself as something nurtured and deepened.

bhagwad_gita::302.verse_sanskrit: स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते । लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान् हि तान् ॥
bhagwad_gita::302.verse_hindi: उस मेरे द्वारा दृढ़ की हुई श्रद्धासे युक्त होकर वह मनुष्य सकामभावपूर्वक उस देवताकी उपासना करता है और उसकी वह कामना पूरी भी होती है परन्तु वह कामनापूर्ति मेरे द्वारा विहित की हुई होती है ॥
bhagwad_gita::302.english_translation: Endowed with that faith, that person seeks that worship, and receives those desires, granted by Me alone.
bhagwad_gita::302.translation_literal: स (that person) / तया (with that) / श्रद्धया (faith) / युक्तः (endowed) / तस्य (of that) / आराधनम् (worship) / ईहते (seeks) / लभते (obtains) / च (and) / ततः (then) / कामान् (desires) / मया (by Me) / एव (alone) / विहितान् (ordained) / हि (indeed) / तान् (those)
bhagwad_gita::302.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::302.essence: Faith draws the result, but the deeper order grants it.
bhagwad_gita::302.simple_meaning: A person with strong faith turns to that chosen deity and gets the desired result, but even that fulfillment is ultimately arranged by Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::302.simple_insight: What feels like a personal gain is still being held within a larger order.
bhagwad_gita::302.detailed_meaning: Krishna is explaining to Arjuna why people with mixed motives worship different deities. He has already said he strengthens their faith; now he adds that the resulting fulfillment also comes through his ordering, not independent power.
bhagwad_gita::302.modern_relevance: You finally get the opportunity you prayed for, and it feels completely earned. This verse asks you to notice the hidden order behind the result, not just your effort.
bhagwad_gita::302.insight: It shifts attention from the visible object of worship to the deeper source that makes any result possible.

bhagwad_gita::303.verse_sanskrit: अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम् । देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि ॥
bhagwad_gita::303.verse_hindi: परन्तु उन अल्पबुद्धिवाले मनुष्योंको उन देवताओंकी आराधनाका फल अन्तवाला नाशवान् ही मिलता है ।  देवताओंका पूजन करनेवाले देवताओंको प्राप्त होते हैं और मेरे भक्त मेरे ही प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::303.english_translation: But the reward gained by those of limited understanding is finite. Those who worship the radiant beings go to the radiant beings; my devotees come to me.
bhagwad_gita::303.translation_literal: अन्तवत्तु (finite indeed) / फलम् (fruit, result) / तेषाम् (of those) / तत् (that) / भवति (becomes) / अल्पमेधसाम् (of the little-wise) / देवान् (to the radiant beings) / देवयजः (worshippers of the radiant beings) / यान्ति (go) / मद्भक्ताः (my devotees) / यान्ति (go) / माम् (to me) / अपि (also)
bhagwad_gita::303.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::303.essence: Finite worship brings finite results; devotion returns you to Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::303.simple_meaning: Half-hearted understanding gives limited results. Those who worship lesser powers reach those powers, while Krishna's devotees reach Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::303.simple_insight: Your deepest allegiance determines your destination.
bhagwad_gita::303.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains devotion. After showing how faith can be placed in many forms, Krishna draws the line: limited worship gives limited fruit, but devotion to him leads to him.
bhagwad_gita::303.modern_relevance: You keep checking three different opinions before sending the message that matters. The mind wants a safe outcome, but the heart follows the thing it truly serves.
bhagwad_gita::303.insight: It shifts attention from short-term gains to the object of devotion itself.

bhagwad_gita::304.verse_sanskrit: अव्यक्तं व्यक्ितमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः । परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::304.verse_hindi: बुद्धिहीन मनुष्य मेरे सर्वश्रेष्ठ अविनाशी परमभावको न जानते हुए अव्यक्त मनइन्द्रियोंसे पर मुझ सच्चिदानन्दघन परमात्माको मनुष्यकी तरह ही शरीर धारण करनेवाला मानते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::304.english_translation: The unwise think I have taken a visible form from the unseen. They do not know my imperishable, supreme nature.
bhagwad_gita::304.translation_literal: अव्यक्तम् (the unmanifest) / व्यक्तिम् (manifest form) / आपन्नम् (entered into) / मन्यन्ते (they think) / माम् (me) / अबुद्धयः (the unwise) / परम् (supreme) / भावम् (nature/state) / अजानन्तः (not knowing) / मम (my) / अव्ययम् (imperishable) / अनुत्तमम् (unsurpassed)
bhagwad_gita::304.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::304.essence: Form can hide the imperishable reality beneath it.
bhagwad_gita::304.simple_meaning: People without clear understanding think Krishna has taken on a limited human body. They do not recognize his imperishable, highest nature beyond what the senses can see.
bhagwad_gita::304.simple_insight: Not everything visible is the full reality. Reverence grows when you stop reducing the vast to the familiar.
bhagwad_gita::304.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is overwhelmed and Krishna begins revealing a deeper way of seeing. Here Krishna explains that ordinary minds mistake his visible human form for his full reality, missing his imperishable supreme nature.
bhagwad_gita::304.modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary, and you dismiss the depth behind their calm face. Later you realise you were only seeing the surface. This verse warns against shrinking what is vast into what is familiar.
bhagwad_gita::304.insight: It shifts the mind from judging by appearance to recognising a deeper reality beyond form.

bhagwad_gita::305.verse_sanskrit: नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः । मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::305.verse_hindi: जो मूढ़ मनुष्य मेरेको अज और अविनाशी ठीक तरहसे नहीं जानते मानते, उन सबके सामने योगमायासे अच्छी तरहसे आवृत हुआ मैं प्रकट नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::305.english_translation: Veiled by yoga-maya, I am not visible to everyone. Deluded people do not recognize me as unborn and imperishable.
bhagwad_gita::305.translation_literal: नाहम् (I am not) / प्रकाशः (manifest) / सर्वस्य (to everyone) / योगमायासमावृतः (covered by yoga-maya) । / मूढः (deluded) / अयम् (this) / न अभिजानाति (does not know) / लोकः (world) / माम् (me) / अजम् (unborn) / अव्ययम् (imperishable) ॥
bhagwad_gita::305.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::305.essence: The hidden divine is missed by confused seeing, not by absence.
bhagwad_gita::305.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is hidden from people who are confused. They do not recognize his unborn, unchanging nature because their minds are covered by the veil of appearance.
bhagwad_gita::305.simple_insight: Not seeing clearly is often the real barrier, not the truth itself.
bhagwad_gita::305.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still shaken, and Krishna is explaining why ordinary vision cannot grasp his true nature. Even while standing before everyone, Krishna says the confused miss him because the veil of appearance covers their seeing.
bhagwad_gita::305.modern_relevance: You can sit beside someone who loves you and still miss what they are trying to say because your mind is already defending itself. The problem is often not absence, but distorted seeing.
bhagwad_gita::305.insight: It shifts attention from demanding proof to clearing the mind that cannot recognize what is already present.

bhagwad_gita::306.verse_sanskrit: वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन । भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन ॥
bhagwad_gita::306.verse_hindi: हे अर्जुन  जो प्राणी भूतकालमें हो चुके हैं, तथा जो वर्तमानमें हैं और जो भविष्यमें होंगे, उन सब प्राणियोंको तो मैं जानता हूँ परन्तु मेरेको कोई मूढ़ मनुष्य नहीं जानता ॥
bhagwad_gita::306.english_translation: Arjuna, I know all beings of the past, the present, and the future. No one knows me.
bhagwad_gita::306.translation_literal: वेद (I know) / अहं (I) / समतीतानि (the past) / वर्तमानानि (the present) / च (and) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / भविष्याणि (the future) / च (and) / भूतानि (beings) / माम् (me) / तु (but) / वेद (knows) / न (not) / कश्चन (anyone)
bhagwad_gita::306.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::306.essence: Everything is visible to the divine; the divine remains unseen to ordinary minds.
bhagwad_gita::306.simple_meaning: Krishna says he knows every being across past, present, and future, but no ordinary person truly knows him.
bhagwad_gita::306.simple_insight: There is humility in seeing how much remains unseen, even while everything else is known.
bhagwad_gita::306.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna speaks about the limits of human understanding. After saying he remains hidden by his own power, Krishna reveals the asymmetry: all beings are open to him, but he is not open to ordinary sight.
bhagwad_gita::306.modern_relevance: You can track every detail of a relationship, a project, or a crisis and still miss the one thing that matters most. Knowing facts is not the same as knowing what stands behind them.
bhagwad_gita::306.insight: It shifts the mind from collecting information to recognising the limits of ordinary perception.

bhagwad_gita::307.verse_sanskrit: इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत । सर्वभूतानि संमोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥
bhagwad_gita::307.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशमें उत्पन्न परंतप  इच्छा राग और द्वेषसे उत्पन्न होनेवाले द्वन्द्वमोहसे मोहित सम्पूर्ण प्राणी संसारमें मूढ़ताको अर्थात् जन्ममरणको प्राप्त हो रहे हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::307.english_translation: O descendant of Bharata, all beings fall into delusion at birth, from the confusion born of desire and aversion, O scorcher of foes.
bhagwad_gita::307.translation_literal: इच्छा-द्वेष (desire and aversion) / समुत्थेन (arising from) / द्वन्द्व-मोहेन (by the delusion of opposites) / भारत (O Bharata) / सर्व-भूतानि (all beings) / संमोहं (delusion) / सर्गे (at birth / in creation) / यान्ति (go to) / परन्तप (O scorcher of foes)
bhagwad_gita::307.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::307.essence: Desire and aversion turn clear seeing into confusion.
bhagwad_gita::307.simple_meaning: Desire and aversion create confusion in living beings, and that confusion keeps them trapped in repeated cycles of ignorance and rebirth.
bhagwad_gita::307.simple_insight: It is relieving to see that confusion has a cause, not just a character flaw.
bhagwad_gita::307.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield, where everything feels split between duty and fear. He explains that ordinary beings are pushed into confusion by attraction and aversion, and that confusion keeps them caught in repeated birth and death.
bhagwad_gita::307.modern_relevance: You know the moment you want one thing badly and hate the other option so much that you cannot think clearly. That tug-of-war is the very fog Krishna names.
bhagwad_gita::307.insight: It shifts the mind from blaming itself to noticing the forces of attraction and rejection that distort judgment.

bhagwad_gita::308.verse_sanskrit: येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम् । ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::308.verse_hindi: परन्तु जिन पुण्यकर्मा मनुष्योंके पाप नष्ट गये हैं, वे द्वन्द्वमोहसे रहित हुए मनुष्य दृढ़व्रती होकर मेरा भजन करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::308.english_translation: But those whose wrongdoing has been cleared away, and whose good deeds have matured, are freed from confusion and worship me with firm resolve.
bhagwad_gita::308.translation_literal: येषाम् (of whom) / तु (but) / अन्तगतं (ended, destroyed) / पापं (wrongdoing) / जनानाम् (of people) / पुण्यकर्मणाम् (whose actions are meritorious) / ते (they) / द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ताः (freed from the confusion of opposites) / भजन्ते (worship, serve) / माम् (me) / दृढव्रताः (firmly resolved)
bhagwad_gita::308.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::308.essence: Clear hearts stop wavering and move toward the divine with resolve.
bhagwad_gita::308.simple_meaning: People whose harmful impulses have been cleared and whose good actions have ripened are no longer torn by confusion. With steady commitment, they turn toward Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::308.simple_insight: Clarity feels possible again when inner conflict stops pulling you apart.
bhagwad_gita::308.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is trapped between duty and grief. Krishna explains that only people whose inner corruption has thinned and whose good actions have ripened can move beyond confusion and turn toward him with steady resolve.
bhagwad_gita::308.modern_relevance: You sit in the car after a hard conversation, replaying every sentence and feeling split in two. The mind that has stopped feeding its own confusion can finally choose cleanly.
bhagwad_gita::308.insight: It shifts the focus from divided impulse to steadiness of commitment.

bhagwad_gita::309.verse_sanskrit: जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये । ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::309.verse_hindi: जरा वृद्धावस्था और मरण मृत्यु से मोक्ष पानेके लिये जो मेरा आश्रय लेकर प्रयत्न करते हैं, वे उस ब्रह्मको, सम्पूर्ण अध्यात्मको और सम्पूर्ण कर्मको भी जान जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::309.english_translation: Those who, seeking release from old age and death, take refuge in me, come to know Brahman, the whole field of the inner life, and all action.
bhagwad_gita::309.translation_literal: जरा (old age) / मरण (death) / मोक्षाय (for release) / माम् (me) / आश्रित्य (having taken refuge) / यतन्ति (they strive) / ये (who) / ते (they) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / तत् (that) / विदुः (know) / कृत्स्नम् (whole) / अध्यात्मम् (inner life) / कर्म (action) / च (and) / अखिलम् (entire)
bhagwad_gita::309.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::309.essence: Refuge in the divine opens total understanding of reality, inner life, and action.
bhagwad_gita::309.simple_meaning: Those who take refuge in Krishna and strive for freedom from aging and death come to know the supreme reality, the whole inner life, and all action.
bhagwad_gita::309.simple_insight: Seeking freedom can become a complete understanding of life, not just an escape from it.
bhagwad_gita::309.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen before war, old age, and death hanging over every human life. Krishna says that those who seek refuge in him to escape that cycle come to understand the supreme reality, the whole inner life, and the nature of action itself.
bhagwad_gita::309.modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed after hearing a diagnosis, and suddenly every theory about life feels thin. The deeper search for relief can open a wider understanding than comfort alone ever could.
bhagwad_gita::309.insight: It shifts the mind from fearing mortality to seeking the whole pattern behind existence and action.

bhagwad_gita::310.verse_sanskrit: साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः । प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः ॥
bhagwad_gita::310.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य अधिभूत, अधिदैव और अधियज्ञके सहित मुझे जानते हैं, वे युक्तचेता मनुष्य अन्तकालमें भी मुझे ही जानते हैं अर्थात् प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::310.english_translation: Those who know me together with the physical realm, the radiant powers, and the inner sacrifice know me even at the time of death.
bhagwad_gita::310.translation_literal: स-अधिभूत-आधिदैवम् (together with the physical realm and the radiant powers) / माम् (me) / स-अधियज्ञम् (together with the inner sacrifice) / च (and) / ये (those who) / विदुः (know) / प्रयाण-काले (at the time of departure/death) / अपि (even) / च (and) / माम् (me) / ते (they) / विदुः (know) / युक्त-चेतसः (those with a disciplined mind)
bhagwad_gita::310.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::310.essence: Complete understanding remains steady even at the moment of departure.
bhagwad_gita::310.simple_meaning: Those who understand Krishna as present in the physical world, the divine powers, and the ritual offering remember him even at death.
bhagwad_gita::310.simple_insight: There is calm in knowing that clear understanding can hold even in the final moment.
bhagwad_gita::310.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, after Krishna has explained the deeper structure of reality, he gives Arjuna the final key: the one who truly understands him in every layer of existence does not lose that understanding at death. The teaching closes the chapter by tying knowledge to the last moment of life.
bhagwad_gita::310.modern_relevance: At a bedside when machines are beeping and everyone is silent, the mind does not reach for trivia. It reaches for what was truly known. This verse points to a clarity strong enough to stay present at the end.
bhagwad_gita::310.insight: It shifts the mind from partial religious ideas to a unified vision of reality.

bhagwad_gita::311.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचकिं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम । अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::311.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे पुरुषोत्तम  वह ब्रह्म क्या है अध्यात्म क्या है कर्म क्या है अधिभूत किसको कहा गया है और अधिदैव किसको कहा जाता है यहाँ अधियज्ञ कौन है और वह इस देहमें कैसे है हे मधूसूदन  नियतात्मा वशीभूत अंतःकरण वाले मनुष्यके द्वारा अन्तकालमें आप कैसे जाननेमें आते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::311.english_translation: Arjuna said: O Supreme Person, what is Brahman? What is the self? What is action? What is called the field of changing things, and what is called the divine principle? What is the sacred offering here in this body, and how are you known at the time of death by those with disciplined minds?
bhagwad_gita::311.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / किम् (what) / तत् (that) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / किम् (what) / अध्यात्मम् (the self / inner principle) / किम् (what) / कर्म (action) / पुरुषोत्तम (O Supreme Person) / अधिभूतम् (the field of changing beings / material existence) / च (and) / किम् (what) / प्रोक्तम् (is said) / अधिदैवम् (the divine principle) / किम् (what) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::311.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::311.essence: Clear seeing starts by asking what each word truly means.
bhagwad_gita::311.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain the key terms of spiritual teaching: Brahman, the self, action, the changing world, and the divine principle.
bhagwad_gita::311.simple_insight: Real understanding begins by asking clean, exact questions.
bhagwad_gita::311.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is still shaken and searching. Before the fighting begins, he asks Krishna to define the deepest terms behind life, death, action, and the imperishable reality he wants to know at the end.
bhagwad_gita::311.modern_relevance: You are standing at a hospital door, a resignation letter in your hand, or a graveside with no easy answers. Before certainty comes, honest questions have to be named.
bhagwad_gita::311.insight: It shifts the mind from vague belief to precise inquiry about what is real.

bhagwad_gita::312.verse_sanskrit: अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहेऽस्मिन्मधुसूदन । प्रयाणकाले च कथं ज्ञेयोऽसि नियतात्मभिः ॥
bhagwad_gita::312.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे पुरुषोत्तम  वह ब्रह्म क्या है अध्यात्म क्या है कर्म क्या है अधिभूत किसको कहा गया है और अधिदैव किसको कहा जाता है यहाँ अधियज्ञ कौन है और वह इस देहमें कैसे है हे मधूसूदन  नियतात्मा वशीभूत अन्तःकरणवाले मनुष्यके द्वारा अन्तकालमें आप कैसे जाननेमें आते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::312.english_translation: Arjuna said: O Madhusudana, who is the sacrifice here, and how does he dwell in this body? And at the time of death, how are you known by those with disciplined minds?
bhagwad_gita::312.translation_literal: अधियज्ञः (the lord of sacrifice) / कथम् (how) / कः (who) / अत्र (here) / देहे (in the body) / अस्मिन् (this) / मधुसूदन (Madhusudana) / प्रयाणकाले (at the time of departure) / च (and) / कथम् (how) / ज्ञेयः (to be known) / असि (you are) / नियतात्मभिः (by those with disciplined minds)
bhagwad_gita::312.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::312.essence: Real understanding begins by asking what remains when life is ending.
bhagwad_gita::312.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks who the inner sacrificer is, how that presence lives in the body, and how a disciplined person can know Krishna at death.
bhagwad_gita::312.simple_insight: It feels honest to admit confusion before asking for clarity.
bhagwad_gita::312.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna has already asked about Brahman, the self, action, and the other hidden realities. He now presses Krishna further: who is the inner lord of sacrifice, how is that presence in the body, and how can a steady mind know Krishna at the final moment?
bhagwad_gita::312.modern_relevance: You are standing in a hospital corridor, waiting for news that could change everything. The mind wants one clear answer: what truly matters now, and how do I hold it when time is running out?
bhagwad_gita::312.insight: It shifts the mind from vague belief to precise questioning about the deepest reality.

bhagwad_gita::313.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचअक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते । भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः ॥
bhagwad_gita::313.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  परम अक्षर ब्रह्म है और जीवका अपना जो होनापन है, उसको अध्यात्म कहते हैं ।  प्राणियों का उद्भव सत्ता को प्रकट करनेवाला जो त्याग है उसको कर्म कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::313.english_translation: The imperishable is the supreme reality. One's own nature is called the inner self. The offering that brings beings into existence is called action.
bhagwad_gita::313.translation_literal: अक्षरम् (imperishable) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / परमम् (highest) / स्वभावः (one's own nature) / अध्यात्मम् (inner self) / उच्यते (is called) / भूतभावोद्भवकरः (that which brings beings into existence) / विसर्गः (offering/releasing) / कर्मसंज्ञितः (called action)
bhagwad_gita::313.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::313.essence: What lasts, what you are, and what you do are not the same.
bhagwad_gita::313.simple_meaning: The imperishable is the highest reality. Inner nature is called the inner self, and the act that brings beings into existence is called action.
bhagwad_gita::313.simple_insight: The world becomes clearer when you see the difference between what never changes, what you are, and what you do.
bhagwad_gita::313.detailed_meaning: Arjuna has asked Krishna to define the terms behind existence before death arrives on the battlefield. Krishna begins by naming the imperishable reality, the inner nature of living beings, and the creative act that produces embodied life.
bhagwad_gita::313.modern_relevance: You are trying to name what matters while everything is already moving toward a hard decision. Before you can act cleanly, you need to know what is lasting, what is your nature, and what is simply an act.
bhagwad_gita::313.insight: It shifts the mind from vague spiritual language to precise categories: reality, nature, and action.

bhagwad_gita::314.verse_sanskrit: अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम् । अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर ॥
bhagwad_gita::314.verse_hindi: हे देहधारियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  क्षरभाव अर्थात् नाशवान् पदार्थको अधिभूत कहते हैं, पुरुष अर्थात् हिरण्यगर्भ ब्रह्माजी अधिदैव हैं और इस देहमें अन्तर्यामीरूपसे मैं ही अधियज्ञ हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::314.english_translation: The perishable world is the lower realm; the cosmic person is the radiant being. I am the inner witness of sacrifice in this body, Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::314.translation_literal: अधिभूतं (the lower realm of embodied existence) / क्षरः (perishable) / भावः (state of being) / पुरुषः (cosmic person) / च (and) / अधिदैवतम् (the radiant being of the gods) / अधियज्ञः (inner witness of sacrifice) / अहम् (I) / एव (indeed) / अत्र (here) / देहे (in the body) / देहभृताम् (of embodied beings) / वर (O best)
bhagwad_gita::314.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::314.essence: The changing world, the cosmic order, and the inner witness are not separate.
bhagwad_gita::314.simple_meaning: The changing world is called the lower realm. The cosmic person is called the radiant being. In this body, Krishna says he himself is the inner witness of sacrifice.
bhagwad_gita::314.simple_insight: What seems separate is ordered from within, and the deepest meaning of action is already present.
bhagwad_gita::314.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna asks Krishna to explain the terms needed for dying with awareness. Krishna answers step by step: the changing world, the cosmic presiding being, and finally himself as the inner witness within every body. The teaching builds toward Krishna's guidance at the moment of death.
bhagwad_gita::314.modern_relevance: You are trying to understand what really matters before a hard goodbye, a hospital room, or a final decision. The mind wants labels; the teaching points to the deeper order behind them.
bhagwad_gita::314.insight: It shifts attention from outer labels to the hidden presence that makes action meaningful.

bhagwad_gita::315.verse_sanskrit: अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम् । यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥
bhagwad_gita::315.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य अन्तकालमें भी मेरा स्मरण करते हुए शरीर छोड़कर जाता है, वह मेरे स्वरुप को ही प्राप्त होता है, इसमें सन्देह नहीं है ॥
bhagwad_gita::315.english_translation: Whoever remembers Me at the end and leaves the body attains My state; there is no doubt.
bhagwad_gita::315.translation_literal: अन्तकाले (at the end of life) / च (and) / माम् (Me) / एव (indeed) / स्मरन् (remembering) / मुक्त्वा (having छोड़कर / leaving) / कलेवरम् (the body) / यः (who) / प्रयाति (goes forth) / सः (that one) / मद्भावम् (My state) / याति (attains) / न (not) / अस्ति (is) / अत्र (here) / संशयः (doubt)
bhagwad_gita::315.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::315.essence: The last remembered presence shapes the next state of being.
bhagwad_gita::315.simple_meaning: A person who remembers Krishna at the moment of death and leaves the body reaches Krishna's state without doubt.
bhagwad_gita::315.simple_insight: The final thought matters most, so the mind can be trained toward what is highest.
bhagwad_gita::315.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is hearing Krishna describe the inner condition that shapes death itself. After explaining the body, the self, and the sacred act, Krishna now gives the decisive promise: remembrance at the final moment carries a person beyond bodily ending.
bhagwad_gita::315.modern_relevance: You are sitting beside a hospital bed, trying to stay steady while everything is slipping away. What the mind holds in that last, fragile moment may matter more than the words anyone says.
bhagwad_gita::315.insight: It shifts attention from physical ending to the quality of final remembrance.

bhagwad_gita::316.verse_sanskrit: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् । तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥
bhagwad_gita::316.verse_hindi: हे कुन्तीपुत्र अर्जुन  मनुष्य अन्तकाल में जिसजिस भी भावका स्मरण करते हुए शरीर छोड़ता है वह उस अन्तकालके भावसे सदा भावित होता हुआ उसउसको ही प्राप्त होता है अर्थात् उसउस योनिमें ही चला जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::316.english_translation: Whatever state a person remembers at the end, that state is reached, because the mind has been shaped by it.
