bhagwad_gita::316.translation_literal: यं यं (whatever) / वा अपि (also indeed) / स्मरन् (remembering) / भावम् (state of being) / त्यजति (abandons) / अन्ते (at the end) / कलेवरम् (the body) / तम् तम् एव (that very) / एति (attains) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / सदा (always) / तद्भावभावितः (formed by that state)
bhagwad_gita::316.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::316.essence: The end follows the state you have trained.
bhagwad_gita::316.simple_meaning: The final thought at death shapes where consciousness goes next. A person tends toward whatever state has been cultivated again and again.
bhagwad_gita::316.simple_insight: What you repeatedly dwell on becomes the shape of your ending.
bhagwad_gita::316.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna deepens the teaching on the final moment: the state of mind at death is not random, but the result of a life repeatedly formed by habit and attention.
bhagwad_gita::316.modern_relevance: You lie awake after a hard conversation, replaying the same fear. That repeated inner loop does not just reflect you — it trains the direction your mind takes next.
bhagwad_gita::316.insight: It shifts attention from the last moment alone to the whole pattern of what the mind has been fed.

bhagwad_gita::317.verse_sanskrit: तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::317.verse_hindi: इसलिये तू सब समयमें मेरा स्मरण कर और युद्ध भी कर ।  मेरेमें मन और बुद्धि अर्पित करनेवाला तू निःसन्देह मेरेको ही प्राप्त होगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::317.english_translation: Therefore, remember Me at all times and fight. With mind and intellect offered to Me, you will surely come to Me.
bhagwad_gita::317.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) / सर्वेषु कालेषु (at all times) / माम् (Me) / अनुस्मर (remember continuously) / युध्य (fight) / च (and) / मयि (in Me) / अर्पित (offered) / मनः (mind) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / माम् (Me) / एव (indeed) / एष्यसि (you will come) / असंशयम् (without doubt)
bhagwad_gita::317.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::317.essence: Action and remembrance can happen together without conflict.
bhagwad_gita::317.simple_meaning: Keep the divine in mind all the time, do your duty, and place your thoughts and understanding there. Then you will surely reach the divine.
bhagwad_gita::317.simple_insight: You do not have to choose between devotion and action. Both can live in the same moment.
bhagwad_gita::317.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen before the battle. Krishna has already taught that the final thought shapes the final destination. Now he goes further: remembrance and action are not opposites, and a warrior can fight without losing inward devotion.
bhagwad_gita::317.modern_relevance: You are in the middle of a hard conversation, heart racing, ready to back away. This verse says you can stay present, do what must be done, and keep your attention anchored.
bhagwad_gita::317.insight: It joins outer duty with inward remembrance, so action no longer fragments the mind.

bhagwad_gita::318.verse_sanskrit: अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना । परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन् ॥
bhagwad_gita::318.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन  अभ्यासयोगसे युक्त और अन्यका चिन्तन न करनेवाले चित्तसे परम दिव्य पुरुषका चिन्तन करता हुआ शरीर छोड़नेवाला मनुष्य उसीको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::318.english_translation: One who departs while remembering the divine person with a mind trained by practice and fixed on nothing else reaches that supreme divine being, O Partha.
bhagwad_gita::318.translation_literal: अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन (joined with the yoga of practice) / चेतसा (with the mind) / नान्यगामिना (not going elsewhere) / परमं (supreme) / पुरुषं (person) / दिव्यं (divine) / याति (goes, reaches) / पार्थ (O Partha) / अनुचिन्तयन् (contemplating, remembering)
bhagwad_gita::318.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::318.essence: What the mind has practiced most will claim you at the end.
bhagwad_gita::318.simple_meaning: A mind trained by steady practice, and not wandering to other things, reaches the supreme divine being when life ends.
bhagwad_gita::318.simple_insight: Steady repetition can shape the mind so deeply that it carries you toward what you love most.
bhagwad_gita::318.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen between action and fear. Krishna continues the teaching about death and remembrance, saying that a mind trained in practice and fixed on the divine reaches the highest divine person.
bhagwad_gita::318.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone in the hospital waiting room, trying to stay steady before the call comes. What your mind has practiced returning to will meet you in the hardest moment.
bhagwad_gita::318.insight: It shifts attention from last-minute panic to lifelong mental training.

bhagwad_gita::319.verse_sanskrit: कविं पुराणमनुशासितारमणोरणीयांसमनुस्मरेद्यः । सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूपमादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् ॥
bhagwad_gita::319.verse_hindi: जो सर्वज्ञ, पुराण, शासन करनेवाला, सूक्ष्मसेसूक्ष्म, सबका धारणपोषण करनेवाला, अज्ञानसे अत्यन्त परे, सूर्यकी तरह प्रकाशस्वरूप  ऐसे अचिन्त्य स्वरूपका चिन्तन करता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::319.english_translation: Whoever remembers the wise, ancient, ruler, subtler than the subtle, supporter of all, beyond thought, radiant like the sun, and beyond darkness...
bhagwad_gita::319.translation_literal: कविम् (the wise one) / पुराणम् (the ancient one) / अनुशासितारम् (the ruler) / अणोः अणीयांसम् (subtler than the subtle) / अनुस्मरेत् (should remember) / यः (who) / सर्वस्य (of all) / धातारम् (supporter) / अचिन्त्यरूपम् (of inconceivable form) / आदित्यवर्णम् (sun-colored, radiant like the sun) / तमसः (than darkness) / परस्तात् (beyond)
bhagwad_gita::319.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::319.essence: Hold the ungraspable source in mind, not the passing form.
bhagwad_gita::319.simple_meaning: Remember the supreme reality as wise, ancient, subtle, sustaining everything, beyond thought, radiant, and beyond darkness.
bhagwad_gita::319.simple_insight: The mind steadies when it turns toward what cannot be shaken, grasped, or dimmed.
bhagwad_gita::319.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is learning how to leave the body without losing his way. Krishna now describes the reality to hold in mind at the end: ancient, subtler than anything, the support of all, beyond darkness.
bhagwad_gita::319.modern_relevance: At the bedside of someone you love, words stop working. What remains is the quiet turning of attention toward what is steady when everything else is slipping.
bhagwad_gita::319.insight: It shifts remembrance from a person or image to the ungraspable source behind all forms.

bhagwad_gita::320.verse_sanskrit: प्रयाणकाले मनसाऽचलेनभक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव । भ्रुवोर्मध्ये प्राणमावेश्य सम्यक्स तं परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::320.verse_hindi: वह भक्तियुक्त मनुष्य अन्तसमयमें अचल मनसे और योगबलके द्वारा भृकुटीके मध्यमें प्राणोंको अच्छी तरहसे प्रविष्ट करके शरीर छोड़नेपर उस परम दिव्य पुरुषको ही प्राप्त होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::320.english_translation: At the time of departure, one who leaves the body with an unmoving mind, devotion, and the power of yoga, placing the life-force between the eyebrows, reaches the divine supreme person.
bhagwad_gita::320.translation_literal: प्रयाणकाले (at the time of departure) / मनसा (with the mind) / अचलेन (unmoving) / भक्त्या (with devotion) / युक्तः (joined) / योगबलेन (by the power of yoga) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / भ्रुवोः (of the two eyebrows) / मध्ये (in the middle) / प्राणम् (the life-force) / आवेश्य (placing) / सम्यक् (properly) / सः (that one) / तम् (that) / परम् (supreme) / पुरुषम् (person) / उपैति (reaches) / दिव्यम् (divine)
bhagwad_gita::320.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::320.essence: Steady devotion carries awareness beyond the body's final threshold.
bhagwad_gita::320.simple_meaning: At death, a devoted person who keeps the mind steady and directs the life-force with yogic focus reaches the divine supreme person.
bhagwad_gita::320.simple_insight: The final moment is not chaos when the mind has been trained to stay still.
bhagwad_gita::320.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna is answering Arjuna’s fear of death and the final moment. After describing the supreme, imperishable goal, he now explains the inner condition that carries a person there: steady mind, devotion, and concentrated yoga at departure.
bhagwad_gita::320.modern_relevance: A surgeon says, 'We need a decision now,' and your chest tightens. This verse points to the kind of inner steadiness that lets a person meet the last, hardest moment without panic.
bhagwad_gita::320.insight: It shifts attention from the fear of leaving the body to the quality of awareness at the moment of leaving.

bhagwad_gita::321.verse_sanskrit: यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्तिविशन्ति यद्यतयो वीतरागाः । यदिच्छन्तो ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्तितत्ते पदं संग्रहेण प्रवक्ष्ये ॥
bhagwad_gita::321.verse_hindi: वेदवेत्ता लोग जिसको अक्षर कहते हैं, वीतराग यति जिसको प्राप्त करते हैं और साधक जिसकी प्राप्तिकी इच्छा करते हुए ब्रह्मचर्यका पालन करते हैं, वह पद मैं तेरे लिये संक्षेपसे कहूँगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::321.english_translation: I will briefly tell you that imperishable state, which the knowers of the Vedas call imperishable, which the detached ascetics enter, and which seekers follow through celibate discipline.
bhagwad_gita::321.translation_literal: यत् (that which) / अक्षरम् (imperishable) / वेद-विदः (knowers of the Vedas) / वदन्ति (call) / विशन्ति (enter) / यत् (which) / यतयः (ascetics) / वीत-रागाः (free from desire) / यत् (which) / इच्छन्तः (seeking) / ब्रह्मचर्यम् (celibate discipline) / चरन्ति (practice) / तत् (that) / ते (to you) / पदम् (state) / संग्रहेण (briefly) / प्रवक्ष्ये (I will speak)
bhagwad_gita::321.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::321.essence: The imperishable is reached by giving up desire, not by feeding it.
bhagwad_gita::321.simple_meaning: Krishna says he will briefly describe the imperishable state that Vedic knowers speak of, detached ascetics enter, and disciplined seekers approach through celibate practice.
bhagwad_gita::321.simple_insight: The deepest goal is not grabbed by wanting more, but by letting wanting fall away.
bhagwad_gita::321.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna still caught between collapse and action, Krishna turns from battlefield duty to the final aim beyond death. He names the imperishable state that sages describe, and says he will explain it plainly before teaching the method to reach it.
bhagwad_gita::321.modern_relevance: You are staring at the message that could change your life, but you keep refreshing instead of answering. The thing that matters most often arrives only when craving stops driving the hand.
bhagwad_gita::321.insight: It shifts the mind from pursuit of experience to release of craving as the condition for deeper realization.

bhagwad_gita::322.verse_sanskrit: सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च । मूर्ध्न्याधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::322.verse_hindi: इन्द्रियोंके सम्पूर्ण द्वारोंको रोककर मनका हृदयमें निरोध करके और अपने प्राणोंको मस्तकमें स्थापित करके योगधारणामें सम्यक् प्रकारसे स्थित हुआ जो ऊँ इस एक अक्षर ब्रह्मका उच्चारण और मेरा स्मरण करता हुआ शरीरको छोड़कर जाता है, वह परमगतिको प्राप्त होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::322.english_translation: Closing all the doors of the senses, holding the mind in the heart, and placing the life-force in the head, one remains fixed in yoga-discipline.
bhagwad_gita::322.translation_literal: सर्वद्वाराणि (all doors) / संयम्य (having restrained) / मनः (mind) / हृदि (in the heart) / निरुध्य (having confined) / च (and) / मूर्ध्नि (in the head) / आधाय (having placed) / आत्मनः (of oneself) / प्राणम् (life-force) / आस्थितः (steadfast) / योगधारणाम् (yoga-discipline)
bhagwad_gita::322.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::322.essence: Mastery of the senses and mind prepares one for the final passage.
bhagwad_gita::322.simple_meaning: At the moment of death, the practitioner shuts the senses, steadies the mind in the heart, and places the life-force at the head through yoga practice.
bhagwad_gita::322.simple_insight: Lasting steadiness begins with disciplined control, not with panic.
bhagwad_gita::322.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna is explaining the final discipline of leaving the body with full awareness. After describing the imperishable goal, he gives the inner method: restrain the senses, gather the mind, and hold the life-force in focused stillness.
bhagwad_gita::322.modern_relevance: A hospital room goes quiet after bad news. Instead of scattering into fear, you can gather yourself, steady your breath, and meet the moment with trained attention.
bhagwad_gita::322.insight: It shifts the mind from accidental reaction to deliberate inner control.

bhagwad_gita::323.verse_sanskrit: ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् । यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::323.verse_hindi: इन्द्रियोंके सम्पूर्ण द्वारोंको रोककर मनका हृदयमें निरोध करके और अपने प्राणोंको मस्तकमें स्थापित करके योगधारणामें सम्यक् प्रकारसे स्थित हुआ जो साधक ऊँ इस एक अक्षर ब्रह्मका उच्चारण और मेरा स्मरण करता हुआ शरीरको छोड़कर जाता है, वह परमगतिको प्राप्त होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::323.english_translation: Uttering Om, the one-syllable Brahman, and remembering Me, one who departs while leaving the body attains the supreme state.
bhagwad_gita::323.translation_literal: ॐ (Om) / इति (thus) / एकाक्षरम् (one-syllable) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / व्याहरन् (uttering) / माम् (Me) / अनुस्मरन् (remembering repeatedly) / यः (who) / प्रयाति (departs) / त्यजन् (leaving) / देहम् (the body) / सः (he) / याति (goes) / परमाम् (supreme) / गतिम् (state, destination)
bhagwad_gita::323.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::323.essence: Final remembrance can carry consciousness beyond the body.
bhagwad_gita::323.simple_meaning: A person who leaves the body while remembering Om and Krishna reaches the highest destination.
bhagwad_gita::323.simple_insight: The final moment is not empty; it can carry the mind straight toward liberation.
bhagwad_gita::323.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield, where death feels near and every choice is stripped bare. After explaining the path of disciplined departure, he says that one who leaves the body while uttering Om and remembering him reaches the supreme state.
bhagwad_gita::323.modern_relevance: At a bedside, a family member grips your hand and the room goes quiet. In that stripped-down moment, what the mind holds most deeply matters more than anything spoken before.
bhagwad_gita::323.insight: It shifts attention from panic at death to the quality of awareness carried into the final release.

bhagwad_gita::324.verse_sanskrit: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः । तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::324.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन  अनन्यचित्तवाला जो मनुष्य मेरा नित्यनिरन्तर स्मरण करता है, उस नित्ययुक्त योगीके लिये मैं सुलभ हूँ अर्थात् उसको सुलभतासे प्राप्त हो जाता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::324.english_translation: Arjuna, for the one whose mind is wholly on me and who remembers me constantly, I am easy to reach.
bhagwad_gita::324.translation_literal: अनन्यचेताः (one-pointed in mind) / सततम् (constantly) / यः (who) / माम् (me) / स्मरति (remembers) / नित्यशः (always) / तस्य (for that one) / अहम् (I) / सुलभः (easy to reach) / पार्थ (Arjuna) / नित्ययुक्तस्य (of the ever-joined) / योगिनः (of the yogi)
bhagwad_gita::324.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::324.essence: Constant remembrance makes the divine easy to reach.
bhagwad_gita::324.simple_meaning: A mind that stays focused on Krishna and remembers him continually finds him easy to reach.
bhagwad_gita::324.simple_insight: Devotion does not have to be dramatic. Steady remembering itself creates closeness.
bhagwad_gita::324.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is being taught how to meet death without fear. After describing disciplined leaving of the body, Krishna adds the heart of devotion: one-pointed remembrance makes him easy to attain.
bhagwad_gita::324.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone before a hard conversation, trying to steady yourself. The mind that keeps returning to what matters becomes less scattered and more able to meet the moment.
bhagwad_gita::324.insight: It shifts devotion from occasional feeling to continuous remembrance.

bhagwad_gita::325.verse_sanskrit: मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम् । नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::325.verse_hindi: महात्मालोग मुझे प्राप्त करके दुःखालय और अशाश्वत पुनर्जन्मको प्राप्त नहीं होते क्योंकि वे परमसिद्धिको प्राप्त हो गये हैं अर्थात् उनको परम प्रेमकी प्राप्ति हो गयी है ॥
bhagwad_gita::325.english_translation: Great souls who reach me do not return to this painful, temporary cycle of birth.
bhagwad_gita::325.translation_literal: माम् (me) / उपेत्य (having attained) / पुनर्जन्म (rebirth) / दुःखालयम् (abode of suffering) / अशाश्वतम् (impermanent) / नाप्नुवन्ति (do not attain) / महात्मानः (great souls) / संसिद्धिम् (perfect fulfillment) / परमाम् (supreme) / गताः (having reached)
bhagwad_gita::325.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::325.essence: True arrival ends the need to come back.
bhagwad_gita::325.simple_meaning: Those who reach Krishna do not come back into the painful cycle of birth and death. They have reached the highest fulfillment.
bhagwad_gita::325.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing the deepest arrival ends the need to come back again.
bhagwad_gita::325.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is being taught how to leave the cycle of repeated birth. Krishna says that great souls who reach him do not return to this painful, temporary world because they have reached the highest fulfillment.
bhagwad_gita::325.modern_relevance: You finally get what you thought would fix everything, and it still feels unfinished. This verse points to a deeper arrival, where the old hunger to keep chasing simply stops.
bhagwad_gita::325.insight: It shifts the goal from temporary relief to final release from the cycle of return.

bhagwad_gita::326.verse_sanskrit: आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन । मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::326.verse_hindi: हे अर्जुन  ब्रह्मलोकतक सभी लोक पुनरावर्ती है परन्तु हे कौन्तेय  मुझे प्राप्त होनेपर पुनर्जन्म नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::326.english_translation: All worlds up to Brahma's realm return again, Arjuna. But having reached me, O son of Kunti, there is no rebirth.
bhagwad_gita::326.translation_literal: आब्रह्मभुवनात् (up to the world of Brahma) / लोकाः (worlds) / पुनरावर्तिनः (returning again) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / माम् (me) / उपेत्य (having reached) / तु (but) / कौन्तेय (son of Kunti) / पुनर्जन्म (rebirth) / न (not) / विद्यते (exists)
bhagwad_gita::326.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::326.essence: Even the highest attainments return, but union with Krishna does not.
bhagwad_gita::326.simple_meaning: Even the highest realms are temporary and lead back into rebirth. Only reaching Krishna ends that cycle completely.
bhagwad_gita::326.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that the deepest security is beyond every passing world.
bhagwad_gita::326.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen before war. Krishna has already spoken of remembrance and liberation, and now he sharpens the point: even the highest heavens are not final. Only reaching him ends the cycle of return.
bhagwad_gita::326.modern_relevance: You finally get what you wanted, and the relief lasts a week. Then the old restlessness comes back. This verse points to a security that does not wear out.
bhagwad_gita::326.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing better conditions to seeking what ends the entire cycle of return.

bhagwad_gita::327.verse_sanskrit: सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः । रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::327.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य ब्रह्माके एक हज़ार चतुर्युगीवाले एक दिनको और सहस्त्र चतुर्युगीपर्यन्त एक रातको जानते हैं, वे मनुष्य ब्रह्माके दिन और रातको जाननेवाले हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::327.english_translation: Those who know that Brahma’s day lasts a thousand yugas, and his night lasts a thousand yugas, know day and night truly.
bhagwad_gita::327.translation_literal: सहस्र-युग-पर्यन्तम् (lasting a thousand yugas) / अहः (day) / यत् (which) / ब्रह्मणः (of Brahma) / विदुः (they know) / रात्रिम् (night) / युग-सहस्र-अन्ताम् (ending in a thousand yugas) / ते (they) / अहः-रात्र-विदः (knowers of day and night) / जनाः (people)
bhagwad_gita::327.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::327.essence: Cosmic time reveals how small ordinary urgency is.
bhagwad_gita::327.simple_meaning: Some people understand the vast scale of Brahma's day and night. They can see time on a cosmic scale, not just as ordinary human hours.
bhagwad_gita::327.simple_insight: A wider view can calm the mind that feels trapped by immediate time.
bhagwad_gita::327.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna shaken and the war still paused, Krishna turns from the soul’s freedom to the scale of cosmic time. He describes Brahma’s immense day and night to prepare Arjuna for a teaching about creation, dissolution, and what lies beyond them.
bhagwad_gita::327.modern_relevance: You watch a deadline panic swallow the whole week, then remember the project is one cycle inside a much larger life. The pressure loosens when time stops feeling like a cage.
bhagwad_gita::327.insight: It shifts attention from human-scale urgency to cosmic rhythm, making creation and dissolution feel natural rather than absolute.

bhagwad_gita::328.verse_sanskrit: अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे । रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके ॥
bhagwad_gita::328.verse_hindi: ब्रह्माजीके दिनके आरम्भकालमें अव्यक्त ब्रह्माजीके सूक्ष्मशरीर से सम्पूर्ण प्राणी पैदा होते हैं और ब्रह्माजीकी रातके आरम्भकालमें उसी अव्यक्तमें सम्पूर्ण प्राणी लीन हो जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::328.english_translation: At the start of Brahma's day, all beings arise from the unmanifest; at the start of Brahma's night, they dissolve back into that same unmanifest.
bhagwad_gita::328.translation_literal: अव्यक्तात् (from the unmanifest) / व्यक्तयः (manifest beings) / सर्वाः (all) / प्रभवन्ति (arise) / अहरागमे (at the coming of day) / रात्र्यागमे (at the coming of night) / प्रलीयन्ते (dissolve) / तत्रैव (there alone) / अव्यक्तसंज्ञके (in the one called unmanifest)
bhagwad_gita::328.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::328.essence: Everything formed returns to the unmanifest in time.
bhagwad_gita::328.simple_meaning: All beings emerge from the unmanifest at the beginning of Brahma's day and return to it at the beginning of Brahma's night.
bhagwad_gita::328.simple_insight: What appears solid is temporary. Life keeps rising and dissolving in a larger rhythm.
bhagwad_gita::328.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna is answering Arjuna's fear of endings with a cosmic pattern. He explains that beings rise from the unmanifest when Brahma's day begins and return there when night begins, showing that birth and dissolution are part of a vast cycle.
bhagwad_gita::328.modern_relevance: You watch a relationship, a job, or even your own plans fall apart and feel like everything is ending. This verse zooms out: forms come, forms go, and the deeper pattern continues.
bhagwad_gita::328.insight: It shifts the mind from panic about endings to seeing change as part of a larger cycle.

bhagwad_gita::329.verse_sanskrit: भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते । रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे ॥
bhagwad_gita::329.verse_hindi: हे पार्थ  वही यह प्राणिसमुदाय उत्पन्न होहोकर प्रकृतिके परवश हुआ ब्रह्माके दिनके समय उत्पन्न होता है और ब्रह्माकी रात्रिके समय लीन होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::329.english_translation: O Arjuna, this entire group of beings is born again and again, and is dissolved at the coming of night; at the coming of day, it rises again, helplessly.
bhagwad_gita::329.translation_literal: भूतग्रामः (group of beings) / सः (that same) / एव (indeed) / अयम् (this) / भूत्वा भूत्वा (having become again and again) / प्रलीयते (is dissolved) / रात्र्यागमे (at the coming of night) / अवशः (helplessly, under compulsion) / पार्थ (O Partha) / प्रभवति (arises) / अहरागमे (at the coming of day)
bhagwad_gita::329.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::329.essence: All formed things return and rise again under nature’s compulsion.
bhagwad_gita::329.simple_meaning: All living beings keep arising and dissolving again and again. They do so under the pull of nature, not by choice.
bhagwad_gita::329.simple_insight: You can stop mistaking repeated change for permanence.
bhagwad_gita::329.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen by grief while Krishna explains the rhythm behind all created life. After describing cosmic day and night, Krishna says every being rises and falls in that cycle under nature’s compulsion.
bhagwad_gita::329.modern_relevance: You build a life, a role, a relationship, then watch it shift overnight. What felt fixed was always moving through a larger rhythm you do not control.
bhagwad_gita::329.insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to temporary forms toward seeing their repeated rising and falling as natural.

bhagwad_gita::330.verse_sanskrit: परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः । यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति ॥
bhagwad_gita::330.verse_hindi: परन्तु उस अव्यक्त ब्रह्माजीके सूक्ष्मशरीर से अन्य अनादि सर्वश्रेष्ठ भावरूप जो अव्यक्त है, उसका सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके नष्ट होनेपर भी नाश नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::330.english_translation: Beyond that unmanifest is another, eternal unmanifest. Even when all beings perish, it does not perish.
bhagwad_gita::330.translation_literal: परस्तस्मात् (beyond that) / तु (but) / भावः (state/being) / अन्यः (another) / अव्यक्तः (unmanifest) / अव्यक्तात् (than the unmanifest) / सनातनः (eternal) / यः (which) / सः (that) / सर्वेषु (in all) / भूतेषु (beings) / नश्यत्सु (when perishing) / न (not) / विनश्यति (perishes)
bhagwad_gita::330.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::330.essence: What is deepest in reality cannot be destroyed by any ending.
bhagwad_gita::330.simple_meaning: There is something beyond the visible world that is eternal and cannot be destroyed, even when all living things disappear.
bhagwad_gita::330.simple_insight: The deepest reality is not vulnerable to collapse, so loss does not have the final word.
bhagwad_gita::330.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna shaken and the armies waiting, Krishna keeps tracing reality beyond birth and death. After describing how beings arise and dissolve, he points to what remains when every form vanishes: the eternal unmanifest.
bhagwad_gita::330.modern_relevance: You watch a relationship, a career, or a plan fall apart and feel the floor disappear. This verse says the deepest ground of reality is still there, untouched by the collapse.
bhagwad_gita::330.insight: It shifts attention from what changes and disappears to what remains present through every change.

bhagwad_gita::331.verse_sanskrit: अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम् । यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
bhagwad_gita::331.verse_hindi: उसीको अव्यक्त और अक्षर कहा गया है और उसीको परमगति कहा गया है तथा जिसको प्राप्त होनेपर जीव फिर लौटकर नहीं आते, वह मेरा परमधाम है ॥
bhagwad_gita::331.english_translation: That is called the unmanifest and the imperishable. It is the highest goal. Having reached it, one does not return. It is my supreme abode.
bhagwad_gita::331.translation_literal: अव्यक्तः (unmanifest) / अक्षरः (imperishable) / इति (thus) / उक्तः (called) / तम् (that) / आहुः (they call) / परमाम् (highest) / गतिम् (goal) / यम् (which) / प्राप्य (having attained) / न (not) / निवर्तन्ते (return) / तत् (that) / धाम (abode) / परमम् (supreme) / मम (my)
bhagwad_gita::331.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::331.essence: The highest arrival is beyond return.
bhagwad_gita::331.simple_meaning: The highest reality is beyond change and form. Whoever reaches it does not come back to the cycle of repeated return.
bhagwad_gita::331.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that the deepest destination is permanent, not temporary.
bhagwad_gita::331.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains what lies beyond all changing worlds. After describing the unmanifest and imperishable, Krishna names it his supreme abode: the final destination from which no one returns.
bhagwad_gita::331.modern_relevance: You finally choose the harder right over the easier wrong, and something in you knows there is no going back. This verse speaks to that irreversible threshold.
bhagwad_gita::331.insight: It shifts the mind from temporary achievement to final release from return.

bhagwad_gita::332.verse_sanskrit: पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया । यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::332.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन अर्जुन  सम्पूर्ण प्राणी जिसके अन्तर्गत हैं और जिससे यह सम्पूर्ण संसार व्याप्त है, वह परम पुरुष परमात्मा तो अनन्यभक्तिसे प्राप्त होनेयोग्य है ॥
bhagwad_gita::332.english_translation: O Arjuna, the supreme person is reached through undivided devotion. All beings dwell within that being, and this entire world is pervaded by that being.
bhagwad_gita::332.translation_literal: पुरुषः (person) / सः (that) / परः (supreme) / पार्थ (O Partha) / भक्त्या (through devotion) / लभ्यः (is attainable) / तु (indeed) / अनन्यया (undivided) / यस्य (whose) / अन्तःस्थानि (situated within) / भूतानि (beings) / येन (by whom) / सर्वम् (all) / इदम् (this) / ततम् (pervaded)
bhagwad_gita::332.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::332.essence: Undivided devotion reaches the one presence that holds all beings.
bhagwad_gita::332.simple_meaning: The supreme person is reached through single-pointed devotion. That presence holds all beings within it and fills the whole world.
bhagwad_gita::332.simple_insight: You are not reaching something distant; you are turning toward the presence already holding everything together.
bhagwad_gita::332.detailed_meaning: Arjuna stands shaken on the battlefield, and Krishna has just described the imperishable highest reality. Now he adds the heart of the path: that supreme person is not reached by divided effort, but by undivided devotion, because every being already rests within that presence.
bhagwad_gita::332.modern_relevance: You sit in your car after a painful phone call, knowing you must answer honestly. The courage comes easier when you remember the person you face is not separate from the whole web of life.
bhagwad_gita::332.insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to direct recognition of shared presence in all beings.

bhagwad_gita::333.verse_sanskrit: यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः । प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ ॥
bhagwad_gita::333.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  जिस काल अर्थात् मार्गमें शरीर छोड़कर गये हुए योगी अनावृत्तिको प्राप्त होते हैं अर्थात् पीछे लौटकर नहीं आते और जिस मार्गमें गये हुए आवृत्तिको प्राप्त होते हैं अर्थात् पीछे लौटकर आते हैं, उस कालको अर्थात् दोनों मार्गोंको मैं कहूँगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::333.english_translation: I will tell you of the time when yogis do not return, and the time when they do, O best of the Bharatas.
bhagwad_gita::333.translation_literal: यत्र (in which) / काले (time) / तु (indeed) / अनावृत्तिम् (non-return) / आवृत्तिम् (return) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / योगिनः (yogis) / प्रयाताः (having departed) / यान्ति (go) / तम् (that) / कालम् (time) / वक्ष्यामि (I will speak) / भरतर्षभ (O best of the Bharatas)
bhagwad_gita::333.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::333.essence: Not every departure leads the same way; some paths return you, others do not.
bhagwad_gita::333.simple_meaning: Krishna says he will explain which departing moments lead to no return and which lead back into return.
bhagwad_gita::333.simple_insight: Some departures open outward; others loop back. Timing matters because direction matters.
bhagwad_gita::333.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Arjuna still stands frozen while Krishna continues the teaching on death and release. After speaking of the imperishable and the supreme being, Krishna now turns to the path of departure itself, promising to explain which way leads beyond return.
bhagwad_gita::333.modern_relevance: You leave a relationship, a job, or a habit and feel the difference immediately: one choice frees you, another pulls you back into the same cycle. This verse points to that hidden direction.
bhagwad_gita::333.insight: It shifts attention from the act of leaving to the quality of the path being taken.

bhagwad_gita::334.verse_sanskrit: अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् । तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::334.verse_hindi: जिस मार्गमें प्रकाशस्वरूप अग्निका अधिपति देवता, दिनका अधिपति देवता, शुक्लपक्षका अधिपति देवता, और छः महीनोंवाले उत्तरायणका अधिपति देवता है, शरीर छोड़कर उस मार्गसे गये हुए ब्रह्मवेत्ता पुरुष पहले ब्रह्मलोकको प्राप्त होकर पीछे ब्रह्माजीके साथ ब्रह्मको प्राप्त हो जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::334.english_translation: Fire, daylight, the bright fortnight, and the six months of the northward course: those who depart then, knowing the supreme reality, go to the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::334.translation_literal: अग्निः (fire) / ज्योतिः (light) / अहः (day) / शुक्लः (bright) / षण्मासा (six months) / उत्तरायणम् (northward course) / तत्र (there) / प्रयाताः (having departed) / गच्छन्ति (go) / ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / ब्रह्मविदः (knowers of the supreme reality) / जनाः (people)
bhagwad_gita::334.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::334.essence: The final passage opens for those who know the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::334.simple_meaning: Those who leave the body during an auspicious path of light and know the supreme reality reach that supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::334.simple_insight: There is calm in knowing that awareness and timing matter more than fear.
bhagwad_gita::334.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before the war. Krishna turns from battle duty to the final question: how the knower of the supreme reality passes beyond return. This verse names the bright path of departure.
bhagwad_gita::334.modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed, signing a document you never wanted to sign. The mind wants certainty, but the teaching points to the quality of consciousness at the threshold, not the panic around it.
bhagwad_gita::334.insight: It shifts attention from fear of death to the clarity with which one meets the final moment.

bhagwad_gita::335.verse_sanskrit: धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् । तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते ॥
bhagwad_gita::335.verse_hindi: जिस मार्गमें धूमका अधिपति देवता, रात्रिका अधिपति देवता, कृष्णपक्षका अधिपति देवता और छः महीनोंवाले दक्षिणायनका अधिपति देवता है, शरीर छोड़कर उस मार्गसे गया हुआ योगी सकाम मनुष्य चन्द्रमाकी ज्योतिको प्राप्त होकर लौट आता है अर्थात् जन्ममरणको प्राप्त होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::335.english_translation: In the path ruled by smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the six months of the southern course, the yogi who departs there returns after reaching the moon's light.
bhagwad_gita::335.translation_literal: धूमः (smoke) / रात्रिः (night) / तथा (and) / कृष्णः (the dark fortnight) / षण्मासा (six months) / दक्षिणायनम् (the southern course) / तत्र (there) / चान्द्रमसम् (lunar) / ज्योतिः (light) / योगी (the yogi) / प्राप्य (having reached) / निवर्तते (returns)
bhagwad_gita::335.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::335.essence: Some routes only delay return; they do not end the cycle.
bhagwad_gita::335.simple_meaning: A person who departs through this darker path reaches a lunar realm and returns again to mortal life.
bhagwad_gita::335.simple_insight: Not every departure leads beyond return. Some paths circle back into the same struggle.
bhagwad_gita::335.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on Kurukshetra, explaining the two post-death courses. After naming the bright path that leads beyond return, he names the darker path: one that ends in return. The point is to distinguish release from recurrence.
bhagwad_gita::335.modern_relevance: You choose what feels easier because it is familiar, then wonder why you are back in the same pattern again. Some choices carry you forward; others quietly send you in circles.
bhagwad_gita::335.insight: It shifts attention from vague spirituality to seeing the difference between a path that frees and a path that repeats.

bhagwad_gita::336.verse_sanskrit: शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते । एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययाऽऽवर्तते पुनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::336.verse_hindi: क्योंकि शुक्ल और कृष्ण  ये दोनों गतियाँ अनादिकालसे जगत्प्राणिमात्र के साथ सम्बन्ध रखनेवाली मानी गई हैं ।  इनमेंसे एक गतिमें जानेवालेको लौटना नहीं पड़ता और दूसरी गतिमें जानेवालेको लौटना पड़ता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::336.english_translation: The bright and the dark are the two eternal paths of the world. One leads to non-return; the other brings return again.
bhagwad_gita::336.translation_literal: शुक्लकृष्णे (the bright and the dark) / गती (paths) / हि (indeed) / एते (these) / जगतः (of the world) / शाश्वते (eternal) / मते (are held to be) । / एकया (by one) / याति (goes) / अनावृत्तिम् (to non-return) / अन्यया (by the other) / आवर्तते (returns) / पुनः (again)
bhagwad_gita::336.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::336.essence: Some choices free you from the cycle; others send you back into it.
bhagwad_gita::336.simple_meaning: Two eternal paths exist. One leads beyond repeated return, and the other brings a person back again.
bhagwad_gita::336.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing not every road leads to the same loop.
bhagwad_gita::336.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Krishna has begun explaining the last journey of life to Arjuna. After naming the bright and dark routes, he now states the larger rule: one path ends rebirth, the other returns the traveler again.
bhagwad_gita::336.modern_relevance: You are standing at a crossroads after a breakup, a resignation letter in hand. One choice ends the old cycle; the other sends you back into it with a new name.
bhagwad_gita::336.insight: It shifts attention from surface success to the deeper direction a life is moving in.

bhagwad_gita::337.verse_sanskrit: नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन । तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन ॥
bhagwad_gita::337.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन  इन दोनों मार्गोंको जाननेवाला कोई भी योगी मोहित नहीं होता ।  अतः हे अर्जुन  तू सब समयमें योगयुक्त हो जा ॥
bhagwad_gita::337.english_translation: O Arjuna, the yogi who knows these two paths is never deluded. Therefore, remain steadfast in yoga at all times.
bhagwad_gita::337.translation_literal: नैते (these not) / सृती (two paths) / पार्थ (O Partha) / जानन् (knowing) / योगी (the yogi) / मुह्यति (is deluded) / कश्चन (anyone) / तस्मात् (therefore) / सर्वेषु (in all) / कालेषु (times) / योगयुक्तः (joined in yoga) / भव (be) / अर्जुन (O Arjuna)
bhagwad_gita::337.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::337.essence: Understanding the two paths keeps the mind unshaken.
bhagwad_gita::337.simple_meaning: A person who understands these two routes after death is not confused. Krishna tells Arjuna to stay connected to yoga at all times.
bhagwad_gita::337.simple_insight: Knowing what is real steadies you when choices feel final.
bhagwad_gita::337.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna has just explained the bright and dark routes after death. Arjuna is frozen between action and renunciation, so Krishna closes the lesson: understanding removes confusion, and steady yoga keeps the mind clear.
bhagwad_gita::337.modern_relevance: You are standing in a hospital corridor after hearing two very different medical opinions. Panic wants to decide for you. Clear understanding, held calmly, keeps you from being dragged by fear.
bhagwad_gita::337.insight: It shifts you from reactive confusion to steady awareness, even when the stakes feel absolute.

bhagwad_gita::338.verse_sanskrit: वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैवदानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम् । अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वायोगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::338.verse_hindi: योगी इसको शुक्ल और कृष्णमार्गके रहस्यको जानकर वेदोंमें, यज्ञोंमें, तपोंमें तथा दानमें जोजो पुण्यफल कहे गये हैं, उन सभी पुण्यफलोंका अतिक्रमण कर जाता है और आदिस्थान परमात्माको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::338.english_translation: Knowing the two paths, the yogi goes beyond all the merits declared in the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities, and gifts, and reaches the primal supreme abode.
bhagwad_gita::338.translation_literal: वेदेषु (in the Vedas) / यज्ञेषु (in sacrifices) / तपःसु (in austerities) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / दानेषु (in gifts) / यत् (which) / पुण्यफलम् (merit-fruit) / प्रदिष्टम् (is declared) / अत्येति (goes beyond) / तत् (that) / सर्वम् (all) / इदम् (this) / विदित्वा (having known) / योगी (the yogi) / परम् (supreme) / स्थानम् (abode) / उपैति (attains) / च (and) / आद्यम् (primordial)
bhagwad_gita::338.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::338.essence: Knowing the way beyond rewards leads to the highest home.
bhagwad_gita::338.simple_meaning: Knowing the two paths frees a yogi from chasing ritual rewards. That understanding leads beyond all promised merit and into the highest state.
bhagwad_gita::338.simple_insight: Relief comes when spiritual practice stops being a transaction and becomes a doorway.
bhagwad_gita::338.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen between action and withdrawal. Krishna closes this chapter by saying that the one who truly knows the two courses after death is no longer bound by ritual merit, but reaches the primal supreme abode.
bhagwad_gita::338.modern_relevance: You finish a long ritual, a donation, or a hard discipline and still feel hungry for approval. This verse cuts through that bargain: real understanding is not about collecting spiritual points.
bhagwad_gita::338.insight: It shifts the mind from earning merit to seeing beyond all reward-based practice.

bhagwad_gita::339.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचइदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे । ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥
bhagwad_gita::339.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  यह अत्यन्त गोपनीय विज्ञानसहित ज्ञान दोषदृष्टिरहित तेरे लिये तो मैं फिर अच्छी तरहसे कहूँगा, जिसको जानकर तू अशुभसे अर्थात् जन्ममरणरूप संसारसे मुक्त हो जायगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::339.english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: I will now tell you this most secret knowledge, joined with direct realization, to you who are not envious. Knowing it, you will be freed from all that is harmful.
bhagwad_gita::339.translation_literal: श्री भगवान् (the Blessed Lord) / उवाच (said) / इदम् (this) / तु (indeed) / ते (to you) / गुह्यतमम् (most secret) / प्रवक्ष्यामि (I will explain) / अनसूयवे (to one without envy) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / विज्ञानसहितम् (together with direct realization) / यत् (which) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / मोक्ष्यसे (you will be freed) / अशुभात् (from what is harmful)
bhagwad_gita::339.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::339.essence: The deepest truth frees only a heart that does not resist it.
bhagwad_gita::339.simple_meaning: Krishna promises to share the deepest teaching with Arjuna because Arjuna is not hostile to it. Understanding this knowledge fully will free him from suffering and the cycle of rebirth.
bhagwad_gita::339.simple_insight: Real understanding opens only in a heart that is open, not defensive.
bhagwad_gita::339.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while two armies wait. Krishna begins Chapter 9 by promising the most secret teaching, but only to a student free from envy. This verse opens the doorway to the royal knowledge that follows.
bhagwad_gita::339.modern_relevance: You finally ask for honest feedback after months of avoiding it. The answer stings less than your resistance does, because openness lets truth actually reach you.
bhagwad_gita::339.insight: It shifts the mind from defensiveness to receptivity, making insight possible.

bhagwad_gita::340.verse_sanskrit: राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् । प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::340.verse_hindi: यह सम्पूर्ण विद्याओंका और सम्पूर्ण गोपनीयोंका राजा है ।  यह अति पवित्र तथा अतिश्रेष्ठ है और इसका फल भी प्रत्यक्ष है ।  यह धर्ममय है, अविनाशी है और करनेमें बहुत सुगम है अर्थात् इसको प्राप्त करना बहुत सुगम है ॥
bhagwad_gita::340.english_translation: This is the king of all knowledge, the king of all secrets. It is supremely pure, directly knowable, aligned with dharma, easy to practice, and imperishable.
bhagwad_gita::340.translation_literal: राजविद्या (king of knowledge) / राजगुह्यं (king of secrets) / पवित्रम् (pure) / इदम् (this) / उत्तमम् (supreme) / प्रत्यक्ष-अवगमम् (directly knowable) / धर्म्यम् (aligned with dharma) / सुसुखम् (very easy) / कर्तुम् (to do) / अव्ययम् (imperishable)
bhagwad_gita::340.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::340.essence: The highest truth is both profound and simple to live.
bhagwad_gita::340.simple_meaning: This teaching is called the highest knowledge because it is pure, direct, righteous, easy to practice, and never lost.
bhagwad_gita::340.simple_insight: The deepest truth does not make life harder; it makes life clearer and lighter.
bhagwad_gita::340.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen and Krishna begins revealing a teaching greater than ordinary wisdom. He names this knowledge as the highest, most secret, pure, direct, and practical path that can actually be lived.
bhagwad_gita::340.modern_relevance: You are standing at a hospital corridor, waiting for a hard diagnosis. The clearest truth is not always the most complicated one; sometimes it is the one you can actually live by.
bhagwad_gita::340.insight: It shifts the mind from treating spiritual understanding as abstract to seeing it as immediate and usable.

bhagwad_gita::341.verse_sanskrit: अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप । अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि ॥
bhagwad_gita::341.verse_hindi: हे परंतप इस धर्मकी महिमापर श्रद्धा न रखनेवाले मनुष्य मेरे प्राप्त न होकर मृत्युरूप संसारके मार्गमें लौटते रहते हैं अर्थात् बारबार जन्मतेमरते रहते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::341.english_translation: O conqueror of foes, people without trust in this dharma do not reach Me and keep returning on the path of repeated death and rebirth.
bhagwad_gita::341.translation_literal: अश्रद्दधानाः (without trust) / पुरुषाः (people) / धर्मस्य (of dharma) / अस्य (of this) / परन्तप (O conqueror of foes) / अप्राप्य (not reaching) / माम् (Me) / निवर्तन्ते (return) / मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि (on the path of the cycle of death and rebirth)
bhagwad_gita::341.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::341.essence: Without trust, the highest teaching cannot carry you beyond repetition.
bhagwad_gita::341.simple_meaning: People who lack trust in this sacred teaching do not reach Krishna and remain trapped in repeated birth and death.
bhagwad_gita::341.simple_insight: Trust is not decoration here; it is the doorway out of repetition.
bhagwad_gita::341.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, where a whole life is being decided in one frozen moment. After praising this teaching as the highest and purest knowledge, he warns that disbelief keeps a person turning in the cycle of death and rebirth instead of reaching him.
bhagwad_gita::341.modern_relevance: You stand at the edge of a hard choice and keep asking for one more guarantee, one more sign. Doubt can become a loop that sends you back to the same fear instead of forward into action.
bhagwad_gita::341.insight: It shifts the mind from treating trust as optional to seeing it as the condition for transformation.

bhagwad_gita::342.verse_sanskrit: मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना । मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः ॥
bhagwad_gita::342.verse_hindi: यह सब संसार मेरे निराकार स्वरूपसे व्याप्त है ।  सम्पूर्ण प्राणी मेरेमें स्थित हैं परन्तु मैं उनमें स्थित नहीं हूँ तथा वे प्राणी भी मुझ में स्थित नहीं हैं  मेरे इस ईश्वरसम्बन्धी योगसामर्थ्य को देख  सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंको उत्पन्न करनेवाला और उनका धारण, भरणपोषण करनेवाला मेरा स्वरूप उन प्राणियोंमें स्थित नहीं है ॥
bhagwad_gita::342.english_translation: All this universe is pervaded by my unmanifest form. All beings dwell in me, but I do not dwell in them.
bhagwad_gita::342.translation_literal: मया (by me) / ततम् (pervaded) / इदम् (this) / सर्वम् (all) / जगत् (world) / अव्यक्त-मूर्तिना (by unmanifest form) / मत्-स्थानि (situated in me) / सर्व-भूतानि (all beings) / न (not) / च (and) / अहम् (I) / तेषु (in them) / अवस्थितः (situated)
bhagwad_gita::342.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::342.essence: The supreme reality holds everything without being held by anything.
bhagwad_gita::342.simple_meaning: Krishna says the whole universe is sustained by his unseen presence. Every being exists within him, yet he is not limited by any being.
bhagwad_gita::342.simple_insight: You can belong to everything without being trapped inside it.
bhagwad_gita::342.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, as Arjuna stands frozen before battle, Krishna begins revealing his deeper nature. He is not just a charioteer or teacher; he is the unseen ground holding every being, while remaining beyond all that appears.
bhagwad_gita::342.modern_relevance: You sit in a crowded room after a breakup, feeling swallowed by everyone else's opinions. This verse reminds you that presence can surround everything without being reduced by it.
bhagwad_gita::342.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing the divine as one object among many to seeing all objects as resting in the divine.

bhagwad_gita::343.verse_sanskrit: न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् । भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::343.verse_hindi: यह सब संसार मेरे निराकार स्वरूपसे व्याप्त है ।  सम्पूर्ण प्राणी मुझ में स्थित हैं परन्तु मैं उनमें स्थित नहीं हूँ तथा वे प्राणी भी मेरेमें स्थित नहीं हैं  मेरे इस ईश्वरसम्बन्धी योगसामर्थ्य को देख  सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंको उत्पन्न करनेवाला और उनका धारण, भरणपोषण करनेवाला मेरा स्वरूप उन प्राणियोंमें स्थित नहीं है ॥
bhagwad_gita::343.english_translation: Behold My divine power: beings are not in Me, and yet I sustain all beings.
bhagwad_gita::343.translation_literal: न / च (not) / मत्स्थानि (situated in Me) / भूतानि (beings) / पश्य (behold) / मे (My) / योगम् (powerful union) / ऐश्वरम् (divine, sovereign) / भूतभृत् (sustainer of beings) / न (not) / च (and not) / भूतस्थः (situated in beings) / मम (My) / आत्मा (self) / भूतभावनः (the source and nourisher of beings)
bhagwad_gita::343.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::343.essence: The supreme reality sustains all beings without being contained by them.
bhagwad_gita::343.simple_meaning: Krishna says that all beings are sustained by him, yet he is not contained within them. He asks Arjuna to see this divine power.
bhagwad_gita::343.simple_insight: You can be the source of everything without being trapped inside what you sustain.
bhagwad_gita::343.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is still receiving Krishna’s teaching about how the supreme reality pervades the world. Krishna now sharpens the point: all beings depend on him, yet he remains untouched by them. This verse deepens the mystery of divine presence.
bhagwad_gita::343.modern_relevance: You keep a family together, answer every message, and hold everything in place — yet no one sees how untouched you remain beneath it all.
bhagwad_gita::343.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing presence as entanglement to seeing it as sustaining without being confined.

bhagwad_gita::344.verse_sanskrit: यथाऽऽकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् । तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय ॥
bhagwad_gita::344.verse_hindi: जैसे सब जगह विचरनेवाली महान् वायु नित्य ही आकाशमें स्थित रहती है, ऐसे ही सम्पूर्ण प्राणी मुझमें ही स्थित रहते हैं  ऐसा तुम मान लो ॥
bhagwad_gita::344.english_translation: As the great wind, moving everywhere, always rests in space, so all beings rest in Me.
bhagwad_gita::344.translation_literal: यथा (just as) / आकाश-स्थितः (स्थित in space) / नित्यम् (always) / वायुः (wind) / सर्वत्र-गः (moving everywhere) / महान् (great) / तथा (so) / सर्वाणि (all) / भूतानि (beings) / मत्-स्थानि (resting in Me) / इति (thus) / उपधारय (understand)
bhagwad_gita::344.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::344.essence: What moves everywhere still rests in the divine.
bhagwad_gita::344.simple_meaning: All living beings exist within Krishna just as wind moves within space. The verse asks Arjuna to hold this vision of divine presence everywhere.
bhagwad_gita::344.simple_insight: You are not separate from the whole. Even movement and change happen within a larger presence.
bhagwad_gita::344.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen by grief and doubt. Krishna has already said that all beings are within his presence; now he gives a vivid image to make that truth feel real: every creature rests in him as wind rests in space.
bhagwad_gita::344.modern_relevance: You sit alone after a hard conversation, replaying every word, feeling cut off from everyone. This verse reminds you that isolation is not the deepest reality; life is held inside something larger.
bhagwad_gita::344.insight: It shifts the mind from scattered separation to a felt sense of shared belonging.

bhagwad_gita::345.verse_sanskrit: सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम् । कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::345.verse_hindi: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  कल्पोंका क्षय होनेपर सम्पूर्ण प्राणी मेरी प्रकृतिको प्राप्त होते हैं और कल्पोंके आदिमें मैं फिर उनकी रचना करता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::345.english_translation: O son of Kunti, at the end of a cosmic cycle all beings enter my nature; at its beginning, I send them forth again.
bhagwad_gita::345.translation_literal: सर्वभूतानि (all beings) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / प्रकृतिं (nature) / यान्ति (go to) / मामिकाम् (my) / कल्पक्षये (at the end of a cosmic cycle) / पुनः (again) / तानि (them) / कल्पादौ (at the beginning of a cosmic cycle) / विसृजामि (I send forth) / अहम् (I)
bhagwad_gita::345.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::345.essence: What seems like ending is only a return before another beginning.
bhagwad_gita::345.simple_meaning: At the end of a vast cycle, every being dissolves back into Krishna's nature. When the next cycle begins, he brings them forth again.
bhagwad_gita::345.simple_insight: You are held inside a larger order, even when everything seems to end.
bhagwad_gita::345.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is frozen by the scale of loss. Krishna widens the frame beyond one war: worlds themselves rise and dissolve in cycles, and every being is gathered back and sent out again. That cosmic rhythm steadies Arjuna's panic.
bhagwad_gita::345.modern_relevance: A project collapses, a relationship ends, a role disappears — and it feels final. This verse pulls the mind back from that panic and shows that endings belong to a larger cycle, not absolute loss.
bhagwad_gita::345.insight: It shifts attention from personal control to the larger rhythm that carries all change.

bhagwad_gita::346.verse_sanskrit: प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः । भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात् ॥
bhagwad_gita::346.verse_hindi: प्रकृतिके वशमें होनेसे परतन्त्र हुए इस सम्पूर्ण प्राणिसमुदायको मैं कल्पोंके आदिमें अपनी प्रकृतिको वशमें करके बारबार रचता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::346.english_translation: Taking hold of my own nature, I repeatedly create this entire multitude of beings, helpless under the sway of nature.
bhagwad_gita::346.translation_literal: प्रकृतिम् (nature) / स्वाम् (my own) / अवष्टभ्य (taking hold of) / विसृजामि (I create, send forth) / पुनः पुनः (again and again) / भूतग्रामम् (multitude of beings) / इमम् (this) / कृत्स्नम् (entire) / अवशम् (helpless, not independent) / प्रकृतेः (of nature) / वशात् (under the sway)
bhagwad_gita::346.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::346.essence: Life unfolds through a power larger than individual will.
bhagwad_gita::346.simple_meaning: Krishna says he keeps bringing forth the whole world again and again through his own nature, while beings remain bound by nature’s power.
bhagwad_gita::346.simple_insight: The world is not random. A deeper order is moving through every cycle of creation.
bhagwad_gita::346.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna widens the lens: creation itself moves in cycles, and beings are carried by nature’s force. This verse explains how the world keeps unfolding under a power greater than individual control.
bhagwad_gita::346.modern_relevance: You watch the same family pattern repeat in a new generation and feel helpless to stop it. This verse points to a larger force shaping the cycle, even when you cannot yet see it clearly.
bhagwad_gita::346.insight: It shifts attention from personal control to the larger forces that shape repeated patterns.

bhagwad_gita::347.verse_sanskrit: न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय । उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु ॥
bhagwad_gita::347.verse_hindi: हे धनञ्जय  उन सृष्टिरचना आदि कर्मोंमें अनासक्त और उदासीनकी तरह रहते हुए मेरेको वे कर्म नहीं बाँधते ॥
bhagwad_gita::347.english_translation: Those actions of creation do not bind me, Dhananjaya, because I remain detached and indifferent to them.
bhagwad_gita::347.translation_literal: न च (and not) / माम् (me) / तानि (those) / कर्माणि (actions) / निबध्नन्ति (bind) / धनञ्जय (Dhananjaya) / उदासीनवत् (like one indifferent) / आसीनम् (remaining) / असक्तम् (unattached) / तेषु (in those) / कर्मसु (actions)
bhagwad_gita::347.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::347.essence: Action can continue without leaving a chain behind.
bhagwad_gita::347.simple_meaning: Creation and world-order do not bind Krishna, because he remains unattached and unconcerned while they happen.
bhagwad_gita::347.simple_insight: You can act in the world without being trapped by it.
bhagwad_gita::347.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna hears Krishna explain how the cosmos itself unfolds. After describing repeated creation and dissolution, Krishna adds that these actions do not bind him, because he stands apart from them, unattached while they continue.
bhagwad_gita::347.modern_relevance: You send the message, make the hard call, and still do not let the role swallow you. The action happens; your identity does not have to cling to it.
bhagwad_gita::347.insight: It shifts the mind from ownership of action to freedom within action.

bhagwad_gita::348.verse_sanskrit: मयाऽध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम् । हेतुनाऽनेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते ॥
bhagwad_gita::348.verse_hindi: प्रकृति मेरी अध्यक्षतामें सम्पूर्ण चराचर जगत् को रचती है ।  हे कुन्तीनन्दन  इसी हेतुसे जगत् का विविध प्रकारसे परिवर्तन होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::348.english_translation: Nature, under my supervision, brings forth all moving and unmoving beings. Because of this, the world keeps changing, O son of Kunti.
bhagwad_gita::348.translation_literal: मया (by me) / अध्यक्षेण (as overseer) / प्रकृतिः (nature) / सूयते (gives birth, brings forth) / सचराचरम् (the moving and the unmoving) / हेतुना (because, by reason) / अनेन (of this) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / जगत् (the world) / विपरिवर्तते (keeps turning, keeps changing)
bhagwad_gita::348.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::348.essence: Change is not chaotic; it unfolds within a higher order.
bhagwad_gita::348.simple_meaning: All changing life unfolds under Krishna's supervision. The world keeps transforming because nature works through his oversight.
bhagwad_gita::348.simple_insight: You can stop feeling abandoned by change. What shifts is not random; it still rests within a larger order.
bhagwad_gita::348.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Krishna keeps answering Arjuna's deepest confusion. After explaining creation and his detachment from it, he now says that nature itself brings forth the whole moving and unmoving world under his supervision, and that this is why everything keeps changing.
bhagwad_gita::348.modern_relevance: A plan collapses, a relationship changes, or a job disappears overnight, and it feels like chaos. This verse says the turning of events is not outside the larger order you cannot yet see.
bhagwad_gita::348.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing change as random to seeing it as governed by a deeper intelligence.

bhagwad_gita::349.verse_sanskrit: अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम् । परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::349.verse_hindi: मूर्खलोग मेरे सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके महान् ईश्वररूप परमभावको न जानते हुए मुझे मनुष्यशरीरके आश्रित मानकर अर्थात् साधारण मनुष्य मानकर मेरी अवज्ञा करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::349.english_translation: Fools despise Me when I dwell in a human form, not knowing My higher nature as the great Lord of all beings.
bhagwad_gita::349.translation_literal: अवजानन्ति (despise) / माम् (Me) / मूढाः (the deluded) / मानुषीम् (human) / तनुम् (form) / आश्रितम् (having taken refuge in) / परम् (higher) / भावम् (nature) / अजानन्तः (not knowing) / मम (My) / भूतमहेश्वरम् (great Lord of beings)
bhagwad_gita::349.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::349.essence: Ordinary appearance can hide the highest reality.
bhagwad_gita::349.simple_meaning: People mock Krishna because they see only a human body and miss his higher nature as the lord of all beings.
bhagwad_gita::349.simple_insight: Respect can fail when we judge by appearance alone. Seeing more deeply changes everything.
bhagwad_gita::349.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna keeps teaching Arjuna while the armies wait. He explains why some people dismiss him: they see only a human body and miss his vast nature as ruler of all beings. This verse answers that misunderstanding directly.
bhagwad_gita::349.modern_relevance: You meet someone in a plain shirt and underestimate them before they speak. Or you dismiss a quiet teacher, a grieving parent, or a soft-spoken leader because the surface seems ordinary.
bhagwad_gita::349.insight: It shifts attention from outer appearance to the deeper reality behind a person.

bhagwad_gita::350.verse_sanskrit: मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः । राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::350.verse_hindi: जिनकी सब आशाएँ व्यर्थ होती हैं, सब शुभकर्म व्यर्थ होते हैं और सब ज्ञान व्यर्थ होते हैं अर्थात् जिनकी आशाएँ, कर्म और ज्ञान सत्फल देनेवाले नहीं होते, ऐसे अविवेकी मनुष्य आसुरी, राक्षसी और मोहिनी फकृतिका आश्रय लेते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::350.english_translation: Those whose hopes, actions, and understanding are all wasted, confused minds take shelter in deluding, demonic, and shadowy nature.
bhagwad_gita::350.translation_literal: मोघाशाः (wasted hopes) / मोघकर्माणः (wasted actions) / मोघज्ञाः (wasted understanding) / विचेतसः (confused-minded) / राक्षसीम् (demonic) / आसुरीम् (of ego and shadow) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / प्रकृतिम् (nature) / मोहिनीम् (deluding) / श्रिताः (having taken refuge in)
bhagwad_gita::350.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::350.essence: A confused mind turns even hope, effort, and learning into waste.
bhagwad_gita::350.simple_meaning: Confused people end up leaning on forces that distort their judgment. Their hopes, actions, and understanding do not bear fruit because they are guided by delusion.
bhagwad_gita::350.simple_insight: Confusion does not stay private; it shapes the kind of life you build.
bhagwad_gita::350.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna explains why some people fail to recognise him. Arjuna is still shaken, and Krishna shows the pattern behind that blindness: a confused mind turns toward delusion, and even hope, action, and learning become wasted.
bhagwad_gita::350.modern_relevance: You keep checking the same toxic chat thread, hoping for clarity, and leave more tangled than before. Delusion feeds on attention and makes every effort misfire.
bhagwad_gita::350.insight: It shifts attention from results alone to the inner quality of the mind guiding them.

bhagwad_gita::351.verse_sanskrit: महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः । भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::351.verse_hindi: परन्तु हे पृथानन्दन  दैवी प्रकृतिके आश्रित अनन्यमनवाले महात्मालोग मुझे सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंका आदि और अविनाशी समझकर मेरा भजन करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::351.english_translation: But, Arjuna, the great-minded ones, relying on the divine nature, worship Me with one-pointed minds, knowing Me as the unborn and imperishable source of all beings.
bhagwad_gita::351.translation_literal: महात्मानः (great-minded ones) / तु (but) / माम् (Me) / पार्थ (Arjuna) / दैवीं प्रकृतिम् (divine nature) / आश्रिताः (having taken refuge in) / भजन्ति (worship) / अनन्य-मनसः (with minds fixed on nothing else) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / भूत-आदिम् (the source of beings) / अव्ययम् (imperishable)
bhagwad_gita::351.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::351.essence: True devotion begins when the mind recognises the imperishable source.
bhagwad_gita::351.simple_meaning: Noble people rely on the divine nature, stay focused on Krishna alone, and worship him as the unborn, imperishable source of all beings.
bhagwad_gita::351.simple_insight: Devotion becomes steady when the mind stops scattering and recognises what never changes.
bhagwad_gita::351.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna explains why some people reject him and others see clearly. The great-minded ones, unlike the deluded, take refuge in the divine nature and worship Krishna as the beginning and end of all beings.
bhagwad_gita::351.modern_relevance: You are standing at the edge of a hard choice, and every noisy opinion is pulling you apart. This verse points to the mind that settles, sees what is lasting, and moves from that place.
bhagwad_gita::351.insight: It shifts devotion from emotion alone to clear recognition and single-hearted attention.

bhagwad_gita::352.verse_sanskrit: सततं कीर्तयन्तो मां यतन्तश्च दृढव्रताः । नमस्यन्तश्च मां भक्त्या नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ॥
bhagwad_gita::352.verse_hindi: नित्य मेरेमें युक्त मनुष्य दृढ़व्रती होकर लगनपूर्वक साधनमें लगे हुए और भक्तिपूर्वक कीर्तन करते हुए तथा नमस्कार करते हुये निरन्तर मेरी उपासना करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::352.english_translation: Ever united with Me, steadfast in vows, they worship Me by chanting, striving, and bowing with devotion.
bhagwad_gita::352.translation_literal: सततं (continuously) / कीर्तयन्तः (chanting) / मां (Me) / यतन्तः (striving) / च (and) / दृढव्रताः (steadfast in vows) / नमस्यन्तः (bowing) / च (and) / मां (Me) / भक्त्या (with devotion) / नित्ययुक्ताः (always united) / उपासते (worship)
bhagwad_gita::352.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::352.essence: Steady devotion becomes a life of continual remembrance.
bhagwad_gita::352.simple_meaning: Devoted people keep chanting, bowing, and striving with steady commitment, always focused on Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::352.simple_insight: Love becomes a practice, not just a feeling.
bhagwad_gita::352.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna describes the people who stay inwardly connected to him. These devotees do not merely believe; they keep chanting, bowing, and practicing with firm resolve.
bhagwad_gita::352.modern_relevance: You light a candle before dawn, repeat the same prayer, and keep showing up even when your mind is tired. Devotion lives in repetition.
bhagwad_gita::352.insight: It shifts devotion from private emotion to repeated, embodied practice.

bhagwad_gita::353.verse_sanskrit: ज्ञानयज्ञेन चाप्यन्ये यजन्तो मामुपासते । एकत्वेन पृथक्त्वेन बहुधा विश्वतोमुखम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::353.verse_hindi: दूसरे साधक ज्ञानयज्ञके द्वारा एकीभावसे अभेदभावसे मेरा पूजन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं और दूसरे कई साधक अपनेको पृथक् मानकर चारों तरफ मुखवाले मेरे विराट्ररुपकी अर्थात् संसारको मेरा विराट्ररुप मानकर सेव्यसेवकभावसे मेरी अनेक प्रकारसे उपासना करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::353.english_translation: Others worship Me through the sacrifice of knowledge, seeing Me as one, as separate, or as the all-facing form.
bhagwad_gita::353.translation_literal: ज्ञानयज्ञेन (through the sacrifice of knowledge) / च (and) / अपि (also) / अन्ये (others) / यजन्तः (worshipping) / माम् (Me) / उपासते (they worship) / एकत्वेन (through oneness) / पृथक्त्वेन (through separateness) / बहुधा (in many ways) / विश्वतोमुखम् (the all-facing one)
bhagwad_gita::353.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::353.essence: The same reality can be approached as one, many, or all-encompassing.
bhagwad_gita::353.simple_meaning: Some people worship Krishna through understanding. They see him as one reality, as separate forms, or as the universal form facing everywhere.
bhagwad_gita::353.simple_insight: There is more than one way to approach the divine, and sincere understanding itself can become worship.
bhagwad_gita::353.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna still stands frozen while Krishna reveals how people come near him. After describing devotion and sacrifice, Krishna adds that some approach through knowledge, seeing him as one, as distinct, or as the all-facing universal form.
bhagwad_gita::353.modern_relevance: You are trying to make sense of a loss, and every explanation feels partial. One person sees unity, another sees difference, another sees the whole pattern. The verse says all three can be forms of reverent seeing.
bhagwad_gita::353.insight: It expands devotion beyond one style of belief and shows that understanding can itself be an offering.

bhagwad_gita::354.verse_sanskrit: अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाऽहमहमौषधम् । मंत्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::354.verse_hindi: क्रतु मैं हूँ, यज्ञ मैं हूँ, स्वधा मैं हूँ, औषध मैं हूँ, मन्त्र मैं हूँ, घृत मैं हूँ, अग्नि मैं हूँ और हवनरूप क्रिया भी मैं हूँ ।  जाननेयोग्य पवित्र, ओंकार, ऋग्वेद, सामवेद और यजुर्वेद भी मैं ही हूँ ।  इस सम्पूर्ण जगत्का पिता, धाता, माता, पितामह, गति, भर्ता, प्रभु, साक्षी, निवास, आश्रय, सुहृद्, उत्पत्ति, प्रलय, स्थान, निधान तथा अविनाशी बीज भी मैं ही हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::354.english_translation: I am the sacrifice, I am the ritual, I am the offering, I am the herb, I am the mantra, I am the ghee, I am the fire, and I am the act of offering. I am the sacred syllable Om, the Vedas, the father, mother, supporter, grandfather, object of knowledge, purifier, and imperishable seed of this world.
bhagwad_gita::354.translation_literal: अहम् (I am) / क्रतुः (ritual sacrifice) / अहम् (I am) / यज्ञः (sacrifice) / स्वधा (offering to ancestors) / अहम् (I am) / अहम् (I am) / औषधम् (herb) / मंत्रः (mantra) / अहम् (I am) / अहम् (I am) / एव (indeed) / आज्यम् (ghee) / अहम् (I am) / अग्निः (fire) / अहम् (I am) / हुतम् (the offering cast into the fire)
bhagwad_gita::354.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::354.essence: All sacred action is already filled with the divine presence.
bhagwad_gita::354.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is every part of sacred ritual: the offering, the chant, the fire, and the act itself. He is also the sacred sound, the Vedas, and the sustaining source of the world.
bhagwad_gita::354.simple_insight: Devotion becomes simpler when every sacred act is seen as already held by the divine.
bhagwad_gita::354.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna expands the teaching beyond duty and fear. He reveals that every sacred act, every ritual element, and every source of wisdom points back to him, making devotion a way of seeing all reality.
bhagwad_gita::354.modern_relevance: You light a lamp before a hard day, whisper a prayer, or sit in silence before a decision. The ritual feels small until you realize the whole act is already held by the divine.
bhagwad_gita::354.insight: It shifts devotion from isolated ceremony to seeing the divine presence in every sacred act and support.

bhagwad_gita::355.verse_sanskrit: पिताऽहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः । वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च ॥
bhagwad_gita::355.verse_hindi: क्रतु मैं हूँ, यज्ञ मैं हूँ, स्वधा मैं हूँ, औषध मैं हूँ, मन्त्र मैं हूँ, घृत मैं हूँ, अग्नि मैं हूँ और हवनरूप क्रिया भी मैं हूँ ।  जाननेयोग्य पवित्र, ओंकार, ऋग्वेद, सामवेद और यजुर्वेद भी मैं ही हूँ ।  इस सम्पूर्ण जगत् का पिता, धाता, माता, पितामह, गति, भर्ता, प्रभु, साक्षी, निवास, आश्रय, सुहृद्, उत्पत्ति, प्रलय, स्थान, निधान तथा अविनाशी बीज भी मैं ही हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::355.english_translation: I am the father of this world, the mother, the supporter, and the grandfather. I am the object of knowledge, the purifier, the sacred syllable Om, and also the Rig, Sama, and Yajur Vedas.
bhagwad_gita::355.translation_literal: पिता (father) / अहम् (I am) / अस्य (of this) / जगतः (world) / माता (mother) / धाता (supporter) / पितामहः (grandfather) / वेद्यम् (to be known) / पवित्रम् (purifier / pure) / ओंकार (sacred syllable Om) / ऋक् (Rig) / साम (Sama) / यजुः (Yajur) / एव (indeed) / च (and)
bhagwad_gita::355.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::355.essence: All sources of life and meaning are gathered in Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::355.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the world’s father, mother, supporter, and ancestor. He is also the sacred sound Om and the Vedas themselves.
bhagwad_gita::355.simple_insight: You are held by something larger than family, ritual, or language.
bhagwad_gita::355.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna unfolds who he really is. After naming himself as the fire, the offering, and the rite, Krishna widens the vision: he is the world’s source, support, and sacred knowing itself.
bhagwad_gita::355.modern_relevance: When everything familiar collapses — family expectations, labels, even your own certainty — this speaks to the ground beneath them all.
bhagwad_gita::355.insight: It shifts attention from asking where the sacred is to recognising that all sacred forms point back to Krishna.

bhagwad_gita::356.verse_sanskrit: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् । प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::356.verse_hindi: क्रतु मैं हूँ, यज्ञ मैं हूँ, स्वधा मैं हूँ, औषध मैं हूँ, मन्त्र मैं हूँ, घृत मैं हूँ, अग्नि मैं हूँ और हवनरूप क्रिया भी मैं हूँ ।  जाननेयोग्य पवित्र, ओंकार, ऋग्वेद, सामवेद और यजुर्वेद भी मैं ही हूँ ।  इस सम्पूर्ण जगत्का पिता, धाता, माता, पितामह, गति, भर्ता, प्रभु, साक्षी, निवास, आश्रय, सुहृद्, उत्पत्ति, प्रलय, स्थान, निधान तथा अविनाशी बीज भी मैं ही हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::356.english_translation: I am the goal, the supporter, the lord, the witness, the refuge, the friend, the source, the dissolution, the resting place, the treasure, and the imperishable seed.
bhagwad_gita::356.translation_literal: गतिः (goal) / भर्ता (supporter) / प्रभुः (lord) / साक्षी (witness) / निवासः (dwelling) / शरणम् (refuge) / सुहृत् (well-wisher) / प्रभवः (source) / प्रलयः (dissolution) / स्थानम् (resting place) / निधानम् (treasure) / बीजम् (seed) / अव्ययम् (imperishable)
bhagwad_gita::356.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::356.essence: Everything rests in one imperishable source.
bhagwad_gita::356.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is everything that supports, witnesses, shelters, begins, ends, and sustains existence.
bhagwad_gita::356.simple_insight: You are not alone inside the world; the deepest reality is already holding, seeing, and guiding everything.
bhagwad_gita::356.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen before battle while Krishna expands the meaning of divine presence. After naming himself in sacred forms and cosmic roles, Krishna now says he is the goal, shelter, witness, source, and imperishable seed of all that exists.
bhagwad_gita::356.modern_relevance: You are sitting in a parked car after a hard call, afraid of what happens next. The verse reminds you that the same reality that receives the ending also holds the beginning.
bhagwad_gita::356.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing the world as separate pieces to seeing one sustaining presence in all roles.

bhagwad_gita::357.verse_sanskrit: तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च । अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन ॥
bhagwad_gita::357.verse_hindi: हे अर्जुन  संसारके हितके लिये मैं ही सूर्यरूपसे तपता हूँ, जलको ग्रहण करता हूँ और फिर उस जलको वर्षारूपसे बरसा देता हूँ ।  और तो क्या कहूँ अमृत और मृत्यु तथा सत् और असत् भी मैं ही हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::357.english_translation: I heat the world as the sun, I hold back the rain and send it forth. I am immortality and death, being and non-being, Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::357.translation_literal: तपामि (I heat) / अहम् (I) / अहम् (I) / वर्षम् (rain) / निगृह्णामि (I hold back) / उत्सृजामि (I release) / च (and) / अमृतम् (immortality) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / मृत्युः (death) / च (and) / सत् (being) / असत् (non-being) / च (and) / अहम् (I am) / अर्जुन (Arjuna)
bhagwad_gita::357.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::357.essence: Opposites do not stand outside the divine; they flow from it.
bhagwad_gita::357.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the force behind sunlight, rain, immortality, death, existence, and non-existence. Everything that sustains and changes the world moves through him.
bhagwad_gita::357.simple_insight: The world feels less random when you see one presence behind both nourishment and loss.
bhagwad_gita::357.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna still stands frozen while Krishna keeps widening the vision. After naming himself as the source of many sacred powers, Krishna now says even heat, rain, immortality, death, being, and non-being all move through him.
bhagwad_gita::357.modern_relevance: You watch a storm flood the street, then clear the next morning, and realize the same sky held both. This verse trains you to see order inside forces that look opposite.
bhagwad_gita::357.insight: It shifts the mind from dividing life into good and bad forces to seeing one reality working through both.

bhagwad_gita::358.verse_sanskrit: त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापायज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते । ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोकमश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान् ॥
bhagwad_gita::358.verse_hindi: वेदत्रयीमें कहे हुए सकाम अनुष्ठानको करनेवाले और सोमरसको पीनेवाले जो पापरहित मनुष्य यज्ञोंके द्वारा इन्द्ररूपसे मेरा पूजन करके स्वर्गप्राप्तिकी प्रार्थना करते हैं, वे पुण्यके फलस्वरूप इन्द्रलोकको प्राप्त करके वहाँ स्वर्गमें देवताओंके दिव्य भोगोंको भोगते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::358.english_translation: Those who know the three Vedas, drink soma, and are purified by sacrifice pray for heaven. Having earned merit, they enjoy the divine pleasures of the realm of the radiant beings.
bhagwad_gita::358.translation_literal: त्रैविद्या (knowers of the three Vedas) / मां (me) / सोमपाः (drinkers of soma) / पूतपापाः (purified from sin) / यज्ञैः (by sacrifices) / इष्ट्वा (having worshipped) / स्वर्गतिम् (heavenly attainment) / प्रार्थयन्ते (they pray for) / ते (they) / पुण्यम् (merit) / आसाद्य (having attained) / सुरेन्द्रलोकम् (realm of the lord of the radiant beings) / अश्नन्ति (they enjoy) / दिव्यान् (divine) / दिवि (in heaven) / देवभोगान् (pleasures of the radiant beings)
bhagwad_gita::358.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::358.essence: Rewarded devotion still keeps you bound to return.
bhagwad_gita::358.simple_meaning: People who perform Vedic sacrifices and seek reward pray for heaven. They gain merit, reach the heavenly realm, and enjoy its pleasures for a time.
bhagwad_gita::358.simple_insight: Chasing reward can take you higher, but only for a while.
bhagwad_gita::358.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen while Krishna opens a wider vision of action, reward, and the limits of ritual. Here Krishna describes people who worship for heavenly gain, showing that even rewarded action remains bound to return.
bhagwad_gita::358.modern_relevance: You finish a big religious event, post the photos, and wait for the praise to feel like enough. The verse reminds you that reward-seeking always keeps you reaching for the next high.
bhagwad_gita::358.insight: It shifts the mind from spiritual transaction to seeing the limits of reward-based worship.

bhagwad_gita::359.verse_sanskrit: ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालंक्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति । एव त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्नागतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते ॥
bhagwad_gita::359.verse_hindi: वे उस विशाल स्वर्गलोकके भोगोंको भोगकर पुण्य क्षीण होनेपर मृत्युलोकमें आ जाते हैं ।  इस प्रकार तीनों वेदोंमें कहे हुए सकाम धर्मका आश्रय लिये हुए भोगोंकी कामना करनेवाले मनुष्य आवागमनको प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
