bhagwad_gita::359.english_translation: After enjoying the vast heaven-world, they return to the mortal world when their merit is exhausted. Thus, those who follow the ritual path of the three Vedas and seek pleasures gain repeated coming and going.
bhagwad_gita::359.translation_literal: ते (they) / तम् (that) / भुक्त्वा (having enjoyed) / स्वर्गलोकम् (heaven-world) / विशालम् (vast) / क्षीणे (having become exhausted) / पुण्ये (merit) / मर्त्यलोकम् (mortal world) / विशन्ति (enter) / एवम् (thus) / त्रयीधर्मम् (the three-Veda ritual dharma) / अनुप्रपन्नाः (having resorted to) / गतागतम् (coming and going) / कामकामा (desiring pleasures) / लभन्ते (obtain)
bhagwad_gita::359.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::359.essence: What is won by wanting is lost by time.
bhagwad_gita::359.simple_meaning: People who seek heavenly rewards through ritual enjoy those rewards for a while, but when their merit is used up, they return to ordinary life and the cycle continues.
bhagwad_gita::359.simple_insight: Short-lived rewards feel satisfying, but they do not end restlessness.
bhagwad_gita::359.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Krishna is exposing the limits of reward-seeking religion. After describing ritualists who aim for heaven, he says even that highest pleasure is temporary: merit fades, the reward ends, and the seeker returns to mortal life.
bhagwad_gita::359.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the applause, the bonus trip — and by Monday the hunger is back. Krishna points to the exhaustion behind every reward that depends on accumulation.
bhagwad_gita::359.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing temporary payoff to seeing the loop beneath it.

bhagwad_gita::360.verse_sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते । तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::360.verse_hindi: जो अनन्य भक्त मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं, मेरेमें निरन्तर लगे हुए उन भक्तोंका योगक्षेम अप्राप्तकी प्राप्ति और प्राप्तकी रक्षा मैं वहन करता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::360.english_translation: Those who think of me alone and worship me with unwavering focus—I carry their welfare and security.
bhagwad_gita::360.translation_literal: अनन्याः (with no other focus) / चिन्तयन्तः (thinking) / माम् (me) / ये (those who) / जनाः (people) / पर्युपासते (worship all around) / तेषाम् (for them) / नित्य-अभियुक्तानाम् (for those always joined) / योग-क्षेमम् (welfare and security) / वहामि (I carry) / अहम् (I)
bhagwad_gita::360.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::360.essence: Unwavering devotion is met by unwavering support.
bhagwad_gita::360.simple_meaning: People who focus on Krishna alone and worship him steadily do not have to carry every burden by themselves. He takes responsibility for their well-being and security.
bhagwad_gita::360.simple_insight: Devotion can feel like being held instead of having to hold everything alone.
bhagwad_gita::360.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. After exposing the limits of ritual and mixed motives, Krishna gives a promise to the devoted: those who turn to him without divided attention are personally sustained by him.
bhagwad_gita::360.modern_relevance: You are staring at a hospital bill, a breakup text, and a job notice all at once. This verse answers the panic that says, 'I have to hold everything myself.'
bhagwad_gita::360.insight: It shifts devotion from asking for favors to trusting steady support. The mind stops clutching and begins relying.

bhagwad_gita::361.verse_sanskrit: येऽप्यन्यदेवता भक्ता यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः । तेऽपि मामेव कौन्तेय यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::361.verse_hindi: हे कुन्तीनन्दन जो भी भक्त मनुष्य श्रद्धापूर्वक अन्य देवताओंका पूजन करते हैं, वे भी करते हैं मेरा ही पूजन, पर करते है अविधिपूर्वक ॥
bhagwad_gita::361.english_translation: Even those who, filled with trust, worship other radiant beings, worship Me alone, but in the wrong way, O son of Kunti.
bhagwad_gita::361.translation_literal: येऽपि (even those who) / अन्यदेवता-भक्ताः (devotees of other radiant beings) / यजन्ते (worship) / श्रद्धया अन्विताः (endowed with trust) / तेऽपि (they also) / माम् एव (Me alone) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / यजन्ति (worship) / अविधिपूर्वकम् (in an improper way)
bhagwad_gita::361.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::361.essence: All sincere worship reaches the one reality, even when the form is confused.
bhagwad_gita::361.simple_meaning: People who worship other radiant beings with trust are still, in a deeper sense, worshipping Krishna, but without the full understanding of how worship truly works.
bhagwad_gita::361.simple_insight: Trust matters, but clear understanding keeps devotion from becoming fragmented.
bhagwad_gita::361.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna still stands frozen while Krishna explains why different forms of worship do not stand apart from the supreme reality. This verse is part of a larger teaching that all sincere worship ultimately reaches Krishna, though not always with full knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::361.modern_relevance: You light a lamp before one name, pray before another, and still feel the same ache for help. The heart reaches upward; the mind only names the doorway differently.
bhagwad_gita::361.insight: It shifts devotion from many separate targets to one underlying source.

bhagwad_gita::362.verse_sanskrit: अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च । न तु मामभिजानन्ति तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति ते ॥
bhagwad_gita::362.verse_hindi: क्योंकि मैं ही सम्पूर्ण यज्ञोंका भोक्ता और स्वामी भी हूँ परन्तु वे मेरेको तत्त्वसे नहीं जानते, इसीसे उनका पतन होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::362.english_translation: For I am the enjoyer and lord of all sacrifices. But those people do not know me in truth, and so they fall away.
bhagwad_gita::362.translation_literal: अहम् (I) / हि (indeed) / सर्वयज्ञानाम् (of all sacrifices) / भोक्ता (the enjoyer) / च (and) / प्रभुः (the lord) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / न (not) / तु (but) / माम् (me) / अभिजानन्ति (they know) / तत्त्वेन (in truth) / अतः (therefore) / च्यवन्ति (fall away) / ते (they)
bhagwad_gita::362.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::362.essence: Every offering matters only when you know who receives it.
bhagwad_gita::362.simple_meaning: All sacrifices ultimately belong to Krishna, who receives them and rules over them. People fall when they do not know this truth clearly.
bhagwad_gita::362.simple_insight: Devotion deepens when you remember who stands behind every offering.
bhagwad_gita::362.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains why worship matters. After saying that all sincere worship reaches him, Krishna adds that he is the one who truly receives every sacrifice. Missing that truth leaves people spiritually adrift.
bhagwad_gita::362.modern_relevance: You give time, money, and attention to what matters most, but forget the deeper source behind it all. That forgetfulness quietly drains the meaning out of your effort.
bhagwad_gita::362.insight: It shifts devotion from ritual performance to clear recognition of the one who receives every offering.

bhagwad_gita::363.verse_sanskrit: यान्ति देवव्रता देवान् पितृ़न्यान्ति पितृव्रताः । भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::363.verse_hindi: सकामभावसे देवताओंका पूजन करनेवाले शरीर छोड़नेपर देवताओंको प्राप्त होते हैं ।  पितरोंका पूजन करनेवाले पितरोंको प्राप्त होते हैं ।  भूतप्रेतोंका पूजन करनेवाले भूतप्रेतोंको प्राप्त होते हैं ।  परन्तु मेरा पूजन करनेवाले मुझे ही प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::363.english_translation: Those devoted to the radiant beings reach the radiant beings. Those devoted to the ancestors reach the ancestors. Those devoted to spirits reach the spirits. But those devoted to me come to me.
bhagwad_gita::363.translation_literal: यान्ति (go/reach) / देवव्रताः (those devoted to radiant beings) / देवान् (the radiant beings) / पितॄन् (the ancestors) / यान्ति (go/reach) / पितृव्रताः (those devoted to the ancestors) / भूतानि (spirits/beings) / यान्ति (go/reach) / भूतेज्याः (those who worship spirits) / यान्ति (go/reach) / मद्याजिनः (those who worship me) / अपि (also) / माम् (me)
bhagwad_gita::363.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::363.essence: Devotion does not stay abstract; it carries you to its chosen end.
bhagwad_gita::363.simple_meaning: People reach the object they devote themselves to. Worship directed toward Krishna leads to Krishna; other devotions lead elsewhere.
bhagwad_gita::363.simple_insight: What you repeatedly honor quietly shapes your destination.
bhagwad_gita::363.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna is explaining how devotion works. After saying that all worship is ultimately aimed at him, Krishna adds that different kinds of worship lead to different ends. This verse sharpens the choice.
bhagwad_gita::363.modern_relevance: You keep returning to the same feed, the same crowd, the same craving. Over time, you start arriving where your attention has been going all along.
bhagwad_gita::363.insight: It shifts devotion from a vague feeling to a directional force that determines what the heart reaches.

bhagwad_gita::364.verse_sanskrit: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::364.verse_hindi: जो भक्त पत्र, पुष्प, फल, जल आदि यथासाध्य प्राप्त वस्तु को भक्तिपूर्वक मेरे अर्पण करता है, उस मेरेमें तल्लीन हुए अन्तःकरणवाले भक्तके द्वारा भक्तिपूर्वक दिये हुए उपहारभेंट को मैं खा लेता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::364.english_translation: Whoever offers me a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water with devotion, I accept that devoted offering from the pure-hearted.
bhagwad_gita::364.translation_literal: पत्रम् (leaf) / पुष्पम् (flower) / फलम् (fruit) / तोयम् (water) / यः (who) / मे (to me) / भक्त्या (with devotion) / प्रयच्छति (offers) / तत् (that) / अहम् (I) / भक्त्युपहृतम् (devotion-offered) / अश्नामि (I accept / consume) / प्रयतात्मनः (of the pure-hearted person)
bhagwad_gita::364.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::364.essence: A small offering becomes complete when devotion fills it.
bhagwad_gita::364.simple_meaning: Even the smallest offering becomes meaningful when it is given with devotion and a sincere heart.
bhagwad_gita::364.simple_insight: You do not need grand gestures to be received. Sincerity makes the offering complete.
bhagwad_gita::364.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna begins teaching the kind of relationship that can hold a life together. He says that a simple leaf, flower, fruit, or water offered with devotion is enough for him to accept.
bhagwad_gita::364.modern_relevance: You bring a small homemade meal to someone grieving, unsure it is enough. What matters is not the size of the gift, but the love carried into it.
bhagwad_gita::364.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to sincerity, showing that wholehearted offering is what truly counts.

bhagwad_gita::365.verse_sanskrit: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् । यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::365.verse_hindi: हे कुन्तीपुत्र  तू जो कुछ करता है, जो कुछ खाता है, जो कुछ यज्ञ करता है, जो कुछ दान देता है और जो कुछ तप करता है, वह सब मेरे अर्पण कर दे ॥
bhagwad_gita::365.english_translation: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give, and whatever austerity you practice, offer it to me.
bhagwad_gita::365.translation_literal: यत्करोषि (whatever you do) / यदश्नासि (whatever you eat) / यज्जुहोषि (whatever you offer in sacrifice) / ददासि (you give) / यत् (whatever) / यत्तपस्यसि (whatever austerity you practice) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / तत्कुरुष्व (do that) / मदर्पणम् (as an offering to me)
bhagwad_gita::365.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::365.essence: Every action becomes complete when it is offered.
bhagwad_gita::365.simple_meaning: Whatever you do in daily life can become an offering. Work, food, giving, sacrifice, and discipline all gain meaning when dedicated to the divine.
bhagwad_gita::365.simple_insight: Ordinary life stops feeling fragmented. Even small actions can carry devotion.
bhagwad_gita::365.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna is showing him how to live without inner division. After teaching that even simple offerings matter, Krishna now widens the practice: every act, from eating to austerity, can be given back to him.
bhagwad_gita::365.modern_relevance: You finish a hard day, eat in silence, answer messages, and keep going. This verse says none of it is too small to be offered with care.
bhagwad_gita::365.insight: It turns daily activity into devotion, so nothing is spiritually wasted.

bhagwad_gita::366.verse_sanskrit: शुभाशुभफलैरेवं मोक्ष्यसे कर्मबन्धनैः । संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा विमुक्तो मामुपैष्यसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::366.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार मेरे अर्पण करनेसे जिनसे कर्मबन्धन होता है, ऐसे शुभ विहित और अशुभ निषिद्ध सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंके फलोंसे तू मुक्त हो जायगा ।  ऐसे अपनेसहित सब कुछ मेरे अर्पण करनेवाला और सबसे मुक्त हुआ तू मेरेको प्राप्त हो जायगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::366.english_translation: In this way, you will be freed from the bonds of action and its results. Given over to renunciation-yoga, released, you will come to me.
bhagwad_gita::366.translation_literal: शुभाशुभफलैः (by auspicious and inauspicious results) / एवम् (thus) / मोक्ष्यसे (you will be freed) / कर्मबन्धनैः (from the bonds of action) / संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा (one whose being is joined to renunciation-yoga) / विमुक्तः (released) / माम् (to me) / उपैष्यसि (you will come)
bhagwad_gita::366.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::366.essence: Freedom begins when even the result is no longer yours to carry.
bhagwad_gita::366.simple_meaning: Offer every action and its results to the divine, and you become free from the bondage created by action.
bhagwad_gita::366.simple_insight: Relief comes from not carrying every outcome as your burden.
bhagwad_gita::366.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna keeps teaching him how to act without being trapped by action. After showing that every offering can be given inwardly, Krishna says this surrender breaks the bonds of karma and leads to union with him.
bhagwad_gita::366.modern_relevance: You send the message, then stare at the screen for hours, replaying every word. This verse says the work can be complete even when the response is not yours to own.
bhagwad_gita::366.insight: It shifts attention from owning results to offering the whole act.

bhagwad_gita::367.verse_sanskrit: समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः । ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::367.verse_hindi: मैं सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें समान हूँ ।  उन प्राणियोंमें न तो कोई मेरा द्वेषी है और न कोई प्रिय है ।  परन्तु जो भक्तिपूर्वक मेरा भजन करते हैं, वे मेरेमें हैं और मैं उनमें हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::367.english_translation: I am equal toward all beings. No one is hated by me, and no one is especially dear. But those who worship me with devotion dwell in me, and I dwell in them.
bhagwad_gita::367.translation_literal: समः (equal) / अहम् (I) / सर्वभूतेषु (toward all beings) / न (not) / मे (to me) / द्वेष्यः (hated one) / अस्ति (is) / न (not) / प्रियः (dear one) / ये (those who) / भजन्ति (worship) / तु (but) / माम् (me) / भक्त्या (with devotion) / मयि (in me) / ते (they) / तेषु (in them) / च (and) / अपि (also) / अहम् (I)
bhagwad_gita::367.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::367.essence: Equality is universal; intimacy is born through devotion.
bhagwad_gita::367.simple_meaning: The divine is not partial or biased. Everyone is met equally, but loving devotion creates a living closeness between the divine and the devotee.
bhagwad_gita::367.simple_insight: You do not have to earn basic worth; devotion changes distance into intimacy.
bhagwad_gita::367.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still speaking on the battlefield to Arjuna, after teaching him to offer every action to the divine. Now he clarifies a subtle point: divine presence is equal everywhere, yet sincere devotion creates a mutual indwelling that transforms relationship.
bhagwad_gita::367.modern_relevance: You send the message, then wait for the reply that might never come. This verse says the deepest presence is not bought by approval; it grows where devotion is real.
bhagwad_gita::367.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to impress the divine to entering a relationship of mutual presence.

bhagwad_gita::368.verse_sanskrit: अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक् । साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः ॥
bhagwad_gita::368.verse_hindi: अगर कोई दुराचारीसेदुराचारी भी अनन्यभावसे मेरा भजन करता है, तो उसको साधु ही मानना चाहिये ।  कारण कि उसने निश्चय बहुत अच्छी तरह कर लिया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::368.english_translation: Even if a person of very bad conduct worships Me with undivided devotion, that person must be regarded as righteous, for the resolve is rightly made.
bhagwad_gita::368.translation_literal: अपि (even) / चेत् (if) / सुदुराचारः (one of very bad conduct) / भजते (worships) / माम् (Me) / अनन्यभाक् (with undivided devotion) / साधुः (righteous) / एव (indeed) / सः (that person) / मन्तव्यः (to be regarded) / सम्यक् (properly) / व्यवसितः (resolved) / हि (indeed) / सः (that person)
bhagwad_gita::368.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::368.essence: Undivided devotion can outweigh even a deeply flawed life.
bhagwad_gita::368.simple_meaning: Even someone with a very bad past is still worthy if that person turns to the divine with one-pointed devotion.
bhagwad_gita::368.simple_insight: You are not frozen by your worst chapter; wholehearted turning can redefine you.
bhagwad_gita::368.detailed_meaning: Arjuna stands shaken on the battlefield, and Krishna keeps widening the horizon of mercy. After saying that devotion binds him to all who turn toward him, Krishna adds a startling claim: even the deeply flawed can be counted as noble if their devotion is single-minded.
bhagwad_gita::368.modern_relevance: Someone who has lied, failed, or hurt others may still choose one honest step tonight: a call, an apology, a return. The past is heavy, but a clean turning still matters.
bhagwad_gita::368.insight: It shifts judgment from moral history to present direction: the decisive fact is where attention and devotion now go.

bhagwad_gita::369.verse_sanskrit: क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति । कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति ॥
bhagwad_gita::369.verse_hindi: वह तत्काल उसी क्षण धर्मात्मा हो जाता है और निरन्तर रहनेवाली शान्तिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ।  हे कुन्तीनन्दन  तुम प्रतिज्ञा करो कि मेरे भक्तका विनाश पतन नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::369.english_translation: One who is devoted to Me quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace. O son of Kunti, declare it boldly: My devotee never perishes.
bhagwad_gita::369.translation_literal: क्षिप्रम् (quickly) / भवति (becomes) / धर्मात्मा (righteous in nature) / शश्वत् (everlasting) / शान्तिम् (peace) / निगच्छति (attains) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / प्रतिजानीहि (declare boldly) / न (not) / मे (My) / भक्तः (devotee) / प्रणश्यति (perishes)
bhagwad_gita::369.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::369.essence: Devotion quickly changes a person and protects them from ruin.
bhagwad_gita::369.simple_meaning: A devoted person quickly becomes upright and finds lasting peace. Krishna says his devotee will not come to ruin.
bhagwad_gita::369.simple_insight: Devotion is not fragile. It steadies you and gives the courage to trust the path.
bhagwad_gita::369.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen by grief and doubt. Krishna answers with reassurance: devotion changes a person quickly, brings lasting peace, and never leaves a true devotee to perish.
bhagwad_gita::369.modern_relevance: You are standing at the hospital corridor after bad news, unsure whether you can keep going. This verse says devotion does not leave you stranded; it steadies you when fear says collapse.
bhagwad_gita::369.insight: It shifts the mind from fear of collapse to trust in a sustaining presence.

bhagwad_gita::370.verse_sanskrit: मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः । स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::370.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन  जो भी पापयोनिवाले हों तथा जो भी स्त्रियाँ, वैश्य और शूद्र हों, वे भी सर्वथा मेरे शरण होकर निःसन्देह परमगतिको प्राप्त हो जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::370.english_translation: O Partha, even those born in difficult circumstances, and women, merchants, and workers, can reach the highest state by taking refuge in me.
bhagwad_gita::370.translation_literal: माम् (me) / हि (indeed) / पार्थ (O Partha) / व्यपाश्रित्य (having taken refuge) / ये (those who) / अपि (even) / स्युः (may be) / पापयोनयः (born in difficult circumstances) / स्त्रियः (women) / वैश्याः (merchants) / तथा (and) / शूद्राः (workers) / ते (they) / अपि (also) / यान्ति (go) / पराम् (highest) / गतिम् (state)
bhagwad_gita::370.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::370.essence: No birth or status can block one who takes refuge.
bhagwad_gita::370.simple_meaning: Anyone, regardless of birth or social position, can reach the highest state by taking refuge in Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::370.simple_insight: Belonging is not limited by background. Trust and surrender can open what status never could.
bhagwad_gita::370.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen by doubt, and Krishna is widening his vision of who can reach the highest state. After saying even the fallen can rise through single-hearted devotion, Krishna adds that birth, gender, and social rank do not bar the way.
bhagwad_gita::370.modern_relevance: You walk into a room already feeling disqualified because of where you came from, what you earn, or how people label you. This verse cuts through that shame: the door is not locked by your background.
bhagwad_gita::370.insight: It shifts the mind from social exclusion to spiritual access through refuge.

bhagwad_gita::371.verse_sanskrit: किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा । अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::371.verse_hindi: जो पवित्र आचरणवाले ब्राह्मण और ऋषिस्वरूप क्षत्रिय भगवान् के भक्त हों, वे परमगतिको प्राप्त हो जायँ, इसमें तो कहना ही क्या है ।  इसलिये इस अनित्य और सुखरहित शरीरको प्राप्त करके तू मेरा भजन कर ॥
bhagwad_gita::371.english_translation: If even pure Brahmins and royal sages devoted to the divine reach the highest state, what to speak of you? So, having come into this impermanent and joyless world, worship Me.
bhagwad_gita::371.translation_literal: किं (what?) / पुनः (again) / ब्राह्मणाः (Brahmins) / पुण्याः (pure, meritorious) / भक्ताः (devotees) / राजर्षयः (royal sages) / तथा (also) / अनित्यम् (impermanent) / असुखम् (joyless) / लोकम् (world) / इमम् (this) / प्राप्य (having attained) / भजस्व (worship) / माम् (Me)
bhagwad_gita::371.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::371.essence: What does not last cannot finally satisfy; turn your life toward the divine.
bhagwad_gita::371.simple_meaning: Even the most virtuous devotees and wise rulers can reach the highest state through devotion. Since this world is temporary and unsatisfying, turn toward Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::371.simple_insight: There is relief in turning toward what lasts instead of clinging to what cannot satisfy.
bhagwad_gita::371.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands shaken while Krishna keeps unfolding the path of devotion. After saying even those born in difficult conditions can reach the highest state, Krishna now adds a final invitation: this world does not last, so make your life a turning toward Me.
bhagwad_gita::371.modern_relevance: You finish something you thought would finally satisfy you, and the relief never comes. The verse points you away from chasing another temporary fix and toward what can actually hold you.
bhagwad_gita::371.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing temporary comfort to orienting life around devotion.

bhagwad_gita::372.verse_sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु । मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः ॥
bhagwad_gita::372.verse_hindi: तू मेरा भक्त हो जा, मेरेमें मनवाला हो जा, मेरा पूजन करनेवाला हो जा और मेरेको नमस्कार कर ।  इस प्रकार मेरे साथ अपनेआपको लगाकर, मेरे परायण हुआ तू मेरेको ही प्राप्त होगा । , ॥
bhagwad_gita::372.english_translation: Fix your mind on me. Be devoted to me. Worship me. Bow to me. United with me in this way, and fully oriented toward me, you will come to me.
bhagwad_gita::372.translation_literal: मत्-मनाः (mind on me) / भव (become) / मत्-भक्तः (my devotee) / मत्-याजी (my worshipper) / माम् (to me) / नमस्कुरु (bow) / माम् (me) / एव (only) / एष्यसि (you will come) / युक्त्वा (having united) / एवम् (thus) / आत्मानम् (yourself) / मत्-परायणः (with me as your highest goal)
bhagwad_gita::372.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::372.essence: Total orientation toward the divine becomes the way to reach the divine.
bhagwad_gita::372.simple_meaning: Krishna asks Arjuna to place his mind, devotion, worship, and respect entirely on him. He promises that this full orientation will lead Arjuna to him.
bhagwad_gita::372.simple_insight: Devotion is not passive feeling; it becomes a complete direction for the mind and life.
bhagwad_gita::372.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna still stands frozen while Krishna gives the closing note of his teaching on divine presence. After showing that even the unlikely and excluded can reach the highest state, Krishna now gives the direct practice: orient everything toward him.
bhagwad_gita::372.modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, deciding whether to tell the truth that will change everything. This verse asks for total alignment, not half-hearted loyalty: let the mind, intention, and action point in one direction.
bhagwad_gita::372.insight: It shifts devotion from emotion alone to a full-life orientation that gathers thought, action, and surrender into one movement.

bhagwad_gita::373.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचभूय एव महाबाहो श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ॥
bhagwad_gita::373.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे महाबाहो अर्जुन  मेरे परम वचनको तुम फिर भी सुनो, जिसे मैं तुम्हारे हितकी कामनासे कहूँगा क्योंकि तुम मेरेमें अत्यन्त प्रेम रखते हो ॥
bhagwad_gita::373.english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: Listen again, O mighty-armed one, to my supreme word, which I will speak for your welfare because you are deeply dear to me.
bhagwad_gita::373.translation_literal: श्रीभगवानुवाच (the Blessed Lord said) / भूयः (again) / एव (indeed) / महाबाहो (O mighty-armed one) / श्रृणु (listen) / मे (to my) / परमम् (supreme) / वचः (word) / यत् (which) / ते (to you) / अहम् (I) / प्रीयमाणाय (to one who is dear) / वक्ष्यामि (will speak) / हितकाम्यया (with desire for your welfare)
bhagwad_gita::373.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::373.essence: Deeper truth arrives as care for the one who is ready.
bhagwad_gita::373.simple_meaning: Krishna asks Arjuna to listen again to a deeper teaching, spoken for Arjuna’s good because he is dear to him.
bhagwad_gita::373.simple_insight: Being loved means being taught what you most need, not only what you want to hear.
bhagwad_gita::373.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna stands overwhelmed while Krishna prepares to reveal a deeper teaching. This verse opens the tenth chapter by showing that the coming wisdom is not abstract; it is spoken personally, out of care, to steady Arjuna before the war.
bhagwad_gita::373.modern_relevance: A mentor leans in after your second failed attempt and says, “Listen carefully — I’m telling you this for your good.” The hardest truths often arrive wrapped in care.
bhagwad_gita::373.insight: It frames teaching as an act of loving concern, not distant instruction.

bhagwad_gita::374.verse_sanskrit: न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः । अहमादिर्हि देवानां महर्षीणां च सर्वशः ॥
bhagwad_gita::374.verse_hindi: मेरे प्रकट होनेको न देवता जानते हैं और न महर्षि क्योंकि मैं सब प्रकारसे देवताओं और महर्षियोंका आदि हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::374.english_translation: The hosts of devas do not know my origin, nor do the great sages, for I am the beginning of the devas and the great sages in every way.
bhagwad_gita::374.translation_literal: न (not) / मे (my) / विदुः (know) / सुरगणाः (hosts of devas) / प्रभवम् (origin) / न (not) / महर्षयः (great sages) / अहम (I) / आदिः (beginning) / हि (indeed) / देवानाम् (of devas) / महर्षीणाम् (of great sages) / च (and) / सर्वशः (in every way)
bhagwad_gita::374.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::374.essence: Even the highest knowers stand inside the source they seek.
bhagwad_gita::374.simple_meaning: Even the devas and great sages do not know Krishna’s full source, because he is their own beginning.
bhagwad_gita::374.simple_insight: Awe deepens when you realize the highest minds still cannot contain the divine.
bhagwad_gita::374.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still shaken and listening. Krishna begins revealing his divine presence in the world, but first says that even the devas and great sages do not fully know his origin, because he stands before all of them as their source.
bhagwad_gita::374.modern_relevance: You think you have understood someone because they are brilliant, spiritual, or widely respected. Then they reveal a depth that even the best minds cannot fully map.
bhagwad_gita::374.insight: It shifts the mind from treating the divine as an object of study to recognising it as the source of all knowers.

bhagwad_gita::375.verse_sanskrit: यो मामजमनादिं च वेत्ति लोकमहेश्वरम् । असम्मूढः स मर्त्येषु सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::375.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य मुझे अजन्मा, अनादि और सम्पूर्ण लोकोंका महान् ईश्वर जानता है अर्थात् दृढ़तासे मानता है, वह मनुष्योंमें असम्मूढ़ जानकार है और वह सम्पूर्ण पापोंसे मुक्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::375.english_translation: One who knows Me as unborn, beginningless, and the great lord of all worlds is undeluded among mortals and is freed from every wrong deed.
bhagwad_gita::375.translation_literal: यः (one who) / माम् (Me) / अजम् (unborn) / अनादिम् (beginningless) / च (and) / वेत्ति (knows) / लोकमहेश्वरम् (the great lord of all worlds) / असम्मूढः (undeluded) / सः (that one) / मर्त्येषु (among mortals) / सर्वपापैः (from all wrong deeds) / प्रमुच्यते (is freed)
bhagwad_gita::375.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::375.essence: Clear recognition of the divine ends confusion and frees action.
bhagwad_gita::375.simple_meaning: Knowing Krishna as unborn, beginningless, and the ruler of all worlds removes confusion and frees a person from wrongdoing.
bhagwad_gita::375.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that clear understanding can cut through confusion and loosen the grip of harmful action.
bhagwad_gita::375.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still shaken while Krishna unfolds his divine presence. After revealing his limitless reach, Krishna says that the person who truly knows him as unborn, beginningless, and lord of all worlds passes beyond confusion and wrongdoing.
bhagwad_gita::375.modern_relevance: You are standing at the edge of a choice that could change everything, and the noise in your head is louder than your judgment. Seeing what is higher than fear can steady the whole mind.
bhagwad_gita::375.insight: It shifts devotion from vague admiration to clear recognition, and that recognition dissolves confusion at its root.

bhagwad_gita::376.verse_sanskrit: बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः क्षमा सत्यं दमः शमः । सुखं दुःखं भवोऽभावो भयं चाभयमेव च ॥
bhagwad_gita::376.verse_hindi: बुद्धि, ज्ञान, असम्मोह, क्षमा, सत्य, दम, शम, सुख, दुःख, भव, अभाव, भय, अभय, अहिंसा, समता, तुष्टि, तप, दान, यश और अपयश  प्राणियोंके ये अनेक प्रकारके और अलगअलग बीस भाव मेरेसे ही होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::376.english_translation: Understanding, wisdom, freedom from confusion, forgiveness, truth, self-restraint, calmness, pleasure, pain, coming into being, ceasing to be, fear, fearlessness, nonviolence, evenness, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and disgrace arise from me alone.
bhagwad_gita::376.translation_literal: बुद्धिः (understanding) / ज्ञानम् (wisdom) / असंमोहः (freedom from confusion) / क्षमा (forgiveness) / सत्यम् (truth) / दमः (self-restraint) / शमः (calmness) / सुखम् (pleasure) / दुःखम् (pain) / भवः (coming into being) / अभावः (ceasing to be) / भयम् (fear) / च (and) / अभयम् (fearlessness) / एव (indeed) / च (and)
bhagwad_gita::376.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::376.essence: All human qualities arise from the same source.
bhagwad_gita::376.simple_meaning: Krishna says that every good and difficult human quality comes from him alone, including wisdom, restraint, joy, fear, courage, and even changes in existence itself.
bhagwad_gita::376.simple_insight: You do not have to manufacture your best qualities alone; they are already being carried by a larger source.
bhagwad_gita::376.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen by fear and doubt. Krishna is not only teaching strategy; he is revealing the source of every human capacity and condition. This verse expands the scale of the conversation from war to the whole texture of life.
bhagwad_gita::376.modern_relevance: You watch your own mood swing before a hard conversation: courage, fear, calm, and shame all seem to arrive uninvited. This verse says those states are not random accidents; they come from one deeper source.
bhagwad_gita::376.insight: It shifts attention from self-blame or self-pride to seeing every state as part of a larger order.

bhagwad_gita::377.verse_sanskrit: अहिंसा समता तुष्टिस्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः । भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::377.verse_hindi: बुद्धि, ज्ञान, असम्मोह, क्षमा, सत्य, दम, शम, सुख, दुःख, भव, अभाव, भय, अभय, अहिंसा, समता, तुष्टि, तप, दान, यश और अपयश  प्राणियोंके ये अनेक प्रकारके और अलगअलग बीस भाव मेरेसे ही होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::377.english_translation: Nonviolence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, honor, and dishonor—all these different states of beings arise from Me alone.
bhagwad_gita::377.translation_literal: अहिंसा (nonviolence) / समता (equanimity) / तुष्टिः (contentment) / तपः (austerity) / दानम् (charity) / यशः (honor) / अयशः (dishonor) / भवन्ति (they become) / भावाḥ (states) / भूतानाम् (of beings) / मत् (from Me) / एव (only) / पृथग्विधाः (of different kinds)
bhagwad_gita::377.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::377.essence: All qualities are expressions of the same divine source.
bhagwad_gita::377.simple_meaning: Nonviolence, balance, contentment, discipline, generosity, honor, and dishonor all arise from Krishna alone in different beings.
bhagwad_gita::377.simple_insight: You do not have to manufacture your best qualities alone; they are already rooted in something larger.
bhagwad_gita::377.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen by conflict. Krishna is revealing that even the finest human qualities—nonviolence, balance, contentment, discipline, generosity, honor, and dishonor—do not arise independently. They all flow from Krishna's presence in beings.
bhagwad_gita::377.modern_relevance: You catch yourself being kind in one conversation and harsh in the next, then wonder which version is real. This verse says the deeper source is bigger than either mood.
bhagwad_gita::377.insight: It shifts attention from self-judgment to the source of qualities, so you can align with what nourishes them.

bhagwad_gita::378.verse_sanskrit: महर्षयः सप्त पूर्वे चत्वारो मनवस्तथा । मद्भावा मानसा जाता येषां लोक इमाः प्रजाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::378.verse_hindi: सात महर्षि और उनसे भी पूर्वमें होनेवाले चार सनकादि तथा चौदह मनु  ये सबकेसब मेरे मनसे पैदा हुए हैं और मेरेमें भाव श्रद्धाभक्ति रखनेवाले हैं, जिनकी संसारमें यह सम्पूर्ण प्रजा है ॥
bhagwad_gita::378.english_translation: The seven great sages, the four ancient sages, and the fourteen Manus were born from my mind. The people of these worlds descend from them.
bhagwad_gita::378.translation_literal: महर्षयः (great sages) / सप्त (seven) / पूर्वे (earlier) / चत्वारः (four) / मनवः (Manus) / तथा (and) / मद्भावाः (born from my being) / मानसा (from the mind) / जाताः (born) / येषाम् (from whom) / लोकाः (worlds) / इमाः (these) / प्रजाः (people)
bhagwad_gita::378.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::378.essence: All lineages and worlds emerge from Krishna’s mind.
bhagwad_gita::378.simple_meaning: Krishna says that the great sages, the ancient sages, and the Manus all arose from him, and all beings in these worlds descend through them.
bhagwad_gita::378.simple_insight: The world is not separate from the divine source that sustains it.
bhagwad_gita::378.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna is answering Arjuna’s need to see beyond the battlefield. After naming his divine qualities, he points to the cosmic chain of creation: sages, primordial teachers, Manus, and all living beings. The teaching widens Arjuna’s vision from one war to the source of all life.
bhagwad_gita::378.modern_relevance: You look at a family tree, a lineage of teachers, or the chain behind a tradition and wonder where it all began. This verse says the deepest source is not random history but a living divine origin.
bhagwad_gita::378.insight: It shifts attention from isolated individuals to the sacred source behind all lineages and life.

bhagwad_gita::379.verse_sanskrit: एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः । सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
bhagwad_gita::379.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य मेरी इस विभूतिको और योगको तत्त्वसे जानता है अर्थात् दृढ़तापूर्वक मानता है, वह अविचल भक्तियोगसे युक्त हो जाता है इसमें कुछ भी संशय नहीं है ॥
bhagwad_gita::379.english_translation: One who truly knows this glory and this yoga of mine becomes steadfast in yoga without doubt.
bhagwad_gita::379.translation_literal: एताम् (this) / विभूतिम् (glory, manifestation) / योगम् (yoga, power of union) / च (and) / मम (my) / यः (who) / वेत्ति (knows) / तत्त्वतः (in truth) / सः (that one) / अविकम्पेन (unshaken) / योगेन (by yoga) / युज्यते (is joined) / न (not) / अत्र (here) / संशयः (doubt)
bhagwad_gita::379.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::379.essence: True recognition of Krishna's presence makes devotion unshakable.
bhagwad_gita::379.simple_meaning: Knowing Krishna's divine manifestations deeply makes devotion steady and unshakable. Real understanding removes doubt and draws the mind into firm union.
bhagwad_gita::379.simple_insight: Clear seeing turns admiration into steadiness. Doubt falls away when the mind recognises what it is really meeting.
bhagwad_gita::379.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Krishna has just named the signs of his presence in the world. He now tells Arjuna that anyone who understands this truth fully will enter unshakable yoga. The teaching shifts from seeing glory to living inside it.
bhagwad_gita::379.modern_relevance: You suddenly recognise the person in front of you is not just a role or label. In that moment, hesitation drops and your whole response becomes steadier and more sincere.
bhagwad_gita::379.insight: It shifts devotion from vague feeling to clear recognition, making commitment firm instead of wavering.

bhagwad_gita::380.verse_sanskrit: अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते । इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::380.verse_hindi: मैं संसारमात्रका प्रभव मूलकारण हूँ, और मुझसे ही सारा संसार प्रवृत्त हो रहा है अर्थात् चेष्टा कर रहा है  ऐसा मेरेको मानकर मेरेमें ही श्रद्धाप्रेम रखते हुए बुद्धिमान् भक्त मेरा ही भजन करते हैं  सब प्रकारसे मेरे ही शरण होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::380.english_translation: I am the source of all; everything moves from me. Knowing this, the wise worship me with wholehearted devotion.
bhagwad_gita::380.translation_literal: अहम् (I am) / सर्वस्य (of all) / प्रभवः (the source) / मत्तः (from me) / सर्वम् (everything) / प्रवर्तते (proceeds, moves forth) / इति (thus) / मत्वा (having known) / भजन्ते (worship) / माम् (me) / बुधाः (the wise) / भावसमन्विताः (endowed with devotion, feeling, wholeheartedness)
bhagwad_gita::380.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::380.essence: Knowing the source turns understanding into devotion.
bhagwad_gita::380.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the source of everything, and wise people respond with devoted worship and full-hearted love.
bhagwad_gita::380.simple_insight: There is relief in giving your heart to the source of everything instead of chasing scattered meanings.
bhagwad_gita::380.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna reveals why devotion is not blind emotion but clear recognition. After showing his manifestations, Krishna says everything arises from him, and the wise naturally turn toward him with wholehearted love.
bhagwad_gita::380.modern_relevance: You are staring at a decision that affects everyone around you, and the pressure to control every outcome is crushing. This verse says the deepest steadiness comes from knowing where life itself flows from.
bhagwad_gita::380.insight: It shifts devotion from sentiment to recognition: when you see the source everywhere, worship becomes natural.

bhagwad_gita::381.verse_sanskrit: मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् । कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ॥
bhagwad_gita::381.verse_hindi: मेरेमें चित्तवाले, मेरेमें प्राणोंको अर्पण करनेवाले भक्तजन आपसमें मेरे गुण, प्रभाव आदिको जानते हुए और उनका कथन करते हुए ही नित्यनिरन्तर सन्तुष्ट रहते हैं और मेरेमें प्रेम करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::381.english_translation: With minds fixed on Me and lives offered to Me, My devotees speak of Me to one another, and find continual joy in that shared devotion.
bhagwad_gita::381.translation_literal: मच्चित्ता (with minds on Me) / मद्गतप्राणा (with lives directed toward Me) / बोधयन्तः (instructing, enlightening) / परस्परम् (one another) / कथयन्तः (speaking, telling) / च (and) / माम् (Me) / नित्यम् (always) / तुष्यन्ति (they are satisfied) / च (and) / रमन्ति (they delight) / च (and)
bhagwad_gita::381.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::381.simple_meaning: People devoted to Krishna keep their minds and lives focused on him. They talk about him together, and that shared remembrance brings them lasting joy.
bhagwad_gita::381.simple_insight: Devotion becomes easier when it is shared. Talking about what you love deepens the love.
bhagwad_gita::381.detailed_meaning: In the middle of Krishna's teaching on devotion, he describes his own followers: they keep their minds on him, place their whole life in his care, and speak of him with each other. Their joy comes from continuous remembrance, not from external success.
bhagwad_gita::381.modern_relevance: You leave a temple gathering or a retreat and the conversation keeps circling back to what moved you most. The feeling lasts because remembrance is being shared, not kept private.
bhagwad_gita::381.insight: It shifts devotion from a private feeling into a living practice of shared remembrance and mutual encouragement.

bhagwad_gita::382.verse_sanskrit: तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम् । ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते ॥
bhagwad_gita::382.verse_hindi: उन नित्यनिरन्तर मेरेमें लगे हुए और प्रेमपूर्वक मेरा भजन करनेवाले भक्तोंको मैं वह बुद्धियोग देता हूँ, जिससे उनको मेरी प्राप्ति हो जाती है ॥
bhagwad_gita::382.english_translation: To those who are always devoted and worship Me with love, I give the discernment that leads them to Me.
bhagwad_gita::382.translation_literal: तेषां (to them) / सततयुक्तानां (of those always devoted) / भजतां (of those worshipping) / प्रीतिपूर्वकम् (with love) / ददामि (I give) / बुद्धियोगं (the yoga of discernment) / तं (that) / येन (by which) / माम् (Me) / उपयान्ति (attain) / ते (they)
bhagwad_gita::382.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::382.essence: Steady devotion itself draws forth the understanding that reaches the divine.
bhagwad_gita::382.simple_meaning: Those who keep turning toward Krishna with steady love receive the discernment that leads them to him.
bhagwad_gita::382.simple_insight: Devotion is not blind emotion; it can become a doorway to clear understanding.
bhagwad_gita::382.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna is showing him that love is not separate from wisdom. To those who keep worshipping with steady devotion, Krishna gives the mind that can find him.
bhagwad_gita::382.modern_relevance: You keep returning to the same prayer, the same practice, the same honest question at 2 a.m. The answer does not always arrive as a sign; sometimes it arrives as clearer seeing.
bhagwad_gita::382.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to a disciplined openness that invites discernment.

bhagwad_gita::383.verse_hindi: उन भक्तोंपर कृपा करनेके लिये ही उनके स्वरूप होनेपन में रहनेवाला मैं उनके अज्ञानजन्य अन्धकारको देदीप्यमान ज्ञानरूप दीपकके द्वारा सर्वथा नष्ट कर देता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::383.english_translation: To show them compassion, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge, dwelling in their own being.
bhagwad_gita::383.translation_literal: तेषाम् (of them) / एव (indeed) / अनुकम्पा-अर्थम् (for compassion) / अहम् (I) / अज्ञान-जम् (born of ignorance) / तमः (darkness) / नाशयामि (I destroy) / आत्म-भाव-स्थः (abiding in their own being) / ज्ञान-दीपेन (with the lamp of knowledge) / भास्वता (shining)
bhagwad_gita::383.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::383.essence: Compassion becomes knowledge that burns away inner darkness.
bhagwad_gita::383.simple_meaning: Out of compassion, Krishna removes the darkness of ignorance from devoted people by giving them the light of understanding from within.
bhagwad_gita::383.simple_insight: Being cared for can feel like a sudden clearing inside, where confusion no longer controls you.
bhagwad_gita::383.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, after describing devoted people who speak of him and stay focused on him. He explains that he does not leave them in confusion; he enters their inner being and destroys ignorance with the lamp of knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::383.modern_relevance: You finally sit with the truth you have been avoiding, and something inside stops arguing. The fog lifts not by force, but by seeing clearly.
bhagwad_gita::383.insight: It shifts devotion from emotional closeness to inner transformation: real connection clears confusion at the root.

bhagwad_gita::384.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचपरं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् । पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::384.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  परम ब्रह्म, परम धाम और महान् पवित्र आप ही हैं ।  आप शाश्वत, दिव्य पुरुष, आदिदेव, अजन्मा और विभु व्यापक हैं  ऐसा सबकेसब ऋषि, देवर्षि नारद, असित, देवल तथा व्यास कहते हैं और स्वयं आप भी मेरे प्रति कहते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::384.english_translation: Arjuna said: You are the supreme reality, the highest refuge, the purest one, the eternal divine person, the first being, unborn, and all-pervading.
bhagwad_gita::384.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / परं (supreme) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / परं (highest) / धाम (abode/refuge) / पवित्रं (pure) / परमं (highest) / भवान् (you are) / पुरुषं (person) / शाश्वतं (eternal) / दिव्यम् (divine) / आदिदेवम् (first being) / अजम् (unborn) / विभुम् (all-pervading)
bhagwad_gita::384.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::384.essence: Recognition turns into surrender when the highest reality stands revealed.
bhagwad_gita::384.simple_meaning: Arjuna recognises Krishna as the highest reality, the purest refuge, eternal, unborn, and present everywhere.
bhagwad_gita::384.simple_insight: Awe can become clarity: the mind bows when it sees what is truly greater than itself.
bhagwad_gita::384.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna has just been overwhelmed by Krishna's cosmic revelation. In that stunned silence, he names Krishna as the highest reality, the pure refuge, and the eternal source of all beings.
bhagwad_gita::384.modern_relevance: You stand before someone’s brutal honesty and feel your defenses collapse. In that moment, respect becomes recognition: what is larger than your fear deserves your surrender.
bhagwad_gita::384.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Krishna as a teacher to seeing him as the source behind everything.

bhagwad_gita::385.verse_sanskrit: आहुस्त्वामृषयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा । असितो देवलो व्यासः स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे ॥
bhagwad_gita::385.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  परम ब्रह्म, परम धाम और महान् पवित्र आप ही हैं ।  आप शाश्वत, दिव्य पुरुष, आदिदेव, अजन्मा और विभु व्यापक हैं  ऐसा सबकेसब ऋषि, देवर्षि नारद, असित, देवल तथा व्यास कहते हैं और स्वयं आप भी मेरे प्रति कहते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::385.english_translation: All the sages speak of you this way: the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa. You yourself also say this to me.
bhagwad_gita::385.translation_literal: आहुः (they say) / त्वाम् (you) / ऋषयः (the sages) / सर्वे (all) / देवर्षिः (the divine sage) / नारदः (Narada) / तथा (and also) / असितः (Asita) / देवलः (Devala) / व्यासः (Vyasa) / स्वयम् (yourself) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / ब्रवीषि (you speak) / मे (to me)
bhagwad_gita::385.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::385.essence: The deepest recognition is echoed by the wise and by Krishna himself.
bhagwad_gita::385.simple_meaning: Arjuna says that all the great sages, including Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa, speak of Krishna this way, and Krishna himself says the same to him.
bhagwad_gita::385.simple_insight: When every trusted voice agrees, doubt begins to soften.
bhagwad_gita::385.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has begun to see Krishna not just as a charioteer, but as the supreme being. He now points to the authority of sages like Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa to confirm what Krishna has already revealed to him.
bhagwad_gita::385.modern_relevance: You keep doubting a hard truth until the people you trust most all say the same thing. Then the resistance weakens, and you can finally listen.
bhagwad_gita::385.insight: It shifts faith from private doubt to confirmed recognition through respected testimony.

bhagwad_gita::386.verse_sanskrit: सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव । न हि ते भगवन् व्यक्ितं विदुर्देवा न दानवाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::386.verse_hindi: हे केशव  मेरेसे आप जो कुछ कह रहे हैं, यह सब मैं सत्य मानता हूँ ।  हे भगवन्  आपके प्रकट होनेको न तो देवता जानते हैं और न दानव ही जानते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::386.english_translation: I accept as true all that you have said, O Keshava. O Bhagavan, neither the devas nor the asuras know your manifested form.
bhagwad_gita::386.translation_literal: सर्वम् (all) / एतत् (this) / ऋतम् (true) / मन्ये (I consider) / यत् (what) / माम् (to me) / वदसि (you speak) / केशव (O Keshava) / न (not) / हि (indeed) / ते (your) / भगवन् (O Bhagavan) / व्यक्ितम् (manifested form) / विदुः (know) / देवाः (the devas) / न (not) / दानवाः (the asuras)
bhagwad_gita::386.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::386.essence: True recognition begins where ordinary beings cannot see.
bhagwad_gita::386.simple_meaning: Arjuna accepts Krishna's words as true and says that even radiant beings and shadow beings do not understand Krishna's revealed form.
bhagwad_gita::386.simple_insight: Some truths are bigger than ordinary understanding, and humility opens the door to them.
bhagwad_gita::386.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has just heard Krishna describe his divine nature. Overwhelmed, he admits that Krishna's words are true and that even radiant beings and shadow beings cannot grasp Krishna's manifested form. The dialogue is moving toward awe and surrender.
bhagwad_gita::386.modern_relevance: Someone explains something life-changing, and your first instinct is to argue. Arjuna does the opposite: he admits the truth before he fully understands it.
bhagwad_gita::386.insight: It shifts the mind from needing total proof to recognising a reality greater than ordinary perception.

bhagwad_gita::387.verse_sanskrit: स्वयमेवात्मनाऽत्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम । भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते ॥
bhagwad_gita::387.verse_hindi: हे भूतभावन  हे भूतेश  हे देवदेव  हे जगत्पते  हे पुरुषोत्तम  आप स्वयं ही अपनेआपसे अपनेआपको जानते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::387.english_translation: O Supreme Person, you alone know yourself by yourself, O source of all beings, lord of all beings, divine of the divine, ruler of the world.
bhagwad_gita::387.translation_literal: स्वयमेव (by oneself alone) / आत्मना (by the self) / आत्मानम् (the self) / वेत्थ (you know) / त्वम् (you) / पुरुषोत्तम (O Supreme Person) / भूतभावन (O source of beings) / भूतेश (O lord of beings) / देवदेव (O divine of the divine) / जगत्पते (O ruler of the world)
bhagwad_gita::387.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::387.essence: The supreme one is known fully only by the supreme one.
bhagwad_gita::387.simple_meaning: Arjuna praises Krishna as the Supreme Person who alone fully knows his own nature and rules over all beings.
bhagwad_gita::387.simple_insight: There is relief in meeting a presence greater than explanation, one that already knows itself and the world.
bhagwad_gita::387.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has begun to see Krishna not as a charioteer alone, but as the Supreme Person behind all existence. He bows in awe and says that Krishna alone fully knows his own nature, while all beings depend on him.
bhagwad_gita::387.modern_relevance: You sit across from someone whose motives you cannot read, yet they seem to hold the whole room together. This verse names that rare recognition: some presence is deeper than your questions.
bhagwad_gita::387.insight: It shifts reverence from asking for proof to recognising a reality that is self-luminous and complete.

bhagwad_gita::388.verse_sanskrit: वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः । याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::388.verse_hindi: जिन विभूतियोंसे आप इन सम्पूर्ण लोकोंको व्याप्त करके स्थित हैं, उन सभी अपनी दिव्य विभूतियोंका सम्पूर्णतासे वर्णन करनेमें आप ही समर्थ हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::388.english_translation: Only you can fully describe your own divine manifestations, by which you pervade and sustain all these worlds.
bhagwad_gita::388.translation_literal: वक्तुमर्हसि (you are able to speak) / अशेषेण (completely) / दिव्याः (divine) / हि (indeed) / आत्मविभूतयः (your own manifestations) / याभिः (by which) / विभूतिभिः (with manifestations) / लोकान् (the worlds) / इमान् (these) / त्वम् (you) / व्याप्य (pervading) / तिष्ठसि (you stand)
bhagwad_gita::388.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::388.essence: Only the source can fully name its own presence in the world.
bhagwad_gita::388.simple_meaning: Arjuna says only Krishna can fully explain his own divine manifestations, because Krishna pervades and supports all the worlds through them.
bhagwad_gita::388.simple_insight: Awe becomes humility: the more reality is seen, the more limited ordinary language feels.
bhagwad_gita::388.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has already admitted that Krishna's nature surpasses ordinary sight. Now, overwhelmed by the revelations, he asks Krishna to describe completely the divine manifestations through which Krishna fills and holds every world.
bhagwad_gita::388.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence seems to change the whole room, but you cannot explain why. Some realities are only understood by the one who embodies them.
bhagwad_gita::388.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to define the whole to receiving the whole through its living expressions.

bhagwad_gita::389.verse_sanskrit: कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन् । केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया ॥
bhagwad_gita::389.verse_hindi: हे योगिन्  हरदम साङ्गोपाङ्ग चिन्तन करता हुआ मैं आपको कैसे जानूँ  और हे भगवन्  किनकिन भावोंमें आप मेरे द्वारा चिन्तन किये जा सकते हैं अर्थात् किनकिन भावोंमें मैं आपका चिन्तन करूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::389.english_translation: O Yogi, how shall I know You by constant contemplation? In what forms should You be contemplated, O Blessed One?
bhagwad_gita::389.translation_literal: कथम् (how) / विद्याम् (may I know) / अहम् (I) / योगिन् (O Yogi) / त्वाम् (You) / सदा (always) / परिचिन्तयन् (contemplating fully) / केषु केषु (in which which) / च (and) / भावेषु (in forms / states) / चिन्त्यः (to be contemplated) / असि (You are) / भगवन् (O Blessed One) / मया (by me)
bhagwad_gita::389.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::389.essence: Devotion needs a form the mind can return to again and again.
bhagwad_gita::389.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna how to keep remembering him and in what forms he should meditate on him.
bhagwad_gita::389.simple_insight: Love wants a way to remember. The heart asks for a thousand doors back to the beloved.
bhagwad_gita::389.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has moved from fear to reverence. After asking Krishna to describe his divine manifestations, he now asks how to hold Krishna in constant contemplation and through which forms that remembrance should happen.
bhagwad_gita::389.modern_relevance: You meet someone who changed your life, then realise you keep forgetting what made them matter. The mind wants a concrete way to stay oriented toward what it reveres.
bhagwad_gita::389.insight: It shifts devotion from vague feeling to specific remembrance through form, image, and attention.

bhagwad_gita::390.verse_sanskrit: विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन । भूयः कथय तृप्तिर्हि श्रृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::390.verse_hindi: हे जनार्दन  आप अपने योग सामर्थ्य को और विभूतियोंको विस्तारसे फिर कहिये क्योंकि आपके अमृतमय वचन सुनतेसुनते मेरी तृप्ति नहीं हो रही है ॥
bhagwad_gita::390.english_translation: O Janardana, tell me again in detail of Your yogic power and Your manifestations, for I am not satisfied hearing Your nectar-like words.
bhagwad_gita::390.translation_literal: विस्तरेण (in detail) / आत्मनः (of Your own) / योगम् (yogic power) / विभूतिम् (manifestations) / च (and) / जनार्दन (O Janardana) / भूयः (again) / कथय (tell) / तृप्तिः (satisfaction) / हि (indeed) / श्रृण्वतः (for the one hearing) / नास्ति (is not) / मे (my) / अमृतम् (nectar-like) / [वचनम्] (words)
bhagwad_gita::390.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::390.essence: True devotion never feels finished hearing the beloved.
bhagwad_gita::390.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to keep speaking about his divine powers and forms, because hearing about them never feels complete.
bhagwad_gita::390.simple_insight: Love for the divine does not run out of listening; it deepens with more hearing.
bhagwad_gita::390.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has stopped asking about war and started asking about Krishna himself. After hearing some of Krishna’s divine manifestations, he wants more. This verse shows devotion turning into an endless hunger to know the beloved more fully.
bhagwad_gita::390.modern_relevance: You find one line in a talk that opens something in you, and you replay it again and again on the walk home. Real longing does not get bored; it wants deeper contact.
bhagwad_gita::390.insight: It shifts attention from getting an answer to staying in living contact with what inspires reverence.

bhagwad_gita::391.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचहन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः । प्राधान्यतः कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे ॥
bhagwad_gita::391.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हाँ, ठीक है ।  मैं अपनी दिव्य विभूतियोंको तेरे लिये प्रधानतासे संक्षेपसे कहूँगा क्योंकि हे कुरुश्रेष्ठ  मेरी विभूतियोंके विस्तारका अन्त नहीं है ॥
bhagwad_gita::391.english_translation: Krishna said: I will tell you briefly of my divine manifestations, chief of them, Arjuna, for there is no end to their विस्तार.
bhagwad_gita::391.translation_literal: श्रीभगवानुवाच (the Blessed Lord said) / हन्त (indeed) / ते (to you) / कथयिष्यामि (I will tell) / दिव्याः (divine) / हि (indeed) / आत्मविभूतयः (my own manifestations) / प्राधान्यतः (chiefly / in the main) / कुरुश्रेष्ठ (O best of the Kurus) / नास्ति (there is not) / अन्तः (end) / विस्तरस्य (of the विस्तार / spread) / मे (of me)
bhagwad_gita::391.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::391.essence: The divine can be named briefly, never exhausted.
bhagwad_gita::391.simple_meaning: Krishna agrees to describe his chief divine manifestations, but only in brief, because his full extent has no limit.
bhagwad_gita::391.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing the divine presence cannot be exhausted or fully measured.
bhagwad_gita::391.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna keeps asking Krishna to explain how to remember him in daily life. Krishna now answers by promising a selective list of his chief manifestations, while making clear that his full greatness cannot be contained in any list.
bhagwad_gita::391.modern_relevance: You ask someone to explain what keeps them steady through chaos, and they give you a few examples — then admit the real answer is bigger than any summary.
bhagwad_gita::391.insight: It shifts attention from trying to catalogue the divine to recognising its limitless presence in what stands out most.

bhagwad_gita::392.verse_sanskrit: अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः । अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥
bhagwad_gita::392.verse_hindi: हे नींदको जीतनेवाले अर्जुन  सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके आदि, मध्य तथा अन्तमें भी मैं ही हूँ और प्राणियोंके अन्तःकरणमें आत्मरूपसे भी मैं ही स्थित हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::392.english_translation: I am the Self, O Gudakesha, seated in the heart of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of all beings.
bhagwad_gita::392.translation_literal: अहम् (I am) / आत्मा (the Self) / गुडाकेश (O Gudakesha) / सर्वभूताशयस्थितः (standing in the heart of all beings) / अहम् (I am) / आदिः (the beginning) / च (and) / मध्यम् (the middle) / च (and) / भूतानाम् (of beings) / अन्तः (the end) / एव (indeed) / च (and)
bhagwad_gita::392.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::392.essence: Everything that exists is held within one enduring presence.
bhagwad_gita::392.simple_meaning: Krishna says he lives within every being as the inner self and is present at every stage of existence: beginning, middle, and end.
bhagwad_gita::392.simple_insight: You are held inside something far larger than your private story.
bhagwad_gita::392.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna asks to hear more of Krishna’s divine manifestations. Krishna answers that he is not distant: he dwells in the heart of every being and is present at every stage of life, from origin to completion.
bhagwad_gita::392.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone in a hospital corridor, watching a life change in silence. This verse says the deepest presence is already there, inside every beginning, middle, and ending.
bhagwad_gita::392.insight: It shifts attention from scattered appearances to the single presence running through all change.

bhagwad_gita::393.verse_sanskrit: आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान् । मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी ॥
bhagwad_gita::393.verse_hindi: मैं अदितिके पुत्रोंमें विष्णु वामन और प्रकाशमान वस्तुओंमें किरणोंवाला सूर्य हूँ ।  मैं मरुतोंका तेज और नक्षत्रोंका अधिपति चन्द्रमा हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::393.english_translation: Among the sons of Aditi, I am Vishnu; among radiant things, I am the sun with rays. I am the brilliance in the Maruts, and among stars, I am the moon.
bhagwad_gita::393.translation_literal: आदित्यानाम् (among the sons of Aditi) / अहम् (I am) / विष्णुः (Vishnu) / ज्योतिषाम् (among radiant things) / रविः (the sun) / अंशुमान् (having rays) / मरीचिः (the brilliance) / मरुताम् (of the Maruts) / अस्मि (I am) / नक्षत्राणाम् (among stars) / अहम् (I am) / शशी (the moon)
bhagwad_gita::393.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::393.essence: Every radiance is a sign of one presence.
bhagwad_gita::393.simple_meaning: Krishna says he appears as Vishnu among the sons of Aditi, as the sun among bright things, as the Maruts' brilliance, and as the moon among stars.
bhagwad_gita::393.simple_insight: The world is not separate from the divine presence you move through every day.
bhagwad_gita::393.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Krishna has begun revealing how his presence fills the world. To Arjuna, he names familiar cosmic powers one by one, showing that the forces of light, brilliance, and order are not random—they are expressions of him.
bhagwad_gita::393.modern_relevance: You step outside after a sleepless night and the morning light hits your face. The warmth, the brightness, the quiet order in it all can feel like more than weather — like presence.
bhagwad_gita::393.insight: It shifts attention from isolated objects to the sacred source shining through them.

bhagwad_gita::394.verse_sanskrit: वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः । इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना ॥
bhagwad_gita::394.verse_hindi: मैं वेदोंमें सामवेद हूँ, देवताओंमें इन्द्र हूँ, इन्द्रियोंमें मन हूँ और प्राणियोंकी चेतना हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::394.english_translation: Among the Vedas, I am the Sama Veda; among the radiant beings, I am Indra. Among the senses, I am the mind; among living beings, I am consciousness.
bhagwad_gita::394.translation_literal: वेदानाम् (among the Vedas) / सामवेदः (the Sama Veda) / अस्मि (I am) / देवानाम् (among the radiant beings) / अस्मि (I am) / वासवः (Indra) / इन्द्रियाणाम् (among the senses) / मनः (mind) / च (and) / अस्मि (I am) / भूतानाम् (among living beings) / अस्मि (I am) / चेतना (consciousness)
bhagwad_gita::394.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::394.essence: The divine is not elsewhere; it is the awareness within everything.
bhagwad_gita::394.simple_meaning: Krishna says he appears as the highest sacred chant, as Indra among radiant beings, as the mind among the senses, and as awareness in all living things.
bhagwad_gita::394.simple_insight: The world is not separate from the divine; even your own mind is a meeting place with it.
bhagwad_gita::394.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has asked for a way to see Krishna everywhere. Krishna answers by naming where his presence shines most clearly: in sacred sound, in the power of Indra, in the mind that guides the senses, and in the awareness inside every living being.
bhagwad_gita::394.modern_relevance: You are sitting in a noisy train, trying to steady yourself before a painful conversation. The calm, the clarity, the awareness watching your fear — all of it can be seen as sacred presence, not random accident.
bhagwad_gita::394.insight: It shifts attention from isolated objects to the living presence that animates them.

bhagwad_gita::395.verse_sanskrit: रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम् । वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरुः शिखरिणामहम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::395.verse_hindi: रुद्रोंमें शंकर और यक्षराक्षसोंमें कुबेर मैं हूँ । वसुओंमें पावक अग्नि और शिखरवाले पर्वतोंमें सुमेरु मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::395.english_translation: Among the Rudras, I am Shankara; among the Yakshas and Rakshasas, I am Kubera. Among the Vasus, I am fire, and among mountain peaks, I am Mount Meru.
bhagwad_gita::395.translation_literal: रुद्राणाम् (among the Rudras) / शङ्करः (Shankara) / च (and) / अस्मि (I am) / वित्तेशः (Kubera, lord of wealth) / यक्षरक्षसाम् (of Yakshas and Rakshasas) / वसूनाम् (among the Vasus) / पावकः (fire) / च (and) / अस्मि (I am) / मेरुः (Meru) / शिखरिणाम् (of mountain peaks) / अहम् (I)
bhagwad_gita::395.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::395.essence: Greatness in the world is a visible sign of Krishna's presence.
bhagwad_gita::395.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is present as the brightest or most powerful form within Rudras, Yakshas, Vasus, fire, and Mount Meru.
bhagwad_gita::395.simple_insight: The world is not separate from the divine; its greatest powers are already expressions of that presence.
bhagwad_gita::395.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna frozen between grief and duty, Krishna keeps revealing how the world is filled with his presence. He points to revered powers, wealth, fire, and the highest mountain peak to show that nothing magnificent stands outside him.
bhagwad_gita::395.modern_relevance: You stand at a cliff edge at dawn and feel the wind, the heat, the vastness, the pull of awe. The world is not empty matter; its grandeur can wake reverence.
bhagwad_gita::395.insight: It shifts attention from isolated objects to the sacred force shining through their greatest forms.

bhagwad_gita::396.verse_sanskrit: पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् । सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः ॥
bhagwad_gita::396.verse_hindi: हे पार्थ  पुरोहितोंमें मुख्य बृहस्पतिको मेरा स्वरूप समझो ।  सेनापतियोंमें स्कन्द और जलाशयोंमें समुद्र मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::396.english_translation: Among priests, know Me as Brihaspati; among commanders, I am Skanda; among waters, I am the ocean.
bhagwad_gita::396.translation_literal: पुरोधसाम् (among priests) / च (and) / मुख्यम् (the chief) / माम् (Me) / विद्धि (know) / पार्थ (O Partha) / बृहस्पतिम् (Brihaspati) / सेनानीनाम् (among commanders) / अहम् (I) / स्कन्दः (Skanda) / सरसाम् (among waters) / अस्मि (am) / सागरः (the ocean)
bhagwad_gita::396.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::396.essence: Greatness in the world is a trace of Krishna everywhere.
bhagwad_gita::396.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the highest among priests, the commander Skanda, and the ocean among all waters.
bhagwad_gita::396.simple_insight: The world is not separate from the divine presence you move through every day.
bhagwad_gita::396.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna keeps revealing how his presence shows up in the world around Arjuna. After naming the greatest among beings and powers, he points to Brihaspati, Skanda, and the ocean to show that excellence and vastness are reflections of him.
bhagwad_gita::396.modern_relevance: You stand at the shore after a hard day and feel small before the dark water. The verse says that same vastness is not empty — it is a sign of the divine everywhere.
bhagwad_gita::396.insight: It trains the mind to recognise greatness, order, and depth as expressions of one source.

bhagwad_gita::397.verse_sanskrit: महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् । यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालयः ॥
bhagwad_gita::397.verse_hindi: महर्षियोंमें भृगु और वाणियोंशब्दों में एक अक्षर अर्थात् प्रणव मैं हूँ ।  सम्पूर्ण यज्ञोंमें जपयज्ञ और स्थिर रहनेवालोंमें हिमालय मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::397.english_translation: Among great sages I am Bhrigu; among words I am the one imperishable syllable. Among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetition; among the steadfast I am the Himalayas.
bhagwad_gita::397.translation_literal: महर्षीणाम् (among great sages) / भृगुः (Bhrigu) / अहम् (I am) / गिराम् (among words) / अस्मि (I am) / एकम् (one) / अक्षरम् (imperishable syllable) / यज्ञानाम् (among sacrifices) / जपयज्ञः (sacrifice of silent repetition) / अस्मि (I am) / स्थावराणाम् (among the steadfast) / हिमालयः (the Himalayas)
bhagwad_gita::397.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::397.essence: The divine appears through the noblest forms of speech, ritual, and nature.
bhagwad_gita::397.simple_meaning: Krishna names his presence in sacred sages, sacred sound, silent repetition, and the Himalayas. He is showing that the divine can be found in revered forms across the world.
bhagwad_gita::397.simple_insight: The world feels less random when you start noticing what points beyond itself.
bhagwad_gita::397.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna continues revealing his divine manifestations. After naming earlier glories, Krishna adds more signs of his presence: among sages, sacred speech, sacrifices, and mountains. The teaching is still part of a larger list, not a final climax.
bhagwad_gita::397.modern_relevance: You are standing before a shrine, a mountain, or a line of chant that suddenly quiets you. The moment feels bigger than the object itself, as if something unseen is shining through it.
bhagwad_gita::397.insight: It trains the mind to recognise the divine through symbols, practices, and forms of greatness.

bhagwad_gita::398.verse_sanskrit: अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारदः । गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः ॥
bhagwad_gita::398.verse_hindi: सम्पूर्ण वृक्षोंमें पीपल, देवर्षियोंमें नारद, गन्धर्वोंमें चित्ररथ और सिद्धोंमें कपिल मुनि मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::398.english_translation: Among all trees I am the sacred fig tree. Among divine sages I am Narada; among celestial musicians, Chitraratha; among perfected sages, the sage Kapila.
bhagwad_gita::398.translation_literal: अश्वत्थः (sacred fig tree) / सर्ववृक्षाणां (among all trees) / देवर्षीणां (among divine sages) / च (and) / नारदः (Narada) / गन्धर्वाणां (among celestial musicians) / चित्ररथः (Chitraratha) / सिद्धानां (among perfected beings) / कपिलः (Kapila) / मुनिः (sage)
bhagwad_gita::398.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::398.essence: The finest forms in creation are windows into Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::398.simple_meaning: Krishna names the most revered example in each group of trees, sages, musicians, and perfected beings, showing how his presence appears through the finest forms in creation.
bhagwad_gita::398.simple_insight: The world is full of reminders. What you admire most can point you back to the divine.
bhagwad_gita::398.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen, and Krishna answers not with strategy but with vision. He continues listing the highest expressions of life — a sacred tree, Narada, Chitraratha, Kapila — so Arjuna can learn to recognize Krishna's presence everywhere.
bhagwad_gita::398.modern_relevance: You are walking through a temple garden after a hard decision, and one tree, one song, one face suddenly steadies you. The world keeps offering small doorways back to what matters.
bhagwad_gita::398.insight: It trains the mind to notice excellence in the world as a pointer to the divine presence behind it.

bhagwad_gita::399.verse_sanskrit: उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम् । ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::399.verse_hindi: घोड़ोंमें अमृतके साथ समुद्रसे प्रकट होनेवाले उच्चैःश्रवा नामक घोड़ेको, श्रेष्ठ हाथियोंमें ऐरावत नामक हाथीको और मनुष्योंमें राजाको मेरी विभूति मानो ॥
bhagwad_gita::399.english_translation: Among horses, know me as Ucchaihshravas, born from nectar. Among royal elephants, I am Airavata, and among humans, I am the king.
bhagwad_gita::399.translation_literal: उच्चैःश्रवसम् (Ucchaihshravas) / अश्वानाम् (among horses) / विद्धि (know) / माम् (me) / अमृतोद्भवम् (born from nectar) / ऐरावतम् (Airavata) / गजेन्द्राणाम् (among royal elephants) / नराणाम् (among humans) / च (and) / नराधिपम् (the king)
bhagwad_gita::399.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::399.essence: Greatness in the world is a visible trace of Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::399.simple_meaning: Krishna says to see his presence in the finest horse, the greatest elephant, and the human king.
bhagwad_gita::399.simple_insight: Awe becomes easier when greatness is recognised as a sign of the divine.
bhagwad_gita::399.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen while Krishna reveals how the divine shines through the world. After naming sacred signs in nature, Krishna points to the most majestic horse, elephant, and ruler as further expressions of his presence.
bhagwad_gita::399.modern_relevance: You watch a leader command a room, a rescue dog save a child, a musician hold everyone silent. Something in you knows: greatness is not random.
bhagwad_gita::399.insight: It trains the mind to recognise excellence as a manifestation of the divine, not as mere accident or status.

bhagwad_gita::400.verse_sanskrit: आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक् । प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्पः सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकिः ॥
bhagwad_gita::400.verse_hindi: आयुधोंमें वज्र और धेनुओंमें कामधेनु मैं हूँ ।  सन्तानउत्पत्तिका हेतु कामदेव मैं हूँ और सर्पोंमें वासुकि मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::400.english_translation: Among weapons, I am the thunderbolt; among cows, I am the wish-fulfilling cow. I am the cause of procreation, and among serpents, I am Vasuki.
bhagwad_gita::400.translation_literal: आयुधानाम् (among weapons) / अहम् (I am) / वज्रम् (the thunderbolt) / धेनूनाम् (among cows) / अस्मि (I am) / कामधुक् (the wish-fulfilling cow) / प्रजनः (the cause of procreation) / च (and) / अस्मि (I am) / कन्दर्पः (Kandarpa, desire-born force) / सर्पाणाम् (among serpents) / अस्मि (I am) / वासुकिः (Vasuki)
bhagwad_gita::400.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::400.essence: Power, fertility, and danger all reveal the same source.
bhagwad_gita::400.simple_meaning: Krishna names more of the finest powers and beings in the world as his expressions: thunderbolt, wish-fulfilling cow, the force behind procreation, and Vasuki among serpents.
bhagwad_gita::400.simple_insight: The ordinary world starts to feel charged with presence, not random pieces.
bhagwad_gita::400.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna still needs a wider vision of who Krishna is. Krishna continues listing the highest or most striking forms in creation, showing that the battlefield, the living world, and even desire and force all point back to him.
bhagwad_gita::400.modern_relevance: You notice a flash of lightning over an empty field, then the calm strength of a cow in the next lane. The world feels less like separate objects and more like one living presence.
bhagwad_gita::400.insight: It trains attention to recognise excellence, force, and generative power as signs of the divine everywhere.

bhagwad_gita::401.verse_sanskrit: अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम् । पितृ़णामर्यमा चास्मि यमः संयमतामहम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::401.verse_hindi: नागोंमें अनन्त शेषनाग और जलजन्तुओंका अधिपति वरुण मैं हूँ ।  पितरोंमें अर्यमा और शासन करनेवालोंमें यमराज मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::401.english_translation: Among serpents I am Ananta; among water beings I am Varuna. Among ancestors I am Aryaman; among those who govern, I am Yama.
bhagwad_gita::401.translation_literal: अनन्तः (Ananta) / च (and) / अस्मि (I am) / नागानाम् (of serpents) / वरुणः (Varuna) / यादसाम् (of water beings) / अहम् (I) / पितृणाम् (of ancestors) / अर्यमा (Aryaman) / च (and) / अस्मि (I am) / यमः (Yama) / संयमताम् (of those who govern) / अहम् (I am)
bhagwad_gita::401.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::401.essence: The divine is visible in every order of existence.
bhagwad_gita::401.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the highest presence among serpents, water beings, ancestors, and rulers. He is showing that his presence runs through every level of the world.
bhagwad_gita::401.simple_insight: Nothing is spiritually ordinary; even structures of power and lineage can be seen as sacred.
bhagwad_gita::401.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is overwhelmed and Krishna begins revealing how his presence appears throughout the world. Here he names serpents, water beings, ancestors, and rulers, showing that the same divine reality animates both nature and social order.
bhagwad_gita::401.modern_relevance: You sit in a room full of titles, family history, and hidden hierarchies. This verse asks you to see the same sacred presence moving through all of it, not just in obvious holy moments.
bhagwad_gita::401.insight: It shifts attention from isolated things to the one presence expressed through many forms.

bhagwad_gita::402.verse_sanskrit: प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम् । मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::402.verse_hindi: दैत्योंमें प्रह्लाद और गणना करनेवालोंमें काल मैं हूँ  ।  पशुओंमें सिंह और पक्षियोंमें गरुड मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::402.english_translation: Among the daityas I am Prahlada; among calculators I am Time. Among beasts I am the lion, and among birds I am Garuda.
bhagwad_gita::402.translation_literal: प्रह्लादः (Prahlada) / च (and) / अस्मि (I am) / दैत्यानाम् (among the daityas) / कालः (Time) / कलयताम् (among those who count) / अहम् (I) / मृगाणाम् (among beasts) / च (and) / मृगेन्द्रः (lion) / अहम् (I) / वैनतेयः (Garuda) / च (and) / पक्षिणाम् (among birds)
bhagwad_gita::402.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::402.essence: Power, devotion, and majesty are all windows into one presence.
bhagwad_gita::402.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is present as Prahlada among the daityas, as Time among those who count, as the lion among beasts, and as Garuda among birds.
bhagwad_gita::402.simple_insight: Strength and devotion are not separate from the divine presence.
bhagwad_gita::402.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is overwhelmed and Krishna begins revealing where divine presence can be seen in the world. He names Prahlada, Time, the lion, and Garuda to show that greatness, power, and devotion all point back to him.
