bhagwad_gita::402.modern_relevance: You watch a child protect a smaller one, or see fierce courage in someone facing illness without flinching. The same force that makes greatness visible is not random — it carries a deeper presence.
bhagwad_gita::402.insight: It trains the mind to recognise the divine in excellence, courage, and devoted steadfastness.

bhagwad_gita::403.verse_sanskrit: पवनः पवतामस्मि रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम् । झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी ॥
bhagwad_gita::403.verse_hindi: पवित्र करनेवालोंमें वायु और शास्त्रधारियोंमें राम मैं हूँ ।  जलजन्तुओंमें मगर मैं हूँ ।  बहनेवाले स्त्रोतोंमें गङ्गाजी मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::403.english_translation: Among purifiers, I am the wind. Among wielders of weapons, I am Rama. Among aquatic beings, I am the crocodile. Among flowing rivers, I am the Ganga.
bhagwad_gita::403.translation_literal: पवनः (the wind) / पवताम् (among purifiers) / अस्मि (I am) / रामः (Rama) / शस्त्रभृताम् (among weapon-bearers) / अहम् (I) / झषाणाम् (among aquatic beings) / मकरः (the crocodile) / च (and) / अस्मि (I am) / स्रोतसाम् (among streams) / अस्मि (I am) / जाह्नवी (the Ganga)
bhagwad_gita::403.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::403.essence: One reality appears as every noble force.
bhagwad_gita::403.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the purifying wind, Rama among warriors, the crocodile among water beings, and the Ganga among rivers.
bhagwad_gita::403.simple_insight: The world becomes charged with meaning when you start seeing the divine in its strongest forms.
bhagwad_gita::403.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Krishna continues showing Arjuna how the highest reality appears through the world’s finest powers. He points to wind, Rama, the crocodile, and the Ganga as living signs of his presence, widening Arjuna’s vision before the war begins.
bhagwad_gita::403.modern_relevance: You are standing by a river at dawn, exhausted and unsure. Then a sudden gust, the current, and the sheer force of nature make your private crisis feel smaller and more bearable.
bhagwad_gita::403.insight: It trains the mind to recognise one sacred presence shining through many forms.

bhagwad_gita::404.verse_sanskrit: सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन । अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वादः प्रवदतामहम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::404.verse_hindi: हे अर्जुन  सम्पूर्ण सर्गोंके आदि, मध्य तथा अन्तमें मैं ही हूँ ।  विद्याओंमें अध्यात्मविद्या और परस्पर शास्त्रार्थ करनेवालोंकातत्त्वनिर्णयके लिये किया जानेवाला वाद मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::404.english_translation: I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of all creation, Arjuna. Among all forms of knowledge, I am the knowledge of the true self; among speakers, I am the reasoned debate that seeks truth.
bhagwad_gita::404.translation_literal: सर्गाणाम् (of creations) / आदिः (the beginning) / अन्तः (the end) / च (and) / मध्यं (the middle) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / अहम् (I) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / अध्यात्मविद्या (knowledge of the true self) / विद्यानाम् (among knowledges) / वादः (reasoned debate) / प्रवदताम् (among those who speak) / अहम् (I)
bhagwad_gita::404.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::404.essence: All creation and all truth-seeking speech point back to Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::404.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the beginning, middle, and end of all creation. He is also the deepest self-knowledge and the honest debate that seeks truth.
bhagwad_gita::404.simple_insight: Reality is not random or separate from the divine; even truth-seeking speech belongs to that same presence.
bhagwad_gita::404.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna keeps revealing where the divine can be seen. After naming many visible forms, Krishna says he is the start, middle, and end of every creation, and the truth-seeking debate among those who study.
bhagwad_gita::404.modern_relevance: You are in a room where two people argue past each other, each trying to win. Krishna points to the kind of speech that actually searches for truth, not ego.
bhagwad_gita::404.insight: It shifts attention from isolated facts to the presence that holds every beginning, process, and ending together.

bhagwad_gita::405.verse_sanskrit: अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्वः सामासिकस्य च । अहमेवाक्षयः कालो धाताऽहं विश्वतोमुखः ॥
bhagwad_gita::405.verse_hindi: अक्षरोंमें अकार और समासोंमें द्वन्द्व समास मैं हूँ ।  अक्षयकाल अर्थात् कालका भी महाकाल तथा सब ओर मुखवाला धाता भी मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::405.english_translation: Among letters I am the letter A. Among compounds I am the dual compound. I am endless time itself, and I am the all-facing sustainer.
bhagwad_gita::405.translation_literal: अक्षराणाम् (among letters) / अकारः (the letter A) / अस्मि (I am) / द्वन्द्वः (dual compound) / सामासिकस्य (among compounds) / च (and) / अहम् (I) / एव (indeed) / अक्षयः (imperishable / endless) / कालः (time) / धाता (sustainer / creator) / अहम् (I am) / विश्वतोमुखः (having faces everywhere / all-facing)
bhagwad_gita::405.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::405.essence: Even letters and time carry Krishna's presence.
bhagwad_gita::405.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is present in the first letter, in a basic kind of compound word, in endless time, and in the all-facing power that sustains the world.
bhagwad_gita::405.simple_insight: The ordinary and the immense are not separate. What seems small still carries the divine presence.
bhagwad_gita::405.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna frozen and the war still waiting, Krishna keeps unfolding how he appears in everything. After naming rivers, winds, and forms of knowledge, he points to language, time, and the power that holds the world together.
bhagwad_gita::405.modern_relevance: You open a book before a hard exam, and even the first letter feels heavy. Or you watch a clock after a loss and realize time itself has become the thing you cannot outrun.
bhagwad_gita::405.insight: It trains the mind to notice the sacred pattern inside language, time, and structure instead of treating them as ordinary background.

bhagwad_gita::406.verse_sanskrit: मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् । कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा ॥
bhagwad_gita::406.verse_hindi: सबका हरण करनेवाली मृत्यु और उत्पन्न होनेवालोंका उभ्दव मैं हूँ तथा स्त्रीजातिमें कीर्ति, श्री, वाक्, स्मृति, मेधा, धृति और क्षमा मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::406.english_translation: I am death that takes everything, and the source of all future beings. Among women, I am fame, fortune, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness, and forgiveness.
bhagwad_gita::406.translation_literal: मृत्युः (death) / सर्वहरः (all-taking) / च (and) / अहम् (I am) / उद्भवः (origin) / च (and) / भविष्यताम् (of those yet to come) । कीर्तिः (fame) / श्रीः (splendour, fortune) / वाक् (speech) / च (and) / नारीणाम् (among women) / स्मृतिः (memory) / मेधा (intelligence) / धृतिः (steadfastness) / क्षमा (forgiveness)
bhagwad_gita::406.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::406.essence: Even death and virtue are expressions of the same divine source.
bhagwad_gita::406.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is both the force that ends all lives and the source of all that is yet to come. He also shines as noble qualities in women: fame, beauty, speech, memory, intelligence, steadiness, and forgiveness.
bhagwad_gita::406.simple_insight: Nothing precious is outside the divine presence, not even the qualities you admire in people.
bhagwad_gita::406.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Krishna keeps revealing where he can be seen in the world. After naming letters, time, and beginnings, he now points Arjuna to death, birth, and human excellence itself. The teaching widens from cosmic power to the qualities that make life dignified.
bhagwad_gita::406.modern_relevance: At a hospital bedside, a family watches both an ending and a beginning at once. This verse helps you see that loss, birth, and every admirable human quality can all be held within one larger presence.
bhagwad_gita::406.insight: It shifts attention from isolated events and traits to the larger source that holds them all.

bhagwad_gita::407.verse_sanskrit: बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम् । मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकरः ॥
bhagwad_gita::407.verse_hindi: गायी जानेवाली श्रुतियोंमें बृहत्साम और वैदिक छन्दोंमें गायत्री छन्द मैं हूँ ।  बारह महीनोंमें मार्गशीर्ष और छः ऋतुओंमें वसन्त मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::407.english_translation: Among hymns I am the Brihat-Sama; among meters I am Gayatri. Among months I am Margashirsha; among seasons I am spring.
bhagwad_gita::407.translation_literal: बृहत्साम (the Brihat-Sama hymn) / तथा (and) / साम्नाम् (among hymns) / गायत्री (Gayatri) / छन्दसाम् (among meters) / अहम् (I am) / मासानाम् (among months) / मार्गशीर्षः (Margashirsha) / अहम् (I am) / ऋतूनाम् (among seasons) / कुसुमाकरः (spring)
bhagwad_gita::407.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::407.essence: Sacred sound, time, and spring all carry the same presence.
bhagwad_gita::407.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the finest sacred chant, the most revered meter, the best month, and the season of spring.
bhagwad_gita::407.simple_insight: Beauty, rhythm, and renewal are not separate from the divine presence.
bhagwad_gita::407.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna keeps expanding Arjuna's vision of where he can be found. After naming death, memory, and speech as his forms, he now points to sacred sound, time, and the turning of the seasons. The teaching is that nothing beautiful or ordered stands outside him.
bhagwad_gita::407.modern_relevance: You hear a hymn in a temple and feel your chest soften. You notice first rain after a dry stretch and something in you wakes up. Krishna says that recognition is not accidental.
bhagwad_gita::407.insight: It shifts attention from isolated beauty to the presence shining through it.

bhagwad_gita::408.verse_sanskrit: द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् । जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::408.verse_hindi: छल करनेवालोंमें जूआ और तेजस्वियोंमें तेज मैं हूँ ।  जीतनेवालोंकी विजय, निश्चय करनेवालोंका निश्चय और सात्त्विक मनुष्योंका सात्त्विक भाव मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::408.english_translation: Among deceivers I am gambling, among the vigorous I am splendor. I am victory, I am resolve, and I am the goodness of the good.
bhagwad_gita::408.translation_literal: द्यूतम् (gambling) / छलयताम् (among deceivers) / अस्मि (I am) / तेजः (splendor) / तेजस्विनाम् (of the vigorous) / अहम् (I) / जयः (victory) / अस्मि (I am) / व्यवसायः (resolve) / अस्मि (I am) / सत्त्वम् (goodness) / सत्त्ववताम् (of the good) / अहम् (I am)
bhagwad_gita::408.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::408.essence: What shines through victory and resolve is not separate from the divine.
bhagwad_gita::408.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is present as the force behind victory, determination, and the goodness found in noble people.
bhagwad_gita::408.simple_insight: Your best qualities are not isolated achievements; they are signs of a larger presence moving through you.
bhagwad_gita::408.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna keeps revealing where divine power appears in ordinary and extraordinary forms. Here Krishna says that even victory, firm resolve, and noble character are expressions of him.
bhagwad_gita::408.modern_relevance: You finally make the hard call after weeks of fear, and the steadiness in that moment feels bigger than personal confidence. This verse names that strength.
bhagwad_gita::408.insight: It shifts the mind from owning success to recognising the source of strength behind success.

bhagwad_gita::409.verse_sanskrit: वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनंजयः । मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासः कवीनामुशना कविः ॥
bhagwad_gita::409.verse_hindi: वृष्णिवंशियोंमें वासुदेव और पाण्डवोंमें धनञ्जय मैं हूँ ।  मुनियोंमें वेदव्यास और कवियोंमें कवि शुक्राचार्य भी मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::409.english_translation: Among the Vrishnis I am Vasudeva; among the Pandavas I am Dhananjaya. Among sages I am Vyasa, and among poets I am Ushana, the poet.
bhagwad_gita::409.translation_literal: वृष्णीनाम् (among the Vrishnis) / वासुदेवः (Vasudeva) / अस्मि (I am) / पाण्डवानाम् (among the Pandavas) / धनंजयः (Dhananjaya) / मुनीनाम् (among sages) / अपि (also) / अहम् (I) / व्यासः (Vyasa) / कवीनाम् (among poets) / उशना (Ushana) / कविः (poet)
bhagwad_gita::409.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::409.essence: Greatness in many forms is one presence showing itself.
bhagwad_gita::409.simple_meaning: Krishna says that the finest examples in different groups of people are his expressions. Greatness in warriors, sages, and poets all points back to him.
bhagwad_gita::409.simple_insight: You do not need to chase fragmented ideals; the same presence can shine through many forms.
bhagwad_gita::409.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, while Arjuna stands frozen, Krishna keeps unfolding his divine presence. After naming his manifestations in nature and power, he now points to living human greatness: the might of Dhananjaya, the wisdom of Vyasa, the brilliance of great poets.
bhagwad_gita::409.modern_relevance: You meet a mentor, a fighter, and a writer who all seem to carry the same rare force. Instead of worshipping separate idols, you begin to sense one current moving through them all.
bhagwad_gita::409.insight: It shifts the mind from isolated admiration to seeing one source expressed in many gifts.

bhagwad_gita::410.verse_sanskrit: दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम् । मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::410.verse_hindi: दमन करनेवालोंमें दण्डनीति और विजय चाहनेवालोंमें नीति मैं हूँ ।  गोपनीय भावोंमें मौन और ज्ञानवानोंमें ज्ञान मैं हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::410.english_translation: Among enforcers, I am punishment; among those seeking victory, I am policy. Among secrets, I am silence; among the wise, I am knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::410.translation_literal: दण्डः (punishment/discipline) / दमयताम् (among those who restrain) / अस्मि (I am) / नीतिḥ (policy/right conduct) / अस्मि (I am) / जिगीषताम् (among those who seek victory) । / मौनम् (silence) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / अस्मि (I am) / गुह्यानाम् (among secrets) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / ज्ञानवताम् (among the wise) / अहम् (I am)
bhagwad_gita::410.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::410.essence: True power is measured by restraint, silence, and clear understanding.
bhagwad_gita::410.simple_meaning: Krishna says he appears as rightful force, strategic conduct, silence, and true understanding wherever they are found.
bhagwad_gita::410.simple_insight: Power does not always shout. The deepest strength can look like restraint, quiet, and clear understanding.
bhagwad_gita::410.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna reveals how the divine works through the world. Here Krishna names four forms of his presence: corrective force, wise strategy, silence, and the knowledge that belongs to the wise.
bhagwad_gita::410.modern_relevance: You are in a room where one harsh word could break everything. The strongest move is not volume — it may be restraint, timing, and the calm choice to say only what is true.
bhagwad_gita::410.insight: It shifts attention from raw force to disciplined, intelligent action shaped by silence.

bhagwad_gita::411.verse_sanskrit: यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन । न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::411.verse_hindi: हे अर्जुन सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंका जो बीज है, वह बीज मैं ही हूँ क्योंकि मेरे बिना कोई भी चरअचर प्राणी नहीं है अर्थात् चरअचर सब कुछ मैं ही हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::411.english_translation: Arjuna, I am the seed of all beings. Without me, nothing moving or unmoving could exist.
bhagwad_gita::411.translation_literal: यच्चापि (and whatever also) / सर्वभूतानाम् (of all beings) / बीजम् (seed) / तत् (that) / अहम् (I am) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / न (not) / तत् (that) / अस्ति (there is) / विना (without) / यत् (which) / स्यात् (would be) / मया (by me) / भूतम् (being) / चराचरम् (moving and unmoving)
bhagwad_gita::411.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::411.essence: All existence grows from one hidden source.
bhagwad_gita::411.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the source of every being. Nothing that moves or stands still can exist without him.
bhagwad_gita::411.simple_insight: You are never truly separate from the source of life.
bhagwad_gita::411.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna still shaken and the battle waiting, Krishna keeps unfolding his divine presence. After naming his manifestations, he says he is the seed of all beings and the source of everything moving and unmoving.
bhagwad_gita::411.modern_relevance: Standing alone in a hospital corridor while waiting for news, it can feel like life has split into separate pieces. This verse says the same source runs through all of it.
bhagwad_gita::411.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing life as scattered events to seeing one living source behind all forms.

bhagwad_gita::412.verse_sanskrit: नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परंतप । एष तूद्देशतः प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया ॥
bhagwad_gita::412.verse_hindi: हे परंतप अर्जुन  मेरी दिव्य विभूतियोंका अन्त नहीं है ।  मैंने तुम्हारे सामने अपनी विभूतियोंका जो विस्तार कहा है, यह तो केवल संक्षेपसे कहा है ॥
bhagwad_gita::412.english_translation: O scorcher of foes, my divine manifestations have no end. What I have described to you is only a brief summary of my vast manifestations.
bhagwad_gita::412.translation_literal: नान्तः (no end) / अस्ति (there is) / मम (of my) / दिव्यानां (of the divine) / विभूतीनां (manifestations) / परंतप (O scorcher of foes) / एषः (this) / तु (only) / उद्देशतः (in brief) / प्रोक्तः (spoken) / विभूतेः (of manifestations) / विस्तारः (expanse) / मया (by me)
bhagwad_gita::412.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::412.essence: No list can contain the divine's endless expressions.
bhagwad_gita::412.simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that his divine manifestations are limitless, and the examples already given are only a brief outline.
bhagwad_gita::412.simple_insight: The world is bigger than your current view, and the sacred can never be fully exhausted by examples.
bhagwad_gita::412.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is hearing Krishna explain how the divine presence appears through countless forms. After naming a few examples, Krishna says those are only a summary, because his manifestations have no limit.
bhagwad_gita::412.modern_relevance: You finally understand one person’s brilliance, then another side of them appears that you never expected. The lesson is humbling: reality always exceeds the list you made.
bhagwad_gita::412.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to contain the divine in examples to recognising endless presence beyond them.

bhagwad_gita::413.verse_sanskrit: यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा । तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसंभवम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::413.verse_hindi: जोजो ऐश्वर्ययुक्त, शोभायुक्त और बलयुक्त प्राणी तथा वस्तु है, उसउसको तुम मेरे ही तेजयोग के अंशसे उत्पन्न हुई समझो ॥
bhagwad_gita::413.english_translation: Whatever being or thing is endowed with splendour, beauty, or power—know that to have arisen from a spark of my radiance.
bhagwad_gita::413.translation_literal: यद्यत् (whatever) / विभूतिमत् (endowed with splendour/power) / सत्त्वम् (being) / श्रीमत् (beautiful, glorious) / ऊर्जितम् (strong, mighty) / एव (indeed) / वा (or) / तत् तत् (that very) / एव (indeed) / अवगच्छ (know) / त्वम् (you) / मम (my) / तेजः-अंश-संभवम् (born from a portion of my radiance)
bhagwad_gita::413.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::413.essence: Every genuine greatness is only a spark of my radiance.
bhagwad_gita::413.simple_meaning: Anything that shines with beauty, strength, or greatness comes from Krishna's radiance. He asks Arjuna to recognize that source in every impressive thing.
bhagwad_gita::413.simple_insight: You can admire greatness without mistaking it for self-made power.
bhagwad_gita::413.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna hears Krishna continue listing the divine manifestations behind the world’s splendor. After saying his glories are endless, Krishna narrows the point: every striking force or beauty is only a trace of his radiance.
bhagwad_gita::413.modern_relevance: You see a leader command a room, a musician fill a hall, or a child radiate unusual courage. The verse asks you not to worship the surface alone, but to notice the source of that brilliance.
bhagwad_gita::413.insight: It shifts attention from isolated excellence to the deeper source behind all excellence.

bhagwad_gita::414.verse_sanskrit: अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन । विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::414.verse_hindi: अथवा हे अर्जुन  तुम्हें इस प्रकार बहुतसी बातें जाननेकी क्या आवश्यकता है मैं अपने किसी एक अंशसे सम्पूर्ण जगत् को व्याप्त करके स्थित हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::414.english_translation: Or, Arjuna, what is the need for all this detailed knowledge? I sustain this entire universe with a single fragment of myself.
bhagwad_gita::414.translation_literal: अथवा (or) / बहुना (with much) / एतेन (by this) / किम् (what) / ज्ञातेन (by knowing) / तव (for you) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / विष्टभ्य (pervading, sustaining) / अहम् (I) / इदम् (this) / कृत्स्नम् (whole) / एकांशेन (with one part) / स्थितः (established) / जगत् (universe)
bhagwad_gita::414.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::414.essence: The whole universe rests in a single fragment of the divine.
bhagwad_gita::414.simple_meaning: Krishna says there is no need for endless detail: even a single part of his presence supports the entire universe.
bhagwad_gita::414.simple_insight: The mind can relax. Reality is already held together by something far larger than your grasp.
bhagwad_gita::414.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, after showing Arjuna his many divine manifestations, Krishna closes the teaching by stepping beyond examples. He tells Arjuna that one fragment of his presence sustains the whole universe, ending the search for a complete inventory of the divine.
bhagwad_gita::414.modern_relevance: You keep asking for one more explanation before you can trust the decision. But sometimes the pattern is already clear, and the rest is just your mind delaying surrender.
bhagwad_gita::414.insight: It shifts attention from counting manifestations to recognising the single source behind them all.

bhagwad_gita::415.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचमदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसंज्ञितम् । यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम ॥
bhagwad_gita::415.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  केवल मेरेपर कृपा करनेके लिये ही आपने जो परम गोपनीय अध्यात्मतत्तव जाननेका वचन कहा, उससे मेरा यह मोह नष्ट हो गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::415.english_translation: Arjuna said: By the gracious words you spoke for my benefit alone, my delusion has been dispelled.
bhagwad_gita::415.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / मदनुग्रहाय (for my grace / for my benefit) / परमम् (supreme) / गुह्यम् (secret) / अध्यात्मसंज्ञितम् (called concerning the inner self) / यत् (which) / त्वया उक्तम् (spoken by you) / वचः (words) / तेन (by that) / मोहः अयम् (this delusion) / विगतः (has gone away) / मम (of mine)
bhagwad_gita::415.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::415.essence: Clarity arrives when the hidden teaching is finally heard as personal grace.
bhagwad_gita::415.simple_meaning: Arjuna says Krishna’s hidden teaching has cleared away his confusion. He feels the words were spoken just for his own good.
bhagwad_gita::415.simple_insight: Real understanding can feel like a fog lifting all at once.
bhagwad_gita::415.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has just heard Krishna speak about the deepest spiritual truth. Before the cosmic vision appears, he pauses in gratitude, saying that Krishna’s secret teaching has already removed his confusion.
bhagwad_gita::415.modern_relevance: After a hard conversation, you suddenly see what you were avoiding all along. The relief is not in winning the argument, but in having the fog lift.
bhagwad_gita::415.insight: It shifts the mind from confusion to gratitude, recognizing clarity as a gift received.

bhagwad_gita::416.verse_sanskrit: भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया । त्वत्तः कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::416.verse_hindi: हे कमलनयन  सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंकी उत्पत्ति और प्रलय मैंने विस्तारपूर्वक आपसे ही सुना है और आपका अविनाशी माहात्म्य भी सुना है ॥
bhagwad_gita::416.english_translation: O lotus-eyed one, I have heard from You in detail about the arising and passing away of all beings, and also about Your imperishable majesty.
bhagwad_gita::416.translation_literal: भवाप्ययौ (arising and passing away) / हि (indeed) / भूतानाम् (of beings) / श्रुतौ (have been heard) / विस्तरशः (in detail) / मया (by me) / त्वत्तः (from You) / कमलपत्राक्ष (O lotus-eyed one) / माहात्म्यम् (majesty) / अपि (also) / च (and) / अव्ययम् (imperishable)
bhagwad_gita::416.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::416.essence: All change is clear only beside what does not change.
bhagwad_gita::416.simple_meaning: Arjuna says he has learned from Krishna about how all beings come and go, and about Krishna's imperishable greatness.
bhagwad_gita::416.simple_insight: Real reverence begins when you see the source behind all change.
bhagwad_gita::416.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has stopped arguing and started seeing. After Krishna's teaching, he says he has understood the rise and fall of all beings and Krishna's imperishable greatness. This prepares him to ask for the cosmic form.
bhagwad_gita::416.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone who has just told you the hard truth, and the room goes quiet. The facts land, but what stays with you is the sense of something larger that cannot be shaken.
bhagwad_gita::416.insight: It shifts attention from the changing world to the unchanging source that gives it meaning.

bhagwad_gita::417.verse_sanskrit: एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर । द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम ॥
bhagwad_gita::417.verse_hindi: हे पुरुषोत्तम  आप अपनेआपको जैसा कहते हैं, यह वास्तवमें ऐसा ही है ।  हे परमेश्वर  आपके ईश्वरसम्बन्धी रूपको मैं देखना चाहता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::417.english_translation: O Supreme Person, everything you have said about yourself is true. Yet I wish to see your divine form.
bhagwad_gita::417.translation_literal: एवम् (thus) / एतत् (this) / यथा (as) / आथ्थ (you have said) / त्वम् (you) / आत्मानम् (yourself) / परमेश्वर (O Supreme Lord) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / इच्छामि (I wish) / ते (your) / रूपम् (form) / ऐश्वरम् (divine) / पुरुषोत्तम (O Supreme Person)
bhagwad_gita::417.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::417.essence: Belief becomes complete only when it wants to see.
bhagwad_gita::417.simple_meaning: Arjuna accepts Krishna’s words as true, but asks to see Krishna’s divine form directly.
bhagwad_gita::417.simple_insight: Trust can deepen into longing for direct experience, not just belief.
bhagwad_gita::417.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has already heard Krishna explain his divine greatness. The armies still wait, the crisis is still alive, and Arjuna now asks for something beyond words: direct sight of Krishna’s supreme, divine form.
bhagwad_gita::417.modern_relevance: A friend explains something painful and true, and you nod because you believe them. But part of you still needs to see the full reality for yourself before you can move forward.
bhagwad_gita::417.insight: It shifts the seeker from verbal understanding to direct vision.

bhagwad_gita::418.verse_sanskrit: मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो । योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयाऽत्मानमव्ययम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::418.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो  मेरे द्वारा आपका वह परम ऐश्वर रूप देखा जा सकता है  ऐसा अगर आप मानते हैं, तो हे योगेश्वर  आप अपने उस अविनाशी स्वरूपको मुझे दिखा दीजिये ॥
bhagwad_gita::418.english_translation: If you think I can see that form, Lord, then show me your imperishable self, Master of yoga.
bhagwad_gita::418.translation_literal: मन्यसे (if you think) / यदि (if) / तत् (that) / शक्यम् (possible) / मया (by me) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / इति (thus) / प्रभो (O Lord) / योगेश्वर (O master of yoga) / ततः (then) / मे (to me) / त्वम् (you) / दर्शय (show) / आत्मानम् (your self) / अव्ययम् (imperishable)
bhagwad_gita::418.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::418.essence: Real vision begins when control gives way to asking.
bhagwad_gita::418.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to reveal his imperishable form if it can be seen by human eyes.
bhagwad_gita::418.simple_insight: There is humility in asking for revelation instead of forcing understanding.
bhagwad_gita::418.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has already asked to see Krishna's divine form. Now he admits that ordinary sight may not be enough and begs Krishna, the master of yoga, to reveal the imperishable form directly. This leads into the vision of the cosmic form.
bhagwad_gita::418.modern_relevance: You stand before a decision too large for your own certainty and finally say, “Show me what is real.” That pause can be wiser than forcing an answer.
bhagwad_gita::418.insight: It shifts the mind from control to receptive seeing.

bhagwad_gita::419.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचपश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः । नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च ॥
bhagwad_gita::419.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे पृथानन्दन  अब मेरे अनेक तरहके, अनेक अनेक वर्णों और आकृतियोंवाले सैकड़ोंहजारों दिव्यरूपोंको तू देख ॥
bhagwad_gita::419.english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: See, Partha, my forms in hundreds and thousands, diverse, divine, and of many colors and shapes.
bhagwad_gita::419.translation_literal: श्री भगवानुवाच (the Blessed Lord said) / पश्य (see) / मे (my) / पार्थ (Partha) / रूपाणि (forms) / शतशः (in hundreds) / अथ (and) / सहस्रशः (in thousands) / नानाविधानि (of many kinds) / दिव्यानि (divine) / नाना-वर्ण-आकृतीनि (of many colors and shapes) / च (and)
bhagwad_gita::419.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::419.essence: The divine cannot be contained in one shape.
bhagwad_gita::419.simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna to look at his countless divine forms, each with different colors and shapes.
bhagwad_gita::419.simple_insight: The divine is not narrow or single-faced. Reality is far larger than one fixed image.
bhagwad_gita::419.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has asked to see Krishna's cosmic form. Krishna begins to reveal it by inviting him to look at countless divine forms, each unlike the other. The teaching is preparing Arjuna for awe.
bhagwad_gita::419.modern_relevance: You think you know someone by one role, one mood, one label. Then a crisis opens and you see how many forms a single life can hold.
bhagwad_gita::419.insight: It shifts the mind from fixed identity to vast, living presence.

bhagwad_gita::420.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन तू बारह आदित्योंको, आठ वसुओंको, ग्यारह रुद्रोंको और दो अश्विनीकुमारोंको तथा उनचास मरुद्गणोंको देख ।  जिनको तूने पहले कभी देखा नहीं, ऐसे बहुतसे आश्चर्यजनक रूपोंको भी तू देख ॥
bhagwad_gita::420.english_translation: See the twelve Adityas, the eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras, the two Ashvins, and the forty-nine Maruts. See many wonders never seen before, O Bharata.
bhagwad_gita::420.translation_literal: पश्य (see) / आदित्यान् (the Adityas) / वसून् (the Vasus) / रुद्रान् (the Rudras) / अश्विनौ (the two Ashvins) / मरुतः (the Maruts) / तथा (and) / बहूनि (many) / अदृष्टपूर्वाणि (never-seen-before) / पश्य (see) / आश्चर्याणि (wonders) / भारत (O Bharata)
bhagwad_gita::420.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::420.essence: The familiar universe is only a small part of what Krishna reveals.
bhagwad_gita::420.simple_meaning: Krishna invites Arjuna to see the cosmic form’s many divine beings and wonders, beyond anything he has seen before.
bhagwad_gita::420.simple_insight: A wider reality is already present; fear shrinks when the mind can hold more than one familiar shape.
bhagwad_gita::420.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has asked to see Krishna’s immeasurable form. Krishna begins unveiling it by pointing out radiant beings and astonishing forms within himself. This verse expands Arjuna’s vision before the full cosmic revelation.
bhagwad_gita::420.modern_relevance: You think one conversation will define everything, then the room opens and you realize there are larger forces, larger patterns, and more than one way to understand what is happening.
bhagwad_gita::420.insight: It trains the mind to widen its frame before it judges what is in front of it.

bhagwad_gita::421.verse_sanskrit: इहैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं पश्याद्य सचराचरम् । मम देहे गुडाकेश यच्चान्यद्द्रष्टुमिच्छसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::421.verse_hindi: हे नींदको जीतनेवाले अर्जुन मेरे इस शरीरके एक देशमें चराचरसहित सम्पूर्ण जगत् को अभी देख ले ।  इसके सिवाय तू और भी जो कुछ देखना चाहता है, वह भी देख ले ॥
bhagwad_gita::421.english_translation: Behold the entire universe, with all that moves and does not move, gathered here in one place in My body. See whatever else you wish to see as well.
bhagwad_gita::421.translation_literal: इह (here) / एकस्थम् (placed in one) / जगत् (world) / कृत्स्नम् (entire) / पश्य (see) / अद्य (now) / सचराचरम् (with moving and unmoving) / मम (my) / देहे (in body) / गुडाकेश (Arjuna) / यत् (whatever) / च (and) / अन्यत् (other) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / इच्छसि (you wish)
bhagwad_gita::421.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::421.essence: Everything you seek is already gathered in the divine form.
bhagwad_gita::421.simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that the whole universe, moving and still, is contained in his body. Arjuna can also look for anything else he wants to see.
bhagwad_gita::421.simple_insight: A wider vision can dissolve the feeling that life is scattered and separate.
bhagwad_gita::421.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is overwhelmed by Krishna's cosmic revelation. Krishna now says the entire moving and unmoving universe is gathered in his body, inviting Arjuna to look beyond ordinary limits before the divine vision is fully opened.
bhagwad_gita::421.modern_relevance: You stand before a decision that feels split into a hundred pieces. Then one clear view arrives: the whole mess belongs to a larger order than your fear.
bhagwad_gita::421.insight: It shifts the mind from fragmented seeing to a sense of all-in-one presence.

bhagwad_gita::422.verse_sanskrit: न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा । दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::422.verse_hindi: परन्तु तू अपनी इस आँखसे अर्थात् चर्मचक्षुसे मेरेको देख ही नहीं सकता, इसलिये मैं तुझे दिव्य चक्षु देता हूँ, जिससे तू मेरी ईश्वरसम्बन्धी सामर्थ्यको देख ॥
bhagwad_gita::422.english_translation: You cannot see me with these ordinary eyes. I give you divine sight, so you may behold my supreme power.
bhagwad_gita::422.translation_literal: न तु (but not) / मां (me) / शक्यसे (you are able) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / अनेन (with this) / एव (only) / स्वचक्षुषा (with your own eyes) / दिव्यम् (divine) / ददामि (I give) / ते (to you) / चक्षुः (eyesight) / पश्य (see) / मे (my) / योगम् (power) / ऐश्वरम् (sovereign)
bhagwad_gita::422.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::422.essence: Ordinary sight cannot hold the infinite; grace must widen the eye.
bhagwad_gita::422.simple_meaning: Ordinary sight is not enough to see Krishna's true form. He gives Arjuna a divine way of seeing so he can witness that supreme power.
bhagwad_gita::422.simple_insight: Some things cannot be grasped by effort alone; they must be granted from beyond ordinary sight.
bhagwad_gita::422.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has asked to see the cosmic form. Krishna has already shown that the universe rests within him, but ordinary eyesight still cannot take it in. So Krishna gives Arjuna divine sight, preparing him to witness the full majesty of the cosmic form.
bhagwad_gita::422.modern_relevance: You can stare at the same problem for hours and still miss what matters. Sometimes clarity does not come from looking harder, but from receiving a wider way of seeing.
bhagwad_gita::422.insight: It shifts the mind from forced inspection to receptive seeing.

bhagwad_gita::423.verse_sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरिः । दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::423.verse_hindi: सञ्जय बोले  हे राजन्  ऐसा कहकर फिर महायोगेश्वर भगवान् श्रीकृष्णने अर्जुनको परम ऐश्वररूप दिखाया ॥
bhagwad_gita::423.english_translation: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus, O King, the great lord of yoga, Hari, revealed to Arjuna the supreme divine form.
bhagwad_gita::423.translation_literal: सञ्जय उवाच (Sanjaya said) / एवम् (thus) / उक्त्वा (having spoken) / ततः (then) / राजन् (O King) / महायोगेश्वरः (the great lord of yoga) / हरिः (Hari) / दर्शयामास (revealed) / पार्थाय (to Arjuna, son of Pritha) / परमम् (supreme) / रूपम् (form) / ऐश्वरम् (divine, majestic)
bhagwad_gita::423.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::423.essence: The answer is not a theory; it arrives as a vision.
bhagwad_gita::423.simple_meaning: Sanjaya tells the king that Krishna then showed Arjuna his supreme divine form.
bhagwad_gita::423.simple_insight: Some moments cannot be explained; they must be shown.
bhagwad_gita::423.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has asked to see Krishna's cosmic reality. Krishna has granted divine sight. Now Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra that Krishna reveals the supreme form to Arjuna, beginning the overwhelming vision that follows.
bhagwad_gita::423.modern_relevance: A person finally asks to see the full truth, not the comforting version. The answer arrives all at once, and it changes everything they thought they could control.
bhagwad_gita::423.insight: It shifts the mind from hearing about the divine to confronting it directly.

bhagwad_gita::424.verse_hindi: जिसके अनेक मुख और नेत्र हैं, अनेक तहरके अद्भुत दर्शन हैं, अनेक दिव्य आभूषण हैं, हाथोंमें उठाये हुए अनेक दिव्य आयुध हैं तथा जिनके गलेमें दिव्य मालाएँ हैं, जो दिव्य वस्त्र पहने हुए हैं, जिनके ललाट तथा शरीरपर दिव्य चन्दन, कुंकुम आदि लगा हुआ है, ऐसे सम्पूर्ण आश्चर्यमय, अनन्तरूपवाले तथा चारों तरफ मुखवाले देवअपने दिव्य स्वरूप को भगवान् ने दिखाया ॥
bhagwad_gita::424.english_translation: With many mouths and eyes, with countless wondrous forms, adorned with many divine ornaments and many uplifted divine weapons.
bhagwad_gita::424.translation_literal: अनेक (many) / वक्त्र (mouths) / नयनम् (eyes) / अनेक (many) / अद्भुत-दर्शनम् (wonderful sights) / अनेक (many) / दिव्य-आभरणम् (divine ornaments) / दिव्य-अनेक-उद्यत-आयुधम् (divine, many, raised weapons)
bhagwad_gita::424.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::424.essence: The divine form cannot be held inside one human image.
bhagwad_gita::424.simple_meaning: The cosmic form appears with countless faces, eyes, ornaments, and divine weapons. It is a vast, overwhelming vision rather than a single human shape.
bhagwad_gita::424.simple_insight: Some truths cannot be reduced to one familiar form.
bhagwad_gita::424.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna has just granted Arjuna divine sight. Sanjaya now describes what Arjuna sees: a limitless form filled with faces, eyes, ornaments, and weapons. This verse is one detail in the unfolding vision, not the full revelation itself.
bhagwad_gita::424.modern_relevance: You finally see the full picture after weeks of narrow thinking, and it is bigger, stranger, and harder to contain than you expected.
bhagwad_gita::424.insight: It trains the mind to accept that reality may exceed ordinary categories and familiar appearances.

bhagwad_gita::425.verse_hindi: जिसके अनेक मुख और नेत्र हैं, अनेक तहरके अद्भुत दर्शन हैं, अनेक दिव्य आभूषण हैं, हाथोंमें उठाये हुए अनेक दिव्य आयुध हैं तथा जिनके गलेमें दिव्य मालाएँ हैं, जो दिव्य वस्त्र पहने हुए हैं, जिनके ललाट तथा शरीरपर दिव्य चन्दन, कुंकुम आदि लगा हुआ है, ऐसे सम्पूर्ण आश्चर्यमय, अनन्त रूपोंवाले तथा चारों तरफ मुखवाले देवअपने दिव्य स्वरूप को भगवान् ने दिखाया ॥
bhagwad_gita::425.english_translation: Wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrances, wondrous in every way, endless, and facing everywhere.
bhagwad_gita::425.translation_literal: दिव्य (divine) / माल्य (garlands) / अम्बर (garments) / धरम् (wearing) / दिव्य (divine) / गन्ध (fragrance) / अनुलेपनम् (anointing) / सर्व (all) / आश्चर्य (wonder) / मयम् (filled with) / देवम् (the radiant one) / अनन्तम् (endless) / विश्वतोमुखम् (facing everywhere)
bhagwad_gita::425.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::425.essence: The divine presence is beautiful, boundless, and impossible to face from only one side.
bhagwad_gita::425.simple_meaning: Krishna's cosmic form is covered in divine garlands, clothes, and fragrance. It is endless, wondrous, and faces in every direction.
bhagwad_gita::425.simple_insight: Awe deepens when the divine is felt as everywhere, not contained in one shape.
bhagwad_gita::425.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still staring at Krishna's cosmic form after the revelation begins. The form is not just vast; it is adorned, living, and impossible to contain. This verse adds to the shock before Arjuna's fear and prayer.
bhagwad_gita::425.modern_relevance: You stand speechless in front of something too vast to fit your plans — a birth, a loss, a revelation. The mind stops arguing when reality becomes larger than your frame.
bhagwad_gita::425.insight: It shifts perception from a single bounded form to an all-facing presence beyond limits.

bhagwad_gita::426.verse_sanskrit: दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता । यदि भाः सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::426.verse_hindi: अगर आकाशमें एक साथ हजारों सूर्य उदित हो जायँ, तो भी उन सबका प्रकाश मिलकर उस महात्माविराट् रूप परमात्मा के प्रकाशके समान शायद ही हो ॥
bhagwad_gita::426.english_translation: If a thousand suns rose together in the sky, their light would still barely match that great being's radiance.
bhagwad_gita::426.translation_literal: दिवि (in the sky) / सूर्यसहस्रस्य (of a thousand suns) / भवेत् (would be) / युगपत् (at once) / उत्थिता (risen) / यदि (if) / भाः (light) / सदृशी (equal) / सा (that) / स्यात् (would be) / भासः (radiance) / तस्य (of that) / महात्मनः (of the great being)
bhagwad_gita::426.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::426.essence: Even the brightest familiar light cannot measure the cosmic form's radiance.
bhagwad_gita::426.simple_meaning: Arjuna says that even a thousand suns rising at once would not match the radiance of Krishna's cosmic form.
bhagwad_gita::426.simple_insight: Some encounters are so overwhelming that ordinary language and ordinary sight both fail.
bhagwad_gita::426.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is staring into Krishna's cosmic form after the battlefield has frozen into awe. He tries to describe the impossible: even a thousand suns would not equal that radiance. The next verse shows him seeing the whole universe inside that body.
bhagwad_gita::426.modern_relevance: You stand in a dark room and suddenly the screen flashes open with a truth you cannot unsee. The mind reaches for comparison, but the experience already exceeds it.
bhagwad_gita::426.insight: It shifts the mind from measuring the divine by familiar things to admitting that ordinary scales collapse before it.

bhagwad_gita::427.verse_sanskrit: तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा । अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा ॥
bhagwad_gita::427.verse_hindi: उस समय अर्जुनने देवोंके देव भगवान् के उस शरीरमें एक जगह स्थित अनेक प्रकारके विभागोंमें विभक्त सम्पूर्ण जगत् को देखा ॥
bhagwad_gita::427.english_translation: There Arjuna saw the entire universe gathered in one place, divided in countless ways within the body of the Lord of the gods.
bhagwad_gita::427.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / एकस्थम् (in one place) / जगत्-कृत्स्नम् (the entire universe) / प्रविभक्तम् (divided) / अनेकधा (in many ways) / अपश्यत् (saw) / देवदेवस्य (of the Lord of the gods) / शरीरे (in the body) / पाण्डवः (the son of Pandu, Arjuna) / तदा (then)
bhagwad_gita::427.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::427.essence: One form can contain the whole universe.
bhagwad_gita::427.simple_meaning: Arjuna saw the whole universe inside Krishna's cosmic form, all held together in one body and yet appearing in countless forms.
bhagwad_gita::427.simple_insight: Awe can break the mind open when it sees how much larger reality is than its fears.
bhagwad_gita::427.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is already overwhelmed by Krishna's cosmic form. In this moment he sees the whole universe gathered inside that single body, divided into countless forms. The vision is so vast that ordinary seeing can no longer hold it.
bhagwad_gita::427.modern_relevance: You open a message expecting one answer, and instead the situation reveals a whole web of hidden causes, loyalties, and consequences. The simple story you carried in your head suddenly looks too small.
bhagwad_gita::427.insight: It shifts the mind from narrow, personal perception to a wider vision of interconnected reality.

bhagwad_gita::428.verse_sanskrit: ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जयः । प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत ॥
bhagwad_gita::428.verse_hindi: भगवान् के विश्वरूपको देखकर अर्जुन बहुत चकित हुए और आश्चर्यके कारण उनका शरीर रोमाञ्चित हो गया ।  वे हाथ जोड़कर विश्वरूप देवको मस्तकसे प्रणाम करके बोले ॥
bhagwad_gita::428.english_translation: Then, overwhelmed with wonder, Arjuna’s hair stood on end. He bowed his head to the divine and spoke with folded hands.
bhagwad_gita::428.translation_literal: ततः (then) / सः (he) / विस्मय-आविष्टः (filled with wonder) / हृष्ट-रोमा (with hair standing on end) / धनञ्जयः (Arjuna) / प्रणम्य (having bowed) / शिरसा (with the head) / देवम् (to the divine) / कृताञ्जलिः (with folded hands) / अभाषत (spoke)
bhagwad_gita::428.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::428.essence: A glimpse of the vast can turn shock into surrender.
bhagwad_gita::428.simple_meaning: Arjuna is stunned by the cosmic form. He bows his head, joins his hands, and begins to speak.
bhagwad_gita::428.simple_insight: A true encounter with greatness can dissolve pride into reverence.
bhagwad_gita::428.detailed_meaning: Arjuna has just seen Krishna’s cosmic form filling everything. Overwhelmed, his body reacts before his mind can speak: his hair stands on end, he bows deeply, and only then finds words. The moment marks awe turning into prayer.
bhagwad_gita::428.modern_relevance: You open a message and realize the truth is bigger than your plan. Before you can argue, your body goes quiet and humility takes over.
bhagwad_gita::428.insight: It shifts the response from analysis to reverent speech when reality exceeds control.

bhagwad_gita::429.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचपश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहेसर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसङ्घान् । ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थमृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान् ॥
bhagwad_gita::429.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे देव  मैं आपके शरीरमें सम्पूर्ण देवताओंको, प्राणियोंके विशेषविशेष समुदायोंको कमलासनपर बैठे हुए ब्रह्माजीको, शङ्करजीको, सम्पूर्ण ऋषियोंको और सम्पूर्ण दिव्य सर्पोंको देख रहा हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::429.english_translation: Arjuna said: O divine one, I see all the gods in your body, and all kinds of distinct beings, Brahma seated on the lotus, Shiva, all the sages, and all the radiant serpents.
bhagwad_gita::429.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / पश्यामि (I see) / देवान् (the gods) / तव (your) / देव (O divine one) / देहे (in the body) / सर्वान् (all) / तथा (and) / भूतविशेषसङ्घान् (groups of distinct beings) / ब्रह्माणम् (Brahma) / ईशम् (the lord) / कमलासनस्थम् (seated on the lotus seat) / ऋषीन् (sages) / च (and) / सर्वान् (all) / उरगान् (serpents) / च (and) / दिव्यान् (radiant / divine)
bhagwad_gita::429.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::429.essence: The many forms of existence appear within one vast body.
bhagwad_gita::429.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees the entire divine order inside Krishna's cosmic body: gods, beings of every kind, Brahma, Shiva, sages, and radiant serpents.
bhagwad_gita::429.simple_insight: A single vision can collapse the boundary between the many and the one.
bhagwad_gita::429.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has already seen Krishna's cosmic form and is overwhelmed. He now describes what that vision contains: every class of being, from gods to sages to Brahma and Shiva, all within Krishna's body. The next verse expands the awe even further.
bhagwad_gita::429.modern_relevance: You stare at a decision that seems private, then suddenly see how many lives, histories, and forces are braided into it. The choice is bigger than your fear.
bhagwad_gita::429.insight: It shifts perception from isolated details to the whole living field contained in one reality.

bhagwad_gita::430.verse_sanskrit: अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रंपश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम् । नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिंपश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप ॥
bhagwad_gita::430.verse_hindi: हे विश्वरूप  हे विश्वेश्वरव  आपको मैं अनेक हाथों, पेटों, मुखों और नेत्रोंवाला तथा सब ओरसे अनन्त रूपोंवाला देख रहा हूँ ।  मैं आपके न आदिको, न मध्यको और न अन्तको ही देख रहा हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::430.english_translation: I see You with many arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes, everywhere without end. I see no beginning, middle, or end of You, O Lord of all, O cosmic form.
bhagwad_gita::430.translation_literal: अनेकबाहु (many-armed) / उदर (bellied) / वक्त्र (mouthed) / नेत्र (eyed) / पश्यामि (I see) / त्वाम् (You) / सर्वतः (everywhere) / अनन्तरूपम् (endless-formed) / न अन्तम् (no end) / न मध्यम् (no middle) / न पुनः तव आदिम् (nor again Your beginning) / पश्यामि (I see) / विश्वेश्वर (Lord of all) / विश्वरूप (cosmic form)
bhagwad_gita::430.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::430.essence: The largest reality has no edge the mind can grasp.
bhagwad_gita::430.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees Krishna’s cosmic form as limitless, with countless arms, mouths, and eyes. He cannot find its beginning, middle, or end.
bhagwad_gita::430.simple_insight: A mind can be overwhelmed by what is greater than it and still stay reverent.
bhagwad_gita::430.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has been granted the vision of Krishna’s universal form. Stunned, he describes an immeasurable presence with countless features and no visible limits. This verse deepens his awe before the form that is about to reveal its full power.
bhagwad_gita::430.modern_relevance: You stand before a truth too large to fit your old categories. The urge to label it fades; reverence begins where control ends.
bhagwad_gita::430.insight: It shifts the mind from measuring reality to bowing before what cannot be contained.

bhagwad_gita::431.verse_sanskrit: किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं चतेजोराशिं सर्वतोदीप्तिमन्तम् । पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ताद्दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::431.verse_hindi: मैं आपको किरीट, गदा, चक्र तथा शङ्ख और पद्म धारण किये हुए देख रहा हूँ ।  आपको तेजकी राशि, सब ओर प्रकाश करनेवाले, देदीप्यमान अग्नि तथा सूर्यके समान कान्तिवाले, नेत्रोंके द्वारा कठिनतासे देखे जानेयोग्य और सब तरफसे अप्रमेयस्वरूप देख रहा हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::431.english_translation: I see you wearing a crown, holding a mace and discus, blazing everywhere, hard to behold, and immeasurable — like fire and the sun in brilliance.
bhagwad_gita::431.translation_literal: किरीटिनम् (crowned) / गदिनम् (mace-bearing) / चक्रिणम् (discus-bearing) / च (and) / तेजोराशिम् (a mass of radiance) / सर्वतोदीप्तिमन्तम् (shining on all sides) / पश्यामि (I see) / त्वाम् (you) / दुर्निरीक्ष्यम् (hard to behold) / समन्तात् (on every side) / दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिम् (with the brilliance of blazing fire and the sun) / अप्रमेयम् (immeasurable)
bhagwad_gita::431.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::431.essence: What is most real cannot be fully held by sight.
bhagwad_gita::431.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees Krishna in a radiant cosmic form, crowned and armed, blazing like fire and the sun, impossible to measure or fully look at.
bhagwad_gita::431.simple_insight: Awe replaces ordinary seeing. The mind meets something too vast to contain.
bhagwad_gita::431.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still staring at Krishna’s cosmic form after the armies have frozen around them. What he sees is overwhelming: crowned, armed, blazing, and beyond measure. This vision deepens his surrender before Krishna explains what this vast form means.
bhagwad_gita::431.modern_relevance: You stand before a decision that strips away all comfort: the relationship, the job, the truth you have avoided. Suddenly the situation feels larger than your plans, and your control looks small.
bhagwad_gita::431.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to grasp the whole picture to yielding before what exceeds comprehension.

bhagwad_gita::432.verse_sanskrit: त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यंत्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् । त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्तासनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे ॥
bhagwad_gita::432.verse_hindi: आप ही जाननेयोग्य परम अक्षर अक्षरब्रह्म हैं, आप ही इस सम्पूर्ण विश्वके परम आश्रय हैं, आप ही सनातनधर्मके रक्षक हैं और आप ही अविनाशी सनातन पुरुष हैं  ऐसा मैं मानता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::432.english_translation: You are the imperishable supreme reality, the highest support of this world, the guardian of eternal dharma, and the eternal person.
bhagwad_gita::432.translation_literal: त्वम् (you) / अक्षरम् (imperishable) / परमम् (supreme) / वेदितव्यम् (to be known) / त्वम् (you) / अस्य (of this) / विश्वस्य (of the universe) / परम् (highest) / निधानम् (support, resting place) / त्वम् (you) / अव्ययः (unchanging) / शाश्वत-धर्म-गोप्ता (guardian of eternal dharma) / सनातनः (eternal) / त्वम् (you) / पुरुषः (person) / मतः (considered) / मे (by me)
bhagwad_gita::432.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::432.essence: What appears overwhelming is actually the world’s deepest support.
bhagwad_gita::432.simple_meaning: Arjuna recognizes Krishna as the highest imperishable reality, the universe's support, the protector of eternal dharma, and the eternal person.
bhagwad_gita::432.simple_insight: Awe turns into trust when the mind sees what never changes.
bhagwad_gita::432.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still overwhelmed by Krishna's cosmic form. After seeing limitless faces and forms, he tries to name what he is beholding: the imperishable source, the world's support, and the guardian of eternal order.
bhagwad_gita::432.modern_relevance: You stand before a decision that could reshape your life, and the usual markers fail. In that moment, the mind reaches for something unshakable to trust.
bhagwad_gita::432.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing power as force to seeing it as the ground that holds all order.

bhagwad_gita::433.verse_sanskrit: अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्यमनन्तबाहुं शशिसूर्यनेत्रम् । पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रम्स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::433.verse_hindi: आपको मैं आदि, मध्य और अन्तसे रहित, अनन्त प्रभावशाली, अनन्त भुजाओंवाले, चन्द्र और सूर्यरूप नेत्रोवाले, प्रज्वलित अग्निके समान मुखोंवाले और अपने तेजसे संसारको संतप्त करते हुए देख रहा हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::433.english_translation: I see you as beginningless, middleless, and endless; of infinite power, with infinite arms, with eyes like the moon and the sun, with mouths blazing like fire, and scorching this world with your own radiance.
bhagwad_gita::433.translation_literal: अनादि (without beginning) / मध्य (middle) / अन्तम् (end) / अनन्तवीर्यम् (of infinite power) / अनन्तबाहुम् (with infinite arms) / शशि-सूर्य-नेत्रम् (with moon-sun eyes) / पश्यामि (I see) / त्वाम् (you) / दीप्त-हुताश-वक्त्रम् (with blazing fire-mouths) / स्व-तेजसा (with own radiance) / विश्वम् (world) / इदम् (this) / तपन्तम् (scorching)
bhagwad_gita::433.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::433.essence: What overwhelms the mind can also dissolve its resistance.
bhagwad_gita::433.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees Krishna as beyond beginning, middle, and end, with limitless power and terrifying cosmic features that burn the world with their own brilliance.
bhagwad_gita::433.simple_insight: Awe can strip away all false certainty and leave only surrender.
bhagwad_gita::433.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is staring at Krishna’s cosmic form after his ordinary sight has broken open. What he sees is beyond time, beyond measure, and overwhelming in force, so this verse becomes part of his stunned response to the divine vision.
bhagwad_gita::433.modern_relevance: You finally face the truth you kept avoiding, and it is bigger than your fear. The mind cannot contain it; only surrender can.
bhagwad_gita::433.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to control reality to yielding before what exceeds it.

bhagwad_gita::434.verse_sanskrit: द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हिव्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः । दृष्ट्वाऽद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदंलोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन् ॥
bhagwad_gita::434.verse_hindi: हे महात्मन्  यह स्वर्ग और पृथ्वीके बीचका अन्तराल और सम्पूर्ण दिशाएँ एक आपसे ही परिपूर्ण हैं ।  आपके इस अद्भुत और उग्ररूपको देखकर तीनों लोक व्यथित व्याकुल हो रहे हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::434.english_translation: The space between heaven and earth and all directions are filled by You alone. Seeing Your wondrous and fierce form, the three worlds tremble, O great one.
bhagwad_gita::434.translation_literal: द्यावापृथिव्योः (of heaven and earth) / इदम् (this) / अन्तरम् (intermediate space) / हि (indeed) / व्याप्तम् (pervaded) / त्वया (by You) / एकेन (alone) / दिशः (directions) / च (and) / सर्वाः (all) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / अद्भुतम् (wondrous) / रूपम् (form) / उग्रम् (fierce) / तव (Your) / इदम् (this) / लोकत्रयम् (three worlds) / प्रव्यथितम् (shaken) / महात्मन् (O great one)
bhagwad_gita::434.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::434.essence: One vision can overwhelm every boundary you thought was real.
bhagwad_gita::434.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees that Krishna fills every direction and every space. The sight of Krishna's vast and fierce form makes all three worlds tremble.
bhagwad_gita::434.simple_insight: Awe can undo the illusion of control in a single moment.
bhagwad_gita::434.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still staring at Krishna's cosmic form. He now sees that every direction and every space are filled by Krishna alone, and that this overwhelming vision has shaken the three worlds. The verse deepens the shock before the next wave of praise.
bhagwad_gita::434.modern_relevance: You open a message expecting a normal reply, and instead you see the full weight of what you’re dealing with. The room, the plan, the future — everything suddenly feels larger than your control.
bhagwad_gita::434.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing reality as manageable to seeing it as vast, living, and beyond personal control.

bhagwad_gita::435.verse_sanskrit: अमी हि त्वां सुरसङ्घाः विशन्तिकेचिद्भीताः प्राञ्जलयो गृणन्ति । स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा महर्षिसिद्धसङ्घाःस्तुवन्ति त्वां स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलाभिः ॥
bhagwad_gita::435.verse_hindi: वे ही देवताओंके समुदाय आपमें प्रविष्ट हो रहे हैं ।  उनमेंसे कई तो भयभीत होकर हाथ जोड़े हुए आपके नामों और गुणोंका कीर्तन कर रहे हैं ।  महर्षियों और सिद्धोंके समुदाय कल्याण हो  मङ्गल हो  ऐसा कहकर उत्तमउत्तम स्तोत्रोंके द्वारा आपकी स्तुति कर रहे हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::435.english_translation: The hosts of the radiant beings enter into you. Some, frightened, join their palms and sing your names and qualities. Great seers and perfected beings praise you with abundant hymns, saying, “May all be well.”
bhagwad_gita::435.translation_literal: अमी (these) / हि (indeed) / त्वां (you) / सुरसङ्घाः (hosts of radiant beings) / विशन्ति (enter) / केचिद् (some) / भीताः (frightened) / प्राञ्जलयः (with joined palms) / गृणन्ति (sing/praise) / स्वस्ति (may it be well) / इति (thus) / उक्त्वा (having said) / महर्षि-सिद्ध-सङ्घाः (hosts of great seers and perfected beings) / स्तुवन्ति (praise) / त्वां (you) / स्तुतिभिः (with praises) / पुष्कलाभिः (abundant, excellent)
bhagwad_gita::435.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::435.essence: Even the highest beings bow when the vast form appears.
bhagwad_gita::435.simple_meaning: Even the radiant beings are drawn into Krishna’s cosmic form. Some are afraid and pray, while seers and perfected beings praise him with rich hymns.
bhagwad_gita::435.simple_insight: Awe can dissolve pride. Even the highest beings respond to the divine with reverence.
bhagwad_gita::435.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still staring at Krishna’s cosmic form. The vision has shaken every level of existence: radiant beings enter it, some tremble before it, and seers and perfected beings respond with prayer and praise. The scene deepens the scale of Krishna’s revelation.
bhagwad_gita::435.modern_relevance: You open a message that changes everything, and the room goes quiet. Some people panic, some bow their heads, and the ones with wisdom respond with respect.
bhagwad_gita::435.insight: It shifts attention from human rank to cosmic reverence, showing that even greatness bows before what is vast.

bhagwad_gita::436.verse_sanskrit: रुद्रादित्या वसवो ये च साध्याविश्वेऽश्िवनौ मरुतश्चोष्मपाश्च । गन्धर्वयक्षासुरसिद्धसङ्घावीक्षन्ते त्वां विस्मिताश्चैव सर्वे ॥
bhagwad_gita::436.verse_hindi: जो ग्यारह रुद्र, बारह आदित्य, आठ वसु, बारह साध्यगण, दस विश्वेदेव और दो अश्विनीकुमार, उनचास मरुद्गण, सात पितृगण तथा गन्धर्व, यक्ष, असुर और सिद्धोंके समुदाय हैं, वे सभी चकित होकर आपको देख रहे हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::436.english_translation: The eleven Rudras, the twelve Adityas, the eight Vasus, the twelve Sadhyas, the Visvedevas, the two Ashvins, the forty-nine Maruts, the ancestors, and the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and Siddhas all gaze at you in wonder.
bhagwad_gita::436.translation_literal: रुद्रादित्या (Rudras and Adityas) / वसवः (Vasus) / ये (who) / च (and) / साध्याः (Sadhyas) / विश्वे (the Visvedevas) / अश्विनौ (the two Ashvins) / मरुतः (Maruts) / च (and) / उष्मपाः (ancestors) / च (and) / गन्धर्व-यक्ष-असुर-सिद्ध-सङ्घाः (hosts of Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and Siddhas) / वीक्षन्ते (look upon) / त्वाम् (you) / विस्मिताः (astonished) / च एव (and indeed) / सर्वे (all)
bhagwad_gita::436.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::436.essence: Even the highest beings stand astonished before Krishna's vastness.
bhagwad_gita::436.simple_meaning: Arjuna says that every class of celestial and powerful beings is astonished and looking at Krishna's cosmic form.
bhagwad_gita::436.simple_insight: Awe can dissolve rank, status, and fear at once.
bhagwad_gita::436.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still staring at Krishna's cosmic form. He sees not only warriors and kings, but every class of radiant beings looking on in wonder. The vision is so vast that even the highest beings are reduced to stunned witnesses.
bhagwad_gita::436.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and realize the whole hierarchy has gone quiet. The moment is bigger than anyone's status, and everyone can feel it.
bhagwad_gita::436.insight: It shifts attention from human rank to the overwhelming scale of the divine presence.

bhagwad_gita::437.verse_sanskrit: रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रंमहाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम् । बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालंदृष्ट्वा लोकाः प्रव्यथितास्तथाऽहम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::437.verse_hindi: हे महाबाहो आपके बहुत मुखों और नेत्रोंवाले, बहुत भुजाओं, जंघाओं और चरणोंवाले, बहुत उदरोंवाले, बहुत विकराल दाढ़ोंवाले महान् रूपको देखकर सब प्राणी व्यथित हो रहे हैं तथा मैं भी व्यथित हो रहा हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::437.english_translation: O mighty-armed one, seeing your great form with many mouths and eyes, many arms, thighs, and feet, many bellies, and terrible fangs, all beings are shaken, and so am I.
bhagwad_gita::437.translation_literal: रूपम् (form) / महत् (great) / ते (your) / बहुवक्त्रनेत्रम् (with many mouths and eyes) / महाबाहो (O mighty-armed one) / बहुबाहूरुपादम् (with many arms, thighs, and feet) / बहूदरम् (with many bellies) / बहुदंष्ट्राकरालम् (terrible with many fangs) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / लोकाः (all beings) / प्रव्यथिताः (are shaken) / तथा (so) / अहम् (I) ॥
bhagwad_gita::437.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::437.essence: A vision of total vastness can shake every observer at once.
bhagwad_gita::437.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees Krishna’s cosmic form and feels overwhelmed. The sight shakes not only him, but all beings around him.
bhagwad_gita::437.simple_insight: Some truths are too vast to meet casually; they unsettle everything familiar.
bhagwad_gita::437.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is staring at Krishna’s cosmic form after asking to see it. The many mouths, eyes, limbs, and fangs are so overwhelming that even the surrounding beings are shaken. This verse records Arjuna’s own trembling response.
bhagwad_gita::437.modern_relevance: You open a message expecting clarity, and instead one sentence changes the whole room inside you. Some revelations do not comfort first; they overwhelm before they reveal.
bhagwad_gita::437.insight: It captures the mind’s shock when confronted with something larger than its frame of reference.

bhagwad_gita::438.verse_sanskrit: नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णंव्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम् । दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्माधृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो ॥
bhagwad_gita::438.verse_hindi: हे विष्णो  आपके अनेक देदीप्यमान वर्ण हैं, आप आकाशको स्पर्श कर रहे हैं, आपका मुख फैला हुआ है आपके नेत्र प्रदीप्त और विशाल हैं ।  ऐसे आपको देखकर भयभीत अन्तःकरणवाला मैं धैर्य और शान्तिको प्राप्त नहीं हो रहा हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::438.english_translation: O Vishnu, seeing you touching the sky, blazing with many colors, with mouths spread wide and bright, vast eyes, my inner being is shaken. I cannot find steadiness or peace.
bhagwad_gita::438.translation_literal: नभःस्पृशम् (touching the sky) / दीप्तम् (blazing) / अनेकवर्णम् (of many colors) / व्यात्ताननम् (with spread-open mouths) / दीप्तविशालनेत्रम् (with blazing vast eyes) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / हि (indeed) / त्वाम् (you) / प्रव्यथितान्तरात्मा (with shaken inner being) / धृतिम् (steadiness) / न विन्दामि (I do not find) / शमम् (peace) / च (and) / विष्णो (O Vishnu)
bhagwad_gita::438.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::438.essence: A true vision can shatter the mind before it can steady it.
bhagwad_gita::438.simple_meaning: Arjuna is overwhelmed by Krishna's cosmic form. The sight shakes his inner being so deeply that he cannot find calm or steadiness.
bhagwad_gita::438.simple_insight: Some experiences are so vast that the mind cannot hold them. Humility begins when control falls away.
bhagwad_gita::438.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has asked to see Krishna's universal form. What he sees is not comforting but overwhelming: a vast, blazing presence beyond ordinary sight. This verse captures his loss of steadiness as awe turns into fear.
bhagwad_gita::438.modern_relevance: You open a message and realize the decision in front of you is bigger than you wanted. The old confidence drops away, and all you can feel is the weight of it.
bhagwad_gita::438.insight: It shifts the reader from trying to master the sacred to admitting helplessness before it.

bhagwad_gita::439.verse_sanskrit: दंष्ट्राकरालानि च ते मुखानिदृष्ट्वैव कालानलसन्निभानि । दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्मप्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥
bhagwad_gita::439.verse_hindi: आपके प्रलयकालकी अग्निके समान प्रज्वलित और दाढ़ोंके कारण विकराल भयानक मुखोंको देखकर मुझे न तो दिशाओंका ज्ञान हो रहा है और न शान्ति ही मिल रही है ।  इसलिये हे देवेश  हे जगन्निवास  आप प्रसन्न होइये ॥
bhagwad_gita::439.english_translation: Seeing your flaming, terrible mouths with their fangs, I can no longer find directions or peace. Be gracious, Lord of the divine beings, dwelling place of the world.
bhagwad_gita::439.translation_literal: दंष्ट्राकरालानि (terrible with fangs) / च (and) / ते (your) / मुखानि (mouths) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / एव (indeed) / कालानलसन्निभानि (resembling the fire of destruction) / दिशः (directions) / न (not) / जाने (I know) / न (not) / लभे (I find) / च (and) / शर्म (peace) / प्रसीद (be gracious) / देवेश (Lord of the divine beings) / जगन्निवास (dwelling place of the world)
bhagwad_gita::439.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::439.essence: True awe ends control and turns the heart toward surrender.
bhagwad_gita::439.simple_meaning: Arjuna is overwhelmed by Krishna's terrifying cosmic form. He cannot orient himself or find peace, and he begs Krishna to soften and show mercy.
bhagwad_gita::439.simple_insight: Overwhelming power can break the mind open into humility and plea.
bhagwad_gita::439.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still looking at Krishna's cosmic form. The many fanged mouths blaze like destruction itself, and Arjuna loses all sense of direction and calm. This cry comes from fear, awe, and surrender.
bhagwad_gita::439.modern_relevance: You open a message and realize your words have already changed everything. For a second, you cannot tell what to do next. That stunned silence is where this verse lives.
bhagwad_gita::439.insight: It shifts the mind from control to surrender when the scale of reality becomes too large to manage.

bhagwad_gita::440.verse_sanskrit: अमी च त्वां धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्राःसर्वे सहैवावनिपालसङ्घैः । भीष्मो द्रोणः सूतपुत्रस्तथाऽसौसहास्मदीयैरपि योधमुख्यैः ॥
bhagwad_gita::440.verse_hindi: हमारे मुख्य योद्धाओंके सहित भीष्म, द्रोण और वह कर्ण भी आपमें प्रविष्ट हो रहे हैं ।  राजाओंके समुदायोंके सहित धृतराष्ट्रके वे ही सबकेसब पुत्र आपके विकराल दाढ़ोंके कारण भयंकर मुखोंमें बड़ी तेजीसे प्रविष्ट हो रहे हैं ।  उनमेंसे कईएक तो चूर्ण हुए सिरोंसहित आपके दाँतोंके बीचमें फँसे हुए दीख रहे हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::440.english_translation: Bhishma, Drona, Karna, and all the sons of Dhritarashtra, along with the hosts of kings and our own chief warriors, are rushing into your fearful mouths. Some are seen caught between your teeth, with crushed heads.
bhagwad_gita::440.translation_literal: अमी (these) / च (and) / त्वां (you) / धृतराष्ट्रस्य (of Dhritarashtra) / पुत्राः (sons) / सर्वे (all) / सह (together with) / एव (indeed) / अवनिपालसङ्घैः (with hosts of kings) / भीष्मः (Bhishma) / द्रोणः (Drona) / सूतपुत्रः (the charioteer's son) / तथा (and) / असौ (that one) / सह (together with) / अस्मदीयैः (with our own) / अपि (also) / योधमुख्यैः (with chief warriors)
bhagwad_gita::440.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::440.essence: Even the greatest warriors are swallowed by what exceeds them.
bhagwad_gita::440.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees the great warriors and kings being pulled into Krishna's terrible cosmic mouth, where some are crushed between the teeth.
bhagwad_gita::440.simple_insight: A human battle suddenly looks powerless against a force far beyond it.
bhagwad_gita::440.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is staring into Krishna's cosmic form and losing all sense of ordinary battle. Bhishma, Drona, Karna, and the Kauravas appear to be rushing into those terrible mouths, showing Arjuna that the war's outcome is already overwhelming human control.
bhagwad_gita::440.modern_relevance: You watch a situation collapse faster than anyone can stop it: a breakup, a lawsuit, a family conflict. Suddenly, all the planning looks tiny beside what is already in motion.
bhagwad_gita::440.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing events as manageable to seeing them as forces larger than personal control.

bhagwad_gita::441.verse_sanskrit: वक्त्राणि ते त्वरमाणा विशन्तिदंष्ट्राकरालानि भयानकानि । केचिद्विलग्ना दशनान्तरेषुसंदृश्यन्ते चूर्णितैरुत्तमाङ्गैः ॥
bhagwad_gita::441.verse_hindi: हमारे मुख्य योद्धाओंके सहित भीष्म, द्रोण और वह कर्ण भी आपमें प्रविष्ट हो रहे हैं ।  राजाओंके समुदायोंके सहित धृतराष्ट्रके वे ही सबकेसब पुत्र आपके विकराल दाढ़ोंके कारण भयंकर मुखोंमें बड़ी तेजीसे प्रविष्ट हो रहे हैं ।  उनमेंसे कईएक तो चूर्ण हुए सिरोंसहित आपके दाँतोंके बीचमें फँसे हुए दीख रहे हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::441.english_translation: Your blazing, terrible mouths swallow them in haste. Some are seen caught between your teeth, with crushed heads.
bhagwad_gita::441.translation_literal: वक्त्राणि (mouths) / ते (your) / त्वरमाणा (hastening) / विशन्ति (enter) / दंष्ट्राकरालानि (with fearsome teeth) / भयानकानि (terrible) / केचिद् (some) / विलग्नाः (stuck) / दशन-अन्तरेषु (between the teeth) / संदृश्यन्ते (are seen) / चूर्णितैः (crushed) / उत्तमाङ्गैः (with heads)
bhagwad_gita::441.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::441.essence: All fighters are already being consumed by time.
bhagwad_gita::441.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees warriors rushing into Krishna's terrible mouths. Some are trapped between the teeth, with their heads crushed.
bhagwad_gita::441.simple_insight: Terror becomes a vision of inevitability: what seems like battle is already being swallowed by time.
bhagwad_gita::441.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is staring into Krishna's cosmic form. The warriors he knows are not merely fighting; they are rushing into those blazing mouths. This verse deepens the vision of total destruction.
bhagwad_gita::441.modern_relevance: You watch a decision spiral past the point of return: the argument, the breakup, the resignation letter already in motion. What looked controllable is already closing its jaws.
bhagwad_gita::441.insight: It shifts perception from human struggle to irreversible cosmic force.

bhagwad_gita::442.verse_sanskrit: यथा नदीनां बहवोऽम्बुवेगाःसमुद्रमेवाभिमुखाः द्रवन्ति । तथा तवामी नरलोकवीराविशन्ति वक्त्राण्यभिविज्वलन्ति ॥
bhagwad_gita::442.verse_hindi: जैसे नदियोंके बहुतसे जलके प्रवाह स्वाभाविक ही समुद्रके सम्मुख दौड़ते हैं, ऐसे ही वे संसारके महान् शूरवीर आपके प्रज्वलित मुखोंमें प्रवेश कर रहे हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::442.english_translation: As many streams of water rush naturally toward the sea, so these great warriors of the world enter your blazing mouths.
bhagwad_gita::442.translation_literal: यथा (as) / नदीनाम् (of rivers) / बहवः (many) / अम्बुवेगाः (water-currents) / समुद्रम् (the sea) / एव (indeed) / अभिमुखाः (facing) / द्रवन्ति (run) / तथा (so) / तव (your) / अमी (these) / नरलोकवीराः (heroes of the human world) / विशन्ति (enter) / वक्त्राणि (mouths) / अभिविज्वलन्ति (blazing)
bhagwad_gita::442.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::442.essence: All motion is already rushing toward its end.
bhagwad_gita::442.simple_meaning: The great warriors are rushing into Krishna’s blazing mouths just as rivers rush toward the sea.
bhagwad_gita::442.simple_insight: Overwhelming force can still move toward one inevitable end.
bhagwad_gita::442.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna sees Krishna’s cosmic form and watches warriors vanish into the blazing mouths. He compares their movement to rivers rushing toward the sea, stunned by the scale of what is happening.
bhagwad_gita::442.modern_relevance: You watch a situation swallow everything you hoped to control: a breakup, a resignation, a diagnosis. Some forces do not negotiate; they carry everything toward their end.
bhagwad_gita::442.insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to recognition of inevitability.

bhagwad_gita::443.verse_sanskrit: यथा प्रदीप्तं ज्वलनं पतङ्गाविशन्ति नाशाय समृद्धवेगाः । तथैव नाशाय विशन्ति लोकास्तवापि वक्त्राणि समृद्धवेगाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::443.verse_hindi: जैसे पतंगे मोहवश अपना नाश करनेके लिये बड़े वेगसे दौड़ते हुए प्रज्वलित अग्निमें प्रविष्ट होते हैं, ऐसे ही ये सब लोग भी मोहवश अपना नाश करनेके लिये बड़े वेगसे दौड़ते हुए आपके मुखोंमें प्रविष्ट हो रहे हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::443.english_translation: As moths rush with great speed into a blazing fire to their destruction, so these people rush with great speed into your mouths to their destruction.
bhagwad_gita::443.translation_literal: यथा (just as) / प्रदीप्तम् (blazing) / ज्वलनम् (fire) / पतङ्गाः (moths) / विशन्ति (enter) / नाशाय (for destruction) / समृद्धवेगाः (with great speed) / तथा (so) / एव (indeed) / नाशाय (for destruction) / विशन्ति (enter) / लोकाः (people) / तव (your) / अपि (also) / वक्त्राणि (mouths) / समृद्धवेगाः (with great speed)
bhagwad_gita::443.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::443.essence: Blind desire runs straight into its own ruin.
bhagwad_gita::443.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees people rushing helplessly into Krishna's blazing mouths, like moths flying into fire and destroying themselves.
bhagwad_gita::443.simple_insight: Some forces are so overwhelming that resistance looks like self-destruction.
bhagwad_gita::443.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is staring at Krishna's cosmic form. He sees warriors, kings, and armies rushing into those terrible, flaming mouths. The image is not instruction but horror: the war's end is already unfolding in divine sight.
bhagwad_gita::443.modern_relevance: You keep walking toward the thing you know will burn you: a toxic relationship, a lie you can no longer sustain, a choice that feels inevitable and wrong.
bhagwad_gita::443.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing destruction as accidental to seeing how blindness can carry people straight into it.

bhagwad_gita::444.verse_sanskrit: लेलिह्यसे ग्रसमानः समन्ताल्लोकान्समग्रान्वदनैर्ज्वलद्भिः । तेजोभिरापूर्य जगत्समग्रंभासस्तवोग्राः प्रतपन्ति विष्णो ॥
bhagwad_gita::444.verse_hindi: आप अपने प्रज्वलित मुखोंद्वारा सम्पूर्ण लोकोंका ग्रसन करते हुए उन्हें चारों ओरसे बारबार चाट रहे हैं और हे विष्णो  आपका उग्र प्रकाश अपने तेजसे सम्पूर्ण जगत् को परिपूर्ण करके सबको तपा रहा है ॥
bhagwad_gita::444.english_translation: You lick up all the worlds from every side with your blazing mouths. Your fierce radiance fills the whole universe and burns it, O Vishnu.
bhagwad_gita::444.translation_literal: लेलिह्यसे (you lick up) / ग्रसमानः (devouring) / समन्तात् (from every side) / लोकान् (worlds) / समग्रान् (all) / वदनैः (with mouths) / ज्वलद्भिः (blazing) / तेजोभिः (with radiances) / आपूर्य (filling) / जगत् (the universe) / समग्रम् (entire) / भासः (light) / तव (your) / उग्राः (fierce) / प्रतपन्ति (burn) / विष्णो (O Vishnu)
bhagwad_gita::444.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::444.essence: Total power leaves no room for control.
bhagwad_gita::444.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees the cosmic form as all-consuming and unbearable. The blazing mouths and fierce radiance show that this vision is not gentle, but overwhelming and world-devouring.
bhagwad_gita::444.simple_insight: Awe can become surrender when the mind meets something too vast to control.
bhagwad_gita::444.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is staring at Krishna's cosmic form and struggling to endure what he sees. The mouths blaze, the worlds are being devoured, and the vision is so immense that speech itself is breaking under its force.
bhagwad_gita::444.modern_relevance: You open a message and realize a decision has already outgrown your comfort. The situation is no longer negotiable, only larger than your fear.
bhagwad_gita::444.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to manage the vast to yielding before it.

bhagwad_gita::445.verse_sanskrit: आख्याहि मे को भवानुग्ररूपोनमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद । विज्ञातुमिच्छामि भवन्तमाद्यंन हि प्रजानामि तव प्रवृत्तिम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::445.verse_hindi: मुझे यह बताइये कि उग्ररूपवाले आप कौन हैं हे देवताओंमें श्रेष्ठ  आपको नमस्कार हो ।  आप प्रसन्न होइये ।  आदिरूप आपको मैं तत्त्वसे जानना चाहता हूँ क्योंकि मैं आपकी प्रवृत्तिको नहीं जानता ॥
bhagwad_gita::445.english_translation: Tell me who You are in this fierce form. Salutations to You, best of the radiant beings; be gracious. I wish to know You, the primal one, for I do not understand Your purpose.
bhagwad_gita::445.translation_literal: आख्याहि (tell) / मे (to me) / कः (who) / भवान् (You are) / उग्र-रूपः (fierce-formed) / नमः अस्तु (salutations be) / ते (to You) / देव-वर (best of the radiant beings) / प्रसीद (be gracious) / विज्ञातुम् इच्छामि (I wish to know) / भवन्तम् (You) / आद्यम् (the primal one) / न हि (indeed not) / प्रजानामि (I know) / तव (Your) / प्रवृत्तिम् (purpose / action)
bhagwad_gita::445.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::445.essence: Fear bows first, then asks to know what stands before it.
bhagwad_gita::445.simple_meaning: Arjuna bows in fear and asks Krishna to reveal who this terrible form is. He wants to understand the primal source behind the overwhelming vision.
bhagwad_gita::445.simple_insight: Awe can become clarity when fear turns into honest asking.
bhagwad_gita::445.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has just seen Krishna's cosmic form devouring the armies. Overwhelmed, he stops resisting, bows, and asks the one question left: who is this fierce presence, and what is its purpose?
bhagwad_gita::445.modern_relevance: You are staring at a message that changes everything, and your first reaction is fear. Before you can act, you have to ask the honest question: what is really happening here?
bhagwad_gita::445.insight: It shifts the mind from panic to reverent inquiry before judgment.
