bhagwad_gita::446.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचकालोऽस्मि लोकक्षयकृत्प्रवृद्धोलोकान्समाहर्तुमिह प्रवृत्तः । ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वेयेऽवस्थिताः प्रत्यनीकेषु योधाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::446.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  मैं सम्पूर्ण लोकोंका क्षय करनेवाला बढ़ा हुआ काल हूँ और इस समय मैं इन सब लोगोंका संहार करनेके लिये यहाँ आया हूँ ।  तुम्हारे प्रतिपक्षमें जो योद्धालोग खड़े हैं, वे सब तुम्हारे युद्ध किये बिना भी नहीं रहेंगे ॥
bhagwad_gita::446.english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: I am Time, the great destroyer of worlds, here to end all beings. Even without you, the warriors standing in the opposing ranks will not survive.
bhagwad_gita::446.translation_literal: श्री भगवानुवाच (the Blessed Lord said) / कालः (Time) / अस्मि (I am) / लोकक्षयकृत् (maker of the destruction of worlds) / प्रवृद्धः (grown mighty) / लोकान् (the worlds / beings) / समाहर्तुम् (to gather up / destroy) / इह (here) / प्रवृत्तः (set in motion / come forth) / ऋते (without) / अपि (even) / त्वाम् (you) / न (not) / भविष्यन्ति (will exist) / सर्वे (all) / ये (who) / अवस्थिताः (standing) / प्रत्यनीकेषु (in the opposing ranks) / योधाः (warriors)
bhagwad_gita::446.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::446.essence: What is ending was never in your hands to preserve.
bhagwad_gita::446.simple_meaning: Krishna reveals that the force of ending is already at work. Arjuna is not being asked to cause death; he is being asked to take part in a battle whose outcome is already decided.
bhagwad_gita::446.simple_insight: The burden of total control falls away. You are responsible for action, not for commanding life and death.
bhagwad_gita::446.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna trembles before the cosmic form. Krishna answers from within that vision, not as a counselor but as the force behind time itself. He tells Arjuna the opposing warriors are already doomed, and his role is no longer to decide fate.
bhagwad_gita::446.modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, about to hear news that will change everything. The moment has already moved beyond your control, and the only honest task left is to face it without pretending otherwise.
bhagwad_gita::446.insight: It shifts the mind from personal control to humble participation in a larger order.

bhagwad_gita::447.verse_sanskrit: तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्वजित्वा शत्रून् भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम् । मयैवैते निहताः पूर्वमेवनिमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन् ॥
bhagwad_gita::447.verse_hindi: इसलिये तुम युद्धके लिये खड़े हो जाओ और यशको प्राप्त करो तथा शत्रुओंको जीतकर धनधान्यसे सम्पन्न राज्यको भोगो ।  ये सभी मेरे द्वारा पहलेसे ही मारे हुए हैं ।  हे सव्यसाचिन्  तुम निमित्तमात्र बन जाओ ॥
bhagwad_gita::447.english_translation: Therefore, rise and win fame. Conquer your enemies and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. They have already been slain by me; become only the instrument, Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::447.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) / त्वम् (you) / उत्तिष्ठ (rise) / यशः (fame) / लभस्व (gain) / जित्वा (having conquered) / शत्रून् (enemies) / भुङ्क्ष्व (enjoy) / राज्यं (kingdom) / समृद्धम् (prosperous) / मया (by me) / एव (indeed) / एते (these) / निहताः (slain) / पूर्वम् (already) / एव (indeed) / निमित्तमात्रम् (mere instrument) / भव (become) / सव्यसाचिन् (Arjuna)
bhagwad_gita::447.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::447.essence: Act fully, but let the larger order carry the result.
bhagwad_gita::447.simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna to stand up, fight, and claim the kingdom, but without ego. The enemies are already defeated in the larger order; Arjuna must only act as the instrument.
bhagwad_gita::447.simple_insight: You can move with full force without carrying the burden of control.
bhagwad_gita::447.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while the cosmic form reveals the war’s outcome. Krishna now turns that vision into action: Arjuna must rise, fight, and reclaim the kingdom, but without claiming authorship of the result.
bhagwad_gita::447.modern_relevance: You’re about to send the message that will change a family forever, and your hands shake. This verse says: do the necessary act cleanly, without pretending you control everything it will unleash.
bhagwad_gita::447.insight: It shifts action from self-importance to right participation in what is already unfolding.

bhagwad_gita::448.verse_sanskrit: द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं चकर्णं तथाऽन्यानपि योधवीरान् । मया हतांस्त्वं जहि मा व्यथिष्ठायुध्यस्व जेतासि रणे सपत्नान् ॥
bhagwad_gita::448.verse_hindi: द्रोण, भीष्म, जयद्रथ और कर्ण तथा अन्य सभी मेरे द्वारा मारे हुए शूरवीरोंको तुम मारो ।  तुम व्यथा मत करो और युद्ध करो ।  युद्धमें तुम निःसन्देह वैरियोंको जीतोगे ॥
bhagwad_gita::448.english_translation: Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna, and the other great warriors have already been slain by Me. Do not falter; fight, and you will surely conquer your enemies in battle.
bhagwad_gita::448.translation_literal: द्रोणं (Drona) / च (and) / भीष्मं (Bhishma) / च (and) / जयद्रथं (Jayadratha) / च (and) / कर्णं (Karna) / तथा (and) / अन्यान् (others) / अपि (also) / योधवीरान् (great warriors) / मया (by Me) / हतान् (slain) / त्वं (you) / जहि (slay) / मा (do not) / व्यथिष्ठाः (be distressed) / आयुध्यस्व (fight) / जेतासि (you will conquer) / रणे (in battle) / सपत्नान् (enemies)
bhagwad_gita::448.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::448.essence: The battle is already decided; your task is only to act.
bhagwad_gita::448.simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that the great warriors are already defeated in the larger order of events. Arjuna should stop trembling, keep fighting, and trust that victory is already assured.
bhagwad_gita::448.simple_insight: Fear loosens when you stop carrying the whole outcome alone.
bhagwad_gita::448.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna still stands shaken before the cosmic form. Krishna names Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna, and the rest as already fallen in His vision, then pushes Arjuna back into action. The verse seals the command: fight without fear.
bhagwad_gita::448.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, end the relationship, or walk into the hearing that changes everything. The body shakes, but the decision is already made.
bhagwad_gita::448.insight: It shifts action from personal doubt to trust in a larger order already at work.

bhagwad_gita::449.verse_sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाचएतच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं केशवस्यकृताञ्जलिर्वेपमानः किरीटी । नमस्कृत्वा भूय एवाह कृष्णंसगद्गदं भीतभीतः प्रणम्य ॥
bhagwad_gita::449.verse_hindi: सञ्जय बोले  भगवान् केशवका यह वचन सुनकर भयसे कम्पित हुए किरीटी अर्जुन हाथ जोड़कर नमस्कार करके और अत्यन्त भयभीत होकर फिर प्रणाम करके गद्गदं वाणीसे भगवान् कृष्णसे बोले ॥
bhagwad_gita::449.english_translation: Sanjaya said: Hearing Krishna's words, Arjuna trembled, folded his hands, bowed again and again, and spoke to Krishna in a choked voice, filled with fear.
bhagwad_gita::449.translation_literal: सञ्जय उवाच (Sanjaya said) / एतत् (this) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / वचनम् (word/speech) / केशवस्य (of Keshava) / कृताञ्जलिः (with folded hands) / वेपमानः (trembling) / किरीटी (the crowned one, Arjuna) / नमस्कृत्वा (having bowed) / भूयः (again) / एव (indeed) / आह (said) / कृष्णम् (to Krishna) / सगद्गदम् (in a choked voice) / भीतभीतः (very frightened) / प्रणम्य (having prostrated)
bhagwad_gita::449.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::449.essence: Awe can break speech before it becomes prayer.
bhagwad_gita::449.simple_meaning: Arjuna is overwhelmed by Krishna's cosmic revelation. He trembles, bows, and can only speak with fear.
bhagwad_gita::449.simple_insight: A true encounter can leave even the strongest person wordless, humbled, and shaken open.
bhagwad_gita::449.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna has just revealed the cosmic form. Arjuna, the crowned warrior, cannot stand before it. He folds his hands, trembles, bows again, and prepares to answer from fear and awe.
bhagwad_gita::449.modern_relevance: You hear a truth that strips away your excuses. Your mouth goes dry, your body tightens, and all you can do is bow to what is real.
bhagwad_gita::449.insight: It shows the collapse of ego before overwhelming reality, setting up Arjuna's prayer of awe.

bhagwad_gita::450.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचस्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्याजगत् प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च । रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्तिसर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::450.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे अन्तर्यामी भगवन्  आपके नाम, गुण, लीलाका कीर्तन करनेसे यह सम्पूर्ण जगत् हर्षित हो रहा है और अनुरागप्रेम को प्राप्त हो रहा है ।  आपके नाम, गुण आदिके कीर्तनसे भयभीत होकर राक्षसलोग दसों दिशाओंमें भागते हुए जा रहे हैं और सम्पूर्ण सिद्धगण आपको नमस्कार कर रहे हैं ।  यह सब होना उचित ही है ॥
bhagwad_gita::450.english_translation: Arjuna said: O Hrishikesha, by chanting Your names and glories, the whole world rejoices and becomes devoted. By that chanting, frightened beings flee in all directions, and all the perfected ones bow to You. This is only fitting.
bhagwad_gita::450.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / स्थाने (rightly; fittingly) / हृषीकेश (O Hrishikesha) / तव (Your) / प्रकीर्त्य (by glorifying; by chanting) / जगत् (the world) / प्रहृष्यति (rejoices greatly) / अनुरज्यते (becomes devoted; becomes attached in love) / च (and) / रक्षांसि (beings of darkness; hostile beings) / भीतानि (frightened) / दिशः (directions) / द्रवन्ति (flee) / सर्वे (all) / नमस्यन्ति (bow down) / च (and) / सिद्धसङ्घाः (assemblies of perfected beings)
bhagwad_gita::450.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::450.essence: The divine name can turn fear into devotion and disorder into reverence.
bhagwad_gita::450.simple_meaning: Arjuna says that praising Krishna fills the world with joy and love, drives fearful forces away, and makes perfected beings bow in respect.
bhagwad_gita::450.simple_insight: Praise changes the atmosphere of the mind and the world around it.
bhagwad_gita::450.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, after seeing Krishna's cosmic form, Arjuna is no longer arguing—he is overwhelmed. With his hands folded, he says that Krishna's glory makes the world rejoice, makes dark forces flee, and makes the perfected bow down.
bhagwad_gita::450.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where fear has spread through everyone, and one steady voice names what is true. The tension shifts at once; panic loses its grip.
bhagwad_gita::450.insight: It shifts attention from fear to reverence, showing that praise can reorder experience.

bhagwad_gita::451.verse_sanskrit: कस्माच्च ते न नमेरन्महात्मन्गरीयसे ब्रह्मणोऽप्यादिकर्त्रे । अनन्त देवेश जगन्निवासत्वमक्षरं सदसत्तत्परं यत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::451.verse_hindi: हे महात्मन्  गुरुओंके भी गुरु और ब्रह्माके भी आदिकर्ता आपके लिये वे सिद्धगण नमस्कार क्यों नहीं करें क्योंकि हे अनन्त  हे देवेश  हे जगन्निवास  आप अक्षरस्वरूप हैं आप सत् भी हैं, असत् भी हैं, और सत्असत् से पर भी जो कुछ है, वह भी आप ही हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::451.english_translation: O great one, why would the perfected beings not bow to you, the greatest teacher, the first maker even of Brahma? Endless Lord of radiant beings, abode of the world, you are the imperishable, the real and the unreal, and beyond both.
bhagwad_gita::451.translation_literal: कस्मात् (why) / च (and) / ते (to you) / न (not) / नमेरन् (would bow) / महात्मन् (O great one) / गरीयसे (to the greater) / ब्रह्मणः (than Brahma) / अपि (even) / आदिकर्त्रे (to the first maker) / अनन्त (endless) / देवेश (Lord of radiant beings) / जगन्निवास (abode of the world) / त्वम् (you) / अक्षरम् (imperishable) / सत् (being) / असत् (non-being) / तत् परम् (beyond that) / यत् (which)
bhagwad_gita::451.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::451.essence: What exceeds all categories naturally draws surrender.
bhagwad_gita::451.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks why anyone would not bow to Krishna, who is greater than even Brahma and beyond all categories of existence and nonexistence.
bhagwad_gita::451.simple_insight: Awe becomes natural when the mind meets something larger than every label it uses.
bhagwad_gita::451.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has seen Krishna's cosmic form and is overwhelmed. His fear turns into reverence as he names Krishna greater than Brahma, the first creator, and beyond all opposites. This verse deepens the prayer before Arjuna asks for mercy.
bhagwad_gita::451.modern_relevance: You stand before a truth that breaks your categories — a diagnosis, a betrayal, a calling you cannot ignore. The mind reaches for labels and fails; reverence begins where certainty ends.
bhagwad_gita::451.insight: It shifts the mind from naming reality to bowing before what exceeds every name.

bhagwad_gita::452.verse_sanskrit: त्वमादिदेवः पुरुषः पुराणस्त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् । वेत्तासि वेद्यं च परं च धामत्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप ॥
bhagwad_gita::452.verse_hindi: आप ही आदिदेव और पुराणपुरुष हैं तथा आप ही इस संसारके परम आश्रय हैं ।  आप ही सबको जाननेवाले, जाननेयोग्य और परमधाम हैं ।  हे अनन्तरूप  आपसे ही सम्पूर्ण संसार व्याप्त है ॥
bhagwad_gita::452.english_translation: You are the first divine presence, the ancient person, the supreme refuge of this universe. You are the knower, the knowable, and the highest abode. O infinite one, the whole world is pervaded by you.
bhagwad_gita::452.translation_literal: त्वम् (you are) / आदिदेवः (the first divine being) / पुरुषः (the supreme person) / पुराणः (ancient) / त्वम् (you are) / अस्य (of this) / विश्वस्य (of the universe) / परम् (highest) / निधानम् (refuge, resting place) / वेत्ता (knower) / असि (you are) / वेद्यम् (the knowable) / च (and) / परम् (highest) / च (and) / धाम (abode) / त्वया (by you) / तम् (pervaded) / विश्वम् (the universe) / अनन्तरूप (O infinite-formed one)
bhagwad_gita::452.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::452.essence: The one you seek is the ground that already holds everything.
bhagwad_gita::452.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees Krishna as the first source, the ancient being, the highest refuge, and the one who pervades everything. Krishna is both the knower and the known.
bhagwad_gita::452.simple_insight: Reverence deepens when the mind sees that everything rests in one all-pervading reality.
bhagwad_gita::452.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is overwhelmed by Krishna’s cosmic form. After asking why the wise would not bow, he now names what he sees: Krishna as the first source, the ancient being, the highest refuge, and the power filling all existence.
bhagwad_gita::452.modern_relevance: You stand before a decision that could change your life, and the room feels too small for it. This verse speaks to the moment when you realise the thing you seek is also what holds the whole scene together.
bhagwad_gita::452.insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to recognition: the sacred is not elsewhere, but already permeating all experience.

bhagwad_gita::453.verse_sanskrit: वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः शशाङ्कःप्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च । नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्वःपुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते ॥
bhagwad_gita::453.verse_hindi: आप ही वायु, यमराज, अग्नि, वरुण, चन्द्रमा, दक्ष आदि प्रजापति और प्रपितामह ब्रह्माजीके भी पिता हैं ।  आपको हजारों बार नमस्कार हो नमस्कार हो   और फिर भी आपको बारबार नमस्कार हो  नमस्कार हो ॥
bhagwad_gita::453.english_translation: You are air, Yama, fire, Varuna, the moon, Prajapati, and the great ancestor. I bow to you a thousand times, and again and again.
bhagwad_gita::453.translation_literal: वायुः (air) / यमः (Yama) / अग्निः (fire) / वरुणः (Varuna) / शशाङ्कः (moon) / प्रजापतिः (Prajapati) / त्वम् (you) / प्रपितामहः (great ancestor) / च (and) / नमः नमः ते (salutations, salutations to you) / अस्तु (may it be) / सहस्रकृत्वः (a thousand times) / पुनः (again) / च (and) / भूयः अपि (again and again) / नमः नमः ते (salutations, salutations to you)
bhagwad_gita::453.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::453.essence: All powers and forces bow inside the one you face.
bhagwad_gita::453.simple_meaning: Arjuna sees Krishna as the source behind all cosmic powers and offers repeated bowing. The response is not argument but reverence.
bhagwad_gita::453.simple_insight: Awe can dissolve pride faster than explanation can.
bhagwad_gita::453.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is overwhelmed by Krishna's cosmic form. After seeing the vast power behind the universe, he names the forces of nature and creation as Krishna's own presence, then bows again and again in reverence.
bhagwad_gita::453.modern_relevance: You stand before something too large to control — a diagnosis, a confession, a loss you cannot undo. The mind stops bargaining and simply bows.
bhagwad_gita::453.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to contain reality to reverently acknowledging its vast source.

bhagwad_gita::454.verse_sanskrit: नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्तेनमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व । अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वंसर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्वः ॥
bhagwad_gita::454.verse_hindi: हे सर्व  आपको आगेसे भी नमस्कार हो  पीछेसे भी नमस्कार हो  सब ओरसे ही नमस्कार हो  हे अनन्तवीर्य  अमित विक्रमवाले आपने सबको समावृत कर रखा है अतः सब कुछ आप ही हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::454.english_translation: Salutations to you from the front, from behind, and from every side. You are endless power and immeasurable might; you pervade all and therefore are all.
bhagwad_gita::454.translation_literal: नमः (salutation) / पुरस्तात् (from the front) / अथ (and) / पृष्ठतः (from behind) / ते (to you) / नमः अस्तु (let there be salutation) / ते (to you) / सर्वतः (from every side) / एव (indeed) / सर्व (all) / अनन्त-वीर्य (endless power) / अमित-विक्रम (immeasurable might) / त्वम् (you) / सर्वम् (all) / समाप्नोषि (pervade, encompass) / ततः (therefore) / असि (are) / सर्वः (all)
bhagwad_gita::454.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::454.essence: Total awe ends the illusion of separation.
bhagwad_gita::454.simple_meaning: Arjuna bows to Krishna from every direction, recognizing that Krishna pervades everything and is beyond ordinary limits.
bhagwad_gita::454.simple_insight: Awe becomes humility when you realize nothing stands outside the divine presence.
bhagwad_gita::454.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has just seen Krishna's cosmic form and can barely hold himself together. The vision overwhelms him, and this verse becomes a full-body bow: front, back, and every direction. He recognises Krishna as all-pervading and beyond measure.
bhagwad_gita::454.modern_relevance: You stand speechless after a moment that dwarfs your pride — a hospital corridor, a funeral, a birth, a breakup. Some encounters leave only one honest response: bowing inwardly.
bhagwad_gita::454.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to reverent surrender before what exceeds control.

bhagwad_gita::455.verse_sanskrit: सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तंहे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति । अजानता महिमानं तवेदंमया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि ॥
bhagwad_gita::455.verse_hindi: आपकी महिमा और स्वरूपको न जानते हुए मेरे सखा हैं ऐसा मानकर मैंने प्रमादसे अथवा प्रेमसे हठपूर्वक बिना सोचेसमझे हे कृष्ण  हे यादव  हे सखे  इस प्रकार जो कुछ कहा है और हे अच्युत  हँसीदिल्लगीमें, चलतेफिरते, सोतेजागते, उठतेबैठते, खातेपीते समयमें अकेले अथवा उन सखाओं, कुटुम्बियों आदिके सामने मेरे द्वारा आपका जो कुछ तिरस्कार किया गया है वह सब अप्रमेयस्वरुप आपसे मैं क्षमा माँगता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::455.english_translation: Thinking of you as a friend, I addressed you carelessly: “O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend.” Not knowing your greatness, I spoke in negligence or affection. I ask forgiveness from your immeasurable form for every disrespect I showed in laughter, play, walking, sleeping, sitting, eating, alone or before companions and relatives.
bhagwad_gita::455.translation_literal: सखा-इति (as a friend) / मत्वा (thinking) / प्रसभम् (boldly, carelessly) / यत् (whatever) / उक्तम् (was said) / हे कृष्ण (O Krishna) / हे यादव (O Yadava) / हे सखः-इति (O friend) / अजानता (not knowing) / महिमानम् (greatness) / तव (your) / इदम् (this) / मया (by me) / प्रमादात् (through negligence) / प्रणयेन (through affection) / वा अपि (or even) / यत् (whatever) / अवहास-अर्थम् (for the sake of joking) / असत्कृतः (treated disrespectfully) / असि (you are) / विहार-शय्या-आसन-भोजनेषु (in recreation, sleep, seat, and भोजन) / एकः अथवा अपि (alone or even) / अच्युत (O infallible one) / तत् (that) / समक्षम (in the presence) / तत् क्षामये (that I ask forgiveness) / त्वाम् (from you) / अहम् (I) / अप्रमेयम् (immeasurable one)
bhagwad_gita::455.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::455.essence: Familiarity without recognition becomes disrespect; awe restores the right relation.
bhagwad_gita::455.simple_meaning: Arjuna apologizes for treating Krishna casually as a friend, not knowing his true greatness. He asks forgiveness for every disrespectful word and act.
bhagwad_gita::455.simple_insight: Real reverence begins when casual familiarity turns into humble recognition.
bhagwad_gita::455.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has just seen Krishna's cosmic form and is overwhelmed. The friend he joked with now appears immeasurable. Struck by shame, Arjuna names his careless words and asks forgiveness before that vast presence.
bhagwad_gita::455.modern_relevance: You joke too freely with someone until one moment reveals how much they carry. Then embarrassment arrives first, and respect becomes honest.
bhagwad_gita::455.insight: It shifts devotion from familiarity to humility, teaching the reader to recognise greatness before speaking lightly.

bhagwad_gita::456.verse_hindi: आपकी महिमा और स्वरूपको न जानते हुए मेरे सखा हैं ऐसा मानकर मैंने प्रमादसे अथवा प्रेमसे भी हठपूर्वक बिना सोचेसमझे हे कृष्ण  हे यादव  हे सखे  इस प्रकार जो कुछ कहा है और हे अच्युत  हँसीदिल्लगीमें, चलतेफिरते, सोतेजागते, उठतेबैठते, खातेपीते समयमें अकेले अथवा उन सखाओं, कुटुम्बियों आदिके सामने मेरे द्वारा आपका जो कुछ तिरस्कार किया गया है, वह सब अप्रमेस्वरूप आपसे मैं क्षमा करवाता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::456.english_translation: Whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while walking, resting, sitting, eating, alone or before others, I ask your immeasurable forgiveness.
bhagwad_gita::456.translation_literal: यत् (whatever) च (and) अवहासार्थम् (for the sake of jest) असत्कृतः (shown disrespect) असि (you were) विहार-शय्या-आसन-भोजनेषु (in walking, resting, sitting, and eating) । एकः (alone) अथवा (or) अपि (also) अच्युत (O infallible one) तत्-समक्षम् (in that presence) तत् (that) क्षामये (I ask forgiveness) त्वाम् (you) अहम् (I) अप्रमेयम् (immeasurable one) ॥
bhagwad_gita::456.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::456.essence: Familiarity can hide greatness until awe breaks through.
bhagwad_gita::456.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to forgive every careless or disrespectful thing he said or did, in private and in public.
bhagwad_gita::456.simple_insight: A humble heart can repair what pride once damaged.
bhagwad_gita::456.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has just seen Krishna's cosmic form and feels overwhelmed by his own carelessness. He now confesses the many times he treated Krishna casually or disrespectfully, and begs forgiveness before the divine presence.
bhagwad_gita::456.modern_relevance: You realize, too late, how casually you spoke to someone who was carrying more than you knew. The apology is no longer about saving face; it is about seeing clearly.
bhagwad_gita::456.insight: It shifts the mind from familiarity to reverence, and from embarrassment to honest repair.

bhagwad_gita::457.verse_sanskrit: पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्यत्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान् । न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्योलोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभाव ॥
bhagwad_gita::457.verse_hindi: आप ही इस चराचर संसारके पिता हैं, आप ही पूजनीय हैं और आप ही गुरुओंके महान् गुरु हैं ।  हे अनन्त प्रभावशाली भगवन्  इस त्रिलोकीमें आपके समान भी दूसरा कोई नहीं है, फिर अधिक तो हो ही कैसे सकता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::457.english_translation: You are the father of all moving and unmoving beings, the highest object of reverence, and the greatest teacher. In the three worlds, no one equals you, much less surpasses you.
bhagwad_gita::457.translation_literal: पिता (father) / असि (are) / लोकस्य (of the world) / चराचरस्य (of the moving and unmoving) / त्वम् (you) / अस्य (of this) / पूज्यः (worthy of worship) / च (and) / गुरुः (teacher) / गरीयान् (the greatest) / न (not) / त्वत्समः (equal to you) / अस्ति (there is) / अभ्यधिकः (greater) / कुतः (how) / अन्यः (another) / लोकत्रये (in the three worlds) / अपि (even) / अप्रतिमप्रभाव (of unmatched power)
bhagwad_gita::457.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::457.essence: Recognition of the highest power dissolves all comparison.
bhagwad_gita::457.simple_meaning: Arjuna recognizes Krishna as the father, teacher, and highest object of reverence for all beings. No one in the three worlds is equal to him.
bhagwad_gita::457.simple_insight: Awe becomes humility when you finally see what stands before you.
bhagwad_gita::457.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has just seen Krishna's cosmic form and is overwhelmed. After apologizing for his earlier familiarity, he now names Krishna as the source, teacher, and unmatched power behind all existence.
bhagwad_gita::457.modern_relevance: You stand before someone whose wisdom exposes your smallness — a mentor, a parent, a truth you can no longer argue with. The only honest response is reverence.
bhagwad_gita::457.insight: It shifts the mind from familiarity and ego to reverence and surrender.

bhagwad_gita::458.verse_sanskrit: तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायंप्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् । पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युःप्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::458.verse_hindi: इसलिये शरीरसे लम्बा पड़कर स्तुति करनेयोग्य आप ईश्वरको मैं प्रणाम करके प्रसन्न करना चाहता हूँ ।  जैसे पिता पुत्रके, मित्र मित्रके और पति पत्नीके अपमानको सह लेता है, ऐसे ही हे देव  आप मेरे द्वारा किया गया अपमान सहनेमें समर्थ हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::458.english_translation: Therefore, bowing down my body, I seek to please You, the worthy Lord of praise. Like a father bearing a son’s fault, a friend bearing a friend’s, or a lover bearing a beloved’s, You should forgive what I have done.
bhagwad_gita::458.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) / प्रणम्य (bowing down) / प्रणिधाय (placing down) / कायम् (the body) / प्रसादये (I seek to please) / त्वाम् (You) / अहम् (I) / ईशम् (the Lord) / ईड्यम् (worthy of praise) / पितेव (like a father) / पुत्रस्य (of a son) / सखा इव (like a friend) / सख्युः (of a friend) / प्रियः (a beloved) / प्रियायाः (of a beloved) / अर्हसि (You should) / देव (O radiant one) / सोढुम् (to bear / forgive)
bhagwad_gita::458.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::458.essence: True reverence asks forgiveness without excuses.
bhagwad_gita::458.simple_meaning: Arjuna bows fully to Krishna and asks for forgiveness, saying Krishna should bear his disrespect the way loved ones bear each other’s faults.
bhagwad_gita::458.simple_insight: Humility can repair what fear and pride have strained.
bhagwad_gita::458.detailed_meaning: Arjuna stands before Krishna’s cosmic form on the battlefield, shaken by awe and guilt. After seeing the vastness of Krishna’s being, he lowers his body completely and asks forgiveness for past familiarity and disrespect.
bhagwad_gita::458.modern_relevance: You realize, halfway through a harsh message, that you crossed a line. Pride wants to defend itself; humility lets you own the harm and ask forgiveness plainly.
bhagwad_gita::458.insight: It shifts the response from self-protection to humble repair.

bhagwad_gita::459.verse_sanskrit: अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वाभयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे । तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपंप्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥
bhagwad_gita::459.verse_hindi: मैंने ऐसा रुप पहले कभी नहीं देखा ।  इस रूपको देखकर मैं हर्षित हो रहा हूँ और साथहीसाथ भयसे मेरा मन अत्यन्त व्यथित हो रहा है ।  अतः आप मुझे अपने उसी देवरूपको सौम्य विष्णुरूपको दिखाइये ।  हे देवेश  हे जगन्निवास  आप प्रसन्न होइये ॥
bhagwad_gita::459.english_translation: I have never seen this form before. Seeing it, I am filled with joy, yet my mind is troubled by fear. Show me again your gentle divine form; be pleased, O Lord of lords, O dwelling of the world.
bhagwad_gita::459.translation_literal: अदृष्टपूर्वम् (never seen before) / हृषितः (delighted) / अस्मि (I am) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / अभयेन (with fearlessness) / च (and) / प्रव्यथितम् (disturbed) / मनः (mind) / मे (my) / तत् (that) / एव (only) / मे (to me) / दर्शय (show) / देव (O divine one) / रूपम् (form) / प्रसीद (be gracious) / देवेश (Lord of lords) / जगन्निवास (dwelling of the world)
bhagwad_gita::459.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::459.essence: A vision can awaken joy and fear at once.
bhagwad_gita::459.simple_meaning: Arjuna is overwhelmed by Krishna's cosmic form. He asks to see the familiar, gentle form again because the vast vision fills him with both awe and fear.
bhagwad_gita::459.simple_insight: Even wonder can become too much; the heart still longs for what feels safe and known.
bhagwad_gita::459.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has just seen Krishna's universal form and cannot bear its intensity. He is thrilled by the revelation, yet shaken by fear. So he asks Krishna to withdraw that overwhelming vision and appear again in the gentler, familiar form.
bhagwad_gita::459.modern_relevance: You finally hear the brutal truth you asked for, and it lands harder than expected. Part of you is grateful; part of you wants the conversation to return to something human again.
bhagwad_gita::459.insight: It shows that revelation must be met with humility, and that surrender can include asking for a form the mind can bear.

bhagwad_gita::460.verse_sanskrit: किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्तमिच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव । तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेनसहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते ॥
bhagwad_gita::460.verse_hindi: मैं आपको वैसे ही किरीटधारी, गदाधारी और हाथमें चक्र लिये हुए देखना चाहता हूँ ।  इसलिये हे सहस्रबाहो  हे विश्वमूर्ते  आप उसी चतुर्भुजरूपसे हो जाइये ॥
bhagwad_gita::460.english_translation: I want to see you again in your crowned form, with mace and discus in your hands. O Thousand-Armed One, O Universal Form, return to that four-armed shape.
bhagwad_gita::460.translation_literal: किरीटिनम् (crowned) / गदिनम् (with mace) / चक्रहस्तम् (with discus in hand) / इच्छामि (I want) / त्वाम् (you) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / अहम् (I) / तथा एव (just so, exactly) / तेन एव (by that very) / रूपेण (form) / चतुर्भुजेन (with four arms) / सहस्रबाहो (O thousand-armed one) / भव (be) / विश्वमूर्ते (O universal form)
bhagwad_gita::460.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::460.essence: The infinite can overwhelm; devotion asks for a form the heart can bear.
bhagwad_gita::460.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to return to the familiar four-armed form with crown, mace, and discus. The overwhelming cosmic form has moved him, but he longs for a shape he can meet with devotion.
bhagwad_gita::460.simple_insight: Awe can be too much to hold. The heart asks for a form it can love without fear.
bhagwad_gita::460.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna has just seen Krishna's vast cosmic form and feels shaken. He now asks Krishna to return to the four-armed form he knows, because the infinite vision is overwhelming and he can meet that gentler form with steadier devotion.
bhagwad_gita::460.modern_relevance: You finally see the full truth of a situation, and it leaves you trembling. After the shock, you want something familiar enough to hold without breaking.
bhagwad_gita::460.insight: It teaches you that reverence can include a need for limits, and that love may ask for a form the mind can bear.

bhagwad_gita::461.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचमया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदंरूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात् । तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यंयन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::461.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे अर्जुन  मैंने प्रसन्न होकर अपनी सामर्थ्यसे यह अत्यन्त श्रेष्ठ, तेजोमय, सबका आदि और अनन्त विश्वरूप तुझे दिखाया है, जिसको तुम्हारे सिवाय पहले किसीने नहीं देखा है ॥
bhagwad_gita::461.english_translation: Krishna said: O Arjuna, I have shown you this supreme, radiant, endless, original form through my grace. No one except you has seen it before.
bhagwad_gita::461.translation_literal: श्रीभगवानुवाच (the Lord said) / मया (by me) / प्रसन्नेन (being pleased) / तव (to you) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / इदम् (this) / रूपम् (form) / परम् (supreme) / दर्शितम् (shown) / आत्मयोगात् (through my own power) / तेजोमयम् (full of radiance) / विश्वम् (all) / अनन्तम् (endless) / आद्यम् (original) / यत् (which) / मे (of me) / त्वदन्येन (by anyone other than you) / न (not) / दृष्टपूर्वम् (seen before)
bhagwad_gita::461.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::461.essence: What is most sacred is seen only by grace.
bhagwad_gita::461.simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that he has revealed this radiant, original, endless form through his own power, and no one else has seen it before.
bhagwad_gita::461.simple_insight: A rare glimpse can feel like grace, not achievement.
bhagwad_gita::461.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has just begged to see Krishna's familiar form again after the overwhelming cosmic vision. Krishna answers that the vision itself came by his grace and power, and that Arjuna has been given a sight no one else has received.
bhagwad_gita::461.modern_relevance: You finally understand something that had been hidden for years — not because you forced it, but because the moment was given to you.
bhagwad_gita::461.insight: It shifts the mind from ownership of insight to gratitude for revelation.

bhagwad_gita::462.verse_sanskrit: न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानैर्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः । एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोकेद्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर ॥
bhagwad_gita::462.verse_hindi: हे कुरुप्रवीर मनुष्यलोकमें इस प्रकारके विश्वरूपवाला मैं न वेदोंके पढ़नेसे, न यज्ञोंके अनुष्ठानसे, न दानसे, न उग्र तपोंसे और न मात्र क्रियाओंसे तेरे कृपापात्रके सिवाय और किसीके द्वारा देखा जाना शक्य हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::462.english_translation: I cannot be seen in this form in the human world by study of the Vedas, sacrifice, charity, severe austerity, or ritual acts—except by you, Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::462.translation_literal: न (not) / वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैः (by Veda-study and sacrifices) / न (not) / दानैः (by gifts) / न (not) / च (and) / क्रियाभिः (by actions) / न (not) / तपोभिः (by austerities) / उग्रैः (severe) / एवंरूपः (of this form) / शक्यः (possible) / अहम् (I) / नृलोके (in the human world) / द्रष्टुम् (to be seen) / त्वदन्येन (by anyone other than you) / कुरुप्रवीर (O best of the Kurus)
bhagwad_gita::462.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::462.essence: The highest vision cannot be forced; it arrives only through grace.
bhagwad_gita::462.simple_meaning: Krishna says his cosmic form cannot be seen through rituals, study, gifts, or harsh austerity. Only Arjuna, by divine grace, has that vision.
bhagwad_gita::462.simple_insight: Not every treasure is earned. Some things are given only when the heart is ready.
bhagwad_gita::462.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has already seen Krishna's cosmic form and wants the familiar four-armed form again. Krishna explains that this vision is not won by scholarship, sacrifice, charity, or austerity. It appears only through special grace.
bhagwad_gita::462.modern_relevance: You can read every book, follow every rule, and still miss what matters most. The moment of real seeing often arrives only after the grip of control finally loosens.
bhagwad_gita::462.insight: It shifts the mind from achievement to receptivity, showing that the deepest vision cannot be forced.

bhagwad_gita::463.verse_sanskrit: मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावोदृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् । व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वंतदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य ॥
bhagwad_gita::463.verse_hindi: यह इस प्रकारका मेरा घोररूप देखकर तेरेको व्यथा नहीं होनी चाहिये और मूढ़भाव भी नहीं होना चाहिये ।  अब निर्भय और प्रसन्न मनवाला होकर तू फिर उसी मेरे इस चतुर्भुज रूपको अच्छी तरह देख ले ॥
bhagwad_gita::463.english_translation: Do not be distressed or confused by this fierce form of mine. Free from fear and calm-minded, look again upon this very form of mine.
bhagwad_gita::463.translation_literal: मा (do not) / ते (your) / व्यथा (distress) / मा (do not) / च (and) / विमूढभावः (confused state) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / रूपम् (form) / घोरम् (fierce) / ईदृक् (such) / मम (my) / इदम् (this) / व्यपेतभीः (fear gone) / प्रीतमनाः (with pleased mind) / पुनः (again) / त्वम् (you) / तदेव (that very) / मे (my) / रूपम् (form) / इदम् (this) / प्रपश्य (look upon)
bhagwad_gita::463.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::463.essence: Fear must drop before the deeper vision can be seen.
bhagwad_gita::463.simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna not to panic after seeing the terrifying form. Fear and confusion should fall away, and Arjuna should look again with a calm, glad mind.
bhagwad_gita::463.simple_insight: Even overwhelming awe can become steady when fear drops away.
bhagwad_gita::463.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has just seen Krishna's terrible cosmic form and is shaken. Krishna immediately soothes him, telling him not to lose his mind or fear. This verse turns the vision from terror back into relationship.
bhagwad_gita::463.modern_relevance: You read a message that changes everything, and your chest tightens before you can think. The first task is not analysis — it is to steady the mind enough to see clearly.
bhagwad_gita::463.insight: It shifts the response from panic to composed seeing, so the mind can receive what is being shown.

bhagwad_gita::464.verse_sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाचइत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वास्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः । आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनंभूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा ॥
bhagwad_gita::464.verse_hindi: सञ्जय बोले  वासुदेवभगवान् ने अर्जुनसे ऐसा कहकर फिर उसी प्रकारसे अपना रूप देवरूप दिखाया और महात्मा श्रीकृष्णने पुनः सौम्यवपु द्विभुजरूप होकर इस भयभीत अर्जुनको आश्वासन दिया ॥
bhagwad_gita::464.english_translation: Sanjaya said: After speaking thus to Arjuna, Vasudeva revealed his own form again. The great one then reassured the frightened Arjuna, taking once more a gentle form.
bhagwad_gita::464.translation_literal: सञ्जय उवाच (Sanjaya said) / इति (thus) / अर्जुनम् (to Arjuna) / वासुदेवः (Vasudeva) / तथा उक्त्वा (having spoken thus) / स्वकम् (his own) / रूपम् (form) / दर्शयामास (showed) / भूयः (again) / आश्वासयामास (reassured) / च (and) / भीतम् (the frightened one) / एनम् (him) / भूत्वा (having become) / पुनः (again) / सौम्य-वपुः (gentle-bodied / gentle form) / महात्मा (the great one)
bhagwad_gita::464.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::464.essence: A vision can shake you; compassion brings you back.
bhagwad_gita::464.simple_meaning: After speaking to Arjuna, Krishna showed his gentler form again and calmed Arjuna’s fear.
bhagwad_gita::464.simple_insight: Fear eases when the overwhelming vision gives way to something human and familiar.
bhagwad_gita::464.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has just seen the terrifying cosmic form and trembles. Sanjaya reports that Krishna, seeing his fear, returns to a gentle form and reassures him. The moment is about mercy after awe.
bhagwad_gita::464.modern_relevance: You finally say the hard truth, and the other person goes quiet. Then you soften your voice, steady your face, and help them breathe again.
bhagwad_gita::464.insight: It shows that revelation must be followed by reassurance when the listener is overwhelmed.

bhagwad_gita::465.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचदृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तवसौम्यं जनार्दन । इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः ॥
bhagwad_gita::465.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे जनार्दन  आपके इस सौम्य मनुष्यरूपको देखकर मैं इस समय स्थिरचित्त हो गया हूँ और अपनी स्वाभाविक स्थितिको प्राप्त हो गया हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::465.english_translation: Arjuna said: Seeing your gentle human form, Janardana, I am calm again and restored to my natural state.
bhagwad_gita::465.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / दृष्ट्वा (having seen) / इदम् (this) / मानुषम् (human) / रूपम् (form) / तव (your) / सौम्यम् (gentle) / जनार्दन (Janardana) / इदानीम् (now) / अस्मि (I am) / संवृत्तः (restored) / सचेताः (fully conscious, calm) / प्रकृतिम् (natural state) / गतः (gone to, returned)
bhagwad_gita::465.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::465.essence: Gentleness restores the mind after overwhelming awe.
bhagwad_gita::465.simple_meaning: Arjuna feels settled again after seeing Krishna’s gentle human form. The terrifying cosmic vision has passed, and his mind returns to normal.
bhagwad_gita::465.simple_insight: A frightening experience can end in relief when the heart meets something familiar and safe again.
bhagwad_gita::465.detailed_meaning: After seeing Krishna’s terrifying cosmic form, Arjuna asks for mercy. Krishna restores his gentle human appearance. In that relief, Arjuna says his mind is steady again and he has returned to his natural state.
bhagwad_gita::465.modern_relevance: You finally hear the softer voice after a brutal confrontation. The body unclenches first, and only then does the mind remember how to breathe.
bhagwad_gita::465.insight: It shows how reassurance can restore clarity after overwhelm.

bhagwad_gita::466.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचसुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम । देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः ॥
bhagwad_gita::466.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  मेरा यह जो रूप तुमने देखा है, इसके दर्शन अत्यन्त ही दुर्लभ हैं ।  इस रूपको देखनेके लिये देवता भी नित्य लालायित रहते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::466.english_translation: Krishna said: The form you have seen is very hard to behold. Even the radiant beings long forever to see it.
bhagwad_gita::466.translation_literal: श्रीभगवानुवाच (the Lord said) / सुदुर्दर्शम् (very hard to behold) / इदम् (this) / रूपम् (form) / दृष्टवान् (seen) / असि (you have) / यत् (which) / मम (of mine) / देवाः (radiant beings) / अपि (even) / अस्य (of this) / रूपस्य (of form) / नित्यम् (always) / दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः (desiring to see)
bhagwad_gita::466.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::466.essence: The vision Arjuna saw is beyond ordinary access, even for radiant beings.
bhagwad_gita::466.simple_meaning: Krishna says Arjuna has seen a form that is extremely rare to behold. Even the radiant beings always long to see it.
bhagwad_gita::466.simple_insight: Some truths are so vast that even the highest beings long for them.
bhagwad_gita::466.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, after Arjuna has been overwhelmed by Krishna's cosmic form and then steadied by Krishna's gentler form, Krishna explains what Arjuna has just been allowed to see. The vision is not ordinary; it is rarer than anything even the radiant beings can behold.
bhagwad_gita::466.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of something that changes you — a raw truth, a deep love, a moment of awe — and later realize most people never see it at all.
bhagwad_gita::466.insight: It shifts the mind from taking sacred experience for granted to recognising its rarity and value.

bhagwad_gita::467.verse_sanskrit: नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया । शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा ॥
bhagwad_gita::467.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार तुमने मुझे देखा है, इस प्रकारका चतुर्भुजरूपवाला मैं न तो वेदोंसे, न तपसे, न दानसे और न यज्ञसे ही देखा जा सकता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::467.english_translation: I cannot be seen in this form through the Vedas, austerity, charity, or sacrifice, as you have seen me.
bhagwad_gita::467.translation_literal: न अहं (not I) / वेदैः (by the Vedas) / न तपसा (not by austerity) / न दानेन (not by charity) / न च ईज्यया (and not by sacrifice) / शक्यः (possible) / एवम्-विधः (of this kind) / द्रष्टुम् (to be seen) / दृष्टवान् असि (you have seen) / माम् (me) / यथा (as)
bhagwad_gita::467.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::467.essence: The deepest vision comes through devotion, not mere accomplishment.
bhagwad_gita::467.simple_meaning: Krishna says that this divine form cannot be fully reached through scripture, austerity, charity, or ritual alone. Arjuna has seen it because a deeper devotion has opened the way.
bhagwad_gita::467.simple_insight: Trying harder is not enough; the heart must be turned toward the divine.
bhagwad_gita::467.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has just been overwhelmed by Krishna’s cosmic form and then calmed by the return to a gentler shape. Krishna now explains that this four-armed vision is not won by study, discipline, gifts, or ritual. The sight Arjuna received came through a deeper opening.
bhagwad_gita::467.modern_relevance: You can read every book, follow every practice, and still miss what matters. In the moment you finally admit you cannot force understanding, a deeper seeing can arrive.
bhagwad_gita::467.insight: It shifts the seeker from achievement to receptivity, showing that devotion opens what effort alone cannot.

bhagwad_gita::468.verse_sanskrit: भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्यमहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन । ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप ॥
bhagwad_gita::468.verse_hindi: परन्तु हे शत्रुतापन अर्जुन  इस प्रकार चतुर्भुजरूपवाला मैं अनन्यभक्तिसे ही तत्त्वसे जाननेमें, सगुणरूपसे देखनेमें और प्राप्त करनेमें शक्य हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::468.english_translation: But only through undivided devotion can I be truly known, seen, and entered, Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::468.translation_literal: भक्त्या (through devotion) / तु (but) / अनन्यया (undivided) / शक्यः (possible) / अहम् (I) / एवंविधः (of this kind) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / ज्ञातुम् (to know) / द्रष्टुम् (to see) / च (and) / तत्त्वेन (in essence) / प्रवेष्टुम् (to enter) / च (and) / परंतप (O scorcher of foes)
bhagwad_gita::468.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::468.essence: Undivided devotion reaches what effort cannot.
bhagwad_gita::468.simple_meaning: Krishna says that his true form can be known, seen, and entered only through single-pointed devotion, not by ordinary effort alone.
bhagwad_gita::468.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing the deepest reality responds to love and single-heartedness, not just achievement.
bhagwad_gita::468.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has just seen Krishna's cosmic form and is overwhelmed. Krishna now explains the final key: this presence cannot be grasped by learning or ritual alone. Only undivided devotion can truly know and enter him.
bhagwad_gita::468.modern_relevance: You can read every book, gather every technique, and still miss what matters. The moment you stop trying to control everything and give yourself fully, understanding begins.
bhagwad_gita::468.insight: It shifts the mind from mastery by force to access through wholehearted devotion.

bhagwad_gita::469.verse_sanskrit: मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः । निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव ॥
bhagwad_gita::469.verse_hindi: हे पाण्डवन  जो मेरे लिये ही कर्म करनेवाला, मेरे ही परायण और मेरा ही भक्त है तथा सर्वथा आसक्तिरहित और प्राणिमात्रके साथ निर्वैर है, वह भक्त मेरेको प्राप्त होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::469.english_translation: O Pandava, the devotee who works for Me alone, takes Me as the highest goal, is devoted to Me, is free from attachment, and bears no enmity toward any being, comes to Me.
bhagwad_gita::469.translation_literal: मत्कर्मकृत् (doing action for Me) / मत्परमः (having Me as the highest) / मद्भक्तः (My devotee) / सङ्गवर्जितः (free from attachment) / निर्वैरः (without hostility) / सर्वभूतेषु (toward all beings) / यः (who) / सः (that one) / माम् (Me) / एति (comes) / पाण्डव (O Pandava)
bhagwad_gita::469.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::469.essence: Devotion matures into freedom when attachment and hostility are gone.
bhagwad_gita::469.simple_meaning: The one who serves Krishna with full devotion, without attachment or hostility toward any being, reaches him.
bhagwad_gita::469.simple_insight: Devotion becomes complete when love is steady, desire is loose, and the heart stops making enemies.
bhagwad_gita::469.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has already seen Krishna's cosmic form and heard that devotion is the only way to know him fully. Now Krishna gives the final shape of that devotion: act for him, hold him as the highest, free yourself from attachment, and drop hostility toward all beings.
bhagwad_gita::469.modern_relevance: You keep replaying the argument in your head after the meeting ends. The verse points to a cleaner way to live: act from devotion, stop gripping the result, and let resentment fall away.
bhagwad_gita::469.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to a whole way of living: action, priority, detachment, and goodwill.

bhagwad_gita::470.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचएवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते । येचाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::470.verse_hindi: जो भक्त इस प्रकार निरन्तर आपमें लगे रहकर आपसगुण भगवान् की उपासना करते हैं और जो अविनाशी निराकारकी ही उपासना करते हैं, उनमेंसे उत्तम योगवेत्ता कौन हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::470.english_translation: Arjuna said: Those devotees who worship You with constant devotion, and those who worship the imperishable, unmanifest reality—who among them are the most accomplished in yoga?
bhagwad_gita::470.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / एवम् (thus) / सततयुक्ताः (constantly devoted) / ये (those who) / भक्ताः (devotees) / त्वाम् (You) / पर्युपासते (worship) / ये (those who) / च (and) / अपि (also) / अक्षरम् (the imperishable) / अव्यक्तम् (the unmanifest) / तेषाम् (of them) / के (which) / योगवित्तमाः (most accomplished in yoga)
bhagwad_gita::470.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::470.essence: Devotion can face the divine as form or as formless reality.
bhagwad_gita::470.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks whether devoted worship of Krishna or worship of the imperishable, formless reality is the higher yoga.
bhagwad_gita::470.simple_insight: It is honest to ask which form of devotion leads deepest.
bhagwad_gita::470.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna still uncertain and the battle waiting, he asks Krishna a sharp question: is loving the personal divine better, or is worshipping the unmanifest absolute higher? Chapter 12 begins by comparing two ways of devotion.
bhagwad_gita::470.modern_relevance: You stand between two paths: a relationship that feels alive, and a principle that feels pure. The question is not weak — it is the mind trying to find the deepest way to give itself.
bhagwad_gita::470.insight: It frames devotion as a real choice between personal love and abstract contemplation, preparing Krishna's answer.

bhagwad_gita::471.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते । श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::471.verse_hindi: मेरेमें मनको लगाकर नित्यनिरन्तर मेरेमें लगे हुए जो भक्त परम श्रद्धासे युक्त होकर मेरी उपासना करते हैं, वे मेरे मतमें सर्वश्रेष्ठ योगी हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::471.english_translation: Those who focus their mind on me, worship me with unwavering devotion, and are filled with supreme trust are, in my view, the highest yogis.
bhagwad_gita::471.translation_literal: मयि (in me) / आवेश्य (placing) / मनः (mind) / ये (who) / माम् (me) / नित्ययुक्ताः (always united) / उपासते (worship) / श्रद्धया (with trust) / परया (highest) / उपेताः (endowed with) / ते (they) / मे (to me / in my view) / युक्ततमाः (most devotedly united) / मताः (are considered)
bhagwad_gita::471.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::471.essence: Full trust and steady remembrance make devotion complete.
bhagwad_gita::471.simple_meaning: Krishna says that the people who keep their mind on him, worship him steadily, and approach him with the highest trust are the best yogis.
bhagwad_gita::471.simple_insight: Devotion is not second-rate. Full-hearted remembrance itself becomes the highest form of yoga.
bhagwad_gita::471.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has asked which seekers are best: those devoted to Krishna's personal form or those who meditate on the formless absolute. Krishna answers by naming the devotee who keeps the mind on him, worships steadily, and trusts completely as the highest.
bhagwad_gita::471.modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, phone in hand, about to hear news that could change everything. In that moment, scattered attention falls away; what remains is the one thing you truly place your heart upon.
bhagwad_gita::471.insight: It shifts devotion from ritual performance to sustained inner focus and trust.

bhagwad_gita::472.verse_sanskrit: ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते । सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::472.verse_hindi: जो अपनी इन्द्रियोंको वशमें करके अचिन्त्य, सब जगह परिपूर्ण, अनिर्देश्य, कूटस्थ, अचल, ध्रुव, अक्षर और अव्यक्तकी उपासना करते हैं, वे प्राणिमात्रके हितमें रत और सब जगह समबुद्धिवाले मनुष्य मुझे ही प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::472.english_translation: Those who worship the unchanging, the indefinable, the unmanifest, the all-pervading, the unthinkable, the unmoving, the eternal, the imperishable—restraining the senses—reach Me alone.
bhagwad_gita::472.translation_literal: ये (those who) / तु (but) / अक्षरम् (the imperishable) / अनिर्देश्यम् (the indefinable) / अव्यक्तम् (the unmanifest) / पर्युपासते (worship all around) / सर्वत्रगम् (all-pervading) / अचिन्त्यम् (unthinkable) / च (and) / कूटस्थम् (unchanging) / अचलम् (unmoving) / ध्रुवम् (eternal)
bhagwad_gita::472.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::472.essence: The deepest devotion reaches what never changes.
bhagwad_gita::472.simple_meaning: People who worship the imperishable, unmanifest reality by controlling their senses and seeing it everywhere ultimately reach Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::472.simple_insight: The mind grows quiet when it stops chasing forms and learns to honor what never changes.
bhagwad_gita::472.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna asks which kind of devotee is best. Krishna answers by describing those who seek the formless, changeless reality with disciplined senses and equal vision. This verse completes the description before Krishna says they reach him.
bhagwad_gita::472.modern_relevance: You close the app after another day of chasing names, images, and reactions. Something deeper in you is tired of surfaces and wants what does not flicker.
bhagwad_gita::472.insight: It shifts devotion from visible forms to steady awareness of what is everywhere and unchanged.

bhagwad_gita::473.verse_sanskrit: संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः । ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::473.verse_hindi: जो अपनी इन्द्रियोंको वशमें करके अचिन्त्य, सब जगह परिपूर्ण, अनिर्देश्य, कूटस्थ, अचल, ध्रुव, अक्षर और अव्यक्तकी उपासना करते हैं, वे प्राणिमात्रके हितमें रत और सब जगह समबुद्धिवाले मनुष्य मुझे ही प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::473.english_translation: Those who restrain the senses, remain even-minded everywhere, and delight in the welfare of all beings reach me alone.
bhagwad_gita::473.translation_literal: संनियम्य (having restrained) / इन्द्रियग्रामम् (the whole group of senses) / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / समबुद्धयः (those with equal understanding) / ते (they) / प्राप्नुवन्ति (attain) / माम् (me) / एव (alone) / सर्वभूतहिते (in the welfare of all beings) / रताः (delighting, devoted)
bhagwad_gita::473.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::473.essence: Reach the divine by mastering yourself and caring for everyone.
bhagwad_gita::473.simple_meaning: Control the senses, stay even-minded with everyone, and care for the good of all beings. That is the way to reach Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::473.simple_insight: Devotion becomes lighter when it stops being private and starts including everyone.
bhagwad_gita::473.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen. Krishna has just praised the highest devotee, and now he shows the shape of that devotion: self-mastery, equal vision, and a heart committed to the welfare of all beings.
bhagwad_gita::473.modern_relevance: You are angry at one person, but the room is full of people who will feel it. This verse asks for the harder move: steady yourself first, then act from care instead of reaction.
bhagwad_gita::473.insight: It shifts devotion from personal feeling to disciplined, universal goodwill.

bhagwad_gita::474.verse_hindi: अव्यक्तमें आसक्त चित्तवाले उन साधकोंको अपने साधनमें कष्ट अधिक होता है क्योंकि देहाभिमानियोंके द्वारा अव्यक्तविषयक गति कठिनतासे प्राप्त की जाती है ॥
bhagwad_gita::474.english_translation: For those whose minds cling to the unmanifest, the struggle is greater. The unmanifest path is hard to reach for embodied beings.
bhagwad_gita::474.translation_literal: क्लेशः (difficulty) / अधिकतरः (greater) / तेषाम् (for them) / अव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम् (of those whose minds are attached to the unmanifest) । अव्यक्ता (unmanifest) / हि (indeed) / गतिः (path/goal) / दुःखम् (painful/difficult) / देहवद्भिः (by embodied beings) / अवाप्यते (is reached)
bhagwad_gita::474.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::474.essence: The subtlest path is hardest for a body-bound mind.
bhagwad_gita::474.simple_meaning: Holding the unmanifest as your focus is harder than it looks. For people still identified with the body, that subtle path is difficult to reach.
bhagwad_gita::474.simple_insight: Not every noble aim is equally easy. Some paths ask for more patience, steadiness, and inner refinement.
bhagwad_gita::474.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield, where a warrior frozen by doubt needs a clear map. After describing the unmanifest path, Krishna warns that it is especially hard for people still bound to bodily identity, so Arjuna can see why devotion to a personal focus is easier.
bhagwad_gita::474.modern_relevance: You sit in silence trying to “just empty the mind,” and the harder you try, the tighter everything feels. Some practices are subtle enough to become a struggle before they become a refuge.
bhagwad_gita::474.insight: It shifts the mind from forcing a lofty practice to choosing the method that fits your current capacity.

bhagwad_gita::475.verse_sanskrit: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः । अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥
bhagwad_gita::475.verse_hindi: परन्तु जो कर्मोंको मेरे अर्पण करके और मेरे परायण होकर अनन्ययोगसे मेरा ही ध्यान करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::475.english_translation: But those who surrender all actions to Me, take Me as their highest aim, and worship Me with single-pointed devotion, meditating on Me alone.
bhagwad_gita::475.translation_literal: ये (those who) / तु (but) / सर्वाणि (all) / कर्माणि (actions) / मयि (in Me) / संन्यस्य (having renounced, offered) / मत्पराः (those devoted to Me as the highest) / अनन्येन (with no other) / एव (indeed) / योगेन (with yoga) / माम् (Me) / ध्यायन्तः (meditating) / उपासते (worship)
bhagwad_gita::475.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::475.essence: Total devotion turns every action into worship.
bhagwad_gita::475.simple_meaning: People who give all their actions to Krishna, make him their highest aim, and worship him with single-minded devotion are described here.
bhagwad_gita::475.simple_insight: There is relief in not carrying your actions alone; devotion turns effort into offering.
bhagwad_gita::475.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna explains the deepest form of devotion. After describing subtler worship, Krishna now names the devotee who places every action at his feet and keeps a single, undivided focus on him.
bhagwad_gita::475.modern_relevance: You finish a hard conversation, then stop replaying it for approval. The action was yours to give; the burden of ownership can be laid down.
bhagwad_gita::475.insight: It shifts action from self-ownership to offering, so effort becomes worship instead of control.

bhagwad_gita::476.verse_sanskrit: तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् । भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::476.verse_hindi: हे पार्थ  मेरेमें आविष्ट चित्तवाले उन भक्तोंका मैं मृत्युरूप संसारसमुद्रसे शीघ्र ही उद्धार करनेवाला बन जाता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::476.english_translation: I quickly become the one who lifts those whose minds are fixed on me from the ocean of mortal existence, O Partha.
bhagwad_gita::476.translation_literal: तेषाम् (of those) / अहम् (I) / समुद्धर्ता (the rescuer) / मृत्यु-संसार-सागरात् (from the ocean of mortal existence) / भवामि (become) / नचिरात् (not after long) / पार्थ (O Partha) / मयि (in me) / आवेशित-चेतसाम् (of those whose minds are fixed)
bhagwad_gita::476.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::476.essence: A mind fixed on Krishna is met by Krishna's saving presence.
bhagwad_gita::476.simple_meaning: Those who place their minds fully on Krishna are not left to struggle alone. He becomes the one who rescues them from the cycle of repeated death and return.
bhagwad_gita::476.simple_insight: Devotion is not abandonment; it is being held when your own strength runs out.
bhagwad_gita::476.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Arjuna is still frozen, and Krishna is answering the devotee's deepest fear: being trapped in the endless ocean of mortality. He promises direct rescue to those whose minds are absorbed in him.
bhagwad_gita::476.modern_relevance: You are sitting in the car after a breakup, staring at the steering wheel, unable to move. This verse speaks to the relief of letting a steadier presence carry what your grip cannot.
bhagwad_gita::476.insight: It shifts devotion from effort alone to a relationship of rescue and trust.

bhagwad_gita::477.verse_sanskrit: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय । निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥
bhagwad_gita::477.verse_hindi: तू मेरेमें मनको लगा और मेरेमें ही बुद्धिको लगा इसके बाद तू मेरेमें ही निवास करेगा  इसमें संशय नहीं है ॥
bhagwad_gita::477.english_translation: Fix your mind on me alone. Place your discerning mind in me, and you will live in me beyond doubt.
bhagwad_gita::477.translation_literal: मयि (in me) / एव (alone) / मनः (mind) / आधत्स्व (place) / मयि (in me) / बुद्धिम् (discerning mind) / निवेशय (fix) / निवसिष्यसि (you will dwell) / मयि (in me) / एव (alone) / अतः (therefore) / ऊर्ध्वम् (afterward) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
bhagwad_gita::477.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::477.essence: A divided mind settles when both thought and feeling rest in the divine.
bhagwad_gita::477.simple_meaning: Keep your mind and discerning mind fixed on Krishna. Then you will abide in him, with no doubt about the result.
bhagwad_gita::477.simple_insight: Single-pointed devotion quiets inner conflict and gives the heart a place to rest.
bhagwad_gita::477.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is still shaken, and Krishna continues the teaching of bhakti. After promising rescue to those devoted to him, he now gives the inner method: place both mind and discernment on him alone.
bhagwad_gita::477.modern_relevance: You are staring at your phone before sending a message that could change a relationship. Half of you wants control, half wants escape. This verse asks for one center, not two.
bhagwad_gita::477.insight: It shifts attention from divided thinking to wholehearted devotion, so the mind stops scattering its power.

bhagwad_gita::478.verse_sanskrit: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् । अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय ॥
bhagwad_gita::478.verse_hindi: अगर तू मनको मेरेमें अचलभावसे स्थिर अर्पण करनेमें समर्थ नहीं है, तो हे धनञ्जय  अभ्यासयोगके द्वारा तू मेरी प्राप्तिकी इच्छा कर ॥
bhagwad_gita::478.english_translation: If you cannot steadily fix your mind on me, then, Dhananjaya, seek me through practice yoga.
bhagwad_gita::478.translation_literal: अथ (then) / चित्तम् (mind) / समाधातुम् (to fix steadily) / न (not) / शक्नोषि (you are able) / मयि (in me) / स्थिरम् (steadily) / अभ्यासयोगेन (through practice yoga) / ततः (then) / माम् (me) / इच्छ (seek/desire) / आप्तुम् (to attain) / धनञ्जय (Dhananjaya)
bhagwad_gita::478.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::478.essence: Practice can lead the mind where stillness cannot yet go.
bhagwad_gita::478.simple_meaning: If steady devotion feels too hard, begin with practice. Keep returning to the divine again and again until the mind learns to stay.
bhagwad_gita::478.simple_insight: You do not need perfect concentration first. Repeated return is enough to begin.
bhagwad_gita::478.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna still stands frozen, and Krishna keeps meeting his wavering mind step by step. After asking him to hold his mind on the divine, Krishna gives a gentler next rung: if that is too hard, use repeated practice to move toward the same love.
bhagwad_gita::478.modern_relevance: You sit down to pray, meditate, or simply stay with one hard truth, and your mind runs off in ten directions. Start again without drama. Repetition can carry you where force cannot.
bhagwad_gita::478.insight: It shifts devotion from a single perfect act to a trainable habit of returning.

bhagwad_gita::479.verse_sanskrit: अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव । मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन् सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::479.verse_hindi: अगर तू अभ्यासयोग में भी असमर्थ है, तो मेरे लिये कर्म करनेके परायण हो जा ।  मेरे लिये कर्मोंको करता हुआ भी तू सिद्धिको प्राप्त हो जायगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::479.english_translation: If you are unable even to practice, then be devoted to working for Me. By doing actions for My sake, you will attain perfection.
bhagwad_gita::479.translation_literal: अभ्यासेऽपि (even in practice) / असमर्थः (unable) / असि (you are) / मत्कर्मपरः (devoted to My work) / भव (become) / मदर्थम् (for My sake) / अपि (even) / कर्माणि (actions) / कुर्वन् (doing) / सिद्धिम् (perfection) / अवाप्स्यसि (you will attain)
bhagwad_gita::479.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::479.essence: Offered action can succeed where practice still fails.
bhagwad_gita::479.simple_meaning: If steady practice is too hard, dedicate your actions to Krishna instead. Even ordinary work offered with devotion can lead to fulfillment.
bhagwad_gita::479.simple_insight: You are not blocked by weakness; you are invited to offer what you can do.
bhagwad_gita::479.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still unable to settle his mind fully on Krishna. Krishna lowers the entry point again: if even practice is too difficult, turn every action into offering. Devotion can carry what discipline cannot yet hold.
bhagwad_gita::479.modern_relevance: You sit at the edge of a hospital bed, too shaken to pray properly, too tired to think clearly. Still, you can wash the cup, make the call, and offer the next act with care.
bhagwad_gita::479.insight: It shifts devotion from a private feeling into a way of acting.

bhagwad_gita::480.verse_sanskrit: अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः । सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् ॥
bhagwad_gita::480.verse_hindi: अगर मेरे योगसमता के आश्रित हुआ तू इसपूर्वश्लोकमें कहे गये साधन को भी करनेमें असमर्थ है, तो मनइन्द्रियोंको वशमें करके सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंके फलका त्याग कर ॥
bhagwad_gita::480.english_translation: If you still cannot do even this while taking refuge in my yoga, then, self-controlled, renounce all fruits of action.
bhagwad_gita::480.translation_literal: अथ (then) / एतत् अपि (this also) / अशक्तः असि (you are unable) / कर्तुम् (to do) / मद्योगम् आश्रितः (taking refuge in my yoga) / सर्व-कर्म-फल-त्यागम् (renunciation of all fruits of action) / ततः (then) / कुरु (do) / यत-आत्मवान् (self-controlled)
bhagwad_gita::480.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::480.essence: Let go of the result; the action itself is the practice.
bhagwad_gita::480.simple_meaning: If even devotion-filled practice feels too hard, give up the need to own the results of your actions. Stay controlled and let the work be enough.
bhagwad_gita::480.simple_insight: There is relief in releasing the demand that every action must pay you back.
bhagwad_gita::480.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna has already offered steadier practices, and now lowers the threshold again: if even that is too hard, renounce attachment to the fruits of action and keep your mind controlled.
bhagwad_gita::480.modern_relevance: You sent the message, then kept checking for a reply that could save or ruin your day. This verse asks you to stop feeding on the outcome and return to the act itself.
bhagwad_gita::480.insight: It shifts attention from owning results to releasing them after sincere effort.

bhagwad_gita::481.verse_hindi: अभ्याससे शास्त्रज्ञान श्रेष्ठ है, शास्त्रज्ञानसे ध्यान श्रेष्ठ है और ध्यानसे भी सब कर्मोंके फलका त्याग श्रेष्ठ है ।  कर्मफलत्यागसे तत्काल ही परमशान्ति प्राप्त हो जाती है ॥
bhagwad_gita::481.english_translation: Knowledge is better than practice; meditation is better than knowledge. Renouncing the fruits of action is better than meditation, and peace follows at once from renunciation.
bhagwad_gita::481.translation_literal: श्रेयो (better) / हि (indeed) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / अभ्यासात् (than practice) / ज्ञानात् (than knowledge) / ध्यानम् (meditation) / विशिष्यते (is superior) / ध्यानात् (than meditation) / कर्मफलत्यागः (renunciation of the fruits of action) / त्यागात् (from renunciation) / शान्तिः (peace) / अनन्तरम् (immediately after)
bhagwad_gita::481.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::481.essence: Peace begins when you stop clinging to what your action produces.
bhagwad_gita::481.simple_meaning: Practice, study, and meditation all help, but letting go of personal reward is even higher. That release brings immediate calm.
bhagwad_gita::481.simple_insight: You do not have to earn peace by forcing control; it comes when grasping ends.
bhagwad_gita::481.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen between duty and grief. Krishna narrows the path step by step: practice, then understanding, then meditation, and finally the deepest release — giving up the fruits of action. That is where peace begins.
bhagwad_gita::481.modern_relevance: You send the hard message, then keep checking your phone for the reaction. The mind burns in that waiting. This verse points to the relief of doing what is right and leaving the outcome alone.
bhagwad_gita::481.insight: It shifts the mind from managing outcomes to releasing them after sincere action.

bhagwad_gita::482.verse_sanskrit: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च । निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी ॥
bhagwad_gita::482.verse_hindi: सब प्राणियोंमें द्वेषभावसे रहित, सबका मित्र प्रेमी और दयालु, ममतारहित, अहंकाररहित, सुखदुःखकी प्राप्तिमें सम, क्षमाशील, निरन्तर सन्तुष्ट, योगी, शरीरको वशमें किये हुए, दृढ़ निश्चयवाला मेरेमें अर्पित मनबुद्धिवाला जो मेरा भक्त है, वह मेरेको प्रिय है ॥
bhagwad_gita::482.english_translation: One who hates no being, is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, equal in pleasure and pain, and forgiving.
bhagwad_gita::482.translation_literal: अद्वेष्टा (free from hatred) / सर्वभूतानां (of all beings) / मैत्रः (friendly) / करुणः (compassionate) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / निर्ममः (without possessiveness) / निरहङ्कारः (without ego) / समदुःखसुखः (equal in pain and pleasure) / क्षमी (forgiving)
bhagwad_gita::482.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::482.essence: Devotion shows up as friendliness, forgiveness, and emotional steadiness.
bhagwad_gita::482.simple_meaning: A devoted person does not hate anyone, treats everyone as a friend, stays compassionate, and does not cling to possessions or ego. Such a person remains steady through joy and sorrow and forgives easily.
bhagwad_gita::482.simple_insight: You can be strong without being hard. Softness, steadiness, and forgiveness are signs of real devotion.
bhagwad_gita::482.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen by grief. Krishna answers not with strategy, but with the character of a true devotee: one who has no hatred, no possessiveness, no ego, and no inner swing between pleasure and pain.
bhagwad_gita::482.modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in traffic, and the old heat rises instantly. This verse asks for a different reflex: no hatred, no inflated self, no need to keep score.
bhagwad_gita::482.insight: It shifts devotion from ritual alone to a transformed way of relating to every person and every feeling.

bhagwad_gita::483.verse_sanskrit: सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः । मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
bhagwad_gita::483.verse_hindi: सब प्राणियोंमें द्वेषभावसे रहित, सबका मित्र प्रेमी और दयालु, ममतारहित, अहंकाररहित, सुखदुःखकी प्राप्तिमें सम, क्षमाशील, निरन्तर सन्तुष्ट,योगी, शरीरको वशमें किये हुए, दृढ़ निश्चयवाला, मेरेमें अर्पित मनबुद्धिवाला जो मेरा भक्त है, वह मेरेको प्रिय है ॥
bhagwad_gita::483.english_translation: The devoted yogi is always content, self-controlled, and steady in resolve. One whose mind and discerning mind are offered to Me is dear to Me.
bhagwad_gita::483.translation_literal: सन्तुष्टः (content) / सततम् (always) / योगी (yogi) / यतात्मा (self-controlled) / दृढनिश्चयः (firm in resolve) / मयि (in Me) / अर्पित (offered) / मनः (mind) / बुद्धिः (discerning mind) / यः (who) / मत्-भक्तः (My devotee) / सः (that one) / मे (to Me) / प्रियः (dear)
bhagwad_gita::483.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::483.essence: Real devotion is a steady mind already placed beyond itself.
bhagwad_gita::483.simple_meaning: A true devotee stays content, controls the body and mind, keeps firm resolve, and places both mind and discernment in Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::483.simple_insight: Devotion is not only feeling; it becomes a steady way of living that makes the heart simple and strong.
bhagwad_gita::483.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna continues shaping a path of devotion. After describing kindness, freedom from hatred, and equality, Krishna names the devotee who has become inwardly steady: content, disciplined, resolved, and fully offered to Him.
bhagwad_gita::483.modern_relevance: You are exhausted, but you still choose not to spiral, not to blame, not to scatter yourself. Something in you stays gathered, and that quiet steadiness is its own devotion.
bhagwad_gita::483.insight: It shifts devotion from emotion alone to a disciplined, inwardly gathered life.

bhagwad_gita::484.verse_sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः । हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥
bhagwad_gita::484.verse_hindi: जिससे किसी प्राणीको उद्वेग नहीं होता और जिसको खुद भी किसी प्राणीसे उद्वेग नहीं होता तथा जो हर्ष, अमर्ष ईर्ष्या, भय और उद्वेगसे रहित है, वह मुझे प्रिय है ॥
bhagwad_gita::484.english_translation: The one who disturbs no one and is disturbed by no one, and who is free from delight, envy, fear, and agitation, is dear to me.
bhagwad_gita::484.translation_literal: यस्मात् (from whom) / न उद्विजते (does not become agitated) / लोकः (the world) / लोकात् (from the world) / न उद्विजते (does not become agitated) / च (and) / यः (who) / हर्ष (delight) / अमर्ष (resentment) / भय (fear) / उद्वेगैः (with agitations) / मुक्तः (freed) / यः (who) / सः (he) / च (and) / मे (to me) / प्रियः (dear)
bhagwad_gita::484.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::484.essence: True devotion leaves no wake of disturbance.
bhagwad_gita::484.simple_meaning: A beloved devotee does not unsettle others and is not easily unsettled by others. Freedom from excitement, envy, fear, and agitation is part of true devotion.
bhagwad_gita::484.simple_insight: There is deep relief in not needing to react, compete, or defend yourself.
bhagwad_gita::484.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield, where every quality is tested under pressure. After describing the devotee as steady, humble, and devoted, he adds one more mark: such a person does not disturb others and is not disturbed by them.
bhagwad_gita::484.modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in traffic, then flips you off through the window. The old reflex rises fast. This verse points to a steadier way: no inner spike, no need to pass the disturbance onward.
bhagwad_gita::484.insight: It shifts the mind from reactive emotion to settled presence that does not spread agitation.

bhagwad_gita::485.verse_sanskrit: अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः । सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
bhagwad_gita::485.verse_hindi: जो आकाङ्क्षासे रहित, बाहरभीतरसे पवित्र, दक्ष, उदासीन, व्यथासे रहित और सभी आरम्भोंका अर्थात् नयेनये कर्मोंके आरम्भका सर्वथा त्यागी है, वह मेरा भक्त मुझे प्रिय है ॥
bhagwad_gita::485.english_translation: One who has no expectation, is pure, skilled, detached, free from anxiety, and has given up all undertakings is dear to me, my devotee.
bhagwad_gita::485.translation_literal: अनपेक्षः (without expectation) / शुचिः (pure) / दक्षः (skilled) / उदासीनः (detached) / गतव्यथः (free from distress) / सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी (one who has given up all undertakings) / यः (who) / मद्भक्तः (my devotee) / सः (that one) / मे (to me) / प्रियः (dear)
bhagwad_gita::485.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::485.essence: True closeness releases craving, anxiety, and compulsive beginning.
bhagwad_gita::485.simple_meaning: Krishna says his beloved devotee has no craving, stays inwardly clean, acts skillfully, remains detached, and drops anxious new beginnings.
bhagwad_gita::485.simple_insight: Devotion here feels light, not needy. Love becomes cleaner when grasping and restless starting are gone.
bhagwad_gita::485.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna defines the devotee who is truly close to him. This verse adds another layer to the chapter’s portrait: the beloved one has no craving, no inner agitation, and no urge to keep launching new projects from restlessness.
bhagwad_gita::485.modern_relevance: You keep opening new tabs, new plans, new fixes because stillness feels unbearable. This verse points to a calmer strength: do what is needed, but stop feeding anxiety with constant beginnings.
bhagwad_gita::485.insight: It shifts devotion from emotional dependence to steady, uncluttered presence.

bhagwad_gita::486.verse_sanskrit: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्ितमान्यः स मे प्रियः ॥
bhagwad_gita::486.verse_hindi: जो न कभी हर्षित होता है, न द्वेष करता है, न शोक करता है, न कामना करता है और जो शुभअशुभ कर्मोंमें रागद्वेषका त्यागी है, वह भक्तिमान् मनुष्य मुझे प्रिय है ॥
bhagwad_gita::486.english_translation: One who neither rejoices, hates, grieves, nor craves, and who has given up attachment to both good and bad actions, is dear to me.
bhagwad_gita::486.translation_literal: यः (who) / न (not) / हृष्यति (rejoices) / न (not) / द्वेष्टि (hates) / न (not) / शोचति (grieves) / न (not) / काङ्क्षति (craves) / शुभाशुभपरित्यागी (one who has abandoned good-and-bad attachment) / भक्तिमान् (devoted) / यः (one who) / सः (that one) / मे (to me) / प्रियः (dear)
bhagwad_gita::486.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::486.essence: Devotion becomes steady when liking and disliking no longer rule the heart.
bhagwad_gita::486.simple_meaning: A devoted person stays free from excitement, hatred, sorrow, and craving. They do not cling to outcomes or label actions as personally theirs.
bhagwad_gita::486.simple_insight: There is relief in not having to chase or resist every feeling.
bhagwad_gita::486.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still speaking on the battlefield to Arjuna, who is frozen by grief and conflict. After describing the qualities of a beloved devotee, he adds another: the person who no longer swings between liking and disliking, and who has dropped attachment to both good and bad action.
bhagwad_gita::486.modern_relevance: You read a message that praises your work and another that criticizes it. If your mood rises and crashes with each one, you are still captive. This verse points to steadiness that does not depend on applause.
bhagwad_gita::486.insight: It teaches you to stop feeding emotional reactions with attachment and aversion.

bhagwad_gita::487.verse_sanskrit: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः ॥
bhagwad_gita::487.verse_hindi: जो शत्रु और मित्रमें तथा मानअपमानमें सम है और शीतउष्ण अनुकूलताप्रतिकूलता तथा सुखदुःखमें सम है एवं आसक्तिसे रहित है, और जो निन्दास्तुतिको समान समझनेवाला, मननशील, जिसकिसी प्रकारसे भी शरीरका निर्वाह होनेमें संतुष्ट, रहनेके स्थान तथा शरीरमें ममताआसक्तिसे रहित और स्थिर बुद्धिवाला है, वह भक्तिमान् मनुष्य मुझे प्रिय है ॥
bhagwad_gita::487.english_translation: One who is equal to enemy and friend, honor and dishonor, heat and cold, pleasure and pain, and is free from attachment is dear to Me.
bhagwad_gita::487.translation_literal: समः (equal) / शत्रौ (to enemy) / च (and) / मित्रे (to friend) / च (and) / तथा (likewise) / मानापमानयोः (in honor and dishonor) / शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु (in cold and heat, pleasure and pain) / समः (equal) / सङ्गविवर्जितः (free from attachment)
bhagwad_gita::487.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::487.essence: Real devotion stays even when life feels hostile or kind.
