bhagwad_gita::487.simple_meaning: A devoted person stays steady through praise and blame, comfort and discomfort, friendship and hostility, without clinging to either side.
bhagwad_gita::487.simple_insight: You can stay open and calm without needing life to treat you kindly.
bhagwad_gita::487.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still describing the devotee Arjuna should become. After listing inner qualities in the battlefield crisis, he adds one more test: the beloved devotee does not wobble under praise, insult, comfort, or pain.
bhagwad_gita::487.modern_relevance: A message lands as criticism, then another person praises you five minutes later. Your mood swings with both. This verse trains you to stay unchanged when attention turns warm or cold.
bhagwad_gita::487.insight: It shifts attention from emotional reactions to steady presence under changing treatment.

bhagwad_gita::488.verse_sanskrit: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित् । अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्ितमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥
bhagwad_gita::488.verse_hindi: जो शत्रु और मित्रमें तथा मानअपमानमें सम है और शीतउष्ण अनुकूलताप्रतिकूलता तथा सुखदुःखमें सम है एवं आसक्तिसे रहित है, और जो निन्दास्तुतिको समान समझनेवाला, मननशील, जिसकिसी प्रकारसे भी शरीरका निर्वाह होनेमें संतुष्ट, रहनेके स्थान तथा शरीरमें ममताआसक्तिसे रहित और स्थिर बुद्धिवाला है, वह भक्तिमान् मनुष्य मुझे प्रिय है ॥
bhagwad_gita::488.english_translation: Equal in praise and blame, silent, content with whatever comes, homeless, steady-minded—the devoted person is dear to me.
bhagwad_gita::488.translation_literal: तुल्य (equal) / निन्दा (blame) / स्तुति (praise) / मौनी (silent) / सन्तुष्टः (content) / येनकेनचित् (by whatever means) / अनिकेतः (without a home) / स्थिरमतिः (steady-minded) / भक्तिमान् (devoted) / मे (to me) / प्रियः (dear) / नरः (person)
bhagwad_gita::488.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::488.essence: Praise and blame lose power over the one who stands steady.
bhagwad_gita::488.simple_meaning: A devoted person stays steady through praise and blame, remains quiet, accepts whatever comes, feels no possessiveness about home, and keeps a firm mind.
bhagwad_gita::488.simple_insight: Real devotion looks calm, unshaken, and unneedy.
bhagwad_gita::488.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still trapped in fear and grief. Krishna describes the devotee who has become inwardly steady: unmoved by praise or blame, free from clinging, and content with whatever life provides.
bhagwad_gita::488.modern_relevance: You post something vulnerable, then watch the comments. Praise inflates, criticism stings, and your day tilts. This verse asks for a steadier center than public reaction.
bhagwad_gita::488.insight: It shifts attention from managing approval to holding inner steadiness in every response.

bhagwad_gita::489.verse_sanskrit: ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते । श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::489.verse_hindi: जो मेरेमें श्रद्धा रखनेवाले और मेरे परायण हुए भक्त पहले कहे हुए इस धर्ममय अमृतका अच्छी तरहसे सेवन करते हैं, वे मुझे अत्यन्त प्रिय हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::489.english_translation: Those devotees who trust, take refuge in Me, and faithfully live this nectar-like teaching are exceedingly dear to Me.
bhagwad_gita::489.translation_literal: ये (those who) / तु (indeed) / धर्म्यामृतम् (nectar of righteous living) / इदम् (this) / यथा उक्तम् (as spoken) / पर्युपासते (diligently practice) / श्रद्दधानाः (with trust) / मत्परमाः (having Me as the highest) / भक्ताः (devotees) / ते (they) / अतीव (very) / मे (to Me) / प्रियाः (dear)
bhagwad_gita::489.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::489.essence: Faithful practice turns devotion into closeness.
bhagwad_gita::489.simple_meaning: People who trust Krishna, hold him as their highest aim, and faithfully practice this teaching are very dear to him.
bhagwad_gita::489.simple_insight: Devotion is not just feeling close; it is living the teaching with trust and steady love.
bhagwad_gita::489.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, after Krishna has described the qualities of a beloved devotee, he closes the chapter with a direct promise: the person who trusts him, makes him the highest aim, and practices this teaching becomes especially dear to him.
bhagwad_gita::489.modern_relevance: You keep returning to the same hard promise you made to yourself, even when no one applauds. That quiet loyalty changes your relationship to the thing you serve.
bhagwad_gita::489.insight: It shifts devotion from emotion alone to faithful, repeated practice grounded in trust.

bhagwad_gita::490.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचप्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च । एतद्वेदितुमिच्छामि ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं च केशव ॥
bhagwad_gita::490.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोलेहे कुन्तीपुत्र अर्जुन  यहरूपसे कहे जानेवाले शरीरको क्षेत्र कहते हैं और इस क्षेत्रको जो जानता है, उसको ज्ञानीलोग क्षेत्रज्ञ नामसे कहते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::490.english_translation: Arjuna said: O Keshava, I wish to understand nature, the field, the knower of the field, wisdom, and what is to be known.
bhagwad_gita::490.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / प्रकृतिं (nature) / पुरुषं (the person) / च एव (and also) / क्षेत्रं (the field) / क्षेत्रज्ञम् (the knower of the field) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / एतत् (this) / वेदितुम् (to know) / इच्छामि (I wish) / ज्ञानम् (wisdom) / ज्ञेयम् (what is to be known) / च (and) / केशव (O Keshava)
bhagwad_gita::490.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::490.essence: Real knowing starts by separating the seen from the seer.
bhagwad_gita::490.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain nature, the body as the field, the knower of that field, wisdom, and the object of knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::490.simple_insight: Real understanding begins by separating what is seen from the one who sees it.
bhagwad_gita::490.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna pauses before the larger teaching begins. He asks Krishna to explain the field, the knower of the field, wisdom, and what should be known. This question opens the chapter on how to distinguish body, mind, and awareness.
bhagwad_gita::490.modern_relevance: You sit in a parked car after a hard conversation, replaying every word. Something in you asks: what part of this was the event, and what part was your reaction?
bhagwad_gita::490.insight: It shifts attention from confusion to discrimination: what is observed, what observes, and what can be truly known.

bhagwad_gita::491.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचइदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते । एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः ॥
bhagwad_gita::491.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे कुन्तीपुत्र अर्जुन  यह  रूपसे कहे जानेवाले शरीरको क्षेत्र कहते हैं और इस क्षेत्रको जो जानता है, उसको ज्ञानीलोग क्षेत्रज्ञ नामसे कहते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::491.english_translation: The body is called the field, O Arjuna. Those who know it call the knower of the field the field-knower.
bhagwad_gita::491.translation_literal: इदम् (this) / शरीरम् (body) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / क्षेत्रम् (field) / इति (thus) / अभिधीयते (is called) / एतत् (this) / यः (who) / वेत्ति (knows) / तम् (that one) / प्राहुः (they call) / क्षेत्रज्ञः (field-knower) / इति (thus) / तद्विदः (those who know this)
bhagwad_gita::491.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::491.essence: The body is observed; the knower is something else.
bhagwad_gita::491.simple_meaning: The body is the field where life unfolds. The one who knows the body is called the knower of the field.
bhagwad_gita::491.simple_insight: You are not just the body you inhabit; there is also the awareness that knows it.
bhagwad_gita::491.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna still frozen, Krishna begins a precise teaching about what a human being really is. He names the body as the field of experience and points to the knower of that field, setting up the deeper distinction that follows.
bhagwad_gita::491.modern_relevance: You catch yourself saying, “my body is tense,” or “my mind is spiraling.” That small sentence already shows two things: what is being observed, and the awareness observing it.
bhagwad_gita::491.insight: It shifts identity from the changing body to the awareness that can notice it.

bhagwad_gita::492.verse_sanskrit: क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत । क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम ॥
bhagwad_gita::492.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन  तू सम्पूर्ण क्षेत्रोंमें क्षेत्रज्ञ मेरेको ही समझ और क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञका जो ज्ञान है, वही मेरे मतमें ज्ञान है ॥
bhagwad_gita::492.english_translation: Know Me as the knower in all fields, Arjuna. In my view, true knowledge is knowing the field and the knower of the field.
bhagwad_gita::492.translation_literal: क्षेत्रज्ञम् (knower of the field) / च (and) / अपि (also) / माम् (Me) / विद्धि (know) / सर्वक्षेत्रेषु (in all fields) / भारत (Arjuna) / क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोः (of field and knower of the field) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / यत् (which) / तत् (that) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / मतम् (considered) / मम (My)
bhagwad_gita::492.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::492.essence: Knowing the field is incomplete without knowing the knower.
bhagwad_gita::492.simple_meaning: Know Krishna as the knower present in every field. Real knowledge is understanding both the field and the one who knows it.
bhagwad_gita::492.simple_insight: You are not trapped inside the changing field; awareness itself is the deeper reality.
bhagwad_gita::492.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is asking what is real beneath body, mind, and change. Krishna answers that the body is the field, and the knower within every field is also his own presence. That distinction becomes the heart of this teaching.
bhagwad_gita::492.modern_relevance: You stare at your reflection after a brutal argument and think, 'I am this mess.' The verse interrupts that collapse: what changes is the field; awareness is deeper than the damage.
bhagwad_gita::492.insight: It shifts attention from identifying with changing conditions to recognizing the witnessing presence behind them.

bhagwad_gita::493.verse_sanskrit: तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक् च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत् । स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे श्रृणु ॥
bhagwad_gita::493.verse_hindi: वह क्षेत्र जो है, जैसा है, जिन विकारोंवाला है और जिससे जो पैदा हुआ है तथा वह क्षेत्रज्ञ भी जो है और जिस प्रभाववाला है, वह सब संक्षेपमें मेरेसे सुन ॥
bhagwad_gita::493.english_translation: Listen to the field, its nature, its changes, its source, and the knower of the field, along with that knower's powers, in brief.
bhagwad_gita::493.translation_literal: तत् (that) / क्षेत्रम् (the field) / यत् (which) / च (and) / यादृक् (what sort) / च (and) / यत्-विकारि (having what changes) / यतः (from where) / च (and) / यत् (what) / सः (that) / च (and) / यः (who) / यत्-प्रभावः (having what power) / च (and) / तत् (that) / समासेन (in brief) / मे (from me) / श्रृणु (hear)
bhagwad_gita::493.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::493.essence: Clear seeing begins by separating the field from the one who knows it.
bhagwad_gita::493.simple_meaning: Krishna is about to explain, in brief, what the field is like, how it changes, where it comes from, and what the knower of the field is like.
bhagwad_gita::493.simple_insight: You do not have to guess at reality; you can learn to examine it closely.
bhagwad_gita::493.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen and Krishna begins teaching the difference between the body-field and the knower within it. After naming that distinction, Krishna now promises a compact explanation of the field’s nature, changes, source, and the knower’s power.
bhagwad_gita::493.modern_relevance: You are staring at a decision that keeps changing shape: the facts, your mood, and your motives all blur together. This verse says to slow down and examine each layer clearly before you act.
bhagwad_gita::493.insight: It shifts the mind from vague reaction to careful discrimination between what is changing and what is aware of it.

bhagwad_gita::494.verse_sanskrit: ऋषिभिर्बहुधा गीतं छन्दोभिर्विविधैः पृथक् । ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैश्चैव हेतुमद्भिर्विनिश्िचतैः ॥
bhagwad_gita::494.verse_hindi: यह क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञका तत्त्व ऋषियोंके द्वारा बहुत विस्तारसे कहा गया है तथा वेदोंकी ऋचाओंद्वारा बहुत प्रकारसे कहा गया है और युक्तियुक्त एवं निश्चित किये हुए ब्रह्मसूत्रके पदोंद्वारा भी कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::494.english_translation: This truth about the field and the knower has been sung in many ways by sages, in varied Vedic hymns, and in the reasoned, conclusive verses of the Brahma Sutras.
bhagwad_gita::494.translation_literal: ऋषिभिः (by sages) / बहुधा (in many ways) / गीतम् (sung) / छन्दोभिः (by hymns or meters) / विविधैः (in varied forms) / पृथक् (separately) / ब्रह्मसूत्रपदैः (by Brahma Sutra verses) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / हेतुमद्भिः (by reasoned, cause-based) / विनिश्चितैः (by conclusive, well-determined [statements])
bhagwad_gita::494.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::494.essence: Ancient sources converge on one disciplined way of seeing.
bhagwad_gita::494.simple_meaning: Sages, Vedic hymns, and the Brahma Sutras all point to the same understanding of the field and the knower.
bhagwad_gita::494.simple_insight: You are not being asked to believe blindly; the teaching is grounded in many clear sources.
bhagwad_gita::494.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna is unpacking the difference between the field and the knower for Arjuna. Before listing the parts of the field, he says this understanding has already been taught by sages, hymns, and the Brahma Sutras.
bhagwad_gita::494.modern_relevance: You hear the same hard truth from a mentor, a book, and your own quiet reflection. The repetition matters: some realities deserve to be confirmed from every angle before you act.
bhagwad_gita::494.insight: It shifts the mind from treating wisdom as opinion to seeing it as a tested, cross-verified understanding.

bhagwad_gita::495.verse_sanskrit: महाभूतान्यहङ्कारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च । इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः ॥
bhagwad_gita::495.verse_hindi: मूल प्रकृति, समष्टि बुद्धि महत्तत्त्व, समष्टि अहंकार, पाँच महाभूत और दस इन्द्रियाँ, एक मन तथा पाँचों इन्द्रियोंके पाँच विषय   यह चौबीस तत्त्वोंवाला क्षेत्र है ॥
bhagwad_gita::495.english_translation: The five great elements, ego, intellect, the unmanifest, the ten senses, the one mind, and the five sense-objects: this is the field in brief.
bhagwad_gita::495.translation_literal: महाभूतानि (the five great elements) / अहङ्कारः (ego) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / अव्यक्तम् (the unmanifest) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / इन्द्रियाणि (the senses) / दश (ten) / एकम् (one) / च (and) / पञ्च (five) / च (and) / इन्द्रियगोचराः (sense-objects)
bhagwad_gita::495.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::495.essence: What you call “me” is a changing system, not a single thing.
bhagwad_gita::495.simple_meaning: The body-mind world is made of many parts: elements, ego, intellect, senses, mind, and sense-objects. Krishna is naming the field so Arjuna can see it clearly.
bhagwad_gita::495.simple_insight: You stop mistaking your changing equipment for who you are.
bhagwad_gita::495.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna begins mapping reality with precision. After introducing the field and the knower of the field, he lists the twenty-four components that make up the field itself, so Arjuna can separate what changes from what knows.
bhagwad_gita::495.modern_relevance: You sit in a therapist’s office after saying, “I don’t know what’s wrong with me.” The first relief is naming the parts: body, thoughts, impulses, roles, reactions. Clarity starts there.
bhagwad_gita::495.insight: It trains the mind to dissect experience into components instead of collapsing everything into a single identity.

bhagwad_gita::496.verse_sanskrit: इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं सङ्घातश्चेतनाधृतिः । एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::496.verse_hindi: इच्छा, द्वेष, सुख, दुःख, संघात, चेतना प्राणशक्ति और धृति  इन विकारोंसहित यह क्षेत्र संक्षेपसे कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::496.english_translation: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the body, consciousness, and steadiness: this field, together with its changes, is briefly described.
bhagwad_gita::496.translation_literal: इच्छा (desire) / द्वेषः (aversion) / सुखं (pleasure) / दुःखं (pain) / सङ्घातः (the body as a composite) / चेतना (consciousness) / धृतिः (steadiness) / एतत् (this) / क्षेत्रम् (field) / समासेन (briefly) / सविकारम् (with changes) / उदाहृतम् (is described)
bhagwad_gita::496.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::496.essence: Your reactions belong to the field, not to the knower.
bhagwad_gita::496.simple_meaning: The field includes the body, feelings, impulses, and the mind's steadiness. All of these are part of what changes, not the knower behind them.
bhagwad_gita::496.simple_insight: You can stop confusing your moods and reactions with who you are.
bhagwad_gita::496.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna begins separating what changes from what truly knows. After naming the field's basic parts, Krishna now includes desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, and steadiness as part of the same changing nature.
bhagwad_gita::496.modern_relevance: You feel a surge of attraction, then irritation, then numbness, and call it your identity. This verse asks you to see those shifts as passing states, not your core.
bhagwad_gita::496.insight: It shifts attention from identifying with reactions to observing them as changing contents of the field.

bhagwad_gita::497.verse_hindi: मानित्वअपनेमें श्रेष्ठताके भाव का न होना, दम्भित्वदिखावटीपन का न होना, अहिंसा, क्षमा, सरलता, गुरुकी सेवा, बाहरभीतरकी शुद्धि, स्थिरता और मनका वशमें होना ॥
bhagwad_gita::497.english_translation: Absence of pride, absence of pretence, nonviolence, forgiveness, simplicity, service to the teacher, purity, steadiness, and self-control.
bhagwad_gita::497.translation_literal: अमानित्वम् (absence of pride) / अदम्भित्वम् (absence of pretence) / अहिंसा (nonviolence) / क्षान्तिः (forgiveness) / आर्जवम् (simplicity) / आचार्य-उपासनम् (service to the teacher) / शौचम् (purity) / स्थैर्यम् (steadiness) / आत्म-विनिग्रहः (self-control)
bhagwad_gita::497.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::497.essence: True strength is quiet discipline, not self-display.
bhagwad_gita::497.simple_meaning: A disciplined life is marked by humility, honesty, nonviolence, forgiveness, simplicity, respect for the teacher, cleanliness, steadiness, and self-mastery.
bhagwad_gita::497.simple_insight: Real strength looks calm, clean, and unforced.
bhagwad_gita::497.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna begins listing the qualities that shape a person fit for clear seeing. After defining the field of body and mind, he names the inner discipline that makes wisdom possible.
bhagwad_gita::497.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that could end a friendship, and your chest tightens. This verse asks whether you can stay honest, clean in motive, and steady instead of performing or striking out.
bhagwad_gita::497.insight: It shifts attention from image-building to character-building, showing that inner discipline prepares the mind for truth.

bhagwad_gita::498.verse_hindi: इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंमें वैराग्यका होना, अहंकारका भी न होना और जन्म, मृत्यु, वृद्धावस्था तथा व्याधियोंमें दुःखरूप दोषोंको बारबार देखना ॥
bhagwad_gita::498.english_translation: Dispassion toward sense objects, absence of ego, and constant seeing of the fault in birth, death, old age, and disease.
bhagwad_gita::498.translation_literal: इन्द्रियार्थेषु (in sense objects) / वैराग्यम् (dispassion) / अहङ्कारः (ego) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / जन्म (birth) / मृत्यु (death) / जरा (old age) / व्याधि (disease) / दुःख (suffering) / दोषानुदर्शनम् (seeing the fault repeatedly)
bhagwad_gita::498.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::498.essence: Freedom begins when desire stops dressing suffering as reward.
bhagwad_gita::498.simple_meaning: Let go of craving for sensory pleasures, drop ego, and keep seeing how birth, death, old age, and illness bring suffering.
bhagwad_gita::498.simple_insight: Clinging loosens when you stop romanticizing what inevitably breaks.
bhagwad_gita::498.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna continues listing the qualities that reveal true understanding. Here, he points to dispassion, humility, and clear sight of life's unavoidable suffering.
bhagwad_gita::498.modern_relevance: You scroll past another perfect-looking life, then feel the pull to compare. This verse asks you to see through the shine: pleasure fades, bodies change, and ego makes everything heavier.
bhagwad_gita::498.insight: It trains you to weaken attachment by repeatedly noticing impermanence and the cost of clinging.

bhagwad_gita::499.verse_hindi: आसक्तिरहित होना पुत्र, स्त्री, घर आदिमें एकात्मता घनिष्ठ सम्बन्ध न होना और अनुकूलताप्रतिकूलताकी प्राप्तिमें चित्तका नित्य सम रहना ॥
bhagwad_gita::499.english_translation: Freedom from attachment to sons, wife, home, and the like; and constant evenness of mind in desired and undesired events.
bhagwad_gita::499.translation_literal: असक्ति (non-attachment) / अनभिष्वङ्गः (no clinging) / पुत्रदारगृहादिषु (in sons, wife, home, and such) / नित्यं (always) / च (and) / समचित्तत्वम् (evenness of mind) / इष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु (in the arrival of the desired and undesired)
bhagwad_gita::499.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::499.essence: Clinging fades; the mind stays level.
bhagwad_gita::499.simple_meaning: Do not cling to family and possessions, and keep your mind steady whether things go your way or not.
bhagwad_gita::499.simple_insight: You can love without gripping. Stability grows when approval and loss stop steering your mood.
bhagwad_gita::499.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen by grief and moral conflict. Krishna continues listing the qualities of clear seeing: not clinging to family and home, and remaining even-minded whether life brings what is wanted or not.
bhagwad_gita::499.modern_relevance: You refresh your phone after a hard conversation, hoping for reassurance, then spiral when it does not come. This verse asks for a steadier center than approval, loss, or family pressure.
bhagwad_gita::499.insight: It trains you to loosen possessiveness and keep the mind balanced through gain and setback.

bhagwad_gita::500.verse_hindi: मेरेमें अनन्ययोगके द्वारा अव्यभिचारिणी भक्तिका होना, एकान्त स्थानमें रहनेका स्वभाव होना और जनसमुदायमें प्रीतिका न होना ॥
bhagwad_gita::500.english_translation: Undivided devotion to me, a love that does not waver, delight in solitude, and no attraction to crowds.
bhagwad_gita::500.translation_literal: मयि (in me) / च (and) / अनन्ययोगेन (with undivided devotion) / भक्ितः (devotion) / अव्यभिचारिणी (unwavering) / विविक्तदेशसेवित्वम् (fondness for secluded places) / अरतिः (lack of delight) / जनसंसदि (in crowds)
bhagwad_gita::500.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::500.essence: True devotion stays with one center and loses interest in the crowd.
bhagwad_gita::500.simple_meaning: Steady devotion to Krishna, a love that does not drift, grows with a taste for solitude and little interest in crowds.
bhagwad_gita::500.simple_insight: Real devotion simplifies life. It pulls attention inward and away from noise that scatters the heart.
bhagwad_gita::500.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is being taught how to see the field and the knower of the field clearly. After describing detachment from distractions, Krishna adds the devotional posture that supports true knowledge: unwavering love, quiet spaces, and less pull toward crowds.
bhagwad_gita::500.modern_relevance: You leave a loud gathering and feel your mind settle only after the car ride home. Some parts of you come alive in silence, not in constant company.
bhagwad_gita::500.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to inward steadiness, where attention stops scattering into social noise.

bhagwad_gita::501.verse_hindi: अध्यात्मज्ञानमें नित्यनिरन्तर रहना, तत्त्वज्ञानके अर्थरूप परमात्माको सब जगह देखना  यह पूर्वोक्त साधनसमुदाय तो ज्ञान है और जो इसके विपरीत है वह अज्ञान है  ऐसा कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::501.english_translation: Constant awareness of the inner reality, and seeing the supreme reality as the meaning of true understanding—this is called knowledge; whatever is contrary to this is ignorance.
bhagwad_gita::501.translation_literal: अध्यात्म-ज्ञान (knowledge of the inner reality) / नित्यत्वम् (constantness) / तत्त्व-ज्ञान-अर्थ-दर्शनम् (seeing the meaning of knowledge of reality) / एतत् (this) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / इति (thus) / प्रोक्तम् (is called) / अज्ञानम् (ignorance) / यत् (which) / अतः अन्यथा (other than this)
bhagwad_gita::501.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::501.essence: Knowledge is seeing reality steadily; everything else is confusion.
bhagwad_gita::501.simple_meaning: Real knowledge means staying aware of the inner reality and seeing the supreme reality everywhere. Anything that misses this is ignorance.
bhagwad_gita::501.simple_insight: Clear seeing feels simpler than grasping at appearances.
bhagwad_gita::501.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna is defining what real understanding looks like. After listing the qualities of a mature seeker, he says knowledge is steady awareness of the inner reality and seeing the supreme reality everywhere; anything else is ignorance.
bhagwad_gita::501.modern_relevance: You keep chasing labels, opinions, and surface facts in a tense conversation, but the deeper issue is what is actually real. This verse pulls attention back to that.
bhagwad_gita::501.insight: It shifts the mind from collecting information to seeing what truly matters beneath appearances.

bhagwad_gita::502.verse_sanskrit: ज्ञेयं यत्तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वाऽमृतमश्नुते । अनादिमत्परं ब्रह्म न सत्तन्नासदुच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::502.verse_hindi: जो ज्ञेय है, उसपरमात्मतत्त्व को मैं अच्छी तरहसे कहूँगा, जिसको जानकर मनुष्य अमरताका अनुभव कर लेता है ।  वह ज्ञेयतत्त्व अनादि और परम ब्रह्म है ।  उसको न सत् कहा जा सकता है और न असत् ही कहा जा सकता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::502.english_translation: I will now tell you what is to be known. Knowing it, one attains freedom. It is beginningless supreme reality, beyond existence and nonexistence.
bhagwad_gita::502.translation_literal: ज्ञेयम् (what is to be known) / यत् (which) / तत् (that) / प्रवक्ष्यामि (I will clearly tell) / यत् (which) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / अमृतम् (freedom / immortality) / अश्नुते (attains) / अनादिमत् (beginningless) / परम् (supreme) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / न (not) / सत् (existent) / तत् (that) / न (not) / असत् (nonexistent) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::502.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::502.essence: The highest reality frees you precisely because it outgrows every label.
bhagwad_gita::502.simple_meaning: Krishna says he will explain the highest reality that can be known. Knowing it brings freedom. It is beginningless, supreme, and beyond ordinary ideas of real and unreal.
bhagwad_gita::502.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing the deepest truth cannot be boxed into simple labels.
bhagwad_gita::502.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen and Krishna begins the teaching on field and knower. After describing the qualities that prepare a seeker, Krishna now points to the highest object of knowledge itself: the beginningless supreme reality that ends confusion.
bhagwad_gita::502.modern_relevance: You are trying to name something that changes your whole life — but every label feels too small. Some truths are not objects you can pin down; they must be known directly.
bhagwad_gita::502.insight: It shifts the mind from arguing about appearances to seeking direct understanding of what underlies them.

bhagwad_gita::503.verse_sanskrit: सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् । सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥
bhagwad_gita::503.verse_hindi: वे परमात्मा सब जगह हाथों और पैरोंवाले, सब जगह नेत्रों, सिरों और मुखोंवाले तथा सब जगह कानोंवाले हैं ।  वे संसारमें सबको व्याप्त करके स्थित हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::503.english_translation: The supreme reality has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere, and ears everywhere. It pervades all things and stands within all things.
bhagwad_gita::503.translation_literal: सर्वतः (everywhere) / पाणिपादम् (hands and feet) / तत् (that) / सर्वतः (everywhere) / अक्षिशिरोमुखम् (eyes, heads, and faces) / सर्वतः (everywhere) / श्रुतिमत् (having ears) / लोके (in the world) / सर्वम् (all) / आवृत्य (covering) / तिष्ठति (stands, remains)
bhagwad_gita::503.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::503.essence: What seems separate is already filled with the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::503.simple_meaning: The supreme reality is not limited to one form or place. It is present everywhere, expressed through all beings and all senses.
bhagwad_gita::503.simple_insight: You can stop feeling cut off from the sacred. Presence is already here, all around and within.
bhagwad_gita::503.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is being taught what the knower of the field is. Krishna now describes the supreme reality as present everywhere, with no outside at all. This verse deepens the vision before the next line explains that it is beyond ordinary senses.
bhagwad_gita::503.modern_relevance: You sit alone in a crowded train after a hard conversation, feeling separate from everyone around you. This verse says the deeper reality has never left the room.
bhagwad_gita::503.insight: It shifts attention from a distant divine object to a presence that already pervades experience.

bhagwad_gita::504.verse_sanskrit: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् । असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च ॥
bhagwad_gita::504.verse_hindi: वे परमात्मा सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियोंसे रहित हैं और सम्पूर्ण इन्द्रियोंके विषयोंको प्रकाशित करनेवाले हैं आसक्तिरहित हैं और सम्पूर्ण संसारका भरणपोषण करनेवाले हैं तथा गुणोंसे रहित हैं और सम्पूर्ण गुणोंके भोक्ता हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::504.english_translation: The supreme reality has no senses, yet illumines every sense-object. It is detached, supports all beings, beyond the three qualities, and yet experiences the qualities.
bhagwad_gita::504.translation_literal: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासम् (shining through the qualities of all senses) / सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् (devoid of all senses) / असक्तम् (unattached) / सर्वभृत् (supporter of all) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / निर्गुणम् (without qualities) / गुणभोक्तृ (enjoyer of qualities) / च (and)
bhagwad_gita::504.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::504.essence: What sustains everything is beyond the senses that perceive it.
bhagwad_gita::504.simple_meaning: The supreme being has no senses, yet makes all perception possible. It is free from attachment, sustains everything, stands beyond the three qualities, and still experiences them all.
bhagwad_gita::504.simple_insight: You are held by what is beyond grasping. That can bring quiet trust.
bhagwad_gita::504.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still stunned by Krishna's teaching about the field and the knower of the field. Krishna now describes the supreme reality in paradox: beyond bodily senses, yet the source of all experience; beyond qualities, yet present to all qualities.
bhagwad_gita::504.modern_relevance: You sit in a hospital corridor, unable to fix the outcome. Something larger than your control is still holding the whole scene together.
bhagwad_gita::504.insight: It shifts attention from visible form to the unseen presence that makes all form possible.

bhagwad_gita::505.verse_sanskrit: बहिरन्तश्च भूतानामचरं चरमेव च । सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थं चान्तिके च तत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::505.verse_hindi: वे परमात्मा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके बाहरभीतर परिपूर्ण हैं और चरअचर प्राणियोंके रूपमें भी वे ही हैं एवं दूरसेदूर तथा नजदीकसेनजदीक भी वे ही हैं ।  वे अत्यन्त सूक्ष्म होनेसे जाननेका विषय नहीं हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::505.english_translation: The supreme reality is inside and outside all beings, moving and unmoving. Because it is subtle, it cannot be known; it is far away and near at hand.
bhagwad_gita::505.translation_literal: बहिः (outside) / अन्तः (inside) / च (and) / भूतानाम् (of beings) / अचरम् (unmoving) / चरम् (moving) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / सूक्ष्मत्वात् (because of subtlety) / तत् (that) / अविज्ञेयम् (not knowable) / दूरस्थम् (far away) / च (and) / अन्तिके (near) / च (and) / तत् (that)
bhagwad_gita::505.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::505.essence: What seems distant is already within everything.
bhagwad_gita::505.simple_meaning: The supreme reality fills everything, inside and outside all beings. It is both moving and still, yet too subtle to grasp directly. It feels far away and also very near.
bhagwad_gita::505.simple_insight: Closeness and distance are both misleading when reality is subtler than the senses.
bhagwad_gita::505.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, while Arjuna stands frozen between two armies, Krishna keeps unfolding the nature of what truly pervades existence. After describing it as beyond senses, he now says it is inside and outside all beings, moving and unmoving, near and far.
bhagwad_gita::505.modern_relevance: You can sit in a crowded train and still feel utterly cut off, or sit alone and feel deeply held. This verse points to a presence that is closer than your own searching.
bhagwad_gita::505.insight: It shifts attention from physical distance to direct recognition of what is already present.

bhagwad_gita::506.verse_sanskrit: अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् । भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च ॥
bhagwad_gita::506.verse_hindi: वे परमात्मा स्वयं विभागरहित होते हुए भी सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें विभक्तकी तरह स्थित हैं ।  वे जाननेयोग्य परमात्मा ही सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंको उत्पन्न करनेवाले, उनका भरणपोषण करनेवाले और संहार करनेवाले हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::506.english_translation: Undivided among beings, it appears divided. Know it as the one who bears, devours, and creates all beings.
bhagwad_gita::506.translation_literal: अविभक्तम् (undivided) / च (and) / भूतेषु (among beings) / विभक्तम् (divided) / इव (as if) / च (and) / स्थितम् (situated) / भूतभर्तृ (bearer of beings) / च (and) / तत् (that) / ज्ञेयम् (to be known) / ग्रसिष्णु (devouring) / प्रभविष्णु (originating) / च (and)
bhagwad_gita::506.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::506.essence: Separation is only appearance; the many are held by one.
bhagwad_gita::506.simple_meaning: The supreme reality seems split into many beings, but it is actually one. It is the source, support, and end of all life.
bhagwad_gita::506.simple_insight: The feeling of separation softens. What seemed isolated is held inside one larger reality.
bhagwad_gita::506.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna explains that the divine is not fragmented by the many lives it animates. What seems separate is one reality appearing in many forms, and that reality sustains, consumes, and creates all beings.
bhagwad_gita::506.modern_relevance: You look across a family table after an ugly argument and see only sides. This verse says the deeper truth is still one shared field, even when everyone appears divided.
bhagwad_gita::506.insight: It shifts perception from isolated parts to one reality expressing itself through many forms.

bhagwad_gita::507.verse_sanskrit: ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते । ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::507.verse_hindi: वह परमात्मा सम्पूर्ण ज्योतियोंका भी ज्योति और अज्ञानसे अत्यन्त परे कहा गया है ।  वह ज्ञानस्वरूप, जाननेयोग्य, ज्ञानसाधनसमुदाय से प्राप्त करनेयोग्य और सबके हृदयमें विराजमान है ॥
bhagwad_gita::507.english_translation: It is the light of all lights, beyond darkness. It is knowledge, the knowable, reached through knowledge, and abiding in every heart.
bhagwad_gita::507.translation_literal: ज्योतिषाम् (of lights) / अपि (even) / तत् (that) / ज्योतिः (light) / तमसः (of darkness) / परम् (beyond) / उच्यते (is said) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / ज्ञेयम् (the knowable) / ज्ञानगम्यम् (reached through knowledge) / हृदि (in the heart) / सर्वस्य (of all) / विष्ठितम् (abiding)
bhagwad_gita::507.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::507.essence: What illumines everything is already nearest to you.
bhagwad_gita::507.simple_meaning: The supreme reality is brighter than all light, beyond ignorance, and present in every heart. It is both what is known and the means of knowing it.
bhagwad_gita::507.simple_insight: You are not searching in the dark for something absent; the deepest clarity is already near.
bhagwad_gita::507.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen and Krishna is revealing the nature of the field, the knower, and the ultimate reality. Here Krishna says that the highest reality is the light of all lights, beyond darkness, and present in every heart.
bhagwad_gita::507.modern_relevance: You sit in a silent room after a painful argument, replaying every word and wondering what is true. The answer is not somewhere far away; clarity is already closer than your panic.
bhagwad_gita::507.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing truth outside to recognising the source of knowing within experience itself.

bhagwad_gita::508.verse_sanskrit: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः । मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::508.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार क्षेत्र, ज्ञान और ज्ञेयको संक्षेपसे कहा गया ।  मेरा भक्त इसको तत्त्वसे जानकर मेरे भावको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::508.english_translation: Thus, field, knowledge, and the knowable have been explained briefly. My devotee, understanding this, attains my state.
bhagwad_gita::508.translation_literal: इति (thus) / क्षेत्रम् (the field) / तथा (and also) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / ज्ञेयम् (the knowable) / च (and) / उक्तम् (has been spoken) / समासतः (briefly) / मद्भक्तः (my devotee) / एतत् (this) / विज्ञाय (having known) / मद्भावाय (to my state) / उपपद्यते (attains)
bhagwad_gita::508.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::508.essence: Clear understanding becomes transformation when devotion receives it.
bhagwad_gita::508.simple_meaning: Krishna summarizes the teaching on the body, knowledge, and the object of knowledge. He says that a devotee who truly understands this reaches his own state.
bhagwad_gita::508.simple_insight: Real understanding is not just mental clarity; it deepens devotion and transforms who you become.
bhagwad_gita::508.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna finishes explaining the field, knowledge, and the knowable. This verse closes the teaching by saying that understanding these truths is not abstract — it leads the devotee into Krishna’s own state.
bhagwad_gita::508.modern_relevance: You finally understand a pattern in your relationships after years of repeating it. The insight matters, but the real shift is that you stop living from confusion and start living from alignment.
bhagwad_gita::508.insight: It turns understanding into a doorway: clear seeing becomes a change in identity and devotion.

bhagwad_gita::509.verse_sanskrit: प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादी उभावपि । विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसंभवान् ॥
bhagwad_gita::509.verse_hindi: प्रकृति और पुरुष  दोनोंको ही तुम अनादि समझो और विकारों तथा गुणोंको भी प्रकृतिसे ही उत्पन्न समझो ।  कार्य और करणके द्वारा होनेवाली क्रियाओंको उत्पन्न करनेमें प्रकृति हेतु कही जाती है और सुखदुःखोंके भोक्तापनमें पुरुष हेतु कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::509.english_translation: Know both Prakriti and Purusha to be beginningless, and know the modifications and qualities to arise from Prakriti.
bhagwad_gita::509.translation_literal: प्रकृतिम् (Prakriti) / पुरुषम् (Purusha) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / विद्धि (know) / अनादी (beginningless) / उभौ (both) / अपि (also) / विकारान् (modifications) / च (and) / गुणान् (qualities) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / विद्धि (know) / प्रकृति-संभवान् (born from Prakriti)
bhagwad_gita::509.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::509.essence: Change belongs to nature; awareness is not caught in it.
bhagwad_gita::509.simple_meaning: Both nature and the conscious knower are without beginning. All changes and qualities come from nature, not from the knower.
bhagwad_gita::509.simple_insight: You stop confusing what changes with what merely sees the change.
bhagwad_gita::509.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna explains the field and its knower. After describing what can be known, Krishna now separates the changeless witness from changing nature, showing where action, qualities, and experience arise.
bhagwad_gita::509.modern_relevance: You feel moods, impulses, and labels shifting all day, then call them “me.” This verse cuts that confusion and points to the deeper awareness beneath the churn.
bhagwad_gita::509.insight: It shifts attention from identifying with changing traits to seeing their source in nature.

bhagwad_gita::510.verse_sanskrit: कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे हेतुः प्रकृतिरुच्यते । पुरुषः सुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::510.verse_hindi: प्रकृति और पुरुष  दोनोंको ही तुम अनादि समझो और विकारों तथा गुणोंको भी प्रकृतिसे ही उत्पन्न समझो ।  कार्य और करणके द्वारा होनेवाली क्रियाओंको उत्पन्न करनेमें प्रकृति हेतु कही जाती है और सुखदुःखोंके भोक्तापनमें पुरुष हेतु कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::510.english_translation: Nature is said to be the cause of the body, the senses, and action. The inner being is said to be the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain.
bhagwad_gita::510.translation_literal: कार्यकारणकर्तृत्वे (in the doership of body, senses, and action) / हेतुः (cause) / प्रकृतिः (nature) / उच्यते (is said) । / पुरुषः (the inner being) / सुखदुःखानाम् (of pleasure and pain) / भोक्तृत्वे (in the state of experiencer) / हेतुः (cause) / उच्यते (is said)
bhagwad_gita::510.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::510.essence: Action belongs to nature; experience belongs to the one who knows.
bhagwad_gita::510.simple_meaning: The body, senses, and actions belong to nature. Pleasure and pain are experienced by the inner being. Krishna separates the changing process from the one who experiences it.
bhagwad_gita::510.simple_insight: You can stop confusing what happens with who you are.
bhagwad_gita::510.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna explains that nature drives bodily action, while the inner being only experiences pleasure and pain. This distinction prepares Arjuna to act without mistaking himself for the moving field.
bhagwad_gita::510.modern_relevance: You watch your body tense before a hard conversation, then feel the sting afterward. This verse reminds you that the surge belongs to nature; the witness is not the storm.
bhagwad_gita::510.insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame to clear witnessing of action and experience.

bhagwad_gita::511.verse_sanskrit: पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान् । कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु ॥
bhagwad_gita::511.verse_hindi: प्रकृतिमें स्थित पुरुष ही प्रकृतिजन्य गुणोंका भोक्ता बनता है और गुणोंका सङ्ग ही उसके ऊँचनीच योनियोंमें जन्म लेनेका कारण बनता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::511.english_translation: The inner being, situated in nature, experiences the qualities born of nature. Attachment to those qualities causes birth in good and bad wombs.
bhagwad_gita::511.translation_literal: पुरुषः (the inner being) / प्रकृतिस्थः (situated in nature) / हि (indeed) / भुङ्क्ते (experiences) / प्रकृतिजान् (born of nature) / गुणान् (qualities) / कारणम् (cause) / गुणसङ्गः (attachment to qualities) / अस्य (of this) / सत्-असत् (good and bad) / योनि-जन्मसु (in womb-births)
bhagwad_gita::511.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::511.essence: Attachment to changing qualities keeps the cycle of birth going.
bhagwad_gita::511.simple_meaning: The inner being, while tied to nature, experiences its changing qualities. Clinging to those qualities is what leads to repeated births in favorable and unfavorable forms.
bhagwad_gita::511.simple_insight: What traps you is not experience itself, but your attachment to its changing moods and pulls.
bhagwad_gita::511.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna is explaining why suffering repeats. The inner being, caught in nature, tastes its changing qualities; that same attachment becomes the cause of future births in better or worse conditions.
bhagwad_gita::511.modern_relevance: You keep replaying the same argument in your head after the call ends. The event is over, but your attachment to its emotional charge keeps pulling you back.
bhagwad_gita::511.insight: It shifts attention from the event to the attachment that keeps the cycle going.

bhagwad_gita::512.verse_sanskrit: उपद्रष्टाऽनुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः । परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः ॥
bhagwad_gita::512.verse_hindi: यह पुरुष प्रकृतिशरीर के साथ सम्बन्ध रखनेसे उपद्रष्टा, उसके साथ मिलकर सम्मति, अनुमति देनेसे अनुमन्ता, अपनेको उसका भरणपोषण करनेवाला माननेसे भर्ता, उसके सङ्गसे सुखदुःख भोगनेसे भोक्ता, और अपनेको उसका स्वामी माननेसे महेश्वर बन जाता है ।  परन्तु स्वरूपसे यह पुरुष परमात्मा कहा जाता है ।  यह देहमें रहता हुआ भी देहसे पर सम्बन्धरहित ही है ॥
bhagwad_gita::512.english_translation: The inner self becomes the witness, consent-giver, supporter, enjoyer, and great lord through its relation with the body. Yet in its true nature, it is called the supreme self and remains beyond the body.
bhagwad_gita::512.translation_literal: उपद्रष्टा (witness) / अनुमन्ता (consenter) / च (and) / भर्ता (supporter) / भोक्ता (enjoyer) / महेश्वरः (great lord) / परमात्मा (supreme self) / इति (thus) / च (and) / अपि (also) / उक्तः (called) / देहे (in the body) / अस्मिन् (this) / पुरुषः (inner self) / परः (beyond)
bhagwad_gita::512.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::512.essence: Identity is borrowed from the body; the true self stands beyond it.
bhagwad_gita::512.simple_meaning: The inner self seems to take on many roles because it is linked with the body, but in its true nature it remains beyond the body.
bhagwad_gita::512.simple_insight: You are not trapped by every role you play. Beneath them, there is something untouched.
bhagwad_gita::512.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen by confusion, and Krishna turns to the deepest distinction in chapter 13. After describing the field and its knower, he explains how the inner self appears to become witness, consent-giver, supporter, enjoyer, and ruler only through body-identification.
bhagwad_gita::512.modern_relevance: You replay one mistake after a hard conversation and start calling yourself the failure, the fixer, the victim, the judge. This verse cuts through that blur: roles arise from identification, not from your deepest nature.
bhagwad_gita::512.insight: It shifts the mind from role-based identity to direct seeing of what remains unchanged beneath experience.

bhagwad_gita::513.verse_sanskrit: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैःसह । सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि न स भूयोऽभिजायते ॥
bhagwad_gita::513.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार पुरुषको और गुणोंके सहित प्रकृतिको जो मनुष्य अलगअलग जानता है, वह सब तरहका बर्ताव करता हुआ भी फिर जन्म नहीं लेता ॥
bhagwad_gita::513.english_translation: Whoever thus knows the purusha and prakriti together with the qualities is not born again, even while living and acting in every way.
bhagwad_gita::513.translation_literal: यः (who) / एवं (thus) / वेत्ति (knows) / पुरुषम् (the purusha) / प्रकृतिम् (prakriti) / च (and) / गुणैः सह (together with the qualities) / सर्वथा (in every way) / वर्तमानः अपि (even while acting) / न (not) / सः (that one) / भूयः (again) / अभिजायते (is born)
bhagwad_gita::513.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::513.essence: Clear seeing frees you while life still continues.
bhagwad_gita::513.simple_meaning: A person who clearly sees the true self, the body-nature, and the qualities that move them is no longer caught in rebirth, even while living normally.
bhagwad_gita::513.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that awareness can be free even while life keeps moving.
bhagwad_gita::513.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains the deepest split in human experience: the knower, the body-nature, and the qualities that shape behavior. This verse says that clear seeing breaks the cycle of repeated birth.
bhagwad_gita::513.modern_relevance: You are in the middle of a painful conversation, but part of you is watching the fear, the anger, and the urge to defend. That inner clarity changes everything about how much the moment owns you.
bhagwad_gita::513.insight: It shifts attention from being trapped inside experience to recognizing the one who can observe it.

bhagwad_gita::514.verse_sanskrit: ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना । अन्ये सांख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे ॥
bhagwad_gita::514.verse_hindi: कई मनुष्य ध्यानयोगके द्वारा, कई सांख्ययोगके द्वारा और कई कर्मयोगके द्वारा अपनेआपसे अपनेआपमें परमात्मतत्त्वका अनुभव करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::514.english_translation: Some realize the true self within through meditation on the self. Others through clear discernment and yoga, and still others through the yoga of action.
bhagwad_gita::514.translation_literal: ध्यानेन (through meditation) / आत्मनि (in the self) / पश्यन्ति (they see) / केचित् (some) / आत्मानम् (the true self) / आत्मना (by the self) / अन्ये (others) / सांख्येन (through discernment) / योगेन (through yoga) / कर्मयोगेन (through the yoga of action) / च (and) / अपरे (others)
bhagwad_gita::514.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::514.essence: The same realization opens through different disciplines.
bhagwad_gita::514.simple_meaning: People realize the true self in different ways: through meditation, through clear discernment, or through the yoga of action.
bhagwad_gita::514.simple_insight: You do not need one perfect doorway. Different temperaments can reach the same realization.
bhagwad_gita::514.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna explains that the true self can be known in more than one way: through meditation, through discernment, or through action done as yoga. The teaching widens the path.
bhagwad_gita::514.modern_relevance: You sit in a quiet room, trying to force clarity before a hard decision, and nothing comes. This verse reminds you that insight may arrive through stillness, analysis, or steady action.
bhagwad_gita::514.insight: It shifts the mind from one-size-fits-all spirituality to a recognition that different practices can lead to the same realization.

bhagwad_gita::515.verse_sanskrit: अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तः श्रुत्वाऽन्येभ्य उपासते । तेऽपि चातितरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::515.verse_hindi: दूसरे मनुष्य इस प्रकार ध्यानयोग, सांख्ययोग, कर्मयोग, आदि साधनोंको नहीं जानते, केवल जीवन्मुक्त महापुरुषोंसे सुनकर उपासना करते हैं, ऐसे वे सुननेके परायण मनुष्य भी मृत्युको तर जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::515.english_translation: Others do not know these paths, but they worship by hearing from others. Even they cross beyond death if they listen with devotion.
bhagwad_gita::515.translation_literal: अन्ये (others) / तु (but) / एवम् (thus) / अजानन्तः (not knowing) / श्रुत्वा (having heard) / अन्येभ्यः (from others) / उपासते (they worship) / ते (they) / अपि (also) / च (and) / अति-तरन्ति (cross beyond) / एव (indeed) / मृत्युम् (death) / श्रुति-परायणाः (devoted to hearing)
bhagwad_gita::515.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::515.essence: Devoted listening can carry a person beyond fear and mortality.
bhagwad_gita::515.simple_meaning: Some people do not understand these practices directly, but they listen to wise teachers and worship with trust. Even they can go beyond death through devoted listening.
bhagwad_gita::515.simple_insight: You do not need perfect understanding before you begin. Honest listening itself can transform you.
bhagwad_gita::515.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has already heard that the field and the knower of the field can be known in different ways. Krishna adds that even people who cannot follow the full teaching can still move toward freedom by listening to realised teachers with devotion.
bhagwad_gita::515.modern_relevance: You sit in a hospital corridor, not knowing what to do next, while one steady voice explains the next step. In that moment, trust in the right guidance matters more than having every answer.
bhagwad_gita::515.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliant certainty to receptive trust in living guidance.

bhagwad_gita::516.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  स्थावर और जंगम जितने भी प्राणी पैदा होते हैं, उनको तुम क्षेत्र और क्षेत्रज्ञके संयोगसे उत्पन्न हुए समझो ॥
bhagwad_gita::516.english_translation: O best among the Bharatas, know that whatever comes into being, moving or unmoving, arises from the union of the field and the knower of the field.
bhagwad_gita::516.translation_literal: यावत् (whatever) / सञ्जायते (comes into being) / किञ्चित् (anything) / सत्त्वम् (being) / स्थावर-जङ्गमम् (moving and unmoving) / क्षेत्र-क्षेत्रज्ञ-संयोगात् (from the union of field and knower-of-field) / तत् (that) / विद्धि (know) / भरतर्षभ (O best among the Bharatas)
bhagwad_gita::516.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::516.essence: All forms arise from the meeting of awareness and changing nature.
bhagwad_gita::516.simple_meaning: All living forms, moving or still, arise from the meeting of the field and the knower of the field.
bhagwad_gita::516.simple_insight: You are invited to look beneath appearances and see what truly gives rise to life.
bhagwad_gita::516.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna teaches the difference between the body-mind field and the knower within it. Here Krishna says every moving and unmoving being arises from their union, pushing Arjuna toward deeper discrimination.
bhagwad_gita::516.modern_relevance: You watch a child sleep, a crowd rush past, a body age in the mirror. Krishna points beneath all forms and says: look for the meeting of awareness and the changing field.
bhagwad_gita::516.insight: It shifts attention from outer forms to the hidden principle that makes any form appear.

bhagwad_gita::517.verse_sanskrit: समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरम् । विनश्यत्स्वविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
bhagwad_gita::517.verse_hindi: जो नष्ट होते हुए सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें परमात्माको नाशरहित और समरूपसे स्थित देखता है, वही वास्तवमें सही देखता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::517.english_translation: One who sees the supreme being equally present in all beings, imperishable amid the perishing, truly sees.
bhagwad_gita::517.translation_literal: समम् (equally) / सर्वेषु (in all) / भूतेषु (beings) / तिष्ठन्तम् (standing) / परमेश्वरम् (the supreme being) / विनश्यत्सु (among the perishing) / अविनश्यन्तम् (imperishable) / यः (who) / पश्यति (sees) / सः (that one) / पश्यति (truly sees)
bhagwad_gita::517.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::517.essence: Real seeing notices one imperishable presence in every changing form.
bhagwad_gita::517.simple_meaning: True seeing means recognizing one unchanging presence in every living being, even while bodies and forms keep changing and disappearing.
bhagwad_gita::517.simple_insight: The world feels less divided when you stop sorting beings into separate categories and notice the same presence in all.
bhagwad_gita::517.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, while Arjuna is overwhelmed by the lives about to be lost, Krishna turns the lesson inward and outward at once. He says the one who sees the supreme being equally present in all beings sees correctly, because forms perish while the one reality remains.
bhagwad_gita::517.modern_relevance: You’re in a hospital corridor, staring at a stranger’s exhausted face, then at your own family member in the next room. The verse asks you to see beyond labels and notice the same living presence in both.
bhagwad_gita::517.insight: It shifts perception from separation to shared presence, changing how you look at every person before you act.

bhagwad_gita::518.verse_sanskrit: समं पश्यन्हि सर्वत्र समवस्थितमीश्वरम् । न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::518.verse_hindi: क्योंकि सब जगह समरूपसे स्थित ईश्वरको समरूपसे देखनेवाला मनुष्य अपनेआपसे अपनी हिंसा नहीं करता, इसलिये वह परमगतिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::518.english_translation: Seeing the divine equally everywhere, a person does not wound the true self by the true self, and reaches the highest state.
bhagwad_gita::518.translation_literal: समम् (equally) / पश्यन् (seeing) / हि (indeed) / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / समवस्थितम् (equally situated) / ईश्वरम् (the divine ruler) / न (not) / हिनस्ति (hurts) / आत्मना (by the true self) / आत्मानम् (the true self) / ततः (therefore) / याति (goes) / पराम् (highest) / गतिम् (state, destination)
bhagwad_gita::518.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::518.essence: Seeing unity everywhere ends the violence that returns to yourself.
bhagwad_gita::518.simple_meaning: Seeing the same divine presence everywhere ends inner self-harm and leads to the highest state.
bhagwad_gita::518.simple_insight: When separation drops, self-sabotage loses its grip.
bhagwad_gita::518.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield, where fear and grief have frozen action. After showing that the same reality stands in every being, he says that one who sees this unity no longer attacks the true self through hatred or confusion.
bhagwad_gita::518.modern_relevance: You replay a harsh conversation in your head and turn it into self-blame. The moment you stop dividing people into enemies and allies, the inner violence eases.
bhagwad_gita::518.insight: It shifts perception from divided beings to one shared presence, ending the reflex to injure yourself through hatred or fear.

bhagwad_gita::519.verse_sanskrit: प्रकृत्यैव च कर्माणि क्रियमाणानि सर्वशः । यः पश्यति तथाऽऽत्मानमकर्तारं स पश्यति ॥
bhagwad_gita::519.verse_hindi: जो सम्पूर्ण क्रियाओंको सब प्रकारसे प्रकृतिके द्वारा ही की जाती हुई देखता है और अपनेआपको अकर्ता देखता अनुभव करता है, वही यथार्थ देखता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::519.english_translation: One who sees all actions as being done only by nature, and sees the true self as the non-doer, sees rightly.
bhagwad_gita::519.translation_literal: प्रकृत्या (by nature) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / कर्माणि (actions) / क्रियमाणानि (being done) / सर्वशः (in every way) / यः (who) / पश्यति (sees) / तथा (thus) / आत्मानम् (the true self) / अकर्तारम् (as non-doer) / सः (that one) / पश्यति (sees)
bhagwad_gita::519.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::519.essence: Freedom begins when you stop claiming every action as yours.
bhagwad_gita::519.simple_meaning: All actions are carried out by nature, while the true self remains a non-doer. Clear seeing means noticing this distinction directly.
bhagwad_gita::519.simple_insight: There is relief in dropping the burden of being the sole author of everything.
bhagwad_gita::519.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before the war. Krishna keeps stripping away the illusion of personal control. Here he says the body-mind acts through nature, while the true self is not the doer at all.
bhagwad_gita::519.modern_relevance: You replay a painful conversation at 2 a.m., convinced you caused everything. This verse loosens that knot: action flows through conditions, and not every movement belongs to your deepest identity.
bhagwad_gita::519.insight: It shifts attention from personal ownership of action to clear witnessing of how action actually occurs.

bhagwad_gita::520.verse_sanskrit: यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति । तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा ॥
bhagwad_gita::520.verse_hindi: जिस कालमें साधक प्राणियोंके अलगअलग भावोंको एक प्रकृतिमें ही स्थित देखता है और उस प्रकृतिसे ही उन सबका विस्तार देखता है, उस कालमें वह ब्रह्मको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::520.english_translation: When one sees all beings as rooted in one nature and all expansion arising from that source, one attains the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::520.translation_literal: यदा (when) / भूतपृथग्भावम् (the separate states of beings) / एकस्थम् (standing in one place) / अनुपश्यति (one sees clearly) / ततः (then) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / विस्तारम् (expansion) / ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / सम्पद्यते (attains) / तदा (at that time)
bhagwad_gita::520.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::520.essence: Many beings are one reality seen through different forms.
bhagwad_gita::520.simple_meaning: When a person sees the many forms of living beings as arising from one underlying reality, that person reaches that reality.
bhagwad_gita::520.simple_insight: Separation starts to soften. What looked divided begins to feel like one living whole.
bhagwad_gita::520.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna is still answering Arjuna’s crisis by showing how a wise person sees. After learning to notice the body, action, and the true self correctly, the seeker now sees many beings as expressions of one source and moves toward Brahman.
bhagwad_gita::520.modern_relevance: You watch a family argument and stop seeing only sides. Beneath the anger, fear, pride, and hurt, you begin to notice one shared human source moving through different forms.
bhagwad_gita::520.insight: It shifts perception from isolated forms to the single reality behind them.

bhagwad_gita::521.verse_sanskrit: अनादित्वान्निर्गुणत्वात्परमात्मायमव्ययः । शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::521.verse_hindi: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  यह पुरुष स्वयं अनादि और गुणोंसे रहित होनेसे अविनाशी परमात्मस्वरूप ही है ।  यह शरीरमें रहता हुआ भी न करता है और न लिप्त होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::521.english_translation: O son of Kunti, this supreme self is beginningless, beyond the gunas, and imperishable. Though abiding in the body, it does not act and is not stained.
bhagwad_gita::521.translation_literal: अनादित्वात् (because of beginninglessness) / निर्गुणत्वात् (because of being beyond the gunas) / परमात्मा (supreme self) / अयम् (this) / अव्ययः (imperishable) । / शरीरस्थः (abiding in the body) / अपि (even though) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / न (not) / करोति (acts) / न (not) / लिप्यते (is stained)
bhagwad_gita::521.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::521.essence: What you are remains unstained, even while life moves through you.
bhagwad_gita::521.simple_meaning: The true self has no beginning, is beyond the three qualities of nature, and cannot be destroyed. Even while living in a body, it neither performs actions nor gets tainted by them.
bhagwad_gita::521.simple_insight: You can be fully present in life without being trapped by everything that happens through you.
bhagwad_gita::521.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before battle. Krishna now explains the inner reality behind action: the true self is beginningless, beyond the changing qualities of nature, and remains untouched even while embodied. This prepares Arjuna to act without confusion.
bhagwad_gita::521.modern_relevance: You said something sharp in anger, then spent the whole night replaying it. The mind wants to fuse you with the mistake; this verse separates the actor from the deeper witness.
bhagwad_gita::521.insight: It shifts identity away from what the body and mind do toward the untouched awareness that remains.

bhagwad_gita::522.verse_sanskrit: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते । सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::522.verse_hindi: जैसे सब जगह व्याप्त आकाश अत्यन्त सूक्ष्म होनेसे कहीं भी लिप्त नहीं होता, ऐसे ही सब जगह परिपूर्ण आत्मा किसी भी देहमें लिप्त नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::522.english_translation: As all-pervading space is not tainted because of its subtlety, so the self, present in every body, is not tainted.
bhagwad_gita::522.translation_literal: यथा (just as) / सर्वगतं (all-pervading) / सौक्ष्म्यात् (because of subtlety) / आकाशं (space) / न (not) / उपलिप्यते (is tainted) / सर्वत्रावस्थितः (present everywhere) / देहे (in the body) / तथा (so) / आत्मा (the true self) / न (not) / उपलिप्यते (is tainted)
bhagwad_gita::522.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::522.essence: What is everywhere cannot be stained by what changes.
bhagwad_gita::522.simple_meaning: The true self is present in every body, but it is never stained or affected by the body it inhabits.
bhagwad_gita::522.simple_insight: You are closer to awareness than to whatever passes through awareness.
bhagwad_gita::522.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen while Krishna explains the difference between the body and the true self. He uses space as an image: just as space is everywhere yet untouched, the true self remains unstained in every body.
bhagwad_gita::522.modern_relevance: You hear a harsh comment and feel it sink into your chest. The verse reminds you that what is aware of the hurt is not the hurt itself.
bhagwad_gita::522.insight: It shifts identity from the changing body to the untouched awareness that witnesses change.

bhagwad_gita::523.verse_sanskrit: यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकमिमं रविः । क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत ॥
bhagwad_gita::523.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन  जैसे एक ही सूर्य सम्पूर्ण संसारको प्रकाशित करता है, ऐसे ही क्षेत्री क्षेत्रज्ञ, आत्मा सम्पूर्ण क्षेत्रको प्रकाशित करता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::523.english_translation: As one sun illuminates this whole world, so the knower of the field illuminates the whole field, O Bharata.
bhagwad_gita::523.translation_literal: यथा (as) / प्रकाशयति (illuminates) / एकः (one) / कृत्स्नं (whole) / लोकम् (world) / इमम् (this) / रविः (sun) / क्षेत्रम् (field) / क्षेत्री (knower of the field) / तथा (so) / कृत्स्नम् (whole) / प्रकाशयति (illuminates) / भारत (O Bharata)
bhagwad_gita::523.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::523.essence: Awareness illuminates everything without being touched by what it sees.
bhagwad_gita::523.simple_meaning: The one who knows the field makes the whole field known, just as one sun lights up the entire world.
bhagwad_gita::523.simple_insight: What reveals your experience is already beyond it.
bhagwad_gita::523.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna is still teaching Arjuna how to see beyond the body and mind. After saying the true self is untouched, he gives a vivid image: the knower of the field illumines the whole field like the sun lights the world.
bhagwad_gita::523.modern_relevance: You sit alone after a painful argument, replaying every sentence. The mind feels like the whole room — until you notice the quiet awareness in which the replay appears.
bhagwad_gita::523.insight: It shifts attention from the contents of experience to the awareness that makes experience visible.

bhagwad_gita::524.verse_sanskrit: क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेवमन्तरं ज्ञानचक्षुषा । भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::524.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार जो ज्ञानरूपी नेत्रसे क्षेत्र और क्षेत्रज्ञके अन्तरविभाग को तथा कार्यकारणसहित प्रकृतिसे स्वयंको अलग जानते हैं, वे परमात्माको प्राप्त हो जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::524.english_translation: In this way, those who know the distinction between the field and the knower of the field with the eye of wisdom, and who know release from the source of nature, attain the supreme.
bhagwad_gita::524.translation_literal: क्षेत्र-क्षेत्रज्ञयोः (of the field and the knower of the field) / एवम् (thus) / अन्तरम् (difference) / ज्ञानचक्षुषा (with the eye of knowledge) / भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षम् (release from material nature) / च (and) / ये (those who) / विदुः (know) / यान्ति (go) / ते (they) / परम् (to the supreme)
bhagwad_gita::524.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::524.essence: Clear seeing separates you from what changes and opens the way beyond it.
bhagwad_gita::524.simple_meaning: True seeing separates the changing field from the one who knows it. That clear discrimination frees a person from identification with nature and leads to the highest state.
bhagwad_gita::524.simple_insight: You do not have to confuse yourself with what changes. Clear seeing brings relief and direction.
bhagwad_gita::524.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna frozen and Krishna still teaching, the chapter reaches its closing point: the body-mind field, the knower, and release from nature. After comparing the true self to sky and sun, Krishna gives the final key to freedom.
bhagwad_gita::524.modern_relevance: You catch yourself saying, "I am a failure," after one brutal conversation. This verse interrupts that collapse: the hurt, the thought, and the one who notices them are not the same.
bhagwad_gita::524.insight: It shifts attention from identifying with the changing field to recognising the witness that stands apart.

bhagwad_gita::525.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचपरं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् । यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::525.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  सम्पूर्ण ज्ञानोंमें उत्तम और पर ज्ञानको मैं फिर कहूँगा, जिसको जानकर सबकेसब मुनिलोग इस संसारसे मुक्त होकर परमसिद्धिको प्राप्त हो गये हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::525.english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: I will speak again of the highest knowledge, the best of all knowledge. Knowing this, all sages have reached the supreme perfection from here.
bhagwad_gita::525.translation_literal: श्री भगवानुवाच (the Blessed Lord said) / परम् (highest) / भूयः (again) / प्रवक्ष्यामि (I will declare) / ज्ञानानाम् (among knowledges) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / उत्तमम् (highest) / यत् (which) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / मुनयः (sages) / सर्वे (all) / पराम् (supreme) / सिद्धिम् (perfection) / इतः (from here) / गताः (have gone)
bhagwad_gita::525.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::525.essence: Some knowledge does not inform you; it completes you.
bhagwad_gita::525.simple_meaning: Krishna says he will teach the highest kind of knowledge, the one that has taken wise seekers to the greatest fulfillment.
bhagwad_gita::525.simple_insight: Real understanding is not information. It is the kind that changes where you stand in life.
bhagwad_gita::525.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Arjuna is still trapped between action and collapse. Krishna pauses before explaining the three gunas and announces a deeper teaching: a knowledge so complete that sages have used it to reach final fulfillment.
bhagwad_gita::525.modern_relevance: You are staring at a message that could change a relationship, and your finger hovers over send. Some knowledge does not add more facts — it changes who can act without fear.
bhagwad_gita::525.insight: It shifts the mind from collecting ideas to seeking the understanding that transforms being itself.

bhagwad_gita::526.verse_sanskrit: इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागताः । सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च ॥
bhagwad_gita::526.verse_hindi: इस ज्ञानका आश्रय लेकर जो मनुष्य मेरी सधर्मताको प्राप्त हो गये हैं, वे महासर्गमें भी पैदा नहीं होते और महाप्रलयमें भी व्यथित नहीं होते ॥
bhagwad_gita::526.english_translation: Having taken refuge in this knowledge, they attain my likeness. They are not born at creation, and they are not troubled at dissolution.
bhagwad_gita::526.translation_literal: इदम् (this) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / उपाश्रित्य (taking refuge in) / मम (my) / साधर्म्यम् (likeness) / आगताः (having attained) / सर्गे (at creation) / अपि (even) / न (not) / उपजायन्ते (are born) / प्रलये (at dissolution) / न (not) / व्यथन्ति (are troubled) / च (and)
bhagwad_gita::526.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::526.essence: True understanding makes beginning and ending stop ruling you.
bhagwad_gita::526.simple_meaning: With this knowledge, a person becomes like Krishna in nature. Such a person is no longer shaken by cosmic creation or destruction.
bhagwad_gita::526.simple_insight: There is calm in knowing that what you truly are is untouched by beginnings and endings.
bhagwad_gita::526.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna continues teaching the highest knowledge: those who understand it share his nature in a profound way, so even the greatest cycles of creation and dissolution no longer disturb them.
bhagwad_gita::526.modern_relevance: You are standing in a hospital corridor after hearing that life will never be the same. This verse speaks to the part of you that can remain steady even when everything around you begins or ends.
bhagwad_gita::526.insight: It shifts attention from temporary events to the unshaken ground beneath them.

bhagwad_gita::527.verse_sanskrit: मम योनिर्महद्ब्रह्म तस्मिन् गर्भं दधाम्यहम् । संभवः सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत ॥
bhagwad_gita::527.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन  मेरी मूल प्रकृति तो उत्पत्तिस्थान है और मैं उसमें जीवरूप गर्भका स्थापन करता हूँ ।  उससे सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंकी उत्पत्ति होती है ॥
bhagwad_gita::527.english_translation: O Bharata, my primal nature is the womb; I place the seed in it. From that, all beings are born.
bhagwad_gita::527.translation_literal: मम (my) / योनिः (womb, source) / महत्-ब्रह्म (great nature) / तस्मिन् (in that) / गर्भम् (seed, embryo) / दधामि (I place) / अहम् (I) / संभवः (coming into being, birth) / सर्व-भूतानाम् (of all beings) / ततः (from that) / भवति (comes to be) / भारत (O Bharata)
bhagwad_gita::527.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::527.essence: All birth comes from a source beyond personal control.
bhagwad_gita::527.simple_meaning: All living forms arise from the union of primal nature and the seed placed within it. Krishna is explaining how birth itself unfolds.
bhagwad_gita::527.simple_insight: The world is not random. Life arises through a deeper order already at work.
bhagwad_gita::527.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna still caught between collapse and action, Krishna shifts from philosophy to cosmic explanation. After speaking of the supreme reality, he explains how all beings come into birth: primal nature is the source, and the seed is placed within it.
bhagwad_gita::527.modern_relevance: A child’s first heartbeat appears on a screen, and no one in the room can explain life in a single sentence. The verse reminds you that existence comes through forces larger than personal control.
bhagwad_gita::527.insight: It shifts attention from isolated individuality to the hidden process that generates every form.

bhagwad_gita::528.verse_sanskrit: सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तयः सम्भवन्ति याः । तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता ॥
bhagwad_gita::528.verse_hindi: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  सम्पूर्ण योनियोंमें प्राणियोंके जितने शरीर पैदा होते हैं, उन सबकी मूल प्रकृति तो माता है और मैं बीजस्थापन करनेवाला पिता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::528.english_translation: O son of Kunti, in all forms of birth, the material nature is the womb, and I am the seed-giving father.
bhagwad_gita::528.translation_literal: सर्वयोनिषु (in all wombs/forms of birth) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / मूर्तयः (forms/bodies) / सम्भवन्ति (come into being) / याः (which) / तासाम् (of those) / ब्रह्म (material nature) / महत् (great) / योनिः (womb/source) / अहम् (I) / बीजप्रदः (seed-giving) / पिता (father)
bhagwad_gita::528.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::528.essence: All forms arise from one source, and the divine gives them life.
bhagwad_gita::528.simple_meaning: All living forms come from the same source of nature, while Krishna says he is the seed-giving father behind their coming into being.
bhagwad_gita::528.simple_insight: You are not isolated from life. Everything that appears is joined by one hidden source.
bhagwad_gita::528.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains how life itself unfolds. After describing nature as the womb of all beings, Krishna says he is the seed-giving father, linking every form of life to a single divine source.
bhagwad_gita::528.modern_relevance: You look at a newborn’s face and then at an old family photo, and the same lineage runs through both. Behind every separate life, there is one shared source you rarely notice.
bhagwad_gita::528.insight: It shifts attention from isolated individuals to the one source from which all forms arise.

bhagwad_gita::529.verse_sanskrit: सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः । निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::529.verse_hindi: हे महाबाहो  प्रकृतिसे उत्पन्न होनेवाले सत्त्व, रज और तम  ये तीनों गुण अविनाशी देहीको देहमें बाँध देते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::529.english_translation: Arjuna, the three qualities of nature—sattva, rajas, and tamas—bind the imperishable inner being to the body.
bhagwad_gita::529.translation_literal: सत्त्वं (sattva) / रजः (rajas) / तमः (tamas) / इति (thus) / गुणाः (qualities) / प्रकृतिसंभवाः (born of nature) / निबध्नन्ति (bind) / महाबाहो (mighty-armed one) / देहे (in the body) / देहिनम् (the embodied one) / अव्ययम् (imperishable)
bhagwad_gita::529.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::529.essence: Nature's three forces keep the changeless one identified with the body.
bhagwad_gita::529.simple_meaning: The three qualities born from nature keep the imperishable inner being tied to the body.
bhagwad_gita::529.simple_insight: You are not trapped by weakness alone; the whole system of nature can keep you identified.
bhagwad_gita::529.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains why beings stay caught in embodied life. Sattva, rajas, and tamas are not just traits; they are forces of nature that bind the unchanging inner being to the body.
bhagwad_gita::529.modern_relevance: You know that moment when you promise yourself you will react calmly, then irritation, craving, or fog takes over anyway? This verse points to the deeper machinery behind that takeover.
bhagwad_gita::529.insight: It shifts attention from moral blame to seeing the forces shaping behavior.

bhagwad_gita::530.verse_sanskrit: तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम् । सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ ॥
bhagwad_gita::530.verse_hindi: हे पापरहित अर्जुन  उन गुणोंमें सत्त्वगुण निर्मल स्वच्छ होनेके कारण प्रकाशक और निर्विकार है ।  वह सुख और ज्ञानकी आसक्तिसे देहीको बाँधता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::530.english_translation: Among those qualities, sattva—because it is pure and luminous and free from affliction—binds the embodied being through attachment to happiness and to knowledge, O sinless one.
bhagwad_gita::530.translation_literal: तत्र (there, among them) / सत्त्वम् (sattva) / निर्मलत्वात् (because of purity) / प्रकाशकम् (luminous, illuminating) / अनामयम् (free from affliction) / सुखसङ्गेन (through attachment to happiness) / बध्नाति (binds) / ज्ञानसङ्गेन (through attachment to knowledge) / च (and) / अनघ (O sinless one)
bhagwad_gita::530.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::530.essence: Even clarity becomes bondage when you cling to its pleasure.
bhagwad_gita::530.simple_meaning: Even purity can become a chain when you cling to comfort or to being wise. Sattva brings light, but attachment to that light still binds.
bhagwad_gita::530.simple_insight: It warns that even good states can trap you when you start clinging to them.
bhagwad_gita::530.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna frozen before battle, Krishna explains the three gunas. After naming sattva as pure and illuminating, he shows the hidden trap: even clarity can bind when a person becomes attached to comfort or to the pride of understanding.
bhagwad_gita::530.modern_relevance: You finally feel calm after weeks of stress, then panic at the thought of losing that calm. You start guarding the feeling instead of living. The grip has simply changed shape.
bhagwad_gita::530.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing refined states to seeing how attachment operates even inside them.

bhagwad_gita::531.verse_sanskrit: रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् । तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::531.verse_hindi: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  तृष्णा और आसक्तिको पैदा करनेवाले रजोगुणको तुम रागस्वरूप समझो ।  वह कर्मोंकी आसक्तिसे शरीरधारीको बाँधता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::531.english_translation: Know rajas as passion-born, born of craving and attachment. It binds the embodied being through attachment to action, O son of Kunti.
bhagwad_gita::531.translation_literal: रजः (rajas) / रागात्मकम् (of the nature of passion) / विद्धि (know) / तृष्णा (craving) / सङ्ग (attachment) / समुद्भवम् (born from) / तत् (that) / निबध्नाति (binds) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / कर्मसङ्गेन (through attachment to action) / देहिनम् (the embodied being)
bhagwad_gita::531.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::531.essence: Craving turns action into a chain.
bhagwad_gita::531.simple_meaning: Restless desire and attachment create rajas. That force traps a person by making them cling to action and its rewards.
