bhagwad_gita::531.simple_insight: You can see how craving quietly turns action into bondage.
bhagwad_gita::531.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna still stands frozen while Krishna explains the three forces that shape human conduct. After describing sattva, Krishna now names rajas: the force of craving and attachment that ties the embodied person to restless doing.
bhagwad_gita::531.modern_relevance: You refresh your inbox again, then check the message thread, then the notifications. The urge feels small, but it keeps pulling you back into the same loop.
bhagwad_gita::531.insight: It shifts attention from the task itself to the craving that clings to it.

bhagwad_gita::532.verse_sanskrit: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् । प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥
bhagwad_gita::532.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशी अर्जुन  सम्पूर्ण देहधारियोंको मोहित करनेवाले तमोगुणको तुम अज्ञानसे उत्पन्न होनेवाला समझो ।  वह प्रमाद, आलस्य और निद्राके द्वारा देहधारियोंको बाँधता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::532.english_translation: Arjuna, know tamas to be born of ignorance and deluding all embodied beings. It binds them through heedlessness, laziness, and sleep.
bhagwad_gita::532.translation_literal: तमः (darkness/inertia) / तु (indeed) / अज्ञानजम् (born of ignorance) / विद्धि (know) / मोहनम् (deluding) / सर्वदेहिनाम् (of all embodied beings) / प्रमाद-आलस्य-निद्राभिः (through heedlessness, laziness, and sleep) / तत् (that) / निबध्नाति (binds) / भारत (Arjuna)
bhagwad_gita::532.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::532.essence: Confusion binds most through laziness, not force.
bhagwad_gita::532.simple_meaning: Tamas is the force of confusion and inertia. It clouds judgment and traps people through carelessness, laziness, and sleepiness.
bhagwad_gita::532.simple_insight: You can spot what drags you down by watching what dulls your mind and delays your action.
bhagwad_gita::532.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still teaching Arjuna on the battlefield, where the three gunas are being explained one by one. After describing sattva and rajas, he now names tamas as the force that clouds living beings and binds them through dullness.
bhagwad_gita::532.modern_relevance: You open your phone “for a minute” and lose half an hour, then feel foggy and late. That drag is not harmless rest; it is tamas quietly taking the wheel.
bhagwad_gita::532.insight: It teaches you to identify inertia by its symptoms: delay, dullness, and mental fog.

bhagwad_gita::533.verse_sanskrit: सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत । ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत ॥
bhagwad_gita::533.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन  सत्त्वगुण सुखमें और रजोगुण कर्ममें लगाकर मनुष्यपर विजय करता है तथा तमोगुण ज्ञानको ढककर एवं प्रमादमें भी लगाकर मनुष्यपर विजंय करता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::533.english_translation: Sattva binds through pleasure, rajas through action, and tamas, covering knowledge, binds through negligence.
bhagwad_gita::533.translation_literal: सत्त्वम् (sattva) / सुखे (in pleasure) / सञ्जयति (binds) / रजः (rajas) / कर्मणि (in action) / भारत (O Bharata) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / आवृत्य (covering) / तु (but) / तमः (tamas) / प्रमादे (in negligence) / सञ्जयति (binds) / उत (also)
bhagwad_gita::533.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::533.essence: Each force traps you in a different way: comfort, activity, or blindness.
bhagwad_gita::533.simple_meaning: Three forces shape human behavior differently: one lures with pleasure, one drives constant activity, and one hides understanding while pulling a person into carelessness.
bhagwad_gita::533.simple_insight: It becomes easier to notice what is steering you before it quietly takes over.
bhagwad_gita::533.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains the three forces that shape every mind and action. This verse shows how each force captures a person in a different way: pleasure, restless doing, or dull confusion.
bhagwad_gita::533.modern_relevance: You open your phone for one quick check and lose twenty minutes, then another hour chasing tasks, then realize you never thought clearly at all. This verse names the three ways the mind gets hijacked.
bhagwad_gita::533.insight: It trains you to spot the hidden mode driving your choices so you can step back before it controls you.

bhagwad_gita::534.verse_sanskrit: रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत । रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा ॥
bhagwad_gita::534.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन  रजोगुण और तमोगुणको दबाकर सत्त्वगुण सत्त्वगुण, और तमोगुणको दबाकर रजोगुण, वैसे ही सत्त्वगुण और रजोगुणको दबाकर तमोगुण बढ़ता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::534.english_translation: Arjuna, when rajas and tamas are subdued, sattva rises. When sattva and tamas are subdued, rajas rises. When sattva and rajas are subdued, tamas rises.
bhagwad_gita::534.translation_literal: रजः (passion) / तमः (inertia) / च (and) / अभिभूय (having overpowered) / सत्त्वम् (purity, clarity) / भवति (becomes) / भारत (Arjuna) / रजः (passion) / सत्त्वम् (purity, clarity) / तमः (inertia) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / तमः (inertia) / सत्त्वम् (purity, clarity) / रजः (passion) / तथा (likewise)
bhagwad_gita::534.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::534.essence: What dominates the mind is temporary, not who you are.
bhagwad_gita::534.simple_meaning: The three qualities keep replacing one another. When one becomes stronger, the others are pushed down.
bhagwad_gita::534.simple_insight: You can stop treating your moods as permanent. What dominates now will not stay forever.
bhagwad_gita::534.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains how the three qualities shape every mind and action. This verse adds the moving pattern: one quality rises only by suppressing the others, showing that inner states are always in flux.
bhagwad_gita::534.modern_relevance: You wake up sharp, then drift into fog by noon, then feel restless at night. The mind is not one fixed mood — it keeps changing hands.
bhagwad_gita::534.insight: It teaches you to notice which quality is currently leading, instead of mistaking a passing state for your nature.

bhagwad_gita::535.verse_sanskrit: सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते । ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत ॥
bhagwad_gita::535.verse_hindi: जब इस मनुष्यशरीरमें सब द्वारोंइन्द्रियों और अन्तःकरण में प्रकाश स्वच्छता और ज्ञान विवेक प्रकट हो जाता है, तब जानना चाहिये कि सत्त्वगुण बढ़ा हुआ है ॥
bhagwad_gita::535.english_translation: When light, clarity, and understanding arise in all the gates of this body, know that sattva has grown strong.
bhagwad_gita::535.translation_literal: सर्वद्वारेषु (in all the gates) / देहेऽस्मिन् (in this body) / प्रकाशः (light) / उपजायते (arises) / ज्ञानम् (understanding) / यदा (when) / तदा (then) / विद्यात् (one should know) / विवृद्धम् (grown strong) / सत्त्वम् (sattva) / इति (thus) / उत (indeed)
bhagwad_gita::535.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::535.essence: Inner brightness is the sign that clarity is taking over.
bhagwad_gita::535.simple_meaning: When the senses and mind become bright, clear, and wise, that is a sign that sattva is increasing.
bhagwad_gita::535.simple_insight: You can notice inner growth by the quality of your awareness, not by outer noise.
bhagwad_gita::535.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna is explaining the three gunas to Arjuna, who is overwhelmed and unable to act clearly. After describing how the other qualities dominate, Krishna now points to the sign of sattva: inner brightness, understanding, and lucidity in the whole body-mind system.
bhagwad_gita::535.modern_relevance: You wake up after a chaotic night and suddenly the room feels sharper, your thoughts less sticky, your reactions slower. That quiet brightness is a sign that your mind has cleared.
bhagwad_gita::535.insight: It shifts attention from judging yourself by mood to reading the quality of awareness itself.

bhagwad_gita::536.verse_sanskrit: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा । रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥
bhagwad_gita::536.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  रजोगुणके बढ़नेपर लोभ, प्रवृत्ति, कर्मोंका आरम्भ, अशान्ति और स्पृहा  ये वृत्तियाँ पैदा होती हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::536.english_translation: O best of the Bharatas, when rajas grows, greed, activity, the beginning of actions, restlessness, and desire arise.
bhagwad_gita::536.translation_literal: लोभः (greed) / प्रवृत्तिः (activity, urge) / आरम्भः (beginning) / कर्मणाम् (of actions) / अशमः (restlessness, lack of peace) / स्पृहा (desire, craving) / रजसि (in rajas) / एतानि (these) / जायन्ते (are born) / विवृद्धे (when increased) / भरतर्षभ (O best of the Bharatas)
bhagwad_gita::536.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::536.essence: Restless wanting multiplies action, but never settles the mind.
bhagwad_gita::536.simple_meaning: When rajas becomes strong, greed, restless activity, constant starting, and craving appear.
bhagwad_gita::536.simple_insight: You can recognize agitation early, before it turns into compulsive wanting.
bhagwad_gita::536.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna explains how the three gunas shape human behavior. After describing sattva, Krishna now shows Arjuna the marks of rajas: the force that drives craving, motion, and unsettled action.
bhagwad_gita::536.modern_relevance: You open five tabs, start three tasks, and still feel unsatisfied. That buzzing urge to keep doing more is not productivity — it is restlessness taking over.
bhagwad_gita::536.insight: It teaches you to notice the signature of rajas in your own mind: urgency, craving, and unfinished motion.

bhagwad_gita::537.verse_sanskrit: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च । तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन ॥
bhagwad_gita::537.verse_hindi: हे कुरुनन्दन  तमोगुणके बढ़नेपर अप्रकाश, अप्रवृत्ति, प्रमाद और मोह  ये वृत्तियाँ भी पैदा होती हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::537.english_translation: O descendant of Kuru, when tamas grows strong, darkness, inertia, negligence, and delusion arise.
bhagwad_gita::537.translation_literal: अप्रकाशः (absence of light) / अप्रवृत्तिः (absence of activity) / प्रमादः (negligence) / मोहः (delusion) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / तमसि (in tamas) / एतानि (these) / जायन्ते (are born) / विवृद्धे (when increased) / कुरुनन्दन (O descendant of Kuru)
bhagwad_gita::537.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::537.essence: Darkness does not stay still; it breeds neglect and confusion.
bhagwad_gita::537.simple_meaning: When tamas becomes stronger, a person loses clarity, becomes inactive, starts neglecting things, and falls into confusion.
bhagwad_gita::537.simple_insight: It feels easier to catch stagnation early than to wake up inside it.
bhagwad_gita::537.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still teaching Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra, where a whole life is being decided in a single moment. After describing the signs of rising sattva and rajas, he now shows what happens when tamas dominates: the mind dims, effort stops, carelessness appears, and confusion follows.
bhagwad_gita::537.modern_relevance: You keep scrolling at 1:13 a.m., telling yourself you will decide tomorrow. By morning, the problem feels heavier, and even simple action feels distant.
bhagwad_gita::537.insight: It teaches you to recognize inertia as a pattern that breeds confusion, not as harmless rest.

bhagwad_gita::538.verse_sanskrit: यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् । तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::538.verse_hindi: जिस समय सत्त्वगुण बढ़ा हो, उस समय यदि देहधारी मनुष्य मर जाता है, तो वह,उत्तमवेत्ताओंके निर्मल लोकोंमें जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::538.english_translation: When sattva is predominant at death, the embodied being reaches the pure worlds of the wise.
bhagwad_gita::538.translation_literal: यदा (when) / सत्त्वे (in sattva) / प्रवृद्धे (having become strong) / तु (indeed) / प्रलयम् (dissolution; death) / याति (goes) / देहभृत् (the embodied one) / तदा (then) / उत्तमविदाम् (of the knowers of the highest) / लोकान् (worlds) / अमलान् (pure, stainless) / प्रतिपद्यते (attains)
bhagwad_gita::538.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::538.essence: A clear state carries consciousness toward a clearer destination.
bhagwad_gita::538.simple_meaning: If a person dies while sattva is strongest, that being reaches pure realms associated with the wise.
bhagwad_gita::538.simple_insight: Your dominant state matters most at the end; it shapes where consciousness moves next.
bhagwad_gita::538.detailed_meaning: Krishna continues explaining the three gunas to Arjuna on the battlefield. After naming the signs of rajas and tamas, he shows the quieter power of sattva: if death comes while clarity is strongest, the being moves toward pure worlds, not confusion.
bhagwad_gita::538.modern_relevance: You are exhausted after a long day, and your mind is either clear or clouded when the hardest conversation arrives. The state you live in most deeply leaves the strongest imprint.
bhagwad_gita::538.insight: It shifts attention from isolated actions to the quality of mind that dominates your life.

bhagwad_gita::539.verse_sanskrit: रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते । तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते ॥
bhagwad_gita::539.verse_hindi: रजोगुणके बढ़नेपर मरनेवाला प्राणी मनुष्ययोनिमें जन्म लेता है तथा तमोगुणके बढ़नेपर मरनेवाला मूढ़योनियोंमें जन्म लेता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::539.english_translation: A being who dies in rajas is born among those attached to action. A being who dies in tamas is born among deluded forms.
bhagwad_gita::539.translation_literal: रजसि (in rajas) / प्रलयं गत्वा (having gone to dissolution, having died) / कर्मसङ्गिषु (among those attached to action) / जायते (is born) । / तथा (similarly) / प्रलीनः (having dissolved, having died) / तमसि (in tamas) / मूढयोनिषु (among deluded births/forms) / जायते (is born)
bhagwad_gita::539.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::539.essence: Your strongest tendency decides the shape of your next beginning.
bhagwad_gita::539.simple_meaning: The state of mind at death shapes the kind of birth that follows. Restless desire leads to another life of attachment; dull confusion leads to a lower, more deluded condition.
bhagwad_gita::539.simple_insight: Your deepest habits do not vanish at the end of a life. They carry their own momentum.
bhagwad_gita::539.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna is explaining the three gunas to Arjuna, who is frozen before battle. After describing how sattva leads upward, Krishna shows the other two forces: rajas pulls a being back into restless action, and tamas sinks it into confusion. This verse completes the contrast.
bhagwad_gita::539.modern_relevance: You keep choosing the same kind of relationship, the same kind of fight, the same kind of excuse. Krishna would say the pattern is already teaching you where it leads.
bhagwad_gita::539.insight: It shifts attention from isolated choices to the dominant force shaping a life over time.

bhagwad_gita::540.verse_sanskrit: कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम् । रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::540.verse_hindi: विवेकी पुरुषोंने शुभकर्मका तो सात्त्विक निर्मल फल कहा है, राजस कर्मका फल दुःख कहा है और तामस कर्मका फल अज्ञान मूढ़ता कहा है ॥
bhagwad_gita::540.english_translation: The result of wholesome action is pure and clear; the result of rajasic action is suffering; the result of tamasic action is ignorance and delusion.
bhagwad_gita::540.translation_literal: कर्मणः (of action) / सुकृतस्य (of well-done, wholesome) / आहुः (they say) / सात्त्विकं (sattvic, pure) / निर्मलं (stainless, clear) / फलम् (fruit, result) / रजसः (of rajas) / तु (but) / फलम् (fruit, result) / दुःखम् (suffering) / अज्ञानम् (ignorance) / तमसः (of tamas) / फलम् (fruit, result)
bhagwad_gita::540.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::540.essence: Action carries its own flavor of result.
bhagwad_gita::540.simple_meaning: Wholesome action leads to a clear, pure result. Restless action leads to suffering. Dark, confused action leads to ignorance and delusion.
bhagwad_gita::540.simple_insight: Your actions shape the kind of life you inherit from them.
bhagwad_gita::540.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna explains the three gunas to Arjuna, who is frozen before war. After showing how the gunas affect rebirth, he now teaches how they color the fruits of action itself. The point is to see what kind of result each kind of action creates.
bhagwad_gita::540.modern_relevance: You send the message in anger, then stare at the screen all night. The words were yours; the fallout was too. This verse helps you see the cost before you act.
bhagwad_gita::540.insight: It shifts attention from the act alone to the quality of mind behind it.

bhagwad_gita::541.verse_sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च । प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च ॥
bhagwad_gita::541.verse_hindi: सत्त्वगुणसे ज्ञान और रजोगुणसे लोभ आदि ही उत्पन्न होते हैं तमोगुणसे प्रमाद, मोह एवं अज्ञान भी उत्पन्न होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::541.english_translation: From sattva comes knowledge; from rajas, greed; from tamas, negligence, delusion, and ignorance.
bhagwad_gita::541.translation_literal: सत्त्वात् (from sattva) / सञ्जायते (is born) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / रजसः (from rajas) / लोभः (greed) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / प्रमादमोहौ (negligence and delusion) / तमसः (from tamas) / भवन्ति (arise) / अज्ञानम् (ignorance) / एव (indeed) / च (and)
bhagwad_gita::541.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::541.essence: Your mental weather has causes: clarity, craving, and confusion each grow from different qualities.
bhagwad_gita::541.simple_meaning: A clear, balanced nature gives rise to understanding. Restless nature produces greed. Heavy, dull nature produces carelessness, delusion, and ignorance.
bhagwad_gita::541.simple_insight: You can stop treating every bad impulse as random and start seeing what kind of energy is feeding it.
bhagwad_gita::541.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna keeps explaining the three gunas to Arjuna, who is frozen before battle. After showing how they shape rebirth and action, Krishna now names their inner effects: sattva brings knowledge, rajas brings greed, and tamas brings confusion.
bhagwad_gita::541.modern_relevance: You open your phone at 1 a.m. and feel the pull to keep scrolling, buying, comparing, numbing. The verse helps you name the force behind the spiral instead of calling it 'just me.'
bhagwad_gita::541.insight: It shifts attention from moral self-blame to pattern recognition: notice which guna is driving the mind, then respond wisely.

bhagwad_gita::542.verse_sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः । जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::542.verse_hindi: सत्त्वगुणमें स्थित मनुष्य ऊर्ध्वलोकोंमें जाते हैं, रजोगुणमें स्थित मनुष्य मृत्युलोकमें जन्म लेते हैं और निन्दनीय तमोगुणकी वृत्तिमें स्थित मनुष्य अधोगतिमें जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::542.english_translation: Those established in sattva go upward; those in rajas remain in the middle; those in the lowest movement of tamas go downward.
bhagwad_gita::542.translation_literal: ऊर्ध्वं (upward) / गच्छन्ति (go) / सत्त्वस्था (those established in sattva) / मध्ये (in the middle) / तिष्ठन्ति (remain) / राजसाः (those in rajas) / जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्थाः (those established in the lowest quality’s movement) / अधः (downward) / गच्छन्ति (go) / तामसाः (those in tamas)
bhagwad_gita::542.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::542.essence: Your inner quality decides the direction of your life.
bhagwad_gita::542.simple_meaning: People shaped by clarity rise to higher states. People ruled by restlessness stay in the middle. People sunk in dullness fall into lower states.
bhagwad_gita::542.simple_insight: Your dominant state shapes the kind of world you keep entering.
bhagwad_gita::542.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and fear. Krishna explains that the three qualities do not just color mood; they determine where a person naturally moves after life and what level of existence they keep returning to.
bhagwad_gita::542.modern_relevance: You keep repeating the same late-night spiral, the same reactive argument, the same drained morning. The state you live from quietly decides the life you keep rebuilding.
bhagwad_gita::542.insight: It shifts attention from isolated actions to the deeper quality that drives them.

bhagwad_gita::543.verse_sanskrit: नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति । गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति ॥
bhagwad_gita::543.verse_hindi: जब विवेकी विचारकुशल मनुष्य तीनों गुणोंके सिवाय अन्य किसीको कर्ता नहीं देखता और अपनेको गुणोंसे पर अनुभव करता है, तब वह मेरे स्वरूपको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::543.english_translation: When the seer understands that no doer exists apart from the three qualities, and knows the divine nature beyond them, that seer reaches my being.
bhagwad_gita::543.translation_literal: नान्यम् (no other) / गुणेभ्यः (than the qualities) / कर्तारम् (doer) / यदा (when) / द्रष्टा (the seer) / अनुपश्यति (sees clearly) / गुणेभ्यः (than the qualities) / च (and) / परम् (beyond) / वेत्ति (knows) / मद्भावम् (my nature) / सः (that one) / अधिगच्छति (attains)
bhagwad_gita::543.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::543.essence: Freedom begins when you stop mistaking qualities for a personal doer.
bhagwad_gita::543.simple_meaning: Clear seeing reveals that action belongs to the three qualities, not to a separate personal doer. When a person sees beyond them, they come to Krishna's nature.
bhagwad_gita::543.simple_insight: It brings relief from the burden of personal control.
bhagwad_gita::543.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna explains that the world runs through the three qualities, not through a separate ego-doer. The one who sees this clearly moves toward Krishna’s own nature.
bhagwad_gita::543.modern_relevance: You replay a painful conversation for hours, blaming yourself for every word. Then it clicks: much of what happened came from moods, habits, and pressures larger than one isolated self.
bhagwad_gita::543.insight: It shifts responsibility from ego to clear seeing, so action can happen without false ownership.

bhagwad_gita::544.verse_hindi: देहधारी विवेकी मनुष्य देहको उत्पन्न करनेवाले इन तीनों गुणोंका अतिक्रमण करके जन्म, मृत्यु और वृद्धावस्थारूप दुःखोंसे रहित हुआ अमरताका अनुभव करता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::544.english_translation: The embodied one who rises beyond these three qualities, which arise from the body, is freed from birth, death, old age, and sorrow, and attains immortality.
bhagwad_gita::544.translation_literal: गुणान् (qualities) / एतान् (these) / अतीत्य (having gone beyond) / त्रीन् (three) / देही (the embodied one) / देहसमुद्भवान् (born from the body) / जन्म-मृत्यु-जरा-दुःखैः (by birth, death, old age, and sorrow) / विमुक्तः (freed) / अमृतम् (immortality) / अश्नुते (attains)
bhagwad_gita::544.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::544.essence: Freedom begins when the three qualities no longer define you.
bhagwad_gita::544.simple_meaning: A person who rises above the three qualities that shape the body is no longer bound by birth, death, old age, or sorrow.
bhagwad_gita::544.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that suffering belongs to change, not to what is deepest in you.
bhagwad_gita::544.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna has just explained the three qualities and their grip on human life. Now he points to the way beyond them: freedom from the cycle of bodily suffering.
bhagwad_gita::544.modern_relevance: You watch your body age in the mirror, then feel the panic rise with every ache, deadline, and loss. This verse says the deepest part of you is not trapped in that churn.
bhagwad_gita::544.insight: It shifts attention from managing symptoms of change to seeing the self as untouched by them.

bhagwad_gita::545.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचकैर्लिंगैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो । किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते ॥
bhagwad_gita::545.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे प्रभो  इन तीनों गुणोंसे अतीत हुआ मनुष्य किन लक्षणोंसे युक्त होता है उसके आचरण कैसे होते हैं और इन तीनों गुणोंका अतिक्रमण कैसे किया जा सकता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::545.english_translation: Arjuna said: O Lord, by what signs is a person known who has gone beyond these three qualities? How does such a person behave, and how does one cross beyond the three qualities?
bhagwad_gita::545.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / कैः लिंगैः (by what signs) / त्रीन् (three) / गुणान् (qualities) / एतान् (these) / अतीतः (gone beyond) / भवति (becomes) / प्रभो (O Lord) / किम् आचारः (what is the conduct) / कथम् च (and how) / एतान् (these) / त्रीन् गुणान् (three qualities) / अतिवर्तते (crosses beyond)
bhagwad_gita::545.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::545.essence: Real freedom must be visible, livable, and learnable.
bhagwad_gita::545.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks how to recognize someone who has gone beyond the three qualities, how that person behaves, and how such freedom is reached.
bhagwad_gita::545.simple_insight: It is okay to ask how real freedom looks before you can live it.
bhagwad_gita::545.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has just heard that a wise person can rise above the three qualities and escape birth, death, and aging. He now asks Krishna for the practical signs, the conduct, and the method, because he wants a lived answer, not a theory.
bhagwad_gita::545.modern_relevance: You hear a calm person speak after a painful breakup and wonder: what changed in them? This is the question behind the question — how does freedom actually show up in a human life?
bhagwad_gita::545.insight: It turns abstract philosophy into a practical test: look for signs, conduct, and method.

bhagwad_gita::546.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव । न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति ॥
bhagwad_gita::546.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  हे पाण्डव  प्रकाश, प्रवृत्ति तथा मोह  ये सभी अच्छी तरहसे प्रवृत्त हो जायँ तो भी गुणातीत मनुष्य इनसे द्वेष नहीं करता, और ये सभी निवृत्त हो जायँ तो इनकी इच्छा नहीं करता ॥
bhagwad_gita::546.english_translation: Krishna said: O Arjuna, the one who has gone beyond the three gunas does not hate light, activity, or confusion when they appear, and does not long for them when they disappear.
bhagwad_gita::546.translation_literal: श्री भगवानुवाच (the Blessed One said) / प्रकाशं (light) / च (and) / प्रवृत्तिं (activity) / च (and) / मोहमेव (and delusion itself) / च (and) / पाण्डव (O Pandava) / न द्वेष्टि (does not hate) / सम्प्रवृत्तानि (when arisen) / न निवृत्तानि (when ceased) / काङ्क्षति (desire)
bhagwad_gita::546.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::546.essence: Freedom begins when changing states stop controlling your response.
bhagwad_gita::546.simple_meaning: A person beyond the three gunas stays even-minded. When clarity, energy, or confusion appear, there is no hatred. When they fade, there is no craving.
bhagwad_gita::546.simple_insight: You stop fighting your changing states and stop chasing the next one.
bhagwad_gita::546.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has asked how someone rises beyond the three gunas. Krishna answers with a test: the mature person does not react with aversion when clarity, drive, or confusion appear, and does not cling when they pass.
bhagwad_gita::546.modern_relevance: You wake up clear one day, restless the next, numb after that. Instead of treating each state like a verdict on your life, you let it move through without panic or pursuit.
bhagwad_gita::546.insight: It teaches you to observe changing inner states without resistance or craving.

bhagwad_gita::547.verse_sanskrit: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते । गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते ॥
bhagwad_gita::547.verse_hindi: जो उदासीनकी तरह स्थित है और जो गुणोंके द्वारा विचलित नहीं किया जा सकता तथा गुण ही गुणोंमें बरत रहे हैं  इस भावसे जो अपने स्वरूपमें ही स्थित रहता है और स्वयं कोई भी चेष्टा नहीं करता ॥
bhagwad_gita::547.english_translation: One who remains like an indifferent witness, unmoved by the three qualities, stands firm and does not stir, knowing only that the qualities are acting among themselves.
bhagwad_gita::547.translation_literal: उदासीनवद् (like one indifferent) / आसीनः (seated, remaining) / गुणैः (by the qualities) / यः (who) / न (not) / विचाल्यते (is shaken) / गुणाः (the qualities) / वर्तन्ते (are acting) / इति (thus) / एव (only) / यः (who) / अवतिष्ठति (remains established) / न (not) / ईङ्गते (moves)
bhagwad_gita::547.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::547.essence: Freedom begins when movement happens, but identity does not.
bhagwad_gita::547.simple_meaning: A wise person stays steady, not shaken by the three qualities, and sees that they are only moving among themselves.
bhagwad_gita::547.simple_insight: You can stop identifying with every passing mood and impulse. That creates a quiet kind of freedom.
bhagwad_gita::547.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna asks how a person rises beyond the three qualities. Krishna answers with a mark of inner maturity: the wise one sits like an uninvolved witness, while the qualities keep shifting around them. This verse sharpens that answer.
bhagwad_gita::547.modern_relevance: A harsh email lands, your chest tightens, and the old urge to react flares up. This verse teaches you to notice the surge without becoming it.
bhagwad_gita::547.insight: It shifts attention from being carried by mental states to remaining established while they change.

bhagwad_gita::548.verse_hindi: जो धीर मनुष्य सुखदुःखमें सम तथा अपने स्वरूपमें स्थित रहता है जो मिट्टीके ढेले, पत्थर और सोनेमें सम रहता है जो प्रियअप्रियमें तथा अपनी निन्दास्तुतिमें सम रहता है जो मानअपमानमें तथा मित्रशत्रुके पक्षमें सम रहता है जो सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंके आरम्भका त्यागी है, वह मनुष्य गुणातीत कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::548.english_translation: The steady one remains equal in pleasure and pain, in a clod of earth, a stone, and gold; equal toward the liked and the disliked, toward praise and blame.
bhagwad_gita::548.translation_literal: समदुःखसुखः (equal in sorrow and joy) / स्वस्थः (established in the true self) / समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः (equal toward clod, stone, and gold) / तुल्यप्रियाप्रियः (equal toward the liked and the disliked) / धीरः (the steadfast one) / तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः (equal toward blame and self-praise)
bhagwad_gita::548.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::548.essence: Steadiness means nothing external gets to decide your center.
bhagwad_gita::548.simple_meaning: A truly steady person does not get shaken by pleasure, pain, praise, blame, wealth, or ordinary objects. They stay centered in themselves.
bhagwad_gita::548.simple_insight: You do not have to be pulled around by every reaction. Steadiness is possible.
bhagwad_gita::548.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna continues teaching Arjuna about the person who has risen above the three gunas. After describing one who is not disturbed by them, he now shows what that looks like in daily life: equal mind in pain and pleasure, praise and blame, gold and dirt.
bhagwad_gita::548.modern_relevance: You open your phone and see praise from one person, criticism from another, and your mood swings before breakfast. This verse reminds you that stability is not controlled by other people's reactions.
bhagwad_gita::548.insight: It trains you to stop measuring your worth by shifting conditions and opinions.

bhagwad_gita::549.verse_sanskrit: मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः । सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::549.verse_hindi: जो धीर मनुष्य सुखदुःखमें सम तथा अपने स्वरूपमें स्थित रहता है जो मिट्टीके ढेले, पत्थर और सोनेमें सम रहता है जो प्रियअप्रियमें तथा अपनी निन्दास्तुतिमें सम रहता है जो मानअपमानमें तथा मित्रशत्रुके पक्षमें सम रहता है जो सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंके आरम्भका त्यागी है, वह मनुष्य गुणातीत कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::549.english_translation: The steady one is equal in honor and dishonor, equal toward friend and foe, and has abandoned all undertakings. Such a person is called beyond the three gunas.
bhagwad_gita::549.translation_literal: मानापमानयोः (in honor and dishonor) / तुल्यः (equal) / तुल्यः (equal) / मित्रारिपक्षयोः (toward friend and enemy sides) / सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी (one who has abandoned all beginnings of action) / गुणातीतः (beyond the gunas) / सः (that one) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::549.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::549.essence: Freedom begins when praise, blame, and personal impulse lose their power over you.
bhagwad_gita::549.simple_meaning: A truly steady person stays the same in praise or insult, with friends or enemies, and no longer starts actions from personal craving. That person rises beyond the three gunas.
bhagwad_gita::549.simple_insight: You can stop living as a puppet of approval, rejection, and impulse.
bhagwad_gita::549.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is being taught how to outgrow the forces that bind ordinary behavior. Krishna describes the person who no longer sways with praise, blame, allies, or enemies, and who has let go of ego-driven action. That is the mark of one beyond the gunas.
bhagwad_gita::549.modern_relevance: A harsh comment lands in a group chat, and your chest tightens. Before you reply, you can notice how quickly praise and insult try to steer you. This verse points to a steadier place.
bhagwad_gita::549.insight: It shifts the mind from social reaction to inner steadiness and non-reactive action.

bhagwad_gita::550.verse_sanskrit: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्ितयोगेन सेवते । स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
bhagwad_gita::550.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य अव्यभिचारी भक्तियोगके द्वारा मेरा सेवन करता है, वह इन गुणोंका अतिक्रमण करके ब्रह्मप्राप्तिका पात्र हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::550.english_translation: Whoever serves Me with unwavering devotion transcends these qualities and becomes fit for union with the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::550.translation_literal: मां (Me) / च (and) / यः (who) / अव्यभिचारेण (with unwavering) / भक्ति-योगेन (through devotion-yoga) / सेवते (serves) / सः (that one) / गुणान् (the qualities) / समतीत्य (having fully transcended) / एतान् (these) / ब्रह्म-भूयाय (for becoming Brahman) / कल्पते (is fit)
bhagwad_gita::550.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::550.essence: Steady devotion can carry you beyond the forces that shape ordinary life.
bhagwad_gita::550.simple_meaning: Steady devotion to Krishna lifts a person beyond the three qualities of nature and makes that person fit for union with the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::550.simple_insight: Love that does not waver can take you past the limits of your ordinary nature.
bhagwad_gita::550.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still trapped in doubt while Krishna explains how to rise above the forces that bind human behavior. This verse gives the turning point: unwavering devotion to Krishna is the way beyond the three qualities and into the highest reality.
bhagwad_gita::550.modern_relevance: You keep trying to fix yourself through sheer will, but the deeper shift comes when your whole heart stays aligned. That steady devotion changes what you can become.
bhagwad_gita::550.insight: It shifts the goal from self-improvement alone to sustained devotion as the force that transforms nature.

bhagwad_gita::551.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाऽहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च । शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च ॥
bhagwad_gita::551.verse_hindi: क्योंकि ब्रह्म, अविनाशी अमृत, शाश्वत धर्म और ऐकान्तिक सुखका आश्रय मैं ही हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::551.english_translation: For I am the foundation of Brahman, of immortality, of the imperishable, of eternal dharma, and of unending bliss.
bhagwad_gita::551.translation_literal: ब्रह्मणः (of Brahman) / हि (indeed) / प्रतिष्ठा (foundation, support) / अहम् (I am) / अमृतस्य (of immortality) / अव्ययस्य (of the imperishable) / च (and) / शाश्वतस्य (of the eternal) / च (and) / धर्मस्य (of dharma) / सुखस्य (of bliss) / ऐकान्तिकस्य (of exclusive, ultimate) / च (and)
bhagwad_gita::551.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::551.essence: All ultimate freedom rests in Krishna, not apart from him.
bhagwad_gita::551.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is the support behind Brahman, immortality, the imperishable, eternal dharma, and ultimate bliss.
bhagwad_gita::551.simple_insight: What you seek at the deepest level is not separate from its source.
bhagwad_gita::551.detailed_meaning: After describing the one who rises beyond the three gunas, Krishna gives the final summit of the chapter. On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna still needing a way beyond inner bondage, Krishna says that the highest reality, lasting freedom, and ultimate fulfilment all rest in him.
bhagwad_gita::551.modern_relevance: You finally reach the edge of a decision you cannot undo: leave the safe life, tell the hard truth, or stop pretending. This verse says the deepest security is not in control, but in what supports all reality.
bhagwad_gita::551.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing separate spiritual goals to recognising their source as one.

bhagwad_gita::552.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् । छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् ॥
bhagwad_gita::552.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  ऊपरकी ओर मूलवाले तथा नीचेकी ओर शाखावाले जिस संसाररूप अश्वत्थवृक्षको अव्यय कहते हैं और वेद जिसके पत्ते हैं, उस संसारवृक्षको जो जानता है, वह सम्पूर्ण वेदोंको जाननेवाला है ॥
bhagwad_gita::552.english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: They speak of the imperishable banyan-like tree of the world, with roots above and branches below. The Vedas are its leaves. One who knows this tree knows the Vedas.
bhagwad_gita::552.translation_literal: श्रीभगवानुवाच (the Blessed Lord said) / ऊर्ध्वमूलम् (with roots above) / अधःशाखम् (with branches below) / अश्वत्थम् (the banyan-like world tree) / प्राहुः (they say) / अव्ययम् (imperishable) / छन्दांसि (the Vedas) / यस्य (whose) / पर्णानि (leaves) / यः (who) / तम् (that) / वेद (knows) / सः (he) / वेदवित् (knower of the Vedas)
bhagwad_gita::552.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::552.essence: Understanding the world-tree is the beginning of true understanding.
bhagwad_gita::552.simple_meaning: The world is like an upside-down tree: its roots are above, its branches below, and the Vedas are its leaves. Truly understanding this structure means understanding the deepest teaching.
bhagwad_gita::552.simple_insight: You stop seeing life as random and start seeing its hidden pattern.
bhagwad_gita::552.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before the war begins. Krishna begins Chapter 15 by describing the world as an upside-down tree of changing life, with the Vedas as its leaves. This verse sets up the whole teaching on how to see beyond appearances.
bhagwad_gita::552.modern_relevance: You open your phone for one answer and get pulled into ten tabs, ten opinions, ten cravings. Krishna points to the deeper pattern underneath that mental branching: learn the structure, not just the surface noise.
bhagwad_gita::552.insight: It shifts attention from scattered appearances to the underlying order that shapes them.

bhagwad_gita::553.verse_sanskrit: अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा     गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः । अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि     कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके ॥
bhagwad_gita::553.verse_hindi: उस संसारवृक्षकी गुणोंसत्त्व, रज और तम के द्वारा बढ़ी हुई तथा विषयरूप कोंपलोंवाली शाखाएँ नीचे, मध्यमें और ऊपर सब जगह फैली हुई हैं ।  मनुष्यलोकमें कर्मोंके अनुसार बाँधनेवाले मूल भी नीचे और ऊपर सभी लोकोंमें व्याप्त हो रहे हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::553.english_translation: Its branches spread below, above, and across. They are nourished by the three qualities, with sense-pleasures as their shoots. In the human world, action-bound roots extend everywhere, tying beings to results.
bhagwad_gita::553.translation_literal: अधः (below) / च (and) / ऊर्ध्वं (above) / प्रसृताः (spread out) / तस्य (of that) / शाखाः (branches) / गुणप्रवृद्धाः (grown by the qualities) / विषयप्रवालाः (with sense-objects as shoots) / अधः (below) / च (and) / मूलानि (roots) / अनुसन्ततानि (extended everywhere) / कर्मानुबन्धीनि (bound by action) / मनुष्यलोके (in the human world)
bhagwad_gita::553.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::553.essence: Craving and action keep the world-tree growing in every direction.
bhagwad_gita::553.simple_meaning: The world-tree spreads everywhere, fed by the three qualities and by desire for sense-pleasures. Its roots reach through human life through action and its consequences.
bhagwad_gita::553.simple_insight: You can feel how deeply life is entangled when desire and action keep feeding the same tree.
bhagwad_gita::553.detailed_meaning: Krishna has just described the upside-down world-tree of existence to Arjuna on the battlefield. Now he shows how it grows: the three qualities feed its branches, sense-pleasures keep them alive, and action binds the roots through human life.
bhagwad_gita::553.modern_relevance: You keep checking one message, then another, then another. Each small craving feeds the whole pattern until it feels like the pattern is running you.
bhagwad_gita::553.insight: It shifts attention from isolated choices to the hidden system of craving and consequence that keeps experience looping.

bhagwad_gita::554.verse_sanskrit: न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते    नान्तो न चादिर्न च संप्रतिष्ठा । अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूल    मसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा ॥
bhagwad_gita::554.verse_hindi: इस संसारवृक्षका जैसा रूप देखनेमें आता है, वैसा यहाँ विचार करनेपर मिलता नहीं क्योंकि इसका न तो आदि है, न अन्त है और न स्थिति ही है ।  इसलिये इस दृढ़ मूलोंवाले संसाररूप अश्वत्थवृक्षको दृढ़ असङ्गतारूप शस्त्रके द्वारा काटकर ॥
bhagwad_gita::554.english_translation: Its form is not perceived here as it truly is: it has no beginning, no end, and no fixed base. Cut down this deeply rooted ashvattha tree with the strong sword of detachment.
bhagwad_gita::554.translation_literal: न (not) / रूपम् (form) / अस्य (of this) / इह (here) / तथा (thus) / उपलभ्यते (is perceived) / न (not) / अन्तः (end) / न (not) / च (and) / आदिः (beginning) / न (not) / च (and) / संप्रतिष्ठा (fixed base) / अश्वत्थम् (ashvattha tree) / एनम् (this) / सु-विरूढ-मूलम् (deeply rooted) / असङ्ग-शस्त्रेण (with the weapon of detachment) / दृढेन (strong) / छित्त्वा (having cut)
bhagwad_gita::554.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::554.essence: What traps you has no fixed form; detachment cuts it cleanly.
bhagwad_gita::554.simple_meaning: The world-tree cannot be grasped as a normal thing, because it has no clear beginning, end, or stable base. Cut through it with firm detachment.
bhagwad_gita::554.simple_insight: What looks solid loses its grip when you stop clinging to it.
bhagwad_gita::554.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna frozen between duty and fear, Krishna explains the world as a vast tree of changing appearances. This verse gives the method: do not try to master it by grasping it; cut through attachment itself.
bhagwad_gita::554.modern_relevance: You keep replaying the breakup, the job offer, the family argument, trying to find the exact point where everything became real. The mind wants a fixed story; this verse says the story itself must be cut loose.
bhagwad_gita::554.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to map life perfectly to severing attachment to appearances.

bhagwad_gita::555.verse_sanskrit: ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्य    यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः । तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये    यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी ॥
bhagwad_gita::555.verse_hindi: उसके बाद उस परमपदपरमात्मा की खोज करनी चाहिये जिसको प्राप्त होनेपर मनुष्य फिर लौटकर संसारमें नहीं आते और जिससे अनादिकालसे चली आनेवाली यह सृष्टि विस्तारको प्राप्त हुई है, उस आदिपुरुष परमात्माके ही मैं शरण हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::555.english_translation: Therefore one should seek that supreme state, reaching which one does not return again. I take refuge in that original Person from whom this ancient creation has spread forth.
bhagwad_gita::555.translation_literal: ततः (therefore) / पदम् (state) / तत् (that) / परिमार्गितव्यम् (should be sought) / यस्मिन् (in which) / गताः (gone) / न (not) / निवर्तन्ति (return) / भूयः (again) / तम् (that) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / आद्यम् (original) / पुरुषम् (Person) / प्रपद्ये (I take refuge) / यतः (from whom) / प्रवृत्तिः (emanation) / प्रसृता (spread forth) / पुराणी (ancient)
bhagwad_gita::555.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::555.essence: The final refuge is a state where return itself stops.
bhagwad_gita::555.simple_meaning: Beyond the changing world lies a supreme state where return stops. Krishna says that state should be sought, and he himself takes refuge in the original Person from whom creation unfolds.
bhagwad_gita::555.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing the deepest search is not endless. Some places in life are meant to end the cycle, not improve it.
bhagwad_gita::555.detailed_meaning: Arjuna stands frozen between two armies while Krishna leads him past the tangled world-tree of change. After showing how to cut free from the lower world, Krishna points to the final destination: the supreme state beyond return, rooted in the original Person.
bhagwad_gita::555.modern_relevance: You keep reopening the same message thread, the same argument, the same regret. At some point you realize the answer is not another round of fixing, but a deeper place to stand.
bhagwad_gita::555.insight: It shifts the mind from managing the cycle to seeking what ends the cycle entirely.

bhagwad_gita::556.verse_sanskrit: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा    अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः । द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै    र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::556.verse_hindi: जो मान और मोहसे रहित हो गये हैं, जिन्होंने आसक्तिसे होनेवाले दोषोंको जीत लिया है, जो नित्यनिरन्तर परमात्मामें ही लगे हुए हैं, जो अपनी दृष्टिसे सम्पूर्ण कामनाओंसे रहित हो गये हैं, जो सुखदुःखरूप द्वन्द्वोंसे मुक्त हो गये हैं, ऐसे ऊँची स्थितिवाले मोहरहित साधक भक्त उस अविनाशी परमपदपरमात्मा को प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::556.english_translation: Free from pride and delusion, victorious over attachment, ever rooted in the true self, desireless, and beyond the opposites of pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach that imperishable state.
bhagwad_gita::556.translation_literal: निर्मानमोहाः (free from pride and delusion) / जितसङ्गदोषाः (who have conquered the fault of attachment) / अध्यात्मनित्याः (ever devoted to the true self) / विनिवृत्तकामाः (whose desires have fully withdrawn) / द्वन्द्वैः (from the pairs of opposites) / विमुक्ताः (freed) / सुखदुःखसंज्ञैः (named pleasure and pain) / गच्छन्ति (they reach) / अमूढाः (the undeluded) / पदम् (state) / अव्ययम् (imperishable) / तत् (that)
bhagwad_gita::556.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::556.essence: Freedom begins when pride, craving, and inner division fall away.
bhagwad_gita::556.simple_meaning: Those who lose pride, cut attachment, stay rooted in the true self, and rise above pleasure and pain reach the imperishable state.
bhagwad_gita::556.simple_insight: Freedom feels less like gaining something and more like losing what kept you divided.
bhagwad_gita::556.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna frozen between duty and grief, Krishna keeps pointing beyond the battlefield. After describing the cosmic tree and the highest abode, he names the inner qualities needed to reach it: no pride, no attachment, no craving, no confusion.
bhagwad_gita::556.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that may end a relationship, or finally leave the safe path that has become false. This verse says clarity arrives when pride, craving, and emotional whiplash stop steering.
bhagwad_gita::556.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing comfort to becoming fit for freedom.

bhagwad_gita::557.verse_sanskrit: न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः । यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
bhagwad_gita::557.verse_hindi: उसपरमपद को न सूर्य, न चन्द्र और न अग्नि ही प्रकाशित कर सकती है और जिसको प्राप्त होकर जीव लौटकर संसारमें नहीं आते, वही मेरा परमधाम है ॥
bhagwad_gita::557.english_translation: The sun, moon, and fire do not illumine that place. Having reached it, one does not return. That supreme abode is Mine.
bhagwad_gita::557.translation_literal: न (not) / तत् (that) / भासयते (illumines) / सूर्यः (the sun) / न (not) / शशाङ्कः (the moon) / न (not) / पावकः (fire) / यत् (which) / गत्वा (having gone) / न (not) / निवर्तन्ते (they return) / तत् (that) / धाम (abode) / परमम् (supreme) / मम (Mine)
bhagwad_gita::557.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::557.essence: The highest home is beyond every ordinary light and beyond return.
bhagwad_gita::557.simple_meaning: Krishna says his highest abode cannot be illuminated by ordinary light, and anyone who reaches it does not come back to the cycle of return.
bhagwad_gita::557.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing the highest goal is beyond ordinary measures and beyond coming back to the same struggle.
bhagwad_gita::557.detailed_meaning: Arjuna stands shaken on the battlefield, and Krishna has been describing the highest reality beyond decay and return. Now Krishna names that goal directly: a supreme abode beyond sun, moon, and fire, reached by those who will not fall back into the cycle.
bhagwad_gita::557.modern_relevance: You leave a hospital room after a final goodbye, and the fluorescent lights feel weak against what just changed. Some thresholds are not about more effort — they are about crossing into a life that cannot be undone.
bhagwad_gita::557.insight: It shifts attention from temporary sources of guidance to the unchanging goal that ends return.

bhagwad_gita::558.verse_sanskrit: ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः । मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥
bhagwad_gita::558.verse_hindi: इस संसारमें जीव बना हुआ आत्मा मेरा ही सनातन अंश है परन्तु वह प्रकृतिमें स्थित मन और पाँचों इन्द्रियोंको आकर्षित करता है अपना मान लेता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::558.english_translation: The embodied being in this world is my eternal part, yet it draws the mind and the five senses, which rest in nature.
bhagwad_gita::558.translation_literal: ममैव (my indeed) / अंशः (part) / जीवलोके (in the world of living beings) / जीवभूतः (become a living being) / सनातनः (eternal) / मनःषष्ठानि (mind as the sixth, together with the five) / इन्द्रियाणि (senses) / प्रकृतिस्थानि (situated in nature) / कर्षति (draws, pulls)
bhagwad_gita::558.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::558.essence: What is eternal gets pulled around by what changes.
bhagwad_gita::558.simple_meaning: The living being is Krishna's eternal part, but it gets pulled by the mind and senses that belong to nature and mistakes them for itself.
bhagwad_gita::558.simple_insight: You are larger than the impulses that tug at you.
bhagwad_gita::558.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, after Krishna has pointed Arjuna toward the supreme abode, he explains why embodied beings still wander. The true self is eternal and related to Krishna, yet the mind and senses, rooted in changing nature, pull it into identification and confusion.
bhagwad_gita::558.modern_relevance: You know the feeling: you meant to stay calm, then one comment, one craving, one memory drags you off center. The verse explains that pull as the mind and senses taking over.
bhagwad_gita::558.insight: It shifts attention from blaming the self to seeing how nature drags awareness into identification.

bhagwad_gita::559.verse_sanskrit: शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः । गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात् ॥
bhagwad_gita::559.verse_hindi: जैसे वायु गन्धके स्थानसे गन्धको ग्रहण करके ले जाती है, ऐसे ही शरीरादिका स्वामी बना हुआ जीवात्मा भी जिस शरीरको छोड़ता है, वहाँसे मनसहित इन्द्रियोंको ग्रहण करके फिर जिस शरीरको प्राप्त होता है, उसमें चला जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::559.english_translation: Just as the wind carries fragrance from its source, the embodied being carries the mind and senses into a new body.
bhagwad_gita::559.translation_literal: शरीरम् (body) / यत् (which) / अवाप्नोति (attains) / यत् (which) / च अपि (and also) / उत्क्रामति (leaves) / ईश्वरः (the lord) / गृहीत्वा (having taken) / एतानि (these) / संयाति (goes forth) / वायुः (wind) / गन्धान् (fragrances) / इव (like) / आशयात् (from a source)
bhagwad_gita::559.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::559.essence: The body changes, but the carried pattern moves on.
bhagwad_gita::559.simple_meaning: The embodied being leaves one body and enters another, carrying the mind and senses along, just as wind carries scent.
bhagwad_gita::559.simple_insight: What moves on is not a fixed personality, but the whole pattern of mind and sense that clings to experience.
bhagwad_gita::559.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, while Arjuna is frozen and Krishna is explaining what truly moves through life and death, the teaching turns subtle. The embodied being does not simply vanish; it carries the mind and senses onward, like wind carrying fragrance from one place to another.
bhagwad_gita::559.modern_relevance: You leave a job, a city, or a relationship, and the same habits travel with you. The outer setting changes fast; the inner pattern arrives first.
bhagwad_gita::559.insight: It shifts attention from the body as the whole self to the carried pattern of mind and senses.

bhagwad_gita::560.verse_sanskrit: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च । अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते ॥
bhagwad_gita::560.verse_hindi: यह जीवात्मा मनका आश्रय लेकर श्रोत्र, नेत्र, त्वचा, रसना और घ्राण  इन पाँचों इन्द्रियोंके द्वारा विषयोंका सेवन करता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::560.english_translation: Taking hold of the mind, the inner being experiences objects through the ears, eyes, skin, tongue, and nose.
bhagwad_gita::560.translation_literal: श्रोत्रम् (ear) / चक्षुः (eye) / स्पर्शनम् (touch) / रसनम् (taste) / घ्राणम् (smell) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / अधिष्ठाय (having taken hold of) / मनः (mind) / च (and) / अयम् (this) / विषयान् (objects) / उपसेवते (enjoys, experiences)
bhagwad_gita::560.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::560.essence: Experience passes through mind and senses; it does not define the true self.
bhagwad_gita::560.simple_meaning: The inner being uses the mind as a base and experiences the world through the five senses.
bhagwad_gita::560.simple_insight: What you call experience is filtered through mind and senses, not raw reality.
bhagwad_gita::560.detailed_meaning: Krishna is explaining to Arjuna why the self seems tied to body and pleasure. After describing how the self moves from one body to another, he adds that it works through mind and the five senses. This verse supports the larger teaching that the true self is not the body.
bhagwad_gita::560.modern_relevance: You scroll, taste, touch, and react, then call it 'me.' But the reaction is moving through your senses and mind, not defining what you are.
bhagwad_gita::560.insight: It shifts attention from sensory experience to the awareness that witnesses it.

bhagwad_gita::561.verse_sanskrit: उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् । विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः ॥
bhagwad_gita::561.verse_hindi: शरीरको छोड़कर जाते हुए या दूसरे शरीरमें स्थित हुए अथवा विषयोंको भोगते हुए भी गुणोंसे युक्त जीवात्माके स्वरूपको मूढ़ मनुष्य नहीं जानते, ज्ञानरूपी नेत्रोंवाले ज्ञानी मनुष्य ही जानते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::561.english_translation: The deluded do not see the inner being departing, staying, or enjoying the world through the qualities. Those with the eye of understanding do see.
bhagwad_gita::561.translation_literal: उत्क्रामन्तम् (departing) / स्थितम् (remaining) / वा (or) / अपि (also) / भुञ्जानम् (enjoying) / वा (or) / गुणान्वितम् (endowed with the qualities) / विमूढाः (the deluded) / न (not) / अनुपश्यन्ति (perceive) / पश्यन्ति (see) / ज्ञानचक्षुषः (those with the eye of knowledge)
bhagwad_gita::561.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::561.essence: What changes is seen by the wise; the true self is not what moves.
bhagwad_gita::561.simple_meaning: Ordinary sight cannot grasp the true self moving through bodies and experiences. Only clear understanding sees what is really happening.
bhagwad_gita::561.simple_insight: It brings relief from identifying with every passing role, state, or sensation.
bhagwad_gita::561.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna explains that the true self is not visible to ordinary perception: it seems to move, stay, and enjoy through changing bodies, but only wisdom can recognize it.
bhagwad_gita::561.modern_relevance: You watch yourself become a different person in every room: child, employee, partner, patient, critic. The verse says the deepest part of you is not any of those shifting masks.
bhagwad_gita::561.insight: It shifts attention from the changing body and moods to the unchanging witness behind them.

bhagwad_gita::562.verse_sanskrit: यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् । यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः ॥
bhagwad_gita::562.verse_hindi: यत्न करनेवाले योगीलोग अपनेआपमें स्थित इस परमात्मतत्त्वका अनुभव करते हैं ।  परन्तु जिन्होंने अपना अन्तःकरण शुद्ध नहीं किया है, ऐसे अविवेकी मनुष्य यत्न करनेपर भी इस तत्त्वका अनुभव नहीं करते ॥
bhagwad_gita::562.english_translation: The striving yogis see this supreme reality abiding in themselves. The unrefined and thoughtless, even while striving, do not see it.
bhagwad_gita::562.translation_literal: यतन्तः (striving) / योगिनः (yogis) / च (and) / एनम् (this) / पश्यन्ति (see) / आत्मनि (in the self) / अवस्थितम् (abiding) । / यतन्तः (striving) / अपि (even) / अकृतात्मानः (those without a purified inner being) / न (not) / एनम् (this) / पश्यन्ति (see) / अचेतसः (the thoughtless)
bhagwad_gita::562.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::562.essence: Seeing the supreme reality depends on inner purification, not effort alone.
bhagwad_gita::562.simple_meaning: People who have disciplined and purified themselves can realize the supreme reality within. Effort without inner refinement is not enough.
bhagwad_gita::562.simple_insight: Real progress feels less like forcing and more like becoming fit to see.
bhagwad_gita::562.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Krishna keeps answering Arjuna’s deeper confusion, not just his fear of fighting. After describing how the inner being moves through bodies and senses, Krishna says only the disciplined can perceive the supreme reality within themselves.
bhagwad_gita::562.modern_relevance: You sit in silence after a fight, trying to understand why the same pattern keeps repeating. More information does not help until your inner state changes enough to see what was hidden.
bhagwad_gita::562.insight: It shifts the goal from trying harder to becoming inwardly clear enough to perceive what is already present.

bhagwad_gita::563.verse_sanskrit: यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् । यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::563.verse_hindi: सूर्यमें आया हुआ जो तेज सम्पूर्ण जगत् को प्रकाशित करता है और जो तेज चन्द्रमामें है तथा जो तेज अग्निमें है, उस तेजको मेरा ही जान ॥
bhagwad_gita::563.english_translation: The radiance in the sun, the moon, and the fire is Mine alone.
bhagwad_gita::563.translation_literal: यत् (which) / आदित्य-गतं (gone into the sun) / तेजः (radiance) / जगत् (the world) / भासयते (illumines) / अखिलम् (entire) / यत् (which) / चन्द्रमसि (in the moon) / यत् (which) / अग्नौ (in fire) / तत् (that) / तेजः (radiance) / विद्धि (know) / मामकम् (Mine)
bhagwad_gita::563.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::563.essence: Every brightness in the world points back to one source.
bhagwad_gita::563.simple_meaning: Krishna says that the light shining in the sun, the moon, and fire belongs to him. All visible brilliance is a sign of his presence.
bhagwad_gita::563.simple_insight: The world feels less random when you notice its brightness has a source.
bhagwad_gita::563.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains how the divine presence runs through all life. Here Krishna points to the most obvious forms of radiance, showing that even the light of the cosmos is not separate from him.
bhagwad_gita::563.modern_relevance: You step outside after a sleepless night and the morning sun still reaches you. The warmth, the glow on water, the flame on your stove — nothing ordinary is truly separate from the source behind it.
bhagwad_gita::563.insight: It shifts attention from isolated objects to the living presence shining through them.

bhagwad_gita::564.verse_sanskrit: गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा । पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः ॥
bhagwad_gita::564.verse_hindi: मैं ही पृथ्वीमें प्रविष्ट होकर अपनी शक्तिसे समस्त प्राणियोंको धारण करता हूँ और मैं ही रसमय चन्द्रमाके रूपमें समस्त ओषधियोंवनस्पतियों को पुष्ट करता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::564.english_translation: Entering the earth, I sustain all beings with my power. Becoming the moon of life-giving essence, I nourish all plants.
bhagwad_gita::564.translation_literal: गाम् (the earth) / आविश्य (entering) / च (and) / भूतानि (beings) / धारयामि (I sustain) / अहम् (I) / ओजसा (with power) / पुष्णामि (I nourish) / च (and) / औषधीः (plants, herbs) / सर्वाः (all) / सोमः (the moon) / भूत्वा (having become) / रसात्मकः (of life-giving essence)
bhagwad_gita::564.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::564.essence: Life is nourished from within by the same presence that holds it together.
bhagwad_gita::564.simple_meaning: Krishna says he enters the earth to support all living beings, and he becomes the moon that nourishes all plants and herbs.
bhagwad_gita::564.simple_insight: The world is not separate from divine support; even ordinary nourishment is held from within.
bhagwad_gita::564.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna reveals how he sustains the world itself. The same presence that fills the earth with strength also becomes the moon’s nourishing essence for plants. This verse is one link in Krishna’s larger explanation of his universal presence.
bhagwad_gita::564.modern_relevance: You water a dying plant on a kitchen sill and think it is a small act. This verse says even that life-giving moisture, firmness, and growth are already held by the divine presence.
bhagwad_gita::564.insight: It shifts attention from isolated objects to the sustaining presence running through them all.

bhagwad_gita::565.verse_sanskrit: अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः । प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::565.verse_hindi: प्राणियोंके शरीरमें रहनेवाला मैं प्राणअपानसे युक्त वैश्वानर होकर चार प्रकारके अन्नको पचाता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::565.english_translation: I become the digestive fire within living beings, joined with the outgoing and incoming breaths, and digest the four kinds of food.
bhagwad_gita::565.translation_literal: अहम् (I) / वैश्वानरः (the digestive fire) / भूत्वा (having become) / प्राणिनाम् (of living beings) / देहम् (the body) / आश्रितः (dwelling in) / प्राण-अपान-समायुक्तः (joined with the inward and outward breaths) / पचामि (I digest) / अन्नम् (food) / चतुर्विधम् (of four kinds)
bhagwad_gita::565.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::565.essence: The divine is already working inside your body as life itself.
bhagwad_gita::565.simple_meaning: Krishna says he lives inside every body as the force that digests food, working through the breaths that sustain life.
bhagwad_gita::565.simple_insight: Ordinary bodily life is not separate from the divine presence.
bhagwad_gita::565.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna still stands frozen while Krishna explains how the supreme reality is present everywhere. After speaking of light, earth, and nourishment, Krishna says he also works inside every living body as the fire that digests food.
bhagwad_gita::565.modern_relevance: You sit at a table after a hard day, too tired to think, and your body still quietly does its work. Even that hidden, ordinary functioning is not outside the sacred.
bhagwad_gita::565.insight: It shifts attention from a distant divinity to the living processes already sustaining you.

bhagwad_gita::566.verse_sanskrit: सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो    मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च । वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो    वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::566.verse_hindi: मैं सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके हृदयमें स्थित हूँ ।  मेरेसे ही स्मृति, ज्ञान और अपोहन संशय आदि दोषोंका नाश होता है ।  सम्पूर्ण वेदोंके द्वारा मैं ही जाननेयोग्य हूँ ।  वेदोंके तत्त्वका निर्णय करनेवाला और वेदोंको जाननेवाला भी मैं ही हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::566.english_translation: I dwell in the hearts of all beings. Memory, knowledge, and removal of doubt come from Me. I am the one known through all the Vedas, the maker of Vedanta, and the knower of the Vedas.
bhagwad_gita::566.translation_literal: सर्वस्य (of all) / च (and) / अहम् (I) / हृदि (in the heart) / सन्निविष्टः (dwelling) / मत्तः (from Me) / स्मृतिः (memory) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / अपोहनम् (removal) / च (and) / वेदैः (through the Vedas) / च (and) / सर्वैः (all) / अहम् (I) / एव (indeed) / वेद्यः (to be known) / वेदान्तकृत् (maker of Vedanta) / वेदविद् (knower of the Vedas) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / अहम् (I)
bhagwad_gita::566.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::566.essence: The deepest knowing comes from the one already dwelling within every heart.
bhagwad_gita::566.simple_meaning: Krishna says He lives in every being’s heart. Memory, understanding, and the clearing of confusion come from Him. All the Vedas point to Him, and He is their final knower.
bhagwad_gita::566.simple_insight: You are not left to figure life out alone; the deepest clarity is already near you.
bhagwad_gita::566.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen and Krishna keeps expanding the teaching. After showing how He sustains life in the world, Krishna now reveals that He also lives in every heart, giving memory, understanding, and the clearing of confusion. Even the Vedas point back to Him.
bhagwad_gita::566.modern_relevance: You sit awake after a painful conversation, replaying every sentence and doubting your own judgment. This verse says the mind’s clarity is not manufactured by strain alone; it can be received from a deeper center.
bhagwad_gita::566.insight: It shifts attention from scattered mental effort to a deeper source of remembrance and discernment.

bhagwad_gita::567.verse_sanskrit: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च । क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::567.verse_hindi: इस संसारमें क्षर नाशवान् और अक्षर अविनाशी  ये दो प्रकारके पुरुष हैं ।  सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके शरीर नाशवान् और कूटस्थ जीवात्मा अविनाशी कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::567.english_translation: In this world, there are two kinds of beings: the perishable and the imperishable. All embodied beings are perishable; the steadfast one is called imperishable.
bhagwad_gita::567.translation_literal: द्वौ (two) / इमौ (these) / पुरुषौ (beings) / लोके (in the world) / क्षरः (perishable) / च (and) / अक्षरः (imperishable) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / क्षरः (perishable) / सर्वाणि (all) / भूतानि (beings) / कूटस्थः (steadfast) / अक्षरः (imperishable) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::567.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::567.essence: What changes is not the whole of you.
bhagwad_gita::567.simple_meaning: There are two kinds of existence here: what changes and what does not. Bodies pass away, but the unchanging reality within remains.
bhagwad_gita::567.simple_insight: You can stop clinging to what fades and rest in what does not.
bhagwad_gita::567.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna widens the frame beyond the war: all bodies are temporary, but the steady reality within them is not. This verse prepares Arjuna to act without mistaking the body for the whole person.
bhagwad_gita::567.modern_relevance: You watch a loved one age in a hospital room and feel time stripping everything away. This verse reminds you that what changes is not the deepest reality of a person.
bhagwad_gita::567.insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with the changing body to recognising the unchanging witness.

bhagwad_gita::568.verse_sanskrit: उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः । यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः ॥
bhagwad_gita::568.verse_hindi: उत्तम पुरुष तो अन्य ही है, जो परमात्मा नामसे कहा गया है ।  वही अविनाशी ईश्वर तीनों लोकोंमें प्रविष्ट होकर सबका भरणपोषण करता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::568.english_translation: The Supreme Self is beyond both the perishable and the imperishable. The imperishable ruler enters the three worlds and sustains them all.
bhagwad_gita::568.translation_literal: उत्तमः (supreme) / पुरुषः (person/self) / तु (indeed) / अन्यः (other) / परमात्मा (supreme self) / इति (thus) / उदाहृतः (is called) । / यः (who) / लोकत्रयम् (the three worlds) / आविश्य (entering) / बिभर्ति (sustains) / अव्ययः (imperishable) / ईश्वरः (ruler)
bhagwad_gita::568.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::568.essence: Even the imperishable witness is not the final reality.
bhagwad_gita::568.simple_meaning: Beyond the changing world and even beyond the unchanging witness stands the highest reality, which enters all three worlds and sustains them.
bhagwad_gita::568.simple_insight: What seems highest is still not the highest. There is a greater presence holding everything together.
bhagwad_gita::568.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is being led through the structure of existence itself. Krishna has already distinguished the changing body from the imperishable witness, and now points higher still: beyond both stands the Supreme Self, the sustaining ruler of all three worlds.
bhagwad_gita::568.modern_relevance: You can understand your thoughts, your habits, even your calm — and still miss the deepest source holding your life together. The mind can map the landscape and never notice the ground beneath it.
bhagwad_gita::568.insight: It shifts the mind from identifying with the imperishable witness to recognising the supreme source that sustains all experience.

bhagwad_gita::569.verse_sanskrit: यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः । अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
bhagwad_gita::569.verse_hindi: मैं क्षरसे अतीत हूँ और अक्षरसे भी उत्तम हूँ, इसलिये लोकमें और वेदमें पुरुषोत्तम नामसे प्रसिद्ध हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::569.english_translation: I am beyond the perishable and even beyond the imperishable. Therefore, I am known in the world and in the Vedas as Purushottama, the Supreme Self.
bhagwad_gita::569.translation_literal: यस्मात् (because) / क्षरम् (the perishable) / अतीतः (beyond) / अहम् (I) / अक्षरात् (than the imperishable) / अपि (also) / च (and) / उत्तमः (higher) / अतः (therefore) / अस्मि (I am) / लोके (in the world) / वेदे (in the Veda) / च (and) / प्रथितः (well known) / पुरुषोत्तमः (Purushottama)
bhagwad_gita::569.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::569.essence: The highest reality lies beyond both change and permanence.
bhagwad_gita::569.simple_meaning: Krishna says he is beyond both the changing world and the unchanging principle behind it. That is why he is called the Supreme Self.
bhagwad_gita::569.simple_insight: Reality is larger than both what fades and what seems permanent.
bhagwad_gita::569.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna has been leading him through the deepest levels of reality. After explaining the perishable, the imperishable, and the supreme being beyond both, Krishna now names himself as that highest reality.
bhagwad_gita::569.modern_relevance: You finally reach the thing you thought would settle everything — the title, the relationship, the achievement — and it still feels incomplete. Krishna points beyond every stopping place.
bhagwad_gita::569.insight: It shifts the mind from settling for any limited identity to recognising the highest reality beyond all categories.

bhagwad_gita::570.verse_sanskrit: यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् । स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत ॥
bhagwad_gita::570.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशी अर्जुन  इस प्रकार जो मोहरहित मनुष्य मुझे पुरुषोत्तम जानता है, वह सर्वज्ञ सब प्रकारसे मेरा ही भजन करता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::570.english_translation: Arjuna, the one who is free from confusion and knows Me as the Supreme Self, worships Me with all his being.
bhagwad_gita::570.translation_literal: यः (who) / माम् (Me) / एवम् (thus) / असम्मूढः (not deluded) / जानाति (knows) / पुरुषोत्तमम् (as the Supreme Self) / सः (that one) / सर्ववित् (all-knowing) / भजति (worships) / माम् (Me) / सर्वभावेन (with all being) / भारत (O Bharata)
bhagwad_gita::570.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::570.essence: Clear seeing of the Supreme Self becomes total devotion.
bhagwad_gita::570.simple_meaning: Knowing Krishna as the Supreme Self removes confusion and leads to wholehearted devotion. Clear understanding and complete worship become one movement.
bhagwad_gita::570.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that true understanding and true devotion do not compete.
bhagwad_gita::570.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, after Krishna has revealed the Supreme Self beyond the changing and the unchanging, he tells Arjuna that clear knowing is not dry theory. The one who truly sees Krishna as Purushottama worships him with complete devotion.
bhagwad_gita::570.modern_relevance: You finally understand someone’s character after a long conflict, and your resistance drops. What was once mixed with doubt becomes wholehearted respect and trust.
bhagwad_gita::570.insight: It shifts devotion from blind feeling to total response grounded in clear seeing.

bhagwad_gita::571.verse_sanskrit: इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयाऽनघ । एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत ॥
bhagwad_gita::571.verse_hindi: हे निष्पाप अर्जुन  इस प्रकार यह अत्यन्त गोपनीय शास्त्र मेरे द्वारा कहा गया है ।  हे भरतवंशी अर्जुन  इसको जानकर मनुष्य ज्ञानवान् तथा प्राप्तप्राप्तव्य और कृतकृत्य हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::571.english_translation: O sinless Arjuna, thus this most secret teaching has been spoken by Me. Knowing this, a person becomes wise and has accomplished all that must be done, O descendant of Bharata.
bhagwad_gita::571.translation_literal: इति (thus) / गुह्यतमम् (most secret) / शास्त्रम् (teaching) / इदम् (this) / उक्तम् (spoken) / मया (by me) / अनघ (O sinless one) / एतत् (this) / बुद्ध्वा (having known) / बुद्धिमान् (wise) / स्यात् (becomes) / कृतकृत्यः (one who has done what must be done) / च (and) / भारत (O descendant of Bharata)
bhagwad_gita::571.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::571.essence: Secret knowledge makes a person complete.
bhagwad_gita::571.simple_meaning: Krishna says he has shared the most hidden teaching. A person who truly understands it becomes wise and feels complete, with nothing essential left undone.
bhagwad_gita::571.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that real understanding can end inner incompleteness.
bhagwad_gita::571.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, after revealing the supreme self and the secret of liberation, Krishna closes the teaching. Arjuna stands at the edge of war, and Krishna says this knowledge is not just information — it is the completion of a human life.
bhagwad_gita::571.modern_relevance: You finish the hardest conversation of your life and sit in silence afterward, knowing the truth has finally been said. Some understandings do not add more to you; they make you whole.
bhagwad_gita::571.insight: It shifts the mind from collecting ideas to recognising the kind of understanding that completes action and ends doubt.

bhagwad_gita::572.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचअभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः । दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::572.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  भयका सर्वथा अभाव अन्तःकरणकी शुद्धि ज्ञानके लिये योगमें दृढ़ स्थिति सात्त्विक दान इन्द्रियोंका दमन यज्ञ स्वाध्याय कर्तव्यपालनके लिये कष्ट सहना शरीरमनवाणीकी सरलता ॥
bhagwad_gita::572.english_translation: Fearlessness, purity of mind, steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge, generosity, self-control, sacrifice, study of the sacred texts, austerity, and straightforwardness.
bhagwad_gita::572.translation_literal: अभयम् (fearlessness) / सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः (purity of being) / ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः (steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge) / दानम् (giving) / दमः (self-control) / च (and) / यज्ञः (sacrifice) / च (and) / स्वाध्यायः (study of sacred texts) / तपः (austerity) / आर्जवम् (straightforwardness)
bhagwad_gita::572.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::572.essence: Right action starts with disciplined character.
bhagwad_gita::572.simple_meaning: A divine life begins with fearlessness, inner purity, self-control, generosity, sacrifice, study, disciplined effort, and honesty.
bhagwad_gita::572.simple_insight: A strong character is built, not wished into existence.
bhagwad_gita::572.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna begins listing the qualities that belong to a life shaped by the divine. Arjuna needs more than courage to fight; he needs a character strong enough to act rightly under pressure.
bhagwad_gita::572.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message, walk into the meeting, or tell the truth that may change everything. Before the outcome, the verse asks for steadiness, honesty, and self-mastery.
bhagwad_gita::572.insight: It shifts attention from winning approval to building the qualities that make right action possible.

bhagwad_gita::573.verse_sanskrit: अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् । दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::573.verse_hindi: अहिंसा, सत्यभाषण क्रोध न करना संसारकी कामनाका त्याग अन्तःकरणमें रागद्वेषजनित हलचलका न होना चुगली न करना प्राणियोंपर दया करना सांसारिक विषयोंमें न ललचाना अन्तःकरणकी कोमलता अकर्तव्य करनेमें लज्जा चपलताका अभाव ॥
bhagwad_gita::573.english_translation: Nonviolence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, inner calm, absence of slander, compassion for all beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, and absence of restlessness.
bhagwad_gita::573.translation_literal: अहिंसा (nonviolence) / सत्य (truth) / अक्रोधः (freedom from anger) / त्यागः (renunciation) / शान्तिः (calm) / अपैशुनम् (absence of slander) / दया (compassion) / भूतेषु (toward beings) / अलोलुप्त्वम् (freedom from greed) / मार्दवम् (gentleness) / ह्रीः (modesty) / अचापलम् (absence of restlessness)
bhagwad_gita::573.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::573.essence: A noble character is proven by how gently it reacts.
bhagwad_gita::573.simple_meaning: A divine life is built from nonviolence, honesty, calm, compassion, restraint, and modest conduct.
bhagwad_gita::573.simple_insight: Virtue is not one grand gesture. It is a steady character that shows up in small reactions.
bhagwad_gita::573.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna continues listing the qualities that mark a noble nature. Arjuna is frozen between duty and fear, and this verse gives him the inner standards that make right action possible.
bhagwad_gita::573.modern_relevance: You are about to send the angry message, repeat the gossip, or take the easy shortcut. This verse asks for a different reflex: soften, tell the truth, and stop the spiral.
bhagwad_gita::573.insight: It trains the mind to replace impulse with restraint, and reaction with humane conduct.

bhagwad_gita::574.verse_sanskrit: तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता । भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत ॥
bhagwad_gita::574.verse_hindi: तेज प्रभाव, क्षमा, धैर्य, शरीरकी शुद्धि, वैरभावका न रहना और मानको न चाहना, हे भरतवंशी अर्जुन  ये सभी दैवी सम्पदाको प्राप्त हुए मनुष्यके लक्षण हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::574.english_translation: Splendor, forgiveness, steadiness, purity, absence of hostility, and lack of pride belong to the one born with divine qualities, O Bharata.
bhagwad_gita::574.translation_literal: तेजः (splendor) / क्षमा (forgiveness) / धृतिः (steadiness) / शौचम् (purity) / अद्रोहः (absence of hostility) / नातिमानिता (lack of pride) / भवन्ति (become) / सम्पदम् (attainment) / दैवीम् (divine) / अभिजातस्य (of one born) / भारत (O Bharata)
bhagwad_gita::574.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::574.essence: True strength looks like forgiveness, steadiness, and no need to dominate.
bhagwad_gita::574.simple_meaning: A person with noble qualities shows strength, forgiveness, steadiness, purity, no hostility, and no pride.
bhagwad_gita::574.simple_insight: You can measure character by how powerfully someone stays gentle.
