bhagwad_gita::574.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna is listing the qualities that mark a truly noble person. After naming nonviolence, truth, and self-control, he adds the traits that make divine character visible in action.
bhagwad_gita::574.modern_relevance: A tense family dinner turns sharp, and everyone is waiting for you to strike back. This verse says real strength can stay clean, calm, and uninflated under pressure.
bhagwad_gita::574.insight: It shifts attention from outer success to the inner traits that reveal a disciplined character.

bhagwad_gita::575.verse_sanskrit: दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च । अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::575.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन  दम्भ करना, घमण्ड करना, अभिमान करना, क्रोध करना, कठोरता रखना और अविवेकका होना भी  ये सभी आसुरीसम्पदाको प्राप्त हुए मनुष्यके लक्षण हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::575.english_translation: O son of Pritha, hypocrisy, arrogance, self-importance, anger, harshness, and ignorance are the marks of one born with demonic qualities.
bhagwad_gita::575.translation_literal: दम्भः (hypocrisy) / दर्पः (arrogance) / अभिमानः (self-importance) / च (and) / क्रोधः (anger) / पारुष्यम् (harshness) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / अज्ञानम् (ignorance) / च (and) / अभिजातस्य (of one born) / पार्थ (O Partha) / सम्पदम् (qualities) / आसुरीम् (demonic)
bhagwad_gita::575.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::575.essence: False pride and cruelty reveal a nature already turned away from wisdom.
bhagwad_gita::575.simple_meaning: False display, pride, self-importance, anger, harsh speech, and ignorance are signs of a destructive nature.
bhagwad_gita::575.simple_insight: It feels clarifying to name the habits that poison character before they harden into identity.
bhagwad_gita::575.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna has just described the qualities of a noble nature. Now he turns to Arjuna and names the opposite pattern: hypocrisy, pride, anger, cruelty, and ignorance. The contrast prepares Arjuna to see what kind of life leads to bondage.
bhagwad_gita::575.modern_relevance: In a tense family argument, someone smiles politely while cutting you down, then explodes when challenged. The verse names that mix of pride, cruelty, and blindness for what it is.
bhagwad_gita::575.insight: It teaches you to spot character by recurring reactions, not by polished appearances.

bhagwad_gita::576.verse_sanskrit: दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता । मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव ॥
bhagwad_gita::576.verse_hindi: दैवीसम्पत्ति मुक्तिके लिये और आसुरीसम्पत्ति बन्धनके लिये है ।  हे पाण्डव तुम दैवीसम्पत्तिको प्राप्त हुए हो, इसलिये तुम्हें शोक चिन्ता नहीं करना चाहिये ॥
bhagwad_gita::576.english_translation: The divine nature leads to freedom; the demonic nature leads to bondage. Do not grieve, Pandava. You are born with the divine nature.
bhagwad_gita::576.translation_literal: दैवी (divine) / सम्पत् (nature or wealth) / विमोक्षाय (for freedom) / निबन्धाय (for bondage) / आसुरी (demonic) / मता (is held to be) / मा (do not) / शुचः (grieve) / सम्पदम् (nature or wealth) / दैवीम् (divine) / अभिजातः (born with) / असि (you are) / पाण्डव (Pandava)
bhagwad_gita::576.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::576.essence: Freedom grows from one kind of character; bondage grows from another.
bhagwad_gita::576.simple_meaning: Qualities that uplift a person lead to freedom, while qualities rooted in ego create bondage. Krishna tells Arjuna not to despair, because Arjuna already has the qualities that lead upward.
bhagwad_gita::576.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing your deeper orientation already points toward freedom.
bhagwad_gita::576.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, after listing the traits of the divine and the demonic, Krishna turns to Arjuna directly. The battlefield is still frozen, but the teaching sharpens: Arjuna is not trapped by fear. His deeper nature already belongs to the side that frees.
bhagwad_gita::576.modern_relevance: You catch yourself spiralling after a harsh conversation, wondering whether you are becoming the kind of person you fear. This verse says to stop and remember what you are already leaning toward.
bhagwad_gita::576.insight: It shifts attention from self-doubt to the qualities you are cultivating, so you can align with what frees rather than what binds.

bhagwad_gita::577.verse_sanskrit: द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन् दैव आसुर एव च । दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे श्रृणु ॥
bhagwad_gita::577.verse_hindi: इस लोकमें दो तरहके प्राणियोंकी सृष्टि है  दैवी और आसुरी ।  दैवीका तो मैंने विस्तारसे वर्णन कर दिया, अब हे पार्थ  तुम मेरेसे आसुरीका विस्तार सुनो ॥
bhagwad_gita::577.english_translation: In this world there are two kinds of beings: the divine and the shadowed. I have already described the divine in detail; now listen to the shadowed, Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::577.translation_literal: द्वौ (two) / भूतसर्गौ (classes of beings) / लोकेऽस्मिन् (in this world) / दैवः (divine) / आसुरः (shadowed) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / दैवः (the divine) / विस्तरशः (in detail) / प्रोक्तः (has been spoken) / आसुरम् (the shadowed) / पार्थ (Arjuna) / मे (from me) / श्रृणु (listen)
bhagwad_gita::577.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::577.essence: Human life divides by inner orientation, not by appearance.
bhagwad_gita::577.simple_meaning: Krishna says there are two broad kinds of human nature: one shaped by clarity and virtue, the other by ego and confusion. He has already explained the first and now turns to the second.
bhagwad_gita::577.simple_insight: It helps you see that character is not random. The way you live reveals which current is shaping you.
bhagwad_gita::577.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Krishna is not just answering Arjuna’s fear of fighting; he is diagnosing the deeper forces that drive human behavior. After describing the divine qualities, he now introduces the opposite pattern so Arjuna can recognize it clearly.
bhagwad_gita::577.modern_relevance: You watch a group chat turn cruel in minutes, and one voice keeps escalating everything. This verse helps you name the pattern: not every reaction comes from the same kind of character.
bhagwad_gita::577.insight: It shifts attention from judging isolated actions to seeing the underlying nature behind them.

bhagwad_gita::578.verse_sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः । न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::578.verse_hindi: आसुरी प्रकृतिवाले मनुष्य प्रवृत्ति और निवृत्तिको नहीं जानते और उनमें न बाह्यशुद्धि, न श्रेष्ठ आचरण तथा न सत्यपालन ही होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::578.english_translation: People of a shadowed nature do not know what should be pursued and what should be withdrawn from. In them, there is no purity, no noble conduct, and no truthfulness.
bhagwad_gita::578.translation_literal: प्रवृत्तिं (what should be pursued) / च (and) / निवृत्तिं (what should be withdrawn from) / च (and) / जना (people) / न (not) / विदुः (know) / असुराः (those of shadowed nature) / न (not) / शौचं (purity) / न (not) / अपि (also) / च (and) / आचारः (noble conduct) / न (not) / सत्यं (truthfulness) / तेषु (in them) / विद्यते (exists)
bhagwad_gita::578.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::578.essence: Without discernment, conduct collapses and truth disappears.
bhagwad_gita::578.simple_meaning: A shadowed nature cannot tell right action from wrong withdrawal. It also lacks purity, good conduct, and honesty.
bhagwad_gita::578.simple_insight: You can judge a person by what they consistently fail to honor: restraint, cleanliness, conduct, and truth.
bhagwad_gita::578.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna continues describing the shadowed temperament to Arjuna. After naming the two kinds of human nature, he now shows how the destructive one behaves: it cannot discern what to do or avoid, and it loses basic integrity.
bhagwad_gita::578.modern_relevance: A group chat turns ugly, and someone keeps feeding it with half-truths, sloppy boundaries, and impulsive replies. The problem is not one mistake — it is a pattern of inner disorder.
bhagwad_gita::578.insight: It trains you to measure character by discernment and basic self-restraint, not by charm or ambition.

bhagwad_gita::579.verse_hindi: वे कहा करते हैं कि संसार असत्य, अप्रतिष्ठित और बिना ईश्वरके अपनेआप केवल स्त्रीपुरुषके संयोगसे पैदा हुआ है ।  इसलिये काम ही इसका कारण है, और कोई कारण नहीं है ॥
bhagwad_gita::579.english_translation: They say the world is unreal, without foundation, and without a ruling order, born only from the union of male and female. They say desire alone is its cause, and nothing else.
bhagwad_gita::579.translation_literal: असत्यम् (untrue) / अप्रतिष्ठम् (without foundation) / ते (they) / जगत् (world) / आहुः (say) / अनीश्वरम् (without a ruling lord) / अपरस्परसम्भूतम् (born without mutual cause) / किम् अन्यत् (what else) / कामहैतुकम् (caused by desire) ॥
bhagwad_gita::579.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::579.essence: Cynical explanations of life can become a permission slip for harmful action.
bhagwad_gita::579.simple_meaning: Some people deny any higher order in the world. They reduce existence to chance, physical union, and desire alone.
bhagwad_gita::579.simple_insight: A shallow explanation can feel confident and still miss what is most real.
bhagwad_gita::579.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna is exposing the mindset behind destructive action. After naming the traits of the asuric person, he shows how such people explain the world itself: no higher order, no moral foundation, only desire and accident. This prepares the warning in the next verse.
bhagwad_gita::579.modern_relevance: A friend shrugs at betrayal and says, “People are just wired this way.” That sentence can sound clever, but it can also erase responsibility and flatten the whole moral world.
bhagwad_gita::579.insight: It shifts the mind from cynical reduction to seeing that beliefs about reality shape conduct.

bhagwad_gita::580.verse_sanskrit: एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः । प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::580.verse_hindi: उपर्युक्त नास्तिक दृष्टिका आश्रय लेनेवाले जो मनुष्य अपने नित्य स्वरूपको नहीं मानते, जिनकी बुद्धि तुच्छ है, जो उग्रकर्मा और संसारके शत्रु हैं, उन मनुष्योंकी सामर्थ्यका उपयोग जगत्का नाश करनेके लिये ही होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::580.english_translation: Holding this view, deluded people with ruined discernment and fierce actions arise only to destroy the world.
bhagwad_gita::580.translation_literal: एताम् (this) / दृष्टिम् (view) / अवष्टभ्य (holding) / नष्टात्मानः (those whose inner being is lost) / अल्पबुद्धयः (those of little discernment) / प्रभवन्ति (arise) / उग्रकर्माणः (fierce in action) / क्षयाय (for destruction) / जगतः (of the world) / अहिताः (harmful ones)
bhagwad_gita::580.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::580.essence: False vision turns strength into destruction.
bhagwad_gita::580.simple_meaning: People who deny their true nature and cling to a false view become small-minded and destructive. Their energy turns toward harming the world instead of serving it.
bhagwad_gita::580.simple_insight: A false view does not stay private; it eventually shapes harmful action.
bhagwad_gita::580.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield at Kurukshetra, where the moral stakes are absolute. After describing the asuric mindset, he shows its outcome: once people lose sight of their true nature, their intelligence shrinks and their force becomes destructive.
bhagwad_gita::580.modern_relevance: A person who keeps feeding cynicism, contempt, and denial of responsibility may start with words, then wreck a family, a team, or a community without noticing the damage.
bhagwad_gita::580.insight: It shifts attention from judging bad behavior alone to seeing the false belief that generates it.

bhagwad_gita::581.verse_hindi: कभी पूरी न होनेवाली कामनाओंका आश्रय लेकर दम्भ, अभिमान और मदमें चूर रहनेवाले तथा अपवित्र व्रत धारण करनेवाले मनुष्य मोहके कारण दुराग्रहोंको धारण करके संसारमें विचरते रहते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::581.english_translation: Taking refuge in desires that can never be filled, filled with hypocrisy, pride, and intoxication, they wander under delusion, holding onto impure vows and false beliefs.
bhagwad_gita::581.translation_literal: कामम् (desire) / आश्रित्य (taking refuge in) / दुष्पूरम् (hard to fill, never fully satisfied) / दम्भ-मान-मदान्विताः (endowed with hypocrisy, pride, and intoxication) / मोहात् (through delusion) / गृहीत्वा (having grasped) / असत्-ग्राहान् (false beliefs, false graspings) / प्रवर्तन्ते (they keep moving) / अशुचि-व्रताः (those with impure vows)
bhagwad_gita::581.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::581.essence: Endless wanting turns the mind into a home for delusion.
bhagwad_gita::581.simple_meaning: People trapped by endless wanting become arrogant, deluded, and stubborn. Their lives keep moving, but they keep holding on to false ideas and impure aims.
bhagwad_gita::581.simple_insight: It feels sobering: unchecked wanting does not just distract you; it distorts your character.
bhagwad_gita::581.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen while Krishna explains what corrupts human judgment. After naming false views in the previous verses, Krishna shows how delusion becomes a way of living: craving, arrogance, and stubborn beliefs keep people moving toward ruin.
bhagwad_gita::581.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing the message thread, hoping the next reply will settle you. Instead, the wanting grows, and with it the need to look right, feel superior, and cling harder.
bhagwad_gita::581.insight: It shifts attention from external success to the hidden habits that deform judgment.

bhagwad_gita::582.verse_sanskrit: चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः । कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्िचताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::582.verse_hindi: वे मृत्युपर्यन्त रहनेवाली अपार चिन्ताओंका आश्रय लेनेवाले, पदार्थोंका संग्रह और उनका भोग करनेमें ही लगे रहनेवाले और जो कुछ है, वह इतना ही है  ऐसा निश्चय करनेवाले होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::582.english_translation: They take refuge in endless worries that last until death, live only for acquiring and enjoying things, and decide that this is all there is.
bhagwad_gita::582.translation_literal: चिन्ताम् (worry) / अपरिमेयाम् (immeasurable) / च (and) / प्रलयान्ताम् (lasting until dissolution/death) / उपाश्रिताः (taking refuge in) / कामोपभोग-परमाः (for whom desire-enjoyment is the highest) / एतावत् (so much only) / इति (thus) / निश्चिताः (deciding firmly)
bhagwad_gita::582.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::582.essence: Endless wanting turns life into a tunnel with no horizon.
bhagwad_gita::582.simple_meaning: People trapped in desire live with endless worry, chase possessions and pleasure, and conclude that material life is all that exists.
bhagwad_gita::582.simple_insight: You can see how craving shrinks a whole life into anxiety and appetite.
bhagwad_gita::582.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna is exposing the inner life of the hostile forces before Arjuna. He describes people who cling to worry, pleasure, and possession as if nothing higher exists. This verse deepens that diagnosis.
bhagwad_gita::582.modern_relevance: You scroll past midnight, checking prices, messages, and comparisons, convinced you still need one more thing. The mind keeps asking for more, and never feels full.
bhagwad_gita::582.insight: It shifts attention from chasing accumulation to noticing how desire manufactures anxiety.

bhagwad_gita::583.verse_hindi: वे आशाकी सैकड़ों फाँसियोंसे बँधे हुए मनुष्य कामक्रोधके परायण होकर पदार्थोंका भोग करनेके लिये अन्यायपूर्वक धनसंचय करनेकी चेष्टा करते रहते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::583.english_translation: Bound by hundreds of cords of hope, driven by desire and anger, they strive to gather wealth unjustly for the enjoyment of desires.
bhagwad_gita::583.translation_literal: आशापाशशतैः (by hundreds of cords of hope) / बद्धाः (bound) / कामक्रोधपरायणाः (devoted to desire and anger) / ईहन्ते (they strive) / कामभोगार्थम् (for the sake of enjoyment of desire) / अन्यायेन (unjustly) / अर्थसञ्चयान् (accumulations of wealth)
bhagwad_gita::583.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::583.essence: Desire and anger turn ambition into injustice.
bhagwad_gita::583.simple_meaning: Endless hopes trap people. Desire and anger drive them to gather wealth by unfair means just to feed more wanting.
bhagwad_gita::583.simple_insight: You can see how craving multiplies itself until fairness no longer matters.
bhagwad_gita::583.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, while Arjuna stands frozen, Krishna describes the inner life of those ruled by the lower nature: trapped by countless hopes, pushed by craving and rage, they chase wealth through injustice. This verse shows the behavior behind that blindness.
bhagwad_gita::583.modern_relevance: A person cuts corners, hides numbers, and calls it ambition. The hunger for more has already turned into a cage.
bhagwad_gita::583.insight: It shifts attention from outward success to the inner forces that corrupt it.

bhagwad_gita::584.verse_sanskrit: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् । इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::584.verse_hindi: इतनी वस्तुएँ तो हमने आज प्राप्त कर लीं और अब इस मनोरथको प्राप्त पूरा कर लेंगे । ,इतना धन तो हमारे पास है ही, इतना धन फिर हो जायगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::584.english_translation: This much I have gained today; I will get this desire fulfilled. This wealth is mine now, and more will be mine again.
bhagwad_gita::584.translation_literal: इदम् (this) / अद्य (today) / मया (by me) / लब्धम् (gained) / इमम् (this) / प्राप्स्ये (I will obtain) / मनोरथम् (desired wish) / इदम् (this) / अस्ति (is) / इदम् (this) / अपि (also) / मे (of me) / भविष्यति (will be) / पुनः (again) / धनम् (wealth)
bhagwad_gita::584.speaker: Unknown
bhagwad_gita::584.essence: Possession feeds appetite when the mind mistakes gain for completion.
bhagwad_gita::584.simple_meaning: A deluded person keeps thinking, “I have gained this, I will get more, and this wealth will keep increasing.”
bhagwad_gita::584.simple_insight: Possession can become a trap when the mind keeps turning gain into hunger.
bhagwad_gita::584.detailed_meaning: Krishna is exposing the inner speech of the demonic-minded person after describing greed, rage, and unfair gain. The speaker is not a hero in battle but a mind trapped in endless acquisition, convinced that today’s gain will lead to tomorrow’s.
bhagwad_gita::584.modern_relevance: You check your account after a bonus and immediately start planning the next purchase, the next upgrade, the next win. The mind never says, enough.
bhagwad_gita::584.insight: It reveals how greed multiplies itself by turning every gain into proof that more is owed.

bhagwad_gita::585.verse_sanskrit: असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि । ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी ॥
bhagwad_gita::585.verse_hindi: वह शत्रु तो हमारे द्वारा मारा गया और उन दूसरे शत्रुओंको भी हम मार डालेंगे ।  हम सर्वसमर्थ हैं ।  हमारे पास भोगसामग्री बहुत है ।  हम सिद्ध हैं ।  हम बड़े बलवान् और सुखी हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::585.english_translation: That enemy has been slain by me, and I will slay the others too. I am the lord, I enjoy, I am accomplished, powerful, and happy.
bhagwad_gita::585.translation_literal: असौ (that) / मया (by me) / हतः (slain) / शत्रुः (enemy) / हनिष्ये (I will slay) / च (and) / अपरान् (others) / अपि (also) / ईश्वरः (lord) / अहम् (I) / अहम् (I) / भोगी (enjoyer) / सिद्धः (accomplished) / अहम् (I) / बलवान् (powerful) / सुखी (happy)
bhagwad_gita::585.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::585.essence: Ego turns achievement into delusion and mistakes possession for mastery.
bhagwad_gita::585.simple_meaning: Pride speaks through the arrogant mind: it claims victory, power, pleasure, success, and happiness as its own.
bhagwad_gita::585.simple_insight: Seeing this kind of self-inflation clearly helps you spot ego before it turns into harm.
bhagwad_gita::585.detailed_meaning: Krishna is listing the inner speech of people trapped in arrogant confusion. After boasting of wealth and plans, they now claim victory, mastery, enjoyment, and strength as if all of it belongs to them. This exposes the blindness that drives destructive action.
bhagwad_gita::585.modern_relevance: After one successful deal, someone starts talking like nothing can stop them. The next decision gets made from a swollen ego, not clear seeing.
bhagwad_gita::585.insight: It teaches you to notice how success can harden into delusion and make a person confuse power with truth.

bhagwad_gita::586.verse_sanskrit: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया । यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::586.verse_hindi: हम धनवान् हैं, बहुतसे मनुष्य हमारे पास हैं, हमारे समान और कौन है हम खूब यज्ञ करेंगे, दान देंगे और मौज करेंगे  इस तरह वे अज्ञानसे मोहित रहते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::586.english_translation: We are rich, surrounded by many people. Who is equal to us? We will sacrifice, give, and enjoy. Deluded by ignorance, they think this way.
bhagwad_gita::586.translation_literal: आढ्यः (rich) / अभिजनवान् (well-born, surrounded by family and followers) / अस्मि (I am) / कः (who) / अन्यः (other) / अस्ति (is) / सदृशः (equal) / मया (to me) / यक्ष्ये (I will sacrifice) / दास्यामि (I will give) / मोदिष्ये (I will rejoice) / इति (thus) / अज्ञान-विमोहिताः (deluded by ignorance)
bhagwad_gita::586.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::586.essence: Pride turns abundance into delusion and makes more wanting feel justified.
bhagwad_gita::586.simple_meaning: Arrogance makes a person feel rich, superior, and endlessly secure. That delusion then turns even sacrifice and giving into excuses for more enjoyment.
bhagwad_gita::586.simple_insight: You can catch pride at its root before it turns into greed, display, and self-deception.
bhagwad_gita::586.detailed_meaning: Krishna is exposing the mindset of the asuric person after Arjuna’s crisis on Kurukshetra. The deluded mind says, “I have wealth, people, and status; no one equals me.” That false certainty feeds greed, vanity, and self-indulgence.
bhagwad_gita::586.modern_relevance: You scroll past your own wins, then start counting what still proves you matter. The urge to announce, compare, and consume can come dressed as confidence.
bhagwad_gita::586.insight: It shifts attention from outward success to the hidden arrogance driving it.

bhagwad_gita::587.verse_sanskrit: अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः । प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ ॥
bhagwad_gita::587.verse_hindi: कामनाओंके कारण तरहतरहसे भ्रमित चित्तवाले, मोहजालमें अच्छी तरहसे फँसे हुए तथा पदार्थों और भोगोंमें अत्यन्त आसक्त रहनेवाले मनुष्य भयङ्कर नरकोंमें गिरते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::587.english_translation: Deluded by many desires, trapped in the net of confusion, and deeply attached to pleasures, people fall into a lower realm of misery.
bhagwad_gita::587.translation_literal: अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ताः (confused by many minds/desires) / मोहजालसमावृताः (covered by the net of delusion) / प्रसक्ताः (attached) / कामभोगेषु (in pleasures of desire) / पतन्ति (fall) / नरके (into a lower realm) / अशुचौ (impure, miserable)
bhagwad_gita::587.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::587.essence: Desire scatters the mind, and confusion turns that scattering into a fall.
bhagwad_gita::587.simple_meaning: A mind pulled in many directions by desire gets caught in confusion and falls into misery through attachment to pleasure.
bhagwad_gita::587.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that confusion is not your nature; it is what unchecked wanting does to the mind.
bhagwad_gita::587.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, where pride, fear, and craving are all visible in human action. He describes people whose minds are scattered by desire, who get trapped in delusion and sink into miserable choices.
bhagwad_gita::587.modern_relevance: You open your phone for one thing and end up half-lost in ten cravings, three tabs, and a bad mood. The mind does not stay neutral for long when it keeps feeding wanting.
bhagwad_gita::587.insight: It shifts attention from chasing pleasure to noticing how desire fragments judgment.

bhagwad_gita::588.verse_sanskrit: आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः । यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::588.verse_hindi: अपनेको सबसे अधिक पूज्य माननेवाले, अकड़ रखनेवाले तथा धन और मानके मदमें चूर रहनेवाले वे मनुष्य दम्भसे अविधिपूर्वक नाममात्रके यज्ञोंसे यजन करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::588.english_translation: Self-important, stubborn, drunk on wealth and praise, they perform ritual in name only, with pretence and without proper method.
bhagwad_gita::588.translation_literal: आत्मसम्भाविताः (self-important) / स्तब्धा (stubborn, rigid) / धनमानमदान्विताः (endowed with wealth-pride and honor-pride) / यजन्ते (they perform ritual) / नामयज्ञैः (with name-only sacrifices) / ते (they) / दम्भेन (with pretence) / अविधिपूर्वकम् (without proper method)
bhagwad_gita::588.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::588.essence: Pride can hollow out sacred action until only appearance remains.
bhagwad_gita::588.simple_meaning: People swollen with pride, wealth, and status may still perform rituals, but only as show. The outer act remains, while the inner sincerity and right method are missing.
bhagwad_gita::588.simple_insight: Real practice feels clean and humble, not flashy or self-congratulatory.
bhagwad_gita::588.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna is exposing the inner decay behind outward piety. After describing deluded people trapped in desire, he shows another mask: ritual done for show by the proud, rich, and stubborn. The issue is not action itself, but false motive.
bhagwad_gita::588.modern_relevance: You post the apology, attend the ceremony, and say the right words — but your chest is tight with image-management. Krishna names the gap between appearance and sincerity.
bhagwad_gita::588.insight: It teaches you to examine motive, not just performance, and to let practice become honest rather than decorative.

bhagwad_gita::589.verse_sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः । मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::589.verse_hindi: वे अहङ्कार, हठ, घमण्ड, कामना और क्रोधका आश्रय लेनेवाले मनुष्य अपने और दूसरोंके शरीरमें रहनेवाले मुझ अन्तर्यामीके साथ द्वेष करते हैं तथा मेरे और दूसरोंके गुणोंमें दोषदृष्टि रखते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::589.english_translation: Those who take refuge in ego, force, arrogance, desire, and anger hate Me, who dwell in their own bodies and in the bodies of others, and they find fault with My qualities.
bhagwad_gita::589.translation_literal: अहङ्कारम् (ego) / बलम् (force) / दर्पम् (arrogance) / कामम् (desire) / क्रोधम् (anger) / च (and) / संश्रिताः (taking refuge in) / माम् (Me) / आत्मपरदेहेषु (in one's own and others' bodies) / प्रद्विषन्तः (hating) / अभ्यसूयकाः (fault-finding, envious)
bhagwad_gita::589.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::589.essence: Ego makes you fight the divine presence you carry yourself.
bhagwad_gita::589.simple_meaning: People ruled by ego, force, arrogance, desire, and anger turn against the divine presence within themselves and others. They also habitually look for faults in what is good.
bhagwad_gita::589.simple_insight: What you feed in yourself becomes the lens through which you see everyone else.
bhagwad_gita::589.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield, after describing the darker forces that distort human conduct. He now names the inner habits that make a person hostile to the divine presence in themselves and in others, setting up the warning that follows.
bhagwad_gita::589.modern_relevance: A group chat turns cruel, and every message assumes bad intent. The same inner heat that makes you snap at yourself also makes you misread everyone else.
bhagwad_gita::589.insight: It shifts attention from outer conflict to the inner attitudes that create contempt, envy, and fault-finding.

bhagwad_gita::590.verse_sanskrit: तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु नराधमान् । क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु ॥
bhagwad_gita::590.verse_hindi: उन द्वेष करनेवाले, क्रूर स्वभाववाले और संसारमें महान् नीच, अपवित्र मनुष्योंको मैं बारबार आसुरी योनियोंमें गिराता ही रहता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::590.english_translation: I cast those hateful, cruel, and vile people again and again into demonic births.
bhagwad_gita::590.translation_literal: तान् (those) / अहम् (I) / द्विषतः (hateful) / क्रूरान् (cruel) / संसारेषु (in the cycles of worldly existence) / नराधमान् (lowest among men) / क्षिपामि (I cast) / अजस्रम् (again and again) / अशुभान् (inauspicious, impure) / आसुरीषु (into demonic) / एव (indeed) / योनिषु (wombs, births)
bhagwad_gita::590.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::590.essence: Repeated hatred drives a person into worse and worse forms of existence.
bhagwad_gita::590.simple_meaning: People who hate, act cruelly, and live in impurity fall into lower births again and again.
bhagwad_gita::590.simple_insight: Cruelty narrows the future. Repeated hostility keeps a person trapped in worse patterns.
bhagwad_gita::590.detailed_meaning: Krishna continues his warning to Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra. After describing the traits of destructive people, he says that those who hate, harm, and degrade themselves do not rise toward freedom; they sink into worse births and conditions.
bhagwad_gita::590.modern_relevance: A person keeps choosing contempt, manipulation, and violence, then wonders why life feels smaller each year. The habits do not stay private; they shape the kind of future being built.
bhagwad_gita::590.insight: It shifts the mind from blaming fate to seeing how repeated cruelty hardens into a downward pattern.

bhagwad_gita::591.verse_sanskrit: असुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि । मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::591.verse_hindi: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  वे मूढ मनुष्य मेरेको प्राप्त न करके ही जन्मजन्मान्तरमें आसुरी योनिको प्राप्त होते हैं, फिर उससे भी अधिक अधम गतिमें अर्थात् भयङ्कर नरकोंमें चले जाते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::591.english_translation: Those deluded beings, born again and again into shadowed births, never reach me and sink into a lower state.
bhagwad_gita::591.translation_literal: असुरीम् (shadowed) / योनिम् (birth) / आपन्नाः (having entered) / मूढाः (deluded ones) / जन्मनि जन्मनि (birth after birth) / माम् (me) / अप्राप्य (not reaching) / एव (indeed) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / ततः (then) / यान्ति (go) / अधमाम् (lower) / गतिम् (state)
bhagwad_gita::591.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::591.essence: Repeated delusion keeps pulling a person farther from the divine.
bhagwad_gita::591.simple_meaning: People trapped in delusion keep taking shadowed births again and again. Because they never turn toward the divine, they sink into still lower states.
bhagwad_gita::591.simple_insight: There is urgency in seeing how repeated confusion hardens into a downward pattern.
bhagwad_gita::591.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna has just described the dark nature of destructive people, and now he shows the end of that path: repeated rebirth in shadowed conditions, with no rise toward him.
bhagwad_gita::591.modern_relevance: You keep making the same self-sabotaging choice after the breakup, after the apology, after the warning. The pattern does not feel dramatic — until you notice it has become your life.
bhagwad_gita::591.insight: It shifts the mind from treating repeated bad choices as isolated mistakes to seeing them as a reinforcing descent.

bhagwad_gita::592.verse_sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः । कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::592.verse_hindi: काम, क्रोध और लोभ  ये तीन प्रकारके नरकके दरवाजे जीवात्माका पतन करनेवाले हैं, इसलिये इन तीनोंका त्याग कर देना चाहिये ॥
bhagwad_gita::592.english_translation: Desire, anger, and greed are the three gates of ruin. Abandon these three.
bhagwad_gita::592.translation_literal: त्रिविधम् (threefold) / नरकस्य (of ruin) / इदम् (this) / द्वारम् (gate) / नाशनम् (destroyer) / आत्मनः (of the self) / कामः (desire) / क्रोधः (anger) / तथा (and also) / लोभः (greed) / तस्मात् (therefore) / एतत् (these) / त्रयम् (three) / त्यजेत् (should abandon)
bhagwad_gita::592.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::592.essence: Three inner forces open the way to ruin; dropping them protects the self.
bhagwad_gita::592.simple_meaning: Desire, anger, and greed are the three forces that drag a person downward. Krishna says they must be given up.
bhagwad_gita::592.simple_insight: You do not have to obey every impulse. Freedom begins when you stop feeding the forces that trap you.
bhagwad_gita::592.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and collapse. Krishna now names the inner enemies that make clear action impossible: desire, anger, and greed. He says these must be dropped before a person can act rightly.
bhagwad_gita::592.modern_relevance: You open your phone to send one sharp message, then another, then another. The urge feels justified, but it is really pulling you into a smaller version of yourself. Stop there.
bhagwad_gita::592.insight: It shifts the mind from impulse-driven reaction to deliberate restraint.

bhagwad_gita::593.verse_sanskrit: एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः । आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::593.verse_hindi: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  इन नरकके तीनों दरवाजोंसे रहित हुआ जो मनुष्य अपने कल्याणका आचरण करता है, वह परमगतिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::593.english_translation: Freed from these three gates of darkness, a person acts for their own good and reaches the highest state.
bhagwad_gita::593.translation_literal: एतैः (from these) / विमुक्तः (freed) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / तैः (by those) / त्रिभिः (three) / नरः (person) / आचरति (practices) / आत्मनः (of one's own) / श्रेयः (well-being) / ततः (then) / याति (goes) / पराम् (highest) / गतिम् (state)
bhagwad_gita::593.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::593.essence: Freedom from the three dark impulses opens the way to your highest good.
bhagwad_gita::593.simple_meaning: When a person is free from desire, anger, and greed, they live in a way that supports their highest good and reach the highest state.
bhagwad_gita::593.simple_insight: Freedom is not emptiness; it gives you room to act in your own best interest.
bhagwad_gita::593.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna continues his warning to Arjuna after naming desire, anger, and greed as the three gates of ruin. He now shows the other side: a person who escapes these forces can live in a way that leads upward, not downward.
bhagwad_gita::593.modern_relevance: You pause before sending the cruel text, buying the thing you do not need, or lashing out in pride. That pause can save your character.
bhagwad_gita::593.insight: It shifts attention from impulse to self-protective action, showing that restraint opens the way to better choices.

bhagwad_gita::594.verse_sanskrit: यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः । न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::594.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य शास्त्रविधिको छोड़कर अपनी इच्छासे मनमाना आचरण करता है, वह न सिद्धिअन्तःकरणकी शुद्धि को, न सुखको और न परमगतिको ही प्राप्त होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::594.english_translation: Whoever sets aside scripture and acts on desire alone does not attain perfection, happiness, or the highest state.
bhagwad_gita::594.translation_literal: यः (whoever) / शास्त्रविधिम् (scriptural rule) / उत्सृज्य (having set aside) / वर्तते (acts) / कामकारतः (under the pull of desire) / न (not) / सः (that person) / सिद्धिम् (perfection) / अवाप्नोति (attains) / न (not) / सुखम् (happiness) / न (not) / पराम् गतिम् (highest state) ॥
bhagwad_gita::594.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::594.essence: Impulse cannot deliver what it promises.
bhagwad_gita::594.simple_meaning: Acting only on impulse, while ignoring wise guidance, blocks real fulfilment, lasting happiness, and the highest good.
bhagwad_gita::594.simple_insight: Freedom without guidance is not freedom at all; it can quietly close every real door.
bhagwad_gita::594.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, after warning Arjuna about the three inner gates of ruin, Krishna sharpens the point: a person who throws aside right guidance and follows desire alone will not reach inner fulfilment, happiness, or the highest aim. The battlefield crisis becomes a lesson in disciplined choice.
bhagwad_gita::594.modern_relevance: You are about to send the text, quit the job, or spend the money because the urge is loud. The verse says impulse can feel decisive while quietly cutting off what you actually want most.
bhagwad_gita::594.insight: It shifts action from craving-led reaction to disciplined choice shaped by what is truly right.

bhagwad_gita::595.verse_sanskrit: तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ । ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::595.verse_hindi: अतः तेरे लिये कर्तव्यअकर्तव्यकी व्यवस्थामें शास्त्र ही प्रमाण है  ऐसा जानकर तू इस लोकमें शास्त्रविधिसे नियत कर्तव्य कर्म करनेयोग्य है ॥
bhagwad_gita::595.english_translation: Therefore, scripture is your authority for deciding what should be done and what should not be done. Knowing the duties laid out in scripture, you should act here in the world.
bhagwad_gita::595.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) / शास्त्रम् (scripture) / प्रमाणम् (authority) / ते (for you) / कार्य-अकार्य-व्यवस्थितौ (in the arrangement of what should be done and what should not be done) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / शास्त्र-विधान-उक्तम् (spoken in scriptural rule) / कर्म (action / duty) / कर्तुम् (to do) / इह (here) / अर्हसि (you are fit / should)
bhagwad_gita::595.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::595.essence: Impulse cannot judge action; a higher standard must.
bhagwad_gita::595.simple_meaning: Right and wrong action should be judged by scripture, not impulse. Knowing that guidance, a person should do the duty set before them.
bhagwad_gita::595.simple_insight: You do not have to invent your own moral compass in the heat of confusion.
bhagwad_gita::595.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has been overwhelmed by doubt. After exposing the ruin caused by desire and lawless action, Krishna closes the argument by grounding right action in scripture. The point is clear: act, but let higher guidance decide what action truly is.
bhagwad_gita::595.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that could end a relationship, and your feelings are shouting louder than your conscience. Krishna says: do not let impulse be the judge.
bhagwad_gita::595.insight: It shifts decision-making from personal craving to a tested standard of right action.

bhagwad_gita::596.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः । तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः ॥
bhagwad_gita::596.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे कृष्ण  जो मनुष्य शास्त्रविधिका त्याग करके श्रद्धापूर्वक देवता आदिका पूजन करते हैं, उनकी निष्ठा फिर कौनसी है सात्त्विकी है अथवा राजसीतामसी ॥
bhagwad_gita::596.english_translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, what is the standing of those who worship with faith while setting aside the rules of scripture? Is it sattvic, rajasic, or tamasic?
bhagwad_gita::596.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / ये (who) / शास्त्रविधिम् (scriptural rule) / उत्सृज्य (having set aside) / यजन्ते (worship) / श्रद्धया (with faith) / अन्विताः (endowed with) / तेषाम् (of them) / निष्ठा (standing / conviction) / तु (then) / का (what) / कृष्ण (O Krishna) / सत्त्वम् (sattva) / आहो (or) / रजः (rajas) / तमः (tamas)
bhagwad_gita::596.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::596.essence: Faith alone does not reveal its quality; the motive beneath it does.
bhagwad_gita::596.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks what kind of faith people have when they worship without following scripture. He wants to know whether their faith is pure, restless, or confused.
bhagwad_gita::596.simple_insight: It is okay to question what drives belief instead of assuming every sincere act is equally clear.
bhagwad_gita::596.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still searching for a way to understand human action. Before Krishna answers, he asks about people who worship with faith but ignore scriptural guidance, wanting to know what quality actually rules them.
bhagwad_gita::596.modern_relevance: You watch someone follow a spiritual trend with total sincerity, but something feels off. The question is not whether they mean well — it is what kind of force is shaping their devotion.
bhagwad_gita::596.insight: It shifts attention from outward sincerity to the inner quality behind belief and practice.

bhagwad_gita::597.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचत्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा । सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां श्रृणु ॥
bhagwad_gita::597.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  मनुष्योंकी वह स्वभावसे उत्पन्न हुई श्रद्धा सात्त्विकी तथा राजसी और तामसी  ऐसे तीन तरहकी ही होती है, उसको तुम मेरेसे सुनो ॥
bhagwad_gita::597.english_translation: The faith of embodied beings is born of their nature. It is of three kinds: sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic. Listen to this.
bhagwad_gita::597.translation_literal: त्रिविधा (threefold) / भवति (is) / श्रद्धा (faith) / देहिनां (of embodied beings) / सा (that) / स्वभावजा (born of nature) / सात्त्विकी (sattvic) / राजसी (rajasic) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / तामसी (tamasic) / चेति (thus) / तां (that) / श्रृणु (listen)
bhagwad_gita::597.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::597.essence: Faith takes the shape of the nature beneath it.
bhagwad_gita::597.simple_meaning: Faith is not all the same. It comes from a person's nature and appears in three forms: clear, restless, or dull.
bhagwad_gita::597.simple_insight: Your deepest beliefs are not random; they reveal the quality of your inner state.
bhagwad_gita::597.detailed_meaning: Arjuna has asked why people worship in different ways. On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Krishna begins his answer by explaining that faith itself reflects a person's nature, and that it can be clear, restless, or dull.
bhagwad_gita::597.modern_relevance: You watch someone defend a choice they barely understand, then realise the energy behind it matters as much as the belief itself. The shape of faith reveals the state underneath.
bhagwad_gita::597.insight: It shifts attention from judging beliefs alone to noticing the inner quality that produces them.

bhagwad_gita::598.verse_sanskrit: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत । श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥
bhagwad_gita::598.verse_hindi: हे भारत  सभी मनुष्योंकी श्रद्धा अन्तःकरणके अनुरूप होती है ।  यह मनुष्य श्रद्धामय है ।  इसलिये जो जैसी श्रद्धावाला है, वही उसका स्वरूप है अर्थात् वही उसकी निष्ठा  स्थिति है ॥
bhagwad_gita::598.english_translation: O Bharata, each person's trust matches their inner nature. A person is made of trust; whatever trust he holds, that is what he becomes.
bhagwad_gita::598.translation_literal: सत्त्वानुरूपा (according to inner nature) / सर्वस्य (of everyone) / श्रद्धा (trust before certainty) / भवति (becomes) / भारत (O Bharata) । / श्रद्धामयः (made of trust) / अयम् (this) / पुरुषः (person) / यः (who) / यत् (whatever) / श्रद्धः (trustful) / सः (that) / एव (indeed) / सः (he) ॥
bhagwad_gita::598.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::598.essence: Trust is not just held; it becomes the person.
bhagwad_gita::598.simple_meaning: A person's deepest trust reflects their inner makeup, and that trust shapes who they become.
bhagwad_gita::598.simple_insight: What you repeatedly trust quietly forms your character.
bhagwad_gita::598.detailed_meaning: In the middle of Arjuna's crisis on the battlefield, Krishna explains that faith is not random. Each person's trust grows from their inner condition, and that trust then shapes their whole life and identity.
bhagwad_gita::598.modern_relevance: You keep returning to the same app, the same voice, the same habit, the same fear. What you trust most quietly starts to define you.
bhagwad_gita::598.insight: It shifts attention from surface belief to the deeper loyalties that form character and action.

bhagwad_gita::599.verse_sanskrit: यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः । प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::599.verse_hindi: सात्त्विक मनुष्य देवताओंका पूजन करते हैं, राजस मनुष्य यक्षों और राक्षसोंका और दूसरे जो तामस मनुष्य हैं, वे प्रेतों और भूतगणोंका पूजन करते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::599.english_translation: The sattvic worship radiant beings; the rajasic worship yakshas and rakshasas; the tamasic worship spirits and hosts of the dead.
bhagwad_gita::599.translation_literal: यजन्ते (worship) / सात्त्विकाः (sattvic) / देवान् (radiant beings) / यक्ष-रक्षांसि (yakshas and rakshasas) / राजसाः (rajasic) / प्रेतान् (spirits of the dead) / भूत-गणान् (hosts of beings) / च (and) / अन्ये (others) / यजन्ते (worship) / तामसाः (tamasic) / जनाः (people)
bhagwad_gita::599.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::599.essence: Faith reveals itself in what each person chooses to revere.
bhagwad_gita::599.simple_meaning: People worship different kinds of beings according to the quality that dominates their nature. Their faith shapes the form their devotion takes.
bhagwad_gita::599.simple_insight: Your deepest tendencies quietly choose what you revere.
bhagwad_gita::599.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna still struggling to understand human nature, Krishna explains that faith is not neutral. The quality ruling a person’s mind shapes whom they worship: the clear worship the radiant, the restless seek powerful intermediaries, and the confused turn to darker forces.
bhagwad_gita::599.modern_relevance: A person who chases charisma, power, or fear usually reveals something about their own inner state. What you keep admiring is often a mirror of what rules you.
bhagwad_gita::599.insight: It shifts attention from outer worship to the quality of mind behind worship.

bhagwad_gita::600.verse_sanskrit: अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः । दम्भाहङ्कारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::600.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य शास्त्रविधिसे रहित घोर तप करते हैं जो दम्भ और अहङ्कारसे अच्छी तरह युक्त हैं जो भोगपदार्थ, आसक्ति और हठसे युक्त हैं जो शरीरमें स्थित पाँच भूतोंको अर्थात् पाञ्चभौतिक शरीरको तथा अन्तःकरणमें स्थित मुझ परमात्माको भी कृश करनेवाले हैं उन अज्ञानियोंको तू आसुर निश्चयवाले आसुरी सम्पदावाले समझ ॥
bhagwad_gita::600.english_translation: People who perform harsh austerities without scriptural guidance, driven by vanity, ego, desire, attachment, and stubbornness, are not purified by them.
bhagwad_gita::600.translation_literal: अशास्त्रविहितम् (not laid down by scripture) / घोरम् (severe, terrible) / तप्यन्ते (they practice austerity) / ये (who) / तपः (austerity) / जनाः (people) / दम्भ-अहङ्कार-संयुक्ताः (joined with hypocrisy and ego) / काम-राग-बल-अन्विताः (endowed with desire, attachment, and forceful stubbornness)
bhagwad_gita::600.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::600.essence: Harsh effort without right guidance can deepen ego instead of cleansing it.
bhagwad_gita::600.simple_meaning: Severe self-punishment without right guidance, mixed with pride and craving, does not make a person better.
bhagwad_gita::600.simple_insight: Not every hard practice is cleansing. Struggle can still feed ego.
bhagwad_gita::600.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna is explaining the difference between real discipline and distorted effort. Here he describes people who force harsh austerity without guidance, driven by vanity, ego, desire, and stubbornness.
bhagwad_gita::600.modern_relevance: Someone bragging about a brutal detox, sleep deprivation, or punishing routine may look committed, but the hidden motive is still control and self-display.
bhagwad_gita::600.insight: It warns you to examine motive before praising endurance. A hard practice can still strengthen the wrong parts of you.

bhagwad_gita::601.verse_sanskrit: कर्षयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः । मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान् ॥
bhagwad_gita::601.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य शास्त्रविधिसे रहित घोर तप करते हैं जो दम्भ और अहङ्कारसे अच्छी तरह युक्त हैं जो भोगपदार्थ, आसक्ति और हठसे युक्त हैं जो शरीरमें स्थित पाँच भूतोंको अर्थात् पाञ्चभौतिक शरीरको तथा अन्तःकरणमें स्थित मुझ परमात्माको भी कृश करनेवाले हैं उन अज्ञानियोंको तू आसुर निश्चयवाले आसुरी सम्पदावाले समझ ॥
bhagwad_gita::601.english_translation: Those who are ignorant and perform terrible austerities without scriptural guidance, wasting away the body’s elements and Me dwelling within the body, should be known as having demonic resolve.
bhagwad_gita::601.translation_literal: कर्षयन्तः (wasting away) / शरीरस्थम् (dwelling in the body) / भूतग्रामम् (the group of elements / body) / अचेतसः (the unthinking) / माम् (Me) / च (and) / एव (also) / अन्तःशरीरस्थम् (dwelling within the body) / तान् (them) / विद्धि (know) / आसुरनिश्चयान् (having demonic resolve)
bhagwad_gita::601.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::601.essence: Harshness is not holiness when it destroys the body and ignores what lives within.
bhagwad_gita::601.simple_meaning: Blind, self-willed austerity can damage the body and ignore the divine presence within it. Such harsh practice is not purity; it comes from confused, destructive resolve.
bhagwad_gita::601.simple_insight: Not every hard practice is noble. Discipline without wisdom can become self-harm.
bhagwad_gita::601.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield, where every choice feels life-and-death. After describing misguided worship and harsh austerity, he sharpens the warning: some people even weaken their own body and ignore the divine presence within it. That is not true discipline.
bhagwad_gita::601.modern_relevance: Someone brags about fasting through exhaustion, sleeping three hours, and calling it commitment. The body is breaking, the mind is proud, and the practice is feeding ego instead of clarity.
bhagwad_gita::601.insight: It shifts discipline from self-punishment to wise restraint that protects both body and intention.

bhagwad_gita::602.verse_sanskrit: आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः । यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं श्रृणु ॥
bhagwad_gita::602.verse_hindi: आहार भी सबको तीन प्रकारका प्रिय होता है और वैसे ही यज्ञ, दान और तप भी तीन प्रकारके होते हैं अर्थात् शास्त्रीय कर्मोंमें भी तीन प्रकारकी रुचि होती है, तू उनके इस भेदको सुन ॥
bhagwad_gita::602.english_translation: Food, sacrifice, charity, and austerity are each of three kinds. Listen to these distinctions.
bhagwad_gita::602.translation_literal: आहारः (food) / तु (indeed) / अपि (also) / सर्वस्य (of everyone) / त्रिविधः (threefold) / भवति (is) / प्रियः (dear) / यज्ञः (sacrifice) / तपः (austerity) / तथा (and likewise) / दानम् (charity) / तेषाम् (of them) / भेदम् (difference) / इमम् (this) / श्रृणु (listen)
bhagwad_gita::602.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::602.essence: Even sacred actions differ; their inner quality decides their worth.
bhagwad_gita::602.simple_meaning: Food, sacrifice, charity, and austerity all come in three kinds. Krishna asks Arjuna to listen to the differences.
bhagwad_gita::602.simple_insight: Not every noble act has the same quality. The inner motive changes everything.
bhagwad_gita::602.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna begins explaining how even sacred acts can differ in quality. After condemning harsh, lawless austerity, he now introduces the threefold nature of food, sacrifice, charity, and discipline.
bhagwad_gita::602.modern_relevance: You choose a meal, make a donation, or push through a hard practice and assume the act itself is enough. Krishna says the inner quality behind it matters just as much.
bhagwad_gita::602.insight: It shifts attention from the outer form of an act to the quality of consciousness behind it.

bhagwad_gita::603.verse_sanskrit: आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः । रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::603.verse_hindi: आयु, सत्त्वगुण, बल, आरोग्य, सुख और प्रसन्नता बढ़ानेवाले, स्थिर रहनेवाले, हृदयको शक्ति देनेवाले, रसयुक्त तथा चिकने  ऐसे आहार अर्थात् भोजन करनेके पदार्थ सात्त्विक मनुष्यको प्रिय होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::603.english_translation: Foods that increase life, purity, strength, health, happiness, and cheerfulness, and are tasty, smooth, firm, and pleasing, are dear to the sattvic person.
bhagwad_gita::603.translation_literal: आयुः (life) / सत्त्व (purity) / बल (strength) / आरोग्य (health) / सुख (happiness) / प्रीतिविवर्धनाः (increasing cheerfulness) / रस्याः (tasty) / स्निग्धाः (smooth) / स्थिराः (firm) / हृद्या (pleasing to the heart) / आहाराः (foods) / सात्त्विकप्रियाः (dear to the sattvic person)
bhagwad_gita::603.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::603.essence: Wholesome food quietly builds the conditions for a steadier life.
bhagwad_gita::603.simple_meaning: Pure, nourishing food supports long life, strength, health, calmness, and happiness. A clear-minded person naturally prefers what is wholesome and steadying.
bhagwad_gita::603.simple_insight: What you eat shapes how steady, clear, and cheerful you feel.
bhagwad_gita::603.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still teaching Arjuna on the battlefield, but now the lesson turns to daily discipline. After explaining that food, sacrifice, and austerity all come in three types, he defines the food that supports a clear and balanced life.
bhagwad_gita::603.modern_relevance: You grab whatever is quick after a draining day, then wonder why your body feels heavy and your mood frays. The choice on your plate quietly shapes your steadiness.
bhagwad_gita::603.insight: It shifts attention from taste alone to the effect food has on energy, mood, and clarity.

bhagwad_gita::604.verse_hindi: अति कड़वे, अति खट्टे, अति नमकीन, अति गरम, अति तीखे, अति रूखे और अति दाहकारक आहार अर्थात् भोजनके पदार्थ राजस मनुष्यको प्रिय होते हैं, जो कि दुःख, शोक और रोगोंको देनेवाले हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::604.english_translation: Bitter, sour, salty, overly hot, pungent, dry, and burning foods are dear to the passionate person. They bring pain, grief, and illness.
bhagwad_gita::604.translation_literal: कटु (bitter) / अम्ल (sour) / लवण (salty) / अत्युष्ण (overly hot) / तीक्ष्ण (pungent) / रूक्ष (dry) / विदाहिनः (burning) / आहाराः (foods) / राजसस्य (of the passionate person) / इष्टाः (dear) / दुःख (pain) / शोक (grief) / आमय (illness) / प्रदाः (giving)
bhagwad_gita::604.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::604.essence: What excites the senses can quietly produce suffering.
bhagwad_gita::604.simple_meaning: Foods that are too sharp, hot, dry, or harsh attract a restless, passionate nature, but they lead to pain, grief, and illness.
bhagwad_gita::604.simple_insight: What feels exciting in the moment can quietly wear you down afterward.
bhagwad_gita::604.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna is teaching Arjuna how the qualities of food reveal the qualities of mind. After describing sattvic food, he now shows the rajasic pattern: what excites the senses often disturbs the person who craves intensity.
bhagwad_gita::604.modern_relevance: You reach for another extra-spicy, late-night meal because your nerves want a hit, not balance. The body feels it later — in sleep, mood, and energy.
bhagwad_gita::604.insight: It shifts attention from taste alone to the mental state that chooses the food and the result it creates.

bhagwad_gita::605.verse_sanskrit: यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत् । उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::605.verse_hindi: जो भोजन अधपका, रसरहित, दुर्गन्धित, बासी और उच्छिष्ट है तथा जो महान् अपवित्र भी है, वह तामस मनुष्यको प्रिय होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::605.english_translation: Food that is half-cooked, tasteless, foul-smelling, stale, leftover, and impure is dear to people ruled by tamas.
bhagwad_gita::605.translation_literal: यातयामम् (half-cooked / stale) / गतरसम् (devoid of taste) / पूति (foul-smelling) / पर्युषितम् (stale / left overnight) / च (and) / यत् (which) / उच्छिष्टम् (leftover) / अपि (even) / च (and) / अमेध्यम् (impure) / भोजनम् (food) / तामसप्रियम् (dear to tamasic people)
bhagwad_gita::605.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::605.essence: What you repeatedly choose to consume reveals the heaviness within.
bhagwad_gita::605.simple_meaning: People dominated by tamas are drawn to food that is stale, tasteless, foul-smelling, leftover, or impure.
bhagwad_gita::605.simple_insight: Your cravings can reveal your condition before your thoughts do.
bhagwad_gita::605.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna is teaching Arjuna how faith shows itself in daily choices. After describing pure and restless habits, he names the food preferred by tamas: stale, impure, and lifeless. The point is to show how inner heaviness shapes appetite.
bhagwad_gita::605.modern_relevance: You open the fridge late at night and reach for whatever is dead easiest, not what actually helps you. The body keeps a record of what the mind has been feeding it.
bhagwad_gita::605.insight: It shifts attention from taste alone to the quality of what you repeatedly accept.

bhagwad_gita::606.verse_sanskrit: अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते । यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः ॥
bhagwad_gita::606.verse_hindi: यज्ञ करना कर्तव्य है  इस तरह मनको समाधान करके फलेच्छारहित मनुष्योंद्वारा जो शास्त्रविधिसे नियत यज्ञ किया जाता है, वह सात्त्विक है ॥
bhagwad_gita::606.english_translation: A sacrifice performed according to scriptural rule by people without desire for reward, with the mind settled on “it must be done,” is sattvic.
bhagwad_gita::606.translation_literal: अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिः (by those without desire for reward) / यज्ञः (sacrifice) / विधिदृष्टः (seen by rule) / यः (which) / इज्यते (is performed) / यष्टव्यम् (must be offered) / एव (indeed) / इति (thus) / मनः (mind) / समाधाय (having settled) / सः (that) / सात्त्विकः (sattvic)
bhagwad_gita::606.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::606.essence: Right action becomes pure when reward stops being the reason.
bhagwad_gita::606.simple_meaning: A sacrifice is pure when it is done because it should be done, not for reward.
bhagwad_gita::606.simple_insight: There is relief in doing what is right without bargaining for a payoff.
bhagwad_gita::606.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still teaching Arjuna on the battlefield, where hesitation has frozen action. After describing lesser kinds of food and conduct, he now defines the pure offering: an act done by rule, with no craving for reward, because duty itself is enough.
bhagwad_gita::606.modern_relevance: You send the apology text even though no one may soften. You do it because it is the right thing, not because you can control the reply.
bhagwad_gita::606.insight: It shifts action from reward-seeking to duty-centered offering.

bhagwad_gita::607.verse_sanskrit: अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् । इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::607.verse_hindi: परन्तु हे भरतश्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  जो यज्ञ फलकी इच्छाको लेकर अथवा दम्भदिखावटीपन के लिये भी किया जाता है, उसको तुम राजस समझो ॥
bhagwad_gita::607.english_translation: But, best of the Bharatas, know that sacrifice to be rajasic when it is performed for reward or for show.
bhagwad_gita::607.translation_literal: अभिसंधाय (with intention) / तु (but) / फलम् (fruit, result) / दम्भार्थम् (for display, for show) / अपि (also) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / यत् (which) / इज्यते (is performed as sacrifice) / भरतश्रेष्ठ (best of the Bharatas) / तम् (that) / यज्ञम् (sacrifice) / विद्धि (know) / राजसम् (rajasic)
bhagwad_gita::607.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::607.essence: An offering for reward or applause loses its purity.
bhagwad_gita::607.simple_meaning: A sacrifice done for personal gain or to look impressive is not pure. Its motive makes it rajasic, driven by restlessness and ego.
bhagwad_gita::607.simple_insight: It exposes the hidden craving to be seen, praised, or rewarded, so you can notice it before it shapes your actions.
bhagwad_gita::607.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen between battle and duty. Krishna now classifies sacrifice by motive: pure offering, selfish offering, and careless offering. This verse names the middle one — action done for gain or display.
bhagwad_gita::607.modern_relevance: You post the donation receipt, the volunteer photo, the perfect caption. The act may help others, but part of you is still feeding on recognition.
bhagwad_gita::607.insight: It shifts attention from the outer act to the motive behind it.

bhagwad_gita::608.verse_sanskrit: विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् । श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते ॥
bhagwad_gita::608.verse_hindi: शास्त्रविधिसे हीन, अन्नदानसे रहित, बिना मन्त्रोंके, बिना दक्षिणाके और बिना श्रद्धाके किये जानेवाले यज्ञको तामस यज्ञ कहते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::608.english_translation: They call a sacrifice dark when it lacks scriptural rule, food offering, mantra, fee, and trust.
bhagwad_gita::608.translation_literal: विधिहीनम् (without rule) / असृष्टान्नम् (without offered food) / मन्त्रहीनम् (without mantra) / अदक्षिणम् (without fee) / श्रद्धाविरहितम् (without trust) / यज्ञम् (sacrifice) / तामसम् (dark) / परिचक्षते (they call)
bhagwad_gita::608.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::608.essence: Ritual without trust becomes empty and heavy.
bhagwad_gita::608.simple_meaning: A sacrifice done without proper guidance, offering, mantra, giving, or trust is called dark and lifeless.
bhagwad_gita::608.simple_insight: What you do matters less than the sincerity and care you bring to it.
bhagwad_gita::608.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Krishna is classifying the three kinds of sacrifice for Arjuna. After describing pure and driven offerings, he names the lowest form: a ritual performed mechanically, without trust or reverence, which cannot uplift the one who performs it.
bhagwad_gita::608.modern_relevance: You light a candle, say the words, and still feel nothing because your attention never arrived. A practice done on autopilot may look complete, yet it carries no real force.
bhagwad_gita::608.insight: It shifts the mind from outward performance to inward sincerity.

bhagwad_gita::609.verse_sanskrit: देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् । ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::609.verse_hindi: देवता, ब्राह्मण, गुरुजन और जीवन्मुक्त महापुरुषका पूजन करना, शुद्धि रखना, सरलता, ब्रह्मचर्यका पालन करना और हिंसा न करना  यह शरीरसम्बन्धी तप कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::609.english_translation: Worship of the radiant beings, the wise, the teacher, and the enlightened; purity, simplicity, celibacy, and non-violence — these are called bodily austerity.
bhagwad_gita::609.translation_literal: देव (radiant beings) / द्विज (twice-born) / गुरु (teacher) / प्राज्ञ (wise) / पूजनम् (worship) / शौचम् (purity) / आर्जवम् (simplicity) / ब्रह्मचर्यम् (celibacy) / अहिंसा (non-violence) / च (and) / शारीरम् (bodily) / तपः (austerity) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::609.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::609.essence: The body itself can become a disciplined offering.
bhagwad_gita::609.simple_meaning: True bodily discipline includes honoring wise teachers, staying clean, living simply, practicing self-restraint, and avoiding harm.
bhagwad_gita::609.simple_insight: Spiritual discipline is not abstract. It begins with how you treat your body and other people.
bhagwad_gita::609.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna now explains that real discipline is not only inner resolve; it also shows up in bodily conduct — respect, cleanliness, simplicity, restraint, and non-harm.
bhagwad_gita::609.modern_relevance: You scroll past a cruel comment, then feel the urge to add one more. The verse asks for a different kind of strength: keep your body, habits, and actions clean enough to deserve your own respect.
bhagwad_gita::609.insight: It shifts discipline from private intention to visible conduct: what you do with the body reveals the quality of your practice.

bhagwad_gita::610.verse_sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::610.verse_hindi: उद्वेग न करनेवाला, सत्य, प्रिय, हितकारक भाषण तथा स्वाध्याय और अभ्यास करना  यह वाणीसम्बन्धी तप कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::610.english_translation: Speech that does not agitate, is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial, together with study and practice, is called austerity of speech.
bhagwad_gita::610.translation_literal: अनुद्वेगकरं (not causing agitation) / वाक्यं (speech) / सत्यं (true) / प्रियहितं (pleasant and beneficial) / च (and) / यत् (which) / स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं (study and practice) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / वाङ्मयं (of speech) / तपः (austerity) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::610.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::610.essence: Speech becomes discipline when it tells the truth without creating harm.
bhagwad_gita::610.simple_meaning: Speech becomes a disciplined practice when it is calm, truthful, kind, helpful, and supported by study.
bhagwad_gita::610.simple_insight: Your words can become a form of self-training, not just self-expression.
bhagwad_gita::610.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still teaching Arjuna how inner discipline takes shape in daily life. After describing bodily austerity, he turns to speech: words should not disturb, should be true, pleasant, and useful, and should be backed by regular study.
bhagwad_gita::610.modern_relevance: You are about to send a text that could inflame everything, or calm it. This verse asks whether your words reduce heat, carry truth, and actually help before you hit send.
bhagwad_gita::610.insight: It shifts speech from impulse to disciplined care, so words become a practice of restraint and usefulness.

bhagwad_gita::611.verse_hindi: मनकी प्रसन्नता, सौम्य भाव, मननशीलता, मनका निग्रह और भावोंकी शुद्धि  इस तरह यह मनसम्बन्धी तप कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::611.english_translation: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-control, and purity of feeling are called mental austerity.
bhagwad_gita::611.translation_literal: मनःप्रसादः (cheerfulness of mind) / सौम्यत्वम् (gentleness) / मौनम् (silence) / आत्मविनिग्रहः (self-restraint) / भावसंशुद्धिः (purity of feeling) / इति (thus) / एतत् (this) / तपः (austerity) / मानसम् (mental) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::611.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::611.essence: A trained mind is its own austerity.
bhagwad_gita::611.simple_meaning: Mental discipline means keeping the mind calm, gentle, quiet, controlled, and clean in its feelings.
bhagwad_gita::611.simple_insight: Inner strength is not noise. It grows when the mind becomes steady and clear.
bhagwad_gita::611.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna is still defining true discipline for Arjuna. After body and speech, he turns to the mind: real austerity is not punishment, but calmness, gentleness, silence, self-restraint, and purity within.
bhagwad_gita::611.modern_relevance: You close your laptop after a tense message and feel the urge to replay every line. The harder practice is not sending another reply — it is keeping the mind soft, quiet, and clean.
bhagwad_gita::611.insight: It shifts discipline from outward performance to inward regulation of thought and feeling.

bhagwad_gita::612.verse_sanskrit: श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्ित्रविधं नरैः । अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते ॥
bhagwad_gita::612.verse_hindi: परम श्रद्धासे युक्त फलेच्छारहित मनुष्योंके द्वारा तीन प्रकारशरीर, वाणी और मन का तप किया जाता है, उसको सात्त्विक कहते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::612.english_translation: That threefold discipline of body, speech, and mind, performed with supreme trust and without craving results, is called sattvic.
bhagwad_gita::612.translation_literal: श्रद्धया (with trust) / परया (supreme) / तप्तं (performed) / तपः (discipline) / तत् (that) / त्रिविधं (threefold) / नरैः (by people) / अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिः (by those not desiring fruit) / युक्तैः (by those joined) / सात्त्विकं (sattvic) / परिचक्षते (they call)
bhagwad_gita::612.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::612.essence: True discipline is clean only when reward is no longer the motive.
bhagwad_gita::612.simple_meaning: Body, speech, and mind are called pure discipline when practiced with trust and without wanting any reward.
bhagwad_gita::612.simple_insight: Real discipline feels lighter when it is not bargaining for payoff.
bhagwad_gita::612.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna is still answering Arjuna’s crisis by defining real inner discipline. After describing discipline of body, speech, and mind, he says that such practice is sattvic only when it is done with trust and no hunger for reward.
bhagwad_gita::612.modern_relevance: You keep the promise to train at dawn, then no one sees the effort and the applause never comes. The practice still counts when you were never negotiating for praise.
bhagwad_gita::612.insight: It shifts discipline from performance for approval to steady practice rooted in trust.

bhagwad_gita::613.verse_sanskrit: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् । क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::613.verse_hindi: जो तप सत्कार, मान और पूजाके लिये तथा दिखानेके भावसे किया जाता है, वह इस लोकमें अनिश्चित और नाशवान् फल देनेवाला तप राजस कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::613.english_translation: Austerity done for honor, praise, and worship, or with a show of display, is said to be rajasic here. It gives unstable, temporary results.
bhagwad_gita::613.translation_literal: सत्कारमानपूजार्थम् (for honor, respect, and worship) / तपः (austerity) / दम्भेन (with pretence, show) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / यत् (that which) / क्रियते (is done) / तत् (that) / इह (here, in this world) / प्रोक्तम् (is said) / राजसम् (rajasic) / चलम् (unstable) / अध्रुवम् (impermanent)
bhagwad_gita::613.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::613.essence: Practice for applause collapses into instability.
bhagwad_gita::613.simple_meaning: Practice done to impress others, gain respect, or look holy is unstable and short-lived. It may bring attention, but not lasting value.
bhagwad_gita::613.simple_insight: You can feel the difference between sincere effort and performance. The second leaves you emptier, even when others clap.
bhagwad_gita::613.detailed_meaning: Krishna continues explaining three kinds of austerity to Arjuna on the battlefield. After describing pure discipline, he turns to the kind done for status, admiration, or display. It looks spiritual, but it is shaky and temporary.
bhagwad_gita::613.modern_relevance: You post the disciplined routine, the perfect meal, the early-morning run — and wait for the praise. The moment approval becomes the fuel, the practice starts to hollow out.
bhagwad_gita::613.insight: It shifts action away from image-making and back toward sincerity.

bhagwad_gita::614.verse_sanskrit: मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः । परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::614.verse_hindi: जो तप मूढ़तापूर्वक हठसे अपनेको पीड़ा देकर अथवा दूसरोंको कष्ट देनेके लिये किया जाता है, वह तप तामस कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::614.english_translation: Austerity done with foolish stubbornness, by torturing oneself or harming others, is called tamasic.
bhagwad_gita::614.translation_literal: मूढग्राहेण (with foolish stubbornness) / आत्मनः (of oneself) / यत् (which) / पीडया (by pain) / क्रियते (is done) / तपः (austerity) / परस्य (of others) / उत्सादनार्थम् (for harming) / वा (or) / तत् (that) / तामसम् (tamasic) / उदाहृतम् (is said)
bhagwad_gita::614.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::614.essence: Pain imposed in ignorance only deepens confusion.
bhagwad_gita::614.simple_meaning: Austerity becomes dark and mistaken when it is done through foolish self-torture or to hurt other people.
bhagwad_gita::614.simple_insight: Real discipline should make you clearer and kinder, not harsher toward yourself or others.
bhagwad_gita::614.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still teaching Arjuna on the battlefield, where confusion could easily turn into harshness. After describing pure and showy forms of austerity, he names the third kind: painful, stubborn, and harmful practice. That kind belongs to ignorance.
bhagwad_gita::614.modern_relevance: You force yourself through a brutal routine because you think suffering proves commitment. Or you use harshness to control someone else. Krishna calls that confusion, not strength.
bhagwad_gita::614.insight: It separates genuine discipline from self-punishment and aggression.

bhagwad_gita::615.verse_sanskrit: दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे । देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::615.verse_hindi: दान देना कर्तव्य है  ऐसे भावसे जो दान देश, काल और पात्रके प्राप्त होनेपर अनुपकारीको दिया जाता है, वह दान सात्त्विक कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::615.english_translation: A gift given with the feeling that giving is a duty, offered to a worthy person at the right place and time, is called sattvic.
bhagwad_gita::615.translation_literal: दातव्यम् (to be given) / इति (thus) / यत् (which) / दानम् (gift) / दीयते (is given) / अनुपकारिणे (to one who does not return a favor) / देशे (in place) / काले (in time) / च (and) / पात्रे (to a worthy recipient) / च (and) / तत् (that) / दानम् (gift) / सात्त्विकम् (sattvic) / स्मृतम् (is remembered as)
bhagwad_gita::615.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::615.essence: Giving becomes pure when nothing is being bought in return.
bhagwad_gita::615.simple_meaning: A gift is pure when it is given as a duty, to the right person, at the right time and place, without expecting anything back.
bhagwad_gita::615.simple_insight: Generosity feels lighter when it is free of self-interest.
bhagwad_gita::615.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna still shaken and Krishna teaching the nature of faith, the discussion turns to giving. After rejecting prideful and harmful charity, Krishna defines the clearest form of giving: timely, fitting, and free from expectation.
bhagwad_gita::615.modern_relevance: You send money to a friend who will never repay you, or help quietly without posting it anywhere. The act feels clean because it was never a transaction.
bhagwad_gita::615.insight: It shifts giving from exchange to offering, so the mind stops counting what comes back.

bhagwad_gita::616.verse_sanskrit: यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः । दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::616.verse_hindi: किन्तु जो दान प्रत्युपकारके लिये अथवा फलप्राप्तिका उद्देश्य बनाकर फिर क्लेशपूर्वक दिया जाता है, वह दान राजस कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::616.english_translation: But charity given in return, or for a desired result, and given grudgingly, is said to be rajasic.
bhagwad_gita::616.translation_literal: यत् (which) / तु (but) / प्रत्युपकारार्थम् (for return-favor) / फलम् (fruit, result) / उद्दिश्य (aiming at) / वा (or) / पुनः (again) / दीयते (is given) / च (and) / परिक्लिष्टम् (with strain, grudgingly) / तत् (that) / दानम् (gift, charity) / राजसम् (rajasic) / स्मृतम् (is called)
bhagwad_gita::616.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::616.essence: A gift becomes lesser the moment it starts asking for something back.
bhagwad_gita::616.simple_meaning: A gift loses its purity when you give it to get something back or to force a result, especially if you give it unwillingly.
bhagwad_gita::616.simple_insight: Generosity feels lighter when it is not secretly a trade.
bhagwad_gita::616.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna is classifying the nature of giving for Arjuna, who is still shaken and searching for right action. After pure giving, Krishna now names a second kind: charity mixed with expectation, strain, and return-seeking.
bhagwad_gita::616.modern_relevance: You send the money, then keep checking whether they thanked you properly. The gift was real, but part of you was still negotiating.
bhagwad_gita::616.insight: It teaches you to notice hidden bargaining inside generosity and strip it out.

bhagwad_gita::617.verse_hindi: जो दान बिना सत्कारके तथा अवज्ञापूर्वक अयोग्य देश और कालमें कुपात्रको दिया जाता है, वह दान तामस कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::617.english_translation: Charity given at the wrong place and time, to an unworthy recipient, without respect and with contempt, is called tamasic.
bhagwad_gita::617.translation_literal: अदेशकाले (at an improper place and time) / यत् (which) / दानम् (gift / charity) / अपात्रेभ्यः (to unworthy recipients) / च (and) / दीयते (is given) / असत्कृतम् (without respect) / अवज्ञातम् (with contempt) / तत् (that) / तामसम् (tamasic) / उदाहृतम् (is said to be)
bhagwad_gita::617.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::617.essence: A gift can become degrading when respect is missing.
bhagwad_gita::617.simple_meaning: A gift given at the wrong time and place, to the wrong person, without respect, is a low form of giving.
bhagwad_gita::617.simple_insight: Even generosity loses its value when it is careless or contemptuous.
bhagwad_gita::617.detailed_meaning: Krishna is classifying kinds of charity for Arjuna on the battlefield, where every action reveals the state of the heart. After praise of pure and self-interested giving, he now names the lowest form: giving badly, to the wrong recipient, with disrespect.
bhagwad_gita::617.modern_relevance: You hand someone cash while looking at your phone, hoping they go away. The act may look generous, but the attitude turns it cold.
bhagwad_gita::617.insight: It shifts attention from the outer act of giving to the quality of respect behind it.

bhagwad_gita::618.verse_sanskrit: तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः । ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा ॥
bhagwad_gita::618.verse_hindi: ऊँ, तत् और सत्  इन तीनों नामोंसे जिस परमात्माका निर्देश किया गया है, उसी परमात्माने सृष्टिके आदिमें वेदों, ब्राह्मणों और यज्ञोंकी रचना की है ॥
bhagwad_gita::618.english_translation: Om, Tat, and Sat are the three names by which the supreme reality is known. By that, the Vedas, the priests, and the sacrifices were established in the beginning.
bhagwad_gita::618.translation_literal: तत् (that) / सत् (being, real) / इति (thus) / निर्देशः (designation, name) / ब्रह्मणः (of Brahman, the supreme reality) / त्रिविधः (threefold) / स्मृतः (is remembered, is known) / ब्राह्मणाः (priests, sacred knowers) / तेन (by that) / वेदाः (the Vedas) / च (and) / यज्ञाः (sacrifices) / च (and) / विहिताः (were ordained, established) / पुरा (in the beginning, formerly)
bhagwad_gita::618.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::618.essence: Sacred action matters because it points beyond itself to what is real.
bhagwad_gita::618.simple_meaning: The sacred syllables Om, Tat, and Sat point to the supreme reality. They also mark the origin of the Vedas, priests, and sacrifices.
bhagwad_gita::618.simple_insight: Sacred words are not decoration; they point the mind back to what is most real.
bhagwad_gita::618.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield, but the teaching has moved from kinds of faith to the deepest frame behind all sacred action. He says that Om, Tat, and Sat are ancient names for the supreme reality, and that Vedic order, priests, and sacrifice arise from that source.
bhagwad_gita::618.modern_relevance: Before a memorial, a wedding, or a vow, people often reach for words that feel bigger than personal opinion. This verse reminds you that some words are meant to align action with what is most real, not just sound holy.
bhagwad_gita::618.insight: It shifts practice from ritual as habit to ritual as alignment with the real.

bhagwad_gita::619.verse_sanskrit: तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः । प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::619.verse_hindi: इसलिये वैदिक सिद्धान्तोंको माननेवाले पुरुषोंकी शास्त्रविधिसे नियत यज्ञ, दान और तपरूप क्रियाएँ सदा ऊँ इस परमात्माके नामका उच्चारण करके ही आरम्भ होती हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::619.english_translation: Therefore, the ritual acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity prescribed by scripture are always begun by uttering Om, for those who speak of Brahman.
bhagwad_gita::619.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) / ओम् इति (Om thus) / उदाहृत्य (having uttered) / यज्ञ (sacrifice) / दान (giving) / तपः-क्रियाः (austerity-acts) / प्रवर्तन्ते (are undertaken) / विधान-उक्ताः (prescribed by rule) / सततम् (always) / ब्रह्म-वादिनाम् (of those who speak of Brahman)
bhagwad_gita::619.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::619.essence: Sacred action begins by naming the supreme reality first.
