bhagwad_gita::619.simple_meaning: People who follow scripture begin sacrifice, giving, and austerity by saying Om.
bhagwad_gita::619.simple_insight: Even disciplined action can begin with reverence, not just habit.
bhagwad_gita::619.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna is explaining the sacred use of sacred sound. After naming Om, Tat, and Sat, he says that those who know Brahman begin their prescribed acts of sacrifice, giving, and austerity by uttering Om.
bhagwad_gita::619.modern_relevance: Before a difficult family conversation, you pause, breathe, and remember what you stand for. That small opening can turn a tense act into a sacred one.
bhagwad_gita::619.insight: It teaches you to begin action with awareness of the supreme reality, not mechanical routine.

bhagwad_gita::620.verse_sanskrit: तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः । दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षि ॥
bhagwad_gita::620.verse_hindi: तत् नामसे कहे जानेवाले परमात्माके लिये ही सब कुछ है  ऐसा मानकर मुक्ति चाहनेवाले मनुष्योंद्वारा फलकी इच्छासे रहित होकर अनेक प्रकारकी यज्ञ और तपरूप क्रियाएँ तथा दानरूप क्रियाएँ की जाती हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::620.english_translation: Thinking “all this is for the supreme reality,” seekers of freedom perform many kinds of sacrifice, austerity, and giving without wanting the result.
bhagwad_gita::620.translation_literal: तत् (that) / इति (thus) / अनभिसन्धाय (without aiming at) / फलम् (fruit, result) / यज्ञ (sacrifice) / तपः (austerity) / क्रियाः (actions) / दान-क्रियाः (acts of giving) / च (and) / विविधाः (various) / क्रियन्ते (are done) / मोक्ष-काङ्क्षि (by those desiring freedom)
bhagwad_gita::620.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::620.essence: Freedom deepens when action stops demanding a private return.
bhagwad_gita::620.simple_meaning: People seeking freedom do sacred actions, self-discipline, and giving without chasing personal reward. They treat the work itself as an offering.
bhagwad_gita::620.simple_insight: You can act with devotion and still let go of what comes back.
bhagwad_gita::620.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen before battle, and Krishna keeps building the inner discipline needed to act rightly. Here he explains that seekers of freedom perform sacrifice, austerity, and giving without clinging to personal gain.
bhagwad_gita::620.modern_relevance: You send the apology, make the donation, or do the hard right thing — and no one thanks you. The act still stands complete without applause.
bhagwad_gita::620.insight: It shifts action from self-benefit to offering, so the mind stops bargaining with life.

bhagwad_gita::621.verse_sanskrit: सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते । प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::621.verse_hindi: हे पार्थ  परमात्माके सत्इस नामका सत्तामात्रमें और श्रेष्ठ भावमें प्रयोग किया जाता है तथा प्रशंसनीय कर्मके साथ सत् शब्द जोड़ा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::621.english_translation: O Partha, the word sat is used for existence itself, for noble being, and for praiseworthy action.
bhagwad_gita::621.translation_literal: सत् (sat; the real / the good) / भावे (in existence / being) / साधुभावे (in noble being) / च (and) / सत् (sat) / इति (thus) / एतत् (this) / प्रयुज्यते (is used) / प्रशस्ते (praiseworthy) / कर्मणि (in action) / तथा (also) / सत्-शब्दः (the word sat) / पार्थ (O Partha) / युज्यते (is joined / applied)
bhagwad_gita::621.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::621.essence: What is real and worthy carries the mark of sat.
bhagwad_gita::621.simple_meaning: The word sat is used for what truly exists, for noble character, and for good action.
bhagwad_gita::621.simple_insight: It gives a clean standard: what is real, noble, and worthy of praise deserves your full trust.
bhagwad_gita::621.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield, where every action feels morally loaded. After saying that sacred acts should be offered without craving reward, he now explains the word sat: it points to reality, goodness, and worthy action.
bhagwad_gita::621.modern_relevance: You sign a document you know is honest, even though no one is watching. The quiet relief comes from knowing the act itself is clean, whether or not it brings applause.
bhagwad_gita::621.insight: It trains you to measure action by truth and worth, not by visible payoff.

bhagwad_gita::622.verse_sanskrit: यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते । कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते ॥
bhagwad_gita::622.verse_hindi: यज्ञ, तप और दानरूप क्रियामें जो स्थिति निष्ठा है, वह भी सत्  ऐसे कही जाती है और उस परमात्माके निमित्त किया जानेवाला कर्म भी सत्  ऐसा ही कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::622.english_translation: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and giving is called sat. Action done for that purpose is also called sat.
bhagwad_gita::622.translation_literal: यज्ञे (in sacrifice) / तपसि (in austerity) / दाने (in giving) / च (and) / स्थितिः (steadfastness) / सत् (sat) / इति (thus) / च (and) / उच्यते (is called) । कर्म (action) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / तत्-अर्थीयं (for that purpose) / सत् (sat) / इति (thus) / एव (indeed) / अभिधीयते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::622.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::622.essence: Steady offering makes ordinary action sacred.
bhagwad_gita::622.simple_meaning: Steady dedication in sacrifice, disciplined effort, and giving is called sat. Any action done for that sacred purpose is also called sat.
bhagwad_gita::622.simple_insight: Your effort becomes meaningful when it is steady and offered with sincerity.
bhagwad_gita::622.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains the quality of true offering. In this verse, Krishna says that steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and giving is itself sacred, and so is any action done for that higher purpose.
bhagwad_gita::622.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for a hard promise no one can verify: caring for a parent, finishing a repair, telling the truth. The steadiness itself gives the act its worth.
bhagwad_gita::622.insight: It shifts attention from the size of the act to the steadiness and intention behind it.

bhagwad_gita::623.verse_sanskrit: अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् । असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह ॥
bhagwad_gita::623.verse_hindi: हे पार्थ  अश्रद्धासे किया हुआ हवन, दिया हुआ दान और तपा हुआ तप तथा और भी जो,कुछ किया जाय, वह सब असत्  ऐसा कहा जाता है ।  उसका फल न यहाँ होता है, न मरनेके बाद ही होता है अर्थात् उसका कहीं भी सत् फल नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::623.english_translation: O Partha, sacrifice, charity, austerity, and any deed done without trust are called unreal. Its fruit exists neither here nor after death.
bhagwad_gita::623.translation_literal: अश्रद्धया (without trust) / हुतं (offered in sacrifice) / दत्तं (given) / तपःतप्तं (austerity performed) / कृतं (done) / च (and) / यत् (whatever) / असत् (unreal) / इति (thus) / उच्यते (is called) / पार्थ (O Partha) / न (not) / च (and) / तत् (that) / प्रेत्य (after death) / न (not) / इह (here)
bhagwad_gita::623.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::623.essence: Trust is what makes action real; without it, effort becomes empty.
bhagwad_gita::623.simple_meaning: Actions like sacrifice, charity, and austerity lose their value when done without trust. They produce no real result in this life or after death.
bhagwad_gita::623.simple_insight: Trust is what makes effort alive; without it, even noble action feels hollow.
bhagwad_gita::623.detailed_meaning: Krishna has just explained that the word 'sat' belongs to real, worthy action. Now, with Arjuna still shaken on the battlefield, he closes the thought by saying that sacrifice, giving, and austerity done without trust are empty and bear no lasting fruit.
bhagwad_gita::623.modern_relevance: You donate money because it looks good, or apologize because others expect it, but your heart is absent. The act may happen, yet it leaves no real trace inside you or around you.
bhagwad_gita::623.insight: It shifts action from performance to sincerity, showing that inner trust is what gives deeds weight.

bhagwad_gita::624.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचसंन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् । त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन ॥
bhagwad_gita::624.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे महाबाहो  हे हृषीकेश  हे केशिनिषूदन  मैं संन्यास और त्यागका तत्त्व अलगअलग जानना चाहता हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::624.english_translation: Arjuna said: O mighty-armed one, O master of the senses, O slayer of Kesi, I wish to know the distinct truth of renunciation and relinquishment.
bhagwad_gita::624.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / संन्यासस्य (of renunciation) / महाबाहो (O mighty-armed one) / तत्त्वम् (the truth) / इच्छामि (I wish) / वेदितुम् (to know) / त्यागस्य (of relinquishment) / च (and) / हृषीकेश (O master of the senses) / पृथक् (separately) / केशिनिषूदन (O slayer of Kesi)
bhagwad_gita::624.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::624.essence: Clear seeing begins with asking what must be separated.
bhagwad_gita::624.simple_meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain the difference between renunciation and relinquishment.
bhagwad_gita::624.simple_insight: Real clarity begins by asking the right distinction.
bhagwad_gita::624.detailed_meaning: On the brink of the final teaching, Arjuna stops Krishna and asks for a clean distinction: what is renunciation, and what is relinquishment? The war still hangs in the air, but Arjuna wants the final framework before he acts.
bhagwad_gita::624.modern_relevance: You are staring at two options that look similar but lead to very different lives. Before you quit, give up, or let go, you need to know what each one really means.
bhagwad_gita::624.insight: It shifts the mind from vague spirituality to precise discernment before action.

bhagwad_gita::625.verse_sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचकाम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः । सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः ॥
bhagwad_gita::625.english_translation: The wise call renunciation the giving up of desire-born actions. The discerning call renunciation the giving up of all results of action.
bhagwad_gita::625.translation_literal: श्रीभगवानुवाच (the Blessed Lord said) / काम्यानां (of desire-born) / कर्मणां (actions) / न्यासं (giving up) / संन्यासं (renunciation) / कवयः (the wise) / विदुः (know) / सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं (giving up all fruits of action) / प्राहुः (they call) / त्यागं (renunciation) / विचक्षणाः (the discerning)
bhagwad_gita::625.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::625.essence: Renunciation means releasing both craving and attachment to results.
bhagwad_gita::625.simple_meaning: Wise people define renunciation in two ways: giving up actions driven by desire, and giving up attachment to all results of action.
bhagwad_gita::625.simple_insight: Freedom begins when you stop clinging to what action might bring you.
bhagwad_gita::625.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Arjuna asks Krishna to separate renunciation from giving up action. Krishna answers by defining both terms carefully, because Arjuna needs a clear way to act without inner bondage.
bhagwad_gita::625.modern_relevance: You send the hard message, hit submit, and then keep checking for approval. This verse cuts that loop: do the work, then release the grip on what comes back.
bhagwad_gita::625.insight: It shifts the mind from controlling outcomes to releasing attachment while still acting.

bhagwad_gita::626.verse_sanskrit: त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः । यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे ॥
bhagwad_gita::626.verse_hindi: श्रीभगवान् बोले  कई विद्वान् काम्यकर्मोंके त्यागको संन्यास कहते हैं और कई विद्वान् सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंके फलके त्यागको त्याग कहते हैं ।  कई विद्वान् कहते हैं कि कर्मोंको दोषकी तरह छोड़ देना चाहिये और कई विद्वान् कहते हैं कि यज्ञ, दान और तपरूप कर्मोंका त्याग नहीं करना चाहिये ॥
bhagwad_gita::626.english_translation: Some wise people say all action should be abandoned as flawed. Others say sacrifice, giving, and disciplined effort should not be abandoned.
bhagwad_gita::626.translation_literal: त्याज्यम् (to be abandoned) / दोषवत् (as flawed) / इति (thus) / एके (some) / कर्म (action) / प्राहुः (say) / मनीषिणः (the wise) / यज्ञदानतपःकर्म (sacrifice-giving-austerity-actions) / न (not) / त्याज्यम् (to be abandoned) / इति (thus) / च (and) / अपरे (others)
bhagwad_gita::626.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::626.essence: Renunciation is not simple refusal; some actions must remain.
bhagwad_gita::626.simple_meaning: Some teachers say action itself should be dropped because it seems flawed. Others say sacrifice, charity, and disciplined effort should never be dropped.
bhagwad_gita::626.simple_insight: Not all renunciation is the same. The real question is what should be released and what must continue.
bhagwad_gita::626.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has asked the final question: what is renunciation, and what is true letting go? Krishna now shows that even wise people disagree. Some reject action itself; others preserve sacrifice, giving, and discipline.
bhagwad_gita::626.modern_relevance: You’re about to quit a commitment because it feels messy and imperfect. Part of you wants to drop everything; part of you knows some responsibilities still matter.
bhagwad_gita::626.insight: It separates blind rejection from wise release, so you can keep what purifies action and drop what binds it.

bhagwad_gita::627.verse_sanskrit: निश्चयं श्रृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम । त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः संप्रकीर्तितः ॥
bhagwad_gita::627.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  तू संन्यास और त्याग  इन दोनोंमेंसे पहले त्यागके विषयमें मेरा निश्चय सुन क्योंकि हे पुरुषश्रेष्ठ  त्याग तीन प्रकारका कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::627.english_translation: Arjuna, first hear my settled view on renunciation. Renunciation is said to be threefold.
bhagwad_gita::627.translation_literal: निश्चयं (settled view) / श्रृणु (hear) / मे (my) / तत्र (there) / त्यागे (on renunciation) / भरतसत्तम (best of the Bharatas) । / त्यागः (renunciation) / हि (indeed) / पुरुषव्याघ्र (tiger among men) / त्रिविधः (threefold) / संप्रकीर्तितः (is declared) ॥
bhagwad_gita::627.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::627.essence: Renunciation is not one thing; it has distinct forms.
bhagwad_gita::627.simple_meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna to listen carefully to his clear view on renunciation. He says renunciation has three forms, so the subject needs to be understood with precision.
bhagwad_gita::627.simple_insight: Clarity replaces confusion when a hard choice is named carefully.
bhagwad_gita::627.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna still stands trapped between action and withdrawal. Krishna begins to untangle the final teaching by saying that renunciation itself must be understood in distinct forms, because not every kind of letting go means the same thing.
bhagwad_gita::627.modern_relevance: You are staring at an email that could end a partnership, and you keep rereading it. Before the decision, you need to know what kind of letting go is actually being asked of you.
bhagwad_gita::627.insight: It shifts the mind from vague renunciation to precise discrimination about what must be released.

bhagwad_gita::628.verse_sanskrit: यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत् । यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::628.verse_hindi: यज्ञ, दान और तपरूप कर्मोंका त्याग नहीं करना चाहिये, प्रत्युत उनको तो करना ही चाहिये क्योंकि यज्ञ, दान और तप  ये तीनों ही कर्म मनीषियोंको पवित्र करनेवाले हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::628.english_translation: Sacrifice, giving, and disciplined effort should not be abandoned; they must be done. These three actions purify thoughtful people.
bhagwad_gita::628.translation_literal: यज्ञ (sacrifice) / दान (giving) / तपःकर्म (discipline-action) / न (not) / त्याज्यम् (to be abandoned) / कार्यम् (to be done) / एव (indeed) / तत् (that) / यज्ञः (sacrifice) / दानम् (giving) / तपः (disciplined effort) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / पावनानि (purifying) / मनीषिणाम् (of thoughtful people)
bhagwad_gita::628.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::628.essence: What purifies you should be done, not dropped.
bhagwad_gita::628.simple_meaning: Sacrifice, giving, and disciplined effort should not be dropped. They are actions that purify a thoughtful person.
bhagwad_gita::628.simple_insight: Doing what cleanses you matters more than escaping effort.
bhagwad_gita::628.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still trapped between renouncing action and acting rightly. Krishna answers by naming three acts that should never be abandoned: sacrifice, giving, and disciplined effort. He is narrowing renunciation into a cleaner, truer form.
bhagwad_gita::628.modern_relevance: You want to skip the donation, the difficult conversation, the morning practice. Something in you calls it optional. Krishna says these are exactly the acts that clear the mind.
bhagwad_gita::628.insight: It shifts renunciation from avoidance to purification through action.

bhagwad_gita::629.verse_sanskrit: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च । कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्िचतं मतमुत्तमम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::629.verse_hindi: हे पार्थ  पूर्वोक्त यज्ञ, दान और तप   इन कर्मोंको तथा दूसरे भी कर्मोंको आसक्ति और फलोंका त्याग करके करना चाहिये  यह मेरा निश्चित किया हुआ उत्तम मत है ॥
bhagwad_gita::629.english_translation: Even these actions, and all other actions, should be done without attachment and without wanting their results. This is my settled and best teaching, O Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::629.translation_literal: एतानि (these) / अपि (also) / तु (indeed) / कर्माणि (actions) / सङ्गं (attachment) / त्यक्त्वा (having given up) / फलानि (results) / च (and) / कर्तव्यानीति (ought to be done) / मे (my) / पार्थ (O Partha) / निश्चितं (settled) / मतम् (opinion/teaching) / उत्तमम् (best)
bhagwad_gita::629.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::629.essence: Right action is complete only when desire for reward is dropped.
bhagwad_gita::629.simple_meaning: Even sacred actions and all other duties should be done without clinging to results. Krishna says this is the best and settled teaching.
bhagwad_gita::629.simple_insight: You can give your full effort without carrying the burden of control.
bhagwad_gita::629.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and fear. Krishna continues his teaching on renunciation, making one thing clear: even offerings, charity, and discipline should be done without attachment to results. This verse sharpens the path of action.
bhagwad_gita::629.modern_relevance: You send the message, make the apology, or hand in the project, then sit with the uncertainty. The value was in doing it rightly, not in controlling how it lands.
bhagwad_gita::629.insight: It shifts action from outcome-hunger to clean participation in what must be done.

bhagwad_gita::630.verse_sanskrit: नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते । मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः ॥
bhagwad_gita::630.verse_hindi: नियत कर्मका तो त्याग करना उचित नहीं है ।  उसका मोहपूर्वक त्याग करना तामस कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::630.english_translation: Abandoning prescribed action is not right. Giving it up in confusion is called tamasic.
bhagwad_gita::630.translation_literal: नियतस्य (of the prescribed) / तु (indeed) / संन्यासः (renunciation) / कर्मणः (of action) / न (not) / उपपद्यते (is उचित / is fitting) । / मोहात् (from confusion) / तस्य (of that) / परित्यागः (abandonment) / तामसः (tamasic) / परिकीर्तितः (is called)
bhagwad_gita::630.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::630.essence: Right action should not be abandoned just because it feels difficult.
bhagwad_gita::630.simple_meaning: You should not give up the work that is properly yours to do. If you drop it out of confusion, that is a dark and dull kind of renunciation.
bhagwad_gita::630.simple_insight: Relief comes from knowing that clarity, not escape, is the real test of renunciation.
bhagwad_gita::630.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still trapped between action and refusal. Krishna now sharpens the teaching: some duties cannot be discarded just because they feel heavy. This verse defines confused renunciation as a failure of understanding.
bhagwad_gita::630.modern_relevance: You are about to quit a hard conversation because it feels uncomfortable, not because it is wrong. The urge to escape can look noble, but confusion is not wisdom.
bhagwad_gita::630.insight: It shifts the mind from avoiding responsibility to testing whether the urge to quit is clear or merely fearful.

bhagwad_gita::631.verse_sanskrit: दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् । स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::631.verse_hindi: जो कुछ कर्म है, वह दुःखरूप ही है  ऐसा समझकर कोई शारीरिक क्लेशके भयसे उसका त्याग कर दे, तो वह राजस त्याग करके भी त्यागके फलको नहीं पाता ॥
bhagwad_gita::631.english_translation: If someone gives up action thinking it is only suffering and fearing bodily strain, that renunciation is passionate, and it brings no fruit of renunciation.
bhagwad_gita::631.translation_literal: दुःखम् (suffering) / इति एव (just so) / यत् (which) / कर्म (action) / कायक्लेश-भयात् (from fear of bodily strain) / त्यजेत् (would abandon) / सः (that one) / कृत्वा (having done) / राजसम् (passionate) / त्यागम् (renunciation) / न (not) / एव (indeed) / त्याग-फलम् (fruit of renunciation) / लभेत् (would obtain)
bhagwad_gita::631.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::631.essence: Fearful withdrawal is not freedom; it is avoidance wearing a noble name.
bhagwad_gita::631.simple_meaning: Giving up your responsibilities because they feel hard is not true renunciation. It is a restless, fear-driven rejection of effort.
bhagwad_gita::631.simple_insight: Real letting go is clear and strong, not scared and avoidant.
bhagwad_gita::631.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still trapped between action and retreat. Krishna corrects a subtle mistake: abandoning duty because it feels painful is not purity, only fear in disguise. That kind of giving up brings no inner gain.
bhagwad_gita::631.modern_relevance: You quit the hard conversation, then tell yourself you are “protecting your peace.” The body may feel safer, but the mind knows the move was avoidance, not freedom.
bhagwad_gita::631.insight: It separates true renunciation from escape, so you stop dressing fear as virtue.

bhagwad_gita::632.verse_sanskrit: कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन । सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः ॥
bhagwad_gita::632.verse_hindi: हे अर्जुन  केवल कर्तव्यमात्र करना है  ऐसा समझकर जो नियत कर्म आसक्ति और फलका त्याग करके किया जाता है, वही सात्त्विक त्याग माना गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::632.english_translation: Arjuna, when fixed duty is done as only duty, without clinging to results, that renunciation is called sattvic.
bhagwad_gita::632.translation_literal: कार्यम् (to be done) / इति एव (thus only) / यत् (which) / कर्म (action) / नियतम् (fixed, prescribed) / क्रियते (is done) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / सङ्गम् (attachment) / त्यक्त्वा (having given up) / फलम् (result, fruit) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / सः (that) / त्यागः (renunciation) / सात्त्विकः (sattvic) / मतः (is considered)
bhagwad_gita::632.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::632.essence: Renunciation means doing what must be done without gripping the result.
bhagwad_gita::632.simple_meaning: Fixed duty becomes pure renunciation when it is done without attachment to personal gain or to the result.
bhagwad_gita::632.simple_insight: You can stay committed without becoming needy about what comes back.
bhagwad_gita::632.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still caught between action and withdrawal. Krishna now refines renunciation: not abandoning duty, but doing the required work with no grasping for reward. That is the cleanest form of letting go.
bhagwad_gita::632.modern_relevance: You send the message that could change everything, then stare at the screen for the reply. This verse says the honesty was the task; the response was never yours to hold.
bhagwad_gita::632.insight: It shifts action from reward-chasing to clean responsibility.

bhagwad_gita::633.verse_sanskrit: न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते । त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः ॥
bhagwad_gita::633.verse_hindi: जो अकुशल कर्मसे द्वेष नहीं करता और कुशल कर्ममें आसक्त नहीं होता, वह त्यागी, बुद्धिमान्, सन्देहरहित और अपने स्वरूपमें स्थित है ॥
bhagwad_gita::633.english_translation: One who neither rejects unwholesome action nor clings to wholesome action is a wise renunciate, free of doubt and established in clear seeing.
bhagwad_gita::633.translation_literal: न द्वेष्टि (does not hate) / अकुशलं (unwholesome) / कर्म (action) / कुशले (in wholesome) / न (not) / अनुषज्जते (clings) / त्यागी (renunciate) / सत्त्वसमाविष्टः (filled with clarity) / मेधावी (wise) / छिन्नसंशयः (cut free of doubt)
bhagwad_gita::633.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::633.essence: Freedom means neither resisting the hard nor craving the pleasant.
bhagwad_gita::633.simple_meaning: A truly wise renunciate does not hate difficult actions and does not become attached to good ones. Such a person is steady, clear, and free of doubt.
bhagwad_gita::633.simple_insight: You stop fighting reality and stop grasping at approval. That inner release makes action cleaner.
bhagwad_gita::633.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has been told that real renunciation is not escape. Krishna now sharpens the point: a person who has seen clearly neither hates difficult work nor clings to pleasant work. That steadiness is true renunciation.
bhagwad_gita::633.modern_relevance: You take the job nobody wants because it matters, but you do not build your identity around being the hero. You do what must be done without craving praise or resenting the task.
bhagwad_gita::633.insight: It shifts renunciation from avoidance to freedom from reaction, so action can stay clean under any condition.

bhagwad_gita::634.verse_sanskrit: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः । यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते ॥
bhagwad_gita::634.verse_hindi: कारण कि देहधारी मनुष्यके द्वारा सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंका त्याग करना सम्भव नहीं है ।  इसलिये जो कर्मफलका त्यागी है, वही त्यागी है  ऐसा कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::634.english_translation: For embodied beings, total renunciation of action is impossible. Therefore, one who renounces the fruits of action is called a renunciant.
bhagwad_gita::634.translation_literal: न (not) / हि (indeed) / देहभृता (by one who bears a body) / शक्यम् (possible) / त्यक्तुम् (to renounce) / कर्माणि (actions) / अशेषतः (without remainder, completely) । / यः (who) / तु (but) / कर्मफलत्यागी (renouncer of the fruits of action) / सः (that one) / त्यागी (renunciant) / इति (thus) / अभिधीयते (is called) ॥
bhagwad_gita::634.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::634.essence: Freedom begins when action continues and attachment stops.
bhagwad_gita::634.simple_meaning: A person with a body cannot give up all action. Real renunciation means giving up attachment to the results, not abandoning work itself.
bhagwad_gita::634.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing you do not need to escape action to be free.
bhagwad_gita::634.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna teaches him the final synthesis of renunciation. Here Krishna clarifies that embodied life always involves action, so true renunciation is not quitting work but letting go of the reward.
bhagwad_gita::634.modern_relevance: You send the hard message, hit submit, and wait for the fallout. You cannot control every consequence, but you can stop clinging to what happens next.
bhagwad_gita::634.insight: It shifts the mind from escaping responsibility to releasing ownership of outcomes.

bhagwad_gita::635.verse_sanskrit: अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम् । भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित् ॥
bhagwad_gita::635.verse_hindi: कर्मफलका त्याग न करनेवाले मनुष्योंको कर्मोंका इष्ट, अनिष्ट और मिश्रित  ऐसे तीन प्रकारका फल मरनेके बाद भी होता है परन्तु कर्मफलका त्याग करनेवालोंको कहीं भी नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::635.english_translation: For those who do not renounce the fruits of action, action produces three kinds of results—pleasant, unpleasant, and mixed—even after death; but for those who renounce the fruits, there is no such result anywhere.
bhagwad_gita::635.translation_literal: अनिष्टम् (unpleasant) / इष्टम् (pleasant) / मिश्रम् (mixed) / च (and) / त्रिविधम् (threefold) / कर्मणः (of action) / फलम् (fruit, result) / भवति (becomes, occurs) / अत्यागिनाम् (for those who do not renounce) / प्रेत्य (after death) / न तु (but not) / संन्यासिनाम् (for renouncers) / क्वचित् (anywhere, at any time)
bhagwad_gita::635.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::635.essence: The chain of action ends when desire for its fruit ends.
bhagwad_gita::635.simple_meaning: If you keep wanting the result of your actions, those actions keep producing effects for you. If you let go of results, that chain ends.
bhagwad_gita::635.simple_insight: There is relief in not carrying your actions as personal baggage.
bhagwad_gita::635.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna deepens the lesson on renunciation: action itself is unavoidable, but bondage comes from clinging to its fruit. That is why this verse distinguishes the renouncer from the one still tied to results.
bhagwad_gita::635.modern_relevance: You send the message, then keep reopening the chat for a reply that decides your mood. The verse points to the hidden chain: craving the result keeps the action alive inside you.
bhagwad_gita::635.insight: It shifts attention from owning outcomes to releasing them after action.

bhagwad_gita::636.verse_sanskrit: पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे । सांख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::636.verse_hindi: हे महाबाहो  कर्मोंका अन्त करनेवाले सांख्यसिद्धान्तमें सम्पूर्ण कर्मोंकी सिद्धिके लिये ये पाँच कारण बताये गये हैं, इनको तू मेरेसे समझ ॥
bhagwad_gita::636.english_translation: O mighty-armed one, learn from Me these five causes, taught in the Sankhya system, for the accomplishment of all actions.
bhagwad_gita::636.translation_literal: पञ्च (five) / एतानि (these) / महाबाहो (O mighty-armed one) / कारणानि (causes) / निबोध (understand) / मे (from Me) / सांख्ये (in Sankhya) / कृतान्ते (in the doctrine of conclusion) / प्रोक्तानि (are said) / सिद्धये (for accomplishment) / सर्वकर्मणाम् (of all actions)
bhagwad_gita::636.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::636.essence: Action has many causes; the ego is not the whole story.
bhagwad_gita::636.simple_meaning: Krishna asks Arjuna to understand the five causes that make any action possible. Human action is not as simple as one person deciding and doing everything alone.
bhagwad_gita::636.simple_insight: It loosens the grip of self-blame and pride. Not everything that happens is carried by one doer.
bhagwad_gita::636.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still trapped in confusion about action and renunciation. Krishna now explains that every action depends on five causes, preparing Arjuna to see that doing is more complex than ego claims.
bhagwad_gita::636.modern_relevance: You replay a mistake at 2 a.m. and ask, “How could I have done that?” Or you take full credit for a win. This verse widens the frame: one person is rarely the whole cause.
bhagwad_gita::636.insight: It shifts the mind from personal monopoly over action to a clearer view of shared causes and conditions.

bhagwad_gita::637.verse_sanskrit: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् । विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::637.verse_hindi: इसमें कर्मोंकी सिद्धिमें अधिष्ठान तथा कर्ता और अनेक प्रकारके करण एवं विविध प्रकारकी अलगअलग चेष्टाएँ और वैसे ही पाँचवाँ कारण दैव संस्कार है ॥
bhagwad_gita::637.english_translation: The field, the doer, the instruments, the many efforts, and the fifth factor, the unseen force, all shape every action.
bhagwad_gita::637.translation_literal: अधिष्ठानम् (the basis) / तथा (and) / कर्ता (the doer) / करणम् (the instruments) / च (and) / पृथग्विधम् (of many kinds) / विविधाः (varied) / च (and) / पृथक् (separate) / चेष्टाः (efforts) / दैवम् (the unseen force) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / अत्र (here) / पञ्चमम् (the fifth)
bhagwad_gita::637.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::637.essence: Action has many causes, and no one factor owns the result.
bhagwad_gita::637.simple_meaning: Every action depends on several causes: the base, the doer, the tools, the different efforts, and a fifth factor beyond human control.
bhagwad_gita::637.simple_insight: It softens blame and pride. Not everything that happens can be reduced to one person’s will.
bhagwad_gita::637.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen by the weight of action and consequence. Krishna now breaks action into its causes: the base, the agent, the instruments, the separate efforts, and a fifth factor beyond them. He is showing why no one acts alone.
bhagwad_gita::637.modern_relevance: You replay a difficult conversation for hours, asking who caused the damage. This verse reminds you that outcomes are rarely single-cause; many forces move together, including factors you could not control.
bhagwad_gita::637.insight: It shifts the mind from absolute personal control to a clearer view of shared causation.

bhagwad_gita::638.verse_sanskrit: शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः । न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः ॥
bhagwad_gita::638.verse_hindi: मनुष्य, शरीर वाणी और मनके द्वारा शास्त्रविहित अथवा शास्त्रविरुद्ध जो कुछ भी कर्म आरम्भ करता है, उसके ये पूर्वोक्त पाँचों हेतु होते हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::638.english_translation: Whatever action a person begins through body, speech, and mind—right or wrong—has these five causes.
bhagwad_gita::638.translation_literal: शरीरवाङ्मनोभिः (through body, speech, and mind) / यत् (whatever) / कर्म (action) / प्रारभते (begins) / नरः (a person) / न्याय्यम् (right, proper) / वा (or) / विपरीतम् (wrong, contrary) / वा (or) / पञ्च (five) / एते (these) / तस्य (of that) / हेतवः (causes)
bhagwad_gita::638.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::638.essence: Every deed comes from five causes, not one isolated doer.
bhagwad_gita::638.simple_meaning: Any action a person starts through body, speech, or mind is driven by five causes, whether the action is proper or improper.
bhagwad_gita::638.simple_insight: You are not the lone maker of your actions; many forces are already at work.
bhagwad_gita::638.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Krishna is breaking Arjuna’s usual idea of agency. After naming five causes behind every action, he adds that any deed begun through body, speech, or mind—right or wrong—arises from those causes, not from a single isolated doer.
bhagwad_gita::638.modern_relevance: You send the message in anger, then later say, “I just snapped.” Krishna points earlier: the body, words, mind, habits, and conditions were already moving.
bhagwad_gita::638.insight: It shifts blame and pride away from a single ego and toward a clearer view of how action actually arises.

bhagwad_gita::639.verse_sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
bhagwad_gita::639.verse_hindi: परन्तु ऐसे पाँच हेतुओंके होनेपर भी जो उस कर्मोंके विषयमें केवल शुद्ध आत्माको कर्ता मानता है, वह दुर्मति ठीक नहीं समझता क्योंकि उसकी बुद्धि शुद्ध नहीं है ॥
bhagwad_gita::639.english_translation: But one who sees only the pure self as the doer, even though these five causes are present, has not seen rightly; such a confused mind does not understand.
bhagwad_gita::639.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / एवम् (thus) / सति (being present) / कर्तारम् (the doer) / आत्मानम् (the self) / केवलम् (only) / तु (but) / यः (who) / पश्यति (sees) / अकृतबुद्धित्वात् (because of unformed understanding) / न (not) / सः (he) / पश्यति (sees) / दुर्मतिः (confused-minded one)
bhagwad_gita::639.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::639.essence: Action has many causes; the pure self is not the lone doer.
bhagwad_gita::639.simple_meaning: Action does not come from the pure self alone. A confused person wrongly thinks the self is the only doer and misses the real causes at work.
bhagwad_gita::639.simple_insight: You can stop carrying the whole burden of authorship. Clear seeing brings relief from false responsibility.
bhagwad_gita::639.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Krishna is dismantling Arjuna's confusion about action. After naming the five causes behind every deed, he warns that a person with muddled understanding wrongly blames or claims the pure self as the sole doer.
bhagwad_gita::639.modern_relevance: You replay a conversation at 1 a.m. and decide, "I caused everything." Krishna cuts through that mental trap: one person is rarely the whole cause.
bhagwad_gita::639.insight: It shifts the mind from personal overclaiming to clear seeing of shared causes.

bhagwad_gita::640.verse_sanskrit: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते । हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::640.verse_hindi: जिसका अहंकृतभाव नहीं है और जिसकी बुद्धि लिप्त नहीं होती, वह इन सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंको मारकर भी न मारता है और न बँधता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::640.english_translation: One who has no sense of separate self and whose understanding remains unstained does not kill, even by killing all these beings, and is not bound.
bhagwad_gita::640.translation_literal: यस्य (whose) / न (not) / अहंकृतः (made by ego; marked by separate self) / भावः (state) / बुद्धिः (understanding) / यस्य (whose) / न (not) / लिप्यते (is stained; clings) / हत्वा अपि (even after killing) / सः (that one) / इमान् लोकान् (these beings) / न (not) / हन्ति (kills) / न (not) / निबध्यते (is bound)
bhagwad_gita::640.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::640.essence: Without egoic ownership, action leaves no stain.
bhagwad_gita::640.simple_meaning: A person who has dropped ego and stays inwardly untouched is not truly the killer, and is not trapped by the act.
bhagwad_gita::640.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that action does not have to stain you when ego is absent.
bhagwad_gita::640.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna is still answering Arjuna's panic about action and guilt. After explaining the many causes behind any deed, he now says the deepest shift is to lose the sense of separate doership. Then even the hardest action does not bind.
bhagwad_gita::640.modern_relevance: You make the call that ends a broken partnership. The words are heavy, but you do not have to carry them as personal guilt if you acted from clarity, not ego.
bhagwad_gita::640.insight: It shifts responsibility from self-image to clear action, so the mind stops clinging to ownership.

bhagwad_gita::641.verse_sanskrit: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना । करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसंग्रहः ॥
bhagwad_gita::641.verse_hindi: ज्ञान, ज्ञेय और परिज्ञाता  इन तीनोंसे कर्मप्रेरणा होती है तथा करण, कर्म और कर्ता  इन तीनोंसे कर्मसंग्रह होता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::641.english_translation: Knowledge, the object known, and the knower—these three drive action. Instrument, act, and actor—these three make up the whole of action.
bhagwad_gita::641.translation_literal: ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / ज्ञेयम् (the object known) / परिज्ञाता (the knower) / त्रिविधा (threefold) / कर्मचोदना (impulse to action) / करणम् (instrument) / कर्म (action) / कर्ता (doer) / इति (thus) / त्रिविधः (threefold) / कर्मसंग्रहः (whole of action)
bhagwad_gita::641.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::641.essence: Action is a system, not a single ego doing everything.
bhagwad_gita::641.simple_meaning: Action is built from three parts: the knower, what is known, and the knowing itself; and also from the tool, the act, and the doer.
bhagwad_gita::641.simple_insight: It loosens the grip of “I alone did this” and shows action as a shared process.
bhagwad_gita::641.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is trying to understand what action really is after Krishna has already shown that the true self does not kill or bind. Krishna now breaks action into its parts—knower, known, and knowing; tool, act, and actor—to prepare Arjuna for deeper discrimination.
bhagwad_gita::641.modern_relevance: You replay a harsh conversation in your head and ask, “Who caused this?” The mind wants one culprit, but the event came from many parts moving together.
bhagwad_gita::641.insight: It shifts the mind from blaming a single doer to seeing the structure behind any action.

bhagwad_gita::642.verse_sanskrit: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः । प्रोच्यते गुणसंख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि ॥
bhagwad_gita::642.verse_hindi: गुणसंख्यान गुणोंके सम्बन्धसे प्रत्येक पदार्थके भिन्नभिन्न भेदोंकी गणना करनेवाले शास्त्रमें गुणोंके भेदसे ज्ञान और कर्म तथा कर्ता तीनतीन प्रकारसे ही कहे जाते हैं, उनको भी तुम यथार्थरूपसे सुनो ॥
bhagwad_gita::642.english_translation: In the analysis of the three qualities, knowledge, action, and the doer are each said to be threefold. Listen now to these distinctions as they truly are.
bhagwad_gita::642.translation_literal: ज्ञानं (knowledge) / कर्म (action) / च (and) / कर्ता (doer) / च (and) / त्रिधा (threefold) / एव (indeed) / गुणभेदतः (according to the distinctions of the qualities) / प्रोच्यते (are said) / गुणसंख्याने (in the analysis of the qualities) / यथावत् (as they truly are) / शृणु (listen) / तानि (those) / अपि (also)
bhagwad_gita::642.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::642.essence: Every action, knower, and deed carries the mark of a quality.
bhagwad_gita::642.simple_meaning: Knowledge, action, and the doer are each understood in three different ways according to the three qualities. Krishna asks Arjuna to listen carefully to this classification.
bhagwad_gita::642.simple_insight: It reminds you that not all thinking, acting, or acting-from-self is the same.
bhagwad_gita::642.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains how action works beneath the surface. After saying that knowledge, action, and the doer can be divided in three ways, Krishna prepares Arjuna to hear how the qualities shape everything.
bhagwad_gita::642.modern_relevance: You can do the same task with a clear mind, a restless mind, or a dull mind. The outer act looks identical, but the inner quality changes everything.
bhagwad_gita::642.insight: It shifts attention from the outer event to the quality of consciousness behind it.

bhagwad_gita::643.verse_sanskrit: सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते । अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::643.verse_hindi: जिस ज्ञानके द्वारा साधक सम्पूर्ण विभक्त प्राणियोंमें विभागरहित एक अविनाशी भावसत्ता को देखता है, उस ज्ञानको तुम सात्त्विक समझो ॥
bhagwad_gita::643.english_translation: Know that knowledge to be sattvic by which one sees the one imperishable reality in all beings, undivided among the divided.
bhagwad_gita::643.translation_literal: सर्वभूतेषु (in all beings) / येन (by which) / एकम् (one) / भावम् (reality/state) / अव्ययम् (imperishable) / ईक्षते (sees) / अविभक्तम् (undivided) / विभक्तेषु (among the divided) / तत् (that) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / विद्धि (know) / सात्त्विकम् (sattvic)
bhagwad_gita::643.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::643.essence: True understanding sees one undivided reality inside every divided form.
bhagwad_gita::643.simple_meaning: Pure understanding sees one unchanging reality in all beings, even though they appear separate.
bhagwad_gita::643.simple_insight: Separation stops feeling final. You begin to notice the same reality shining through every face.
bhagwad_gita::643.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna frozen before battle, Krishna turns from action to vision. He explains that the highest clear understanding sees one imperishable reality in all beings, even though they appear divided.
bhagwad_gita::643.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after an argument and see only sides, labels, and distance. This verse asks you to look again and notice the shared humanity beneath the split.
bhagwad_gita::643.insight: It shifts perception from surface differences to the underlying unity that makes judgment softer.

bhagwad_gita::644.verse_sanskrit: पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान् । वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::644.verse_hindi: परन्तु जो ज्ञान अर्थात् जिस ज्ञानके द्वारा मनुष्य सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें अलगअलग अनेक भावोंको अलगअलग रूपसे जानता है, उस ज्ञानको तुम राजस समझो ॥
bhagwad_gita::644.english_translation: But know that knowledge as rajasic by which one sees many different beings as separate and distinct in all beings.
bhagwad_gita::644.translation_literal: पृथक्त्वेन (by separateness) / तु (but) / यत् (which) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / नानाभावान् (many states/traits) / पृथग्विधान् (separately formed) / वेत्ति (knows) / सर्वेषु भूतेषु (in all beings) / तत् (that) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / विद्धि (know) / राजसम् (rajasic)
bhagwad_gita::644.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::644.essence: Dividing everything into parts is not clarity; it is restless seeing.
bhagwad_gita::644.simple_meaning: Knowledge that only notices differences and treats every being as separate is restless and driven by ego.
bhagwad_gita::644.simple_insight: You can stop mistaking sharp division for real understanding.
bhagwad_gita::644.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Krishna continues explaining the three kinds of understanding after Arjuna’s collapse. He contrasts the clear vision that sees unity with the restless mind that only sorts beings into separate pieces. This verse names that divided seeing as rajasic.
bhagwad_gita::644.modern_relevance: You meet someone new and instantly reduce them to labels, roles, and differences. The mind feels precise, but it is only chopping reality into pieces and calling that insight.
bhagwad_gita::644.insight: It shifts the mind from categorising everything separately to asking whether the seeing itself is restless and partial.

bhagwad_gita::645.verse_sanskrit: यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम् । अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::645.verse_hindi: किंतु जो ज्ञान एक कार्यरूप शरीरमें ही सम्पूर्णके तरह आसक्त है तथा जो युक्तिरहित, वास्तविक ज्ञानसे रहित और तुच्छ है, वह तामस कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::645.english_translation: But knowledge that clings to one body as if it were the whole, without reason, without truth, and petty, is called dark.
bhagwad_gita::645.translation_literal: यत् (which) / तु (but) / कृत्स्नवत् (as if complete) / एकस्मिन् (in one) / कार्ये (in body/action) / सक्तम् (attached) / अहैतुकम् (without reason) / अतत्त्वार्थवत् (without knowledge of reality) / अल्पम् (small/petty) / च (and) / तत् (that) / तामसम् (dark/tamas) / उदाहृतम् (is called)
bhagwad_gita::645.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::645.essence: Small certainty can hide the least real understanding.
bhagwad_gita::645.simple_meaning: A dark kind of understanding mistakes one limited thing for the whole, lacks clear reasoning, and stays small and confused.
bhagwad_gita::645.simple_insight: You can stop treating a narrow view as total truth.
bhagwad_gita::645.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna explains how understanding can differ in quality. After praising clear and balanced knowledge, Krishna names the lowest kind: a cramped view that mistakes one limited form for the whole and cannot see reality properly.
bhagwad_gita::645.modern_relevance: You’re certain your first angry reaction is the full story, and you build a whole argument on it. This verse warns that a tiny, rigid view can feel complete while missing reality.
bhagwad_gita::645.insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to a partial picture toward testing whether a view actually fits reality.

bhagwad_gita::646.verse_sanskrit: नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् । अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::646.verse_hindi: जो कर्म शास्त्रविधिसे नियत किया हुआ और कर्तृत्वाभिमानसे रहित हो तथा फलेच्छारहित मनुष्यके द्वारा बिना रागद्वेषके किया हुआ हो, वह सात्त्विक कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::646.english_translation: Action that is guided by duty, free from attachment, and done without craving results is called sattvic.
bhagwad_gita::646.translation_literal: नियतं (prescribed) / सङ्गरहितम् (free from attachment) / अरागद्वेषतः (without attraction and aversion) / कृतम् (done) / अफलप्रेप्सुना (by one not seeking fruit) / कर्म (action) / यत् (which) / तत् (that) / सात्त्विकम् (sattvic) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::646.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::646.essence: The purest action asks for nothing back.
bhagwad_gita::646.simple_meaning: Action is pure when it follows duty, is free from attachment, and is done without craving the result.
bhagwad_gita::646.simple_insight: You can act fully without being pulled by wanting. That makes the work clean and steady.
bhagwad_gita::646.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still trapped between collapse and action. Krishna now classifies kinds of action, showing that the highest form is duty done without attachment, craving, or inner push and pull.
bhagwad_gita::646.modern_relevance: You send the message you’ve been avoiding, knowing it may change everything. What makes it right is not the reaction you get, but the clean intention behind it.
bhagwad_gita::646.insight: It shifts attention from reward-seeking to duty-shaped action, so effort stays steady and uncorrupted.

bhagwad_gita::647.verse_sanskrit: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः । क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::647.verse_hindi: परन्तु जो कर्म भोगोंको चाहनेवाले मनुष्यके द्वारा अहंकार अथवा परिश्रमपूर्वक किया जाता है, वह राजस कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::647.english_translation: But action done with desire for pleasure, or with ego, or with great strain, is said to be rajasic.
bhagwad_gita::647.translation_literal: यत् (which) / तु (but) / कामेप्सुना (by one desiring pleasure) / कर्म (action) / साहङ्कारेण (with ego) / वा (or) / पुनः (again) / क्रियते (is done) / बहुलायासम् (with great effort) / तत् (that) / राजसम् (rajasic) / उदाहृतम् (is called)
bhagwad_gita::647.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::647.essence: Desire and ego turn action restless, even when it looks productive.
bhagwad_gita::647.simple_meaning: Action driven by craving, ego, or strain belongs to restlessness, not clarity. It is active, but it is not clean.
bhagwad_gita::647.simple_insight: You can spot the difference between healthy effort and effort fueled by wanting.
bhagwad_gita::647.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna frozen and the war still waiting, Krishna explains how action can be shaped by the three qualities. After describing clear action, he now names the kind driven by desire, pride, and strain.
bhagwad_gita::647.modern_relevance: You keep pushing because you want the praise, the win, the proof. The work gets done, but it leaves you tighter than before.
bhagwad_gita::647.insight: It teaches you to notice when effort is powered by craving and self-importance, not purpose.

bhagwad_gita::648.verse_sanskrit: अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् । मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::648.verse_hindi: जो कर्म परिणाम, हानि, हिंसा और सामर्थ्यको न देखकर मोहपूर्वक आरम्भ किया जाता है, वह तामस कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::648.english_translation: Action begun in delusion, ignoring its consequences, harm, and one’s own capacity, is called tamasic.
bhagwad_gita::648.translation_literal: अनुबन्धम् (consequence) / क्षयम् (loss) / हिंसाम् (harm) / अनपेक्ष्य (without considering) / च (and) / पौरुषम् (one’s own capacity) / मोहात् (from delusion) / आरभ्यते (is begun) / कर्म (action) / यत् (which) / तत् (that) / तामसम् (tamasic) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::648.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::648.essence: Blind action begins where clear seeing is absent.
bhagwad_gita::648.simple_meaning: Action driven by confusion, without considering consequences, damage, or your real ability, is dark and unwise.
bhagwad_gita::648.simple_insight: You feel the warning light before rushing ahead. Clear seeing can stop avoidable damage.
bhagwad_gita::648.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Krishna is sorting action into three kinds for Arjuna. After describing pure and passionate action, he turns to the worst kind: action launched in confusion, without weighing results, harm, or strength.
bhagwad_gita::648.modern_relevance: You hit send on the angry message, then realize it will wound three people and solve nothing. This verse asks for one breath of clear seeing before the damage starts.
bhagwad_gita::648.insight: It teaches you to pause long enough to judge consequences before acting.

bhagwad_gita::649.verse_sanskrit: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::649.verse_hindi: जो कर्ता रागरहित, अनहंवादी, धैर्य और उत्साहयुक्त तथा सिद्धि और असिद्धिमें निर्विकार है, वह सात्त्विक कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::649.english_translation: The doer who is free from attachment, free from ego, endowed with steadiness and enthusiasm, and unchanged by success or failure is called sattvic.
bhagwad_gita::649.translation_literal: मुक्तसङ्गः (free from attachment) / अनहंवादी (not speaking 'I') / धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः (endowed with steadiness and enthusiasm) / सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः (in success and failure) / निर्विकारः (unchanged) / कर्ता (doer) / सात्त्विकः (sattvic) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::649.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::649.essence: Pure action leaves the ego out and stays calm in victory or defeat.
bhagwad_gita::649.simple_meaning: A truly pure doer works without attachment, ego, or inner disturbance, and remains steady whether the result succeeds or fails.
bhagwad_gita::649.simple_insight: There is relief in acting wholeheartedly without having to defend your pride afterward.
bhagwad_gita::649.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna is not only judging actions but the kind of person behind them. After describing rajasic and tamasic action, he now shows Arjuna the sattvic doer: steady, humble, energetic, and inwardly even whether victory comes or not.
bhagwad_gita::649.modern_relevance: You sent the message, made the call, and waited for the reply that could change everything. Your chest tightens. This verse asks you to stay clear inside, no matter what answer comes back.
bhagwad_gita::649.insight: It shifts attention from ownership and outcome to steadiness of character in action.

bhagwad_gita::650.verse_sanskrit: रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः । हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः ॥
bhagwad_gita::650.verse_hindi: जो कर्ता रागी, कर्मफलकी इच्छावाला, लोभी, हिंसाके स्वभाववाला, अशुद्ध और हर्षशोकसे युक्त है, वह राजस कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::650.english_translation: The doer ruled by craving, chasing results, greedy, violent in nature, impure, and tossed by joy and sorrow is called passionate.
bhagwad_gita::650.translation_literal: रागी (dominated by craving) / कर्मफलप्रेप्सुः (seeking the fruit of action) / लुब्धः (greedy) / हिंसात्मकः (of violent nature) / अशुचिः (impure) / हर्षशोकान्वितः (joined with joy and sorrow) / कर्ता (doer) / राजसः (passionate) / परिकीर्तितः (is called)
bhagwad_gita::650.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::650.essence: Craving turns action into a chase for reward and emotional swing.
bhagwad_gita::650.simple_meaning: A person driven by craving, greed, and attachment to results acts in a restless, passionate way and stays pulled between pleasure and disappointment.
bhagwad_gita::650.simple_insight: You can see how craving makes action noisy, unstable, and exhausting.
bhagwad_gita::650.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna explains the three kinds of action and the three kinds of doer. After describing the clear and the confused, Krishna names the middle state: action driven by craving, reward-hunger, and emotional swings.
bhagwad_gita::650.modern_relevance: You hit refresh after sending the message, hoping for praise, then sink when it is ignored. That swing reveals a mind acting for reward, not from steadiness.
bhagwad_gita::650.insight: It teaches you to notice when desire for payoff is contaminating your action.

bhagwad_gita::651.verse_sanskrit: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः । विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते ॥
bhagwad_gita::651.verse_hindi: जो कर्ता असावधान, अशिक्षित, ऐंठअकड़वाला, जिद्दी, उपकारीका अपकार करनेवाला, आलसी, विषादी और दीर्घसूत्री है, वह तामस कहा जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::651.english_translation: A careless, crude, stubborn, deceitful, lazy, gloomy, and procrastinating doer is called tamasic.
bhagwad_gita::651.translation_literal: अयुक्तः (undisciplined/careless) / प्राकृतः (crude/unenlightened) / स्तब्धः (stubborn/obstinate) / शठः (deceitful) / नैष्कृतिकः (malicious/ungrateful) / अलसः (lazy) / विषादी (gloomy) / दीर्घसूत्री (procrastinating) / च (and) / कर्ता (doer) / तामसः (tamasic) / उच्यते (is called)
bhagwad_gita::651.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::651.essence: Dullness in the doer makes even action inert and harmful.
bhagwad_gita::651.simple_meaning: A person who acts carelessly, lazily, stubbornly, and deceitfully is working from tamasic energy. That kind of action is dull, delayed, and harmful.
bhagwad_gita::651.simple_insight: It helps you notice when resistance, delay, and self-deception are draining your actions.
bhagwad_gita::651.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna frozen and Krishna sorting the nature of action, the teaching now turns to the lowest kind of doer. After describing clear and passionate action, Krishna names the dull, delaying, and harmful pattern that keeps a person stuck.
bhagwad_gita::651.modern_relevance: You keep postponing the hard email, then tell yourself you will do it tomorrow. The task is still there, but your energy has gone heavy, vague, and self-protective.
bhagwad_gita::651.insight: It shifts attention from excuses to the quality of the doer behind the deed.

bhagwad_gita::652.verse_sanskrit: बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं श्रृणु । प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय ॥
bhagwad_gita::652.verse_hindi: हे धनञ्जय  अब तू गुणोंके अनुसार बुद्धि और धृतिके भी तीन प्रकारके भेद अलगअलगरूपसे सुन, जो कि मेरे द्वारा पूर्णरूपसे कहे जा रहे हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::652.english_translation: O Dhananjaya, now hear the threefold distinctions of understanding and steadfastness according to the three qualities, fully and separately explained.
bhagwad_gita::652.translation_literal: बुद्धेः (of understanding) / भेदम् (the distinctions) / धृतेः (of steadfastness) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / गुणतः (according to the qualities) / त्रिविधम् (threefold) / श्रृणु (hear) / प्रोच्यमानम् (being explained) / अशेषेण (completely) / पृथक्त्वेन (separately) / धनञ्जय (O Dhananjaya)
bhagwad_gita::652.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::652.essence: Understanding and resolve differ by the quality that shapes them.
bhagwad_gita::652.simple_meaning: Krishna asks Arjuna to listen to the three kinds of understanding and steadfastness, explained separately according to the three qualities.
bhagwad_gita::652.simple_insight: Clear seeing begins by sorting what kind of mind is at work.
bhagwad_gita::652.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna still stands torn between action and collapse. Krishna now turns to the inner equipment behind choice itself: understanding and steadfastness. He prepares Arjuna to see how the three qualities shape the mind before explaining each one.
bhagwad_gita::652.modern_relevance: You are staring at two job offers, one safe and one honest, and your mind keeps changing its story. First notice what kind of understanding is speaking, then decide.
bhagwad_gita::652.insight: It shifts attention from the decision itself to the quality of mind making the decision.

bhagwad_gita::653.verse_sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये । बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥
bhagwad_gita::653.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन  जो बुद्धि प्रवृत्ति और निवृत्तिको, कर्तव्य और अकर्तव्यको, भय और अभयको तथा बन्धन और मोक्षको जानती है, वह बुद्धि सात्त्विकी है ॥
bhagwad_gita::653.english_translation: O Partha, the intellect that knows what leads forward and what withdraws, what should be done and not done, what is fear and fearlessness, what binds and what frees, is sattvic.
bhagwad_gita::653.translation_literal: प्रवृत्तिम् (forward action) / च (and) / निवृत्तिम् (withdrawal) / च (and) / कार्याकार्ये (what should be done and what should not be done) / भयाभये (fear and fearlessness) / बन्धम् (bondage) / मोक्षम् (freedom) / च (and) / या (which) / वेत्ति (knows) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / सा (that) / पार्थ (O Partha) / सात्त्विकी (sattvic)
bhagwad_gita::653.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::653.essence: True intelligence recognizes the difference between bondage and freedom.
bhagwad_gita::653.simple_meaning: A clear mind can tell the difference between action and withdrawal, right and wrong action, fear and fearlessness, bondage and freedom.
bhagwad_gita::653.simple_insight: You do not need more noise; you need better seeing.
bhagwad_gita::653.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands unable to act. Krishna now classifies the powers of understanding, showing that the highest intellect can distinguish duty from non-duty, fear from fearlessness, and bondage from freedom.
bhagwad_gita::653.modern_relevance: You are staring at a message you know will change everything. The real question is not what feels safer, but whether your mind can see what binds and what frees.
bhagwad_gita::653.insight: It trains discernment: not every option is equal, and clear seeing separates duty from confusion.

bhagwad_gita::654.verse_sanskrit: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च । अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥
bhagwad_gita::654.verse_hindi: हे पार्थ  मनुष्य जिसके द्वारा धर्म और अधर्मको, कर्तव्य और अकर्तव्यको भी ठीक तरहसे नहीं जानता, वह बुद्धि राजसी है ॥
bhagwad_gita::654.english_translation: Arjuna, the intellect that does not truly know right action and wrong action, duty and what should not be done, is rajasic.
bhagwad_gita::654.translation_literal: यया (by which) / धर्मम् (right action) / अधर्मम् (wrong action) / च (and) / कार्यम् (what should be done) / च (and) / अकार्यम् (what should not be done) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / अयथावत् (not properly) / प्रजानाति (understands) / बुद्धिः (intellect) / सा (that) / पार्थ (Arjuna) / राजसी (rajasic)
bhagwad_gita::654.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::654.essence: Restless intelligence cannot tell duty from harm.
bhagwad_gita::654.simple_meaning: A restless, rajasic mind misreads right action and wrong action. It cannot clearly tell what should be done and what should be avoided.
bhagwad_gita::654.simple_insight: Clarity is not just intelligence; it is the ability to see what truly matters.
bhagwad_gita::654.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen, and Krishna begins sorting the states of mind that shape action. After describing clear understanding, he now names the mind that gets duty and non-duty mixed up: rajasic intelligence.
bhagwad_gita::654.modern_relevance: You are staring at two replies before sending one that could change a relationship. One part of you knows what is right; another part keeps spinning. That spinning is rajasic confusion.
bhagwad_gita::654.insight: It trains you to notice when agitation is distorting judgment and to pause until duty becomes clear.

bhagwad_gita::655.verse_sanskrit: अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसाऽऽवृता । सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥
bhagwad_gita::655.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन  तमोगुणसे घिरी हुई जो बुद्धि अधर्मको धर्म और सम्पूर्ण चीजोंको उलटा मान लेती है, वह तामसी है ॥
bhagwad_gita::655.english_translation: The mind covered by darkness calls wrongdoing right and reverses everything.
bhagwad_gita::655.translation_literal: अधर्मम् (wrongdoing) / धर्मम् इति (as right) / या (which) / मन्यते (thinks) / तमसा (by darkness) / आवृता (covered) / सर्वार्थान् (all meanings / all aims) / विपरीतान् (reversed) / च (and) / बुद्धिः (intelligence) / सा (that) / पार्थ (O Partha) / तामसी (dark, inert)
bhagwad_gita::655.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::655.essence: Darkness can make the wrong choice feel morally correct.
bhagwad_gita::655.simple_meaning: A mind clouded by darkness mistakes wrongdoing for righteousness and gets its judgment completely reversed.
bhagwad_gita::655.simple_insight: It warns you that confusion can feel convincing, so you must question your own certainty.
bhagwad_gita::655.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen, and Krishna begins sorting the kinds of understanding that shape action. After describing clear and confused intelligence, he names the darkest kind: a mind so covered that it calls adharma righteous and sees everything backward.
bhagwad_gita::655.modern_relevance: You defend a choice in your head at 1 a.m., and it starts sounding noble. This verse catches that moment when self-justification begins to wear the mask of conscience.
bhagwad_gita::655.insight: It trains you to test your judgments before acting, especially when a bad choice feels emotionally comfortable.

bhagwad_gita::656.verse_sanskrit: धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः । योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी ॥
bhagwad_gita::656.verse_hindi: हे पार्थ  समतासे युक्त जिस अव्यभिचारिणी धृतिके द्वारा मनुष्य मन, प्राण और इन्द्रियोंकी क्रियाओंको धारण करता है, वह धृति सात्त्विकी है ॥
bhagwad_gita::656.english_translation: O Partha, that steadfastness by which one holds steady the functions of mind, life-force, and senses through unwavering yoga is sattvic steadfastness.
bhagwad_gita::656.translation_literal: धृत्या (by steadfastness) / यया (by which) / धारयते (one holds steady) / मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः (the activities of mind, life-force, and senses) / योगेन (through yoga) / अव्यभिचारिण्या (unwavering) / धृतिः (steadfastness) / सा (that) / पार्थ (O Partha) / सात्त्विकी (sattvic)
bhagwad_gita::656.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::656.essence: Steadiness becomes pure when it keeps the whole being aligned.
bhagwad_gita::656.simple_meaning: True steadfastness is the power to keep the mind, life-force, and senses steady through yoga, without wavering.
bhagwad_gita::656.simple_insight: You do not need to be pulled around by every urge. Steadiness itself is a form of strength.
bhagwad_gita::656.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen by doubt. Krishna now explains what real firmness looks like: not stubbornness, but the steady holding of mind, breath, and senses through yoga. This verse names the pure form of that inner strength.
bhagwad_gita::656.modern_relevance: You're about to send the message, make the call, or walk into the room, and your body wants to bolt. This verse points to the kind of steadiness that keeps you aligned when nerves, impulses, and distractions all surge at once.
bhagwad_gita::656.insight: It teaches you to regulate inner forces instead of being ruled by them.

bhagwad_gita::657.verse_sanskrit: यया तु धर्मकामार्थान् धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन । प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी ॥
bhagwad_gita::657.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन अर्जुन  फलकी इच्छावाला मनुष्य जिस धृतिके द्वारा धर्म, काम भोग और अर्थको अत्यन्त आसक्तिपूर्वक धारण करता है, वह धृति राजसी है ॥
bhagwad_gita::657.english_translation: Arjuna, the steadiness that clings intensely to duty, pleasure, and wealth, while craving results, is passionate steadiness.
bhagwad_gita::657.translation_literal: यया (by which) / तु (but) / धर्मकामार्थान् (duty, desire, and wealth) / धृत्या (by steadiness) / धारयते (one holds) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / प्रसङ्गेन (through attachment) / फलाकाङ्क्षी (one desiring results) / धृतिः (steadiness) / सा (that) / पार्थ (Partha) / राजसी (passionate)
bhagwad_gita::657.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::657.essence: Steadiness becomes restless when it is tied to reward.
bhagwad_gita::657.simple_meaning: A person can appear steady and disciplined, yet still be driven by attachment to duty, pleasure, and wealth, along with desire for results. That kind of firmness is restless, not pure.
bhagwad_gita::657.simple_insight: Not all self-control is clean. You can look composed while still being pulled by wanting.
bhagwad_gita::657.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Krishna is sorting Arjuna's inner life into clear types. After describing higher steadiness, he now names a lesser kind: the firmness that holds onto duty, pleasure, and wealth because it wants payoff. It is still discipline, but mixed with craving.
bhagwad_gita::657.modern_relevance: You keep a strict routine, but every habit is secretly aimed at applause, profit, or control. The outside looks disciplined; the inside is bargaining.
bhagwad_gita::657.insight: It separates true discipline from ambition disguised as discipline, so you can see what is actually driving your effort.

bhagwad_gita::658.verse_sanskrit: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च । न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी ॥
bhagwad_gita::658.verse_hindi: हे पार्थ  दुष्ट बुद्धिवाला मनुष्य जिस धृतिके द्वारा निद्रा, भय, चिन्ता, दुःख और घमण्डको भी नहीं छोड़ता, वह धृति तामसी है ॥
bhagwad_gita::658.english_translation: The dull-minded one does not let go of sleep, fear, grief, sorrow, and pride. That steadfastness is tamasic, Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::658.translation_literal: यया (by which) / स्वप्नम् (sleep) / भयम् (fear) / शोकम् (grief) / विषादम् (sorrow) / मदम् (pride) / एव (even) / च (and) / न विमुञ्चति (does not let go) / दुर्मेधाः (the dull-minded one) / धृतिः (steadfastness) / सा (that) / पार्थ (Arjuna) / तामसी (tamasic)
bhagwad_gita::658.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::658.essence: Clinging to fear and sorrow is not strength; it is tamasic inertia.
bhagwad_gita::658.simple_meaning: Some people hold on to sleepiness, fear, grief, despair, and pride instead of releasing them. That kind of stubbornness is dull and tamasic.
bhagwad_gita::658.simple_insight: Not every kind of firmness is strength; some of it is just clinging to what keeps you heavy.
bhagwad_gita::658.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Krishna is classifying the kinds of resolve that drive action. After describing sattvic and rajasic steadfastness, he names the lowest form: the mind that cannot release fear, grief, sorrow, sleep, or pride.
bhagwad_gita::658.modern_relevance: You keep replaying the same failure in bed at 2 a.m., feeding the fear instead of setting it down. Krishna calls that not strength, but heaviness.
bhagwad_gita::658.insight: It shifts you to notice whether your resolve is clarifying action or merely preserving mental fog.

bhagwad_gita::659.verse_sanskrit: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ । अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति ॥
bhagwad_gita::659.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  अब तीन प्रकारके सुखको भी तुम मेरेसे सुनो ।  जिसमें अभ्याससे रमण होता है और जिससे दुःखोंका अन्त हो जाता है, ऐसा वह परमात्मविषयक बुद्धिकी प्रसन्नतासे पैदा होनेवाला जो सुख सांसारिक आसक्तिके कारण आरम्भमें विषकी तरह और परिणाममें अमृतकी तरह होता है, वह सुख सात्त्विक कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::659.english_translation: O best of the Bharatas, hear from me now about three kinds of happiness. The happiness that comes from practice, ends sorrow, and first feels like poison but later like nectar is called sattvic.
bhagwad_gita::659.translation_literal: सुखम् (happiness) / तु (indeed) / इदानीम् (now) / त्रिविधम् (threefold) / श्रृणु (hear) / मे (from me) / भरतर्षभ (O best of the Bharatas) / अभ्यासात् (from practice) / रमते (finds delight) / यत्र (where) / दुःख-अन्तम् (end of sorrow) / च (and) / निगच्छति (attains)
bhagwad_gita::659.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::659.essence: True happiness begins as discipline and ends as relief.
bhagwad_gita::659.simple_meaning: Krishna describes a higher kind of happiness: it grows through practice, brings lasting relief, and feels difficult at first but sweet in the end.
bhagwad_gita::659.simple_insight: Real ease often starts as effort before it becomes relief.
bhagwad_gita::659.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands shaken while Krishna finishes his teaching on the three qualities of life. After describing lower forms of steadiness, Krishna now turns to sattvic happiness — the kind that grows through practice and ends sorrow.
bhagwad_gita::659.modern_relevance: You keep returning to the meditation cushion even when it feels awkward and unrewarding. Weeks later, the mind settles, and the struggle that once felt heavy starts to feel like home.
bhagwad_gita::659.insight: It shifts the mind to value disciplined practice that matures into freedom from suffering.

bhagwad_gita::660.verse_sanskrit: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् । तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::660.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशियोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन  अब तीन प्रकारके सुखको भी तुम मेरेसे सुनो ।  जिसमें अभ्याससे रमण होता है और जिससे दुःखोंका अन्त हो जाता है, ऐसा वह परमात्मविषयक बुद्धिकी प्रसन्नतासे पैदा होनेवाला जो सुख सांसारिक आसक्तिके कारण आरम्भमें विषकी तरह और परिणाममें अमृतकी तरह होता है, वह सुख सात्त्विक कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::660.english_translation: That happiness is called sattvic, which seems like poison at first and like nectar in the end, born from clarity of the discerning mind and the peace of inner understanding.
bhagwad_gita::660.translation_literal: यत् (which) / तत् (that) / अग्रे (at first) / विष-इव (like poison) / परिणामे (in the end) / अमृत-उपमम् (like nectar) / तत् (that) / सुखम् (happiness) / सात्त्विकम् (sattvic) / प्रोक्तम् (is said) / आत्म-बुद्धि-प्रसाद-जम् (born from the peace of self-understanding)
bhagwad_gita::660.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::660.essence: Lasting ease can begin as discomfort and end as release.
bhagwad_gita::660.simple_meaning: A calm, clear happiness may feel difficult at first, but it ends in deep relief. It comes from a mind that sees clearly and settles inwardly.
bhagwad_gita::660.simple_insight: What feels hard now may be the very thing that brings lasting ease.
bhagwad_gita::660.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna now distinguishes the three kinds of happiness, showing that the highest one begins with discipline and inner clarity, even if it feels bitter before it ripens.
bhagwad_gita::660.modern_relevance: You start therapy, meditation, or a hard conversation and feel worse before you feel better. The discomfort is not a sign of failure; it may be the beginning of real ease.
bhagwad_gita::660.insight: It shifts you to value what strengthens clear seeing over what merely feels pleasant at first.

bhagwad_gita::661.verse_sanskrit: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् । परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::661.verse_hindi: जो सुख इन्द्रियों और विषयोंके संयोगसे आरम्भमें अमृतकी तरह और परिणाममें विषकी तरह होता है, वह सुख राजस कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::661.english_translation: The pleasure that begins like nectar from contact between the senses and their objects, but ends like poison, is called rajasic pleasure.
bhagwad_gita::661.translation_literal: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगात् (from contact of senses and objects) / यत् (which) / तत् (that) / अग्रे (at first) / अमृतोपमम् (like nectar) / परिणामे (in the end) / विषमिव (like poison) / तत् (that) / सुखम् (pleasure) / राजसम् (rajasic) / स्मृतम् (is said to be)
bhagwad_gita::661.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::661.essence: What feels sweetest first can become the harshest later.
bhagwad_gita::661.simple_meaning: Pleasures that come from sensory contact can feel wonderful at first, but they often leave pain, restlessness, or disappointment afterward.
bhagwad_gita::661.simple_insight: Not every pleasure is worth trusting. Some delights borrow their sweetness from the future.
bhagwad_gita::661.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna stands frozen while Krishna explains why not all happiness is equal. After describing higher, steadier joy, Krishna now names the kind that comes from sense contact: exciting at first, damaging later.
bhagwad_gita::661.modern_relevance: You open the app for one quick scroll after midnight, then another, then another. The rush feels harmless in the moment, but the next morning tells the truth.
bhagwad_gita::661.insight: It trains you to judge pleasure by its full arc, not its first taste.

bhagwad_gita::662.verse_sanskrit: यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः । निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::662.verse_hindi: निद्रा, आलस्य और प्रमादसे उत्पन्न होनेवाला जो सुख आरम्भमें और परिणाममें अपनेको मोहित करनेवाला है, वह सुख तामस कहा गया है ॥
bhagwad_gita::662.english_translation: That pleasure, born of sleep, laziness, and negligence, deludes the self at the beginning and at the end; it is called tamasic.
bhagwad_gita::662.translation_literal: यत् (which) / अग्रे (at first) / च (and) / अनुबन्धे (in the end) / च (and) / सुखम् (pleasure) / मोहनम् (deluding) / आत्मनः (of the self) / निद्रा-आलस्य-प्रमाद-उत्थम् (born of sleep, laziness, and negligence) / तत् (that) / तामसम् (tamasic) / उदाहृतम् (is called)
bhagwad_gita::662.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::662.essence: Pleasure that dulls you is not relief; it is confusion in disguise.
bhagwad_gita::662.simple_meaning: Pleasure that comes from sleep, laziness, and carelessness feels good only briefly. It dulls the mind and leaves a person more confused.
bhagwad_gita::662.simple_insight: Not every comfort restores you. Some pleasures quietly drain your clarity.
bhagwad_gita::662.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna finishes classifying the three kinds of pleasure. After describing higher and mixed forms, Krishna names the lowest one: the comfort that comes from sleep, laziness, and negligence, and leaves the mind dulled.
bhagwad_gita::662.modern_relevance: You keep scrolling after midnight because stopping feels strangely pleasant. In the morning, the fog is heavier, not lighter. That comfort was never rest; it was drift.
bhagwad_gita::662.insight: It teaches you to test pleasure by its aftereffect, not its first taste.

bhagwad_gita::663.verse_sanskrit: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः । सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्ित्रभिर्गुणैः ॥
bhagwad_gita::663.verse_hindi: पृथ्वीमें या स्वर्गमें अथवा देवताओंमें तथा इनके सिवाय और कहीं भी वह ऐसी कोई वस्तु नहीं है, जो प्रकृतिसे उत्पन्न इन तीनों गुणोंसे रहित हो ॥
bhagwad_gita::663.english_translation: There is nothing on earth, in heaven, or among the radiant beings that is free from the three qualities born of nature.
bhagwad_gita::663.translation_literal: न (not) / तत् (that) / अस्ति (there is) / पृथिव्याम् (on earth) / वा (or) / दिवि (in heaven) / देवेषु (among the radiant beings) / वा (or) / पुनः (again) / सत्त्वम् (being) / प्रकृतिजैः (born of nature) / मुक्तम् (freed) / यत् (which) / एभिः (from these) / स्यात् (may be) / त्रिभिः (three) / गुणैः (qualities)
bhagwad_gita::663.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::663.essence: No state is free from the three qualities of nature.
bhagwad_gita::663.simple_meaning: Everything in the world is shaped by the three qualities of nature. Nothing in the material order is completely free from them.
bhagwad_gita::663.simple_insight: You stop idealising any place, person, or state as untouchable. Everything changing is still under the same laws.
bhagwad_gita::663.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna is explaining the structure behind human behavior just before the final teaching on duty. Arjuna needs to see that no being or realm is outside the play of the three qualities, because that insight prepares him for the next verse on social roles.
bhagwad_gita::663.modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems effortlessly calm, then catch their irritation under pressure. The verse cuts through the fantasy that any person or status is beyond temperament, habit, and conditioning.
bhagwad_gita::663.insight: It shifts attention from judging appearances to seeing the forces that shape every response.

bhagwad_gita::664.verse_sanskrit: ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परंतप । कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः ॥
bhagwad_gita::664.verse_hindi: हे परंतप  ब्राह्मण, क्षत्रिय, वैश्य और शूद्रोंके कर्म स्वभावसे उत्पन्न हुए तीनों गुणोंके द्वारा विभक्त किये गये हैं ॥
