bhagwad_gita::664.english_translation: O scorcher of foes, the duties of priests, warriors, merchants, and workers are divided according to the qualities born of their nature.
bhagwad_gita::664.translation_literal: ब्राह्मण-क्षत्रिय-विशां (of priests, warriors, merchants) / शूद्राणां (of workers) / च (and) / परंतप (O scorcher of foes) / कर्माणि (duties / actions) / प्रविभक्तानि (are divided) / स्वभाव-प्रभवैः (born of one’s nature) / गुणैः (by the qualities)
bhagwad_gita::664.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::664.essence: Your rightful work comes from your nature, not imitation.
bhagwad_gita::664.simple_meaning: Different kinds of work belong to different people according to their nature and qualities.
bhagwad_gita::664.simple_insight: You do not have to copy someone else’s role. Your nature points toward the work that fits you.
bhagwad_gita::664.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Arjuna still hesitates while Krishna keeps unfolding the structure of right action. Here Krishna explains that social roles and duties are not random; they arise from the qualities built into a person's nature.
bhagwad_gita::664.modern_relevance: A student keeps forcing themselves into a career because everyone praises it, while their real strengths are elsewhere. The pressure eases when they stop copying and start listening to what fits.
bhagwad_gita::664.insight: It shifts attention from borrowed identity to the work that matches your actual nature.

bhagwad_gita::665.verse_sanskrit: शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च । ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::665.verse_hindi: मनका निग्रह करना इन्द्रियोंको वशमें करना धर्मपालनके लिये कष्ट सहना बाहरभीतरसे शुद्ध रहना दूसरोंके अपराधको क्षमा करना शरीर, मन आदिमें सरलता रखना वेद, शास्त्र आदिका ज्ञान होना यज्ञविधिको अनुभवमें लाना और परमात्मा, वेद आदिमें आस्तिक भाव रखना  ये सबकेसब ब्राह्मणके स्वाभाविक कर्म हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::665.english_translation: Self-restraint, control of the senses, austerity, purity, forgiveness, honesty, knowledge, realization, and faith in the supreme reality are the natural duties of a brahmin.
bhagwad_gita::665.translation_literal: शमः (control of the mind) / दमः (control of the senses) / तपः (austerity) / शौचम् (purity) / क्षान्तिः (forgiveness) / आर्जवम् (straightforwardness) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / विज्ञानम् (realized understanding) / आस्तिक्यम् (faith) / ब्रह्मकर्म (brahmin duty) / स्वभावजम् (born of nature)
bhagwad_gita::665.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::665.essence: True duty begins as disciplined character, not public role.
bhagwad_gita::665.simple_meaning: A person's natural work can include self-control, purity, forgiveness, honesty, knowledge, and trust in the supreme reality. These qualities belong to a brahmin by nature.
bhagwad_gita::665.simple_insight: Character is not random; it is trained through steady restraint, honesty, and inner cleanliness.
bhagwad_gita::665.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna is explaining how human nature divides different kinds of work. After describing the qualities of brahmin life, he lists the inner disciplines that define it: calmness, self-control, purity, forgiveness, straightforwardness, knowledge, realization, and faith.
bhagwad_gita::665.modern_relevance: Before a difficult conversation, you can feel the urge to bluff, snap, or hide. This verse points to a different strength: stay clean in speech, steady in mind, and honest in intent.
bhagwad_gita::665.insight: It shifts duty from outer status to inner formation: the right work grows from the qualities you cultivate.

bhagwad_gita::666.verse_sanskrit: शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् । दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::666.verse_hindi: शूरवीरता, तेज, धैर्य, प्रजाके संचालन आदिकी विशेष चतुरता, युद्धमें कभी पीठ न दिखाना, दान करना और शासन करनेका भाव  ये सबकेसब क्षत्रियके स्वाभाविक कर्म हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::666.english_translation: Valor, radiance, firmness, quick skill, never fleeing in battle, generosity, and leadership are the natural duties of a warrior.
bhagwad_gita::666.translation_literal: शौर्यम् (valor) / तेजः (radiance) / धृतिः (firmness) / दाक्ष्यम् (skillfulness) / युद्धे (in battle) / च (and) / अपि (also) / अपलायनम् (not fleeing) / दानम् (generosity) / ईश्वरभावः (leadership / lordliness) / च (and) / क्षात्रम् (of a warrior) / कर्म (duty) / स्वभावजम् (born of nature)
bhagwad_gita::666.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::666.essence: True strength serves, stands firm, and does not retreat.
bhagwad_gita::666.simple_meaning: A warrior’s natural duties include courage, steadiness, skill, generosity, and refusing to run from battle.
bhagwad_gita::666.simple_insight: Your role asks for courage, not comfort.
bhagwad_gita::666.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still explaining how human work fits different natures. After describing the duties of thinkers, he names the qualities that belong to warriors: courage, strength, steadiness, skill, generosity, and standing firm in battle.
bhagwad_gita::666.modern_relevance: A parent walks into a tense school meeting and stays calm while everyone expects defensiveness. The verse points to that kind of steadiness: meet pressure with courage, not retreat.
bhagwad_gita::666.insight: It shifts duty from self-protection to fearless responsibility.

bhagwad_gita::667.verse_sanskrit: कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् । परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::667.verse_hindi: खेती करना, गायोंकी रक्षा करना और शुद्ध व्यापार करना  ये सबकेसब वैश्यके स्वाभाविक कर्म हैं, तथा चारों वर्णोंकी सेवा करना शूद्रका भी स्वाभाविक कर्म है ॥
bhagwad_gita::667.english_translation: Farming, cattle-keeping, and trade are the natural work of the merchant class. Service to others is the natural work of the worker class.
bhagwad_gita::667.translation_literal: कृषि (farming) / गौरक्ष्य (cow-protection) / वाणिज्य (trade) / वैश्यकर्म (the work of the merchant class) / स्वभावजम् (born of nature) / परिचर्यात्मकम् (service-oriented) / कर्म (work) / शूद्रस्य (of the worker class) / अपि (also) / स्वभावजम् (born of nature)
bhagwad_gita::667.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::667.essence: Every nature has its own rightful work.
bhagwad_gita::667.simple_meaning: Different kinds of work suit different people. Farming, cattle care, trade, and service are described as natural duties for two social groups.
bhagwad_gita::667.simple_insight: You do not need to copy someone else’s role. Fulfil the work that fits your nature.
bhagwad_gita::667.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna is still answering Arjuna’s crisis by explaining how human society holds together. After naming the duties of teachers and rulers, he now names the work of merchants and service workers, showing that every role has its own rightful place.
bhagwad_gita::667.modern_relevance: You are forcing yourself into a career that looks impressive but drains you. Relief comes when you stop asking, “What should I be?” and start asking, “What fits my nature?”
bhagwad_gita::667.insight: It shifts attention from status-seeking to honest fit: the right work is the work aligned with your nature and role.

bhagwad_gita::668.verse_sanskrit: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः । स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु ॥
bhagwad_gita::668.verse_hindi: अपनेअपने कर्ममें तत्परतापूर्वक लगा हुआ मनुष्य सम्यक् सिद्धिपरमात्माको प्राप्त कर लेता है ।  अपने कर्ममें लगा हुआ मनुष्य जिस प्रकार सिद्धिको प्राप्त होता है उस प्रकारको तू मेरेसे सुन ॥
bhagwad_gita::668.english_translation: A person devoted to their own work attains perfection. Listen as I explain how a person devoted to their own work reaches that perfection.
bhagwad_gita::668.translation_literal: स्वे स्वे (in each one's own) / कर्मणि (in work) / अभिरतः (delighting in, devoted) / संसिद्धिम् (perfection, fulfillment) / लभते (attains) / नरः (a person) । / स्वकर्मनिरतः (fixed in one's own work) / सिद्धिम् (perfection) / यथा (how) / विन्दति (attains) / तत् (that) / शृणु (hear)
bhagwad_gita::668.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::668.essence: Fulfillment comes from living your own work, not someone else’s.
bhagwad_gita::668.simple_meaning: A person reaches fulfillment by staying devoted to their own duty, rather than chasing someone else’s role.
bhagwad_gita::668.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing your lane is enough. You do not need to borrow another person’s life to grow.
bhagwad_gita::668.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna frozen and the war waiting, Krishna shifts from social order to inner duty. He says that a person matures by staying devoted to their own work, and this becomes one step in his larger teaching on action.
bhagwad_gita::668.modern_relevance: You are comparing your path to a friend’s promotion, a sibling’s marriage, a stranger’s confidence. The verse cuts through that ache: your fulfillment grows where your own responsibility is.
bhagwad_gita::668.insight: It redirects attention from imitation to rightful action, showing that steady devotion to one's role leads to completion.

bhagwad_gita::669.verse_sanskrit: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः ॥
bhagwad_gita::669.verse_hindi: जिस परमात्मासे सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंकी उत्पत्ति होती है और जिससे यह सम्पूर्ण संसार व्याप्त है, उस परमात्माका अपने कर्मके द्वारा पूजन करके मनुष्य सिद्धिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::669.english_translation: By worshipping the one from whom all beings arise and by whom this whole world is pervaded, a person attains perfection through their own work.
bhagwad_gita::669.translation_literal: यतः (from whom) / प्रवृत्तिः (arising) / भूतानाम् (of beings) / येन (by whom) / सर्वम् इदम् (all this) / ततम् (is pervaded) / स्वकर्मणा (by one's own work) / तम् (that) / अभ्यर्च्य (having worshipped) / सिद्धिम् (perfection) / विन्दति (attains) / मानवः (a person)
bhagwad_gita::669.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::669.essence: Offering your work to the source of life turns ordinary action into fulfillment.
bhagwad_gita::669.simple_meaning: A person reaches fulfillment by offering their own work to the source of all beings and all existence.
bhagwad_gita::669.simple_insight: Your daily effort can feel sacred, not ordinary.
bhagwad_gita::669.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna on the battlefield, where duty feels unbearable and every choice seems charged with loss. After explaining that people are fulfilled through their own work, he adds the deeper reason: work itself becomes complete when it is offered to the source behind all life.
bhagwad_gita::669.modern_relevance: You are doing something difficult that no one will fully understand — caring for a parent, finishing a lonely project, keeping a promise. The verse says that the act itself becomes complete when offered beyond the ego.
bhagwad_gita::669.insight: It shifts action from self-display to offering, so the mind stops measuring worth by applause.

bhagwad_gita::670.verse_sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::670.verse_hindi: अच्छी तरहसे अनुष्ठान किये हुए परधर्मसे गुणरहित अपना धर्म श्रेष्ठ है ।  कारण कि स्वभावसे नियत किये हुए स्वधर्मरूप कर्मको करता हुआ मनुष्य पापको प्राप्त नहीं होता ॥
bhagwad_gita::670.english_translation: One's own duty, though imperfect, is better than another's duty well performed. Doing the work set by one's nature, a person does not incur wrongdoing.
bhagwad_gita::670.translation_literal: श्रेयान् (better) / स्वधर्मः (one's own duty) / विगुणः (without qualities, imperfect) / परधर्मात् (than another's duty) / स्वनुष्ठितात् (well performed) / स्वभावनियतं (fixed by one's own nature) / कर्म (action, work) / कुर्वन् (doing) / न (not) / आप्नोति (attains) / किल्बिषम् (wrongdoing, fault)
bhagwad_gita::670.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::670.essence: Your imperfect duty is cleaner than a borrowed perfection.
bhagwad_gita::670.simple_meaning: It is better to do your own duty, even imperfectly, than to do someone else's duty well. Acting according to your nature does not lead you into wrongdoing.
bhagwad_gita::670.simple_insight: You can stop measuring yourself against other people's lives. Peace comes from doing what is actually yours.
bhagwad_gita::670.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is frozen by doubt, and Krishna keeps returning him to action. After teaching sacrifice and devotion through work, Krishna now sharpens the point: the duty born of your own nature is safer than copying someone else's path.
bhagwad_gita::670.modern_relevance: You are tempted to take the job that looks impressive, the role that earns praise, the life that belongs to someone else. This verse says the mismatch itself creates friction; your own work, even imperfectly done, keeps you clean.
bhagwad_gita::670.insight: It shifts the mind from comparison to alignment: choose the work that matches your nature, not the work that flatters your ego.

bhagwad_gita::671.verse_sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
bhagwad_gita::671.verse_hindi: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  दोषयुक्त होनेपर भी सहज कर्मका त्याग नहीं करना चाहिये क्योंकि सम्पूर्ण कर्म धुएँसे अग्निकी तरह किसीनकिसी दोषसे युक्त हैं ॥
bhagwad_gita::671.english_translation: O son of Kunti, one should not abandon one's natural duty, even if it has flaws. All undertakings are clouded by some defect, just as fire is veiled by smoke.
bhagwad_gita::671.translation_literal: सहजम् (natural) / कर्म (action, duty) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / सदोषम् (with fault) / अपि (even) / न (not) / त्यजेत् (should abandon) / सर्वारम्भाः (all undertakings) / हि (indeed) / दोषेण (by fault/defect) / धूमेन (by smoke) / अग्निः (fire) / इव (like) / आवृताः (covered)
bhagwad_gita::671.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::671.essence: Your right work is still right, even when it is imperfect.
bhagwad_gita::671.simple_meaning: Do not give up your natural duty just because it is imperfect. Every action has some flaw in it.
bhagwad_gita::671.simple_insight: You can stay committed without demanding perfection from yourself or your work.
bhagwad_gita::671.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Krishna continues guiding Arjuna after praising one’s own duty. He now warns him not to reject his natural role because it is imperfect. The battlefield decision still stands, and this verse removes the excuse of “not ideal.”
bhagwad_gita::671.modern_relevance: You are about to send the apology, start the difficult conversation, or take the job that fits your values but feels messy. Imperfection is not a reason to freeze.
bhagwad_gita::671.insight: It shifts the mind from perfectionism to faithful action despite flaws.

bhagwad_gita::672.verse_sanskrit: असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः । नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति ॥
bhagwad_gita::672.verse_hindi: जिसकी बुद्धि सब जगह आसक्तिरहित है, जिसने शरीरको वशमें कर रखा है, जो स्पृहारहित है, वह मनुष्य सांख्ययोगके द्वारा नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::672.english_translation: One whose mind is detached everywhere, who has mastered the self, and who is free from craving attains the highest perfection of non-action through renunciation.
bhagwad_gita::672.translation_literal: असक्तबुद्धिः (detached-minded) / सर्वत्र (everywhere) / जितात्मा (one who has conquered the self) / विगतस्पृहः (free from craving) / नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं (perfection of non-action) / परमाम् (highest) / संन्यासेन (through renunciation) / अधिगच्छति (attains)
bhagwad_gita::672.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::672.essence: Freedom arrives when the mind stops reaching outward.
bhagwad_gita::672.simple_meaning: A person who is detached everywhere, self-controlled, and free from craving reaches the highest state of actionlessness through renunciation.
bhagwad_gita::672.simple_insight: There is relief in not needing to grasp anything. Freedom grows when wanting loosens its hold.
bhagwad_gita::672.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, after Krishna has urged Arjuna to do his own duty without clinging, he now describes the inner state that makes freedom possible. The body stands in battle, but the mind no longer reaches outward for possession or reward.
bhagwad_gita::672.modern_relevance: You finish a hard conversation and keep replaying it for approval. The mind that stops reaching for praise finds a quieter kind of strength.
bhagwad_gita::672.insight: It shifts attention from outward gain to inward freedom, showing that mastery begins when craving ends.

bhagwad_gita::673.verse_sanskrit: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे । समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा ॥
bhagwad_gita::673.verse_hindi: हे कौन्तेय  सिद्धिअन्तःकरणकी शुद्धि को प्राप्त हुआ साधक ब्रह्मको, जो कि ज्ञानकी परा निष्ठा है, जिस प्रकारसे प्राप्त होता है, उस प्रकारको तुम मुझसे संक्षेपमें ही समझो ॥
bhagwad_gita::673.english_translation: Listen to me briefly, O Arjuna, as I explain how one who has reached perfection attains the supreme reality, the highest culmination of knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::673.translation_literal: सिद्धिं प्राप्तः (having attained perfection) / यथा (how) / ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / तथा (so) / आप्नोति (attains) / निबोध (listen carefully) / मे (from me) / समासेन (briefly) / एव (indeed) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / निष्ठा (culmination / steadfastness) / ज्ञानस्य (of knowledge) / या (which) / परा (supreme)
bhagwad_gita::673.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::673.essence: Knowledge has a highest point: direct arrival, not endless thinking.
bhagwad_gita::673.simple_meaning: Krishna asks Arjuna to listen briefly as he explains how a perfected seeker reaches the supreme reality, the highest point of knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::673.simple_insight: Real understanding is not endless theory; it leads somewhere, and that destination changes everything.
bhagwad_gita::673.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, with Arjuna still frozen and the war about to begin, Krishna turns from renunciation to the final destination of wisdom. He promises a brief explanation of how inner perfection leads to the supreme reality, the highest completion of knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::673.modern_relevance: You have read, reflected, and still feel stuck at the edge of a hard choice. At some point, understanding must become arrival — not more analysis.
bhagwad_gita::673.insight: It shifts the mind from collecting ideas to seeking the final state those ideas point toward.

bhagwad_gita::674.verse_sanskrit: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्याऽऽत्मानं नियम्य च । शब्दादीन् विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च ॥
bhagwad_gita::674.verse_hindi: जो विशुद्ध सात्त्विकी बुद्धिसे युक्त, वैराग्यके आश्रित, एकान्तका सेवन करनेवाला और नियमित भोजन करनेवाला साधक धैर्यपूर्वक इन्द्रियोंका नियमन करके, शरीरवाणीमनको वशमें करके, शब्दादि विषयोंका त्याग करके और रागद्वेषको छोड़कर निरन्तर ध्यानयोगके परायण हो जाता है, वह अहंकार, बल, दर्प, काम, क्रोध और परिग्रहका त्याग करके एवं निर्मम तथा शान्त होकर ब्रह्मप्राप्तिका पात्र हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::674.english_translation: Endowed with purified understanding, holding the self steady with firm resolve, giving up sense-objects, and casting away attraction and aversion...
bhagwad_gita::674.translation_literal: बुद्ध्या (with understanding) / विशुद्धया (purified) / युक्तः (endowed) / धृत्या (with firmness) / आत्मानम् (the self) / नियम्य (having restrained) / च (and) / शब्दादीन् (sound and so on) / विषयान् (sense-objects) / त्यक्त्वा (having abandoned) / राग-द्वेषौ (attraction and aversion) / व्युदस्य (having cast away) / च (and)
bhagwad_gita::674.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::674.essence: Purified resolve cuts the pull of craving and aversion.
bhagwad_gita::674.simple_meaning: A person with clear understanding steadies the mind, restrains the senses, gives up sense pleasures, and drops attraction and aversion.
bhagwad_gita::674.simple_insight: Freedom starts when impulse no longer runs the show.
bhagwad_gita::674.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna still needs a way back to inner steadiness. Krishna explains the discipline of a seeker who wants Brahman: purified understanding, firm resolve, restraint of the senses, and release from craving and aversion.
bhagwad_gita::674.modern_relevance: You open your phone to escape one uncomfortable message, then another craving follows. The mind keeps pulling until you deliberately stop feeding it.
bhagwad_gita::674.insight: It shifts attention from reacting to training the mind to stay steady under pressure.

bhagwad_gita::675.verse_sanskrit: विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः । ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः ॥
bhagwad_gita::675.verse_hindi: जो विशुद्ध सात्त्विकी बुद्धिसे युक्त, वैराग्यके आश्रित, एकान्तका सेवन करनेवाला और नियमित भोजन करनेवाला साधक धैर्यपूर्वक इन्द्रियोंका नियमन करके, शरीरवाणीमनको वशमें करके, शब्दादि विषयोंका त्याग करके और रागद्वेषको छोड़कर निरन्तर ध्यानयोगके परायण हो जाता है, वह अहंकार, बल, दर्प, काम, क्रोध और परिग्रहका त्याग करके एवं निर्मम तथा शान्त होकर ब्रह्मप्राप्तिका पात्र हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::675.english_translation: Dwelling in solitude, eating lightly, and controlling speech, body, and mind, one stays absorbed in meditation, grounded in non-attachment.
bhagwad_gita::675.translation_literal: विविक्तसेवी (dwelling in solitude) / लघ्वाशी (eating lightly) / यतवाक्कायमानसः (one whose speech, body, and mind are restrained) / ध्यानयोगपरो (devoted to meditation-yoga) / नित्यं (always) / वैराग्यं (non-attachment) / समुपाश्रितः (taking refuge in)
bhagwad_gita::675.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::675.essence: Freedom grows from deliberate simplicity and steady restraint.
bhagwad_gita::675.simple_meaning: A serious seeker lives simply, keeps the senses under control, and stays devoted to meditation with non-attachment.
bhagwad_gita::675.simple_insight: There is calm in a life that is deliberately uncluttered.
bhagwad_gita::675.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Krishna is finishing his map of inner freedom for Arjuna. After describing the purified mind, he adds the daily disciplines that support it: solitude, light eating, restraint of speech, body, and mind, and steady meditation rooted in non-attachment.
bhagwad_gita::675.modern_relevance: You turn off your phone, skip the extra noise, and sit alone before dawn. The mind settles faster when the day stops feeding it distractions.
bhagwad_gita::675.insight: It shifts the focus from heroic moments to the habits that make inner steadiness possible.

bhagwad_gita::676.verse_sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् । विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
bhagwad_gita::676.verse_hindi: जो विशुद्ध सात्त्विकी बुद्धिसे युक्त, वैराग्यके आश्रित, एकान्तका सेवन करनेवाला और नियमित भोजन करनेवाला साधक धैर्यपूर्वक इन्द्रियोंका नियमन करके, शरीरवाणीमनको वशमें करके, शब्दादि विषयोंका त्याग करके और रागद्वेषको छोड़कर निरन्तर ध्यानयोगके परायण हो जाता है, वह अहंकार, बल, दर्प, काम, क्रोध और परिग्रहका त्याग करके एवं निर्मम तथा शान्त होकर ब्रह्मप्राप्तिका पात्र हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::676.english_translation: Free from ego, force, pride, desire, anger, and possession, one becomes peaceful, without “mine,” and fit for union with the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::676.translation_literal: अहङ्कारम् (ego) / बलम् (force) / दर्पम् (pride) / कामम् (desire) / क्रोधम् (anger) / परिग्रहम् (possessiveness) / विमुच्य (having released) / निर्ममः (without mine-ness) / शान्तः (peaceful) / ब्रह्मभूयाय (for becoming the supreme reality) / कल्पते (is fit)
bhagwad_gita::676.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::676.essence: Peace begins when the sense of ownership ends.
bhagwad_gita::676.simple_meaning: Let go of ego, pride, craving, anger, and possessiveness. When the sense of “mine” falls away, the mind becomes peaceful and ready for the supreme reality.
bhagwad_gita::676.simple_insight: Freedom feels lighter than victory. What you release matters more than what you collect.
bhagwad_gita::676.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen, and Krishna is finishing his teaching on renunciation. After showing the discipline of meditation, he names the inner poisons that block freedom: ego, force, pride, desire, anger, and possessiveness.
bhagwad_gita::676.modern_relevance: You type a reply full of defensiveness, then stop before sending. In that pause, you can feel the grip of “I must win” loosening. That release is the real turning point.
bhagwad_gita::676.insight: It shifts the goal from self-protection to inner freedom by dropping the habits that harden the mind.

bhagwad_gita::677.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति । समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::677.verse_hindi: वह ब्रह्मभूतअवस्थाको प्राप्त प्रसन्न मनवाला साधक न तो किसीके लिये शोक करता है और न किसीकी इच्छा करता है ।  ऐसा सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंमें समभाववाला साधक मेरी पराभक्तिको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::677.english_translation: One who has become Brahman, serene in mind, grieves not and desires not. Equal toward all beings, that person attains supreme devotion to Me.
bhagwad_gita::677.translation_literal: ब्रह्मभूतः (having become Brahman) / प्रसन्नात्मा (serene-minded) / न (not) / शोचति (grieves) / न (not) / काङ्क्षति (desires) / समः (equal) / सर्वेषु (in all) / भूतेषु (beings) / मद्भक्तिम् (devotion to Me) / लभते (attains) / पराम् (supreme)
bhagwad_gita::677.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::677.essence: Freedom from craving makes room for the highest devotion.
bhagwad_gita::677.simple_meaning: A person who has reached a steady, clear state no longer grieves or chases after things. Seeing all beings equally, that person reaches the highest devotion to Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::677.simple_insight: Stillness is not emptiness; it can become the doorway to deep love.
bhagwad_gita::677.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna has been taught to loosen his grip on fear, pride, and craving. Krishna now shows the fruit of that inner freedom: a mind that is calm, equal toward all beings, and ready for the deepest devotion.
bhagwad_gita::677.modern_relevance: You finally stop checking your phone after sending the hard message. The chest unclenches, the need for reassurance fades, and something steadier than anxiety begins to move you.
bhagwad_gita::677.insight: It shifts the mind from grasping and comparison to equal seeing and wholehearted devotion.

bhagwad_gita::678.verse_sanskrit: भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः । ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::678.verse_hindi: उस पराभक्तिसे मेरेको, मैं जितना हूँ और जो हूँ  इसको तत्त्वसे जान लेता है तथा मेरेको तत्त्वसे जानकर फिर तत्काल मेरेमें प्रविष्ट हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::678.english_translation: Through devoted love, one truly knows Me as I am. Knowing Me in truth, one enters into Me at once.
bhagwad_gita::678.translation_literal: भक्त्या (through devoted love) / माम् (Me) / अभिजानाति (knows truly) / यावान् (as much as) / यः (who) / च (and) / अस्मि (I am) / तत्त्वतः (in truth) / ततः (then) / माम् (Me) / तत्त्वतः (in truth) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / विशते (enters) / तत्-अनन्तरम् (immediately after)
bhagwad_gita::678.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::678.essence: Devoted love turns understanding into immediate nearness.
bhagwad_gita::678.simple_meaning: Devoted love lets a person know Krishna truly, beyond surface ideas. That true knowing leads straight into closeness with him.
bhagwad_gita::678.simple_insight: Love is not just feeling; it becomes the way to real understanding and intimacy.
bhagwad_gita::678.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, after Krishna has described the calm devotee who no longer clings or grieves, he gives the culmination of bhakti. The final question is no longer how to act, but how to know the divine directly and completely.
bhagwad_gita::678.modern_relevance: You can study someone for years and still miss them. Then one act of wholehearted love cuts through every theory and makes them unmistakably real.
bhagwad_gita::678.insight: It shifts devotion from emotion alone to a mode of direct knowing that changes relationship into union.

bhagwad_gita::679.verse_sanskrit: सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः । मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::679.verse_hindi: मेरा आश्रय लेनेवाला भक्त सदा सब कर्म करता हुआ भी मेरी कृपासे शाश्वत अविनाशी पदको प्राप्त हो जाता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::679.english_translation: A devotee who takes refuge in me, while always doing all actions, attains the eternal, imperishable state through my grace.
bhagwad_gita::679.translation_literal: सर्वकर्माणि (all actions) / अपि (even) / सदा (always) / कुर्वाणः (doing) / मद्व्यपाश्रयः (taking refuge in me) / मत्प्रसादात् (by my grace) / अवाप्नोति (attains) / शाश्वतम् (eternal) / पदम् (state) / अव्ययम् (imperishable)
bhagwad_gita::679.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::679.essence: Continuous action and complete refuge can lead to the same unchanging state.
bhagwad_gita::679.simple_meaning: Keep doing all your work, but rely on Krishna rather than your own control. That surrender leads to an eternal, unchanging state.
bhagwad_gita::679.simple_insight: You can stay active without feeling alone in the burden. Grace makes the path feel supported.
bhagwad_gita::679.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra battlefield, Arjuna is being shown the final shape of devotion. Krishna says that even while a person keeps acting in the world, taking refuge in him leads to the imperishable state beyond fear and loss.
bhagwad_gita::679.modern_relevance: You send the hard message, sign the painful form, or walk into the difficult room anyway. The body acts; the grip on control loosens.
bhagwad_gita::679.insight: It shifts action from self-reliance to surrendered participation, where effort continues but ownership of the result is released.

bhagwad_gita::680.verse_sanskrit: चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः । बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥
bhagwad_gita::680.verse_hindi: चित्तसे सम्पूर्ण कर्म मुझमें अर्पण करके, मेरे परायण होकर तथा समताका आश्रय लेकर निरन्तर मुझमें चित्तवाला हो जा ॥
bhagwad_gita::680.english_translation: With your mind, surrender all actions to Me. Take refuge in the discipline of clear understanding and remain constantly focused on Me.
bhagwad_gita::680.translation_literal: चेतसा (with the mind) / सर्वकर्माणि (all actions) / मयि (in Me) / संन्यस्य (having renounced, having placed aside) / मत्परः (devoted to Me, having Me as the highest) / बुद्धियोगम् (the discipline of discernment) / उपाश्रित्य (taking refuge in) / मच्चित्तः (with mind fixed on Me) / सततं (constantly) / भव (be)
bhagwad_gita::680.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::680.essence: Hand over the action, and let the mind stay gathered there.
bhagwad_gita::680.simple_meaning: Give every action to Krishna, rely on clear understanding, and keep your mind steadily on the divine.
bhagwad_gita::680.simple_insight: You do not have to carry everything yourself. Steady devotion can hold what the ego cannot.
bhagwad_gita::680.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna is still frozen between duty and despair. Krishna now gives the inner method: offer every action to him, rely on disciplined understanding, and keep the mind fixed there. This verse prepares Arjuna to act without being scattered by fear.
bhagwad_gita::680.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that changes everything, and your hand hovers over the button. Instead of spiraling, you place the whole act in something larger than fear and stay centered.
bhagwad_gita::680.insight: It shifts attention from self-protection to steady alignment with the highest aim.

bhagwad_gita::681.verse_sanskrit: मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि । अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि ॥
bhagwad_gita::681.verse_hindi: मेरेमें चित्तवाला होकर तू मेरी कृपासे सम्पूर्ण विघ्नोंको तर जायगा और यदि तू अहंकारके कारण मेरी बात नहीं सुनेगा तो तेरा पतन हो जायगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::681.english_translation: Centered in me, you will cross all obstacles through my grace. But if you do not listen because of ego, you will fall.
bhagwad_gita::681.translation_literal: मच्चित्तः (with mind fixed on me) / सर्वदुर्गाणि (all difficulties) / मत्प्रसादात् (by my grace) / तरिष्यसि (you will cross over) / अथ (but) / चेत् (if) / त्वम् (you) / अहङ्कारात् (from ego) / न (not) / श्रोष्यसि (you will listen) / विनङ्क्ष्यसि (you will perish/fall)
bhagwad_gita::681.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::681.essence: Grace opens the way; ego closes it.
bhagwad_gita::681.simple_meaning: Keep your attention fixed on the divine, and you can cross every obstacle through grace. Refuse that guidance out of ego, and you will fall.
bhagwad_gita::681.simple_insight: Surrender brings relief; resistance makes the same path collapse.
bhagwad_gita::681.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is still frozen while Krishna finishes his final instruction. After teaching action, offering, and surrender, Krishna now warns him plainly: stay inwardly with me and obstacles lose their power; let ego block hearing, and ruin follows.
bhagwad_gita::681.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that could end a relationship, and your pride keeps rewriting the words. Stay open enough to hear what is true, or the same ego will trip you into the wrong choice.
bhagwad_gita::681.insight: It shifts you from self-protection to receptive surrender, where guidance can actually reach you.

bhagwad_gita::682.verse_sanskrit: यदहङ्कारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे । मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति ॥
bhagwad_gita::682.verse_hindi: अहंकारका आश्रय लेकर तू जो ऐसा मान रहा है कि मैं युद्ध नहीं करूँगा, तेरा यह निश्चय मिथ्या झूठा है क्योंकि तेरी क्षात्रप्रकृति तेरेको युद्धमें लगा देगी ॥
bhagwad_gita::682.english_translation: Relying on ego, you think, 'I will not fight.' That resolve is false; your nature will drive you into battle.
bhagwad_gita::682.translation_literal: यत् (which) / अहङ्कारम् (ego) / आश्रित्य (taking refuge in) / न (not) / योत्स्ये (I will fight) इति (thus) / मन्यसे (you think) / मिथ्या (false) / एषः (this) / व्यवसायः (resolve) / ते (your) / प्रकृतिः (nature) / त्वाम् (you) / नियोक्ष्यति (will impel)
bhagwad_gita::682.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::682.essence: Ego cannot veto what your nature has already chosen.
bhagwad_gita::682.simple_meaning: Refusing your duty out of pride will not hold. Your deeper nature will still push you toward the action that fits you.
bhagwad_gita::682.simple_insight: It brings relief from fake control: denial cannot erase what you are built to do.
bhagwad_gita::682.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has dropped into paralysis and Krishna is stripping away every excuse. After telling him to act without ego, Krishna says even this refusal is unstable: Arjuna's warrior nature will still drive him back into battle.
bhagwad_gita::682.modern_relevance: You sit in the car outside the house, rehearsing the text you do not want to send. The longer you delay, the more obvious it becomes: avoidance is not the same as freedom.
bhagwad_gita::682.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protective refusal to honest alignment with one's real duty.

bhagwad_gita::683.verse_sanskrit: स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा । कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत् ॥
bhagwad_gita::683.verse_hindi: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  अपने स्वभावजन्य कर्मसे बँधा हुआ तू मोहके कारण जो नहीं करना चाहता, उसको तू क्षात्रप्रकृतिके परवश होकर करेगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::683.english_translation: Bound by your own nature-born duty, you will do what you do not want to do in confusion. Even against your will, you will act.
bhagwad_gita::683.translation_literal: स्वभावजेन (born of one's own nature) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / निबद्धः (bound) / स्वेन (by one's own) / कर्मणा (by action) / कर्तुं (to do) / न इच्छसि (you do not wish) / यत् (that which) / मोहात् (from confusion) / करिष्यसि (you will do) / अवशः अपि (even unwillingly) / तत् (that)
bhagwad_gita::683.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::683.essence: Resistance cannot cancel what your nature is already set to do.
bhagwad_gita::683.simple_meaning: Your own nature pushes you toward certain actions. Confusion may make you resist them, but you may still end up doing them anyway.
bhagwad_gita::683.simple_insight: It can feel relieving to stop fighting what your character and role are already asking of you.
bhagwad_gita::683.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna keeps resisting the war. Krishna tells him that his warrior nature is already shaping his choices. Even if Arjuna refuses in confusion, that same nature will still drive him to act.
bhagwad_gita::683.modern_relevance: You keep saying you won't send the message, quit the job, or tell the hard truth. Hours later, the same pressure inside you pushes you to do it anyway.
bhagwad_gita::683.insight: It shifts you from self-deception to honest recognition of the forces already moving your behavior.

bhagwad_gita::684.verse_sanskrit: ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति । भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥
bhagwad_gita::684.verse_hindi: हे अर्जुन  ईश्वर सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके हृदयमें रहता है और अपनी मायासे शरीररूपी यन्त्रपर आरूढ़ हुए सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंको उनके स्वभावके अनुसार भ्रमण कराता रहता है ॥
bhagwad_gita::684.english_translation: O Arjuna, the Lord abides in the heart of all beings and, by His maya, causes all beings mounted on a body-machine to revolve according to their nature.
bhagwad_gita::684.translation_literal: ईश्वरः (the Lord) / सर्वभूतानाम् (of all beings) / हृद्देशे (in the heart-place) / अर्जुन (Arjuna) / तिष्ठति (dwells) / भ्रामयन् (causing to revolve) / सर्वभूतानि (all beings) / यन्त्रारूढानि (mounted on a machine) / मायया (by maya)
bhagwad_gita::684.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::684.essence: The deeper mover is not your ego, and surrender begins there.
bhagwad_gita::684.simple_meaning: The divine lives in every being’s heart and moves all beings through maya, as if they were riding a body-machine and turning according to their nature.
bhagwad_gita::684.simple_insight: You are not as in control as you think, and that can be deeply humbling.
bhagwad_gita::684.detailed_meaning: Krishna is still answering Arjuna’s refusal to fight. After saying Arjuna’s nature will drive him, he now explains the deeper force behind all movement: the divine within every being, and the veil of maya that makes bodies seem self-directed. This prepares Arjuna to surrender.
bhagwad_gita::684.modern_relevance: You keep replaying the same argument in your head, certain you are choosing freely, yet your fears and habits keep steering you back. This verse points to the deeper forces already moving the machine.
bhagwad_gita::684.insight: It shifts responsibility from egoic control to humble surrender to the deeper order already at work.

bhagwad_gita::685.verse_sanskrit: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत । तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::685.verse_hindi: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन  तू सर्वभावसे उस ईश्वरकी ही शरणमें चला जा ।  उसकी कृपासे तू परमशान्तिसंसारसे सर्वथा उपरति को और अविनाशी परमपदको प्राप्त हो जायगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::685.english_translation: Surrender to the divine with your whole being, Arjuna. By that grace, you will reach supreme peace and the eternal abode.
bhagwad_gita::685.translation_literal: तमेव (to that alone) / शरणं (refuge) / गच्छ (go) / सर्वभावेन (with all your being) / भारत (O descendant of Bharata) / तत्प्रसादात् (by that grace) / परां (supreme) / शान्तिं (peace) / स्थानं (abode) / प्राप्स्यसि (you will attain) / शाश्वतम् (eternal)
bhagwad_gita::685.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::685.essence: Wholehearted surrender opens the door to lasting peace.
bhagwad_gita::685.simple_meaning: Give yourself entirely to the divine, and you will receive deep peace and the eternal home beyond change.
bhagwad_gita::685.simple_insight: It can feel relieving to stop carrying everything alone and let grace do what effort cannot.
bhagwad_gita::685.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, Arjuna is frozen between duty and grief. Krishna has already shown him the hidden order behind action, mind, and devotion. Now he gives the final turn: not struggle, but complete refuge in the divine.
bhagwad_gita::685.modern_relevance: You are standing at a hospital corridor, unable to fix what is happening inside the room. At some point, clenched control becomes exhaustion; this verse points to the release of handing the burden over.
bhagwad_gita::685.insight: It shifts the mind from self-managed strain to wholehearted surrender, trusting grace to complete what effort cannot.

bhagwad_gita::686.verse_sanskrit: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया । विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
bhagwad_gita::686.verse_hindi: यह गुह्यसे भी गुह्यतर शरणागतिरूप ज्ञान मैंने तुझे कह दिया ।  अब तू इसपर अच्छी तरहसे विचार करके जैसा चाहता है, वैसा कर ॥
bhagwad_gita::686.english_translation: Thus I have explained to you the most secret wisdom. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish.
bhagwad_gita::686.translation_literal: इति (thus) / ते (to you) / ज्ञानम् (wisdom) / आख्यातम् (has been explained) / गुह्यात् (than the secret) / गुह्यतरम् (more secret) / मया (by me) / विमृश्य (having reflected upon) / एतत् (this) / अशेषेण (completely) / यथा (as) / इच्छसि (you wish) / तथा (so) / कुरु (do)
bhagwad_gita::686.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::686.essence: True guidance ends by returning choice to you.
bhagwad_gita::686.simple_meaning: Krishna says he has given Arjuna the deepest teaching. Arjuna should think it through completely and then decide what to do.
bhagwad_gita::686.simple_insight: Real freedom includes thinking clearly before choosing.
bhagwad_gita::686.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has heard Krishna’s final teaching about surrender and inner freedom. Krishna does not force obedience. He gives the deepest instruction, then leaves Arjuna responsible for his own choice.
bhagwad_gita::686.modern_relevance: You’ve heard every side of a painful decision and still feel pulled apart. The clearest voice may not be the loudest one — it may be the one that leaves room for honest choice.
bhagwad_gita::686.insight: It shifts the mind from pressure to responsibility: understand fully, then decide without inner coercion.

bhagwad_gita::687.verse_sanskrit: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::687.verse_hindi: सबसे अत्यन्त गोपनीय वचन तू फिर मेरेसे सुन ।  तू मेरा अत्यन्त प्रिय है, इसलिये मैं तेरे हितकी बात कहूँगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::687.english_translation: Listen again to My most secret word. You are dear to Me, so I will speak for your good.
bhagwad_gita::687.translation_literal: सर्वगुह्यतमं (most secret) / भूयः (again) / श्रृणु (listen) / मे (my) / परमं (highest) / वचः (word) / इष्टः असि (you are dear) / मे (to me) / दृढम् (truly) / इति (thus) / ततः (therefore) / वक्ष्यामि (I will speak) / ते (to you) / हितम् (what is good)
bhagwad_gita::687.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::687.essence: The deepest teaching is spoken as care, not command.
bhagwad_gita::687.simple_meaning: Krishna asks Arjuna to hear one more secret teaching. Because Arjuna is dear to him, Krishna will speak only what is truly beneficial.
bhagwad_gita::687.simple_insight: Being loved means being told what helps, not just what comforts.
bhagwad_gita::687.detailed_meaning: On the Kurukshetra field, Arjuna has already been told the deepest teaching: surrender to Krishna. Krishna now pauses before the final command and says there is still a more secret word to hear. He speaks as a teacher who cares personally for Arjuna's welfare.
bhagwad_gita::687.modern_relevance: A friend stops you before you make the wrong call and says, 'Hear me out once more — I’m telling you this because I care.' That moment can change everything.
bhagwad_gita::687.insight: It shifts the listener from passive hearing to trusting that the next instruction is meant for their good.

bhagwad_gita::688.verse_sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु । मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥
bhagwad_gita::688.verse_hindi: तू मेरा भक्त हो जा, मेरेमें मनवाला हो जा, मेरा पूजन करनेवाला हो जा और मेरेको नमस्कार कर ।  ऐसा करनेसे तू मेरेको ही प्राप्त हो जायगा  यह मैं तेरे सामने सत्य प्रतिज्ञा करता हूँ क्योंकि तू मेरा अत्यन्त प्रिय है ॥
bhagwad_gita::688.english_translation: Fix your mind on me, become my devotee, worship me, and bow to me. You will come to me; I promise you this truly, because you are dear to me.
bhagwad_gita::688.translation_literal: मन्मना (with mind on me) / भव (become) / मद्भक्तः (my devotee) / मद्याजी (my worshipper) / माम् (to me) / नमस्कुरु (bow) / माम् (me) / एव (only) / एष्यसि (you will come) / सत्यम् (truth) / ते (to you) / प्रतिजाने (I promise) / प्रियः (dear) / असि (you are) / मे (to me)
bhagwad_gita::688.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::688.essence: Wholehearted devotion becomes the shortest path home.
bhagwad_gita::688.simple_meaning: Krishna asks Arjuna to keep his mind on him, love him, worship him, and show reverence. He promises that this wholehearted devotion leads to union with him.
bhagwad_gita::688.simple_insight: Devotion is not vague feeling; it becomes a whole-life orientation that steadies the heart.
bhagwad_gita::688.detailed_meaning: On the edge of battle, Arjuna is still wavering. Krishna now gives the simplest direct path: keep your mind on me, love me, worship me, and bow in reverence. This is the final turn from hesitation to complete surrender.
bhagwad_gita::688.modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, about to say the one honest sentence that could change everything. This verse asks for a single-hearted turn toward what is highest, even when fear is loud.
bhagwad_gita::688.insight: It shifts devotion from sentiment to commitment: attention, love, action, and humility all point in one direction.

bhagwad_gita::689.verse_sanskrit: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज । अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥
bhagwad_gita::689.verse_hindi: सम्पूर्ण धर्मोंका आश्रय छोड़कर तू केवल मेरी शरणमें आ जा ।  मैं तुझे सम्पूर्ण पापोंसे मुक्त कर दूँगा, चिन्ता मत कर ॥
bhagwad_gita::689.english_translation: Abandon all duties and take refuge in Me alone. I will free you from all wrongdoing; do not grieve.
bhagwad_gita::689.translation_literal: सर्वधर्मान् (all duties) / परित्यज्य (having abandoned) / माम् (to Me) / एकम् (alone) / शरणम् (refuge) / व्रज (go) / अहम् (I) / त्वा (you) / सर्वपापेभ्यः (from all wrongdoing) / मोक्षयिष्यामि (will free) / मा (do not) / शुचः (grieve)
bhagwad_gita::689.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::689.essence: Total refuge ends the burden of fear.
bhagwad_gita::689.simple_meaning: Let go of every lesser support and place yourself fully in Krishna's care. He promises freedom from all wrongdoing and asks Arjuna not to grieve.
bhagwad_gita::689.simple_insight: There is relief in surrendering what you cannot finally control.
bhagwad_gita::689.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna has been broken open by doubt. After teaching him every path, Krishna gives the final, most secret instruction: stop clinging to every other support and come to Me alone. This is the closing turn of the entire dialogue.
bhagwad_gita::689.modern_relevance: You are standing outside a hospital room, phone in hand, after the call that changed everything. At some point, control runs out. This verse speaks to the moment you stop bargaining and finally place the burden down.
bhagwad_gita::689.insight: It shifts the mind from self-managed control to complete reliance on the divine.

bhagwad_gita::690.verse_sanskrit: इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन । न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति ॥
bhagwad_gita::690.verse_hindi: यह सर्वगुह्यतम वचन अतपस्वीको मत कहना अभक्तको कभी मत कहना जो सुनना नहीं चाहता, उसको मत कहना और जो मेरेमें दोषदृष्टि करता है, उससे भी मत कहना ॥
bhagwad_gita::690.english_translation: Never speak this to one without discipline, one without devotion, one unwilling to listen, or one who finds fault with me.
bhagwad_gita::690.translation_literal: इदम् (this) / ते (to you) / न (not) / अतपस्काय (to one without discipline) / न (not) / अभक्ताय (to one without devotion) / कदाचन (ever) / न (not) / च (and) / अशुश्रूषवे (to one unwilling to listen) / वाच्यम् (to be spoken) / न (not) / च (and) / माम् (me) / यः (who) / अभ्यसूयति (finds fault with)
bhagwad_gita::690.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::690.essence: Deep truth must be shared only with those ready to receive it.
bhagwad_gita::690.simple_meaning: Keep this deepest teaching away from people who are unreceptive, undisciplined, or hostile to Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::690.simple_insight: Sacred truth needs the right listener. Not every ear is ready for what can transform it.
bhagwad_gita::690.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna has finished his final teaching to Arjuna. After revealing surrender as the way to freedom, he now guards that teaching: it should not be given to the undisciplined, the unreceptive, the unwilling, or the hostile.
bhagwad_gita::690.modern_relevance: You finally say something honest and life-changing, but the room is wrong for it. Some people want a debate, not transformation; some ears are simply not open yet.
bhagwad_gita::690.insight: It teaches discernment in sharing wisdom: protect what is sacred from contempt and unreadiness.

bhagwad_gita::691.verse_sanskrit: य इमं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति । भक्ितं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः ॥
bhagwad_gita::691.verse_hindi: मेरेमें पराभक्ति करके जो इस परम गोपनीय संवादगीताग्रन्थ को मेरे भक्तोंमें कहेगा, वह मुझे ही प्राप्त होगा  इसमें कोई सन्देह नहीं है ॥
bhagwad_gita::691.english_translation: Whoever shares this supreme secret among my devotees, with devoted love for me, will surely come to me without doubt.
bhagwad_gita::691.translation_literal: यः (whoever) / इमम् (this) / परमम् (supreme) / गुह्यम् (secret) / मद्भक्तेषु (among my devotees) / अभिधास्यति (will speak, will declare) / भक्तिम् (devotion) / मयि (in me) / पराम् (highest) / कृत्वा (having made) / माम् (me) / एव (indeed) / एष्यति (will come, will attain) / असंशयः (without doubt)
bhagwad_gita::691.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::691.essence: Devotion deepens when sacred truth is passed on.
bhagwad_gita::691.simple_meaning: Anyone who shares this deepest teaching with devoted love will reach Krishna without doubt.
bhagwad_gita::691.simple_insight: Teaching what you love deepens your own bond with it.
bhagwad_gita::691.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, after Krishna has offered the final surrender, he adds one more promise: the deepest teaching is not meant to stay locked inside Arjuna. Whoever speaks it to Krishna's devotees with devotion becomes one of those who reaches Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::691.modern_relevance: You finally understand something life-changing after a long crisis, and your first instinct is to keep it private. The verse says the truth ripens when you pass it on with reverence.
bhagwad_gita::691.insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to shared transmission.

bhagwad_gita::692.verse_sanskrit: न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्िचन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः । भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि ॥
bhagwad_gita::692.verse_hindi: उसके समान मेरा अत्यन्त प्रिय कार्य करनेवाला मनुष्योंमें कोई भी नहीं है और इस भूमण्डलपर उसके समान मेरा दूसरा कोई प्रियतर होगा भी नहीं ॥
bhagwad_gita::692.english_translation: Among all human beings, no one does what is more dear to me than he does. On this earth, no one will ever be dearer than he is.
bhagwad_gita::692.translation_literal: न च (and not) / तस्मात् (than him) / मनुष्येषु (among human beings) / कश्चित् (anyone) / मे (to me) / प्रिय-कृत्तमः (most dear-doing) / भविता (will become) / न च (and not) / मे (to me) / तस्मात् (than him) / अन्यः (another) / प्रियतरो (dearer) / भुवि (on earth)
bhagwad_gita::692.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::692.essence: Sharing this teaching becomes the highest form of devotion.
bhagwad_gita::692.simple_meaning: Anyone who passes on this sacred teaching becomes especially dear to Krishna. No one on earth can surpass that devotion.
bhagwad_gita::692.simple_insight: Teaching what you have received is not small. It is treated as a deeply loving act.
bhagwad_gita::692.detailed_meaning: The war is over, and Krishna is giving Arjuna the final seal on the whole dialogue. After warning him to share this teaching carefully, Krishna now says that the one who spreads it with devotion becomes the dearest person on earth to him.
bhagwad_gita::692.modern_relevance: You explain a hard-earned lesson to someone who is ready to hear it, not to impress them. The act of passing on what truly helped you becomes its own offering.
bhagwad_gita::692.insight: It shifts the reader from private ownership of wisdom to generous transmission of it.

bhagwad_gita::693.verse_sanskrit: अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः । ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः ॥
bhagwad_gita::693.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य हम दोनोंके इस धर्ममय संवादका अध्ययन करेगा, उसके द्वारा भी मैं ज्ञानयज्ञसे पूजित होऊँगा  ऐसा मेरा मत है ॥
bhagwad_gita::693.english_translation: Whoever studies this sacred dialogue of ours will also worship me through the sacrifice of knowledge; that is my view.
bhagwad_gita::693.translation_literal: अध्येष्यते (will study) / च (also) / यः (whoever) / इमम् (this) / धर्म्यम् (sacred, righteous) / संवादम् (dialogue) / आवयोः (of us two) / ज्ञानयज्ञेन (through the sacrifice of knowledge) / तेन (by that one) / अहम् (I) / इष्टः (worshipped) / स्याम् (may be) / इति (thus) / मे (my) / मतिः (view)
bhagwad_gita::693.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::693.essence: Sincere study of this dialogue becomes worship itself.
bhagwad_gita::693.simple_meaning: Reading and studying Krishna and Arjuna’s sacred dialogue is itself a form of worship through knowledge.
bhagwad_gita::693.simple_insight: You do not have to wait for a ritual moment; sincere study can already be an offering.
bhagwad_gita::693.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna is finishing his teaching to Arjuna after the crisis has been named and answered. He says that anyone who studies this sacred dialogue between them is performing a sacrifice of knowledge and is worshipping him.
bhagwad_gita::693.modern_relevance: You open a book late at night because a hard decision is waiting tomorrow. The reading is not escape; it becomes an offering that steadies your mind before you act.
bhagwad_gita::693.insight: It turns study into practice, and learning into an act of reverence rather than information gathering.

bhagwad_gita::694.verse_sanskrit: श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च श्रृणुयादपि यो नरः । सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभाँल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::694.verse_hindi: श्रद्धावान् और दोषदृष्टिसे रहित जो मनुष्य इस गीताग्रन्थको सुन भी लेगा, वह भी सम्पूर्ण पापोंसे मुक्त होकर पुण्यकारियोंके शुभ लोकोंको प्राप्त हो जायगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::694.english_translation: Even a person who listens to this with trust and without fault-finding becomes free and reaches the auspicious realms earned by noble action.
bhagwad_gita::694.translation_literal: श्रद्धावान् (trustful) / अनसूयः (without fault-finding) / च (and) / श्रृणुयात् (may listen) / अपि (even) / यः (who) / नरः (person) / सः (that one) / अपि (even) / मुक्तः (freed) / शुभान् (auspicious) / लोकान् (realms) / प्राप्नुयात् (may attain) / पुण्यकर्मणाम् (of those with noble actions)
bhagwad_gita::694.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::694.essence: Trustful listening can open the door to freedom.
bhagwad_gita::694.simple_meaning: A person who listens with trust and without criticism is lifted free and reaches a better state earned by good action.
bhagwad_gita::694.simple_insight: You do not need perfect understanding to begin; open listening itself can change you.
bhagwad_gita::694.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield, after Krishna has finished his teaching, he widens the promise beyond Arjuna. Anyone who hears this dialogue with trust and an open mind can be freed from confusion and reach a higher state.
bhagwad_gita::694.modern_relevance: You hear a hard truth in a quiet room and feel the urge to dismiss it. The verse says the turning point is not brilliance — it is listening without defensiveness.
bhagwad_gita::694.insight: It shifts the reader from judging teaching to receiving it, making openness itself the first practice.

bhagwad_gita::695.verse_sanskrit: कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा । कच्चिदज्ञानसंमोहः प्रनष्टस्ते धनञ्जय ॥
bhagwad_gita::695.verse_hindi: हे पृथानन्दन  क्या तुमने एकाग्रचित्तसे इसको सुना और हे धनञ्जय  क्या तुम्हारा अज्ञानसे उत्पन्न मोह नष्ट हुआ ॥
bhagwad_gita::695.english_translation: O Partha, have you heard this with one-pointed mind? O Dhananjaya, has the delusion born of ignorance been destroyed in you?
bhagwad_gita::695.translation_literal: कच्चिद् (whether) / एतत् (this) / श्रुतम् (heard) / पार्थ (O Partha) / त्वया (by you) / एकाग्रेण (with one-pointed) / चेतसा (mind) / कच्चिद् (whether) / अज्ञान-संमोहः (delusion born of ignorance) / प्रनष्टः (destroyed) / ते (your) / धनञ्जय (O Dhananjaya)
bhagwad_gita::695.speaker: Krishna
bhagwad_gita::695.essence: True listening should end confusion, not just collect words.
bhagwad_gita::695.simple_meaning: Krishna asks whether Arjuna has listened carefully and whether his confusion has been cleared away.
bhagwad_gita::695.simple_insight: Being heard fully can be the first sign that confusion is loosening.
bhagwad_gita::695.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Kurukshetra, Krishna has finished his long teaching and turns to Arjuna, checking whether the words have truly landed. The war still waits, but the real test is whether Arjuna's ignorance and confusion have been broken.
bhagwad_gita::695.modern_relevance: After a hard conversation, you pause and ask yourself: did I really listen, or just hear the words? That moment decides whether confusion is still running the show.
bhagwad_gita::695.insight: It shifts attention from passive hearing to whether understanding has actually taken root.

bhagwad_gita::696.verse_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचनष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत । स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥
bhagwad_gita::696.verse_hindi: अर्जुन बोले  हे अच्युत  आपकी कृपासे मेरा मोह नष्ट हो गया है और स्मृति प्राप्त हो गयी है ।  मैं सन्देहरहित होकर स्थित हूँ ।  अब मैं आपकी आज्ञाका पालन करूँगा ॥
bhagwad_gita::696.english_translation: Arjuna said: By your grace, O Achyuta, my delusion is destroyed and memory restored. I stand free of doubt and will do what you say.
bhagwad_gita::696.translation_literal: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / नष्टः (destroyed) / मोहः (delusion) / स्मृतिः (memory) / लब्धा (obtained) / त्वत्-प्रसादात् (by your grace) / मया (by me) / अच्युत (O Achyuta) / स्थितः अस्मि (I am standing) / गत-सन्देहः (without doubt) / करिष्ये (I will do) / वचनम् (word) / तव (your)
bhagwad_gita::696.speaker: Arjuna
bhagwad_gita::696.essence: Grace ends confusion and turns insight into obedience.
bhagwad_gita::696.simple_meaning: Arjuna says Krishna's grace has removed his confusion. His doubt is gone, and he is ready to follow Krishna's instruction.
bhagwad_gita::696.simple_insight: Relief comes when inner conflict ends and the next step becomes clear.
bhagwad_gita::696.detailed_meaning: On Kurukshetra, Arjuna has been shattered by grief and hesitation. After Krishna's teaching, he speaks with a changed mind: confusion has fallen away, clarity has returned, and he is ready to act in alignment with Krishna.
bhagwad_gita::696.modern_relevance: You finally make the call after days of avoidance. The knot in your chest loosens, not because the choice became easy, but because you know what you must do.
bhagwad_gita::696.insight: It shifts you from paralysis and second-guessing into clear, committed action.

bhagwad_gita::697.verse_sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाचइत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः । संवादमिममश्रौषमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम् ॥
bhagwad_gita::697.verse_hindi: सञ्जय बोले  इस प्रकार मैंने भगवान् वासुदेव और महात्मा पृथानन्दन अर्जुनका यह रोमाञ्चित करनेवाला अद्भुत संवाद सुना ॥
bhagwad_gita::697.english_translation: Sanjaya said: Thus I heard this wondrous, hair-raising dialogue between Vasudeva and the great-souled Partha.
bhagwad_gita::697.translation_literal: सञ्जय उवाच (Sanjaya said) / इति (thus) / अहम् (I) / वासुदेवस्य (of Vasudeva) / पार्थस्य (of Partha) / च (and) / महात्मनः (of the great-souled one) / संवादम् (dialogue) / इमम् (this) / अश्रौषम् (I heard) / अद्भुतम् (wonderful) / रोमहर्षणम् (hair-raising)
bhagwad_gita::697.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::697.essence: A true dialogue can leave the listener shaken and changed.
bhagwad_gita::697.simple_meaning: Sanjaya closes by saying he heard this astonishing exchange between Krishna and Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::697.simple_insight: Some truths arrive as living experience, not secondhand theory.
bhagwad_gita::697.detailed_meaning: The war is still paused on Kurukshetra. Arjuna has just regained clarity, and Krishna’s teaching is complete. Sanjaya ends by telling Dhritarashtra that he personally heard this extraordinary dialogue between Vasudeva and the great-souled Arjuna.
bhagwad_gita::697.modern_relevance: You sit in a silent car after a life-changing conversation, still feeling the words in your body. Some exchanges are not just heard; they rearrange you.
bhagwad_gita::697.insight: It frames the Gita as a witnessed transformation, not a detached lecture.

bhagwad_gita::698.verse_hindi: व्यासजीकी कृपासे मैंने स्वयं इस परम गोपनीय योग गीताग्रन्थ को कहते हुए साक्षात् योगेश्वर भगवान् श्रीकृष्णसे सुना है ॥
bhagwad_gita::698.english_translation: By Vyasa's grace, I heard this supreme secret yoga directly from Krishna, the Lord of yoga, as he spoke it himself.
bhagwad_gita::698.translation_literal: व्यासप्रसादात् (by Vyasa's grace) / श्रुतवान् (I heard) / एतत् (this) / गुहम् (secret) / अहम् (I) / परम् (supreme) / योगम् (yoga) / योगेश्वरात् (from the Lord of yoga) / कृष्णात् (from Krishna) / साक्षात् (directly) / कथयतः (speaking) / स्वयम् (himself)
bhagwad_gita::698.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::698.essence: The deepest teaching is received, not invented.
bhagwad_gita::698.simple_meaning: Sanjaya says he heard the highest secret teaching directly from Krishna, by Vyasa's grace.
bhagwad_gita::698.simple_insight: Some truths are not guessed; they are received through grace and direct hearing.
bhagwad_gita::698.detailed_meaning: The war is over, and Sanjaya looks back on the entire dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna. He says this teaching was not ordinary speech but the highest secret, heard directly from Krishna himself through Vyasa's grace.
bhagwad_gita::698.modern_relevance: You replay a conversation that changed everything and realise its force came from how directly it was spoken. Some guidance lands only when it is heard without distortion.
bhagwad_gita::698.insight: It shifts attention from secondhand opinion to direct transmission of what matters most.

bhagwad_gita::699.verse_sanskrit: राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम् । केशवार्जुनयोः पुण्यं हृष्यामि च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
bhagwad_gita::699.verse_hindi: हे राजन्  भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण और अर्जुनके इस पवित्र और अद्भुत संवादको याद करकरके मैं बारबार हर्षित हो रहा हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::699.english_translation: O King, remembering again and again this wondrous, holy dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.
bhagwad_gita::699.translation_literal: राजन् (O King) / संस्मृत्य (remembering again and again) / संस्मृत्य (remembering again and again) / संवादम् (dialogue) / इमम् (this) / अद्भुतम् (wonderful, astonishing) / केशव-अर्जुनयोः (of Krishna and Arjuna) / पुण्यम् (holy, purifying) / हृष्यामि (I rejoice) / च (and) / मुहुः मुहुः (again and again)
bhagwad_gita::699.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::699.essence: A sacred conversation keeps giving joy each time it is remembered.
bhagwad_gita::699.simple_meaning: Sanjaya tells Dhritarashtra that he keeps remembering Krishna and Arjuna's sacred, astonishing conversation and feels joy each time.
bhagwad_gita::699.simple_insight: Some words stay alive because they carry real power. Recalling them can lift the heart again and again.
bhagwad_gita::699.detailed_meaning: The war is over, and Sanjaya is speaking to King Dhritarashtra. He does not summarize the Gita coldly; he relives it. The dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna has become so holy and astonishing that simply remembering it fills him with joy.
bhagwad_gita::699.modern_relevance: You replay a conversation that changed you — a teacher's words, a hard truth, a moment of clarity — and the memory still steadies you.
bhagwad_gita::699.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the lasting transformation a true teaching leaves behind.

bhagwad_gita::700.verse_sanskrit: तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः । विस्मयो मे महान् राजन् हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः ॥
bhagwad_gita::700.verse_hindi: हे राजन्  भगवान् श्रीकृष्णके उस अत्यन्त अद्भुत विराट्रूपको याद करकरके मेरेको बड़ा भारी आश्चर्य हो रहा है और मैं बारबार हर्षित हो रहा हूँ ॥
bhagwad_gita::700.english_translation: Remembering that astonishing form of Krishna again and again, I feel great wonder, O King, and I rejoice again and again.
bhagwad_gita::700.translation_literal: तत् (that) / च (and) / संस्मृत्य (remembering) / संस्मृत्य (remembering again and again) / रूपम् (form) / अति-अद्भुतम् (extremely wondrous) / हरेः (of Krishna) / विस्मयः (wonder) / मे (my) / महान् (great) / राजन् (O king) / हृष्यामि (I rejoice) / च (and) / पुनः पुनः (again and again)
bhagwad_gita::700.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::700.essence: Remembering Krishna's vast form still overwhelms the mind with wonder.
bhagwad_gita::700.simple_meaning: Sanjaya says that remembering Krishna's astonishing cosmic form fills him with wonder and repeated joy.
bhagwad_gita::700.simple_insight: A true glimpse of the divine leaves the mind stunned and the heart refreshed.
bhagwad_gita::700.detailed_meaning: The war is over, but Sanjaya is still shaken. After recounting Krishna's teaching and Arjuna's vision, he pauses to say that remembering Krishna's cosmic form fills him with wonder and joy. The vision still lives in him.
bhagwad_gita::700.modern_relevance: You replay a moment that changed you — a funeral, a birth, a breakup, a sudden act of grace — and it still stops you cold. Some experiences keep unfolding long after they end.
bhagwad_gita::700.insight: It turns memory into reverence, showing that real vision keeps renewing awe.

bhagwad_gita::701.verse_sanskrit: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः । तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥
bhagwad_gita::701.verse_hindi: जहाँ योगेश्वर भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण हैं और जहाँ गाण्डीवधनुषधारी अर्जुन हैं, वहाँ ही श्री, विजय, विभूति और अचल नीति है  ऐसा मेरा मत है ॥
bhagwad_gita::701.english_translation: Where Krishna, the master of yoga, is present, and where Arjuna, the bow-bearer, is present, there are prosperity, victory, glory, and firm justice. This is my conviction.
bhagwad_gita::701.translation_literal: यत्र (where) / योगेश्वरः (master of yoga) / कृष्णः (Krishna) / यत्र (where) / पार्थः (Arjuna, son of Pritha) / धनुर्धरः (bow-bearer) / तत्र (there) / श्रीः (prosperity, grace) / विजयः (victory) / भूतिः (glory, power) / ध्रुवा (firm, steadfast) / नीतिः (right order, justice) / मम (my)
bhagwad_gita::701.speaker: Sanjaya
bhagwad_gita::701.essence: Right action carries its own victory.
bhagwad_gita::701.simple_meaning: Sanjaya says that wherever Krishna and Arjuna are together, success, prosperity, and right order are assured.
bhagwad_gita::701.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that true guidance and right action can carry a situation through.
bhagwad_gita::701.detailed_meaning: The war is over, and Sanjaya is closing the Gita for Dhritarashtra. After witnessing Krishna’s teaching and Arjuna’s transformation, he gives his final judgment: wherever Krishna and Arjuna stand together, that side has the force of truth, victory, and stability.
bhagwad_gita::701.modern_relevance: You are about to send the message that will change everything. The room is tense, but you know the decision is aligned. This verse names that strange calm: when principle and courage stand together, the path opens.
bhagwad_gita::701.insight: It shifts attention from fear of outcome to alignment with what is right and steady.

dhammapada::1.verse_sanskrit: Manopubbangama dhamma, manosetha manomaya; manasa ce padutthena bhasati va karoti va, tato nam dukkhamanveti, cakkam va vahato padam.
dhammapada::1.verse_hindi: Mind is the forerunner of all actions. All deeds are led by mind, created by mind. If one speaks or acts with a corrupt mind, suffering follows — as the wheel follows the hoof of an ox.
dhammapada::1.english_translation: Mind is the forerunner of all actions. All deeds are led by mind, created by mind. If one speaks or acts with a corrupt mind, suffering follows — as the wheel follows the hoof of an ox.
dhammapada::1.translation_literal: mano (mind) + pubbangama (forerunner) + dhamma (phenomena/actions); manosa (by mind) + ce (if) + padutthena (corrupt/defiled); dukkham (suffering) + anveti (follows); cakkam (wheel) + va (like) + vahato (of the bearer/ox) + padam (hoof/foot)
dhammapada::1.speaker: Buddha
dhammapada::1.essence: A troubled mind makes every step a wound.
dhammapada::1.simple_meaning: Whatever you think repeatedly shapes the actions you take, and those actions return to you as your life experience. A mind filled with bitterness or confusion will produce speech and behavior that causes harm — and that harm circles back.
dhammapada::1.simple_insight: You are not punished for your anger. You are punished by it. The mind is not a neutral tool — it is the author of your world.
dhammapada::1.detailed_meaning: The Buddha opens the Dhammapada with the most fundamental teaching: mind precedes everything. Not only do our thoughts shape our actions, but the quality of mind we bring to an action determines its fruit. A deed done with agitation, greed, or ill-will — regardless of its external appearance — produces suffering. The wheel-and-ox image is precise: just as the wheel has no choice but to follow the ox's foot, suffering has no choice but to follow a defiled action. This is not moral punishment from outside — it is the mechanical consequence of how consciousness works.
dhammapada::1.modern_relevance: In an age of reactive posting, impulsive decisions, and constant mental noise, this verse is a direct diagnostic: trace your suffering back to the quality of attention you brought to your choices. Cognitive behavioral therapy and mindfulness research both confirm what this verse asserts — the interpretive lens of the mind determines the emotional outcome of any experience.
dhammapada::1.insight: Most people try to fix their circumstances. The Buddha says fix your mind first. The outer world is downstream of the inner one.

dhammapada::2.verse_sanskrit: Manopubbangama dhamma, manosetha manomaya; manasa ce pasannena bhasati va karoti va, tato nam sukhamanveti, chaya va anapayini.
dhammapada::2.verse_hindi: Mind is the forerunner of all actions. All deeds are led by mind, created by mind. If one speaks or acts with a serene mind, happiness follows — as a shadow that never departs.
dhammapada::2.english_translation: Mind is the forerunner of all actions. All deeds are led by mind, created by mind. If one speaks or acts with a serene mind, happiness follows — as a shadow that never departs.
dhammapada::2.translation_literal: manasa (by mind) + ce (if) + pasannena (serene/clear/pure); sukham (happiness/ease) + anveti (follows); chaya (shadow) + va (like) + anapayini (never departing/always present)
dhammapada::2.speaker: Buddha
dhammapada::2.essence: A steady mind casts happiness like a shadow.
dhammapada::2.simple_meaning: Just as verse one warned of a troubled mind producing suffering, this verse offers the counterpart: a mind that is calm, clear, and kind produces speech and action that bring lasting ease — not as a reward given from outside, but as a natural consequence.
dhammapada::2.simple_insight: You don't chase happiness. You cultivate the mind that happiness naturally accompanies.
dhammapada::2.detailed_meaning: The second verse of the Dhammapada is the mirror image of the first. Where verse one tracked the mechanics of suffering, this tracks the mechanics of well-being. Pasannena — the word for 'serene' — carries connotations of clarity, brightness, purity. The shadow image is beautiful in its intimacy: a shadow is not a reward, not a gift, not an achievement. It simply follows. This is the Buddha's point — happiness is not something you earn or find, it is something that cannot help but accompany a mind that has been steadied.
dhammapada::2.modern_relevance: Positive psychology research on what makes people genuinely happy points not to circumstances but to baseline states of mind — attention quality, emotional regulation, sense of meaning. This verse anticipated that finding by 2,500 years. The implication is radical: you already have access to what you're looking for. The work is in the mind, not in the world.
dhammapada::2.insight: Happiness is not a destination. It is the atmosphere of a clear mind — it travels with you once you stop disturbing it.

dhammapada::3.verse_sanskrit: Appamado amatapadam, pamado maccuno padam; appamatta na miyanti, ye pamatta yatha mata.
dhammapada::3.verse_hindi: Heedfulness is the path to the Deathless; heedlessness is the path to death. The heedful do not die; the heedless are as if already dead.
dhammapada::3.english_translation: Heedfulness is the path to the Deathless; heedlessness is the path to death. The heedful do not die; the heedless are as if already dead.
dhammapada::3.translation_literal: appamado (heedfulness/diligence/non-negligence) + amatapadam (path to the deathless/immortal); pamado (heedlessness/negligence) + maccuno (of death) + padam (path); appamatta (the heedful) + na miyanti (do not die); ye pamatta (those who are heedless) + yatha mata (as if dead)
dhammapada::3.speaker: Buddha
dhammapada::3.essence: To pay attention fully is to be fully alive.
dhammapada::3.simple_meaning: To be heedful means to be fully awake and attentive in your actions, speech, and mind. To be heedless is to sleepwalk through life — technically alive but not truly living. The verse frames attention itself as the doorway to what is lasting.
dhammapada::3.simple_insight: Most people die long before their bodies do — lost in distraction, habit, and drift. Heedfulness is the practice of showing up to your own life.
dhammapada::3.detailed_meaning: Appamada — often translated as heedfulness, diligence, or non-negligence — is one of the Buddha's most frequently emphasized virtues. His final words, according to tradition, were an instruction to practice with appamada. The verse draws a stark contrast: those who remain alert and intentional in their practice are connected to something that transcends ordinary mortality, while those who are careless are already disconnected from the living pulse of awareness. This is not a moral threat — it is a description of two modes of being.
dhammapada::3.modern_relevance: In an attention economy designed to fragment focus and keep you in reactive mode, heedfulness is an act of resistance. Research on flow states, deep work, and presence all point to the same thing this verse points to: the quality of attention you bring to life determines the quality of life itself.
dhammapada::3.insight: You can be breathing and still be absent. The verse asks: are you actually here, or just present in body?

dhammapada::4.verse_sanskrit: Sabbapapassa akaranam, kusalassa upasampada; sacittapariyodapanam — etam Buddhassa sasanam.
dhammapada::4.verse_hindi: To abstain from all evil, to cultivate the good, to purify the mind — this is the teaching of all Buddhas.
dhammapada::4.english_translation: To abstain from all evil, to cultivate the good, to purify the mind — this is the teaching of all Buddhas.
dhammapada::4.translation_literal: sabbapapassa (of all evil) + akaranam (non-doing/abstaining); kusalassa (of the wholesome/skillful) + upasampada (cultivation/undertaking); sacittapariyodapanam (purification of one's own mind); etam (this) + Buddhassa (of the Buddhas) + sasanam (teaching/instruction)
dhammapada::4.speaker: Buddha
dhammapada::4.essence: Stop harming. Start building. Purify within.
dhammapada::4.simple_meaning: The entire path of practice can be compressed into three movements: refrain from harmful action, actively cultivate wholesome qualities, and work directly on the mind itself. This triple formula is the distillation of all genuine teaching.
dhammapada::4.simple_insight: Ethics, virtue, and inner clarity are not three separate projects — they are one movement at three depths. Start anywhere and you are drawn toward all three.
dhammapada::4.detailed_meaning: This verse, sometimes called the 'Ovada Patimokkha,' is considered the summary of the entire teaching. It operates at three levels: the outer (behavior), the relational (what you build and contribute), and the inner (the quality of mind itself). What makes this profound is the sequence: abstaining from harm creates the conditions for cultivation; cultivation creates the conditions for purification. Each stage depends on the previous. And the final stage — purifying the mind — is not a metaphor for being virtuous; it is a direct instruction to work on the mind's deepest tendencies.
dhammapada::4.modern_relevance: In a world that often treats ethics as bureaucratic compliance and self-improvement as productivity optimization, this verse insists on integration: your behavior, your contributions, and your inner life are not separate domains. You cannot genuinely improve your mind while continuing to harm others; you cannot truly help others while your mind remains clouded.
dhammapada::4.insight: Most ethical frameworks stop at behavior. This one goes all the way to the source — the mind that generates behavior.

dhammapada::5.verse_sanskrit: Attana va katam papam, attana samkilissati; attana akatam papam, attanava visujjhati; suddhi asuddhi paccattam, nanno annam visodhaye.
dhammapada::5.verse_hindi: By oneself is evil done; by oneself one is defiled. By oneself evil is left undone; by oneself one is purified. Purity and impurity depend on oneself — no one can purify another.
dhammapada::5.english_translation: By oneself is evil done; by oneself one is defiled. By oneself evil is left undone; by oneself one is purified. Purity and impurity depend on oneself — no one can purify another.
dhammapada::5.translation_literal: attana (by oneself) + va (indeed) + katam (done) + papam (evil/harm); samkilissati (is defiled/polluted); akatam (undone/not done); visujjhati (is purified/cleansed); suddhi (purity) + asuddhi (impurity) + paccattam (personal/individual); nanno (no other) + annam (another) + visodhaye (can purify)
dhammapada::5.speaker: Buddha
dhammapada::5.essence: No one can clear your mind for you — only you.
dhammapada::5.simple_meaning: Responsibility for the quality of your mind and life rests entirely with you. You cannot outsource your inner development. What you do — or don't do — shapes you, and no one else can shape you in their place.
dhammapada::5.simple_insight: We are quick to blame circumstances and quick to credit teachers. But this verse insists: the one doing the work and the one receiving the result are the same person, always.
dhammapada::5.detailed_meaning: This verse is the Buddha's clearest statement of radical personal responsibility. It does not mean you are isolated or that community and guidance are irrelevant — it means that even with the best guidance, transformation occurs only through your own sincere effort. The Pali word 'attana' (oneself) appears three times, hammering the point. Importantly, this is not a teaching of blame — it is a teaching of power. If you created your current state, you can uncreate it. The same agency that led to harm can be redirected.
