dheesh_gita::47.simple_insight: Faith allows you to connect with the formless in ways your mind can recognize and hold.
dheesh_gita::47.detailed_meaning: The Divine Teacher explains to the wise seekers that although the true self has no fixed shape, faithful devotees experience it as either a physical form or radiant light, bridging the unseen and the seen.
dheesh_gita::47.modern_relevance: When you can't fully grasp something invisible, your trust creates images or symbols that help you feel connected and real.
dheesh_gita::47.insight: It teaches you to accept that the true self transcends form, yet personal faith personalizes that experience with meaningful images.

dheesh_gita::48.verse_sanskrit:
सानन्दाः कृतकृत्याः स्युर्नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
स्युः प्रपञ्चमयादस्मात् स्थूलाद्वै विषयात्परे ॥
dheesh_gita::48.verse_hindi: आनन्दित और कृतकृत्य होते हैं इसमें विचार की कोई बात नहीं है। इस स्थूलप्रपञ्चमय विषय से परे
dheesh_gita::48.english_translation: Those who are joyful and fulfilled have no need to question this; they have surpassed the gross, worldly realm.
dheesh_gita::48.translation_literal: सानन्दाः (joyful) कृतकृत्याः (fulfilled) स्युः (are) नात्र (here not) कार्या (to be done) विचारणा (questioning) । स्युः (are) प्रपञ्चमयादस्मात् (from this world of illusion) स्थूलात् (gross) वै (indeed) विषयात् (realm) परे (beyond) ॥
dheesh_gita::48.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::48.essence: Joy and fulfillment arise when you move beyond the heavy worldly realm and stop doubting.
dheesh_gita::48.simple_meaning: You feel truly joyful and complete when you stop questioning and move beyond the heavy, material world.
dheesh_gita::48.simple_insight: There is peace in letting go of endless questioning about the gross world.
dheesh_gita::48.detailed_meaning: This verse teaches that those who have transcended the heavy, illusory material world feel joy and completeness without needing to question or doubt.
dheesh_gita::48.modern_relevance: After exhausting yourself worrying about material concerns, you finally feel a calm joy when you stop overthinking and accept what is beyond.
dheesh_gita::48.insight: It teaches you to rest in fulfillment beyond the noisy, unstable material world instead of chasing endless questions.

dheesh_gita::49.verse_sanskrit:
इन्द्रियौघास्ततः सन्ति तन्मात्राण्याखिलानि च ।
तन्मात्रेभ्यः परे पारे वृत्तयश्च भवन्त्यहो ॥
dheesh_gita::49.verse_hindi: इन्द्रियां है, इन्द्रियो से परे सभी तन्मात्राएँ हैं, अहो ! तन्मात्राओं से परे वृत्तियां हैं,
dheesh_gita::49.english_translation: There are the senses, beyond them are the subtle elements, and beyond those are the functions.
dheesh_gita::49.translation_literal: इन्द्रियौघाः (the senses) ततः (then) सन्ति (are) तन्मात्राणि (subtle elements) अखिलानि (all) च (and) । तन्मात्रेभ्यः (from the subtle elements) परे (beyond) पारे (further beyond) वृत्तयः (functions/activities) च (also) भवन्ति (exist) अहो (alas) ॥
dheesh_gita::49.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::49.essence: Your senses reveal only the surface; subtler layers and mental activities lie beyond.
dheesh_gita::49.simple_meaning: Your senses are only the outermost layer; beyond them lie subtler elements and deeper mental functions.
dheesh_gita::49.simple_insight: You realize your direct experience is only a surface layer of reality.
dheesh_gita::49.detailed_meaning: This verse explains a layered view of experience. First come the senses (Indriyas), then the subtle elements beyond them, and beyond those are the mental functions or activities (Vrittis). It points to deeper levels of reality beyond what you immediately perceive.
dheesh_gita::49.modern_relevance: You notice how your immediate senses only catch part of what’s happening, while your feelings and thoughts reveal deeper layers influencing you.
dheesh_gita::49.insight: It shifts your attention from just physical sensation to recognizing subtler influences behind perceptions.

dheesh_gita::50.verse_sanskrit:
ताभ्यः पारं गता भावा भावेभ्योऽपि पर महत् ।
महतोऽपि परं नित्यं कुर्वते दर्शनं मम ॥
dheesh_gita::50.verse_hindi: वृत्तियों से परे भाव है, भाव से भी परे महत् है और महत से परे मेरा दर्शन
dheesh_gita::50.english_translation: Beyond thoughts are feelings, beyond feelings is the great principle, and beyond the great is my vision.
dheesh_gita::50.translation_literal: ताभ्यः (from those) / पारं (beyond) / गता (gone) / भावा (feelings) / भावेभ्यः (from feelings) / अपि (even) / पर (beyond) / महत् (the great principle) / महतोऽपि (even beyond the great) / परं (beyond) / नित्यं (eternal) / कुर्वते (does) / दर्शनं (vision) / मम (my)
dheesh_gita::50.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::50.essence: Your deepest vision transcends thoughts, feelings, and even the great cosmic principle.
dheesh_gita::50.simple_meaning: Your experience goes beyond thoughts and feelings to a greater, eternal vision beyond all mental layers.
dheesh_gita::50.simple_insight: There's a vastness within you that transcends all mental activity and emotional states.
dheesh_gita::50.detailed_meaning: This verse reveals a layered journey inward: from passing thoughts to feelings, then to a greater cosmic principle (mahat), and finally to an even deeper, eternal vision — the speaker points to the ultimate inner reality beyond all mental phenomena.
dheesh_gita::50.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by your swirling thoughts and emotions, remember there is a deeper awareness beyond them all waiting to be seen.
dheesh_gita::50.insight: It teaches you to look past surface experiences toward the eternal vision that underlies them.

dheesh_gita::51.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानिनो योगनिष्णाता भक्ता मे तत्त्वचिन्तकाः।
एतद्रपं परं ज्ञात्वा चिरं शान्तिमवाप्तुत ॥
dheesh_gita::51.verse_hindi: तत्त्वचिन्तक योगनिष्णात मेरे ज्ञानी भक्त नित्य करते हैं। इस परम रूप को जानकर आप लोग चिरकाल तक शान्ति मान कर
dheesh_gita::51.english_translation: My wise devotees, skilled in yoga and devoted seekers of truth, having known this supreme form, attain lasting peace.
dheesh_gita::51.translation_literal: ज्ञानिनो (wise) योगनिष्णाता (skilled in yoga) भक्ता (devotees) मे (my) तत्त्वचिन्तकाः (seekers of truth) । एतद् (this) रपं (form) परं (supreme) ज्ञात्वा (having known) चिरं (long) शान्तिम् (peace) अवाप्तुत् (attain) ॥
dheesh_gita::51.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::51.essence: Knowing the supreme truth with devotion and skill leads to lasting peace.
dheesh_gita::51.simple_meaning: Those who are wise, devoted, and skilled in yoga understand the supreme truth and find lasting peace.
dheesh_gita::51.simple_insight: You can feel calm and steady when you truly grasp the highest reality.
dheesh_gita::51.detailed_meaning: The verse speaks to wise and devoted practitioners who combine knowledge, devotion, and yoga practice. By deeply understanding the supreme form of truth, they achieve enduring inner peace, highlighting the power of integrated spiritual paths.
dheesh_gita::51.modern_relevance: After long searching, you finally grasp a deep truth that quiets your restless mind and fills you with lasting calm.
dheesh_gita::51.insight: It teaches you to integrate wisdom, devotion, and practice to settle the mind permanently.

dheesh_gita::52.verse_sanskrit:
अहमेवास्मि सद्रूपश्चिद्रूपोऽपि महर्षयः !
अहमानन्दरूपोऽस्मि नृनमत्र न संशयः ॥
dheesh_gita::52.verse_hindi: हे महर्षियों ! मैं ही सतरूप हूँ, मैं ही चित रूप भी है और मैं ही आनन्दरूप हूँ इसमें सन्देह नहीं हैं ।
dheesh_gita::52.english_translation: O great sages! I am the true self, the pure consciousness, and the very form of bliss beyond doubt.
dheesh_gita::52.translation_literal: अहमेव (I alone) अस्मि (am) सद्रूप (true form) चिद्रूप (consciousness form) अपि (also) महर्षयः (great sages) अहमानन्दरूपः (I am the bliss form) अस्मि (am) नृनम् (of humans) अत्र (here) न (no) संशयः (doubt)
dheesh_gita::52.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::52.essence: Your true self is pure consciousness and bliss without any doubt.
dheesh_gita::52.simple_meaning: You are the true self who is pure consciousness and the essence of joy without any doubt.
dheesh_gita::52.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your true nature is pure awareness and bliss.
dheesh_gita::52.detailed_meaning: A divine teacher addresses the great sages, affirming that the true self is not only pure consciousness but also the very form of bliss itself, beyond any doubt or confusion.
dheesh_gita::52.modern_relevance: When stress clouds your mind, remember you are more than thoughts—you are pure awareness and innate joy.
dheesh_gita::52.insight: Recognize your identity as pure consciousness and joy rather than your changing thoughts or feelings.

dheesh_gita::53.verse_sanskrit:
विभुश्च निविकारोऽहं निराकारश्च निर्गुणः ।
द्वान्दातीतश्च निर्लिप्तो ज्ञानरूपोऽप्यदं ध्रुवम् ॥
dheesh_gita::53.verse_hindi: मैं विभु, निर्विकार, निर्गुण निराकार, निर्लिप्त,  द्वन्द्वातीत और निश्चय ही ज्ञानस्वरूप हूँ
dheesh_gita::53.english_translation: I am all-pervading, unchanging, formless, beyond qualities, unattached, beyond duality, and the certain form of knowledge.
dheesh_gita::53.translation_literal: विभुश्च (all-pervading) / निविकारोऽहं (unchanging I am) / निराकारश्च (formless also) / निर्गुणः (beyond qualities) / द्वान्दातीतश्च (beyond duality also) / निर्लिप्तो (unattached) / ज्ञानरूपोऽप्यदं (this also the form of knowledge) / ध्रुवम् (certain/unchanging)
dheesh_gita::53.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::53.essence: The true self is the unchanging, formless knowledge beyond all opposites and attachments.
dheesh_gita::53.simple_meaning: You are the all-present, unchanging essence without form or qualities, free from attachment and beyond all opposites, the true form of knowledge.
dheesh_gita::53.simple_insight: Feeling your true self as steady and beyond change brings deep inner peace.
dheesh_gita::53.detailed_meaning: In this verse, Shri Dheesh reveals the nature of the true self as unlimited, beyond physical form and qualities, untouched by duality or attachment, and embodying pure, certain knowledge.
dheesh_gita::53.modern_relevance: When everything around you shifts—opinions, moods, situations—remember that your true self remains steady, formless, and free of attachment.
dheesh_gita::53.insight: It teaches you to recognize your identity beyond changing feelings, roles, and thoughts, as the unchanging knowing presence.

dheesh_gita::54.verse_hindi: हे महर्षि गण ! मेरी मूल प्रकृति स्वरुप अवस्था में मुझमें ही लीन रहकर अद्वैतभाव को अवश्य उत्पन्न करती है।
dheesh_gita::54.english_translation: O great sages, my original nature, in its true state, remains absorbed in me and surely manifests the non-dual reality.
dheesh_gita::54.translation_literal: स्वरूपावास्थितौ (in true nature's state) / मूल-प्रकृतिमें (in original nature) / महर्षयः (great sages) / मल्लीना (absorbed) / भावम (state) / अद्वैतम् (non-duality) / आविर्भावयति (manifests) / अन्यम् (other)
dheesh_gita::54.speaker: Shri Dhish
dheesh_gita::54.essence: Your original nature is fully absorbed and naturally reveals the unity beyond division.
dheesh_gita::54.simple_meaning: Your original nature stays fully absorbed within itself and reveals the non-dual reality beyond apparent differences.
dheesh_gita::54.simple_insight: There is a profound calm in knowing your true nature is always unified and whole beyond appearances.
dheesh_gita::54.detailed_meaning: The speaker addresses great sages, explaining that the original nature remains fully absorbed in its own true state, from which the non-dual nature of reality naturally arises, pointing to the underlying oneness beyond all duality.
dheesh_gita::54.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by conflicting thoughts or roles, remember your true self is always quietly whole and undivided beneath the noise.
dheesh_gita::54.insight: This verse shifts your view from fragmented identity to seeing the self as an indivisible whole beneath all appearances.

dheesh_gita::55.verse_sanskrit:
सा व्युत्थानदशायान्तु स्तं रूपं त्रिगुणात्मकम् ।
धृत्वा दृश्य प्रपञ्भस्य सृष्टिस्थितिलयक्रियाः ॥
dheesh_gita::55.verse_hindi: किन्तु हे विप्रो ! यह व्युत्थान दशा में अपने त्रिगुणात्मक रूप को धारण करके दृश्य प्रपंञ्च की सृष्टि, स्थिति, और लयक्रिया को
dheesh_gita::55.english_translation: But, O wise one, in the state of dissolution, it takes on its three-gunic form, sustaining the visible world’s creation, maintenance, and dissolution.
dheesh_gita::55.translation_literal: सा (that) / व्युत्थानदशायान्तु (in the state of dissolution indeed) / स्तं (its) / रूपं (form) / त्रिगुणात्मकम् (of three qualities) / धृत्वा (holding) / दृश्य (visible) / प्रपञ्भस्य (of the manifested world) / सृष्टिस्थितिलयक्रियाः (creation, maintenance, and dissolution activities)
dheesh_gita::55.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::55.essence: The visible world cycles through creation, maintenance, and destruction under three fundamental qualities.
dheesh_gita::55.simple_meaning: In the state of dissolution, the natural world holds its three fundamental qualities and carries out the processes of creation, maintenance, and destruction.
dheesh_gita::55.simple_insight: Everything visible undergoes cycles of birth, existence, and end, driven by changing qualities.
dheesh_gita::55.detailed_meaning: The verse describes the natural world during its dissolution phase, showing how it still embodies the three fundamental qualities (gunas) and continues the cosmic processes of creation, sustenance, and destruction, forming the backdrop for deeper philosophical inquiry.
dheesh_gita::55.insight: It reveals that change and transformation are continuous cycles governed by underlying qualities, not random events.

dheesh_gita::56.verse_sanskrit:
कुर्वाणाऽऽस्ते सदा विप्राः ! मदाज्ञायशवर्तिनी।
मत्मक्रित्याश्च भो विप्रा: ! तमस्सत्वरजोगुणाः ॥
dheesh_gita::56.verse_hindi: मेरी आज्ञा के वशवर्तिनी होकर सदा करती रहती है। हे ब्राह्मणों ! मेरी प्रकृतिक सत्व रज तम यह तीनों गुण
dheesh_gita::56.english_translation: O Brahmins, you always act under my command. You are the forces of nature — sattva, rajas, and tamas.
dheesh_gita::56.translation_literal: कुर्वाणा (doing) अस्ते (always) सदा (constantly) विप्राः (Brahmins) ! मदाज्ञाय (under my command) शवर्तिनी (acting). मत्मक्रित्याश्च (also by my will) भो (O) विप्रा: (Brahmins) ! तमस्सत्वरजोगुणाः (the qualities tamas, sattva, rajas).
dheesh_gita::56.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::56.essence: Your actions always flow from the divine command through nature's three qualities.
dheesh_gita::56.simple_meaning: You always act by following the divine command, shaped by the three qualities of nature: sattva, rajas, and tamas.
dheesh_gita::56.simple_insight: You can feel connected knowing your actions arise naturally from deeper forces beyond yourself.
dheesh_gita::56.detailed_meaning: The speaker addresses the Brahmins, explaining that their actions are not random but always occur under the divine's command, shaped by the three fundamental qualities of nature: sattva (harmony), rajas (activity), and tamas (inertia). This verse reveals that even disciplined acting is supported by natural forces.
dheesh_gita::56.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by choices, know that your actions are influenced by deeper qualities within you, guiding your behavior naturally.
dheesh_gita::56.insight: This verse shifts your view from seeing actions as isolated choices to understanding them as expressions of underlying natural qualities.

dheesh_gita::57.verse_hindi: मेरे सञ्चिदानन्दमय त्रिभावों से जाने जाते हैं। अहो ! मैं ही अध्यात्म अधिदेव और अधिभूत इन तीनों भावों से ही प्रकट होकर
dheesh_gita::57.english_translation: My true self is known by three states: spiritual, divine, and material nature; I manifest through these three aspects.
dheesh_gita::57.translation_literal: ज्ञायन् (knowing) ए (my) सच्चिदानन्दरूपैः (of true consciousness-bliss form) त्रिभिः (by three) मम (my) नव (new) अध्यात्म (spiritual) अधिदैव (divine) अधिभूत (material) भावैः (states) अहो (ah!) त्रिभिः (by three).
dheesh_gita::57.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::57.essence: The true self reveals itself through spiritual, divine, and natural states simultaneously.
dheesh_gita::57.simple_meaning: You are the true self recognized through three states: spiritual, divine, and natural. You show yourself through all these aspects together.
dheesh_gita::57.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing you appear in many forms but remain one true self.
dheesh_gita::57.detailed_meaning: The speaker reveals that the true self is known through three states: spiritual nature (adhyatma), divine nature (adhidaiva), and material nature (adhibhuta). This verse explains how the self expresses through these distinct yet intertwined aspects.
dheesh_gita::57.modern_relevance: When you feel pulled between your thoughts, feelings, and surroundings, remember they are all parts of your true self expressing differently.
dheesh_gita::57.insight: Recognize the threefold nature of your experience as unified expressions of your true self, dissolving inner division.

dheesh_gita::58.verse_sanskrit:
आविर्भयात्मभक्तेभ्यो ज्ञानिभ्यः सत्वरं ध्रुवम ।
अहमेव प्रयच्छामि तत्त्वज्ञान न संशयः ॥
dheesh_gita::58.verse_hindi: अपने ज्ञानी भक्तों को निश्चय ही शीघ्र सत्वज्ञान प्रदान करता हूँ इसमें सन्देह नहीं
dheesh_gita::58.english_translation: I certainly grant the knowledge of truth quickly to devoted seekers and wise ones; there is no doubt about this.
dheesh_gita::58.translation_literal: आविर्भयात्मभक्तेभ्यो (to devoted seekers) / ज्ञानिभ्यः (to wise ones) / सत्वरं (quickly) / ध्रुवम (certainly) / अहमेव (I alone) / प्रयच्छामि (grant) / तत्त्वज्ञान (knowledge of truth) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
dheesh_gita::58.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::58.essence: Devoted and wise seekers are swiftly granted clear knowledge without doubt.
dheesh_gita::58.simple_meaning: If you seek truth with devotion and wisdom, you will be granted clear understanding swiftly and without doubt.
dheesh_gita::58.simple_insight: There’s comfort in knowing true seeking leads to certain and swift insight.
dheesh_gita::58.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the teacher promises that anyone who approaches with both devoted love and clear wisdom will be swiftly granted the knowledge of reality’s essence, removing all uncertainty.
dheesh_gita::58.modern_relevance: When you genuinely commit your heart and mind to learning, answers often arrive sooner than expected.
dheesh_gita::58.insight: It encourages combining heartfelt devotion with clear thinking to receive knowledge quickly and confidently.

dheesh_gita::59.verse_sanskrit:
तदा मे ज्ञानिनो भक्ता भावत्रय्याश्रयादध्रुवम् ।
अघट्यघटनायां या प्रकृति, पटीयसी ॥
dheesh_gita::59.verse_hindi: तब मेरे ज्ञानी भक्त त्रिभाव की सहायता से ही मेरी त्रिगुणमयी प्रकृति का
dheesh_gita::59.english_translation: Then my wise devotees, relying on the threefold attitude, firmly master my three-guṇa nature, unaffected by events.
dheesh_gita::59.translation_literal: तदा (then) मे (my) ज्ञानिनः (wise devotees) भक्ता (devoted) भावत्रय्या (threefold attitude) आश्रयात् (by reliance) अध्रुवम् (unshaken) । अघट्य (not affected) अघटना (by events) या (which) प्रकृति (nature), पटीयसी (master).
dheesh_gita::59.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::59.essence: Steadfast devotion rooted in threefold attitude overcomes nature’s shifting influence.
dheesh_gita::59.simple_meaning: You can stay steady and unshaken through life’s changes by relying on devoted love expressed in three attitudes.
dheesh_gita::59.simple_insight: Feeling steady and safe comes from trusting your devotion, not from controlling what happens.
dheesh_gita::59.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the teacher explains how wise devotees who base themselves on three devoted attitudes can master the three qualities in nature without being disturbed by external events.
dheesh_gita::59.modern_relevance: When life tosses you between ups and downs, your sincere devotion can anchor you firmly beyond all fluctuations.
dheesh_gita::59.insight: It teaches you to rely on heartfelt devotion to remain unshaken by external changes or outcomes.

dheesh_gita::60.verse_sanskrit:
तस्यास्त्रैगुण्यमय्या हि कृत्वा तात्त्विकदर्शनम् ।
मामकीनां लभन्तेऽन्ते मुक्ति सायुज्यनामिकाम् ॥
dheesh_gita::60.verse_hindi: यथार्थ रूप में दर्शन करके अन्त मेरी सायुज्य मुक्ति को प्राप्त होते हैं
dheesh_gita::60.english_translation: By realizing the true nature through that threefold mode, my followers ultimately attain liberation called union with me.
dheesh_gita::60.translation_literal: तस्यास्त्रैगुण्यमय्या (by that threefold mode) हि (indeed) कृत्वा (having done) तात्त्विकदर्शनम् (true nature vision) मामकीनां (of my followers) लभन्ते (attain) अन्ते (at the end) मुक्ति (liberation) सायुज्यनामिकाम् (called union with me)
dheesh_gita::60.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::60.essence: Complete true seeing through all qualities leads to final union and freedom.
dheesh_gita::60.simple_meaning: Fully understanding the true nature through all its qualities leads followers to ultimate freedom called union.
dheesh_gita::60.simple_insight: There is hope in knowing clear understanding leads to lasting union beyond this life.
dheesh_gita::60.detailed_meaning: After teaching about the three qualities (gunas) and true nature, the speaker explains that those who truly see this reach a final state of freedom called union with the teacher, marking the culmination of the spiritual path.
dheesh_gita::60.modern_relevance: After years of searching through life's ups and downs, you finally glimpse your true self, feeling a deep freedom arise inside.
dheesh_gita::60.insight: It shifts focus from partial knowledge to full realization as the key to lasting inner freedom.

dheesh_gita::61.verse_hindi: मेरे स्वरूप ज्ञान की प्राप्तिके लिये सब प्रकारसे उत्तम त्रिभावात्मक अद्भुत तटस्थ ज्ञान ही श्रेष्ठ उपाय है
dheesh_gita::61.english_translation: For realizing my true nature, the supreme method is the wondrous, detached knowledge involving three attitudes.
dheesh_gita::61.translation_literal: त्रिभावात्मकमेवास्ति (involving three attitudes only) / तटस्थज्ञानमद्भुतम् (detached knowledge wondrous) / मत्स्वरूपावबोधाय (for my true nature realization) / सूपायः (method) / सर्ववोत्तमः (best of all)
dheesh_gita::61.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::61.essence: Realizing your true nature requires a detached knowledge embracing three complementary attitudes.
dheesh_gita::61.simple_meaning: To understand your true self, the best way is to use a special kind of knowledge that is detached and looks at things from three different attitudes.
dheesh_gita::61.simple_insight: You can approach knowing yourself deeply by stepping back and seeing from multiple views without getting caught up.
dheesh_gita::61.detailed_meaning: Shri Dheesh teaches that to recognize the true self, one must adopt a unique, detached knowledge that embraces three perspectives. This method is the highest way to clear confusion and see reality beyond appearances.
dheesh_gita::61.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by conflicting thoughts and feelings, stepping back with calm, varied perspectives helps you see who you really are.
dheesh_gita::61.insight: It teaches shifting from a single biased view to a spacious, detached awareness that holds multiple attitudes simultaneously.

dheesh_gita::62.verse_sanskrit:
मत्कारणदशायां वै सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणः
त्रिभावा अवतिष्ठन्तेऽद्वैतरूपे न संशयः ॥
dheesh_gita::62.verse_hindi: मेरी कारणदशा में सत् चित् और आनन्दरूप तीनों भाव निस्सन्देह अद्वैतरूप में ही रहते हैं
dheesh_gita::62.english_translation: In my causal state, the forms of existence, consciousness, and bliss surely dwell as the non-dual reality.
dheesh_gita::62.translation_literal: मत्कारणदशायां (in my causal state) / वै (indeed) / सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणः (forms of existence, consciousness, and bliss) / त्रिभावा (three states/forms) / अवतिष्ठन्ते (dwell) / अद्वैतरूपे (in non-dual form) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
dheesh_gita::62.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::62.essence: Existence, consciousness, and bliss exist inseparably as one non-dual reality within you.
dheesh_gita::62.simple_meaning: Existence, consciousness, and bliss are not separate but united in the deepest reality of the true self.
dheesh_gita::62.simple_insight: You can feel the peace that comes from knowing all is one inside you.
dheesh_gita::62.detailed_meaning: The verse describes the deepest state of the true self, called the causal state, where the three essential qualities—existence, consciousness, and bliss—are inseparable and appear as one non-dual reality, revealing the essence of Advaita philosophy.
dheesh_gita::62.modern_relevance: In moments of deep calm or meditation, you might glimpse that your sense of separate self dissolves into simple being, pure awareness, and joy as one.
dheesh_gita::62.insight: It shifts your view from seeing parts to recognizing a seamless unity in your experience of self.

dheesh_gita::63.verse_sanskrit:
नन्नध्यात्माधिदैवाधिभूतभावस्त्रिभिध्रुवम् ।
प्रकृतेर्मे प्रजातस्य कार्यब्रह्मण एव हि ॥
dheesh_gita::63.verse_hindi: मैं ही अध्यात्म अधिदैव और अधिभूतरूपी तीनों मेरी ही प्रकृति से उत्पन्न
dheesh_gita::63.english_translation: I am the unchanging reality behind the self, the divine, and the material nature; the cause of all beings is the creative power within me.
dheesh_gita::63.translation_literal: नन (not) / अध्यात्म (self-related) / अधिदैव (higher-divine) / अधिभूत (higher-material) / भाव (states/essences) / त्रिभि (threefold) / ध्रुवम् (unchanging) । प्रकृतेः (of nature) / मे (my) / प्रजातस्य (of beings) / कार्य (cause) / ब्रह्मण (creative power) / एव (indeed) / हि (certainly) ॥
dheesh_gita::63.speaker: Shambhu Dheesh
dheesh_gita::63.essence: One unchanging reality underlies self, divine, and nature as their true source.
dheesh_gita::63.simple_meaning: There is one unchanging reality underlying the self, the divine, and the material world; all beings arise from this creative power.
dheesh_gita::63.simple_insight: You are connected to a single unchanging source beyond everything you see or feel.
dheesh_gita::63.detailed_meaning: The teacher reveals that the self (adhyatma), the divine (adhidaiva), and the material world (adhibhuta) are all expressions of one unchanging reality. This creative power is the cause of all beings and arises from the teacher's own nature.
dheesh_gita::63.modern_relevance: When you feel fragmented by your thoughts, emotions, or surroundings, remember they all come from one steady source within you.
dheesh_gita::63.insight: Recognize the unity behind apparent diversity, shifting your view from separation to oneness.

dheesh_gita::64.verse_sanskrit:
अङ्गोपाङ्गानि सर्वाणि व्याप्नुवन्नु पृथक् पृथक्।
विश्व प्रकाशये सर्वमहं वैचित्र्यसङ्कुलम् ॥
dheesh_gita::64.verse_hindi: कार्यब्रह्म के सभी अंगो उपांगों में पृथक पृथक् भावों से अवश्य ही व्यापक रहकर नाना वैचित्र्य पूर्ण सम्पूर्ण जगत को प्रकाशित करता हूँ
dheesh_gita::64.english_translation: I pervade all the limbs and parts individually, illuminating the entire world with diverse manifestations.
dheesh_gita::64.translation_literal: अङ्गोपाङ्गानि (limbs and parts) / सर्वाणि (all) / व्याप्नुवन् (pervading) / पृथक् (separately) / पृथक् (separately) / विश्व (world) / प्रकाशये (illuminating) / सर्व (all) / अहम (I) / वैचित्र्यसङ्कुलम् (full of diversity)
dheesh_gita::64.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::64.essence: One presence fills all parts, shining through all diverse forms.
dheesh_gita::64.simple_meaning: The presence is spread throughout every part separately, shining through all the world's diverse forms.
dheesh_gita::64.simple_insight: Presence is everywhere, distinct yet united in illuminating diversity.
dheesh_gita::64.detailed_meaning: A divine presence explains how it fills and shines through every limb and part distinctly, reflecting the world's full variety and complexity.
dheesh_gita::64.insight: It reveals how the true self manifests uniquely everywhere while remaining one presence.

dheesh_gita::65.verse_sanskrit:
स्थानं तन्नास्ति विश्वास्मिन् व्याप्तं यन्न विभावतः।
यदब्रह्मेविराडरूपैः पश्यन्तो ज्ञानिनो हि माम् ॥
dheesh_gita::65.verse_hindi: इस जगत में ऐसा स्थान नहीं है जो त्रिभाव से व्याप्त न हो, मेरे ज्ञानी भक्त जो ब्रह्म ईश और विराट रूप में मेरा दर्शन
dheesh_gita::65.english_translation: There is no place in this world untouched by the threefold nature; my wise devotees perceive me as Brahman, the supreme being, and as the cosmic form.
dheesh_gita::65.translation_literal: स्थानं (place) तन्नास्ति (there is not) विश्वास्मिन् (in this world) व्याप्तं (pervaded) यन्न (which) विभावतः (by the threefold nature) यदब्रह्मेव (that Brahman alone) इरा (supreme being) अडरूपैः (cosmic forms) पश्यन्तो (seeing) ज्ञानिनः (the wise ones) हि (indeed) माम् (me)
dheesh_gita::65.speaker: Shri Deesh
dheesh_gita::65.essence: The divine fully pervades all places and appears as both supreme being and cosmic form.
dheesh_gita::65.simple_meaning: Every part of the universe is filled with the divine presence, and those who understand this see the divine both as the supreme being and as the cosmic form.
dheesh_gita::65.simple_insight: Feeling that you are never truly alone because the divine is everywhere around you.
dheesh_gita::65.detailed_meaning: The speaker explains to seekers that the world is completely filled with the divine’s presence. The wise perceive the divine not just as an abstract supreme being but also in its cosmic, all-encompassing form. This insight helps deepen devotion and connection.
dheesh_gita::65.modern_relevance: When you feel isolated, remember that everything around you is connected through the divine presence, seen or unseen.
dheesh_gita::65.insight: It encourages you to recognize the divine in all places and forms, strengthening your sense of unity and devotion.

dheesh_gita::66.verse_sanskrit:
उन्मजन्ति निमजनन्ति भक्ता मे भक्तिसागरे ।
तत्रापि कारणं वित्त नित्यभावत्रयं खलु ॥
dheesh_gita::66.verse_hindi: भक्ति सागर में उन्मजन और निमजन करते हैं यहां भी नित्य भाव त्रय को ही कारण जानो
dheesh_gita::66.english_translation: In the ocean of devotion, some immerse themselves deeply while others dive shallowly; even there, the reason is always the three constant states.
dheesh_gita::66.translation_literal: उन्मजन्ति (immerse deeply) / निमजनन्ति (immerse shallowly) / भक्ता (devotees) / मे (my) / भक्तिसागरे (in the ocean of devotion) / तत्रापि (even there) / कारणं (the reason) / वित्त (cause/factor) / नित्यभावत्रयं (three constant states) / खलु (indeed)
dheesh_gita::66.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::66.essence: The depth of your devotion depends on three steady inner states shaping your experience.
dheesh_gita::66.simple_meaning: Devotees in the ocean of devotion dive deeply or shallowly, but the true cause is always three constant inner states.
dheesh_gita::66.simple_insight: How deeply you connect in devotion reflects steady feelings within you.
dheesh_gita::66.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the teacher explains that in devotion, different people connect at different depths—some fully immerse, others only partially. Yet, the reason for their experience lies in three fundamental, steady inner states that shape the quality of their devotion.
dheesh_gita::66.modern_relevance: When you feel close or distant in your heartfelt commitments, it often depends on consistent feelings inside you that shape your connection.
dheesh_gita::66.insight: Recognize that lasting devotion arises from steady emotional states, not just external acts.

dheesh_gita::67.verse_sanskrit:
यत्तद्ब्रह्म मनोवाचामगोचरमितीरितम् ।
तत सर्वकारणं वित्त साध्यात्मिकमित्यपि ॥
dheesh_gita::67.verse_hindi: जो मन और वाणी के अगोचर कहे गये हैं वह ब्रह्म हैं उनको सबका कारण और सबका अध्यात्म जानो॥
dheesh_gita::67.english_translation: That which is beyond the reach of mind and speech is Brahman; know it as the cause of all and the essence of spirituality.
dheesh_gita::67.translation_literal: यत्तद्ब्रह्म (That which is Brahman) / मनोवाचामगोचरमितीरितम् (beyond mind and speech) / तत (that) / सर्वकारणं (cause of all) / वित्त (essence) / साध्यात्मिकमित्यपि (also called spiritual essence)
dheesh_gita::67.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::67.essence: The deepest reality is beyond mind and speech yet causes all that exists.
dheesh_gita::67.simple_meaning: The supreme reality is beyond what your mind can grasp or your words can express. It is the cause behind everything and the core of spiritual truth.
dheesh_gita::67.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing the deepest reality is beyond your restless mind and words.
dheesh_gita::67.detailed_meaning: Suta explains that Brahman, the supreme reality, transcends the limits of mind and speech. Though unseen and unspeakable, it is the ultimate cause and essence behind all existence, inviting the seeker to realize this profound truth.
dheesh_gita::67.modern_relevance: When language and thoughts fail to capture your deepest experiences, you glimpse something greater that underlies everything you face.
dheesh_gita::67.insight: It shifts your focus from trying to grasp with mind or words to acknowledging a reality beyond conceptual limits.

dheesh_gita::68.verse_sanskrit:
अनाद्यन्तमनं दिव्यमजरं ध्रुवमव्ययम् ।
अप्रतय॑मविक्षेयं ब्रह्माग्रे समवर्तते ॥
dheesh_gita::68.verse_hindi: अनादि, अनन्त, अजन्मा, दिव्य, अजर, अमर, नाशरहित, अनूह्य और अज्ञेय ब्रह्म प्रथम है
dheesh_gita::68.english_translation: The supreme reality is without beginning or end, infinite, unborn, divine, imperishable, eternal, indestructible, untraceable, and beyond all understanding.
dheesh_gita::68.translation_literal: अनाद्यन्तमनं (without beginning or end) / दिव्यमजरं (divine and imperishable) / ध्रुवमव्ययम् (constant and indestructible) / अप्रतय॑मविक्षेयं (untraceable and beyond examination) / ब्रह्माग्रे (at the beginning is Brahman) / समवर्तते (is established)
dheesh_gita::68.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::68.essence: The supreme reality is infinite, eternal, and beyond all comprehension or decay.
dheesh_gita::68.simple_meaning: The supreme reality is infinite, eternal, without beginning or end, and cannot be fully understood or destroyed.
dheesh_gita::68.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing the true self is timeless and beyond all change.
dheesh_gita::68.detailed_meaning: This verse describes the supreme reality as limitless and eternal. It is beyond birth, death, and decay, existing before everything else and beyond any human understanding. It establishes the foundation for the spiritual teaching that follows.
dheesh_gita::68.modern_relevance: When life feels chaotic and everything changes, remembering the timeless and unchanging source within offers deep calm and stability.
dheesh_gita::68.insight: It shifts your perspective from fleeting events to the eternal presence beneath all change.

dheesh_gita::69.verse_sanskrit:
स्वेच्छया मायया यत्तजगजन्मादिकारणम् ।
ईश्वराख्यं तु तत्तत्वमधिदैवमिति स्मृतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::69.verse_hindi: अपनी इच्छारूपिणी माया से जो जगत की सृष्टि स्थिति और लय के कारण हैं ईश्वर हैं। वह ईश्वर तत्त्व अधिदेव कहलाते हैं
dheesh_gita::69.english_translation: The supreme being called Ishvara is the principle behind creation, sustenance, and dissolution, arising from the divine power called maya.
dheesh_gita::69.translation_literal: स्वेच्छया (by own will) / मायया (by maya) / यत् (that which) / जगत् (world) / जन्मादि (birth and so on) / कारणम् (cause) / ईश्वराख्यम् (called Ishvara) / तु (but) / तत् (that) / तत्त्वम् (principle) / अधिदैवम् (supreme divine) / इति (thus) / स्मृतम् (is remembered)
dheesh_gita::69.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::69.essence: A supreme willful power called Ishvara governs all creation, preservation, and dissolution.
dheesh_gita::69.simple_meaning: The world’s birth, existence, and end arise from a divine power called maya, which is governed by the supreme being Ishvara.
dheesh_gita::69.simple_insight: There is a higher organizing force shaping everything, beyond random chance or chaos.
dheesh_gita::69.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the narrator explains that the entire cycle of the world—its creation, maintenance, and destruction—comes from a divine power called maya. This power acts with its own will and is recognized as Ishvara, the supreme principle controlling cosmic functions.
dheesh_gita::69.modern_relevance: When life feels unpredictable or chaotic, recognizing a greater organizing force can bring calm and trust in the natural flow.
dheesh_gita::69.insight: This teaches you to see the universe as a purposeful whole, not fragmented random events.

dheesh_gita::70.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वज्ञः सदगुरुनित्यो ह्यांतर्यामी कृपानिधिः ।
सर्वसद्गुणसारात्मा दोषशन्यः परः पुमान ॥
dheesh_gita::70.verse_hindi: सर्वज्ञ, सद्गुरु, नित्य, अन्तर्यामी, कृपासागर, सब सद्गुणों के साररूप, दोषशून्य पुरूषोत्तम है
dheesh_gita::70.english_translation: The supreme being is all-knowing, the eternal true teacher, the inner witness, an ocean of compassion, the essence of all virtues, free from faults.
dheesh_gita::70.translation_literal: सर्वज्ञः (all-knowing) / सदगुरुनित्यो (eternal true teacher) / ह्यांतर्यामी (indeed inner witness) / कृपानिधिः (ocean of compassion) / सर्वसद्गुणसारात्मा (essence of all good qualities) / दोषशन्यः (free from faults) / परः (supreme) / पुमान (being)
dheesh_gita::70.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::70.essence: The supreme being is the flawless, compassionate, eternal inner teacher.
dheesh_gita::70.simple_meaning: The supreme being is all-knowing, always present within, full of compassion, the source of all good qualities, and completely free from faults.
dheesh_gita::70.simple_insight: You can trust in a presence that is perfectly wise, compassionate, and faultless.
dheesh_gita::70.detailed_meaning: This verse describes the supreme being as the all-knowing, eternal teacher who dwells inside all beings. It highlights the divine as full of compassion, embodying all virtues and without any faults, establishing the highest ideal.
dheesh_gita::70.modern_relevance: When everything feels uncertain, you can remember a perfect inner presence that knows all, cares deeply, and is completely without flaw.
dheesh_gita::70.insight: It invites you to recognize an unchanging, compassionate presence within that guides and supports without error.

dheesh_gita::71.verse_sanskrit:
यत्कार्यव्रह्म विश्वस्य निधानं प्राकृतात्मकम् ।
विराडाख्यं स्थूलतरमधिभूतं तदुच्यते ॥
dheesh_gita::71.verse_hindi: और जो विश्व के निधान, प्राकृतात्मक, स्थूलतर और विराटरूप कार्य्यब्रहम हैं, वह अधिभूत कहे जाते हैं।
dheesh_gita::71.english_translation: The cause called the highest matter or primal nature, the support and foundation of the entire universe, is known as the 'Adhibhuta'.
dheesh_gita::71.translation_literal: यत्कार्यव्रह्म (that cause of effect and reality) / विश्वस्य (of the universe) / निधानं (the foundation/treasure) / प्राकृतात्मकम् (primal nature) / विराडाख्यं (called vast or cosmic) / स्थूलतरम् (more gross) / अधिभूतं (the highest matter) / तदुच्यते (is said)
dheesh_gita::71.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::71.essence: All visible reality arises from a fundamental primal matter called Adhibhuta.
dheesh_gita::71.simple_meaning: The universe is supported by a primal, physical cause called the 'Adhibhuta', which is the foundation of all matter and forms the natural world.
dheesh_gita::71.simple_insight: You can feel grounded knowing all visible things arise from a common primal source.
dheesh_gita::71.detailed_meaning: In a teaching moment, the verse explains that the cosmic universe rests on a primal, physical foundation known as Adhibhuta. This is the material cause behind all visible things, representing the natural world’s fundamental essence.
dheesh_gita::71.modern_relevance: When you look around, everything you touch or see shares a common material origin, reminding you of the unity behind diversity.
dheesh_gita::71.insight: It shifts your view from seeing things as separate to recognizing the natural world’s unity as one primal source.

dheesh_gita::72.verse_hindi: अध्यात्म अधिदैव और अधिभूतरूप भावत्रय सम्बन्धी उत्तम तत्त्व फिर मैं आपलोगों से ही कहता हूँ सुनो
dheesh_gita::72.english_translation: Again I will explain the supreme truth related to the threefold nature of the self, the divine, and the natural world; listen carefully.
dheesh_gita::72.translation_literal: पुनः (again) वः (to you all) सम्प्रवक्ष्येऽहम् (I will explain) श्रूयताम् (listen) तत्त्वम् (truth) उत्तमम् (supreme) नन्व (indeed) अध्यात्म (self) अधिदैव (divine) अधिभूत (natural world) भावत्रय (threefold nature) अनुरगम् (related)
dheesh_gita::72.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::72.essence: A supreme truth connects self, divine, and natural world as a threefold reality.
dheesh_gita::72.simple_meaning: I will now explain the supreme truth about the threefold nature of self, the divine, and the natural world. Listen carefully.
dheesh_gita::72.simple_insight: There is a deeper, interconnected truth about self, divine, and nature worth understanding.
dheesh_gita::72.detailed_meaning: The speaker prepares the listeners for a profound teaching about the threefold aspects of existence: self, divine presence, and natural reality. This sets the stage for deeper inquiry into fundamental principles.
dheesh_gita::72.insight: It opens your mind to seeing self, divine, and nature as interconnected realms to explore.

dheesh_gita::73.verse_sanskrit:
यथाध्यात्माधिदैवधिभूतभावत्रयं द्विजाः ।
विद्यते कारणे नूनं कार्येष्वपि तथैव तत् ॥
dheesh_gita::73.verse_hindi: हे ब्राह्मणो ! अध्यात्म अधिदेव और अधिभूत ये तीनों भाव जिस प्रकार कारण में हैं उसी प्रकार वह कार्य में भी अवश्य हैं
dheesh_gita::73.english_translation: O Brahmins, just as the three aspects—spiritual, divine, and material—exist in the cause, they also exist in the effect.
dheesh_gita::73.translation_literal: यथा (just as) अध्यात्म (spiritual) अधि (beyond) देवा (divine) अधिभूत (material) भाव (aspects) त्रयम् (three) द्विजाः (Brahmins) विद्यते (exists) कारणे (in the cause) नूनम् (certainly) कार्येषु (in the effect) अपि (also) तथैव (in the same way) तत् (that)
dheesh_gita::73.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::73.essence: The threefold reality within the cause also pervades the effect without exception.
dheesh_gita::73.simple_meaning: The three aspects—spiritual, divine, and material—are present both in the origin and in what results from it.
dheesh_gita::73.simple_insight: Understanding that what causes something and what results from it share the same fundamental qualities brings clarity.
dheesh_gita::73.detailed_meaning: In this teaching addressed to the Brahmins, the speaker explains that the three fundamental aspects—spiritual, divine, and material—are not only present in the source but also permeate the results or effects, emphasizing the unity behind change.
dheesh_gita::73.modern_relevance: When you create or start something, remember its essence remains present in the outcome, connecting beginning and end deeply.
dheesh_gita::73.insight: It shifts your view to see cause and effect as inseparable, sharing the same essential nature.

dheesh_gita::74.verse_sanskrit:
विस्तरात्सम्प्रवक्ष्येऽहं तत्स्वरूपं निशम्यताम् ।
अहमेव स्वकीयां तां महामायामुपाश्रितः ॥
dheesh_gita::74.verse_hindi: उनका विस्तार से स्वरूप मैं कहता हूँ सुनो। हे महर्षियों! मैं ही अपनी उन महामाया का आश्रय करके
dheesh_gita::74.english_translation: I will now explain their true nature in detail. Hear this, great sages: I take refuge in that great illusion myself.
dheesh_gita::74.translation_literal: विस्तरात्सम्प्रवक्ष्येऽहं (in detail I will explain) / तत्स्वरूपं (that nature) / निशम्यताम् (listen) / अहमेव (I myself) / स्वकीयां (my own) / तां (that) / महामायाम् (great illusion) / उपाश्रितः (having taken refuge)
dheesh_gita::74.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::74.essence: The true self exists while residing within and depending on the great illusion.
dheesh_gita::74.simple_meaning: The speaker declares they will explain the true nature of things and reveals that they themselves depend on the great illusion shaping the world.
dheesh_gita::74.simple_insight: Even the teacher acknowledges the power of the great illusion surrounding all things.
dheesh_gita::74.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the teacher addresses the sages, preparing to reveal the deep true nature behind appearances. He admits that he himself rests in the great illusion (Maya) that shapes the manifest world, setting the stage for profound insight.
dheesh_gita::74.modern_relevance: When you take a moment to question what you truly are, you realize even your deepest beliefs rest on appearances and assumptions.
dheesh_gita::74.insight: It invites recognizing that the true self engages with illusion, prompting deeper inquiry beyond surface reality.

dheesh_gita::75.verse_hindi: सर्वदा अध्यात्मभाव से ऋषि, अधिदैव भाव से देवता और
dheesh_gita::75.english_translation: The sage always appears as the highest seer through spiritual presence, and as a deity through transcendent essence.
dheesh_gita::75.translation_literal: विभ्राणः (appearing) अध्यात्मभावेन (by spiritual feeling) ऋषि-रूपं (sage form) सदोत्तमम् (best eternal) । तथाऽधिदैवभावेन (and by transcendent divine feeling) देवता-रूपम् (deity form) आदधत् (assumed) ॥
dheesh_gita::75.speaker: Narrator
dheesh_gita::75.essence: One being can show spiritual insight and transcendent presence simultaneously.
dheesh_gita::75.simple_meaning: A person can appear as a great seer by their spiritual nature and as a divine being by their transcendent qualities.
dheesh_gita::75.simple_insight: A single person can embody both deep insight and transcendent presence at once.
dheesh_gita::75.detailed_meaning: This verse describes how a figure can manifest two aspects: the inner seer (the sage) through spiritual awareness, and the divine form through a higher transcendent state. It explains a dual nature of perception and presence.
dheesh_gita::75.insight: It invites seeing that people or teachers can have multiple layers — inner wisdom and elevated presence — beyond the surface.

dheesh_gita::76.verse_hindi: अधिभूत भाव से पितृरूप उत्तमता से धारण करके अनेक ब्रह्माण्ड समूह का संरक्षण करता हूँ
dheesh_gita::76.english_translation: I, the great sage, embody the supreme form of the ancestors through the constitutive nature and protect countless clusters of universes.
dheesh_gita::76.translation_literal: तथाधिभूतभावेन (through the constitutive nature) / पितृरूपमधिश्रयन् (resting in the form of ancestors) / नानाब्रह्माण्डसंघातं (countless clusters of universes) / संरक्षामि (I protect) / महार्षयः (the great sage)
dheesh_gita::76.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::76.essence: A supreme ancestral form sustains and protects countless universes through cosmic nature.
dheesh_gita::76.simple_meaning: The speaker claims to embody a supreme ancestral form and protect countless universes through a fundamental cosmic nature.
dheesh_gita::76.simple_insight: There is a vast protective presence behind all creation, beyond individual identity.
dheesh_gita::76.detailed_meaning: The great sage declares his cosmic role as the protector of many universes, embodying a supreme ancestral aspect through the foundational nature of reality, expressing his vast cosmic authority in this moment.
dheesh_gita::76.insight: Recognize the vast interconnectedness and protection operating beyond what you can see or control.

dheesh_gita::77.verse_sanskrit:
आकाशं प्रथमं भूतं श्रोत्रमध्यात्ममुच्यते !
आधिभूतं तथा शब्दो दिशस्तनाधिदैवतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::77.verse_hindi: पञ्च महाभूतों में प्रथम भूत आकाश है, वहां श्रोत्र अध्यात्म, शब्द अधिभूत और दिशाएँ अधिदेव कही गई है
dheesh_gita::77.english_translation: Among the five great elements, the first is space; it is called the ear or inner self. Sound is the intermediate element, and directions are the presiding deities.
dheesh_gita::77.translation_literal: आकाशं (space) प्रथमं (first) भूतं (element) श्रोत्रम् (ear) अध्यात्मम् (inner self) उच्यते (is called) ! आधिभूतं (intermediate element) तथा (also) शब्दः (sound) दिशः (directions) तनाधि (presiding over) देवीतम् (deities) ॥
dheesh_gita::77.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::77.essence: Space is the first element, symbolizing the inner faculty that hears beyond physical sound.
dheesh_gita::77.simple_meaning: The first of the five great elements is space, which represents the inner faculty of hearing. Sound is the next element, and directions are the powers governing them.
dheesh_gita::77.simple_insight: You can sense that your true self is like an inner ear, receiving beyond the physical.
dheesh_gita::77.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the five great elements (pancha mahabhutas) are introduced, focusing on the first: space. Space is described as the faculty of hearing and the inner self. Sound is the next step as the intermediary element, while directions are the divine forces governing space. This sets a foundation for understanding how the inner being perceives the world.
dheesh_gita::77.modern_relevance: When you listen deeply, you realize your awareness is more than just physical hearing—it’s a spacious inner presence connecting all things.
dheesh_gita::77.insight: Recognize that hearing is not just a sense but a symbol for your inner receptive nature, linking outer and inner worlds.

dheesh_gita::78.verse_sanskrit:
द्वितीय मारुतं भूतं त्वगध्यात्म च विश्रुतम् ।
स्पष्टव्यमधिभूतञ्च विद्युत्तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::78.verse_hindi: द्वितीय भूत वायु है, यहां वक् अध्यात्म, स्पर्श अधिभूत और विद्युत् अधिदेव कहे गये हैं
dheesh_gita::78.english_translation: The second elemental being is the wind, here referred to as the inner essence of speech, the element of touch, and the divine presence of lightning.
dheesh_gita::78.translation_literal: द्वितीय (second) / मारुतं (wind) / भूतं (elemental being) / त्वग (skin) / अध्यात्म (inner essence) / च (and) / विश्रुतम् (famous, heard) / स्पष्टव्यम् (touch) / अधिभूतञ्च (the elemental) / विद्युत् (lightning) / तत्र (there) / अधिदैवतम् (divine presence)
dheesh_gita::78.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::78.essence: Wind embodies body, speech, and divine energy simultaneously in layered reality.
dheesh_gita::78.simple_meaning: This verse identifies wind as the second elemental force, linked to the inner essence of speech, the sense of touch, and the divine presence symbolized by lightning.
dheesh_gita::78.simple_insight: Recognizing the wind as more than air connects your body, senses, and the divine energy around you.
dheesh_gita::78.detailed_meaning: The verse classifies the wind (Marut) as the second elemental force, associating it with the inner spiritual aspect of speech (vāk), the physical sense of touch (adhibhootam), and the divine power symbolized by lightning (adhidaivatam), revealing layers of meaning beyond the physical element.
dheesh_gita::78.modern_relevance: When you feel the breeze or touch something, you're experiencing a subtle connection to deeper energies that shape your communication and sensing.
dheesh_gita::78.insight: It teaches you to see ordinary elements as bridges between body, mind, and the divine energy.

dheesh_gita::79.verse_sanskrit:
तृतीयं ज्योतिरित्याहुश्चक्षुरध्यात्ममुच्यते ।
अधिभूतं ततो रूपं सूर्यस्तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::79.verse_hindi: तृतीय भूत ज्योति अर्थात् अग्नि है, यहां चक्षु अध्यात्म, रूप अधिभत और सूर्य अधिदेव कहे गये हैं।
dheesh_gita::79.english_translation: The third element is light, called fire; the spiritual eye is called sight; the form is called the material element; the sun is called the presiding deity.
dheesh_gita::79.translation_literal: तृतीयं (third) ज्योतिरिति (light-called) आहुः (they say) चक्षुर् (eye) अध्यात्ममुच्यते (spiritual-called) । अधिभूतं (material) ततो (then) रूपं (form) सूर्यः (sun) तत्र (there) अधिदैवतम् (presiding deity) ॥
dheesh_gita::79.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::79.essence: True sight perceives the spiritual light beyond material form and physical eyes.
dheesh_gita::79.simple_meaning: Light is the third element and symbolizes fire. The spiritual eye means inner vision. The physical form belongs to the material world, and the sun represents the divine presence overseeing all.
dheesh_gita::79.simple_insight: There's a deeper way of seeing that goes beyond what your physical eyes capture.
dheesh_gita::79.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the teacher explains how different layers of perception and reality relate: fire is the third elemental force, sight is the spiritual eye that perceives beyond, the physical form belongs to the material world, and the sun stands as the divine overseer.
dheesh_gita::79.modern_relevance: When you look at something, you can become aware of the difference between what your eyes see and what your deeper awareness senses.
dheesh_gita::79.insight: It teaches you to distinguish between physical perception and spiritual insight, opening a clearer inner vision.

dheesh_gita::80.verse_sanskrit:
चतुर्थमापो विज्ञेयं जिहा चाध्यात्ममुच्यते ।
अधिभूत रसश्चात्र सोमस्तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::80.verse_hindi: चतुर्थ भूत जल है वहां जिह्व़ा अध्यात्म, रस अधिभूत और सोम अधिदैव कहे गये है
dheesh_gita::80.english_translation: The fourth element is water; the tongue is the inner self, taste is the physical essence, and soma is the celestial deity.
dheesh_gita::80.translation_literal: चतुर्थमापो (fourth is water) / विज्ञेयं (to be known) / जिहा (tongue) / च (and) / अध्यात्म (inner self) / उच्यते (is called) / अधिभूत (physical essence) / रसश् (taste) / च (and) / अत्र (there) / सोमः (soma) / तत्र (there) / अधिदैवतम् (celestial deity)
dheesh_gita::80.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::80.essence: Your tongue and taste connect physical reality with your inner self and the divine.
dheesh_gita::80.simple_meaning: Water is the fourth element, the tongue represents the inner self, taste is the physical experience, and soma symbolizes the divine aspect.
dheesh_gita::80.simple_insight: You sense more than flavor; your tongue links body, self, and higher essence.
dheesh_gita::80.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the fourth elemental principle, water, is explored through three aspects: the tongue (inner self), taste (physical sensation), and soma (the divine presence). This shows how the physical and spiritual connect through sensory experience.
dheesh_gita::80.modern_relevance: When you savor food or drink, your tongue is not just sensing flavor but connecting your body and deeper self to something beyond.
dheesh_gita::80.insight: It teaches you to recognize sensory experience as a bridge between the physical world and your inner being.

dheesh_gita::81.verse_sanskrit:
पृथिवी पञ्चमं भूतं घ्राणभाध्यात्ममुच्यते ।
अधिभूतं तथा गन्धों वायुस्तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::81.verse_hindi: पंचम भूत पृथिवी है. यहां प्राण अध्यात्म, गन्ध अधिभूत और वायु अधिदैव कहे गये हैं
dheesh_gita::81.english_translation: Earth is the fifth element, called the body perceived by smell; Prana is the inner being, smell is the physical element, and air is the divine presence in it.
dheesh_gita::81.translation_literal: पृथिवी (Earth) / पञ्चमं (fifth) / भूतं (element) / घ्राणभाध्यात्ममुच्यते (called the body perceived by smell) / । / अधिभूतं (physical element) / तथा (also) / गन्धों (smell) / वायुस्तत्राधिदैवतम् (air is the divine presence there) / ॥
dheesh_gita::81.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::81.essence: Earth is body sensed by smell, breath is inner life, air is divine presence within.
dheesh_gita::81.simple_meaning: Earth is the fifth element, experienced through smell. It includes the physical body, the breath inside, and the divine presence represented by air.
dheesh_gita::81.simple_insight: Your physical senses connect you to both the natural world and a deeper presence beyond it.
dheesh_gita::81.detailed_meaning: This verse explains the layers of experience related to the element earth: how the body perceives it through smell, how breath (Prana) relates to the inner being, and how air represents a divine presence beyond the physical.
dheesh_gita::81.modern_relevance: When you breathe deeply and notice the scents around you, you connect to your body, your breath, and something greater beyond them.
dheesh_gita::81.insight: It teaches you to recognize the unity of body, breath, and spirit within the natural world you experience.

dheesh_gita::82.verse_hindi: तत्वदर्शी ब्राह्मण कहते है कि पाद ( पैर) अध्यात्म है, गन्तव्य अधिभूत है और वहां विष्णु अधिदैव हैं
dheesh_gita::82.english_translation: The wise brahmins say the foot represents the spiritual self, the destination is the physical world, and Vishnu is the presiding divinity there.
dheesh_gita::82.translation_literal: पादावध्यात्ममित्याहु (foot is spiritual self they say) / ब्रहाह्मणास्तत्त्वदर्शिनः (brahmins who see truth) / अधिभूतं (the physical world) / तु (but) / गन्तव्यं (destination to be reached) / विष्णुस्तत्राधिदैवतम् (Vishnu there is presiding divinity)
dheesh_gita::82.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::82.essence: Every part of reality symbolizes a deeper spiritual aspect and divine presence.
dheesh_gita::82.simple_meaning: The foot symbolizes the spiritual self, the physical world is the place to go, and Vishnu presides there.
dheesh_gita::82.simple_insight: Symbols point to layers of reality beyond the obvious physical world.
dheesh_gita::82.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, the brahmins who understand reality say that the foot represents the spiritual self, the physical world is the target to be experienced, and Vishnu is the divine presence overseeing it.
dheesh_gita::82.insight: It invites you to see everyday things as symbols for deeper realities beyond what you normally perceive.

dheesh_gita::83.verse_hindi: निम्न गतिशील अपान है, वहां पायु अध्यात्म, विसर्ग अधिभून और मिन अधिदेव है।
dheesh_gita::83.english_translation: The downward-moving breath is called apana; the upward-moving breath is prana; the external vital force is visarga; among these, the friend is the higher being.
dheesh_gita::83.translation_literal: अवागूगानरपानश्च (downward-moving breath and apana) पायुरध्यात्ममुच्यते (prana is called the upward-moving breath) । अधिभूतं (the external vital force) विसर्गश्च (and visarga) मित्रः (the friend) तत्र (there) अधिदैवतम् (is the higher being) ॥
dheesh_gita::83.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::83.essence: Your breath flows in dual currents held and guided by a higher inner presence.
dheesh_gita::83.simple_meaning: Breath moves in two directions: downward called apana and upward called prana. The external vital force is visarga, and the higher being governs these forces as a friend.
dheesh_gita::83.simple_insight: There's a deeper presence guiding your breath beyond what you feel.
dheesh_gita::83.detailed_meaning: This verse explains the vital life forces: apana (downward breath), prana (upward breath), and visarga (external vital energy). It reveals that these forces are held in harmony by the higher being, seen as a friend guiding life within.
dheesh_gita::83.modern_relevance: When you notice your breath rushing or slowing, there's a subtle inner presence balancing these flows beyond your control.
dheesh_gita::83.insight: It teaches you to sense the inner presence harmonizing dual forces of breath beyond conscious effort.

dheesh_gita::84.verse_sanskrit:
प्रजनः सर्वभूतानामुपस्योऽध्यात्ममुच्यते ।
अधिभूतं तथा शुक्रं देवतञ्च प्रजापतिः ॥
dheesh_gita::84.verse_hindi: सब जीवों का उत्पादक उपस्थ अध्यात्म है, शुक अधिभूत और प्रजापति अधिदैव है
dheesh_gita::84.english_translation: The origin of all beings is called the inner self; the physical is the external, and the divine lord is the supreme controller.
dheesh_gita::84.translation_literal: प्रजनः (origin) / सर्वभूतानाम् (of all beings) / उपस्यः (worshipped/considered) / अध्यात्मम् (inner self) / उच्यते (is called) / अधिभूतं (that which is physical) / तथा (also) / शुक्रं (the pure/external) / देवतं (divine being) / च (and) / प्रजापतिः (lord of creatures)
dheesh_gita::84.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::84.essence: Your true origin is the inner self beyond body and nature.
dheesh_gita::84.simple_meaning: All living beings come from the inner self. The body is the physical form, and a higher divine force governs beyond that.
dheesh_gita::84.simple_insight: You are much more than your physical body or surroundings; your true source is deeper within.
dheesh_gita::84.detailed_meaning: This verse explains that the source of all living beings is the inner self or spiritual essence. The physical body is called the external, and the divine ruler or supreme force governs all creation. It sets the foundation for understanding existence beyond just the material.
dheesh_gita::84.modern_relevance: When you feel limited by your body or circumstances, remember you come from a deeper source beyond physical things.
dheesh_gita::84.insight: It shifts your view from identifying as just a body to recognizing your inner self as the true source of life.

dheesh_gita::85.verse_sanskrit:
हस्तावध्यात्ममित्याहुरध्यात्मदिनो जनाः ।
अधिभूतं च कर्माणि शकस्तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::85.verse_hindi: अध्यात्म शस्त्र के पण्डितगण दोनों हाथों को अध्यात्म कहते हैं, कर्म अधिभूत और शक्र वहां अधिदैव है
dheesh_gita::85.english_translation: Scholars of spiritual knowledge call the two hands spirituality; actions belong to the physical realm, and Shakra governs the divine realm there.
dheesh_gita::85.translation_literal: हस्तावध्यात्मम् (hands - spirituality) इत्याहुः (say) अध्यात्मदिनो (scholars of spiritual knowledge) जनाः (people) । अधिभूतं (physical realm) च (and) कर्माणि (actions) शकः (Shakra) तत्र (there) अधिदैवतम् (divine realm) ॥
dheesh_gita::85.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::85.essence: Physical action, inner spirituality, and divine influence are distinct, interconnected realms.
dheesh_gita::85.simple_meaning: Spiritual scholars say the two hands represent spirituality; physical actions belong to the natural world, and Shakra rules the divine aspect.
dheesh_gita::85.simple_insight: The verse connects physical action, spiritual practice, and divine influence as distinct but linked domains.
dheesh_gita::85.detailed_meaning: The verse explains a teaching of spiritual scholars who view the two hands symbolizing spirituality (inner practice). Actions belong to the physical realm, while Shakra, a divine figure, governs the divine realm influencing those actions.
dheesh_gita::85.insight: It clarifies that action involves physical effort, inner spirituality, and a higher influence working together.

dheesh_gita::86.verse_sanskrit:
वैश्वदेवी ततः पूर्वा वागध्यात्ममिहोच्यते ।
वक्तव्यमधिभूतञ्च बह्निस्तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::86.verse_hindi: विश्वेदेव से उत्पन्न प्रथम वाणी अध्यात्म है, वक्तव्य अधिभूत और वहां वह्यी अधिदेव है
dheesh_gita::86.english_translation: From the supreme being Vaishvadevi arose the first speech, representing the spiritual; the spoken word relates to the material, and the fire there represents the presiding divine force.
dheesh_gita::86.translation_literal: वैश्वदेवी (Vaishvadevi) / ततः (then) / पूर्वा (first) / वाग् (speech) / अध्यात्मम् (spiritual) / इह (here) / उच्यते (is called) / वक्तव्यं (spoken word) / अधिभूतं (material) / च (and) / बह्नि (fire) / तत्र (there) / अधिदैवतम् (presiding divine force)
dheesh_gita::86.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::86.essence: Speech arises from the spiritual and links material and divine forces.
dheesh_gita::86.simple_meaning: The first speech that came from Vaishvadevi is spiritual; the words spoken connect to the physical world, and fire there symbolizes the divine presence.
dheesh_gita::86.simple_insight: Speech links the spiritual, material, and divine in a living, layered way.
dheesh_gita::86.detailed_meaning: This verse explains that Vaishvadevi, a supreme entity, produced the very first speech, which is spiritual. The spoken words relate to the material world, while fire symbolizes the divine energy present there. It maps how speech connects different realms.
dheesh_gita::86.insight: It reveals that communication is a bridge uniting inner spirit, outer matter, and divine force.

dheesh_gita::87.verse_hindi: समस्त संसार का कर्ता अहंकार अध्यात्म है, अभिमान अधिभूत और रुद्र वहां अधिदैव है
dheesh_gita::87.english_translation: The sense of separate self is the maker of the entire world; ego governs the physical realm, and Rudra presides as the divine force there.
dheesh_gita::87.translation_literal: अहङ्कारः (sense of separate self) तथाऽध्यात्म (and spiritual principle) सर्वसंसारकारकम् (maker of entire world) । अभिमानः (ego) अधिभूतञ्च (presiding over physical realm) रुद्रः (Rudra) तत्र (there) अधिदैवतम् (divine force) ॥
dheesh_gita::87.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::87.essence: Your sense of separate self creates the world, ego governs the body, and divine power rules the physical realm.
dheesh_gita::87.simple_meaning: The sense of being a separate self creates the whole world. Ego controls the physical body, and a divine power like Rudra governs that realm.
dheesh_gita::87.simple_insight: Understanding ego as the builder of your experience brings relief and clarity.
dheesh_gita::87.detailed_meaning: This verse explains the cosmic roles: the sense of separate self (Ahamkara) creates the world of experience; the ego (Abhimana) controls the physical body; and Rudra, a divine principle, governs the forces within that bodily realm.
dheesh_gita::87.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your body's needs or emotions, remember that your ego is shaping that experience, while a higher force guides the deeper flow.
dheesh_gita::87.insight: Recognize that your sense of self and ego build your perceived world, shifting focus from external events to internal processes.

dheesh_gita::88.verse_hindi: यथार्थ देखनेवाले विद्वद गण बुद्धि को अध्यात्म, ज्ञेय को अधिभूत और क्षेत्रज्ञ को अधिदैव कहते हैं।
dheesh_gita::88.english_translation: Scholars say intellect is about the inner being, the known is the material, and the knower is beyond nature.
dheesh_gita::88.translation_literal: बुद्धि (intellect) / अध्यात्म (inner being) / इति (thus) / आहुः (say) / यथा (as) / एव (indeed) / अभिदर्शिनः (those who see truly) । बुद्धव्यम् (to be known) / अधिभूतं (material) / तु (but) / क्षेत्रज्ञ (knower) / च (and) / अधिदैवतम् (beyond nature) ॥
dheesh_gita::88.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::88.essence: Intellect is the inner self; what is known is material; the knower transcends nature.
dheesh_gita::88.simple_meaning: Intellect relates to your inner being, what is known is the material world, and the knower is beyond material nature.
dheesh_gita::88.simple_insight: You can feel a connection between your mind, the world you perceive, and a deeper self beyond both.
dheesh_gita::88.detailed_meaning: This teaching distinguishes three levels: intellect as the inner spiritual faculty, the known as the physical material world, and the knower as the pure awareness beyond nature. It sets a foundation for understanding the self beyond appearances.
dheesh_gita::88.modern_relevance: When you analyze your thoughts, feelings, and surroundings, you can sense a difference between your mind, the things you experience, and a deeper part of you watching it all.
dheesh_gita::88.insight: It teaches you to identify intellect as the inner guide, separate from what you perceive and from your deeper awareness.

dheesh_gita::89.verse_sanskrit:
अध्यात्म मन इत्हासु पञ्चभूतात्मवारकम् ।
अधिभूतञ्च संकल्पश्चन्द्रमांश्चाधिदैवतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::89.verse_hindi: पञ्चभूतों से आत्मा को आवृत करनेवाला मन अध्यात्म है, संकल्प अधिभूत और चन्द्रमा अधिदैव है
dheesh_gita::89.english_translation: The inner science is the mind that covers the true self with the five elements; intention is the physical nature, and the moon represents the higher divine.
dheesh_gita::89.translation_literal: अध्यात्म (inner science) / मन (mind) / इत्हासु (in beings) / पञ्चभूतात्म (five-element-self) / वारकम् (covering) / अधिभूतञ्च (physical nature also) / संकल्पश्च (intention too) / चन्द्रमांश्च (and the moon) / अधिदैवतम् (higher divine)
dheesh_gita::89.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::89.essence: Your mind and intentions veil your true self with layers of nature and higher influence.
dheesh_gita::89.simple_meaning: The mind covers the true self with the five elements. Intention connects to physical nature, and the moon symbolizes the higher divine aspect.
dheesh_gita::89.simple_insight: You can feel how your mind and intentions shape what you experience as yourself.
dheesh_gita::89.detailed_meaning: This verse describes how the mind envelops the true self with the physical five elements. Intention belongs to the physical domain, and the moon symbolizes the higher divine influence, showing layers of inner experience to understand.
dheesh_gita::89.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your thoughts and feelings, remember they are coverings over your deeper self, shaped by your intentions and higher awareness.
dheesh_gita::89.insight: It teaches you to see your mind and intentions as layers over your true self, inviting you to look beyond them.

dheesh_gita::90.verse_sanskrit:
वेदः शब्दमयं ज्ञेयं मत्स्वरूपं न संशयः।
मन्त्रास्तत्राधिभूतं स्यादीश्वरश्चाधिदैवतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::90.verse_hindi: वेद को निःसन्देह मेरा शब्दमय स्वरुप जानना चाहिये। वेद विज्ञ कहते हैं कि वहां श्रुतियां अधिभूत, ईश्वर,अधिदेव
dheesh_gita::90.english_translation: The Vedas are undoubtedly my word-based nature. The Vedas declare that there are layers: the physical, the divine ruler, and the celestial beings.
dheesh_gita::90.translation_literal: वेदः (Vedas) शब्दमयं (word-based) ज्ञेयं (to be known) मत्स्वरूपं (my own nature) न (not) संशयः (doubt). मन्त्रास्तत्राधिभूतं (the physical in the mantras there) स्याद् (exists) ईश्वरः (the divine ruler) च (and) अधिदैवतम् (the celestial beings).
dheesh_gita::90.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::90.essence: The Vedas are my word-rooted nature layered with physical, divine, and celestial realities.
dheesh_gita::90.simple_meaning: The Vedas are not just texts; they are the word-expression of the speaker’s true nature, containing physical, divine, and celestial layers.
dheesh_gita::90.simple_insight: You realize the sacred texts are alive with multiple levels of meaning beyond just words.
dheesh_gita::90.detailed_meaning: The speaker declares that the Vedas are the direct word-based expression of his true essence. These sacred mantras contain layers: the material world (adhibhoot), the divine ruler (ishwara), and the celestial beings (adhidaivatam), revealing a complex reality behind the words.
dheesh_gita::90.modern_relevance: When you read a complex text or listen to someone wise, you can discover layers of meaning—what seems simple holds deeper levels if you look closely.
dheesh_gita::90.insight: It teaches you to perceive sacred or profound teachings as multi-layered realities, not just literal words.

dheesh_gita::91.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानमध्यात्ममित्याहुर्वेदनिष्णातबुद्धयः।
सरस्वत्याश्च गायत्र्याः सावित्र्याश्च तथैव हि ॥
dheesh_gita::91.verse_hindi: और ज्ञान अध्यात्म है। हे विप्रो ! मेरी शक्ति ही सरस्वती गायत्री और सावित्री
dheesh_gita::91.english_translation: Knowledge is the essence of the inner self. O learned one, my power is Saraswati, Gayatri, and Savitri.
dheesh_gita::91.translation_literal: ज्ञानमध्यात्ममित्याहुः (knowledge is inner self) वेदनिष्णातबुद्धयः (learned wise ones say) सरस्वत्याश्च (and Saraswati) गायत्र्याः (Gayatri's) सावित्र्याश्च (and Savitri's) तथैव (likewise) हि (indeed)
dheesh_gita::91.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::91.essence: Knowledge is not outside but the inner essence that empowers you.
dheesh_gita::91.simple_meaning: True knowledge is the essence of your inner being, the core of your existence and power.
dheesh_gita::91.simple_insight: You hold the sacred power of wisdom within yourself, not just outside sources.
dheesh_gita::91.detailed_meaning: This verse highlights that knowledge is not just external learning but the very heart of the inner self. The divine power behind Saraswati, Gayatri, and Savitri is the same power within you, connecting spiritual wisdom to your own being.
dheesh_gita::91.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by information, remember that your deepest wisdom comes from within, not just from outside voices.
dheesh_gita::91.insight: It shifts your view from seeking knowledge externally to recognizing your inner self as the source of true wisdom.

dheesh_gita::92.verse_sanskrit:
मच्छक्तिरेव वेदेषु त्रीणि रूपाणि विभ्रंती ।
ज्ञानशक्तिः क्रियाशक्तियज्ञशक्तिस्तथा द्विजाः ॥
dheesh_gita::92.verse_hindi: ये तीन रूप धारण, करके वेदों में ज्ञानशक्ति, क्रियाशक्ति और यज्ञ शक्ति
dheesh_gita::92.english_translation: The three powers you possess manifest in the Vedas: wisdom power, action power, and ritual power.
dheesh_gita::92.translation_literal: मच्छक्तिरेव (my power alone) / वेदेषु (in the Vedas) / त्रीणि (three) / रूपाणि (forms) / विभ्रंती (manifest) / ज्ञानशक्तिः (wisdom power) / क्रियाशक्तिः (action power) / यज्ञशक्तिः (ritual power) / तथा (also) / द्विजाः (twice-born ones)
dheesh_gita::92.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::92.essence: You embody three essential powers: knowing, acting, and offering sacredly.
dheesh_gita::92.simple_meaning: You have three core powers expressed in teachings: the power to understand, the power to act, and the power to perform sacred practices.
dheesh_gita::92.simple_insight: Recognizing these three powers helps you see your full capacity beyond just doing or knowing alone.
dheesh_gita::92.detailed_meaning: The speaker explains that within the Vedas, three distinct powers arise from the divine source: wisdom (understanding), action (doing), and ritual (sacred offering). These together guide those committed to spiritual and dharmic life, showing a balanced approach to knowledge and practice.
dheesh_gita::92.modern_relevance: You juggle learning facts, taking meaningful steps, and honoring deeper values in your daily choices — all three are your natural strengths.
dheesh_gita::92.insight: It shifts your view from seeing knowledge, action, and ritual as separate to recognizing them as interconnected powers you already possess.

dheesh_gita::93.verse_sanskrit:
एतन्छक्तित्रय नून समुत्पादयतेतराम् ।
नात्र कश्चन सन्देहो विद्यते विमपुङ्गवाः ॥
dheesh_gita::93.verse_hindi: इन तीन शक्तियों को अवश्य ही उत्पन्न करती है है ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठो! इसमें कुछ सन्देह नहीं
dheesh_gita::93.english_translation: The supreme being certainly produces these three powers; there is no doubt about this.
dheesh_gita::93.translation_literal: एतत् (this) शक्तित्रय (three powers) नून (certainly) समुत्पादयते (produces) अन्यतम् (other) न (not) कश्चन (anyone) सन्देहः (doubt) विद्यते (exists) विमपुङ्गवाः (O best of Brahmins)
dheesh_gita::93.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::93.essence: The supreme being unquestionably produces the three fundamental powers without any doubt.
dheesh_gita::93.simple_meaning: The supreme being definitely brings forth three fundamental forces; there is no doubt about this fact.
dheesh_gita::93.simple_insight: You can feel certainty that the source of these powers is undeniable and true.
dheesh_gita::93.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, the supreme being is declared as the unquestioned origin of three fundamental powers, addressing a respected Brahmin to affirm this truth clearly.
dheesh_gita::93.modern_relevance: When you face confusion about where your strength and energy come from, remember some forces behind you are certain and reliable.
dheesh_gita::93.insight: It teaches you to accept certain foundational forces as real and unquestionable, providing a stable base for further inquiry.

dheesh_gita::94.verse_hindi: वेद और वेदसम्मत शास्त्र एक ही हैं इस कारण उन वेदसम्मत शास्त्रों में भी त्रिभावों का निःसन्देह ऐसा ही सादृश्य है।
dheesh_gita::94.english_translation: The scriptures accepted by the Vedas are one and the same; among them, the three modes certainly share the same resemblance.
dheesh_gita::94.translation_literal: गमागमयोरेक् (coming and going are one) यान्छास्त्रेऽपि (even in scriptures) वेदसम्मते (accepted by the Vedas) । सादृश्यं (resemblance) तु (but) त्रिभावानाम् (of the three modes) एवमेव (just so) अस्ति (exists) असंशयम् (without doubt) ॥
dheesh_gita::94.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::94.essence: All Vedic-approved scriptures reveal the same three fundamental modes.
dheesh_gita::94.simple_meaning: All scriptures accepted by the Vedas are essentially the same and clearly show the same three fundamental qualities.
dheesh_gita::94.simple_insight: You see unity beneath diversity when you recognize the common thread in sacred teachings.
dheesh_gita::94.detailed_meaning: This verse explains that the various scriptures recognized by the Vedas are not different in essence; all share the same three modes or qualities, highlighting a fundamental unity in spiritual teachings.
dheesh_gita::94.modern_relevance: When you explore different teachings or traditions, you discover the same core principles repeating, no matter the source.
dheesh_gita::94.insight: It helps you see beyond surface differences to the shared structure beneath diverse teachings.

dheesh_gita::95.verse_sanskrit:
अन्तःकरणमेवास्ति कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः।
अहंहकारो मनो बुद्धिश्चित्तश्चैतचतुष्टयम ॥
dheesh_gita::95.verse_hindi: अन्तःकरण ही बन्ध और मोक्ष का कारण है, यहां मन बुद्धि चित्त और अहंकार यह चारों ही
dheesh_gita::95.english_translation: The inner instrument alone is the cause of bondage and freedom; the mind, intellect, inner state, and sense of self are its four parts.
dheesh_gita::95.translation_literal: अन्तःकरणम् (inner instrument) एव (alone) अस्ति (is) कारणम् (cause) बन्ध (bondage) मोक्षयोः (and freedom) । अहंहकारः (sense of self) मनः (mind) बुद्धिः (intellect) चित्तः (inner state) च (and) एतत् (this) चतुष्टयम् (fourfold) ॥
dheesh_gita::95.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::95.essence: Your own mind, intellect, inner state, and ego create your bondage or freedom.
dheesh_gita::95.simple_meaning: Your inner faculties—the mind, intellect, inner feelings, and ego—are the cause of feeling trapped or free.
dheesh_gita::95.simple_insight: Recognizing how your inner self creates limitation or liberation brings deep awareness.
dheesh_gita::95.detailed_meaning: This teaching explains that the inner mechanism called the 'inner instrument'—made of mind, intellect, inner state, and ego—is responsible for causing either bondage or freedom. Understanding these parts is key for spiritual insight.
dheesh_gita::95.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck or free in life, it’s often your own thoughts, choices, and sense of self shaping that experience.
dheesh_gita::95.insight: It teaches you to observe and refine your inner instruments to move from limitation to freedom.

dheesh_gita::96.verse_sanskrit:
तत्राधिभूतमेशस्ति मा तत्राधिदेवतम् ।
ममानन्दविलासश्च तत्राध्यात्म समुच्यते ॥
dheesh_gita::96.verse_hindi: अधिभूत, ब्रह्मा अधिदैव और मेरा आनन्द विलास अध्यात्म कहा जाता है।
dheesh_gita::96.english_translation: There, the supreme lord of the physical realm is called Adhibhuta; the supreme deity of the divine realm is called Adhidaiva; and my joyful play is called Adhyatma.
dheesh_gita::96.translation_literal: तत्र (there) / अधिभूत (supreme-lord-of-physical) / ईशः (lord) / अस्ति (is) / मा (not) / तत्र (there) / अधिदेवताम् (supreme-deity-of-divine) / मम (my) / आनन्द (joy) / विलासः (play) / च (and) / तत्र (there) / अध्यात्म (inner-being) / समुच्यते (is called)
dheesh_gita::96.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::96.essence: The true self is the joyful presence beyond physical and divine realms.
dheesh_gita::96.simple_meaning: The verse names three aspects of reality: the physical world’s supreme controller, the divine realm’s supreme being, and the joyful inner self called the true self.
dheesh_gita::96.simple_insight: You can feel connected to the joyful essence that transcends body and divine forms.
dheesh_gita::96.detailed_meaning: This verse explains three layers of existence: the physical world ruled by Adhibhuta, the divine realm ruled by Adhidaiva, and the inner joyful self called Adhyatma, highlighting the true self beyond all external forms.
dheesh_gita::96.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by your body or beliefs, remember your true self is a joyful presence beyond all appearances.
dheesh_gita::96.insight: It shifts focus from external powers to the joyful inner being as your true identity.

dheesh_gita::97.verse_sanskrit:
जगद्धारधर्मस्याधिभूतं कर्म प्रोच्यते ।
उपासनाधिदैवं स्यादध्यात्मं ज्ञानमुच्यते ॥
