dheesh_gita::97.verse_hindi: जगदधारक धर्म का अधिभूत कर्म अधिदेव उपासना और अध्यात्म जानकार है
dheesh_gita::97.english_translation: The foundation of the duty that sustains the world is called action; worship is the higher divine aspect, and spiritual knowledge is the highest.
dheesh_gita::97.translation_literal: जगद्धारधर्मस्य (of the duty that sustains the world) / अधिभूतं (the foundational) / कर्म (action) / प्रोच्यते (is called) / उपासनाधिदैवं (worship is the higher divine) / स्याद (is) / अध्यात्मं (spiritual knowledge) / ज्ञानमुच्यते (is called knowledge)
dheesh_gita::97.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::97.essence: Duty unfolds from action to worship and finally to spiritual knowledge.
dheesh_gita::97.simple_meaning: True duty begins with action, rises through devoted worship, and culminates in spiritual knowledge.
dheesh_gita::97.simple_insight: You are part of a deeper order where doing leads naturally to devotion and understanding.
dheesh_gita::97.detailed_meaning: The verse explains the layers of duty sustaining the world: the base is action (karma), built upon by worship (upasana) as a divine expression, and reaching its peak in spiritual wisdom (jnana). It shows the progression from doing to devotion to knowing.
dheesh_gita::97.modern_relevance: You finish your work, feel a connection beyond yourself, then begin to understand your deeper purpose.
dheesh_gita::97.insight: It teaches you to see your everyday actions as the first step toward higher devotion and inner clarity.

dheesh_gita::98.verse_sanskrit:
धर्माङ्गेप्वपि सर्वेषु प्रत्येक विद्यते द्विजाः ।
सम्बन्धी दि त्रिभावानां संशयो नात्र कश्चन ॥
dheesh_gita::98.verse_hindi: हे ब्राह्मणो! सब ब्रह्मांडों में से प्रत्येक धर्मांगो के साथ भी भावत्रय का सम्बन्ध है इसमें कुछ संशय नहीं
dheesh_gita::98.english_translation: O Brahmin, in every part of the cosmic order, the three states of being are undoubtedly connected.
dheesh_gita::98.translation_literal: धर्माङ्गेप्वपि (in parts of dharma) / सर्वेषु (in all) / प्रत्येक (each) / विद्यते (exists) / द्विजाः (O Brahmin) / सम्बन्धी (connected) / दि (the) / त्रिभावानां (three states of being) / संशयो (doubt) / नात्र (not here) / कश्चन (anyone)
dheesh_gita::98.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::98.essence: Every part of existence is inseparably connected through three fundamental states.
dheesh_gita::98.simple_meaning: Every part of the universe is connected with three fundamental states of existence without any doubt.
dheesh_gita::98.simple_insight: There is certainty in how everything is woven together in three basic ways.
dheesh_gita::98.detailed_meaning: Addressing a Brahmin, the verse states that within every part of the cosmic system, three fundamental modes or states are inseparably connected, leaving no room for doubt about their relationship.
dheesh_gita::98.modern_relevance: When you notice how different parts of your life are connected by common feelings or states, it reminds you that everything shares deeper bonds.
dheesh_gita::98.insight: It teaches you to see unity in diversity by recognizing three essential qualities underlying all parts of existence.

dheesh_gita::99.verse_sanskrit:
वेद एवास्ति भो विप्राः ! मदाज्ञायाः प्रकाशकः।
वेदसम्मतशास्त्राणि तस्य व्याख्यानिमानि च ॥
dheesh_gita::99.verse_hindi: हे ब्राह्मणों ! वेद ही मेरी आज्ञा का प्रकाशक है और वेदसम्मत शास्त्रसमूह उसकी व्याख्यारूप है
dheesh_gita::99.english_translation: O Brahmins! The Vedas are the source revealing my command, and the scriptures aligned with the Vedas are their explanation.
dheesh_gita::99.translation_literal: वेद (Vedas) एव (indeed) अस्ति (are) भो (O) विप्राः (Brahmins) ! मदाज्ञायाः (of my command) प्रकाशकः (illuminator). वेदसम्मतशास्त्राणि (Veda-approved scriptures) तस्य (of that) व्याख्यानिमानि (explanations) च (also).
dheesh_gita::99.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::99.essence: Foundational texts reveal divine commands, explained by accepted scriptures.
dheesh_gita::99.simple_meaning: The Vedas reveal the divine command, and the scriptures accepted by the Vedas explain it.
dheesh_gita::99.simple_insight: Scriptures guide understanding by illuminating the divine's instructions.
dheesh_gita::99.detailed_meaning: Addressing the Brahmins, the speaker states that the Vedas disclose the divine will, and the scriptures accepted by the Vedas serve as detailed explanations, setting the foundation for authoritative teachings.
dheesh_gita::99.insight: It shows the importance of foundational texts and their accepted interpretations for clear guidance.

dheesh_gita::100.verse_sanskrit:
अहमेवासम्यतो वेदे शास्त्रेषु तत्परेषु च।
लौकिकी परकीया च समाधिनामिका तथा ॥
dheesh_gita::100.verse_hindi: इस कारण वेद और वेदसम्मत शास्त्रों में मैं ही समाधिभाषा लौकिकभाषा और परकीय भाषा रूप से
dheesh_gita::100.english_translation: Because I alone am the measure in the Vedas and scriptures, in worldly and transcendental speech, and in the language of absorbed presence.
dheesh_gita::100.translation_literal: अहम् (I) एव (alone) अस्मि (am) यतो (because) वेदे (in the Vedas) शास्त्रेषु (in scriptures) तत्परेषु (in the supreme) च (and) लौकिकी (worldly) परकीया (transcendental) च (and) समाधिनामिका (of absorbed presence) तथा (also)
dheesh_gita::100.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::100.essence: You alone are the true measure behind all teachings and experiences.
dheesh_gita::100.simple_meaning: You are the ultimate reference point in all scriptures, teachings, worldly speech, and even the language of deep meditation.
dheesh_gita::100.simple_insight: You hold the true standard within yourself, beyond any external authority.
dheesh_gita::100.detailed_meaning: This verse declares that the true self is the ultimate standard by which all scriptures, worldly language, and spiritual experiences are measured. It teaches that the self is the core reference beyond external teachings.
dheesh_gita::100.modern_relevance: When advice or information from many sources overwhelm you, remember your own inner knowing is the true guide.
dheesh_gita::100.insight: It teaches you to trust your inner standard rather than relying only on external texts or opinions.

dheesh_gita::101.verse_sanskrit:
एतत्रयेण धृत्वाऽहं त्रिभावं भामि सन्ततम् ।
अधिभूतञ्च विद्यानां सर्वासां शास्त्रमुच्यते ॥
dheesh_gita::101.verse_hindi: विविध भावो को धारण करके निरन्तर प्रकाशित होता हूँ। सब विद्याओ का अधिभूत शास्त्र,
dheesh_gita::101.english_translation: By sustaining these three states, I constantly shine; the supreme science of all knowledges is called the one beyond the physical.
dheesh_gita::101.translation_literal: एतत्रयेण (by these three) धृत्वा (holding) अहं (I) त्रिभावं (three states) भामि (shine) सन्ततम् (constantly) । अधिभूतञ्च (the one beyond the physical) विद्यानां (of knowledges) सर्वासां (all) शास्त्रम् (science) उच्यते (is called) ॥
dheesh_gita::101.speaker: Shambhu Dheesh
dheesh_gita::101.essence: Sustaining three inner states constantly reveals the highest wisdom beyond the physical.
dheesh_gita::101.simple_meaning: You maintain three different inner states steadily, which lets you shine constantly. This steady balance is the highest knowledge beyond the physical.
dheesh_gita::101.simple_insight: Feeling steady in diverse states allows your inner light to shine continuously.
dheesh_gita::101.detailed_meaning: The speaker explains that by sustaining three fundamental states of being, one can shine without interruption. This triple state is called the supreme science that transcends ordinary knowledge tied to the physical world.
dheesh_gita::101.modern_relevance: When your mood shifts among different feelings but you stay grounded in all, your true strength and clarity shine through.
dheesh_gita::101.insight: It teaches you to integrate and hold diverse inner experiences steadily to access deeper wisdom.

dheesh_gita::102.verse_sanskrit:
अधिदैवमृषिः प्रोक्तमध्यात्म वेद उच्यते।
अधिभूतं ध्रुवं सृष्टः पिण्डसृष्टिमहर्षयः ! ॥
dheesh_gita::102.verse_hindi: अधिदैव ऋषि और अध्यात्म वेद कहा गया है। हे महर्षिगण ! सृष्टिका अधिभूत पिण्ड सृष्टि ही है,
dheesh_gita::102.english_translation: The supreme seer is called adhidaiva and the spiritual knowledge is called adhyatma-veda. O great sages, the created world is the physical creation, the adhidaiva is the supreme seer.
dheesh_gita::102.translation_literal: अधिदैवमृषिः (adhidaiva-seer) प्रोक्तमध्यात्म (called spiritual) वेद (knowledge) उच्यते (is said) । अधिभूतं (the physical) ध्रुवं (constant) सृष्टः (created) पिण्डसृष्टिमहर्षयः (physical creation, O great sages) ॥
dheesh_gita::102.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::102.essence: The highest seer transcends the physical world and is revealed by spiritual knowledge.
dheesh_gita::102.simple_meaning: There is a highest seer beyond the physical world, and spiritual knowledge reveals this supreme reality.
dheesh_gita::102.simple_insight: You can feel the presence of something beyond what you see and touch.
dheesh_gita::102.detailed_meaning: The verse explains to the sages that the highest seer (adhidaiva) is beyond the physical creation (adhibhuta), and the spiritual knowledge (adhyatmaveda) reveals this truth beyond the material world.
dheesh_gita::102.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by daily distractions, you can remember that your true awareness looks beyond what your senses show.
dheesh_gita::102.insight: It helps you shift from identifying with the physical world to recognizing a deeper, unchanging seer within.

dheesh_gita::103.verse_hindi: अधिदैव ब्रह्माण्ड सृष्टि ही है और अध्यात्म मेरे चित् और सत्भाव में आनन्दका निस्य विलास कहा गया है
dheesh_gita::103.english_translation: The supreme being is indeed the entire cosmos, and the true self is the eternal, blissful play of pure awareness.
dheesh_gita::103.translation_literal: ब्रह्माण्डसृष्टिरेवास्ति (indeed the cosmos exists) / नूनं (surely) / तत्राधिदैवतम् (there the supreme being) / सचितोर्नित्यमानन्दविलासः (the eternal blissful play of pure awareness) / अध्यात्ममुच्यते (is called the true self)
dheesh_gita::103.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::103.essence: The true self is the eternal joyful presence of the entire cosmos as supreme reality.
dheesh_gita::103.simple_meaning: Everything that exists is the supreme reality, and your true self is the joyful, eternal experience of pure awareness.
dheesh_gita::103.simple_insight: You can feel connected to something vast and joyful that never ends.
dheesh_gita::103.detailed_meaning: This verse explains that the entire cosmos is the supreme reality, and the true self is the eternal, blissful play of pure awareness, revealing a foundational view in Vedantic philosophy about reality and self.
dheesh_gita::103.modern_relevance: When you feel lost or small, remember you are an unending flow of joy connected to everything around you.
dheesh_gita::103.insight: Recognize that your true self is not limited but the timeless, joyful presence behind all appearances.

dheesh_gita::104.verse_sanskrit:
अनन्तकोटिब्रह्माण्ड-कारणं यच्च प्रोच्यते ।
पिण्डनाशोऽधिभूतं स्यात्मलयस्य महर्षयः ! ॥
dheesh_gita::104.verse_hindi: जो अनन्त कोटि ब्रह्माण्डो का कारण है। हे महर्षिगण !
dheesh_gita::104.english_translation: O great seers, that which is the cause of infinite millions of universes is the dissolution of the body and the fundamental element.
dheesh_gita::104.translation_literal: अनन्तकोटिब्रह्माण्ड-कारणं (cause of infinite millions of universes) / यच्च (that which) / प्रोच्यते (is said) / पिण्डनाशोऽधिभूतं (dissolution of the body and the fundamental element) / स्यात्मलयस्य (of the self's dissolution) / महर्षयः (O great seers)!
dheesh_gita::104.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::104.essence: The end of the physical body is the cause behind countless universes.
dheesh_gita::104.simple_meaning: The cause behind countless universes is the dissolution of the physical body and the underlying material nature.
dheesh_gita::104.simple_insight: The vast cosmos and the end of physical form are linked as one profound process.
dheesh_gita::104.detailed_meaning: Addressing the great sages, the verse explains that the ultimate cause behind countless universes is the transformation or dissolution of the physical body and fundamental nature, signaling a deep metaphysical connection between cosmic cycles and individual dissolution.
dheesh_gita::104.insight: It shifts your view to see your physical end as part of a vast cosmic process, connecting self and universe.

dheesh_gita::105.verse_sanskrit:
प्राहुरज्ञाश्च यं मृत्यु जीवानां रोमहर्पणम् ।
ब्रह्माण्डप्रलयश्चास्ति विप्रा:! तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::105.verse_hindi: प्रलय का पिण्ड प्रलय अधिभूत है जिसको अज्ञ लोग जीवो का रोमाञ्चकारी मृत्यु कहते हैं, अधिदेव ब्रह्माण्ड प्रलय है
dheesh_gita::105.english_translation: Ignorant people call the dissolution of living beings a terrifying death; the sages know it as the cosmic dissolution, the supreme divine event.
dheesh_gita::105.translation_literal: प्राहु: (they say) / अज्ञाश्च (ignorant people) / यं (that which) / मृत्यु (death) / जीव - आनां (of living beings) / रोमहर्पणम् (causing hair to stand on end / terrifying) / ब्रह्माण्डप्रलयश्चास्ति (and the cosmic dissolution is) / विप्रा: (the sages) / तत्र (there) / अधिदैवतम् (the supreme divine event)
dheesh_gita::105.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::105.essence: What seems like terrifying death is the universe's profound cosmic transformation.
dheesh_gita::105.simple_meaning: What ignorant people fear as death is really the universe dissolving and renewing itself, a supreme cosmic event known by the wise.
dheesh_gita::105.simple_insight: Fear of death softens when seen as part of a grand cosmic renewal.
dheesh_gita::105.detailed_meaning: This verse contrasts two views: ordinary people see death as frightening and final, while the sages recognize it as the cosmic dissolution, a vast universal transformation involving all creation.
dheesh_gita::105.modern_relevance: When you face loss or endings, remembering they are part of a larger cycle can ease fear and open acceptance.
dheesh_gita::105.insight: It shifts your view of death from personal loss to cosmic transformation, reducing fear and fostering acceptance.

dheesh_gita::106.verse_sanskrit:
अध्यात्म तत्र जीवानां मत्सायुज्यसमागमः ।
जीवस्यावरणं नूनं बन्धकारणमुच्यते ॥
dheesh_gita::106.verse_hindi: और अध्यात्म प्रलय जीवों के मत्सायुज्य प्राप्त होने को कहते है। पाश अर्थात् आवरण ही जीव के बन्धन का कारण कहा जाता है ।
dheesh_gita::106.english_translation: Spirituality is the union of the self with the supreme at dissolution; the covering of the self is indeed the cause of bondage.
dheesh_gita::106.translation_literal: अध्यात्म (spirituality) / तत्र (there) / जीवानां (of beings) / मत्सायुज्यसमागमः (union with the supreme at dissolution) / जीवस्यावरणं (covering of the self) / नूनं (indeed) / बन्धकारणम् (cause of bondage) / उच्यते (is said).
dheesh_gita::106.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::106.essence: Bondage arises from the hidden layers that veil your true self from itself.
dheesh_gita::106.simple_meaning: True spirituality is joining with the supreme reality when the false coverings around the self fall away. These coverings cause bondage.
dheesh_gita::106.simple_insight: There’s freedom waiting behind the layers that hide who you really are.
dheesh_gita::106.detailed_meaning: The verse explains that spirituality means the merging of the individual self with the supreme reality at the end of cycles. The false coverings or veils over the self create bondage, preventing this union.
dheesh_gita::106.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck or limited, it’s often because you’re hiding your true self behind fears and false identities.
dheesh_gita::106.insight: Recognize that removing false beliefs and identifications reveals your natural freedom and connection to the supreme.

dheesh_gita::107.verse_sanskrit:
अधिभूतं हि यस्यास्ति कोषाणां पञ्चकं बुधाः ।
अधिदैवमविद्या मे सत्सत्ताऽध्यात्ममुच्यते ॥
dheesh_gita::107.verse_hindi: हे  विज्ञो! जिसका पञ्चकोष अधिभूत अविद्या अधिदेव और मेरी सत सत्ता अध्यात्म है
dheesh_gita::107.english_translation: The wise say the five sheaths belong to the physical world, ignorance, the divine, and my true being is the inner self.
dheesh_gita::107.translation_literal: अधिभूतं (physical world) हि (indeed) यस्यास्ति (which has) कोषाणां (of sheaths) पञ्चकं (five) बुधाः (the wise) । अधिदैवम् (the divine) अविद्या (ignorance) मे (my) सत् (true) सत्त्वा (being) अध्यात्मम् (inner self) उच्यते (is called) ॥
dheesh_gita::107.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::107.essence: You are a layered being: body, ignorance, divine aspect, and your true self at the core.
dheesh_gita::107.simple_meaning: You consist of five layers: the physical body, ignorance, the divine presence, and at the core, your true inner self.
dheesh_gita::107.simple_insight: You can feel grounded knowing your true self is beyond confusion and appearances.
dheesh_gita::107.detailed_meaning: A teacher explains that human existence includes five sheaths: the physical body, the veil of ignorance, the divine aspect, and most importantly, the true inner self called the Atman or inner being. This reveals the layered nature of identity.
dheesh_gita::107.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by your body's needs and confusing thoughts, remember there is a clear, unchanging inner self beneath it all.
dheesh_gita::107.insight: This verse helps you distinguish between fleeting layers of existence and your unchanging true self, improving self-awareness.

dheesh_gita::108.verse_sanskrit:
सामञ्जस्यसुरक्षार्थ सृष्टेरुत्पद्यते तु यः।
देवासुराख्यसंग्रामः पूर्णः सोऽपि त्रिभावतः ॥
dheesh_gita::108.verse_hindi: सृष्टि के सामञ्जस्य की रक्षा के लिये जो देवासुर संग्राम हुआ करता है वह भी त्रिभाव से पूर्ण है
dheesh_gita::108.english_translation: The conflict known as the divine and shadow beings' battle arises to protect creation's harmony and is fulfilled in three modes.
dheesh_gita::108.translation_literal: सामञ्जस्य (of harmony) / सुरक्षा (protection) / अर्थ (for the purpose) / सृष्टे (of creation) / उत्पद्यते (arises) / तु (but) / यः (who) / देवासुराख्यसंग्रामः (battle called divine-shadow beings) / पूर्णः (complete) / सः (that) / अपि (also) / त्रिभावतः (in three modes)
dheesh_gita::108.speaker: Narrator
dheesh_gita::108.essence: Conflict between radiant and shadow beings preserves creation’s harmony through three modes.
dheesh_gita::108.simple_meaning: The battle between divine and shadow beings happens to protect the harmony of creation and involves three fundamental modes.
dheesh_gita::108.simple_insight: Even conflicts serve a greater balance beyond apparent opposition.
dheesh_gita::108.detailed_meaning: The narrator explains that the recurring conflict between radiant and shadowy beings is not random but serves to maintain the balance within creation, expressed through three essential qualities or modes.
dheesh_gita::108.insight: Recognize that apparent conflicts can maintain deeper balance and are part of natural order.

dheesh_gita::109.verse_sanskrit:
विज्ञा महर्षयो नात्र काचित् कार्या विचारणा।
धर्माधर्ममयीनां यदवृत्तीनां द्वन्द्वसङ्गरम् ॥
dheesh_gita::109.verse_hindi: हे विज्ञ ब्राह्मणों ! यह निःसन्देह है। धर्मा-धर्म वृत्तियों का जो द्वन्द्ध युद्ध
dheesh_gita::109.english_translation: O wise sages, there is certainly a conflict of opposing duties and unrighteousness in these activities.
dheesh_gita::109.translation_literal: विज्ञा (O wise) / महर्षयो (great seers) / नात्र (here not) / काचित् (any) / कार्या (actions to be done) / विचारणा (consideration) / धर्माधर्ममयीनां (of right and wrong) / यदवृत्तीनां (of those activities) / द्वन्द्वसङरम् (conflict of opposites)
dheesh_gita::109.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::109.essence: Some actions inherently involve a conflict between right and wrong duties.
dheesh_gita::109.simple_meaning: Sometimes, your actions involve a real struggle between what is right and what is wrong.
dheesh_gita::109.simple_insight: You can feel tension when your choices pull you in opposite directions.
dheesh_gita::109.detailed_meaning: The verse warns that in life, actions often involve a clash between what is considered right and wrong, creating internal conflict that wise seekers must recognize and navigate.
dheesh_gita::109.modern_relevance: You hesitate, unsure if the task before you is fully right or if some part feels off or unfair.
dheesh_gita::109.insight: It helps you recognize and accept that some actions naturally involve conflicting duties, requiring clear discernment and balance.

dheesh_gita::110.verse_sanskrit:
अन्तः करणमासाध जायते नित्यमदभुतम् ।
देवासुराख्ययुद्धस्य तदेवाध्यात्ममुच्यते ॥
dheesh_gita::110.verse_hindi: अन्तःकरण में नित्य होता है वही उसका अध्यात्म है
dheesh_gita::110.english_translation: The inner instrument that constantly arises is called the true self in the war between radiant and shadow beings.
dheesh_gita::110.translation_literal: अन्तःकरणमासाध (inner instrument arises) / जायते (arises) / नित्यम् (constantly) / अदभुतम् (wonderful) । / देवासुराख्ययुद्धस्य (of the war called divine and shadow beings) / तदेव (that itself) / अध्यात्ममुच्यते (is called true self) ॥
dheesh_gita::110.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::110.essence: An inner instrument constantly arises and is the true self amid conflict.
dheesh_gita::110.simple_meaning: Inside you, a constant inner instrument arises that guides your awareness; this is called your true self during the struggle of radiant and shadow forces.
dheesh_gita::110.simple_insight: You carry a living inner awareness that emerges anew in every moment of conflict.
dheesh_gita::110.detailed_meaning: In the midst of the cosmic battle between radiant beings and shadow beings, there is an inner instrument—like a mental mechanism—that continually arises within us. This inner presence is called the true self, reflecting the spiritual essence active during such struggles.
dheesh_gita::110.modern_relevance: When you face inner conflicts or tough choices, a constant inner awareness arises to guide you through the struggle.
dheesh_gita::110.insight: It teaches you to recognize an ever-present inner awareness that witnesses conflict without being overwhelmed.

dheesh_gita::111.verse_sanskrit:
देवासरं देवलोके युद्ध नैमित्तिकं तु यद ।
भवेतदेव भो विमा आस्ते खल्वपिदैवतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::111.verse_hindi: हे ब्राह्मणो ! देवलोक के नैमित्तिक देवासुर संग्राम ही अधिदेव हैं
dheesh_gita::111.english_translation: O Brahmin! The occasional battles between devas and asuras in the divine realm are the supreme divine acts.
dheesh_gita::111.translation_literal: देवासरं (deva and asura) / देवलोके (in the divine realm) / युद्ध (battle) / नैमित्तिकं (occasional) / तु (but) / यद् (that) / भवेत (happens) / देव (divine) / भो (indeed) / विमा (supreme) / आस्ते (is) / खल्वपि (even though) / अदैवतम् (divine act)
dheesh_gita::111.speaker: Narrator
dheesh_gita::111.essence: Occasional divine battles are themselves supreme expressions of cosmic order.
dheesh_gita::111.simple_meaning: Battles between divine and shadowy beings happen sometimes in the divine realm and are considered supreme divine acts.
dheesh_gita::111.simple_insight: Sometimes conflict in higher realms is part of a greater cosmic order.
dheesh_gita::111.detailed_meaning: The narrator explains that in the divine realm, occasional battles between radiant beings (devas) and shadowy beings (asuras) occur, and these conflicts themselves are regarded as supreme divine acts, reflecting cosmic dynamics beyond ordinary human experience.
dheesh_gita::111.insight: Recognize that even apparent conflicts in higher realms serve a greater purpose in cosmic balance.

dheesh_gita::112.verse_sanskrit:
दैवीनामासुरीणाञ्च सम्पत्तीनां प्रभावतः।
जायते मृत्युलोके यदमहायुद्धं परस्परम् ॥
dheesh_gita::112.verse_hindi: और मृत्युलोक में देवी और आसुरी सम्पत्ति के प्रभाव से जो परस्पर महासंग्राम होता है ।
dheesh_gita::112.english_translation: In the mortal realm, a great conflict arises between the forces of divine and shadowy energies.
dheesh_gita::112.translation_literal: दैवीनाम् (of the divine) आसुरीणाम् (of the shadowy beings) च (and) सम्पत्तीनाम् (of the powers) प्रभावतः (because of the influence) जायते (arises) मृत्युलोके (in the mortal world) यत् (that) महायुद्धम् (great war) परस्परम् (between each other)
dheesh_gita::112.speaker: Narrator
dheesh_gita::112.essence: A great battle erupts in the mortal world between opposing cosmic forces.
dheesh_gita::112.simple_meaning: A massive battle occurs in the mortal world between divine and shadowy forces due to their influence.
dheesh_gita::112.simple_insight: Conflict often arises from opposing forces within the world around us.
dheesh_gita::112.detailed_meaning: The verse describes a scene where opposing cosmic forces—divine and shadowy—engage in a massive battle in the mortal realm, setting the stage for larger cosmic events unfolding in the story.
dheesh_gita::112.insight: Recognize that much conflict comes from the clash of opposing influences beyond individual control.

dheesh_gita::113.verse_sanskrit:
अधिभूतं तदेवास्ति तस्य युद्धस्य निश्चितम् ।
ममैव प्रकृतिनमाश्रयेण ममैव तु ॥
dheesh_gita::113.verse_hindi: वही उसका अधिभूत है यह निश्चय है। हे विप्रो! मेरी ही प्रकृति मेरे ही आश्रय से
dheesh_gita::113.english_translation: The natural world is surely the field of that battle; it depends on my own nature and support.
dheesh_gita::113.translation_literal: अधिभूतं (natural world) तदेवास्ति (is indeed that) तस्य (of that) युद्धस्य (battle) निश्चितम् (certain) । ममैव (my own) प्रकृतिनमाश्रयेण (by nature's support) ममैव (indeed my own) तु (but) ॥
dheesh_gita::113.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::113.essence: The battle occurs within the natural world sustained by the speaker's own nature.
dheesh_gita::113.simple_meaning: The battle takes place in the natural world, which is controlled and supported by the speaker's own nature.
dheesh_gita::113.simple_insight: The world we struggle in is shaped by the forces within and around us.
dheesh_gita::113.detailed_meaning: This verse states that the battlefield is the natural world, which is firmly linked to the speaker's own nature and support. It reflects the deep connection between the conflict and the fundamental forces sustaining it, though it does not stand alone as a teaching.
dheesh_gita::113.insight: Recognize that your challenges arise within the natural order shaped by your own nature and conditions.

dheesh_gita::114.verse_sanskrit:
आविर्भावयते सष्टि-प्रपञ्चं सन्ततं द्विजाः ।
कारणं बन्धनस्यातः प्रकृतेर्मे गुणत्रयम् ॥
dheesh_gita::114.verse_hindi: सृष्टिप्रपञ्च निरन्तर प्रकट करती है इस कारण मेरी प्रकृति के तीन गुण बंधन के हेतु होते हैं
dheesh_gita::114.english_translation: The continuous manifestation of creation happens because my nature's three qualities are the cause of bondage.
dheesh_gita::114.translation_literal: आविर्भावयते (manifests) सष्टि-प्रपञ्चं (creation and world) सन्ततं (continuous) द्विजाः (twice-born/beings) कारणं (cause) बन्धनस्य (of bondage) आतः (from) प्रकृतेः (nature's) मे (my) गुणत्रयम् (three qualities)
dheesh_gita::114.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::114.essence: Three qualities of nature cause the endless cycle of creation and bondage.
dheesh_gita::114.simple_meaning: Creation keeps unfolding endlessly because the three qualities of nature cause the cycle of bondage.
dheesh_gita::114.simple_insight: Understanding that your nature's qualities keep you tied to the cycle brings clarity and opens a way beyond.
dheesh_gita::114.detailed_meaning: Shri Dheesh explains that the ongoing unfolding of the universe happens because the three innate qualities of nature cause the binding cycle affecting beings seeking freedom.
dheesh_gita::114.modern_relevance: You notice how your habits and moods keep repeating, pulling you back into the same patterns again and again.
dheesh_gita::114.insight: It teaches you to recognize how these three qualities shape your experience and bind you, so you can start to loosen their hold.

dheesh_gita::115.verse_sanskrit:
ये त्रिभावाश्रयान्मे तु पश्यन्ति प्रकृति मम ।
त्रिभिर्गुणैर्न वध्यन्ते प्रकृतेस्ते कदाचन ॥
dheesh_gita::115.verse_hindi: परन्तु जो मेरे तीनों भावों का आश्रय ग्रहण करके मेरी प्रकृति को देखते हैं वह प्रकृति के तीनों गुणो से कभी बन्धन प्राप्त नहीं होते
dheesh_gita::115.english_translation: Those who see my nature through my three aspects are never bound by the three qualities of nature.
dheesh_gita::115.translation_literal: ये (those) / त्रिभावाश्रयान्मे (by my three aspects) / तु (but) / पश्यन्ति (see) / प्रकृति (nature) / मम (my) / त्रिभिर्गुणैः (by three qualities) / न (not) / वध्यन्ते (are bound) / प्रकृतेः (of nature) / ते (they) / कदाचन (ever)
dheesh_gita::115.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::115.essence: Seeing your true nature beyond its qualities frees you from their binding influence.
dheesh_gita::115.simple_meaning: If you understand your true nature through its three aspects, you won’t be trapped by nature’s changing qualities.
dheesh_gita::115.simple_insight: There is freedom in seeing yourself beyond the shifting qualities that usually bind you.
dheesh_gita::115.detailed_meaning: Shri Dheesh explains that when someone perceives their own nature through its three aspects—often referring to the three qualities or modes of the natural world—they do not become entangled or limited by those qualities. This teaching shows a way to transcend the usual bindings of nature by clear understanding.
dheesh_gita::115.modern_relevance: When you notice your moods, habits, and reactions but see them as parts of you—not all of you—you gain freedom from their grip.
dheesh_gita::115.insight: It teaches you to recognize your true self beyond temporary traits, freeing your mind from reactive patterns.

dheesh_gita::116.verse_sanskrit:
मामकीनं स्वकीयञ्च गृहीत्वाऽऽदर्शमुत्तमम् ।
ममैषा प्रकृतिविषा: ! संसारेऽपारसीमाने ॥
dheesh_gita::116.verse_hindi: हे विप्रो ! मेरे और अपने उदाहरण को लेकर मेरी यह प्रकृति अपार संसार में
dheesh_gita::116.english_translation: O wise one! Taking my example and your own, this nature of mine is the poison that limits the boundless world.
dheesh_gita::116.translation_literal: मामकीनं (mine) स्वकीयञ्च (own) गृहीत्वाऽऽदर्शमुत्तमम् (taking as the highest example) । ममैषा (this mine) प्रकृतिविषा: (nature is poison) ! संसारेऽपारसीमाने (in the boundless world limiting) ॥
dheesh_gita::116.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::116.essence: Your own nature can act like poison that limits the boundless world.
dheesh_gita::116.simple_meaning: Your own nature can act like poison, limiting the vastness of existence around you.
dheesh_gita::116.simple_insight: You may feel trapped by your own nature, but recognizing it is the first step to freedom.
dheesh_gita::116.detailed_meaning: A teacher addresses a wise listener, explaining how their own nature acts like poison, restricting the infinite world. This reveals how personal tendencies can limit perception and freedom in life.
dheesh_gita::116.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck or limited, it often comes from your own habits and reactions narrowing your experience.
dheesh_gita::116.insight: It shifts your view to see your natural tendencies as the real limits, not the outside world.

dheesh_gita::117.verse_sanskrit:
नारीधारां नृधाराश्च प्रोत्पाद्य विश्वमश्नुते ।
अतो धाराद्वयेऽस्मिश्च बन्धमोक्षदशाद्वयम् ॥
dheesh_gita::117.verse_hindi: स्त्रीधारा और पुरुषधारा को उत्पन्न करके जगत को परिव्याप्त करती है इस कारण इन दोनों धाराओ में बन्धन दशा और मुक्तदशा इन दोनों की चरितार्थक विचार से
dheesh_gita::117.english_translation: By manifesting the feminine and masculine currents, the universe is pervaded; thus these two currents embody the states of bondage and liberation.
dheesh_gita::117.translation_literal: नारीधारां (feminine current) / नृधाराश्च (masculine current) / प्रोत्पाद्य (having generated) / विश्वमश्नुते (the universe pervades) / अतः (therefore) / धाराद्वयेऽस्मि (in these two currents) / च (and) / बन्धमोक्षदशाद्वयम् (the two states of bondage and liberation)
dheesh_gita::117.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::117.essence: Two fundamental forces underlie existence—one binds, the other frees.
dheesh_gita::117.simple_meaning: The universe is shaped by two forces, often understood as feminine and masculine currents, which represent the states of being bound and being free.
dheesh_gita::117.simple_insight: You exist within currents that both limit and liberate you simultaneously.
dheesh_gita::117.detailed_meaning: This verse explains how the universe is pervaded by two fundamental currents, symbolized as feminine and masculine energies, representing the opposing experiences of bondage and freedom. It points to the dynamic interplay that shapes existence and spiritual states.
dheesh_gita::117.modern_relevance: You might feel torn between pressures that keep you stuck and impulses urging you toward freedom and growth.
dheesh_gita::117.insight: It helps you see your life as a balance of forces: some that restrict and others that release, shifting your perspective from struggle to flow.

dheesh_gita::118.verse_sanskrit:
कर्तुं सार्थकमेवास्ति द्विधा भावत्रयं खलु ।
स्पृष्ठेर्दशायां दम्पत्योः क्षेत्रवीजे महर्षयः ! ॥
dheesh_gita::118.verse_hindi: निश्चय ही त्रिभाव के दो भेद हैं। हे महर्षिगण ! सृष्टि दशा में स्त्री और पुरुष में क्षेत्र और बीज
dheesh_gita::118.english_translation: There are indeed two distinctions in the threefold states: in the state of creation, between the female and male as field and seed, O great sages!
dheesh_gita::118.translation_literal: कर्तुं (to do) सार्थकमेवास्ति (is truly meaningful) द्विधा (in two ways) भावत्रयं (the threefold states) खलु (indeed) । स्पृष्टेर्दशायां (in the state of creation) दम्पत्योः (of the couple) क्षेत्रवीजे (field and seed) महर्षयः (great sages) !
dheesh_gita::118.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::118.essence: Creation unfolds through two complementary principles: the receptive field and the active seed.
dheesh_gita::118.simple_meaning: The three states of existence have two distinct forms, especially seen in creation as female and male, symbolized as field and seed.
dheesh_gita::118.simple_insight: Understanding dual distinctions within creation helps clarify how life unfolds between complementary forces.
dheesh_gita::118.detailed_meaning: Addressing great sages, the verse explains that the threefold states of existence have two distinct aspects, particularly in the creative phase where female and male represent the field and the seed, foundational for life.
dheesh_gita::118.insight: It invites you to recognize dual complementary roles in creation as fundamental to all life processes.

dheesh_gita::119.verse_sanskrit:
अधिभूतं तथा चास्ते पितरस्त्वाधिदैवतम् ।
भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः ॥
dheesh_gita::119.verse_hindi: अधिभूत, पितृगण अधिदैव और वहां भूतभावोद्भवकर विसर्गरूपी कर्म
dheesh_gita::119.english_translation: There is the physical nature, the ancestors as the presiding spirits, and the karmic energy that arises from the state of beings.
dheesh_gita::119.translation_literal: अधिभूतं (physical nature) / तथा (also) / चास्ते (there is) / पितरः (ancestors) / त्व् (as) / अधिदैवतम् (presiding spirits) / भूतभावोद्भवकरः (arising from the state of beings) / विसर्गः (energy/release) / कर्मसंज्ञितः (called karma)
dheesh_gita::119.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::119.essence: Actions arise from the physical world, ancestral forces, and living energy combined.
dheesh_gita::119.simple_meaning: Actions come from three sources: the physical world, inherited influences from ancestors, and the energy born from the state of all beings.
dheesh_gita::119.simple_insight: You are connected to a living flow of nature, heritage, and energetic consequence.
dheesh_gita::119.detailed_meaning: This verse explains that action (karma) is not isolated but comes from three layers: the natural physical world (adhibhuta), the ancestral or spiritual influences (adhidaiva), and the energy generated by the state of living beings. These combine to shape how karma arises.
dheesh_gita::119.modern_relevance: When you act, your choices reflect who you are physically, your inherited background, and the invisible energy of your environment.
dheesh_gita::119.insight: It teaches you to see your actions as the result of interconnected layers beyond just yourself, broadening perspective on responsibility.

dheesh_gita::120.verse_sanskrit:
अध्यात्म प्रोच्यते तत्र नात्र कश्चन संशयः ।
मुक्तेदशायां दम्पत्योमल्लिङ्गं प्रकृतिश्च मे ॥
dheesh_gita::120.verse_hindi: अध्यात्म कहा जाता है इसमें कुछ संदेह नहीं और मुकिदशा में स्त्री और पुरुष में मेरी प्रकृति और मेरा लिंगरूप
dheesh_gita::120.english_translation: There is no doubt that this is called spiritual knowledge, and in the state of freedom, my nature and my form are like the union of male and female.
dheesh_gita::120.translation_literal: अध्यात्म (spiritual knowledge) / प्रोच्यते (is called) / तत्र (there) / नात्र (not here) / कश्चन (anyone) / संशयः (doubt) / मुक्तेदशायां (in the state of freedom) / दम्पत्यो (of the couple) / मल्लिङ्गं (union) / प्रकृतिश्च (and nature) / मे (my)
dheesh_gita::120.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::120.essence: True freedom reveals your nature as a harmonious union beyond duality.
dheesh_gita::120.simple_meaning: Spiritual knowledge is certain and clear, showing that in freedom, the true nature is a union like male and female together.
dheesh_gita::120.simple_insight: Your deepest nature is not separate but a harmonious union beyond opposites.
dheesh_gita::120.detailed_meaning: The verse teaches that spiritual knowledge is unquestionable and that in the state of inner freedom, the true nature of the self is like the union of male and female, symbolizing a complete harmony beyond duality.
dheesh_gita::120.modern_relevance: When you feel torn between conflicting parts of yourself, remember your true nature is a balanced union beyond any division.
dheesh_gita::120.insight: It shifts your view from seeing identity as divided to recognizing wholeness beyond opposites.

dheesh_gita::121.verse_sanskrit:
अधिभूतं तथास्ते सच्चिद्भावावधिदैवतम् ।
परमानन्द एवास्ति तत्राध्यात्म न संशयः ॥
dheesh_gita::121.verse_hindi: अधिभूत, मेरा सत् और चिदभाव अधिदैव और वहाँ  निःसन्देह परमानन्द ही अध्यात्म है
dheesh_gita::121.english_translation: The supreme reality in you is the natural world, pure consciousness, and the divine principle; beyond doubt, supreme bliss is the inner truth.
dheesh_gita::121.translation_literal: अधिभूतं (natural world) / तथास्ते (also is) / सच्चिद्भावावधिदैवतम् (pure consciousness and divine principle) / परमानन्द (supreme bliss) / एवास्ति (indeed is) / तत्र (there) / अध्यात्म (inner truth) / न (no) / संशयः (doubt)
dheesh_gita::121.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::121.essence: You are fundamentally the natural world, pure awareness, and supreme bliss without doubt.
dheesh_gita::121.simple_meaning: You are made of the natural world, pure consciousness, and the divine principle, and your true self is supreme joy without doubt.
dheesh_gita::121.simple_insight: Recognizing your unity with nature, consciousness, and joy brings deep peace and confidence.
dheesh_gita::121.detailed_meaning: This verse explains the threefold nature within: the physical world (Adhibhuta), pure consciousness (Satchidbhava), and the divine principle (Adhidaivata). It affirms that supreme bliss represents the inner truth, leaving no room for doubt.
dheesh_gita::121.modern_relevance: When life feels fragmented, remembering you are nature, awareness, and joy can restore balance and clarity.
dheesh_gita::121.insight: It shifts your view from separation to seeing yourself as a unified presence of nature, awareness, and bliss.

dheesh_gita::122.verse_sanskrit:
ब्राह्मणा: !  इत्यमेवाहं त्रिभावैर्दैशकालयोः।
पात्रेऽपि दर्शनं दत्त्वा स्वभक्तान ज्ञानिनो ध्रुवम् ॥
dheesh_gita::122.verse_hindi: हे ब्राह्मणों! मैं इसी प्रकार सब देश काल और पात्रो में त्रिभावों से दर्शन देकर प्रकृति के धन से अपने ज्ञानी भक्तों को
dheesh_gita::122.english_translation: O Brahmins! In all lands, times, and forms, I reveal myself through three modes, granting true knowledge to my devoted seekers.
dheesh_gita::122.translation_literal: ब्राह्मणा: (O Brahmins) ! (exclamation) इत्य (thus) एव (indeed) अहं (I) त्रिभावैः (by three modes) दैशकालयोः (of country, time) पात्रेऽपि (even in forms) दर्शनं (appearance) दत्त्वा (giving) स्वभक्तान् (own devotees) ज्ञानिनः (the wise) ध्रुवम् (certainly)
dheesh_gita::122.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::122.essence: The divine reveals itself in many forms to guide devoted seekers to true knowledge.
dheesh_gita::122.simple_meaning: The divine appears in all places, times, and forms through three modes to grant true knowledge to devoted seekers.
dheesh_gita::122.simple_insight: The divine meets you wherever you are, in the way you can understand.
dheesh_gita::122.detailed_meaning: The speaker addresses Brahmins, explaining how the divine manifests across different countries, eras, and forms through three modes, always providing true knowledge to devoted and wise followers.
dheesh_gita::122.insight: It shows that the divine presence is accessible in many ways, tailored to the seeker’s readiness.

dheesh_gita::123.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकृतेर्वन्धनान्नूनं मोचयामि न संशयः।
एतद्गहरहस्यं यः कथितं विमपुङ्गवाः ॥
dheesh_gita::123.verse_hindi: निश्चय ही बचाया करता हूँ इसमें सन्देह नहीं ! हे ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठो ! मैंने आपलोगों से यह गूढ रहस्य कहा है
dheesh_gita::123.english_translation: I certainly liberate from the bonds of nature, there is no doubt. O best of Brahmins, I have revealed this profound secret to you.
dheesh_gita::123.translation_literal: प्रकृतेर्वन्धनान्नूनं (from nature's bonds certainly) मोचयामि (I liberate) न (not) संशयः (doubt). एतद्गहरहस्यं (this profound secret) यः (who) कथितं (spoken) विमपुङ्गवाः (O best Brahmins).
dheesh_gita::123.speaker: Teacher
dheesh_gita::123.essence: Freedom from nature’s bonds is certain and this profound secret has been revealed.
dheesh_gita::123.simple_meaning: There is no doubt that I free you from the bonds of the natural world. I have shared this deep secret with you.
dheesh_gita::123.simple_insight: You can feel certain that liberation from natural limitations is possible and has been revealed to you.
dheesh_gita::123.detailed_meaning: The Teacher promises Arjuna and the Brahmins that liberation from the binding forces of nature is certain. This moment reveals a profound secret crucial to escaping reactivity and limitation inherent in the natural world.
dheesh_gita::123.modern_relevance: When you feel trapped by your habits or circumstances, this verse reminds you true freedom beyond those limits is possible and certain.
dheesh_gita::123.insight: It shifts your view from feeling stuck in nature’s cycles to knowing liberation is accessible and assured.

dheesh_gita::124.verse_sanskrit:
शुद्धभावमयो यश्च पूर्णशक्तिप्रकाशकः ।
ओतत्सदिति मन्त्रों हि मद्भावत्रयवाचकः ॥
dheesh_gita::124.verse_hindi: शुद्ध भावमय पूर्ण शक्ति प्रकाशक जो मेरे तीनों भावों का पाचक ॐ ततसत मन्त्र है
dheesh_gita::124.english_translation: The pure state filled with complete power that illuminates is the sacred Om Tat Sat mantra representing my three aspects.
dheesh_gita::124.translation_literal: शुद्धभावमयो (pure state filled) / यश्च (and who) / पूर्णशक्तिप्रकाशकः (full power illuminator) / ओतत्सदिति (Om Tat Sat) / मन्त्रों (mantras) / हि (indeed) / मद्भावत्रयवाचकः (my three aspects indicatives)
dheesh_gita::124.speaker: Shambhu Dheesh
dheesh_gita::124.essence: Om Tat Sat mantra embodies and reveals pure power in three unified aspects.
dheesh_gita::124.simple_meaning: The sacred Om Tat Sat mantra expresses the pure and complete power of my threefold nature.
dheesh_gita::124.simple_insight: You sense a deep, radiant power that unites three essential aspects of being.
dheesh_gita::124.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the divine teacher explains that the mantra Om Tat Sat embodies a pure, illuminating power representing three fundamental aspects of the divine nature, revealing an essential truth beyond ordinary words.
dheesh_gita::124.modern_relevance: When you chant or hear Om Tat Sat, you connect to a deep source of pure power that integrates many parts of yourself.
dheesh_gita::124.insight: It invites you to recognize how a simple mantra can hold vast, unified power beyond surface appearances.

dheesh_gita::125.verse_hindi: उसका निरन्तर जप और उसके अर्थी की भावना द्वारा ज्ञान निष्णात और मन्त्रतत्व परायण मेरे भक्तो को
dheesh_gita::125.english_translation: The continuous disciplined practice and heartfelt understanding of meaning by my devoted followers who are skilled in knowledge and dedicated to mantra essence.
dheesh_gita::125.translation_literal: भावना (feeling) / अभि (towards) / तद् (that) / अर्थानां (meanings) / तपः (disciplined practice) / च (and) / निरन्तरम् (continuous) / मद्-भक्ता (my devotees) / अज्ञान-निष्णातैः (knowledge-skilled) / मन्त्र-तत्व-परायणैः (dedicated to mantra essence)
dheesh_gita::125.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::125.essence: Continuous disciplined effort with heartfelt meaning leads to mastery and deep understanding.
dheesh_gita::125.simple_meaning: Steady, continuous effort combined with sincere feeling leads to deep mastery and understanding.
dheesh_gita::125.simple_insight: You feel empowered when disciplined effort and heartfelt focus bring clarity.
dheesh_gita::125.detailed_meaning: This verse praises those who combine continuous disciplined effort (tapas) with heartfelt understanding of the meaning behind their practice, especially those skilled in knowledge and dedicated to mantra essence, highlighting how inner devotion and steady effort cultivate mastery.
dheesh_gita::125.modern_relevance: You keep returning to your practice, even when results seem slow, because you trust that steady effort and heartfelt focus will deepen your understanding.
dheesh_gita::125.insight: It teaches you to combine consistent effort with sincere feeling to unlock deeper wisdom and skill.

dheesh_gita::126.verse_hindi: अविभक्त ज्ञान पूर्ण अन्तर्दृष्टि प्राप्त होती है। मेरे ही सत् चित् और आनन्द इन तीनों भावों को आश्रय करके
dheesh_gita::126.english_translation: Undivided, full knowledge arises from the unity of my truth, consciousness, and bliss.
dheesh_gita::126.translation_literal: अविभक्तज्ञानपूर्णा (undivided knowledge-full) तैरन्तदृष्टिराप्यते (from these arises vision) । ममैव (my own) सच्चिदानन्द (truth-consciousness-bliss) भावत्रयसमाश्रयात् (because of the support of the three states) ॥
dheesh_gita::126.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::126.essence: Complete insight arises from embracing truth, awareness, and joy as one.
dheesh_gita::126.simple_meaning: Complete and undivided insight arises when truth, awareness, and joy are experienced as one within you.
dheesh_gita::126.simple_insight: You can feel the deep peace of knowing everything as one unified reality.
dheesh_gita::126.detailed_meaning: Shri Dheesh explains that when the three qualities—truth (Sat), consciousness (Chit), and bliss (Ananda)—are united and embraced together, a complete, undivided knowledge or inner vision naturally arises.
dheesh_gita::126.modern_relevance: When you connect your authentic self with clear awareness and genuine joy, you naturally see your life and choices with clarity and completeness.
dheesh_gita::126.insight: It teaches you to recognize that true wisdom comes from experiencing truth, awareness, and joy as inseparable.

dheesh_gita::127.verse_sanskrit:
नन्नध्यात्माधिदेवाधिभूतरूपं महर्षयः ।
भावत्रयं हि सर्वस्मिन् कार्यव्रह्मणि भासते ॥
dheesh_gita::127.verse_hindi: हे महर्षियों ! अध्यात्म अधिदैव और अधिभूतरूपी त्रिभाव सम्पूर्ण कार्य ब्रह्म में निश्चय ही प्रकट हैं
dheesh_gita::127.english_translation: O great sages, the three aspects of self, divine, and nature are indeed revealed in the complete supreme reality of action.
dheesh_gita::127.translation_literal: न न (not not) अध्यात्म (self) अधिदेव (divine) अधिभूत (nature) रूपं (form) महर्षयः (great sages) । भावत्रयं (three aspects) हि (indeed) सर्वस्मिन् (in all) कार्यब्रह्मणि (in the supreme reality of action) भासते (shines) ॥
dheesh_gita::127.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::127.essence: Self, divine, and nature reveal themselves as one in the supreme reality of action.
dheesh_gita::127.simple_meaning: The three fundamental aspects—your true self, the divine presence, and the natural world—are all expressed in the supreme reality behind every action.
dheesh_gita::127.simple_insight: You are not separate from the divine or nature; all three live through your actions.
dheesh_gita::127.detailed_meaning: The verse addresses great sages, explaining that the threefold nature—self (Atman), divine (Adhideva), and nature (Adhibhuta)—are revealed as one unified reality in the supreme principle that underlies all actions. This teaching points to the essential unity behind apparent diversity.
dheesh_gita::127.modern_relevance: When you act, recognize that your true self, the divine, and the natural world are not separate but interwoven in what you do.
dheesh_gita::127.insight: It teaches you to see your actions as expressions of an integrated reality beyond separation.

dheesh_gita::128.verse_sanskrit:
दृश्य नातो भवेद किश्चिच्छून्यं भावत्रयेण वै ॥
प्राप्य भक्ते पराकाष्ठां ज्ञानयोगान्तिमस्थलीम् ॥
dheesh_gita::128.verse_hindi: इस कारण त्रिभाव से रहित कोई दृश्य हो ही नहीं सका । मेरे ज्ञानी भक्त जब ज्ञानयोग की अन्तिम स्थलरूपा भक्ति की पराकाष्ठा को प्राप्त करके
dheesh_gita::128.english_translation: Therefore, nothing can be seen without the threefold nature; my wise devotees reach the highest peak of devotion, the final stage of Jnana Yoga.
dheesh_gita::128.translation_literal: दृश्य (visible) न (not) आतः (from) भवेत् (can be) कश्चित् (anyone) शून्यम् (void) भावत्रयेण (by threefold nature) वै (indeed) ॥ प्राप्य (attaining) भक्ते (devotee) पराकाष्ठां (highest point) ज्ञानयोगान्तिम् (final of knowledge yoga) स्थलीम् (stage/place) ॥
dheesh_gita::128.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::128.essence: True wisdom culminates in the highest devotion beyond mere knowledge.
dheesh_gita::128.simple_meaning: Nothing can be truly seen without the threefold nature of existence. The wisest devotees reach the highest devotion, which is the final stage of wisdom practice.
dheesh_gita::128.simple_insight: You realize that deep knowledge naturally leads to the highest devotion, completing your inner journey.
dheesh_gita::128.detailed_meaning: The verse explains that nothing is visible without the interplay of the three fundamental qualities (gunas). It teaches that wise devotees who pursue knowledge ultimately reach the peak of devotion, which represents the final stage in the path of knowledge yoga, blending wisdom and love.
dheesh_gita::128.modern_relevance: You might master a skill or study deeply, but without heartfelt commitment and love, your understanding feels incomplete.
dheesh_gita::128.insight: It shifts how you see wisdom—from pure intellect to a fullness completed by devoted love.

dheesh_gita::129.verse_sanskrit:
यदा मे ज्ञानिनो भक्ता मां द्रष्टुं शक्नुवन्ति ह ।
सर्वेषु देशकालेषु तदा भावत्रयं मम ॥
dheesh_gita::129.verse_hindi: मेरे दर्शन करने में समर्थ होते हैं तब वह सब देश और काल में मेरे त्रिभाव का
dheesh_gita::129.english_translation: When the wise devotees can truly see me everywhere and at all times, then my threefold nature is revealed.
dheesh_gita::129.translation_literal: यदा (when) मे (my) ज्ञानिनो (wise ones) भक्ता (devotees) मां (me) द्रष्टुं (to see) शक्नुवन्ति (are able) ह (indeed) । सर्वेषु (in all) देशकालेषु (places and times) तदा (then) भावत्रयं (threefold nature) मम (my) ॥
dheesh_gita::129.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::129.essence: True devotion reveals the divine's presence across all places and times.
dheesh_gita::129.simple_meaning: When wise devotees truly perceive the divine, they see the divine's presence everywhere and at every time, revealing its threefold nature.
dheesh_gita::129.simple_insight: You can feel the divine is always near, in every place and moment.
dheesh_gita::129.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the teacher explains that when wise devotees attain true vision, they recognize the divine's presence everywhere and at all times, understanding its threefold nature beyond space and time.
dheesh_gita::129.modern_relevance: You notice a moment when your love or faith makes you feel connected everywhere you go and at every time, as if nothing is separate.
dheesh_gita::129.insight: It invites you to recognize the divine's constant presence beyond limits of place or time, deepening your devotional connection.

dheesh_gita::130.verse_sanskrit:
भवन्त्यनुभवन्तस्ते मच्चिता नात्र संशयः ।
अघट्यघटनायां या प्रकृति पटीयसी ॥
dheesh_gita::130.verse_hindi: अनुभव करते हुए निःसन्देह मद्गतचित्त हो जाते हैं। उस समय अघटन घटना पटीयसी
dheesh_gita::130.english_translation: Those who experience become undoubtedly absorbed in me; during the unfolding of events, that nature prevails.
dheesh_gita::130.translation_literal: भवन्ति (become) अनुभवन्तः (experiencing) ते (those) मच्चिता (mind fixed on me) न (not) अत्र (here) संशयः (doubt) । अघट्य (eventless) अघटना (event) याः (which) प्रकृति (nature) पटीयसी (prevails) ॥
dheesh_gita::130.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::130.essence: True trust arises naturally when your heart fully experiences the divine without doubt.
dheesh_gita::130.simple_meaning: When you deeply experience your connection with the divine, your mind becomes free of doubt and fully trusting.
dheesh_gita::130.simple_insight: You feel a calm certainty when your heart is fully engaged with the divine presence.
dheesh_gita::130.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the speaker explains that those who genuinely experience the divine presence become fully absorbed and free from doubt. This trust arises naturally during the unfolding of life’s events, showing how inner connection grows through lived experience.
dheesh_gita::130.modern_relevance: You’ve faced uncertainty but found moments when your trust felt rock solid, even without proof—this is that trust growing.
dheesh_gita::130.insight: The verse teaches you to let lived experience build your trust in the divine, moving beyond intellectual doubts.

dheesh_gita::131.verse_sanskrit:
सा त्रैगुण्यमयी देवी तमःसत्त्वरजोऽभिधैः ।
त्रिभिगुणैस्तदा नालं बद्धं भक्तान मम प्रियान् ॥
dheesh_gita::131.verse_hindi: त्रिगुणमयी मेरी प्रकृति देवी सत्त्व रज और तमरूपी तीनों गुणों से मेरे भक्तों को बन्धन करने में असमर्थ हो जाती है।
dheesh_gita::131.english_translation: My nature, composed of the three qualities—goodness, passion, and ignorance—cannot bind my devoted followers.
dheesh_gita::131.translation_literal: सा (she/that) त्रैगुण्यमयी (composed of three qualities) देवी (divine feminine) तमःसत्त्वरजोऽभिधैः (by ignorance, goodness, passion - ablative) त्रिभिगुणैः (threefold qualities) तदा (then) नालं (not at all) बद्धं (bound) भक्तान (devotees) मम (my) प्रियान् (dear ones)
dheesh_gita::131.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::131.essence: Devoted love transcends the three qualities and cannot be bound by nature’s forces.
dheesh_gita::131.simple_meaning: Your devoted love goes beyond the three qualities of nature and cannot be held back or bound by them.
dheesh_gita::131.simple_insight: You feel safe knowing your devotion makes you free no matter what pulls try to bind you.
dheesh_gita::131.detailed_meaning: The speaker explains how their nature is made of three fundamental qualities—goodness, passion, and ignorance. Yet, these qualities cannot bind those who are devoted to them, showing the unique power of devoted love to transcend natural limitations.
dheesh_gita::131.modern_relevance: When you commit fully to something meaningful, distractions and doubts lose their grip and cannot stop your progress.
dheesh_gita::131.insight: It shifts your focus from being trapped by fluctuating moods to trusting the steady power of devotion.

dheesh_gita::132.verse_sanskrit:
अहो मत्प्रकृतिश्चैव विद्यारूपं समाश्रिता।
नयते ज्ञानिनो भक्तान् मत्सायुज्यं न संशयः ॥
dheesh_gita::132.verse_hindi: अहो ! मेरी प्रकृति ही विद्यारूप धारण करके ज्ञानी भक्तो को मत्सायुज्य प्राप्त कराती है, इसमें सन्वेह नहीं
dheesh_gita::132.english_translation: Ah! My nature itself, assuming the form of knowledge, leads wise devotees to union with me without doubt.
dheesh_gita::132.translation_literal: अहो (ah) / मत् (my) / प्रकृतिश्चैव (nature itself) / विद्यारूपं (knowledge-form) / समाश्रिता (assuming) / नयते (leads) / ज्ञानिनः (wise devotees) / भक्तान् (devotees) / मत्सायुज्यं (union with me) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
dheesh_gita::132.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::132.essence: Your nature as inner wisdom naturally guides devoted seekers to assured union without doubt.
dheesh_gita::132.simple_meaning: Your true nature takes the form of knowledge and leads devoted seekers to assured union with the divine.
dheesh_gita::132.simple_insight: You can trust that your inner wisdom naturally draws you toward deep connection without doubt.
dheesh_gita::132.detailed_meaning: Here, Shri Dheesh reveals that his very nature manifests as knowledge which guides wise devotees steadily toward union with him, affirming that this path is certain and free of hesitation.
dheesh_gita::132.modern_relevance: When you follow your inner wisdom, even amidst confusion, it steadily brings you closer to what you truly seek without second-guessing.
dheesh_gita::132.insight: It teaches you to trust your own knowledge as the reliable path to deep connection and fulfillment.

dheesh_gita::133.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञात्वा लोकोत्तरं दिव्यं तत्त्वातीतं कृपानिधे!।
परतत्वात्मकं सम्यक् स्वरूपं ते यथार्थतः ॥
dheesh_gita::133.verse_hindi: हे कृपानिधे ! आपके लोकोत्तर दिव्य और तत्त्वातीत परम तत्त्वरूपी स्वरुप को यथार्थ रूप से
dheesh_gita::133.english_translation: Knowing your divine, transcendental nature beyond all worlds, the true supreme reality as it is.
dheesh_gita::133.translation_literal: ज्ञात्वा (knowing) / लोकोत्तरं (beyond the worlds) / दिव्यं (divine) / तत्त्वातीतं (beyond the principle) / कृपानिधे (O treasure of compassion) / परतत्वात्मकं (supreme nature) / सम्यक् (correctly) / स्वरूपं (form) / ते (your) / यथार्थतः (truly)
dheesh_gita::133.speaker: Guru
dheesh_gita::133.essence: Your true nature transcends all worlds and is the supreme reality itself.
dheesh_gita::133.simple_meaning: You can recognize your true self as divine and beyond all worldly limitations, the supreme reality itself.
dheesh_gita::133.simple_insight: You carry within you a vast, unchanging reality beyond everyday appearances.
dheesh_gita::133.detailed_meaning: The Guru addresses the compassionate student, revealing that their true essence is beyond the physical world and concepts. This teaching points to recognizing the supreme reality within oneself as it truly is.
dheesh_gita::133.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by daily chaos, remembering your deeper, unchanging nature can bring calm and perspective.
dheesh_gita::133.insight: It guides you to see beyond surface distractions and identify with your highest, unchanging truth.

dheesh_gita::134.verse_hindi: भलीभांति जानकर और सम्पूर्ण दृश्य प्रपञ्च समूह में परिव्याप्त आपके त्रिभावात्मक स्वरुप का परम अद्भुत रहस्य
dheesh_gita::134.english_translation: Fully understanding and pervading all that is visible, the supreme wondrous secret is the threefold nature of your true self.
dheesh_gita::134.translation_literal: दृश्यम् (visible) अप्रपञ्चन (not illusion) जाञ्च (knowing) च (and) परिव्याप्नुवतः (pervading) अखिलम् (all) । त्रिभावात्मकरूपस्य (of the threefold-nature true self) रहस्यं (secret) परमाद्भुतम् (supreme wondrous) ॥
dheesh_gita::134.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::134.essence: Your true self is a wondrous secret fully present in three interwoven forms.
dheesh_gita::134.simple_meaning: Your true self has three aspects that fully pervade all visible reality, revealing a supreme and wondrous secret.
dheesh_gita::134.simple_insight: Knowing your threefold nature opens a deep awe and connection within you.
dheesh_gita::134.detailed_meaning: The verse reveals the profound teaching that the true self exists simultaneously in three forms, fully present throughout all that is seen. This secret is central to understanding the nature of existence and self, pointing to a wondrous interconnectedness beyond illusion.
dheesh_gita::134.modern_relevance: When you recognize your mind, body, and deeper awareness as one whole, you find a richer, more wondrous sense of who you truly are.
dheesh_gita::134.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as separate parts to knowing the unified, threefold nature of your being.

dheesh_gita::135.verse_sanskrit:
समाकर्ण्य वयं जाताः कृतकृत्या न संशयः ।
किन्त्यन्यदेव नो जातं परं कौतूहलं ह्रदि ॥
dheesh_gita::135.verse_hindi: सुनकर हम निस्सन्देह कृतकृत्य हुए है; परन्तु हमारे हृदय में एक अन्य ही महान् कौतूहल (आश्चर्य) उत्पन्न हुआ है
dheesh_gita::135.english_translation: Hearing this, we are surely fulfilled; yet another great wonder has arisen in our hearts.
dheesh_gita::135.translation_literal: समाकर्ण्य (having heard) / वयं (we) / जाताः (have become) / कृतकृत्या (fulfilled) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt) / किन्तु (but) / अन्यदेव (indeed another) / नः (our) / जातं (arisen) / परं (great) / कौतूहलं (wonder) / ह्रदि (in the heart)
dheesh_gita::135.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::135.essence: Satisfaction with understanding can coexist with fresh, deeper curiosity.
dheesh_gita::135.simple_meaning: We have heard and feel satisfied, but a new, deeper curiosity has appeared in our hearts.
dheesh_gita::135.simple_insight: Sometimes, understanding one thing leads to new deeper questions inside.
dheesh_gita::135.detailed_meaning: After hearing a teaching, the listeners express certainty and satisfaction, yet they reveal a fresh, profound wonder has arisen within them, indicating ongoing inquiry.
dheesh_gita::135.modern_relevance: You finish reading something that answers a question, but suddenly a new deeper question emerges inside you.
dheesh_gita::135.insight: Recognize that learning often opens new questions instead of closing them, inviting ongoing exploration.

dheesh_gita::136.verse_sanskrit:
पश्यामः साम्प्रतं सप्त-ज्ञानभूमेरुपर्यो ।
भवन्तं सुखमासीनं सुरम्ये कमलासने ॥
dheesh_gita::136.verse_hindi: अहो ! इस समय हम देख रहे हैं कि सप्त ज्ञानभूमि के ऊपर सुरम्य कमल पर आप सुखपूर्वक आसीन है
dheesh_gita::136.english_translation: Behold now, we see you peacefully seated on the beautiful lotus above the seven realms of knowledge.
dheesh_gita::136.translation_literal: पश्यामः (we see) साम्प्रतं (now) सप्त-ज्ञानभूमेर् (on seven knowledge-lands) उपर्यो (above) भवन्तं (you) सुखमासीनं (peacefully seated) सुरम्ये (beautiful) कमलासने (on lotus seat)
dheesh_gita::136.speaker: Narrator
dheesh_gita::136.essence: A serene presence above profound realms draws focused attention now.
dheesh_gita::136.simple_meaning: We are currently seeing you sitting comfortably on a beautiful lotus above the seven realms of knowledge.
dheesh_gita::136.simple_insight: A calm, elevated presence can inspire awe and peaceful attention.
dheesh_gita::136.detailed_meaning: As the scene unfolds, the narrator describes someone peacefully seated on a beautiful lotus above seven realms of knowledge, setting the stage for a significant moment of spiritual teaching or revelation.
dheesh_gita::136.insight: This verse invites you to recognize moments of calm and elevated perspective before deep teaching begins.

dheesh_gita::137.verse_sanskrit:
धीश सर्वज्ञ ! सर्व्वात्मन्नासितस्यास्य ते विभो ।
सौन्दर्य कमलस्यास्ते वांगमनोबुद्धयगोचरम् ॥
dheesh_gita::137.verse_hindi: हे सर्वात्मन् ! हे। विभो! सर्वज्ञ धीश ! जिस पर आप बैठे हुए हैं, उस कमल का सौन्दर्य वाक्, मन और बुद्धि से अतीत है
dheesh_gita::137.english_translation: O all-knowing lord! The beauty of the lotus on which you sit is beyond speech, mind, and intellect.
dheesh_gita::137.translation_literal: धीश (lord) / सर्वज्ञ (all-knowing) / सर्व्वात्मन्नासितस्यास्य (of the one in whom all selves reside) / ते (your) / विभो (lord) / सौन्दर्य (beauty) / कमलस्य (of the lotus) / अस्ते (is) / ते (your) / वांग् (speech) / मनो (mind) / बुद्धि (intellect) / अगोचरम् (beyond perception)
dheesh_gita::137.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::137.essence: True beauty of the divine's seat transcends mind, speech, and intellect.
dheesh_gita::137.simple_meaning: The beauty of the lotus where the divine sits cannot be fully expressed by words, mind, or intellect.
dheesh_gita::137.simple_insight: Some beauties are beyond what your thoughts or words can capture.
dheesh_gita::137.detailed_meaning: A revered figure addresses the all-knowing divine, marveling that the beauty of the lotus seat surpasses all forms of mental and verbal expression, highlighting the divine's transcendence.
dheesh_gita::137.insight: It shows that some experiences or truths are beyond conceptual or verbal grasp.

dheesh_gita::138.verse_sanskrit:
शरीरं भवतो धीश ! रक्तवर्णमपि प्रभो!।
अतीतं सर्ववर्णेभ्यो रक्तादिभ्योऽधुनात्यलम् ॥
dheesh_gita::138.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो धीश ! आपके शरीर का वर्ण रक्त होने पर भी वह रक्त आदि सब रंगों से अतीत होकर
dheesh_gita::138.english_translation: O wise lord, your body, though of red color, surpasses all colors including red itself.
dheesh_gita::138.translation_literal: शरीरं (body) / भवतो (your) / धीश (lord) / रक्तवर्णमपि (even red color) / प्रभो (O lord) / अतीतं (beyond) / सर्ववर्णेभ्यो (all colors) / रक्तादिभ्योऽधुनात्यलम् (surpassing red and others)
dheesh_gita::138.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::138.essence: The visible form can transcend its ordinary colors and point to a higher reality.
dheesh_gita::138.simple_meaning: Your body is red, yet it goes beyond all colors, including red itself.
dheesh_gita::138.simple_insight: Sometimes what appears ordinary carries a depth that goes beyond appearances.
dheesh_gita::138.detailed_meaning: The verse addresses a wise lord, admiring how the body’s red color transcends all other colors, hinting at a deeper reality beyond physical forms.
dheesh_gita::138.insight: It invites seeing beyond surface appearances to the deeper essence that surpasses physical traits.

dheesh_gita::139.verse_sanskrit:
तर्पयत्यस्मदीयां वै रूपदर्शनलालसाम् ।
चक्रपद्मत्रिशूलैस्तु मोदकेन च भूपितैः ॥
dheesh_gita::139.verse_hindi: हमारी रूपदर्शन तृष्णा को इस समय भलीभांति तृप्त कर रहा है। अपने चक्र, पद्म, त्रिशूल और मोदकरूप दिव्यास्त्रो से विभूषित
dheesh_gita::139.english_translation: Right now, my desire to see forms is fully satisfied by the divine weapons adorned with the discus, lotus, trident, and mace.
dheesh_gita::139.translation_literal: तर्पयति (satisfies) अस्मदीयां (my) वै (indeed) रूपदर्शनलालसाम् (desire to see forms) । चक्रपद्मत्रिशूलैः (with discus, lotus, trident) तु (indeed) मोदकेन (by mace) च (and) भूपितैः (by weapons) ॥
dheesh_gita::139.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::139.essence: Seeing sacred symbols can satisfy a deep yearning for connection and meaning.
dheesh_gita::139.simple_meaning: At this moment, the speaker's desire to see divine forms is fully fulfilled by the sight of the divine weapons.
dheesh_gita::139.simple_insight: Sometimes, seeing symbols of power and beauty can deeply satisfy a restless longing.
dheesh_gita::139.detailed_meaning: The speaker expresses that their craving to witness divine manifestations is currently gratified by observing the divine weapons adorned with discus, lotus, trident, and mace, each symbolizing cosmic power and protection.
dheesh_gita::139.insight: It highlights how visual symbols can momentarily fulfill a deep desire for connection or understanding.

dheesh_gita::140.verse_sanskrit:
करैदिव्यैरेभिरस्वैर्भवान् नित्यं चतुर्भुजः ।
कैवल्याभ्युदयौ दातुमिवाश्वासयते च नः ॥
dheesh_gita::140.verse_hindi: आप चतुर्भुज होकर इन हाथो से अभ्युदय और निःश्रेयस प्रदान करने के लिये मानो हमको नित्य अशान्वित कर रहे हैं।
dheesh_gita::140.english_translation: You, with your four arms, act as if constantly assuring us of liberation and ultimate well-being.
dheesh_gita::140.translation_literal: करै (doing) / दिव्यैः (divine) / एभिः (by these) / अस्वैः (own hands) / भवान् (you) / नित्यम् (always) / चतुर्भुजः (four-armed) / कैवल्याभ्युदयौ (liberation and prosperity) / दातुम् (to give) / इव (as if) / आश्वासयते (assures) / च (and) / नः (us)
dheesh_gita::140.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::140.essence: A steady, divine presence acts constantly to assure your freedom and well-being.
dheesh_gita::140.simple_meaning: You appear as a four-armed being who constantly acts to assure us of freedom and the best outcome.
dheesh_gita::140.simple_insight: There is comfort in sensing a steady presence working for your highest freedom.
dheesh_gita::140.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the speaker perceives a four-armed divine figure whose actions seem to constantly promise liberation and well-being, offering reassurance amid uncertainty.
dheesh_gita::140.modern_relevance: When life feels overwhelming, sensing a steady force working for your true freedom can bring calm and trust.
dheesh_gita::140.insight: It invites you to trust in the steady support working beyond your view, easing your burden.

dheesh_gita::141.verse_sanskrit:
समाधत्ते च नो बुद्धिं भवान् भूत्वा गजाननः ।
उपदिष्टा वयं पूर्व भवता यत्ततस्तव ॥
dheesh_gita::141.verse_hindi: और आप गजवदन होकर हमारी बुद्धि को समाहित कर रहे हैं । आपने पहले जो हमें उपदेश दिया है उसके द्वारा
dheesh_gita::141.english_translation: And you, as Gajanan, are uniting our intellect; through your previous teachings.
dheesh_gita::141.translation_literal: समाधत्ते (unites) / च (and) / नो (our) / बुद्धिं (intellect) / भवान् (you) / भूत्वा (being) / गजाननः (Gajanan) / उपदिष्टा (taught) / वयं (we) / पूर्व (before) / भवता (by you) / यत्ततस्तव (that that is yours)
dheesh_gita::141.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::141.essence: The divine unites our intellect through past teachings already received.
dheesh_gita::141.simple_meaning: The divine Gajanan is uniting our intellect through the teachings you have given us before.
dheesh_gita::141.simple_insight: You feel your mind gathering focus through the guidance of prior instruction.
dheesh_gita::141.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the figure called Gajanan is said to be harmonizing the intellect of the listeners, building on the teachings previously shared, indicating a process of deepening understanding.
dheesh_gita::141.insight: It highlights how prior guidance shapes current mental clarity and focus.

dheesh_gita::142.verse_sanskrit:
ईशा ज्ञातुं स्वरूपस्य रहस्य यत्किमप्यहो ।
सुन्दरी लोहिताङ्गीन्तु भवद्वामाङ्कवत्तिनीम् ॥
dheesh_gita::142.verse_hindi: अहो ! हम आपके स्वरुप के रहस्य को तो यत्किञ्चित् समझने में समर्थ हुए हैं परन्तु आपके वाम-अंक-वर्तिनी
dheesh_gita::142.english_translation: Alas! We have somewhat understood the secret of your true nature, but your left side—adorned with a beautiful reddish form—remains unknown.
dheesh_gita::142.translation_literal: ईशा (divine lady) / ज्ञातुं (to know) / स्वरूपस्य (of the true nature) / रहस्य (secret) / यत्किमपि (something) / अहो (alas) / सुन्दरी (beautiful) / लोहिताङ्गी (red-bodied) / तु (but) / भवद्वामाङ्कवत्तिनीम् (your left side wearing)
dheesh_gita::142.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::142.essence: Partial understanding of the true self reveals mysteries that remain hidden and beautiful.
dheesh_gita::142.simple_meaning: Someone claims to have partly understood the secret of your true nature but is still puzzled by your left side's beautiful reddish form.
dheesh_gita::142.simple_insight: Some mysteries of the divine or true self remain beyond our current understanding.
dheesh_gita::142.detailed_meaning: A speaker expresses partial insight into the divine's true nature but confesses that certain aspects—specifically the beautiful reddish left side—remain mysterious, highlighting the depths still to be explored.
dheesh_gita::142.insight: It teaches that even deep understanding can leave some truths hidden, inviting humility and ongoing inquiry.

dheesh_gita::143.verse_sanskrit:
शंखक्त्यब्जचक्रातिीवभूषितचतुर्भुजाम् ।
यां विश्वमोहिनी देवीं षोडशी शक्तिशालिनीम् ॥
dheesh_gita::143.verse_hindi: शंख,चक्र शक्ति और पद्म से अति विभूषित चतुर्भजा लोहितवर्णांगी और शक्ति शालिनी षोडशी जगत् मोहिनी
dheesh_gita::143.english_translation: The sixteenth Shakti, adorned with conch, disc, and lotus, four-armed, radiant red, enchants the entire world.
dheesh_gita::143.translation_literal: शंखक्त्यब्जचक्रातिीवभूषितचतुर्भुजाम् (conch-lotus-disc-adorned four-armed) / यां (whom) / विश्वमोहिनी (world-enchanting) / देवीं (goddess) / षोडशी (sixteenth) / शक्तिशालिनीम् (powerful one)
dheesh_gita::143.speaker: Narrator
dheesh_gita::143.essence: A radiant divine power captivates the universe through symbolic adornment and presence.
dheesh_gita::143.simple_meaning: A powerful divine figure, the sixteenth Shakti, is described as richly adorned and captivating the whole world.
dheesh_gita::143.simple_insight: The image evokes awe and reverence for a radiant power that mesmerizes all.
dheesh_gita::143.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the narrator describes the sixteenth Shakti, a divine feminine power, richly decorated with symbolic items like conch, disc, and lotus, with four arms and a radiant red body that captivates the entire universe.
dheesh_gita::143.insight: Recognize that symbols convey deeper qualities of power and presence beyond the physical form.

dheesh_gita::144.verse_sanskrit:
पश्यामो वयमेतस्याः स्वरूपस्याधुनावधि।
नाज्ञासिष्म रहस्यं तत् कृपां कृत्वैव साम्प्रतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::144.verse_hindi: जिस देवी को हम लोग देखते हैं उनके स्वरुप का रहस्य अभी तक हमारे समझ में नहीं आया, इसलिये इस  समय कृपा करके ही
dheesh_gita::144.english_translation: We see this divine form, but its true nature remains unknown; only now has grace allowed some understanding.
dheesh_gita::144.translation_literal: पश्यामो (we see) / वयमेतस्याः (this) / स्वरूपस्य (of the form) / अधुनाऽवधि (until now) / नाज्ञासिष्म (we did not know) / रहस्यं (the secret) / तत् (that) / कृपां (grace) / कृत्वैव (having done) / साम्प्रतम् (just now)
dheesh_gita::144.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::144.essence: Some truths reveal themselves only when grace opens the way to understanding.
dheesh_gita::144.simple_meaning: We have seen the divine form, but its secret nature was not understood until now, only revealed through grace.
dheesh_gita::144.simple_insight: There is humility in realizing that some truths come only through grace and not through effort alone.
dheesh_gita::144.detailed_meaning: The speaker acknowledges seeing a divine form whose true nature remains a mystery. Until now, understanding was lacking, but through grace, some clarity is now possible.
dheesh_gita::144.modern_relevance: You encounter something profound that feels beyond your full understanding, yet a moment of openness or kindness reveals new meaning.
dheesh_gita::144.insight: Recognize that some deeper truths require openness and grace, not just personal effort, to become clear.

dheesh_gita::145.verse_sanskrit:
"कास्तेऽसौ? तत्स्वरुपं कि तद्रहस्यञ्च विस्तृतम् ।
व्यस्तो वर्णयित्वैतव कृतकृत्यान कुरुप्व नः ॥
dheesh_gita::145.verse_hindi: वे कौन हैं ? उनका स्वरूप क्या है? और उनका विस्तारित रहस्य क्या है ? सो विस्तार पूर्वक वर्णन करके हमको कृतकृत्य कीजिये।
dheesh_gita::145.english_translation: Who are they? What is their true nature? And what is their vast mystery? Please describe all this fully so we may be grateful.
dheesh_gita::145.translation_literal: कः (who) + अस्ति (is) + असौ (he/that) ? / तत् (that) + स्वरूपम् (true nature) / किम् (what) + तद् (that) + रहस्यञ्च (mystery and) + विस्तृतम् (extended) / व्यवस्थित (arranged) + वर्णयित्वा (describing) + एतव (this) + कृतकृत्यान (grateful) + कुरु (do) + नः (to us)
dheesh_gita::145.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::145.essence: Asking clearly about unknown beings and their deep nature opens the way to understanding.
dheesh_gita::145.simple_meaning: This verse asks who these beings are, what their true nature is, and requests a full explanation of their mystery with gratitude.
dheesh_gita::145.simple_insight: Curiosity opens the door to understanding what is hidden and profound.
dheesh_gita::145.detailed_meaning: The speaker questions the identity and true nature of certain beings, seeking a thorough explanation of their mysterious qualities, expressing readiness to receive this knowledge with gratitude.
dheesh_gita::145.insight: It encourages honest inquiry and openness before knowing, highlighting the value of clear explanation and gratitude.

dheesh_gita::146.verse_sanskrit:
शक्तिरेषा ममैवास्ते सर्वकार्यसहायिका।
सिद्धि नाम्ना च यामाहुब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः ॥
dheesh_gita::146.verse_hindi: मेरे सब कार्यों में सहायिका ये देवी मेरी ही शक्ति है, वेदज्ञ ब्राहण गण जिनका सिद्धि नाम से अभिहित करते हैं
dheesh_gita::146.english_translation: This power that assists me in all tasks is indeed mine; the wise who have transcended the Vedas call it Siddhi (accomplishment).
dheesh_gita::146.translation_literal: शक्तिरेषा (this power) मम (my) एव (indeed) अस्ते (exists) सर्वकार्यसहायिका (assistant in all tasks)। सिद्धि (Siddhi) नाम्ना (by the name) च (also) यामाः (they are called) ब्राह्मणा (brahmins) वेदपारगाः (transcended the Vedas) ॥
dheesh_gita::146.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::146.essence: The power that aids all your actions is truly your own inner strength.
dheesh_gita::146.simple_meaning: There is a power that helps you in every action, and it is truly yours. Wise teachers call this power 'Siddhi' or accomplishment.
dheesh_gita::146.simple_insight: You can feel supported by an inner power in everything you do.
dheesh_gita::146.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the speaker affirms that the energy assisting all actions is their own. Those who have mastered knowledge beyond the scriptures recognize this power as 'Siddhi', meaning accomplishment or success.
dheesh_gita::146.modern_relevance: When you face a challenge, remember the strength you rely on is your own inner power supporting you throughout.
dheesh_gita::146.insight: Recognize that the force enabling your success is your own power, not something external.

dheesh_gita::147.verse_sanskrit:
ममैव प्रकृतिविप्रा: ! सदा त्रैगुण्यशोभिता।
अत्यन्तं सा प्रसीदन्ती सिद्धिरूपञ्च विभ्रती ॥
dheesh_gita::147.verse_hindi: हे विप्रवृन्द ! मेरी त्रिगुणशोभित प्रकृति ही सिद्धिरूप धारण करके सदा मेरी सेवा में अति प्रसन्न होकर
dheesh_gita::147.english_translation: O wise ones! My nature, adorned by the three qualities, always serves me joyfully, embodying perfection.
dheesh_gita::147.translation_literal: ममैव (my own) / प्रकृतिविप्रा: (nature, wise ones) / सदा (always) / त्रैगुण्यशोभिता (adorned with three qualities) / अत्यन्तं (extremely) / सा (she) / प्रसीदन्ती (being pleased) / सिद्धिरूपञ्च (form of perfection) / विभ्रती (serving)
dheesh_gita::147.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::147.essence: Your nature joyfully serves the divine, embodying perfection through three qualities.
dheesh_gita::147.simple_meaning: Your nature, shaped by three qualities, naturally serves the divine with joy and perfection.
dheesh_gita::147.simple_insight: You can feel deep happiness when your actions flow from your true nature in service.
dheesh_gita::147.detailed_meaning: The divine teacher addresses the wise listeners, explaining that the natural world, influenced by three qualities, remains happily devoted and embodies perfection while serving the divine self fully.
dheesh_gita::147.modern_relevance: When your work or actions arise naturally from who you are, they feel joyful and fulfilling without struggle.
dheesh_gita::147.insight: Recognize and trust your natural tendencies as expressions of joyful, devoted service rather than resisting them.

dheesh_gita::148.verse_sanskrit:
सेवायां में रता निखं मामुपाश्रित्य राजते ।
पूर्णाङ्गललिता रम्या षोडशी सर्वसुन्दरी ॥
dheesh_gita::148.verse_hindi: रत रहती हुई निरन्तर मेरा आश्रय करके शोभायमान है। पुर्ण अवयव सुशोभित षोड़शी सर्व सौन्दर्य समन्विता
dheesh_gita::148.english_translation: She remains delighted in service, shining by taking refuge in me; a perfectly formed, charming sixteen-year-old, adorned with all beauty.
dheesh_gita::148.translation_literal: सेवायां (in service) में (in) रता (delighted) निखं (purely) मामुपाश्रित्य (taking refuge in me) राजते (shines) । पूर्णाङ्गललिता (perfectly formed and graceful) रम्या (charming) षोडशी (sixteen-year-old) सर्वसुन्दरी (all-beautiful)
