dheesh_gita::148.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::148.essence: True beauty shines when you delight in devoted service and take refuge in the divine.
dheesh_gita::148.simple_meaning: When you find joy in serving and rely on the divine, you naturally radiate beauty and grace.
dheesh_gita::148.simple_insight: Joyful service rooted in trust makes you radiate a captivating presence.
dheesh_gita::148.detailed_meaning: This verse describes a young woman who finds happiness by serving with devotion and taking refuge in the divine. Her beauty and grace symbolize the inner charm that blooms from sincere service and trust.
dheesh_gita::148.modern_relevance: You feel truly yourself and radiant when you serve others wholeheartedly without hesitation or doubt.
dheesh_gita::148.insight: It teaches you to root your actions in trust and devotion, letting your natural grace emerge through service.

dheesh_gita::149.verse_sanskrit:
चक्राब्जशंखशक्तीनां धारिणी शक्तिरूपिणी ।
सिद्धिर्विच्यातते नैव सेवातो मे कदाचन ॥
dheesh_gita::149.verse_hindi: मनोहारिणी शहद चक्र शक्ति पद्म धारिणी शक्तिरूपिणी सिद्धि किसी समय भी मेरी सेवा से च्युत नहीं होती है
dheesh_gita::149.english_translation: The power that holds the discus, conch, and mace, the form of power itself, never abandons me because of my service.
dheesh_gita::149.translation_literal: चक्राब्जशंखशक्तीनां (discus-conch-mace-of) धारिणी (holder) शक्तिरूपिणी (power-form) । सिद्धिर्विच्यातते (success/attainment-falls) नैव (never) सेवातो (from service) मे (my) कदाचन (ever) ॥
dheesh_gita::149.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::149.essence: Steadfast devotion never lets the sustaining power abandon you.
dheesh_gita::149.simple_meaning: The divine power that carries mighty weapons never leaves you when you serve faithfully.
dheesh_gita::149.simple_insight: You can trust that sincere devotion always keeps vital support near.
dheesh_gita::149.detailed_meaning: This verse speaks of the divine power symbolized by powerful weapons like the discus, conch, and mace, which represent strength and authority. It assures that this power never leaves the devotee as long as they remain devoted and in service.
dheesh_gita::149.modern_relevance: When you consistently support your team or loved ones, the strength you rely on stays with you, never abandoning your efforts.
dheesh_gita::149.insight: It teaches you to maintain steady devotion, knowing that true power remains with those who serve sincerely.

dheesh_gita::150.verse_sanskrit:
अपि चन्निरपक्षोऽहं तत्सेवाऽऽदानकर्मणि ।
शुश्रूपते तथाप्येपा धृत्वा रूपं चतुर्विधम् ॥
dheesh_gita::150.verse_hindi: यद्यपि मैं इसकी सेवा ग्रहण करने में निरपेक्ष रहता हूँ तो भी यह चतुर्विध रूप धारण करके मेरी सेवा की इच्छा करती है
dheesh_gita::150.english_translation: Although I remain impartial in receiving that service, it desires to serve me in four distinct forms.
dheesh_gita::150.translation_literal: अपि (even) च (also) निःपक्षः (impartial) अहं (I) तत् (that) सेवा (service) आदानकर्मणि (in receiving action) । शुश्रूपते (desires to serve) तथापि (even so) एषा (this) धृत्वा (holding) रूपं (form) चतुर्विधम् (fourfold) ॥
dheesh_gita::150.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::150.essence: Devotion reaches out to you persistently in many forms, even without your bias.
dheesh_gita::150.simple_meaning: Even if you remain neutral and do not favor any service, the divine expresses devotion to you in four distinct ways.
dheesh_gita::150.simple_insight: You can receive devoted care even when you do not seek or prefer it.
dheesh_gita::150.detailed_meaning: The speaker notes that although they remain impartial and do not cling to receiving service, the divine still expresses devotion through four different forms of connection. This highlights the divine's persistent and multifaceted love, regardless of personal bias.
dheesh_gita::150.modern_relevance: You might feel indifferent or unsure about spiritual practices, yet you still experience caring or support coming to you in unexpected ways.
dheesh_gita::150.insight: It shifts your view from needing to choose or desire devotion to recognizing it arrives regardless of your preferences.

dheesh_gita::151.verse_sanskrit:
नन्वध्यात्माधिदेवाधिभूतानि सहजं तथा ।
सिद्धरस्या हि रूपाणि चत्वारि ब्राह्मणोत्तमाः ॥
dheesh_gita::151.verse_hindi: इसी कारण हे ब्राह्मण श्रेष्ठो! इस सिद्धि के चार भेद हैं यथा-अधिभूतसिद्धि, अधिदेवसिद्धि, अध्यात्मसिद्धि और सहजसिद्धि
dheesh_gita::151.english_translation: Indeed, O best Brahmin, the four types of mastery are: mastery over the physical realm, mastery over the divine realm, mastery over the self, and innate mastery.
dheesh_gita::151.translation_literal: नन्व (indeed) / अध्यात्म (of the self) / अधि (over) / देव (divine) / अधि (over) / भूता (physical beings) / सहजं (innate) / तथा (also) / सिद्धरस्या (masteries) / हि (indeed) / रूपाणि (types/forms) / चत्वारि (four) / ब्राह्मणोत्तमाः (best Brahmin)
dheesh_gita::151.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::151.essence: Mastery appears in four forms: physical, divine, self, and innate effortlessly.
dheesh_gita::151.simple_meaning: There are four kinds of mastery: control over the physical world, the divine realm, the inner self, and natural, effortless skill.
dheesh_gita::151.simple_insight: You can recognize mastery in many forms, not just what you control consciously.
dheesh_gita::151.detailed_meaning: The verse addresses a great Brahmin, explaining that true mastery occurs in four domains: over the physical world, the divine realm, the self, and an effortless, innate mastery that arises naturally.
dheesh_gita::151.modern_relevance: When you excel in your work, your relationships, your inner growth, and also in moments when things come naturally, you experience these four types of mastery.
dheesh_gita::151.insight: This verse teaches you to see mastery beyond effort, including natural ease and deep inner control.

dheesh_gita::152.verse_sanskrit:
ऐश्वर्य्यस्य चिता यद्वत् वलस्य च सता यथा ।
सम्बन्धः कर्मणः शक्तया रूपस्य तेजसा सह ॥
dheesh_gita::152.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार चित् के साथ ऐश्वर्य का सम्बन्ध है, सत् के साथ बल का सम्बन्ध है, शक्ति के साथ कर्म का सम्बन्ध है और तेजके साथ रूप का सम्बन्ध है
dheesh_gita::152.english_translation: Just as prosperity is connected with the mind, strength with existence, action with power, and form with brilliance.
dheesh_gita::152.translation_literal: ऐश्वर्य्यस्य (of prosperity) चिता (mind) यद्वत् (just as) वलस्य (of strength) च (and) सता (existence) यथा (as) । सम्बन्धः (connection) कर्मणः (of action) शक्तया (with power) रूपस्य (of form) तेजसा (with brilliance) सह (together) ॥
dheesh_gita::152.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::152.essence: Prosperity, strength, action, and form are linked to mind, existence, power, and brilliance.
dheesh_gita::152.simple_meaning: Prosperity, strength, action, and form are each connected to specific aspects of our inner and outer nature like mind, existence, power, and brilliance.
dheesh_gita::152.simple_insight: You sense how different qualities like strength and prosperity arise through your inner energies and being.
dheesh_gita::152.detailed_meaning: This verse describes how prosperity relates to mind, strength to existence, action to power, and form to brilliance, revealing the interconnectedness of inner faculties and outer reality.
dheesh_gita::152.modern_relevance: You notice how your mental focus energizes your efforts, shaping your strength and the outcomes you create.
dheesh_gita::152.insight: It teaches you to see qualities like strength and prosperity as expressions of deeper inner connections, not separate things.

dheesh_gita::153.verse_sanskrit:
तथैवास्ते च सम्बन्धः सिद्धेः सार्द्धे मया ध्रुवम् ।
सम्बन्धोऽयमपूर्वोऽस्ति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
dheesh_gita::153.verse_hindi: उसी प्रकार मेरे साथ सिद्धि का नित्य सम्बन्ध है । यह सम्बन्ध अलौकिक है, इसमें विचार नहीं  करना चाहिए।
dheesh_gita::153.english_translation: Just as the supreme success is always with me, this connection is extraordinary and should not be questioned.
dheesh_gita::153.translation_literal: तथैवास्ते (just so exists) च (also) सम्बन्धः (connection) सिद्धेः (of success) सार्द्धे (alongside) मया (with me) ध्रुवम् (constant). सम्बन्धः (connection) अयम् (this) पूर्वः (unusual) अस्ति (is) न (not) अत्र (here) कार्या (to be done) विचारणा (consideration).
dheesh_gita::153.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::153.essence: Steady connection with true success exists beyond doubt and questioning.
dheesh_gita::153.simple_meaning: You share a steady, extraordinary connection with true success that requires no doubt or questioning.
dheesh_gita::153.simple_insight: Trusting this constant connection brings calm beyond uncertainty.
dheesh_gita::153.detailed_meaning: The speaker affirms a constant, extraordinary connection with supreme success, emphasizing it is beyond ordinary reasoning or doubt, inviting the listener to accept this as a steady truth without overthinking.
dheesh_gita::153.modern_relevance: When you feel uncertain about your efforts, remember some connections—like your true purpose—are steady and need no second-guessing.
dheesh_gita::153.insight: Encourages you to trust steady, extraordinary connections without overanalyzing or doubting them.

dheesh_gita::154.verse_sanskrit:
विष्णोः प्रिया यथा लक्ष्मीः प्रिया श्यामा शिवस्य च ।
ब्रह्ममय्या महाशक्ते प्रिय आस्ते यथा पुनः ॥
dheesh_gita::154.verse_hindi: हे विज्ञो ! जिस प्रकार विष्णु को लक्ष्मी प्रिय है, शम्भु को श्यामा प्रिय है और पुनः जिस प्रकार ब्रह्मरूपिणी महाशक्ति को
dheesh_gita::154.english_translation: Just as Lakshmi is dear to Vishnu, and Shyama is dear to Shambhu, similarly the great power in the form of Brahman is dear.
dheesh_gita::154.translation_literal: विष्णोः (to Vishnu) / प्रिया (dear) / यथा (just as) / लक्ष्मीः (Lakshmi) / प्रिया (dear) / श्यामा (Shyama) / शिवस्य (to Shiva) / च (and) / ब्रह्ममय्या (made of Brahman) / महाशक्ते (great power) / प्रिय (dear) / आस्ते (is) / यथा (just as) / पुनः (again)
dheesh_gita::154.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::154.essence: Deep love and devotion connect great powers and their beloveds, revealing the nature of true connection.
dheesh_gita::154.simple_meaning: Certain powerful beings are deeply loved by their divine counterparts, showing a pattern of devotion and connection.
dheesh_gita::154.simple_insight: You can feel deeply cherished just as these divine pairs are lovingly connected.
dheesh_gita::154.detailed_meaning: This verse illustrates how Lakshmi loves Vishnu, Shyama loves Shiva (Shambhu), and likewise the great power embodied in Brahman is loved, highlighting intimate bonds of devotion among divine forms.
dheesh_gita::154.modern_relevance: You might notice the quiet, unspoken love in your closest relationships — this verse reflects that profound connection.
dheesh_gita::154.insight: It invites you to recognize your own worthiness of deep, devoted love and connection.

dheesh_gita::155.verse_sanskrit:
चिद्विलासात्मको भावः स्वकार्यब्रह्मणः खलु ।
अरुणोऽस्ति यथा विज्ञाः ! सूर्यदेवस्य च प्रियः ॥
dheesh_gita::155.verse_hindi: स्वकार्य ब्रह्म का चिद विलास रूप भाव प्रिय है, एवं जिस प्रकार सूर्यदेव को अरुण प्रिय है
dheesh_gita::155.english_translation: The nature of the supreme reality is to delight in its own work, just as the sun god loves the reddish dawn.
dheesh_gita::155.translation_literal: चिद्विलासात्मको (of consciousness, play-nature) / भावः (nature) / स्वकार्यब्रह्मणः (of own-work Brahman) / खलु (indeed) / अरुणोऽस्ति (is reddish dawn) / यथा (just as) / विज्ञाः (those who know) / सूर्यदेवस्य (of the sun god) / च (and) / प्रियः (dear)
dheesh_gita::155.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::155.essence: The supreme reality naturally delights in its own spontaneous activity.
dheesh_gita::155.simple_meaning: The supreme reality naturally enjoys its own actions, just like the sun loves the red dawn every day.
dheesh_gita::155.simple_insight: Joy can come from embracing your true nature and the work it naturally flows into.
dheesh_gita::155.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the supreme reality is described as delighting in its own inherent activity. Like the sun god eagerly embraces the reddish dawn, the divine essence takes pleasure in its spontaneous actions. This portrays the nature of pure consciousness as joyful and self-engaged.
dheesh_gita::155.modern_relevance: You might notice how some moments of your work or creativity feel effortless and deeply satisfying, just like dawn’s quiet beauty.
dheesh_gita::155.insight: It teaches you to see your true work as a source of joy, not as a burden or obligation.

dheesh_gita::156.verse_sanskrit:
महार्षयस्तथैवास्ते सिद्धिरेपा हि मे प्रिया।
परन्तु निर्विकारं मां निर्लिप्त ज्ञानरूपिणम् ॥
dheesh_gita::156.verse_hindi: उसी प्रकारसे हे महर्षि गण ! मुझको यह सिद्धि ही प्रिय है, परन्तु निर्लिप्त निर्विकार और ज्ञान स्वरुप  मुझको
dheesh_gita::156.english_translation: O great sages, I also cherish this perfection, but I prefer the unchanging, detached form of knowledge.
dheesh_gita::156.translation_literal: महार्षयः (great sages) तथैव (in the same way) अस्मि (I am) ते (your) सिद्धिः (perfection) एषा (this) हि (indeed) मे (to me) प्रिया (dear) । परंतु (but) निर्विकारं (unchanging) माम् (me) निर्लिप्त (detached) ज्ञानरूपिणम् (knowledge-formed) ॥
dheesh_gita::156.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::156.essence: True perfection is the steady, detached knowledge beyond all change.
dheesh_gita::156.simple_meaning: You value perfection, but you especially prefer knowledge that is steady, detached, and beyond change.
dheesh_gita::156.simple_insight: There is peace in preferring steady, unaffected knowledge over fleeting achievements.
dheesh_gita::156.detailed_meaning: In a dialogue with great sages, the speaker acknowledges their admiration for spiritual achievements but reveals a deeper preference: knowledge that is unchanging and free from attachment, emphasizing the ideal of pure wisdom beyond fluctuations.
dheesh_gita::156.modern_relevance: You might feel proud of your accomplishments but find deeper satisfaction when your understanding remains calm and unaffected by external ups and downs.
dheesh_gita::156.insight: It shifts your focus from valuing external success to embracing an inner, detached clarity of understanding.

dheesh_gita::157.verse_sanskrit:
स्वप्रेमावरणे सिद्धिर्नासज्जयितुमस्त्यलम् ।
अलौकिकोऽस्ति सम्बन्धः सिद्धयैवं मे महर्षयः ! ॥
dheesh_gita::157.verse_hindi: सिद्धि अपने प्रेम आचरण से फंसा नहीं सकती। हे महर्षिगण ! इस प्रकार का सिद्धि के साथ मेरा अलौकिक सम्बन्ध है
dheesh_gita::157.english_translation: Perfection cannot be conquered when covered by self-love. O great sages, this is how my supernatural connection with perfection is.
dheesh_gita::157.translation_literal: स्वप्रेमावरणे (in the covering of self-love) / सिद्धिः (perfection) / न (not) / असज्जयितुम् (to conquer) / अस्ति (is) / अलम् (possible) / अलौकिकोऽस्ति (is supernatural) / सम्बन्धः (connection) / सिद्धयैवं (thus with perfection) / मे (my) / महर्षयः (great sages)
dheesh_gita::157.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::157.essence: Self-love conceals perfection, blocking true conquest or realization.
dheesh_gita::157.simple_meaning: Perfection or true accomplishment cannot be overcome or truly attained when it is hidden beneath self-centered love or ego. The speaker shares a unique, higher connection to such perfection.
dheesh_gita::157.simple_insight: Letting go of self-love opens you to a higher, unshakable connection with true accomplishment.
dheesh_gita::157.detailed_meaning: The speaker addresses great sages, explaining that when perfection is covered by self-love, it cannot be fully realized or overcome. This moment reveals the speaker's extraordinary relationship with perfection, beyond ordinary experience.
dheesh_gita::157.modern_relevance: When your success feels tied to your ego or self-image, true mastery remains elusive, no matter how much you achieve.
dheesh_gita::157.insight: It teaches you to see self-love as a barrier to true mastery and to cultivate detachment to connect with deeper accomplishment.

dheesh_gita::158.verse_sanskrit:
मन्त्रसिद्धिस्तपासिद्धिर्योगसिद्धिस्तथैव च ।
एवं नानाविधा लोके विख्याता याश्च सिद्धयः ॥
dheesh_gita::158.verse_hindi: जगत में जो, मन्त्रसिद्धि तपसिद्धि और योगसिद्धि, इस प्रकार नानाविध सिद्धियां प्रचलित हैं
dheesh_gita::158.english_translation: In the world, various types of accomplishments like mastery of mantras, success in disciplined effort, and perfection in yoga are well known.
dheesh_gita::158.translation_literal: मन्त्रसिद्धिस्तपासिद्धिर्योगसिद्धिस्तथैव च (mantra mastery, disciplined effort mastery, yoga mastery, likewise) / एवं (thus) / नानाविधा (various kinds) / लोके (in the world) / विख्याता (well known) / याश्च (and which) / सिद्धयः (accomplishments)
dheesh_gita::158.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::158.essence: Spiritual success is known in many varied forms, each respected and real.
dheesh_gita::158.simple_meaning: There are many well-known kinds of spiritual achievements like mastering mantras, disciplined effort, and yoga.
dheesh_gita::158.simple_insight: You can find many paths to accomplishment, each with its own focus and strength.
dheesh_gita::158.detailed_meaning: This verse lists the common types of spiritual success recognized in the world: mastery of sacred chants (mantra), success through disciplined effort (tapas), and perfection in yoga practice. It introduces the idea that spiritual progress can take various forms.
dheesh_gita::158.modern_relevance: You notice people succeed in different ways—through focused practice, disciplined habits, or deep connection—and each path has value.
dheesh_gita::158.insight: It teaches you to appreciate different kinds of spiritual or personal mastery without needing just one way.

dheesh_gita::159.verse_sanskrit:
उत याः सिद्धयो विमा ऐश्यः सन्त्यणिमादयः ।
जैव्यो वा सिद्धयः सन्ति या मेधामतिभादयः ॥
dheesh_gita::159.verse_hindi: और हे विप्रगण! जगत् में जो अणिमा लघिमा आदि ऐसी  सिद्धियां हैं अथवा जो मेधाप्रतिभा आदि जैवसिद्धियां प्रचलित हैं
dheesh_gita::159.english_translation: O scholars, the world contains siddhis like subtlety, lightness, and others, as well as natural gifts like intelligence and brilliance.
dheesh_gita::159.translation_literal: उत (indeed) / याः (which) / सिद्धयो (powers) / विमा (subtlety) / ऐश्यः (lightness) / सन्ति (are) / अणिमादयः (and others like minuteness) । / जैव्यो (natural) / वा (or) / सिद्धयः (powers) / सन्ति (are) / या (which) / मेधामतिभादयः (intelligence and brilliance) ॥
dheesh_gita::159.speaker: Narrator
dheesh_gita::159.essence: Special powers and natural talents both exist in the world.
dheesh_gita::159.simple_meaning: There are extraordinary powers like becoming very small or light, and natural talents like intelligence existing in the world.
dheesh_gita::159.simple_insight: Exceptional abilities and talents exist around you, both subtle and natural.
dheesh_gita::159.detailed_meaning: The verse lists various supernatural powers (siddhis) such as extreme subtlety and lightness, as well as natural capabilities like intelligence, introducing the topic of special abilities present in the world.
dheesh_gita::159.insight: It invites you to recognize the diverse range of abilities—both mystical and natural—that can arise in human experience.

dheesh_gita::160.verse_sanskrit:
ओषधीसिद्धयो याश्च या रसायनमूलिकाः ।
पदार्थसिद्धयो याश्च विश्वस्मिन्मन्त्रदर्शिनः ! ॥
dheesh_gita::160.verse_hindi: या जगत में जो औषधि. सिद्धि ,रसायनसिद्धि और पदार्थसिद्धि नाम से प्रचलित हैं और हे मन्त्रदर्शि गण!
dheesh_gita::160.english_translation: Those in the world who have mastery over herbs, alchemy, and substances are indeed seers of mantras.
dheesh_gita::160.translation_literal: ओषधीसिद्धयो (herb-mastery) / याश्च (and those) / या (who) / रसायनमूलिकाः (rooted in alchemy) / पदार्थसिद्धयो (mastery of substances) / याश्च (and those) / विश्वस्मिन्मन्त्रदर्शिनः (world-in mantra-seers)
dheesh_gita::160.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::160.essence: Mastery of healing and substances coincides with deep spiritual insight.
dheesh_gita::160.simple_meaning: Some people in the world have special knowledge about healing plants, alchemy, and material substances and also understand sacred mantras.
dheesh_gita::160.simple_insight: Certain skills and spiritual insight often come together as a combined mastery.
dheesh_gita::160.detailed_meaning: The verse describes individuals recognized for expertise in healing herbs, alchemy, and material science, who also possess deep insight into sacred mantras, indicating their special status and powers.
dheesh_gita::160.insight: It highlights how specialized practical knowledge can link with spiritual understanding, showing the value of integrated wisdom.

dheesh_gita::161.verse_sanskrit:
बलसिद्धिद्रव्यसिद्धिः सिद्भिश्च पुरुषार्थगा।
सम्मोहनादयः ख्याताः सन्ति वा याश्च सिद्धयः ॥
dheesh_gita::161.verse_hindi: जगत में  जो धनसिद्धि. बलसिद्धि, पुरुषार्थसिद्धि, संमोहिन करने की सिद्धि आदि प्रचलित है और जगत में जो
dheesh_gita::161.english_translation: In the world, achievements like wealth, strength, success through effort, and the power to enchant are known and recognized.
dheesh_gita::161.translation_literal: बलसिद्धि (strength-success) / द्रव्यसिद्धिः (wealth-success) / सिद्भिश्च (and success) / पुरुषार्थगा (achievements through effort) / सम्मोहनादयः (power to enchant and such) / ख्याताः (are known) / सन्ति (exist) / वा (or) / याश्च (which) / सिद्धयः (successes)
dheesh_gita::161.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::161.essence: Common worldly successes like strength, wealth, and influence are known but not the whole truth.
dheesh_gita::161.simple_meaning: Many kinds of worldly successes like power, wealth, and influence are recognized and talked about in the world.
dheesh_gita::161.simple_insight: Worldly achievements are varied and familiar but do not define the full picture of success.
dheesh_gita::161.detailed_meaning: This verse lists common worldly achievements such as gaining strength, wealth, and influence through effort or enchantment, reflecting familiar successes people seek and recognize in life.
dheesh_gita::161.modern_relevance: You see many people chasing money, power, or social influence, considering these the main markers of success.
dheesh_gita::161.insight: It invites you to notice how many achievements are celebrated but also to question what true success means beyond them.

dheesh_gita::162.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानस्य सिद्धयो नाना वेदशास्त्रप्रकाशिकाः ।
सर्वास्तास्न्ति मत्सिद्धेरङ्गभूता न संशयः ॥
dheesh_gita::162.verse_hindi: वेद  तथा नानाशास्त्र के प्रकाश की जो नाना ज्ञान सम्बन्धीय सिद्धियां हैं वह  सब मेरी सिद्धि की ही अंगभूत हैं इसमें सन्देह नहीं।
dheesh_gita::162.english_translation: All the various knowledges revealed by the Vedas and other scriptures are undoubtedly parts of my own perfection.
dheesh_gita::162.translation_literal: ज्ञानस्य (of knowledge) / सिद्धयो (perfections) / नाना (various) / वेदशास्त्रप्रकाशिकाः (Vedas and scriptures illuminating) / । (.) / सर्वास्तास्न्ति (all these exist) / मत्सिद्धेरङ्गभूता (as parts of my perfection) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt) / ॥
dheesh_gita::162.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::162.essence: All genuine knowledge is unified as parts of one perfect whole without doubt.
dheesh_gita::162.simple_meaning: All the different insights from the Vedas and other scriptures are parts of a single perfect truth without doubt.
dheesh_gita::162.simple_insight: You can feel confident that all genuine wisdom is interconnected and comes from one source.
dheesh_gita::162.detailed_meaning: This verse explains that the many types of knowledge found in the Vedas and other sacred texts are not separate truths but aspects of one complete perfection, affirming their unity and reliability.
dheesh_gita::162.modern_relevance: When you study different ideas or teachings, you can see them as pieces of one larger truth rather than separate, conflicting views.
dheesh_gita::162.insight: It teaches you to recognize diverse teachings as expressions of one underlying perfection, reducing confusion and fostering integration.

dheesh_gita::163.verse_hindi: हे विप्रो! जन्म, पद,औषधि मन्त्र, उपासना, तप, संयम और समाधि के द्वारा अलौकिक सिद्धियां प्राप्त होती हैं
dheesh_gita::163.english_translation: O Brahmin! Extraordinary accomplishments are attained through birth, social position, herbs, mantras, worship, austerity, self-restraint, and absorbed presence.
dheesh_gita::163.translation_literal: जन्मौपधिपदोपास्तितपोमन्त्रसमाधिभिः (through birth, social position, herbs, mantras, worship, austerity, self-restraint, absorbed presence) / संयमेनापि (also by self-restraint) / लभ्यन्ते (are attained) / सिद्धयोऽलौकिका (extraordinary accomplishments) / द्विजाः (O Brahmins)!
dheesh_gita::163.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::163.essence: Steady discipline and restraint unlock extraordinary spiritual accomplishments.
dheesh_gita::163.simple_meaning: Special spiritual powers come from birth circumstances, rituals, austerity, self-control, and deep meditation.
dheesh_gita::163.simple_insight: Your steady discipline can open doors to uncommon inner abilities.
dheesh_gita::163.detailed_meaning: A teacher addresses Brahmins, explaining that extraordinary powers arise not just by chance but through a combination of birth, social status, sacred herbs, chanting, worship, austerity, self-restraint, and deep meditative absorption.
dheesh_gita::163.modern_relevance: You notice how steady habits and self-control quietly build your strength, even when results feel distant.
dheesh_gita::163.insight: It teaches that consistent inner discipline and restraint are the path to rare spiritual abilities.

dheesh_gita::164.verse_sanskrit:
अष्टोपायाः प्रधाना हि सन्तीमे सिद्धिलब्धये ।
सन्ति जातिस्मरत्वादिसिद्धयो जन्मसिद्धयः॥
dheesh_gita::164.verse_hindi: सिद्धिलाभ के लिये ये ही पाठ उपाय प्रधान हैं। जातिस्मरत्व आदि सिद्धियां जन्म सिद्धियां हैं
dheesh_gita::164.english_translation: The eight main methods are essential for attaining accomplishment; achievements like remembering past lives are innate.
dheesh_gita::164.translation_literal: अष्टोपायाः (eight methods) / प्रधाना (main) / हि (indeed) / सन्ति (are) / मे (for me) / सिद्धिलब्धये (for attainment of success) / सन्ति (are) / जातिस्मरत्वादि (such as remembering past births) / सिद्धयः (achievements) / जन्मसिद्धयः (innate from birth)
dheesh_gita::164.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::164.essence: True accomplishment arises by practicing eight essential methods, beyond natural abilities.
dheesh_gita::164.simple_meaning: There are eight main methods or practices that are necessary to achieve true success; abilities like recalling past lives come naturally.
dheesh_gita::164.simple_insight: Knowing the right methods gives confidence that success is within reach.
dheesh_gita::164.detailed_meaning: In a teaching moment, the narrator explains that true accomplishment arises from practicing eight primary methods. Some powers, like remembering past births, are natural, but mastery comes from applying these key practices.
dheesh_gita::164.modern_relevance: You feel stuck trying to grow, but focusing on essential proven steps can unlock your progress steadily.
dheesh_gita::164.insight: Focus on mastering core methods rather than waiting for innate talents to appear.

dheesh_gita::165.verse_sanskrit:
या सिद्धगुटिका कायकल्पश्चैव रसायनम ।
अन्या चैवंविधा सिद्धिरोषधीसिद्धिरुच्यते ॥
dheesh_gita::165.verse_hindi: सिद्धगुटि का कायाकल्प रसायन और इस प्रकार को अन्यान्य सिद्धियां ओषधि सिद्धियां कहलाती हैं
dheesh_gita::165.english_translation: The perfected elixir that renews the body is called Kayakalpa Rasayana; other such accomplishments are known as medicinal achievements.
dheesh_gita::165.translation_literal: या (which) / सिद्धगुटिका (perfected pill) / कायकल्पश्चैव (and body-renewal) / रसायनम (elixir) / अन्याः (others) / चैवंविधा (thus kinds of) / सिद्धिः (accomplishment) / ओषधीसिद्धिः (medicinal accomplishment) / उच्यते (is called)
dheesh_gita::165.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::165.essence: Certain rare elixirs renew the body, while others are medicinal achievements.
dheesh_gita::165.simple_meaning: There is a special elixir called Kayakalpa Rasayana that rejuvenates the body; other kinds of such accomplishments are known as medicinal achievements.
dheesh_gita::165.simple_insight: Some practices or substances can refresh and renew the body in extraordinary ways.
dheesh_gita::165.detailed_meaning: The verse describes different kinds of perfected substances or methods that restore and refresh the body. It distinguishes Kayakalpa Rasayana as a rejuvenating elixir, while other similar achievements fall under medicinal accomplishments. It categorizes types of healing and renewal.
dheesh_gita::165.insight: It highlights that some remedies aim not just to heal but to renew and transform the body's vitality.

dheesh_gita::166.verse_sanskrit:
नैमित्तिक्यश्च या देव-शक्तयो राजशक्तयः ।
अन्याश्चैवविधाः सर्वाः शक्तयः पदसिद्धयः ॥
dheesh_gita::166.verse_hindi: राजशक्ति और नैमित्तिक देवशक्ति और अन्यान्य इस प्रकार को सव शक्तियां पद-सिद्धियां कहलाती हैं
dheesh_gita::166.english_translation: The royal power, the occasional divine powers, and all other types of powers are called accomplished powers.
dheesh_gita::166.translation_literal: नैमित्तिक्यश्च (occasional) / या (which) / देव-शक्तयो (divine powers) / राजशक्तयः (royal powers) / अन्याश्चैवविधाः (and other kinds) / सर्वाः (all) / शक्तयः (powers) / पदसिद्धयः (accomplished powers)
dheesh_gita::166.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::166.essence: Different kinds of powers are classified as accomplished powers.
dheesh_gita::166.simple_meaning: There are different kinds of powers like royal power, divine powers that arise occasionally, and others; all these are called accomplished powers.
dheesh_gita::166.simple_insight: Understanding that various forms of power have distinct roles can clarify how influence works.
dheesh_gita::166.detailed_meaning: This verse classifies different sources of power, including royal authority, divine occasional powers, and others, labeling them all as accomplished powers. It is a descriptive categorization rather than a teaching moment, setting the stage for further discussion.
dheesh_gita::166.insight: It shows the variety of powers operating in the world but offers no direct guidance on how to relate to them.

dheesh_gita::167.verse_sanskrit:
उपास्तेः सिद्धयः सन्ति देवतादर्शनादयः।
यासु सिद्धिषु लब्धामु जायतेऽभ्युदयो ध्रुवम् ॥
dheesh_gita::167.verse_hindi: देवदर्शनादि उपासना सिद्धियां कहलाती हैं जिनके प्राप्त होने पर अवश्य अभ्युदय होता है।
dheesh_gita::167.english_translation: The perfections attained through worship like seeing the radiant beings surely bring steady progress.
dheesh_gita::167.translation_literal: उपास्तेः (worship) सिद्धयः (perfections) सन्ति (are) देवतादर्शनादयः (like seeing radiant beings). यासु (in which) सिद्धिषु (perfections) लब्धामु (having obtained) जायतेऽभ्युदयो (arises progress) ध्रुवम् (certainly).
dheesh_gita::167.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::167.essence: Sacred devotional experiences naturally create steady and certain progress.
dheesh_gita::167.simple_meaning: When you sincerely worship and have sacred experiences like seeing radiant beings, it brings clear and steady growth in your spiritual journey.
dheesh_gita::167.simple_insight: You can trust that heartfelt devotion naturally leads to real progress over time.
dheesh_gita::167.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the teacher explains that perfections or spiritual achievements gained through devotional practices such as visions of radiant beings produce certain and lasting progress. This encourages the student to trust the power of devotion's fruits.
dheesh_gita::167.modern_relevance: When you feel deeply connected during a heartfelt ritual or moment of devotion, that feeling is a sign of steady inner growth.
dheesh_gita::167.insight: It shifts the mind to value devotional experiences as trustworthy markers of spiritual advancement.

dheesh_gita::168.verse_sanskrit:
षड़वशीकरणादीनि यानि कर्माणि सन्ति च ।
अन्यान्यन्तर्भवन्त्येवं मन्त्रसिद्रौ न संशयः ॥
dheesh_gita::168.verse_hindi: वशीकरणादि षट्कर्म तथा उसी प्रकार की और सिद्धियां मन्त्रसिद्धि के अन्तर्गत हैं इसमें सन्देह नहीं है
dheesh_gita::168.english_translation: There is no doubt that six types of actions like control rituals and similar accomplishments fall under the power of mantra mastery.
dheesh_gita::168.translation_literal: षड़वशीकरणादीनि (six control rituals etc.) / यानि (which) / कर्माणि (actions) / सन्ति (are) / च (also) / अन्यान्यन्तर्भवन्ति (others exist within) / एवं (thus) / मन्त्रसिद्धौ (in mantra mastery) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
dheesh_gita::168.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::168.essence: Certain ritual actions clearly belong within mantra mastery without doubt.
dheesh_gita::168.simple_meaning: Certain six kinds of ritual actions, including control rituals, are part of mantra mastery, and this is beyond doubt.
dheesh_gita::168.simple_insight: Some spiritual practices clearly belong to a broader system of mantra power.
dheesh_gita::168.detailed_meaning: This verse states that six specific ritual actions, such as those for control or influence, are included within mantra mastery. It affirms without doubt their place in this spiritual practice.
dheesh_gita::168.insight: Recognize that complex spiritual abilities often come as parts of a larger unified practice.

dheesh_gita::169.verse_sanskrit:
नैवास्त्यवाम्वधा सिद्धिदैवी वा कापि लौकिकी।
या संयमसमाधिभ्यां लभ्येत तपसा न वा ॥
dheesh_gita::169.verse_hindi: तप संयम और समाधि द्वारा दैवी या लौकिकी ऐसी कोई भी सिद्धि नहीं जो प्राप्त न हो सके
dheesh_gita::169.english_translation: There is no divine or earthly accomplishment that cannot be attained through discipline, control, and absorbed presence.
dheesh_gita::169.translation_literal: नैवास्ति (not exists) अवाम्वधा (any) सिद्धि (accomplishment) दैवी (divine) वा (or) कापि (any) लौकिकी (earthly) । या (which) संयम (control) समाधिभ्यां (through absorbed presence) लभ्येत (is attained) तपसा (through disciplined effort) न (not) वा (or) ॥
dheesh_gita::169.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::169.essence: All accomplishments are attainable through disciplined effort, self-control, and deep focus.
dheesh_gita::169.simple_meaning: Any great success, whether related to the divine or the world, can be reached by sustained effort, self-control, and deep focus.
dheesh_gita::169.simple_insight: You can trust that steady discipline opens every door to accomplishment.
dheesh_gita::169.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, the speaker highlights that no special power or worldly achievement is out of reach when approached with disciplined effort, self-restraint, and deep absorption. This encourages perseverance through sustained practice.
dheesh_gita::169.modern_relevance: When you commit to a challenging project or personal goal, consistent focus and self-control become your most powerful tools to succeed.
dheesh_gita::169.insight: It teaches you to rely on disciplined, focused effort as the true source of accomplishment, not external factors.

dheesh_gita::170.verse_sanskrit:
चतुर्विधा हि लभ्यन्ते सिद्धयो निश्चितं द्विजाः ।
उपायैरष्टभि: प्रोक्तैनात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
dheesh_gita::170.verse_hindi: हे विप्रो ! इन आठ उपायों के द्वारा चतुर्विध ही सिद्धियां निश्चय प्राप्त हुआ करती है इसमें विचार नहीं करना चाहिए
dheesh_gita::170.english_translation: O Brahmin, four types of accomplishments are certainly attained through these eight methods; there is no need to doubt this.
dheesh_gita::170.translation_literal: चतुर्विधा (four types) हि (indeed) लभ्यन्ते (are attained) सिद्धयो (accomplishments) निश्चितं (certainly) द्विजाः (Brahmins) । / उपायैः (by methods) अष्टभिः (eight) प्रोक्तैः (spoken) अनात्र (here not) कार्या (to be done) विचारणा (doubting) ॥
dheesh_gita::170.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::170.essence: Certain successes arise reliably from a defined set of methods without doubt.
dheesh_gita::170.simple_meaning: There are four kinds of definite achievements that can be reached by following eight specific methods, without any doubt.
dheesh_gita::170.simple_insight: You can trust that following clear steps leads to real success.
dheesh_gita::170.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the teacher addresses the Brahmins, assuring them that through eight specific methods, four definite accomplishments can be attained. There is no need for hesitation or doubt about this truth.
dheesh_gita::170.modern_relevance: When you follow proven steps in your work or practice, success becomes certain without second-guessing yourself.
dheesh_gita::170.insight: It shifts your mind from uncertainty to confident trust in the methods you follow.

dheesh_gita::171.verse_sanskrit:
अनन्ताः सिद्धयो याश्च लोके मच्छक्तिसम्भवाः ।
विभक्तास्सन्ति तास्सर्वाश्चतुर्धेव मया पुरा ॥
dheesh_gita::171.verse_hindi: संसार में मेरी शक्ति से उत्पन्न जो अनन्त प्रकार की सिद्धियां हैं मेरे द्वारा पहले ही से वह सभी चार श्रेणियों में विभक्त हैं
dheesh_gita::171.english_translation: The countless powers born from me in the world are previously divided by me into four categories.
dheesh_gita::171.translation_literal: अनन्ताः (countless) / सिद्धयो (powers) / याश्च (which) / लोके (in the world) / मच्छक्तिसम्भवाः (from me born of power) / विभक्ताः (divided) / सन्ति (are) / ताः (those) / सर्वाः (all) / चतुर्धे (in four parts) / मया (by me) / पुरा (before).
dheesh_gita::171.speaker: Shambhu Dheesh
dheesh_gita::171.essence: Infinite powers arise from the divine, organized into four distinct categories.
dheesh_gita::171.simple_meaning: Infinite kinds of powers in the world come from the divine and are grouped into four types.
dheesh_gita::171.simple_insight: There's structure and order even in the vastness of your potential.
dheesh_gita::171.detailed_meaning: Shambhu Dheesh explains to the listener that all the infinite powers seen in the world originate from the divine and have been systematically divided into four main categories by that divine source.
dheesh_gita::171.modern_relevance: You may feel overwhelmed by your abilities and options, but underlying them is a clear structure guiding your strengths.
dheesh_gita::171.insight: Recognize that your diverse abilities are not random but belong to distinct groups, helping you understand and focus your potential.

dheesh_gita::172.verse_sanskrit:
तासाञ्च लब्धये नूनमुपाया अष्ट निर्मिताः ।
तैरेव ताश्च प्राप्यन्ते निश्चितं विप्रपुङ्गवाः ! ॥
dheesh_gita::172.verse_hindi: और उनकी प्राप्ति के लिये ही आठ उपाय मैंने विधान किये हैं, हे ब्राह्मणो! उन्हीं के द्वारा वह अवश्य प्राप्त होती हैं।
dheesh_gita::172.english_translation: I have prescribed eight methods precisely for attaining them, O Brahmins! By these alone, they are surely attained.
dheesh_gita::172.translation_literal: तासाञ्च (those also) लब्धये (for obtaining) नूनम् (certainly) उपायाः (methods) अष्ट (eight) निर्मिताः (established) । तैरेव (by those only) ताश्च (those) प्राप्यन्ते (are obtained) निश्चितं (definitely) विप्रपुङ्गवाः (learned Brahmins) !
dheesh_gita::172.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::172.essence: Clear, defined methods are essential and sufficient to achieve definite goals.
dheesh_gita::172.simple_meaning: There are eight specific methods laid out to achieve certain goals, and only by following these methods can one definitely succeed.
dheesh_gita::172.simple_insight: Knowing clear, defined ways exist brings confidence and direction to your efforts.
dheesh_gita::172.detailed_meaning: The speaker addresses learned Brahmins, explaining that eight particular methods have been formulated to attain the desired results. These methods are reliable and must be followed to ensure success.
dheesh_gita::172.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by choices, having a clear set of steps can guide your efforts and reduce doubt.
dheesh_gita::172.insight: Trust and commit to proven methods rather than guessing; this focus sharpens your path.

dheesh_gita::173.verse_sanskrit:
कुर्वाणा लौकिकं कार्ये सन्ति याः सिद्धयोऽखिलाः ।
ता ज्ञेया निखिला विप्रा आधिभौतिकसिद्धयः ॥
dheesh_gita::173.verse_hindi: हे विप्रो ! सब लौकिक कार्यकारिणी सिद्धियो को आधिभौतिक सिद्धियां,
dheesh_gita::173.english_translation: O wise one, all worldly accomplishments are known as achievements of the physical plane.
dheesh_gita::173.translation_literal: कुर्वाणा (doing) लौकिकं (worldly) कार्ये (actions) सन्ति (are) याः (which) सिद्धयोऽखिलाः (all accomplishments) । ता (those) ज्ञेया (are to be known) निखिला (all) विप्रा (wise ones) आधिभौतिकसिद्धयः (achievements of the physical realm) ॥
dheesh_gita::173.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::173.essence: Worldly achievements are only physical accomplishments, not true success of the self.
dheesh_gita::173.simple_meaning: All achievements in the world are only accomplishments of the physical realm, not ultimate or spiritual success.
dheesh_gita::173.simple_insight: You can recognize that worldly success is limited and does not define your true nature.
dheesh_gita::173.detailed_meaning: The verse addresses the wise, explaining that all successes related to worldly actions are achievements in the physical plane, distinct from spiritual or inner accomplishments.
dheesh_gita::173.modern_relevance: You might celebrate a promotion or award, but these wins belong to the surface world, not your deeper being.
dheesh_gita::173.insight: It shifts your view to see worldly success as separate from your inner growth or spiritual progress.

dheesh_gita::174.verse_sanskrit:
या देवकार्यकारिण्यः सिद्धयः सम्प्रकीर्तिताः।
ता ज्ञेया आधिदैविक्यः सिद्धयो निखिलाः खलु ॥
dheesh_gita::174.verse_hindi: देवकार्य कारिणी सभी सिद्धियों को अधिदैविक सिद्धियां और
dheesh_gita::174.english_translation: The accomplishments achieved through performing divine tasks are known as transcendental accomplishments; indeed, all accomplishments belong to this higher realm.
dheesh_gita::174.translation_literal: या (which) / देवकार्यकारिण्यः (performing divine tasks) / सिद्धयः (accomplishments) / सम्प्रकीर्तिताः (are proclaimed) / ता (those) / ज्ञेया (to be known) / आधिदैविक्यः (transcendental) / सिद्धयो (accomplishments) / निखिलाः (all) / खलु (indeed)
dheesh_gita::174.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::174.essence: True accomplishments arise only from actions aligned with the higher realm.
dheesh_gita::174.simple_meaning: Accomplishments that come from performing divine or higher-purpose actions are called transcendental accomplishments, and all true achievements belong to this higher realm.
dheesh_gita::174.simple_insight: You can feel peace knowing your real successes come from aligning with a higher purpose.
dheesh_gita::174.detailed_meaning: This verse explains that accomplishments achieved through actions aligned with the divine or higher purpose are called transcendental accomplishments. It teaches that real success transcends ordinary effort and belongs wholly to a higher realm beyond mere material gains.
dheesh_gita::174.modern_relevance: You gave your time and energy to a cause bigger than yourself and saw results that felt meaningful beyond just personal gain.
dheesh_gita::174.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing results to aligning your actions with a higher purpose, recognizing true accomplishment as that alignment.

dheesh_gita::175.verse_sanskrit:
सिद्धयो ज्ञानविज्ञान-प्रकाशिन्यश्च या इह ।
आध्यात्मिक्यश्च सर्वास्ताः सिद्धयः प्रोचिरे बुधैः ॥
dheesh_gita::175.verse_hindi: ज्ञानविज्ञान प्रकाशक सब सिद्धियों को संसार में बुधगण अध्यात्मिक सिद्धियां कहते हैं।
dheesh_gita::175.english_translation: All spiritual accomplishments that illuminate wisdom and knowledge are called spiritual achievements by the wise in this world.
dheesh_gita::175.translation_literal: सिद्धयो (accomplishments) ज्ञानविज्ञान-प्रकाशिन्यश्च (illuminating wisdom and knowledge) या (which) इह (in this world) । आध्यात्मिक्यश्च (and spiritual) सर्वास्ताः (all) सिद्धयः (perfections/accomplishments) प्रोचिरे (are called) बुधैः (by the wise) ॥
dheesh_gita::175.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::175.essence: True achievement is the clear inner wisdom that shines through knowledge.
dheesh_gita::175.simple_meaning: Spiritual achievements are those that bring clear wisdom and knowledge, recognized by wise people everywhere.
dheesh_gita::175.simple_insight: Real accomplishment feels like your inner wisdom shining bright and guiding you.
dheesh_gita::175.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the wise define spiritual achievements as accomplishments that illuminate both wisdom and knowledge, emphasizing the importance of inner spiritual growth beyond external success.
dheesh_gita::175.modern_relevance: When you learn deeply and your understanding lights up, you experience real accomplishment beyond just finishing tasks.
dheesh_gita::175.insight: It shifts focus from external results to inner illumination as the true mark of achievement.

dheesh_gita::176.verse_sanskrit:
भवतां मन्त्रद्रष्ट्रणां सिद्धयोऽन्तर्गता इह ।
नैवात्र विस्मयः कार्यों भवद्भिविमपुङ्गवाः ! ॥
dheesh_gita::176.verse_hindi: मन्त्रद्रष्टा आपलोगों की सिद्धियां हे विप्रश्रेष्ठो! इसी सिद्धि के अन्तर्गत हैं इसमें विस्मय न करो
dheesh_gita::176.english_translation: O best of the wise, the accomplishments of those who perceive mantras lie within this very accomplishment; do not be amazed by anything else here.
dheesh_gita::176.translation_literal: भवतां (your) मन्त्रद्रष्ट्रणां (of the mantra-seers) सिद्धयोऽन्तर्गता (accomplishments are contained) इह (here) । नैवात्र (not here) विस्मयः (amazement) कार्यों (is to be done) भवद्भिविमपुङ्गवाः (O best of the wise) ! ॥
dheesh_gita::176.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::176.essence: True accomplishment lies within inner realization, not in external wonders.
dheesh_gita::176.simple_meaning: The true accomplishments of those who understand sacred teachings are found within themselves; you should not be amazed by anything external.
dheesh_gita::176.simple_insight: There's comfort in knowing your true success is already inside you, beyond appearances.
dheesh_gita::176.detailed_meaning: The narrator addresses wise listeners, explaining that all the true powers and accomplishments of those who understand sacred mantras are contained within their inner realization. No external wonder should distract from this inner truth.
dheesh_gita::176.modern_relevance: You may chase achievements or praise, but real mastery quietly grows inside, unnoticed by others.
dheesh_gita::176.insight: It shifts focus from external validation to inner realization as the true mark of accomplishment.

dheesh_gita::177.verse_sanskrit:
सहजाख्या तु था सिद्धिर्वते विज्ञसत्तमाः!।
एताभ्यः सर्वसिद्धिभ्यः सां नितान्तमलौकिकी ॥
dheesh_gita::177.verse_hindi: परन्तु हे विज्ञवरों ! सहज नाम्नी जो सिद्धि है वह इन सब सिद्धियों से अत्यन्त अलौकिक है
dheesh_gita::177.english_translation: But, O best among the learned, the state called Sahaja is supremely transcendent beyond all other attainments.
dheesh_gita::177.translation_literal: सहजाख्या (called Sahaja) / तु (but) / था (is) / सिद्धिः (attainment) / वते (O learned ones) / विज्ञसत्तमाः (best among the knowledgeable) / एताभ्यः (than these) / सर्वसिद्धिभ्यः (all attainments) / सां (that) / नितान्तम् (completely) / अलौकिकी (transcendent, beyond the world)
dheesh_gita::177.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::177.essence: The natural, effortless state exceeds every other spiritual achievement.
dheesh_gita::177.simple_meaning: The natural, innate state called Sahaja is far beyond all other spiritual achievements or powers.
dheesh_gita::177.simple_insight: You feel awe knowing the simplest true state is the highest attainment.
dheesh_gita::177.detailed_meaning: Suta addresses wise listeners, emphasizing that the effortless, natural state called Sahaja is superior to all complex accomplishments, highlighting its supreme transcendence beyond worldly or spiritual attainments.
dheesh_gita::177.modern_relevance: You might strive for certifications or skills, but the simplest natural state within you is the highest achievement.
dheesh_gita::177.insight: It shifts your focus from chasing many accomplishments to recognizing the supreme value of spontaneous natural being.

dheesh_gita::178.verse_sanskrit:
ममावतारवृन्देऽसौ स्वत एव प्रकाशते।
तत्वज्ञानमहात्मानो मनोनाशेन वै ध्रुवम् ॥
dheesh_gita::178.verse_hindi: मेरे अवतारों में इस सहज सिद्धि का स्वतः ही अत्यन्त विकाश होता है और महापुरुषगण जब तत्ववान वासनाक्षय और मनोनाश के द्वारा
dheesh_gita::178.english_translation: Among my incarnations, this natural realization shines forth on its own; great beings attain it through destroying desires and the mind.
dheesh_gita::178.translation_literal: ममावतारवृन्दे (among my incarnations) / असौ (this) / स्वत (naturally) / एव (indeed) / प्रकाशते (shines forth) / तत्वज्ञानमहात्मनो (of great beings with true knowledge) / मनोनाशेन (by destruction of mind) / वै (indeed) / ध्रुवम् (certainly)
dheesh_gita::178.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::178.essence: True realization naturally arises when desires and restless mind dissolve completely.
dheesh_gita::178.simple_meaning: True realization happens naturally in divine incarnations and in great beings who destroy desires and the restless mind.
dheesh_gita::178.simple_insight: There is a natural clarity waiting when you let go of desires and quiet your mind.
dheesh_gita::178.detailed_meaning: This verse describes how divine incarnations effortlessly embody true understanding, while great spiritual beings achieve it by overcoming desire and calming the restless mind, highlighting two paths to realization.
dheesh_gita::178.modern_relevance: After restless nights and endless wanting, you find clarity emerges naturally when you finally quiet your mind and release craving.
dheesh_gita::178.insight: This verse invites you to see realization as a natural blossoming once desire and mental noise are removed.

dheesh_gita::179.verse_sanskrit:
निर्वासनतया चैवोन्मूलयन्तः स्वजीवताम् ।
शिवरूपीभवन्तश्च समाधौ निर्विकल्पके ॥
dheesh_gita::179.verse_hindi: अपने जीवभाव को निश्चय नाश करके ही शिवस्वरूप हो निर्विकल्प समाधिस्थ
dheesh_gita::179.english_translation: By completely destroying the sense of individual self, one attains the nature of the supreme being and abides in undisturbed, formless absorption.
dheesh_gita::179.translation_literal: निर्वासनतया (by absence of self) चैव (also) ओन्मूलयन्तः (uprooting) स्वजीवताम् (of individual selves) । शिवरूपीभवन्तश्च (becoming like Shiva) समाधौ (in absorption) निर्विकल्पके (without differentiation) ॥
dheesh_gita::179.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::179.essence: Uprooting the separate self reveals the supreme being resting in undisturbed absorption.
dheesh_gita::179.simple_meaning: You must completely let go of your sense of being a separate self to become like the supreme and rest in undisturbed stillness.
dheesh_gita::179.simple_insight: There is freedom in losing the grip on who you think you are.
dheesh_gita::179.detailed_meaning: This verse describes the deep spiritual state where the false sense of separate self (ego) is entirely removed. Achieving this, the practitioner abides as the supreme being in a state of formless, undisturbed meditation called samadhi.
dheesh_gita::179.modern_relevance: When you stop clinging to your personal identity and stories, you find a calm space beyond all mental noise.
dheesh_gita::179.insight: It shifts your focus from identifying with thoughts to resting as pure awareness without distinctions.

dheesh_gita::180.verse_sanskrit:
तिष्ठन्तो यान्ति मय्येव लयमेकान्ततो यदा ।
मदिच्छया तदा तेषु सहजा कहिचिद्भवेत् ॥
dheesh_gita::180.verse_hindi: रहते हुए मुझ में ही एकदम लीन होते हैं तब उनमें मेरी इच्छा से कभी कभी सहज सिद्धि का विकाश हुआ करता है
dheesh_gita::180.english_translation: When they remain completely absorbed in me, then by my will, sometimes a natural perfection arises in them.
dheesh_gita::180.translation_literal: तिष्ठन्तो (remaining) यान्ति (go) मयि (in me) एव (only) लयम् (absorption) एकान्ततः (completely) यदा (when) । मदिच्छया (by my desire) तदा (then) तेषु (in them) सहज (natural) कहिचित् (sometimes) भवेत् (arises) ॥
dheesh_gita::180.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::180.essence: Complete absorption in the divine allows natural transformation to arise by divine will.
dheesh_gita::180.simple_meaning: When you remain completely absorbed in the divine presence, natural growth or perfection sometimes spontaneously arises by divine will.
dheesh_gita::180.simple_insight: You can relax into the divine and allow natural transformation to unfold without force.
dheesh_gita::180.detailed_meaning: In this teaching moment, the teacher explains that when a person remains fully absorbed in the divine, the divine's will sometimes brings about effortless natural perfection within them, showing how devotion opens the way for spontaneous spiritual progress.
dheesh_gita::180.modern_relevance: You’ve felt moments when simply being present and connected brings unexpected growth without effort or planning.
dheesh_gita::180.insight: It teaches you to let go of control and trust that deep absorption in devotion can naturally transform you.

dheesh_gita::181.verse_sanskrit:
उन्नताः सहजा बहव्यः सिद्धयो यद्यपि द्विजाः ।
तास्वहो सन्ति मुख्यास्तु त्रयस्त्रिंशच केवलम् ॥
dheesh_gita::181.verse_hindi: हे ब्राह्मणों ! यद्यपि उच्चश्रेणी की सहज सिद्धियां अनेक है तो भी अहो! उनमें से केवल तैतीस ही मुख्य हैं।
dheesh_gita::181.english_translation: O Brahmins, although there are many natural perfections, only thirty-three are considered principal.
dheesh_gita::181.translation_literal: उन्नताः (elevated) / सहजा (natural) / बहव्यः (many) / सिद्धयो (perfections) / यद्यपि (although) / द्विजाः (twice-born/Brahmins) / तासु (among them) / अहो (oh) / सन्ति (are) / मुख्याः (principal) / तु (indeed) / त्रयः (thirty) / त्रिंशत् (three) / केवलम् (only)
dheesh_gita::181.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::181.essence: Among many natural perfections, only a select few are truly principal.
dheesh_gita::181.simple_meaning: Many natural perfections exist, but only thirty-three are recognized as main or most important.
dheesh_gita::181.simple_insight: Even vast qualities have a few key ones that truly stand out.
dheesh_gita::181.detailed_meaning: Addressing Brahmins, the verse states that among many natural perfections or accomplishments, only thirty-three are regarded as the most important or leading ones, highlighting select qualities as especially significant.
dheesh_gita::181.insight: It encourages focusing on key strengths rather than being overwhelmed by many minor qualities.

dheesh_gita::182.verse_sanskrit:
योगिवृन्देऽवतारेषु जीवन्मुक्तमहात्मनु ।
तपस्विषु प्रकाशन्ते त्रयस्त्रिंशच सिद्धयः ॥
dheesh_gita::182.verse_hindi: अवतारों में, योगियों में और जीवन्मुक्त महापुरुषों तथा तपस्वियों में तैतीस प्रकार की सिद्धियां प्रकट होती हैं
dheesh_gita::182.english_translation: Among incarnations, yogis, liberated great beings, and ascetics, thirty-three kinds of perfections appear.
dheesh_gita::182.translation_literal: योगिवृन्देऽवतारेषु (among incarnations and yogi groups) / जीवन्मुक्तमहात्मनु (liberated great souls) / तपस्विषु (in ascetics) / प्रकाशन्ते (manifest) / त्रयस्त्रिंशच (thirty-three) / सिद्धयः (perfections)
dheesh_gita::182.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::182.essence: True freedom manifests in many diverse extraordinary abilities across realized beings.
dheesh_gita::182.simple_meaning: There are thirty-three types of extraordinary abilities that appear in incarnations, yogis, liberated beings, and ascetics.
dheesh_gita::182.simple_insight: Recognizing diverse manifestations of true freedom inspires trust in the vastness of inner potential.
dheesh_gita::182.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the narrator describes how different kinds of realized beings—incarnations, yogis, liberated souls, and ascetics—display thirty-three distinct spiritual powers, showing the variety and richness of true freedom and mastery.
dheesh_gita::182.modern_relevance: You may see people around you who seem to have unique strengths or calmness that feels beyond ordinary — this verse reminds you these are varied expressions of deep inner freedom.
dheesh_gita::182.insight: It shifts your view to appreciate many forms of mastery beyond common measures, opening curiosity to different spiritual qualities.

dheesh_gita::183.verse_sanskrit:
समाहितैर्भवद्भिस्ताः श्रूयन्तां वर्णयाम्यहम् ।
तासां नामानि पुण्यानि भवतामन्तिके द्विजाः ! ॥
dheesh_gita::183.verse_hindi: हे ब्राह्मणो ! उनके पवित्र नामों का वर्णन आपके समीप करता हूँ उनको आप लोग सावधान होकर सुनो
dheesh_gita::183.english_translation: O Brahmins, I describe here the sacred names of those who are composed; listen carefully to them.
dheesh_gita::183.translation_literal: समाहितैः (composed) भवत्भिः (by you) ताः (those) श्रूयन्तां (may be heard) वर्णयामि (I describe) अहम् (I) तासां (their) नामानि (names) पुण्यानि (sacred) भवतामन्तिके (near you) द्विजाः (Brahmins)
dheesh_gita::183.speaker: Narrator
dheesh_gita::183.essence: Careful attention is needed to receive sacred teaching about composed beings.
dheesh_gita::183.simple_meaning: The speaker invites the Brahmins to attentively hear a description of the sacred names of composed persons near them.
dheesh_gita::183.simple_insight: Inviting careful attention prepares the mind for important knowledge.
dheesh_gita::183.detailed_meaning: As the scene opens, the speaker addresses the Brahmins, asking them to listen attentively as he describes the sacred names of composed individuals near them, setting the stage for an important teaching.
dheesh_gita::183.insight: It shows the importance of focused listening before receiving valuable teachings.

dheesh_gita::184.verse_sanskrit:
एताः सर्वाः सिद्धयो हि वेदशास्त्रेषु वर्णिताः ।
अणिमा लघिमा प्राप्तिः प्राकाम्यं महिमा तथा ॥
dheesh_gita::184.verse_hindi: ये सब सिद्धयां वेद और शास्त्रो में वर्णित है अणिमा, लघिमा, प्राप्ति, प्राकास्य, महिमा,
dheesh_gita::184.english_translation: All these perfections are indeed described in the Vedas and scriptures: subtlety, lightness, attainment, prior existence, and greatness.
dheesh_gita::184.translation_literal: एताः (these) सर्वाः (all) सिद्धयो (perfections) हि (indeed) वेदशास्त्रेषु (in Vedas and scriptures) वर्णिताः (described) । अणिमा (subtlety) लघिमा (lightness) प्राप्तिः (attainment) प्राकाम्यं (prior existence) महिमा (greatness) तथा (also) ॥
dheesh_gita::184.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::184.essence: Ancient wisdom describes subtle, powerful qualities that the true self can attain.
dheesh_gita::184.simple_meaning: Ancient teachings describe special subtle qualities like becoming very small, light, powerful, and existing before all else.
dheesh_gita::184.simple_insight: You carry ancient, subtle qualities that connect you to vast inner powers.
dheesh_gita::184.detailed_meaning: Ancient texts list five special abilities or perfections that a realized being attains: becoming tiny, light, gaining supernatural powers, existing everywhere before others, and having greatness. This verse highlights these as known spiritual achievements.
dheesh_gita::184.modern_relevance: When you feel small or powerless, remember subtle strengths like lightness and greatness already dwell within you, described long ago.
dheesh_gita::184.insight: It teaches you to recognize and trust the hidden, subtle capacities within your own being.

dheesh_gita::185.verse_sanskrit:
वशित्वं गरिमेशित्वे तथा कामावसायिता ।
दूरश्रवणमेवालं परकायप्रवेशनम् ॥
dheesh_gita::185.verse_hindi: वशित्व, गरिमा, ईशित्व, कामावसायिता, दूरश्रवण, परकायप्रवेश,
dheesh_gita::185.english_translation: Control, prestige, mastery, desire, hearing from afar, and entering another's body are all connected to the restless mind.
dheesh_gita::185.translation_literal: वशित्वं (control) / गरिमेशित्वे (prestige and mastery) / तथा (also) / कामावसायिता (desire) / दूरश्रवणमेवालं (hearing from afar alone) / परकायप्रवेशनम् (entering another's body)
dheesh_gita::185.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::185.essence: Feelings of control, pride, desire, and illusions arise from the restless mind.
dheesh_gita::185.simple_meaning: Many feelings like control, pride, desire, and even sensing distant things come from the restless mind.
dheesh_gita::185.simple_insight: You can feel how your mind creates feelings of control and longing that may not be real.
dheesh_gita::185.detailed_meaning: This verse lists experiences—control, prestige, desire, illusions like hearing from afar, and feeling as if entering another's body—that arise due to the restless mind, highlighting how mental activity shapes perception.
dheesh_gita::185.modern_relevance: When you feel jealous of others' success or imagine things beyond your reach, your mind is spinning stories that fuel desire and pride.
dheesh_gita::185.insight: It teaches you to notice that these feelings and illusions are products of your restless mind, not fixed realities.

dheesh_gita::186.verse_sanskrit:
मनोयायित्वभेवेति सर्वज्ञत्वमभीप्सितम् ।
बाद्विस्तम्भो जलस्तम्भः चिरजीवित्वमेव वा ॥
dheesh_gita::186.verse_hindi: मनोयायित्व, अभीप्सित सर्वज्ञत्व, वह्यीस्तम्स, जलस्तम्भ, चिरजी, वित्य,
dheesh_gita::186.english_translation: The desire for mastery over the mind, the wish for omniscience, external obstacles, water barriers, or even long life — none of these are truly sought.
dheesh_gita::186.translation_literal: मनोयायित्व (mind-control) / भेवेति (desires) / सर्वज्ञत्वम् (omniscience) / अभीप्सितम् (desired) / बाद्वि (by external obstacles) / स्तम्भः (barrier) / जलः (water) / स्तम्भः (barrier) / चिरजीवित्वम् (long life) / एव (indeed) / वा (or)
dheesh_gita::186.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::186.essence: True desire is beyond mind control, omniscience, obstacles, and longevity.
dheesh_gita::186.simple_meaning: You might think you want to control your mind, know everything, overcome obstacles, or live forever, but these are not your true desires.
dheesh_gita::186.simple_insight: There's freedom in seeing that these common wishes do not define your deepest longing.
dheesh_gita::186.detailed_meaning: This verse reflects on common human desires—mastery over the restless mind, complete knowledge, overcoming physical barriers, or even long life—suggesting these are not the true goals the inner being seeks.
dheesh_gita::186.modern_relevance: When you chase total control or perfect knowledge, you often miss what truly matters inside.
dheesh_gita::186.insight: It shifts focus from craving external achievements to recognizing deeper, authentic desires beyond surface wishes.

dheesh_gita::187.verse_hindi: वायुस्तम्भ, क्षत्रस्तम्भ, पिपासास्तम्भ, निद्रास्तम्भ, कायव्यूह, वाक् सिद्धि, ईप्सितमृतानयन,
dheesh_gita::187.english_translation: The cessation of breath, hunger, thirst, and sleep, along with the dissolution of the body and the perfection of speech, leads to the desired death.
dheesh_gita::187.translation_literal: वायुस्तम्भः (breath cessation) / क्षुतपिपासानिद्रास्तम्भनमेव (hunger-thirst-sleep cessation indeed) / कायवसृदश्य (body dissolution) / वाकसिद्धिमृतानयनमीप्सितम् (speech perfection desired death)
dheesh_gita::187.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::187.essence: Mastery of bodily urges and speech precedes the wished-for death.
dheesh_gita::187.simple_meaning: Stopping natural urges and dissolving the body are steps toward the desired death and perfection.
dheesh_gita::187.simple_insight: The body and its needs can be transcended, but this verse is part of a larger teaching.
dheesh_gita::187.detailed_meaning: This verse describes advanced yogic practices involving control of bodily functions and urges, culminating in a perfected state and desired death. It is part of a complex teaching, not standalone.
dheesh_gita::187.insight: It shifts focus from physical needs toward mastery over body and speech, but requires broader context to apply.

dheesh_gita::188.verse_sanskrit:
सृष्टिसंहारवर्तृत्वं प्राणार्पणमेव च ।
प्राणानाञ्च प्रदानञ्च लोभादीनाञ्च स्तम्भनम् ॥
dheesh_gita::188.english_translation: Creation, destruction, sustaining life, offering of life force, and control over desires arise from attachment.
dheesh_gita::188.translation_literal: सृष्टिसंहारवर्तृत्वं (creation-destruction-sustaining) / प्राणार्पणमेव (life-force-offering-only) / च (and) / प्राणानाञ्च (of lives) / प्रदानञ्च (giving) / लोभादीनाञ्च (from desires and others) / स्तम्भनम् (restraint)
dheesh_gita::188.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::188.essence: Desire underlies all creation, destruction, life-giving, and self-restraint.
dheesh_gita::188.simple_meaning: The cycles of creation and destruction, sustaining life, offering life, and controlling desires all stem from attachment or desire.
dheesh_gita::188.simple_insight: You feel how desire both creates and binds life’s flow.
dheesh_gita::188.detailed_meaning: The verse explains that the processes of creating, sustaining, and destroying arise together with offering vital energy and controlling desires. These actions are all linked to attachment and desire, showing how desire influences life’s fundamental rhythms.
dheesh_gita::188.modern_relevance: You notice how your wants drive both your energy and your restraint, shaping your daily choices.
dheesh_gita::188.insight: It shifts your view to see desire as the root of both action and self-control, not separate forces.

dheesh_gita::189.verse_sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणां स्तम्भनञ्च बुद्धिस्तम्भनमेव च ।
कल्पवृक्षत्वसत्यानुसन्धाने अमरत्वकम् ॥
dheesh_gita::189.verse_hindi: इन्द्रियस्तम्भन, बुद्धिस्तम्भन, कल्पवृक्षत्व, अमरत्व और सत्यानुसन्धान|
dheesh_gita::189.english_translation: The stopping of the senses and the stopping of the discerning mind, the true pursuit of reality, and the state of immortality are all one.
dheesh_gita::189.translation_literal: इन्द्रियाणां (of senses) स्तम्भनञ्च (stopping) बुद्धिस्तम्भनमेव (discerning mind stopping also) च (and) । कल्पवृक्षत्वसत्यानुसन्धाने (the state of a wish-fulfilling tree and true investigation) अमरत्वकम् (immortality) ॥
dheesh_gita::189.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::189.essence: Stopping senses and mind together reveals the timeless reality beneath appearances.
dheesh_gita::189.simple_meaning: When your senses and discerning mind stop their activity, you reach true understanding and the experience of timelessness.
dheesh_gita::189.simple_insight: You can feel peace by quieting both your senses and your thinking mind.
dheesh_gita::189.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, the speaker explains that controlling the senses and calming the discerning mind together lead to a deep investigation of reality, like a wish-fulfilling tree, revealing immortality beyond ordinary experience.
dheesh_gita::189.modern_relevance: You close your phone, silence distractions, and calm your racing thoughts — that's when you touch something beyond time.
dheesh_gita::189.insight: It teaches you to simultaneously restrain sensory input and quiet mental activity to access profound stillness.

dheesh_gita::190.verse_sanskrit:
अघटयघटनायां या प्रकृतिमे पटीयसी।
जगद्विमोहिनी सैव महामायापराभिधा ॥
dheesh_gita::190.verse_hindi: जो अघटन घटना पटीयसी जगद्विमोहिनी मेरी प्रकृति है और जिसका दूसरा नाम महामाया है वही
dheesh_gita::190.english_translation: The nature that accepts both event and non-event, which deludes the world, is my nature, also called the great illusion.
dheesh_gita::190.translation_literal: अघटयघटनायां (in event and non-event) / या (which) / प्रकृतिमे (my nature) / पटीयसी (accepts) / जगद्विमोहिनी (deluding the world) / सैव (indeed) / महामायापराभिधा (called the great illusion)
dheesh_gita::190.speaker: Shambhu Dheesh
dheesh_gita::190.essence: Your nature embraces all experience, even the illusions that confuse the world.
dheesh_gita::190.simple_meaning: Your essential nature accepts everything that happens and does not happen, creating the illusion that confuses the world.
dheesh_gita::190.simple_insight: There is freedom in knowing your nature includes all experiences, even illusions that seem real.
dheesh_gita::190.detailed_meaning: The divine teacher explains that the true self's nature embraces both events and their absence, which creates the great illusion that confuses the world. This moment reveals the foundational nature behind appearances and confusion.
dheesh_gita::190.modern_relevance: You feel overwhelmed by life's ups and downs, but your true nature quietly holds all experiences without getting lost.
dheesh_gita::190.insight: It teaches you to recognize that your nature includes both change and stability, dissolving confusion.

dheesh_gita::191.verse_sanskrit:
महतो ज्ञानिनश्चैवं योगिनोऽपि तपस्विनः।
सिद्धिसाथैरनेकैर्ही मोह्यंती निरन्तरम् ॥
dheesh_gita::191.verse_hindi: तपसियों को योगियों को और बड़े बड़े ज्ञानियों को भी नानासिद्धियों के द्वारा ही निरन्तर विमोहित करके
dheesh_gita::191.english_translation: Great sages, yogis, and wise ones are continuously deluded by many mystical powers.
dheesh_gita::191.translation_literal: महतो (great) / ज्ञानिनः (wise ones) / च (and) / एवम् (thus) / योगिनः (yogis) / अपि (also) / तपस्विनः (ascetics) / सिद्धिसाथैः (by mystical powers) / अनेकैः (many) / ही (indeed) / मोह्यंती (are deluded) / निरन्तरम् (continuously)
dheesh_gita::191.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::191.essence: Even the most advanced seekers face continuous illusions from powerful distractions.
dheesh_gita::191.simple_meaning: Even the most accomplished wise people, yogis, and ascetics can be constantly misled by various mystical powers.
dheesh_gita::191.simple_insight: It’s humbling and freeing to know that even experts can be deceived and still grow.
dheesh_gita::191.detailed_meaning: This verse reveals that great sages, yogis, and ascetics—despite their advanced spiritual attainments—are often still caught in illusions caused by many mystical powers, showing the subtlety of distractions on the spiritual path.
dheesh_gita::191.modern_relevance: You might have felt confident in your knowledge or discipline, only to find unexpected doubts or distractions pulling you off course.
dheesh_gita::191.insight: Recognize that no matter your progress, subtle distractions can cloud your clarity, inviting ongoing vigilance.

dheesh_gita::192.verse_sanskrit:
आवागमनचक्रेऽस्मिन् स्वविलासात्मके मुहुः ।
मोक्षमार्गञ्च रुन्धना पूर्णयेत समन्ततः ॥
dheesh_gita::192.verse_hindi: मुक्तिमार्ग को रोकती हुई अपने विलास स्वरुप इस अवागमनचक्र मे चारों ओर बार बार  घुमाया करती है
dheesh_gita::192.english_translation: The cycle of coming and going, in its own playful nature, repeatedly obstructs the path to freedom from all sides.
dheesh_gita::192.translation_literal: आवागमनचक्रेऽस्मिन् (in the cycle of coming and going) / स्वविलासात्मके (in its own playful nature) / मुहुः (again and again) / मोक्षमार्गञ्च (the path to freedom) / रुन्धना (blocking) / पूर्णयेत (completely) / समन्ततः (from all sides)
dheesh_gita::192.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::192.essence: Your own restless nature repeatedly blocks your path to freedom.
dheesh_gita::192.simple_meaning: Your own restless habits keep you trapped in cycles that block your path to freedom.
dheesh_gita::192.simple_insight: You can feel how your repeated patterns keep you from moving forward.
dheesh_gita::192.detailed_meaning: This verse describes how the natural cycle of coming and going, driven by one's own inner restlessness and attachments, repeatedly blocks the seeker’s path to liberation. It highlights the inner obstacle as one's own nature rather than an external force.
dheesh_gita::192.modern_relevance: You find yourself stuck in repeating the same mistakes or distractions, unable to move toward your deeper goals despite wanting freedom.
dheesh_gita::192.insight: It teaches you to recognize that your own patterns and inner distractions are the real obstacles to freedom.

dheesh_gita::193.verse_sanskrit:
ब्राह्मणाः प्रकृतिमऽसौ महामायापराभिधा ।
किन्तु मे ज्ञानिनो भक्तान मोहितुं न कदाप्यलम् ॥
dheesh_gita::193.verse_hindi: परन्तु हे ब्राह्मणों! महामायानाम्नी यह मेरी प्रकृति मेरे ज्ञानी भक्तों को कदापि विमोहित नहीं कर सकती
dheesh_gita::193.english_translation: O Brahmins! This nature of mine, called great illusion, can never delude my knowledgeable devotees.
dheesh_gita::193.translation_literal: ब्राह्मणाः (Brahmins) / प्रकृतिमऽसौ (this nature) / महामायापराभिधा (called great illusion) / किन्तु (but) / मे (my) / ज्ञानिनो (knowledgeable) / भक्तान (devotees) / मोहितुं (to delude) / न (not) / कदापि (ever) / अलम् (able)
dheesh_gita::193.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::193.essence: Devoted knowledge makes you immune to the illusion of the natural world.
dheesh_gita::193.simple_meaning: The divine nature may appear as a great illusion, but it can never confuse those who are devoted with knowledge.
dheesh_gita::193.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that sincere devotion keeps your mind clear and steady.
dheesh_gita::193.detailed_meaning: The speaker addresses Brahmins, explaining that although the divine nature appears as a powerful illusion called Maya, it cannot mislead those devoted seekers who possess true understanding. This reassures that devotion combined with wisdom protects from confusion.
dheesh_gita::193.modern_relevance: When distractions and doubts cloud your mind, your sincere trust and understanding keep you steady and clear.
dheesh_gita::193.insight: It teaches you to rely on devoted wisdom as a shield against the mind’s confusion and distractions.

dheesh_gita::194.verse_sanskrit:
कुलाङ्गनानां साध्वीनामङ्गानाशिव दर्शनम् ।
ज्ञानिनां मम भक्तानां भवेत् सिद्धिप्रकाशनम् ॥
dheesh_gita::194.verse_hindi: मेरे ज्ञानी भक्तो का सिद्धियो को प्रकाश करना सती कुल कामिनियों के अंग दिखाने के समान होता है
dheesh_gita::194.english_translation: For my wise devotees, revealing spiritual accomplishments is like showing the limbs of impure women to virtuous women.
dheesh_gita::194.translation_literal: कुलाङ्गनानां (of impure women) साध्वीनाम् (of virtuous women) अङ्गान् (limbs) अशिव (impure) दर्शनम् (showing) । ज्ञानिनाम् (of the wise) मम (my) भक्तानाम् (devotees) भवेत् (is) सिद्धिप्रकाशनम् (revealing spiritual accomplishments) ॥
dheesh_gita::194.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::194.essence: Spiritual accomplishments are precious and must be shared wisely, not carelessly revealed.
dheesh_gita::194.simple_meaning: Revealing spiritual achievements carelessly can be harmful, just like exposing private parts to the wrong people.
dheesh_gita::194.simple_insight: There's wisdom in keeping some spiritual progress private and sacred.
dheesh_gita::194.detailed_meaning: This verse compares showing spiritual accomplishments to exposing private parts of impure women to virtuous women, warning that careless display can cause harm or misunderstanding. It teaches devotees to value discretion and humility in revealing their spiritual growth.
dheesh_gita::194.modern_relevance: You might hesitate to share your inner growth because some people may misunderstand or judge you harshly.
dheesh_gita::194.insight: It teaches you to protect your inner progress by sharing it only with those who understand and respect it.

dheesh_gita::195.verse_sanskrit:
पुरुषांश्च परान् कांश्चिद् यथा काश्चित् कुलाङ्गनाः।
दर्शनाय निजाङ्गानां न क्षमन्ते कदाचन ॥
dheesh_gita::195.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार हे विप्रो! कोई भी कुलकामिनियां कदापि किन्हीं पर-पुरुषों को अपने अंगों को नहीं दिखा सकती
dheesh_gita::195.english_translation: Just as no woman attached to her family can ever show her own limbs to other men,
dheesh_gita::195.translation_literal: पुरुषांश्च (men) / परान् (others) / कांश्चिद् (some) / यथा (just as) / काश्चित् (anyone) / कुलाङगनाः (family-attached women) / दर्शनाय (for showing) / निजाङ्गानां (own limbs) / न (not) / क्षमन्ते (can) / कदाचन (ever)
dheesh_gita::195.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::195.essence: Family loyalty creates natural boundaries that are never crossed.
dheesh_gita::195.simple_meaning: Some women devoted to their family never reveal their own bodies to other men.
dheesh_gita::195.simple_insight: Protecting what is sacred to you creates boundaries that feel natural and necessary.
dheesh_gita::195.detailed_meaning: This verse uses the example of family-attached women who never expose their own bodies to other men. It illustrates cultural boundaries about propriety and respect within relationships, reflecting social norms rather than a universal spiritual teaching.
dheesh_gita::195.insight: Recognize that some social boundaries arise from respect and loyalty within close relationships.

dheesh_gita::196.verse_sanskrit:
भवन्त्युत्कण्ठिताः किन्तु सर्वथा जनसंसदि।
दर्शनाय निजागानां निर्लज्जाः कुलटा मुहुः ॥
dheesh_gita::196.verse_hindi: परन्तु निर्लजा कुलटा अर्थात् व्यभिचारिणी स्त्रियां जनसमाज में सब प्रकार से अपने अंगों को बार बार  दिखाने के लिये उत्कण्ठित रहती हैं
dheesh_gita::196.english_translation: Yet shameless women, driven by desire, repeatedly expose their bodies openly in public gatherings.
dheesh_gita::196.translation_literal: भवन्ति (are) उत्कण्ठिताः (eager) किन्तु (but) सर्वथा (entirely) जनसंसदि (in public gatherings) दर्शनाय (for showing) निजागानां (own body parts) निर्लज्जाः (shameless) कुलटा (immoral women) मुहुः (again and again)
dheesh_gita::196.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::196.essence: Restless craving can cause shameless, repeated public exposure despite social norms.
dheesh_gita::196.simple_meaning: Some women, without shame, repeatedly seek attention by showing themselves openly in public.
dheesh_gita::196.simple_insight: There is a restless craving for attention that can drive shameless behavior in society.
dheesh_gita::196.detailed_meaning: In a public setting, certain women driven by desire show their bodies repeatedly without shame, highlighting social behavior viewed as inappropriate by the narrator.
dheesh_gita::196.insight: It reveals how craving for attention can lead to repeated actions despite social norms.

dheesh_gita::197.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वसामर्थ्यवन्तोऽपि मद्भक्ता ज्ञानिनस्तथा ।
सिद्धिं स्वां नैव भो विप्रा! द्योतयन्ते कदाचन ॥
dheesh_gita::197.verse_hindi: उसी प्रकार मेरे ज्ञानी भक्तगण सर्वसमर्थ होने पर भी अपनी सिद्धि को कदापि प्रकट नहीं करते
dheesh_gita::197.english_translation: Even though my devoted wise ones possess all power, they never reveal their perfection.
dheesh_gita::197.translation_literal: सर्वसामर्थ्यवन्तः (all-powerful) अपि (even) मद्भक्ता (my devotees) ज्ञानिनः (wise ones) तथा (also) सिद्धिम् (perfection) स्वाम् (their own) नैव (never) भो (indeed) विप्रा (wise men) द्योतयन्ते (reveal) कदाचन (ever)
dheesh_gita::197.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::197.essence: True power is revealed through humble silence, not proud display.
dheesh_gita::197.simple_meaning: Devoted and wise people who have achieved great power do not display their accomplishments or seek recognition.
dheesh_gita::197.simple_insight: There is dignity and strength in quiet humility, beyond the need to prove yourself.
dheesh_gita::197.detailed_meaning: The narrator describes how those devoted to the divine and wise in understanding possess great inner power but choose not to reveal their spiritual achievements, showing humility and self-restraint.
dheesh_gita::197.modern_relevance: You may have skills or insights that impress others, yet you choose to stay humble rather than boast or seek praise.
dheesh_gita::197.insight: It encourages shifting from showing off achievements to embodying quiet confidence and letting your growth speak for itself.

dheesh_gita::198.verse_sanskrit:
योगिनों भक्तिहीनास्तु लक्ष्यहीनास्तपस्विनः ।
साधका उग्रकर्म्माणो ज्ञानहीनास्तथा द्विजाः! ॥
dheesh_gita::198.verse_hindi: किन्तु हे ब्राह्मणो ! लक्ष्य हीन तप हीन, भक्ति हीन योगी और ज्ञान हीन उनका साधक वाणिक वृत्ति ले
dheesh_gita::198.english_translation: But O Brahmin, yogis without devotion, ascetics without purpose, practitioners of harsh acts, and twice-born without wisdom are all misguided.
dheesh_gita::198.translation_literal: योगिनों (yogis) भक्तिहीनास्तु (without devotion) लक्ष्यहीनास्तपस्विनः (without purpose ascetics) । साधका (practitioners) उग्रकर्म्माणो (harsh actions) ज्ञानहीनास्तथा (without wisdom also) द्विजाः (twice-born) ॥
dheesh_gita::198.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::198.essence: Effort without devotion, purpose, and wisdom is ineffective and misguided.
dheesh_gita::198.simple_meaning: Effort alone is not enough; without devotion, clear purpose, and wisdom, practices fail to bring true growth.
