dheesh_gita::198.simple_insight: True progress requires more than hard work—it needs heart, clarity, and insight.
dheesh_gita::198.detailed_meaning: The verse warns that yogis without devoted love, ascetics lacking clear purpose, practitioners who perform harsh actions, and learned people without wisdom are all missing essential qualities needed for true spiritual progress.
dheesh_gita::198.modern_relevance: You might push yourself through tasks, but without clear goals, passion, and understanding, your efforts feel hollow and ineffective.
dheesh_gita::198.insight: It teaches you to check if your actions have meaning, love, and clear understanding behind them, not just effort alone.

dheesh_gita::199.verse_sanskrit:
स्वीयाः सिद्धीर्वणिग्वृत्त्या सम्प्रकाश्य पतन्सलम् ।
प्रकाश्याः सिद्धयो नैव सर्वथाऽतो महात्मभिः ॥
dheesh_gita::199.verse_hindi: अपनी सिद्धयो को प्रकट करके अत्यन्त पतित होते हैं; इसलिये सर्वथा महात्माओं को सिद्धियां प्रकाशित नहीं करना चाहिये।
dheesh_gita::199.english_translation: Those who reveal their achievements boastfully fall greatly; therefore, truly noble beings should not display their achievements.
dheesh_gita::199.translation_literal: स्वीयाः (own) सिद्धीः (achievements) वणि-वृत्त्या (with boastful conduct) सम्प्रकाश्य (having revealed) पतन्-शलम् (fall greatly) । प्रकाश्याः (having revealed) सिद्धयः (achievements) नैव (not) सर्वथा (at all) महात्मभिः (by noble beings) ॥
dheesh_gita::199.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::199.essence: Boasting about your achievements leads to downfall; true greatness stays humble and quiet.
dheesh_gita::199.simple_meaning: Showing off your accomplishments with pride leads to a downfall; truly great people keep their achievements private.
dheesh_gita::199.simple_insight: There is safety and dignity in humility rather than in boasting about your success.
dheesh_gita::199.detailed_meaning: This verse warns against revealing one's successes with pride, which leads to downfall. It teaches that noble or great individuals keep their achievements discreet to protect their stature and avoid harm.
dheesh_gita::199.modern_relevance: You feel tempted to post every success online, but sometimes holding back protects your peace and respect more than sharing.
dheesh_gita::199.insight: It teaches you to embrace humility and avoid boasting, preserving your true strength and respect.

dheesh_gita::200.verse_sanskrit:
कदाचिभ्रातरः पुत्रा आत्मीयाः स्वजना उत ।
दैवादनिच्छयेक्षेरन यथाङ्गानि कुलस्त्रियाः ॥
dheesh_gita::200.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार भ्राता पुत्र आत्मीय और स्वजन अनिच्छा से कभी कभी कुल कामिनी का अंग दर्शन दैवात् कर लेते हैं
dheesh_gita::200.english_translation: Just as brothers, sons, and loved ones sometimes unwillingly see parts of the family woman due to fate.
dheesh_gita::200.translation_literal: कदाचि (sometimes) भ्रातरः (brothers) पुत्रा (sons) आत्मीयाः (loved ones) स्वजना (own people) उत (also) दैवाद् (by fate) अनिच्छया (unwillingly) अक्षेरन् (see) यथा (just as) अङ्गानि (parts) कुलस्त्रियाः (family woman)
dheesh_gita::200.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::200.essence: Some experiences happen unwillingly due to forces beyond personal control.
dheesh_gita::200.simple_meaning: Sometimes family members unwillingly see parts of a woman in their family because of fate or circumstance.
dheesh_gita::200.simple_insight: Sometimes people witness things they do not want to see, beyond their control.
dheesh_gita::200.detailed_meaning: This verse describes how brothers, sons, and close relatives sometimes, without desire, are forced by fate to notice aspects of a family woman. It shows how circumstances can compel observation beyond personal wishes.
dheesh_gita::200.insight: It reveals how some events or perceptions happen beyond our will, reminding us to accept situations we cannot change.

dheesh_gita::201.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानिनां मम भक्तानां सिद्धीनां वैभव तथा।
प्रकटत्वं हठादयाति देवाल्लोके कदाचन ॥
dheesh_gita::201.verse_hindi: उसी प्रकार मेरे ज्ञानी भक्तों का सिद्धिवैभव दैवात् कभी कभी जगत् में हठात् प्रकाशित हो जाता है
dheesh_gita::201.english_translation: Just as the perfected wisdom of my devoted followers sometimes suddenly manifests in the world of beings.
dheesh_gita::201.translation_literal: ज्ञानिनां (of the wise) / मम (my) / भक्तानां (devoted) / सिद्धीनां (perfected) / वैभव (glory) / तथा (also) / प्रकटत्वं (manifestation) / हठात् (suddenly) / अयाति (comes) / देवल्लोके (in the world of beings) / कदाचन (sometimes)
dheesh_gita::201.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::201.essence: Deep devotion and wisdom can suddenly manifest their power in the world.
dheesh_gita::201.simple_meaning: Sometimes, the perfected achievements of deeply devoted and wise followers suddenly become visible in the world.
dheesh_gita::201.simple_insight: There is hope in knowing your inner growth can show up unexpectedly and powerfully.
dheesh_gita::201.detailed_meaning: Shri Dheesh explains that the remarkable qualities of those who combine deep wisdom and devoted love sometimes appear suddenly and powerfully in the world, revealing their inner strength beyond ordinary perception.
dheesh_gita::201.modern_relevance: At moments you least expect, your quiet dedication and insight can suddenly become clear to others, even if you never sought recognition.
dheesh_gita::201.insight: It teaches you to trust that your growth and effort can reveal themselves spontaneously without forcing or timing them.

dheesh_gita::202.verse_sanskrit:
हस्ताभ्यां मे यथा सिद्धिद्धाभ्यां विप्रा निरन्तरम् ।
मायामोहितजीवेभ्यः शक्त्यर्थो प्रददत्यलम् ॥
dheesh_gita::202.verse_hindi: हे विप्रो ! मेरी सिद्धि जिस प्रकार दो हाथोंसे मायाविमोहित जीवों को निरन्तर अर्थ और शक्ति को भलीभांति देती हुई
dheesh_gita::202.english_translation: O wise one, just as my two hands continuously grant power and purpose to beings deluded by illusion.
dheesh_gita::202.translation_literal: हस्ताभ्यां (with two hands) मे (my) सिद्धिद्धाभ्यां (to the perfected) विप्रा (O wise one) निरन्तरम् (continuously) मायामोहितजीवेभ्यः (to beings deluded by illusion) शक्त्यर्थो (power and purpose) प्रददत्यलम् (I bestow)
dheesh_gita::202.speaker: Shambhu Dheesh
dheesh_gita::202.essence: You receive steady strength and purpose even when clouded by illusion.
dheesh_gita::202.simple_meaning: You are continuously given strength and a meaningful purpose, even when confused by illusion.
dheesh_gita::202.simple_insight: There is comfort knowing you are supported even when you feel lost or confused.
dheesh_gita::202.detailed_meaning: The speaker assures the wise being that just like his hands constantly give strength and purpose, beings confused by illusion are never abandoned but continuously supported.
dheesh_gita::202.modern_relevance: When doubts cloud your mind and you feel overwhelmed, remember unseen forces keep empowering you steadily.
dheesh_gita::202.insight: It shifts your view from isolation in confusion to trust in ongoing unseen support.

dheesh_gita::203.verse_sanskrit:
बध्नात्यस्मिन् हि संसारे कारागारे चिरन्तने ।
तथाऽन्याभ्यां स्वहस्नाभ्यां धर्मार्थों वितरन्त्यहो ॥
dheesh_gita::203.verse_hindi: चिरन्तन कारागार रूपी संसार में फंसा रखती है, उसी प्रकार अपने अन्य दो हाथों से धर्म और अर्थ देती हुई
dheesh_gita::203.english_translation: In this long-lasting prison called the cycle of reactivity, the divine holds you fast with one hand while giving religion and wealth with the other two.
dheesh_gita::203.translation_literal: बध्नाति (binds) अस्मिन् (in this) हि (indeed) संसारे (in the cycle of reactivity) कारागारे (in prison) चिरन्तने (long-lasting) । तथाऽन्याभ्यां (thus with the other) स्वहस्नाभ्यां (own two hands) धर्मार्थों (religion and wealth) वितरन्त्यहो (giving) ॥
dheesh_gita::203.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::203.essence: The cycle of reactivity traps you while offering rewards that deepen the hold.
dheesh_gita::203.simple_meaning: The endless cycle of reactivity traps you like a prison, but at the same time offers religion and wealth as distractions or promises.
dheesh_gita::203.simple_insight: There's a tension between feeling trapped and being tempted by what seems valuable in life.
dheesh_gita::203.detailed_meaning: Suta describes the cycle of reactivity as a long-lasting prison that binds beings tightly. Despite this captivity, the same cycle offers religion and wealth through other means, creating an illusion of freedom and reward while keeping one trapped.
dheesh_gita::203.modern_relevance: You feel stuck in routines and pressures but still chase status and purpose that keep you tied down.
dheesh_gita::203.insight: Recognize how attractions to purpose and rewards can also be chains, not just freedoms.

dheesh_gita::204.verse_sanskrit:
मदत्ते ज्ञानिभक्तेभ्यः कैवल्याभ्युदयो ध्रुवम् ।
साधका मोहिता अज्ञाः कर्मस्वासक्तमानसाः ॥
dheesh_gita::204.verse_hindi: ज्ञानीभक्तों को अभ्युदय और निःश्रेयस अवश्य प्रदान करती है। मोहित, ज्ञानहीन, कर्मासक्तचित्त साधक
dheesh_gita::204.english_translation: For the wise and devoted, liberation surely arises; but for deluded, ignorant, and action-attached seekers, it does not.
dheesh_gita::204.translation_literal: मदत्ते (arises) ज्ञानि-भक्तेभ्यः (to the wise and devoted) कैवल्य-ाभ्युदयो (liberation and rise) ध्रुवम् (certainly) । साधका (seekers) मोहिता (deluded) अज्ञाः (ignorant) कर्म-स्वासक्त-मानसाः (with minds attached to action) ॥
dheesh_gita::204.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::204.essence: True freedom arises only when wisdom and devoted love come together, not from mere action.
dheesh_gita::204.simple_meaning: Freedom or liberation definitely arises for those who combine wisdom and devoted love. But seekers who are confused, ignorant, and attached to their actions do not reach it.
dheesh_gita::204.simple_insight: You can feel hope knowing clear understanding and devotion open freedom’s door.
dheesh_gita::204.detailed_meaning: This verse contrasts two types of seekers: those who have wisdom and devoted love, who will certainly attain liberation, and those who are confused, ignorant, and fixated on their actions, who remain bound. This teaching appears at a moment clarifying what truly leads beyond the cycle of reactivity.
dheesh_gita::204.modern_relevance: You might know people who chase success without deeper understanding or care, staying stuck; this shows how wisdom and heartfelt devotion help break free.
dheesh_gita::204.insight: It teaches you to combine clear understanding with heartfelt devotion rather than relying only on busy doing.

dheesh_gita::205.verse_sanskrit:
माययोत्पादिताः सिद्धीः संसारे क्षणभङ्गराः।
परिणामस्वभावा हि लब्ध्वा तत्सेवया मुहुः ॥
dheesh_gita::205.verse_hindi: क्षणभङ्गर परिणामशील और माया से उत्पन्न सिद्धियो को संसार में प्राप्त करके उनकी सेवा द्वारा बार बार
dheesh_gita::205.english_translation: Powers born of illusion are fleeting in the cycle of change; their nature is to transform, so even after gaining them, you will repeatedly serve their results.
dheesh_gita::205.translation_literal: मायया (by illusion) उत्पादिताः (produced) सिद्धयः (powers) संसार (in the world) क्षणभङ्गराः (momentary/fleeting) । परिणामस्वभावाः (by nature of change) हि (indeed) लब्ध्वा (having obtained) तत् (that) सेवया (by service) मुहुः (again and again) ।
dheesh_gita::205.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::205.essence: Powers born of illusion are fleeting and repeatedly bind those who seek them.
dheesh_gita::205.simple_meaning: Powers created by illusion are temporary and always changing. Even after gaining them, you end up serving their effects over and over.
dheesh_gita::205.simple_insight: There’s relief in seeing that chasing illusory powers only leads to repeated cycles of attachment.
dheesh_gita::205.detailed_meaning: In the midst of worldly change, many seek special powers that come from illusion. But these powers fade quickly, and their changing nature traps the seeker into serving their consequences repeatedly. This teaching highlights the futility of chasing such transient gains.
dheesh_gita::205.modern_relevance: You finally get a promotion or a prized possession, but the satisfaction fades fast, and you find yourself chasing the next thing again.
dheesh_gita::205.insight: It teaches you to recognize how chasing fleeting achievements only pulls you back into the cycle of desire and service.

dheesh_gita::206.verse_sanskrit:
नरके स्वर्गलोके च लोकयोः पितृप्रेतयोः ।
नित्यं घूयमानास्ते सन्तप्यन्ते त्रितापतः ॥
dheesh_gita::206.verse_hindi: नरकलोक, स्वर्गलोक प्रेतलोक और पितृलोक में नित्य घूमते हुए वह त्रिताप से तापित होते रहते हैं
dheesh_gita::206.english_translation: Those who wander constantly among the realms of hell, heaven, ancestors, and spirits endure suffering from the threefold pain.
dheesh_gita::206.translation_literal: नरके (in hell) / स्वर्गलोके (in heaven) / च (and) / लोकयोः (in realms) / पितृप्रेतयोः (of ancestors and spirits) / नित्यं (constantly) / घूयमानास्ते (they wander) / सन्तप्यन्ते (are tormented) / त्रितापतः (by threefold pain)
dheesh_gita::206.speaker: Narrator
dheesh_gita::206.essence: Endless wandering through realms does not end inner suffering.
dheesh_gita::206.simple_meaning: Some beings endlessly roam different realms but remain trapped in suffering from threefold pain.
dheesh_gita::206.simple_insight: Endless wandering in different states does not free from suffering.
dheesh_gita::206.detailed_meaning: The narrator describes beings who endlessly move through various realms, including hell, heaven, ancestors, and spirits, yet they continue to suffer the threefold pain, indicating that mere movement among realms does not end distress.
dheesh_gita::206.insight: It shows that changing external circumstances alone cannot end inner suffering.

dheesh_gita::207.verse_sanskrit:
किन्तु मे ज्ञानिनो भक्ताः परमानन्दसागरम् ।
स्वरूपं तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा सचिदानन्दरूपकम् ॥
dheesh_gita::207.verse_hindi: परन्तु मेरे ज्ञानी भक्तगण परमानन्दसागर सचिदानन्दमय स्वरूप को यथार्थ रूप से जानकर
dheesh_gita::207.english_translation: But my wise devotees, having truly known the supreme blissful essence of consciousness and existence,
dheesh_gita::207.translation_literal:
किन्तु (but) मे (my) ज्ञानिनो (wise) भक्ताः (devotees) परमानन्दसागरम् (supreme bliss ocean) ।
स्वरूपं (form) तत्त्वतो (truly) ज्ञात्वा (knowing) सचिदानन्दरूपकम् (consciousness-existence-bliss form) ॥
dheesh_gita::207.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::207.essence: True devotion arises from deeply knowing your blissful conscious self.
dheesh_gita::207.simple_meaning: Those who truly understand their own blissful and conscious true nature become devoted in the deepest way.
dheesh_gita::207.simple_insight: Knowing your true blissful self brings a devotion that goes beyond simple faith or learning.
dheesh_gita::207.detailed_meaning: The verse speaks to wise devotees who have deeply realized their own true essence as an ocean of supreme bliss united with consciousness and existence. This realization transforms their devotion into something profound and unshakable.
dheesh_gita::207.modern_relevance: When you experience your own deepest joy and true self, your connection to life and love becomes more heartfelt and genuine.
dheesh_gita::207.insight: It teaches you to connect devotion with direct experience of your true nature rather than just belief.

dheesh_gita::208.verse_sanskrit:
समस्तसिद्धिसर्वस्वं मामेव प्राप्नुवन्त्यलम् ।
निरापदं पदं श्रेष्ठमधिकुर्वन्ति मे ततः ॥
dheesh_gita::208.verse_hindi: समस्त सिद्धियों का सर्वस्व अर्थात् परमसिद्धि रूपी मुझको ही भलीभांति प्राप्त करते हैं उसके बाद मेरे परमपद के अनायास अधिकारी हो जाते है
dheesh_gita::208.english_translation: All perfections and the highest attainments come to me alone; thereafter, they easily become rightful to my supreme state.
dheesh_gita::208.translation_literal: समस्त (all) सिद्धिसर्वस्वं (perfections and all wealth) मामेव (to me alone) प्राप्नुवन्ति (attain) अलम् (only) । निरापदं (without fault) पदं (state) श्रेष्ठम् (highest) अधिकुर्वन्ति (make) मे (my) ततः (thereafter) ॥
dheesh_gita::208.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::208.essence: All highest attainments begin within and naturally lead to your supreme state.
dheesh_gita::208.simple_meaning: Every highest perfection and attainment comes to the true self first, making the supreme state naturally accessible.
dheesh_gita::208.simple_insight: You can trust that all true excellence begins within you, opening the way to your highest state.
dheesh_gita::208.detailed_meaning: This verse expresses that all ultimate achievements and perfections arise first in the true self, making the supreme state effortless and secure thereafter. It highlights the divine source within that grounds all spiritual progress.
dheesh_gita::208.modern_relevance: When you realize your own inner strength and growth, the path to your fullest potential feels natural and assured.
dheesh_gita::208.insight: It shifts focus from external achievements to recognizing your inner source as the foundation of all true success.

dheesh_gita::209.verse_sanskrit:
मच्छक्तिरूपिणी सिद्धिः प्रभावात्यन्तशोभिनी ।
मद्भक्तोर्विमुखाञ्जीवान मत्तोऽलञ्च  निवर्त्य सा ॥
dheesh_gita::209.verse_hindi: मेरी शक्तिरूपिणी सिद्धि अति प्रभावशालिनी है।  वह मुझमें भक्तिहीन जीवों को मुझसे अत्यन्त विमुख करके
dheesh_gita::209.english_translation: My power called Siddhi is supremely glorious; it turns beings without devotion away from me and returns to me.
dheesh_gita::209.translation_literal: मच्छक्तिरूपिणी (my power in form) / सिद्धिः (Siddhi) / प्रभावात्यन्तशोभिनी (supremely glorious) / मद्भक्तोर्विमुखाञ्जीवान (beings without my devotion turned away) / मत्तः (from me) / अलञ्च (also) / निवर्त्य (returns) / सा (she)
dheesh_gita::209.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::209.essence: Without devotion, even the greatest power turns away and withdraws.
dheesh_gita::209.simple_meaning: Power that flows through devotion is radiant and effective; without devotion, beings turn away and the power withdraws.
dheesh_gita::209.simple_insight: You see how devotion is the key that keeps the divine power close to you.
dheesh_gita::209.detailed_meaning: The verse describes a divine power named Siddhi, radiant and supreme, which sustains beings only if they have devotion. Those lacking devotion turn away, causing this power to withdraw, highlighting devotion's central role.
dheesh_gita::209.modern_relevance: When you lose passion or heartfelt connection to your purpose, your inner energy and effectiveness fade away.
dheesh_gita::209.insight: It teaches you that heartfelt devotion or sincere connection is essential to sustain your strength and influence.

dheesh_gita::210.verse_sanskrit:
संसारापारपाथोधावज्ञानावर्तसम्भ्रमे ।
निपात्य नितरां शश्वत् क्लिश्नातीह महर्षयः ॥
dheesh_gita::210.verse_hindi: और अज्ञान रूपी आवर्त (जलभंवर) से संकुल इस संसाररूपी अपार समुद्र में निरन्तर गिराकर सर्वदा क्लेशित करती है ।
dheesh_gita::210.english_translation: The great sages are constantly overwhelmed by the endless ocean of worldly existence, caught in the whirlpool of ignorance and confusion.
dheesh_gita::210.translation_literal: संसारापारपाथोधावज्ञानावर्तसम्भ्रमे (in the endless ocean of worldly existence, from the whirlpool of ignorance and confusion) / निपात्य (throwing down) / नितरां (constantly) / शश्वत् (always) / क्लिश्नाति (are distressed) / इह (here) / महर्षयः (the great sages)
dheesh_gita::210.speaker: Narrator
dheesh_gita::210.essence: Even great sages are deeply troubled by the confusion within endless worldly existence.
dheesh_gita::210.simple_meaning: Great sages suffer continuously, caught in the vast ocean of worldly life and trapped by the whirlpool of ignorance and confusion.
dheesh_gita::210.simple_insight: Even the wisest can be overwhelmed by deep confusion in the cycle of life.
dheesh_gita::210.detailed_meaning: The verse describes the great sages who, despite their wisdom, find themselves struggling within the vast and confusing cycle of worldly existence. They are tossed by the endless ocean of life, caught in the whirlpool of ignorance and mental turmoil.
dheesh_gita::210.modern_relevance: You may feel lost in overwhelming confusion, like being stuck in a stormy sea with no clear direction.
dheesh_gita::210.insight: It reveals that confusion and suffering are common even among the wise, highlighting the universal challenge of transcending ignorance.

dheesh_gita::211.verse_sanskrit:
भजतोऽनन्यभक्तया मां भूयोऽसौ साधकान वरान् ।
मत्समीपं समानीय कृतार्थान् कुरुते द्रुतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::211.verse_hindi: और पुनः वह मुझमें अनन्य भक्ति करनेवाले श्रेष्ठ साधकों को मेरे निकट पहुंचा कर शीघ्र कृतार्थ कर देती है
dheesh_gita::211.english_translation: The divine brings those who worship exclusively to the highest seekers near, swiftly fulfilling them completely.
dheesh_gita::211.translation_literal: भजतोऽनन्यभक्तया (worshipping with exclusive devotion) / मां (me) / भूयोऽसौ (again that) / साधकान (seekers) / वरान् (best) / मत्समीपं (near me) / समानीय (bringing) / कृतार्थान् (fulfilled) / कुरुते (makes) / द्रुतम् (quickly)
dheesh_gita::211.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::211.essence: Exclusive devotion draws you near and brings quick, complete fulfillment.
dheesh_gita::211.simple_meaning: Those who worship with exclusive devotion are brought near to the divine and quickly become fulfilled.
dheesh_gita::211.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing sincere devotion is met with swift support and fulfillment.
dheesh_gita::211.detailed_meaning: The text describes how the divine responds to sincere worship. Those who devote themselves exclusively are brought close and quickly experience fulfillment, highlighting the power of devoted love in the spiritual journey.
dheesh_gita::211.modern_relevance: When you focus your heart fully on what matters most, support and results tend to come faster than expected.
dheesh_gita::211.insight: It teaches you to deepen your devotion, trusting that wholehearted focus invites swift positive transformation.

dheesh_gita::212.verse_sanskrit:
यथा स्नेहमयी माता स्वात्मजानतियत्नतः ।
वर्द्धयन्ती प्रसादेन पुष्णन्ती पालयन्त्यपि ॥
dheesh_gita::212.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार स्नेहमयी माता अपने पुत्रो को बड़े यत्न से पालती पोसती और प्रसन्नता से बढ़ाती हुई
dheesh_gita::212.english_translation: Just as a loving mother carefully knows her own child and lovingly nurtures, nourishes, and protects it with joy.
dheesh_gita::212.translation_literal: यथा (just as) स्नेहमयी (loving) माता (mother) स्वात्मजानति (knows her own child) यत्नतः (with effort) वर्द्धयन्ती (growing) प्रसादेन (with kindness) पुष्णन्ती (nourishing) पालयन्ति (protecting) अपि (also)
dheesh_gita::212.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::212.essence: You are lovingly nurtured and protected just like a child by its mother.
dheesh_gita::212.simple_meaning: You are cared for tenderly and joyfully, just like a loving mother cares for her child.
dheesh_gita::212.simple_insight: You can feel safe knowing you are nurtured with deep, affectionate care.
dheesh_gita::212.detailed_meaning: The verse compares the divine care to a loving mother who knows her child's needs intimately and protects with joy. It expresses the warmth and devoted care offered even before any request.
dheesh_gita::212.modern_relevance: When you feel vulnerable or overwhelmed, remember how a mother's loving care protects and nurtures you unconditionally.
dheesh_gita::212.insight: It invites you to receive care openly, trusting that loving support is always present.

dheesh_gita::213.verse_sanskrit:
अधिकारयते क्षिप्रं परमं मङ्गलास्पदम् ।
तथा कारुण्यपूर्णाऽसौ सिद्धिर्मातेव सर्वदा ॥
dheesh_gita::213.verse_hindi: परम मङ्गलमय अधिकार को शीघ्र प्राप्त करा देती है उसी प्रकार करुणामयी यह सिद्धि सदा माता के समान
dheesh_gita::213.english_translation: The highest auspicious authority is quickly attained, and similarly, this compassionate perfection is always like a mother.
dheesh_gita::213.translation_literal: अधिकारयते (grants) क्षिप्रं (quickly) परमं (highest) मङ्गलास्पदम् (auspiciousness) । / तथा (thus) कारुण्यपूर्णा (full of compassion) असौ (that) सिद्धिः (perfection) मतेव (like) सर्वदा (always) ॥
dheesh_gita::213.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::213.essence: Compassion grants swift highest blessing like a constant, caring mother.
dheesh_gita::213.simple_meaning: You can quickly attain the greatest blessing when you trust in compassion, which is always like a caring mother.
dheesh_gita::213.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing compassion supports you like a steady, loving mother.
dheesh_gita::213.detailed_meaning: This verse teaches that the highest auspicious power or authority is quickly granted. It compares this perfection to a compassionate mother, emphasizing that such kindness is constant and nurturing.
dheesh_gita::213.modern_relevance: When you face difficult moments, feeling compassion like a mother's care can quickly bring you strength and peace.
dheesh_gita::213.insight: It shifts your trust toward compassion as a nurturing force that swiftly brings blessings.

dheesh_gita::214.verse_hindi: आर्त जिज्ञासु और अर्थार्थी इन मेरे त्रिविध भक्तों को निश्चय ही परम आनन्द समूह और उत्साह भलीभांति देती हुई
dheesh_gita::214.english_translation: I surely give my threefold devotees—those in distress, seekers of meaning, and those desiring gain—supreme joy, enthusiasm, and delight.
dheesh_gita::214.translation_literal: आर्त्त (distressed) / अनर्थार्थीनः (those seeking relief from misfortune) / भक्तान् (devotees) / जिज्ञासून् (seekers) / त्रि-निमान् (threefold) / मम (my) / नृन (men) / आनंद (joy) / सन्दोमुत्साहञ्च (delight and enthusiasm) / ददति (gives) / अलम् (certainly)
dheesh_gita::214.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::214.essence: Devotion blesses seekers, sufferers, and desiring hearts with joy and enthusiasm.
dheesh_gita::214.simple_meaning: Devotion brings joy and enthusiasm to three kinds of followers: those in pain, those searching for meaning, and those wanting success.
dheesh_gita::214.simple_insight: No matter your struggle or desire, devotion can fill you with joy and energy.
dheesh_gita::214.detailed_meaning: The verse addresses three groups of devotees: those suffering (aartta), those seeking understanding (jijnasa), and those desiring results (artharthi). The speaker assures that each will receive great joy and enthusiasm through their devoted connection.
dheesh_gita::214.modern_relevance: When you're overwhelmed by hardship, curiosity, or ambition, holding devotion can bring unexpected joy and renewed energy.
dheesh_gita::214.insight: It teaches you to embrace devotion through any life state—pain, inquiry, or desire—and find joyful strength.

dheesh_gita::215.verse_sanskrit:
विघतेऽग्रेसरान क्षिप्रमाभिमुख्येन मे च तान ।
मम सेवारतायाश्च स्वरूपं प्रकृतदिधा ॥
dheesh_gita::215.verse_hindi: उनको शीघ्र मेरी ओर अग्रसर करती है । मेरी सेवा में रत प्रकृति  के स्वरूप दो प्रकार से विभक्त है,
dheesh_gita::215.english_translation: The two aspects of my nature swiftly move forward toward me, engaged in my service.
dheesh_gita::215.translation_literal: विघतेऽग्रेसरान (disperse leaders) / क्षिप्रमाभिमुख्येन (swiftly forward-facing) / मे (my) / च (and) / तान (those) / मम (my) / सेवारतायाश्च (engaged in service) / स्वरूपं (form) / प्रकृतदिधा (twofold nature)
dheesh_gita::215.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::215.essence: Two parts of my nature move quickly to serve me.
dheesh_gita::215.simple_meaning: Two aspects of my nature move quickly toward me, both involved in service.
dheesh_gita::215.simple_insight: There is a dynamic unfolding within that supports devoted action.
dheesh_gita::215.detailed_meaning: This verse describes two aspects of the speaker's nature moving swiftly toward the speaker, both engaged in service. It reflects an internal movement but lacks wider context, making it hard to isolate as a standalone teaching.
dheesh_gita::215.insight: It hints that the inner nature actively participates in service, suggesting dynamic engagement within.

dheesh_gita::216.verse_sanskrit:
विभक्तं वर्तते विज्ञा: ! नात्र कार्या विचारणा।
एका पराभिधा ज्ञेया द्वितीयाऽपरनामिका ॥
dheesh_gita::216.verse_hindi: हे विज्ञवरों ! इसमें विचारने की कोई बात नहीं है, एक को परा और एक को अपरा जानो
dheesh_gita::216.english_translation: O wise ones! There is no need for debate here: one is the supreme, the other is the non-supreme.
dheesh_gita::216.translation_literal: विभक्तं (divided) / वर्तते (exists) / विज्ञा: (wise ones) / नात्र (not here) / कार्या (to be done) / विचारणा (debate) / एका (one) / पराभिधा (supreme) / ज्ञेया (to be known) / द्वितीयाऽपरनामिका (second is the non-supreme)
dheesh_gita::216.speaker: Teacher
dheesh_gita::216.essence: Reality divides simply into supreme and non-supreme without confusion.
dheesh_gita::216.simple_meaning: There is no confusion: understand that one reality is supreme and the other is not.
dheesh_gita::216.simple_insight: Clarity brings relief when you see things as simply supreme and non-supreme.
dheesh_gita::216.detailed_meaning: The teacher clarifies to the wise listeners that the complex debate is unnecessary; reality divides simply into the supreme and the non-supreme, setting the stage for deeper understanding.
dheesh_gita::216.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by complexity, you find peace by seeing the clear difference between what truly matters and what does not.
dheesh_gita::216.insight: It teaches you to stop overcomplicating and recognize the fundamental division in reality.

dheesh_gita::217.verse_sanskrit:
अपरानामिका जीवान प्रकृतिमेऽखिलानलम् ।
गुणत्रयात्मके जाले स्वस्मिन्नाश्लिष्य मायया ॥
dheesh_gita::217.verse_hindi: अपरा नाम की मेरी प्रकृति अपने त्रिगुणात्मक जाल में सब जीवों को माया से  फंसा कर
dheesh_gita::217.english_translation: The lower nature, made of the three qualities, entangles all living beings in the web of illusion within itself.
dheesh_gita::217.translation_literal: अपरानामिका (lower named) / जीवान (living beings) / प्रकृतिमेऽखिलानलम् (in nature, all-fire) / गुणत्रयात्मके (of the three qualities, nature) / जाले (in the net) / स्वस्मिन्नाश्लिष्य (trapping in itself) / मायया (by illusion)
dheesh_gita::217.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::217.essence: The three qualities of nature trap all beings in illusion within themselves.
dheesh_gita::217.simple_meaning: Your lower nature, made of three basic qualities, traps all living beings in a web of illusion.
dheesh_gita::217.simple_insight: You can feel how your natural tendencies shape what traps you in confusion.
dheesh_gita::217.detailed_meaning: This verse explains that the lower part of your nature, composed of three qualities (guna), holds all living beings captive within a deceptive web called illusion (maya). It sets the stage for understanding how the natural world entangles the true self.
dheesh_gita::217.modern_relevance: When you notice your moods and impulses pulling you into confusion, that’s your nature’s web of qualities at work.
dheesh_gita::217.insight: Recognize how your three basic qualities create patterns that trap your awareness in illusion.

dheesh_gita::218.verse_sanskrit:
इन्द्रस्यानुभवं तैश्च कारयन्ती निरन्तरम् ।
स्वविलासात्मकं लीलामयं जनयते जगत् ॥
dheesh_gita::218.verse_hindi: उनको द्वन्द्व का अनुभव निरन्तर कराती हुई अपने विलासरूपी लीलामय संसार को प्रकट करती है
dheesh_gita::218.english_translation: The duality experienced by Indra continuously causes the playful, self-expressive world to manifest.
dheesh_gita::218.translation_literal: इन्द्रस्यानुभवं (Indra's experience) / तैश्च (by them) / कारयन्ती (causing) / निरन्तरम् (continuously) / स्वविलासात्मकं (self-playful) / लीलामयं (playful) / जनयते (creates) / जगत् (the world)
dheesh_gita::218.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::218.essence: The world is a continuous playful expression born from experiencing duality within.
dheesh_gita::218.simple_meaning: The world appears as a playful expression arising from the ongoing experience of duality within consciousness.
dheesh_gita::218.simple_insight: You can see your inner conflicts as the source of the world's lively, creative play.
dheesh_gita::218.detailed_meaning: Indra, as a symbol of consciousness, experiences duality—opposites like pleasure and pain—which continuously causes the world to appear as a playful, creative expression. This verse reveals the world as a dynamic dance born from inner contrasts.
dheesh_gita::218.modern_relevance: When your mind swings between opposing feelings, you create the colorful, ever-changing reality you live in.
dheesh_gita::218.insight: It teaches you to recognize how your inner dual experiences shape your perception of the world as a creative play.

dheesh_gita::219.verse_sanskrit:
परा में प्रकृनिर्धन्या साधकानां ह्रदम्बुजे।
भ्रद्रावली  पराभक्ति सन्निवेश्य महर्षयः ! ॥
dheesh_gita::219.verse_hindi: और हे महर्षिगण ! मेरी धन्या परा प्रकृति साधकों के ह्रदय पल में मेरी भक्ति रूपिणी भृंगावली को संनिविष्ट करके
dheesh_gita::219.english_translation: O great sages! In the heart-lotus of sincere seekers deprived of higher nature, I reside as devoted loving care.
dheesh_gita::219.translation_literal: परा (higher) / में (in) / प्रकृनि (nature) / निर्धन्या (deprived) / साधकानां (of seekers) / ह्रदम्बुजे (in the heart-lotus); भ्रद्रावली (devoted loving care) /  पराभक्ति (supreme devotion) / सन्निवेश्य (residing) / महर्षयः (O great sages)!
dheesh_gita::219.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::219.essence: Devoted love quietly inhabits the heart even when higher nature feels absent.
dheesh_gita::219.simple_meaning: Within those who lack higher nature, devoted loving care quietly resides in the heart.
dheesh_gita::219.simple_insight: Even when you feel empty inside, devoted love can still quietly grow in your heart.
dheesh_gita::219.detailed_meaning: Addressing great sages, the verse reveals that even seekers who lack refined higher nature carry within their heart a quiet, devoted loving care, symbolized as a bee, showing that devotion can dwell deeply despite internal poverty.
dheesh_gita::219.modern_relevance: When you feel disconnected or lacking in confidence, a quiet devoted care still lives inside you, ready to guide your heart.
dheesh_gita::219.insight: It shifts your view from external lack to recognizing devotion already present within your heart.

dheesh_gita::220.verse_sanskrit:
वीक्षयन्ती त्रयाणाञ्च गुणानां वैभवं मुहुः।
 द्वन्द्वातीतं पदं नीत्वा मामेनान दर्शयत्यहो ॥
dheesh_gita::220.verse_hindi: त्रिगुणा वैभव को बार बार  दर्शन कराती हुई उनको द्वन्दातीत पद में पहुंचा कर अहो ! मेरा दर्शन करा देती है
dheesh_gita::220.english_translation: Repeatedly observing the grandeur of the three qualities, she leads them beyond duality to reveal me.
dheesh_gita::220.translation_literal: वीक्षयन्ती (observing) त्रयाणाञ्च (of the three) गुणानां (qualities) वैभवं (grandeur) मुहुः (repeatedly) द्वन्द्वातीतं (beyond duality) पदं (state) नीत्वा (leading) माम् (me) एना (by her) दर्शयत्य (shows) अहो (ah, behold)
dheesh_gita::220.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::220.essence: You can witness the three qualities and still stand beyond all duality.
dheesh_gita::220.simple_meaning: The restless mind repeatedly sees the three qualities and is guided beyond all dualities to experience the true self.
dheesh_gita::220.simple_insight: There's freedom when you realize your true self is beyond all opposing forces.
dheesh_gita::220.detailed_meaning: The restless mind constantly encounters the three qualities (sattva, rajas, tamas). This verse describes how, through wisdom, these qualities are observed until the seeker is guided beyond their conflicts to see the true self.
dheesh_gita::220.modern_relevance: You notice your moods and impulses cycling, but a deeper part of you watches calmly beyond these ups and downs.
dheesh_gita::220.insight: It teaches you to observe your changing qualities without being caught, shifting attention beyond dualities to the unchanging self.

dheesh_gita::221.verse_sanskrit:
अतो विज्ञवरा अत्र प्रकृतेर्मे दशाद्वये ।
ममं सिद्धिस्वरूपस्य विकाशोऽपि द्विधा भवेत् ॥
dheesh_gita::221.verse_hindi: इसी कारण हे विज्ञवरों! मेरी प्रकृति की इन दो दशाओं में मेरी सिद्धि के स्वरूप का विकास भी द्विविध होता है।
dheesh_gita::221.english_translation: Therefore, O wise ones, in these two states of my nature, the manifestation of the true form of my perfection also becomes dual.
dheesh_gita::221.translation_literal: अतो (therefore) / विज्ञवरा (O wise ones) / अत्र (here) / प्रकृतेर्मे (of my nature) / दशाद्वये (in two states) / ममं (my) / सिद्धिस्वरूपस्य (of the true form of perfection) / विकाशः (manifestation) / अपि (also) / द्विधा (twofold) / भवेत् (becomes)
dheesh_gita::221.speaker: Shambhu
dheesh_gita::221.essence: True perfection unfolds within nature in two distinct, complementary states.
dheesh_gita::221.simple_meaning: Your true perfection develops through two different states of your nature.
dheesh_gita::221.simple_insight: There is a richness in knowing your growth is not one single path but has multiple expressions.
dheesh_gita::221.detailed_meaning: The teacher Shambhu addresses wise students, explaining that his nature expresses the true form of perfection in two distinct ways, indicating a complex unfolding of realization beyond a single approach.
dheesh_gita::221.modern_relevance: When you grow, you may find your progress takes different shapes, not just one fixed path, reflecting complexity in your development.
dheesh_gita::221.insight: Recognize that your growth and realization can manifest through multiple, complementary states rather than a single fixed form.

dheesh_gita::222.verse_sanskrit:
अपरा सिद्धिरेकास्ति द्वितीया च परामिधा ! ।
नैकोक्तसिद्धिरूपाणि नानारूपाणि विभ्रती ॥
dheesh_gita::222.verse_hindi: एक परा सिद्धि और दूसरी अपरा सिद्धि नाम से अभिहित होती है। सिद्धि के जो अनेक रूप पहले कहे गये हैं
dheesh_gita::222.english_translation: There is one superior accomplishment and another inferior accomplishment; the various forms of accomplishment mentioned earlier are not singular.
dheesh_gita::222.translation_literal: अपरा (inferior) / सिद्धि (accomplishment) / एक (one) / अस्ति (exists) / द्वितीया (second) / च (and) / परामिधा (superior) / नै (not) / एकोक्त (singularly mentioned) / सिद्धि (accomplishment) / रूपाणि (forms) / नानारूपाणि (various forms) / विभ्रती (are)
dheesh_gita::222.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::222.essence: Accomplishments exist in many forms, including higher and lower levels.
dheesh_gita::222.simple_meaning: There are different kinds of accomplishments: one higher and another lower; many forms exist rather than just one.
dheesh_gita::222.simple_insight: Understanding that success or progress has levels makes growth less daunting and more relatable.
dheesh_gita::222.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, the speaker explains that accomplishments are not all the same; there is a higher form of accomplishment and a lower one. The many previously mentioned forms are diverse and cannot be reduced to one alone.
dheesh_gita::222.modern_relevance: You notice some achievements feel deeper or more lasting than others, reminding you that not all progress is equal.
dheesh_gita::222.insight: Recognize that achievements differ in quality and depth, helping you focus on what truly matters.

dheesh_gita::223.verse_sanskrit:
सिद्धिर्मेऽस्त्यपरानाम्नी नात्र वः संशयो भवेत् ।
ज्ञानाधिकारिणो विप्राः ! पूज्या सिद्धिः पराभिधा ॥
dheesh_gita::223.verse_hindi: वह अनेक रूपधारिणी सिद्धि मेरी अपरा सिद्धि है इसमें आपलोगों को सन्देह नहीं होना चाहिये। हे ज्ञान के अधिकारी ब्राह्मणो ! जो पूज्या परा नाम की सिद्धि है
dheesh_gita::223.english_translation: My accomplishment is the supreme among many; there is no doubt about this, O wise Brahmins worthy of knowledge! The revered accomplishment is called the highest.
dheesh_gita::223.translation_literal: सिद्धिर्मेऽस्ति (accomplishment mine is) अपरा (inferior) न (not) अत्र (here) वः (your) संशयो (doubt) भवेत् (may be) । ज्ञानाधिकारिणः (possessors of knowledge) विप्राः (Brahmins) पूज्या (revered) सिद्धिः (accomplishment) पराभिधा (called the highest) ॥
dheesh_gita::223.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::223.essence: The highest accomplishment is unmistakably supreme and honored by those who know.
dheesh_gita::223.simple_meaning: There are many forms of accomplishment, but the highest one is certain and respected by those who seek true knowledge.
dheesh_gita::223.simple_insight: Knowing your greatest success is beyond doubt brings confidence and clarity to your path.
dheesh_gita::223.detailed_meaning: The speaker addresses learned Brahmins, emphasizing that among many kinds of achievements, the highest accomplishment is clearly superior and worthy of respect, removing any doubt about its status.
dheesh_gita::223.modern_relevance: When you've worked hard and reached a peak in your field, recognizing that achievement as truly supreme helps you trust your journey and keep moving forward.
dheesh_gita::223.insight: It guides you to honor your ultimate achievements without hesitation or self-doubt.

dheesh_gita::224.verse_sanskrit:
चिन्मयी सात्विकी नित्या हिताऽद्वैतविधायिनी।
स्वरूपानन्दसन्दोहयोतिनी सा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
dheesh_gita::224.verse_hindi: वह चिन्मयी सात्त्विकी नित्या हिता अद्वैतकारिणी और स्वारूपानन्द सन्दोह प्रकाशिनी कही गई है।
dheesh_gita::224.english_translation: She is described as consciousness-filled, pure, eternal, beneficial, leading to non-duality, and illuminating the bliss of true nature.
dheesh_gita::224.translation_literal: चिन्मयी (consciousness-filled) / सात्विकी (pure) / नित्या (eternal) / हिताऽद्वैतविधायिनी (beneficial, non-duality leading) / स्वरूपानन्दसन्दोहयोतिनी (true nature bliss illuminating) / सा (she) / प्रकीर्तिता (is described)
dheesh_gita::224.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::224.essence: Your true self is pure, eternal consciousness that reveals bliss beyond all duality.
dheesh_gita::224.simple_meaning: The true self is pure consciousness, always present and beneficial, revealing the experience of eternal bliss beyond duality.
dheesh_gita::224.simple_insight: You can feel the relief of connecting with a pure, unchanging source of bliss inside you.
dheesh_gita::224.detailed_meaning: This verse describes the true self as pure consciousness that is always present, completely pure, and guides one beyond duality to experience lasting bliss. It presents a deep philosophical view of the self's nature in Vedanta.
dheesh_gita::224.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by confusion and conflict, knowing your true nature is a pure, unchanging source of joy can bring calm and clarity.
dheesh_gita::224.insight: It invites you to recognize your essence as pure awareness that naturally reveals deep joy beyond mental noise.

dheesh_gita::225.verse_sanskrit:
ऐश्यो मे सिद्धयो विप्राः ! कामनामन्तरेण मे।
प्रकटत्वं हि संसारे नैव यान्ति कदाचन ॥
dheesh_gita::225.verse_hindi: हे ब्राह्मणो ! मेरी ऐसी  सिद्धियां मेरी इच्छा के बिना संसार में कदापि प्रकाशित नहीं ही हो सकती
dheesh_gita::225.english_translation: O Brahmins! My achievements can never manifest in the world without my desire.
dheesh_gita::225.translation_literal: ऐश्यो (achievement) / मे (my) / सिद्धयो (perfections) / विप्राः (O Brahmins) / कामना (desire) / अन्तर (without) / एण (by) / मे (my) / प्रकटत्वं (manifestation) / हि (indeed) / संसारे (in the world) / नैव (never) / यान्ति (they go) / कदाचन (ever)
dheesh_gita::225.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::225.essence: No achievement can manifest in the world without your inner desire.
dheesh_gita::225.simple_meaning: Your accomplishments cannot appear without your own desire and intention behind them.
dheesh_gita::225.simple_insight: You feel empowered knowing your intentions ignite your success.
dheesh_gita::225.detailed_meaning: Addressing the Brahmins, the speaker explains that no accomplishment can manifest in the world without the inner desire that fuels it. Without the motivating wish, even potential achievements remain hidden.
dheesh_gita::225.modern_relevance: You hesitate starting a project without full commitment; this reminds you that your desire sparks real progress.
dheesh_gita::225.insight: It teaches you to recognize that inner desire is essential to bringing your actions and achievements into reality.

dheesh_gita::226.verse_sanskrit:
मामकीना यतः शक्तिर्न स्वेच्छाचारिणी भवेत् ।
अतो ममावतारेषु ज्ञानिष्वपि कदाचन ॥
dheesh_gita::226.verse_hindi: क्योंकि मेरा शक्ति स्वेच्छाचारिणी नहीं हो सकती, इसी कारण मेरे अवतारों मे  और कभी कभी मेरे ज्ञानी भक्तों में भी
dheesh_gita::226.english_translation: Because my power can never act according to its own will, in my incarnations and sometimes even in my wise devotees.
dheesh_gita::226.translation_literal: मामकीना (my power) यतः (because) शक्तिर् (energy/power) न (not) स्वेच्छाचारिणी (acting of own will) भवेत् (can be) । अतो (therefore) मम (my) अवतारेषु (in incarnations) ज्ञानिषु (in wise ones) अपि (even) कदाचन (sometimes) ॥
dheesh_gita::226.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::226.essence: True power never acts from selfish will but always follows higher wisdom.
dheesh_gita::226.simple_meaning: My power never acts selfishly or by its own desires, even in my incarnations or wise followers.
dheesh_gita::226.simple_insight: You can trust that true power always serves a higher purpose beyond personal will.
dheesh_gita::226.detailed_meaning: The speaker reveals that their divine power is never driven by self-will or selfish desires. This holds true across their incarnations and even in wise devotees, emphasizing that true power aligns with higher wisdom, not personal whims.
dheesh_gita::226.modern_relevance: You might feel restless wanting control, but real strength comes from aligning with a greater purpose, not personal whims.
dheesh_gita::226.insight: It shifts the mind from imagining power as personal control to seeing it as service to a higher order.

dheesh_gita::227.verse_sanskrit:
मद्भक्तेषु प्रकाशेरन्नैश्यो मे सिद्धयः स्वतः।
ममावतारन्दानामाविर्भावो महर्षयः ॥
dheesh_gita::227.verse_hindi: मेरी ऐसी  सिद्धयों का प्रकाश स्वत: हुआ करता है। हे महर्षिगण ! मेरे अवतार समूह का अविर्भाव
dheesh_gita::227.english_translation: My followers' devotion naturally reveals my powers. O great sages, the appearance of my incarnations occurs.
dheesh_gita::227.translation_literal: मद्भक्तेषु (in my devotees) प्रकाशे (in the light) न (not) ऐश्यः (envy) मे (my) सिद्धयः (powers) स्वतः (by themselves)। मम (my) अवतारन्दानाम् (of incarnations) आविर्भावः (appearance) महर्षयः (great sages)॥
dheesh_gita::227.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::227.essence: Devotion naturally reveals divine power and the arrival of divine beings.
dheesh_gita::227.simple_meaning: True devotion in followers naturally brings forth the divine's power and reveals the appearance of divine beings.
dheesh_gita::227.simple_insight: Devotion itself naturally awakens a powerful presence without effort or envy.
dheesh_gita::227.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the teacher explains to great sages that the sincere devotion of followers naturally manifests the divine's powers and the emergence of divine incarnations, emphasizing devotion's spontaneous, radiant effect.
dheesh_gita::227.modern_relevance: You notice how genuine care and faith in something greater can naturally inspire strength and transformation around you.
dheesh_gita::227.insight: It teaches you that sincere devotion itself is a natural force that brings forth divine manifestations without struggle.

dheesh_gita::228.verse_sanskrit:
अथवा ज्ञानिभक्तषु ह्यौश्याः सिद्धेः प्रकाशनम् ।
समष्टेजीववर्गस्य कर्मणो निघ्नमस्त्यहो ॥
dheesh_gita::228.verse_hindi: अथवा ज्ञानी भक्तों में ऐसी  सिद्धि का विकास अहो ! जीवों के समष्टि कर्माधीन है।
dheesh_gita::228.english_translation: Or among the wise and devoted, such perfection unfolds, for the collective of beings remains bound by action.
dheesh_gita::228.translation_literal: अथवा (or) ज्ञानि-भक्तषु (among wise and devoted) हि (indeed) औश्याः (perfection) सिद्धेः (of accomplishment) प्रकाशनम् (manifestation) । समष्टे (collective) जीववर्गस्य (of beings) कर्मणः (by action) निघ्नमस्ति (is not broken) अहो (indeed) ॥
dheesh_gita::228.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::228.essence: Wisdom and devotion coexist with being bound by the results of collective actions.
dheesh_gita::228.simple_meaning: Even those who are wise and devoted experience progress, but all living beings remain bound by the consequences of their actions.
dheesh_gita::228.simple_insight: There's comfort knowing wisdom and devotion don't erase the need to engage with life's responsibilities.
dheesh_gita::228.detailed_meaning: The verse reflects on how even the enlightened and devoted among living beings continue to be influenced by their collective actions, emphasizing that ultimate freedom requires more than devotion or wisdom alone.
dheesh_gita::228.modern_relevance: You might know deeply what is right and love what you do, yet still feel caught in the results of your efforts.
dheesh_gita::228.insight: It shifts your view to accept that wisdom and devotion do not exempt you from acting responsibly within life's laws.

dheesh_gita::229.verse_sanskrit:
सन्त्यत: सिद्धयो विप्रा ऐश्योऽत्यन्तं सुदुर्लभाः।
स्वरूप मम सिद्धेश्च ज्ञात्वा सम्यङ्महर्षयः ॥
dheesh_gita::229.verse_hindi: इसी कारण हे ब्राह्मणो ! ऐसी  सिद्धियां अत्यन्त दुर्लभ है। हे महर्षियों ! आप मेरे स्वरूप और मेरी सिद्धि के स्वरूप को भलीप्रकार जानकर
dheesh_gita::229.english_translation: Therefore, O Brahmins, such attainments are extremely rare. O great sages, know well my nature and the nature of my attainments.
dheesh_gita::229.translation_literal: सन्त्यत: (therefore) सिद्धयो (attainments) विप्रा (O Brahmins) ऐश्योऽत्यन्तं (are exceedingly) सुदुर्लभाः (rare)। स्वरूप (nature) मम (my) सिद्धेश्च (and of attainments) ज्ञात्वा (knowing) सम्यङ्महर्षयः (O great sages) ॥
dheesh_gita::229.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::229.essence: Truly knowing the true self and its attainments is extremely rare, even among sages.
dheesh_gita::229.simple_meaning: Understanding the true nature of the inner being and its achievements is very rare, even for wise people.
dheesh_gita::229.simple_insight: There is special value and rarity in truly knowing the true self and its success.
dheesh_gita::229.detailed_meaning: The verse addresses learned Brahmins and sages, pointing out that realizing the true nature of the inner being and its powers is extremely rare. This knowledge is not common, even among those who seek wisdom.
dheesh_gita::229.modern_relevance: You might meet many who claim insight, but truly understanding your own inner nature and achievements is a rare and precious clarity.
dheesh_gita::229.insight: It teaches you to value and seek deep understanding of your true self beyond surface knowledge.

dheesh_gita::230.verse_sanskrit:
कदाचिदपरासिद्धेर्माश्लिष्यध्वं हि बन्धने ।
चिन्मच्या मे परासिद्धेमहत्वं परमाद्भुतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::230.verse_hindi: कभी भी मेरी अपरा सिद्धि के बन्धन-जाल में न फंसो और मेरी चिन्मयी परासिद्धि के परम अद्भुत महत्त्व को
dheesh_gita::230.english_translation: Never get caught in the bondage of my lower accomplishments; grasp the supreme, wondrous importance of my supreme, conscious accomplishment.
dheesh_gita::230.translation_literal: कदाचिद (never) अपरासिद्धेः (of lower accomplishment) माश्लिष्यध्वं (do not get caught) हि (indeed) बन्धने (in bondage) । चिन्मयि (conscious) मे (my) परासिद्धे (supreme accomplishment) महत्त्वं (importance) परमाद्भुतम् (supremely wondrous) ॥
dheesh_gita::230.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::230.essence: True value lies beyond small successes in the supreme conscious accomplishment.
dheesh_gita::230.simple_meaning: Avoid being trapped by minor achievements and instead understand the supreme, conscious accomplishment's profound importance.
dheesh_gita::230.simple_insight: There's freedom in seeing beyond small wins to the greater, conscious achievement.
dheesh_gita::230.detailed_meaning: The speaker warns against getting caught in superficial or lower levels of success, urging to recognize the supreme, conscious accomplishment that holds true and wondrous value beyond fleeting achievements.
dheesh_gita::230.modern_relevance: You might celebrate small milestones but risk missing the deeper meaning and lasting impact of your highest efforts.
dheesh_gita::230.insight: Shift your focus from transient successes to appreciating the profound value of your highest, conscious achievements.

dheesh_gita::231.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञात्वोपास्य च तामेवाद्वैतानन्दप्रकाशकम् ।
द्वन्द्वातीतं लभध्वं हि शाश्वतं परमं पदम् ॥
dheesh_gita::231.verse_hindi: जानकर और उसकी ही उपासना करके इन्द्वातीत अद्वैतानन्द प्रकाशक सनातन परमपद को प्राप्त करो
dheesh_gita::231.english_translation: Know and worship that which reveals non-dual bliss; attain the eternal supreme state beyond all dualities.
dheesh_gita::231.translation_literal: ज्ञात्व (knowing) / उपास्य (worshipping) / च (and) / ताम् (that) / एव (indeed) / अद्वैतानन्दप्रकाशकम् (non-dual bliss revealer) / द्वन्द्वातीतं (beyond dualities) / लभध्वं (attain) / हि (indeed) / शाश्वतं (eternal) / परमं (supreme) / पदम् (state)
dheesh_gita::231.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::231.essence: Knowing and honoring the source beyond all dualities leads to eternal supreme bliss.
dheesh_gita::231.simple_meaning: You can realize and honor the source of non-dual bliss to attain the eternal supreme state beyond all opposites.
dheesh_gita::231.simple_insight: There's peace in knowing and connecting with what is beyond all conflict and change.
dheesh_gita::231.detailed_meaning: The verse teaches the seeker to understand and revere the source that reveals non-dual bliss. It invites transcending all pairs of opposites to reach an eternal supreme state, highlighting the essence of Vedantic wisdom.
dheesh_gita::231.modern_relevance: When facing confusion or conflict, turning inward to what is beyond opposites offers lasting peace and clarity.
dheesh_gita::231.insight: It shifts focus from external dualities to the inner, unchanging source of bliss and being.

dheesh_gita::232.verse_sanskrit:
स्थिरं लक्ष्यं विधायैवं द्विजाः ! सिद्धिस्वरूपिणि ।
आयुधे मोदके नूनं त्रिशूले मे त्रितापके ॥
dheesh_gita::232.verse_hindi: हे ब्राह्मणो! आप इस प्रकार स्थिर लक्ष्य रखकर मेरे त्रिताप रूपी त्रिशूल और सिद्धि रूपी मोदक जो आयुध हैं
dheesh_gita::232.english_translation: O Brahmin! Fix your steady aim on me, whose trident is the embodiment of suffering, and whose sweet treat is the embodiment of success.
dheesh_gita::232.translation_literal: स्थिरं (steady) लक्ष्यं (aim) विधायैवं (thus fixing) द्विजाः (O Brahmins) ! सिद्धिस्वरूपिणि (embodiment of success) । आयुधे (in the weapons) मोदके (sweet treat) नूनं (certainly) त्रिशूले (trident) मे (my) त्रितापके (embodiment of suffering) ॥
dheesh_gita::232.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::232.essence: Steadily aiming at a goal means accepting both its challenges and successes.
dheesh_gita::232.simple_meaning: Hold a steady focus on your goal, accepting both the difficulties and the rewards it brings.
dheesh_gita::232.simple_insight: You can embrace struggle and success together by fixing your aim firmly.
dheesh_gita::232.detailed_meaning: Addressing a Brahmin, the verse encourages focusing steadily on the divine figure who carries both the trident (symbolizing suffering) and the sweet treat (symbolizing success). It teaches to hold purpose firmly despite hardship.
dheesh_gita::232.modern_relevance: You decide to pursue a challenging goal, knowing it will test you but also bring fulfillment if achieved.
dheesh_gita::232.insight: It teaches to hold firm to your purpose, welcoming both hardships and rewards as parts of the journey.

dheesh_gita::233.verse_sanskrit:
दृष्टिक्षेपं न कुर्वीरन भवन्तो हि कदाचन।
चक्रपद्मस्वरूपौ हि धर्ममोक्षौ निरन्तरम् ॥
dheesh_gita::233.verse_hindi: उनकी ओर कभी भी दृष्टि रखो और चक्र और पद्मरूपी धर्म और मोक्ष पर निरन्तर लक्ष्य रखकर
dheesh_gita::233.english_translation: Never divert your gaze; continuously fix it on the lotus-like wheel that is Dharma and Moksha.
dheesh_gita::233.translation_literal: दृष्टिक्षेपं (gaze diversion) / न (not) / कुर्वीत (should do) / अरन् (ever) / भवन्तः (you all) / हि (indeed) / कदाचन (at any time) । चक्रपद्मस्वरूपौ (wheel and lotus form) / हि (indeed) / धर्ममोक्षौ (dharma and moksha) / निरन्तरम् (continuously) ॥
dheesh_gita::233.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::233.essence: Unwavering focus on your true purpose leads to lasting freedom.
dheesh_gita::233.simple_meaning: Never let your attention wander; always keep your focus on your true purpose and freedom.
dheesh_gita::233.simple_insight: There’s strength in steady focus: your direction clarifies when you don’t get distracted.
dheesh_gita::233.detailed_meaning: The verse advises to keep unwavering attention on the eternal symbols of Dharma (righteous purpose) and Moksha (freedom). It encourages maintaining continuous focus without distraction to fulfill one’s deeper calling.
dheesh_gita::233.modern_relevance: You start a project but your phone buzzes constantly. This reminds you to hold your focus on what truly matters.
dheesh_gita::233.insight: It teaches you to train your attention steadily on your deeper goals, resisting momentary distractions.

dheesh_gita::234.verse_sanskrit:
अग्रेसरेयुः संलक्ष्य बाधां नेयुः कदाचन ।
सत्यमेतद्धि जानीत नात्र कश्चन संशयः ॥
dheesh_gita::234.verse_hindi: अग्रसर हो, कभी बाधा को प्राप्त नहीं होगे, इसको सत्य जानो, इसमें कुछ संशय नहीं है
dheesh_gita::234.english_translation: Advance boldly; you will never encounter obstacles. Know this as truth without any doubt.
dheesh_gita::234.translation_literal: अग्रेसरेयुः (advance) / संलक्ष्य (encountering) / बाधां (obstacle) / नेयुः (will not go) / कदाचन (ever) / सत्यमेतद्धि (this is truth indeed) / जानीत (know) / नात्र (here not) / कश्चन (anyone) / संशयः (doubt)
dheesh_gita::234.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::234.essence: True obstacles do not exist; bold forward action meets no real resistance.
dheesh_gita::234.simple_meaning: You should move forward courageously because obstacles will never truly stop you. This is certain.
dheesh_gita::234.simple_insight: You feel empowered knowing that real blockages don’t exist on your path.
dheesh_gita::234.detailed_meaning: A teacher encourages the listener to advance confidently, assuring that no real obstacle will prevent progress. This moment aims to inspire fearless action without hesitation.
dheesh_gita::234.modern_relevance: You face a tough challenge but realize hesitating only creates imaginary blocks. Taking bold steps clears your way.
dheesh_gita::234.insight: It shifts your mindset to see obstacles as illusions, freeing you to act decisively and without fear.

dheesh_gita::235.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वशक्तिमन् ! धीश! भगवन् ! सर्वसिद्धिद!।
हे विभो ! सर्वसिद्धीनां नित्याधारस्वरूपवन् ! ॥
dheesh_gita::235.verse_hindi: हे सर्वशक्तिमान, विभो ! हे सर्वसिद्धियों के नित्य आधार स्वरुप ! हे सर्वसिद्धिदायिन्! हे भगवन् धीश !
dheesh_gita::235.english_translation: O all-powerful Lord! O source of all accomplishments, eternal and unchanging! O bestower of all successes! O revered Lord Dheesh!
dheesh_gita::235.translation_literal: सर्वशक्तिमन् (all-powerful) / धीश (Lord) / भगवन् (revered Lord) / सर्वसिद्धिद (giver of all accomplishments) / हे (O) / विभो (Lord) / सर्वसिद्धीनां (of all accomplishments) / नित्याधारस्वरूपवन् (eternal source form)
dheesh_gita::235.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::235.essence: The divine Dheesh is the eternal source of all power and success.
dheesh_gita::235.simple_meaning: This is a respectful address praising the divine Dheesh as all-powerful, eternal, and the source of all success.
dheesh_gita::235.simple_insight: There is reverence in recognizing a presence that is unchanging and empowers all achievements.
dheesh_gita::235.detailed_meaning: In this verse, someone respectfully calls out to Lord Dheesh, praising his infinite power, eternal nature, and role as the foundation of all successes. It sets a tone of devotion and acknowledgement before teaching or action.
dheesh_gita::235.insight: It reminds you to recognize the deeper source behind your achievements and strength.

dheesh_gita::236.verse_sanskrit:
परासिद्धे: कृपाप्राप्यतै  पूर्व तद्दर्शनं ध्रुवम् ।
आवश्यकीयमेवास्ति तदुपायानतो वद ॥
dheesh_gita::236.verse_hindi: परासिद्धि की कृपा प्राप्ति के लिए प्रथम उनके दर्शनलाभ की निश्चय ही आवश्यकता है अतः उसके उपाय कहें
dheesh_gita::236.english_translation: To attain supreme accomplishment, first the vision of the divine is absolutely necessary; therefore, explain the means to that.
dheesh_gita::236.translation_literal: परासिद्धे: (of supreme accomplishment) कृपाप्राप्यतै (for obtaining grace) पूर्व (first) तद्-दर्शनं (that vision) ध्रुवम् (certain) । आवश्यकीयम् (necessary) एवास्ति (indeed is) तद्-उपायानतः (therefore, the means) वद (speak) ॥
dheesh_gita::236.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::236.essence: Clear vision of the divine is the necessary first step toward highest accomplishment.
dheesh_gita::236.simple_meaning: To achieve the highest success, you must first have a clear vision or experience of the divine. Without this, the path cannot begin.
dheesh_gita::236.simple_insight: Knowing clearly what you aim for makes the journey real and possible.
dheesh_gita::236.detailed_meaning: The narrator explains that before one can attain supreme accomplishment or grace, it is essential to first have a clear vision or understanding of the divine. This verse sets the stage for revealing the methods to achieve that vision.
dheesh_gita::236.modern_relevance: Before you can reach your biggest goals, you need a clear picture of what success truly means to you.
dheesh_gita::236.insight: It shifts focus to clarifying your goal before taking action, making efforts more grounded and directed.

dheesh_gita::237.verse_sanskrit:
यर्न: स्याद्दर्शनं नूनं परासिद्धभिरापदम् ।
यथा वा नः कतार्थत्वमुपदिश्यामहे तथा ॥
dheesh_gita::237.verse_hindi: जिनके द्वारा परासिद्धि के दर्शन हमलोगों को अनायास ही हो अथवा जिस प्रकार से हमलोग कृतार्थ हो सो उपदेश कीजिये
dheesh_gita::237.english_translation: Teach us in a way that we effortlessly perceive supreme accomplishment or clearly understand what we have achieved.
dheesh_gita::237.translation_literal: यः (who) नः (to us) स्यात् (may be) दर्शनं (vision/perception) नूनं (certainly) परासिद्धभिः (by supreme accomplishments) आपदम् (easily) यथा (as) वा (or) नः (our) कतार्थत्वम् (accomplishment) उपदिश्यामहे (we teach) तथा (thus)
dheesh_gita::237.speaker: Student
dheesh_gita::237.essence: True understanding can arise effortlessly when shown clearly.
dheesh_gita::237.simple_meaning: Ask for guidance to recognize clearly and easily what has been truly accomplished or understood.
dheesh_gita::237.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that clarity and understanding can come naturally, without struggle.
dheesh_gita::237.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the student requests the teacher to provide instruction that either allows effortless perception of the highest success or clear understanding of what has been achieved. This sets the stage for wisdom that reveals true accomplishment beyond confusion.
dheesh_gita::237.modern_relevance: You wonder if you’re making real progress and long for a clear sign that your efforts are bearing fruit without overthinking.
dheesh_gita::237.insight: It shifts the mind to seek guidance that reveals clear understanding naturally, not through forced effort.

dheesh_gita::238.verse_sanskrit:
विद्यास्वरूपिणी नित्यां परासिद्धिं मदाश्रयाम् ।
तत्वनानसुनिष्णाताः महापौरष् शालिनः ॥
dheesh_gita::238.verse_hindi: नित्या और विद्यास्वरूपिणी मेरी परासिद्धि का दर्शन
dheesh_gita::238.english_translation: My supreme accomplishment is the eternal embodiment of wisdom.
dheesh_gita::238.translation_literal: विद्या (wisdom) स्वरूपिणी (embodiment) नित्यां (eternal) परासिद्धिं (supreme accomplishment) मदाश्रयाम् (my refuge) तत्वनानसुनिष्णाताः (expert in various truths) महापौरष् (great hero) शालिनः (possessed of)
dheesh_gita::238.speaker: Shambhu Dheesh
dheesh_gita::238.essence: True greatness is living as the eternal embodiment of profound wisdom.
dheesh_gita::238.simple_meaning: The highest achievement is to be the eternal embodiment of wisdom, mastering many truths.
dheesh_gita::238.simple_insight: You carry an unchanging strength rooted in deep understanding.
dheesh_gita::238.detailed_meaning: Shambhu Dheesh declares that true greatness comes from embodying eternal wisdom and mastering various fundamental truths, presenting this as the highest accomplishment.
dheesh_gita::238.modern_relevance: When your knowledge and experience become your steady foundation, you move through life with confidence and grace.
dheesh_gita::238.insight: Recognize that embodying wisdom means living with grounded clarity beyond temporary knowledge.

dheesh_gita::239.verse_sanskrit:
दिव्यदृष्टया निरीक्षन्ते ज्ञानिना ज्ञानभूमिषु।
तत्वज्ञाः शान्तचेतस्काः साधकास्तु यथायथम् ॥
dheesh_gita::239.verse_hindi: ज्ञान भूमियों में तत्त्वज्ञाननिष्ठ ज्ञानी महापुरुषों को दिव्यदृष्टि से हुआ करता है और इस संसार में शान्तचित्त तत्व ज्ञानी साधक
dheesh_gita::239.english_translation: Those deeply rooted in wisdom perceive the realms of knowledge with divine vision, while in the world, calm-minded seekers of truth appear accordingly.
dheesh_gita::239.translation_literal: दिव्यदृष्टया (with divine vision) / निरीक्षन्ते (observe) / ज्ञानिना (by the wise) / ज्ञानभूमिषु (in the realms of knowledge) / तत्त्वज्ञाः (knowers of truth) / शान्तचेतस्काः (calm-minded) / साधकाः (seekers) / यथायथम् (as appropriate)
dheesh_gita::239.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::239.essence: Clear inner vision and calmness together reveal the true nature of knowledge.
dheesh_gita::239.simple_meaning: Wise people perceive deeper truths clearly, and sincere seekers maintain calm minds while pursuing those truths.
dheesh_gita::239.simple_insight: There is peace in seeing truth clearly and staying calm in your pursuit.
dheesh_gita::239.detailed_meaning: This verse describes how enlightened individuals perceive knowledge realms with a special inner vision, while genuine seekers remain calm and steady in the world as they pursue truth.
dheesh_gita::239.modern_relevance: When you study complex ideas, your calm focus helps you see the core clearly, while others may only grasp surface details.
dheesh_gita::239.insight: It teaches you to cultivate calmness while seeking clear understanding, balancing perception with peaceful steadiness.

dheesh_gita::240.verse_sanskrit:
क्रमादग्रेसरन्तीह सप्तसु ज्ञानभूमिषु ।
मम विद्यास्वरूपायाः परासिद्धेस्तथातथम् ॥
dheesh_gita::240.verse_hindi: क्रमशः जैसे जैसे सप्तज्ञान भूमियों में अग्रसर होते जाते हैं वैसे वैसे मेरी विद्या रूपिणी परासिद्धि के
dheesh_gita::240.english_translation: Step by step, as you advance through the seven fields of knowledge, so too does the supreme perfection of my form of wisdom.
dheesh_gita::240.translation_literal: क्रमाद (step by step) अग्रसरन्तीह (advancing here) सप्तसु (in seven) ज्ञानभूमिषु (fields of knowledge) । मम (my) विद्या (wisdom) स्वरूपायाः (of form) परासिद्धेः (supreme perfection) तथातथम् (so also)
dheesh_gita::240.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::240.essence: Wisdom’s highest form unfolds gradually through steady progress in learning.
dheesh_gita::240.simple_meaning: As you progress gradually through different areas of knowledge, your understanding and mastery of wisdom naturally deepen and become more complete.
dheesh_gita::240.simple_insight: You can trust that steady learning leads to natural growth in your deepest understanding.
dheesh_gita::240.detailed_meaning: The speaker describes how moving progressively through seven distinct fields of knowledge leads to the full realization of the supreme form of wisdom. This moment highlights the unfolding journey of learning as a path to mastery and insight.
dheesh_gita::240.modern_relevance: When you tackle new skills or ideas one step at a time, your confidence and clarity unfold naturally, even if you can't see it immediately.
dheesh_gita::240.insight: It teaches you to value steady progress, knowing that wisdom is not instant but builds perfectly over time.

dheesh_gita::241.verse_sanskrit:
उत्तरोत्तरमत्यन्तं स्पष्ट रूपस्य दर्शनम् ।
प्राप्नुवन्तो निमज्जन्ति परमानन्दसागरे ॥
dheesh_gita::241.verse_hindi: उत्तरोत्तर स्वरूप का अत्यन्त स्पष्ट दर्शन प्राप्त करते हुए परमानन्द सागर में निमग्न होते जाते हैं
dheesh_gita::241.english_translation: Gradually, by ever clearer seeing of the true form, they immerse deeper into the ocean of supreme bliss.
dheesh_gita::241.translation_literal: उत्तरोत्तर (gradually) / अत्यन्त (extremely) / स्पष्ट (clear) / रूपस्य (of form) / दर्शनम् (seeing) / प्राप्नुवन्तः (they attain) / निमज्जन्ति (they immerse) / परमानन्दसागरे (in the ocean of supreme bliss)
dheesh_gita::241.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::241.essence: Clearer insight naturally draws you deeper into profound joy.
dheesh_gita::241.simple_meaning: As your understanding of the true nature becomes clearer and clearer, you immerse yourself more deeply in great joy.
dheesh_gita::241.simple_insight: Feeling your happiness grow as your insight brightens brings a sense of deep fulfillment.
dheesh_gita::241.detailed_meaning: Suta describes how seekers, by progressively perceiving the true nature of reality more clearly, are drawn deeply into supreme happiness, illustrating the transformative power of insight on the journey to liberation.
dheesh_gita::241.modern_relevance: You notice moments when understanding something fully brings a deep calm and joy that swells within you, like settling into a peaceful sea.
dheesh_gita::241.insight: It encourages you to deepen your clarity, showing that clearer understanding naturally leads to profound joy and immersion in peace.

dheesh_gita::242.verse_sanskrit:
अहं ज्ञानस्वरूपोऽस्मि नूनं विज्ञवरा द्विजाः ।
तटस्थञ्च स्वरूपश्च द्विविध ज्ञानमीरितम् ॥
dheesh_gita::242.verse_hindi: हे विज्ञवर ब्राह्मणो ! मैं ज्ञानस्वरुप ही हूँ और ज्ञान दो प्रकार का कहा गया है। एक तटस्थज्ञान और दूसरा स्वरुप ज्ञान।
dheesh_gita::242.english_translation: O learned Brahmins! I am the embodiment of knowledge, and knowledge is said to be of two kinds: impartial knowledge and knowledge of the true nature.
dheesh_gita::242.translation_literal: अहं (I) / ज्ञानस्वरूपः (embodiment of knowledge) / अस्मि (am) / नूनम् (indeed) / विज्ञवरा (learned ones) / द्विजाः (Brahmins) / तटस्थम् (impartial) / च (and) / स्वरूपश्च (and of true nature) / द्विविध (two kinds) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / ईरितम् (said)
dheesh_gita::242.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::242.essence: Knowledge includes both detached clarity and intimate self-understanding.
dheesh_gita::242.simple_meaning: Knowledge has two forms: one is unbiased observation, and the other is understanding your true nature.
dheesh_gita::242.simple_insight: You carry both clear seeing and deep self-awareness within you.
dheesh_gita::242.detailed_meaning: The speaker addresses learned Brahmins, explaining that knowledge is not singular but has two forms: detached observation and direct realization of the true self. This verse introduces a key philosophical distinction in understanding wisdom.
dheesh_gita::242.modern_relevance: When you learn something new, it helps to both see facts clearly and understand what they reveal about who you really are.
dheesh_gita::242.insight: It teaches you to distinguish between simply noticing things and deeply knowing your own essence.

dheesh_gita::243.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञाता ज्ञानं तथा ज्ञेयमेषां भानै: समन्वितः।
यत्र त्रिपुटिसम्बन्धो विद्यते विप्रपुङ्गवाः ॥
dheesh_gita::243.verse_hindi: हे श्रेष्ठ ब्राह्मणों ! जहां ज्ञाता और ज्ञेयों के भान से युक्त त्रिपुटि का सम्बन्ध है वही
dheesh_gita::243.english_translation: O noble Brahmins! Wherever the knower and the known are united in the awareness of the threefold connection, there the wise excel.
dheesh_gita::243.translation_literal: ज्ञाता (knower) / ज्ञानं (knowledge) / तथा (and) / ज्ञेयम् (that which is to be known) / एषां (of these) / भानै: (by awareness) / समन्वितः (united) / यत्र (where) / त्रिपुटि (threefold) / सम्बन्धः (connection) / विद्यते (exists) / विप्रपुङ्गवाः (the wise)
dheesh_gita::243.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::243.essence: True wisdom is the clear unity of knower, known, and knowledge.
dheesh_gita::243.simple_meaning: Wisdom arises when the knower, what is known, and the knowledge itself are clearly connected and understood as one.
dheesh_gita::243.simple_insight: You feel the power of clarity when your mind, knowledge, and self align together.
dheesh_gita::243.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, the wise Brahmins are told that true wisdom comes where the knower (the self), the known (the object), and knowledge itself are not separate but integrated clearly in awareness.
dheesh_gita::243.modern_relevance: When you focus and see clearly how you, your thoughts, and the world around connect, understanding flows effortlessly.
dheesh_gita::243.insight: It teaches you to recognize the inseparability of your awareness, what you observe, and the knowledge gained.

dheesh_gita::244.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानं स्यात्तत्तटस्थाख्यं स्वरूपज्ञानकारणम् ।
ज्ञानेऽस्मिश्च तटस्थाख्ये स्वरूपस्य द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
dheesh_gita::244.verse_hindi: स्वरूप ज्ञान का कारण भूत तटस्थ ज्ञान है हे ब्राह्मणों ! इस तटस्थशान मे
dheesh_gita::244.english_translation: The cause of true self-knowledge is detached knowledge; O Brahmins, the enlightened are those who know this detached awareness of the true self.
dheesh_gita::244.translation_literal: ज्ञानं (knowledge) स्यात् (is) तत्तटस्थाख्यं (called detached) स्वरूपज्ञानकारणम् (cause of true self-knowledge) । ज्ञानेऽस्मि (in knowledge) च (also) तटस्थाख्ये (called detached) स्वरूपस्य (of true self) द्विजोत्तमाः (best of Brahmins) ॥
dheesh_gita::244.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::244.essence: Clear self-knowledge arises from calm, detached awareness of your true nature.
dheesh_gita::244.simple_meaning: True understanding of your real self comes from steady, detached awareness that does not get caught in distractions.
dheesh_gita::244.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing that clear self-awareness comes from calm detachment.
dheesh_gita::244.detailed_meaning: This verse teaches that the root of knowing the true self is a special kind of knowledge called detached awareness. The best among the Brahmins are those who grasp this calm, steady insight into the true self, beyond distractions and attachments.
dheesh_gita::244.modern_relevance: When your mind stops chasing every thought or emotion, you begin to see who you really are beyond the noise.
dheesh_gita::244.insight: It guides you to cultivate calm, steady witnessing as the foundation for clear self-understanding.

dheesh_gita::245.verse_sanskrit:
सच्चिदानन्दभावानामनुभूतिः पृथक् पृथक् ।
स्यादतस्तत्र सम्पूर्ण दृश्यजातं प्रतीयते ॥
dheesh_gita::245.verse_hindi: सत् चित् और आनन्दभावों का स्वरुप पृथक् पृथक् अनुभूत होता है इस कारण उस अवस्था में सम्पूर्ण दृश्यसमूह प्रतीत होता है
dheesh_gita::245.english_translation: The nature of existence, consciousness, and bliss are experienced distinctly; thus, in that state, the entire range of phenomena is perceived as complete.
dheesh_gita::245.translation_literal: सच्चिदानन्दभावानाम् (existence-consciousness-bliss states) अनुभूतिः (experience) पृथक् पृथक् (separately/individually) स्यात् (is) अतः (therefore) तत्र (in that) सम्पूर्ण (complete) दृश्यजातम् (phenomena/seen things) प्रतीयते (appears/is perceived)
dheesh_gita::245.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::245.essence: Distinct experiences of existence, consciousness, and bliss reveal the fullness of all phenomena.
dheesh_gita::245.simple_meaning: Existence, awareness, and joy can be felt as separate experiences, yet in that awareness, everything appears complete and unified.
dheesh_gita::245.simple_insight: There is freedom in seeing distinct inner states while also sensing the fullness of all experience.
dheesh_gita::245.detailed_meaning: This teaching explores how the three fundamental qualities—existence, consciousness, and bliss—are each experienced distinctly by the inner being. Yet, in such a state, the entire world of appearances manifests as complete and unified, revealing a profound vision of reality.
dheesh_gita::245.modern_relevance: When you meditate deeply, you might notice different feelings clearly, yet sense a connectedness that holds everything together.
dheesh_gita::245.insight: It shifts perception from fragmented feelings to a unified experience of reality, revealing hidden wholeness in diversity.

dheesh_gita::246.verse_sanskrit:
यत्र त्रिपुटिसम्बन्धलेशमात्रं न विद्यते ।
सच्चिदानन्दभावानामनुभूतिः पृथड्न च ॥
dheesh_gita::246.verse_hindi: जहां त्रिपुटि सम्बन्ध का लेशमात्र नहीं है, जहां सत् चित् और आनन्द भाव का स्वतंत्र अनुभव नहीं है
dheesh_gita::246.english_translation: Where there is not even a trace of the triple bond, there is a direct experience of truth, consciousness, and bliss.
dheesh_gita::246.translation_literal: यत्र (where) त्रिपुटिसम्बन्धलेशमात्रं (triple-bond-connection-trace only) न (not) विद्यते (exists) । सच्चिदानन्दभावानाम् (truth-consciousness-bliss-states) अनुभूतिः (experience) पृथड्न (direct) च (and) ॥
dheesh_gita::246.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::246.essence: Freedom from all bonds reveals direct experience of truth, consciousness, and bliss.
dheesh_gita::246.simple_meaning: When no binding connections remain, you can directly experience truth, consciousness, and bliss.
dheesh_gita::246.simple_insight: There is freedom and clarity when you let go of all limiting attachments.
dheesh_gita::246.detailed_meaning: The verse describes a state without the triple bond—attachments or ties that bind the self. In this freeing moment, the true self reveals itself as pure truth, consciousness, and bliss, beyond all restrictions.
dheesh_gita::246.modern_relevance: You know that deep moment when distractions and obligations fall away, and you feel fully present and joyful without effort.
dheesh_gita::246.insight: It teaches you to recognize the conditions that obscure your true self and to release them for direct experience.

dheesh_gita::247.verse_sanskrit:
यत्राप्येतत्त्रयं तिष्ठेदावेऽद्धैते निरन्तरम् ।
उदेति निश्चितं तत्र स्वरूपज्ञानमुत्तमम ॥
dheesh_gita::247.verse_hindi: और जहां यह तीनों ही अद्वैत भाव में निरन्तर स्थित है वहीं उत्तम स्वरूपज्ञान का उदय होता है
dheesh_gita::247.english_translation: And where these three continuously exist in non-dual awareness, there surely arises the highest knowledge of true nature.
dheesh_gita::247.translation_literal: यत्रापि (wherever) एतत् (this) त्रयम् (three) तिष्ठेत् (remain) अवेऽद्धैते (in non-duality) निरन्तरम् (continuously) उदेति (arises) निश्चितं (certainly) तत्र (there) स्वरूपज्ञानम् (knowledge of true nature) उत्तमम् (highest)
dheesh_gita::247.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::247.essence: Continuous non-dual awareness brings forth the highest knowledge of true self.
dheesh_gita::247.simple_meaning: When your mind continuously remains in a state of non-dual awareness, the highest understanding of your true self naturally arises.
dheesh_gita::247.simple_insight: There is profound clarity and peace when you see beyond separation into oneness.
dheesh_gita::247.detailed_meaning: This verse teaches that when the three elements (likely mind, intellect, and inner state) remain united in non-dual awareness without interruption, the highest knowledge of one’s true nature emerges. It points to the moment of awakening beyond division.
dheesh_gita::247.modern_relevance: When your thoughts, feelings, and awareness stop dividing experience, a deep clarity about who you really are naturally surfaces.
dheesh_gita::247.insight: It teaches you to cultivate continuous non-dual awareness, which opens the door to profound self-knowledge.

dheesh_gita::248.verse_hindi: तटस्थ ज्ञान बहुभावो से युक्त है क्योकि अहंतत्व और महत्तत्व दोनों संयोग से उसका अस्तित्व है
dheesh_gita::248.english_translation: I exist as the detached witness, joined with many states, because of the union of ego and grandeur.
dheesh_gita::248.translation_literal: यत्तः (that which) अस्तित्वं (existence) तटस्थस्य (of the detached) अहं (I) अहत्व (ego-ness) योगतः (by union) तटस्थानम् (detached state) अन्त्यस्मान् (from the end) अभुभावैः (many states) समन्वितम् (joined)
dheesh_gita::248.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::248.essence: You exist as a detached witness combining ego and greatness without being defined by either.
