dheesh_gita::349.verse_hindi: हे सर्वज्ञ ! ज्ञान भूमियों का महान् अद्भुत रहस्य और अविभक्तज्ञान के प्रकाश करने वाली शैलो को सुनकर
dheesh_gita::349.english_translation: O All-Knowing One! Hear the great wondrous secret of the realms of knowledge and the illuminating path of undivided wisdom.
dheesh_gita::349.translation_literal: हे (O) सर्वज्ञ (All-Knowing) / ज्ञानभूमीनां (of the realms of knowledge) / हे (O) सर्वज्ञ (All-Knowing) / महाद्भुतम् (great wondrous) / तथाऽविभक्तज्ञानस्य (and of undivided wisdom) / शैलीं (path/style) / श्रुत्वा (hearing) / प्रकाशिकाम् (illuminating)
dheesh_gita::349.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::349.essence: A wondrous secret reveals the unified and illuminating nature of true wisdom.
dheesh_gita::349.simple_meaning: There is a great and wondrous secret about the realms of knowledge and the clear path of undivided wisdom that the listener is invited to hear.
dheesh_gita::349.simple_insight: You feel invited into a profound mystery that could change how you understand knowledge itself.
dheesh_gita::349.detailed_meaning: Addressing a wise listener, the verse introduces a profound secret about the nature of knowledge and the unified wisdom that shines beyond division, setting the stage for deep inquiry.
dheesh_gita::349.modern_relevance: You stand at the edge of a new insight, ready to uncover the hidden unity behind scattered facts and ideas.
dheesh_gita::349.insight: It shifts your curiosity from fragmented understanding to seeking the seamless, illuminating whole of wisdom.

dheesh_gita::350.verse_sanskrit:
अस्माकं संशयाः सर्वे दूरीभूता न संशयः ।
अस्मानुपदिशैतञ्च कृपां कृत्वाऽधुना प्रभो ! ॥
dheesh_gita::350.verse_hindi: हमारी सब शंकाएं दूर हो गई हैं इसमें सन्देह नहीं। अब हे प्रभो । कृपा करके
dheesh_gita::350.english_translation: All our doubts have been dispelled without a doubt. Now, O Lord, please show your grace.
dheesh_gita::350.translation_literal: अस्माकं (our) संशयाः (doubts) सर्वे (all) दूरीभूता (have been removed) न (not) संशयः (doubt) । अस्मानुपदिशैतञ्च (to us this instruction) कृपां (grace) कृत्वा (having done) अधुना (now) प्रभो (O Lord) ।
dheesh_gita::350.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::350.essence: Complete clarity removes all doubt and opens the way for compassionate support.
dheesh_gita::350.simple_meaning: All doubts have completely vanished. Now the speaker asks the divine for grace.
dheesh_gita::350.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing uncertainty has ended and openness to receive help.
dheesh_gita::350.detailed_meaning: After receiving teachings or clarity, the speaker expresses that all doubts are gone and requests the divine for compassion and guidance ahead.
dheesh_gita::350.modern_relevance: You finish a difficult conversation or learning with relief and quietly ask for support to move forward.
dheesh_gita::350.insight: It encourages embracing clarity with gratitude and openness to further guidance or support.

dheesh_gita::351.verse_sanskrit:
को नन्वज्ञानभूमीनां प्रभावादूरक्षयन् मुदा ।
मुमुक्षून साधकासीवानयते ज्ञानभूमिकाः ॥
dheesh_gita::351.verse_hindi: हमको यह भी आज्ञा कीजिये कि अज्ञानभूमियों के प्रभाव से बचाकर मुमुक्षु साधक जीवों को आनन्दपूर्वक ज्ञानभूमियों में कौन पहूँचाता है ?
dheesh_gita::351.english_translation: Who, protecting seekers from the influence of ignorance, joyfully leads them to the grounds of knowledge?
dheesh_gita::351.translation_literal: को (who) नन्व (surely) ज्ञानभूमीनां (of knowledge grounds) प्रभावात् (from influence) ऊरक्षयन् (protecting) मुदा (joyfully) मुमुक्षून् (seekers) साधकाः (practitioners) ईशवानयते (leads) ज्ञानभूमिकाः (to knowledge grounds)
dheesh_gita::351.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::351.essence: Joyful guidance protects seekers from ignorance and leads them to knowledge.
dheesh_gita::351.simple_meaning: Someone joyfully protects seekers from ignorance and leads them into the realm of knowledge.
dheesh_gita::351.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing a joyful guide can free you from confusion.
dheesh_gita::351.detailed_meaning: A seeker asks who helps aspirants escape the grip of ignorance and reach clear understanding, highlighting the need for a protector or teacher to guide earnest learners.
dheesh_gita::351.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by doubt and confusion, having someone who cheerfully supports your learning makes all the difference.
dheesh_gita::351.insight: It shifts your focus from struggling alone to trusting in guidance that joyfully removes confusion.

dheesh_gita::352.verse_sanskrit:
अतीत्याज्ञानभूमीश्च कैरुपायैर्मुमुक्षवः ।
लभन्ते ज्ञानभूमिर्हि साधकाः सत्त्वरं ध्रुवम् ॥
dheesh_gita::352.verse_hindi: किन उपायों द्वारा मुमुक्षु साधक अज्ञान भूमियों को अतिक्रमण करके शीघ्र ही ज्ञान भूमियों को प्राप्त करते हैं।
dheesh_gita::352.english_translation: By which means do seekers quickly overcome the lands of ignorance and attain the land of knowledge, which is steadfast reality?
dheesh_gita::352.translation_literal: अतीत्याज्ञानभूमीश्च (overcoming lands of ignorance) कैरुपायैर्मुमुक्षवः (by which means do seekers) लभन्ते (attain) ज्ञानभूमिः (land of knowledge) हि (indeed) साधकाः (practitioners) सत्त्वरं (steadfast reality) ध्रुवम् (fixed, certain)
dheesh_gita::352.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::352.essence: Seekers cross confusion using specific means to gain steady, true knowledge.
dheesh_gita::352.simple_meaning: Seekers use certain methods to leave behind confusion and reach steady, clear knowledge.
dheesh_gita::352.simple_insight: There is hope and clear direction for moving from doubt to certainty.
dheesh_gita::352.detailed_meaning: At a moment of questioning, seekers wonder how to move beyond their confusion. This verse highlights the possibility of crossing ignorance to arrive at a firm, true understanding—an essential step for spiritual progress.
dheesh_gita::352.modern_relevance: You feel stuck in doubt, unsure how to find clarity. This reminds you there are clear ways forward to steady understanding.
dheesh_gita::352.insight: It shifts focus to discovering practical means to escape confusion and find firm knowledge.

dheesh_gita::353.verse_sanskrit:
क्रमादग्रेसरन्तश्च सप्तमु ज्ञानभूमिषु ।
भवन्तं प्राप्नुवन्त्यन्ते सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणम् ॥
dheesh_gita::353.verse_hindi: और सातों ज्ञानभूमियों में क्रमशः अग्रसर होते हुए अन्त में सच्चिदानन्द स्वरूप आप को प्राप्त होते हैं
dheesh_gita::353.english_translation: Progressing step by step through the seven stages of knowledge, you ultimately reach the state of pure existence, consciousness, and bliss.
dheesh_gita::353.translation_literal: क्रमादग्रेसरन्तश्च (step by step advancing) / सप्तमु (seven) / ज्ञानभूमिषु (knowledge fields) / भवन्तं (you) / प्राप्नुवन्ति (attain) / अन्ते (in the end) / सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणम् (form of existence, consciousness, bliss)
dheesh_gita::353.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::353.essence: True understanding unfolds gradually, culminating in pure being, awareness, and joy.
dheesh_gita::353.simple_meaning: You progress through seven levels of knowledge and finally realize your true nature as pure existence, consciousness, and bliss.
dheesh_gita::353.simple_insight: There is a natural unfolding in understanding that leads you to deep peace and joy.
dheesh_gita::353.detailed_meaning: This verse describes a spiritual journey through seven stages of deepening knowledge, culminating in realizing the true self as pure existence, consciousness, and bliss. It suggests a gradual awakening rather than sudden insight.
dheesh_gita::353.modern_relevance: When you learn something new step by step, you build confidence and clarity until everything feels deeply meaningful and joyful.
dheesh_gita::353.insight: It teaches you to trust gradual growth in understanding rather than expecting instant enlightenment.

dheesh_gita::354.verse_sanskrit:
ब्राह्मणा: ! नयते नूनं सर्वलोकहितप्रदः।
ब्रहमाण्डपिण्डस्पायाः सृष्टेश्च धारको महान् ॥
dheesh_gita::354.verse_hindi: ब्राह्मणो ! सर्व लोक हितकर, ब्रह्माण्ड पिण्डात्मक सृष्टि का धारक और अभ्युदय और मुक्ति विधायक यह महान्
dheesh_gita::354.english_translation: The brahmana is indeed the great supporter of the cosmic creation, the benefactor of all worlds' welfare, and the establisher of growth and freedom.
dheesh_gita::354.translation_literal: ब्राह्मणा: (O brahmana) / नयते (leads) / नूनं (indeed) / सर्वलोकहितप्रदः (giver of welfare to all worlds) / ब्रहमाण्डपिण्डस्पायाः (of the cosmic egg) / सृष्टेश्च (and of creation) / धारको (the supporter) / महान् (great)
dheesh_gita::354.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::354.essence: The brahmana supports creation and advances welfare and freedom for all worlds.
dheesh_gita::354.simple_meaning: The brahmana is described as the great supporter of the cosmic creation and the one who benefits all worlds with growth and freedom.
dheesh_gita::354.simple_insight: There is reverence for the role that sustains and nurtures universal welfare and growth.
dheesh_gita::354.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the brahmana is praised as the great supporter who holds the cosmic creation and guides the welfare of all worlds, emphasizing his vital role in sustaining existence and enabling progress and liberation.
dheesh_gita::354.insight: It highlights the importance of a sustaining force that upholds welfare and growth beyond individual concerns.

dheesh_gita::355.verse_sanskrit:
मानवान धर्म एवायं कैवल्याभ्युदयप्रदः।
संरक्ष्याज्ञानभूमिभ्यो ज्ञानभूमीनिरन्तरम् ॥
dheesh_gita::355.verse_hindi: धर्म ही मनुष्यों को अज्ञान भूमियों से बचाकर ज्ञान भूमियों में निरन्तर ही पहुंचा देता है।
dheesh_gita::355.english_translation: Dharma alone continuously protects humans from the realms of ignorance and leads them to realms of knowledge.
dheesh_gita::355.translation_literal: मानवान (humans) / धर्म (dharma) / एवायं (alone this) / कैवल्याभ्युदयप्रदः (freedom-rise-giver) / संरक्ष्याज्ञानभूमिभ्यो (protecting from ignorance-realms) / ज्ञानभूमीनिरन्तरम् (to knowledge-realms continuously)
dheesh_gita::355.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::355.essence: Your true purpose continually shields you from ignorance and leads to wisdom.
dheesh_gita::355.simple_meaning: Your true purpose protects you from confusion and keeps leading you toward clear understanding.
dheesh_gita::355.simple_insight: Knowing your purpose brings trust that confusion won't hold you back forever.
dheesh_gita::355.detailed_meaning: This verse teaches that dharma, or your true purpose, acts as a guardian. It saves humans from ignorance and continually brings them into deeper wisdom, showing the ongoing journey from confusion to clarity.
dheesh_gita::355.modern_relevance: When you feel lost or overwhelmed by doubts, your purpose is the steady guide that draws you toward clarity and confidence.
dheesh_gita::355.insight: It teaches you to see your purpose as a protective force that keeps moving you beyond confusion toward lasting knowledge.

dheesh_gita::356.verse_sanskrit:
ददञ्चभ्युदयं सम्यक सम्प्राप्य्यान्तिमा क्रमात ।
ज्ञानभूर्मि ततो दत्ते निःश्रेयसमहो परम ॥
dheesh_gita::356.verse_hindi: और क्रमशः अभ्युदय को सम्यक् प्रदान करता हुआ अन्तिम ज्ञानभूमि में पहुंचाकर अहो ! तदनन्तर कैवल्य प्रदान करता है
dheesh_gita::356.english_translation: Gradually, it grants proper progress, reaching the final field of knowledge, then bestows supreme freedom.
dheesh_gita::356.translation_literal: ददञ्चभ्युदयं (gradually progress) / सम्यक (properly) / सम्प्राप्य्यान्तिमा (reaching final) / क्रमात (in order) / ज्ञानभूर्मि (field of knowledge) / ततो (then) / दत्ते (gives) / निःश्रेयसमहो (supreme freedom) / परम (ultimate)
dheesh_gita::356.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::356.essence: True freedom unfolds only after gradual, proper progress to final knowledge.
dheesh_gita::356.simple_meaning: Progress happens gradually and properly, leading you to the deepest knowledge and then to ultimate freedom.
dheesh_gita::356.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing growth is a step-by-step journey toward true freedom.
dheesh_gita::356.detailed_meaning: This verse teaches that spiritual or intellectual progress is not sudden but unfolds gradually. One reaches the final profound understanding—the ultimate knowledge—before receiving complete inner freedom. The teaching encourages patience and trust in the natural order of growth.
dheesh_gita::356.modern_relevance: You have been learning and growing slowly, and though it might feel slow sometimes, you are moving toward your deepest clarity and freedom.
dheesh_gita::356.insight: It teaches you to trust gradual progress; deep freedom comes only after steady, proper growth.

dheesh_gita::357.verse_sanskrit:
अहमेवास्मि धर्मस्य स्थितिस्थानं द्विजर्षभाः ।
धर्माकृतिर्ममैवास्ते शक्तिरेव सनातनी ॥
dheesh_gita::357.verse_hindi: हे विप्रो ! धर्म का मैं ही स्थिति स्थान हूँ और धर्मरूपा मेरी ही सनातनी शक्ति
dheesh_gita::357.english_translation: O Brahmin, I alone am the foundation and abode of dharma; my eternal power is the very form of dharma.
dheesh_gita::357.translation_literal: अहमेवास्मि (I alone am) धर्मस्य (of dharma) स्थितिस्थानं (foundation and abode) द्विजर्षभाः (O best of Brahmins) । धर्माकृतिर्ममैवास्ते (dharma-form is indeed mine) शक्तिर् एव (power itself) सनातनी (eternal) ॥
dheesh_gita::357.speaker: Shambhu
dheesh_gita::357.essence: True purpose is inseparable from an eternal, unchanging power that sustains it.
dheesh_gita::357.simple_meaning: Your true purpose is supported by an eternal power that forms its very essence and foundation.
dheesh_gita::357.simple_insight: There is strength in knowing your purpose is rooted in something timeless and unshakable.
dheesh_gita::357.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the divine teacher addresses the Brahmin, revealing that the foundation and abiding place of dharma is inseparable from an eternal power that embodies dharma itself. This teaches that one's true purpose is grounded in a timeless, unchanging reality.
dheesh_gita::357.modern_relevance: When you doubt your direction, remember your deepest purpose is supported by a power beyond time and circumstance.
dheesh_gita::357.insight: It shifts your view from seeing purpose as fragile to recognizing it as inherently stable and eternally grounded.

dheesh_gita::358.verse_sanskrit:
विराटसृष्टे: प्रवाहस्य धारणं कृतवत्यहो।
ममेव सात्त्विकी शक्तिर्नूनं धम्मों महर्षयः !॥
dheesh_gita::358.verse_hindi: अहो ! विराट् सृष्टि के प्रवाह को निश्चय ही धारण किये हुए हैं। हे महर्षिगण! निश्चय मेरी ही सत्त्वगुणमयी शक्ति धर्म है ।
dheesh_gita::358.english_translation: Ah! The great sages surely uphold the flow of the vast creation. Indeed, my power is the quality of goodness that sustains the laws.
dheesh_gita::358.translation_literal: विराटसृष्टे: (of the vast creation) / प्रवाहस्य (of the flow) / धारणं (support) / कृतवत्यहो (have indeed done) / ममेव (mine alone) / सात्त्विकी (of the quality of goodness) / शक्तिर्नूनं (power indeed) / धम्मों (the laws/duties) / महर्षयः (great sages)
dheesh_gita::358.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::358.essence: A steady power of goodness sustains the flow and laws of the vast creation.
dheesh_gita::358.simple_meaning: There is a power of goodness that supports the flow of the entire vast creation and upholds its laws.
dheesh_gita::358.simple_insight: You are part of a vast flow supported by a steady power of goodness.
dheesh_gita::358.detailed_meaning: The verse praises the great sages who maintain the natural order of the vast universe. It reveals that the sustaining power behind this order is a quality of goodness, a steady force that upholds all laws and dharmas in creation.
dheesh_gita::358.modern_relevance: When everything around you feels chaotic, knowing a steady power of goodness holds all things can ground your trust and calm your mind.
dheesh_gita::358.insight: It shifts your view from random chaos to a flow held by an underlying power of goodness.

dheesh_gita::359.verse_sanskrit:
मात्र कश्चन सन्देहो विद्यते द्विजसत्तमाः ।
विद्ययते विप्रशार्दूला: ! शक्ति मे त्रिगुणात्मिका ॥
dheesh_gita::359.verse_hindi: हे ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठो ! इस विषय में कोई सन्देह नहीं है है विप्रपुन्ग्वों! मेरी शक्ति त्रिगुणात्मिका है
dheesh_gita::359.english_translation: O best of Brahmins! There is no doubt in this matter: my power is composed of the three qualities.
dheesh_gita::359.translation_literal: मात्र (only) कश्चन (any) सन्देहो (doubt) विद्यते (exists) द्विजसत्तमाः (best of Brahmins) । विद्ययते (exists) विप्रशार्दूला: (wise Brahmins) ! शक्ति (power) मे (my) त्रिगुणात्मिका (composed of three qualities) ॥
dheesh_gita::359.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::359.essence: The divine power clearly consists of three fundamental qualities without doubt.
dheesh_gita::359.simple_meaning: There is no doubt that the divine power is made up of three qualities.
dheesh_gita::359.simple_insight: You can trust that power arises from the natural three qualities without confusion.
dheesh_gita::359.detailed_meaning: The speaker addresses the learned Brahmins to clarify that there is no uncertainty about the divine power's nature, which is composed of the three fundamental qualities (gunas). This sets a foundation for understanding the interplay of these qualities.
dheesh_gita::359.modern_relevance: When facing complex situations, it helps to remember that underlying forces are often composed of basic, understandable parts.
dheesh_gita::359.insight: It helps you to recognize that complex qualities arise from three fundamental forces, simplifying your understanding.

dheesh_gita::360.verse_sanskrit:
आकर्षणविशिष्टा या सा शक्तीराजसी मता ।
विकर्षणेन सम्पृक्ता शक्ति तामसी तथा ॥
dheesh_gita::360.verse_hindi: आकर्षणशक्ति विशिष्ठ राजसिक शक्ति कहलाती है और विकर्षण शक्ति विशिष्ट तामसिक कहलाती है
dheesh_gita::360.english_translation: The power of attraction is classified as rajasic energy, and the power of repulsion is classified as tamasic energy.
dheesh_gita::360.translation_literal: आकर्षणविशिष्टा (attraction-specific) / या (which) / सा (that) / शक्तीराजसी (power is rajasic) / मता (considered) / । / विकर्षणेन (by repulsion) / सम्पृक्ता (combined) / शक्ति (power) / तामसी (is tamasic) / तथा (also) / ॥
dheesh_gita::360.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::360.essence: Energy moves you either by attraction or repulsion, shaping your inner drive.
dheesh_gita::360.simple_meaning: Two kinds of energy shape your actions: attraction draws you forward, repulsion holds you back.
dheesh_gita::360.simple_insight: You can feel energized by desire or stuck by resistance within yourself.
dheesh_gita::360.detailed_meaning: The narrator explains two fundamental forces affecting human nature: rajasic energy, which attracts and motivates action, and tamasic energy, which repels and causes inertia. Understanding these helps clarify why we sometimes feel pulled toward or away from things.
dheesh_gita::360.modern_relevance: When you want something deeply, you feel energized; when you resist or avoid, you feel drained or stuck.
dheesh_gita::360.insight: Recognize when attraction or repulsion drives your choices, helping you act with clearer awareness.

dheesh_gita::361.verse_sanskrit:
सामञ्जस्य प्रकुर्वाणा तयोः शत्योद्वयोरिह ।
सात्विकी सैव धम्मोऽस्ति शक्तिमें नात्र संशयः ॥
dheesh_gita::361.verse_hindi: और उन दोनों शक्तियों का इस संसार में समन्वय करने वाली मेरी जो सात्विक शक्ति है वही धर्म है इसमें सन्देह नहीं है
dheesh_gita::361.english_translation: The harmonious coordinating power of these two energies in this world is my sattvic energy; this is certainly dharma without doubt.
dheesh_gita::361.translation_literal: सामञ्जस्य (harmony) प्रकुर्वाणा (creating/coordinating) तयोः (of those two) शत्योद्वयोरिह (powers here in this world) । सात्विकी (pure/sattvic) सैव (indeed) धम्मः (law/duty) अस्ति (is) शक्तिमे (my power) नत्र (there is no) संशयः (doubt) ॥
dheesh_gita::361.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::361.essence: True purpose arises from the harmony of two fundamental inner energies.
dheesh_gita::361.simple_meaning: Your true purpose is the harmony created by the balanced interplay of your inner energies in the world.
dheesh_gita::361.simple_insight: There is clarity and trust in knowing your purpose comes from inner balance.
dheesh_gita::361.detailed_meaning: In this moment, Shri Dheesh explains that the true dharma or purpose is the natural harmony created by the two fundamental energies in the world, coordinated by a pure, sattvic power that belongs to the divine teacher.
dheesh_gita::361.modern_relevance: You feel torn between competing desires or responsibilities; finding your purpose means harmonizing these forces within you.
dheesh_gita::361.insight: It teaches you to see your purpose as the natural balance of your inner drives and energies, not separate or conflicting forces.

dheesh_gita::362.verse_sanskrit:
परिव्याप्नोति धर्मस्य शक्तिरेषैव धारिका ।
परमाणुभ्य आ नूनं पूर्णां ब्रह्माण्डविस्तृतिम् ॥
dheesh_gita::362.verse_hindi: यही धर्म की धारिका शक्ति परमाणु से लेकर ब्रह्माण्ड के विस्तार पर्यन्त में परिव्याप्त है
dheesh_gita::362.english_translation: The power that upholds dharma pervades everything from the smallest particle to the vast expanse of the universe.
dheesh_gita::362.translation_literal: परिव्याप्नोति (pervades) धर्मस्य (of dharma) शक्तिरेषैव (by this very power) धारिका (that supports) । परमाणुभ्य (from the atom) आ (to) नूनं (certainly) पूर्णां (complete) ब्रह्माण्डविस्तृतिम् (expanse of the universe) ॥
dheesh_gita::362.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::362.essence: The power supporting your purpose extends from the tiniest atom to the whole universe.
dheesh_gita::362.simple_meaning: The force that sustains your true purpose exists everywhere—from the tiniest particle to the vast universe.
dheesh_gita::362.simple_insight: Your deeper purpose connects you to everything around you, big and small.
dheesh_gita::362.detailed_meaning: This verse reveals that the energy supporting dharma—the true guiding principle—is present everywhere. It spans from the smallest particles to the entire universe, showing that purpose is universal and all-encompassing.
dheesh_gita::362.modern_relevance: When you feel small or disconnected, remembering your purpose links you to something vast and powerful beyond immediate surroundings.
dheesh_gita::362.insight: It shifts your focus from isolated actions to seeing your purpose as part of a universal flow that supports all existence.

dheesh_gita::363.verse_sanskrit:
शक्ते:  संधारिकाया मे धर्मस्यैव प्रभावतः ।
सूयेन्द्वादिग्रहाः सर्वे तथा नक्षत्रमण्डलम् ॥
dheesh_gita::363.verse_hindi: धर्म की धारिका शक्ति के प्रभाव से ही सब सूर्य चन्द्र आदि ग्रह उपग्रह आदि और नक्षत्र मण्डल
dheesh_gita::363.english_translation: By the power that sustains dharma, all the planets like the sun, moon, and their satellites, along with the constellation, exist.
dheesh_gita::363.translation_literal: शक्तेः (by the power) / संधारिकाया (of the sustainer) / मे (my) / धर्मस्यैव (of dharma itself) / प्रभावतः (by the influence) / सूयेन्द्वादिग्रहाः (sun, moon, planets) / सर्वे (all) / तथा (thus) / नक्षत्रमण्डलम् (constellation)
dheesh_gita::363.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::363.essence: All celestial bodies exist due to the sustaining power of dharma.
dheesh_gita::363.simple_meaning: The power that upholds dharma is also the force behind the existence of the sun, moon, planets, and stars.
dheesh_gita::363.simple_insight: You can sense a single power holding all cosmic order together.
dheesh_gita::363.detailed_meaning: This verse explains how the sustaining power of dharma is the cause behind all celestial bodies like the sun, moon, planets, and constellations, highlighting cosmic order's divine support.
dheesh_gita::363.insight: It shows that the universe’s harmony depends on one sustaining force, inviting trust in the natural order.

dheesh_gita::364.verse_sanskrit:
उपग्रहादयोऽप्येवं विराड्देहे ममानिशम् ।
स्वस्वकक्षामुपाश्रित्य भ्रमन्ते हि समन्ततः ॥
dheesh_gita::364.verse_hindi: मेरे विराट् देह में चौतरफ अपनी अपनी कक्षा में निरन्तर परिभ्रमण करते है
dheesh_gita::364.english_translation: In my cosmic body, various beings constantly move around within their own realms.
dheesh_gita::364.translation_literal: उपग्रहादयोऽपि (satellites and others) एवम् (thus) विराट् देहे (in the cosmic body) मम (my) निशम् (continuously) स्व स्व कक्षाम् (their own orbits) उपाश्रित्य (depending on) भ्रमन्ते (they wander) हि (indeed) समन्ततः (all around).
dheesh_gita::364.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::364.essence: Many beings move continuously in their own realms within the vast cosmic body.
dheesh_gita::364.simple_meaning: Various beings move continuously within their own areas inside the vast cosmic body.
dheesh_gita::364.simple_insight: You are part of a vast system where many different forces move in their own place.
dheesh_gita::364.detailed_meaning: This verse describes the cosmic body filled with many beings like satellites, each moving in their own distinct orbits. It shows the vastness and order within the cosmic form, highlighting the interplay of many parts within the whole.
dheesh_gita::364.insight: It invites you to see yourself as part of a larger system, each element moving in its own role without confusion.

dheesh_gita::365.verse_sanskrit:
सृष्टरक्षाञ्च कुर्वन्ति साहाय्यं ददतो मिव:।
देवासुरेण युद्धेन देव्याः सृष्टेः पवित्रताम् ॥
dheesh_gita::365.verse_hindi: और परस्पर को सहायता देकर सृष्टि की रक्षा करते हैं। धर्म की उत्तम धारिका शक्ति देवासुर संग्राम के द्वारा दैवी सृष्टि की पवित्रता
dheesh_gita::365.english_translation: The beings protect creation by helping each other; through the conflict of devas and asuras, the divine world's purity is maintained.
dheesh_gita::365.translation_literal: सृष्ट (creation) रक्षाञ्च (and protection) कुर्वन्ति (do) साहाय्यं (help) ददतो (giving) मिवः (like). देवासुरेण (by devas and asuras) युद्धेन (by war) देव्याः (of the divine) सृष्टेः (creation's) पवित्रताम् (purity).
dheesh_gita::365.speaker: Narrator
dheesh_gita::365.essence: Creation’s protection depends on mutual support and cosmic struggle preserving purity.
dheesh_gita::365.simple_meaning: Creation is protected because beings help one another, and the conflict between divine and shadow forces keeps the divine world pure.
dheesh_gita::365.simple_insight: Helping each other sustains the world’s balance and its sacredness through struggle.
dheesh_gita::365.detailed_meaning: The narrator describes how all beings mutually support and protect creation. The ongoing battle between devas and asuras symbolizes the dynamic tension preserving the divine world's purity. This verse sets the cosmic stage rather than teaching a direct lesson.
dheesh_gita::365.insight: It shows that cooperation and conflict together maintain balance, not just peace alone.

dheesh_gita::366.verse_sanskrit:
सम्पादयन्ती धर्मस्य धारिका शक्तिरुत्तमा।
प्रतिष्ठापयते देवान् स्वस्वलोकेऽसुरांस्तथा ॥
dheesh_gita::366.verse_hindi: सम्पादन करती हुई देवताओं और असुरो को अपने अपने लोको में सुप्रतिष्ठित रखती है
dheesh_gita::366.english_translation: The highest power upholds dharma by establishing the radiant beings and the shadow beings firmly in their own realms.
dheesh_gita::366.translation_literal: सम्पादयन्ती (upholding) धर्मस्य (of dharma) धारिका (supporting) शक्तिः (power) उत्तमा (supreme) प्रतिष्ठापयते (establishes) देवान् (the radiant beings) स्वस्व (their own) लोके (in realms) असुरान् (shadow beings) तथा (also)
dheesh_gita::366.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::366.essence: Supreme power maintains cosmic order by holding all beings in their places.
dheesh_gita::366.simple_meaning: A supreme power maintains order by placing radiant and shadow beings firmly in their own worlds.
dheesh_gita::366.simple_insight: Order arises when every being is supported in their rightful place.
dheesh_gita::366.detailed_meaning: The verse describes a supreme force that sustains cosmic order (dharma) by firmly establishing radiant beings (devas) and shadow beings (asuras) in their respective realms, maintaining balance in the universe.
dheesh_gita::366.insight: It shifts the mind to see that balance depends on respecting roles and boundaries in a complex system.

dheesh_gita::367.verse_sanskrit:
निश्चितं मातृभावेन विज्ञाः ! धर्ममयेण मे।
प्रकृतेः पालिता जीवाः पोपिताश्च निरन्तरम् ॥
dheesh_gita::367.verse_hindi: हे विज्ञो! मेरी प्रकृति के धर्ममय मातृभाव के द्वारा ही निरन्तर पालित पोषित होकर जीव
dheesh_gita::367.english_translation: Certainly, O wise one! The beings are continuously nurtured and cared for by my nature's inherent nurturing disposition.
dheesh_gita::367.translation_literal: निश्चितं (certainly) मातृभावेन (by motherly disposition) विज्ञाः (O wise one) धर्ममयेण (full of dharma) मे (my) प्रकृतेः (of nature) पालिता (maintained) जीवाः (beings) पोपिताश्च (and nourished) निरन्तरम् (continuously)
dheesh_gita::367.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::367.essence: Life is continuously nurtured by the caring nature of the divine principle.
dheesh_gita::367.simple_meaning: All beings are constantly cared for and nurtured by the natural, sustaining power of the divine nature.
dheesh_gita::367.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that life is always supported by a nurturing force.
dheesh_gita::367.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the teacher addresses the wise listener, explaining that all living beings are continuously sustained by the nurturing aspect of the divine nature, which is full of dharma. This sets the foundation for understanding how life is upheld.
dheesh_gita::367.insight: Recognize that life is supported by an inherent nurturing force beyond your control or effort.

dheesh_gita::368.verse_sanskrit:
उद्भिजात्स्वेदजं गत्वा स्वेदजादण्डजं तथा ।
ततो गच्छन्त्यदो विप्रा: ! अण्डजाञ्च  जरायुजम् ॥
dheesh_gita::368.verse_hindi: हे विप्रों  ! उद्भिज से स्वेदज, स्वेदज से अण्डज, अण्डज से जरायुज और
dheesh_gita::368.english_translation: O wise ones! From the sprout comes the sweat-born; from the sweat-born comes the egg-born; from the egg-born comes the birth from the womb.
dheesh_gita::368.translation_literal: उद्भिजात् (from the sprout) स्वेदजं (the sweat-born) गत्वा (going to) स्वेदजादण्डजं (from sweat-born the egg-born) तथा (also) । ततो (then) गच्छन्ति (go) अदो (from the egg) विप्रा: (the wise ones) ! अण्डजाञ्च (and from the egg) जरायुजम् (the womb-born) ॥
dheesh_gita::368.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::368.essence: Life emerges through successive natural forms from plants to womb-born beings.
dheesh_gita::368.simple_meaning: Life develops in stages: from plants to sweat-born beings, then to egg-born, and finally to womb-born creatures.
dheesh_gita::368.simple_insight: Life unfolds through natural stages beyond human control or preference.
dheesh_gita::368.detailed_meaning: This verse describes the natural progression of life forms, explaining how beings arise from plants (sprouts), then sweat-born creatures, egg-born creatures, and finally womb-born beings, situating living processes within a natural evolutionary order.
dheesh_gita::368.insight: It shifts focus from human distinctions to understanding life as a continuous natural process.

dheesh_gita::369.verse_sanskrit:
जरायुनाद्योनितो हि मर्त्ययोनि गताः पुनः।
भवन्ति मोक्षमार्गस्य नूनमतेऽधिकारिणः ॥
dheesh_gita::369.verse_hindi: जरायुज योनि से मनुष्य योनि में पहुंचकर अवश्य ही वह कैवल्यमार्ग अर्थात् मोक्षमार्ग के अधिकारी धन जाते हैं।
dheesh_gita::369.english_translation: Those born in mortal forms from parents like Jarayu certainly qualify for the path of freedom.
dheesh_gita::369.translation_literal: जरायुनाद्योनितो (from Jarayu and others) / हि (indeed) / मर्त्ययोनि (mortal womb) / गताः (gone) / पुनः (again) / भवन्ति (become) / मोक्षमार्गस्य (of the path of freedom) / नूनमतेऽधिकारिणः (certainly qualified).
dheesh_gita::369.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::369.essence: Human birth uniquely qualifies you for the path to inner freedom.
dheesh_gita::369.simple_meaning: Being born as a human gives you the opportunity and eligibility to pursue inner freedom.
dheesh_gita::369.simple_insight: Your human life holds a special chance to awaken and free yourself.
dheesh_gita::369.detailed_meaning: Suta declares that beings born into mortal human life, such as those descended from Jarayu, have the unique qualification to pursue the path leading to inner freedom, highlighting the significance of human birth in spiritual progress.
dheesh_gita::369.modern_relevance: You may feel stuck or ordinary, but your human experience is a rare opportunity to awaken beyond limitations.
dheesh_gita::369.insight: Recognize your human life as a precious chance to engage actively with spiritual freedom.

dheesh_gita::370.verse_sanskrit:
ज्ञानं हि धर्माधर्मस्य मानवेभ्यो हि केवलम् ।
कृतास्ते मोक्षमार्गस्य पथिका ददता मया ॥
dheesh_gita::370.verse_hindi: मैंने केवल मनुष्यों को ही धर्म अधर्म का मान प्रदान करके उनको कैवल्य मार्ग का पथिक बना दिया है
dheesh_gita::370.english_translation: I have given humans the sense of right and wrong, making them travelers on the path to freedom.
dheesh_gita::370.translation_literal: ज्ञानं (knowledge) हि (indeed) धर्माधर्मस्य (of right and wrong) मानवेभ्यो (to humans) हि (indeed) केवलम् (only) । कृतास्ते (have made them) मोक्षमार्गस्य (of the path to freedom) पथिका (travelers) ददता (giving) मया (by me) ॥
dheesh_gita::370.speaker: Teacher
dheesh_gita::370.essence: Knowing right and wrong makes humans travelers on the path to freedom.
dheesh_gita::370.simple_meaning: Humans receive the sense of right and wrong to become travelers on the path to inner freedom.
dheesh_gita::370.simple_insight: You carry within you the guidance needed to move toward freedom.
dheesh_gita::370.detailed_meaning: A divine teacher explains that by giving humans the ability to distinguish right from wrong, they become capable of traveling the path toward freedom, highlighting knowledge as the foundation for moral and spiritual progress.
dheesh_gita::370.modern_relevance: When facing a tough choice, your inner sense of right and wrong points you toward true freedom.
dheesh_gita::370.insight: Recognize that your moral awareness is a tool guiding you beyond confusion toward clarity and freedom.

dheesh_gita::371.verse_sanskrit:
धारिका शक्तिरेवासौ धर्मस्य विभपुड्वा: ! ।
क्रमादुन्नमयन्ती वै मानवानुत्तरोत्तरम् ॥
dheesh_gita::371.verse_hindi: हे विप्र  श्रेष्ठो! यह धर्म की  धारिका शक्ति ही मनुष्यों की क्रमशः उत्तरोत्तर उन्नति
dheesh_gita::371.english_translation: O noble one! It is the sustaining power of dharma that gradually elevates humans step by step.
dheesh_gita::371.translation_literal: धारिका (sustaining) शक्तिरेव (power indeed) असौ (that) धर्मस्य (of dharma) विभपुड्वा: (supporter) । क्रम (stepwise) अदुन्नमयन्ती (raising) वै (indeed) मानवा (humans) उत्तरोत्तरम् (progressively upwards) ॥
dheesh_gita::371.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::371.essence: Steady support from right principles lifts humans progressively upward.
dheesh_gita::371.simple_meaning: The steady power that upholds what is right guides humans to improve gradually over time.
dheesh_gita::371.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that growth unfolds one step at a time, supported by a steady force.
dheesh_gita::371.detailed_meaning: This verse explains that dharma—the principle of rightness—is like a power that holds and lifts humans. It guides their gradual progress, showing how moral strength supports steady personal and collective growth.
dheesh_gita::371.modern_relevance: When you feel stuck in your growth, remember your values are the steady power helping you improve step by step.
dheesh_gita::371.insight: It teaches you to trust slow, steady progress rooted in right action, not rushing but consistent uplift.

dheesh_gita::372.verse_sanskrit:
कृत्वाऽधिकारिणो ज्ञानभूमेरन्ते च तानहो ।
कैवल्यपदवी तेभ्यः प्रदत्ते च शनैः शनैः  ॥
dheesh_gita::372.verse_hindi: कराकर ही और अहो ! अन्त में उनको ज्ञान भूमि का अधिकारी बनाकर शनैः शनैः कैवल्य पद प्रदान करती है।
dheesh_gita::372.english_translation: By performing their rightful actions, they gradually become entitled to the land of knowledge and are gently granted the state of complete freedom.
dheesh_gita::372.translation_literal: कृत्वा (having done) / अधिकारिणः (entitled) / ज्ञानभूमेः (of the land of knowledge) / अन्ते (in the end) / च (and) / तान् (them) / अहो (oh!) / कैवल्यपदवी (the state of complete freedom) / तेभ्यः (to them) / प्रदत्ते (is given) / च (and) / शनैः शनैः (gradually)
dheesh_gita::372.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::372.essence: Steady, rightful action gradually leads to knowledge and complete freedom.
dheesh_gita::372.simple_meaning: When you do your rightful duties sincerely, you slowly gain knowledge and eventually reach complete inner freedom.
dheesh_gita::372.simple_insight: There is calm hope in steady effort; freedom unfolds with patient commitment.
dheesh_gita::372.detailed_meaning: In this teaching moment, the verse explains that by faithfully performing one's assigned duties, a person gradually becomes fit for higher knowledge and is eventually granted the state of liberation, emphasizing steady progress over haste.
dheesh_gita::372.modern_relevance: You keep showing up and doing your part, even when results aren’t immediate, trusting that growth will come over time.
dheesh_gita::372.insight: This verse shifts your focus from rushing results to consistent, patient action as the path to freedom.

dheesh_gita::373.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वेषां रक्षको धर्मः सर्वजीवहितमदः।
निखिलव्यापकश्चास्ति सव्यभ्योऽभ्युदयमदः ॥
dheesh_gita::373.verse_hindi: धर्म सर्वव्यापक, सजीव हितकारी सर्व रक्षक सबको अभ्युदयप्रद
dheesh_gita::373.english_translation: Dharma is the protector of all and the benefactor of all living beings; it is all-pervading and brings welfare to everyone.
dheesh_gita::373.translation_literal: सर्वेषां (of all) / रक्षको (protector) / धर्मः (dharma) / सर्वजीवहितमदः (benefactor of all living beings) / निखिलव्यापकश्चास्ति (is all-pervading) / सव्यभ्योऽभ्युदयमदः (brings welfare to everyone)
dheesh_gita::373.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::373.essence: True purpose is universal protection and care for the welfare of all beings.
dheesh_gita::373.simple_meaning: Your true purpose is to protect and benefit all living beings everywhere without exception.
dheesh_gita::373.simple_insight: Feeling connected to a purpose bigger than yourself brings care for all life.
dheesh_gita::373.detailed_meaning: In this verse, dharma is described as the universal protector and benefactor of every living being. It emphasizes that true purpose is not self-centered but all-encompassing, aiming to uplift the welfare of all beings.
dheesh_gita::373.modern_relevance: You wake up knowing your work affects many, not just yourself, inspiring care beyond your immediate circle.
dheesh_gita::373.insight: It shifts your focus from personal gain to acting for the welfare of all life around you.

dheesh_gita::374.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वेषां मानसे नूनं मत्स्वरूपप्रकाशकः।
साधकानां हि जीवानां शिवत्वस्य विधायकः ॥
dheesh_gita::374.verse_hindi: और सबके हृदय में मेरे स्वरुप का प्रकाश करनेवाला एवं साधक जीवों को शिवत्वप्रदानकारक है
dheesh_gita::374.english_translation: In every mind, I illuminate the true nature; for seekers, I grant the state of auspiciousness.
dheesh_gita::374.translation_literal: सर्वेषां (of all) मानसे (in the mind) नूनं (indeed) मत्स्वरूपप्रकाशकः (the illuminator of my true nature)। साधकानां (of seekers) हि (indeed) जीवानां (of living beings) शिवत्वस्य (of auspicious state) विधायकः (the grantor) ॥
dheesh_gita::374.speaker: Shambhu
dheesh_gita::374.essence: The true self shines in every mind and grants seekers the blessing of peace.
dheesh_gita::374.simple_meaning: The divine presence shines in every mind and reveals the true self. For those sincerely seeking, it grants the blessing of a peaceful and auspicious state.
dheesh_gita::374.simple_insight: You are a living light; seekers are quietly guided toward peace through your inner truth.
dheesh_gita::374.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the teacher explains that the divine essence shines within all minds, revealing the true nature. Those who sincerely seek this truth are granted the state of auspiciousness, symbolizing peace and spiritual well-being.
dheesh_gita::374.modern_relevance: When you pause and reflect, your inner clarity can quietly guide others who are searching for calm and meaning.
dheesh_gita::374.insight: Recognize that your inner being illuminates your mind and can inspire peace in others seeking truth.

dheesh_gita::375.verse_sanskrit:
धर्मोऽयं ब्राह्मणाः ! प्रोक्तः सार्वभौमस्वरूपभाक् ।
साधारणविशेषाभ्यां द्विधा भिन्नो न संशयः ॥
dheesh_gita::375.verse_hindi: हे ब्राह्मणों ! सांधारण और विशेष रूप से दो प्रकार का यह सार्व: भौमखरूपी धर्म कहा गया है यह निःसन्देह है
dheesh_gita::375.english_translation: O Brahmins, this universal dharma has two forms: the general and the specific, without doubt.
dheesh_gita::375.translation_literal: धर्मः (dharma) / अयम् (this) / ब्राह्मणाः (O Brahmins) / प्रोक्तः (was said) / सार्वभौमस्वरूपभाक् (of universal nature) / साधारणविशेषाभ्यां (by general and specific) / द्विधा (twofold) / भिन्नः (different) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
dheesh_gita::375.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::375.essence: Dharma includes both universal and specific aspects, clearly distinct.
dheesh_gita::375.simple_meaning: The idea of dharma here is described as having two clear aspects: a universal general part and a specific distinct part.
dheesh_gita::375.simple_insight: Understanding dharma as both universal and specific helps you see its true complexity.
dheesh_gita::375.detailed_meaning: The narrator addresses the Brahmins, explaining that dharma is not one single thing but has two kinds—the universal aspect that applies broadly, and the particular aspect that differs by context.
dheesh_gita::375.insight: It teaches you to recognize that rules or duties often have general principles and special details depending on the situation.

dheesh_gita::376.verse_sanskrit:
साधारणस्तयोर्धर्मः सर्वजीवहिते रतः।
अधिकारविशेषस्य जीवानां केन्द्रभागिनाम् ॥
dheesh_gita::376.verse_hindi: उनमे से साधारण धर्म सर्वजीव हिततत्पर है और अधिकार विशेष के केन्द्रो से युक्त जीवों का
dheesh_gita::376.english_translation: The common dharma is dedicated to the welfare of all beings, especially those with specific roles and central faculties.
dheesh_gita::376.translation_literal: साधारणस्तयोः (common/ordinary of the two) / धर्मः (duty) / सर्वजीवहिते (for the welfare of all beings) / रतः (engaged/dedicated) / अधिकारविशेषस्य (of specific authority/role) / जीवानां (of beings) / केन्द्रभागिनाम् (having central parts/faculties)
dheesh_gita::376.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::376.essence: Your general duty is to serve the welfare of all, focusing on those tied to your specific role.
dheesh_gita::376.simple_meaning: Your general duty is to work for the good of all living beings, especially those who depend on your specific role or central position.
dheesh_gita::376.simple_insight: You feel naturally drawn to help others, especially those closest to your responsibilities.
dheesh_gita::376.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, the idea is that among various duties, the common one is caring for all beings, with special attention to those who have particular roles or central faculties. It highlights a balance between universal care and specific responsibility.
dheesh_gita::376.modern_relevance: You find yourself juggling work and family, knowing your main duty is to care for those depending on you while not losing sight of the bigger picture.
dheesh_gita::376.insight: It shifts your focus from isolated tasks to a wider sense of responsibility that includes both all beings and those directly impacted by your role.

dheesh_gita::377.verse_sanskrit:
विशेषस्तु विशेषेण हित सम्पादयत्यलम् ।
साधारणस्य धर्मस्य वर्णयेऽङ्गानि साम्प्रतम् ॥
dheesh_gita::377.verse_hindi: विशेष धर्म निश्चय ही परम हित सम्पादन करता है। मैं इस समय साधारण धर्म के अंगवर्णन करता हूँ
dheesh_gita::377.english_translation: Specific duty surely achieves the highest benefit. Now I describe the aspects of common duty.
dheesh_gita::377.translation_literal: विशेषस्तु (specific) विशेषेण (by specific) हित (benefit) सम्पादयति (achieves) अलम् (certainly) । साधारणस्य (common) धर्मस्य (duty) वर्णयेऽङ्गानि (aspects describe) साम्प्रतम् (now) ॥
dheesh_gita::377.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::377.essence: Fulfilling your unique duty brings the greatest benefit beyond common duties.
dheesh_gita::377.simple_meaning: Doing your specific duty brings the greatest benefit. Now, the parts of common duty are explained.
dheesh_gita::377.simple_insight: Knowing your unique role brings clarity and confidence in action.
dheesh_gita::377.detailed_meaning: The teacher marks a turning point: although common duties exist, your specific duty has the power to bring the highest benefit. This verse frames a teaching on how focusing on what is uniquely yours leads to true success.
dheesh_gita::377.modern_relevance: You juggle many tasks, but the most meaningful progress comes when you focus on what only you can do best.
dheesh_gita::377.insight: Shift your energy from general tasks to your unique responsibilities for clearer purpose.

dheesh_gita::378.verse_sanskrit:
आकर्ण्यन्तां भवद्भिश्च सावधानेन चेतसा।
चतुर्विंशतितत्त्वानां नूनं सन्त्यनुरूपतः ॥
dheesh_gita::378.verse_hindi: आप सावधान चित्त से सुनिए। चौबीस तत्वों के अनुरूप पूर्णावयव
dheesh_gita::378.english_translation: Listen carefully with a focused mind. There are indeed twenty-four essential elements in order.
dheesh_gita::378.translation_literal: आकर्ण्यन्तां (let them listen) / भवद्भिश्च (by you also) / सावधानेन (with careful) / चेतसा (mind) / चतुर्विंशतितत्त्वानां (of twenty-four elements) / नूनं (indeed) / सन्ति (are) / अनुरूपतः (in proper order)
dheesh_gita::378.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::378.essence: Careful, focused listening reveals the ordered nature of fundamental reality.
dheesh_gita::378.simple_meaning: Pay close attention with a calm mind. There are twenty-four fundamental elements arranged properly.
dheesh_gita::378.simple_insight: Calm focus opens the door to understanding complex truths step by step.
dheesh_gita::378.detailed_meaning: At this moment, the narrator invites the listener to pay careful attention. The teaching will explain twenty-four fundamental elements, setting the stage for deep philosophical inquiry.
dheesh_gita::378.modern_relevance: You sit down, quiet your distractions, and prepare to grasp a complex system piece by piece.
dheesh_gita::378.insight: It teaches you to quiet the mind and prepare to receive structured knowledge fully.

dheesh_gita::379.verse_sanskrit:
अङ्गानि पूर्णधर्मस्य चतुर्विंशतिरेव भोः !।
दानं हि त्रिविध प्रोक्तं विद्यार्थाभयभेदतः ॥
dheesh_gita::379.verse_hindi: साधारण धर्म के निश्चय चौबीस ही अंग हैं। दान त्रिविध कहा गया है, यथा-अर्थदान, विद्यादान और अभयदान
dheesh_gita::379.english_translation: The complete dharma has exactly twenty-four parts. Charity is described in three forms: giving wealth, giving knowledge, and giving protection from fear.
dheesh_gita::379.translation_literal: अङ्गानि (parts) / पूर्णधर्मस्य (of complete dharma) / चतुर्विंशतिरेव (exactly twenty-four) / भोः (are)! / दानं (charity) / हि (indeed) / त्रिविध (threefold) / प्रोक्तं (is said) / विद्यार्थाभयभेदतः (due to the distinctions of wealth, knowledge, and fearlessness)
dheesh_gita::379.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::379.essence: True duty includes giving wealth, knowledge, and fearless support equally.
dheesh_gita::379.simple_meaning: Complete duty includes twenty-four parts, and charity is threefold: giving money, teaching, and removing fear.
dheesh_gita::379.simple_insight: Giving takes many forms—sharing what you have, what you know, and safety.
dheesh_gita::379.detailed_meaning: In this teaching by Suta, dharma is explained as having twenty-four essential parts. Among these, charity is emphasized in three forms: sharing material resources, imparting knowledge, and offering protection to those in need.
dheesh_gita::379.modern_relevance: You help a friend not just by lending money, but also by sharing advice and supporting them through tough times.
dheesh_gita::379.insight: Expand your idea of giving beyond money to include knowledge and emotional safety.

dheesh_gita::380.verse_sanskrit:
कायिकं वाचिकञ्चैव तथा मानसमेव च ।
तपोऽपि त्रिविधः प्रोक्तं तपोविद्भिर्महात्मभिः ॥
dheesh_gita::380.verse_hindi: तपोवेत्ता महात्माओं ने तप के भी शारीरिक वाचनिक मानसिक रूप से तीन भेद कहे हैं
dheesh_gita::380.english_translation: The great beings have described austerity as threefold: physical, verbal, and mental.
dheesh_gita::380.translation_literal: कायिकं (physical) / वाचिकञ्चैव (and verbal) / तथा (also) / मानसमेव (mental indeed) / च (and) / तपोऽपि (austerity also) / त्रिविधः (threefold) / प्रोक्तं (described) / तपोविद्भिः (by austerity-knowers) / महात्मभिः (great beings)
dheesh_gita::380.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::380.essence: Real discipline includes your body, speech, and mind working as one.
dheesh_gita::380.simple_meaning: Discipline or austerity is practiced through three aspects: physical actions, spoken words, and mental focus.
dheesh_gita::380.simple_insight: True effort involves what you do, say, and think in harmony.
dheesh_gita::380.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, the great sages explain that austerity is not just about physical practices but also includes control over speech and mind. This expands the idea of discipline beyond the body to a holistic self-mastery.
dheesh_gita::380.modern_relevance: You realize that real self-control isn’t just about what you do but also how you speak and the thoughts you nurture.
dheesh_gita::380.insight: It teaches you to balance your physical actions, speech, and mental intentions as one integrated discipline.

dheesh_gita::381.verse_sanskrit:
षडविधः कर्मयज्ञोऽस्ति नित्यो नैमित्तिकस्तथा ।
काम्योऽध्यात्मोऽधिदेवा षष्ठश्चैवाधिभौतिकः ॥
dheesh_gita::381.verse_hindi: कर्मयज्ञ नित्य नैमित्तिक काम्य  और अध्यातम अधिदैव अधिभूत रूप से षड्विध है
dheesh_gita::381.english_translation: There are six types of sacred actions: eternal, occasional, desire-driven, spiritual, divine, and physical.
dheesh_gita::381.translation_literal: षडविधः (six types) कर्मयज्ञोऽस्ति (of sacred actions are) नित्यो (eternal) नैमित्तिकस्तथा (occasional also) काम्योऽध्यात्मोऽधिदेवा (desire-driven, spiritual, divine) षष्ठश्चैवाधिभौतिकः (and sixth is physical)
dheesh_gita::381.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::381.essence: Actions serve six distinct purposes, blending duty, desire, spirit, and nature.
dheesh_gita::381.simple_meaning: Actions can be understood in six ways: always ongoing, occasional, driven by desire, connected to spirit, linked to the divine, or rooted in the physical world.
dheesh_gita::381.simple_insight: Recognizing many types of action helps you see your efforts as part of a larger whole.
dheesh_gita::381.detailed_meaning: This verse explains the sixfold classification of sacred actions known as karmayajna, including those that are constant, occasional, motivated by desire, spiritual, divine, and natural-physical. It lays a foundation for understanding how actions serve different roles in life and practice.
dheesh_gita::381.modern_relevance: You juggle tasks that feel routine, urgent, inspired by passion, or connected to your deeper values—each has its unique meaning.
dheesh_gita::381.insight: It teaches you to recognize the different motivations behind your actions, guiding clearer intention and balance.

dheesh_gita::382.verse_sanskrit:
उपास्तियज्ञभेद्राश्च विद्यन्ते नवधा दनु ।
ते सर्व भक्तिमूलाः स्युर्योगमूलास्तथैव च ॥
dheesh_gita::382.verse_hindi: उपासना यज्ञ के नौ  ही भेद है वह सब भक्ति और योगमूलक हैं
dheesh_gita::382.english_translation: There are nine types of worship and sacrifice; all are rooted in devotion and yoga.
dheesh_gita::382.translation_literal: उपास्ति (worship) यज्ञभेद्राश्च (and types of sacrifice) विद्यन्ते (exist) नवधा (ninefold) दनु (are) । ते (they) सर्व (all) भक्तिमूलाः (rooted in devotion) स्युः (are) योगमूलाः (rooted in yoga) तथैव (also) च (and) ॥
dheesh_gita::382.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::382.essence: All forms of worship and sacrifice arise from devotion and yoga.
dheesh_gita::382.simple_meaning: Worship and sacrifice come in nine forms, but all are based on devotion and yoga.
dheesh_gita::382.simple_insight: Knowing your practice connects to devotion and yoga brings a deeper sense of purpose.
dheesh_gita::382.detailed_meaning: The verse explains that worship and sacrifice have nine different forms, but each is rooted in devotion and yoga. This reveals how outward rituals are united by inner love and wisdom.
dheesh_gita::382.modern_relevance: When you perform any act of devotion or service, remembering that all forms come from the same source helps you focus and deepen your intention.
dheesh_gita::382.insight: It shifts your view from seeing rituals as separate acts to understanding them as expressions of devotion and inner connection.

dheesh_gita::383.verse_sanskrit:
उपास्तेरास्ति योगो हि स्थली देहो न संशयः ।
तस्याश्चैव द्विजा: ! ज्ञेया भक्तिः प्राणस्वरूपिणी ॥
dheesh_gita::383.verse_hindi: उपासना का योग स्थूलदेह है यह निस्सन्देह है। हे ब्राहाणो ! भक्ति उसी की ही प्राणरूपिणी है।
dheesh_gita::383.english_translation: The practice of devotion is indeed embodied in the physical body; O Brahmins, devotion is the very essence of life.
dheesh_gita::383.translation_literal: उपास्तेरास्ति (in worship/practice there is) योगो (union/yoga) हि (indeed) स्थली (physical/earthly) देहो (body) न (not) संशयः (doubt) । तस्याः (of that) च (also) एव (indeed) द्विजाः (brahmins) ! ज्ञेया (to be known) भक्तिः (devotion) प्राणस्वरूपिणी (life-form/essence) ॥
dheesh_gita::383.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::383.essence: Devotion is the living essence present within your physical body.
dheesh_gita::383.simple_meaning: Devotion is not separate from your body; it is the living essence of life within you.
dheesh_gita::383.simple_insight: You can feel devotion as a vibrant, living presence within your own body.
dheesh_gita::383.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the teacher addresses Brahmins, clarifying that true devotional practice is grounded in the physical body itself. Devotion is described as the very life force, emphasizing that spiritual practice is not separate from daily living or the body.
dheesh_gita::383.modern_relevance: When you pause and feel your breath or heartbeat, you connect to devotion flowing naturally through your body, not somewhere far away.
dheesh_gita::383.insight: It teaches you to recognize devotion as an embodied experience, not just a distant emotion or abstract idea.

dheesh_gita::384.verse_sanskrit:
मन्त्री हठो लयो राज इनि भेदाचतुर्विधात् ।
चतुर्षापासना वेद्या नूनं योगविचारतः ॥
dheesh_gita::384.verse_hindi: योग के  विचार से उपासना मन्त्र हठ लय राजन चतुर्विध भेद से निश्चय ही चतुर्विध जाननी चाहिये
dheesh_gita::384.english_translation: From the yoga perspective, the mantra, effort, rhythm, and king represent four distinct types; these four kinds of worship must be known.
dheesh_gita::384.translation_literal: मन्त्री (mantra) / हठो (effort) / लयो (rhythm) / राज (king) / इनि (these) / भेदाचतुर्विधात् (fourfold distinctions) / चतुर्षापासना (four types of worship) / वेद्या (must be known) / नूनं (certainly) / योगविचारतः (from yoga consideration)
dheesh_gita::384.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::384.essence: Worship divides into four distinct types that must be understood through yoga.
dheesh_gita::384.simple_meaning: There are four kinds of worship based on mantra, effort, rhythm, and the king; these four must be understood from the yoga viewpoint.
dheesh_gita::384.simple_insight: Understanding different types of worship opens the way for deeper practice.
dheesh_gita::384.detailed_meaning: The verse introduces that from the yoga viewpoint, worship divides into four types distinguished by mantra, effort, rhythm, and king; these four forms should be clearly known to advance in spiritual practice.
dheesh_gita::384.insight: It highlights the need to recognize different methods of devotion or practice to find the one suited to your path.

dheesh_gita::385.verse_sanskrit:
तथा भक्तिमभेदन पञ्चश्रोपासनास्त्यहो।
रागदेषादिसञ्जुष्टा भक्ता मेऽशुचयो द्विजा: ! ॥
dheesh_gita::385.verse_hindi: और अहो ! भक्ति के भेद से उपासना पंचविध है। हे ब्राह्मणों ! रागद्वेष युक्त और अशुचि
dheesh_gita::385.english_translation: There are five kinds of worship distinguished by devotion. O Brahmins, many devotees are attached to likes and dislikes and impure.
dheesh_gita::385.translation_literal: तथा (thus) भक्तिमभेदन (by devotion's distinction) पञ्चश्रोपासनास्त्यहो (five kinds of worship exist) । रागदेषादिसञ्जुष्टा (attached to likes and dislikes) भक्ता (devotees) मेऽशुचयो (my impure ones) द्विजा: (Brahmins) ॥
dheesh_gita::385.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::385.essence: True devotion includes many forms but is blocked by attachment and impurity.
dheesh_gita::385.simple_meaning: Devotion can be expressed in five different ways. Many devotees get stuck in attachment and impurity, which blocks true worship.
dheesh_gita::385.simple_insight: You can be devoted yet still be limited by your likes and dislikes.
dheesh_gita::385.detailed_meaning: The verse explains that devotion includes five distinct types of worship. The speaker addresses Brahmins, warning that many devotees are hindered by their attachments to preferences and impurities, which prevent pure devotion.
dheesh_gita::385.modern_relevance: You might feel deeply committed to your passion or belief but still find yourself judging or clinging to what you like or dislike, blocking deeper connection.
dheesh_gita::385.insight: Recognize how attachment to preferences can limit your experience of true devotion and open-hearted worship.

dheesh_gita::386.verse_sanskrit:
मां सदोपासते मूढा आसुरीप्वेव शक्तिषु ।
सकामाः फलमिच्छन्तः शुभं भक्तगणा मम ॥
dheesh_gita::386.verse_hindi: मेरे मूढ़ भक्तगण आसुरी शक्तियों में ही मेरी सदा उपासना करते हैं । शुभ फलेच्छु सकाम भक्तगण
dheesh_gita::386.english_translation: Foolish devotees worship me only through ego-driven powers, desiring good results.
dheesh_gita::386.translation_literal: मां (me) सदोपासते (always worship) मूढा (foolish) आसुरीप्वेव (only by egoistic powers) शक्तिषु (in powers) । सकामाः (desiring results) फलमिच्छन्तः (wanting fruits) शुभं (good) भक्तगणा (devotees) मम (my) ॥
dheesh_gita::386.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::386.essence: True devotion is free from desires for any results, even good ones.
dheesh_gita::386.simple_meaning: Some devotees worship the divine only through selfish desires, hoping for good results rather than pure devotion.
dheesh_gita::386.simple_insight: You feel the difference between wanting and truly loving without expectation.
dheesh_gita::386.detailed_meaning: The divine teacher explains that many so-called devotees are blinded by ego and desire, worshiping only for personal gain and good outcomes instead of genuine connection.
dheesh_gita::386.modern_relevance: You may find yourself doing things for praise or benefits, not from true care or devotion.
dheesh_gita::386.insight: It teaches you to notice when your devotion is mixed with personal gain and to move toward selfless love.

dheesh_gita::387.verse_sanskrit:
मामेवोपासते शश्वन्नूनं देवीषु शक्तिषु ।
विषयानन्द एवाहो ब्रह्मनन्दानुभावकाः ॥
dheesh_gita::387.verse_hindi: मेरी दैवी शक्तियों में निरन्तर ही मेरी ही उपासना करते हैं। अहो! विषयानन्द में ही ब्रह्मानन्द का अनुभव करने वाले
dheesh_gita::387.english_translation: They always worship only me among the divine powers. Truly, those who find joy in worldly pleasures also experience the supreme reality's bliss.
dheesh_gita::387.translation_literal: मामेव (only me) उपासते (worship) शश्वन्नूनं (always indeed) देवीषु (in divine powers) शक्तिषु (in energies) । विषयानन्द (worldly pleasure) एवाहो (indeed) ब्रह्मनन्द (supreme reality's bliss) अनुभावकाः (experiencers) ॥
dheesh_gita::387.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::387.essence: Joy in worldly experience can reveal the bliss of the supreme reality within.
dheesh_gita::387.simple_meaning: Those who appear to worship divine energies actually worship the supreme reality. Even joy from the world can be a way to experience deeper bliss.
dheesh_gita::387.simple_insight: Joy in ordinary life can connect you to the highest experience within.
dheesh_gita::387.detailed_meaning: The verse describes how beings devoted to various divine energies essentially worship the supreme reality behind them. It reveals that worldly pleasures, when experienced fully, can lead to the bliss of the supreme reality, linking devotion with joy.
dheesh_gita::387.modern_relevance: You notice your excitement and happiness in everyday things can sometimes bring a profound sense of peace beyond the moment.
dheesh_gita::387.insight: It shifts your view from seeing worldly joy as mere distraction to recognizing it as a possible doorway to the highest bliss.

dheesh_gita::388.verse_sanskrit:
स्वभावादेव जायन्ते भक्तवृन्दा ममोन्नताः ।
मल्लीलाविग्रहोपास्ती रतात्मानो न संशयः ॥
dheesh_gita::388.verse_hindi: मेरे उन्नत भक्त गण स्वभाव से ही मेरे लीलाविग्रह की उपासना में रतात्मा होते हैं इसमें सन्देह नहीं
dheesh_gita::388.english_translation: My exalted devotees naturally delight in worshipping my playful form without any doubt.
dheesh_gita::388.translation_literal: स्वभावादेव (by nature only) जायन्ते (are born) भक्तवृन्दा (devotee groups) ममोन्नताः (my exalted) । मल्लीलाविग्रहोपास्ती (worship of the playful form) रतात्मानो (absorbed in) न (not) संशयः (doubt) ॥
dheesh_gita::388.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::388.essence: True devotion arises naturally and joyfully from within without any doubt.
dheesh_gita::388.simple_meaning: Devotees who are spiritually advanced naturally enjoy worshipping the divine’s playful form without any doubt.
dheesh_gita::388.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing devotion can arise effortlessly from your true nature.
dheesh_gita::388.detailed_meaning: The verse reveals how exalted devotees, by their very nature, are absorbed in worshipping the divine’s playful form—called Mallila—without hesitation. It celebrates spontaneous devotion as a natural expression of deep love and connection.
dheesh_gita::388.modern_relevance: When you feel naturally drawn to a person or passion, it shows your true self expressing love without struggle or doubt.
dheesh_gita::388.insight: It encourages trusting your natural devotion as genuine and effortless, deepening your connection without second-guessing.

dheesh_gita::389.verse_sanskrit:
भक्ता में ज्ञानिनो रूपे सगुणे निर्गुणे तथा ।
मामुपास्य निमज्जन्ति परमानन्दसागरे ॥
dheesh_gita::389.verse_hindi: और ज्ञानीभक्तगण मेरे सगुणरूप तथा निर्गुणरूप में मेरी उपासना करके परमानन्दसागर में मग्न होते हैं
dheesh_gita::389.english_translation: Devotees and wise ones worship me in both manifest and unmanifest forms, immersing themselves in the ocean of supreme bliss.
dheesh_gita::389.translation_literal: भक्ता (devotees) / में (in) / ज्ञानिनो (wise ones) / रूपे (form) / सगुणे (with qualities) / निर्गुणे (without qualities) / तथा (and) / मामुपास्य (worship me) / निमज्जन्ति (immerse) / परमानन्दसागरे (in supreme bliss ocean)
dheesh_gita::389.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::389.essence: Worshiping the divine with or without form unites you in supreme bliss.
dheesh_gita::389.simple_meaning: Both devoted lovers and seekers of wisdom worship the divine in forms with qualities or without and immerse themselves in supreme bliss.
dheesh_gita::389.simple_insight: You can connect deeply with the divine whether through form or formlessness and feel immense joy.
dheesh_gita::389.detailed_meaning: This verse describes how both devotees, who love the divine with form, and wise seekers, who perceive the divine without form, worship and immerse themselves in supreme bliss. It shows the unity of devotion and wisdom in spiritual experience.
dheesh_gita::389.modern_relevance: When you pray or meditate, it doesn't matter if you picture the divine as a form or just feel a formless presence—you can experience deep peace and joy either way.
dheesh_gita::389.insight: It shifts you to accept multiple valid approaches to spiritual connection, all leading to profound joy.

dheesh_gita::390.verse_sanskrit:
श्रवणं मननश्चैव निदिध्यासनमेव च ।
ज्ञानयज्ञस्य भेदाः स्युत्रिविधा हि महर्षयः ॥
dheesh_gita::390.verse_hindi: हे महर्षिगण! श्रवण मनन और निदिध्यासन रूप से ज्ञानयज्ञ के तीन भेद कहे गये हैं
dheesh_gita::390.english_translation: O great seers! The knowledge practice has three types: hearing, reflection, and deep meditation.
dheesh_gita::390.translation_literal: श्रवणं (hearing) मननश्चैव (and reflection also) निदिध्यासनमेव (and deep meditation alone) च (also) । ज्ञानयज्ञस्य (of the knowledge practice) भेदाः (divisions) स्युत्रिविधा (three types) हि (indeed) महर्षयः (great seers) ॥
dheesh_gita::390.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::390.essence: True knowledge unfolds through hearing, reflection, and deep meditation as distinct stages.
dheesh_gita::390.simple_meaning: Gaining true knowledge involves three steps: listening carefully, thinking deeply, and meditating fully.
dheesh_gita::390.simple_insight: Real understanding comes in stages, each building your inner clarity and connection.
dheesh_gita::390.detailed_meaning: The narrator explains to the assembly of great seers that the practice of knowledge divides into three parts: hearing or listening to teachings, reflecting on them thoughtfully, and deeply meditating to absorb their meaning fully. This framework guides seekers on the wisdom path.
dheesh_gita::390.modern_relevance: When learning something new, you first hear it, then mull it over, and finally absorb it deeply, just like building any skill.
dheesh_gita::390.insight: Recognize learning as a process: intake, contemplation, and deep integration, not just quick knowledge.

dheesh_gita::391.verse_sanskrit:
चतुर्विंशतिरेतानि धर्मस्य प्राकृतान्यहो।
अङ्गानि सर्वजीवानां साधकानि हितस्य नुः॥
dheesh_gita::391.verse_hindi: धर्म के अहो ! ये चौबीस स्वभावसिद्ध अङ्ग सर्व जीव हितसाधक कहे गये है
dheesh_gita::391.english_translation: O Aho of Dharma! These twenty-four natural qualities of Dharma are all beneficial limbs for all beings.
dheesh_gita::391.translation_literal: चतुर्विंशतिरेतानि (twenty-four) धर्मस्य (of dharma) प्राकृतान्यहो (natural, O Aho) अङ्गानि (limbs) सर्वजीवानां (of all beings) साधकानि (beneficial) हितस्य (for welfare) नुः (they are)
dheesh_gita::391.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::391.essence: Natural qualities of dharma are universal supports for the welfare of all beings.
dheesh_gita::391.simple_meaning: There are twenty-four natural qualities of dharma that help all beings live well and fulfill their purpose.
dheesh_gita::391.simple_insight: Knowing your natural qualities can guide you toward what truly benefits you and others.
dheesh_gita::391.detailed_meaning: The verse addresses the idea that dharma consists of twenty-four natural qualities or limbs that support the welfare of every living being, highlighting a universal framework for ethical and purposeful living.
dheesh_gita::391.modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed by choices, but recognizing your natural strengths can clarify what really supports your growth and well-being.
dheesh_gita::391.insight: This verse invites you to recognize and cultivate your inherent qualities as the foundation for meaningful action.

dheesh_gita::392.verse_sanskrit:
विभिन्नरुचयो लोका नानाशक्तिमया यतः ।
अतः साधारणो धर्मः सर्वमाणिहितावहः ॥
dheesh_gita::392.verse_hindi: क्योंकि लोक में रुचि विभिन्न है और सामर्थ्य भी विभिन्न है इस कारण साधारण धर्म सर्वप्राणिहितप्रद है
dheesh_gita::392.english_translation: Because people have different tastes and strengths, the common duty is to protect all living beings.
dheesh_gita::392.translation_literal: विभिन्नरुचयो (different tastes) / लोका (people) / नानाशक्तिमया (with various strengths) / यतः (because) / अतः (therefore) / साधारणो (common) / धर्मः (duty) / सर्वमाणिहितावहः (protecting all beings)
dheesh_gita::392.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::392.essence: Your shared duty is to protect all beings despite their differences.
dheesh_gita::392.simple_meaning: People differ in what they like and what they can do, so your basic duty is to protect and care for all living beings.
dheesh_gita::392.simple_insight: You can feel connected by embracing care for everyone, despite their differences.
dheesh_gita::392.detailed_meaning: In a world full of diverse individuals with varied tastes and powers, the teaching urges that the shared duty is to act for the welfare of all living beings, emphasizing a universal ethic beyond personal differences.
dheesh_gita::392.modern_relevance: At work or in your community, you meet people with very different strengths and preferences. Remembering your duty to support everyone creates harmony.
dheesh_gita::392.insight: This shifts your focus from judging differences to embracing a duty of universal care and protection.

dheesh_gita::393.verse_sanskrit:
अङ्गैः पूर्णस्य धर्मस्य चतुर्विंशतिसङ्घयकैः ।
स्वरूपं चेद्विजानीयुः सर्वलोकहितालयम् ॥
dheesh_gita::393.verse_hindi: यदि चौबीस अङ्गो से पूर्ण धर्म के सर्वलोकहितकर स्वरूप को
dheesh_gita::393.english_translation: If the twenty-four limbs of complete dharma are known, they reveal the nature that benefits all realms.
dheesh_gita::393.translation_literal: अङ्गैः (by limbs) / पूर्णस्य (complete) / धर्मस्य (of dharma) / चतुर्विंशति (twenty-four) / सङ्घयकैः (assemblies) / स्वरूपं (nature) / चेद् (if) / ज्ञानीयुः (known) / सर्वलोकहितालयम् (benefiting all worlds)
dheesh_gita::393.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::393.essence: Complete dharma is made of many parts that serve the welfare of all.
dheesh_gita::393.simple_meaning: Understanding the full set of twenty-four parts of complete dharma reveals its true nature that supports the welfare of all beings.
dheesh_gita::393.simple_insight: You feel connected knowing dharma is meant to help everyone around you.
dheesh_gita::393.detailed_meaning: The narrator introduces dharma as a complete system made of twenty-four parts that together reveal its true nature: to promote the welfare of all worlds. This sets the stage for exploring dharma’s full meaning and purpose.
dheesh_gita::393.modern_relevance: When you learn all aspects of your responsibilities, you see how your work supports the wider community.
dheesh_gita::393.insight: It shifts your view from isolated duties to a unified purpose benefiting all beings.

dheesh_gita::394.verse_sanskrit:
धर्मजिज्ञासवो नूनमुदारहृदयास्तदा।।
श्रीगुरोः पदवी पूज्यां प्राप्नुयुः सर्वमाणिनाम् ॥
dheesh_gita::394.verse_hindi: धर्म जिज्ञासु जान जायें तो वह उदार हृदय होकर सब प्राणियों के ही गुरू की पूज्यपदवी को प्राप्त कर लेते हैं।
dheesh_gita::394.english_translation: Those who seek to understand their true purpose become generous-hearted and attain the revered status of teacher for all beings.
dheesh_gita::394.translation_literal: धर्म (duty/true purpose) / जिज्ञासवः (seekers/inquirers) / नूनम् (indeed/surely) / उदारहृदयाः (generous-hearted) / तदा (then) // श्रीगुरोः (of the revered teacher) / पदवी (status/position) / पूज्यां (worthy of honor) / प्राप्नुयुः (they attain) / सर्वमाणिनाम् (of all beings)
dheesh_gita::394.speaker: Narrator
dheesh_gita::394.essence: Seeking true purpose with an open heart leads to universal respect as a guide.
dheesh_gita::394.simple_meaning: When you sincerely seek to understand your deep purpose, your heart grows generous and you earn respect as a teacher to all beings.
dheesh_gita::394.simple_insight: True purpose softens your heart and naturally brings you honor and connection.
dheesh_gita::394.detailed_meaning: The verse describes those who earnestly inquire into their dharma (true purpose). Their openness and generosity grow so much that they reach a revered status like a teacher respected by all beings. It highlights the transformative power of sincere searching.
dheesh_gita::394.modern_relevance: You dive deep into your work or life’s meaning, and others naturally begin to look up to you with respect and trust.
dheesh_gita::394.insight: It teaches that sincere inquiry transforms your attitude and others’ recognition, turning you into a living example and guide.

dheesh_gita::395.verse_sanskrit:
यावन्तो धर्ममार्गा वै जनिष्यन्ते युगे युगे।
साधारणस्य धर्मस्य कियन्त्यङ्गान्यमीपुः ते ॥
dheesh_gita::395.verse_hindi: युगयुग मे जितने ही धर्म मार्ग पैदा होंगे वे सब साधारण धर्म के इन अंशों मे से कुछ अंशों का
dheesh_gita::395.english_translation: In every age, many paths of dharma arise, all containing parts of the common dharma.
dheesh_gita::395.translation_literal: यावन्तो (as many) धर्ममार्गा (paths of dharma) वै (indeed) जनिष्यन्ते (will arise) युगे युगे (in every age) / साधारणस्य (of the common) धर्मस्य (dharma) कियन्ति (some) अङ्गानि (parts) अन्य (other) मीपुः (among them) ते (those)
dheesh_gita::395.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::395.essence: Many dharma paths arise, all containing elements of a shared common dharma.
dheesh_gita::395.simple_meaning: Many different paths of dharma appear in each age, but all share some common parts.
dheesh_gita::395.simple_insight: It feels reassuring that many paths can lead to the same core truth.
dheesh_gita::395.detailed_meaning: This verse describes how through every era, various dharma paths emerge, each carrying parts of a shared common dharma. It sets the stage for understanding dharma’s diversity yet unity.
dheesh_gita::395.modern_relevance: You see people follow different lifestyles and beliefs, yet many share similar basic values deep down.
dheesh_gita::395.insight: It shifts your view from seeing paths as separate to recognizing shared foundations beneath diversity.

dheesh_gita::396.verse_sanskrit:
गृहीत्वैव प्रयास्यन्ति कृतार्थत्वम संशयम् ।
प्रादुर्भुनाश्च ये लोके धर्ममार्गा द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
dheesh_gita::396.verse_hindi: आश्रय लेकर ही निःसन्देह कृतकृत्यता को प्राप्त होंगे।  हे ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठों! संसार में जितने धर्ममार्ग
dheesh_gita::396.english_translation: By taking firm hold, they surely attain the sense of accomplishment. O best of Brahmins! Among all paths of righteousness in the world,
dheesh_gita::396.translation_literal: गृहीत्वैव (by firmly taking) प्रयास्यन्ति (will exert/try) कृतार्थत्वम (the sense of accomplishment) संशयम् (without doubt) । प्रादुर्भुनाश्च (indeed arise) ये (who) लोके (in the world) धर्ममार्गा (paths of righteousness) द्विजोत्तमाः (best of Brahmins) ॥
dheesh_gita::396.speaker: Suta
dheesh_gita::396.essence: Firm effort without doubt brings undeniable accomplishment.
dheesh_gita::396.simple_meaning: If you hold firmly and put in effort, you will definitely feel accomplished without any doubt.
dheesh_gita::396.simple_insight: There is confidence in knowing that steady effort leads to real success.
dheesh_gita::396.detailed_meaning: The narrator addresses the best of Brahmins, explaining that those who firmly commit to their righteous efforts without hesitation will surely experience a true sense of accomplishment in the world’s many paths.
dheesh_gita::396.modern_relevance: You’re working on a tough project. When you hold steady and keep trying, you will feel that your efforts truly pay off.
dheesh_gita::396.insight: It teaches you to commit fully and trust that steady effort will bring clear results.

dheesh_gita::397.verse_sanskrit:
अधुनावधि तेऽप्येवं कृतार्थत्वं गता ध्रुवम् ।
मात्र कश्चन सन्देहो विद्यते विमपुङ्गवाः॥
dheesh_gita::397.verse_hindi: अभी तक उत्पन्न हुए हैं, वह भी ऐसे ही कृतार्थता को प्राप्त हुए हैं हे विप्रो ! इसमें कुछ सन्देह नहीं है।
dheesh_gita::397.english_translation: Until now, even those born have certainly attained fulfillment; there is no doubt about this, O wise one.
dheesh_gita::397.translation_literal: अधुनात् (until now) अवधि (limit/period) तेऽपि (even those) एवम् (in this way) कृतार्थत्वं (fulfillment) गता (have attained) ध्रुवम् (certainly) मात्र (only) कश्चन (anyone) सन्देहो (doubt) विद्यते (exists) विमपुङ्गवाः (O wise one)
dheesh_gita::397.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::397.essence: Fulfillment is already achieved by those who walk the path; doubt is unnecessary.
dheesh_gita::397.simple_meaning: Those born until now have certainly achieved fulfillment. There is no doubt about this truth.
dheesh_gita::397.simple_insight: You can trust that fulfillment has already been achieved by those who came before you.
dheesh_gita::397.detailed_meaning: In this moment, the speaker acknowledges that all those born so far have attained a state of fulfillment. Addressing a wise person, this verse confirms certainty about spiritual accomplishment already reached by predecessors.
dheesh_gita::397.modern_relevance: When you wonder if others before you have truly succeeded, remember their fulfillment is certain and doubt only clouds your view.
dheesh_gita::397.insight: It shifts your mind from questioning your progress to trusting the proven fulfillment of those on the path.

dheesh_gita::398.verse_sanskrit:
प्रपूर्णत्वं हि धर्मस्य शाश्वतस्येदमेव नु।
एतदेव महत्त्वच पितृभावोऽप्ययं ध्रुवम् ॥
dheesh_gita::398.verse_hindi: यही शाश्वत धर्म की निश्चय पूर्णता है; यही महत्त्व है और निश्चय यही पितृभाव है
dheesh_gita::398.english_translation: This is truly the complete and eternal nature of dharma; this greatness is certainly the reverence for one's ancestors.
dheesh_gita::398.translation_literal: प्रपूर्णत्वं (completeness) / हि (indeed) / धर्मस्य (of dharma) / शाश्वतस्य (eternal) / एतदेव (this indeed) / महत्त्वच (and greatness) / पितृभावोऽपि (reverence for ancestors also) / यम् (which) / ध्रुवम् (certainly)
dheesh_gita::398.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::398.essence: Complete and eternal dharma is founded on reverence for one's ancestors.
dheesh_gita::398.simple_meaning: Dharma is truly complete and eternal when it includes respect and reverence for your ancestors.
dheesh_gita::398.simple_insight: Feeling connected to those who came before gives your purpose lasting strength.
dheesh_gita::398.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, the timeless nature of dharma is revealed as complete when it embraces reverence for ancestors. This connects your current actions to a greater, enduring lineage and responsibility.
dheesh_gita::398.modern_relevance: When you pause to honor your family history, your daily choices gain deeper meaning and continuity.
dheesh_gita::398.insight: It shifts your view of duty from isolated acts to a continuous honoring of your roots and legacy.

dheesh_gita::399.verse_sanskrit:
अन्यधर्मान्न यो दृष्टि बाधते वा कदाचन ।
यथायोग्यन्तु सर्वभ्यो द्विविधाऽभ्युदयमदः ॥
dheesh_gita::399.verse_hindi: जो धर्म अन्य धर्मों से द्वेष न करे अथवा अन्य धर्मों को कभी बाधा न दे और सबको यथाधिकार उभय विध अभ्युदय प्रदान करे और सबको
dheesh_gita::399.english_translation: One who never hates or obstructs other paths and allows everyone their rightful growth experiences twofold progress.
dheesh_gita::399.translation_literal: अन्यधर्मान्न (other paths not) / यो (who) / दृष्टि (view) / बाधते (obstructs) / वा (or) / कदाचन (ever) / यथा (according to) / योग्यन्तु (may be proper) / सर्वभ्यो (to all) / द्विविधाऽभ्युदयमदः (twofold progress indeed)
dheesh_gita::399.speaker: Unknown
dheesh_gita::399.essence: True growth happens when you respect and uplift all rightful paths without obstruction.
dheesh_gita::399.simple_meaning: You should never hate or obstruct other people's ways and allow everyone to grow according to their own right.
dheesh_gita::399.simple_insight: There is strength and expansion when you support everyone’s rightful journey without conflict.
dheesh_gita::399.detailed_meaning: This teaching advises that a person should not oppose or hinder other paths or beliefs. Instead, they should allow everyone their rightful place and growth, leading to twofold advancement — personal and collective.
dheesh_gita::399.modern_relevance: In your team or community, progress happens fastest when you respect others' roles and don't block their efforts.
dheesh_gita::399.insight: It shifts your focus from competition to cooperation, recognizing that supporting others enhances your own growth.

dheesh_gita::400.verse_sanskrit:
निःश्रेयसस्य चाऽध्वानं यस्तु दर्शयतेऽखिलान् ।
धर्मः सनातनो नूनमियं हयुपनिषन्मता ॥
dheesh_gita::400.verse_hindi: निःश्रेयस का मार्ग बताए  वही सनातन धर्म है यही उपनिषद् है
