dheesh_gita::691.simple_meaning: You become able to perceive the divine by practicing deep meditation and devotion that leads to direct experience.
dheesh_gita::691.simple_insight: You feel the power of devotion combined with deep inner experience to connect with the divine.
dheesh_gita::691.detailed_meaning: In this verse, the teacher explains that those who engage in sustained meditation and devote themselves with wisdom gain direct, personal experience of the divine presence, enabling true perception beyond intellectual knowledge.
dheesh_gita::691.modern_relevance: When you quiet your mind and stay devoted to your purpose, you begin to sense deeper truths beyond words or concepts.
dheesh_gita::691.insight: It teaches you to value sustained devotion and direct personal experience as the path to truly perceiving the divine.

dheesh_gita::692.verse_sanskrit:
चतुर्वर्णाश्रमस्थानां स्वधर्मासक्तचेतसाम्।
जीवानां किनु  वक्तव्यं श्रद्धालूनां मयि ध्रुवम् ॥
dheesh_gita::692.verse_hindi: चारों वर्ण और चारों आश्रमो के स्वधर्मानुरत जीवों की तो बात ही क्या है मुझमें अटल श्रद्धा रखनेवाले
dheesh_gita::692.english_translation: For those devoted to their own duties in the four classes and stages of life, what need is there to speak? For the faithful, I am always steadfast.
dheesh_gita::692.translation_literal: चतुर्वर्णाश्रमस्थानां (four classes and stages of life) / स्वधर्मासक्तचेतसाम् (attached-minded to own duties) / जीवानाां (of beings) / किनु (indeed) / वक्तव्यं (to be spoken) / श्रद्धालूनां (of the faithful) / मयि (in me) / ध्रुवम् (steadfast)
dheesh_gita::692.speaker: Shri Dheesh
dheesh_gita::692.essence: Faith deepens naturally when you stay devoted to your own true duties.
dheesh_gita::692.simple_meaning: Those who are devoted to their own duties in life’s classes and stages do not need extra proof. For those with firm trust, the divine is always steady.
dheesh_gita::692.simple_insight: There is deep comfort knowing faith grows naturally when you commit to your true role.
dheesh_gita::692.detailed_meaning: The teacher addresses beings who follow their personal duties within the four social classes and life stages. He suggests that for those who are faithful and devoted to their responsibilities, no further explanation is needed because their trust in the divine is unshakable.
dheesh_gita::692.modern_relevance: You feel grounded when you focus fully on your own role instead of comparing yourself to others or doubting your place.
dheesh_gita::692.insight: It encourages you to build trust by engaging sincerely with your own responsibilities, deepening your inner steadiness.

dheesh_gita::693.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वेषामेव जीवानां चतुर्वर्गफलमदा!
वर्त्तते धीशगीतेयं सत्यं सत्यं न संशयः ॥
dheesh_gita::693.verse_hindi: जीवमात्र को ही यह धीशगीता चतुर्वर्ग फलप्रद है। यह सत्य है सत्य है, इसमें सन्देह नहीं है
dheesh_gita::693.english_translation: The Dheesh Gita truly grants the four goals of life to all living beings; this is the truth beyond doubt.
dheesh_gita::693.translation_literal: सर्वेषामेव (to all) / जीवानां (living beings) / चतुर्वर्गफलमदा (giver of four goals' fruits) / वर्त्तते (exists) / धीशगीतेयं (this Dheesh Gita) / सत्यं (truth) / सत्यं (truth) / न (not) / संशयः (doubt)
dheesh_gita::693.speaker: Narrator
dheesh_gita::693.essence: This teaching universally offers all beings the four essential goals of life without doubt.
dheesh_gita::693.simple_meaning: This teaching promises to fulfill the four main aims of life for every living being without any doubt.
dheesh_gita::693.simple_insight: There is certainty in this teaching's power to provide life's true purpose.
dheesh_gita::693.detailed_meaning: The narrator affirms that the Dheesh Gita is a reliable scripture that offers all living beings the four classical aims of life, emphasizing its unquestionable truth and universal applicability.
dheesh_gita::693.insight: It reassures that the teachings can universally guide one's pursuit of meaningful goals in life.

hans_gita::1.verse_sanskrit:
सत्यं दमं क्षमां प्रज्ञां प्रशंसन्ति पितामह ।
विद्वांसो मनुजा लोके कथमेतन्मतं तव ॥
hans_gita::1.verse_hindi: पितामह ! संसार में बहुत से विद्वान् सत्य, इन्द्रिय-संयम, क्षमा और प्रज्ञा (उत्तम बुद्धि)-की प्रशंसा करते हैं। इस विषय में आपका कैसा मत है?
hans_gita::1.english_translation: Grandfather, many wise people in the world praise truth, self-control, forgiveness, and wisdom. What is your view on this?
hans_gita::1.translation_literal: सत्यं (truth) दमं (self-control) क्षमां (forgiveness) प्रज्ञां (wisdom) प्रशंसन्ति (praise) पितामह (grandfather) । विद्वांसः (wise people) मनुजा (humans) लोके (in the world) कथमेतत् (how this) मतं (opinion) तव (your) ॥
hans_gita::1.speaker: Yudhishthira
hans_gita::1.essence: The question opens the path to discern which virtues truly matter.
hans_gita::1.simple_meaning: Many wise people praise qualities like truth, self-control, forgiveness, and wisdom. Yudhishthira asks Bhishma for his opinion.
hans_gita::1.simple_insight: It invites reflection on how to value key virtues, but does not assert a teaching itself.
hans_gita::1.detailed_meaning: As the battle pauses, Yudhishthira respectfully asks Bhishma for his view on the praise of noble qualities by wise people, seeking guidance on these virtues' true importance.
hans_gita::1.modern_relevance: You overhear many people valuing honesty, patience, and wisdom—wondering what truly matters most.
hans_gita::1.insight: It opens a space for questioning common values rather than giving direct advice.

hans_gita::2.verse_sanskrit:
अत्र ते वर्तयिष्येऽहमितिहासं पुरातनम् ।
साध्यानामिह संवादं हंसस्य च युधिष्ठिर ॥
hans_gita::2.verse_hindi: युधिष्ठिर! इस विषय में साध्यगणों का हंस के साथ जो संवाद हुआ था, वही प्राचीन इतिहास मैं तुम्हें सुना रहा हूँ
hans_gita::2.english_translation: Yudhishthira, I will now tell you the ancient history of the dialogue between the sages and the Hamsa.
hans_gita::2.translation_literal: अत्र (here) / ते (to you) / वर्तयिष्येऽहम् (I will tell) / इतिहासं (history) / पुरातनम् (ancient) / साध्यानाम् (of the sages) / इह (here) / संवादं (dialogue) / हंसस्य (of the Hamsa) / च (and) / युधिष्ठिर (O Yudhishthira)
hans_gita::2.speaker: Bhishma
hans_gita::2.essence: Ancient wisdom dialogues prepare the ground for deep spiritual teaching.
hans_gita::2.simple_meaning: I will tell you the old story of the conversation between the sages and the Hamsa.
hans_gita::2.simple_insight: Stories rooted in ancient wisdom prepare us to receive deeper teachings.
hans_gita::2.detailed_meaning: Bhishma prepares Yudhishthira to hear the ancient dialogue between the wise sages and the Hamsa, setting the stage for profound spiritual teachings ahead.
hans_gita::2.insight: Recognizing the value of foundational stories helps open the mind for deeper learning.

hans_gita::3.verse_sanskrit:
हंसो भूत्वाथ सौवर्णस्त्वजो नित्यः प्रजापतिः ।
स वै पर्येति लोकांस्त्रीनथ साध्यानुपागमत् ॥
hans_gita::3.verse_hindi: एक समय नित्य अजन्मा प्रजापति सुवर्णमय हंस का रूप धारण करके तीनों लोकों में विचर रहे थे। घूमते-घामते वे साध्यगणों के पास जा पहुँचे
hans_gita::3.english_translation: Once, the eternal unborn Prajapati took the form of a golden swan and wandered through the three realms, eventually arriving among the perfected beings.
hans_gita::3.translation_literal: हंसो (swan) / भूत्वा (having become) / त (that) / सौवर्णस्त्वजः (golden-bodied) / नित्यः (eternal) / प्रजापतिः (Prajapati) । / स (he) / वै (indeed) / पर्येति (wanders) / लोकान् (worlds) / त्रीण् (three) / अथ (and) / साध्यान् (perfected beings) / उपागमत् (approached) ॥
hans_gita::3.speaker: Unknown
hans_gita::3.essence: The eternal takes form and journeys to meet the perfected beings across all realms.
hans_gita::3.simple_meaning: The eternal, unborn Prajapati took the form of a golden swan and traveled through the three worlds to reach the perfected beings.
hans_gita::3.simple_insight: Sometimes, transformation and journey lead to new understanding and connection.
hans_gita::3.detailed_meaning: The eternal Prajapati, symbolizing the supreme creative force, assumes the form of a golden swan and moves across the three worlds. This sets the stage for teaching by showing the divine presence among the perfected beings, the 'sadhyas'.
hans_gita::3.insight: Transformation and presence in diverse realms open paths to deeper wisdom and connection.

hans_gita::4.verse_sanskrit:
शकुने वयं स्म देवा वै साध्यास्त्वामनुयुज्महे ।
पृच्छामस्त्वां मोक्षधर्मं भवांश्च किल मोक्षवित् ॥
hans_gita::4.verse_hindi: हंस! हम लोग साध्य देवता हैं और आपसे मोक्षधर्म के विषय में प्रश्न करना चाहते हैं; क्योंकि आप मोक्ष-तत्त्व के ज्ञाता हैं, यह बात सर्वदा प्रसिद्ध है
hans_gita::4.english_translation: Hamsa, we are the accomplished deities and wish to ask you about the path of liberation, for you are known as the knower of liberation.
hans_gita::4.translation_literal: शकुने (by whom) / वयं (we) / स्म (indeed) / देवा (deities) / वै (certainly) / साध्याः (accomplished) / त्वाम् (you) / अनुयुज्महे (seek to question) / पृच्छामः (we ask) / त्वां (you) / मोक्षधर्मं (liberation's path) / भवांश्च (indeed you) / किल (certainly) / मोक्षवित् (knower of liberation)
hans_gita::4.speaker: Bhishma
hans_gita::4.essence: True seekers approach the wise to understand the path to freedom.
hans_gita::4.simple_meaning: A group of accomplished beings respectfully asks the wise Hamsa about the path to liberation, recognizing his deep understanding.
hans_gita::4.simple_insight: Seeking guidance from one known for deep wisdom opens the door to understanding freedom.
hans_gita::4.detailed_meaning: In this opening moment, the accomplished deities approach Hamsa, the divine swan symbolizing wisdom, requesting instruction on the nature and path of liberation, acknowledging his reputation as a true knower.
hans_gita::4.insight: Recognize when to seek guidance from true wisdom beyond yourself to move toward freedom.

hans_gita::5.verse_sanskrit:
श्रुतोऽसि नः पण्डितो धीरवादी साधुशब्दश्चरते ते पतत्रिन् ।
किं मन्यसे श्रेष्ठतमं द्विज त्वं कस्मिन्मनस्ते रमते महात्मन् ॥
hans_gita::5.verse_hindi: महात्मन्! हमने सुना है कि आप पण्डित और धीर वक्ता हैं। पतत्रिन्! आपकी उत्तम वाणी का सर्वत्र प्रचार है। पक्षिप्रवर! आपके मत में सर्वश्रेष्ठ वस्तु क्या है? आपका मन किसमें रमता है?
hans_gita::5.english_translation: Great soul, we have heard you are wise and calm in speech. O supreme bird, your noble words spread everywhere. What do you consider the highest? Where does your mind delight?
hans_gita::5.translation_literal: श्रुतः (heard) असि (you are) नः (our) पण्डितः (wise) धीरवादी (calm speaker) साधु शब्दः (noble word) श्चरते (spreads) ते (your) पतत्रिन् (supreme bird) । किं (what) मन्यसे (do you consider) श्रेष्ठतमं (the best) द्विज (twice-born/one addressed) त्वं (you) कस्मिन् (in what) मन् (mind) अस्ते (is) रमते (delights) महात्मन् (great soul) ॥
hans_gita::5.speaker: Yudhishthira
hans_gita::5.essence: The greatest wisdom is revealed by what the mind truly delights in.
hans_gita::5.simple_meaning: Someone respectfully asks what the wise and calm teacher considers the highest and what brings joy to their mind.
hans_gita::5.simple_insight: Curious respect opens the door to deeper wisdom by asking what truly matters to a great soul.
hans_gita::5.detailed_meaning: Yudhishthira addresses the divine Swan, praising its wisdom and calm speech. He asks what the highest truth is and what the enlightened mind delights in, setting the stage for teaching.
hans_gita::5.modern_relevance: You meet someone known for calm wisdom and ask them directly what they value most and where their mind finds peace.
hans_gita::5.insight: It invites shifting focus from external reputation to the inner source of joy and highest value.

hans_gita::6.verse_sanskrit:
तन्नः कार्यं पक्षिवर प्रशाधियत्कर्मणां मन्यसे श्रेष्ठमेकम् ।
यत्कृत्वा वै पुरुषः सर्वबन्धैर्विमुच्यते विहगेन्द्रेह शीघ्रम् ॥
hans_gita::6.verse_hindi: पक्षिराज! खगश्रेष्ठ! समस्त कार्यों में से जिस एक कार्य को आप सबसे उत्तम समझते हों तथा जिसके करने से जीव को सब प्रकार के बन्धनों से शीघ्र छुटकारा मिल सके, उसी का हमें उपदेश कीजिये
hans_gita::6.english_translation: O king of birds, greatest among all, please teach me that one action you consider the best, which frees a person quickly from all bonds.
hans_gita::6.translation_literal: तन् (that) नः (to us) कार्यं (action) पक्षिवर (king of birds) प्रशाधियत् (please teach) कर्मणां (of actions) मन्यसे (you think) श्रेष्ठम् (best) एकम् (one) । यत् (which) कृत्वा (having done) वै (indeed) पुरुषः (person) सर्वबन्धैः (all bonds) विमुच्यते (is freed) विहगेन्द्रे (O lord of birds) शीघ्रम् (quickly) ॥
hans_gita::6.speaker: Yudhishthira
hans_gita::6.essence: The one best action can swiftly free a person from all bonds.
hans_gita::6.simple_meaning: You ask the divine Swan to share the single best action that quickly frees a person from all attachments and bondage.
hans_gita::6.simple_insight: We seek the one action that truly frees us from all limitations and attachments.
hans_gita::6.detailed_meaning: Yudhishthira respectfully requests the divine Swan, revered as the king of birds, to reveal the supreme action that when performed liberates a person swiftly from all bonds of suffering and limitation.
hans_gita::6.insight: It invites you to focus on the most effective practice that releases you from cycles of reactivity and limitation.

hans_gita::7.verse_sanskrit:
इदं कार्यममृताशाः श‍ृणोमि तपो दमः सत्यमात्माभिगुप्तिः ।
ग्रन्थीन् विमुच्य हृदयस्य सर्वान् प्रियाप्रिये स्वं वशमानयीत ॥
hans_gita::7.verse_hindi: अमृतभोजी देवताओं! मैं तो सुनता हूँ कि तप, इन्द्रियसंयम, सत्यभाषण और मनोनिग्रह आदि कार्य ही सबसे उत्तम हैं। हृदय की सारी गाँठे खोलकर प्रिय और अप्रिय को अपने वश में करे अर्थात् उनके लिये हर्ष एवं विषाद न करे
hans_gita::7.english_translation: Those who seek immortality, hear this: austerity, sense control, truthful speech, and mind mastery are the highest practices; freeing all knots of the heart, controlling likes and dislikes without causing joy or sorrow.
hans_gita::7.translation_literal: इदं (this) कार्यम् (practice) अमृताशाः (those seeking immortality) शृणोमि (I hear) तपः (austerity) दमः (sense control) सत्यं (truth) आत्माभिगुप्तिः (mind mastery) । ग्रन्थीन् (knots) विमुच्य (freeing) हृदयस्य (of the heart) सर्वान् (all) प्रिया-अप्रिये (likes-dislikes) स्वं (own) वशमानयीत् (should control) ॥
hans_gita::7.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::7.essence: Discipline and truth free the heart from emotional bondage to likes and dislikes.
hans_gita::7.simple_meaning: The best practice is to discipline yourself with austerity, control your senses, speak truth, and master your mind, freeing your heart from attachment to likes and dislikes.
hans_gita::7.simple_insight: There is peace in not letting likes or dislikes control your heart.
hans_gita::7.detailed_meaning: The divine Swan teaches that those seeking lasting freedom must practice austerity, control their senses, speak truthfully, and discipline their mind. This unties the knots in the heart, so it no longer reacts with joy or sorrow to what it likes or dislikes.
hans_gita::7.modern_relevance: You find yourself overwhelmed by emotional ups and downs, craving approval or fearing criticism; learning to steady your heart brings peace.
hans_gita::7.insight: It teaches you to release emotional reactivity by mastering self-discipline and truthfulness, calming your inner fluctuations.

hans_gita::8.verse_sanskrit:
नारुन्तुदः स्यान्न नृशंसवादीन हीनतः परमभ्याददीत ।
ययास्य वाचा पर उद्विजेत न तां वदेद्रुषतीं पापलोक्याम् ॥
hans_gita::8.verse_hindi: किसी के मर्म में आघात न पहुँचाये। दूसरों से निष्ठुर वचन न बोले। किसी नीच मनुष्य से अध्यात्मशास्त्र का उपदेश न ग्रहण करे तथा जिसे सुनकर दूसरों को उद्वेग हो, ऐसी नरक में डालनेवाली अमङ्गलमयी बात भी मुँह से न निकाले॥
hans_gita::8.english_translation: Do not hurt anyone's heart. Do not speak harsh words to others. Do not learn spiritual teachings from a low-minded person. Do not utter words that disturb others and lead them to the lower realm.
hans_gita::8.translation_literal: नारुन्तुदः (not hurting) स्यान्न (should be) नृशंसवादीन (harsh-speaking) हीनतः (from a low person) परमभ्याददीत (should not be learned). ययास्य (which) वाचा (by speech) पर (others) उद्विजेत (are disturbed) न (not) तां (that) वदेत् (should speak) रुषतीं (leading to punishment) पापलोक्याम् (the lower realm).
hans_gita::8.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::8.essence: Kind speech and wise learning protect both yourself and others from harm.
hans_gita::8.simple_meaning: You should not hurt others with harsh words, avoid learning spiritual teachings from unworthy people, and never say things that disturb or harm others deeply.
hans_gita::8.simple_insight: You realize how powerful kind speech is and how choosing who you listen to protects your peace.
hans_gita::8.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Hamsa advises avoiding cruelty in speech and not accepting spiritual lessons from those who lack integrity. He warns that words causing others distress lead them deeper into suffering, emphasizing responsible communication and wise learning.
hans_gita::8.modern_relevance: You send a message that unintentionally hurts a friend, or find misleading advice online and wonder how to protect your heart and mind.
hans_gita::8.insight: It teaches you to guard your speech and learning sources to protect yourself and others from harm and confusion.

hans_gita::9.verse_sanskrit:
वाक्सायका वदनान्निष्पतन्ति यैराहतः शोचति रात्र्यहानि ।
परस्य नामर्मसु ते पतन्ति तान् पण्डितो नावसृजेत्परेषु ॥
hans_gita::9.verse_hindi: वचनरूपी बाण जब मुँह से निकल पड़ते हैं, तब उनके द्वारा बींधा गया मनुष्य रात-दिन शोक में डूबा रहता है; क्योंकि वे दूसरो के मर्मपर आघात पहुँचाते हैं, इसलिये विद्वान् पुरुष को किसी दूसरे मनुष्य पर वाग्बाण का प्रयोग नहीं करना चाहिये
hans_gita::9.english_translation: Words are like arrows shot from the mouth that cause pain day and night; the wise do not use verbal arrows to hurt others.
hans_gita::9.translation_literal: वाक्सायका (words as arrows) / वदनान्निष्पतन्ति (from the mouth fly out) / यैराहतः (by which struck) / शोचति (suffers) / रात्र्यहानि (day and night) / परस्य (of another) / नामर्मसु (to the vital points) / ते (they) / पतन्ति (fall) / तान् (them) / पण्डितो (the wise) / नावसृजेत्परेषु (should not release on others)
hans_gita::9.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::9.essence: Words can pierce others like arrows; true wisdom avoids causing pain with speech.
hans_gita::9.simple_meaning: Words can cause lasting pain like arrows. A wise person avoids hurting others with speech.
hans_gita::9.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing your words hold power—use them to heal, not hurt.
hans_gita::9.detailed_meaning: Hamsa teaches that spoken words, like arrows, can deeply wound others causing ongoing pain. The wise avoid harmful speech to protect others' hearts and minds.
hans_gita::9.modern_relevance: After a harsh message sent in anger, you notice the lasting hurt it caused and wish you'd held back.
hans_gita::9.insight: It teaches you to restrain harmful speech and practice thoughtful, compassionate communication.

hans_gita::10.verse_sanskrit:
परश्चेदेनमति वादबानैर्भृशं विध्येच्छम एवेह कार्यः ।
संरोष्यमाणः प्रतिहृष्यते यः स आदत्ते सुकृतं वै परस्य ॥
hans_gita::10.verse_hindi: दूसरा कोई भी यदि इस विद्वान् पुरुष को कटुवचन रूपी बाणों से बहुत अधिक चोट पहुँचाये तो भी उसे शान्त ही रहना चाहिये। जो दूसरों के क्रोध करने पर भी स्वयं बदले में प्रसन्न ही रहता है, वह उसके पुण्य को ग्रहण कर लेता है
hans_gita::10.english_translation: If others fiercely attack this wise person with harsh words, he remains calm; one who stays pleased despite others' anger inherits their goodness.
hans_gita::10.translation_literal: परश्चेत् (if others) एनाम् (him) अति (excessively) वादबानैः (with harsh speakers) भ्रृशं (greatly) विध्येच्छाम् (attack) एवेह (indeed) कार्यः (should) । संरोष्यमाणः (angered) प्रतिहृष्यते (is pleased in return) यः (who) स (he) आदत्ते (receives) सुकृतं (good deed) वै (indeed) परस्य (of another) ॥
hans_gita::10.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::10.essence: Calmness in the face of harsh attack transforms others' anger into your own good.
hans_gita::10.simple_meaning: You should remain calm and peaceful even if others insult or attack you harshly. Staying pleased despite anger around you brings you goodness.
hans_gita::10.simple_insight: There is strength and peace in staying calm when others lash out at you.
hans_gita::10.detailed_meaning: Hamsa teaches that even if others speak harshly or attack a wise person verbally, the wise remain calm and peaceful. This calmness transforms the negativity into goodness for the calm one, showing mastery over reactivity.
hans_gita::10.modern_relevance: When someone criticizes or attacks you online or in person, choosing calmness lets you stay above the conflict and receive unexpected goodwill.
hans_gita::10.insight: It shifts your response from reacting to others' anger to peacefully accepting it, turning hostility into a source of your own strength.

hans_gita::11.verse_sanskrit:
क्षेपाभिमानादभिषङ्गव्यलीकं निगृह्णाति ज्वलितं यश्च मन्युम् ।
अदुष्टचेता मुदितोऽनसूयुः स आदत्ते सुकृतं वै परेषाम् ॥
hans_gita::11.verse_hindi: जो जगत् में निन्दा करानेवाले और आवेशमें डालनेके कारण अप्रिय प्रतीत होनेवाले प्रज्वलित क्रोधको रोक लेता है, चित्तमें कोई विकार या दोष नहीं आने देता, प्रसन्न रहता और दूसरोंके दोष नहीं देखता है, वह पुरुष अपने प्रति शत्रुभाव रखनेवाले लोगोंके पुण्य ले लेता है
hans_gita::11.english_translation: One who restrains the blazing anger caused by insult and provocation, keeps a pure mind without faults, stays joyful, and does not see faults in others, inherits the merit of those hostile to him.
hans_gita::11.translation_literal: क्षेपाभिमानादभिषङ्गव्यलीकं (from insult, pride, and provocation) / निगृह्णाति (restrains) / ज्वलितं (blazing) / यश्च (and who) / मन्युम् (anger) / अदुष्टचेता (impurity-free mind) / मुदितः (joyful) / अनसूयुः (without envy) / स (that person) / आदत्ते (receives) / सुकृतं (merit) / वै (certainly) / परेषाम् (of others)
hans_gita::11.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::11.essence: Mastering anger and faultfinding turns hostility into your own merit.
hans_gita::11.simple_meaning: Stopping angry outbursts caused by insult, keeping a peaceful and joyful mind, and not criticizing others brings great merit.
hans_gita::11.simple_insight: Calmness in anger brings you unexpected strength and reward.
hans_gita::11.detailed_meaning: The divine Swan teaches that anger fueled by insult harms the mind. A person who controls such anger, remains joyful and free of envy, and does not focus on others' faults gains the merit of even those who oppose him. This shows the power of equanimity.
hans_gita::11.modern_relevance: When someone pushes your buttons at work or home, holding back anger and staying kind earns respect and peace you can't see immediately.
hans_gita::11.insight: It shifts your response from reaction to mastery, turning enemies' energy into your own gain.

hans_gita::12.verse_sanskrit:
आक्रुश्यमानो न वदामि किंचित् क्षमाम्यहं ताड्यमानश्च नित्यम् ।
श्रेष्ठं ह्येतत् यत् क्षमामाहुरार्याः सत्यं तथैवार्जवमानृशंस्यम् ॥
hans_gita::12.verse_hindi: मुझे कोई गाली दे तो भी बदले में मैं कुछ नहीं कहता हूं। कोई मार दे तो उसे सदा क्षमा ही करता हूँ; क्योंकि श्रेष्ठ जन क्षमा, सत्य, सरलता और दया को ही उत्तम बताते हैं
hans_gita::12.english_translation: If anyone insults me, I do not respond in kind; if struck, I always forgive, for the noble value forgiveness, truth, simplicity, and compassion above all.
hans_gita::12.translation_literal: आक्रुश्यमानो (not retaliating) / न (not) / वदामि (I speak) / किंचित् (anything) / क्षमामि (I forgive) / अहं (I) / ताड्यमानः (being struck) / च (and) / नित्यम् (always) / श्रेष्ठम् (the best) / हि (indeed) / एतत् (this) / यत् (that) / क्षमामाहुः (forgiveness they say) / आर्याः (the noble ones) / सत्यं (truth) / तथा (also) / एव (indeed) / अर्जवम् (simplicity) / अनृशंस्यम् (compassion).
hans_gita::12.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::12.essence: True strength is shown by forgiving insults and harm with truth and compassion.
hans_gita::12.simple_meaning: You choose not to fight back when insulted or hurt but respond with forgiveness, truth, simplicity, and compassion because these qualities are the highest virtues.
hans_gita::12.simple_insight: You feel strength and peace by forgiving instead of reacting with anger or hurt.
hans_gita::12.detailed_meaning: The divine Swan, Hamsa, teaches that even when faced with insult or harm, responding with forgiveness and truth is the noblest way. This teaching comes during the moment of imparting wisdom on how a liberated person remains steady and kind despite adversity.
hans_gita::12.modern_relevance: When someone snaps at you at work or home, you don't lash out but hold to quiet forgiveness and honesty instead.
hans_gita::12.insight: It teaches you to pause and respond with forgiveness rather than escalation, shifting your reaction from reactivity to calm dignity.

hans_gita::13.verse_hindi: वेदाध्ययन का सार है सत्यभाषण, सत्यभाषण का सार है इन्द्रियसंयम और इन्द्रियसंयम का फल है मोक्ष। यही सम्पूर्ण शास्त्रों का उपदेश है
hans_gita::13.english_translation: The essence of the Vedas and Upanishads is truthfulness; the essence of truthfulness is self-control; the essence of self-control is liberation. This is the teaching of all the scriptures.
hans_gita::13.translation_literal: वेदस्योपनिषत्सत्यं (Vedas and Upanishads truthfulness) / सत्यस्योपनिषद्दमः (truthfulness self-control) / दमस्योपनिषन्मोक्षं (self-control liberation) / एतत्सर्वानुशासनम् (this all teaching)
hans_gita::13.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::13.essence: Truthfulness leads to self-control, and self-control leads to freedom.
hans_gita::13.simple_meaning: Truthfulness is the core of sacred teachings. Speaking truth leads to controlling your senses, and controlling your senses brings freedom.
hans_gita::13.simple_insight: You can trust that being truthful naturally guides you toward self-mastery and inner freedom.
hans_gita::13.detailed_meaning: Hamsa explains that the core message of the Vedas and Upanishads is truthfulness. Speaking truth consistently develops control over the senses, and this control ultimately grants liberation. This verse connects sacred knowledge to practical self-discipline and freedom.
hans_gita::13.modern_relevance: When you choose honesty in your words, it strengthens your ability to resist distractions and unhealthy impulses, which leads to real personal freedom.
hans_gita::13.insight: It teaches you to see truthfulness as the foundation for discipline, which in turn opens the door to freedom.

hans_gita::14.verse_sanskrit:
वाचो वेगं मनसः क्रोधवेगं विवित्सा वेगमुदरोपस्थ वेगम् ।
एतान् वेगान् यो विषहदुदीर्णांस्तं मन्येऽहं ब्राह्मणं वै मुनिं च ॥
hans_gita::14.verse_hindi: जो वाणी का वेग, मन और क्रोध का वेग, तृष्णा का वेग तथा पेट और जननेन्द्रिय का वेग-इन सब प्रचण्ड वेगों को सह लेता है, उसी को मैं ब्रह्मवेत्ता और मुनि मानता हूँ
hans_gita::14.english_translation: I consider a person a true knower of the supreme reality and a sage who endures the fierce impulses of speech, mind, anger, desire, and the urges of the body and senses.
hans_gita::14.translation_literal: वाचो (of speech) वेगं (impulse) मनसः (of mind) क्रोधवेगं (impulse of anger) विवित्सा (desire) वेगम् (impulse) उदर (stomach) उपस्थ (genitals) वेगम् (impulse) एतान् (these) वेगान् (impulses) यो (who) विषहति (endures) उदीर्णांश् (fierce) तं (that) मन्ये (I consider) अहं (I) ब्राह्मणं (knower of supreme reality) वै (indeed) मुनिं (sage) च (also)
hans_gita::14.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::14.essence: Mastery comes from enduring your strongest impulses without losing yourself.
hans_gita::14.simple_meaning: A true sage is one who can calmly endure the strongest impulses of speech, mind, anger, desire, and bodily urges.
hans_gita::14.simple_insight: You gain strength and wisdom by not being overwhelmed by your strongest impulses.
hans_gita::14.detailed_meaning: Hamsa teaches that true wisdom and mastery come from enduring intense impulses like speech, thoughts, anger, cravings, and bodily urges without losing balance. This teaching comes as part of guiding a seeker to become a sage who controls inner turbulence.
hans_gita::14.modern_relevance: When your anger flares or your desires pull hard, you feel the power to stay calm is freedom itself.
hans_gita::14.insight: It teaches you to meet strong internal urges with steady endurance, building lasting self-mastery.

hans_gita::15.verse_sanskrit:
अक्रोधनः क्रुध्यतां वै विशिष्टस्तथा तितिक्षुरतितिक्षोर्विशिष्टः ।
अमानुषान्मानुषो वै विशिष्टस् तथा ज्ञानाज्ज्ञानवान्वै प्रधानः ॥
hans_gita::15.verse_hindi: क्रोधी मनुष्यों से क्रोध न करनेवाला मनुष्य श्रेष्ठ है। असहनशील से सहनशील पुरुष बड़ा है। मनुष्येतर प्राणियों से मनुष्य ही बढ़कर है। तथा अज्ञानी से ज्ञानवान् ही श्रेष्ठ है।
hans_gita::15.english_translation: A person who does not get angry at angry people is superior. The tolerant one surpasses the intolerant. Among beings beyond humans, the human is superior. Likewise, the wise surpass the ignorant.
hans_gita::15.translation_literal: अक्रोधनः (non-anger) क्रुध्यतां (of those who are angry) वै (indeed) विशिष्टः (superior) तथा (also) तितिक्षुरतितिक्षोः (of the tolerant and the more tolerant) विशिष्टः (superior) अमानुषान् (non-human beings) मानवः (the human) वै (indeed) विशिष्टः (superior) तथा (also) ज्ञानात् (than knowledge) ज्ञानवान् (the wise) वै (indeed) प्रधानः (the foremost)
hans_gita::15.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::15.essence: True superiority lies in calmness amid anger and wisdom over ignorance.
hans_gita::15.simple_meaning: You are better when you don't get angry at angry people. Being patient is greater than being impatient. Humans are higher than non-humans, and wise people are above the ignorant.
hans_gita::15.simple_insight: You feel stronger and more peaceful when you don't let anger pull you in.
hans_gita::15.detailed_meaning: The divine Swan teaches that not reacting with anger to anger shows true strength. Tolerance is a mark of greatness. Among all beings, humans are distinguished, and wisdom elevates a person beyond ignorance. This moment emphasizes equanimity as a key quality.
hans_gita::15.modern_relevance: When someone snaps at you during a stressful day, you can choose calm instead of reacting, showing true strength in patience.
hans_gita::15.insight: It teaches you to pause before responding, choosing patience over reactive anger and valuing wisdom over ignorance.

hans_gita::16.verse_sanskrit:
आक्रुश्यमानो नाक्रोशेन्मन्युरेव तितिक्षतः 
आक्रोष्टारं निर्दहति सुकृतं चास्य विन्दति ॥
hans_gita::16.verse_hindi: जो दूसरे के द्वारा गाली दी जाने पर भी बदले में उसे गाली नहीं देता, उस क्षमाशील मनुष्य का दबा हुआ क्रोध ही उस गाली देनेवाले को भस्म कर देता है और उसके पुण्य को भी ले लेता है
hans_gita::16.english_translation: A patient person does not retaliate when insulted; their restrained anger burns the offender and claims their merit.
hans_gita::16.translation_literal: आक्रुश्यमानो (not angry) / नाक्रोशेन् (not getting angry) / मन्यु (anger) / एव (indeed) / तितिक्षतः (because of endurance) / आक्रोष्टारं (the one who insults) / निर्दहति (burns) / सुकृतं (the good deed) / च (and) / अस्य (his) / विन्दति (attains)
hans_gita::16.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::16.essence: Resisting anger when insulted quietly protects your virtue and weakens the offense.
hans_gita::16.simple_meaning: When you don’t respond to insults with anger, your self-control protects your good actions and overcomes the harm done.
hans_gita::16.simple_insight: You can grow stronger by not reacting—your patience quietly transforms conflict.
hans_gita::16.detailed_meaning: Hamsa teaches that a person who faces insults without anger restrains their own reactive impulse. This restraint acts like a fire that consumes the harm intended by the offender while preserving the patient person’s merit.
hans_gita::16.modern_relevance: When someone snaps at you during a stressful meeting, staying calm protects your integrity and quietly diffuses the tension.
hans_gita::16.insight: It teaches you to replace reactive anger with steady patience, shifting your power from conflict to composure.

hans_gita::17.verse_sanskrit:
यो नात्युक्तः प्राह रूक्षं प्रियं वा यो वा हतो न प्रतिहन्ति धैर्यात् ।
पापं च यो नेच्छति तस्य हन्तुस्तस्मै देवाः स्पृहयन्ते सदैव ॥
hans_gita::17.verse_hindi: जो दूसरों के द्वारा अपने लिये कड़वी बात कही जाने पर भी उसके प्रति कठोर या प्रिय कुछ भी नहीं कहता तथा किसी के द्वारा चोट खाकर भी धैर्य के कारण बदले में न तो मारने वाले को मारता है और न उसकी बुराई ही चाहता है, उस महात्मा से मिलने के लिये देवता भी सदा लालायित रहते हैं
hans_gita::17.english_translation: One who, when harsh or kind words are spoken to him, does not respond with harshness or favoritism, and who, even when harmed, does not retaliate but remains patient and wishes no harm on the attacker, such a great being is always desired by the divine.
hans_gita::17.translation_literal: यो (who) नात्युक्तः (not excessively spoken) प्राह (speaks) रूक्षं (harsh) प्रियं (kind) वा (or) यो (who) वा (also) हतो (when killed/harmed) न (not) प्रतिहन्ति (retaliates) धैर्यात् (from patience) । पापं (wrong/evil) च (also) यो (who) नेच्छति (does not wish) तस्य (to him) हन्तुस्तस्मै (let him be killed) देवाः (the divine) स्पृहयन्ते (desire) सदैव (always) ॥
hans_gita::17.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::17.essence: True strength is patient calm that refuses to harm even when harmed.
hans_gita::17.simple_meaning: You can face harsh words or harm without reacting in anger or revenge. Staying patient and wishing no harm brings respect even from the divine.
hans_gita::17.simple_insight: There's strength and peace in patience that doesn't seek revenge, attracting a higher presence.
hans_gita::17.detailed_meaning: Hamsa teaches that a person who remains steady and patient, not returning harshness or violence even when attacked, embodies great strength. Such a person’s nature is so pure that divine beings are drawn to them.
hans_gita::17.modern_relevance: When someone insults you or treats you unfairly at work or home, staying calm and not retaliating can protect your peace and inspire respect.
hans_gita::17.insight: It shifts your response from reacting in anger to embracing patience and non-retaliation, which changes your whole presence.

hans_gita::18.verse_sanskrit:
पापीयसः क्षमेतैव श्रेयसः सदृशस्य च ।
विमानितो हतोऽऽक्रुष्ट एवं सिद्धिं गमिष्यति ॥
hans_gita::18.verse_hindi: पाप करनेवाला अपराधी अवस्था में अपने से बड़ा हो या बराबर, उसके द्वारा अपमानित होकर, मार खाकर और गाली सुनकर भी उसे क्षमा ही कर देना चाहिये। ऐसा करनेवाला पुरुष परम सिद्धि को प्राप्त होगा
hans_gita::18.english_translation: One who is sinful should forgive even those equal or greater who insult, strike, or abuse them; such a person attains supreme perfection.
hans_gita::18.translation_literal: पापीयसः (sinful person) क्षमेतैव (should indeed forgive) श्रेयसः (the excellent one) सदृशस्य (of equal) च (and) । विमानितो (insulted) हतोऽऽक्रुष्ट (struck and abused) एवं (thus) सिद्धिं (perfection) गमिष्यति (will attain) ॥
hans_gita::18.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::18.essence: Forgiving harm from equals or superiors leads to supreme spiritual perfection.
hans_gita::18.simple_meaning: You should forgive even those who are equal or greater than you if they insult or harm you. Forgiveness leads to the highest spiritual attainment.
hans_gita::18.simple_insight: You feel the relief and strength that comes from forgiving others despite their offenses.
hans_gita::18.detailed_meaning: Hamsa teaches that even when a sinful person is insulted, beaten, or abused by someone equal or greater, forgiving them is the way to reach the highest spiritual state. This teaching comes as a guide for living beyond ego and resentment.
hans_gita::18.modern_relevance: You face criticism or harsh words from a colleague or stranger, yet choosing forgiveness frees your heart rather than chaining you to anger.
hans_gita::18.insight: It shifts the mind from reacting with resentment to responding with forgiveness, which purifies your heart and opens the way to inner growth.

hans_gita::19.verse_sanskrit:
सदाहमार्यान्निभृतोऽप्युपासे न मे विवित्सा न चमेऽस्ति रोषः ।  
न चाप्यहं लिप्समानः परैमि न चैव किंचिद्विषयेण यामि ॥
hans_gita::19.verse_hindi: यद्यपि मैं सब प्रकार से परिपूर्ण हूँ (मुझे कुछ जानना या पाना शेष नहीं है) तो भी मैं श्रेष्ठ पुरुषों की उपासना (सत्सङ्ग) करता रहता हूँ। मुझपर न तृष्णा का वश चलता है न रोष का। मैं कुछ पाने के लोभ से धर्म का उल्लङ्घन नहीं करता और न विषय की प्राप्ति के लिये ही कहीं आता-जाता हूँ
hans_gita::19.english_translation: Although I am complete in every way, I still worship the noble ones. I am free from desire and anger; I do not violate dharma out of greed nor pursue worldly objects.
hans_gita::19.translation_literal: सदा (always) अहमआर्य (I am noble) निहृतः (free from greed) अपि (even) उपासे (worship) न (not) मे (my) विवित्सा (desire) न (nor) च (and) मे (my) अस्ति (is) रोषः (anger) न (nor) च (and) अपि (also) अहं (I) लिप्समानः (attached) परम् (other) एषि (go) न (not) च (and) एव (indeed) किंचित् (anything) विषयेन (for objects) यामि (go).
hans_gita::19.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::19.essence: True fulfillment includes humble respect without craving or anger.
hans_gita::19.simple_meaning: You may be fulfilled and lack nothing, yet you continue to respect and follow noble people without craving or anger and without breaking your true purpose.
hans_gita::19.simple_insight: You can stay humble and peaceful even when you have everything you need.
hans_gita::19.detailed_meaning: The divine Swan teaches that even when fully fulfilled and free of desire, one should still honor noble people through devotion and respect. This attitude avoids attachment and anger and maintains right conduct, showing true inner freedom.
hans_gita::19.modern_relevance: You’ve achieved your goals but still seek inspiration from mentors without jealousy or frustration, acting with respect and no selfish motives.
hans_gita::19.insight: It teaches you to keep humility and respect alive, even when you feel complete, avoiding desire and anger.

hans_gita::20.verse_sanskrit:
नाहं शप्तः प्रतिशपामि किंचिद् दमं द्वारं ह्यमृतस्येह वेद्मि ।
गुह्यं ब्रह्म तदिदं वा ब्रवीमि न मानुषाच्छ्रेष्ठतरं हि किंचित् ॥
hans_gita::20.verse_hindi: कोई मुझे शाप दे दे तो भी मैं बदले में उसे शाप नहीं देता। इन्द्रियसंयम को ही मोक्ष का द्वार मानता हूँ। इस समय तुम लोगों को एक बहुत गुप्त बात बता रहा हूँ, सुनो। मनुष्य योनि से बढ़कर है
hans_gita::20.english_translation: Even if someone curses me, I do not curse back. I consider control of the senses as the door to freedom. Now I reveal a very secret truth: the human birth is supreme.
hans_gita::20.translation_literal: नाहं (I not) शप्तः (cursed) प्रतिशपामि (return curse) किंचिद् (at all) दमं (control) द्वारं (door) हि (indeed) अमृतस्य (of immortality) एष (this) वेद्मि (I know) । गुह्यं (secret) ब्रह्म (supreme reality) तत् (that) इदं (this) वा (indeed) ब्रवीमि (I speak) न (not) मानुषात् (than human) श्रेष्ठतरं (better) हि (indeed) किंचित् (anything) ॥
hans_gita::20.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::20.essence: True freedom comes from mastery over your senses, not from returning harm.
hans_gita::20.simple_meaning: You should not repay harm with harm. Controlling your senses is the way to true freedom. Human life is precious and highest in value.
hans_gita::20.simple_insight: You feel calm knowing harm need not be met with harm; control brings real freedom.
hans_gita::20.detailed_meaning: Hamsa teaches that even if cursed, one should not curse back. Instead, mastering the senses is the true gateway to liberation. This secret teaching honors human life as the highest opportunity for freedom.
hans_gita::20.modern_relevance: You face criticism or harsh words but choose not to respond in kind. Instead, you focus on steadying your impulses to stay centered.
hans_gita::20.insight: It teaches you to pause before reacting and use self-discipline as your path to freedom.

hans_gita::21.verse_sanskrit:
विमुच्यमानः पापेभ्यो धनेभ्य इव चन्द्रमाः ।
विरजाः कालमाकाङ्क्षन् धीरो धैर्येण सिध्यति ॥
hans_gita::21.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार चन्द्रमा बादलों के औट से निकलने पर अपनी प्रभा से प्रकाशित हो उठता है, उसी प्रकार पापों से मुक्त हुआ निर्मल अन्त:करण वाला धीर पुरुष धैर्यपूर्वक काल की प्रतीक्षा करता हुआ सिद्धि को प्राप्त हो जाता है
hans_gita::21.english_translation: Just as the moon shines brightly after emerging from behind clouds, a pure-hearted, patient person freed from faults attains success by calmly awaiting time.
hans_gita::21.translation_literal: विमुच्यमानः (being freed) / पापेभ्यो (from faults) / धनेभ्य (from impurities) / इव (like) / चन्द्रमाः (the moon) / विरजाः (pure) / कालमाकाङ्क्षन् (awaiting time) / धीरो (the steadfast one) / धैर्येण (with patience) / सिध्यति (succeeds)
hans_gita::21.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::21.essence: Pure patience waiting calmly for time leads to true success like the moon emerging from clouds.
hans_gita::21.simple_meaning: Like the moon brightens after clouds clear, a patient and pure person achieves success by waiting calmly for the right time.
hans_gita::21.simple_insight: You can find peace knowing that patience and purity lead to true accomplishment.
hans_gita::21.detailed_meaning: The divine Swan teaches that just as the moon shines clear after clouds pass, a person freed from faults and impurities who patiently waits for the right moment will achieve success. This moment arrives naturally through time and steady endurance.
hans_gita::21.modern_relevance: You finished a tough project but the results aren’t visible yet. Holding steady and patient will bring the recognition you deserve.
hans_gita::21.insight: Shift from anxious rushing to steady trust in timing; patience itself prepares you for success.

hans_gita::22.verse_sanskrit:
यः सर्वेषां भवति ह्यर्चनीय उत्सेधनस्तम्भ इवाभिजातः ।
यस्मै वाचं सुप्रशस्तां वदन्ति स वै देवान्गच्छति संयतात्मा ॥
hans_gita::22.verse_hindi: जो अपने मन को वश में रखनेवाला विद्वान् पुरुष ऊँचे उठाने वाले खम्भे की भाँति उच्चकुल में उत्पन्न हुआ सबके लिये आदर के योग्य हो जाता है तथा जिसके प्रति सब लोग प्रसन्नतापूर्वक मधुर वचन बोलते हैं, वह मनुष्य देवभाव को प्राप्त हो जाता है
hans_gita::22.english_translation: The wise person who masters the mind becomes revered by all like a noble pillar and is spoken of with respect; such a one attains the state of the divine.
hans_gita::22.translation_literal: यः (who) / सर्वेषां (of all) / भवति (becomes) / हि (indeed) / अर्चनीय (respected) / उत्सेधन-स्तम्भ (pillar that raises high) / इव (like) / अभिजातः (noble-born) । / यस्मै (to whom) / वाचं (speech) / सुप्रशस्तां (praiseworthy) / वदन्ति (speak) / स (that one) / वै (indeed) / देवान् (divine) / गच्छति (attains) / संयतात्मा (self-controlled) ॥
hans_gita::22.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::22.essence: Mastering your mind brings respect and leads to the divine state.
hans_gita::22.simple_meaning: Controlling your mind makes you respected by everyone, like a noble pillar, and leads you to the divine state.
hans_gita::22.simple_insight: You feel honored and peaceful when your mind is steady and respected by others.
hans_gita::22.detailed_meaning: Hamsa teaches that a person who has self-control over their restless mind is admired by all, like a noble pillar that supports greatness. Such a person is spoken of with praise and attains a higher spiritual state.
hans_gita::22.modern_relevance: In a noisy world, when you calm your mind, people notice your steadiness and treat you with respect.
hans_gita::22.insight: It teaches you to cultivate mental discipline so others naturally honor and trust you.

hans_gita::23.verse_sanskrit:
न तथा वक्तुमिच्छन्ति कल्याणान् पुरुषे गुणान् ।
यथैषां वक्तुमिच्छन्ति नैर्गुण्यमनुयुञ्जकाः ॥
hans_gita::23.verse_hindi: किसी से ईर्ष्या रखनेवाले मनुष्य जिस तरह उसके दोषों का वर्णन करना चाहते हैं, उस प्रकार उसके कल्याणमय गुण का बखान करना नहीं चाहते हैं
hans_gita::23.english_translation: Those who envy a person do not want to describe their good qualities but focus on their faults.
hans_gita::23.translation_literal: न (not) / तथा (also) / वक्तुमिच्छन्ति (wish to speak) / कल्याणान् (good) / पुरुषे (in a person) / गुणान् (qualities) / यथैषां (just as) / वक्तुमिच्छन्ति (wish to speak) / नैर्गुण्यम् (faults) / अनुयुञ्जकाः (those who follow/engage)
hans_gita::23.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::23.essence: Envy makes you ignore good qualities and fixate only on faults.
hans_gita::23.simple_meaning: When you feel envy, you focus on someone's faults instead of their good qualities.
hans_gita::23.simple_insight: Envy narrows your view and steals your ability to appreciate others.
hans_gita::23.detailed_meaning: Hamsa explains how envy changes perception: a person consumed by envy refuses to acknowledge another's good qualities and instead highlights faults, distorting reality and blocking clear seeing.
hans_gita::23.modern_relevance: When scrolling social media, you might catch yourself focusing on others' flaws instead of their strengths, driven by envy.
hans_gita::23.insight: Recognize envy as a filter that shifts attention from positive to negative, clearing it reveals balance.

hans_gita::24.verse_sanskrit:
यस्य वाङ्मनसी गुप्ते सम्यक्प्रणिहिते सदा ।
वेदास्तपश्च त्यागश्च स इदं सर्वमाप्नुयात् ॥
hans_gita::24.verse_hindi: जिसकी वाणी और मन सुरक्षित होकर सदा सब प्रकार से परमात्मा में लगे रहते हैं, वह वेदाध्ययन, तप और त्याग- इन सबके फल को पा लेता है
hans_gita::24.english_translation: One whose speech and mind are always securely devoted to the supreme being attains the fruit of the Vedas, austerity, and renunciation.
hans_gita::24.translation_literal: यस्य (whose) वाङ्मनसी (speech and mind) गुप्ते (secured) सम्यक्प्रणिहिते (fully devoted) सदा (always) । वेदास्तपश्च (Vedas, austerity also) त्यागश्च (and renunciation) स (that one) इदं (this) सर्वमाप्नुयात् (attains all) ॥
hans_gita::24.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::24.essence: Steady devotion of mind and speech brings the full fruit of spiritual disciplines.
hans_gita::24.simple_meaning: If your mind and speech are always devoted steadily and securely to the supreme being, you receive the full benefits of sacred knowledge, disciplined practice, and renunciation.
hans_gita::24.simple_insight: There's power in steady devotion that surpasses effort and study alone.
hans_gita::24.detailed_meaning: Hamsa teaches that when both speech and mind remain securely fixed on the supreme being, a person naturally attains the fruits of studying sacred texts, disciplined austerity, and renunciation. This verse highlights devotion as the root cause and foundation for spiritual progress.
hans_gita::24.modern_relevance: You speak kindly and keep your focus on what truly matters; over time, this steady devotion brings results beyond mere effort or knowledge.
hans_gita::24.insight: It shows that steady, secure devotion in both what you say and think is more fruitful than scattered effort or ritual alone.

hans_gita::25.verse_sanskrit:
आक्रोशनावमानाभ्यां नाबुधान् गर्हयेद् बुधः ।   
तस्मान्न वर्धयेदन्यं न चात्मानं विहिंसयेत् ॥
hans_gita::25.verse_hindi: अतः समझदार मनुष्य को चाहिये कि वह कटुवचन कहने या अपमान करने वाले अज्ञानियों को उनके उक्त दोष बताकर समझाने का प्रयत्न न करे। उसके सामने दूसरे को बढ़ावा न दे तथा उस पर आक्षेप करके उसके द्वारा अपनी हिंसा न कराये
hans_gita::25.english_translation: A wise person should not insult the ignorant who speak harsh words or insults. They should neither encourage such behavior nor harm themselves through retaliation.
hans_gita::25.translation_literal: आक्रोशन (harsh words) / अवमानाभ्यां (insults) / न (not) / आबुधान् (ignorant) / गर्हयेत् (should insult) / बुधः (wise person) । तस्मात् (therefore) / न (not) / वर्धयेत् (should encourage) / अन्यं (another) / न (nor) / च (and) / आत्मानं (self) / विहिंसयेत् (should harm) ॥
hans_gita::25.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::25.essence: Responding to harshness with calm preserves your peace and dignity.
hans_gita::25.simple_meaning: A wise person does not insult or retaliate against those who speak harshly or insult them and avoids encouraging such negativity.
hans_gita::25.simple_insight: There is strength in choosing not to respond to insults with more harm.
hans_gita::25.detailed_meaning: In a moment of conflict, the Hamsa advises that a wise person should not respond to harsh insults or disrespect from ignorant people by insulting them back or encouraging such behavior. Instead, the wise keep peace and avoid self-harm through reaction.
hans_gita::25.modern_relevance: When someone sends you a harsh message online or in person, you feel the urge to respond sharply but holding back protects your peace and dignity.
hans_gita::25.insight: It teaches you to break the cycle of conflict by refusing to escalate insults and protecting your own well-being.

hans_gita::26.verse_sanskrit:
अमृतस्येव सन्तृप्येदवमानस्य वै द्विजः ।  
सुखं ह्यवमतः शेते योऽवमन्ता स नश्यति ॥
hans_gita::26.verse_hindi: विद्वान् को चाहिये कि वह अपमान पाकर अमृत पीने की भाँति संतुष्ट हो; क्योंकि अपमानित पुरुष तो सुख से सोता है, किंतु अपमान करने वाले का नाश हो जाता है
hans_gita::26.english_translation: A wise person should be satisfied like drinking nectar even when insulted; the insulted one sleeps happily, but the insulter is destroyed.
hans_gita::26.translation_literal: अमृतस्येव (like nectar) सन्तृप्येत (should be satisfied) एव (indeed) अवमानस्य (of insult) वै (certainly) द्विजः (the twice-born/wise) । सुखं (happily) हि (indeed) अवमतः (the insulted) शेते (sleeps) यः (who) अवमन्ता (the insulter) स (he) नश्यति (is destroyed) ॥
hans_gita::26.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::26.essence: Peaceful acceptance of insult protects you, while the insulter harms themselves.
hans_gita::26.simple_meaning: Being insulted can be endured with calm satisfaction like tasting nectar. Those insulted remain peaceful, while those who insult lose their strength or standing.
hans_gita::26.simple_insight: You can stay peaceful and content even when others put you down.
hans_gita::26.detailed_meaning: The divine Swan teaches that a truly wise person accepts insult without anger or disturbance, finding satisfaction like tasting nectar. While the insulted remain peaceful and unaffected, those who insult others ultimately bring ruin upon themselves.
hans_gita::26.modern_relevance: You receive harsh criticism or disrespect at work or in social life, yet you remain calm and composed, unaffected by others’ negativity.
hans_gita::26.insight: It shifts your response from reactive pain to calm acceptance, showing insult harms the insulter more than you.

hans_gita::27.verse_sanskrit:
यत्क्रोधनो यजते यद्ददाति यद्वा तपस्तप्यति यज्जुहोति ।
वैवस्वतस्तद्धरतेऽस्य सर्वं मोघः श्रमो भवति हि क्रोधनस्य ॥
hans_gita::27.verse_hindi: क्रोधी मनुष्य जो यज्ञ करता है, दान देता है, तप करता है अथवा जो हवन करता है, उसके उन सब कर्मो के फल को यमराज हर लेते हैं। क्रोध करने वाले का वह किया हुआ सारा परिश्रम व्यर्थ जाता है
hans_gita::27.english_translation: When a person who is angry performs sacrifice, gives charity, fasts, or offers oblations, all their efforts are taken by the ruler of death and become fruitless.
hans_gita::27.translation_literal: यत्क्रोधनो (who is angry) यजते (performs sacrifice) यद्ददाति (gives) यद्वा (or) तपस्तप्यति (fasts) यज्जुहोति (offers oblations) । वैवस्वतः (the ruler of death) तद्धरतेऽस्य (takes that of him) सर्वं (all) मोघः (fruitless) श्रमः (effort) भवति (becomes) हि (indeed) क्रोधनस्य (of anger) ॥
hans_gita::27.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::27.essence: Anger turns even your best actions into wasted effort.
hans_gita::27.simple_meaning: If you perform rituals or give charity while angry, your efforts lose their effect and become wasted.
hans_gita::27.simple_insight: You feel the frustration of effort lost to your own anger.
hans_gita::27.detailed_meaning: Hamsa explains that when a person acts out of anger—even in sacred acts like sacrifice or charity—their inner state spoils the value of those actions, making all their effort fruitless before death claims its due.
hans_gita::27.modern_relevance: You worked hard to help someone but snapped in frustration, leaving the impact of your kindness diminished.
hans_gita::27.insight: It teaches you to calm anger before acting so your efforts truly benefit others and yourself.

hans_gita::28.verse_sanskrit:
चत्वारि यस्य द्वाराणि सुगुप्तान्यमरोत्तमाः ।
उपस्थमुदरं हस्तौ वाक्चतुर्थी स धर्मवित् ॥
hans_gita::28.verse_hindi: देवेश्वरों! जिस पुरुष के उपस्थ, उदर, दोनों हाथ और वाणी-ये चारों द्वार सुरक्षित होते हैं, वही धर्मज्ञ है
hans_gita::28.english_translation: The person whose four gates—genitals, abdomen, both hands, and speech—are well guarded, is truly wise in dharma.
hans_gita::28.translation_literal:
चत्वारि (four) यस्य (whose) द्वाराणि (gates) सुगुप्तानि (well guarded) अमरोत्तमाः (excellent) ।
उपस्थम् (genitals) उदरं (abdomen) हस्तौ (in hands) वाक् (speech) चतुर्थी (the fourth) स (that) धर्मवित् (knower of dharma) ॥
hans_gita::28.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::28.essence: True wisdom is shown by self-control over body and speech.
hans_gita::28.simple_meaning: A person who carefully controls their body parts and speech lives in true discipline and understands right conduct.
hans_gita::28.simple_insight: You feel steadiness and control when your actions and words align with your inner values.
hans_gita::28.detailed_meaning: The divine Swan explains that guarding the four gates—sexual organs, stomach, hands, and speech—is a mark of one who truly knows righteous living. This moment highlights self-restraint as the foundation of dharma.
hans_gita::28.modern_relevance: You pause before speaking or acting, knowing your words and deeds shape your life and relationships.
hans_gita::28.insight: It teaches you to practice self-restraint consistently in what you say, do, and even desire.

hans_gita::29.verse_sanskrit:
सत्यं दमं ह्यार्जवमानृशंस्यं धृतिं तितिक्षामभिसेवमानः ।   
स्वाध्यायनित्योऽस्पृहयन्परेषाम्  एकान्तशील्यूर्ध्वगतिर्भवेत्सः ॥
hans_gita::29.verse_hindi: जो सत्य, इन्द्रिय-संयम, सरलता, दया, धैर्य और क्षमा का अधिक सेवन करता है, सदा स्वाध्याय में लगा रहता है, दूसरे की वस्तु नहीं लेना चाहता तथा एकान्त में निवास करता है, वह ऊर्ध्वगति को प्राप्त होता है
hans_gita::29.english_translation: One who practices truthfulness, self-restraint, simplicity, compassion, patience, and forgiveness, constantly studies the scriptures, does not covet others' possessions, and dwells in solitude, attains the highest state.
hans_gita::29.translation_literal: सत्यं (truthfulness) / दमं (self-restraint) / ह्यार्जवमानृशंस्यं (and simplicity without blame) / धृतिं (patience) / तितिक्षामभिसेवमानः (and forgiveness practicing) / स्वाध्यायनित्योऽस्पृहयन् (constantly engaged in self-study, without coveting) / परेषाम् (others') / एकान्तशील्यूर्ध्वगतिर्भवेत्सः (solitude-loving attains highest state)
hans_gita::29.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::29.essence: Living with truth, self-control, compassion, and solitude leads to spiritual advancement.
hans_gita::29.simple_meaning: By practicing truth, self-control, kindness, patience, forgiveness, constant learning, not desiring others' things, and loving solitude, you reach a higher state of being.
hans_gita::29.simple_insight: You feel steady and free when you live simply and avoid craving what isn’t yours.
hans_gita::29.detailed_meaning: Hamsa teaches that a person who embraces qualities like truthfulness, self-restraint, kindness, patience, forgiveness, continuous study, non-attachment to others’ possessions, and solitude, develops the discipline needed to rise spiritually.
hans_gita::29.modern_relevance: After a long day of distractions, you choose to unplug, read quietly, and release envy, feeling a lightness that lifts you beyond stress.
hans_gita::29.insight: This verse guides you to replace craving with steady habits of integrity and calm study, shaping your character upward.

hans_gita::30.verse_sanskrit:
सर्वानेताननुचरन् वत्सवच्चतुरः स्तनान् ।  
न पावनतमं किंचित्सत्यादध्यगमं क्वचित् ॥
hans_gita::30.verse_hindi: जैसे बछड़ा अपनी माता के चारों स्तनों का पान करता है, उसी प्रकार मनुष्य को उपर्युक्त सभी सद्गुणों का सेवन करना चाहिये। मैंने अबतक सत्य से बढ़कर परम पावन वस्तु कहीं किसी को नहीं समझा है
hans_gita::30.english_translation: Just as a calf drinks from all four teats of its mother, you should embrace all the virtues mentioned; I have found nothing purer than truth anywhere.
hans_gita::30.translation_literal: सर्वानेतानुचरन् (embracing all these) वत्सवच्चतुरः (like a calf, all four) स्तनान् (teats) / न (not) पावनतमं (more pure) किंचित् (anything) सत्याद (than truth) अध्यगमं (found) क्वचित् (anywhere)
hans_gita::30.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::30.essence: Taking in all virtues fully leads you closest to the purest reality: truth.
hans_gita::30.simple_meaning: You should take in all good qualities completely, just like a calf drinks from all teats of its mother, because nothing is purer than truth.
hans_gita::30.simple_insight: There's comfort in knowing that embracing all virtues leads you closer to the purest reality, truth.
hans_gita::30.detailed_meaning: The divine Swan teaches that just as a calf drinks from all its mother’s teats, a person should absorb all the good qualities described before. Among all virtues, truth stands as the most sacred and pure, beyond comparison.
hans_gita::30.modern_relevance: You face choices about which values to adopt. Taking in all positive qualities without picking and choosing helps you grow genuinely and steadily.
hans_gita::30.insight: It shifts your practice from selective virtue to embracing all goodness, recognizing truth as the ultimate purifier.

hans_gita::31.verse_sanskrit:
आचक्षेऽहं मनुष्येभ्यो देवेभ्यः प्रतिसञ्चरन् ।
सत्यं स्वर्गस्य सोपानं पारावारस्य नौरिव ॥
hans_gita::31.verse_hindi: मैं चारों ओर घूमकर मनुष्यों और देवताओं से कहा करता हूँ कि जैसे जहाज समुद्र से पार होने का साधन है, उसी प्रकार सत्य ही स्वर्गलोक में पहुँचने की सीढ़ी है
hans_gita::31.english_translation: I tell humans and devas everywhere that truth is the ladder to the higher realm, just as a ship is the means to cross the ocean.
hans_gita::31.translation_literal: आचक्षेऽहं (I tell) मनुष्येभ्यो (to humans) देवेभ्यः (to devas) प्रतिसञ्चरन् (going around) । सत्यं (truth) स्वर्गस्य (of the higher realm) सोपानं (ladder) पारावारस्य (of crossing over) नौरिव (like a ship) ॥
hans_gita::31.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::31.essence: Truth is the essential vehicle to cross from the ordinary to the higher realm.
hans_gita::31.simple_meaning: Truth is the essential means to reach a higher state, just like a ship helps cross an ocean.
hans_gita::31.simple_insight: You can trust that truth will guide you beyond any boundary or challenge.
hans_gita::31.detailed_meaning: The divine Swan (Hamsa) teaches that truth is like a ship that carries beings across the vast ocean of existence to reach the higher realm, addressing both humans and radiant beings (devas).
hans_gita::31.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by challenges, recognizing truth as your steady guide helps you navigate through uncertainty and reach your goals.
hans_gita::31.insight: It shifts your focus from fleeting methods to relying on truth as the reliable vehicle for transformation.

hans_gita::32.verse_sanskrit:
यादृशैः संनिवसति यादृशांश्चोपसेवते ।
यादृगिच्छेच्च भवितुं तादृग्भवति पूरुषः ॥
hans_gita::32.verse_hindi: पुरुष जैसे लोगों के साथ रहता है, जैसे मनुष्यों का सेवन करता हैं और जैसा होना चाहता है, वैसा ही होता है
hans_gita::32.english_translation: A person associates with those like themselves, serves similar people, and becomes what they desire.
hans_gita::32.translation_literal: यादृशैः (with similar) संनिवसति (associates) यादृशाः (similar) च (and) उपसेवते (serves) यदृग् (as) इच्छेच् (desires) भवितुं (to become) तादृग् (such) भवति (becomes) पूरुषः (person)
hans_gita::32.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::32.essence: You become like those you associate with and what you deeply desire.
hans_gita::32.simple_meaning: You tend to live with and help people like yourself, and you become what you deeply want.
hans_gita::32.simple_insight: You feel how your surroundings and desires quietly shape who you are becoming.
hans_gita::32.detailed_meaning: The Swan teaches that a person naturally associates with those similar in nature, serves them, and aligns with their deepest desires. This moment shows how environment and intention shape identity.
hans_gita::32.modern_relevance: You notice how your close friends and daily interactions slowly mold your attitudes and choices.
hans_gita::32.insight: It shifts attention to choosing your company and desires wisely, knowing they form your character.

hans_gita::33.verse_sanskrit:
यदि सन्तं सेवति यद्यसन्तं तपस्विनं यदि वा स्तेनमेव ।
वासो यथा रङ्गवशं प्रयाति तथा स तेषां वशमभ्युपैति ॥
hans_gita::33.verse_hindi: जैसे वस्त्र जिस रंग में रँगा जाय, वैसा ही हो जाता है, उसी प्रकार यदि कोई सज्जन, असज्जन, तपस्वी अथवा चोर का सेवन करता है तो वह उन्हीं-जैसा हो जाता है अर्थात् उसपर उन्हीं का रंग चढ़ जाता है
hans_gita::33.english_translation: Just as a cloth takes the color it is dyed in, a person becomes like the company they keep, whether noble or corrupt.
hans_gita::33.translation_literal: यदि (if) सन्तं (a noble person) सेवति (associates with) यद्यसन्तं (or with an ignoble person) तपस्विनं (an ascetic) यदि (or) वा (also) स्तेनमेव (even a thief) । वासो (cloth) यथा (as) रङ्गवशं (under influence of color) प्रयाति (goes) तथा (so) स (that person) तेषां (of them) वशमभ्युपैति (comes under control/influence) ॥
hans_gita::33.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::33.essence: You become like those whose company you keep, absorbing their qualities.
hans_gita::33.simple_meaning: Your character changes to match those you spend time with, whether good or bad.
hans_gita::33.simple_insight: You feel how deeply others influence who you become inside.
hans_gita::33.detailed_meaning: Hamsa explains that just as cloth absorbs dye, a person absorbs qualities from those they associate with. Spending time with noble or corrupt people shapes your nature accordingly.
hans_gita::33.modern_relevance: You notice how spending time with certain friends changes your mood, thoughts, and even habits over weeks.
hans_gita::33.insight: It teaches you to choose your associations carefully because they shape your habits and character.

hans_gita::34.verse_sanskrit:
सदा देवाः साधुभिः संवदन्ते न मानुषं विषयं यान्ति द्रष्टुम् ।
नेन्दुः समः स्यादसमो हि वायुर्उच्चावचं विषयं यः स वेद ॥
hans_gita::34.verse_hindi: देवतालोग सदा सत्पुरुषों के सङ्ग - उन्हीं के साथ वार्तालाप करते हैं; इसीलिये वे मनुष्यों के क्षणभङ्गर भोगों की ओर देखने भी नहीं जाते। जो विभिन्न विषयों के नश्वर स्वभाव को ठीक-ठीक जानता है, उसकी समानता न चन्द्रमा कर सकते हैं न वायु
hans_gita::34.english_translation: The divine realms always converse with the virtuous; they do not turn to fleeting human desires. One who truly knows the transient nature of all objects is as equal as the moon and the wind.
hans_gita::34.translation_literal: सदा (always) देवाः (divine beings) साधुभिः (with virtuous) संवदन्ते (converse) न (not) मानुषं (human) विषयं (objects) यान्ति (go) द्रष्टुम् (to see) । नेन्दुः (moon) समः (equal) स्याद (is) असमः (unequal) हि (indeed) वायुर्उच्चावचं (wind-high-sounding) विषयं (object) यः (who) स (that) वेद (knows) ॥
hans_gita::34.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::34.essence: True knowledge of impermanence makes you steady like the moon and wind.
hans_gita::34.simple_meaning: The divine speak only with the virtuous and ignore fleeting human desires. Knowing the transient nature of all things keeps you steady and equal like the moon and wind.
hans_gita::34.simple_insight: You feel calm and steady when you see desires as temporary and unimportant.
hans_gita::34.detailed_meaning: The divine realms engage only with virtuous beings, avoiding the fleeting distractions of human desires. The Hamsa teaches that true knowledge of the temporary nature of all objects leads to inner steadiness, like the calm moon and the constant wind.
hans_gita::34.modern_relevance: You notice how chasing every passing craving leaves you restless, but understanding their temporary nature brings calm and balance.
hans_gita::34.insight: It teaches you to see desires as passing phenomena, which keeps your mind steady and unaffected.

hans_gita::35.verse_sanskrit:
अदुष्टं वर्तमाने तु हृदयान्तरपूरुषे ।
तेनैव देवाः प्रीयन्ते सतां मार्गस्थितेन वै ॥
hans_gita::35.verse_hindi: हृदयगुफा में रहने वाला अन्तर्यामी आत्मा जब दोषभाव से रहित हो जाता है, उस अवस्था में उसका साक्षात्कार करनेवाला पुरुष सन्मार्गगामी समझा जाता है। उसकी इस स्थिति से ही देवता प्रसन्न होते हैं
hans_gita::35.english_translation: When the inner self dwelling in the heart is free from faults, the divine beings delight in the one who walks the path of truth.
hans_gita::35.translation_literal: अदुष्टं (faultless) / वर्तमाने (existing) / तु (but) / हृदयान्तरपूरुषे (in the heart's inner self) / तेनैव (by that same) / देवाः (divine beings) / प्रीयन्ते (are pleased) / सतां (of the virtuous) / मार्गस्थितेन (standing on the path) / वै (indeed)
hans_gita::35.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::35.essence: Inner faultlessness draws the divine's pleasure toward those on the true path.
hans_gita::35.simple_meaning: When your inner self is free from faults, divine beings are pleased with your steady commitment to the true path.
hans_gita::35.simple_insight: You feel the quiet joy of being accepted when you live without fault inside.
hans_gita::35.detailed_meaning: The Hamsa explains that when the inner self, residing deep in the heart, becomes free of faults and impurities, it is recognized as walking the true path. This state pleases divine beings, signaling spiritual progress and alignment with the highest truth.
hans_gita::35.modern_relevance: You notice how people naturally trust and appreciate you when your heart is sincere and free of blame.
hans_gita::35.insight: It teaches you to cultivate inner purity, as this steadies your path and attracts positive support beyond yourself.

hans_gita::36.verse_sanskrit:
शिश्नोदरे येऽभिरताः सदैव  स्तेना नरा वाक्परुषाश्च नित्यम् ।
अपेतदोषानिति तान् विदित्वा दूराद्देवाः सम्परिवर्जयन्ति ॥
hans_gita::36.verse_hindi: किंतु जो सदा पेट पालने और उपस्थ इन्द्रियों के भोग भोगने में ही लगे रहते हैं तथा जो चोरी करने एवं सदा कठोर वचन बोलनेवाले हैं, वे यदि प्रायश्चित्त आदि के द्वारा उक्त कर्मो के दोष से छूट जायँ तो भी देवतालोग उन्हें पहचान कर दूर से ही त्याग देते हैं
hans_gita::36.english_translation: Those who are always attached to bodily pleasures, stealing, and harsh speech, even if freed by penance, are rejected by the divine from afar.
hans_gita::36.translation_literal: शिश्नोदरे (in the body and stomach) / येऽभिरताः (who are attached) / सदैव (always) / स्तेना (thieves) / नरा (men/people) / वाक्परुषाश्च (and harsh speech) / नित्यम् (constantly) / अपेतदोषानि (having escaped faults) / इति (thus) / तान् (them) / विदित्वा (knowing) / दूरात् (from afar) / देवाः (divine beings) / सम्परिवर्जयन्ति (avoid/reject).
hans_gita::36.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::36.essence: Harmful habits keep you distant from the divine, despite outward attempts to atone.
hans_gita::36.simple_meaning: People who are always attached to bodily pleasures, stealing, and harsh speech remain rejected by the divine, even if they try to atone.
hans_gita::36.simple_insight: Changing habits is not enough if harm still defines you; true acceptance requires deeper transformation.
hans_gita::36.detailed_meaning: Hamsa explains that some people are deeply attached to selfish pleasures and harmful actions like stealing and harsh words. Even if they perform penance to cleanse these faults, the divine beings recognize their true nature and avoid them from a distance, showing that surface changes can't hide deep harm.
hans_gita::36.modern_relevance: You might apologize repeatedly after hurting others, but without true change, people still keep their distance from you.
hans_gita::36.insight: It teaches you that superficial fixes don’t rebuild trust; genuine transformation comes from changing harmful tendencies.

hans_gita::37.verse_sanskrit:
न वै देवा हीनसत्त्वेन तोष्याः सर्वाशिना दुष्कृतकर्मणा वा ।
सत्यव्रता ये तु नराः कृतज्ञा धर्मे रतास्तैः सह सम्भजन्ते ॥
hans_gita::37.verse_hindi: सत्त्वगुण से रहित और सब कुछ भक्षण करनेवाले पापाचारी मनुष्य देवताओं को संतुष्ट नहीं कर सकते। जो मनुष्य नियमपूर्वक सत्य बोलने वाले, कृतज्ञ और धर्मपरायण हैं, उन्हीं के साथ देवता स्नेह-सम्बन्ध स्थापित करते हैं
hans_gita::37.english_translation: Beings devoid of goodness and indulging in all harmful deeds cannot please the radiant beings. Only those who are truthful, grateful, and devoted to dharma form affectionate bonds with the radiant beings.
hans_gita::37.translation_literal: न (not) वै (indeed) देवा (radiant beings) हीनसत्त्वेन (devoid of goodness) तोष्याः (pleased) सर्वाशिना (all-consuming) दुष्कृतकर्मणा (of harmful deeds) वा (or)। सत्यव्रता (truthful) ये (who) तु (indeed) नराः (humans) कृतज्ञा (grateful) धर्मे (in dharma) रतास्तैः (devoted to them) सह (with) सम्भजन्ते (form bonds) ॥
hans_gita::37.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::37.essence: True affection from the radiant beings comes only through honesty, gratitude, and dharma.
hans_gita::37.simple_meaning: Only people who act with goodness, speak truth, feel grateful, and follow dharma form loving bonds with the divine.
hans_gita::37.simple_insight: You feel warmth and belonging when you live honestly and gratefully.
hans_gita::37.detailed_meaning: The divine Swan teaches that radiant beings are not pleased by harmful, selfish actions. Instead, they connect lovingly with those who are truthful, grateful, and devoted to righteous living, showing that integrity and dharma build true spiritual relationships.
hans_gita::37.modern_relevance: You notice who truly supports you: those honest and grateful, not those who harm or take without care.
hans_gita::37.insight: It teaches you to cultivate truthfulness, gratitude, and righteous conduct as the foundation for deeper bonds beyond appearances.

hans_gita::38.verse_sanskrit:
अव्याहृतं व्याकृताच्छ्रेय आहुः सत्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तद्द्वितीयम् ।
धर्मं वदेद्व्याहृतं तत्तृतीयं प्रियंवदेद्व्याहृतं तच्चतुर्थम् ॥
hans_gita::38.verse_hindi: व्यर्थ बोलने की अपेक्षा मौन रहना अच्छा बताया गया है, (यह वाणी की प्रथम विशेषता है) सत्य बोलना वाणी की दूसरी विशेषता है, प्रिय बोलना वाणी की तीसरी विशेषता है। धर्मसम्मत बोलना यह वाणी की चौथी विशेषता है (इनमें उत्तरोत्तर श्रेष्ठता है)
hans_gita::38.english_translation: Remaining silent is better than speaking meaningless words, speaking truth is second, speaking kindly is third, and speaking in accordance with dharma is fourth.
hans_gita::38.translation_literal: अव्याहृतं (not-spoken) व्याकृताच् (than spoken) श्रेष्ठ (better) आहुः (they say) सत्यं (truth) वदेत् (speak) व्याहृतं (spoken) तत् (that) द्वितीयम् (second) । धर्मं (dharma) वदेत् (speak) व्याहृतं (spoken) तत् (that) तृतीयम् (third) प्रियं (pleasant) वदेत् (speak) व्याहृतं (spoken) तत् (that) चतुर्थम् (fourth) ॥
hans_gita::38.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::38.essence: Choosing silence or speech guided by truth, kindness, and dharma leads to wise communication.
hans_gita::38.simple_meaning: It's best to remain silent rather than speak meaningless words. Speaking truth is better, then speaking kindly, and finally speaking in a way that follows dharma is best.
hans_gita::38.simple_insight: You feel the relief and strength of choosing words wisely or staying silent.
hans_gita::38.detailed_meaning: Hamsa teaches that speech has qualities ranked by value: silence is best when words are pointless; truth must guide speech; kindness makes it acceptable; and finally, speech must align with dharma to be most virtuous.
hans_gita::38.modern_relevance: You find yourself tempted to reply with harsh words but pause, realizing silence or kind truth serves better.
hans_gita::38.insight: It shifts your communication from impulsive speech to mindful, value-based expression or silence.

hans_gita::39.verse_sanskrit:
केनायमावृतो लोकः केन वा न प्रकाशते ।
केन त्यजति मित्राणि केन स्वर्गं न गच्छति ॥
hans_gita::39.verse_hindi: हंस! इस जगत् को किसने आवृत कर रखा है? किस कारण से उसका स्वरूप प्रकाशित नहीं होता है? मनुष्य किस हेतु से मित्रों का त्याग करता है? और किस दोष से वह स्वर्ग में नहीं जाने पाता ?
hans_gita::39.english_translation: Hamsa! Who has veiled this world? By what cause is its nature not revealed? Why does a person abandon friends? What fault stops them from reaching the higher realm?
hans_gita::39.translation_literal: केन (by whom) / अयम (this) / आवृतः (covered) / लोकः (world) / केन (by whom) / वा (or) / न (not) / प्रकाशते (is revealed) / केन (by whom) / त्यजति (abandons) / मित्राणि (friends) / केन (by whom) / स्वर्गं (higher realm) / न (not) / गच्छति (goes)
hans_gita::39.speaker: Yudhishthira
hans_gita::39.essence: Questioning who or what conceals reality and breaks bonds reveals the roots of confusion.
hans_gita::39.simple_meaning: This asks who causes the world to seem hidden and why people abandon friends and miss the higher realm.
hans_gita::39.simple_insight: You feel the pull to understand what blocks connection and clarity in life.
hans_gita::39.detailed_meaning: Yudhishthira questions the cause behind the world's hidden nature, the abandonment of friends, and the failure to reach the higher realm, seeking insight from Hamsa about these fundamental obstacles.
hans_gita::39.modern_relevance: You pause, wondering why some truths stay hidden and why close bonds sometimes break without clear reason.
hans_gita::39.insight: It invites you to investigate what veils reality and causes disconnection, opening space for deeper clarity.

hans_gita::40.verse_sanskrit:
अज्ञानेनावृतो लोको मात्सर्यान्न प्रकाशते ।
लोभात्त्यजति मित्राणि सङ्गात्स्वर्गं न गच्छति ॥
hans_gita::40.verse_hindi: देवताओं! अज्ञान ने इस लोक को आवृत कर रखा है। आपस में डाह होने के कारण इसका स्वरूप प्रकाशित नहीं होता। मनुष्य लोभ से मित्रों का त्याग करता है। और आसक्तिदोष के कारण वह स्वर्ग में नहीं जाने पाता
hans_gita::40.english_translation: Ignorance covers the world; envy hides its true light. Greed makes one abandon friends, and attachment stops one from reaching the higher realm.
hans_gita::40.translation_literal: अज्ञानेनावृतो (covered by ignorance) / लोको (the world) / मात्सर्यान्न (due to envy not) / प्रकाशते (shines). / लोभात्त्यजति (from greed abandons) / मित्राणि (friends) / सङ्गात्स्वर्गं (due to attachment, the higher realm) / न (not) / गच्छति (goes).
hans_gita::40.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::40.essence: Envy, greed, and attachment blind you and block your true progress.
hans_gita::40.simple_meaning: Ignorance, envy, and greed hide the world's true nature. Attachment causes separation and blocks progress to higher states.
hans_gita::40.simple_insight: You feel trapped when envy and greed cloud your view and relationships.
hans_gita::40.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, the divine Swan explains how ignorance veils the world and envy dims its true brightness. Greed causes people to abandon friends, and attachment stops the soul from reaching the higher spiritual realm.
hans_gita::40.modern_relevance: When jealousy spreads in your circle, and you hold on tightly to possessions or people, you lose connection and clarity.
hans_gita::40.insight: Recognize how envy and greed fracture your relationships and cloud your perception, preventing inner freedom.

hans_gita::41.verse_sanskrit:
कः स्विदेको रमते ब्राह्मणानां कः स्विदेको बहुभिर्जोषमास्ते ।
कः स्विदेको बलवान् दुर्बलोऽपि कः स्विदेषां कलहं नान्ववैति ॥
hans_gita::41.verse_hindi: हंस! ब्राह्मणों में कौन एकमात्र सुख को अनुभव करता है? वह कौन ऐसा एक मनुष्य है, जो बहुतों के साथ रहकर भी चुप रहता है? वह कौन एक मनुष्य है, जो दुर्बल होने पर भी बलवान् है तथा इनमें कौन ऐसा है, जो किसी के साथ कलह नहीं करता?
hans_gita::41.english_translation: Among Brahmins, who alone experiences true joy? Who stays silent among many? Who is strong though weak? Who avoids conflict with others?
hans_gita::41.translation_literal: कः (who) स्विदेकः (alone) रमते (enjoys) ब्राह्मणानां (of Brahmins) कः (who) स्विदेकः (alone) बहुभिः (with many) जोषम् (silence) आसते (has) । कः (who) स्विदेकः (alone) बलवान् (strong) दुर्बलः (weak) अपि (even) कः (who) स्विदेषां (of these) कलहं (quarrel) न (not) अन्ववैति (joins) ॥
hans_gita::41.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::41.essence: True strength is silent peace amid many voices and no conflict.
hans_gita::41.simple_meaning: True happiness among people comes from being quietly present, strong inwardly even if weak outwardly, and avoiding fights.
hans_gita::41.simple_insight: There's power in calmness and peace, even when surrounded by noise and conflict.
hans_gita::41.detailed_meaning: The Swan teaches that among learned people, the one who alone finds joy is the one who remains silent among many, shows inner strength despite weakness, and avoids quarrels, highlighting the marks of equanimity and wisdom.
hans_gita::41.modern_relevance: In a noisy meeting where everyone argues, you find calm strength by listening quietly and not joining conflicts.
hans_gita::41.insight: This verse shifts focus from external power to inner calm and conflict avoidance as true strength.

hans_gita::42.verse_sanskrit:
प्राज्ञ एको रमते ब्राह्मणानां प्राज्ञश्चैको बहुभिर्जोषमास्ते ।
प्राज्ञ एको बलवान् दुर्बलोऽपि प्राज्ञ एषां कलहं नान्ववैति ॥
hans_gita::42.verse_hindi: देवताओं! ब्राह्मणों में जो ज्ञानी है, एकमात्र वही परम सुख को अनुभव करता है। ज्ञानी ही बहुतों के साथ रहकर भी मौन रहता है। एकमात्र ज्ञानी दुर्बल होने पर भी बलवान् है और इनमें ज्ञानी ही किसी के साथ कलह नहीं करता है।
hans_gita::42.english_translation: Among the wise Brahmins, only the true sage experiences supreme joy. The wise remain silent even among many, are strong though weak, and do not quarrel with anyone.
hans_gita::42.translation_literal: प्राज्ञ (wise) एको (one) रमते (delights) ब्राह्मणानां (among Brahmins) प्राज्ञः (wise one) च (also) एको (one) बहुभिः (with many) जोषः (silence) आस्ते (exists) । प्राज्ञः (wise one) एको (one) बलवान् (strong) दुर्बलः (weak) अपि (even) प्राज्ञः (wise one) एषाम् (of them) कलहम् (quarrel) न (not) अन्ववैति (engages) ॥
hans_gita::42.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::42.essence: Quiet wisdom holds strength and peace, even amid many and in weakness.
hans_gita::42.simple_meaning: A truly wise person enjoys deep joy, stays silent among crowds, is strong despite weakness, and avoids quarrels.
hans_gita::42.simple_insight: You can be quietly powerful and peaceful, even when surrounded by conflict.
hans_gita::42.detailed_meaning: Hamsa teaches that among Brahmins, the one who is truly wise experiences a unique joy. This wise person remains calm and silent even in groups, carries inner strength despite apparent weakness, and avoids conflict with others completely.
hans_gita::42.modern_relevance: You sit in a noisy meeting, but inside you hold calm strength and choose peace over argument.
hans_gita::42.insight: It teaches you to find power in silence and peace, not in loudness or force.

hans_gita::43.verse_sanskrit:
किं ब्राह्मणानां देवत्वं किं च साधुत्वमुच्यते ।
असाधुत्वं च किं तेषां किमेषां मानुषं मतम् ॥
hans_gita::43.verse_hindi: हंस ब्राह्मणों का देवत्व क्या है? उनमें साधुता क्या बतायी जाती है? उनके भीतर असाधुता और मनुष्यता क्या मानी गयी है?
hans_gita::43.english_translation: What is the divine nature of brahmins? What is said about their goodness? What is understood as their lack of goodness and their humanity?
hans_gita::43.translation_literal: किं (what) ब्राह्मणानां (of brahmins) देवत्वं (divine nature) किं (what) च (and) साधुत्वं (goodness) उच्यते (is said) । असाधुत्वं (lack of goodness) च (and) किं (what) तेषां (of them) किमेषां (what) मानुषं (humanity) मतम् (is understood) ॥
hans_gita::43.speaker: Hamsa
hans_gita::43.essence: True goodness and failure in others are questions, not fixed answers.
hans_gita::43.simple_meaning: It asks what true divine qualities and goodness mean for brahmins, and what counts as their failures and human traits.
hans_gita::43.simple_insight: You realize that appearances of goodness or failure may hide deeper truths about others.
hans_gita::43.detailed_meaning: Hamsa questions the surface qualities attributed to brahmins—divine status, goodness, or failures—and challenges the common ideas about what makes them truly good or flawed.
