ram_gita::6.english_translation: Hearing all of Lakshmana's words, the compassionate lord, the jewel of kings, pleased to teach, began to dispel the darkness of ignorance in the eager listener.
ram_gita::6.translation_literal: श्रुत्वाथ (hearing) सौमित्रवचः (Saumitra's words, Lakshmana's words) अखिलं (all) तदा (then) प्राह (spoke) प्रपन्नार्तिहरः (remover of distress to surrenderers) प्रसन्नधीः (with pleased mind) विज्ञानम् (knowledge) अज्ञानतमःप्रशान्तये (to dispel the darkness of ignorance) श्रुतिप्रपन्नं (who surrendered to the revealed teachings) क्षितिपालभूषणः (jewel of kings, protector of the land)
ram_gita::6.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::6.essence: The teacher welcomes sincere seekers to dispel their darkness of ignorance.
ram_gita::6.simple_meaning: Lakshmana spoke his doubts, and Rama, pleased to teach, began to share knowledge to remove his ignorance.
ram_gita::6.simple_insight: When you sincerely seek, the right guidance comes with clarity and kindness.
ram_gita::6.detailed_meaning: Lakshmana, eager for knowledge, expresses his confusion. Rama, the compassionate lord and protector, responds with joy to teach and dispel his ignorance, setting the stage for the teachings ahead.
ram_gita::6.insight: It shows the importance of openness to learning and a teacher’s readiness to share wisdom with care.

ram_gita::7.verse_sanskrit:
आदौ स्ववर्णाश्रमवर्णिताः क्रियाः कृत्वा समासादितशुद्धमानसः ।
समाप्य तत्पूर्वमुपात्तसाधनः समाश्रयेत्सद्गुरुमात्मलब्धये ॥
ram_gita::7.verse_hindi: सबसे पहले अपने-अपने वर्ण और आश्रम के लिये (शास्त्रों में) बतलायी हुई क्रियाओं का यथावत् पालनकर चित्त शुद्ध हो जाने पर उन कर्मो को छोड़ दे और शम दमादि साधनों से सम्पन्न हो आत्मज्ञान की प्राप्ति के लिये सद्गुरु की शरण में जाय
ram_gita::7.english_translation: First, perform the prescribed duties of your own class and stage; when your mind is purified, give up those actions and, accomplished in self-restraint, seek the true teacher for self-realization.
ram_gita::7.translation_literal: आदौ (first) स्ववर्णाश्रमवर्णिताः (own class and stage prescribed) क्रियाः (actions) कृत्वा (having done) समासादित (attained) शुद्धमानसः (pure mind) । समाप्य (having completed) तत्पूर्वम् (previous) उपात्तसाधनः (acquired means) समाश्रयेत् (should seek refuge) सद्गुरुम् (true teacher) आत्मलब्धये (for self-realization) ॥
ram_gita::7.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::7.essence: Purify the mind through duty, then renounce action and seek true guidance.
ram_gita::7.simple_meaning: Begin by faithfully doing the duties assigned to your social role until your mind becomes pure, then give up those actions and seek a true teacher for self-knowledge.
ram_gita::7.simple_insight: There’s clarity and readiness in following your path before turning inward for deeper wisdom.
ram_gita::7.detailed_meaning: Rama advises Lakshmana to first perform the prescribed duties according to one’s social class and stage of life. When these actions purify the mind and self-control is achieved, one should renounce those duties and approach a true teacher to attain self-realization.
ram_gita::7.modern_relevance: You focus fully on your current responsibilities until you feel mentally clear, then you seek guidance to grow beyond them.
ram_gita::7.insight: It teaches you to honor your present obligations fully while preparing the mind for deeper spiritual learning.

ram_gita::8.verse_sanskrit:
क्रिया श्रीरोद्भवहेतुरादृता प्रियाप्रियौ तौ भवतः सुरागिणः ।
धर्मेतरौ तत्र पुनः शरीरकम् पुनः क्रिया चक्रवदीर्यते भवः ॥
ram_gita::8.verse_hindi: कर्म देहान्तर की प्राप्ति के लिये ही स्वीकार किये गये हैं, क्योंकि उनमें प्रेम रखने वाले पुरुषों से इष्ट-अनिष्ट दोनों ही प्रकार की क्रियाएँ होती हैं। उनसे धर्म और अधर्म दोनों ही की प्राप्ति होती है और उनके कारण शरीर प्राप्त होता है जिससे फिर कर्म होते हैं। इसी प्रकार यह संसार चक्र के समान चलता रहता है
ram_gita::8.english_translation: Actions are accepted only to obtain another body, because those who care experience both wanted and unwanted actions. From these arise right and wrong, leading again to bodies and actions, thus the cycle of existence continues.
ram_gita::8.translation_literal: क्रिया (action) / श्रीरः (body) / उत्पत्तेः (cause) / हेतुः (cause) / अदृता (not without) / प्रिया (liked) / अप्रियौ (disliked) / तौ (those two) / भवतः (are) / सुरागिणः (those who love) / धर्मेतरौ (other than dharma) / तत्र (there) / पुनः (again) / शरीरकम् (of body) / पुनः (again) / क्रिया (action) / चक्रवती (wheel-like) / एर्यते (turns) / भवः (world/existence)
ram_gita::8.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::8.essence: Desire and aversion drive actions, which bind beings to repeated existence cycles.
ram_gita::8.simple_meaning: You perform actions because you want another life; desires and dislikes cause both good and bad actions, which bring new bodies and more actions, creating a continuous cycle.
ram_gita::8.simple_insight: There's a pull in wanting and avoiding that keeps you trapped in endless action and rebirth.
ram_gita::8.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that all actions arise because beings desire another physical existence. Those attached to what they like or dislike create good and bad deeds, which lead to new bodies and further actions, perpetuating the cycle of life.
ram_gita::8.modern_relevance: You keep chasing what feels good and avoiding what feels bad, unaware this cycle keeps pulling you back again and again.
ram_gita::8.insight: It teaches you to see how desire and aversion cause actions that keep you bound to repeated experiences.

ram_gita::9.verse_sanskrit:
अज्ञानमेवास्य हि मूलकारणं तद्धानमेवात्र विधौ विधीयते ।
विद्यैव तन्नाशविधौ पटीयसी न कर्म तज्जं सविरोधमीरितम् ॥
ram_gita::9.verse_hindi: संसार का मूल कारण अज्ञान ही है। और इन (शास्त्रीय) विधिवाक्यों में उस (अज्ञान) का नाश ही (संसार से मुक्त होने का) उपाय बतलाया गया है। अज्ञान का नाश करने में ज्ञान ही समर्थ है, कर्म नहीं, क्योंकि उस (अज्ञान) से उत्पन्न होने वाला कर्म उसका विरोधी नहीं हो सकता
ram_gita::9.english_translation: The root cause of the cycle of reactivity is deep confusion. The scriptural teachings prescribe its removal. Only clear understanding can remove deep confusion; action born from confusion cannot oppose it.
ram_gita::9.translation_literal: अज्ञानम् (ignorance) एव (indeed) अस्य (of this) हि (certainly) मूलकारणम् (root cause) तद्धानम् (that knowledge) एव (alone) अत्र (here) विधौ (in the scripture) विधीयते (is prescribed) । विद्यैव (only knowledge) तन्नाशः (its destruction) विधौ (in scripture) पटीयसी (is possible) न (not) कर्म (action) तज्जम् (that-born) सविरोधम् (against it) ईरितम् (is possible) ॥
ram_gita::9.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::9.essence: Only clear understanding can remove deep confusion that causes the endless cycle of reactivity.
ram_gita::9.simple_meaning: The root cause of repeated suffering is deep confusion. Only true knowledge can remove this confusion, not actions born from that confusion.
ram_gita::9.simple_insight: There's hope in knowing that understanding, not endless effort, frees you from confusion.
ram_gita::9.detailed_meaning: Rama teaches Lakshmana that the endless cycle of reactivity stems from deep confusion (avidya). The scriptures instruct removing this confusion by gaining clear understanding (vidya), because actions born from confusion cannot remove it.
ram_gita::9.modern_relevance: You might try solving problems by more doing, but sometimes only seeing clearly can truly end your struggle.
ram_gita::9.insight: Shift focus from trying harder to seeking clear understanding; true change comes from knowledge, not more action.

ram_gita::10.verse_sanskrit:
नाज्ञानहानिर्न च रागसंक्षयो भवेत्ततः कर्म सदोषमुद्भवेत् ।
ततः पुनः संसृतिरप्यवारिता तस्माद्बुधो ज्ञानविचारवान्भवेत् ॥
ram_gita::10.verse_hindi: कर्मद्वारा अज्ञान का नाश अथवा राग का क्षय नहीं हो सकता बल्कि उससे दूसरे सदोष कर्म की उत्पत्ति होती है। उससे पुनः संसार की प्राप्ति होना अनिवार्य है। इसलिये बुद्धिमान् को ज्ञानविचार में ही तत्पर होना चाहिये
ram_gita::10.english_translation: Ignorance is not destroyed, nor attachment diminished, by action; instead, action causes further flawed karma. Thus, rebirth in the cycle continues. Therefore, the wise should focus on knowledge and reflection.
ram_gita::10.translation_literal: नाज्ञानहानिः (ignorance destruction) न (not) च (and) रागसंक्षयः (attachment diminution) भवेत्ततः (happens from that) कर्म (action) सदोषम् (flawed) उद्भवेत् (arises) । ततः (thereafter) पुनः (again) संसृतिः (rebirth) अपि (also) अवारितः (unavoidable) तस्मात् (therefore) बुधः (wise) ज्ञानविचारवान् (of knowledge and reflection) भवेत् (should be).
ram_gita::10.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::10.essence: Action alone cannot end confusion; only knowledge and reflection can free you.
ram_gita::10.simple_meaning: You cannot remove deep confusion or attachment through action alone; it only leads to more flawed actions and continued rebirth. Wisdom and reflection are needed.
ram_gita::10.simple_insight: There's relief in knowing that effort without insight only prolongs struggle.
ram_gita::10.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that simply acting cannot remove ignorance or attachment, because actions themselves produce further flawed consequences, binding one again to the cycle of rebirth. Only focused knowledge and thoughtful reflection can break this cycle.
ram_gita::10.modern_relevance: You keep trying to fix problems by doing more tasks, but without understanding, you only create more stress and complications.
ram_gita::10.insight: It teaches you to shift from reactive doing to thoughtful understanding to break repeated patterns.

ram_gita::11.verse_sanskrit:
ननु क्रिया वेदमुखेन चोदिता तथैव विद्या पुरुषार्थसाधनम् ।
कर्तव्यता प्राणभृतः प्रचोदिता विद्यासहायत्वमुपैति सा पुनः ॥
ram_gita::11.verse_hindi: कुछ वितर्क वादी ऐसा कहते हैं कि-जिस प्रकार वेद के कथनानुसार ज्ञान पुरुषार्थ का साधक है वैसे ही कर्म वेदविहित हैं;  और प्राणियों के लिये कर्मो की अवश्य कर्तव्यता का विधान भी है इसलिये वे कर्म ज्ञान के सहकारी हो जाते हैं।
ram_gita::11.english_translation: Some argue that just as the Vedas declare knowledge as the means to achieve the goal, so too are actions prescribed by the Vedas; therefore, actions become cooperative with knowledge because living beings must perform their duties.
ram_gita::11.translation_literal: ननु (indeed) क्रिया (action) वेदमुखेन (by Vedas) चोदिता (prescribed) तथैव (just so) विद्या (knowledge) पुरुषार्थसाधनम् (means to achieve the goal). कर्तव्यता (duty) प्राणभृतः (for living beings) प्रचोदिता (enjoined). विद्यासहायत्वम् (cooperation with knowledge) उपैति (attains) सा (that) पुनः (again).
ram_gita::11.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::11.essence: Duty-bound actions support and cooperate with the pursuit of true knowledge.
ram_gita::11.simple_meaning: Actions are prescribed by sacred teachings and must be done as duty; these actions support and cooperate with gaining true knowledge.
ram_gita::11.simple_insight: You see your duties not as separate but as helping your deeper understanding.
ram_gita::11.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that some thinkers say sacred scriptures teach knowledge as the path to the goal, but also prescribe actions. Since living beings must perform duties, these actions work together with knowledge rather than oppose it.
ram_gita::11.modern_relevance: When you follow your responsibilities, you’re not just doing tasks — you’re supporting your growth in understanding and purpose.
ram_gita::11.insight: It shifts your view to see duty and wisdom as partners, not opposites, aligning action with learning.

ram_gita::12.verse_sanskrit:
कर्माकृतौ दोषमपि श्रुतिर्जगौ तस्मात्सदा कार्यमिदं मुमुक्षुणा ।
ननु स्वतन्त्रा ध्रुवकार्यकारिणी विद्य न किञ्चिन्मनसाप्यपेक्षते ॥
ram_gita::12.verse_hindi: साथ ही श्रुति ने कर्म न करने में दोष भी बतलाया है; इसलिये मुमुक्षु को कर्म सदा ही करते रहना चाहिये, और यदि कोई कहे कि ज्ञान स्वतन्त्र है। एवं निश्चय ही अपना फल देने वाला है उसे मन से भी किसी और की सहायता की आवश्यकता नहीं है
ram_gita::12.english_translation: The scriptures say that even inaction has fault; therefore, a seeker must always perform action. Knowledge is independent and certain to yield results without any mental expectation.
ram_gita::12.translation_literal: कर्माकृतौ (not doing action) दोषम् (fault) अपि (also) श्रुति: (scripture) जगौ (declared) तस्मात् (therefore) सदा (always) कार्यम् (action) इदं (this) मुमुक्षुणा (by the seeker). ननु (indeed) स्वतन्त्राः (independent) ध्रुवकार्यकारिणी (certainly-result-producing) विद्य (knowledge) न (not) किञ्चित् (any) मनसा (by mind) अपि (even) अपेक्षते (needs).
ram_gita::12.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::12.essence: A true seeker must keep acting because even inaction is flawed.
ram_gita::12.simple_meaning: You should always act because even not acting is considered wrong. True knowledge works on its own and needs no mental expectations.
ram_gita::12.simple_insight: You feel the relief that doing nothing isn’t an option when seeking freedom.
ram_gita::12.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that scriptures declare inaction to be faulty. A seeker of freedom must keep acting, trusting knowledge is self-sufficient and does not depend on mental hopes.
ram_gita::12.modern_relevance: You hesitate to act because you fear doing nothing might be safer, but growth comes from steady effort even when results seem unclear.
ram_gita::12.insight: It teaches you to commit to consistent action without relying on mental outcomes or doubts.

ram_gita::13.verse_sanskrit:
न सत्यकार्योऽपि हि यद्वदध्वरः प्रकाङ्क्षतेऽन्यानपि कारकादिकान् ।
तथैव विद्या विधितः प्रकाशितैर्विशिष्यते कर्मभिरेव मुक्तये ॥
ram_gita::13.verse_hindi: तो उसका यह कहना ठीक नहीं, क्योंकि जिस प्रकार (वेदोक्त) यज्ञ सत्य कर्म होने पर भी अन्य कारकादि की अपेक्षा करता ही है, उसी प्रकार विधि से प्रकाशित कर्मों के द्वारा ही ज्ञान मुक्ति का साधक हो सकता है। (अत: कर्मों का त्याग उचित नहीं है)
ram_gita::13.english_translation: It is not correct to say that even true actions do not expect other causes; similarly, one attains knowledge and freedom only through prescribed actions.
ram_gita::13.translation_literal: न (not) / सत्यकार्योऽपि (even true actions) / हि (indeed) / यद्वदध्वरः (expect) / प्रकाङ्क्षतेऽन्यानपि (other causes also) / कारकादिकान् (causes and others) । / तथैव (similarly) / विद्या (knowledge) / विधितः (prescribed) / प्रकाशितैः (illuminated) / विशिष्यते (attains) / कर्मभिरेव (by actions only) / मुक्तये (for freedom) ॥
ram_gita::13.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::13.essence: Freedom and knowledge arise through prescribed action, not by abandoning action.
ram_gita::13.simple_meaning: Even true actions depend on other causes. Likewise, knowledge and freedom arise through properly prescribed actions, so abandoning them is not correct.
ram_gita::13.simple_insight: You can trust that acting rightly is the real way to knowledge and freedom, not quitting action.
ram_gita::13.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that just as true sacrifices depend on many causes, knowledge and inner freedom come only through performing the right, prescribed actions. This moment corrects the mistaken idea that abandoning action leads to freedom.
ram_gita::13.modern_relevance: You might think stepping back from responsibilities leads to peace, but real growth happens by fully engaging with your rightful duties.
ram_gita::13.insight: It teaches you to see disciplined action as the vehicle for wisdom and freedom, not something to reject.

ram_gita::14.verse_sanskrit:
केचिद्वदन्तीति वितर्कवादिनस्तदप्यसदृष्टविरोधकारणात् ।
देहाभिमानादभिवर्धते क्रिया विद्या गताहङ्कृतितः प्रसिध्द्यति ॥
ram_gita::14.verse_hindi: (सिद्धान्ती-) ऐसा जो कोई कुतर्की कहते हैं उनके कथन में प्रत्यक्ष विरोध होने के कारण वह ठीक नहीं है, क्योंकि कर्म देहाभिमान से होता है और ज्ञान अहंकार के नाश होने पर सिद्ध होता है
ram_gita::14.english_translation: Some argue illogically, but their view is flawed because actions arise from identification with the body, while true knowledge arises when the sense of separate self is destroyed.
ram_gita::14.translation_literal: केचित् (some) वदन्ति (say) इति (thus) वितर्कवादिनः (those who argue with reasoning) तद् (that) अपि (also) असदृष्टविरोधकारणात् (because of contradiction with what is seen as false) । देहाभिमानात् (from body-identification) अभिवर्धते (arises) क्रिया (action) । विद्या (knowledge) गताः (gone) अहङ्कृतितः (from destruction of ego-sense) प्रसिध्यति (is established) ॥
ram_gita::14.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::14.essence: Actions arise from body-identification; true knowledge arises when ego dissolves.
ram_gita::14.simple_meaning: Actions happen because you identify with your body, but true understanding comes when the sense of separate self disappears.
ram_gita::14.simple_insight: There's freedom in knowing that your actions stem from body-fixation, not your true self.
ram_gita::14.detailed_meaning: Rama explains that some argue incorrectly because they don't see that actions arise from identifying with the body. True knowledge appears only when the ego, the sense of separate self, is destroyed.
ram_gita::14.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by your roles or appearance, remember your actions come from that identification—not your deeper awareness.
ram_gita::14.insight: Recognize that your action urges arise from body attachment; wisdom requires dissolving ego fixation.

ram_gita::15.verse_sanskrit:
विशुद्धविज्ञानविरोचनाञ्चिता विद्यात्मवृत्तिश्चरमेति भण्यते ।
उदेति कर्माखिलकारकादिभिर्निहन्ति विद्याखिलकारकादिकम् ॥
ram_gita::15.verse_hindi: (वेदान्तवाक्यों का विचार करते-करते) विशुद्ध विज्ञान के प्रकाश से उद्भासित जो चरम आत्मवृत्ति होती है उसी का नाम विद्या (आत्मज्ञान) है। इसके अतिरिक्त कर्म सम्पूर्ण कारकादि की सहायता से होता है, किन्तु विद्या समस्त कारकादि का (अनित्यत्व की भावनाद्वारा) नाश कर देती है
ram_gita::15.english_translation: The highest self-activity revealed by pure knowledge is called wisdom; all actions depend on causes, but wisdom destroys the sense of impermanence in all causes.
ram_gita::15.translation_literal: विशुद्धविज्ञानविरोचनाञ्चिता (illuminated by pure knowledge) / विद्यात्मवृत्तिश्चरमेति (the supreme self-activity is called wisdom) / भण्यते (is said). / उदेति (arises) / कर्माखिलकारकादिभिर्निहन्ति (all actions are caused by causes) / विद्याखिलकारकादिकम् (but wisdom destroys all causes etc.)
ram_gita::15.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::15.essence: Pure wisdom reveals the unchanging self and destroys all illusions of impermanence.
ram_gita::15.simple_meaning: Wisdom is the highest pure self-awareness that shines clearly and ends deep confusion about impermanence, unlike actions which depend on causes.
ram_gita::15.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing true wisdom removes all doubts about what changes.
ram_gita::15.detailed_meaning: Rama explains that pure knowledge reveals the supreme self-activity called wisdom, which transcends the shifting causes behind all actions by destroying the illusion of impermanence and confusion.
ram_gita::15.modern_relevance: When everything around you feels uncertain and you grasp for stability, realizing that pure awareness dissolves all doubts brings deep calm.
ram_gita::15.insight: It teaches you to shift attention from the changing causes to the unchanging self-awareness that reveals true clarity.

ram_gita::16.verse_sanskrit:
तस्मात्त्यजेत्कार्यमशेषतः सुधीर्विद्याविरोधान्न समुच्चयो भवेत् ॥
आत्मानुसन्धानपरायणः सदानिवृत्तसर्वेन्द्रियवृत्तिगोचरः ॥
ram_gita::16.verse_hindi: इसलिये समस्त इन्द्रियों के विषयों से निवृत्त होकर निरन्तर आत्मानुसन्धान में लगा हुआ बुद्धिमान् पुरुष सम्पूर्ण कर्मों का सर्वथा त्याग कर दे। क्योंकि विद्या का विरोधी होने के कारण कर्म का उसके साथ समुच्चय नहीं हो सकता
ram_gita::16.english_translation: Therefore, a wise person, detached from all sense objects and constantly engaged in self-inquiry, should completely renounce all actions because actions cannot coexist with knowledge that opposes them.
ram_gita::16.translation_literal: तस्मात् (therefore) त्यजेत् (should abandon) कार्यम् (actions) अशेषतः (completely) सुधीः (wise persons) विद्या-विरोधात् (due to opposition to knowledge) न (not) समुच्चयः (coexistence) भवेत् (happens) आत्मानुसन्धान-परायणः (engaged in self-inquiry) सदानिवृत्तः (always detached) सर्वेन्द्रिय-वृत्ति-गोचरः (free from all sense objects)
ram_gita::16.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::16.essence: True self-inquiry requires fully letting go of all action and sense distractions.
ram_gita::16.simple_meaning: A truly wise person stops all actions and distractions to focus fully on self-inquiry, because action conflicts with deep knowledge.
ram_gita::16.simple_insight: You feel peace when you release all doing and turn inward to yourself.
ram_gita::16.detailed_meaning: Rama instructs that when someone is deeply engaged in seeking the true self and detached from all sensory distractions, they should completely renounce all actions. This is because true knowledge and active doing cannot exist together in conflict.
ram_gita::16.modern_relevance: You’ve been caught in endless busywork, but real clarity comes when you stop acting and look deeply within.
ram_gita::16.insight: It teaches you to choose inner exploration over external doing, recognizing that one blocks the other.

ram_gita::17.verse_sanskrit:
यावच्छारीरादिषु माययात्मधीस्तावद्विधेयो विधिवादकर्मणाम् ।
नेतीति वाक्यैरखिलं निषिध्य तत्ज्ञात्वा परात्मानमथ त्यजेत्क्रियाः ॥
ram_gita::17.verse_hindi: जबतक माया से मोहित रहने के कारण मनुष्य का शरीरादि में आत्मभाव है तभी तक उसे वैदिक कर्मानुष्ठान कर्तव्य है। ‘नेति नेति’ आदि वाक्यों से सम्पूर्ण अनात्मवस्तुओं का निषेध करके अपने परमात्मस्वरूप को जान लेने पर फिर उसे समस्त कर्मो को छोड़ देना चाहिये।
ram_gita::17.english_translation: As long as the mind is deluded by illusion and identifies with the body, one must perform Vedic rituals. But knowing the supreme self through 'not this, not this,' rejecting all non-self, one should then abandon all actions.
ram_gita::17.translation_literal: यावत् (as long as) शारीरादिषु (in the body and so on) माययात्मधीः (mind deluded by illusion) तावत् (that much) विधेयः (must be done) विधिवाद्-कर्मणाम् (of ritualistic actions) न एति एति (not this, not this) वाक्यैः (by words) अखिलं (all) निषिध्य (rejecting) तत् ज्ञात्वा (knowing that) परात्मानम् (the supreme self) अथ (then) त्यजेत् क्रियाः (should abandon actions).
ram_gita::17.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::17.essence: True self-knowledge ends illusion-based doing and frees you from all ritual actions.
ram_gita::17.simple_meaning: You must perform ritual actions while caught in illusion identifying with the body. But when you truly know your supreme self by rejecting all that is not it, you should give up all actions.
ram_gita::17.simple_insight: Freedom comes when you see past illusion and stop acting from false identity.
ram_gita::17.detailed_meaning: Rama teaches Lakshmana that as long as the mind is trapped in illusion identifying with the body, performing prescribed rituals is necessary. However, once one understands the supreme self by negating all non-self through 'not this, not this,' all ritual actions should be abandoned, indicating liberation from binding duties.
ram_gita::17.modern_relevance: You keep pushing through routines and roles driven by a false sense of who you are. But realizing your true self invites you to rest and release those efforts.
ram_gita::17.insight: This verse shifts the mind from acting out of false identity to resting in true self-awareness, freeing you from compulsive doing.

ram_gita::18.verse_sanskrit:
यदा परात्मात्मविभेदभेदकं विज्ञानमात्मन्यवभाति भास्वरम् ।
तदैव माया प्रविलीयतेऽञ्जसा सकारका कारणमात्मसंसृतेः ॥
ram_gita::18.verse_hindi: जिस समय परमात्मा और जीवात्मा के भेद को दूर करने वाला प्रकाशमय विज्ञान अन्त:करण में स्पष्टतया भासित होने लगता है उसी समय आत्मा के लिये संसार-प्राप्ति की कारण माया अनायास ही कारकादि के सहित लीन हो जाती है
ram_gita::18.english_translation: When the illuminating knowledge that removes the distinction between the supreme being and the individual self clearly shines within the heart, then the cause of the soul’s entanglement in the world, Maya, naturally dissolves along with its causes.
ram_gita::18.translation_literal: यदा (when) परात्मात्मविभेदभेदकं (that which distinguishes the supreme being and the individual self) विज्ञानम् (knowledge) आत्मन्यवभाति (shines within the self) भास्वरम् (brightly) । तदैव (then indeed) माया (illusion) प्रविलीयतेऽञ्जसा (is effortlessly dissolved) सकारका (with causes) कारणम् (cause) आत्मसंसृतेः (of the soul's worldly entanglement) ॥
ram_gita::18.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::18.essence: Clear inner knowledge that reveals oneness dissolves the root cause of illusion effortlessly.
ram_gita::18.simple_meaning: When you clearly see no real difference between the supreme being and yourself, the illusion that causes your entanglement in the world naturally fades away.
ram_gita::18.simple_insight: There is freedom in seeing yourself and the supreme as one, letting all confusion dissolve.
ram_gita::18.detailed_meaning: Rama teaches Lakshmana that when the inner knowledge fully reveals the oneness of the supreme being and the individual self, the binding illusion called Maya and its causes naturally vanish, freeing the self from worldly entanglement.
ram_gita::18.modern_relevance: You’ve struggled feeling separate and stuck; suddenly, a clear understanding dawns that you and the universe are deeply connected, and your worries begin to loosen.
ram_gita::18.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing separation to recognizing unity, dissolving the root cause of confusion.

ram_gita::19.verse_sanskrit:
श्रुतिप्रमाणाभिविनाशिता च सा कथं भविषत्यपि कार्यकारिणी ।
विज्ञानमात्रादमलाद्वितीयतस्तस्मादविद्या न पुनर्भविष्यति ॥
ram_gita::19.verse_hindi: श्रुति-प्रमाण से उसके नष्ट कर दिये जाने पर फिर वह किस प्रकार अपना कार्य करने में समर्थ हो सकती है? इसलिये उस एकमात्र ज्ञानस्वरूप निर्मल और अद्वितीय बोध की प्राप्ति होनेपर फिर अविद्या उत्पन्न नहीं हो सकती
ram_gita::19.english_translation: When the source of knowledge is destroyed, how can ignorance still perform any action? Once you attain pure, unique knowledge, ignorance cannot arise again.
ram_gita::19.translation_literal: श्रुति-प्रमाण (scriptural proof) / अभि-नाशिता (having been destroyed) / च (and) / सा (that) / कथं (how) / भविष्यति (will be) / अपि (even) / कार्यकारिणी (able to perform work) । / विज्ञानमात्रात् (from only knowledge) / अमलात् (pure) / अद्वितीयतस्तस्मात् (unique, therefore) / अविद्या (ignorance) / न (not) / पुनः (again) / भविष्यति (will arise) ॥
ram_gita::19.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::19.essence: True knowledge, once fully attained, permanently ends the power of ignorance.
ram_gita::19.simple_meaning: If the original source of true knowledge is gone, ignorance cannot function. Pure and unique knowledge stops ignorance from arising again.
ram_gita::19.simple_insight: You can feel safe knowing real knowledge breaks the cycle of confusion forever.
ram_gita::19.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that once the foundational truth (scriptural proof) is fully realized and known as pure, ignorance loses its power and cannot return to cause confusion or misaction.
ram_gita::19.modern_relevance: When you fully understand something deeply, old doubts and confusion lose their grip and can't trick you again.
ram_gita::19.insight: It shifts your approach from fighting ignorance repeatedly to cultivating unshakable, pure knowledge that prevents confusion from arising.

ram_gita::20.verse_sanskrit:
यदि स्म नष्टा न पुनः प्रसूयते कर्ताहमस्येति मतिः कथं भवेत् ।
तस्मात्स्वतन्त्रा न किमप्यपेक्षते विद्य विमोक्षाय विभाति केवला ॥
ram_gita::20.verse_hindi: जब एक बार नष्ट हो जाने पर अविद्या का फिर जन्म ही नहीं होता तो बोधवान्को मैं कर्ता हूँ ऐसी बुद्धि कैसे हो सकती है? इसलिये ज्ञान स्वतन्त्र है, उसे जीव के मोक्ष के लिये किसी और (कर्मादि) की अपेक्षा नहीं है, वह स्वयं अकेला ही उसके लिये समर्थ है
ram_gita::20.english_translation: If ignorance, once destroyed, never arises again, how can there be the idea that I am the doer? Therefore, knowledge is independent; it requires nothing else for liberation and alone is capable of it.
ram_gita::20.translation_literal: यदि (if) स्म (indeed) नष्टा (destroyed) न (not) पुनः (again) प्रसूयते (is born) कर्ता (doer) अहम् (I) अस्येति (this) मतिः (thought) कथं (how) भवेत् (can be) । तस्मात् (therefore) स्वतन्त्रः (independent) न (not) किमपि (anything) अपेक्षते (expects) विद्या (knowledge) विमोक्षाय (for liberation) विभाति (shines) केवला (alone) ॥
ram_gita::20.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::20.essence: True knowledge alone is self-sufficient and fully frees without needing anything else.
ram_gita::20.simple_meaning: When ignorance is completely gone and never returns, the idea of ‘I am the doer’ cannot arise. True knowledge is self-sufficient and alone liberates.
ram_gita::20.simple_insight: You can feel complete freedom because true understanding depends on nothing but itself.
ram_gita::20.detailed_meaning: In this teaching, Rama explains to Lakshmana that once ignorance is destroyed, it does not return, so the sense of being a separate doer disappears. Knowledge is independent and alone able to bring liberation, needing no other cause or condition.
ram_gita::20.modern_relevance: When you deeply understand something, you realize you don’t need to cling to external validation or control to feel whole and free.
ram_gita::20.insight: It teaches you to trust that true understanding alone is enough for inner freedom without relying on external actions or results.

ram_gita::21.verse_sanskrit:
सा तैत्तिरीयश्रुतिराह सादरं न्यासं प्रशस्ताखिलकर्मणां स्फुटम् ।
एतावदित्याह च वाजिनां श्रुतिर्ज्ञानं विमोक्षाय न कर्म साधनम् ॥
ram_gita::21.verse_hindi: इसके सिवा तैत्तिरीय शाखा की प्रसिद्ध श्रुति भी स्पष्ट कहती है कि समस्त कर्मों का त्याग करना ही अच्छा है, तथा ‘एतावत्’ इत्यादि वाजसनेयी शाखा की श्रुति भी कहती है कि मोक्ष का साधन ज्ञान ही है कर्म नहीं
ram_gita::21.english_translation: Besides this, the famous Taittiriya tradition respectfully teaches that giving up all actions is best, and the Vajasaneyi tradition clearly states that knowledge, not action, is the means to freedom.
ram_gita::21.translation_literal: सा (that) तैत्तिरीयश्रुतिः (Taittiriya tradition) आह (says) सादरं (respectfully) न्यासं (renunciation) प्रशस्ताखिलकर्मणां (best of all actions) स्फुटम् (clearly) । एतावदिति (this much) आह (says) च (also) वाजिनां (of the Vajasaneyi) श्रुतिर्ः (tradition) ज्ञानं (knowledge) विमोक्षाय (for liberation) न (not) कर्म (action) साधनम् (means) ॥
ram_gita::21.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::21.essence: Freedom is gained through knowledge, not through performing all actions.
ram_gita::21.simple_meaning: The best teaching is to give up all actions because true freedom comes from knowledge, not from doing.
ram_gita::21.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing freedom is found in understanding, not in constant doing.
ram_gita::21.detailed_meaning: Rama cites two ancient Vedic traditions: the Taittiriya branch teaches respectful renunciation of all actions, while the Vajasaneyi branch emphasizes that knowledge alone leads to liberation, not action. This highlights knowledge’s supreme role.
ram_gita::21.modern_relevance: When overwhelmed by endless tasks, remember that clarity and understanding can bring freedom beyond doing more.
ram_gita::21.insight: It shifts focus from striving through actions to seeking clear understanding as the true path to freedom.

ram_gita::22.verse_sanskrit:
विद्यासमत्वेन तु दर्शितस्त्वया क्रतुर्न दृष्टान्त उदाहृतः समः ।
फलैः पृथक्त्वाद्बहुकारकैः क्रतुः संसाध्यते ज्ञानमतो विपर्ययम् ॥
ram_gita::22.verse_hindi: और तुमने जो ज्ञान की समानता में यज्ञादि का दृष्टान्त दिया सो ठीक नहीं है, क्योंकि उन दोनों के फल अलग-अलग हैं। इसके अतिरिक्त यज्ञ तो (होता, ऋत्विक, यजमान आदि) बहुत-से कारकों से सिद्ध होता है और ज्ञान इससे विपरीत है (अर्थात् वह कारकादि से साध्य नहीं है)
ram_gita::22.english_translation: Your example of sacrifice to show equality in knowledge is incorrect because their results differ; sacrifice requires many factors, but knowledge cannot be achieved through such means.
ram_gita::22.translation_literal: विद्या (knowledge) समत्वेन (with equality) तु (but) दर्शितः (shown) त्वया (by you) क्रतुर्न (sacrifice not) दृष्टान्त (example) उदाहृतः (given) समः (equal) फलैः (by results) पृथक्त्वात् (difference) बहुकारकैः (by many factors) क्रतुः (of sacrifice) संसाध्यते (is accomplished) ज्ञानमतो (from knowledge) विपर्ययम् (contrary)
ram_gita::22.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::22.essence: Knowledge and sacrifice differ fundamentally; knowledge isn't attained through external factors.
ram_gita::22.simple_meaning: You cannot compare knowledge to sacrifice because their purposes and outcomes are different; knowledge is not achieved by external rituals or many factors like sacrifice is.
ram_gita::22.simple_insight: There's freedom in seeing knowledge as independent of rituals and external factors.
ram_gita::22.detailed_meaning: Rama points out to Lakshmana that using the example of sacrifice to explain the equality of knowledge is mistaken because sacrifice depends on many conditions and yields varied results, whereas knowledge is not bound by such factors and cannot be attained through them.
ram_gita::22.modern_relevance: You might notice how some achievements require many steps and helpers, but true understanding comes from within and can't be forced by external means.
ram_gita::22.insight: It shifts your mind from expecting knowledge as an outcome of external effort to realizing it as an inner, self-contained truth.

ram_gita::23.verse_sanskrit:
सप्रत्यवायो ह्यहमित्यनात्मधीरज्ञप्रसिद्धा न तु तत्त्वदर्शिनः ।
तस्माद्बुधैस्त्याज्यमविक्रियात्मभिर्विधानतः कर्म विधिप्रकाशितम् ॥
ram_gita::23.verse_hindi: (कर्म के त्याग करने से) मैं अवश्य प्रायश्चित्तभागी होऊँगा-ऐसी अनात्म-बुद्धि अज्ञानियों को हुआ करती है, तत्त्वज्ञानी को नहीं। इसलिये विकाररहित चित्तवाले बोधवान् पुरुष को विहित कर्मों का भी विधिपूर्वक त्याग कर देना चाहिये
ram_gita::23.english_translation: Those ignorant in false self think 'I surely suffer from abandoning action,' not the wise who see reality. Therefore, the wise with steady mind must rightly renounce prescribed actions.
ram_gita::23.translation_literal: सप्रत्यवायः (with abandoning) हि (indeed) अहम् (I) इति (thus) अनात्म (not-self) धीः (intellect) अज्ञ (ignorant) प्रसिद्धाः (known) न (not) तत्त्वदर्शिनः (knowers of truth). तस्मात् (therefore) बुधैः (by the wise) त्याज्यम् (to be abandoned) अविक्रियात्मभिः (with unmoving self) विधानतः (according to rule) कर्म (action) विधिप्रकाशितम् (prescribed).
ram_gita::23.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::23.essence: True wisdom knows renouncing action rightly causes no harm to the self.
ram_gita::23.simple_meaning: Only those confused by false identity think they lose by abandoning action. The wise with steady minds renounce prescribed actions properly.
ram_gita::23.simple_insight: There's peace in knowing true wisdom does not depend on constant doing.
ram_gita::23.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that those attached to the false sense of self believe abandoning actions causes punishment. But the truly wise, with steady inner awareness, understand the nature of reality and can renounce actions rightly without harm.
ram_gita::23.modern_relevance: You worry stopping a routine task will cause failure, but deep calm comes when you trust wisdom beyond constant doing.
ram_gita::23.insight: It shifts focus from fear of losing by stopping to trust in steady inner wisdom beyond action.

ram_gita::24.verse_sanskrit:
श्रद्धान्वितस्तत्त्वमसीति वाक्यतो गुरोः प्रसादादपि शुद्धमानसः ।
विज्ञाय चैकात्म्यमथात्मजीवयोः सुखी भवेन्मेरुरिवाप्रकम्पनः ॥
ram_gita::24.verse_hindi: फिर शुद्धचित्त होकर श्रद्धापूर्वक गुरु की कृपा से ‘तत्त्वमसि’ इस महावाक्य के द्वारा परमात्मा और जीवात्मा की एकता जानकर सुमेरु के समान निश्चल एवं सुखी हो जाय
ram_gita::24.english_translation: By pure mind and trust, through the teacher's grace, knowing 'You are that'—the unity of supreme and individual self—you become stable and happy like Mount Meru.
ram_gita::24.translation_literal: श्रद्धान्वितः (with trust) तत्त्वमसि (You are that) इति (thus) वाक्यतः (by the statement) गुरोः (of the teacher) प्रसादात् (by grace) अपि (also) शुद्धमानसः (pure mind) । विज्ञाय (knowing) च (and) एकात्म्यम् (unity) अथ (then) आत्मजीवयोः (of the supreme self and individual self) सुखी (happy) भवेत् (becomes) मेरुरिव (like Mount Meru) अप्रकम्पनः (unshaken) ॥
ram_gita::24.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::24.essence: Trusting the teaching reveals your unshakable unity with the true self.
ram_gita::24.simple_meaning: With trust and a pure mind, through the teacher's blessing, you understand that the supreme self and individual self are one, becoming stable and happy like a mountain.
ram_gita::24.simple_insight: Trusting the teaching brings calm joy and unshakable peace within.
ram_gita::24.detailed_meaning: Rama teaches that when you truly trust your teacher and understand the teaching 'You are that,' you realize the oneness of the supreme and individual self. This knowledge makes you steady and joyful like the unshakable Mount Meru.
ram_gita::24.modern_relevance: After doubting yourself, you finally trust the guidance that reveals your inner strength and feel steady and peaceful despite life's storms.
ram_gita::24.insight: It shifts your mind from doubt and restlessness to steady trust and joyful stability in your true nature.

ram_gita::25.verse_sanskrit:
आदौ पदार्थावगतिर्हि कारणं वाक्यार्थविज्ञानविधौ विधानतः ।
तत्त्वम्पदार्थौ परमात्मजीवकावसीति चैकात्म्यमथानयोर्भवेत् ॥
ram_gita::25.verse_hindi: यह नियम ही है कि प्रत्येक वाक्य का अर्थ जानने में पहले उसके पके अर्थ का ज्ञान ही कारण है। इस ‘तत्त्वमसि’ महावाक्य के ‘तत्’ और ‘त्वम्’ पद क्रम से परमात्मा और जीवात्मा के वाचक हैं और ‘असि’ उन दोनों की एकता करता है
ram_gita::25.english_translation: The principle is that understanding the true meaning of each sentence requires knowing its mature sense first; in the phrase 'You are that,' 'You' and 'That' refer to the supreme being and the true self, and 'are' unites them as one.
ram_gita::25.translation_literal: आदौ (in the beginning) पदार्थ (meaning) अवगतिर्हि (understanding indeed) कारणं (cause) वाक्यार्थविज्ञानविधौ (in method of knowing sentence meaning) विधानतः (by rule) । तत्त्वम् (the truth) पदार्थौ (words) परमात्म (supreme being) जीवका (living being) आवसीति (is present) च (and) ऐकात्म्यम् (oneness) अथानयोः (of these two) भवेत् (arises) ॥
ram_gita::25.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::25.essence: Understanding 'You are that' reveals the supreme and true self as one reality.
ram_gita::25.simple_meaning: To understand a sentence’s full meaning, you must grasp its mature sense first; 'You are that' reveals the unity of your true self with the supreme being.
ram_gita::25.simple_insight: Recognising your oneness with the supreme brings clarity and dissolves separation.
ram_gita::25.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that understanding profound truths requires grasping the mature meaning behind words. He uses the phrase 'You are that' to show the supreme being and the true self are not separate but united as one, a central teaching in non-dual philosophy.
ram_gita::25.modern_relevance: When reading something complex, you often need to understand the big picture before the details make sense; similarly, seeing your true self as one with the supreme changes everything.
ram_gita::25.insight: It shifts your view from seeing yourself as separate to recognising your essential unity with the supreme reality.

ram_gita::26.verse_sanskrit:
प्रत्यक्परोक्षादि विरोधमात्मनोर्विहाय सङ्गृह्य तयोश्चिदात्मताम् ।
संशोधितां लक्षणया च लक्षितां ज्ञात्वा स्वमात्मानमथाद्वयो भवेत् ॥
ram_gita::26.verse_hindi: इन दोनों (जीवात्मा और परमात्मा) में जीवात्मा प्रत्यक (अन्त:करण का साक्षी) है और परमात्मा परोक्ष (इन्द्रियातीत) है, इस (वाच्यार्थरूप) विरोध को छोड़कर और लक्षणावृत्ति से लक्षित उनकी शुद्ध चेतनता को ग्रहण कर उसे ही अपना आत्मा जाने और इस प्रकार एकीभाव से स्थित हो
ram_gita::26.english_translation: Discarding the apparent opposition between the individual self and the supreme self, grasp their pure consciousness and realize your true self as one with it.
ram_gita::26.translation_literal: प्रत्यक्परोक्षादि (direct and indirect) / विरोधम् (opposition) / आत्मनोः (of the self) / विहाय (leaving behind) / सङ्गृह्य (grasping) / तयोः (of both) / चिदात्मताम् (consciousness nature) / संशोधिताम् (refined) / लक्षणया (by characteristic) / च (and) / लक्षिताम् (marked) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / स्वम् (own) / आत्मानम् (self) / अथ (thus) / अद्वय (non-dual) / भवेत् (becomes)
ram_gita::26.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::26.essence: Releasing apparent opposition reveals your true self as pure, unified consciousness.
ram_gita::26.simple_meaning: You can let go of the seeming difference between your individual self and the supreme self, and realize both are one pure awareness.
ram_gita::26.simple_insight: There's freedom in seeing your true self beyond any inner divisions or confusion.
ram_gita::26.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that the apparent conflict between the individual self (the direct witness) and the supreme self (beyond senses) is only a surface illusion. When you set aside this opposition and recognize their shared pure consciousness, you realize your true self is non-dual.
ram_gita::26.modern_relevance: When your mind feels torn between who you think you are and a deeper truth, this teaches you to see beyond that conflict and find unity within.
ram_gita::26.insight: It teaches you to notice apparent conflicts in your identity and step beyond them into non-dual awareness.

ram_gita::27.verse_sanskrit:
एकात्मकत्वाज्जहती न सम्भवेत्तथाजहल्लक्षणता विरोधतः ।
सोऽयम्पदार्थाविव भागलक्षणा युज्येत तत्त्वम्पदयोरदोषतः ॥
ram_gita::27.verse_hindi: इन ‘तत्’ और ‘त्वम्’ पदों में एकरूप होने के कारण जहतीलक्षणा नहीं हो सकती और परस्पर विरोध होने के कारण अजहल्लक्षणा भी नहीं हो सकती। इसलिये ‘सोऽयम्’ (यह वही है) इन दोनों पदों के अर्थ की भाँति इन ‘तत्’ और ‘त्वम्’ पदों में भी भागत्यागलक्षणा ही निर्दोषता से हो सकती है
ram_gita::27.english_translation: Because 'that' and 'you' are one, they cannot have negation by difference or contradiction; thus, 'That same' rightly indicates non-partition between them without fault.
ram_gita::27.translation_literal: एकात्मकत्वाज्जहती (from oneness negation) / न (not) / सम्भवेत्तथाजहल्लक्षणता (possible contradiction negation) / विरोधतः (because of opposition) / सोऽयम् (that same) / पदार्थाविव (like the meaning of words) / भागलक्षणा (non-partition indication) / युज्येत (should be joined) / तत्त्वम्पदयोरदोषतः (without fault of the two principles)
ram_gita::27.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::27.essence: True oneness means no contradiction or division can exist between what is one.
ram_gita::27.simple_meaning: When two terms refer to the exact same reality, they cannot be truly different or contradictory. Saying 'that same' shows they are united without any division or error.
ram_gita::27.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing apparent differences vanish when you see underlying unity.
ram_gita::27.detailed_meaning: Rama explains that the words 'that' (tat) and 'you' (tvam) are not separate or opposing concepts but are truly one. Therefore, neither contradiction nor negation applies to them, and the phrase 'that same' properly expresses their perfect unity.
ram_gita::27.modern_relevance: You might feel torn between who you appear to be and who you truly are. This teaching shows these identities are not opposing but one and the same.
ram_gita::27.insight: It shifts your mind from seeing separation to recognizing unity beneath difference.

ram_gita::28.verse_sanskrit:
रसादिपञ्चीकृतभूतसम्भवं भोगालयं दुःखसुखादिकर्मणाम् ।
शरीरमाद्यन्तवदादिकर्मजं मायामयं स्थूलमुपाधिमात्मनः ॥
ram_gita::28.verse_hindi: पृथिवी आदि पञ्चीकृत भूतों से उत्पन्न हुए, सुख-दुःखादि कर्म-भोगों के आश्रय और पूर्वोपार्जित कर्मफल से प्राप्त होने वाले इस मायामय आदि-अन्तवान् शरीर को विज्ञजन आत्मा की स्थूल उपाधि मानते हैं
ram_gita::28.english_translation: The body, born from earth and other elements, is the mind's gross covering formed by the fruits of past actions and is the dwelling for experiencing pleasure and pain.
ram_gita::28.translation_literal: रसादि (taste and so on) / पञ्चीकृत (composed of five) / भूतसम्भवं (arising from elements) / भोगालयं (place of experience) / दुःखसुखादि (pain, pleasure, etc.) / कर्मणाम् (of actions) / शरीरम् (body) / आद्यन्तवत् (from beginning to end) / आदिकर्मजम् (born of past actions) / मायामयं (made of illusion) / स्थूलम् (gross) / उपाधिम् (covering) / आत्मनः (of the self)
ram_gita::28.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::28.essence: The body is a temporary, illusory covering formed by past actions for experience.
ram_gita::28.simple_meaning: The body is a temporary, illusory form made from earth and past actions that houses experience of pleasure and pain.
ram_gita::28.simple_insight: You can feel free knowing the body is just a passing shell shaped by past causes.
ram_gita::28.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that the physical body arises from the five elements and past actions. It is an illusory, gross covering that the true self temporarily inhabits to experience joy and suffering.
ram_gita::28.modern_relevance: When you feel trapped by your body’s limits or moods, remember it is a temporary place shaped by past causes, not your true self.
ram_gita::28.insight: This verse shifts focus from identifying with the body to seeing it as a transient vessel shaped by past karma and illusion.

ram_gita::29.verse_sanskrit:
सूक्ष्मं मनोबुद्धिदशेन्द्रियैर्युतं प्राणैरपञ्चीकृतभूतसम्भवम् ।
भोक्तुः सुखादेरनुसाधनं भवेत् शरीरमन्यद्विदुरात्मनो बुधाः ॥
ram_gita::29.verse_hindi: और मन, बुद्धि, दस इन्द्रियाँ तथा पाँच प्राण (इन सत्रह अङ्गों) से युक्त और अपञ्चीकृत भूतों से उत्पन्न हुए सूक्ष्म शरीर को जो भोक्ता के सुख-दुःखादि अनुभव को साधन है, आत्मा का दूसरा देह मानते हैं
ram_gita::29.english_translation: The subtle body, composed of mind, intellect, ten senses, and five vital breaths born of unmodified elements, is known by the wise as the second body of the true self, serving as the instrument for experiencing pleasure and pain.
ram_gita::29.translation_literal: सूक्ष्मं (subtle) मनोबुद्धिदशेन्द्रियैर्युतं (mind-intellect-ten-senses-with) प्राणैरपञ्चीकृतभूतसम्भवम् (vital-breaths-five-unmodified-elements-born) । भोक्तुः (of the experiencer) सुखादेरनुसाधनं (pleasure-pain-instrument) भवेत् (is) शरीरमन्यद्विदुरात्मनो (body-second-known-true-self) बुधाः (wise) ॥
ram_gita::29.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::29.essence: Pleasure and pain happen in the subtle body, not in your true self.
ram_gita::29.simple_meaning: You have a subtle body made of mind, senses, and vital breaths that experiences pleasure and pain, but this is not your true self.
ram_gita::29.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing that pain and pleasure are experiences of a subtle body, not who you truly are.
ram_gita::29.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that beyond the physical body there exists a subtle body comprising mind, intellect, senses, and vital breaths. This body experiences sensations like pleasure and pain, but the wise recognize it as distinct from the true self, the unchanging inner being.
ram_gita::29.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by emotions or sensations, remember these arise in a subtle part of you, not your true self.
ram_gita::29.insight: It shifts your understanding from identifying with fluctuating sensations to recognizing the deeper, unchanging self behind them.

ram_gita::30.verse_sanskrit:
अनाद्यनिर्वाच्यमपीह कारणं मायाप्रधानं तु परं शरीरकम् ।
उपाधिभेदात्तु यतः पृथक्स्थितं स्वात्मानमात्मन्यवधारयेत्क्रमात् ॥
ram_gita::30.verse_hindi: (इनके अतिरिक्त) अनादि और अनिर्वाच्य मायामय कारणशरीर ही जीव का तीसरा देह है। इस प्रकार उपाधि-भेद से सर्वथा पृथक् स्थित अपने आत्मरूप को क्रमशः (उपाधियों का बाध करते हुए) अपने हृदय से निश्चय करे
ram_gita::30.english_translation: The eternal, indescribable cause here is the body made of illusion; by distinguishing these coverings, one should gradually recognize the true self within the heart, separate from all identities.
ram_gita::30.translation_literal: अनाद्यनिर्वाच्यमपीह (eternal, indescribable here) / कारणं (cause) / मायाप्रधानं (illusion-based) / तु (but) / परं (supreme) / शरीरकम् (body) / उपाधिभेदात् (due to distinctions of coverings) / तु (but) / यतः (therefore) / पृथक् (separate) / स्थितं (situated) / स्वात्मानम् (true self) / आत्मन्य् (in the self) / अवधारयेत् (should recognize) / क्रमात् (gradually)
ram_gita::30.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::30.essence: Your true self is distinct from the illusory body and its coverings.
ram_gita::30.simple_meaning: Your body is a temporary, illusory covering. By seeing through these layers, you can realize your true self beyond all identities.
ram_gita::30.simple_insight: There's peace in knowing you are deeper than any outer form or label.
ram_gita::30.detailed_meaning: Rama explains that the body formed by illusion is not the true self. By carefully observing and removing these false identities, one can gradually recognize the eternal true self dwelling within the heart.
ram_gita::30.modern_relevance: You may feel defined by your appearance or roles, but beneath these lies your unchanged true self waiting to be seen.
ram_gita::30.insight: It teaches you to separate your sense of self from changing outer conditions and identities.

ram_gita::31.verse_sanskrit:
कोशेष्वयं तेषु तु तत्तदाकृतिर्विभाति सङ्गात्स्फतिकोपलो यथा ।
असङ्गरूपोऽयमजो यतोऽद्वयो विज्ञायतेऽस्मिन्परितो विचारिते ॥
ram_gita::31.verse_hindi: स्फटिकमणि के समान यह आत्मा भी (अन्नमयादि) भिन्न-भिन्न कोशों में उनके सङ्ग से उन्हीं के आकार का भासने लगता है। किन्तु इसका भली प्रकार विचार करने से यह अद्वितीय होने के कारण असङ्गरूप और अजन्मा निश्चित होता है
ram_gita::31.english_translation: Like a crystal shining with the colors of different vessels, the true self appears shaped by associations but is actually unborn and without attachments when deeply examined.
ram_gita::31.translation_literal: कोशेष्वयं (in vessels themselves) तेषु (in them) तु (but) तत्तदाकृति: (that respective shape) विभाति (shines) सङ्गात् (from association) स्फतिकोपलो (crystal gem) यथा (like) । असङ्गरूप: (without attachment form) अयम् (this) अजो (unborn) यतः (because) अद्वय: (non-dual) विज्ञायते (is known) अस्मिन् (in this) परित: (around) विचारिते (considered) ॥
ram_gita::31.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::31.essence: The true self appears many ways but is actually unborn, free, and without attachments.
ram_gita::31.simple_meaning: The true self looks like it takes on many forms depending on surroundings, but when you examine it deeply, it is actually unborn and not attached to any form.
ram_gita::31.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing your true self is untouched by the shapes or roles you take on.
ram_gita::31.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that the true self appears differently in various contexts like a crystal reflecting colors from different vessels. Yet, upon careful reflection, it is revealed as unborn, free of attachments, and uniquely non-dual.
ram_gita::31.modern_relevance: When you feel defined by your roles or circumstances, this verse reminds you that your essence is beyond all changing forms and untouched by external labels.
ram_gita::31.insight: It shifts your understanding from identifying with external roles or appearances to recognizing your unchanging inner reality.

ram_gita::32.verse_sanskrit:
बुद्धेस्त्रिधा वृत्तिरपीह दृश्यते स्वप्नादिभेदेन गुणत्रयात्मनः  ।
अन्योन्यतोऽस्मिन्व्यभिचारितो मृषा नित्ये परे ब्रह्मणि केवले शिवे ॥
ram_gita::32.verse_hindi: त्रिगुणात्मिका बुद्धि की ही स्वप्न, जाग्रत् और सुषुप्ति भेद से तीन प्रकार की वृत्तियाँ दिखायी देती हैं, किन्तु इन तीनों वृत्तियों में से प्रत्येक का एक-दूसरी में व्यभिचार होने के कारण, ये (तीनों ही) एकमात्र कल्याणस्वरूप नित्य परब्रह्म में मिथ्या हैं (अर्थात् उसमे इन वृत्तियों का सर्वथा अभाव है)
ram_gita::32.english_translation: The discerning mind appears in three forms—like dream, waking, and deep sleep—but all are false and intermingled; only in the supreme reality, the pure blissful, are they absent.
ram_gita::32.translation_literal: बुद्धेस्त्रिधा (of the discerning mind threefold) / वृत्तिरपीह (forms also here) / दृश्यते (are seen) / स्वप्नादिभेदेन (by dream and others' difference) / गुणत्रयात्मनः (of the three qualities nature) / अन्योन्यतोऽस्मिन् (mutually in these) / व्यभिचारितो (intermingled) / मृषा (false) / नित्ये (in the eternal) / परे (supreme) / ब्रह्मणि (reality) / केवले (alone) / शिवे (blissful).
ram_gita::32.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::32.essence: The mind’s three shifting states are intertwined illusions absent only in the supreme reality.
ram_gita::32.simple_meaning: The mind shows itself in three shifting states like waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, but these are mixed illusions. Only the highest reality is free from these false appearances.
ram_gita::32.simple_insight: You can find peace knowing the restless mind’s states are not truly real.
ram_gita::32.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that the mind’s activity appears in three states—waking, dreaming, and deep sleep—each influenced by the three qualities (gunas) of nature. These states are interwoven illusions that do not exist in the supreme, blissful reality.
ram_gita::32.modern_relevance: When your thoughts confuse and shift constantly, remember that your true self is beyond these restless states.
ram_gita::32.insight: Recognize that your changing mental states are temporary illusions, freeing your awareness to rest in the unchanging supreme.

ram_gita::33.verse_sanskrit:
देहेन्द्रियप्राणमनश्चिदात्मनां  सङ्घादजस्त्रं परिवर्तते धियः ।
वृत्तिस्तमोमूलतयाज्ञलक्षणा यावद्भवेत्तावदसौ भवोद्भवः ॥
ram_gita::33.verse_hindi: बुद्धि की वृत्ति ही देह, इन्द्रिय, प्राण, मन और चेतन आत्मा के संघातरूप से निरन्तर परिवर्तित होती रहती है। यह वृत्ति तमोगुण से उत्पन्न होने वाली होने के कारण अज्ञानरूपा है और जबतक यह रहती है तबतक ही संसार में जन्म होता रहता है
ram_gita::33.english_translation: The activity of the discerning mind continuously changes due to the union of body, senses, life-force, mind, and conscious self; born from the root of darkness it causes ignorance, and as long as it persists, the cycle of birth continues.
ram_gita::33.translation_literal: देह (body) / इन्द्रिय (senses) / प्राण (life-force) / मन (mind) / चिदात्मनां (conscious self) / सङ्घात (union) / अज (unborn) / त्रं (activity) / परिवर्तते (changes) / धियः (of the discerning mind) / वृत्ति (activity) / तमोमूलतः (from the root of darkness) / अज्ञानरूपा (ignorance-like) / यावत् (as long as) / भवेत् (exists) / तावत् (that much) / असौ (that) / भवोद्भवः (cycle of birth and rebirth)
ram_gita::33.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::33.essence: Restless mental activity born of ignorance keeps the cycle of rebirth alive.
ram_gita::33.simple_meaning: Your discerning mind keeps changing because it mixes with body, senses, life-force, and mind, creating ignorance that traps you in cycles of rebirth.
ram_gita::33.simple_insight: You can feel how your restless mind keeps you bound to repeating patterns beyond your control.
ram_gita::33.detailed_meaning: Rama explains that the activity of the discerning mind arises from the combined influence of body, senses, life-force, mind, and conscious self. This activity originates in darkness (ignorance), causing ongoing cycles of birth and rebirth until it ceases.
ram_gita::33.modern_relevance: When your thoughts endlessly shift, reacting to every sensation and impulse, you feel stuck in repeated habits and patterns you can’t break free from.
ram_gita::33.insight: Recognize that the restless mind's constant changes are the root cause of your repeated cycles of reaction and becoming.

ram_gita::34.verse_sanskrit:
नेतिप्रमाणेन निराकृताखिलो हृदा समास्वादितचिद्घनामृतः ।
त्यजेदशेषं जगदात्तसद्रसं पीत्वा यथाम्भः प्रजहाति तत्फलम् ॥
ram_gita::34.verse_hindi: नेति-नेति’ आदि श्रुति-प्रमाण से निखिल संसार का बाध करके और हृदय में चिङ्घनामृत का आस्वादन करके सम्पूर्ण जगत् को, उसके साररूपा सत् (ब्रह्म) को ग्रहण करके त्याग दे, जैसे नारियल के जल को पीकर मनुष्य उसे फेंक देते हैं
ram_gita::34.english_translation: Reject all of the world by 'not this, not this' reasoning and, having tasted the nectar of pure consciousness in your heart, renounce everything as a man discards a coconut's water after drinking it.
ram_gita::34.translation_literal: नेति-नेति (not this, not this) / आदि (beginning) / श्रुति-प्रमाण (scriptural evidence) / से (by) / निखिल (entire) / संसार (world) / का (of) / बाध (obstruction) / करके (doing) / और (and) / हृदय (heart) / में (in) / चिङ्घनामृत (nectar of pure consciousness) / का (of) / आस्वादन (tasting) / करके (doing) / सम्पूर्ण (complete) / जगत् (world) / को (to) / उसके (its) / साररूपा (essence form) / सत् (truth) / (ब्रह्म) / को (to) / ग्रहण (acceptance) / करके (doing) / त्याग (renunciation) / दे (give up) / जैसे (like) / नारियल (coconut) / के (of) / जल (water) / को (object marker) / पीकर (after drinking) / मनुष्य (man) / उसे (it) / फेंक (throw) / देते (gives)
ram_gita::34.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::34.essence: Fully embrace your true self, then effortlessly release all else like discarded water.
ram_gita::34.simple_meaning: Use clear reasoning to reject everything that is not your true self, fully experience your pure inner being, then let go of all worldly attachments like discarding empty water.
ram_gita::34.simple_insight: There is freedom in fully tasting your true self and then releasing all else without clinging.
ram_gita::34.detailed_meaning: Rama teaches Lakshmana to use the 'not this, not this' method to reject the illusory world, fully taste the bliss of pure consciousness in the heart, and then renounce all worldly things effortlessly, like discarding coconut water after drinking.
ram_gita::34.modern_relevance: You’ve learned the truth about yourself deeply; now it’s time to let go of old attachments that no longer serve you.
ram_gita::34.insight: It teaches you to discern and fully experience your true self before releasing all that does not serve that truth.

ram_gita::35.verse_sanskrit:
कदाचिदात्मा न मृतो न जायते न क्षीयते नापि विवर्धतेऽनवः ।
निरस्तसर्वातिशयः सुखात्मकः स्वयम्प्रभः सर्वगतोऽयमद्वयः ॥
ram_gita::35.verse_hindi: आत्मा न कभी मरता है न जन्मता । है; वह न कभी क्षीण होता है और न । बढ़ता ही है। वह पुरातन, सम्पूर्ण विशेषणों से रहित, सुखस्वरूप, स्वयंप्रकाश, सर्वगत और अद्वितीय है
ram_gita::35.english_translation: The true self is never dead, never born, never diminished, never increased; it is ancient, free of all qualities, blissful, self-illuminated, all-pervading, and unique.
ram_gita::35.translation_literal: कदाचित् (never) आत्मा (true self) न (not) मृतो (dead) न (not) जायते (is born) न (not) क्षीयते (diminished) न (not) अपि (also) विवर्धते (increased) अनवः (never) । निरस्त (free) सर्वातिशयः (of all qualities) सुखात्मकः (blissful) स्वयम् (self) प्रभः (illuminated) सर्वगतः (all-pervading) अयम् (this) अद्वयः (unique) ॥
ram_gita::35.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::35.essence: Your true self is eternal, unchanging, blissful, and uniquely whole beyond all qualities.
ram_gita::35.simple_meaning: The true self never dies or is born, never loses or gains anything. It is ancient, pure happiness, self-lit, everywhere, and one of a kind.
ram_gita::35.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing your true being cannot be harmed or changed.
ram_gita::35.detailed_meaning: Rama teaches Lakshmana that the true self is not affected by birth, death, or change. It exists beyond all qualities and time, illuminating itself and filling all space without a second like it.
ram_gita::35.modern_relevance: When fears of loss or change overwhelm you, remember your deepest self remains untouched and whole regardless of life’s shifts.
ram_gita::35.insight: It shifts your focus from fleeting events to recognizing your unchanging essence beneath all change.

ram_gita::36.verse_sanskrit:
एवंविधे ज्ञानमये सुखात्मके कथं भवो दुःखमयः प्रतीयते ।
अज्ञानतोऽध्यासवशात्प्रकाशते ज्ञाने विलीयेत विरोधतः क्षणात् ॥
ram_gita::36.verse_hindi: जो इस प्रकार ज्ञानमय और सुखस्वरूप है उसमें (ज्ञान होने के बाद) यह दु:खमय संसार कैसे प्रतीत हो सकता है? यह तो अध्यास के कारण अज्ञान से ही प्रतीत होता है, ज्ञान से तो एक क्षण में ही लीन हो जाता है, क्योंकि ज्ञान और अज्ञान का परस्पर विरोध है
ram_gita::36.english_translation: How can that which is made of knowledge and is the essence of happiness appear sorrowful? It seems so only because of ignorance and superimposition; knowledge dissolves it instantly as they are opposed.
ram_gita::36.translation_literal: एवंविधे (in this way) ज्ञानमये (made of knowledge) सुखात्मके (essence of happiness) कथं (how) भवो (becomes) दुःखमयः (sorrowful) प्रतीयते (appears) । अज्ञानतः (due to ignorance) अध्यात्सवशात् (because of superimposition) प्रकाशते (is seen) ज्ञाने (by knowledge) विलीयेत (dissolves) विरोधतः (due to opposition) क्षणात् (in a moment) ॥
ram_gita::36.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::36.essence: Sorrow appears only from ignorance; true knowledge removes it instantly.
ram_gita::36.simple_meaning: Something made of pure knowledge and happiness cannot really seem sorrowful. Suffering appears only because of ignorance and confusion, and true knowledge quickly removes that illusion.
ram_gita::36.simple_insight: There’s freedom in seeing sorrow as a temporary mistake of perception, not reality.
ram_gita::36.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that the true self, made of pure knowledge and happiness, cannot actually be sorrowful. The world seems painful only because ignorance and mental superimposition cloud the vision. Real knowledge instantly removes this false appearance.
ram_gita::36.modern_relevance: You might feel overwhelmed by sadness or stress, but this teaches that those feelings come from confusion, not your true self.
ram_gita::36.insight: It shifts the mind from accepting suffering as real to seeing it as a mistaken overlay removable by clear understanding.

ram_gita::37.verse_sanskrit:
यदन्यदन्यत्र विभाव्यते भ्रमादध्यासमित्याहुरमुं विपश्चितः ।
असर्पभूतेऽहिविभावनं यथा रज्ज्वादिके तद्वदपीश्वरे जगत् ॥
ram_gita::37.verse_hindi: भ्रम से जो अन्य में अन्य की प्रतीति होती है उसी को विद्वानों ने अध्यास कहा है। जिस प्रकार असर्परूप रज्जु में सर्प की प्रतीति होती है, उसी प्रकार ईश्वर में संसार की प्रतीति हो रही है
ram_gita::37.english_translation: Scholars call the illusion of seeing one thing as another 'adhyasa'; just as a snake is perceived in a rope, the world is perceived in the supreme being.
ram_gita::37.translation_literal: यद् (that which) अन्यद् (other) अन्यत्र (elsewhere) विभाव्यते (is perceived) भ्रमात् (from illusion) अध्यासम् (superimposition) इति (thus) आहुः (say) अमुन् (by the wise) विपश्चितः (the learned); असर्पभूतेऽहि (in a rope that is like a snake) विभावनम् (perception) यथा (just as) रज्ज्वादिके (in a rope etc.) तद् (that) वद (like) अपीश्वरे (in the supreme being) जगत् (the world).
ram_gita::37.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::37.essence: The world is a mistaken perception superimposed on the supreme reality, like a snake seen in a rope.
ram_gita::37.simple_meaning: Sometimes your mind mistakes one thing for another, like seeing a snake in a rope. Similarly, the world appears as something real but is actually a superimposed illusion.
ram_gita::37.simple_insight: There’s comfort in realizing your worries often arise from mistaken perceptions, not reality itself.
ram_gita::37.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that what we perceive as the world is actually a superimposition, a confusion like mistaking a rope for a snake. This teaching reveals how illusion (Maya) causes us to see the unreal as real.
ram_gita::37.modern_relevance: When you panic seeing a shadow that looks like a threat, it’s like this—your mind’s quick mistake creates needless fear.
ram_gita::37.insight: This verse teaches you to question what you perceive and recognize how your mind overlays false images on reality.

ram_gita::38.verse_sanskrit:
विकल्पमायारहिते चिदात्मकेऽहङ्कार एष प्रथमः प्रकल्पितः ।
अध्यास एवात्मनि सर्वकारणे निरामये ब्रह्मणि केवले परे ॥
ram_gita::38.verse_hindi: जो विकल्प और माया से रहित है। उस सबके कारण निरामय, अद्वितीय और चित्स्वरूप परमात्मा ब्रह्म में पहले इस ‘अहंकार’ रूप अध्यास की ही कल्पना होती है
ram_gita::38.english_translation: The first manifestation is ego, free from alternatives and illusion, existing as pure consciousness in the supreme reality, untouched by causes.
ram_gita::38.translation_literal: विकल्पमायारहिते (free from alternatives and illusion) / चिदात्मकेऽहङ्कार (ego in pure consciousness) / एष (this) / प्रथमः (first) / प्रकल्पितः (manifested) / अध्यास (superimposition) / एवात्मनि (only in the self) / सर्वकारणे (in all causes) / निरामये (free from disease or impurity) / ब्रह्मणि (in Brahman) / केवले (alone) / परे (supreme)
ram_gita::38.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::38.essence: Ego is the first false identity appearing in pure consciousness beyond all cause.
ram_gita::38.simple_meaning: Ego is the first false sense of self that appears in pure consciousness, free from illusion and causes.
ram_gita::38.simple_insight: You can feel relief knowing ego is just the first false impression, not your true self.
ram_gita::38.detailed_meaning: Rama explains that ego is the first superimposed identity appearing in the true self, which itself is pure consciousness and untouched by any cause or illusion. Recognising ego as a false appearance leads to deeper realisation.
ram_gita::38.modern_relevance: When you feel a strong 'I' or separate self, remember this sense is a first false image, not your true being.
ram_gita::38.insight: It shifts your view from identifying as ego to seeing ego as a temporary, cause-free illusion within pure awareness.

ram_gita::39.verse_sanskrit:
इच्छादिरागादि सुखादिधर्मिकाः सदा धियः संसृतिहेतवः परे ।
यस्मात्प्रसुप्तौ तदभावतः परः सुखस्वरूपेण विभाव्यते हि नः ॥
ram_gita::39.verse_hindi: सबके साक्षी आत्मा में इच्छा, अनिच्छा, राग-द्वेष और सुख-दुःखादिरूप बुद्धि की वृत्तियाँ ही जन्म-मरणरूप संसार को कारण हैं; क्योंकि सुषुप्ति में इनका अभाव हो जाने पर हमें आत्मा का सुखरूप से भान होता है
ram_gita::39.english_translation: Desires, aversions, attachments, and feelings of pleasure and pain in the mind are the causes of the cycle of birth and death; because in deep sleep, their absence reveals to us the blissful nature of the true self.
ram_gita::39.translation_literal: इच्छा (desire) / आदिरागादि (attachment and so forth) / सुखादि (pleasure and so on) / धर्मिकाः (righteous) / सदा (always) / धियः (thoughts) / संसृतिहेतवः (cause of rebirth) / परे (beyond) / यस्मात् (because) / प्रसुप्तौ (in deep sleep) / तदभावतः (their absence) / परः (higher) / सुखस्वरूपेण (in blissful nature) / विभाव्यते (is revealed) / हि (indeed) / नः (to us)
ram_gita::39.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::39.essence: The absence of desires reveals the blissful true self beyond the restless mind.
ram_gita::39.simple_meaning: Your desires, dislikes, attachments, and feelings of pleasure and pain create the cycle of rebirth. When these disappear in deep sleep, you experience the bliss of your true self.
ram_gita::39.simple_insight: You can sense your true joy when the mind’s restless impulses are silent.
ram_gita::39.detailed_meaning: Rama explains that the mind’s constant fluctuations—desire, attachment, pleasure, and pain—cause the endless cycle of rebirth. Yet in deep sleep, when these mental activities cease, the true self’s blissful nature becomes evident to us.
ram_gita::39.modern_relevance: After a long, busy day filled with cravings and worries, the relief you feel in deep rest hints at a deeper joy beyond your thoughts.
ram_gita::39.insight: This verse teaches you to recognize that the restless mind’s cravings are not your true nature, which is peaceful and blissful.

ram_gita::40.verse_sanskrit:
अनाद्यविद्योद्भवबुद्धिबिम्बितो जीवप्रकाशोऽयमितीर्यते चितः ।
आत्माधियः साक्षितया पृथक्स्थितो बुध्द्यापरिच्छिन्नपरः स एव हि ॥
ram_gita::40.verse_hindi: अनादि अविद्या से उत्पन्न हुई बुद्धि में प्रतिबिम्बित चेतन का प्रकाश ही ‘जीव’ कहलाता है। बुद्धि के साक्षीरूप से आत्मा उससे पृथक् है, वह परात्मा तो बुद्धि के परिच्छेद से रहित है
ram_gita::40.english_translation: The living being is the light of consciousness reflected in intellect born from beginningless ignorance; the true self is separate from intellect as its witness and beyond its distinctions.
ram_gita::40.translation_literal:
अनाद्य (beginningless) / विद्या (ignorance) / उद्भव (arisen) / बुद्धि (intellect) / बिम्बितः (reflected) / जीव (living being) / प्रकाशः (light) / अयम् (this) / इतीर्यते (is called) / चितः (of consciousness) ।
आत्माधियः (true self) / साक्षितया (by witnessing) / पृथक् (separate) / स्थितः (situated) / बुद्धि (intellect) / अपरिच्छिन्न (without division) / परः (beyond) / स (that) / एव (indeed) / हि (certainly) ॥
ram_gita::40.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::40.essence: Your true self is the unchanging watcher beyond intellect and its illusions.
ram_gita::40.simple_meaning: The living being is consciousness shining through intellect, which comes from endless ignorance. The true self is separate, watching intellect without being affected by its changes.
ram_gita::40.simple_insight: You can feel peace knowing your real self is untouched by your restless mind.
ram_gita::40.detailed_meaning: Rama explains that the living being (jiva) is consciousness reflected in the intellect, which originates from beginningless ignorance (avidya). Yet the true self (atman) exists as the witness, separate and beyond the fluctuating intellect, untouched by its divisions.
ram_gita::40.modern_relevance: When your thoughts overwhelm you, remember there's a quiet part of you observing it all, untouched and steady.
ram_gita::40.insight: It teaches you to shift from identifying with your thoughts to recognizing yourself as their impartial observer.

ram_gita::41.verse_sanskrit:
चिद्बिम्बसाक्ष्यात्मधियां प्रसङ्गतस्त्वेकत्र वासादनलाक्तलोहवत् ।
अन्योन्यमध्यासवशात्प्रतीयते जडाजडत्वं च चिदात्मचेतसोः ॥
ram_gita::41.verse_hindi: अग्नि से तपे हुए लोहे के समान चिदाभास, साक्षी आत्मा तथा बुद्धि के एकत्र रहने से परस्पर अन्योन्याध्यास होने के कारण क्रमश: उनकी चेतनता और जडता प्रतीत होती है। (अर्थात् जिस प्रकार अग्नि से तपे हुए लोहपिण्ड में अग्नि और लोहे का तादात्म्य हो जाने से लोहे का आकार अग्नि में और अग्नि की उष्णता लोहे में दिखायी देने लगती है उसी प्रकार बुद्धि और आत्मा का तादात्म्य हो जाने से आत्मा की चेतनता बुद्धि आदि में और बुद्धि आदि की जडता आत्मा में प्रतीत होने लगती है। इसलिये अध्यासवश बुद्धि से लेकर शरीरपर्यन्त अनात्म वस्तुओं को ही आत्मा मानने लगते हैं)
ram_gita::41.english_translation: Like fire-heated iron, the reflection of consciousness, the witnessing self, and the discerning mind, when dwelling together, mutually superimpose qualities, causing their distinctness and dullness to appear.
ram_gita::41.translation_literal: चिद्बिम्बसाक्ष्यात्मधियां (reflection of consciousness, witnessing self, discerning mind) / प्रसङ्गतस्त्वेकत्र (when together in contact) / वासादनलाक्तलोहवत् (like fire-heated iron) / अन्योन्यमध्यासवशात् (due to mutual superimposition) / प्रतीयते (appears) / जडाजडत्वं (dullness and distinctness) / च (and) / चिदात्मचेतसोः (of consciousness and self-awareness).
ram_gita::41.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::41.essence: Your true self and mind mix, creating illusions of difference and dullness.
ram_gita::41.simple_meaning: When the true self, mind, and awareness stay together, they mix their qualities, making you see dullness and difference where there is none.
ram_gita::41.simple_insight: There’s a gentle confusion in how your mind and self blend, making things seem separate and unclear.
ram_gita::41.detailed_meaning: Rama explains to Lakshmana that just as heated iron and fire blend to show qualities of each other, the true self and the discerning mind overlap. This overlap makes the pure self appear mixed with dullness and difference, causing confusion about what is real.
ram_gita::41.modern_relevance: Like when your thoughts and feelings blend so much you can’t tell what’s really you, this verse shows how mind and true self confuse each other’s qualities.
ram_gita::41.insight: It teaches you to see the mind’s qualities as overlays on your true self, not as your real nature.

ram_gita::42.verse_sanskrit:
गुरोः सकाशादपि वेदवाक्यतः सञ्जातविद्यानुभवो निरीक्ष्य तम् ।
स्वात्मानमात्मस्थमुपाधिवर्जितं त्यजेदशेषं जडमात्मगोचरम् ॥
ram_gita::42.verse_hindi: गुरु के समीप रहने से और वेदवाक्यों से आत्मज्ञान का अनुभव होने पर अपने हृदयस्थ उपाधिरहित आत्मा का साक्षात्कार करके आत्मारूप से प्रतीत होने वाले देहादि सम्पूर्ण जड पदार्थों का त्याग कर देना चाहिये
ram_gita::42.english_translation: When the knowledge born from being near the Guru and studying the Vedas is experienced, one should abandon all inert matter perceived as the body by realizing the self within the heart, free from all attachments.
ram_gita::42.translation_literal: गुरोः (of the guru) सकाशात् (near) अपि (also) वेदवाक्यतः (from the Vedic sayings) सञ्जातविद्यानुभवः (knowledge experience born) निरीक्ष्य (upon observing) तम् (that) स्वात्मानम् (own self) आत्मस्थम् (in the self) उपाधिवर्जितम् (free from limiting adjuncts) त्यजेत् (should abandon) अशेषम् (complete) जडम् (inert) आत्मगोचरम् (perceived by the self)
ram_gita::42.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::42.essence: True knowledge arises by realizing the self beyond all attachments and rejecting what is not you.
ram_gita::42.simple_meaning: By learning from the Guru and sacred texts, you realize the true self free from all limits and give up identifying with the body and inert things.
ram_gita::42.simple_insight: You feel a quiet freedom when you stop clinging to what is not truly you.
ram_gita::42.detailed_meaning: Rama teaches that after receiving guidance from the Guru and understanding the Vedas, the seeker must observe and realize the self within the heart that is free from all limiting attachments and reject all inert matter perceived as the body and external objects.
ram_gita::42.modern_relevance: After reading or hearing wise advice, you begin to feel who you truly are beyond your job, belongings, and body—and you start letting go of those identifications.
ram_gita::42.insight: It guides you to shift focus from outer identifications to the inner self free of attachments.

ram_gita::43.verse_sanskrit:
प्रकाशरूपोऽहमजोऽहमद्वयोऽसकृद्विभातोऽहमतीव निर्मलः ।
विशुद्धविज्ञानघनो निरामयः सम्पूर्ण आनन्दमयोऽहमक्रियः ॥
ram_gita::43.verse_hindi: मैं प्रकाशस्वरूप, अजन्मा, अद्वितीय, निरन्तर भासमान, अत्यन्त निर्मल, विशुद्ध विज्ञानघन, निरामय, क्रियारहित और एकमात्र आनन्दस्वरूप हूँ
ram_gita::43.english_translation: I am the embodiment of light, unborn, unique, ever shining, supremely pure, dense with pure knowledge, free from disease, actionless, and the sole source of bliss.
ram_gita::43.translation_literal: प्रकाशरूपोऽहम (light-form I-am) / अज (unborn) / अहम् (I-am) / अद्वयोऽस (non-dual I-am) / कृत्-विभातः (ever shining) / अहम् (I am) / तीव (intensely) / निर्मलः (pure) / विशुद्ध-विज्ञान-घनः (pure-knowledge-dense) / निरामयः (free-from-disease) / सम्पूर्ण (complete) / आनन्दमयः (blissful) / अहम् (I am) / क्रियः (actionless)
ram_gita::43.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::43.essence: Your true self is an unborn, pure light that is always free and joyful.
ram_gita::43.simple_meaning: You are the eternal light that never began, perfectly pure, full of true knowledge, free from illness, without any action, and the source of complete joy.
ram_gita::43.simple_insight: Feel the peace of knowing your true self is untouched, pure, and full of bliss beyond all change.
ram_gita::43.detailed_meaning: Rama reveals to Lakshmana that his true self is a radiant, unborn presence beyond duality, completely pure and filled with perfect knowledge. This self is free from all decay and activity, embodying pure joy, showing the ultimate nature beyond the physical world.
ram_gita::43.modern_relevance: When you feel overwhelmed by illness, mistakes, or constant doing, remember your core being is untouched, pure, and always peaceful beneath it all.
ram_gita::43.insight: This verse shifts focus from your changing body and mind to your unchanging, radiant true self beyond all action.

ram_gita::44.verse_hindi: मैं सदा ही मुक्त, अचिन्त्यशक्ति, अतीन्द्रिय, अविकृतरूप और अनन्तपार हूँ। वेदवादी पण्डितजन अहर्निश मेरा हृदय में चिन्तन करते हैं
ram_gita::44.english_translation: I am always free, of inconceivable power, beyond the senses, immutable, infinite and transcendent. The wise scholars constantly contemplate me in their hearts through the Vedas.
ram_gita::44.translation_literal: सदैव (always) मुक्तः (free) अहम् (I am) अचिन्त्यशक्तिमान् (of inconceivable power) अतीन्द्रिय (beyond senses) ज्ञान (knowledge) म अविक्रियात्मकः (immutable) । अनन्तपारः (infinite and transcendent) अहम् (I am) अहर्निशं (day and night) बुधैः (by the wise) विभावितः (contemplated) अहम् (I am) हृदि (in the heart) वेदवादिभिः (by the Vedic scholars) ॥
ram_gita::44.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::44.essence: Your true self is eternally free, beyond senses, infinitely powerful, and unchanging.
ram_gita::44.simple_meaning: You are forever free, beyond what the senses perceive, unchanging and infinitely vast. Wise people realize this truth through deep reflection.
ram_gita::44.simple_insight: Feeling your limitless and unchanging nature brings deep inner strength and peace.
ram_gita::44.detailed_meaning: Rama reveals that his true nature is always free, beyond sensory experience, and unchanging. Wise scholars use the Vedas to contemplate this supreme reality within their hearts, highlighting the deep spiritual knowledge at the core of existence.
ram_gita::44.modern_relevance: When stress tries to shake you, remember your true self is unchanging and beyond any challenge you face.
ram_gita::44.insight: It teaches you to recognize your inner being as vast, constant, and beyond sensory fluctuations.

ram_gita::45.verse_sanskrit:
एवं सदात्मानमखण्डितात्मना विचारमाणस्य विशुद्धभावना ।
हन्यादविद्यामचिरेण कारकै रसायनं यद्वदुपासितं रुजः ॥
ram_gita::45.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार सदा आत्मा का अखण्ड वृत्ति से चिन्तन करने वाले पुरुष के अन्त: करण में उत्पन्न हुई विशुद्ध भावना तुरन्त ही कारकादि के सहित अविद्या का नाश कर देती है, जिस प्रकार नियमानुसार सेवन की हुई ओषधि रोग को नष्ट कर डालती है
ram_gita::45.english_translation: Thus, a person who constantly contemplates the true self with an undivided mind develops a pure inner state that quickly destroys ignorance and its causes just like medicine cures disease when properly taken.
ram_gita::45.translation_literal: एवं (thus) सदात्मानम् (true self) अखण्डितात्मना (with undivided mind) विचारमाणस्य (contemplating) विशुद्धभावना (pure feeling) । हन्याद (destroys) अविद्याम् (ignorance) अचिरेण (quickly) कारकै (causes) रसायनं (medicine) यत् (which) वद् (like) उपासितं (worshiped) रुजः (disease) ॥
ram_gita::45.speaker: Rama
ram_gita::45.essence: Steady, undivided focus on your true self quickly dissolves ignorance like medicine cures illness.
ram_gita::45.simple_meaning: When you steadily focus on your true self, a pure feeling arises inside that quickly removes ignorance and its causes, like medicine curing disease.
ram_gita::45.simple_insight: You can feel a cleansing power inside when your attention is steady and undivided.
ram_gita::45.detailed_meaning: Rama teaches that when a person continually contemplates the true self without distraction, a pure inner state forms that acts like medicine, swiftly destroying ignorance and its causes. This moment follows deep teaching on self-knowledge, showing the power of sustained reflection.
ram_gita::45.modern_relevance: You sit quietly, focusing fully on your core self despite distractions, and soon confusion about who you are begins to lift like a fever breaking.
ram_gita::45.insight: It teaches you to maintain steady attention on your true self, enabling clarity to dissolve deep confusion naturally.

ram_gita::46.verse_sanskrit:
विविक्त आसीन उपारतेन्द्रियो विनिर्जितात्मा विमलान्तराशयः ।
विभावयेदेकमनन्यसाधनो विज्ञानदृक्केवल आत्मसंस्थितः ॥
ram_gita::46.verse_hindi: (आत्मचिन्तन करने वाले पुरुष को चाहिये कि) एकान्त देश में इन्द्रियों को उनके विषयों से हटाकर और अन्त:करण को अपने अधीन करके बैठे तथा आत्मा में स्थित होकर और किसी साधन का आश्रय न लेकर शुद्धचित्त हुआ केवल ज्ञानदृष्टिद्वारा एक आत्मा की ही भावना करे
