ramacharitamanas::24.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is calm, honest, and attentive. Nothing flashy happens, yet your breathing changes and your mind settles. Some spaces carry a force you feel before you can name it.
ramacharitamanas::24.insight: It shifts attention from formal holiness to lived transformation: a place is sacred by what it does to people.

ramacharitamanas::25.verse_sanskrit: सुनि समुझहिं जन मुदित मन मज्जहिं अति अनुराग। लहहिं चारि फल अछत तनु साधु समाज प्रयाग ॥
ramacharitamanas::25.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य इस संत समाज रूपी तीर्थराज का प्रभाव प्रसन्न मन से सुनते और समझते हैं और फिर अत्यन्त प्रेमपूर्वक इसमें गोते लगाते हैं, वे इस शरीर के रहते ही धर्म, अर्थ, काम, मोक्ष- चारों फल पा जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::25.english_translation: People who hear, understand, and lovingly immerse themselves in this holy company of saints gain the four aims of life while still living in the body.
ramacharitamanas::25.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / समुझहिं (understand) / जन (people) / मुदित मन (with joyful mind) / मज्जहिं (immerse themselves) / अति अनुराग (with great love) / लहहिं (they obtain) / चारि फल (four fruits) / अछत तनु (while the body remains) / साधु समाज (holy company of saints) / प्रयाग (Prayag)
ramacharitamanas::25.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::25.essence: Love sacred company, and life’s four aims can flower in one body.
ramacharitamanas::25.simple_meaning: Listening to and lovingly entering the company of saints brings a person the four aims of life even before death.
ramacharitamanas::25.simple_insight: You do not have to wait for some distant finish line to feel life opening up.
ramacharitamanas::25.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising the holy company of saints at Prayag as a living field of transformation. Anyone who hears, understands, and enters it with love can receive the four aims of life while still embodied.
ramacharitamanas::25.modern_relevance: You sit in a room where one calm, honest conversation changes your whole week. Something in you softens, clears, and starts moving again. That is the power Tulsidas points to.
ramacharitamanas::25.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing results alone to trusting the transforming power of holy company.

ramacharitamanas::26.verse_sanskrit: मज्जन फल पेखिअ ततकाला। काक होहिं पिक बकउ मराला॥ सुनि आचरज करै जनि कोई। सतसंगति महिमा नहिं गोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::26.verse_hindi: इस तीर्थराज में स्नान का फल तत्काल ऐसा देखने में आता है कि कौए कोयल बन जाते हैं और बगुले हंस। यह सुनकर कोई आश्चर्य न करे, क्योंकि सत्संग की महिमा छिपी नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::26.english_translation: The result of bathing appears at once: crows become cuckoos, and herons become swans. Do not be surprised; the greatness of holy company is no secret.
ramacharitamanas::26.translation_literal: मज्जन (bathing) / फल (result) / पेखिअ (is seen) / ततकाला (at once) । काक (crow) / होहिं (become) / पिक (cuckoo) / बकउ (heron) / मराला (swan) ॥ सुनि (hearing) / आचरज (surprise) / करै (should do) / जनि (not) / कोई (anyone) । सतसंगति (holy company) / महिमा (greatness) / नहिं (not) / गोई (hidden) ॥
ramacharitamanas::26.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::26.essence: Holy company can transform even the most hardened nature.
ramacharitamanas::26.simple_meaning: Being in the company of the holy changes people quickly and visibly. Even those with rough habits can become gentle and pure.
ramacharitamanas::26.simple_insight: You are shaped by the company you keep, often faster than you realize.
ramacharitamanas::26.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising the power of satsang in the sacred bathing place. He says its effect is immediate: a crow can become a cuckoo, a heron a swan. The point is that holy company transforms character in plain sight.
ramacharitamanas::26.modern_relevance: You spend an evening with people who gossip, and your mind feels heavier the next morning. You spend the same evening with someone calm and sincere, and your own speech softens. Company changes you fast.
ramacharitamanas::26.insight: It shifts attention from abstract ideals to the people and environments that quietly reshape conduct.

ramacharitamanas::27.verse_sanskrit: बालमीक नारद घटजोनी। निज निज मुखनि कही निज होनी॥ जलचर थलचर नभचर नाना। जे जड़ चेतन जीव जहाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::27.verse_hindi: वाल्मीकिजी, नारदजी और अगस्त्यजी ने अपने-अपने मुखों से अपनी होनी (जीवन का वृत्तांत) कही है। जल में रहने वाले, जमीन पर चलने वाले और आकाश में विचरने वाले नाना प्रकार के जड़-चेतन जितने जीव इस जगत में हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::27.english_translation: Valmiki, Narad, and Agastya have each told their own life story in their own words. Countless beings in the world exist in water, on land, and in the sky, both living and inert.
ramacharitamanas::27.translation_literal: बालमीक (Valmiki) / नारद (Narad) / घटजोनी (born from the pot; Agastya) / निज (own) / निज (own) / मुखनि (with mouths; words) / कही (said) / निज होनी (one's own fate/life story) / जलचर (water-dwellers) / थलचर (land-dwellers) / नभचर (sky-dwellers) / नाना (various) / जे (which) / जड़ (inert) / चेतन (sentient) / जीव (living beings) / जहाना (in the world)
ramacharitamanas::27.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::27.essence: True teaching comes from lived truth, not borrowed talk.
ramacharitamanas::27.simple_meaning: Great sages have spoken from their own experience, and the world contains countless beings in every realm, living and nonliving.
ramacharitamanas::27.simple_insight: Real wisdom is grounded in lived experience, not abstract claims.
ramacharitamanas::27.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues praising the power of holy company by pointing to great sages like Valmiki, Narad, and Agastya. He widens the lens to all creatures across water, land, and sky, showing that the truth he is about to unfold applies to the whole living world.
ramacharitamanas::27.modern_relevance: You hear three different people describe the same difficult year from their own angle. None of them is lying; each is speaking from lived reality. That is the kind of listening this verse invites.
ramacharitamanas::27.insight: It shifts attention from secondhand opinion to testimony rooted in direct seeing.

ramacharitamanas::28.verse_sanskrit: मति कीरति गति भूति भलाई। जब जेहिं जतन जहाँ जेहिं पाई॥ सो जानब सतसंग प्रभाऊ। लोकहुँ बेद न आन उपाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::28.verse_hindi: उनमें से जिसने जिस समय जहाँ कहीं भी जिस किसी यत्न से बुद्धि, कीर्ति, सद्गति, विभूति (ऐश्वर्य) और भलाई पाई है, सो सब सत्संग का ही प्रभाव समझना चाहिए। वेदों में और लोक में इनकी प्राप्ति का दूसरा कोई उपाय नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::28.english_translation: Whatever wisdom, fame, good destiny, wealth, and well-being anyone gains anywhere, through any effort, should be known as the power of holy company. In the world and in the Vedas, there is no other way.
ramacharitamanas::28.translation_literal: मति (wisdom) / कीरति (fame) / गति (good destiny) / भूति (wealth, splendor) / भलाई (well-being) / जब (when) / जेहिं (by which) / जतन (effort, means) / जहाँ (where) / जेहिं (by which) / पाई (obtained) / सो (that) / जानब (should know) / सतसंग (holy company) / प्रभाऊ (power, influence) / लोकहुँ (in the world too) / बेद (the Vedas) / न (not) / आन (other) / उपाऊ (means)
ramacharitamanas::28.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::28.essence: Holy company is the hidden source of every lasting good.
ramacharitamanas::28.simple_meaning: Every gain worth having — wisdom, reputation, prosperity, and goodness — comes from the influence of good company. The world and the Vedas say there is no other source.
ramacharitamanas::28.simple_insight: You are shaped by the people and atmospheres you keep close.
ramacharitamanas::28.detailed_meaning: In the holy forest setting, Tulsidas turns from examples to a principle: every real gain in life traces back to satsang. Wisdom, honor, prosperity, and goodness do not arise by accident; they come from the company you keep.
ramacharitamanas::28.modern_relevance: You leave a room after an hour with one friend feeling steadier, clearer, and kinder — and after another feeling scattered. This verse says those shifts are not small; they are the real cause of your growth.
ramacharitamanas::28.insight: It shifts attention from isolated effort to the shaping power of environment and association.

ramacharitamanas::29.verse_sanskrit: बिनु सतसंग बिबेक न होई। राम कृपा बिनु सुलभ न सोई॥ सतसंगत मुद मंगल मूला। सोई फल सिधि सब साधन फूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::29.verse_hindi: सत्संग के बिना विवेक नहीं होता और श्री रामजी की कृपा के बिना वह सत्संग सहज में मिलता नहीं। सत्संगति आनंद और कल्याण की जड़ है। सत्संग की सिद्धि (प्राप्ति) ही फल है और सब साधन तो फूल है ॥
ramacharitamanas::29.english_translation: Without holy company, discernment does not arise. Without Ram's grace, that holy company is not easily found. Holy company is the root of joy and well-being. Its attainment is the fruit; all other practices are only flowers.
ramacharitamanas::29.translation_literal: बिनु (without) / सतसंग (holy company) / बिबेक (discernment) / न होई (does not happen) / राम कृपा (Ram's grace) / बिनु (without) / सुलभ (easily found) / न सोई (not that) / सतसंगत (in holy company) / मुद (joy) / मंगल (well-being) / मूला (root) / सोई (that) / फल (fruit) / सिधि (accomplishment) / सब (all) / साधन (practices) / फूला (flowers)
ramacharitamanas::29.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::29.essence: Holy company awakens discernment, and grace makes holy company possible.
ramacharitamanas::29.simple_meaning: Clear seeing comes from good company, and that good company itself is found through Ram's grace. Real joy and well-being begin there; all other practices are secondary.
ramacharitamanas::29.simple_insight: You can stop treating insight like a solo achievement. The right company and a humble heart do more than effort alone.
ramacharitamanas::29.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues explaining how wisdom grows. He says discernment does not appear in isolation, and even the blessing of holy company is not easy to secure without Ram's grace. In this devotional world, the real treasure is not technique but the company that awakens the heart.
ramacharitamanas::29.modern_relevance: You keep trying to think your way out of the same loop, but one honest conversation with the right person changes everything. Sometimes clarity arrives only after grace has arranged the room.
ramacharitamanas::29.insight: It shifts the mind from self-made progress to grace-supported transformation through uplifting company.

ramacharitamanas::30.verse_sanskrit: सठ सुधरहिं सतसंगति पाई। पारस परस कुधात सुहाई॥ बिधि बस सुजन कुसंगत परहीं। फनि मनि सम निज गुन अनुसरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::30.verse_hindi: दुष्ट भी सत्संगति पाकर सुधर जाते हैं, जैसे पारस के स्पर्श से लोहा सुहावना हो जाता है (सुंदर सोना बन जाता है), किन्तु दैवयोग से यदि कभी सज्जन कुसंगति में पड़ जाते हैं, तो वे वहाँ भी साँप की मणि के समान अपने गुणों का ही अनुसरण करते हैं। (अर्थात् जिस प्रकार साँप का संसर्ग पाकर भी मणि उसके विष को ग्रहण नहीं करती तथा अपने सहज गुण प्रकाश को नहीं छोड़ती, उसी प्रकार साधु पुरुष दुष्टों के संग में रहकर भी दूसरों को प्रकाश ही देते हैं, दुष्टों का उन पर कोई प्रभाव नहीं पड़ता।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::30.english_translation: The wicked improve through holy company, like base metal turning beautiful by touch of the philosopher's stone. By fate, if the good fall into bad company, they still follow their own nature, like a serpent's jewel.
ramacharitamanas::30.translation_literal: सठ (wicked) / सुधरहिं (become सुधर, improve) / सतसंगति (holy company) / पाई (having obtained) / पारस (philosopher's stone) / परस (touch) / कुधात (base metal) / सुहाई (becomes beautiful) / बिधि (fate) / बस (under control) / सुजन (good people) / कुसंगत (bad company) / परहीं (fall) / फनि (serpent) / मनि (jewel) / सम (like) / निज (own) / गुन (nature/qualities) / अनुसरहीं (follow)
ramacharitamanas::30.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::30.essence: Right company can transform the fallen, but true virtue keeps its own nature.
ramacharitamanas::30.simple_meaning: Bad people can improve through good company. Good people stay true to their nature even in harmful company and keep radiating goodness.
ramacharitamanas::30.simple_insight: The people around you matter, but a steady character is harder to shake than bad influence.
ramacharitamanas::30.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues explaining the power of saintly company. He says even a wicked person can सुधर through association with the good, while a truly good person remains unchanged even in corrupt company. The point is to show how powerful satsang really is.
ramacharitamanas::30.modern_relevance: You join a group chat where gossip is normal, and after a week you feel your own tone changing. Then one calm, principled friend walks in and the whole room lifts. Company shapes people, but character can outlast it.
ramacharitamanas::30.insight: It shifts attention from judging people by labels to noticing how association transforms conduct and reveals steady virtue.

ramacharitamanas::31.verse_sanskrit: बिधि हरि हर कबि कोबिद बानी। कहत साधु महिमा सकुचानी॥ सो मो सन कहि जात न कैसें। साक बनिक मनि गुन गन जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::31.verse_hindi: ब्रह्मा, विष्णु, शिव, कवि और पण्डितों की वाणी भी संत महिमा का वर्णन करने में सकुचाती है, वह मुझसे किस प्रकार नहीं कही जाती, जैसे साग-तरकारी बेचने वाले से मणियों के गुण समूह नहीं कहे जा सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::31.english_translation: Even Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, poets, and scholars hesitate to describe the greatness of the saint. How can I speak of it, like a vegetable seller explaining the qualities of jewels?
ramacharitamanas::31.translation_literal: बिधि (Brahma) / हरि (Vishnu, Ram) / हर (Shiva) / कबि (poets) / कोबिद (scholars) / बानी (speech) / कहत (speaking) / साधु (saints) / महिमा (greatness) / सकुचानी (hesitate, feel shy) / सो (that) / मो (to me) / सन (from) / कहि (tell) / जात (is going) / न (not) / कैसें (how) / साक बनिक (vegetable seller) / मनि (jewels) / गुन (qualities) / गन (group, collection) / जैसें (like)
ramacharitamanas::31.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::31.essence: Saintly greatness outruns every attempt to measure it.
ramacharitamanas::31.simple_meaning: The greatness of saintly people is beyond ordinary description. Even the highest beings and the wisest speakers fall short, so the poet humbly admits his own limits.
ramacharitamanas::31.simple_insight: It softens pride. Some things are not meant to be mastered by language, only respected with humility.
ramacharitamanas::31.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses in the Balkand to praise saints after describing the power of holy company. He says even Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, and learned poets cannot fully measure a saint's greatness, so his own speech can only bow before it.
ramacharitamanas::31.modern_relevance: You try to explain a mentor who changed your life, but every sentence feels too small. Some people cannot be reduced to a profile or a title; they can only be honored.
ramacharitamanas::31.insight: It shifts the mind from judging saintly character to approaching it with reverence and humility.

ramacharitamanas::32.verse_sanskrit: बंदउँ संत समान चित हित अनहित नहिं कोइ। अंजलि गत सुभ सुमन जिमि सम सुगंध कर दोइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::32.verse_hindi: मैं संतों को प्रणाम करता हूँ, जिनके चित्त में समता है, जिनका न कोई मित्र है और न शत्रु! जैसे अंजलि में रखे हुए सुंदर फूल (जिस हाथ ने फूलों को तोड़ा और जिसने उनको रखा उन) दोनों ही हाथों को समान रूप से सुगंधित करते हैं (वैसे ही संत शत्रु और मित्र दोनों का ही समान रूप से कल्याण करते हैं।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::32.english_translation: I bow to the saint whose mind is equal to friend and foe alike. Like flowers in folded hands, both hands are made fragrant together.
ramacharitamanas::32.translation_literal: बंदउँ (I bow) / संत (saints) / समान चित (equal-minded) / हित (friend) / अनहित (foe) / नहिं (not) / कोइ (anyone) / अंजलि (folded hands) / गत (placed) / सुभ (beautiful) / सुमन (flowers) / जिमि (like) / सम (equally) / सुगंध (fragrance) / कर (hands) / दोइ (both)
ramacharitamanas::32.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::32.essence: A balanced heart blesses friend and foe with the same fragrance.
ramacharitamanas::32.simple_meaning: A true saint does not divide people into friend and enemy. Their balanced heart brings benefit to everyone, just as flowers fragrance both hands that hold them.
ramacharitamanas::32.simple_insight: You can stop sorting people into sides and meet them with the same calm goodwill.
ramacharitamanas::32.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising the nature of saints after saying even great minds struggle to describe them. He now gives the clearest mark of sainthood: a mind so even that friend and foe are treated alike, and everyone touched by it is uplifted.
ramacharitamanas::32.modern_relevance: You read a message from someone who hurt you, then feel your chest tighten before you reply. This verse asks for a larger heart: respond without turning people into permanent enemies.
ramacharitamanas::32.insight: It shifts judgment into equal regard, so your response is guided by steadiness rather than preference.

ramacharitamanas::33.verse_sanskrit: संत सरल चित जगत हित जानि सुभाउ सनेहु। बालबिनय सुनि करि कृपा राम चरन रति देहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::33.verse_hindi: संत सरल हृदय और जगत के हितकारी होते हैं, उनके ऐसे स्वभाव और स्नेह को जानकर मैं विनय करता हूँ, मेरी इस बाल-विनय को सुनकर कृपा करके श्री रामजी के चरणों में मुझे प्रीति दें ॥
ramacharitamanas::33.english_translation: Saints are simple-hearted and seek the welfare of the world. Knowing their nature and affection, I humbly ask: hearing this childlike prayer, please grant me love for Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::33.translation_literal: संत (saints) / सरल (simple) / चित (mind/heart) / जगत (world) / हित (welfare) / जानि (knowing) / सुभाउ (nature) / सनेहु (affection/love) / बालबिनय (childlike prayer) / सुनि (hearing) / करि (doing) / कृपा (grace) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / रति (love/attachment) / देहु (give)
ramacharitamanas::33.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::33.essence: Saintly simplicity awakens love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::33.simple_meaning: True saints are simple, loving, and concerned for everyone’s good. Seeing that, the poet asks for grace to feel devotion to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::33.simple_insight: Real goodness softens the heart and makes devotion feel natural, not forced.
ramacharitamanas::33.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has just praised saints as equal-minded and free of enemies. Now he says their simple, benevolent nature shows the shape of holiness itself, and he asks that this childlike prayer draw him into love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::33.modern_relevance: You meet someone who never gossips, never competes, and somehow leaves everyone calmer. Their quiet kindness makes you want to become better, not louder.
ramacharitamanas::33.insight: It shifts admiration into practice: let noble company awaken devotion, not comparison.

ramacharitamanas::34.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि बंदि खल गन सतिभाएँ। जे बिनु काज दाहिनेहु बाएँ॥ पर हित हानि लाभ जिन्ह केरें। उजरें हरष बिषाद बसेरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::34.verse_hindi: अब मैं सच्चे भाव से दुष्टों को प्रणाम करता हूँ, जो बिना ही प्रयोजन, अपना हित करने वाले के भी प्रतिकूल आचरण करते हैं। दूसरों के हित की हानि ही जिनकी दृष्टि में लाभ है, जिनको दूसरों के उजड़ने में हर्ष और बसने में विषाद होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::34.english_translation: Again, I bow with sincere feeling to the wicked, who, without cause, act against even those who do them good. They count others' loss as gain; they rejoice when others are ruined and grieve when others prosper.
ramacharitamanas::34.translation_literal: बहुरि (again) / बंदि (bowing) / खल गन (the wicked) / सतिभाएँ (with true feeling) / जे (who) / बिनु काज (without cause) / दाहिनेहु (to the right-side, favorable) / बाएँ (to the left-side, hostile) / पर हित (others' welfare) / हानि (loss) / लाभ (gain) / जिन्ह केरें (for whom) / उजरें (ruin) / हरष (joy) / बिषाद (sorrow) / बसेरें (dwelling)
ramacharitamanas::34.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::34.essence: Even malice can be read clearly when you refuse to be swept away by it.
ramacharitamanas::34.simple_meaning: Even harmful people are acknowledged here. They oppose goodness for no reason, and they treat other people’s suffering as their own gain.
ramacharitamanas::34.simple_insight: You can stop taking hostility personally and see it as a sign of inner confusion.
ramacharitamanas::34.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening his praise with a surprising bow to the cruel and malicious, just after honoring the balanced and kind. He describes people who oppose good without reason, and whose joy rises from others' ruin. The point is to name a mind captured by distortion.
ramacharitamanas::34.modern_relevance: A colleague smiles while quietly blocking your work, then acts wounded when you succeed. The verse helps you see that some resistance is not about you — it is a mind addicted to comparison and harm.
ramacharitamanas::34.insight: It trains you to recognize distorted motives without getting pulled into their mood.

ramacharitamanas::35.verse_sanskrit: हरि हर जस राकेस राहु से। पर अकाज भट सहसबाहु से॥ जे पर दोष लखहिं सहसाखी। पर हित घृत जिन्ह के मन माखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::35.verse_hindi: जो हरि और हर के यश रूपी पूर्णिमा के चन्द्रमा के लिए राहु के समान हैं (अर्थात जहाँ कहीं भगवान विष्णु या शंकर के यश का वर्णन होता है, उसी में वे बाधा देते हैं) और दूसरों की बुराई करने में सहस्रबाहु के समान वीर हैं। जो दूसरों के दोषों को हजार आँखों से देखते हैं और दूसरों के हित रूपी घी के लिए जिनका मन मक्खी के समान है (अर्थात् जिस प्रकार मक्खी घी में गिरकर उसे खराब कर देती है और स्वयं भी मर जाती है, उसी प्रकार दुष्ट लोग दूसरों के बने-बनाए काम को अपनी हानि करके भी बिगाड़ देते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::35.english_translation: Like Rahu to the moon of Hari and Hara's fame, they are like Sahasrabahu in doing harm to others' work. They spot others' faults with a thousand eyes, and their mind is like a fly drawn to another's good like ghee, ruining it even at their own loss.
ramacharitamanas::35.translation_literal: हरि (Hari) / हर (Hara) / जस (fame) / राकेस (moon) / राहु (Rahu) / से (like) / पर (other) / अकाज (harmful deed) / भट (warrior) / सहसबाहु (Sahasrabahu) / से (like) / जे (who) / पर (other) / दोष (fault) / लखहिं (see) / सहसाखी (thousand-eyed) / पर हित (others' good) / घृत (ghee) / जिन्ह (whose) / के (of) / मन (mind) / माखी (fly)
ramacharitamanas::35.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::35.essence: Some minds cannot bear goodness, so they spoil it and call it insight.
ramacharitamanas::35.simple_meaning: Evil people block good work, obsess over others' faults, and ruin what helps others even when it harms themselves.
ramacharitamanas::35.simple_insight: It exposes the mind that feeds on criticism and destroys what it cannot create.
ramacharitamanas::35.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still describing the nature of the wicked in the opening movement of the Balkand. After praising the saints, he turns to those who oppose goodness itself: they hinder noble work, hunt for flaws, and spoil another's welfare even at their own expense.
ramacharitamanas::35.modern_relevance: A group chat turns sour because one person keeps hunting for flaws in every plan. The project stalls, morale drops, and even their own reputation takes the hit.
ramacharitamanas::35.insight: It trains you to recognize destructive criticism as a pattern of inner corruption, not just bad manners.

ramacharitamanas::36.verse_sanskrit: तेज कृसानु रोष महिषेसा। अघ अवगुन धन धनी धनेसा॥ उदय केत सम हित सबही के। कुंभकरन सम सोवत नीके ॥
ramacharitamanas::36.verse_hindi: जो तेज (दूसरों को जलाने वाले ताप) में अग्नि और क्रोध में यमराज के समान हैं, पाप और अवगुण रूपी धन में कुबेर के समान धनी हैं, जिनकी बढ़ती सभी के हित का नाश करने के लिए केतु (पुच्छल तारे) के समान है और जिनके कुम्भकर्ण की तरह सोते रहने में ही भलाई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::36.english_translation: They blaze like fire, rage like Yama, hoard evil and faults like Kubera hoards treasure, rise like a comet to ruin everyone’s good, and sleep well only like Kumbhakarna.
ramacharitamanas::36.translation_literal: तेज (radiance/heat) / कृसानु (fire) / रोष (anger) / महिषेसा (lord of death) । / अघ (sin) / अवगुन (faults) / धन (wealth) / धनी (rich) / धनेसा (lord of wealth) । / उदय (rising) / केत (comet) / सम (like) / हित (good) / सबही (of everyone) / के (of) । / कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / सम (like) / सोवत (sleeping) / नीके (well)
ramacharitamanas::36.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::36.essence: Destructive people poison even their rise, and peace comes only in their absence.
ramacharitamanas::36.simple_meaning: Evil people burn others with their presence, rage destructively, collect faults like treasure, and even their rise harms everyone. They rest only when they are asleep.
ramacharitamanas::36.simple_insight: It helps you see destructive character as a pattern, not a mystery.
ramacharitamanas::36.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is continuing his harsh portrait of the wicked in Balkand. After naming their harmful nature, he compares them to fire, death, wealth, a comet, and Kumbhakarna to show how their very presence, growth, and rest all serve harm rather than good.
ramacharitamanas::36.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose every comment leaves the room colder, whose success seems to create new damage, and whose silence is the only relief. The verse names that pattern without flinching.
ramacharitamanas::36.insight: It shifts the mind from moral confusion to clear seeing of destructive tendencies.

ramacharitamanas::37.verse_sanskrit: पर अकाजु लगि तनु परिहरहीं। जिमि हिम उपल कृषी दलि गरहीं॥ बंदउँ खल जस सेष सरोषा। सहस बदन बरनइ पर दोषा ॥
ramacharitamanas::37.verse_hindi: जैसे ओले खेती का नाश करके आप भी गल जाते हैं, वैसे ही वे दूसरों का काम बिगाड़ने के लिए अपना शरीर तक छोड़ देते हैं। मैं दुष्टों को (हजार मुख वाले) शेषजी के समान समझकर प्रणाम करता हूँ, जो पराए दोषों का हजार मुखों से बड़े रोष के साथ वर्णन करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::37.english_translation: Like hailstones that ruin crops and then melt away, such people ruin others' work and waste away their own bodies. I bow to the wicked, like Shesha with a thousand mouths, who angrily describe the faults of others with a thousand tongues.
ramacharitamanas::37.translation_literal: पर (for others) / अकाजु (harmful deed) / लगि (for the sake of) / तनु (body) / परिहरहीं (they abandon) / जिमि (like) / हिम (hail) / उपल (stones) / कृषी (crop) / दलि (destroying) / गरहीं (they melt away) / बंदउँ (I bow) / खल (wicked) / जस (like) / सेष (Shesha) / सरोषा (angrily) / सहस (thousand) / बदन (mouths) / बरनइ (describe) / पर (others') / दोषा (faults)
ramacharitamanas::37.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::37.essence: Malice destroys others and consumes the one who carries it.
ramacharitamanas::37.simple_meaning: People driven by malice ruin others even at the cost of their own well-being. They obsess over other people's faults and speak about them with anger.
ramacharitamanas::37.simple_insight: Malice always burns the one carrying it. Seeing that clearly makes judgment less tempting.
ramacharitamanas::37.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is in the middle of a string of comparisons about bad people. After praising harmful traits in earlier lines, he now shows how malice destroys both the target and the person who carries it. The verse is a supporting image in that larger catalogue.
ramacharitamanas::37.modern_relevance: A group chat turns into a pile-on, and someone keeps adding more fuel just to feel righteous. The room gets darker, but the person feeding it is the first to be scorched.
ramacharitamanas::37.insight: It shifts attention from blaming others to seeing how corrosive fault-finding becomes in the mind that repeats it.

ramacharitamanas::38.verse_sanskrit: पुनि प्रनवउँ पृथुराज समाना। पर अघ सुनइ सहस दस काना॥ बहुरि सक्र सम बिनवउँ तेही। संतत सुरानीक हित जेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::38.verse_hindi: पुनः उनको राजा पृथु (जिन्होंने भगवान का यश सुनने के लिए दस हजार कान माँगे थे) के समान जानकर प्रणाम करता हूँ, जो दस हजार कानों से दूसरों के पापों को सुनते हैं। फिर इन्द्र के समान मानकर उनकी विनय करता हूँ, जिनको सुरा (मदिरा) नीकी और हितकारी मालूम देती है (इन्द्र के लिए भी सुरानीक अर्थात् देवताओं की सेना हितकारी है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::38.english_translation: I bow again to the one like King Prithu, who hears others' faults with ten thousand ears. I bow again to the one like Indra, to whom the hosts of the gods seem always beneficial.
ramacharitamanas::38.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / प्रनवउँ (I bow) / पृथुराज (King Prithu) / समाना (like) / पर (others' ) / अघ (faults, sins) / सुनइ (hears) / सहस (thousand) / दस (ten) / काना (ears) ॥ बहुरि (again) / सक्र (Indra) / सम (like) / बिनवउँ (I pray/bow) / तेही (to that one) / संतत (always) / सुरानीक (hosts of gods) / हित (beneficial) / जेही (to whom) ॥
ramacharitamanas::38.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::38.essence: Corruption makes wrongdoing feel useful and other people's faults worth hearing.
ramacharitamanas::38.simple_meaning: The poet is mocking a corrupt person: he listens eagerly to others' faults and treats harmful things as useful.
ramacharitamanas::38.simple_insight: It exposes how vice distorts perception: the mind starts hearing wrong as right and harm as help.
ramacharitamanas::38.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues his denunciation of the wicked in Balkand. He says this person is like King Prithu in having countless ears for hearing others' faults, and like Indra in finding even harmful pleasures pleasing. The verse deepens the portrait of moral corruption.
ramacharitamanas::38.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with gossip, and one person leans in for every detail. What should have felt ugly starts feeling entertaining. This verse catches that slide before it hardens into habit.
ramacharitamanas::38.insight: It trains you to notice how craving can make bad things seem attractive and other people's flaws seem fascinating.

ramacharitamanas::39.verse_sanskrit: बचन बज्र जेहि सदा पिआरा। सहस नयन पर दोष निहारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::39.verse_hindi: जिनको कठोर वचन रूपी वज्र सदा प्यारा लगता है और जो हजार आँखों से दूसरों के दोषों को देखते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::39.english_translation: Those who love harsh words like thunder and see others' faults with a thousand eyes.
ramacharitamanas::39.translation_literal: बचन (words) / बज्र (thunderbolt) / जेहि (to whom) / सदा (always) / पिआरा (dear) / सहस (thousand) / नयन (eyes) / पर (others' ) / दोष (faults) / निहारा (see)
ramacharitamanas::39.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::39.essence: A cruel mind loves sharp speech and hunts for flaws.
ramacharitamanas::39.simple_meaning: Evil people enjoy harsh speech and constantly scan others for flaws.
ramacharitamanas::39.simple_insight: It warns you how bitterness trains the mind to hunt for faults.
ramacharitamanas::39.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the nature of the malicious person in a devotional passage. Such a person delights in cutting speech and uses endless scrutiny to find defects in others, setting up the contrast with the humble attitude that follows.
ramacharitamanas::39.modern_relevance: A group chat turns sour, and one person keeps replying with sharp jabs and instant criticism. The habit is not just rude; it trains the mind to live on fault-finding.
ramacharitamanas::39.insight: It shifts attention from judging others to noticing the aggression behind judgment.

ramacharitamanas::40.verse_sanskrit: उदासीन अरि मीत हित सुनत जरहिं खल रीति। जानि पानि जुग जोरि जन बिनती करइ सप्रीति ॥
ramacharitamanas::40.verse_hindi: दुष्टों की यह रीति है कि वे उदासीन, शत्रु अथवा मित्र, किसी का भी हित सुनकर जलते हैं। यह जानकर दोनों हाथ जोड़कर यह जन प्रेमपूर्वक उनसे विनय करता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::40.english_translation: The wicked burn even at hearing good done to the indifferent, enemy, or friend. Knowing this, this person bows with both hands joined and speaks with love.
ramacharitamanas::40.translation_literal: उदासीन (indifferent) / अरि (enemy) / मीत (friend) / हित (good, welfare) / सुनत (hearing) / जरहिं (burn) / खल (wicked) / रीति (nature, manner) / जानि (knowing) / पानि (hands) / जुग (pair) / जोरि (joining) / जन (this person) / बिनती (request, plea) / करइ (makes) / सप्रीति (with love)
ramacharitamanas::40.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::40.essence: Goodwill stays clean even when envy answers it.
ramacharitamanas::40.simple_meaning: Wicked people resent good news no matter who receives it. Knowing that, the speaker still offers a loving, respectful plea.
ramacharitamanas::40.simple_insight: You can stay gentle without being naive. Courtesy can remain intact even when others are hostile.
ramacharitamanas::40.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has just praised a listener who welcomes truth and rejects criticism of the good. He now adds a warning: some people burn at any mention of another’s welfare. Even so, he folds his hands and speaks with affection.
ramacharitamanas::40.modern_relevance: You share good news in a family group chat, and one person immediately twists it into envy. You do not have to answer with the same heat; you can stay respectful and clear.
ramacharitamanas::40.insight: It teaches you to meet hostility with composure, not imitation, and to keep your own manners clean.

ramacharitamanas::41.verse_sanskrit: मैं अपनी दिसि कीन्ह निहोरा। तिन्ह निज ओर न लाउब भोरा॥ बायस पलिअहिं अति अनुरागा। होहिं निरामिष कबहुँ कि कागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::41.verse_hindi: मैंने अपनी ओर से विनती की है, परन्तु वे अपनी ओर से कभी नहीं चूकेंगे। कौओं को बड़े प्रेम से पालिए, परन्तु वे क्या कभी मांस के त्यागी हो सकते हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::41.english_translation: I have pleaded from my side, but they will never turn from theirs. Feed crows with great affection, but can crows ever become meatless?
ramacharitamanas::41.translation_literal: मैं (I) / अपनी दिसि (from my side) / कीन्ह (made) / निहोरा (a plea) / तिन्ह (they) / निज ओर (their own side) / न लाउब (will not turn) / भोरा (foolishly / ever) / बायस (crows) / पलिअहिं (are fed / nurtured) / अति अनुरागा (with great affection) / होहिं (become) / निरामिष (without meat) / कबहुँ (ever) / कि (can) / कागा (crows)
ramacharitamanas::41.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::41.essence: Kindness does not remake a fixed nature.
ramacharitamanas::41.simple_meaning: A plea has been made, but stubborn people do not change. Affection cannot turn a crow into a meatless bird.
ramacharitamanas::41.simple_insight: Not everyone softens when treated kindly. Some natures stay fixed, and seeing that clearly saves needless hope.
ramacharitamanas::41.detailed_meaning: The speaker has already asked for peace, but expects no change from the other side. Using the image of crows, Tulsidas says some beings remain what they are, even under care and affection. The verse prepares the move toward judging both saintly and unworthy conduct.
ramacharitamanas::41.modern_relevance: You keep explaining yourself to someone who twists every word back into blame. At some point, clarity matters more than another attempt to be understood.
ramacharitamanas::41.insight: It teaches you to stop expecting transformation where only habit and nature are ruling.

ramacharitamanas::42.verse_sanskrit: बंदउँ संत असज्जन चरना। दुःखप्रद उभय बीच कछु बरना॥ बिछुरत एक प्रान हरि लेहीं। मिलत एक दुख दारुन देहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::42.verse_hindi: अब मैं संत और असंत दोनों के चरणों की वन्दना करता हूँ, दोनों ही दुःख देने वाले हैं, परन्तु उनमें कुछ अन्तर कहा गया है। वह अंतर यह है कि एक (संत) तो बिछुड़ते समय प्राण हर लेते हैं और दूसरे (असंत) मिलते हैं, तब दारुण दुःख देते हैं। (अर्थात् संतों का बिछुड़ना मरने के समान दुःखदायी होता है और असंतों का मिलना।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::42.english_translation: I bow to the feet of saints and the wicked alike. Both bring pain, yet in different ways: separation from a saint feels like losing one’s life, while meeting the wicked brings terrible suffering.
ramacharitamanas::42.translation_literal: बंदउँ (I bow) / संत (saints) / असज्जन (the wicked) / चरना (feet) / दुःखप्रद (pain-giving) / उभय (both) / बीच (between) / कछु (some) / बरना (to describe) / बिछुरत (upon separation) / एक (one) / प्रान (life) / हरि (take away) / लेहीं (they take) / मिलत (upon meeting) / एक (one) / दुख (pain) / दारुन (terrible) / देहीं (they give)
ramacharitamanas::42.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::42.essence: The right company feels like life; the wrong company feels like injury.
ramacharitamanas::42.simple_meaning: Saints and wicked people both affect you deeply, but in opposite ways. Losing the company of a saint feels unbearable, while meeting the wicked brings harsh suffering.
ramacharitamanas::42.simple_insight: It helps you value the company that uplifts you and stay alert to what drains you.
ramacharitamanas::42.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses his narration to compare two kinds of company. A saint’s absence feels like life leaving the body; a wicked person’s presence creates immediate pain. The teaching prepares the reader to see why association matters so much.
ramacharitamanas::42.modern_relevance: You leave a mentor’s house after an honest conversation and feel strangely hollow, then spend ten minutes with someone toxic and feel your chest tighten. Company changes the shape of the mind.
ramacharitamanas::42.insight: It shifts attention toward the quality of association, not just the content of conversation.

ramacharitamanas::43.verse_sanskrit: उपजहिं एक संग जग माहीं। जलज जोंक जिमि गुन बिलगाहीं॥ सुधा सुरा सम साधु असाधू। जनक एक जग जलधि अगाधू ॥
ramacharitamanas::43.verse_hindi: दोनों (संत और असंत) जगत में एक साथ पैदा होते हैं, पर (एक साथ पैदा होने वाले) कमल और जोंक की तरह उनके गुण अलग-अलग होते हैं। (कमल दर्शन और स्पर्श से सुख देता है, किन्तु जोंक शरीर का स्पर्श पाते ही रक्त चूसने लगती है।) साधु अमृत के समान (मृत्यु रूपी संसार से उबारने वाला) और असाधु मदिरा के समान (मोह, प्रमाद और जड़ता उत्पन्न करने वाला) है, दोनों को उत्पन्न करने वाला जगत रूपी अगाध समुद्र एक ही है। (शास्त्रों में समुद्रमन्थन से ही अमृत और मदिरा दोनों की उत्पत्ति बताई गई है।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::43.english_translation: Saints and unholy people arise together in the world, yet their qualities differ like a lotus and a leech. The saint is like nectar and the unholy like liquor; both come from the same vast ocean of the world.
ramacharitamanas::43.translation_literal: उपजहिं (arise) / एक संग (together) / जग माहीं (in the world) / जलज (lotus) / जोंक (leech) / जिमि (like) / गुन (qualities) / बिलगाहीं (differ) / सुधा (nectar) / सुरा (liquor) / सम (equal) / साधु (saint) / असाधू (unholy) / जनक (source) / एक (one) / जग जलधि (world-ocean) / अगाधू (bottomless, vast)
ramacharitamanas::43.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::43.essence: Shared origin does not make shared character.
ramacharitamanas::43.simple_meaning: Good and bad people can come from the same world, but their nature is completely different. One gives nourishment; the other drains and harms.
ramacharitamanas::43.simple_insight: You can stop being fooled by appearances and look for character instead.
ramacharitamanas::43.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is reflecting on saints and unholy people after praising both. He says they may appear in the same world, yet their nature is as different as a lotus and a leech, or nectar and liquor. The shared source does not make their qualities equal.
ramacharitamanas::43.modern_relevance: Two coworkers may come from the same office, the same training, even the same family culture. One leaves people steadier; the other leaves them depleted. Shared background never guarantees shared character.
ramacharitamanas::43.insight: It shifts attention from origin to nature, teaching you to judge by effect rather than by surface similarity.

ramacharitamanas::44.verse_sanskrit: भल अनभल निज निज करतूती। लहत सुजस अपलोक बिभूती॥ सुधा सुधाकर सुरसरि साधू। गरल अनल कलिमल सरि ब्याधू ॥ गुन अवगुन जानत सब कोई। जो जेहि भाव नीक तेहि सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::44.verse_hindi: भले और बुरे अपनी-अपनी करनी के अनुसार सुंदर यश और अपयश की सम्पत्ति पाते हैं। अमृत, चन्द्रमा, गंगाजी और साधु एवं विष, अग्नि, कलियुग के पापों की नदी अर्थात् कर्मनाशा और हिंसा करने वाला व्याध, इनके गुण-अवगुण सब कोई जानते हैं, किन्तु जिसे जो भाता है, उसे वही अच्छा लगता है॥4-5॥
ramacharitamanas::44.english_translation: The good and the bad reap fame or disgrace according to their own deeds. Everyone knows the qualities and faults of nectar, the moon, the Ganges, the virtuous, poison, fire, the river of sins, and the hunter. Yet each person favors what pleases them.
ramacharitamanas::44.translation_literal: भल (good) / अनभल (bad) / निज निज (each one's own) / करतूती (deeds) / लहत (receive) / सुजस (good fame) / अपलोक (bad fame) / बिभूती (wealth) ॥ सुधा (nectar) / सुधाकर (moon) / सुरसरि (Ganges) / साधू (virtuous) / गरल (poison) / अनल (fire) / कलिमल (sins of Kali age) / सरि (river) / ब्याधू (hunter) ॥ गुन (qualities) / अवगुन (faults) / जानत (know) / सब कोई (everyone) / जो जेहि (whatever to whom) / भाव (pleases) / नीक (good) / तेहि सोई (that alone)
ramacharitamanas::44.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::44.essence: Knowing right from wrong does not stop desire from choosing.
ramacharitamanas::44.simple_meaning: People receive praise or blame according to their own actions. Everyone knows what is good or harmful, yet they still prefer what suits their liking.
ramacharitamanas::44.simple_insight: It feels sobering: knowing the difference is not the same as living it.
ramacharitamanas::44.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues his reflection on saintly and unholy people. He says their deeds bring their own results, and even when everyone knows what is wholesome or harmful, personal liking still bends judgment.
ramacharitamanas::44.modern_relevance: You know the third late-night drink will wreck your sleep, yet you reach for it anyway. Clear seeing is not the same as clear choosing.
ramacharitamanas::44.insight: It shifts attention from public opinion to the inner habit that keeps choosing what it already likes.

ramacharitamanas::45.verse_sanskrit: भलो भलाइहि पै लहइ लहइ निचाइहि नीचु। सुधा सराहिअ अमरताँ गरल सराहिअ मीचु ॥
ramacharitamanas::45.verse_hindi: भला भलाई ही ग्रहण करता है और नीच नीचता को ही ग्रहण किए रहता है। अमृत की सराहना अमर करने में होती है और विष की मारने में ॥
ramacharitamanas::45.english_translation: The good take in goodness; the lowly keep lowliness. Nectar is praised for making one immortal, poison for killing.
ramacharitamanas::45.translation_literal: भलो (good) / भलाइहि (goodness) / पै (indeed) / लहइ (takes) / लहइ (takes) / निचाइहि (lowliness) / नीचु (lowly) / सुधा (nectar) / सराहिअ (is praised) / अमरताँ (for immortality) / गरल (poison) / सराहिअ (is praised) / मीचु (for death)
ramacharitamanas::45.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::45.essence: Nature pulls in its own kind of result.
ramacharitamanas::45.simple_meaning: A person tends to receive what matches their nature. Goodness leads to good results, while poison leads to harm.
ramacharitamanas::45.simple_insight: Your character shapes what you can truly hold onto.
ramacharitamanas::45.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is explaining moral likeness through simple images after describing how saints and the wicked differ in the world. The point is that each nature naturally attracts its own kind of result, just as nectar preserves life and poison destroys it.
ramacharitamanas::45.modern_relevance: You keep returning to the same kind of friends, the same habits, the same mess. What you nurture in yourself decides what your life keeps feeding back to you.
ramacharitamanas::45.insight: It shifts attention from blaming circumstances to examining the quality you are cultivating.

ramacharitamanas::46.verse_sanskrit: खल अघ अगुन साधु गुन गाहा। उभय अपार उदधि अवगाहा॥ तेहि तें कछु गुन दोष बखाने। संग्रह त्याग न बिनु पहिचाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::46.verse_hindi: दुष्टों के पापों और अवगुणों की और साधुओं के गुणों की कथाएँ- दोनों ही अपार और अथाह समुद्र हैं। इसी से कुछ गुण और दोषों का वर्णन किया गया है, क्योंकि बिना पहचाने उनका ग्रहण या त्याग नहीं हो सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::46.english_translation: The tales of the wicked's faults and the saintly's virtues are both unfathomable oceans. So a few qualities and faults are described, because no one can accept or reject what is not recognized.
ramacharitamanas::46.translation_literal: खल (wicked) / अघ (sins) / अगुन (faults) / साधु (saintly) / गुन (virtues) / गाहा (tales) / उभय (both) / अपार (boundless) / उदधि (ocean) / अवगाहा (unfathomable) / तेहि तें (therefore) / कछु (some) / गुन (virtues) / दोष (faults) / बखाने (described) / संग्रह (acceptance) / त्याग (rejection) / न (not) / बिनु (without) / पहिचाने (recognizing)
ramacharitamanas::46.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::46.essence: Recognition must come before acceptance or rejection.
ramacharitamanas::46.simple_meaning: Good and bad qualities are both vast and hard to fully measure. We name a few so people can know what to accept and what to avoid.
ramacharitamanas::46.simple_insight: Clear seeing comes before wise choice. You cannot choose well until you can tell what is what.
ramacharitamanas::46.detailed_meaning: The narrator pauses in Balkand to explain a general principle before the story moves on. Human goodness and wrongdoing are both too vast to fully map, so scripture points out enough signs for readers to recognize, accept, or reject with discernment.
ramacharitamanas::46.modern_relevance: You meet someone polished in public and cruel in private, and your first impression wobbles. This verse says: don’t rush. Learn the signs before you trust, keep, or cut away.
ramacharitamanas::46.insight: It trains the mind to recognize patterns before making moral judgments or life choices.

ramacharitamanas::47.verse_sanskrit: भलेउ पोच सब बिधि उपजाए। गनि गुन दोष बेद बिलगाए॥ कहहिं बेद इतिहास पुराना। बिधि प्रपंचु गुन अवगुन साना ॥
ramacharitamanas::47.verse_hindi: भले-बुरे सभी ब्रह्मा के पैदा किए हुए हैं, पर गुण और दोषों को विचार कर वेदों ने उनको अलग-अलग कर दिया है। वेद, इतिहास और पुराण कहते हैं कि ब्रह्मा की यह सृष्टि गुण-अवगुणों से सनी हुई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::47.english_translation: The good and the bad are all created by Brahma, but the Vedas separate them by weighing their qualities and faults. The Vedas, Itihasa, and Puranas say that Brahma's creation is filled with qualities and faults.
ramacharitamanas::47.translation_literal: भलेउ (good) / पोच (base) / सब (all) / बिधि (Brahma) / उपजाए (created) / गनि (counting, weighing) / गुन (qualities) / दोष (faults) / बेद (Vedas) / बिलगाए (separated) ॥ कहहिं (say) / बेद (Vedas) / इतिहास (Itihasa) / पुराना (Puranas) / बिधि (Brahma's) / प्रपंचु (world-display, creation) / गुन (qualities) / अवगुन (faults) / साना (mixed, filled) ॥
ramacharitamanas::47.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::47.essence: The world is mixed; clear seeing separates what is worth keeping from what is not.
ramacharitamanas::47.simple_meaning: Creation contains both excellence and flaw. Sacred teaching does not deny that mix; it helps you see and sort it clearly.
ramacharitamanas::47.simple_insight: You stop expecting purity from the world and start seeing it accurately.
ramacharitamanas::47.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is widening the lens after saying good and bad are both present everywhere. He points to the Vedas, Itihasa, and Puranas as guides that help the reader judge qualities and faults without confusion.
ramacharitamanas::47.modern_relevance: You open a news app and feel everything is either heroic or corrupt. Then you remember: real life is mixed. Clear seeing means not flattening people, events, or yourself into one label.
ramacharitamanas::47.insight: It trains the mind to distinguish mixed reality instead of reacting with simplistic praise or blame.

ramacharitamanas::48.verse_sanskrit: दुख सुख पाप पुन्य दिन राती। साधु असाधु सुजाति कुजाती॥ दानव देव ऊँच अरु नीचू। अमिअ सुजीवनु माहुरु मीचू ॥ माया ब्रह्म जीव जगदीसा। लच्छि अलच्छि रंक अवनीसा॥ कासी मग सुरसरि क्रमनासा। मरु मारव महिदेव गवासा ॥ सरग नरक अनुराग बिरागा। निगमागम गुन दोष बिभागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::48.verse_hindi: दुःख-सुख, पाप-पुण्य, दिन-रात, साधु-असाधु, सुजाति-कुजाति, दानव-देवता, ऊँच-नीच, अमृत-विष, सुजीवन (सुंदर जीवन)-मृत्यु, माया-ब्रह्म, जीव-ईश्वर, सम्पत्ति-दरिद्रता, रंक-राजा, काशी-मगध, गंगा-कर्मनाशा, मारवाड़-मालवा, ब्राह्मण-कसाई, स्वर्ग-नरक, अनुराग-वैराग्य (ये सभी पदार्थ ब्रह्मा की सृष्टि में हैं।) वेद-शास्त्रों ने उनके गुण-दोषों का विभाग कर दिया है॥3-5॥
ramacharitamanas::48.english_translation: Pain and pleasure, sin and merit, day and night, the good and the bad, noble birth and low birth, demons and radiant beings, high and low, nectar and poison, life-giving and deadly, illusion and the supreme reality, the individual and the lord of the world, wealth and poverty, beggar and king, Kashi and Magadh, the Ganga and the Karmanasha, Marwar and Malwa, priest and butcher, heaven and lower realm, attachment and detachment, all are part of creation. The Vedas and scriptures divide their qualities and faults.
ramacharitamanas::48.translation_literal: दुख (pain) / सुख (pleasure) / पाप (sin) / पुन्य (merit) / दिन (day) / राती (night) / साधु (good) / असाधु (bad) / सुजाति (noble birth) / कुजाती (low birth) / दानव (demon) / देव (radiant being) / ऊँच (high) / अरु (and) / नीचू (low) / अमिअ (nectar) / सुजीवनु (life-giving) / माहुरु (poison) / मीचू (deadly) / माया (illusion) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / जीव (individual) / जगदीसा (lord of the world) / लच्छि (wealth) / अलच्छि (poverty) / रंक (beggar) / अवनीसा (king) / कासी (Kashi) / मग (Magadh) / सुरसरि (Ganga) / क्रमनासा (Karmanasha) / मरु (Marwar) / मारव (Marwar) / महिदेव (priest) / गवासा (butcher) / सरग (heaven) / नरक (lower realm) / अनुराग (attachment) / बिरागा (detachment) / निगमागम (Vedas and scriptures) / गुन (qualities) / दोष (faults) / बिभागा (division)
ramacharitamanas::48.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::48.essence: Opposites are built into creation; wisdom is learning their difference.
ramacharitamanas::48.simple_meaning: The world contains every opposite: joy and sorrow, virtue and fault, wealth and poverty, attachment and detachment. Sacred teaching does not erase these pairs; it helps you recognize and distinguish them.
ramacharitamanas::48.simple_insight: You do not need to deny life’s opposites. Clear seeing begins when you stop confusing them.
ramacharitamanas::48.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is explaining the structure of the world itself, not telling a story event. Creation contains every pair of opposites, from pleasure and pain to attachment and detachment. The scriptures do not deny this mixed world; they sort and name it so a seeker can see clearly.
ramacharitamanas::48.modern_relevance: You are scrolling through a feed where one post feels inspiring and the next feels cruel. Instead of collapsing into confusion, you can notice: both belong to the same world, but they are not the same thing.
ramacharitamanas::48.insight: It trains the mind to distinguish without denial: to see mixed reality clearly instead of demanding a world with only one side.

ramacharitamanas::49.verse_sanskrit: जड़ चेतन गुन दोषमय बिस्व कीन्ह करतार। संत हंस गुन गहहिं पय परिहरि बारि बिकार ॥
ramacharitamanas::49.verse_hindi: विधाता ने इस जड़-चेतन विश्व को गुण-दोषमय रचा है, किन्तु संत रूपी हंस दोष रूपी जल को छोड़कर गुण रूपी दूध को ही ग्रहण करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::49.english_translation: The creator made this world of inert and conscious beings, full of virtues and faults. Saints, like swans, take the milk and leave the water's impurities.
ramacharitamanas::49.translation_literal: जड़ (inert) / चेतन (conscious) / गुन (qualities) / दोषमय (full of faults) / बिस्व (world) / कीन्ह (made) / करतार (the creator) / संत (saints) / हंस (swans) / गुन (qualities) / गहहिं (grasp) / पय (milk) / परिहरि (leaving aside) / बारि (water) / बिकार (impurity)
ramacharitamanas::49.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::49.essence: Wisdom keeps the essence and leaves the impurity behind.
ramacharitamanas::49.simple_meaning: The world contains both good and bad. Wise people notice the difference and hold on to what is valuable while letting the rest pass away.
ramacharitamanas::49.simple_insight: You do not have to absorb everything around you. Discernment lets you keep what nourishes and drop what pollutes.
ramacharitamanas::49.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses the story to explain how the world works. Creation contains both qualities and flaws, but saints are like swans: they separate the nourishing from the impure. That discernment becomes the basis for the next teaching.
ramacharitamanas::49.modern_relevance: You open a comment thread full of praise, cruelty, half-truths, and one useful idea. You do not have to swallow all of it. Keep the useful part and let the rest sink.
ramacharitamanas::49.insight: It trains the mind to separate value from noise instead of reacting to everything as equal.

ramacharitamanas::50.verse_sanskrit: अस बिबेक जब देइ बिधाता। तब तजि दोष गुनहिं मनु राता॥ काल सुभाउ करम बरिआईं। भलेउ प्रकृति बस चुकइ भलाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::50.verse_hindi: विधाता जब इस प्रकार का (हंस का सा) विवेक देते हैं, तब दोषों को छोड़कर मन गुणों में अनुरक्त होता है। काल स्वभाव और कर्म की प्रबलता से भले लोग (साधु) भी माया के वश में होकर कभी-कभी भलाई से चूक जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::50.english_translation: When the creator grants this kind of clear seeing, the mind turns away from faults and rests in virtues. Yet time, nature, and the force of action are so strong that even good people sometimes miss the good and fall under appearance.
ramacharitamanas::50.translation_literal: अस (such) / बिबेक (clear seeing) / जब (when) / देइ (gives) / बिधाता (the creator) / तब (then) / तजि (leaving) / दोष (faults) / गुनहिं (in virtues) / मनु (the mind) / राता (absorbed) ॥ / काल (time) / सुभाउ (nature) / करम (action) / बरिआईं (strength, force) / भलेउ (even the good) / प्रकृति (nature) / बस (under control) / चुकइ (misses, slips) / भलाईं (the good) ॥
ramacharitamanas::50.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::50.essence: Clear seeing helps, but even good people can still slip.
ramacharitamanas::50.simple_meaning: Clear seeing lets the mind choose virtues over faults. But time, nature, and past action can still pull even good people off course.
ramacharitamanas::50.simple_insight: It softens self-blame and sharpens humility: even goodness needs vigilance.
ramacharitamanas::50.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues the reflection on the world’s mixed nature. After the hamsa image, he says that true discernment lets a person hold to what is good, yet even noble people can slip when time, nature, and action press on them.
ramacharitamanas::50.modern_relevance: You meant well, but stress, habit, and old patterns still hijacked your best intentions. The verse names that failure without excuse, and without cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::50.insight: It teaches you to expect weakness without romanticising it, and to keep choosing what is good anyway.

ramacharitamanas::51.verse_sanskrit: सो सुधारि हरिजन जिमि लेहीं। दलि दुख दोष बिमल जसु देहीं॥ खलउ करहिं भल पाइ सुसंगू। मिटइ न मलिन सुभाउ अभंगू ॥
ramacharitamanas::51.verse_hindi: भगवान के भक्त जैसे उस चूक को सुधार लेते हैं और दुःख-दोषों को मिटाकर निर्मल यश देते हैं, वैसे ही दुष्ट भी कभी-कभी उत्तम संग पाकर भलाई करते हैं, परन्तु उनका कभी भंग न होने वाला मलिन स्वभाव नहीं मिटता ॥
ramacharitamanas::51.english_translation: As devotees correct their faults and give pure fame by removing sorrow and defects, so even the wicked may do good in good company; yet their ingrained dark nature does not disappear.
ramacharitamanas::51.translation_literal: सो (thus) / सुधारि (correcting) / हरिजन (the divine’s people, devotees) / जिमि (as) / लेहीं (take, accept) / दलि (crushing) / दुख (sorrow) / दोष (faults) / बिमल (pure) / जसु (fame) / देहीं (give) // खलउ (even the wicked) / करहिं (do) / भल (good) / पाइ (having found) / सुसंगू (good company) / मिटइ (is erased) / न (not) / मलिन (dark, impure) / सुभाउ (nature) / अभंगू (unbroken, lasting)
ramacharitamanas::51.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::51.essence: Good company can polish conduct, but it cannot instantly erase a hardened nature.
ramacharitamanas::51.simple_meaning: Good company can help even bad people do some good, but a deeply rooted bad nature does not disappear quickly.
ramacharitamanas::51.simple_insight: Not every improvement is transformation. Some changes are real, but the deepest habits may still remain underneath.
ramacharitamanas::51.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand teaching on how character is formed, Tulsidas compares true devotees and flawed people. Devotees can correct faults and shine with pure reputation, while even the wicked may act well in good company. But their hardened nature still clings.
ramacharitamanas::51.modern_relevance: Someone can act decent at a retreat, in therapy, or around respected friends, then return home and fall back into the same pattern. Environment matters, but it does not erase the deeper habit overnight.
ramacharitamanas::51.insight: It shifts attention from temporary improvement to the harder work of changing the underlying pattern.

ramacharitamanas::52.verse_sanskrit: लखि सुबेष जग बंचक जेऊ। बेष प्रताप पूजिअहिं तेऊ॥ उघरहिं अंत न होइ निबाहू। कालनेमि जिमि रावन राहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::52.verse_hindi: जो (वेषधारी) ठग हैं, उन्हें भी अच्छा (साधु का सा) वेष बनाए देखकर वेष के प्रताप से जगत पूजता है, परन्तु एक न एक दिन वे चौड़े आ ही जाते हैं, अंत तक उनका कपट नहीं निभता, जैसे कालनेमि, रावण और राहु का हाल हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::52.english_translation: People may honor a false appearance when they see a fine disguise, but deception cannot last. In the end, it is exposed, as with Kalanemi, Ravana, and Rahu.
ramacharitamanas::52.translation_literal: लखि (seeing) / सुबेष (fine disguise) / जग (the world) / बंचक (deceivers) / जेऊ (those) । / बेष (appearance) / प्रताप (power, splendor) / पूजिअहिं (are honored) / तेऊ (they) ॥ / उघरहिं (are exposed) / अंत (in the end) / न होइ (does not happen) / निबाहू (continuance, lasting) । / कालनेमि (Kalanemi) / जिमि (like) / रावन (Ravana) / राहू (Rahu) ॥
ramacharitamanas::52.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::52.essence: A pleasing disguise can win honor, but deception always breaks.
ramacharitamanas::52.simple_meaning: A good-looking disguise can win respect for a while, but falsehood does not last. In time, deception is revealed.
ramacharitamanas::52.simple_insight: A polished mask can fool people briefly, but reality always catches up.
ramacharitamanas::52.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, Tulsidas is warning that a pleasing outer form can make even deceivers look worthy for a time. But Kalanemi, Ravana, and Rahu stand as examples of masks that eventually fail, because falsehood cannot endure.
ramacharitamanas::52.modern_relevance: A charming speaker walks into the room in a crisp suit, says all the right things, and everyone relaxes. Weeks later, the pattern cracks. The image held for a while; the character did not.
ramacharitamanas::52.insight: It trains you to look past appearances and judge by what remains when the mask slips.

ramacharitamanas::53.verse_sanskrit: किएहुँ कुबेषु साधु सनमानू। जिमि जग जामवंत हनुमानू॥ हानि कुसंग सुसंगति लाहू। लोकहुँ बेद बिदित सब काहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::53.verse_hindi: बुरा वेष बना लेने पर भी साधु का सम्मान ही होता है, जैसे जगत में जाम्बवान् और हनुमान् जी का हुआ। बुरे संग से हानि और अच्छे संग से लाभ होता है, यह बात लोक और वेद में है और सभी लोग इसको जानते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::53.english_translation: Even a bad disguise still receives the honor due to a saint, as the world honored Jambavan and Hanuman. Loss comes from bad company, gain from good company. This is known in both worldly life and the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::53.translation_literal: किएहुँ (even after doing) / कुबेषु (bad disguise) / साधु (saintly) / सनमानू (respect) / जिमि (like) / जग (world) / जामवंत (Jambavan) / हनुमानू (Hanuman) / हानि (loss) / कुसंग (bad company) / सुसंगति (good company) / लाहू (gain) / लोकहुँ (in the world) / बेद (the Vedas) / बिदित (known) / सब (all) / काहू (by anyone)
ramacharitamanas::53.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::53.essence: Company quietly shapes character more than appearance does.
ramacharitamanas::53.simple_meaning: A person is shaped by the company they keep. Good company brings benefit; bad company brings harm.
ramacharitamanas::53.simple_insight: You are not just choosing people. You are choosing the direction your life takes.
ramacharitamanas::53.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, Tulsidas pauses the story to teach a general truth through examples like Jambavan and Hanuman. Even a false outer appearance can draw respect, but the deeper point is sharper: companionship changes character, and everyone knows it.
ramacharitamanas::53.modern_relevance: You leave a room after two hours with one friend feeling lighter, and after two hours with another feeling strangely smaller. The verse names that difference: company is never neutral.
ramacharitamanas::53.insight: It shifts attention from judging appearances to noticing the moral force of relationships.

ramacharitamanas::54.verse_sanskrit: गगन चढ़इ रज पवन प्रसंगा। कीचहिं मिलइ नीच जल संगा॥ साधु असाधु सदन सुक सारीं। सुमिरहिं राम देहिं गनि गारीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::54.verse_hindi: पवन के संग से धूल आकाश पर चढ़ जाती है और वही नीच (नीचे की ओर बहने वाले) जल के संग से कीचड़ में मिल जाती है। साधु के घर के तोता-मैना राम-राम सुमिरते हैं और असाधु के घर के तोता-मैना गिन-गिनकर गालियाँ देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::54.english_translation: Dust rises into the sky with the help of the wind, and mud forms when it joins low water. Parrots and mynas in the homes of the good keep repeating Ram's name, while parrots and mynas in the homes of the bad keep counting out insults.
ramacharitamanas::54.translation_literal: गगन (sky) / चढ़इ (rises) / रज (dust) / पवन (wind) / प्रसंगा (through association) / कीचहिं (into mud) / मिलइ (joins) / नीच (low) / जल (water) / संगा (with association) / साधु (good) / असाधु (bad) / सदन (homes) / सुक (parrots) / सारीं (mynas) / सुमिरहिं (remember/recite) / राम (Ram) / देहिं (give) / गनि (counting) / गारीं (abuses)
ramacharitamanas::54.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::54.essence: Association decides whether the same nature rises or sinks.
ramacharitamanas::54.simple_meaning: The kind of company you keep changes how you speak, think, and live. Good company lifts you upward; bad company pulls you down.
ramacharitamanas::54.simple_insight: You are shaped by the atmosphere around you, often more than by intention alone.
ramacharitamanas::54.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas compares dust and water to show how association changes nature: one rises with wind, the other becomes mud. Then he points to a simple household sign — birds in a good home repeat Ram's name, while birds in a bad home learn abuse.
ramacharitamanas::54.modern_relevance: A child repeats the language heard at home. A group chat can make you kinder or crueler without you noticing. The verse warns that your surroundings are teaching you all the time.
ramacharitamanas::54.insight: It shifts attention from isolated willpower to the quality of the environment you repeatedly enter.

ramacharitamanas::55.verse_sanskrit: धूम कुसंगति कारिख होई। लिखिअ पुरान मंजु मसि सोई॥ सोइ जल अनल अनिल संघाता। होइ जलद जग जीवन दाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::55.verse_hindi: कुसंग के कारण धुआँ कालिख कहलाता है, वही धुआँ (सुसंग से) सुंदर स्याही होकर पुराण लिखने के काम में आता है और वही धुआँ जल, अग्नि और पवन के संग से बादल होकर जगत को जीवन देने वाला बन जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::55.english_translation: Through bad company, smoke becomes soot. In good use, that same soot becomes beautiful ink for writing the Puranas. The same smoke, joined with water, fire, and wind, becomes a cloud that gives life to the world.
ramacharitamanas::55.translation_literal: धूम (smoke) / कुसंगति (bad company) / कारिख (soot) / होई (becomes) / लिखिअ (is written) / पुरान (Puranas) / मंजु (beautiful) / मसि (ink) / सोई (that same) / सोइ (that same) / जल (water) / अनल (fire) / अनिल (wind) / संघाता (with union) / होइ (becomes) / जलद (cloud) / जग (world) / जीवन (life) / दाता (giver)
ramacharitamanas::55.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::55.essence: Association can stain, refine, or transform the same thing.
ramacharitamanas::55.simple_meaning: Bad company turns a thing ugly and useless, but the same thing can become useful and life-giving in the right company.
ramacharitamanas::55.simple_insight: What surrounds you can change your whole nature for better or worse.
ramacharitamanas::55.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is building a lesson about association through images from nature. Smoke can stain as soot, serve as ink for sacred writing, or become a cloud that brings rain. The point is that contact shapes character and use.
ramacharitamanas::55.modern_relevance: A friend group starts normalizing gossip, late-night chaos, and shortcuts. The same person who felt clear a month ago now feels dull and reactive. Environment is not background — it is formation.
ramacharitamanas::55.insight: It shifts attention from judging things alone to seeing how company changes their effect.

ramacharitamanas::56.verse_sanskrit: ग्रह भेजष जल पवन पट पाइ कुजोग सुजोग। होहिं कुबस्तु सुबस्तु जग लखहिं सुलच्छन लोग ॥
ramacharitamanas::56.verse_hindi: ग्रह, औषधि, जल, वायु और वस्त्र- ये सब भी कुसंग और सुसंग पाकर संसार में बुरे और भले पदार्थ हो जाते हैं। चतुर एवं विचारशील पुरुष ही इस बात को जान पाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::56.english_translation: Planets, medicine, water, wind, and cloth become bad or good through bad company or good company. Wise people alone can see this.
ramacharitamanas::56.translation_literal: ग्रह (planets) / भेजष (medicine) / जल (water) / पवन (wind) / पट (cloth) / पाइ (having obtained) / कुजोग (bad association) / सुजोग (good association) / होहिं (become) / कुबस्तु (bad thing) / सुबस्तु (good thing) / जग (world) / लखहिं (see) / सुलच्छन (wise, discerning) / लोग (people)
ramacharitamanas::56.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::56.essence: Association can turn even neutral things harmful or beneficial.
ramacharitamanas::56.simple_meaning: Even neutral things can become harmful or helpful depending on the company they keep. Wise people understand how surroundings change character.
ramacharitamanas::56.simple_insight: You start noticing that context shapes character, not just intention.
ramacharitamanas::56.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still teaching through examples about bad and good association. After smoke, dust, and water, he widens the point: even planets, medicine, water, wind, and cloth change their effect through contact. The lesson is that company transforms nature.
ramacharitamanas::56.modern_relevance: A calm habit breaks down after a few nights with people who mock it. A helpful routine suddenly feels toxic in a chaotic room. The verse reminds you that environment quietly edits character.
ramacharitamanas::56.insight: It shifts attention from judging things in isolation to noticing the influence of surroundings and association.

ramacharitamanas::57.verse_sanskrit: सम प्रकास तम पाख दुहुँ नाम भेद बिधि कीन्ह। ससि सोषक पोषक समुझि जग जस अपजस दीन्ह ॥
ramacharitamanas::57.verse_hindi: महीने के दोनों पखवाड़ों में उजियाला और अँधेरा समान ही रहता है, परन्तु विधाता ने इनके नाम में भेद कर दिया है (एक का नाम शुक्ल और दूसरे का नाम कृष्ण रख दिया)। एक को चन्द्रमा का बढ़ाने वाला और दूसरे को उसका घटाने वाला समझकर जगत ने एक को सुयश और दूसरे को अपयश दे दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::57.english_translation: The bright half and the dark half are equal in light and darkness, yet the creator gave them different names. Seeing one as the moon’s nourisher and the other as its diminisher, the world gave one fame and the other blame.
ramacharitamanas::57.translation_literal: सम (equal) / प्रकास (light) / तम (darkness) / पाख (fortnight) / दुहुँ (both) / नाम (names) / भेद (difference) / बिधि (the creator) / कीन्ह (made) / ससि (moon) / सोषक (one that drains) / पोषक (one that nourishes) / समुझि (understanding) / जग (the world) / जस (fame) / अपजस (blame) / दीन्ह (gave)
ramacharitamanas::57.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::57.essence: Names create praise and blame where nature is the same.
ramacharitamanas::57.simple_meaning: Two halves of the month are equally light and dark, but people label one good and the other bad. The verse warns that reputation often comes from naming, not from real difference.
ramacharitamanas::57.simple_insight: It softens quick judgment. You start noticing how easily the mind turns labels into value.
ramacharitamanas::57.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has just shown how bad company and good company change the same things into different results. He then widens the point: even the moon’s bright and dark halves are equal, yet the world assigns praise to one and blame to the other. The lesson is to see through appearances and labels.
ramacharitamanas::57.modern_relevance: A team meeting turns tense because one person is called a “leader” and another a “problem,” even though both are doing similar work. The verse asks you to look past the label before deciding what is actually true.
ramacharitamanas::57.insight: It trains the mind to separate appearance from value and to question the stories society attaches to the same reality.

ramacharitamanas::58.verse_sanskrit: जड़ चेतन जग जीव जत सकल राममय जानि। बंदउँ सब के पद कमल सदा जोरि जुग पानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::58.verse_hindi: जगत में जितने जड़ और चेतन जीव हैं, सबको राममय जानकर मैं उन सबके चरणकमलों की सदा दोनों हाथ जोड़कर वन्दना करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::58.english_translation: Knowing all inert and conscious beings in the world as filled with Ram, I always bow to the lotus feet of all with both hands joined.
ramacharitamanas::58.translation_literal: जड़ (inert) / चेतन (conscious) / जग (world) / जीव (living beings) / जत (as many as) / सकल (all) / राममय (filled with Ram) / जानि (knowing) / बंदउँ (I bow) / सब के (of all) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / सदा (always) / जोरि (joining) / जुग (both) / पानि (hands)
ramacharitamanas::58.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::58.essence: Seeing Ram everywhere turns every bow into worship.
ramacharitamanas::58.simple_meaning: Everything in the world, living and non-living, is seen as filled with Ram, so the speaker bows to all beings with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::58.simple_insight: Respect becomes easier when you stop sorting life into sacred and ordinary.
ramacharitamanas::58.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is moving into a devotional vision of the whole world. He sees every living and non-living thing as filled with Ram, and from that vision he offers reverence to all beings before asking for grace.
ramacharitamanas::58.modern_relevance: You are stuck in traffic, irritated by strangers, and then one small act of patience changes the whole mood. The person who cut you off is not outside the sacred field.
ramacharitamanas::58.insight: It shifts the mind from selective reverence to seeing the divine presence in everyone and everything.

ramacharitamanas::59.verse_sanskrit: देव दनुज नर नाग खग प्रेत पितर गंधर्ब। बंदउँ किंनर रजनिचर कृपा करहु अब सर्ब ॥
ramacharitamanas::59.verse_hindi: देवता, दैत्य, मनुष्य, नाग, पक्षी, प्रेत, पितर, गंधर्व, किन्नर और निशाचर सबको मैं प्रणाम करता हूँ। अब सब मुझ पर कृपा कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::59.english_translation: I bow to the radiant beings, the shadow beings, humans, serpents, birds, spirits, ancestors, celestial singers, hidden beings, night-wanderers, and all others. May all now show me grace.
ramacharitamanas::59.translation_literal: देव (radiant beings) / दनुज (shadow beings) / नर (humans) / नाग (serpents) / खग (birds) / प्रेत (spirits) / पितर (ancestors) / गंधर्ब (celestial singers) / बंदउँ (I bow) / किंनर (hidden beings) / रजनिचर (night-wanderers) / कृपा (grace) / करहु (do) / अब (now) / सर्ब (all)
ramacharitamanas::59.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::59.essence: Devotion becomes complete when no being is left outside respect.
ramacharitamanas::59.simple_meaning: The speaker bows to every kind of being, from radiant beings to night-wanderers, and asks for their grace.
ramacharitamanas::59.simple_insight: Respect grows when you stop ranking beings and start seeing shared worth everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::59.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas widens his prayer beyond human society. After seeing all beings as filled with Ram, he bows to every category of life and asks for grace from all. The verse turns devotion into universal reverence.
ramacharitamanas::59.modern_relevance: You walk through a crowded train station, irritated by strangers, workers, and noise. Then you remember that every face carries a life as real as yours. The hard edges soften.
ramacharitamanas::59.insight: It shifts the mind from selective respect to universal reverence for all forms of life.

ramacharitamanas::60.verse_sanskrit: आकर चारि लाख चौरासी। जाति जीव जल थल नभ बासी॥ सीय राममय सब जग जानी। करउँ प्रनाम जोरि जुग पानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::60.verse_hindi: चौरासी लाख योनियों में चार प्रकार के (स्वेदज, अण्डज, उद्भिज्ज, जरायुज) जीव जल, पृथ्वी और आकाश में रहते हैं, उन सबसे भरे हुए इस सारे जगत को श्री सीताराममय जानकर मैं दोनों हाथ जोड़कर प्रणाम करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::60.english_translation: The world holds 8.4 million forms of life, dwelling in water, on land, and in the sky. Seeing all of creation filled with Sita and Ram, I bow with both hands joined.
ramacharitamanas::60.translation_literal: आकर (forms) / चारि लाख चौरासी (four hundred eighty-four hundred-thousand, 8.4 million) / जाति (species or kinds) / जीव (living beings) / जल (water) / थल (land) / नभ (sky) / बासी (dwellers)॥ / सीय राममय (filled with Sita and Ram) / सब जग (the whole world) / जानी (having known) / करउँ (I do) / प्रनाम (salutation) / जोरि (joining) / जुग पानी (both hands) ॥
ramacharitamanas::60.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::60.essence: Everything alive becomes worthy of bowing when seen as filled with Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::60.simple_meaning: All forms of life across water, land, and sky are seen as filled with Sita and Ram, so the poet bows to all of creation.
ramacharitamanas::60.simple_insight: Respect grows when you see every living form as worthy of reverence.
ramacharitamanas::60.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is closing his universal salutation. After bowing to all kinds of beings, he widens the vision further: the whole world, from creatures in water to those in the sky, is pervaded by Sita and Ram. That vision turns the poem into an act of reverence.
ramacharitamanas::60.modern_relevance: You step outside and notice pigeons, street dogs, ants, and people all sharing the same morning air. The mind softens when it stops ranking life and starts honouring it.
ramacharitamanas::60.insight: It shifts attention from classification to reverence, making every encounter feel sacred and equal.

ramacharitamanas::61.verse_sanskrit: जानि कृपाकर किंकर मोहू। सब मिलि करहु छाड़ि छल छोहू॥ निज बुधि बल भरोस मोहि नाहीं। तातें बिनय करउँ सब पाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::61.verse_hindi: मुझको अपना दास जानकर कृपा की खान आप सब लोग मिलकर छल छोड़कर कृपा कीजिए। मुझे अपने बुद्धि-बल का भरोसा नहीं है, इसीलिए मैं सबसे विनती करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::61.english_translation: Knowing me as your servant, O treasure of compassion, all of you together, leave aside deceit and pity me. I have no भरोसा in my own intelligence or strength, so I bow before everyone and ask for grace.
ramacharitamanas::61.translation_literal: जानि (knowing) / कृपाकर (compassion-giver) / किंकर (servant) / मोहू (me) / सब (all) / मिलि (together) / करहु (do) / छाड़ि (leaving) / छल (deceit) / छोहू (pity, grace) / निज (own) / बुधि (intelligence) / बल (strength) / भरोस (trust) / मोहि (to me) / नाहीं (not) / तातें (therefore) / बिनय (humble request) / करउँ (I do) / सब पाहीं (before all)
ramacharitamanas::61.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::61.essence: Real devotion begins by dropping pride in your own power.
ramacharitamanas::61.simple_meaning: The poet asks everyone to treat him as a humble servant and to show mercy. He admits he has no confidence in his own intelligence or strength, so he comes asking for help.
ramacharitamanas::61.simple_insight: It feels safe to stop pretending you can do everything alone.
ramacharitamanas::61.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening his hands before the whole gathered world and asking for grace. He calls himself a servant, rejects pride in his own mind and strength, and prepares the way to praise Ram with humility instead of ego.
ramacharitamanas::61.modern_relevance: You sit down to write, speak, or create, and the blank page feels bigger than your skill. The first honest move is not performance — it is admitting you need help.
ramacharitamanas::61.insight: It shifts the mind from self-confidence to humble receptivity before speaking or creating.

ramacharitamanas::62.verse_sanskrit: करन चहउँ रघुपति गुन गाहा। लघु मति मोरि चरित अवगाहा॥ सूझ न एकउ अंग उपाऊ। मन मति रंक मनोरथ राउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::62.verse_hindi: मैं श्री रघुनाथजी के गुणों का वर्णन करना चाहता हूँ, परन्तु मेरी बुद्धि छोटी है और श्री रामजी का चरित्र अथाह है। इसके लिए मुझे उपाय का एक भी अंग अर्थात् कुछ (लेशमात्र) भी उपाय नहीं सूझता। मेरे मन और बुद्धि कंगाल हैं, किन्तु मनोरथ राजा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::62.english_translation: I want to sing the qualities of Raghupati, but my intellect is small and Ram's character is unfathomable. No part of the method appears to me. My mind and understanding are poor, yet my aspiration is royal.
ramacharitamanas::62.translation_literal: करन चहउँ (want to do) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / गुन गाहा (song of qualities) / लघु मति (small intellect) / मोरि (my) / चरित (character) / अवगाहा (deep, unfathomable) / सूझ न (does not appear) / एकउ (even one) / अंग (part) / उपाऊ (means) / मन मति (mind and understanding) / रंक (poor) / मनोरथ (desire) / राउ (king)
ramacharitamanas::62.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::62.essence: Longing can be royal even when the mind feels poor.
ramacharitamanas::62.simple_meaning: The poet wants to praise Ram, but he feels too limited to do it well. His desire is vast, yet he cannot see a clear way forward.
ramacharitamanas::62.simple_insight: A humble mind can still reach toward greatness without pretending to be equal to it.
ramacharitamanas::62.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is speaking as he begins his devotional retelling. He wants to sing Ram's glory, but he feels his own mind is too small and Ram's character too deep. The verse captures the tension between devotion and human limitation.
ramacharitamanas::62.modern_relevance: You open a blank page before writing something that matters, then freeze because the subject feels larger than your skill. The reverence is real, and so is the fear of not measuring up.
ramacharitamanas::62.insight: It shifts the reader from self-confidence to humble inquiry before what is vast.

ramacharitamanas::63.verse_sanskrit: मति अति नीच ऊँचि रुचि आछी। चहिअ अमिअ जग जुरइ न छाछी॥ छमिहहिं सज्जन मोरि ढिठाई। सुनिहहिं बालबचन मन लाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::63.verse_hindi: मेरी बुद्धि तो अत्यन्त नीची है और चाह बड़ी ऊँची है, चाह तो अमृत पाने की है, पर जगत में जुड़ती छाछ भी नहीं। सज्जन मेरी ढिठाई को क्षमा करेंगे और मेरे बाल वचनों को मन लगाकर (प्रेमपूर्वक) सुनेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::63.english_translation: My mind is very low, and my desire is very high. I seek nectar, but in this world even buttermilk does not mix. Good people will forgive my boldness and listen to my childish words with care.
ramacharitamanas::63.translation_literal: मति (mind) / अति (very) / नीच (low) / ऊँचि (high) / रुचि (desire) / आछी (good) / चहिअ (is wanted) / अमिअ (nectar) / जग (world) / जुरइ (mixes) / न (not) / छाछी (buttermilk) / छमिहहिं (will forgive) / सज्जन (good people) / मोरि (my) / ढिठाई (boldness) / सुनिहहिं (will listen) / बालबचन (childish words) / मन (mind) / लाई (placing)
ramacharitamanas::63.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::63.essence: Humility can ask for nectar without pretending to deserve it.
ramacharitamanas::63.simple_meaning: The speaker admits to having a humble mind but an elevated desire, and asks kind people to forgive the boldness and listen with affection.
ramacharitamanas::63.simple_insight: You do not need perfection to begin. Honest longing can still be heard with grace.
