ramacharitamanas::63.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is beginning his devotional telling of Ram's story. He bows low, says his mind is unworthy, and asks learned, good-hearted listeners to pardon his awkward speech and hear him kindly. The verse opens the heart before the story begins.
ramacharitamanas::63.modern_relevance: You send the first draft anyway, even though you know it is rough. What matters is sincerity, not polish — and the right people can hear devotion beneath imperfect words.
ramacharitamanas::63.insight: It teaches you to ask for grace before speaking, and to value longing over self-importance.

ramacharitamanas::64.verse_sanskrit: जौं बालक कह तोतरि बाता। सुनहिं मुदित मन पितु अरु माता॥ हँसिहहिं कूर कुटिल कुबिचारी। जे पर दूषन भूषनधारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::64.verse_hindi: जैसे बालक जब तोतले वचन बोलता है, तो उसके माता-पिता उन्हें प्रसन्न मन से सुनते हैं, किन्तु क्रूर, कुटिल और बुरे विचार वाले लोग जो दूसरों के दोषों को ही भूषण रूप से धारण किए रहते हैं (अर्थात् जिन्हें पराए दोष ही प्यारे लगते हैं), हँसेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::64.english_translation: Like a child babbling with a lisp, parents listen with delight. Cruel, crooked, and ill-minded people laugh, feeding on others' faults.
ramacharitamanas::64.translation_literal: जौं (as) / बालक (child) / कह (speaks) / तोतरि (lisping) / बाता (speech) / सुनहिं (they hear) / मुदित (glad) / मन (mind) / पितु (father) / अरु (and) / माता (mother) / हँसिहहिं (they will laugh) / कूर (cruel) / कुटिल (crooked) / कुबिचारी (ill-minded) / जे (those who) / पर (others') / दूषन (faults) / भूषनधारी (wearing as ornaments)
ramacharitamanas::64.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::64.essence: Love hears imperfection as sweetness; cruelty turns it into a joke.
ramacharitamanas::64.simple_meaning: Good people listen to imperfect speech with affection, like parents hearing a child. Bad-minded people enjoy mocking and noticing faults in others.
ramacharitamanas::64.simple_insight: You can tell the quality of a heart by what it does with someone else's imperfection.
ramacharitamanas::64.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is apologizing for his own rough, childlike verse. He says loving readers will hear it like parents hear a toddler's speech, while harsh people will only seize on flaws and laugh.
ramacharitamanas::64.modern_relevance: You send a half-finished message, then see the reply. One person understands what you meant; another circles the typo and misses your heart. This verse knows both kinds of readers.
ramacharitamanas::64.insight: It trains you to read others with generosity and to notice when your own mind feeds on criticism.

ramacharitamanas::65.verse_sanskrit: निज कबित्त केहि लाग न नीका। सरस होउ अथवा अति फीका॥ जे पर भनिति सुनत हरषाहीं। ते बर पुरुष बहुत जग नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::65.verse_hindi: रसीली हो या अत्यन्त फीकी, अपनी कविता किसे अच्छी नहीं लगती? किन्तु जो दूसरे की रचना को सुनकर हर्षित होते हैं, ऐसे उत्तम पुरुष जगत में बहुत नहीं हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::65.english_translation: What poem of one's own does not seem pleasing, whether sweet or extremely dull? But those who rejoice when hearing another's composition are rare indeed.
ramacharitamanas::65.translation_literal: निज (one's own) / कबित्त (poem) / केहि (to whom) / लाग (seems) / न (not) / नीका (good, pleasing) / सरस (sweet, pleasing) / होउ (be) / अथवा (or) / अति (very) / फीका (bland, dull) / जे (those who) / पर (another's) / भनिति (speech, composition) / सुनत (while hearing) / हरषाहीं (rejoice) / ते (they) / बर (excellent) / पुरुष (persons) / बहुत (many) / जग (in the world) / नाहीं (are not)
ramacharitamanas::65.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::65.essence: True greatness can rejoice in another person's work.
ramacharitamanas::65.simple_meaning: People naturally love their own work, no matter how good or bad it is. Truly noble people are the ones who can joyfully appreciate someone else's creation.
ramacharitamanas::65.simple_insight: It feels refreshing to step out of self-importance and genuinely enjoy another person's gift.
ramacharitamanas::65.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is speaking in his own voice, humbly reflecting on poetry itself. He says everyone is biased toward their own work, but only a rare few can hear another person's words with joy. The verse becomes a test of character.
ramacharitamanas::65.modern_relevance: You post something and keep checking for likes, secretly convinced it deserves more. Then a friend shares their work, and you can either compare or genuinely celebrate it. That response reveals the quality of your mind.
ramacharitamanas::65.insight: It trains the mind to notice self-bias and replace comparison with sincere appreciation.

ramacharitamanas::66.verse_sanskrit: जग बहु नर सर सरि सम भाई। जे निज बाढ़ि बढ़हि जल पाई॥ सज्जन सकृत सिंधु सम कोई। देखि पूर बिधु बाढ़इ जोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::66.verse_hindi: हे भाई! जगत में तालाबों और नदियों के समान मनुष्य ही अधिक हैं, जो जल पाकर अपनी ही बाढ़ से बढ़ते हैं (अर्थात् अपनी ही उन्नति से प्रसन्न होते हैं)। समुद्र सा तो कोई एक बिरला ही सज्जन होता है, जो चन्द्रमा को पूर्ण देखकर (दूसरों का उत्कर्ष देखकर) उमड़ पड़ता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::66.english_translation: Most people are like ponds and rivers: they grow only when they receive water. Rare is the noble person like the ocean, who swells when the moon is full and others rise.
ramacharitamanas::66.translation_literal: जग (world) / बहु (many) / नर (people) / सर (pond) / सरि (river) / सम (like) / भाई (brother) / जे (those who) / निज (their own) / बाढ़ि (increase) / बढ़हि (grow) / जल (water) / पाई (having received) / सज्जन (noble people) / सकृत (once) / सिंधु (ocean) / सम (like) / कोई (someone) / देखि (seeing) / पूर (fullness) / बिधु (moon) / बाढ़इ (swells) / जोई (who)
ramacharitamanas::66.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::66.essence: Nobility is measured by joy in another's rise.
ramacharitamanas::66.simple_meaning: Most people are pleased only when their own status grows. A rare noble person feels enlarged when someone else shines.
ramacharitamanas::66.simple_insight: It feels freeing to stop competing with everyone and start rejoicing in their good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::66.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses in Balkand to describe human nature. Most people are like ponds that rise only when fed. A truly noble person is like the ocean: another's fullness does not threaten them; it deepens them.
ramacharitamanas::66.modern_relevance: Your colleague gets praised in the meeting, and your stomach tightens for a second. This verse asks whether their success can become your joy instead of your private defeat.
ramacharitamanas::66.insight: It shifts the mind from self-comparison to spacious rejoicing in others' growth.

ramacharitamanas::67.verse_sanskrit: भाग छोट अभिलाषु बड़ करउँ एक बिस्वास। पैहहिं सुख सुनि सुजन सब खल करिहहिं उपहास ॥
ramacharitamanas::67.verse_hindi: मेरा भाग्य छोटा है और इच्छा बहुत बड़ी है, परन्तु मुझे एक विश्वास है कि इसे सुनकर सज्जन सभी सुख पावेंगे और दुष्ट हँसी उड़ावेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::67.english_translation: My means are small and my desire is great, but I have one confidence: hearing this, the good will feel joy, and the wicked will mock.
ramacharitamanas::67.translation_literal: भाग (fate/lot) / छोट (small) / अभिलाषु (desire) / बड़ (great) / करउँ (I do) / एक (one) / बिस्वास (confidence) / पैहहिं (will receive) / सुख (joy) / सुनि (hearing) / सुजन (the good people) / सब (all) / खल (the wicked) / करिहहिं (will do) / उपहास (mockery)
ramacharitamanas::67.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::67.essence: Small means can still carry a great offering.
ramacharitamanas::67.simple_meaning: The poet says his resources are limited, but he trusts that good people will find joy in hearing this work, while critics may laugh.
ramacharitamanas::67.simple_insight: You can offer your best without needing universal approval. Honest work finds its own readers.
ramacharitamanas::67.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses before continuing his retelling and admits the scale of his desire exceeds his own limits. He trusts that sincere readers will feel joy, even if harsh critics mock the work. The verse opens his humble, devotional stance as a poet.
ramacharitamanas::67.modern_relevance: You post something sincere after weeks of work, then watch the comments split in two. Some people feel it deeply; others sneer. The verse says that is normal — keep going.
ramacharitamanas::67.insight: It shifts attention from public approval to the response of the sincere reader.

ramacharitamanas::68.verse_sanskrit: खल परिहास होइ हित मोरा। काक कहहिं कलकंठ कठोरा॥ हंसहि बक दादुर चातकही। हँसहिं मलिन खल बिमल बतकही ॥
ramacharitamanas::68.verse_hindi: किन्तु दुष्टों के हँसने से मेरा हित ही होगा। मधुर कण्ठ वाली कोयल को कौए तो कठोर ही कहा करते हैं। जैसे बगुले हंस को और मेंढक पपीहे को हँसते हैं, वैसे ही मलिन मन वाले दुष्ट निर्मल वाणी को हँसते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::68.english_translation: The wicked's mockery becomes my benefit. The crow calls the cuckoo harsh, the heron mocks the swan, and the frog mocks the chatak. In the same way, impure minds laugh at pure speech.
ramacharitamanas::68.translation_literal: खल (wicked) / परिहास (mockery) / होइ (becomes) / हित (benefit) / मोरा (my) / काक (crow) / कहहिं (call) / कलकंठ (sweet-throated cuckoo) / कठोरा (harsh) / हंसहि (laugh at) / बक (heron) / दादुर (frog) / चातकही (the chatak) / हँसहिं (laugh) / मलिन (impure) / खल (wicked) / बिमल (pure) / बतकही (speech)
ramacharitamanas::68.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::68.essence: Mockery from the impure only confirms the purity of the words.
ramacharitamanas::68.simple_meaning: Wicked people may mock pure speech, but their ridicule only proves their own limitation. The pure remain pure, just as birds with dull eyesight cannot judge beauty.
ramacharitamanas::68.simple_insight: Other people's mockery does not define your worth.
ramacharitamanas::68.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is speaking in the Balkand, defending his devotional poetry before critics. He says the mockery of harsh-minded people only reveals their own nature, while those with refined hearts will recognise the value of his words.
ramacharitamanas::68.modern_relevance: You post something honest and a few cynical comments come in fast. Their sneers do not change the truth of what you said; they only show what kind of mind is reading it.
ramacharitamanas::68.insight: It shifts attention from public approval to the quality of the listener and the purity of the message.

ramacharitamanas::69.verse_sanskrit: कबित रसिक न राम पद नेहू। तिन्ह कहँ सुखद हास रस एहू॥ भाषा भनिति भोरि मति मोरी। हँसिबे जो हँसें नहिं खोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::69.verse_hindi: जो न तो कविता के रसिक हैं और न जिनका श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में प्रेम है, उनके लिए भी यह कविता सुखद हास्यरस का काम देगी। प्रथम तो यह भाषा की रचना है, दूसरे मेरी बुद्धि भोली है, इससे यह हँसने के योग्य ही है, हँसने में उन्हें कोई दोष नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::69.english_translation: Even those who do not delight in poetry or love Ram's feet may still find this verse pleasantly amusing. It is written in a simple tongue, and my mind is plain; laughing at it is no fault.
ramacharitamanas::69.translation_literal: कबित (poetry) / रसिक (connoisseur) / न (not) / राम पद (Ram's feet) / नेहू (love) / तिन्ह कहँ (for them) / सुखद (pleasant) / हास रस (humorous flavor) / एहू (this)॥ / भाषा (language) / भनिति (composition) / भोरि मति (simple mind) / मोरी (my) / हँसिबे (to laugh) / जो (if) / हँसें (they laugh) / नहिं (not) / खोरी (fault) ॥
ramacharitamanas::69.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::69.essence: Simple words can still carry devotion, and even laughter need not be a fault.
ramacharitamanas::69.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says this verse may still amuse readers who do not care for poetry or love Ram. He calls his own language simple and says people may laugh without blame.
ramacharitamanas::69.simple_insight: A humble voice lowers the barrier to devotion and invites even skeptics to listen.
ramacharitamanas::69.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses before the story and speaks directly to the reader. He knows some listeners may not love poetry or Ram's feet, so he offers this verse as harmless, simple amusement. The humility prepares the heart for devotion.
ramacharitamanas::69.modern_relevance: You send a message to a group chat and worry it sounds too plain. Instead of defending it, you smile and let the words stand. Humility can open more doors than polish.
ramacharitamanas::69.insight: It frames the coming story as accessible, lowering pride so the reader can receive it.

ramacharitamanas::70.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु पद प्रीति न सामुझि नीकी। तिन्हहि कथा सुनि लागिहि फीकी॥ हरि हर पद रति मति न कुतर की। तिन्ह कहँ मधुर कथा रघुबर की ॥
ramacharitamanas::70.verse_hindi: जिन्हें न तो प्रभु के चरणों में प्रेम है और न अच्छी समझ ही है, उनको यह कथा सुनने में फीकी लगेगी। जिनकी श्री हरि (भगवान विष्णु) और श्री हर (भगवान शिव) के चरणों में प्रीति है और जिनकी बुद्धि कुतर्क करने वाली नहीं है (जो श्री हरि-हर में भेद की या ऊँच-नीच की कल्पना नहीं करते), उन्हें श्री रघुनाथजी की यह कथा मीठी लगेगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::70.english_translation: Those without love for the Lord's feet and without clear understanding find this story bland. Those whose hearts love Hari and Hara, and whose minds do not twist into clever arguments, find the story of Raghubar sweet.
ramacharitamanas::70.translation_literal: प्रभु पद (the Lord's feet) / प्रीति (love) / न (not) / सामुझि (understanding) / नीकी (good) / तिन्हहि (to them) / कथा (story) / सुनि (having heard) / लागिहि (will seem) / फीकी (bland) / हरि (Hari) / हर (Hara) / पद (feet) / रति (love) / मति (mind) / न (not) / कुतर (crooked argument) / की (of) / तिन्ह कहँ (for them) / मधुर (sweet) / कथा (story) / रघुबर की (of Raghubar)
ramacharitamanas::70.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::70.essence: Devotion makes the same story taste sweet; argument makes it go flat.
ramacharitamanas::70.simple_meaning: Ram's story feels dull to people without devotion or good understanding. But for those who love the divine and avoid twisted arguments, it becomes sweet.
ramacharitamanas::70.simple_insight: The heart receives devotion as sweetness; a combative mind hears only noise.
ramacharitamanas::70.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is explaining how this poem should be received. After dismissing mockers, he says the story will seem bland to people lacking love for Ram's feet and sound understanding. But those devoted to Hari and Hara, and free from crooked argument, will find Raghubar's कथा sweet.
ramacharitamanas::70.modern_relevance: You open a sacred talk with folded arms, ready to debate every line. Someone else listens with devotion and leaves quietly changed. The same words can taste flat or life-giving, depending on the mind that receives them.
ramacharitamanas::70.insight: It shifts attention from judging the teaching to preparing the mind that hears it.

ramacharitamanas::71.verse_sanskrit: राम भगति भूषित जियँ जानी। सुनिहहिं सुजन सराहि सुबानी॥ कबि न होउँ नहिं बचन प्रबीनू। सकल कला सब बिद्या हीनू ॥
ramacharitamanas::71.verse_hindi: सज्जनगण इस कथा को अपने जी में श्री रामजी की भक्ति से भूषित जानकर सुंदर वाणी से सराहना करते हुए सुनेंगे। मैं न तो कवि हूँ, न वाक्य रचना में ही कुशल हूँ, मैं तो सब कलाओं तथा सब विद्याओं से रहित हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::71.english_translation: Knowing this tale to be adorned with devotion to Ram, the good will hear it and praise it in beautiful speech. I am no poet, nor skilled in wording; I am devoid of all arts and all learning.
ramacharitamanas::71.translation_literal: राम भगति (devotion to Ram) / भूषित (adorned) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानी (knowing) / सुनिहहिं (will hear) / सुजन (good people) / सराहि (praising) / सुबानी (beautiful speech) / कबि (poet) / न होउँ (I am not) / नहिं (not) / बचन (speech/words) / प्रबीनू (skilled) / सकल कला (all arts) / सब बिद्या (all learning) / हीनू (without)
ramacharitamanas::71.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::71.essence: Devotion makes plain speech beautiful, even without poetic skill.
ramacharitamanas::71.simple_meaning: Good people will hear this story as devotion to Ram, while the speaker humbly says he has no poetic skill or learning.
ramacharitamanas::71.simple_insight: Real devotion does not need polish; sincerity carries its own beauty.
ramacharitamanas::71.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses before continuing the story to bow his own voice low. He says the worthy will receive this telling as devotion to Ram, even though he himself claims no mastery of poetry, language, art, or learning.
ramacharitamanas::71.modern_relevance: You post something heartfelt and worry it sounds clumsy. A friend reads it and feels the honesty immediately. That is the kind of beauty Tulsidas trusts here.
ramacharitamanas::71.insight: It shifts attention from performance to sincerity, and from verbal skill to devotional intent.

ramacharitamanas::72.verse_sanskrit: आखर अरथ अलंकृति नाना। छंद प्रबंध अनेक बिधाना॥ भाव भेद रस भेद अपारा। कबित दोष गुन बिबिध प्रकारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::72.verse_hindi: नाना प्रकार के अक्षर, अर्थ और अलंकार, अनेक प्रकार की छंद रचना, भावों और रसों के अपार भेद और कविता के भाँति-भाँति के गुण-दोष होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::72.english_translation: There are many kinds of letters, meanings, and ornaments; many kinds of meter and composition; countless shades of feeling and flavor; and many kinds of poetic faults and virtues.
ramacharitamanas::72.translation_literal: आखर (letters) / अरथ (meaning) / अलंकृति (ornamentation) / नाना (many kinds) / छंद (meter) / प्रबंध (composition) / अनेक (many) / बिधाना (methods) / भाव (feelings) / भेद (differences) / रस (aesthetic flavor) / भेद (differences) / अपारा (boundless) / कबित (poetry) / दोष (faults) / गुन (qualities) / बिबिध (various) / प्रकारा (types)
ramacharitamanas::72.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::72.essence: True devotion begins with admitting your limits.
ramacharitamanas::72.simple_meaning: Poetry has many forms, styles, emotions, and qualities, both good and flawed. The speaker is admitting how vast and subtle the art of composition is.
ramacharitamanas::72.simple_insight: Humility begins where your limits are named plainly.
ramacharitamanas::72.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is introducing his own weakness as a poet before singing the Ram story. He names the vast craft of poetry—letters, meanings, meters, emotions, flavors, virtues, and faults—to show that he knows how little of it he truly commands.
ramacharitamanas::72.modern_relevance: You open a blank document and realise how much craft you do not yet own. Instead of pretending mastery, you name the gap honestly and begin anyway.
ramacharitamanas::72.insight: It shifts the mind from performance to honest self-assessment before speaking.

ramacharitamanas::73.verse_sanskrit: कबित बिबेक एक नहिं मोरें। सत्य कहउँ लिखि कागद कोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::73.verse_hindi: इनमें से काव्य सम्बन्धी एक भी बात का ज्ञान मुझमें नहीं है, यह मैं कोरे कागज पर लिखकर (शपथपूर्वक) सत्य-सत्य कहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::73.english_translation: I have no poetic discernment at all. I speak the truth, writing it on a blank sheet of paper.
ramacharitamanas::73.translation_literal: कबित (poetic craft) / बिबेक (discernment) / एक (one) / नहिं (not) / मोरें (in me) / सत्य (truth) / कहउँ (I speak) / लिखि (writing) / कागद (paper) / कोरें (blank)
ramacharitamanas::73.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::73.essence: Truth matters more than poetic skill.
ramacharitamanas::73.simple_meaning: The poet says he has no skill in poetry and is speaking honestly, with nothing hidden.
ramacharitamanas::73.simple_insight: Humility can be its own kind of strength.
ramacharitamanas::73.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still introducing his work before the story fully begins. After listing the many features of poetry, he now disowns any mastery of them, insisting he writes plainly and truthfully rather than with literary pride.
ramacharitamanas::73.modern_relevance: Before a presentation, you admit you are not trying to impress anyone — only to be honest. That kind of plain speaking often lands deeper than polished performance.
ramacharitamanas::73.insight: It shifts the reader from performance to sincerity, valuing truth over display.

ramacharitamanas::74.verse_sanskrit: भनिति मोरि सब गुन रहित बिस्व बिदित गुन एक। सो बिचारि सुनिहहिं सुमति जिन्ह कें बिमल बिबेक ॥
ramacharitamanas::74.verse_hindi: मेरी रचना सब गुणों से रहित है, इसमें बस, जगत्प्रसिद्ध एक गुण है। उसे विचारकर अच्छी बुद्धिवाले पुरुष, जिनके निर्मल ज्ञान है, इसको सुनेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::74.english_translation: My composition lacks every merit, yet it has one quality known throughout the world. Thinking of that, wise people with pure discernment will listen to it.
ramacharitamanas::74.translation_literal: भनिति (composition/speech) / मोरि (my) / सब (all) / गुन (qualities) / रहित (without) / बिस्व (world) / बिदित (known) / गुन (quality) / एक (one) / सो (that) / बिचारि (thinking/considering) / सुनिहहिं (will listen) / सुमति (wise people) / जिन्ह कें (whose) / बिमल (pure) / बिबेक (discernment)
ramacharitamanas::74.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::74.essence: Humility can hide the one quality that truly matters.
ramacharitamanas::74.simple_meaning: The poet says his work has no literary merit, but it has one famous quality that wise readers will notice and hear it for that reason.
ramacharitamanas::74.simple_insight: Humility opens the door. What matters most may be hidden behind a modest first impression.
ramacharitamanas::74.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has just admitted he lacks poetic skill. Now he adds a final self-effacing line: his work has one world-known quality that discerning readers will recognize. This is a preface to the power of Ram's name, not a standalone teaching.
ramacharitamanas::74.modern_relevance: You publish something you poured your heart into and still feel it is imperfect. A few careful readers may come for the polish, but stay for the one thing that feels true.
ramacharitamanas::74.insight: It frames the text as modest in style but powerful in essence, inviting readers to look past surface flaws.

ramacharitamanas::75.verse_sanskrit: एहि महँ रघुपति नाम उदारा। अति पावन पुरान श्रुति सारा॥ मंगल भवन अमंगल हारी। उमा सहित जेहि जपत पुरारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::75.verse_hindi: इसमें श्री रघुनाथजी का उदार नाम है, जो अत्यन्त पवित्र है, वेद-पुराणों का सार है, कल्याण का भवन है और अमंगलों को हरने वाला है, जिसे पार्वतीजी सहित भगवान शिवजी सदा जपा करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::75.english_translation: In this, the noble name of Raghupati is supremely pure, the essence of the Puranas and the Vedas. It is a house of auspiciousness and the remover of inauspiciousness, and Lord Shiva, along with Uma, always chants it.
ramacharitamanas::75.translation_literal: एहि महँ (in this) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / नाम (name) / उदारा (noble, generous) / अति (very) / पावन (pure, purifying) / पुरान (Puranas) / श्रुति (Vedas, sacred revelation) / सारा (essence) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / भवन (house, abode) / अमंगल (inauspiciousness) / हारी (remover) / उमा (Uma, Parvati) / सहित (together with) / जेहि (which) / जपत (chanting) / पुरारी (Shiva, destroyer of the three cities)
ramacharitamanas::75.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::75.essence: Ram’s name itself carries purity, protection, and blessing.
ramacharitamanas::75.simple_meaning: Ram’s name is pure, sacred, and powerful. It brings good and removes what is harmful, and even Shiva and Parvati repeat it.
ramacharitamanas::75.simple_insight: There is comfort in a name that feels bigger than fear and stronger than bad luck.
ramacharitamanas::75.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses his praise to say that Ram’s name itself is the heart of all sacred teaching. It is not just beautiful poetry; even Shiva and Parvati repeat it, showing that devotion to Ram is the highest refuge.
ramacharitamanas::75.modern_relevance: When the room feels heavy before a hard conversation, one steady phrase can change your whole center. Some names do that: they gather courage, clear fear, and remind you what is worth holding onto.
ramacharitamanas::75.insight: It shifts attention from outer rituals to the living power of remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::76.verse_sanskrit: भनिति बिचित्र सुकबि कृत जोऊ। राम नाम बिनु सोह न सोउ॥ बिधुबदनी सब भाँति सँवारी। सोह न बसन बिना बर नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::76.verse_hindi: जो अच्छे कवि के द्वारा रची हुई बड़ी अनूठी कविता है, वह भी राम नाम के बिना शोभा नहीं पाती। जैसे चन्द्रमा के समान मुख वाली सुंदर स्त्री सब प्रकार से सुसज्जित होने पर भी वस्त्र के बिना शोभा नहीं देती ॥
ramacharitamanas::76.english_translation: Even a beautifully crafted poem does not shine without Ram's name. A lovely woman, though adorned in every way, does not look complete without clothes.
ramacharitamanas::76.translation_literal: भनिति (speech/poem) / बिचित्र (striking, varied) / सुकबि (good poet) / कृत (made) / जोऊ (whatever) / राम नाम (Ram's name) / बिनु (without) / सोह (shines, looks beautiful) / न (not) / सोउ (that too) / बिधुबदनी (moon-faced woman) / सब भाँति (in every way) / सँवारी (adorned) / सोह (shines, looks beautiful) / न (not) / बसन (clothes) / बिना (without) / बर नारी (beautiful woman)
ramacharitamanas::76.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::76.essence: Ram's name is what makes beauty feel complete.
ramacharitamanas::76.simple_meaning: Even the best poetry and the most beautiful appearance feel incomplete without Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::76.simple_insight: What seems polished still needs devotion to feel whole.
ramacharitamanas::76.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising the power of Ram's name while composing his own poem. He says even fine poetry lacks true beauty without that name, just as a beautifully adorned woman still seems incomplete without clothes.
ramacharitamanas::76.modern_relevance: You polish the slide, fix the lighting, and rehearse the speech one more time. Still, something feels missing until the purpose behind it is real.
ramacharitamanas::76.insight: It shifts attention from surface polish to the sacred center that gives form its meaning.

ramacharitamanas::77.verse_sanskrit: सब गुन रहित कुकबि कृत बानी। राम नाम जस अंकित जानी॥ सादर कहहिं सुनहिं बुध ताही। मधुकर सरिस संत गुनग्राही ॥
ramacharitamanas::77.verse_hindi: इसके विपरीत, कुकवि की रची हुई सब गुणों से रहित कविता को भी, राम के नाम एवं यश से अंकित जानकर, बुद्धिमान लोग आदरपूर्वक कहते और सुनते हैं, क्योंकि संतजन भौंरे की भाँति गुण ही को ग्रहण करने वाले होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::77.english_translation: Even a poem lacking all merit is honored when it bears Ram's name and praise. Wise people respectfully speak and listen to it, just as saints, like bees, gather only the sweetness of virtue.
ramacharitamanas::77.translation_literal: सब (all) / गुन रहित (without qualities) / कुकबि (bad poet) / कृत (composed) / बानी (speech, verse) / राम नाम (Ram's name) / जस (praise, glory) / अंकित (marked, inscribed) / जानी (knowing)॥ / सादर (with respect) / कहहिं (they speak) / सुनहिं (they hear) / बुध (the wise) / ताही (that) / मधुकर (bee) / सरिस (like) / संत (saints) / गुनग्राही (one who grasps virtues)॥
ramacharitamanas::77.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::77.essence: Ram's name can make even flawed words worthy of respect.
ramacharitamanas::77.simple_meaning: Even weak poetry becomes worthy when it carries Ram's name and praise. Wise people focus on the good in it, not the defects.
ramacharitamanas::77.simple_insight: You can train yourself to notice what is holy and helpful, even inside something imperfect.
ramacharitamanas::77.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still opening the Ramcharitmanas by apologizing for his own poetry. He says that even if the verse itself lacks beauty, it becomes honorable because Ram's name and glory are woven into it. Wise listeners, like saints, hear for the virtue inside it.
ramacharitamanas::77.modern_relevance: You open a half-finished message someone sent at midnight and almost dismiss it because the writing is messy. Then one honest line lands and changes everything. Wisdom learns to catch that line.
ramacharitamanas::77.insight: It shifts attention from surface flaws to the good hidden within speech, art, and people.

ramacharitamanas::78.verse_sanskrit: जदपि कबित रस एकउ नाहीं। राम प्रताप प्रगट एहि माहीं॥ सोइ भरोस मोरें मन आवा। केहिं न सुसंग बड़प्पनु पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::78.verse_hindi: यद्यपि मेरी इस रचना में कविता का एक भी रस नहीं है, तथापि इसमें श्री रामजी का प्रताप प्रकट है। मेरे मन में यही एक भरोसा है। भले संग से भला, किसने बड़प्पन नहीं पाया? ॥
ramacharitamanas::78.english_translation: Even if this poem has no poetic flavor at all, Ram's glory shines forth in it. That is the only confidence in my mind: who has not gained greatness through good company?
ramacharitamanas::78.translation_literal: जदपि (although) / कबित (poetry) / रस (flavor, aesthetic essence) / एकउ (even one) / नाहीं (not) / राम (Ram) / प्रताप (glory, power) / प्रगट (manifest) / एहि (in this) / माहीं (in) ॥ / सोइ (that only) / भरोस (confidence, trust) / मोरें (my) / मन (mind) / आवा (came) / केहिं (who) / न (not) / सुसंग (good company) / बड़प्पनु (greatness) / पावा (got) ॥
ramacharitamanas::78.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::78.essence: Flawed words become radiant when Ram shines through them.
ramacharitamanas::78.simple_meaning: The poet says his own writing may lack beauty, but Ram's greatness still shines through it. He trusts that good company lifts everything up.
ramacharitamanas::78.simple_insight: You do not need perfect skill when the right presence is carrying the work.
ramacharitamanas::78.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas speaks in his own voice, apologising for his poetic craft while placing all confidence in Ram's presence within the Ramcharitmanas. He says that even flawed words can gain greatness through noble association, just as this text is lifted by Ram.
ramacharitamanas::78.modern_relevance: You send a rough draft, unsure it is good enough. Then one strong idea, one honest line, changes everything. The work is still yours, but its power comes from what it is near.
ramacharitamanas::78.insight: It shifts attention from technical perfection to the transforming force of noble company and divine presence.

ramacharitamanas::79.verse_sanskrit: धूमउ तजइ सहज करुआई। अगरु प्रसंग सुगंध बसाई॥ भनिति भदेस बस्तु भलि बरनी। राम कथा जग मंगल करनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::79.verse_hindi: धुआँ भी अगर के संग से सुगंधित होकर अपने स्वाभाविक कड़ुवेपन को छोड़ देता है। मेरी कविता अवश्य भद्दी है, परन्तु इसमें जगत का कल्याण करने वाली रामकथा रूपी उत्तम वस्तु का वर्णन किया गया है। (इससे यह भी अच्छी ही समझी जाएगी।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::79.english_translation: Smoke loses its natural bitterness beside incense and takes on fragrance. My verse may be crude, but it describes the noble story of Ram, which brings welfare to the world.
ramacharitamanas::79.translation_literal: धूमउ (smoke too) / तजइ (leaves) / सहज (natural) / करुआई (bitterness) / अगरु (incense) / प्रसंग (in company / by contact) / सुगंध (fragrance) / बसाई (dwells) / भनिति (poetry) / भदेस (coarse / crude) / बस्तु (thing / matter) / भलि (good) / बरनी (described) / राम कथा (story of Ram) / जग मंगल करनी (world-welfare causing)
ramacharitamanas::79.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::79.essence: Ram’s story makes even rough words fragrant.
ramacharitamanas::79.simple_meaning: A rough poem becomes worthy because it carries Ram’s story. Just as smoke takes on fragrance near incense, this verse gains value from its holy subject.
ramacharitamanas::79.simple_insight: Even imperfect words can carry real grace when they point toward what is sacred.
ramacharitamanas::79.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is closing his humble preface to the Ramcharitmanas. He admits his poetry is plain, but says Ram’s story changes everything it touches, just as incense can perfume smoke. The verse prepares the reader to receive the text through devotion, not literary pride.
ramacharitamanas::79.modern_relevance: You send a clumsy message, then realize the apology mattered more than the wording. A sincere heart can make even rough speech feel clean.
ramacharitamanas::79.insight: It shifts attention from polish to presence: the worth of expression comes from the devotion behind it.

ramacharitamanas::80.verse_sanskrit: मंगल करनि कलिमल हरनि तुलसी कथा रघुनाथ की। गति कूर कबिता सरित की ज्यों सरित पावन पाथ की॥ प्रभु सुजस संगति भनिति भलि होइहि सुजन मन भावनी भव अंग भूति मसान की सुमिरत सुहावनि पावनी॥
ramacharitamanas::80.verse_hindi: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि श्री रघुनाथजी की कथा कल्याण करने वाली और कलियुग के पापों को हरने वाली है। मेरी इस भद्दी कविता रूपी नदी की चाल पवित्र जल वाली नदी (गंगाजी) की चाल की भाँति टेढ़ी है। प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी के सुंदर यश के संग से यह कविता सुंदर तथा सज्जनों के मन को भाने वाली हो जाएगी। श्मशान की अपवित्र राख भी श्री महादेवजी के अंग के संग से सुहावनी लगती है और स्मरण करते ही पवित्र करने वाली होती है।
ramacharitamanas::80.english_translation: Tulsidas says: Rama's story brings auspiciousness and removes the impurities of this age. My crude poem moves like a crooked river, but the company of Rama's fame will make it pleasing to noble hearts. Even ashes from a cremation ground become lovely and purifying when remembered with Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::80.translation_literal: मंगल (auspiciousness) / करनि (doing, causing) / कलिमल (the impurities of Kali age) / हरनि (removing) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / कथा (story, narration) / रघुनाथ की (of Raghunath, Rama) / गति (movement, course) / कूर (crooked, rough) / कबिता (poetry) / सरित (river) / की (of) / ज्यों (like) / सरित (river) / पावन (pure) / पाथ (water) / की (of) / प्रभु (Lord) / सुजस (beautiful fame) / संगति (company, association) / भनिति (speech, verse) / भलि (good, beautiful) / होइहि (will become) / सुजन (noble people) / मन (mind) / भावनी (delighting, pleasing) / भव (worldly existence) / अंग (body) / भूति (ash) / मसान (cremation ground) / की (of) / सुमिरत (remembering) / सुहावनि (beautiful, delightful) / पावनी (purifying)
ramacharitamanas::80.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::80.essence: Rama's fame can make even rough words beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::80.simple_meaning: Rama's story brings goodness and washes away the impurities of this age. Even a rough poem becomes beautiful when joined with his praise.
ramacharitamanas::80.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that sincerity matters more than polish when the heart is turned toward the divine.
ramacharitamanas::80.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses before his own poem and bows to Rama's glory. He admits his verse is rough, but says Rama's fame can make even imperfect words pleasing. The point is clear: the worth of the telling comes from the one being told.
ramacharitamanas::80.modern_relevance: You send a clumsy message to someone you love, worried it sounds awkward. Then they reply warmly, because the feeling was real. That's the power Tulsidas trusts in Rama's name.
ramacharitamanas::80.insight: It shifts attention from literary perfection to the transforming power of devotion.

ramacharitamanas::81.verse_sanskrit: दोहाः प्रिय लागिहि अति सबहि मम भनिति राम जस संग। दारु बिचारु कि करइ कोउ बंदिअ मलय प्रसंग ॥
ramacharitamanas::81.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के यश के संग से मेरी कविता सभी को अत्यन्त प्रिय लगेगी। जैसे मलय पर्वत के संग से काष्ठमात्र (चंदन बनकर) वंदनीय हो जाता है, फिर क्या कोई काठ (की तुच्छता) का विचार करता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::81.english_translation: My speech will become dear to everyone through the company of Ram's glory. Like ordinary wood honored by contact with the Malaya sandalwood mountain, who then thinks about its base nature?
ramacharitamanas::81.translation_literal: प्रिय (dear) / लागिहि (will become) / अति (very) / सबहि (to all) / मम (my) / भनिति (speech/poetry) / राम जस (Ram's glory) / संग (with company) / दारु (wood) / बिचारु (thought) / कि (what) / करइ (does) / कोउ (anyone) / बंदिअ (worshipped/honored) / मलय प्रसंग (contact with Malaya mountain)
ramacharitamanas::81.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::81.essence: Ram's glory makes even plain speech worthy of love.
ramacharitamanas::81.simple_meaning: A humble poem becomes beloved when it is joined to Ram's glory. Contact with greatness can make even something plain worthy of honor.
ramacharitamanas::81.simple_insight: You do not need to be impressive on your own. Let what is noble touch your words, work, and life.
ramacharitamanas::81.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is apologizing for the plainness of his verse in the Balkand frame. He says Ram's glory will make even rough poetry beloved, just as ordinary wood becomes honored when it is associated with sandalwood from Malaya. The verse defends devotion as the source of poetic worth.
ramacharitamanas::81.modern_relevance: You send a rough draft late at night, worried it sounds ordinary. Then one sharp, honest line changes everything. The value was never just in polish; it was in what gave the words their life.
ramacharitamanas::81.insight: It shifts attention from personal brilliance to the power of association with what is sacred and true.

ramacharitamanas::82.verse_sanskrit: स्याम सुरभि पय बिसद अति गुनद करहिं सब पान। गिरा ग्राम्य सिय राम जस गावहिं सुनहिं सुजान ॥
ramacharitamanas::82.verse_hindi: श्यामा गो काली होने पर भी उसका दूध उज्ज्वल और बहुत गुणकारी होता है। यही समझकर सब लोग उसे पीते हैं। इसी तरह गँवारू भाषा में होने पर भी श्री सीतारामजी के यश को बुद्धिमान लोग बड़े चाव से गाते और सुनते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::82.english_translation: Even a black cow's milk is pure and nourishing, so wise people drink it. In the same way, even though the language is simple, wise people gladly sing and hear the praise of Sita and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::82.translation_literal: स्याम (black) / सुरभि (cow) / पय (milk) / बिसद (clear, pure) / अति (very) / गुनद (full of qualities) / करहिं (do) / सब (all) / पान (drinking) / गिरा (speech, language) / ग्राम्य (simple, rustic) / सिय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / जस (praise, glory) / गावहिं (sing) / सुनहिं (hear) / सुजान (wise people)
ramacharitamanas::82.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::82.essence: Simple words become sacred when they carry loving praise.
ramacharitamanas::82.simple_meaning: Even plain, rustic language becomes sweet and nourishing when it carries praise of Sita and Ram. Wise people do not reject the form; they receive the devotion within it.
ramacharitamanas::82.simple_insight: You can let sincerity matter more than polish. What is true and loving reaches people even in simple words.
ramacharitamanas::82.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is defending his own humble Awadhi verse at the start of the Ramcharitmanas. He says that just as black cow's milk is still pure and nourishing, simple language can still carry the highest praise of Sita and Ram, and wise listeners will value the devotion, not the polish.
ramacharitamanas::82.modern_relevance: You send a heartfelt message that is awkward, unedited, and maybe a little plain. The person who matters feels it anyway. Real care does not need perfect packaging to land.
ramacharitamanas::82.insight: It shifts attention from literary elegance to the sincerity of what is being offered.

ramacharitamanas::83.verse_sanskrit: मनि मानिक मुकुता छबि जैसी। अहि गिरि गज सिर सोह न तैसी॥ नृप किरीट तरुनी तनु पाई। लहहिं सकल सोभा अधिकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::83.verse_hindi: मणि, माणिक और मोती की जैसी सुंदर छबि है, वह साँप, पर्वत और हाथी के मस्तक पर वैसी शोभा नहीं पाती। राजा के मुकुट और नवयुवती स्त्री के शरीर को पाकर ही ये सब अधिक शोभा को प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::83.english_translation: Gems and pearls are not truly beautiful on a snake, a mountain, or an elephant's head. They gain greater splendour when placed on a king's crown or a young woman's body.
ramacharitamanas::83.translation_literal: मनि (gem) / मानिक (ruby) / मुकुता (pearl) / छबि (beauty) / जैसी (like) / अहि (snake) / गिरि (mountain) / गज (elephant) / सिर (head) / सोह (adorns) / न (not) / तैसी (that kind) / नृप (king) / किरीट (crown) / तरुनी (young woman) / तनु (body) / पाई (having obtained) / लहहिं (receive) / सकल (all) / सोभा (splendour) / अधिकाई (greater)
ramacharitamanas::83.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::83.essence: Beauty appears fully only when placed where it belongs.
ramacharitamanas::83.simple_meaning: A gem looks best when it belongs where it truly fits. Out of place, even something precious loses its beauty.
ramacharitamanas::83.simple_insight: Right things shine more brightly in the right setting.
ramacharitamanas::83.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising his own telling of Ram's story. He says even precious jewels only reveal their full beauty when placed well, just as simple speech becomes radiant when joined to Ram's glory. This verse prepares the claim that his humble poetry gains worth through devotion.
ramacharitamanas::83.modern_relevance: A talented person can look ordinary in the wrong role, then suddenly seem brilliant in the right team, room, or responsibility. Fit changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::83.insight: It shifts attention from raw value to right placement and context.

ramacharitamanas::84.verse_sanskrit: तैसेहिं सुकबि कबित बुध कहहीं। उपजहिं अनत अनत छबि लहहीं॥ भगति हेतु बिधि भवन बिहाई। सुमिरत सारद आवति धाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::84.verse_hindi: इसी तरह, बुद्धिमान लोग कहते हैं कि सुकवि की कविता भी उत्पन्न और कहीं होती है और शोभा अन्यत्र कहीं पाती है (अर्थात कवि की वाणी से उत्पन्न हुई कविता वहाँ शोभा पाती है, जहाँ उसका विचार, प्रचार तथा उसमें कथित आदर्श का ग्रहण और अनुसरण होता है)। कवि के स्मरण करते ही उसकी भक्ति के कारण सरस्वतीजी ब्रह्मलोक को छोड़कर दौड़ी आती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::84.english_translation: In the same way, wise poets say their poetry is born in one place and finds its beauty in another. Out of devotion, Saraswati leaves her abode and rushes down at the poet's remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::84.translation_literal: तैसेहिं (in the same way) / सुकबि (good poet) / कबित (poetry) / बुध (wise people) / कहहीं (say) / उपजहिं (arises) / अनत (elsewhere) / अनत (elsewhere) / छबि (beauty, grace) / लहहीं (obtains)॥ भगति (devotion) / हेतु (because of) / बिधि (Brahma) / भवन (abode) / बिहाई (leaving behind) / सुमिरत (remembering) / सारद (Saraswati) / आवति (comes) / धाई (running) ॥
ramacharitamanas::84.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::84.essence: Devoted remembrance draws inspiration that the self cannot force.
ramacharitamanas::84.simple_meaning: Good poetry takes shape in one place but shines in another. Because of devotion, Saraswati leaves her own abode and comes running when the poet remembers her.
ramacharitamanas::84.simple_insight: Real inspiration feels received, not manufactured.
ramacharitamanas::84.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising sacred poetry itself. He says a true poet's words may be born from the poet, but their beauty appears where listeners receive them. In devotion, Saraswati herself rushes to the poet's aid.
ramacharitamanas::84.modern_relevance: You stare at a blank page, then a line arrives that feels larger than you. The best work often feels borrowed from somewhere beyond effort, not forced from willpower.
ramacharitamanas::84.insight: It shifts authorship from ego to devotion, showing that inspired speech comes when the mind remembers the divine.

ramacharitamanas::85.verse_sanskrit: राम चरित सर बिनु अन्हवाएँ। सो श्रम जाइ न कोटि उपाएँ॥ कबि कोबिद अस हृदयँ बिचारी। गावहिं हरि जस कलि मल हारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::85.verse_hindi: सरस्वतीजी की दौड़ी आने की वह थकावट रामचरित रूपी सरोवर में उन्हें नहलाए बिना दूसरे करोड़ों उपायों से भी दूर नहीं होती। कवि और पण्डित अपने हृदय में ऐसा विचारकर कलियुग के पापों को हरने वाले श्री हरि के यश का ही गान करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::85.english_translation: Only bathing in Ram's story can wash away this fatigue; no other effort of millions can remove it. Poets and scholars, reflecting this in their hearts, sing only the praises of Hari, who removes the stains of the age of conflict.
ramacharitamanas::85.translation_literal: राम चरित (Ram's story) / सर (lake) / बिनु (without) / अन्हवाएँ (bathing) / सो (that) / श्रम (fatigue) / जाइ (goes) / न (not) / कोटि (crores/millions) / उपाएँ (means) / कबि (poets) / कोबिद (scholars) / अस (thus) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारी (having reflected) / गावहिं (sing) / हरि (Hari/Ram) / जस (praise) / कलि (age of conflict) / मल (stains) / हारी (remover)
ramacharitamanas::85.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::85.essence: Ram's story cleans what countless remedies cannot.
ramacharitamanas::85.simple_meaning: Only Ram's story can wash away the weariness in the mind. Wise poets therefore sing Ram's praise, because it removes the stains of this difficult age.
ramacharitamanas::85.simple_insight: There is relief in turning from noise to devotion. Some fatigue is lifted only by what is sacred.
ramacharitamanas::85.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising the power of Ram's story itself. He says that the weariness created by worldly life cannot be removed by countless other remedies. Seeing this, poets and scholars naturally sing Ram's praise, because it purifies the age.
ramacharitamanas::85.modern_relevance: You have tried podcasts, advice threads, and another self-help book, but the heaviness remains. Then a single hymn, prayer, or story settles something deeper than analysis ever could.
ramacharitamanas::85.insight: It shifts attention from external fixes to devotional listening and praise as real purification.

ramacharitamanas::86.verse_sanskrit: कीन्हें प्राकृत जन गुन गाना। सिर धुनि गिरा लगत पछिताना॥ हृदय सिंधु मति सीप समाना। स्वाति सारदा कहहिं सुजाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::86.verse_hindi: संसारी मनुष्यों का गुणगान करने से सरस्वतीजी सिर धुनकर पछताने लगती हैं (कि मैं क्यों इसके बुलाने पर आई)। बुद्धिमान लोग हृदय को समुद्र, बुद्धि को सीप और सरस्वती को स्वाति नक्षत्र के समान कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::86.english_translation: When ordinary people are praised, Saraswati shakes her head in regret. The wise say the heart is an ocean, the intellect is a shell, and Saraswati comes like the Swati star.
ramacharitamanas::86.translation_literal: कीन्हें (done) / प्राकृत जन (ordinary people) / गुन गाना (singing praise of virtues) / सिर धुनि (shaking the head) / गिरा (speech) / लगत (becoming) / पछिताना (regretful) / हृदय (heart) / सिंधु (ocean) / मति (intellect) / सीप (shell) / समाना (compared) / स्वाति (Swati star) / सारदा (Saraswati) / कहहिं (say) / सुजाना (the wise)
ramacharitamanas::86.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::86.essence: True poetry appears when a receptive mind meets a vast heart.
ramacharitamanas::86.simple_meaning: Praise of ordinary people is shallow. True poetry comes when the heart is vast, the mind is receptive, and inspiration arrives like rare rain.
ramacharitamanas::86.simple_insight: Great expression does not come from forcing words. It comes when the mind is ready to receive something deeper.
ramacharitamanas::86.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is explaining why sacred poetry can arise at all. He says ordinary praise is too small to hold Saraswati's grace. A wise person sees the heart as an ocean, the intellect as a shell, and inspiration as Swati rain that turns inward readiness into beauty.
ramacharitamanas::86.modern_relevance: You stare at a blank page after ten half-finished drafts, trying to force brilliance. The line finally arrives only when your mind settles enough to receive it.
ramacharitamanas::86.insight: It shifts creativity from effortful performance to receptive depth.

ramacharitamanas::87.verse_sanskrit: जौं बरषइ बर बारि बिचारू। हो हिं कबित मुकुतामनि चारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::87.verse_hindi: इसमें यदि श्रेष्ठ विचार रूपी जल बरसता है तो मुक्ता मणि के समान सुंदर कविता होती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::87.english_translation: If rich thought rains down, poetry becomes a beautiful pearl necklace.
ramacharitamanas::87.translation_literal: जौं (if) / बरषइ (rains) / बर (excellent) / बारि (water) / बिचारू (thought, reflection) / हो हिं (become) / कबित (poetry) / मुकुतामनि (pearls) / चारू (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::87.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::87.essence: Deep thought turns poetry into something precious.
ramacharitamanas::87.simple_meaning: When deep thought flows into poetry, the result is something beautiful and precious, like pearls.
ramacharitamanas::87.simple_insight: Good words feel richer when they carry real thought, not just sound.
ramacharitamanas::87.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing what makes sacred poetry shine. After saying that ordinary praise is not enough, he explains that only when reflection rains into verse does poetry become as lovely and valuable as a string of pearls.
ramacharitamanas::87.modern_relevance: A speech full of polished lines can still feel empty. But when someone has truly thought through what they are saying, even a short message lands with weight and beauty.
ramacharitamanas::87.insight: It shifts attention from clever wording to the depth of thought beneath the wording.

ramacharitamanas::88.verse_sanskrit: जुगुति बेधि पुनि पोहिअहिं रामचरित बर ताग। पहिरहिं सज्जन बिमल उर सोभा अति अनुराग ॥
ramacharitamanas::88.verse_hindi: उन कविता रूपी मुक्तामणियों को युक्ति से बेधकर फिर रामचरित्र रूपी सुंदर तागे में पिरोकर सज्जन लोग अपने निर्मल हृदय में धारण करते हैं, जिससे अत्यन्त अनुराग रूपी शोभा होती है (वे आत्यन्तिक प्रेम को प्राप्त होते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::88.english_translation: Wise readers thread those pearl-like verses onto the beautiful string of Ram's story and wear them in their pure hearts, where they blossom as deep love.
ramacharitamanas::88.translation_literal: जुगुति (with skill) / बेधि (piercing, threading) / पुनि (again) / पोहिअहिं (are strung) / रामचरित (Ram's story) / बर (beautiful, excellent) / ताग (thread) / पहिरहिं (wear) / सज्जन (good people) / बिमल (pure) / उर (heart) / सोभा (splendor) / अति (greatly) / अनुराग (loving attachment)
ramacharitamanas::88.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::88.essence: Ram's story turns beautiful words into living devotion.
ramacharitamanas::88.simple_meaning: Good people take beautiful verses, connect them with Ram's story, and keep them in a pure heart. That turns poetry into deep love.
ramacharitamanas::88.simple_insight: Beautiful words matter most when they shape the heart, not just the mind.
ramacharitamanas::88.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has just compared true poetry to pearl-like verses born from clear thought. Now he says those verses become fully fruitful only when threaded into Ram's story and held in a pure heart. The result is not display, but loving devotion.
ramacharitamanas::88.modern_relevance: You save a line on your phone because it touched something real. Later, it matters only if it changes how you speak, choose, and love.
ramacharitamanas::88.insight: It shifts reading from collecting clever lines to letting sacred meaning reshape the heart.

ramacharitamanas::89.verse_sanskrit: जे जनमे कलिकाल कराला। करतब बायस बेष मराला॥ चलत कुपंथ बेद मग छाँड़े। कपट कलेवर कलि मल भाँड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::89.verse_hindi: जो कराल कलियुग में जन्मे हैं, जिनकी करनी कौए के समान है और वेष हंस का सा है, जो वेदमार्ग को छोड़कर कुमार्ग पर चलते हैं, जो कपट की मूर्ति और कलियुग के पापों के भाँड़ें हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::89.english_translation: Those born in the terrible age of Kali act like crows but dress like swans. They walk the wrong path, abandon the Vedas, and become masks of deceit and vessels of the age's corruption.
ramacharitamanas::89.translation_literal: जे (those) / जनमे (were born) / कलिकाल (the age of Kali) / कराला (terrible) । / करतब (deeds) / बायस (crow) / बेष (form/disguise) / मराला (swan) ॥ / चलत (walking) / कुपंथ (wrong path) / बेद (Veda) / मग (path) / छाँड़े (abandoned) । / कपट (deceit) / कलेवर (body/form) / कलि (Kali age) / मल (filth) / भाँड़े (vessels) ॥
ramacharitamanas::89.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::89.essence: False holiness hides corruption, but conduct always reveals the mask.
ramacharitamanas::89.simple_meaning: People can look noble while acting corrupt. They reject right conduct, follow the wrong path, and become full of deceit.
ramacharitamanas::89.simple_insight: Outward polish means nothing if the mind and actions are crooked.
ramacharitamanas::89.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing a dark pattern in Kali Yuga: people who seem refined on the outside but live by hypocrisy and wrongdoing. This line prepares the sharper warning that follows about false devotees and moral pretenders.
ramacharitamanas::89.modern_relevance: A polished speech, a clean profile picture, and the right vocabulary can still hide selfish motives. The real test is whether someone's conduct matches their appearance.
ramacharitamanas::89.insight: It trains you to judge character by conduct, not costume.

ramacharitamanas::90.verse_sanskrit: बंचक भगत कहाइ राम के। किंकर कंचन कोह काम के॥ तिन्ह महँ प्रथम रेख जग मोरी। धींग धरम ध्वज धंधक धोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::90.verse_hindi: जो श्री रामजी के भक्त कहलाकर लोगों को ठगते हैं, जो धन (लोभ), क्रोध और काम के गुलाम हैं और जो धींगाधींगी करने वाले, धर्मध्वजी (धर्म की झूठी ध्वजा फहराने वाले दम्भी) और कपट के धन्धों का बोझ ढोने वाले हैं, संसार के ऐसे लोगों में सबसे पहले मेरी गिनती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::90.english_translation: I count myself first among the world’s hypocrites: those who call themselves Ram’s devotees while deceiving others, those enslaved by greed, anger, and desire, and those who wear the banner of dharma while carrying the burden of deceit.
ramacharitamanas::90.translation_literal: बंचक (deceivers) / भगत (devotees) / कहाइ (called) / राम के (of Ram) / किंकर (servants) / कंचन (gold, greed) / कोह (anger) / काम (desire) / के (of) ॥ / तिन्ह (among those) / महँ (in) / प्रथम (first) / रेख (count) / जग (world) / मोरी (my) / धींग (boastful show) / धरम (dharma) / ध्वज (banner) / धंधक (deceitful trade) / धोरी (bearers)
ramacharitamanas::90.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::90.essence: Pretended devotion collapses under greed, anger, desire, and deceit.
ramacharitamanas::90.simple_meaning: False devotion is exposed here. People may wear the name of Ram, but greed, anger, desire, pride, and deceit reveal what they really serve.
ramacharitamanas::90.simple_insight: It stings because self-deception is easier to spot in others than in ourselves.
ramacharitamanas::90.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is speaking in a self-critical voice, listing the kinds of people who pretend to be holy while living by greed, anger, desire, and hypocrisy. He includes himself first, turning the criticism inward before he continues the larger teaching.
ramacharitamanas::90.modern_relevance: You post a quote about values, then snap at your family five minutes later. The gap between image and impulse is exactly what this verse refuses to hide.
ramacharitamanas::90.insight: It shifts attention from public appearance to private motive, asking the reader to examine whether devotion is real or only performed.

ramacharitamanas::91.verse_sanskrit: जौं अपने अवगुन सब कहऊँ। बाढ़इ कथा पार नहिं लहऊँ ॥ ताते मैं अति अलप बखाने। थोरे महुँ जानिहहिं सयाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::91.verse_hindi: यदि मैं अपने सब अवगुणों को कहने लगूँ तो कथा बहुत बढ़ जाएगी और मैं पार नहीं पाऊँगा। इससे मैंने बहुत कम अवगुणों का वर्णन किया है। बुद्धिमान लोग थोड़े ही में समझ लेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::91.english_translation: If I were to tell all my faults, the story would grow too long and I would never finish. So I have described only a few. Wise people will understand from so little.
ramacharitamanas::91.translation_literal: जौं (if) / अपने (own) / अवगुन (faults) / सब (all) / कहऊँ (I tell) / बाढ़इ (grows) / कथा (story) / पार (end / shore) / नहिं (not) / लहऊँ (I reach) ॥ ताते (therefore) / मैं (I) / अति (very) / अलप (few) / बखाने (described) / थोरे (few) / महुँ (in) / जानिहहिं (will understand) / सयाने (wise people) ॥
ramacharitamanas::91.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::91.essence: A few clear examples can carry a whole warning.
ramacharitamanas::91.simple_meaning: The speaker says he has only mentioned a few faults because listing every fault would make the story endless. Wise readers will understand the point from the small amount said.
ramacharitamanas::91.simple_insight: You do not need to say everything for the truth to land.
ramacharitamanas::91.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses in his moral critique of corrupt people and apologises for brevity. He says that if he listed every flaw, the narration would never end, so he has only named a few examples. The wise will grasp the warning from that small sample.
ramacharitamanas::91.modern_relevance: You write a long message pointing out what went wrong, then delete half of it because the point is already clear. Sometimes restraint makes a criticism sharper, not weaker.
ramacharitamanas::91.insight: It teaches the reader to state the essential point without drowning it in excess detail.

ramacharitamanas::92.verse_sanskrit: समुझि बिबिधि बिधि बिनती मोरी। कोउ न कथा सुनि देइहि खोरी॥ एतेहु पर करिहहिं जे असंका। मोहि ते अधिक ते जड़ मति रंका ॥
ramacharitamanas::92.verse_hindi: मेरी अनेकों प्रकार की विनती को समझकर, कोई भी इस कथा को सुनकर दोष नहीं देगा। इतने पर भी जो शंका करेंगे, वे तो मुझसे भी अधिक मूर्ख और बुद्धि के कंगाल हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::92.english_translation: Understanding my many kinds of humble request, no one will fault this story. Even so, whoever still doubts it is more foolish than I am, poor in understanding.
ramacharitamanas::92.translation_literal: समुझि (understanding) / बिबिधि बिधि (many kinds of) / बिनती (humble request) / मोरी (my) / कोउ (anyone) / न (not) / कथा (story) / सुनि (hearing) / देइहि (will give) / खोरी (fault) ॥ / एतेहु (even on this) / पर (still) / करिहहिं (will do) / जे (who) / असंका (doubt) / मोहि (me) / ते (than) / अधिक (more) / ते (than) / जड़ (foolish) / मति (understanding) / रंका (poor) ॥
ramacharitamanas::92.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::92.essence: Humble speech asks for trust before criticism.
ramacharitamanas::92.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he has already asked humbly, so no fair listener should criticize the story. Anyone who still doubts it is being foolish.
ramacharitamanas::92.simple_insight: A sincere request deserves a sincere hearing.
ramacharitamanas::92.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still setting the tone for his retelling of Ram's story. After admitting his own limits, he asks the reader to listen with generosity. This verse protects the devotional mood before the narration moves forward.
ramacharitamanas::92.modern_relevance: You share something tender and personal, and before anyone has even finished reading, they start picking at it. This verse asks for a fair hearing before judgment.
ramacharitamanas::92.insight: It shifts the reader from suspicion to receptive listening before the story unfolds.

ramacharitamanas::93.verse_sanskrit: कबि न होउँ नहिं चतुर कहावउँ। मति अनुरूप राम गुन गावउँ॥ कहँ रघुपति के चरित अपारा। कहँ मति मोरि निरत संसारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::93.verse_hindi: मैं न तो कवि हूँ, न चतुर कहलाता हूँ, अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार श्री रामजी के गुण गाता हूँ। कहाँ तो श्री रघुनाथजी के अपार चरित्र, कहाँ संसार में आसक्त मेरी बुद्धि ! ॥।
ramacharitamanas::93.english_translation: I am neither a poet nor one to be called clever; I sing Ram's virtues according to my own understanding. Where are the endless deeds of Raghupati, and where is my mind, still tied to the world?
ramacharitamanas::93.translation_literal: कबि (poet) / न होउँ (I am not) / नहिं (not) / चतुर (clever) / कहावउँ (I am called) / मति (intellect) / अनुरूप (according to) / राम (Ram) / गुन (virtues) / गावउँ (I sing) ॥ कहँ (where) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / के (of) / चरित (deeds) / अपारा (boundless) / कहँ (where) / मति (mind/intellect) / मोरि (my) / निरत (attached) / संसारा (world) ॥
ramacharitamanas::93.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::93.essence: Great praise begins with admitting your own smallness.
ramacharitamanas::93.simple_meaning: The poet says he is not a great scholar; he can only sing Ram's boundless virtues as best as he understands them, while knowing his own mind is still worldly and limited.
ramacharitamanas::93.simple_insight: Humility makes devotion honest. You do not need greatness to praise what is greater than you.
ramacharitamanas::93.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening his hymn with self-effacement. He places Ram's limitless deeds on one side and his own limited, worldly mind on the other, admitting the gap before he speaks at all. That humility becomes the foundation of the whole telling.
ramacharitamanas::93.modern_relevance: You sit down to write, present, or pray, and immediately feel unqualified. Instead of pretending expertise, you begin honestly from your actual understanding — and that honesty makes the work truer.
ramacharitamanas::93.insight: It shifts expression from self-display to sincere offering, so the focus stays on Ram rather than the speaker.

ramacharitamanas::94.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं मारुत गिरि मेरु उड़ाहीं। कहहु तूल केहि लेखे माहीं॥ समुझत अमित राम प्रभुताई। करत कथा मन अति कदराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::94.verse_hindi: जिस हवा से सुमेरु जैसे पहाड़ उड़ जाते हैं, कहिए तो, उसके सामने रूई किस गिनती में है। श्री रामजी की असीम प्रभुता को समझकर कथा रचने में मेरा मन बहुत हिचकता है- ॥
ramacharitamanas::94.english_translation: The wind that can lift Mount Meru can make cotton count for nothing. Understanding Ram's immeasurable greatness, my mind hesitates to tell this story.
ramacharitamanas::94.translation_literal: जेहिं (that which) / मारुत (wind) / गिरि (mountain) / मेरु (Meru) / उड़ाहीं (lift away) / कहहु (say) / तूल (cotton) / केहि (what) / लेखे (count) / माहीं (in the world) / समुझत (understanding) / अमित (immeasurable) / राम (Ram) / प्रभुताई (greatness, lordship) / करत (doing) / कथा (story) / मन (mind) / अति (very) / कदराई (hesitates)
ramacharitamanas::94.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::94.essence: Ram's greatness makes even the storyteller fall silent.
ramacharitamanas::94.simple_meaning: Ram's greatness is beyond measure, so the poet feels too small and hesitant to describe it fully.
ramacharitamanas::94.simple_insight: Humility opens the heart: some truths are so vast that reverence matters more than cleverness.
ramacharitamanas::94.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still framing his retelling of Ram's story. After apologising for his limits, he says Ram's greatness is so immense that even the strongest wind can move Meru, while cotton is nothing beside it. That awe makes him pause before speaking.
ramacharitamanas::94.modern_relevance: You sit down to write about someone who changed your life, and every sentence feels too small. The hesitation itself is respect; not everything sacred can be captured cleanly.
ramacharitamanas::94.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to master the subject to approaching it with humility and awe.

ramacharitamanas::95.verse_sanskrit: सारद सेस महेस बिधि आगम निगम पुरान। नेति नेति कहि जासु गुन करहिं निरंतर गान ॥
ramacharitamanas::95.verse_hindi: सरस्वतीजी, शेषजी, शिवजी, ब्रह्माजी, शास्त्र, वेद और पुराण- ये सब 'नेति-नेति' कहकर (पार नहीं पाकर 'ऐसा नहीं', ऐसा नहीं कहते हुए) सदा जिनका गुणगान किया करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::95.english_translation: Saraswati, Shesha, Shiva, Brahma, the scriptures, the Vedas, and the Puranas all sing endlessly of the one whose qualities they describe only by saying, 'not this, not this.'
ramacharitamanas::95.translation_literal: सारद (Saraswati) / सेस (Shesha) / महेस (Shiva) / बिधि (Brahma) / आगम (scriptures) / निगम (Vedas) / पुरान (Puranas) / नेति नेति (not this, not this) / कहि (saying) / जासु (whose) / गुन (qualities) / करहिं (do) / निरंतर (continually) / गान (singing)
ramacharitamanas::95.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::95.essence: The greatest praise is knowing words cannot contain him.
ramacharitamanas::95.simple_meaning: Even the greatest beings and the sacred texts can only point to Ram indirectly. His qualities are so vast that they keep praising him without ever exhausting him.
ramacharitamanas::95.simple_insight: There is comfort in not needing to capture the infinite perfectly. Reverence can continue even when language falls short.
ramacharitamanas::95.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has already admitted his own smallness. Now he says that even Saraswati, Shesha, Shiva, Brahma, the Vedas, and the Puranas can only approach Ram through 'not this, not this.' Their praise never ends because his greatness never runs out.
ramacharitamanas::95.modern_relevance: You try to explain someone you love, and every sentence feels too small. That frustration is not failure; it is a sign that the thing you are touching is larger than your words.
ramacharitamanas::95.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to define the divine to staying in humble, endless praise.

ramacharitamanas::96.verse_sanskrit: सब जानत प्रभु प्रभुता सोई। तदपि कहें बिनु रहा न कोई॥ तहाँ बेद अस कारन राखा। भजन प्रभाउ भाँति बहु भाषा ॥
ramacharitamanas::96.verse_hindi: यद्यपि प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी की प्रभुता को सब ऐसी (अकथनीय) ही जानते हैं, तथापि कहे बिना कोई नहीं रहा। इसमें वेद ने ऐसा कारण बताया है कि भजन का प्रभाव बहुत तरह से कहा गया है। (अर्थात भगवान की महिमा का पूरा वर्णन तो कोई कर नहीं सकता, परन्तु जिससे जितना बन पड़े उतना भगवान का गुणगान करना चाहिए, क्योंकि भगवान के गुणगान रूपी भजन का प्रभाव बहुत ही अनोखा है, उसका नाना प्रकार से शास्त्रों में वर्णन है। थोड़ा सा भी भगवान का भजन मनुष्य को सहज ही भवसागर से तार देता है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::96.english_translation: Everyone knows the Lord's greatness, yet no one can stop speaking of it. The Vedas give the reason: praise has many forms and great power.
ramacharitamanas::96.translation_literal: सब (all) / जानत (know) / प्रभु (the Lord) / प्रभुता (greatness) / सोई (that very) / तदपि (still) / कहें (to speak) / बिनु (without) / रहा (remained) / न (not) / कोई (anyone)॥ तहाँ (there) / बेद (the Vedas) / अस (such) / कारन (reason) / राखा (gave) / भजन (praise/devotion) / प्रभाउ (power/effect) / भाँति (ways) / बहु (many) / भाषा (forms of speech) ॥
ramacharitamanas::96.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::96.essence: Ram's greatness overflows into praise, and praise itself changes the one who speaks.
ramacharitamanas::96.simple_meaning: Everyone already knows Ram's greatness, yet people still keep speaking of it. The scriptures say praise itself has many forms and great power.
ramacharitamanas::96.simple_insight: It feels natural to keep returning to what you love most.
ramacharitamanas::96.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is pausing in the Balkand to explain why saints keep singing Ram even after admitting his greatness cannot be fully described. The point is not repetition; it is that praise itself transforms the one who speaks and listens.
ramacharitamanas::96.modern_relevance: You hear a song that reminds you of someone you miss, and you play it again. Not because the feeling is unfinished, but because love keeps finding new words. Ram's praise works the same way.
ramacharitamanas::96.insight: It shifts devotion from a duty to a living force that keeps deepening through speech.

ramacharitamanas::97.verse_sanskrit: एक अनीह अरूप अनामा। अज सच्चिदानंद पर धामा॥ ब्यापक बिस्वरूप भगवाना। तेहिं धरि देह चरित कृत नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::97.verse_hindi: जो परमेश्वर एक है, जिनके कोई इच्छा नहीं है, जिनका कोई रूप और नाम नहीं है, जो अजन्मा, सच्चिदानन्द और परमधाम है और जो सबमें व्यापक एवं विश्व रूप हैं, उन्हीं भगवान ने दिव्य शरीर धारण करके नाना प्रकार की लीला की है ॥
ramacharitamanas::97.english_translation: The one supreme being has no desire, no form, and no name. Unborn, pure awareness and bliss, the supreme abode, all-pervading and universal in form, that divine one takes a body and performs many plays.
ramacharitamanas::97.translation_literal: एक (one) / अनीह (without desire) / अरूप (without form) / अनामा (without name) / अज (unborn) / सच्चिदानंद (being-consciousness-bliss) / पर धामा (supreme abode) / व्यापक (all-pervading) / बिस्वरूप (universal form) / भगवाना (the divine) / तेहिं (that one) / धरि (having taken) / देह (body) / चरित (play/acts) / कृत (done) / नाना (many)
ramacharitamanas::97.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::97.essence: The formless one enters form without losing anything.
ramacharitamanas::97.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond form, name, and desire, yet he enters the world in a body and acts in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::97.simple_insight: It feels vast and intimate at once: the highest reality is not distant from life.
ramacharitamanas::97.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has just said Ram's glory cannot be fully spoken. Now he names that glory: Ram is beyond form, birth, and desire, yet he still appears in the world through a body and divine play. This sets up why his story can be both human and transcendent.
ramacharitamanas::97.modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary at first, then realize their calm changes the whole room. Ram's greatness works like that: the limitless can still arrive in a visible, human way.
ramacharitamanas::97.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing divinity as remote to seeing it as present within lived action.

ramacharitamanas::98.verse_sanskrit: सो केवल भगतन हित लागी। परम कृपाल प्रनत अनुरागी॥ जेहि जन पर ममता अति छोहू। जेहिं करुना करि कीन्ह न कोहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::98.verse_hindi: वह लीला केवल भक्तों के हित के लिए ही है, क्योंकि भगवान परम कृपालु हैं और शरणागत के बड़े प्रेमी हैं। जिनकी भक्तों पर बड़ी ममता और कृपा है, जिन्होंने एक बार जिस पर कृपा कर दी, उस पर फिर कभी क्रोध नहीं किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::98.english_translation: That play exists only for the sake of devotees. The supreme compassionate one loves those who surrender. He holds deep affection for his people, and once he shows mercy, he never turns to anger again.
ramacharitamanas::98.translation_literal: सो (that) / केवल (only) / भगतन (of devotees) / हित (for welfare) / लागी (for the sake of) / परम (supreme) / कृपाल (compassionate) / प्रनत (the surrendered) / अनुरागी (loving)॥ / जेहि (for whom) / जन (people) / पर (on) / ममता (affection) / अति (great) / छोहू (tenderness) / । / जेहिं (by whom) / करुना (compassion) / करि (having done) / कीन्ह (did) / न (not) / कोहू (anger)॥
ramacharitamanas::98.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::98.essence: Ram’s mercy is for the surrendered, and it does not turn back.
ramacharitamanas::98.simple_meaning: Ram's divine play is meant for devotees. He is deeply loving toward those who surrender, and once he shows kindness, he does not turn hostile again.
ramacharitamanas::98.simple_insight: You can rest in a love that does not keep score or withdraw its grace.
ramacharitamanas::98.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, Tulsidas pauses the story to explain Ram's nature. After describing the supreme being beyond form, he says Ram’s descent and actions are for devotees' welfare alone: he is tender toward the surrendered, full of compassion, and never returns to anger after giving grace.
ramacharitamanas::98.modern_relevance: After you finally admit you need help, the person who stays patient instead of shaming you changes everything. This verse points to a love that meets surrender with warmth, not punishment.
ramacharitamanas::98.insight: It shifts devotion from fear to trust by showing that grace, once given, is not revoked.

ramacharitamanas::99.verse_sanskrit: गई बहोर गरीब नेवाजू। सरल सबल साहिब रघुराजू॥ बुध बरनहिं हरि जस अस जानी। करहिं पुनीत सुफल निज बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::99.verse_hindi: वे प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी गई हुई वस्तु को फिर प्राप्त कराने वाले, गरीब नवाज (दीनबन्धु), सरल स्वभाव, सर्वशक्तिमान और सबके स्वामी हैं। यही समझकर बुद्धिमान लोग उन श्री हरि का यश वर्णन करके अपनी वाणी को पवित्र और उत्तम फल (मोक्ष और दुर्लभ भगवत्प्रेम) देने वाली बनाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::99.english_translation: Lord Raghunath restores what is lost. Gentle, mighty, and sovereign, Hari is praised by the wise, and that praise purifies speech and bears great fruit.
ramacharitamanas::99.translation_literal: गई (gone/lost) / बहोर (again, back) / गरीब नेवाजू (kind to the poor) / सरल (simple, gentle) / सबल (powerful) / साहिब (lord) / रघुराजू (king of Raghu)॥ / बुध (wise) / बरनहिं (describe, praise) / हरि (Hari) / जस (glory, praise) / अस (thus, in this way) / जानी (knowing) / करहिं (make, do) / पुनीत (pure) / सुफल (fruitful, with good result) / निज (own) / बानी (speech, words)॥
ramacharitamanas::99.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::99.essence: Praise of Ram purifies speech and turns words fruitful.
ramacharitamanas::99.simple_meaning: Ram is gentle, powerful, and kind to the poor. Wise people praise his glory, and that praise purifies their speech and gives it lasting fruit.
ramacharitamanas::99.simple_insight: Praise becomes worthwhile when it points the heart toward Ram and cleanses the way you speak.
ramacharitamanas::99.detailed_meaning: The narrator continues describing Ram as the gracious lord who restores what has been lost. Knowing his glory, wise people sing his praise, and that very speech becomes pure and fruitful. This supports the opening teaching about Ram’s divine nature and compassion.
ramacharitamanas::99.modern_relevance: After a day of talking too much, you hear yourself repeat complaints, gossip, and half-truths. Then one honest prayer or remembrance of Ram changes the whole tone of your voice.
ramacharitamanas::99.insight: It shifts speech from noise to devotion, making words an offering instead of a habit.

ramacharitamanas::100.verse_sanskrit: तेहिं बल मैं रघुपति गुन गाथा। कहिहउँ नाइ राम पद माथा॥ मुनिन्ह प्रथम हरि कीरति गाई। तेहिं मग चलत सुगम मोहि भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::100.verse_hindi: उसी बल से (महिमा का यथार्थ वर्णन नहीं, परन्तु महान फल देने वाला भजन समझकर भगवत्कृपा के बल पर ही) मैं श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर श्री रघुनाथजी के गुणों की कथा कहूँगा। इसी विचार से (वाल्मीकि, व्यास आदि) मुनियों ने पहले हरि की कीर्ति गाई है। भाई! उसी मार्ग पर चलना मेरे लिए सुगम होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::100.english_translation: By that power alone I will sing the praises of Raghupati, bowing my head at Ram's feet. The sages first sang Hari's glory; following that path makes it easy for me too.
ramacharitamanas::100.translation_literal: तेहिं (by that) / बल (power) / मैं (I) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / गुन (qualities) / गाथा (song, कथा) / कहिहउँ (I will speak) / नाइ (bowing) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / माथा (head)॥ / मुनिन्ह (by the sages) / प्रथम (first) / हरि (Hari, Ram) / कीरति (glory, praise) / गाई (sang) / तेहिं (that) / मग (path) / चलत (walking) / सुगम (easy) / मोहि (for me) / भाई (brother) ॥
ramacharitamanas::100.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::100.essence: True praise begins with bowed head, not clever speech.
ramacharitamanas::100.simple_meaning: The poet says he can speak of Ram only by Ram's grace. He bows first, then follows the path the sages used: praising the divine before trying to describe it.
ramacharitamanas::100.simple_insight: Humility opens the way. Praise becomes possible only after surrender.
ramacharitamanas::100.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is not launching a story; he is stopping to take permission from Ram before speaking. He says the sages already walked this path by singing Hari's glory first, and he will do the same so his words remain blessed and easy.
ramacharitamanas::100.modern_relevance: Before you explain something sacred, personal, or deeply important, you pause. You don't rush to sound clever; you begin with respect, because some words only come cleanly after humility.
ramacharitamanas::100.insight: It shifts speech from self-confidence to reverent dependence, so the words feel received rather than manufactured.

ramacharitamanas::101.verse_sanskrit: अति अपार जे सरित बर जौं नृप सेतु कराहिं। चढ़ि पिपीलिकउ परम लघु बिनु श्रम पारहि जाहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::101.verse_hindi: जो अत्यन्त बड़ी श्रेष्ठ नदियाँ हैं, यदि राजा उन पर पुल बँधा देता है, तो अत्यन्त छोटी चींटियाँ भी उन पर चढ़कर बिना ही परिश्रम के पार चली जाती हैं। (इसी प्रकार मुनियों के वर्णन के सहारे मैं भी श्री रामचरित्र का वर्णन सहज ही कर सकूँगा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::101.english_translation: If a king builds a bridge over vast rivers, even tiny ants cross them without effort.
ramacharitamanas::101.translation_literal: अति अपार (extremely vast) / जे (which) / सरित (rivers) / बर (excellent, great) / जौं (if) / नृप (king) / सेतु (bridge) / कराहिं (build) / चढ़ि (climbing) / पिपीलिकउ (even an ant) / परम लघु (very small) / बिनु श्रम (without effort) / पारहि (across) / जाहिं (go)
ramacharitamanas::101.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::101.essence: A great bridge lets even the smallest cross without strain.
ramacharitamanas::101.simple_meaning: A great bridge makes crossing huge rivers easy, even for the smallest creature. In the same way, a wise helper can make a huge task feel possible.
ramacharitamanas::101.simple_insight: Support from the right source can turn a daunting task into an easy crossing.
ramacharitamanas::101.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is preparing to tell Ram's story and comparing his effort to ants crossing a river bridge. The point is not the ant, but the bridge: with the right support, even a tiny capacity can reach the far shore.
ramacharitamanas::101.modern_relevance: You open a document that once felt impossible, and the right template is already there. What looked overwhelming becomes manageable because someone built the bridge before you arrived.
ramacharitamanas::101.insight: It shifts attention from personal strength to enabling conditions that make action possible.

ramacharitamanas::102.verse_sanskrit: एहि प्रकार बल मनहि देखाई। करिहउँ रघुपति कथा सुहाई॥ ब्यास आदि कबि पुंगव नाना। जिन्ह सादर हरि सुजस बखाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::102.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार मन को बल दिखलाकर मैं श्री रघुनाथजी की सुहावनी कथा की रचना करूँगा। व्यास आदि जो अनेकों श्रेष्ठ कवि हो गए हैं, जिन्होंने बड़े आदर से श्री हरि का सुयश वर्णन किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::102.english_translation: In this way, I steady my mind and will compose the lovely story of Raghupati. Vyasa and many other great poets have respectfully sung Hari's fame.
ramacharitamanas::102.translation_literal: एहि प्रकार (in this way) / बल (strength) / मनहि (the mind) / देखाई (showing) / करिहउँ (I will do) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / कथा (story) / सुहाई (lovely, pleasing)॥ / ब्यास (Vyasa) / आदि (and others) / कबि पुंगव (best among poets) / नाना (many) / जिन्ह (who) / सादर (with respect) / हरि (Hari) / सुजस (glorious fame) / बखाना (described) ॥
ramacharitamanas::102.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::102.essence: Humility steadies the mind before sacred work begins.
ramacharitamanas::102.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he will steady his mind and then tell Ram's beautiful story, following the example of great poets who praised Hari with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::102.simple_insight: A humble mind can still create something beautiful when it leans on reverence.
ramacharitamanas::102.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening his retelling of Ram's story. After bowing to earlier poets like Vyasa, he says he will gather his mind's strength and begin a graceful narration. This is the poet preparing himself, not yet the teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::102.modern_relevance: Before starting a difficult project, you take a breath, collect yourself, and remember the people who did it well before you. That steadies your hand more than raw confidence ever could.
ramacharitamanas::102.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to disciplined humility before creative work.

ramacharitamanas::103.verse_sanskrit: चरन कमल बंदउँ तिन्ह केरे। पुरवहुँ सकल मनोरथ मेरे॥ कलि के कबिन्ह करउँ परनामा। जिन्ह बरने रघुपति गुन ग्रामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::103.verse_hindi: मैं उन सब (श्रेष्ठ कवियों) के चरणकमलों में प्रणाम करता हूँ, वे मेरे सब मनोरथों को पूरा करें। कलियुग के भी उन कवियों को मैं प्रणाम करता हूँ, जिन्होंने श्री रघुनाथजी के गुण समूहों का वर्णन किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::103.english_translation: I bow to the feet of those poets; may they fulfill all my desires. I bow to the poets of Kali Yuga who have described the virtues and hosts of Raghupati.
ramacharitamanas::103.translation_literal: चरन कमल (lotus feet) / बंदउँ (I bow) / तिन्ह केरे (of those) / पुरवहुँ (may fulfill) / सकल (all) / मनोरथ (desires) / मेरे (my) / कलि के (of Kali Yuga's) / कबिन्ह (poets) / करउँ (I do) / परनामा (salutation) / जिन्ह (who) / बरने (described) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / गुन (virtues) / ग्रामा (hosts, groups)
ramacharitamanas::103.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::103.essence: True devotion begins by honoring those who kept Ram's name alive.
