ramacharitamanas::103.simple_meaning: The poet bows to earlier poets who praised Ram, asking their blessings. He also honors the poets of the present age who have sung Ram's virtues.
ramacharitamanas::103.simple_insight: Praise itself becomes an offering when it is given with humility and gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::103.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening his own telling of Ram's story by bowing to the poets before him. He treats their praise of Ram as sacred inheritance, not competition. This verse sets a devotional tone before the story moves forward.
ramacharitamanas::103.modern_relevance: You open a book, an essay, or a song and remember it did not begin with you. Someone else cleared the path, and gratitude makes your own work cleaner.
ramacharitamanas::103.insight: It shifts creation from self-display to reverent participation in a shared tradition.

ramacharitamanas::104.verse_sanskrit: जे प्राकृत कबि परम सयाने। भाषाँ जिन्ह हरि चरित बखाने॥ भए जे अहहिं जे होइहहिं आगें। प्रनवउँ सबहि कपट सब त्यागें ॥
ramacharitamanas::104.verse_hindi: जो बड़े बुद्धिमान प्राकृत कवि हैं, जिन्होंने भाषा में हरि चरित्रों का वर्णन किया है, जो ऐसे कवि पहले हो चुके हैं, जो इस समय वर्तमान हैं और जो आगे होंगे, उन सबको मैं सारा कपट त्यागकर प्रणाम करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::104.english_translation: I bow to all poets without deceit: the wise earthly poets who have described Hari's deeds in language, those who have lived before, those who live now, and those who will come after.
ramacharitamanas::104.translation_literal: जे (those who) / प्राकृत (earthly, worldly) / कबि (poets) / परम सयाने (very wise) / भाषाँ (in language) / जिन्ह (who) / हरि चरित (Hari's deeds) / बखाने (described) / भए (were) / जे (who) / अहहिं (are) / जे (who) / होइहहिं (will be) / आगें (in future) / प्रनवउँ (I bow) / सबहि (to all) / कपट (deceit) / सब (all) / त्यागें (having abandoned)
ramacharitamanas::104.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::104.essence: Humility honors every true voice before it speaks.
ramacharitamanas::104.simple_meaning: The poet bows to every sincere poet who has ever described Ram's deeds, past, present, and future, and does so without any deceit or ego.
ramacharitamanas::104.simple_insight: Real humility makes room for everyone who has served the same sacred story.
ramacharitamanas::104.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening his work by bowing to earlier, current, and future poets who have sung Ram's story. He is not claiming ownership of the tale; he begins by setting aside pride so his own telling can enter a long tradition.
ramacharitamanas::104.modern_relevance: Before you publish the article, post the poem, or launch the project, you remember the people who taught you how to do it. The work feels cleaner when ego steps aside.
ramacharitamanas::104.insight: It shifts authorship from self-display to gratitude and lineage.

ramacharitamanas::105.verse_sanskrit: होहु प्रसन्न देहु बरदानू। साधु समाज भनिति सनमानू॥ जो प्रबंध बुध नहिं आदरहीं। सो श्रम बादि बाल कबि करहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::105.verse_hindi: आप सब प्रसन्न होकर यह वरदान दीजिए कि साधु समाज में मेरी कविता का सम्मान हो, क्योंकि बुद्धिमान लोग जिस कविता का आदर नहीं करते, मूर्ख कवि ही उसकी रचना का व्यर्थ परिश्रम करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::105.english_translation: Be pleased and grant this boon: let the noble community honor this poem. Wise people do not respect a composition, so foolish poets labor in vain.
ramacharitamanas::105.translation_literal: होहु (be) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / देहु (give) / बरदानू (boon) / साधु समाज (noble community) / भनिति (poem/speech) / सनमानू (honor) / जो (which) / प्रबंध (composition) / बुध (wise people) / नहिं (do not) / आदरहीं (respect) / सो (that) / श्रम (effort) / बादि (in vain) / बाल कबि (foolish poets) / करहीं (do) ॥
ramacharitamanas::105.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::105.essence: A work matters when the wise can honor it.
ramacharitamanas::105.simple_meaning: The poet asks for a blessing: may thoughtful people honor this poem, because writing that no wise person values is wasted effort.
ramacharitamanas::105.simple_insight: Good work wants the right audience. Recognition matters less than offering something worthy to the sincere.
ramacharitamanas::105.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening the Ramcharitmanas by bowing to earlier poets and asking for blessing. He wants his work welcomed by saintly listeners, because he knows a composition has meaning only when the wise receive it well.
ramacharitamanas::105.modern_relevance: You finish something deeply personal and send it into the world, not knowing whether anyone will understand it. The verse carries that quiet hope: let the right people receive what you made.
ramacharitamanas::105.insight: It shifts attention from applause to worthy reception, and from vanity to sincere offering.

ramacharitamanas::106.verse_sanskrit: कीरति भनिति भूति भलि सोई। सुरसरि सम सब कहँ हित होई॥ राम सुकीरति भनिति भदेसा। असमंजस अस मोहि अँदेसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::106.verse_hindi: कीर्ति, कविता और सम्पत्ति वही उत्तम है, जो गंगाजी की तरह सबका हित करने वाली हो। श्री रामचन्द्रजी की कीर्ति तो बड़ी सुंदर (सबका अनन्त कल्याण करने वाली ही) है, परन्तु मेरी कविता भद्दी है। यह असामंजस्य है (अर्थात इन दोनों का मेल नहीं मिलता), इसी की मुझे चिन्ता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::106.english_translation: Good fame, good speech, and good wealth are only those that benefit everyone like the Ganga. Ram's fame is truly beautiful, but my poetry is crude. That mismatch troubles me.
ramacharitamanas::106.translation_literal: कीरति (fame) / भनिति (speech, poetry) / भूति (wealth) / भलि (good) / सोई (that only) / सुरसरि (Ganga, river of the gods) / सम (like) / सब कहँ (for all) / हित (benefit) / होई (is) / राम (Ram) / सुकीरति (good fame) / भनिति (speech, poetry) / भदेसा (crude, awkward) / असमंजस (mismatch, confusion) / अस (thus) / मोहि (to me) / अँदेसा (anxiety, worry)
ramacharitamanas::106.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::106.essence: True worth helps everyone; anything else is only decoration.
ramacharitamanas::106.simple_meaning: Only fame, speech, and wealth that help everyone are truly good. Ram's glory is pure and beneficial, but the poet feels his own words fall short of that standard.
ramacharitamanas::106.simple_insight: You can admire greatness without pretending your own work already matches it.
ramacharitamanas::106.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still speaking in his humble preface, asking learned listeners to pardon his crude verse. He measures all value by one test: does it benefit everyone like the Ganga? Ram's glory passes that test; his own poetry worries him.
ramacharitamanas::106.modern_relevance: You publish something heartfelt and then reread it at midnight, noticing every rough edge. The gap between what you meant and what you made can sting — but it can also keep you honest.
ramacharitamanas::106.insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to usefulness: value is what blesses others, not what flatters the maker.

ramacharitamanas::107.verse_sanskrit: तुम्हरी कृपाँ सुलभ सोउ मोरे। सिअनि सुहावनि टाट पटोरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::107.verse_hindi: परन्तु हे कवियों! आपकी कृपा से यह बात भी मेरे लिए सुलभ हो सकती है। रेशम की सिलाई टाट पर भी सुहावनी लगती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::107.english_translation: Yet by your grace, even that may be easy for me. Silk stitching looks lovely even on coarse sackcloth.
ramacharitamanas::107.translation_literal: तुम्हरी (your) / कृपाँ (by grace) / सुलभ (easy, attainable) / सोउ (that too) / मोरे (for me) / सिअनि (stitching, sewing) / सुहावनि (beautiful, lovely) / टाट (coarse sackcloth) / पटोरे (on sackcloth)
ramacharitamanas::107.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::107.essence: Grace can make rough work beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::107.simple_meaning: By your grace, even something difficult becomes possible for me. Just as fine stitching can make rough cloth look beautiful, your kindness can make my poor poetry acceptable.
ramacharitamanas::107.simple_insight: Humility opens the door to grace. What feels inadequate can still become beautiful when offered sincerely.
ramacharitamanas::107.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is asking learned listeners to forgive the roughness of his verse. After praising simple, useful poetry, he admits his own work may be plain and imperfect, yet says their grace can make it pleasing — like fine stitching on coarse cloth.
ramacharitamanas::107.modern_relevance: You send out a draft that still feels rough, then wait for feedback with a tight chest. This line softens that fear: sincerity and grace can make imperfect work land beautifully.
ramacharitamanas::107.insight: It shifts the mind from self-judgment to receptive humility, trusting that effort plus grace can refine the result.

ramacharitamanas::108.verse_sanskrit: सरल कबित कीरति बिमल सोइ आदरहिं सुजान। सहज बयर बिसराइ रिपु जो सुनि करहिं बखान ॥
ramacharitamanas::108.verse_hindi: चतुर पुरुष उसी कविता का आदर करते हैं, जो सरल हो और जिसमें निर्मल चरित्र का वर्णन हो तथा जिसे सुनकर शत्रु भी स्वाभाविक बैर को भूलकर सराहना करने लगें ॥
ramacharitamanas::108.english_translation: Wise people honor poetry that is simple and pure, and even enemies forget their natural hostility when they hear it praised.
ramacharitamanas::108.translation_literal: सरल (simple) / कबित (poetry) / कीरति (praise, fame) / बिमल (pure) / सोइ (that only) / आदरहिं (honor) / सुजान (wise people) / सहज (natural) / बयर (enmity) / बिसराइ (forgetting) / रिपु (enemy) / जो (who) / सुनि (hearing) / करहिं (do) / बखान (praise, recitation)
ramacharitamanas::108.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::108.essence: Pure praise is so natural it can soften even an enemy.
ramacharitamanas::108.simple_meaning: Good poetry is simple, pure, and worthy of respect. Its beauty is so natural that even an enemy can hear it and set aside hostility.
ramacharitamanas::108.simple_insight: There is relief in beauty that needs no defense and no cleverness to be real.
ramacharitamanas::108.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising the kind of verse he wants to write about Ram. After saying that true fame should benefit everyone, he says wise readers honor poetry that is simple and pure, because real beauty softens even an enemy’s mind.
ramacharitamanas::108.modern_relevance: You read something so honest that your guard drops for a moment. No flashy argument, no hidden agenda — just words clean enough to make suspicion feel unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::108.insight: It shifts attention from cleverness to purity of expression, showing that genuine beauty can dissolve resistance.

ramacharitamanas::109.verse_sanskrit: सो न होई बिनु बिमल मति मोहि मति बल अति थोर। करहु कृपा हरि जस कहउँ पुनि पुनि करउँ निहोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::109.verse_hindi: ऐसी कविता बिना निर्मल बुद्धि के होती नहीं और मेरी बुद्धि का बल बहुत ही थोड़ा है, इसलिए बार-बार निहोरा करता हूँ कि हे कवियों! आप कृपा करें, जिससे मैं हरि यश का वर्णन कर सकूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::109.english_translation: Poetry like this cannot arise without pure understanding, and my understanding is very weak. So I beg again and again: poets, be kind, so I may describe the glory of Hari.
ramacharitamanas::109.translation_literal: सो (that) / न होई (does not happen) / बिनु (without) / बिमल मति (pure understanding) / मोहि (my) / मति बल (strength of understanding) / अति थोर (very little) / करहु कृपा (do kindness) / हरि जस (Hari's glory) / कहउँ (I may speak) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / करउँ निहोर (I make request)
ramacharitamanas::109.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::109.essence: True praise begins with humility and a plea for grace.
ramacharitamanas::109.simple_meaning: Pure praise needs a clear mind, and the poet admits his own mind is too weak. He begs for grace so he can speak of Ram's glory.
ramacharitamanas::109.simple_insight: Humility opens the door to real devotion. The prayer itself becomes part of the praise.
ramacharitamanas::109.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is turning to the poets and learned listeners before beginning Ram's story. He says his own understanding is too small to do justice to Hari's glory, so he asks for their grace and help. This verse sets the devotional tone for the narration that follows.
ramacharitamanas::109.modern_relevance: You sit down to write, speak, or create, and the words feel smaller than what you want to express. Instead of pretending certainty, you ask for help and begin honestly.
ramacharitamanas::109.insight: It shifts creation from self-confidence to surrendered offering.

ramacharitamanas::110.verse_sanskrit: कबि कोबिद रघुबर चरित मानस मंजु मराल। बालबिनय सुनि सुरुचि लखि मो पर होहु कृपाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::110.verse_hindi: कवि और पण्डितगण! आप जो रामचरित्र रूपी मानसरोवर के सुंदर हंस हैं, मुझ बालक की विनती सुनकर और सुंदर रुचि देखकर मुझ पर कृपा करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::110.english_translation: O poets and scholars, you graceful swans on the lovely lake of Ram's story, hear this child's plea and, seeing my good intent, be kind to me.
ramacharitamanas::110.translation_literal: कबि (poets) / कोबिद (scholars) / रघुबर (Ram) / चरित (deeds/story) / मानस (lake of the mind; here, the sacred lake) / मंजु (beautiful) / मराल (swans) / बालबिनय (child's plea) / सुनि (hearing) / सुरुचि (good taste; good intent) / लखि (seeing) / मो (to me) / पर (upon) / होहु (be) / कृपाल (kind, compassionate)
ramacharitamanas::110.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::110.essence: Humility opens the door before the story even begins.
ramacharitamanas::110.simple_meaning: Tulsidas humbly asks learned readers to listen kindly to his childlike request and judge his work with goodwill.
ramacharitamanas::110.simple_insight: Real devotion begins with humility, not performance.
ramacharitamanas::110.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening his telling of Ram's story. Before the narrative begins, he bows to poets and scholars, comparing them to swans on a beautiful lake. He asks them to hear his simple plea kindly and look at his good intention.
ramacharitamanas::110.modern_relevance: You send a draft to someone you respect, knowing it is rough but sincere. You are not demanding praise — only a fair hearing and a little grace.
ramacharitamanas::110.insight: It teaches you to approach worthy listeners with humility and honest intent.

ramacharitamanas::111.verse_sanskrit: बंदउँ मुनि पद कंजु रामायन जेहिं निरमयउ। सखर सुकोमल मंजु दोष रहित दूषन सहित ॥
ramacharitamanas::111.verse_hindi: मैं उन वाल्मीकि मुनि के चरण कमलों की वंदना करता हूँ, जिन्होंने रामायण की रचना की है, जो खर (राक्षस) सहित होने पर भी (खर (कठोर) से विपरीत) बड़ी कोमल और सुंदर है तथा जो दूषण (राक्षस) सहित होने पर भी दूषण अर्थात् दोष से रहित है ॥
ramacharitamanas::111.english_translation: I bow to the sage's lotus feet that gave us the Ramayana, which is soft and beautiful, yet free of faults even though it contains Khara and Dushana.
ramacharitamanas::111.translation_literal: बंदउँ (I bow) / मुनि (sage) / पद (feet) / कंजु (lotus) / रामायन (Ramayana) / जेहिं (which) / निरमयउ (was composed) / सखर (with Khara) / सुकोमल (very tender) / मंजु (beautiful) / दोष रहित (free of faults) / दूषन सहित (with Dushana)
ramacharitamanas::111.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::111.essence: Beauty can contain hardness without becoming hard itself.
ramacharitamanas::111.simple_meaning: Tulsidas bows to Valmiki, praising the Ramayana as a beautiful work that remains pure and graceful even though it includes fierce and harsh characters.
ramacharitamanas::111.simple_insight: Great art can hold conflict without losing its grace.
ramacharitamanas::111.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening his own retelling by bowing to Valmiki, the sage who composed the Ramayana. He praises the original poem as delicate and beautiful, yet untouched by flaw, even though it contains the fierce demons Khara and Dushana.
ramacharitamanas::111.modern_relevance: A film can show violence, betrayal, and grief without becoming cruel itself. The maker's touch can remain gentle even while the story enters darkness.
ramacharitamanas::111.insight: It teaches you to recognize purity of intention even inside difficult material.

ramacharitamanas::112.verse_sanskrit: बंदउँ चारिउ बेद भव बारिधि बोहित सरिस। जिन्हहि न सपनेहुँ खेद बरनत रघुबर बिसद जसु ॥
ramacharitamanas::112.verse_hindi: मैं चारों वेदों की वन्दना करता हूँ, जो संसार समुद्र के पार होने के लिए जहाज के समान हैं तथा जिन्हें श्री रघुनाथजी का निर्मल यश वर्णन करते स्वप्न में भी खेद (थकावट) नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::112.english_translation: I bow to the four Vedas, which are like a boat for crossing the ocean of worldly life, and which never tire, even in dreams, of describing the pure fame of Raghunath.
ramacharitamanas::112.translation_literal: बंदउँ (I bow) / चारिउ (four) / बेद (Vedas) / भव (worldly existence) / बारिधि (ocean) / बोहित (boat) / सरिस (like) / जिन्हहि (those who) / न (not) / सपनेहुँ (even in dreams) / खेद (fatigue) / बरनत (describing) / रघुबर (Raghunath) / बिसद (pure) / जसु (fame)
ramacharitamanas::112.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::112.essence: True scripture carries seekers across confusion without ever losing freshness.
ramacharitamanas::112.simple_meaning: The four Vedas are praised as a boat that helps people cross the ocean of worldly life, and they never grow tired of praising Ram's pure glory.
ramacharitamanas::112.simple_insight: Real guidance does not wear out. It keeps carrying people forward and keeps praising what is highest.
ramacharitamanas::112.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening his praise of sacred learning in the Balkand. After bowing to Valmiki, he bows to the four Vedas as the boat that carries beings across the ocean of worldly existence. Their endless praise of Ram prepares the ground for the sacred story that follows.
ramacharitamanas::112.modern_relevance: You are exhausted by endless feeds, advice threads, and half-answers. Then one clear source arrives, and it still feels fresh on the hundredth reading because it points beyond confusion.
ramacharitamanas::112.insight: It shifts attention from scattered opinions to a trustworthy source that carries the seeker across confusion.

ramacharitamanas::113.verse_sanskrit: बंदउँ बिधि पद रेनु भव सागर जेहिं कीन्ह जहँ। संत सुधा ससि धेनु प्रगटे खल बिष बारुनी॥14च॥
ramacharitamanas::113.verse_hindi: मैं ब्रह्माजी के चरण रज की वन्दना करता हूँ, जिन्होंने भवसागर बनाया है, जहाँ से एक ओर संतरूपी अमृत, चन्द्रमा और कामधेनु निकले और दूसरी ओर दुष्ट मनुष्य रूपी विष और मदिरा उत्पन्न हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::113.english_translation: I bow to the dust of Brahma's feet, who made this world-ocean, from which saints, nectar, the moon, and Kamadhenu arose, while evil people arose like poison and liquor.
ramacharitamanas::113.translation_literal: बंदउँ (I bow) / बिधि (Brahma) / पद (feet) / रेनु (dust) / भव सागर (world-ocean) / जेहिं (by whom) / कीन्ह (made) / जहँ (where) / संत (saints) / सुधा (nectar) / ससि (moon) / धेनु (cow) / प्रगटे (arose) / खल (evil people) / बिष (poison) / बारुनी (liquor) /
ramacharitamanas::113.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::113.essence: The same creation yields nectar for some and poison for others.
ramacharitamanas::113.simple_meaning: Brahma is praised as the creator of the world-ocean, where both noble and harmful things appear. Saints and blessings arise on one side; poison and corrupting forces on the other.
ramacharitamanas::113.simple_insight: Creation holds both beauty and danger. The same world can nourish virtue or feed corruption.
ramacharitamanas::113.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is moving through a chain of praise at the opening of the Ramcharitmanas. After honoring Valmiki and the Vedas, he bows to Brahma, the creator, and describes the created world as a vast ocean that produces both sacred gifts and destructive poisons.
ramacharitamanas::113.modern_relevance: You walk into the same city and one person leaves inspired, another leaves hardened. The place did not change; what it brings out in people did.
ramacharitamanas::113.insight: It shifts attention from blaming the world itself to seeing how the same conditions can reveal either refinement or corruption.

ramacharitamanas::114.verse_sanskrit: बिबुध बिप्र बुध ग्रह चरन बंदि कहउँ कर जोरि। होइ प्रसन्न पुरवहु सकल मंजु मनोरथ मोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::114.verse_hindi: देवता, ब्राह्मण, पंडित, ग्रह- इन सबके चरणों की वंदना करके हाथ जोड़कर कहता हूँ कि आप प्रसन्न होकर मेरे सारे सुंदर मनोरथों को पूरा करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::114.english_translation: I bow with joined hands to the gods, Brahmins, wise ones, and planets. Be pleased and fulfill all my lovely wishes.
ramacharitamanas::114.translation_literal: बिबुध (gods) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / बुध (wise ones) / ग्रह (planets) / चरन (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / कहउँ (I say) / कर (hands) / जोरि (joining) / होइ (be) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / पुरवहु (fulfill) / सकल (all) / मंजु (lovely) / मनोरथ (wishes) / मोरि (my)
ramacharitamanas::114.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::114.essence: Respectful humility invites help before any worthy beginning.
ramacharitamanas::114.simple_meaning: The poet offers respect to all auspicious powers and asks them to bless the completion of his wishes.
ramacharitamanas::114.simple_insight: Humility opens the way for a prayer to be heard.
ramacharitamanas::114.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still in his opening invocation, bowing to every source of blessing before beginning the sacred story. He asks the gods, Brahmins, wise ones, and even the planets to be pleased so his work may succeed.
ramacharitamanas::114.modern_relevance: Before starting something important, you pause, clear your pride, and ask for support from everyone who can help. The work begins better when ego steps aside.
ramacharitamanas::114.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to reverent preparation before action.

ramacharitamanas::115.verse_sanskrit: पुनि बंदउँ सारद सुरसरिता। जुगल पुनीत मनोहर चरिता॥ मज्जन पान पाप हर एका। कहत सुनत एक हर अबिबेका ॥
ramacharitamanas::115.verse_hindi: फिर मैं सरस्वती और देवनदी गंगाजी की वंदना करता हूँ। दोनों पवित्र और मनोहर चरित्र वाली हैं। एक (गंगाजी) स्नान करने और जल पीने से पापों को हरती है और दूसरी (सरस्वतीजी) गुण और यश कहने और सुनने से अज्ञान का नाश कर देती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::115.english_translation: I again bow to Saraswati and the sacred Ganga. Both are pure and lovely in character. One removes sin through bathing and drinking; the other destroys ignorance through speaking and hearing.
ramacharitamanas::115.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / बंदउँ (I bow) / सारद (Saraswati) / सुरसरिता (river of the gods, Ganga) / जुगल (both) / पुनीत (pure) / मनोहर (lovely) / चरिता (character, conduct) / मज्जन (bathing) / पान (drinking) / पाप (sin, impurity) / हर (removes) / एका (one) / कहत (speaking) / सुनत (hearing) / एक (the other, one) / हर (removes) / अबिबेका (ignorance, lack of discrimination)
ramacharitamanas::115.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::115.essence: Water clears the body; wise words clear confusion.
ramacharitamanas::115.simple_meaning: Saraswati and Ganga are both honored here. One cleanses through water; the other cleanses through hearing and speaking, removing ignorance.
ramacharitamanas::115.simple_insight: Purity is not only physical. Words, listening, and understanding can also cleanse the mind.
ramacharitamanas::115.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is offering his opening salutations before the main narration begins. He bows first to Saraswati and Ganga, praising them as two pure powers: one washes away impurity through bathing, the other removes confusion through speech and hearing.
ramacharitamanas::115.modern_relevance: You step out of a shower feeling clean, but your mind is still crowded with noise from the day. A single honest conversation, a wise podcast, or one clear teaching can cleanse that clutter more deeply than water.
ramacharitamanas::115.insight: It shifts attention from outer cleansing alone to the cleansing power of hearing, speech, and understanding.

ramacharitamanas::116.verse_sanskrit: गुर पितु मातु महेस भवानी। प्रनवउँ दीनबंधु दिन दानी॥ सेवक स्वामि सखा सिय पी के। हित निरुपधि सब बिधि तुलसी के ॥
ramacharitamanas::116.verse_hindi: श्री महेश और पार्वती को मैं प्रणाम करता हूँ, जो मेरे गुरु और माता-पिता हैं, जो दीनबन्धु और नित्य दान करने वाले हैं, जो सीतापति श्री रामचन्द्रजी के सेवक, स्वामी और सखा हैं तथा मुझ तुलसीदास का सब प्रकार से कपटरहित (सच्चा) हित करने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::116.english_translation: I bow to my guru, father, mother, Shiva, and Parvati; to the friend of the humble and giver every day. I bow to the servant, master, and companion of Sita's lord, Ram, who always acts for my welfare without any selfish motive.
ramacharitamanas::116.translation_literal: गुर (teacher) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / महेस (Shiva) / भवानी (Parvati) / प्रनवउँ (I bow) / दीनबंधु (friend of the humble) / दिन दानी (daily giver) / सेवक (servant) / स्वामि (master) / सखा (companion) / सिय पी (Sita's lord) / के (of) / हित (welfare) / निरुपधि (without selfish motive) / सब बिधि (in every way) / तुलसी के (of Tulsidas)
ramacharitamanas::116.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::116.essence: Devotion bows to the one who serves without self-interest.
ramacharitamanas::116.simple_meaning: Tulsidas offers reverence to Shiva, Parvati, and Ram, and says Ram is the humble friend and daily benefactor who works for his good without any hidden motive.
ramacharitamanas::116.simple_insight: There is comfort in being held by a presence that wants your welfare without asking anything in return.
ramacharitamanas::116.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas begins his hymn by bowing to Shiva and Parvati, then turns to Ram as his lord, companion, and selfless helper. In this opening of Balkand, he defines the relationship that will guide the whole retelling: humble devotion to a divine presence that acts only for the devotee's good.
ramacharitamanas::116.modern_relevance: You call the one person who has never used your trust against you. They listen, steady you, and want your good without leverage. That kind of relationship changes how you understand love.
ramacharitamanas::116.insight: It shifts the mind from transactional loyalty to grateful surrender.

ramacharitamanas::117.verse_sanskrit: कलि बिलोकि जग हित हर गिरिजा। साबर मंत्र जाल जिन्ह सिरिजा॥ अनमिल आखर अरथ न जापू। प्रगट प्रभाउ महेस प्रतापू ॥
ramacharitamanas::117.verse_hindi: जिन शिव-पार्वती ने कलियुग को देखकर, जगत के हित के लिए, शाबर मन्त्र समूह की रचना की, जिन मंत्रों के अक्षर बेमेल हैं, जिनका न कोई ठीक अर्थ होता है और न जप ही होता है, तथापि श्री शिवजी के प्रताप से जिनका प्रभाव प्रत्यक्ष है ॥
ramacharitamanas::117.english_translation: Seeing the age of Kali, Shiva and Girija created a network of sabar mantras for the welfare of the world. Their letters do not match neatly, their meaning is not plain, and they are not chanted in the usual way, yet their power appears openly through Shiva's greatness.
ramacharitamanas::117.translation_literal: कलि (the age of Kali) / बिलोकि (seeing) / जग हित (for the welfare of the world) / हर (Shiva) / गिरिजा (Parvati) / साबर मंत्र (sabar mantras) / जाल (net, collection) / जिन्ह (which) / सिरिजा (created) / अनमिल (unmatched) / आखर (letters) / अरथ (meaning) / न (not) / जापू (chanting) / प्रगट (manifest) / प्रभाउ (power, effect) / महेस (Shiva) / प्रतापू (greatness, might)
ramacharitamanas::117.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::117.essence: Power for the world's good can work beyond neat words and neat logic.
ramacharitamanas::117.simple_meaning: Shiva and Parvati created powerful mantras for the welfare of the world. Their words may look irregular and hard to parse, but their effect is real through Shiva's power.
ramacharitamanas::117.simple_insight: What matters is not polished form, but living power that helps people.
ramacharitamanas::117.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Shiva and Parvati as he prepares to enter Ram's story. He says they created sabar mantras for the world's good: the letters may look uneven, the meaning may seem unclear, and the chant may not follow ordinary rules, yet Shiva's power makes them effective.
ramacharitamanas::117.modern_relevance: You open a prayer book and the lines look strange, almost broken. Still, something in them steadies you because the practice carries a force larger than neat explanation.
ramacharitamanas::117.insight: It shifts attention from outer polish to the real force behind a practice.

ramacharitamanas::118.verse_sanskrit: सो उमेस मोहि पर अनुकूला। करिहिं कथा मुद मंगल मूला॥ सुमिरि सिवा सिव पाइ पसाऊ। बस्नउँ रामचरित चित चाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::118.verse_hindi: वे उमापति शिवजी मुझ पर प्रसन्न होकर (श्री रामजी की) इस कथा को आनन्द और मंगल की मूल (उत्पन्न करने वाली) बनाएँगे। इस प्रकार पार्वतीजी और शिवजी दोनों का स्मरण करके और उनका प्रसाद पाकर मैं चाव भरे चित्त से श्री रामचरित्र का वर्णन करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::118.english_translation: May Lord Shiva be favorable to me, so that he makes this story the source of joy and auspiciousness. Remembering Shiva and Parvati and receiving their grace, I now speak the Ramcharit with a loving heart.
ramacharitamanas::118.translation_literal: सो (that) / उमेस (Lord of Uma, Shiva) / मोहि (to me) / पर (upon) / अनुकूला (favorable) / करिहिं (may make) / कथा (story) / मुद (joy) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मूला (root) / सुमिरि (remembering) / सिवा (Shiva and Parvati) / सिव (Shiva) / पाइ (having received) / पसाऊ (grace) / बस्नउँ (I dwell / I speak) / रामचरित (Ram's story) / चित (mind) / चाऊ (loving desire)
ramacharitamanas::118.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::118.essence: Devotion turns storytelling into an offering that carries joy.
ramacharitamanas::118.simple_meaning: Tulsidas asks Shiva to bless his telling of Ram's story, so it becomes a source of joy and blessing. He writes with devotion, after remembering Shiva and Parvati and receiving their grace.
ramacharitamanas::118.simple_insight: Before sacred speech, he bows. Devotion opens the heart and makes the telling worthy.
ramacharitamanas::118.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening the Ramcharitmanas by invoking Shiva and Parvati. He says their grace will make this telling fruitful and joyful, then declares that he will speak Ram's story with a loving mind. The verse frames the whole work as blessed devotion, not mere narration.
ramacharitamanas::118.modern_relevance: Before you send the message, write the post, or speak in the meeting, you pause and ask for steadiness. The words land better when they come from reverence instead of ego.
ramacharitamanas::118.insight: It shifts speech from self-expression to offering, so the words carry warmth, humility, and trust.

ramacharitamanas::119.verse_sanskrit: भनिति मोरि सिव कृपाँ बिभाती। ससि समाज मिलि मनहुँ सुराती॥ जे एहि कथहि सनेह समेता। कहिहहिं सुनिहहिं समुझि सचेता ॥ होइहहिं राम चरन अनुरागी। कलि मल रहित सुमंगल भागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::119.verse_hindi: मेरी कविता श्री शिवजी की कृपा से ऐसी सुशोभित होगी, जैसी तारागणों के सहित चन्द्रमा के साथ रात्रि शोभित होती है, जो इस कथा को प्रेम सहित एवं सावधानी के साथ समझ-बूझकर कहें-सुनेंगे, वे कलियुग के पापों से रहित और सुंदर कल्याण के भागी होकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों के प्रेमी बन जाएँगे॥5-6॥
ramacharitamanas::119.english_translation: My verse will be adorned by Shiva's grace like the night is adorned by the moon with stars. Those who hear and speak this story with love and attention will be freed from the stains of Kali and become lovers of Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::119.translation_literal: भनिति (poetry) / मोरि (my) / सिव (Shiva) / कृपाँ (by grace) / बिभाती (is adorned, shines) / ससि (moon) / समाज (company, assembly) / मिलि (together) / मनहुँ (as if) / सुराती (night, starry night)॥ / जे (those who) / एहि (this) / कथहि (story) / सनेह (love) / समेता (with) / कहिहहिं (will speak) / सुनिहहिं (will hear) / समुझि (understanding) / सचेता (careful, alert) ॥ / होइहहिं (will become) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / अनुरागी (loving) / कलि (Kali age) / मल (stain) / रहित (free from) / सुमंगल (great auspiciousness) / भागी (participants, sharers) ॥
ramacharitamanas::119.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::119.essence: Love-filled attention turns hearing into transformation.
ramacharitamanas::119.simple_meaning: The poet says his words will shine by Shiva's grace. Anyone who hears and speaks this story with love and care will become devoted to Ram and freed from the age's stain.
ramacharitamanas::119.simple_insight: Devotion is not passive listening; it changes the listener into someone cleaner, steadier, and more loving.
ramacharitamanas::119.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is pausing before the story fully unfolds to bless the act of telling itself. He says the poem will be made beautiful by Shiva's grace, and that anyone who receives it with love and attention will become attached to Ram's feet and untouched by Kali's corruption.
ramacharitamanas::119.modern_relevance: You open a book late at night, half-distracted, and one page lands differently. The difference is not just information — it is how carefully and lovingly you received it.
ramacharitamanas::119.insight: It shifts reading from consumption to reverent participation, where attention itself becomes purifying.

ramacharitamanas::120.verse_sanskrit: सपनेहुँ साचेहुँ मोहि पर जौं हर गौरि पसाउ। तौ फुर होउ जो कहेउँ सब भाषा भनिति प्रभाउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::120.verse_hindi: यदि मु् झ पर श्री शिवजी और पार्वतीजी की स्वप्न में भी सचमुच प्रसन्नता हो, तो मैंने इस भाषा कविता का जो प्रभाव कहा है, वह सब सच हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::120.english_translation: If Shiva and Parvati are truly pleased with me, even in a dream, then everything I have said about the power of this language-poem will come true.
ramacharitamanas::120.translation_literal: सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / साचेहुँ (truly) / मोहि पर (upon me) / जौं (if) / हर (Shiva) / गौरि (Parvati) / पसाउ (grace, favor) / तौ (then) / फुर (true) / होउ (may it be) / जो (that which) / कहेउँ (I said) / सब (all) / भाषा (language) / भनिति (poetic composition) / प्रभाउ (power, effect)
ramacharitamanas::120.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::120.essence: True speech needs blessing before it can become real.
ramacharitamanas::120.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says his words will have power only if Shiva and Parvati truly bless him. He asks that the poem he is about to write prove true through their grace.
ramacharitamanas::120.simple_insight: Creative work feels lighter when you stop claiming it alone and ask for blessing instead.
ramacharitamanas::120.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening the Ramcharitmanas by bowing to Shiva and Parvati. He says the poem's power will be real only if they are pleased with him, even in a dream. This humble invocation prepares the reader for the sacred story to follow.
ramacharitamanas::120.modern_relevance: You hit send on something you spent weeks writing and still feel exposed. The work matters, but you know its worth is larger than your ego. That is the spirit here.
ramacharitamanas::120.insight: It shifts authorship from self-importance to humble offering, so the work is received as grace rather than display.

ramacharitamanas::121.verse_sanskrit: बंदउँ अवध पुरी अति पावनि। सरजू सरि कलि कलुष नसावनि॥ प्रनवउँ पुर नर नारि बहोरी। ममता जिन्ह पर प्रभुहि न थोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::121.verse_hindi: मैं अति पवित्र श्री अयोध्यापुरी और कलियुग के पापों का नाश करने वाली श्री सरयू नदी की वन्दना करता हूँ। फिर अवधपुरी के उन नर-नारियों को प्रणाम करता हूँ, जिन पर प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी की ममता थोड़ी नहीं है (अर्थात् बहुत है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::121.english_translation: I bow to the holy city of Ayodhya and to the Saryu River, destroyer of the sins of Kali. I bow again to the men and women of that city, on whom Lord Ram's affection rests greatly.
ramacharitamanas::121.translation_literal: बंदउँ (I bow) / अवध पुरी (Ayodhya city) / अति पावनि (most holy) / सरजू सरि (Saryu river) / कलि कलुष (the impurities of Kali age) / नसावनि (destroyer) / प्रनवउँ (I salute) / पुर नर नारि (the city’s men and women) / बहोरी (again) / ममता (affection) / जिन्ह पर (on whom) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / न थोरी (not little)
ramacharitamanas::121.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::121.essence: A place becomes holy when Ram's affection rests there.
ramacharitamanas::121.simple_meaning: Ayodhya and the Saryu are holy, and Tulsidas bows to the people of that city because Ram loves them deeply.
ramacharitamanas::121.simple_insight: Holy places matter because love lives there. Reverence can begin with a city, a river, and the people held dear by Ram.
ramacharitamanas::121.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening his praise of Ayodhya, the city where Ram's story gathers its deepest tenderness. He bows to the sacred city, the Saryu River, and the people of Ayodhya because they are wrapped in Ram's special affection.
ramacharitamanas::121.modern_relevance: You walk into a neighborhood where every wall seems to remember a family’s story. Some places feel charged because love, memory, and devotion have lived there for generations.
ramacharitamanas::121.insight: It shifts attention from abstract holiness to the sacredness of a place beloved by the divine.

ramacharitamanas::122.verse_sanskrit: सिय निंदक अघ ओघ नसाए। लोक बिसोक बनाइ बसाए॥ बंदउँ कौसल्या दिसि प्राची। कीरति जासु सकल जग माची ॥
ramacharitamanas::122.verse_hindi: उन्होंने (अपनी पुरी में रहने वाले) सीताजी की निंदा करने वाले (धोबी और उसके समर्थक पुर-नर-नारियों) के पाप समूह को नाश कर उनको शोकरहित बनाकर अपने लोक (धाम) में बसा दिया। मैं कौशल्या रूपी पूर्व दिशा की वन्दना करता हूँ, जिसकी कीर्ति समस्त संसार में फैल रही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::122.english_translation: He destroyed the heap of sins of those who slandered Sita and settled them in a sorrow-free realm. I bow to Kausalya, the east, whose fame has spread through the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::122.translation_literal: सिय (Sita) / निंदक (slanderer) / अघ (sins) / ओघ (heap, flood) / नसाए (destroyed) / लोक (world, realm) / बिसोक (free from sorrow) / बनाइ (making) / बसाए (settled) / बंदउँ (I bow) / कौसल्या (Kausalya) / दिसि (direction) / प्राची (east) / कीरति (fame) / जासु (whose) / सकल (whole) / जग (world) / माची (spread)
ramacharitamanas::122.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::122.essence: Ram's grace can turn even offenders into the sorrow-free.
ramacharitamanas::122.simple_meaning: Ram removes the burden of those who insult Sita and gives them peace. Tulsidas then praises Kausalya as the east from which Ram's glory rose into the world.
ramacharitamanas::122.simple_insight: Even hostility can be transformed when grace is greater than offense.
ramacharitamanas::122.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ayodhya and the family that gave the world Ram. He says Ram even redeemed the people who mocked Sita, freeing them from sorrow. Then he turns to Kausalya, the mother who made Ram's appearance possible.
ramacharitamanas::122.modern_relevance: Someone spreads cruelty about a person online, and the whole room hardens around it. This verse points to a higher response: not only refusing bitterness, but transforming the atmosphere so harm loses its home.
ramacharitamanas::122.insight: It shifts attention from punishment to redemptive power: the highest response to insult is to end its hold.

ramacharitamanas::123.verse_sanskrit: प्रगटेउ जहँ रघुपति ससि चारू। बिस्व सुखद खल कमल तुसारू॥ दसरथ राउ सहित सब रानी। सुकृत सुमंगल मूरति मानी ॥ करउँ प्रनाम करम मन बानी। करहु कृपा सुत सेवक जानी॥ जिन्हहि बिरचि बड़ भयउ बिधाता। महिमा अवधि राम पितु माता ॥
ramacharitamanas::123.verse_hindi: जहाँ (कौशल्या रूपी पूर्व दिशा) से विश्व को सुख देने वाले और दुष्ट रूपी कमलों के लिए पाले के समान श्री रामचन्द्रजी रूपी सुंदर चंद्रमा प्रकट हुए। सब रानियों सहित राजा दशरथजी को पुण्य और सुंदर कल्याण की मूर्ति मानकर मैं मन, वचन और कर्म से प्रणाम करता हूँ। अपने पुत्र का सेवक जानकर वे मुझ पर कृपा करें, जिनको रचकर ब्रह्माजी ने भी बड़ाई पाई तथा जो श्री रामजी के माता और पिता होने के कारण महिमा की सीमा हैं॥3-4॥
ramacharitamanas::123.english_translation: Where the beautiful moon-like Ram appeared, bringing joy to the world and frost to the wicked lotus. I bow with mind, speech, and body to King Dasharath and all the queens, who are honored as forms of virtue and auspiciousness. May they show grace to me as their servant and son, for even Brahma gained greatness by creating them, and Ram's mother and father are the measure of all glory.
ramacharitamanas::123.translation_literal: प्रगटेउ (appeared) / जहँ (where) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu line, Ram) / ससि (moon) / चारू (beautiful) / बिस्व (world) / सुखद (giver of joy) / खल (wicked) / कमल (lotus) / तुसारू (frost) / दसरथ राउ (King Dasharath) / सहित (together with) / सब (all) / रानी (queens) / सुकृत (virtuous deed) / सुमंगल (very auspicious) / मूरति (form) / मानी (considered) / करउँ (I do) / प्रनाम (bow) / करम (action) / मन (mind) / बानी (speech) / करहु (do) / कृपा (grace) / सुत (son) / सेवक (servant) / जानी (knowing) / जिन्हहि (whom) / बिरचि (having created) / बड़ (great) / भयउ (became) / बिधाता (Brahma) / महिमा (glory) / अवधि (limit) / राम (Ram) / पितु (father) / माता (mother)
ramacharitamanas::123.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::123.essence: Ram's birth makes even family life a field of reverence.
ramacharitamanas::123.simple_meaning: Ram appears like a moon that brings joy to the world. Tulsidas bows to Dasharath and the queens, asking them to bless him as their servant and son.
ramacharitamanas::123.simple_insight: Devotion can be humble and intimate at once: you bow not from distance, but from belonging.
ramacharitamanas::123.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand's opening praise, Tulsidas turns from the city and river to Ram's birth in Dasharath's house. He celebrates Ram's appearance, honors Dasharath and the queens, and asks for their grace as a devotee who comes as a servant and child.
ramacharitamanas::123.modern_relevance: You walk into a house where a newborn has just arrived, and the whole room softens. The right response is not analysis but reverence, gratitude, and a wish to belong well.
ramacharitamanas::123.insight: It shifts attention from the miracle alone to the sacred relationships that made that miracle visible.

ramacharitamanas::124.verse_sanskrit: बंदउँ अवध भुआल सत्य प्रेम जेहि राम पद। बिछुरत दीनदयाल प्रिय तनु तृन इव परिहरेउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::124.verse_hindi: मैं अवध के राजा श्री दशरथजी की वन्दना करता हूँ, जिनका श्री रामजी के चरणों में सच्चा प्रेम था, जिन्होंने दीनदयालु प्रभु के बिछुड़ते ही अपने प्यारे शरीर को मामूली तिनके की तरह त्याग दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::124.english_translation: I bow to the king of Ayodhya, Dasharath, whose love for Ram's feet was true. At separation from the compassionate Lord, he gave up his beloved body like a blade of grass.
ramacharitamanas::124.translation_literal: बंदउँ (I bow) / अवध भुआल (king of Ayodhya) / सत्य प्रेम (true love) / जेहि (whose) / राम पद (Ram's feet) / बिछुरत (at separation) / दीनदयाल (compassionate Lord) / प्रिय तनु (beloved body) / तृन इव (like grass) / परिहरेउ (gave up)
ramacharitamanas::124.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::124.essence: Separation from what you love can empty life at once.
ramacharitamanas::124.simple_meaning: Dasharath is praised for loving Ram deeply. When Ram was separated from him, he let go of his body as easily as dropping a blade of grass.
ramacharitamanas::124.simple_insight: Love can be so complete that separation becomes unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::124.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses in Ayodhya to honor King Dasharath after Ram's exile has torn the family apart. Dasharath's love for Ram is so deep that separation from Ram becomes fatal, and his body is said to fall away like grass.
ramacharitamanas::124.modern_relevance: You watch a parent go quiet after a child leaves for good, the house suddenly too large. Some bonds are not sentimental; they are life itself.
ramacharitamanas::124.insight: It turns grief into a measure of love, not weakness.

ramacharitamanas::125.verse_sanskrit: प्रनवउँ परिजन सहित बिदेहू। जाहि राम पद गूढ़ सनेहू॥ जोग भोग महँ राखेउ गोई। राम बिलोकत प्रगटेउ सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::125.verse_hindi: मैं परिवार सहित राजा जनकजी को प्रणाम करता हूँ, जिनका श्री रामजी के चरणों में गूढ़ प्रेम था, जिसको उन्होंने योग और भोग में छिपा रखा था, परन्तु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखते ही वह प्रकट हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::125.english_translation: I bow with Janaka and his family to the king of Videha, whose deep love for Ram's feet was hidden in both yoga and worldly life. The moment he saw Ram, that love appeared.
ramacharitamanas::125.translation_literal: प्रनवउँ (I bow) / परिजन सहित (with family) / बिदेहू (the king of Videha, Janaka) / जाहि (whose) / राम पद (Ram's feet) / गूढ़ सनेहू (deep hidden love) / जोग भोग महँ (in yoga and in enjoyment/worldly life) / राखेउ गोई (kept hidden) / राम बिलोकत (seeing Ram) / प्रगटेउ (appeared) / सोई (that very love)
ramacharitamanas::125.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::125.essence: Hidden love becomes unmistakable in Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::125.simple_meaning: Janaka's love for Ram was so deep that he kept it hidden through both spiritual practice and ordinary life. Seeing Ram made that hidden love visible.
ramacharitamanas::125.simple_insight: Real devotion does not need display. It stays hidden until the beloved appears.
ramacharitamanas::125.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is moving through the great devotees of Ayodhya and Mithila. After praising Dasharath, he now bows to Janaka and his household, saying that Janaka's love for Ram was already there, quietly held in both renunciation and enjoyment, and then burst into view when Ram came before him.
ramacharitamanas::125.modern_relevance: You can go through meetings, family duties, and private discipline with a love you never announce. Then one encounter with what you truly value makes everything in you obvious.
ramacharitamanas::125.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to inward reality, showing that true love becomes visible only in the right presence.

ramacharitamanas::126.verse_sanskrit: प्रनवउँ प्रथम भरत के चरना। जासु नेम ब्रत जाइ न बरना॥ राम चरन पंकज मन जासू। लुबुध मधुप इव तजइ न पासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::126.verse_hindi: (भाइयों में) सबसे पहले मैं श्री भरतजी के चरणों को प्रणाम करता हूँ, जिनका नियम और व्रत वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता तथा जिनका मन श्री रामजी के चरणकमलों में भौंरे की तरह लुभाया हुआ है, कभी उनका पास नहीं छोड़ता ॥
ramacharitamanas::126.english_translation: I bow first to Bharata's feet. His discipline and vows cannot be described. His mind stays fixed on Ram's lotus feet like a bee drawn to a flower, never leaving their nearness.
ramacharitamanas::126.translation_literal: प्रनवउँ (I bow) / प्रथम (first) / भरत के चरना (to Bharata's feet) / जासु (whose) / नेम (discipline, vow) / ब्रत (vow, observance) / जाइ न बरना (cannot be described) / राम चरन पंकज (Ram's lotus feet) / मन जासू (whose mind) / लुबुध (greedy, enamoured) / मधुप इव (like a bee) / तजइ न पासू (does not leave the nearness)
ramacharitamanas::126.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::126.essence: Perfect devotion keeps the mind where the heart already lives.
ramacharitamanas::126.simple_meaning: Bharata is praised for two things: his unmatched discipline and his mind's unbroken attachment to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::126.simple_insight: There is peace in loving one center so completely that everything else loses its pull.
ramacharitamanas::126.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is moving through the great devotees of Ram in Balkand. After praising Dasharath and Janak, he bows first to Bharata, whose vows are beyond words and whose mind clings to Ram's feet like a bee to nectar.
ramacharitamanas::126.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone during a family dinner, but one person across the table has your full attention. Bharata shows what it means to let love become steadiness instead of distraction.
ramacharitamanas::126.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to disciplined, unwavering attention.

ramacharitamanas::127.verse_sanskrit: बंदउँ लछिमन पद जल जाता। सीतल सुभग भगत सुख दाता॥ रघुपति कीरति बिमल पताका। दंड समान भयउ जस जाका ॥
ramacharitamanas::127.verse_hindi: मैं श्री लक्ष्मणजी के चरण कमलों को प्रणाम करता हूँ, जो शीतल सुंदर और भक्तों को सुख देने वाले हैं। श्री रघुनाथजी की कीर्ति रूपी विमल पताका में जिनका (लक्ष्मणजी का) यश (पताका को ऊँचा करके फहराने वाले) दंड के समान हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::127.english_translation: I bow to Lakshman's feet, cool, beautiful, and giving joy to devotees. His fame became the staff that lifted the spotless banner of Raghunath's glory.
ramacharitamanas::127.translation_literal: बंदउँ (I bow) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / पद (feet) / जल जाता (cooling like water) / सीतल (cool) / सुभग (beautiful) / भगत (devotees) / सुख दाता (giver of joy) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / कीरति (fame) / बिमल (spotless) / पताका (banner) / दंड (staff/pole) / समान (like) / भयउ (became) / जस (whose fame) / जाका (of whom)
ramacharitamanas::127.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::127.essence: True devotion lifts another's glory without asking for its own.
ramacharitamanas::127.simple_meaning: Lakshman is praised as gentle, beautiful, and a source of joy for devotees. His own fame serves Ram's glory like the pole that holds up a banner.
ramacharitamanas::127.simple_insight: Quiet service can become the support that makes greatness visible.
ramacharitamanas::127.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is moving through his opening praises of Ram's closest devotees. After honoring Janak and Bharat, he bows to Lakshman: the brother whose presence cools pain and whose reputation holds up Ram's honor like a banner on its staff.
ramacharitamanas::127.modern_relevance: You stay up all night helping a sibling rehearse, then stand in the back while they shine. No one names your role, but the whole moment leans on you.
ramacharitamanas::127.insight: It shifts attention from being seen to supporting what should be seen.

ramacharitamanas::128.verse_sanskrit: सेष सहस्रसीस जग कारन। जो अवतरेउ भूमि भय टारन॥ सदा सो सानुकूल रह मो पर। कृपासिन्धु सौमित्रि गुनाकर ॥
ramacharitamanas::128.verse_hindi: जो हजार सिर वाले और जगत के कारण (हजार सिरों पर जगत को धारण कर रखने वाले) शेषजी हैं, जिन्होंने पृथ्वी का भय दूर करने के लिए अवतार लिया, वे गुणों की खान कृपासिन्धु सुमित्रानंदन श्री लक्ष्मणजी मुझ पर सदा प्रसन्न रहें ॥
ramacharitamanas::128.english_translation: May Lakshman, the thousand-headed Shesha who supports the world and descended to remove the earth's fear, the ocean of compassion and mine of virtues, always remain favorable to me.
ramacharitamanas::128.translation_literal: सेष (Shesha) / सहस्रसीस (thousand-headed) / जग कारन (cause of the world) / जो (who) / अवतरेउ (descended) / भूमि (earth) / भय (fear) / टारन (to remove) / सदा (always) / सो (that one) / सानुकूल (favorable) / रह (remain) / मो पर (toward me) / कृपासिन्धु (ocean of compassion) / सौमित्रि (son of Sumitra, Lakshman) / गुनाकर (mine of virtues)
ramacharitamanas::128.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::128.essence: The truest protector is compassionate strength.
ramacharitamanas::128.simple_meaning: Lakshman is praised as Shesha himself, who came to remove the world's fear and who should always stay gracious toward the speaker.
ramacharitamanas::128.simple_insight: Real strength is compassionate. The one who protects others is the one worthy of reverence.
ramacharitamanas::128.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues his opening praise of Ram's companions. After honoring Bharat and Lakshman, he now identifies Lakshman with Shesha, the thousand-headed support of the world, and asks that this compassionate protector remain kind to him.
ramacharitamanas::128.modern_relevance: Someone who quietly holds everything together in a family, team, or crisis rarely asks for credit. This verse bows to that kind of steady, protective presence.
ramacharitamanas::128.insight: It shifts attention from heroic display to the unseen person who bears burdens and removes fear for others.

ramacharitamanas::129.verse_sanskrit: रिपुसूदन पद कमल नमामी। सूर सुसील भरत अनुगामी॥ महाबीर बिनवउँ हनुमाना। राम जासु जस आप बखाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::129.verse_hindi: मैं श्री शत्रुघ्नजी के चरणकमलों को प्रणाम करता हूँ, जो बड़े वीर, सुशील और श्री भरतजी के पीछे चलने वाले हैं। मैं महावीर श्री हनुमानजी की विनती करता हूँ, जिनके यश का श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने स्वयं (अपने श्रीमुख से) वर्णन किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::129.english_translation: I bow to Shatrughna, the slayer of foes, whose lotus feet are followed by Bharata. I beseech Hanuman, the great hero, whose fame Ram himself has described.
ramacharitamanas::129.translation_literal: रिपुसूदन (slayer of foes) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / नमामी (I bow) / सूर (brave) / सुसील (well-mannered) / भरत (Bharata) / अनुगामी (follower) / महाबीर (great hero) / बिनवउँ (I beseech) / हनुमाना (Hanuman) / राम (Ram) / जासु (whose) / जस (fame) / आप (himself) / बखाना (described)
ramacharitamanas::129.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::129.essence: Ram’s own praise makes Hanuman’s greatness undeniable.
ramacharitamanas::129.simple_meaning: Tulsidas offers praise to Shatrughna and Hanuman. Hanuman’s greatness is so pure that Ram himself speaks of it.
ramacharitamanas::129.simple_insight: True greatness needs no self-promotion; Ram’s praise is enough.
ramacharitamanas::129.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is moving through his opening praises in Balkand. After honoring Lakshman and before turning fully to Hanuman, he names Shatrughna as brave and devoted, then bows to Hanuman whose glory Ram himself has already declared.
ramacharitamanas::129.modern_relevance: You hear a leader mention someone’s character in a room they are not in. That kind of praise lands deeper than any self-introduction ever could.
ramacharitamanas::129.insight: It shifts attention from self-advertisement to a life so devoted that its worth is recognised by the highest witness.

ramacharitamanas::130.verse_sanskrit: प्रनवउँ पवनकुमार खल बन पावक ग्यान घन। जासु हृदय आगार बसहिं राम सर चाप धर ॥
ramacharitamanas::130.verse_hindi: मैं पवनकुमार श्री हनुमान् जी को प्रणाम करता हूँ, जो दुष्ट रूपी वन को भस्म करने के लिए अग्निरूप हैं, जो ज्ञान की घनमूर्ति हैं और जिनके हृदय रूपी भवन में धनुष-बाण धारण किए श्री रामजी निवास करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::130.english_translation: I bow to Hanuman, son of the wind, fire to the forest of wickedness, a mass of wisdom, in whose heart Rama with bow and arrow dwells.
ramacharitamanas::130.translation_literal: प्रनवउँ (I bow) / पवनकुमार (son of the wind) / खल (wicked) / बन (forest) / पावक (fire) / ग्यान (wisdom) / घन (mass/cloud) / जासु (whose) / हृदय (heart) / आगार (house) / बसहिं (dwells) / राम (Rama) / सर (arrow) / चाप (bow) / धर (holding)
ramacharitamanas::130.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::130.essence: Greatness is complete only when Rama lives at the center of the heart.
ramacharitamanas::130.simple_meaning: Hanuman is praised as the destroyer of evil, the embodiment of wisdom, and the devoted heart where Rama lives.
ramacharitamanas::130.simple_insight: True strength is not self-display. It becomes pure when the heart is fully occupied by Rama.
ramacharitamanas::130.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is introducing Hanuman in the opening praises of Balkand. He is not just strong; he burns wickedness, radiates wisdom, and is so devoted that Rama with bow and arrow lives in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::130.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where gossip, ego, and noise are already spreading. The person who changes the atmosphere is not the loudest one — it is the one whose heart is already anchored in something higher.
ramacharitamanas::130.insight: It shifts admiration from power alone to power joined with devotion and clarity.

ramacharitamanas::131.verse_sanskrit: कपिपति रीछ निसाचर राजा। अंगदादि जे कीस समाजा॥ बंदउँ सब के चरन सुहाए। अधम सरीर राम जिन्ह पाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::131.verse_hindi: वानरों के राजा सुग्रीवजी, रीछों के राजा जाम्बवानजी, राक्षसों के राजा विभीषणजी और अंगदजी आदि जितना वानरों का समाज है, सबके सुंदर चरणों की मैं वदना करता हूँ, जिन्होंने अधम (पशु और राक्षस आदि) शरीर में भी श्री रामचन्द्रजी को प्राप्त कर लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::131.english_translation: I bow to the lovely feet of Sugriva, king of the monkeys, Jambavan, king of the bears, Vibhishana, king of the demons, and Angada and the whole monkey company. Though born in lowly bodies, they found Ram.
ramacharitamanas::131.translation_literal: कपिपति (king of monkeys) / रीछ (bears) / निसाचर (night-walkers, demons) / राजा (kings) / अंगदादि (Angada and others) / जे (who) / कीस (monkeys) / समाजा (company) / बंदउँ (I bow) / सब (all) / के (of) / चरन (feet) / सुहाए (lovely) / अधम (lowly) / सरीर (bodies) / राम (Ram) / जिन्ह (whom) / पाए (found/obtained)
ramacharitamanas::131.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::131.essence: Lowly forms become glorious when they find Ram.
ramacharitamanas::131.simple_meaning: Tulsidas bows to Ram's devotees from every kind of being. Their bodies may be lowly, but they reached Ram through devotion.
ramacharitamanas::131.simple_insight: No birth is too low when the heart is fully turned toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::131.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is listing Ram's devotees one by one: Sugriva, Jambavan, Vibhishana, Angada, and the whole monkey host. In this devotional sweep, he honors them because they found Ram despite humble or feared forms of birth.
ramacharitamanas::131.modern_relevance: You feel out of place in a room full of polished people, yet the person who truly belongs may be the one with the deepest loyalty. Rank never blocks devotion.
ramacharitamanas::131.insight: It shifts attention from social status to the purity of one’s turning toward Ram.

ramacharitamanas::132.verse_sanskrit: रघुपति चरन उपासक जेते। खग मृग सुर नर असुर समेते॥ बंदउँ पद सरोज सब केरे। जे बिनु काम राम के चेरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::132.verse_hindi: पशु, पक्षी, देवता, मनुष्य, असुर समेत जितने श्री रामजी के चरणों के उपासक हैं, मैं उन सबके चरणकमलों की वंदना करता हूँ, जो श्री रामजी के निष्काम सेवक हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::132.english_translation: I bow to all who worship the feet of the Lord of the Raghu clan—birds, beasts, radiant beings, humans, and beings of shadow. I bow to the lotus feet of all who serve Ram without desire.
ramacharitamanas::132.translation_literal: रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / चरन (feet) / उपासक (worshippers) / जेते (all who are) / खग (birds) / मृग (beasts) / सुर (radiant beings) / नर (humans) / असुर (beings of shadow) / समेते (together with) / बंदउँ (I bow) / पद (feet) / सरोज (lotus) / सब केरे (of all) / जे (who) / बिनु (without) / काम (desire) / राम (Ram) / के (of) / चेरे (servants)
ramacharitamanas::132.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::132.essence: Desireless service makes every servant of Ram sacred.
ramacharitamanas::132.simple_meaning: All beings who worship Ram and serve him without desire are worthy of reverence. Tulsidas bows to them all, from animals and birds to humans and radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::132.simple_insight: Real devotion levels status. What matters is not who you are, but whether your heart serves without wanting reward.
ramacharitamanas::132.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is listing the many kinds of beings who belong to Ram—birds, beasts, radiant beings, humans, and beings of shadow. He bows not only to Ram’s devotees, but to the lotus feet of every desireless servant of Ram, turning devotion itself into the highest honor.
ramacharitamanas::132.modern_relevance: You meet the quiet volunteer who never posts about their work, yet keeps showing up. Everyone notices the loud achiever; Tulsidas notices the one who serves without asking for credit.
ramacharitamanas::132.insight: It shifts admiration away from status and toward selfless devotion. The mind learns to honor surrender, not performance.

ramacharitamanas::133.verse_sanskrit: सुक सनकादि भगत मुनि नारद। जे मुनिबर बिग्यान बिसारद॥ प्रनवउँ सबहि धरनि धरि सीसा। करहु कृपा जन जानि मुनीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::133.verse_hindi: शुकदेवजी, सनकादि, नारदमुनि आदि जितने भक्त और परम ज्ञानी श्रेष्ठ मुनि हैं, मैं धरती पर सिर टेककर उन सबको प्रणाम करता हूँ, हे मुनीश्वरों! आप सब मुझको अपना दास जानकर कृपा कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::133.english_translation: I bow my head to Shukadeva, Sanaka and the other devotees, and to the great sages who are masters of spiritual wisdom. O chief sages, know me as your servant and show me compassion.
ramacharitamanas::133.translation_literal: सुक (Shuka) / सनकादि (Sanaka and others) / भगत (devotees) / मुनि (sages) / नारद (Narada) / जे (who) / मुनिबर (best among sages) / बिग्यान (knowledge) / बिसारद (skilled, expert)॥ / प्रनवउँ (I bow) / सबहि (to all) / धरनि (earth) / धरि (placing) / सीसा (head)॥ / करहु (do) / कृपा (compassion) / जन (me) / जानि (knowing) / मुनीसा (O chief sages)॥
ramacharitamanas::133.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::133.essence: True wisdom begins by bowing before it speaks.
ramacharitamanas::133.simple_meaning: The poet bows to saintly devotees and great sages, asking them to see him as their servant and bless him with compassion.
ramacharitamanas::133.simple_insight: Humility opens the door to grace. Respect for the wise is itself part of the path.
ramacharitamanas::133.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still in his opening praise, bowing not only to Ram's devotees but to the great sages who hold both devotion and clear understanding. He asks them for mercy before the story fully begins, showing that reverence comes before speech.
ramacharitamanas::133.modern_relevance: You enter a room full of people who know more than you do, and you stop performing. You listen, lower your pride, and ask to learn.
ramacharitamanas::133.insight: It shifts the reader from self-importance to reverent receptivity before any deeper teaching can land.

ramacharitamanas::134.verse_sanskrit: जनकसुता जग जननि जानकी। अतिसय प्रिय करुनानिधान की॥ ताके जुग पद कमल मनावउँ। जासु कृपाँ निरमल मति पावउँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::134.verse_hindi: राजा जनक की पुत्री, जगत की माता और करुणा निधान श्री रामचन्द्रजी की प्रियतमा श्री जानकीजी के दोनों चरण कमलों को मैं मनाता हूँ, जिनकी कृपा से निर्मल बुद्धि पाऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::134.english_translation: Janaki, daughter of King Janaka, mother of the world, and most beloved of the compassionate Lord, I bow to her lotus feet. By her grace, I may gain a pure mind.
ramacharitamanas::134.translation_literal: जनकसुता (daughter of Janaka) / जग जननि (mother of the world) / जानकी (Janaki) / अतिसय प्रिय (most beloved) / करुनानिधान की (of the treasure of compassion) / ताके (of her) / जुग पद कमल (pair feet lotus) / मनावउँ (I bow/meditate upon) / जासु (whose) / कृपाँ (by grace) / निरमल (pure) / मति (mind/intellect) / पावउँ (I may obtain)
ramacharitamanas::134.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::134.essence: Pure mind comes through humble bowing, not mental force.
ramacharitamanas::134.simple_meaning: Tulsidas bows to Sita's lotus feet and asks for her grace to receive a pure, clear mind.
ramacharitamanas::134.simple_insight: There is relief in asking for help from someone who embodies purity and care.
ramacharitamanas::134.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is moving through a chain of reverence in the Balkand, honoring Ram's devotees before turning to Sita, Janaka's daughter and Ram's beloved. He bows to her feet, not as a formality, but as a plea for the clarity that devotion can give.
ramacharitamanas::134.modern_relevance: You feel mentally crowded after a day of noise, opinions, and self-doubt. Instead of forcing clarity, you turn toward what is steady and ask for a cleaner mind.
ramacharitamanas::134.insight: It shifts attention from self-made certainty to grace received through reverence.

ramacharitamanas::135.verse_sanskrit: पुनि मन बचन कर्म रघुनायक। चरन कमल बंदउँ सब लायक॥ राजीवनयन धरें धनु सायक। भगत बिपति भंजन सुखदायक ॥
ramacharitamanas::135.verse_hindi: फिर मैं मन, वचन और कर्म से कमलनयन, धनुष-बाणधारी, भक्तों की विपत्ति का नाश करने और उन्हें सुख देने वाले भगवान् श्री रघुनाथजी के सर्व समर्थ चरण कमलों की वन्दना करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::135.english_translation: Again, with mind, speech, and action, I bow to the lotus feet of Raghunath, who is all-powerful. Lotus-eyed, bow-bearing, he removes the suffering of devotees and gives them joy.
ramacharitamanas::135.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / मन (mind) / बचन (speech) / कर्म (action) / रघुनायक (Lord of Raghu) / चरन कमल (lotus feet) / बंदउँ (I bow) / सब लायक (worthy of all) / राजीवनयन (lotus-eyed) / धरें (holding) / धनु सायक (bow and arrows) / भगत (devotees') / बिपति (trouble) / भंजन (destroyer) / सुखदायक (giver of joy)
ramacharitamanas::135.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::135.essence: Total devotion makes suffering lose its grip.
ramacharitamanas::135.simple_meaning: The speaker offers full worship to Ram with mind, words, and actions, praising him as lotus-eyed, armed with bow and arrows, and the remover of devotees’ suffering.
ramacharitamanas::135.simple_insight: Wholehearted devotion feels steady because it trusts Ram to carry both pain and joy.
ramacharitamanas::135.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still in his opening praise, moving from the saints and Sita to Ram himself. He bows not casually but with mind, speech, and action, naming Ram as the one who protects devotees, destroys suffering, and gives joy.
ramacharitamanas::135.modern_relevance: You are halfway through a prayer before the day starts, and your mind is already split between worry and to-do lists. This verse gathers you back into one offering instead of three scattered parts.
ramacharitamanas::135.insight: It turns devotion into total alignment: thought, speech, and action bow together.

ramacharitamanas::136.verse_sanskrit: गिरा अरथ जल बीचि सम कहिअत भिन्न न भिन्न। बंदउँ सीता राम पद जिन्हहि परम प्रिय खिन्न ॥
ramacharitamanas::136.verse_hindi: जो वाणी और उसके अर्थ तथा जल और जल की लहर के समान कहने में अलग-अलग हैं, परन्तु वास्तव में अभिन्न (एक) हैं, उन श्री सीतारामजी के चरणों की मैं वंदना करता हूँ, जिन्हें दीन-दुःखी बहुत ही प्रिय हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::136.english_translation: I bow to the feet of Sita and Ram, who seem different like speech and meaning, yet are truly one, and who are especially dear to the humble and afflicted.
ramacharitamanas::136.translation_literal: गिरा (speech) / अरथ (meaning) / जल (water) / बीचि (wave) / सम (like) / कहिअत (are said) / भिन्न (different) / न भिन्न (not different) / बंदउँ (I bow) / सीता राम पद (the feet of Sita and Ram) / जिन्हहि (to whom) / परम प्रिय (most dear) / खिन्न (the humble and afflicted)
ramacharitamanas::136.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::136.essence: What seems divided is one in devotion.
ramacharitamanas::136.simple_meaning: Sita and Ram may appear separate, like words and their meaning, but they are truly one. Tulsidas bows to them as the refuge of the humble and suffering.
ramacharitamanas::136.simple_insight: Separation can be an appearance; devotion sees the deeper unity and feels held by it.
ramacharitamanas::136.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening his devotional praise before the Sita-Ram section. He bows to their feet and says they are like speech and meaning, or water and its wave: distinct in appearance, inseparable in reality. Their grace belongs especially to the humble and afflicted.
ramacharitamanas::136.modern_relevance: You can hear a loved one’s words as distance, or you can hear the care inside them. This verse asks you to look for the meaning beneath the surface and to trust what truly binds.
ramacharitamanas::136.insight: It shifts attention from outer difference to inner unity, especially in love and devotion.

ramacharitamanas::137.verse_sanskrit: बंदउँ नाम राम रघुबर को। हेतु कृसानु भानु हिमकर को॥ बिधि हरि हरमय बेद प्रान सो। अगुन अनूपम गुन निधान सो ॥
ramacharitamanas::137.verse_hindi: मैं श्री रघुनाथजी के नाम 'राम' की वंदना करता हूँ, जो कृशानु (अग्नि), भानु (सूर्य) और हिमकर (चन्द्रमा) का हेतु अर्थात् 'र' 'आ' और 'म' रूप से बीज है। वह 'राम' नाम ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और शिवरूप है। वह वेदों का प्राण है, निर्गुण, उपमारहित और गुणों का भंडार है ॥
ramacharitamanas::137.english_translation: I bow to the name “Ram” of Raghubar, the source of fire, sun, and moon. That name is Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva in one; it is the life of the Vedas, beyond qualities, matchless, and a storehouse of virtues.
ramacharitamanas::137.translation_literal: बंदउँ (I bow) / नाम (name) / राम (Ram) / रघुबर को (of Raghubar) / हेतु (cause/source) / कृसानु (fire) / भानु (sun) / हिमकर (moon) / को (of) / बिधि (Brahma) / हरि (Vishnu) / हरमय (filled with Shiva) / बेद (Vedas) / प्रान (life) / सो (that) / अगुन (without qualities) / अनूपम (matchless) / गुन (virtues) / निधान (storehouse) / सो (that)
ramacharitamanas::137.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::137.essence: Ram's name contains what the mind cannot fully describe.
ramacharitamanas::137.simple_meaning: Ram's name is not just a sound. It is treated as the source of creation, the life of the Vedas, beyond qualities, and full of all virtues.
ramacharitamanas::137.simple_insight: A single sacred name can hold more power than any description.
ramacharitamanas::137.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram's name itself, not just Ram's form. In the Balkand, the hymn turns from story to devotion: the name is presented as the essence of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva, and as the deepest support of sacred speech.
ramacharitamanas::137.modern_relevance: You are repeating a name under your breath while the room is still dark and your mind is noisy. The verse says the name itself can gather scattered attention and carry more than explanation ever could.
ramacharitamanas::137.insight: It shifts devotion from image or ritual to the living power of remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::138.verse_sanskrit: महामंत्र जोइ जपत महेसू। कासीं मुकुति हेतु उपदेसू॥ महिमा जासु जान गनराऊ। प्रथम पूजिअत नाम प्रभाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::138.verse_hindi: जो महामंत्र है, जिसे महेश्वर श्री शिवजी जपते हैं और उनके द्वारा जिसका उपदेश काशी में मुक्ति का कारण है तथा जिसकी महिमा को गणेशजी जानते हैं, जो इस 'राम' नाम के प्रभाव से ही सबसे पहले पूजे जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::138.english_translation: The great mantra that Mahesha repeats, and that teaches liberation in Kashi, is known by Ganarau. By the power of Ram's name, Ganesh is worshipped first.
ramacharitamanas::138.translation_literal: महामंत्र (great mantra) / जोइ (which) / जपत (repeats) / महेसू (Mahesha) / कासीं (in Kashi) / मुकुति (liberation) / हेतु (for cause) / उपदेसू (teaching) / महिमा (glory) / जासु (whose) / जान (knows) / गनराऊ (Ganarau) / प्रथम (first) / पूजिअत (is worshipped) / नाम (name) / प्रभाऊ (power)
ramacharitamanas::138.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::138.essence: Ram's name itself carries the power that devotion seeks.
ramacharitamanas::138.simple_meaning: Ram's name is the highest mantra. Shiva repeats it, Kashi teaches liberation through it, and even Ganesh is honored first because of its power.
ramacharitamanas::138.simple_insight: Repetition becomes reverence when the name itself carries power.
ramacharitamanas::138.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram's name as the central force of devotion. He says Shiva repeats it, Kashi points to it as the way to freedom, and even Ganesh's first worship is tied to its power. The verse lifts the name above ritual and makes it the source of blessing.
ramacharitamanas::138.modern_relevance: You are anxious before a hard phone call, so you keep returning to one steady phrase. The mind settles not because the problem vanished, but because the anchor is stronger than the fear.
ramacharitamanas::138.insight: It shifts attention from external rituals to the power of inward remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::139.verse_sanskrit: जान आदिकबि नाम प्रतापू। भयउ सुद्ध करि उलटा जापू॥ सहस नाम सम सुनि सिव बानी। जपि जेईं पिय संग भवानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::139.verse_hindi: आदिकवि श्री वाल्मीकिजी रामनाम के प्रताप को जानते हैं, जो उल्टा नाम ('मरा', 'मरा') जपकर पवित्र हो गए। श्री शिवजी के इस वचन को सुनकर कि एक राम-नाम सहस्र नाम के समान है, पार्वतीजी सदा अपने पति (श्री शिवजी) के साथ राम-नाम का जप करती रहती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::139.english_translation: Valmiki knew the power of Ram's name. By chanting it backward, he became pure. Hearing Shiva's word that one Ram-name equals a thousand names, Parvati always chants Ram's name with her husband.
ramacharitamanas::139.translation_literal: जान (knew) / आदिकबि (the first poet, Valmiki) / नाम (name) / प्रतापू (power, glory) / भयउ (became) / सुद्ध (pure) / करि (having made) / उलटा (reversed) / जापू (chanting)॥ / सहस (thousand) / नाम (names) / सम (equal to) / सुनि (hearing) / सिव (Shiva) / बानी (word, speech) / जपि (chanting) / जेईं (who) / पिय (beloved husband) / संग (with) / भवानी (Parvati)
ramacharitamanas::139.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::139.essence: Ram's name works even when the chanting begins in error.
ramacharitamanas::139.simple_meaning: Ram's name has such power that even a reversed chant made Valmiki pure. Shiva says one Ram-name equals a thousand names, and Parvati repeats it with him.
ramacharitamanas::139.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that a single sincere name can carry more power than effortful repetition.
ramacharitamanas::139.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram's name through Valmiki, Shiva, and Parvati. Valmiki's backward chant becomes holy, and Shiva's praise makes Parvati cling to that name. The scene shows that devotion works because the name itself is alive with power.
ramacharitamanas::139.modern_relevance: You are muttering the same prayer while driving through traffic, barely awake. The words feel small, but the verse says a single sacred name can still change the one who repeats it.
ramacharitamanas::139.insight: It shifts attention from the perfection of technique to the sincerity of remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::140.verse_sanskrit: हरषे हेतु हेरि हर ही को। किय भूषन तिय भूषन ती को॥ नाम प्रभाउ जान सिव नीको। कालकूट फलु दीन्ह अमी को ॥
ramacharitamanas::140.verse_hindi: नाम के प्रति पार्वतीजी के हृदय की ऐसी प्रीति देखकर श्री शिवजी हर्षित हो गए और उन्होंने स्त्रियों में भूषण रूप (पतिव्रताओं में शिरोमणि) पार्वतीजी को अपना भूषण बना लिया। (अर्थात् उन्हें अपने अंग में धारण करके अर्धांगिनी बना लिया)। नाम के प्रभाव को श्री शिवजी भलीभाँति जानते हैं, जिस (प्रभाव) के कारण कालकूट जहर ने उनको अमृत का फल दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::140.english_translation: Seeing Parvati's love for the Name, Shiva became delighted and took the ornament among women as his own ornament. Shiva knows the power of the Name well: it turned poison into nectar for him.
ramacharitamanas::140.translation_literal: हरषे (rejoiced) / हेतु (because) / हेरि (seeing) / हर (Shiva) / ही (indeed) / को (of) / किय (made) / भूषन (ornament) / तिय (women) / भूषन (ornament) / ती (that) / को (of) ॥ नाम (Name) / प्रभाउ (power) / जान (knowing) / सिव (Shiva) / नीको (well) / को (that) / कालकूट (halahala poison) / फलु (result) / दीन्ह (gave) / अमी (nectar) / को (to) ॥
ramacharitamanas::140.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::140.essence: The Name can turn poison into nectar.
ramacharitamanas::140.simple_meaning: Shiva rejoices in Parvati's devotion to Ram's name. He knows that the name's power can turn poison into nectar.
ramacharitamanas::140.simple_insight: Faith grows stronger when you see it transform even poison into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::140.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking in the Balkand frame, responding to Parvati's love for Ram's name. He honors her devotion and recalls his own experience with the poison that became harmless through the Name. The point is the Name's living power.
ramacharitamanas::140.modern_relevance: You are sitting with someone who has held on through a terrible year, and they say one practice kept them alive. You stop arguing with theory because you can see the change in them.
ramacharitamanas::140.insight: It shifts attention from abstract belief to the felt power of devotion in action.

ramacharitamanas::141.verse_sanskrit: बरषा रितु रघुपति भगति तुलसी सालि सुदास। राम नाम बर बरन जुग सावन भादव मास ॥
ramacharitamanas::141.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी की भक्ति वर्षा ऋतु है, तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि उत्तम सेवकगण धान हैं और 'राम' नाम के दो सुंदर अक्षर सावन-भादो के महीने हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::141.english_translation: Devotion to Raghupati is the rainy season; Tulsi says worthy servants are the rice crop, and the two lovely syllables of Ram’s name are the months of Sawan and Bhadon.
ramacharitamanas::141.translation_literal: बरषा रितु (rainy season) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / भगति (devotion) / तुलसी (Tulsi) / सालि (rice crop) / सुदास (good servants) / राम (Ram) / नाम (name) / बर (excellent) / बरन (syllables) / जुग (pair) / सावन (Sawan) / भादव (Bhadon) / मास (months)
ramacharitamanas::141.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::141.essence: Ram’s name is the season in which devotion ripens into service.
ramacharitamanas::141.simple_meaning: Ram’s devotion is like the rainy season that nourishes everything. His name is like the two monsoon months, and devoted servants are the ripe crop that grows from it.
ramacharitamanas::141.simple_insight: You are not just hearing a name. You are entering a season that makes devotion grow naturally.
ramacharitamanas::141.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram’s name after explaining its power through Shiva’s words. He now turns that teaching into a living image: devotion is the nourishing season, sincere servants are the crop, and Ram’s two syllables are the monsoon months that make everything flourish.
ramacharitamanas::141.modern_relevance: You hear a name repeated in a crowded temple, and suddenly the whole room feels alive. That is what happens when remembrance stops being sound and starts becoming climate.
ramacharitamanas::141.insight: It shifts the mind from treating devotion as a ritual to seeing it as a living force that ripens character.

ramacharitamanas::142.verse_sanskrit: आखर मधुर मनोहर दोऊ। बरन बिलोचन जन जिय जोऊ॥ ससुमिरत सुलभ सुखद सब काहू। लोक लाहु परलोक निबाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::142.verse_hindi: दोनों अक्षर मधुर और मनोहर हैं, जो वर्णमाला रूपी शरीर के नेत्र हैं, भक्तों के जीवन हैं तथा स्मरण करने में सबके लिए सुलभ और सुख देने वाले हैं और जो इस लोक में लाभ और परलोक में निर्वाह करते हैं (अर्थात् भगवान के दिव्य धाम में दिव्य देह से सदा भगवत्सेवा में नियुक्त रखते हैं।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::142.english_translation: Both syllables are sweet and lovely. They are the eyes of the alphabet, the life of devotees. Remembering them is easy and brings happiness to everyone. They give gain in this world and support beyond it.
ramacharitamanas::142.translation_literal: आखर (letters/syllables) / मधुर (sweet) / मनोहर (delightful) / दोऊ (both) / बरन (letters) / बिलोचन (eyes) / जन (devotees/people) / जिय (life) / जोऊ (indeed) / ससुमिरत (remembering) / सुलभ (easy to obtain) / सुखद (happiness-giving) / सब (all) / काहू (to anyone) / लोक (this world) / लाहु (gain) / परलोक (the other world) / निबाहू (support/continuance)
ramacharitamanas::142.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::142.essence: Ram’s name is simple enough for anyone and strong enough for both worlds.
ramacharitamanas::142.simple_meaning: The two syllables of Ram's name are beautiful, easy to remember, and bring happiness. They help in this world and support a person beyond it.
ramacharitamanas::142.simple_insight: A sacred name can feel simple and still carry everything you need.
ramacharitamanas::142.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising the two syllables of Ram’s name after linking them to devotion, seasons, and the sweetness of remembrance. He says they are easy for anyone, bring joy, and support a devotee both in ordinary life and beyond it.
ramacharitamanas::142.modern_relevance: You are exhausted, scrolling past a hundred noisy thoughts, and one short prayer calms the whole mind. Some words do not just sound beautiful — they hold you together.
ramacharitamanas::142.insight: It shifts attention from complexity to the steady power of simple remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::143.verse_sanskrit: कहत सुनत सुमिरत सुठि नीके। राम लखन सम प्रिय तुलसी के॥ बरनत बरन प्रीति बिलगाती। ब्रह्म जीव सम सहज सँघाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::143.verse_hindi: ये कहने, सुनने और स्मरण करने में बहुत ही अच्छे (सुंदर और मधुर) हैं, तुलसीदास को तो श्री राम-लक्ष्मण के समान प्यारे हैं। इनका ('र' और 'म' का) अलग-अलग वर्णन करने में प्रीति बिलगाती है (अर्थात बीज मंत्र की दृष्टि से इनके उच्चारण, अर्थ और फल में भिन्नता दिख पड़ती है), परन्तु हैं ये जीव और ब्रह्म के समान स्वभाव से ही साथ रहने वाले (सदा एक रूप और एक रस), ॥
