ramacharitamanas::143.english_translation: Speaking, hearing, and remembering them is deeply delightful. Tulsi finds Ram and Lakshman as dear as his own life. Their distinction in description awakens love, yet they are naturally united like Brahman and the individual being.
ramacharitamanas::143.translation_literal: कहत (speaking) / सुनत (hearing) / सुमिरत (remembering) / सुठि (very) / नीके (good, delightful) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / सम (like) / प्रिय (dear) / तुलसी के (to Tulsi's) ॥ बरनत (describing) / बरन (letter, form) / प्रीति (love) / बिलगाती (separates, differentiates) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / जीव (individual being) / सम (like) / सहज (naturally) / सँघाती (joined together, united) ॥
ramacharitamanas::143.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::143.essence: The sacred name is sweet because love and unity live inside it.
ramacharitamanas::143.simple_meaning: The names are sweet to speak, hear, and remember. Tulsi loves Ram and Lakshman deeply, and the two names are distinct in form yet naturally united in essence.
ramacharitamanas::143.simple_insight: Love turns a name into presence. Repeating it becomes a way of staying close.
ramacharitamanas::143.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, Tulsidas is praising the sacred power of Ram-naam after describing the two syllables as sweet and life-giving. He now says that speaking, hearing, and remembering them is deeply pleasing, and that Ram and Lakshman are dear to him while the two sounds remain inseparable in their inner unity.
ramacharitamanas::143.modern_relevance: You whisper a name under your breath while waiting for a call that matters. The sound itself steadies you, because love can live inside repetition.
ramacharitamanas::143.insight: It shifts attention from explanation to intimate remembrance, showing that devotion can make a name itself feel alive.

ramacharitamanas::144.verse_sanskrit: नर नारायन सरिस सुभ्राता। जग पालक बिसेषि जन त्राता॥ भगति सुतिय कल करन बिभूषन। जग हित हेतु बिमल बिधु पूषन ॥
ramacharitamanas::144.verse_hindi: ये दोनों अक्षर नर-नारायण के समान सुंदर भाई हैं, ये जगत का पालन और विशेष रूप से भक्तों की रक्षा करने वाले हैं। ये भक्ति रूपिणी सुंदर स्त्री के कानों के सुंदर आभूषण (कर्णफूल) हैं और जगत के हित के लिए निर्मल चन्द्रमा और सूर्य हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::144.english_translation: These two letters are like noble brothers, like Nara and Narayana. They protect the world, and especially protect their devotees. They are the beautiful ornaments in the ear of devotion, and for the good of the world they shine like the pure moon and sun.
ramacharitamanas::144.translation_literal: नर (Nara) / नारायन (Narayana) / सरिस (like) / सुभ्राता (good brothers)। / जग (world) / पालक (protector) / बिसेषि (especially) / जन (devotees/people) / त्राता (saviour, protector)॥ / भगति (devotion) / सुतिय (beautiful ear-ornament) / कल (artful, lovely) / करन (ear) / बिभूषन (ornament)॥ / जग (world) / हित (good, welfare) / हेतु (for the sake of) / बिमल (pure) / बिधु (moon) / पूषन (sun)॥
ramacharitamanas::144.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::144.essence: Holy remembrance protects devotees and brightens the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::144.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are like noble brothers who protect the world, especially those who devote themselves to Ram. They are like beautiful ornaments for devotion and shine for the welfare of all.
ramacharitamanas::144.simple_insight: Love for Ram is not abstract; it feels like protection, beauty, and steady light in life.
ramacharitamanas::144.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising the holy names as if they were living companions. After saying they are sweet to speak, hear, and remember, he now calls them world-protectors, especially for devotees. The praise rises toward a full devotional vision before moving on to the fruits of remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::144.modern_relevance: You whisper a name under your breath while walking into a hospital waiting room. It steadies you before the news arrives. Some words do that: they protect the heart before they explain anything.
ramacharitamanas::144.insight: It shifts remembrance from habit to shelter, showing that devotion can actively guard the mind.

ramacharitamanas::145.verse_sanskrit: स्वाद तोष सम सुगति सुधा के। कमठ सेष सम धर बसुधा के॥ जन मन मंजु कंज मधुकर से। जीह जसोमति हरि हलधर से ॥
ramacharitamanas::145.verse_hindi: ये सुंदर गति (मोक्ष) रूपी अमृत के स्वाद और तृप्ति के समान हैं, कच्छप और शेषजी के समान पृथ्वी के धारण करने वाले हैं, भक्तों के मन रूपी सुंदर कमल में विहार करने वाले भौंरे के समान हैं और जीभ रूपी यशोदाजी के लिए श्री कृष्ण और बलरामजी के समान (आनंद देने वाले) हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::145.english_translation: Their taste is like the nectar of liberation and complete satisfaction; they uphold the earth like the tortoise and the serpent; they dwell like a bee in the beautiful lotus of the devotee’s mind; and to the tongue, they are like Krishna and Balarama to Yashoda.
ramacharitamanas::145.translation_literal: स्वाद (taste) / तोष (contentment) / सम (like) / सुगति (good passage, liberation) / सुधा (nectar) के (of) / कमठ (tortoise) / सेष (serpent Shesha) / सम (like) / धर (to hold) / बसुधा (earth) के (of) / जन (people, devotees) / मन (mind) / मंजु (beautiful) / कंज (lotus) / मधुकर (bee) से (like) / जीह (tongue) / जसोमति (Yashoda) / हरि (Hari, Ram) / हलधर (Balarama) से (like)
ramacharitamanas::145.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::145.essence: Ram’s name sustains the mind and delights the tongue.
ramacharitamanas::145.simple_meaning: Ram’s name is as satisfying as nectar, as sustaining as the beings who hold up the earth, and as sweet to a devotee’s mind and tongue as a bee to a lotus.
ramacharitamanas::145.simple_insight: Devotion becomes both nourishment and delight: it supports you, then fills you with joy.
ramacharitamanas::145.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram’s name through layered images. After describing Ram and Lakshman as beloved and protective, he now says their praise is nectar-like, sustaining like the great beings who bear the earth, and irresistibly sweet in the devotee’s mind and speech.
ramacharitamanas::145.modern_relevance: You whisper a name in the dark while the room feels heavy. The words do not just comfort you — they steady you, sweeten you, and hold you together.
ramacharitamanas::145.insight: It shifts remembrance from mere recitation to living support, making devotion feel nourishing rather than formal.

ramacharitamanas::146.verse_sanskrit: एकु छत्रु एकु मुकुटमनि सब बरननि पर जोउ। तुलसी रघुबर नाम के बरन बिराजत दोउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::146.verse_hindi: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- श्री रघुनाथजी के नाम के दोनों अक्षर बड़ी शोभा देते हैं, जिनमें से एक (रकार) छत्ररूप (रेफ र्) से और दूसरा (मकार) मुकुटमणि (अनुस्वार) रूप से सब अक्षरों के ऊपर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::146.english_translation: Tulsidas says: the two letters of Lord Raghunath's name shine with great splendor, one like a royal umbrella and the other like a crown jewel, standing above all letters.
ramacharitamanas::146.translation_literal: एकु (one) / छत्रु (umbrella) / एकु (one) / मुकुटमनि (crown-jewel) / सब (all) / बरननि (letters) / पर (above) / जोउ (shine) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / रघुबर (Lord of Raghu) / नाम (name) / के (of) / बरन (letters) / बिराजत (shine) / दोउ (both)
ramacharitamanas::146.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::146.essence: Ram's name shines with the dignity of the one it names.
ramacharitamanas::146.simple_meaning: The two letters in Ram's name are imagined as royal ornaments above every other letter. The verse praises the beauty and greatness of the name itself.
ramacharitamanas::146.simple_insight: Even the smallest part of a sacred name can carry majesty.
ramacharitamanas::146.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram's name itself, not telling a story event. He sees the letters of 'Raghubar' as royal symbols, with one like a parasol and the other like a crown jewel. The verse prepares the next teaching: name and the one named are deeply joined.
ramacharitamanas::146.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of a loved one's name on your phone and feel your day change. A name can carry presence, memory, and power long before the person arrives.
ramacharitamanas::146.insight: It shifts attention from the object to the living power carried by its name.

ramacharitamanas::147.verse_sanskrit: समुझत सरिस नाम अरु नामी। प्रीति परसपर प्रभु अनुगामी॥ नाम रूप दुइ ईस उपाधी। अकथ अनादि सुसामुझि साधी ॥
ramacharitamanas::147.verse_hindi: समझने में नाम और नामी दोनों एक से हैं, किन्तु दोनों में परस्पर स्वामी और सेवक के समान प्रीति है (अर्थात् नाम और नामी में पूर्ण एकता होने पर भी जैसे स्वामी के पीछे सेवक चलता है, उसी प्रकार नाम के पीछे नामी चलते हैं। प्रभु श्री रामजी अपने 'राम' नाम का ही अनुगमन करते हैं (नाम लेते ही वहाँ आ जाते हैं)। नाम और रूप दोनों ईश्वर की उपाधि हैं, ये (भगवान के नाम और रूप) दोनों अनिर्वचनीय हैं, अनादि हैं और सुंदर (शुद्ध भक्तियुक्त) बुद्धि से ही इनका (दिव्य अविनाशी) स्वरूप जानने में आता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::147.english_translation: Name and the named are equal in understanding, yet there is mutual love like master and servant. The Lord follows his own name. Name and form are both divine labels, beyond speech, without beginning, and known only by pure devotion.
ramacharitamanas::147.translation_literal: समुझत (in understanding) / सरिस (equal) / नाम (name) / अरु (and) / नामी (the named one) / प्रीति (love) / परसपर (mutual) / प्रभु (the Lord) / अनुगामी (follows) / नाम (name) / रूप (form) / दुइ (both) / ईस (divine) / उपाधी (labels) / अकथ (unspeakable) / अनादि (without beginning) / सुसामुझि (pure understanding) / साधी (attained)
ramacharitamanas::147.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::147.essence: Ram's name is not a sign pointing away from him; it brings him near.
ramacharitamanas::147.simple_meaning: Ram's name and Ram himself are one, yet they relate like beloved companions. His name, his form, and his presence are beyond ordinary speech and can be known through pure devotion.
ramacharitamanas::147.simple_insight: You do not reach Ram by effort alone; sincere devotion makes the name alive and present.
ramacharitamanas::147.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is teaching a deep truth about Ram's name in the Balkand. After praising the beauty of the name, he explains that the name and Ram are equal, yet lovingly distinct in relation. This verse prepares the claim that chanting the name is meeting Ram himself.
ramacharitamanas::147.modern_relevance: You whisper someone's name before calling them, and they answer from the next room. In devotion, the name is like that: not a label, but a living presence that turns attention into meeting.
ramacharitamanas::147.insight: It shifts practice from treating sacred words as symbols to meeting presence through sound itself.

ramacharitamanas::148.verse_sanskrit: को बड़ छोट कहत अपराधू। सुनि गुन भेदु समुझिहहिं साधू॥ देखिअहिं रूप नाम आधीना। रूप ग्यान नहिं नाम बिहीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::148.verse_hindi: इन (नाम और रूप) में कौन बड़ा है, कौन छोटा, यह कहना तो अपराध है। इनके गुणों का तारतम्य (कमी-बेशी) सुनकर साधु पुरुष स्वयं ही समझ लेंगे। रूप नाम के अधीन देखे जाते हैं, नाम के बिना रूप का ज्ञान नहीं हो सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::148.english_translation: Calling one greater or lesser is an offense. The wise understand the difference by hearing the qualities. Form is known through name; without name, form cannot be known.
ramacharitamanas::148.translation_literal: को (who) / बड़ (big) / छोट (small) / कहत (saying) / अपराधू (offense) / सुनि (hearing) / गुन (qualities) / भेदु (difference) / समुझिहहिं (will understand) / साधू (the wise) ॥ / देखिअहिं (are seen) / रूप (form) / नाम (name) / आधीना (dependent) ॥ / रूप (form) / ग्यान (knowledge) / नहिं (not) / नाम (name) / बिहीना (without) ॥
ramacharitamanas::148.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::148.essence: Name and form are inseparable; each reveals what the other cannot.
ramacharitamanas::148.simple_meaning: Do not rank name above form or form above name. Wise people understand their relationship: form depends on name, and form cannot be known without name.
ramacharitamanas::148.simple_insight: It softens the urge to compare and rank, and replaces it with a quieter way of understanding.
ramacharitamanas::148.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is deepening the idea that Ram's name and Ram's form are not separate rivals. After saying they belong together, he now warns against judging one as superior. The teaching is that name helps the mind recognize form, and form gives name living presence.
ramacharitamanas::148.modern_relevance: You see a face in a crowd and cannot place it until someone says the name. Then memory clicks into place. The mind needs both recognition and naming; forcing one to stand alone only creates confusion.
ramacharitamanas::148.insight: It shifts the mind from comparison to interdependence: name and form complete each other.

ramacharitamanas::149.verse_sanskrit: रूप बिसेष नाम बिनु जानें। करतल गत न परहिं पहिचानें॥ सुमिरिअ नाम रूप बिनु देखें। आवत हृदयँ सनेह बिसेषें ॥
ramacharitamanas::149.verse_hindi: कोई सा विशेष रूप बिना उसका नाम जाने हथेली पर रखा हुआ भी पहचाना नहीं जा सकता और रूप के बिना देखे भी नाम का स्मरण किया जाए तो विशेष प्रेम के साथ वह रूप हृदय में आ जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::149.english_translation: A specific form cannot be recognized without knowing its name, even if it lies in the palm of your hand. But if the name is remembered without seeing the form, that form comes into the heart with special love.
ramacharitamanas::149.translation_literal: रूप (form) / बिसेष (specific) / नाम (name) / बिनु (without) / जानें (knowing) / करतल (palm of the hand) / गत (placed) / न (not) / परहिं (fall) / पहिचानें (recognized)॥ / सुमिरिअ (remember) / नाम (name) / रूप (form) / बिनु (without) / देखें (seeing) / आवत (comes) / हृदयँ (into the heart) / सनेह (love) / बिसेषें (with special)
ramacharitamanas::149.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::149.essence: Remembrance can summon presence before sight does.
ramacharitamanas::149.simple_meaning: A form is hard to recognize without its name, and a remembered name can bring that form vividly into the heart even before you see it.
ramacharitamanas::149.simple_insight: Love can begin before sight. A name can call the heart toward what it has not yet met.
ramacharitamanas::149.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is explaining the mystery of Ram's name and form in the middle of a devotional teaching on how the two relate. He says name and form work together: one helps you recognize the other, and remembrance can draw the beloved presence inward.
ramacharitamanas::149.modern_relevance: You hear a friend mention someone you care about, and suddenly their face and presence feel close again. A name can do that work before any meeting ever happens.
ramacharitamanas::149.insight: It shifts devotion from needing direct sight to trusting remembrance as a real bridge to presence.

ramacharitamanas::150.verse_sanskrit: नाम रूप गति अकथ कहानी। समुझत सुखद न परति बखानी॥ अगुन सगुन बिच नाम सुसाखी। उभय प्रबोधक चतुर दुभाषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::150.verse_hindi: नाम और रूप की गति की कहानी (विशेषता की कथा) अकथनीय है। वह समझने में सुखदायक है, परन्तु उसका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। निर्गुण और सगुण के बीच में नाम सुंदर साक्षी है और दोनों का यथार्थ ज्ञान कराने वाला चतुर दुभाषिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::150.english_translation: The movement of name and form is an indescribable story. It is sweet to understand, but impossible to fully describe. Between the formless and the formed, the name is a lovely witness and a skilled interpreter for both.
ramacharitamanas::150.translation_literal: नाम (name) / रूप (form) / गति (movement, nature) / अकथ (unspeakable) / कहानी (story) / समुझत (understanding) / सुखद (pleasant) / न (not) / परति (falls) / बखानी (into description)॥ / अगुन (without qualities, formless) / सगुन (with qualities, formed) / बिच (between) / नाम (name) / सुसाखी (good witness) / उभय (both) / प्रबोधक (awakener, explainer) / चतुर (skilled) / दुभाषी (interpreter) ॥
ramacharitamanas::150.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::150.essence: Name bridges what cannot be fully spoken or seen.
ramacharitamanas::150.simple_meaning: Name and form have a mystery that cannot be fully explained. The name stands between the formless and the formed, helping people understand both.
ramacharitamanas::150.simple_insight: Some truths are easier to recognise than to explain, and that is enough to guide you.
ramacharitamanas::150.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is deepening the earlier discussion of name and form. After saying the name can be known before the form, he now explains why: Ram's name bridges what has qualities and what does not, making the highest truth approachable in ordinary speech.
ramacharitamanas::150.modern_relevance: You know someone by their voice note before you ever meet them in person. The name carries presence across distance, making what is unseen feel near and real.
ramacharitamanas::150.insight: It shifts the mind from demanding total explanation to using name as a bridge to deeper understanding.

ramacharitamanas::151.verse_sanskrit: राम नाम मनिदीप धरु जीह देहरीं द्वार। तुलसी भीतर बाहेरहुँ जौं चाहसि उजिआर ॥
ramacharitamanas::151.verse_hindi: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं, यदि तू भीतर और बाहर दोनों ओर उजाला चाहता है, तो मुख रूपी द्वार की जीभ रूपी देहली पर रामनाम रूपी मणि-दीपक को रख ॥
ramacharitamanas::151.english_translation: Tulsidas says: If you want light both within and without, place Ram's name like a jewel-lamp on the threshold of your tongue.
ramacharitamanas::151.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / नाम (name) / मनि-दीप (jewel-lamp) / धरु (place) / जीह (tongue) / देहरीं (on the threshold) / द्वार (door) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / भीतर (inside) / बाहेरहुँ (and outside too) / जौं (if) / चाहसि (you want) / उजिआर (light)
ramacharitamanas::151.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::151.essence: Ram's name lights both the inside and the outside.
ramacharitamanas::151.simple_meaning: Keep Ram's name on your tongue like a lamp at the doorway. That single practice brings light to your inner life and your outer life.
ramacharitamanas::151.simple_insight: A simple remembrance can steady everything — what you say shapes the atmosphere you live in.
ramacharitamanas::151.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is closing the thought about name and form by turning it into a practice. He tells the reader that Ram's name, held on the tongue, becomes a lamp that brightens both the inner world and the outer world.
ramacharitamanas::151.modern_relevance: You catch yourself muttering a worried story while standing in a crowded kitchen, phone buzzing, mind split in ten directions. One steady remembrance can change the whole room you carry around.
ramacharitamanas::151.insight: It shifts attention from scattered chatter to a single sustaining remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::152.verse_sanskrit: नाम जीहँ जपि जागहिं जोगी। बिरति बिरंचि प्रपंच बियोगी॥ ब्रह्मसुखहि अनुभवहिं अनूपा। अकथ अनामय नाम न रूपा ॥
ramacharitamanas::152.verse_hindi: ब्रह्मा के बनाए हुए इस प्रपंच (दृश्य जगत) से भलीभाँति छूटे हुए वैराग्यवान् मुक्त योगी पुरुष इस नाम को ही जीभ से जपते हुए (तत्व ज्ञान रूपी दिन में) जागते हैं और नाम तथा रूप से रहित अनुपम, अनिर्वचनीय, अनामय ब्रह्मसुख का अनुभव करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::152.english_translation: Freed from the world of appearances, awakened yogis keep chanting the Name with the tongue. They experience a unique bliss beyond speech—pure, formless, and beyond name and form.
ramacharitamanas::152.translation_literal: नाम (Name) / जीहँ (with the tongue) / जपि (chanting) / जागहिं (remain awake) / जोगी (yogis) / बिरति (detached) / बिरंचि (Brahma's) / प्रपंच (manifest world) / बियोगी (separated from) / ब्रह्मसुखहि (the bliss of the supreme reality) / अनुभवहिं (experience) / अनूपा (matchless) / अकथ (unspeakable) / अनामय (free from affliction) / नाम (name) / न (not) / रूपा (form)
ramacharitamanas::152.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::152.essence: The Name wakes the mind beyond name and form.
ramacharitamanas::152.simple_meaning: Detached yogis stay awake to the world’s illusion by chanting the Name. They taste a bliss beyond words, beyond name and form.
ramacharitamanas::152.simple_insight: You do not have to chase experiences to be spiritually awake; steady remembrance can open a deeper peace.
ramacharitamanas::152.detailed_meaning: The teaching turns from the earlier praise of Ram's Name into its highest philosophical claim. Tulsidas says that liberated yogis, already free from the world of appearances, keep repeating the Name and directly taste a bliss that cannot be described.
ramacharitamanas::152.modern_relevance: You are scrolling at 1 a.m., trying to quiet a mind that will not stop naming everything: success, failure, comparison, fear. This verse points to a quieter awareness that does not need the noise to feel real.
ramacharitamanas::152.insight: It shifts attention from chasing mental labels to resting in a deeper awareness that words cannot hold.

ramacharitamanas::153.verse_sanskrit: जाना चहहिं गूढ़ गति जेऊ। नाम जीहँ जपि जानहिं तेऊ॥ साधक नाम जपहिं लय लाएँ। होहिं सिद्ध अनिमादिक पाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::153.verse_hindi: जो परमात्मा के गूढ़ रहस्य को (यथार्थ महिमा को) जानना चाहते हैं, वे (जिज्ञासु) भी नाम को जीभ से जपकर उसे जान लेते हैं। (लौकिक सिद्धियों के चाहने वाले अर्थार्थी) साधक लौ लगाकर नाम का जप करते हैं और अणिमादि (आठों) सिद्धियों को पाकर सिद्ध हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::153.english_translation: Those who seek the hidden way know it by chanting the Name with the tongue. Seekers who practice with focused concentration attain the eight powers and become accomplished.
ramacharitamanas::153.translation_literal: जाना चहहिं (wish to know) / गूढ़ गति (hidden way) / जेऊ (those who) / नाम (the Name) / जीहँ (with the tongue) / जपि (chanting) / जानहिं (know) / तेऊ (they) / साधक (practitioners) / नाम (the Name) / जपहिं (chant) / लय लाएँ (with focused absorption) / होहिं (become) / सिद्ध (accomplished) / अनिमादिक (beginning with atomic power) / पाएँ (having attained)
ramacharitamanas::153.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::153.essence: The Name opens both hidden truth and extraordinary attainment.
ramacharitamanas::153.simple_meaning: People who want to understand the deepest mystery can reach it through chanting the divine name. Even those seeking special powers can gain them by steady, absorbed repetition.
ramacharitamanas::153.simple_insight: There is relief in this: the deepest access does not require status, only sincere repetition.
ramacharitamanas::153.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is building on the claim that Ram's name brightens both inside and outside. He now says that seekers of hidden truth and seekers of spiritual powers alike reach their goal by repeating the Name with focused attention.
ramacharitamanas::153.modern_relevance: You are scrolling for the perfect method, the perfect teacher, the perfect sign. The verse says the door is simpler than your search: steady repetition with attention changes what you can know.
ramacharitamanas::153.insight: It shifts the seeker from chasing rare experiences to trusting disciplined repetition.

ramacharitamanas::154.verse_sanskrit: जपहिं नामु जन आरत भारी। मिटहिं कुसंकट होहिं सुखारी॥ राम भगत जग चारि प्रकारा। सुकृती चारिउ अनघ उदारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::154.verse_hindi: (संकट से घबड़ाए हुए) आर्त भक्त नाम जप करते हैं, तो उनके बड़े भारी बुरे-बुरे संकट मिट जाते हैं और वे सुखी हो जाते हैं। जगत में चार प्रकार के (1- अर्थार्थी-धनादि की चाह से भजने वाले, 2-आर्त संकट की निवृत्ति के लिए भजने वाले, 3-जिज्ञासु-भगवान को जानने की इच्छा से भजने वाले, 4-ज्ञानी-भगवान को तत्व से जानकर स्वाभाविक ही प्रेम से भजने वाले) रामभक्त हैं और चारों ही पुण्यात्मा, पापरहित और उदार हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::154.english_translation: People in deep distress chant Ram's name. Their great troubles disappear, and they become happy. In the world, there are four kinds of Ram devotees. All four are virtuous, pure, and generous.
ramacharitamanas::154.translation_literal: जपहिं (chant) / नामु (the name) / जन (people) / आरत (in distress) / भारी (greatly) / मिटहिं (are removed) / कुसंकट (grave troubles) / होहिं (become) / सुखारी (happy) ॥ / राम (Ram's) / भगत (devotees) / जग (in the world) / चारि (four) / प्रकारा (kinds) ॥ / सुकृती (virtuous) / चारिउ (all four) / अनघ (free from sin) / उदारा (generous) ॥
ramacharitamanas::154.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::154.essence: Ram's name turns distress into relief and ordinary seekers into noble devotees.
ramacharitamanas::154.simple_meaning: People in deep distress find relief by chanting Ram's name. The verse also says there are four kinds of Ram devotees, and all of them are virtuous and generous.
ramacharitamanas::154.simple_insight: You do not need perfect conditions to pray; even pain can become a doorway to grace.
ramacharitamanas::154.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is explaining the power of Ram's name in the middle of a devotional teaching. He says that people crushed by trouble can chant and find relief, then broadens the view: all four kinds of Ram devotees are pure-hearted and noble.
ramacharitamanas::154.modern_relevance: You are sitting in a parked car after a call that went badly, hands still shaking. Instead of spiralling, you repeat one sacred name and feel the grip loosen. The mind needs a refuge before it needs a solution.
ramacharitamanas::154.insight: It shifts the mind from panic to refuge, teaching that distress itself can turn into devotion.

ramacharitamanas::155.verse_sanskrit: चहू चतुर कहुँ नाम अधारा। ग्यानी प्रभुहि बिसेषि पिआरा॥ चहुँ जुग चहुँ श्रुति नाम प्रभाऊ। कलि बिसेषि नहिं आन उपाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::155.verse_hindi: चारों ही चतुर भक्तों को नाम का ही आधार है, इनमें ज्ञानी भक्त प्रभु को विशेष रूप से प्रिय हैं। यों तो चारों युगों में और चारों ही वेदों में नाम का प्रभाव है, परन्तु कलियुग में विशेष रूप से है। इसमें तो (नाम को छोड़कर) दूसरा कोई उपाय ही नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::155.english_translation: All wise devotees depend on the Name; among them, the discerning devotee is especially dear to the Lord. Through all four ages and all four Vedas, the Name has power; in Kali Yuga, there is no other way.
ramacharitamanas::155.translation_literal: चहू (four) / चतुर (wise) / कहुँ (for) / नाम (Name) / अधारा (support, refuge) / ग्यानी (knowing, discerning) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / बिसेषि (especially) / पिआरा (dear) / चहुँ (four) / जुग (ages) / चहुँ (four) / श्रुति (Vedas) / नाम (Name) / प्रभाऊ (power, influence) / कलि (Kali age) / बिसेषि (especially) / नहिं (not) / आन (other) / उपाऊ (means, way)
ramacharitamanas::155.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::155.essence: Ram's Name is the one refuge that still works when everything else fails.
ramacharitamanas::155.simple_meaning: The Name of Ram is the support for all sincere seekers, especially those who understand deeply. Its power exists in every age, but in this age it is the surest way.
ramacharitamanas::155.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing you do not need a complicated method — sincere remembrance is enough.
ramacharitamanas::155.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is speaking in the Balkand after describing different kinds of devotees. He now gathers them into one truth: all wise seekers rely on Ram's Name, and the discerning one is especially dear. The verse crowns the teaching by saying this Name works in every age, but most powerfully in Kali Yuga.
ramacharitamanas::155.modern_relevance: You are exhausted, overbooked, and trying ten fixes at once while life keeps slipping sideways. This verse says stop hunting for a clever workaround: return to the one practice that still holds you when everything else scatters.
ramacharitamanas::155.insight: It shifts attention from scattered methods to one steady refuge: remembrance of Ram.

ramacharitamanas::156.verse_sanskrit: सकल कामना हीन जे राम भगति रस लीन। नाम सुप्रेम पियूष ह्रद तिन्हहुँ किए मन मीन ॥
ramacharitamanas::156.verse_hindi: जो सब प्रकार की (भोग और मोक्ष की भी) कामनाओं से रहित और श्री रामभक्ति के रस में लीन हैं, उन्होंने भी नाम के सुंदर प्रेम रूपी अमृत के सरोवर में अपने मन को मछली बना रखा है (अर्थात् वे नाम रूपी सुधा का निरंतर आस्वादन करते रहते हैं, क्षणभर भी उससे अलग होना नहीं चाहते) ॥
ramacharitamanas::156.english_translation: Those free of all desire and absorbed in the taste of Ram devotion also keep their minds as fish in the lake of sweet love for the Name.
ramacharitamanas::156.translation_literal: सकल (all) / कामना (desire) / हीन (free from) / जे (who) / राम (Ram) / भगति (devotion) / रस (essence/taste) / लीन (absorbed) / नाम (Name) / सुप्रेम (of pure love) / पियूष (nectar) / ह्रद (lake) / तिन्हहुँ (even they) / किए (made) / मन (mind) / मीन (fish)
ramacharitamanas::156.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::156.essence: Even desireless devotion still longs to stay in Ram's Name.
ramacharitamanas::156.simple_meaning: Even people who have no desire left and are already absorbed in Ram's devotion still keep their minds immersed in loving remembrance of the Name.
ramacharitamanas::156.simple_insight: Love for Ram does not end need; it transforms longing into constant remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::156.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the highest devotees in this Balkand passage. Even those who have dropped every worldly wish and are already immersed in Ram's devotion still keep their minds swimming in the nectar of the Name, unable to stay apart from it.
ramacharitamanas::156.modern_relevance: You finally finish the goal you chased for months, and the quiet afterward feels strange. What remains is not hunger for more, but the sweetness of what you keep returning to.
ramacharitamanas::156.insight: It shifts devotion from occasional practice to continuous inward attraction.

ramacharitamanas::157.verse_sanskrit: अगुन सगुन दुइ ब्रह्म सरूपा। अकथ अगाध अनादि अनूपा॥ मोरें मत बड़ नामु दुहू तें। किए जेहिं जुग िनज बस निज बूतें ॥
ramacharitamanas::157.verse_hindi: निर्गुण और सगुण ब्रह्म के दो स्वरूप हैं। ये दोनों ही अकथनीय, अथाह, अनादि और अनुपम हैं। मेरी सम्मति में नाम इन दोनों से बड़ा है, जिसने अपने बल से दोनों को अपने वश में कर रखा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::157.english_translation: Unmanifest and manifest are two forms of the supreme reality. Both are indescribable, immeasurable, beginningless, and incomparable. In my view, the Name is greater than both, because it has brought both under its own command.
ramacharitamanas::157.translation_literal: अगुन (without qualities / unmanifest) / सगुन (with qualities / manifest) / दुइ (two) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / सरूपा (forms) । अकथ (unspeakable) / अगाध (bottomless) / अनादि (beginningless) / अनूपा (incomparable) ॥ मोरें (in my view) / मत (opinion) / बड़ (greater) / नामु (the Name) / दुहू (of both) / तें (than) । किए (made) / जेहिं (which) / जुग (both) / निज बस (under its own control) / निज बूतें (by its own power) ॥
ramacharitamanas::157.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::157.essence: The Name is greater than every form because it contains them both.
ramacharitamanas::157.simple_meaning: The divine has both formless and formed aspects, but the sacred Name is greater than both because it controls them.
ramacharitamanas::157.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that a simple Name can carry what seems too vast to hold.
ramacharitamanas::157.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is explaining the power of Ram's Name after praising devotion that needs nothing else. He says the divine appears both as formless and as personal form, yet the Name is even greater because it reaches and contains both.
ramacharitamanas::157.modern_relevance: You are overwhelmed in a temple, a prayer room, or even a silent walk, unsure what to hold onto. A single name can steady the mind when vast ideas feel out of reach.
ramacharitamanas::157.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract thinking to a direct, usable refuge: repeat the Name and let it gather everything else.

ramacharitamanas::158.verse_sanskrit: प्रौढ़ि सुजन जनि जानहिं जन की। कहउँ प्रतीति प्रीति रुचि मन की॥ एकु दारुगत देखिअ एकू। पावक सम जुग ब्रह्म बिबेकू ॥ उभय अगम जुग सुगम नाम तें। कहेउँ नामु बड़ ब्रह्म राम तें॥ ब्यापकु एकु ब्रह्म अबिनासी। सत चेतन घन आनँद रासी ॥
ramacharitamanas::158.verse_hindi: सज्जनगण इस बात को मुझ दास की ढिठाई या केवल काव्योक्ति न समझें। मैं अपने मन के विश्वास, प्रेम और रुचि की बात कहता हूँ। ( िनर्गुण और सगुण) दोनों प्रकार के ब्रह्म का ज्ञान अग्नि के समान है। निर्गुण उस अप्रकट अग्नि के समान है, जो काठ के अंदर है, परन्तु दिखती नहीं और सगुण उस प्रकट अग्नि के समान है, जो प्रत्यक्ष दिखती है। (तत्त्वतः दोनों एक ही हैं, केवल प्रकट-अप्रकट के भेद से भिन्न मालूम होती हैं। इसी प्रकार निर्गुण और सगुण तत्त्वतः एक ही हैं। इतना होने पर भी) दोनों ही जानने में बड़े कठिन हैं, परन्तु नाम से दोनों सुगम हो जाते हैं। इसी से मैंने नाम को (निर्गुण) ब्रह्म से और (सगुण) राम से बड़ा कहा है, ब्रह्म व्यापक है, एक है, अविनाशी है, सत्ता, चैतन्य और आनन्द की घन राशि है॥2-3॥
ramacharitamanas::158.english_translation: Do not take this as mere boldness or poetry. I speak from conviction, love, and inward taste. The knowledge of both the formless and the formed supreme reality is like fire hidden in wood and fire made visible. Both are hard to know, but the divine name makes both easy. That is why I call the name greater than both the supreme reality and Ram. The supreme reality is all-pervading, one, imperishable, a dense treasury of being, awareness, and bliss.
ramacharitamanas::158.translation_literal: प्रौढ़ि (boldness / mere show) / सुजन (good people) / जनि (do not) / जानहिं (think/know) / जन की (of this servant) / कहउँ (I speak) / प्रतीति (conviction) / प्रीति (love) / रुचि (taste) / मन की (of the mind) / एकु (one) / दारुगत (in wood) / देखिअ (is seen) / एकू (one) / पावक (fire) / सम (like) / जुग (both) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / बिबेकू (knowledge/discrimination) / उभय (both) / अगम (hard to reach) / जुग (both) / सुगम (easy) / नाम तें (through the name) / कहेउँ (I said) / नामु (the name) / बड़ (greater) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / राम तें (than Ram) / ब्यापकु (all-pervading) / एकु (one) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / अबिनासी (imperishable) / सत (being) / चेतन (awareness) / घन (dense) / आनँद (bliss) / रासी (treasury)
ramacharitamanas::158.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::158.essence: The divine name opens what even the supreme reality can hide.
ramacharitamanas::158.simple_meaning: The divine name makes what is hardest to know easy to approach. Tulsidas says the name is greater than both the formless absolute and Ram's visible form because it opens access to both.
ramacharitamanas::158.simple_insight: You do not have to master everything before you can begin. A living name can carry you into what intellect alone cannot hold.
ramacharitamanas::158.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is explaining why he trusts Ram's name so deeply. After saying the name reaches beyond both formless and formed Brahman, he pauses to defend himself: this is not poetic exaggeration, but lived conviction. The claim is the peak of a devotional argument about access.
ramacharitamanas::158.modern_relevance: You are staring at a complex problem at 1:13 a.m., with five tabs open and no clarity. The answer is not always more analysis; sometimes one steady practice cuts through what the mind keeps multiplying.
ramacharitamanas::158.insight: It shifts the seeker from intellectual control to devotional access through repetition and trust.

ramacharitamanas::159.verse_sanskrit: अस प्रभु हृदयँ अछत अबिकारी। सकल जीव जग दीन दुखारी॥ नाम निरूपन नाम जतन तें। सोउ प्रगटत जिमि मोल रतन तें ॥
ramacharitamanas::159.verse_hindi: ऐसे विकाररहित प्रभु के हृदय में रहते भी जगत के सब जीव दीन और दुःखी हैं। नाम का निरूपण करके (नाम के यथार्थ स्वरूप, महिमा, रहस्य और प्रभाव को जानकर) नाम का जतन करने से (श्रद्धापूर्वक नाम जप रूपी साधन करने से) वही ब्रह्म ऐसे प्रकट हो जाता है, जैसे रत्न के जानने से उसका मूल्य ॥
ramacharitamanas::159.english_translation: Even while the changeless Lord dwells within the heart, all beings in the world remain poor and sorrowful. By understanding the true nature of the Name and practicing the Name with devotion, that supreme reality becomes manifest, just as a jewel reveals its worth when known.
ramacharitamanas::159.translation_literal: अस (such) / प्रभु (Lord) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / अछत (dwelling) / अबिकारी (unchanging) / सकल (all) / जीव (beings) / जग (world) / दीन (poor, helpless) / दुखारी (sorrowful) / नाम (Name) / निरूपन (true explanation) / नाम (Name) / जतन (practice, effort) / तें (by) / सोउ (that also) / प्रगटत (becomes manifest) / जिमि (as) / मोल (value) / रतन (jewel) / तें (from, by)
ramacharitamanas::159.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::159.essence: The Name reveals what is already present but still unseen.
ramacharitamanas::159.simple_meaning: The changeless Lord is already within every heart, yet people still suffer. Knowing the power of the Name and practicing it makes that presence clear, like a jewel whose worth is revealed when understood.
ramacharitamanas::159.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing the divine presence is already near; practice simply uncovers what was hidden.
ramacharitamanas::159.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is explaining the glory of Ram's Name after reflecting on the relation between the formless and the personal divine. He says the Lord already dwells in the heart, yet ordinary beings remain trapped in sorrow until the Name is understood and practiced.
ramacharitamanas::159.modern_relevance: You can sit in a quiet room with your phone off and still feel strangely far from yourself. The problem is not absence; it is not yet knowing how to meet what is already present.
ramacharitamanas::159.insight: It shifts devotion from distant belief to direct practice: understand the Name, repeat it, and let presence become clear.

ramacharitamanas::160.verse_sanskrit: निरगुन तें एहि भाँति बड़ नाम प्रभाउ अपार। कहउँ नामु बड़ राम तें निज बिचार अनुसार ॥
ramacharitamanas::160.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार निर्गुण से नाम का प्रभाव अत्यंत बड़ा है। अब अपने विचार के अनुसार कहता हूँ, कि नाम (सगुण) राम से भी बड़ा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::160.english_translation: In this way, the power of the Name is far greater than the formless. I say, according to my own understanding, that the Name is greater than Ram himself.
ramacharitamanas::160.translation_literal: निरगुन (the formless) / तें (than) / एहि भाँति (in this way) / बड़ (greater) / नाम (the Name) / प्रभाउ (power) / अपार (boundless) / कहउँ (I say) / नामु (the Name) / बड़ (greater) / राम तें (than Ram) / निज (my own) / बिचार (understanding) / अनुसार (according to)
ramacharitamanas::160.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::160.essence: The Name can hold more power than the form it names.
ramacharitamanas::160.simple_meaning: The sacred Name has immense power, greater even than the formless absolute and, by the poet's view, greater than Ram's visible form.
ramacharitamanas::160.simple_insight: The heart can cling to a name when form feels distant, and that name can carry everything.
ramacharitamanas::160.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still building his case in Balkand: the formless supreme reality is beyond grasp, yet the Name is even more accessible and powerful. He now makes the bold devotional claim that Ram's Name surpasses Ram's visible form, setting up the next verse about effortless repetition by devotees.
ramacharitamanas::160.modern_relevance: When someone you love is far away, their name can steady you more than a photo or memory. You whisper it under stress, and the whisper itself becomes a lifeline.
ramacharitamanas::160.insight: It shifts devotion from needing a visible presence to trusting the living power of remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::161.verse_sanskrit: राम भगत हित नर तनु धारी। सहि संकट किए साधु सुखारी॥ नामु सप्रेम जपत अनयासा। भगत होहिं मुद मंगल बासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::161.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने भक्तों के हित के लिए मनुष्य शरीर धारण करके स्वयं कष्ट सहकर साधुओं को सुखी किया, परन्तु भक्तगण प्रेम के साथ नाम का जप करते हुए सहज ही में आनन्द और कल्याण के घर हो जाते हैं ॥।
ramacharitamanas::161.english_translation: Ram took a human body for the sake of devotees, endured hardship, and made the holy ones happy. But devotees, with loving repetition of the Name, reach joy and auspiciousness with ease.
ramacharitamanas::161.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / भगत (devotees) / हित (for the benefit) / नर तनु (human body) / धारी (having taken) / सहि (enduring) / संकट (hardships) / किए (made) / साधु (holy ones) / सुखारी (happy) / नामु (the Name) / सप्रेम (with love) / जपत (repeating) / अनयासा (easily) / भगत (devotees) / होहिं (become) / मुद (joy) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / बासा (dwelling)
ramacharitamanas::161.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::161.essence: Ram bears suffering for devotees; the Name gives them joy with ease.
ramacharitamanas::161.simple_meaning: Ram took human form to help devotees and bore suffering himself. But devotees who lovingly repeat the Name reach joy and blessing with ease.
ramacharitamanas::161.simple_insight: Love makes the hard path feel light, and the Name brings what struggle alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::161.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is comparing two ways Ram blesses the world: first, Ram himself comes in human form and endures pain to protect the good; then he says the devotee’s path is even gentler, because loving repetition of the Name itself becomes a home of joy and blessing.
ramacharitamanas::161.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for everyone else, carrying the weight yourself. Then one quiet practice—a name, a prayer, a remembered presence—makes the whole burden feel bearable.
ramacharitamanas::161.insight: It shifts devotion from effortful strain to loving repetition that changes the inner climate.

ramacharitamanas::162.verse_sanskrit: राम एक तापस तिय तारी। नाम कोटि खल कुमति सुधारी॥ रिषि हित राम सुकेतुसुता की। सहित सेन सुत कीन्हि बिबाकी ॥ सहित दोष दुख दास दुरासा। दलइ नामु जिमि रबि निसि नासा॥ भंजेउ राम आपु भव चापू। भव भय भंजन नाम प्रतापू ॥
ramacharitamanas::162.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने एक तपस्वी की स्त्री (अहिल्या) को ही तारा, परन्तु नाम ने करोड़ों दुष्टों की बिगड़ी बुद्धि को सुधार दिया। श्री रामजी ने ऋषि विश्वामिश्र के हित के लिए एक सुकेतु यक्ष की कन्या ताड़का की सेना और पुत्र (सुबाहु) सहित समाप्ति की, परन्तु नाम अपने भक्तों के दोष, दुःख और दुराशाओं का इस तरह नाश कर देता है जैसे सूर्य रात्रि का। श्री रामजी ने तो स्वयं शिवजी के धनुष को तोड़ा, परन्तु नाम का प्रताप ही संसार के सब भयों का नाश करने वाला है॥2-3॥
ramacharitamanas::162.english_translation: Ram saved a single ascetic's wife, but the name purified millions of crooked minds. Ram destroyed Tadka and Subahu for Vishvamitra's sake, but the name destroys a devotee's faults, sorrow, and cravings like the sun destroys night. Ram broke Shiva's bow, but the name's power removes all fear in the world.
ramacharitamanas::162.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / एक (one) / तापस (ascetic) / तिय (woman) / तारी (saved) । / नाम (name) / कोटि (crores) / खल (wicked) / कुमति (crooked understanding) / सुधारी (corrected) ॥ / रिषि (sage) / हित (for the sake of) / राम (Ram) / सुकेतुसुता (daughter of Suketu) / की (of) । / सहित (together with) / सेन (army) / सुत (son) / कीन्हि (did) / बिबाकी (destroyed) ॥ / सहित (along with) / दोष (faults) / दुख (sorrow) / दास (of devotee) / दुरासा (bad desires) । / दलइ (destroys) / नामु (name) / जिमि (like) / रबि (sun) / निसि (night) / नासा (destruction) ॥ / भंजेउ (broke) / राम (Ram) / आपु (himself) / भव (worldly existence) / चापू (bow) । / भव (worldly existence) / भय (fear) / भंजन (destroyer) / नाम (name) / प्रतापू (power) ॥
ramacharitamanas::162.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::162.essence: Ram's name does what even Ram's mighty deeds cannot reach.
ramacharitamanas::162.simple_meaning: Ram's deeds helped a few specific beings, but his name changes countless minds, removes sorrow, and destroys fear far more widely.
ramacharitamanas::162.simple_insight: You can feel the difference between one heroic act and a living presence that keeps working in people.
ramacharitamanas::162.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram's name against Ram's own great deeds. In the Balkand, Ram saves Ahalya, defeats Tadka and Subahu for Vishvamitra, and breaks Shiva's bow. Yet the poet says the name does even more: it cleanses minds, removes sorrow, and ends fear.
ramacharitamanas::162.modern_relevance: One brave act may help the person in front of you. But a word, a reminder, or a practice can keep working long after the moment has passed — in grief, in panic, in the mind at 2 a.m.
ramacharitamanas::162.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic deeds to the lasting power of remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::163.verse_sanskrit: दंडक बन प्रभु कीन्ह सुहावन। जन मन अमित नाम किए पावन॥ निसिचर निकर दले रघुनंदन। नामु सकल कलि कलुष निकंदन ॥
ramacharitamanas::163.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामजी ने (भयानक) दण्डक वन को सुहावना बनाया, परन्तु नाम ने असंख्य मनुष्यों के मनों को पवित्र कर दिया। श्री रघुनाथजी ने राक्षसों के समूह को मारा, परन्तु नाम तो कलियुग के सारे पापों की जड़ उखाड़ने वाला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::163.english_translation: Lord Ram made the Dandaka forest beautiful, but the name purified countless minds. Raghunandan slew the hosts of demons, but the name uproots all the sins of Kali Yuga.
ramacharitamanas::163.translation_literal: दंडक बन (Dandaka forest) / प्रभु (Lord) / कीन्ह (made) / सुहावन (beautiful) / जन मन (people's minds) / अमित (countless) / नाम (name) / किए (made) / पावन (pure) / निसिचर निकर (hosts of demons) / दले (slew) / रघुनंदन (Raghunandan) / नामु (name) / सकल (all) / कलि (of Kali Yuga) / कलुष (impurity) / निकंदन (uprooter)
ramacharitamanas::163.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::163.essence: Ram's name works where even Ram's deeds cannot reach.
ramacharitamanas::163.simple_meaning: Ram beautified the Dandaka forest and defeated the demons there, but his name cleanses far more deeply by purifying countless minds and destroying the root of corruption in the age of Kali.
ramacharitamanas::163.simple_insight: What Ram does in one place, his name can do everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::163.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram's presence in the Dandaka forest, where Ram made the wild place lovely and destroyed the demons. But he turns the teaching higher: Ram's name reaches farther than his physical deeds, purifying countless hearts and cutting through the darkness of the age.
ramacharitamanas::163.modern_relevance: A place can feel changed after you leave it, but a name, a memory, or a prayer can keep working long after the moment is gone. Some help is local; some keeps cleansing from within.
ramacharitamanas::163.insight: It shifts attention from visible heroic action to the inward power of remembrance and devotion.

ramacharitamanas::164.verse_sanskrit: सबरी गीध सुसेवकनि सुगति दीन्हि रघुनाथ। नाम उधारे अमित खल बेद बिदित गुन गाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::164.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी ने तो शबरी, जटायु आदि उत्तम सेवकों को ही मुक्ति दी, परन्तु नाम ने अगनित दुष्टों का उद्धार किया। नाम के गुणों की कथा वेदों में प्रसिद्ध है ॥
ramacharitamanas::164.english_translation: Raghunath gave liberation to devoted servants like Sabari and Jatayu, but the Name delivered countless wrongdoers. The glory of the Name is famed in the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::164.translation_literal: सबरी (Sabari) / गीध (vulture; Jatayu) / सुसेवकनि (excellent servants) / सुगति (good destiny; liberation) / दीन्हि (gave) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath; Ram) / नाम (the Name) / उधारे (rescued) / अमित (countless) / खल (wrongdoers) / बेद (Vedas) / बिदित (known) / गुन (qualities) / गाथ (song; praise)
ramacharitamanas::164.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::164.essence: The Name saves even those no one else would count as worthy.
ramacharitamanas::164.simple_meaning: Ram gives liberation to faithful servants like Sabari and Jatayu, but his Name saves countless fallen people. Even the Vedas praise that power.
ramacharitamanas::164.simple_insight: The Name reaches people who feel beyond saving. That is what makes devotion so wide and merciful.
ramacharitamanas::164.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is widening the claim after praising Ram's grace in the forest. Sabari and Jatayu received Ram's direct blessing, but the verse says the Name goes even further, lifting countless fallen people. The point is the Name's reach is larger than any single encounter.
ramacharitamanas::164.modern_relevance: Someone who feels too ashamed to walk into a temple, too messy to ask for help, too late to begin again — this verse says the Name still meets them there.
ramacharitamanas::164.insight: It shifts devotion from privilege to accessibility, showing that the Name can redeem anyone, not only the already pure.

ramacharitamanas::165.verse_sanskrit: राम सुकंठ बिभीषन दोऊ। राखे सरन जान सबु कोऊ ॥ नाम गरीब अनेक नेवाजे। लोक बेद बर बिरिद बिराजे ॥
ramacharitamanas::165.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने सुग्रीव और विभीषण दोनों को ही अपनी शरण में रखा, यह सब कोई जानते हैं, परन्तु नाम ने अनेक गरीबों पर कृपा की है। नाम का यह सुंदर विरद लोक और वेद में विशेष रूप से प्रकाशित है ॥
ramacharitamanas::165.english_translation: Ram took both Sugriva and Vibhishana into his refuge; everyone knows that. But the Name has blessed many poor people. This beautiful glory shines in both worldly tradition and scripture.
ramacharitamanas::165.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सुकंठ (Sugriva) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / दोऊ (both) / राखे (kept) / सरन (in refuge) / जान (knows) / सबु (everyone) / कोऊ (someone) ॥ नाम (Name) / गरीब (poor) / अनेक (many) / नेवाजे (blessed) / लोक (worldly tradition) / बेद (scripture) / बर (excellent) / बिरिद (glory) / बिराजे (shines) ॥
ramacharitamanas::165.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::165.essence: Ram shelters the famous; the Name lifts the overlooked.
ramacharitamanas::165.simple_meaning: Ram protects Sugriva and Vibhishana, which everyone already knows. The Name, however, has blessed countless humble people, and that fame is praised everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::165.simple_insight: You do not need status to be held by the divine Name.
ramacharitamanas::165.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram's refuge in a broader devotional argument. After naming famous examples like Sugriva and Vibhishana, he turns to the Name itself and says its mercy reaches far beyond the famous, lifting ordinary and overlooked people too.
ramacharitamanas::165.modern_relevance: You feel unseen after helping everyone else, and then one quiet practice still steadies you. No audience is needed for what truly holds you up.
ramacharitamanas::165.insight: It shifts devotion from exceptional cases to universal access: the Name is available to the lowly, not only the celebrated.

ramacharitamanas::166.verse_sanskrit: राम भालु कपि कटुक बटोरा। सेतु हेतु श्रमु कीन्ह न थोरा॥ नामु लेत भवसिन्धु सुखाहीं। करहु बिचारु सुजन मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::166.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने तो भालू और बंदरों की सेना बटोरी और समुद्र पर पुल बाँधने के लिए थोड़ा परिश्रम नहीं किया, परन्तु नाम लेते ही संसार समुद्र सूख जाता है। सज्जनगण! मन में विचार कीजिए (कि दोनों में कौन बड़ा है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::166.english_translation: Ram gathered the bears and monkeys and did not spare himself in building the bridge. But by taking the Name, the ocean of becoming dries up. Good people, reflect on this in your own mind.
ramacharitamanas::166.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / भालु (bears) / कपि (monkeys) / कटुक (severe) / बटोरा (gathered) / सेतु (bridge) / हेतु (for the sake of) / श्रमु (effort) / कीन्ह (did) / न (not) / थोरा (little) / नामु (Name) / लेत (taking) / भवसिन्धु (ocean of becoming) / सुखाहीं (dries up) / करहु (do) / बिचारु (reflection) / सुजन (good people) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::166.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::166.essence: The Name can dissolve what even great effort must cross.
ramacharitamanas::166.simple_meaning: Ram did the hard work of gathering the monkey and bear army and building the bridge. Yet even the ocean of suffering dries up when the Name is taken.
ramacharitamanas::166.simple_insight: The heart can rest: effort matters, but remembrance can carry what effort cannot.
ramacharitamanas::166.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas turns from the battlefield story to a devotional comparison. Ram mobilizes the bear and monkey forces and labours to build the bridge to Lanka, yet the poet says the Name itself dries up the ocean of becoming. The verse asks listeners to weigh action against remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::166.modern_relevance: You spent weeks fixing what looked impossible, then one quiet moment of remembrance steadied everything. After all the pushing, you realize some burdens loosen not by force, but by calling the Name.
ramacharitamanas::166.insight: It shifts attention from heroic effort alone to the transforming power of remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::167.verse_sanskrit: राम सकुल रन रावनु मारा। सीय सहित निज पुर पगु धारा॥ राजा रामु अवध रजधानी। गावत गुन सुर मुनि बर बानी ॥ सेवक सुमिरत नामु सप्रीती। बिनु श्रम प्रबल मोह दलु जीती॥ फिरत सनेहँ मगन सुख अपनें। नाम प्रसाद सोच नहिं सपनें ॥
ramacharitamanas::167.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने कुटुम्ब सहित रावण को युद्ध में मारा, तब सीता सहित उन्होंने अपने नगर (अयोध्या) में प्रवेश किया। राम राजा हुए, अवध उनकी राजधानी हुई, देवता और मुनि सुंदर वाणी से जिनके गुण गाते हैं, परन्तु सेवक (भक्त) प्रेमपूर्वक नाम के स्मरण मात्र से बिना परिश्रम मोह की प्रबल सेना को जीतकर प्रेम में मग्न हुए अपने ही सुख में विचरते हैं, नाम के प्रसाद से उन्हें सपने में भी कोई चिन्ता नहीं सताती॥3-4॥
ramacharitamanas::167.english_translation: Ram killed Ravana in battle, along with his whole clan, and then entered his city with Sita. Ram became king; Ayodhya became his capital. Devas and sages sing his qualities in beautiful speech. But servants, remembering his name with love, conquer the great army of delusion without effort. Lost in love, they wander in their own bliss; by the grace of the name, worry never reaches them, even in dreams.
ramacharitamanas::167.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सकुल (with his whole clan) / रन (in battle) / रावनु (Ravana) / मारा (killed) / सीय सहित (along with Sita) / निज पुर (his own city) / पगु धारा (placed his feet; entered) / राजा (king) / रामु (Ram) / अवध (Ayodhya) / रजधानी (capital city) / गावत (singing) / गुन (qualities) / सुर (devas) / मुनि (sages) / बर (excellent) / बानी (speech) / सेवक (servants/devotees) / सुमिरत (remembering) / नामु (the name) / सप्रीती (with love) / बिनु (without) / श्रम (effort) / प्रबल (powerful) / मोह (delusion) / दलु (army) / जीती (conquered) / फिरत (wandering) / सनेहँ (in love) / मगन (immersed) / सुख अपनें (in their own bliss) / नाम (name) / प्रसाद (grace) / सोच (worry) / नहिं (not) / सपनें (even in dreams)
ramacharitamanas::167.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::167.essence: Ram's name defeats delusion more easily than struggle does.
ramacharitamanas::167.simple_meaning: Ram defeats Ravana, returns to Ayodhya, and becomes king. His devotees, remembering his name with love, overcome delusion effortlessly and live free of worry.
ramacharitamanas::167.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that love and remembrance can do what strain cannot.
ramacharitamanas::167.detailed_meaning: Ravana is dead, Sita is safe, and Ram enters Ayodhya as king. The scene widens from victory to glory: devas and sages praise him, yet Tulsidas turns to the deeper miracle — devotees who remember Ram's name conquer delusion without struggle.
ramacharitamanas::167.modern_relevance: You finish a brutal project, the crisis is over, and everyone wants the victory story. But the real change is quieter: something in you has loosened, and the old panic no longer runs the room.
ramacharitamanas::167.insight: It shifts attention from outer achievement to the inner freedom created by loving remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::168.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्म राम तें नामु बड़ बर दायक बर दानि। रामचरित सत कोटि महँ लिय महेस जियँ जानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::168.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार नाम (निर्गुण) ब्रह्म और (सगुण) राम दोनों से बड़ा है। यह वरदान देने वालों को भी वर देने वाला है। श्री शिवजी ने अपने हृदय में यह जानकर ही सौ करोड़ राम चरित्र में से इस 'राम' नाम को (साररूप से चुनकर) ग्रहण किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::168.english_translation: The name of Ram is greater than Ram and greater than the supreme reality. It is the giver of boons to all boon-givers. Shiva knows this in his heart and has chosen this name from hundreds of millions of Ram's stories.
ramacharitamanas::168.translation_literal: ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / राम (Ram) / तें (than) / नामु (the name) / बड़ (greater) / बर दायक (boon-giving) / बर दानि (boon-giver) / रामचरित (Ram's stories) / सत कोटि (hundreds of millions) / महँ (among) / लिय (taken) / महेस (Shiva) / जियँ (in heart) / जानि (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::168.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::168.essence: The name holds more power than the whole story.
ramacharitamanas::168.simple_meaning: Ram's name is more powerful than even Ram's own stories and greater than the supreme reality in its accessible form. Shiva keeps that name in his heart because it gives the highest blessing.
ramacharitamanas::168.simple_insight: The heart can rest in a single sacred name instead of chasing endless explanations.
ramacharitamanas::168.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses in the middle of praising Ram's glory to make a bold claim: the name of Ram is even more powerful than the vast story of Ram himself. Shiva, who knows every one of those stories, has chosen the name as their essence.
ramacharitamanas::168.modern_relevance: You are exhausted after reading, listening, and analyzing everything, but one phrase still steadies you. When life is too much to hold in thought, a single name or mantra can become the place your mind comes home.
ramacharitamanas::168.insight: It shifts devotion from information to repetition, from understanding every detail to resting in the living name.

ramacharitamanas::169.verse_sanskrit: नाम प्रसाद संभु अबिनासी। साजु अमंगल मंगल रासी॥ सुक सनकादि सिद्ध मुनि जोगी। नाम प्रसाद ब्रह्मसुख भोगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::169.verse_hindi: नाम ही के प्रसाद से शिवजी अविनाशी हैं और अमंगल वेष वाले होने पर भी मंगल की राशि हैं। शुकदेवजी और सनकादि सिद्ध, मुनि, योगी गण नाम के ही प्रसाद से ब्रह्मानन्द को भोगते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::169.english_translation: By the grace of the Name, Shiva is imperishable and, though marked by inauspicious signs, is a treasury of auspiciousness. By the grace of the Name, Sukadeva, the Sanakadi sages, the perfected ones, and the yogis taste the bliss of the supreme reality.
ramacharitamanas::169.translation_literal: नाम (the Name) / प्रसाद (by grace) / संभु (Shiva) / अबिनासी (imperishable) / साजु (adorned) / अमंगल (inauspicious) / मंगल (auspicious) / रासी (heap/treasury) / सुक (Sukadeva) / सनकादि (Sanaka and others) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / मुनि (sages) / जोगी (yogis) / नाम प्रसाद (by the grace of the Name) / ब्रह्मसुख (bliss of the supreme reality) / भोगी (one who tastes/enjoys)
ramacharitamanas::169.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::169.essence: The Name does what power and purity alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::169.simple_meaning: The divine Name is so powerful that it sustains Shiva and lets great sages and yogis taste supreme bliss.
ramacharitamanas::169.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that spiritual greatness is not forced by effort alone; grace is what makes it possible.
ramacharitamanas::169.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is building a case for the power of Ram's Name. After saying the Name is greater than both the formless absolute and Ram's own form, he shows its reach: it sustains Shiva and lets saints like Sukadeva and the Sanakadi sages taste supreme bliss.
ramacharitamanas::169.modern_relevance: You are exhausted after trying to hold everything together by willpower alone. Then one steady practice, one sacred repetition, one remembered name settles you more deeply than control ever could.
ramacharitamanas::169.insight: It shifts attention from personal effort alone to the transforming power of remembrance and grace.

ramacharitamanas::170.verse_sanskrit: नारद जानेउ नाम प्रतापू। जग प्रिय हरि हरि हर प्रिय आपू॥ नामु जपत प्रभु कीन्ह प्रसादू। भगत सिरोमनि भे प्रहलादू ॥
ramacharitamanas::170.verse_hindi: नारदजी ने नाम के प्रताप को जाना है। हरि सारे संसार को प्यारे हैं, (हरि को हर प्यारे हैं) और आप (श्री नारदजी) हरि और हर दोनों को प्रिय हैं। नाम के जपने से प्रभु ने कृपा की, जिससे प्रह्लाद, भक्त शिरोमणि हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::170.english_translation: Narada knew the power of the Name. Hari is dear to the whole world, and the whole world is dear to Hari. By chanting the Name, the Lord showed grace, and Prahlada became the foremost devotee.
ramacharitamanas::170.translation_literal: नारद (Narada) / जानेउ (knew) / नाम प्रतापू (the power of the Name) / जग (world) / प्रिय (dear) / हरि (Hari) / हरि (Hari) / हर प्रिय (dear to Hari) / आपू (self) / नामु (the Name) / जपत (chanting) / प्रभु (the Lord) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रसादू (grace) / भगत सिरोमनि (foremost devotee) / भे (became) / प्रहलादू (Prahlada)
ramacharitamanas::170.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::170.essence: The Name itself can turn a seeker into a beloved devotee.
ramacharitamanas::170.simple_meaning: Narada understood the power of Ram's name. The whole world is dear to Ram, and Ram is dear to the whole world. Chanting that name made Prahlada a great devotee.
ramacharitamanas::170.simple_insight: Devotion is not earned by status; it deepens through sincere repetition of the divine name.
ramacharitamanas::170.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses the larger devotional argument to show famous examples. Narada understands the power of the Name, and Prahlada becomes the model devotee through chanting. The point is simple: the Name itself carries grace.
ramacharitamanas::170.modern_relevance: You are muttering a prayer while sitting in a hospital corridor, too tired to explain your fear. The words feel small, but the verse says they are not small at all.
ramacharitamanas::170.insight: It shifts attention from personal effort alone to the transforming power of repeated remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::171.verse_sanskrit: ध्रुवँ सगलानि जपेउ हरि नाऊँ। पायउ अचल अनूपम ठाऊँ॥ सुमिरि पवनसुत पावन नामू। अपने बस करि राखे रामू ॥
ramacharitamanas::171.verse_hindi: ध्रुवजी ने ग्लानि से (विमाता के वचनों से दुःखी होकर सकाम भाव से) हरि नाम को जपा और उसके प्रताप से अचल अनुपम स्थान (ध्रुवलोक) प्राप्त किया। हनुमान् जी ने पवित्र नाम का स्मरण करके श्री रामजी को अपने वश में कर रखा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::171.english_translation: Dhruva chanted Hari's name in sorrow and gained an unshakable, incomparable place. Hanuman remembered the pure name and kept Ram under his sway.
ramacharitamanas::171.translation_literal: ध्रुवँ (Dhruva) / सगलानि (in sorrow) / जपेउ (chanted) / हरि (Hari) / नाऊँ (name) / पायउ (obtained) / अचल (unshakable) / अनूपम (incomparable) / ठाऊँ (place) ॥ / सुमिरि (remembering) / पवनसुत (son of the wind) / पावन (pure) / नामू (name) / अपने (his own) / बस (control) / करि (having made) / राखे (kept) / रामू (Ram) ॥
ramacharitamanas::171.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::171.essence: Constant remembrance turns sorrow into nearness to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::171.simple_meaning: Dhruva gained an unshakable place by repeating Ram's name in pain. Hanuman held Ram close through constant remembrance of the pure name.
ramacharitamanas::171.simple_insight: Devotion does not beg for power; it quietly receives what it keeps remembering.
ramacharitamanas::171.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is building a chain of examples for the power of Ram's name. Dhruva, hurt by rejection, turns to Hari and gains a place no one can shake. Hanuman then shows the highest form of that same remembrance: love so complete that Ram is held close in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::171.modern_relevance: You are sitting alone after a brutal message, replaying the words again and again. The mind can keep circling pain — or keep circling the name that steadies it.
ramacharitamanas::171.insight: It shifts attention from injury and loss toward a remembrance that steadies the whole heart.

ramacharitamanas::172.verse_sanskrit: अपतु अजामिलु गजु गनिकाऊ। भए मुकुत हरि नाम प्रभाऊ॥ कहौं कहाँ लगि नाम बड़ाई। रामु न सकहिं नाम गुन गाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::172.verse_hindi: नीच अजामिल, गज और गणिका (वेश्या) भी श्री हरि के नाम के प्रभाव से मुक्त हो गए। मैं नाम की बड़ाई कहाँ तक कहूँ, राम भी नाम के गुणों को नहीं गा सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::172.english_translation: A fallen man like Ajamil, an elephant, and a courtesan all found freedom through the power of Ram's name. How far can I praise the name's greatness? Even Ram cannot sing the name's qualities.
ramacharitamanas::172.translation_literal: अपतु (fallen / lowly) / अजामिलु (Ajamil) / गजु (elephant) / गनिकाऊ (courtesan) / भए (became) / मुकुत (free) / हरि (Ram) / नाम (name) / प्रभाऊ (power) / कहौं (I say) / कहाँ लगि (how far) / नाम (name) / बड़ाई (greatness) / रामु (Ram) / न सकहिं (cannot) / नाम (name) / गुन (qualities) / गाई (sing)
ramacharitamanas::172.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::172.essence: Ram's name rescues the unworthy and exceeds every attempt to praise it.
ramacharitamanas::172.simple_meaning: Ram's name can free even people seen as low or broken. Its greatness is beyond measure, so vast that even Ram cannot fully describe it.
ramacharitamanas::172.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that no life is too stained for grace to reach.
ramacharitamanas::172.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is listing famous examples of unlikely rescue: Ajamil, the elephant, and the courtesan all found release through Ram's name. The point is not their merit but the name's power, which exceeds even Ram's own praise.
ramacharitamanas::172.modern_relevance: A person with a ruined reputation walks into a temple after years away, ashamed to even look up. This verse says the door is still open, and the name is stronger than the shame.
ramacharitamanas::172.insight: It shifts attention from personal worthiness to the transforming power of remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::173.verse_sanskrit: नामु राम को कलपतरु कलि कल्यान निवासु। जो सुमिरत भयो भाँग तें तुलसी तुलसीदासु ॥
ramacharitamanas::173.verse_hindi: कलियुग में राम का नाम कल्पतरु (मन चाहा पदार्थ देने वाला) और कल्याण का निवास (मुक्ति का घर) है, जिसको स्मरण करने से भाँग सा (निकृष्ट) तुलसीदास तुलसी के समान (पवित्र) हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::173.english_translation: Ram's name is a wish-fulfilling tree in Kali Yuga, a home of well-being. By remembering it, Tulsidas, once base as bhang, became pure as tulsi.
ramacharitamanas::173.translation_literal: नामु (name) / राम (Ram) / को (of) / कलपतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / कलि (Kali Yuga) / कल्यान (well-being) / निवासु (abode) / जो (which) / सुमिरत (remembering) / भयो (became) / भाँग (bhang; base intoxicant) / तें (from) / तुलसी (tulsi) / तुलसीदासु (Tulsidas)
ramacharitamanas::173.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::173.essence: Ram's name can purify even what seems beyond repair.
ramacharitamanas::173.simple_meaning: Ram's name is described as the source of all good in this age. Remembering it transformed Tulsidas from base and fallen to pure and blessed.
ramacharitamanas::173.simple_insight: You are not fixed by where you start. Remembrance can remake you.
ramacharitamanas::173.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses in the Balkand to praise Ram's name after showing its power on figures like Dhruva, Ajamila, and the elephant king. He turns the praise inward: the same name that lifted them also changed him, making the impure fit for devotion.
ramacharitamanas::173.modern_relevance: You catch yourself feeling unworthy after a mistake, then keep returning to the same prayer, mantra, or quiet remembrance. Slowly, the shame loosens. What seemed small starts remaking you.
ramacharitamanas::173.insight: It shifts attention from self-judgment to the transforming power of repeated remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::174.verse_sanskrit: चहुँ जुग तीनि काल तिहुँ लोका। भए नाम जपि जीव बिसोका॥ बेद पुरान संत मत एहू। सकल सुकृत फल राम सनेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::174.verse_hindi: (केवल कलियुग की ही बात नहीं है,) चारों युगों में, तीनों काल में और तीनों लोकों में नाम को जपकर जीव शोकरहित हुए हैं। वेद, पुराण और संतों का मत यही है कि समस्त पुण्यों का फल श्री रामजी में (या राम नाम में) प्रेम होना है ॥
ramacharitamanas::174.english_translation: In all four ages, all three times, and all three worlds, beings become free from sorrow by repeating the Name. The Vedas, Puranas, and saints all agree: the fruit of all merit is love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::174.translation_literal: चहुँ (four) / जुग (ages) / तीनि (three) / काल (times) / तिहुँ (three) / लोका (worlds) / भए (became) / नाम (Name) / जपि (reciting) / जीव (beings) / बिसोका (free from sorrow) / बेद (Vedas) / पुरान (Puranas) / संत (saints) / मत (view) / एहू (this) / सकल (all) / सुकृत (merit) / फल (fruit) / राम (Ram) / सनेहू (love)
ramacharitamanas::174.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::174.essence: Ram's Name frees sorrow, and love for Ram is the highest fruit.
ramacharitamanas::174.simple_meaning: Across every age and realm, repeating Ram's name frees beings from sorrow. All scripture and saints agree that the highest result of good deeds is love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::174.simple_insight: You do not have to carry sorrow alone; devotion can soften what effort cannot.
ramacharitamanas::174.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still praising Ram's name after citing examples like Ajamila, the elephant, and the courtesan. He broadens the claim: this works in every age, every time, and every world. The point is no longer one rescue story, but a universal law of devotion.
ramacharitamanas::174.modern_relevance: You are sitting in a quiet room after a hard day, replaying one mistake for the tenth time. The mind keeps circling, but a single steady remembrance can loosen the knot faster than endless self-blame.
ramacharitamanas::174.insight: It shifts attention from self-criticism to repeated remembrance, treating devotion as a practical cure for mental heaviness.

ramacharitamanas::175.verse_sanskrit: ध्यानु प्रथम जुग मख बिधि दूजें। द्वापर परितोषत प्रभु पूजें॥ कलि केवल मल मूल मलीना। पाप पयोनिधि जन मन मीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::175.verse_hindi: पहले (सत्य) युग में ध्यान से, दूसरे (त्रेता) युग में यज्ञ से और द्वापर में पूजन से भगवान प्रसन्न होते हैं, परन्तु कलियुग केवल पाप की जड़ और मलिन है, इसमें मनुष्यों का मन पाप रूपी समुद्र में मछली बना हुआ है (अर्थात पाप से कभी अलग होना ही नहीं चाहता, इससे ध्यान, यज्ञ और पूजन नहीं बन सकते) ॥
ramacharitamanas::175.english_translation: In the first age, meditation pleases the divine; in the second, sacrifice; in the third, worship. But in Kali Yuga alone, impurity is rooted deep, and the human mind is like a fish in the ocean of wrongdoing.
ramacharitamanas::175.translation_literal: ध्यानु (meditation) / प्रथम (first) / जुग (age) / मख (sacrifice) / बिधि (by method) / दूजें (second) / द्वापर (Dvapara) / परितोषत (is pleased) / प्रभु (the lord) / पूजें (by worship) / कलि (Kali Yuga) / केवल (only) / मल (impurity) / मूल (root) / मलीना (stained) / पाप (wrongdoing) / पयोनिधि (ocean) / जन (people's) / मन (mind) / मीना (fish)
ramacharitamanas::175.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::175.essence: The age changes; the practice must change with it.
ramacharitamanas::175.simple_meaning: Different ages call for different spiritual practices. In Kali Yuga, human minds are so pulled toward wrongdoing that ordinary rituals cannot easily cleanse them.
ramacharitamanas::175.simple_insight: It can feel sobering, but also clarifying: not every age asks the same practice of us.
ramacharitamanas::175.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is explaining why the age of Kali is spiritually difficult. In earlier ages, meditation, sacrifice, and worship fit human capacity more naturally. Now the mind is restless and drawn toward impurity, so the next verse turns toward Ram's name as the remedy.
ramacharitamanas::175.modern_relevance: You open your phone at midnight and fall into one more loop of outrage, scrolling, and craving. The problem is not just bad content; the mind itself keeps swimming toward it.
ramacharitamanas::175.insight: It shifts attention from ideal rituals to the actual condition of the mind, so the remedy matches the age.

ramacharitamanas::176.verse_sanskrit: नाम कामतरु काल कराला। सुमिरत समन सकल जग जाला॥ राम नाम कलि अभिमत दाता। हित परलोक लोक पितु माता ॥
ramacharitamanas::176.verse_hindi: ऐसे कराल (कलियुग के) काल में तो नाम ही कल्पवृक्ष है, जो स्मरण करते ही संसार के सब जंजालों को नाश कर देने वाला है। कलियुग में यह राम नाम मनोवांछित फल देने वाला है, परलोक का परम हितैषी और इस लोक का माता-पिता है (अर्थात परलोक में भगवान का परमधाम देता है और इस लोक में माता-पिता के समान सब प्रकार से पालन और रक्षण करता है।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::176.english_translation: In this fierce age, the Name is the wish-fulfilling tree. Remembering it destroys all worldly tangles. In Kali Yuga, Ram's Name gives the desired fruit, and it is the best friend of the next world and the mother and father of this world.
ramacharitamanas::176.translation_literal: नाम (Name) / कामतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / काल (time, age) / कराला (fierce, dreadful) / सुमिरत (remembering) / समन (destroyer) / सकल (all) / जग (world) / जाला (entanglements, web) ॥ राम (Ram) / नाम (Name) / कलि (in Kali Yuga) / अभिमत (desired, wished-for) / दाता (giver) / हित (benefit) / परलोक (next world) / लोक (this world) / पितु (father) / माता (mother) ॥
ramacharitamanas::176.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::176.essence: Ram's Name is the one support that feeds both this life and the next.
ramacharitamanas::176.simple_meaning: Ram's Name is the great support in this difficult age. Remembering it clears confusion, gives what is needed, and protects both this life and the next.
ramacharitamanas::176.simple_insight: You don't need more complexity to feel held. One steady remembrance can simplify everything.
ramacharitamanas::176.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is speaking in the Balkand after describing how different ages have different spiritual supports. He now says that in Kali Yuga, Ram's Name itself is the wish-fulfilling tree: it removes life's entanglements, gives what is truly needed, and becomes the safest refuge for both present life and what follows it.
ramacharitamanas::176.modern_relevance: You are staring at three unpaid bills, a buzzing phone, and a mind that won't stop spinning. One calm remembrance can cut through the noise faster than another plan.
ramacharitamanas::176.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing many remedies to relying on one steady refuge.

ramacharitamanas::177.verse_sanskrit: नहिं कलि करम न भगति बिबेकू। राम नाम अवलंबन एकू॥ कालनेमि कलि कपट निधानू। नाम सुमति समरथ हनुमानू ॥
ramacharitamanas::177.verse_hindi: कलियुग में न कर्म है, न भक्ति है और न ज्ञान ही है, राम नाम ही एक आधार है। कपट की खान कलियुग रूपी कालनेमि के (मारने के) लिए राम नाम ही बुद्धिमान और समर्थ श्री हनुमान् जी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::177.english_translation: In Kali Yuga, there is no action, no devotion, and no discernment; Ram's name alone is the one support. For the deceitful Kali, Ram's name is the wise and capable Hanuman.
ramacharitamanas::177.translation_literal: नहिं (not) / कलि (in Kali Yuga) / करम (action) / न (not) / भगति (devotion) / बिबेकू (discernment) / राम नाम (Ram's name) / अवलंबन (support) / एकू (only one) / कालनेमि (Kalnemi) / कलि (Kali) / कपट (deceit) / निधानू (treasure) / नाम (name) / सुमति (wise mind) / समरथ (capable) / हनुमानू (Hanuman)
ramacharitamanas::177.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::177.essence: Ram's name remains when every other support fails.
ramacharitamanas::177.simple_meaning: In this age, action, devotion, and discernment all feel weakened. Ram's name becomes the one reliable support, strong enough to face deceit and confusion.
ramacharitamanas::177.simple_insight: You do not need perfect strength to begin; one true name can steady a fractured mind.
ramacharitamanas::177.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, Tulsidas has just said that in Kali Yuga only Ram's name remains powerful. He now sharpens that claim: ordinary action, devotion, and discernment are all too weak on their own, so Ram's name becomes the one refuge, like Hanuman against deception.
ramacharitamanas::177.modern_relevance: You are exhausted, scrolling past bad news at midnight, too tired to meditate, too scattered to think clearly, too drained to do much of anything. Even then, one short prayer can hold you together.
ramacharitamanas::177.insight: It shifts the mind from relying on personal capacity to relying on a sacred anchor.

ramacharitamanas::178.verse_sanskrit: राम नाम नरकेसरी कनककसिपु कलिकाल। जापक जन प्रहलाद जिमि पालिहि दलि सुरसाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::178.verse_hindi: राम नाम श्री नृसिंह भगवान है, कलियुग हिरण्यकशिपु है और जप करने वाले जन प्रह्लाद के समान हैं, यह राम नाम देवताओं के शत्रु (कलियुग रूपी दैत्य) को मारकर जप करने वालों की रक्षा करेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::178.english_translation: The name of Ram is the lion-man, Kalikal is Hiranyakashipu. The one who chants, like Prahlad, will be protected as the divine destroys the wicked force.
ramacharitamanas::178.translation_literal: राम नाम (the name of Ram) / नरकेसरी (lion-man) / कनककसिपु (Hiranyakashipu) / कलिकाल (the age of Kali) / जापक जन (chanting people) / प्रहलाद जिमि (like Prahlad) / पालिहि (will protect) / दलि (crushing) / सुरसाल (the enemy of the radiant beings)
ramacharitamanas::178.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::178.essence: Ram's name protects the devotee by destroying the force that threatens them.
ramacharitamanas::178.simple_meaning: Ram's name is compared to a lion-man who destroys the dark force of this age. Anyone who repeats it is protected like Prahlad.
ramacharitamanas::178.simple_insight: There is courage in repeating Ram's name until fear loses its grip.
ramacharitamanas::178.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is building a chain of praise for Ram's name in Balkand. After calling it the only support in Kali age, he says that chanting it is like Prahlad's devotion before Hiranyakashipu: the name itself becomes protection and destroys what threatens the devotee.
ramacharitamanas::178.modern_relevance: You are sitting in a hospital waiting room, trying not to panic while a loved one is inside. Repeating one sacred name can steady the heart the way Prahlad stood steady before danger.
ramacharitamanas::178.insight: It shifts devotion from ornament to shelter: repetition becomes active protection against fear and disorder.

ramacharitamanas::179.verse_sanskrit: भायँ कुभायँ अनख आलस हूँ। नाम जपत मंगल दिसि दसहूँ॥ सुमिरि सो नाम राम गुन गाथा। करउँ नाइ रघुनाथहि माथा ॥॥
ramacharitamanas::179.verse_hindi: अच्छे भाव (प्रेम) से, बुरे भाव (बैर) से, क्रोध से या आलस्य से, किसी तरह से भी नाम जपने से दसों दिशाओं में कल्याण होता है। उसी (परम कल्याणकारी) राम नाम का स्मरण करके और श्री रघुनाथजी को मस्तक नवाकर मैं रामजी के गुणों का वर्णन करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::179.english_translation: Whether with good feeling or bad, with anger or laziness, chanting the Name brings blessing in all ten directions. Remembering that Name, Ram's qualities, and bowing to Raghunath, I now sing Ram's glory.
ramacharitamanas::179.translation_literal: भायँ (with feeling) / कुभायँ (with bad feeling) / अनख (anger) / आलस (laziness) / हूँ (even) / नाम (Name) / जपत (chanting) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / दिसि दसहूँ (all ten directions) ॥ / सुमिरि (remembering) / सो (that) / नाम (Name) / राम (Ram) / गुन (qualities) / गाथा (song, narration) / अथा (I begin) / करउँ (I do) / नाइ (bowing) / रघुनाथहि (to Raghunath) / माथा (head) ॥॥
ramacharitamanas::179.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::179.essence: The Name works even before your heart is pure.
ramacharitamanas::179.simple_meaning: Ram's name brings blessing even when the mind is not pure. Tulsidas says he remembers that name, bows to Ram, and then begins singing Ram's qualities.
ramacharitamanas::179.simple_insight: You do not need perfect feelings to begin. Reverence can start before clarity does.
ramacharitamanas::179.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is turning from doctrine to praise. After declaring that Ram's name alone is the support in this age, he says that even mixed, angry, or lazy chanting still brings blessing. Then he bows to Ram and begins his hymn.
ramacharitamanas::179.modern_relevance: You're half-distracted, tired, and not feeling especially sincere, yet you still open the prayer app or whisper the mantra before sleep. This verse says that imperfect starting still matters.
