ramacharitamanas::179.insight: It shifts practice from waiting for the right mood to beginning anyway, trusting the Name itself.

ramacharitamanas::180.verse_sanskrit: मोरि सुधारिहि सो सब भाँती। जासु कृपा नहिं कृपाँ अघाती॥ राम सुस्वामि कुसेवकु मोसो। निज दिसि देखि दयानिधि पोसो ॥
ramacharitamanas::180.verse_hindi: वे (श्री रामजी) मेरी (बिगड़ी) सब तरह से सुधार लेंगे, जिनकी कृपा कृपा करने से नहीं अघाती। राम से उत्तम स्वामी और मुझ सरीखा बुरा सेवक! इतने पर भी उन दयानिधि ने अपनी ओर देखकर मेरा पालन किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::180.english_translation: He will set everything right in every way. His grace never tires of giving grace. Ram is the best master, and I am a poor servant; even so, that ocean of compassion has looked toward me and sustained me.
ramacharitamanas::180.translation_literal: मोरि (my) / सुधारिहि (will सुधारना; set right) / सो (that one) / सब (all) / भाँती (ways) / जासु (whose) / कृपा (grace) / नहिं (not) / कृपाँ (in grace-giving) / अघाती (tired, exhausted) / राम (Ram) / सुस्वामि (excellent master) / कुसेवकु (bad servant) / मोसो (like me) / निज (own) / दिसि (toward) / देखि (seeing) / दयानिधि (ocean of compassion) / पोसो (sustained, nourished)
ramacharitamanas::180.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::180.essence: Ram's grace keeps working even on an unworthy servant.
ramacharitamanas::180.simple_meaning: Ram will put everything right. His compassion does not get exhausted, even when the devotee is flawed and unworthy.
ramacharitamanas::180.simple_insight: You can stop fearing your own mess when you trust a grace that does not wear out.
ramacharitamanas::180.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is speaking as a humble devotee, looking at his own faults and still trusting Ram completely. The verse turns personal weakness into the proof of Ram's kindness: the worse the servant, the more astonishing the master's care.
ramacharitamanas::180.modern_relevance: You reread the apology draft for the tenth time, convinced you've ruined everything. Then one kind reply arrives and you remember: a real bond is not cancelled by your clumsiness.
ramacharitamanas::180.insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to trust in a compassion that keeps working on you.

ramacharitamanas::181.verse_sanskrit: लोकहुँ बेद सुसाहिब रीती। बिनय सुनत पहिचानत प्रीती॥ गनी गरीब ग्राम नर नागर। पंडित मूढ़ मलीन उजागर ॥
ramacharitamanas::181.verse_hindi: लोक और वेद में भी अच्छे स्वामी की यही रीति प्रसिद्ध है कि वह विनय सुनते ही प्रेम को पहचान लेता है। अमीर-गरीब, गँवार-नगर निवासी, पण्डित-मूर्ख, बदनाम-यशस्वी ॥
ramacharitamanas::181.english_translation: The way of a true lord is known in the world and in the Vedas: he recognizes love the moment he hears humility. Rich and poor, villagers and city folk, learned and simple, stained and radiant alike.
ramacharitamanas::181.translation_literal: लोकहुँ (in the world too) / बेद (the Vedas) / सुसाहिब (good lord) / रीती (custom, way) / बिनय (humility, prayer) / सुनत (hearing) / पहिचानत (recognizes) / प्रीती (love) / गनी (rich) / गरीब (poor) / ग्राम नर (village people) / नागर (city people) / पंडित (learned) / मूढ़ (foolish) / मलीन (stained) / उजागर (radiant, known)
ramacharitamanas::181.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::181.essence: True greatness notices humility, not status.
ramacharitamanas::181.simple_meaning: A noble master can tell when someone is sincere and loving, no matter their status or background. Wealth, learning, or reputation do not matter to him.
ramacharitamanas::181.simple_insight: You do not need to impress what is truly worthy. Sincerity is enough to be seen.
ramacharitamanas::181.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses in the Balkand to describe Ram's nature as the ideal lord. Ram does not judge by class, learning, or reputation; he immediately recognizes humble devotion in anyone who comes near him.
ramacharitamanas::181.modern_relevance: You walk into a room convinced your accent, clothes, or job title will decide how you're received. Then one person listens without ranking you, and the whole body relaxes. That is the kind of presence this verse praises.
ramacharitamanas::181.insight: It shifts attention from social status to the quality of your approach. Humility becomes the real signal of connection.

ramacharitamanas::182.verse_sanskrit: सुकबि कुकबि निज मति अनुहारी। नृपहि सराहत सब नर नारी॥ साधु सुजान सुसील नृपाला। ईस अंस भव परम कृपाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::182.verse_hindi: सुकवि-कुकवि, सभी नर-नारी अपनी-अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार राजा की सराहना करते हैं और साधु, बुद्धिमान, सुशील, ईश्वर के अंश से उत्पन्न कृपालु राजा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::182.english_translation: Poets, whether good or bad, praise the king according to their own understanding. Noble, wise, and virtuous kings are seen as compassionate rulers, born of a divine portion.
ramacharitamanas::182.translation_literal: सुकबि (good poet) / कुकबि (bad poet) / निज मति अनुहारी (according to their own understanding) / नृपहि (the king) / सराहत (praise) / सब नर नारी (all men and women) / साधु (noble) / सुजान (wise) / सुसील (virtuous) / नृपाला (king) / ईस अंस (a portion of the divine) / भव (born) / परम कृपाला (supremely compassionate)
ramacharitamanas::182.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::182.essence: True nobility is recognized by the wise, not by every voice.
ramacharitamanas::182.simple_meaning: People praise a king according to their own nature. A truly noble king is wise, virtuous, and deeply compassionate.
ramacharitamanas::182.simple_insight: Real character draws different responses from different people, but virtue remains visible to the wise.
ramacharitamanas::182.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing King Ram in Ayodhya. Some praise him well, some poorly, each from their own level of understanding. The verse turns from public opinion to Ram's true nature: noble, wise, virtuous, and compassionate.
ramacharitamanas::182.modern_relevance: A leader gets praised wildly in one meeting and attacked in the next. The noise changes, but steady character still shows itself to anyone paying attention.
ramacharitamanas::182.insight: It shifts attention from popularity to the qualities that make a ruler worthy of trust.

ramacharitamanas::183.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सनमानहिं सबहि सुबानी। भनिति भगति नति गति पहिचानी॥ यह प्राकृत महिपाल सुभाऊ। जान सिरोमनि कोसलराऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::183.verse_hindi: सबकी सुनकर और उनकी वाणी, भक्ति, विनय और चाल को पहचानकर सुंदर (मीठी) वाणी से सबका यथायोग्य सम्मान करते हैं। यह स्वभाव तो संसारी राजाओं का है, कोसलनाथ श्री रामचन्द्रजी तो चतुरशिरोमणि हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::183.english_translation: Listening to all, he honors everyone with gracious speech, recognizing devotion, humility, and conduct. Such is the nature of ordinary kings; Koshal's lord Ram is the wisest of all.
ramacharitamanas::183.translation_literal: सुनि (listening) / सनमानहिं (honor respectfully) / सबहि (everyone) / सुबानी (with gracious speech) / भनिति (speech/utterance) / भगति (devotion) / नति (humility/bowing) / गति (conduct/way) / पहिचानी (recognizing) / यह (this) / प्राकृत (ordinary) / महिपाल (king) / सुभाऊ (nature) / जान (know) / सिरोमनि (crest-jewel) / कोसलराऊ (king of Kosala)
ramacharitamanas::183.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::183.essence: True greatness recognizes devotion and answers with grace.
ramacharitamanas::183.simple_meaning: Ram honors everyone with kind words because he sees the devotion, humility, and conduct behind their speech. Ordinary kings may do this too, but Ram does it with unmatched wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::183.simple_insight: Being truly respectful means seeing the person beneath the words.
ramacharitamanas::183.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the poet turns from describing ordinary kings to Ram's deeper nature. Ram does not merely hear speech; he recognizes devotion, humility, and intention, and answers each person with fitting grace. This is why he stands above all rulers.
ramacharitamanas::183.modern_relevance: A manager skims your message, but one person notices the nervousness behind your careful wording and responds gently. That small recognition changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::183.insight: It shifts attention from surface words to the intention and character behind them.

ramacharitamanas::184.verse_sanskrit: रीझत राम सनेह निसोतें। को जग मंद मलिनमति मोतें ॥
ramacharitamanas::184.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी तो विशुद्ध प्रेम से ही रीझते हैं, पर जगत में मुझसे बढ़कर मूर्ख और मलिन बुद्धि और कौन होगा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::184.english_translation: Ram is pleased only by pure love. Who in the world is more foolish and impure-minded than I?
ramacharitamanas::184.translation_literal: रीझत (is pleased) / राम (Ram) / सनेह (love) / निसोतें (only through) । / को (who) / जग (in the world) / मंद (foolish) / मलिनमति (impure-minded) / मोतें (than me) ॥
ramacharitamanas::184.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::184.essence: Pure love reaches Ram; self-contempt only reveals how much love is needed.
ramacharitamanas::184.simple_meaning: Ram responds to pure love, not status or cleverness. The speaker calls himself unworthy and unclean-minded beside that standard.
ramacharitamanas::184.simple_insight: Love, not merit, is what opens the heart. That softens pride and makes devotion feel possible.
ramacharitamanas::184.detailed_meaning: The narrator has just praised Ram as the king who sees each person rightly and speaks with fitting kindness. Now the thought turns inward: Ram is won only by love, while the speaker feels himself the least worthy of all. The verse prepares the humility that follows.
ramacharitamanas::184.modern_relevance: You rehearse your apology ten times before sending it, convinced you are too messy to be received well. This verse answers that fear: what matters is the sincerity of your heart.
ramacharitamanas::184.insight: It shifts attention from self-judgment to the quality of love offered.

ramacharitamanas::185.verse_sanskrit: सठ सेवक की प्रीति रुचि रखिहहिं राम कृपालु। उपल किए जलजान जेहिं सचिव सुमति कपि भालु ॥
ramacharitamanas::185.verse_hindi: तथापि कृपालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी मुझ दुष्ट सेवक की प्रीति और रुचि को अवश्य रखेंगे, जिन्होंने पत्थरों को जहाज और बंदर-भालुओं को बुद्धिमान मंत्री बना लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::185.english_translation: Yet compassionate Ram will surely keep the love and devotion of this wicked servant, since he made stones into boats and monkeys and bears into wise ministers.
ramacharitamanas::185.translation_literal: सठ (wicked) / सेवक (servant) / की (of) / प्रीति (love) / रुचि (devotion, liking) / रखिहहिं (will keep) / राम (Ram) / कृपालु (compassionate) / उपल (stones) / किए (made) / जलजान (boats) / जेहिं (by whom) / सचिव (ministers) / सुमति (good counsel) / कपि (monkeys) / भालु (bears)
ramacharitamanas::185.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::185.essence: Ram keeps even flawed devotion and turns the unfit into helpers.
ramacharitamanas::185.simple_meaning: Ram's compassion is so great that even a flawed devotee can still be accepted. He once turned stones into boats and humble beings into wise helpers.
ramacharitamanas::185.simple_insight: You do not need to be flawless to be held by compassion.
ramacharitamanas::185.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is speaking as a humble devotee, comparing his own weakness to Ram's limitless grace. In the Balkand, after praising Ram's gentle nature, he recalls how Ram turned stones into boats and made monkeys and bears into trusted ministers, proving that no one is beyond his acceptance.
ramacharitamanas::185.modern_relevance: You send the apology after the messy mistake, expecting silence. Instead, the relationship survives because mercy is stronger than your embarrassment.
ramacharitamanas::185.insight: It shifts devotion from self-judgment to trust in Ram's welcoming grace.

ramacharitamanas::186.verse_sanskrit: हौंहु कहावत सबु कहत राम सहत उपहास। साहिब सीतानाथ सो सेवक तुलसीदास ॥
ramacharitamanas::186.verse_hindi: सब लोग मुझे श्री रामजी का सेवक कहते हैं और मैं भी (बिना लज्जा-संकोच के) कहलाता हूँ (कहने वालों का विरोध नहीं करता), कृपालु श्री रामजी इस निन्दा को सहते हैं कि श्री सीतानाथजी, जैसे स्वामी का तुलसीदास सा सेवक है ॥
ramacharitamanas::186.english_translation: Everyone calls me Ram's servant, and I too accept the name without shame. Merciful Ram, Lord of Sita, bears the mockery that such a servant as Tulsidas belongs to him.
ramacharitamanas::186.translation_literal: हौंहु (I too) / कहावत (being called) / सबु (everyone) / कहत (says) / राम (Ram) / सहत (bears) / उपहास (mockery) / साहिब (lord/master) / सीतानाथ (Lord of Sita) / सो (that) / सेवक (servant) / तुलसीदास (Tulsidas)
ramacharitamanas::186.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::186.essence: True devotion keeps its honor even under mockery.
ramacharitamanas::186.simple_meaning: Tulsidas openly accepts being called Ram's servant, even if people mock him. He treats that identity as an honor, not an insult.
ramacharitamanas::186.simple_insight: There is freedom in belonging so fully that other people's ridicule loses its power.
ramacharitamanas::186.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is speaking in his own voice, defending the life of devotion he has chosen. People mock him for calling himself Ram's servant, but he accepts it gladly and says Ram bears that mockery too. His shame is gone; his allegiance is complete.
ramacharitamanas::186.modern_relevance: You tell someone you prayed, or volunteered, or chose a quieter life, and they smirk. The old urge is to explain yourself. This verse says: let them laugh. A true commitment does not need permission.
ramacharitamanas::186.insight: It shifts the mind from defending your identity to wearing devotion openly, even under ridicule.

ramacharitamanas::187.verse_sanskrit: अति बड़ि मोरि ढिठाई खोरी। सुनि अघ नरकहुँ नाक सकोरी॥ समुझि सहम मोहि अपडर अपनें। सो सुधि राम कीन्हि नहिं सपनें ॥
ramacharitamanas::187.verse_hindi: यह मेरी बहुत बड़ी ढिठाई और दोष है, मेरे पाप को सुनकर नरक ने भी नाक सिकोड़ ली है (अर्थात नरक में भी मेरे लिए ठौर नहीं है)। यह समझकर मुझे अपने ही कल्पित डर से डर हो रहा है, किन्तु भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने तो स्वप्न में भी इस पर (मेरी इस ढिठाई और दोष पर) ध्यान नहीं दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::187.english_translation: My insolence and faults are very great. Hearing of my sins, even hell would wrinkle its nose. Knowing this, I am afraid of my own imagined fear, yet Lord Ram has not noticed it even in a dream.
ramacharitamanas::187.translation_literal: अति बड़ि (very great) / मोरि (my) / ढिठाई (insolence) / खोरी (fault, blemish) । / सुनि (hearing) / अघ (sin) / नरकहुँ (even hell) / नाक (nose) / सकोरी (wrinkled) ॥ / समुझि (understanding) / सहम (I am frightened) / मोहि (me) / अपडर (imagined fear) / अपनें (of my own) ॥ / सो (that) / सुधि (notice, care) / राम (Ram) / कीन्हि (did) / नहिं (not) / सपनें (even in a dream) ॥
ramacharitamanas::187.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::187.essence: Ram sees beyond the shame you keep replaying.
ramacharitamanas::187.simple_meaning: The speaker feels deeply unworthy and ashamed, yet says Ram has not even noticed these faults in a dream.
ramacharitamanas::187.simple_insight: Even self-condemnation loosens when you believe you are still held in Ram's care.
ramacharitamanas::187.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is speaking in his own voice, after calling himself Ram's servant. He confesses his faults so openly that even hell would reject him, yet he says Ram has ignored them completely. The verse turns shame into trust.
ramacharitamanas::187.modern_relevance: You replay one embarrassing mistake at 2 a.m. and decide it defines you. Then someone you love answers your message with simple warmth, and your whole story softens.
ramacharitamanas::187.insight: It shifts the mind from self-punishment to trust in grace.

ramacharitamanas::188.verse_sanskrit: सुनि अवलोकि सुचित चख चाही। भगति मोरि मति स्वामि सराही॥ कहत नसाइ होइ हियँ नीकी। रीझत राम जानि जन जी की ॥
ramacharitamanas::188.verse_hindi: वरन मेरे प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने तो इस बात को सुनकर, देखकर और अपने सुचित्त रूपी चक्षु से निरीक्षण कर मेरी भक्ति और बुद्धि की (उलटे) सराहना की, क्योंकि कहने में चाहे बिगड़ जाए (अर्थात् मैं चाहे अपने को भगवान का सेवक कहता-कहलाता रहूँ), परन्तु हृदय में अच्छापन होना चाहिए। (हृदय में तो अपने को उनका सेवक बनने योग्य नहीं मानकर पापी और दीन ही मानता हूँ, यह अच्छापन है।) श्री रामचन्द्रजी भी दास के हृदय की (अच्छी) स्थिति जानकर रीझ जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::188.english_translation: Hearing, seeing, and examining with his discerning gaze, my devotion and mind were praised by my master. Words may go awry, but the heart must be good. Ram is pleased when he knows a servant's heart is true.
ramacharitamanas::188.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / अवलोकि (seeing) / सुचित (careful, discerning) / चख (eye) / चाही (saw, examined) / भगति (devotion) / मोरि (my) / मति (mind, understanding) / स्वामि (master) / सराही (praised) / कहत (in speaking) / नसाइ (may spoil, go awry) / होइ (be) / हियँ (in the heart) / नीकी (good, wholesome) / रीझत (is pleased) / राम (Ram) / जानि (knowing) / जन (servant) / जी (heart, being) / की (of)
ramacharitamanas::188.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::188.essence: Ram is pleased by a truthful heart, not flawless speech.
ramacharitamanas::188.simple_meaning: Ram values a sincere heart more than perfect words. Even if speech is clumsy, true devotion and good intent please him.
ramacharitamanas::188.simple_insight: You can stop performing and still be loved for what is genuine inside.
ramacharitamanas::188.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still speaking from his humble self-praise in Balkand. He says Ram noticed his devotion with a discerning eye and approved it, because Ram cares less about polished speech than the servant's inner truth.
ramacharitamanas::188.modern_relevance: You fumble your words in a meeting, then worry all night that you sounded foolish. This verse says the deeper measure is not polish, but whether your intent was honest.
ramacharitamanas::188.insight: It shifts attention from perfect expression to sincere inner alignment.

ramacharitamanas::189.verse_sanskrit: रहति न प्रभु चित चूक किए की। करत सुरति सय बार हिए की॥ जेहिं अघ बधेउ ब्याध जिमि बाली। फिरि सुकंठ सोइ कीन्हि कुचाली ॥
ramacharitamanas::189.verse_hindi: प्रभु के चित्त में अपने भक्तों की हुई भूल-चूक याद नहीं रहती (वे उसे भूल जाते हैं) और उनके हृदय (की अच्छाई-नेकी) को सौ-सौ बार याद करते रहते हैं। जिस पाप के कारण उन्होंने बालि को व्याध की तरह मारा था, वैसी ही कुचाल फिर सुग्रीव ने चली ॥
ramacharitamanas::189.english_translation: The Lord does not keep a devotee’s mistake in mind. He remembers the heart’s goodness a hundred times. The very same wrong that killed Bali like a hunter’s arrow was repeated by Sugriva.
ramacharitamanas::189.translation_literal: रहति (remains) / न (not) / प्रभु (the Lord) / चित (in mind) / चूक (mistake) / किए की (done by) / करत (doing) / सुरति (remembrance) / सय बार (a hundred times) / हिए की (of the heart)॥ / जेहिं (by which) / अघ (sin/wrong) / बधेउ (was killed) / ब्याध (hunter) / जिमि (like) / बाली (Bali) / फिरि (again) / सुकंठ (Sugriva) / सोइ (that same) / कीन्हि (did) / कुचाली (wrong deed)॥
ramacharitamanas::189.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::189.essence: Ram remembers devotion more than failure.
ramacharitamanas::189.simple_meaning: Ram does not dwell on a devotee’s mistake. He remembers the good in the heart again and again, even when a person repeats the same fault.
ramacharitamanas::189.simple_insight: It feels safe to keep trying when mercy is stronger than memory of failure.
ramacharitamanas::189.detailed_meaning: After Bali’s death and Sugriva’s rise, the story turns to Ram’s way of seeing people. Tulsidas says Ram does not fixate on a follower’s lapse; he keeps returning to the heart’s devotion, even when the same old weakness appears again.
ramacharitamanas::189.modern_relevance: You disappoint someone once, then fear they’ll never trust you again. This verse offers a different kind of relationship: one that notices failure, but refuses to make failure the whole story.
ramacharitamanas::189.insight: It shifts attention from a person’s slip to their deeper intention, making room for restoration instead of permanent judgment.

ramacharitamanas::190.verse_sanskrit: सोइ करतूति बिभीषन केरी। सपनेहूँ सो न राम हियँ हेरी॥ ते भरतहि भेंटत सनमाने। राजसभाँ रघुबीर बखाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::190.verse_hindi: वही करनी विभीषण की थी, परन्तु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने स्वप्न में भी उसका मन में विचार नहीं किया। उलटे भरतजी से मिलने के समय श्री रघुनाथजी ने उनका सम्मान किया और राजसभा में भी उनके गुणों का बखान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::190.english_translation: That was the same conduct of Vibhishana, yet Ram never even thought of it in a dream. Instead, when he met Bharat, Raghubir honored him and praised his virtues in the royal court.
ramacharitamanas::190.translation_literal: सोइ (that same) / करतूति (conduct, deed) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / केरी (of) / सपनेहूँ (even in a dream) / सो (that) / न (not) / राम (Ram) / हियँ (in the heart) / हेरी (saw, remembered) / ते (then) / भरतहि (Bharat) / भेंटत (meeting) / सनमाने (honored) / राजसभाँ (in the royal court) / रघुबीर (Raghubir, Ram) / बखाने (praised, described)
ramacharitamanas::190.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::190.essence: True regard remembers worth, not old mistakes.
ramacharitamanas::190.simple_meaning: Ram did not hold Vibhishana's past against him. He honored Bharat and openly praised Vibhishana's worth in court.
ramacharitamanas::190.simple_insight: Being near greatness means others are not trapped forever by their past.
ramacharitamanas::190.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, Tulsidas is showing how Ram sees people. Vibhishana’s old actions are not stored as a grievance, and Bharat receives full honor. This verse deepens the earlier claim that Ram remembers only what is good in a devotee.
ramacharitamanas::190.modern_relevance: A family argument can leave one person carrying a mistake for years. You keep replaying it, but the other person may be ready to meet you fresh. Ram’s way is to let worth speak louder than history.
ramacharitamanas::190.insight: It shifts attention from judging people by old faults to recognizing present character and giving honor where it is due.

ramacharitamanas::191.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु तरु तर कपि डार पर ते किए आपु समान। तुलसी कहूँ न राम से साहिब सील निधान ॥
ramacharitamanas::191.verse_hindi: प्रभु (श्री रामचन्द्रजी) तो वृक्ष के नीचे और बंदर डाली पर (अर्थात कहाँ मर्यादा पुरुषोत्तम सच्चिदानन्दघन परमात्मा श्री रामजी और कहाँ पेड़ों की शाखाओं पर कूदने वाले बंदर), परन्तु ऐसे बंदरों को भी उन्होंने अपने समान बना लिया। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी सरीखे शीलनिधान स्वामी कहीं भी नहीं हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::191.english_translation: The Lord made the monkeys like himself, though he was under the tree and they were on the branches. Tulsidas says no master of virtue is like Ram.
ramacharitamanas::191.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / तरु तर (under the tree) / कपि (monkeys) / डार पर (on the branch) / ते (those) / किए (made) / आपु (himself) / समान (equal) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / कहूँ (says) / न (not) / राम (Ram) / से (like) / साहिब (master) / सील (virtue) / निधान (treasure)
ramacharitamanas::191.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::191.essence: Ram's greatness is measured by how completely he lifts others to himself.
ramacharitamanas::191.simple_meaning: Ram's greatness is so complete that he lifts even the monkeys around him to his own level. Tulsidas says no one matches Ram's virtue.
ramacharitamanas::191.simple_insight: You don't need status to be close to the divine; grace makes closeness possible.
ramacharitamanas::191.detailed_meaning: In the midst of Ram's forest story, the poet pauses to praise a startling reversal: the Lord is under the tree, while the monkeys leap on the branches, yet Ram makes them equal to himself. Tulsidas uses that image to declare Ram unmatched in virtue.
ramacharitamanas::191.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone seems polished, connected, and important. Then one person treats the least impressive person with full respect, and the whole hierarchy collapses.
ramacharitamanas::191.insight: It shifts attention from rank to grace, showing that true greatness elevates others instead of towering over them.

ramacharitamanas::192.verse_sanskrit: राम निकाईं रावरी है सबही को नीक। जौं यह साँची है सदा तौ नीको तुलसीक ॥
ramacharitamanas::192.verse_hindi: हे श्री रामजी! आपकी अच्छाई से सभी का भला है (अर्थात आपका कल्याणमय स्वभाव सभी का कल्याण करने वाला है) यदि यह बात सच है तो तुलसीदास का भी सदा कल्याण ही होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::192.english_translation: O Ram, your goodness brings good to everyone. If that is true, then Tulsi's good is assured forever.
ramacharitamanas::192.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / निकाईं (goodness) / रावरी (your) / है (is) / सबही (everyone) / को (to) / नीक (good) / जौं (if) / यह (this) / साँची (true) / है (is) / सदा (always) / तौ (then) / नीको (good) / तुलसीक (Tulsi's)
ramacharitamanas::192.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::192.essence: Ram's goodness is so complete that it covers everyone, including the devotee.
ramacharitamanas::192.simple_meaning: Ram's nature is good for everyone, and Tulsidas says that if this is true, his own welfare is secure forever.
ramacharitamanas::192.simple_insight: There is comfort in trusting that a loving presence does not exclude you.
ramacharitamanas::192.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is closing a praise section by turning from Ram's universal goodness to his own hope. He says Ram's kindness reaches everyone, so if that nature is real, even the poet can rest in it.
ramacharitamanas::192.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love quietly help everyone in the room, from the intern to the janitor. Seeing that steady goodness, you finally believe there is room for you too.
ramacharitamanas::192.insight: It shifts trust from self-protection to confidence in Ram's universal care.

ramacharitamanas::193.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि निज गुन दोष कहि सबहि बहुरि सिरु नाइ। बरनउँ रघुबर बिसद जसु सुनि कलि कलुष नसाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::193.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार अपने गुण-दोषों को कहकर और सबको फिर सिर नवाकर मैं श्री रघुनाथजी का निर्मल यश वर्णन करता हूँ, जिसके सुनने से कलियुग के पाप नष्ट हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::193.english_translation: In this way, after speaking of my own virtues and faults and bowing to everyone again, I describe the pure glory of Raghubar, whose hearing destroys the stains of Kali Yuga.
ramacharitamanas::193.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / निज (own) / गुन (virtues) / दोष (faults) / कहि (having said) / सबहि (to everyone) / बहुरि (again) / सिरु नाइ (bowing the head) / बरनउँ (I describe) / रघुबर (Raghubar) / बिसद (pure, spotless) / जसु (glory, praise) / सुनि (hearing) / कलि (Kali Yuga) / कलुष (stains, impurities) / नसाइ (destroyed)
ramacharitamanas::193.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::193.essence: True praise begins by emptying the ego.
ramacharitamanas::193.simple_meaning: The poet says he will speak humbly, after bowing to everyone, and then praise Ram. Hearing this praise removes the impurities of the present age.
ramacharitamanas::193.simple_insight: Humility does not weaken the message; it purifies it.
ramacharitamanas::193.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is turning from introduction to invocation. After acknowledging his own limits and bowing to all, he begins the praise of Ram that will carry the listener through the rest of the work. This is the doorway into the sacred story.
ramacharitamanas::193.modern_relevance: Before a family gathering, you swallow your pride, apologize first, and speak gently. The room changes because your words are no longer trying to win — they are trying to bless.
ramacharitamanas::193.insight: It teaches you to begin with humility so the message can reach cleanly.

ramacharitamanas::194.verse_sanskrit: जागबलिक जो कथा सुहाई। भरद्वाज मुनिबरहि सुनाई॥ कहिहउँ सोइ संबाद बखानी। सुनहुँ सकल सज्जन सुखु मानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::194.verse_hindi: मुनि याज्ञवल्क्यजी ने जो सुहावनी कथा मुनिश्रेष्ठ भरद्वाजजी को सुनाई थी, उसी संवाद को मैं बखानकर कहूँगा, सब सज्जन सुख का अनुभव करते हुए उसे सुनें ॥
ramacharitamanas::194.english_translation: Yajnavalkya told Bharadvaja the lovely story. I will now recount that same dialogue; listen, all good people, with joy.
ramacharitamanas::194.translation_literal: जागबलिक (Yajnavalkya) / जो (which) / कथा (story) / सुहाई (beautiful, lovely) / भरद्वाज मुनिबरहि (to the great sage Bharadvaja) / सुनाई (was told)॥ / कहिहउँ (I shall tell) / सोइ (that same) / संबाद (dialogue) / बखानी (describing, recounting)॥ / सुनहुँ (listen) / सकल (all) / सज्जन (good people) / सुखु मानी (with joy, taking happiness) ॥
ramacharitamanas::194.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::194.essence: A cherished teaching stays alive by being faithfully retold.
ramacharitamanas::194.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he will retell the same beautiful dialogue Yajnavalkya once told Bharadvaja, and asks good people to listen with joy.
ramacharitamanas::194.simple_insight: A sacred story becomes living again when it is retold with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::194.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening the frame of the Ramcharitmanas's larger sacred dialogue. He points back to Yajnavalkya and Bharadvaja, then announces that he will now recount that same cherished conversation for the listener's benefit.
ramacharitamanas::194.modern_relevance: You hear an elder say, “Let me tell you how this was first shared,” and the room quiets. The story matters because it has been carried carefully from one listener to the next.
ramacharitamanas::194.insight: It invites the reader to receive the text as a preserved conversation, not a private opinion.

ramacharitamanas::195.verse_sanskrit: संभु कीन्ह यह चरित सुहावा। बहुरि कृपा करि उमहि सुनावा॥ सोइ सिव कागभुसुंडिहि दीन्हा। राम भगत अधिकारी चीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::195.verse_hindi: शिवजी ने पहले इस सुहावने चरित्र को रचा, फिर कृपा करके पार्वतीजी को सुनाया। वही चरित्र शिवजी ने काकभुशुण्डिजी को रामभक्त और अधिकारी पहचानकर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::195.english_translation: Shiva first composed this lovely account, then, out of grace, told it to Parvati. The same account Shiva gave to Kakbhushundi, recognizing him as a devoted and worthy listener of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::195.translation_literal: संभु (Shiva) / कीन्ह (made) / यह (this) / चरित (account, story) / सुहावा (lovely) / बहुरि (again) / कृपा (grace) / करि (doing) / उमहि (to Uma/Parvati) / सुनावा (made hear, told) / सोइ (the same) / सिव (Shiva) / कागभुसुंडिहि (to Kakbhushundi) / दीन्हा (gave) / राम-भगत (Ram-devotee) / अधिकारी (worthy, qualified) / चीन्हा (recognized)
ramacharitamanas::195.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::195.essence: Devotion makes a listener worthy of the deepest story.
ramacharitamanas::195.simple_meaning: Shiva created this beautiful account, then shared it with Parvati and later with Kakbhushundi, whom he recognized as worthy because of his devotion to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::195.simple_insight: Real worth is not status or learning, but the heart that can receive and keep devotion.
ramacharitamanas::195.detailed_meaning: The frame story widens: Shiva is not only the teller of Ram's story to Parvati, but also the one who passes it on to Kakbhushundi. The verse highlights that devotion itself makes a listener worthy of receiving sacred story.
ramacharitamanas::195.modern_relevance: A teacher notices that one student is listening with real hunger, not just collecting facts. That student gets the deeper version, because attention shaped by love can hold more than cleverness.
ramacharitamanas::195.insight: It shifts the reader from chasing credentials to becoming receptive through devotion and sincerity.

ramacharitamanas::196.verse_sanskrit: तेहि सन जागबलिक पुनि पावा। तिन्ह पुनि भरद्वाज प्रति गावा॥ ते श्रोता बकता समसीला। सवँदरसी जानहिं हरिलीला ॥
ramacharitamanas::196.verse_hindi: उन काकभुशुण्डिजी से फिर याज्ञवल्क्यजी ने पाया और उन्होंने फिर उसे भरद्वाजजी को गाकर सुनाया। वे दोनों वक्ता और श्रोता (याज्ञवल्क्य और भरद्वाज) समान शील वाले और समदर्शी हैं और श्री हरि की लीला को जानते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::196.english_translation: Yajnavalkya received it again from Kakbhushundi and then sang it to Bharadvaja. Both the speaker and the listener are alike in character, and they know the play of the divine.
ramacharitamanas::196.translation_literal: तेहि सन (from that one) / जागबलिक (Yajnavalkya) / पुनि (again) / पावा (received) / तिन्ह (they) / पुनि (again) / भरद्वाज प्रति (to Bharadvaja) / गावा (sang, recited) / ते (they) / श्रोता (listener) / बकता (speaker) / समसीला (of equal character) / सवँदरसी (seeing equally) / जानहिं (know) / हरिलीला (the play of Hari)
ramacharitamanas::196.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::196.essence: Sacred teaching travels only between minds of equal steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::196.simple_meaning: Yajnavalkya passed the story on to Bharadvaja, and both men shared the same noble temperament and equal vision. They understood the divine play.
ramacharitamanas::196.simple_insight: True listening and true speaking arise from the same steady character.
ramacharitamanas::196.detailed_meaning: Yajnavalkya is passing along the sacred story he had received from Kakbhushundi, and Bharadvaja listens with the same depth. Tulsidas pauses to say that both are fit for this teaching because they are equal in character and vision.
ramacharitamanas::196.modern_relevance: Two people sit across from each other after midnight, one sharing something precious, the other listening without interrupting. The exchange feels rare because both have the same seriousness and humility.
ramacharitamanas::196.insight: It shifts attention from information alone to the character that can truly receive and carry it.

ramacharitamanas::197.verse_sanskrit: जानहिं तीनि काल निज ग्याना। करतल गत आमलक समाना॥ औरउ जे हरिभगत सुजाना। कहहिं सुनहिं समुझहिं बिधि नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::197.verse_hindi: वे अपने ज्ञान से तीनों कालों की बातों को हथेली पर रखे हुए आँवले के समान (प्रत्यक्ष) जानते हैं। और भी जो सुजान (भगवान की लीलाओं का रहस्य जानने वाले) हरि भक्त हैं, वे इस चरित्र को नाना प्रकार से कहते, सुनते और समझते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::197.english_translation: Those who know through their own wisdom know the three times as clearly as an amla fruit in the palm. And other wise devotees of Hari speak, hear, and understand this story in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::197.translation_literal: जानहिं (they know) / तीनि काल (three times) / निज ग्याना (through their own knowledge) / करतल गत (placed in the palm) / आमलक समाना (like an amla fruit) / औरउ (and also) / जे (who) / हरिभगत (devotees of Hari) / सुजाना (wise) / कहहिं (speak) / सुनहिं (hear) / समुझहिं (understand) / बिधि नाना (in many ways)
ramacharitamanas::197.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::197.essence: True devotees hold the story in clear awareness and many living forms.
ramacharitamanas::197.simple_meaning: Wise devotees understand Ram's story clearly. They can speak about it, hear it, and grasp it in many different ways.
ramacharitamanas::197.simple_insight: Real understanding makes the same story alive from many angles.
ramacharitamanas::197.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues the chain of transmission: Shiva gave the story to Parvati, then to Kak Bhushundi, then to Yajnavalkya, and now it reaches Bharadvaja. He says true devotees and the truly wise can hold the story clearly and share it in many forms.
ramacharitamanas::197.modern_relevance: You hear the same family story at different reunions, and each time a wiser relative notices something new. Real understanding is not brittle; it deepens with every telling.
ramacharitamanas::197.insight: It shifts the reader from passive listening to active, layered understanding.

ramacharitamanas::198.verse_sanskrit: मैं पुनि निज गुर सन सुनी कथा सो सूकरखेत। समुझी नहिं तसि बालपन तब अति रहेउँ अचेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::198.verse_hindi: फिर वही कथा मैंने वाराह क्षेत्र में अपने गुरुजी से सुनी, परन्तु उस समय मैं लड़कपन के कारण बहुत बेसमझ था, इससे उसको उस प्रकार (अच्छी तरह) समझा नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::198.english_translation: I heard that same story again from my guru in the sacred place of Varaha, but I was still childish and very unaware, so I could not understand it properly then.
ramacharitamanas::198.translation_literal: मैं (I) / पुनि (again) / निज (my own) / गुर (guru) / सन (from) / सुनी (heard) / कथा (story) / सो (that same) / सूकरखेत (Varaha-ksetra) / समुझी (understood) / नहिं (not) / तसि (thus) / बालपन (childhood) / तब (then) / अति (very) / रहेउँ (I was) / अचेत (unaware)
ramacharitamanas::198.speaker: Kak Bhushundi
ramacharitamanas::198.essence: Understanding waits for readiness; the same story can arrive too early.
ramacharitamanas::198.simple_meaning: The speaker heard the story before, but as a child he could not truly grasp it.
ramacharitamanas::198.simple_insight: It is humbling to admit that understanding often comes only after we are ready for it.
ramacharitamanas::198.detailed_meaning: Kak Bhushundi is recalling an earlier hearing of Ram's story from his teacher at Varaha-ksetra. He admits that, because he was still childish and unaware, the teaching did not fully land. The next verse continues the thought.
ramacharitamanas::198.modern_relevance: You read a life-changing book at sixteen and barely remember it. Years later, the same lines hit differently because your mind is finally ready.
ramacharitamanas::198.insight: It shifts the reader from pretending to know toward recognising that maturity is needed for real understanding.

ramacharitamanas::199.verse_sanskrit: श्रोता बकता ग्याननिधि कथा राम कै गूढ़। किमि समुझौं मैं जीव जड़ कलि मल ग्रसित बिमूढ़॥30ख॥
ramacharitamanas::199.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी की गूढ़ कथा के वक्ता (कहने वाले) और श्रोता (सुनने वाले) दोनों ज्ञान के खजाने (पूरे ज्ञानी) होते हैं। मैं कलियुग के पापों से ग्रसा हुआ महामूढ़ जड़ जीव भला उसको कैसे समझ सकता था? ॥
ramacharitamanas::199.english_translation: Both the speaker and the listener of Ram's hidden story are reservoirs of wisdom. How could I, a dull being covered by the stains of Kali, ever understand it?
ramacharitamanas::199.translation_literal: श्रोता (listener) / बकता (speaker) / ग्याननिधि (ocean of wisdom) / कथा (story) / राम कै (of Ram) / गूढ़ (hidden, profound) / किमि (how) / समुझौं (would I understand) / मैं (I) / जीव (being) / जड़ (dull) / कलि (of Kali age) / मल (stains) / ग्रसित (gripped) / बिमूढ़ (deluded)
ramacharitamanas::199.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::199.essence: Ram's deepest story yields only to humility and wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::199.simple_meaning: Ram's story is so deep that only truly wise listeners and speakers can grasp it. The poet admits that, burdened by confusion and the age of decline, he cannot fully understand it alone.
ramacharitamanas::199.simple_insight: Humility opens the door to learning. Real understanding begins when you stop pretending you already know.
ramacharitamanas::199.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses after recalling how little he understood the story in his youth. He says Ram's hidden कथा needs both a wise speaker and a wise listener, and that his own mind, clouded by Kali's stains, was not fit to grasp it.
ramacharitamanas::199.modern_relevance: You open a dense book at midnight, reread the same paragraph three times, and finally admit you need help. That honest admission is the beginning of understanding.
ramacharitamanas::199.insight: It shifts the mind from self-confidence to receptive inquiry, making learning possible.

ramacharitamanas::200.verse_sanskrit: तदपि कही गुर बारहिं बारा। समुझि परी कछु मति अनुसारा॥ भाषाबद्ध करबि मैं सोई। मोरें मन प्रबोध जेहिं होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::200.verse_hindi: तो भी गुरुजी ने जब बार-बार कथा कही, तब बुद्धि के अनुसार कुछ समझ में आई। वही अब मेरे द्वारा भाषा में रची जाएगी, जिससे मेरे मन को संतोष हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::200.english_translation: Even so, my guru told the story again and again. Then, according to my own understanding, some of it became clear. I will now put that same story into language, so my mind may find peace.
ramacharitamanas::200.translation_literal: तदपि (even then) / कही (was told) / गुर (the teacher) / बारहिं बारा (again and again) / समुझि (having understood) / परी (fell) / कछु (some) / मति (understanding) / अनुसारा (according to) / भाषाबद्ध (put into language) / करबि (I will do) / मैं (I) / सोई (that same) / मोरें (for my) / मन (mind) / प्रबोध (awakening / settling) / जेहिं (by which) / होई (may happen)
ramacharitamanas::200.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::200.essence: Repetition can turn confusion into usable understanding.
ramacharitamanas::200.simple_meaning: Repeated hearing from the teacher finally brought a little understanding. The speaker now wants to retell the story in simple language so the mind can settle.
ramacharitamanas::200.simple_insight: Slow understanding is still real understanding. Repetition can turn confusion into clarity.
ramacharitamanas::200.detailed_meaning: After admitting earlier confusion, the narrator says the guru’s repeated telling has finally allowed some understanding to arise. He now resolves to retell Ram’s story in language he can grasp, so his own mind can become steady.
ramacharitamanas::200.modern_relevance: You replay the same conversation on the drive home, and only then does the meaning click. Sometimes understanding comes not from one perfect hearing, but from hearing it again with a calmer mind.
ramacharitamanas::200.insight: It shifts the reader from expecting instant comprehension to trusting repeated reflection.

ramacharitamanas::201.verse_sanskrit: जस कछु बुधि बिबेक बल मेरें। तस कहिहउँ हियँ हरि के प्रेरें॥ निज संदेह मोह भ्रम हरनी। करउँ कथा भव सरिता तरनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::201.verse_hindi: जैसा कुछ मुझमें बुद्धि और विवेक का बल है, मैं हृदय में हरि की प्रेरणा से उसी के अनुसार कहूँगा। मैं अपने संदेह, अज्ञान और भ्रम को हरने वाली कथा रचता हूँ, जो संसार रूपी नदी के पार करने के लिए नाव है ॥
ramacharitamanas::201.english_translation: Whatever little strength of understanding and discrimination I have, I will speak by Ram's inspiration from my heart. I compose a story that removes doubt, delusion, and confusion, and serves as a boat to cross the river of worldly becoming.
ramacharitamanas::201.translation_literal: जस (as) / कछु (whatever little) / बुधि (understanding) / बिबेक (discrimination) / बल (strength) / मेरें (in me) / तस (so) / कहिहउँ (I will speak) / हियँ (in the heart) / हरि (Ram) / के (of) / प्रेरें (by inspiration) / निज (own) / संदेह (doubt) / मोह (delusion) / भ्रम (confusion) / हरनी (removing) / करउँ (I compose) / कथा (story) / भव (worldly becoming) / सरिता (river) / तरनी (boat)
ramacharitamanas::201.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::201.essence: Ram's prompting turns limited understanding into a boat across confusion.
ramacharitamanas::201.simple_meaning: The poet says he will speak only as much as Ram inspires in his heart. He offers this story as a boat that carries readers beyond doubt, confusion, and delusion.
ramacharitamanas::201.simple_insight: You do not need perfect clarity to begin; honest guidance can still carry you through confusion.
ramacharitamanas::201.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening his telling of Ram's life. He bows to Ram's inner prompting, admits his own limited understanding, and presents the Ramcharitmanas as a saving boat for confused minds. This frames the whole work as help, not ornament.
ramacharitamanas::201.modern_relevance: You sit down to write, pray, or speak and feel unqualified. Instead of pretending certainty, you offer what clarity you do have and let that sincerity carry others too.
ramacharitamanas::201.insight: It shifts the mind from self-confidence to surrendered guidance, and from confusion to a usable path.

ramacharitamanas::202.verse_sanskrit: बुध बिश्राम सकल जन रंजनि। रामकथा कलि कलुष बिभंजनि॥ रामकथा कलि पंनग भरनी। पुनि बिबेक पावक कहुँ अरनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::202.verse_hindi: रामकथा पण्डितों को विश्राम देने वाली, सब मनुष्यों को प्रसन्न करने वाली और कलियुग के पापों का नाश करने वाली है। रामकथा कलियुग रूपी साँप के लिए मोरनी है और विवेक रूपी अग्नि के प्रकट करने के लिए अरणि (मंथन की जाने वाली लकड़ी) है, (अर्थात इस कथा से ज्ञान की प्राप्ति होती है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::202.english_translation: The story of Ram gives rest to the wise, delights all people, and destroys the impurities of Kali Yuga. The story of Ram is a she-monkey for the serpent of Kali, and the tinder-stick that brings forth the fire of discrimination.
ramacharitamanas::202.translation_literal: बुध (wise) / बिश्राम (rest) / सकल (all) / जन (people) / रंजनि (delighting) / रामकथा (the story of Ram) / कलि (of Kali Yuga) / कलुष (impurity) / बिभंजनि (destroying) ॥ रामकथा (the story of Ram) / कलि (of Kali Yuga) / पंनग (snake) / भरनी (she-monkey) / पुनि (again) / बिबेक (discrimination) / पावक (fire) / कहुँ (for) / अरनी (tinder-stick) ॥
ramacharitamanas::202.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::202.essence: Ram's story soothes the heart and ignites clear seeing.
ramacharitamanas::202.simple_meaning: Ram's story calms the wise, delights everyone, and burns away the corruption of the age. It also stirs discrimination, like tinder bringing fire to life.
ramacharitamanas::202.simple_insight: A sacred story can both soothe the heart and sharpen the mind.
ramacharitamanas::202.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has begun praising his own telling of Ram's story. After saying he will speak only as inspired, he now explains why this कथा matters: it comforts learned people, delights ordinary listeners, burns the stains of Kali Yuga, and awakens clear discrimination.
ramacharitamanas::202.modern_relevance: A worn-out mind scrolls for distraction at midnight, then stumbles onto a story that quiets the noise and makes you see your life clearly. Some words do both at once.
ramacharitamanas::202.insight: It frames sacred narrative as both emotional relief and a trigger for clear seeing.

ramacharitamanas::203.verse_sanskrit: रामकथा कलि कामद गाई। सुजन सजीवनि मूरि सुहाई॥ सोइ बसुधातल सुधा तरंगिनि। भय भंजनि भ्रम भेक भुअंगिनि ॥
ramacharitamanas::203.verse_hindi: रामकथा कलियुग में सब मनोरथों को पूर्ण करने वाली कामधेनु गौ है और सज्जनों के लिए सुंदर संजीवनी जड़ी है। पृथ्वी पर यही अमृत की नदी है, जन्म-मरण रूपी भय का नाश करने वाली और भ्रम रूपी मेंढकों को खाने के लिए सर्पिणी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::203.english_translation: Ram's story is the wish-fulfilling cow in this age of conflict, and a lovely healing herb for good people. On earth it is a river of nectar, destroying fear, and a serpent that swallows the frogs of confusion.
ramacharitamanas::203.translation_literal: रामकथा (Ram's story) / कलि (in the age of conflict) / कामद (wish-fulfilling) / गाई (cow) / सुजन (for good people) / सजीवनि (life-giving herb) / मूरि (herb) / सुहाई (beautiful) / सोइ (that) / बसुधातल (on the earth) / सुधा (nectar) / तरंगिनि (river) / भय (fear) / भंजनि (destroyer) / भ्रम (confusion) / भेक (frogs) / भुअंगिनि (serpent)
ramacharitamanas::203.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::203.essence: Ram's story gives what fear and confusion take away.
ramacharitamanas::203.simple_meaning: Ram's story gives people what they truly need: comfort, healing, and freedom from fear and confusion.
ramacharitamanas::203.simple_insight: The heart relaxes when it turns to a story that restores rather than disturbs.
ramacharitamanas::203.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising the power of Ram's story itself. After saying it can carry people across the flood of worldly suffering, he now describes it as a source of wish-fulfillment, healing, nectar, and protection from fear and confusion.
ramacharitamanas::203.modern_relevance: You open a feed full of panic, comparison, and noise, and feel yourself shrinking. Then one story, one prayer, one remembered truth steadies you again. Some words do not entertain you; they restore you.
ramacharitamanas::203.insight: It shifts attention from scattered craving to a source of emotional and spiritual restoration.

ramacharitamanas::204.verse_sanskrit: असुर सेन सम नरक निकंदिनि। साधु बिबुध कुल हित गिरिनंदिनि॥ संत समाज पयोधि रमा सी। बिस्व भार भर अचल छमा सी ॥
ramacharitamanas::204.verse_hindi: यह रामकथा असुरों की सेना के समान नरकों का नाश करने वाली और साधु रूप देवताओं के कुल का हित करने वाली पार्वती (दुर्गा) है। यह संत-समाज रूपी क्षीर समुद्र के लिए लक्ष्मीजी के समान है और सम्पूर्ण विश्व का भार उठाने में अचल पृथ्वी के समान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::204.english_translation: Ram-katha is like an army of demons that destroys hells, and like a boon to the noble and the gods' line. It is like Lakshmi to the ocean of saints, and like the steady earth that bears the weight of the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::204.translation_literal: असुर सेन (army of demons) / सम (like) / नरक (hells) / निकंदिनि (destroyer) / साधु (noble) / बिबुध (gods) / कुल (lineage) / हित (benefit) / गिरिनंदिनि (daughter of the mountain) / संत (saints) / समाज (assembly) / पयोधि (ocean) / रमा सी (like Lakshmi) / बिस्व (world) / भार (burden) / भर (bearing) / अचल (steady) / छमा सी (like the earth)
ramacharitamanas::204.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::204.essence: Ram-katha destroys suffering and becomes steady support for the world.
ramacharitamanas::204.simple_meaning: Ram-katha is praised as a force that destroys suffering, supports the good, nourishes saints, and bears the weight of the world with steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::204.simple_insight: What nourishes the heart can also carry the heaviest burdens.
ramacharitamanas::204.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues his praise of Ram-katha in Balkand, piling up images to show its many powers. After calling it the cure for worldly corruption, he now says it destroys suffering, helps the noble, sustains saints, and holds the world together like the earth itself.
ramacharitamanas::204.modern_relevance: A friend calls you at midnight after a breakup, a family crisis, and a job loss all in one week. You listen without flinching, help without drama, and stay steady. This verse praises that kind of sustaining presence.
ramacharitamanas::204.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing devotion as private feeling to seeing it as support that protects, nourishes, and carries others.

ramacharitamanas::205.verse_sanskrit: जम गन मुहँ मसि जग जमुना सी। जीवन मुकुति हेतु जनु कासी॥ रामहि प्रिय पावनि तुलसी सी। तुलसिदास हित हियँ हुलसी सी ॥
ramacharitamanas::205.verse_hindi: यमदूतों के मुख पर कालिख लगाने के लिए यह जगत में यमुनाजी के समान है और जीवों को मुक्ति देने के लिए मानो काशी ही है। यह श्री रामजी को पवित्र तुलसी के समान प्रिय है और तुलसीदास के लिए हुलसी (तुलसीदासजी की माता) के समान हृदय से हित करने वाली है ॥
ramacharitamanas::205.english_translation: It is like the Yamuna in the world, blackening the faces of Yama's messengers; it is like Kashi, the place that gives beings freedom. It is dear to Ram like holy Tulsi, and to Tulsidas it is as dear and helpful as his mother Hulsī.
ramacharitamanas::205.translation_literal: जम गन (for Yama's messengers) / मुहँ (face) / मसि (ink, blackness) / जग (world) / जमुना सी (like the Yamuna) / जीवन (of beings) / मुकुति (freedom) / हेतु (for the sake of) / जनु (as if) / कासी (Kashi) / रामहि (to Ram) / प्रिय (dear) / पावनि (holy) / तुलसी सी (like Tulsi) / तुलसिदास (Tulsidas) / हित (beneficial, helpful) / हियँ (in the heart) / हुलसी सी (like Hulsī)
ramacharitamanas::205.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::205.essence: What Ram loves becomes the very thing that frees and nourishes.
ramacharitamanas::205.simple_meaning: Ram's story is described as sacred, liberating, and deeply beloved by Ram himself. Tulsidas also says it feels personally life-giving to him, like a mother’s care.
ramacharitamanas::205.simple_insight: What you love most can become what heals you most.
ramacharitamanas::205.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ramkatha as the heart of the whole text. He says it purifies darkness, gives freedom, and is dear to Ram himself. For Tulsidas, it is not abstract doctrine but intimate nourishment, like a mother’s care.
ramacharitamanas::205.modern_relevance: You open a book or song after a day that felt heavy, and something in it washes the mind clean. The words do not just entertain — they steady you, free you, and feel personally meant for you.
ramacharitamanas::205.insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to intimacy: what is sacred is also what sustains.

ramacharitamanas::206.verse_sanskrit: सिवप्रिय मेकल सैल सुता सी। सकल सिद्धि सुख संपति रासी॥ सदगुन सुरगन अंब अदिति सी। रघुबर भगति प्रेम परमिति सी ॥
ramacharitamanas::206.verse_hindi: यह रामकथा शिवजी को नर्मदाजी के समान प्यारी है, यह सब सिद्धियों की तथा सुख-सम्पत्ति की राशि है। सद्गुण रूपी देवताओं के उत्पन्न और पालन-पोषण करने के लिए माता अदिति के समान है। श्री रघुनाथजी की भक्ति और प्रेम की परम सीमा सी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::206.english_translation: Ram's story is as dear to Shiva as the Mekal mountain's daughter is to the river. It is a treasury of every power, joy, and fortune. It is like Aditi, mother of the gods, who bears and nourishes every noble quality. It is the highest limit of devotion and love for Raghubar.
ramacharitamanas::206.translation_literal: सिवप्रिय (dear to Shiva) / मेकल सैल (Mekal mountain) / सुता (daughter) / सी (like) / सकल (all) / सिद्धि (accomplishment, power) / सुख (joy) / संपति (wealth, fortune) / रासी (heap, treasury) / सदगुन (good qualities) / सुरगन (group of radiant beings) / अंब (mother) / अदिति (Aditi) / सी (like) / रघुबर (Raghubar) / भगति (devotion) / प्रेम (love) / परमिति (highest limit) / सी (like)
ramacharitamanas::206.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::206.essence: Ram's story is devotion at its highest fullness.
ramacharitamanas::206.simple_meaning: Ram's story is described as a source of every blessing, every good quality, and the highest form of love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::206.simple_insight: Devotion is not small or sentimental here; it becomes the fullest, richest way a heart can live.
ramacharitamanas::206.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still praising Ram's story in the opening of Balkand. He compares it to sacred, life-giving sources and then lifts it higher: this story is not only holy, it is the fullest treasure of devotion to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::206.modern_relevance: You open a story because you are tired, and somewhere inside it you feel steadier, cleaner, more alive. Some words do not just entertain — they gather your scattered heart and return it to what matters.
ramacharitamanas::206.insight: It shifts the reader from seeing devotion as one practice among many to seeing it as the fullest human flowering.

ramacharitamanas::207.verse_sanskrit: रामकथा मंदाकिनी चित्रकूट चित चारु। तुलसी सुभग सनेह बन सिय रघुबीर बिहारु ॥
ramacharitamanas::207.verse_hindi: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि रामकथा मंदाकिनी नदी है, सुंदर (निर्मल) चित्त चित्रकूट है और सुंदर स्नेह ही वन है, जिसमें श्री सीतारामजी विहार करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::207.english_translation: Tulsidas says that the story of Ram is the Mandakini River, a beautiful and pure mind is Chitrakoot, and loving affection is the forest where Sita and Raghubir delight.
ramacharitamanas::207.translation_literal: रामकथा (the story of Ram) / मंदाकिनी (Mandakini) / चित्रकूट (Chitrakoot) / चित (mind) / चारु (beautiful) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / सुभग (lovely) / सनेह (affection) / बन (forest) / सिय (Sita) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / बिहारु (sporting, delighting)
ramacharitamanas::207.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::207.essence: Love makes a home where Ram can dwell.
ramacharitamanas::207.simple_meaning: Ram's story is like a sacred river, a pure and beautiful mind is like Chitrakoot, and loving affection is the forest where Ram and Sita delight together.
ramacharitamanas::207.simple_insight: The divine feels near when the heart is clean and love is alive.
ramacharitamanas::207.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is not just describing a place; he is turning devotion into landscape. Ram's story becomes a river, a pure mind becomes Chitrakoot, and loving affection becomes the forest where Sita and Ram move freely. The whole scene says devotion is a living world.
ramacharitamanas::207.modern_relevance: You open a book after a brutal day, and suddenly the room feels different. The words do not just inform you — they change the atmosphere. That is how love and attention can turn an ordinary place into shelter.
ramacharitamanas::207.insight: It shifts devotion from an idea into a lived environment created by mind and feeling.

ramacharitamanas::208.verse_sanskrit: रामचरित चिंतामति चारू। संत सुमति तिय सुभग सिंगारू॥ जग मंगल गुनग्राम राम के। दानि मुकुति धन धरम धाम के ॥
ramacharitamanas::208.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का चरित्र सुंदर चिन्तामणि है और संतों की सुबुद्धि रूपी स्त्री का सुंदर श्रंगार है। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुण-समूह जगत् का कल्याण करने वाले और मुक्ति, धन, धर्म और परमधाम के देने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::208.english_translation: Ram's story is a beautiful wish-fulfilling jewel. It is the lovely ornament of a wise devotee's heart. Ram's qualities bring welfare to the world and give liberation, wealth, dharma, and the highest home.
ramacharitamanas::208.translation_literal: रामचरित (Ram's story) / चिंतामति (wish-fulfilling jewel) / चारू (beautiful) / संत (saintly) / सुमति (wise understanding) / तिय (woman) / सुभग (beautiful) / सिंगारू (ornament) / जग (world) / मंगल (welfare) / गुनग्राम (group of qualities) / राम के (of Ram) / दानि (giver) / मुकुति (liberation) / धन (wealth) / धरम (dharma) / धाम (abode) / के (of)
ramacharitamanas::208.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::208.essence: Ram's story beautifies the heart and gives every true blessing.
ramacharitamanas::208.simple_meaning: Ram's life story is priceless and beautiful. It adorns a wise heart and brings blessing, freedom, prosperity, dharma, and the highest home.
ramacharitamanas::208.simple_insight: What you love shapes you; Ram's story refines the heart and makes it fruitful.
ramacharitamanas::208.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses in Balkand to praise the story itself. Ram's character is not just something to hear about; it is a treasure that decorates the mind, delights the wise, and gives every real blessing a person can seek.
ramacharitamanas::208.modern_relevance: You open a book late at night after a day that left you scattered. One page steadies you, not because it distracts you, but because it gives your mind something worthy to wear.
ramacharitamanas::208.insight: It shifts attention from entertainment to transformation: Ram's story is meant to adorn and remould the mind.

ramacharitamanas::209.verse_sanskrit: सदगुर ग्यान बिराग जोग के। बिबुध बैद भव भीम रोग के॥ जननि जनक सिय राम प्रेम के। बीज सकल ब्रत धरम नेम के ॥
ramacharitamanas::209.verse_hindi: ज्ञान, वैराग्य और योग के लिए सद्गुरु हैं और संसार रूपी भयंकर रोग का नाश करने के लिए देवताओं के वैद्य (अश्विनीकुमार) के समान हैं। ये श्री सीतारामजी के प्रेम के उत्पन्न करने के लिए माता-पिता हैं और सम्पूर्ण व्रत, धर्म और नियमों के बीज हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::209.english_translation: The true teacher is for wisdom, non-attachment, and yoga, and is like the divine physicians who destroy the terrible disease of worldly existence. He is the mother and father of love for Sita and Ram, and the seed of all vows, duty, and discipline.
ramacharitamanas::209.translation_literal: सदगुर (true teacher) / ग्यान (wisdom) / बिराग (non-attachment) / जोग (yoga) / के (for) / बिबुध (divine) / बैद (physicians) / भव (worldly existence) / भीम (terrible) / रोग (disease) / के (of) / जननि (mother) / जनक (father) / सिय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / प्रेम (love) / के (of) / बीज (seed) / सकल (all) / ब्रत (vows) / धरम (duty) / नेम (discipline) / के (of)
ramacharitamanas::209.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::209.essence: The true teacher heals confusion and plants love at the same time.
ramacharitamanas::209.simple_meaning: A true teacher gives wisdom, non-attachment, and yoga, heals the suffering of worldly life, and awakens love for Sita and Ram. Such a teacher is the source of vows, duty, and discipline.
ramacharitamanas::209.simple_insight: Real guidance does more than inform you. It heals confusion, softens attachment, and turns devotion into practice.
ramacharitamanas::209.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising the true teacher in the middle of a devotional chain of verses. After calling Ram's story a priceless jewel, he now says the teacher gives wisdom, detachment, and discipline, cures the illness of worldly suffering, and awakens love for Sita and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::209.modern_relevance: A mentor who only gives advice leaves you unchanged. The one who steadies your mind, breaks your cravings, and makes your love more disciplined is the one who actually changes your life.
ramacharitamanas::209.insight: It shifts the reader from seeing guidance as information to seeing it as transformation.

ramacharitamanas::210.verse_sanskrit: समन पाप संताप सोक के। प्रिय पालक परलोक लोक के॥ सचिव सुभट भूपति बिचार के। कुंभज लोभ उदधि अपार के ॥
ramacharitamanas::210.verse_hindi: पाप, संताप और शोक का नाश करने वाले तथा इस लोक और परलोक के प्रिय पालन करने वाले हैं। विचार (ज्ञान) रूपी राजा के शूरवीर मंत्री और लोभ रूपी अपार समुद्र के सोखने के लिए अगस्त्य मुनि हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::210.english_translation: The remover of sin, suffering, and grief, and the loving protector of this world and the next. The wise minister of the king called discernment, and Agastya for drying up the vast ocean of greed.
ramacharitamanas::210.translation_literal: समन (remover) / पाप (sin) / संताप (suffering) / सोक (grief) / के (of) / प्रिय (dear) / पालक (protector) / परलोक (other world) / लोक (this world) / के (of) / सचिव (minister) / सुभट (brave warrior) / भूपति (king) / बिचार (discernment) / के (of) / कुंभज (Agastya-born) / लोभ (greed) / उदधि (ocean) / अपार (boundless) / के (of)
ramacharitamanas::210.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::210.essence: Ram removes suffering and greed while protecting every life.
ramacharitamanas::210.simple_meaning: Ram removes suffering and protects people here and beyond. He is also like a brave minister for clear judgment and like Agastya for drying up greed.
ramacharitamanas::210.simple_insight: It feels reassuring to know that Ram does more than save — he also steadies the mind and drains greed.
ramacharitamanas::210.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues his opening praise of Ram by piling up images. Ram is not only beloved and protective in ordinary life and after death; he also supports clear judgment and destroys greed, just as Agastya dried up the ocean.
ramacharitamanas::210.modern_relevance: When anxiety, grief, and wanting all hit at once, you need more than comfort. You need something that calms pain, sharpens judgment, and cuts through greed in one stroke.
ramacharitamanas::210.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as only tender protection to seeing him as the force that clears pain and craving too.

ramacharitamanas::211.verse_sanskrit: काम कोह कलिमल करिगन के। केहरि सावक जन मन बन के॥ अतिथि पूज्य प्रियतम पुरारि के। कामद घन दारिद दवारि के ॥
ramacharitamanas::211.verse_hindi: भक्तों के मन रूपी वन में बसने वाले काम, क्रोध और कलियुग के पाप रूपी हाथियों को मारने के लिए सिंह के बच्चे हैं। शिवजी के पूज्य और प्रियतम अतिथि हैं और दरिद्रता रूपी दावानल के बुझाने के लिए कामना पूर्ण करने वाले मेघ हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::211.english_translation: For the mind-forest of devotees, Ram is a lion cub that kills the elephants of desire, anger, and the sins of the age. He is Shiva's honored and beloved guest, and a cloud that pours fulfillment to quench the wildfire of poverty.
ramacharitamanas::211.translation_literal: काम (desire) / कोह (anger) / कलिमल (sins of the age) / करिगन (elephants) / के (of) / केहरि (lion) / सावक (cub) / जन (people/devotees) / मन (mind) / बन (forest) / के (of) / अतिथि (guest) / पूज्य (worthy of worship) / प्रियतम (most beloved) / पुरारि (Shiva) / के (of) / कामद (wish-fulfilling) / घन (cloud) / दारिद (poverty) / दवारि (forest-fire extinguisher) / के (of)
ramacharitamanas::211.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::211.essence: Ram is the force that burns inner poison and brings relief.
ramacharitamanas::211.simple_meaning: Ram destroys desire, anger, and the corruptions of the age for devoted hearts. He is also dear to Shiva and brings relief like rain after a drought.
ramacharitamanas::211.simple_insight: You can feel protected by what you love most; it meets both your struggle and your need.
ramacharitamanas::211.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram in a devotional chain of epithets. After calling Ram the teacher, healer, and support of life, he now describes Ram as the force that destroys inner enemies, delights Shiva, and ends the burning hardship of poverty.
ramacharitamanas::211.modern_relevance: When your mind feels like a dry forest — one email away from anger, craving, or panic — this verse offers a different center. Ram is the presence that burns away what harms you and brings relief where life feels scorched.
ramacharitamanas::211.insight: It shifts attention from managing symptoms to taking refuge in the presence that removes the root causes.

ramacharitamanas::212.verse_sanskrit: मंत्र महामनि बिषय ब्याल के। मेटत कठिन कुअंक भाल के॥ हरन मोह तम दिनकर कर से। सेवक सालि पाल जलधर से ॥
ramacharitamanas::212.verse_hindi: विषय रूपी साँप का जहर उतारने के लिए मन्त्र और महामणि हैं। ये ललाट पर लिखे हुए कठिनता से मिटने वाले बुरे लेखों (मंद प्रारब्ध) को मिटा देने वाले हैं। अज्ञान रूपी अन्धकार को हरण करने के लिए सूर्य किरणों के समान और सेवक रूपी धान के पालन करने में मेघ के समान हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::212.english_translation: They are the mantra and great jewel for the poison of desire. They erase the hard, bad marks written on the forehead. They are like the sun's rays that remove the darkness of delusion, and like rainclouds that nourish a servant like rice plants.
ramacharitamanas::212.translation_literal: मंत्र (sacred chant) / महामनि (great jewel) / बिषय (desire; sense-objects) / ब्याल (snake) के (of) / मेटत (removing) / कठिन (hard) / कुअंक (bad mark) / भाल (forehead) के (of) / हरन (removing) / मोह (delusion) / तम (darkness) / दिनकर (sun) / कर (ray; hand) से (by) / सेवक (servant) / सालि (rice plant) / पाल (nourishing) / जलधर (raincloud) से (like)
ramacharitamanas::212.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::212.essence: Ram's presence cures craving, clears confusion, and nourishes devotion.
ramacharitamanas::212.simple_meaning: Ram's name and grace remove desire's poison, erase bad fate, and clear away delusion. They also nourish devoted servants like rain nourishes crops.
ramacharitamanas::212.simple_insight: What feels stuck and poisoned can be transformed by devotion and steady care.
ramacharitamanas::212.detailed_meaning: In Tulsidas's praise of Ram, the poet piles up images: poison, dark marks on the forehead, and inner darkness. Ram is not only the cure for delusion; he also nourishes those who serve him, like rain feeding crops.
ramacharitamanas::212.modern_relevance: You open your phone after a brutal day and feel the old spiral start again. One steady practice, one remembered name, one act of trust can interrupt the poison and feed what is still alive in you.
ramacharitamanas::212.insight: It shifts the mind from helplessness before craving to confidence in healing through remembrance and service.

ramacharitamanas::213.verse_sanskrit: अभिमत दानि देवतरु बर से। सेवत सुलभ सुखद हरि हर से॥ सुकबि सरद नभ मन उडगन से। रामभगत जन जीवन धन से ॥
ramacharitamanas::213.verse_hindi: मनोवांछित वस्तु देने में श्रेष्ठ कल्पवृक्ष के समान हैं और सेवा करने में हरि-हर के समान सुलभ और सुख देने वाले हैं। सुकवि रूपी शरद् ऋतु के मन रूपी आकाश को सुशोभित करने के लिए तारागण के समान और श्री रामजी के भक्तों के तो जीवन धन ही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::213.english_translation: They are like the finest wish-fulfilling tree, giving whatever is desired. Serving them is easy and brings joy, like serving Hari and Hara. For good poets, they are like stars in the autumn sky. For Ram's devotees, they are the very wealth of life.
ramacharitamanas::213.translation_literal: अभिमत (desired) / दानि (giving) / देवतरु (divine tree) / बर (best, excellent) / से (like) / सेवत (serving) / सुलभ (easy to approach) / सुखद (joy-giving) / हरि (Hari) / हर (Hara) / से (like) / सुकबि (good poets) / सरद (autumn) / नभ (sky) / मन (mind) / उडगन (stars) / से (like) / रामभगत (Ram-devotees) / जन (people) / जीवन (life) / धन (wealth) / से (like)
ramacharitamanas::213.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::213.essence: Ram is the easy giver who becomes a devotee’s true wealth.
ramacharitamanas::213.simple_meaning: Ram and Shiva are easy to approach, grant what is needed, and become the greatest treasure for poets and devotees.
ramacharitamanas::213.simple_insight: Devotion feels rich because what you love starts to feel like life’s real wealth.
ramacharitamanas::213.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram in the Balkand frame, piling up images to show how completely Ram satisfies different kinds of people. The verse is not a scene in the story so much as a devotional portrait: Ram becomes easy access, beauty, and the deepest treasure for those who love him.
ramacharitamanas::213.modern_relevance: You open your phone after a draining day and see the one message that steadies you. Some presences do not demand performance; they simply restore you. That is the feeling Tulsidas gives to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::213.insight: It shifts devotion from duty to delight: the beloved becomes both easy to approach and enough to sustain you.

ramacharitamanas::214.verse_sanskrit: सकल सुकृत फल भूरि भोग से। जग हित निरुपधि साधु लोग से॥ सेवक मन मानस मराल से। पावन गंग तरंग माल से ॥
ramacharitamanas::214.verse_hindi: सम्पूर्ण पुण्यों के फल महान भोगों के समान हैं। जगत का छलरहित (यथार्थ) हित करने में साधु-संतों के समान हैं। सेवकों के मन रूपी मानसरोवर के लिए हंस के समान और पवित्र करने में गंगाजी की तरंगमालाओं के समान हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::214.english_translation: The fruits of all good deeds are like great pleasures. The truly selfless saints are the world’s real welfare. For a servant’s mind, they are like swans on Manasarovar, and like a garland of Ganga’s waves that purifies everything.
ramacharitamanas::214.translation_literal: सकल (all) / सुकृत (good deeds) / फल (fruit) / भूरि (great, abundant) / भोग (pleasures, enjoyments) / से (like) / जग (world) / हित (welfare) / निरुपधि (without deceit, selfless) / साधु (saints) / लोग (people) / से (like) / सेवक (servant) / मन (mind) / मानस (Manasarovar) / मराल (swan) / से (like) / पावन (purifying) / गंग (Ganga) / तरंग (waves) / माल (garland, row) / से (like)
ramacharitamanas::214.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::214.essence: Selfless saints purify the mind the way sacred waters cleanse everything they touch.
ramacharitamanas::214.simple_meaning: Good people are like pure, cleansing water for the mind. They give real welfare without hidden motives and lift a devotee’s heart like swans on a clear lake.
ramacharitamanas::214.simple_insight: You feel steadied by good company; it quietly cleans the mind and points it toward what is pure.
ramacharitamanas::214.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising the qualities of Ram’s devotees and saintly people in a devotional chain of comparisons. After saying Ram is like a wish-fulfilling tree and easily gives refuge, he now shows what true saints do for others: they purify, guide, and benefit without selfishness.
ramacharitamanas::214.modern_relevance: A friend who never competes with you, never gossips, and somehow leaves your mind lighter after every conversation — that is the kind of presence this verse honors.
ramacharitamanas::214.insight: It shifts attention from impressive achievement to the quiet power of selfless companionship.

ramacharitamanas::215.verse_sanskrit: कुपथ कुतरक कुचालि कलि कपट दंभ पाषंड। दहन राम गुन ग्राम जिमि इंधन अनल प्रचंड ॥
ramacharitamanas::215.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के गुणों के समूह कुमार्ग, कुतर्क, कुचाल और कलियुग के कपट, दम्भ और पाखण्ड को जलाने के लिए वैसे ही हैं, जैसे ईंधन के लिए प्रचण्ड अग्नि ॥
ramacharitamanas::215.english_translation: Sri Ram’s qualities burn away wrong paths, crooked reasoning, bad conduct, and the deceit, pride, and hypocrisy of Kali Yuga, just as a fierce fire burns fuel.
ramacharitamanas::215.translation_literal: कुपथ (wrong path) / कुतरक (crooked reasoning) / कुचालि (bad conduct) / कलि (Kali Yuga) / कपट (deceit) / दंभ (pride) / पाषंड (hypocrisy) / दहन (burning) / राम गुन ग्राम (the cluster of Ram’s qualities) / जिमि (just as) / इंधन (fuel) / अनल (fire) / प्रचंड (fierce)
ramacharitamanas::215.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::215.essence: Ram’s qualities do what fire does to fuel: they consume falsehood completely.
ramacharitamanas::215.simple_meaning: Ram’s virtues destroy false paths, bad reasoning, and the pride and hypocrisy of the age, just as fire consumes dry fuel.
ramacharitamanas::215.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that truth does not merely resist falsehood — it burns it away.
ramacharitamanas::215.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram at the end of a chain of comparisons. After calling Ram’s devotees and qualities precious and life-giving, he says Ram’s virtues act like a blazing fire in Kali Yuga, consuming crooked conduct, deceptive thinking, and spiritual pretence.
ramacharitamanas::215.modern_relevance: You open a feed full of confident nonsense, half-truths, and polished performance. One clear standard cuts through it all: does this make you more honest, or more performative?
ramacharitamanas::215.insight: It shifts attention from arguing with falsehood to strengthening the qualities that naturally dissolve it.

ramacharitamanas::216.verse_sanskrit: रामचरित राकेस कर सरिस सुखद सब काहु। सज्जन कुमुद चकोर चित हित बिसेषि बड़ लाहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::216.verse_hindi: रामचरित्र पूर्णिमा के चन्द्रमा की किरणों के समान सभी को सुख देने वाले हैं, परन्तु सज्जन रूपी कुमुदिनी और चकोर के चित्त के लिए तो विशेष हितकारी और महान लाभदायक हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::216.english_translation: Ram's story is like the moon's rays, giving joy to everyone, but especially to the lotus-hearted and the cakora-hearted, for whom it brings great benefit.
ramacharitamanas::216.translation_literal: रामचरित (Ram's story) / राकेस (the moon) / कर (rays) / सरिस (like) / सुखद (giving joy) / सब काहु (to everyone) / सज्जन (virtuous people) / कुमुद (lotus) / चकोर (cakora bird) / चित (mind) / हित (beneficial) / बिसेषि (especially) / बड़ (great) / लाहु (gain)
ramacharitamanas::216.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::216.essence: Ram's story shines on everyone, but devotion receives its fullest light.
ramacharitamanas::216.simple_meaning: Ram's story brings joy to everyone, like moonlight. But it brings the deepest benefit to noble hearts that are already turned toward him.
ramacharitamanas::216.simple_insight: The same truth lands differently depending on the heart receiving it.
ramacharitamanas::216.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has just compared Ram's qualities to fire that burns away corruption. Now he turns to the opposite image: Ram's story as moonlight. It comforts all people, but it becomes especially nourishing for the devoted, who receive it as their own delight.
ramacharitamanas::216.modern_relevance: A song plays in a crowded room and everyone hears it, but one person goes still because it matches something already alive inside them. Ram's story works like that: universal, yet deepest for the receptive heart.
ramacharitamanas::216.insight: It shifts attention from mere exposure to inward readiness: the same sacred story can comfort all, but transform the devoted most.

ramacharitamanas::217.verse_sanskrit: कीन्हि प्रस्न जेहि भाँति भवानी। जेहि बिधि संकर कहा बखानी॥ सो सब हेतु कहब मैं गाई। कथा प्रबंध बिचित्र बनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::217.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार श्री पार्वतीजी ने श्री शिवजी से प्रश्न किया और जिस प्रकार से श्री शिवजी ने विस्तार से उसका उत्तर कहा, वह सब कारण मैं विचित्र कथा की रचना करके गाकर कहूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::217.english_translation: I will sing and tell the whole cause, just as Bhavani asked and Shiva explained, by composing this wondrous narrative.
ramacharitamanas::217.translation_literal: कीन्हि (did) / प्रस्न (question) / जेहि भाँति (in the way) / भवानी (Bhavani, Parvati) / जेहि बिधि (in the way) / संकर (Shankar, Shiva) / कहा (said) / बखानी (explained) / सो (that) / सब (all) / हेतु (cause) / कहब (I will tell) / मैं (I) / गाई (singing) / कथा (story) / प्रबंध (composition) / बिचित्र (wondrous) / बनाई (made)
ramacharitamanas::217.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::217.essence: The story will be told by following the divine question and answer.
ramacharitamanas::217.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he will retell the whole story exactly as Parvati asked and Shiva answered, shaping it into a beautiful, sung narrative.
ramacharitamanas::217.simple_insight: A sacred story can be retold with devotion and artistry without losing its source.
ramacharitamanas::217.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening the frame of the Ramcharitmanas. He promises to sing the story the way Parvati questioned Shiva and the way Shiva answered her, turning that divine conversation into a crafted narrative for listeners.
ramacharitamanas::217.modern_relevance: A teacher says, “Let me tell you the whole backstory,” and suddenly the scattered pieces make sense. Good explanation doesn’t flatten the truth; it gives it a form people can actually receive.
ramacharitamanas::217.insight: It shifts attention from isolated events to the larger pattern that gives them meaning.

ramacharitamanas::218.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं यह कथा सुनी नहिं होई। जनि आचरजु करै सुनि सोई॥ कथा अलौकिक सुनहिं जे ग्यानी। नहिं आचरजु करहिं अस जानी ॥ रामकथा कै मिति जग नाहीं। असि प्रतीति तिन्ह के मन माहीं॥ नाना भाँति राम अवतारा। रामायन सत कोटि अपारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::218.verse_hindi: जिसने यह कथा पहले न सुनी हो, वह इसे सुनकर आश्चर्य न करे। जो ज्ञानी इस विचित्र कथा को सुनते हैं, वे यह जानकर आश्चर्य नहीं करते कि संसार में रामकथा की कोई सीमा नहीं है (रामकथा अनंत है)। उनके मन में ऐसा विश्वास रहता है। नाना प्रकार से श्री रामचन्द्रजी के अवतार हुए हैं और सौ करोड़ तथा अपार रामायण हैं॥2-3॥
ramacharitamanas::218.english_translation: One who has not heard this story before should not be astonished on hearing it. Wise listeners do not marvel, knowing that Ram's story has no limit in the world. In their hearts they hold this conviction. Ram appears in many forms, and there are countless, boundless Ramayanas.
ramacharitamanas::218.translation_literal: जेहिं (by whom) / यह (this) / कथा (story) / सुनी (heard) / नहिं (not) / होई (has been) / जनि (do not) / आचरजु (wonder) / करै (do) / सुनि (having heard) / सोई (that one)॥ / कथा (story) / अलौकिक (beyond the ordinary) / सुनहिं (hear) / जे (who) / ग्यानी (the wise) / नहिं (not) / आचरजु (wonder) / करहिं (do) / अस (thus) / जानी (knowing) ॥ / रामकथा (story of Ram) / कै (of) / मिति (limit) / जग (world) / नाहीं (is not) / असि (such) / प्रतीति (conviction) / तिन्ह (their) / के (of) / मन (mind) / माहीं (within) ॥ / नाना (many) / भाँति (kinds) / राम (Ram) / अवतारा (incarnations) / रामायन (Ramayanas) / सत (hundred) / कोटि (crores) / अपारा (boundless) ॥
ramacharitamanas::218.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::218.essence: Ram's story is too vast for one telling.
ramacharitamanas::218.simple_meaning: Ram's story is endless, so a wise listener does not treat its wonder as strange. The divine appears in countless forms, and no single telling can contain it.
ramacharitamanas::218.simple_insight: You can stop trying to fit the sacred into one neat frame.
ramacharitamanas::218.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening the story he has promised to retell after Shiva's explanation to Parvati. He warns new listeners not to be startled by the vastness of Ram's tale, because the wise already know it cannot be contained in one version.
ramacharitamanas::218.modern_relevance: You hear one person describe a life-changing event, then another tells it differently, and both are sincere. The mind relaxes when it stops demanding one perfect account of what is ultimately vast.
ramacharitamanas::218.insight: It shifts the reader from fixed expectations to reverent openness toward many tellings of the same sacred reality.

ramacharitamanas::219.verse_sanskrit: कलपभेद हरिचरित सुहाए। भाँति अनेक मुनीसन्ह गाए॥ करिअ न संसय अस उर आनी। सुनिअ कथा सादर रति मानी ॥
