ramacharitamanas::219.verse_hindi: कल्पभेद के अनुसार श्री हरि के सुंदर चरित्रों को मुनीश्वरों ने अनेकों प्रकार से गया है। हृदय में ऐसा विचार कर संदेह न कीजिए और आदर सहित प्रेम से इस कथा को सुनिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::219.english_translation: In different ages, the lovely deeds of Hari have been sung by sages in many ways. Keep no doubt in your heart; listen to this story with reverence and loving attention.
ramacharitamanas::219.translation_literal: कलपभेद (according to age-difference) / हरिचरित (Hari's deeds) / सुहाए (beautiful) / भाँति अनेक (many kinds) / मुनीसन्ह (by sages) / गाए (sung)॥ / करिअ (do) / न (not) / संसय (doubt) / अस (thus) / उर (in the heart) / आनी (bringing) / सुनिअ (listen) / कथा (story) / सादर (with reverence) / रति (loving attention) / मानी (holding)
ramacharitamanas::219.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::219.essence: Many tellings can still carry one living truth.
ramacharitamanas::219.simple_meaning: Ram's stories have been told in many forms by sages across ages. Do not doubt them; listen respectfully and with loving attention.
ramacharitamanas::219.simple_insight: You can soften your resistance and let the story work on you.
ramacharitamanas::219.detailed_meaning: After explaining that different tellings of Ram's story exist, the narrator reassures the listener that this variety is natural. The point is not to argue over versions, but to receive Ram's deeds with respect and trust.
ramacharitamanas::219.modern_relevance: You open three tabs, compare five opinions, and still feel stuck. This verse asks for a different move: stop demanding certainty first, and let reverent attention do its work.
ramacharitamanas::219.insight: It shifts the mind from skepticism and comparison to receptive listening.

ramacharitamanas::220.verse_sanskrit: राम अनंत अनंत गुन अमित कथा बिस्तार। सुनि आचरजु न मानिहहिं जिन्ह कें बिमल बिचार ॥
ramacharitamanas::220.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी अनन्त हैं, उनके गुण भी अनन्त हैं और उनकी कथाओं का विस्तार भी असीम है। अतएव जिनके विचार निर्मल हैं, वे इस कथा को सुनकर आश्चर्य नहीं मानेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::220.english_translation: Ram is endless, his qualities are endless, and the spread of his story is endless. Those with pure understanding will not be surprised to hear it.
ramacharitamanas::220.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / अनंत (endless) / अनंत (endless) / गुन (qualities) / अमित (immeasurable) / कथा (story) / बिस्तार (expansion, spread) / सुनि (hearing) / आचरजु (surprise) / न (not) / मानिहहिं (will regard) / जिन्ह कें (whose) / बिमल (pure) / बिचार (understanding, discernment)
ramacharitamanas::220.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::220.essence: Pure understanding makes room for Ram's endlessness.
ramacharitamanas::220.simple_meaning: Ram is limitless, so his qualities and stories cannot be fully counted. A clear mind accepts that without surprise.
ramacharitamanas::220.simple_insight: You stop demanding that the infinite fit inside your small expectations.
ramacharitamanas::220.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is closing a reflection on Ram's story in Balkand. After saying that wise people should not doubt these wondrous accounts, he states the reason: Ram's nature, virtues, and story are boundless. The verse widens the reader's mind before the narration continues.
ramacharitamanas::220.modern_relevance: You open a book, a biography, or a loved one's story and keep trying to reduce it to one neat explanation. But some lives cannot be boxed in. Clear seeing begins when you stop expecting the infinite to feel ordinary.
ramacharitamanas::220.insight: It shifts the mind from skepticism about wonder to receptivity toward what cannot be measured.

ramacharitamanas::221.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि सब संसय करि दूरी। सिर धरि गुर पद पंकज धूरी॥ पुनि सबही बिनवउँ कर जोरी। करत कथा जेहिं लाग न खोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::221.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार सब संदेहों को दूर करके और श्री गुरुजी के चरणकमलों की रज को सिर पर धारण करके मैं पुनः हाथ जोड़कर सबकी विनती करता हूँ, जिससे कथा की रचना में कोई दोष स्पर्श न करने पावे ॥
ramacharitamanas::221.english_translation: In this way, clearing away all doubts, I place the dust of the guru's lotus feet on my head. I again fold my hands and ask everyone to listen, so that no flaw may touch this telling of the story.
ramacharitamanas::221.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / सब (all) / संसय (doubts) / करि (having done) / दूरी (far away) / सिर (head) / धरि (placing) / गुर (guru's) / पद (feet) / पंकज (lotus) / धूरी (dust) / पुनि (again) / सबही (everyone) / बिनवउँ (I request) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined) / करत (doing) / कथा (story) / जेहिं (so that) / लाग (touches) / न (not) / खोरी (flaw)
ramacharitamanas::221.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::221.essence: Humility clears the way for a faultless telling.
ramacharitamanas::221.simple_meaning: The speaker clears doubt, bows to the teacher, and asks for respectful attention so the telling remains free of fault.
ramacharitamanas::221.simple_insight: Humility makes room for a cleaner hearing. When the ego softens, the story can be received without distortion.
ramacharitamanas::221.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening his telling of Ram's story. After clearing away doubt, he bows to the guru and asks the listeners to receive the कथा with care. This is the formal threshold before the sacred narrative begins.
ramacharitamanas::221.modern_relevance: Before a difficult conversation, you take a breath, drop the urge to sound clever, and ask to be understood clearly. That humility keeps the whole exchange from turning messy.
ramacharitamanas::221.insight: It teaches you to begin sacred or serious speech with humility, respect, and a clean intention.

ramacharitamanas::222.verse_sanskrit: सादर सिवहि नाइ अब माथा। बरनउँ बिसद राम गुन गाथा॥ संबत सोरह सै एकतीसा। करउँ कथा हरि पद धरि सीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::222.verse_hindi: अब मैं आदरपूर्वक श्री शिवजी को सिर नवाकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुणों की निर्मल कथा कहता हूँ। श्री हरि के चरणों पर सिर रखकर संवत् 1631 में इस कथा का आरंभ करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::222.english_translation: I bow to Shiva with respect and then sing the pure story of Ram's virtues. In 1631, I begin this tale with my head at Hari's feet.
ramacharitamanas::222.translation_literal: सादर (with respect) / सिवहि (to Shiva) / नाइ (bowing) / अब (now) / माथा (head) / बरनउँ (I describe) / बिसद (pure, clear) / राम (Ram) / गुन (virtues) / गाथा (story, song) / संबत (year) / सोरह सै (sixteen hundred) / एकतीसा (thirty-one) / करउँ (I do) / कथा (story) / हरि (Hari) / पद (feet) / धरि (placing) / सीसा (head)
ramacharitamanas::222.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::222.essence: Reverence comes before any true telling.
ramacharitamanas::222.simple_meaning: The poet begins by bowing to Shiva and placing his head at Hari's feet before telling Ram's pure story.
ramacharitamanas::222.simple_insight: A true beginning is an act of reverence, not self-assertion.
ramacharitamanas::222.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas opens the Ramcharitmanas after clearing doubt and honoring the teacher. He bows first to Shiva, then to Ram, marking this as a sacred telling rather than ordinary poetry. The verse sets the devotional tone for the whole work.
ramacharitamanas::222.modern_relevance: Before you speak, post, or present, you pause and remember what you owe to what is larger than your own voice. The best work begins in humility.
ramacharitamanas::222.insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to reverent offering.

ramacharitamanas::223.verse_sanskrit: नौमी भौम बार मधुमासा। अवधपुरीं यह चरित प्रकासा॥ जेहि दिन राम जनम श्रुति गावहिं। तीरथ सकल जहाँ चलि आवहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::223.verse_hindi: चैत्र मास की नवमी तिथि मंगलवार को श्री अयोध्याजी में यह चरित्र प्रकाशित हुआ। जिस दिन श्री रामजी का जन्म होता है, वेद कहते हैं कि उस दिन सारे तीर्थ वहाँ (श्री अयोध्याजी में) चले आते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::223.english_translation: On the ninth day of the bright half of Chaitra, on a Tuesday, this event was revealed in Ayodhya. The Vedas say that on the day Ram is born, all sacred places come there.
ramacharitamanas::223.translation_literal: नौमी (ninth day) / भौम बार (Tuesday) / मधुमासा (in the month of spring) / अवधपुरीं (in Ayodhya city) / यह चरित (this event/story) / प्रकासा (became manifest) / जेहि दिन (on which day) / राम जनम (Ram's birth) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / गावहिं (sing) / तीरथ सकल (all sacred places) / जहाँ (where) / चलि आवहिं (come walking)
ramacharitamanas::223.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::223.essence: Ram's birth turns Ayodhya into the centre of all holiness.
ramacharitamanas::223.simple_meaning: Ram's birth is placed on an auspicious day in Ayodhya, and the verse says all sacred places gather there for it.
ramacharitamanas::223.simple_insight: Some moments feel so holy that everything else seems to come and honour them.
ramacharitamanas::223.detailed_meaning: The birth story is opening in Ayodhya. Tulsidas marks the exact auspicious day and says Ram's arrival is so sacred that all holy places themselves come to witness it. It prepares the reader for a birth that changes the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::223.modern_relevance: A family waits in a hospital corridor for a child to be born, and the room feels larger than the building. Some arrivals make ordinary time feel consecrated.
ramacharitamanas::223.insight: It shifts attention from an ordinary birth date to a world-changing sacred arrival.

ramacharitamanas::224.verse_sanskrit: असुर नाग खग नर मुनि देवा। आइ करहिं रघुनायक सेवा॥ जन्म महोत्सव रचहिं सुजाना। करहिं राम कल कीरति गाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::224.verse_hindi: असुर-नाग, पक्षी, मनुष्य, मुनि और देवता सब अयोध्याजी में आकर श्री रघुनाथजी की सेवा करते हैं। बुद्धिमान लोग जन्म का महोत्सव मनाते हैं और श्री रामजी की सुंदर कीर्ति का गान करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::224.english_translation: Asuras, serpents, birds, humans, sages, and radiant beings all come to serve Raghunath. Wise people celebrate his birth festival and sing the beautiful glory of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::224.translation_literal: असुर (asuras) / नाग (serpents) / खग (birds) / नर (humans) / मुनि (sages) / देवा (radiant beings) / आइ (coming) / करहिं (do) / रघुनायक (Raghunath) / सेवा (service) / जन्म (birth) / महोत्सव (great festival) / रचहिं (arrange) / सुजाना (the wise) / करहिं (do) / राम (Ram) / कल (beautiful) / कीरति (glory) / गाना (singing)
ramacharitamanas::224.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::224.essence: Ram's birth draws every being into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::224.simple_meaning: All kinds of beings gather in Ayodhya to serve Ram and celebrate his birth with song and festivity.
ramacharitamanas::224.simple_insight: Joy becomes shared when something sacred arrives. The whole world seems to lean toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::224.detailed_meaning: Ram has just been born in Ayodhya, and the celebration spills beyond ordinary human limits. Beings from every realm come to honor him, while the wise mark his birth with festival and song. This verse expands the scene of his arrival.
ramacharitamanas::224.modern_relevance: A room fills with people for a newborn’s naming ceremony, and even the quiet ones are smiling. Some moments make everyone softer, kinder, and strangely united.
ramacharitamanas::224.insight: It shifts attention from private celebration to a shared response to the divine presence.

ramacharitamanas::225.verse_sanskrit: मज्जहिं सज्जन बृंद बहु पावन सरजू नीर। जपहिं राम धरि ध्यान उर सुंदर स्याम सरीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::225.verse_hindi: सज्जनों के बहुत से समूह उस दिन श्री सरयूजी के पवित्र जल में स्नान करते हैं और हृदय में सुंदर श्याम शरीर श्री रघुनाथजी का ध्यान करके उनके नाम का जप करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::225.english_translation: Many noble people bathe in the holy waters of the Sarayu and, holding the beautiful dark form of Ram in their hearts, chant his name.
ramacharitamanas::225.translation_literal: मज्जहिं (bathe) / सज्जन (noble people) / बृंद (groups) / बहु (many) / पावन (holy) / सरजू (Sarayu) / नीर (water) / जपहिं (chant) / राम (Ram) / धरि (holding) / ध्यान (meditation) / उर (heart) / सुंदर (beautiful) / स्याम (dark) / सरीर (form/body)
ramacharitamanas::225.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::225.essence: Purity deepens when bathing is joined with loving remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::225.simple_meaning: Many good people bathe in the holy Sarayu and keep Ram in their hearts while chanting his name.
ramacharitamanas::225.simple_insight: Sacred remembrance turns a river bath into devotion, not just ritual.
ramacharitamanas::225.detailed_meaning: On Ram’s birth day in Ayodhya, crowds gather at the Sarayu. Noble people bathe in its waters and hold Ram’s beautiful dark form in their hearts while repeating his name. The verse adds to the festival atmosphere, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::225.modern_relevance: At dawn, before the city wakes, someone stands in a river or under a shower, quietly repeating a beloved name. The act is ordinary; the attention turns it into reverence.
ramacharitamanas::225.insight: It shifts ritual from outward cleaning to inward remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::226.verse_sanskrit: दरस परस मज्जन अरु पाना। हरइ पाप कह बेद पुराना॥ नदी पुनीत अमित महिमा अति। कहि न सकइ सारदा बिमल मति ॥
ramacharitamanas::226.verse_hindi: वेद-पुराण कहते हैं कि श्री सरयूजी का दर्शन, स्पर्श, स्नान और जलपान पापों को हरता है। यह नदी बड़ी ही पवित्र है, इसकी महिमा अनन्त है, जिसे विमल बुद्धि वाली सरस्वतीजी भी नहीं कह सकतीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::226.english_translation: The sight, touch, bathing in, and drinking of the Sarayu remove sin, say the ancient Vedas and Puranas. This river is sacred, its greatness is endless, and even pure-minded Saraswati cannot fully describe it.
ramacharitamanas::226.translation_literal: दरस (sight) / परस (touch) / मज्जन (bathing) / अरु (and) / पाना (drinking) / हरइ (removes) / पाप (sin) / कह (say) / बेद (Vedas) / पुराना (Puranas) / नदी (river) / पुनीत (sacred) / अमित (immeasurable) / महिमा (glory) / अति (very) / कहि न सकइ (cannot say) / सारदा (Saraswati) / बिमल (pure) / मति (mind/intellect)
ramacharitamanas::226.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::226.essence: Presence near the sacred can cleanse what speech cannot reach.
ramacharitamanas::226.simple_meaning: The Sarayu is so sacred that even seeing, touching, bathing in, or drinking from it is said to remove wrongdoing. Its greatness cannot be fully described.
ramacharitamanas::226.simple_insight: Some places carry a holiness that feels larger than language, as if presence itself cleanses you.
ramacharitamanas::226.detailed_meaning: As Ayodhya prepares for Ram's birth, the narration turns to the Sarayu river that flows beside the city. The verse praises its sacred power and says even Saraswati cannot fully describe its greatness, setting the stage for Ram's holy arrival.
ramacharitamanas::226.modern_relevance: You stand beside a river at dawn, tired and carrying too much. The water, the silence, the cold air all feel cleansing before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::226.insight: It shifts attention from explanation to reverence, showing that some realities are meant to be encountered, not fully measured.

ramacharitamanas::227.verse_sanskrit: राम धामदा पुरी सुहावनि। लोक समस्त बिदित अति पावनि॥ चारि खानि जग जीव अपारा। अवध तजें तनु नहिं संसारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::227.verse_hindi: यह शोभायमान अयोध्यापुरी श्री रामचन्द्रजी के परमधाम की देने वाली है, सब लोकों में प्रसिद्ध है और अत्यन्त पवित्र है। जगत में (अण्डज, स्वेदज, उद्भिज्ज और जरायुज) चार खानि (प्रकार) के अनन्त जीव हैं, इनमें से जो कोई भी अयोध्याजी में शरीर छोड़ते हैं, वे फिर संसार में नहीं आते (जन्म-मृत्यु के चक्कर से छूटकर भगवान के परमधाम में निवास करते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::227.english_translation: Beautiful Ayodhya is the abode that grants Ram's supreme dwelling. It is renowned in all worlds and supremely pure. Of the countless beings born in the four forms of life, whoever leaves the body in Ayodhya does not return to the cycle of rebirth.
ramacharitamanas::227.translation_literal: राम धामदा (giver of Ram's abode) / पुरी (city) / सुहावनि (beautiful)। लोक (worlds) / समस्त (all) / बिदित (known) / अति (very) / पावनि (pure)॥ चारि (four) / खानि (forms of birth) / जग (world) / जीव (living beings) / अपारा (countless)। अवध (Ayodhya) / तजें (leaving) / तनु (body) / नहिं (not) / संसारा (cycle of rebirth) ॥
ramacharitamanas::227.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::227.essence: A pure place can end the cycle of return.
ramacharitamanas::227.simple_meaning: Ayodhya is described as a supremely pure city of Ram. Even beings from any of the four kinds of life who die there do not return to rebirth.
ramacharitamanas::227.simple_insight: There is relief in a place where the cycle ends and release is possible.
ramacharitamanas::227.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ayodhya after describing the sacred Sarayu. He says the city is so pure and so tied to Ram that even beings from any form of life who die there are freed from return to rebirth. The passage deepens Ayodhya into a threshold of liberation.
ramacharitamanas::227.modern_relevance: A place can change the shape of your mind so completely that old habits lose their grip. Some spaces feel like a clean break from the life you were repeating.
ramacharitamanas::227.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary geography to sacred presence as a force that ends recurrence.

ramacharitamanas::228.verse_sanskrit: सब बिधि पुरी मनोहर जानी। सकल सिद्धिप्रद मंगल खानी॥ बिमल कथा कर कीन्ह अरंभा। सुनत नसाहिं काम मद दंभा ॥
ramacharitamanas::228.verse_hindi: इस अयोध्यापुरी को सब प्रकार से मनोहर, सब सिद्धियों की देने वाली और कल्याण की खान समझकर मैंने इस निर्मल कथा का आरंभ किया, जिसके सुनने से काम, मद और दम्भ नष्ट हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::228.english_translation: Knowing Ayodhya to be lovely in every way, the giver of all attainments and a mine of auspiciousness, I begin this pure story, whose hearing destroys desire, pride, and arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::228.translation_literal: सब बिधि (in every way) / पुरी (city) / मनोहर (beautiful) / जानी (knowing) / सकल (all) / सिद्धि-प्रद (giver of attainments) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / खानी (mine) / बिमल (pure) / कथा (story) / कर (of) / कीन्ह (made) / अरंभा (beginning) / सुनत (on hearing) / नसाहिं (are destroyed) / काम (desire) / मद (pride) / दंभा (arrogance)
ramacharitamanas::228.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::228.essence: A pure story can wash away desire, pride, and arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::228.simple_meaning: Ayodhya is described as beautiful, auspicious, and full of blessings. The pure story begins there, and hearing it destroys desire, pride, and arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::228.simple_insight: A sacred story can quiet the inner distortions that keep us restless and self-important.
ramacharitamanas::228.detailed_meaning: The narrator turns from the holy river to Ayodhya, Ram's city, and sets up the story as a cleansing force. Before the birth narrative fully begins, Tulsidas frames this place and this tale as spiritually powerful enough to weaken desire, pride, and arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::228.modern_relevance: You open a book late at night because your mind feels crowded with wanting, comparison, and self-importance. Some stories do not entertain you; they quietly strip those layers away.
ramacharitamanas::228.insight: It shifts reading from entertainment to purification, treating sacred कथा as something that reforms the inner state.

ramacharitamanas::229.verse_sanskrit: रामचरितमानस एहि नामा। सुनत श्रवन पाइअ बिश्रामा॥ मन करि बिषय अनल बन जरई। होई सुखी जौं एहिं सर परई ॥
ramacharitamanas::229.verse_hindi: इसका नाम रामचरित मानस है, जिसके कानों से सुनते ही शांति मिलती है। मन रूपी हाथी विषय रूपी दावानल में जल रहा है, वह यदि इस रामचरित मानस रूपी सरोवर में आ पड़े तो सुखी हो जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::229.english_translation: This is called Ramcharitmanas. Hearing it brings rest to the ears. The mind, like an elephant, burns in the forest fire of desire; if it falls into this lake, it becomes happy.
ramacharitamanas::229.translation_literal: रामचरितमानस (Ramcharitmanas) / एहि (this) / नामा (name) / सुनत (on hearing) / श्रवन (the ears) / पाइअ (is obtained) / बिश्रामा (rest) / मन (mind) / करि (as) / बिषय (sense-objects) / अनल (fire) / बन (forest) / जरई (burns) / होई (becomes) / सुखी (happy) / जौं (if) / एहिं (in this) / सर (lake) / परई (falls)
ramacharitamanas::229.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::229.essence: Ram's story cools the mind that desire has burned.
ramacharitamanas::229.simple_meaning: Hearing this sacred story brings calm. A mind burned by desire can find relief and happiness in it.
ramacharitamanas::229.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that rest is available when the mind feels consumed.
ramacharitamanas::229.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas opens his sacred retelling by naming it Ramcharitmanas. He says it is not just a story but a cooling lake for the mind, especially when desire has set it on fire. The whole work begins as medicine.
ramacharitamanas::229.modern_relevance: You are doomscrolling at 1:13 a.m., mind racing after a hard day. One quiet, faithful reading can feel like stepping out of heat into shade.
ramacharitamanas::229.insight: It reframes sacred listening as mental refuge, not entertainment.

ramacharitamanas::230.verse_sanskrit: रामचरितमानस मुनि भावन। बिरचेउ संभु सुहावन पावन॥ त्रिबिध दोष दुख दारिद दावन। कलि कुचालि कुलि कलुष नसावन ॥
ramacharitamanas::230.verse_hindi: यह रामचरित मानस मुनियों का प्रिय है, इस सुहावने और पवित्र मानस की शिवजी ने रचना की। यह तीनों प्रकार के दोषों, दुःखों और दरिद्रता को तथा कलियुग की कुचालों और सब पापों का नाश करने वाला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::230.english_translation: The Ramcharitmanas is dear to sages. Shiva composed this lovely, purifying मानस. It destroys the three kinds of faults, suffering, poverty, crooked conduct in the age of Kali, and all stains.
ramacharitamanas::230.translation_literal: रामचरितमानस (the story of Ram as a sacred mind-text) / मुनि (sages) / भावन (dear to the heart) / बिरचेउ (composed) / संभु (Shiva) / सुहावन (lovely) / पावन (purifying) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / दोष (faults) / दुख (suffering) / दारिद (poverty) / दावन (burning up) / कलि (the age of Kali) / कुचालि (crooked conduct) / कुलि (family stains) / कलुष (impurity) / नसावन (destroying)
ramacharitamanas::230.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::230.essence: Sacred hearing can burn away what distorts a life.
ramacharitamanas::230.simple_meaning: The Ramcharitmanas is loved by sages, beautifully composed by Shiva, and powerful enough to burn away faults, suffering, poverty, bad conduct, and impurity.
ramacharitamanas::230.simple_insight: A sacred story can cleanse the mind more deeply than argument.
ramacharitamanas::230.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is introducing his work as Shiva's own beloved composition, treasured by sages and meant to purify the listener. This verse is not yet the full argument; it is a praise of the text's spiritual power before the next line explains how Shiva kept it in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::230.modern_relevance: You open a book after a brutal day, not for information but for relief. Some words do more than explain; they settle the mind, soften shame, and clear the dust of a hard season.
ramacharitamanas::230.insight: It shifts reading from entertainment to purification, treating sacred words as active medicine for the mind.

ramacharitamanas::231.verse_sanskrit: रचि महेस निज मानस राखा। पाइ सुसमउ सिवा सन भाषा॥ तातें रामचरितमानस बर। धरेउ नाम हियँ हेरि हरषि हर ॥
ramacharitamanas::231.verse_hindi: श्री महादेवजी ने इसको रचकर अपने मन में रखा था और सुअवसर पाकर पार्वतीजी से कहा। इसी से शिवजी ने इसको अपने हृदय में देखकर और प्रसन्न होकर इसका सुंदर 'रामचरित मानस' नाम रखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::231.english_translation: Shri Mahadev composed it and kept it in his own mind; when the right moment came, he spoke it to Parvati. Therefore Shiva, seeing it in his heart and rejoicing, gave it the beautiful name 'Ramcharitmanas.'
ramacharitamanas::231.translation_literal: रचि (composing) / महेस (Shiva) / निज (own) / मानस (mind) / राखा (kept) / पाइ (having found) / सुसमउ (good time) / सिवा (to Parvati) / सन (with) / भाषा (spoke) / तातें (therefore) / रामचरितमानस (Ram's story-mind) / बर (excellent) / धरेउ (placed) / नाम (name) / हियँ (in the heart) / हेरि (seeing) / हरषि (rejoicing) / हर (Shiva)
ramacharitamanas::231.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::231.essence: What is cherished inwardly gains its true name when shared.
ramacharitamanas::231.simple_meaning: Shiva composed this sacred story in his heart, then shared it with Parvati at the right time. That is why it received the name Ramcharitmanas.
ramacharitamanas::231.simple_insight: What is held with love in the heart becomes worthy of sharing.
ramacharitamanas::231.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses before beginning the story to explain its sacred title. Shiva has already composed this Ram-story within himself, treasured it inwardly, and then spoken it to Parvati when the moment was right. The name itself comes from Shiva's joy.
ramacharitamanas::231.modern_relevance: You draft a letter in your notes app for weeks before sending it to the one person who needs it most. The timing matters, but the care you held for it matters first.
ramacharitamanas::231.insight: It shifts attention from public display to inward ripening before speech or action.

ramacharitamanas::232.verse_sanskrit: कहउँ कथा सोइ सुखद सुहाई। सादर सुनहु सुजन मन लाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::232.verse_hindi: मैं उसी सुख देने वाली सुहावनी रामकथा को कहता हूँ, हे सज्जनों! आदरपूर्वक मन लगाकर इसे सुनिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::232.english_translation: I tell that same सुखद and सुहावनी Ram story; listen with respect and a focused mind, good people.
ramacharitamanas::232.translation_literal: कहउँ (I tell) / कथा (story) / सोइ (that same) / सुखद (giving joy) / सुहाई (beautiful, pleasing) / सादर (with respect) / सुनहु (listen) / सुजन (good people) / मन (mind) / लाई (applying, focused)
ramacharitamanas::232.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::232.simple_meaning: The poet invites good people to listen carefully to the beautiful Ram story that gives joy.
ramacharitamanas::232.simple_insight: A sacred story asks for more than hearing; it asks for attention.
ramacharitamanas::232.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has just introduced the Ramcharitmanas through Shiva's praise of it. Now he turns directly to the listener and asks for respectful, focused attention before unfolding the story of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::232.modern_relevance: A friend starts telling you something that matters deeply, and you half-listen while checking your phone. This verse asks for the kind of attention that says: I am here, and I want to receive this fully.
ramacharitamanas::232.insight: It shifts reading from casual consumption to deliberate listening.

ramacharitamanas::233.verse_sanskrit: जस मानस जेहि बिधि भयउ जग प्रचार जेहि हेतु। अब सोइ कहउँ प्रसंग सब सुमिरि उमा बृषकेतु ॥
ramacharitamanas::233.verse_hindi: यह रामचरित मानस जैसा है, जिस प्रकार बना है और जिस हेतु से जगत में इसका प्रचार हुआ, अब वही सब कथा मैं श्री उमा-महेश्वर का स्मरण करके कहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::233.english_translation: I will now recount the whole story, remembering Uma and Bhushana, just as this Ramcharitmanas arose in the world and spread for its purpose.
ramacharitamanas::233.translation_literal: जस (as) / मानस (the mind-text) / जेहि बिधि (in whichever way) / भयउ (became) / जग (in the world) / प्रचार (spread) / जेहि हेतु (for which purpose) / अब (now) / सोइ (that same) / कहउँ (I tell) / प्रसंग (account) / सब (all) / सुमिरि (remembering) / उमा (Uma) / बृषकेतु (Shiva)
ramacharitamanas::233.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::233.essence: The story begins as remembrance, not performance.
ramacharitamanas::233.simple_meaning: The poet says he will now tell the full account of how this sacred work came to be known in the world, while remembering Uma and Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::233.simple_insight: A sacred work is not just written; it is offered with remembrance and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::233.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has just invited listeners into the story. Before the tale unfolds, he pauses to explain that he will recount the origin, spread, and purpose of this Ramcharitmanas while keeping Uma and Shiva in mind. The verse frames the whole text as devotional remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::233.modern_relevance: Before a long family story gets told, someone pauses and says why it matters and who it honors. That pause changes the whole mood: this is not casual narration, but an offering with intention.
ramacharitamanas::233.insight: It shifts the reader from passive listening to reverent reception, treating the text as an offering rather than entertainment.

ramacharitamanas::234.verse_sanskrit: संभु प्रसाद सुमति हियँ हुलसी। रामचरितमानस कबि तुलसी॥ करइ मनोहर मति अनुहारी। सुजन सुचित सुनि लेहु सुधारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::234.verse_hindi: श्री शिवजी की कृपा से उसके हृदय में सुंदर बुद्धि का विकास हुआ, जिससे यह तुलसीदास श्री रामचरित मानस का कवि हुआ। अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार तो वह इसे मनोहर ही बनाता है, किन्तु फिर भी हे सज्जनो! सुंदर चित्त से सुनकर इसे आप सुधार लीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::234.english_translation: By Shiva's grace, a good mind arose in his heart, and Tulsidas became the poet of Ramcharitmanas. He shapes it as beautifully as his own understanding allows, yet, good people, listen with a pure mind and improve it.
ramacharitamanas::234.translation_literal: संभु (Shiva) / प्रसाद (grace) / सुमति (good understanding) / हियँ (in the heart) / हुलसी (blossomed) / रामचरितमानस (Ramcharitmanas) / कबि (poet) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / करइ (does) / मनोहर (beautiful) / मति (understanding) / अनुहारी (according to) / सुजन (good people) / सुचित (pure-minded) / सुनि (hearing) / लेहु (take) / सुधारी (improve)
ramacharitamanas::234.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::234.essence: Grace makes the offering possible; humility keeps it open to correction.
ramacharitamanas::234.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says Shiva's grace gave him clear understanding, and he wrote Ramcharitmanas as best he could. He asks good listeners to receive it with a pure mind and refine it.
ramacharitamanas::234.simple_insight: Humility deepens devotion: even sacred work is offered as a draft before the divine.
ramacharitamanas::234.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses in the Balkand frame to speak about his own role. He says Shiva's grace opened his understanding, making him the poet of Ramcharitmanas. He also asks listeners to receive the work kindly and correct it with a clear mind.
ramacharitamanas::234.modern_relevance: You finish something heartfelt and still feel it could be better. Instead of defending every line, you offer it honestly, ask for thoughtful correction, and let humility protect the work.
ramacharitamanas::234.insight: It shifts the reader from self-importance to receptive humility, treating spiritual speech as service rather than ownership.

ramacharitamanas::235.verse_sanskrit: सुमति भूमि थल हृदय अगाधू। बेद पुरान उदधि घन साधू॥ बरषहिं राम सुजस बर बारी। मधुर मनोहर मंगलकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::235.verse_hindi: सुंदर (सात्त्वकी) बुद्धि भूमि है, हृदय ही उसमें गहरा स्थान है, वेद-पुराण समुद्र हैं और साधु-संत मेघ हैं। वे (साधु रूपी मेघ) श्री रामजी के सुयश रूपी सुंदर, मधुर, मनोहर और मंगलकारी जल की वर्षा करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::235.english_translation: The mind of good understanding is the field; the deep heart is its ground. The Vedas and Puranas are the ocean, and the saints are the clouds. They shower the beautiful water of Ram’s glory, sweet, lovely, and auspicious.
ramacharitamanas::235.translation_literal: सुमति (good understanding) / भूमि (field, ground) / थल (land, surface) / हृदय (heart) / अगाधू (deep, unfathomable) / बेद (Vedas) / पुरान (Puranas) / उदधि (ocean) / घन (clouds) / साधू (saints) / बरषहिं (rain, shower) / राम (Ram) / सुजस (good fame, glory) / बर (excellent) / बारी (water) / मधुर (sweet) / मनोहर (lovely) / मंगलकारी (auspicious)
ramacharitamanas::235.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::235.essence: True understanding becomes fertile only when Ram’s praise falls into it.
ramacharitamanas::235.simple_meaning: A clear mind is like fertile ground, the heart is its depth, sacred texts are the ocean, and saints are the clouds that rain down Ram’s glorious praise.
ramacharitamanas::235.simple_insight: It feels like wisdom is nourishment, not information — something that softens and refreshes the heart.
ramacharitamanas::235.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has just introduced himself as the poet by Shiva’s grace. Now he explains how this sacred poem comes into being: a pure mind is the field, the heart is the depth, the Vedas and Puranas are the ocean, and saints are the clouds that pour Ram’s praise as life-giving rain.
ramacharitamanas::235.modern_relevance: You sit with a book open, but nothing sinks in until the right words arrive from someone wise and loving. Then the mind feels watered, and the heart starts to open.
ramacharitamanas::235.insight: It shifts learning from collecting facts to receiving words that purify and enliven the heart.

ramacharitamanas::236.verse_sanskrit: लीला सगुन जो कहहिं बखानी। सोइ स्वच्छता करइ मल हानी॥ प्रेम भगति जो बरनि न जाई। सोइ मधुरता सुसीतलताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::236.verse_hindi: सगुण लीला का जो विस्तार से वर्णन करते हैं, वही राम सुयश रूपी जल की निर्मलता है, जो मल का नाश करती है और जिस प्रेमाभक्ति का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता, वही इस जल की मधुरता और सुंदर शीतलता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::236.english_translation: The clear water is Ram's radiant fame; devotion is its sweetness and cooling touch.
ramacharitamanas::236.translation_literal: लीला (divine play) / सगुन (with attributes) / जो (which) / कहहिं (they speak) / बखानी (describing in detail) / सोइ (that itself) / स्वच्छता (clearness) / करइ (does) / मल (impurity) / हानी (destruction) / प्रेम (love) / भगति (devotion) / जो (which) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाई (can be said) / सोइ (that itself) / मधुरता (sweetness) / सुसीतलताई (coolness)
ramacharitamanas::236.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::236.essence: Ram's praise purifies; love makes that praise sweet and cooling.
ramacharitamanas::236.simple_meaning: Describing Ram's manifest play purifies the heart, and love-filled devotion gives that praise its sweetness and cooling calm.
ramacharitamanas::236.simple_insight: Praise is not just information here; it washes the heart and softens the mind.
ramacharitamanas::236.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is comparing his own telling of Ram's visible deeds to clean water that removes inner dirt. He then says the deeper force behind that praise is love-devotion, which cannot be fully described but gives the whole stream its sweetness and cooling peace.
ramacharitamanas::236.modern_relevance: You hear a story that leaves you strangely calmer after a hard day. The details are beautiful, but what really changes you is the devotion behind them — it rinses off the grime of the day.
ramacharitamanas::236.insight: It shifts reading from analysis to purification: hearing Ram's story becomes a cleansing act, not just a mental exercise.

ramacharitamanas::237.verse_sanskrit: सो जल सुकृत सालि हित होई। राम भगत जन जीवन सोई॥ मेधा महि गत सो जल पावन। सकिलि श्रवन मग चलेउ सुहावन ॥ भरेउ सुमानस सुथल थिराना। सुखद सीत रुचि चारु चिराना ॥
ramacharitamanas::237.verse_hindi: वह (राम सुयश रूपी) जल सत्कर्म रूपी धान के लिए हितकर है और श्री रामजी के भक्तों का तो जीवन ही है। वह पवित्र जल बुद्धि रूपी पृथ्वी पर गिरा और सिमटकर सुहावने कान रूपी मार्ग से चला और मानस (हृदय) रूपी श्रेष्ठ स्थान में भरकर वहीं स्थिर हो गया। वही पुराना होकर सुंदर, रुचिकर, शीतल और सुखदाई हो गया॥4-5॥
ramacharitamanas::237.english_translation: That sacred water is beneficial for the rice of good deeds, and it is the life of devotees of Ram. Falling on the earth of understanding, it gathers, flows through the pleasant path of the ears, fills the excellent lake-like mind, and remains there. There it becomes old yet beautiful, pleasing, cool, and delightful.
ramacharitamanas::237.translation_literal: सो (that) / जल (water) / सुकृत (good deeds) / सालि (rice) / हित (beneficial) / होई (becomes) / राम (Ram) / भगत (devotee) / जन (people) / जीवन (life) / सोई (that only)॥ / मेधा (understanding) / महि (earth) / गत (gone/fallen) / सो (that) / जल (water) / पावन (pure) / सकिलि (gathered) / श्रवन (ears) / मग (path) / चलेउ (went) / सुहावन (pleasant)॥ / भरेउ (filled) / सुमानस (good mind / lake-like mind) / सुथल (excellent place) / थिराना (became steady) / सुखद (giving joy) / सीत (cool) / रुचि (pleasing) / चारु (beautiful) / चिराना (long-lasting/aged)॥
ramacharitamanas::237.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::237.essence: Ram's praise nourishes action and settles into the heart as cooling devotion.
ramacharitamanas::237.simple_meaning: Ram's praise is like pure water: it nourishes good action, enters the mind through hearing, and settles there as something cooling and lasting.
ramacharitamanas::237.simple_insight: Beautiful words can become a steady inner refuge when they are taken in deeply.
ramacharitamanas::237.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues the image of Ram's fame as sacred water. It falls into the mind through listening, fills the heart, and stays there like a cool, beloved presence. The verse explains why sacred narration nourishes devotion rather than just informing the listener.
ramacharitamanas::237.modern_relevance: You hear a line in a quiet room, and it stays with you all day — not as information, but as comfort. Some words do not just pass through; they settle, cool the mind, and quietly reshape it.
ramacharitamanas::237.insight: It shifts reading from collecting ideas to letting sacred speech soak into the mind until it becomes a lived presence.

ramacharitamanas::238.verse_sanskrit: सुठि सुंदर संबाद बर बिरचे बुद्धि बिचारि। तेइ एहि पावन सुभग सर घाट मनोहर चारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::238.verse_hindi: इस कथा में बुद्धि से विचारकर जो चार अत्यन्त सुंदर और उत्तम संवाद (भुशुण्डि-गरुड़, शिव-पार्वती, याज्ञवल्क्य-भरद्वाज और तुलसीदास और संत) रचे हैं, वही इस पवित्र और सुंदर सरोवर के चार मनोहर घाट हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::238.english_translation: Carefully considered, these beautiful dialogues are the four lovely ghats of this holy, charming lake.
ramacharitamanas::238.translation_literal: सुठि (very) / सुंदर (beautiful) / संबाद (dialogues) / बर (excellent) / बिरचे (crafted) / बुद्धि (with discernment) / बिचारि (having reflected) / तेइ (those only) / एहि (of this) / पावन (holy) / सुभग (charming) / सर (lake) / घाट (ghats/banks) / मनोहर (delightful) / चारि (four)
ramacharitamanas::238.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::238.essence: Wise form makes sacred teaching easy to enter.
ramacharitamanas::238.simple_meaning: The four great dialogues in this work are like four beautiful banks around a holy lake. They were shaped with careful thought and wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::238.simple_insight: Great teaching can be arranged so gracefully that it becomes easy to enter and remember.
ramacharitamanas::238.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the structure of his own sacred retelling. He says the four major dialogues — Bhushundi-Garuda, Shiva-Parvati, Yajnavalkya-Bharadvaja, and the poet's own exchange with saints — are the four beautiful banks of this holy lake of Ram's story.
ramacharitamanas::238.modern_relevance: You open a book and the hardest ideas feel welcoming because the author has shaped them with care. The structure itself becomes part of the teaching.
ramacharitamanas::238.insight: It shifts attention from isolated lines to the architecture that holds them together.

ramacharitamanas::239.verse_sanskrit: सप्त प्रबंध सुभग सोपाना। ग्यान नयन निरखत मन माना॥ रघुपति महिमा अगुन अबाधा। बरनब सोइ बर बारि अगाधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::239.verse_hindi: सात काण्ड ही इस मानस सरोवर की सुंदर सात सीढ़ियाँ हैं, जिनको ज्ञान रूपी नेत्रों से देखते ही मन प्रसन्न हो जाता है। श्री रघुनाथजी की निर्गुण (प्राकृतिक गुणों से अतीत) और निर्बाध (एकरस) महिमा का जो वर्णन किया जाएगा, वही इस सुंदर जल की अथाह गहराई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::239.english_translation: The seven books are the beautiful seven steps of this Manas lake. Seeing them with the eye of wisdom, the mind is pleased. The boundless, unfettered glory of Raghupati is the same endless deep water that will be described.
ramacharitamanas::239.translation_literal: सप्त (seven) / प्रबंध (books or sections) / सुभग (beautiful) / सोपाना (steps or stairways) / ग्यान (wisdom) / नयन (eyes) / निरखत (seeing) / मन (mind) / माना (is pleased)॥ / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / महिमा (glory) / अगुन (without qualities) / अबाधा (unfettered, unobstructed) / बरनब (to be described) / सोइ (that same) / बर (excellent) / बारि (water) / अगाधा (bottomless, unfathomable)॥
ramacharitamanas::239.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::239.essence: The poem's vastness becomes accessible through wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::239.simple_meaning: The seven books of the Ramcharitmanas are like seven beautiful steps into a lake. With clear understanding, the mind feels delight, and Ram's boundless glory is the deep water beneath it all.
ramacharitamanas::239.simple_insight: A calm mind can enter devotion without fear of its depth.
ramacharitamanas::239.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is introducing the whole Ramcharitmanas as a sacred lake. The seven Kands are its seven steps, and the reader is invited to approach Ram's limitless glory with wisdom, not confusion. This verse frames the entire poem as something to enter gradually and joyfully.
ramacharitamanas::239.modern_relevance: You open a long, unfamiliar book and feel intimidated by its size. Then one clear guide shows you the entry steps, and the whole thing stops feeling heavy. This verse turns vastness into welcome.
ramacharitamanas::239.insight: It shifts the reader from overwhelm to reverent approach, seeing depth as invitation rather than obstacle.

ramacharitamanas::240.verse_sanskrit: राम सीय जस सलिल सुधासम। उपमा बीचि बिलास मनोरम॥ पुरइनि सघन चारु चौपाई। जुगुति मंजु मनि सीप सुहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::240.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी और सीताजी का यश अमृत के समान जल है। इसमें जो उपमाएँ दी गई हैं, वही तरंगों का मनोहर विलास है। सुंदर चौपाइयाँ ही इसमें घनी फैली हुई पुरइन (कमलिनी) हैं और कविता की युक्तियाँ सुंदर मणि (मोती) उत्पन्न करने वाली सुहावनी सीपियाँ हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::240.english_translation: The fame of Ram and Sita is like nectar-water. The comparisons are its lovely waves. The beautiful chaupais spread like dense lotus leaves, and the poetic devices are charming shells that produce fine pearls.
ramacharitamanas::240.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सीय (Sita) / जस (fame) / सलिल (water) / सुधा-सम (like nectar) / उपमा (comparisons) / बीचि (waves) / बिलास (play/display) / मनोरम (beautiful) / पुरइनि (lotus leaves) / सघन (dense) / चारु (beautiful) / चौपाई (chaupais) / जुगुति (devices/skill) / मंजु (lovely) / मनि (jewel) / सीप (shell) / सुहाई (charming)
ramacharitamanas::240.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::240.essence: Ram and Sita's praise is the nectar; poetry only reveals its beauty.
ramacharitamanas::240.simple_meaning: Ram and Sita's praise is like nectar-filled water. The comparisons are the waves, the chaupais are the lotus leaves, and the poetic craft is the shell that makes pearls.
ramacharitamanas::240.simple_insight: Even the form of sacred poetry can become part of devotion.
ramacharitamanas::240.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing his own composition after introducing the seven-kand lake of the Ram story. He says Ram and Sita's fame is the nectar-water itself, while the imagery, meters, and poetic skill are the beautiful forms that make that sacred lake pleasing to the eye.
ramacharitamanas::240.modern_relevance: You reread a passage until the words themselves start to shine. The message matters, but the shape of the message can carry its own grace.
ramacharitamanas::240.insight: It shifts attention from plain content to how devotion is carried through poetic form.

ramacharitamanas::241.verse_sanskrit: छंद सोरठा सुंदर दोहा। सोइ बहुरंग कमल कुल सोहा॥ अरथ अनूप सुभाव सुभासा। सोइ पराग मकरंद सुबासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::241.verse_hindi: जो सुंदर छन्द, सोरठे और दोहे हैं, वही इसमें बहुरंगे कमलों के समूह सुशोभित हैं। अनुपम अर्थ, ऊँचे भाव और सुंदर भाषा ही पराग (पुष्परज), मकरंद (पुष्परस) और सुगंध हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::241.english_translation: The beautiful meters, soratha and doha, are the colorful lotuses that adorn it. Its unmatched meaning, noble feeling, and lovely language are the pollen, nectar, and fragrance.
ramacharitamanas::241.translation_literal: छंद (meter) / सोरठा (soratha) / सुंदर (beautiful) / दोहा (doha) / सोइ (that itself) / बहुरंग (many-colored) / कमल (lotus) / कुल (cluster) / सोहा (adorns)॥ / अरथ (meaning) / अनूप (matchless) / सुभाव (noble feeling) / सुभासा (beautiful language) / सोइ (that itself) / पराग (pollen) / मकरंद (nectar) / सुबासा (sweet fragrance)॥
ramacharitamanas::241.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::241.essence: Beautiful form and deep meaning bloom together.
ramacharitamanas::241.simple_meaning: The poem’s beauty lies in its form, meaning, feeling, and language. Each part is compared to flowers, pollen, nectar, and fragrance.
ramacharitamanas::241.simple_insight: Beauty can carry wisdom when every part of it is carefully shaped.
ramacharitamanas::241.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing his own Ramcharitmanas as a lotus-filled lake. The soratha and doha are the flowers, while the meaning, feeling, and language are the pollen, nectar, and scent. He is showing that devotion can be carried by poetic craft itself.
ramacharitamanas::241.modern_relevance: You read a line that lands because the words, rhythm, and feeling all work together. Nothing feels forced, and yet the message stays with you long after the page is closed.
ramacharitamanas::241.insight: It shifts attention from bare content to the living form that makes meaning memorable.

ramacharitamanas::242.verse_sanskrit: सुकृत पुंज मंजुल अलि माला। ग्यान बिराग बिचार मराला॥ धुनि अवरेब कबित गुन जाती। मीन मनोहर ते बहुभाँती ॥
ramacharitamanas::242.verse_hindi: सत्कर्मों (पुण्यों) के पुंज भौंरों की सुंदर पंक्तियाँ हैं, ज्ञान, वैराग्य और विचार हंस हैं। कविता की ध्वनि वक्रोक्ति, गुण और जाति ही अनेकों प्रकार की मनोहर मछलियाँ हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::242.english_translation: The mass of good deeds is a lovely line of bees. Knowledge, detachment, and reflection are swans. The poem's tones, figures, qualities, and styles are many kinds of beautiful fish.
ramacharitamanas::242.translation_literal: सुकृत (good deeds) / पुंज (mass, cluster) / मंजुल (lovely) / अलि (bee) / माला (garland) / ग्यान (knowledge) / बिराग (detachment) / बिचार (reflection, discernment) / मराला (swan) / धुनि (sound, tone) / अवरेब (figures of speech, ornament) / कबित (poetry) / गुन (qualities) / जाती (styles, kinds) / मीन (fish) / मनोहर (beautiful) / ते (those) / बहुभाँती (many kinds)
ramacharitamanas::242.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::242.essence: True beauty in speech comes from wisdom, detachment, and good action.
ramacharitamanas::242.simple_meaning: Tulsidas compares poetic beauty to a pond full of living forms: good deeds, wisdom, detachment, and careful thought all become part of the poem's charm.
ramacharitamanas::242.simple_insight: Beauty can carry discipline and wisdom without losing delight.
ramacharitamanas::242.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still describing the inner beauty of his poem, not shifting into a new teaching. After calling the verses a lake of nectar, he says its ornament is made of good deeds, wisdom, detachment, reflection, sound, style, and poetic figures.
ramacharitamanas::242.modern_relevance: You open a book expecting ornament, and find substance instead. The lines stay beautiful, but their beauty comes from character, discernment, and restraint.
ramacharitamanas::242.insight: It turns literary beauty into a moral and contemplative act, not just decoration.

ramacharitamanas::243.verse_sanskrit: अरथ धरम कामादिक चारी। कहब ग्यान बिग्यान बिचारी॥ नव रस जप तप जोग बिरागा। ते सब जलचर चारु तड़ागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::243.verse_hindi: अर्थ, धर्म, काम, मोक्ष- ये चारों, ज्ञान-विज्ञान का विचार के कहना, काव्य के नौ रस, जप, तप, योग और वैराग्य के प्रसंग- ये सब इस सरोवर के सुंदर जलचर जीव हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::243.english_translation: The four aims of life, knowledge and discernment, the nine poetic moods, chanting, austerity, yoga, and detachment — all these are the beautiful creatures living in this lake.
ramacharitamanas::243.translation_literal: अरथ (meaning/wealth) / धरम (righteous duty) / कामादिक (desire and the rest) / चारी (four) / कहब (speaking) / ग्यान (knowledge) / बिग्यान (discernment) / बिचारी (having reflected) / नव (nine) / रस (flavors) / जप (chanting) / तप (austerity) / जोग (yoga) / बिरागा (detachment) / ते (those) / सब (all) / जलचर (water-creatures) / चारु (beautiful) / तड़ागा (lake)
ramacharitamanas::243.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::243.essence: Many sacred ideas can live together in one beautiful work.
ramacharitamanas::243.simple_meaning: The poet compares many sacred ideas and poetic qualities to beautiful creatures in a lake. He is praising the richness of the poem itself, not giving a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::243.simple_insight: Beauty can hold many kinds of value at once without losing its harmony.
ramacharitamanas::243.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing his own poem as a lake filled with graceful life. After naming the poem’s flowers and bees in the previous verses, he now says that ideas like the four aims of life, knowledge, the nine moods, chanting, austerity, yoga, and detachment all move within it as lovely water creatures.
ramacharitamanas::243.modern_relevance: You open a book expecting one lesson and find a whole world inside it — ethics, longing, discipline, insight, and beauty all moving together without clashing.
ramacharitamanas::243.insight: It shifts attention from single-point meaning to layered richness, where many truths can coexist in one form.

ramacharitamanas::244.verse_sanskrit: सुकृती साधु नाम गुन गाना। ते बिचित्र जलबिहग समाना॥ संतसभा चहुँ दिसि अवँराई। श्रद्धा रितु बसंत सम गाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::244.verse_hindi: सुकृती (पुण्यात्मा) जनों के, साधुओं के और श्री रामनाम के गुणों का गान ही विचित्र जल पक्षियों के समान है। संतों की सभा ही इस सरोवर के चारों ओर की अमराई (आम की बगीचियाँ) हैं और श्रद्धा वसन्त ऋतु के समान कही गई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::244.english_translation: The songs of the virtuous, the good, and the praises of Ram's name are like strange water-birds. The assembly of saints surrounds this lake on all sides, and trust is like the spring season.
ramacharitamanas::244.translation_literal: सुकृती (virtuous ones) / साधु (saints) / नाम (name) / गुन (qualities) / गाना (singing) / ते (they) / बिचित्र (strange/wondrous) / जलबिहग (water-birds) / समाना (like) / संतसभा (assembly of saints) / चहुँ दिसि (on all four sides) / अवँराई (surrounding grove) / श्रद्धा (trust) / रितु (season) / बसंत (spring) / सम (like) / गाई (said/sung)
ramacharitamanas::244.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::244.essence: Trust lets Ram's praise bloom around you like spring.
ramacharitamanas::244.simple_meaning: The praise of Ram's name and the company of saints belong together. Trust makes that sacred gathering bloom like spring.
ramacharitamanas::244.simple_insight: Faith feels less like effort and more like entering a living garden of support.
ramacharitamanas::244.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the inner landscape of devotion as a lake filled with birds and surrounded by flowering groves. The singing of Ram's name, the presence of saints, and trust itself all belong to the same sacred ecology.
ramacharitamanas::244.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where one steady person changes everything. Their trust quiets the noise, and suddenly the whole space feels alive, as if something good has started blooming.
ramacharitamanas::244.insight: It shifts devotion from a private feeling into a living environment shaped by trust and saintly company.

ramacharitamanas::245.verse_sanskrit: भगति निरूपन बिबिध बिधाना। छमा दया दम लता बिताना॥ सम जम नियम फूल फल ग्याना। हरि पद रति रस बेद बखाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::245.verse_hindi: नाना प्रकार से भक्ति का निरूपण और क्षमा, दया तथा दम (इन्द्रिय निग्रह) लताओं के मण्डप हैं। मन का निग्रह, यम (अहिंसा, सत्य, अस्तेय, ब्रह्मचर्य और अपरिग्रह), नियम (शौच, संतोष, तप, स्वाध्याय और ईश्वर प्रणिधान) ही उनके फूल हैं, ज्ञान फल है और श्री हरि के चरणों में प्रेम ही इस ज्ञान रूपी फल का रस है। ऐसा वेदों ने कहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::245.english_translation: Devotion unfolds in many forms. Forgiveness, compassion, and self-restraint are its lattice. Restraint of the mind, discipline, and observance are its flowers; knowledge is its fruit, and love for Hari’s feet is the juice of that fruit. The Vedas say so.
ramacharitamanas::245.translation_literal: भगति (devotion) / निरूपन (description) / बिबिध (various) / बिधाना (forms) / छमा (forgiveness) / दया (compassion) / दम (self-restraint) / लता (vines) / बिताना (bower) / सम (mental restraint) / जम (yama) / नियम (observance) / फूल (flowers) / फल (fruit) / ग्याना (knowledge) / हरि (Hari) / पद (feet) / रति (love) / रस (juice/essence) / बेद (Vedas) / बखाना (described)
ramacharitamanas::245.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::245.essence: Devotion is a whole life: restraint first, love at the end.
ramacharitamanas::245.simple_meaning: Devotion is not just feeling. It grows through forgiveness, compassion, self-control, discipline, and right conduct, then ripens into knowledge and love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::245.simple_insight: Spiritual feeling becomes real when it changes conduct first.
ramacharitamanas::245.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the inner shape of devotion in the middle of his praise of Ram’s story. He says devotion is not a single emotion but a living garden: forgiveness, compassion, and self-restraint support it, discipline and right conduct flower in it, and knowledge ripens into love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::245.modern_relevance: You can feel inspired in a temple and still snap at your family an hour later. This verse says devotion is proven in how gently you speak, how tightly you hold your impulses, and how steadily love matures into action.
ramacharitamanas::245.insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to visible character.

ramacharitamanas::246.verse_sanskrit: औरउ कथा अनेक प्रसंगा। तेइ सुक पिक बहुबरन बिहंगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::246.verse_hindi: इस (रामचरित मानस) में और भी जो अनेक प्रसंगों की कथाएँ हैं, वे ही इसमें तोते, कोयल आदि रंग-बिरंगे पक्षी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::246.english_translation: The many side-stories in this text are the colorful birds, like parrots and cuckoos.
ramacharitamanas::246.translation_literal: औरउ (also) / कथा (stories) / अनेक (many) / प्रसंगा (occasions, episodes) / तेइ (those very) / सुक (parrots) / पिक (cuckoos) / बहुबरन (many-colored) / बिहंगा (birds)
ramacharitamanas::246.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::246.essence: The side-stories are not distractions; they are the beauty of the whole.
ramacharitamanas::246.simple_meaning: The many episodes in this book are like bright birds in a garden. They decorate the larger story rather than stand alone.
ramacharitamanas::246.simple_insight: It invites you to enjoy the variety without losing sight of the whole.
ramacharitamanas::246.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing his own poem as a living garden. The main story is the tree and flowers; the many side episodes are the birds that make it beautiful. He is preparing the reader for a rich, layered telling rather than a straight line.
ramacharitamanas::246.modern_relevance: You open a long family story and keep noticing the digressions, the old jokes, the side tales. Then you realize those detours are what make the memory feel alive.
ramacharitamanas::246.insight: It shifts attention from demanding a single thread to receiving the full texture of the telling.

ramacharitamanas::247.verse_sanskrit: पुलक बाटिका बाग बन सुख सुबिहंग बिहारु। माली सुमन सनेह जल सींचत लोचन चारु ॥
ramacharitamanas::247.verse_hindi: कथा में जो रोमांच होता है, वही वाटिका, बाग और वन है और जो सुख होता है, वही सुंदर पक्षियों का विहार है। निर्मल मन ही माली है, जो प्रेमरूपी जल से सुंदर नेत्रों द्वारा उनको सींचता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::247.english_translation: The thrill in the story is the garden, orchard, and forest. The delight is the beautiful birds’ play. The pure mind is the gardener, watering them with the water of love through lovely eyes.
ramacharitamanas::247.translation_literal: पुलक (thrill) / बाटिका (garden) / बाग (orchard) / बन (forest) / सुख (delight) / सुबिहंग (beautiful birds) / बिहारु (play) / माली (gardener) / सुमन (flowers) / सनेह जल (water of love) / सींचत (watering) / लोचन चारु (beautiful eyes)
ramacharitamanas::247.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::247.essence: A pure mind makes the story bloom.
ramacharitamanas::247.simple_meaning: The story is like a garden full of delight, and a pure mind tends it with loving attention.
ramacharitamanas::247.simple_insight: A receptive mind turns listening into nourishment, not just information.
ramacharitamanas::247.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is closing a passage on how the Ramcharitmanas should be received. After describing bhakti as a garden of virtues and other stories as birds in flight, he says the real beauty is in the listener's pure mind, which waters the tale with loving attention.
ramacharitamanas::247.modern_relevance: You open a beloved book after a hard day, and the words only come alive because you meet them with care. The story blooms because your attention is tender, not distracted.
ramacharitamanas::247.insight: It shifts reading from passive consumption to active, loving participation.

ramacharitamanas::248.verse_sanskrit: जे गावहिं यह चरित सँभारे। तेइ एहि ताल चतुर रखवारे॥ सदा सुनहिं सादर नर नारी। तेइ सुरबर मानस अधिकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::248.verse_hindi: जो लोग इस चरित्र को सावधानी से गाते हैं, वे ही इस तालाब के चतुर रखवाले हैं और जो स्त्री-पुरुष सदा आदरपूर्वक इसे सुनते हैं, वे ही इस सुंदर मानस के अधिकारी उत्तम देवता हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::248.english_translation: Those who carefully sing this sacred story are the skilled keepers of this lake. Men and women who always listen to it with reverence are the worthy beings of this beautiful Manas.
ramacharitamanas::248.translation_literal: जे (who) / गावहिं (sing) / यह (this) / चरित (story) / सँभारे (carefully, with care) / तेइ (they only) / एहि (of this) / ताल (lake) / चतुर (skilled) / रखवारे (keepers, guardians) ॥ / सदा (always) / सुनहिं (listen) / सादर (with reverence) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / तेइ (they only) / सुरबर (excellent beings) / मानस (of Manas) / अधिकारी (worthy, entitled) ॥
ramacharitamanas::248.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::248.essence: Reverent listening makes a person worthy of sacred truth.
ramacharitamanas::248.simple_meaning: People who sing this story carefully and listen to it with respect become worthy guardians of its sacred meaning.
ramacharitamanas::248.simple_insight: Respectful attention itself is a form of devotion, and devotion makes you fit to receive more.
ramacharitamanas::248.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising the Ramcharitmanas itself as a sacred lake. The people who sing it with care and hear it with reverence are not just audience members — they are the true guardians and rightful heirs of this devotional world.
ramacharitamanas::248.modern_relevance: You open a book that matters to you, but half your mind is on notifications. This verse says the real receiver is the one who arrives fully, with care, and lets reverence do the work.
ramacharitamanas::248.insight: It shifts reading from casual consumption to devoted participation.

ramacharitamanas::249.verse_sanskrit: अति खल जे बिषई बग कागा। एहि सर निकट न जाहिं अभागा॥ संबुक भेक सेवार समाना। इहाँ न बिषय कथा रस नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::249.verse_hindi: जो अति दुष्ट और विषयी हैं, वे अभागे बगुले और कौए हैं, जो इस सरोवर के समीप नहीं जाते, क्योंकि यहाँ (इस मानस सरोवर में) घोंघे, मेंढक और सेवार के समान विषय रस की नाना कथाएँ नहीं हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::249.english_translation: The deeply wicked and pleasure-chasing birds stay away from this lake. This lake has no many-colored tales of worldly desire, like snails, frogs, and weeds.
ramacharitamanas::249.translation_literal: अति (very) / खल (wicked) / जे (who) / बिषई (pleasure-chasing) / बग (heron) / कागा (crow) / एहि (this) / सर (lake) / निकट (near) / न (not) / जाहिं (go) / अभागा (unfortunate ones) / संबुक (snails) / भेक (frogs) / सेवार (weeds) / समाना (like) / इहाँ (here) / न (not) / बिषय (worldly desire) / कथा (stories) / रस (flavor) / नाना (many kinds)
ramacharitamanas::249.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::249.essence: Craving minds avoid what cannot feed their hunger.
ramacharitamanas::249.simple_meaning: Only the greedy and corrupt stay away from this sacred pool. It offers no entertainment for craving minds, only pure devotional nourishment.
ramacharitamanas::249.simple_insight: What feeds your cravings can also keep you far from what is holy.
ramacharitamanas::249.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the Manas lake as a pure, sacred place in Balkand. He says corrupt, pleasure-driven people avoid it because it offers no cheap worldly flavor. The verse sharpens the contrast between true devotion and restless craving.
ramacharitamanas::249.modern_relevance: A feed full of gossip and outrage can keep you scrolling for hours, but it will never leave you nourished. Some places, books, and conversations have no bait for the restless mind.
ramacharitamanas::249.insight: It shifts attention away from craving-based entertainment toward what actually purifies the mind.

ramacharitamanas::250.verse_sanskrit: तेहि कारन आवत हियँ हारे। कामी काक बलाक बिचारे॥ आवत ऐहिं सर अति कठिनाई। राम कृपा बिनु आइ न जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::250.verse_hindi: इसी कारण बेचारे कौवे और बगुले रूपी विषयी लोग यहाँ आते हुए हृदय में हार मान जाते हैं, क्योंकि इस सरोवर तक आने में कठिनाइयाँ बहुत हैं। श्री रामजी की कृपा बिना यहाँ नहीं आया जाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::250.english_translation: For that reason, selfish people like crows and herons lose heart before coming here. Reaching this lake is very difficult. Without Ram's grace, no one can come here.
ramacharitamanas::250.translation_literal: तेहि (for that) / कारन (reason) / आवत (coming) / हियँ (in the heart) / हारे (defeated) / कामी (desire-driven) / काक (crows) / बलाक (herons) / बिचारे (poor) / आवत (coming) / ऐहिं (to this) / सर (lake) / अति (very) / कठिनाई (difficulty) / राम (Ram) / कृपा (grace) / बिनु (without) / आइ (coming) / न (not) / जाई (can be done)
ramacharitamanas::250.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::250.essence: Only grace opens the place desire cannot reach.
ramacharitamanas::250.simple_meaning: Selfish, desire-driven people cannot easily reach this sacred place. Only Ram's grace makes the journey possible.
ramacharitamanas::250.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that some doors open only through grace, not force.
ramacharitamanas::250.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the sacred lake of the Manas as a place that repels the selfish. Crows and herons stand for restless, desire-driven minds. The verse says the journey itself is hard, and only Ram's grace allows anyone to enter.
ramacharitamanas::250.modern_relevance: You keep trying to force your way into a conversation, a relationship, or a room where your motives are wrong. The harder you push, the more resistance you meet. Sometimes the real entrance is humility, not effort.
ramacharitamanas::250.insight: It shifts attention from forcing access to seeking the grace that makes access possible.

ramacharitamanas::251.verse_sanskrit: कठिन कुसंग कुपंथ कराला। तिन्ह के बचन बाघ हरि ब्याला॥ गृह कारज नाना जंजाला। ते अति दुर्गम सैल बिसाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::251.verse_hindi: घोर कुसंग ही भयानक बुरा रास्ता है, उन कुसंगियों के वचन ही बाघ, सिंह और साँप हैं। घर के कामकाज और गृहस्थी के भाँति-भाँति के जंजाल ही अत्यंत दुर्गम बड़े-बड़े पहाड़ हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::251.english_translation: Dangerous bad company is a terrible road. The words of such people are tigers, lions, and snakes. Household duties and endless domestic entanglements are steep, impassable mountains.
ramacharitamanas::251.translation_literal: कठिन (difficult) / कुसंग (bad company) / कुपंथ (bad road) / कराला (terrible) / तिन्ह (their) / के (of) / बचन (words) / बाघ (tiger) / हरि (lion) / ब्याला (snake) / गृह (household) / कारज (work) / नाना (many) / जंजाला (entanglements) / ते (those) / अति (very) / दुर्गम (hard to cross) / सैल (mountains) / बिसाला (great)
ramacharitamanas::251.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::251.essence: Bad company turns ordinary life into an obstacle course.
ramacharitamanas::251.simple_meaning: Bad company makes life harder, and its speech can be dangerous. Even household responsibilities can feel like huge obstacles when the mind is pulled off course.
ramacharitamanas::251.simple_insight: You start seeing how your surroundings shape your mind before they shape your choices.
ramacharitamanas::251.detailed_meaning: The narrator is warning seekers near the opening of the Balkand. After describing the pure lake of Ram's story, he shows why some people cannot approach it: bad company, harmful speech, and the heavy clutter of worldly obligations all become obstacles on the path.
ramacharitamanas::251.modern_relevance: You spend an hour with people who mock every good intention, and by dinner your mind feels heavier. The verse names that drag clearly: company, speech, and the clutter that keeps pulling you away.
ramacharitamanas::251.insight: It teaches you to protect attention by choosing your surroundings carefully and seeing pressure for what it is.

ramacharitamanas::252.verse_sanskrit: बन बहु बिषम मोह मद माना। नदीं कुतर्क भयंकर नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::252.verse_hindi: मोह, मद और मान ही बहुत से बीहड़ वन हैं और नाना प्रकार के कुतर्क ही भयानक नदियाँ हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::252.english_translation: Delusion, pride, and conceit are many wild forests; many terrible false reasonings are rivers.
ramacharitamanas::252.translation_literal: बन (forest) / बहु (many) / बिषम (wild, difficult) / मोह (delusion) / मद (pride) / माना (conceit) / नदीं (rivers) / कुतर्क (false reasoning) / भयंकर (terrible) / नाना (many)
ramacharitamanas::252.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::252.essence: Pride and confusion turn the path itself into a wilderness.
ramacharitamanas::252.simple_meaning: Delusion, pride, and conceit are like dangerous forests, and twisted arguments are like terrifying rivers. They make the spiritual path hard to cross.
ramacharitamanas::252.simple_insight: Some obstacles are not outside you. They are the habits of mind that turn the path into a wilderness.
ramacharitamanas::252.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the inner landscape that blocks entry into Ram's teaching. Delusion, pride, and conceit become wild forests; false arguments become dangerous rivers. The next verse adds that only trust and saintly company can cross this terrain.
ramacharitamanas::252.modern_relevance: You keep rereading the same argument thread at midnight, and each reply makes you more certain and more lost. The real obstacle is not the topic — it is the mind that turns everything into a maze.
ramacharitamanas::252.insight: It shifts attention from external difficulty to the mind's own distortions, so you stop treating confusion as reality.

ramacharitamanas::253.verse_sanskrit: जे श्रद्धा संबल रहित नहिं संतन्ह कर साथ। तिन्ह कहुँ मानस अगम अति जिन्हहि न प्रिय रघुनाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::253.verse_hindi: जिनके पास श्रद्धा रूपी राह खर्च नहीं है और संतों का साथ नहीं है और जिनको श्री रघुनाथजी प्रिय हैं, उनके लिए यह मानस अत्यंत ही अगम है। (अर्थात् श्रद्धा, सत्संग और भगवत्प्रेम के बिना कोई इसको नहीं पा सकता) ॥
ramacharitamanas::253.english_translation: Without trust, the company of saints, and love for Raghunath, the Manas remains extremely hard to enter.
ramacharitamanas::253.translation_literal: जे (those who) / श्रद्धा (trust before certainty) / संबल (support) / रहित (without) / नहिं (not) / संतन्ह (of saints) / कर (of) / साथ (company) / तिन्ह कहुँ (for them) / मानस (Manas) / अगम (hard to reach) / अति (very) / जिन्हहि (to whom) / न प्रिय (not dear) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::253.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::253.essence: Trust and love are the doorway into sacred meaning.
ramacharitamanas::253.simple_meaning: The Ramcharitmanas cannot be entered by effort alone. Trust, good company, and love for Ram are the real keys.
ramacharitamanas::253.simple_insight: Reading becomes reception, not just study, when the heart is prepared.
ramacharitamanas::253.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has just described the world as full of bad company, crooked reasoning, and heavy distractions. Now he says the Manas is still beyond reach unless a person brings trust, saintly company, and love for Raghunath.
ramacharitamanas::253.modern_relevance: You open a sacred book late at night, but your mind is noisy and skeptical. The words stay flat until trust and longing soften you enough to receive them.
ramacharitamanas::253.insight: It shifts the reader from intellectual access to devotional readiness.

ramacharitamanas::254.verse_sanskrit: जौं करि कष्ट जाइ पुनि कोई। जातहिं नीद जुड़ाई होई॥ जड़ता जाड़ बिषम उर लागा। गएहुँ न मज्जन पाव अभागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::254.verse_hindi: यदि कोई मनुष्य कष्ट उठाकर वहाँ तक पहुँच भी जाए, तो वहाँ जाते ही उसे नींद रूपी ज़ूडी आ जाती है। हृदय में मूर्खता रूपी बड़ा कड़ा जाड़ा लगने लगता है, जिससे वहाँ जाकर भी वह अभागा स्नान नहीं कर पाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::254.english_translation: Even if someone endures hardship and reaches there, sleep overtakes them on arrival. A harsh cold of foolishness settles in the heart, and the unlucky one still cannot bathe.
ramacharitamanas::254.translation_literal: जौं (if) / करि (having done) / कष्ट (hardship) / जाइ (goes) / पुनि (again) / कोई (someone) / जातहिं (upon going) / नीद (sleep) / जुड़ाई (comes on) / होई (becomes) / जड़ता (foolishness) / जाड़ (cold) / बिषम (harsh) / उर (heart) / लागा (clings) / गएहुँ (even after going) / न (not) / मज्जन (bathing) / पाव (gets) / अभागा (unfortunate one)
ramacharitamanas::254.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::254.essence: Arrival means nothing without an awake mind.
ramacharitamanas::254.simple_meaning: Even after reaching the sacred lake through effort, a foolish mind becomes dull and sleepy there, so the person still misses the cleansing bath.
ramacharitamanas::254.simple_insight: Hard effort means little if the mind stays dull and unready.
ramacharitamanas::254.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing a seeker who has already crossed difficulty and arrived at the holy lake, yet still fails to receive its blessing. The obstacle is not distance but inner dullness, which leaves the person unable to benefit from what was reached.
ramacharitamanas::254.modern_relevance: You finally sit down to meditate after a long day, but your mind is foggy and half-asleep. The place is right, the effort is real, yet the inner readiness is missing.
ramacharitamanas::254.insight: It shifts attention from reaching the goal to arriving awake and receptive.

ramacharitamanas::255.verse_sanskrit: करि न जाइ सर मज्जन पाना। फिरि आवइ समेत अभिमाना। जौं बहोरि कोउ पूछन आवा। सर निंदा करि ताहि बुझावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::255.verse_hindi: उससे उस सरोवर में स्नान और उसका जलपान तो किया नहीं जाता, वह अभिमान सहित लौट आता है। फिर यदि कोई उससे (वहाँ का हाल) पूछने आता है, तो वह (अपने अभाग्य की बात न कहकर) सरोवर की निंदा करके उसे समझाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::255.english_translation: One cannot bathe in that lake or drink its water. He returns, still full of pride. If someone later asks him about it, he blames the lake and misleads the listener.
ramacharitamanas::255.translation_literal: करि न जाइ (cannot be done) / सर (lake) / मज्जन (bathing) / पाना (drinking) / फिरि (again) / आवइ (comes) / समेत (with) / अभिमाना (pride) / जौं (if) / बहोरि (again) / कोउ (someone) / पूछन (to ask) / आवा (came) / सर (lake) / निंदा (blame) / करि (doing) / ताहि (him) / बुझावा (explains/misleads)
ramacharitamanas::255.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::255.essence: Pride leaves empty-handed and still blames the blessing.
ramacharitamanas::255.simple_meaning: A proud person cannot truly receive the lake’s blessing. He leaves unchanged, then blames the lake instead of admitting his own failure.
ramacharitamanas::255.simple_insight: It exposes how pride protects itself by turning every missed blessing into someone else’s fault.
ramacharitamanas::255.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, Tulsidas is describing a holy lake reached only by those fit to receive it. A person who goes there with pride cannot benefit, and when he returns empty-handed, he hides his own failure by speaking badly of the lake.
ramacharitamanas::255.modern_relevance: You leave a hard conversation unchanged, then tell everyone the other person was impossible. The real barrier was your own pride, but it feels easier to blame the room.
ramacharitamanas::255.insight: It shifts attention from blaming the world to noticing the ego that blocked reception in the first place.

ramacharitamanas::256.verse_sanskrit: सकल बिघ्न ब्यापहिं नहिं तेही। राम सुकृपाँ बिलोकहिं जेही॥ सोइ सादर सर मज्जनु करई। महा घोर त्रयताप न जरई ॥
ramacharitamanas::256.verse_hindi: ये सारे विघ्न उसको नहीं व्यापते (बाधा नहीं देते) जिसे श्री रामचंद्रजी सुंदर कृपा की दृष्टि से देखते हैं। वही आदरपूर्वक इस सरोवर में स्नान करता है और महान् भयानक त्रिताप से (आध्यात्मिक, आधिदैविक, आधिभौतिक तापों से) नहीं जलता ॥
ramacharitamanas::256.english_translation: All obstacles do not affect the one whom Ram looks upon with gracious favor. That person reverently bathes in this lake and does not burn in the terrible threefold suffering.
ramacharitamanas::256.translation_literal: सकल (all) / बिघ्न (obstacles) / ब्यापहिं (afflict) / नहिं (not) / तेही (that one) / राम (Ram) / सुकृपाँ (with gracious favor) / बिलोकहिं (look upon) / जेही (whom) / सोइ (that very one) / सादर (with reverence) / सर (lake) / मज्जनु (bathing) / करई (does) / महा (great) / घोर (terrible) / त्रयताप (threefold suffering) / न (not) / जरई (burns)
ramacharitamanas::256.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::256.essence: Ram's gracious glance makes even hardship powerless.
ramacharitamanas::256.simple_meaning: Ram's gracious glance removes obstacles. The one who approaches this holy lake with respect is freed from the burning pressure of life's three kinds of suffering.
ramacharitamanas::256.simple_insight: It brings relief: grace can meet you where effort alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::256.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing a sacred lake after saying that arrogant visitors cannot truly enter its blessing. Now he turns to the opposite case: the person whom Ram favors. Such a person comes reverently, bathes properly, and escapes the burning pressure of the world's threefold suffering.
ramacharitamanas::256.modern_relevance: You walk into a crowded room carrying exhaustion, deadlines, and a mind full of static. Some days, one moment of grace or humility changes the whole atmosphere before you even speak.
ramacharitamanas::256.insight: It shifts the reader from self-reliance alone to receptive trust in Ram's grace.

ramacharitamanas::257.verse_sanskrit: ते नर यह सर तजहिं न काऊ। जिन्ह कें राम चरन भल भाऊ॥ जो नहाइ चह एहिं सर भाई। सो सतसंग करउ मन लाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::257.verse_hindi: जिनके मन में श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणों में सुंदर प्रेम है, वे इस सरोवर को कभी नहीं छोड़ते। हे भाई! जो इस सरोवर में स्नान करना चाहे, वह मन लगाकर सत्संग करे ॥
ramacharitamanas::257.english_translation: Those whose hearts love Ram's feet never leave this lake. Brother, whoever wants to bathe in this lake should join good company with full attention.
ramacharitamanas::257.translation_literal: ते (those) / नर (people) / यह (this) / सर (lake) / तजहिं (leave) / न (not) / काऊ (ever) / जिन्ह कें (for whom) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / भल (good) / भाऊ (love) ॥ जो (who) / नहाइ (bathe) / चह (wants) / एहिं (in this) / सर (lake) / भाई (brother) / सो (that one) / सतसंग (good company) / करउ (should do) / मन (mind) / लाई (attentively) ॥
ramacharitamanas::257.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::257.essence: Good company is the doorway to lasting devotion.
ramacharitamanas::257.simple_meaning: People who love Ram deeply never turn away from this sacred lake. The way to enter it is to keep company with the wise and listen with attention.
ramacharitamanas::257.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that true devotion keeps you close, and good company helps you enter it.
ramacharitamanas::257.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, Tulsidas turns the Mansarovar into a living symbol of Ram's presence. He says the ones who truly love Ram's feet never leave it, and anyone who wants to bathe there must come through satsang.
ramacharitamanas::257.modern_relevance: You feel scattered after a long week, then sit with one steady friend who speaks honestly and quietly. The mind settles faster than it ever did alone.
ramacharitamanas::257.insight: It shifts the seeker from chasing spiritual experiences to seeking the company that makes devotion possible.

ramacharitamanas::258.verse_sanskrit: अस मानस मानस चख चाही। भइ कबि बुद्धि बिमल अवगाही॥ भयउ हृदयँ आनंद उछाहू। उमगेउ प्रेम प्रमोद प्रबाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::258.verse_hindi: ऐसे मानस सरोवर को हृदय के नेत्रों से देखकर और उसमें गोता लगाकर कवि की बुद्धि निर्मल हो गई, हृदय में आनंद और उत्साह भर गया और प्रेम तथा आनंद का प्रवाह उमड़ आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::258.english_translation: Seeing and plunging into such a Manas lake with the inner eye, the poet's understanding became pure. Joy and eagerness rose in the heart, and a flood of love and delight surged forth.
ramacharitamanas::258.translation_literal: अस (such) / मानस (Manas lake) / मानस चख (inner eye) / चाही (seeing) / भइ (became) / कबि बुद्धि (poet's understanding) / बिमल (pure) / अवगाही (having plunged into) / भयउ (became) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / आनंद (joy) / उछाहू (eagerness) / उमगेउ (surged up) / प्रेम (love) / प्रमोद (delight) / प्रबाहू (flood)
ramacharitamanas::258.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::258.essence: Inner seeing can wash the mind clean and awaken joy.
ramacharitamanas::258.simple_meaning: Seeing the sacred lake with inner vision and immersing in it purified the poet's mind. Joy, eagerness, love, and delight all rose together in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::258.simple_insight: Real understanding can feel like a cleansing flood, not just a thought.
ramacharitamanas::258.detailed_meaning: After describing the sacred Manas lake, the poet turns inward. By seeing it with the heart's eye and diving into its meaning, his understanding becomes clear, and the verse overflows with joy, love, and creative energy.
ramacharitamanas::258.modern_relevance: You read a line that suddenly lands after weeks of confusion. Something inside loosens, and the rest of your day feels brighter because you finally see it clearly.
ramacharitamanas::258.insight: It shifts reading from passive noticing to inward absorption that purifies understanding.

ramacharitamanas::259.verse_sanskrit: चली सुभग कबिता सरिता सो। राम बिमल जस जल भरित सो। सरजू नाम सुमंगल मूला। लोक बेद मत मंजुल कूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::259.verse_hindi: उससे वह सुंदर कविता रूपी नदी बह निकली, जिसमें श्री रामजी का निर्मल यश रूपी जल भरा है। इस (कवितारूपिणी नदी) का नाम सरयू है, जो संपूर्ण सुंदर मंगलों की जड़ है। लोकमत और वेदमत इसके दो सुंदर किनारे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::259.english_translation: A beautiful river of poetry flowed forth, filled with the pure water of Ram's glory. Its name is Sarayu, the root of all auspiciousness, with the views of the world and the Vedas as its two lovely banks.
ramacharitamanas::259.translation_literal: चली (flowed) / सुभग (beautiful) / कबिता (poetry) / सरिता (river) / सो (that) / राम (Ram) / बिमल (pure) / जस (glory) / जल (water) / भरित (filled) / सो (that) / सरजू (Sarayu) / नाम (name) / सुमंगल (very auspicious) / मूला (root) / लोक (world/common view) / बेद (Veda) / मत (view/doctrine) / मंजुल (lovely) / कूला (banks)
ramacharitamanas::259.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::259.essence: Ram's glory makes the river itself feel sacred.
