ramacharitamanas::259.simple_meaning: A poetic river flows with Ram's pure glory. It is called Sarayu, and it stands as the source of all good fortune, with worldly understanding and Vedic teaching as its two banks.
ramacharitamanas::259.simple_insight: Beauty becomes sacred when it carries remembrance of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::259.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the sacred river Sarayu as a flowing poem born from his vision of Ram's spotless fame. He presents it as a holy stream with both common tradition and Vedic authority supporting it, preparing the reader for the river's purifying power.
ramacharitamanas::259.modern_relevance: A song, a poem, or even a family story can feel ordinary until it carries what you most revere. Then it becomes a place people return to for cleansing and meaning.
ramacharitamanas::259.insight: It turns a landscape into a living vessel of remembrance, not mere scenery.

ramacharitamanas::260.verse_sanskrit: नदी पुनीत सुमानस नंदिनि। कलिमल तृन तरु मूल निकंदिनि ॥
ramacharitamanas::260.verse_hindi: यह सुंदर मानस सरोवर की कन्या सरयू नदी बड़ी पवित्र है और कलियुग के (छोटे-बड़े) पाप रूपी तिनकों और वृक्षों को जड़ से उखाड़ फेंकने वाली है ॥
ramacharitamanas::260.english_translation: The sacred river Sumanas’s daughter destroys the roots of the sins of the age.
ramacharitamanas::260.translation_literal: नदी (river) / पुनीत (pure, sacred) / सुमानस (Sumanas) / नंदिनि (daughter) / कलिमल (the impurities of Kali age) / तृन (grass) / तरु (tree) / मूल (root) / निकंदिनि (uprooting, cutting off)
ramacharitamanas::260.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::260.essence: Purity can uproot corruption before it takes hold.
ramacharitamanas::260.simple_meaning: Saryu is described as a pure river that uproots the small and large impurities of the present age.
ramacharitamanas::260.simple_insight: Some places do more than hold water—they change the people who come near them.
ramacharitamanas::260.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues praising the sacred geography around the new poem. After describing the Manas lake and the river of Ram’s fame, he names Saryu as its holy daughter, a river whose presence cleanses the age’s corruption.
ramacharitamanas::260.modern_relevance: You walk into a temple courtyard after a week of noise, and your breathing changes before your thoughts do. Some environments quietly strip away what has clung to you.
ramacharitamanas::260.insight: It shifts attention from outer scenery to the purifying effect of sacred company and place.

ramacharitamanas::261.verse_sanskrit: श्रोता त्रिबिध समाज पुर ग्राम नगर दुहुँ कूल। संतसभा अनुपम अवध सकल सुमंगल मूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::261.verse_hindi: तीनों प्रकार के श्रोताओं का समाज ही इस नदी के दोनों किनारों पर बसे हुए पुरवे, गाँव और नगर में है और संतों की सभा ही सब सुंदर मंगलों की जड़ अनुपम अयोध्याजी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::261.english_translation: The three kinds of listeners live in the towns, villages, and cities on both banks. The assembly of saints is incomparable Ayodhya, the root of all auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::261.translation_literal: श्रोता (listeners) / त्रिबिध (three kinds) / समाज (assembly) / पुर (towns) / ग्राम (villages) / नगर (cities) / दुहुँ (both) / कूल (banks) / संतसभा (assembly of saints) / अनुपम (incomparable) / अवध (Ayodhya) / सकल (all) / सुमंगल (auspicious) / मूल (root)
ramacharitamanas::261.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::261.essence: Saintly company turns ordinary places into Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::261.simple_meaning: Listeners of every kind are present on both banks, and the company of saints is like incomparable Ayodhya, the source of all good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::261.simple_insight: Good company turns a place into something sacred and alive.
ramacharitamanas::261.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the river-like spread of Ram's story and the people gathered to hear it. On both banks are towns, villages, and cities, filled with different kinds of listeners. In that gathered saintly company, Ayodhya itself appears as the root of all auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::261.modern_relevance: A crowded hall, a livestream chat, and a few sincere listeners can feel very different. One group is just an audience; the other becomes a place where something meaningful can actually begin.
ramacharitamanas::261.insight: It shifts attention from the crowd itself to the quality of the gathering.

ramacharitamanas::262.verse_sanskrit: रामभगति सुरसरितहि जाई। मिली सुकीरति सरजु सुहाई॥ सानुज राम समर जसु पावन। मिलेउ महानदु सोन सुहावन ॥
ramacharitamanas::262.verse_hindi: सुंदर कीर्ति रूपी सुहावनी सरयूजी रामभक्ति रूपी गंगाजी में जा मिलीं। छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण सहित श्री रामजी के युद्ध का पवित्र यश रूपी सुहावना महानद सोन उसमें आ मिला ॥
ramacharitamanas::262.english_translation: Ram-bhakti went to the divine river and met the lovely Sarayu. The sacred fame of Ram's battle, along with Lakshman, joined it like the beautiful river Son joining the Ganga.
ramacharitamanas::262.translation_literal: रामभगति (Ram-devotion) / सुरसरितहि (to the divine river) / जाई (went) / मिली (met/joined) / सुकीरति (good fame) / सरजु (Sarayu) / सुहाई (lovely) ॥ / सानुज (with younger brother) / राम (Ram) / समर (battle) / जसु (fame) / पावन (pure) / मिलेउ (joined) / महानदु (great river) / सोन (Son) / सुहावन (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::262.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::262.essence: Ram's devotion and fame flow together like holy rivers.
ramacharitamanas::262.simple_meaning: Ram's devotion and Ram's pure fame are pictured as holy rivers joining together. The verse praises how devotion, honor, and Ram's heroic story flow into one sacred stream.
ramacharitamanas::262.simple_insight: What you love and what you honor can become one current in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::262.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the sacred geography of the Ramcharitmanas as a living landscape. Ram-bhakti becomes the Ganga, Ram's pure fame becomes Sarayu, and the battle glory of Ram and Lakshman joins them like the Son river. The verse turns story into pilgrimage.
ramacharitamanas::262.modern_relevance: You hear a song about someone you deeply admire, and suddenly the whole room feels charged with reverence. Memory, devotion, and public honor can merge into one feeling.
ramacharitamanas::262.insight: It turns Ram's story into sacred flow, showing devotion and fame as spiritually inseparable.

ramacharitamanas::263.verse_sanskrit: जुग बिच भगति देवधुनि धारा। सोहति सहित सुबिरति बिचारा॥ त्रिबिध ताप त्रासक तिमुहानी। राम सरूप सिंधु समुहानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::263.verse_hindi: दोनों के बीच में भक्ति रूपी गंगाजी की धारा ज्ञान और वैराग्य के सहित शोभित हो रही है। ऐसी तीनों तापों को डराने वाली यह तिमुहानी नदी रामस्वरूप रूपी समुद्र की ओर जा रही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::263.english_translation: In the middle lies the stream of devotion, the river of divine inspiration. It shines with wisdom and non-attachment. This three-fear-destroying meeting point flows toward the ocean of Ram's form.
ramacharitamanas::263.translation_literal: जुग बिच (between the two ages) / भगति (devotion) / देवधुनि (divine river) / धारा (stream) / सोहति (shines) / सहित (together with) / सुबिरति (good non-attachment) / बिचारा (reflection) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / ताप (heat/suffering) / त्रासक (frightening, destroyer) / तिमुहानी (meeting point of three waters) / राम सरूप (Ram-shaped) / सिंधु (ocean) / समुहानी (flowing toward, meeting)
ramacharitamanas::263.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::263.essence: Devotion becomes complete when wisdom and non-attachment flow with it.
ramacharitamanas::263.simple_meaning: Devotion shines when joined with wisdom and non-attachment. Together, they carry a person toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::263.simple_insight: Devotion becomes steady and safe when it is guided by clear seeing and letting go.
ramacharitamanas::263.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is extending the river image from the previous verses. The stream of Ram-bhakti now appears joined with wisdom and non-attachment, like a sacred confluence. In this moment, devotion is shown not as emotion alone, but as a force that leads straight to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::263.modern_relevance: You feel pulled in three directions after a loss, a success, or a family conflict. A quieter devotion, joined with clear seeing and non-attachment, keeps you from being swept away.
ramacharitamanas::263.insight: It shifts devotion from raw feeling into a balanced current that carries the mind toward Ram.

ramacharitamanas::264.verse_sanskrit: मानस मूल मिली सुरसरिही। सुनत सुजन मन पावन करिही॥ बिच बिच कथा बिचित्र बिभागा। जनु सरि तीर तीर बन बागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::264.verse_hindi: इस (कीर्ति रूपी सरयू) का मूल मानस (श्री रामचरित) है और यह (रामभक्ति रूपी) गंगाजी में मिली है, इसलिए यह सुनने वाले सज्जनों के मन को पवित्र कर देगी। इसके बीच-बीच में जो भिन्न-भिन्न प्रकार की विचित्र कथाएँ हैं, वे ही मानो नदी तट के आस-पास के वन और बाग हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::264.english_translation: The root of the Manas has merged into the sacred river of Ram-bhakti, and hearing it will purify the minds of noble people. The varied stories in between are like forests and gardens along the riverbank.
ramacharitamanas::264.translation_literal: मानस मूल (the root of the Manas) / मिली (has merged) / सुरसरिही (into the sacred river) / सुनत (hearing) / सुजन (noble people) / मन (mind) / पावन (pure) / करिही (will make) // बिच बिच (between, in between) / कथा (stories) / बिचित्र (varied, wondrous) / बिभागा (sections, divisions) / जनु (as if) / सरि तीर (riverbank) / तीर (banks) / बन (forest) / बागा (gardens)
ramacharitamanas::264.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::264.essence: The whole poem is a river of Ram-devotion, and every story along it purifies.
ramacharitamanas::264.simple_meaning: The Ramcharitmanas is presented as a sacred river flowing into Ram-devotion, and listening to it cleanses the mind. The many stories within it are like beautiful forests and gardens along the riverbank.
ramacharitamanas::264.simple_insight: The teaching feels alive and welcoming: even the side stories are part of the cleansing flow.
ramacharitamanas::264.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas steps back from the story and describes his own poem. In Balkand, he says the Manas has its root in the sacred stream of Ram-devotion, and its many episodes are like trees and gardens beside that river, all meant to purify the listener.
ramacharitamanas::264.modern_relevance: You open a book expecting one main point, then realize even the side stories are doing the work. The whole thing is arranged to soften the heart, not just inform the mind.
ramacharitamanas::264.insight: It teaches readers to receive the whole text as a devotional landscape, not just chase isolated lessons.

ramacharitamanas::265.verse_sanskrit: उमा महेस बिबाह बराती। ते जलचर अगनित बहुभाँती॥ रघुबर जनम अनंद बधाई। भवँर तरंग मनोहरताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::265.verse_hindi: श्री पार्वतीजी और शिवजी के विवाह के बाराती इस नदी में बहुत प्रकार के असंख्य जलचर जीव हैं। श्री रघुनाथजी के जन्म की आनंद-बधाइयाँ ही इस नदी के भँवर और तरंगों की मनोहरता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::265.english_translation: The wedding procession of Uma and Mahesh is filled with countless kinds of water creatures. The joy-filled greetings at the birth of Raghubar are the whirlpools and waves that make it beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::265.translation_literal: उमा (Parvati) / महेस (Shiva) / बिबाह (wedding) / बराती (wedding guests) / ते (those) / जलचर (water-dwellers) / अगनित (countless) / बहुभाँती (of many kinds) / रघुबर (Raghubar, Ram) / जनम (birth) / अनंद (joy) / बधाई (congratulations) / भवँर (whirlpools) / तरंग (waves) / मनोहरताई (beauty)
ramacharitamanas::265.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::265.essence: Nature itself becomes festival when Ram appears.
ramacharitamanas::265.simple_meaning: The verse compares the river's creatures to Shiva and Parvati's wedding guests, and its whirlpools and waves to the joy around Ram's birth.
ramacharitamanas::265.simple_insight: Even nature seems to celebrate when the divine story unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::265.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the sacred river as if it is alive with Ram's story. Its creatures become the wedding guests of Shiva and Parvati, and its moving waters become the joyful signs of Ram's birth, turning scenery into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::265.modern_relevance: A quiet river, a crowded street, even the weather can feel different when a life-changing event is near. The world seems to participate, not just watch.
ramacharitamanas::265.insight: It turns ordinary scenery into a living sign of sacred joy.

ramacharitamanas::266.verse_sanskrit: दोहाः बालचरित चहु बंधु के बनज बिपुल बहुरंग। नृप रानी परिजन सुकृत मधुकर बारि बिहंग ॥
ramacharitamanas::266.verse_hindi: चारों भाइयों के जो बालचरित हैं, वे ही इसमें खिले हुए रंग-बिरंगे बहुत से कमल हैं। महाराज श्री दशरथजी तथा उनकी रानियों और कुटुम्बियों के सत्कर्म (पुण्य) ही भ्रमर और जल पक्षी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::266.english_translation: The childhood deeds of the four brothers are like many lotuses of many colors. King Dasharath, the queens, and the family’s good deeds are the bees and waterbirds around them.
ramacharitamanas::266.translation_literal: बालचरित (childhood deeds) / चहु बंधु के (of the four brothers) / बनज (lotuses) / बिपुल (many) / बहुरंग (many-colored) / नृप (king) / रानी (queens) / परिजन (family) / सुकृत (good deeds) / मधुकर (bees) / बारि (water) / बिहंग (birds)
ramacharitamanas::266.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::266.essence: Goodness around Ram makes even childhood feel like a blooming river.
ramacharitamanas::266.simple_meaning: The four brothers’ childhood stories are compared to many colorful lotuses, while Dasharath’s family virtues are the bees and birds gathered around them.
ramacharitamanas::266.simple_insight: A holy family’s goodness makes every small scene feel alive and beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::266.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the flowing landscape around Ram’s birth story. The brothers’ childhood deeds are the bright lotuses in the river, and Dasharath’s household virtues are the creatures moving around them. It is decorative praise, not a new teaching.
ramacharitamanas::266.modern_relevance: You look back at old family photos and realize the real beauty was never the pose. It was the care, sacrifice, and warmth that surrounded every ordinary moment.
ramacharitamanas::266.insight: It turns a family story into a living scene of grace, making virtue feel visible and tangible.

ramacharitamanas::267.verse_sanskrit: सीय स्वयंबर कथा सुहाई। सरित सुहावनि सो छबि छाई॥ नदी नाव पटु प्रस्न अनेका। केवट कुसल उतर सबिबेका ॥
ramacharitamanas::267.verse_hindi: श्री सीताजी के स्वयंवर की जो सुन्दर कथा है, वह इस नदी में सुहावनी छबि छा रही है। अनेकों सुंदर विचारपूर्ण प्रश्न ही इस नदी की नावें हैं और उनके विवेकयुक्त उत्तर ही चतुर केवट हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::267.english_translation: The beautiful story of Sita's swayamvara shines like a lovely river. Many graceful, thoughtful questions are its boats, and wise answers are the skilled boatmen.
ramacharitamanas::267.translation_literal: सीय (of Sita) / स्वयंबर (swayamvara) / कथा (story) / सुहाई (beautiful) / सरित (river) / सुहावनि (pleasant) / सो (that) / छबि (beauty) / छाई (spread) / नदी (river) / नाव (boats) / पटु (skilled) / प्रस्न (questions) / अनेका (many) / केवट (boatman) / कुसल (skillful) / उतर (answers) / सबिबेका (wise)
ramacharitamanas::267.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::267.essence: Questions and wise answers carry the story like boats on a river.
ramacharitamanas::267.simple_meaning: The story of Sita's swayamvara is being compared to a beautiful river. Its questions and answers are like boats and boatmen that carry the story forward.
ramacharitamanas::267.simple_insight: A good story carries you when every question has a fitting answer.
ramacharitamanas::267.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still in the opening river image of the Balkand, where the whole Ram story is being pictured as a flowing stream. Here, Sita's swayamvara is one bright feature in that stream: its questions and answers move the story onward.
ramacharitamanas::267.modern_relevance: A family gathering turns into a chain of questions, stories, and sharp replies that keep everyone leaning in. The conversation itself becomes the pleasure.
ramacharitamanas::267.insight: It frames storytelling as something that moves through curiosity and wise responses, not just events.

ramacharitamanas::268.verse_sanskrit: सुनि अनुकथन परस्पर होई। पथिक समाज सोह सरि सोई॥ घोर धार भृगुनाथ रिसानी। घाट सुबद्ध राम बर बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::268.verse_hindi: इस कथा को सुनकर पीछे जो आपस में चर्चा होती है, वही इस नदी के सहारे-सहारे चलने वाले यात्रियों का समाज शोभा पा रहा है। परशुरामजी का क्रोध इस नदी की भयानक धारा है और श्री रामचंद्रजी के श्रेष्ठ वचन ही सुंदर बँधे हुए घाट हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::268.english_translation: Hearing the story and the back-and-forth discussion it inspires, the company of travelers along this river becomes beautiful. Parashurama's fierce anger is the river's wild current, and Ram's noble words are its well-built banks.
ramacharitamanas::268.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / अनुकथन (back-and-forth discussion) / परस्पर (among one another) / होई (happens) / पथिक (travelers) / समाज (company) / सोह (adorns) / सरि (river) / सोई (that) ॥ / घोर (fierce) / धार (current) / भृगुनाथ (Lord of Bhrigu, Parashurama) / रिसानी (angry) / घाट (banks/ghats) / सुबद्ध (well-built) / राम (Ram) / बर (excellent) / बानी (words) ॥
ramacharitamanas::268.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::268.essence: Ram's words turn a dangerous current into a passage.
ramacharitamanas::268.simple_meaning: Listening to this story makes the whole gathering feel beautiful. Parashurama's anger is like a rough current, while Ram's fine words are like strong riverbanks that hold everything together.
ramacharitamanas::268.simple_insight: Even conflict can become part of a larger beauty when wisdom gives it shape.
ramacharitamanas::268.detailed_meaning: The story is pausing at the Sita swayamvar, and Tulsidas turns the whole narration into a river image. Parashurama's fury is the dangerous current; Ram's calm, fitting words are the banks that let the journey continue.
ramacharitamanas::268.modern_relevance: A tense family dinner starts to spiral when one harsh comment lands. Then one person speaks carefully, and the whole room steadies. That is the kind of bank this verse praises.
ramacharitamanas::268.insight: It teaches you to see good speech as structure: it contains conflict without denying it.

ramacharitamanas::269.verse_sanskrit: सानुज राम बिबाह उछाहू। सो सुभ उमग सुखद सब काहू॥ कहत सुनत हरषहिं पुलकाहीं। ते सुकृती मन मुदित नहाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::269.verse_hindi: भाइयों सहित श्री रामचंद्रजी के विवाह का उत्साह ही इस कथा नदी की कल्याणकारिणी बाढ़ है, जो सभी को सुख देने वाली है। इसके कहने-सुनने में जो हर्षित और पुलकित होते हैं, वे ही पुण्यात्मा पुरुष हैं, जो प्रसन्न मन से इस नदी में नहाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::269.english_translation: The joy of Ram's wedding with his brothers is this story's blessed flood. Those who hear it with delight and goosebumps are the truly fortunate, bathing in it with a joyful mind.
ramacharitamanas::269.translation_literal: सानुज (with brothers) / राम (Ram) / बिबाह (wedding) / उछाहू (joy, celebration) / सो (that) / सुभ (auspicious) / उमग (overflowing delight) / सुखद (giving joy) / सब (all) / काहू (to whomsoever) / कहत (saying) / सुनत (hearing) / हरषहिं (they rejoice) / पुलकाहीं (they thrill, their hair stands on end) / ते (those) / सुकृती (fortunate, virtuous) / मन (mind) / मुदित (glad) / नहाहीं (bathe)
ramacharitamanas::269.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::269.essence: Joy in Ram's wedding marks a heart made ready for blessing.
ramacharitamanas::269.simple_meaning: Ram's wedding story brings joy to everyone. Those who listen with delight and emotion are the fortunate ones.
ramacharitamanas::269.simple_insight: Joy itself becomes a sign that the heart is ready to receive blessing.
ramacharitamanas::269.detailed_meaning: The Sita-swayamvar story is moving toward its celebration, and Tulsidas pauses to praise the feeling around it. Ram's wedding with his brothers present is described as a flood of auspicious joy, and anyone who hears it with delight is called fortunate.
ramacharitamanas::269.modern_relevance: You hear a family story at a wedding and suddenly everyone is smiling through tears. Some moments don't just entertain you — they wash you clean from the inside.
ramacharitamanas::269.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the heart's response, treating joyful reverence as spiritual fitness.

ramacharitamanas::270.verse_sanskrit: राम तिलक हित मंगल साजा। परब जोग जनु जुरे समाजा। काई कुमति केकई केरी। परी जासु फल बिपति घनेरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::270.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी के राजतिलक के लिए जो मंगल साज सजाया गया, वही मानो पर्व के समय इस नदी पर यात्रियों के समूह इकट्ठे हुए हैं। कैकेयी की कुबुद्धि ही इस नदी में काई है, जिसके फलस्वरूप बड़ी भारी विपत्ति आ पड़ी ॥
ramacharitamanas::270.english_translation: For Ram's coronation, auspicious preparations were made. It was like a festive gathering of travellers. Kaikeyi's evil-mindedness was the moss, and its fruit was a great flood of suffering.
ramacharitamanas::270.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / तिलक (coronation) / हित (for the sake of) / मंगल (auspicious) / साजा (arranged) / परब (festival) / जोग (as if fitting) / जनु (like) / जुरे (assembled) / समाजा (group) / काई (moss) / कुमति (evil-mindedness) / केकई (Kaikeyi's) / केरी (of) / परी (fell) / जासु (whose) / फल (fruit) / बिपति (calamity) / घनेरी (very great)
ramacharitamanas::270.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::270.essence: Joy can be undone by one corrupted mind.
ramacharitamanas::270.simple_meaning: Ram's coronation was being prepared with joy, but Kaikeyi's wrong thinking became the cause of a terrible disaster.
ramacharitamanas::270.simple_insight: A single corrupted intention can spoil a whole season of joy.
ramacharitamanas::270.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the court is alive with preparations for Ram's coronation. The mood is festive, like travellers gathering at a holy riverbank. But Tulsidas turns the scene dark: Kaikeyi's poisoned mind is the moss that will cling to everything and bring disaster.
ramacharitamanas::270.modern_relevance: A room full of celebration can change in one sentence when one person brings hidden resentment. The mood, the plans, even the future can tilt because of one unspoken corruption.
ramacharitamanas::270.insight: It shifts attention from the visible celebration to the hidden cause that will unravel it.

ramacharitamanas::271.verse_sanskrit: समन अमित उतपात सब भरत चरित जपजाग। कलि अघ खल अवगुन कथन ते जलमल बग काग ॥
ramacharitamanas::271.verse_hindi: संपूर्ण अनगिनत उत्पातों को शांत करने वाला भरतजी का चरित्र नदी तट पर किया जाने वाला जपयज्ञ है। कलियुग के पापों और दुष्टों के अवगुणों के जो वर्णन हैं, वे ही इस नदी के जल का कीचड़ और बगुले-कौए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::271.english_translation: Bharat's character is the ritual-fire that burns away countless disturbances. Talk of the sins of Kali Yuga and the faults of the wicked is only the mud, herons, and crows in this river.
ramacharitamanas::271.translation_literal: समन (pacifying) / अमित (countless) / उतपात (disturbances) / सब (all) / भरत चरित (Bharat's character) / जपजाग (ritual-fire of chanting and sacrifice) / कलि अघ (sins of Kali Yuga) / खल (wicked) / अवगुन (faults) / कथन (talk, description) / ते (from, as) / जलमल (water-mud, dirt) / बग (herons) / काग (crows)
ramacharitamanas::271.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::271.essence: Bharat's character purifies what criticism only stains.
ramacharitamanas::271.simple_meaning: Bharat's character is so pure that it calms chaos and purifies the mind. By contrast, empty talk about corruption and bad people only adds dirt and distraction.
ramacharitamanas::271.simple_insight: Real purity is lived, not discussed. A steady character can quiet what endless criticism only stirs up.
ramacharitamanas::271.detailed_meaning: After the wedding joy and the royal preparations, Tulsidas turns to Bharat. In the middle of Ayodhyakand's heartbreak, Bharat's conduct becomes the standard that steadies everything. His character is praised as a force that settles disturbance, while blame and cynicism are dismissed as river-mud.
ramacharitamanas::271.modern_relevance: A family group chat fills with complaints, blame, and old grievances after one bad decision. One person stays calm, does the needed work, and refuses the noise. That person changes the room more than ten arguments.
ramacharitamanas::271.insight: It shifts attention from judging corruption to embodying steadiness that actually cleans the situation.

ramacharitamanas::272.verse_sanskrit: कीरति सरित छहूँ रितु रूरी। समय सुहावनि पावनि भूरी॥ हिम हिमसैलसुता सिव ब्याहू। सिसिर सुखद प्रभु जनम उछाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::272.verse_hindi: यह कीर्तिरूपिणी नदी छहों ऋतुओं में सुंदर है। सभी समय यह परम सुहावनी और अत्यंत पवित्र है। इसमें शिव-पार्वती का विवाह हेमंत ऋतु है। श्री रामचंद्रजी के जन्म का उत्सव सुखदायी शिशिर ऋतु है ॥
ramacharitamanas::272.english_translation: The river of fame is beautiful in all six seasons. It is always lovely, always pure. Shiva and Parvati's wedding is the cool season of winter. Lord Ram's birth celebration is the joy-giving season of early winter.
ramacharitamanas::272.translation_literal: कीरति (fame) / सरित (river) / छहूँ (six) / रितु (seasons) / रूरी (beautiful) / समय (time) / सुहावनि (lovely) / पावनि (purifying) / भूरी (much) ॥ / हिम (cold) / हिमसैलसुता (daughter of the snowy mountain) / सिव (Shiva) / ब्याहू (wedding) / सिसिर (winter) / सुखद (pleasant) / प्रभु (Lord) / जनम (birth) / उछाहू (joy)
ramacharitamanas::272.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::272.essence: Ram's story stays fresh, pure, and life-giving in every season.
ramacharitamanas::272.simple_meaning: Ram's story is like a sacred river that stays beautiful and pure through every season. Shiva and Parvati's wedding and Ram's birth are presented as two especially blessed moments in that flow.
ramacharitamanas::272.simple_insight: Sacred events do not fade with time; they keep giving freshness, beauty, and meaning again and again.
ramacharitamanas::272.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses in the Balkand to praise Ram's story itself. He compares it to a river that remains beautiful in every season, then names two great sacred moments within it: Shiva and Parvati's wedding, and Ram's birth. The verse lifts the whole narrative into devotional celebration.
ramacharitamanas::272.modern_relevance: You return to an old family story at a festival table, and it still feels alive. Some memories do not age into the past; they keep washing the present clean.
ramacharitamanas::272.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the enduring holiness of remembering it.

ramacharitamanas::273.verse_sanskrit: बरनब राम बिबाह समाजू। सो मुद मंगलमय रितुराजू॥ ग्रीषम दुसह राम बनगवनू। पंथकथा खर आतप पवनू ॥
ramacharitamanas::273.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी के विवाह समाज का वर्णन ही आनंद-मंगलमय ऋतुराज वसंत है। श्री रामजी का वनगमन दुःसह ग्रीष्म ऋतु है और मार्ग की कथा ही कड़ी धूप और लू है ॥
ramacharitamanas::273.english_translation: The account of Ram's wedding assembly is the joyful spring. Ram's exile to the forest is unbearable summer. The story of the journey is harsh sun and hot wind.
ramacharitamanas::273.translation_literal: बरनन (description) / राम (Ram) / बिबाह समाजू (wedding assembly) / सो (that) / मुद (joy) / मंगलमय (full of auspiciousness) / रितुराजू (king of seasons, spring) || ग्रीषम (summer) / दुसह (hard to bear) / राम (Ram) / बनगवनू (going to the forest) / पंथकथा (story of the path/journey) / खर (harsh) / आतप (sun heat) / पवनू (wind)
ramacharitamanas::273.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::273.essence: Ram's joy and exile are two seasons of the same sacred story.
ramacharitamanas::273.simple_meaning: Ram's wedding is like spring, full of joy and blessing. His exile is like unbearable summer, and the journey itself feels scorching and harsh.
ramacharitamanas::273.simple_insight: Joy and sorrow can belong to the same life, and both can be seen clearly.
ramacharitamanas::273.detailed_meaning: The poem is still painting Ram's life through the seasons. His wedding shines like spring, but the next turn is exile, which burns like summer heat. The contrast prepares the reader for the emotional fracture that follows.
ramacharitamanas::273.modern_relevance: A wedding album sits beside a train ticket to a new city, and both belong to the same week. One moment glows; the next feels like leaving everything behind.
ramacharitamanas::273.insight: It teaches you to see a single life as holding opposite seasons without confusion.

ramacharitamanas::274.verse_sanskrit: बरषा घोर निसाचर रारी। सुरकुल सालि सुमंगलकारी॥ राम राज सुख बिनय बड़ाई। बिसद सुखद सोइ सरद सुहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::274.verse_hindi: राक्षसों के साथ घोर युद्ध ही वर्षा ऋतु है, जो देवकुल रूपी धान के लिए सुंदर कल्याण करने वाली है। रामचंद्रजी के राज्यकाल का जो सुख, विनम्रता और बड़ाई है, वही निर्मल सुख देने वाली सुहावनी शरद् ऋतु है ॥
ramacharitamanas::274.english_translation: The fierce war with the night-roamers is the rainy season, bringing great blessing to the crop of the radiant ones. The joy, humility, and greatness of Ram's reign are the lovely autumn, giving pure and refreshing happiness.
ramacharitamanas::274.translation_literal: बरषा (rainy season) / घोर (fierce) / निसाचर (night-roamers) / रारी (war) / सुरकुल (family of radiant beings) / सालि (paddy crop) / सुमंगलकारी (bringing great auspiciousness) ॥ राम राज (Ram's reign) / सुख (joy) / बिनय (humility) / बड़ाई (greatness) / बिसद (pure) / सुखद (giving happiness) / सोइ (that) / सरद (autumn) / सुहाई (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::274.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::274.essence: Even battle can nourish goodness, and rightful rule becomes calm beauty.
ramacharitamanas::274.simple_meaning: The poet compares Ram's story to seasons: fierce battles are like rain that nourishes goodness, and Ram's reign is like clear autumn, full of peace, humility, and delight.
ramacharitamanas::274.simple_insight: Even struggle can nourish what is good, and right rule can feel like a season of calm.
ramacharitamanas::274.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues his seasonal metaphor for Ram's life. The war with the night-roamers becomes the nourishing monsoon, while Ram's reign becomes the clean, pleasant autumn. The passage turns the whole story into a cycle where conflict and peace both serve a higher harmony.
ramacharitamanas::274.modern_relevance: A tense family meeting leaves everyone raw, yet it clears the air and makes honesty possible. Later, when things settle, the room feels lighter than before. Hard seasons and calm seasons both have their place.
ramacharitamanas::274.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing conflict as only damage to seeing it as part of a larger restoration.

ramacharitamanas::275.verse_sanskrit: सती सिरोमनि सिय गुन गाथा। सोइ गुन अमल अनूपम पाथा॥ भरत सुभाउ सुसीतलताई। सदा एकरस बरनि न जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::275.verse_hindi: सती-शिरोमणि श्री सीताजी के गुणों की जो कथा है, वही इस जल का निर्मल और अनुपम गुण है। श्री भरतजी का स्वभाव इस नदी की सुंदर शीतलता है, जो सदा एक सी रहती है और जिसका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::275.english_translation: The story of Sita, the foremost devoted woman, is this water's pure and incomparable quality. Bharat's nature is this river's lovely coolness, always the same and beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::275.translation_literal: सती-शिरोमनि (foremost among devoted women) / सिय (Sita) / गुन (qualities) / गाथा (story, account) / सोइ (that same) / गुन (quality) / अमल (pure, spotless) / अनूपम (matchless) / पाथा (path, water) || भरत (Bharat) / सुभाउ (nature, temperament) / सुसीतलताई (coolness, soothingness) / सदा (always) / एकरस (of one taste, unchanged) / बरनि (described) / न जाई (cannot be)
ramacharitamanas::275.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::275.essence: Pure character is calm, steady, and impossible to exhaust in words.
ramacharitamanas::275.simple_meaning: Sita's character is like pure, clear water. Bharat's nature is like a river's cool, steady flow that never changes and cannot be fully described.
ramacharitamanas::275.simple_insight: True goodness feels cleansing and steady, not flashy or noisy.
ramacharitamanas::275.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is comparing the wedding gathering to sacred water imagery. Sita's virtues are pure and unmatched, while Bharat's calm, unchanging nature is like a cool river. The verse prepares the reader for the brothers' tender bond in the next line.
ramacharitamanas::275.modern_relevance: In a room full of loud opinions, one person stays gentle, steady, and unshaken. You feel it immediately: this is the kind of character that cools everyone around them.
ramacharitamanas::275.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic display to quiet, reliable virtue.

ramacharitamanas::276.verse_sanskrit: अवलोकनि बोलनि मिलनि प्रीति परसपर हास। भायप भलि चहु बंधु की जल माधुरी सुबास ॥
ramacharitamanas::276.verse_hindi: चारों भाइयों का परस्पर देखना, बोलना, मिलना, एक-दूसरे से प्रेम करना, हँसना और सुंदर भाईपना इस जल की मधुरता और सुगंध है ॥
ramacharitamanas::276.english_translation: The four brothers' seeing, speaking, meeting, loving one another, laughing, and beautiful brotherhood are the water's sweetness and fragrance.
ramacharitamanas::276.translation_literal: अवलोकनि (looking at one another) / बोलनि (speaking) / मिलनि (meeting) / प्रीति (love) / परसपर (mutual) / हास (laughter) / भायप (brotherhood) / भलि (beautiful) / चहु बंधु (the four brothers) / की (of) / जल (water) / माधुरी (sweetness) / सुबास (fragrance)
ramacharitamanas::276.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::276.essence: Brotherly love is the sweetness that makes life fragrant.
ramacharitamanas::276.simple_meaning: The four brothers' affection makes their togetherness feel sweet and fragrant, like pure water.
ramacharitamanas::276.simple_insight: Love shared naturally makes a family feel light, warm, and alive.
ramacharitamanas::276.detailed_meaning: In the closing comparison of this passage, the narrator turns the brothers' bond into the sweetness of clean water. Their glances, words, meetings, laughter, and mutual affection are presented as the fragrance of their brotherhood.
ramacharitamanas::276.modern_relevance: A family group chat fills with teasing, care, and easy laughter after a hard week. Nothing dramatic is said, yet the room feels softer because everyone is simply glad to be together.
ramacharitamanas::276.insight: It shifts attention from grand events to the quiet sweetness created by mutual affection.

ramacharitamanas::277.verse_sanskrit: आरति बिनय दीनता मोरी। लघुता ललित सुबारि न थोरी॥ अदभुत सलिल सुनत गुनकारी। आस पिआस मनोमल हारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::277.verse_hindi: मेरा आर्तभाव, विनय और दीनता इस सुंदर और निर्मल जल का कम हलकापन नहीं है (अर्थात् अत्यंत हलकापन है)। यह जल बड़ा ही अनोखा है, जो सुनने से ही गुण करता है और आशा रूपी प्यास को और मन के मैल को दूर कर देता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::277.english_translation: My distress, humility, and meekness are not a small part of this lovely, pure water. This wondrous water blesses even by hearing of it; it removes the mind's dirt and the thirst of hope.
ramacharitamanas::277.translation_literal: आरति (distress) / बिनय (humility) / दीनता (meekness) / मोरी (my) / लघुता (smallness) / ललित (lovely) / सुबारि (pure water) / न थोरी (not little) / अदभुत (wondrous) / सलिल (water) / सुनत (on hearing) / गुनकारी (beneficial) / आस (hope) / पिआस (thirst) / मनोमल (mind-dirt) / हारी (removes)
ramacharitamanas::277.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::277.essence: Humility becomes cleansing when it is offered to the divine.
ramacharitamanas::277.simple_meaning: Humility, distress, and meekness are like pure water here. Just hearing of it helps remove hope's thirst and the mind's dirt.
ramacharitamanas::277.simple_insight: Smallness before the divine can become cleansing, not shameful.
ramacharitamanas::277.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues praising the sacred water that carries Ram's presence. He says his own humility, distress, and meekness are part of that purity. Even hearing about this water begins to cleanse longing and inner stain.
ramacharitamanas::277.modern_relevance: You hear a song or prayer after a hard day, and something in you loosens before you can explain why. Some things heal simply by being received with humility.
ramacharitamanas::277.insight: It shifts the reader from self-importance to receptivity, showing that humility itself can purify the mind.

ramacharitamanas::278.verse_sanskrit: राम सुप्रेमहि पोषत पानी। हरत सकल कलि कलुष गलानी॥ भव श्रम सोषक तोषक तोषा। समन दुरित दुख दारिद दोषा ॥
ramacharitamanas::278.verse_hindi: यह जल श्री रामचंद्रजी के सुंदर प्रेम को पुष्ट करता है, कलियुग के समस्त पापों और उनसे होने वाली ग्लानि को हर लेता है। (संसार के जन्म-मृत्यु रूप) श्रम को सोख लेता है, संतोष को भी संतुष्ट करता है और पाप, दरिद्रता और दोषों को नष्ट कर देता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::278.english_translation: The water nourishes Ram's loving devotion, removes the stains of Kali Yuga, soothes the weariness of worldly wandering, satisfies contentment, and destroys faults, suffering, poverty, and defects.
ramacharitamanas::278.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सुप्रेमहि (loving devotion) / पोषत (nourishes) / पानी (water) / हरत (removes) / सकल (all) / कलि (of Kali Yuga) / कलुष (stains) / गलानी (weariness, shame) / भव (worldly becoming) / श्रम (weariness) / सोषक (soaking up) / तोषक (satisfying) / तोषा (contentment) / समन (removes) / दुरित (faults) / दुख (suffering) / दारिद (poverty) / दोषा (defects)
ramacharitamanas::278.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::278.essence: Sacred water feeds love for Ram and strips away life’s stains.
ramacharitamanas::278.simple_meaning: The water strengthens love for Ram and removes the stains, weariness, suffering, poverty, and faults of worldly life.
ramacharitamanas::278.simple_insight: Purity is not just cleansing; it can also deepen devotion and lighten the heart.
ramacharitamanas::278.detailed_meaning: In the sacred lake being praised, the speaker says this water does more than cleanse the body. It nourishes love for Ram, removes the burdens of Kali Yuga, and eases the pain, poverty, and flaws that weigh on human life.
ramacharitamanas::278.modern_relevance: You stand under a shower after a day that felt contaminated by bad news, guilt, and exhaustion. Some places do more than clean you — they give you back a softer heart.
ramacharitamanas::278.insight: It shifts cleansing from a physical act to a devotional renewal that clears both burden and doubt.

ramacharitamanas::279.verse_sanskrit: काम कोह मद मोह नसावन। बिमल बिबेक बिराग बढ़ावन॥ सादर मज्जन पान किए तें। मिटहिं पाप परिताप हिए तें ॥
ramacharitamanas::279.verse_hindi: यह जल काम, क्रोध, मद और मोह का नाश करने वाला और निर्मल ज्ञान और वैराग्य को बढ़ाने वाला है। इसमें आदरपूर्वक स्नान करने से और इसे पीने से हृदय में रहने वाले सब पाप-ताप मिट जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::279.english_translation: It destroys desire, anger, pride, and delusion, and increases pure discernment and non-attachment. Reverent bathing in it, and drinking it, removes the sins and inner suffering stored in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::279.translation_literal: काम (desire) / कोह (anger) / मद (pride) / मोह (delusion) / नसावन (destroying) / बिमल (pure) / बिबेक (discernment) / बिराग (non-attachment) / बढ़ावन (increasing) / सादर (with reverence) / मज्जन (bathing) / पान (drinking) / किए (having done) / तें (from) / मिटहिं (are removed) / पाप (sins) / परिताप (burning distress) / हिए तें (from the heart)
ramacharitamanas::279.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::279.essence: Sacred contact can transform the mind, not just the body.
ramacharitamanas::279.simple_meaning: Ram's sacred water removes desire, anger, pride, and delusion. It deepens clear seeing and non-attachment, and it washes away inner suffering from the heart.
ramacharitamanas::279.simple_insight: Inner cleansing is possible. What you take in with reverence can reshape the mind itself.
ramacharitamanas::279.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the holy water connected with Ram's praise. He says that reverent contact with it does more than purify the body: it weakens craving, anger, pride, and confusion, while strengthening clear seeing and non-attachment.
ramacharitamanas::279.modern_relevance: You step out of a tense shower after a day of arguments, doomscrolling, and self-criticism. Some experiences don't just refresh you; they change what keeps repeating in your mind.
ramacharitamanas::279.insight: It shifts the aim from external cleansing to inner reordering: less craving, more discernment, less grip, more release.

ramacharitamanas::280.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह एहिं बारि न मानस धोए। ते कायर कलिकाल बिगोए॥ तृषित निरखि रबि कर भव बारी। फिरिहहिं मृग जिमि जीव दुखारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::280.verse_hindi: जिन्होंने इस (राम सुयश रूपी) जल से अपने हृदय को नहीं धोया, वे कायर कलिकाल के द्वारा ठगे गए। जैसे प्यासा हिरन सूर्य की किरणों के रेत पर पड़ने से उत्पन्न हुए जल के भ्रम को वास्तविक जल समझकर पीने को दौड़ता है और जल न पाकर दुःखी होता है, वैसे ही वे (कलियुग से ठगे हुए) जीव भी (विषयों के पीछे भटककर) दुःखी होंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::280.english_translation: Those who do not wash their minds in this water are fools misled by the age of darkness. Like a thirsty deer chasing a mirage in the sun's rays, they run after life and suffer.
ramacharitamanas::280.translation_literal: जिन्ह (those who) / एहिं बारि (in this water) / न (not) / मानस (mind) / धोए (washed) / ते (they) / कायर (cowardly) / कलिकाल (the dark age) / बिगोए (ruined, deceived) ॥ तृषित (thirsty) / निरखि (seeing) / रबि कर (sun rays) / भव बारी (world-water, mirage water) / फिरिहहिं (they will run around) / मृग (deer) / जिमि (like) / जीव (living beings) / दुखारी (suffering) ॥
ramacharitamanas::280.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::280.essence: Ignore Ram's remembrance, and mirages begin to look like water.
ramacharitamanas::280.simple_meaning: Without cleansing the mind with Ram's praise, a person gets trapped by illusions and chases things that cannot satisfy. That only leads to suffering.
ramacharitamanas::280.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that not every desire deserves pursuit.
ramacharitamanas::280.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising the sacred water of Ram's name and glory. He warns that anyone who ignores it stays vulnerable to the tricks of Kali Yuga, like a thirsty deer running after a mirage and ending up empty.
ramacharitamanas::280.modern_relevance: You scroll for one more answer, one more purchase, one more distraction — and still feel dry. The mind that never pauses for Ram's name keeps chasing reflections and calling them relief.
ramacharitamanas::280.insight: It shifts attention from chasing appearances to cleansing the mind with remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::281.verse_sanskrit: मति अनुहारि सुबारि गुन गन गनि मन अन्हवाइ। सुमिरि भवानी संकरहि कह कबि कथा सुहाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::281.verse_hindi: अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार इस सुंदर जल के गुणों को विचार कर, उसमें अपने मन को स्नान कराकर और श्री भवानी-शंकर को स्मरण करके कवि (तुलसीदास) सुंदर कथा कहता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::281.english_translation: Thinking over its virtues in line with one’s own understanding, bathing the mind in that beautiful water, and remembering Bhavani and Shankar, the poet speaks the lovely कथा.
ramacharitamanas::281.translation_literal: मति (understanding) / अनुहारि (according to) / सुबारि (beautiful water) / गुन गन (groups of qualities) / गनि (counting) / मन (mind) / अन्हवाइ (bathing) / सुमिरि (remembering) / भवानी (Bhavani) / संकरहि (Shankar) / कह (says) / कबि (poet) / कथा (story) / सुहाइ (lovely)
ramacharitamanas::281.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::281.essence: Pure speech begins with a purified mind.
ramacharitamanas::281.simple_meaning: The poet says he will reflect on the water’s qualities, bathe his mind in them, remember Shiva and Parvati, and then tell the beautiful story.
ramacharitamanas::281.simple_insight: Before telling sacred stories, the mind is purified and the divine is remembered.
ramacharitamanas::281.detailed_meaning: The opening frame of the Balkand is still being set. Tulsidas prepares to speak by cleansing his mind in the virtues of Ram’s glory and invoking Bhavani and Shankar. This verse is a transition, not the main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::281.modern_relevance: Before speaking at a memorial, you pause, breathe, and gather yourself so your words carry care instead of noise.
ramacharitamanas::281.insight: It shifts the reader from casual speech to reverent preparation.

ramacharitamanas::282.verse_sanskrit: अब रघुपति पद पंकरुह हियँ धरि पाइ प्रसाद। कहउँ जुगल मुनिबर्य कर मिलन सुभग संबाद ॥
ramacharitamanas::282.verse_hindi: मैं अब श्री रघुनाथजी के चरण कमलों को हृदय में धारण कर और उनका प्रसाद पाकर दोनों श्रेष्ठ मुनियों के मिलन का सुंदर संवाद वर्णन करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::282.english_translation: Now, holding the lotus feet of Raghupati in my heart and receiving His grace, I describe the beautiful dialogue of the meeting of the two great sages.
ramacharitamanas::282.translation_literal: अब (now) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / पद (feet) / पंकरुह (lotus) / हियँ (in the heart) / धरि (placing) / पाइ (having received) / प्रसाद (grace) / कहउँ (I describe) / जुगल (the two) / मुनिबर्य (best of sages) / कर (of) / मिलन (meeting) / सुभग (beautiful) / संबाद (dialogue)
ramacharitamanas::282.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::282.essence: Grace comes first; the telling comes after.
ramacharitamanas::282.simple_meaning: The poet says he writes only after holding Ram in his heart and receiving grace. Then he will tell the beautiful dialogue between two great sages.
ramacharitamanas::282.simple_insight: Even telling the story begins with humility and grace.
ramacharitamanas::282.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses before entering the next scene. He bows inwardly to Ram, asks for grace, and only then turns to the meeting of Bharadvaj and Yajnavalkya. The verse marks a devotional transition from praise into narration.
ramacharitamanas::282.modern_relevance: Before speaking about something sacred or important, you take a breath, steady yourself, and remember you are not the source of the whole meaning. Then the words come cleaner.
ramacharitamanas::282.insight: It shifts writing and speech from self-expression to reverent offering.

ramacharitamanas::283.verse_sanskrit: भरद्वाज मुनि बसहिं प्रयागा। तिन्हहि राम पद अति अनुरागा॥ तापस सम दम दया निधाना। परमारथ पथ परम सुजाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::283.verse_hindi: भरद्वाज मुनि प्रयाग में बसते हैं, उनका श्री रामजी के चरणों में अत्यंत प्रेम है। वे तपस्वी, निगृहीत चित्त, जितेन्द्रिय, दया के निधान और परमार्थ के मार्ग में बड़े ही चतुर हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::283.english_translation: Bharadwaj Muni lives in Prayag. He has deep love for Ram's feet. He is an ascetic, master of self-control, a treasure of compassion, and deeply skilled in the path of higher purpose.
ramacharitamanas::283.translation_literal: भरद्वाज मुनि (sage Bharadwaj) / बसहिं (live) / प्रयागा (in Prayag) / तिन्हहि (for him) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / अति (very) / अनुरागा (deep love) / तापस (ascetic) / सम (equal-minded) / दम (self-restraint) / दया (compassion) / निधाना (treasure) / परमारथ (higher purpose) / पथ (path) / परम (supremely) / सुजाना (wise)
ramacharitamanas::283.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::283.essence: Deep love for Ram becomes discipline, compassion, and wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::283.simple_meaning: Bharadwaj lives in Prayag and loves Ram deeply. He is disciplined, compassionate, and wise about the higher path.
ramacharitamanas::283.simple_insight: A devoted life is not only feeling; it also shows up as restraint, compassion, and clear conduct.
ramacharitamanas::283.detailed_meaning: The story has moved to Prayag, where Bharadwaj Muni lives as a great devotee of Ram. Tulsidas pauses to describe his inner character before the sacred meeting of the two sages, showing why his words carry spiritual weight.
ramacharitamanas::283.modern_relevance: Someone can live quietly in one place, unseen by crowds, and still be inwardly complete. The real measure is not attention but the steadiness of love, discipline, and compassion.
ramacharitamanas::283.insight: It shifts attention from status to character: devotion must mature into self-mastery and care for others.

ramacharitamanas::284.verse_sanskrit: माघ मकरगत रबि जब होई। तीरथपतिहिं आव सब कोई॥ देव दनुज किंनर नर श्रेनीं। सादर मज्जहिं सकल त्रिबेनीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::284.verse_hindi: माघ में जब सूर्य मकर राशि पर जाते हैं, तब सब लोग तीर्थराज प्रयाग को आते हैं। देवता, दैत्य, किन्नर और मनुष्यों के समूह सब आदरपूर्वक त्रिवेणी में स्नान करते हैं॥।2॥
ramacharitamanas::284.english_translation: When the sun enters Capricorn in the month of Magha, everyone comes to the lord of pilgrimages. Gods, demons, celestial beings, and human groups all bathe reverently in the Triveni.
ramacharitamanas::284.translation_literal: माघ (the month of Magha) / मकरगत (entered Capricorn) / रबि (sun) / जब (when) / होई (becomes) / तीरथपतिहिं (to the lord of pilgrimages) / आव (come) / सब (all) / कोई (everyone) / देव (deities) / दनुज (demons) / किंनर (celestial beings) / नर (humans) / श्रेनीं (groups) / सादर (with reverence) / मज्जहिं (bathe) / सकल (all) / त्रिबेनीं (Triveni)
ramacharitamanas::284.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::284.essence: Sacred places erase rank; reverence pulls everyone to the same water.
ramacharitamanas::284.simple_meaning: At the sacred time of Magha, all kinds of beings come to Prayagraj and bathe at the Triveni with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::284.simple_insight: Some places draw everyone equally when reverence is strong enough.
ramacharitamanas::284.detailed_meaning: Bhardwaj’s sacred setting opens into a larger vision of Prayag. When the sun enters Capricorn in Magha, even deities, beings of shadow, celestial singers, and human crowds gather at the confluence to bathe. The verse prepares for the holiness of the place, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::284.modern_relevance: A festival morning at a riverbank, with families, strangers, and pilgrims all moving toward the same water, makes status feel small and reverence feel shared.
ramacharitamanas::284.insight: It shifts attention from who arrives to the shared act of honoring what is sacred.

ramacharitamanas::285.verse_sanskrit: पूजहिं माधव पद जलजाता। परसि अखय बटु हरषहिं गाता॥ भरद्वाज आश्रम अति पावन। परम रम्य मुनिबर मन भावन ॥
ramacharitamanas::285.verse_hindi: श्री वेणीमाधवजी के चरणकमलों को पूजते हैं और अक्षयवट का स्पर्श कर उनके शरीर पुलकित होते हैं। भरद्वाजजी का आश्रम बहुत ही पवित्र, परम रमणीय और श्रेष्ठ मुनियों के मन को भाने वाला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::285.english_translation: They worship the lotus feet of Madhava and rejoice on touching the Akshaya Banyan. Bharadwaja's hermitage is very pure, supremely beautiful, and dear to the hearts of great sages.
ramacharitamanas::285.translation_literal: पूजहिं (worship) / माधव पद जलजाता (Madhava's lotus feet) / परसि (touching) / अखय बटु (Akshaya Banyan) / हरषहिं (rejoice) / गाता (bodies) / भरद्वाज आश्रम (Bharadwaja's hermitage) / अति पावन (very pure) / परम रम्य (supremely beautiful) / मुनिबर मन भावन (pleasing to the minds of great sages)
ramacharitamanas::285.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::285.essence: Sacred places awaken joy before any teaching begins.
ramacharitamanas::285.simple_meaning: Pilgrims worship the sacred place, touch the eternal banyan tree, and feel joy. Bharadwaja's hermitage is described as pure, beautiful, and beloved by sages.
ramacharitamanas::285.simple_insight: Holy places matter because they gather reverence, memory, and joy into one lived experience.
ramacharitamanas::285.detailed_meaning: At Prayag, the crowd of pilgrims has already been described. Now Tulsidas turns to Bharadwaja's hermitage itself: a place where people worship Madhava, touch the Akshaya Banyan, and feel their bodies thrill with devotion. The scene deepens the sanctity of the pilgrimage setting.
ramacharitamanas::285.modern_relevance: You step into an old temple courtyard after a long train ride, and the noise in your head drops. The place itself changes how you stand, breathe, and remember what matters.
ramacharitamanas::285.insight: It shifts attention from sightseeing to reverent presence in a charged place.

ramacharitamanas::286.verse_sanskrit: तहाँ होइ मुनि रिषय समाजा। जाहिं जे मज्जन तीरथराजा॥ मज्जहिं प्रात समेत उछाहा। कहहिं परसपर हरि गुन गाहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::286.verse_hindi: तीर्थराज प्रयाग में जो स्नान करने जाते हैं, उन ऋषि-मुनियों का समाज वहाँ (भरद्वाज के आश्रम में) जुटता है। प्रातःकाल सब उत्साहपूर्वक स्नान करते हैं और फिर परस्पर भगवान् के गुणों की कथाएँ कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::286.english_translation: There, a gathering of sages and seers assembled. Those who bathe at the king of holy places bathe there at dawn with joy, and then they speak to one another of the divine's qualities.
ramacharitamanas::286.translation_literal: तहाँ (there) / होइ (happens) / मुनि (sage) / रिषय (seers) / समाजा (assembly) / जाहिं (go) / जे (those who) / मज्जन (bathing) / तीरथराजा (king of holy places) / मज्जहिं (bathe) / प्रात (in the morning) / समेत (together with) / उछाहा (joy) / कहहिं (say) / परसपर (to one another) / हरि (the divine / Ram) / गुन (qualities) / गाहा (songs, praises)
ramacharitamanas::286.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::286.essence: Holy gathering becomes praise when people meet with joy.
ramacharitamanas::286.simple_meaning: At Prayag, sages gather, bathe joyfully at dawn, and spend their time speaking about Ram's qualities.
ramacharitamanas::286.simple_insight: Shared devotion makes even a ritual gathering feel alive and meaningful.
ramacharitamanas::286.detailed_meaning: At Bharadwaj's sacred hermitage in Prayag, pilgrims and sages arrive for the holy bath. After bathing at dawn, they gather in fellowship and speak of Ram's virtues. The verse is scene-setting, preparing for the deeper teaching that follows.
ramacharitamanas::286.modern_relevance: At a quiet morning gathering after a difficult night, people wash up, breathe, and begin talking about what keeps them steady. The ritual matters because it opens the heart.
ramacharitamanas::286.insight: It shows how sacred practice naturally turns into shared remembrance and praise.

ramacharitamanas::287.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्म निरूपन धरम बिधि बरनहिं तत्त्व बिभाग। ककहिं भगति भगवंत कै संजुत ग्यान बिराग ॥
ramacharitamanas::287.verse_hindi: ब्रह्म का निरूपण, धर्म का विधान और तत्त्वों के विभाग का वर्णन करते हैं तथा ज्ञान-वैराग्य से युक्त भगवान् की भक्ति का कथन करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::287.english_translation: They describe Brahman, the law of dharma, the divisions of reality, and devotion to the Lord joined with knowledge and dispassion.
ramacharitamanas::287.translation_literal: ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / निरूपन (exposition) / धरम (dharma) / बिधि (law, method) / बरनहिं (they describe) / तत्त्व (principles, realities) / बिभाग (division, distinctions) / ककहिं (they speak) / भगति (devotion) / भगवंत (the Lord) / कै (of) / संजुत (joined with) / ग्यान (knowledge) / बिराग (dispassion)
ramacharitamanas::287.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::287.essence: True devotion matures when knowledge and dispassion join it.
ramacharitamanas::287.simple_meaning: The gathering of sages discusses the supreme reality, dharma, the structure of existence, and devotion joined with knowledge and detachment.
ramacharitamanas::287.simple_insight: Real understanding is not dry theory; it ripens into devotion and a freer, less grasping life.
ramacharitamanas::287.detailed_meaning: At Bharadvaja’s sacred hermitage in Prayag, the sages have come for the holy month of bathing. Their conversations turn from ritual to the deepest questions: reality, dharma, the parts of existence, and devotion shaped by knowledge and dispassion. This verse names the sacred atmosphere of that study.
ramacharitamanas::287.modern_relevance: In a quiet study group after a long day, someone asks the question beneath all the others: what is real, how should I live, and what kind of love frees me instead of binding me?
ramacharitamanas::287.insight: It shifts the mind from ritual alone to a fuller vision where understanding, ethics, and devotion belong together.

ramacharitamanas::288.verse_sanskrit: एहि प्रकार भरि माघ नहाहीं। पुनि सब निज निज आश्रम जाहीं॥ प्रति संबत अति होइ अनंदा। मकर मज्जि गवनहिं मुनिबृंदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::288.verse_hindi: इसी प्रकार माघ के महीनेभर स्नान करते हैं और फिर सब अपने-अपने आश्रमों को चले जाते हैं। हर साल वहाँ इसी तरह बड़ा आनंद होता है। मकर में स्नान करके मुनिगण चले जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::288.english_translation: In this way they bathe through the whole month of Magha, then all return to their own hermitages. Each year there is great joy there. After bathing in Magha, the sages depart.
ramacharitamanas::288.translation_literal: एहि प्रकार (in this way) / भरि (throughout) / माघ (the month of Magha) / नहाहीं (they bathe) / पुनि (then) / सब (all) / निज निज (each one's own) / आश्रम (hermitage) / जाहीं (they go) / प्रति संबत (every year) / अति (very) / होइ (is) / अनंदा (joy) / मकर (in Magha / during the Makara period) / मज्जि (having bathed) / गवनहिं (they depart) / मुनिबृंदा (the group of sages)
ramacharitamanas::288.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::288.essence: Sacred gatherings end, but their joy sends everyone home renewed.
ramacharitamanas::288.simple_meaning: The sages bathe for the whole month of Magha, then return to their hermitages. Every year, this gathering brings great joy.
ramacharitamanas::288.simple_insight: Sacred practice can also be a yearly reunion that renews everyone’s spirit.
ramacharitamanas::288.detailed_meaning: At Bharadvaja’s hermitage near Prayag, the sages have finished their month-long bathing and shared talks on dharma, devotion, and wisdom. This verse simply closes that annual gathering: the joy of the meeting ends, and everyone returns to their own ashrams.
ramacharitamanas::288.modern_relevance: After a week-long retreat, everyone packs their bags, still glowing from shared prayers and long conversations. The real gift was not only the ritual — it was being together again.
ramacharitamanas::288.insight: It frames spiritual life as a rhythm of return: gathering, renewing, and then going back to serve.

ramacharitamanas::289.verse_sanskrit: एक बार भरि मकर नहाए। सब मुनीस आश्रमन्ह सिधाए॥ जागबलिक मुनि परम बिबेकी। भरद्वाज राखे पद टेकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::289.verse_hindi: एक बार पूरे मकरभर स्नान करके सब मुनीश्वर अपने-अपने आश्रमों को लौट गए। परम ज्ञानी याज्ञवल्क्य मुनि को चरण पकड़कर भरद्वाजजी ने रख लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::289.english_translation: After bathing through the whole month of Makar, all the sages returned to their own hermitages. Bharadvaja held the feet of the supremely discerning sage Yajnavalkya.
ramacharitamanas::289.translation_literal: एक बार (once) / भरि (throughout) / मकर (Makar month) / नहाए (bathed) / सब (all) / मुनीस (sages) / आश्रमन्ह (to hermitages) / सिधाए (departed)॥ / जागबलिक (Yajnavalkya) / मुनि (sage) / परम (supremely) / बिबेकी (discerning) / भरद्वाज (Bharadvaja) / राखे (held) / पद (feet) / टेकी (with support)॥
ramacharitamanas::289.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::289.essence: True learning begins with humility before the wise.
ramacharitamanas::289.simple_meaning: After the annual bathing festival ends, the sages go back to their hermitages. Bharadvaja honors Yajnavalkya by holding his feet.
ramacharitamanas::289.simple_insight: Respect deepens when knowledge is met with humility.
ramacharitamanas::289.detailed_meaning: The month-long bathing gathering at Makar has ended, and the sages are leaving for their hermitages. Bharadvaja stops Yajnavalkya with deep reverence, holding his feet before the next exchange of teaching begins.
ramacharitamanas::289.modern_relevance: A conference ends, people head for the parking lot, and one person stays back to thank the elder who changed their thinking. Real learning begins with humility.
ramacharitamanas::289.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the posture of reverence that makes teaching possible.

ramacharitamanas::290.verse_sanskrit: सादर चरन सरोज पखारे। अति पुनीत आसन बैठारे॥ करि पूजा मुनि सुजसु बखानी। बोले अति पुनीत मृदु बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::290.verse_hindi: आदरपूर्वक उनके चरण कमल धोए और बड़े ही पवित्र आसन पर उन्हें बैठाया। पूजा करके मुनि याज्ञवल्क्यजी के सुयश का वर्णन किया और फिर अत्यंत पवित्र और कोमल वाणी से बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::290.english_translation: With reverence he washed the lotus feet and seated him on a supremely pure seat. He worshiped him, praised the sage's good fame, and then spoke in an utterly pure, gentle voice.
ramacharitamanas::290.translation_literal: सादर (with reverence) / चरन (feet) / सरोज (lotus) / पखारे (washed) / अति (very) / पुनीत (pure) / आसन (seat) / बैठारे (seated) / करि (having done) / पूजा (worship) / मुनि (sage) / सुजसु (good fame) / बखानी (praised) / बोले (spoke) / अति (very) / पुनीत (pure) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (speech)
ramacharitamanas::290.speaker: Bharadvaja
ramacharitamanas::290.essence: Reverence creates the right space for truth to be spoken.
ramacharitamanas::290.simple_meaning: Bharadvaja welcomes Yajnavalkya with deep respect, worships him, and speaks gently after praising his fame.
ramacharitamanas::290.simple_insight: Respect opens the way for real questioning. Humility comes before wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::290.detailed_meaning: At Bharadvaja's hermitage, the guest is Yajnavalkya, the sage everyone honours. Bharadvaja washes his feet, seats him carefully, worships him, and only then begins the sacred conversation that will lead into his doubt about the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::290.modern_relevance: You greet someone whose advice matters, pull out the best chair, and listen before speaking. That small act of reverence changes the whole tone of the conversation.
ramacharitamanas::290.insight: It teaches you to begin inquiry with humility, not ego.

ramacharitamanas::291.verse_sanskrit: नाथ एक संसउ बड़ मोरें। करगत बेदतत्त्व सबु तोरें॥ कहत सो मोहि लागत भय लाजा। जौं न कहउँ बड़ होइ अकाजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::291.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! मेरे मन में एक बड़ा संदेह है, वेदों का तत्त्व सब आपकी मुट्ठी में है (अर्थात् आप ही वेद का तत्त्व जानने वाले होने के कारण मेरा संदेह निवारण कर सकते हैं) पर उस संदेह को कहते मुझे भय और लाज आती है (भय इसलिए कि कहीं आप यह न समझें कि मेरी परीक्षा ले रहा है, लाज इसलिए कि इतनी आयु बीत गई, अब तक ज्ञान न हुआ) और यदि नहीं कहता तो बड़ी हानि होती है (क्योंकि अज्ञानी बना रहता हूँ) ॥
ramacharitamanas::291.english_translation: Lord, I have a great doubt. The essence of the Vedas is in your hand. Yet I feel fear and shame in speaking it. If I do not ask, a great loss remains.
ramacharitamanas::291.translation_literal: नाथ (lord) / एक (one) / संसउ (doubt) / बड़ (great) / मोरें (in me) / करगत (in-hand) / बेदतत्त्व (essence of the Vedas) / सबु (all) / तोरें (yours) / कहत (speaking) / सो (that) / मोहि (to me) / लागत (feels) / भय (fear) / लाजा (shame) / जौं (if) / न (not) / कहउँ (I speak) / बड़ (great) / होइ (becomes) / अकाजा (loss / harm)
ramacharitamanas::291.speaker: Bharadvaja
ramacharitamanas::291.essence: Real learning begins when shame is smaller than the question.
ramacharitamanas::291.simple_meaning: Bharadvaja admits a deep doubt, says Yajnavalkya knows the Vedic truth, and hesitates to ask because of fear and shame. Still, he knows silence would leave him worse off.
ramacharitamanas::291.simple_insight: Honest questioning matters more than protecting pride.
ramacharitamanas::291.detailed_meaning: In Bharadvaja's ashram, after respectful welcome, Bharadvaja turns to Yajnavalkya with a difficult question. He already trusts the teacher's depth, but his own hesitation is strong. This verse opens the real teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::291.modern_relevance: You know the answer is sitting in the room, but your throat tightens before you ask. Pride wants silence; growth needs the question.
ramacharitamanas::291.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to honest inquiry.

ramacharitamanas::292.verse_sanskrit: संत कहहिं असि नीति प्रभु श्रुति पुरान मुनि गाव। होइ न बिमल बिबेक उर गुर सन किएँ दुराव ॥
ramacharitamanas::292.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! संत लोग ऐसी नीति कहते हैं और वेद, पुराण तथा मुनिजन भी यही बतलाते हैं कि गुरु के साथ छिपाव करने से हृदय में निर्मल ज्ञान नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::292.english_translation: Saints say this rule, and the Vedas, Puranas, and sages sing it too: if a disciple hides things from the guru, the heart does not gain pure understanding.
ramacharitamanas::292.translation_literal: संत (saints) / कहहिं (say) / असि (this) / नीति (rule) / प्रभु (Lord) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / पुरान (the Puranas) / मुनि (sages) / गाव (sing) / होइ (becomes) / न (not) / बिमल (pure) / बिबेक (clear seeing) / उर (in the heart) / गुर (guru) / सन (with) / किएँ (by doing) / दुराव (hiding)
ramacharitamanas::292.speaker: Yajnavalkya
ramacharitamanas::292.essence: Hiddenness before the teacher blocks clear seeing.
ramacharitamanas::292.simple_meaning: A seeker cannot gain clear understanding by hiding things from the teacher. Honest openness is necessary for real learning.
ramacharitamanas::292.simple_insight: Growth begins when you stop protecting your confusion and let it be seen.
ramacharitamanas::292.detailed_meaning: Yajnavalkya is answering Bharadvaja's question in the opening frame of the Ramcharitmanas. Before he reveals the deeper teaching, he says the disciple must not conceal anything from the guru, because hiddenness blocks clean understanding.
ramacharitamanas::292.modern_relevance: You sit in a therapy session and keep editing the story to look better. Nothing changes until you tell the whole truth. Hiding pain preserves it.
ramacharitamanas::292.insight: It shifts learning from self-protection to honest inquiry with a guide.

ramacharitamanas::293.verse_sanskrit: अस बिचारि प्रगटउँ निज मोहू। हरहु नाथ करि जन पर छोहू॥ राम नाम कर अमित प्रभावा। संत पुरान उपनिषद गावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::293.verse_hindi: यही सोचकर मैं अपना अज्ञान प्रकट करता हूँ। हे नाथ! सेवक पर कृपा करके इस अज्ञान का नाश कीजिए। संतों, पुराणों और उपनिषदों ने राम नाम के असीम प्रभाव का गान किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::293.english_translation: Thinking thus, I reveal my own confusion. O Lord, show mercy to your servant and remove this ignorance. The saints, the Puranas, and the Upanishads have sung the limitless power of Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::293.translation_literal: अस (thus) / बिचारि (thinking) / प्रगटउँ (I reveal) / निज (my own) / मोहू (confusion, delusion) / हरहु (remove) / नाथ (O Lord) / करि (doing) / जन (servant) / पर (upon) / छोहू (mercy) / राम (Ram) / नाम (name) / कर (of) / अमित (limitless) / प्रभावा (power, influence) / संत (saints) / पुरान (Puranas) / उपनिषद (Upanishads) / गावा (have sung)
ramacharitamanas::293.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::293.essence: Humility opens the way for Ram's name to work.
ramacharitamanas::293.simple_meaning: Parvati admits her confusion and asks Shiva to remove it. She then says that saints, Puranas, and Upanishads praise the limitless power of Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::293.simple_insight: You do not have to hide confusion. Honest humility opens the door to grace.
ramacharitamanas::293.detailed_meaning: Parvati is questioning Shiva in the Balkand frame, and her hesitation turns into confession. She admits her own confusion, asks for mercy, and points to the long tradition that praises Ram's name as immensely powerful.
ramacharitamanas::293.modern_relevance: You sit with a teacher, finally admitting, “I don’t understand.” That honesty is not failure. It is often the first real opening to change.
ramacharitamanas::293.insight: It shifts the mind from protecting its image to asking directly for help and trusting the power of remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::294.verse_sanskrit: संतत जपत संभु अबिनासी। सिव भगवान ग्यान गुन रासी॥ आकर चारि जीव जग अहहीं। कासीं मरत परम पद लहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::294.verse_hindi: कल्याण स्वरूप, ज्ञान और गुणों की राशि, अविनाशी भगवान् शम्भु निरंतर राम नाम का जप करते रहते हैं। संसार में चार जाति के जीव हैं, काशी में मरने से सभी परम पद को प्राप्त करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::294.english_translation: The immortal Shiva, who is the storehouse of wisdom and virtues, keeps chanting Ram's name without pause. All beings fall into four classes, and dying in Kashi grants the highest state.
ramacharitamanas::294.translation_literal: संतत (continually) / जपत (chanting) / संभु (Shiva) / अबिनासी (imperishable) / सिव (Shiva) / भगवान (divine lord) / ग्यान (wisdom) / गुन (virtues) / रासी (heap, storehouse) / आकर (kinds, forms) / चारि (four) / जीव (living beings) / जग (world) / अहहीं (are) / कासीं (in Kashi) / मरत (dying) / परम पद (highest state) / लहहीं (obtain)
ramacharitamanas::294.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::294.essence: Steady remembrance of Ram lifts even Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::294.simple_meaning: Shiva keeps repeating Ram's name, and Kashi is praised as a place where dying leads to the highest state.
ramacharitamanas::294.simple_insight: Repetition becomes reverence when it is steady, humble, and directed toward the divine.
ramacharitamanas::294.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is explaining Ram's name through Shiva's own example. He says Shiva, the imperishable one full of wisdom and virtues, chants constantly; then he adds the traditional teaching about Kashi and the highest state, preparing the next verse's deeper explanation.
ramacharitamanas::294.modern_relevance: An old prayer keeps returning to your mouth while you sit beside a hospital bed, unable to fix anything. In that helplessness, repetition becomes refuge, not routine.
ramacharitamanas::294.insight: It shifts devotion from occasional feeling to steady remembrance that can carry a whole life.

ramacharitamanas::295.verse_sanskrit: सोपि राम महिमा मुनिराया। सिव उपदेसु करत करि दाया॥ रामु कवन प्रभु पूछउँ तोही। कहिअ बुझाइ कृपानिधि मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::295.verse_hindi: हे मुनिराज! वह भी राम (नाम) की ही महिमा है, क्योंकि शिवजी महाराज दया करके (काशी में मरने वाले जीव को) राम नाम का ही उपदेश करते हैं (इसी से उनको परम पद मिलता है)। हे प्रभो! मैं आपसे पूछता हूँ कि वे राम कौन हैं? हे कृपानिधान! मुझे समझाकर कहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::295.english_translation: That too is the glory of Ram, O sage-king, for Shiva, out of compassion, teaches the name of Ram. O Lord, I ask you: who is Ram? O treasure of mercy, please explain this to me.
ramacharitamanas::295.translation_literal: सोपि (that too) / राम (Ram) / महिमा (glory) / मुनिराया (O sage-king) / सिव (Shiva) / उपदेसु (instruction) / करत (doing) / करि (with) / दाया (compassion) / रामु (Ram) / कवन (which / who) / प्रभु (Lord) / पूछउँ (I ask) / तोही (you) / कहिअ (please say) / बुझाइ (making understand) / कृपानिधि (treasure of mercy) / मोही (to me)
ramacharitamanas::295.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::295.essence: Praise of Ram naturally leads to the question of who Ram is.
ramacharitamanas::295.simple_meaning: Ram's greatness includes the fact that Shiva teaches people to repeat Ram's name. The speaker then asks a direct question: who is Ram? Please explain clearly.
ramacharitamanas::295.simple_insight: Real devotion begins with honest questioning, not pretending to understand.
ramacharitamanas::295.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, the listener has already heard that Shiva guides souls toward Ram's name in Kashi. Now that same listener turns to the deeper question: if Ram's name is so powerful, who is Ram himself? The verse opens the door to revelation.
ramacharitamanas::295.modern_relevance: You hear a name repeated everywhere — in songs, in prayers, in family talk — but one quiet question remains: who is this really about? Honest seeking begins there.
ramacharitamanas::295.insight: It shifts the mind from repeating a sacred idea to wanting direct understanding of its source.

ramacharitamanas::296.verse_sanskrit: एक राम अवधेस कुमारा। तिन्ह कर चरित बिदित संसारा॥ नारि बिरहँ दुखु लहेउ अपारा। भयउ रोषु रन रावनु मारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::296.verse_hindi: एक राम तो अवध नरेश दशरथजी के कुमार हैं, उनका चरित्र सारा संसार जानता है। उन्होंने स्त्री के विरह में अपार दुःख उठाया और क्रोध आने पर युद्ध में रावण को मार डाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::296.english_translation: One Ram is the prince of Ayodhya. His deeds are known throughout the world. He suffered immense sorrow in separation from his wife, and when anger arose in battle, he killed Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::296.translation_literal: एक (one) / राम (Ram) / अवधेस (lord of Ayodhya) / कुमारा (prince) । / तिन्ह (his) / कर (of) / चरित (deeds, conduct) / बिदित (known) / संसारा (in the world) ॥ / नारि (wife) / बिरहँ (in separation) / दुखु (sorrow) / लहेउ (he experienced) / अपारा (immeasurable) । / भयउ (became) / रोषु (anger) / रन (in battle) / रावनु (Ravana) / मारा (killed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::296.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::296.essence: Ram’s greatness includes grief, anger, and decisive action.
ramacharitamanas::296.simple_meaning: Ram is known everywhere as Ayodhya’s prince. He suffered deep sorrow when separated from Sita, and in battle he killed Ravana in anger.
ramacharitamanas::296.simple_insight: Even the ideal person feels loss and anger; what matters is how those forces are met and resolved.
ramacharitamanas::296.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses the story to name Ram in human terms: Ayodhya’s prince, beloved and widely known. The verse reminds the listener that Ram can feel the pain of separation and also act decisively in war, setting up the deeper question of his nature.
ramacharitamanas::296.modern_relevance: You can be admired by everyone and still be pierced by private grief. Even then, life may demand that you face the hard moment and act.
ramacharitamanas::296.insight: It shifts the reader from seeing Ram as only tender to seeing the full range of his embodied response.

ramacharitamanas::297.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु सोइ राम कि अपर कोउ जाहि जपत त्रिपुरारि। सत्यधाम सर्बग्य तुम्ह कहहु बिबेकु बिचारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::297.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! वही राम हैं या और कोई दूसरे हैं, जिनको शिवजी जपते हैं? आप सत्य के धाम हैं और सब कुछ जानते हैं, ज्ञान विचार कर कहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::297.english_translation: O Lord, is the one whom Tripurari worships truly Ram, or someone else? You are the abode of truth and all-knowing; speak with discrimination and reflection.
ramacharitamanas::297.translation_literal: प्रभु (O Lord) / सोइ (that very) / राम (Ram) / कि (or) / अपर (other) / कोउ (someone) / जाहि (whom) / जपत (chanting) / त्रिपुरारि (Tripurari, Shiva) / सत्यधाम (abode of truth) / सर्बग्य (all-knowing) / तुम्ह (you) / कहहु (say) / बिबेकु (discriminating wisdom) / बिचारि (having reflected)
ramacharitamanas::297.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::297.essence: Real devotion can begin with a question.
ramacharitamanas::297.simple_meaning: Parvati asks whether the Ram worshipped by Shiva is the same Ram she has heard about. She asks Yajnavalkya to explain clearly and thoughtfully.
ramacharitamanas::297.simple_insight: It is okay to ask plainly when devotion meets confusion. Honest questions can open the door to deeper understanding.
ramacharitamanas::297.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, Parvati is listening to Shiva's praise of Ram and feels a deep doubt. She asks Yajnavalkya whether the Ram Shiva chants is truly the same Ram, then asks him to answer with clear judgment.
ramacharitamanas::297.modern_relevance: You hear one person praise a name with complete devotion, while your own mind still hesitates. Instead of pretending certainty, you ask the question directly and let understanding begin there.
ramacharitamanas::297.insight: It shifts the mind from passive hearing to active inquiry, seeking clear understanding instead of borrowed belief.

ramacharitamanas::298.verse_sanskrit: जैसें मिटै मोर भ्रम भारी। कहहु सो कथा नाथ बिस्तारी॥ जागबलिक बोले मुसुकाई। तुम्हहि बिदित रघुपति प्रभुताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::298.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! जिस प्रकार से मेरा यह भारी भ्रम मिट जाए, आप वही कथा विस्तारपूर्वक कहिए। इस पर याज्ञवल्क्यजी मुस्कुराकर बोले, श्री रघुनाथजी की प्रभुता को तुम जानते हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::298.english_translation: “Lord, tell that story in full, so my great confusion may be removed.” Yajnavalkya smiled and replied, “You already know the majesty of Raghupati.”
ramacharitamanas::298.translation_literal: जैसें (so that) / मिटै (is removed) / मोर (my) / भ्रम (confusion) / भारी (heavy) / कहहु (tell) / सो (that) / कथा (story) / नाथ (Lord) / बिस्तारी (in full) ॥ / जागबलिक (Yajnavalkya) / बोले (said) / मुसुकाई (smiling) / तुम्हहि (to you) / बिदित (known) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / प्रभुताई (majesty) ॥
ramacharitamanas::298.speaker: Yajnavalkya
ramacharitamanas::298.essence: Clear seeing begins by admitting confusion and asking for the full story.
ramacharitamanas::298.simple_meaning: The listener asks for the story in full so his confusion can be cleared. Yajnavalkya answers that the listener already knows Ram's greatness.
ramacharitamanas::298.simple_insight: Real understanding begins when confusion is named honestly.
ramacharitamanas::298.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, Yajnavalkya is answering Bharadvaja’s sincere question about Ram. Bharadvaja asks for the story in full so his heavy confusion can be cleared, and Yajnavalkya gently points out that Bharadvaja already knows Ram’s greatness and is ready to hear deeper truth.
ramacharitamanas::298.modern_relevance: You sit with a teacher after rereading the same paragraph three times, finally admitting, “I’m still lost.” That honest admission is where clarity can begin.
ramacharitamanas::298.insight: It shifts the mind from pretending to know toward asking clean, direct questions.

ramacharitamanas::299.verse_sanskrit: रामभगत तुम्ह मन क्रम बानी। चतुराई तुम्हारि मैं जानी॥ चाहहु सुनै राम गुन गूढ़ा कीन्हिहु प्रस्न मनहुँ अति मूढ़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::299.verse_hindi: तुम मन, वचन और कर्म से श्री रामजी के भक्त हो। तुम्हारी चतुराई को मैं जान गया। तुम श्री रामजी के रहस्यमय गुणों को सुनना चाहते हो, इसी से तुमने ऐसा प्रश्न किया है मानो बड़े ही मूढ़ हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::299.english_translation: You are a devotee of Ram in mind, speech, and action. I know your cleverness. You want to hear Ram's hidden qualities, so you asked as if you were very dull.
ramacharitamanas::299.translation_literal: रामभगत (devotee of Ram) / तुम्ह (you) / मन (mind) / क्रम (deed, action) / बानी (speech) / चतुराई (cleverness) / तुम्हारि (your) / मैं (I) / जानी (have known) / चाहहु (you wish) / सुनै (to hear) / राम (Ram) / गुन (qualities) / गूढ़ा (hidden, profound) / कीन्हिहु (you made) / प्रस्न (question) / मनहुँ (as if) / अति (very) / मूढ़ा (foolish)
ramacharitamanas::299.speaker: Yajnavalkya
ramacharitamanas::299.essence: Sincere questioning often hides a deeper devotion.
ramacharitamanas::299.simple_meaning: Yajnavalkya sees that Bharadvaja is asking with devotion and intelligence, not ignorance. The question is a way of inviting a deeper teaching about Ram.
ramacharitamanas::299.simple_insight: Real curiosity can wear humility. A sincere question opens the door to deeper understanding.
ramacharitamanas::299.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, Bharadvaja asks Yajnavalkya to clear his confusion about Ram. Yajnavalkya smiles and sees through the pose: Bharadvaja is already devoted and wise. This verse marks the moment when the teacher recognises the student's readiness for deeper truth.
ramacharitamanas::299.modern_relevance: You ask a question in a meeting and pretend you are unsure, but you already know the issue is bigger than the surface answer. The right teacher notices that and gives you the deeper layer.
ramacharitamanas::299.insight: It shifts inquiry from casual asking to devoted readiness for deeper teaching.

ramacharitamanas::300.verse_sanskrit: तात सुनहु सादर मनु लाई। कहउँ राम कै कथा सुहाई॥ महामोहु महिषेसु बिसाला। रामकथा कालिका कराला ॥
