ramacharitamanas::300.verse_hindi: हे तात! तुम आदरपूर्वक मन लगाकर सुनो, मैं श्री रामजी की सुंदर कथा कहता हूँ। बड़ा भारी अज्ञान विशाल महिषासुर है और श्री रामजी की कथा (उसे नष्ट कर देने वाली) भयंकर कालीजी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::300.english_translation: Listen respectfully, dear one. I will tell the lovely story of Ram. Great delusion is the vast buffalo-demon, and Ram's story is fierce Kali who destroys it.
ramacharitamanas::300.translation_literal: तात (dear one) / सुनहु (listen) / सादर (respectfully) / मनु (mind) / लाई (placing) / कहउँ (I will tell) / राम (Ram) / कै (of) / कथा (story) / सुहाई (lovely) / महामोहु (great delusion) / महिषेसु (buffalo-demon) / बिसाला (vast) / रामकथा (story of Ram) / कालिका (Kali) / कराला (fierce)
ramacharitamanas::300.speaker: Yajnavalkya
ramacharitamanas::300.essence: Ram's story destroys confusion at its root.
ramacharitamanas::300.simple_meaning: Listen carefully to Ram's beautiful story. It is so powerful that it destroys deep confusion completely.
ramacharitamanas::300.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that confusion is not stronger than a true story.
ramacharitamanas::300.detailed_meaning: Yajnavalkya is answering Bharadvaja's question about Ram's greatness. He pauses the dialogue to invite careful listening, then says Ram's story is not just beautiful — it is the force that destroys deep confusion at its root.
ramacharitamanas::300.modern_relevance: You are exhausted after ten tabs, three opinions, and one spiraling doubt. Then one clear account lands and the fog starts to lift. Some truths do that: they don't decorate confusion, they end it.
ramacharitamanas::300.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing explanations to receiving a clarifying teaching.

ramacharitamanas::301.verse_sanskrit: रामकथा ससि किरन समाना। संत चकोर करहिं जेहि पाना॥ ऐसेइ संसय कीन्ह भवानी। महादेव तब कहा बखानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::301.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी की कथा चंद्रमा की किरणों के समान है, जिसे संत रूपी चकोर सदा पान करते हैं। ऐसा ही संदेह पार्वतीजी ने किया था, तब महादेवजी ने विस्तार से उसका उत्तर दिया था ॥
ramacharitamanas::301.english_translation: Ram's story is like moonlight; the saints are chakor birds who drink it. Such a doubt was raised by Parvati, and then Mahadev explained it fully.
ramacharitamanas::301.translation_literal: रामकथा (Ram's story) / ससि (moon) / किरन (rays) / समाना (like) / संत (saints) / चकोर (chakor bird) / करहिं (do) / जेहि (which) / पाना (drinking) / ऐसेइ (just so) / संसय (doubt) / कीन्ह (made) / भवानी (Parvati) / महादेव (Mahadev/Shiva) / तब (then) / कहा (said) / बखानी (explained fully)
ramacharitamanas::301.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::301.essence: Ram's story feeds the devoted heart like moonlight feeds the chakor.
ramacharitamanas::301.simple_meaning: Ram's story is as nourishing to saints as moonlight is to a chakor bird. Parvati's question led Shiva to explain it in detail.
ramacharitamanas::301.simple_insight: Some teachings are not just heard — they are drunk in by the heart.
ramacharitamanas::301.detailed_meaning: In the opening frame of the Balkand, Parvati wonders about the glory of Ram's story. Shiva answers by comparing it to moonlight that the saintly heart cannot stop drinking, preparing the ground for the deeper dialogue that follows.
ramacharitamanas::301.modern_relevance: A friend sends you one verse at midnight, and it lands harder than a long lecture ever could. Some words do not inform you; they feed you.
ramacharitamanas::301.insight: It frames Ram-katha as something the devoted return to again and again, not as a one-time lesson.

ramacharitamanas::302.verse_sanskrit: कहउँ सो मति अनुहारि अब उमा संभु संबाद। भयउ समय जेहि हेतु जेहि सुनु मुनि मिटिहि बिषाद ॥
ramacharitamanas::302.verse_hindi: अब मैं अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार वही उमा और शिवजी का संवाद कहता हूँ। वह जिस समय और जिस हेतु से हुआ, उसे हे मुनि! तुम सुनो, तुम्हारा विषाद मिट जाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::302.english_translation: Now I will tell, according to my understanding, the dialogue between Uma and Shiva. Hear why and when it took place, O sage, and your sorrow will be removed.
ramacharitamanas::302.translation_literal: कहउँ (I will tell) / सो (that) / मति (understanding) / अनुहारि (according to) / अब (now) / उमा (Uma) / संभु (Shiva) / संबाद (dialogue) / भयउ (became / took place) / समय (time) / जेहि (which) / हेतु (cause) / जेहि (which) / सुनु (listen) / मुनि (sage) / मिटिहि (will be removed) / बिषाद (sorrow)
ramacharitamanas::302.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::302.essence: Understanding the setting dissolves confusion before the teaching even begins.
ramacharitamanas::302.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he will explain the dialogue between Uma and Shiva, including when and why it happened, so the sage's sorrow can disappear.
ramacharitamanas::302.simple_insight: A hard question can ease when its context is finally made clear.
ramacharitamanas::302.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening the Shiva-Parvati frame story for the listener. He promises to explain the dialogue's timing and purpose, because understanding that background will remove the sage's confusion and prepare him for the deeper teaching ahead.
ramacharitamanas::302.modern_relevance: You hear half a conversation and spiral for hours. Then someone gives the missing context, and the whole thing settles. Relief often begins with the right frame.
ramacharitamanas::302.insight: It shifts the mind from vague unease to patient listening for context.

ramacharitamanas::303.verse_sanskrit: एक बार त्रेता जुग माहीं। संभु गए कुंभज रिषि पाहीं॥ संग सती जगजननि भवानी। पूजे रिषि अखिलेस्वर जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::303.verse_hindi: एक बार त्रेता युग में शिवजी अगस्त्य ऋषि के पास गए। उनके साथ जगज्जननी भवानी सतीजी भी थीं। ऋषि ने संपूर्ण जगत् के ईश्वर जानकर उनका पूजन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::303.english_translation: Once, in the Treta age, Shiva went to the sage Kumbhaja. Sati, Bhavani, the mother of the world, was with him. Knowing them as the Lord of all, the sage worshipped them.
ramacharitamanas::303.translation_literal: एक बार (once) / त्रेता जुग माहीं (in the Treta age) / संभु (Shiva) / गए (went) / कुंभज रिषि पाहीं (to sage Kumbhaja) / संग (with) / सती (Sati) / जगजननि भवानी (Bhavani, mother of the world) / पूजे (worshipped) / रिषि (the sage) / अखिलेस्वर (Lord of all) / जानी (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::303.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::303.essence: True recognition turns presence into worship.
ramacharitamanas::303.simple_meaning: Shiva and Sati visit the sage Agastya, and the sage honors them as supreme beings.
ramacharitamanas::303.simple_insight: Respect becomes natural when you truly see who stands before you.
ramacharitamanas::303.detailed_meaning: In Treta Yuga, Shiva arrives at Agastya’s hermitage with Sati beside him. Agastya recognises their divine stature and offers worship. This is a scene-setting verse that prepares the later telling of Ram’s story and the Shiva-Parvati dialogue.
ramacharitamanas::303.modern_relevance: You meet an elder at a quiet ashram and instinctively lower your voice. Recognition changes your behavior before any words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::303.insight: It shows that reverence begins with clear seeing, not formality.

ramacharitamanas::304.verse_sanskrit: रामकथा मुनिबर्ज बखानी। सुनी महेस परम सुखु मानी॥ रिषि पूछी हरिभगति सुहाई। कही संभु अधिकारी पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::304.verse_hindi: मुनिवर अगस्त्यजी ने रामकथा विस्तार से कही, जिसको महेश्वर ने परम सुख मानकर सुना। फिर ऋषि ने शिवजी से सुंदर हरिभक्ति पूछी और शिवजी ने उनको अधिकारी पाकर (रहस्य सहित) भक्ति का निरूपण किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::304.english_translation: Agastya narrated the story of Ram in full. Mahesh listened and felt supreme joy. Then the sage asked about the lovely devotion to Hari, and Shiva explained it to one who was fit to receive it.
ramacharitamanas::304.translation_literal: रामकथा (the story of Ram) / मुनिबर्ज (best among sages) / बखानी (was narrated) / सुनी (heard) / महेस (Mahesh, Shiva) / परम (supreme) / सुखु (joy) / मानी (considered)॥ / रिषि (sage) / पूछी (asked) / हरिभगति (devotion to Hari) / सुहाई (lovely) / कही (spoke) / संभु (Shiva) / अधिकारी (fit recipient) / पाई (having found) ॥
ramacharitamanas::304.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::304.essence: Devotion is revealed only to the one prepared to receive it.
ramacharitamanas::304.simple_meaning: Agastya tells Ram's story, and Shiva listens with deep joy. Then Agastya asks Shiva about loving devotion to Ram, and Shiva answers because the sage is ready for it.
ramacharitamanas::304.simple_insight: Real devotion begins when the heart is ready to hear it, not just when the words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::304.detailed_meaning: At Agastya's hermitage, the Ram story has already filled the air. Shiva has listened in bliss. Now the sage turns from narration to the deeper question: what is true devotion to Ram? The verse marks the move from hearing the story to receiving its heart.
ramacharitamanas::304.modern_relevance: You hear a story about someone who stayed loyal when it cost everything, and something in you opens. A real answer lands only after the listener is ready to receive it.
ramacharitamanas::304.insight: It shifts attention from the story itself to the inner readiness needed to absorb its meaning.

ramacharitamanas::305.verse_sanskrit: कहत सुनत रघुपति गुन गाथा। कछु दिन तहाँ रहे गिरिनाथा॥ मुनि सन बिदा मागि त्रिपुरारी। चले भवन सँग दच्छकुमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::305.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी के गुणों की कथाएँ कहते-सुनते कुछ दिनों तक शिवजी वहाँ रहे। फिर मुनि से विदा माँगकर शिवजी दक्षकुमारी सतीजी के साथ घर (कैलास) को चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::305.english_translation: Shiva stayed there for some days, hearing and speaking the stories of Raghupati's virtues. Then Tripurari took leave of the sage and went home with Dakshakumari.
ramacharitamanas::305.translation_literal: कहत (speaking) / सुनत (hearing) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan, Ram) / गुन (virtues) / गाथा (stories) / कछु (some) / दिन (days) / तहाँ (there) / रहे (remained) / गिरिनाथा (Lord of the mountain, Shiva)॥ / मुनि (sage) / सन (from) / बिदा (farewell) / मागि (asking) / त्रिपुरारी (destroyer of the three cities, Shiva) / चले (went) / भवन (home) / सँग (with) / दच्छकुमारी (daughter of Daksha, Sati) ॥
ramacharitamanas::305.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::305.essence: Love stays where Ram is praised, then departs without reluctance.
ramacharitamanas::305.simple_meaning: Shiva spent a few days there listening to Ram's virtues, then took leave of the sage and returned home with Sati.
ramacharitamanas::305.simple_insight: Even a great devotee stays longer where Ram is praised.
ramacharitamanas::305.detailed_meaning: After Agastya has spoken of Ram and answered Shiva's question about devotion, Shiva remains for a few days, absorbed in Ram's qualities. Then he respectfully takes leave and returns to Kailash with Sati. The verse simply closes that devotional visit.
ramacharitamanas::305.modern_relevance: You linger after a conversation because it touched something deep. The room is ordinary, but the words keep pulling you back toward what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::305.insight: It shows devotion as a natural longing to remain near Ram's praise, then leave with grace.

ramacharitamanas::306.verse_sanskrit: तेहि अवसर भंजन महिभारा। हरि रघुबंस लीन्ह अवतारा॥ पिता बचन तजि राजु उदासी। दंडक बन बिचरत अबिनासी ॥
ramacharitamanas::306.verse_hindi: उन्हीं दिनों पृथ्वी का भार उतारने के लिए श्री हरि ने रघुवंश में अवतार लिया था। वे अविनाशी भगवान् उस समय पिता के वचन से राज्य का त्याग करके तपस्वी या साधु वेश में दण्डकवन में विचर रहे थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::306.english_translation: In those days, to relieve the burden of the earth, Hari took birth in the Raghu line. The imperishable one renounced the kingdom, obeyed his father's word, and wandered in the Dandaka forest.
ramacharitamanas::306.translation_literal: तेहि अवसर (at that time) / भंजन (removing) / महिभारा (burden of the earth) / हरि (Hari) / रघुबंस (Raghu line) / लीन्ह (took) / अवतारा (incarnation) ॥ पिता (father) / बचन (word) / तजि (leaving) / राजु (kingdom) / उदासी (in renunciation) / दंडक बन (Dandaka forest) / बिचरत (wandering) / अबिनासी (imperishable one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::306.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::306.essence: True greatness keeps a promise, even at the cost of power.
ramacharitamanas::306.simple_meaning: Ram came to lift the earth's burden. He gave up the throne, kept his father's word, and lived in the forest.
ramacharitamanas::306.simple_insight: Greatness is shown by keeping a promise, even when it costs everything.
ramacharitamanas::306.detailed_meaning: Shiva has been listening to Ram's story with longing. The narration now turns to Ram's own descent into the world: he is born to relieve the earth's burden, yet he also accepts exile at his father's command. This verse joins divinity with obedience.
ramacharitamanas::306.modern_relevance: You are offered a promotion that would require breaking a promise you made at home. Nobody would know, but you would. This verse measures success by whether you keep faith when it hurts.
ramacharitamanas::306.insight: It shifts the mind from self-advancement to faithful action under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::307.verse_sanskrit: हृदयँ बिचारत जात हर केहि बिधि दरसनु होइ। गुप्त रूप अवतरेउ प्रभु गएँ जान सबु कोइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::307.verse_hindi: शिवजी हृदय में विचारते जा रहे थे कि भगवान् के दर्शन मुझे किस प्रकार हों। प्रभु ने गुप्त रूप से अवतार लिया है, मेरे जाने से सब लोग जान जाएँगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::307.english_translation: Shiva kept wondering in his heart, “How can I have the Lord’s vision? The Lord has taken birth in hidden form; if I go, everyone will know.”
ramacharitamanas::307.translation_literal: हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारत (thinking) / जात (going) / हर (the Lord) / केहि बिधि (by what way) / दरसनु (vision) / होइ (may happen) / गुप्त रूप (hidden form) / अवतरेउ (has descended) / प्रभु (the Lord) / गएँ (by going) / जान (will know) / सबु (all) / कोइ (people)
ramacharitamanas::307.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::307.essence: True devotion waits when closeness would disturb the beloved’s hidden work.
ramacharitamanas::307.simple_meaning: Shiva longs to see Ram, but he worries that his presence will reveal Ram’s hidden birth to everyone around him.
ramacharitamanas::307.simple_insight: Even devotion can tremble with caution when love is trying to protect what it adores.
ramacharitamanas::307.detailed_meaning: Shiva has stayed near the place of Ram’s hidden descent, longing only for a glimpse. But he also knows that if he goes openly, the secret of Ram’s birth may be exposed. The verse captures his inward conflict.
ramacharitamanas::307.modern_relevance: You want to reach out to someone you deeply admire, but you hesitate because your attention might expose what they are trying to keep private. Love can be careful.
ramacharitamanas::307.insight: It shows how devotion can balance longing with restraint, choosing reverence over impulsive closeness.

ramacharitamanas::308.verse_sanskrit: संकर उर अति छोभु सती न जानहिं मरमु सोइ। तुलसी दरसन लोभु मन डरु लोचन लालची ॥
ramacharitamanas::308.verse_hindi: श्री शंकरजी के हृदय में इस बात को लेकर बड़ी खलबली उत्पन्न हो गई, परन्तु सतीजी इस भेद को नहीं जानती थीं। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि शिवजी के मन में (भेद खुलने का) डर था, परन्तु दर्शन के लोभ से उनके नेत्र ललचा रहे थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::308.english_translation: Shiva's heart was deeply stirred, but Sati did not understand the secret. Tulsidas says: his mind feared exposure, yet his eyes longed for the sight.
ramacharitamanas::308.translation_literal: संकर (Shankar/Shiva) / उर (heart) / अति (very) / छोभु (disturbance) / सती (Sati) / न (not) / जानहिं (know) / मरमु (secret) / सोइ (that) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / दरसन (sight) / लोभु (desire) / मन (mind) / डरु (fear) / लोचन (eyes) / लालची (greedy, longing)
ramacharitamanas::308.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::308.essence: Longing for Ram can outweigh even the fear of being exposed.
ramacharitamanas::308.simple_meaning: Shiva is shaken because he senses a divine secret, while Sati cannot yet understand it. He fears being found out, but his longing to see Ram is stronger than his fear.
ramacharitamanas::308.simple_insight: Love can make you tremble and still pull you forward.
ramacharitamanas::308.detailed_meaning: Shiva, already sensing that Ram has appeared in hidden form, is torn between caution and longing. Sati beside him does not grasp the secret. Tulsidas captures a devotee's inner conflict: fear of error, but an even greater hunger for darshan.
ramacharitamanas::308.modern_relevance: You know something matters deeply, but you hesitate because you might misunderstand it or look foolish. Still, your heart keeps leaning toward the meeting, the truth, the person you want to see.
ramacharitamanas::308.insight: It shifts devotion from calm certainty to trembling desire, showing that longing itself can be sacred.

ramacharitamanas::309.verse_sanskrit: रावन मरन मनुज कर जाचा। प्रभु बिधि बचनु कीन्ह चह साचा॥ जौं नहिं जाउँ रहइ पछितावा। करत बिचारु न बनत बनावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::309.verse_hindi: रावण ने (ब्रह्माजी से) अपनी मृत्यु मनुष्य के हाथ से माँगी थी। ब्रह्माजी के वचनों को प्रभु सत्य करना चाहते हैं। मैं जो पास नहीं जाता हूँ तो बड़ा पछतावा रह जाएगा। इस प्रकार शिवजी विचार करते थे, परन्तु कोई भी युक्ति ठीक नहीं बैठती थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::309.english_translation: Ravana had asked Brahma for death at the hands of a human. The Lord wanted Brahma's words to come true. If I do not go, there will be deep regret. Shiva thought in this way, but no solution seemed workable.
ramacharitamanas::309.translation_literal: रावन (Ravana) / मरन (death) / मनुज (human) / कर (by the hand) / जाचा (asked for) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बिधि (Brahma) / बचनु (word) / कीन्ह (made/did) / चह (wants) / साचा (true) / जौं (if) / नहिं (not) / जाउँ (go) / रहइ (remains) / पछितावा (regret) / करत (doing) / बिचारु (thought) / न (not) / बनत (becomes) / बनावा (solution/plan)
ramacharitamanas::309.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::309.essence: A vow can trap even the wise when truth demands an impossible path.
ramacharitamanas::309.simple_meaning: Shiva worries that Ravana's boon must be fulfilled, but he cannot see a way to make it happen without going himself.
ramacharitamanas::309.simple_insight: Even divine plans can feel like a burden when compassion and duty pull in opposite directions.
ramacharitamanas::309.detailed_meaning: Shiva, watching the unfolding story of Ravana's boon, feels trapped by truth itself. Ravana had asked for death by a human hand, and Shiva wants that promise fulfilled. Yet staying away would leave him with regret, and no clever plan seems possible.
ramacharitamanas::309.modern_relevance: You know a promise must be kept, but every option feels costly. You keep turning it over in your mind, hoping for a path that satisfies duty without creating regret.
ramacharitamanas::309.insight: It shows the strain of holding a difficult truth when no easy solution exists.

ramacharitamanas::310.verse_sanskrit: ऐहि बिधि भए सोचबस ईसा। तेही समय जाइ दससीसा॥ लीन्ह नीच मारीचहि संगा। भयउ तुरउ सोइ कपट कुरंगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::310.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार महादेवजी चिन्ता के वश हो गए। उसी समय नीच रावण ने जाकर मारीच को साथ लिया और वह (मारीच) तुरंत कपट मृग बन गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::310.english_translation: In this way, Shiva fell into concern. At that very time, the vile Ravana went and took Maricha along, and Maricha at once became a deceptive deer.
ramacharitamanas::310.translation_literal: ऐहि बिधि (in this way) / भए (became) / सोचबस (under the control of concern) / ईसा (Shiva) / तेही समय (at that very time) / जाइ (going) / दससीसा (Ravana) / लीन्ह (took) / नीच (vile) / मारीचहि (Maricha) / संगा (along with) / भयउ (became) / तुरउ (immediately) / सोइ (that one) / कपट (deceptive) / कुरंगा (deer)
ramacharitamanas::310.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::310.essence: A trap works best when fear and deception arrive together.
ramacharitamanas::310.simple_meaning: Shiva becomes troubled, while Ravana recruits Maricha, who instantly takes the form of a deceptive deer.
ramacharitamanas::310.simple_insight: Deception begins when concern and ego move together.
ramacharitamanas::310.detailed_meaning: The story has moved from Shiva's uneasy realization to Ravana's next scheme. Ravana brings Maricha into the plot, and Maricha quickly becomes the fake deer that will lure Sita. This is the setup for the trap, not the teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::310.modern_relevance: A manipulative plan starts quietly: one person feels uneasy, another steps in with a clever lie, and the trap is set before anyone sees it coming.
ramacharitamanas::310.insight: It shows how deceit often enters through a prepared accomplice and a believable disguise.

ramacharitamanas::311.verse_sanskrit: करि छलु मूढ़ हरी बैदेही। प्रभु प्रभाउ तस बिदित न तेही॥ मृग बधि बंधु सहित हरि आए। आश्रमु देखि नयन जल छाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::311.verse_hindi: मूर्ख (रावण) ने छल करके सीताजी को हर लिया। उसे श्री रामचंद्रजी के वास्तविक प्रभाव का कुछ भी पता न था। मृग को मारकर भाई लक्ष्मण सहित श्री हरि आश्रम में आए और उसे खाली देखकर (अर्थात् वहाँ सीताजी को न पाकर) उनके नेत्रों में आँसू भर आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::311.english_translation: The fool abducted Vaidehi by deceit, not knowing the true power of Ram. After killing the deer, Hari returned with his brother, and tears filled his eyes when he saw the empty hermitage.
ramacharitamanas::311.translation_literal: करि (having done) / छलु (deceit) / मूढ़ (fool) / हरी (abducted) / बैदेही (Vaidehi, Sita) / प्रभु (lord) / प्रभाउ (power) / तस (that) / बिदित (known) / न (not) / तेही (to him) / मृग (deer) / बधि (killing) / बंधु (brother) / सहित (together with) / हरि (Hari) / आए (came) / आश्रमु (hermitage) / देखि (seeing) / नयन (eyes) / जल (water/tears) / छाए (covered)
ramacharitamanas::311.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::311.essence: Deceit ignores power, but emptiness makes love weep.
ramacharitamanas::311.simple_meaning: Ravana deceived Sita because he did not understand Ram's power. Ram returned with Lakshman, saw the empty hermitage, and wept.
ramacharitamanas::311.simple_insight: Some losses begin with ignorance, and grief arrives the moment love finds emptiness.
ramacharitamanas::311.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ravana has just used deception to carry away Sita. Ram and Lakshman return after the deer episode and find the hermitage empty. The sight breaks Ram's composure, and the scene turns from action to sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::311.modern_relevance: You come home and notice the silence first: the untouched cup, the missing voice, the chair still facing the window. Only then do you understand what has been taken.
ramacharitamanas::311.insight: It shifts the mind from triumph to consequence: every deceit creates a wound that must later be felt.

ramacharitamanas::312.verse_sanskrit: बिरह बिकल नर इव रघुराई। खोजत बिपिन फिरत दोउ भाई॥ कबहूँ जोग बियोग न जाकें। देखा प्रगट बिरह दुखु ताकें ॥
ramacharitamanas::312.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी मनुष्यों की भाँति विरह से व्याकुल हैं और दोनों भाई वन में सीता को खोजते हुए फिर रहे हैं। जिनके कभी कोई संयोग-वियोग नहीं है, उनमें प्रत्यक्ष विरह का दुःख देखा गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::312.english_translation: Raghurai is tormented by separation like an ordinary man. Both brothers wander the forest searching for Sita. In one who is never joined or parted, the pain of separation is seen openly.
ramacharitamanas::312.translation_literal: बिरह (separation) / बिकल (distressed) / नर इव (like a man) / रघुराई (Raghurai, Ram) / खोजत (searching) / बिपिन (forest) / फिरत (wandering) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / कबहूँ (at any time) / जोग (union) / बियोग (separation) / न (not) / जाकें (in whom) / देखा (seen) / प्रगट (manifest) / बिरह (separation) / दुखु (pain) / ताकें (in that one)
ramacharitamanas::312.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::312.essence: Even the untouched one can appear pierced by separation.
ramacharitamanas::312.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman wander the forest in grief, searching for Sita. The verse says that even one beyond all union and separation can appear to suffer separation.
ramacharitamanas::312.simple_insight: Love can make even the untouched seem wounded. Grief is not always a weakness; sometimes it reveals depth.
ramacharitamanas::312.detailed_meaning: After Sita is taken, Ram and Lakshman search the forest in anguish. Tulsidas pauses the story to show something startling: Ram, who is beyond ordinary coming together and parting, now appears to feel separation like any human lover.
ramacharitamanas::312.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after the message that changed everything. The person who seemed unshakable now looks as vulnerable as you feel.
ramacharitamanas::312.insight: It shifts the reader from seeing Ram as distant power to seeing divine love as fully human and emotionally present.

ramacharitamanas::313.verse_sanskrit: अति बिचित्र रघुपति चरित जानहिं परम सुजान। जे मतिमंद बिमोह बस हृदयँ धरहिं कछु आन ॥
ramacharitamanas::313.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी का चरित्र बड़ा ही विचित्र है, उसको पहुँचे हुए ज्ञानीजन ही जानते हैं। जो मंदबुद्धि हैं, वे तो विशेष रूप से मोह के वश होकर हृदय में कुछ दूसरी ही बात समझ बैठते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::313.english_translation: The deeds of Raghupati are wondrous. Only the most wise know them. Those with dull understanding, deluded by confusion, take something else to be in their heart.
ramacharitamanas::313.translation_literal: अति (very) / बिचित्र (wondrous, strange) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / चरित (deeds, conduct) / जानहिं (know) / परम सुजान (the supremely wise) / जे (those who) / मतिमंद (dull-minded) / बिमोह बस (under the power of delusion) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / धरहिं (hold, take) / कछु (something) / आन (other, different)
ramacharitamanas::313.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::313.essence: Ram's actions look strange until clear seeing reveals them.
ramacharitamanas::313.simple_meaning: Ram's life and actions are hard to understand. Wise people see their true meaning, while confused people mistake them for something else.
ramacharitamanas::313.simple_insight: Humility opens the door to real understanding. Pride and confusion make even holy things look ordinary or wrong.
ramacharitamanas::313.detailed_meaning: In the forest, after Sita's abduction and Ram's grief, Tulsidas steps back from the scene and names a deeper problem: Ram's actions cannot be read by surface thinking. The wise understand; the confused project their own ideas instead.
ramacharitamanas::313.modern_relevance: You read a text message in anger and decide the other person is cold. Later you learn they were rushing to a hospital. The mind fills gaps with its own story.
ramacharitamanas::313.insight: It shifts the mind from quick judgment to careful seeing, especially when the truth is hidden by emotion.

ramacharitamanas::314.verse_sanskrit: संभु समय तेहि रामहि देखा। उपजा हियँ अति हरषु बिसेषा ॥ भरि लोचन छबिसिंधु निहारी। कुसमय जानि न कीन्हि चिन्हारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::314.verse_hindi: श्री शिवजी ने उसी अवसर पर श्री रामजी को देखा और उनके हृदय में बहुत भारी आनंद उत्पन्न हुआ। उन शोभा के समुद्र (श्री रामचंद्रजी) को शिवजी ने नेत्र भरकर देखा, परन्तु अवसर ठीक न जानकर परिचय नहीं किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::314.english_translation: At that moment Shiva saw Ram, and immense joy arose in his heart. He gazed at the ocean of beauty with full eyes, but knowing the timing was not right, he did not greet him.
ramacharitamanas::314.translation_literal: संभु (Shiva) / समय तेहि (at that moment) / रामहि (Ram) / देखा (saw) / उपजा (arose) / हियँ (in the heart) / अति (great) / हरषु (joy) / बिसेषा (special, immense) ॥ / भरि (filled) / लोचन (eyes) / छबिसिंधु (ocean of beauty) / निहारी (having seen) / कुसमय (bad time, not the right moment) / जानि (knowing) / न (not) / कीन्हि (did) / चिन्हारी (greeting, recognition) ॥
ramacharitamanas::314.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::314.essence: Deep devotion can wait without losing its joy.
ramacharitamanas::314.simple_meaning: Shiva sees Ram and feels overwhelming joy, but he does not step forward because the moment is not right.
ramacharitamanas::314.simple_insight: Sometimes love is shown by restraint, not by immediate action.
ramacharitamanas::314.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Shiva finally sees Ram. His heart fills with joy at once, but he holds back from greeting Ram because the moment is not fitting. The verse captures devotion so deep it waits for the right time.
ramacharitamanas::314.modern_relevance: You spot someone you deeply admire across a crowded hall, and your first urge is to rush forward. Instead, you pause, let the moment ripen, and honor the situation.
ramacharitamanas::314.insight: It teaches reverence with timing: affection is real, but it also knows when to wait.

ramacharitamanas::315.verse_sanskrit: जय सच्चिदानंद जग पावन। अस कहि चलेउ मनोज नसावन॥ चले जात सिव सती समेता। पुनि पुनि पुलकत कृपानिकेता ॥
ramacharitamanas::315.verse_hindi: जगत् को पवित्र करने वाले सच्चिदानंद की जय हो, इस प्रकार कहकर कामदेव का नाश करने वाले श्री शिवजी चल पड़े। कृपानिधान शिवजी बार-बार आनंद से पुलकित होते हुए सतीजी के साथ चले जा रहे थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::315.english_translation: Victory to the sacred, consciousness-bliss form who purifies the world. Saying this, Shiva, who destroys desire, moved on with Sati. The abode of grace walked again and again, thrilled with joy.
ramacharitamanas::315.translation_literal: जय (victory) / सच्चिदानंद (existence-consciousness-bliss) / जग पावन (world-purifying) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / चलेउ (went) / मनोज नसावन (destroyer of desire) / चले (walking) / जात (going) / सिव (Shiva) / सती (Sati) / समेता (together with) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / पुलकत (thrilled, bristling) / कृपानिकेता (abode of grace)
ramacharitamanas::315.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::315.essence: True devotion keeps moving, but joy keeps breaking through.
ramacharitamanas::315.simple_meaning: Shiva praises Ram as the pure, blissful one who cleanses the world, then walks on with Sati, repeatedly stirred by joy at what he has seen.
ramacharitamanas::315.simple_insight: A glimpse of the divine can leave even the greatest devotee trembling with joy.
ramacharitamanas::315.detailed_meaning: Shiva has just seen Ram and is leaving with Sati. Overcome with devotion, he praises Ram as the pure, blissful one who sanctifies the world. The verse shows Shiva still glowing with that vision as Sati walks beside him, unaware of the depth of his joy.
ramacharitamanas::315.modern_relevance: You leave a temple, a concert, or a hospital room still shaken by what you witnessed. Your face changes before your words do. Some encounters keep echoing in the body long after they end.
ramacharitamanas::315.insight: It shifts attention from outer motion to inner transformation: real encounter leaves visible signs.

ramacharitamanas::316.verse_sanskrit: सतीं सो दसा संभु कै देखी। उर उपजा संदेहु बिसेषी॥ संकरु जगतबंद्य जगदीसा। सुर नर मुनि सब नावत सीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::316.verse_hindi: सतीजी ने शंकरजी की वह दशा देखी तो उनके मन में बड़ा संदेह उत्पन्न हो गया। (वे मन ही मन कहने लगीं कि) शंकरजी की सारा जगत् वंदना करता है, वे जगत् के ईश्वर हैं, देवता, मनुष्य, मुनि सब उनके प्रति सिर नवाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::316.english_translation: Sati saw that state of Shiva, and a deep doubt arose in her heart. Shiva is worshipped by the whole world; he is the lord of the world, and gods, humans, and sages all bow their heads to him.
ramacharitamanas::316.translation_literal: सतीं (Sati) / सो (that) / दसा (state) / संभु (Shiva) / कै (of) / देखी (saw) / उर (in heart) / उपजा (arose) / संदेहु (doubt) / बिसेषी (great)॥ / संकरु (Shiva) / जगतबंद्य (worshipped by the world) / जगदीसा (lord of the world) / सुर (devas) / नर (humans) / मुनि (sages) / सब (all) / नावत (bow) / सीसा (heads) ॥
ramacharitamanas::316.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::316.essence: Even the most revered figure can be doubted when the heart cannot read devotion.
ramacharitamanas::316.simple_meaning: Sati sees Shiva behaving in a surprising way and doubts it. She remembers that everyone in the world bows to Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::316.simple_insight: Status and reverence can still be misunderstood when the heart is clouded by doubt.
ramacharitamanas::316.detailed_meaning: Sati is watching Shiva in the Shiva-Parvati frame of Balkand, just after he has bowed to Ram. The sight unsettles her because Shiva is normally the most revered being in the world. Her doubt begins here.
ramacharitamanas::316.modern_relevance: You watch a respected mentor act in a way you did not expect, and your first reaction is suspicion. The verse shows how quickly reverence can turn into doubt when you cannot yet see the larger devotion behind the act.
ramacharitamanas::316.insight: It shifts attention from Shiva’s outer status to Sati’s inner misunderstanding.

ramacharitamanas::317.verse_sanskrit: तिन्ह नृपसुतहि कीन्ह परनामा। कहि सच्चिदानंद परधामा॥ भए मगन छबि तासु बिलोकी। अजहुँ प्रीति उर रहति न रोकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::317.verse_hindi: उन्होंने एक राजपुत्र को सच्चिदानंद परधाम कहकर प्रणाम किया और उसकी शोभा देखकर वे इतने प्रेममग्न हो गए कि अब तक उनके हृदय में प्रीति रोकने से भी नहीं रुकती ॥
ramacharitamanas::317.english_translation: They bowed to that prince, calling him the supreme being beyond all worlds. Seeing his beauty, they were so absorbed in love that their hearts still could not stop it.
ramacharitamanas::317.translation_literal: तिन्ह (they) / नृपसुतहि (to the king's son) / कीन्ह (made) / परनामा (bowed) / कहि (saying) / सच्चिदानंद (being of truth-consciousness-bliss) / परधामा (supreme abode) / भए (became) / मगन (immersed) / छबि (beauty) / तासु (of him) / बिलोकी (seeing) / अजहुँ (even now) / प्रीति (love) / उर (in the heart) / रहति (remains) / न (not) / रोकी (stopped)
ramacharitamanas::317.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::317.essence: Seeing the divine beauty awakens love that does not fade.
ramacharitamanas::317.simple_meaning: Shiva and Parvati bow to the prince and recognize him as the supreme reality. His beauty awakens such love that it still overflows in their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::317.simple_insight: Real recognition deepens love instead of reducing it.
ramacharitamanas::317.detailed_meaning: Shiva and Parvati have come into the scene and see the young prince before them. Shiva bows first, naming him as the supreme reality, and his beauty leaves them both absorbed. The moment shows reverence turning into love.
ramacharitamanas::317.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm presence changes the room before they speak. Respect comes first, then a strange warmth stays with you long after you leave.
ramacharitamanas::317.insight: It shifts devotion from distant praise to immediate, lived recognition.

ramacharitamanas::318.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्म जो ब्यापक बिरज अज अकल अनीह अभेद। सो कि देह धरि होइ नर जाहि न जानत बेद ॥
ramacharitamanas::318.verse_hindi: जो ब्रह्म सर्वव्यापक, मायारहित, अजन्मा, अगोचर, इच्छारहित और भेदरहित है और जिसे वेद भी नहीं जानते, क्या वह देह धारण करके मनुष्य हो सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::318.english_translation: Can the all-pervading, pure, unborn, inactive, desireless, and undivided supreme reality take a human body, when even the Vedas do not know it?
ramacharitamanas::318.translation_literal: ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / जो (which) / ब्यापक (all-pervading) / बिरज (pure, free from dust) / अज (unborn) / अकल (inactive) / अनीह (desireless) / अभेद (undivided) / सो (that) / कि (can?) / देह (body) / धरि (having taken) / होइ (becomes) / नर (human) / जाहि (which) / न (not) / जानत (know) / बेद (the Vedas)
ramacharitamanas::318.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::318.essence: What seems impossible may be beyond the reach of ordinary understanding.
ramacharitamanas::318.simple_meaning: The supreme reality is beyond birth, action, desire, and division. The verse asks how such a reality could possibly take a human body.
ramacharitamanas::318.simple_insight: Some truths are larger than the mind’s first conclusion. Humility begins when certainty gives way to wonder.
ramacharitamanas::318.detailed_meaning: Sati has just seen Shiva bow to a young prince and feels doubt rise. The poem pauses on that doubt: how could the all-pervading supreme reality ever become a human being? It sets up the deeper revelation that follows.
ramacharitamanas::318.modern_relevance: You hear a claim that seems impossible and your first instinct is to dismiss it. This verse catches that reflex and asks you to sit with the limits of your own understanding before judging too quickly.
ramacharitamanas::318.insight: It shifts the mind from quick disbelief to patient discernment.

ramacharitamanas::319.verse_sanskrit: बिष्नु जो सुर हित नरतनु धारी। सोउ सर्बग्य जथा त्रिपुरारी॥ खोजइ सो कि अग्य इव नारी। ग्यानधाम श्रीपति असुरारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::319.verse_hindi: देवताओं के हित के लिए मनुष्य शरीर धारण करने वाले जो विष्णु भगवान् हैं, वे भी शिवजी की ही भाँति सर्वज्ञ हैं। वे ज्ञान के भंडार, लक्ष्मीपति और असुरों के शत्रु भगवान् विष्णु क्या अज्ञानी की तरह स्त्री को खोजेंगे? ॥
ramacharitamanas::319.english_translation: Vishnu, who took a human form for the good of the gods, is all-knowing like Tripurari. Would the Lord of wisdom, Lakshmi's lord, and the enemy of demons search for a woman like someone ignorant?
ramacharitamanas::319.translation_literal: बिष्नु (Vishnu) / जो (who) / सुर हित (for the good of the gods) / नरतनु (human form) / धारी (having taken) / सोउ (he also) / सर्बग्य (all-knowing) / जथा (like) / त्रिपुरारी (Shiva)॥ / खोजइ (would search) / सो (he) / कि (would) / अग्य (ignorant) / इव (like) / नारी (woman) / ग्यानधाम (abode of wisdom) / श्रीपति (lord of Lakshmi) / असुरारी (enemy of demons)॥
ramacharitamanas::319.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::319.essence: Ram's human actions never come from ignorance.
ramacharitamanas::319.simple_meaning: Vishnu, who has taken human form for the good of the gods, is all-knowing. He would not go searching for a woman like someone who does not know what he is doing.
ramacharitamanas::319.simple_insight: The mind is being asked to trust what it already knows: Ram's actions are never blind or foolish.
ramacharitamanas::319.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, the sages are defending Ram's divinity after his human birth is doubted. They insist that Vishnu, like Shiva, is all-knowing. The line rejects the idea that Ram could behave like an ignorant man.
ramacharitamanas::319.modern_relevance: When someone you trust makes a hard choice you do not understand, the mind rushes to doubt. This verse asks you to pause and remember: wisdom is often hidden inside the action.
ramacharitamanas::319.insight: It shifts the reader from suspicious interpretation to reverent confidence in Ram's awareness.

ramacharitamanas::320.verse_sanskrit: संभुगिरा पुनि मृषा न होई। सिव सर्बग्य जान सबु कोई॥ अस संसय मन भयउ अपारा। होइ न हृदयँ प्रबोध प्रचारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::320.verse_hindi: फिर शिवजी के वचन भी झूठे नहीं हो सकते। सब कोई जानते हैं कि शिवजी सर्वज्ञ हैं। सती के मन में इस प्रकार का अपार संदेह उठ खड़ा हुआ, किसी तरह भी उनके हृदय में ज्ञान का प्रादुर्भाव नहीं होता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::320.english_translation: Shiva's words cannot be false. Everyone knows Shiva is all-knowing. Yet an immense doubt arose in Sati's mind, and no awakening of understanding could enter her heart.
ramacharitamanas::320.translation_literal: संभु-गिरा (Shiva's words) / पुनि (again) / मृषा (false) / न (not) / होई (be) । / सिव (Shiva) / सर्बग्य (all-knowing) / जान (know) / सबु (all) / कोई (everyone) ॥ / अस (such) / संसय (doubt) / मन (mind) / भयउ (arose) / अपारा (vast) । / होइ (become) / न (not) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / प्रबोध (awakening) / प्रचारा (spread) ॥
ramacharitamanas::320.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::320.essence: Truth can be known and still not enter the heart.
ramacharitamanas::320.simple_meaning: Sati knows Shiva speaks truth, yet doubt still takes over her mind. Her heart cannot receive clarity.
ramacharitamanas::320.simple_insight: Knowing the truth is not the same as being able to live it.
ramacharitamanas::320.detailed_meaning: Sati has heard Shiva's words about Ram, but her mind cannot settle. She knows Shiva is all-knowing, yet doubt keeps growing inside her. This moment shows the fracture between understanding and inner readiness.
ramacharitamanas::320.modern_relevance: You read the message twice, know it is probably right, and still feel your chest tighten. The mind can accept a fact while the heart keeps resisting it.
ramacharitamanas::320.insight: It separates intellectual certainty from inner acceptance, showing how doubt can block clear seeing.

ramacharitamanas::321.verse_sanskrit: जद्यपि प्रगट न कहेउ भवानी। हर अंतरजामी सब जानी॥ सुनहि सती तव नारि सुभाऊ। संसय अस न धरिअ उर काऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::321.verse_hindi: यद्यपि भवानीजी ने प्रकट कुछ नहीं कहा, पर अन्तर्यामी शिवजी सब जान गए। वे बोले- हे सती! सुनो, तुम्हारा स्त्री स्वभाव है। ऐसा संदेह मन में कभी न रखना चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::321.english_translation: Although you did not say it openly, the all-knowing Lord within knows everything. Listen, Sati: such doubt should never be kept in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::321.translation_literal: जद्यपि (although) / प्रगट (openly) / न (not) / कहेउ (said) / भवानी (Bhavani) / हर (Shiva) / अंतरजामी (inner-knower) / सब (everything) / जानी (knew)॥ / सुनहि (listen) / सती (Sati) / तव (your) / नारि (womanly) / सुभाऊ (nature) / संसय (doubt) / अस (such) / न (not) / धरिअ (should be kept) / उर (in the heart) / काऊ (at all)॥
ramacharitamanas::321.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::321.essence: Unspoken doubt still reshapes the heart.
ramacharitamanas::321.simple_meaning: Shiva sees Sati's hidden doubt and warns her not to keep such suspicion in her heart.
ramacharitamanas::321.simple_insight: Hidden doubt is heavier than spoken doubt; naming it is the first step toward clarity.
ramacharitamanas::321.detailed_meaning: Sati has not voiced her suspicion, but Shiva, who knows the heart from within, reads it instantly. In the middle of this tense exchange, he warns her that doubt should not be harboured inwardly, because it will distort what comes next.
ramacharitamanas::321.modern_relevance: You smile in the conversation, but your mind has already started mistrusting. The problem is not only what you say out loud; it is the doubt you keep feeding in silence.
ramacharitamanas::321.insight: It shifts attention from outward politeness to the hidden belief shaping your response.

ramacharitamanas::322.verse_sanskrit: जासु कथा कुंभज रिषि गाई। भगति जासु मैं मुनिहि सुनाई॥ सोइ मम इष्टदेव रघुबीरा। सेवत जाहि सदा मुनि धीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::322.verse_hindi: जिनकी कथा का अगस्त्य ऋषि ने गान किया और जिनकी भक्ति मैंने मुनि को सुनाई, ये वही मेरे इष्टदेव श्री रघुवीरजी हैं, जिनकी सेवा ज्ञानी मुनि सदा किया करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::322.english_translation: The sage Agastya sang Ram's story, and I taught the sage his devotion. That same Raghubir is my chosen deity, whom steady sages always serve.
ramacharitamanas::322.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / कथा (story) / कुंभज रिषि (sage Kumbhaja/Agastya) / गाई (sang) / भगति (devotion) / जासु (whose) / मैं (I) / मुनिहि (to the sage) / सुनाई (taught, made heard) / सोइ (that same) / मम (my) / इष्टदेव (chosen deity) / रघुबीरा (Raghubir, Ram) / सेवत (serving) / जाहि (whom) / सदा (always) / मुनि (sages) / धीरा (steady, wise)
ramacharitamanas::322.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::322.essence: The wise do not outgrow devotion; they deepen into it.
ramacharitamanas::322.simple_meaning: Agastya praised Ram's story, and Shiva says he taught that devotion to the sage. The same Ram is Shiva's chosen Lord, and wise sages always serve Him.
ramacharitamanas::322.simple_insight: Devotion is not beneath wisdom; it is what wisdom naturally bows to.
ramacharitamanas::322.detailed_meaning: In the opening frame of Balkand, Shiva is speaking to Parvati about Ram's greatness. He says that Agastya once sang Ram's story, and Shiva himself taught that devotion to a sage. The point is simple and immense: Ram is the chosen Lord even of the most steady, wise seekers.
ramacharitamanas::322.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm is deeper than their intelligence. They do not argue about what matters; they quietly serve it. This verse says real wisdom ends in reverence, not pride.
ramacharitamanas::322.insight: It shifts the mind from treating devotion as emotional weakness to seeing it as the crown of discernment.

ramacharitamanas::323.verse_sanskrit: मुनि धीर जोगी सिद्ध संतत बिमल मन जेहि ध्यावहीं। कहि नेति निगम पुरान आगम जासु कीरति गावहीं॥ सोइ रामु ब्यापक ब्रह्म भुवन निकाय पति माया धनी। अवतरेउ अपने भगत हित निजतंत्र नित रघुकुलमनी॥
ramacharitamanas::323.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी मुनि, योगी और सिद्ध निरंतर निर्मल चित्त से जिनका ध्यान करते हैं तथा वेद, पुराण और शास्त्र 'नेति-नेति' कहकर जिनकी कीर्ति गाते हैं, उन्हीं सर्वव्यापक, समस्त ब्रह्मांडों के स्वामी, मायापति, नित्य परम स्वतंत्र, ब्रह्मा रूप भगवान् श्री रामजी ने अपने भक्तों के हित के लिए (अपनी इच्छा से) रघुकुल के मणिरूप में अवतार लिया है।
ramacharitamanas::323.english_translation: Ascetics, sages, yogis, and perfected beings meditate on him with pure minds. The Vedas, Puranas, and scriptures sing his glory as 'not this, not this.' He is Ram: all-pervading Brahman, lord of all worlds, master of illusion, eternally independent. For the sake of his devotees, the jewel of Raghu took birth by his own will.
ramacharitamanas::323.translation_literal: मुनि धीर (steady sages) / जोगी (yogis) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / संतत (continuously) / बिमल मन (pure mind) / जेहि (whom) / ध्यावहीं (meditate on) / कहि (saying) / नेति (not this) / निगम (Vedas) / पुरान (Puranas) / आगम (scriptures) / जासु (whose) / कीरति (glory) / गावहीं (sing) / सोइ (that same) / रामु (Ram) / ब्यापक (all-pervading) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / भुवन (worlds) / निकाय (assemblies) / पति (lord) / माया धनी (master of illusion) / अवतरेउ (descended) / अपने (his own) / भगत हित (for devotees' sake) / निजतंत्र (self-willed, independent) / नित (eternal) / रघुकुलमनी (jewel of the Raghu line)
ramacharitamanas::323.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::323.essence: The limitless one becomes visible through love.
ramacharitamanas::323.simple_meaning: Ram is the supreme reality beyond description, yet he appears in the world by his own will for the sake of his devotees.
ramacharitamanas::323.simple_insight: It brings awe and comfort together: the highest reality is not distant from love.
ramacharitamanas::323.detailed_meaning: Shiva has just been explaining Ram’s greatness to Parvati. Now the praise rises to its peak: sages meditate on him, scriptures fail to capture him, and yet that same boundless Ram chooses to enter the world for his devotees. This is the heart of the verse.
ramacharitamanas::323.modern_relevance: You can spend years trying to define someone you love, only to discover their deepest truth is that they showed up for you when they could have stayed beyond reach.
ramacharitamanas::323.insight: It shifts the mind from abstract divinity to personal grace: the boundless one becomes approachable through devotion.

ramacharitamanas::324.verse_sanskrit: लाग न उर उपदेसु जदपि कहेउ सिवँ बार बहु। बोले बिहसि महेसु हरिमाया बलु जानि जियँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::324.verse_hindi: यद्यपि शिवजी ने बहुत बार समझाया, फिर भी सतीजी के हृदय में उनका उपदेश नहीं बैठा। तब महादेवजी मन में भगवान् की माया का बल जानकर मुस्कुराते हुए बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::324.english_translation: Although Shiva had explained many times, the teaching did not settle in Sati's heart. Then Mahadeva, knowing in his mind the power of the divine veil, smiled and spoke.
ramacharitamanas::324.translation_literal: लाग (settled) / न (not) / उर (heart) / उपदेसु (instruction) / जदपि (although) / कहेउ (said) / सिवँ (Shiva) / बार (times) / बहु (many) / बोले (spoke) / बिहसि (smiling) / महेसु (Mahesh) / हरिमाया (the divine veil) / बलु (power) / जानि (knowing) / जियँ (in the mind/heart)
ramacharitamanas::324.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::324.essence: A warning can fail when the mind is already trapped.
ramacharitamanas::324.simple_meaning: Sati still does not accept Shiva's warning. Shiva understands that the divine veil is affecting her mind, and he smiles as he speaks.
ramacharitamanas::324.simple_insight: Not every warning lands. Sometimes the mind is already caught before it can listen.
ramacharitamanas::324.detailed_meaning: Sati has heard Shiva's advice many times, but doubt still rules her heart. Shiva sees that the divine veil is at work and, rather than forcing the point, speaks with a knowing smile. The verse sets up the next test he gives her.
ramacharitamanas::324.modern_relevance: You keep repeating the same warning to someone you love, but they still cannot hear it. Sometimes the problem is not the words — it is the state of mind receiving them.
ramacharitamanas::324.insight: It shifts attention from the message itself to the receiver's readiness to receive it.

ramacharitamanas::325.verse_sanskrit: जौं तुम्हरें मन अति संदेहू। तौ किन जाइ परीछा लेहू॥ तब लगि बैठ अहउँ बटछाहीं। जब लगि तुम्ह ऐहहु मोहि पाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::325.verse_hindi: जो तुम्हारे मन में बहुत संदेह है तो तुम जाकर परीक्षा क्यों नहीं लेती? जब तक तुम मेरे पास लौट आओगी तब तक मैं इसी बड़ की छाँह में बैठा हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::325.english_translation: If your mind is full of doubt, then go and test it yourself. Until you return to me, I will sit beneath this banyan tree.
ramacharitamanas::325.translation_literal: जौं (if) / तुम्हरें (your) / मन (mind) / अति (very) / संदेहू (doubt) / तौ (then) / किन (why not) / जाइ (go) / परीछा (test) / लेहू (take) / तब लगि (until then) / बैठ (sit) / अहउँ (I am) / बटछाहीं (beneath the banyan tree) / जब लगि (until) / तुम्ह (you) / ऐहहु (will come) / मोहि (to me) / पाहीं (near)
ramacharitamanas::325.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::325.essence: Doubt is answered by seeing, not by pressure.
ramacharitamanas::325.simple_meaning: If doubt is troubling you, go examine the matter for yourself. Shiva says he will wait under the banyan tree until Sati returns.
ramacharitamanas::325.simple_insight: Doubt is not punished here; it is invited to look closely and find out.
ramacharitamanas::325.detailed_meaning: In the opening frame of Ramcharitmanas, Shiva has explained Ram's greatness to Sati, but her doubt remains. Rather than forcing belief, he tells her to investigate for herself and waits calmly beneath the banyan tree while she goes to test the truth.
ramacharitamanas::325.modern_relevance: You keep rereading the message because something feels off. Instead of spiraling, step back, check the facts, and let reality answer the doubt.
ramacharitamanas::325.insight: It shifts the mind from anxious suspicion to direct investigation.

ramacharitamanas::326.verse_sanskrit: जैसें जाइ मोह भ्रम भारी। करेहु सो जतनु बिबेक बिचारी॥ चलीं सती सिव आयसु पाई। करहिं बेचारु करौं का भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::326.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार तुम्हारा यह अज्ञानजनित भारी भ्रम दूर हो, (भली-भाँति) विवेक के द्वारा सोच-समझकर तुम वही करना। शिवजी की आज्ञा पाकर सती चलीं और मन में सोचने लगीं कि भाई! क्या करूँ (कैसे परीक्षा लूँ)? ॥
ramacharitamanas::326.english_translation: As you remove this heavy confusion, act with clear seeing and careful thought. Sati received Shiva's command and went away, wondering, “Sister, what should I do?”
ramacharitamanas::326.translation_literal: जैसें (as) / जाइ (going away) / मोह (delusion) / भ्रम (confusion) / भारी (heavy) / करेहु (do) / सो (that) / जतनु (effort) / बिबेक (clear seeing) / बिचारी (having considered) / चलीं (she went) / सती (Sati) / सिव (Shiva) / आयसु (command) / पाई (having received) / करहिं (doing) / बेचारु (consideration) / करौं (what should I do) / का (what) / भाई (sister/brother)
ramacharitamanas::326.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::326.essence: Confusion ends only when clear seeing replaces anxious doubt.
ramacharitamanas::326.simple_meaning: Clear seeing is the cure for confusion. Sati obeys Shiva, but her mind still turns in doubt as she goes to test him.
ramacharitamanas::326.simple_insight: A restless mind cannot be forced into trust; it must be seen through clearly.
ramacharitamanas::326.detailed_meaning: After Shiva has warned Sati again and again, he sends her to judge for herself. She walks away under his command, but her mind keeps circling in doubt. This verse shows the moment where confusion is still stronger than trust.
ramacharitamanas::326.modern_relevance: You keep rereading the message, then asking three friends what it meant. The facts are there, but your mind is still spinning. Clear seeing has to replace suspicion.
ramacharitamanas::326.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional suspicion to careful self-examination before acting.

ramacharitamanas::327.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ संभु अस मन अनुमाना। दच्छसुता कहुँ नहिं कल्याना॥ मोरेहु कहें न संसय जाहीं। बिधि बिपरीत भलाई नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::327.verse_hindi: इधर शिवजी ने मन में ऐसा अनुमान किया कि दक्षकन्या सती का कल्याण नहीं है। जब मेरे समझाने से भी संदेह दूर नहीं होता तब (मालूम होता है) विधाता ही उलटे हैं, अब सती का कुशल नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::327.english_translation: Shiva then thought: 'There is no good for Sati, the daughter of Daksha. Even my words cannot remove this doubt. Fate itself seems reversed, and no well-being remains for her.'
ramacharitamanas::327.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / संभु (Shiva) / अस (thus) / मन (mind) / अनुमाना (concluded) / दच्छसुता (daughter of Daksha) / कहुँ (for) / नहिं (not) / कल्याना (well-being)॥ / मोरेहु (even by me) / कहें (having said) / न (not) / संसय (doubt) / जाहीं (goes away) / बिधि (fate) / बिपरीत (reversed) / भलाई (good) / नाहीं (not)॥
ramacharitamanas::327.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::327.essence: Some doubts cannot be undone once the heart has moved.
ramacharitamanas::327.simple_meaning: Shiva sees that Sati will not be well, and even his warning cannot remove her doubt. He feels the situation has turned against what is good.
ramacharitamanas::327.simple_insight: Sometimes wisdom arrives too late to change what a mind has already chosen.
ramacharitamanas::327.detailed_meaning: Shiva has already warned Sati not to test Ram by going to Daksha's sacrifice. Watching her doubt remain unshaken, he sees that her path is now heading toward pain. This verse marks his quiet, painful recognition that counsel alone will not stop what is unfolding.
ramacharitamanas::327.modern_relevance: You explain the risk clearly, but the other person is already committed to the mistake. At some point, seeing the truth does not mean you can stop the fall.
ramacharitamanas::327.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to force understanding to seeing when a choice has already hardened.

ramacharitamanas::328.verse_sanskrit: होइहि सोइ जो राम रचि राखा। को करि तर्क बढ़ावै साखा॥ अस कहि लगे जपन हरिनामा। गईं सती जहँ प्रभु सुखधामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::328.verse_hindi: जो कुछ राम ने रच रखा है, वही होगा। तर्क करके कौन शाखा (विस्तार) बढ़ावे। (मन में) ऐसा कहकर शिवजी भगवान् श्री हरि का नाम जपने लगे और सतीजी वहाँ गईं, जहाँ सुख के धाम प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::328.english_translation: What Ram has woven, that alone will happen. Why stretch arguments further? Saying this, Shiva began chanting the name of Hari, and Sati went to where Lord Ram, the abode of bliss, was.
ramacharitamanas::328.translation_literal: होइहि (will happen) / सोइ (that only) / जो (which) / राम (Ram) / रचि (having woven) / राखा (has kept) / को (who) / करि (doing) / तर्क (argument) / बढ़ावै (would increase) / साखा (branch) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / लगे (began) / जपन (chanting) / हरिनामा (the name of Hari) / गईं (went) / सती (Sati) / जहँ (where) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सुखधामा (abode of bliss)
ramacharitamanas::328.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::328.essence: What Ram has arranged does not need your argument.
ramacharitamanas::328.simple_meaning: Everything unfolds as Ram has already arranged it. Shiva stops arguing, turns to chanting Ram's name, and Sati goes on toward Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::328.simple_insight: There is peace in stopping the argument and trusting what is already set in motion.
ramacharitamanas::328.detailed_meaning: Shiva sees that Sati's doubt will not be eased by more reasoning. In this Balkand scene, he recognises Ram's design as final, abandons debate, and turns to chanting Ram's name while Sati moves toward the place where Ram is present.
ramacharitamanas::328.modern_relevance: You have already explained yourself three times in the group chat, and the conversation still circles. At some point, the wiser move is to stop forcing the point and let reality unfold.
ramacharitamanas::328.insight: It shifts the mind from argumentative control to surrendering to what cannot be changed.

ramacharitamanas::329.verse_sanskrit: पुनि पुनि हृदयँ बिचारु करि धरि सीता कर रूप। आगें होइ चलि पंथ तेहिं जेहिं आवत नरभूप ॥
ramacharitamanas::329.verse_hindi: सती बार-बार मन में विचार कर सीताजी का रूप धारण करके उस मार्ग की ओर आगे होकर चलीं, जिससे (सतीजी के विचारानुसार) मनुष्यों के राजा रामचंद्रजी आ रहे थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::329.english_translation: Again and again, after pondering in her heart, Sati took on Sita’s form and went ahead on the path by which the king of men, Ram, was coming.
ramacharitamanas::329.translation_literal: पुनि पुनि (again and again) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारु (thought, reflection) / करि (having done) / धरि (taking on) / सीता (Sita) / कर (of) / रूप (form) / आगें (ahead) / होइ (having become) / चलि (went) / पंथ (path) / तेहिं (that) / जेहिं (by which) / आवत (coming) / नरभूप (king of men)
ramacharitamanas::329.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::329.essence: Repeated thought can turn into self-deception.
ramacharitamanas::329.simple_meaning: Sati keeps thinking, then disguises herself as Sita and moves toward the path where Ram is expected to come.
ramacharitamanas::329.simple_insight: A restless mind can dress itself as innocence and still move toward confusion.
ramacharitamanas::329.detailed_meaning: Shiva has already sensed that Sati’s test is turning against her. Now she keeps thinking, takes Sita’s form, and moves toward the path where Ram will arrive. This is the moment her inner doubt turns into outward action.
ramacharitamanas::329.modern_relevance: You rehearse a story in your head until it feels true, then act from it. The costume may look convincing, but the mind behind it is still driving the scene.
ramacharitamanas::329.insight: It shows how repeated rumination can lead a person to act out an assumption instead of seeing clearly.

ramacharitamanas::330.verse_sanskrit: लछिमन दीख उमाकृत बेषा। चकित भए भ्रम हृदयँ बिसेषा॥ कहि न सकत कछु अति गंभीरा। प्रभु प्रभाउ जानत मतिधीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::330.verse_hindi: सतीजी के बनावटी वेष को देखकर लक्ष्मणजी चकित हो गए और उनके हृदय में बड़ा भ्रम हो गया। वे बहुत गंभीर हो गए, कुछ कह नहीं सके। धीर बुद्धि लक्ष्मण प्रभु रघुनाथजी के प्रभाव को जानते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::330.english_translation: Seeing Uma's disguised form, Lakshman was startled and deeply confused. He became very grave and could say nothing. The steady-minded Lakshman knew the power of the Lord.
ramacharitamanas::330.translation_literal: लछिमन (Lakshman) / दीख (saw) / उमाकृत (made by Uma) / बेषा (form, disguise) / चकित (startled) / भए (became) / भ्रम (confusion) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिसेषा (greatly) / कहि (to say) / न (not) / सकत (able) / कछु (anything) / अति (very) / गंभीरा (grave, serious) / प्रभु (Lord) / प्रभाउ (power, influence) / जानत (knowing) / मतिधीरा (steady-minded)
ramacharitamanas::330.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::330.essence: Confusion does not have to become speech.
ramacharitamanas::330.simple_meaning: Lakshman is startled by Sati's disguise and falls into deep confusion. He stays quiet, because he understands Ram's power and does not rush to speak.
ramacharitamanas::330.simple_insight: Not every strange moment needs a reaction. A steady mind can stay quiet until the truth is clear.
ramacharitamanas::330.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sati has appeared in a false form to test Ram. Lakshman sees the disguise, feels confusion rise, and goes silent. His seriousness shows both caution and his clear respect for Ram's unseen power.
ramacharitamanas::330.modern_relevance: You notice something off in a conversation and feel your mind jump ahead. Lakshman’s pause reminds you that not every suspicion deserves instant speech.
ramacharitamanas::330.insight: It teaches you to hold back speech when perception is unsettled and to trust steady discernment over impulse.

ramacharitamanas::331.verse_sanskrit: सती कपटु जानेउ सुरस्वामी। सबदरसी सब अंतरजामी॥ सुमिरत जाहि मिटइ अग्याना। सोइ सरबग्य रामु भगवाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::331.verse_hindi: सब कुछ देखने वाले और सबके हृदय की जानने वाले देवताओं के स्वामी श्री रामचंद्रजी सती के कपट को जान गए, जिनके स्मरण मात्र से अज्ञान का नाश हो जाता है, वही सर्वज्ञ भगवान् श्री रामचंद्रजी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::331.english_translation: Lord Ram, who sees everything and knows every heart, understood Sati's deception. By remembering Him, ignorance is destroyed. He is the all-knowing, glorious Ram.
ramacharitamanas::331.translation_literal: सती (Sati) / कपटु (deception) / जानेउ (knew) / सुरस्वामी (lord of the radiant beings) / सबदरसी (all-seeing) / सब (all) / अंतरजामी (knower of all hearts)॥ / सुमिरत (remembering) / जाहि (whom) / मिटइ (is destroyed) / अग्याना (ignorance) / सोइ (that same) / सरबग्य (all-knowing) / रामु (Ram) / भगवाना (the glorious one)॥
ramacharitamanas::331.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::331.essence: Ram's clear seeing ends deception and ignorance at once.
ramacharitamanas::331.simple_meaning: Ram sees through Sati's disguise because He knows every heart. Remembering Him removes ignorance, because He is fully aware of all things.
ramacharitamanas::331.simple_insight: You do not have to hide from clear seeing. Real remembrance makes self-deception lose its power.
ramacharitamanas::331.detailed_meaning: Sati has approached Ram in disguise, hoping to conceal her true intention. But Ram, the one who sees all and knows every heart, immediately understands the deception. The verse turns the scene into a lesson about divine awareness and the ending of ignorance.
ramacharitamanas::331.modern_relevance: You rehearse a lie in your head before a difficult conversation, then feel exposed the moment the other person looks at you calmly. This verse says clear seeing can strip away the mask before words even begin.
ramacharitamanas::331.insight: It shifts attention from concealment to inner honesty, showing that remembrance of Ram dissolves confusion at its root.

ramacharitamanas::332.verse_sanskrit: सती कीन्ह चह तहँहुँ दुराऊ। देखहु नारि सुभाव प्रभाऊ॥ निज माया बलु हृदयँ बखानी। बोले बिहसि रामु मृदु बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::332.verse_hindi: स्त्री स्वभाव का असर तो देखो कि वहाँ (उन सर्वज्ञ भगवान् के सामने) भी सतीजी छिपाव करना चाहती हैं। अपनी माया के बल को हृदय में बखानकर, श्री रामचंद्रजी हँसकर कोमल वाणी से बोले ॥
ramacharitamanas::332.english_translation: Sati still tried to hide it there too. See the power of a woman's nature. Ram smiled softly and spoke, saying in his heart that this was the strength of his own illusion.
ramacharitamanas::332.translation_literal: सती (Sati) / कीन्ह चह (wanted to do) / तहँहुँ (there too) / दुराऊ (concealment, hiding) / देखहु (see) / नारि (woman) / सुभाव (natural disposition) / प्रभाऊ (power, influence) / निज (own) / माया (illusion) / बलु (strength) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बखानी (described, acknowledged) / बोले (spoke) / बिहसि (smiling) / रामु (Ram) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (words)
ramacharitamanas::332.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::332.simple_meaning: Sati still tried to conceal herself, and Ram gently recognized that this was the force of his own illusion at work.
ramacharitamanas::332.simple_insight: Even hidden motives cannot escape clear seeing.
ramacharitamanas::332.detailed_meaning: Sati, disguised as Parvati, is still trying to keep her identity hidden from Ram. Ram sees through the concealment without anger and speaks with a soft smile, showing his all-knowing awareness and the play of his own illusion in the scene.
ramacharitamanas::332.modern_relevance: You rehearse a harmless excuse in your head before speaking, but the other person already senses the dodge. Ram's calm seeing cuts through the mask without cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::332.insight: It shifts the mind from clever concealment to honest recognition of what is already visible.

ramacharitamanas::333.verse_sanskrit: जोरि पानि प्रभु कीन्ह प्रनामू। पिता समेत लीन्ह निज नामू॥ कहेउ बहोरि कहाँ बृषकेतू। बिपिन अकेलि फिरहु केहि हेतू ॥
ramacharitamanas::333.verse_hindi: पहले प्रभु ने हाथ जोड़कर सती को प्रणाम किया और पिता सहित अपना नाम बताया। फिर कहा कि वृषकेतु शिवजी कहाँ हैं? आप यहाँ वन में अकेली किसलिए फिर रही हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::333.english_translation: The Lord bowed with joined hands and gave his name along with his father’s. Then he asked, “Where is Shiva, the Bull-bannered one? Why do you wander alone in the forest?”
ramacharitamanas::333.translation_literal: जोरि (joining) / पानि (hands) / प्रभु (the Lord) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रनामू (salutation) / पिता (father) / समेत (along with) / लीन्ह (took) / निज (his own) / नामू (name) / कहेउ (said) / बहोरि (again) / कहाँ (where) / बृषकेतू (Shiva) / बिपिन (forest) / अकेलि (alone) / फिरहु (wander) / केहि (what) / हेतू (reason)
ramacharitamanas::333.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::333.essence: Grace answers suspicion without losing composure.
ramacharitamanas::333.simple_meaning: Ram respectfully greets Sati, identifies himself through his father, and asks where Shiva is and why she is alone in the forest.
ramacharitamanas::333.simple_insight: Even in a tense moment, Ram meets confusion with courtesy.
ramacharitamanas::333.detailed_meaning: Sati has come to test Ram’s identity in the forest. Ram answers not with anger but with grace: he bows, names himself through Dasharath, and gently asks about Shiva and her lonely wandering. The scene shows his calm dignity before Sati’s doubt turns heavier.
ramacharitamanas::333.modern_relevance: Someone questions you in a guarded tone, and you can feel the tension rise. You still answer with respect, stay composed, and ask the real question underneath the surface.
ramacharitamanas::333.insight: It teaches you to keep dignity and courtesy even when others are testing you.

ramacharitamanas::334.verse_sanskrit: राम बचन मृदु गूढ़ सुनि उपजा अति संकोचु। सती सभीत महेस पहिं चलीं हृदयँ बड़ सोचु ॥
ramacharitamanas::334.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के कोमल और रहस्य भरे वचन सुनकर सतीजी को बड़ा संकोच हुआ। वे डरती हुई (चुपचाप) शिवजी के पास चलीं, उनके हृदय में बड़ी चिन्ता हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::334.english_translation: Hearing Ram's gentle, veiled words, Sati felt deep shame. Fearful, she went to Mahesh, her heart full of worry.
ramacharitamanas::334.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बचन (words) / मृदु (gentle) / गूढ़ (hidden, profound) / सुनि (hearing) / उपजा (arose) / अति (very) / संकोचु (shame, hesitation)। / सती (Sati) / सभीत (fearful) / महेस (Mahesh/Shiva) / पहिं (to) / चलीं (went) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बड़ (great) / सोचु (worry)
ramacharitamanas::334.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::334.essence: Hidden doubt turns into shame when clear seeing meets it.
ramacharitamanas::334.simple_meaning: Sati hears Ram's calm, subtle words and feels embarrassed and uneasy. She goes back to Shiva with fear and heavy worry in her heart.
ramacharitamanas::334.simple_insight: A half-truth can create more inner pain than an open mistake.
ramacharitamanas::334.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sati has tested Ram and now hears his gentle, knowing reply. His words unsettle her. Ashamed and afraid, she returns to Shiva, already feeling the weight of what she has done.
ramacharitamanas::334.modern_relevance: You send a message trying to hide your real doubt, and the reply lands too cleanly. Suddenly your own pretence feels loud. The heart knows when it has been seen.
ramacharitamanas::334.insight: It shows how concealment collapses under clear seeing, pushing the mind into shame and self-correction.

ramacharitamanas::335.verse_sanskrit: मैं संकर कर कहा न माना। निज अग्यानु राम पर आना॥ जाइ उतरु अब देहउँ काहा। उर उपजा अति दारुन दाहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::335.verse_hindi: कि मैंने शंकरजी का कहना न माना और अपने अज्ञान का श्री रामचन्द्रजी पर आरोप किया। अब जाकर मैं शिवजी को क्या उत्तर दूँगी? (यों सोचते-सोचते) सतीजी के हृदय में अत्यन्त भयानक जलन पैदा हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::335.english_translation: I did not obey Shankar’s words and placed my ignorance upon Ram. What answer will I give now? As she thought this, a fierce burning rose in Sati’s heart.
ramacharitamanas::335.translation_literal: मैं (I) / संकर (Shankar) / कर (of) / कहा (said) / न (not) / माना (obeyed) / निज (own) / अग्यानु (ignorance) / राम (on Ram) / पर (upon) / आना (bringing) / जाइ (going) / उतरु (answer) / अब (now) / देहउँ (I will give) / काहा (what) / उर (heart) / उपजा (arose) / अति (very) / दारुन (fierce) / दाहा (burning)
ramacharitamanas::335.speaker: Sati
ramacharitamanas::335.essence: The first pain of error is finally seeing it clearly.
ramacharitamanas::335.simple_meaning: Sati realizes she ignored Shiva’s warning and wrongly blamed Ram. Shame and inner burning rise as she faces the consequence of her mistake.
ramacharitamanas::335.simple_insight: Self-deception hurts first. Clear seeing begins the moment you admit, “I was wrong.”
ramacharitamanas::335.detailed_meaning: Sati has gone to test Ram and now feels the result of that choice. After hearing Ram’s gentle words, she sees that she ignored Shiva’s counsel and projected her own confusion onto Ram. The burning in her heart is the pain of recognition.
ramacharitamanas::335.modern_relevance: You reread the message after sending the accusation and feel your stomach drop. The ache is not punishment from outside — it is the cost of seeing your own mistake clearly.
ramacharitamanas::335.insight: It shifts the mind from blaming outward to witnessing its own confusion.

ramacharitamanas::336.verse_sanskrit: जाना राम सतीं दुखु पावा। निज प्रभाउ कछु प्रगटि जनावा॥ सतीं दीख कौतुकु मग जाता। आगें रामु सहित श्री भ्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::336.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने जान लिया कि सतीजी को दुःख हुआ, तब उन्होंने अपना कुछ प्रभाव प्रकट करके उन्हें दिखलाया। सतीजी ने मार्ग में जाते हुए यह कौतुक देखा कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित आगे चले जा रहे हैं। (इस अवसर पर सीताजी को इसलिए दिखाया कि सतीजी श्री राम के सच्चिदानंदमय रूप को देखें, वियोग और दुःख की कल्पना जो उन्हें हुई थी, वह दूर हो जाए तथा वे प्रकृतिस्थ हों।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::336.english_translation: Ram understood that Sati was distressed, so he revealed a little of his power to her. As Sati watched on the road, she saw the wonder of Ram walking ahead with Sita and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::336.translation_literal: जाना (understood) / राम (Ram) / सतीं (Sati) / दुखु (distress) / पावा (received) / निज (his own) / प्रभाउ (power, influence) / कछु (some) / प्रगटि (revealing) / जनावा (made known) / सतीं (Sati) / दीख (saw) / कौतुकु (wonder) / मग (road, path) / जाता (going) / आगें (ahead) / रामु (Ram) / सहित (together with) / श्री भ्राता (the honored brother)
ramacharitamanas::336.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::336.essence: A glimpse of Ram corrects confusion before it hardens.
ramacharitamanas::336.simple_meaning: Ram sees Sati's distress and briefly reveals his divine power. Sati then sees Ram walking ahead with Sita and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::336.simple_insight: Sometimes a hidden truth is shown just enough to soften confusion.
ramacharitamanas::336.detailed_meaning: After Sati doubts what she has seen, Ram notices her distress and reveals a glimpse of his power. On the road, Sati then sees Ram, Sita, and Lakshman moving ahead in a wondrous form, preparing the deeper revelation that follows.
ramacharitamanas::336.modern_relevance: You misread someone, then catch one small moment that changes everything. A single clear sight can dissolve a whole spiral of doubt.
ramacharitamanas::336.insight: It shifts attention from Sati's inner confusion to the revealing of Ram's presence.

ramacharitamanas::337.verse_sanskrit: फिरि चितवा पाछें प्रभु देखा। सहित बंधु सिय सुंदर बेषा॥ जहँ चितवहिं तहँ प्रभु आसीना। सेवहिं सिद्ध मुनीस प्रबीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::337.verse_hindi: (तब उन्होंने) पीछे की ओर फिरकर देखा, तो वहाँ भी भाई लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी के साथ श्री रामचन्द्रजी सुंदर वेष में दिखाई दिए। वे जिधर देखती हैं, उधर ही प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी विराजमान हैं और सुचतुर सिद्ध मुनीश्वर उनकी सेवा कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::337.english_translation: Turning back, she saw the Lord again there, together with his brother and Sita in a beautiful form. Wherever she looked, the Lord was seated there, and perfected sages and wise ascetics were serving him.
ramacharitamanas::337.translation_literal: फिरि (again/turning back) / चितवा (looked) / पाछें (behind/back) / प्रभु (Lord) / देखा (saw) / सहित (together with) / बंधु (brother) / सिय (Sita) / सुंदर (beautiful) / बेषा (form/attire)॥ / जहँ (where) / चितवहिं (she looks) / तहँ (there) / प्रभु (Lord) / आसीना (seated) / सेवहिं (serve) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / मुनीस (great sages) / प्रबीना (wise/expert)
ramacharitamanas::337.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::337.essence: Ram appears everywhere to the one who can truly see.
ramacharitamanas::337.simple_meaning: Sati turns and sees Ram, Lakshman, and Sita again in a beautiful form. Wherever she looks, Ram is present, and sages are serving him.
ramacharitamanas::337.simple_insight: The divine form is not limited by one place. It can appear wherever sincere vision turns.
ramacharitamanas::337.detailed_meaning: Sati has already doubted Shiva's words and now sees Ram's presence unfolding before her eyes. As she turns, Ram appears again with Lakshman and Sita, and then appears everywhere she looks, served by sages. The scene prepares her deeper realization.
ramacharitamanas::337.modern_relevance: You keep searching one corner of the room for an answer, then notice it was never confined to one spot. The same truth keeps showing up from every angle once your attention changes.
ramacharitamanas::337.insight: It shifts attention from chasing one fixed image to recognising presence as all-pervading.

ramacharitamanas::338.verse_sanskrit: देखे सिव बिधि बिष्नु अनेका। अमित प्रभाउ एक तें एका॥ बंदत चरन करत प्रभु सेवा। बिबिध बेष देखे सब देवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::338.verse_hindi: सतीजी ने अनेक शिव, ब्रह्मा और विष्णु देखे, जो एक से एक बढ़कर असीम प्रभाव वाले थे। (उन्होंने देखा कि) भाँति-भाँति के वेष धारण किए सभी देवता श्री रामचन्द्रजी की चरणवन्दना और सेवा कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::338.english_translation: Sati saw countless Shivas, Brahmas, and Vishnus, each more immeasurably radiant than the last. She saw all the radiant beings in many forms bowing at Ram's feet and serving him.
ramacharitamanas::338.translation_literal: देखे (saw) / सिव (Shiva) / बिधि (Brahma) / बिष्नु (Vishnu) / अनेका (many) / अमित (immeasurable) / प्रभाउ (power, radiance) / एक तें एका (one greater than another) / बंदत (bowing) / चरन (feet) / करत (doing) / प्रभु (lord) / सेवा (service) / बिबिध (various) / बेष (forms, disguises) / देखे (saw) / सब (all) / देवा (radiant beings)
ramacharitamanas::338.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::338.essence: The greatest beings are the ones who bow first.
ramacharitamanas::338.simple_meaning: Sati sees endless divine forms, each radiant and powerful, all bowing to Ram and serving him in different disguises.
ramacharitamanas::338.simple_insight: Real greatness bows before humility. The highest beings are shown as servants, not rivals.
ramacharitamanas::338.detailed_meaning: Sati is still following the strange figure she met on the road. As her vision deepens, she sees countless forms of Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu, and other radiant beings, all serving Ram in different disguises. The scene reveals Ram's hidden supremacy before the next verse expands it further.
ramacharitamanas::338.modern_relevance: You meet someone quietly helping everyone in the room, while the loudest people keep seeking attention. Real stature often shows up as service, not display.
ramacharitamanas::338.insight: It shifts the mind from ranking power by appearance to recognising reverence as the mark of true greatness.

ramacharitamanas::339.verse_sanskrit: सती बिधात्री इंदिरा देखीं अमित अनूप। जेहिं जेहिं बेष अजादि सुर तेहि तेहि तन अनुरूप ॥
ramacharitamanas::339.verse_hindi: उन्होंने अनगिनत अनुपम सती, ब्रह्माणी और लक्ष्मी देखीं। जिस-जिस रूप में ब्रह्मा आदि देवता थे, उसी के अनुकूल रूप में (उनकी) ये सब (शक्तियाँ) भी थीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::339.english_translation: Sati saw countless incomparable forms of the divine feminine powers—Brahma's consort, Lakshmi, and others. In whatever form the ancient beings appeared, their forms matched that appearance.
ramacharitamanas::339.translation_literal: सती (Sati) / बिधात्री (Brahma's consort) / इंदिरा (Lakshmi) / देखीं (saw) / अमित (countless) / अनूप (matchless) / जेहिं जेहिं (in whichever) / बेष (form) / अजादि (the ancient ones, beginning with Brahma) / सुर (radiant beings) / तेहि तेहि (in that very) / तन (body/form) / अनुरूप (matching)
ramacharitamanas::339.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::339.essence: Each radiant being appears in the form that belongs to it.
ramacharitamanas::339.simple_meaning: Sati sees endless divine forms, and each form matches the being it belongs to. The scene shows a universe where every power appears in a fitting shape.
ramacharitamanas::339.simple_insight: Reality is not random or flat; each presence carries a form that belongs to it.
ramacharitamanas::339.detailed_meaning: In the midst of Sati's vision, she sees Brahma's consort, Lakshmi, and countless other unmatched forms. The sight is not a single teaching yet, but part of a larger revelation: every radiant being appears in a form suited to its nature.
ramacharitamanas::339.modern_relevance: You meet someone and instantly sense their role, their energy, their place in the room. Some presences fit themselves so completely that the outer form feels inevitable.
ramacharitamanas::339.insight: It prepares the mind to see form and essence as aligned, not accidental.

ramacharitamanas::340.verse_sanskrit: देखे जहँ जहँ रघुपति जेते। सक्तिन्ह सहित सकल सुर तेते॥ जीव चराचर जो संसारा। देखे सकल अनेक प्रकारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::340.verse_hindi: सतीजी ने जहाँ-जहाँ जितने रघुनाथजी देखे, शक्तियों सहित वहाँ उतने ही सारे देवताओं को भी देखा। संसार में जो चराचर जीव हैं, वे भी अनेक प्रकार के सब देखे ॥
ramacharitamanas::340.english_translation: Wherever Sati saw Raghu's lord, she saw all the radiant beings there with their powers. She also saw all moving and unmoving beings in the world, in many forms.
ramacharitamanas::340.translation_literal: देखे (saw) / जहँ जहँ (wherever, wherever) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / जेते (as many as) / सक्तिन्ह (with powers) / सहित (together with) / सकल (all) / सुर (radiant beings) / तेते (so many) ॥ / जीव (living beings) / चराचर (moving and unmoving) / जो (which) / संसारा (world) / देखे (saw) / सकल (all) / अनेक (many) / प्रकारा (kinds) ॥
ramacharitamanas::340.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::340.essence: One presence appears in endless forms.
ramacharitamanas::340.simple_meaning: Sati sees Ram everywhere and, with him, all the radiant beings and all living forms in the world.
ramacharitamanas::340.simple_insight: The same presence fills every form, so nothing stands apart from it.
ramacharitamanas::340.detailed_meaning: Sati is still in her vision of the cosmic form. Wherever she looks for Raghu's lord, she sees countless radiant beings with their powers and all moving and unmoving life in endless variety. This verse expands the revelation before the next line turns to worship.
ramacharitamanas::340.modern_relevance: You walk into a crowded station and suddenly notice how many lives are moving at once — each with its own burden, each part of one larger field of reality.
ramacharitamanas::340.insight: It shifts attention from isolated figures to the shared presence behind all forms.
