ramacharitamanas::341.verse_sanskrit: पूजहिं प्रभुहि देव बहु बेषा। राम रूप दूसर नहिं देखा॥ अवलोके रघुपति बहुतेरे। सीता सहित न बेष घनेरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::341.verse_hindi: (उन्होंने देखा कि) अनेकों वेष धारण करके देवता प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी की पूजा कर रहे हैं, परन्तु श्री रामचन्द्रजी का दूसरा रूप कहीं नहीं देखा। सीता सहित श्री रघुनाथजी बहुत से देखे, परन्तु उनके वेष अनेक नहीं थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::341.english_translation: Many deities worshiped the Lord in many forms, but no second form of Ram was seen. Raghunath was seen many times with Sita, but not in many disguises.
ramacharitamanas::341.translation_literal: पूजहिं (worship) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / देव (deities) / बहु (many) / बेषा (forms, disguises) / राम (Ram) / रूप (form) / दूसर (another) / नहिं (not) / देखा (seen) ॥ / अवलोके (saw) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / बहुतेरे (many) / सीता सहित (with Sita) / न (not) / बेष (forms, disguises) / घनेरे (many, numerous) ॥
ramacharitamanas::341.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::341.essence: Ram does not need many forms to be fully present.
ramacharitamanas::341.simple_meaning: The deities appeared in many forms, but Ram did not appear as a second, separate form. Sita and Ram were seen many times, yet not in countless disguises.
ramacharitamanas::341.simple_insight: Some truths do not multiply into appearances. The heart is being shown one steady presence, not a crowd of changing masks.
ramacharitamanas::341.detailed_meaning: Sati is watching the divine mystery unfold. She sees countless deities taking forms to honor Ram, yet Ram himself remains singular. In this moment, Tulsidas is leading her toward a terrifying recognition that the same beloved presence is everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::341.modern_relevance: You keep scrolling through polished versions of the same person, same brand, same promise. Then one presence cuts through all the noise because it does not need costumes to be real.
ramacharitamanas::341.insight: It shifts attention from changing appearances to the one reality beneath them.

ramacharitamanas::342.verse_sanskrit: सोइ रघुबर सोइ लछिमनु सीता। देखि सती अति भईं सभीता॥ हृदय कंप तन सुधि कछु नाहीं। नयन मूदि बैठीं मग माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::342.verse_hindi: (सब जगह) वही रघुनाथजी, वही लक्ष्मण और वही सीताजी- सती ऐसा देखकर बहुत ही डर गईं। उनका हृदय काँपने लगा और देह की सारी सुध-बुध जाती रही। वे आँख मूँदकर मार्ग में बैठ गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::342.english_translation: Seeing the same Raghubar, the same Lakshman, and the same Sita, Sati became very frightened. Her heart trembled; she lost all bodily awareness and sat down on the path with her eyes closed.
ramacharitamanas::342.translation_literal: सोइ (that same) / रघुबर (Lord of the Raghu clan) / सोइ (that same) / लछिमनु (Lakshman) / सीता (Sita) / देखि (seeing) / सती (Sati) / अति (greatly) / भईं (became) / सभीता (afraid) / हृदय (heart) / कंप (trembled) / तन (body) / सुधि (awareness) / कछु (some) / नाहीं (not) / नयन (eyes) / मूदि (closing) / बैठीं (sat) / मग (path) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::342.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::342.essence: Overwhelm can silence the body before the mind understands.
ramacharitamanas::342.simple_meaning: Sati sees Ram, Lakshman, and Sita in every form and becomes overwhelmed with fear. Her heart shakes, her senses fail, and she sits down with her eyes closed.
ramacharitamanas::342.simple_insight: When the mind cannot hold what it sees, the body gives way first.
ramacharitamanas::342.detailed_meaning: Sati has already been seeing divine forms everywhere on the path. Now the sight of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita in every form overwhelms her completely. Her fear becomes physical: her heart trembles, her awareness slips, and she collapses into stillness before the next revelation.
ramacharitamanas::342.modern_relevance: You open a message and realize you have misunderstood the whole situation. Your chest tightens, your thoughts scatter, and you need a moment before you can even respond.
ramacharitamanas::342.insight: It shows how shock can shut down perception before understanding catches up.

ramacharitamanas::343.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि बिलोकेउ नयन उघारी। कछु न दीख तहँ दच्छकुमारी॥ पुनि पुनि नाइ राम पद सीसा। चलीं तहाँ जहँ रहे गिरीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::343.verse_hindi: फिर आँख खोलकर देखा, तो वहाँ दक्षकुमारी (सतीजी) को कुछ भी न दिख पड़ा। तब वे बार-बार श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर वहाँ चलीं, जहाँ श्री शिवजी थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::343.english_translation: She opened her eyes again, but saw nothing there. Then, bowing again and again at Ram's feet, she went to where Shiva was.
ramacharitamanas::343.translation_literal: बहुरि (again) / बिलोकेउ (looked) / नयन (eyes) / उघारी (opened) / कछु (something) / न (not) / दीख (seen) / तहँ (there) / दच्छकुमारी (daughter of Daksha) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / नाइ (bowing) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / सीसा (head) / चलीं (went) / तहाँ (there) / जहँ (where) / रहे (were staying) / गिरीसा (Shiva)
ramacharitamanas::343.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::343.essence: Sight can fail, but devotion keeps moving.
ramacharitamanas::343.simple_meaning: Sati opens her eyes again but cannot see Ram's form. She keeps bowing to Ram and then goes to Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::343.simple_insight: Even confusion can become reverence when the heart keeps bowing.
ramacharitamanas::343.detailed_meaning: Sati has just seen Ram and Sita in a divine vision and then lost sight of them. Startled, she opens her eyes again and finds nothing. Still shaken, she bows to Ram again and walks back to Shiva, where the next question will come.
ramacharitamanas::343.modern_relevance: You double-check the message, the email, the screen — and the clarity is gone. In that small panic, the only steady response is to bow to what is higher than your confusion.
ramacharitamanas::343.insight: It shows how reverence continues even after perception fails, and how the scene moves toward Shiva's questioning.

ramacharitamanas::344.verse_sanskrit: गईं समीप महेस तब हँसि पूछी कुसलात। लीन्हि परीछा कवन बिधि कहहु सत्य सब बात ॥
ramacharitamanas::344.verse_hindi: जब पास पहुँचीं, तब श्री शिवजी ने हँसकर कुशल प्रश्न करके कहा कि तुमने रामजी की किस प्रकार परीक्षा ली, सारी बात सच-सच कहो ॥
ramacharitamanas::344.english_translation: Then Mahesh came near, smilingly asked after her welfare, and said, "Tell me truly: in what way did you test Ram? Tell the whole truth."
ramacharitamanas::344.translation_literal: गईं (went) / समीप (near) / महेस (Shiva) / तब (then) / हँसि (smiling) / पूछी (asked) / कुसलात (welfare) / लीन्हि (took) / परीछा (test) / कवन (which) / बिधि (way) / कहहु (tell) / सत्य (truth) / सब (all) / बात (matter)
ramacharitamanas::344.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::344.essence: Shiva invites truth, not performance, after Sati's failed test.
ramacharitamanas::344.simple_meaning: Shiva comes near Sati, asks kindly about her well-being, and asks her to tell the truth about how she tested Ram.
ramacharitamanas::344.simple_insight: Honest conversation begins where pride ends.
ramacharitamanas::344.detailed_meaning: Sati has just returned after trying to test Ram and finding herself shaken. Shiva meets her with a smile and asks what really happened. The moment is a gentle but piercing opening for truth before her fear turns into denial.
ramacharitamanas::344.modern_relevance: You come home after a conversation you wish you could take back. The other person is calm, not accusing, and that calm makes it harder to hide. Truth has a way of arriving softly.
ramacharitamanas::344.insight: It shifts the mind from concealment to confession, showing that clarity begins with telling the whole story.

ramacharitamanas::345.verse_sanskrit: सतीं समुझि रघुबीर प्रभाऊ। भय बस सिव सन कीन्ह दुराऊ॥ कछु न परीछा लीन्हि गोसाईं। कीन्ह प्रनामु तुम्हारिहि नाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::345.verse_hindi: सतीजी ने श्री रघुनाथजी के प्रभाव को समझकर डर के मारे शिवजी से छिपाव किया और कहा- हे स्वामिन् ! मैंने कुछ भी परीक्षा नहीं ली, (वहाँ जाकर) आपकी ही तरह प्रणाम किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::345.english_translation: Sati understood the power of Ram and, out of fear, concealed the truth from Shiva. "I did not test him at all, lord; I bowed to you in the same way."
ramacharitamanas::345.translation_literal: सतीं (Sati) / समुझि (having understood) / रघुबीर (Ram, lord of the Raghu line) / प्रभाऊ (power, influence) / भय बस (under the force of fear) / सिव सन (from Shiva) / कीन्ह (did) / दुराऊ (concealment) / कछु (anything) / न (not) / परीछा (test) / लीन्हि (took) / गोसाईं (lord) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रनामु (bow) / तुम्हारिहि (to you) / नाईं (like, in the manner of)
ramacharitamanas::345.speaker: Sati
ramacharitamanas::345.essence: Recognition of greatness can make concealment feel safer than honesty.
ramacharitamanas::345.simple_meaning: Sati hides what she did because she has realized Ram's power and feels afraid to speak plainly to Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::345.simple_insight: Fear makes honesty shrink; clear seeing begins when pride stops defending itself.
ramacharitamanas::345.detailed_meaning: After Sati returns from trying to test Ram, she stands before Shiva and cannot tell the whole truth. She has felt Ram's power and now speaks carefully, hiding her act because fear and shame have entered the scene.
ramacharitamanas::345.modern_relevance: You come home after saying something careless in a meeting, then soften the story when someone asks what happened. The real issue is not the event — it is the fear of being seen clearly.
ramacharitamanas::345.insight: It shows how ego protects itself once it meets something greater than it expected.

ramacharitamanas::346.verse_sanskrit: जो तुम्ह कहा सो मृषा न होई। मोरें मन प्रतीति अति सोई॥ तब संकर देखेउ धरि ध्याना। सतीं जो कीन्ह चरित सबु जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::346.verse_hindi: आपने जो कहा वह झूठ नहीं हो सकता, मेरे मन में यह बड़ा (पूरा) विश्वास है। तब शिवजी ने ध्यान करके देखा और सतीजी ने जो चरित्र किया था, सब जान लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::346.english_translation: What you said cannot be false; I trust it deeply in my mind. Then Shiva looked through meditation and understood everything Sati had done.
ramacharitamanas::346.translation_literal: जो (which/what) तुम्ह (you) कहा (said) सो (that) मृषा (false) न (not) होई (is) / मोरें (my) मन (mind) प्रतीति (trust/conviction) अति (very) सोई (that) / तब (then) संकर (Shiva) देखेउ (saw) धरि (holding) ध्याना (meditation) / सतीं (Sati) जो (which) कीन्ह (did) चरित (deed/conduct) सबु (all) जाना (understood)
ramacharitamanas::346.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::346.essence: Trust may begin with words, but truth appears in still seeing.
ramacharitamanas::346.simple_meaning: Shiva tells Sati he trusts her words, then sees through meditation that she has hidden the truth about what happened.
ramacharitamanas::346.simple_insight: Trust can be sincere and still miss what is hidden. Clear seeing often comes only after quiet reflection.
ramacharitamanas::346.detailed_meaning: Sati has just tried to conceal her test of Ram from Shiva. Shiva accepts her words at first, but then turns inward in meditation and sees the full truth of her actions. The scene shifts from spoken trust to inner knowing.
ramacharitamanas::346.modern_relevance: Someone gives you a neat explanation after a tense conversation, and you want to accept it. Later, when you sit quietly and replay the details, you realize something important was left out.
ramacharitamanas::346.insight: It shifts the mind from surface trust to deeper discernment through still attention.

ramacharitamanas::347.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि राममायहि सिरु नावा। प्रेरि सतिहि जेहिं झूँठ कहावा॥ हरि इच्छा भावी बलवाना। हृदयँ बिचारत संभु सुजाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::347.verse_hindi: फिर श्री रामचन्द्रजी की माया को सिर नवाया, जिसने प्रेरणा करके सती के मुँह से भी झूठ कहला दिया। सुजान शिवजी ने मन में विचार किया कि हरि की इच्छा रूपी भावी प्रबल है ॥
ramacharitamanas::347.english_translation: Again he bowed to the power of Ram's illusion, which had made even Sati speak falsely. Wise Shiva reflected in his heart that the will of Hari and the force of what is to come are mighty.
ramacharitamanas::347.translation_literal: बहुरि (again) / राममायहि (to Ram's illusion) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / प्रेरि (having impelled) / सतिहि (Sati) / जेहिं (which) / झूँठ (falsehood) / कहावा (was made to speak) / हरि (Hari) / इच्छा (will) / भावी (what is to come) / बलवाना (powerful) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारत (reflecting) / संभु (Shiva) / सुजाना (wise)
ramacharitamanas::347.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::347.essence: Even falsehood can serve a power larger than human control.
ramacharitamanas::347.simple_meaning: Shiva bows to Ram's mysterious power and realises that divine will and what must unfold are stronger than human certainty.
ramacharitamanas::347.simple_insight: It softens the urge to control everything. Some events reveal a larger order only after they happen.
ramacharitamanas::347.detailed_meaning: Sati has tested Shiva by taking the form of Sita. After seeing through the deception, Shiva bows again, now to Ram's mysterious power. In that moment, he understands that even falsehood can be carried by a greater will.
ramacharitamanas::347.modern_relevance: You replay a conversation and realise the mistake was already in motion before you understood it. The verse meets that helpless moment and says: some outcomes are bigger than your private certainty.
ramacharitamanas::347.insight: It shifts the mind from personal control to humility before a larger unfolding.

ramacharitamanas::348.verse_sanskrit: सतीं कीन्ह सीता कर बेषा। सिव उर भयउ बिषाद बिसेषा॥ जौं अब करउँ सती सन प्रीती। मिटइ भगति पथु होइ अनीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::348.verse_hindi: सतीजी ने सीताजी का वेष धारण किया, यह जानकर शिवजी के हृदय में बड़ा विषाद हुआ। उन्होंने सोचा कि यदि मैं अब सती से प्रीति करता हूँ तो भक्तिमार्ग लुप्त हो जाता है और बड़ा अन्याय होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::348.english_translation: Sati took on Sita's form, and Shiva felt deep sorrow in his heart. He thought, 'If I now show affection to Sati, the path of devotion will be lost and great wrongdoing will follow.'
ramacharitamanas::348.translation_literal: सतीं (Sati) / कीन्ह (made) / सीता (Sita) / कर (of the hand; as) / बेषा (form/disguise) / सिव (Shiva) / उर (heart) / भयउ (became) / बिषाद (sorrow) / बिसेषा (great) / जौं (if) / अब (now) / करउँ (I do) / सती सन (with Sati) / प्रीती (affection) / मिटइ (would be erased) / भगति (devotion) / पथु (path) / होइ (would become) / अनीती (wrongdoing)
ramacharitamanas::348.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::348.essence: Clear seeing can require refusing even sincere attachment.
ramacharitamanas::348.simple_meaning: Sati appears as Sita, and Shiva feels sorrow. He sees that continuing personal affection would damage devotion and create wrongdoing.
ramacharitamanas::348.simple_insight: Real devotion includes the courage to stop even what feels emotionally natural.
ramacharitamanas::348.detailed_meaning: Sati has tested Shiva by taking Sita's form. Shiva sees through the disguise and feels pain, not desire. In this moment, he recognises that private attachment would corrupt the higher path he must protect.
ramacharitamanas::348.modern_relevance: You realise a relationship is becoming a trap, not a bond. Even though your heart wants to hold on, you step back because staying would blur what is right.
ramacharitamanas::348.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional impulse to clear moral seeing.

ramacharitamanas::349.verse_sanskrit: परम पुनीत न जाइ तजि किएँ प्रेम बड़ पापु। प्रगटि न कहत महेसु कछु हृदयँ अधिक संतापु ॥
ramacharitamanas::349.verse_hindi: सती परम पवित्र हैं, इसलिए इन्हें छोड़ते भी नहीं बनता और प्रेम करने में बड़ा पाप है। प्रकट करके महादेवजी कुछ भी नहीं कहते, परन्तु उनके हृदय में बड़ा संताप है ॥
ramacharitamanas::349.english_translation: Sati is supremely pure, so I cannot abandon her; yet loving her is a great wrong. Mahesh says nothing aloud, but his heart burns with deep distress.
ramacharitamanas::349.translation_literal: परम पुनीत (supremely pure) / न जाइ तजि (cannot be abandoned) / किएँ प्रेम (by loving) / बड़ पापु (great wrong) / प्रगटि (outwardly) / न कहत (does not say) / महेसु (Mahesh/Shiva) / कछु (anything) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / अधिक (great) / संतापु (distress)
ramacharitamanas::349.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::349.essence: Purity and attachment can clash until the heart aches in silence.
ramacharitamanas::349.simple_meaning: Shiva feels torn: Sati is pure, yet his attachment to her now feels wrong. He says nothing, but the pain inside him is intense.
ramacharitamanas::349.simple_insight: Some conflicts cannot be spoken first; they have to be carried honestly until the heart can release them.
ramacharitamanas::349.detailed_meaning: Sati has taken Sita's form, and Shiva instantly sees the danger to his devotion. He knows she is pure, yet he also knows his attachment has become a fault. He stays silent, holding the sorrow inside.
ramacharitamanas::349.modern_relevance: You realize someone you care about is not who you thought they were. No dramatic speech comes out, only that tight, silent ache in the chest.
ramacharitamanas::349.insight: It shows the mind can recognize a painful truth before the tongue can speak it.

ramacharitamanas::350.verse_sanskrit: तब संकर प्रभु पद सिरु नावा। सुमिरत रामु हृदयँ अस आवा॥ एहिं तन सतिहि भेंट मोहि नाहीं। सिव संकल्पु कीन्ह मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::350.verse_hindi: तब शिवजी ने प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरण कमलों में सिर नवाया और श्री रामजी का स्मरण करते ही उनके मन में यह आया कि सती के इस शरीर से मेरी (पति-पत्नी रूप में) भेंट नहीं हो सकती और शिवजी ने अपने मन में यह संकल्प कर लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::350.english_translation: Then Shiva bowed his head at the Lord's feet. Remembering Ram, this thought arose in his heart: 'I cannot meet Sati in this body.' Shiva made that resolve in his mind.
ramacharitamanas::350.translation_literal: तब (then) / संकर (Shiva) / प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / सुमिरत (remembering) / रामु (Ram) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / अस (thus) / आवा (came)॥ / एहिं (in this) / तन (body) / सतिहि (Sati) / भेंट (meeting) / मोहि (to me) / नाहीं (not) / सिव (Shiva) / संकल्पु (resolve) / कीन्ह (made) / मन (mind) / माहीं (within)॥
ramacharitamanas::350.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::350.simple_meaning: Shiva bows to Ram and realizes that his bond with Sati cannot continue in this body. He quietly resolves this in his mind.
ramacharitamanas::350.simple_insight: Letting go can be an act of reverence, not rejection.
ramacharitamanas::350.detailed_meaning: After seeing Sati's mistaken disguise, Shiva is filled with sorrow but does not cling. He bows to Ram, remembers him, and accepts that this body cannot sustain the old bond. The verse marks his inward decision to release the attachment.
ramacharitamanas::350.modern_relevance: You realize a relationship, role, or season has ended while sitting alone after midnight. Instead of forcing what no longer fits, you bow inwardly and let the next step become clear.
ramacharitamanas::350.insight: It teaches you to release a bond without bitterness when continuing would violate what is real.

ramacharitamanas::351.verse_sanskrit: अस बिचारि संकरु मतिधीरा। चले भवन सुमिरत रघुबीरा॥ चलत गगन भै गिरा सुहाई। जय महेस भलि भगति दृढ़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::351.verse_hindi: स्थिर बुद्धि शंकरजी ऐसा विचार कर श्री रघुनाथजी का स्मरण करते हुए अपने घर (कैलास) को चले। चलते समय सुंदर आकाशवाणी हुई कि हे महेश ! आपकी जय हो। आपने भक्ति की अच्छी दृढ़ता की ॥
ramacharitamanas::351.english_translation: Thinking thus, the steadfast Shiva went home, remembering Raghubir. As he walked, a lovely voice from the sky said, “Victory to Mahesh! Your devotion is firm and true.”
ramacharitamanas::351.translation_literal: अस (thus) / बिचारि (thinking) / संकरु (Shiva) / मतिधीरा (steadfast in mind) / चले (went) / भवन (to home) / सुमिरत (remembering) / रघुबीरा (Raghubir)॥ / चलत (while walking) / गगन (from the sky) / भै (became/was) / गिरा (voice) / सुहाई (lovely)॥ / जय (victory) / महेस (to Mahesh) / भलि (good/true) / भगति (devotion) / दृढ़ाई (firmness) ॥
ramacharitamanas::351.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::351.essence: True devotion keeps walking even after the choice is made.
ramacharitamanas::351.simple_meaning: Shiva leaves after remembering Ram, and a voice from the sky praises the firmness of his devotion.
ramacharitamanas::351.simple_insight: Steady devotion is seen, honored, and answered.
ramacharitamanas::351.detailed_meaning: Shiva has just chosen not to break his reverence for Sati and Ram. He turns back toward Kailash, still remembering Raghubir, and the sky itself praises the firmness of his devotion. The moment confirms that his inner loyalty is the real victory.
ramacharitamanas::351.modern_relevance: You walk away from a conflict without needing the last word. Later, the quiet in you says what applause never could: you stayed true.
ramacharitamanas::351.insight: It shifts attention from proving yourself to remaining faithful under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::352.verse_sanskrit: अस पन तुम्ह बिनु करइ को आना। रामभगत समरथ भगवाना॥ सुनि नभगिरा सती उर सोचा। पूछा सिवहि समेत सकोचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::352.verse_hindi: आपको छोड़कर दूसरा कौन ऐसी प्रतिज्ञा कर सकता है। आप श्री रामचन्द्रजी के भक्त हैं, समर्थ हैं और भगवान् हैं। इस आकाशवाणी को सुनकर सतीजी के मन में चिन्ता हुई और उन्होंने सकुचाते हुए शिवजी से पूछा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::352.english_translation: Who else can make such a vow except you? You are Ram's devotee, mighty, and divine. Hearing the voice from the sky, Sati felt troubled and shyly asked Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::352.translation_literal: अस (such) / पन (vow) / तुम्ह (you) / बिनु (without) / करइ (can make) / को (who) / आना (other) / रामभगत (Ram-devotee) / समरथ (capable) / भगवाना (divine)॥ / सुनि (hearing) / नभगिरा (voice from the sky) / सती (Sati) / उर (heart) / सोचा (thought, worry) / पूछा (asked) / सिवहि (to Shiva) / समेत (with) / सकोचा (shyness, hesitation) ॥
ramacharitamanas::352.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::352.essence: Praise can awaken doubt before it becomes understanding.
ramacharitamanas::352.simple_meaning: A voice from the sky praises Shiva's vow and calls him Ram's devotee. Sati becomes uneasy and, with hesitation, asks Shiva about it.
ramacharitamanas::352.simple_insight: Curiosity can open the door to a deeper truth, even when it begins with unease.
ramacharitamanas::352.detailed_meaning: After Shiva bows to Ram and turns toward Kailash, a heavenly voice praises his vow and his devotion. Sati hears it and feels troubled, then shyly questions Shiva. The verse sets up the doubt that leads to her testing of Shiva's devotion.
ramacharitamanas::352.modern_relevance: You hear someone praised for a choice you don't fully understand, and your mind tightens. That uneasy question can become the beginning of real seeing.
ramacharitamanas::352.insight: It shifts attention from outward praise to the inner question that follows it.

ramacharitamanas::353.verse_sanskrit: कीन्ह कवन पन कहहु कृपाला। सत्यधाम प्रभु दीनदयाला॥ जदपि सतीं पूछा बहु भाँती। तदपि न कहेउ त्रिपुर आराती ॥
ramacharitamanas::353.verse_hindi: हे कृपालु! कहिए, आपने कौन सी प्रतिज्ञा की है? हे प्रभो! आप सत्य के धाम और दीनदयालु हैं। यद्यपि सतीजी ने बहुत प्रकार से पूछा, परन्तु त्रिपुरारि शिवजी ने कुछ न कहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::353.english_translation: "O compassionate one, tell me what vow you made. O Lord, you are the abode of truth and the friend of the humble." Though Sati asked in many ways, the destroyer of the three cities still said nothing.
ramacharitamanas::353.translation_literal: कीन्ह (did/made) / कवन (which) / पन (vow) / कहहु (tell) / कृपाला (O compassionate one) / सत्यधाम (abode of truth) / प्रभु (Lord) / दीनदयाला (friend of the humble) / जदपि (although) / सतीं (Sati) / पूछा (asked) / बहु भाँती (in many ways) / तदपि (still) / न (not) / कहेउ (said) / त्रिपुर आराती (Shiva, enemy of Tripura)
ramacharitamanas::353.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::353.essence: Silence can carry a truth that words are not yet fit to hold.
ramacharitamanas::353.simple_meaning: Sati keeps asking Shiva what vow he made, but he stays silent even after she pleads in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::353.simple_insight: Sometimes the deepest answer is withheld until the listener is ready.
ramacharitamanas::353.detailed_meaning: Sati has heard the sky proclaim Shiva's greatness and Ram-bhakti. Curious and uneasy, she presses Shiva for the meaning of his vow. Shiva, knowing more than he says, remains silent. The moment builds suspense before Sati's misunderstanding deepens.
ramacharitamanas::353.modern_relevance: You keep asking the same question, but the other person only smiles and changes the subject. Silence can feel like a wall when you want certainty.
ramacharitamanas::353.insight: It shows that not every truth is spoken immediately; some are revealed only through patience and inner readiness.

ramacharitamanas::354.verse_sanskrit: सतीं हृदयँ अनुमान किय सबु जानेउ सर्बग्य। कीन्ह कपटु मैं संभु सन नारि सहज जड़ अग्य ॥
ramacharitamanas::354.verse_hindi: सतीजी ने हृदय में अनुमान किया कि सर्वज्ञ शिवजी सब जान गए। मैंने शिवजी से कपट किया, स्त्री स्वभाव से ही मूर्ख और बेसमझ होती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::354.english_translation: Sita understood in her heart that the all-knowing Shiva had seen everything. "I deceived Shiva; by nature, a woman is foolish and naive."
ramacharitamanas::354.translation_literal: सतीं (Sati) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / अनुमान (inference) / किय (made) / सबु (everything) / जानेउ (knew) / सर्बग्य (the all-knowing one) / कीन्ह (did) / कपटु (deceit) / मैं (I) / संभु सन (with Shiva) / नारि (woman) / सहज (by nature) / जड़ (foolish) / अग्य (ignorant)
ramacharitamanas::354.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::354.essence: Self-deception collapses the moment it is truly seen.
ramacharitamanas::354.simple_meaning: Sati realizes Shiva already knows what happened, and she feels ashamed for having hidden the truth from him.
ramacharitamanas::354.simple_insight: Shame grows when the mind sees its own concealment clearly.
ramacharitamanas::354.detailed_meaning: Sati has tested Shiva and now feels the sting of being seen by the all-knowing Lord. In this moment of private shame, the story turns from curiosity to self-recognition, preparing the deeper lesson about deceit and relationship.
ramacharitamanas::354.modern_relevance: You rehearse a lie in your head, then realize the other person already understood. The heat in your face is not from being caught — it is from finally seeing yourself clearly.
ramacharitamanas::354.insight: It shifts attention from the outer act of deception to the inner moment of self-awareness.

ramacharitamanas::355.verse_sanskrit: जलु पय सरिस बिकाइ देखहु प्रीति कि रीति भलि। बिलग होइ रसु जाइ कपट खटाई परत पुनि ॥
ramacharitamanas::355.verse_hindi: प्रीति की सुंदर रीति देखिए कि जल भी (दूध के साथ मिलकर) दूध के समान भाव बिकता है, परन्तु फिर कपट रूपी खटाई पड़ते ही पानी अलग हो जाता है (दूध फट जाता है) और स्वाद (प्रेम) जाता रहता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::355.english_translation: See the beautiful way of love: water mixed with milk seems to become milk, but a little sourness of deceit separates it and the taste is lost.
ramacharitamanas::355.translation_literal: जलु (water) / पय (milk) / सरिस (like) / बिकाइ (appears to become) / देखहु (see) / प्रीति (love) / कि (of) / रीति (way) / भलि (beautiful) / बिलग (separate) / होइ (becomes) / रसु (taste/essence) / जाइ (goes) / कपट (deceit) / खटाई (sourness) / परत (falls/enters) / पुनि (again)
ramacharitamanas::355.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::355.essence: Deceit separates what love has blended.
ramacharitamanas::355.simple_meaning: Love looks pure when trust is present, but deceit quickly separates hearts and destroys the sweetness.
ramacharitamanas::355.simple_insight: It leaves a quiet warning: trust is fragile, and once deceit enters, closeness changes at once.
ramacharitamanas::355.detailed_meaning: After Sati doubts Shiva and hides her intention, the narrator compares love to water mixed with milk. The mixture looks whole until deceit enters, and then the bond separates and its sweetness is gone.
ramacharitamanas::355.modern_relevance: A friendship feels easy while everyone is honest. One hidden lie, one edited message, one half-truth in a group chat — and the warmth changes instantly.
ramacharitamanas::355.insight: It teaches you to see deceit as the force that breaks intimacy, not a small flaw to ignore.

ramacharitamanas::356.verse_sanskrit: हृदयँ सोचु समुझत निज करनी। चिंता अमित जाइ नहिं बरनी॥ कृपासिंधु सिव परम अगाधा। प्रगट न कहेउ मोर अपराधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::356.verse_hindi: अपनी करनी को याद करके सतीजी के हृदय में इतना सोच है और इतनी अपार चिन्ता है कि जिसका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। (उन्होंने समझ लिया कि) शिवजी कृपा के परम अथाह सागर हैं। इससे प्रकट में उन्होंने मेरा अपराध नहीं कहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::356.english_translation: Remembering her own conduct, Sati's heart filled with endless remorse and unspoken anxiety. Shiva is an ocean of compassion, so he did not openly speak of my fault.
ramacharitamanas::356.translation_literal: हृदयँ (in the heart) / सोचु (thought, remorse) / समुझत (remembering, understanding) / निज करनी (one's own deed) / चिंता (anxiety) / अमित (immeasurable) / जाइ (goes) / नहिं (not) / बरनी (described) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / सिव (Shiva) / परम (supreme) / अगाधा (deep, unfathomable) / प्रगट (openly) / न कहेउ (did not say) / मोर (my) / अपराधा (fault, offense)
ramacharitamanas::356.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::356.essence: Compassion can hide a fault, but it cannot hide it from the heart.
ramacharitamanas::356.simple_meaning: Sati feels deep remorse over what she did. She also realizes that Shiva is so compassionate that he does not expose her fault openly.
ramacharitamanas::356.simple_insight: Guilt becomes heavier when you see how gentle the other person has been.
ramacharitamanas::356.detailed_meaning: After testing Shiva and returning home, Sati is trapped in her own remorse. She sees Shiva's vast compassion and understands why he has not publicly named her mistake. The scene turns inward: her hidden guilt is now impossible to ignore.
ramacharitamanas::356.modern_relevance: You replay a conversation at midnight and realize the other person already chose kindness. That realization stings more than any argument could.
ramacharitamanas::356.insight: It shifts attention from blame to self-recognition, showing how compassion can make guilt feel sharper.

ramacharitamanas::357.verse_sanskrit: संकर रुख अवलोकि भवानी। प्रभु मोहि तजेउ हृदयँ अकुलानी॥ निज अघ समुझि न कछु कहि जाई। तपइ अवाँ इव उर अधिकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::357.verse_hindi: शिवजी का रुख देखकर सतीजी ने जान लिया कि स्वामी ने मेरा त्याग कर दिया और वे हृदय में व्याकुल हो उठीं। अपना पाप समझकर कुछ कहते नहीं बनता, परन्तु हृदय (भीतर ही भीतर) कुम्हार के आँवे के समान अत्यन्त जलने लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::357.english_translation: Seeing Shiva's mood, Bhavani understood: "My lord has abandoned me." Her heart grew restless. Realizing her own fault, she could say nothing, yet inside she burned like a kiln.
ramacharitamanas::357.translation_literal: संकर (Shiva) / रुख (mood, bearing) / अवलोकि (seeing) / भवानी (Bhavani) / प्रभु (lord) / मोहि (me) / तजेउ (abandoned) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / अकुलानी (restless) / निज (own) / अघ (fault) / समुझि (understanding) / न (not) / कछु (anything) / कहि (say) / जाई (can be said) / तपइ (burns) / अवाँ (kiln) / इव (like) / उर (heart) / अधिकाई (greatly)
ramacharitamanas::357.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::357.essence: A guilty mind turns silence into fire.
ramacharitamanas::357.simple_meaning: Sati sees Shiva's change in mood and feels abandoned. She knows her own fault, cannot speak, and burns with inner anguish.
ramacharitamanas::357.simple_insight: Seeing clearly can hurt before it heals.
ramacharitamanas::357.detailed_meaning: Sati has just tested Ram by taking a form to witness him, and now she reads Shiva's silence as rejection. The scene turns inward: shame, regret, and fear churn together, showing a mind that can no longer hide from itself.
ramacharitamanas::357.modern_relevance: You notice the unread message, the shorter reply, the sudden distance in someone's voice. Before anyone says a word, your mind has already built the whole wound.
ramacharitamanas::357.insight: It shows how perception can become self-torment when the mind turns its own fault into a burning story.

ramacharitamanas::358.verse_sanskrit: सतिहि ससोच जानि बृषकेतू। कहीं कथा सुंदर सुख हेतू॥ बरनत पंथ बिबिध इतिहासा। बिस्वनाथ पहुँचे कैलासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::358.verse_hindi: वृषकेतु शिवजी ने सती को चिन्तायुक्त जानकर उन्हें सुख देने के लिए सुंदर कथाएँ कहीं। इस प्रकार मार्ग में विविध प्रकार के इतिहासों को कहते हुए विश्वनाथ कैलास जा पहुँचे ॥
ramacharitamanas::358.english_translation: Seeing Sati troubled, Lord Shiva told beautiful stories to give her comfort. Speaking of many histories along the way, the Lord of the universe reached Kailash.
ramacharitamanas::358.translation_literal: सतिहि (Sati) / ससोच (troubled) / जानि (knowing) / बृषकेतू (Shiva, bull-bannered) / कहीं (told) / कथा (stories) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुख हेतू (for comfort)॥ / बरनत (describing) / पंथ (the path) / बिबिध (various) / इतिहासा (histories) / बिस्वनाथ (Lord of the universe) / पहुँचे (reached) / कैलासा (Kailash)॥
ramacharitamanas::358.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::358.essence: Gentle words can carry someone through a hard moment.
ramacharitamanas::358.simple_meaning: Shiva noticed Sati’s disturbed mind and spoke pleasant stories to soothe her as they traveled to Kailash.
ramacharitamanas::358.simple_insight: Kindness can begin with noticing someone’s unease and choosing words that calm, not sharpen it.
ramacharitamanas::358.detailed_meaning: After Sati’s distress rises from Shiva’s silent inner turn, Shiva does not argue. He softens the moment by telling her beautiful stories on the road to Kailash, and the journey continues until they reach home.
ramacharitamanas::358.modern_relevance: A friend is spiraling after a tense conversation, and you do not answer with more logic. You shift the tone, tell a gentler story, and help them breathe again.
ramacharitamanas::358.insight: It teaches you to meet emotional pain with soothing speech instead of confrontation.

ramacharitamanas::359.verse_sanskrit: तहँ पुनि संभु समुझि पन आपन। बैठे बट तर करि कमलासन॥ संकर सहज सरूपु सम्हारा। लागि समाधि अखंड अपारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::359.verse_hindi: वहाँ फिर शिवजी अपनी प्रतिज्ञा को याद करके बड़ के पेड़ के नीचे पद्मासन लगाकर बैठ गए। शिवजी ने अपना स्वाभाविक रूप संभाला। उनकी अखण्ड और अपार समाधि लग गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::359.english_translation: Then Shiva remembered his vow and sat beneath the banyan tree in lotus posture. Shiva gathered his natural form, and an unbroken, boundless absorption arose.
ramacharitamanas::359.translation_literal: तहँ (there) / पुनि (again) / संभु (Shiva) / समुझि (remembering) / पन (vow) / आपन (own) / बैठे (sat) / बट तर (beneath the banyan tree) / करि (doing) / कमलासन (lotus posture)॥ / संकर (Shiva) / सहज (natural) / सरूपु (form) / सम्हारा (gathered/held) / लागि (came upon) / समाधि (complete absorption) / अखंड (unbroken) / अपारा (boundless)॥
ramacharitamanas::359.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::359.essence: Remembered restraint opens into boundless stillness.
ramacharitamanas::359.simple_meaning: Shiva sits down, remembers his vow, settles into lotus posture, returns to his natural state, and enters deep, unbroken absorption.
ramacharitamanas::359.simple_insight: Stillness is not escape; it is the mind returning to its rightful shape.
ramacharitamanas::359.detailed_meaning: After seeing Sati’s distress, Shiva reaches the banyan tree on Mount Kailash. He remembers his vow, sits in lotus posture, and turns inward. The scene shifts from outer movement to a vast, steady absorption.
ramacharitamanas::359.modern_relevance: You step away from the argument, sit down, and stop feeding the spiral. The body becomes still first; then the mind remembers how to be quiet.
ramacharitamanas::359.insight: It shifts attention from reaction to inward steadiness, showing that deep calm begins with a deliberate pause.

ramacharitamanas::360.verse_sanskrit: सती बसहिं कैलास तब अधिक सोचु मन माहिं। मरमु न कोऊ जान कछु जुग सम दिवस सिराहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::360.verse_hindi: तब सतीजी कैलास पर रहने लगीं। उनके मन में बड़ा दुःख था। इस रहस्य को कोई कुछ भी नहीं जानता था। उनका एक-एक दिन युग के समान बीत रहा था ॥
ramacharitamanas::360.english_translation: Then Sati remained on Kailasa, and great sorrow filled her mind. No one understood this hidden cause, and each day passed like an age.
ramacharitamanas::360.translation_literal: सती (Sati) / बसहिं (resided) / कैलास (Kailasa) / तब (then) / अधिक (great) / सोचु (sorrow) / मन (mind) / माहिं (within) / मरमु (secret cause) / न (not) / कोऊ (anyone) / जान (knows) / कछु (anything) / जुग (ages) / सम (like) / दिवस (days) / सिराहिं (passed)
ramacharitamanas::360.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::360.essence: Private sorrow can turn ordinary time into an age.
ramacharitamanas::360.simple_meaning: Sati stays on Kailasa, but her mind is filled with deep sorrow. No one knows the reason, and time feels unbearably slow to her.
ramacharitamanas::360.simple_insight: Hidden pain can make even a single day feel endless.
ramacharitamanas::360.detailed_meaning: After Shiva has spoken gently to Sati, she remains on Kailasa, but her heart is already troubled. The reason is still hidden from everyone around her. This verse shows the quiet beginning of a long inner crisis.
ramacharitamanas::360.modern_relevance: You sit through a family dinner smiling, while one sentence keeps replaying in your head. Everyone sees you there. No one sees the storm you are carrying.
ramacharitamanas::360.insight: It shifts attention from outward normalcy to the private burden underneath it.

ramacharitamanas::361.verse_sanskrit: नित नव सोचु सती उर भारा। कब जैहउँ दुख सागर पारा॥ मैं जो कीन्ह रघुपति अपमाना। पुनि पतिबचनु मृषा करि जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::361.verse_hindi: सतीजी के हृदय में नित्य नया और भारी सोच हो रहा था कि मैं इस दुःख समुद्र के पार कब जाऊँगी। मैंने जो श्री रघुनाथजी का अपमान किया और फिर पति के वचनों को झूठ जाना- ॥
ramacharitamanas::361.english_translation: A fresh grief kept rising in Sati’s heart: when will I cross this ocean of sorrow? I insulted Raghupati, and then I treated my husband’s words as false.
ramacharitamanas::361.translation_literal: नित (constantly) / नव (new) / सोचु (grief, thought) / सती (Sati) / उर (heart) / भारा (weighed heavily) / कब (when) / जैहउँ (shall I go) / दुख (sorrow) / सागर (ocean) / पारा (across)॥ मैं (I) / जो (that which) / कीन्ह (did) / रघुपति (Raghupati, Ram) / अपमाना (insult) / पुनि (again) / पतिबचनु (husband’s word) / मृषा (false) / करि (making) / जाना (considered)॥
ramacharitamanas::361.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::361.essence: Regret grows when the heart remembers its own betrayal.
ramacharitamanas::361.simple_meaning: Sati feels a new wave of grief and shame. She remembers insulting Ram and doubting Shiva’s words, and she longs to be free of that sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::361.simple_insight: Shame becomes heavier when the mind keeps replaying what it already knows was wrong.
ramacharitamanas::361.detailed_meaning: After leaving Shiva’s meditation, Sati sits with a heart full of regret. She keeps reliving the moment she insulted Ram and dismissed Shiva’s warning. This verse shows the inner weight that will drive her next response.
ramacharitamanas::361.modern_relevance: You lie awake after saying something cruel, and the memory returns sharper each time. The mind does not let you escape what the heart knows it must answer.
ramacharitamanas::361.insight: It shows how regret deepens when the mind keeps revisiting a violated value.

ramacharitamanas::362.verse_sanskrit: सो फलु मोहि बिधाताँ दीन्हा। जो कछु उचित रहा सोइ कीन्हा॥ अब बिधि अस बूझिअ नहिं तोही। संकर बिमुख जिआवसि मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::362.verse_hindi: उसका फल विधाता ने मुझको दिया, जो उचित था वही किया, परन्तु हे विधाता! अब तुझे यह उचित नहीं है, जो शंकर से विमुख होने पर भी मुझे जिला रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::362.english_translation: That fate gave me the result. I did what was proper. But now, O fate, this is not proper: you keep me alive even after I turned away from Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::362.translation_literal: सो (that) / फलु (result) / मोहि (to me) / बिधाताँ (by fate) / दीन्हा (gave) / जो (which) / कछु (some) / उचित (proper) / रहा (was) / सोइ (that itself) / कीन्हा (did) / अब (now) / बिधि (fate) / अस (thus) / बूझिअ (understand) / नहिं (not) / तोही (you) / संकर (Shiva) / बिमुख (turned away from) / जिआवसि (you keep alive) / मोही (me)
ramacharitamanas::362.speaker: Sati
ramacharitamanas::362.essence: Regret deepens when the mind cannot escape its own verdict.
ramacharitamanas::362.simple_meaning: Sati feels the consequence of her own choice. She says she received the result of what she did, but now she is troubled that fate is still keeping her alive after she turned away from Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::362.simple_insight: Regret becomes sharper when you see your own part in the pain.
ramacharitamanas::362.detailed_meaning: Sati has left Shiva and is tormented on Kailash. Alone with her thoughts, she judges her own act and then turns the blame outward, asking why she is still being sustained after betraying what was right. The verse shows a mind caught in self-reproach.
ramacharitamanas::362.modern_relevance: You replay the message you should never have sent, then stare at the screen wondering why the day still continues. The discomfort is not just pain — it is your own conscience speaking back.
ramacharitamanas::362.insight: It exposes the mind’s split between owning consequences and resisting them, making regret impossible to hide.

ramacharitamanas::363.verse_sanskrit: कहि न जाइ कछु हृदय गलानी। मन महुँ रामहि सुमिर सयानी॥ जौं प्रभु दीनदयालु कहावा। आरति हरन बेद जसु गावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::363.verse_hindi: सतीजी के हृदय की ग्लानि कुछ कही नहीं जाती। बुद्धिमती सतीजी ने मन में श्री रामचन्द्रजी का स्मरण किया और कहा- हे प्रभो! यदि आप दीनदयालु कहलाते हैं और वेदों ने आपका यह यश गाया है कि आप दुःख को हरने वाले हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::363.english_translation: The pain in Sati's heart cannot be spoken. Wise Sati remembered Ram in her mind: “If you are called the compassionate lord of the poor, and the Vedas sing your fame as the remover of sorrow...”
ramacharitamanas::363.translation_literal: कहि न जाइ (cannot be said) / कछु (some) / हृदय (heart) / गलानी (pain, remorse) / मन महुँ (in the mind) / रामहि (Ram) / सुमिर (remembering) / सयानी (wise one) / जौं (if) / प्रभु (lord) / दीनदयालु (compassionate to the poor) / कहावा (is called) / आरति (sorrow, distress) / हरन (remover) / बेद (Vedas) / जसु (fame, praise) / गावा (sang)
ramacharitamanas::363.speaker: Sati
ramacharitamanas::363.essence: Remorse becomes prayer when the mind remembers mercy.
ramacharitamanas::363.simple_meaning: Sati feels deep remorse and turns her mind to Ram, recalling his reputation as the compassionate one who removes suffering.
ramacharitamanas::363.simple_insight: When regret becomes unbearable, remembrance can become a refuge.
ramacharitamanas::363.detailed_meaning: Sati has just felt the weight of her mistake after insulting Shiva. Alone in her remorse, she turns inward and remembers Ram's mercy. This verse is her appeal to Ram's known compassion before she makes her next plea.
ramacharitamanas::363.modern_relevance: You replay a painful conversation at 2 a.m., unable to sleep. In that raw moment, the mind reaches for the one presence it trusts to be merciful.
ramacharitamanas::363.insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to seeking compassionate refuge.

ramacharitamanas::364.verse_sanskrit: तौ मैं बिनय करउँ कर जोरी। छूटउ बेगि देह यह मोरी॥ जौं मोरें सिव चरन सनेहू। मन क्रम बचन सत्य ब्रतु एहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::364.verse_hindi: तो मैं हाथ जोड़कर विनती करती हूँ कि मेरी यह देह जल्दी छूट जाए। यदि मेरा शिवजी के चरणों में प्रेम है और मेरा यह (प्रेम का) व्रत मन, वचन और कर्म (आचरण) से सत्य है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::364.english_translation: Then I fold my hands and pray: let this body be released quickly. If I truly love Shiva's feet, and if my vow is true in mind, speech, and action,
ramacharitamanas::364.translation_literal: तौ (then) / मैं (I) / बिनय (humble request) / करउँ (do) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined) / छूटउ (may be released) / बेगि (quickly) / देह (body) / यह (this) / मोरी (mine) / जौं (if) / मोरें (in my) / सिव (Shiva) / चरन (feet) / सनेहू (love) / मन (mind) / क्रम (deed) / बचन (speech) / सत्य (true) / ब्रतु (vow) / एहू (this)
ramacharitamanas::364.speaker: Sati
ramacharitamanas::364.essence: True love asks for a life that matches its vow.
ramacharitamanas::364.simple_meaning: Sati prays for her body to end quickly, saying that if her love for Shiva is true, her vow should be proven true in mind, speech, and action.
ramacharitamanas::364.simple_insight: Love becomes real when it is lived completely, not just felt privately.
ramacharitamanas::364.detailed_meaning: Sati, shaken by the insult of hearing Ram spoken of lightly, stands before the divine and asks for release from this body. She measures her devotion by one standard: whether her love for Shiva is true in thought, speech, and conduct.
ramacharitamanas::364.modern_relevance: You say you stand by someone, but the real test comes when loyalty costs you comfort, image, or certainty. Sati wants her whole life to match her vow.
ramacharitamanas::364.insight: It shifts devotion from sentiment to embodied commitment.

ramacharitamanas::365.verse_sanskrit: तौ सबदरसी सुनिअ प्रभु करउ सो बेगि उपाइ। होइ मरनु जेहिं बिनहिं श्रम दुसह बिपत्ति बिहाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::365.verse_hindi: तो हे सर्वदर्शी प्रभो! सुनिए और शीघ्र वह उपाय कीजिए, जिससे मेरा मरण हो और बिना ही परिश्रम यह (पति-परित्याग रूपी) असह्य विपत्ति दूर हो जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::365.english_translation: O all-seeing Lord, hear me and quickly make a way by which I may die, and this unbearable hardship of leaving my husband may end without effort.
ramacharitamanas::365.translation_literal: तौ (then) / सबदरसी (all-seeing) / सुनिअ (please hear) / प्रभु (Lord) / करउ (do) / सो (that) / बेगि (quickly) / उपाइ (means, उपाय) / होइ (may happen) / मरनु (death) / जेहिं (by which) / बिनहिं (without) / श्रम (effort, labor) / दुसह (unbearable) / बिपत्ति (hardship, calamity) / बिहाइ (passing away, leaving behind)
ramacharitamanas::365.speaker: Sati
ramacharitamanas::365.essence: When suffering becomes unbearable, the heart asks only for release.
ramacharitamanas::365.simple_meaning: Sati begs for an easy end to the unbearable pain of being separated from Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::365.simple_insight: Some suffering feels so complete that only release seems like mercy.
ramacharitamanas::365.detailed_meaning: Sati, overwhelmed by shame and pain after doubting Ram, turns to Shiva and asks for a swift end. She wants the unbearable crisis of this marriage-state to pass without further struggle.
ramacharitamanas::365.modern_relevance: You reach the point where every phone call, every room, every memory hurts. You stop asking for answers and just want the weight to lift.
ramacharitamanas::365.insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to surrender when pain has become too heavy to carry.

ramacharitamanas::366.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि दुखित प्रजेसकुमारी। अकथनीय दारुन दुखु भारी॥ बीतें संबत सहस सतासी। तजी समाधि संभु अबिनासी ॥
ramacharitamanas::366.verse_hindi: दक्षसुता सतीजी इस प्रकार बहुत दुःखित थीं, उनको इतना दारुण दुःख था कि जिसका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। सत्तासी हजार वर्ष बीत जाने पर अविनाशी शिवजी ने समाधि खोली ॥
ramacharitamanas::366.english_translation: In this way, the daughter of the king of the mountains was filled with sorrow, a grief too terrible to describe. After eighty-seven thousand years had passed, the imperishable Shiva came out of meditation.
ramacharitamanas::366.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / दुखित (grieved) / प्रजेसकुमारी (daughter of the lord of the people) / अकथनीय (unspeakable) / दारुन (terrible) / दुखु (sorrow) / भारी (heavy) ॥ / बीतें (having passed) / संबत (years) / सहस (thousand) / सतासी (eighty-seven) / तजी (left) / समाधि (meditation) / संभु (Shiva) / अबिनासी (imperishable) ॥
ramacharitamanas::366.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::366.essence: Great grief can pass through vast silence before the next awakening.
ramacharitamanas::366.simple_meaning: Sati suffers unbearable grief while Shiva remains in deep meditation for a very long time. The verse simply marks the passage of time before the next turning point.
ramacharitamanas::366.simple_insight: Some pain lasts long enough to feel endless, while life keeps moving toward the next awakening.
ramacharitamanas::366.detailed_meaning: Sati has just pleaded to leave her body because of the insult to Shiva. This verse lingers on her unbearable grief and then jumps ahead through an immense span of time until Shiva finally emerges from meditation, setting up the next exchange.
ramacharitamanas::366.modern_relevance: You sit with a heartbreak that feels frozen in time, while the rest of the world keeps moving. Then, without warning, something in you finally stirs again.
ramacharitamanas::366.insight: It slows the reader down before the next revelation, showing that transformation often follows a long stillness.

ramacharitamanas::367.verse_sanskrit: राम नाम सिव सुमिरन लागे। जानेउ सतीं जगतपति जागे॥ जाइ संभु पद बंदनु कीन्हा। सनमुख संकर आसनु दीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::367.verse_hindi: शिवजी रामनाम का स्मरण करने लगे, तब सतीजी ने जाना कि अब जगत के स्वामी (शिवजी) जागे। उन्होंने जाकर शिवजी के चरणों में प्रणाम किया। शिवजी ने उनको बैठने के लिए सामने आसन दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::367.english_translation: Shiva began remembering Ram's name, and Sati understood that the Lord of the world had awakened. She went and bowed at Shiva's feet. Shiva gave her a seat facing him.
ramacharitamanas::367.translation_literal: राम नाम (Ram's name) / सिव (Shiva) / सुमिरन (remembering) / लागे (began) / जानेउ (understood) / सतीं (Sati) / जगतपति (Lord of the world) / जागे (awakened) / जाइ (going) / संभु (Shiva) / पद (feet) / बंदनु (bowing) / कीन्हा (did) / सनमुख (facing) / संकर (Shiva) / आसनु (seat) / दीन्हा (gave)
ramacharitamanas::367.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::367.essence: Reverence restores closeness before words can.
ramacharitamanas::367.simple_meaning: Shiva turns to Ram's name, and Sati recognizes his awakened state. She bows to him, and he seats her with honor.
ramacharitamanas::367.simple_insight: Devotion changes the whole atmosphere of a relationship. Even a small gesture of reverence can restore dignity and closeness.
ramacharitamanas::367.detailed_meaning: Sati has just pleaded for relief from the pain of seeing Shiva withdraw into meditation. Now Shiva begins repeating Ram's name, and Sati realizes he has awakened to the divine presence. She approaches with respect, and Shiva receives her properly.
ramacharitamanas::367.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a tense silence, and one person softens first. A respectful gesture breaks the chill before any argument can continue.
ramacharitamanas::367.insight: It teaches you to let reverence lead the next move. Respect can reopen a relationship faster than explanation.

ramacharitamanas::368.verse_sanskrit: लगे कहन हरि कथा रसाला। दच्छ प्रजेस भए तेहि काला॥ देखा बिधि बिचारि सब लायक। दच्छहि कीन्ह प्रजापति नायक ॥
ramacharitamanas::368.verse_hindi: शिवजी भगवान हरि की रसमयी कथाएँ कहने लगे। उसी समय दक्ष प्रजापति हुए। ब्रह्माजी ने सब प्रकार से योग्य देख-समझकर दक्ष को प्रजापतियों का नायक बना दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::368.english_translation: Shiva began speaking the sweet stories of Hari. At that time, Daksha the lord of creatures arose. Seeing and considering all things, Brahma made Daksha the leader of the prajapatis.
ramacharitamanas::368.translation_literal: लगे (began) / कहन (to speak) / हरि (Hari) / कथा (stories) / रसाला (full of nectar) / दच्छ (Daksha) / प्रजेस (lord of creatures) / भए (became) / तेहि काला (at that time) / देखा (saw) / बिधि (Brahma) / बिचारि (having considered) / सब (all) / लायक (fit) / दच्छहि (Daksha) / कीन्ह (made) / प्रजापति (lord of creatures) / नायक (leader)
ramacharitamanas::368.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::368.essence: Authority can arrive while devotion quietly continues.
ramacharitamanas::368.simple_meaning: Shiva was speaking about Hari when Daksha rose to power. Brahma, after considering who was fit, appointed Daksha as leader of the prajapatis.
ramacharitamanas::368.simple_insight: Power can rise in one place even as devotion continues in another.
ramacharitamanas::368.detailed_meaning: In the opening frame of the story, Shiva is still speaking the sweet stories of Hari to Parvati. At that same moment, Brahma sees Daksha as qualified and appoints him leader of the prajapatis. It is a scene-setting verse, not the main turn of the argument.
ramacharitamanas::368.modern_relevance: A meeting continues in one room while, elsewhere, someone gets promoted and starts believing the title defines them. The change in status matters less than what it does to the heart.
ramacharitamanas::368.insight: It sets up the contrast between outer authority and the inner state that follows it.

ramacharitamanas::369.verse_sanskrit: बड़ अधिकार दच्छ जब पावा। अति अभिनामु हृदयँ तब आवा॥ नहिं कोउ अस जनमा जग माहीं। प्रभुता पाइ जाहि मद नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::369.verse_hindi: जब दक्ष ने इतना बड़ा अधिकार पाया, तब उनके हृदय में अत्यन्त अभिमान आ गया। जगत में ऐसा कोई नहीं पैदा हुआ, जिसको प्रभुता पाकर मद न हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::369.english_translation: When Daksha gained such great authority, pride arose in his heart. No one is born in this world who does not become intoxicated after gaining power.
ramacharitamanas::369.translation_literal: बड़ (great) / अधिकार (authority, power) / दच्छ (Daksha) / जब (when) / पावा (gained) / अति (very) / अभिनामु (pride) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / तब (then) / आवा (came) / नहिं (not) / कोउ (anyone) / अस (such) / जनमा (born) / जग माहीं (in the world) / प्रभुता (lordship, power) / पाइ (having obtained) / जाहि (who) / मद (intoxication, arrogance) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::369.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::369.essence: Power easily turns into pride unless the heart stays watchful.
ramacharitamanas::369.simple_meaning: Daksha gained great authority, and that success made him arrogant. The verse warns that power often feeds pride in anyone who receives it.
ramacharitamanas::369.simple_insight: Success can quietly distort character unless it is watched closely.
ramacharitamanas::369.detailed_meaning: Shiva has begun telling Parvati how Daksha came to prominence. As soon as Daksha receives high authority, his heart fills with pride. The verse pauses the story to show the inner danger that power brings before the sacrifice begins.
ramacharitamanas::369.modern_relevance: You get promoted, your name is suddenly on every email, and people start treating you differently. Before long, the role can feel like proof that you matter more than others.
ramacharitamanas::369.insight: It shifts attention from external status to the ego reaction status can trigger.

ramacharitamanas::370.verse_sanskrit: दच्छ लिए मुनि बोलि सब करन लगे बड़ जाग। नेवते सादर सकल सुर जे पावत मख भाग ॥
ramacharitamanas::370.verse_hindi: दक्ष ने सब मुनियों को बुला लिया और वे बड़ा यज्ञ करने लगे। जो देवता यज्ञ का भाग पाते हैं, दक्ष ने उन सबको आदर सहित निमन्त्रित किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::370.english_translation: Daksha gathered all the sages and began a great sacrifice. He invited with respect all the radiant beings who receive a share in the sacrifice.
ramacharitamanas::370.translation_literal: दच्छ (Daksha) / लिए (took, gathered) / मुनि (sages) / बोलि (calling) / सब (all) / करन लगे (began to do) / बड़ (great) / जाग (sacrifice) / नेवते (invited) / सादर (respectfully) / सकल (all) / सुर (radiant beings) / जे (who) / पावत (receive) / मख (sacrifice) / भाग (share)
ramacharitamanas::370.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::370.essence: Pride often enters first as a perfectly arranged invitation.
ramacharitamanas::370.simple_meaning: Daksha gathers the sages and begins a large sacrifice, inviting all the radiant beings who receive offerings there.
ramacharitamanas::370.simple_insight: Some moments are just setup: the real turning point comes after the gathering begins.
ramacharitamanas::370.detailed_meaning: Daksha has risen in pride and now moves to display his power through a grand sacrifice. He summons the sages and respectfully invites the radiant beings who normally receive a share, setting the stage for the conflict that follows.
ramacharitamanas::370.modern_relevance: A meeting invite goes out to everyone except the one person who matters most. The exclusion is polite on the surface, but it already contains the wound.
ramacharitamanas::370.insight: It trains attention on the social gesture before the rupture, where pride first becomes visible.

ramacharitamanas::371.verse_sanskrit: किंनर नाग सिद्ध गंधर्बा। बधुन्ह समेत चले सुर सर्बा॥ बिष्नु बिरंचि महेसु बिहाई। चले सकल सुर जान बनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::371.verse_hindi: (दक्ष का निमन्त्रण पाकर) किन्नर, नाग, सिद्ध, गन्धर्व और सब देवता अपनी-अपनी स्त्रियों सहित चले। विष्णु, ब्रह्मा और महादेवजी को छोड़कर सभी देवता अपना-अपना विमान सजाकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::371.english_translation: (On receiving Daksha's invitation) the Kinnaras, Nagas, Siddhas, Gandharvas, and all the radiant beings went along with their wives. Leaving Vishnu, Brahma, and Mahesh aside, all the radiant beings set out in their own celestial vehicles.
ramacharitamanas::371.translation_literal: किंनर (Kinnaras) / नाग (serpent beings) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / गंधर्बा (Gandharvas) / बधुन्ह (with wives) / समेत (together) / चले (went) / सुर (radiant beings) / सर्बा (all) ॥ / बिष्नु (Vishnu) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / महेसु (Mahesh) / बिहाई (leaving aside) / चले (went) / सकल (all) / सुर (radiant beings) / जान (celestial vehicles) / बनाई (making/arranging) ॥
ramacharitamanas::371.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::371.essence: Not every grand gathering deserves your presence.
ramacharitamanas::371.simple_meaning: All kinds of celestial beings went to Daksha's ceremony with their wives. Vishnu, Brahma, and Shiva did not go.
ramacharitamanas::371.simple_insight: Some gatherings are not worth joining, even if everyone else is going.
ramacharitamanas::371.detailed_meaning: Daksha's great sacrifice is underway, and the invitation has pulled in every kind of radiant being. Yet Vishnu, Brahma, and Mahesh stay away. The verse simply shows the scale of the event and the striking absence that prepares the coming tension.
ramacharitamanas::371.modern_relevance: Everyone is RSVPing yes to the big event, and your phone keeps lighting up. But three names stay out of the room. Sometimes wisdom is knowing which crowd does not deserve your presence.
ramacharitamanas::371.insight: It shifts attention from social inclusion to discernment about where not to go.

ramacharitamanas::372.verse_sanskrit: सतीं बिलोके ब्योम बिमाना। जात चले सुंदर बिधि नाना॥ सुर सुंदरी करहिं कल गाना। सुनत श्रवन छूटहिं मुनि ध्याना ॥
ramacharitamanas::372.verse_hindi: सतीजी ने देखा, अनेकों प्रकार के सुंदर विमान आकाश में चले जा रहे हैं, देव-सुन्दरियाँ मधुर गान कर रही हैं, जिन्हें सुनकर मुनियों का ध्यान छूट जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::372.english_translation: Sati saw many beautiful celestial vehicles moving through the sky. The divine maidens sang sweetly, and hearing them, the sages lost their meditation.
ramacharitamanas::372.translation_literal: सतीं (Sati) / बिलोके (saw) / ब्योम (sky) / बिमाना (aircraft, celestial vehicles) / जात चले (moving along) / सुंदर (beautiful) / बिधि नाना (of many kinds) ॥ / सुर (divine beings) / सुंदरी (maidens) / करहिं (do) / कल गाना (sweet singing) / सुनत (hearing) / श्रवन (ears) / छूटहिं (are broken) / मुनि (sages) / ध्याना (meditation) ॥
ramacharitamanas::372.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::372.essence: Beauty can scatter even a disciplined mind.
ramacharitamanas::372.simple_meaning: Sati notices the gods passing overhead in beautiful flying vehicles, while the celestial women sing so sweetly that even sages lose concentration.
ramacharitamanas::372.simple_insight: Even sacred attention can be pulled outward by beauty and movement.
ramacharitamanas::372.detailed_meaning: At Daksha's sacrifice, Sati looks up and sees the gods traveling to the ceremony in shining aerial vehicles. Their music is so alluring that even deep meditators are distracted. The scene builds the tension before Sati asks Shiva what is happening.
ramacharitamanas::372.modern_relevance: You are trying to stay focused, but a flood of notifications, music, and movement keeps pulling your attention away. The mind can be broken by beauty before it is broken by pain.
ramacharitamanas::372.insight: It shows how quickly the senses can interrupt inward absorption, even in the presence of spiritual discipline.

ramacharitamanas::373.verse_sanskrit: पूछेउ तब सिवँ कहेउ बखानी। पिता जग्य सुनि कछु हरषानी॥ जौं महेसु मोहि आयसु देहीं। कछु िदन जाइ रहौं मिस एहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::373.verse_hindi: सतीजी ने (विमानों में देवताओं के जाने का कारण) पूछा, तब शिवजी ने सब बातें बतलाईं। पिता के यज्ञ की बात सुनकर सती कुछ प्रसन्न हुईं और सोचने लगीं कि यदि महादेवजी मुझे आज्ञा दें, तो इसी बहाने कुछ दिन पिता के घर जाकर रहूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::373.english_translation: Then Sati asked Shiva, and he explained everything. Hearing that her father was performing a sacrifice, Sati felt some joy and thought, "If Mahesh gives me permission, I will go stay at my father's house for a few days under that pretext."
ramacharitamanas::373.translation_literal: पूछेउ (asked) / तब (then) / सिवँ (Shiva) / कहेउ (told) / बखानी (explained) / पिता (father's) / जग्य (sacrifice) / सुनि (hearing) / कछु (some) / हरषानी (felt joy) / जौं (if) / महेसु (Mahesh/Shiva) / मोहि (me) / आयसु (permission) / देहीं (gives) / कछु (some) / िदन (days) / जाइ (going) / रहौं (I stay) / मिस (as a pretext) / एहीं (this)
ramacharitamanas::373.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::373.essence: A simple family invitation can awaken buried longing and pain.
ramacharitamanas::373.simple_meaning: Sati asks Shiva about the gathering and becomes glad when she hears her father is holding a sacrifice. She hopes Shiva will let her visit her father's home for a few days.
ramacharitamanas::373.simple_insight: A small opening can reveal a much deeper conflict already waiting underneath.
ramacharitamanas::373.detailed_meaning: Sati sees the gods traveling and asks Shiva why. Shiva explains that her father is holding a sacrifice. Her first reaction is hope: she wants permission to go home for a short visit. The verse quietly sets up the emotional tension that follows.
ramacharitamanas::373.modern_relevance: You hear one family message and suddenly old feelings wake up. A simple invitation can carry hope, longing, and the fear of what will happen next.
ramacharitamanas::373.insight: It sets up the hidden tension between outward politeness and inner hurt.

ramacharitamanas::374.verse_sanskrit: पति परित्याग हृदयँ दुखु भारी। कहइ न निज अपराध बिचारी॥ बोली सती मनोहर बानी। भय संकोच प्रेम रस सानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::374.verse_hindi: क्योंकि उनके हृदय में पति द्वारा त्यागी जाने का बड़ा भारी दुःख था, पर अपना अपराध समझकर वे कुछ कहती न थीं। आखिर सतीजी भय, संकोच और प्रेमरस में सनी हुई मनोहर वाणी से बोलीं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::374.english_translation: With a heart heavy with grief at being set aside by her husband, she said nothing, seeing her own fault. Then Sati spoke in a gentle voice, sweetened by fear, modesty, and love.
ramacharitamanas::374.translation_literal: पति (husband) / परित्याग (abandonment) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / दुखु (pain) / भारी (heavy) / कहइ (speaks) / न (not) / निज (own) / अपराध (fault) / बिचारी (having considered) / बोली (spoke) / सती (Sati) / मनोहर (lovely) / बानी (speech) / भय (fear) / संकोच (hesitation) / प्रेम रस (the essence of love) / सानी (mixed)
ramacharitamanas::374.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::374.essence: Love speaks softly even when it is wounded.
ramacharitamanas::374.simple_meaning: Sati feels deep hurt and shame, so she speaks carefully and gently. Her words come from fear, hesitation, and love.
ramacharitamanas::374.simple_insight: Even painful speech can stay tender when the heart is full of love and self-awareness.
ramacharitamanas::374.detailed_meaning: Sati has seen Shiva's attention turn away from the sacrifice and feels the sting of being set aside. She blames herself, not him, and speaks only after holding back her grief. The moment shows her inner conflict before she asks to go to her father’s house.
ramacharitamanas::374.modern_relevance: You reread a message three times before sending it, knowing one careless sentence could wound someone you love. The heart is full, but the voice must stay gentle.
ramacharitamanas::374.insight: It shows how self-doubt, love, and restraint can shape speech before a difficult request.

ramacharitamanas::375.verse_sanskrit: पिता भवन उत्सव परम जौं प्रभु आयसु होइ। तौ मैं जाउँ कृपायतन सादर देखन सोइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::375.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! मेरे पिता के घर बहुत बड़ा उत्सव है। यदि आपकी आज्ञा हो तो हे कृपाधाम! मैं आदर सहित उसे देखने जाऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::375.english_translation: O Lord, there is a great celebration at my father's house. If you permit, O abode of grace, I shall go respectfully to see it.
ramacharitamanas::375.translation_literal: पिता भवन (father's house) / उत्सव (festival, celebration) / परम (great, supreme) / जौं (if) / प्रभु (Lord) / आयसु (permission, command) / होइ (is) / तौ (then) / मैं (I) / जाउँ (may go) / कृपायतन (abode of grace) / सादर (respectfully) / देखन (to see) / सोइ (that)
ramacharitamanas::375.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::375.essence: Respectful desire asks before it moves.
ramacharitamanas::375.simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva for permission to visit her father's grand celebration and see it with respect.
ramacharitamanas::375.simple_insight: Even a simple visit becomes meaningful when it is done with humility and permission.
ramacharitamanas::375.detailed_meaning: Parvati, hearing of her father's yajna, asks Shiva if she may go and see the celebration. Her request is gentle, respectful, and full of the tension between family feeling and marital duty.
ramacharitamanas::375.modern_relevance: You hear your family is gathering for a major event, but your partner is uneasy about it. The question is not just whether you can go — it is whether you can go with respect and care.
ramacharitamanas::375.insight: It teaches you to seek permission and move without entitlement, even when the pull of family is strong.

ramacharitamanas::376.verse_sanskrit: कहेहु नीक मोरेहूँ मन भावा। यह अनुचित नहिं नेवत पठावा॥ दच्छ सकल निज सुता बोलाईं। हमरें बयर तुम्हउ बिसराईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::376.verse_hindi: शिवजी ने कहा- तुमने बात तो अच्छी कही, यह मेरे मन को भी पसंद आई पर उन्होंने न्योता नहीं भेजा, यह अनुचित है। दक्ष ने अपनी सब लड़कियों को बुलाया है, किन्तु हमारे बैर के कारण उन्होंने तुमको भी भुला दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::376.english_translation: You spoke well; I also like it. Yet it is improper that no invitation was sent. Daksha has called all his daughters, but because of our old enmity, you were forgotten too.
ramacharitamanas::376.translation_literal: कहेहु (you said) / नीक (well) / मोरेहूँ (to me also) / मन (mind) / भावा (was pleasing) / यह (this) / अनुचित (improper) / नहिं (not) / नेवत (invitation) / पठावा (sent) / दच्छ (Daksha) / सकल (all) / निज (own) / सुता (daughters) / बोलाईं (called) / हमरें (our) / बयर (enmity) / तुम्हउ (you also) / बिसराईं (forgot)
ramacharitamanas::376.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::376.essence: Old enmity can turn even an invitation into exclusion.
ramacharitamanas::376.simple_meaning: Shiva agrees that Parvati's wish is reasonable, but says the lack of invitation is disrespectful. Daksha invited his daughters, yet left Parvati out because of old hostility.
ramacharitamanas::376.simple_insight: Even a fair desire can be blocked by wounded pride and old resentment.
ramacharitamanas::376.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati after she wants to visit Daksha's sacrifice. He admits her request is good, but points out the insult: Daksha invited everyone except her because of their broken relationship. The tension is building toward a painful family rupture.
ramacharitamanas::376.modern_relevance: You hear about a family gathering everyone was invited to except one person. The exclusion is polite on the surface, but everyone feels the old wound underneath.
ramacharitamanas::376.insight: It shows how unresolved hostility turns even a simple invitation into a social wound.

ramacharitamanas::377.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मसभाँ हम सन दुखु माना। तेहि तें अजहुँ करहिं अपमाना॥ जौं बिनु बोलें जाहु भवानी। रहइ न सीलु सनेहु न कानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::377.verse_hindi: एक बार ब्रह्मा की सभा में हम से अप्रसन्न हो गए थे, उसी से वे अब भी हमारा अपमान करते हैं। हे भवानी! जो तुम बिना बुलाए जाओगी तो न शील-स्नेह ही रहेगा और न मान-मर्यादा ही रहेगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::377.english_translation: In Brahma's assembly, I was once slighted. Because of that, they still insult us. O Bhavani, if you go without being invited, neither decorum nor affection nor honor will remain.
ramacharitamanas::377.translation_literal: ब्रह्मसभाँ (in Brahma's assembly) / हम (we) / सन (with) / दुखु (hurt) / माना (considered) / तेहि तें (because of that) / अजहुँ (still) / करहिं (they do) / अपमाना (insult) / जौं (if) / बिनु बोलें (without being called) / जाहु (you go) / भवानी (Bhavani) / रहइ (remains) / न (not) / सीलु (decorum) / सनेहु (affection) / न (nor) / कानी (honor, respect)
ramacharitamanas::377.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::377.essence: Uninvited presence can turn affection into insult.
ramacharitamanas::377.simple_meaning: Shiva says that being excluded once still matters, so going uninvited would break decorum, affection, and respect.
ramacharitamanas::377.simple_insight: Respect for a host protects relationships. Ignoring that boundary can damage even a loving bond.
ramacharitamanas::377.detailed_meaning: Shiva is explaining to Parvati why he will not go to Daksha's sacrifice uninvited. A past slight in Brahma's assembly still stings, and he sees the same danger here: entering where one is unwelcome would invite more disrespect.
ramacharitamanas::377.modern_relevance: You know that moment when a family gathering is tense and one person says, “Just show up anyway”? Sometimes forcing access only deepens the wound.
ramacharitamanas::377.insight: It teaches you to honor social boundaries instead of treating closeness as entitlement.

ramacharitamanas::378.verse_sanskrit: जदपि मित्र प्रभु पितु गुर गेहा। जाइअ बिनु बोलेहुँ न सँदेहा॥ तदपि बिरोध मान जहँ कोई। तहाँ गएँ कल्यानु न होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::378.verse_hindi: यद्यपि इसमें संदेह नहीं कि मित्र, स्वामी, पिता और गुरु के घर बिना बुलाए भी जाना चाहिए तो भी जहाँ कोई विरोध मानता हो, उसके घर जाने से कल्याण नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::378.english_translation: Even though there is no doubt that one may go without invitation to the home of a friend, lord, father, or teacher, if someone feels hostility there, going there brings no good.
ramacharitamanas::378.translation_literal: जदपि (although) / मित्र (friend) / प्रभु (lord) / पितु (father) / गुर (teacher) / गेहा (home) / जाइअ (one should go) / बिनु बोलेहुँ (without being called) / न (no) / सँदेहा (doubt) / तदपि (still) / बिरोध (hostility) / मान (feeling) / जहँ (where) / कोई (someone) / तहाँ (there) / गएँ (by going) / कल्यानु (good) / न होई (does not happen)
ramacharitamanas::378.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::378.essence: Closeness without welcome turns even rightful presence into harm.
ramacharitamanas::378.simple_meaning: You may visit a friend, parent, teacher, or lord without invitation, but not where your presence is unwelcome. Forced closeness brings no good.
ramacharitamanas::378.simple_insight: Not every right is worth exercising. Wisdom notices where presence will heal and where it will only deepen hurt.
ramacharitamanas::378.detailed_meaning: Shiva is trying to dissuade Parvati from going uninvited to Daksha's sacrifice. He admits that close relations can be approached freely, but warns that a place charged with hostility will not become auspicious through insistence.
ramacharitamanas::378.modern_relevance: You know that message you want to send after the argument, just to prove you still can? Sometimes the mature move is to wait until the room is willing again.
ramacharitamanas::378.insight: It teaches restraint: do not force entry where resentment is active. Respect the emotional reality of the space before you step in.

ramacharitamanas::379.verse_sanskrit: भाँति अनेक संभु समुझावा। भावी बस न ग्यानु उर आवा॥ कह प्रभु जाहु जो बिनहिं बोलाएँ। नहिं भलि बात हमारे भाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::379.verse_hindi: शिवजी ने बहुत प्रकार से समझाया, पर होनहारवश सती के हृदय में बोध नहीं हुआ। फिर शिवजी ने कहा कि यदि बिना बुलाए जाओगी, तो हमारी समझ में अच्छी बात न होगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::379.english_translation: Shiva explained in many ways, but by fate no understanding arose in Sati's heart. Then Shiva said, 'If you go without being invited, it is not a good thing in our view.'
ramacharitamanas::379.translation_literal: भाँति अनेक (in many ways) / संभु (Shiva) / समुझावा (explained) / भावी बस (by fate's power) / न (not) / ग्यानु (understanding) / उर (in the heart) / आवा (came) / कह (said) / प्रभु (the Lord) / जाहु (go) / जो (if) / बिनहिं बोलाएँ (without being invited) / नहिं (not) / भलि (good) / बात (thing) / हमारे (our) / भाएँ (view)
ramacharitamanas::379.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::379.essence: Forcing entry where you are unwelcome brings harm.
ramacharitamanas::379.simple_meaning: Shiva tries to reason with Sati, but she still cannot see clearly. He warns her that going uninvited is not wise.
ramacharitamanas::379.simple_insight: Not every desire deserves action. Sometimes the clearest choice is to stop and listen.
ramacharitamanas::379.detailed_meaning: In the Shiva–Sati frame of Balkand, Shiva has already tried to dissuade Sati from going to Daksha's place. He explains again, but her mind remains fixed. This verse shows his final warning: entering where you are unwelcome will bring harm.
ramacharitamanas::379.modern_relevance: You already know the room is tense, but you still want to walk in and prove a point. The wiser move is to pause before turning hurt into a scene.
ramacharitamanas::379.insight: It shifts the mind from impulse to restraint, especially when pride wants to override warning.

ramacharitamanas::380.verse_sanskrit: कहि देखा हर जतन बहु रहइ न दच्छकुमारि। दिए मुख्य गन संग तब बिदा कीन्ह त्रिपुरारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::380.verse_hindi: शिवजी ने बहुत प्रकार से कहकर देख लिया, किन्तु जब सती किसी प्रकार भी नहीं रुकीं, तब त्रिपुरारि महादेवजी ने अपने मुख्य गणों को साथ देकर उनको बिदा कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::380.english_translation: Shiva tried many ways to stop her, but when Sati would not stay, Tripurari sent her off with his chief attendants.
ramacharitamanas::380.translation_literal: कहि (having said) / देखा (saw) / हर (Shiva) / जतन (means, effort) / बहु (many) / रहइ (remained) / न (not) / दच्छकुमारि (Daksha’s daughter, Sati) / दिए (gave) / मुख्य (chief) / गन (attendants) / संग (with) / तब (then) / बिदा (farewell, send-off) / कीन्ह (made) / त्रिपुरारि (Shiva)
ramacharitamanas::380.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::380.essence: Love cannot force a heart to stay.
ramacharitamanas::380.simple_meaning: Shiva tried to persuade Sati not to go, but she would not listen. So he finally sent her off with his attendants.
ramacharitamanas::380.simple_insight: Even love cannot always stop a chosen path.
ramacharitamanas::380.detailed_meaning: Sati is determined to go to her father Daksha’s house despite Shiva’s warnings. After trying many ways to hold her back, Shiva gives up the argument and sends her with his attendants. The verse sets up the painful separation that follows.
ramacharitamanas::380.modern_relevance: You warn someone you love, but they still walk into the conversation you know will hurt them. At some point, care becomes letting them go.
ramacharitamanas::380.insight: It shows the limit of persuasion and the dignity of releasing control when another person insists on their own course.

ramacharitamanas::381.verse_sanskrit: पिता भवन जब गईं भवानी। दच्छ त्रास काहुँ न सनमानी॥ सादर भलेहिं मिली एक माता। भगिनीं मिलीं बहुत मुसुकाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::381.verse_hindi: भवानी जब पिता (दक्ष) के घर पहुँची, तब दक्ष के डर के मारे किसी ने उनकी आवभगत नहीं की, केवल एक माता भले ही आदर से मिली। बहिनें बहुत मुस्कुराती हुई मिलीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::381.english_translation: When Bhavani reached her father's house, no one honored her out of fear of Daksha. Only one mother welcomed her respectfully, and the sisters greeted her with forced smiles.
ramacharitamanas::381.translation_literal: पिता भवन (father's house) / जब (when) / गईं (went) / भवानी (Bhavani) / दच्छ (Daksha) / त्रास (fear) / काहुँ (anyone) / न (not) / सनमानी (honoured) / सादर (respectfully) / भलेहिं (well) / मिली (met) / एक (one) / माता (mother) / भगिनीं (sisters) / मिलीं (met) / बहुत (much) / मुसुकाता (smiling)
ramacharitamanas::381.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::381.essence: Fear can make even family feel like strangers.
ramacharitamanas::381.simple_meaning: Bhavani returned to her father's house, but fear of Daksha made everyone cold. Only one mother showed respect, while her sisters smiled without warmth.
ramacharitamanas::381.simple_insight: A room can be full of people and still feel utterly lonely.
ramacharitamanas::381.detailed_meaning: Bhavani has come back to Daksha's home after Shiva's warning, but the family atmosphere is poisoned by fear and insult. Instead of welcome, she meets silence, one respectful mother, and sisters whose smiles hide discomfort.
ramacharitamanas::381.modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering and feel the room tighten. People smile, but no one really meets your eyes. The verse captures how fear turns even home into a place of distance.
ramacharitamanas::381.insight: It shows how social fear can erase warmth and make courtesy feel empty.

ramacharitamanas::382.verse_sanskrit: दच्छ न कछु पूछी कुसलाता। सतिहि बिलोकी जरे सब गाता॥ सतीं जाइ देखेउ तब जागा। कतहूँ न दीख संभु कर भागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::382.verse_hindi: दक्ष ने तो उनकी कुछ कुशल तक नहीं पूछी, सतीजी को देखकर उलटे उनके सारे अंग जल उठे। तब सती ने जाकर यज्ञ देखा तो वहाँ कहीं शिवजी का भाग दिखाई नहीं दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::382.english_translation: Daksha did not even ask after her well-being. Seeing Sati, all his body burned with anger. Then Sati went and saw the sacrifice, but nowhere could she see any share of Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::382.translation_literal: दच्छ (Daksha) / न (not) / कछु (any) / पूछी (asked) / कुसलाता (well-being) / सतिहि (Sati) / बिलोकी (seeing) / जरे (burned) / सब (all) / गाता (bodies/limbs)॥ / सतीं (Sati) / जाइ (going) / देखेउ (saw) / तब (then) / जागा (sacrifice) / कतहूँ (anywhere) / न (not) / दीख (was seen) / संभु (Shiva) / कर (of) / भागा (share/portion) ॥
ramacharitamanas::382.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::382.simple_meaning: Daksha ignores Sati completely, and his anger flares at her presence. Sati then looks for Shiva's share in the sacrifice and finds none.
ramacharitamanas::382.simple_insight: Being treated as unwelcome can reveal a wound instantly.
ramacharitamanas::382.detailed_meaning: Sati has returned to her father Daksha's sacrifice, but the welcome is cruel and cold. Daksha does not even ask after her health, and his hostility burns at the sight of her. She then looks for Shiva's place in the ritual and finds that he has been left out.
ramacharitamanas::382.modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering and no one asks how you are. The silence itself tells you where you stand, and one missing seat says everything.
ramacharitamanas::382.insight: It shows how insult and exclusion can become immediately visible, before anyone says a word.
