ramacharitamanas::383.verse_sanskrit: तब चित चढ़ेउ जो संकर कहेऊ। प्रभु अपमानु समुझि उर दहेऊ॥ पाछिल दुखु न हृदयँ अस ब्यापा। जस यह भयउ महा परितापा ॥
ramacharitamanas::383.verse_hindi: तब शिवजी ने जो कहा था, वह उनकी समझ में आया। स्वामी का अपमान समझकर सती का हृदय जल उठा। पिछला (पति परित्याग का) दुःख उनके हृदय में उतना नहीं व्यापा था, जितना महान् दुःख इस समय (पति अपमान के कारण) हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::383.english_translation: Then Sati understood what Shiva had said. Seeing her lord insulted, her heart burned. The earlier grief had not weighed on her heart as much as this great pain did.
ramacharitamanas::383.translation_literal: तब (then) / चित (in the mind) / चढ़ेउ (rose) / जो (what) / संकर (Shiva) / कहेऊ (had said) / प्रभु (lord) / अपमानु (insult) / समुझि (understanding) / उर (heart) / दहेऊ (burned) / पाछिल (previous) / दुखु (sorrow) / न (not) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / अस (so) / ब्यापा (spread) / जस (as) / यह (this) / भयउ (became) / महा (great) / परितापा (pain)
ramacharitamanas::383.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::383.essence: Insult to the one you love can burn deeper than your own sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::383.simple_meaning: Sati finally understood Shiva’s warning, and the insult to her husband hurt her more than her earlier grief had.
ramacharitamanas::383.simple_insight: Some wounds become unbearable when love is publicly dishonoured.
ramacharitamanas::383.detailed_meaning: Sati has reached her father Daksha’s sacrifice and seen Shiva slighted. In that instant, Shiva’s earlier words come alive in her mind, and the pain of her husband’s humiliation overwhelms everything else.
ramacharitamanas::383.modern_relevance: You hear a cruel joke made about someone you love in front of everyone. The embarrassment lands harder than the original problem, because disrespect cuts deeper than pain.
ramacharitamanas::383.insight: It shifts attention from private hurt to the sharper pain of public dishonour.

ramacharitamanas::384.verse_sanskrit: जद्यपि जग दारुन दुख नाना। सब तें कठिन जाति अवमाना॥ समुझि सो सतिहि भयउ अति क्रोधा। बहु बिधि जननीं कीन्ह प्रबोधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::384.verse_hindi: यद्यपि जगत में अनेक प्रकार के दारुण दुःख हैं, तथापि, जाति अपमान सबसे बढ़कर कठिन है। यह समझकर सतीजी को बड़ा क्रोध हो आया। माता ने उन्हें बहुत प्रकार से समझाया-बुझाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::384.english_translation: Although the world holds many terrible sorrows, insult to one’s own kind is the hardest to bear. Realizing this, Sati became intensely angry, and her mother tried in many ways to calm her.
ramacharitamanas::384.translation_literal: जद्यपि (although) / जग (world) / दारुन (terrible) / दुख (sorrows) / नाना (many) / सब तें (among all) / कठिन (hardest) / जाति (one’s own kind / family line) / अवमाना (insult) / समुझि (understanding) / सो (that) / सतिहि (to Sati) / भयउ (became) / अति (very) / क्रोधा (anger) / बहु बिधि (in many ways) / जननीं (mother) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रबोधा (calming / counsel)
ramacharitamanas::384.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::384.essence: Humiliation of one’s own people can burn hotter than any ordinary pain.
ramacharitamanas::384.simple_meaning: Many kinds of suffering exist, but humiliation of one’s own family or group cuts the deepest. Sati felt that sting, and her mother kept trying to calm her.
ramacharitamanas::384.simple_insight: Some wounds are not physical at all; they come from shame, loyalty, and the need to protect what is closest.
ramacharitamanas::384.detailed_meaning: In Daksha’s sacrifice, Sati has seen Shiva insulted and feels the pain as her own. The scene shifts from shock to anger as her mother tries to soothe her, but the deeper wound is already driving the story forward.
ramacharitamanas::384.modern_relevance: A relative is mocked at a family gathering, and your chest tightens before you can think. The hurt is not just for them — it touches your sense of belonging and dignity.
ramacharitamanas::384.insight: It shows how insult can trigger protective anger before reason has a chance to intervene.

ramacharitamanas::385.verse_sanskrit: सिव अपमानु न जाइ सहि हृदयँ न होइ प्रबोध। सकल सभहि हठि हटकि तब बोलीं बचन सक्रोध ॥
ramacharitamanas::385.verse_hindi: परन्तु उनसे शिवजी का अपमान सहा नहीं गया, इससे उनके हृदय में कुछ भी प्रबोध नहीं हुआ। तब वे सारी सभा को हठपूर्वक डाँटकर क्रोधभरे वचन बोलीं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::385.english_translation: But she could not bear Shiva's insult, and no counsel could reach her heart. Then, pushing aside the whole assembly, she spoke angry words.
ramacharitamanas::385.translation_literal: सिव (Shiva) / अपमानु (insult) / न जाइ (cannot) / सहि (bear) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / न होइ (does not happen) / प्रबोध (clear counsel) / सकल (all) / सभहि (assembly) / हठि (forcefully) / हटकि (pushing aside) / तब (then) / बोलीं (she spoke) / बचन (words) / सक्रोध (with anger)
ramacharitamanas::385.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::385.essence: Insult to what you love can silence all reason.
ramacharitamanas::385.simple_meaning: Sati cannot bear the insult to Shiva, and no advice can calm her. She turns away from the assembly and speaks in anger.
ramacharitamanas::385.simple_insight: Pride and hurt can make even wise counsel useless.
ramacharitamanas::385.detailed_meaning: At Daksha's sacrifice, Sati has heard Shiva insulted in front of everyone. The assembly tries to calm her, but her grief and anger have already taken over. This verse shows the moment before she speaks her protest.
ramacharitamanas::385.modern_relevance: Someone mocks the person you love in a room full of people, and your chest tightens before you can think. The mind shuts the door on advice when hurt feels like honor.
ramacharitamanas::385.insight: It shows how wounded loyalty can override reason and turn the mind against counsel.

ramacharitamanas::386.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु सभासद सकल मुनिंदा। कही सुनी जिन्ह संकर निंदा॥ सो फलु तुरत लहब सब काहूँ। भली भाँति पछिताब पिताहूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::386.verse_hindi: हे सभासदों और सब मुनीश्वरो! सुनो। जिन लोगों ने यहाँ शिवजी की निंदा की या सुनी है, उन सबको उसका फल तुरंत ही मिलेगा और मेरे पिता दक्ष भी भलीभाँति पछताएँगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::386.english_translation: Listen, all members of the assembly and all sages. Everyone who has spoken or heard Shiva's slander will quickly bear its result, and my father Daksha will surely repent deeply.
ramacharitamanas::386.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / सभासद (members of the assembly) / सकल (all) / मुनिंदा (sages) / कही (spoken) / सुनी (heard) / जिन्ह (those who) / संकर (Shiva) / निंदा (slander) / सो (that) / फलु (result) / तुरत (immediately) / लहब (will receive) / सब (all) / काहूँ (of anyone) / भली भाँति (well) / पछिताब (will regret) / पिताहूँ (father too)
ramacharitamanas::386.speaker: Sati
ramacharitamanas::386.essence: Insult carries its own punishment, and the speaker is not spared.
ramacharitamanas::386.simple_meaning: Sati warns the assembly that anyone involved in insulting Shiva will face the consequence at once, including her father.
ramacharitamanas::386.simple_insight: Words spoken in contempt do not vanish. They return as pain, regret, and damage to relationship.
ramacharitamanas::386.detailed_meaning: In Daksha's assembly, Sati has heard Shiva insulted and her anger rises to a breaking point. She turns on the gathered sages and warns that everyone who spoke or even heard the slander will bear its result, and Daksha himself will regret it.
ramacharitamanas::386.modern_relevance: A family dinner turns sharp when someone mocks a person who is absent. The room feels lighter for a second, then heavier for days. Public contempt always leaves a mark.
ramacharitamanas::386.insight: It shifts the mind from casual criticism to awareness of the cost of disrespect.

ramacharitamanas::387.verse_sanskrit: संत संभु श्रीपति अपबादा। सुनिअ जहाँ तहँ असि मरजादा॥ काटिअ तासु जीभ जो बसाई। श्रवन मूदि न त चलिअ पराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::387.verse_hindi: जहाँ संत, शिवजी और लक्ष्मीपति श्री विष्णु भगवान की निंदा सुनी जाए, वहाँ ऐसी मर्यादा है कि यदि अपना वश चले तो उस (निंदा करने वाले) की जीभ काट लें और नहीं तो कान मूँदकर वहाँ से भाग जाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::387.english_translation: Where saints, Shiva, and Lord Vishnu are insulted, such conduct is never proper. If one has the power, cut out the slanderer's tongue; otherwise, cover your ears and leave at once.
ramacharitamanas::387.translation_literal: संत (saints) / संभु (Shiva) / श्रीपति (Lord Vishnu) / अपबादा (insults, slander) / सुनिअ (if heard) / जहाँ (where) / तहँ (there) / असि (such) / मरजादा (right conduct, proper standard) / काटिअ (cut) / तासु (his) / जीभ (tongue) / जो (if) / बसाई (one has power) / श्रवन (ears) / मूदि (cover) / न (not) / त (then) / चलिअ (go) / पराई (away, elsewhere)
ramacharitamanas::387.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::387.simple_meaning: A person should not tolerate insults against saints, Shiva, or Vishnu. The proper response is to stop listening and leave.
ramacharitamanas::387.simple_insight: Respect is not passive. Sometimes the cleanest response is to refuse the room entirely.
ramacharitamanas::387.detailed_meaning: In the Shiva-led frame narrative, Parvati has just heard Shiva condemn the insult of a devotee. Tulsidas sharpens that warning into a rule of conduct: when sacred figures are abused, a righteous person must not linger and absorb it.
ramacharitamanas::387.modern_relevance: You open a group chat and see mockery aimed at someone you respect. You do not need to argue with every cruel voice. Sometimes dignity means closing the thread and walking away.
ramacharitamanas::387.insight: It trains the reader to protect reverence by refusing to participate in contempt.

ramacharitamanas::388.verse_sanskrit: जगदातमा महेसु पुरारी। जगत जनक सब के हितकारी॥ पिता मंदमति निंदत तेही। दच्छ सुक्र संभव यह देही ॥
ramacharitamanas::388.verse_hindi: त्रिपुर दैत्य को मारने वाले भगवान महेश्वर सम्पूर्ण जगत की आत्मा हैं, वे जगत्पिता और सबका हित करने वाले हैं। मेरा मंदबुद्धि पिता उनकी निंदा करता है और मेरा यह शरीर दक्ष ही के वीर्य से उत्पन्न है ॥
ramacharitamanas::388.english_translation: Shiva, destroyer of Tripura, is the self of the world, the father of the universe, and the benefactor of all. My foolish father reviles him, and this body was born from Daksha's own seed.
ramacharitamanas::388.translation_literal: जगदातमा (self of the world) / महेसु (great lord Shiva) / पुरारी (destroyer of Tripura) / जगत जनक (father of the world) / सब के हितकारी (benefactor of all)॥ / पिता (father) / मंदमति (foolish-minded) / निंदत (reviles) / तेही (him) / दच्छ (Daksha) / सुक्र (seed) / संभव (born) / यह (this) / देही (body)॥
ramacharitamanas::388.speaker: Sati
ramacharitamanas::388.essence: A heart that sees Shiva clearly cannot remain in insult.
ramacharitamanas::388.simple_meaning: Sati praises Shiva as the universal benefactor and condemns her father's insult of him. She feels torn because her body itself came from Daksha's lineage.
ramacharitamanas::388.simple_insight: Love becomes unbearable when respect is broken; the heart refuses to stay where the beloved is mocked.
ramacharitamanas::388.detailed_meaning: At Daksha's sacrifice, Sati hears Shiva insulted in front of everyone. She answers with fierce devotion, naming Shiva as the world's self and benefactor, then turns against the body born from Daksha's line. This sets up her decision to leave that body behind.
ramacharitamanas::388.modern_relevance: You sit at a family dinner while someone casually mocks the person you love most. The room goes silent, and suddenly staying polite feels impossible.
ramacharitamanas::388.insight: It shows how devotion can become moral clarity: once reverence is violated, compromise feels like self-betrayal.

ramacharitamanas::389.verse_sanskrit: तजिहउँ तुरत देह तेहि हेतू। उर धरि चंद्रमौलि बृषकेतू॥ अस कहि जोग अगिनि तनु जारा। भयउ सकल मख हाहाकारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::389.verse_hindi: इसलिए चन्द्रमा को ललाट पर धारण करने वाले वृषकेतु शिवजी को हृदय में धारण करके मैं इस शरीर को तुरंत ही त्याग दूँगी। ऐसा कहकर सतीजी ने योगाग्नि में अपना शरीर भस्म कर डाला। सारी यज्ञशाला में हाहाकार मच गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::389.english_translation: Therefore, I will immediately leave this body for his sake, keeping Lord Shiva, the one with the moon on his brow and the bull-banner, in my heart. Saying this, Sati burned her body in the fire of yoga. The whole sacrificial arena erupted in uproar.
ramacharitamanas::389.translation_literal: तजिहउँ (I will abandon) / तुरत (immediately) / देह (body) / तेहि हेतू (for that reason) / उर धरि (placing in the heart) / चंद्रमौलि (moon-crowned one) / बृषकेतू (bull-bannered one) / अस कहि (saying thus) / जोग अगिनि (yoga fire) / तनु (body) / जारा (burned) / भयउ (became) / सकल (entire) / मख (sacrificial arena) / हाहाकारा (uproar)
ramacharitamanas::389.speaker: Sati
ramacharitamanas::389.essence: Devotion can become so absolute that the body is no longer bearable.
ramacharitamanas::389.simple_meaning: Sati decides to give up her body for Shiva and burns herself in the fire of yogic power, causing chaos in the sacrificial arena.
ramacharitamanas::389.simple_insight: Love and insult both become unbearable here; the body itself becomes the final protest.
ramacharitamanas::389.detailed_meaning: At Daksha's sacrifice, Sati hears her husband Shiva mocked and shamed. Holding Shiva in her heart, she resolves to abandon her body at once. Her self-immolation shatters the ritual gathering and marks the breaking point of the scene.
ramacharitamanas::389.modern_relevance: You sit at a family table where someone you love is being mocked. The room keeps eating, but you cannot. Something in you breaks before the conversation does.
ramacharitamanas::389.insight: It shows how inner loyalty can be stronger than social pressure, even when the cost is total.

ramacharitamanas::390.verse_sanskrit: सती मरनु सुनि संभु गन लगे करन मख खीस। जग्य बिधंस बिलोकि भृगु रच्छा कीन्हि मुनीस ॥ ॥
ramacharitamanas::390.verse_hindi: सती का मरण सुनकर शिवजी के गण यज्ञ विध्वंस करने लगे। यज्ञ विध्वंस होते देखकर मुनीश्वर भृगुजी ने उसकी रक्षा की ॥
ramacharitamanas::390.english_translation: Hearing of Sati's death, Shiva's attendants began to disrupt the sacrifice. Seeing the sacrifice being ruined, the sage Bhrigu protected it.
ramacharitamanas::390.translation_literal: सती (Sati) / मरनु (death) / सुनि (hearing) / संभु (Shiva) / गन (attendants) / लगे (began) / करन (to do) / मख (sacrifice) / खीस (trouble, disruption) / जग्य (sacrifice) / बिधंस (destruction) / बिलोकि (seeing) / भृगु (Bhrigu) / रच्छा (protection) / कीन्हि (did) / मुनीस (great sage)
ramacharitamanas::390.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::390.essence: Anger spreads fast; steadiness protects what rage would destroy.
ramacharitamanas::390.simple_meaning: When Sati's death reached Shiva's attendants, they moved to wreck the sacrifice. Bhrigu saw the danger and protected the ritual.
ramacharitamanas::390.simple_insight: A single death can ignite a chain of anger, and a wise response can still hold the line.
ramacharitamanas::390.detailed_meaning: Sati has left her body, and the news reaches Shiva's camp. His attendants rush to disrupt the sacrifice in anger, while Bhrigu, watching the danger unfold, moves to protect what remains. The verse is a scene of rising chaos, not the passage's main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::390.modern_relevance: A family chat turns explosive after one painful message, and everyone starts taking sides. Before the whole situation burns down, someone steady has to protect what still matters.
ramacharitamanas::390.insight: It shifts attention from revenge to containment when emotions begin to spread.

ramacharitamanas::391.verse_sanskrit: समाचार सब संकर पाए। बीरभद्रु करि कोप पठाए॥ जग्य बिधंस जाइ तिन्ह कीन्हा। सकल सुरन्ह बिधिवत फलु दीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::391.verse_hindi: ये सब समाचार शिवजी को मिले, तब उन्होंने क्रोध करके वीरभद्र को भेजा। उन्होंने वहाँ जाकर यज्ञ विध्वंस कर डाला और सब देवताओं को यथोचित फल (दंड) दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::391.english_translation: When Shiva received the news, he sent Virabhadra in anger. Virabhadra went there and destroyed the sacrifice, giving all the radiant beings their due punishment.
ramacharitamanas::391.translation_literal: समाचार (news) / सब (all) / संकर (Shiva) / पाए (received) । / बीरभद्रु (Virabhadra) / करि (doing) / कोप (anger) / पठाए (sent) ॥ / जग्य (sacrifice) / बिधंस (destruction) / जाइ (going) / तिन्ह (they) / कीन्हा (did) । / सकल (all) / सुरन्ह (radiant beings) / बिधिवत (properly / according to rule) / फलु (result / due) / दीन्हा (gave) ॥
ramacharitamanas::391.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::391.essence: Violating reverence brings a forceful reckoning.
ramacharitamanas::391.simple_meaning: Shiva hears what happened and sends Virabhadra to destroy Daksha's sacrifice. The heavenly beings involved receive the consequences of their actions.
ramacharitamanas::391.simple_insight: Actions that violate reverence do not disappear quietly; they return with force.
ramacharitamanas::391.detailed_meaning: After Sati's death, the news reaches Shiva. He responds by sending Virabhadra, who storms the sacrifice and tears it apart. This is the immediate consequence of Daksha's insult and the rupture it caused in the sacred order.
ramacharitamanas::391.modern_relevance: A room full of people thinks a cruel joke will pass unnoticed. It doesn't. The damage comes back fast, and everyone has to face what they helped create.
ramacharitamanas::391.insight: It shows that disrespect and cruelty trigger consequences that cannot be contained by ceremony or status.

ramacharitamanas::392.verse_sanskrit: भै जगबिदित दच्छ गति सोई। जसि कछु संभु बिमुख कै होई॥ यह इतिहास सकल जग जानी। ताते मैं संछेप बखानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::392.verse_hindi: दक्ष की जगत्प्रसिद्ध वही गति हुई, जो शिवद्रोही की हुआ करती है। यह इतिहास सारा संसार जानता है, इसलिए मैंने संक्षेप में वर्णन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::392.english_translation: Daksha met the well-known fate that befalls one who turns away from Shiva. The whole world knows this story, so I have told it briefly.
ramacharitamanas::392.translation_literal: भै (became) / जगबिदित (world-known) / दच्छ (Daksha) / गति (fate) / सोई (that)। / जसि (as) / कछु (some) / संभु (Shiva) / बिमुख (turned away) / कै (of) / होई (happens)॥ / यह (this) / इतिहास (story) / सकल (entire) / जग (world) / जानी (knows) / ताते (therefore) / मैं (I) / संछेप (briefly) / बखानी (narrated)॥
ramacharitamanas::392.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::392.essence: Turning away from Shiva brings a fate everyone remembers.
ramacharitamanas::392.simple_meaning: Daksha suffered the fate that comes to one who turns away from Shiva. Everyone already knows this story, so the poet tells it briefly.
ramacharitamanas::392.simple_insight: Some stories are repeated because their warning is unforgettable.
ramacharitamanas::392.detailed_meaning: After Sati’s death, Shiva’s followers attack Daksha’s sacrifice. This verse steps back from the scene and says Daksha’s downfall is already famous: turning away from Shiva brings ruin. The poet moves quickly because the next verse will return to Sati’s own vow.
ramacharitamanas::392.modern_relevance: A family argument has already gone too far, and everyone can feel the damage. Some choices become public lessons because the consequences are so clear that no one needs the full retelling.
ramacharitamanas::392.insight: It frames the episode as a remembered warning, not just a private feud.

ramacharitamanas::393.verse_sanskrit: सतीं मरत हरि सन बरु मागा। जनम जनम सिव पद अनुरागा॥ तेहि कारन हिमगिरि गृह जाई। जनमीं पारबती तनु पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::393.verse_hindi: सती ने मरते समय भगवान हरि से यह वर माँगा कि मेरा जन्म-जन्म में शिवजी के चरणों में अनुराग रहे। इसी कारण उन्होंने हिमाचल के घर जाकर पार्वती के शरीर से जन्म लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::393.english_translation: Sati asked Hari for one boon at the time of death: may love for Shiva's feet remain through every birth. For that reason, she went to the home of Himavan and was born as Parvati in a new body.
ramacharitamanas::393.translation_literal: सतीं (Sati) / मरत (at dying) / हरि (Hari) / सन (from) / बरु (boon) / मागा (asked) / जनम (birth) / जनम (birth) / सिव (Shiva) / पद (feet) / अनुरागा (loving attachment) ॥ तेहि (for that) / कारन (reason) / हिमगिरि (Himavan) / गृह (house) / जाई (going) / जनमीं (was born) / पारबती (Parvati) / तनु (body) / पाई (having obtained)
ramacharitamanas::393.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::393.essence: Love that clings to the divine returns in every life.
ramacharitamanas::393.simple_meaning: Sati asks for one blessing before death: unwavering love for Shiva in every life. That prayer becomes the reason she is born again as Parvati.
ramacharitamanas::393.simple_insight: Real devotion does not end with one lifetime; it keeps returning with you.
ramacharitamanas::393.detailed_meaning: After the sacrifice, the story turns to Sati's final wish. Before leaving her body, she asks Hari for a love that will always remain fixed on Shiva's feet. That longing leads to her rebirth as Parvati in Himavan's home.
ramacharitamanas::393.modern_relevance: You meet someone who changed your life, and even after years, your heart still returns to them. This verse says the deepest love does not fade with time; it shapes who you become next.
ramacharitamanas::393.insight: It shifts devotion from a passing feeling to a lasting orientation of the heart.

ramacharitamanas::394.verse_sanskrit: जब तें उमा सैल गृह जाईं। सकल सिद्धि संपति तहँ छाईं॥ जहँ तहँ मुनिन्ह सुआश्रम कीन्हे। उचित बास हिम भूधर दीन्हे ॥
ramacharitamanas::394.verse_hindi: जब से उमाजी हिमाचल के घर जन्मीं, तबसे वहाँ सारी सिद्धियाँ और सम्पत्तियाँ छा गईं। मुनियों ने जहाँ-तहाँ सुंदर आश्रम बना लिए और हिमाचल ने उनको उचित स्थान दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::394.english_translation: From the time Uma came to the mountain-house, all blessings and abundance spread there. Sages built lovely hermitages everywhere, and Himachal gave them proper places to live.
ramacharitamanas::394.translation_literal: जब तें (from the time) / उमा (Uma) / सैल (mountain) / गृह (house) / जाईं (came) / सकल (all) / सिद्धि (powers, attainments) / संपति (wealth, abundance) / तहँ (there) / छाईं (spread) ॥ / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / मुनिन्ह (by the sages) / सुआश्रम (beautiful hermitages) / कीन्हे (were made) / उचित (proper) / बास (dwelling places) / हिम भूधर (the mountain-bearing one, Himachal) / दीन्हे (gave)
ramacharitamanas::394.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::394.essence: Sacred presence turns a place into a refuge.
ramacharitamanas::394.simple_meaning: Uma's arrival made the mountain land blessed and prosperous. Sages settled there in beautiful hermitages, and Himachal welcomed them with suitable places to live.
ramacharitamanas::394.simple_insight: A sacred presence changes a place without force. What is worthy naturally gathers around it.
ramacharitamanas::394.detailed_meaning: Shiva is recalling how Parvati's birth transformed her father's mountain home. Once Uma arrived, the whole region became blessed, and sages came to live there in peace. The verse is a descriptive bridge, showing the holiness that surrounds her before the next line adds more detail.
ramacharitamanas::394.modern_relevance: A home feels different the moment a kind, steady person enters it. Calm spreads, guests feel welcome, and even the atmosphere seems to settle into order.
ramacharitamanas::394.insight: It shifts attention from decoration to presence: blessing is shown through the life a place begins to hold.

ramacharitamanas::395.verse_sanskrit: सदा सुमन फल सहित सब द्रुम नव नाना जाति। प्रगटीं सुंदर सैल पर मनि आकर बहु भाँति ॥
ramacharitamanas::395.verse_hindi: उस सुंदर पर्वत पर बहुत प्रकार के सब नए-नए वृक्ष सदा पुष्प-फलयुक्त हो गए और वहाँ बहुत तरह की मणियों की खानें प्रकट हो गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::395.english_translation: All kinds of new trees, always full of flowers and fruit, appeared on the beautiful mountain. Mines of gems of many kinds also emerged there.
ramacharitamanas::395.translation_literal: सदा (always) / सुमन (flowers) / फल सहित (with fruits) / सब द्रुम (all trees) / नव (new) / नाना जाति (many kinds) / प्रगटीं (appeared) / सुंदर सैल (beautiful mountain) / पर (on) / मनि आकर (gem mines) / बहु भाँति (in many forms)
ramacharitamanas::395.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::395.essence: Blessing turns barren ground into abundance.
ramacharitamanas::395.simple_meaning: The mountain becomes abundantly fertile and rich, with flowering trees, fruit, and many kinds of gems.
ramacharitamanas::395.simple_insight: Blessing can transform a place into abundance without effort or struggle.
ramacharitamanas::395.detailed_meaning: After Sati’s rebirth as Parvati, the Himalayan home of Shiva and Parvati is described as overflowing with beauty. New trees bear flowers and fruit, and the mountain itself reveals hidden gem mines, showing the land as naturally blessed.
ramacharitamanas::395.modern_relevance: A neglected home suddenly feels alive after one loving person arrives and begins caring for it. The same rooms, the same walls — yet everything seems to bloom.
ramacharitamanas::395.insight: It shifts attention from scarcity to the way presence can make a place flourish.

ramacharitamanas::396.verse_sanskrit: सरिता सब पुनीत जलु बहहीं। खग मृग मधुप सुखी सब रहहीं॥ सहज बयरु सब जीवन्ह त्यागा। गिरि पर सकल करहिं अनुरागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::396.verse_hindi: सारी नदियों में पवित्र जल बहता है और पक्षी, पशु, भ्रमर सभी सुखी रहते हैं। सब जीवों ने अपना स्वाभाविक बैर छोड़ दिया और पर्वत पर सभी परस्पर प्रेम करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::396.english_translation: All rivers flow with pure water there, and birds, animals, and bees all live happily. All creatures have given up their natural hostility, and on the mountain everyone loves one another.
ramacharitamanas::396.translation_literal: सरिता (rivers) / सब (all) / पुनीत (pure, sanctified) / जलु (water) / बहहीं (flow) / खग (birds) / मृग (deer, animals) / मधुप (bees) / सुखी (happy) / सब (all) / रहहीं (remain) / सहज (natural) / बयरु (enmity) / सब (all) / जीवन्ह (of creatures) / त्यागा (abandoned) / गिरि (mountain) / पर (on) / सकल (all) / करहिं (do) / अनुरागा (love, affection)
ramacharitamanas::396.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::396.simple_meaning: The mountain has become so blessed that nature itself feels peaceful there. Even creatures that usually live by fear or hostility now live in harmony.
ramacharitamanas::396.simple_insight: A truly sacred place changes how beings relate to one another.
ramacharitamanas::396.detailed_meaning: In the Himalayas, after Parvati has come to her father’s home, the whole mountain seems transformed. Rivers run pure, birds and animals thrive, and even natural hostility among living beings disappears. The scene shows the mountain’s holiness through the peace it creates.
ramacharitamanas::396.modern_relevance: You walk into a home where everyone is tense, and somehow one calm person changes the whole room. No one is forced to soften, yet the atmosphere does it for them.
ramacharitamanas::396.insight: It shifts attention from decoration to atmosphere: real sanctity makes conflict lose its grip.

ramacharitamanas::397.verse_sanskrit: सोह सैल गिरिजा गृह आएँ। जिमि जनु रामभगति के पाएँ॥ नित नूतन मंगल गृह तासू। ब्रह्मादिक गावहिं जसु जासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::397.verse_hindi: पार्वतीजी के घर आ जाने से पर्वत ऐसा शोभायमान हो रहा है जैसा रामभक्ति को पाकर भक्त शोभायमान होता है। उस (पर्वतराज) के घर नित्य नए-नए मंगलोत्सव होते हैं, जिसका ब्रह्मादि यश गाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::397.english_translation: The mountain shines with Girija’s arrival, just as a devotee shines upon gaining Ram-bhakti. His home holds ever-new celebrations, and Brahma and the other radiant beings sing his praise.
ramacharitamanas::397.translation_literal: सोह (shone) / सैल (mountain) / गिरिजा (Girija, Parvati) / गृह (house/home) / आएँ (having come) / जिमि (just as) / जनु (as if) / रामभगति (Ram-devotion) / के (of) / पाएँ (having obtained) / नित (always) / नूतन (new) / मंगल (auspicious celebrations) / गृह (in the home) / तासू (of him) / ब्रह्मादिक (Brahma and others) / गावहिं (sing) / जसु (praise/glory) / जासू (whose)
ramacharitamanas::397.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::397.essence: Love turns an ordinary home into a place of continual auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::397.simple_meaning: Parvati’s arrival makes the mountain-home radiant and full of celebration. Tulsidas compares that joy to the glow of a devotee who has gained loving devotion to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::397.simple_insight: True joy is not external decoration; it is the warmth that comes when love fills a home.
ramacharitamanas::397.detailed_meaning: Parvati has come to the mountain home of Himachal, and the whole place seems transformed. Tulsidas compares that brightness to the inner radiance of a devotee who has found Ram-bhakti, showing how devotion turns even a home into a place of celebration.
ramacharitamanas::397.modern_relevance: A house feels different the day someone you love walks back in after a long absence. The rooms are the same, but everything seems alive again.
ramacharitamanas::397.insight: It shifts attention from outer beauty to the joy created by loving presence and devotion.

ramacharitamanas::398.verse_sanskrit: नारद समाचार सब पाए। कोतुकहीं गिरि गेह सिधाए॥ सैलराज बड़ आदर कीन्हा। पद पखारि बर आसनु दीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::398.verse_hindi: जब नारदजी ने ये सब समाचार सुने तो वे कौतुक ही से हिमाचल के घर पधारे। पर्वतराज ने उनका बड़ा आदर किया और चरण धोकर उनको उत्तम आसन दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::398.english_translation: When Narad heard all the news, he went to the mountain home out of curiosity. The mountain king showed him great respect, washed his feet, and offered him a fine seat.
ramacharitamanas::398.translation_literal: नारद (Narad) / समाचार (news) / सब (all) / पाए (heard) / कोतुकहीं (out of curiosity) / गिरि (mountain) / गेह (home) / सिधाए (went)॥ / सैलराज (king of mountains) / बड़ (great) / आदर (respect) / कीन्हा (did) / पद (feet) / पखारि (washing) / बर (excellent) / आसनु (seat) / दीन्हा (gave) ॥
ramacharitamanas::398.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::398.essence: Honor opens the door before words do.
ramacharitamanas::398.simple_meaning: Narad hears the news and visits the mountain palace. Himachal welcomes him with honor, washes his feet, and seats him respectfully.
ramacharitamanas::398.simple_insight: True respect begins with humble welcome, not status.
ramacharitamanas::398.detailed_meaning: Narad arrives at Himachal's home after hearing the news of Parvati's presence and the growing auspiciousness there. The mountain king greets the sage with full honor, showing the reverence that shapes the whole scene before the deeper exchange begins.
ramacharitamanas::398.modern_relevance: A respected elder walks into your home, and you stop everything to greet them properly. The way you receive a guest reveals the culture of your heart.
ramacharitamanas::398.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the etiquette of reverence and welcome.

ramacharitamanas::399.verse_sanskrit: नारि सहित मुनि पद सिरु नावा। चरन सलिल सबु भवनु सिंचावा॥ निज सौभाग्य बहुत गिरि बरना। सुता बोलि मेली मुनि चरना ॥
ramacharitamanas::399.verse_hindi: फिर अपनी स्त्री सहित मुनि के चरणों में सिर नवाया और उनके चरणोदक को सारे घर में छिड़काया। हिमाचल ने अपने सौभाग्य का बहुत बखान किया और पुत्री को बुलाकर मुनि के चरणों पर डाल दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::399.english_translation: Then, along with his wife, he bowed his head at the sage's feet and sprinkled the water from the sage's feet all over the house. Himachal praised his own great good fortune and called his daughter forward, placing her at the sage's feet.
ramacharitamanas::399.translation_literal: नारि सहित (along with wife) / मुनि पद (sage's feet) / सिरु नावा (bowed head) / चरन सलिल (water from the feet) / सबु भवनु (entire house) / सिंचावा (sprinkled) / निज (own) / सौभाग्य (good fortune) / बहुत (greatly) / गिरि बरना (Himachal praised) / सुता (daughter) / बोलि (calling) / मेली (placed) / मुनि चरना (at the sage's feet)
ramacharitamanas::399.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::399.essence: True honor is offering yourself, not just respect.
ramacharitamanas::399.simple_meaning: Himachal honors the sage with full humility, uses the sacred foot-water to bless the home, and offers his daughter to the sage's feet.
ramacharitamanas::399.simple_insight: Respect becomes complete when pride turns into offering.
ramacharitamanas::399.detailed_meaning: Parvati has returned to her parents' home, and Narad has arrived as an honored guest. Himachal bows with his wife, sprinkles the sage's foot-water through the house, praises his fortune, and brings his daughter forward. The scene builds toward Narad's judgment of Parvati.
ramacharitamanas::399.modern_relevance: You welcome a revered teacher into your home and suddenly every gesture matters — the bow, the water, the words, the trust behind them.
ramacharitamanas::399.insight: It shows how reverence moves from ceremony into surrender, preparing the heart to receive guidance.

ramacharitamanas::400.verse_sanskrit: त्रिकालग्य सर्बग्य तुम्ह गति सर्बत्र तुम्हारि। कहहु सुता के दोष गुन मुनिबर हृदयँ बिचारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::400.verse_hindi: (और कहा-) हे मुनिवर! आप त्रिकालज्ञ और सर्वज्ञ हैं, आपकी सर्वत्र पहुँच है। अतः आप हृदय में विचार कर कन्या के दोष-गुण कहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::400.english_translation: O best of sages, you know the three times and are all-knowing; your reach is everywhere. So, reflect in your heart and speak of your daughter’s faults and virtues.
ramacharitamanas::400.translation_literal: त्रिकालग्य (knower of the three times) / सर्बग्य (all-knowing) / तुम्ह (you) / गति (reach) / सर्बत्र (everywhere) / तुम्हारि (your) / कहहु (speak) / सुता (daughter) / के (of) / दोष (faults) / गुन (virtues) / मुनिबर (best of sages) / हृदयँ (in heart) / बिचारि (having considered)
ramacharitamanas::400.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::400.essence: True judgment sees both fault and virtue before speaking.
ramacharitamanas::400.simple_meaning: Parvati asks Narada to judge her daughter fairly, because he is wise and can see everywhere. She wants him to think carefully and speak honestly about the girl's faults and virtues.
ramacharitamanas::400.simple_insight: Good judgment begins with careful attention, not quick praise or criticism.
ramacharitamanas::400.detailed_meaning: In Himachal’s home, Narada has just arrived and been honored. Parvati now speaks to him with respect, asking him to weigh her daughter’s qualities and flaws in his heart. The verse sets up Narada’s response, not the main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::400.modern_relevance: You’re asking a trusted mentor for honest feedback before a big decision. You don’t want flattery — you want someone to look closely and tell the truth kindly.
ramacharitamanas::400.insight: It shifts the mind toward balanced evaluation: see both strengths and flaws before forming a judgment.

ramacharitamanas::401.verse_sanskrit: कह मुनि बिहसि गूढ़ मृदु बानी। सुता तुम्हारि सकल गुन खानी॥ सुंदर सहज सुसील सयानी। नाम उमा अंबिका भवानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::401.verse_hindi: नारद मुनि ने हँसकर रहस्ययुक्त कोमल वाणी से कहा- तुम्हारी कन्या सब गुणों की खान है। यह स्वभाव से ही सुंदर, सुशील और समझदार है। उमा, अम्बिका और भवानी इसके नाम हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::401.english_translation: The sage smiled and spoke in soft, hidden words: “Your daughter is a mine of every virtue. She is beautiful, naturally gentle, well-mannered, and wise. Her names are Uma, Ambika, and Bhavani.”
ramacharitamanas::401.translation_literal: कह (said) / मुनि (the sage) / बिहसि (smiling, with a smile) / गूढ़ (hidden, subtle) / मृदु (soft, gentle) / बानी (speech) / सुता (daughter) / तुम्हारि (your) / सकल (all) / गुन (virtues) / खानी (mine, source) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सहज (natural, innate) / सुसील (well-mannered, virtuous) / सयानी (wise, mature) / नाम (names) / उमा (Uma) / अंबिका (Ambika) / भवानी (Bhavani)
ramacharitamanas::401.speaker: Narada
ramacharitamanas::401.essence: Gentle speech can bless more than it judges.
ramacharitamanas::401.simple_meaning: Narada gently praises Parvati as naturally beautiful, virtuous, and wise, using her sacred names to honor her character.
ramacharitamanas::401.simple_insight: True praise sees character first and speaks with care.
ramacharitamanas::401.detailed_meaning: Parvati’s parents have asked the sage to judge their daughter. Narada smiles and answers not with blunt facts, but with delicate praise. He names her virtues and sacred identities, turning a family concern into a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::401.modern_relevance: You’re introducing someone to parents who are anxious and watching every word. A thoughtful response can calm the room without lying or flattering too much.
ramacharitamanas::401.insight: It teaches you to answer sensitive questions with kindness, precision, and respect.

ramacharitamanas::402.verse_sanskrit: सब लच्छन संपन्न कुमारी। होइहि संतत पियहि पिआरी॥ सदा अचल एहि कर अहिवाता। एहि तें जसु पैहहिं पितु माता ॥
ramacharitamanas::402.verse_hindi: कन्या सब सुलक्षणों से सम्पन्न है, यह अपने पति को सदा प्यारी होगी। इसका सुहाग सदा अचल रहेगा और इससे इसके माता-पिता यश पावेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::402.english_translation: The maiden has every auspicious mark. She will always be dear to her husband. Her married life will remain unbroken, and her parents will gain honor through her.
ramacharitamanas::402.translation_literal: सब (all) / लच्छन (marks, signs) / संपन्न (endowed with) / कुमारी (maiden) / होइहि (will be) / संतत (always) / पियहि (to the beloved husband) / पिआरी (dear)॥ / सदा (always) / अचल (unmoving, unbroken) / एहि (this) / कर (of) / अहिवाता (married life, auspicious wifely state) / एहि तें (from this) / जसु (fame, honor) / पैहहिं (will obtain) / पितु माता (father and mother)॥
ramacharitamanas::402.speaker: Narada
ramacharitamanas::402.essence: A woman’s virtue can bless her marriage and uplift her whole family.
ramacharitamanas::402.simple_meaning: The girl is blessed with every good sign. She will remain dear to her husband, her married life will stay secure, and her parents will be honored through her.
ramacharitamanas::402.simple_insight: A life of virtue and harmony can bring dignity not only to one person, but to an entire family.
ramacharitamanas::402.detailed_meaning: Narada is praising Sita before Janaka’s court. He says the princess is marked by every auspicious quality, will remain beloved to her husband, and will bring lasting honor to her parents. The verse continues the blessing before the marriage is formally celebrated.
ramacharitamanas::402.modern_relevance: A family watches their daughter step into a new life, and everyone quietly hopes she will be cherished, respected, and safe. That wish for her well-being carries the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::402.insight: It shifts attention from display to lasting character, showing that true honor comes from the quality of one’s life and bonds.

ramacharitamanas::403.verse_sanskrit: होइहि पूज्य सकल जग माहीं। एहि सेवत कछु दुर्लभ नाहीं॥ एहि कर नामु सुमिरि संसारा। त्रिय चढ़िहहिं पतिब्रत असिधारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::403.verse_hindi: यह सारे जगत में पूज्य होगी और इसकी सेवा करने से कुछ भी दुर्लभ न होगा। संसार में स्त्रियाँ इसका नाम स्मरण करके पतिव्रता रूपी तलवार की धार पर चढ़ जाएँगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::403.english_translation: She will be revered throughout the world. Serving her brings nothing unattainable. By remembering her name, women will walk the razor’s edge of wifely fidelity.
ramacharitamanas::403.translation_literal: होइहि (will become) / पूज्य (worthy of worship) / सकल जग (all the world) / माहीं (in) / एहि (her) / सेवत (serving) / कछु (anything) / दुर्लभ (hard to obtain) / नाहीं (not) ॥ एहि (her) / कर (of) / नामु (name) / सुमिरि (remembering) / संसारा (the world) / त्रिय (women) / चढ़िहहिं (will ascend) / पतिब्रत (wifely fidelity) / असिधारा (razor’s edge) ॥
ramacharitamanas::403.speaker: Nārada
ramacharitamanas::403.essence: Her name becomes a support for steadfast fidelity.
ramacharitamanas::403.simple_meaning: Nārada says Sita will be honored everywhere, and even remembering her name will help women uphold steadfast fidelity.
ramacharitamanas::403.simple_insight: Her example turns devotion into courage, not fear.
ramacharitamanas::403.detailed_meaning: Nārada is praising Sita to Parvati and Janaka after describing her flawless qualities. He says her presence will be revered everywhere, and her very name will strengthen women to live with unwavering fidelity. This is part of his larger blessing, not a standalone teaching.
ramacharitamanas::403.modern_relevance: A young woman hears a story about someone who stayed loyal under pressure and feels steadier in her own choices. An ideal can become a support beam when life asks for integrity.
ramacharitamanas::403.insight: It shifts admiration into imitation: remembering a noble example strengthens conduct.

ramacharitamanas::404.verse_sanskrit: सैल सुलच्छन सुता तुम्हारी। सुनहु जे अब अवगुन दुइ चारी॥ अगुन अमान मातु पितु हीना। उदासीन सब संसय छीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::404.verse_hindi: हे पर्वतराज! तुम्हारी कन्या सुलच्छनी है। अब इसमें जो दो-चार अवगुण हैं, उन्हें भी सुन लो। गुणहीन, मानहीन, माता-पिताविहीन, उदासीन, संशयहीन (लापरवाह) ॥
ramacharitamanas::404.english_translation: O king of the mountain, your daughter is full of good marks. Listen now to the two or four faults in her. She is without qualities, without pride, without mother and father, and unconcerned, with all doubts cut away.
ramacharitamanas::404.translation_literal: सैल (mountain) / सुलच्छन (full of good marks) / सुता (daughter) / तुम्हारी (your) / सुनहु (listen) / जे (that) / अब (now) / अवगुन (faults) / दुइ चारी (two or four)॥ / अगुन (without qualities) / अमान (without pride) / मातु पितु हीना (without mother and father) / उदासीन (unconcerned) / सब संसय छीना (all doubts cut away)॥
ramacharitamanas::404.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::404.essence: Her greatest 'faults' are the marks of freedom.
ramacharitamanas::404.simple_meaning: The speaker praises the princess, then lists playful 'faults': she has no pride, no worldly attachment, no parents to cling to, and no doubts or hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::404.simple_insight: What looks like a flaw is actually spiritual freedom and simplicity.
ramacharitamanas::404.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the princess's qualities are being described before the swayamvar. The speaker turns praise into a teasing paradox, calling her 'faults' the very traits that make her fit for a rare, extraordinary match.
ramacharitamanas::404.modern_relevance: Someone calls you 'too simple' because you do not chase status, drama, or constant approval. What they call a lack may be the exact steadiness that makes you whole.
ramacharitamanas::404.insight: It flips the meaning of weakness and shows that humility, detachment, and certainty can be the highest strengths.

ramacharitamanas::405.verse_sanskrit: जोगी जटिल अकाम मन नगन अमंगल बेष। अस स्वामी एहि कहँ मिलिहि परी हस्त असि रेख ॥
ramacharitamanas::405.verse_hindi: योगी, जटाधारी, निष्काम हृदय, नंगा और अमंगल वेष वाला, ऐसा पति इसको मिलेगा। इसके हाथ में ऐसी ही रेखा पड़ी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::405.english_translation: A yogi, matted-haired, desireless, naked, and in an inauspicious garb—such a husband will she get. Such is the mark drawn on her hand.
ramacharitamanas::405.translation_literal: जोगी (yogi) / जटिल (matted-haired) / अकाम (without desire) / मन (mind) / नगन (naked) / अमंगल (inauspicious) / बेष (garb) / अस (such) / स्वामी (husband/master) / एहि (this) / कहँ (for) / मिलिहि (will get) / परी (fallen) / हस्त (hand) / असि (such) / रेख (line/mark)
ramacharitamanas::405.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::405.essence: Outer appearance can hide the life that truly belongs.
ramacharitamanas::405.simple_meaning: The child’s future husband is described as a renunciant with an inauspicious appearance, because that is what her hand-mark shows.
ramacharitamanas::405.simple_insight: What looks undesirable can still be the shape of a destined life.
ramacharitamanas::405.detailed_meaning: In Himalaya’s home, the family is hearing Narada’s prediction about Parvati’s marriage. The description sounds harsh and unsettling: her husband will look like a wandering renunciant, not a royal groom. This line sharpens the tension before the family reacts.
ramacharitamanas::405.modern_relevance: You hear a forecast that sounds nothing like the life you wanted. The first reaction is disappointment; the deeper question is whether appearances are hiding a greater fit.
ramacharitamanas::405.insight: It shifts attention from social image to the deeper truth of what a life is meant to hold.

ramacharitamanas::406.verse_sanskrit: सुनि मुनि गिरा सत्य जियँ जानी। दुख दंपतिहि उमा हरषानी॥ नारदहूँ यह भेदु न जाना। दसा एक समुझब बिलगाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::406.verse_hindi: नारद मुनि की वाणी सुनकर और उसको हृदय में सत्य जानकर पति-पत्नी (हिमवान् और मैना) को दुःख हुआ और पार्वतीजी प्रसन्न हुईं। नारदजी ने भी इस रहस्य को नहीं जाना, क्योंकि सबकी बाहरी दशा एक सी होने पर भी भीतरी समझ भिन्न-भिन्न थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::406.english_translation: Hearing the sage's words, they knew them true in their hearts. The parents felt sorrow, and Uma felt joy. Even Narada did not know this hidden difference: though the outer state seemed the same, the inner understanding was different.
ramacharitamanas::406.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (sage) / गिरा (speech) / सत्य (true) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानी (knowing) / दुख (sorrow) / दंपतिहि (to the couple) / उमा (Uma) / हरषानी (rejoiced)॥ / नारदहूँ (even Narada) / यह (this) / भेदु (difference) / न (not) / जाना (knew) / दसा (state) / एक (one) / समुझब (to understand) / बिलगाना (different)
ramacharitamanas::406.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::406.essence: The same words can become grief or joy, depending on the heart that receives them.
ramacharitamanas::406.simple_meaning: The same words can land differently in different hearts. Himavan and Maina feel grief, while Uma feels joy, because each understands the same message in a different way.
ramacharitamanas::406.simple_insight: A single truth can comfort one person and wound another.
ramacharitamanas::406.detailed_meaning: At Parvati's swayamvar, Narada's teasing prophecy has just been spoken. Himavan and Maina hear the warning and grieve, while Uma recognises the deeper meaning and rejoices. Even Narada misses the inner difference, because outwardly everyone seems calm.
ramacharitamanas::406.modern_relevance: A family hears the same diagnosis in the hospital corridor. One person hears disaster, another hears a path forward, and a third hears only noise. The words are identical; the inner state is not.
ramacharitamanas::406.insight: It trains you to notice that understanding depends on readiness, not just on hearing the same facts.

ramacharitamanas::407.verse_sanskrit: सकल सखीं गिरिजा गिरि मैना। पुलक सरीर भरे जल नैना॥ होइ न मृषा देवरिषि भाषा। उमा सो बचनु हृदयँ धरि राखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::407.verse_hindi: सारी सखियाँ, पार्वती, पर्वतराज हिमवान् और मैना सभी के शरीर पुलकित थे और सभी के नेत्रों में जल भरा था। देवर्षि के वचन असत्य नहीं हो सकते, (यह विचारकर) पार्वती ने उन वचनों को हृदय में धारण कर लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::407.english_translation: All the companions, Parvati, Himalaya, and Maina were thrilled, their eyes filled with tears. Thinking, “The words of the divine sage cannot be false,” Uma held those words in her heart.
ramacharitamanas::407.translation_literal: सकल (all) / सखीं (companions) / गिरिजा (Parvati) / गिरि (mountain, Himalaya) / मैना (Maina) / पुलक (thrill) / सरीर (body) / भरे (filled) / जल (water, tears) / नैना (eyes) / होइ (being) / न (not) / मृषा (false) / देवरिषि (divine sage) / भाषा (speech) / उमा (Uma/Parvati) / सो (that) / बचनु (words) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / धरि (holding) / राखा (kept)
ramacharitamanas::407.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::407.essence: Trust lets a hard truth enter before it is fully understood.
ramacharitamanas::407.simple_meaning: Parvati and her family are moved to tears and accept Narada's words as true. Parvati keeps that promise in her heart.
ramacharitamanas::407.simple_insight: Trust can begin before proof appears. A held word can quietly reshape a life.
ramacharitamanas::407.detailed_meaning: Narada has just spoken the startling truth about Parvati's future marriage. Himalaya, Maina, and the gathered companions are shaken, but Parvati does not reject the message. She receives the sage's words as true and keeps them inwardly, even before the full meaning unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::407.modern_relevance: A friend tells you something difficult to hear, and you feel the sting before you understand it. You do not dismiss it; you let it settle and watch what it changes in you.
ramacharitamanas::407.insight: It teaches you to receive a difficult truth without immediate resistance.

ramacharitamanas::408.verse_sanskrit: उपजेउ सिव पद कमल सनेहू। मिलन कठिन मन भा संदेहू॥ जानि कुअवसरु प्रीति दुराई। सखी उछँग बैठी पुनि जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::408.verse_hindi: उन्हें शिवजी के चरण कमलों में स्नेह उत्पन्न हो आया, परन्तु मन में यह संदेह हुआ कि उनका मिलना कठिन है। अवसर ठीक न जानकर उमा ने अपने प्रेम को छिपा लिया और फिर वे सखी की गोद में जाकर बैठ गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::408.english_translation: Love for Shiva's lotus feet arose in her heart, but she doubted whether meeting him would be difficult. Seeing the wrong moment, Uma hid her love and went back to sit in her companion's lap.
ramacharitamanas::408.translation_literal: उपजेउ (arose) / सिव (Shiva) / पद कमल (lotus feet) / सनेहू (love) / मिलन (meeting) / कठिन (difficult) / मन (mind) / भा (became) / संदेहू (doubt) / जानि (knowing) / कुअवसरु (wrong time) / प्रीति (love) / दुराई (hid) / सखी (companion) / उछँग (lap) / बैठी (sat) / पुनि (again) / जाई (went)
ramacharitamanas::408.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::408.essence: True feeling can stay hidden until the right moment arrives.
ramacharitamanas::408.simple_meaning: Uma feels devotion for Shiva, but she also feels doubt and hides that feeling for the moment.
ramacharitamanas::408.simple_insight: Love can be real and still wait for the right moment.
ramacharitamanas::408.detailed_meaning: Parvati's heart turns toward Shiva, but the situation is not yet ready for union. She feels the love, senses the obstacle, hides her emotion, and returns to sit quietly with her companion. The scene prepares the tension that follows.
ramacharitamanas::408.modern_relevance: You feel something deeply in a room where saying it would only make things awkward. So you smile, stay quiet, and wait for a better moment.
ramacharitamanas::408.insight: It shows how devotion can be inwardly alive even when outwardly restrained.

ramacharitamanas::409.verse_sanskrit: झूठि न होइ देवरिषि बानी। सोचहिं दंपति सखीं सयानी॥ उर धरि धीर कहइ गिरिराऊ। कहहु नाथ का करिअ उपाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::409.verse_hindi: देवर्षि की वाणी झूठी न होगी, यह विचार कर हिमवान् , मैना और सारी चतुर सखियाँ चिन्ता करने लगीं। फिर हृदय में धीरज धरकर पर्वतराज ने कहा- हे नाथ! कहिए, अब क्या उपाय किया जाए? ॥
ramacharitamanas::409.english_translation: The sage's word cannot be false. The husband, wife, and wise attendants grew anxious. Keeping courage in his heart, the mountain king said, “Lord, tell me what should be done now.”
ramacharitamanas::409.translation_literal: झूठि (false) / न होइ (does not become) / देवरिषि (divine sage) / बानी (speech) / सोचहिं (worry) / दंपति (the married pair) / सखीं (female companions) / सयानी (wise) / उर (in the heart) / धरि (placing) / धीर (steadiness) / कहइ (said) / गिरिराऊ (mountain king) / कहहु (tell) / नाथ (lord) / का (what) / करिअ (should be done) / उपाऊ (remedy, course)
ramacharitamanas::409.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::409.essence: Truth is accepted first; the next step is asked for second.
ramacharitamanas::409.simple_meaning: They trust the sage's words, but that trust brings worry. Himavan stays steady and asks what remedy is possible now.
ramacharitamanas::409.simple_insight: Even anxiety can become a calm request for guidance instead of panic.
ramacharitamanas::409.detailed_meaning: In Kailash, Parvati's family has just heard that the sage's prediction will not fail. That certainty makes them anxious about the hard outcome ahead. Himavan gathers himself and asks Shiva what can be done.
ramacharitamanas::409.modern_relevance: You get a message that a difficult truth is probably real, and your first impulse is to spiral. Then you breathe, steady yourself, and ask the one useful question: what now?
ramacharitamanas::409.insight: It shifts the mind from fear to practical surrender: stop resisting the truth and ask for the next right step.

ramacharitamanas::410.verse_sanskrit: कह मुनीस हिमवंत सुनु जो बिधि लिखा लिलार। देव दनुज नर नाग मुनि कोउ न मेटनिहार ॥
ramacharitamanas::410.verse_hindi: मुनीश्वर ने कहा- हे हिमवान् ! सुनो, विधाता ने ललाट पर जो कुछ लिख दिया है, उसको देवता, दानव, मनुष्य, नाग और मुनि कोई भी नहीं मिटा सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::410.english_translation: The sage said, “Listen, Himavan: whatever fate has written on the forehead, no being can erase.”
ramacharitamanas::410.translation_literal: कह (said) / मुनीस (sage) / हिमवंत (Himavan) / सुनु (listen) / जो (whatever) / बिधि (by fate) / लिखा (written) / लिलार (on the forehead) / देव (devas) / दनुज (demons) / नर (humans) / नाग (serpents) / मुनि (sages) / कोउ (anyone) / न (not) / मेटनिहार (able to erase)
ramacharitamanas::410.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::410.essence: No force can erase what has already been written.
ramacharitamanas::410.simple_meaning: Whatever has been written on the forehead cannot be erased by anyone, no matter how powerful or wise.
ramacharitamanas::410.simple_insight: Some things are beyond control, and peace begins when you stop fighting reality.
ramacharitamanas::410.detailed_meaning: Himavan and Mena are distressed because Shiva's marriage seems difficult. The sage answers by naming a hard truth: no power can erase what has already been written. This prepares the way for accepting the next instruction.
ramacharitamanas::410.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone, hoping the verdict will change. The email is already sent, the result already fixed. Sometimes the only honest move is to stop wrestling what cannot be rewritten.
ramacharitamanas::410.insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to acceptance of what cannot be changed.

ramacharitamanas::411.verse_sanskrit: तदपि एक मैं कहउँ उपाई। होइ करै जौं दैउ सहाई॥ जस बरु मैं बरनेउँ तुम्ह पाहीं। मिलिहि उमहि तस संसय नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::411.verse_hindi: तो भी एक उपाय मैं बताता हूँ। यदि दैव सहायता करें तो वह सिद्ध हो सकता है। उमा को वर तो निःसंदेह वैसा ही मिलेगा, जैसा मैंने तुम्हारे सामने वर्णन किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::411.english_translation: Still, I will suggest one way. If the divine helps, it can succeed. The bride Uma will surely get the same groom I described to you.
ramacharitamanas::411.translation_literal: तदपि (still) / एक (one) / मैं (I) / कहउँ (say) / उपाई (remedy, way) / होइ (may happen) / करै (does, makes) / जौं (if) / दैउ (the divine, fate) / सहाई (helper) / जस (as) / बरु (bridegroom) / मैं (I) / बरनेउँ (described) / तुम्ह (to you) / पाहीं (near, to) / मिलिहि (will meet, will get) / उमहि (Uma) / तस (that same) / संसय (doubt) / नाहीं (no) /
ramacharitamanas::411.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::411.essence: A workable path exists, but success still rests on grace.
ramacharitamanas::411.simple_meaning: Shiva offers one possible solution, but only if divine help makes it work. He assures that Uma will get the same groom he has already described.
ramacharitamanas::411.simple_insight: Even a wise plan still depends on forces beyond personal control.
ramacharitamanas::411.detailed_meaning: Himavan, Maina, and the worried companions have just heard that the sage's words cannot fail. Shiva now softens the tension by offering a possible way forward for Uma's marriage, while admitting that success depends on divine support.
ramacharitamanas::411.modern_relevance: You have a careful plan, but the room is still full of uncertainty. You can do your part clearly and still admit that some outcomes need help beyond you.
ramacharitamanas::411.insight: It shifts the mind from rigid control to humble action supported by grace.

ramacharitamanas::412.verse_sanskrit: जे जे बर के दोष बखाने। ते सब सिव पहिं मैं अनुमाने॥ जौं बिबाहु संकर सन होई। दोषउ गुन सम कह सबु कोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::412.verse_hindi: परन्तु मैंने वर के जो-जो दोष बतलाए हैं, मेरे अनुमान से वे सभी शिवजी में हैं। यदि शिवजी के साथ विवाह हो जाए तो दोषों को भी सब लोग गुणों के समान ही कहेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::412.english_translation: The faults I listed in a bridegroom all belong to Shiva in my view. If marriage happens with Shiva, everyone will call those faults virtues.
ramacharitamanas::412.translation_literal: जे जे (whatever) / बर (bridegroom) / के (of) / दोष (faults) / बखाने (described) / ते सब (all those) / सिव पहिं (in Shiva) / मैं (I) / अनुमाने (consider) ॥ / जौं (if) / बिबाहु (marriage) / संकर सन (with Shankar) / होई (happens) / दोषउ (faults also) / गुन (virtues) / सम (like) / कह (say) / सबु कोई (everyone)
ramacharitamanas::412.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::412.simple_meaning: Parvati says that the flaws she mentioned in a bridegroom are not real flaws in Shiva. If Shiva becomes the husband, people will see those same traits as virtues.
ramacharitamanas::412.simple_insight: Love changes the way the heart judges. What seemed like a defect can become beautiful when seen through devotion.
ramacharitamanas::412.detailed_meaning: Parvati is weighing Shiva as the possible bridegroom for her daughter and listing what others might call flaws. Then she realizes that Shiva's greatness changes the meaning of every trait. In this moment, devotion transforms judgment.
ramacharitamanas::412.modern_relevance: You watch someone you care about through a thousand small habits that outsiders would call flaws. The same quiet, the same roughness, the same strangeness feels precious because love has already changed the verdict.
ramacharitamanas::412.insight: It shifts attention from social judgment to the lens of devotion, where character is seen as sacred rather than defective.

ramacharitamanas::413.verse_sanskrit: जौं अहि सेज सयन हरि करहीं। बुध कछु तिन्ह कर दोषु न धरहीं॥ भानु कृसानु सर्ब रस खाहीं। तिन्ह कहँ मंद कहत कोउ नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::413.verse_hindi: जैसे विष्णु भगवान शेषनाग की शय्या पर सोते हैं, तो भी पण्डित लोग उनको कोई दोष नहीं लगाते। सूर्य और अग्निदेव अच्छे-बुरे सभी रसों का भक्षण करते हैं, परन्तु उनको कोई बुरा नहीं कहता ॥
ramacharitamanas::413.english_translation: As Vishnu rests on Sheshnag, wise people do not blame him. The sun and fire consume every kind of essence, yet no one calls them bad.
ramacharitamanas::413.translation_literal:
जौं (if) / अहि-सेज (serpent-bed) / सयन (sleeping) / हरि (Hari, Ram) / करहीं (do) / बुध (the wise) / कछु (any) / तिन्ह (their) / कर (of) / दोषु (fault) / न धरहीं (do not hold)
भानु (sun) / कृसानु (fire) / सर्ब (all) / रस (essence) / खाहीं (eat) / तिन्ह कहँ (for them) / मंद (bad) / कहत (calling) / कोउ (anyone) / नाहीं (does not)
ramacharitamanas::413.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::413.essence: Great beings are measured by their nature, not by ordinary standards.
ramacharitamanas::413.simple_meaning: Great beings are not judged by ordinary rules. What seems like a fault in them is part of their nature and power.
ramacharitamanas::413.simple_insight: It eases the mind to stop forcing small rules onto what is larger than them.
ramacharitamanas::413.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-Swayamvar debate, the speaker is defending Shiva by comparing him to great powers in nature. Just as Vishnu resting on Sheshnag, the sun, and fire are not blamed for what they naturally do, Shiva should not be judged by ordinary standards.
ramacharitamanas::413.modern_relevance: You see a leader, teacher, or parent do something that would look wrong in anyone else. The mind rushes to judge. This verse asks you to pause and ask whether the same rule even applies.
ramacharitamanas::413.insight: It shifts judgment from surface appearance to the nature and role of what is being seen.

ramacharitamanas::414.verse_sanskrit: सुभ अरु असुभ सलिल सब बहई। सुरसरि कोउ अपुनीत न कहई॥ समरथ कहुँ नहिं दोषु गोसाईं। रबि पावक सुरसरि की नाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::414.verse_hindi: गंगाजी में शुभ और अशुभ सभी जल बहता है, पर कोई उन्हें अपवित्र नहीं कहता। सूर्य, अग्नि और गंगाजी की भाँति समर्थ को कुछ दोष नहीं लगता ॥
ramacharitamanas::414.english_translation: Good and bad waters both flow in the river, yet no one calls the river impure. In the same way, no fault clings to the capable, just as it does not cling to the sun, fire, or the river.
ramacharitamanas::414.translation_literal: सुभ (good) / अरु (and) / असुभ (bad) / सलिल (water) / सब (all) / बहई (flows) / सुरसरि (river of the gods) / कोउ (anyone) / अपुनीत (impure) / न (not) / कहई (calls) / समरथ (capable, powerful) / कहुँ (for) / नहिं (not) / दोषु (fault) / गोसाईं (lord) / रबि (sun) / पावक (fire) / सुरसरि (river of the gods) / की (of) / नाईं (like)
ramacharitamanas::414.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::414.essence: Real strength stays pure even in mixed surroundings.
ramacharitamanas::414.simple_meaning: Pure and impure things can flow together, yet the river stays pure. In the same way, great beings are not diminished by the faults around them.
ramacharitamanas::414.simple_insight: It brings relief from petty judgment and reminds you that strength can remain clean in a messy world.
ramacharitamanas::414.detailed_meaning: In the middle of Sita's swayamvar, the discussion turns to Shiva's worthiness as a bridegroom. Tulsidas answers objections by saying that the truly powerful are like the sun, fire, and Ganga: contact with impurity does not diminish them.
ramacharitamanas::414.modern_relevance: You work in a room full of gossip, shortcuts, and mixed motives, yet you keep your standards intact. That is what this verse defends: character strong enough to stay clean in contaminated surroundings.
ramacharitamanas::414.insight: It shifts judgment from surface contamination to inner capacity and steadiness.

ramacharitamanas::415.verse_sanskrit: जौं अस हिसिषा करहिं नर जड़ बिबेक अभिमान। परहिं कलप भरि नरक महुँ जीव कि ईस समान ॥
ramacharitamanas::415.verse_hindi: यदि मूर्ख मनुष्य ज्ञान के अभिमान से इस प्रकार होड़ करते हैं, तो वे कल्पभर के लिए नरक में पड़ते हैं। भला कहीं जीव भी ईश्वर के समान (सर्वथा स्वतंत्र) हो सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::415.english_translation: If foolish people, out of pride in their understanding, compete like this, they fall into lower realms for ages. Can a living being ever be equal to the supreme being?
ramacharitamanas::415.translation_literal: जौं (if) / अस (such) / हिसिषा (competition) / करहिं (do) / नर (people) / जड़ (foolish) / बिबेक (discernment) / अभिमान (pride) / परहिं (fall) / कलप भरि (for a whole age) / नरक महुँ (into lower realms) / जीव (a living being) / कि (can) / ईस (the supreme being) / समान (equal)
ramacharitamanas::415.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::415.essence: Pride in insight collapses the very clarity it claims.
ramacharitamanas::415.simple_meaning: Pride in one's own intelligence becomes a trap. A human being cannot claim the same freedom or power as the supreme reality.
ramacharitamanas::415.simple_insight: It softens the urge to prove yourself and replaces it with humility.
ramacharitamanas::415.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is closing a line of comparison about the supreme being's freedom. After examples like the sun, fire, and the Ganga, he warns that foolish pride in reasoning only leads to downfall. The point is simple: a living being is not the supreme being.
ramacharitamanas::415.modern_relevance: You win an argument, then keep replaying it in your head because being right felt too good. The verse cuts that loop: intelligence without humility becomes self-destruction.
ramacharitamanas::415.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to clear limits, so discernment can stay clean.

ramacharitamanas::416.verse_sanskrit: सुरसरि जल कृत बारुनि जाना। कबहुँ न संत करहिं तेहि पाना॥ सुरसरि मिलें सो पावन जैसें। ईस अनीसहि अंतरु तैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::416.verse_hindi: गंगा जल से भी बनाई हुई मदिरा को जानकर संत लोग कभी उसका पान नहीं करते। पर वही गंगाजी में मिल जाने पर जैसे पवित्र हो जाती है, ईश्वर और जीव में भी वैसा ही भेद है ॥
ramacharitamanas::416.english_translation: Saints never drink liquor, even if it is made from Ganga water. When it mixes with the Ganga, it becomes pure; in the same way, there is a difference between the divine and the individual self.
ramacharitamanas::416.translation_literal: सुरसरि (Ganga) / जल (water) / कृत (made) / बारुनि (liquor) / जाना (known) / कबहुँ (never) / न (not) / संत (saints) / करहिं (do) / तेहि (that) / पाना (drinking) / सुरसरि (Ganga) / मिलें (when mixed) / सो (that) / पावन (pure) / जैसें (as) / ईस (the divine) / अनीसहि (the individual self) / अंतरु (difference) / तैसें (thus)
ramacharitamanas::416.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::416.essence: Contact can purify, but it never makes the finite infinite.
ramacharitamanas::416.simple_meaning: Saints avoid impurity even in disguised form. The verse then says the divine and the individual self are not the same, just as polluted water becomes pure only by joining the Ganga.
ramacharitamanas::416.simple_insight: Real discernment sees what cannot be made equal by appearance alone.
ramacharitamanas::416.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, Tulsidas is explaining how great beings are not touched by impurity, and then turns to a deeper point: even when water is mixed with the Ganga, its nature changes only through contact with the sacred river. That image points to the difference between the supreme reality and the individual self.
ramacharitamanas::416.modern_relevance: A person may sit in the same room, wear the same clothes, and speak the same language as a mentor, but still not become that mentor. Proximity can refine you, but it does not erase the difference between source and reflection.
ramacharitamanas::416.insight: It shifts the mind from surface resemblance to essential distinction.

ramacharitamanas::417.verse_sanskrit: संभु सहज समरथ भगवाना। एहि बिबाहँ सब बिधि कल्याना॥ दुराराध्य पै अहहिं महेसू। आसुतोष पुनि किएँ कलेसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::417.verse_hindi: शिवजी सहज ही समर्थ हैं, क्योंकि वे भगवान हैं, इसलिए इस विवाह में सब प्रकार कल्याण है, परन्तु महादेवजी की आराधना बड़ी कठिन है, फिर भी क्लेश (तप) करने से वे बहुत जल्द संतुष्ट हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::417.english_translation: Shiva is naturally capable, for he is the divine. This marriage is blessed in every way. Yet Mahadeva is hard to win, and through hardship he becomes quickly pleased.
ramacharitamanas::417.translation_literal: संभु (Shiva) / सहज (naturally) / समरथ (capable) / भगवाना (the divine) / एहि (this) / बिबाहँ (marriage) / सब (all) / बिधि (ways) / कल्याना (auspicious) / दुराराध्य (hard to worship) / पै (yet) / अहहिं (are) / महेसू (Mahesh) / आसुतोष (quickly pleased) / पुनि (again) / किएँ (through doing) / कलेसू (hardship / austerity)
ramacharitamanas::417.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::417.essence: What is hard to win yields to sincere hardship.
ramacharitamanas::417.simple_meaning: Shiva is powerful and naturally auspicious, but he is not easy to please. He responds to sincere effort and austerity.
ramacharitamanas::417.simple_insight: Real devotion is not casual. It becomes serious enough to move even what seems hard to reach.
ramacharitamanas::417.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, the poem pauses to praise Shiva before the contest begins. Tulsidas says the marriage is blessed because Shiva himself is powerful and auspicious, yet he is won only through difficult worship and disciplined effort.
ramacharitamanas::417.modern_relevance: You show up with a half-hearted apology, hoping the tension will vanish. It does not. Some things respond only when your effort becomes real and sustained.
ramacharitamanas::417.insight: It shifts devotion from casual wishing to serious, sustained practice that can actually transform a situation.

ramacharitamanas::418.verse_sanskrit: जौं तपु करै कुमारि तुम्हारी। भाविउ मेटि सकहिं त्रिपुरारी॥ जद्यपि बर अनेक जग माहीं। एहि कहँ सिव तजि दूसर नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::418.verse_hindi: यदि तुम्हारी कन्या तप करे, तो त्रिपुरारि महादेवजी होनहार को मिटा सकते हैं। यद्यपि संसार में वर अनेक हैं, पर इसके लिए शिवजी को छोड़कर दूसरा वर नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::418.english_translation: If your daughter performs austerity, Tripurari can alter what is fated. Though many bridegrooms exist in the world, none but Shiva is fit for her.
ramacharitamanas::418.translation_literal: जौं (if) / तपु (austerity) / करै (does) / कुमारि (daughter) / तुम्हारी (your) / भाविउ (what is fated) / मेटि (erase) / सकहिं (can) / त्रिपुरारी (Tripurari/Shiva) / जद्यपि (although) / बर (grooms) / अनेक (many) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / एहि (for this one) / कहँ (for) / सिव (Shiva) / तजि (leaving) / दूसर (other) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::418.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::418.essence: Some unions are so fitting they seem to rewrite fate.
ramacharitamanas::418.simple_meaning: Shiva alone is the right match for this daughter, and his grace can overcome what seems fixed by fate.
ramacharitamanas::418.simple_insight: Rightful love is not random; it carries a depth that can change what looks fixed.
ramacharitamanas::418.detailed_meaning: In King Janak’s court, the bow contest is approaching, and the question of Sita’s bridegroom is being framed as a matter of destiny and fitness. The verse declares that Shiva alone truly suits her, hinting that this marriage is ordained beyond ordinary choice.
ramacharitamanas::418.modern_relevance: You meet someone and everyone has opinions, but one choice keeps feeling unmistakably right. This verse speaks to that quiet certainty that some bonds are not just convenient — they are fitting.
ramacharitamanas::418.insight: It shifts attention from social options to the deeper rightness of a bond.

ramacharitamanas::419.verse_sanskrit: बर दायक प्रनतारति भंजन। कृपासिंधु सेवक मन रंजन॥ इच्छित फल बिनु सिव अवराधें। लहिअ न कोटि जोग जप साधें ॥
ramacharitamanas::419.verse_hindi: शिवजी वर देने वाले, शरणागतों के दुःखों का नाश करने वाले, कृपा के समुद्र और सेवकों के मन को प्रसन्न करने वाले हैं। शिवजी की आराधना किए बिना करोड़ों योग और जप करने पर भी वांछित फल नहीं मिलता ॥
ramacharitamanas::419.english_translation: Shiva is the giver of boons, the remover of the suffering of those who seek refuge, an ocean of grace, and delight to his servants. Without worshipping Shiva, even millions of yogic practices and chants cannot bring the desired result.
ramacharitamanas::419.translation_literal: बर दायक (boon-giving) / प्रनतारति भंजन (destroyer of the suffering of the surrendered) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of grace) / सेवक मन रंजन (delighter of the minds of servants) / इच्छित फल (desired result) / बिनु (without) / सिव अवराधें (worshipping Shiva) / लहिअ न (is not obtained) / कोटि जोग (millions of yogic practices) / जप साधें (through chants and disciplines)
ramacharitamanas::419.speaker: Narada
ramacharitamanas::419.essence: Devotion opens what technique cannot reach.
ramacharitamanas::419.simple_meaning: Shiva is praised as the one who grants boons, removes suffering, and delights his devotees. The verse says that even endless spiritual practice cannot replace worship of him.
ramacharitamanas::419.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that devotion matters more than sheer effort.
ramacharitamanas::419.detailed_meaning: Narada is speaking in the Sita-swayamvar scene, explaining Shiva's greatness to Parvati. He says Shiva answers those who take refuge in him, and that no amount of ritual or discipline can substitute for that devoted relation.
ramacharitamanas::419.modern_relevance: You have done every technique, every checklist, every self-improvement hack, and still feel blocked. The verse says some doors open only through reverent relationship, not sheer technique.
ramacharitamanas::419.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to control outcomes through method alone to seeking the deeper source of blessing.

ramacharitamanas::420.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि नारद सुमिरि हरि गिरिजहि दीन्हि असीस। होइहि यह कल्यान अब संसय तजहु गिरीस ॥
ramacharitamanas::420.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर भगवान का स्मरण करके नारदजी ने पार्वती को आशीर्वाद दिया। (और कहा कि-) हे पर्वतराज! तुम संदेह का त्याग कर दो, अब यह कल्याण ही होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::420.english_translation: Having said this, Narada remembered Hari and blessed Girija. “This will bring welfare; O lord of the mountains, give up your doubt.”
ramacharitamanas::420.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (having said) / नारद (Narada) / सुमिरि (remembering) / हरि (Hari) / गिरिजहि (to Girija) / दीन्हि (gave) / असीस (blessing) / होइहि (will be) / यह (this) / कल्यान (welfare) / अब (now) / संसय (doubt) / तजहु (give up) / गिरीस (lord of the mountains)
ramacharitamanas::420.speaker: Narada
ramacharitamanas::420.essence: Blessing begins when doubt is released.
ramacharitamanas::420.simple_meaning: Narada blesses Parvati after remembering Hari and tells Shiva to let go of doubt. He assures them that what follows will be auspicious.
ramacharitamanas::420.simple_insight: Trust can calm uncertainty before the result is visible.
ramacharitamanas::420.detailed_meaning: After hearing the earlier exchange about Shiva as the only fitting bridegroom, Narada remembers Hari and gives Parvati a blessing. He then tells Girish to drop his doubt, because the coming turn in the story will bring good.
ramacharitamanas::420.modern_relevance: A friend texts, “I think this will work out,” right after the interview that felt shaky. You do not have proof yet, but the reassurance steadies your chest.
ramacharitamanas::420.insight: It shifts the mind from suspicion to trust in what is unfolding.

ramacharitamanas::421.verse_sanskrit: कहि अस ब्रह्मभवन मुनि गयऊ। आगिल चरित सुनहु जस भयऊ॥ पतिहि एकांत पाइ कह मैना। नाथ न मैं समुझे मुनि बैना ॥
ramacharitamanas::421.verse_hindi: यों कहकर नारद मुनि ब्रह्मलोक को चले गए। अब आगे जो चरित्र हुआ उसे सुनो। पति को एकान्त में पाकर मैना ने कहा- हे नाथ! मैंने मुनि के वचनों का अर्थ नहीं समझा ॥
ramacharitamanas::421.english_translation: Saying this, the sage Narada went to Brahmaloka. Hear now how the rest of the story unfolded. Finding her husband alone, Maina said, "Lord, I did not understand the sage's words."
ramacharitamanas::421.translation_literal: कहि (saying) / अस (thus) / ब्रह्मभवन (Brahma's abode) / मुनि (sage) / गयऊ (went) / आगिल (further / next) / चरित (deeds / story) / सुनहु (listen) / जस (as) / भयऊ (happened) / पतिहि (to husband) / एकांत (solitude) / पाइ (having obtained) / कह (said) / मैना (Maina) / नाथ (Lord) / न (not) / मैं (I) / समुझे (understood) / मुनि (sage's) / बैना (words)
ramacharitamanas::421.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::421.essence: Uncertainty after a sacred message becomes the doorway to the next teaching.
ramacharitamanas::421.simple_meaning: Narada leaves after speaking, and Maina tells her husband she did not understand the sage's words.
ramacharitamanas::421.simple_insight: Not every sacred word lands immediately; sometimes confusion opens the next step.
ramacharitamanas::421.detailed_meaning: Narada has just spoken to Shiva and Parvati, then departs to Brahmaloka. In the quiet that follows, Maina turns to her husband in private and admits she has not understood the sage's meaning. The next part of the story begins from that uncertainty.
ramacharitamanas::421.modern_relevance: A conversation ends, and you replay the last sentence in your head while the room goes quiet. You know something important was said, but the meaning has not settled yet.
ramacharitamanas::421.insight: It shifts attention from the speaker's departure to the listener's unresolved doubt, which drives the story forward.

ramacharitamanas::422.verse_sanskrit: जौं घरु बरु कुलु होइ अनूपा। करिअ बिबाहु सुता अनुरूपा॥ न त कन्या बरु रहउ कुआरी। कंत उमा मम प्रानपिआरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::422.verse_hindi: जो हमारी कन्या के अनुकूल घर, वर और कुल उत्तम हो तो विवाह कीजिए। नहीं तो लड़की चाहे कुमारी ही रहे (मैं अयोग्य वर के साथ उसका विवाह नहीं करना चाहती), क्योंकि हे स्वामिन् ! पार्वती मुझको प्राणों के समान प्यारी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::422.english_translation: If the house, groom, and family are excellent, arrange the marriage to a fitting daughter. Otherwise, let the daughter remain unmarried; Parvati is dear to me as my own life.
ramacharitamanas::422.translation_literal: जौं (if) / घरु (house) / बरु (groom) / कुलु (family) / होइ (becomes) / अनूपा (excellent) / करिअ (do) / बिबाहु (marriage) / सुता (daughter) / अनुरूपा (suitable) / न (not) / त (then) / कन्या (daughter) / बरु (better) / रहउ (remain) / कुआरी (unmarried) / कंत (husband/lord) / उमा (Parvati) / मम (my) / प्रानपिआरी (dear as life)
ramacharitamanas::422.speaker: Maina
ramacharitamanas::422.essence: Love refuses a match that would wound the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::422.simple_meaning: Maina says a daughter should marry only a truly suitable match. If no such match exists, it is better for her to remain unmarried than be joined badly.
ramacharitamanas::422.simple_insight: Love can be protective, not possessive. Sometimes the kindest choice is refusing a harmful arrangement.
ramacharitamanas::422.detailed_meaning: In Shiva and Parvati's family story, Maina speaks privately to her husband after Narad leaves. She wants only a worthy match for Parvati and refuses any marriage that would dishonour her daughter or bring lasting pain.
ramacharitamanas::422.modern_relevance: A parent reviews a proposal and feels the pressure to say yes quickly. Maina's stance is different: affection must still have standards, or it stops protecting the one you love.
ramacharitamanas::422.insight: It teaches you to value fit over haste, and to protect dignity even under social pressure.

ramacharitamanas::423.verse_sanskrit: जौं न मिलिहि बरु गिरिजहि जोगू। गिरि जड़ सहज कहिहि सबु लोगू॥ सोइ बिचारि पति करेहु बिबाहू। जेहिं न बहोरि होइ उर दाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::423.verse_hindi: यदि पार्वती के योग्य वर न मिला तो सब लोग कहेंगे कि पर्वत स्वभाव से ही जड़ (मूर्ख) होते हैं। हे स्वामी! इस बात को विचारकर ही विवाह कीजिएगा, जिसमें फिर पीछे हृदय में सन्ताप न हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::423.english_translation: If no suitable groom is found for Girija, everyone will call the mountains foolish by nature. Thinking of that, O lord, arrange the marriage only in a way that leaves no later sorrow in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::423.translation_literal: जौं (if) / न (not) / मिलिहि (is found) / बरु (groom) / गिरिजहि (for Girija) / जोगू (fit, suitable) / गिरि (mountain) / जड़ (inert, foolish) / सहज (by nature) / कहिहि (will say) / सबु (all) / लोगू (people) / सोइ (that) / बिचारि (thinking) / पति (husband, lord) / करेहु (do) / बिबाहू (marriage) / जेहिं (in which) / न (not) / बहोरि (again, later) / होइ (happens) / उर (heart) / दाहू (burning, sorrow)
ramacharitamanas::423.speaker: Maina
ramacharitamanas::423.essence: Choose so the heart has no reason to burn later.
ramacharitamanas::423.simple_meaning: Maina asks Shiva to arrange Parvati's marriage wisely, so no one can later mock the mountains and no regret will burn in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::423.simple_insight: Careful choices now can prevent a lifetime of regret later.
ramacharitamanas::423.detailed_meaning: Maina speaks privately to Shiva after Narada's warning. She is not chasing desire; she is trying to protect her daughter Parvati and her family’s honour. The marriage must be chosen so it will not turn into lasting sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::423.modern_relevance: A parent signs the papers, then lies awake replaying every clause and compromise. One rushed choice can echo for years; this verse asks for foresight before commitment.
ramacharitamanas::423.insight: It shifts the mind from immediate convenience to consequences that will return later.

ramacharitamanas::424.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि परी चरन धरि सीसा। बोले सहित सनेह गिरीसा॥ बरु पावक प्रगटै ससि माहीं। नारद बचनु अन्यथा नाहीं ॥
