ramacharitamanas::424.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार कहकर मैना पति के चरणों पर मस्तक रखकर गिर पड़ीं। तब हिमवान् ने प्रेम से कहा- चाहे चन्द्रमा में अग्नि प्रकट हो जाए, पर नारदजी के वचन झूठे नहीं हो सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::424.english_translation: Saying this, Maina fell at her husband's feet and bowed her head. Then Himavan said with love, "Even if fire appears in the moon, Narad's words cannot be false."
ramacharitamanas::424.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (having said) / परी (fell) / चरन (feet) / धरि (placing) / सीसा (head) / बोले (spoke) / सहित (with) / सनेह (love) / गिरीसा (Lord of the mountains) / बरु (even if) / पावक (fire) / प्रगटै (appears) / ससि (moon) / माहीं (in) / नाहीं (not) / नारद (Narad) / बचनु (words) / अन्यथा (false) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::424.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::424.essence: Faith holds firm when the mind cannot verify the outcome.
ramacharitamanas::424.simple_meaning: Maina bows in humility, and Himavan affirms that Narad's words are certain, even if they seem impossible.
ramacharitamanas::424.simple_insight: Trust steadies the heart when logic cannot yet see the way.
ramacharitamanas::424.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-Parvati wedding dialogue, Maina submits her concern at her husband's feet. Himavan answers with loving certainty that Narad's statement cannot be false, even if it seems as impossible as fire in the moon.
ramacharitamanas::424.modern_relevance: You are staring at a message from someone wiser than you, but the plan still looks impossible. This verse says: some guidance is worth trusting before it makes sense.
ramacharitamanas::424.insight: It shifts the mind from demanding proof to resting in trustworthy guidance.

ramacharitamanas::425.verse_sanskrit: प्रिया सोचु परिहरहु सबु सुमिरहु श्रीभगवान। पारबतिहि निरमयउ जेहिं सोइ करिहि कल्यान ॥
ramacharitamanas::425.verse_hindi: हे प्रिये! सब सोच छोड़कर श्री भगवान का स्मरण करो, जिन्होंने पार्वती को रचा है, वे ही कल्याण करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::425.english_translation: Beloved, let go of all worry and remember the Supreme Lord. The one who created Parvati will bring welfare.
ramacharitamanas::425.translation_literal: प्रिया (beloved) / सोचु (worry) / परिहरहु (give up) / सबु (all) / सुमिरहु (remember) / श्रीभगवान (the Supreme Lord) / पारबतिहि (Parvati) / निरमयउ (created) / जेहिं (who) / सोइ (that same one) / करिहि (will do) / कल्यान (welfare)
ramacharitamanas::425.speaker: Himavan
ramacharitamanas::425.essence: Trust the one who made her to protect her future.
ramacharitamanas::425.simple_meaning: Worry is unnecessary when the divine power that created Parvati is being remembered. Trust that same power to bring a good result.
ramacharitamanas::425.simple_insight: You do not have to carry every fear alone. Trust can soften panic into steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::425.detailed_meaning: Himavan and Maina are deciding how to honor Parvati's future. After Maina fears social shame if the marriage is not right, Himavan answers with faith: stop worrying and remember the Supreme Lord, who created Parvati and will ensure her welfare.
ramacharitamanas::425.modern_relevance: You are refreshing your phone for news about your child, your interview, your test. The mind keeps spinning. This verse asks for one clean move: stop feeding fear and place the outcome in higher hands.
ramacharitamanas::425.insight: It shifts attention from anxious prediction to trust in a greater order.

ramacharitamanas::426.verse_sanskrit: अब जौं तुम्हहि सुता पर नेहू। तौ अस जाइ सिखावनु देहू॥ करै सो तपु जेहिं मिलहिं महेसू। आन उपायँ न मिटिहि कलेसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::426.verse_hindi: अब यदि तुम्हें कन्या पर प्रेम है, तो जाकर उसे यह शिक्षा दो कि वह ऐसा तप करे, जिससे शिवजी मिल जाएँ। दूसरे उपाय से यह क्लेश नहीं मिटेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::426.english_translation: If you truly love your daughter, then teach her this: let her perform such tapas that she attains Shiva. No other means will end this sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::426.translation_literal: अब (now) / जौं (if) / तुम्हहि (to you) / सुता (daughter) / पर (for) / नेहू (love) / तौ (then) / अस (this) / जाइ (go) / सिखावनु (instruction) / देहू (give) / करै (may do) / सो (that) / तपु (austerity) / जेहिं (by which) / मिलहिं (may be attained) / महेसू (Shiva) / आन (other) / उपायँ (by means) / न (not) / मिटिहि (will end) / कलेसू (sorrow)
ramacharitamanas::426.speaker: Himavan
ramacharitamanas::426.essence: True love guides longing toward its rightful fulfillment.
ramacharitamanas::426.simple_meaning: Himavan says that if he truly loves his daughter, he should guide her toward the tapas that leads to Shiva. No other remedy can remove her sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::426.simple_insight: Real care does not just comfort pain; it points toward the one thing that can truly fulfill it.
ramacharitamanas::426.detailed_meaning: Parvati’s parents are speaking after her deep longing for Shiva becomes clear. Himavan tells Maina that love for their daughter should not stop at sympathy. It should help her toward the discipline that will unite her with Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::426.modern_relevance: Your friend is heartbroken over someone they cannot forget. You can offer distractions, or you can help them choose the one practice that actually changes their life.
ramacharitamanas::426.insight: It shifts support from soothing feelings to guiding someone toward the discipline that matches their deepest longing.

ramacharitamanas::427.verse_sanskrit: नारद बचन सगर्भ सहेतू। सुंदर सब गुन निधि बृषकेतू॥ अस बिचारि तुम्ह तजहु असंका। सबहि भाँति संकरु अकलंका ॥
ramacharitamanas::427.verse_hindi: नारदजी के वचन रहस्य से युक्त और सकारण हैं और शिवजी समस्त सुंदर गुणों के भण्डार हैं। यह विचारकर तुम (मिथ्या) संदेह को छोड़ दो। शिवजी सभी तरह से निष्कलंक हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::427.english_translation: Narad's words are meaningful and well-grounded. Shiva, the Bull-bannered one, is a treasure-house of all beautiful qualities. Thinking this way, you should abandon doubt. Shiva is flawless in every respect.
ramacharitamanas::427.translation_literal: नारद (Narad) / बचन (words) / सगर्भ (meaningful, with reason) / सहेतू (well-grounded) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सब (all) / गुन (qualities) / निधि (treasure-house) / बृषकेतू (Bull-bannered Shiva) ॥ / अस (thus) / बिचारि (thinking) / तुम्ह (you) / तजहु (abandon) / असंका (doubt) / सबहि भाँति (in every way) / संकरु (Shiva) / अकलंका (flawless) ॥
ramacharitamanas::427.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::427.essence: Doubt falls when character is seen clearly.
ramacharitamanas::427.simple_meaning: Narad's words are sincere and justified, and Shiva is full of noble qualities. So abandon doubt and trust Shiva's purity.
ramacharitamanas::427.simple_insight: Doubt softens when you remember the character of the one being questioned.
ramacharitamanas::427.detailed_meaning: In the Shiva-Parvati frame, Parvati's mother is still uncertain about Shiva's worth. Shiva answers by defending Narad's counsel and affirming Shiva's own spotless character, clearing away suspicion before Parvati approaches her daughter.
ramacharitamanas::427.modern_relevance: A friend warns you not to trust someone, but you know the person’s character from years of steady conduct. You stop feeding suspicion and look at the evidence of who they have always been.
ramacharitamanas::427.insight: It shifts the mind from suspicion to settled trust by recalling character, not gossip.

ramacharitamanas::428.verse_sanskrit: सुनि पति बचन हरषि मन माहीं। गई तुरत उठि गिरिजा पाहीं॥ उमहि बिलोकि नयन भरे बारी। सहित सनेह गोद बैठारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::428.verse_hindi: पति के वचन सुन मन में प्रसन्न होकर मैना उठकर तुरंत पार्वती के पास गईं। पार्वती को देखकर उनकी आँखों में आँसू भर आए। उसे स्नेह के साथ गोद में बैठा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::428.english_translation: Hearing her husband's words, Maina felt joy in her heart. She rose at once and went to Girija. Seeing Uma, tears filled her eyes. With affection, she seated her in her lap.
ramacharitamanas::428.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / पति (husband) / बचन (words) / हरषि (rejoicing) / मन (mind) / माहीं (within) / गई (went) / तुरत (immediately) / उठि (rising) / गिरिजा (Girija) / पाहीं (to the presence of)॥ / उमहि (Uma) / बिलोकि (seeing) / नयन (eyes) / भरे (filled) / बारी (with tears) / सहित (together with) / सनेह (affection) / गोद (lap) / बैठारी (seated)
ramacharitamanas::428.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::428.essence: Trust turns hesitation into tears and tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::428.simple_meaning: Maina hears her husband's words, feels glad, and goes at once to see Parvati. When she sees her daughter, tears come to her eyes and she holds her lovingly in her lap.
ramacharitamanas::428.simple_insight: Love moves quickly. Joy, tears, and tenderness can all live in the same moment.
ramacharitamanas::428.detailed_meaning: After hearing Shiva's reassuring words, Maina goes straight to Parvati. The tension of doubt softens into a mother's relief. This is a quiet family moment before the larger divine story moves forward.
ramacharitamanas::428.modern_relevance: You get a call that changes the mood of the whole house. One sentence from someone you trust, and the fear loosens before you even realize it.
ramacharitamanas::428.insight: It shifts attention from suspicion to affectionate reconnection, showing how trust restores warmth fast.

ramacharitamanas::429.verse_sanskrit: बारहिं बार लेति उर लाई। गदगद कंठ न कछु कहि जाई॥ जगत मातु सर्बग्य भवानी। मातु सुखद बोलीं मृदु बानी ॥ सुनहि मातु मैं दीख अस सपन सुनावउँ तोहि। सुंदर गौर सुबिप्रबर अस उपदेसेउ मोहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::429.verse_hindi: फिर बार-बार उसे हृदय से लगाने लगीं। प्रेम से मैना का गला भर आया, कुछ कहा नहीं जाता। जगज्जननी भवानीजी तो सर्वज्ञ ठहरीं। (माता के मन की दशा को जानकर) वे माता को सुख देने वाली कोमल वाणी से बोलीं- ॥ माँ! सुन, मैं तुझे सुनाती हूँ, मैंने ऐसा स्वप्न देखा है कि मुझे एक सुंदर गौरवर्ण श्रेष्ठ ब्राह्मण ने ऐसा उपदेश दिया है- ॥
ramacharitamanas::429.english_translation: Again and again she held her close to her heart. Her throat choked with love, and she could say nothing. Bhavani, the all-knowing mother of the world, then spoke gently to comfort her mother: “Listen, Mother. I will tell you a dream. A beautiful, fair Brahmin gave me this teaching.”
ramacharitamanas::429.translation_literal: बारहिं बार (again and again) / लेति (taking) / उर (heart) / लाई (brought close) / गदगद (choked with emotion) / कंठ (throat) / न (not) / कछु (anything) / कहि (saying) / जाई (can be said) / जगत मातु (mother of the world) / सर्बग्य (all-knowing) / भवानी (Bhavani) / मातु सुखद (giving comfort to the mother) / बोलीं (spoke) / मृदु बानी (soft words) / सुनहि (listen) / मातु (Mother) / मैं (I) / दीख (saw) / अस (such) / सपन (dream) / सुनावउँ (I will tell) / तोहि (to you) / सुंदर (beautiful) / गौर (fair) / सुबिप्रबर (best Brahmin) / अस (such) / उपदेसेउ (gave teaching) / मोहि (to me)
ramacharitamanas::429.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::429.essence: Gentle reassurance prepares the heart for truth.
ramacharitamanas::429.simple_meaning: Parvati comforts her mother with gentle words and begins to explain a dream in which a noble Brahmin gave her a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::429.simple_insight: Love can steady grief enough for wisdom to enter.
ramacharitamanas::429.detailed_meaning: After Shiva’s hint, Parvati’s mother is overwhelmed with emotion and holds her close. Parvati, called Bhavani and the world’s mother, answers with tenderness. She begins recounting the dream that will lead to the sacred instruction about tapas.
ramacharitamanas::429.modern_relevance: You sit beside a parent who is upset, holding their hand while your own voice shakes. Before advice can help, care has to soften the room.
ramacharitamanas::429.insight: It shows that reassurance opens the way for guidance; tenderness comes before instruction.

ramacharitamanas::430.verse_sanskrit: करहि जाइ तपु सैलकुमारी। नारद कहा सो सत्य बिचारी॥ मातु पितहि पुनि यह मत भावा। तपु सुखप्रद दुख दोष नसावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::430.verse_hindi: हे पार्वती! नारदजी ने जो कहा है, उसे सत्य समझकर तू जाकर तप कर। फिर यह बात तेरे माता-पिता को भी अच्छी लगी है। तप सुख देने वाला और दुःख-दोष का नाश करने वाला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::430.english_translation: O daughter of the mountain, go and perform austerity, taking Narada's words as true. Your parents also approve this counsel. Austerity brings ease and destroys suffering and flaws.
ramacharitamanas::430.translation_literal: करहि (do) / जाइ (going) / तपु (austerity) / सैलकुमारी (daughter of the mountain) / नारद (Narada) / कहा (said) / सो (that) / सत्य (true) / बिचारी (considering) / मातु पितहि (to mother and father) / पुनि (also) / यह (this) / मत (opinion/counsel) / भावा (pleased) / तपु (austerity) / सुखप्रद (giver of ease) / दुख (sorrow) / दोष (faults) / नसावा (destroys)
ramacharitamanas::430.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::430.essence: Austerity clears suffering and strengthens the life within.
ramacharitamanas::430.simple_meaning: Parvati is told to accept Narada's advice and go do austerity. Her parents agree, and the verse praises austerity as something that brings ease and removes suffering and flaws.
ramacharitamanas::430.simple_insight: Real discipline can feel demanding, yet it clears the heart and steadies the mind.
ramacharitamanas::430.detailed_meaning: Parvati has just heard her mother's loving concern, and now the guidance turns practical. The counsel is to trust Narada, accept the family’s approval, and begin tapas. This verse prepares the way for the larger teaching on the power of disciplined effort.
ramacharitamanas::430.modern_relevance: You know that moment when a mentor's hard advice finally lands, and even your family quietly agrees? This is that turning point: stop circling the decision and begin the practice.
ramacharitamanas::430.insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to sustained practice, treating discipline as cleansing rather than punishment.

ramacharitamanas::431.verse_sanskrit: तपबल रचइ प्रपंचु बिधाता। तपबल बिष्नु सकल जग त्राता॥ तपबल संभु करहिं संघारा। तपबल सेषु धरइ महिभारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::431.verse_hindi: तप के बल से ही ब्रह्मा संसार को रचते हैं और तप के बल से ही बिष्णु सारे जगत का पालन करते हैं। तप के बल से ही शम्भु (रुद्र रूप से) जगत का संहार करते हैं और तप के बल से ही शेषजी पृथ्वी का भार धारण करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::431.english_translation: By the power of tapas, the Creator creates the world. By the power of tapas, Vishnu protects the whole world. By the power of tapas, Shiva destroys. By the power of tapas, Shesha bears the weight of the earth.
ramacharitamanas::431.translation_literal: तपबल (power of tapas) / रचइ (creates) / प्रपंचु (the world) / बिधाता (the Creator) / तपबल (power of tapas) / बिष्नु (Vishnu) / सकल (whole) / जग (world) / त्राता (protector) / तपबल (power of tapas) / संभु (Shiva) / करहिं (do) / संघारा (destruction) / तपबल (power of tapas) / सेषु (Shesha) / धरइ (bears) / महिभारा (the earth's burden)
ramacharitamanas::431.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::431.essence: Tapas is the hidden power behind every great act.
ramacharitamanas::431.simple_meaning: Disciplined effort is shown as the force behind all cosmic functions: creation, protection, destruction, and support. The verse praises tapas as the energy that makes everything possible.
ramacharitamanas::431.simple_insight: Real power is not random talent; it is sustained discipline that can carry huge responsibility.
ramacharitamanas::431.detailed_meaning: Parvati has just been urged to go and practice tapas. To make that instruction feel undeniable, the verse expands the idea: Brahma creates, Vishnu preserves, Shiva dissolves, and Shesha supports the earth through tapas. The whole cosmos is presented as disciplined effort in action.
ramacharitamanas::431.modern_relevance: You keep showing up before dawn while everyone else sleeps, training for a race or caring for a sick parent. What looks ordinary is what holds the whole day together.
ramacharitamanas::431.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing discipline as sacrifice to seeing it as the hidden force that sustains everything.

ramacharitamanas::432.verse_sanskrit: तप अधार सब सृष्टि भवानी। करहि जाइ तपु अस जियँ जानी॥ सुनत बचन बिसमित महतारी। सपन सुनायउ गिरिहि हँकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::432.verse_hindi: हे भवानी! सारी सृष्टि तप के ही आधार पर है। ऐसा जी में जानकर तू जाकर तप कर। यह बात सुनकर माता को बड़ा अचरज हुआ और उसने हिमवान् को बुलाकर वह स्वप्न सुनाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::432.english_translation: O Bhavani, all creation rests on tapas. Knowing this in your heart, go and perform tapas. Hearing these words, the mother was astonished and called Himalaya, then told him the dream.
ramacharitamanas::432.translation_literal: तप (austerity) / अधार (basis) / सब (all) / सृष्टि (creation) / भवानी (Bhavani) / करहि (do) / जाइ (go) / तपु (austerity) / अस (thus) / जियँ (in heart) / जानी (knowing) / सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words) / बिसमित (astonished) / महतारी (mother) / सपन (dream) / सुनायउ (told) / गिरिहि (to Himalaya) / हँकारी (calling out)
ramacharitamanas::432.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::432.essence: Creation itself depends on disciplined effort.
ramacharitamanas::432.simple_meaning: Tapas is presented as the basis of creation, and Parvati is urged to undertake it. Her mother is amazed by the message and tells Himalaya about the dream.
ramacharitamanas::432.simple_insight: Great longing is not random; it asks for discipline before it becomes fruit.
ramacharitamanas::432.detailed_meaning: In Shiva's telling of Parvati's story, the message comes that all creation rests on tapas, so Parvati must go and practice it. Her mother is startled by the command and rushes to tell Himalaya the dream.
ramacharitamanas::432.modern_relevance: A parent hears their child say, with total certainty, that a hard path is calling them. The room goes still. What looks like delay is actually the preparation for a life-changing calling.
ramacharitamanas::432.insight: It frames discipline as the hidden support of all becoming, not a punishment or side task.

ramacharitamanas::433.verse_sanskrit: मातु पितहि बहुबिधि समुझाई। चलीं उमा तप हित हरषाई॥ प्रिय परिवार पिता अरु माता। भए बिकल मुख आव न बाता ॥ बेदसिरा मुनि आइ तब सबहि कहा समुझाइ। पारबती महिमा सुनत रहे प्रबोधहि पाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::433.verse_hindi: माता-पिता को बहुत तरह से समझाकर बड़े हर्ष के साथ पार्वतीजी तप करने के लिए चलीं। प्यारे कुटुम्बी, पिता और माता सब व्याकुल हो गए। किसी के मुँह से बात नहीं निकलती ॥ तब वेदशिरा मुनि ने आकर सबको समझाकर कहा। पार्वतीजी की महिमा सुनकर सबको समाधान हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::433.english_translation: After reassuring her parents in many ways, Uma joyfully set out to do tapas. Her dear family, father, and mother were all distraught; no one could speak. Then the sage Vedashira came and explained everything to them, and hearing of Parvati's greatness, they were comforted.
ramacharitamanas::433.translation_literal: मातु पितहि (to mother and father) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / समुझाई (having explained) / चलीं (went) / उमा (Uma) / तप हित (for tapas) / हरषाई (with joy) / प्रिय परिवार (dear family) / पिता अरु माता (father and mother) / भए (became) / बिकल (distressed) / मुख (mouth) / आव (comes) / न (not) / बाता (speech) / बेदसिरा (Vedashira) / मुनि (sage) / आइ (having come) / तब (then) / सबहि (to everyone) / कहा (said) / समुझाइ (explaining) / पारबती (Parvati) / महिमा (greatness) / सुनत (hearing) / रहे (remained) / प्रबोधहि (comforted) / पाइ (having obtained)
ramacharitamanas::433.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::433.essence: A worthy discipline can wound the family that loves you.
ramacharitamanas::433.simple_meaning: Parvati leaves for austerity after reassuring her parents, while her family grieves until a sage consoles them by explaining her greatness.
ramacharitamanas::433.simple_insight: Choosing a demanding path can hurt the people who love you, even when the choice is right.
ramacharitamanas::433.detailed_meaning: After Shiva's instruction, Parvati prepares to leave home for tapas. She explains herself to her parents, but their hearts break at her departure. Vedashira arrives and calms the family by revealing the greatness behind her choice.
ramacharitamanas::433.modern_relevance: You accept a fellowship overseas, and your parents go silent at the dinner table. You know the choice is right, but you also feel the cost. This verse understands both sides.
ramacharitamanas::433.insight: It shows that discipline can require leaving comfort behind, and that others may need time to understand the sacrifice.

ramacharitamanas::434.verse_sanskrit: उर धरि उमा प्रानपति चरना। जाइ बिपिन लागीं तपु करना॥ अति सुकुमार न तनु तप जोगू। पति पद सुमिरि तजेउ सबु भोगू ॥
ramacharitamanas::434.verse_hindi: प्राणपति (शिवजी) के चरणों को हृदय में धारण करके पार्वतीजी वन में जाकर तप करने लगीं। पार्वतीजी का अत्यन्त सुकुमार शरीर तप के योग्य नहीं था, तो भी पति के चरणों का स्मरण करके उन्होंने सब भोगों को तज दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::434.english_translation: Holding the feet of her lord in her heart, Uma went into the forest to practice austerity. Her body was very delicate and unsuited for austerity, yet remembering her husband's feet, she gave up all pleasures.
ramacharitamanas::434.translation_literal: उर धरि (holding in the heart) / उमा (Uma) / प्रानपति (lord of life) / चरना (feet) / जाइ (going) / बिपिन (forest) / लागीं (began) / तपु करना (to do austerity) / अति (very) / सुकुमार (delicate) / न तनु (the body not) / तप जोगू (fit for austerity) / पति पद (husband's feet) / सुमिरि (remembering) / तजेउ (gave up) / सबु भोगू (all pleasures)
ramacharitamanas::434.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::434.essence: Remembrance of the beloved makes hardship bearable.
ramacharitamanas::434.simple_meaning: Uma leaves comfort behind and goes into the forest to practice austerity, keeping Shiva in her heart. Though her body is delicate, her devotion makes her give up every pleasure.
ramacharitamanas::434.simple_insight: Love can make sacrifice feel natural, even when the body resists.
ramacharitamanas::434.detailed_meaning: Parvati, now fully resolved, enters the forest to begin her long austerity for Shiva. The poem stresses the mismatch between her delicate body and the harsh practice ahead, making her choice feel all the more powerful.
ramacharitamanas::434.modern_relevance: You cancel the soft weekend plans, turn off the phone, and sit with the hard thing you keep avoiding. What carries you is not toughness, but love for what matters.
ramacharitamanas::434.insight: It shifts the mind from comfort-seeking to disciplined remembrance of what you value most.

ramacharitamanas::435.verse_sanskrit: नित नव चरन उपज अनुरागा। बिसरी देह तपहिं मनु लागा॥ संबत सहस मूल फल खाए। सागु खाइ सत बरष गवाँए ॥
ramacharitamanas::435.verse_hindi: स्वामी के चरणों में नित्य नया अनुराग उत्पन्न होने लगा और तप में ऐसा मन लगा कि शरीर की सारी सुध बिसर गई। एक हजार वर्ष तक उन्होंने मूल और फल खाए, फिर सौ वर्ष साग खाकर बिताए ॥
ramacharitamanas::435.english_translation: A fresh love for the lotus feet kept rising every day, and the mind became absorbed in austerity until the body was forgotten. For a thousand years they lived on roots and fruits, then spent a hundred years eating only greens.
ramacharitamanas::435.translation_literal: नित (every day) / नव (new) / चरन (feet) / उपज (arose) / अनुरागा (love) / बिसरी (forgot) / देह (body) / तपहिं (in austerity) / मनु (mind) / लागा (became engaged) / संबत (years) / सहस (thousand) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruits) / खाए (ate) / सागु (greens) / खाइ (eating) / सत (hundred) / बरष (years) / गवाँए (spent)
ramacharitamanas::435.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::435.simple_meaning: Parvati's devotion keeps deepening. She becomes so absorbed in penance that she forgets her body and lives for years on very simple food.
ramacharitamanas::435.simple_insight: Love can make hardship feel light when the heart is fixed on what matters.
ramacharitamanas::435.detailed_meaning: Parvati has gone into the forest to win Shiva through severe tapas. Her devotion keeps renewing itself each day, and the austerity becomes so total that bodily comfort drops out of awareness. This verse adds the long duration of her practice.
ramacharitamanas::435.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for a hard practice long after the novelty is gone — the run, the study session, the caregiving shift — because something deeper than comfort now drives you.
ramacharitamanas::435.insight: It shifts the mind from measuring discomfort to sustaining devotion through repetition.

ramacharitamanas::436.verse_sanskrit: कछु दिन भोजनु बारि बतासा। किए कठिन कछु दिन उपबासा॥ बेल पाती महि परइ सुखाई। तीनि सहस संबत सोइ खाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::436.verse_hindi: कुछ दिन जल और वायु का भोजन किया और फिर कुछ दिन कठोर उपवास किए, जो बेल पत्र सूखकर पृथ्वी पर गिरते थे, तीन हजार वर्ष तक उन्हीं को खाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::436.english_translation: For some days she lived on water and air; for some days she kept a hard fast. When bel leaves dried and fell to the ground, she ate only those for three thousand years.
ramacharitamanas::436.translation_literal: कछु दिन (for some days) / भोजनु (food) / बारि (water) / बतासा (air) / किए (did) / कठिन (hard) / कछु दिन (for some days) / उपबासा (fasting) / बेल पाती (bel leaves) / महि (on the earth) / परइ (fell) / सुखाई (dried) / तीनि सहस (three thousand) / संबत (years) / सोइ (those very) / खाई (ate)
ramacharitamanas::436.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::436.essence: Steady restraint can become a force stronger than appetite.
ramacharitamanas::436.simple_meaning: Parvati kept intensifying her austerity: first water and air, then hard fasting, then only dried bel leaves for three thousand years.
ramacharitamanas::436.simple_insight: Real devotion can be so steady that comfort stops mattering.
ramacharitamanas::436.detailed_meaning: Parvati is deep in the forest, trying to win Shiva through severe tapas. After water, air, and hard fasting, she survives on dried bel leaves for three thousand years. This verse shows the relentless discipline that prepares the next transformation.
ramacharitamanas::436.modern_relevance: You keep showing up before sunrise while everyone else sleeps, repeating the same practice until it changes you. Progress often looks like this: quiet, severe, and invisible.
ramacharitamanas::436.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic effort to sustained restraint over time.

ramacharitamanas::437.verse_sanskrit: पुनि परिहरे सुखानेउ परना। उमहि नामु तब भयउ अपरना॥ देखि उमहि तप खीन सरीरा। ब्रह्मगिरा भै गगन गभीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::437.verse_hindi: फिर सूखे पर्ण (पत्ते) भी छोड़ दिए, तभी पार्वती का नाम 'अपर्णा' हुआ। तप से उमा का शरीर क्षीण देखकर आकाश से गंभीर ब्रह्मवाणी हुई- ॥
ramacharitamanas::437.english_translation: She even gave up dry leaves. Then Uma became Aparna. Seeing Uma's body weakened by austerity, a grave voice from the sky spoke.
ramacharitamanas::437.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / परिहरे (gave up) / सुखानेउ (dried) / परना (leaves) / उमहि (to Uma) / नामु (name) / तब (then) / भयउ (became) / अपरना (Aparna) / देखि (seeing) / उमहि (Uma) / तप (austerity) / खीन (worn thin) / सरीरा (body) / ब्रह्मगिरा (voice of Brahma) / भै (became) / गगन (sky) / गभीरा (deep)
ramacharitamanas::437.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::437.essence: Total devotion can become a new identity.
ramacharitamanas::437.simple_meaning: Uma gives up even dry leaves as food. Because of this extreme austerity, she becomes known as Aparna, and a deep heavenly voice speaks when her body grows frail.
ramacharitamanas::437.simple_insight: True longing can strip away comfort completely, yet still remain steady.
ramacharitamanas::437.detailed_meaning: Uma has already endured years of severe tapas in the forest. She now gives up even dry leaves, earning the name Aparna. Seeing her body grow thin, the sky itself answers with a grave divine voice, setting up the promise that her devotion has reached its fulfillment.
ramacharitamanas::437.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for something that matters, even when comfort is gone and your energy is low. The name changes when the commitment becomes complete.
ramacharitamanas::437.insight: It shows that devotion can become so total that even self-denial turns into identity.

ramacharitamanas::438.verse_sanskrit: भयउ मनोरथ सुफल तव सुनु गिरिराजकुमारि। परिहरु दुसह कलेस सब अब मिलिहहिं त्रिपुरारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::438.verse_hindi: हे पर्वतराज की कुमारी! सुन, तेरा मनोरथ सफल हुआ। तू अब सारे असह्य क्लेशों को (कठिन तप को) त्याग दे। अब तुझे शिवजी मिलेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::438.english_translation: O daughter of the mountain king, listen: your wish has borne fruit. Give up all unbearable hardship now. Shiva will meet you.
ramacharitamanas::438.translation_literal: भयउ (has become) / मनोरथ (wish) / सुफल (fruitful) / तव (your) / सुनु (listen) / गिरिराजकुमारि (daughter of the mountain king) / परिहरु (give up) / दुसह (unbearable) / कलेस (hardship) / सब (all) / अब (now) / मिलिहहिं (will meet) / त्रिपुरारि (Shiva, enemy of Tripura)
ramacharitamanas::438.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::438.essence: Your longing has ripened; now release the strain.
ramacharitamanas::438.simple_meaning: Parvati is told that her long penance has succeeded, and she can stop the severe hardship because Shiva will now come to her.
ramacharitamanas::438.simple_insight: Patient longing can ripen into fulfillment without forcing it.
ramacharitamanas::438.detailed_meaning: Parvati has endured fierce austerity on the mountain. Shiva's voice now answers her effort: the wish behind her tapas has matured, and the burden can fall away because the union she sought is at hand.
ramacharitamanas::438.modern_relevance: You keep showing up before dawn, training for months, and nothing seems to move. Then the moment comes when the work quietly opens its own door.
ramacharitamanas::438.insight: It teaches that sincere effort can reach a point where the outcome arrives on its own.

ramacharitamanas::439.verse_sanskrit: अस तपु काहुँ न कीन्ह भवानी। भए अनेक धीर मुनि ग्यानी॥ अब उर धरहु ब्रह्म बर बानी। सत्य सदा संतत सुचि जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::439.verse_hindi: हे भवानी! धीर, मुनि और ज्ञानी बहुत हुए हैं, पर ऐसा (कठोर) तप किसी ने नहीं किया। अब तू इस श्रेष्ठ ब्रह्मा की वाणी को सदा सत्य और निरंतर पवित्र जानकर अपने हृदय में धारण कर ॥
ramacharitamanas::439.english_translation: Bhavani, no one has performed austerity like this. Many steadfast sages and knowers have existed. Keep this supreme word of Brahma in your heart, knowing it always true and pure.
ramacharitamanas::439.translation_literal: अस (such) / तपु (austerity) / काहुँ (by anyone) / न (not) / कीन्ह (done) / भवानी (Bhavani) / भए (became) / अनेक (many) / धीर (steadfast) / मुनि (sages) / ग्यानी (knowers) / अब (now) / उर (heart) / धरहु (hold) / ब्रह्म (Brahma) / बर (excellent) / बानी (word) / सत्य (true) / सदा (always) / संतत (continuous) / सुचि (pure) / जानी (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::439.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::439.essence: Rare effort must be met with steady trust.
ramacharitamanas::439.simple_meaning: No one has done austerity like this before. Brahma's word should be held in the heart as always true and pure.
ramacharitamanas::439.simple_insight: Deep effort deserves a steady heart that can receive the answer without doubt.
ramacharitamanas::439.detailed_meaning: Parvati has endured severe tapas in the mountains, and the divine voice now answers her. The speaker praises the rarity of her effort, then tells her to trust Brahma's promise and carry it in her heart, because the long waiting is about to bear fruit.
ramacharitamanas::439.modern_relevance: You have pushed through months of practice, waiting, and uncertainty, and then the guidance finally arrives. The harder part now is not effort — it's trusting the answer enough to let it land.
ramacharitamanas::439.insight: It shifts attention from proving your effort to receiving confirmation with trust.

ramacharitamanas::440.verse_sanskrit: आवै पिता बोलावन जबहीं। हठ परिहरि घर जाएहु तबहीं॥ मिलहिं तुम्हहि जब सप्त रिषीसा। जानेहु तब प्रमान बागीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::440.verse_hindi: जब तेरे पिता बुलाने को आवें, तब हठ छोड़कर घर चली जाना और जब तुम्हें सप्तर्षि मिलें तब इस वाणी को ठीक समझना ॥
ramacharitamanas::440.english_translation: When your father calls you, then leave your stubbornness and go home. When you meet the seven great sages, then know this speech to be true.
ramacharitamanas::440.translation_literal: आवै (comes) / पिता (father) / बोलावन (for calling) / जबहीं (when) / हठ (stubbornness) / परिहरि (leaving aside) / घर (home) / जाएहु (go) / तबहीं (then) / मिलहिं (meet) / तुम्हहि (you) / जब (when) / सप्त (seven) / रिषीसा (great sages) / जानेहु (know) / तब (then) / प्रमान (proof) / बागीसा (speech of the lord of speech)
ramacharitamanas::440.speaker: Brahma
ramacharitamanas::440.essence: Truth ripens in stages; stubbornness must yield before confirmation arrives.
ramacharitamanas::440.simple_meaning: Parvati is told to stop resisting, return home when her father calls, and trust the message when the seven sages confirm it.
ramacharitamanas::440.simple_insight: Sometimes the next right step is to stop arguing with reality and let confirmation arrive.
ramacharitamanas::440.detailed_meaning: Parvati has endured severe tapas for Shiva. Brahma’s voice now reassures her that her wish will be fulfilled, but not recklessly: first she must respond to her father’s call, then wait for the seven sages to confirm the truth. The verse guides her out of stubbornness and into trust.
ramacharitamanas::440.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone, waiting for someone to finally confirm what you already feel. This verse says: stop forcing it, go home, and let reality answer in its own time.
ramacharitamanas::440.insight: It shifts the mind from forcing certainty to recognizing the right timing of confirmation.

ramacharitamanas::441.verse_sanskrit: सुनत गिरा बिधि गगन बखानी। पुलक गात गिरिजा हरषानी॥ उमा चरित सुंदर मैं गावा। सुनहु संभु कर चरित सुहावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::441.verse_hindi: (इस प्रकार) आकाश से कही हुई ब्रह्मा की वाणी को सुनते ही पार्वतीजी प्रसन्न हो गईं और (हर्ष के मारे) उनका शरीर पुलकित हो गया। (याज्ञवल्क्यजी भरद्वाजजी से बोले कि-) मैंने पार्वती का सुंदर चरित्र सुनाया, अब शिवजी का सुहावना चरित्र सुनो ॥
ramacharitamanas::441.english_translation: Hearing the voice spoken from the sky, Parvati rejoiced, and her body thrilled with joy. "I have sung the lovely story of Uma; now listen to the graceful story of Shiva."
ramacharitamanas::441.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / गिरा (speech, voice) / बिधि (Brahma) / गगन (sky) / बखानी (spoken, proclaimed) / पुलक (horripilation, thrill) / गात (body) / गिरिजा (Parvati) / हरषानी (rejoiced) / उमा (Uma, Parvati) / चरित (story, conduct) / सुंदर (beautiful) / मैं (I) / गावा (sung, narrated) / सुनहु (listen) / संभु (Shiva) / कर (of) / चरित (story, conduct) / सुहावा (graceful, pleasing)
ramacharitamanas::441.speaker: Yajnavalkya
ramacharitamanas::441.essence: Joy at confirmation opens the way to the next teaching.
ramacharitamanas::441.simple_meaning: Parvati is delighted when she hears Brahma's message from the sky. Yajnavalkya then shifts from Uma's story to Shiva's story.
ramacharitamanas::441.simple_insight: Joy opens the heart to the next truth.
ramacharitamanas::441.detailed_meaning: In the frame dialogue, Brahma's sky-voice has just confirmed Parvati's vow. Parvati feels delight and goosebumps. Yajnavalkya pauses, says he has finished Uma's beautiful story, and prepares Bharadvaja to hear Shiva's story next.
ramacharitamanas::441.modern_relevance: You finally hear the answer you were waiting for after a long stretch of uncertainty. Relief arrives first; only then does the next part of the story become possible.
ramacharitamanas::441.insight: It marks a transition from Parvati's testing to Shiva's deeper story.

ramacharitamanas::442.verse_sanskrit: जब तें सतीं जाइ तनु त्यागा। तब तें सिव मन भयउ बिरागा॥ जपहिं सदा रघुनायक नामा। जहँ तहँ सुनहिं राम गुन ग्रामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::442.verse_hindi: जब से सती ने जाकर शरीर त्याग किया, तब से शिवजी के मन में वैराग्य हो गया। वे सदा श्री रघुनाथजी का नाम जपने लगे और जहाँ-तहाँ श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुणों की कथाएँ सुनने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::442.english_translation: Since Sati abandoned her body, Shiva's mind turned away from worldly attachment. He always chanted the name of Raghunath and listened everywhere to the stories of Ram's virtues.
ramacharitamanas::442.translation_literal: जब तें (since) / सतीं (Sati) / जाइ (having gone) / तनु (body) / त्यागा (abandoned) / तब तें (from then on) / सिव (Shiva) / मन (mind) / भयउ (became) / बिरागा (detached) / जपहिं (chant) / सदा (always) / रघुनायक (Raghunath) / नामा (name) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / सुनहिं (hear) / राम (Ram) / गुन (virtues) / ग्रामा (tales)
ramacharitamanas::442.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::442.essence: Loss can strip attachment and deepen remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::442.simple_meaning: After Sati left her body, Shiva became detached from worldly attachment. He kept repeating Ram's name and listening to Ram's stories everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::442.simple_insight: Loss can become a doorway to deeper devotion instead of bitterness.
ramacharitamanas::442.detailed_meaning: After Sati's departure, Shiva is shown in a new inner state. The shock of loss does not harden him; it loosens worldly attachment and turns him toward Ram's name and praise. This verse marks that inward turning.
ramacharitamanas::442.modern_relevance: A relationship ends, and instead of spiraling into replaying the hurt, you begin walking, breathing, and returning to what steadies you. Grief can either trap you or redirect you.
ramacharitamanas::442.insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to remembrance and devotional listening.

ramacharitamanas::443.verse_sanskrit: चिदानंद सुखधाम सिव बिगत मोह मद काम। बिचरहिं महि धरि हृदयँ हरि सकल लोक अभिराम ॥
ramacharitamanas::443.verse_hindi: चिदानन्द, सुख के धाम, मोह, मद और काम से रहित शिवजी सम्पूर्ण लोकों को आनंद देने वाले भगवान श्री हरि (श्री रामचन्द्रजी) को हृदय में धारण कर (भगवान के ध्यान में मस्त हुए) पृथ्वी पर विचरने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::443.english_translation: Shiva, the abode of bliss and consciousness, free from delusion, pride, and desire, wandered the earth with Ram in his heart, delighting all the worlds.
ramacharitamanas::443.translation_literal: चिदानंद (bliss and consciousness) / सुखधाम (abode of joy) / सिव (Shiva) / बिगत (free from) / मोह (delusion) / मद (pride) / काम (desire) / बिचरहिं (wandered) / महि (on the earth) / धरि (holding) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / हरि (Ram) / सकल (all) / लोक (worlds) / अभिराम (delighting)
ramacharitamanas::443.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::443.essence: A heart filled with Ram turns presence itself into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::443.simple_meaning: Shiva, free from delusion, pride, and desire, walked the earth with Ram held in his heart, bringing joy to all beings.
ramacharitamanas::443.simple_insight: When the heart is full of Ram, even ordinary movement becomes a blessing to others.
ramacharitamanas::443.detailed_meaning: After Sati's departure, Shiva has turned inward and lives in remembrance of Ram. This verse shows him as detached yet radiant, wandering the world with Ram in his heart. His presence itself now gives joy, and the next verse expands on how he teaches and sings Ram's praise.
ramacharitamanas::443.modern_relevance: You meet someone who has stopped needing attention, status, or validation. They still move through the world, but their calm changes the atmosphere around them.
ramacharitamanas::443.insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to a lived presence that quietly benefits everyone nearby.

ramacharitamanas::444.verse_sanskrit: कतहुँ मुनिन्ह उपदेसहिं ग्याना। कतहुँ राम गुन करहिं बखाना॥ जदपि अकाम तदपि भगवाना। भगत बिरह दुख दुखित सुजाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::444.verse_hindi: वे कहीं मुनियों को ज्ञान का उपदेश करते और कहीं श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुणों का वर्णन करते थे। यद्यपि सुजान शिवजी निष्काम हैं, तो भी वे भगवान अपने भक्त (सती) के वियोग के दुःख से दुःखी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::444.english_translation: He taught wisdom to the sages here and praised Ram's virtues there. Though Shiva is desireless, he still feels the sorrow of separation from his devotee.
ramacharitamanas::444.translation_literal: कतहुँ (here and there) / मुनिन्ह (to the sages) / उपदेसहिं (they teach) / ग्याना (wisdom) / कतहुँ (here and there) / राम (Ram) / गुन (virtues) / करहिं (they do) / बखाना (praise) / जदपि (although) / अकाम (desireless) / तदपि (still) / भगवाना (the divine one) / भगत (devotee) / बिरह (separation) / दुख (pain) / दुखित (made sorrowful) / सुजाना (the wise one)
ramacharitamanas::444.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::444.essence: True detachment still feels the wound of loving separation.
ramacharitamanas::444.simple_meaning: Shiva spends his time teaching sages and praising Ram, yet he still feels pain when separated from his devotee.
ramacharitamanas::444.simple_insight: Love can remain pure and still ache. Detachment does not cancel tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::444.detailed_meaning: After Sati's departure, Shiva wanders the world in quiet devotion. He teaches sages and sings Ram's praise, but his heart still feels the wound of separation. This verse shows that even the desireless one is moved by bhakti.
ramacharitamanas::444.modern_relevance: You can be composed in public, giving guidance to others, while still carrying a private ache for someone you love. Strength does not erase tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::444.insight: It shifts devotion from a ritual act to a living bond that can feel absence.

ramacharitamanas::445.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि गयउ कालु बहु बीती। नित नै होइ राम पद प्रीती॥ नेमु प्रेमु संकर कर देखा। अबिचल हृदयँ भगति कै रेखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::445.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार बहुत समय बीत गया। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में नित नई प्रीति हो रही है। शिवजी के (कठोर) नियम, (अनन्य) प्रेम और उनके हृदय में भक्ति की अटल टेक को (जब श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने) देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::445.english_translation: In this way, much time passed, and Shiva's love for Ram's feet grew ever new. When Ram saw Shiva's vow, love, and the unbroken line of devotion in his heart...
ramacharitamanas::445.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / गयउ (passed) / कालु (time) / बहु (much) / बीती (passed) / नित (daily) / नै (new) / होइ (becomes) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / प्रीती (love) / नेमु (vow / discipline) / प्रेमु (love) / संकर (Shiva) / कर (of) / देखा (saw) / अबिचल (unshaken) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / भगति (devotion) / कै (of) / रेखा (line / mark)
ramacharitamanas::445.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::445.essence: Time tests devotion and makes it more alive.
ramacharitamanas::445.simple_meaning: Time passes, but Shiva's love for Ram only deepens. Ram sees Shiva's steady vow, loving heart, and unbroken devotion.
ramacharitamanas::445.simple_insight: Steady love does not fade with time; it grows stronger through repetition.
ramacharitamanas::445.detailed_meaning: Shiva has been living in devotion, speaking of Ram, teaching others, and holding Ram in his heart. As time passes, that love keeps becoming fresh. In this moment, Ram notices the firmness of Shiva's vow and the unbroken line of devotion within him.
ramacharitamanas::445.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone or something long after the first excitement is gone. The feeling is no longer new, but the bond has become deeper, steadier, and harder to break.
ramacharitamanas::445.insight: It shifts attention from intensity to constancy, showing that devotion matures through repetition.

ramacharitamanas::446.verse_sanskrit: प्रगटे रामु कृतग्य कृपाला। रूप सील निधि तेज बिसाला॥ बहु प्रकार संकरहि सराहा। तुम्ह बिनु अस ब्रतु को निरबाहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::446.verse_hindi: तब कृतज्ञ (उपकार मानने वाले), कृपालु, रूप और शील के भण्डार, महान् तेजपुंज भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी प्रकट हुए। उन्होंने बहुत तरह से शिवजी की सराहना की और कहा कि आपके बिना ऐसा (कठिन) व्रत कौन निबाह सकता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::446.english_translation: Then Ram appeared—grateful, compassionate, a treasure of beauty and virtue, vast in radiance. In many ways he praised Shiva and said, “Without you, who could carry out such a vow?”
ramacharitamanas::446.translation_literal: प्रगटे (appeared) / रामु (Ram) / कृतग्य (grateful) / कृपाला (compassionate) / रूप (beauty) / सील (virtue) / निधि (treasure) / तेज (radiance) / बिसाला (vast) ॥ / बहु प्रकार (many ways) / संकरहि (to Shiva) / सराहा (praised) / तुम्ह बिनु (without you) / अस (such) / ब्रतु (vow) / को (who) / निरबाहा (could carry out)
ramacharitamanas::446.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::446.essence: Even the divine honors sincere devotion with gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::446.simple_meaning: Ram appears in radiant form and praises Shiva, saying that such a vow could not be fulfilled without him.
ramacharitamanas::446.simple_insight: True greatness remembers help. Devotion deepens when power bows to support.
ramacharitamanas::446.detailed_meaning: Shiva has been singing Ram's praise and holding fast to his vow through long devotion. Now Ram appears before him, radiant and full of grace, and honors Shiva openly. The moment reveals mutual devotion: Ram acknowledges Shiva's support, and Shiva's love receives its fruit.
ramacharitamanas::446.modern_relevance: You finally finish a hard promise with help from someone who stayed behind the scenes. The relief is not just success — it is being seen and thanked by the person you served.
ramacharitamanas::446.insight: It shifts devotion from one-sided worship to mutual recognition and gratitude.

ramacharitamanas::447.verse_sanskrit: बहुबिधि राम सिवहि समुझावा। पारबती कर जन्मु सुनावा॥ अति पुनीत गिरिजा कै करनी। बिस्तर सहित कृपानिधि बरनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::447.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने बहुत प्रकार से शिवजी को समझाया और पार्वतीजी का जन्म सुनाया। कृपानिधान श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने विस्तारपूर्वक पार्वतीजी की अत्यन्त पवित्र करनी का वर्णन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::447.english_translation: Ram explained many things to Shiva and told him of Parvati's birth. The treasure of compassion, Ram, described Girija's supremely pure conduct in detail.
ramacharitamanas::447.translation_literal: बहुबिधि (in many ways) / राम (Ram) / सिवहि (to Shiva) / समुझावा (explained) / पारबती (Parvati) / कर (of) / जन्मु (birth) / सुनावा (told) ॥ अति (very) / पुनीत (pure) / गिरिजा (Girija/Parvati) / कै (of) / करनी (conduct/acts) / बिस्तर सहित (with विस्तार, in detail) / कृपानिधि (treasure of compassion) / बरनी (described) ॥
ramacharitamanas::447.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::447.essence: Respect opens the way before any request is made.
ramacharitamanas::447.simple_meaning: Ram explains Parvati's birth to Shiva and praises her pure conduct in detail.
ramacharitamanas::447.simple_insight: Love deepens when the divine remembers and honors the beloved's virtue.
ramacharitamanas::447.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, Ram is speaking to Shiva before the marriage request that follows. He patiently explains Parvati's origin and then praises her spotless conduct, preparing the ground for Shiva to accept the union.
ramacharitamanas::447.modern_relevance: You are trying to ask for something important, but first you show respect for the other person's values. That careful recognition can open the door more than pressure ever will.
ramacharitamanas::447.insight: It teaches you to begin with reverence, not demand.

ramacharitamanas::448.verse_sanskrit: अब बिनती मम सुनहु सिव जौं मो पर निज नेहु। जाइ बिबाहहु सैलजहि यह मोहि मागें देहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::448.verse_hindi: (फिर उन्होंने शिवजी से कहा-) हे शिवजी! यदि मुझ पर आपका स्नेह है, तो अब आप मेरी विनती सुनिए। मुझे यह माँगें दीजिए कि आप जाकर पार्वती के साथ विवाह कर लें ॥
ramacharitamanas::448.english_translation: Then Ram said to Shiva: "If you love me, listen to my request. Grant me this: go and marry Parvati."
ramacharitamanas::448.translation_literal: अब (now) / बिनती (request) / मम (my) / सुनहु (listen) / सिव (Shiva) / जौं (if) / मो पर (on me) / निज (your own) / नेहु (love) / जाइ (go) / बिबाहहु (marry) / सैलजहि (Parvati, daughter of the mountain) / यह (this) / मोहि (to me) / मागें (asked-for) / देहु (give)
ramacharitamanas::448.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::448.essence: Love asks without demanding, and reverence answers it.
ramacharitamanas::448.simple_meaning: Ram asks Shiva to accept his loving request and marry Parvati. The line shows Ram speaking with affection and honor toward Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::448.simple_insight: Love can take the form of a request that honors the other person.
ramacharitamanas::448.detailed_meaning: Ram has just appeared before Shiva and praised him. In this intimate exchange, Ram asks Shiva to fulfill a request: marry Parvati. The moment reveals mutual reverence between the divine figures and sets up Shiva's response of obedience and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::448.modern_relevance: A child asks a parent for something not as a demand, but as a sign of trust. The request itself carries love: "If you care for me, hear me."
ramacharitamanas::448.insight: It shifts attention from command to loving invitation, where relationship matters more than force.

ramacharitamanas::449.verse_sanskrit: कह सिव जदपि उचित अस नाहीं। नाथ बचन पुनि मेटि न जाहीं॥ सिर धरि आयसु करिअ तुम्हारा। परम धरमु यह नाथ हमारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::449.verse_hindi: शिवजी ने कहा- यद्यपि ऐसा उचित नहीं है, परन्तु स्वामी की बात भी मेटी नहीं जा सकती। हे नाथ! मेरा यही परम धर्म है कि मैं आपकी आज्ञा को सिर पर रखकर उसका पालन करूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::449.english_translation: Shiva said, “Even if this is not proper, a lord’s command cannot be undone. I bear your order on my head; this is my highest duty, my lord.”
ramacharitamanas::449.translation_literal: कह (said) / सिव (Shiva) / जदपि (although) / उचित (proper) / अस (this) / नाहीं (not) / नाथ (lord) / बचन (word/command) / पुनि (again) / मेटि (erased) / न (not) / जाहीं (go) / सिर (head) / धरि (placing) / आयसु (command) / करिअ (should be done) / तुम्हारा (your) / परम (highest) / धरमु (duty) / यह (this) / नाथ (lord) / हमारा (our/mine)
ramacharitamanas::449.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::449.essence: Duty begins where personal opinion ends.
ramacharitamanas::449.simple_meaning: Shiva says that even if something feels improper, a lord's command cannot be ignored. He treats obedience to that command as his highest duty.
ramacharitamanas::449.simple_insight: True respect shows up as action, not agreement.
ramacharitamanas::449.detailed_meaning: Shiva is answering Ram after being asked to go ahead with the marriage of Parvati. He admits the request is not ideal, yet says a lord’s word must still be carried out. The moment reveals devotion expressed as disciplined obedience.
ramacharitamanas::449.modern_relevance: Your manager asks you to fix a messy mistake you did not create. You know it is awkward, but you do it cleanly because the responsibility is now yours.
ramacharitamanas::449.insight: It shifts the mind from personal preference to rightful responsibility.

ramacharitamanas::450.verse_sanskrit: मातु पिता गुर प्रभु कै बानी। बिनहिं बिचार करिअ सुभ जानी॥ तुम्ह सब भाँति परम हितकारी। अग्या सिर पर नाथ तुम्हारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::450.verse_hindi: माता, पिता, गुरु और स्वामी की बात को बिना ही विचारे शुभ समझकर करना (मानना) चाहिए। फिर आप तो सब प्रकार से मेरे परम हितकारी हैं। हे नाथ! आपकी आज्ञा मेरे सिर पर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::450.english_translation: The words of mother, father, teacher, and master should be accepted as good without hesitation. You are my greatest well-wisher in every way, O Lord. Your command rests on my head.
ramacharitamanas::450.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / पिता (father) / गुर (teacher) / प्रभु (master) / कै (of) / बानी (words) / बिनहिं (without) / बिचार (consideration) / करिअ (should be done) / सुभ (good) / जानी (knowing) / तुम्ह (you) / सब (all) / भाँति (ways) / परम (greatest) / हितकारी (beneficial) / अग्या (command) / सिर (head) / पर (on) / नाथ (Lord) / तुम्हारी (your)
ramacharitamanas::450.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::450.essence: Right guidance is obeyed before the mind starts arguing.
ramacharitamanas::450.simple_meaning: A child should accept the words of parents, teacher, and master as right without arguing. Shiva says Ram is his greatest well-wisher, so Ram's command is above his own will.
ramacharitamanas::450.simple_insight: Real respect means letting wise guidance shape your actions, even when your own preference resists.
ramacharitamanas::450.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, Shiva has already asked for a boon from Ram. Now he bows deeper, saying that a true disciple does not weigh the words of parents, teacher, or master like a bargain. He places Ram's command above himself.
ramacharitamanas::450.modern_relevance: Your mentor gives you hard feedback after a messy mistake, and your first urge is to defend yourself. This verse asks for a different move: hear the correction first, ego second.
ramacharitamanas::450.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to obedient trust in rightful guidance.

ramacharitamanas::451.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु तोषेउ सुनि संकर बचना। भक्ति बिबेक धर्म जुत रचना॥ कह प्रभु हर तुम्हार पन रहेऊ। अब उर राखेहु जो हम कहेऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::451.verse_hindi: शिवजी की भक्ति, ज्ञान और धर्म से युक्त वचन रचना सुनकर प्रभु रामचन्द्रजी संतुष्ट हो गए। प्रभु ने कहा- हे हर! आपकी प्रतिज्ञा पूरी हो गई। अब हमने जो कहा है, उसे हृदय में रखना ॥
ramacharitamanas::451.english_translation: Rama was pleased to hear Shiva's words, full of devotion, discernment, and dharma. Rama said, “O Hari, your vow is fulfilled. Now keep in your heart what I have said.”
ramacharitamanas::451.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / तोषेउ (was pleased) / सुनि (hearing) / संकर (Shiva) / बचना (words) / भक्ति (devotion) / बिबेक (discernment) / धर्म (dharma) / जुत (joined with) / रचना (composition) ॥ कह (said) / प्रभु (the Lord) / हर (Hari) / तुम्हार (your) / पन (vow) / रहेऊ (has remained fulfilled) ॥ अब (now) / उर (in the heart) / राखेहु (keep) / जो (what) / हम (we) / कहेऊ (have said) ॥
ramacharitamanas::451.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::451.essence: Devotion is complete only when the heart keeps what it hears.
ramacharitamanas::451.simple_meaning: Ram is pleased by Shiva's devotional words and confirms that Shiva's vow has been fulfilled. He then asks Shiva to keep Ram's instruction in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::451.simple_insight: True devotion is mutual: reverence is answered, and the heart receives a living instruction.
ramacharitamanas::451.detailed_meaning: Shiva has just spoken with perfect devotion, wisdom, and dharma, and Ram is satisfied. Ram then tells Shiva that his vow stands fulfilled and asks him to hold Ram's words within his heart. The scene seals their mutual reverence.
ramacharitamanas::451.modern_relevance: You finally hear the apology, the gratitude, or the recognition you hoped for. The moment is not just relief — it becomes a shared bond when the other person asks you to carry the exchange forward.
ramacharitamanas::451.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to relationship: reverence is completed by remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::452.verse_sanskrit: अंतरधान भए अस भाषी। संकर सोइ मूरति उर राखी॥ तबहिं सप्तरिषि सिव पहिं आए। बोले प्रभु अति बचन सुहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::452.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार कहकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी अन्तर्धान हो गए। शिवजी ने उनकी वह मूर्ति अपने हृदय में रख ली। उसी समय सप्तर्षि शिवजी के पास आए। प्रभु महादेवजी ने उनसे अत्यन्त सुहावने वचन कहे- ॥
ramacharitamanas::452.english_translation: After speaking thus, Shri Ramchandra disappeared. Shiva kept that very image in his heart. Then the seven sages came to Shiva, and the Lord spoke to them with very pleasing words.
ramacharitamanas::452.translation_literal: अंतरधान (disappeared) / भए (became) / अस (thus) / भाषी (having spoken) / संकर (Shiva) / सोइ (that very) / मूरति (form/image) / उर (in the heart) / राखी (kept)॥ / तबहिं (then) / सप्तरिषि (the seven sages) / सिव पहिं (to Shiva) / आए (came) / बोले (spoke) / प्रभु (the Lord) / अति (very) / बचन (words) / सुहाए (pleasing)॥
ramacharitamanas::452.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::452.essence: What devotion receives, the heart keeps.
ramacharitamanas::452.simple_meaning: Ram disappears after speaking. Shiva holds Ram's image in his heart. Then the seven sages arrive, and Shiva speaks kindly to them.
ramacharitamanas::452.simple_insight: What is loved deeply stays alive inwardly, even after the visible form is gone.
ramacharitamanas::452.detailed_meaning: Ram has just answered Shiva and vanished from sight. Shiva does not lose him; he keeps Ram's form in his heart. Then the seven sages arrive, and the scene turns to Shiva's gracious welcome.
ramacharitamanas::452.modern_relevance: Someone leaves the room after a brief, life-changing conversation. The words are over, but the presence stays with you, and you carry it into the next meeting.
ramacharitamanas::452.insight: It shifts attention from what disappears outwardly to what devotion preserves inwardly.

ramacharitamanas::453.verse_sanskrit: पारबती पहिं जाइ तुम्ह प्रेम परिच्छा लेहु। गिरिहि प्रेरि पठएहु भवन दूरि करेहु संदेहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::453.verse_hindi: आप लोग पार्वती के पास जाकर उनके प्रेम की परीक्षा लीजिए और हिमाचल को कहकर (उन्हें पार्वती को लिवा लाने के लिए भेजिए तथा) पार्वती को घर भिजवाइए और उनके संदेह को दूर कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::453.english_translation: Go to Parvati and test her love. Ask Himachal to send her home and remove her doubt.
ramacharitamanas::453.translation_literal: पारबती (Parvati) / पहिं (to) / जाइ (go) / तुम्ह (you) / प्रेम (love) / परिच्छा (test) / लेहु (take) / गिरिहि (to Himachal) / प्रेरि (having urged) / पठएहु (send) / भवन (home) / दूरि (away) / करेहु (make) / संदेहु (doubt)
ramacharitamanas::453.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::453.essence: Love proves itself when doubt is cleared.
ramacharitamanas::453.simple_meaning: Go to Parvati, test her love, and remove the doubt that still surrounds her choice.
ramacharitamanas::453.simple_insight: True devotion is not blind confusion; it becomes clear when doubt is removed.
ramacharitamanas::453.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking after Ram has vanished from sight and left his blessing behind. The sages are told to approach Parvati, test the steadiness of her love, and send her home without hesitation. The moment is about confirming devotion, not performing a miracle.
ramacharitamanas::453.modern_relevance: A family is waiting for a decision that will change everything, but one person still hesitates. Before the next step, the doubt has to be cleared honestly.
ramacharitamanas::453.insight: It shifts attention from outward display to the steadiness of love under scrutiny.

ramacharitamanas::454.verse_sanskrit: रिषिन्ह गौरि देखी तहँ कैसी। मूरतिमंत तपस्या जैसी॥ बोले मुनि सुनु सैलकुमारी। करहु कवन कारन तपु भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::454.verse_hindi: ऋषियों ने (वहाँ जाकर) पार्वती को कैसी देखा, मानो मूर्तिमान् तपस्या ही हो। मुनि बोले- हे शैलकुमारी! सुनो, तुम किसलिए इतना कठोर तप कर रही हो? ॥
ramacharitamanas::454.english_translation: The sages saw Parvati there, like living austerity itself. The sage said, “Listen, daughter of the mountain: why are you performing such severe penance?”
ramacharitamanas::454.translation_literal: रिषिन्ह (the sages) / गौरि (Parvati) / देखी (saw) / तहँ (there) / कैसी (how) / मूरतिमंत (embodied) / तपस्या (austerity) / जैसी (like)॥ / बोले (spoke) / मुनि (the sage) / सुनु (listen) / सैलकुमारी (daughter of the mountain) / करहु (are you doing) / कवन (what) / कारन (reason) / तपु (penance) / भारी (severe)॥
ramacharitamanas::454.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::454.essence: Austerity without its reason still invites a question.
ramacharitamanas::454.simple_meaning: The sages see Parvati as the living form of austerity and ask why she is doing such severe penance.
ramacharitamanas::454.simple_insight: Real devotion is visible in the body, but its reason must still be spoken aloud.
ramacharitamanas::454.detailed_meaning: The sages arrive and behold Parvati absorbed in severe tapas, so intense that she seems like austerity made visible. They are moved to ask why the mountain princess is enduring such hardship, opening the next exchange about her devotion.
ramacharitamanas::454.modern_relevance: A friend notices you skipping meals, sleeping less, and pushing yourself hard for something no one else can see. The first question is not praise — it is: what are you doing this for?
ramacharitamanas::454.insight: It shifts attention from the outward display of discipline to the motive beneath it.

ramacharitamanas::455.verse_sanskrit: केहि अवराधहु का तुम्ह चहहू। हम सन सत्य मरमु किन कहहू॥ कहत बचन मनु अति सकुचाई। हँसिहहु सुनि हमारि जड़ताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::455.verse_hindi: तुम किसकी आराधना करती हो और क्या चाहती हो? हमसे अपना सच्चा भेद क्यों नहीं कहतीं? (पार्वती ने कहा-) बात कहते मन बहुत सकुचाता है। आप लोग मेरी मूर्खता सुनकर हँसेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::455.english_translation: Who do you worship, and what do you want? Why not tell us your true secret? Parvati said, "My mind feels very shy to speak. You will laugh when you hear my foolishness."
ramacharitamanas::455.translation_literal: केहि (whom) / अवराधहु (do you worship) / का (what) / तुम्ह (you) / चहहू (want) / हम सन (to us) / सत्य (true) / मरमु (secret/heart) / किन (why not) / कहहू (tell) ॥ कहत (speaking) / बचन (words) / मनु (mind) / अति (very) / सकुचाई (shrank/shy) / हँसिहहु (you will laugh) / सुनि (hearing) / हमारि (my) / जड़ताई (foolishness) ॥
ramacharitamanas::455.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::455.essence: True longing is shy before it becomes speech.
ramacharitamanas::455.simple_meaning: Parvati asks who she should worship and what she truly wants, but she feels shy to reveal her heart because she fears being laughed at.
ramacharitamanas::455.simple_insight: Even sincere longing can feel vulnerable before it finds words.
ramacharitamanas::455.detailed_meaning: Parvati stands before the sages, and they ask her to reveal the truth of her devotion. She hesitates, not because she lacks faith, but because honest longing can feel exposing. This moment opens the deeper question of what her heart truly seeks.
ramacharitamanas::455.modern_relevance: You start to answer a question in a group chat, then delete it three times because it feels too honest. The heart often knows first; the voice arrives later.
ramacharitamanas::455.insight: It shows how devotion begins with trust enough to speak what the mind wants to hide.

ramacharitamanas::456.verse_sanskrit: मनु हठ परा न सुनइ सिखावा। चहत बारि पर भीति उठावा॥ नारद कहा सत्य सोइ जाना। बिनु पंखन्ह हम चहहिं उड़ाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::456.verse_hindi: मन ने हठ पकड़ लिया है, वह उपदेश नहीं सुनता और जल पर दीवाल उठाना चाहता है। नारदजी ने जो कह दिया उसे सत्य जानकर मैं बिना ही पाँख के उड़ना चाहती हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::456.english_translation: The mind has grown stubborn; it will not listen to instruction and wants to raise a wall on water. Narada spoke the truth, and I know it: without wings, I still want to fly.
ramacharitamanas::456.translation_literal: मनु (mind) / हठ (obstinacy) / परा (has fallen) / न (not) / सुनइ (listens) / सिखावा (instruction) / चहत (wants) / बारि (water) / पर (on) / भीति (wall) / उठावा (to raise) ॥ नारद (Narada) / कहा (said) / सत्य (truth) / सोइ (that) / जाना (known) / बिनु (without) / पंखन्ह (wings) / हम (we/I) / चहहिं (want) / उड़ाना (to fly)
ramacharitamanas::456.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::456.essence: Desire can make the mind deny what it already knows.
ramacharitamanas::456.simple_meaning: Parvati admits that her mind has become stubborn. She knows Narada spoke the truth, yet she still wants the impossible: to fly without wings.
ramacharitamanas::456.simple_insight: It feels honest to see how desire can override reason, even when the truth is already known.
ramacharitamanas::456.detailed_meaning: Parvati is speaking to the sages in Shiva's frame narrative. They have asked why she practices such severe tapas, and she confesses that her mind has fixed itself on Shiva. Even truth cannot easily move a mind captured by longing.
ramacharitamanas::456.modern_relevance: You know the advice is right, but you keep checking the same message, chasing the same person, making the same impossible plan. Wanting can make the mind ignore reality.
ramacharitamanas::456.insight: It exposes the mind's refusal to learn when desire has taken over, and invites honest self-observation.

ramacharitamanas::457.verse_sanskrit: देखहु मुनि अबिबेकु हमारा। चाहिअ सदा सिवहि भरतारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::457.verse_hindi: हे मुनियों! आप मेरा अज्ञान तो देखिए कि मैं सदा शिवजी को ही पति बनाना चाहती हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::457.english_translation: O sages, look at my lack of discernment: I always wish for Shiva as my husband.
ramacharitamanas::457.translation_literal: देखहु (look) / मुनि (sages) / अबिबेकु (lack of discernment) / हमारा (my) / चाहिअ (want) / सदा (always) / सिवहि (Shiva) / भरतारा (husband)
ramacharitamanas::457.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::457.essence: True devotion chooses one beloved without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::457.simple_meaning: Parvati humbly admits to the sages that she wants Shiva alone as her husband.
ramacharitamanas::457.simple_insight: Love becomes clear when the heart stops bargaining and chooses one beloved completely.
ramacharitamanas::457.detailed_meaning: Parvati is speaking in the opening frame of the Balkand, answering the sages after Narad's teaching has stirred her. She calls her own mind foolish because it wants only Shiva, setting up the devotion that follows.
ramacharitamanas::457.modern_relevance: You know that moment when everyone expects you to be practical, but your heart has already chosen? You stop explaining and simply name what you want.
ramacharitamanas::457.insight: It shifts attention from social approval to wholehearted devotion.

ramacharitamanas::458.verse_sanskrit: सुनत बचन बिहसे रिषय गिरिसंभव तव देह। नारद कर उपदेसु सुनि कहहु बसेउ किसु गेह ॥
ramacharitamanas::458.verse_hindi: पार्वतीजी की बात सुनते ही ऋषि लोग हँस पड़े और बोले- तुम्हारा शरीर पर्वत से ही तो उत्पन्न हुआ है! भला, कहो तो नारद का उपदेश सुनकर आज तक किसका घर बसा है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::458.english_translation: Hearing this, the sages laughed and said: 'O daughter of the mountain, your body arose from the mountain itself! Tell us, after hearing Narada's counsel, whose household has ever truly settled?'
ramacharitamanas::458.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words) / बिहसे (laughed) / रिषय (sages) / गिरिसंभव (mountain-born) / तव (your) / देह (body) / नारद (Narada) / कर (of) / उपदेसु (instruction) / सुनि (hearing) / कहहु (say) / बसेउ (settled) / किसु (whose) / गेह (household)
ramacharitamanas::458.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::458.essence: True counsel can unsettle the household before it reveals a higher calling.
ramacharitamanas::458.simple_meaning: The sages laugh at Parvati's statement and point out that Narada's advice has a strange effect: it unsettles household life instead of settling it.
ramacharitamanas::458.simple_insight: Some counsel does not create peace right away; it first shakes the mind loose from old assumptions.
ramacharitamanas::458.detailed_meaning: Parvati has just spoken of her wish to marry Shiva. The sages respond with a smile, reminding her that Narada's words often unsettle ordinary household life. This verse keeps the playful frame moving toward the deeper question of devotion and destiny.
ramacharitamanas::458.modern_relevance: A friend gives you advice that sounds wise, but it leaves your plans wobbling instead of secure. Sometimes the right teaching does not make life tidier first — it makes false certainty collapse.
ramacharitamanas::458.insight: It shifts attention from social comfort to the disruptive power of true counsel.

ramacharitamanas::459.verse_sanskrit: दच्छसुतन्ह उपदेसेन्हि जाई। तिन्ह फिरि भवनु न देखा आई॥ चित्रकेतु कर घरु उन घाला। कनककसिपु कर पुनि अस हाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::459.verse_hindi: उन्होंने जाकर दक्ष के पुत्रों को उपदेश दिया था, जिससे उन्होंने फिर लौटकर घर का मुँह भी नहीं देखा। चित्रकेतु के घर को नारद ने ही चौपट किया। फिर यही हाल हिरण्यकशिपु का हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::459.english_translation: He went and instructed the sons of Daksha, and they never returned home again. Narada ruined the house of Citraketu, and the same happened with Hiranyakashipu.
ramacharitamanas::459.translation_literal: दच्छसुतन्ह (the sons of Daksha) / उपदेसेन्हि (he instructed) / जाई (having gone) / तिन्ह (they) / फिरि (again) / भवनु (home) / न देखा (did not see) / आई (coming) / चित्रकेतु (of Citraketu) / कर (of) / घरु (house) / उन (that one) / घाला (ruined) / कनककसिपु (Hiranyakashipu) / कर (of) / पुनि (again) / अस (such) / हाला (condition)
ramacharitamanas::459.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::459.essence: True teaching can sever old attachments in a single stroke.
ramacharitamanas::459.simple_meaning: Narada's teaching turned those who heard him away from ordinary household life. The verse lists famous examples to show how strongly his words changed people.
ramacharitamanas::459.simple_insight: Some teachings do not leave you unchanged. They pull your attention so completely that old attachments lose their grip.
ramacharitamanas::459.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, Parvati is asking about Narada's strange power. The narrator answers by naming examples: the sons of Daksha, Citraketu, and Hiranyakashipu all changed drastically after Narada's influence. The point is not a single event, but Narada's transformative force.
ramacharitamanas::459.modern_relevance: You hear one honest conversation and suddenly your old routine feels thin. A mentor, book, or warning can do that — it can break a comfortable life open.
ramacharitamanas::459.insight: It shifts attention from social normalcy to the force of transformative instruction.

ramacharitamanas::460.verse_sanskrit: नारद सिख जे सुनहिं नर नारी। अवसि होहिं तजि भवनु भिखारी॥ मन कपटी तन सज्जन चीन्हा। आपु सरिस सबही चह कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::460.verse_hindi: जो स्त्री-पुरुष नारद की सीख सुनते हैं, वे घर-बार छोड़कर अवश्य ही भिखारी हो जाते हैं। उनका मन तो कपटी है, शरीर पर सज्जनों के चिह्न हैं। वे सभी को अपने समान बनाना चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::460.english_translation: Those who listen to Narad's teaching, men or women, certainly become beggars after leaving home. Their mind is deceitful, while their body wears the marks of a saint. They want to make everyone like themselves.
ramacharitamanas::460.translation_literal: नारद (Narad) / सिख (teaching) / जे (who) / सुनहिं (hear) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / अवसि (certainly) / होहिं (become) / तजि (leaving) / भवनु (home) / भिखारी (beggars) / मन (mind) / कपटी (deceitful) / तन (body) / सज्जन (saintly) / चीन्हा (marked) / आपु (self) / सरिस (like) / सबही (everyone) / चह (want) / कीन्हा (to make)
ramacharitamanas::460.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::460.essence: Outer sainthood means nothing if the mind stays crooked.
ramacharitamanas::460.simple_meaning: People who blindly follow Narad's advice leave ordinary life behind, but their outer appearance can hide a crooked mind. They often try to reshape others in their own image.
ramacharitamanas::460.simple_insight: Not every holy-looking person is wise. The real test is whether the mind is honest and humble.
ramacharitamanas::460.detailed_meaning: Parvati is pressing Shiva about Narad's words and their effect on women. The sages answer by mocking Narad's teaching as one that turns people away from ordinary household life while leaving inner deceit untouched. The line sharpens the argument before Parvati's question about the kind of husband she is being asked to accept.
ramacharitamanas::460.modern_relevance: Someone quotes a spiritual line on social media, dresses the part, and sounds elevated at dinner—but still manipulates everyone around them. The warning is about mismatch between appearance and mind.
ramacharitamanas::460.insight: It shifts attention from outward holiness to inner honesty and exposes the danger of moral imitation without transformation.

ramacharitamanas::461.verse_sanskrit: तेहि कें बचन मानि बिस्वासा। तुम्ह चाहहु पति सहज उदासा॥ निर्गुन निलज कुबेष कपाली। अकुल अगेह दिगंबर ब्याली ॥
ramacharitamanas::461.verse_hindi: उनके वचनों पर विश्वास मानकर तुम ऐसा पति चाहती हो जो स्वभाव से ही उदासीन, गुणहीन, निर्लज्ज, बुरे वेषवाला, नर-कपालों की माला पहनने वाला, कुलहीन, बिना घर-बार का, नंगा और शरीर पर साँपों को लपेटे रखने वाला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::461.english_translation: Believing his words, you want a husband who is naturally detached, without qualities, shameless, oddly dressed, wearing a garland of skulls, without lineage, without a home, naked, and wrapped in serpents.
ramacharitamanas::461.translation_literal: तेहि कें (of that) / बचन (words) / मानि (having believed) / बिस्वासा (trust) / तुम्ह (you) / चाहहु (desire) / पति (husband) / सहज (by nature) / उदासा (detached) / निर्गुन (without qualities) / निलज (shameless) / कुबेष (strange appearance) / कपाली (skull-bearing) / अकुल (without lineage) / अगेह (without home) / दिगंबर (sky-clad) / ब्याली (serpent-adorned)
ramacharitamanas::461.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::461.essence: Borrowed praise can turn sacred choice into confusion.
ramacharitamanas::461.simple_meaning: The speaker mocks Sati for wanting a husband who is detached, unconventional, and frightening in appearance.
ramacharitamanas::461.simple_insight: Not every attractive-sounding idea deserves trust. False praise can make a wrong choice feel noble.
ramacharitamanas::461.detailed_meaning: Narad has stirred confusion, and Sati is weighing his words. In this Balkand passage, the speaker ridicules the idea that she would choose a husband like Shiva, describing him in shocking terms to expose the misunderstanding at the heart of the scene.
ramacharitamanas::461.modern_relevance: A friend forwards a polished message about someone you barely know, and suddenly everyone sounds convincing. This verse warns how easily borrowed opinions can distort judgment.
ramacharitamanas::461.insight: It shifts the mind from accepting reputation at face value to examining what the words are really claiming.

ramacharitamanas::462.verse_sanskrit: कहहु कवन सुखु अस बरु पाएँ। भल भूलिहु ठग के बौराएँ॥ पंच कहें सिवँ सती बिबाही। पुनि अवडेरि मराएन्हि ताही ॥
ramacharitamanas::462.verse_hindi: ऐसे वर के मिलने से कहो, तुम्हें क्या सुख होगा? तुम उस ठग (नारद) के बहकावे में आकर खूब भूलीं। पहले पंचों के कहने से शिव ने सती से विवाह किया था, परन्तु फिर उसे त्यागकर मरवा डाला॥
ramacharitamanas::462.english_translation: What happiness would you gain from finding such a husband? You have been badly misled by that trickster. At first, on the advice of the council, Shiva married Sati, but later he abandoned her and caused her death.
ramacharitamanas::462.translation_literal: कहहु (tell) / कवन (what) / सुखु (happiness) / अस (such) / बरु (husband) / पाएँ (having found) / भल (well) / भूलिहु (you have been mistaken) / ठग (trickster) / के (of) / बौराएँ (deluded) / पंच (council of five) / कहें (having said) / सिवँ (Shiva) / सती (Sati) / बिबाही (married) / पुनि (then) / अवडेरि (later) / मराएन्हि (caused to die) / ताही (her)
ramacharitamanas::462.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::462.essence: Blind trust in bad advice turns choice into regret.
ramacharitamanas::462.simple_meaning: A false guide can make a choice look wise when it is not. The verse warns that blind trust in bad advice brings pain and regret.
ramacharitamanas::462.simple_insight: Not every persuasive voice deserves trust. Clear seeing protects you from choices that later turn bitter.
ramacharitamanas::462.detailed_meaning: Parvati has been drawn into Narad's warning about marriage, and the story turns to Shiva and Sati as the example. The speaker points out how misleading advice can lead to a disastrous choice, making this a caution about delusion and poor judgment.
ramacharitamanas::462.modern_relevance: A friend forwards a confident voice note, and you almost act on it before checking the facts. The damage from one bad recommendation can take years to undo.
ramacharitamanas::462.insight: It shifts the mind from obedience to scrutiny, asking you to test advice before surrendering to it.

ramacharitamanas::463.verse_sanskrit: अब सुख सोवत सोचु नहिं भीख मागि भव खाहिं। सहज एकाकिन्ह के भवन कबहुँ कि नारि खटाहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::463.verse_hindi: अब शिव को कोई चिन्ता नहीं रही, भीख माँगकर खा लेते हैं और सुख से सोते हैं। ऐसे स्वभाव से ही अकेले रहने वालों के घर भी भला क्या कभी स्त्रियाँ टिक सकती हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::463.english_translation: Now Shiva has no worry. He begs for food and sleeps in comfort. Can a woman ever stay in the home of one who is naturally alone?
ramacharitamanas::463.translation_literal: अब (now) / सुख (comfort) / सोवत (sleeping) / सोचु (worry) / नहिं (not) / भीख (alms) / मागि (having begged) / भव (world) / खाहिं (eat) / सहज (natural) / एकाकिन्ह (of the solitary) / के (of) / भवन (home) / कबहुँ (ever) / कि (whether) / नारि (woman) / खटाहिं (stay)
ramacharitamanas::463.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::463.essence: A life built for solitude cannot easily hold domestic life.
ramacharitamanas::463.simple_meaning: Shiva is described as carefree and naturally solitary. The verse argues that a woman would not stay long in the home of someone who lives like that.
ramacharitamanas::463.simple_insight: Some choices reveal a mismatch so deep that no persuasion can hide it.
ramacharitamanas::463.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, the debate over Shiva as a husband is still unfolding. The speaker dismisses the idea that a naturally solitary ascetic can be a fitting household partner, using Shiva's wandering, begging life as the argument.
ramacharitamanas::463.modern_relevance: You meet someone who loves silence, freedom, and living out of a backpack. You love homes, routines, and shared meals. The gap is not small — it shapes the whole future.
ramacharitamanas::463.insight: It frames compatibility as a matter of lived nature, not just affection or clever argument.

ramacharitamanas::464.verse_sanskrit: अजहूँ मानहु कहा हमारा। हम तुम्ह कहुँ बरु नीक बिचारा॥ अति सुंदर सुचि सुखद सुसीला। गावहिं बेद जासु जस लीला ॥
ramacharitamanas::464.verse_hindi: अब भी हमारा कहा मानो, हमने तुम्हारे लिए अच्छा वर विचारा है। वह बहुत ही सुंदर, पवित्र, सुखदायक और सुशील है, जिसका यश और लीला वेद गाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::464.english_translation: Still accept what I say. I have chosen a good bridegroom for you. He is very beautiful, pure, delightful, and well-mannered; the Vedas sing of his fame and play.
ramacharitamanas::464.translation_literal: अजहूँ (still / even now) / मानहु (accept / believe) / कहा (what is said) / हमारा (our) / हम (we) / तुम्ह (for you) / कहुँ (for) / बरु (bridegroom) / नीक (good / excellent) / बिचारा (chosen / considered) ॥ अति (very) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुचि (pure) / सुखद (joy-giving) / सुसीला (well-mannered) / गावहिं (sing) / बेद (the Vedas) / जासु (whose) / जस (fame) / लीला (play / divine acts) ॥
ramacharitamanas::464.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::464.essence: Trust the one who sees the worth you cannot yet see.
ramacharitamanas::464.simple_meaning: Shiva tells Parvati to trust his choice. The bridegroom he has in mind is beautiful, pure, gracious, and praised by the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::464.simple_insight: Trust grows when the one speaking has already seen the whole picture.
ramacharitamanas::464.detailed_meaning: In the frame story, Shiva is answering Parvati’s doubts about the best bridegroom. He urges her to accept his judgment and begins describing Ram’s qualities. The verse is part of a larger praise, not the full conclusion.
ramacharitamanas::464.modern_relevance: A parent reassures a worried family that the person they chose is truly worthy. The details matter, but the deeper message is simpler: let wisdom speak before suspicion takes over.
ramacharitamanas::464.insight: It shifts attention from doubt to reverent trust in a wiser judgment.

ramacharitamanas::465.verse_sanskrit: दूषन रहित सकल गुन रासी। श्रीपति पुर बैकुंठ निवासी॥ अस बरु तुम्हहि मिलाउब आनी। सुनत बिहसि कह बचन भवानी ॥
