ramacharitamanas::465.verse_hindi: वह दोषों से रहित, सारे सद् गुणों की राशि, लक्ष्मी का स्वामी और वैकुण्ठपुरी का रहने वाला है। हम ऐसे वर को लाकर तुमसे मिला देंगे। यह सुनते ही पार्वतीजी हँसकर बोलीं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::465.english_translation: He is free of faults, a treasury of every virtue, the lord of Lakshmi, and a resident of Vaikuntha. "I will bring you such a bridegroom," she said. Hearing this, Parvati smiled and replied:
ramacharitamanas::465.translation_literal: दूषन-रहित (faultless) / सकल (all) / गुन (virtues) / रासी (heap, treasury) / श्रीपति (lord of Lakshmi) / पुर (city) / बैकुंठ (Vaikuntha) / निवासी (resident) / अस (such) / बरु (bridegroom) / तुम्हहि (to you) / मिलाउब (I will bring) / आनी (bringing) / सुनत (hearing) / बिहसि (smiling, laughing) / कह (said) / बचन (words) / भवानी (Parvati)
ramacharitamanas::465.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::465.essence: Ram is praised as the faultless source of every virtue.
ramacharitamanas::465.simple_meaning: Shiva describes Ram as flawless, full of virtues, and fit to be the ideal bridegroom. Parvati hears this and smiles, about to answer.
ramacharitamanas::465.simple_insight: Praise becomes a doorway: the heart recognizes what words can only point toward.
ramacharitamanas::465.detailed_meaning: In the Shiva-Parvati frame of Balkand, Shiva is describing Ram as the perfect match for Sita: faultless, virtuous, and divine. Parvati hears the praise and smiles, because this is not just a description but a shared recognition of Ram's greatness.
ramacharitamanas::465.modern_relevance: You hear someone speak about a person they truly admire, and their voice changes. The praise is not performance — it reveals recognition, affection, and certainty all at once.
ramacharitamanas::465.insight: It shifts attention from outward description to inward recognition of Ram's worth.

ramacharitamanas::466.verse_sanskrit: सत्य कहेहु गिरिभव तनु एहा। हठ न छूट छूटै बरु देहा॥ कनकउ पुनि पषान तें होई। जारेहुँ सहजु न परिहर सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::466.verse_hindi: आपने यह सत्य ही कहा कि मेरा यह शरीर पर्वत से उत्पन्न हुआ है, इसलिए हठ नहीं छूटेगा, शरीर भले ही छूट जाए। सोना भी पत्थर से ही उत्पन्न होता है, सो वह जलाए जाने पर भी अपने स्वभाव (सुवर्णत्व) को नहीं छोड़ता ॥
ramacharitamanas::466.english_translation: You have spoken truthfully: my body is born of the mountain, so stubbornness will not leave it even if the body falls away. Gold comes from stone; even when burned, it does not give up its nature.
ramacharitamanas::466.translation_literal: सत्य (truth) / कहेहु (you have said) / गिरिभव (born of the mountain) / तनु (body) / एहा (this) / हठ (stubbornness) / न (not) / छूट (will leave) / छूटै (may leave) / बरु (rather) / देहा (body) / कनकउ (gold also) / पुनि (again) / पषान (stone) / तें (from) / होई (becomes) / जारेहुँ (even when burned) / सहजु (natural nature) / न (not) / परिहर (abandons) / सोई (that)
ramacharitamanas::466.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::466.essence: Deep nature survives pressure; force cannot easily remake it.
ramacharitamanas::466.simple_meaning: Parvati admits her stubborn resolve: even death will not change her nature. She compares herself to gold that keeps its essential quality even under fire.
ramacharitamanas::466.simple_insight: Some traits run so deep that pressure only reveals them more clearly.
ramacharitamanas::466.detailed_meaning: Parvati answers the earlier praise of an ideal bride by speaking with fierce honesty. She says her mountain-born nature is fixed, and even if her body perishes, her resolve will not change. The verse sets up the deeper question of whether her will can align with the teaching that follows.
ramacharitamanas::466.modern_relevance: You keep saying you'll soften, compromise, and let it go. Then the same old reaction returns in the first hard conversation. Parvati names that deep pattern without pretending it is easy to erase.
ramacharitamanas::466.insight: It shifts attention from surface promises to the enduring shape of character under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::467.verse_sanskrit: नारद बचन न मैं परिहरऊँ। बसउ भवनु उजरउ नहिं डरउँ॥ गुर कें बचन प्रतीति न जेही। सपनेहुँ सुगम न सुख सिधि तेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::467.verse_hindi: अतः मैं नारदजी के वचनों को नहीं छोड़ूँगी, चाहे घर बसे या उजड़े, इससे मैं नहीं डरती। जिसको गुरु के वचनों में विश्वास नहीं है, उसको सुख और सिद्धि स्वप्न में भी सुगम नहीं होती ॥
ramacharitamanas::467.english_translation: I will not abandon Narad's words. I do not fear whether the home stands or falls. One who does not trust the guru's words cannot easily find happiness or success, even in dreams.
ramacharitamanas::467.translation_literal: नारद (Narad) / बचन (words) / न (not) / मैं (I) / परिहरऊँ (abandon) / बसउ (let it remain built) / भवनु (home) / उजरउ (let it be destroyed) / नहिं (not) / डरउँ (I fear) / गुर (guru) / कें (of) / बचन (words) / प्रतीति (trust) / न (not) / जेही (one who has) / सपनेहुँ (even in dreams) / सुगम (easy) / न (not) / सुख (happiness) / सिधि (success, attainment) / तेही (for that one)
ramacharitamanas::467.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::467.essence: Trust in guidance opens the door that effort alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::467.simple_meaning: Parvati says she will not abandon Narad's counsel, even if her home is ruined. Trust in the guru's words is what makes happiness and success possible.
ramacharitamanas::467.simple_insight: There is relief in stopping the inner argument and leaning into guidance you already trust.
ramacharitamanas::467.detailed_meaning: In Shiva's telling of the marriage story, Parvati responds to Narad's warning with complete confidence. She says she will not reject his words, even if it costs her comfort or security. The verse turns on trust in the guru as the doorway to fulfilment.
ramacharitamanas::467.modern_relevance: Your mentor gives you hard advice that doesn't flatter you. You can keep defending your old plan, or you can let the guidance land and change course before the damage grows.
ramacharitamanas::467.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to receptivity, making guidance more important than comfort.

ramacharitamanas::468.verse_sanskrit: महादेव अवगुन भवन बिष्नु सकल गुन धाम। जेहि कर मनु रम जाहि सन तेहि तेही सन काम ॥
ramacharitamanas::468.verse_hindi: माना कि महादेवजी अवगुणों के भवन हैं और विष्णु समस्त सद् गुणों के धाम हैं, पर जिसका मन जिसमें रम गया, उसको तो उसी से काम है ॥
ramacharitamanas::468.english_translation: Mahadev is the abode of faults and Vishnu the home of all virtues; yet the mind seeks whatever it is attached to.
ramacharitamanas::468.translation_literal: महादेव (Shiva) / अवगुन (faults) / भवन (abode) / बिष्नु (Vishnu) / सकल (all) / गुन (virtues) / धाम (home) / जेहि (whichever) / कर (of) / मनु (mind) / रम (is absorbed) / जाहि (goes) / सन (with) / तेहि (that) / तेही (that very) / सन (with) / काम (concern)
ramacharitamanas::468.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::468.essence: Love decides the mind’s allegiance more than praise or blame.
ramacharitamanas::468.simple_meaning: People are drawn to what their mind already loves. Labels about virtue or fault matter less than where the heart is actually settled.
ramacharitamanas::468.simple_insight: You stop arguing with appearances and notice what your mind is truly choosing.
ramacharitamanas::468.detailed_meaning: Parvati is pressing Shiva with a devotional paradox: even if one deity is praised as full of faults and another as full of virtues, the mind clings to the one it loves. The verse explains why devotion overrides comparison.
ramacharitamanas::468.modern_relevance: You keep saying you want one thing, but your browser history, late-night scrolling, and secret habits keep pulling you elsewhere. Your attention reveals your real devotion.
ramacharitamanas::468.insight: It shifts the reader from judging objects by reputation to examining where the mind repeatedly returns.

ramacharitamanas::469.verse_sanskrit: जौं तुम्ह मिलतेहु प्रथम मुनीसा। सुनतिउँ सिख तुम्हारि धरि सीसा॥ अब मैं जन्मु संभु हित हारा। को गुन दूषन करै बिचारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::469.verse_hindi: हे मुनीश्वरों! यदि आप पहले मिलते, तो मैं आपका उपदेश सिर-माथे रखकर सुनती, परन्तु अब तो मैं अपना जन्म शिवजी के लिए हार चुकी! फिर गुण-दोषों का विचार कौन करे? ॥
ramacharitamanas::469.english_translation: O sages, if you had come first, I would have held your teaching to my head. But now I have given my life to Shiva. Who would still weigh virtues and faults?
ramacharitamanas::469.translation_literal: जौं (if) / तुम्ह (you) / मिलतेहु (had met) / प्रथम (first) / मुनीसा (O sages) / सुनतिउँ (I would have heard) / सिख (teaching) / तुम्हारि (your) / धरि (placing) / सीसा (head) / अब (now) / मैं (I) / जन्मु (life / birth) / संभु (Shiva) / हित (for the sake of) / हारा (have lost / given up) / को (who) / गुन (virtue) / दूषन (fault) / करै (does) / बिचारा (consideration)
ramacharitamanas::469.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::469.essence: Once the heart has chosen, fault-finding loses its power.
ramacharitamanas::469.simple_meaning: Parvati says she would have listened to the sages earlier, but now she has given herself to Shiva, so judging by merits and faults no longer matters to her.
ramacharitamanas::469.simple_insight: Love can make old calculations feel irrelevant.
ramacharitamanas::469.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, Parvati answers the sages with complete devotion to Shiva. She says timing has already decided her heart: if they had come before, she would have listened differently, but now her life belongs to Shiva, so arguments about qualities and flaws have lost force.
ramacharitamanas::469.modern_relevance: You already chose your person, your path, your promise. At that point, endless comparison stops feeling wise and starts feeling disloyal.
ramacharitamanas::469.insight: It shifts attention from weighing options to honoring the commitment already made.

ramacharitamanas::470.verse_sanskrit: जौं तुम्हरे हठ हृदयँ बिसेषी। रहि न जाइ बिनु किएँ बरेषी॥ तौ कौतुकिअन्ह आलसु नाहीं। बर कन्या अनेक जग माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::470.verse_hindi: यदि आपके हृदय में बहुत ही हठ है और विवाह की बातचीत (बरेखी) किए बिना आपसे रहा ही नहीं जाता, तो संसार में वर-कन्या बहुत हैं। खिलवाड़ करने वालों को आलस्य तो होता नहीं (और कहीं जाकर कीजिए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::470.english_translation: If your heart is so stubborn that you cannot stop without a formal proposal, then there are many brides and grooms in the world. Let the playful ones take no rest.
ramacharitamanas::470.translation_literal: जौं (if) / तुम्हरे (your) / हठ (stubbornness) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिसेषी (very much) / रहि न जाइ (cannot remain) / बिनु किएँ (without doing) / बरेषी (formal proposal / matchmaking) / तौ (then) / कौतुकिअन्ह (for the playful ones) / आलसु (laziness / rest) / नाहीं (not) / बर (groom) / कन्या (bride) / अनेक (many) / जग (world) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::470.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::470.essence: Dignity can answer pressure with a smile.
ramacharitamanas::470.simple_meaning: Sita says that if someone insists on a formal marriage proposal, there are plenty of other brides and grooms in the world. She answers with sharp wit, not submission.
ramacharitamanas::470.simple_insight: You can answer pressure with dignity and humor instead of yielding.
ramacharitamanas::470.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the marriage challenge has become a test of will. Sita speaks back to the demand for formal matchmaking with calm irony, refusing to be treated as one more ordinary choice. Her words keep the exchange alive and sharpen the tension before the decisive vow.
ramacharitamanas::470.modern_relevance: A relative keeps pushing, “So when are you settling down?” You smile, but you do not bend. Sita’s reply is the voice of self-respect under pressure.
ramacharitamanas::470.insight: It teaches you to hold your ground without anger, using wit to protect your dignity.

ramacharitamanas::471.verse_sanskrit: जन्म कोटि लगि रगर हमारी। बरउँ संभु न त रहउँ कुआरी॥ तजउँ न नारद कर उपदेसू। आपु कहहिं सत बार महेसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::471.verse_hindi: मेरा तो करोड़ जन्मों तक यही हठ रहेगा कि या तो शिवजी को वरूँगी, नहीं तो कुमारी ही रहूँगी। स्वयं शिवजी सौ बार कहें, तो भी नारदजी के उपदेश को न छोड़ूँगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::471.english_translation: My resolve will last for countless births: I will marry Shiva, or remain unmarried. I will not abandon Narada's counsel, even if Shiva himself speaks a hundred times.
ramacharitamanas::471.translation_literal: जन्म (births) / कोटि (crores, countless) / लगि (for) / रगर (resolve, stubborn vow) / हमारी (my) / बरउँ (I marry) / संभु (Shiva) / न (or not) / त (then) / रहउँ (I remain) / कुआरी (unmarried maiden)॥ / तजउँ (I abandon) / न (not) / नारद (Narada) / कर (of) / उपदेसू (counsel) / आपु (himself) / कहहिं (says) / सत (hundred) / बार (times) / महेसू (Shiva)॥
ramacharitamanas::471.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::471.essence: True devotion does not bend just because the pressure repeats.
ramacharitamanas::471.simple_meaning: Parvati says her vow is fixed: she will marry Shiva or stay unmarried forever. She will not give up Narada's advice, even if Shiva says otherwise many times.
ramacharitamanas::471.simple_insight: A sincere vow can become stronger than pressure, fear, or repetition.
ramacharitamanas::471.detailed_meaning: Parvati is answering the sages in the Shiva frame of Balkand. She declares that her heart is set on Shiva alone, and she will not turn away from Narada's guidance. The scene shows devotion becoming resolve before the marriage is complete.
ramacharitamanas::471.modern_relevance: A family keeps pushing you toward the “practical” choice, but you already know what your heart has chosen. Parvati’s steadiness is the courage to stay with a vow under pressure.
ramacharitamanas::471.insight: It shifts the mind from external persuasion to inner commitment.

ramacharitamanas::472.verse_sanskrit: मैं पा परउँ कहइ जगदंबा। तुम्ह गृह गवनहु भयउ बिलंबा॥ देखि प्रेमु बोले मुनि ग्यानी। जय जय जगदंबिके भवानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::472.verse_hindi: जगज्जननी पार्वतीजी ने फिर कहा कि मैं आपके पैरों पड़ती हूँ। आप अपने घर जाइए, बहुत देर हो गई। (शिवजी में पार्वतीजी का ऐसा) प्रेम देखकर ज्ञानी मुनि बोले- हे जगज्जननी! हे भवानी! आपकी जय हो! जय हो!! ॥
ramacharitamanas::472.english_translation: The Mother of the universe said, “I bow at your feet. Please go home; it has grown late.” Seeing such love, the wise sage exclaimed, “Victory, victory to the Mother of the universe, Bhavani!”
ramacharitamanas::472.translation_literal: मैं (I) / पा परउँ (I bow down) / कहइ (said) / जगदंबा (Mother of the universe) / तुम्ह (you) / गृह (home) / गवनहु (go) / भयउ (became) / बिलंबा (delay) / देखि (seeing) / प्रेमु (love) / बोले (said) / मुनि (sage) / ग्यानी (wise) / जय जय (victory, victory) / जगदंबिके (to the Mother of the universe) / भवानी (Bhavani)
ramacharitamanas::472.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::472.essence: True love bows, even while asking someone to leave.
ramacharitamanas::472.simple_meaning: Parvati lovingly asks Shiva to go home, and the sage responds with praise at her devotion.
ramacharitamanas::472.simple_insight: Love can be humble without losing strength.
ramacharitamanas::472.detailed_meaning: In the Shiva-Parvati frame of Balkand, Parvati speaks with tenderness, bowing even as she gently sends Shiva home. A sage watching this exchange is moved by her love and breaks into praise, revealing how sacred their devotion appears.
ramacharitamanas::472.modern_relevance: You keep one eye on the clock while someone you love lingers at the door, unwilling to end the moment. Real affection can be soft, patient, and still direct.
ramacharitamanas::472.insight: It shows that reverence and intimacy can exist together without conflict.

ramacharitamanas::473.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह माया भगवान सिव सकल गजत पितु मातु। नाइ चरन सिर मुनि चले पुनि पुनि हरषत गातु ॥
ramacharitamanas::473.verse_hindi: आप माया हैं और शिवजी भगवान हैं। आप दोनों समस्त जगत के माता-पिता हैं। (यह कहकर) मुनि पार्वतीजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर चल दिए। उनके शरीर बार-बार पुलकित हो रहे थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::473.english_translation: You are the divine veil, and Shiva and the entire world are your father and mother. After bowing to Parvati's feet, the sages departed, their bodies trembling with repeated joy.
ramacharitamanas::473.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / माया (the veil of appearance) / भगवान (the divine) / सिव (Shiva) / सकल (entire) / गजत (world) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / नाइ (bowing) / चरन (feet) / सिर (head) / मुनि (sages) / चले (went) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / हरषत (rejoicing) / गातु (body)
ramacharitamanas::473.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::473.essence: Humility ends the exchange; joy remains.
ramacharitamanas::473.simple_meaning: The sages honor Parvati respectfully and leave, filled with joy. The scene closes the exchange between Parvati and Shiva's framing narration.
ramacharitamanas::473.simple_insight: Respect can end a sacred exchange cleanly, leaving only joy behind.
ramacharitamanas::473.detailed_meaning: Parvati has just spoken with deep devotion in Shiva's frame narrative. The sages respond with reverence, bow to her feet, and depart. Their joy shows the scene is moving from dialogue into the next part of the story.
ramacharitamanas::473.modern_relevance: You finish a heartfelt conversation, lower your head in gratitude, and walk away lighter than before. Some moments do not need more explanation.
ramacharitamanas::473.insight: It shifts the reader from argument to reverence, showing how humility ends tension.

ramacharitamanas::474.verse_sanskrit: जाइ मुनिन्ह हिमवंतु पठाए। करि बिनती गिरजहिं गृह ल्याए॥ बहुरि सप्तरिषि सिव पहिं जाई। कथा उमा कै सकल सुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::474.verse_hindi: मुनियों ने जाकर हिमवान् को पार्वतीजी के पास भेजा और वे विनती करके उनको घर ले आए, फिर सप्तर्षियों ने शिवजी के पास जाकर उनको पार्वतीजी की सारी कथा सुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::474.english_translation: The sages went and sent Himavan to Parvati. They persuaded her and brought her home. Then the seven sages went to Shiva and told him all of Uma's story.
ramacharitamanas::474.translation_literal: जाइ (going) / मुनिन्ह (by the sages) / हिमवंतु (Himavan) / पठाए (was sent) / करि (doing) / बिनती (request) / गिरजहिं (Parvati) / गृह (home) / ल्याए (brought) / बहुरि (then) / सप्तरिषि (the seven sages) / सिव पहिं (to Shiva) / जाई (going) / कथा (story) / उमा कै (of Uma) / सकल (all) / सुनाई (told)
ramacharitamanas::474.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::474.essence: Reconciliation often begins when one wise messenger carries the whole story.
ramacharitamanas::474.simple_meaning: The sages first bring Himavan to Parvati, then go to Shiva and explain everything that happened with Uma.
ramacharitamanas::474.simple_insight: Some situations need patient mediation before anyone can hear the full truth.
ramacharitamanas::474.detailed_meaning: Parvati has just asked Shiva to let her return home. The sages act as go-betweens: they send for Himavan, bring Parvati back with respectful persuasion, then report the whole matter to Shiva. The verse moves the frame story forward, not the teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::474.modern_relevance: A family argument cools only after one trusted person talks to each side separately. Before resolution comes, someone has to carry the story carefully.
ramacharitamanas::474.insight: It shows the value of mediation: separate hearts are reached one by one before harmony returns.

ramacharitamanas::475.verse_sanskrit: भए मगन सिव सुनत सनेहा। हरषि सप्तरिषि गवने गेहा॥ मनु थिर करि तब संभु सुजाना। लगे करन रघुनायक ध्याना ॥
ramacharitamanas::475.verse_hindi: पार्वतीजी का प्रेम सुनते ही शिवजी आनन्दमग्न हो गए। सप्तर्षि प्रसन्न होकर अपने घर (ब्रह्मलोक) को चले गए। तब सुजान शिवजी मन को स्थिर करके श्री रघुनाथजी का ध्यान करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::475.english_translation: Shiva became absorbed with joy on hearing of Parvati's love. The Saptarishis, pleased, returned to their home. Then wise Shiva steadied his mind and began meditating on Raghunath.
ramacharitamanas::475.translation_literal: भए (became) / मगन (absorbed, delighted) / सिव (Shiva) / सुनत (hearing) / सनेहा (love, affection) / हरषि (rejoicing) / सप्तरिषि (Saptarishis) / गवने (went) / गेहा (home) / मनु (mind) / थिर (steady) / करि (making) / तब (then) / संभु (Shiva) / सुजाना (wise one) / लगे (began) / करन (to do) / रघुनायक (Raghunath, Lord of Raghu) / ध्याना (meditation)
ramacharitamanas::475.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::475.essence: Joy in love naturally settles into meditation on Ram.
ramacharitamanas::475.simple_meaning: Shiva feels joy on hearing about Parvati's love, and then turns his steady mind toward meditating on Ram.
ramacharitamanas::475.simple_insight: Love naturally turns attention toward the beloved. Joy becomes quieter, deeper devotion.
ramacharitamanas::475.detailed_meaning: After Parvati's loving exchange, Shiva is moved with delight. The Saptarishis leave, and in that calm opening Shiva gathers his mind and begins meditating on Ram. The scene shifts from shared affection to focused bhakti.
ramacharitamanas::475.modern_relevance: You hear someone speak warmly about the person you revere, and your whole mood softens. After the room empties, you sit quietly and return to the one presence that steadies you.
ramacharitamanas::475.insight: It shifts devotion from emotion alone into settled remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::476.verse_sanskrit: तारकु असुर भयउ तेहि काला। भुज प्रताप बल तेज बिसाला॥ तेहिं सब लोक लोकपति जीते। भए देव सुख संपति रीते ॥
ramacharitamanas::476.verse_hindi: उसी समय तारक नाम का असुर हुआ, जिसकी भुजाओं का बल, प्रताप और तेज बहुत बड़ा था। उसने सब लोक और लोकपालों को जीत लिया, सब देवता सुख और सम्पत्ति से रहित हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::476.english_translation: At that time, the demon Taraka arose, immense in arm-strength, power, and radiance. He conquered all worlds and their rulers, and the radiant beings were stripped of joy and prosperity.
ramacharitamanas::476.translation_literal: तारकु (Taraka) / असुर (demon) / भयउ (became) / तेहि काला (at that time) / भुज (arms) / प्रताप (splendor, power) / बल (strength) / तेज (radiance) / बिसाला (vast) / तेहिं (he) / सब (all) / लोक (worlds) / लोकपति (lords of worlds) / जीते (conquered) / भए (became) / देव (radiant beings) / सुख (happiness) / संपति (prosperity) / रीते (deprived, empty)
ramacharitamanas::476.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::476.essence: Unchecked power empties the world around it.
ramacharitamanas::476.simple_meaning: Taraka, a powerful demon, rose at that time and conquered all the worlds, leaving the radiant beings deprived of joy and prosperity.
ramacharitamanas::476.simple_insight: Power without restraint spreads suffering until it is checked.
ramacharitamanas::476.detailed_meaning: The story shifts back to an older cosmic crisis: Taraka has become so strong that even the rulers of the worlds cannot stop him. The radiant beings are left helpless, setting up the need for divine intervention in the next verse.
ramacharitamanas::476.modern_relevance: A person or system grows unchecked, dominates every room, and leaves everyone else drained. The danger is not just strength — it is strength without limits.
ramacharitamanas::476.insight: It frames oppression as the natural result of power severed from restraint.

ramacharitamanas::477.verse_sanskrit: अजर अमर सो जीति न जाई। हारे सुर करि बिबिध लराई॥ तब बिरंचि सन जाइ पुकारे। देखे बिधि सब देव दुखारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::477.verse_hindi: वह अजर-अमर था, इसलिए किसी से जीता नहीं जाता था। देवता उसके साथ बहुत तरह की लड़ाइयाँ लड़कर हार गए। तब उन्होंने ब्रह्माजी के पास जाकर पुकार मचाई। ब्रह्माजी ने सब देवताओं को दुःखी देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::477.english_translation: He was deathless, so no one could defeat him. The radiant beings fought him in many ways and lost. Then they went to Brahma and cried out for help. Brahma saw all the radiant beings in sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::477.translation_literal: अजर (deathless) / अमर (undying) / सो (that one) / जीति (defeated) / न (not) / जाई (can be) / हारे (lost) / सुर (radiant beings) / करि (having done) / बिबिध (various) / लराई (battles) / तब (then) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / सन (to) / जाइ (going) / पुकारे (cried out) / देखे (saw) / बिधि (Brahma) / सब (all) / देव (radiant beings) / दुखारे (grieved)
ramacharitamanas::477.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::477.essence: Force fails against what cannot yet be ended.
ramacharitamanas::477.simple_meaning: That demon could not be defeated because he had no death. The radiant beings tried many battles and still lost, so they went to Brahma for help.
ramacharitamanas::477.simple_insight: Some problems cannot be solved by force alone; you need to see the deeper cause.
ramacharitamanas::477.detailed_meaning: Tarak has become unstoppable, and even the radiant beings have failed against him. Defeated and distressed, they go to Brahma for guidance. This verse sets up the crisis before the solution is revealed in the next line.
ramacharitamanas::477.modern_relevance: You keep trying the same fix on the same problem, and nothing changes. At some point, the answer is not more force — it is a wiser question.
ramacharitamanas::477.insight: It shifts attention from repeated struggle to the need for a deeper remedy.

ramacharitamanas::478.verse_sanskrit: सब सन कहा बुझाइ बिधि दनुज निधन तब होइ। संभु सुक्र संभूत सुत एहि जीतइ रन सोइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::478.verse_hindi: ब्रह्माजी ने सबको समझाकर कहा- इस दैत्य की मृत्यु तब होगी जब शिवजी के वीर्य से पुत्र उत्पन्न हो, इसको युद्ध में वही जीतेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::478.english_translation: Brahma explained to everyone: this demon will die only when a son is born from Shiva's seed; only he will defeat him in battle.
ramacharitamanas::478.translation_literal: सब (everyone) / सन (to) / कहा (said) / बुझाइ (explaining) / बिधि (Brahma) / दनुज (demon) / निधन (death) / तब (then) / होइ (will happen) / संभु (Shiva) / सुक्र (seed) / संभूत (born) / सुत (son) / एहि (this) / जीतइ (will defeat) / रन (battle) / सोइ (that one)
ramacharitamanas::478.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::478.essence: The enemy falls only when the right cause is born.
ramacharitamanas::478.simple_meaning: Brahma tells the gods that the demon can only be killed by a son born from Shiva's power.
ramacharitamanas::478.simple_insight: Some problems cannot be solved by force alone; the right cause must first appear.
ramacharitamanas::478.detailed_meaning: Brahma is answering the gods after Taraka has defeated the worlds. He explains the hidden condition for Taraka's death: only a son born from Shiva can destroy him. The verse is part of the larger plan, not the climax itself.
ramacharitamanas::478.modern_relevance: A team keeps trying the same fixes and nothing changes. Then someone finally names the real condition that must exist before the problem can end.
ramacharitamanas::478.insight: It shifts attention from repeated effort to the deeper cause that must be created first.

ramacharitamanas::479.verse_sanskrit: मोर कहा सुनि करहु उपाई। होइहि ईस्वर करिहि सहाई॥ सतीं जो तजी दच्छ मख देहा। जनमी जाइ हिमाचल गेहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::479.verse_hindi: मेरी बात सुनकर उपाय करो। ईश्वर सहायता करेंगे और काम हो जाएगा। सतीजी ने जो दक्ष के यज्ञ में देह का त्याग किया था, उन्होंने अब हिमाचल के घर जाकर जन्म लिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::479.english_translation: Listen to my words and take a remedy. The divine will help, and the task will be done. Sati, who gave up her body in Daksha's sacrifice, has now been born in Himachal's house.
ramacharitamanas::479.translation_literal: मोर (my) / कहा (words) / सुनि (hearing) / करहु (do) / उपाई (remedy, means) / होइहि (will happen) / ईस्वर (the divine) / करिहि (will do) / सहाई (help) / सतीं (Sati) / जो (who) / तजी (gave up) / दच्छ (Daksha) / मख (sacrifice) / देहा (body) / जनमी (was born) / जाइ (going) / हिमाचल (Himachal) / गेहा (house)
ramacharitamanas::479.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::479.essence: Help arrives when the larger order is trusted.
ramacharitamanas::479.simple_meaning: Shiva tells Parvati to trust the divine help and explains that Sati has now taken birth in Himachal's home after leaving her previous body.
ramacharitamanas::479.simple_insight: Even impossible turns begin with trust and the right next step.
ramacharitamanas::479.detailed_meaning: In Shiva's frame narration, the gods are seeking a way to defeat the invincible demon. Shiva speaks of a remedy and then points to Sati's rebirth in Himachal's house, setting up the larger story of how divine purpose will unfold through her next life.
ramacharitamanas::479.modern_relevance: You are staring at a problem that feels sealed shut. Someone wiser says: stop forcing the whole answer, take the next right step, and let help arrive in its own time.
ramacharitamanas::479.insight: It shifts the mind from panic to trust in a larger order already at work.

ramacharitamanas::480.verse_sanskrit: तेहिं तपु कीन्ह संभु पति लागी। सिव समाधि बैठे सबु त्यागी॥ जदपि अहइ असमंजस भारी। तदपि बात एक सुनहु हमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::480.verse_hindi: उन्होंने शिवजी को पति बनाने के लिए तप किया है, इधर शिवजी सब छोड़-छाड़कर समाधि लगा बैठे हैं। यद्यपि है तो बड़े असमंजस की बात, तथापि मेरी एक बात सुनो ॥
ramacharitamanas::480.english_translation: She performed austerity to win Shiva as husband. Shiva sat in meditation, abandoning everything. Though the situation is highly puzzling, still listen to my one suggestion.
ramacharitamanas::480.translation_literal: तेहिं (then/by that) / तपु (austerity) / कीन्ह (did) / संभु (Shiva) / पति (husband) / लागी (for) / सिव (Shiva) / समाधि (meditative absorption) / बैठे (sat) / सबु (all) / त्यागी (having abandoned) / जदपि (although) / अहइ (is) / असमंजस (puzzling) / भारी (great) / तदपि (still) / बात (matter) / एक (one) / सुनहु (listen) / हमारी (our/my)
ramacharitamanas::480.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::480.essence: A blocked situation needs a clear next move, not panic.
ramacharitamanas::480.simple_meaning: Parvati is describing a strange situation: she has done austerity for Shiva, but Shiva remains absorbed in meditation and detached from everything. She is about to propose a way forward.
ramacharitamanas::480.simple_insight: Even a tangled problem can open when someone is willing to listen carefully.
ramacharitamanas::480.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, Parvati is hearing the cosmic backstory of her own marriage to Shiva. The issue is impossible on the surface: one side has done severe austerity, the other sits withdrawn in meditation. This verse sets up the plan that will break the deadlock.
ramacharitamanas::480.modern_relevance: Two people want the same future, but one is withdrawn and unreachable. Before forcing a solution, someone has to name the problem clearly and listen for the next right move.
ramacharitamanas::480.insight: It shifts attention from the impossible-looking situation to the first practical step that can change it.

ramacharitamanas::481.verse_sanskrit: पठवहु कामु जाइ सिव पाहीं। करै छोभु संकर मन माहीं॥ तब हम जाइ सिवहि सिर नाई। करवाउब बिबाहु बरिआई ॥
ramacharitamanas::481.verse_hindi: तुम जाकर कामदेव को शिवजी के पास भेजो, वह शिवजी के मन में क्षोभ उत्पन्न करे (उनकी समाधि भंग करे)। तब हम जाकर शिवजी के चरणों में सिर रख देंगे और जबरदस्ती (उन्हें राजी करके) विवाह करा देंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::481.english_translation: Send Kama to Shiva. Let him stir Shiva's mind. Then we will go bow to Shiva and arrange the marriage by force.
ramacharitamanas::481.translation_literal: पठवहु (send) / कामु (Kama) / जाइ (going) / सिव (Shiva) / पाहीं (to) / करै (may do) / छोभु (disturbance) / संकर (Shankar) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / तब (then) / हम (we) / जाइ (going) / सिवहि (to Shiva) / सिर (head) / नाई (bowing) / करवाउब (we will get done) / बिबाहु (marriage) / बरिआई (by force)
ramacharitamanas::481.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::481.essence: Great aims often need both strategy and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::481.simple_meaning: The gods decide to send Kama to disturb Shiva's deep meditation, then bow to Shiva and press for the marriage.
ramacharitamanas::481.simple_insight: Sometimes action begins with patience, then moves with respect and courage.
ramacharitamanas::481.detailed_meaning: The gods are trying to unite Shiva and Parvati, but Shiva is still absorbed in meditation. They settle on a bold plan: send Kama to unsettle Shiva first, then approach him humbly and arrange the marriage.
ramacharitamanas::481.modern_relevance: A team knows the main decision-maker is deeply set in a position. Instead of forcing the issue, they first prepare the ground, then approach with respect and a clear plan.
ramacharitamanas::481.insight: It shows that wise action can combine strategy, humility, and timing.

ramacharitamanas::482.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि भलेहिं देवहित होई। मत अति नीक कहइ सबु कोई॥ अस्तुति सुरन्ह कीन्हि अति हेतू। प्रगटेउ बिषमबान झषकेतू ॥
ramacharitamanas::482.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार से भले ही देवताओं का हित हो (और तो कोई उपाय नहीं है) सबने कहा- यह सम्मति बहुत अच्छी है। फिर देवताओं ने बड़े प्रेम से स्तुति की। तब विषम (पाँच) बाण धारण करने वाला और मछली के चिह्नयुक्त ध्वजा वाला कामदेव प्रकट हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::482.english_translation: In this way, everyone agreed that this was the best course for the gods' welfare. Then the gods praised him with deep affection, and Kamadeva appeared, bearing five arrows and the banner marked with a fish.
ramacharitamanas::482.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / भलेहिं (indeed good) / देवहित (for the welfare of the gods) / होई (becomes) । / मत (opinion) / अति (very) / नीक (good) / कहइ (says) / सबु (everyone) / कोई (one) ॥ / अस्तुति (praise) / सुरन्ह (by the gods) / कीन्हि (did) / अति (very) / हेतू (with affection) । / प्रगटेउ (appeared) / बिषमबान (five-arrowed one) / झषकेतू (fish-bannered one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::482.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::482.essence: A risky plan becomes clear when everyone agrees to the cost.
ramacharitamanas::482.simple_meaning: The gods agree that this plan is best for them, and they praise Kamadeva so he will appear and help.
ramacharitamanas::482.simple_insight: Sometimes a difficult goal feels justified only after everyone risks something together.
ramacharitamanas::482.detailed_meaning: The gods have decided that only Kamadeva can disturb Shiva's meditation. After their affectionate praise, Kamadeva appears, ready to take on the dangerous task that will move the story toward Sita's marriage.
ramacharitamanas::482.modern_relevance: A group chat settles on the one uncomfortable plan nobody loves but everyone knows is necessary. Then someone steps up to do the hard part, and the whole room exhales.
ramacharitamanas::482.insight: It frames the mission as a collective choice and prepares for decisive action.

ramacharitamanas::483.verse_sanskrit: सुरन्ह कही निज बिपति सब सुनि मन कीन्ह बिचार। संभु बिरोध न कुसल मोहि बिहसि कहेउ अस मार ॥
ramacharitamanas::483.verse_hindi: देवताओं ने कामदेव से अपनी सारी विपत्ति कही। सुनकर कामदेव ने मन में विचार किया और हँसकर देवताओं से यों कहा कि शिवजी के साथ विरोध करने में मेरी कुशल नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::483.english_translation: The gods told Kamadeva their whole plight. Hearing it, Kamadeva thought it over and laughed, saying, "I have no success in opposing Shiva."
ramacharitamanas::483.translation_literal: सुरन्ह (the gods) / कही (told) / निज (their own) / बिपति (trouble) / सब (all) / सुनि (hearing) / मन (mind) / कीन्ह (did) / बिचार (consideration) / संभु (Shiva) / बिरोध (opposition) / न (not) / कुसल (success) / मोहि (to me) / बिहसि (laughing) / कहेउ (said) / अस (thus) / मार (Kamadeva)
ramacharitamanas::483.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::483.essence: Clear seeing begins with admitting a force you cannot casually oppose.
ramacharitamanas::483.simple_meaning: The gods explain their problem to Kamadeva. He thinks it over and admits that opposing Shiva will not end well for him.
ramacharitamanas::483.simple_insight: Not every mission is worth forcing. Some resistance is wiser to respect than to challenge.
ramacharitamanas::483.detailed_meaning: The gods have asked Kamadeva to disturb Shiva's meditation so Parvati's marriage can proceed. After hearing their plea, Kamadeva pauses, weighs the danger, and laughs at the thought of confronting Shiva. This verse shows his awareness before he agrees to act.
ramacharitamanas::483.modern_relevance: Your friends want you to push a risky idea in a meeting, but you can already feel the room's resistance. Before speaking, you quietly assess whether the fight is worth it.
ramacharitamanas::483.insight: It shifts the mind from impulsive action to clear-eyed assessment of risk and consequence.

ramacharitamanas::484.verse_sanskrit: तदपि करब मैं काजु तुम्हारा। श्रुति कह परम धरम उपकारा॥ पर हित लागि तजइ जो देही। संतत संत प्रसंसहिं तेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::484.verse_hindi: तथापि मैं तुम्हारा काम तो करूँगा, क्योंकि वेद दूसरे के उपकार को परम धर्म कहते हैं। जो दूसरे के हित के लिए अपना शरीर त्याग देता है, संत सदा उसकी बड़ाई करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::484.english_translation: Still, I will do your work, because the Vedas call helping others the highest dharma. Those who give up their own body for another's good are always praised by the wise.
ramacharitamanas::484.translation_literal: तदपि (still) / करब (will do) / मैं (I) / काजु (work) / तुम्हारा (your) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / कह (say) / परम (highest) / धरम (dharma) / उपकारा (helping others) / पर हित (for another's good) / लागि (for the sake of) / तजइ (abandons) / जो (who) / देही (body) / संतत (always) / संत (the wise) / प्रसंसहिं (praise) / तेही (that one)
ramacharitamanas::484.speaker: Kamadeva
ramacharitamanas::484.essence: Helping another is the highest law of action.
ramacharitamanas::484.simple_meaning: Helping others is the highest duty. A person who gives up even his own body for someone else's good is praised by good people.
ramacharitamanas::484.simple_insight: There is dignity in putting another person's welfare before your own comfort.
ramacharitamanas::484.detailed_meaning: Kamadeva has been urged to act for the gods' benefit despite the danger. He answers that helping others is the highest duty, and that self-sacrifice for another's good wins the praise of the wise.
ramacharitamanas::484.modern_relevance: You stay late to finish a task that protects your team, even though no one can repay you. The quiet respect you feel afterward is exactly what this verse honors.
ramacharitamanas::484.insight: It shifts action from self-protection to service, treating sacrifice for others as the mark of a noble life.

ramacharitamanas::485.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि चलेउ सबहि सिरु नाई। सुमन धनुष कर सहित सहाई॥ चलत मार अस हृदयँ बिचारा। सिव बिरोध ध्रुब मरनु हमारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::485.verse_hindi: यों कह और सबको सिर नवाकर कामदेव अपने पुष्प के धनुष को हाथ में लेकर (वसन्तादि) सहायकों के साथ चला। चलते समय कामदेव ने हृदय में ऐसा विचार किया कि शिवजी के साथ विरोध करने से मेरा मरण निश्चित है ॥
ramacharitamanas::485.english_translation: Saying this, he bowed to everyone and departed with his flower-bow and helpers. As he walked, Kama thought in his heart, "Opposing Shiva means certain death for me."
ramacharitamanas::485.translation_literal: अस कहि (saying thus) / चलेउ (departed) / सबहि (to everyone) / सिरु नाई (bowing the head) / सुमन धनुष (flower-bow) / कर (in hand) / सहित (with) / सहाई (helpers) / चलत (while walking) / मार (Kama) / अस (thus) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारा (thought) / सिव (Shiva) / बिरोध (opposition) / ध्रुब (certain) / मरनु (death) / हमारा (my)
ramacharitamanas::485.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::485.essence: He goes forward knowing the cost may be his life.
ramacharitamanas::485.simple_meaning: Kama leaves respectfully with his helpers, but he knows opposing Shiva will surely destroy him.
ramacharitamanas::485.simple_insight: Even bold action can carry quiet fear underneath.
ramacharitamanas::485.detailed_meaning: Kama has agreed to help the devas and now sets out with his flower-bow and companions. But as he walks, he privately recognizes the danger: challenging Shiva will likely mean his death. The verse builds tension before the confrontation.
ramacharitamanas::485.modern_relevance: You say yes to a hard task, then feel the knot in your stomach as you walk into the meeting. Courage and fear can travel together.
ramacharitamanas::485.insight: It shows that commitment can continue even when the mind foresees danger.

ramacharitamanas::486.verse_sanskrit: तब आपन प्रभाउ बिस्तारा। निज बस कीन्ह सकल संसारा॥ कोपेउ जबहिं बारिचरकेतू। छन महुँ मिटे सकल श्रुति सेतू ॥
ramacharitamanas::486.verse_hindi: तब उसने अपना प्रभाव फैलाया और समस्त संसार को अपने वश में कर लिया। जिस समय उस मछली के चिह्न की ध्वजा वाले कामदेव ने कोप किया, उस समय क्षणभर में ही वेदों की सारी मर्यादा मिट गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::486.english_translation: Then he spread his influence and brought the whole world under his control. When Kamadeva, whose flag bears the fish emblem, grew angry, the boundary set by the Vedas vanished in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::486.translation_literal: तब (then) / आपन (own) / प्रभाउ (influence) / बिस्तारा (spread) / निज (own) / बस (control) / कीन्ह (made) / सकल (entire) / संसार (world) / कोपेउ (became angry) / जबहिं (when) / बारिचरकेतू (fish-bannered one) / छन महुँ (in an instant) / मिटे (were erased) / सकल (all) / श्रुति (Vedic) / सेतू (boundary)
ramacharitamanas::486.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::486.essence: Desire can erase discipline in a moment.
ramacharitamanas::486.simple_meaning: Kamadeva spreads his power over the world, and when he becomes angry, even the limits set by the Vedas collapse at once.
ramacharitamanas::486.simple_insight: Unchecked desire can sweep away restraint before reason even notices.
ramacharitamanas::486.detailed_meaning: Kamadeva has arrived to disturb Shiva's austerity. His influence spreads everywhere, and the very order protected by sacred discipline begins to break. This verse shows the force of desire before the next line lists the virtues that flee from it.
ramacharitamanas::486.modern_relevance: A single notification, one glance, one craving, and the whole careful plan you built at night can start unraveling before breakfast.
ramacharitamanas::486.insight: It shifts attention from outer order to the power of desire to dissolve inner discipline.

ramacharitamanas::487.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मचर्ज ब्रत संजम नाना। धीरज धरम ग्यान बिग्याना॥ सदाचार जप जोग बिरागा। सभय बिबेक कटकु सबु भागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::487.verse_hindi: ब्रह्मचर्य, नियम, नाना प्रकार के संयम, धीरज, धर्म, ज्ञान, विज्ञान, सदाचार, जप, योग, वैराग्य आदि विवेक की सारी सेना डरकर भाग गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::487.english_translation: Many forms of self-restraint, patience, dharma, knowledge, discernment, right conduct, chanting, yoga, and detachment all fled in fear; the whole army of clear seeing ran away.
ramacharitamanas::487.translation_literal: ब्रह्मचर्ज (celibacy/self-restraint) / ब्रत (vows) / संजम (restraint) / नाना (many kinds) / धीरज (patience) / धरम (dharma) / ग्यान (knowledge) / बिग्याना (discernment) / सदाचार (right conduct) / जप (chanting) / जोग (yoga) / बिरागा (detachment) / सभय (fearful) / बिबेक (clear seeing/discernment) / कटकु (army) / सबु (all) / भागा (fled)
ramacharitamanas::487.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::487.essence: Craving can rout every discipline the mind has built.
ramacharitamanas::487.simple_meaning: Desire can overwhelm even the best habits and insights. When the mind is seized by craving, restraint, discernment, and discipline all collapse at once.
ramacharitamanas::487.simple_insight: It reminds you how quickly self-control can vanish when desire takes over.
ramacharitamanas::487.detailed_meaning: As Kamadeva’s influence spreads in the Sita-swayamvar scene, even the strongest inner disciplines are shown retreating. Brahmacharya, vows, patience, knowledge, right conduct, chanting, yoga, and detachment cannot stand against the force now moving through the world.
ramacharitamanas::487.modern_relevance: You open one app “just for a minute,” and an hour disappears. The habits you trusted most feel weak in front of a single craving.
ramacharitamanas::487.insight: It shifts attention from moral ideals to the power that can suddenly sweep them aside.

ramacharitamanas::488.verse_sanskrit: भागेउ बिबेकु सहाय सहित सो सुभट संजुग महि मुरे। सदग्रंथ पर्बत कंदरन्हि महुँ जाइ तेहि अवसर दुरे॥ होनिहार का करतार को रखवार जग खरभरु परा। दुइ माथ केहि रतिनाथ जेहि कहुँ कोपि कर धनु सरु धरा॥
ramacharitamanas::488.verse_hindi: विवेक अपने सहायकों सहित भाग गया, उसके योद्धा रणभूमि से पीठ दिखा गए। उस समय वे सब सद्ग्रन्थ रूपी पर्वत की कन्दराओं में जा छिपे (अर्थात ज्ञान, वैराग्य, संयम, नियम, सदाचारादि ग्रंथों में ही लिखे रह गए, उनका आचरण छूट गया)। सारे जगत् में खलबली मच गई (और सब कहने लगे) हे विधाता! अब क्या होने वाला है? हमारी रक्षा कौन करेगा? ऐसा दो सिर वाला कौन है, जिसके लिए रति के पति कामदेव ने कोप करके हाथ में धनुष-बाण उठाया है?
ramacharitamanas::488.english_translation: Wisdom fled with its helpers; its warriors turned back in battle. They hid in the caves of the sacred texts. The world fell into turmoil: “Who will protect us now? What two-headed being is this, for whom the lord of desire has raised bow and arrows in anger?”
ramacharitamanas::488.translation_literal: भागेउ (fled) / बिबेकु (wisdom, clear seeing) / सहाय सहित (with helpers) / सो (those) / सुभट (warriors) / संजुग (in battle) / महि (on the earth) / मुरे (turned back, retreated) / सदग्रंथ (sacred texts) / पर्बत (mountains) / कंदरन्हि (caves) / महुँ (in) / जाइ (going) / तेहि (that) / अवसर (time) / दुरे (hid themselves) / होनिहार (what is to happen) / का (what) / करतार (maker, ordainer) / को (who) / रखवार (protector) / जग (world) / खरभरु (turmoil) / परा (fell) / दुइ (two) / माथ (heads) / केहि (which) / रतिनाथ (lord of desire) / जेहि कहुँ (for whom) / कोपि (angrily) / कर (hand) / धनु (bow) / सरु (arrows) / धरा (held)
ramacharitamanas::488.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::488.essence: Clear seeing retreats when desire rules the mind.
ramacharitamanas::488.simple_meaning: Clear seeing and its allies retreat when desire takes over. What remains is confusion, fear, and a world that no longer knows how to protect itself.
ramacharitamanas::488.simple_insight: It shows how quickly judgment collapses when craving takes command.
ramacharitamanas::488.detailed_meaning: The poem continues the picture of desire conquering the world. Wisdom, restraint, and the virtues that support them are driven into hiding, while everyone panics and asks who can protect them from this force.
ramacharitamanas::488.modern_relevance: A room full of smart people can still make a terrible choice when attraction, ego, or impulse takes the wheel. Later, everyone wonders how no one stopped it.
ramacharitamanas::488.insight: It shifts attention from cleverness to the need for steady self-rule before desire spreads.

ramacharitamanas::489.verse_sanskrit: जे सजीव जग अचर चर नारि पुरुष अस नाम। ते निज निज मरजाद तजि भए सकल बस काम ॥
ramacharitamanas::489.verse_hindi: जगत में स्त्री-पुरुष संज्ञा वाले जितने चर-अचर प्राणी थे, वे सब अपनी-अपनी मर्यादा छोड़कर काम के वश में हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::489.english_translation: All living beings in the world—moving and unmoving, men and women—left their proper bounds and fell under desire.
ramacharitamanas::489.translation_literal: जे (those who) / सजीव (living beings) / जग (world) / अचर चर (unmoving and moving) / नारि पुरुष (women and men) / अस (such) / नाम (by name) / ते (they) / निज निज (their own) / मरजाद (bounds, propriety) / तजि (leaving) / भए (became) / सकल (all) / बस (under control) / काम (desire)
ramacharitamanas::489.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::489.essence: Desire makes beings abandon the limits that protect them.
ramacharitamanas::489.simple_meaning: Desire overwhelmed every kind of being and made them abandon the limits that normally guide their conduct.
ramacharitamanas::489.simple_insight: It reminds you how quickly wanting can dissolve judgment and self-control.
ramacharitamanas::489.detailed_meaning: After the sages' disciplined powers are scattered, the poem turns to a wider collapse: every living being, moving or still, man or woman, loses its own marjada. This verse marks the total spread of desire's rule.
ramacharitamanas::489.modern_relevance: A group chat starts with one flirtatious message, and suddenly everyone is joking, posturing, and crossing lines they would normally keep. Desire spreads fast and makes people betray their own standards.
ramacharitamanas::489.insight: It shifts attention from blaming others to noticing how desire first weakens your own boundaries.

ramacharitamanas::490.verse_sanskrit: सब के हृदयँ मदन अभिलाषा। लता निहारि नवहिं तरु साखा॥ नदीं उमगि अंबुधि कहुँ धाईं। संगम करहिं तलाव तलाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::490.verse_hindi: सबके हृदय में काम की इच्छा हो गई। लताओं (बेलों) को देखकर वृक्षों की डालियाँ झुकने लगीं। नदियाँ उमड़-उमड़कर समुद्र की ओर दौड़ीं और ताल-तलैयाँ भी आपस में संगम करने (मिलने-जुलने) लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::490.english_translation: Desire for pleasure rose in every heart. Seeing the vines, tree branches bowed. Rivers surged toward the ocean, and ponds and pools rushed to mingle together.
ramacharitamanas::490.translation_literal: सब के (of all) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / मदन (desire) / अभिलाषा (longing) / लता (vines) / निहारि (seeing) / नवहिं (bow) / तरु (trees) / साखा (branches) / नदीं (rivers) / उमगि (surging) / अंबुधि (ocean) / कहुँ (toward) / धाईं (ran) / संगम (union) / करहिं (make) / तलाव (ponds) / तलाईं (pools)
ramacharitamanas::490.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::490.essence: Desire bends even the natural world toward itself.
ramacharitamanas::490.simple_meaning: Desire spreads through all living things and even through nature itself. The verse says the whole world seems to move toward union under its force.
ramacharitamanas::490.simple_insight: It reminds you how powerful craving can be when it takes over the mind and distorts everything around it.
ramacharitamanas::490.detailed_meaning: The scene is already under the pressure of desire from the previous verse. Tulsidas now shows that not only people, but even trees, rivers, ponds, and vines seem swept into longing. It is a vivid way of showing how overwhelming desire can be.
ramacharitamanas::490.modern_relevance: You open your phone for one quick check, and suddenly everything feels urgent, attractive, and unfinished. Desire spreads fast, and soon the whole day bends around it.
ramacharitamanas::490.insight: It shifts attention from the object of craving to the way craving spreads and captures perception.

ramacharitamanas::491.verse_sanskrit: जहँ असि दसा जड़न्ह कै बरनी। को कहि सकइ सचेतन करनी॥ पसु पच्छी नभ जल थल चारी। भए काम बस समय बिसारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::491.verse_hindi: जब जड़ (वृक्ष, नदी आदि) की यह दशा कही गई, तब चेतन जीवों की करनी कौन कह सकता है? आकाश, जल और पृथ्वी पर विचरने वाले सारे पशु-पक्षी (अपने संयोग का) समय भुलाकर काम के वश में हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::491.english_translation: When even inert things were described like this, who can describe what conscious beings did? Animals and birds in sky, water, and land all forgot time and fell under desire.
ramacharitamanas::491.translation_literal: जहँ (where) / असि (such) / दसा (condition) / जड़न्ह (of inert things) / कै (of) / बरनी (described) / को (who) / कहि (having said) / सकइ (can) / सचेतन (conscious beings) / करनी (conduct, actions)॥ / पसु (animals) / पच्छी (birds) / नभ (sky) / जल (water) / थल (land) / चारी (moving about) / भए (became) / काम (desire) / बस (under control) / समय (time) / बिसारी (forgetting)॥
ramacharitamanas::491.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::491.essence: Desire spreads so widely that even time is forgotten.
ramacharitamanas::491.simple_meaning: Even trees and rivers seemed stirred by desire, so conscious beings were even more overwhelmed. Animals and birds everywhere forgot time and fell under desire.
ramacharitamanas::491.simple_insight: Unchecked desire can spread until it distorts the whole world around you.
ramacharitamanas::491.detailed_meaning: After the first signs of desire in nature, the narration widens the scene. Not only trees and rivers, but animals and birds across sky, water, and land are swept up. This verse deepens the warning before the next line names all beings caught in it.
ramacharitamanas::491.modern_relevance: A group chat turns flirty, then the whole office starts acting strange. One mood spreads fast, and suddenly everyone has forgotten what mattered an hour ago.
ramacharitamanas::491.insight: It shifts attention from private impulse to contagious social drift, showing how desire can overtake judgment.

ramacharitamanas::492.verse_sanskrit: मदन अंध ब्याकुल सब लोका। निसि दिनु नहिं अवलोकहिं कोका॥ देव दनुज नर किंनर ब्याला। प्रेत पिसाच भूत बेताला ॥
ramacharitamanas::492.verse_hindi: सब लोक कामान्ध होकर व्याकुल हो गए। चकवा-चकवी रात-दिन नहीं देखते। देव, दैत्य, मनुष्य, किन्नर, सर्प, प्रेत, पिशाच, भूत, बेताल- ॥
ramacharitamanas::492.english_translation: The whole world was blinded by desire and became restless. Night and day, the chakravaka birds did not meet. Devas, asuras, humans, kinnars, serpents, pretas, pisachas, bhutas, and vetalas—
ramacharitamanas::492.translation_literal: मदन (desire) / अंध (blind) / ब्याकुल (restless) / सब (all) / लोका (worlds, beings) / निसि (night) / दिनु (day) / नहिं (not) / अवलोकहिं (look at) / कोका (chakravaka birds) / देव (devas) / दनुज (asuras) / नर (humans) / किंनर (kinnars) / ब्याला (serpents) / प्रेत (pretas) / पिसाच (pisachas) / भूत (bhutas) / बेताला (vetalas)
ramacharitamanas::492.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::492.essence: Desire blinds every kind of being and leaves no world untouched.
ramacharitamanas::492.simple_meaning: Desire has made every kind of being restless and blind. The poet begins listing how universal this disturbance is.
ramacharitamanas::492.simple_insight: Restlessness is not a private failure; it spreads through every level of life.
ramacharitamanas::492.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, Tulsidas is describing a world stirred by desire before the wedding scene unfolds. He widens the lens from nature to every class of being, showing that craving has touched all creation, which prepares the next verse’s deeper warning.
ramacharitamanas::492.modern_relevance: A room full of people keeps refreshing their phones, each pretending to be calm. The unease is shared, not personal — and that is exactly the point.
ramacharitamanas::492.insight: It shifts attention from one person's craving to desire as a universal force that disturbs all beings.

ramacharitamanas::493.verse_sanskrit: इन्ह कै दसा न कहेउँ बखानी। सदा काम के चेरे जानी॥ सिद्ध बिरक्त महामुनि जोगी। तेपि कामबस भए बियोगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::493.verse_hindi: ये तो सदा ही काम के गुलाम हैं, यह समझकर मैंने इनकी दशा का वर्णन नहीं किया। सिद्ध, विरक्त, महामुनि और महान् योगी भी काम के वश होकर योगरहित या स्त्री के विरही हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::493.english_translation: I will not describe their condition in detail, knowing that they are always slaves of desire. Even perfected sages, detached renunciates, great seers, and yogis fell under desire and became separated.
ramacharitamanas::493.translation_literal: इन्ह कै (of these) / दसा (condition) / न कहेउँ (I did not say) / बखानी (describe in detail) / सदा (always) / काम के (of desire) / चेरे (slaves) / जानी (knowing) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / बिरक्त (detached renunciates) / महामुनि (great sages) / जोगी (yogis) / तेपि (even they) / कामबस (under the sway of desire) / भए (became) / बियोगी (separated, estranged)
ramacharitamanas::493.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::493.essence: Even the disciplined can fall when desire takes control.
ramacharitamanas::493.simple_meaning: Desire can overpower even the most disciplined people. Tulsidas says he will not dwell on their downfall, because they were already enslaved by it.
ramacharitamanas::493.simple_insight: It is humbling to see that no one is immune to craving.
ramacharitamanas::493.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing how desire spreads through the world. Even perfected sages, renunciates, great seers, and yogis are not spared. The verse is a supporting step in a larger warning about how desire distorts vision and conduct.
ramacharitamanas::493.modern_relevance: A person who has meditated for years can still be undone by a single craving, a single message, a single pull. Skill does not cancel vulnerability.
ramacharitamanas::493.insight: It shifts attention from spiritual status to the hidden force that can still capture the mind.

ramacharitamanas::494.verse_sanskrit: भए कामबस जोगीस तापस पावँरन्हि की को कहै। देखहिं चराचर नारिमय जे ब्रह्ममय देखत रहे॥ अबला बिलोकहिं पुरुषमय जगु पुरुष सब अबलामयं। दुइ दंड भरि ब्रह्मांड भीतर कामकृत कौतुक अयं॥
ramacharitamanas::494.verse_hindi: जब योगीश्वर और तपस्वी भी काम के वश हो गए, तब पामर मनुष्यों की कौन कहे? जो समस्त चराचर जगत को ब्रह्ममय देखते थे, वे अब उसे स्त्रीमय देखने लगे। स्त्रियाँ सारे संसार को पुरुषमय देखने लगीं और पुरुष उसे स्त्रीमय देखने लगे। दो घड़ी तक सारे ब्राह्मण्ड के अंदर कामदेव का रचा हुआ यह कौतुक (तमाशा) रहा।
ramacharitamanas::494.english_translation: When even yogis and ascetics fell under desire, what can be said of ordinary people? Those who once saw all moving and unmoving beings as filled with the supreme reality now saw them as woman-filled; women saw the world as man-filled; men saw the world as woman-filled. For two moments, the entire cosmos became a play made by desire.
ramacharitamanas::494.translation_literal: भए (became) / कामबस (under the power of desire) / जोगीस (yogis) / तापस (ascetics) / पावँरन्हि (of the lowly) / की (of) / को (who) / कहै (can say) / देखहिं (they see) / चराचर (moving and unmoving) / नारिमय (filled with women) / जे (those who) / ब्रह्ममय (filled with the supreme reality) / देखत रहे (were seeing) / अबला (women) / बिलोकहिं (see) / पुरुषमय (filled with men) / जगु (world) / पुरुष (men) / सब (all) / अबलामयं (filled with women) / दुइ (two) / दंड (moments) / भरि (for) / ब्रह्मांड (cosmos) / भीतर (within) / कामकृत (made by desire) / कौतुक (play) / अयं (this)
ramacharitamanas::494.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::494.essence: Desire does not just tempt; it rewrites how the world appears.
ramacharitamanas::494.simple_meaning: Even the disciplined can lose clear seeing when desire takes over. The world is no longer seen as it is, but through craving and projection.
ramacharitamanas::494.simple_insight: It reminds you how quickly desire can distort reality and turn clear vision into obsession.
ramacharitamanas::494.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has just described desire spreading through every class of being. Here he shows the deeper damage: even those who once saw the world as filled with the supreme reality now see only projections of attraction. The passage leads into the warning that only Ram's protection can save anyone in such a state.
ramacharitamanas::494.modern_relevance: You open your phone to check one message, and suddenly every face, every post, every silence seems loaded with attraction or rejection. Desire has quietly rewritten the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::494.insight: It shifts attention from outer objects to the mind that distorts them.

ramacharitamanas::495.verse_sanskrit: धरी न काहूँ धीर सब के मन मनसिज हरे। जे राखे रघुबीर ते उबरे तेहि काल महुँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::495.verse_hindi: किसी ने भी हृदय में धैर्य नहीं धारण किया, कामदेव ने सबके मन हर लिए। श्री रघुनाथजी ने जिनकी रक्षा की, केवल वे ही उस समय बचे रहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::495.english_translation: No one kept composure; Kamadeva seized every mind. Only those protected by Raghubir survived that moment.
ramacharitamanas::495.translation_literal: धरी (held) / न (not) / काहूँ (by anyone) / धीर (steadiness) / सब के (of all) / मन (minds) / मनसिज (Kamadeva) / हरे (stole) / जे (those who) / राखे (protected) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / ते (they) / उबरे (were saved) / तेहि (that) / काल महुँ (in that time)
ramacharitamanas::495.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::495.essence: Desire topples everyone; only Ram's protection holds.
ramacharitamanas::495.simple_meaning: No one stayed steady; desire overwhelmed every mind. Only those protected by Ram were saved in that crisis.
ramacharitamanas::495.simple_insight: It reminds you how quickly desire can sweep away restraint, and how fragile self-control becomes without support.
ramacharitamanas::495.detailed_meaning: In the opening of the Sita-swayamvar, the assembly is shaken by Kamadeva's force. Even disciplined sages lose composure. Tulsidas says only those under Raghubir's protection remain safe, showing this as a moment of crisis rather than a general rule.
ramacharitamanas::495.modern_relevance: A room full of people can look composed until attraction, envy, or panic hits. Then the careful mask slips. This verse names that collapse and the need for a steadier refuge.
ramacharitamanas::495.insight: It shifts attention from personal control alone to the need for divine protection when the mind is overrun.

ramacharitamanas::496.verse_sanskrit: उभय घरी अस कौतुक भयऊ। जौ लगि कामु संभु पहिं गयऊ॥ सिवहि बिलोकि ससंकेउ मारू। भयउ जथाथिति सबु संसारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::496.verse_hindi: दो घड़ी तक ऐसा तमाशा हुआ, जब तक कामदेव शिवजी के पास पहुँच गया। शिवजी को देखकर कामदेव डर गया, तब सारा संसार फिर जैसा-का तैसा स्थिर हो गया।
ramacharitamanas::496.english_translation: For two moments this strange spectacle lasted, until Kama reached Shiva. Seeing Shiva, Kama grew afraid, and the whole world returned to its natural order.
ramacharitamanas::496.translation_literal: उभय (both) / घरी (moments) / अस (such) / कौतुक (wonder/spectacle) / भयऊ (became) / जौ लगि (until) / कामु (Kama) / संभु (Shiva) / पहिं (to) / गयऊ (went)॥ / सिवहि (Shiva) / बिलोकि (seeing) / ससंकेउ (became afraid) / मारू (Kama) / भयउ (became) / जथाथिति (in its proper state) / सबु (all) / संसारू (world)॥
ramacharitamanas::496.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::496.essence: Fearless presence restores the world to order.
ramacharitamanas::496.simple_meaning: For a brief time, desire disturbed even the highest beings, but Shiva's presence restored order. The world settled back into its proper state.
ramacharitamanas::496.simple_insight: Even chaos loses its grip when fearless presence returns.
ramacharitamanas::496.detailed_meaning: The marriage of Shiva and Parvati has drawn everyone into an extraordinary disturbance. Even the gods are unsettled, and Kama has slipped into Shiva's presence. The moment Shiva is seen, Kama recoils, and the cosmos snaps back into balance.
ramacharitamanas::496.modern_relevance: A room full of tension can feel unbearable until one calm person walks in and everyone straightens up. Presence can restore order faster than argument.
ramacharitamanas::496.insight: It shows that true steadiness can dissolve disorder without force.

ramacharitamanas::497.verse_sanskrit: भए तुरत सब जीव सुखारे। जिमि मद उतरि गएँ मतवारे॥ रुद्रहि देखि मदन भय माना। दुराधरष दुर्गम भगवाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::497.verse_hindi: तुरंत ही सब जीव वैसे ही सुखी हो गए, जैसे मतवाले (नशा पिए हुए) लोग मद (नशा) उतर जाने पर सुखी होते हैं। दुराधर्ष (जिनको पराजित करना अत्यन्त ही कठिन है) और दुर्गम (जिनका पार पाना कठिन है) भगवान (सम्पूर्ण ऐश्वर्य, धर्म, यश, श्री, ज्ञान और वैराग्य रूप छह ईश्वरीय गुणों से युक्त) रुद्र (महाभयंकर) शिवजी को देखकर कामदेव भयभीत हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::497.english_translation: At once all living beings became happy, like drunken men after the intoxication wears off. Seeing Rudra, Kama felt fear. The Lord was hard to approach and impossible to overcome.
ramacharitamanas::497.translation_literal: भए (became) / तुरत (at once) / सब (all) / जीव (living beings) / सुखारे (made happy) / जिमि (like) / मद (intoxication) / उतरि गएँ (having worn off) / मतवारे (drunken ones) / रुद्रहि (Rudra) / देखि (seeing) / मदन (Kama) / भय (fear) / माना (felt) / दुराधरष (hard to overcome) / दुर्गम (hard to approach) / भगवाना (the Lord)
ramacharitamanas::497.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::497.essence: True steadiness makes desire itself lose courage.
ramacharitamanas::497.simple_meaning: When Shiva appears, the disturbing force of desire loses its grip, and everyone feels relief again.
ramacharitamanas::497.simple_insight: It brings the relief of seeing that fear and agitation can vanish in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::497.detailed_meaning: During Shiva’s encounter with Kama in the Balkand, the whole atmosphere changes at once. The living beings feel relief, and Kama himself loses courage before Rudra’s terrible power. This verse marks the shift from disturbance to calm.
ramacharitamanas::497.modern_relevance: A tense room after a heated argument can change the moment one steady person walks in. The mood drops, the panic fades, and everyone breathes again.
ramacharitamanas::497.insight: It shifts attention from emotional chaos to the stabilising presence that ends it.

ramacharitamanas::498.verse_sanskrit: फिरत लाज कछु करि नहिं जाई। मरनु ठानि मन रचेसि उपाई॥ प्रगटेसि तुरत रुचिर रितुराजा। कुसुमित नव तरु राजि बिराजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::498.verse_hindi: लौट जाने में लज्जा मालूम होती है और करते कुछ बनता नहीं। आखिर मन में मरने का निश्चय करके उसने उपाय रचा। तुरंत ही सुंदर ऋतुराज वसन्त को प्रकट किया। फूले हुए नए-नए वृक्षों की कतारें सुशोभित हो गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::498.english_translation: Unable to turn back in shame, he resolved in his mind to die and devised a plan. At once he manifested the lovely king of seasons, and rows of blooming young trees shone forth.
ramacharitamanas::498.translation_literal: फिरत (turning back) / लाज (shame) / कछु (some) / करि (doing) / नहिं (not) / जाई (can be done) / मरनु (death) / ठानि (having resolved) / मन (mind) / रचेसि (he devised) / उपाई (a means) / प्रगटेसि (manifested) / तुरत (at once) / रुचिर (beautiful) / रितुराजा (king of seasons) / कुसुमित (flowering) / नव (new) / तरु (trees) / राजि (rows) / बिराजा (shone forth)
ramacharitamanas::498.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::498.essence: Even shame can become the threshold for a new beginning.
ramacharitamanas::498.simple_meaning: He could not turn back in shame, so he resolved to die and set about a plan. Then spring appeared at once, and fresh flowering trees filled the scene.
ramacharitamanas::498.simple_insight: The mind under pressure still creates a way forward, even from despair.
ramacharitamanas::498.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, the atmosphere shifts around the struggle with Shiva's bow. The poet shows how even shame and desperation become a force of action, as the world itself seems to answer by blooming into spring.
ramacharitamanas::498.modern_relevance: You miss your exit, sit in the car for a moment, and feel the sting of having no easy way back. Then you take the next turn and keep going.
ramacharitamanas::498.insight: It shifts attention from inner embarrassment to the fact that action can still transform the moment.

ramacharitamanas::499.verse_sanskrit: बन उपबन बापिका तड़ागा। परम सुभग सब दिसा बिभागा॥ जहँ तहँ जनु उमगत अनुरागा। देखि मुएहुँ मन मनसिज जागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::499.verse_hindi: वन-उपवन, बावली-तालाब और सब दिशाओं के विभाग परम सुंदर हो गए। जहाँ-तहाँ मानो प्रेम उम़ड़ रहा है, जिसे देखकर मरे मनों में भी कामदेव जाग उठा ॥
ramacharitamanas::499.english_translation: The forests, groves, pools, and tanks became beautiful in every direction. Love seemed to rise everywhere, and even dead hearts were stirred by desire at the sight.
ramacharitamanas::499.translation_literal: बन (forest) / उपबन (groves) / बापिका (small ponds) / तड़ागा (lakes) / परम सुभग (extremely beautiful) / सब दिसा (all directions) / बिभागा (sections)॥ / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / जनु (as if) / उमगत (rising) / अनुरागा (love)॥ / देखि (seeing) / मुएहुँ (even the dead) / मन (mind) / मनसिज (desire-born one) / जागा (awoke)॥
ramacharitamanas::499.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::499.essence: Beauty can awaken longing even in a numb heart.
ramacharitamanas::499.simple_meaning: The whole landscape becomes so beautiful that it seems to awaken love even in hearts that were lifeless.
ramacharitamanas::499.simple_insight: Beauty can reawaken what seemed numb, distant, or gone.
ramacharitamanas::499.detailed_meaning: The scene is still unfolding in the forest during the Sita-katha. Tulsidas lingers on the transformed landscape—trees, groves, ponds, and lakes—so lovely that the very sight seems to stir desire in even lifeless hearts. It is a descriptive bridge, not the passage's main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::499.modern_relevance: You walk into a courtyard after rain, and the smell of wet earth, flowers, and quiet light suddenly softens your mood before you can explain why.
ramacharitamanas::499.insight: It shifts attention from inner heaviness to how surroundings can quietly reshape feeling.

ramacharitamanas::500.verse_sanskrit: जागइ मनोभव मुएहुँ मन बन सुभगता न परै कही। सीतल सुगंध सुमंद मारुत मदन अनल सखा सही॥ बिकसे सरन्हि बहु कंज गुंजत पुंज मंजुल मधुकरा। कलहंस पिक सुक सरस रव करि गान नाचहिं अपछरा
ramacharitamanas::500.verse_hindi: मरे हुए मन में भी कामदेव जागने लगा, वन की सुंदरता कही नहीं जा सकती। कामरूपी अग्नि का सच्चा मित्र शीतल-मन्द-सुगंधित पवन चलने लगा। सरोवरों में अनेकों कमल खिल गए, जिन पर सुंदर भौंरों के समूह गुंजार करने लगे। राजहंस, कोयल और तोते रसीली बोली बोलने लगे और अप्सराएँ गा-गाकर नाचने लगीं॥
ramacharitamanas::500.english_translation: Desire awakens even in a dead mind; the forest's beauty cannot be described. A cool, gentle, fragrant breeze becomes the true friend of the fire of desire. Many lotuses bloom in the lakes, clusters of bees hum sweetly, and swans, cuckoos, and parrots sing while heavenly dancers dance and sing.
ramacharitamanas::500.translation_literal: जागइ (awakens) / मनोभव (desire) / मुएहुँ (even in the dead) / मन (mind) / बन (forest) / सुभगता (beauty) / न परै (cannot be put) / कही (in words) / सीतल (cool) / सुगंध (fragrant) / सुमंद (gentle) / मारुत (breeze) / मदन (desire) / अनल (fire) / सखा (friend) / सही (truly) / बिकसे (bloomed) / सरन्हि (in the lakes) / बहु (many) / कंज (lotuses) / गुंजत (humming) / पुंज (clusters) / मंजुल (sweet) / मधुकरा (bees) / कलहंस (swans) / पिक (cuckoos) / सुक (parrots) / सरस (sweet) / रव (voices) / करि (doing) / गान (singing) / नाचहिं (dance) / अपछरा (celestial dancers)
ramacharitamanas::500.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::500.essence: Beauty itself can awaken desire in a heart that seemed finished.
ramacharitamanas::500.simple_meaning: The forest becomes so beautiful that it stirs desire even in a dead heart. Breezes, flowers, birds, and bees all seem to join that awakening.
ramacharitamanas::500.simple_insight: Beauty can stir longing even where feeling seemed gone.
ramacharitamanas::500.detailed_meaning: As the forest scene unfolds, nature itself seems to conspire with desire. The beauty is so intense that even a dead heart would stir. This is not a teaching yet, but a vivid setup for the coming encounter.
ramacharitamanas::500.modern_relevance: You walk into a garden after a hard breakup, expecting nothing, and one scent, one birdcall, one breeze brings everything back. The world can reopen a closed heart without asking permission.
ramacharitamanas::500.insight: It frames attraction as something awakened by atmosphere, not forced by will.

ramacharitamanas::501.verse_sanskrit: सकल कला करि कोटि बिधि हारेउ सेन समेत। चली न अचल समाधि सिव कोपेउ हृदयनिकेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::501.verse_hindi: कामदेव अपनी सेना समेत करोड़ों प्रकार की सब कलाएँ (उपाए) करके हार गया, पर शिवजी की अचल समाधि न डिगी। तब कामदेव क्रोधित हो उठा ॥
ramacharitamanas::501.english_translation: Kama, with his countless arts and his army, was defeated. Shiva's unshaken meditation did not move, and then Kama grew furious.
ramacharitamanas::501.translation_literal: सकल (all) / कला (arts, skills) / करि (having done) / कोटि बिधि (in millions of ways) / हारेउ (was defeated) / सेन (army) / समेत (together with) / चली (moved) / न (not) / अचल (unmoving) / समाधि (meditation) / सिव (Shiva) / कोपेउ (became angry) / हृदयनिकेत (dwelling in the heart)
ramacharitamanas::501.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::501.essence: Desire fails before unshaken stillness, then turns to rage.
ramacharitamanas::501.simple_meaning: Kama tried every possible tactic, but Shiva's deep meditation stayed unmoved. Failing to break that stillness, Kama became angry.
ramacharitamanas::501.simple_insight: Some temptations lose power when they meet true inner stillness.
ramacharitamanas::501.detailed_meaning: In the forest scene around Shiva's meditation, even Kama arrives with an entire arsenal of seductive force. He uses every art he has, but Shiva remains unmoved. This verse marks the moment when desire, frustrated by stillness, turns to anger.
ramacharitamanas::501.modern_relevance: You are halfway through a late-night scroll, trying to pull yourself out of focus, and every distraction has already tried its turn. The mind that stays steady does not need to fight back.
ramacharitamanas::501.insight: It shows that unshaken attention can outlast even the strongest pull of desire.

ramacharitamanas::502.verse_sanskrit: देखि रसाल बिटप बर साखा। तेहि पर चढ़ेउ मदनु मन माखा॥ सुमन चाप निज सर संधाने। अति रिस ताकि श्रवन लगि ताने ॥
ramacharitamanas::502.verse_hindi: आम के वृक्ष की एक सुंदर डाली देखकर मन में क्रोध से भरा हुआ कामदेव उस पर चढ़ गया। उसने पुष्प धनुष पर अपने (पाँचों) बाण चढ़ाए और अत्यन्त क्रोध से (लक्ष्य की ओर) ताककर उन्हें कान तक तान लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::502.english_translation: Seeing a beautiful mango branch, Madana climbed it, his mind inflamed with anger. He strung his flower-bow and, glaring fiercely, drew the bowstring to his ear.
ramacharitamanas::502.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / रसाल (mango) / बिटप (tree) / बर (best) / साखा (branch) / तेहि पर (on that) / चढ़ेउ (climbed) / मदनु (Madana) / मन (mind) / माखा (filled with anger) / सुमन (flower) / चाप (bow) / निज (own) / सर (arrows) / संधाने (strung) / अति रिस (great anger) / ताकि (aiming) / श्रवन लगि (up to the ear) / ताने (drew)
ramacharitamanas::502.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::502.essence: Desire arms itself the moment it sees an opening.
ramacharitamanas::502.simple_meaning: Madana, angered and eager, climbs a beautiful branch and prepares his flower arrows to attack Shiva’s meditation.
ramacharitamanas::502.simple_insight: Desire grows bold when it finds a weakness to exploit.
ramacharitamanas::502.detailed_meaning: Shiva’s meditation has already resisted every trick. Now Madana spots a beautiful mango branch, climbs it, and prepares his flower arrows with fierce intent. This verse sets up the next blow in the attempt to disturb Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::502.modern_relevance: You feel calm until one tempting image hooks your attention and the whole mind rushes forward. The reaction is sudden, almost automatic, and hard to stop once it starts.
ramacharitamanas::502.insight: It shows how desire becomes aggressive when it senses an opening.

ramacharitamanas::503.verse_sanskrit: छाड़े बिषम बिसिख उर लागे। छूटि समाधि संभु तब जागे॥ भयउ ईस मन छोभु बिसेषी। नयन उघारि सकल दिसि देखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::503.verse_hindi: कामदेव ने तीक्ष्ण पाँच बाण छोड़े, जो शिवजी के हृदय में लगे। तब उनकी समाधि टूट गई और वे जाग गए। ईश्वर (शिवजी) के मन में बहुत क्षोभ हुआ। उन्होंने आँखें खोलकर सब ओर देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::503.english_translation: Kamadeva shot his sharp arrows, and they struck Shiva's heart. Then Shiva's meditation broke, and he awoke. The Lord felt deep disturbance in his mind. Opening his eyes, he looked all around.
ramacharitamanas::503.translation_literal: छाड़े (released) / बिषम (sharp, piercing) / बिसिख (arrows) / उर (heart) / लागे (struck) / छूटि (broken, released) / समाधि (meditation) / संभु (Shiva) / तब (then) / जागे (awoke) / भयउ (became) / ईस (the Lord) / मन (mind) / छोभु (disturbance) / बिसेषी (great) / नयन (eyes) / उघारि (opening) / सकल (all) / दिसि (directions) / देखी (looked)
ramacharitamanas::503.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::503.essence: Desire breaks stillness in a single strike.
ramacharitamanas::503.simple_meaning: Kamadeva's arrows break Shiva's meditation and stir his mind. He wakes, opens his eyes, and looks around in anger.
ramacharitamanas::503.simple_insight: Even the deepest stillness can be disturbed, and the first reaction is a sudden awakening.
ramacharitamanas::503.detailed_meaning: Kamadeva has already climbed the mango tree and aimed his flower arrows at Shiva, who sits in unbroken meditation. The arrows land, the trance breaks, and Shiva wakes in disturbed surprise. This is the immediate turning point before his fierce response.
ramacharitamanas::503.modern_relevance: You were finally focused, then one notification, one comment, one memory shattered the calm. The mind wakes instantly, and not always gently.
ramacharitamanas::503.insight: It shows how desire can interrupt stillness and trigger an immediate, reactive awakening.

ramacharitamanas::504.verse_sanskrit: सौरभ पल्लव मदनु बिलोका। भयउ कोपु कंपेउ त्रैलोका॥ तब सिवँ तीसर नयन उघारा। चितवन कामु भयउ जरि छारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::504.verse_hindi: जब आम के पत्तों में (छिपे हुए) कामदेव को देखा तो उन्हें बड़ा क्रोध हुआ, जिससे तीनों लोक काँप उठे। तब शिवजी ने तीसरा नेत्र खोला, उनको देखते ही कामदेव जलकर भस्म हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::504.english_translation: When Shiva saw Kama hidden among the mango leaves, great anger arose and the three worlds trembled. Then Shiva opened his third eye; at one glance, Kama burned to ashes.
ramacharitamanas::504.translation_literal: सौरभ (fragrance) / पल्लव (leaves) / मदनु (Kama) / बिलोका (saw) / भयउ (became) / कोपु (anger) / कंपेउ (trembled) / त्रैलोका (three worlds) / तब (then) / सिवँ (Shiva) / तीसर (third) / नयन (eye) / उघारा (opened) / चितवन (look) / कामु (Kama) / भयउ (became) / जरि (burned) / छारा (ashes)
ramacharitamanas::504.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::504.essence: Clear seeing can burn desire to ashes.
ramacharitamanas::504.simple_meaning: Shiva notices Kama hiding in the leaves, becomes furious, and opens his third eye. Kama is instantly reduced to ashes.
ramacharitamanas::504.simple_insight: Some forces cannot survive clear seeing. False desire burns when it is fully exposed.
ramacharitamanas::504.detailed_meaning: Shiva has been drawn out of deep meditation by Kama's attempt to disturb him. Seeing the hidden intruder, Shiva's anger shakes creation itself, and his third eye ends the deception at once. The scene leads into the public aftermath.
ramacharitamanas::504.modern_relevance: You finally notice the craving hiding inside a harmless-looking habit. The moment you see it clearly, it loses its power to run your day.
ramacharitamanas::504.insight: It shifts the mind from being seduced by desire to seeing desire as something that can be ended by clear awareness.

ramacharitamanas::505.verse_sanskrit: हाहाकार भयउ जग भारी। डरपे सुर भए असुर सुखारी॥ समुझि कामसुख सोचहिं भोगी। भए अकंटक साधक जोगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::505.verse_hindi: जगत में बड़ा हाहाकर मच गया। देवता डर गए, दैत्य सुखी हुए। भोगी लोग कामसुख को याद करके चिन्ता करने लगे और साधक योगी निष्कंटक हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::505.english_translation: There was a great uproar in the world. The radiant beings were afraid, and the beings of shadow were pleased. Those who chase pleasure worried about desire; seekers of yoga became free of disturbance.
ramacharitamanas::505.translation_literal: हाहाकार (uproar) / भयउ (became) / जग (world) / भारी (great) । डरपे (were afraid) / सुर (radiant beings) / भए (became) / असुर (beings of shadow) / सुखारी (pleased) ॥ समुझि (remembering) / कामसुख (pleasure of desire) / सोचहिं (worry) / भोगी (pleasure-seekers) / भोगी ॥ भए (became) / अकंटक (free of disturbance) / साधक (seekers) / जोगी (yoga practitioners) ॥
ramacharitamanas::505.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::505.essence: What ruins craving frees the one who seeks discipline.
ramacharitamanas::505.simple_meaning: The world reacts in opposite ways: some are shaken by the fall of desire, while seekers feel relief and freedom.
ramacharitamanas::505.simple_insight: It can feel like chaos for one part of you and liberation for another.
