ramacharitamanas::505.detailed_meaning: After Shiva burns Kamadeva, the whole world reacts. The radiant beings tremble, the shadowy beings rejoice, and ordinary pleasure-seekers feel anxious. But the seekers of yoga feel relief, because the force of distraction has been removed.
ramacharitamanas::505.modern_relevance: A breakup, a temptation, or a habit finally losing its grip can feel like disaster to one circle of people and relief to another. What weakens craving can unsettle the restless mind and steady the one who is serious.
ramacharitamanas::505.insight: It contrasts two responses to the same event: craving panics, discipline relaxes.

ramacharitamanas::506.verse_sanskrit: जोगी अकंटक भए पति गति सुनत रति मुरुछित भई। रोदति बदति बहु भाँति करुना करति संकर पहिं गई॥ अति प्रेम करि बिनती बिबिध बिधि जोरि कर सन्मुख रही। प्रभु आसुतोष कृपाल सिव अबला निरखि बोले सही॥
ramacharitamanas::506.verse_hindi: योगी निष्कंटक हो गए, कामदेव की स्त्री रति अपने पति की यह दशा सुनते ही मूर्च्छित हो गई। रोती-चिल्लाती और भाँति-भाँति से करुणा करती हुई वह शिवजी के पास गई। अत्यन्त प्रेम के साथ अनेकों प्रकार से विनती करके हाथ जोड़कर सामने खड़ी हो गई। शीघ्र प्रसन्न होने वाले कृपालु शिवजी अबला (असहाय स्त्री) को देखकर सुंदर (उसको सान्त्वना देने वाले) वचन बोले।
ramacharitamanas::506.english_translation: The yogis became free of disturbance. Hearing of her husband's condition, Rati fainted. Weeping and grieving in many ways, she went to Shiva. With deep love she stood before him, hands joined, and Shiva, the compassionate one, spoke gentle words to the helpless woman.
ramacharitamanas::506.translation_literal: जोगी (yogis) / अकंटक (free from disturbance) / भए (became) / पति (husband) / गति (condition) / सुनत (hearing) / रति (Rati) / मुरुछित (fainted) / भई (became) / रोदति (weeping) / बदति (speaking) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / करुना (compassion) / करति (doing) / संकर (Shiva) / पहिं (to) / गई (went) / अति (very) / प्रेम (love) / करि (doing) / बिनती (request) / बिबिध बिधि (various ways) / जोरि कर (joining hands) / सन्मुख (in front) / रही (stood) / प्रभु (lord) / आसुतोष (quickly pleased) / कृपाल (compassionate) / सिव (Shiva) / अबला (helpless woman) / निरखि (seeing) / बोले (spoke) / सही (gentle/appropriate)
ramacharitamanas::506.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::506.essence: Relief for one side can be devastation for another.
ramacharitamanas::506.simple_meaning: The yogis are now free from disturbance. Rati, hearing what happened to her husband, faints in grief and goes to Shiva, pleading with him in tears.
ramacharitamanas::506.simple_insight: Even divine power is met with tenderness here. Grief opens the door to mercy.
ramacharitamanas::506.detailed_meaning: After Shiva burns Kama, the yogis can meditate without interruption, but the scene immediately turns to Rati's anguish. She hears that her husband has been reduced to ashes, faints, then goes weeping to Shiva and begs for mercy. Shiva sees her suffering and prepares to answer gently.
ramacharitamanas::506.modern_relevance: A person gets the worst possible call in the middle of the day, drops everything, and walks into the only room where help might still exist. Grief does that: it strips away pride and asks for mercy.
ramacharitamanas::506.insight: It shifts attention from cosmic event to human cost, showing that even victory carries sorrow for someone.

ramacharitamanas::507.verse_sanskrit: अब तें रति तव नाथ कर होइहि नामु अनंगु। बिनु बपु ब्यापिहि सबहि पुनि सुनु निज मिलन प्रसंगु ॥
ramacharitamanas::507.verse_hindi: हे रति! अब से तेरे स्वामी का नाम अनंग होगा। वह बिना ही शरीर के सबको व्यापेगा। अब तू अपने पति से मिलने की बात सुन ॥
ramacharitamanas::507.english_translation: O Rati, from now on your husband will be named Ananga. Without a body, he will pervade everyone. Now listen to the story of your reunion.
ramacharitamanas::507.translation_literal: अब तें (from now on) / रति (Rati) / तव (your) / नाथ (husband, lord) / कर (of) / होइहि (will become) / नामु (name) / अनंगु (Ananga, bodiless one) / बिनु (without) / बपु (body) / ब्यापिहि (will pervade) / सबहि (everyone) / पुनि (again) / सुनु (listen) / निज (own) / मिलन (meeting, union) / प्रसंगु (story, occasion)
ramacharitamanas::507.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::507.essence: What loses form can still continue to move through the world.
ramacharitamanas::507.simple_meaning: Rati is told that Kama will lose his body and live on as Ananga, moving through everyone invisibly. The verse points toward the story of how they will meet again.
ramacharitamanas::507.simple_insight: Loss can transform desire, but it does not always erase it.
ramacharitamanas::507.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the opening frame of the Balkand, recounting how Rati mourns after Kama is burned. He tells her that Kama will return as Ananga, bodiless yet still active, before moving on to the promise of Rati's reunion with him.
ramacharitamanas::507.modern_relevance: A breakup leaves someone saying, 'I can't even think straight.' The feeling still moves through the body, even after the old form of love is gone.
ramacharitamanas::507.insight: It shifts attention from physical form to the continuing force of longing.

ramacharitamanas::508.verse_sanskrit: जब जदुबंस कृष्न अवतारा। होइहि हरन महा महिभारा॥ कृष्न तनय होइहि पति तोरा। बचनु अन्यथा होइ न मोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::508.verse_hindi: जब पृथ्वी के बड़े भारी भार को उतारने के लिए यदुवंश में श्री कृष्ण का अवतार होगा, तब तेरा पति उनके पुत्र (प्रद्युम्न) के रूप में उत्पन्न होगा। मेरा यह वचन अन्यथा नहीं होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::508.english_translation: When Krishna descends in the Yadu line to lift the great burden of the earth, your husband will be born as his son. My word never fails.
ramacharitamanas::508.translation_literal: जब (when) / जदुबंस (Yadu line) / कृष्न (Krishna) / अवतारा (incarnation) / होइहि (will happen) / हरन (removal) / महा (great) / महिभारा (burden of the earth)॥ / कृष्न (Krishna) / तनय (son) / होइहि (will become) / पति (husband) / तोरा (your) / बचनु (word) / अन्यथा (otherwise) / होइ (be) / न (not) / मोरा (mine) ॥
ramacharitamanas::508.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::508.essence: A divine promise can outlast even death and return as form.
ramacharitamanas::508.simple_meaning: Shiva tells Rati that her husband will return in a future birth as Krishna's son, and his promise will come true.
ramacharitamanas::508.simple_insight: Even loss can be held inside a larger promise.
ramacharitamanas::508.detailed_meaning: Shiva comforts Rati after her husband is reduced to bodiless form. He reveals a future birth: when Krishna appears to lift the earth’s burden, Rati’s husband will return as Krishna’s son. The verse matters because Shiva’s promise gives grief a horizon.
ramacharitamanas::508.modern_relevance: You are standing beside someone whose life has split into before and after. The comfort that helps most is not explanation, but a promise you can trust when nothing else makes sense.
ramacharitamanas::508.insight: It shifts grief from finality to continuity, showing that a broken moment may belong to a larger arc.

ramacharitamanas::509.verse_sanskrit: रति गवनी सुनि संकर बानी। कथा अपर अब कहउँ बखानी॥ देवन्ह समाचार सब पाए। ब्रह्मादिक बैकुंठ सिधाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::509.verse_hindi: शिवजी के वचन सुनकर रति चली गई। अब दूसरी कथा बखानकर (विस्तार से) कहता हूँ। ब्रह्मादि देवताओं ने ये सब समाचार सुने तो वे वैकुण्ठ को चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::509.english_translation: Hearing Shiva's words, Rati departed. Now I tell another story in detail. After hearing all this news, the gods, including Brahma, went to Vaikuntha.
ramacharitamanas::509.translation_literal: रति (Rati) / गवनी (went away) / सुनि (having heard) / संकर (Shiva's) / बानी (words) / कथा (story) / अपर (another) / अब (now) / कहउँ (I tell) / बखानी (in detail) / देवन्ह (the gods) / समाचार (news) / सब (all) / पाए (received) / ब्रह्मादिक (Brahma and others) / बैकुंठ (Vaikuntha) / सिधाए (went)
ramacharitamanas::509.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::509.essence: The story turns from one divine scene to the next.
ramacharitamanas::509.simple_meaning: Rati leaves after hearing Shiva's words, and the narrator shifts to another story. The gods hear the news and go to Vaikuntha.
ramacharitamanas::509.simple_insight: Some moments close one chapter and quietly open the next.
ramacharitamanas::509.detailed_meaning: Shiva has just finished explaining Rati's future and the larger cosmic arrangement. Rati departs, the scene turns, and the gods led by Brahma hear the news and move toward Vaikuntha. It is a transition verse, not the main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::509.modern_relevance: A conversation ends, and everyone in the room instantly shifts to the next task. The emotional moment has passed, but the story keeps moving.
ramacharitamanas::509.insight: It marks a narrative turn, reminding the reader that sacred stories move through connected scenes.

ramacharitamanas::510.verse_sanskrit: सब सुर बिष्नु बिरंचि समेता। गए जहाँ सिव कृपानिकेता॥ पृथक-पृथक तिन्ह कीन्हि प्रसंसा। भए प्रसन्न चंद्र अवतंसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::510.verse_hindi: फिर वहाँ से विष्णु और ब्रह्मा सहित सब देवता वहाँ गए, जहाँ कृपा के धाम शिवजी थे। उन सबने शिवजी की अलग-अलग स्तुति की, तब शशिभूषण शिवजी प्रसन्न हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::510.english_translation: Then all the gods, along with Vishnu and Brahma, went to where Shiva, the abode of grace, dwelt. Each one praised Shiva in his own way, and Shashibhushan became pleased.
ramacharitamanas::510.translation_literal: सब (all) / सुर (gods) / बिष्नु (Vishnu) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / समेता (together with) / गए (went) / जहाँ (where) / सिव (Shiva) / कृपानिकेता (abode of grace)॥ / पृथक-पृथक (separately) / तिन्ह (they) / कीन्हि (did) / प्रसंसा (praise) / भए (became) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / चंद्र अवतंसा (he who wears the moon as a crest)
ramacharitamanas::510.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::510.essence: Sincere praise opens the way for grace.
ramacharitamanas::510.simple_meaning: All the gods went to Shiva and praised him individually. Shiva was pleased by their devotion.
ramacharitamanas::510.simple_insight: Respect offered sincerely reaches where power alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::510.detailed_meaning: The gods gather before Shiva, the compassionate one, after hearing the larger cosmic news. Vishnu and Brahma come with the others, each offering praise. This verse sets up Shiva's response to their request in the next line.
ramacharitamanas::510.modern_relevance: A room full of powerful people can still feel tense until someone speaks with genuine respect. Real admiration softens pride faster than status ever can.
ramacharitamanas::510.insight: It frames reverence as the opening move before asking for help or guidance.

ramacharitamanas::511.verse_sanskrit: बोले कृपासिंधु बृषकेतू। कहहु अमर आए केहि हेतू॥ कह बिधि तुम्ह प्रभु अंतरजामी। तदपि भगति बस बिनवउँ स्वामी ॥
ramacharitamanas::511.verse_hindi: कृपा के समुद्र शिवजी बोले- हे देवताओं! कहिए, आप किसलिए आए हैं? ब्रह्माजी ने कहा- हे प्रभो! आप अन्तर्यामी हैं, तथापि हे स्वामी! भक्तिवश मैं आपसे विनती करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::511.english_translation: Shiva, the ocean of compassion, said: "Tell me, immortals, what brings you here?" Brahma said: "Lord, you are the indweller of all hearts. Still, out of devotion, I bow to you, master."
ramacharitamanas::511.translation_literal: बोले (spoke) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / बृषकेतू (Shiva) / कहहु (tell) / अमर (immortals) / आए (have come) / केहि हेतू (for what reason) ॥ / कह (said) / बिधि (Brahma) / तुम्ह (you) / प्रभु (Lord) / अंतरजामी (indweller of all hearts) / तदपि (still) / भगति बस (by devotion) / बिनवउँ (I bow / I pray) / स्वामी (master) ॥
ramacharitamanas::511.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::511.essence: Knowing everything does not cancel devotion; it deepens it.
ramacharitamanas::511.simple_meaning: Shiva asks the gods why they have come. Brahma answers that even though Shiva knows every heart, he still bows to him in devotion.
ramacharitamanas::511.simple_insight: Real reverence does not depend on being seen or understood first.
ramacharitamanas::511.detailed_meaning: In the sacred gathering, Shiva welcomes the gods and asks why they have come. Brahma replies with humility: Shiva already knows every heart, yet devotion still moves him to bow and speak.
ramacharitamanas::511.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone already knows the answer, but you still speak with humility. Respect is not reduced by insight; it becomes deeper because of it.
ramacharitamanas::511.insight: It shifts the mind from performing respect to offering it sincerely, even when no explanation is needed.

ramacharitamanas::512.verse_sanskrit: सकल सुरन्ह के हृदयँ अस संकर परम उछाहु। निज नयनन्हि देखा चहहिं नाथ तुम्हार बिबाहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::512.verse_hindi: हे शंकर! सब देवताओं के मन में ऐसा परम उत्साह है कि हे नाथ! वे अपनी आँखों से आपका विवाह देखना चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::512.english_translation: All the gods feel such great joy in their hearts, O Shankar, that they want to see your wedding with their own eyes, O Lord.
ramacharitamanas::512.translation_literal: सकल (all) / सुरन्ह के (of the radiant beings) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / अस (such) / संकर (Shankar) / परम (supreme) / उछाहु (joy) / निज (own) / नयनन्हि (with eyes) / देखा (to see) / चहहिं (they desire) / नाथ (Lord) / तुम्हार (your) / बिबाहु (wedding)
ramacharitamanas::512.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::512.essence: Joy in Shiva’s wedding draws every heart toward direct seeing.
ramacharitamanas::512.simple_meaning: The gods are so delighted that they want to witness Shiva’s wedding themselves.
ramacharitamanas::512.simple_insight: Pure joy makes even the heavenly beings want to be present, not just informed.
ramacharitamanas::512.detailed_meaning: The gods have come to Shiva’s dwelling and praised him. Now they reveal their real longing: not a blessing, but the chance to behold Shiva’s wedding with their own eyes. The scene builds devotional excitement before the next request.
ramacharitamanas::512.modern_relevance: A family gathers before a wedding, and everyone keeps leaning toward the doorway for the first glimpse. Some moments are so sacred and joyful that people do not want a summary — they want to witness them live.
ramacharitamanas::512.insight: It shifts attention from hearing about holiness to wanting direct presence with it.

ramacharitamanas::513.verse_sanskrit: यह उत्सव देखिअ भरि लोचन। सोइ कछु करहु मदन मद मोचन॥ कामु जारि रति कहुँ बरु दीन्हा। कृपासिन्धु यह अति भल कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::513.verse_hindi: हे कामदेव के मद को चूर करने वाले! आप ऐसा कुछ कीजिए, जिससे सब लोग इस उत्सव को नेत्र भरकर देखें। हे कृपा के सागर! कामदेव को भस्म करके आपने रति को जो वरदान दिया, सो बहुत ही अच्छा किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::513.english_translation: O destroyer of Cupid's pride, let everyone behold this festival with full eyes. O ocean of grace, you did very well to burn Cupid and grant Rati a boon.
ramacharitamanas::513.translation_literal: यह (this) / उत्सव (festival) / देखिअ (should be seen) / भरि (filled) / लोचन (eyes) / सोइ (that only) / कछु (something) / करहु (do) / मदन (Cupid) / मद (pride/intoxication) / मोचन (liberator) / कामु (desire/Cupid) / जारि (burning) / रति (Rati) / कहुँ (to/for) / बरु (boon) / दीन्हा (gave) / कृपासिन्धु (ocean of grace) / यह (this) / अति (very) / भल (good) / कीन्हा (did)
ramacharitamanas::513.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::513.essence: True grace destroys craving and still leaves room for blessing.
ramacharitamanas::513.simple_meaning: Shiva asks Ram to make the wedding festival fully visible to everyone, and praises Ram for destroying desire's arrogance while still blessing Rati.
ramacharitamanas::513.simple_insight: Devotion can hold both awe and clarity: it sees the beauty of the moment and the grace behind it.
ramacharitamanas::513.detailed_meaning: Shiva, speaking to Ram in the midst of the divine wedding preparations, asks that the celebration be made fully visible to all. He also reflects on Ram's earlier act of burning Cupid and yet showing mercy to Rati, seeing both power and compassion together.
ramacharitamanas::513.modern_relevance: At a wedding where everyone is trying to capture the perfect moment, one person quietly notices the deeper grace behind the celebration. Beauty feels fuller when pride and longing no longer distort it.
ramacharitamanas::513.insight: It trains attention to see sacred joy without getting lost in desire or spectacle.

ramacharitamanas::514.verse_sanskrit: सासति करि पुनि करहिं पसाऊ। नाथ प्रभुन्ह कर सहज सुभाऊ॥ पारबतीं तपु कीन्ह अपारा। करहु तासु अब अंगीकारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::514.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! श्रेष्ठ स्वामियों का यह सहज स्वभाव ही है कि वे पहले दण्ड देकर फिर कृपा किया करते हैं। पार्वती ने अपार तप किया है, अब उन्हें अंगीकार कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::514.english_translation: O Lord, it is the natural conduct of noble masters to punish first and then show grace. Parvati has performed immense austerity; now accept her.
ramacharitamanas::514.translation_literal: सासति (punishment) / करि (having done) / पुनि (again) / करहिं (they do) / पसाऊ (grace) / नाथ (lord) / प्रभुन्ह (of masters) / कर (of) / सहज (natural) / सुभाऊ (nature) / पारबतीं (Parvati) / तपु (austerity) / कीन्ह (did) / अपारा (immeasurable) / करहु (do) / तासु (her) / अब (now) / अंगीकारा (acceptance)
ramacharitamanas::514.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::514.essence: Grace arrives after endurance is fully seen.
ramacharitamanas::514.simple_meaning: A noble master may first test or discipline someone, then show mercy. Parvati has already done immense austerity, so she should now be accepted.
ramacharitamanas::514.simple_insight: Endurance matters, but so does the moment when effort is finally received.
ramacharitamanas::514.detailed_meaning: In Shiva's heavenly narration, the gods are urging acceptance of Parvati after her severe tapas. The verse frames grace as the natural act of a noble lord: first the trial, then the blessing. The plea is to stop delaying and welcome her devotion.
ramacharitamanas::514.modern_relevance: You kept showing up for months, proving yourself in silence, while everyone else moved on. Then the door finally opens. This verse holds that long-awaited moment of being received.
ramacharitamanas::514.insight: It shifts the mind from proving worth forever to recognising when effort has already been answered.

ramacharitamanas::515.verse_sanskrit: सुनि बिधि बिनय समुझि प्रभु बानी। ऐसेइ होउ कहा सुखु मानी॥ तब देवन्ह दुंदुभीं बजाईं। बरषि सुमन जय जय सुर साईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::515.verse_hindi: ब्रह्माजी की प्रार्थना सुनकर और प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के वचनों को याद करके शिवजी ने प्रसन्नतापूर्वक कहा- 'ऐसा ही हो।' तब देवताओं ने नगाड़े बजाए और फूलों की वर्षा करके 'जय हो! देवताओं के स्वामी जय हो' ऐसा कहने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::515.english_translation: Hearing Brahma's prayer and remembering the Lord's words, Shiva gladly said, 'So be it.' Then the devas rang their drums, showered flowers, and cried, 'Victory, victory to the Lord of the devas!'
ramacharitamanas::515.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / बिधि (Brahma) / बिनय (prayer) / समुझि (remembering, understanding) / प्रभु (Lord) / बानी (words) / ऐसेइ (just so) / होउ (let it be) / कहा (said) / सुखु (happily) / मानी (accepting) / तब (then) / देवन्ह (the devas) / दुंदुभीं (drums) / बजाईं (were sounded) / बरषि (showering) / सुमन (flowers) / जय जय (victory, victory) / सुर (devas) / साईं (Lord)
ramacharitamanas::515.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::515.essence: Right consent turns tension into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::515.simple_meaning: Shiva agrees with Brahma's prayer and Ram's words, then the devas celebrate with drums, flowers, and praise.
ramacharitamanas::515.simple_insight: Approval becomes joy when the heart recognises what is right.
ramacharitamanas::515.detailed_meaning: In the middle of the Sita-swayamvar scene, Shiva hears Brahma's prayer and remembers Ram's words. He gladly consents, and the devas respond at once with drums, flowers, and praise. The moment seals divine approval of the unfolding event.
ramacharitamanas::515.modern_relevance: You finally hear the confirmation you were waiting for, and the room shifts. Relief spreads, people smile, and what was uncertain now feels blessed.
ramacharitamanas::515.insight: It shifts attention from hesitation to wholehearted assent, showing how right action can be recognised and celebrated immediately.

ramacharitamanas::516.verse_sanskrit: अवसरु जानि सप्तरिषि आए। तुरतहिं बिधि गिरिभवन पठाए॥ प्रथम गए जहँ रहीं भवानी। बोले मधुर बचन छल सानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::516.verse_hindi: उचित अवसर जानकर सप्तर्षि आए और ब्रह्माजी ने तुरंत ही उन्हें हिमाचल के घर भेज दिया। वे पहले वहाँ गए जहाँ पार्वतीजी थीं और उनसे छल से भरे मीठे (विनोदयुक्त, आनंद पहुँचाने वाले) वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::516.english_translation: Knowing the right moment, the seven sages arrived, and Brahma immediately sent them to Himavan's home. They first went where Parvati was and spoke sweet, playful words filled with a hidden purpose.
ramacharitamanas::516.translation_literal: अवसरु (opportune moment) / जानि (knowing) / सप्तरिषि (seven sages) / आए (came) / तुरतहिं (immediately) / बिधि (Brahma) / गिरिभवन (mountain-home) / पठाए (sent) / प्रथम (first) / गए (went) / जहँ (where) / रहीं (was staying) / भवानी (Parvati) / बोले (spoke) / मधुर (sweet) / बचन (words) / छल (deception) / सानी (mixed with)
ramacharitamanas::516.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::516.essence: Sweet words can carry a hidden agenda.
ramacharitamanas::516.simple_meaning: The seven sages arrive at the right moment and first go to Parvati. They speak in sweet words, but their words carry a hidden intention.
ramacharitamanas::516.simple_insight: Not every gentle word is innocent; timing and motive both matter.
ramacharitamanas::516.detailed_meaning: After Shiva has agreed in principle, the seven sages come at the right moment. Brahma sends them to Himavan's house, where Parvati is waiting. They approach her first and begin speaking in soft, flattering words that conceal their real purpose.
ramacharitamanas::516.modern_relevance: A friendly message lands in your inbox just after a tense conversation. The tone feels warm, but something underneath it is steering the exchange. You sense the hidden agenda before the words finish.
ramacharitamanas::516.insight: It trains you to notice both tone and intention, not just pleasant speech.

ramacharitamanas::517.verse_sanskrit: कहा हमार न सुनेहु तब नारद कें उपदेस॥ अब भा झूठ तुम्हार पन जारेउ कामु महेस ॥
ramacharitamanas::517.verse_hindi: नारदजी के उपदेश से तुमने उस समय हमारी बात नहीं सुनी। अब तो तुम्हारा प्रण झूठा हो गया, क्योंकि महादेवजी ने काम को ही भस्म कर डाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::517.english_translation: You did not listen to our words then, despite Narada's counsel. Now your vow has become false, because Mahadeva has burned Kama to ashes.
ramacharitamanas::517.translation_literal: कहा (said) / हमार (our) / न (not) / सुनेहु (you listened) / तब (then) / नारद कें (to Narada) / उपदेस (instruction) / अब (now) / भा (has become) / झूठ (false) / तुम्हार (your) / पन (vow) / जारेउ (burned) / कामु (Kama) / महेस (Mahadeva)
ramacharitamanas::517.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::517.essence: A vow loses force when action contradicts it.
ramacharitamanas::517.simple_meaning: Parvati reminds Shiva that he ignored Narada's warning before, so his vow now seems broken because he has burned Kama.
ramacharitamanas::517.simple_insight: A warning ignored once can return as a painful contradiction later.
ramacharitamanas::517.detailed_meaning: In the Shiva-Parvati frame of Balkand, the sages arrive after the earlier tension around Parvati's wish and Shiva's restraint. Parvati points out the irony: Shiva once did not heed Narada's advice, but now he has destroyed Kama, making his earlier vow seem untrue.
ramacharitamanas::517.modern_relevance: You promised you were fine with something, then reacted sharply when it actually happened. The contradiction stings because everyone can see it now.
ramacharitamanas::517.insight: It exposes the gap between a stated vow and a later action that breaks it.

ramacharitamanas::518.verse_sanskrit: सुनि बोलीं मुसुकाइ भवानी। उचित कहेहु मुनिबर बिग्यानी॥ तुम्हरें जान कामु अब जारा। अब लगि संभु रहे सबिकारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::518.verse_hindi: यह सुनकर पार्वतीजी मुस्कुराकर बोलीं- हे विज्ञानी मुनिवरों! आपने उचित ही कहा। आपकी समझ में शिवजी ने कामदेव को अब जलाया है, अब तक तो वे विकारयुक्त (कामी) ही रहे! ॥
ramacharitamanas::518.english_translation: Hearing this, Bhavani smiled and said, "You have spoken rightly, O wise sages. In your view, Shiva burned desire only now; until now, he was still ruled by passion."
ramacharitamanas::518.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / बोलीं (spoke) / मुसुकाइ (smiling) / भवानी (Bhavani) / उचित (rightly) / कहेहु (you have spoken) / मुनिबर (O best of sages) / बिग्यानी (wise) / तुम्हरें (in your view) / जान (knowing) / कामु (desire) / अब (now) / जारा (burned) / अब लगि (until now) / संभु (Shiva) / रहे (remained) / सबिकारा (with passions)
ramacharitamanas::518.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::518.essence: A smile can agree with words while quietly correcting them.
ramacharitamanas::518.simple_meaning: Parvati answers the sages with a smile, agreeing with their words in a teasing way. She says that, by their view, Shiva only just burned desire, and before that he was still full of passion.
ramacharitamanas::518.simple_insight: Even sacred conversation can carry gentle irony and hidden truth.
ramacharitamanas::518.detailed_meaning: In Shiva's frame-story, the sages speak to Parvati with careful praise. She smiles and replies playfully, turning their words back on them. Her answer is part of a larger exchange about Shiva, desire, and the meaning of true renunciation.
ramacharitamanas::518.modern_relevance: Someone compliments a person for being "so calm now," and the room laughs because everyone knows the change took time. A smile can carry both agreement and a sharper truth than the words alone.
ramacharitamanas::518.insight: It shows how a listener can accept praise while quietly exposing its limits.

ramacharitamanas::519.verse_sanskrit: हमरें जान सदासिव जोगी। अज अनवद्य अकाम अभोगी॥ जौं मैं सिव सेये अस जानी। प्रीति समेत कर्म मन बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::519.verse_hindi: किन्तु हमारी समझ से तो शिवजी सदा से ही योगी, अजन्मे, अनिन्द्य, कामरहित और भोगहीन हैं और यदि मैंने शिवजी को ऐसा समझकर ही मन, वचन और कर्म से प्रेम सहित उनकी सेवा की है ॥
ramacharitamanas::519.english_translation: But in my understanding, Shiva is always a yogi: unborn, blameless, free from desire, and beyond enjoyment. If I have served Shiva with love in thought, speech, and action, knowing him thus...
ramacharitamanas::519.translation_literal: हमरें (in my) / जान (understanding) / सदासिव (Shiva forever) / जोगी (yogi) / अज (unborn) / अनवद्य (blameless) / अकाम (without desire) / अभोगी (without enjoyment) ॥ जौं (if) / मैं (I) / सिव (Shiva) / सेये (served) / अस (thus) / जानी (knowing) / प्रीति (love) / समेत (together with) / कर्म (action) / मन (mind) / बानी (speech) ॥
ramacharitamanas::519.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::519.essence: True devotion serves without trying to possess.
ramacharitamanas::519.simple_meaning: Parvati says she has always understood Shiva as a pure renunciant, and that her loving service was offered to him with that understanding in mind, speech, and action.
ramacharitamanas::519.simple_insight: Love becomes steady when it is based on a clear, reverent understanding of who the other truly is.
ramacharitamanas::519.detailed_meaning: Parvati is answering the sages in Shiva's own frame narrative. They have just doubted whether Shiva could truly be beyond desire. She replies that she has always known him as the eternal renunciant, and that her devotion has always been shaped by that vision.
ramacharitamanas::519.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone because you know their character, not because you need constant proof. That kind of devotion stays clean when understanding comes before expectation.
ramacharitamanas::519.insight: It shifts devotion from emotional impulse to informed reverence, where service follows clear seeing.

ramacharitamanas::520.verse_sanskrit: तौ हमार पन सुनहु मुनीसा। करिहहिं सत्य कृपानिधि ईसा॥ तुम्ह जो कहा हर जारेउ मारा। सोइ अति बड़ अबिबेकु तुम्हारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::520.verse_hindi: तो हे मुनीश्वरो! सुनिए, वे कृपानिधान भगवान मेरी प्रतिज्ञा को सत्य करेंगे। आपने जो यह कहा कि शिवजी ने कामदेव को भस्म कर दिया, यही आपका बड़ा भारी अविवेक है ॥
ramacharitamanas::520.english_translation: O great sages, listen. The merciful Lord will make my vow true. What you said—that Shiva burned Kama to ashes—is your great mistake.
ramacharitamanas::520.translation_literal: तौ (then) / हमार (my) / पन (vow) / सुनहु (listen) / मुनीसा (great sages) / करिहहिं (will make) / सत्य (true) / कृपानिधि (treasure of compassion) / ईसा (the Lord) / तुम्ह (you) / जो (what) / कहा (said) / हर (Shiva) / जारेउ (burned) / मारा (destroyed) / सोइ (that) / अति (very) / बड़ (great) / अबिबेकु (mistake) / तुम्हारा (your)
ramacharitamanas::520.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::520.essence: True understanding corrects even confident misunderstanding.
ramacharitamanas::520.simple_meaning: Parvati says Shiva will prove her vow true, and she corrects the sages: their idea that Shiva burned Kama is a serious mistake.
ramacharitamanas::520.simple_insight: Confidence can be calm and firm. You can correct error without losing composure.
ramacharitamanas::520.detailed_meaning: Parvati answers the sages in the frame story of Balkand. Smiling, she defends Shiva and says the merciful Lord will uphold her vow. She then challenges their understanding of Shiva's destruction of Kama, calling it a major misunderstanding.
ramacharitamanas::520.modern_relevance: In a room full of people confidently repeating the wrong story, you do not need to shout. A steady correction can be stronger than argument.
ramacharitamanas::520.insight: It shifts the mind from accepting inherited claims to seeing clearly and correcting them.

ramacharitamanas::521.verse_sanskrit: तात अनल कर सहज सुभाऊ। हिम तेहि निकट जाइ नहिं काऊ॥ गएँ समीप सो अवसि नसाई। असि मन्मथ महेस की नाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::521.verse_hindi: हे तात! अग्नि का तो यह सहज स्वभाव ही है कि पाला उसके समीप कभी जा ही नहीं सकता और जाने पर वह अवश्य नष्ट हो जाएगा। महादेवजी और कामदेव के संबंध में भी यही न्याय (बात) समझना चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::521.english_translation: O dear one, fire is naturally such that snow cannot come near it. If snow goes close, it is surely destroyed. The same rule applies to the union of Shambhu and Kamadeva.
ramacharitamanas::521.translation_literal: तात (dear one) / अनल (fire) / कर (of) / सहज (natural) / सुभाऊ (nature) / हिम (snow) / तेहि (to that) / निकट (near) / जाइ (goes) / नहिं (not) / काऊ (anyone)॥ / गएँ (going) / समीप (near) / सो (that) / अवसि (certainly) / नसाई (is destroyed) / असि (thus) / मन्मथ (Kamadeva) / महेस (Mahesha/Shiva) / की (of) / नाई (like) ॥
ramacharitamanas::521.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::521.essence: Some opposites destroy each other on contact.
ramacharitamanas::521.simple_meaning: Fire and snow cannot coexist. In the same way, Shiva and Kamadeva cannot meet without destruction.
ramacharitamanas::521.simple_insight: Some forces are so opposite that closeness itself becomes impossible.
ramacharitamanas::521.detailed_meaning: Parvati has asked how Shiva, the great ascetic, could destroy Kamadeva with a mere glance. The sage answers with a simple image: fire and snow cannot stay together. This verse explains why Shiva's purity and Kamadeva's desire cannot coexist.
ramacharitamanas::521.modern_relevance: You try to keep a clear boundary with something that always pulls you off center. The more you let it in, the more it dissolves your focus.
ramacharitamanas::521.insight: It teaches you to recognize incompatible states before forcing them together.

ramacharitamanas::522.verse_sanskrit: हियँ हरषे मुनि बचन सुनि देखि प्रीति बिस्वास। चले भवानिहि नाइ सिर गए हिमाचल पास ॥
ramacharitamanas::522.verse_hindi: पार्वती के वचन सुनकर और उनका प्रेम तथा विश्वास देखकर मुनि हृदय में बड़े प्रसन्न हुए। वे भवानी को सिर नवाकर चल दिए और हिमाचल के पास पहुँचे ॥
ramacharitamanas::522.english_translation: Hearing Parvati's words and seeing her love and trust, the sages were delighted in their hearts. Bowing to Bhavani, they set out and reached near Mount Himachal.
ramacharitamanas::522.translation_literal: हियँ (in the heart) / हरषे (were delighted) / मुनि (sages) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / देखि (seeing) / प्रीति (love) / बिस्वास (trust) / चले (went) / भवानिहि (to Bhavani) / नाइ (bowing) / सिर (head) / गए (went) / हिमाचल (Himachal) / पास (near)
ramacharitamanas::522.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::522.essence: Trust and reverence make the next teaching possible.
ramacharitamanas::522.simple_meaning: The sages felt joy at Parvati's loving trust. They bowed to her and went on to Mount Himachal.
ramacharitamanas::522.simple_insight: Respect and trust open the way for honest teaching.
ramacharitamanas::522.detailed_meaning: Parvati has been asking carefully about Shiva's teaching. The sages see her sincerity, feel glad, bow to her, and continue toward Himachal. This verse simply moves the story forward to the next exchange.
ramacharitamanas::522.modern_relevance: A teacher notices the student is listening with real trust, not just waiting to interrupt. The conversation changes immediately; respect makes the next truth possible.
ramacharitamanas::522.insight: It shows that sincere listening earns a deeper response and carries a conversation forward.

ramacharitamanas::523.verse_sanskrit: सबु प्रसंगु गिरिपतिहि सुनावा। मदन दहन सुनि अति दुखु पावा॥ बहुरि कहेउ रति कर बरदाना। सुनि हिमवंत बहुत सुखु माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::523.verse_hindi: उन्होंने पर्वतराज हिमाचल को सब हाल सुनाया। कामदेव का भस्म होना सुनकर हिमाचल बहुत दुःखी हुए। फिर मुनियों ने रति के वरदान की बात कही, उसे सुनकर हिमवान् ने बहुत सुख माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::523.english_translation: They told Himavan the whole story. Hearing that Kama had been burned, he felt deep sorrow. Then they spoke of Rati’s boon, and hearing that, Himavan felt great relief.
ramacharitamanas::523.translation_literal: सबु प्रसंगु (the whole account) / गिरिपतिहि (to Himavan, lord of the mountains) / सुनावा (they told) / मदन दहन (burning of Kama) / सुनि (hearing) / अति दुखु (great sorrow) / पावा (felt) / बहुरि (again) / कहेउ (they said) / रति कर (of Rati) / बरदाना (boon) / सुनि (hearing) / हिमवंत (Himavan) / बहुत सुखु (great happiness) / माना (felt)
ramacharitamanas::523.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::523.essence: Partial news wounds; the fuller story restores ease.
ramacharitamanas::523.simple_meaning: The sages explain the events to Himavan. He grieves at Kama’s destruction, then feels relief when he hears of Rati’s boon.
ramacharitamanas::523.simple_insight: A heart can move from grief to relief when the whole story is finally known.
ramacharitamanas::523.detailed_meaning: In the Himalayas, the sages explain the turn of events to Himavan, Parvati’s father. He is first pained by the burning of Kama, then comforted when he hears that Rati has received a boon. This is a quiet emotional turn before the marriage arrangements begin.
ramacharitamanas::523.modern_relevance: You hear only the worst part of a story and your chest tightens. Then one more detail arrives, and the whole picture changes. Relief often comes from context, not control.
ramacharitamanas::523.insight: It shifts the mind from partial hearing to fuller understanding, where sorrow can soften.

ramacharitamanas::524.verse_sanskrit: हृदयँ बिचारि संभु प्रभुताई। सादर मुनिबर लिए बोलाई। सुदिनु सुनखतु सुघरी सोचाई। बेगि बेदबिधि लगन धराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::524.verse_hindi: शिवजी के प्रभाव को मन में विचार कर हिमाचल ने श्रेष्ठ मुनियों को आदरपूर्वक बुला लिया और उनसे शुभ दिन, शुभ नक्षत्र और शुभ घड़ी शोधवाकर वेद की विधि के अनुसार शीघ्र ही लग्न निश्चय कराकर लिखवा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::524.english_translation: Considering Shiva's power in his heart, Himachal respectfully summoned the best sages. He chose an auspicious day, a lucky star, and a favorable hour, and quickly fixed the wedding time according to Vedic procedure.
ramacharitamanas::524.translation_literal: हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारि (having considered) / संभु (Shiva) / प्रभुताई (power, majesty) / सादर (respectfully) / मुनिबर (best sages) / लिए (took, summoned) / बोलाई (having called) / सुदिनु (auspicious day) / सुनखतु (auspicious star) / सुघरी (favorable hour) / सोचाई (having selected) / बेगि (quickly) / बेदबिधि (according to Vedic procedure) / लगन (wedding time) / धराई (fixed, arranged)
ramacharitamanas::524.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::524.essence: Reverence turns even planning into a sacred act.
ramacharitamanas::524.simple_meaning: Himachal, thinking of Shiva's greatness, called the sages and fixed the wedding time by choosing an auspicious day, star, and hour.
ramacharitamanas::524.simple_insight: Even a sacred occasion is prepared with care, respect, and the right timing.
ramacharitamanas::524.detailed_meaning: After hearing the sages' account, Himachal reflects on Shiva's greatness and acts with reverence. He summons the finest sages, consults them for the right auspicious timing, and arranges the marriage according to Vedic custom. The scene moves the story from grief into preparation.
ramacharitamanas::524.modern_relevance: Before a family wedding, everyone is checking dates, calling elders, and making sure the timing feels right. Beneath the logistics is reverence: some moments deserve care, not haste.
ramacharitamanas::524.insight: It shifts attention from impulse to proper preparation, showing that important acts deserve thoughtful timing and respect.

ramacharitamanas::525.verse_sanskrit: पत्री सप्तरिषिन्ह सोइ दीन्ही। गहि पद बिनय हिमाचल कीन्ही॥ जाइ बिधिहि तिन्ह दीन्हि सो पाती। बाचत प्रीति न हृदयँ समाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::525.verse_hindi: फिर हिमाचल ने वह लग्नपत्रिका सप्तर्षियों को दे दी और चरण पकड़कर उनकी विनती की। उन्होंने जाकर वह लग्न पत्रिका ब्रह्माजी को दी। उसको पढ़ते समय उनके हृदय में प्रेम समाता न था ॥
ramacharitamanas::525.english_translation: Then Himachal gave that wedding proposal to the seven sages and, bowing at their feet, made his request. They went and gave that proposal to Brahma. As he read it, his heart could not contain its joy.
ramacharitamanas::525.translation_literal: पत्री (wedding proposal letter) / सप्तरिषिन्ह (to the seven sages) / सोइ (that) / दीन्ही (gave) / गहि (grasping) / पद (feet) / बिनय (humble request) / हिमाचल (Himachal) / कीन्ही (made) / जाइ (going) / बिधिहि (to Brahma) / तिन्ह (they) / दीन्हि (gave) / सो पाती (that letter) / बाचत (reading) / प्रीति (love/joy) / न (not) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / समाती (contained)
ramacharitamanas::525.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::525.essence: A sacred announcement can make even the messenger’s heart overflow.
ramacharitamanas::525.simple_meaning: Himachal sends the wedding proposal through the seven sages and bows to ask for help. Brahma receives it with such joy that his heart overflows.
ramacharitamanas::525.simple_insight: Even a formal request can carry devotion and delight when the moment is right.
ramacharitamanas::525.detailed_meaning: Himachal has chosen the auspicious path for the wedding and places the proposal in the hands of the seven sages. They carry it to Brahma, who reads it with overflowing delight. The verse simply moves the story forward toward the blessed marriage.
ramacharitamanas::525.modern_relevance: You send the final message that makes everything real: the date, the plan, the commitment. The room is quiet, but your chest is full because the waiting is over.
ramacharitamanas::525.insight: It shifts attention from the request itself to the shared joy it awakens.

ramacharitamanas::526.verse_sanskrit: लगन बाचि अज सबहि सुनाई। हरषे मुनि सब सुर समुदाई॥ सुमन बृष्टि नभ बाजन बाजे। मंगल कलस दसहुँ दिसि साजे ॥
ramacharitamanas::526.verse_hindi: ब्रह्माजी ने लग्न पढ़कर सबको सुनाया, उसे सुनकर सब मुनि और देवताओं का सारा समाज हर्षित हो गया। आकाश से फूलों की वर्षा होने लगी, बाजे बजने लगे और दसों दिशाओं में मंगल कलश सजा दिए गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::526.english_translation: Brahma read out the auspicious wedding time, and all the sages and the assembly of the radiant beings rejoiced. Flowers rained from the sky, drums sounded, and auspicious pots were set in all ten directions.
ramacharitamanas::526.translation_literal: लगन (auspicious time) / बाचि (reading out) / अज (Brahma) / सबहि (to everyone) / सुनाई (announced) / हरषे (rejoiced) / मुनि (sages) / सब (all) / सुर (radiant beings) / समुदाई (assembly) / सुमन (flowers) / बृष्टि (shower) / नभ (sky) / बाजन (drums/instruments) / बाजे (sounded) / मंगल (auspicious) / कलस (pots) / दसहुँ (ten) / दिसि (directions) / साजे (set up)
ramacharitamanas::526.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::526.essence: A blessed moment draws the whole world into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::526.simple_meaning: Brahma announces the auspicious wedding time, and everyone rejoices. Flowers fall from the sky, music begins, and auspicious pots are arranged everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::526.simple_insight: Joy becomes visible when a moment is truly blessed.
ramacharitamanas::526.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, the wedding preparations for Ram and Sita have reached their sacred peak. After the auspicious time is announced, sages and radiant beings rejoice, and the heavens respond with flowers, music, and signs of celebration.
ramacharitamanas::526.modern_relevance: A family hears the final confirmation that the ceremony can begin. The room changes at once — relief, joy, and movement replace all the waiting.
ramacharitamanas::526.insight: It turns a private arrangement into a shared celebration, where even the sky seems to participate.

ramacharitamanas::527.verse_sanskrit: लगे सँवारन सकल सुर बाहन बिबिध बिमान। होहिं सगुन मंगल सुभद करहिं अपछरा गान ॥
ramacharitamanas::527.verse_hindi: सब देवता अपने भाँति-भाँति के वाहन और विमान सजाने लगे, कल्याणप्रद मंगल शकुन होने लगे और अप्सराएँ गाने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::527.english_translation: All the radiant beings began arranging their various mounts and celestial vehicles. Auspicious signs appeared, and the celestial dancers began to sing.
ramacharitamanas::527.translation_literal: लगे (began) / सँवारन (to arrange, prepare) / सकल (all) / सुर (radiant beings) / बाहन (mounts) / बिबिध (various) / बिमान (celestial vehicles) / होहिं (became) / सगुन (auspicious signs) / मंगल (auspicious) / सुभद (blessed, beneficial) / करहिं (do) / अपछरा (celestial dancers) / गान (song)
ramacharitamanas::527.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::527.essence: The world itself joins in when the sacred moment arrives.
ramacharitamanas::527.simple_meaning: The heavens are getting ready for a sacred wedding. Everything around the event turns auspicious, and the celestial singers begin their song.
ramacharitamanas::527.simple_insight: Some moments feel bigger than people alone — the whole world seems to bless them.
ramacharitamanas::527.detailed_meaning: The wedding preparations for Ram and Sita are underway. The radiant beings ready their vehicles, good omens appear, and the celestial dancers sing. This verse supports the larger scene of cosmic celebration rather than delivering a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::527.modern_relevance: A room fills with flowers, music starts before the guests arrive, and everyone can feel something important is about to happen. The atmosphere itself announces the moment.
ramacharitamanas::527.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the sacred mood surrounding it.

ramacharitamanas::528.verse_sanskrit: सिवहि संभु गन करहिं सिंगारा। जटा मुकुट अहि मौरु सँवारा॥ कुंडल कंकन पहिरे ब्याला। तन बिभूति पट केहरि छाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::528.verse_hindi: शिवजी के गण शिवजी का श्रृंगार करने लगे। जटाओं का मुकुट बनाकर उस पर साँपों का मौर सजाया गया। शिवजी ने साँपों के ही कुंडल और कंकण पहने, शरीर पर विभूति रमायी और वस्त्र की जगह बाघम्बर लपेट लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::528.english_translation: Shiva's attendants began adorning Shiva. They made a crown from his matted hair and decorated it with serpents. He wore serpent earrings and bracelets, smeared sacred ash on his body, and wrapped tiger skin instead of cloth.
ramacharitamanas::528.translation_literal: सिवहि (Shiva) / संभु (Shambhu) / गन (attendants) / करहिं (do) / सिंगारा (adornment) / जटा (matted hair) / मुकुट (crown) / अहि (serpent) / मौरु (crest) / सँवारा (decorated) / कुंडल (earrings) / कंकन (bracelets) / पहिरे (wore) / ब्याला (serpents) / तन (body) / बिभूति (sacred ash) / पट (cloth) / केहरि छाला (tiger skin)
ramacharitamanas::528.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::528.essence: True grandeur can wear the marks of renunciation.
ramacharitamanas::528.simple_meaning: Shiva is being ceremonially dressed by his attendants, with serpents, ash, and tiger skin as his adornment.
ramacharitamanas::528.simple_insight: Greatness here is stripped of luxury and wrapped in renunciation.
ramacharitamanas::528.detailed_meaning: At the wedding scene in Balkand, the divine guests are being prepared for the ceremony. Shiva's attendants dress him in his own wild, ascetic splendor, turning serpents, ash, and tiger skin into royal adornment before the next verse completes the image.
ramacharitamanas::528.modern_relevance: A room full of people may prize polished clothes and status symbols, yet the person who has nothing to prove can wear simplicity like a crown.
ramacharitamanas::528.insight: It shifts attention from outer luxury to the dignity of renunciation.

ramacharitamanas::529.verse_sanskrit: ससि ललाट सुंदर सिर गंगा। नयन तीनि उपबीत भुजंगा॥ गरल कंठ उर नर सिर माला। असिव बेष सिवधाम कृपाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::529.verse_hindi: शिवजी के सुंदर मस्तक पर चन्द्रमा, सिर पर गंगाजी, तीन नेत्र, साँपों का जनेऊ, गले में विष और छाती पर नरमुण्डों की माला थी। इस प्रकार उनका वेष अशुभ होने पर भी वे कल्याण के धाम और कृपालु हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::529.english_translation: The moon adorns his forehead, the Ganga crowns his head, and three eyes shine. Snakes form his sacred thread; poison rests in his throat; a garland of human skulls hangs on his chest. Though his appearance is fearsome, Shiva is the abode of grace and compassion.
ramacharitamanas::529.translation_literal: ससि (moon) / ललाट (forehead) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सिर (head) / गंगा (Ganga) / नयन (eyes) / तीनि (three) / उपबीत (sacred thread) / भुजंगा (snakes) / गरल (poison) / कंठ (throat) / उर (chest) / नर (human) / सिर (heads/skulls) / माला (garland) / असिव (inauspicious) / बेष (appearance) / सिवधाम (abode of Shiva) / कृपाला (compassionate)
ramacharitamanas::529.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::529.essence: Fearsome appearance can hide the gentlest heart.
ramacharitamanas::529.simple_meaning: Shiva’s form looks fierce and inauspicious, yet it is filled with beauty, holiness, and compassion.
ramacharitamanas::529.simple_insight: What looks frightening at first can still hold deep kindness.
ramacharitamanas::529.detailed_meaning: As Shiva is being adorned for the wedding procession, the poet pauses to describe his strange, powerful form: moon, Ganga, snakes, poison, and skull garland. The verse turns that eerie image into a statement of grace, preparing for the wonder of his presence.
ramacharitamanas::529.modern_relevance: A person walks into a room with tattoos, scars, and a hard face, and everyone assumes the worst. Then they speak gently, help quietly, and carry more tenderness than anyone expected.
ramacharitamanas::529.insight: It shifts attention from outward appearance to the deeper character beneath it.

ramacharitamanas::530.verse_sanskrit: कर त्रिसूल अरु डमरु बिराजा। चले बसहँ चढ़ि बाजहिं बाजा॥ देखि सिवहि सुरत्रिय मुसुकाहीं। बर लायक दुलहिनि जग नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::530.verse_hindi: एक हाथ में त्रिशूल और दूसरे में डमरू सुशोभित है। शिवजी बैल पर चढ़कर चले। बाजे बज रहे हैं। शिवजी को देखकर देवांगनाएँ मुस्कुरा रही हैं (और कहती हैं कि) इस वर के योग्य दुलहिन संसार में नहीं मिलेगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::530.english_translation: The trident and drum shine in Shiva's hands. Shiva rides forward on the bull while music plays. Seeing Shiva, the celestial women smile and say, 'No bride in the world is worthy of this groom.'
ramacharitamanas::530.translation_literal: कर (in hand) / त्रिसूल (trident) / अरु (and) / डमरु (drum) / बिराजा (shone) / चले (went) / बसहँ (on the bull) / चढ़ि (riding) / बाजहिं (sound) / बाजा (instruments)॥ / देखि (seeing) / सिवहि (Shiva) / सुरत्रिय (celestial women) / मुसुकाहीं (smiled) / बर (groom) / लायक (worthy) / दुलहिनि (bride) / जग (world) / नाहीं (not)॥
ramacharitamanas::530.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::530.essence: Shiva's wedding procession draws delighted admiration from the heavens.
ramacharitamanas::530.simple_meaning: Shiva arrives in splendid wedding procession, and the celestial women admire him as an unmatched groom.
ramacharitamanas::530.simple_insight: A sacred marriage can be celebrated with joy, wonder, and playful admiration.
ramacharitamanas::530.detailed_meaning: Shiva is now entering the wedding procession with his symbols of power and renunciation, riding the bull as music plays. The celestial women smile at his extraordinary form, praising him as a groom without equal. The verse is part of the larger scene of the divine wedding.
ramacharitamanas::530.modern_relevance: At a wedding procession, everyone turns to look at the groom and smiles at the beauty of the moment. Some arrivals carry a presence so complete that admiration comes before words.
ramacharitamanas::530.insight: It frames divine presence as something so striking that even onlookers respond with delight.

ramacharitamanas::531.verse_sanskrit: बिष्नु बिरंचि आदि सुरब्राता। चढ़ि चढ़ि बाहन चले बराता॥ सुर समाज सब भाँति अनूपा। नहिं बरात दूल्हे अनुरूपा ॥
ramacharitamanas::531.verse_hindi: विष्णु और ब्रह्मा आदि देवताओं के समूह अपने-अपने वाहनों (सवारियों) पर चढ़कर बारात में चले। देवताओं का समाज सब प्रकार से अनुपम (परम सुंदर) था, पर दूल्हे के योग्य बारात न थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::531.english_translation: Vishnu, Brahma, and the host of other radiant beings rode on their own mounts and went in the wedding procession. The company of radiant beings was splendid in every way, yet it was not a procession fit for the groom.
ramacharitamanas::531.translation_literal: बिष्नु (Vishnu) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / आदि (and other) / सुरब्राता (brotherhood of radiant beings) / चढ़ि चढ़ि (riding one after another) / बाहन (mounts) / चले (went) / बराता (wedding procession)॥ / सुर समाज (company of radiant beings) / सब भाँति (in every way) / अनूपा (unique, incomparable) / नहिं (not) / बरात (procession) / दूल्हे (of the groom) / अनुरूपा (fit, suitable)॥
ramacharitamanas::531.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::531.essence: Splendor can still be mismatched when it lacks true fit.
ramacharitamanas::531.simple_meaning: Vishnu, Brahma, and the other radiant beings joined the wedding procession on their own mounts. The procession was beautiful, but it still did not match the groom's greatness.
ramacharitamanas::531.simple_insight: Even the most splendid company can feel incomplete beside true greatness.
ramacharitamanas::531.detailed_meaning: In Shiva's wedding procession, the heavens themselves join in celebration. Vishnu, Brahma, and other radiant beings arrive on their mounts, filling the scene with splendor. Yet this verse pauses on the irony: even such a glorious procession still falls short of matching Shiva, the groom.
ramacharitamanas::531.modern_relevance: A grand event can be full of expensive details, perfect lighting, and famous guests — and still feel oddly wrong. The real measure is not spectacle, but fit.
ramacharitamanas::531.insight: It shifts attention from outward grandeur to whether the whole scene truly matches its center.

ramacharitamanas::532.verse_sanskrit: बिष्नु कहा अस बिहसि तब बोलि सकल दिसिराज। बिलग बिलग होइ चलहु सब निज निज सहित समाज ॥
ramacharitamanas::532.verse_hindi: तब विष्णु भगवान ने सब दिक्पालों को बुलाकर हँसकर ऐसा कहा- सब लोग अपने-अपने दल समेत अलग-अलग होकर चलो ॥
ramacharitamanas::532.english_translation: Then Vishnu smiled and said to all the guardians of the directions: "All of you, with your own retinues, go separately."
ramacharitamanas::532.translation_literal: बिष्नु (Vishnu) / कहा (said) / अस (thus) / बिहसि (smiling) / तब (then) / बोलि (speaking) / सकल (all) / दिसिराज (guardians of the directions) / बिलग बिलग (separately, separately) / होइ (become) / चलहु (go) / सब (all) / निज निज (each one's own) / सहित (with) / समाज (retinue, company)
ramacharitamanas::532.speaker: Vishnu
ramacharitamanas::532.essence: Order protects joy from turning into spectacle.
ramacharitamanas::532.simple_meaning: Vishnu tells the direction-guardians to go separately with their own groups. The wedding procession should not move as one huge crowd.
ramacharitamanas::532.simple_insight: Even a joyful occasion needs order. Pride and chaos can be softened by simple, wise coordination.
ramacharitamanas::532.detailed_meaning: At Shiva's wedding procession in Balkand, the celestial crowd has gathered in grand style. Vishnu smiles and tells the guardians of the directions to split into their own groups and move separately, keeping the procession orderly and fitting for the occasion.
ramacharitamanas::532.modern_relevance: A group chat explodes before a big event, everyone talking at once and nobody hearing the plan. One calm voice says, 'Split up, handle your parts, and move cleanly.'
ramacharitamanas::532.insight: It teaches coordination without ego: even celebration works best when each person knows their place.

ramacharitamanas::533.verse_sanskrit: बर अनुहारि बरात न भाई। हँसी करैहहु पर पुर जाई॥ बिष्नु बचन सुनि सुर मुसुकाने। निज निज सेन सहित बिलगाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::533.verse_hindi: हे भाई! हम लोगों की यह बारात वर के योग्य नहीं है। क्या पराए नगर में जाकर हँसी कराओगे? विष्णु भगवान की बात सुनकर देवता मुस्कुराए और वे अपनी-अपनी सेना सहित अलग हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::533.english_translation: Brother, this procession is not fit for the groom. Will you go to a foreign city and invite ridicule? Hearing Vishnu's words, the devas smiled and separated into their own armies.
ramacharitamanas::533.translation_literal: बर (fit) / अनुहारि (according to) / बरात (wedding procession) / न (not) / भाई (brother) / हँसी (laughter, ridicule) / करैहहु (will cause) / पर पुर (foreign city) / जाई (going) / बिष्नु (Vishnu) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / सुर (devas) / मुसुकाने (smiled) / निज निज (their own) / सेन (armies) / सहित (with) / बिलगाने (separated)
ramacharitamanas::533.speaker: Vishnu
ramacharitamanas::533.essence: A playful remark can bring a grand procession back into harmony.
ramacharitamanas::533.simple_meaning: Vishnu jokes that the divine wedding procession is not suited to the groom's dignity, so the devas separate into their own groups.
ramacharitamanas::533.simple_insight: Even sacred moments can carry lightness. Humour can organize a crowd without breaking reverence.
ramacharitamanas::533.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the celestial guests arrive in a grand procession. Vishnu speaks playfully, saying this display is not fitting for the groom and would cause laughter in a foreign city. The devas smile and rearrange themselves.
ramacharitamanas::533.modern_relevance: At a formal event, one person cracks a dry joke and the whole room relaxes. Tension drops, everyone finds their place, and the occasion feels alive instead of stiff.
ramacharitamanas::533.insight: It shows how wit can restore order in a grand gathering without losing dignity.

ramacharitamanas::534.verse_sanskrit: मनहीं मन महेसु मुसुकाहीं। हरि के बिंग्य बचन नहिं जाहीं॥ अति प्रिय बचन सुनत प्रिय केरे। भृंगिहि प्रेरि सकल गन टेरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::534.verse_hindi: महादेवजी (यह देखकर) मन-ही-मन मुस्कुराते हैं कि विष्णु भगवान के व्यंग्य-वचन (दिल्लगी) नहीं छूटते! अपने प्यारे (विष्णु भगवान) के इन अति प्रिय वचनों को सुनकर शिवजी ने भी भृंगी को भेजकर अपने सब गणों को बुलवा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::534.english_translation: Shiva smiles inwardly: Hari’s playful words never fail to amuse. Hearing those beloved words from his beloved, Shiva sends Bhṛngi to summon all his attendants.
ramacharitamanas::534.translation_literal: मनहीं मन (in his own mind) / महेसु (Shiva) / मुसुकाहीं (smile) / हरि के (of Hari) / बिंग्य (playful, teasing) / बचन (words) / नहिं जाहीं (do not go away, never fail) / अति (very) / प्रिय (dear) / बचन (words) / सुनत (hearing) / प्रिय केरे (of the beloved) / भृंगिहि (Bhṛngi) / प्रेरि (sending) / सकल (all) / गन (attendants) / टेरे (called)
ramacharitamanas::534.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::534.essence: Even divine reverence can answer with a smile.
ramacharitamanas::534.simple_meaning: Shiva smiles at Hari’s teasing words and quickly calls his attendants together through Bhṛngi.
ramacharitamanas::534.simple_insight: Even the highest devotion can be tender, playful, and full of warmth.
ramacharitamanas::534.detailed_meaning: Vishnu has just sent the gods off in separate groups for the wedding procession. Shiva hears the playful tone and smiles to himself. Amused and delighted by Hari’s words, he sends Bhṛngi to gather all his attendants.
ramacharitamanas::534.modern_relevance: A friend teases you in a group chat, and instead of taking offense, you laugh because you know the affection behind it. That ease is the mood here.
ramacharitamanas::534.insight: It shows devotion as a living relationship, where reverence includes delight and play.

ramacharitamanas::535.verse_sanskrit: सिव अनुसासन सुनि सब आए। प्रभु पद जलज सीस तिन्ह नाए॥ नाना बाहन नाना बेषा। बिहसे सिव समाज निज देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::535.verse_hindi: शिवजी की आज्ञा सुनते ही सब चले आए और उन्होंने स्वामी के चरण कमलों में सिर नवाया। तरह-तरह की सवारियों और तरह-तरह के वेष वाले अपने समाज को देखकर शिवजी हँसे ॥
ramacharitamanas::535.english_translation: Hearing Shiva's command, everyone came and bowed their heads at the lord's lotus feet. Seeing his own company with many different mounts and many different disguises, Shiva laughed.
ramacharitamanas::535.translation_literal: सिव (Shiva) / अनुसासन (command) / सुनि (hearing) / सब (all) / आए (came) / प्रभु (lord) / पद (feet) / जलज (lotus-like) / सीस (head) / तिन्ह (they) / नाए (bowed) / नाना (many kinds of) / बाहन (mounts) / नाना (many kinds of) / बेषा (disguises) / बिहसे (laughed) / सिव (Shiva) / समाज (company) / निज (own) / देखा (seeing)
ramacharitamanas::535.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::535.essence: True majesty can smile at its own strange variety.
ramacharitamanas::535.simple_meaning: Shiva's followers arrive, bow to the lord, and Shiva laughs at the varied forms in his own company.
ramacharitamanas::535.simple_insight: It leaves a sense of playful order: even the divine gathering is full of variety, not stiffness.
ramacharitamanas::535.detailed_meaning: Shiva has called his attendants to the wedding scene. They come at once, bow to the lord, and then Shiva looks over the strange mix of mounts and disguises in his own retinue and smiles. The verse sets up the comic, wondrous procession before the main arrival.
ramacharitamanas::535.modern_relevance: A wedding convoy rolls in with scooters, cars, and borrowed outfits, and everyone is trying a little too hard. The moment still works because the joy is real, not polished.
ramacharitamanas::535.insight: It frames sacred gathering as alive, varied, and lightly self-aware rather than formal and rigid.

ramacharitamanas::536.verse_sanskrit: कोउ मुख हीन बिपुल मुख काहू। बिनु पद कर कोउ बहु पद बाहू॥ बिपुल नयन कोउ नयन बिहीना। रिष्टपुष्ट कोउ अति तनखीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::536.verse_hindi: कोई बिना मुख का है, किसी के बहुत से मुख हैं, कोई बिना हाथ-पैर का है तो किसी के कई हाथ-पैर हैं। किसी के बहुत आँखें हैं तो किसी के एक भी आँख नहीं है। कोई बहुत मोटा-ताजा है, तो कोई बहुत ही दुबला-पतला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::536.english_translation: Some have no mouth, some have many mouths. Some have no hands or feet, some have many hands and feet. Some have many eyes, some have no eyes. Some are very fat, and some are very thin.
ramacharitamanas::536.translation_literal: कोउ (someone) / मुख हीन (without a mouth) / बिपुल (many) / मुख (mouths) / काहू (someone) / बिनु (without) / पद (feet) / कर (hands) / कोउ (someone) / बहु (many) / पद (feet) / बाहू (arms) / बिपुल (many) / नयन (eyes) / कोउ (someone) / नयन (eyes) / बिहीना (without) / रिष्टपुष्ट (stout) / कोउ (someone) / अति (very) / तनखीना (thin)
ramacharitamanas::536.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::536.essence: Life appears in countless forms, each with its own shape.
ramacharitamanas::536.simple_meaning: Different beings appear with very different bodies: some lack mouths or limbs, some have many, some have many eyes, and some are thin or stout.
ramacharitamanas::536.simple_insight: Apparent difference is part of the same vast order. The world is full of forms, not fixed identities.
ramacharitamanas::536.detailed_meaning: In Shiva’s retelling of the cosmic scene at the Sita-swayamvar, the assembled beings are described in all their strange forms. This verse lists their bodies and features, preparing for the larger vision of a universe filled with countless kinds of beings.
ramacharitamanas::536.modern_relevance: You walk into a crowded train and see every kind of body, face, and posture at once. The mind wants to sort and judge; the verse simply notices how varied life already is.
ramacharitamanas::536.insight: It shifts attention from sameness to the sheer range of living forms.

ramacharitamanas::537.verse_sanskrit: तन कीन कोउ अति पीन पावन कोउ अपावन गति धरें। भूषन कराल कपाल कर सब सद्य सोनित तन भरें॥ खर स्वान सुअर सृकाल मुख गन बेष अगनित को गनै। बहु जिनस प्रेत पिसाच जोगि जमात बरनत नहिं बनै॥
ramacharitamanas::537.verse_hindi: कोई बहुत दुबला, कोई बहुत मोटा, कोई पवित्र और कोई अपवित्र वेष धारण किए हुए है। भयंकर गहने पहने हाथ में कपाल लिए हैं और सब के सब शरीर में ताजा खून लपेटे हुए हैं। गधे, कुत्ते, सूअर और सियार के से उनके मुख हैं। गणों के अनगिनत वेषों को कौन गिने? बहुत प्रकार के प्रेत, पिशाच और योगिनियों की जमाते हैं। उनका वर्णन करते नहीं बनता।
ramacharitamanas::537.english_translation: Some are extremely thin, some extremely stout; some bear auspicious forms, some in inauspicious forms. They wear terrible ornaments and skulls in their hands, and their bodies are smeared with fresh blood. Their faces are like donkeys, dogs, pigs, and jackals. Who can count the countless forms of the attendants? Many kinds of ghosts, spirits, and yoginis are there; their company cannot be described.
ramacharitamanas::537.translation_literal: तन (body) / कीन (made) / कोउ (some) / अति (very) / पीन (stout) / पावन (auspicious) / कोउ (some) / अपावन (inauspicious) / गति (form/state) / धरें (having taken) ॥ भूषन (ornaments) / कराल (terrible) / कपाल (skulls) / कर (in hand) / सब (all) / सद्य (fresh) / सोनित (blood) / तन (body) / भरें (smeared) ॥ खर (donkey) / स्वान (dog) / सुअर (pig) / सृकाल (jackal) / मुख (face) / गन (company) / बेष (forms) / अगनित (countless) / को (of) / गनै (count) ॥ बहु (many) / जिनस (kinds) / प्रेत (ghosts) / पिसाच (spirits) / जोगि (yoginis) / जमात (crowd) / बरनत (describing) / नहिं (not) / बनै (possible)
ramacharitamanas::537.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::537.essence: Countless forms gather around Shiva, too strange to fully name.
ramacharitamanas::537.simple_meaning: Shiva's attendants appear in countless strange forms, some beautiful and some terrifying, with wild ornaments and fierce faces. The verse is describing their bizarre crowd, not teaching a doctrine.
ramacharitamanas::537.simple_insight: Sometimes a scene is meant to overwhelm you, not explain itself.
ramacharitamanas::537.detailed_meaning: Shiva has summoned his attendants, and the vision becomes surreal: deformed bodies, skull ornaments, blood-smeared forms, animal faces, and countless kinds of spirits. Tulsidas lingers on the spectacle to show the vast, untamed energy of Shiva's retinue before the next verse adds their movement and song.
ramacharitamanas::537.modern_relevance: A festival crowd spills out of a side street at midnight: painted faces, strange costumes, drums, laughter, and masks that are half playful and half unsettling. The point is the atmosphere, not a lesson.
ramacharitamanas::537.insight: It trains attention to receive vivid scene-setting without forcing a moral onto every detail.

ramacharitamanas::538.verse_sanskrit: नाचहिं गावहिं गीत परम तरंगी भूत सब। देखत अति बिपरीत बोलहिं बचन बिचित्र बिधि ॥
ramacharitamanas::538.verse_hindi: भूत-प्रेत नाचते और गाते हैं, वे सब बड़े मौजी हैं। देखने में बहुत ही बेढंगे जान पड़ते हैं और बड़े ही विचित्र ढंग से बोलते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::538.english_translation: The spirits dance and sing, all full of wild delight. They look utterly strange and speak in wonderfully odd ways.
ramacharitamanas::538.translation_literal: नाचहिं (dance) / गावहिं (sing) / गीत (songs) / परम (supremely) / तरंगी (playful, whimsical) / भूत सब (all spirits) / देखत (seeing) / अति (very) / बिपरीत (strange, contrary) / बोलहिं (they speak) / बचन (words) / बिचित्र (wonderful, peculiar) / बिधि (way)
ramacharitamanas::538.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::538.essence: The divine wedding turns even the strange into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::538.simple_meaning: The spirits are dancing, singing, and speaking in strange, playful ways. The verse simply describes their odd, lively behavior.
ramacharitamanas::538.simple_insight: Sometimes a scene is meant to be seen, not interpreted. Wonder can stand on its own.
ramacharitamanas::538.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession is being described in all its strange splendor. Around this divine marriage, spirits and uncanny beings are dancing and singing with wild delight, adding to the scene’s playful, otherworldly atmosphere before the bridegroom’s barat moves on.
ramacharitamanas::538.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall and everything feels slightly unreal — loud music, strange costumes, people laughing too hard. Some moments are meant to overwhelm you with color and motion.
ramacharitamanas::538.insight: It trains attention to notice vivid scene-setting without forcing a moral lesson onto every detail.

ramacharitamanas::539.verse_sanskrit: जस दूलहु तसि बनी बराता। कौतुक बिबिध होहिं मग जाता॥ इहाँ हिमाचल रचेउ बिताना। अति बिचित्र नहिं जाइ बखाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::539.verse_hindi: जैसा दूल्हा है, अब वैसी ही बारात बन गई है। मार्ग में चलते हुए भाँति-भाँति के कौतुक (तमाशे) होते जाते हैं। इधर हिमाचल ने ऐसा विचित्र मण्डप बनाया कि जिसका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::539.english_translation: As the bridegroom is, so has the wedding party become. On the way, all kinds of marvels arise. Here, Himachal has built a wondrous pavilion beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::539.translation_literal: जस (as) / दूलहु (bridegroom) / तसि (so) / बनी (became) / बराता (wedding party)। / कौतुक (marvels, amusements) / बिबिध (various) / होहिं (happen) / मग (road) / जाता (going)॥ / इहाँ (here) / हिमाचल (Himachal) / रचेउ (built) / बिताना (pavilion, canopy)। / अति (very) / बिचित्र (wonderful, strange) / नहिं (not) / जाइ (can be) / बखाना (described)॥
ramacharitamanas::539.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::539.essence: A great union makes the whole world seem newly arranged.
ramacharitamanas::539.simple_meaning: The wedding procession matches the bridegroom’s grandeur, and the journey is full of wonders. Himachal has prepared an indescribably beautiful pavilion for the ceremony.
ramacharitamanas::539.simple_insight: Great occasions reshape everything around them; even the road and the setting begin to feel alive with celebration.
ramacharitamanas::539.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession is arriving for Sita and Ram’s marriage. Tulsidas pauses the story to show how the entire scene has turned extraordinary: the party, the road, and the pavilion all reflect the grandeur of the moment.
ramacharitamanas::539.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall and everything feels transformed — the lights, the music, even the air. A sacred or joyful moment changes the whole world around it.
ramacharitamanas::539.insight: It shifts attention from plot to atmosphere, showing how devotion makes even the setting feel sacred.

ramacharitamanas::540.verse_sanskrit: सैल सकल जहँ लगि जग माहीं। लघु बिसाल नहिं बरनि सिराहीं॥ बन सागर सब नदी तलावा। हिमगिरि सब कहुँ नेवत पठावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::540.verse_hindi: जगत में जितने छोटे-बड़े पर्वत थे, जिनका वर्णन करके पार नहीं मिलता तथा जितने वन, समुद्र, नदियाँ और तालाब थे, हिमाचल ने सबको नेवता भेजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::540.english_translation: Himachal sent invitations to all mountains, forests, seas, rivers, and lakes in the world.
ramacharitamanas::540.translation_literal: सैल (mountains) / सकल (all) / जहँ लगि (as far as) / जग माहीं (in the world) / लघु (small) / बिसाल (great) / नहिं (not) / बरनि (describing) / सिराहीं (comes to an end) / बन (forests) / सागर (seas) / सब (all) / नदी (rivers) / तलावा (ponds) / हिमगिरि (Himalaya) / सब कहुँ (to all) / नेवत (invitation) / पठावा (sent)
ramacharitamanas::540.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::540.essence: A sacred celebration becomes large enough to include the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::540.simple_meaning: Himachal sent invitations to every mountain, forest, sea, river, and lake in the world.
ramacharitamanas::540.simple_insight: Even a wedding becomes cosmic when joy is shared with everything around it.
ramacharitamanas::540.detailed_meaning: The wedding celebration is being prepared in the Himalayas. Himachal is not inviting only people; he sends summons to the whole living landscape — mountains, forests, seas, rivers, and lakes — so the marriage of Shiva and Parvati becomes a universal festival.
ramacharitamanas::540.modern_relevance: You plan a wedding, and suddenly every cousin, neighbor, and old family friend gets included. The joy feels bigger than the guest list — as if the whole world should be there.
ramacharitamanas::540.insight: It frames the event as a celebration that includes the entire world, not just the immediate family.

ramacharitamanas::541.verse_sanskrit: कामरूप सुंदर तन धारी। सहित समाज सहित बर नारी॥ गए सकल तुहिमाचल गेहा। गावहिं मंगल सहित सनेहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::541.verse_hindi: वे सब अपनी इच्छानुसार रूप धारण करने वाले सुंदर शरीर धारण कर सुंदरी स्त्रियों और समाजों के साथ हिमाचल के घर गए। सभी स्नेह सहित मंगल गीत गाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::541.english_translation: All those who could take whatever form they wished, with beautiful bodies, along with their companions and women, went to Himachal's home. Everyone sang auspicious songs with affection.
ramacharitamanas::541.translation_literal: कामरूप (able to assume desired forms) / सुंदर (beautiful) / तन (body) / धारी (bearing) / सहित (together with) / समाज (companions) / सहित (together with) / बर (excellent) / नारी (women) / गए (went) / सकल (all) / तुहिमाचल (Himachal) / गेहा (home) / गावहिं (sing) / मंगल (auspicious songs) / सहित (with) / सनेहा (affection)
ramacharitamanas::541.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::541.essence: A sacred gathering becomes joyful when everyone arrives in love.
ramacharitamanas::541.simple_meaning: The guests arrive in splendid forms, bringing their companions and women, and they enter Himachal's home singing auspicious songs with love.
ramacharitamanas::541.simple_insight: Joy multiplies when people come together with goodwill and celebration.
ramacharitamanas::541.detailed_meaning: As Sita's swayamvar gathers momentum, the invited guests reach Himachal's home in dazzling forms. The scene is still ceremonial and festive, with everyone arriving together and filling the space with loving, auspicious songs.
ramacharitamanas::541.modern_relevance: A wedding hall fills before the ceremony begins: relatives in bright clothes, music starting up, everyone arriving with smiles and excitement. The moment is about shared joy, not a single speech.
ramacharitamanas::541.insight: It shifts attention from doctrine to atmosphere: the sacred event is unfolding through collective celebration.

ramacharitamanas::542.verse_sanskrit: प्रथमहिं गिरि बहु गृह सँवराए। जथाजोगु तहँ तहँ सब छाए॥ पुर सोभा अवलोकि सुहाई। लागइ लघु बिरंचि निपुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::542.verse_hindi: हिमाचल ने पहले ही से बहुत से घर सजवा रखे थे। यथायोग्य उन-उन स्थानों में सब लोग उतर गए। नगर की सुंदर शोभा देखकर ब्रह्मा की रचना चातुरी भी तुच्छ लगती थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::542.english_translation: Himachal had already prepared many houses. Everyone settled in the right place. Seeing the city’s beauty, even Brahma’s skill seemed small.
ramacharitamanas::542.translation_literal: प्रथमहिं (first) / गिरि (the mountain) / बहु (many) / गृह (houses) / सँवराए (made ready) / जथाजोगु (as fitting) / तहँ तहँ (here and there) / सब (all) / छाए (spread out, settled) / पुर (city) / सोभा (beauty, splendor) / अवलोकि (seeing) / सुहाई (beautiful) / लागइ (seemed) / लघु (small) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / निपुनाई (skill, craftsmanship)
ramacharitamanas::542.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::542.essence: Prepared welcome can make greatness feel ordinary.
ramacharitamanas::542.simple_meaning: Himachal has already arranged homes for everyone, and the city is so beautiful that even Brahma’s craftsmanship seems small beside it.
ramacharitamanas::542.simple_insight: Beauty can be so complete that it humbles even the maker in your mind.
ramacharitamanas::542.detailed_meaning: At Himachal’s grand welcome for the divine marriage gathering, the guests are already being placed in prepared homes throughout the city. The splendor of the place is so overwhelming that the poet says even Brahma’s creative skill feels minor here.
ramacharitamanas::542.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where every flower, light, and seat has been arranged with care. Before anyone speaks, the whole place tells you: you were expected, and you were welcomed.
ramacharitamanas::542.insight: It shifts attention from mere arrangement to the feeling of being fully received.

ramacharitamanas::543.verse_sanskrit: लघु लाग बिधि की निपुनता अवलोकि पुर सोभा सही। बन बाग कूप तड़ाग सरिता सुभग सब सक को कही॥ मंगल बिपुल तोरन पताका केतु गृह गृह सोहहीं। बनिता पुरुष सुंदर चतुर छबि देखि मुनि मन मोहहीं॥
ramacharitamanas::543.verse_hindi: नगर की शोभा देखकर ब्रह्मा की निपुणता सचमुच तुच्छ लगती है। वन, बाग, कुएँ, तालाब, नदियाँ सभी सुंदर हैं, उनका वर्णन कौन कर सकता है? घर-घर बहुत से मंगल सूचक तोरण और ध्वजा-पताकाएँ सुशोभित हो रही हैं। वहाँ के सुंदर और चतुर स्त्री-पुरुषों की छबि देखकर मुनियों के भी मन मोहित हो जाते हैं॥
ramacharitamanas::543.english_translation: Seeing the beauty of the city, Brahma's skill seems small. Forests, gardens, wells, ponds, and rivers are all lovely; who can describe them all? Great auspicious banners and flags adorn every house. The beautiful and clever women and men there enchant even the sages' minds.
ramacharitamanas::543.translation_literal: लघु (small) / लाग (seems) / बिधि (Brahma) / की (of) / निपुनता (skill) / अवलोकि (seeing) / पुर (city) / सोभा (beauty) / सही (truly) / बन (forest) / बाग (garden) / कूप (wells) / तड़ाग (ponds) / सरिता (rivers) / सुभग (beautiful) / सब (all) / सक (able) / को (who) / कही (say)॥ / मंगल (auspicious) / बिपुल (many) / तोरन (festive arches) / पताका (flags) / केतु (banners) / गृह गृह (house by house) / सोहहीं (shine)॥ / बनिता (women) / पुरुष (men) / सुंदर (beautiful) / चतुर (clever) / छबि (beauty) / देखि (seeing) / मुनि (sages) / मन (minds) / मोहहीं (are enchanted)॥
ramacharitamanas::543.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::543.essence: Beauty can be so complete it makes even creation seem modest.
ramacharitamanas::543.simple_meaning: The city is so beautiful that even Brahma's craftsmanship seems small by comparison. Every part of it, from gardens to rivers to houses, is adorned and enchanting.
ramacharitamanas::543.simple_insight: Some places feel so complete that language itself runs out.
ramacharitamanas::543.detailed_meaning: The guests have entered Himachal's splendid city for Sita's swayamvar. Tulsidas lingers on the setting: gardens, waters, banners, and graceful people everywhere. The verse deepens the wonder before the next line reveals why this city feels almost beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::543.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding venue where every lamp, flower, and doorway has been arranged with care. Before anyone speaks, the whole place already tells you that something sacred is about to happen.
ramacharitamanas::543.insight: It shifts attention from utility to sacred beauty, showing how an environment can elevate the mind before any event begins.

ramacharitamanas::544.verse_sanskrit: जगदंबा जहँ अवतरी सो पुरु बरनि कि जाइ। रिद्धि सिद्धि संपत्ति सुख नित नूतन अधिकाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::544.verse_hindi: जिस नगर में स्वयं जगदम्बा ने अवतार लिया, क्या उसका वर्णन हो सकता है? वहाँ ऋद्धि, सिद्धि, सम्पत्ति और सुख नित-नए बढ़ते जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::544.english_translation: Can the city where Jagadamba herself incarnated ever be described? There, prosperity, accomplishment, wealth, and joy keep increasing anew every day.
ramacharitamanas::544.translation_literal: जगदंबा (world-mother) / जहँ (where) / अवतरी (incarnated) / सो (that) / पुरु (city) / बरनि (described) / कि (whether) / जाइ (can be done) / रिद्धि (prosperity) / सिद्धि (accomplishment) / संपत्ति (wealth) / सुख (joy) / नित (daily) / नूतन (new) / अधिकाइ (increase)
ramacharitamanas::544.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::544.essence: A place touched by the divine keeps becoming more abundant.
ramacharitamanas::544.simple_meaning: The city where the world-mother was born cannot be fully described. Its prosperity, success, wealth, and joy keep growing every day.
ramacharitamanas::544.simple_insight: Some places feel alive with blessing, as if goodness keeps renewing itself there.
ramacharitamanas::544.detailed_meaning: The narration lingers on the splendour of the city before Sita’s wedding procession arrives. After describing its beauty, the poet says even that is not enough, because this is the city where Jagadamba appeared and everything keeps flourishing.
ramacharitamanas::544.modern_relevance: You walk into a home where the air feels different — calmer, warmer, somehow more generous. No one can list why it feels blessed, but everyone can feel it.
ramacharitamanas::544.insight: It shifts attention from material beauty alone to the sacred presence that makes abundance deepen.

ramacharitamanas::545.verse_sanskrit: नगर निकट बरात सुनि आई। पुर खरभरु सोभा अधिकाई॥ करि बनाव सजि बाहन नाना। चले लेन सादर अगवाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::545.verse_hindi: बारात को नगर के निकट आई सुनकर नगर में चहल-पहल मच गई, जिससे उसकी शोभा बढ़ गई। अगवानी करने वाले लोग बनाव-श्रृंगार करके तथा नाना प्रकार की सवारियों को सजाकर आदर सहित बारात को लेने चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::545.english_translation: Hearing that the marriage procession had reached near the city, the city became lively and even more beautiful. People dressed up, decorated many kinds of vehicles, and went out respectfully to welcome it.
ramacharitamanas::545.translation_literal: नगर (city) / निकट (near) / बरात (marriage procession) / सुनि (hearing) / आई (came) / पुर (city) / खरभरु (commotion, bustle) / सोभा (beauty) / अधिकाई (increased)॥ / करि (having done) / बनाव (dressing up, adornment) / सजि (decorated) / बाहन (vehicles, mounts) / नाना (various) / चले (went) / लेन (to receive) / सादर (respectfully) / अगवाना (welcome party, going ahead)॥
ramacharitamanas::545.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::545.essence: Arrival itself can beautify an entire city.
ramacharitamanas::545.simple_meaning: The city became lively when the wedding procession came close. People prepared themselves, decorated their rides, and went out respectfully to welcome it.
ramacharitamanas::545.simple_insight: Joy spreads when a long-awaited arrival is near.
ramacharitamanas::545.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the wedding procession is finally close to the city. The streets stir, people dress up, and the welcome party goes out with honor. The verse lingers on the festive movement before the great meeting of Ram and Sita.
