ramacharitamanas::545.modern_relevance: A neighborhood wakes up because the guests everyone has waited for are finally turning into the lane. People sweep the steps, straighten their clothes, and step out smiling before the first knock.
ramacharitamanas::545.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the shared excitement it creates.

ramacharitamanas::546.verse_sanskrit: हियँ हरषे सुर सेन निहारी। हरिहि देखि अति भए सुखारी॥ सिव समाज जब देखन लागे। बिडरि चले बाहन सब भागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::546.verse_hindi: देवताओं के समाज को देखकर सब मन में प्रसन्न हुए और विष्णु भगवान को देखकर तो बहुत ही सुखी हुए, किन्तु जब शिवजी के दल को देखने लगे तब तो उनके सब वाहन (सवारियों के हाथी, घोड़े, रथ के बैल आदि) डरकर भाग चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::546.english_translation: The gods were delighted to see their host. Seeing Hari made them deeply happy. But when they looked at Shiva's company, all their mounts fled in fear.
ramacharitamanas::546.translation_literal: हियँ (in the heart) / हरषे (rejoiced) / सुर (gods) / सेन (host/army) / निहारी (seeing) । / हरिहि (Hari) / देखि (seeing) / अति (very) / भए (became) / सुखारी (happy) ॥ / सिव (Shiva) / समाज (company/assembly) / जब (when) / देखन (to see) / लागे (began) । / बिडरि (frightened) / चले (ran) / बाहन (mounts/vehicles) / सब (all) / भागे (fled) ॥
ramacharitamanas::546.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::546.essence: Divine presence can delight the heart and unsettle the body at once.
ramacharitamanas::546.simple_meaning: The gods felt joy at the sight of the divine company, but their mounts panicked when they saw Shiva's group.
ramacharitamanas::546.simple_insight: Some presences calm the heart; others make the body instinctively recoil.
ramacharitamanas::546.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the marriage procession is arriving and the city is alive with wonder. The gods rejoice at the sight of the divine assembly and feel even greater joy seeing Hari. Then Shiva's company appears, so awe-inspiring that the mounts of the gods scatter in fear.
ramacharitamanas::546.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where one person instantly relaxes everyone, while another's intensity makes people go silent. Presence itself changes the atmosphere before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::546.insight: It shows how sacred presence can be felt before it is understood, and how fear can arise from awe.

ramacharitamanas::547.verse_sanskrit: धरि धीरजु तहँ रहे सयाने। बालक सब लै जीव पराने॥ गएँ भवन पूछहिं पितु माता। कहहिं बचन भय कंपित गाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::547.verse_hindi: कुछ बड़ी उम्र के समझदार लोग धीरज धरकर वहाँ डटे रहे। लड़के तो सब अपने प्राण लेकर भागे। घर पहुँचने पर जब माता-पिता पूछते हैं, तब वे भय से काँपते हुए शरीर से ऐसा वचन कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::547.english_translation: The wise stayed there with patience. The boys fled with their lives. When they returned home, their mothers and fathers asked them, and they answered with trembling bodies.
ramacharitamanas::547.translation_literal: धरि (holding) / धीरजु (patience) / तहँ (there) / रहे (remained) / सयाने (the wise) / बालक (boys) / सब (all) / लै (taking) / जीव (life) / पराने (ran away) / गएँ (having gone) / भवन (home) / पूछहिं (they ask) / पितु (father) / माता (mother) / कहहिं (they speak) / बचन (words) / भय (fear) / कंपित (trembling) / गाता (body)
ramacharitamanas::547.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::547.essence: Fear sends some running while steadiness holds its ground.
ramacharitamanas::547.simple_meaning: The elders stayed calm, but the younger people ran away in fear. Later, they went home shaking and had to explain what happened to their parents.
ramacharitamanas::547.simple_insight: Fear reveals itself quickly. Calm presence is not the same as panic.
ramacharitamanas::547.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession has reached the city, but Shiva's strange, fearsome company has unsettled everyone. Some wiser people hold their ground, while the younger ones flee home trembling. The scene builds the shock that makes the next reaction even sharper.
ramacharitamanas::547.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and instantly feel you are the least prepared person there. Some people stay composed, but others rush out and rehearse excuses before they even reach home.
ramacharitamanas::547.insight: It contrasts steady composure with panic, showing how the same situation exposes different levels of inner steadiness.

ramacharitamanas::548.verse_sanskrit: कहिअ काह कहि जाइ न बाता। जम कर धार किधौं बरिआता॥ बरु बौराह बसहँ असवारा। ब्याल कपाल बिभूषन छारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::548.verse_hindi: क्या कहें, कोई बात कही नहीं जाती। यह बारात है या यमराज की सेना? दूल्हा पागल है और बैल पर सवार है। साँप, कपाल और राख ही उसके गहने हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::548.english_translation: What can be said? No words can describe it. Is this a wedding procession or Yama's army? The groom is wild, riding a bull, with snakes, skulls, and ash as ornaments.
ramacharitamanas::548.translation_literal: कहिअ (can be said) / काह (what) / कहि (having said) / जाइ (goes) / न (not) / बाता (speech, words) ॥ जम (Yama) / कर (of) / धार (army, line) / किधौं (or) / बरिआता (wedding procession) ॥ बरु (indeed) / बौराह (mad, wild) / बसहँ (bull) / असवारा (rider) । ब्याल (snakes) / कपाल (skulls) / बिभूषन (ornaments) / छारा (ash) ॥
ramacharitamanas::548.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::548.essence: Shiva's procession shatters every ordinary expectation of beauty.
ramacharitamanas::548.simple_meaning: The crowd is stunned by Shiva's appearance. His wedding procession looks terrifying, unlike any ordinary marriage.
ramacharitamanas::548.simple_insight: A mind that expects the familiar can feel shock before it feels wonder.
ramacharitamanas::548.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession of Shiva is arriving, and the onlookers cannot make sense of what they see. Instead of royal splendor, they see ash, snakes, skulls, and a bull. The verse captures their bewildered fear before the deeper divine grandeur is understood.
ramacharitamanas::548.modern_relevance: You open the door expecting a neat, normal scene and find complete chaos instead. The first reaction is disbelief before understanding catches up.
ramacharitamanas::548.insight: It shifts attention from polished appearance to the startling reality beneath it.

ramacharitamanas::549.verse_sanskrit: तन छार ब्याल कपाल भूषन नगन जटिल भयंकरा। सँग भूत प्रेत पिसाच जोगिनि बिकट मुख रजनीचरा॥ जो जिअत रहिहि बरात देखत पुन्य बड़ तेहि कर सही। देखिहि सो उमा बिबाहु घर घर बात असि लरिकन्ह कही॥
ramacharitamanas::549.verse_hindi: दूल्हे के शरीर पर राख लगी है, साँप और कपाल के गहने हैं, वह नंगा, जटाधारी और भयंकर है। उसके साथ भयानक मुखवाले भूत, प्रेत, पिशाच, योगिनियाँ और राक्षस हैं, जो बारात को देखकर जीता बचेगा, सचमुच उसके बड़े ही पुण्य हैं और वही पार्वती का विवाह देखेगा। लड़कों ने घर-घर यही बात कही।
ramacharitamanas::549.english_translation: His body was smeared with ash, adorned with snakes and skulls, naked, matted-haired, and terrifying. With him were fearsome ghosts, spirits, ghouls, yoginis, and wild-eyed night-walkers. The boys said, 'Whoever lives to see this wedding procession is truly blessed; that person will see Uma's marriage.' They carried this story from house to house.
ramacharitamanas::549.translation_literal: तन (body) / छार (ash) / ब्याल (snakes) / कपाल (skulls) / भूषन (ornaments) / नगन (naked) / जटिल (matted-haired) / भयंकरा (terrifying) / सँग (with) / भूत (ghosts) / प्रेत (spirits) / पिसाच (ghouls) / जोगिनि (yoginis) / बिकट (fearsome) / मुख (faces) / रजनीचरा (night-walkers) / जो (whoever) / जिअत (alive) / रहिहि (will remain) / बरात (wedding procession) / देखत (seeing) / पुन्य (merit) / बड़ (great) / तेहि (that) / कर (of) / सही (truly) / देखिहि (will see) / सो (that one) / उमा (Uma) / बिबाहु (wedding) / घर घर (from house to house) / बात (talk) / असि (thus) / लरिकन्ह (by the boys) / कही (said)
ramacharitamanas::549.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::549.essence: The most terrifying sight can also be a blessed one.
ramacharitamanas::549.simple_meaning: The boys describe Shiva's strange wedding procession and joke that anyone who survives seeing it is blessed enough to witness Uma's wedding.
ramacharitamanas::549.simple_insight: Even fear can turn into wonder when you are caught inside a sacred moment.
ramacharitamanas::549.detailed_meaning: The boys have just seen Shiva's bizarre wedding procession and are running home in shock. They describe his ash-smeared, snake-adorned form and the eerie crowd around him, then laugh that only a highly blessed person could survive seeing such a sight and witness Uma's marriage.
ramacharitamanas::549.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with screenshots after someone shows up in the most unexpected way at a formal event. People panic, then joke, then realize they have witnessed something unforgettable.
ramacharitamanas::549.insight: It turns shock into awe and prepares the reader for Shiva's marriage as a sacred, otherworldly event.

ramacharitamanas::550.verse_sanskrit: समुझि महेस समाज सब जननि जनक मुसुकाहिं। बाल बुझाए बिबिध बिधि निडर होहु डरु नाहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::550.verse_hindi: महेश्वर (शिवजी) का समाज समझकर सब लड़कों के माता-पिता मुस्कुराते हैं। उन्होंने बहुत तरह से लड़कों को समझाया कि निडर हो जाओ, डर की कोई बात नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::550.english_translation: Seeing that it is Lord Shiva’s company, all the parents smile. They reassure the boys in many ways: “Be fearless; there is nothing to fear.”
ramacharitamanas::550.translation_literal: समुझि (understanding) / महेस (Shiva) / समाज (company or gathering) / सब (all) / जननि (mothers) / जनक (fathers) / मुसुकाहिं (smile) / बाल (boys) / बुझाए (reassured) / बिबिध बिधि (in many ways) / निडर (fearless) / होहु (be) / डरु (fear) / नाहिं (not)
ramacharitamanas::550.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::550.essence: Clear seeing turns fear into a smile.
ramacharitamanas::550.simple_meaning: The parents realize this is Shiva’s wedding party, so they smile and calm the boys, telling them not to be afraid.
ramacharitamanas::550.simple_insight: Fear eases when the scene is understood correctly.
ramacharitamanas::550.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, Shiva’s strange wedding procession arrives and frightens the onlookers. Seeing the boys’ fear, the parents smile and reassure them. This verse is a small narrative bridge before the wedding welcome begins.
ramacharitamanas::550.modern_relevance: A child sees a masked performer at a festival and starts to cry. The parent leans down, names what is happening, and the fear melts. Understanding changes the whole feeling of the moment.
ramacharitamanas::550.insight: It shifts panic into calm by naming the situation clearly.

ramacharitamanas::551.verse_sanskrit: लै अगवान बरातहि आए। दिए सबहि जनवास सुहाए॥ मैनाँ सुभ आरती सँवारी। संग सुमंगल गावहिं नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::551.verse_hindi: अगवान लोग बारात को लिवा लाए, उन्होंने सबको सुंदर जनवासे ठहरने को दिए। मैना (पार्वतीजी की माता) ने शुभ आरती सजाई और उनके साथ की स्त्रियाँ उत्तम मंगलगीत गाने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::551.english_translation: The attendants brought the wedding party in and gave everyone pleasant lodging. Maina prepared a blessed aarti, and the women with her sang auspicious songs.
ramacharitamanas::551.translation_literal: लै (taking) / अगवान (the attendants) / बरातहि (the wedding party) / आए (came) / दिए (gave) / सबहि (to everyone) / जनवास (lodging) / सुहाए (pleasant) / मैनाँ (Maina) / सुभ (auspicious) / आरती (aarti) / सँवारी (prepared) / संग (with) / सुमंगल (auspicious) / गावहिं (sing) / नारी (women)
ramacharitamanas::551.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::551.essence: True welcome is shown in the care prepared before anyone asks.
ramacharitamanas::551.simple_meaning: The wedding party is welcomed properly, with lodging, aarti, and songs of blessing.
ramacharitamanas::551.simple_insight: Hospitality can turn a formal gathering into a sacred welcome.
ramacharitamanas::551.detailed_meaning: Shiva’s wedding party has arrived at Maina’s home. The hosts arrange comfortable lodging, and Maina prepares aarti while the women sing auspicious songs. The scene builds the joyful atmosphere before Shiva’s strange form is revealed.
ramacharitamanas::551.modern_relevance: The guests are arriving before dawn, shoes piled at the door, tea already warming on the stove. Someone has thought of everything, and the whole house feels ready to receive.
ramacharitamanas::551.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle of arrival to the care that makes welcome complete.

ramacharitamanas::552.verse_sanskrit: कंचन थार सोह बर पानी। परिछन चली हरहि हरषानी॥ बिकट बेष रुद्रहि जब देखा। अबलन्ह उर भय भयउ बिसेषा ॥
ramacharitamanas::552.verse_hindi: सुंदर हाथों में सोने का थाल शोभित है, इस प्रकार मैना हर्ष के साथ शिवजी का परछन करने चलीं। जब महादेवजी को भयानक वेष में देखा तब तो स्त्रियों के मन में बड़ा भारी भय उत्पन्न हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::552.english_translation: Mina, delighted, went to perform Shiva's ceremonial welcome with a golden tray. But when she saw Rudra in a fierce form, a great fear rose in the hearts of the women.
ramacharitamanas::552.translation_literal: कंचन (golden) / थार (tray) / सोह (shone) / बर (well) / पानी (water) / परिछन (ceremonial welcome) / चली (went) / हरहि (for Shiva) / हरषानी (delighted) / बिकट (fierce) / बेष (form) / रुद्रहि (Rudra/Shiva) / जब (when) / देखा (saw) / अबलन्ह (women) / उर (in heart) / भय (fear) / भयउ (became) / बिसेषा (great)
ramacharitamanas::552.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::552.essence: A joyful welcome can collapse into fear before the unexpected.
ramacharitamanas::552.simple_meaning: Mina goes joyfully to welcome Shiva, but his fierce appearance frightens the women.
ramacharitamanas::552.simple_insight: Even joy can turn to fear when expectation meets something overwhelming.
ramacharitamanas::552.detailed_meaning: At the wedding preparations in Kailash, Mina comes forward with a golden tray to honor Shiva. The celebration breaks into shock when his fierce appearance appears before the women. This moment shows the emotional clash between festive expectation and divine awe.
ramacharitamanas::552.modern_relevance: You walk into a room expecting a warm introduction, and the person you came to meet feels intimidating instead. The body reacts before the mind can catch up.
ramacharitamanas::552.insight: It shows how quickly the mind can shift from welcome to alarm when appearances unsettle it.

ramacharitamanas::553.verse_sanskrit: भागि भवन पैठीं अति त्रासा। गए महेसु जहाँ जनवासा॥ मैना हृदयँ भयउ दुखु भारी। लीन्ही बोली गिरीसकुमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::553.verse_hindi: बहुत ही डर के मारे भागकर वे घर में घुस गईं और शिवजी जहाँ जनवासा था, वहाँ चले गए। मैना के हृदय में बड़ा दुःख हुआ, उन्होंने पार्वतीजी को अपने पास बुला लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::553.english_translation: Overcome with fear, she ran inside the house. Mahesh went to the guest quarters. Deep sorrow filled Maina’s heart, and she called Parvati to her side.
ramacharitamanas::553.translation_literal: भागि (running) / भवन (house) / पैठीं (entered) / अति (very) / त्रासा (afraid) / गए (went) / महेसु (Mahesh/Shiva) / जहाँ (where) / जनवासा (guest quarters) / मैना (Maina) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / भयउ (became) / दुखु (sorrow) / भारी (heavy) / लीन्ही (took) / बोली (called) / गिरीसकुमारी (Parvati, daughter of the mountain)
ramacharitamanas::553.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::553.essence: Fear can break the welcome of a sacred moment.
ramacharitamanas::553.simple_meaning: Maina is frightened by Shiva’s fierce appearance, runs inside, and then calls Parvati to comfort her and explain the situation.
ramacharitamanas::553.simple_insight: Fear can make even a welcome meeting collapse into confusion.
ramacharitamanas::553.detailed_meaning: At Parvati’s marriage setting in Balkand, Shiva arrives in a terrifying form. Maina cannot bear the sight, runs into the house, and then, shaken and sorrowful, calls Parvati to her side. The moment turns from ceremony to family worry.
ramacharitamanas::553.modern_relevance: You open the door expecting a normal visit, then freeze because the person standing there feels overwhelming. Fear changes the whole room before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::553.insight: It shows how fear interrupts hospitality and pushes a person back into protective instinct.

ramacharitamanas::554.verse_sanskrit: अधिक सनेहँ गोद बैठारी। स्याम सरोज नयन भरे बारी॥ जेहिं बिधि तुम्हहि रूपु अस दीन्हा। तेहिं जड़ बरु बाउर कस कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::554.verse_hindi: और अत्यन्त स्नेह से गोद में बैठाकर अपने नीलकमल के समान नेत्रों में आँसू भरकर कहा- जिस विधाता ने तुमको ऐसा सुंदर रूप दिया, उस मूर्ख ने तुम्हारे दूल्हे को बावला कैसे बनाया? ॥
ramacharitamanas::554.english_translation: With deep affection she lifted her into her lap, tears filling her blue-lotus eyes. "The one who gave you such beauty—how did that fool make your bridegroom so bewildered?"
ramacharitamanas::554.translation_literal: अधिक (more) / सनेहँ (with affection) / गोद (lap) / बैठारी (having seated) / स्याम (dark-blue) / सरोज (lotus) / नयन (eyes) / भरे (filled) / बारी (tears) / जेहिं (by whom) / बिधि (fate-maker) / तुम्हहि (you) / रूपु (beauty/form) / अस (such) / दीन्हा (gave) / तेहिं (that one) / जड़ (foolish) / बरु (bridegroom) / बाउर (mad/bewildered) / कस (how) / कीन्हा (made)
ramacharitamanas::554.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::554.essence: Beauty here is so overwhelming it leaves the bridegroom dazed.
ramacharitamanas::554.simple_meaning: Parvati lovingly takes Sita into her lap, tears in her eyes, and marvels that the same maker who gave Sita such beauty has made her bridegroom so bewildered.
ramacharitamanas::554.simple_insight: Love can be tender and playful at once, even in the middle of sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::554.detailed_meaning: After Shiva's frightening form has startled Maina, Parvati draws Sita close with affection. In this small family moment, she looks at Sita's beauty and jokes in wonder that the one destined for her must be overwhelmed by it.
ramacharitamanas::554.modern_relevance: At a wedding, an elder pulls the bride close, tears shining, and says with a smile, "How did fate make such a beautiful match so lopsided?"
ramacharitamanas::554.insight: It shifts the scene from fear to affectionate wonder, showing how warmth can soften tension instantly.

ramacharitamanas::555.verse_sanskrit: कस कीन्ह बरु बौराह बिधि जेहिं तुम्हहि सुंदरता दई। जो फलु चहिअ सुरतरुहिं सो बरबस बबूरहिं लागई॥ तुम्ह सहित गिरि तें गिरौं पावक जरौं जलनिधि महुँ परौं। घरु जाउ अपजसु होउ जग जीवत बिबाहु न हौं करौं॥
ramacharitamanas::555.verse_hindi: जिस विधाता ने तुमको सुंदरता दी, उसने तुम्हारे लिए वर बावला कैसे बनाया? जो फल कल्पवृक्ष में लगना चाहिए, वह जबर्दस्ती बबूल में लग रहा है। मैं तुम्हें लेकर पहाड़ से गिर पड़ूँगी, आग में जल जाऊँगी या समुद्र में कूद पड़ूँगी। चाहे घर उजड़ जाए और संसार भर में अपकीर्ति फैल जाए, पर जीते जी मैं इस बावले वर से तुम्हारा विवाह न करूँगी।
ramacharitamanas::555.english_translation: How did the one who gave you beauty give you this mad husband? The fruit meant for a wish-fulfilling tree is being forced onto a thorny bush. I would rather fall from a mountain with you, burn in fire, or plunge into the sea than let this marriage happen while I live, even if the house is ruined and the world speaks ill of me.
ramacharitamanas::555.translation_literal: कस (how) / कीन्ह (made) / बरु (husband / boon) / बौराह (mad) / बिधि (the maker) / जेहिं (by whom) / तुम्हहि (you) / सुंदरता (beauty) / दई (gave) / जो (which) / फलु (fruit) / चहिअ (is desired) / सुरतरुहिं (to the wish-fulfilling tree) / सो (that) / बरबस (forcibly) / बबूरहिं (to the thorny bush) / लागई (is attached) / तुम्ह सहित (with you) / गिरि तें (from the mountain) / गिरौं (I may fall) / पावक (fire) / जरौं (I may burn) / जलनिधि महुँ (into the ocean) / परौं (I may fall) / घरु (house) / जाउ (let go / be ruined) / अपजसु (disgrace) / होउ (let it be) / जग (world) / जीवत (while living) / बिबाहु (marriage) / न हौं करौं (I will not do)
ramacharitamanas::555.speaker: Maina
ramacharitamanas::555.essence: Protective love can refuse the whole world to defend a child.
ramacharitamanas::555.simple_meaning: Maina is overwhelmed by grief and refuses to accept this marriage. She says the girl deserves a worthy match, not this foolish one, and she would rather face ruin than consent.
ramacharitamanas::555.simple_insight: Love can become fierce enough to reject even social pressure and shame.
ramacharitamanas::555.detailed_meaning: In Kailash's family scene, Maina sees her daughter being matched with a suitor she considers unworthy. Her affection turns into anguish and defiance, and she speaks as a mother who would risk everything rather than betray her child's dignity.
ramacharitamanas::555.modern_relevance: A parent sits through a marriage discussion, hearing polite praise for a match that feels wrong in the gut. The room wants agreement; the heart wants protection. Maina's refusal is that raw, protective instinct.
ramacharitamanas::555.insight: It shows how deep care can override fear of gossip, loss, or social approval.

ramacharitamanas::556.verse_sanskrit: भईं बिकल अबला सकल दुखित देखि गिरिनारि। करि बिलापु रोदति बदति सुता सनेहु सँभारि ॥।
ramacharitamanas::556.verse_hindi: हिमाचल की स्त्री (मैना) को दुःखी देखकर सारी स्त्रियाँ व्याकुल हो गईं। मैना अपनी कन्या के स्नेह को याद करके विलाप करती, रोती और कहती थीं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::556.english_translation: All the women were distressed to see the mountain lady in sorrow. Mena wept, lamented, and spoke, remembering her daughter's love.
ramacharitamanas::556.translation_literal: भईं (became) / बिकल (agitated) / अबला (women) / सकल (all) / दुखित (grieved) / देखि (seeing) / गिरिनारि (mountain-lady) / करि (doing) / बिलापु (lamentation) / रोदति (weeping) / बदति (speaks) / सुता (daughter) / सनेहु (love) / सँभारि (remembering)
ramacharitamanas::556.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::556.essence: A mother’s grief pulls everyone into the same wound.
ramacharitamanas::556.simple_meaning: All the women around Mena are shaken by her grief. Mena herself weeps and speaks while remembering her daughter's love.
ramacharitamanas::556.simple_insight: Shared sorrow spreads quickly, especially when a mother’s love is being torn apart.
ramacharitamanas::556.detailed_meaning: In the Himalaya’s home, Mena sees her daughter’s suffering and breaks down. The women around her are shaken too. This verse deepens the family grief before the complaint against Narada and the sorrow over Parvati’s fate.
ramacharitamanas::556.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and instantly feel the tension in a mother’s face, the silence in the women around her, the grief no one has named yet. Some pain enters everyone at once.
ramacharitamanas::556.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the emotional contagion of loss.

ramacharitamanas::557.verse_sanskrit: नारद कर मैं काह बिगारा। भवनु मोर जिन्ह बसत उजारा॥ अस उपदेसु उमहि जिन्ह दीन्हा। बौरे बरहि लागि तपु कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::557.verse_hindi: मैंने नारद का क्या बिगाड़ा था, जिन्होंने मेरा बसता हुआ घर उजाड़ दिया और जिन्होंने पार्वती को ऐसा उपदेश दिया कि जिससे उसने बावले वर के लिए तप किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::557.english_translation: What harm did I do to Narada, who ruined my settled home? He gave Uma such counsel that she performed austerity for a foolish bridegroom.
ramacharitamanas::557.translation_literal: नारद (Narada) / कर (of) / मैं (I) / काह (what) / बिगारा (harmed) / भवनु (home) / मोर (my) / जिन्ह (who) / बसत (dwelling) / उजारा (destroyed)॥ / अस (such) / उपदेसु (counsel) / उमहि (to Uma) / जिन्ह (who) / दीन्हा (gave) / बौरे (foolish) / बरहि (bridegroom) / लागि (for) / तपु (austerity) / कीन्हा (performed)॥
ramacharitamanas::557.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::557.essence: A careless counsel can reorder an entire life.
ramacharitamanas::557.simple_meaning: Parvati complains that Narada disturbed her peaceful home by advising Uma to do austerity for an unusual bridegroom.
ramacharitamanas::557.simple_insight: Not every piece of advice brings peace. Some counsel creates longing, disruption, and a life that can never return to ordinary comfort.
ramacharitamanas::557.detailed_meaning: In Shiva's telling to Parvati, the story turns to Narada's visit and the chain of events it set off. Parvati laments that his counsel upset her household and led Uma into severe austerity for an unlikely bridegroom.
ramacharitamanas::557.modern_relevance: A friend sends one message, meant as a clever suggestion, and suddenly a relationship, a plan, or a family mood changes shape overnight.
ramacharitamanas::557.insight: It warns you to measure advice by its consequences, not by how clever it sounds.

ramacharitamanas::558.verse_sanskrit: साचेहुँ उन्ह कें मोह न माया। उदासीन धनु धामु न जाया॥ पर घर घालक लाज न भीरा। बाँझ कि जान प्रसव कै पीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::558.verse_hindi: सचमुच उनके न किसी का मोह है, न माया, न उनके धन है, न घर है और न स्त्री ही है, वे सबसे उदासीन हैं। इसी से वे दूसरे का घर उजाड़ने वाले हैं। उन्हें न किसी की लाज है, न डर है। भला, बाँझ स्त्री प्रसव की पीड़ा को क्या जाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::558.english_translation: Truly, they have no attachment, no illusion, no wealth, no home, and no wife; they are utterly indifferent. That is why they are destroyers of another's home. They have no shame and no fear. How can a barren woman know the pain of childbirth?
ramacharitamanas::558.translation_literal: साचहुँ (truly) / उन्ह कें (for them) / मोह (attachment) / न (not) / माया (illusion) / उदासीन (indifferent) / धनु (wealth) / धामु (home) / न जाया (not wife) / पर घर (another's home) / घालक (destroyer) / लाज (shame) / न भीरा (no fear) / बाँझ (barren woman) / कि (how) / जान (know) / प्रसव (childbirth) / कै (of) / पीरा (pain)
ramacharitamanas::558.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::558.essence: Grief turns private pain into a fierce accusation.
ramacharitamanas::558.simple_meaning: Parvati is blaming the beings who ruined her home, saying they are detached, shameless, and unable to understand a mother's suffering.
ramacharitamanas::558.simple_insight: Pain makes judgment fierce. Grief often speaks by turning suffering into accusation.
ramacharitamanas::558.detailed_meaning: Parvati has just heard that Narad's counsel helped bring ruin into her household. In her grief, she lashes out at those she sees as responsible, calling them detached, shameless, and blind to a mother's pain. This is part of a larger emotional complaint, not a complete teaching.
ramacharitamanas::558.modern_relevance: A parent watches a family fracture after one careless remark and says, 'You don't know what this cost.' Grief turns into sharp moral language before calm returns.
ramacharitamanas::558.insight: It shows how wounded love can judge others through the lens of its own loss.

ramacharitamanas::559.verse_sanskrit: जननिहि बिकल बिलोकि भवानी। बोली जुत बिबेक मृदु बानी॥ अस बिचारि सोचहि मति माता। सो न टरइ जो रचइ बिधाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::559.verse_hindi: माता को विकल देखकर पार्वतीजी विवेकयुक्त कोमल वाणी बोलीं- हे माता! जो विधाता रच देते हैं, वह टलता नहीं, ऐसा विचार कर तुम सोच मत करो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::559.english_translation: Seeing her mother distressed, Bhavani spoke with gentle, discerning words: "Mother, do not grieve. What the Creator has written does not turn aside."
ramacharitamanas::559.translation_literal: जननिहि (the mother) / बिकल (distressed) / बिलोकि (seeing) / भवानी (Bhavani) / बोली (spoke) / जुत (with) / बिबेक (discernment) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (speech) / अस (thus) / बिचारि (considering) / सोचहि (grieve) / मति (mind) / माता (mother) / सो (that) / न टरइ (does not turn away) / जो (which) / रचइ (creates) / बिधाता (the Creator)
ramacharitamanas::559.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::559.essence: Peace begins when you stop resisting what cannot be changed.
ramacharitamanas::559.simple_meaning: Parvati gently tells her mother not to grieve, because what is ordained cannot be avoided.
ramacharitamanas::559.simple_insight: Some pain eases when you stop fighting what cannot be changed.
ramacharitamanas::559.detailed_meaning: Parvati sees her mother upset and answers with calm, thoughtful words. She is not arguing; she is softening resistance. In this family moment, she teaches that what the Creator has set in motion will not be undone by worry.
ramacharitamanas::559.modern_relevance: You stare at a message you cannot take back, then pace the room replaying every line. Parvati’s answer is the pause that ends the spiral: some things cannot be rewritten by panic.
ramacharitamanas::559.insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to calm acceptance of what cannot be altered.

ramacharitamanas::560.verse_sanskrit: करम लिखा जौं बाउर नाहू। तौ कत दोसु लगाइअ काहू॥ तुम्ह सन मिटहिं कि बिधि के अंका। मातु ब्यर्थ जनि लेहु कलंका ॥
ramacharitamanas::560.verse_hindi: जो मेरे भाग्य में बावला ही पति लिखा है, तो किसी को क्यों दोष लगाया जाए? हे माता! क्या विधाता के अंक तुमसे मिट सकते हैं? वृथा कलंक का टीका मत लो ॥
ramacharitamanas::560.english_translation: If a foolish husband was written into my fate, why blame anyone? Mother, can the marks of the creator be erased? Do not take this useless stain upon yourself.
ramacharitamanas::560.translation_literal: करम (fate / action written) / लिखा (written) / जौं (if) / बाउर (foolish) / नाहू (husband) / तौ (then) / कत (why) / दोसु (blame) / लगाइअ (should be placed) / काहू (on anyone) ॥ तुम्ह (your) / सन (with) / मिटहिं (can be erased) / कि (can?) / बिधि (creator) / के (of) / अंका (marks) ॥ मातु (mother) / ब्यर्थ (useless) / जनि (do not) / लेहु (take) / कलंका (stain / shame) ॥
ramacharitamanas::560.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::560.essence: What cannot be changed should not be blamed.
ramacharitamanas::560.simple_meaning: Parvati tells her mother not to blame anyone for her marriage, because what has been written by fate cannot be changed.
ramacharitamanas::560.simple_insight: There is relief in stopping the search for someone to blame.
ramacharitamanas::560.detailed_meaning: Parvati sees her mother distressed and answers gently. She says her husband is what fate has written for her, so no one should be blamed. The moment turns grief into acceptance and protects her mother from needless shame.
ramacharitamanas::560.modern_relevance: You replay the breakup, the job loss, the diagnosis, hunting for the one person to blame. Then someone wiser says: stop. Some things are already written into the shape of your life.
ramacharitamanas::560.insight: It shifts the mind from blame to acceptance, so energy stops leaking into regret and shame.

ramacharitamanas::561.verse_sanskrit: जनि लेहु मातु कलंकु करुना परिहरहु अवसर नहीं। दुखु सुखु जो लिखा लिलार हमरें जाब जहँ पाउब तहीं॥ सुनि उमा बचन बिनीत कोमल सकल अबला सोचहीं। बहु भाँति बिधिहि लगाइ दूषन नयन बारि बिमोचहीं॥
ramacharitamanas::561.verse_hindi: हे माता! कलंक मत लो, रोना छोड़ो, यह अवसर विषाद करने का नहीं है। मेरे भाग्य में जो दुःख-सुख लिखा है, उसे मैं जहाँ जाऊँगी, वहीं पाऊँगी! पार्वतीजी के ऐसे विनय भरे कोमल वचन सुनकर सारी स्त्रियाँ सोच करने लगीं और भाँति-भाँति से विधाता को दोष देकर आँखों से आँसू बहाने लगीं।
ramacharitamanas::561.english_translation: Do not take this as disgrace, Mother. Let go of grief; this is no time for sorrow. The joy and sorrow written on my brow will meet me wherever I go. Hearing Uma's gentle, humble words, all the women reflected, blamed fate in many ways, and shed tears.
ramacharitamanas::561.translation_literal: जनि (do not) / लेहु (take) / मातु (Mother) / कलंकु (disgrace) / करुना (compassion / grief) / परिहरहु (give up) / अवसर (occasion / time) / नहीं (not) / दुखु (sorrow) / सुखु (joy) / जो (which) / लिखा (written) / लिलार (on the forehead) / हमरें (for me) / जाब (will go) / जहँ (where) / पाउब (will find) / तहीं (there) / सुनि (hearing) / उमा (Uma) / बचन (words) / बिनीत (humble) / कोमल (gentle) / सकल (all) / अबला (women) / सोचहीं (reflect) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / बिधिहि (fate) / लगाइ (placing) / दूषन (blame) / नयन (eyes) / बारि (water / tears) / बिमोचहीं (release)
ramacharitamanas::561.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::561.essence: Some grief must be faced, not fought.
ramacharitamanas::561.simple_meaning: Parvati tells her mother not to feel ashamed or keep grieving. She says whatever joy or sorrow is written for her will find her wherever she goes, and the women around her begin to weep and blame fate.
ramacharitamanas::561.simple_insight: There is calm in accepting what cannot be changed, even when the heart still aches.
ramacharitamanas::561.detailed_meaning: In the Shiva-Parvati frame of Balkand, Parvati speaks gently to her mother after distressing news about her marriage and fate. Her words carry quiet acceptance: what has been written cannot be escaped. The women listening are moved into grief and reflection.
ramacharitamanas::561.modern_relevance: A family group chat has just turned into a flood of blame after bad news. One person stops the spiral and says, with quiet steadiness, that some things cannot be undone and must be faced as they are.
ramacharitamanas::561.insight: It shifts the mind from protest to acceptance, so pain is met without extra shame or resistance.

ramacharitamanas::562.verse_sanskrit: तेहि अवसर नारद सहित अरु रिषि सप्त समेत। समाचार सुनि तुहिनगिरि गवने तुरत निकेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::562.verse_hindi: इस समाचार को सुनते ही हिमाचल उसी समय नारदजी और सप्त ऋषियों को साथ लेकर अपने घर गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::562.english_translation: At that moment, Narada and the seven sages came along, and after hearing the news, Himavan immediately returned home.
ramacharitamanas::562.translation_literal: तेहि अवसर (at that moment) / नारद (Narada) / सहित (together with) / अरु (and) / रिषि (sages) / सप्त (seven) / समेत (along with) / समाचार (news) / सुनि (having heard) / तुहिनगिरि (Himavan) / गवने (went) / तुरत (immediately) / निकेत (home)
ramacharitamanas::562.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::562.essence: News arrives, and the whole household turns toward what it means.
ramacharitamanas::562.simple_meaning: Narada and the seven sages arrived, and Himavan hurried home after hearing the news.
ramacharitamanas::562.simple_insight: Some moments are so important that everyone present moves at once.
ramacharitamanas::562.detailed_meaning: After Parvati accepts her fate, the scene shifts. Narada arrives with the seven sages, and Himavan rushes home with the news, setting up the next revelation about Parvati's true identity.
ramacharitamanas::562.modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent, then one message lands and everyone starts moving at once. Some news changes the whole room before anyone has time to think.
ramacharitamanas::562.insight: It keeps the narrative moving from private grief to public revelation.

ramacharitamanas::563.verse_sanskrit: तब नारद सबही समुझावा। पूरुब कथा प्रसंगु सुनावा॥ मयना सत्य सुनहु मम बानी। जगदंबा तव सुता भवानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::563.verse_hindi: तब नारदजी ने पूर्वजन्म की कथा सुनाकर सबको समझाया (और कहा) कि हे मैना! तुम मेरी सच्ची बात सुनो, तुम्हारी यह लड़की साक्षात जगज्जनी भवानी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::563.english_translation: Then Narad explained everything to all. He told the story of the past birth. "Mena, hear my true words: your daughter is the world-mother, Bhavani."
ramacharitamanas::563.translation_literal: तब (then) / नारद (Narad) / सबही (everyone) / समुझावा (explained) / पूरुब (past) / कथा (story) / प्रसंगु (episode) / सुनावा (told) / मयना (Mena) / सत्य (true) / सुनहु (listen) / मम (my) / बानी (words) / जगदंबा (world-mother) / तव (your) / सुता (daughter) / भवानी (Bhavani)
ramacharitamanas::563.speaker: Narad
ramacharitamanas::563.essence: A wise voice reveals the divine identity hidden inside an ordinary birth.
ramacharitamanas::563.simple_meaning: Narad explains the hidden identity of Mena's daughter by recounting her past birth and calling her the world-mother Bhavani.
ramacharitamanas::563.simple_insight: What looks like an ordinary daughter is carrying a far greater presence than anyone can see.
ramacharitamanas::563.detailed_meaning: Narad has arrived after the troubling news, and he now calms the gathering by revealing Sita's true identity to Mena. This is not the full revelation yet, but the opening explanation that prepares everyone for the deeper truth about her divine nature.
ramacharitamanas::563.modern_relevance: A family hears difficult news about a daughter’s future, and one wise voice reframes the whole moment: what seems fragile is actually sacred and immense.
ramacharitamanas::563.insight: It shifts attention from surface appearance to hidden identity and meaning.

ramacharitamanas::564.verse_sanskrit: अजा अनादि सक्ति अबिनासिनि। सदा संभु अरधंग निवासिनि॥ जग संभव पालन लय कारिनि। निज इच्छा लीला बपु धारिनि ॥
ramacharitamanas::564.verse_hindi: ये अजन्मा, अनादि और अविनाशिनी शक्ति हैं। सदा शिवजी के अर्द्धांग में रहती हैं। ये जगत की उत्पत्ति, पालन और संहार करने वाली हैं और अपनी इच्छा से ही लीला शरीर धारण करती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::564.english_translation: She is birthless, beginningless, and imperishable power. She always dwells as Shiva's half. She brings forth, sustains, and dissolves the world, and takes a form of her own will for divine play.
ramacharitamanas::564.translation_literal: अजा (birthless) / अनादि (beginningless) / सक्ति (power) / अबिनासिनि (imperishable) / सदा (always) / संभु (Shiva) / अरधंग (half-body) / निवासिनि (dwelling) / जग (world) / संभव (creation) / पालन (sustenance) / लय (dissolution) / कारिनि (doer) / निज (own) / इच्छा (will) / लीला (divine play) / बपु (form/body) / धारिनि (one who takes)
ramacharitamanas::564.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::564.essence: She is eternal power, not a passing figure in the tale.
ramacharitamanas::564.simple_meaning: Parvati is described as the eternal power behind creation, preservation, and dissolution. She is not born or destroyed, and she takes form by her own will.
ramacharitamanas::564.simple_insight: The divine feminine is shown as timeless power, not a temporary character in a story.
ramacharitamanas::564.detailed_meaning: Narad has just explained Parvati's previous birth to Menaka and the others. Now the narration lifts beyond biography: it identifies Parvati as the eternal power who stays with Shiva, governs creation and dissolution, and appears in form by her own will.
ramacharitamanas::564.modern_relevance: A person may look like only a role, a body, or a name on paper. But some presences in life feel larger than biography — steady, formative, and impossible to reduce to one incident.
ramacharitamanas::564.insight: It shifts attention from Parvati's story to her cosmic nature as the power behind all change.

ramacharitamanas::565.verse_sanskrit: जनमीं प्रथम दच्छ गृह जाई। नामु सती सुंदर तनु पाई॥ तहँहुँ सती संकरहि बिबाहीं। कथा प्रसिद्ध सकल जग माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::565.verse_hindi: पहले ये दक्ष के घर जाकर जन्मी थीं, तब इनका सती नाम था, बहुत सुंदर शरीर पाया था। वहाँ भी सती शंकरजी से ही ब्याही गई थीं। यह कथा सारे जगत में प्रसिद्ध है ॥
ramacharitamanas::565.english_translation: She was first born in Daksha's house, where she received the name Sati and a beautiful body. There too, Sati was married to Shiva. This story is famous throughout the world.
ramacharitamanas::565.translation_literal: जनमीं (was born) / प्रथम (first) / दच्छ गृह (in Daksha's house) / जाई (having gone) / नामु (name) / सती (Sati) / सुंदर तनु (beautiful body) / पाई (having obtained)॥ / तहँहुँ (there also) / सती (Sati) / संकरहि (to Shiva) / बिबाहीं (was married) / कथा (story) / प्रसिद्ध (famous) / सकल जग (throughout the whole world) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::565.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::565.essence: Sati's former life is recalled to prepare for a deeper revelation.
ramacharitamanas::565.simple_meaning: Sati was first born in Daksha's house, married Shiva, and became well known across the world.
ramacharitamanas::565.simple_insight: Some stories carry their own authority because they are remembered everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::565.detailed_meaning: Narad is explaining Parvati's previous birth to clear the mystery of her identity. He first reminds the listeners that she once appeared as Sati, Daksha's daughter, and was already married to Shiva. This prepares the way for the deeper revelation that follows.
ramacharitamanas::565.modern_relevance: A family keeps repeating a story everyone already knows, because the real point is not the facts — it is what those facts are about to reveal.
ramacharitamanas::565.insight: It sets up the identity of the speaker's former life before the deeper divine recognition begins.

ramacharitamanas::566.verse_sanskrit: एक बार आवत सिव संगा। देखेउ रघुकुल कमल पतंगा॥ भयउ मोहु सिव कहा न कीन्हा। भ्रम बस बेषु सीय कर लीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::566.verse_hindi: एक बार इन्होंने शिवजी के साथ आते हुए (राह में) रघुकुल रूपी कमल के सूर्य श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखा, तब इन्हें मोह हो गया और इन्होंने शिवजी का कहना न मानकर भ्रमवश सीताजी का वेष धारण कर लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::566.english_translation: Once, while coming with Shiva, she saw Ram, the sun of the Raghu line, and became deluded. Ignoring Shiva's words, she took on Sita's form under the spell of confusion.
ramacharitamanas::566.translation_literal: एक बार (once) / आवत (coming) / सिव संगा (with Shiva) / देखेउ (saw) / रघुकुल कमल पतंगा (the sun of the Raghu-line lotus) / भयउ (became) / मोहु (delusion) / सिव (Shiva) / कहा (said) / न कीन्हा (did not do) / भ्रम बस (under the spell of confusion) / बेषु (form/disguise) / सीय कर (of Sita) / लीन्हा (took)
ramacharitamanas::566.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::566.essence: Delusion makes imitation feel like devotion.
ramacharitamanas::566.simple_meaning: Sati saw Ram and became confused. She ignored Shiva's warning and took Sita's form.
ramacharitamanas::566.simple_insight: Delusion can make even a sacred choice become a mistake.
ramacharitamanas::566.detailed_meaning: Shiva and Sati are moving together when Sati sees Ram, the radiant lord of the Raghu line. Struck by fascination and not listening to Shiva, she assumes Sita's form. This moment sets up the reason Shiva later turns away from her.
ramacharitamanas::566.modern_relevance: You see someone admired by everyone and instantly want to become like them. In that rush, you copy the surface and miss the deeper truth.
ramacharitamanas::566.insight: It shows how attraction without clear seeing leads to imitation instead of understanding.

ramacharitamanas::567.verse_sanskrit: सिय बेषु सतीं जो कीन्ह तेहिं अपराध संकर परिहरीं। हर बिरहँ जाइ बहोरि पितु कें जग्य जोगानल जरीं॥ अब जनमि तुम्हरे भवन निज पति लागि दारुन तपु किया। अस जानि संसय तजहु गिरिजा सर्बदा संकरप्रिया॥
ramacharitamanas::567.verse_hindi: सतीजी ने जो सीता का वेष धारण किया, उसी अपराध के कारण शंकरजी ने उनको त्याग दिया। फिर शिवजी के वियोग में ये अपने पिता के यज्ञ में जाकर वहीं योगाग्नि से भस्म हो गईं। अब इन्होंने तुम्हारे घर जन्म लेकर अपने पति के लिए कठिन तप किया है ऐसा जानकर संदेह छोड़ दो, पार्वतीजी तो सदा ही शिवजी की प्रिया (अर्द्धांगिनी) हैं।
ramacharitamanas::567.english_translation: Because Sati once took on Sita's form, Shiva left her for that offense. In separation from Shiva, she later went to her father's sacrifice and burned herself in the fire of yoga. Now she has been born in your house and has done severe austerity for her husband. Knowing this, cast away doubt, Girija is always dear to Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::567.translation_literal: सिय बेषु (Sita's form) / सतीं (Sati) / जो कीन्ह (who took) / तेहिं अपराध (that offense) / संकर (Shiva) / परिहरीं (left) / हर बिरहँ (in separation from Shiva) / जाइ (going) / बहोरि (again) / पितु कें जग्य (to the father's sacrifice) / जोगानल (fire of yoga) / जरीं (burned) / अब (now) / जनमि (having been born) / तुम्हरे भवन (in your house) / निज पति लागि (for her own husband) / दारुन तपु (severe austerity) / किया (did) / अस जानि (knowing this) / संसय (doubt) / तजहु (give up) / गिरिजा (Girija) / सर्बदा (always) / संकरप्रिया (dear to Shiva)
ramacharitamanas::567.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::567.essence: Trust the bond that has already endured loss and return.
ramacharitamanas::567.simple_meaning: Parvati should not doubt Shiva's love. Sati's past, her suffering, and her present birth as Parvati all prove that she is always dear to Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::567.simple_insight: Love that survives death and rebirth asks for trust, not suspicion.
ramacharitamanas::567.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the opening frame of the story. He recalls Sati's old mistake, her death in her father's sacrifice, and her rebirth as Parvati, who has now done severe penance for Shiva. The point is to remove Parvati's doubt and confirm her place beside him.
ramacharitamanas::567.modern_relevance: You replay an old misunderstanding in your mind while the other person keeps showing up with care. The mind wants proof; the heart needs trust. This verse asks you to stop feeding suspicion.
ramacharitamanas::567.insight: It shifts the mind from suspicion to confidence in a bond that has already been tested.

ramacharitamanas::568.verse_sanskrit: सुनि नारद के बचन तब सब कर मिटा बिषाद। छन महुँ ब्यापेउ सकल पुर घर घर यह संबाद ॥
ramacharitamanas::568.verse_hindi: तब नारद के वचन सुनकर सबका विषाद मिट गया और क्षणभर में यह समाचार सारे नगर में घर-घर फैल गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::568.english_translation: Hearing Narad's words, everyone's sorrow vanished. In a moment, the news spread through the whole city, house to house.
ramacharitamanas::568.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / नारद (Narad's) / के (of) / बचन (words) / तब (then) / सब (all) / कर (of) / मिटा (vanished) / बिषाद (sorrow) / छन महुँ (in a moment) / ब्यापेउ (spread) / सकल (entire) / पुर (city) / घर घर (house to house) / यह (this) / संबाद (news)
ramacharitamanas::568.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::568.essence: One true message can dissolve collective sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::568.simple_meaning: Narad's words remove everyone's sadness, and the good news quickly spreads through the whole city.
ramacharitamanas::568.simple_insight: Hope can travel faster than fear when the right words arrive.
ramacharitamanas::568.detailed_meaning: Narad has just spoken, and the tension in the city breaks. The sorrow lifts at once, and the news races from house to house, preparing everyone for the joy that follows.
ramacharitamanas::568.modern_relevance: A tense family group chat suddenly goes quiet after one reassuring message. One clear sentence can dissolve hours of dread and spread relief instantly.
ramacharitamanas::568.insight: It shows how truthful reassurance can calm a whole community at once.

ramacharitamanas::569.verse_sanskrit: तब मयना हिमवंतु अनंदे। पुनि पुनि पारबती पद बंदे॥ नारि पुरुष सिसु जुबा सयाने। नगर लोग सब अति हरषाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::569.verse_hindi: तब मैना और हिमवान आनंद में मग्न हो गए और उन्होंने बार-बार पार्वती के चरणों की वंदना की। स्त्री, पुरुष, बालक, युवा और वृद्ध नगर के सभी लोग बहुत प्रसन्न हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::569.english_translation: Then Maina and Himavan overflowed with joy and repeatedly bowed at Parvati's feet. Men, women, children, youths, and elders—all the people of the city were deeply delighted.
ramacharitamanas::569.translation_literal: तब (then) / मयना (Maina) / हिमवंतु (Himavan) / अनंदे (rejoiced) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / पारबती (Parvati) / पद (feet) / बंदे (bowed) / नारि (women) / पुरुष (men) / सिसु (children) / जुबा (youths) / सयाने (elders) / नगर लोग (city people) / सब (all) / अति (very) / हरषाने (delighted)
ramacharitamanas::569.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::569.essence: Joy becomes complete when an entire community shares it.
ramacharitamanas::569.simple_meaning: Maina, Himavan, and everyone in the city felt great joy and honored Parvati with repeated bows.
ramacharitamanas::569.simple_insight: Joy deepens when gratitude is shared openly, not kept private.
ramacharitamanas::569.detailed_meaning: After Narad's words remove the earlier sorrow, Maina and Himavan rejoice at Parvati's role in the unfolding blessing. Their happiness spreads through the city, and everyone joins in celebration before the wedding preparations begin.
ramacharitamanas::569.modern_relevance: The message lands when a family gets good news after days of tension, and relief turns into shared celebration. One person's blessing can lift an entire home.
ramacharitamanas::569.insight: It shifts attention from private relief to communal gratitude and celebration.

ramacharitamanas::570.verse_sanskrit: लगे होन पुर मंगल गाना। सजे सबहिं हाटक घट नाना॥ भाँति अनेक भई जेवनारा। सूपसास्त्र जस कछु ब्यवहारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::570.verse_hindi: नगर में मंगल गीत गाए जाने लगे और सबने भाँति-भाँति के सुवर्ण के कलश सजाए। पाक शास्त्र में जैसी रीति है, उसके अनुसार अनेक भाँति की ज्योनार हुई (रसोई बनी) ॥
ramacharitamanas::570.english_translation: The city began singing auspicious songs, and many golden vessels were arranged. In many different ways, the feast was prepared according to the rules of cooking.
ramacharitamanas::570.translation_literal: लगे (began) / होन (to happen) / पुर (city) / मंगल (auspicious) / गाना (singing) / सजे (were arranged) / सबहिं (all) / हाटक (golden) / घट (pots/vessels) / नाना (various) / भाँति (ways) / अनेक (many) / भई (was made) / जेवनारा (feast/meal) / सूपसास्त्र (cookery rules) / जस (as) / कछु (some) / ब्यवहारा (custom/procedure)
ramacharitamanas::570.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::570.essence: A sacred arrival turns the whole city into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::570.simple_meaning: The whole city celebrates with songs, gold vessels, and a grand feast prepared in proper order.
ramacharitamanas::570.simple_insight: Joy becomes visible when a home prepares to welcome something sacred.
ramacharitamanas::570.detailed_meaning: At Himavan’s house, the news has spread and the mood has turned festive. The city fills with auspicious songs, golden vessels are set out, and a proper feast is prepared for the arriving wedding party. This verse is part of the celebration, not the teaching.
ramacharitamanas::570.modern_relevance: The kitchen is crowded, the lights are up, and relatives keep arriving with trays and flowers. Everyone is busy because something precious is about to be welcomed.
ramacharitamanas::570.insight: It shifts attention from private emotion to shared preparation and collective joy.

ramacharitamanas::571.verse_sanskrit: सो जेवनार कि जाइ बखानी। बसहिं भवन जेहिं मातु भवानी॥ सादर बोले सकल बराती। बिष्नु बिरंचि देव सब जाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::571.verse_hindi: जिस घर में स्वयं माता भवानी रहती हों, वहाँ की ज्योनार (भोजन सामग्री) का वर्णन कैसे किया जा सकता है? हिमाचल ने आदरपूर्वक सब बारातियों, विष्णु, ब्रह्मा और सब जाति के देवताओं को बुलवाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::571.english_translation: How can the feast be described, where Mother Bhavani herself dwells? With reverence, Himachal invited all the wedding guests, Vishnu, Brahma, and all classes of deities.
ramacharitamanas::571.translation_literal: सो (that) / जेवनार (feast) / कि (how) / जाइ (can be told) / बखानी (described) / बसहिं (dwells) / भवन (house) / जेहिं (in which) / मातु (mother) / भवानी (Bhavani) / सादर (with respect) / बोले (called) / सकल (all) / बराती (wedding guests) / बिष्नु (Vishnu) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / देव (deities) / सब (all) / जाती (classes)
ramacharitamanas::571.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::571.essence: Presence makes ordinary hospitality feel beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::571.simple_meaning: The wedding feast is beyond description because Bhavani herself lives there. Himachal respectfully invites all the guests, including Vishnu, Brahma, and every class of divine beings.
ramacharitamanas::571.simple_insight: Some moments feel too full for ordinary words. Reverence turns even a feast into something sacred.
ramacharitamanas::571.detailed_meaning: At Himachal's home, the wedding preparations for Parvati are complete. The joy is so great that the poet says the feast itself cannot be fully described, because Bhavani is present there. Even Vishnu, Brahma, and all the heavenly guests are invited with honor.
ramacharitamanas::571.modern_relevance: A home fills with guests, the kitchen runs hot, and everyone keeps smiling because one beloved person has arrived. The whole gathering feels larger than the food on the table.
ramacharitamanas::571.insight: It shifts attention from the meal itself to the sanctity of the gathering and the honor shown to each guest.

ramacharitamanas::572.verse_sanskrit: बिबिधि पाँति बैठी जेवनारा। लागे परुसन निपुन सुआरा॥ नारिबृंद सुर जेवँत जानी। लगीं देन गारीं मृदु बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::572.verse_hindi: भोजन (करने वालों) की बहुत सी पंगतें बैठीं। चतुर रसोइए परोसने लगे। स्त्रियों की मंडलियाँ देवताओं को भोजन करते जानकर कोमल वाणी से गालियाँ देने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::572.english_translation: Many rows of diners were seated. Skilled cooks began serving them. The women, seeing the gods eating, began offering playful teasing in gentle words.
ramacharitamanas::572.translation_literal: बिबिधि (various) / पाँति (rows, lines) / बैठी (seated) / जेवनारा (diners, meal) / लागे (began) / परुसन (to serve, to dish out) / निपुन (skilled, expert) / सुआरा (cooks) / नारिबृंद (groups of women) / सुर (devas, radiant beings) / जेवँत (eating) / जानी (having known) / लगीं (began) / देन (to give) / गारीं (teasing reproaches, jibes) / मृदु (soft, gentle) / बानी (speech, words)
ramacharitamanas::572.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::572.essence: Celebration turns even teasing into sweetness.
ramacharitamanas::572.simple_meaning: Guests sat in many rows while expert cooks served the food. The women, seeing the divine guests eating, began teasing them with gentle, playful words.
ramacharitamanas::572.simple_insight: Joy can be so full that even teasing becomes part of the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::572.detailed_meaning: In Himachal's grand feast for Shiva and the wedding guests, the meal is underway. Rows of diners are seated, cooks move quickly, and the women watch the radiant guests eat with delighted, playful mockery. The verse adds color and movement to the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::572.modern_relevance: At a wedding buffet, the aunties see the groom's side eating too slowly and start smiling, teasing, and laughing across the hall. The food is good, but the shared delight is what fills the room.
ramacharitamanas::572.insight: It shifts attention from the meal itself to the social warmth surrounding it.

ramacharitamanas::573.verse_sanskrit: गारीं मधुर स्वर देहिं सुंदरि बिंग्य बचन सुनावहीं। भोजनु करहिं सुर अति बिलंबु बिनोदु सुनि सचु पावहीं॥ जेवँत जो बढ्यो अनंदु सो मुख कोटिहूँ न परै कह्यो। अचवाँइ दीन्हें पान गवने बास जहँ जाको रह्यो॥
ramacharitamanas::573.verse_hindi: सब सुंदरी स्त्रियाँ मीठे स्वर में गालियाँ देने लगीं और व्यंग्य भरे वचन सुनाने लगीं। देवगण विनोद सुनकर बहुत सुख अनुभव करते हैं, इसलिए भोजन करने में बड़ी देर लगा रहे हैं। भोजन के समय जो आनंद बढ़ा वह करोड़ों मुँह से भी नहीं कहा जा सकता। (भोजन कर चुकने पर) सबके हाथ-मुँह धुलवाकर पान दिए गए। फिर सब लोग, जो जहाँ ठहरे थे, वहाँ चले गए।
ramacharitamanas::573.english_translation: The beautiful women spoke sweetly, offering teasing jests. The gods ate with delight and took their time, because the feast was so enjoyable. The joy of the meal cannot be told even with millions of mouths. After water for washing and betel leaves were given, everyone returned to their own lodging.
ramacharitamanas::573.translation_literal: गारीं (teasing words) / मधुर स्वर (sweet voice) / देहिं (give) / सुंदरि (beautiful women) / बिंग्य बचन (sarcastic words) / सुनावहीं (make heard) / भोजनु (meal) / करहिं (do) / सुर (deities) / अति (very) / बिलंबु (delay) / बिनोदु (playful delight) / सुनि (hearing) / सचु (true joy) / पावहीं (receive) / जेवँत (while eating) / जो (which) / बढ्यो (grew) / अनंदु (joy) / सो (that) / मुख (mouth) / कोटिहूँ (even millions) / न (not) / परै (falls) / कह्यो (spoken) / अचवाँइ (water for rinsing) / दीन्हें (having given) / पान (betel leaves) / गवने (went away) / बास (dwelling) / जहँ (where) / जाको (each one's) / रह्यो (remained)
ramacharitamanas::573.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::573.essence: True hospitality makes even delay feel like delight.
ramacharitamanas::573.simple_meaning: The feast is so joyful and playful that even the guests linger over it. After the meal, everyone is properly attended to and sent back to their places.
ramacharitamanas::573.simple_insight: Joy can be shared without hurry; good hospitality leaves people full, relaxed, and content.
ramacharitamanas::573.detailed_meaning: In Himavan's house, the wedding feast for the gods is in full swing. The women joke, the guests laugh, and the meal stretches on in delighted delay. This verse lingers on the overflowing celebration before the guests return to their rest.
ramacharitamanas::573.modern_relevance: At a wedding table where everyone keeps talking long after the food is finished, the room itself becomes the memory. No one wants to leave because the welcome felt complete.
ramacharitamanas::573.insight: It turns attention from the food itself to the atmosphere of generous celebration and care.

ramacharitamanas::574.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि मुनिन्ह हिमवंत कहुँ लगन सुनाई आइ। समय बिलोकि बिबाह कर पठए देव बोलाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::574.verse_hindi: फिर मुनियों ने लौटकर हिमवान् को लगन (लग्न पत्रिका) सुनाई और विवाह का समय देखकर देवताओं को बुला भेजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::574.english_translation: Then the sages returned and informed Himavan about the wedding date. Seeing the proper time, they sent for the deities.
ramacharitamanas::574.translation_literal: बहुरि (again) / मुनिन्ह (the sages) / हिमवंत कहुँ (to Himavan) / लगन (wedding date) / सुनाई (informed) / आइ (coming) / समय (time) / बिलोकि (having seen) / बिबाह (marriage) / कर (for doing) / पठए (sent) / देव (the deities) / बोलाइ (calling)
ramacharitamanas::574.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::574.essence: The wedding is now formally set in motion.
ramacharitamanas::574.simple_meaning: The sages returned to Himavan, told him the wedding date, and arranged for the deities to be invited at the right time.
ramacharitamanas::574.simple_insight: Some moments are about timing and preparation, not revelation.
ramacharitamanas::574.detailed_meaning: The marriage arrangements for Sita and Ram are moving forward. The sages return to Himavan, announce the auspicious date, and summon the deities. This verse simply advances the ceremony toward its sacred beginning.
ramacharitamanas::574.modern_relevance: The guest list is finally set, the hall is booked, and the ceremony can begin. Some verses matter because they move the moment into place.
ramacharitamanas::574.insight: It shifts attention from meaning to sequence: the sacred event now moves into formal preparation.

ramacharitamanas::575.verse_sanskrit: बोलि सकल सुर सादर लीन्हे। सबहि जथोचित आसन दीन्हे॥ बेदी बेद बिधान सँवारी। सुभग सुमंगल गावहिं नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::575.verse_hindi: सब देवताओं को आदर सहित बुलवा लिया और सबको यथायोग्य आसन दिए। वेद की रीति से वेदी सजाई गई और स्त्रियाँ सुंदर श्रेष्ठ मंगल गीत गाने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::575.english_translation: All the radiant beings were invited respectfully and given seats according to custom. The altar was arranged according to Vedic rule, and women sang beautiful, auspicious songs.
ramacharitamanas::575.translation_literal: बोलि (calling) / सकल (all) / सुर (radiant beings) / सादर (respectfully) / लीन्हे (were brought) / सबहि (to all) / जथोचित (according to propriety) / आसन (seats) / दीन्हे (given) / बेदी (altar) / बेद (Veda) / बिधान (rule) / सँवारी (arranged) / सुभग (beautiful) / सुमंगल (highly auspicious) / गावहिं (sing) / नारी (women)
ramacharitamanas::575.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::575.essence: Reverence is shown first in the way a space is prepared.
ramacharitamanas::575.simple_meaning: The gods are welcomed properly, the wedding altar is prepared, and the women sing auspicious songs.
ramacharitamanas::575.simple_insight: Order and reverence turn a ceremony into something sacred.
ramacharitamanas::575.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s wedding, the preparations move with perfect ritual care. The celestial guests are seated with honor, the altar is arranged by Vedic custom, and the whole scene fills with auspicious song before the sacred marriage begins.
ramacharitamanas::575.modern_relevance: A family gathers before a wedding, checking every seat, every offering, every detail. No one is rushing; everyone is making space for what matters.
ramacharitamanas::575.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to reverent preparation. The sacred begins in how carefully people make room for it.

ramacharitamanas::576.verse_sanskrit: सिंघासनु अति दिब्य सुहावा। जाइ न बरनि बिरंचि बनावा॥ बैठे सिव बिप्रन्ह सिरु नाई। हृदयँ सुमिरि निज प्रभु रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::576.verse_hindi: वेदिका पर एक अत्यन्त सुंदर दिव्य सिंहासन था, जिस (की सुंदरता) का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता, क्योंकि वह स्वयं ब्रह्माजी का बनाया हुआ था। ब्राह्मणों को सिर नवाकर और हृदय में अपने स्वामी श्री रघुनाथजी का स्मरण करके शिवजी उस सिंहासन पर बैठ गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::576.english_translation: The throne on the altar was so wonderfully divine that even Brahma could not describe its beauty. Shiva bowed to the Brahmins, remembered his own lord Raghunath in his heart, and sat on that throne.
ramacharitamanas::576.translation_literal: सिंघासनु (throne) / अति (very) / दिब्य (divine) / सुहावा (beautiful) / जाइ न (cannot go) / बरनि (described) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / बनावा (made) / बैठे (sat) / सिव (Shiva) / बिप्रन्ह (to the Brahmins) / सिरु नाई (bowing the head) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / सुमिरि (remembering) / निज (own) / प्रभु (lord) / रघुराई (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::576.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::576.essence: Greatness is complete only when it bows before the divine.
ramacharitamanas::576.simple_meaning: A magnificently divine throne was prepared. Shiva honored the Brahmins, remembered Ram in his heart, and took his seat.
ramacharitamanas::576.simple_insight: Even in greatness, humility stays first.
ramacharitamanas::576.detailed_meaning: At Ram and Sita’s wedding, the sacred hall is ready and the divine throne has been set. Shiva arrives with reverence, bows to the Brahmins, remembers Ram inwardly, and sits. The moment highlights holiness joined with humility.
ramacharitamanas::576.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is watching, and the spotlight could easily become yours. Instead, you greet the elders first, steady yourself, and remember what matters before taking your seat.
ramacharitamanas::576.insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing that true dignity begins with humility and remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::577.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि मुनीसन्ह उमा बोलाईं। करि सिंगारु सखीं लै आईं॥ देखत रूपु सकल सुर मोहे। बरनै छबि अस जग कबि को है ॥
ramacharitamanas::577.verse_hindi: फिर मुनीश्वरों ने पार्वतीजी को बुलाया। सखियाँ श्रृंगार करके उन्हें ले आईं। पार्वतीजी के रूप को देखते ही सब देवता मोहित हो गए। संसार में ऐसा कवि कौन है, जो उस सुंदरता का वर्णन कर सके? ॥
ramacharitamanas::577.english_translation: Then the sages called Uma. Her companions brought her, fully adorned. Seeing her form, all the radiant beings were enchanted. Who in this world could describe such beauty?
ramacharitamanas::577.translation_literal: बहुरि (then) / मुनीसन्ह (the sages) / उमा (Uma) / बोलाईं (called) / करि (having done) / सिंगारु (adornment) / सखीं (companions) / लै (taking) / आईं (brought) / देखत (seeing) / रूपु (form/beauty) / सकल (all) / सुर (radiant beings) / मोहे (were enchanted) / बरनै (to describe) / छबि (beauty/grace) / अस (such) / जग (in the world) / कबि (poet) / को (who) / है (is)
ramacharitamanas::577.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::577.essence: Beauty can overwhelm speech before it can be named.
ramacharitamanas::577.simple_meaning: Parvati is brought in beautifully dressed, and her beauty leaves the radiant beings spellbound. The verse ends by saying no poet could fully describe her grace.
ramacharitamanas::577.simple_insight: Some presence is beyond description. Even admiration falls silent before it.
ramacharitamanas::577.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-Ram wedding scene, the sages call Uma forward after the divine seat is prepared. Her companions bring her in adorned and radiant, and even the radiant beings are overwhelmed by her beauty. The verse pauses on wonder rather than doctrine.
ramacharitamanas::577.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when someone enters and everyone feels it at once. No caption, no review, no analysis can fully hold that kind of presence.
ramacharitamanas::577.insight: It shifts attention from explanation to awe, showing that some realities are meant to be witnessed, not reduced.

ramacharitamanas::578.verse_sanskrit: जगदंबिका जानि भव भामा। सुरन्ह मनहिं मन कीन्ह प्रनामा॥ सुंदरता मरजाद भवानी। जाइ न कोटिहुँ बदन बखानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::578.verse_hindi: पार्वतीजी को जगदम्बा और शिवजी की पत्नी समझकर देवताओं ने मन ही मन प्रणाम किया। भवानीजी सुंदरता की सीमा हैं। करोड़ों मुखों से भी उनकी शोभा नहीं कही जा सकती ॥
ramacharitamanas::578.english_translation: Knowing her as the Mother of the universe and the wife of Shiva, the devas bowed to her inwardly. Bhavani is the limit of beauty; even millions of mouths cannot describe her radiance.
ramacharitamanas::578.translation_literal: जगदंबिका (mother of the universe) / जानि (knowing) / भव भामा (Bhavani, Shiva's consort) / सुरन्ह (by the devas) / मनहिं (in the mind) / मन कीन्ह (made) / प्रनामा (salutation)॥ / सुंदरता (beauty) / मरजाद (limit) / भवानी (Bhavani) / जाइ न (cannot go) / कोटिहुँ (even millions) / बदन (mouths) / बखानी (describe)
ramacharitamanas::578.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::578.essence: True greatness makes even praise fall silent.
ramacharitamanas::578.simple_meaning: The devas silently honor Parvati as the Mother of the universe and praise her beauty as beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::578.simple_insight: Some presence is so complete that even praise feels too small.
ramacharitamanas::578.detailed_meaning: At Parvati's arrival for the divine gathering, the devas recognize her not just as Shiva's consort but as the Mother of the universe. Her beauty and majesty overwhelm language itself, so they bow inwardly before she even speaks.
ramacharitamanas::578.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm, dignity, and warmth make the whole room soften. Nobody says it out loud, but everyone feels they are in the presence of something rare.
ramacharitamanas::578.insight: It shifts attention from spoken praise to inward reverence when words cannot match what is seen.

ramacharitamanas::579.verse_sanskrit: कोटिहुँ बदन नहिं बनै बरनत जग जननि सोभा महा। सकुचहिं कहत श्रुति सेष सारद मंदमति तुलसीकहा॥ छबिखानि मातु भवानि गवनीं मध्य मंडप सिव जहाँ। अवलोकि सकहिं न सकुच पति पद कमल मनु मधुकरु तहाँ॥
ramacharitamanas::579.verse_hindi: जगज्जननी पार्वतीजी की महान शोभा का वर्णन करोड़ों मुखों से भी करते नहीं बनता। वेद, शेषजी और सरस्वतीजी तक उसे कहते हुए सकुचा जाते हैं, तब मंदबुद्धि तुलसी किस गिनती में है? सुंदरता और शोभा की खान माता भवानी मंडप के बीच में, जहाँ शिवजी थे, वहाँ गईं। वे संकोच के मारे पति (शिवजी) के चरणकमलों को देख नहीं सकतीं, परन्तु उनका मन रूपी भौंरा तो वहीं (रसपान कर रहा) था।
ramacharitamanas::579.english_translation: Millions of mouths cannot describe the great splendor of the mother of the world. Even the Vedas, Shesha, and Saraswati hesitate to speak of it; then what count has Tulsidas, with his dull mind? The fountain of beauty, Mother Bhavani, went into the center of the pavilion where Shiva stood. She could not bring herself to look at her husband's lotus feet, yet her mind, like a bee, remained there drinking the nectar.
ramacharitamanas::579.translation_literal: कोटिहुँ (even millions) / बदन (mouths) / नहिं (not) / बनै (is possible) / बरनत (while describing) / जग जननि (mother of the world) / सोभा (splendor) / महा (great) / सकुचहिं (hesitate / feel shy) / कहत (in speaking) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / सेष (Shesha) / सारद (Saraswati) / मंदमति (slow-minded) / तुलसीकहा (Tulsidas said) / छबिखानि (mine of beauty) / मातु भवानि (Mother Bhavani) / गवनीं (went) / मध्य मंडप (to the center of the pavilion) / सिव (Shiva) / जहाँ (where) / अवलोकि (seeing) / सकहिं (is able) / न (not) / सकुच (shyness) / पति पद कमल (husband's lotus feet) / मनु (mind) / मधुकरु (bee) / तहाँ (there)
ramacharitamanas::579.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::579.essence: True reverence can be too deep for words and too shy for direct gaze.
ramacharitamanas::579.simple_meaning: Parvati's beauty is beyond description, and even sacred authorities hesitate to speak of it. She enters the pavilion where Shiva sits, and although she cannot openly look at his feet, her mind remains drawn to them.
ramacharitamanas::579.simple_insight: Love can be shy on the outside and still utterly devoted inside.
ramacharitamanas::579.detailed_meaning: Parvati has just been brought into the assembly after the sages' arrangements. Tulsidas pauses the scene to praise her beauty, then shows her moving toward Shiva with reverence and modesty. The moment matters because it prepares the sacred meeting of Shiva and Bhavani.
ramacharitamanas::579.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and cannot meet someone's eyes, yet your whole attention is already with them. The body hesitates; the heart has arrived.
ramacharitamanas::579.insight: It shifts attention from outward composure to inward devotion and restraint.

ramacharitamanas::580.verse_sanskrit: मुनि अनुसासन गनपतिहि पूजेउ संभु भवानि। कोउ सुनि संसय करै जनि सुर अनादि जियँ जानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::580.verse_hindi: मुनियों की आज्ञा से शिवजी और पार्वतीजी ने गणेशजी का पूजन किया। मन में देवताओं को अनादि समझकर कोई इस बात को सुनकर शंका न करे (कि गणेशजी तो शिव-पार्वती की संतान हैं, अभी विवाह से पूर्व ही वे कहाँ से आ गए?) ॥
ramacharitamanas::580.english_translation: By the sages' instruction, Shiva and Parvati worshipped Ganapati. Knowing the gods are beginningless, no one should doubt this on hearing it.
ramacharitamanas::580.translation_literal: मुनि (sages) / अनुसासन (instruction) / गनपतिहि (Ganapati) / पूजेउ (worshipped) / संभु (Shiva) / भवानि (Parvati) / कोउ (anyone) / सुनि (hearing) / संसय (doubt) / करै (should make) / जनि (do not) / सुर (the gods) / अनादि (beginningless) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानि (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::580.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::580.essence: Beginningless beings do not fit ordinary chronology.
ramacharitamanas::580.simple_meaning: Shiva and Parvati first worship Ganesh as the sages direct. The poet adds that no one should be troubled by doubt, because the divine beings are beyond ordinary time.
ramacharitamanas::580.simple_insight: Some sacred events are not meant to be judged by ordinary chronology.
ramacharitamanas::580.detailed_meaning: At the start of the marriage ceremony, the sages direct Shiva and Parvati to honor Ganapati first. Tulsidas pauses to prevent confusion: divine beings are beginningless, so this ritual order should not be read like ordinary family history.
ramacharitamanas::580.modern_relevance: You hear a story that seems to break the timeline, and your first instinct is to argue. The verse asks you to stop and trust the larger sacred frame before forcing it into neat logic.
ramacharitamanas::580.insight: It shifts the mind from literal suspicion to reverent understanding of sacred time.

ramacharitamanas::581.verse_sanskrit: जसि बिबाह कै बिधि श्रुति गाई। महामुनिन्ह सो सब करवाई॥ गहि गिरीस कुस कन्या पानी। भवहि समरपीं जानि भवानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::581.verse_hindi: वेदों में विवाह की जैसी रीति कही गई है, महामुनियों ने वह सभी रीति करवाई। पर्वतराज हिमाचल ने हाथ में कुश लेकर तथा कन्या का हाथ पकड़कर उन्हें भवानी (शिवपत्नी) जानकर शिवजी को समर्पण किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::581.english_translation: The Vedas describe the rite of marriage, and the great sages carried it out in full. Himachal took sacred grass in hand, joined the bride's hand, and offered Bhavani to Shiva, knowing her as the divine consort.
ramacharitamanas::581.translation_literal: जसि (as) / बिबाह (marriage) / कै (of) / बिधि (rite, method) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / गाई (sang, described) / महामुनिन्ह (by the great sages) / सो (that) / सब (all) / करवाई (was carried out)॥ / गहि (taking) / गिरीस (Himachal, lord of the mountains) / कुस (sacred grass) / कन्या (the bride) / पानी (hand) / भवहि (to Shiva) / समरपीं (offered) / जानि (knowing) / भवानी (Bhavani) ॥
ramacharitamanas::581.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::581.essence: Marriage becomes complete when it is offered through sacred rite.
ramacharitamanas::581.simple_meaning: The marriage is performed according to sacred custom, and Himachal formally gives Parvati's hand to Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::581.simple_insight: A holy union is honored through proper rite, not casual feeling.
ramacharitamanas::581.detailed_meaning: The mountain king Himachal is arranging Parvati's marriage to Shiva. The sages guide every step according to sacred law, and he ceremonially gives his daughter away. The verse prepares for the moment when the marriage itself is completed.
ramacharitamanas::581.modern_relevance: A family gathers for a wedding and every small ritual matters more than it seems. The ceremony is not decoration; it is the shape that gives the union dignity and meaning.
ramacharitamanas::581.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the sacred order that frames it.

ramacharitamanas::582.verse_sanskrit: पानिग्रहन जब कीन्ह महेसा। हियँ हरषे तब सकल सुरेसा॥ बेदमन्त्र मुनिबर उच्चरहीं। जय जय जय संकर सुर करहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::582.verse_hindi: जब महेश्वर (शिवजी) ने पार्वती का पाणिग्रहण किया, तब (इन्द्रादि) सब देवता हृदय में बड़े ही हर्षित हुए। श्रेष्ठ मुनिगण वेदमंत्रों का उच्चारण करने लगे और देवगण शिवजी का जय-जयकार करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::582.english_translation: When Mahesha took Parvati's hand in marriage, all the lords of the devas rejoiced in their hearts. The best sages recited Vedic मंत्रas, and the devas cried victory to Shankara.
ramacharitamanas::582.translation_literal: पानिग्रहन (marriage, taking the hand) / जब (when) / कीन्ह (did, performed) / महेसा (Mahesha, Shiva) / हियँ (in the heart) / हरषे (rejoiced) / तब (then) / सकल (all) / सुरेसा (lords of the devas) / बेदमन्त्र (Vedic mantras) / मुनिबर (best sages) / उच्चरहीं (recited) / जय जय जय (victory, victory, victory) / संकर (Shankara, Shiva) / सुर (devas) / करहीं (did, made)
ramacharitamanas::582.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::582.essence: A rightful union makes the whole world rejoice.
ramacharitamanas::582.simple_meaning: Shiva and Parvati's marriage filled the heavenly beings with joy. The sages chanted sacred words, and the divine hosts celebrated Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::582.simple_insight: Some moments are so right that even the world around them seems to rejoice.
ramacharitamanas::582.detailed_meaning: Shiva has just accepted Parvati in marriage, completing the sacred union after the formal rites. The celestial beings, sages, and divine attendants respond with joy, chants, and praise. This verse is a celebratory bridge into the larger wedding scene.
ramacharitamanas::582.modern_relevance: A wedding crowd goes quiet for a second, then breaks into smiles and applause as the couple takes the final vow. Everyone feels it: something fitting has just been made complete.
ramacharitamanas::582.insight: It shifts attention from private ceremony to shared cosmic celebration.

ramacharitamanas::583.verse_sanskrit: बाजहिं बाजन बिबिध बिधाना। सुमनबृष्टि नभ भै बिधि नाना॥ हर गिरिजा कर भयउ बिबाहू। सकल भुवन भरि रहा उछाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::583.verse_hindi: अनेकों प्रकार के बाजे बजने लगे। आकाश से नाना प्रकार के फूलों की वर्षा हुई। शिव-पार्वती का विवाह हो गया। सारे ब्राह्माण्ड में आनंद भर गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::583.english_translation: Many kinds of instruments began to play. Flowers rained down from the sky in many forms. Shiva and Girija were married. Joy filled all the worlds.
ramacharitamanas::583.translation_literal: बाजहिं (were sounding) / बाजन (musical instruments) / बिबिध (various) / बिधाना (kinds) / सुमनबृष्टि (rain of flowers) / नभ (sky) / भै (became) / बिधि (in many ways) / नाना (various) / हर (Shiva) / गिरिजा (Parvati) / कर (of) / भयउ (became) / बिबाहू (marriage) / सकल (all) / भुवन (worlds) / भरि (filled) / रहा (remained) / उछाहू (joy)
ramacharitamanas::583.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::583.essence: Their union turns one marriage into a joy shared by all worlds.
ramacharitamanas::583.simple_meaning: The wedding of Shiva and Parvati is celebrated with music, flowers, and joy spreading through every world.
ramacharitamanas::583.simple_insight: Some moments are so blessed that joy seems to move through everything at once.
ramacharitamanas::583.detailed_meaning: The wedding rites are complete. As Shiva and Parvati unite, drums sound, flowers fall from the sky, and the celebration expands beyond the couple to all realms. The scene marks cosmic harmony, not just a personal marriage.
ramacharitamanas::583.modern_relevance: A wedding hall goes quiet for a second, then erupts in cheers as the couple walks in. The happiness is bigger than the room — everyone feels carried by it.
ramacharitamanas::583.insight: It shifts attention from private celebration to a moment that restores harmony everywhere.

ramacharitamanas::584.verse_sanskrit: दासीं दास तुरग रथ नागा। धेनु बसन मनि बस्तु बिभागा॥ अन्न कनकभाजन भरि जाना। दाइज दीन्ह न जाइ बखाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::584.verse_hindi: दासी, दास, रथ, घोड़े, हाथी, गायें, वस्त्र और मणि आदि अनेक प्रकार की चीजें, अन्न तथा सोने के बर्तन गाड़ियों में लदवाकर दहेज में दिए, जिनका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::584.english_translation: Servants, male servants, horses, chariots, elephants, cows, clothes, jewels, goods, food, and gold vessels were all given as dowry, beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::584.translation_literal: दासीं (female servants) / दास (male servants) / तुरग (horses) / रथ (chariots) / नागा (elephants) / धेनु (cows) / बसन (clothes) / मनि (jewels) / बस्तु (goods) / बिभागा (various kinds) / अन्न (food) / कनकभाजन (gold vessels) / भरि (filled) / जाना (were loaded) / दाइज (dowry) / दीन्ह (given) / न जाइ (cannot be) / बखाना (described)
ramacharitamanas::584.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::584.essence: Love can overflow into gifts too many to count.
ramacharitamanas::584.simple_meaning: Himachal gave a vast dowry for the wedding, loading carts with servants, animals, clothes, jewels, food, and gold vessels. The gifts were so many they could not be fully described.
ramacharitamanas::584.simple_insight: Some offerings are too abundant to count. Love can show itself as generous, overflowing giving.
ramacharitamanas::584.detailed_meaning: Shiva and Parvati’s wedding has just been celebrated, and now Himachal prepares the bride’s gifts. The verse lists the wealth and goods sent as dowry, not to teach a doctrine, but to show the scale of honor and celebration around the marriage.
ramacharitamanas::584.modern_relevance: A wedding warehouse is packed with boxes, furniture, and gifts from both families, and no one can keep track anymore. The scene is about overflow, not calculation.
ramacharitamanas::584.insight: It shifts attention from the items themselves to the abundance and honor behind them.

ramacharitamanas::585.verse_sanskrit: दाइज दियो बहु भाँति पुनि कर जोरि हिमभूधर कह्यो। का देउँ पूरनकाम संकर चरन पंकज गहि रह्यो॥ सिवँ कृपासागर ससुर कर संतोषु सब भाँतिहिं कियो। पुनि गहे पद पाथोज मयनाँ प्रेम परिपूरन हियो॥
ramacharitamanas::585.verse_hindi: बहुत प्रकार का दहेज देकर, फिर हाथ जोड़कर हिमाचल ने कहा- हे शंकर! आप पूर्णकाम हैं, मैं आपको क्या दे सकता हूँ? (इतना कहकर) वे शिवजी के चरणकमल पकड़कर रह गए। तब कृपा के सागर शिवजी ने अपने ससुर का सभी प्रकार से समाधान किया। फिर प्रेम से परिपूर्ण हृदय मैनाजी ने शिवजी के चरण कमल पकड़े (और कहा-)।
ramacharitamanas::585.english_translation: Having given many gifts, Himachal folded his hands and said, “What can I give you, O Shankar, who are already complete?” Then he held Shiva’s lotus feet. The ocean of grace Shiva satisfied his father-in-law in every way. Then Parvati, her heart full of love, held Shiva’s lotus feet.
