ramacharitamanas::585.translation_literal: दाइज (dowry/gifts) / दियो (gave) / बहु भाँति (in many kinds) / पुनि (again) / कर जोरि (with joined hands) / हिमभूधर (Himachal) / कह्यो (said) / का (what) / देउँ (shall I give) / पूरनकाम (fully fulfilled) / संकर (Shankar/Shiva) / चरन पंकज (lotus feet) / गहि (grasping) / रह्यो (remained)॥ / सिवँ (Shiva) / कृपासागर (ocean of grace) / ससुर (father-in-law) / कर (of) / संतोषु (satisfaction) / सब भाँतिहिं (in every way) / कियो (did) / पुनि (then) / गहे (held) / पद पाथोज (lotus feet) / मयनाँ (Maina) / प्रेम (love) / परिपूरन (full) / हियो (heart)॥
ramacharitamanas::585.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::585.essence: Completeness receives nothing and still gives everything.
ramacharitamanas::585.simple_meaning: Himalaya gives gifts to Shiva but says Shiva needs nothing. Shiva responds with grace, and Maina then bows to his feet in love.
ramacharitamanas::585.detailed_meaning: At Shiva and Parvati’s wedding, Himachal offers rich gifts and then humbly admits he can give nothing to one who is already complete. Shiva accepts him with grace, and Maina follows with a heart overflowing in devotion. The verse deepens the wedding’s sacred exchange.
ramacharitamanas::585.modern_relevance: At a wedding where the gifts are extravagant, the real moment is the bowed head, the softened pride, the heart that knows it cannot repay love. Some bonds are answered by humility, not by exchange.
ramacharitamanas::585.insight: It shifts attention from giving things to offering reverence, gratitude, and surrender.

ramacharitamanas::586.verse_sanskrit: नाथ उमा मम प्रान सम गृहकिंकरी करेहु। छमेहु सकल अपराध अब होइ प्रसन्न बरु देहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::586.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! यह उमा मुझे मेरे प्राणों के समान (प्यारी) है। आप इसे अपने घर की टहलनी बनाइएगा और इसके सब अपराधों को क्षमा करते रहिएगा। अब प्रसन्न होकर मुझे यही वर दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::586.english_translation: O Lord, Uma is dear to me as my own life. Please make her a servant in your household, forgive all her faults, and now be pleased to grant this boon.
ramacharitamanas::586.translation_literal: नाथ (O Lord) / उमा (Uma) / मम (my) / प्रान (life) / सम (like) / गृहकिंकरी (household servant) / करेहु (make) / छमेहु (forgive) / सकल (all) / अपराध (faults) / अब (now) / होइ (become) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / बरु (boon) / देहु (give)
ramacharitamanas::586.speaker: Himalaya
ramacharitamanas::586.essence: True affection asks for mercy, not status.
ramacharitamanas::586.simple_meaning: Himalaya asks Shiva to accept Uma as part of his household, forgive her mistakes, and bless her with kindness.
ramacharitamanas::586.simple_insight: Love becomes humble when it asks for grace instead of demanding perfection.
ramacharitamanas::586.detailed_meaning: After bringing rich gifts for Shiva, Himalaya folds his hands and speaks as a father, not a king. He calls Uma dear as his own life, asks Shiva to keep her in his home, and begs forgiveness for her faults before requesting the blessing.
ramacharitamanas::586.modern_relevance: You introduce your daughter to someone you deeply respect and quietly ask for kindness toward her imperfections. That mix of pride, love, and humility is all in this line.
ramacharitamanas::586.insight: It teaches you to ask for acceptance with humility, not entitlement.

ramacharitamanas::587.verse_sanskrit: बहु बिधि संभु सासु समुझाई। गवनी भवन चरन सिरु नाई॥ जननीं उमा बोलि तब लीन्ही। लै उछंग सुंदर सिख दीन्ही ॥
ramacharitamanas::587.verse_hindi: शिवजी ने बहुत तरह से अपनी सास को समझाया। तब वे शिवजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर घर गईं। फिर माता ने पार्वती को बुला लिया और गोद में बिठाकर यह सुंदर सीख दी- ॥
ramacharitamanas::587.english_translation: Shiva explained in many ways to his mother-in-law. Then she bowed her head at Shiva's feet and returned home. After that, the mother called Parvati and, seating her in her lap, gave her this beautiful instruction.
ramacharitamanas::587.translation_literal: बहु बिधि (in many ways) / संभु (Shiva) / सासु (mother-in-law) / समुझाई (explained) / गवनी (went) / भवन (home) / चरन (feet) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing) / जननीं (mother) / उमा (Parvati) / बोलि (calling) / तब (then) / लीन्ही (took) / लै (taking) / उछंग (lap) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सिख (instruction) / दीन्ही (gave)
ramacharitamanas::587.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::587.essence: A private lesson follows the public bow.
ramacharitamanas::587.simple_meaning: Shiva persuades Parvati's mother-in-law, who then goes home. Parvati's mother calls her aside and prepares to give her an important lesson.
ramacharitamanas::587.simple_insight: Some lessons begin with family, not philosophy.
ramacharitamanas::587.detailed_meaning: At the close of the Sita-swayamvar scene, the household tension softens. Shiva has already reassured his mother-in-law, and now Parvati is drawn into the private teaching that will shape her understanding of married life and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::587.modern_relevance: A mother pulls her daughter aside after a family gathering and says, quietly, what really matters. The advice lands because it comes from love, not performance.
ramacharitamanas::587.insight: It shifts attention from the public moment to the intimate instruction that follows.

ramacharitamanas::588.verse_sanskrit: करेहु सदा संकर पद पूजा। नारिधरमु पति देउ न दूजा॥ बचन कहत भरे लोचन बारी। बहुरि लाइ उर लीन्हि कुमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::588.verse_hindi: हे पार्वती! तू सदाशिवजी के चरणों की पूजा करना, नारियों का यही धर्म है। उनके लिए पति ही देवता है और कोई देवता नहीं है। इस प्रकार की बातें कहते-कहते उनकी आँखों में आँसू भर आए और उन्होंने कन्या को छाती से चिपटा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::588.english_translation: O Parvati, always worship the feet of Shankar. For women, the husband is the only deity, and no other. Saying these words, her eyes filled with tears, and she drew the girl close to her chest.
ramacharitamanas::588.translation_literal: करेहु (do) / सदा (always) / संकर (Shankar) / पद (feet) / पूजा (worship) / नारिधरमु (women's dharma) / पति (husband) / देउ (deity) / न दूजा (not another) / बचन (words) / कहत (speaking) / भरे (filled) / लोचन (eyes) / बारी (water/tears) / बहुरि (again) / लाइ (bringing) / उर (chest) / लीन्हि (took) / कुमारी (girl)
ramacharitamanas::588.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::588.essence: A mother's blessing carries both duty and tears.
ramacharitamanas::588.simple_meaning: Parvati is told to worship Shiva and to regard her husband as her highest devotion. The mother speaks with tears and holds her daughter close.
ramacharitamanas::588.simple_insight: Love can sound like instruction when a mother is trying to prepare a child for life.
ramacharitamanas::588.detailed_meaning: In the Shiva-Parvati frame of Balkand, Parvati’s mother is giving her final guidance before sending her back. She tells her daughter to honor Shiva above all, then breaks into tears and embraces her, showing both duty and maternal tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::588.modern_relevance: A mother adjusts her daughter's dupatta before a wedding and gives one last serious warning about marriage. The advice may sound old-fashioned, but the emotion is familiar: protect, prepare, and let go.
ramacharitamanas::588.insight: It links family guidance with social duty, showing how a private blessing becomes a rule for conduct.

ramacharitamanas::589.verse_sanskrit: कत बिधि सृजीं नारि जग माहीं। पराधीन सपनेहूँ सुखु नाहीं॥ भै अति प्रेम बिकल महतारी। धीरजु कीन्ह कुसमय बिचारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::589.verse_hindi: (फिर बोलीं कि) विधाता ने जगत में स्त्री जाति को क्यों पैदा किया? पराधीन को सपने में भी सुख नहीं मिलता। यों कहती हुई माता प्रेम में अत्यन्त विकल हो गईं, परन्तु कुसमय जानकर (दुःख करने का अवसर न जानकर) उन्होंने धीरज धरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::589.english_translation: Why was woman created in this world? Even in dreams, one who is dependent finds no happiness. Speaking this way, the mother was overwhelmed with love, but seeing the untimely moment, she steadied herself.
ramacharitamanas::589.translation_literal: कत (why) / बिधि (the creator) / सृजीं (created) / नारि (woman) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / पराधीन (dependent) / सपनेहूँ (even in dreams) / सुखु (happiness) / नाहीं (not) / भै (became) / अति (very) / प्रेम (love) / बिकल (distressed) / महतारी (mother) / धीरजु (patience) / कीन्ह (did) / कुसमय (untimely moment) / बिचारी (considering)
ramacharitamanas::589.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::589.essence: Love may overwhelm, but restraint keeps it from breaking the moment.
ramacharitamanas::589.simple_meaning: Maina, overwhelmed by love for Parvati, asks why dependence brings no happiness and then restrains herself, seeing that this is not the right moment for grief.
ramacharitamanas::589.simple_insight: Love can make the heart overflow, but wisdom knows when to hold it back.
ramacharitamanas::589.detailed_meaning: Parvati has just heard her mother teach the duty of worship and wifely conduct. Maina is swept up in affection and sorrow, wondering why dependence feels so painful, but she checks herself and stays composed because the moment is not right for open grief.
ramacharitamanas::589.modern_relevance: You get a text that stings, and your first impulse is to pour everything out. Then you remember: not every feeling needs immediate release. Some moments ask for restraint.
ramacharitamanas::589.insight: It shows the difference between emotional surge and wise self-control.

ramacharitamanas::590.verse_sanskrit: पुनि पुनि मिलति परति गहि चरना। परम प्रेमु कछु जाइ न बरना॥ सब नारिन्ह मिलि भेंटि भवानी। जाइ जननि उर पुनि लपटानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::590.verse_hindi: मैना बार-बार मिलती हैं और (पार्वती के) चरणों को पकड़कर गिर पड़ती हैं। बड़ा ही प्रेम है, कुछ वर्णन नहीं किया जाता। भवानी सब स्त्रियों से मिल-भेंटकर फिर अपनी माता के हृदय से जा लिपटीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::590.english_translation: Maina again and again met her, grasped her feet, and fell before her. Such immense love cannot be described. Bhavani met all the women, then went and clung again to her mother's heart.
ramacharitamanas::590.translation_literal: पुनि पुनि (again and again) / मिलति (meeting) / परति (falling) / गहि (grasping) / चरना (feet) / परम प्रेमु (supreme love) / कछु (something) / जाइ न बरना (cannot be described) / सब नारिन्ह (all women) / मिलि (meeting together) / भेंटि (greeting) / भवानी (Bhavani) / जाइ (going) / जननि (mother) / उर (heart/chest) / पुनि (again) / लपटानी (clung)
ramacharitamanas::590.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::590.essence: Love that deep needs no explanation.
ramacharitamanas::590.simple_meaning: Maina repeatedly bows to Parvati with overwhelming love. Parvati greets the women, then returns to her mother's embrace.
ramacharitamanas::590.simple_insight: Love can be so full that words fail and the body speaks instead.
ramacharitamanas::590.detailed_meaning: Parvati has just spoken with her mother after the marriage arrangements. Maina cannot stop bowing to her daughter and holding her feet, while Parvati moves among the women and then returns to her mother's arms. The moment is soaked in tenderness, not doctrine.
ramacharitamanas::590.modern_relevance: You finally see your daughter after months away. You keep touching her shoulder, then stepping back, then hugging her again because the heart has more to say than speech can carry.
ramacharitamanas::590.insight: It shifts attention from explanation to embodied affection, showing that some feelings are expressed through repeated gestures, not arguments.

ramacharitamanas::591.verse_sanskrit: जननिहि बहुरि मिलि चली उचित असीस सब काहूँ दईं। फिरि फिरि बिलोकति मातु तन तब सखीं लै सिव पहिं गईं॥ जाचक सकल संतोषि संकरु उमा सहित भवन चले। सब अमर हरषे सुमन बरषि निसान नभ बाजे भले॥
ramacharitamanas::591.verse_hindi: पार्वतीजी माता से फिर मिलकर चलीं, सब किसी ने उन्हें योग्य आशीर्वाद दिए। पार्वतीजी फिर-फिरकर माता की ओर देखती जाती थीं। तब सखियाँ उन्हें शिवजी के पास ले गईं। महादेवजी सब याचकों को संतुष्ट कर पार्वती के साथ घर (कैलास) को चले। सब देवता प्रसन्न होकर फूलों की वर्षा करने लगे और आकाश में सुंदर नगाड़े बजाने लगे।
ramacharitamanas::591.english_translation: Parvati returned after meeting her mother; everyone gave her fitting blessings. She kept looking back at her mother again and again. Then her companions led her to Shiva. Mahadeva satisfied all the petitioners and left for Kailasa with Uma. All the radiant beings rejoiced, showered flowers, and the skies resounded with drums.
ramacharitamanas::591.translation_literal: जननिहि (to the mother) / बहुरि (again) / मिलि (meeting) / चली (went) / उचित (fitting) / असीस (blessings) / सब काहूँ (to everyone) / दईं (gave) / फिरि फिरि (again and again) / बिलोकति (looking) / मातु (mother) / तन (toward) / तब (then) / सखीं (companions) / लै (taking) / सिव पहिं (to Shiva) / गईं (went) / जाचक (petitioners) / सकल (all) / संतोषि (satisfying) / संकरु (Shankar/Shiva) / उमा सहित (with Uma) / भवन (home) / चले (went) / सब अमर (all radiant beings) / हरषे (rejoiced) / सुमन (flowers) / बरषि (showering) / निसान (drums) / नभ (sky) / बाजे (resounded) / भले (beautifully)
ramacharitamanas::591.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::591.essence: A loving farewell can carry the whole family forward.
ramacharitamanas::591.simple_meaning: Parvati leaves her mother after receiving blessings, keeps looking back, and then goes to Shiva. Shiva returns to Kailasa with her, while the heavenly beings rejoice and shower flowers.
ramacharitamanas::591.simple_insight: Some departures are tender, not final. Love can bless a separation without ending the bond.
ramacharitamanas::591.detailed_meaning: Parvati has finished her visit with her mother, and the family parting is full of affection. She keeps glancing back even as her companions take her to Shiva. The scene closes with Shiva and Uma leaving together, while the heavens celebrate the reunion.
ramacharitamanas::591.modern_relevance: You leave your childhood home after a wedding or a move, then keep looking back through the car window. The goodbye is real, but so is the blessing that carries you forward.
ramacharitamanas::591.insight: It turns a departure into a blessed transition, not a loss.

ramacharitamanas::592.verse_sanskrit: चले संग हिमवंतु तब पहुँचावन अति हेतु। बिबिध भाँति परितोषु करि बिदा कीन्ह बृषकेतु ॥
ramacharitamanas::592.verse_hindi: तब हिमवान् अत्यन्त प्रेम से शिवजी को पहुँचाने के लिए साथ चले। वृषकेतु (शिवजी) ने बहुत तरह से उन्हें संतोष कराकर विदा किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::592.english_translation: Then Himavan, with great affection, accompanied Shiva to see him off. Bṛṣaketu soothed him in many ways and bade him farewell.
ramacharitamanas::592.translation_literal: चले (went) / संग (with) / हिमवंतु (Himavan) / तब (then) / पहुँचावन (to escort) / अति (very) / हेतु (out of affection) / बिबिध (various) / भाँति (ways) / परितोषु (satisfaction / reassurance) / करि (having done) / बिदा (farewell) / कीन्ह (made) / बृषकेतु (Shiva)
ramacharitamanas::592.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::592.essence: True affection can make parting feel complete and peaceful.
ramacharitamanas::592.simple_meaning: Himavan lovingly goes with Shiva to see him off, and Shiva sends him back after comforting him in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::592.simple_insight: Love can make farewell gentle instead of painful.
ramacharitamanas::592.detailed_meaning: After Parvati’s meeting with her mother, the scene shifts to departure. Himavan walks with Shiva out of deep affection, and Shiva soothes him with many kinds of kindness before sending him back. The moment is about respectful parting, not doctrine.
ramacharitamanas::592.modern_relevance: You walk a friend to the cab at midnight, still talking because neither of you wants the moment to end. Some goodbyes become tender because both people know the bond is secure.
ramacharitamanas::592.insight: It shows how affection can honor departure without clinging to it.

ramacharitamanas::593.verse_sanskrit: तुरत भवन आए गिरिराई। सकल सैल सर लिए बोलाई॥ आदर दान बिनय बहुमाना। सब कर बिदा कीन्ह हिमवाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::593.verse_hindi: पर्वतराज हिमाचल तुरंत घर आए और उन्होंने सब पर्वतों और सरोवरों को बुलाया। हिमवान ने आदर, दान, विनय और बहुत सम्मानपूर्वक सबकी विदाई की ॥
ramacharitamanas::593.english_translation: Himalaya returned home at once. He summoned all the mountains and lakes. With honor, gifts, humility, and great respect, Himalaya bade them farewell.
ramacharitamanas::593.translation_literal: तुरत (at once) / भवन (home) / आए (came) / गिरिराई (king of mountains) / सकल (all) / सैल (mountains) / सर (lakes) / लिए (having) / बोलाई (summoned) / आदर (honor) / दान (gifts) / बिनय (humility) / बहुमाना (great respect) / सब कर (of all) / बिदा (farewell) / कीन्ह (made) / हिमवाना (Himalaya)
ramacharitamanas::593.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::593.essence: True grandeur includes knowing how to let everyone go well.
ramacharitamanas::593.simple_meaning: Himalaya returns home, gathers the mountains and lakes, and sends everyone away with honor and generosity.
ramacharitamanas::593.simple_insight: Even a great host can part with grace, without clinging to the moment.
ramacharitamanas::593.detailed_meaning: Himalaya has just escorted Shiva and Parvati onward. Back at his home, he gathers the mountains and lakes around him and sends them off properly. The scene shows royal hospitality and the calm after the sacred departure.
ramacharitamanas::593.modern_relevance: The guests have left after a wedding, and the house still smells of flowers and food. You thank everyone, pack the gifts, and close the door with grace instead of emptiness.
ramacharitamanas::593.insight: It shifts attention from holding on to an event to completing it with dignity.

ramacharitamanas::594.verse_sanskrit: जबहिं संभु कैलासहिं आए। सुर सब निज निज लोक सिधाए॥ जगत मातु पितु संभु भवानी। तेहिं सिंगारु न कहउँ बखानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::594.verse_hindi: जब शिवजी कैलास पर्वत पर पहुँचे, तब सब देवता अपने-अपने लोकों को चले गए। (तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि) पार्वतीजी और शिवजी जगत के माता-पिता हैं, इसलिए मैं उनके श्रृंगार का वर्णन नहीं करता ॥
ramacharitamanas::594.english_translation: When Shiva reached Kailash, all the devas returned to their own realms. The world’s mother and father are Shiva and Parvati, so I do not describe their adornment.
ramacharitamanas::594.translation_literal: जबहिं (when) / संभु (Shiva) / कैलासहिं (to Kailash) / आए (came) / सुर (devas) / सब (all) / निज निज (their own) / लोक (realms) / सिधाए (departed) / जगत (world) / मातु (mother) / पितु (father) / संभु (Shiva) / भवानी (Parvati) / तेहिं (their) / सिंगारु (adornment) / न (not) / कहउँ (I speak) / बखानी (describe)
ramacharitamanas::594.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::594.essence: Some presence is too vast for description; reverence begins where speech ends.
ramacharitamanas::594.simple_meaning: Shiva returns to Kailash, the other beings leave, and Tulsidas pauses to say he will not try to describe Shiva and Parvati’s beauty.
ramacharitamanas::594.simple_insight: Some forms are too revered for ordinary description. Silence can be a kind of praise.
ramacharitamanas::594.detailed_meaning: Shiva comes back to Kailash after the welcome at Himachal’s home. The devas depart to their own worlds. Tulsidas then steps in, calling Shiva and Parvati the parents of the world, and says their splendour is beyond what he can properly describe.
ramacharitamanas::594.modern_relevance: You enter a temple after the crowd has thinned and the air still feels charged. Some moments do not need commentary; they ask for reverent attention instead.
ramacharitamanas::594.insight: It shifts the reader from trying to capture everything with words to recognising when reverence is better than explanation.

ramacharitamanas::595.verse_sanskrit: करहिं बिबिध बिधि भोग बिलासा। गनन्ह समेत बसहिं कैलासा॥ हर गिरिजा बिहार नित नयऊ। एहि बिधि बिपुल काल चलि गयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::595.verse_hindi: शिव-पार्वती विविध प्रकार के भोग-विलास करते हुए अपने गणों सहित कैलास पर रहने लगे। वे नित्य नए विहार करते थे। इस प्रकार बहुत समय बीत गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::595.english_translation: Shiva and Parvati enjoyed many kinds of pleasures and lived with their attendants on Kailash. They spent each day in fresh delight. In this way, a great deal of time passed.
ramacharitamanas::595.translation_literal: करहिं (they do) / बिबिध बिधि (various kinds) / भोग (enjoyments) / बिलासा (delights, playful pleasures) / गनन्ह समेत (together with attendants) / बसहिं (they live) / कैलासा (on Kailash)॥ / हर (Shiva) / गिरिजा (Parvati) / बिहार (pastimes, amusements) / नित (daily, always) / नयऊ (new) / एहि बिधि (in this way) / बिपुल (great, abundant) / काल (time) / चलि गयऊ (passed away)
ramacharitamanas::595.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::595.essence: Joy shared in the right company makes time pass unnoticed.
ramacharitamanas::595.simple_meaning: Shiva and Parvati live on Kailash with their attendants, enjoying fresh pastimes each day. Time passes quietly in their company.
ramacharitamanas::595.simple_insight: Some moments are so full they seem to make time disappear.
ramacharitamanas::595.detailed_meaning: On Kailash, Shiva and Parvati live among their attendants in ease and joy. Their days pass in fresh play and companionship. This verse is a calm bridge in the opening frame, marking the long span of time before the next divine event.
ramacharitamanas::595.modern_relevance: A long evening with people you love can feel like no time has passed. The clock moves, but shared joy makes the hours light.
ramacharitamanas::595.insight: It turns attention from dramatic action to the quiet fullness of sacred companionship.

ramacharitamanas::596.verse_sanskrit: जब जनमेउ षटबदन कुमारा। तारकु असुरु समर जेहिं मारा॥ आगम निगम प्रसिद्ध पुराना। षन्मुख जन्मु सकल जग जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::596.verse_hindi: तब छ: मुखवाले पुत्र (स्वामिकार्तिक) का जन्म हुआ, जिन्होंने (बड़े होने पर) युद्ध में तारकासुर को मारा। वेद, शास्त्र और पुराणों में स्वामिकार्तिक के जन्म की कथा प्रसिद्ध है और सारा जगत उसे जानता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::596.english_translation: Then the six-faced son was born, who later slew the demon Taraka in battle. His birth is famed in the Vedas, scriptures, and Puranas, and the whole world knows of the six-faced one.
ramacharitamanas::596.translation_literal: जब (then) / जनमेउ (was born) / षटबदन (six-faced) / कुमारा (son) / तारकु (Taraka) / असुरु (demon) / समर (battle) / जेहिं (by whom) / मारा (was killed) / आगम (scriptures) / निगम (Vedas) / प्रसिद्ध (well-known) / पुराना (Puranas) / षन्मुख (six-faced one) / जन्मु (birth) / सकल (all) / जग (world) / जाना (knew)
ramacharitamanas::596.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::596.essence: A famous birth is introduced before its full story unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::596.simple_meaning: Kartikeya is born, and his later victory over Taraka is already part of his fame. The verse simply marks his celebrated arrival.
ramacharitamanas::596.simple_insight: Some births arrive already wrapped in renown.
ramacharitamanas::596.detailed_meaning: The scene stays with Shiva and Parvati on Kailash, but the narration briefly turns to their son Kartikeya. His six-faced birth and future killing of Taraka are mentioned as famous, widely known facts, not as a teaching. The verse supports the larger story rather than completing it.
ramacharitamanas::596.modern_relevance: A family announcement goes out and everyone already knows the name before the child has even grown. The moment is about fame and recognition, not a lesson you can apply directly.
ramacharitamanas::596.insight: It frames a celebrated figure through public memory, not personal instruction.

ramacharitamanas::597.verse_sanskrit: जगु जान षन्मुख जन्मु कर्मु प्रतापु पुरुषारथु महा। तेहि हेतु मैं बृषकेतु सुत कर चरित संछेपहिं कहा॥ यह उमा संभु बिबाहु जे नर नारि कहहिं जे गावहीं। कल्यान काज बिबाह मंगल सर्बदा सुखु पावहीं॥
ramacharitamanas::597.verse_hindi: षडानन (स्वामिकार्तिक) के जन्म, कर्म, प्रताप और महान पुरुषार्थ को सारा जगत जानता है, इसलिए मैंने वृषकेतु (शिवजी) के पुत्र का चरित्र संक्षेप में ही कहा है। शिव-पार्वती के विवाह की इस कथा को जो स्त्री-पुरुष कहेंगे और गाएँगे, वे कल्याण के कार्यों और विवाहादि मंगलों में सदा सुख पाएँगे।
ramacharitamanas::597.english_translation: The world knows the birth, deeds, glory, and great effort of Shanmukha, so I have told the story of Shiva's son only in brief. Whoever men and women speak or sing of the marriage of Uma and Shambhu will find lasting joy in auspicious works and wedding rites.
ramacharitamanas::597.translation_literal: जगु (the world) / जान (knows) / षन्मुख (Shanmukha) / जन्मु (birth) / कर्मु (deeds) / प्रतापु (glory) / पुरुषारथु (great effort) / महा (great) / तेहि हेतु (for that reason) / मैं (I) / बृषकेतु सुत (son of Vrishaketu) / कर (of) / चरित (story) / संछेपहिं (in brief) / कहा (told)॥ यह (this) / उमा (Uma) / संभु (Shambhu) / बिबाहु (marriage) / जे (who) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / कहहिं (speak) / जे (who) / गावहीं (sing) / कल्यान काज (auspicious works) / बिबाह मंगल (wedding auspiciousness) / सर्बदा (always) / सुखु (joy) / पावहीं (obtain)॥
ramacharitamanas::597.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::597.essence: Holy stories bless the lives that keep repeating them.
ramacharitamanas::597.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he has only briefly told Shanmukha's story, because the world already knows it. He adds that singing or speaking of Shiva and Uma's marriage brings lasting joy and blessings to good works and weddings.
ramacharitamanas::597.simple_insight: Sacred stories are not just remembered; they are meant to bless the listener's life.
ramacharitamanas::597.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses after Shiva's frame story and turns to praise the marriage of Uma and Shambhu. He says Shanmukha's birth and glory are already known, so he keeps that tale brief, then declares that singing this marriage story brings joy to all auspicious occasions.
ramacharitamanas::597.modern_relevance: At a wedding where relatives keep reciting the couple's story and blessings, the room changes. The words are not decoration; they shape the mood, calm the mind, and make the celebration feel held by something larger.
ramacharitamanas::597.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the power of spoken remembrance in making the event sacred.

ramacharitamanas::598.verse_sanskrit: चरित सिंधु गिरिजा रमन बेद न पावहिं पारु। बरनै तुलसीदासु किमि अति मतिमंद गवाँरु ॥
ramacharitamanas::598.verse_hindi: गिरिजापति महादेवजी का चरित्र समुद्र के समान (अपार) है, उसका पार वेद भी नहीं पाते। तब अत्यन्त मन्दबुद्धि और गँवार तुलसीदास उसका वर्णन कैसे कर सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::598.english_translation: Shiva's story is an ocean; even the Vedas cannot reach its far shore. How can dull-minded Tulsidas describe it?
ramacharitamanas::598.translation_literal: चरित (story/character) / सिंधु (ocean) / गिरिजा-रमन (Shiva, beloved of Girija) / बेद (the Vedas) / न (not) / पावहिं (reach) / पारु (the far shore) / बरनै (describe) / तुलसीदासु (Tulsidas) / किमि (how) / अति (very) / मतिमंद (dull-minded) / गवाँरु (rustic/ignorant)
ramacharitamanas::598.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::598.essence: True devotion begins where description fails.
ramacharitamanas::598.simple_meaning: Shiva's character is so vast that even the Vedas cannot fully describe it, and Tulsidas humbly says he cannot do it justice.
ramacharitamanas::598.simple_insight: Greatness can make a person humble instead of proud.
ramacharitamanas::598.detailed_meaning: After hearing of Shiva's marriage and glory, Tulsidas pauses and bows. He says Shiva's character is like an endless ocean, beyond even the Vedas. The doha is not about inability alone; it is an act of reverence before something too vast to contain.
ramacharitamanas::598.modern_relevance: You try to explain someone you deeply admire, and every sentence feels too small. The more you love what you are describing, the more honest it becomes to admit its depth.
ramacharitamanas::598.insight: It shifts the mind from performance to reverence, teaching that some realities are best approached with humility.

ramacharitamanas::599.verse_sanskrit: संभु चरित सुनि सरस सुहावा। भरद्वाज मुनि अति सुखु पावा॥ बहु लालसा कथा पर बाढ़ी। नयनन्हि नीरु रोमावलि ठाढ़ी ॥
ramacharitamanas::599.verse_hindi: शिवजी के रसीले और सुहावने चरित्र को सुनकर मुनि भरद्वाजजी ने बहुत ही सुख पाया। कथा सुनने की उनकी लालसा बहुत बढ़ गई। नेत्रों में जल भर आया तथा रोमावली खड़ी हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::599.english_translation: Hearing Shiva's charming, delightful story, sage Bharadvaja felt great joy. His longing to hear more grew strong. Tears filled his eyes, and the hair on his body stood on end.
ramacharitamanas::599.translation_literal: संभु (Shiva) / चरित (story or conduct) / सुनि (hearing) / सरस (sweet, full of feeling) / सुहावा (pleasant, charming) / भरद्वाज (Bharadvaja) / मुनि (sage) / अति (very) / सुखु (joy) / पावा (received)॥ / बहु (much) / लालसा (longing) / कथा (story) / पर (for) / बाढ़ी (increased)॥ / नयनन्हि (in the eyes) / नीरु (water, tears) / रोमावलि (hair standing on end) / ठाढ़ी (stood up)॥
ramacharitamanas::599.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::599.essence: Love for the divine makes the body answer before words do.
ramacharitamanas::599.simple_meaning: Bharadvaja feels deep joy listening to Shiva's story. His longing grows, and his body shows signs of devotion: tears and goosebumps.
ramacharitamanas::599.simple_insight: Real devotion is not cold admiration. It stirs the body, softens the heart, and makes listening itself feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::599.detailed_meaning: In the frame story, Bharadvaja is listening as Shiva's story unfolds. The tale is so sweet to him that joy rises, longing deepens, and his body responds with tears and goosebumps. The verse shows devotion before words return.
ramacharitamanas::599.modern_relevance: You hear a song from childhood in a crowded train, and suddenly your eyes sting. Some truths are felt before they are explained — and the body knows first.
ramacharitamanas::599.insight: It shifts attention from understanding devotion intellectually to recognising devotion as a full-bodied response of love and longing.

ramacharitamanas::600.verse_sanskrit: प्रेम बिबस मुख आव न बानी। दसा देखि हरषे मुनि ग्यानी॥ अहो धन्य तब जन्मु मुनीसा। तुम्हहि प्रान सम प्रिय गौरीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::600.verse_hindi: वे प्रेम में मुग्ध हो गए, मुख से वाणी नहीं निकलती। उनकी यह दशा देखकर ज्ञानी मुनि याज्ञवल्क्य बहुत प्रसन्न हुए (और बोले-) हे मुनीश! अहा हा! तुम्हारा जन्म धन्य है, तुमको गौरीपति शिवजी प्राणों के समान प्रिय हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::600.english_translation: Overwhelmed by love, he could not speak. Seeing his state, the wise sage Yajnavalkya rejoiced. "Ah, blessed is your birth, O great sage. Shiva is dear to you as life itself."
ramacharitamanas::600.translation_literal: प्रेम (love) / बिबस (overcome) / मुख (mouth) / आव (came) / न (not) / बानी (speech) / दसा (condition) / देखि (seeing) / हरषे (rejoiced) / मुनि (sage) / ग्यानी (wise) / अहो (ah) / धन्य (blessed) / तब (your) / जन्मु (birth) / मुनीसा (O sage) / तुम्हहि (to you) / प्रान (life) / सम (like) / प्रिय (dear) / गौरीसा (Shiva, lord of Gauri)
ramacharitamanas::600.speaker: Yajnavalkya
ramacharitamanas::600.essence: Real devotion can make speech unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::600.simple_meaning: Love leaves Bharadvaj speechless, and Yajnavalkya blesses him for loving Shiva as dearly as life itself.
ramacharitamanas::600.simple_insight: Deep devotion can be so full that words fall away.
ramacharitamanas::600.detailed_meaning: Bharadvaj has just heard Shiva's story and is overwhelmed with delight. His silence is not emptiness but love. Yajnavalkya sees that response and blesses him, calling his birth fortunate because Shiva lives in his heart as dearly as life.
ramacharitamanas::600.modern_relevance: You sit quietly after hearing a song, a prayer, or a story that hits something deep. You do not need a commentary. The silence itself proves the heart has been touched.
ramacharitamanas::600.insight: It shifts the reader from speaking about devotion to recognising devotion as a living state.

ramacharitamanas::601.verse_sanskrit: सिव पद कमल जिन्हहि रति नाहीं। रामहि ते सपनेहुँ न सोहाहीं॥ बिनु छल बिस्वनाथ पद नेहू। राम भगत कर लच्छन एहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::601.verse_hindi: शिवजी के चरण कमलों में जिनकी प्रीति नहीं है, वे श्री रामचन्द्रजी को स्वप्न में भी अच्छे नहीं लगते। विश्वनाथ श्री शिवजी के चरणों में निष्कपट (विशुद्ध) प्रेम होना यही रामभक्त का लक्षण है ॥
ramacharitamanas::601.english_translation: Those who have no love for Shiva's lotus feet are not pleasing to Ram even in a dream. Pure love for Shiva's feet is the mark of Ram's devotee.
ramacharitamanas::601.translation_literal: सिव (Shiva) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / जिन्हहि (for whom) / रति (love) / नाहीं (not) / रामहि (to Ram) / ते (they) / सपनेहुँ (even in dream) / न (not) / सोहाहीं (are pleasing) / बिनु (without) / छल (deceit) / बिस्वनाथ (Lord of the universe) / पद (feet) / नेहू (love) / राम (Ram) / भगत (devotee) / कर (of) / लच्छन (mark) / एहू (this)
ramacharitamanas::601.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::601.essence: Pure love for Shiva is one sign of a heart devoted to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::601.simple_meaning: A true devotee of Ram has sincere love for Shiva as well. Without that pure devotion to Shiva, Ram does not fully accept a person.
ramacharitamanas::601.simple_insight: Devotion is not narrow. A loving heart becomes more sincere, not more divided.
ramacharitamanas::601.detailed_meaning: In Bharadvaja's conversation with Yajnavalkya, the teaching turns from Shiva's story to the nature of devotion itself. The verse says that love for Shiva and love for Ram cannot be separated; a Ram devotee is marked by pure, deceit-free reverence for Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::601.modern_relevance: You admire one teacher online, but mock the other tradition that shaped them. The verse cuts through that split: real devotion is not selective respect; it is clean, consistent reverence.
ramacharitamanas::601.insight: It shifts devotion from personal preference to a wider, cleaner loyalty that honors both Ram and Shiva.

ramacharitamanas::602.verse_sanskrit: सिव सम को रघुपति ब्रतधारी। बिनु अघ तजी सती असि नारी॥ पनु करि रघुपति भगति देखाई। को सिव सम रामहि प्रिय भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::602.verse_hindi: शिवजी के समान रघुनाथजी (की भक्ति) का व्रत धारण करने वाला कौन है? जिन्होंने बिना ही पाप के सती जैसी स्त्री को त्याग दिया और प्रतिज्ञा करके श्री रघुनाथजी की भक्ति को दिखा दिया। हे भाई! श्री रामचन्द्रजी को शिवजी के समान और कौन प्यारा है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::602.english_translation: Who keeps the vow of Raghupati like Shiva does? Who, without any fault, abandoned Sati in that way and proved devotion to Raghupati by his vow? Brother, who is as dear to Ram as Shiva?
ramacharitamanas::602.translation_literal: सिव (Shiva) / सम (like) / को (who) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / ब्रतधारी (vow-bearer) / बिनु (without) / अघ (fault) / तजी (abandoned) / सती (Sati) / असि (such) / नारी (woman) / पनु (vow) / करि (having made) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / भगति (devotion) / देखाई (showed) / को (who) / सिव (Shiva) / सम (like) / रामहि (to Ram) / प्रिय (dear) / भाई (brother)
ramacharitamanas::602.speaker: Yajnavalkya
ramacharitamanas::602.essence: Shiva’s vow-bound devotion makes him uniquely dear to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::602.simple_meaning: Shiva is held up as the greatest devotee of Ram. His vow and devotion make him uniquely dear to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::602.simple_insight: Deep devotion is not just feeling; it is loyalty that shapes every choice.
ramacharitamanas::602.detailed_meaning: Yajnavalkya is explaining Shiva’s place in Ram’s heart. After praising Shiva’s devotion, he asks who could match Shiva’s vow-bound love. The point is not comparison for its own sake, but to show how complete Shiva’s bhakti is.
ramacharitamanas::602.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone even when no one notices, and even when it costs you status. That quiet loyalty is what makes a bond unbreakable.
ramacharitamanas::602.insight: It shifts attention from public devotion to steadfast loyalty that proves itself through action.

ramacharitamanas::603.verse_sanskrit: प्रथमहिं मैं कहि सिव चरित बूझा मरमु तुम्हार। सुचि सेवक तुम्ह राम के रहित समस्त बिकार ॥
ramacharitamanas::603.verse_hindi: मैंने पहले ही शिवजी का चरित्र कहकर तुम्हारा भेद समझ लिया। तुम श्री रामचन्द्रजी के पवित्र सेवक हो और समस्त दोषों से रहित हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::603.english_translation: I have already told Shiva's story and understood your inner nature. You are a pure servant of Ram, free from all faults.
ramacharitamanas::603.translation_literal: प्रथमहिं (first) / मैं (I) / कहि (having told) / सिव चरित (Shiva's character/story) / बूझा (understood) / मरमु (inner secret / essence) / तुम्हार (your) / सुचि (pure) / सेवक (servant) / तुम्ह (you) / राम के (of Ram) / रहित (free) / समस्त (all) / बिकार (defects / impurities)
ramacharitamanas::603.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::603.essence: Pure service to Ram leaves no room for corruption.
ramacharitamanas::603.simple_meaning: Shiva says he already understands the listener's nature: the listener is a pure servant of Ram, free from faults.
ramacharitamanas::603.simple_insight: Being truly devoted changes how you are seen: your service itself becomes your identity.
ramacharitamanas::603.detailed_meaning: In the opening frame of the Ramcharitmanas, Shiva speaks to Parvati after praising Ram-bhakti. He says he has already described Shiva's story and now understands the listener's inner nature: a pure servant of Ram, untouched by impurities. This prepares the way for the story of Ram's deeds.
ramacharitamanas::603.modern_relevance: A mentor sees through your polished words and names the real thing: your character shows in what you serve. Quiet loyalty leaves a clearer mark than self-promotion ever can.
ramacharitamanas::603.insight: It shifts attention from status to devotion: what you serve reveals who you are.

ramacharitamanas::604.verse_sanskrit: मैं जाना तुम्हार गुन सीला। कहउँ सुनहु अब रघुपति लीला॥ सुनु मुनि आजु समागम तोरें। कहि न जाइ जस सुखु मन मोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::604.verse_hindi: मैंने तुम्हारा गुण और शील जान लिया। अब मैं श्री रघुनाथजी की लीला कहता हूँ, सुनो। हे मुनि! सुनो, आज तुम्हारे मिलने से मेरे मन में जो आनंद हुआ है, वह कहा नहीं जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::604.english_translation: I have understood your virtues and character. Now I will tell the play of Raghupati; listen. O sage, the joy in my mind from meeting you today cannot be spoken.
ramacharitamanas::604.translation_literal: मैं (I) / जाना (have known) / तुम्हार (your) / गुन (virtues) / सीला (character) / कहउँ (I will tell) / सुनहु (listen) / अब (now) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / लीला (play) / सुनु (listen) / मुनि (sage) / आजु (today) / समागम (meeting) / तोरें (by your) / कहि न जाइ (cannot be said) / जस (as) / सुखु (joy) / मन (mind) / मोरें (my)
ramacharitamanas::604.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::604.essence: True meeting creates joy before any words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::604.simple_meaning: The speaker recognizes the sage's character and then turns to Ram's story, saying the joy of this meeting is beyond words.
ramacharitamanas::604.simple_insight: Some meetings open the heart so fully that words fall short.
ramacharitamanas::604.detailed_meaning: The speaker has just judged the sage's purity and is now ready to continue the sacred telling. Before speaking of Ram, he pauses to honor the meeting itself, saying the joy of this encounter cannot be expressed.
ramacharitamanas::604.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence immediately feels clean and steady. Before the agenda begins, you just want to say: being with you has already changed the room.
ramacharitamanas::604.insight: It teaches you to begin sacred or important speech by acknowledging the quality of the relationship first.

ramacharitamanas::605.verse_sanskrit: राम चरित अति अमित मुनीसा। कहि न सकहिं सत कोटि अहीसा॥ तदपि जथाश्रुत कहउँ बखानी। सुमिरि गिरापति प्रभु धनुपानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::605.verse_hindi: हे मुनीश्वर! रामचरित्र अत्यन्त अपार है। सौ करोड़ शेषजी भी उसे नहीं कह सकते। तथापि जैसा मैंने सुना है, वैसा वाणी के स्वामी (प्रेरक) और हाथ में धनुष लिए हुए प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी का स्मरण करके कहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::605.english_translation: O sage, Ram’s story is immeasurable. Even a hundred million Sheshas cannot tell it fully. Still, I speak as I have heard it, remembering the Lord of speech and the Lord who holds the bow.
ramacharitamanas::605.translation_literal: राम चरित (Ram's story) / अति (extremely) / अमित (immeasurable) / मुनीसा (O sage) । / कहि न सकहिं (cannot tell) / सत कोटि (hundreds of millions) / अहीसा (Sheshas) ॥ / तदपि (still) / जथाश्रुत (as heard) / कहउँ (I speak) / बखानी (describing) । / सुमिरि (remembering) / गिरापति (lord of speech) / प्रभु (lord) / धनुपानी (bow in hand) ॥
ramacharitamanas::605.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::605.essence: Ram’s story can be spoken only through humble remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::605.simple_meaning: Ram’s story is so vast that no one can fully describe it. The speaker can only tell it as he has heard it, with reverence and memory of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::605.simple_insight: There is humility in knowing that sacred beauty exceeds your words.
ramacharitamanas::605.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses before beginning the story of Ram. He tells Parvati and the listening sage that Ram’s life is too vast for any complete telling, even for the cosmic serpent Shesha. So he speaks only as he has heard, in remembrance of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::605.modern_relevance: You try to explain a moment that changed your life, but the words keep falling short. That failure is not weakness. Some things deserve reverent telling, not tidy explanation.
ramacharitamanas::605.insight: It shifts the reader from trying to master sacred meaning to approaching it with humility and remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::606.verse_sanskrit: सारद दारुनारि सम स्वामी। रामु सूत्रधर अंतरजामी॥ जेहि पर कृपा करहिं जनु जानी। कबि उर अजिर नचावहिं बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::606.verse_hindi: सरस्वतीजी कठपुतली के समान हैं और अन्तर्यामी स्वामी श्री रामचन्द्रजी (सूत पकड़कर कठपुतली को नचाने वाले) सूत्रधार हैं। अपना भक्त जानकर जिस कवि पर वे कृपा करते हैं, उसके हृदय रूपी आँगन में सरस्वती को वे नचाया करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::606.english_translation: Saraswati is like a puppet; Ram is the inner controller who holds the strings. When he shows grace to a poet as his own, he makes her words dance in the poet's heart-courtyard.
ramacharitamanas::606.translation_literal: सारद (Saraswati) / दारुनारि (like a puppet-woman) / सम (like) / स्वामी (master) / रामु (Ram) / सूत्रधर (string-holder, puppeteer) / अंतरजामी (inner-knower)॥ / जेहि (whom) / पर (upon) / कृपा (grace) / करहिं (they do) / जनु (as if) / जानी (knowing) / कबि (poet) / उर (heart) / अजिर (courtyard) / नचावहिं (make dance) / बानी (speech)॥
ramacharitamanas::606.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::606.essence: Grace makes words move where willpower cannot.
ramacharitamanas::606.simple_meaning: Ram is the inner controller of speech and inspiration. A poet can speak beautifully only when Ram's grace makes words arise within the heart.
ramacharitamanas::606.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing creativity is received, not forced.
ramacharitamanas::606.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening his praise of Ram by admitting that even speech itself is not fully his own. Ram is the hidden controller, and when he blesses a poet, Saraswati's words begin to move in the heart like a dance. The hymn begins from humility.
ramacharitamanas::606.modern_relevance: You sit staring at a blank page, waiting for the right sentence to arrive. Then, suddenly, it does. This verse reminds you that the best words often come when ego stops gripping the wheel.
ramacharitamanas::606.insight: It shifts authorship from personal control to received grace, so speech becomes an offering rather than a performance.

ramacharitamanas::607.verse_sanskrit: प्रनवउँ सोइ कृपाल रघुनाथा। बरनउँ बिसद तासु गुन गाथा॥ परम रम्य गिरिबरु कैलासू। सदा जहाँ सिव उमा निवासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::607.verse_hindi: उन्हीं कृपालु श्री रघुनाथजी को मैं प्रणाम करता हूँ और उन्हीं के निर्मल गुणों की कथा कहता हूँ। कैलास पर्वतों में श्रेष्ठ और बहुत ही रमणीय है, जहाँ शिव-पार्वतीजी सदा निवास करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::607.english_translation: I bow to that compassionate Lord of the Raghu line and sing the spotless story of His virtues. Mount Kailash is the most beautiful of mountains, where Shiva and Uma always dwell.
ramacharitamanas::607.translation_literal: प्रनवउँ (I bow) / सोइ (that same) / कृपाल (compassionate) / रघुनाथा (Lord of the Raghu line) / बरनउँ (I describe) / बिसद (spotless, clear) / तासु (His) / गुन (virtues) / गाथा (story, hymn) / परम (supremely) / रम्य (beautiful) / गिरिबरु (best mountain) / कैलासू (Kailash) / सदा (always) / जहाँ (where) / सिव (Shiva) / उमा (Uma) / निवासू (residence, dwelling)
ramacharitamanas::607.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::607.essence: Reverence comes first; only then can the story of Ram be told.
ramacharitamanas::607.simple_meaning: Tulsidas bows to Ram and begins praising His pure qualities. He then describes Kailash as the beautiful home of Shiva and Uma.
ramacharitamanas::607.simple_insight: Praise opens the heart before the story begins.
ramacharitamanas::607.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is opening the Ramcharitmanas in his own voice. He first bows to compassionate Ram, then sets a sacred frame by describing Kailash, where Shiva and Uma dwell. The verse prepares the listener for a devotional retelling.
ramacharitamanas::607.modern_relevance: Before speaking about something sacred or important, you pause, bow inwardly, and choose reverence over haste. That changes the whole tone of what follows.
ramacharitamanas::607.insight: It teaches you to begin with humility and devotion, not self-importance.

ramacharitamanas::608.verse_sanskrit: सिद्ध तपोधन जोगिजन सुर किंनर मुनिबृंद। बसहिं तहाँ सुकृती सकल सेवहिं सिव सुखकंद ॥
ramacharitamanas::608.verse_hindi: सिद्ध, तपस्वी, योगीगण, देवता, किन्नर और मुनियों के समूह उस पर्वत पर रहते हैं। वे सब बड़े पुण्यात्मा हैं और आनंदकन्द श्री महादेवजी की सेवा करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::608.english_translation: Siddhas, ascetics, yogis, devas, kinnaras, and hosts of sages dwell there. All of them are virtuous and serve Shiva, the source of joy.
ramacharitamanas::608.translation_literal: सिद्ध (perfected beings) / तपोधन (wealthy in austerity) / जोगिजन (yogis) / सुर (devas) / किंनर (kinnaras) / मुनिबृंद (groups of sages) / बसहिं (dwell) / तहाँ (there) / सुकृती (virtuous ones) / सकल (all) / सेवहिं (serve) / सिव (Shiva) / सुखकंद (source of joy)
ramacharitamanas::608.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::608.essence: Holy places are recognized by the devotion they attract.
ramacharitamanas::608.simple_meaning: That holy mountain is home to many exalted beings, and they all serve Shiva there.
ramacharitamanas::608.simple_insight: A sacred place is defined by the quality of devotion it gathers.
ramacharitamanas::608.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing Kailash, the mountain where Shiva and Uma dwell. Siddhas, yogis, devas, kinnaras, and sages live there in purity, and their shared life is service to Shiva. The verse supports the earlier praise of Kailash before the next verse explains who can and cannot reach it.
ramacharitamanas::608.modern_relevance: A quiet place filled with sincere people feels different the moment you enter. The room itself is not the miracle; the devotion, discipline, and humility of the people there make it feel alive.
ramacharitamanas::608.insight: It shifts attention from the place alone to the character of those who are drawn to it.

ramacharitamanas::609.verse_sanskrit: हरि हर बिमुख धर्म रति नाहीं। ते नर तहँ सपनेहुँ नहिं जाहीं॥ तेहि गिरि पर बट बिटप बिसाला। नित नूतन सुंदर सब काला ॥
ramacharitamanas::609.verse_hindi: जो भगवान विष्णु और महादेवजी से विमुख हैं और जिनकी धर्म में प्रीति नहीं है, वे लोग स्वप्न में भी वहाँ नहीं जा सकते। उस पर्वत पर एक विशाल बरगद का पेड़ है, जो नित्य नवीन और सब काल (छहों ऋतुओं) में सुंदर रहता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::609.english_translation: Those who turn away from Hari and Shiva and feel no love for dharma cannot even reach that mountain in a dream. On that mountain stands a vast banyan tree, ever fresh and beautiful in every season.
ramacharitamanas::609.translation_literal: हरि (Hari) / हर (Shiva) / बिमुख (turned away) / धर्म (dharma) / रति (love, delight) / नाहीं (not) / ते (those) / नर (people) / तहँ (there) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / नहिं (not) / जाहीं (go) / तेहि (that) / गिरि (mountain) / पर (on) / बट (banyan) / बिटप (tree) / बिसाला (vast) / नित (always) / नूतन (new) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सब (all) / काला (times, seasons)
ramacharitamanas::609.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::609.essence: Only a dharmic heart can enter the sacred place.
ramacharitamanas::609.simple_meaning: Only those who love the divine and live by dharma can reach that sacred mountain. A huge banyan tree there stays fresh and beautiful in every season.
ramacharitamanas::609.simple_insight: A pure place is not entered by force; the heart must already belong there.
ramacharitamanas::609.detailed_meaning: The narration is describing Kailash, Shiva's dwelling. Tulsidas says people who turn away from Hari and Shiva and feel no love for dharma cannot even dream of reaching it. Then he turns to the mountain's beauty, especially its vast banyan tree.
ramacharitamanas::609.modern_relevance: You can walk into a temple, a retreat, or a quiet room and still remain elsewhere inside. The verse says some places are reached by the heart long before the feet arrive.
ramacharitamanas::609.insight: It shifts attention from physical access to inner fit: reverence and dharma make a person belong where they stand.

ramacharitamanas::610.verse_sanskrit: त्रिबिध समीर सुसीतलि छाया। सिव बिश्राम बिटप श्रुति गाया॥ एक बार तेहि तर प्रभु गयऊ। तरु बिलोकि उर अति सुखु भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::610.verse_hindi: वहाँ तीनों प्रकार की (शीतल, मंद और सुगंध) वायु बहती रहती है और उसकी छाया बड़ी ठंडी रहती है। वह शिवजी के विश्राम करने का वृक्ष है, जिसे वेदों ने गाया है। एक बार प्रभु श्री शिवजी उस वृक्ष के नीचे गए और उसे देखकर उनके हृदय में बहुत आनंद हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::610.english_translation: Three kinds of cool, gentle, fragrant winds blow there, and its shade is very soothing. The Vedas sing of it as Shiva's resting tree. Once, the Lord went beneath it and felt great joy at the sight of the tree.
ramacharitamanas::610.translation_literal: त्रिबिध (threefold) / समीर (wind) / सुसीतलि (very cool) / छाया (shade) / सिव (Shiva's) / बिश्राम (rest) / बिटप (tree) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / गाया (sung) ॥ एक बार (once) / तेहि (that) / तर (under) / प्रभु (the Lord) / गयऊ (went) / तरु (tree) / बिलोकि (seeing) / उर (heart) / अति (very) / सुखु (joy) / भयऊ (became) ॥
ramacharitamanas::610.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::610.essence: Even Shiva delights in a place that naturally brings rest.
ramacharitamanas::610.simple_meaning: The tree’s shade and breeze are so soothing that even Shiva rests there, and he feels joy just seeing it.
ramacharitamanas::610.simple_insight: Sacred places can feel like relief itself — a calm so deep it softens even the most elevated heart.
ramacharitamanas::610.detailed_meaning: On Mount Kailash, the poet describes a holy tree praised by the Vedas. Its cool shade and gentle air make it Shiva's resting place. Shiva comes beneath it, and simply seeing the tree fills his heart with delight.
ramacharitamanas::610.modern_relevance: You step into a quiet courtyard after a noisy commute, and your whole body loosens before anyone speaks. Some places restore you before they explain anything.
ramacharitamanas::610.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic events to the power of a pure, calming environment.

ramacharitamanas::611.verse_sanskrit: निज कर डासि नागरिपु छाला। बैठे सहजहिं संभु कृपाला॥ कुंद इंदु दर गौर सरीरा। भुज प्रलंब परिधन मुनिचीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::611.verse_hindi: अपने हाथ से बाघम्बर बिछाकर कृपालु शिवजी स्वभाव से ही (बिना किसी खास प्रयोजन के) वहाँ बैठ गए। कुंद के पुष्प, चन्द्रमा और शंख के समान उनका गौर शरीर था। बड़ी लंबी भुजाएँ थीं और वे मुनियों के से (वल्कल) वस्त्र धारण किए हुए थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::611.english_translation: Having spread the tiger-skin with his own hands, compassionate Shiva sat there naturally. His fair body shone like a jasmine flower, the moon, and a conch. His arms were long, and he wore the bark cloth of a sage.
ramacharitamanas::611.translation_literal: निज (own) / कर (hand) / डासि (spreading out) / नागरिपु (enemy of the serpent, Shiva) / छाला (tiger skin) / बैठे (sat) / सहजहिं (naturally) / संभु (Shiva) / कृपाला (compassionate) / कुंद (jasmine) / इंदु (moon) / दर (like) / गौर (fair) / सरीरा (body) / भुज (arms) / प्रलंब (long) / परिधन (garments) / मुनिचीरा (sage's bark cloth)
ramacharitamanas::611.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::611.essence: Majesty can appear as complete simplicity.
ramacharitamanas::611.simple_meaning: Shiva sits calmly on a tiger skin, with a bright fair body, long arms, and simple sage clothing.
ramacharitamanas::611.simple_insight: True greatness can sit lightly. Power does not need display.
ramacharitamanas::611.detailed_meaning: On the mountain where Shiva is resting, the poem lingers on his appearance: he lays out the tiger skin himself and sits without strain. The scene is devotional description, preparing the reader to see his calm, radiant presence before the next line turns to his feet and ornaments.
ramacharitamanas::611.modern_relevance: A person walks into a room wearing no badge of importance, yet everyone feels the steadiness. No performance, no self-importance — just quiet presence.
ramacharitamanas::611.insight: It shifts attention from status to composure, showing that dignity can be simple and unforced.

ramacharitamanas::612.verse_sanskrit: तरुन अरुन अंबुज सम चरना। नख दुति भगत हृदय तम हरना॥ भुजग भूति भूषन त्रिपुरारी। आननु सरद चंद छबि हारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::612.verse_hindi: उनके चरण नए (पूर्ण रूप से खिले हुए) लाल कमल के समान थे, नखों की ज्योति भक्तों के हृदय का अंधकार हरने वाली थी। साँप और भस्म ही उनके भूषण थे और उन त्रिपुरासुर के शत्रु शिवजी का मुख शरद (पूर्णिमा) के चन्द्रमा की शोभा को भी हरने वाला (फीकी करने वाला) था ॥
ramacharitamanas::612.english_translation: His feet were like fresh red lotuses, and the shine of his nails removed the darkness from devotees' hearts. Serpents and ash were his ornaments, and the face of Tripurari outshone even the beauty of the autumn moon.
ramacharitamanas::612.translation_literal: तरुन (fresh) / अरुन (red) / अंबुज (lotus) / सम (like) / चरना (feet) / नख (nails) / दुति (radiance) / भगत (devotees') / हृदय (heart) / तम (darkness) / हरना (removing) / भुजग (serpents) / भूति (ash) / भूषन (ornaments) / त्रिपुरारी (Tripurari, Shiva) / आननु (face) / सरद (autumn) / चंद (moon) / छबि (beauty) / हारी (outshining)
ramacharitamanas::612.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::612.essence: Shiva's beauty is measured by how it clears devotion's darkness.
ramacharitamanas::612.simple_meaning: Shiva is described as radiantly beautiful: his feet are like red lotuses, his nails dispel devotees' inner darkness, and his face surpasses the autumn moon.
ramacharitamanas::612.simple_insight: True beauty is not decoration; it clears the heart and makes reverence feel natural.
ramacharitamanas::612.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still describing Shiva resting beneath the tree. After the quiet scene-setting, he turns to Shiva's form itself: lotus-like feet, luminous nails, serpent and ash ornaments, and a face brighter than the autumn moon. The passage deepens the devotional atmosphere before the story moves on.
ramacharitamanas::612.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm changes the whole room. Nothing flashy about them — yet their presence makes your own mind feel less crowded.
ramacharitamanas::612.insight: It shifts attention from outward ornament to a presence that transforms the heart.

ramacharitamanas::613.verse_sanskrit: जटा मुकुट सुरसरित सिर लोचन नलिन बिसाल। नीलकंठ लावन्यनिधि सोह बालबिधु भाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::613.verse_hindi: उनके सिर पर जटाओं का मुकुट और गंगाजी (शोभायमान) थीं। कमल के समान बड़े-बड़े नेत्र थे। उनका नील कंठ था और वे सुंदरता के भंडार थे। उनके मस्तक पर द्वितीया का चन्द्रमा शोभित था ॥
ramacharitamanas::613.english_translation: His head bore a matted-crown, the Ganga rested there, and his eyes were vast lotuses. Blue-throated, a treasure of beauty, he shone with the crescent moon on his brow.
ramacharitamanas::613.translation_literal: जटा मुकुट (matted-crown) / सुरसरित (the heavenly river, Ganga) / सिर (head) / लोचन (eyes) / नलिन (lotus) / बिसाल (vast) / नीलकंठ (blue-throated one) / लावन्यनिधि (treasure of beauty) / सोह (shone) / बालबिधु (young moon) / भाल (forehead)
ramacharitamanas::613.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::613.essence: Beauty and stillness meet in Shiva's form.
ramacharitamanas::613.simple_meaning: Shiva is described as radiant and beautiful, with matted hair, the Ganga on his head, lotus-like eyes, a blue throat, and the crescent moon on his forehead.
ramacharitamanas::613.simple_insight: Reverence deepens when beauty and stillness are seen together.
ramacharitamanas::613.detailed_meaning: Shiva sits in the sacred scene before Parvati speaks. Tulsidas pauses to paint his form: matted hair, Ganga, lotus eyes, blue throat, crescent moon. The verse is not a teaching by itself; it prepares the devotional mood around Shiva's presence.
ramacharitamanas::613.modern_relevance: You enter a quiet temple after a long, noisy day and suddenly notice stillness has a face. Beauty feels less like decoration and more like peace made visible.
ramacharitamanas::613.insight: It shifts attention from Shiva's role in the story to his presence as a living image of calm, grace, and majesty.

ramacharitamanas::614.verse_sanskrit: बैठे सोह कामरिपु कैसें। धरें सरीरु सांतरसु जैसें॥ पारबती भल अवसरु जानी। गईं संभु पहिं मातु भवानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::614.verse_hindi: कामदेव के शत्रु शिवजी वहाँ बैठे हुए ऐसे शोभित हो रहे थे, मानो शांतरस ही शरीर धारण किए बैठा हो। अच्छा मौका जानकर शिवपत्नी माता पार्वतीजी उनके पास गईं।
ramacharitamanas::614.english_translation: Shiva, enemy of desire, sat there like peace itself taking form. Seeing the right moment, Parvati, Mother Bhavani, went to Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::614.translation_literal: बैठे (sat) / सोह (shone) / कामरिपु (enemy of desire) / कैसें (how) / धरें (holding) / सरीरु (body) / सांतरसु (peaceful essence) / जैसें (as if) || पारबती (Parvati) / भल (good) / अवसरु (opportunity) / जानी (knowing) / गईं (went) / संभु (Shiva) / पहिं (to) / मातु भवानी (Mother Bhavani)
ramacharitamanas::614.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::614.essence: Calm presence creates the opening for wisdom to begin.
ramacharitamanas::614.simple_meaning: Shiva sat in perfect calm, and Parvati approached him at the right moment.
ramacharitamanas::614.simple_insight: Stillness makes the right conversation possible.
ramacharitamanas::614.detailed_meaning: In the opening frame of the Balkand, Shiva is seated in serene composure while Parvati, noticing the fitting moment, comes to him. The scene prepares the sacred dialogue that will unfold between them.
ramacharitamanas::614.modern_relevance: You finally catch someone after their phone is off and the room is quiet. The hard conversation lands because the moment is open, not forced.
ramacharitamanas::614.insight: It shifts attention from forcing speech to waiting for the right opening.

ramacharitamanas::615.verse_sanskrit: जानि प्रिया आदरु अति कीन्हा। बाम भाग आसनु हर दीन्हा॥ बैठीं सिव समीप हरषाई। पूरुब जन्म कथा चित आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::615.verse_hindi: अपनी प्यारी पत्नी जानकार शिवजी ने उनका बहुत आदर-सत्कार किया और अपनी बायीं ओर बैठने के लिए आसन दिया। पार्वतीजी प्रसन्न होकर शिवजी के पास बैठ गईं। उन्हें पिछले जन्म की कथा स्मरण हो आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::615.english_translation: Knowing her as his beloved, Shiva showed her great respect and gave her a seat on his left side. Parvati sat near Shiva, delighted, and the memory of her previous birth came to her mind.
ramacharitamanas::615.translation_literal: जानि (knowing) / प्रिया (beloved) / आदरु (respect) / अति (very) / कीन्हा (did) / बाम (left) / भाग (side) / आसनु (seat) / हर (Shiva) / दीन्हा (gave) / बैठीं (sat) / सिव (Shiva) / समीप (near) / हरषाई (delighted) / पूरुब (previous) / जन्म (birth) / कथा (story) / चित (mind) / आई (came)
ramacharitamanas::615.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::615.essence: Respect creates the opening where remembrance returns.
ramacharitamanas::615.simple_meaning: Shiva welcomes Parvati with great honor and gives her a seat beside him. As she sits happily near him, she remembers the story of her earlier birth.
ramacharitamanas::615.simple_insight: Love makes room. Respect opens the way for deeper remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::615.detailed_meaning: Shiva is seated in calm radiance when Parvati comes to him. He honors her fully and seats her beside him. That tenderness awakens her memory of her former birth, preparing the next part of their sacred conversation.
ramacharitamanas::615.modern_relevance: Someone makes space for you in a crowded room without being asked. That small gesture softens you, and an old memory or feeling suddenly rises to the surface.
ramacharitamanas::615.insight: It shows how reverent welcome can open the mind to deeper remembrance and inquiry.

ramacharitamanas::616.verse_sanskrit: पति हियँ हेतु अधिक अनुमानी। बिहसि उमा बोलीं प्रिय बानी॥ कथा जो सकल लोक हितकारी। सोइ पूछन चह सैल कुमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::616.verse_hindi: स्वामी के हृदय में (अपने ऊपर पहले की अपेक्षा) अधिक प्रेम समझकर पार्वतीजी हँसकर प्रिय वचन बोलीं। (याज्ञवल्क्यजी कहते हैं कि) जो कथा सब लोगों का हित करने वाली है, उसे ही पार्वतीजी पूछना चाहती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::616.english_translation: Seeing that her husband held her in even greater affection, Uma smiled and spoke sweetly. "I wish to ask about the story that brings benefit to all beings, daughter of the mountain."
ramacharitamanas::616.translation_literal: पति (husband) / हियँ (in the heart) / हेतु (love) / अधिक (more) / अनुमानी (having understood) / बिहसि (smiling) / उमा (Uma) / बोलीं (spoke) / प्रिय (sweet) / बानी (words)॥ कथा (story) / जो (which) / सकल (all) / लोक (worlds/people) / हितकारी (beneficial) / सोइ (that very) / पूछन (to ask) / चह (wants) / सैल (mountain) / कुमारी (daughter) ॥
ramacharitamanas::616.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::616.essence: A loving question can open the door to a teaching that benefits all.
ramacharitamanas::616.simple_meaning: Parvati smiles and asks to hear the story that benefits everyone. Her question opens the deeper teaching that follows.
ramacharitamanas::616.simple_insight: Curiosity can be loving, not just intellectual. A sincere question can open the door to wisdom for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::616.detailed_meaning: Shiva has welcomed Parvati beside him, and she notices his special affection. Smiling, she says she wants to hear only the story that helps all beings. This gentle question sets up the sacred teaching that follows.
ramacharitamanas::616.modern_relevance: At a family dinner, someone asks the one question that matters instead of filling the room with small talk. That single honest question changes the whole conversation.
ramacharitamanas::616.insight: It shifts attention from casual chatter to the question that can help everyone.

ramacharitamanas::617.verse_sanskrit: बिस्वनाथ मम नाथ पुरारी। त्रिभुवन महिमा बिदित तुम्हारी॥ चर अरु अचर नाग नर देवा। सकल करहिं पद पंकज सेवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::617.verse_hindi: (पार्वतीजी ने कहा-) हे संसार के स्वामी! हे मेरे नाथ! हे त्रिपुरासुर का वध करने वाले! आपकी महिमा तीनों लोकों में विख्यात है। चर, अचर, नाग, मनुष्य और देवता सभी आपके चरण कमलों की सेवा करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::617.english_translation: O Lord of the universe, my Lord, destroyer of Tripura, your glory is known in all three worlds. Moving and unmoving beings, serpents, humans, and radiant beings all serve your lotus feet.
ramacharitamanas::617.translation_literal: बिस्वनाथ (lord of the universe) / मम (my) / नाथ (lord) / पुरारी (destroyer of Tripura) / त्रिभुवन (three worlds) / महिमा (glory) / बिदित (known) / तुम्हारी (your) / चर (moving beings) / अरु (and) / अचर (unmoving beings) / नाग (serpents) / नर (humans) / देवा (radiant beings) / सकल (all) / करहिं (do) / पद पंकज (lotus feet) / सेवा (service)
ramacharitamanas::617.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::617.essence: True greatness draws every being into service.
ramacharitamanas::617.simple_meaning: Parvati praises Shiva as the lord of all worlds and says every kind of being serves his feet.
ramacharitamanas::617.simple_insight: Reverence becomes natural when greatness is seen clearly.
ramacharitamanas::617.detailed_meaning: Parvati, warmed by Shiva's welcome, turns from curiosity to praise. She names him lord of the universe, destroyer of Tripura, and says that every kind of being in creation serves his feet. This is devotion recognizing cosmic greatness.
ramacharitamanas::617.modern_relevance: You meet someone who carries quiet authority, and the room changes without anyone speaking. Respect rises on its own because the person’s presence makes ego feel small.
ramacharitamanas::617.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to reverent recognition of what is greater.

ramacharitamanas::618.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु समरथ सर्बग्य सिव सकल कला गुन धाम। जोग ग्यान बैराग्य निधि प्रनत कलपतरु नाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::618.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! आप समर्थ, सर्वज्ञ और कल्याणस्वरूप हैं। सब कलाओं और गुणों के निधान हैं और योग, ज्ञान तथा वैराग्य के भंडार हैं। आपका नाम शरणागतों के लिए कल्पवृक्ष है ॥
ramacharitamanas::618.english_translation: O Lord, you are mighty, all-knowing, the source of every art and virtue. You are the treasury of yoga, wisdom, and detachment, and your name is a wish-fulfilling tree for those who seek refuge.
ramacharitamanas::618.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / समरथ (mighty, capable) / सर्बग्य (all-knowing) / सिव (auspicious) / सकल (all) / कला (arts) / गुन (virtues) / धाम (abode, treasury) / जोग (yoga) / ग्यान (wisdom) / बैराग्य (detachment) / निधि (treasury) / प्रनत (for the surrendered) / कलपतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / नाम (name)
ramacharitamanas::618.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::618.essence: Ram contains every virtue, and his name shelters the surrendered.
ramacharitamanas::618.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as all-powerful, all-knowing, and full of every virtue. His name itself grants refuge to anyone who turns to him.
ramacharitamanas::618.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing you do not need to earn refuge; you can simply turn and be held.
ramacharitamanas::618.detailed_meaning: Parvati is listening to Shiva describe Ram’s greatness and responds with reverence. She praises Ram as the source of all skill, virtue, yoga, wisdom, and detachment, then names his very name as a wish-fulfilling refuge for anyone who surrenders.
ramacharitamanas::618.modern_relevance: You are exhausted, and the phone is full of advice, fixes, and noise. One steady name, one trusted presence, can feel like the first place your mind finally rests.
ramacharitamanas::618.insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to refuge: not just praising Ram, but relying on his name as shelter.

ramacharitamanas::619.verse_sanskrit: जौं मो पर प्रसन्न सुखरासी। जानिअ सत्य मोहि निज दासी॥ तौ प्रभु हरहु मोर अग्याना। कहि रघुनाथ कथा बिधि नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::619.verse_hindi: हे सुख की राशि ! यदि आप मुझ पर प्रसन्न हैं और सचमुच मुझे अपनी दासी (या अपनी सच्ची दासी) जानते हैं, तो हे प्रभो! आप श्री रघुनाथजी की नाना प्रकार की कथा कहकर मेरा अज्ञान दूर कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::619.english_translation: If you are pleased with me and truly know me as your own servant, then, Lord, remove my ignorance by telling me the many stories of Raghunath.
ramacharitamanas::619.translation_literal: जौं (if) / मो पर (on me) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / सुखरासी (storehouse of joy) / जानिअ (know) / सत्य (truly) / मोहि (me) / निज (own) / दासी (servant) / तौ (then) / प्रभु (Lord) / हरहु (remove) / मोर (my) / अग्याना (ignorance) / कहि (tell) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / कथा (stories) / बिधि नाना (many kinds)
ramacharitamanas::619.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::619.essence: Humility opens the door to wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::619.simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to treat her as his own devoted servant and remove her ignorance by speaking the many stories of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::619.simple_insight: Real learning begins with humility: ask to be taught, not to seem wise.
ramacharitamanas::619.detailed_meaning: Parvati has been listening to Shiva’s praise of Ram and now asks for more. She says that if Shiva truly loves and accepts her, he should erase her ignorance by narrating Ram’s many stories. The verse opens the next teaching through her humble request.
ramacharitamanas::619.modern_relevance: You sit with someone who knows more than you and stop pretending. Instead of performing understanding, you ask the real question that clears the fog.
ramacharitamanas::619.insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to sincere asking, making room for understanding to enter.

ramacharitamanas::620.verse_sanskrit: जासु भवनु सुरतरु तर होई। सहि कि दरिद्र जनित दुखु सोई॥ ससिभूषन अस हृदयँ बिचारी। हरहु नाथ मम मति भ्रम भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::620.verse_hindi: जिसका घर कल्पवृक्ष के नीचे हो, वह भला दरिद्रता से उत्पन्न दुःख को क्यों सहेगा? हे शशिभूषण! हे नाथ! हृदय में ऐसा विचार कर मेरी बुद्धि के भारी भ्रम को दूर कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::620.english_translation: How can one whose home is beneath the wish-fulfilling tree endure the suffering born of poverty? O Shashibhushan, O Lord, consider this in your heart and remove the great confusion of my mind.
ramacharitamanas::620.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / भवनु (home) / सुरतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / तर (beneath) / होई (is) / सहि (endure) / कि (whether) / दरिद्र (poverty) / जनित (born of) / दुखु (suffering) / सोई (that) / ससिभूषन (Shashibhushan) / अस (thus) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारी (considering) / हरहु (remove) / नाथ (Lord) / मम (my) / मति (mind) / भ्रम (confusion) / भारी (heavy)
ramacharitamanas::620.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::620.essence: Abundance makes poverty's fear look absurd.
ramacharitamanas::620.simple_meaning: A person sheltered by abundance should not suffer the pain of poverty. The speaker asks the Lord to think this way and remove the heavy confusion from his mind.
ramacharitamanas::620.simple_insight: When the heart is already full, fear of lack starts to look unreal.
ramacharitamanas::620.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still speaking to Ram in the opening Balkand frame, after praising Him as all-powerful and the source of every good quality. He now asks Ram to clear his mind, using the image of a home beneath a wish-fulfilling tree: how could such a person remain burdened by poverty?
ramacharitamanas::620.modern_relevance: You have food in the fridge, rent paid, and still panic when the savings dip. The mind keeps inventing scarcity even in the middle of enough.
ramacharitamanas::620.insight: It shifts attention from external lack to the mind's habit of magnifying fear.

ramacharitamanas::621.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु जे मुनि परमारथबादी। कहहिं राम कहुँ ब्रह्म अनादी॥ सेस सारदा बेद पुराना। सकल करहिं रघुपति गुन गाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::621.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! जो परमार्थतत्व (ब्रह्म) के ज्ञाता और वक्ता मुनि हैं, वे श्री रामचन्द्रजी को अनादि ब्रह्म कहते हैं और शेष, सरस्वती, वेद और पुराण सभी श्री रघुनाथजी का गुण गाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::621.english_translation: O Lord, the sages who speak of the highest reality call Ram the beginningless supreme reality. Shesha, Saraswati, the Vedas, and the Puranas all sing the praises of Raghupati.
ramacharitamanas::621.translation_literal: प्रभु (O Lord) / जे (who) / मुनि (sages) / परमारथबादी (speaking of the highest reality) / कहहिं (call) / राम (Ram) / कहुँ (as) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / अनादी (beginningless) / सेस (Shesha) / सारदा (Saraswati) / बेद (Vedas) / पुराना (Puranas) / सकल (all) / करहिं (do) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / गुन (qualities) / गाना (singing)
ramacharitamanas::621.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::621.essence: Ram stands as the beginningless reality all sacred voices praise.
ramacharitamanas::621.simple_meaning: Wise sages call Ram the beginningless supreme reality, and every sacred source keeps praising him.
ramacharitamanas::621.simple_insight: It brings reverence and wonder: the highest truth is not distant; it is already being sung everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::621.detailed_meaning: In the middle of a devotional appeal, the speaker turns to the deepest claim available: the sages of insight call Ram beginningless and supreme. Even Shesha, Saraswati, the Vedas, and the Puranas are shown as praising him.
ramacharitamanas::621.modern_relevance: You hear a chant in a temple, a verse in a book, and a line from a teacher — all pointing the same way. The mind relaxes when it sees that the deepest truth is being echoed everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::621.insight: It shifts the mind from treating Ram as a local deity to recognising him as the ground of all sacred speech.

ramacharitamanas::622.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह पुनि राम राम दिन राती। सादर जपहु अनँग आराती॥ रामु सो अवध नृपति सुत सोई। की अज अगुन अलखगति कोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::622.verse_hindi: और हे कामदेव के शत्रु! आप भी दिन-रात आदरपूर्वक राम-राम जपा करते हैं- ये राम वही अयोध्या के राजा के पुत्र हैं? या अजन्मे, निर्गुण और अगोचर कोई और राम हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::622.english_translation: And you, enemy of desire, also chant Ram's name day and night with reverence. Is Ram the prince of Ayodhya, or some unborn, attribute-free, ungraspable reality?
ramacharitamanas::622.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / पुनि (also) / राम (Ram) / राम (Ram) / दिन राती (day and night) / सादर (with reverence) / जपहु (chant) / अनँग आराती (enemy of desire) / रामु (Ram) / सो (that) / अवध (Ayodhya) / नृपति (king) / सुत (son) / सोई (that very) / की (or) / अज (unborn) / अगुन (without qualities) / अलखगति (ungraspable state) / कोई (some one / some other)
ramacharitamanas::622.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::622.essence: Ram is both the prince and the unborn reality.
ramacharitamanas::622.simple_meaning: Shiva says that even the destroyer of desire chants Ram's name constantly, then asks whether Ram is only Dasharath's son or the unborn, attribute-free reality itself.
ramacharitamanas::622.simple_insight: The name points beyond the person. Reverence deepens into wonder.
ramacharitamanas::622.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, Shiva speaks to Parvati while unfolding Ram's greatness. He points to the strange fact that even Kama's enemy chants Ram's name constantly, then opens the central question: is Ram merely the prince of Ayodhya, or the unborn, formless reality behind all form?
ramacharitamanas::622.modern_relevance: You hear a name repeated so often in a prayer hall that it stops sounding like a name and starts feeling like a presence. Then one question arrives: are you remembering a person, or touching something far larger?
ramacharitamanas::622.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as only a historical figure to recognising his divine reality.

ramacharitamanas::623.verse_sanskrit: जौं नृप तनय त ब्रह्म किमि नारि बिरहँ मति भोरि। देखि चरित महिमा सुनत भ्रमति बुद्धि अति मोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::623.verse_hindi: यदि वे राजपुत्र हैं तो ब्रह्म कैसे? (और यदि ब्रह्म हैं तो) स्त्री के विरह में उनकी मति बावली कैसे हो गई? इधर उनके ऐसे चरित्र देखकर और उधर उनकी महिमा सुनकर मेरी बुद्धि अत्यन्त चकरा रही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::623.english_translation: If they are a prince, how can they be Brahman? And if they are Brahman, how can their mind be so bewildered by separation from a woman? Seeing their conduct and hearing their glory, my understanding is utterly confused.
ramacharitamanas::623.translation_literal: जौं (if) / नृप-तनय (king's son, prince) / त (then) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / किमि (how) / नारि-बिरहँ (in woman's separation) / मति (mind) / भोरि (bewildered) / देखि (seeing) / चरित (conduct) / महिमा (glory) / सुनत (hearing) / भ्रमति (wanders/confused) / बुद्धि (intellect) / अति (very) / मोरि (my)
ramacharitamanas::623.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::623.essence: Greatness can look human, and human feeling can hide greatness.
ramacharitamanas::623.simple_meaning: Parvati is confused by Ram's human-like actions and divine glory. She cannot reconcile his royal life, his grief in separation, and his supreme nature.
ramacharitamanas::623.simple_insight: It is okay to question what does not yet fit together. Honest confusion can open the door to deeper seeing.
ramacharitamanas::623.detailed_meaning: Parvati has heard Shiva praise Ram as the unborn supreme reality, yet she sees Ram acting like a grieving human prince. Caught between his divine greatness and his tender conduct, she admits her mind cannot yet hold both truths.
ramacharitamanas::623.modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems ordinary in one moment and astonishingly wise in another. Their contradictions unsettle you, but that discomfort can become the beginning of real understanding.
ramacharitamanas::623.insight: It shifts the mind from quick labels to patient questioning, so deeper meaning can emerge.

ramacharitamanas::624.verse_sanskrit: जौं अनीह ब्यापक बिभु कोऊ। कहहु बुझाइ नाथ मोहि सोऊ॥ अग्य जानि रिस उर जनि धरहू। जेहि बिधि मोह मिटै सोइ करहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::624.verse_hindi: यदि इच्छारहित, व्यापक, समर्थ ब्रह्म कोई और हैं, तो हे नाथ! मुझे उसे समझाकर कहिए। मुझे नादान समझकर मन में क्रोध न लाइए। जिस तरह मेरा मोह दूर हो, वही कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::624.english_translation: If some other desireless, all-pervading, mighty supreme reality exists, then, Lord, explain that to me. Do not grow angry, thinking me ignorant. Do whatever removes my delusion.
ramacharitamanas::624.translation_literal: जौं (if) / अनीह (desireless) / ब्यापक (all-pervading) / बिभु (mighty, supreme) / कोऊ (someone) / कहहु (please say) / बुझाइ (explaining) / नाथ (Lord) / मोहि (to me) / सोऊ (that one) / अग्य (ignorant) / जानि (knowing) / रिस (anger) / उर (in the heart) / जनि (do not) / धरहू (keep) / जेहि (by which) / बिधि (way) / मोह (delusion) / मिटै (is removed) / सोइ (that only) / करहू (do)
ramacharitamanas::624.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::624.essence: Honest questioning is the doorway through which delusion leaves.
ramacharitamanas::624.simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to explain the idea of a desireless, all-pervading supreme reality. She asks him not to be offended by her confusion and to answer in whatever way removes her delusion.
ramacharitamanas::624.simple_insight: Real understanding begins with honest questioning, not pretending to know.
ramacharitamanas::624.detailed_meaning: In Shiva’s teaching to Parvati, the conversation has reached a careful test. Parvati is not rejecting the idea; she is asking for clarity. She wants Shiva to explain how the supreme reality can be desireless, all-pervading, and yet still relatable to human experience.
ramacharitamanas::624.modern_relevance: You are in a late-night conversation with someone wiser than you, and your questions feel clumsy. Instead of nodding along, you finally ask the thing that actually matters: explain it so the confusion can leave.
ramacharitamanas::624.insight: It shifts the mind from passive listening to fearless inquiry for the sake of clear seeing.

ramacharitamanas::625.verse_sanskrit: मैं बन दीखि राम प्रभुताई। अति भय बिकल न तुम्हहि सुनाई॥ तदपि मलिन मन बोधु न आवा। सो फलु भली भाँति हम पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::625.verse_hindi: मैंने (पिछले जन्म में) वन में श्री रामचन्द्रजी की प्रभुता देखी थी, परन्तु अत्यन्त भयभीत होने के कारण मैंने वह बात आपको सुनाई नहीं। तो भी मेरे मलिन मन को बोध न हुआ। उसका फल भी मैंने अच्छी तरह पा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::625.english_translation: I saw Ram's majesty in the forest before, but fear kept me from telling you. Even so, my impure mind did not awaken. I received the full fruit of that.
