ramacharitamanas::625.translation_literal: मैं (I) / बन (forest) / दीखि (saw) / राम प्रभुताई (Ram's majesty) / अति (very) / भय (fear) / बिकल (agitated) / न (not) / तुम्हहि (to you) / सुनाई (told) / तदपि (even so) / मलिन (impure) / मन (mind) / बोधु (awakening) / न (not) / आवा (came) / सो (that) / फलु (fruit/result) / भली भाँति (well) / हम (we/I) / पावा (received)
ramacharitamanas::625.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::625.essence: Fear can silence truth, but confusion still bears its own fruit.
ramacharitamanas::625.simple_meaning: Parvati says she once saw Ram's greatness in the forest, but fear stopped her from speaking. Because her mind remained unclear, she suffered the result of that confusion.
ramacharitamanas::625.simple_insight: Hidden fear can block understanding, even when the truth is already seen.
ramacharitamanas::625.detailed_meaning: Parvati is still asking Shiva about Ram's strange human-like actions. She admits that she once saw Ram's majesty in the forest but was too frightened to speak clearly. Her own clouded mind kept her from fully understanding, and that confusion brought its own pain.
ramacharitamanas::625.modern_relevance: You notice the right answer in a tense meeting, but fear of looking foolish keeps you silent. Later, the missed moment weighs on you more than speaking ever would have.
ramacharitamanas::625.insight: It shifts the mind from passive seeing to honest recognition. Fear may block insight, but unspoken truth still shapes the result.

ramacharitamanas::626.verse_sanskrit: अजहूँ कछु संसउ मन मोरें। करहु कृपा बिनवउँ कर जोरें॥ प्रभु तब मोहि बहु भाँति प्रबोधा। नाथ सो समुझि करहु जनि क्रोधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::626.verse_hindi: अब भी मेरे मन में कुछ संदेह है। आप कृपा कीजिए, मैं हाथ जोड़कर विनती करती हूँ। हे प्रभो! आपने उस समय मुझे बहुत तरह से समझाया था (फिर भी मेरा संदेह नहीं गया), हे नाथ! यह सोचकर मुझ पर क्रोध न कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::626.english_translation: I still have some doubt in my mind. Please show me kindness; I bow with folded hands. Lord, you explained it to me in many ways before, but do not be angry with me for still not understanding.
ramacharitamanas::626.translation_literal: अजहूँ (still now) / कछु (some) / संसउ (doubt) / मन (mind) / मोरें (in my) / करहु (do) / कृपा (kindness) / बिनवउँ (I request) / कर (hands) / जोरें (folded together) / प्रभु (Lord) / तब (then) / मोहि (me) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / प्रबोधा (you instructed) / नाथ (Lord) / सो (that) / समुझि (understanding) / करहु (do) / जनि (do not) / क्रोधा (anger)
ramacharitamanas::626.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::626.essence: Doubt can be sacred when it is asked with humility.
ramacharitamanas::626.simple_meaning: Parvati still has a doubt and asks Shiva to explain again without anger. She is humble, honest, and still searching for understanding.
ramacharitamanas::626.simple_insight: Real learning can include repeated questions. Humility keeps the door open when understanding is not yet complete.
ramacharitamanas::626.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, Parvati is still not fully satisfied with Shiva's explanation. She folds her hands and asks him not to be angry, because she wants the truth clearly enough to let her doubt dissolve.
ramacharitamanas::626.modern_relevance: You replay the conversation after everyone leaves the room, still unsure what was really meant. Instead of pretending you understood, you ask again with humility.
ramacharitamanas::626.insight: It normalizes honest questioning and shows that clarity can require patient, respectful repetition.

ramacharitamanas::627.verse_sanskrit: तब कर अस बिमोह अब नाहीं। रामकथा पर रुचि मन माहीं॥ कहहु पुनीत राम गुन गाथा। भुजगराज भूषन सुरनाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::627.verse_hindi: मुझे अब पहले जैसा मोह नहीं है, अब तो मेरे मन में रामकथा सुनने की रुचि है। हे शेषनाग को अलंकार रूप में धारण करने वाले देवताओं के नाथ! आप श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुणों की पवित्र कथा कहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::627.english_translation: I am no longer deluded as before. My mind now longs to hear Ram's story. Please tell the pure tale of Ram's virtues, O ornament of Shesha and lord of the radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::627.translation_literal: तब (then) / कर (of doing) / अस (such) / बिमोह (delusion) / अब (now) / नाहीं (not) / रामकथा (story of Ram) / पर (toward) / रुचि (interest, taste) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in)॥ कहहु (tell) / पुनीत (pure) / राम (Ram) / गुन (virtues) / गाथा (song, tale) / भुजगराज (king of serpents, Shesha) / भूषन (ornament) / सुरनाथा (lord of radiant beings)
ramacharitamanas::627.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::627.essence: Clear seeing turns the mind toward Ram's story.
ramacharitamanas::627.simple_meaning: Parvati says her confusion has cleared, and now she wants to hear Ram's story and virtues with a pure mind.
ramacharitamanas::627.simple_insight: Clarity changes what the heart wants. Once confusion falls away, devotion becomes the natural hunger.
ramacharitamanas::627.detailed_meaning: Parvati has already admitted doubt and received explanation from Shiva. Now she says the old confusion is gone, and her mind has turned toward Ram's story. This is the moment when curiosity becomes devotion.
ramacharitamanas::627.modern_relevance: After a long argument, you finally stop defending yourself and ask for the real story. The noise has dropped away. What you want now is something true enough to settle the mind.
ramacharitamanas::627.insight: It shifts attention from confusion to receptive listening, showing that devotion begins when the mind is ready to hear.

ramacharitamanas::628.verse_sanskrit: बंदउँ पद धरि धरनि सिरु बिनय करउँ कर जोरि। बरनहु रघुबर बिसद जसु श्रुति सिद्धांत निचोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::628.verse_hindi: मैं पृथ्वी पर सिर टेककर आपके चरणों की वंदना करती हूँ और हाथ जोड़कर विनती करती हूँ। आप वेदों के सिद्धांत को निचोड़कर श्री रघुनाथजी का निर्मल यश वर्णन कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::628.english_translation: I bow with my head to the earth and join my hands in prayer. Please describe the pure glory of Raghubar, distilled from the essence of the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::628.translation_literal: बंदउँ (I bow) / पद धरि (placing [my] feet) / धरनि सिरु (head on the earth) / बिनय करउँ (I make a request) / कर जोरि (with joined hands) / बरनहु (describe) / रघुबर (Raghubar) / बिसद जसु (pure glory) / श्रुति (Vedas) / सिद्धांत (essence) / निचोरि (having squeezed out)
ramacharitamanas::628.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::628.essence: Humility opens the way to hearing Ram clearly.
ramacharitamanas::628.simple_meaning: Parvati bows respectfully and asks Shiva to describe Ram's pure glory, distilled from the essence of the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::628.simple_insight: Real devotion begins by bowing low enough to ask with sincerity.
ramacharitamanas::628.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, Parvati has already expressed lingering doubt and renewed interest in Ram-katha. Now she bows in humility before Shiva and asks him to speak only of Ram's spotless glory, drawn from the deepest Vedic essence.
ramacharitamanas::628.modern_relevance: You finally ask the teacher the question you were afraid to ask. Pride drops, and real learning begins the moment you stop performing certainty.
ramacharitamanas::628.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to receptive listening before sacred truth.

ramacharitamanas::629.verse_sanskrit: जदपि जोषिता नहिं अधिकारी। दासी मन क्रम बचन तुम्हारी॥ गूढ़उ तत्त्व न साधु दुरावहिं। आरत अधिकारी जहँ पावहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::629.verse_hindi: यद्यपि स्त्री होने के कारण मैं उसे सुनने की अधिकारिणी नहीं हूँ, तथापि मैं मन, वचन और कर्म से आपकी दासी हूँ। संत लोग जहाँ आर्त अधिकारी पाते हैं, वहाँ गूढ़ तत्त्व भी उससे नहीं छिपाते ॥
ramacharitamanas::629.english_translation: Although I am not formally qualified to hear it as a woman, I am your servant in mind, deed, and speech. Wise people do not hide even the deepest truth from one who is truly distressed.
ramacharitamanas::629.translation_literal: जदपि (although) / जोषिता (woman) / नहिं (not) / अधिकारी (qualified) / दासी (servant) / मन (mind) / क्रम (action) / बचन (speech) / तुम्हारी (your) / गूढ़उ (even hidden) / तत्त्व (truth) / न (not) / साधु (the wise) / दुरावहिं (hide) / आरत (distressed) / अधिकारी (fit one) / जहँ (where) / पावहिं (find) /
ramacharitamanas::629.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::629.essence: Sincere need can qualify a person for hidden truth.
ramacharitamanas::629.simple_meaning: Parvati says she may not be formally qualified, but her devotion makes her worthy. She asks that even the deepest truth be shared with someone who is sincerely distressed.
ramacharitamanas::629.simple_insight: Humility and sincere need matter more than status. Honest longing can bring the guidance that pride cannot reach.
ramacharitamanas::629.detailed_meaning: In Shiva's outer-frame telling, Parvati lowers herself completely before the teacher. She says she is only a servant in mind, action, and speech, yet she asks for the hidden truth because true distress makes a listener worthy of mercy.
ramacharitamanas::629.modern_relevance: You sit in a quiet room after a breakup, finally admitting you do not understand what happened. The bravado is gone. This verse says honest need can unlock the answer.
ramacharitamanas::629.insight: It shifts the mind from entitlement to receptivity, showing that humility invites deeper teaching.

ramacharitamanas::630.verse_sanskrit: अति आरति पूछउँ सुरराया। रघुपति कथा कहहु करि दाया॥ प्रथम सो कारन कहहु बिचारी। निर्गुन ब्रह्म सगुन बपु धारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::630.verse_hindi: हे देवताओं के स्वामी! मैं बहुत ही आर्तभाव (दीनता) से पूछती हूँ, आप मुझ पर दया करके श्री रघुनाथजी की कथा कहिए। पहले तो वह कारण विचारकर बतलाइए, जिससे निर्गुण ब्रह्म सगुण रूप धारण करता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::630.english_translation: O lord of the devas, I ask with deep humility: please, out of compassion, tell the story of Raghupati. First, reflect and explain the reason why the formless supreme reality takes a manifest form.
ramacharitamanas::630.translation_literal: अति (very) / आरति (distress) / पूछउँ (I ask) / सुरराया (lord of the devas) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / कथा (story) / कहहु (tell) / करि (doing) / दाया (compassion) / प्रथम (first) / सो (that) / कारन (reason) / कहहु (tell) / बिचारी (having considered) / निर्गुन (without qualities) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / सगुन (with qualities) / बपु (form/body) / धारी (having taken)
ramacharitamanas::630.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::630.essence: The deepest question is why the formless becomes visible.
ramacharitamanas::630.simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to tell Ram's story and explain why the formless supreme reality appears in a visible form.
ramacharitamanas::630.simple_insight: Curiosity becomes devotion when it asks not just who Ram is, but why the infinite becomes personal.
ramacharitamanas::630.detailed_meaning: Parvati, speaking from reverence and longing, asks Shiva to explain Ram's story. She goes deeper than biography and asks the central mystery of the text: why the formless supreme reality takes on a manifest form for the world.
ramacharitamanas::630.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence feels larger than their body, and you want to know what makes them so real. This verse names that hunger: not just to admire, but to understand the mystery behind the appearance.
ramacharitamanas::630.insight: It shifts the mind from surface story to the deeper question of why the divine becomes approachable.

ramacharitamanas::631.verse_sanskrit: पुनि प्रभु कहहु राम अवतारा। बालचरित पुनि कहहु उदारा॥ कहहु जथा जानकी बिबाहीं। राज तजा सो दूषन काहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::631.verse_hindi: फिर हे प्रभु! श्री रामचन्द्रजी के अवतार (जन्म) की कथा कहिए तथा उनका उदार बाल चरित्र कहिए। फिर जिस प्रकार उन्होंने श्री जानकीजी से विवाह किया, वह कथा कहिए और फिर यह बतलाइए कि उन्होंने जो राज्य छोड़ा, सो किस दोष से ॥
ramacharitamanas::631.english_translation: Then, Lord, tell of Ram’s descent, and then his noble childhood. Tell how Janaki was married, and then explain by what fault he gave up the kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::631.translation_literal: पुनि (then again) / प्रभु (Lord) / कहहु (tell) / राम (Ram) / अवतारा (descent/incarnation) / बालचरित (childhood deeds) / पुनि (again) / कहहु (tell) / उदारा (noble) / कहहु (tell) / जथा (how) / जानकी (Janaki) / बिबाहीं (was married) / राज (kingdom) / तजा (gave up) / सो (that) / दूषन (fault) / काहीं (by what)
ramacharitamanas::631.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::631.essence: A true story is understood by its whole arc, not one event.
ramacharitamanas::631.simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to continue the story: Ram’s birth, his childhood, Sita’s marriage, and why he left the kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::631.simple_insight: The heart wants the whole story, not just the ending.
ramacharitamanas::631.detailed_meaning: Parvati is listening to Shiva’s telling of Ram’s life and asks him to move step by step through the great turning points: Ram’s descent, his gentle childhood, Sita’s marriage, and the reason he renounced the throne. The verse gathers the whole arc before the exile story unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::631.modern_relevance: A child asks, “Tell me everything from the beginning.” You realize the hardest moments in a life only make sense when you see the full chain, not one painful scene cut loose from the rest.
ramacharitamanas::631.insight: It invites the listener to follow Ram’s life as a complete arc, not isolated events.

ramacharitamanas::632.verse_sanskrit: बन बसि कीन्हे चरित अपारा। कहहु नाथ जिमि रावन मारा॥ राज बैठि कीन्हीं बहु लीला। सकल कहहु संकर सुखसीला ॥
ramacharitamanas::632.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! फिर उन्होंने वन में रहकर जो अपार चरित्र किए तथा जिस तरह रावण को मारा, वह कहिए। हे सुखस्वरूप शंकर! फिर आप उन सारी लीलाओं को कहिए जो उन्होंने राज्य (सिंहासन) पर बैठकर की थीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::632.english_translation: O Lord, tell how He lived in the forest and how Ravana was slain. O blissful Shiva, tell all the deeds He performed while seated on the throne.
ramacharitamanas::632.translation_literal: बन (forest) / बसि (living) / कीन्हे (did) / चरित (deeds, conduct) / अपारा (boundless) / कहहु (tell) / नाथ (Lord) / जिमि (how) / रावन (Ravana) / मारा (was slain) / राज (kingdom, throne) / बैठि (sitting) / कीन्हीं (did) / बहु (many) / लीला (divine deeds) / सकल (all) / कहहु (tell) / संकर (Shiva) / सुखसीला (of gentle blissful nature)
ramacharitamanas::632.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::632.essence: Ram’s greatness must be told through exile, victory, and rule together.
ramacharitamanas::632.simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to describe Ram’s forest life, Ravana’s defeat, and the many deeds Ram did as king.
ramacharitamanas::632.simple_insight: Devotion wants the whole story, not just the ending.
ramacharitamanas::632.detailed_meaning: Parvati is still asking Shiva to unfold Ram’s life step by step. After Ram’s birth, childhood, and marriage, she now wants the exile, Ravana’s death, and the royal years too. This verse is a request for the next span of the story, not its conclusion.
ramacharitamanas::632.modern_relevance: Someone asks you to tell the full story, not the highlight reel: the hard years, the victory, and the quiet years after success. Real understanding comes from the whole arc.
ramacharitamanas::632.insight: It shifts attention from a single event to the full pattern of a life.

ramacharitamanas::633.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि कहहु करुनायतन कीन्ह जो अचरज राम। प्रजा सहित रघुबंसमनि किमि गवने निज धाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::633.verse_hindi: हे कृपाधाम! फिर वह अद्भुत चरित्र कहिए जो श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने किया- वे रघुकुल शिरोमणि प्रजा सहित किस प्रकार अपने धाम को गए? ॥
ramacharitamanas::633.english_translation: O abode of compassion, tell again the wondrous act that Ram performed: how did the jewel of the Raghu line go to his own home with the people?
ramacharitamanas::633.translation_literal: बहुरि (again) / कहहु (tell) / करुनायतन (abode of compassion) / कीन्ह (did) / जो (which) / अचरज (wonderful) / राम (Ram) / प्रजा (people) / सहित (together with) / रघुबंसमनि (jewel of the Raghu lineage) / किमि (how) / गवने (went) / निज (own) / धाम (home)
ramacharitamanas::633.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::633.essence: Ram's greatest wonder is returning home with everyone who belongs with him.
ramacharitamanas::633.simple_meaning: The speaker asks to hear again how Ram, along with his people, returned to his own home after his wondrous deeds.
ramacharitamanas::633.simple_insight: Some endings are not ordinary endings. They feel like a return to where everything truly belongs.
ramacharitamanas::633.detailed_meaning: The listener is still asking Shiva to continue the story of Ram. After Ram's birth, childhood, marriage, exile, and victory, the next desire is to hear the final homecoming: how Ram, the jewel of the Raghu line, returned with his people.
ramacharitamanas::633.modern_relevance: After a long year of sacrifice, the family finally unlocks the old house, carries in the last box, and stands in the doorway together. The real victory is not the struggle — it is coming home whole.
ramacharitamanas::633.insight: It shifts attention from heroic events to the sacred completion of return.

ramacharitamanas::634.verse_sanskrit: पुनि प्रभु कहहु सो तत्त्व बखानी। जेहिं बिग्यान मगन मुनि ग्यानी॥ भगति ग्यान बिग्यान बिरागा। पुनि सब बरनहु सहित बिभागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::634.verse_hindi: हे प्रभु! फिर आप उस तत्त्व को समझाकर कहिए, जिसकी अनुभूति में ज्ञानी मुनिगण सदा मग्न रहते हैं और फिर भक्ति, ज्ञान, विज्ञान और वैराग्य का विभाग सहित वर्णन कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::634.english_translation: O Lord, speak again of that truth, in which wise sages remain absorbed. Also describe devotion, knowledge, discernment, and non-attachment, with their distinctions.
ramacharitamanas::634.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / प्रभु (Lord) / कहहु (speak) / सो (that) / तत्त्व (truth) / बखानी (explaining) / जेहिं (in which) / बिग्यान (discernment) / मगन (absorbed) / मुनि (sages) / ग्यानी (knowing ones) / भगति (devotion) / ग्यान (knowledge) / बिग्यान (discernment) / बिरागा (non-attachment) / पुनि (again) / सब (all) / बरनहु (describe) / सहित (together with) / बिभागा (distinctions)
ramacharitamanas::634.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::634.essence: Real understanding begins by asking for the distinctions.
ramacharitamanas::634.simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to explain the deepest truth again, along with the differences between devotion, knowledge, discernment, and non-attachment.
ramacharitamanas::634.simple_insight: Real understanding grows by asking again, not by pretending you already know.
ramacharitamanas::634.detailed_meaning: In the opening frame of Balkand, Parvati keeps pressing Shiva for a fuller account of Ram's truth. She wants the deepest principle explained clearly, along with the differences among devotion, knowledge, discernment, and non-attachment.
ramacharitamanas::634.modern_relevance: You hear a spiritual idea once in a lecture, then sit with it all week because it still feels unfinished. That second question is not failure; it is real learning.
ramacharitamanas::634.insight: It shifts the mind from passive listening to precise inquiry about how these paths differ.

ramacharitamanas::635.verse_sanskrit: और राम रहस्य अनेका। कहहु नाथ अति बिमल बिबेका॥ जो प्रभु मैं पूछा नहिं होई। सोउ दयाल राखहु जनि गोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::635.verse_hindi: (इसके सिवा) श्री रामचन्द्रजी के और भी जो अनेक रहस्य (छिपे हुए भाव अथवा चरित्र) हैं, उनको कहिए। हे नाथ! आपका ज्ञान अत्यन्त निर्मल है। हे प्रभो! जो बात मैंने न भी पूछी हो, हे दयालु! उसे भी आप छिपा न रखिएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::635.english_translation: (Besides this) tell also the many other hidden mysteries of Ram. O Lord, your understanding is utterly pure. O merciful one, do not keep hidden even what I did not ask.
ramacharitamanas::635.translation_literal: और (and) राम (Ram) रहस्य (mysteries) अनेका (many) / कहहु (tell) नाथ (Lord) अति (very) बिमल (pure) बिबेका (discernment) / जो (whatever) प्रभु (Lord) मैं (I) पूछा (asked) नहिं (not) होई (happened) / सोउ (that too) दयाल (merciful one) राखहु (keep) जनि (do not) गोई (hidden)
ramacharitamanas::635.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::635.essence: True inquiry asks for what has not yet been asked.
ramacharitamanas::635.simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to explain Ram’s many hidden mysteries and to share even the things she has not thought to ask. She trusts his pure understanding and wants nothing left concealed.
ramacharitamanas::635.simple_insight: Curiosity becomes devotion when it asks for the whole truth, not just the part it already expects.
ramacharitamanas::635.detailed_meaning: In the opening of Balkand, Parvati keeps pressing Shiva to unfold Ram’s deeper nature. After asking for Ram’s hidden truths, she adds one more request: reveal even the things she has not known to ask. The verse deepens the dialogue into complete openness.
ramacharitamanas::635.modern_relevance: You finally sit with someone wise enough to tell you the hard part, not just the polished version. You want the whole answer, including the part you didn’t know to ask about.
ramacharitamanas::635.insight: It shifts inquiry from selective questions to full receptivity, asking for what lies beyond your own awareness.

ramacharitamanas::636.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह त्रिभुवन गुर बेद बखाना। आन जीव पाँवर का जाना॥ प्रस्न उमा कै सहज सुहाई। छल बिहीन सुनि सिव मन भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::636.verse_hindi: वेदों ने आपको तीनों लोकों का गुरु कहा है। दूसरे पामर जीव इस रहस्य को क्या जानें! पार्वतीजी के सहज सुंदर और छलरहित (सरल) प्रश्न सुनकर शिवजी के मन को बहुत अच्छे लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::636.english_translation: The Vedas call you the teacher of the three worlds. What can ordinary beings know of this mystery? Shiva's mind was delighted by Parvati's simple, sincere question.
ramacharitamanas::636.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / त्रिभुवन (three worlds) / गुर (teacher) / बेद (Vedas) / बखाना (describe, declare) / आन (other) / जीव (beings) / पाँवर (weak, lowly) / का (what) / जाना (know) / प्रस्न (question) / उमा (Parvati) / कै (of) / सहज (natural, simple) / सुहाई (beautiful) / छल (deceit) / बिहीन (free from) / सुनि (hearing) / सिव (Shiva) / मन (mind) / भाई (was pleased)
ramacharitamanas::636.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::636.simple_meaning: The Vedas praise Ram as the teacher of all three worlds, while ordinary people cannot fully grasp that mystery. Shiva is pleased by Parvati's simple, honest question.
ramacharitamanas::636.simple_insight: Sincere questioning opens the heart more than cleverness does.
ramacharitamanas::636.detailed_meaning: Shiva is answering Parvati in the opening frame of the Ramcharitmanas. He reminds her that the Vedas call Ram the teacher of the three worlds, then gently says that ordinary beings cannot fully grasp such mystery. Parvati's honest question pleases him because it invites true teaching.
ramacharitamanas::636.modern_relevance: You sit with someone wiser than you and finally ask the plain question you were embarrassed to voice. That honesty changes the whole conversation.
ramacharitamanas::636.insight: It shifts attention from intellectual pride to humble receptivity.

ramacharitamanas::637.verse_sanskrit: हर हियँ रामचरित सब आए। प्रेम पुलक लोचन जल छाए॥ श्रीरघुनाथ रूप उर आवा। परमानंद अमित सुख पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::637.verse_hindi: श्री महादेवजी के हृदय में सारे रामचरित्र आ गए। प्रेम के मारे उनका शरीर पुलकित हो गया और नेत्रों में जल भर आया। श्री रघुनाथजी का रूप उनके हृदय में आ गया, जिससे स्वयं परमानन्दस्वरूप शिवजी ने भी अपार सुख पाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::637.english_translation: All the stories of Ram entered Shiva's heart. Love made his body tremble, and tears filled his eyes. Ram's form arose within his heart, and Shiva, whose nature is supreme bliss, tasted boundless joy.
ramacharitamanas::637.translation_literal: हर (all) / हियँ (in the heart) / रामचरित (the deeds and stories of Ram) / सब (all) / आए (came) / प्रेम (love) / पुलक (hairs standing on end) / लोचन (eyes) / जल (water/tears) / छाए (were filled) ॥ / श्रीरघुनाथ (Lord Ram) / रूप (form) / उर (in the heart) / आवा (came) / परमानंद (supreme bliss) / अमित (immeasurable) / सुख (joy) / पावा (found)
ramacharitamanas::637.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::637.essence: Ram's remembrance turns devotion into visible joy.
ramacharitamanas::637.simple_meaning: Shiva becomes so filled with love for Ram that his body trembles, his eyes fill with tears, and Ram's form brings him immense joy.
ramacharitamanas::637.simple_insight: Love for the divine can overflow into the body, not just the mind.
ramacharitamanas::637.detailed_meaning: Parvati has asked Shiva to reveal Ram's hidden greatness. As Shiva speaks, he is no detached commentator — Ram's whole story rises in his heart. The vision moves him so deeply that devotion becomes visible in tears, trembling, and bliss.
ramacharitamanas::637.modern_relevance: You hear a song that takes you straight back to someone you love, and your throat tightens before you can explain why. Some truths are felt first in the body.
ramacharitamanas::637.insight: It shows that remembrance can become embodied devotion, where feeling and vision deepen each other.

ramacharitamanas::638.verse_sanskrit: मगन ध्यान रस दंड जुग पुनि मन बाहेर कीन्ह। रघुपति चरित महेस तब हरषित बरनै लीन्ह॥111।
ramacharitamanas::638.verse_hindi: शिवजी दो घड़ी तक ध्यान के रस (आनंद) में डूबे रहे, फिर उन्होंने मन को बाहर खींचा और तब वे प्रसन्न होकर श्री रघुनाथजी का चरित्र वर्णन करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::638.english_translation: For two watches Shiva remained immersed in the taste of meditation, then drew his mind outward and, delighted, began to narrate the deeds of Raghupati.
ramacharitamanas::638.translation_literal: मगन (immersed) / ध्यान (meditation) / रस (taste, essence) / दंड जुग (two watches) / पुनि (again) / मन (mind) / बाहेर (outward) / कीन्ह (made) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / चरित (deeds, story) / महेस (Shiva) / तब (then) / हरषित (delighted) / बरनै (to describe) / लीन्ह (began)
ramacharitamanas::638.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::638.essence: Meditation ripens into joy when Ram's story is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::638.simple_meaning: Shiva sat absorbed in meditation, then turned back with joy to speak Ram's story.
ramacharitamanas::638.simple_insight: Even deep inward absorption gives way to joy when Ram's story begins.
ramacharitamanas::638.detailed_meaning: Shiva has been listening to Parvati and reliving Ram's life in his heart. After being lost in meditation for a while, he gathers himself and, delighted, starts narrating Ram's deeds. The verse marks the shift from inward absorption to loving speech.
ramacharitamanas::638.modern_relevance: You sit quietly after a long day, phone face down, and the mind finally settles. Then one memory of someone you love brings warmth back into the room. Devotion does that: it turns silence into praise.
ramacharitamanas::638.insight: It shifts attention from private absorption to expressive remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::639.verse_sanskrit: झूठेउ सत्य जाहि बिनु जानें। जिमि भुजंग बिनु रजु पहिचानें॥ जेहि जानें जग जाइ हेराई। जागें जथा सपन भ्रम जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::639.verse_hindi: जिसके बिना जाने झूठ भी सत्य मालूम होता है, जैसे बिना पहचाने रस्सी में साँप का भ्रम हो जाता है और जिसके जान लेने पर जगत का उसी तरह लोप हो जाता है, जैसे जागने पर स्वप्न का भ्रम जाता रहता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::639.english_translation: Without knowing it, falsehood appears true, like mistaking a rope for a snake. Knowing it, the world vanishes like a dream after waking.
ramacharitamanas::639.translation_literal: झूठेउ (false) / सत्य (true) / जाहि (which) / बिनु जानें (without knowing) / जिमि (like) / भुजंग (snake) / बिनु रजु (without rope) / पहिचानें (having recognized) / जेहि जानें (which knowing) / जग (world) / जाइ हेराई (goes away, disappears) / जागें (upon waking) / जथा (as) / सपन (dream) / भ्रम (illusion) / जाई (goes away)
ramacharitamanas::639.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::639.essence: Clear seeing dissolves the world of error like waking from a dream.
ramacharitamanas::639.simple_meaning: Ignorance makes false things seem real. Clear understanding removes the illusion, just as waking ends a dream.
ramacharitamanas::639.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that confusion is not final; understanding can dissolve what once felt overwhelming.
ramacharitamanas::639.detailed_meaning: Shiva is describing the state of spiritual confusion after dwelling on Ram's story. He says ignorance makes the unreal seem real, just as a rope can be mistaken for a snake. But once true understanding arises, the whole false appearance drops away like a dream after waking.
ramacharitamanas::639.modern_relevance: You read one harsh text at midnight and suddenly your whole friendship feels broken. By morning, the panic looks smaller. Clear seeing can undo a whole world built by fear.
ramacharitamanas::639.insight: It shifts the mind from reacting to appearances to checking what is actually real.

ramacharitamanas::640.verse_sanskrit: बंदउँ बालरूप सोइ रामू। सब सिधि सुलभ जपत जिसु नामू॥ मंगल भवन अमंगल हारी। द्रवउ सो दसरथ अजिर बिहारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::640.verse_hindi: मैं उन्हीं श्री रामचन्द्रजी के बाल रूप की वंदना करता हूँ, जिनका नाम जपने से सब सिद्धियाँ सहज ही प्राप्त हो जाती हैं। मंगल के धाम, अमंगल के हरने वाले और श्री दशरथजी के आँगन में खेलने वाले (बालरूप) श्री रामचन्द्रजी मुझ पर कृपा करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::640.english_translation: I bow to that child-form of Ram. All powers come easily by repeating his name. He is the home of auspiciousness, the remover of inauspiciousness. May that Ram, who played in Dasharath's courtyard, soften my heart.
ramacharitamanas::640.translation_literal: बंदउँ (I bow) / बालरूप (child-form) / सोइ (that same) / रामू (Ram) / सब (all) / सिधि (powers, attainments) / सुलभ (easy to obtain) / जपत (repeating) / जिसु (whose) / नामू (name) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / भवन (abode) / अमंगल (inauspiciousness) / हारी (remover) / द्रवउँ (may soften) / सो (that) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / अजिर (courtyard) / बिहारी (one who plays)
ramacharitamanas::640.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::640.essence: Ram’s name gives what striving cannot.
ramacharitamanas::640.simple_meaning: Ram’s child form is worthy of reverence, and repeating his name brings every attainment easily. He is the source of auspiciousness and the remover of what harms.
ramacharitamanas::640.simple_insight: There is relief in turning to a presence that already carries what you need.
ramacharitamanas::640.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas begins his praise of Ram’s child form after Shiva has turned back from deep meditation and is ready to speak. He bows to the playful child in Dasharath’s courtyard, saying Ram’s name alone brings every attainment and clears away all that is harmful.
ramacharitamanas::640.modern_relevance: You are exhausted, scrolling for the next fix, and nothing sticks. Then one simple practice steadies you again: return to what is worthy, repeat it, and let the noise fall away.
ramacharitamanas::640.insight: It shifts attention from chasing scattered remedies to resting in a single sacred refuge.

ramacharitamanas::641.verse_sanskrit: करि प्रनाम रामहि त्रिपुरारी। हरषि सुधा सम गिरा उचारी॥ धन्य धन्य गिरिराजकुमारी। तुम्ह समान नहिं कोउ उपकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::641.verse_hindi: त्रिपुरासुर का वध करने वाले शिवजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी को प्रणाम करके आनंद में भरकर अमृत के समान वाणी बोले- हे गिरिराजकुमारी पार्वती! तुम धन्य हो! धन्य हो!! तुम्हारे समान कोई उपकारी नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::641.english_translation: Shiva bowed to Ram and, overjoyed, spoke words like nectar: "Blessed, blessed is Giriraj's daughter. No one serves like you."
ramacharitamanas::641.translation_literal: करि (having done) / प्रनाम (salutation) / रामहि (to Ram) / त्रिपुरारी (Shiva, destroyer of the three cities) / हरषि (rejoicing) / सुधा सम (like nectar) / गिरा (speech) / उचारी (uttered) / धन्य धन्य (blessed, blessed) / गिरिराजकुमारी (daughter of the mountain king, Parvati) / तुम्ह (you) / समान (equal) / नहिं (not) / कोउ (anyone) / उपकारी (one who does good / serves)
ramacharitamanas::641.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::641.essence: Humility that asks for Ram is itself a great service.
ramacharitamanas::641.simple_meaning: Shiva first bows to Ram, then praises Parvati for asking about Ram's story. He calls her blessed and says no one serves like she does.
ramacharitamanas::641.simple_insight: True devotion includes honoring the one who asks with humility.
ramacharitamanas::641.detailed_meaning: Shiva, the great devotee, has just bowed to Ram. Filled with joy, he turns to Parvati and praises her for the good she has done by asking for Ram's कथा. Her question opens the way for sacred teaching to continue.
ramacharitamanas::641.modern_relevance: Someone asks a sincere question in a quiet room, and the whole mood changes. The person answering does not just give information — he honors the humility that made the question possible.
ramacharitamanas::641.insight: It shifts attention from the answer alone to the devotion and receptivity that make the answer possible.

ramacharitamanas::642.verse_sanskrit: पूँछेहु रघुपति कथा प्रसंगा। सकल लोक जग पावनि गंगा॥ तुम्ह रघुबीर चरन अनुरागी। कीन्हिहु प्रस्न जगत हित लागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::642.verse_hindi: जो तुमने श्री रघुनाथजी की कथा का प्रसंग पूछा है, जो कथा समस्त लोकों के लिए जगत को पवित्र करने वाली गंगाजी के समान है। तुमने जगत के कल्याण के लिए ही प्रश्न पूछे हैं। तुम श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों में प्रेम रखने वाली हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::642.english_translation: You have asked about the story of Raghupati, a tale that purifies all worlds like the Ganga. You asked for the welfare of the world, for you love the feet of the Lord of the Raghu clan.
ramacharitamanas::642.translation_literal: पूँछेहु (you asked) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / कथा (story) / प्रसंगा (context, episode) / सकल (all) / लोक (worlds) / जग (world) / पावनि (purifying) / गंगा (Ganga) / तुम्ह (you) / रघुबीर (hero of the Raghu clan) / चरन (feet) / अनुरागी (loving, attached in devotion) / कीन्हिहु (you did) / प्रस्न (question) / जगत (world) / हित (welfare) / लागी (for the sake of)
ramacharitamanas::642.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::642.essence: A question asked in love can purify everyone who hears it.
ramacharitamanas::642.simple_meaning: Parvati’s question is praised as sincere and beneficial because it comes from love for Ram and seeks the good of the world.
ramacharitamanas::642.simple_insight: A sincere question can become an act of devotion when it is asked for everyone’s good.
ramacharitamanas::642.detailed_meaning: Shiva is answering Parvati in the opening frame of Balkand. He praises her for asking about Ram’s story, calling it as purifying as the Ganga. Her curiosity is not idle; it comes from love for Ram and concern for the world’s welfare.
ramacharitamanas::642.modern_relevance: You ask a question in a meeting not to sound clever, but because people are confused and the room needs clarity. That kind of question changes the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::642.insight: It reframes inquiry as service: asking well can be an act of devotion, not just curiosity.

ramacharitamanas::643.verse_sanskrit: राम कृपा तें पारबति सपनेहुँ तव मन माहिं। सोक मोह संदेह भ्रम मम बिचार कछु नाहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::643.verse_hindi: हे पार्वती! मेरे विचार में तो श्री रामजी की कृपा से तुम्हारे मन में स्वप्न में भी शोक, मोह, संदेह और भ्रम कुछ भी नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::643.english_translation: O Parvati, by Ram's grace there is not even in a dream any sorrow, delusion, doubt, or confusion in your mind.
ramacharitamanas::643.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / कृपा (grace) / तें (by) / पारबति (Parvati) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / तव (your) / मन (mind) / माहिं (in) / सोक (sorrow) / मोह (delusion) / संदेह (doubt) / भ्रम (confusion) / मम (my) / बिचार (view) / कछु (some) / नाहिं (not)
ramacharitamanas::643.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::643.essence: Ram's grace leaves no space for sorrow or confusion.
ramacharitamanas::643.simple_meaning: Ram's grace can make the mind so clear that sorrow, confusion, doubt, and delusion do not enter it.
ramacharitamanas::643.simple_insight: There is relief in trusting that grace can steady the mind more deeply than effort can.
ramacharitamanas::643.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the opening frame of Ramcharitmanas. After praising her devotion and asking her to hear Ram's story, he says her mind is already free from sorrow and confusion by Ram's grace, preparing her to receive the teaching without doubt.
ramacharitamanas::643.modern_relevance: You replay a painful conversation at 2 a.m., trying to untangle every meaning. Then something settles, and the mind stops spinning. This verse points to that kind of inward clarity.
ramacharitamanas::643.insight: It shifts attention from mental noise to the quiet confidence that comes from grace.

ramacharitamanas::644.verse_sanskrit: तदपि असंका कीन्हिहु सोई। कहत सुनत सब कर हित होई॥ जिन्ह हरिकथा सुनी नहिं काना। श्रवन रंध्र अहिभवन समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::644.verse_hindi: फिर भी तुमने इसीलिए वही (पुरानी) शंका की है कि इस प्रसंग के कहने-सुनने से सबका कल्याण होगा। जिन्होंने अपने कानों से भगवान की कथा नहीं सुनी, उनके कानों के छिद्र साँप के बिल के समान हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::644.english_translation: Still, you asked that very question so that hearing and speaking this story may do good to everyone. The ears of those who have never heard the divine story are like snake holes.
ramacharitamanas::644.translation_literal: तदपि (still) / असंका (without doubt) / कीन्हिहु (you did) / सोई (that very) / कहत (speaking) / सुनत (hearing) / सब (all) / कर (of) / हित (good) / होई (becomes) ॥ / जिन्ह (those who) / हरिकथा (the story of Hari) / सुनी (heard) / नहिं (not) / काना (ears) / श्रवन (ear) / रंध्र (opening) / अहि (snake) / भवन (dwelling) / समाना (like)
ramacharitamanas::644.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::644.essence: Ram's story itself is a blessing to anyone who hears it.
ramacharitamanas::644.simple_meaning: Hearing and speaking Ram's story brings benefit to everyone. People who never listen to it remain spiritually empty, like snake holes with no life in them.
ramacharitamanas::644.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that listening itself can cleanse and uplift you.
ramacharitamanas::644.detailed_meaning: Shiva is answering Parvati in the opening Balkand frame. He says she asked about Ram's story for a good reason: simply hearing and speaking it benefits all. Those who never hear Hari's story miss a life-giving gift.
ramacharitamanas::644.modern_relevance: You put on a podcast in the car because your mind felt scattered, and halfway through you notice your breathing has softened. Some words do that: they quietly change the room inside you.
ramacharitamanas::644.insight: It shifts attention from clever analysis to receptive listening as a form of care.

ramacharitamanas::645.verse_sanskrit: नयनन्हि संत दरस नहिं देखा। लोचन मोरपंख कर लेखा॥ तेसिर कटु तुंबरि समतूला। जे न नमत हरि गुर पद मूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::645.verse_hindi: जिन्होंने अपने नेत्रों से संतों के दर्शन नहीं किए, उनके वे नेत्र मोर के पंखों पर दिखने वाली नकली आँखों की गिनती में हैं। वे सिर कड़वी तूँबी के समान हैं, जो श्री हरि और गुरु के चरणतल पर नहीं झुकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::645.english_translation: Those who have never seen saints with their eyes have eyes like the false eyes painted on peacock feathers. Their heads are like bitter gourds, unbowed at the feet of Hari and the guru.
ramacharitamanas::645.translation_literal: नयनन्हि (with the eyes) / संत (holy ones) / दरस (darshan, sacred sight) / नहिं देखा (have not seen) / लोचन (eyes) / मोरपंख (peacock feather) / कर लेखा (like the markings) / तेसिर (those heads) / कटु (bitter) / तुंबरि (gourd) / समतूला (equal to) / जे (those who) / न नमत (do not bow) / हरि (Hari) / गुर (guru) / पद मूला (at the foot of the feet)
ramacharitamanas::645.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::645.essence: Sight without reverence is almost useless.
ramacharitamanas::645.simple_meaning: Without meeting holy people, even eyes and a head lose their worth. Real sight is shown by humility before the divine and the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::645.simple_insight: It asks you to value reverence over mere seeing, and humility over pride.
ramacharitamanas::645.detailed_meaning: In Shiva’s teaching to Parvati, Tulsidas turns from doubt to the value of holy company. He says that eyes that never behold saints and a head that never bows to Hari and the guru have missed their true purpose. The verse prepares the next line about devotion.
ramacharitamanas::645.modern_relevance: You can scroll through a hundred spiritual posts and still miss what matters. One quiet meeting with someone rooted in humility can change how you see everything.
ramacharitamanas::645.insight: It shifts attention from display and information to reverence, humility, and the company you keep.

ramacharitamanas::646.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह हरिभगति हृदयँ नहिं आनी। जीवत सव समान तेइ प्रानी॥ जो नहिं करइ राम गुन गाना। जीह सो दादुर जीह समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::646.verse_hindi: जिन्होंने भगवान की भक्ति को अपने हृदय में स्थान नहीं दिया, वे प्राणी जीते हुए ही मुर्दे के समान हैं, जो जीभ श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुणों का गान नहीं करती, वह मेंढक की जीभ के समान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::646.english_translation: Those who have not brought devotion to Ram into their hearts are like the dead while still alive. A tongue that does not sing Ram's virtues is like a frog's tongue.
ramacharitamanas::646.translation_literal: जिन्ह (those who) / हरि-भगति (devotion to Ram) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / नहिं (not) / आनी (brought) / जीवत (alive) / सव समान (like the dead) / तेइ (those) / प्रानी (beings)॥ / जो (which) / नहिं (does not) / करइ (do) / राम (Ram) / गुन (virtues) / गाना (singing) / जीह (tongue) / सो (that) / दादुर (frog) / जीह (tongue) / समाना (similar) ॥
ramacharitamanas::646.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::646.essence: Life without devotion is only motion; speech without praise is empty noise.
ramacharitamanas::646.simple_meaning: A person who keeps no devotion for Ram is spiritually lifeless. A tongue that never praises Ram is as useless as a frog's croak.
ramacharitamanas::646.simple_insight: What you love and praise reveals whether your life is truly awake.
ramacharitamanas::646.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, Tulsidas is building a devotional argument with Parvati listening in the frame. After praising saints and holy hearing, he sharpens the point: a heart untouched by devotion and a tongue silent about Ram have missed the very meaning of life.
ramacharitamanas::646.modern_relevance: You scroll through a hundred voices before breakfast, but nothing stays with you. Then one name, one song, one truth keeps returning. This verse asks whether your heart has actually been moved by anything real.
ramacharitamanas::646.insight: It shifts the reader from merely existing and speaking to living with devotion and using speech for praise.

ramacharitamanas::647.verse_sanskrit: कुलिस कठोर निठुर सोइ छाती। सुनि हरिचरित न जो हरषाती॥ गिरिजा सुनहु राम कै लीला। सुर हित दनुज बिमोहनसीला ॥
ramacharitamanas::647.verse_hindi: वह हृदय वज्र के समान कड़ा और निष्ठुर है, जो भगवान के चरित्र सुनकर हर्षित नहीं होता। हे पार्वती! श्री रामचन्द्रजी की लीला सुनो, यह देवताओं का कल्याण करने वाली और दैत्यों को विशेष रूप से मोहित करने वाली है ॥
ramacharitamanas::647.english_translation: That heart is as hard as a thunderbolt and cruel, which does not rejoice on hearing the deeds of the divine. O Parvati, listen to Ram's play: it brings benefit to the radiant beings and bewilders the forces of ego and shadow.
ramacharitamanas::647.translation_literal: कुलिस (thunderbolt) / कठोर (hard) / निठुर (cruel) / सोइ (that) / छाती (heart) / सुनि (hearing) / हरिचरित (the deeds of Hari) / न (not) / जो (which) / हरषाती (rejoices)॥ / गिरिजा (O Parvati) / सुनहु (listen) / राम कै (of Ram) / लीला (play) / सुर हित (for the benefit of the radiant beings) / दनुज (the forces of ego and shadow) / बिमोहनसीला (having the nature of bewildering)॥
ramacharitamanas::647.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::647.essence: A heart that cannot rejoice at Ram's story has already hardened.
ramacharitamanas::647.simple_meaning: A heart that feels no joy at hearing Ram's story has become hard. Tulsidas then invites Parvati to hear Ram's play, which blesses the good and confounds the forces of ego and shadow.
ramacharitamanas::647.simple_insight: Joy at the divine's story is a sign of a living, responsive heart.
ramacharitamanas::647.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas turns from the earlier warning about deadened hearing and speech to a direct devotional invitation. He tells Parvati that Ram's play should be heard because it nourishes the radiant beings and unsettles the forces of ego and shadow.
ramacharitamanas::647.modern_relevance: You keep scrolling past stories of kindness, sacrifice, and grace without feeling anything. That numbness is not neutrality; it is a heart that has gone hard. Hearing what is noble should still move you.
ramacharitamanas::647.insight: It shifts the reader from emotional numbness to receptive devotion, treating delight in Ram's story as a spiritual test.

ramacharitamanas::648.verse_sanskrit: रामकथा सुरधेनु सम सेवत सब सुख दानि। सतसमाज सुरलोक सब को न सुनै अस जानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::648.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की कथा कामधेनु के समान सेवा करने से सब सुखों को देने वाली है और सत्पुरुषों के समाज ही सब देवताओं के लोक हैं, ऐसा जानकर इसे कौन न सुनेगा! ॥
ramacharitamanas::648.english_translation: Ram's story is like a wish-fulfilling cow: serving it gives every joy. The company of the good is itself a higher realm; knowing this, who would not listen?
ramacharitamanas::648.translation_literal: रामकथा (the story of Ram) / सुरधेनु (wish-fulfilling cow) / सम (like) / सेवत (serving) / सब (all) / सुख (joys) / दानि (giver) / सतसमाज (company of the good) / सुरलोक (higher realm) / सब (all) / को (who) / न (not) / सुनै (would listen) / अस (thus) / जानि (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::648.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::648.essence: Ram's story nourishes completely, and good company is its own reward.
ramacharitamanas::648.simple_meaning: Ram's story brings every kind of joy, like a wish-fulfilling cow. Good company itself feels like a higher realm, so listening to this story is natural.
ramacharitamanas::648.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that sacred stories and good company nourish you from the inside.
ramacharitamanas::648.detailed_meaning: Parvati is hearing Shiva's praise of Ram's story in Balkand. After saying that a heart unmoved by Ram's past is hard as thunderbolt, the teaching now turns tender: Ram's story itself feeds every need, and the company of the wise is like living in a higher realm.
ramacharitamanas::648.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where every conversation is cynical, then into another where people speak with honesty and care. One drains you; the other restores you. This verse points you toward the second room.
ramacharitamanas::648.insight: It shifts attention from entertainment to nourishment, and from casual company to people who deepen devotion.

ramacharitamanas::649.verse_sanskrit: रामकथा सुंदर कर तारी। संसय बिहग उड़ावनिहारी॥ रामकथा कलि बिटप कुठारी। सादर सुनु गिरिराजकुमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::649.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की कथा हाथ की सुंदर ताली है, जो संदेह रूपी पक्षियों को उड़ा देती है। फिर रामकथा कलियुग रूपी वृक्ष को काटने के लिए कुल्हाड़ी है। हे गिरिराजकुमारी! तुम इसे आदरपूर्वक सुनो ॥
ramacharitamanas::649.english_translation: Ram's story is a beautiful clap of the hands that drives away the birds of doubt. Ram's story is an axe for cutting down the tree of Kali Yuga. Listen to it with reverence, Giriraj's daughter.
ramacharitamanas::649.translation_literal: रामकथा (Ram's story) / सुंदर (beautiful) / कर (hand) / तारी (clap) / संसय (doubt) / बिहग (birds) / उड़ावनिहारी (that which drives away) / रामकथा (Ram's story) / कलि (Kali Yuga) / बिटप (tree) / कुठारी (axe) / सादर (with reverence) / सुनु (listen) / गिरिराजकुमारी (daughter of the mountain king)
ramacharitamanas::649.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::649.essence: Ram's story clears doubt and cuts through confusion.
ramacharitamanas::649.simple_meaning: Ram's story removes doubt and destroys the habits of confusion. It is powerful enough to clear the mind and cut through what weakens spiritual life.
ramacharitamanas::649.simple_insight: You do not have to wrestle every doubt alone; sincere listening can weaken it.
ramacharitamanas::649.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the opening frame of the Balkand, praising Ram's story as more than poetry. He says it can scatter doubt and cut through the dark age's grip, so Parvati should hear it with respect.
ramacharitamanas::649.modern_relevance: You are half-listening to a podcast while ten tabs stay open in your head. Then one clear line lands and the noise drops. That is the kind of force this verse gives Ram's story.
ramacharitamanas::649.insight: It shifts the mind from skeptical scattering to receptive listening.

ramacharitamanas::650.verse_sanskrit: राम नाम गुन चरित सुहाए। जनम करम अगनित श्रुति गाए॥ जथा अनंत राम भगवाना। तथा कथा कीरति गुन नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::650.verse_hindi: वेदों ने श्री रामचन्द्रजी के सुंदर नाम, गुण, चरित्र, जन्म और कर्म सभी अनगिनत कहे हैं। जिस प्रकार भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी अनन्त हैं, उसी तरह उनकी कथा, कीर्ति और गुण भी अनंत हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::650.english_translation: The Vedas sing of Ram's beautiful name, virtues, deeds, birth, and actions as endless. Just as Lord Ram is infinite, so too are his stories, fame, and qualities without end.
ramacharitamanas::650.translation_literal: राम नाम (Ram's name) / गुन (virtues) / चरित (deeds, conduct) / सुहाए (beautiful, pleasing) / जनम (birth) / करम (actions) / अगनित (countless) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / गाए (sing, praise) / जथा (just as) / अनंत (endless) / राम भगवाना (Lord Ram) / तथा (so) / कथा (story) / कीरति (fame, glory) / गुन (qualities) / नाना (many, varied)
ramacharitamanas::650.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::650.essence: Ram cannot be fully described because his glory has no limit.
ramacharitamanas::650.simple_meaning: Ram's name, qualities, life, and deeds are beyond counting. His greatness cannot be exhausted, so every telling of him remains incomplete and alive.
ramacharitamanas::650.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing the sacred cannot be finished or owned. Love keeps discovering more.
ramacharitamanas::650.detailed_meaning: Shiva is describing Ram's story to Parvati in Balkand. After praising Ram-katha as a remover of doubt, he says the Vedas themselves cannot finish describing Ram's name, birth, deeds, and glory. The teaching is that Ram is limitless, so devotion to him never runs dry.
ramacharitamanas::650.modern_relevance: You reread a letter from someone you love and notice a detail you missed before. Some presences are like that: the more closely you look, the more they reveal.
ramacharitamanas::650.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to contain Ram in one definition to receiving him as inexhaustible.

ramacharitamanas::651.verse_sanskrit: तदपि जथा श्रुत जसि मति मोरी। कहिहउँ देखि प्रीति अति तोरी॥ उमा प्रस्न तव सहज सुहाई। सुखद संतसंमत मोहि भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::651.verse_hindi: तो भी तुम्हारी अत्यन्त प्रीति देखकर, जैसा कुछ मैंने सुना है और जैसी मेरी बुद्धि है, उसी के अनुसार मैं कहूँगा। हे पार्वती! तुम्हारा प्रश्न स्वाभाविक ही सुंदर, सुखदायक और संतसम्मत है और मुझे तो बहुत ही अच्छा लगा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::651.english_translation: Still, according to what I have heard and as my understanding allows, I will speak, moved by your great affection. O Uma, your question is naturally beautiful, pleasing, and approved by the wise, and I am very glad of it.
ramacharitamanas::651.translation_literal: तदपि (still) / जथा (as) / श्रुत (heard) / जसि (as) / मति (understanding) / मोरी (my) / कहिहउँ (I will speak) / देखि (seeing) / प्रीति (affection) / अति (very much) / तोरी (your) / उमा (Uma) / प्रस्न (question) / तव (your) / सहज (natural) / सुहाई (beautiful) / सुखद (pleasing) / संतसंमत (approved by the wise) / मोहि (to me) / भाई (became pleasing)
ramacharitamanas::651.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::651.essence: Honest teaching begins with a worthy question.
ramacharitamanas::651.simple_meaning: Shiva says he will answer as best he can, guided by what he has heard and understood, because Parvati's question is sincere, beautiful, and worthy of the wise.
ramacharitamanas::651.simple_insight: A good question opens the door to honest teaching.
ramacharitamanas::651.detailed_meaning: In the opening frame of the Balkand, Shiva is speaking to Parvati. Her devotion and curiosity have drawn him into teaching the Ram story. He says he will answer only as far as his hearing and understanding allow, because her question is sincere and worthy.
ramacharitamanas::651.modern_relevance: Someone asks a careful question in a quiet room, not to win an argument but to understand. The best answer begins there — with respect, not performance.
ramacharitamanas::651.insight: It teaches you to meet sincere inquiry with humility and care, not with display.

ramacharitamanas::652.verse_sanskrit: एक बात नहिं मोहि सोहानी। जदपि मोह बस कहेहु भवानी॥ तुम्ह जो कहा राम कोउ आना। जेहि श्रुति गाव धरहिं मुनि ध्याना ॥
ramacharitamanas::652.verse_hindi: परंतु हे पार्वती! एक बात मुझे अच्छी नहीं लगी, यद्यपि वह तुमने मोह के वश होकर ही कही है। तुमने जो यह कहा कि वे राम कोई और हैं, जिन्हें वेद गाते और मुनिजन जिनका ध्यान धरते हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::652.english_translation: One thing does not please me, though you said it under the spell of delusion, O Bhavani. You said that Ram is someone else, the one whom the Vedas sing and the sages meditate on.
ramacharitamanas::652.translation_literal: एक बात (one thing) / नहिं (not) / मोहि (to me) / सोहानी (pleasing) / जदपि (though) / मोह बस (under the sway of delusion) / कहेहु (you said) / भवानी (O Bhavani) / तुम्ह (you) / जो (that) / कहा (said) / राम (Ram) / कोउ आना (someone else) / जेहि (whom) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / गाव (sing) / धरहिं (hold) / मुनि (sages) / ध्याना (meditation)
ramacharitamanas::652.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::652.essence: Ram is not another being; he is the one the Vedas already praise.
ramacharitamanas::652.simple_meaning: Shiva gently corrects Parvati: Ram is not someone separate from the one praised in the Vedas and meditated on by sages.
ramacharitamanas::652.simple_insight: False separation falls away when devotion sees clearly.
ramacharitamanas::652.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, Shiva is answering Parvati's question about Ram's identity. He pauses on one point: the idea that Ram is some other being. That misunderstanding must be corrected, because the whole devotional teaching depends on knowing Ram as the supreme reality praised by the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::652.modern_relevance: You hear someone reduce what you love most into a name or a role. The correction matters: the deepest reality is not a distant concept, but the one already being praised and sought.
ramacharitamanas::652.insight: It shifts attention from labels and separateness to the unity behind all reverence.

ramacharitamanas::653.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं सुनहिं अस अधम नर ग्रसे जे मोह पिसाच। पाषंडी हरि पद बिमुख जानहिं झूठ न साच ॥
ramacharitamanas::653.verse_hindi: जो मोह रूपी पिशाच के द्वारा ग्रस्त हैं, पाखण्डी हैं, भगवान के चरणों से विमुख हैं और जो झूठ-सच कुछ भी नहीं जानते, ऐसे अधम मनुष्य ही इस तरह कहते-सुनते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::653.english_translation: Such vile people speak and listen this way—people seized by the demon of delusion, hypocrites, turned away from Hari's feet, and unable to tell false from true.
ramacharitamanas::653.translation_literal: कहहिं (they say) / सुनहिं (they hear) / अस (such) / अधम (base) / नर (people) / ग्रसे (seized) / जे (who) / मोह (delusion) / पिसाच (demon) / पाषंडी (hypocrites) / हरि (Hari) / पद (feet) / बिमुख (turned away) / जानहिं (know) / झूठ (false) / न (not) / साच (true)
ramacharitamanas::653.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::653.essence: Delusion destroys the ability to recognize truth.
ramacharitamanas::653.simple_meaning: People caught in delusion, hypocrisy, and rejection of the divine lose the ability to tell truth from falsehood.
ramacharitamanas::653.simple_insight: Clarity begins when you admit your own blind spots instead of defending them.
ramacharitamanas::653.detailed_meaning: Shiva is answering Parvati in the Balkand, pushing back against the idea that Ram could be anything other than the supreme Lord. He says only the most deluded, hypocritical people speak otherwise, because their minds can no longer recognize truth.
ramacharitamanas::653.modern_relevance: You are scrolling through a comment thread where everyone is certain, angry, and wrong. The loudest voices often sound convincing precisely because they have lost contact with what is real.
ramacharitamanas::653.insight: It shifts the reader from arguing over appearances to checking whether the mind itself is clouded.

ramacharitamanas::654.verse_sanskrit: अग्य अकोबिद अंध अभागी। काई बिषय मुकुर मन लागी॥ लंपट कपटी कुटिल बिसेषी। सपनेहुँ संतसभा नहिं देखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::654.verse_hindi: जो अज्ञानी, मूर्ख, अंधे और भाग्यहीन हैं और जिनके मन रूपी दर्पण पर विषय रूपी काई जमी हुई है, जो व्यभिचारी, छली और बड़े कुटिल हैं और जिन्होंने कभी स्वप्न में भी संत समाज के दर्शन नहीं किए ॥
ramacharitamanas::654.english_translation: Ignorant, foolish, blind, and unfortunate, their minds are coated with the moss of worldly cravings. Lustful, deceitful, and deeply crooked, they have never even seen the company of the good in a dream.
ramacharitamanas::654.translation_literal: अग्य (ignorant) / अकोबिद (unwise) / अंध (blind) / अभागी (unfortunate) / काई (moss) / बिषय (sense-objects) / मुकुर (mirror) / मन (mind) / लागी (clung to) / लंपट (lustful) / कपटी (deceitful) / कुटिल (crooked) / बिसेषी (especially) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / संतसभा (company of the good) / नहिं (not) / देखी (seen)
ramacharitamanas::654.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::654.essence: A stained mind cannot recognise what is pure.
ramacharitamanas::654.simple_meaning: People trapped in desire cannot see clearly. Their minds are stained, their character is twisted, and they have never truly come near the company of the wise.
ramacharitamanas::654.simple_insight: Clarity begins when the mind stops being coated by craving.
ramacharitamanas::654.detailed_meaning: Shiva is answering Parvati in the Balkand, warning that some people reject Ram not from insight but from inner corruption. He describes minds covered by desire like a mirror coated with moss, unable to reflect truth or recognise the company of the good.
ramacharitamanas::654.modern_relevance: You keep arguing with a message, but the real issue is the fog in your own head. When craving, ego, or resentment takes over, even good advice sounds wrong.
ramacharitamanas::654.insight: It shifts attention from debating ideas to noticing the state of the mind that judges them.

ramacharitamanas::655.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं ते बेद असंमत बानी। जिन्ह कें सूझ लाभु नहिं हानी॥ मुकुर मलिन अरु नयन बिहीना। राम रूप देखहिं किमि दीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::655.verse_hindi: और जिन्हें अपने लाभ-हानि नहीं सूझती, वे ही ऐसी वेदविरुद्ध बातें कहा करते हैं, जिनका हृदय रूपी दर्पण मैला है और जो नेत्रों से हीन हैं, वे बेचारे श्री रामचन्द्रजी का रूप कैसे देखें! ॥
ramacharitamanas::655.english_translation: Those who cannot see gain or loss speak such contrary words. With a stained mirror and no eyes, how can the poor see Ram's form?
ramacharitamanas::655.translation_literal: कहहिं (speak) / ते (those) / बेद (Veda) / असंमत (not accepted) / बानी (speech) / जिन्ह कें (for whom) / सूझ (appears) / लाभु (gain) / नहिं (not) / हानी (loss) / मुकुर (mirror) / मलिन (stained) / अरु (and) / नयन (eyes) / बिहीना (without) / राम रूप (Ram's form) / देखहिं (see) / किमि (how) / दीना (poor ones)
ramacharitamanas::655.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::655.essence: Clouded seeing turns even Ram invisible.
ramacharitamanas::655.simple_meaning: People who cannot tell gain from loss end up speaking against what the Vedas teach. Their mind is dirty and their vision is gone, so they cannot recognize Ram's form.
ramacharitamanas::655.simple_insight: Clear seeing begins with an honest mind; without it, even the sacred looks invisible.
ramacharitamanas::655.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the kind of person who rejects devotion without real understanding. Their inner mirror is stained by desire and confusion, so they cannot perceive Ram's form or value what the Vedas point toward.
ramacharitamanas::655.modern_relevance: You dismiss a relationship, a teacher, or a hard truth because it threatens your comfort. Later, you realize the problem was never the thing itself — your own clouded seeing was blocking it.
ramacharitamanas::655.insight: It shifts attention from arguing with sacred truth to cleaning the mind that cannot receive it.

ramacharitamanas::656.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह कें अगुन न सगुन बिबेका। जल्पहिं कल्पित बचन अनेका॥ हरिमाया बस जगत भ्रमाहीं। तिन्हहि कहत कछु अघटित नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::656.verse_hindi: जिनको निर्गुण-सगुण का कुछ भी विवेक नहीं है, जो अनेक मनगढ़ंत बातें बका करते हैं, जो श्री हरि की माया के वश में होकर जगत में (जन्म-मृत्यु के चक्र में) भ्रमते फिरते हैं, उनके लिए कुछ भी कह डालना असंभव नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::656.english_translation: Those who lack discernment between the formless and the formed, who utter countless imagined words, wander the world under Hari's veil of illusion; for them, nothing impossible can be said.
ramacharitamanas::656.translation_literal: जिन्ह कें (for whom) / अगुन (without qualities, formless) / न (not) / सगुन (with qualities, formed) / बिबेका (discernment) / जल्पहिं (they speak) / कल्पित (imagined) / बचन (words) / अनेका (many) / हरिमाया (Hari's illusion) / बस (under the control of) / जगत (world) / भ्रमाहीं (they wander) / तिन्हहि (for them) / कहत (saying) / कछु (anything) / अघटित (impossible) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::656.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::656.essence: Without discernment, imagination starts sounding like fact.
ramacharitamanas::656.simple_meaning: People who cannot tell the difference between the formless and the formed get lost in imagination and confusion. Under the veil of illusion, even absurd claims can seem normal to them.
ramacharitamanas::656.simple_insight: Clear seeing protects you from confusion that sounds clever but goes nowhere.
ramacharitamanas::656.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still answering the earlier claim about who can truly see Ram's form. He says that people without discernment, trapped in Hari's illusion, wander in confusion and can end up saying anything at all.
ramacharitamanas::656.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with confident opinions, half-remembered facts, and dramatic certainty. You can feel the room tilt away from reality. This verse names that drift before it takes over.
ramacharitamanas::656.insight: It shifts attention from loud speculation to discernment between what is real and what is imagined.

ramacharitamanas::657.verse_sanskrit: बातुल भूत बिबस मतवारे। ते नहिं बोलहिं बचन बिचारे॥ जिन्ह कृत महामोह मद पाना। तिन्ह कर कहा करिअ नहिं काना ॥
ramacharitamanas::657.verse_hindi: जिन्हें वायु का रोग (सन्निपात, उन्माद आदि) हो गया हो, जो भूत के वश हो गए हैं और जो नशे में चूर हैं, ऐसे लोग विचारकर वचन नहीं बोलते। जिन्होंने महामोह रूपी मदिरा पी रखी है, उनके कहने पर कान नहीं देना चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::657.english_translation: People afflicted by madness, possessed by spirits, or drunk with intoxication do not speak thoughtfully. Do not listen to those who have drunk the wine of delusion.
ramacharitamanas::657.translation_literal: बातुल (mad) / भूत (spirits) / बिबस (helpless) / मतवारे (intoxicated) / ते (those) / नहिं (do not) / बोलहिं (speak) / बचन (words) / बिचारे (thoughtfully)॥ / जिन्ह (those who) / कृत (done) / महामोह (great delusion) / मद पाना (drunk wine) / तिन्ह कर (of them) / कहा (what) / करिअ (should be done) / नहिं (not) / काना (ear)॥
ramacharitamanas::657.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::657.essence: Delusion speaks loudly, but its words deserve no authority.
ramacharitamanas::657.simple_meaning: People lost to madness, possession, or intoxication do not speak wisely. The same is true of those drunk on deep delusion: their words should not guide you.
ramacharitamanas::657.simple_insight: Not every voice deserves your trust. Delusion can sound confident and still be empty.
ramacharitamanas::657.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is answering a line of skeptical argument in the Balkand. After saying that confused people cannot judge Ram properly, he adds a sharper comparison: minds overtaken by madness, spirits, or intoxication cannot speak with discernment. Their words are not reliable.
ramacharitamanas::657.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with hot takes at midnight, each one louder than the last. You do not have to treat every confident voice as clear sight.
ramacharitamanas::657.insight: It teaches you to separate volume from wisdom and refuse guidance from a clouded mind.

ramacharitamanas::658.verse_sanskrit: अस निज हृदयँ बिचारि तजु संसय भजु राम पद। सुनु गिरिराज कुमारि भ्रम तम रबि कर बचन मम ॥
ramacharitamanas::658.verse_hindi: अपने हृदय में ऐसा विचार कर संदेह छोड़ दो और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों को भजो। हे पार्वती! भ्रम रूपी अंधकार के नाश करने के लिए सूर्य की किरणों के समान मेरे वचनों को सुनो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::658.english_translation: Reflect thus in your own heart, give up doubt, and worship Ram's feet. Listen, O daughter of the mountain king: my words are like the sun's rays that destroy the darkness of confusion.
ramacharitamanas::658.translation_literal: अस (thus) / निज (own) / हृदयँ (heart) / बिचारि (having reflected) / तजु (give up) / संसय (doubt) / भजु (worship) / राम पद (Ram's feet) / सुनु (listen) / गिरिराज कुमारि (daughter of the mountain king) / भ्रम (confusion) / तम (darkness) / रबि कर (sun's rays) / बचन (words) / मम (my)
ramacharitamanas::658.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::658.essence: Clear seeing begins when doubt is surrendered to devotion.
ramacharitamanas::658.simple_meaning: Think carefully, drop your doubt, and turn to Ram with devotion. Shiva tells Parvati that his words can cut through confusion like sunlight.
ramacharitamanas::658.simple_insight: Doubt loses its grip when you reflect honestly and let devotion guide you.
ramacharitamanas::658.detailed_meaning: In the opening frame of the Ramcharitmanas, Shiva is answering Parvati's questions about Ram's nature. He tells her to examine the matter within her own heart, release doubt, and take refuge in Ram's feet, because his teaching will clear confusion like sunlight.
ramacharitamanas::658.modern_relevance: You are spiraling at 1:13 a.m., rereading the same message thread and making it mean everything. Stop, look inward, and let one clear principle cut the noise.
ramacharitamanas::658.insight: It shifts the mind from scattered speculation to inward reflection and devotional trust.

ramacharitamanas::659.verse_sanskrit: सगुनहि अगुनहि नहिं कछु भेदा। गावहिं मुनि पुरान बुध बेदा॥ अगुन अरूप अलख अज जोई। भगत प्रेम बस सगुन सो होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::659.verse_hindi: सगुण और निर्गुण में कुछ भी भेद नहीं है- मुनि, पुराण, पण्डित और वेद सभी ऐसा कहते हैं। जो निर्गुण, अरूप (निराकार), अलख (अव्यक्त) और अजन्मा है, वही भक्तों के प्रेमवश सगुण हो जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::659.english_translation: There is no difference at all between the manifest and the unmanifest. The sages, the Puranas, the wise, and the Vedas all sing this. The one who is unmanifest, formless, unseen, and unborn becomes manifest through the love of devotees.
ramacharitamanas::659.translation_literal: सगुनहि (in the manifest) / अगुनहि (in the unmanifest) / नहिं (not) / कछु (any) / भेदा (difference) / गावहिं (sing) / मुनि (sages) / पुरान (Puranas) / बुध (the wise) / बेदा (Vedas) / अगुन (unmanifest) / अरूप (formless) / अलख (unseen) / अज (unborn) / जोई (who) / भगत (devotees) / प्रेम (love) / बस (under the power of) / सगुन (manifest) / सो (that one) / होई (becomes)
ramacharitamanas::659.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::659.essence: Love turns the unseen into presence.
ramacharitamanas::659.simple_meaning: There is no real split between the formless divine and the visible form. The sages say the formless one appears in form through the love of devotees.
ramacharitamanas::659.simple_insight: Love is not a distraction from the divine; it is the way the divine becomes close enough to touch.
ramacharitamanas::659.detailed_meaning: In the Bala Kanda, the teaching turns from doubt to devotion. The speaker says that learned tradition agrees: the formless, unborn reality is not separate from form, because loving devotion draws that reality into a visible presence.
ramacharitamanas::659.modern_relevance: You feel something holy in a song, a face, or a small ritual at your kitchen counter. What seems invisible is not absent; love gives it shape you can meet.
ramacharitamanas::659.insight: It shifts the mind from treating form and formlessness as opposites to seeing devotion as the bridge between them.

ramacharitamanas::660.verse_sanskrit: जो गुन रहित सगुन सोइ कैसें। जलु हिम उपल बिलग नहिं जैसें॥ जासु नाम भ्रम तिमिर पतंगा। तेहि किमि कहिअ बिमोह प्रसंगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::660.verse_hindi: जो निर्गुण है वही सगुण कैसे है? जैसे जल और ओले में भेद नहीं। (दोनों जल ही हैं, ऐसे ही निर्गुण और सगुण एक ही हैं।) जिसका नाम भ्रम रूपी अंधकार के मिटाने के लिए सूर्य है, उसके लिए मोह का प्रसंग भी कैसे कहा जा सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::660.english_translation: How can the formless be different from the formed? Water and hail are not separate. How can delusion be spoken of for one whose name is the sun that destroys the darkness of confusion?
ramacharitamanas::660.translation_literal: जो (which) / गुन रहित (without qualities) / सगुन (with qualities) / सोइ (that same one) / कैसें (how) / जलु (water) / हिम (hail) / उपल (ice-stone) / बिलग (separate) / नहिं (not) / जैसें (as) / जासु (whose) / नाम (name) / भ्रम (confusion) / तिमिर (darkness) / पतंगा (sun) / तेहि (for that one) / किमि (how) / कहिअ (can be said) / बिमोह (delusion) / प्रसंगा (occasion)
ramacharitamanas::660.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::660.essence: Ram's form and formlessness are not two different truths.
ramacharitamanas::660.simple_meaning: The divine can appear with form and still remain beyond form. Ram's name itself removes confusion, so there is no real basis for doubt about his nature.
ramacharitamanas::660.simple_insight: You do not need to force a choice between heart and understanding. Reverence and clarity can point to the same reality.
ramacharitamanas::660.detailed_meaning: Parvati is listening as Shiva explains Ram's nature. The teaching has moved beyond simple devotion into a subtle point: Ram is both beyond form and present in form. Tulsidas uses this verse to erase the last trace of doubt.
ramacharitamanas::660.modern_relevance: You are trying to make sense of someone you deeply admire, but your mind keeps splitting them into contradictions. This verse says the split is in your seeing, not in the reality before you.
ramacharitamanas::660.insight: It shifts the mind from dividing form and essence to seeing them as one reality.

ramacharitamanas::661.verse_sanskrit: राम सच्चिदानंद दिनेसा। नहिं तहँ मोह निसा लवलेसा॥ सहज प्रकासरूप भगवाना। नहिं तहँ पुनि बिग्यान बिहाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::661.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी सच्चिदानन्दस्वरूप सूर्य हैं। वहाँ मोह रूपी रात्रि का लवलेश भी नहीं है। वे स्वभाव से ही प्रकाश रूप और (षडैश्वर्ययुक्त) भगवान है, वहाँ तो विज्ञान रूपी प्रातःकाल भी नहीं होता (अज्ञान रूपी रात्रि हो तब तो विज्ञान रूपी प्रातःकाल हो, भगवान तो नित्य ज्ञान स्वरूप हैं।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::661.english_translation: Ram is consciousness, being, and bliss, like the sun. There is not even the slightest darkness of delusion there. He is naturally radiant and the Lord himself; there is no need for dawn of understanding there.
ramacharitamanas::661.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सच्चिदानंद (existence-consciousness-bliss) / दिनेसा (sun) / नहिं (not) / तहँ (there) / मोह (delusion) / निसा (night) / लवलेसा (slightest trace) ॥ / सहज (natural) / प्रकासरूप (form of light) / भगवाना (the Lord) / नहिं (not) / तहँ (there) / पुनि (again) / बिग्यान (understanding) / बिहाना (dawn) ॥
ramacharitamanas::661.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::661.essence: Ram is pure radiance, where confusion cannot even begin.
ramacharitamanas::661.simple_meaning: Ram is pure awareness and bliss itself. In his presence, delusion has no place, and even the idea of a dawn after darkness does not apply.
ramacharitamanas::661.simple_insight: Some truths do not need to be discovered gradually; they simply shine and remove confusion at once.
ramacharitamanas::661.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is unfolding a philosophical vision of Ram as more than a heroic prince. After explaining that the divine has no real split between form and formlessness, he says Ram is pure radiance itself, beyond delusion and beyond any need for a later awakening.
ramacharitamanas::661.modern_relevance: You sit in the car after a hard conversation, replaying every line, trying to figure out what was real. This verse points to a clarity so complete that confusion cannot survive in it.
ramacharitamanas::661.insight: It shifts the mind from treating understanding as gradual repair to seeing clarity as a full illumination.

ramacharitamanas::662.verse_sanskrit: हरष बिषाद ग्यान अग्याना। जीव धर्म अहमिति अभिमाना॥ राम ब्रह्म ब्यापक जग जाना। परमानंद परेस पुराना ॥
ramacharitamanas::662.verse_hindi: हर्ष, शोक, ज्ञान, अज्ञान, अहंता और अभिमान- ये सब जीव के धर्म हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी तो व्यापक ब्रह्म, परमानन्दस्वरूप, परात्पर प्रभु और पुराण पुरुष हैं। इस बात को सारा जगत जानता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::662.english_translation: Joy and sorrow, knowledge and ignorance, the sense of separate self and pride — these belong to the embodied being. Ram is the all-pervading supreme reality, the bliss beyond all, the ancient supreme lord. Everyone in the world knows this.
ramacharitamanas::662.translation_literal: हरष (joy) / बिषाद (sorrow) / ग्यान (knowledge) / अग्याना (ignorance) / जीव (embodied being) / धर्म (nature) / अहमिति (I-ness) / अभिमाना (pride) ॥ राम (Ram) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / ब्यापक (all-pervading) / जग (world) / जाना (known) । परमानंद (supreme bliss) / परेस (supreme lord) / पुराना (ancient) ॥
ramacharitamanas::662.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::662.essence: Your moods and ego belong to change; Ram belongs to the vast.
ramacharitamanas::662.simple_meaning: Joy, sorrow, knowledge, ignorance, self-importance, and pride belong to the individual being. Ram is the all-pervading supreme reality, pure bliss, and the ancient supreme lord.
ramacharitamanas::662.simple_insight: It loosens the grip of moods and ego by placing them on one side, and Ram’s vastness on the other.
ramacharitamanas::662.detailed_meaning: In the opening of Balkand, Shiva’s frame narration is lifting Parvati beyond ordinary categories. After explaining that Ram is beyond the split of form and formlessness, the text now contrasts the changing states of a living being with Ram’s unchanging nature.
ramacharitamanas::662.modern_relevance: You check your phone after a harsh email and feel yourself swing from confidence to shame. The verse says those swings belong to the changing mind, not to the vast reality you rest in.
ramacharitamanas::662.insight: It trains the mind to separate passing mental states from the unchanging ground beneath them.

ramacharitamanas::663.verse_sanskrit: पुरुष प्रसिद्ध प्रकाश निधि प्रगट परावर नाथ। रघुकुलमनि मम स्वामि सोइ कहि सिवँ नायउ माथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::663.verse_hindi: जो (पुराण) पुरुष प्रसिद्ध हैं, प्रकाश के भंडार हैं, सब रूपों में प्रकट हैं, जीव, माया और जगत सबके स्वामी हैं, वे ही रघुकुल मणि श्री रामचन्द्रजी मेरे स्वामी हैं- ऐसा कहकर शिवजी ने उनको मस्तक नवाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::663.english_translation: Saying, "He is the famed Person, the storehouse of light, manifest in all forms, the lord of all beyond and within. He, the jewel of Raghu's line, is my master," Shiva bowed his head.
ramacharitamanas::663.translation_literal: पुरुष (Person) / प्रसिद्ध (famed) / प्रकाश (light) / निधि (storehouse) / प्रगट (manifest) / परावर (beyond and within) / नाथ (lord) / रघुकुलमनि (jewel of the Raghu line) / मम (my) / स्वामि (master) / सोइ (that very one) / कहि (saying) / सिवँ (Shiva) / नायउ (bowed) / माथ (head)
ramacharitamanas::663.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::663.simple_meaning: Shiva identifies Ram as the supreme master, the source of light, and bows in reverence.
ramacharitamanas::663.simple_insight: Reverence becomes natural when you recognise greatness clearly.
ramacharitamanas::663.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, Shiva is speaking about Ram's true nature, not merely praising him politely. He names Ram as the lord of all realms and then bows his head, showing that even divine knowledge ends in devotion.
ramacharitamanas::663.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm changes the whole room, and your ego softens without argument. Recognition turns into respect before you even plan it.
ramacharitamanas::663.insight: It shifts the mind from intellectual description to lived reverence.

ramacharitamanas::664.verse_sanskrit: निज भ्रम नहिं समुझहिं अग्यानी। प्रभु पर मोह धरहिं जड़ प्रानी॥ जथा गगन घन पटल निहारी। झाँपेउ भानु कहहिं कुबिचारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::664.verse_hindi: अज्ञानी मनुष्य अपने भ्रम को तो समझते नहीं और वे मूर्ख प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी पर उसका आरोप करते हैं, जैसे आकाश में बादलों का परदा देखकर कुविचारी (अज्ञानी) लोग कहते हैं कि बादलों ने सूर्य को ढँक लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::664.english_translation: Ignorant people do not understand their own confusion. Deluded beings blame the divine, just as foolish people see clouds in the sky and say the sun has been covered.
ramacharitamanas::664.translation_literal: निज (one's own) / भ्रम (delusion) / नहिं (not) / समुझहिं (understand) / अग्यानी (the ignorant) / प्रभु (the Lord) / पर (on) / मोह (delusion) / धरहिं (place) / जड़ (dull) / प्रानी (creatures) / जथा (just as) / गगन (sky) / घन (cloud) / पटल (veil/layer) / निहारी (seeing) / झाँपेउ (covered) / भानु (sun) / कहहिं (say) / कुबिचारी (ill-thinking people)
ramacharitamanas::664.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::664.essence: Confusion blames the divine for what it cannot see.
ramacharitamanas::664.simple_meaning: People who are confused do not see their own confusion. Instead, they blame Ram, like someone who mistakes clouds for the sun being gone.
ramacharitamanas::664.simple_insight: It brings humility: the mind often blames what it cannot yet understand.
ramacharitamanas::664.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is deepening a teaching in Balkand: Ram is the supreme reality, yet confused minds project their own blindness onto him. The image is simple and sharp — clouds do not cover the sun, but foolish people think they do.
ramacharitamanas::664.modern_relevance: You read a message in a bad mood and decide the other person is cold. Later you realise your own fear was doing the talking. The verse points to that mistake before it hardens into blame.
ramacharitamanas::664.insight: It shifts blame inward first: check your perception before judging what you see.

ramacharitamanas::665.verse_sanskrit: चितव जो लोचन अंगुलि लाएँ। प्रगट जुगल ससि तेहि के भाएँ॥ उमा राम बिषइक अस मोहा। नभ तम धूम धूरि जिमि सोहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::665.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य आँख में अँगुली लगाकर देखता है, उसके लिए तो दो चन्द्रमा प्रकट (प्रत्यक्ष) हैं। हे पार्वती! श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विषय में इस प्रकार मोह की कल्पना करना वैसा ही है, जैसा आकाश में अंधकार, धुएँ और धूल का सोहना (दिखना)। (आकाश जैसे निर्मल और निर्लेप है, उसको कोई मलिन या स्पर्श नहीं कर सकता, इसी प्रकार भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी नित्य निर्मल और निर्लेप हैं।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::665.english_translation: If a person looks with a finger in the eye, two moons seem visible. O Uma, imagining such delusion about Ram is like seeing darkness, smoke, and dust in the sky.
