ramacharitamanas::665.translation_literal: चितव (looks) / जो (who) / लोचन (eye) / अंगुलि (finger) / लाएँ (having placed) / प्रगट (visible) / जुगल (two) / ससि (moons) / तेहि (to that one) / के भाएँ (appear) / उमा (Uma) / राम (Ram) / बिषइक (regarding) / अस (such) / मोहा (delusion) / नभ (sky) / तम (darkness) / धूम (smoke) / धूरि (dust) / जिमि (like) / सोहा (appears beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::665.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::665.essence: Confusion distorts vision; Ram's purity is never the problem.
ramacharitamanas::665.simple_meaning: A confused mind can project impurity onto Ram, just as an eye pressed by a finger can see two moons. Ram is never actually stained.
ramacharitamanas::665.simple_insight: What you see can be distorted by your own confusion. Clear seeing restores reverence and removes blame.
ramacharitamanas::665.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is answering a mistaken way of looking at Ram in the Balkand frame. He tells Parvati that just as a strained eye sees two moons, a confused mind imagines fault in Ram. The problem is the viewer, not Ram's purity.
ramacharitamanas::665.modern_relevance: You read one harsh comment and suddenly the whole person looks corrupt. The distortion may be in your own hurt, not in what they truly are.
ramacharitamanas::665.insight: It shifts attention from judging the object to examining the lens that is judging it.

ramacharitamanas::666.verse_sanskrit: बिषय करन सुर जीव समेता। सकल एक तें एक सचेता॥ सब कर परम प्रकासक जोई। राम अनादि अवधपति सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::666.verse_hindi: विषय, इन्द्रियाँ, इन्द्रियों के देवता और जीवात्मा- ये सब एक की सहायता से एक चेतन होते हैं। (अर्थात विषयों का प्रकाश इन्द्रियों से, इन्द्रियों का इन्द्रियों के देवताओं से और इन्द्रिय देवताओं का चेतन जीवात्मा से प्रकाश होता है।) इन सबका जो परम प्रकाशक है (अर्थात जिससे इन सबका प्रकाश होता है), वही अनादि ब्रह्म अयोध्या नरेश श्री रामचन्द्रजी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::666.english_translation: The objects of sense, the senses, the presiding beings of the senses, and the individual being all become conscious through one source. The supreme illuminator of all is that same beginningless Ram, lord of Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::666.translation_literal: बिषय (sense objects) / करन (senses) / सुर (presiding beings) / जीव समेता (together with the individual being) / सकल (all) / एक तें (through one) / एक (one by one) / सचेता (made conscious) ॥ / सब कर (of all) / परम प्रकासक (supreme illuminator) / जोई (who) / राम (Ram) / अनादि (beginningless) / अवधपति (lord of Ayodhya) / सोई (that same) ॥
ramacharitamanas::666.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::666.essence: All awareness shines because Ram is already shining through it.
ramacharitamanas::666.simple_meaning: Everything in experience depends on one supreme source for its awareness and existence. Ram is that beginningless source of all light.
ramacharitamanas::666.simple_insight: The world feels separate, but its life comes from one hidden source.
ramacharitamanas::666.detailed_meaning: In the Uttarkand-style philosophical flow, Tulsidas explains that sense objects, senses, their presiding beings, and the individual being all borrow awareness from one source. The point is to lift the listener beyond appearances and identify Ram as the supreme illuminator behind all consciousness.
ramacharitamanas::666.modern_relevance: You are staring at three screens, a buzzing phone, and a mind split in ten directions. The verse cuts through the noise: every bit of awareness you have is borrowed from a deeper source.
ramacharitamanas::666.insight: It shifts attention from fragmented experience to the single reality that makes experience possible.

ramacharitamanas::667.verse_sanskrit: जगत प्रकास्य प्रकासक रामू। मायाधीस ग्यान गुन धामू॥ जासु सत्यता तें जड़ माया। भास सत्य इव मोह सहाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::667.verse_hindi: यह जगत प्रकाश्य है और श्री रामचन्द्रजी इसके प्रकाशक हैं। वे माया के स्वामी और ज्ञान तथा गुणों के धाम हैं। जिनकी सत्ता से, मोह की सहायता पाकर जड़ माया भी सत्य सी भासित होती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::667.english_translation: Ram is the light that reveals the world. He is the master of maya and the source of knowledge and qualities. By his reality, inert maya appears real through the help of delusion.
ramacharitamanas::667.translation_literal: जगत (world) / प्रकास्य (that which is to be illuminated) / प्रकासक (illuminator) / रामू (Ram) / मायाधीस (master of maya) / ग्यान (knowledge) / गुन (qualities) / धामू (abode/source) / जासु (whose) / सत्यता (reality) / तें (through) / जड़ (inert) / माया (maya) / भास (appears) / सत्य इव (as if real) / मोह (delusion) / सहाया (with the help of)
ramacharitamanas::667.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::667.essence: Ram is the light that makes even illusion seem real.
ramacharitamanas::667.simple_meaning: Ram is the light that makes the world visible. He rules maya and is the source of knowledge and good qualities. Even illusion seems real only because of his reality.
ramacharitamanas::667.simple_insight: What seems most solid may be only a surface effect. Trust the deeper source that makes everything visible.
ramacharitamanas::667.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still explaining to Parvati why ordinary sight is unreliable. After saying the world depends on a single source of awareness, he names that source: Ram. In this verse, Ram is not just a person in the story but the light by which reality is known.
ramacharitamanas::667.modern_relevance: You stare at a message thread and build a whole story from three words. Later, you realize you were reacting to your own projection. This verse points to the light behind the projection.
ramacharitamanas::667.insight: It shifts attention from appearances to the source that makes appearances possible.

ramacharitamanas::668.verse_sanskrit: रजत सीप महुँ भास जिमि जथा भानु कर बारि। जदपि मृषा तिहुँ काल सोइ भ्रम न सकइ कोउ टारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::668.verse_hindi: जैसे सीप में चाँदी की और सूर्य की किरणों में पानी की (बिना हुए भी) प्रतीति होती है। यद्यपि यह प्रतीति तीनों कालों में झूठ है, तथापि इस भ्रम को कोई हटा नहीं सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::668.english_translation: As silver appears in mother-of-pearl and water appears in sunbeams, so the unreal appears real. Though false in all three times, no one can remove that illusion.
ramacharitamanas::668.translation_literal: रजत (silver) / सीप (mother-of-pearl) / महुँ (in) / भास (appears) / जिमि (as) / जथा (as) / भानु (sun) / कर (of) / बारि (water) / जदपि (although) / मृषा (false) / तिहुँ (three) / काल (times) / सोइ (that) / भ्रम (illusion) / न (not) / सकइ (can) / कोउ (anyone) / टारि (remove)
ramacharitamanas::668.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::668.essence: False appearance can feel real even after it is disproved.
ramacharitamanas::668.simple_meaning: What seems real can be only an illusion, like silver seen in shell or water seen in sunlight. Even knowing it is false, the mind may still not let go of the mistake.
ramacharitamanas::668.simple_insight: Seeing clearly is not the same as seeing perfectly; old illusions can keep their grip.
ramacharitamanas::668.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is explaining how Ram alone is the light behind all appearance. In this doha, he gives a familiar example: shell looks like silver, and sunlight can seem like water. The point is that false appearance can persist even when reason knows better.
ramacharitamanas::668.modern_relevance: You double-check the message, know the rumor is baseless, and still feel your stomach tighten. The mind can keep projecting what is not there.
ramacharitamanas::668.insight: It trains the reader to question appearances and notice how perception can mistake one thing for another.

ramacharitamanas::669.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि जग हरि आश्रित रहई। जदपि असत्य देत दुख अहई॥ जौं सपनें सिर काटै कोई। बिनु जागें न दूरि दुख होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::669.verse_hindi: इसी तरह यह संसार भगवान के आश्रित रहता है। यद्यपि यह असत्य है, तो भी दुःख तो देता ही है, जिस तरह स्वप्न में कोई सिर काट ले तो बिना जागे वह दुःख दूर नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::669.english_translation: In this way, the world remains dependent on Hari. Though unreal, it still causes suffering, just as if someone cuts off a head in a dream, the pain does not end until waking.
ramacharitamanas::669.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / जग (world) / हरि (Hari) / आश्रित (dependent) / रहई (remains) / जदपि (although) / असत्य (unreal) / देत (gives) / दुख (pain) / अहई (is) / जौं (if) / सपनें (in a dream) / सिर (head) / काटै (cuts) / कोई (someone) / बिनु (without) / जागें (waking) / न (not) / दूरि (removed) / दुख (pain) / होई (is)
ramacharitamanas::669.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::669.essence: Illusion can hurt until awareness wakes up.
ramacharitamanas::669.simple_meaning: The world may not be ultimately real, but it still produces suffering. Like a dream injury, its pain lasts until awareness changes.
ramacharitamanas::669.simple_insight: You do not escape pain by denying it. You escape it by waking up to what is actually real.
ramacharitamanas::669.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, the narration is explaining how Ram relates to the world he sustains. The world depends on Hari, yet its appearances can still wound like a nightmare. The point is to show why illusion hurts until true understanding arrives.
ramacharitamanas::669.modern_relevance: You replay a humiliating message in bed at 2 a.m., and your chest still tightens even though the moment is over. The event passed, but the mind kept it alive.
ramacharitamanas::669.insight: It shifts attention from arguing with appearances to seeing how the mind manufactures suffering from them.

ramacharitamanas::670.verse_sanskrit: जासु कृपाँ अस भ्रम मिटि जाई। गिरिजा सोइ कृपाल रघुराई॥ आदि अंत कोउ जासु न पावा। मति अनुमानि निगम अस गावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::670.verse_hindi: हे पार्वती! जिनकी कृपा से इस प्रकार का भ्रम मिट जाता है, वही कृपालु श्री रघुनाथजी हैं। जिनका आदि और अंत किसी ने नहीं (जान) पाया। वेदों ने अपनी बुद्धि से अनुमान करके इस प्रकार (नीचे लिखे अनुसार) गाया है- ॥
ramacharitamanas::670.english_translation: O Girija, the compassionate Raghunath alone is the one whose grace removes such confusion. No one has found his beginning or end. The Vedas sing of him by reasoning and inference.
ramacharitamanas::670.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / कृपाँ (by grace) / अस (such) / भ्रम (confusion) / मिटि जाई (is removed) / गिरिजा (O Girija) / सोइ (that same) / कृपाल (compassionate) / रघुराई (Raghunath) / आदि (beginning) / अंत (end) / कोउ (anyone) / जासु (of whom) / न (not) / पावा (found) / मति (intellect) / अनुमानि (by inference) / निगम (the Vedas) / अस (thus) / गावा (sang)
ramacharitamanas::670.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::670.essence: Grace clears confusion; the supreme reality remains beyond full measure.
ramacharitamanas::670.simple_meaning: Ram's grace clears confusion. His beginning and end cannot be found, and even the Vedas describe him only through reasoned hints.
ramacharitamanas::670.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that the deepest truth is not grasped by force, but received through grace.
ramacharitamanas::670.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the Balkand frame, explaining Ram as the reality that ends confusion. The verse moves from grace to mystery: Ram can clear the mind, yet no one can fully trace his beginning or end, so even the Vedas speak of him indirectly.
ramacharitamanas::670.modern_relevance: You keep rereading the same paragraph, sure the answer should finally click. Then a calmer mind sees what effort missed: some things are understood only when confusion falls away.
ramacharitamanas::670.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to master the ultimate with logic alone to receiving understanding through a clearer state of mind.

ramacharitamanas::671.verse_sanskrit: बिनु पद चलइ सुनइ बिनु काना। कर बिनु करम करइ बिधि नाना॥ आनन रहित सकल रस भोगी। बिनु बानी बकता बड़ जोगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::671.verse_hindi: वह (ब्रह्म) बिना ही पैर के चलता है, बिना ही कान के सुनता है, बिना ही हाथ के नाना प्रकार के काम करता है, बिना मुँह (जिव्हा) के ही सारे (छहों) रसों का आनंद लेता है और बिना ही वाणी के बहुत योग्य वक्ता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::671.english_translation: Without feet, it walks; without ears, it hears. Without hands, it performs countless acts. Without a mouth, it enjoys every flavor. Without speech, it is a great speaker.
ramacharitamanas::671.translation_literal: बिनु (without) / पद (feet) / चलइ (walks) / सुनइ (hears) / बिनु (without) / काना (ears) / कर (hands) / बिनु (without) / करम (actions) / करइ (does) / बिधि (modes) / नाना (many) / आनन (mouth) / रहित (without) / सकल (all) / रस (flavors) / भोगी (one who enjoys) / बिनु (without) / बानी (speech) / बकता (speaker) / बड़ (great) / जोगी (sage)
ramacharitamanas::671.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::671.essence: The supreme reality acts freely without needing a body.
ramacharitamanas::671.simple_meaning: The supreme reality is beyond physical limits. It acts, hears, sees, enjoys, and speaks without needing a body like ours.
ramacharitamanas::671.simple_insight: What seems impossible to the senses becomes natural when the mind stops limiting reality.
ramacharitamanas::671.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing Ram's supreme nature through paradox. After saying the divine cannot be grasped by ordinary confusion, he shows that the supreme reality is not trapped by body, senses, or speech. This verse begins that explanation.
ramacharitamanas::671.modern_relevance: A child asks how you can know someone who is far away. You answer with presence, not hardware. The deepest reality does not need a body to be fully active.
ramacharitamanas::671.insight: It shifts the mind from physical limitation to divine freedom.

ramacharitamanas::672.verse_sanskrit: तन बिनु परस नयन बिनु देखा। ग्रहइ घ्रान बिनु बास असेषा॥ असि सब भाँति अलौकिक करनी। महिमा जासु जाइ नहिं बरनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::672.verse_hindi: वह बिना ही शरीर (त्वचा) के स्पर्श करता है, बिना ही आँखों के देखता है और बिना ही नाक के सब गंधों को ग्रहण करता है (सूँघता है)। उस ब्रह्म की करनी सभी प्रकार से ऐसी अलौकिक है कि जिसकी महिमा कही नहीं जा सकती ॥
ramacharitamanas::672.english_translation: He touches without a body, sees without eyes, and perceives every scent without a nose. In every way, that supreme reality acts in a way beyond the ordinary, and its greatness cannot be described.
ramacharitamanas::672.translation_literal: तन (body) / बिनु (without) / परस (touching) / नयन (eyes) / बिनु (without) / देखा (seeing) / ग्रहइ (grasps) / घ्रान (nose) / बिनु (without) / बास (smell) / असेषा (all, complete) / असि (such) / सब (all) / भाँति (ways) / अलौकिक (beyond the ordinary) / करनी (action, conduct) / महिमा (greatness) / जासु (whose) / जाइ (can be) / नहिं (not) / बरनी (described)
ramacharitamanas::672.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::672.essence: The supreme reality works beyond every human limit.
ramacharitamanas::672.simple_meaning: The supreme reality is not limited by a body or senses. It can perceive and act in ways ordinary beings cannot understand or describe.
ramacharitamanas::672.simple_insight: You are being asked to stop measuring the divine by human limits.
ramacharitamanas::672.detailed_meaning: Shiva continues explaining Ram's nature to Parvati. After saying Ram is beyond ordinary beginnings and endings, he shows that Ram's actions are not bound by body, eyes, ears, or nose. This is a direct glimpse into Ram's divine nature.
ramacharitamanas::672.modern_relevance: You try to explain a person you love, but words keep falling short. Some realities cannot be boxed into ordinary categories — they are known by their effect, not by measurement.
ramacharitamanas::672.insight: It shifts the mind from literal expectation to reverent recognition of what exceeds ordinary form.

ramacharitamanas::673.verse_sanskrit: जेहि इमि गावहिं बेद बुध जाहि धरहिं मुनि ध्यान। सोइ दसरथ सुत भगत हित कोसलपति भगवान ॥
ramacharitamanas::673.verse_hindi: जिसका वेद और पंडित इस प्रकार वर्णन करते हैं और मुनि जिसका ध्यान धरते हैं, वही दशरथनंदन, भक्तों के हितकारी, अयोध्या के स्वामी भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::673.english_translation: The one whom the Vedas and the wise describe, and whom sages meditate upon, is the same Ram, son of Dasharath, friend of devotees, and Lord of Kosala.
ramacharitamanas::673.translation_literal: जेहि (whom) / इमि (thus) / गावहिं (sing/praise) / बेद (the Vedas) / बुध (the wise) / जाहि (whom) / धरहिं (hold) / मुनि (sages) / ध्यान (meditation) / सोइ (that very one) / दसरथ सुत (son of Dasharath) / भगत हित (for devotees' welfare) / कोसलपति (lord of Kosala) / भगवान (the divine Lord)
ramacharitamanas::673.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::673.essence: The highest reality is the same Ram who protects devotees.
ramacharitamanas::673.simple_meaning: The Vedas and wise teachers speak of Ram, and sages meditate on him. He is Dasharath's son, the protector of devotees, and the lord of Kosala.
ramacharitamanas::673.simple_insight: It feels reassuring to know the highest reality is also a loving king who cares for devotees.
ramacharitamanas::673.detailed_meaning: Shiva's frame narration is moving from description of Ram's nature into praise of his identity. After saying the divine acts without ordinary limits, the verse names that same presence as Ram of Ayodhya — the beloved of devotees and sovereign of Kosala.
ramacharitamanas::673.modern_relevance: You hear a hymn in a temple, then see a father carrying his sleeping child home through the rain. The same greatness can be intimate, near, and protective.
ramacharitamanas::673.insight: It shifts the mind from abstract divinity to a personal, approachable presence that can be loved and trusted.

ramacharitamanas::674.verse_sanskrit: कासीं मरत जंतु अवलोकी। जासु नाम बल करउँ बिसोकी॥ सोइ प्रभु मोर चराचर स्वामी। रघुबर सब उर अंतरजामी ॥
ramacharitamanas::674.verse_hindi: (हे पार्वती !) जिनके नाम के बल से काशी में मरते हुए प्राणी को देखकर मैं उसे (राम मंत्र देकर) शोकरहित कर देता हूँ (मुक्त कर देता हूँ), वही मेरे प्रभु रघुश्रेष्ठ श्री रामचन्द्रजी जड़-चेतन के स्वामी और सबके हृदय के भीतर की जानने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::674.english_translation: O Parvati, seeing a being dying in Kashi, I free it from sorrow by the power of whose name. That same Lord is my master of all moving and unmoving beings, Raghu's श्रेष्ठ, the indweller in every heart.
ramacharitamanas::674.translation_literal: कासीं (in Kashi) / मरत (dying) / जंतु (being) / अवलोकी (seeing) / जासु (whose) / नाम (name) / बल (power) / करउँ (I do) / बिसोकी (free from sorrow) / सोइ (that same) / प्रभु (Lord) / मोर (my) / चराचर (moving and unmoving) / स्वामी (master) / रघुबर (Raghu's श्रेष्ठ) / सब (all) / उर (heart) / अंतरजामी (inner-knower)
ramacharitamanas::674.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::674.essence: Ram's name reaches where fear and death cannot.
ramacharitamanas::674.simple_meaning: Shiva says Ram's name has such power that it can free a dying being from sorrow. He calls Ram the master of all beings and the indweller of every heart.
ramacharitamanas::674.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that surrender to Ram's name is enough, even at the edge of death.
ramacharitamanas::674.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the Balkand frame. He describes Ram's name as so powerful that even a dying being in Kashi can be freed from sorrow. This leads into his praise of Ram as the master of all beings and the inner knower of every heart.
ramacharitamanas::674.modern_relevance: At a hospital bedside, words fail and everyone grows quiet. In that moment, this verse says the deepest help is not control but a name, a presence, and trust that reaches beyond fear.
ramacharitamanas::674.insight: It shifts devotion from ritual performance to inward reliance on Ram's name and presence.

ramacharitamanas::675.verse_sanskrit: बिबसहुँ जासु नाम नर कहहीं। जनम अनेक रचित अघ दहहीं॥ सादर सुमिरन जे नर करहीं। भव बारिधि गोपद इव तरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::675.verse_hindi: विवश होकर (बिना इच्छा के) भी जिनका नाम लेने से मनुष्यों के अनेक जन्मों में किए हुए पाप जल जाते हैं। फिर जो मनुष्य आदरपूर्वक उनका स्मरण करते हैं, वे तो संसार रूपी (दुस्तर) समुद्र को गाय के खुर से बने हुए गड्ढे के समान (अर्थात बिना किसी परिश्रम के) पार कर जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::675.english_translation: Even without intention, people speak that name, and sins from many births burn away. Those who remember that name with reverence cross the ocean of becoming as easily as a cow's hoofprint.
ramacharitamanas::675.translation_literal: बिबसहुँ (even without wish) / जासु (whose) / नाम (name) / नर (people) / कहहीं (speak) / जनम (births) / अनेक (many) / रचित (done) / अघ (sins) / दहहीं (burn away) / सादर (with reverence) / सुमिरन (remembering) / जे (those who) / नर (people) / करहीं (do) / भव (worldly becoming) / बारिधि (ocean) / गोपद (cow's hoofprint) / इव (like) / तरहीं (cross)
ramacharitamanas::675.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::675.essence: Ram's name turns burden into passage.
ramacharitamanas::675.simple_meaning: Even saying Ram's name can burn away the burden of past wrongs. Remembering Him with reverence carries a person across the cycle of suffering with ease.
ramacharitamanas::675.simple_insight: You do not have to be perfect before turning toward Ram. Sincere remembrance itself begins to clear the way.
ramacharitamanas::675.detailed_meaning: In the opening of Balkand, Shiva explains Ram's divine power to Parvati. He says the name itself has such force that even casual utterance can burn away accumulated wrongs, while reverent remembrance carries a devotee across the vast ocean of worldly becoming.
ramacharitamanas::675.modern_relevance: You are half-distracted, whispering a prayer before a hard phone call. Nothing around you has changed, yet your chest loosens. That is the power this verse points to: remembrance can move you before circumstances do.
ramacharitamanas::675.insight: It shifts attention from self-improvement alone to the transforming power of devoted remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::676.verse_sanskrit: राम सो परमातमा भवानी। तहँ भ्रम अति अबिहित तव बानी॥ अस संसय आनत उर माहीं। ग्यान बिराग सकल गुन जाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::676.verse_hindi: हे पार्वती! वही परमात्मा श्री रामचन्द्रजी हैं। उनमें भ्रम (देखने में आता) है, तुम्हारा ऐसा कहना अत्यन्त ही अनुचित है। इस प्रकार का संदेह मन में लाते ही मनुष्य के ज्ञान, वैराग्य आदि सारे सद्गुण नष्ट हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::676.english_translation: O Bhavani, Ram is the supreme reality. To see confusion in him is utterly improper. Once doubt enters the heart, wisdom, detachment, and every noble quality are destroyed.
ramacharitamanas::676.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सो (that) / परमातमा (supreme reality) / भवानी (Bhavani) / तहँ (there) / भ्रम (delusion/confusion) / अति (very) / अबिहित (wrong/improper) / तव (your) / बानी (speech)॥ / अस (such) / संसय (doubt) / आनत (bringing) / उर (heart) / माहीं (within) / ग्यान (wisdom) / बिराग (detachment) / सकल (all) / गुन (qualities) / जाहीं (go away)॥
ramacharitamanas::676.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::676.essence: Doubt about Ram destroys the very qualities needed to know him.
ramacharitamanas::676.simple_meaning: Ram is the supreme reality, and doubting him is a serious mistake. Doubt does not stay small; it weakens wisdom, detachment, and every good quality.
ramacharitamanas::676.simple_insight: Clear faith protects the heart. Doubt does not just question — it erodes what is best in you.
ramacharitamanas::676.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the opening frame of the story. She has raised a doubt about Ram's nature, and Shiva answers sharply: Ram is the supreme reality, and such confusion is unworthy. The warning is that doubt corrodes wisdom and detachment.
ramacharitamanas::676.modern_relevance: You hear one cynical comment about someone you trust, and suddenly your whole mind starts rearranging the story. This verse warns how quickly doubt can poison clarity, restraint, and steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::676.insight: It shifts the mind from entertaining suspicion to protecting clear understanding.

ramacharitamanas::677.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सिव के भ्रम भंजन बचना। मिटि गै सब कुतरक कै रचना॥ भइ रघुपति पद प्रीति प्रतीती। दारुन असंभावना बीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::677.verse_hindi: शिवजी के भ्रमनाशक वचनों को सुनकर पार्वतीजी के सब कुतर्कों की रचना मिट गई। श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों में उनका प्रेम और विश्वास हो गया और कठिन असम्भावना (जिसका होना- सम्भव नहीं, ऐसी मिथ्या कल्पना) जाती रही! ॥
ramacharitamanas::677.english_translation: Hearing Shiva’s words that shattered doubt, all of Parvati’s twisted arguments vanished. Her love and trust in the feet of Raghupati arose, and the impossible doubt was gone.
ramacharitamanas::677.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सिव (Shiva) के (of) / भ्रम (doubt) / भंजन (shattering) / बचना (words) / मिटि गै (were erased) / सब (all) / कुतरक (crooked arguments) / कै (of) / रचना (formation)॥ भइ (became) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / पद (feet) / प्रीति (love) / प्रतीती (trust) / दारुन (terrible) / असंभावना (impossibility) / बीती (passed away)॥
ramacharitamanas::677.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::677.essence: Doubt falls away when trust in Ram takes root.
ramacharitamanas::677.simple_meaning: Parvati hears Shiva’s clear words and her doubts disappear. Love and trust in Ram replace confusion.
ramacharitamanas::677.simple_insight: Clear words can break a mind’s resistance and open the heart to trust.
ramacharitamanas::677.detailed_meaning: In Shiva’s conversation with Parvati, her skeptical arguments collapse under his direct explanation of Ram’s nature. What remains is not debate, but devotion: trust in Raghupati’s feet and the end of impossible doubt.
ramacharitamanas::677.modern_relevance: You’ve argued yourself into a corner at 1:13 a.m., rereading the same message and making the worst-case story bigger. Then one honest sentence from someone you trust cuts through it.
ramacharitamanas::677.insight: It shifts the mind from suspicion to trust by showing that clarity can dissolve overthinking.

ramacharitamanas::678.verse_sanskrit: पुनि पुनि प्रभु पद कमल गहि जोरि पंकरुह पानि। बोलीं गिरिजा बचन बर मनहुँ प्रेम रस सानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::678.verse_hindi: बार- बार स्वामी (शिवजी) के चरणकमलों को पकड़कर और अपने कमल के समान हाथों को जोड़कर पार्वतीजी मानो प्रेमरस में सानकर सुंदर वचन बोलीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::678.english_translation: Again and again, holding the Lord's lotus feet and folding her lotus-like hands, Girija spoke beautiful words, as if mixed with the nectar of love.
ramacharitamanas::678.translation_literal: पुनि पुनि (again and again) / प्रभु (lord) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / गहि (grasping) / जोरि (joining) / पंकरुह (lotus-like) / पानि (hands) / बोलीं (spoke) / गिरिजा (Girija) / बचन (words) / बर (excellent) / मनहुँ (as if) / प्रेम (love) / रस (nectar/essence) / सानि (mixed, kneaded)
ramacharitamanas::678.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::678.essence: Love turns surrender into beautiful speech.
ramacharitamanas::678.simple_meaning: Parvati, moved by love, bows again and again to Shiva and speaks with a heart softened by devotion.
ramacharitamanas::678.simple_insight: Love makes the heart gentle enough to listen, yield, and speak beautifully.
ramacharitamanas::678.detailed_meaning: Parvati has just heard Shiva clear away her doubts about Ram. In response, she repeatedly grasps Shiva's feet and folds her hands, then speaks from a heart fully softened by love and trust. This verse shows her humility before the next revelation.
ramacharitamanas::678.modern_relevance: After a hard conversation, you finally realize the other person was right. Your shoulders drop, your hands unclench, and gratitude replaces the urge to argue.
ramacharitamanas::678.insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to reverent listening.

ramacharitamanas::679.verse_sanskrit: ससि कर सम सुनि गिरा तुम्हारी। मिटा मोह सरदातप भारी॥ तुम्ह कृपाल सबु संसउ हरेऊ। राम स्वरूप जानि मोहि परेऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::679.verse_hindi: आपकी चन्द्रमा की किरणों के समान शीतल वाणी सुनकर मेरा अज्ञान रूपी शरद-ऋतु (क्वार) की धूप का भारी ताप मिट गया। हे कृपालु! आपने मेरा सब संदेह हर लिया, अब श्री रामचन्द्रजी का यथार्थ स्वरूप मेरी समझ में आ गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::679.english_translation: Hearing your speech, clear as moonbeams, the heavy heat of autumn confusion has vanished. O compassionate one, you have removed all doubt; now I understand the true form of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::679.translation_literal: ससि (moon) / कर (ray) / सम (like) / सुनि (hearing) / गिरा (speech) / तुम्हारी (your) / मिटा (vanished) / मोह (delusion) / सरदातप (autumn heat) / भारी (heavy) / तुम्ह (you) / कृपाल (compassionate one) / सबु (all) / संसउ (doubt) / हरेऊ (removed) / राम (Ram) / स्वरूप (true form) / जानि (knowing) / मोहि (to me) / परेऊ (became clear)
ramacharitamanas::679.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::679.essence: Compassionate words can dissolve confusion and reveal Ram clearly.
ramacharitamanas::679.simple_meaning: Parvati says Shiva's gentle words have removed her confusion and doubts. She now understands Ram more clearly.
ramacharitamanas::679.simple_insight: Real understanding feels like cool relief after a long, exhausting heat.
ramacharitamanas::679.detailed_meaning: Parvati has been asking Shiva to clear away her doubts about Ram. After hearing his compassionate answer, she feels her confusion dissolve. This verse marks the moment her understanding settles into certainty.
ramacharitamanas::679.modern_relevance: You finally talk to someone who explains the thing you've been circling for weeks. The tension drops, and what felt tangled suddenly looks simple.
ramacharitamanas::679.insight: It shifts the mind from suspicion to clear seeing, where doubt no longer rules the heart.

ramacharitamanas::680.verse_sanskrit: नाथ कृपाँ अब गयउ बिषादा। सुखी भयउँ प्रभु चरन प्रसादा॥ अब मोहि आपनि किंकरि जानी। जदपि सहज जड़ नारि अयानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::680.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! आपकी कृपा से अब मेरा विषाद जाता रहा और आपके चरणों के अनुग्रह से मैं सुखी हो गई। यद्यपि मैं स्त्री होने के कारण स्वभाव से ही मूर्ख और ज्ञानहीन हूँ, तो भी अब आप मुझे अपनी दासी जानकर- ॥
ramacharitamanas::680.english_translation: By your grace, O Lord, my sorrow is gone, and by the favor of your feet I have become joyful. Though I am naturally dull and ignorant, still know me as your servant.
ramacharitamanas::680.translation_literal: नाथ (Lord) / कृपाँ (by grace) / अब (now) / गयउ (has gone) / बिषादा (sorrow) / सुखी (joyful) / भयउँ (I became) / प्रभु (Lord) / चरन (feet) / प्रसादा (by favor) / अब (now) / मोहि (me) / आपनि (your own) / किंकरि (servant) / जानी (know) / जदपि (although) / सहज (by nature) / जड़ (dull) / नारि (woman) / अयानी (ignorant)
ramacharitamanas::680.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::680.essence: True relief begins when the heart stops defending itself.
ramacharitamanas::680.simple_meaning: Parvati says her sorrow has ended through Shiva's grace, and she asks to be accepted as his servant despite her own limitations.
ramacharitamanas::680.simple_insight: Peace begins when pride drops and the heart asks to be held, not proven.
ramacharitamanas::680.detailed_meaning: Parvati, listening to Shiva's tender explanation, feels her doubt dissolve. She bows further, saying sorrow has left her through his grace and that she now wants to be known as his servant. The passage turns from understanding to surrender.
ramacharitamanas::680.modern_relevance: After a long argument, you finally stop defending yourself and say, 'I hear you. I want to come back.' That softening is the real turning point.
ramacharitamanas::680.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to humble belonging.

ramacharitamanas::681.verse_sanskrit: प्रथम जो मैं पूछा सोइ कहहू। जौं मो पर प्रसन्न प्रभु अहहू॥ राम ब्रह्म चिनमय अबिनासी। सर्ब रहित सब उर पुर बासी ॥
ramacharitamanas::681.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! यदि आप मुझ पर प्रसन्न हैं, तो जो बात मैंने पहले आपसे पूछी थी, वही कहिए। (यह सत्य है कि) श्री रामचन्द्रजी ब्रह्म हैं, चिन्मय (ज्ञानस्वरूप) हैं, अविनाशी हैं, सबसे रहित और सबके हृदय रूपी नगरी में निवास करने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::681.english_translation: O Lord, if you are pleased with me, then tell me again the question I asked before. Ram is Brahman, consciousness itself, imperishable, beyond all, and dwelling in every heart-city.
ramacharitamanas::681.translation_literal: प्रथम (first) / जो (which) / मैं (I) / पूछा (asked) / सोइ (that same) / कहहू (tell) / जौं (if) / मो पर (on me) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / प्रभु (Lord) / अहहू (you are) / राम (Ram) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / चिनमय (consciousness-made) / अबिनासी (imperishable) / सर्ब (all) / रहित (without) / सब (all) / उर (heart) / पुर (city) / बासी (dweller)
ramacharitamanas::681.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::681.essence: Ram is the imperishable presence dwelling in every heart.
ramacharitamanas::681.simple_meaning: Parvati asks Shiva to repeat her earlier question, then states that Ram is the supreme reality: conscious, imperishable, beyond all limits, and present in every heart.
ramacharitamanas::681.simple_insight: The mind settles when Ram is seen as present everywhere, not distant or limited.
ramacharitamanas::681.detailed_meaning: In Shiva’s telling to Parvati, the listener has already been soothed by Ram’s praise. Now Parvati asks for the deeper answer she first came for: who Ram truly is. The verse lifts the discussion from devotion into clear understanding of Ram’s divine nature.
ramacharitamanas::681.modern_relevance: You finally feel calm after a long talk, then realise the real question is still waiting underneath. What is this presence you keep turning toward, and why does it feel so intimate?
ramacharitamanas::681.insight: It shifts the mind from asking about events to recognising Ram’s all-pervading nature.

ramacharitamanas::682.verse_sanskrit: नाथ धरेउ नरतनु केहि हेतू। मोहि समुझाइ कहहु बृषकेतू॥ उमा बचन सुनि परम बिनीता। रामकथा पर प्रीति पुनीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::682.verse_hindi: फिर हे नाथ! उन्होंने मनुष्य का शरीर किस कारण से धारण किया? हे धर्म की ध्वजा धारण करने वाले प्रभो! यह मुझे समझाकर कहिए। पार्वती के अत्यन्त नम्र वचन सुनकर और श्री रामचन्द्रजी की कथा में उनका विशुद्ध प्रेम देखकर- ॥
ramacharitamanas::682.english_translation: Then, O Lord, why did you take a human body? O bearer of the bull-banner, explain this to me. Hearing Parvati's very humble words and seeing her pure love for Ram's story—
ramacharitamanas::682.translation_literal: नाथ (lord) / धरेउ (took/assumed) / नरतनु (human body) / केहि हेतू (for what reason) / मोहि (to me) / समुझाइ (explaining) / कहहु (tell) / बृषकेतू (bull-bannered one) / उमा (Parvati) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / परम (supremely) / बिनीता (humble) / रामकथा (Ram-story) / पर (on) / प्रीति (love) / पुनीता (pure)
ramacharitamanas::682.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::682.essence: Sincere wonder opens the door to deeper understanding.
ramacharitamanas::682.simple_meaning: Parvati asks why the divine took a human form and asks Shiva to explain it clearly. Her humility and pure love for Ram's story deepen the question.
ramacharitamanas::682.simple_insight: Real understanding begins with a sincere question, not a polished answer.
ramacharitamanas::682.detailed_meaning: Parvati, softened by Shiva's earlier praise of Ram, asks the deeper question behind the incarnation: why did Ram take a human body at all? Her humility and love for the story open the door to Shiva's teaching.
ramacharitamanas::682.modern_relevance: You hear a story about someone extraordinary, and one question keeps returning: why would greatness choose limitation? That honest curiosity is where understanding starts.
ramacharitamanas::682.insight: It shifts the mind from accepting the surface story to asking for the purpose beneath it.

ramacharitamanas::683.verse_sanskrit: हियँ हरषे कामारि तब संकर सहज सुजान। बहु बिधि उमहि प्रसंसि पुनि बोले कृपानिधान ॥
ramacharitamanas::683.verse_hindi: तब कामदेव के शत्रु, स्वाभाविक ही सुजान, कृपा निधान शिवजी मन में बहुत ही हर्षित हुए और बहुत प्रकार से पार्वती की बड़ाई करके फिर बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::683.english_translation: Then Shiva, enemy of desire and naturally wise, was filled with joy in his heart. Praising Parvati in many ways, the treasure of compassion spoke again.
ramacharitamanas::683.translation_literal: हियँ (in heart) / हरषे (rejoiced) / कामारि (enemy of desire) / तब (then) / संकर (Shankar, Shiva) / सहज (naturally) / सुजान (wise) / बहु बिधि (in many ways) / उमहि (to Uma/Parvati) / प्रसंसि (praising) / पुनि (again) / बोले (spoke) / कृपानिधान (treasure of compassion)
ramacharitamanas::683.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::683.essence: Devoted questioning draws out a fuller teaching.
ramacharitamanas::683.simple_meaning: Shiva feels delighted, praises Parvati, and then continues speaking.
ramacharitamanas::683.simple_insight: A sincere question opens the way for a deeper answer.
ramacharitamanas::683.detailed_meaning: Parvati has just asked why Ram took a human birth. Shiva, pleased by her devotion and readiness, responds with joy. This line is a transition: the teacher approves the listener before unfolding the sacred story.
ramacharitamanas::683.modern_relevance: A mentor sees you are finally ready to hear the hard answer. Before the lesson comes, there is a moment of recognition: yes, you are asking the right question.
ramacharitamanas::683.insight: It shows that reverent listening itself prepares the mind for truth.

ramacharitamanas::684.verse_sanskrit: सुनु सुभ कथा भवानि रामचरितमानस बिमल। कहा भुसुंडि बखानि सुना बिहग नायक गरुड़ ॥
ramacharitamanas::684.verse_hindi: हे पार्वती! निर्मल रामचरितमानस की वह मंगलमयी कथा सुनो जिसे काकभुशुण्डि ने विस्तार से कहा और पक्षियों के राजा गरुड़जी ने सुना था ॥
ramacharitamanas::684.english_translation: O Parvati, listen to the pure Ramcharitmanas, the auspicious story that Bhushundi narrated and Garuda heard, lord of birds.
ramacharitamanas::684.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / सुभ (auspicious) / कथा (story) / भवानि (O Parvati) / रामचरितमानस (Ramcharitmanas) / बिमल (pure) / कहा (told) / भुसुंडि (Bhushundi) / बखानि (described in detail) / सुना (heard) / बिहग (bird) / नायक (lord) / गरुड़ (Garuda)
ramacharitamanas::684.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::684.essence: A pure story is itself a blessing before its meaning arrives.
ramacharitamanas::684.simple_meaning: Shiva invites Parvati to hear the pure and auspicious Ram story, told by Bhushundi and heard by Garuda.
ramacharitamanas::684.simple_insight: Some stories are worth hearing because they carry purity, blessing, and living devotion.
ramacharitamanas::684.detailed_meaning: Shiva is still answering Parvati’s question in the frame narrative. He points to the Ramcharitmanas itself as a pure, auspicious account: the story Bhushundi narrated to Garuda. The verse is a doorway, not the teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::684.modern_relevance: Someone lowers their voice and says, 'Listen to this one carefully.' Before the details even begin, you feel that what follows is meant to cleanse attention, not just entertain it.
ramacharitamanas::684.insight: It shifts the reader from casual listening to reverent reception.

ramacharitamanas::685.verse_sanskrit: सो संबाद उदार जेहि बिधि भा आगें कहब। सुनहु राम अवतार चरति परम सुंदर अनघ ॥
ramacharitamanas::685.verse_hindi: वह श्रेष्ठ संवाद जिस प्रकार हुआ, वह मैं आगे कहूँगा। अभी तुम श्री रामचन्द्रजी के अवतार का परम सुंदर और पवित्र (पापनाशक) चरित्र सुनो ॥
ramacharitamanas::685.english_translation: I will tell that noble dialogue later, as it happened. First, listen to the most beautiful and pure story of Ram's incarnation.
ramacharitamanas::685.translation_literal: सो (that) / संबाद (dialogue) / उदार (noble) / जेहि बिधि (in the manner in which) / भा (happened) / आगें (later) / कहब (I will tell) / सुनहु (listen) / राम (Ram) / अवतार (incarnation) / चरति (story/character) / परम (supreme/most) / सुंदर (beautiful) / अनघ (stainless/pure)
ramacharitamanas::685.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::685.essence: The main story must be heard before the explanation arrives.
ramacharitamanas::685.simple_meaning: Shiva pauses the story and tells Parvati that he will explain the earlier dialogue later. For now, he asks her to listen to the beautiful, pure account of Ram's incarnation.
ramacharitamanas::685.simple_insight: Some stories need a wider frame before their meaning can fully open.
ramacharitamanas::685.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the opening frame of Balkand. He sets aside the earlier dialogue and turns her attention to Ram's incarnation, promising to return to the details afterward. The verse prepares the listener for the sacred narrative that follows.
ramacharitamanas::685.modern_relevance: A friend starts telling you a story, then stops and says, “Wait — first hear the main event.” That pause matters: it tells you what deserves your full attention before the details arrive.
ramacharitamanas::685.insight: It teaches you to receive the central truth first, before getting lost in side details.

ramacharitamanas::686.verse_sanskrit: हरि गुन नाम अपार कथा रूप अगनित अमित। मैं निज मति अनुसार कहउँ उमा सादर सुनहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::686.verse_hindi: श्री हरि के गुण, मान, कथा और रूप सभी अपार, अगणित और असीम हैं। फिर भी हे पार्वती! मैं अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार कहता हूँ, तुम आदरपूर्वक सुनो ॥
ramacharitamanas::686.english_translation: The divine's qualities, names, stories, and forms are endless and immeasurable. Still, O Parvati, I speak according to my own understanding; listen with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::686.translation_literal: हरि (the divine) / गुन (qualities) / नाम (names) / अपार (boundless) / कथा (stories) / रूप (forms) / अगनित (countless) / अमित (immeasurable) / मैं (I) / निज (own) / मति (understanding) / अनुसार (according to) / कहउँ (I speak) / उमा (O Uma/Parvati) / सादर (with reverence) / सुनहु (listen)
ramacharitamanas::686.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::686.essence: The divine is too vast for complete speech; humility is the right beginning.
ramacharitamanas::686.simple_meaning: Ram's qualities, names, stories, and forms cannot be fully counted. The speaker can only offer a humble account and asks Parvati to listen respectfully.
ramacharitamanas::686.simple_insight: There is peace in admitting that the highest reality is larger than any one explanation.
ramacharitamanas::686.detailed_meaning: After promising to tell the sacred story, Tulsidas pauses and bows to the limit of language. Speaking to Parvati, he says Ram's glory cannot be measured, only approached with reverence. This verse opens the devotional mood of the narration.
ramacharitamanas::686.modern_relevance: You try to explain someone you love deeply, and every sentence feels too small. The heart knows more than language can hold, so you speak carefully and with respect.
ramacharitamanas::686.insight: It shifts the reader from mastering the divine with words to approaching it with humility and reverence.

ramacharitamanas::687.verse_sanskrit: सुनु गिरिजा हरिचरित सुहाए। बिपुल बिसद निगमागम गाए॥ हरि अवतार हेतु जेहि होई। इदमित्थं कहि जाइ न सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::687.verse_hindi: हे पार्वती! सुनो, वेद-शास्त्रों ने श्री हरि के सुंदर, विस्तृत और निर्मल चरित्रों का गान किया है। हरि का अवतार जिस कारण से होता है, वह कारण 'बस यही है' ऐसा नहीं कहा जा सकता (अनेकों कारण हो सकते हैं और ऐसे भी हो सकते हैं, जिन्हें कोई जान ही नहीं सकता) ॥
ramacharitamanas::687.english_translation: O Girija, listen to the lovely deeds of Hari. The Vedas and scriptures sing them in many clear ways. The cause for Hari's incarnation cannot be stated as only this and nothing else.
ramacharitamanas::687.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / गिरिजा (O Girija) / हरिचरित (the deeds of Hari) / सुहाए (lovely) / बिपुल (many) / बिसद (clear, pure) / निगमागम (Vedas and scriptures) / गाए (have sung) ॥ / हरि (Hari) / अवतार (incarnation) / हेतु (cause) / जेहि (which) / होई (is) / इदमित्थं (only this, exactly thus) / कहि जाइ (can be said) / न (not) / सोई (that) ॥
ramacharitamanas::687.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::687.essence: Ram's coming cannot be trapped in one explanation.
ramacharitamanas::687.simple_meaning: The sacred texts praise Ram's beautiful deeds in many ways, and no single explanation can fully capture why he comes into the world.
ramacharitamanas::687.simple_insight: Some realities are too vast for one neat answer. Reverence begins where certainty ends.
ramacharitamanas::687.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the opening frame of Balkand, preparing her for Ram's birth-story. He says the scriptures sing Hari's beautiful deeds in many ways, but the reason for Ram's incarnation cannot be reduced to one simple explanation.
ramacharitamanas::687.modern_relevance: You keep trying to reduce a life-changing choice to one clean reason — a job move, a breakup, a sudden return to prayer. Some things are bigger than the story you can tell about them.
ramacharitamanas::687.insight: It trains the mind to stop forcing sacred or complex events into a single explanation.

ramacharitamanas::688.verse_sanskrit: राम अतर्क्य बुद्धि मन बानी। मत हमार अस सुनहि सयानी॥ तदपि संत मुनि बेद पुराना। जस कछु कहहिं स्वमति अनुमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::688.verse_hindi: हे सयानी! सुनो, हमारा मत तो यह है कि बुद्धि, मन और वाणी से श्री रामचन्द्रजी की तर्कना नहीं की जा सकती। तथापि संत, मुनि, वेद और पुराण अपनी-अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार जैसा कुछ कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::688.english_translation: O wise one, know this: Ram cannot be grasped by intellect, mind, or speech. Yet saints, sages, the Vedas, and the Puranas speak as best they can, each from its own understanding.
ramacharitamanas::688.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / अतर्क्य (beyond argument) / बुद्धि (intellect) / मन (mind) / बानी (speech) / मत (opinion) / हमार (our) / अस (thus) / सुनहि (listen) / सयानी (wise one)॥ / तदपि (even so) / संत (saints) / मुनि (sages) / बेद (Vedas) / पुराना (Puranas) / जस (as) / कछु (whatever) / कहहिं (they say) / स्वमति (their own understanding) / अनुमाना (by inference) ॥
ramacharitamanas::688.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::688.essence: Ram stands beyond thought, while every description remains partial.
ramacharitamanas::688.simple_meaning: Ram cannot be fully captured by thinking, feeling, or speaking. Even the saints and scriptures can only describe him from their own limited understanding.
ramacharitamanas::688.simple_insight: Humility opens the door: the deepest reality is larger than your concepts.
ramacharitamanas::688.detailed_meaning: Shiva is explaining Ram's nature to Parvati in the Balkand frame. After saying Ram's glory is beyond full description, he adds that saints, sages, the Vedas, and the Puranas can only speak from partial understanding. The verse sets the limit of all explanation.
ramacharitamanas::688.modern_relevance: You keep trying to explain a loss, a love, or a calling in perfect words, and every sentence falls short. Some realities are bigger than the language you bring to them.
ramacharitamanas::688.insight: It shifts the mind from total explanation to reverent humility before what cannot be reduced.

ramacharitamanas::689.verse_sanskrit: तस मैं सुमुखि सुनावउँ तोही। समुझि परइ जस कारन मोही॥ जब जब होई धरम कै हानी। बाढ़हिं असुर अधम अभिमानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::689.verse_hindi: और जैसा कुछ मेरी समझ में आता है, हे सुमुखि! वही कारण मैं तुमको सुनाता हूँ। जब-जब धर्म का ह्रास होता है और नीच अभिमानी राक्षस बढ़ जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::689.english_translation: And as far as I understand, O gentle one, I will tell you that reason. Whenever dharma declines and low, arrogant beings grow strong...
ramacharitamanas::689.translation_literal: तस (thus) / मैं (I) / सुमुखि (gentle one) / सुनावउँ (I explain) / तोही (to you) / समुझि (understanding) / परइ (comes) / जस (as) / कारन (reason) / मोही (to me) / जब जब (whenever) / होई (happens) / धरम (dharma) / कै (of) / हानी (decline) / बाढ़हिं (grow) / असुर (beings of ego and shadow) / अधम (low) / अभिमानी (arrogant)
ramacharitamanas::689.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::689.essence: The divine appears when dharma breaks down.
ramacharitamanas::689.simple_meaning: Shiva begins explaining why Ram appears in the world: whenever righteousness declines and arrogant forces rise, the divine comes to restore balance.
ramacharitamanas::689.simple_insight: You are not abandoned when disorder grows; higher help arrives when things seem most broken.
ramacharitamanas::689.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the opening of the Ram story. After saying Ram cannot be fully grasped by mind or speech, he gives the first clear reason for the incarnation: when dharma declines and arrogant forces dominate, Ram appears.
ramacharitamanas::689.modern_relevance: When a workplace turns toxic and cruelty starts looking normal, it can feel like decency has lost. This verse says that collapse is often the very moment restoration begins.
ramacharitamanas::689.insight: It shifts attention from despair over decline to confidence that renewal answers moral collapse.

ramacharitamanas::690.verse_sanskrit: करहिं अनीति जाइ नहिं बरनी। सीदहिं बिप्र धेनु सुर धरनी॥ तब तब प्रभु धरि बिबिध सरीरा। हरहिं कृपानिधि सज्जन पीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::690.verse_hindi: और वे ऐसा अन्याय करते हैं कि जिसका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता तथा ब्राह्मण, गो, देवता और पृथ्वी कष्ट पाते हैं, तब-तब वे कृपानिधान प्रभु भाँति-भाँति के (दिव्य) शरीर धारण कर सज्जनों की पीड़ा हरते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::690.english_translation: They commit injustice beyond description, and priests, cows, the radiant beings, and the earth suffer. Then and again, the Lord takes many forms and removes the suffering of the good.
ramacharitamanas::690.translation_literal: करहिं (they do) / अनीति (injustice) / जाइ नहिं बरनी (cannot be described) / सीदहिं (suffer) / बिप्र (priests) / धेनु (cows) / सुर (radiant beings) / धरनी (earth) / तब तब (then and again) / प्रभु (the Lord) / धरि (taking) / बिबिध (various) / सरीरा (bodies) / हरहिं (remove) / कृपानिधि (treasure of compassion) / सज्जन (good people) / पीरा (pain)
ramacharitamanas::690.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::690.essence: Ram appears wherever injustice makes the good suffer.
ramacharitamanas::690.simple_meaning: When injustice becomes unbearable and the good suffer, Ram takes different forms to remove their pain.
ramacharitamanas::690.simple_insight: You are not abandoned when wrongdoing grows heavy; protection can arrive in many forms.
ramacharitamanas::690.detailed_meaning: Parvati has asked why Ram takes birth again and again. Shiva explains that whenever injustice rises and the good suffer, Ram appears in many forms to relieve them. This verse gives the reason for divine descent.
ramacharitamanas::690.modern_relevance: When cruelty spreads and decent people feel cornered, it can seem like no help is coming. This verse answers that despair with a larger trust: protection may arrive in unexpected forms.
ramacharitamanas::690.insight: It shifts the mind from helplessness to trust that right action can reappear when needed most.

ramacharitamanas::691.verse_sanskrit: असुर मारि थापहिं सुरन्ह राखहिं निज श्रुति सेतु। जग बिस्तारहिं बिसद जस राम जन्म कर हेतु ॥
ramacharitamanas::691.verse_hindi: वे असुरों को मारकर देवताओं को स्थापित करते हैं, अपने (श्वास रूप) वेदों की मर्यादा की रक्षा करते हैं और जगत में अपना निर्मल यश फैलाते हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के अवतार का यह कारण है ॥
ramacharitamanas::691.english_translation: They destroy the asuras, establish the radiant beings, protect the order of the Vedas, and spread their pure fame through the world. This is the reason for Ram's birth.
ramacharitamanas::691.translation_literal: असुर (demons/hostile beings) / मारि (killing) / थापहिं (they establish) / सुरन्ह (the radiant beings) / राखहिं (they protect) / निज (their own) / श्रुति (Vedas) / सेतु (bridge/order) / जग (world) / बिस्तारहिं (they spread) / बिसद (pure) / जस (fame/glory) / राम (Ram) / जन्म (birth) / कर (of) / हेतु (reason/cause)
ramacharitamanas::691.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::691.essence: Ram comes to restore order, protect dharma, and remove what distorts the world.
ramacharitamanas::691.simple_meaning: Ram appears to remove destructive forces, restore righteous order, protect sacred teaching, and spread his pure fame across the world.
ramacharitamanas::691.simple_insight: It brings relief to see that divine action is not random: it restores order, protects what matters, and leaves a lasting example.
ramacharitamanas::691.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is explaining to Parvati why Ram takes birth. After saying that dharma declines and the world suffers, he adds the result of Ram's descent: hostile forces are removed, the righteous are upheld, sacred order is protected, and Ram's glory fills the world.
ramacharitamanas::691.modern_relevance: When a family system is breaking down and one person finally steps in to protect what is right, the goal is not applause. The real work is restoring order, defending the vulnerable, and setting a standard others can trust.
ramacharitamanas::691.insight: It shifts attention from Ram's birth as a miracle to Ram's birth as purposeful restoration.

ramacharitamanas::692.verse_sanskrit: सोइ जस गाइ भगत भव तरहीं। कृपासिंधु जन हित तनु धरहीं॥ राम जनम के हेतु अनेका। परम बिचित्र एक तें एका ॥
ramacharitamanas::692.verse_hindi: उसी यश को गा-गाकर भक्तजन भवसागर से तर जाते हैं। कृपासागर भगवान भक्तों के हित के लिए शरीर धारण करते हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के जन्म लेने के अनेक कारण हैं, जो एक से एक बढ़कर विचित्र हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::692.english_translation: By singing that glory, devotees cross beyond the cycle of reactivity. The ocean of mercy takes form for the good of his people. Ram's birth has many causes, each stranger than the last.
ramacharitamanas::692.translation_literal: सोइ (that same) / जस (glory) / गाइ (singing) / भगत (devotees) / भव (worldly becoming) / तरहीं (cross over) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of mercy) / जन हित (for the good of people) / तनु (body/form) / धरहीं (take) / राम जनम (Ram's birth) / के हेतु (for the cause) / अनेका (many) / परम (supremely) / बिचित्र (wonderful/strange) / एक तें एका (one more than another)
ramacharitamanas::692.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::692.essence: Ram's glory carries devotees across suffering, and his birth serves mercy.
ramacharitamanas::692.simple_meaning: Devotees cross beyond suffering by singing Ram's glory. Ram takes form out of mercy for the good of his people, and his birth has many wondrous reasons.
ramacharitamanas::692.simple_insight: Praise changes the singer first. It turns devotion into relief, and relief into trust.
ramacharitamanas::692.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is explaining Ram's descent before the story fully unfolds. He says devotees are saved by singing Ram's glory, because Ram appears in the world out of mercy for the good of all. His birth is not simple; it carries many wondrous purposes.
ramacharitamanas::692.modern_relevance: You are exhausted, but you still hum the name of what steadies you on the train home. The act is small; the shift is not. Recalling the beloved can carry you through what raw effort cannot.
ramacharitamanas::692.insight: It shifts the mind from treating devotion as ornament to seeing it as a way across suffering.

ramacharitamanas::693.verse_sanskrit: जनम एक दुइ कहउँ बखानी। सावधान सुनु सुमति भवानी॥ द्वारपाल हरि के प्रिय दोऊ। जय अरु बिजय जान सब कोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::693.verse_hindi: हे सुंदर बुद्धि वाली भवानी! मैं उनके दो-एक जन्मों का विस्तार से वर्णन करता हूँ, तुम सावधान होकर सुनो। श्री हरि के जय और विजय दो प्यारे द्वारपाल हैं, जिनको सब कोई जानते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::693.english_translation: O Bhavani, beautiful in wisdom, I will describe one or two of their births in detail; listen carefully. Jay and Vijay are the two beloved gatekeepers of Hari, and everyone knows them.
ramacharitamanas::693.translation_literal: जनम (births) / एक (one) / दुइ (two) / कहउँ (I tell) / बखानी (in detail) / सावधान (carefully) / सुनु (listen) / सुमति (good wisdom) / भवानी (Bhavani) / द्वारपाल (gatekeepers) / हरि (Hari) / के (of) / प्रिय (beloved) / दोऊ (both) / जय (Jay) / अरु (and) / बिजय (Vijay) / जान (know) / सब (everyone) / कोऊ (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::693.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::693.essence: Even a brief beginning can hide a much larger sacred story.
ramacharitamanas::693.simple_meaning: Shiva tells Parvati to listen carefully as he begins the story of Hari's two beloved gatekeepers, Jay and Vijay, whose births he will explain.
ramacharitamanas::693.simple_insight: Some stories begin with a mystery. Patient listening reveals how even a curse can become part of a larger design.
ramacharitamanas::693.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the Balkand frame and preparing her for a deeper account. He introduces Jay and Vijay, Hari's beloved gatekeepers, and signals that their story will explain how they came to take birth in the world.
ramacharitamanas::693.modern_relevance: Someone starts a long family story with, “Listen carefully, this matters.” You lean in, because the smallest detail may explain a wound, a pattern, or a destiny-shaped turn.
ramacharitamanas::693.insight: It shifts attention from the surface event to the hidden backstory that gives it meaning.

ramacharitamanas::694.verse_sanskrit: बिप्र श्राप तें दूनउ भाई। तामस असुर देह तिन्ह पाई॥ कनककसिपु अरु हाटकलोचन। जगत बिदित सुरपति मद मोचन ॥
ramacharitamanas::694.verse_hindi: उन दोनों भाइयों ने ब्राह्मण (सनकादि) के शाप से असुरों का तामसी शरीर पाया। एक का नाम था हिरण्यकशिपु और दूसरे का हिरण्याक्ष। ये देवराज इन्द्र के गर्व को छुड़ाने वाले सारे जगत में प्रसिद्ध हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::694.english_translation: By the curse of the brahmins, the two brothers received bodies of darkness as asuras. One was Hiranyakashipu and the other Hiranyaksha, known throughout the world as the removers of Indra's pride.
ramacharitamanas::694.translation_literal: बिप्र (brahmin) / श्राप (curse) / तें (by) / दूनउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / तामस (dark) / असुर (asura) / देह (body) / तिन्ह (they) / पाई (received) ॥ / कनककसिपु (Hiranyakashipu) / अरु (and) / हाटकलोचन (Hiranyaksha) / जगत (world) / बिदित (known) / सुरपति (Indra) / मद (pride) / मोचन (remover) ॥
ramacharitamanas::694.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::694.essence: Pride can make someone famous, but it also prepares the fall.
ramacharitamanas::694.simple_meaning: The two brothers were born with dark asura bodies because of a brahmin's curse. They became famous across the world for humbling Indra's pride.
ramacharitamanas::694.simple_insight: Pride invites correction. Power that forgets humility eventually meets a force that breaks it.
ramacharitamanas::694.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues explaining the earlier births of Ram's future enemies. The two brothers, Hiranyakashipu and Hiranyaksha, are introduced as cursed beings with asura bodies, famous for shaking Indra's pride. This sets up the larger divine drama behind their later defeat.
ramacharitamanas::694.modern_relevance: A person who has built their whole identity on status can feel untouchable for years. Then one blunt failure exposes the arrogance underneath and changes the whole story.
ramacharitamanas::694.insight: It shifts attention from surface greatness to the karmic force that eventually corrects inflated ego.

ramacharitamanas::695.verse_sanskrit: बिजई समर बीर बिख्याता। धरि बराह बपु एक निपाता॥ होइ नरहरि दूसर पुनि मारा। जन प्रहलाद सुजस बिस्तारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::695.verse_hindi: वे युद्ध में विजय पाने वाले विख्यात वीर थे। इनमें से एक (हिरण्याक्ष) को भगवान ने वराह (सूअर) का शरीर धारण करके मारा, फिर दूसरे (हिरण्यकशिपु) का नरसिंह रूप धारण करके वध किया और अपने भक्त प्रह्लाद का सुंदर यश फैलाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::695.english_translation: They were famous warriors, victorious in battle. One was slain when the divine took the form of Varaha; then the other was killed when the divine appeared as Narasimha, and the glory of Prahlad spread beautifully.
ramacharitamanas::695.translation_literal: बिजई (victorious) / समर (battle) / बीर (warriors) / बिख्याता (famous) / धरि (taking) / बराह बपु (Varaha form) / एक (one) / निपाता (was struck down) / होइ (becoming) / नरहरि (Narasimha) / दूसर (the other) / पुनि (then) / मारा (killed) / जन (the people) / प्रहलाद (Prahlad) / सुजस (good fame) / बिस्तारा (spread)
ramacharitamanas::695.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::695.essence: Pride falls, while devotion keeps its name alive.
ramacharitamanas::695.simple_meaning: Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakashipu were powerful enemies, but the divine destroyed them in two different forms and made Prahlad's devotion famous.
ramacharitamanas::695.simple_insight: Power built on pride does not last. Devotion, not violence, becomes the lasting glory.
ramacharitamanas::695.detailed_meaning: Shiva is recounting the earlier births of two gatekeepers who became the demon brothers Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakashipu. One fell to Varaha, the other to Narasimha. Their defeat also lifted Prahlad's devotion into lasting fame.
ramacharitamanas::695.modern_relevance: A person can dominate a room, a company, even a whole family, and still be undone by arrogance. What remains remembered is not force, but the goodness that survives it.
ramacharitamanas::695.insight: It shifts attention from brute strength to the moral law that outlives it.

ramacharitamanas::696.verse_sanskrit: भए निसाचर जाइ तेइ महाबीर बलवान। कुंभकरन रावन सुभट सुर बिजई जग जान ॥
ramacharitamanas::696.verse_hindi: वे ही (दोनों) जाकर देवताओं को जीतने वाले तथा बड़े योद्धा, रावण और कुम्भकर्ण नामक बड़े बलवान और महावीर राक्षस हुए, जिन्हें सारा जगत जानता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::696.english_translation: They became the mighty, powerful demons who conquered the radiant beings: Kumbhakarna and Ravana, the world knows them as great warriors.
ramacharitamanas::696.translation_literal: भए (became) / निसाचर (demons, night-walkers) / जाइ (going) / तेइ (those same) / महाबीर (great warriors) / बलवान (powerful) / कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / रावन (Ravana) / सुभट (excellent warriors) / सुर (radiant beings) / बिजई (victorious over) / जग (world) / जान (knows)
ramacharitamanas::696.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::696.essence: Great power can still belong to a mind ruled by pride.
ramacharitamanas::696.simple_meaning: Those same two brothers were born again as the powerful demon kings Kumbhakarna and Ravana, known everywhere for their strength and victories.
ramacharitamanas::696.simple_insight: Power and fame can still become a prison when they serve ego.
ramacharitamanas::696.detailed_meaning: The story turns to Ravana's past. The same beings who were once cursed and reborn now appear as the mighty Kumbhakarna and Ravana, feared across the world. This line sets up their future fall and the reason they cannot escape their fate.
ramacharitamanas::696.modern_relevance: A person can become famous for strength, wins, and dominance, yet still be trapped by the same pride underneath. Public victory does not mean inner freedom.
ramacharitamanas::696.insight: It shifts attention from outward success to the deeper character that drives it.

ramacharitamanas::697.verse_sanskrit: मुकुत न भए हते भगवाना। तीनि जनम द्विज बचन प्रवाना॥ एक बार तिन्ह के हित लागी। धरेउ सरीर भगत अनुरागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::697.verse_hindi: भगवान के द्वारा मारे जाने पर भी वे (हिरण्याक्ष और हिरण्यकशिपु) इसीलिए मुक्त नहीं हुए कि ब्राह्मण के वचन (शाप) का प्रमाण तीन जन्म के लिए था। अतः एक बार उनके कल्याण के लिए भक्तप्रेमी भगवान ने फिर अवतार लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::697.english_translation: Even when slain by the divine, they were not freed, because the Brahmin's words bound them to three births. For their welfare, the devotee-loving divine took form again.
ramacharitamanas::697.translation_literal: मुकुत (freed) / न (not) / भए (became) / हते (slain) / भगवाना (by the divine) / तीनि (three) / जनम (births) / द्विज (Brahmin) / बचन (word) / प्रवाना (binding authority) / एक (one) / बार (time) / तिन्ह (for them) / के (of) / हित (welfare) / लागी (for the sake of) / धरेउ (took) / सरीर (body) / भगत (devotee) / अनुरागी (loving)
ramacharitamanas::697.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::697.essence: Mercy keeps returning until even the bound are reached.
ramacharitamanas::697.simple_meaning: Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakashipu were not freed just because the divine killed them. A Brahmin's curse kept them bound to three births, so the divine returned for their welfare.
ramacharitamanas::697.simple_insight: Love is stronger than punishment; even judgment can become a path back to grace.
ramacharitamanas::697.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas explains why the divine appears again and again in the world. Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakashipu were slain, but a curse tied them to three births. So Ram takes form once more, not out of obligation, but out of loving concern for their eventual good.
ramacharitamanas::697.modern_relevance: You think one harsh consequence will finally end a pattern, but it doesn't. Some people need repeated chances, and the deepest care keeps returning even after failure.
ramacharitamanas::697.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing divine action as punishment to seeing it as patient rescue.

ramacharitamanas::698.verse_sanskrit: कस्यप अदिति तहाँ पितु माता। दसरथ कौसल्या बिख्याता॥ एक कलप एहि बिधि अवतारा। चरित पवित्र किए संसारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::698.verse_hindi: वहाँ (उस अवतार में) कश्यप और अदिति उनके माता-पिता हुए, जो दशरथ और कौसल्या के नाम से प्रसिद्ध थे। एक कल्प में इस प्रकार अवतार लेकर उन्होंने संसार में पवित्र लीलाएँ कीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::698.english_translation: There, Kashyapa and Aditi were the father and mother, known as Dasharatha and Kaushalya. In one cosmic age, he descended in this way and made the world pure through his sacred deeds.
ramacharitamanas::698.translation_literal: कस्यप (Kashyapa) / अदिति (Aditi) / तहाँ (there) / पितु (father) / माता (mother) / दसरथ (Dasharatha) / कौसल्या (Kaushalya) / बिख्याता (renowned)॥ / एक (one) / कलप (cosmic age) / एहि बिधि (in this manner) / अवतारा (incarnation) / चरित (deeds, play) / पवित्र (pure) / किए (made) / संसार (world) ॥
ramacharitamanas::698.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::698.essence: Divinity takes birth in a human family and sanctifies the world.
ramacharitamanas::698.simple_meaning: Ram's divine birth is described as a descent of Kashyapa and Aditi as Dasharatha and Kaushalya. His life purified the world through sacred deeds.
ramacharitamanas::698.simple_insight: The divine enters family life without losing grandeur.
ramacharitamanas::698.detailed_meaning: The narration returns to Ram's cosmic identity. Tulsidas links the ancient divine pair Kashyapa and Aditi to Dasharatha and Kaushalya, reminding the reader that Ram's birth in Ayodhya was not ordinary. His life itself becomes a force that purifies the world.
ramacharitamanas::698.modern_relevance: A child is born in a quiet hospital room, yet the whole family feels changed. Some arrivals do not just join a home — they cleanse it, reorder it, and make everyone around them more upright.
ramacharitamanas::698.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary biography to sacred presence entering human history.

ramacharitamanas::699.verse_sanskrit: एक कलप सुर देखि दुखारे। समर जलंधर सन सब हारे॥ संभु कीन्ह संग्राम अपारा। दनुज महाबल मरइ न मारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::699.verse_hindi: एक कल्प में सब देवताओं को जलन्धर दैत्य से युद्ध में हार जाने के कारण दुःखी देखकर शिवजी ने उसके साथ बड़ा घोर युद्ध किया, पर वह महाबली दैत्य मारे नहीं मरता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::699.english_translation: In one age, seeing the radiant beings distressed because all had been defeated by Jalandhar in battle, Shiva fought a fierce war with him. But the powerful demon could not be slain.
ramacharitamanas::699.translation_literal: एक कलप (in one age) / सुर (radiant beings) / देखि (seeing) / दुखारे (distressed) / समर (battle) / जलंधर (Jalandhar) / सन (with) / सब (all) / हारे (defeated) / संभु (Shiva) / कीन्ह (made) / संग्राम (war) / अपारा (fierce, immense) / दनुज (demon) / महाबल (greatly powerful) / मरइ (is slain) / न (not) / मारा (slain)
ramacharitamanas::699.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::699.essence: Raw power still fails against what cannot yet be ended.
ramacharitamanas::699.simple_meaning: The radiant beings were defeated by Jalandhar, so Shiva fought him in a terrible battle, but Jalandhar could not be killed.
ramacharitamanas::699.simple_insight: Even great force can meet a limit; some struggles are only part of a larger story.
ramacharitamanas::699.detailed_meaning: The poem shifts into an old cosmic episode: the radiant beings have been beaten by Jalandhar, and Shiva enters a fierce battle to protect them. The point is not victory yet, but setting up the impossible enemy whose defeat will require more than strength.
ramacharitamanas::699.modern_relevance: You’ve done everything you can, but the problem still stands there, unchanged. Some conflicts cannot be solved by force alone; they need a deeper opening.
ramacharitamanas::699.insight: It shifts attention from heroic effort to the limits of force when ego is deeply entrenched.

ramacharitamanas::700.verse_sanskrit: परम सती असुराधिप नारी। तेहिं बल ताहि न जितहिं पुरारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::700.verse_hindi: उस दैत्यराज की स्त्री परम सती (बड़ी ही पतिव्रता) थी। उसी के प्रताप से त्रिपुरासुर (जैसे अजेय शत्रु) का विनाश करने वाले शिवजी भी उस दैत्य को नहीं जीत सके ॥
ramacharitamanas::700.english_translation: The wife of the lord of the demons was utterly devoted. Because of her power, even Tripurari could not defeat him.
ramacharitamanas::700.translation_literal: परम (utterly) / सती (devoted wife) / असुराधिप (lord of the demons) / नारी (woman, wife) / तेहिं (by that) / बल (power) / ताहि (him) / न (not) / जितहिं (could defeat) / पुरारी (Shiva, destroyer of Tripura)
ramacharitamanas::700.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::700.essence: Steadfast devotion can shield even the seemingly invincible.
ramacharitamanas::700.simple_meaning: The demon king's wife was so devoted that even Shiva could not defeat him because of her power.
ramacharitamanas::700.simple_insight: Devotion and steadfastness can shape events in ways strength alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::700.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, the story recalls a past cosmic struggle. The demon king had a wife of great fidelity, and that vow gave him protection so strong that even Shiva could not overcome him. The next verse explains how that protection was broken.
ramacharitamanas::700.modern_relevance: A person may look untouchable from the outside, but one quiet bond of loyalty can hold far more power than force or status.
ramacharitamanas::700.insight: It shifts attention from visible strength to the hidden power of faithfulness and vows.

ramacharitamanas::701.verse_sanskrit: छल करि टारेउ तासु ब्रत प्रभु सुर कारज कीन्ह। जब तेहिं जानेउ मरम तब श्राप कोप करि दीन्ह ॥
ramacharitamanas::701.verse_hindi: प्रभु ने छल से उस स्त्री का व्रत भंग कर देवताओं का काम किया। जब उस स्त्री ने यह भेद जाना, तब उसने क्रोध करके भगवान को शाप दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::701.english_translation: The Lord used deceit to break her vow and complete the gods' task. When she understood the deception, she cursed him in anger.
ramacharitamanas::701.translation_literal: छल करि (by deceit) / टारेउ (broke away) / तासु (her) / ब्रत (vow) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सुर (gods) / कारज (task) / कीन्ह (did) / जब (when) / तेहिं (she) / जानेउ (understood) / मरम (secret) / तब (then) / श्राप (curse) / कोप करि (with anger) / दीन्ह (gave)
ramacharitamanas::701.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::701.essence: Deception may finish the task, but it also plants a curse.
ramacharitamanas::701.simple_meaning: The Lord completed the gods' task by breaking the woman's vow through deceit. Once she understood what had happened, she cursed him in anger.
ramacharitamanas::701.simple_insight: Even divine play can carry a sharp human cost, and wounded trust answers with anger.
ramacharitamanas::701.detailed_meaning: Shiva is recounting an old cosmic episode to Parvati: the gods need help against Jalandhar, whose power is protected by his wife's chastity. The Lord breaks that protection through deception, and when she sees the truth, she curses him. This verse marks the turning point.
ramacharitamanas::701.modern_relevance: A hidden trick gets the result you wanted, but the person who was deceived will not stay silent. Winning by manipulation always leaves a wound behind.
ramacharitamanas::701.insight: It shows that a short-term victory gained through deceit can still trigger a deeper consequence.

ramacharitamanas::702.verse_sanskrit: तासु श्राप हरि दीन्ह प्रमाना। कौतुकनिधि कृपाल भगवाना॥ तहाँ जलंधर रावन भयऊ। रन हति राम परम पद दयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::702.verse_hindi: लीलाओं के भंडार कृपालु हरि ने उस स्त्री के शाप को प्रामाण्य दिया (स्वीकार किया)। वही जलन्धर उस कल्प में रावण हुआ, जिसे श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने युद्ध में मारकर परमपद दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::702.english_translation: The compassionate Lord of play accepted that curse. That Jalandhara became Ravana, whom Ram killed in battle and granted the highest state.
ramacharitamanas::702.translation_literal: तासु (that) / श्राप (curse) / हरि (Hari) / दीन्ह (gave) / प्रमाना (as proof, accepted) / कौतुकनिधि (treasure of play) / कृपाल (compassionate) / भगवाना (the Lord) ॥ / तहाँ (there) / जलंधर (Jalandhara) / रावन (Ravana) / भयऊ (became) / रन (in battle) / हति (having killed) / राम (Ram) / परम पद (highest state) / दयऊ (gave)
ramacharitamanas::702.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::702.essence: What looks like a curse becomes part of Ram's larger design.
ramacharitamanas::702.simple_meaning: Ram accepted the curse and later appeared as Ravana's slayer. The verse explains that Jalandhara was born again as Ravana and was freed by Ram in battle.
ramacharitamanas::702.simple_insight: Even a curse can be folded into a larger divine purpose.
ramacharitamanas::702.detailed_meaning: The story turns from the cursed wife of Jalandhara to a larger divine pattern. Ram accepts that curse, Jalandhara is reborn as Ravana, and Ram later kills him in battle, giving him release. This prepares the next verse about why Ram takes human form.
ramacharitamanas::702.modern_relevance: A mistake, setback, or harsh consequence can feel final in the moment. Later, you may see it was one thread in a much larger pattern you could not yet read.
ramacharitamanas::702.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing events as random punishment to seeing them as part of a wider arc.

ramacharitamanas::703.verse_sanskrit: एक जनम कर कारन एहा। जेहि लगि राम धरी नरदेहा॥ प्रति अवतार कथा प्रभु केरी। सुनु मुनि बरनी कबिन्ह घनेरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::703.verse_hindi: एक जन्म का कारण यह था, जिससे श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने मनुष्य देह धारण किया। हे भरद्वाज मुनि! सुनो, प्रभु के प्रत्येक अवतार की कथा का कवियों ने नाना प्रकार से वर्णन किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::703.english_translation: The reason for this birth was that Ram took a human body. Listen, best of sages: poets have described the Lord's many incarnations in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::703.translation_literal: एक (one) / जनम (birth) / कर (of) / कारन (cause) / एहा (this) / जेहि (for which) / लगि (because) / राम (Ram) / धरी (took) / नरदेहा (human body) / प्रति (each) / अवतार (incarnation) / कथा (story) / प्रभु (Lord's) / केरी (of) / सुनु (listen) / मुनि (sage) / बरनी (described) / कबिन्ह (by poets) / घनेरी (many)
ramacharitamanas::703.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::703.essence: Ram's human birth is never accidental; it serves a larger purpose.
ramacharitamanas::703.simple_meaning: Ram took a human body for a reason. Poets have told the stories of his many forms in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::703.simple_insight: There is meaning behind every descent into the human world.
ramacharitamanas::703.detailed_meaning: After the story of Jalandhar and the earlier curse, the narration turns to Bharadvaj and explains why Ram appears in human form. The verse steps back from one episode to the larger pattern of Ram's incarnations.
ramacharitamanas::703.modern_relevance: You look back at a hard season and ask why it happened at all. This verse points to a larger pattern: some arrivals in human life are not random, but purposeful.
ramacharitamanas::703.insight: It shifts attention from isolated events to the deeper reason behind repeated divine descent.

ramacharitamanas::704.verse_sanskrit: नारद श्राप दीन्ह एक बारा। कलप एक तेहि लगि अवतारा॥ गिरिजा चकित भईं सुनि बानी। नारद बिष्नुभगत पुनि ग्यानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::704.verse_hindi: एक बार नारदजी ने शाप दिया, अतः एक कल्प में उसके लिए अवतार हुआ। यह बात सुनकर पार्वतीजी बड़ी चकित हुईं (और बोलीं कि) नारदजी तो विष्णु भक्त और ज्ञानी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::704.english_translation: Once Narad gave a curse, and for one kalpa that became the cause of an incarnation. Hearing this, Parvati was astonished and said, 'Narad is a devotee of Vishnu and also a sage of wisdom.'
ramacharitamanas::704.translation_literal: नारद (Narad) / श्राप (curse) / दीन्ह (gave) / एक बारा (once) / कलप (kalpa) / एक (one) / तेहि (for that) / लगि (because) / अवतारा (incarnation) / गिरिजा (Parvati) / चकित (astonished) / भईं (became) / सुनि (hearing) / बानी (words) / नारद (Narad) / बिष्नुभगत (devotee of Vishnu) / पुनि (also) / ग्यानी (wise)
ramacharitamanas::704.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::704.essence: A wise devotee can still become the cause of a cosmic turn.
ramacharitamanas::704.simple_meaning: Narad's curse led to an incarnation for one cosmic age. Parvati is surprised because Narad is known as both a devotee and a wise sage.
ramacharitamanas::704.simple_insight: Even revered people can act in surprising ways, and a single moment can shape a vast story.
ramacharitamanas::704.detailed_meaning: Shiva is telling Parvati why Ram takes birth in the world. He mentions a past curse from Narad as one cause, and Parvati is stunned because Narad is usually known as a great devotee and wise sage. The verse sets up her question about how such a figure could curse at all.
ramacharitamanas::704.modern_relevance: You hear a respected elder say something sharp at a family gathering, and everyone freezes. The person you trusted as calm and wise has a hidden side, and the whole room wants the backstory.
ramacharitamanas::704.insight: It shifts attention from simple labels to the deeper causes behind a person's actions.

ramacharitamanas::705.verse_sanskrit: कारन कवन श्राप मुनि दीन्हा। का अपराध रमापति कीन्हा॥ यह प्रसंग मोहि कहहु पुरारी। मुनि मन मोह आचरज भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::705.verse_hindi: मुनि ने भगवान को शाप किस कारण से दिया। लक्ष्मीपति भगवान ने उनका क्या अपराध किया था? हे पुरारि (शंकरजी)! यह कथा मुझसे कहिए। मुनि नारद के मन में मोह होना बड़े आश्चर्य की बात है ॥
ramacharitamanas::705.english_translation: What was the reason the sage was cursed? What offense did the Lord of Lakshmi commit? O Purari, tell me this episode. It is deeply astonishing that the sage Narada's mind became deluded.
ramacharitamanas::705.translation_literal: कारन (reason) / कवन (which) / श्राप (curse) / मुनि (sage) / दीन्हा (gave) / का (what) / अपराध (offense) / रमापति (Lord of Lakshmi) / कीन्हा (did) / यह (this) / प्रसंग (episode) / मोहि (to me) / कहहु (tell) / पुरारी (O Purari) / मुनि (sage) / मन (mind) / मोह (delusion) / आचरज (wonder) / भारी (great)
ramacharitamanas::705.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::705.essence: Even the wise can be shaken; the real task is to ask why.
ramacharitamanas::705.simple_meaning: Parvati asks why Narada was cursed, what offense Ram committed, and why Narada's mind became confused. She wants Shiva to explain the strange episode.
ramacharitamanas::705.simple_insight: Curiosity becomes the doorway to a deeper understanding of how even great sages can be tested.
ramacharitamanas::705.detailed_meaning: Parvati, hearing that Narada once fell into delusion, is startled. She turns to Shiva and asks why the sage was cursed, what Ram had done, and how such a wise seeker could be shaken. The verse opens the inquiry that leads into the story.
ramacharitamanas::705.modern_relevance: You hear a respected person make a disastrous choice, and your first reaction is disbelief. Instead of judging fast, you ask what pressure, pride, or blind spot led there.
ramacharitamanas::705.insight: It shifts the mind from quick judgment to patient questioning.
