ramacharitamanas::706.verse_sanskrit: बोले बिहसि महेस तब ग्यानी मूढ़ न कोइ। जेहि जस रघुपति करहिं जब सो तस तेहि छन होइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::706.verse_hindi: तब महादेवजी ने हँसकर कहा- न कोई ज्ञानी है न मूर्ख। श्री रघुनाथजी जब जिसको जैसा करते हैं, वह उसी क्षण वैसा ही हो जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::706.english_translation: Then Mahadev smiled and said: no one is truly wise or foolish. When Raghunath makes someone what they are, they become that in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::706.translation_literal: बोले (said) / बिहसि (smiling, with a smile) / महेस (Mahesh, Shiva) / तब (then) / ग्यानी (wise one) / मूढ़ (foolish one) / न (not) / कोइ (anyone) / जेहि (whom) / जस (as, in the manner) / रघुपति (Raghupati, Ram) / करहिं (does, makes) / जब (when) / सो (that one) / तस (so, thus) / तेहि (that) / छन (moment) / होइ (becomes)
ramacharitamanas::706.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::706.essence: Ram can remake any person in a single moment.
ramacharitamanas::706.simple_meaning: Shiva says no one is fixed as wise or foolish. Ram can shape any person instantly into whatever form he wills.
ramacharitamanas::706.simple_insight: It loosens pride. You stop clinging to your current identity and stay open to being transformed.
ramacharitamanas::706.detailed_meaning: Parvati has asked Shiva why Narad was cursed. Shiva answers with a smile: wisdom and foolishness are not final labels. In Ram's presence, a person can be changed at once, so the deeper mystery is divine power, not human status.
ramacharitamanas::706.modern_relevance: You were certain you were the same person who walked into the meeting yesterday. Then one hard conversation, one honest apology, one unexpected grace later — your whole self feels rearranged.
ramacharitamanas::706.insight: It shifts attention from self-judgment to surrender to transformation. Identity becomes something received, not defended.

ramacharitamanas::707.verse_sanskrit: कहउँ राम गुन गाथ भरद्वाज सादर सुनहु। भव भंजन रघुनाथ भजु तुलसी तजि मान मद ॥
ramacharitamanas::707.verse_hindi: (याज्ञवल्क्यजी कहते हैं-) हे भरद्वाज! मैं श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुणों की कथा कहता हूँ, तुम आदर से सुनो। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- मान और मद को छोड़कर आवागमन का नाश करने वाले रघुनाथजी को भजो ॥
ramacharitamanas::707.english_translation: I sing the story of Ram's virtues. Listen with respect, Bharadvaj. Tulsidas says: give up pride and arrogance, and worship Raghunath, the destroyer of the cycle of rebirth.
ramacharitamanas::707.translation_literal: कहउँ (I speak) / राम (Ram) / गुन (virtues) / गाथ (song, story) / भरद्वाज (Bharadvaj) / सादर (with respect) / सुनहु (listen) / भव (cycle of existence) / भंजन (destroyer) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath, Lord of Raghu) / भजु (worship) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / तजि (leaving aside) / मान (pride) / मद (arrogance)
ramacharitamanas::707.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::707.essence: Humility opens the door that pride keeps shut.
ramacharitamanas::707.simple_meaning: A sacred teacher invites respectful listening and says the real path is to drop pride and worship Ram, who ends repeated rebirth.
ramacharitamanas::707.simple_insight: There is relief in humility: you do not have to carry your ego into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::707.detailed_meaning: Yajnavalkya speaks to Bharadvaj in the opening of the Ram story. He asks for attentive listening, then turns the teaching into a direct invitation: abandon pride and arrogance, and take refuge in Ram, whose grace frees one from repeated wandering.
ramacharitamanas::707.modern_relevance: You enter a room already needing to look impressive, and the whole conversation hardens. This verse cuts that reflex before it starts: drop the performance, listen well, and let devotion begin where ego ends.
ramacharitamanas::707.insight: It shifts attention from self-display to receptive listening and humble devotion.

ramacharitamanas::708.verse_sanskrit: हिमगिरि गुहा एक अति पावनि। बह समीप सुरसरी सुहावनि॥ आश्रम परम पुनीत सुहावा। देखि देवरिषि मन अति भावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::708.verse_hindi: हिमालय पर्वत में एक बड़ी पवित्र गुफा थी। उसके समीप ही सुंदर गंगाजी बहती थीं। वह परम पवित्र सुंदर आश्रम देखने पर नारदजी के मन को बहुत ही सुहावना लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::708.english_translation: In the Himalayas there was a very sacred cave. Nearby flowed the beautiful Ganga. The supremely pure, lovely hermitage delighted the mind of the divine seer Narada.
ramacharitamanas::708.translation_literal: हिमगिरि (Himalaya mountain) / गुहा (cave) / एक (one) / अति (very) / पावनि (purifying, sacred) / बह (flowed) / समीप (nearby) / सुरसरी (river of the devas, Ganga) / सुहावनि (beautiful, pleasing) / आश्रम (hermitage) / परम (supremely) / पुनीत (pure, sanctified) / सुहावा (pleasant, delightful) / देखि (seeing) / देवरिषि (divine seer) / मन (mind) / अति (very) / भावा (was pleased)
ramacharitamanas::708.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::708.essence: Sacred places can settle the mind before any teaching begins.
ramacharitamanas::708.simple_meaning: A sacred cave, the Ganga nearby, and a pure hermitage make Narada feel deeply pleased.
ramacharitamanas::708.simple_insight: Some places quiet the mind before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::708.detailed_meaning: Narada comes upon a holy hermitage in the Himalayas, with a cave and the Ganga close by. The setting itself softens him. This verse simply paints the sacred scene before the deeper teaching begins.
ramacharitamanas::708.modern_relevance: You step into a temple courtyard after a noisy commute. The bells, the water, the stillness — before you pray, something in you has already softened.
ramacharitamanas::708.insight: It shifts attention from inner chatter to the power of sacred surroundings to calm and prepare the mind.

ramacharitamanas::709.verse_sanskrit: निरखि सैल सरि बिपिन बिभागा। भयउ रमापति पद अनुरागा॥ सुमिरत हरिहि श्राप गति बाधी। सहज बिमल मन लागि समाधी ॥
ramacharitamanas::709.verse_hindi: पर्वत, नदी और वन के (सुंदर) विभागों को देखकर नादरजी का लक्ष्मीकांत भगवान के चरणों में प्रेम हो गया। भगवान का स्मरण करते ही उन (नारद मुनि) के शाप की (जो शाप उन्हें दक्ष प्रजापति ने दिया था और जिसके कारण वे एक स्थान पर नहीं ठहर सकते थे) गति रुक गई और मन के स्वाभाविक ही निर्मल होने से उनकी समाधि लग गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::709.english_translation: Seeing the mountains, river, and forest, Narada developed love for the feet of Lakshmipati. Remembering Hari, the movement of his curse was halted, and with a naturally pure mind, he entered samadhi.
ramacharitamanas::709.translation_literal: निरखि (seeing) / सैल (mountain) / सरि (river) / बिपिन (forest) / बिभागा (arrangements) / भयउ (became) / रमापति (Lakshmipati) / पद (feet) / अनुरागा (loving attachment)॥ / सुमिरत (remembering) / हरिहि (Hari) / श्राप (curse) / गति (movement) / बाधी (was stopped) / सहज (natural) / बिमल (pure) / मन (mind) / लागि (became attached) / समाधी (complete stillness)॥
ramacharitamanas::709.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::709.essence: Remembering Ram can still even a cursed, restless mind.
ramacharitamanas::709.simple_meaning: Narada sees the beauty of the place and falls into loving remembrance of Ram. That remembrance quiets his curse and naturally settles his mind into deep stillness.
ramacharitamanas::709.simple_insight: Beauty can turn the mind inward and make restlessness fall away.
ramacharitamanas::709.detailed_meaning: Narada has come to a holy hermitage by the Himalayas, where river, mountain, and forest all seem alive with sanctity. The sight awakens love for Ram, and that love stops the restless movement caused by his curse. His mind becomes pure and still.
ramacharitamanas::709.modern_relevance: You step out of a noisy train station into a quiet riverside path, and your breathing changes before you even notice it. Sometimes the right place, seen rightly, can settle a scattered mind.
ramacharitamanas::709.insight: It shifts attention from outer restlessness to inner stillness through remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::710.verse_sanskrit: मुनि गति देखि सुरेस डेराना। कामहि बोलि कीन्ह सनमाना॥ सहित सहाय जाहु मम हेतू। चलेउ हरषि हियँ जलचरकेतू ॥
ramacharitamanas::710.verse_hindi: नारद मुनि की (यह तपोमयी) स्थिति देखकर देवराज इंद्र डर गया। उसने कामदेव को बुलाकर उसका आदर-सत्कार किया (और कहा कि) मेरे (हित के) लिए तुम अपने सहायकों सहित (नारद की समाधि भंग करने को) जाओ। (यह सुनकर) मीनध्वज कामदेव मन में प्रसन्न होकर चला ॥
ramacharitamanas::710.english_translation: Seeing Narada's absorbed state, Indra grew afraid. He summoned Kama and honored him, saying, 'Go with your helpers for my sake.' Delighted in his heart, Kama went forth.
ramacharitamanas::710.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / गति (state) / देखि (seeing) / सुरेस (lord of the gods, Indra) / डेराना (became afraid) / कामहि (Kama) / बोलि (calling) / कीन्ह (made) / सनमाना (honor) / सहित (together with) / सहाय (helpers) / जाहु (go) / मम (my) / हेतू (for the sake) / चलेउ (went) / हरषि (joyfully) / हियँ (in heart) / जलचरकेतू (Kama)
ramacharitamanas::710.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::710.essence: Fear makes power protect itself by breaking another's stillness.
ramacharitamanas::710.simple_meaning: Indra fears Narada's deep meditation and sends Kama to break it. Kama leaves happily with his helpers.
ramacharitamanas::710.simple_insight: Even a powerful mind can feel threatened by someone else's inner steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::710.detailed_meaning: Narada is deep in spiritual absorption near the Himalayan hermitage. Indra, alarmed by that power, calls Kama and respectfully sends him to disrupt Narada's meditation. The verse shows jealousy turning into manipulation.
ramacharitamanas::710.modern_relevance: You see someone stay calm under pressure while everyone else spirals. Instead of learning from them, a jealous mind tries to unsettle them. That reaction reveals fear more than strength.
ramacharitamanas::710.insight: It exposes how insecurity can turn admiration into sabotage.

ramacharitamanas::711.verse_sanskrit: सुनासीर मन महुँ असि त्रासा। चहत देवरिषि मम पुर बासा॥ जे कामी लोलुप जग माहीं। कुटिल काक इव सबहि डेराहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::711.verse_hindi: इन्द्र के मन में यह डर हुआ कि देवर्षि नारद मेरी पुरी (अमरावती) का निवास (राज्य) चाहते हैं। जगत में जो कामी और लोभी होते हैं, वे कुटिल कौए की तरह सबसे डरते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::711.english_translation: Indra feared that the divine sage Narada wanted to dwell in his city. In the world, the lustful and greedy fear everyone, like crooked crows do.
ramacharitamanas::711.translation_literal: सुनासीर (Indra) / मन महुँ (in the mind) / असि (such) / त्रासा (fear) / चहत (wanting) / देवरिषि (divine sage) / मम (my) / पुर (city) / बासा (dwelling) ॥ जे (those who) / कामी (lustful) / लोलुप (greedy) / जग माहीं (in the world) / कुटिल (crooked) / काक (crow) / इव (like) / सबहि (everyone) / डेराहीं (fear) ॥
ramacharitamanas::711.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::711.essence: Desire turns the mind suspicious and afraid of everyone.
ramacharitamanas::711.simple_meaning: Greed and desire make the mind suspicious. A person ruled by craving starts fearing everyone, even harmless people.
ramacharitamanas::711.simple_insight: It feels freeing to see that suspicion often comes from your own craving, not from other people.
ramacharitamanas::711.detailed_meaning: After Narada’s austere devotion shakes the heavens, Indra panics and imagines Narada wants his throne-city. Tulsidas then widens the scene: anyone ruled by desire and greed lives in fear, always expecting loss.
ramacharitamanas::711.modern_relevance: You see a coworker glance at your project and instantly assume they want to take credit. That reflex often reveals your own insecurity more than their intent.
ramacharitamanas::711.insight: It shifts the mind from projecting threat onto others to noticing how craving distorts perception.

ramacharitamanas::712.verse_sanskrit: सूख हाड़ लै भाग सठ स्वान निरखि मृगराज। छीनि लेइ जनि जान जड़ तिमि सुरपतिहि न लाज ॥
ramacharitamanas::712.verse_hindi: जैसे मूर्ख कुत्ता सिंह को देखकर सूखी हड्डी लेकर भागे और वह मूर्ख यह समझे कि कहीं उस हड्डी को सिंह छीन न ले, वैसे ही इन्द्र को (नारदजी मेरा राज्य छीन लेंगे, ऐसा सोचते) लाज नहीं आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::712.english_translation: Like a foolish dog running with a dry bone at the sight of a lion, Indra thought Narad would steal his kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::712.translation_literal: सूख (dry) / हाड़ (bone) / लै (taking) / भाग (runs) / सठ (foolish) / स्वान (dog) / निरखि (seeing) / मृगराज (lion) / छीनि (snatch away) / लेइ (takes) / जनि (do not) / जान (know) / जड़ (foolish one) / तिमि (thus) / सुरपतिहि (to Indra) / लाज (shame)
ramacharitamanas::712.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::712.essence: Fear makes a ruler defend a loss that never existed.
ramacharitamanas::712.simple_meaning: A foolish mind imagines a threat where none exists and panics over what it cannot truly protect.
ramacharitamanas::712.simple_insight: You can notice how fear shrinks perception and makes ordinary things feel like attacks.
ramacharitamanas::712.detailed_meaning: Narad's austerity has unsettled Indra. Instead of seeing clearly, Indra imagines his throne is in danger. Tulsidas mocks that fear with a sharp image: a dog running from a lion while clutching a bone.
ramacharitamanas::712.modern_relevance: You see a senior's unread message and instantly assume you're in trouble. The mind grabs a tiny fear, then builds a whole disaster around it.
ramacharitamanas::712.insight: It trains the mind to spot projection, not reality, before reacting.

ramacharitamanas::713.verse_sanskrit: तेहि आश्रमहिं मदन जब गयऊ। निज मायाँ बसंत निरमयऊ॥ कुसुमित बिबिध बिटप बहुरंगा। कूजहिं कोकिल गुंजहिं भृंगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::713.verse_hindi: जब कामदेव उस आश्रम में गया, तब उसने अपनी माया से वहाँ वसन्त ऋतु को उत्पन्न किया। तरह-तरह के वृक्षों पर रंग-बिरंगे फूल खिल गए, उन पर कोयलें कूकने लगीं और भौंरे गुंजार करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::713.english_translation: When Kama entered that hermitage, he used his illusion to create spring there. Trees of many kinds blossomed in many colors, cuckoos sang, and bees hummed.
ramacharitamanas::713.translation_literal: तेहि (that) / आश्रमहिं (in the hermitage) / मदन (Kama) / जब (when) / गयऊ (went) / निज (his own) / मायाँ (illusion/power) / बसंत (spring) / निरमयऊ (created) / कुसुमित (blossomed) / बिबिध (various) / बिटप (trees) / बहुरंगा (many-colored) / कूजहिं (were singing) / कोकिल (cuckoos) / गुंजहिं (were humming) / भृंगा (bees)
ramacharitamanas::713.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::713.essence: Desire can dress itself as spring and still unsettle the heart.
ramacharitamanas::713.simple_meaning: Kama enters the hermitage and makes spring appear. Flowers bloom, cuckoos call, and bees hum all around.
ramacharitamanas::713.simple_insight: Beauty can arrive as temptation, not just delight.
ramacharitamanas::713.detailed_meaning: In the hermitage, Kama arrives and instantly stirs the atmosphere with spring-like beauty. Trees bloom, birds call, and bees hum. This is not peace; it is the setup for desire to awaken and disturb the sages' stillness.
ramacharitamanas::713.modern_relevance: You open your phone for one quick check, and suddenly the whole evening has changed. One small spark can turn calm attention into restless wanting.
ramacharitamanas::713.insight: It shows how desire often enters through beauty, then reshapes the whole mindscape.

ramacharitamanas::714.verse_sanskrit: चली सुहावनि त्रिबिध बयारी। काम कृसानु बढ़ावनिहारी॥ रंभादिक सुर नारि नबीना। सकल असमसर कला प्रबीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::714.verse_hindi: कामाग्नि को भड़काने वाली तीन प्रकार की (शीतल, मंद और सुगंध) सुहावनी हवा चलने लगी। रम्भा आदि नवयुवती देवांगनाएँ, जो सब की सब कामकला में निपुण थीं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::714.english_translation: A pleasant threefold breeze began to blow, fanning the fire of desire. Rambha and other youthful celestial women, all skilled in every art of seduction, appeared.
ramacharitamanas::714.translation_literal: चली (began to blow) / सुहावनि (pleasant) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / बयारी (breeze) / काम (desire) / कृसानु (fire) / बढ़ावनिहारी (that which increases) ॥ / रंभा (Rambha) / आदिक (and others) / सुर (celestial) / नारि (women) / नबीना (young) / सकल (all) / असमसर (unequalled) / कला (arts) / प्रबीना (skilled) ॥
ramacharitamanas::714.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::714.essence: Desire spreads when the surroundings begin to feed it.
ramacharitamanas::714.simple_meaning: A soft, pleasant wind rises, and beautiful celestial women appear, adding to the atmosphere of desire.
ramacharitamanas::714.simple_insight: Desire grows through atmosphere, not just choice.
ramacharitamanas::714.detailed_meaning: In the sage's forest retreat, Madana has just entered and spring has been conjured around the hermitage. Now the scene thickens: a sweet threefold breeze blows, and Rambha and other celestial women appear, skilled in alluring arts. It is a setup, not the climax.
ramacharitamanas::714.modern_relevance: A playlist, a perfume, a late-night scroll — small cues can stir cravings before you notice them. The mind is often led by atmosphere long before it feels led by choice.
ramacharitamanas::714.insight: It shows how temptation builds through sensory stimulation and social imagery before any overt action begins.

ramacharitamanas::715.verse_sanskrit: करहिं गान बहु तान तरंगा। बहुबिधि क्रीड़हिं पानि पतंगा॥ देखि सहाय मदन हरषाना। कीन्हेसि पुनि प्रपंच बिधि नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::715.verse_hindi: वे बहुत प्रकार की तानों की तरंग के साथ गाने लगीं और हाथ में गेंद लेकर नाना प्रकार के खेल खेलने लगीं। कामदेव अपने इन सहायकों को देखकर बहुत प्रसन्न हुआ और फिर उसने नाना प्रकार के मायाजाल किए ॥
ramacharitamanas::715.english_translation: They sang with many flowing melodies and played many kinds of ball games. Seeing these helpers, Kama was delighted and created yet more forms of illusion.
ramacharitamanas::715.translation_literal: करहिं (they do) / गान (song) / बहु (many) / तान (melodies) / तरंगा (waves) / बहुबिधि (many kinds) / क्रीड़हिं (they खेलते हैं / play) / पानि (hand) / पतंगा (ball) / देखि (seeing) / सहाय (helpers) / मदन (Kama) / हरषाना (became delighted) / कीन्हेसि (he made) / पुनि (again) / प्रपंच (illusion / contrivance) / बिधि (manner) / नाना (many)
ramacharitamanas::715.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::715.essence: Desire never rests; it keeps inventing new temptations.
ramacharitamanas::715.simple_meaning: The nymphs sing and play to stir desire, and Kama responds by creating even more seductive illusions.
ramacharitamanas::715.simple_insight: Desire feeds on stimulation and always asks for more.
ramacharitamanas::715.detailed_meaning: In the grove, Kama has already filled the air with spring, music, and beautiful attendants to disturb the sage's meditation. Here the seduction intensifies: the celestial women sing and play, Kama grows pleased, and the whole scene becomes a deliberate web of temptation.
ramacharitamanas::715.modern_relevance: You open one harmless video, and the feed keeps changing shape to hold your attention. The pull does not stop at enough; it learns your weakness and keeps decorating it.
ramacharitamanas::715.insight: It shows how craving escalates by multiplying distractions around itself.

ramacharitamanas::716.verse_sanskrit: काम कला कछु मुनिहि न ब्यापी। निज भयँ डरेउ मनोभव पापी॥ सीम कि चाँपि सकइ कोउ तासू। बड़ रखवार रमापति जासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::716.verse_hindi: परन्तु कामदेव की कोई भी कला मुनि पर असर न कर सकी। तब तो पापी कामदेव अपने ही (नाश के) भय से डर गया। लक्ष्मीपति भगवान जिसके बड़े रक्षक हों, भला, उसकी सीमा (मर्यादा) को कोई दबा सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::716.english_translation: No art of desire could touch the sage. The sinful god of desire grew afraid of his own ruin. Who can crush the boundary of one protected by the Lord of Lakshmi?
ramacharitamanas::716.translation_literal: काम कला (arts of desire) / कछु (any) / मुनिहि (the sage) / न (not) / ब्यापी (affected) / निज (own) / भयँ (from fear) / डरेउ (became afraid) / मनोभव (desire-born one) / पापी (sinful) / सीम (boundary) / कि (can?) / चाँपि (press down) / सकइ (can) / कोउ (anyone) / तासू (his) / बड़ (great) / रखवार (protector) / रमापति (Lord of Lakshmi) / जासू (whose)
ramacharitamanas::716.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::716.essence: Desire fails where the protected mind cannot be breached.
ramacharitamanas::716.simple_meaning: Desire could not disturb the sage, and desire itself became afraid. No one can overrun the limits of someone guarded by the Lord of Lakshmi.
ramacharitamanas::716.simple_insight: Inner steadiness makes temptation lose its power.
ramacharitamanas::716.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sages remain undisturbed while Kamadeva sends every weapon of temptation. The verse turns the scene into a lesson: when divine protection is strong, even desire recoils in fear.
ramacharitamanas::716.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with flirtation, pressure, and subtle bait, but one person simply does not bite. The noise loses force when the mind is already guarded.
ramacharitamanas::716.insight: It shifts attention from resisting temptation to standing in a protection stronger than temptation.

ramacharitamanas::717.verse_sanskrit: सहित सहाय सभीत अति मानि हारि मन मैन। गहेसि जाइ मुनि चरन तब कहि सुठि आरत बैन ॥
ramacharitamanas::717.verse_hindi: तब अपने सहायकों समेत कामदेव ने बहुत डरकर और अपने मन में हार मानकर बहुत ही आर्त (दीन) वचन कहते हुए मुनि के चरणों को जा पकड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::717.english_translation: Then Kama, with all his helpers, grew very afraid, admitted defeat in his mind, and went to clasp the sage's feet, speaking very humble and distressed words.
ramacharitamanas::717.translation_literal: सहित (along with) / सहाय (helpers) / सभीत (very afraid) / अति (greatly) / मानि हारि (having accepted defeat) / मन मैन (in the mind) / गहेसि (he grasped) / जाइ (going) / मुनि (sage) / चरन (feet) / तब (then) / कहि (speaking) / सुठि (very) / आरत (distressed) / बैन (words)
ramacharitamanas::717.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::717.essence: Fear makes pride bow before humility.
ramacharitamanas::717.simple_meaning: Kama loses his courage, gives up his pride, and humbly approaches the sage's feet with distressed words.
ramacharitamanas::717.simple_insight: Pride collapses fast when it meets a greater steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::717.detailed_meaning: Kama has just tried and failed to disturb Narada. Frightened and defeated, he comes with his companions and clings to the sage's feet, speaking in a pleading voice. The scene is moving toward Narada's response, not making a final teaching yet.
ramacharitamanas::717.modern_relevance: You send the apology text after a harsh argument, then stare at the screen before hitting send. The hard part is not the words — it's dropping the ego first.
ramacharitamanas::717.insight: It shows that defeat becomes bearable only when pride is set down.

ramacharitamanas::718.verse_sanskrit: भयउ न नारद मन कछु रोषा। कहि प्रिय बचन काम परितोषा॥ नाइ चरन सिरु आयसु पाई। गयउ मदन तब सहित सहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::718.verse_hindi: नारदजी के मन में कुछ भी क्रोध न आया। उन्होंने प्रिय वचन कहकर कामदेव का समाधान किया। तब मुनि के चरणों में सिर नवाकर और उनकी आज्ञा पाकर कामदेव अपने सहायकों सहित लौट गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::718.english_translation: Narad felt no anger at all. He spoke kindly and satisfied Kama. Then, bowing his head at the sage's feet and receiving the sage's permission, Kama returned with his helpers.
ramacharitamanas::718.translation_literal: भयउ (became) / न (not) / नारद (Narad) / मन (mind) / कछु (any) / रोषा (anger) । कहि (speaking) / प्रिय (pleasant) / बचन (words) / काम (Kama) / परितोषा (satisfied) ॥ नाइ (bowing) / चरन (feet) / सिरु (head) / आयसु (permission) / पाई (having obtained) । गयउ (went) / मदन (Kama) / तब (then) / सहित (with) / सहाई (helpers) ॥
ramacharitamanas::718.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::718.essence: Gentleness ends conflict more surely than force.
ramacharitamanas::718.simple_meaning: Narad stays calm, speaks kindly, and sends Kama away peacefully after Kama bows and receives permission.
ramacharitamanas::718.simple_insight: Calm speech can end what anger would only inflame.
ramacharitamanas::718.detailed_meaning: Narad has just faced Kama's attempt to disturb his austerity. Instead of anger, he answers with kindness. Kama bows, accepts Narad's authority, and leaves with his helpers. The scene shows restraint defeating provocation.
ramacharitamanas::718.modern_relevance: Someone snaps at you in a meeting, expecting a fight. You lower your voice, answer cleanly, and the whole room softens. Not every provocation deserves your heat.
ramacharitamanas::718.insight: It teaches you to answer pressure with composure instead of reflexive retaliation.

ramacharitamanas::719.verse_sanskrit: मुनि सुसीलता आपनि करनी। सुरपति सभाँ जाइ सब बरनी॥ सुनि सब कें मन अचरजु आवा। मुनिहि प्रसंसि हरिहि सिरु नावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::719.verse_hindi: देवराज इन्द्र की सभा में जाकर उसने मुनि की सुशीलता और अपनी करतूत सब कही, जिसे सुनकर सबके मन में आश्चर्य हुआ और उन्होंने मुनि की बड़ाई करके श्री हरि को सिर नवाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::719.english_translation: He went to Indra's court and told everyone of the sage's gentleness and of his own conduct. Hearing this, everyone was amazed. They praised the sage and bowed their heads to Hari.
ramacharitamanas::719.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / सुसीलता (gentleness) / आपनि (own) / करनी (conduct) / सुरपति (lord of the gods, Indra) / सभाँ (in the court) / जाइ (going) / सब (all) / बरनी (described) / सुनि (hearing) / सब कें (everyone's) / मन (mind) / अचरजु (wonder) / आवा (came) / मुनिहि (the sage) / प्रसंसि (having praised) / हरिहि (Hari) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed)
ramacharitamanas::719.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::719.essence: Humility and virtue win respect even in a divine court.
ramacharitamanas::719.simple_meaning: He reported the sage's goodness and his own actions in Indra's court. Everyone was astonished, praised the sage, and bowed to Hari.
ramacharitamanas::719.simple_insight: Good conduct can leave even powerful beings humbled and amazed.
ramacharitamanas::719.detailed_meaning: After being defeated in pride, Narad goes to Indra's court and recounts both the sage's gentleness and his own behavior. The assembly is struck with wonder, praises the sage, and bows to Hari. The scene shows how humility and virtue outshine ego.
ramacharitamanas::719.modern_relevance: You explain a tense incident to a room full of people, expecting judgment. Instead, your honesty makes the whole room quiet, and respect rises where defensiveness could have been.
ramacharitamanas::719.insight: It shifts attention from self-importance to the power of truthful, humble conduct.

ramacharitamanas::720.verse_sanskrit: तब नारद गवने सिव पाहीं। जिता काम अहमिति मन माहीं॥ मार चरति संकरहि सुनाए। अतिप्रिय जानि महेस सिखाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::720.verse_hindi: तब नारदजी शिवजी के पास गए। उनके मन में इस बात का अहंकार हो गया कि हमने कामदेव को जीत लिया। उन्होंने कामदेव के चरित्र शिवजी को सुनाए और महादेवजी ने उन (नारदजी) को अत्यन्त प्रिय जानकर (इस प्रकार) शिक्षा दी- ॥
ramacharitamanas::720.english_translation: Then Narad went to Shiva, proud in his mind that he had conquered desire. He told Shiva of desire's defeat, and Shiva, knowing him to be dear, gave him this teaching.
ramacharitamanas::720.translation_literal: तब (then) / नारद (Narad) / गवने (went) / सिव पाहीं (to Shiva) / जिता (conquered) / काम (desire) / अहमिति (ego-sense) / मन माहीं (in the mind)॥ / मार चरति (the conduct of desire) / संकरहि (to Shiva) / सुनाए (told) / अतिप्रिय (very dear) / जानि (knowing) / महेस (Mahesh/Shiva) / सिखाए (taught)॥
ramacharitamanas::720.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::720.essence: A conquered desire can return as pride.
ramacharitamanas::720.simple_meaning: Narad becomes proud after defeating desire and goes to Shiva to boast. Shiva, seeing him as dear, teaches him a lesson.
ramacharitamanas::720.simple_insight: Winning one battle can still feed the very ego that needs watching.
ramacharitamanas::720.detailed_meaning: Narad has just calmed desire and impressed the gods, but that victory turns into pride. He goes to Shiva and recounts the conquest. Shiva, who loves him, responds not with praise alone but with instruction, because the real danger is the ego that follows success.
ramacharitamanas::720.modern_relevance: You finally handled a temptation, a deadline, or a hard conversation well — and immediately started narrating your victory to yourself. That second story can be the trap.
ramacharitamanas::720.insight: It shifts attention from outer victory to the mind's hidden self-congratulation.

ramacharitamanas::721.verse_sanskrit: बार बार बिनवउँ मुनि तोही। जिमि यह कथा सुनायहु मोही॥ तिमि जनि हरिहि सुनावहु कबहूँ। चलेहुँ प्रसंग दुराएहु तबहूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::721.verse_hindi: हे मुनि! मैं तुमसे बार-बार विनती करता हूँ कि जिस तरह यह कथा तुमने मुझे सुनाई है, उस तरह भगवान श्री हरि को कभी मत सुनाना। चर्चा भी चले तब भी इसको छिपा जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::721.english_translation: O sage, I beg you again and again: never tell Hari this story as you told it to me. Even if the topic comes up, keep it hidden.
ramacharitamanas::721.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / बिनवउँ (I beg) / मुनि (sage) / तोही (to you) / जिमि (as) / यह (this) / कथा (story) / सुनायहु (you told) / मोही (to me) / तिमि (so) / जनि (do not) / हरिहि (to Hari) / सुनावहु (tell) / कबहूँ (ever) / चलेहुँ (even if it comes up) / प्रसंग (topic) / दुराएहु (hide) / तबहूँ (then too)
ramacharitamanas::721.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::721.essence: Humility sometimes begins by asking for silence.
ramacharitamanas::721.simple_meaning: Narad asks the sage not to repeat the story to Hari, even casually. He wants the matter kept hidden.
ramacharitamanas::721.simple_insight: Some truths are not for display. Reverence sometimes means knowing what should stay unspoken.
ramacharitamanas::721.detailed_meaning: After hearing the tale of Shiva and Kamadeva, Narad becomes uneasy and ashamed of his own pride. He turns to the sage and begs him not to repeat the story to Hari, even if the subject arises again.
ramacharitamanas::721.modern_relevance: You tell a friend something embarrassing in confidence, then spend the next day praying it never comes back around. That instinct to protect what is tender is in Narad's plea.
ramacharitamanas::721.insight: It shifts the mind from publicizing every experience to guarding what humility requires be kept private.

ramacharitamanas::722.verse_sanskrit: संभु दीन्ह उपदेस हित नहिं नारदहि सोहान। भरद्वाज कौतुक सुनहु हरि इच्छा बलवान ॥
ramacharitamanas::722.verse_hindi: यद्यपि शिवजी ने यह हित की शिक्षा दी, पर नारदजी को वह अच्छी न लगी। हे भरद्वाज! अब कौतुक (तमाशा) सुनो। हरि की इच्छा बड़ी बलवान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::722.english_translation: Although Shiva gave this beneficial counsel, Narada did not like it. Listen, Bharadvaja, to the marvel: the will of Hari is mighty indeed.
ramacharitamanas::722.translation_literal: संभु (Shiva) / दीन्ह (gave) / उपदेस (instruction) / हित (beneficial) / नहिं (not) / नारदहि (to Narada) / सोहान (pleased) / भरद्वाज (Bharadvaja) / कौतुक (wonder) / सुनहु (listen) / हरि (Hari) / इच्छा (will) / बलवान (powerful)
ramacharitamanas::722.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::722.essence: Hari's will outruns every human plan.
ramacharitamanas::722.simple_meaning: Shiva gave Narada good advice, but Narada did not accept it. The real wonder is that Hari's will is stronger than anyone's plan.
ramacharitamanas::722.simple_insight: Relief comes from seeing that pride cannot outrun a greater will.
ramacharitamanas::722.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Bharadvaja after Narada's pride has been stirred. He points out that even wise counsel may be rejected, then opens the larger truth: Hari's will governs the unfolding of events, not human ego.
ramacharitamanas::722.modern_relevance: You can carefully plan a conversation, a move, even a whole future — and still watch it go sideways. This verse steadies the mind: the larger order is not yours to control.
ramacharitamanas::722.insight: It shifts attention from personal control to trust in a greater unfolding.

ramacharitamanas::723.verse_sanskrit: राम कीन्ह चाहहिं सोइ होई। करै अन्यथा अस नहिं कोई॥ संभु बचन मुनि मन नहिं भाए। तब बिरंचि के लोक सिधाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::723.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी जो करना चाहते हैं, वही होता है, ऐसा कोई नहीं जो उसके विरुद्ध कर सके। श्री शिवजी के वचन नारदजी के मन को अच्छे नहीं लगे, तब वे वहाँ से ब्रह्मलोक को चल दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::723.english_translation: Whatever Ram desires comes to be. No one can do otherwise. The sage did not like Shiva's words, so he went to Brahmaloka.
ramacharitamanas::723.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / कीन्ह (did) / चाहहिं (wishes) / सोइ (that only) / होई (happens) / करै (do) / अन्यथा (otherwise) / अस (such) / नहिं (not) / कोई (anyone) / संभु (Shiva) / बचन (words) / मुनि (sage) / मन (mind) / नहिं (not) / भाए (pleased) / तब (then) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / के (of) / लोक (world) / सिधाए (went)
ramacharitamanas::723.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::723.essence: Ram's will overrides every other plan.
ramacharitamanas::723.simple_meaning: Everything happens according to Ram's will, and no one can overturn it. Narad did not accept Shiva's words and left for Brahmaloka.
ramacharitamanas::723.simple_insight: It brings relief to stop fighting reality and trust that a larger will is already at work.
ramacharitamanas::723.detailed_meaning: Narad has just heard Shiva's warning about the story he asked to hear. The warning does not satisfy him, because he has already glimpsed a deeper truth: Ram's will governs everything. He turns away and goes to Brahmaloka.
ramacharitamanas::723.modern_relevance: You plan every detail of a family event, and then one small change ruins the schedule. This verse reminds you that life does not obey your control — and that peace begins when you stop demanding that it should.
ramacharitamanas::723.insight: It shifts the mind from control to trust in a larger order.

ramacharitamanas::724.verse_sanskrit: एक बार करतल बर बीना। गावत हरि गुन गान प्रबीना॥ छीरसिंधु गवने मुनिनाथा। जहँ बस श्रीनिवास श्रुतिमाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::724.verse_hindi: एक बार गानविद्या में निपुण मुनिनाथ नारदजी हाथ में सुंदर वीणा लिए, हरिगुण गाते हुए क्षीरसागर को गए, जहाँ वेदों के मस्तकस्वरूप (मूर्तिमान वेदांतत्व) लक्ष्मी निवास भगवान नारायण रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::724.english_translation: Once, Narada, master of song, took his beautiful veena and went singing the praises of Hari to the Ocean of Milk, where Lord Narayana, the dwelling of Lakshmi and the crown of the Vedas, resides.
ramacharitamanas::724.translation_literal: एक बार (once) / करतल बर बीना (beautiful veena in hand) / गावत (singing) / हरि गुन गान (praise of Hari's virtues) / प्रबीना (skilled, masterful) / छीरसिंधु (Ocean of Milk) / गवने (went) / मुनिनाथा (lord of sages, Narada) / जहँ (where) / बस (dwells) / श्रीनिवास (Lakshmi's abode, Narayana) / श्रुतिमाथा (head/crown of the Vedas)
ramacharitamanas::724.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::724.essence: Devotion moves the seeker straight toward the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::724.simple_meaning: Narada, skilled in music and devotion, goes to Vishnu’s abode in the Ocean of Milk while singing his praises.
ramacharitamanas::724.simple_insight: Devotion is not static; it moves, sings, and seeks the beloved directly.
ramacharitamanas::724.detailed_meaning: Narada, the sage-singer, leaves with his veena and heads to Vishnu’s cosmic abode in the Ocean of Milk. The scene sets up a divine meeting, but the verse itself is only the approach, not the teaching.
ramacharitamanas::724.modern_relevance: You’re walking into a room already humming the words you want to say. The verse captures that charged moment before an important encounter begins.
ramacharitamanas::724.insight: It frames devotion as an approach, not just a feeling.

ramacharitamanas::725.verse_sanskrit: हरषि मिले उठि रमानिकेता। बैठे आसन रिषिहि समेता॥ बोले बिहसि चराचर राया। बहुते दिनन कीन्हि मुनि दाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::725.verse_hindi: रमानिवास भगवान उठकर बड़े आनंद से उनसे मिले और ऋषि (नारदजी) के साथ आसन पर बैठ गए। चराचर के स्वामी भगवान हँसकर बोले- हे मुनि! आज आपने बहुत दिनों पर दया की ॥
ramacharitamanas::725.english_translation: The Lord of all beings rose joyfully to meet the sage and sat with him. Smiling, the Lord of the moving and unmoving said, "Sage, you have shown great kindness after so many days."
ramacharitamanas::725.translation_literal: हरषि (with joy) / मिले (met) / उठि (rising) / रमानिकेता (the Lord of Lakshmi's abode) / बैठे (sat) / आसन (on a seat) / रिषिहि (with the sage) / समेता (together) ॥ / बोले (spoke) / बिहसि (smiling) / चराचर राया (king of the moving and unmoving) / बहुते (many) / दिनन (days) / कीन्हि (did) / मुनि (sage) / दाया (kindness) ॥
ramacharitamanas::725.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::725.essence: Real greatness rises to greet the seeker.
ramacharitamanas::725.simple_meaning: Ram welcomes Narad with joy, sits with him, and speaks kindly. The scene shows warm divine hospitality before Narad tells the story of desire.
ramacharitamanas::725.simple_insight: There is comfort in being received with warmth, not judgment.
ramacharitamanas::725.detailed_meaning: Narad has come to Ram after wandering through the higher realms. Ram rises to greet him, seats him beside himself, and speaks with a smile. This gentle welcome sets up the next turn, when Narad will speak and the lesson on pride and desire will unfold.
ramacharitamanas::725.modern_relevance: You walk into a room carrying embarrassment, and the other person stands up to meet you with a smile. The tension drops before a single explanation is needed.
ramacharitamanas::725.insight: It shifts attention from status to welcome: true greatness makes room for others first.

ramacharitamanas::726.verse_sanskrit: काम चरित नारद सब भाषे। जद्यपि प्रथम बरजि सिवँ राखे॥ अति प्रचंड रघुपति कै माया। जेहि न मोह अस को जग जाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::726.verse_hindi: यद्यपि श्री शिवजी ने उन्हें पहले से ही बरज रखा था, तो भी नारदजी ने कामदेव का सारा चरित्र भगवान को कह सुनाया। श्री रघुनाथजी की माया बड़ी ही प्रबल है। जगत में ऐसा कौन जन्मा है, जिसे वे मोहित न कर दें ॥
ramacharitamanas::726.english_translation: Although Shiva had warned him earlier, Narada still recounted the full story of desire to the Lord. Raghupati's power of illusion is immense; who in the world is not deluded by it?
ramacharitamanas::726.translation_literal: काम चरित (the story of desire) / नारद (Narada) / सब (all) / भाषे (spoke, told) / जद्यपि (although) / प्रथम (earlier, first) / बरजि (having warned, forbidden) / सिवँ (by Shiva) / राखे (was kept) / अति (very) / प्रचंड (fierce, powerful) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / कै (of) / माया (the veil of appearance) / जेहि (whom) / न (not) / मोह (delusion) / अस (such) / को (who) / जग (in the world) / जाया (is born)
ramacharitamanas::726.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::726.essence: Pride invites delusion; clear seeing begins with humility.
ramacharitamanas::726.simple_meaning: Narada tells Ram the story of desire even after Shiva warned him not to. The verse says Ram's power of illusion is so strong that no one in the world is beyond being affected by it.
ramacharitamanas::726.simple_insight: Even a wise person can slip when pride enters. Humility is what keeps clear seeing alive.
ramacharitamanas::726.detailed_meaning: Narada has just met Ram in the sea of milk, and the conversation is turning toward a test of his wisdom. Tulsidas explains that Shiva had already cautioned Narada, yet Narada still speaks of desire. The point is Ram's overwhelming power to unsettle even the proud.
ramacharitamanas::726.modern_relevance: You think you’re above a mistake because you’ve read the warning signs. Then one flattering comment or one ego boost and your judgment bends. Pride is often the first crack.
ramacharitamanas::726.insight: It shifts attention from intellectual confidence to self-observation, showing how pride can blind even a careful mind.

ramacharitamanas::727.verse_sanskrit: रूख बदन करि बचन मृदु बोले श्रीभगवान। तुम्हरे सुमिरन तें मिटहिं मोह मार मद मान ॥
ramacharitamanas::727.verse_hindi: भगवान रूखा मुँह करके कोमल वचन बोले- हे मुनिराज! आपका स्मरण करने से दूसरों के मोह, काम, मद और अभिमान मिट जाते हैं (फिर आपके लिए तो कहना ही क्या है!) ॥
ramacharitamanas::727.english_translation: With a stern face, the Lord spoke gently: "By remembering you, delusion, desire, pride, and ego vanish."
ramacharitamanas::727.translation_literal: रूख (stern) / बदन (face) / करि (making) / बचन (words) / मृदु (gentle) / बोले (spoke) / श्रीभगवान (the Lord) / तुम्हरे (your) / सुमिरन (remembering) / तें (from) / मिटहिं (are erased) / मोह (delusion) / मार (desire) / मद (pride) / मान (ego)
ramacharitamanas::727.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::727.essence: Pure remembrance dissolves the very distortions it never carries.
ramacharitamanas::727.simple_meaning: Remembering the divine removes delusion, desire, pride, and ego. Even the Lord praises the power of a devotee's remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::727.simple_insight: Real devotion clears the mind so thoroughly that even the highest praise bows to it.
ramacharitamanas::727.detailed_meaning: Narad has just told the Lord the story of desire, and Ram answers with gentle irony. He says that remembering Narad removes delusion and pride from others, which shows how pure Narad's own remembrance is.
ramacharitamanas::727.modern_relevance: Someone you respect quietly thanks you for helping them stay steady. Their words land harder than praise because they reveal what your presence has been doing all along.
ramacharitamanas::727.insight: It shifts the focus from self-importance to the cleansing power of steady remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::728.verse_sanskrit: सुनु मुनि मोह होइ मन ताकें। ग्यान बिराग हृदय नहिं जाकें॥ ब्रह्मचरज ब्रत रत मतिधीरा। तुम्हहि कि करइ मनोभव पीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::728.verse_hindi: हे मुनि! सुनिए, मोह तो उसके मन में होता है, जिसके हृदय में ज्ञान-वैराग्य नहीं है। आप तो ब्रह्मचर्यव्रत में तत्पर और बड़े धीर बुद्धि हैं। भला, कहीं आपको भी कामदेव सता सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::728.english_translation: Listen, sage: delusion arises in a mind that lacks wisdom and non-attachment. You are devoted to celibate discipline and steady understanding—how could desire trouble you?
ramacharitamanas::728.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / मुनि (sage) / मोह (delusion) / होइ (arises) / मन (mind) / ताकें (in that one) / ग्यान (wisdom) / बिराग (non-attachment) / हृदय (heart) / नहिं (not) / जाकें (in whom) / ब्रह्मचरज (celibate discipline) / ब्रत (vow) / रत (absorbed) / मतिधीरा (steady-minded) / तुम्हहि (you) / कि (how) / करइ (can do) / मनोभव (desire) / पीरा (pain)
ramacharitamanas::728.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::728.essence: Desire cannot disturb a mind rooted in wisdom and non-attachment.
ramacharitamanas::728.simple_meaning: Delusion belongs to a mind without wisdom or detachment. Ram tells Narad that his disciplined, steady mind is beyond desire's disturbance.
ramacharitamanas::728.simple_insight: A settled mind feels protected, not hunted by craving.
ramacharitamanas::728.detailed_meaning: Narad has just spoken about desire, and Ram answers gently but firmly. He explains that confusion only takes root where wisdom and detachment are missing. Narad's celibate discipline and steady mind make him beyond such trouble.
ramacharitamanas::728.modern_relevance: You are scrolling at midnight, half-restless, half-curious, and the urge grows stronger. Ram points to the real issue: craving enters only where the mind is already unguarded.
ramacharitamanas::728.insight: It shifts attention from fighting desire to strengthening the mind that receives it.

ramacharitamanas::729.verse_sanskrit: नारद कहेउ सहित अभिमाना। कृपा तुम्हारि सकल भगवाना॥ करुनानिधि मन दीख बिचारी। उर अंकुरेउ गरब तरु भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::729.verse_hindi: नारदजी ने अभिमान के साथ कहा- भगवन! यह सब आपकी कृपा है। करुणानिधान भगवान ने मन में विचारकर देखा कि इनके मन में गर्व के भारी वृक्ष का अंकुर पैदा हो गया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::729.english_translation: Narada spoke with pride, "All this is your grace, O Lord." The compassionate Lord considered in his mind and saw that a very heavy tree of pride had sprouted in Narada's heart.
ramacharitamanas::729.translation_literal: नारद (Narada) / कहेउ (spoke) / सहित (with) / अभिमाना (pride) / कृपा (grace) / तुम्हारि (your) / सकल (all) / भगवाना (O Lord) / करुनानिधि (ocean of compassion) / मन (mind) / दीख (saw) / बिचारी (having considered) / उर (heart) / अंकुरेउ (sprouted) / गरब (pride) / तरु (tree) / भारी (heavy)
ramacharitamanas::729.speaker: Narada
ramacharitamanas::729.essence: Ram sees pride the moment it begins to grow.
ramacharitamanas::729.simple_meaning: Narada praises Ram, but pride has quietly begun growing inside him. Ram sees the hidden flaw at once.
ramacharitamanas::729.simple_insight: Praise can still feed ego if the heart slips toward self-importance.
ramacharitamanas::729.detailed_meaning: Narada has just spoken to Ram after the earlier exchange about delusion and detachment. He says the right words, but a subtle pride has entered his heart. Ram, seeing inwardly, notices the first sprout of that pride before it grows.
ramacharitamanas::729.modern_relevance: You get thanked in public for doing the right thing, and a small part of you starts enjoying the spotlight. The warning is simple: even holy-sounding words can hide self-importance.
ramacharitamanas::729.insight: It teaches you to watch the hidden motive beneath even noble speech and spiritual pride.

ramacharitamanas::730.verse_sanskrit: बेगि सो मैं डारिहउँ उखारी। पन हमार सेवक हितकारी॥ मुनि कर हित मम कौतुक होई। अवसि उपाय करबि मैं सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::730.verse_hindi: मैं उसे तुरंत ही उखाड़ फेंकूँगा, क्योंकि सेवकों का हित करना हमारा प्रण है। मैं अवश्य ही वह उपाय करूँगा, जिससे मुनि का कल्याण और मेरा खेल हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::730.english_translation: I will uproot it at once. Serving the welfare of my servants is my vow. I will surely do whatever brings the sage good and makes my play complete.
ramacharitamanas::730.translation_literal: बेगि (quickly) / सो (that) / मैं (I) / डारिहउँ (will throw down) / उखारी (uprooting) / पन (vow) / हमार (our) / सेवक (servants) / हितकारी (beneficial) / मुनि (sage) / कर (of) / हित (welfare) / मम (my) / कौतुक (play) / होई (becomes) / अवसि (certainly) / उपाय (means) / करबि (to do) / मैं (I) / सोई (that)
ramacharitamanas::730.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::730.essence: Ram makes his servant's welfare his own vow.
ramacharitamanas::730.simple_meaning: Ram says he will remove the obstacle at once, because protecting his devotee is his promise. He will arrange whatever is needed for the sage's good.
ramacharitamanas::730.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing devotion is not ignored; care answers care.
ramacharitamanas::730.detailed_meaning: Narad has just spoken with a trace of pride, and Ram responds not with anger but with a vow. In this Balkand moment, Ram treats the welfare of his servant as his own concern, turning the sage's issue into his play.
ramacharitamanas::730.modern_relevance: You send a message late at night because someone you care about is struggling. You don't calculate whether it is convenient. You act because their well-being matters to you.
ramacharitamanas::730.insight: It shifts attention from self-importance to protective care for those who rely on you.

ramacharitamanas::731.verse_sanskrit: तब नारद हरि पद सिर नाई। चले हृदयँ अहमिति अधिकाई॥ श्रीपति निज माया तब प्रेरी। सुनहु कठिन करनी तेहि केरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::731.verse_hindi: तब नारदजी भगवान के चरणों में सिर नवाकर चले। उनके हृदय में अभिमान और भी बढ़ गया। तब लक्ष्मीपति भगवान ने अपनी माया को प्रेरित किया। अब उसकी कठिन करनी सुनो ॥
ramacharitamanas::731.english_translation: Then Narada bowed his head at Hari's feet and departed. Pride grew even stronger in his heart. Then the Lord of Lakshmi stirred his own illusion. Listen now to the difficult deed it performed.
ramacharitamanas::731.translation_literal: तब (then) / नारद (Narada) / हरि पद (Hari's feet) / सिर नाई (bowing the head) / चले (departed) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / अहमिति (I-am-ness / ego) / अधिकाई (increased greatly) / श्रीपति (Lord of Lakshmi) / निज (own) / माया (illusion) / तब (then) / प्रेरी (stirred / impelled) / सुनहु (listen) / कठिन (difficult) / करनी (deed / doing) / तेहि (that) / केरी (of it)
ramacharitamanas::731.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::731.essence: Even devotion can feed ego if the heart is not watched.
ramacharitamanas::731.simple_meaning: Narada bows to Hari, but pride grows in him. Seeing this, the divine power of illusion is set in motion, and the next verse begins the trouble it causes.
ramacharitamanas::731.simple_insight: A small trace of pride can survive even after devotion. That is where confusion begins.
ramacharitamanas::731.detailed_meaning: Narada has just praised Hari, but the praise has fed his pride instead of dissolving it. Seeing that inner swelling, the Lord of Lakshmi lets illusion take over, setting up the test that will expose Narada's hidden ego.
ramacharitamanas::731.modern_relevance: You finish a beautiful prayer, a helpful post, or a sincere apology — and still secretly want applause. That hidden craving is where the next mistake begins.
ramacharitamanas::731.insight: It shifts attention from outward devotion to the ego that can hide inside it.

ramacharitamanas::732.verse_sanskrit: बिरचेउ मग महुँ नगर तेहिं सत जोजन बिस्तार। श्रीनिवासपुर तें अधिक रचना बिबिध प्रकार ॥
ramacharitamanas::732.verse_hindi: उस (हरिमाया) ने रास्ते में सौ योजन (चार सौ कोस) का एक नगर रचा। उस नगर की भाँति-भाँति की रचनाएँ लक्ष्मीनिवास भगवान विष्णु के नगर (वैकुण्ठ) से भी अधिक सुंदर थीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::732.english_translation: She built a city on the road, stretching one hundred yojanas wide. Its many kinds of structures were even more splendid than the city of Vishnu's abode.
ramacharitamanas::732.translation_literal: बिरचेउ (built) / मग महुँ (on the road) / नगर (city) / तेहिं (that) / सत जोजन (one hundred yojanas) / बिस्तार (spread, width) / श्रीनिवासपुर (the city of Vishnu's abode) / तें (than) / अधिक (greater, more) / रचना (construction, arrangement) / बिबिध प्रकार (of many kinds)
ramacharitamanas::732.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::732.essence: Appearance can outshine reality and still be only illusion.
ramacharitamanas::732.simple_meaning: The divine illusion created a vast, beautiful city on the road, more splendid than Vishnu's own abode.
ramacharitamanas::732.simple_insight: What looks solid can be conjured in an instant and vanish just as quickly.
ramacharitamanas::732.detailed_meaning: Narad has just been unsettled by the divine illusion. On the road before him, a huge city appears, complete in every detail and even more dazzling than Vishnu's own abode. The verse lingers on the scale of the illusion before the next scene unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::732.modern_relevance: You walk into a perfectly staged showroom and almost believe the story it tells. The lights, the layout, the polish — all of it can be designed to shape your mind before you notice.
ramacharitamanas::732.insight: It trains attention to question appearances before trusting them.

ramacharitamanas::733.verse_sanskrit: बसहिं नगर सुंदर नर नारी। जनु बहु मनसिज रति तनुधारी॥ तेहिं पुर बसइ सीलनिधि राजा। अगनित हय गय सेन समाजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::733.verse_hindi: उस नगर में ऐसे सुंदर नर-नारी बसते थे, मानो बहुत से कामदेव और (उसकी स्त्री) रति ही मनुष्य शरीर धारण किए हुए हों। उस नगर में शीलनिधि नाम का राजा रहता था, जिसके यहाँ असंख्य घोड़े, हाथी और सेना के समूह (टुकड़ियाँ) थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::733.english_translation: In that city lived beautiful men and women, as if many Cupids and Rati had taken human bodies. In that city lived King Sīl-nidhi, with countless horses, elephants, and armies.
ramacharitamanas::733.translation_literal: बसहिं (they live) / नगर (city) / सुंदर (beautiful) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / जनु (as if) / बहु (many) / मनसिज (Cupid) / रति (Rati) / तनु-धारी (body-bearing) / तेहिं (in that) / पुर (city) / बसइ (lives) / सीलनिधि (Sīl-nidhi, ocean of virtue) / राजा (king) / अगनित (countless) / हय (horses) / गय (elephants) / सेन (army) / समाजा (assemblies/groups)
ramacharitamanas::733.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::733.essence: Splendor can dazzle the eye and still remain only a display.
ramacharitamanas::733.simple_meaning: The verse describes a splendid city full of beautiful people and a powerful king with vast armies.
ramacharitamanas::733.simple_insight: Greatness can look dazzling from the outside, yet it is still only a scene in the story.
ramacharitamanas::733.detailed_meaning: Narad has just been led through a miraculous city created by divine illusion. This verse paints its surface beauty: radiant people, a virtuous king, and immense military power. The next verse deepens the illusion by showing even greater splendor.
ramacharitamanas::733.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where everything gleams — lights, flowers, polished smiles, perfect order. It feels complete at first glance, yet you still do not know what holds it together.
ramacharitamanas::733.insight: It trains the mind to notice appearance without mistaking it for reality.

ramacharitamanas::734.verse_sanskrit: सत सुरेस सम बिभव बिलासा। रूप तेज बल नीति निवासा॥ बिस्वमोहनी तासु कुमारी। श्री बिमोह जिसु रूपु निहारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::734.verse_hindi: उसका वैभव और विलास सौ इन्द्रों के समान था। वह रूप, तेज, बल और नीति का घर था। उसके विश्वमोहिनी नाम की एक (ऐसी रूपवती) कन्या थी, जिसके रूप को देखकर लक्ष्मीजी भी मोहित हो जाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::734.english_translation: His wealth and splendor were like those of a hundred Indras. He was a dwelling of beauty, radiance, strength, and noble conduct. He had a daughter named Vishvamohini, whose form could even enchant Lakshmi herself.
ramacharitamanas::734.translation_literal: सत (hundred) / सुरेस (lords of the devas) / सम (equal to) / बिभव (wealth) / बिलासा (splendor, luxury) / रूप (beauty, form) / तेज (radiance) / बल (strength) / नीति (noble conduct) / निवासा (dwelling, abode) / बिस्वमोहनी (world-bewitching) / तासु (his) / कुमारी (daughter, maiden) / श्री (Lakshmi) / बिमोह (delight, enchantment) / जिसु (whose) / रूपु (form) / निहारी (seeing, beholding)
ramacharitamanas::734.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::734.essence: Splendor here is a prelude, not the point.
ramacharitamanas::734.simple_meaning: The king's court was unimaginably splendid, and his daughter was so beautiful that even Lakshmi would be enchanted by her.
ramacharitamanas::734.simple_insight: Some scenes exist only to prepare the stage for wonder.
ramacharitamanas::734.detailed_meaning: In Janak's city, Tulsidas pauses to paint the royal house before Sita's swayamvar. The king's splendor, virtues, and daughter are described in superhuman terms, building the sense that something extraordinary is about to unfold.
ramacharitamanas::734.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall before the guests arrive, and everything already feels charged — lights, flowers, silence, expectation. The setting itself tells you that an important meeting is coming.
ramacharitamanas::734.insight: It shifts attention from plot to atmosphere, showing how grandeur can foreshadow a decisive turning point.

ramacharitamanas::735.verse_sanskrit: सोइ हरिमाया सब गुन खानी। सोभा तासु कि जाइ बखानी॥ करइ स्वयंबर सो नृपबाला। आए तहँ अगनित महिपाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::735.verse_hindi: वह सब गुणों की खान भगवान की माया ही थी। उसकी शोभा का वर्णन कैसे किया जा सकता है। वह राजकुमारी स्वयंवर करना चाहती थी, इससे वहाँ अगणित राजा आए हुए थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::735.english_translation: She was the divine veil of appearance, a storehouse of every virtue. Her beauty cannot be described. She chose a swayamvara, and countless kings gathered there.
ramacharitamanas::735.translation_literal: सोइ (that very) / हरिमाया (the divine veil of appearance of Hari) / सब (all) / गुन (virtues) / खानी (mine, storehouse) / सोभा (beauty, splendor) / तासु (her) / कि (how) / जाइ (can be) / बखानी (described) / करइ (does) / स्वयंबर (swayamvara) / सो (that) / नृपबाला (princess) / आए (came) / तहँ (there) / अगनित (countless) / महिपाला (kings)
ramacharitamanas::735.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::735.essence: True splendor needs no praise; it gathers kings by itself.
ramacharitamanas::735.simple_meaning: She was a princess of extraordinary beauty and virtues. Her swayamvara drew countless kings, and her splendor was beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::735.simple_insight: Some presence is so complete that language fails before it.
ramacharitamanas::735.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s city, the princess’s beauty and qualities are being introduced before the swayamvara begins. She is so remarkable that even her appearance feels beyond words, and kings from everywhere arrive, setting the stage for the contest.
ramacharitamanas::735.modern_relevance: A room falls quiet when someone with real presence walks in. No exaggeration is needed; people simply turn their heads. Some qualities announce themselves before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::735.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary admiration to the force of character that naturally draws the world in.

ramacharitamanas::736.verse_sanskrit: मुनि कौतुकी नगर तेहि गयऊ। पुरबासिन्ह सब पूछत भयऊ॥ सुनि सब चरित भूपगृहँ आए। करि पूजा नृप मुनि बैठाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::736.verse_hindi: खिलवाड़ी मुनि नारदजी उस नगर में गए और नगरवासियों से उन्होंने सब हाल पूछा। सब समाचार सुनकर वे राजा के महल में आए। राजा ने पूजा करके मुनि को (आसन पर) बैठाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::736.english_translation: The curious sage went to the city and asked the townspeople about everything. Hearing the whole story, he came to the king's palace. The king worshipped the sage and seated him with honor.
ramacharitamanas::736.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / कौतुकी (curious, playful) / नगर (city) / तेहि (that) / गयऊ (went) / पुरबासिन्ह (townspeople) / सब (all) / पूछत (asking) / भयऊ (became)॥ / सुनि (having heard) / सब (all) / चरित (events, story) / भूपगृहँ (to the king's house) / आए (came)॥ / करि (doing) / पूजा (worship, honor) / नृप (king) / मुनि (sage) / बैठाए (seated)॥
ramacharitamanas::736.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::736.essence: Curiosity enters politely, and the truth starts to reveal itself.
ramacharitamanas::736.simple_meaning: Narada visits the city, asks the people what is happening, then goes to the king's palace, where the king honors him and gives him a seat.
ramacharitamanas::736.simple_insight: Respect opens the next conversation. A sincere question and a humble welcome can move a whole story forward.
ramacharitamanas::736.detailed_meaning: Narada, the curious sage, arrives in the city where the princess's swayamvar is being prepared. He asks the townspeople for the full story, then goes to the king's palace. The king receives him with honor, setting up the next decisive question.
ramacharitamanas::736.modern_relevance: You hear a strange rumor about a family wedding and ask around before judging. Then you show up respectfully, listen first, and the real story begins to unfold.
ramacharitamanas::736.insight: It shifts attention from gossip to careful inquiry and respectful listening before any judgment is made.

ramacharitamanas::737.verse_sanskrit: आनि देखाई नारदहि भूपति राजकुमारि। कहहु नाथ गुन दोष सब एहि के हृदयँ बिचारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::737.verse_hindi: (फिर) राजा ने राजकुमारी को लाकर नारदजी को दिखलाया (और पूछा कि-) हे नाथ! आप अपने हृदय में विचार कर इसके सब गुण-दोष कहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::737.english_translation: The king brought the princess and showed her to Narada, asking, “O Lord, think in your heart and tell me all her virtues and faults.”
ramacharitamanas::737.translation_literal: आनि (bringing) / देखाई (showed) / नारदहि (to Narada) / भूपति (the king) / राजकुमारि (the princess) / कहहु (say) / नाथ (O lord) / गुन (virtues) / दोष (faults) / सब (all) / एहि (of this) / के (of) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारि (having considered)
ramacharitamanas::737.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::737.essence: Wise choice begins with clear judgment, not excitement.
ramacharitamanas::737.simple_meaning: The king presents the princess to Narada and asks him to judge her qualities and flaws from the heart.
ramacharitamanas::737.simple_insight: Not every important decision comes from impulse; some require calm, honest assessment.
ramacharitamanas::737.detailed_meaning: King Janaka brings Sita before Narada in the midst of the swayamvar preparations. He asks the sage to judge her qualities and faults carefully. The scene moves the story from beauty and wonder into a test of discernment.
ramacharitamanas::737.modern_relevance: Before a major commitment, you want someone wise to look past the excitement and tell you what is actually there. The heart can rush; clear seeing takes longer.
ramacharitamanas::737.insight: It shifts attention from attraction to discernment, asking for an honest reading before commitment.

ramacharitamanas::738.verse_sanskrit: देखि रूप मुनि बिरति बिसारी। बड़ी बार लगि रहे निहारी॥ लच्छन तासु बिलोकि भुलाने। हृदयँ हरष नहिं प्रगट बखाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::738.verse_hindi: उसके रूप को देखकर मुनि वैराग्य भूल गए और बड़ी देर तक उसकी ओर देखते ही रह गए। उसके लक्षण देखकर मुनि अपने आपको भी भूल गए और हृदय में हर्षित हुए, पर प्रकट रूप में उन लक्षणों को नहीं कहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::738.english_translation: Seeing her beauty, the sage forgot detachment and kept looking for a long time. Seeing her marks, he was delighted inwardly, but did not speak them aloud.
ramacharitamanas::738.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / रूप (form, beauty) / मुनि (sage) / बिरति (detachment) / बिसारी (forgot) / बड़ी (great) / बार (time) / लगि (for) / रहे (remained) / निहारी (staring, gazing) ॥ / लच्छन (marks, signs) / तासु (of her) / बिलोकि (seeing) / भुलाने (were bewildered, forgot themselves) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / हरष (joy) / नहिं (not) / प्रगट (openly) / बखाने (described, spoke) ॥
ramacharitamanas::738.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::738.simple_meaning: Narad sees Sita's beauty and becomes absorbed. He feels joy inside, but keeps his thoughts to himself.
ramacharitamanas::738.simple_insight: Even a detached mind can be overwhelmed by beauty and remain silent.
ramacharitamanas::738.detailed_meaning: Narad has come to King Janak's palace to judge Sita for the swayamvar. The moment he sees her, his usual detachment slips. He keeps looking, feels joy inwardly, and says nothing, revealing how powerful her presence is.
ramacharitamanas::738.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a wedding and lose your practiced composure for a moment. The face is calm, but inside everything has shifted before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::738.insight: It shows how beauty can unsettle even a disciplined observer and how strong feeling can remain unspoken.

ramacharitamanas::739.verse_sanskrit: जो एहि बरइ अमर सोइ होई। समरभूमि तेहि जीत न कोई॥ सेवहिं सकल चराचर ताही। बरइ सीलनिधि कन्या जाही ॥
ramacharitamanas::739.verse_hindi: (लक्षणों को सोचकर वे मन में कहने लगे कि) जो इसे ब्याहेगा, वह अमर हो जाएगा और रणभूमि में कोई उसे जीत न सकेगा। यह शीलनिधि की कन्या जिसको वरेगी, सब चर-अचर जीव उसकी सेवा करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::739.english_translation: Whoever marries her becomes immortal; no one can defeat him on the battlefield. Whomsoever this daughter of the treasury of virtue chooses, all moving and unmoving beings will serve.
ramacharitamanas::739.translation_literal: जो (who) / एहि (this) / बरइ (marries) / अमर (immortal) / सोइ (that one) / होई (becomes) / समरभूमि (battlefield) / तेहि (him) / जीत (defeat) / न (not) / कोई (anyone) / सेवहिं (serve) / सकल (all) / चराचर (moving and unmoving) / ताही (that one) / बरइ (chooses to marry) / सीलनिधि (treasury of virtue) / कन्या (daughter) / जाही (whom)
ramacharitamanas::739.speaker: Narad
ramacharitamanas::739.essence: Virtue makes a person unconquerable and universally honoured.
ramacharitamanas::739.simple_meaning: Narad sees Sita's qualities and thinks the man who marries her will be invincible, and all beings will serve the one she chooses.
ramacharitamanas::739.simple_insight: Real worth draws protection and respect without force.
ramacharitamanas::739.detailed_meaning: Narad has just seen Janaki's beauty and qualities in King Janak's palace. As he keeps looking, his mind fills with awe: the man who wins her hand will be unconquerable, and the one she chooses will be honoured by all creation. It is a thought born from wonder.
ramacharitamanas::739.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose character changes the room before they speak. Their steadiness, grace, and integrity make force look small.
ramacharitamanas::739.insight: It shifts attention from outward power to the quiet force of virtue and worth.

ramacharitamanas::740.verse_sanskrit: लच्छन सब बिचारि उर राखे। कछुक बनाइ भूप सन भाषे॥ सुता सुलच्छन कहि नृप पाहीं। नारद चले सोच मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::740.verse_hindi: सब लक्षणों को विचारकर मुनि ने अपने हृदय में रख लिया और राजा से कुछ अपनी ओर से बनाकर कह दिए। राजा से लड़की के सुलक्षण कहकर नारदजी चल दिए। पर उनके मन में यह चिन्ता थी कि- ॥
ramacharitamanas::740.english_translation: After considering all the signs, the sage kept them in his heart and spoke to the king in a slightly altered way. He praised the princess's excellent marks and then departed, but worry remained in Narad's mind.
ramacharitamanas::740.translation_literal: लच्छन (signs) / सब (all) / बिचारि (having considered) / उर (in the heart) / राखे (kept) / कछुक (a little) / बनाइ (making) / भूप (king) / सन (to) / भाषे (spoke) / सुता (daughter) / सुलच्छन (having auspicious marks) / कहि (saying) / नृप (king) / पाहीं (to) / नारद (Narad) / चले (went) / सोच (worry) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::740.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::740.essence: Careful words can hide a mind already in conflict.
ramacharitamanas::740.simple_meaning: Narad notices the signs, holds his thoughts back, and speaks to the king in a careful way. He leaves, but his mind stays troubled.
ramacharitamanas::740.simple_insight: Sometimes the real conflict begins after the right words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::740.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Narad has examined Sita's signs and sensed what they mean. He tells King Janak enough to move the scene forward, but not enough to reveal his own inner reaction. As he leaves, desire and worry begin to tug at him.
ramacharitamanas::740.modern_relevance: You leave a family gathering after saying something polite, but your mind keeps replaying the conversation in the car. The real story is happening under the surface.
ramacharitamanas::740.insight: It shows how a person can speak calmly while carrying a private storm inside.

ramacharitamanas::741.verse_sanskrit: करौं जाइ सोइ जतन बिचारी। जेहि प्रकार मोहि बरै कुमारी॥ जप तप कछु न होइ तेहि काला। हे बिधि मिलइ कवन बिधि बाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::741.verse_hindi: मैं जाकर सोच-विचारकर अब वही उपाय करूँ, जिससे यह कन्या मुझे ही वरे। इस समय जप-तप से तो कुछ हो नहीं सकता। हे विधाता! मुझे यह कन्या किस तरह मिलेगी? ॥
ramacharitamanas::741.english_translation: I will go and think of the right plan, the one by which the princess will choose me. At this time, no chanting or austerity can help. O Fate, by what means can I win this girl?
ramacharitamanas::741.translation_literal: करौं (I will do) / जाइ (going) / सोइ (that) / जतन (effort, plan) / बिचारी (having thought) / जेहि प्रकार (by which way) / मोहि (me) / बरै (chooses as husband) / कुमारी (the princess) / जप (chanting) / तप (austerity) / कछु (something) / न होइ (does not happen) / तेहि काला (at that time) / हे बिधि (O Fate) / मिलइ (may I get) / कवन बिधि (by what means) / बाला (the girl)
ramacharitamanas::741.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::741.essence: Winning requires the right method, not just desire.
ramacharitamanas::741.simple_meaning: The speaker decides to think carefully and find a way to win the princess. Prayer and austerity feel useless in that moment.
ramacharitamanas::741.simple_insight: Sometimes the next step is not more effort, but a clearer plan.
ramacharitamanas::741.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the swayamvar is near and the challenge is real. The speaker realizes raw devotion or ritual alone will not work here, so he turns to strategy and asks how the princess can be won.
ramacharitamanas::741.modern_relevance: You’ve tried being sincere, patient, and well-prepared, but the moment still needs a smarter move. Sometimes the answer is not more intensity — it’s better direction.
ramacharitamanas::741.insight: It shifts the mind from vague striving to practical, situation-specific action.

ramacharitamanas::742.verse_sanskrit: एहि अवसर चाहिअ परम सोभा रूप बिसाल। जो बिलोकि रीझै कुअँरि तब मेलै जयमाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::742.verse_hindi: इस समय तो बड़ी भारी शोभा और विशाल (सुंदर) रूप चाहिए, जिसे देखकर राजकुमारी मुझ पर रीझ जाए और तब जयमाल (मेरे गले में) डाल दे ॥
ramacharitamanas::742.english_translation: At this moment, only great splendor and a vast, beautiful form are needed—one that the princess will see, delight in, and then place the garland around my neck.
ramacharitamanas::742.translation_literal: एहि अवसर (at this moment) / चाहिअ (is needed) / परम (greatest) / सोभा (splendor) / रूप (form, beauty) / बिसाल (vast, expansive) / जो (which) / बिलोकि (seeing) / रीझै (is pleased) / कुअँरि (princess) / तब (then) / मेलै (places) / जयमाल (garland of victory)
ramacharitamanas::742.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::742.essence: Pride hunts for approval through appearance.
ramacharitamanas::742.simple_meaning: The sage is thinking that the only thing needed now is a stunning appearance that will win the princess's heart and bring the garland to him.
ramacharitamanas::742.simple_insight: Sometimes the whole game feels like it depends on one perfect moment of presence.
ramacharitamanas::742.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, Narad has just realized he cannot win Sita by his own effort. He looks for a way to appear irresistible, believing beauty alone will make the princess choose him. This verse captures that anxious calculation.
ramacharitamanas::742.modern_relevance: You are getting ready for a wedding, interview, or stage entrance and start believing everything depends on how you look. The mind narrows to one thought: will they be impressed?
ramacharitamanas::742.insight: It exposes the ego's belief that outer charm can control another person's choice.

ramacharitamanas::743.verse_sanskrit: हरि सन मागौं सुंदरताई। होइहि जात गहरु अति भाई॥ मोरें हित हरि सम नहिं कोऊ। एहि अवसर सहाय सोइ होऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::743.verse_hindi: (एक काम करूँ कि) भगवान से सुंदरता माँगूँ, पर भाई! उनके पास जाने में तो बहुत देर हो जाएगी, किन्तु श्री हरि के समान मेरा हितू भी कोई नहीं है, इसलिए इस समय वे ही मेरे सहायक हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::743.english_translation: I should ask Hari for beauty, but getting to Him takes too long, brother. No one is as helpful to me as Hari, so let Him be my aid now.
ramacharitamanas::743.translation_literal: हरि (Hari) / सन (from) / मागौं (I ask for) / सुंदरताई (beauty) / होइहि (will be) / जात (going) / गहरु (delay) / अति (very) / भाई (brother) / मोरें (for me) / हित (well-wisher) / हरि (Hari) / सम (equal to) / नहिं (not) / कोऊ (anyone) / एहि (this) / अवसर (occasion) / सहाय (helper) / सोइ (that one) / होऊ (be)
ramacharitamanas::743.speaker: Narada
ramacharitamanas::743.essence: Hari alone can help when every other plan feels too slow.
ramacharitamanas::743.simple_meaning: Narada wants beauty, but he knows only Hari can truly help him right now. He turns to Hari because no one else can do what is needed.
ramacharitamanas::743.simple_insight: Relief comes from knowing whom to turn to first.
ramacharitamanas::743.detailed_meaning: Narada stands before the divine problem of winning a bride and realizes that ordinary effort will not be enough. He asks Hari for beauty, then immediately admits that Hari alone can help him in this moment.
ramacharitamanas::743.modern_relevance: You are preparing for a meeting that could change everything, and your own confidence feels thin. The mind stops bargaining and simply turns to the one source of help it trusts.
ramacharitamanas::743.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance to direct appeal for grace.

ramacharitamanas::744.verse_sanskrit: बहुबिधि बिनय कीन्हि तेहि काला। प्रगटेउ प्रभु कौतुकी कृपाला॥ प्रभु बिलोकि मुनि नयन जुड़ाने। होइहि काजु हिएँ हरषाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::744.verse_hindi: उस समय नारदजी ने भगवान की बहुत प्रकार से विनती की। तब लीलामय कृपालु प्रभु (वहीं) प्रकट हो गए। स्वामी को देखकर नारदजी के नेत्र शीतल हो गए और वे मन में बड़े ही हर्षित हुए कि अब तो काम बन ही जाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::744.english_translation: At that moment, Narada offered many kinds of prayers. Then the playful, compassionate Lord appeared. Seeing the Lord, Narada's eyes cooled, and his heart filled with joy: now the task would surely be done.
ramacharitamanas::744.translation_literal: बहुबिधि (many kinds) / बिनय (prayer, humble request) / कीन्हि (made) / तेहि काला (at that time) / प्रगटेउ (appeared) / प्रभु (the Lord) / कौतुकी (playful) / कृपाला (compassionate) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बिलोकि (seeing) / मुनि (sage Narada) / नयन (eyes) / जुड़ाने (became cool) / होइहि (will happen) / काजु (task) / हिएँ (in the heart) / हरषाने (rejoiced)
ramacharitamanas::744.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::744.essence: Sincere prayer meets a compassionate response.
ramacharitamanas::744.simple_meaning: Narada prays in many ways, and Ram appears in response. Seeing him, Narada feels relief and joy because his request now has a chance to succeed.
ramacharitamanas::744.simple_insight: Prayer is not empty when the heart is sincere; help can arrive the moment you stop doubting.
ramacharitamanas::744.detailed_meaning: Narada has been asking Ram for a boon after the earlier exchange about beauty and praise. In this moment, Ram appears before him as the playful, compassionate Lord. Narada's fear settles, and hope rises, because the answer has finally come close.
ramacharitamanas::744.modern_relevance: You send the final message after days of hesitation, then see the reply appear. The tightness in your chest loosens instantly. Relief can feel like grace arriving on time.
ramacharitamanas::744.insight: It shifts the mind from anxious pleading to confident expectation once help has truly arrived.

ramacharitamanas::745.verse_sanskrit: अति आरति कहि कथा सुनाई। करहु कृपा करि होहु सहाई॥ आपन रूप देहु प्रभु मोहीं। आन भाँति नहिं पावौं ओही ॥
ramacharitamanas::745.verse_hindi: नारदजी ने बहुत आर्त (दीन) होकर सब कथा कह सुनाई (और प्रार्थना की कि) कृपा कीजिए और कृपा करके मेरे सहायक बनिए। हे प्रभो! आप अपना रूप मुझको दीजिए और किसी प्रकार मैं उस (राजकन्या) को नहीं पा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::745.english_translation: Narad, deeply distressed, told the whole story and prayed, "Please be merciful and help me. Lord, give me your own form; otherwise I cannot obtain her in any other way."
ramacharitamanas::745.translation_literal: अति (very) / आरति (distress) / कहि (having said) / कथा (story) / सुनाई (told) / करहु (do) / कृपा (mercy) / करि (having) / होहु (be) / सहाई (helper) / आपन (own) / रूप (form) / देहु (give) / प्रभु (Lord) / मोहीं (to me) / आन (other) / भाँति (way) / नहिं (not) / पावौं (I may obtain) / ओही (that one)
ramacharitamanas::745.speaker: Narad
ramacharitamanas::745.essence: True help begins when pride gives way to honest need.
ramacharitamanas::745.simple_meaning: Narad asks for mercy and help. He says he wants the Lord's own form, because no other way can win the princess.
ramacharitamanas::745.simple_insight: Need becomes clear when pride drops. Then prayer stops performing and starts asking honestly.
ramacharitamanas::745.detailed_meaning: Narad has just seen Ram appear and now pours out his distress. He asks for help, then admits the deeper desire: he wants the Lord's own form to win the princess. The scene turns from praise to pleading.
ramacharitamanas::745.modern_relevance: You stand outside a doorway, rehearsing confidence, but the real request is simpler: help me become what is needed. Honest need changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::745.insight: It shifts the mind from clever strategy to direct surrender and need.

ramacharitamanas::746.verse_sanskrit: जेहि बिधि नाथ होइ हित मोरा। करहु सो बेगि दास मैं तोरा॥ निज माया बल देखि बिसाला। हियँ हँसि बोले दीनदयाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::746.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! जिस तरह मेरा हित हो, आप वही शीघ्र कीजिए। मैं आपका दास हूँ। अपनी माया का विशाल बल देख दीनदयालु भगवान मन ही मन हँसकर बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::746.english_translation: O Lord, do whatever is best for me, and do it quickly. I am Your servant. Seeing the vast power of My own illusion, the compassionate Lord smiled inwardly and spoke.
ramacharitamanas::746.translation_literal: जेहि बिधि (in whatever way) / नाथ (Lord) / होइ (becomes) / हित (benefit) / मोरा (my) / करहु (do) / सो (that) / बेगि (quickly) / दास (servant) / मैं (I) / तोरा (Your) / निज (own) / माया (illusion/power of appearance) / बल (strength) / देखि (seeing) / बिसाला (vast) / हियँ (in the heart) / हँसि (smiling) / बोले (spoke) / दीनदयाला (compassionate one)
ramacharitamanas::746.speaker: Narada
ramacharitamanas::746.essence: True surrender asks for the highest good, not personal preference.
ramacharitamanas::746.simple_meaning: Narada asks the Lord to do whatever will truly help him, quickly, and calls himself the Lord's servant. The Lord, seeing the vast power of illusion, smiles and answers.
ramacharitamanas::746.simple_insight: Real surrender asks for what is truly best, not just what is wanted.
ramacharitamanas::746.detailed_meaning: Narada has just begged for a form of the Lord he can truly understand. Now he goes further: he asks only for what will serve his highest good and calls himself the Lord's servant. The Lord smiles, seeing how powerful illusion is, and prepares to answer his request.
ramacharitamanas::746.modern_relevance: You finally admit you do not know what will help most. In that honest moment, you stop bargaining and ask for what is truly good.
ramacharitamanas::746.insight: It shifts the mind from demanding a preferred outcome to asking for the best outcome.

ramacharitamanas::747.verse_sanskrit: जेहि बिधि होइहि परम हित नारद सुनहु तुम्हार। सोइ हम करब न आन कछु बचन न मृषा हमार ॥
ramacharitamanas::747.verse_hindi: हे नारदजी! सुनो, जिस प्रकार आपका परम हित होगा, हम वही करेंगे, दूसरा कुछ नहीं। हमारा वचन असत्य नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::747.english_translation: O Narada, listen: whatever will be for your highest good, that alone I will do. I will do nothing else. My word is never false.
ramacharitamanas::747.translation_literal: जेहि बिधि (in whatever way) / होइहि (will become) / परम हित (highest good) / नारद (Narada) / सुनहु (listen) / तुम्हार (your) / सोइ (that alone) / हम (we/I) / करब (will do) / न (not) / आन कछु (anything else) / बचन (word) / न मृषा (not false) / हमार (our/my)
ramacharitamanas::747.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::747.essence: True care tells the truth and chooses what helps, not what flatters.
ramacharitamanas::747.simple_meaning: Ram tells Narada that he will do only what truly benefits him, and that his promise is always true.
ramacharitamanas::747.simple_insight: There is deep comfort in a presence that chooses your welfare and never lies.
ramacharitamanas::747.detailed_meaning: Narada has come asking for help, and Ram answers with calm certainty. He promises to act only for Narada's highest good, then grounds that promise in the truthfulness of his word. This moment turns request into reassurance.
ramacharitamanas::747.modern_relevance: You finally tell someone the real problem, and they don't rush to please you. They say, 'I won't give you what you want if it harms you.' That kind of honesty feels rare.
ramacharitamanas::747.insight: It shifts trust from getting what you ask for to receiving what truly helps.

ramacharitamanas::748.verse_sanskrit: कुपथ माग रुज ब्याकुल रोगी। बैद न देइ सुनहु मुनि जोगी॥ एहि बिधि हित तुम्हार मैं ठयऊ। कहि अस अंतरहित प्रभु भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::748.verse_hindi: हे योगी मुनि! सुनिए, रोग से व्याकुल रोगी कुपथ्य माँगे तो वैद्य उसे नहीं देता। इसी प्रकार मैंने भी तुम्हारा हित करने की ठान ली है। ऐसा कहकर भगवान अन्तर्धान हो गए ॥
