ramacharitamanas::748.english_translation: O yogi sage, listen: when a sick patient asks for harmful food, the physician does not give it. In the same way, I have decided what is truly good for you. Saying this, the Lord disappeared.
ramacharitamanas::748.translation_literal: कुपथ (harmful food) / माग (asks for) / रुज (sick) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / रोगी (patient) / बैद (physician) / न देइ (does not give) / सुनहु (listen) / मुनि (sage) / जोगी (yogi) / एहि बिधि (in this way) / हित (good) / तुम्हार (your) / मैं (I) / ठयऊ (decided) / कहि (saying) / अस (thus) / अंतरहित (vanished) / प्रभु (the Lord) / भयऊ (became)
ramacharitamanas::748.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::748.essence: True care sometimes refuses the thing most loudly asked for.
ramacharitamanas::748.simple_meaning: Ram refuses Narada's request because it would not be good for him, just as a doctor refuses harmful food to a sick patient. He vanishes after making the point.
ramacharitamanas::748.simple_insight: Not every request should be granted. Care sometimes means refusing what the other person wants.
ramacharitamanas::748.detailed_meaning: Narada has just asked for a blessing, and Ram answers with gentle firmness. He compares himself to a physician and Narada to a sick man craving the wrong remedy. The teaching is not to satisfy desire, but to protect true welfare.
ramacharitamanas::748.modern_relevance: A friend begs you to cover for them again, and you know it will only deepen the mess. Saying no can be the most caring response.
ramacharitamanas::748.insight: It shifts the mind from pleasing requests to protecting real welfare.

ramacharitamanas::749.verse_sanskrit: माया बिबस भए मुनि मूढ़ा। समुझी नहिं हरि गिरा निगूढ़ा॥ गवने तुरत तहाँ रिषिराई। जहाँ स्वयंबर भूमि बनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::749.verse_hindi: (भगवान की) माया के वशीभूत हुए मुनि ऐसे मूढ़ हो गए कि वे भगवान की अगूढ़ (स्पष्ट) वाणी को भी न समझ सके। ऋषिराज नारदजी तुरंत वहाँ गए जहाँ स्वयंवर की भूमि बनाई गई थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::749.english_translation: Deluded by maya, the sage became foolish and could not understand the hidden words of Hari. Then the king of sages hurried to the place where the swayamvar ground had been prepared.
ramacharitamanas::749.translation_literal: माया (veil of appearance) / बिबस (overpowered) / भए (became) / मुनि (sage) / मूढ़ा (foolish) / समुझी (understood) / नहिं (not) / हरि (Hari, Ram) / गिरा (speech) / निगूढ़ा (hidden) / गवने (went) / तुरत (immediately) / तहाँ (there) / रिषिराई (king of sages) / जहाँ (where) / स्वयंबर (swayamvar) / भूमि (ground) / बनाई (made)
ramacharitamanas::749.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::749.essence: Pride makes a wise mind miss what is plainly before it.
ramacharitamanas::749.simple_meaning: Maya clouds Narad's judgment, so he cannot grasp Ram's subtle warning. Still caught in that confusion, he rushes to the swayamvar ground.
ramacharitamanas::749.simple_insight: Pride can make even a wise mind miss the warning right in front of it.
ramacharitamanas::749.detailed_meaning: Narad has just been warned by Ram in a gentle, hidden way, but the illusion of his own importance blinds him. Unaware of the trap forming inside his own mind, he hurries to the prepared swayamvar ground.
ramacharitamanas::749.modern_relevance: You reread a message three times and still miss the obvious tone because you are already sure you are right. Narad's mistake is that kind of blindness.
ramacharitamanas::749.insight: It shows how self-importance can block clear seeing, even when the truth is already being spoken.

ramacharitamanas::750.verse_sanskrit: निज निज आसन बैठे राजा। बहु बनाव करि सहित समाजा॥ मुनि मन हरष रूप अति मोरें। मोहि तजि आनहि बरिहि न भोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::750.verse_hindi: राजा लोग खूब सज-धजकर समाज सहित अपने-अपने आसन पर बैठे थे। मुनि (नारद) मन ही मन प्रसन्न हो रहे थे कि मेरा रूप बड़ा सुंदर है, मुझे छोड़ कन्या भूलकर भी दूसरे को न वरेगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::750.english_translation: The kings sat on their own seats, all decorated and assembled. The sage felt delighted in his mind: “My form is so beautiful that the maiden will surely choose me and no one else, not even by mistake.”
ramacharitamanas::750.translation_literal: निज निज (their own) / आसन (seats) / बैठे (sat) / राजा (kings) / बहु (much) / बनाव (adornment) / करि (having done) / सहित (with) / समाजा (assembly) / मुनि (sage) / मन (mind) / हरष (joy) / रूप (form) / अति (very) / मोरें (mine) / मोहि (me) / तजि (leaving) / आनहि (another) / बरिहि (will choose) / न (not) / भोरें (even by mistake / at dawn)
ramacharitamanas::750.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::750.essence: Pride makes a person certain of being chosen before the test begins.
ramacharitamanas::750.simple_meaning: The kings are seated in splendor for the swayamvar, and Narada privately becomes proud of his own appearance, thinking Sita will choose no one but him.
ramacharitamanas::750.simple_insight: Pride can blind even a wise mind before the moment of choice arrives.
ramacharitamanas::750.detailed_meaning: At the swayamvar hall in Mithila, the kings sit in full display before the assembled court. Narada looks at himself with secret delight, convinced his beauty will win Sita. The next verse shows how that vanity is about to be shattered.
ramacharitamanas::750.modern_relevance: You check your reflection before entering the room and decide, almost automatically, that you’ll be the one chosen, noticed, preferred. That small inner boast is where trouble begins.
ramacharitamanas::750.insight: It exposes how self-admiration quietly distorts judgment before reality has even spoken.

ramacharitamanas::751.verse_sanskrit: मुनि हित कारन कृपानिधाना। दीन्ह कुरूप न जाइ बखाना॥ सो चरित्र लखि काहुँ न पावा। नारद जानि सबहिं सिर नावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::751.verse_hindi: कृपानिधान भगवान ने मुनि के कल्याण के लिए उन्हें ऐसा कुरूप बना दिया कि जिसका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता, पर यह चरित कोई भी न जान सका। सबने उन्हें नारद ही जानकर प्रणाम किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::751.english_translation: For the welfare of the sage, the gracious Lord made him so ugly that it cannot be described. No one could understand that whole episode, and everyone bowed, knowing him to be Narada.
ramacharitamanas::751.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / हित (welfare) / कारन (for the sake of) / कृपानिधाना (treasure of grace) / दीन्ह (gave) / कुरूप (ugly form) / न जाइ (cannot be) / बखाना (described) / सो (that) / चरित्र (episode / conduct) / लखि (seeing / understanding) / काहुँ (anyone) / न (not) / पावा (found / understood) / नारद (Narada) / जानि (knowing) / सबहिं (everyone) / सिर (head) / नावा (bowed)
ramacharitamanas::751.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::751.essence: Grace can disguise itself as humiliation to save you from pride.
ramacharitamanas::751.simple_meaning: Narada was transformed into an ugly form for his own good, and no one could fully understand the divine play behind it. Everyone still bowed to him as Narada.
ramacharitamanas::751.simple_insight: Even humiliation can be part of grace, and the deepest workings of the divine are not always obvious at first.
ramacharitamanas::751.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, Narada arrives proud of his beauty. To protect him from his own vanity, the gracious Lord makes him unrecognisable. The crowd cannot grasp the hidden reason, but they still honour him as Narada.
ramacharitamanas::751.modern_relevance: You get corrected in public, and your first instinct is embarrassment. Later you realise the sting saved you from a bigger fall. Not every loss is a punishment.
ramacharitamanas::751.insight: It shifts the mind from pride in appearance to humility before unseen correction.

ramacharitamanas::752.verse_sanskrit: रहे तहाँ दुइ रुद्र गन ते जानहिं सब भेउ। बिप्रबेष देखत फिरहिं परम कौतुकी तेउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::752.verse_hindi: वहाँ शिवजी के दो गण भी थे। वे सब भेद जानते थे और ब्राह्मण का वेष बनाकर सारी लीला देखते-फिरते थे। वे भी बड़े मौजी थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::752.english_translation: There, two of Shiva's attendants were present. They knew all the secrets and wandered about watching the divine play in the guise of Brahmins, full of delight.
ramacharitamanas::752.translation_literal: रहे (remained/were present) / तहाँ (there) / दुइ (two) / रुद्र गन (Shiva's attendants) / ते (those) / जानहिं (know) / सब (all) / भेउ (secrets, distinctions) / बिप्रबेष (Brahmin disguise) / देखत (seeing) / फिरहिं (wander about) / परम (supreme, great) / कौतुकी (delighted, playful) / तेउ (they also)
ramacharitamanas::752.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::752.essence: True sight keeps its joy even behind a disguise.
ramacharitamanas::752.simple_meaning: Two attendants of Shiva were there too. They understood the whole hidden play and moved about in Brahmin disguise, watching everything with delight.
ramacharitamanas::752.simple_insight: Not every observer is fooled by appearances; some see through the costume and still enjoy the scene.
ramacharitamanas::752.detailed_meaning: Narad has just arrived at the swayamvar, swollen with pride about his beauty. The gathering is already full of hidden watchers. Two of Shiva's attendants are there in Brahmin disguise, seeing the whole play clearly while staying amused and unseen.
ramacharitamanas::752.modern_relevance: At a crowded wedding, you notice two quiet elders who seem ordinary but miss nothing. They are not there to impress anyone; they are simply watching the whole drama with calm amusement.
ramacharitamanas::752.insight: It shifts attention from outward roles to the hidden awareness that sees through every costume.

ramacharitamanas::753.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं समाज बैठे मुनि जाई। हृदयँ रूप अहमिति अधिकाई॥ तहँ बैठे महेस गन दोऊ। बिप्रबेष गति लखइ न कोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::753.verse_hindi: नारदजी अपने हृदय में रूप का बड़ा अभिमान लेकर जिस समाज (पंक्ति) में जाकर बैठे थे, ये शिवजी के दोनों गण भी वहीं बैठ गए। ब्राह्मण के वेष में होने के कारण उनकी इस चाल को कोई न जान सका ॥
ramacharitamanas::753.english_translation: Narada sat in the assembly with pride in his heart. Shiva's two attendants sat there too, unseen in the disguise of brahmins.
ramacharitamanas::753.translation_literal: जेहिं (in which) / समाज (assembly) / बैठे (sat) / मुनि (sage) / जाई (going) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / रूप (beauty) / अहमिति (ego-pride) / अधिकाई (greatly) / तहँ (there) / बैठे (sat) / महेस (Shiva) / गन (attendants) / दोऊ (both) / बिप्रबेष (brahmin disguise) / गति (manner/behavior) / लखइ (sees) / न (not) / कोऊ (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::753.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::753.essence: Pride walks in blind; the hidden world watches back.
ramacharitamanas::753.simple_meaning: Narada sits among the assembly, proud of his beauty, while Shiva's two attendants also sit there in disguise, unnoticed by anyone.
ramacharitamanas::753.simple_insight: Pride makes a person easy to misread, while disguise hides the real play happening around them.
ramacharitamanas::753.detailed_meaning: Narada enters the gathering already swollen with pride about his beauty. Unseen, Shiva's two attendants take seats there in brahmin disguise. The scene sets up the hidden mockery that will expose Narada's vanity.
ramacharitamanas::753.modern_relevance: You walk into a room convinced everyone is noticing you. Meanwhile, the real story is already unfolding in the corners you are too busy admiring yourself to see.
ramacharitamanas::753.insight: It shows how self-regard blinds a person to what is actually happening around them.

ramacharitamanas::754.verse_sanskrit: करहिं कूटि नारदहि सुनाई। नीकि दीन्हि हरि सुंदरताई॥ रीझिहि राजकुअँरि छबि देखी। इन्हहि बरिहि हरि जानि बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::754.verse_hindi: वे नारदजी को सुना-सुनाकर, व्यंग्य वचन कहते थे- भगवान ने इनको अच्छी 'सुंदरता' दी है। इनकी शोभा देखकर राजकुमारी रीझ ही जाएगी और 'हरि' (वानर) जानकर इन्हीं को खास तौर से वरेगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::754.english_translation: They mock Narad, saying, "What fine beauty Hari has given him! Seeing his charm, the princess will be delighted and, knowing him to be a monkey, will choose him specially."
ramacharitamanas::754.translation_literal: करहिं (they do) / कूटि (mocking, joking) / नारदहि (to Narad) / सुनाई (saying, making heard) / नीकि (fine, good) / दीन्हि (given) / हरि (Hari) / सुंदरताई (beauty) / रीझिहि (will be pleased) / राजकुअँरि (the princess) / छबि (beauty, charm) / देखी (seeing) / इन्हहि (this one) / बरिहि (will choose) / हरि (Hari) / जानि (knowing) / बिसेषी (especially, specially)
ramacharitamanas::754.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::754.essence: Mock praise feeds pride before pride can defend itself.
ramacharitamanas::754.simple_meaning: Shiva's attendants tease Narad with sharp, mocking praise. Their joke sets up Narad's growing vanity and the coming confusion.
ramacharitamanas::754.simple_insight: Flattery can sound harmless while quietly feeding the ego.
ramacharitamanas::754.detailed_meaning: Narad has arrived among Shiva's attendants, already proud of his beauty. The attendants laugh and mock him, praising his looks in a way that plants vanity deeper. This verse is a teasing setup for the illusion that follows.
ramacharitamanas::754.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with half-joking compliments about your new profile photo. You laugh, but the praise lands deeper than you admit. That tiny swell of pride is the trap.
ramacharitamanas::754.insight: It shows how praise can distort judgment before a person even notices the shift.

ramacharitamanas::755.verse_sanskrit: मुनिहि मोह मन हाथ पराएँ। हँसहिं संभु गन अति सचु पाएँ॥ जदपि सुनहिं मुनि अटपटि बानी। समुझि न परइ बुद्धि भ्रम सानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::755.verse_hindi: नारद मुनि को मोह हो रहा था, क्योंकि उनका मन दूसरे के हाथ (माया के वश) में था। शिवजी के गण बहुत प्रसन्न होकर हँस रहे थे। यद्यपि मुनि उनकी अटपटी बातें सुन रहे थे, पर बुद्धि भ्रम में सनी हुई होने के कारण वे बातें उनकी समझ में नहीं आती थीं (उनकी बातों को वे अपनी प्रशंसा समझ रहे थे) ॥
ramacharitamanas::755.english_translation: Narada was deluded, for his mind was in the grip of illusion. Shiva's attendants laughed with great delight. Though the sage heard their strange words, his mind was clouded, so he could not understand them.
ramacharitamanas::755.translation_literal: मुनिहि (to the sage) / मोह (delusion) / मन (mind) / हाथ (hand) / पराएँ (placed elsewhere, in another's control) / हँसहिं (they laugh) / संभु (Shiva) / गन (attendants) / अति (greatly) / सचु (happily) / पाएँ (having found) / जदपि (although) / सुनहिं (they hear) / मुनि (sage) / अटपटि (strange) / बानी (words) / समुझि (understanding) / न (not) / परइ (is possible) / बुद्धि (intellect) / भ्रम (confusion) / सानी (mixed with, soaked in)
ramacharitamanas::755.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::755.essence: Pride turns even ridicule into self-praise.
ramacharitamanas::755.simple_meaning: Narad is caught in delusion and cannot understand the teasing around him. Shiva's attendants laugh because they know he has misunderstood everything.
ramacharitamanas::755.simple_insight: Pride blinds the mind so completely that even mockery can sound like praise.
ramacharitamanas::755.detailed_meaning: Narad has just entered the gathering, swollen with pride about his beauty. Shiva's attendants keep teasing him, but his mind is already clouded by vanity. This verse shows the delusion settling in before the next turn of the scene.
ramacharitamanas::755.modern_relevance: You reread a message three times, sure it means praise, while everyone else can see the sarcasm. When self-image takes over, even clear signals get distorted.
ramacharitamanas::755.insight: It shows how vanity filters perception, making the mind hear what it wants instead of what is there.

ramacharitamanas::756.verse_sanskrit: काहुँ न लखा सो चरित बिसेषा। सो सरूप नृपकन्याँ देखा॥ मर्कट बदन भयंकर देही। देखत हृदयँ क्रोध भा तेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::756.verse_hindi: इस विशेष चरित को और किसी ने नहीं जाना, केवल राजकन्या ने (नारदजी का) वह रूप देखा। उनका बंदर का सा मुँह और भयंकर शरीर देखते ही कन्या के हृदय में क्रोध उत्पन्न हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::756.english_translation: No one understood this strange event. The princess saw that form. Seeing his monkey face and fearsome body, anger rose in her heart.
ramacharitamanas::756.translation_literal: काहुँ (no one) / न (not) / लखा (understood, saw) / सो (that) / चरित (deed, event) / बिसेषा (strange, special) / सो (that) / सरूप (form, appearance) / नृपकन्याँ (the king's daughter, princess) / देखा (saw) / मर्कट (monkey) / बदन (face) / भयंकर (fearsome) / देही (body) / देखत (seeing) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / क्रोध (anger) / भा (became) / तेही (then, in her)
ramacharitamanas::756.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::756.essence: A strange appearance can turn curiosity into anger in one breath.
ramacharitamanas::756.simple_meaning: No one understood the strange incident except the princess, and when she saw the ugly, fearsome form, anger rose in her heart.
ramacharitamanas::756.simple_insight: First impressions can harden instantly into judgment, before the deeper meaning is even seen.
ramacharitamanas::756.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, Narad's pride has already set the scene in motion. The princess alone sees his strange form clearly, and his monkey face and frightening body trigger anger. This moment pushes the episode toward the next reaction.
ramacharitamanas::756.modern_relevance: You open a profile photo and decide everything in two seconds. The mind has already judged the person before the story is even known.
ramacharitamanas::756.insight: It shows how appearance can trigger instant emotional judgment before understanding arrives.

ramacharitamanas::757.verse_sanskrit: सखीं संग लै कुअँरि तब चलि जनु राजमराल। देखत फिरइ महीप सब कर सरोज जयमाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::757.verse_hindi: तब राजकुमारी सखियों को साथ लेकर इस तरह चली मानो राजहंसिनी चल रही है। वह अपने कमल जैसे हाथों में जयमाला लिए सब राजाओं को देखती हुई घूमने लगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::757.english_translation: Then the princess, taking her companions with her, moved like a royal swan. Holding the garland in her lotus-like hands, she looked around at all the kings.
ramacharitamanas::757.translation_literal: सखीं (companions) / संग (with) / लै (taking) / कुअँरि (princess) / तब (then) / चलि (walking) / जनु (as if) / राजमराल (royal swan) / देखत (seeing) / फिरइ (wanders/turns) / महीप (kings) / सब (all) / कर (hands) / सरोज (lotus) / जयमाल (victory garland)
ramacharitamanas::757.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::757.essence: Grace moves through the crowd before it chooses.
ramacharitamanas::757.simple_meaning: The princess walks into the assembly with her companions, graceful and composed, carrying the garland as she looks at the gathered kings.
ramacharitamanas::757.simple_insight: Grace can be calm and searching at the same time.
ramacharitamanas::757.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Sita enters the swayamvar with her companions and the garland in hand. She moves with royal grace, scanning the assembled kings before choosing among them. This verse sets up the decisive moment that follows.
ramacharitamanas::757.modern_relevance: You enter a room full of people judging, waiting, and hoping. You keep your composure, look steadily, and choose with your own eyes.
ramacharitamanas::757.insight: It shifts attention to deliberate choice under public pressure.

ramacharitamanas::758.verse_sanskrit: जेहि दिसि बैठे नारद फूली। सो दिसि तेहिं न बिलोकी भूली॥ पुनि-पुनि मुनि उकसहिं अकुलाहीं। देखि दसा हर गन मुसुकाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::758.verse_hindi: जिस ओर नारदजी (रूप के गर्व में) फूले बैठे थे, उस ओर उसने भूलकर भी नहीं ताका। नारद मुनि बार-बार उचकते और छटपटाते हैं। उनकी दशा देखकर शिवजी के गण मुसकराते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::758.english_translation: Narad sat puffed up in one direction, and she did not look that way even by mistake. Again and again the sage leapt and fidgeted, and Shiva's attendants smiled at his condition.
ramacharitamanas::758.translation_literal: जेहि दिसि (in whichever direction) / बैठे (was seated) / नारद (Narad) / फूली (puffed up, inflated) / सो दिसि (that direction) / तेहिं (she) / न (not) / बिलोकी (looked) / भूली (by mistake) / पुनि-पुनि (again and again) / मुनि (sage) / उकसहिं (leapt up) / अकुलाहीं (fidgeted, grew restless) / देखि (seeing) / दसा (condition) / हर गन (Shiva's attendants) / मुसुकाहीं (smiled)
ramacharitamanas::758.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::758.essence: Pride suffers most when nobody looks back.
ramacharitamanas::758.simple_meaning: The princess refuses to look at the proud sage, and his embarrassment grows. Even Shiva's attendants smile at the scene.
ramacharitamanas::758.simple_insight: Pride can make you restless when attention never comes back to you.
ramacharitamanas::758.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Narad has arrived swollen with pride, expecting admiration. The princess turns away from him completely. He keeps jumping and squirming, and even Shiva's attendants laugh. The scene sets up the humiliation behind his later curse.
ramacharitamanas::758.modern_relevance: You send the message, then watch the screen. No reply. No view. No sign that your performance landed. The silence itself becomes the mirror.
ramacharitamanas::758.insight: It exposes how vanity depends on being noticed, and how quickly dignity collapses when attention is withheld.

ramacharitamanas::759.verse_sanskrit: धरि नृपतनु तहँ गयउ कृपाला। कुअँरि हरषि मेलेउ जयमाला॥ दुलहिनि लै गे लच्छिनिवासा। नृपसमाज सब भयउ निरासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::759.verse_hindi: कृपालु भगवान भी राजा का शरीर धारण कर वहाँ जा पहुँचे। राजकुमारी ने हर्षित होकर उनके गले में जयमाला डाल दी। लक्ष्मीनिवास भगवान दुलहिन को ले गए। सारी राजमंडली निराश हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::759.english_translation: The compassionate Lord took a king's form and went there. The princess joyfully placed the victory garland around his neck. The Lord who dwells with Lakshmi took the bride away. The whole gathering of kings was left in despair.
ramacharitamanas::759.translation_literal: धरि (having assumed) / नृपतनु (a king's body) / तहँ (there) / गयउ (went) / कृपाला (the compassionate one) / कुअँरि (the princess) / हरषि (in joy) / मेलेउ (placed) / जयमाला (victory garland) / दुलहिनि (the bride) / लै (taking) / गे (went) / लच्छिनिवासा (the dwelling of Lakshmi) / नृपसमाज (the assembly of kings) / सब (all) / भयउ (became) / निरासा (despondent)
ramacharitamanas::759.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::759.essence: Grace chooses the one pride could not win.
ramacharitamanas::759.simple_meaning: Ram appears in human form at the swayamvar, Sita chooses him, and every other king loses hope.
ramacharitamanas::759.simple_insight: What looks like a contest is already decided by grace.
ramacharitamanas::759.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the swayamvar reaches its turning point. Ram enters in human form, Sita joyfully places the garland on him, and the proud kings are left defeated. The scene shifts from public challenge to divine choice.
ramacharitamanas::759.modern_relevance: You can spend months competing for something, only to realize the deepest choice was never about status at all. One quiet decision can end all the noise.
ramacharitamanas::759.insight: It shifts attention from rivalry and display to grace and rightful recognition.

ramacharitamanas::760.verse_sanskrit: मुनि अति बिकल मोहँ मति नाठी। मनि गिरि गई छूटि जनु गाँठी॥ तब हर गन बोले मुसुकाई। निज मुख मुकुर बिलोकहु जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::760.verse_hindi: मोह के कारण मुनि की बुद्धि नष्ट हो गई थी, इससे वे (राजकुमारी को गई देख) बहुत ही विकल हो गए। मानो गाँठ से छूटकर मणि गिर गई हो। तब शिवजी के गणों ने मुसकराकर कहा- जाकर दर्पण में अपना मुँह तो देखिए! ॥
ramacharitamanas::760.english_translation: The sage's mind was overwhelmed by delusion and became unsteady, like a jewel slipping loose from a knot. Then Shiva's attendants smiled and said, "Go look at your own face in a mirror."
ramacharitamanas::760.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / अति (very) / बिकल (disturbed) / मोहँ (by delusion) / मति (mind) / नाठी (destroyed) / मनि (jewel) / गिरि (fell) / गई (went) / छूटि (slipping free) / जनु (as if) / गाँठी (from a knot) / तब (then) / हर (Shiva) / गन (attendants) / बोले (spoke) / मुसुकाई (smiling) / निज (own) / मुख (face) / मुकुर (mirror) / बिलोकहु (look) / जाई (go)
ramacharitamanas::760.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::760.essence: Delusion breaks self-command; seeing yourself can break the spell.
ramacharitamanas::760.simple_meaning: Nārada loses self-control because of pride and desire. Shiva's attendants point him back to himself by telling him to look at his own face.
ramacharitamanas::760.simple_insight: Pride makes you lose sight of yourself. A little self-check can reveal what delusion hides.
ramacharitamanas::760.detailed_meaning: Nārada has just been dazzled by the swayamvar scene and by his own vanity. His mind slips out of balance, and Shiva's attendants gently mock him into awareness, setting up the moment when he will finally see his own face and react.
ramacharitamanas::760.modern_relevance: You reread your own message five times after sending it, suddenly certain everyone noticed your mistake. One honest look at your reaction can expose the story your ego is telling.
ramacharitamanas::760.insight: It shifts attention from outer excitement to self-observation, showing how delusion can be exposed by direct seeing.

ramacharitamanas::761.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि दोउ भागे भयँ भारी। बदन दीख मुनि बारि निहारी॥ बेषु बिलोकि क्रोध अति बाढ़ा। तिन्हहि सराप दीन्ह अति गाढ़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::761.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर वे दोनों बहुत भयभीत होकर भागे। मुनि ने जल में झाँककर अपना मुँह देखा। अपना रूप देखकर उनका क्रोध बहुत बढ़ गया। उन्होंने शिवजी के उन गणों को अत्यन्त कठोर शाप दिया- ॥
ramacharitamanas::761.english_translation: Saying this, both fled in great fear. The sage looked into the water and saw his own face. Seeing his appearance, his anger rose sharply, and he gave those attendants a severe curse.
ramacharitamanas::761.translation_literal: अस कहि (saying this) / दोउ (both) / भागे (fled) / भयँ भारी (with great fear) / बदन (face) / दीख (saw) / मुनि (the sage) / बारि (in water) / निहारी (looking) / बेषु (appearance) / बिलोकि (seeing) / क्रोध (anger) / अति (very) / बाढ़ा (increased) / तिन्हहि (to them) / सराप (curse) / दीन्ह (gave) / अति गाढ़ा (very severe)
ramacharitamanas::761.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::761.essence: Wounded pride turns a small slight into a harsh curse.
ramacharitamanas::761.simple_meaning: The two attendants ran away in fear. The sage saw his own reflection, became furious, and cursed them harshly.
ramacharitamanas::761.simple_insight: Humiliation can turn quickly into anger when the mind is caught off guard.
ramacharitamanas::761.detailed_meaning: At the Sita-swayamvar, Shiva's attendants have mocked the sage's appearance and fled. The sage looks into water, sees his own face, and his wounded pride erupts into a fierce curse. This moment triggers the next turn in the story.
ramacharitamanas::761.modern_relevance: You catch your reflection after a careless comment and feel the sting rise all over again. One embarrassed moment can become a long chain of anger.
ramacharitamanas::761.insight: It shows how wounded self-image can harden into retaliation almost instantly.

ramacharitamanas::762.verse_sanskrit: होहु निसाचर जाइ तुम्ह कपटी पापी दोउ। हँसेहु हमहि सो लेहु फल बहुरि हँसेहु मुनि कोउ॥।135॥
ramacharitamanas::762.verse_hindi: तुम दोनों कपटी और पापी जाकर राक्षस हो जाओ। तुमने हमारी हँसी की, उसका फल चखो। अब फिर किसी मुनि की हँसी करना।135॥
ramacharitamanas::762.english_translation: You two are deceitful and sinful. Go and be born as demons. You mocked me; now take the fruit. Mock another sage again, if you dare.
ramacharitamanas::762.translation_literal: होहु (be) / निसाचर (demon) / जाइ (go) / तुम्ह (you both) / कपटी (deceitful) / पापी (sinful) / दोउ (both) / हँसेहु (you mocked) / हमहि (me) / सो (that) / लेहु (take) / फल (fruit) / बहुरि (again) / हँसेहु (mock) / मुनि (sage) / कोउ (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::762.speaker: Muni
ramacharitamanas::762.essence: Mocking a sage ripens into your own downfall.
ramacharitamanas::762.simple_meaning: The sage curses the two mockers, telling them to become demons and suffer the result of their insult.
ramacharitamanas::762.simple_insight: Cruel laughter returns to the one who throws it.
ramacharitamanas::762.detailed_meaning: The two youths have mocked the sage's appearance, and his anger bursts out in a curse. He sends them away to a lower form of existence as the direct fruit of their ridicule.
ramacharitamanas::762.modern_relevance: You laugh at someone’s humiliation in a group chat, and the joke lands harder than you expected. Mockery does not vanish; it changes hands and comes back as damage.
ramacharitamanas::762.insight: It turns ridicule into consequence, warning that contempt shapes the future of the one who speaks it.

ramacharitamanas::763.verse_sanskrit: पुनि जल दीख रूप निज पावा। तदपि हृदयँ संतोष न आवा॥ फरकत अधर कोप मन माहीं। सपदि चले कमलापति पाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::763.verse_hindi: मुनि ने फिर जल में देखा, तो उन्हें अपना (असली) रूप प्राप्त हो गया, तब भी उन्हें संतोष नहीं हुआ। उनके होठ फड़क रहे थे और मन में क्रोध (भरा) था। तुरंत ही वे भगवान कमलापति के पास चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::763.english_translation: Seeing his own form again in the water, the sage still found no peace in his heart. His lips trembled with anger, and he immediately went to Kamalapati.
ramacharitamanas::763.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / जल (water) / दीख (saw) / रूप (form) / निज (own) / पावा (obtained) / तदपि (even then) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / संतोष (contentment) / न (not) / आवा (came) / फरकत (trembling) / अधर (lips) / कोप (anger) / मन (mind) / माहीं (within) / सपदि (immediately) / चले (went) / कमलापति (Lord of the lotus) / पाहीं (to the presence of)
ramacharitamanas::763.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::763.essence: A restored appearance can still leave anger untouched.
ramacharitamanas::763.simple_meaning: The sage sees his own form restored, but anger still burns. Instead of calming down, he goes straight to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::763.simple_insight: Restoring the outer form does not always restore the heart.
ramacharitamanas::763.detailed_meaning: The cursed sage looks into the water and sees his original form return, but the insult still stings. He cannot settle his mind. Burning with anger, he heads at once to Ram, setting up the next outburst.
ramacharitamanas::763.modern_relevance: You finally get the apology you wanted, but your chest is still tight. The issue was never just the words — the wound has already gone deeper.
ramacharitamanas::763.insight: It shows that outer correction does not automatically heal wounded pride.

ramacharitamanas::764.verse_sanskrit: देहउँ श्राप कि मरिहउँ जाई। जगत मोरि उपहास कराई॥ बीचहिं पंथ मिले दनुजारी। संग रमा सोइ राजकुमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::764.verse_hindi: (मन में सोचते जाते थे-) जाकर या तो शाप दूँगा या प्राण दे दूँगा। उन्होंने जगत में मेरी हँसी कराई। दैत्यों के शत्रु भगवान हरि उन्हें बीच रास्ते में ही मिल गए। साथ में लक्ष्मीजी और वही राजकुमारी थीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::764.english_translation: I will curse them, or I will die. They made me a laughingstock in the world. The enemy of demons met them on the road, along with Lakshmi and that princess.
ramacharitamanas::764.translation_literal: देहउँ (I will give) / श्राप (curse) / कि (or) / मरिहउँ (I will die) / जाई (going) / जगत (world) / मोरि (my) / उपहास (mockery) / कराई (made) / बीचहिं (in the middle) / पंथ (road/path) / मिले (met) / दनुजारी (enemy of demons) / संग (with) / रमा (Lakshmi) / सोइ (that same) / राजकुमारी (princess)
ramacharitamanas::764.speaker: Narada
ramacharitamanas::764.essence: Wounded pride looks for revenge until grace interrupts it.
ramacharitamanas::764.simple_meaning: Narada burns with shame and anger after being mocked. He thinks of cursing the offenders or dying, and then sees Ram with Sita on the road.
ramacharitamanas::764.simple_insight: Pride turns humiliation into rage. The mind that wants honor can be shattered in a moment.
ramacharitamanas::764.detailed_meaning: Narada has just been humiliated after mistaking his own worth. Still seething, he vows either to curse or die. Then, on the road, he sees Ram with Sita, and the encounter becomes the turning point of his wounded pride.
ramacharitamanas::764.modern_relevance: You leave a room after being laughed at in front of everyone. Your chest is hot, your mind is already drafting revenge, and then one unexpected sight interrupts the spiral.
ramacharitamanas::764.insight: It shows how injured ego immediately seeks retaliation, even before understanding what is happening.

ramacharitamanas::765.verse_sanskrit: बोले मधुर बचन सुरसाईं। मुनि कहँ चले बिकल की नाईं॥ सुनत बचन उपजा अति क्रोधा। माया बस न रहा मन बोधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::765.verse_hindi: देवताओं के स्वामी भगवान ने मीठी वाणी में कहा- हे मुनि! व्याकुल की तरह कहाँ चले? ये शब्द सुनते ही नारद को बड़ा क्रोध आया, माया के वशीभूत होने के कारण मन में चेत नहीं रहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::765.english_translation: The Lord of the gods spoke gently: “O sage, why are you leaving in such distress?” Hearing those words, Narada became very angry; under the veil of appearance, his mind lost its clarity.
ramacharitamanas::765.translation_literal: बोले (spoke) / मधुर (sweet, gentle) / बचन (words) / सुरसाईं (Lord of the gods) / मुनि (sage) / कहँ (to) / चले (are going) / बिकल (distressed) / की नाईं (like)॥ / सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words) / उपजा (arose) / अति (very) / क्रोधा (anger) / माया (veil of appearance) / बस (under the control of) / न (not) / रहा (remained) / मन (mind) / बोधा (clear awareness)॥
ramacharitamanas::765.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::765.essence: Pride hears insult where gentleness was offered.
ramacharitamanas::765.simple_meaning: The divine speaks gently, but Narada takes offense and loses his composure. The veil of appearance clouds his judgment.
ramacharitamanas::765.simple_insight: Even gentle words can trigger pride when the mind is already unsettled.
ramacharitamanas::765.detailed_meaning: Narada has just seen the Lord and still feels unsatisfied. In this moment, the Lord speaks softly, but Narada hears insult instead of grace. His anger rises at once, showing how quickly the mind can be ruled by illusion.
ramacharitamanas::765.modern_relevance: Someone texts you a calm correction, and you instantly read disrespect into it. The words were mild; the wound was already waiting. That is how the mind gets trapped.
ramacharitamanas::765.insight: It shows how pride distorts perception, turning a kind response into a personal slight.

ramacharitamanas::766.verse_sanskrit: पर संपदा सकहु नहिं देखी। तुम्हरें इरिषा कपट बिसेषी॥ मथत सिंधु रुद्रहि बौरायहु। सुरन्ह प्रेरि बिष पान करायहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::766.verse_hindi: (मुनि ने कहा-) तुम दूसरों की सम्पदा नहीं देख सकते, तुम्हारे ईर्ष्या और कपट बहुत है। समुद्र मथते समय तुमने शिवजी को बावला बना दिया और देवताओं को प्रेरित करके उन्हें विषपान कराया ॥
ramacharitamanas::766.english_translation: You cannot bear to see another’s wealth. Your envy and deceit are extreme. You churned the ocean and bewildered Shiva, and you urged the radiant beings to make him drink poison.
ramacharitamanas::766.translation_literal: पर (other) / संपदा (wealth, prosperity) / सकहु (you can) / नहिं (not) / देखी (seeing) / तुम्हरें (your) / इरिषा (envy) / कपट (deceit) / बिसेषी (very great) / मथत (churning) / सिंधु (ocean) / रुद्रहि (Shiva) / बौरायहु (you bewildered) / सुरन्ह (the radiant beings) / प्रेरि (urging) / बिष (poison) / पान (drinking) / करायहु (you caused)
ramacharitamanas::766.speaker: Narad
ramacharitamanas::766.essence: Accusation reveals the accuser’s own agitation more than the one being blamed.
ramacharitamanas::766.simple_meaning: Narad rebukes Ram for jealousy and deceit, accusing him of causing Shiva to drink poison during the churning of the ocean.
ramacharitamanas::766.simple_insight: Sharp criticism can expose hidden pride and make self-deception impossible to ignore.
ramacharitamanas::766.detailed_meaning: Narad, still angry after meeting Ram, pours out a rebuke in the middle of the story. He accuses Ram of jealousy, trickery, and of using the churning of the ocean to make Shiva drink poison. The verse continues his accusation, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::766.modern_relevance: A friend calls out your hidden resentment after you downplay someone else’s success. The sting is real, but so is the mirror it holds up.
ramacharitamanas::766.insight: It shows how anger can become accusation, turning one person’s hurt into a sweeping moral attack.

ramacharitamanas::767.verse_sanskrit: असुर सुरा बिष संकरहि आपु रमा मनि चारु। स्वारथ साधक कुटिल तुम्ह सदा कपट ब्यवहारु ॥
ramacharitamanas::767.verse_hindi: असुरों को मदिरा और शिवजी को विष देकर तुमने स्वयं लक्ष्मी और सुंदर (कौस्तुभ) मणि ले ली। तुम बड़े धोखेबाज और मतलबी हो। सदा कपट का व्यवहार करते हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::767.english_translation: You gave poison to the demons and to Shiva, and took Lakshmi and the beautiful gem for yourself. You are cunning, selfish, and always act with deceit.
ramacharitamanas::767.translation_literal: असुर (demons) / सुरा (liquor) / बिष (poison) / संकरहि (to Shiva) / आपु (yourself) / रमा (Lakshmi) / मनि (gem) / चारु (beautiful) / स्वारथ (self-interest) / साधक (one who pursues) / कुटिल (crooked) / तुम्ह (you) / सदा (always) / कपट (deceit) / ब्यवहारु (conduct)
ramacharitamanas::767.speaker: Narad
ramacharitamanas::767.essence: Pride sees unfairness everywhere and calls it truth.
ramacharitamanas::767.simple_meaning: Narad accuses the divine of acting unfairly and selfishly, giving poison to some and taking the best for himself.
ramacharitamanas::767.simple_insight: It feels like righteous anger when favoritism is exposed.
ramacharitamanas::767.detailed_meaning: Narad, stung by what he sees as humiliation, confronts the divine with sharp words in the Balkand frame. He lists examples of apparent unfairness and calls the divine crooked and self-serving, setting up the next line about complete freedom.
ramacharitamanas::767.modern_relevance: A colleague gets praised for work you did, and the pattern feels obvious. The hurt is not just about the loss — it's about seeing the same unfairness repeated again and again.
ramacharitamanas::767.insight: It reveals how wounded pride turns every event into proof of bias.

ramacharitamanas::768.verse_sanskrit: परम स्वतंत्र न सिर पर कोई। भावइ मनहि करहु तुम्ह सोई॥ भलेहि मंद मंदेहि भल करहू। बिसमय हरष न हियँ कछु धरहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::768.verse_hindi: तुम परम स्वतंत्र हो, सिर पर तो कोई है नहीं, इससे जब जो मन को भाता है, (स्वच्छन्दता से) वही करते हो। भले को बुरा और बुरे को भला कर देते हो। हृदय में हर्ष-विषाद कुछ भी नहीं लाते ॥
ramacharitamanas::768.english_translation: You are utterly independent; no one stands above your head. You do whatever pleases your mind. You turn good into bad and bad into good, and your heart holds neither joy nor sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::768.translation_literal: परम स्वतंत्र (utterly independent) / न (not) / सिर (head) / पर (above) / कोई (anyone) / भावइ (pleases) / मनहि (the mind) / करहु (you do) / तुम्ह (you) / सोई (that same) / भलेहि (good) / मंद (bad) / मंदेहि (bad one) / भल (good) / करहू (you do) / बिसमय (wonder) / हरष (joy) / न (not) / हियँ (in the heart) / कछु (anything) / धरहू (you hold)
ramacharitamanas::768.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::768.essence: Freedom without restraint becomes moral blindness.
ramacharitamanas::768.simple_meaning: You act without restraint, answer to no one, and feel no remorse or delight. The verse condemns a mind so unchecked that it inverts moral judgment.
ramacharitamanas::768.simple_insight: Unchecked power dulls conscience. The mind that answers to nothing can no longer tell right from wrong.
ramacharitamanas::768.detailed_meaning: A sage is rebuking a being who has grown arrogant through power and deception. The accusation is not just cruelty, but inner lawlessness: no higher standard, no moral shame, no emotional balance. This verse exposes the collapse of discernment before the next charge lands.
ramacharitamanas::768.modern_relevance: A manager rewrites the story after every mistake, always making themselves the hero. After a while, even their own conscience stops protesting. That numbness is what this verse warns against.
ramacharitamanas::768.insight: It shifts attention from external freedom to moral accountability: power without restraint becomes blindness.

ramacharitamanas::769.verse_sanskrit: डहकि डहकि परिचेहु सब काहू। अति असंक मन सदा उछाहू॥ करम सुभासुभ तुम्हहि न बाधा। अब लगि तुम्हहि न काहूँ साधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::769.verse_hindi: सबको ठग-ठगकर परक गए हो और अत्यन्त निडर हो गए हो, इसी से (ठगने के काम में) मन में सदा उत्साह रहता है। शुभ-अशुभ कर्म तुम्हें बाधा नहीं देते। अब तक तुम को किसी ने ठीक नहीं किया था ॥
ramacharitamanas::769.english_translation: You have deceived everyone and grown fearless. Your mind is always eager for trickery. Good and bad actions do not restrain you. Until now, no one has set you right.
ramacharitamanas::769.translation_literal: डहकि डहकि (deceiving again and again) / परिचेहु (you have deceived) / सब काहू (everyone) / अति असंक (extremely fearless) / मन (mind) / सदा (always) / उछाहू (eager enthusiasm) / करम (action) / सुभासुभ (good and bad) / तुम्हहि (to you) / न बाधा (do not hinder) / अब लगि (until now) / तुम्हहि (you) / न काहूँ (by anyone) / साधा (set right)
ramacharitamanas::769.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::769.essence: Repeated deceit makes fearlessness look like strength until reality corrects it.
ramacharitamanas::769.simple_meaning: Ravana is being called out for repeated deceit and reckless fearlessness. He has ignored moral limits so long that no one has corrected him.
ramacharitamanas::769.simple_insight: Unchecked habit makes wrongdoing feel normal until correction finally arrives.
ramacharitamanas::769.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is being rebuked after his own arrogance has gone too far. The speaker points to a mind trained in deceit, untouched by moral consequence, and warns that no one has yet restrained him.
ramacharitamanas::769.modern_relevance: A person keeps bending the truth in meetings, then starts believing the lie is just strategy. Eventually the pattern hardens into character, and someone finally has to name it.
ramacharitamanas::769.insight: It exposes how repeated deception dulls conscience and invites correction before damage deepens.

ramacharitamanas::770.verse_sanskrit: भले भवन अब बायन दीन्हा। पावहुगे फल आपन कीन्हा॥ बंचेहु मोहि जवनि धरि देहा। सोइ तनु धरहु श्राप मम एहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::770.verse_hindi: अबकी तुमने अच्छे घर बैना दिया है (मेरे जैसे जबर्दस्त आदमी से छेड़खानी की है।) अतः अपने किए का फल अवश्य पाओगे। जिस शरीर को धारण करके तुमने मुझे ठगा है, तुम भी वही शरीर धारण करो, यह मेरा शाप है ॥
ramacharitamanas::770.english_translation: You have made a good bargain now. You will surely reap the fruit of your deed. The body with which you deceived me, take that same body now—this is my curse.
ramacharitamanas::770.translation_literal: भले (good) / भवन (bargain) / अब (now) / बायन (bargain) / दीन्हा (gave) / पावहुगे (you will receive) / फल (fruit) / आपन (your own) / कीन्हा (done) / बंचेहु (you deceived) / मोहि (me) / जवनि (with which) / धरि (having taken) / देहा (body) / सोइ (that same) / तनु (body) / धरहु (take) / श्राप (curse) / मम (my) / एहा (this)
ramacharitamanas::770.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::770.essence: Deceit returns in the same form it used to harm.
ramacharitamanas::770.simple_meaning: Ravana curses the deceiver, saying the person will suffer the result of their own actions and keep the same body they used for the trick.
ramacharitamanas::770.simple_insight: Deception does not disappear. It comes back as a consequence shaped by your own act.
ramacharitamanas::770.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana realizes he has been tricked by the disguised figure before him. Furious and wounded in pride, he turns the insult into a curse: the same body used for deception will become the body that suffers the result.
ramacharitamanas::770.modern_relevance: You find out the person who promised honesty edited the numbers behind your back. The anger is real, but so is the pattern: every hidden act leaves a mark that returns.
ramacharitamanas::770.insight: It shifts attention from the immediate insult to the moral consequence built into the act itself.

ramacharitamanas::771.verse_sanskrit: कपि आकृति तुम्ह कीन्हि हमारी। करिहहिं कीस सहाय तुम्हारी॥ मम अपकार कीन्ह तुम्ह भारी। नारि बिरहँ तुम्ह होब दुखारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::771.verse_hindi: तुमने हमारा रूप बंदर का सा बना दिया था, इससे बंदर ही तुम्हारी सहायता करेंगे। (मैं जिस स्त्री को चाहता था, उससे मेरा वियोग कराकर) तुमने मेरा बड़ा अहित किया है, इससे तुम भी स्त्री के वियोग में दुःखी होंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::771.english_translation: You gave me a monkey's form; monkeys will help you. You harmed me greatly; you too will suffer separation from a woman.
ramacharitamanas::771.translation_literal: कपि (monkey) / आकृति (form) / तुम्ह (you) / कीन्हि (made) / हमारी (my) / करिहहिं (will do) / कीस (monkeys) / सहाय (help) / तुम्हारी (your) / मम (my) / अपकार (harm) / कीन्ह (did) / तुम्ह (you) / भारी (greatly) / नारि (woman) / बिरहँ (in separation) / तुम्ह (you) / होब (will become) / दुखारी (sorrowful)
ramacharitamanas::771.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::771.essence: Humiliated pride answers injury with a curse.
ramacharitamanas::771.simple_meaning: Ravana curses Narada: because Narada made him look like a monkey, monkeys will aid his enemy. Because Narada caused his grief, Narada will also know the pain of separation.
ramacharitamanas::771.simple_insight: Pride turns hurt into revenge, and revenge always mirrors the wound.
ramacharitamanas::771.detailed_meaning: Narada has just been cursed after provoking Ravana's pride. Ravana, stung by humiliation and loss, answers with a bitter curse: the very beings he mocked will become the helpers of his downfall, and the pain of separation will return to the one who caused it.
ramacharitamanas::771.modern_relevance: Someone humiliates you in a group chat, and your first impulse is to strike back with a sharper message. Ravana shows how quickly wounded ego turns pain into a curse.
ramacharitamanas::771.insight: It exposes how insult hardens into retaliation, and how retaliation often recreates the original harm.

ramacharitamanas::772.verse_sanskrit: श्राप सीस धरि हरषि हियँ प्रभु बहु बिनती कीन्हि॥ निज माया कै प्रबलता करषि कृपानिधि लीन्हि ॥
ramacharitamanas::772.verse_hindi: शाप को सिर पर चढ़ाकर, हृदय में हर्षित होते हुए प्रभु ने नारदजी से बहुत विनती की और कृपानिधान भगवान ने अपनी माया की प्रबलता खींच ली ॥
ramacharitamanas::772.english_translation: Placing the curse on his head, the Lord gladly made many humble requests. The compassionate Lord then drew back the force of his own illusion.
ramacharitamanas::772.translation_literal: श्राप (curse) / सीस धरि (placing on the head) / हरषि (with joy) / हियँ (in the heart) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बहु (many) / बिनती (requests) / कीन्हि (made) / निज (own) / माया (illusion) / कै (of) / प्रबलता (power/force) / करषि (drawing back) / कृपानिधि (treasure of compassion) / लीन्हि (took away)
ramacharitamanas::772.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::772.essence: Real greatness can accept blame and remain joyful.
ramacharitamanas::772.simple_meaning: The Lord accepts the curse without bitterness, speaks politely, and then withdraws the power of his illusion.
ramacharitamanas::772.simple_insight: Even power bows here; humility can hold what force cannot.
ramacharitamanas::772.detailed_meaning: Narad has just spoken a curse after being unsettled by the Lord's playful illusion. Instead of anger, Ram accepts it with joy, speaks with respect, and lets the illusion's force recede. The scene shows divine humility before the curse takes effect.
ramacharitamanas::772.modern_relevance: Someone criticizes you harshly in front of others, and your first impulse is to defend yourself. Instead, you listen, stay steady, and answer without ego.
ramacharitamanas::772.insight: It teaches you to absorb offense without retaliation and respond from steadiness, not wounded pride.

ramacharitamanas::773.verse_sanskrit: जब हरि माया दूरि निवारी। नहिं तहँ रमा न राजकुमारी॥ तब मुनि अति सभीत हरि चरना। गहे पाहि प्रनतारति हरना ॥
ramacharitamanas::773.verse_hindi: जब भगवान ने अपनी माया को हटा लिया, तब वहाँ न लक्ष्मी ही रह गईं, न राजकुमारी ही। तब मुनि ने अत्यन्त भयभीत होकर श्री हरि के चरण पकड़ लिए और कहा- हे शरणागत के दुःखों को हरने वाले! मेरी रक्षा कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::773.english_translation: When Hari removed the veil of illusion, neither Lakshmi nor the princess remained there. Then the sage, greatly frightened, held Hari's feet and cried, "Protect me, remover of the suffering of those who seek refuge."
ramacharitamanas::773.translation_literal: जब (when) / हरि (Hari) / माया (the veil of appearance) / दूरि (away) / निवारी (removed) / नहिं (not) / तहँ (there) / रमा (Lakshmi) / न (not) / राजकुमारी (princess) / तब (then) / मुनि (sage) / अति (very) / सभीत (frightened) / हरि (Hari) / चरना (feet) / गहे (held) / पाहि (protect) / प्रनतारति (the suffering of those who seek refuge) / हरना (remover)
ramacharitamanas::773.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::773.simple_meaning: When the illusion lifts, the sage sees only Hari and falls at his feet for protection.
ramacharitamanas::773.simple_insight: Fear softens when false appearances drop away and refuge becomes clear.
ramacharitamanas::773.detailed_meaning: Narad has just been humbled after his pride brought on a curse. When Hari removes the veil of illusion, the scene of beauty vanishes, and the sage is left shaken. In that naked moment, he surrenders and begs for protection.
ramacharitamanas::773.modern_relevance: You finally get the message after a humiliation, a breakup, or a mistake strips away your story about yourself. What remains is the need to ask for help honestly.
ramacharitamanas::773.insight: It shifts attention from appearance and pride to refuge and surrender.

ramacharitamanas::774.verse_sanskrit: मृषा होउ मम श्राप कृपाला। मम इच्छा कह दीनदयाला॥ मैं दुर्बचन कहे बहुतेरे। कह मुनि पाप मिटिहिं किमि मेरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::774.verse_hindi: हे कृपालु! मेरा शाप मिथ्या हो जाए। तब दीनों पर दया करने वाले भगवान ने कहा कि यह सब मेरी ही इच्छा (से हुआ) है। मुनि ने कहा- मैंने आप को अनेक खोटे वचन कहे हैं। मेरे पाप कैसे मिटेंगे? ॥
ramacharitamanas::774.english_translation: O compassionate one, may my curse become false. O giver of mercy, this was your own will. I have spoken many harsh words, O sage. How can my wrongdoing be erased?
ramacharitamanas::774.translation_literal: मृषा (false) / होउ (may become) / मम (my) / श्राप (curse) / कृपाला (O compassionate one) / मम (my) / इच्छा (will) / कह (said) / दीनदयाला (O giver of mercy to the humble) / मैं (I) / दुर्बचन (harsh words) / कहे (spoken) / बहुतेरे (many) / कह (said) / मुनि (sage) / पाप (wrongdoing) / मिटिहिं (will be erased) / किमि (how) / मेरे (my)
ramacharitamanas::774.speaker: Narada
ramacharitamanas::774.essence: Humility begins when the speaker asks mercy for his own wrong words.
ramacharitamanas::774.simple_meaning: Narada admits his harsh words and asks Ram to make the curse ineffective. He also wonders how his own wrongdoing can ever be cleared.
ramacharitamanas::774.simple_insight: Even a proud mistake becomes prayer when it is owned honestly.
ramacharitamanas::774.detailed_meaning: Narada, shaken after seeing Ram withdraw the illusion, falls into humility. He asks Ram to let his curse fail and confesses that he spoke many harsh words. The moment turns from pride to repentance, preparing the way for Ram's instruction about Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::774.modern_relevance: You snap in anger, then replay the words later in silence. The embarrassment is real, but so is the opening to own it cleanly instead of defending yourself.
ramacharitamanas::774.insight: It shifts the mind from self-justification to humble admission, making repentance the doorway to relief.

ramacharitamanas::775.verse_sanskrit: जपहु जाइ संकर सत नामा। होइहि हृदयँ तुरत बिश्रामा॥ कोउ नहिं सिव समान प्रिय मोरें। असि परतीति तजहु जनि भोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::775.verse_hindi: (भगवान ने कहा-) जाकर शंकरजी के शतनाम का जप करो, इससे हृदय में तुरंत शांति होगी। शिवजी के समान मुझे कोई प्रिय नहीं है, इस विश्वास को भूलकर भी न छोड़ना ॥
ramacharitamanas::775.english_translation: Go and recite the hundred names of Shankar. Your heart will find peace at once. No one is dear to me like Shiva. Never let this conviction fade, even in a dream.
ramacharitamanas::775.translation_literal: जपहु (recite) / जाइ (go) / संकर (Shankar) / सत नामा (hundred names) / होइहि (will become) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / तुरत (immediately) / बिश्रामा (rest, peace) / कोउ (anyone) / नहिं (not) / सिव (Shiva) / समान (like) / प्रिय (dear) / मोरें (to me) / असि (such) / परतीति (conviction) / तजहु (abandon) / जनि (never) / भोरें (even in a dream)
ramacharitamanas::775.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::775.essence: Shiva's remembrance calms the heart because Ram treasures Shiva above all.
ramacharitamanas::775.simple_meaning: Ram tells the sage to recite Shiva's hundred names, because that will bring immediate calm. He also says that no one is dear to him like Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::775.simple_insight: Devotion settles the heart fastest when it recognizes the sacred bond between Ram and Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::775.detailed_meaning: After the sage's fear and confusion, Ram gives him a remedy, not a lecture: recite Shiva's hundred names and the heart will settle. He then reveals the deeper truth behind the cure — Shiva is Ram's dearest devotee and closest beloved.
ramacharitamanas::775.modern_relevance: You are spiraling after a harsh conversation, and one trusted practice brings you back to center. The mind calms faster when it leans toward what it reveres most.
ramacharitamanas::775.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract belief to a concrete practice that restores steadiness through remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::776.verse_sanskrit: जेहि पर कृपा न करहिं पुरारी। सो न पाव मुनि भगति हमारी॥ अस उर धरि महि बिचरहु जाई। अब न तुम्हहि माया निअराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::776.verse_hindi: हे मुनि ! पुरारि (शिवजी) जिस पर कृपा नहीं करते, वह मेरी भक्ति नहीं पाता। हृदय में ऐसा निश्चय करके जाकर पृथ्वी पर विचरो। अब मेरी माया तुम्हारे निकट नहीं आएगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::776.english_translation: O sage, one on whom Purari does not show grace does not attain my devotion. Hold this certainty in your heart and roam the earth. Now my veil of appearance will not come near you.
ramacharitamanas::776.translation_literal: जेहि (on whom) / पर (upon) / कृपा (grace) / न (not) / करहिं (do) / पुरारी (Purari, Shiva) / सो (that one) / न (not) / पाव (attains) / मुनि (sage) / भगति (devotion) / हमारी (my)॥ / अस (thus) / उर (heart) / धरि (holding) / महि (earth) / बिचरहु (wander) / जाई (going) / अब (now) / न (not) / तुम्हहि (to you) / माया (veil of appearance) / निअराई (will approach)॥
ramacharitamanas::776.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::776.essence: Grace from Shiva makes Ram’s devotion possible.
ramacharitamanas::776.simple_meaning: Ram tells the sage that Shiva’s grace is necessary to receive his devotion. With that certainty in heart, the sage can now live freely, and illusion will no longer trouble him.
ramacharitamanas::776.simple_insight: Relief comes from knowing devotion is not self-made; grace can open what effort alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::776.detailed_meaning: After Shiva has spoken in the frame story, Ram answers the sage directly. He says that only the one blessed by Shiva can truly receive his devotion. The sage is then told to keep that certainty and continue living in the world, free from the pull of illusion.
ramacharitamanas::776.modern_relevance: You keep trying to force clarity through effort alone, but some doors open only when trust arrives first. Once that settles in, the noise loses its grip.
ramacharitamanas::776.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance alone to trust in grace as the opening to devotion.

ramacharitamanas::777.verse_sanskrit: बहुबिधि मुनिहि प्रबोधि प्रभु तब भए अंतरधान। सत्यलोक नारद चले करत राम गुन गान ॥
ramacharitamanas::777.verse_hindi: बहुत प्रकार से मुनि को समझा-बुझाकर (ढाँढस देकर) तब प्रभु अंतर्द्धान हो गए और नारदजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुणों का गान करते हुए सत्य लोक (ब्रह्मलोक) को चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::777.english_translation: After comforting the sage in many ways, the Lord then disappeared. Narada went on to Satyaloka singing the praises of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::777.translation_literal: बहुबिधि (in many ways) / मुनिहि (the sage) / प्रबोधि (having comforted) / प्रभु (the Lord) / तब (then) / भए (became) / अंतरधान (invisible, disappeared) / सत्यलोक (to Satyaloka) / नारद (Narada) / चले (went) / करत (doing) / राम (Ram's) / गुन (qualities) / गान (singing)
ramacharitamanas::777.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::777.essence: True devotion keeps singing after the teacher is gone.
ramacharitamanas::777.simple_meaning: The Lord reassures the sage, then vanishes. Narada leaves singing Ram's praises.
ramacharitamanas::777.simple_insight: Comfort can end in silence, and devotion keeps moving.
ramacharitamanas::777.detailed_meaning: After Shiva's teaching to Parvati, Narada has been instructed and soothed. Ram disappears from the scene, and Narada departs toward Satyaloka, still absorbed in singing Ram's qualities. The verse closes the encounter, not with argument, but with devotion continuing on its own.
ramacharitamanas::777.modern_relevance: A hard conversation ends, and the room goes quiet. One person leaves calmer than before, still repeating the words that steadied him. The meeting is over, but the inner effect keeps moving.
ramacharitamanas::777.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the after-effect devotion leaves behind.

ramacharitamanas::778.verse_sanskrit: हर गन मुनिहि जात पथ देखी। बिगत मोह मन हरष बिसेषी॥ अति सभीत नारद पहिं आए। गहि पद आरत बचन सुहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::778.verse_hindi: शिवजी के गणों ने जब मुनि को मोहरहित और मन में बहुत प्रसन्न होकर मार्ग में जाते हुए देखा तब वे अत्यन्त भयभीत होकर नारदजी के पास आए और उनके चरण पकड़कर दीन वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::778.english_translation: Seeing the sage walking on the path, the attendants of Shiva felt their delusion gone and their joy rise. Terrified, they came to Narada, held his feet, and spoke humble words.
ramacharitamanas::778.translation_literal: हर (Shiva's attendants) / गन (attendants) / मुनिहि (the sage) / जात (going) / पथ (path) / देखी (seeing) / बिगत (gone) / मोह (delusion) / मन (mind) / हरष (joy) / बिसेषी (great) / अति (very) / सभीत (afraid) / नारद (Narada) / पहिं (to) / आए (came) / गहि (holding) / पद (feet) / आरत (humble) / बचन (words) / सुहाए (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::778.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::778.essence: A clear mind unsettles fear and invites humility.
ramacharitamanas::778.simple_meaning: Shiva's attendants saw Narada walking free of confusion and felt both joy and fear. They rushed to him, bowed at his feet, and spoke with humility.
ramacharitamanas::778.simple_insight: A clear mind changes the whole atmosphere around it, even in those who once felt threatened.
ramacharitamanas::778.detailed_meaning: After Shiva has instructed Narada and Narada has set off, Shiva's attendants see him walking away transformed. His delusion is gone, his mind is light, and they are suddenly afraid of what their own mistake has caused. They hurry to Narada and beg with folded humility.
ramacharitamanas::778.modern_relevance: You leave a tense meeting calmer than everyone else, and the room notices. Even people who resisted you can feel the force of a steady mind.
ramacharitamanas::778.insight: It shifts attention from outer conflict to the power of inner composure and humility.

ramacharitamanas::779.verse_sanskrit: हर गन हम न बिप्र मुनिराया। बड़ अपराध कीन्ह फल पाया॥ श्राप अनुग्रह करहु कृपाला। बोले नारद दीनदयाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::779.verse_hindi: हे मुनिराज! हम ब्राह्मण नहीं हैं, शिवजी के गण हैं। हमने बड़ा अपराध किया, जिसका फल हमने पा लिया। हे कृपालु! अब शाप दूर करने की कृपा कीजिए। दीनों पर दया करने वाले नारदजी ने कहा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::779.english_translation: We are not priests or sages, O great seer. We committed a great offense and have received its fruit. O compassionate one, please grant a release from this curse," said Narad, the friend of the humble.
ramacharitamanas::779.translation_literal: हर गन (Shiva's attendants) / हम न (we are not) / बिप्र (priests) / मुनि-राया (king among sages) / बड़ (great) / अपराध (offense) / कीन्ह (did) / फल (fruit) / पाया (received) / श्राप (curse) / अनुग्रह (grace) / करहु (do) / कृपाला (compassionate one) / बोले (spoke) / नारद (Narad) / दीन-दयाला (friend of the humble)
ramacharitamanas::779.speaker: Narad
ramacharitamanas::779.essence: Pride softens when fault is openly owned.
ramacharitamanas::779.simple_meaning: Narad admits the attendants were wrong and asks the sage to soften the curse they have earned.
ramacharitamanas::779.simple_insight: Humility opens the door that pride keeps shut.
ramacharitamanas::779.detailed_meaning: The shiva-gana have been frightened by Narad’s changed mood and rush to him in fear. Here they confess their offense, accept the result of their own mistake, and beg him to lessen the curse before the story turns to the next stage.
ramacharitamanas::779.modern_relevance: You realize you’ve crossed a line in a conversation and stop defending yourself. The first healing move is not explanation — it is honest admission and a request for mercy.
ramacharitamanas::779.insight: It teaches you to own the harm first, then ask for repair.

ramacharitamanas::780.verse_sanskrit: निसिचर जाइ होहु तुम्ह दोऊ। बैभव बिपुल तेज बल होऊ॥ भुज बल बिस्व जितब तुम्ह जहिआ। धरिहहिं बिष्नु मनुज तनु तहिआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::780.verse_hindi: तुम दोनों जाकर राक्षस होओ, तुम्हें महान ऐश्वर्य, तेज और बल की प्राप्ति हो। तुम अपनी भुजाओं के बल से जब सारे विश्व को जीत लोगे, तब भगवान विष्णु मनुष्य का शरीर धारण करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::780.english_translation: Go and be born as demons. You will gain vast splendor, brilliance, and strength. When you conquer the world with your arms, Vishnu will take a human body.
ramacharitamanas::780.translation_literal: निसिचर (demon) / जाइ (go) / होहु (be) / तुम्ह (you) / दोऊ (both) / बैभव (splendor) / बिपुल (vast) / तेज (radiance) / बल (strength) / होऊ (become) / भुज (arms) / बल (power) / बिस्व (world) / जितब (to conquer) / तुम्ह (you) / जहिआ (when) / धरिहहिं (will take) / बिष्नु (Vishnu) / मनुज (human) / तनु (body) / तहिआ (then)
ramacharitamanas::780.speaker: Narada
ramacharitamanas::780.essence: Even exile from grace can become the doorway to return.
ramacharitamanas::780.simple_meaning: The two cursed beings are told to take demon birth, grow powerful, and force the divine incarnation to appear in human form.
ramacharitamanas::780.simple_insight: Even a curse can become the hidden path to release.
ramacharitamanas::780.detailed_meaning: Narada has just been asked to soften his curse on two frightened attendants. Instead, he tells them their fall has a purpose: they will become powerful demons, rule through strength, and create the conditions for Vishnu's human incarnation.
ramacharitamanas::780.modern_relevance: A setback can look cruel at first, yet later you see it pushed everything into motion. What felt like ruin may have been the pressure that changed the whole story.
ramacharitamanas::780.insight: It reframes suffering as part of a larger divine pattern, not a dead end.

ramacharitamanas::781.verse_sanskrit: समर मरन हरि हाथ तुम्हारा। होइहहु मुकुत न पुनि संसारा॥ चले जुगल मुनि पद सिर नाई। भए निसाचर कालहि पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::781.verse_hindi: युद्ध में श्री हरि के हाथ से तुम्हारी मृत्यु होगी, जिससे तुम मुक्त हो जाओगे और फिर संसार में जन्म नहीं लोगे। वे दोनों मुनि के चरणों में सिर नवाकर चले और समय पाकर राक्षस हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::781.english_translation: Your death will come by the hand of Hari in battle, and you will be freed from rebirth. The two bowed their heads to the sage's feet and departed; in due time, they became demons.
ramacharitamanas::781.translation_literal: समर (battle) / मरन (death) / हरि (Hari) / हाथ (hand) / तुम्हारा (your) / होइहहु (you will become) / मुकुत (freed) / न (not) / पुनि (again) / संसारा (worldly existence) / चले (went) / जुगल (the pair) / मुनि (sage) / पद (feet) / सिर (head) / नाई (bowing) / भए (became) / निसाचर (night-wanderers) / कालहि (time/fate) / पाई (having obtained)
ramacharitamanas::781.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::781.essence: What looks like ruin can also be the door out.
ramacharitamanas::781.simple_meaning: The sage's curse is also a hidden blessing: they will die at Hari's hands in battle and be freed from rebirth. Then they bow and leave, later taking demon birth.
ramacharitamanas::781.simple_insight: Even a curse can carry release when it serves a larger purpose.
ramacharitamanas::781.detailed_meaning: Narada has just cursed two arrogant gatekeepers, and the sage's anger is being turned into a larger divine plan. They are told their death will come through Hari in battle, ending their cycle of return. After bowing to the sage, they depart and later take demon birth.
ramacharitamanas::781.modern_relevance: A harsh consequence at work can feel like pure punishment at first. Later, you realize it forced a hard reset that broke a pattern you could not break yourself.
ramacharitamanas::781.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing only punishment to seeing hidden release inside consequence.

ramacharitamanas::782.verse_sanskrit: एक कलप एहि हेतु प्रभु लीन्ह मनुज अवतार। सुर रंजन सज्जन सुखद हरि भंजन भुमि भार ॥
ramacharitamanas::782.verse_hindi: देवताओं को प्रसन्न करने वाले, सज्जनों को सुख देने वाले और पृथ्वी का भार हरण करने वाले भगवान ने एक कल्प में इसी कारण मनुष्य का अवतार लिया था ॥
ramacharitamanas::782.english_translation: For this very reason, the Lord took a human incarnation in one age: to delight the radiant beings, give joy to the good, and lift the burden of the earth.
ramacharitamanas::782.translation_literal: एक (one) / कलप (age) / एहि (this) / हेतु (reason) / प्रभु (Lord) / लीन्ह (took) / मनुज (human) / अवतार (incarnation) / सुर (radiant beings) / रंजन (delighting) / सज्जन (good people) / सुखद (giving joy) / हरि (the Lord) / भंजन (removing) / भुमि (earth) / भार (burden)
ramacharitamanas::782.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::782.essence: Ram enters the world to relieve suffering and restore harmony.
ramacharitamanas::782.simple_meaning: Ram took birth as a human to please the radiant beings, bless good people, and remove the earth’s burden.
ramacharitamanas::782.simple_insight: Great power can enter the world as relief, not display.
ramacharitamanas::782.detailed_meaning: After the cursed brothers are sent toward their future births, Tulsidas steps back and reveals why Ram appears in human form at all: not for spectacle, but to restore balance, delight the radiant beings, and bring comfort to the good.
ramacharitamanas::782.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is tense, and you lower the temperature without asking for credit. Some people enter a situation to add weight; others enter to remove it.
ramacharitamanas::782.insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to world-relief: real greatness reduces burden.

ramacharitamanas::783.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि जनम करम हरि केरे। सुंदर सुखद बिचित्र घनेरे॥ कलप कलप प्रति प्रभु अवतरहीं। चारु चरित नानाबिधि करहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::783.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार भगवान के अनेक सुंदर, सुखदायक और अलौकिक जन्म और कर्म हैं। प्रत्येक कल्प में जब-जब भगवान अवतार लेते हैं और नाना प्रकार की सुंदर लीलाएँ करते हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::783.english_translation: In this way, the divine births and actions are many, beautiful, delightful, and wondrous. In every age, the divine descends again and again and performs many kinds of lovely deeds.
ramacharitamanas::783.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / जनम (births) / करम (actions) / हरि केरे (of Hari) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुखद (delightful) / बिचित्र (wondrous) / घनेरे (many)॥ / कलप कलप प्रति (in every age) / प्रभु (the Lord) / अवतरहीं (descend) / चारु (lovely) / चरित (deeds, conduct) / नानाबिधि (of many kinds) / करहीं (do, perform)॥
ramacharitamanas::783.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::783.essence: Ram returns again and again, and each return is fresh wonder.
ramacharitamanas::783.simple_meaning: Ram's births and deeds are many, beautiful, and wondrous. Again and again, he appears in each age and performs many kinds of lovely acts.
ramacharitamanas::783.simple_insight: The divine presence is not distant or one-time; it keeps returning in forms that renew faith.
ramacharitamanas::783.detailed_meaning: After the story of the demon's promised end, the narration widens into a larger truth: Ram's appearances are not a single event. Across ages, he returns in many beautiful forms and acts, making his story endlessly rich before the sages continue the praise.
ramacharitamanas::783.modern_relevance: A child asks why the same bedtime story never gets old, and you realize the answer: what truly matters returns in new forms. Love, courage, and grace are not exhausted by one appearance.
ramacharitamanas::783.insight: It shifts attention from one fixed event to a recurring divine pattern that keeps revealing fresh meaning.

ramacharitamanas::784.verse_sanskrit: तब-तब कथा मुनीसन्ह गाई। परम पुनीत प्रबंध बनाई॥ बिबिध प्रसंग अनूप बखाने। करहिं न सुनि आचरजु सयाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::784.verse_hindi: तब-तब मुनीश्वरों ने परम पवित्र काव्य रचना करके उनकी कथाओं का गान किया है और भाँति-भाँति के अनुपम प्रसंगों का वर्णन किया है, जिनको सुनकर समझदार (विवेकी) लोग आश्चर्य नहीं करते ॥
ramacharitamanas::784.english_translation: Again and again, the sages sang this story. They composed a supremely pure work. They described many unmatched episodes, and wise people do not find them surprising.
ramacharitamanas::784.translation_literal: तब-तब (again and again) / कथा (story) / मुनीसन्ह (by the sages) / गाई (was sung) / परम (supremely) / पुनीत (pure) / प्रबंध (composition) / बनाई (made) / बिबिध (various) / प्रसंग (episodes) / अनूप (matchless) / बखाने (described) / करहिं (do) / न (not) / सुनि (hearing) / आचरजु (surprise) / सयाने (the wise)
ramacharitamanas::784.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::784.essence: Ram's story is too vast for one telling.
ramacharitamanas::784.simple_meaning: Sages have long sung Ram's story in many pure, beautiful forms. Wise people hear these varied episodes and are not astonished, because they know the divine story is limitless.
ramacharitamanas::784.simple_insight: A deep story does not become smaller by being retold. It becomes richer.
ramacharitamanas::784.detailed_meaning: After describing Ram's many births and deeds, the narrator says that wise sages have repeatedly sung this story in sacred forms. They have told many unmatched episodes, and those who truly understand are not surprised, because Ram's story cannot be contained in one telling.
ramacharitamanas::784.modern_relevance: You hear the same lesson from a mentor, a podcast, and an old friend, and it still lands differently each time. A real truth keeps revealing new angles without losing itself.
ramacharitamanas::784.insight: It shifts you from expecting a single complete telling to recognizing that profound meaning comes through many forms.

ramacharitamanas::785.verse_sanskrit: हरि अनंत हरि कथा अनंता। कहहिं सुनहिं बहुबिधि सब संता॥ रामचंद्र के चरित सुहाए। कलप कोटि लगि जाहिं न गाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::785.verse_hindi: श्री हरि अनंत हैं (उनका कोई पार नहीं पा सकता) और उनकी कथा भी अनंत है। सब संत लोग उसे बहुत प्रकार से कहते-सुनते हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के सुंदर चरित्र करोड़ों कल्पों में भी गाए नहीं जा सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::785.english_translation: Hari is endless, and Hari's story is endless. All saints speak and hear it in many ways. The beautiful deeds of Ramchandra cannot be sung even in countless ages.
ramacharitamanas::785.translation_literal: हरि (Hari) / अनंत (endless) / हरि (Hari) / कथा (story) / अनंता (endless) / कहहिं (speak) / सुनहिं (hear) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / सब (all) / संता (saints) / रामचंद्र (Ramchandra) / के (of) / चरित (deeds, conduct) / सुहाए (beautiful) / कलप (ages) / कोटि (crores, countless) / लगि (until) / जाहिं (go) / न (not) / गाए (sung)
ramacharitamanas::785.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::785.essence: Ram's story is inexhaustible; devotion deepens because it never runs out.
ramacharitamanas::785.simple_meaning: The divine and Ram's story have no limit. Saints keep speaking and listening to them, yet they can never be fully exhausted.
ramacharitamanas::785.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing the sacred story is bigger than any single telling.
ramacharitamanas::785.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses the narration to praise Ram's greatness. After saying that divine births and deeds are endlessly varied, he adds that even the finest minds cannot finish describing Ram's beautiful life. The verse opens into devotion, not closure.
ramacharitamanas::785.modern_relevance: You reread a letter from someone you love and still find new meaning in it. Some things do not get smaller with repetition; they keep revealing more.
ramacharitamanas::785.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to finish Ram's story to entering it with humility and wonder.

ramacharitamanas::786.verse_sanskrit: यह प्रसंग मैं कहा भवानी। हरिमायाँ मोहहिं मुनि ग्यानी॥ प्रभु कौतुकी प्रनत हितकारी। सेवत सुलभ सकल दुखहारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::786.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं कि) हे पार्वती! मैंने यह बताने के लिए इस प्रसंग को कहा कि ज्ञानी मुनि भी भगवान की माया से मोहित हो जाते हैं। प्रभु कौतुकी (लीलामय) हैं और शरणागत का हित करने वाले हैं। वे सेवा करने में बहुत सुलभ और सब दुःखों के हरने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::786.english_translation: I told this story, O Bhavani, to show that even wise sages are deluded by the divine veil of appearance. The Lord is playful, kind to the surrendered, easy to serve, and the remover of all suffering.
ramacharitamanas::786.translation_literal: यह (this) / प्रसंग (episode) / मैं (I) / कहा (said) / भवानी (Bhavani) / हरि-मायाँ (the divine veil of appearance) / मोहहिं (delude) / मुनि (sage) / ग्यानी (wise) / प्रभु (Lord) / कौतुकी (playful) / प्रनत (the surrendered) / हितकारी (benefactor) / सेवत (by serving) / सुलभ (easy to reach) / सकल (all) / दुखहारी (remover of suffering)
ramacharitamanas::786.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::786.essence: Even the wise are fooled; surrender makes Ram near.
ramacharitamanas::786.simple_meaning: Even learned sages can be confused by divine illusion. Ram is playful, kind to those who surrender, easy to approach through service, and able to remove suffering.
ramacharitamanas::786.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing you do not need to be perfect to come close to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::786.detailed_meaning: Shiva speaks to Parvati after reflecting on Ram's story. He explains why he told this episode: even great sages can be veiled by maya, yet Ram remains gentle, accessible, and devoted to the welfare of anyone who turns to him.
ramacharitamanas::786.modern_relevance: You can spend years studying a problem and still miss the obvious because your own assumptions are in the way. Humility opens the door faster than cleverness.
ramacharitamanas::786.insight: It shifts the mind from self-confidence in understanding to humble dependence on Ram's grace.

ramacharitamanas::787.verse_sanskrit: सुर नर मुनि कोउ नाहिं जेहि न मोह माया प्रबल। अस बिचारि मन माहिं भजिअ महामाया पतिहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::787.verse_hindi: देवता, मनुष्य और मुनियों में ऐसा कोई नहीं है, जिसे भगवान की महान बलवती माया मोहित न कर दे। मन में ऐसा विचारकर उस महामाया के स्वामी (प्रेरक) श्री भगवान का भजन करना चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::787.english_translation: No one among gods, humans, or sages escapes the great force of maya. Knowing this in the mind, worship the Lord of that great maya.
ramacharitamanas::787.translation_literal: सुर (gods) / नर (humans) / मुनि (sages) / कोउ नाहिं (no one) / जेहि (whom) / न मोह (does not delude) / माया (maya) / प्रबल (powerful) / अस (thus) / बिचारि (thinking) / मन माहिं (in the mind) / भजिअ (one should worship) / महामाया (great maya) / पतिहि (the Lord)
ramacharitamanas::787.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::787.essence: Even the wise are shaken by illusion; devotion begins with that humility.
ramacharitamanas::787.simple_meaning: Even the wise can be confused by the force of illusion. Knowing that, the heart should turn to Ram, who stands above that power.
ramacharitamanas::787.simple_insight: It brings humility: you stop trusting your own clarity too much and lean on Ram instead.
ramacharitamanas::787.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the opening of Balkand, after saying that Ram's story is endless and that even sages are touched by divine illusion. He now draws the lesson: no being is untouched, so the wise respond with devotion.
ramacharitamanas::787.modern_relevance: You reread the same message three times and still misread the tone. Pride in your own certainty only makes the mistake worse; humility steadies you.
ramacharitamanas::787.insight: It shifts the mind from self-confidence in perception to humble reliance on the divine.

ramacharitamanas::788.verse_sanskrit: अपर हेतु सुनु सैलकुमारी। कहउँ बिचित्र कथा बिस्तारी॥ जेहि कारन अज अगुन अरूपा। ब्रह्म भयउ कोसलपुर भूपा ॥
ramacharitamanas::788.verse_hindi: हे गिरिराजकुमारी! अब भगवान के अवतार का वह दूसरा कारण सुनो- मैं उसकी विचित्र कथा विस्तार करके कहता हूँ- जिस कारण से जन्मरहित, निर्गुण और रूपरहित (अव्यक्त सच्चिदानंदघन) ब्रह्म अयोध्यापुरी के राजा हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::788.english_translation: O daughter of the mountain king, hear now the other reason. I will विस्तार this wondrous story: for that cause, the unborn, formless, attribute-less supreme reality became the king of Kosala.
ramacharitamanas::788.translation_literal: अपर (other) / हेतु (reason) / सुनु (listen) / सैलकुमारी (daughter of the mountain king) / कहउँ (I tell) / बिचित्र (wondrous) / कथा (story) / बिस्तारी (at length) / जेहि (for which) / कारन (cause) / अज (unborn) / अगुन (without qualities) / अरूपा (formless) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / भयउ (became) / कोसलपुर (Kosala city) / भूपा (king)
ramacharitamanas::788.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::788.essence: The formless supreme reality entered history as Kosala's king.
ramacharitamanas::788.simple_meaning: Shiva tells Parvati there is another reason for Ram's birth: the unborn, formless supreme reality took human form and became king of Kosala.
ramacharitamanas::788.simple_insight: The infinite entered a human life on purpose, not by accident.
ramacharitamanas::788.detailed_meaning: Shiva is explaining to Parvati why Ram appeared in Ayodhya. This is not just a birth story; it is a revelation that the unborn, formless supreme reality chose kingship in a human world, preparing her to understand Ram's deeper nature.
ramacharitamanas::788.modern_relevance: A child asks why a great leader would leave comfort and live among ordinary people. The answer is not ambition but intention: sometimes the highest presence enters the smallest room for a reason.
ramacharitamanas::788.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram's birth as event to seeing it as deliberate descent.

ramacharitamanas::789.verse_sanskrit: जो प्रभु बिपिन फिरत तुम्ह देखा। बंधु समेत धरें मुनिबेषा॥ जासु चरित अवलोकि भवानी। सती सरीर रहिहु बौरानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::789.verse_hindi: जिन प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को तुमने भाई लक्ष्मणजी के साथ मुनियों का सा वेष धारण किए वन में फिरते देखा था और हे भवानी! जिनके चरित्र देखकर सती के शरीर में तुम ऐसी बावली हो गई थीं कि- ॥
ramacharitamanas::789.english_translation: You saw that Lord Ram wandering in the forest with Lakshman, dressed like a sage. Seeing his deeds, O Bhavani, Sati became so bewildered that she lost her composure.
ramacharitamanas::789.translation_literal: जो (who) / प्रभु (Lord) / बिपिन (forest) / फिरत (wandering) / तुम्ह (you) / देखा (saw) / बंधु (brother) / समेत (together with) / धरें (wearing) / मुनिबेषा (sage-attire) / जासु (whose) / चरित (deeds) / अवलोकि (seeing) / भवानी (Bhavani) / सती (Sati) / सरीर (body) / रहिहु (became) / बौरानी (bewildered)
