ramacharitamanas::789.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::789.essence: Ram's conduct can bewilder even the wise.
ramacharitamanas::789.simple_meaning: Ram was seen in the forest with Lakshman, dressed like a sage. His conduct was so extraordinary that Sati lost her composure when she saw it.
ramacharitamanas::789.simple_insight: A sacred life can unsettle old assumptions before it ever explains itself.
ramacharitamanas::789.detailed_meaning: Shiva is reminding Parvati of the moment Sati saw Ram and Lakshman wandering in the forest in sage-like dress. Ram's conduct was so unusual and radiant that it confused Sati, setting up the deeper story of her doubt and Shiva's explanation.
ramacharitamanas::789.modern_relevance: You meet someone quietly helping others while carrying their own burden, and their steadiness throws your assumptions off. Some lives do not announce their greatness; they expose your blindness.
ramacharitamanas::789.insight: It shifts attention from appearances to the moral force of conduct.

ramacharitamanas::790.verse_sanskrit: अजहुँ न छाया मिटति तुम्हारी। तासु चरित सुनु भ्रम रुज हारी॥ लीला कीन्हि जो तेहिं अवतारा। सो सब कहिहउँ मति अनुसारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::790.verse_hindi: अब भी तुम्हारे उस बावलेपन की छाया नहीं मिटती, उन्हीं के भ्रम रूपी रोग के हरण करने वाले चरित्र सुनो। उस अवतार में भगवान ने जो-जो लीला की, वह सब मैं अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार तुम्हें कहूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::790.english_translation: Even now the shadow of your bewilderment has not faded. Listen to the deeds that destroy confusion and illness. I will tell, as far as my understanding allows, all the play the divine performed in that incarnation.
ramacharitamanas::790.translation_literal: अजहुँ (even now) / न (not) / छाया (shadow) / मिटति (fades) / तुम्हारी (your) / तासु (of that) / चरित (deeds, conduct) / सुनु (listen) / भ्रम (confusion, delusion) / रुज (illness) / हारी (destroying) / लीला (play, divine acts) / कीन्हि (did) / जो (which) / तेहिं (in that) / अवतारा (incarnation) / सो (that) / सब (all) / कहिहउँ (I will tell) / मति (understanding) / अनुसारा (according to)
ramacharitamanas::790.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::790.essence: Ram’s deeds heal confusion by being truly heard.
ramacharitamanas::790.simple_meaning: Parvati still carries confusion, so Shiva says he will describe Ram’s deeds, which remove that confusion and heal the mind.
ramacharitamanas::790.simple_insight: Clear hearing can dissolve the fog that keeps returning in the mind.
ramacharitamanas::790.detailed_meaning: Shiva is still speaking to Parvati in the outer frame of the story. She has seen Ram in the forest, yet her wonder and confusion remain. So Shiva promises to recount Ram’s incarnation and deeds in full, as far as his understanding can go.
ramacharitamanas::790.modern_relevance: You replay the same conversation in your head after midnight, trying to make sense of what happened. A clear account can calm what rumination keeps inflaming.
ramacharitamanas::790.insight: It shifts the reader from muddled reaction to patient listening for understanding.

ramacharitamanas::791.verse_sanskrit: भरद्वाज सुनि संकर बानी। सकुचि सप्रेम उमा मुसुकानी॥ लगे बहुरि बरनै बृषकेतू। सो अवतार भयउ जेहि हेतू ॥
ramacharitamanas::791.verse_hindi: (याज्ञवल्क्यजी ने कहा-) हे भरद्वाज! शंकरजी के वचन सुनकर पार्वतीजी सकुचाकर प्रेमसहित मुस्कुराईं। फिर वृषकेतु शिवजी जिस कारण से भगवान का वह अवतार हुआ था, उसका वर्णन करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::791.english_translation: Bharadwaj, hearing Shiva's words, Uma smiled shyly with love. Then the Bull-bannered Lord began describing the reason for that incarnation.
ramacharitamanas::791.translation_literal: भरद्वाज (Bharadwaj) / सुनि (hearing) / संकर (Shankar/Shiva) / बानी (words) / सकुचि (with shyness) / सप्रेम (with love) / उमा (Uma/Parvati) / मुसुकानी (smiled) / लगे (began) / बहुरि (again) / बरनै (to describe) / बृषकेतू (Bull-bannered one, Shiva) / सो (that) / अवतार (incarnation) / भयउ (became/was) / जेहि (for which) / हेतू (reason)
ramacharitamanas::791.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::791.essence: Love opens the way to understanding why the divine comes into form.
ramacharitamanas::791.simple_meaning: Parvati reacts lovingly to Shiva's words, and Shiva then starts explaining why Ram took that incarnation.
ramacharitamanas::791.simple_insight: Some truths unfold slowly, with reverence and patience.
ramacharitamanas::791.detailed_meaning: In the frame story, Shiva is speaking to Parvati through the sage tradition. Parvati responds with shy, loving delight, and Shiva turns to the central question: why Ram took human form. This verse opens the explanation.
ramacharitamanas::791.modern_relevance: You hear one sentence that changes everything, and you go quiet before asking the next question. Real understanding often begins with that pause.
ramacharitamanas::791.insight: It shifts the reader from receiving a story to listening for its reason.

ramacharitamanas::792.verse_sanskrit: सो मैं तुम्ह सन कहउँ सबु सुनु मुनीस मन लाइ। रामकथा कलि मल हरनि मंगल करनि सुहाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::792.verse_hindi: हे मुनीश्वर भरद्वाज! मैं वह सब तुमसे कहता हूँ, मन लगाकर सुनो। श्री रामचन्द्रजी की कथा कलियुग के पापों को हरने वाली, कल्याण करने वाली और बड़ी सुंदर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::792.english_translation: O best of sages, I tell you all this. Listen with attention: Ram's story removes the impurities of the age, brings auspiciousness, and is beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::792.translation_literal: सो (that) / मैं (I) / तुम्ह (to you) / सन (with) / कहउँ (tell) / सबु (all) / सुनु (listen) / मुनीस (O best of sages) / मन (mind) / लाइ (applying) / रामकथा (Ram's story) / कलि (of Kali age) / मल (impurity) / हरनि (removing) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / करनि (doing) / सुहाइ (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::792.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::792.essence: Ram's story purifies the listener and makes life auspicious.
ramacharitamanas::792.simple_meaning: Tulsidas tells Bharadvaj to listen carefully because Ram's story removes the impurities of this age and brings goodness and beauty.
ramacharitamanas::792.simple_insight: Something holy can cleanse the mind just by being heard with attention.
ramacharitamanas::792.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas turns from Shiva's narration to a direct invitation to Bharadvaj. Before beginning the story of Ram, he declares its power: this is not just a tale, but a cleansing, auspicious force for the listener.
ramacharitamanas::792.modern_relevance: You open a story while your mind is crowded with noise, guilt, and half-finished thoughts. Then one clear, beautiful truth lands and everything feels less contaminated.
ramacharitamanas::792.insight: It shifts the reader from passive hearing to attentive listening, treating Ram's story as a cleansing practice.

ramacharitamanas::793.verse_sanskrit: स्वायंभू मनु अरु सतरूपा। जिन्ह तें भै नरसृष्टि अनूपा॥ दंपति धरम आचरन नीका। अजहुँ गाव श्रुति जिन्ह कै लीका ॥
ramacharitamanas::793.verse_hindi: स्वायम्भुव मनु और (उनकी पत्नी) शतरूपा, जिनसे मनुष्यों की यह अनुपम सृष्टि हुई, इन दोनों पति-पत्नी के धर्म और आचरण बहुत अच्छे थे। आज भी वेद जिनकी मर्यादा का गान करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::793.english_translation: Svayambhu Manu and Shatarupa gave rise to the unmatched human race. Their conduct as husband and wife was excellent, and even today the Vedas praise their standard of conduct.
ramacharitamanas::793.translation_literal: स्वायंभू (born of himself) / मनु (Manu) / अरु (and) / सतरूपा (Shatarupa) / जिन्ह तें (from whom) / भै (became) / नरसृष्टि (human creation) / अनूपा (unique) / दंपति (the married pair) / धरम (dharma) / आचरन (conduct) / नीका (good) / अजहुँ (even now) / गाव (sing) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / जिन्ह कै (whose) / लीका (standard, line)
ramacharitamanas::793.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::793.essence: Exemplary conduct turns a family line into a lasting standard.
ramacharitamanas::793.simple_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa were the original human couple, and their married life was exemplary. Their conduct became a model that the Vedas still praise.
ramacharitamanas::793.simple_insight: A good life can become a standard that outlives you.
ramacharitamanas::793.detailed_meaning: Yajnavalkya continues the sacred lineage in the Balkand. After naming the first human couple, he pauses to honor their conduct: Manu and Shatarupa are not just ancestors, but a model of righteous household life that even scripture remembers.
ramacharitamanas::793.modern_relevance: A couple quietly keeps promises, raises children with care, and never makes a show of it. Years later, their children still measure love by that example.
ramacharitamanas::793.insight: It shifts attention from ancestry alone to the moral quality that makes a lineage worthy of remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::794.verse_sanskrit: नृप उत्तानपाद सुत तासू। ध्रुव हरिभगत भयउ सुत जासू॥ लघु सुत नाम प्रियब्रत ताही। बेद पुरान प्रसंसहिं जाही ॥
ramacharitamanas::794.verse_hindi: राजा उत्तानपाद उनके पुत्र थे, जिनके पुत्र (प्रसिद्ध) हरिभक्त ध्रुवजी हुए। उन (मनुजी) के छोटे लड़के का नाम प्रियव्रत था, जिनकी प्रशंसा वेद और पुराण करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::794.english_translation: King Uttanapada was their son; from him was born Dhruva, the devotee of Hari. His younger son was named Priyavrata, whom the Vedas and Puranas praise.
ramacharitamanas::794.translation_literal: नृप (king) / उत्तानपाद (Uttanapada) / सुत (son) / तासू (of him) / ध्रुव (Dhruva) / हरिभगत (devotee of Hari) / भयउ (became) / सुत (son) / जासू (whose) / लघु (younger) / सुत (son) / नाम (name) / प्रियब्रत (Priyavrata) / ताही (of him) / बेद (Vedas) / पुरान (Puranas) / प्रसंसहिं (praise) / जाही (whom)
ramacharitamanas::794.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::794.essence: Famous sons are being named to carry the lineage forward.
ramacharitamanas::794.simple_meaning: Uttanapada had two famous sons: Dhruva, known for devotion, and Priyavrata, praised in sacred tradition. The verse is naming ancestral figures, not teaching a direct lesson.
ramacharitamanas::794.simple_insight: It places the story in a sacred lineage, reminding you that greatness often arrives through family and inheritance.
ramacharitamanas::794.detailed_meaning: The narration continues through the genealogy of Manu. After mentioning Uttanapada, it names his famous son Dhruva, remembered for devotion to Hari, and then Priyavrata, whose virtue is praised by the Vedas and Puranas. The verse serves as a bridge in the lineage, not a standalone teaching.
ramacharitamanas::794.modern_relevance: A family tree is being read aloud at a ceremony, and one name after another carries a whole history of character, duty, and memory. Some verses simply place you inside that inherited world.
ramacharitamanas::794.insight: It shifts attention from individual drama to the larger sacred lineage that frames the story.

ramacharitamanas::795.verse_sanskrit: देवहूति पुनि तासु कुमारी। जो मुनि कर्दम कै प्रिय नारी॥ आदि देव प्रभु दीनदयाला। जठर धरेउ जेहिं कपिल कृपाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::795.verse_hindi: पुनः देवहूति उनकी कन्या थी, जो कर्दम मुनि की प्यारी पत्नी हुई और जिन्होंने आदि देव, दीनों पर दया करने वाले समर्थ एवं कृपालु भगवान कपिल को गर्भ में धारण किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::795.english_translation: Devahuti was also his daughter, who became the beloved wife of the sage Kardama. She bore in her womb the primal Lord, the compassionate and powerful Kapila.
ramacharitamanas::795.translation_literal: देवहूति (Devahuti) / पुनि (also) / तासु (his) / कुमारी (daughter) / जो (who) / मुनि (sage) / कर्दम (Kardama) / कै (of) / प्रिय (beloved) / नारी (wife) / आदि (primal) / देव (divine being) / प्रभु (Lord) / दीनदयाला (compassionate to the poor) / जठर (womb) / धरेउ (carried) / जेहिं (in whom) / कपिल (Kapila) / कृपाला (gracious)
ramacharitamanas::795.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::795.essence: A quiet family line becomes the birthplace of profound teaching.
ramacharitamanas::795.simple_meaning: Devahuti, daughter of Manu, became Kardama’s wife and gave birth to Kapila, the compassionate teacher of deep wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::795.simple_insight: Great spiritual wisdom enters the world through an ordinary family line.
ramacharitamanas::795.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is listing Manu’s descendants to show the sacred family line continuing. Devahuti, Manu’s daughter, becomes Kardama’s wife, and through her Kapila is born. The verse prepares for Kapila’s teaching on insight and reality.
ramacharitamanas::795.modern_relevance: A family photo can look ordinary, yet it may hide the person who changes everything for others. What seems like a genealogy is really the arrival of a teacher.
ramacharitamanas::795.insight: It shifts attention from names and lineage to the moment a teacher appears in a family line.

ramacharitamanas::796.verse_sanskrit: सांख्य सास्त्र जिन्ह प्रगट बखाना। तत्व बिचार निपुन भगवाना॥ तेहिं मनु राज कीन्ह बहु काला। प्रभु आयसु सब बिधि प्रतिपाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::796.verse_hindi: तत्वों का विचार करने में अत्यन्त निपुण जिन (कपिल) भगवान ने सांख्य शास्त्र का प्रकट रूप में वर्णन किया, उन (स्वायम्भुव) मनुजी ने बहुत समय तक राज्य किया और सब प्रकार से भगवान की आज्ञा (रूप शास्त्रों की मर्यादा) का पालन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::796.english_translation: Kapila, the divine one, clearly expounded the science of Samkhya and was skilled in discerning truth. Manu ruled for a long time, and in every way he followed the Lord's command.
ramacharitamanas::796.translation_literal: सांख्य सास्त्र (the Samkhya teaching) / जिन्ह (who) / प्रगट (clearly) / बखाना (explained) / तत्व (truth-principles) / बिचार (discernment) / निपुन (skilled) / भगवाना (the divine one)॥ / तेहिं (then) / मनु (Manu) / राज (rule) / कीन्ह (did) / बहु (much) / काला (time)॥ / प्रभु (the Lord's) / आयसु (command) / सब बिधि (in every way) / प्रतिपाला (was followed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::796.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::796.essence: Truth means little unless life actually follows it.
ramacharitamanas::796.simple_meaning: Kapila taught the Samkhya system with clarity, and Manu spent a long time ruling while following the Lord's command in every way.
ramacharitamanas::796.simple_insight: Real greatness is not just insight; it is living by what you understand.
ramacharitamanas::796.detailed_meaning: The verse looks back on Kapila, whose teaching of truth-principles became a clear doctrine, and on Manu, who ruled for a long time without departing from divine order. It sets up the next sorrowful realization: even a righteous life can still leave the heart unsatisfied.
ramacharitamanas::796.modern_relevance: You can know the right principles, hold a responsible role for years, and still feel the ache of something missing. Mere order is not the same as inner fulfillment.
ramacharitamanas::796.insight: It links understanding with disciplined conduct, showing that knowledge must be lived, not just admired.

ramacharitamanas::797.verse_sanskrit: होइ न बिषय बिराग भवन बसत भा चौथपन॥ हृदयँ बहुत दुख लाग जनम गयउ हरिभगति बिनु ॥
ramacharitamanas::797.verse_hindi: घर में रहते बुढ़ापा आ गया, परन्तु विषयों से वैराग्य नहीं होता (इस बात को सोचकर) उनके मन में बड़ा दुःख हुआ कि श्री हरि की भक्ति बिना जन्म यों ही चला गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::797.english_translation: Even after living in the house until old age, worldly attachment did not fade. Their heart felt deep sorrow that life had passed without devotion to Hari.
ramacharitamanas::797.translation_literal: होइ न (does not happen) / बिषय (worldly objects) / बिराग (dispassion) / भवन बसत (living in the house) / भा (became) / चौथपन (old age) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बहुत दुख (great sorrow) / लाग (felt) / जनम (life) / गयउ (went away) / हरिभगति (devotion to Hari) / बिनु (without)
ramacharitamanas::797.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::797.essence: A life can be long and still remain unfinished inside.
ramacharitamanas::797.simple_meaning: Living long is not the same as becoming free from craving. The pain here is realizing that a whole life can pass without devotion.
ramacharitamanas::797.simple_insight: It brings a quiet urgency: don’t wait for age to do the work of letting go.
ramacharitamanas::797.detailed_meaning: In the story of Manu, even after years of household life, the mind has not turned away from desire. That realization hurts him deeply, because he sees that an entire life can slip by without Hari-bhakti.
ramacharitamanas::797.modern_relevance: You look up from years of routine, a mortgage, school runs, and deadlines, and suddenly realize the same cravings still run the show. That sting can become the start of real turning.
ramacharitamanas::797.insight: It shifts the mind from postponing detachment to seeing urgency in the present moment.

ramacharitamanas::798.verse_sanskrit: बरबस राज सुतहि तब दीन्हा। नारि समेत गवन बन कीन्हा॥ तीरथ बर नैमिष बिख्याता। अति पुनीत साधक सिधि दाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::798.verse_hindi: तब मनुजी ने अपने पुत्र को जबर्दस्ती राज्य देकर स्वयं स्त्री सहित वन को गमन किया। अत्यन्त पवित्र और साधकों को सिद्धि देने वाला तीर्थों में श्रेष्ठ नैमिषारण्य प्रसिद्ध है ॥
ramacharitamanas::798.english_translation: Then Manu forcibly gave the kingdom to his son and went to the forest with his wife. Naimisharanya, famous among holy places, is extremely pure and grants accomplishment to seekers.
ramacharitamanas::798.translation_literal: बरबस (forcibly) / राज सुतहि (to the son, the kingdom) / तब (then) / दीन्हा (gave) / नारि समेत (together with wife) / गवन (going) / बन (to the forest) / कीन्हा (did) / तीरथ (holy place) / बर (best) / नैमिष (Naimish) / बिख्याता (famous) / अति (very) / पुनीत (pure) / साधक (seekers) / सिधि (accomplishment) / दाता (giver)
ramacharitamanas::798.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::798.essence: True renunciation is giving away power before it owns you.
ramacharitamanas::798.simple_meaning: Manu hands the kingdom to his son and leaves for the forest with his wife. Naimisharanya is described as a deeply pure place that helps seekers succeed.
ramacharitamanas::798.simple_insight: Sometimes renunciation means handing over what you ruled and walking away without looking back.
ramacharitamanas::798.detailed_meaning: Manu has grown weary of worldly life. He gives the kingdom to his son, takes Shatarupa with him, and heads toward Naimisharanya, a sacred place known for purity and spiritual attainment. The verse marks the beginning of their withdrawal from power.
ramacharitamanas::798.modern_relevance: You finally sign the business over to your child, close the office door, and book the train to a quiet ashram town. What you built can now live without you.
ramacharitamanas::798.insight: It shifts the mind from holding power to releasing it cleanly.

ramacharitamanas::799.verse_sanskrit: बसहिं तहाँ मुनि सिद्ध समाजा। तहँ हियँ हरषि चलेउ मनु राजा॥ पंथ जात सोहहिं मतिधीरा। ग्यान भगति जनु धरें सरीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::799.verse_hindi: वहाँ मुनियों और सिद्धों के समूह बसते हैं। राजा मनु हृदय में हर्षित होकर वहीं चले। वे धीर बुद्धि वाले राजा-रानी मार्ग में जाते हुए ऐसे सुशोभित हो रहे थे मानों ज्ञान और भक्ति ही शरीर धारण किए जा रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::799.english_translation: There the company of sages and perfected beings dwelt. King Manu, filled with joy, went there. The wise king and queen shone on the path, as if wisdom and devotion had taken bodily form.
ramacharitamanas::799.translation_literal: बसहिं (they dwell) / तहाँ (there) / मुनि (sages) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / समाजा (assembly) / तहँ (there) / हियँ (in the heart) / हरषि (rejoicing) / चलेउ (went) / मनु (Manu) / राजा (king) / पंथ (path) / जात (going) / सोहहिं (shone) / मतिधीरा (wise and steadfast) / ग्यान (wisdom) / भगति (devotion) / जनु (as if) / धरें (having taken) / सरीरा (bodies)
ramacharitamanas::799.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::799.essence: Inner wisdom and devotion make even a simple walk radiant.
ramacharitamanas::799.simple_meaning: Manu and his queen travel joyfully to a sacred place where sages and perfected beings live. Their calm, wise bearing makes them seem like wisdom and devotion themselves.
ramacharitamanas::799.simple_insight: A life guided by devotion and clear judgment changes the way a person even walks.
ramacharitamanas::799.detailed_meaning: Manu has already given up the throne and sent his son to rule. Now he and his queen head toward the sacred hermitage at Naimish, a place filled with sages and perfected beings. Their journey itself becomes a visible sign of inner maturity.
ramacharitamanas::799.modern_relevance: You see an older couple quietly entering a temple town after leaving behind power and family control. They do not look defeated. They look transformed by what they have chosen.
ramacharitamanas::799.insight: It shifts attention from outer status to the visible grace of a life aligned with higher values.

ramacharitamanas::800.verse_sanskrit: पहुँचे जाइ धेनुमति तीरा। हरषि नहाने निरमल नीरा॥ आए मिलन सिद्ध मुनि ग्यानी। धरम धुरंधर नृपरिषि जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::800.verse_hindi: (चलते-चलते) वे गोमती के किनारे जा पहुँचे। हर्षित होकर उन्होंने निर्मल जल में स्नान किया। उनको धर्मधुरंधर राजर्षि जानकर सिद्ध और ज्ञानी मुनि उनसे मिलने आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::800.english_translation: They reached the bank of the Gomati River and bathed joyfully in its pure water. Knowing them as a king-sage steadfast in dharma, perfected sages and wise ascetics came to meet them.
ramacharitamanas::800.translation_literal: पहुँचे (reached) / जाइ (going) / धेनुमति (Gomati) / तीरा (bank) / हरषि (with joy) / नहाने (bathed) / निरमल (pure) / नीरा (water) / आए (came) / मिलन (to meet) / सिद्ध (perfected sages) / मुनि (ascetics) / ग्यानी (wise) / धरम (dharma) / धुरंधर (bearer) / नृपरिषि (king-sage) / जानी (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::800.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::800.essence: Steady conduct draws reverence before any words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::800.simple_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa reach the Gomati river, bathe happily, and are honored by sages who come to meet them.
ramacharitamanas::800.simple_insight: A pure, steady life draws respect without asking for it.
ramacharitamanas::800.detailed_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa have left behind palace life and are travelling as seekers. At the Gomati bank, they bathe with joy. Their dharmic steadiness is so evident that siddhas and wise sages come forward to welcome them.
ramacharitamanas::800.modern_relevance: You arrive at a quiet river after a long drive, tired but clear-headed. People who know your conduct don't need an introduction; they feel your steadiness the moment you arrive.
ramacharitamanas::800.insight: It shows how visible character becomes: dharma attracts recognition naturally, without self-promotion.

ramacharitamanas::801.verse_sanskrit: जहँ जहँ तीरथ रहे सुहाए। मुनिन्ह सकल सादर करवाए॥ कृस सरीर मुनिपट परिधाना। सत समाज नित सुनहिं पुराना ॥
ramacharitamanas::801.verse_hindi: जहाँ-जहाँ सुंदर तीर्थ थे, मुनियों ने आदरपूर्वक सभी तीर्थ उनको करा दिए। उनका शरीर दुर्बल हो गया था। वे मुनियों के से (वल्कल) वस्त्र धारण करते थे और संतों के समाज में नित्य पुराण सुनते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::801.english_translation: Wherever there were lovely pilgrimage places, the sages respectfully had them perform the rites there. Their bodies grew lean, they wore the bark garments of ascetics, and they constantly listened to the Puranas in gatherings of holy people.
ramacharitamanas::801.translation_literal: जहँ जहँ (wherever) / तीरथ (pilgrimage place) / रहे (were) / सुहाए (beautiful) / मुनिन्ह (by the sages) / सकल (all) / सादर (respectfully) / करवाए (had performed) / कृस (lean) / सरीर (body) / मुनिपट (ascetic garment) / परिधाना (wearing) / सत समाज (holy gathering) / नित (daily) / सुनहिं (they hear) / पुराना (the Puranas)
ramacharitamanas::801.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::801.essence: Sacred living reshapes the body, habits, and mind together.
ramacharitamanas::801.simple_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa lived like ascetics on their pilgrimage. They stayed lean, wore simple bark clothes, and spent their days listening to sacred stories among holy people.
ramacharitamanas::801.simple_insight: A holy life is not loud. It is steady, simple, and shaped by what you choose to keep near you.
ramacharitamanas::801.detailed_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa are still on their sacred journey. At every beautiful pilgrimage place, sages honor them, their bodies grow lean from austerity, and they live like ascetics, listening daily to the Puranas in holy company.
ramacharitamanas::801.modern_relevance: You step away from noise for a while, eat simply, keep your phone away, and sit with people who remind you what matters. That quiet discipline changes you.
ramacharitamanas::801.insight: It shifts attention from comfort and display to steady practice, simplicity, and nourishing company.

ramacharitamanas::802.verse_sanskrit: द्वादस अच्छर मंत्र पुनि जपहिं सहित अनुराग। बासुदेव पद पंकरुह दंपति मन अति लाग ॥
ramacharitamanas::802.verse_hindi: और द्वादशाक्षर मन्त्र (ऊँ नमो भगवते वासुदेवाय) का प्रेम सहित जप करते थे। भगवान वासुदेव के चरणकमलों में उन राजा-रानी का मन बहुत ही लग गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::802.english_translation: They then chanted the twelve-syllable mantra with love, and the king and queen’s minds became deeply fixed at the lotus feet of Vasudeva.
ramacharitamanas::802.translation_literal: द्वादस (twelve) / अच्छर (syllables) / मंत्र (mantra) / पुनि (again) / जपहिं (they chant) / सहित (with) / अनुराग (love) / बासुदेव (Vasudeva) / पद (feet) / पंकरुह (lotus) / दंपति (the couple) / मन (mind) / अति (very) / लाग (attached)
ramacharitamanas::802.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::802.essence: Love turns repetition into fixed devotion.
ramacharitamanas::802.simple_meaning: The king and queen repeated a sacred twelve-syllable mantra with love, and their hearts settled completely on Ram’s lotus feet.
ramacharitamanas::802.simple_insight: Love makes repetition become devotion, and devotion makes the heart steady.
ramacharitamanas::802.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the old king and queen have reached holy places and bathed in sacred water. Now they chant the twelve-syllable mantra with deep affection, and their minds turn fully toward Vasudeva, preparing for the austerity that follows.
ramacharitamanas::802.modern_relevance: You keep repeating a prayer, name, or line while walking alone before dawn. At first it feels like habit; then one day your mind is no longer scattered.
ramacharitamanas::802.insight: It shows how loving repetition gathers the mind and turns practice into surrender.

ramacharitamanas::803.verse_sanskrit: करहिं अहार साक फल कंदा। सुमिरहिं ब्रह्म सच्चिदानंदा॥ पुनि हरि हेतु करन तप लागे। बारि अधार मूल फल त्यागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::803.verse_hindi: वे साग, फल और कन्द का आहार करते थे और सच्चिदानंद ब्रह्म का स्मरण करते थे। फिर वे श्री हरि के लिए तप करने लगे और मूल-फल को त्यागकर केवल जल के आधार पर रहने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::803.english_translation: They ate leaves, fruits, and roots, and remembered the supreme reality, full of being, consciousness, and bliss. Then, for the sake of Hari, they began austerity, giving up roots and fruits and living only on water.
ramacharitamanas::803.translation_literal: करहिं (they ate) / अहार (food) / साक (leafy vegetables) / फल (fruits) / कंदा (roots and tubers) / सुमिरहिं (they remembered) / ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / सच्चिदानंदा (full of being, consciousness, and bliss) / पुनि (then) / हरि (Hari) / हेतु (for the sake of) / करन (doing) / तप (austerity) / लागे (they began) / बारि (water) / अधार (as support) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruits) / त्यागे (they gave up)
ramacharitamanas::803.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::803.essence: Devotion becomes real when comfort is willingly reduced.
ramacharitamanas::803.simple_meaning: They lived on simple food, kept remembering the supreme reality, and then took up harder austerity for Ram by giving up even roots and fruits.
ramacharitamanas::803.simple_insight: Real devotion often starts with small restraint and grows into a steadier, simpler life.
ramacharitamanas::803.detailed_meaning: The king and queen are already deep in devotion, moving through holy places with their bodies weakened by longing. Now their practice becomes stricter: they eat only what is simple, keep Ram in mind, and begin austerity that strips life down to water alone.
ramacharitamanas::803.modern_relevance: You clear the pantry after a hard month and decide to live simply for a while. The point is not punishment. It is making room for what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::803.insight: It shifts attention from comfort to disciplined remembrance, showing that devotion can reshape daily habits.

ramacharitamanas::804.verse_sanskrit: उर अभिलाष निरंतर होई। देखिअ नयन परम प्रभु सोई॥ अगुन अखंड अनंत अनादी। जेहि चिंतहिं परमारथबादी ॥
ramacharitamanas::804.verse_hindi: हृदय में निरंतर यही अभिलाषा हुआ करती कि हम (कैसे) उन परम प्रभु को आँखों से देखें, जो निर्गुण, अखंड, अनंत और अनादि हैं और परमार्थवादी (ब्रह्मज्ञानी, तत्त्ववेत्ता) लोग जिनका चिन्तन किया करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::804.english_translation: A constant longing lived in the heart: may we see that supreme Lord with our own eyes. He is without qualities, unbroken, endless, and beginningless, the one contemplative sages keep in mind.
ramacharitamanas::804.translation_literal: उर (in the heart) / अभिलाष (longing) / निरंतर (constantly) / होई (was) / देखिअ (may be seen) / नयन (with the eyes) / परम प्रभु (supreme Lord) / सोई (that one) / अगुन (without qualities) / अखंड (unbroken) / अनंत (endless) / अनादी (beginningless) / जेहि (whom) / चिंतहिं (contemplate) / परमारथबादी (those established in the highest truth)
ramacharitamanas::804.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::804.essence: True devotion wants direct sight, not just distant reverence.
ramacharitamanas::804.simple_meaning: The heart keeps wanting direct vision of the supreme Lord, who is beyond qualities, endless, and beyond beginning.
ramacharitamanas::804.simple_insight: A deeper longing can be holy in itself, not a weakness to suppress.
ramacharitamanas::804.detailed_meaning: King Dasharath and Queen Kaushalya have already turned to austerity and remembrance. Their practice now matures into one desire: to behold Ram directly. The verse shifts from discipline to yearning, showing devotion ripening into vision.
ramacharitamanas::804.modern_relevance: You finish meditation and still feel restless, not because you failed, but because the heart wants more than calm. It wants contact, not just technique.
ramacharitamanas::804.insight: It shifts devotion from ritual effort to a hunger for direct presence.

ramacharitamanas::805.verse_sanskrit: नेति नेति जेहि बेद निरूपा। निजानंद निरुपाधि अनूपा॥ संभु बिरंचि बिष्नु भगवाना। उपजहिं जासु अंस तें नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::805.verse_hindi: जिन्हें वेद 'नेति-नेति' (यह भी नहीं, यह भी नहीं) कहकर निरूपण करते हैं। जो आनंदस्वरूप, उपाधिरहित और अनुपम हैं एवं जिनके अंश से अनेक शिव, ब्रह्मा और विष्णु भगवान प्रकट होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::805.english_translation: The Vedas describe the supreme reality as "not this, not this." It is self-blissful, beyond all attributes, unmatched. From its partial expression arise the many forms of Shiva, Brahma, and Vishnu.
ramacharitamanas::805.translation_literal: नेति नेति (not this, not this) / जेहि (whom) / बेद (the Vedas) / निरूपा (describe) / निजानंद (self-bliss) / निरुपाधि (without limiting attributes) / अनूपा (matchless) / संभु (Shiva) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / बिष्नु (Vishnu) / भगवाना (the divine lords) / उपजहिं (arise) / जासु (whose) / अंस (partial expression) / तें (from) / नाना (many)
ramacharitamanas::805.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::805.essence: The source of all forms cannot be captured by any form.
ramacharitamanas::805.simple_meaning: The highest reality cannot be fully described by any name or concept. It is pure, attribute-free bliss, and even the great forms of Shiva, Brahma, and Vishnu come from a partial expression of it.
ramacharitamanas::805.simple_insight: You do not have to fit ultimate reality into a mental box. The mind relaxes when it stops trying to own the infinite.
ramacharitamanas::805.detailed_meaning: In the forest dialogue of Balkand, the sages are speaking of Ram in the highest terms. After longing to see the formless Lord, this verse says that the supreme reality lies beyond description, yet from it even Shiva, Brahma, and Vishnu emerge.
ramacharitamanas::805.modern_relevance: You keep trying to explain your deepest experience in a text thread, and every sentence feels too small. Some things are real precisely because they exceed your words.
ramacharitamanas::805.insight: It shifts the mind from defining the absolute to revering what cannot be contained.

ramacharitamanas::806.verse_sanskrit: ऐसेउ प्रभु सेवक बस अहई। भगत हेतु लीलातनु गहई॥ जौं यह बचन सत्य श्रुति भाषा। तौ हमार पूजिहि अभिलाषा ॥
ramacharitamanas::806.verse_hindi: ऐसे (महान) प्रभु भी सेवक के वश में हैं और भक्तों के लिए (दिव्य) लीला विग्रह धारण करते हैं। यदि वेदों में यह वचन सत्य कहा है, तो हमारी अभिलाषा भी अवश्य पूरी होगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::806.english_translation: Even such a Lord comes under the control of his devotee and takes a visible form for devotion. If this word of the Vedas is true, then our longing must also be fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::806.translation_literal: ऐसेउ (even such) / प्रभु (Lord) / सेवक (servant, devotee) / बस (under control) / अहई (is) / भगत (devotee) / हेतु (for the sake of) / लीलातनु (play-form, visible divine body) / गहई (takes, assumes) / जौं (if) / यह (this) / बचन (word) / सत्य (true) / श्रुति (heard revelation, Veda) / भाषा (spoken, stated) / तौ (then) / हमार (our) / पूजिहि (will be fulfilled, will be honored) / अभिलाषा (longing, desire)
ramacharitamanas::806.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::806.essence: The Lord answers devotion by becoming reachable.
ramacharitamanas::806.simple_meaning: The supreme Lord is said to answer devotion by taking form for devotees. That promise gives the speaker confidence that a long-held longing will be fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::806.simple_insight: Hope becomes steady when longing is joined to trust in the divine response.
ramacharitamanas::806.detailed_meaning: In the forest, saints speak of the formless supreme Lord and then turn to a daring hope: that same Lord becomes reachable for devotees. This verse is the emotional hinge between yearning and assurance.
ramacharitamanas::806.modern_relevance: You have waited through another night of prayer, grief, or uncertainty, wondering whether anything hears you. This verse answers with quiet confidence: devotion is not wasted; longing can meet response.
ramacharitamanas::806.insight: It shifts the mind from private longing to trusting that devotion can draw a real response.

ramacharitamanas::807.verse_sanskrit: एहि विधि बीते बरष षट सहस बारि आहार। संबत सप्त सहस्र पुनि रहे समीर अधार ॥
ramacharitamanas::807.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार जल का आहार (करके तप) करते छह हजार वर्ष बीत गए। फिर सात हजार वर्ष वे वायु के आधार पर रहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::807.english_translation: In this way, six thousand years passed on a diet of water. Then for seven thousand years more, they lived sustained by air.
ramacharitamanas::807.translation_literal: एहि विधि (in this way) / बीते (passed) / बरष (years) / षट (six) / सहस (thousand) / बारि (water) / आहार (food) / संबत (years) / सप्त (seven) / सहस्र (thousand) / पुनि (again) / रहे (remained) / समीर (air) / अधार (support)
ramacharitamanas::807.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::807.essence: Enduring restraint changes a person more than short intensity ever can.
ramacharitamanas::807.simple_meaning: They kept up severe austerity for thousands of years, first living on water, then on air.
ramacharitamanas::807.simple_insight: Real change is built by long restraint, not a burst of enthusiasm.
ramacharitamanas::807.detailed_meaning: The verse continues the account of a vast penance begun after the earlier praise of the supreme being. The ascetics do not stop at one hard phase; they deepen the restraint year after year, showing extreme discipline before the next step of the story.
ramacharitamanas::807.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone, then finally place it face down for ten minutes. Real discipline is not dramatic — it is repeated refusal, long enough to reshape you.
ramacharitamanas::807.insight: It shifts attention from quick effort to sustained self-mastery over time.

ramacharitamanas::808.verse_sanskrit: बरष सहस दस त्यागेउ सोऊ। ठाढ़े रहे एक पद दोऊ ॥ बिधि हरि हर तप देखि अपारा। मनु समीप आए बहु बारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::808.verse_hindi: दस हजार वर्ष तक उन्होंने वायु का आधार भी छोड़ दिया। दोनों एक पैर से खड़े रहे। उनका अपार तप देखकर ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और शिवजी कई बार मनुजी के पास आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::808.english_translation: For ten thousand years they gave up even support from the air. Both stood on one foot. Seeing their immense austerity, Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva came many times to Manu.
ramacharitamanas::808.translation_literal: बरष (years) / सहस (thousand) / दस (ten) / त्यागेउ (gave up) / सोऊ (that too) / ठाढ़े (standing) / रहे (remained) / एक (one) / पद (foot) / दोऊ (both) / बिधि (Brahma) / हरि (Vishnu) / हर (Shiva) / तप (austerity) / देखि (seeing) / अपारा (immeasurable) / मनु (Manu) / समीप (near) / आए (came) / बहु (many) / बारा (times)
ramacharitamanas::808.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::808.essence: Enduring discipline can draw the highest attention.
ramacharitamanas::808.simple_meaning: They kept up extreme austerity for ten thousand years, standing on one foot. Their discipline was so great that Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva came to Manu again and again.
ramacharitamanas::808.simple_insight: Steady discipline can become so powerful that even the highest powers take notice.
ramacharitamanas::808.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, Manu and Shatarupa are deep in austerity. They have already given up food and even air support. Now they stand on one foot for ten thousand years, and their extraordinary tapas draws repeated visits from Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::808.modern_relevance: You keep showing up before sunrise, long after the excitement is gone. No one claps. Still, the work changes you so completely that even your own standards feel different.
ramacharitamanas::808.insight: It shifts attention from short effort to sustained self-mastery that commands respect.

ramacharitamanas::809.verse_sanskrit: मागहु बर बहु भाँति लोभाए। परम धीर नहिं चलहिं चलाए॥ अस्थिमात्र होइ रहे सरीरा। तदपि मनाग मनहिं नहिं पीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::809.verse_hindi: उन्होंने इन्हें अनेक प्रकार से ललचाया और कहा कि कुछ वर माँगो। पर ये परम धैर्यवान (राजा-रानी अपने तप से किसी के) डिगाए नहीं डिगे। यद्यपि उनका शरीर हड्डियों का ढाँचा मात्र रह गया था, फिर भी उनके मन में जरा भी पीड़ा नहीं थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::809.english_translation: They tried many ways to tempt them and said, "Ask for a boon." But the steadfast pair could not be shaken. Though their bodies were reduced to little more than bones, their minds still felt no pain.
ramacharitamanas::809.translation_literal: मागहु (ask) / बर (boon) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / लोभाए (tempted) / परम धीर (utterly steadfast) / नहिं (not) / चलहिं (are shaken) / चलाए (by being shaken) ॥ / अस्थिमात्र (only bones) / होइ (having become) / रहे (remained) / सरीरा (the body) / तदपि (even so) / मनाग (slightest) / मनहिं (in the mind) / नहिं (not) / पीरा (pain) ॥
ramacharitamanas::809.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::809.essence: Temptation cannot move a mind rooted in tapas.
ramacharitamanas::809.simple_meaning: The divine beings tried to tempt the king and queen with boons, but they could not be shaken. Even when their bodies were nearly reduced to bones, they felt no pain in their minds.
ramacharitamanas::809.simple_insight: Real strength is staying unmoved when the body is exhausted and temptation is loud.
ramacharitamanas::809.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, the king and queen have endured extreme austerity for thousands of years. The divine beings try to tempt them into asking for rewards, but their resolve does not break. This verse shows the depth of their tapas before the blessing is finally given.
ramacharitamanas::809.modern_relevance: You are worn down after months of caring for a sick parent, yet a shortcut would betray what you stand for. Their steadiness shows what it means not to bend.
ramacharitamanas::809.insight: It shifts attention from reward-seeking to unshaken endurance under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::810.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु सर्बग्य दास निज जानी। गति अनन्य तापस नृप रानी॥ मागु मागु बरु भै नभ बानी। परम गभीर कृपामृत सानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::810.verse_hindi: सर्वज्ञ प्रभु ने अनन्य गति (आश्रय) वाले तपस्वी राजा-रानी को 'निज दास' जाना। तब परम गंभीर और कृपा रूपी अमृत से सनी हुई यह आकाशवाणी हुई कि 'वर माँगो' ॥
ramacharitamanas::810.english_translation: The all-knowing Lord recognized the ascetic king and queen as his own servants, devoted to a single refuge. Then a deep, nectar-like voice from the sky said, “Ask for a boon.”
ramacharitamanas::810.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / सर्बग्य (all-knowing) / दास (servant) / निज (own) / जानी (having known) / गति (refuge) / अनन्य (single, without another) / तापस (ascetic) / नृप (king) / रानी (queen) ॥ मागु (ask) / मागु (ask) / बरु (boon) / भै (became) / नभ (sky) / बानी (voice) / परम (supreme) / गभीर (deep) / कृपामृत (nectar of grace) / सानी (mixed with)
ramacharitamanas::810.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::810.essence: Single-minded devotion is recognized before it is rewarded.
ramacharitamanas::810.simple_meaning: Ram recognizes the king and queen as devoted servants who have no refuge but him. Then a voice from the sky invites them to ask for a boon.
ramacharitamanas::810.simple_insight: Being fully known by the divine feels like being finally seen and safely held.
ramacharitamanas::810.detailed_meaning: After years of severe penance, the king and queen stand before the result of their longing. Ram sees their single-minded devotion and claims them as his own. The sky then speaks with tender authority, opening the door for their wish to be granted.
ramacharitamanas::810.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for years with no guarantee anyone notices. Then, in one quiet moment, someone finally names your devotion and asks what you need.
ramacharitamanas::810.insight: It shifts the mind from striving for approval to trusting that sincere devotion is already seen.

ramacharitamanas::811.verse_sanskrit: मृतक जिआवनि गिरा सुहाई। श्रवन रंध्र होइ उर जब आई॥ हृष्ट पुष्ट तन भए सुहाए। मानहुँ अबहिं भवन ते आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::811.verse_hindi: मुर्दे को भी जिला देने वाली यह सुंदर वाणी कानों के छेदों से होकर जब हृदय में आई, तब राजा-रानी के शरीर ऐसे सुंदर और हृष्ट-पुष्ट हो गए, मानो अभी घर से आए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::811.english_translation: The beautiful speech that could revive the dead entered through the ears and reached the heart. Then the king and queen’s bodies became radiant and full of life, as if they had just come home.
ramacharitamanas::811.translation_literal: मृतक (dead) / जिआवनि (reviving) / गिरा (speech) / सुहाई (beautiful) / श्रवन (ears) / रंध्र (openings) / होइ (having become) / उर (heart) / जब (when) / आई (came) / हृष्ट (joyful) / पुष्ट (robust) / तन (bodies) / भए (became) / सुहाए (radiant) / मानहुँ (as if) / अबहिं (just now) / भवन (home) / ते (from) / आए (came)
ramacharitamanas::811.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::811.essence: Grace can revive a heart before it can explain itself.
ramacharitamanas::811.simple_meaning: The king and queen hear words so sweet they feel life return to them. Their grief lifts, and their bodies seem renewed.
ramacharitamanas::811.simple_insight: Tender words can restore what despair has drained away.
ramacharitamanas::811.detailed_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa have been worn down by years of tapas and longing. Now the divine voice reaches them, and the effect is immediate: the same bodies that had been austere and aged suddenly look fresh and alive. The moment shows how Ram's grace enters through hearing.
ramacharitamanas::811.modern_relevance: After a night of bad news, one calm voice on the phone changes everything. Your shoulders drop, your breathing returns, and the body remembers hope before the mind does.
ramacharitamanas::811.insight: It shifts attention from harshness to the healing power of sound and trust.

ramacharitamanas::812.verse_sanskrit: श्रवन सुधा सम बचन सुनि पुलक प्रफुल्लित गात। बोले मनु करि दंडवत प्रेम न हृदयँ समात ॥
ramacharitamanas::812.verse_hindi: कानों में अमृत के समान लगने वाले वचन सुनते ही उनका शरीर पुलकित और प्रफुल्लित हो गया। तब मनुजी दण्डवत करके बोले- प्रेम हृदय में समाता न था- ॥
ramacharitamanas::812.english_translation: Hearing words as sweet as nectar, their bodies thrilled with joy. Then Manu bowed and spoke, his heart too full of love to contain.
ramacharitamanas::812.translation_literal: श्रवन (ears) / सुधा सम (like nectar) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / पुलक (horripilation) / प्रफुल्लित (blossomed) / गात (body) / बोले (spoke) / मनु (Manu) / करि (having done) / दंडवत (prostration) / प्रेम (love) / न (not) / हृदयँ (in heart) / समात (contained)
ramacharitamanas::812.speaker: Manu
ramacharitamanas::812.essence: Love overflows when grace is finally heard.
ramacharitamanas::812.simple_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa hear Ram's gracious words and are overwhelmed with joy and reverence. Their love is so full that ordinary speech cannot hold it.
ramacharitamanas::812.simple_insight: Real devotion leaves no room for self-consciousness; the heart bows before the mind can explain.
ramacharitamanas::812.detailed_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa have just heard Ram answer them with boundless grace. The words land like nectar, their bodies tremble with joy, and Manu bows down in gratitude. This verse shows the immediate human response to divine kindness.
ramacharitamanas::812.modern_relevance: You finally hear the apology you never expected from someone you love. Your chest loosens, tears come, and you can only bow your head because gratitude is bigger than language.
ramacharitamanas::812.insight: It shifts the reader from analysis to reverent response: first receive, then bow.

ramacharitamanas::813.verse_sanskrit: सुनु सेवक सुरतरु सुरधेनू। बिधि हरि हर बंदित पद रेनू॥ सेवत सुलभ सकल सुखदायक। प्रनतपाल सचराचर नायक ॥
ramacharitamanas::813.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! सुनिए, आप सेवकों के लिए कल्पवृक्ष और कामधेनु हैं। आपके चरण रज की ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और शिवजी भी वंदना करते हैं। आप सेवा करने में सुलभ हैं तथा सब सुखों के देने वाले हैं। आप शरणागत के रक्षक और जड़-चेतन के स्वामी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::813.english_translation: Listen: for servants, you are the wish-fulfilling tree and the wish-fulfilling cow. Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva bow to the dust of your feet. You are easy to reach through service, giver of all happiness, protector of those who take refuge, and lord of all moving and unmoving beings.
ramacharitamanas::813.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / सेवक (for servants) / सुरतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / सुरधेनू (wish-fulfilling cow) / बिधि (Brahma) / हरि (Vishnu/Ram) / हर (Shiva) / बंदित (worshipped) / पद (feet) / रेनू (dust) / सेवत (through service) / सुलभ (easy to attain) / सकल (all) / सुखदायक (giver of happiness) / प्रनतपाल (protector of the surrendered) / सचराचर (moving and unmoving) / नायक (lord)
ramacharitamanas::813.speaker: Manu
ramacharitamanas::813.essence: Service makes the highest presence feel near.
ramacharitamanas::813.simple_meaning: Ram is the easiest refuge for a devoted servant. He gives joy, protects those who surrender, and is honored even by Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::813.simple_insight: Devotion is not small or weak; it opens the door to the greatest protection and grace.
ramacharitamanas::813.detailed_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa have just heard Ram's answering words and are overwhelmed. Manu now praises Ram as the giver of all blessings, easy to reach through service, and the protector of all who take refuge. The verse lifts Ram above every cosmic power.
ramacharitamanas::813.modern_relevance: You keep helping someone who never seems to notice, and then one day they stand by you when it matters most. This verse says that real service is never wasted.
ramacharitamanas::813.insight: It shifts the mind from bargaining with the divine to serving with trust, knowing refuge itself is the reward.

ramacharitamanas::814.verse_sanskrit: जौं अनाथ हित हम पर नेहू। तौ प्रसन्न होई यह बर देहू॥ जोसरूप बस सिव मन माहीं। जेहिं कारन मुनि जतन कराहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::814.verse_hindi: हे अनाथों का कल्याण करने वाले! यदि हम लोगों पर आपका स्नेह है, तो प्रसन्न होकर यह वर दीजिए कि आपका जो स्वरूप शिवजी के मन में बसता है और जिस (की प्राप्ति) के लिए मुनि लोग यत्न करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::814.english_translation: If you truly love us, O protector of the helpless, then be pleased and grant this boon: let us behold the form that dwells in Shiva's heart and that sages strive to attain.
ramacharitamanas::814.translation_literal: जौं (if) / अनाथ (the helpless) / हित (for the welfare of) / हम (us) / पर (on) / नेहू (affection) / तौ (then) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / होई (becoming) / यह (this) / बर (boon) / देहू (give) / जो (which) / सरूप (form) / बस (dwells) / सिव (Shiva) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / जेहिं (for which) / कारन (because) / मुनि (sages) / जतन (effort) / कराहीं (make)
ramacharitamanas::814.speaker: Manu
ramacharitamanas::814.essence: True devotion asks for vision, not advantage.
ramacharitamanas::814.simple_meaning: Manu asks Ram to show the form that even Shiva holds in his heart and that sages seek through effort.
ramacharitamanas::814.simple_insight: Longing becomes clear when it asks for the highest vision, not comfort.
ramacharitamanas::814.detailed_meaning: Manu has already praised Ram as the giver of all blessings. Now, in the middle of his prayer, he asks for the rarest gift: a direct vision of Ram's form, the same form cherished by Shiva and sought by sages. The moment turns devotion into a request for revelation.
ramacharitamanas::814.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you deeply admire, and you do not ask for favors or shortcuts. You ask for the one thing that matters most: to truly see who they are.
ramacharitamanas::814.insight: It shifts prayer from asking for benefits to asking for direct vision of the divine form.

ramacharitamanas::815.verse_sanskrit: जो भुसुंडि मन मानस हंसा। सगुन अगुन जेहि निगम प्रसंसा॥ देखहिं हम सो रूप भरि लोचन। कृपा करहु प्रनतारति मोचन ॥
ramacharitamanas::815.verse_hindi: जो काकभुशुण्डि के मन रूपी मान सरोवर में विहार करने वाला हंस है, सगुण और निर्गुण कहकर वेद जिसकी प्रशंसा करते हैं, हे शरणागत के दुःख मिटाने वाले प्रभो! ऐसी कृपा कीजिए कि हम उसी रूप को नेत्र भरकर देखें ॥
ramacharitamanas::815.english_translation: O Lord, who dwells in the swan-like mind of Kakabhushundi, whom the Vedas praise as both with form and without form, grant us your grace so that we may behold that form with our eyes full of longing.
ramacharitamanas::815.translation_literal: जो (who) / भुसुंडि (Bhushundi) / मन (mind) / मानस (mind-lake) / हंसा (swan) / सगुन (with form) / अगुन (without form) / जेहि (whom) / निगम (Vedas) / प्रसंसा (praise) / देखहिं (may see) / हम (we) / सो (that) / रूप (form) / भरि (full) / लोचन (eyes) / कृपा (grace) / करहु (do) / प्रनतारति (distress of the surrendered) / मोचन (remover)
ramacharitamanas::815.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::815.essence: Trust seeks a face, not an idea.
ramacharitamanas::815.simple_meaning: The speaker asks to see Ram’s divine form directly, with eyes full of longing, and praises him as beyond ordinary categories of form and formlessness.
ramacharitamanas::815.simple_insight: There is comfort in wanting to see what the heart already trusts.
ramacharitamanas::815.detailed_meaning: In the sacred dialogue of Balkand, Tulsidas turns to Ram with a devotee’s longing. He praises Ram as the one the Vedas describe in both personal and formless ways, then asks for the grace to see that beloved form fully.
ramacharitamanas::815.modern_relevance: You scroll past a thousand images, but one face still matters more than all of them. This verse names that ache: not information, but a clear, loving glimpse of what you trust.
ramacharitamanas::815.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract belief to direct longing for presence.

ramacharitamanas::816.verse_sanskrit: दंपति बचन परम प्रिय लागे। मृदुल बिनीत प्रेम रस पागे॥ भगत बछल प्रभु कृपानिधाना। बिस्वबास प्रगटे भगवाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::816.verse_hindi: राजा-रानी के कोमल, विनययुक्त और प्रेमरस में पगे हुए वचन भगवान को बहुत ही प्रिय लगे। भक्तवत्सल, कृपानिधान, सम्पूर्ण विश्व के निवास स्थान (या समस्त विश्व में व्यापक), सर्वसमर्थ भगवान प्रकट हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::816.english_translation: The king and queen’s gentle, humble, love-filled words were dear to the Lord. Compassionate to devotees, a treasure of grace, the all-pervading Lord appeared.
ramacharitamanas::816.translation_literal: दंपति (the couple) / बचन (words) / परम प्रिय (most dear) / लागे (became) / मृदुल (gentle) / बिनीत (humble) / प्रेम रस (the nectar of love) / पागे (soaked) / भगत बछल (devotee-loving) / प्रभु (Lord) / कृपानिधाना (treasure of grace) / बिस्वबास (world-abode / all-pervading) / प्रगटे (appeared) / भगवाना (the divine Lord)
ramacharitamanas::816.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::816.essence: Humility and love draw the divine into view.
ramacharitamanas::816.simple_meaning: Gentle, humble words filled with love please the divine, and the beloved Lord appears to those who speak with devotion.
ramacharitamanas::816.simple_insight: Softness and sincerity can open what force never can.
ramacharitamanas::816.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar setting, the king and queen speak with humility and love. Their prayer delights Ram, who is tender toward devotees and full of grace, and he reveals himself in response to their heartfelt words.
ramacharitamanas::816.modern_relevance: You finally say what matters without posturing or pressure. The other person softens, because honest warmth reaches places argument never touches.
ramacharitamanas::816.insight: It shifts attention from performance to sincerity: devotion opens the way for revelation.

ramacharitamanas::817.verse_sanskrit: नील सरोरुह नील मनि नील नीरधर स्याम। लाजहिं तन सोभा निरखि कोटि कोटि सत काम ॥
ramacharitamanas::817.verse_hindi: भगवान के नीले कमल, नीलमणि और नीले (जलयुक्त) मेघ के समान (कोमल, प्रकाशमय और सरस) श्यामवर्ण (चिन्मय) शरीर की शोभा देखकर करोड़ों कामदेव भी लजा जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::817.english_translation: Seeing the beauty of the divine blue body, even millions of love-gods feel ashamed.
ramacharitamanas::817.translation_literal: नील (blue) / सरोरुह (lotus) / नील (blue) / मनि (jewel) / नील (blue) / नीरधर (cloud) / स्याम (dark-blue) / लाजहिं (feel ashamed) / तन (body) / सोभा (beauty) / निरखि (seeing) / कोटि कोटि (countless) / सत काम (love-gods)
ramacharitamanas::817.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::817.essence: True beauty makes desire bow in silence.
ramacharitamanas::817.simple_meaning: Ram's blue form is so beautiful that even countless love-gods lose their pride before it.
ramacharitamanas::817.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, the king and queen's loving words have pleased Ram, and the poem now lingers on his form. His blue radiance is compared to lotus, sapphire, and rainclouds, not to describe fashion but to show divine beauty overwhelming all ordinary desire.
ramacharitamanas::817.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone so calm and radiant that your restless wanting suddenly feels small. The mind falls quiet because it has met something greater than appetite.
ramacharitamanas::817.insight: It shifts attention from attraction as craving to beauty as reverence.

ramacharitamanas::818.verse_sanskrit: सरद मयंक बदन छबि सींवा। चारु कपोल चिबुक दर ग्रीवा॥ अधर अरुन रद सुंदर नासा। बिधु कर निकर बिनिंदक हासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::818.verse_hindi: उनका मुख शरद (पूर्णिमा) के चन्द्रमा के समान छबि की सीमास्वरूप था। गाल और ठोड़ी बहुत सुंदर थे, गला शंख के समान (त्रिरेखायुक्त, चढ़ाव-उतार वाला) था। लाल होठ, दाँत और नाक अत्यन्त सुंदर थे। हँसी चन्द्रमा की किरणावली को नीचा दिखाने वाली थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::818.english_translation: His face shone like the autumn moon. His cheeks, chin, neck, lips, teeth, nose, and smile were all exquisitely beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::818.translation_literal: सरद (autumn) / मयंक (moon) / बदन (face) / छबि (beauty) / सींवा (boundary, limit) / चारु (beautiful) / कपोल (cheeks) / चिबुक (chin) / दर (like) / ग्रीवा (neck) / अधर (lips) / अरुन (red) / रद (teeth) / सुंदर (beautiful) / नासा (nose) / बिधु (moon) / कर (rays, hands) / निकर (group) / बिनिंदक (surpassing, putting to shame) / हासा (smile)
ramacharitamanas::818.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::818.essence: His beauty exceeds every image used to describe it.
ramacharitamanas::818.simple_meaning: His face is described as moonlike and every feature as beautifully formed, with a smile brighter than moonbeams.
ramacharitamanas::818.simple_insight: Beauty can quiet the mind before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::818.detailed_meaning: The scene is still focused on Ram's divine form as he stands revealed to the assembled king and queen. After the first glimpse of his radiance, the poet lingers on each feature, showing that even ordinary beauty language fails to contain him.
ramacharitamanas::818.modern_relevance: You catch someone’s face in soft evening light and forget your next sentence. Some presence needs no introduction; it rearranges the room by simply being seen.
ramacharitamanas::818.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary description to reverent seeing, where every feature becomes a sign of grace.

ramacharitamanas::819.verse_sanskrit: नव अंबुज अंबक छबि नीकी। चितवनि ललित भावँतीजी की॥ भृकुटि मनोज चाप छबि हारी। तिलक ललाट पटल दुतिकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::819.verse_hindi: नेत्रों की छवि नए (खिले हुए) कमल के समान बड़ी सुंदर थी। मनोहर चितवन जी को बहुत प्यारी लगती थी। टेढ़ी भौंहें कामदेव के धनुष की शोभा को हरने वाली थीं। ललाट पटल पर प्रकाशमय तिलक था ॥
ramacharitamanas::819.english_translation: His eyes were beautifully like new lotus blossoms. His graceful glance delighted everyone. His arched brows outshone Cupid's bow. A radiant tilak glowed on his forehead.
ramacharitamanas::819.translation_literal: नव (new) / अंबुज (lotus) / अंबक (eyes) / छबि (beauty) / नीकी (beautiful) / चितवनि (glance) / ललित (graceful) / भावँतीजी (delighting) / की (of) / भृकुटि (brows) / मनोज (Cupid) / चाप (bow) / छबि (beauty) / हारी (outshining) / तिलक (tilak mark) / ललाट (forehead) / पटल (surface) / दुतिकारी (radiant)
ramacharitamanas::819.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::819.essence: Ram's presence is so beautiful that even a glance feels like grace.
ramacharitamanas::819.simple_meaning: His face is described in beautiful detail: lotus-like eyes, a charming glance, arched brows, and a glowing tilak on the forehead.
ramacharitamanas::819.simple_insight: Beauty can steady the mind before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::819.detailed_meaning: The poem is lingering on Ram's appearance in the Sita-swayamvar scene. After the earlier lines on his face and smile, this verse adds the eyes, brows, and tilak, building a full vision of his divine beauty before the story moves on.
ramacharitamanas::819.modern_relevance: You catch sight of someone across a crowded room and everything in you goes quiet. Before they speak, their presence already changes the atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::819.insight: It shifts attention from plot to presence, letting beauty itself carry the moment.

ramacharitamanas::820.verse_sanskrit: कुंडल मकर मुकुट सिर भ्राजा। कुटिल केस जनु मधुप समाजा॥ उर श्रीबत्स रुचिर बनमाला। पदिक हार भूषन मनिजाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::820.verse_hindi: कानों में मकराकृत (मछली के आकार के) कुंडल और सिर पर मुकुट सुशोभित था। टेढ़े (घुँघराले) काले बाल ऐसे सघन थे, मानो भौंरों के झुंड हों। हृदय पर श्रीवत्स, सुंदर वनमाला, रत्नजड़ित हार और मणियों के आभूषण सुशोभित थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::820.english_translation: Earrings shaped like makara shone on the ears, and a crown on the head. The dark, curling hair clustered like a swarm of bees. On the chest shone the Srivatsa mark, a lovely forest garland, jeweled necklaces, and ornaments set with gems.
ramacharitamanas::820.translation_literal: कुंडल (earrings) / मकर (makara-shaped) / मुकुट (crown) / सिर (head) / भ्राजा (shone) / कुटिल (curly) / केस (hair) / जनु (as if) / मधुप (bees) / समाजा (swarm) / उर (chest) / श्रीबत्स (Srivatsa mark) / रुचिर (lovely) / बनमाला (forest garland) / पदिक (footed/jewelled) / हार (necklace) / भूषन (ornaments) / मनिजाला (set with gems)
ramacharitamanas::820.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::820.essence: Ram’s beauty turns every ornament into a sign of presence.
ramacharitamanas::820.simple_meaning: The verse describes Ram’s divine beauty and ornaments: earrings, crown, curly hair, the Srivatsa mark, garland, necklace, and jeweled adornments.
ramacharitamanas::820.simple_insight: Beauty here is not decoration alone; it feels like sacred presence made visible.
ramacharitamanas::820.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, the narrator keeps painting Ram’s form piece by piece. After the face and eyes, this verse lingers on the crown, earrings, hair, chest mark, garland, and jewels, deepening the image of a prince whose beauty itself draws reverence.
ramacharitamanas::820.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone entering a room, and the whole atmosphere changes. Not because of display, but because presence can make ornament feel secondary.
ramacharitamanas::820.insight: It trains attention to see radiance as character made visible, not mere appearance.

ramacharitamanas::821.verse_sanskrit: केहरि कंधर चारु जनेऊ। बाहु बिभूषन सुंदर तेऊ॥ मकरि कर सरिस सुभग भुजदंडा। कटि निषंग कर सर कोदंडा ॥
ramacharitamanas::821.verse_hindi: सिंह की सी गर्दन थी, सुंदर जनेऊ था। भुजाओं में जो गहने थे, वे भी सुंदर थे। हाथी की सूँड के समान (उतार-चढ़ाव वाले) सुंदर भुजदंड थे। कमर में तरकस और हाथ में बाण और धनुष (शोभा पा रहे) थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::821.english_translation: The neck was like a lion's, and the sacred thread was beautiful. The ornaments on the arms were lovely. The upper arms were graceful like an elephant's trunk. A quiver hung at the waist, and bow and arrows shone in the hand.
ramacharitamanas::821.translation_literal: केहरि (lion) / कंधर (neck) / चारु (beautiful) / जनेऊ (sacred thread) / बाहु (arms) / बिभूषन (ornaments) / सुंदर (beautiful) / तेऊ (those too) / मकरि (crocodile) / कर (hand) / सरिस (like) / सुभग (graceful, lovely) / भुजदंडा (upper arms) / कटि (waist) / निषंग (quiver) / कर (hand) / सर (arrows) / कोदंडा (bow)
ramacharitamanas::821.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::821.essence: Grace and power can live in the same body.
ramacharitamanas::821.simple_meaning: The verse describes Ram's graceful body and the weapons and ornaments that adorned him.
ramacharitamanas::821.simple_insight: Beauty and strength are joined together here, not set against each other.
ramacharitamanas::821.detailed_meaning: The scene stays on Ram's form during the Sita-swayamvar. After his face and crown are described, the poet moves to his neck, sacred thread, arms, waist, bow, and arrows. The point is not action yet, but the overwhelming presence of the prince before the contest begins.
ramacharitamanas::821.modern_relevance: You notice someone enter the room and everything about them feels composed: posture, clothes, and readiness all match. Nothing is wasted, nothing is exaggerated.
ramacharitamanas::821.insight: It trains attention to see dignity as harmony of appearance, bearing, and readiness.

ramacharitamanas::822.verse_sanskrit: तड़ित बिनिंदक पीत पट उदर रेख बर तीनि। नाभि मनोहर लेति जनु जमुन भँवर छबि छीनि ॥
ramacharitamanas::822.verse_hindi: (स्वर्ण-वर्ण का प्रकाशमय) पीताम्बर बिजली को लजाने वाला था। पेट पर सुंदर तीन रेखाएँ (त्रिवली) थीं। नाभि ऐसी मनोहर थी, मानो यमुनाजी के भँवरों की छबि को छीने लेती हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::822.english_translation: The shining yellow cloth outshone lightning. Three graceful lines marked the belly. The navel was so lovely it seemed to steal the beauty of Yamuna's whirlpools.
ramacharitamanas::822.translation_literal: तड़ित (lightning) / बिनिंदक (shaming) / पीत पट (yellow cloth) / उदर (belly) / रेख (lines) / बर (graceful) / तीनि (three) / नाभि (navel) / मनोहर (lovely) / लेति (takes) / जनु (as if) / जमुन (Yamuna) / भँवर (whirlpools) / छबि (beauty) / छीनि (steals)
ramacharitamanas::822.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::822.essence: Even Ram's smallest features are radiant enough to eclipse nature's beauty.
ramacharitamanas::822.simple_meaning: Ram's body is described as radiant and beautiful: his yellow garment shines like lightning, his belly has three graceful lines, and his navel is so lovely it seems to surpass the beauty of the Yamuna's whirlpools.
ramacharitamanas::822.simple_insight: Beauty here is not decoration; it draws the mind toward reverence.
ramacharitamanas::822.detailed_meaning: The poet is still describing Ram's divine form in the Sita-swayamvar scene. After the crown, curls, ornaments, and arms, the vision moves to his waist and navel, building the sense that every part of Ram's body is perfect and sacred.
ramacharitamanas::822.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone walking into a room and everything else fades for a second. The verse names that rare presence that doesn't ask for attention but quietly takes it.
ramacharitamanas::822.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary appearance to form as a carrier of devotion.

ramacharitamanas::823.verse_sanskrit: पद राजीव बरनि नहिं जाहीं। मुनि मन मधुप बसहिं जेन्ह माहीं॥ बाम भाग सोभति अनुकूला। आदिसक्ति छबिनिधि जगमूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::823.verse_hindi: जिनमें मुनियों के मन रूपी भौंरे बसते हैं, भगवान के उन चरणकमलों का तो वर्णन ही नहीं किया जा सकता। भगवान के बाएँ भाग में सदा अनुकूल रहने वाली, शोभा की राशि जगत की मूलकारण रूपा आदि शक्ति श्री जानकीजी सुशोभित हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::823.english_translation: The lotus feet cannot be described. Munis live in the honey of their minds there. On his left side shines the ever-auspicious one, the original power, the source of the universe, Sita.
ramacharitamanas::823.translation_literal: पद (feet) / राजीव (lotus) / बरनि (described) / नहिं (not) / जाहीं (go) / मुनि (sages) / मन (mind) / मधुप (bee) / बसहिं (reside) / जेन्ह (in which) / माहीं (within)॥ / बाम (left) / भाग (side) / सोभति (shines) / अनुकूला (favourable / ever-kind) / आदिसक्ति (original power) / छबिनिधि (treasure of beauty) / जगमूला (root of the world)॥
ramacharitamanas::823.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::823.essence: Ram’s presence draws the mind home, and Sita completes his divine radiance.
ramacharitamanas::823.simple_meaning: Ram's feet are beyond description, and sages rest their minds on them. Beside him shines Sita, the original power and source of the world.
ramacharitamanas::823.simple_insight: Devotion finds a resting place, and beauty becomes more than form — it becomes the center of the world.
ramacharitamanas::823.detailed_meaning: In the opening vision of Ram's divine form, the poet lingers on what cannot be fully spoken: his lotus feet, where sages place their minds like bees in honey. Then Sita appears at his left, not as ornament but as the original power that completes the sacred image.
ramacharitamanas::823.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence calms a crowded room, and everyone around them naturally settles. The mind stops chasing and simply rests. That is the kind of still beauty this verse points to.
ramacharitamanas::823.insight: It shifts attention from outward description to inward devotion, showing that reverence is where the mind belongs.

ramacharitamanas::824.verse_sanskrit: जासु अंस उपजहिं गुनखानी। अगनित लच्छि उमा ब्रह्मानी॥ भृकुटि बिलास जासु जग होई। राम बाम दिसि सीता सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::824.verse_hindi: जिनके अंश से गुणों की खान अगणित लक्ष्मी, पार्वती और ब्रह्माणी (त्रिदेवों की शक्तियाँ) उत्पन्न होती हैं तथा जिनकी भौंह के इशारे से ही जगत की रचना हो जाती है, वही (भगवान की स्वरूपा शक्ति) श्री सीताजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी की बाईं ओर स्थित हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::824.english_translation: From whose power arise countless Lakshmis, Parvati, and Brahmani, and by whose brow's play the world comes into being, that very divine power, Sita, stands on Ram's left.
ramacharitamanas::824.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / अंस (power or portion) / उपजहिं (arise) / गुनखानी (storehouse of qualities) / अगनित (countless) / लच्छि (Lakshmi) / उमा (Parvati) / ब्रह्मानी (Brahmani) / भृकुटि (brow) / बिलास (play or movement) / जासु (whose) / जग (world) / होई (comes into being) / राम (Ram) / बाम दिसि (left side) / सीता (Sita) / सोई (that very one)
ramacharitamanas::824.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::824.essence: The power behind creation stands beside Ram as Sita.
ramacharitamanas::824.simple_meaning: Sita is shown as the divine power of Ram. She is not just beside him; she is the force from which greatness, creation, and beauty emerge.
ramacharitamanas::824.simple_insight: It invites reverence for the power that stands quietly beside greatness and makes greatness possible.
ramacharitamanas::824.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, Tulsidas pauses before the marriage moment to reveal Sita's cosmic stature. She is described as the power from which countless divine forms arise and by whose slightest movement the world unfolds, yet she stands at Ram's left in loving presence.
ramacharitamanas::824.modern_relevance: At a wedding, everyone admires the groom's entrance, but the room changes when the bride arrives. This verse reminds you that quiet presence can carry the deepest power.
ramacharitamanas::824.insight: It shifts attention from visible status to the hidden power that supports and completes it.

ramacharitamanas::825.verse_sanskrit: छबिसमुद्र हरि रूप बिलोकी। एकटक रहे नयन पट रोकी॥ चितवहिं सादर रूप अनूपा। तृप्ति न मानहिं मनु सतरूपा ॥
ramacharitamanas::825.verse_hindi: शोभा के समुद्र श्री हरि के रूप को देखकर मनु-शतरूपा नेत्रों के पट (पलकें) रोके हुए एकटक (स्तब्ध) रह गए। उस अनुपम रूप को वे आदर सहित देख रहे थे और देखते-देखते अघाते ही न थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::825.english_translation: Seeing Hari’s radiant form, Manu and Shatarupa stood fixed, their eyes unblinking. With reverence, they kept gazing at the incomparable form and never felt satisfied.
ramacharitamanas::825.translation_literal: छबिसमुद्र (ocean of beauty) / हरि (Hari) / रूप (form) / बिलोकी (seeing) / एकटक (fixedly) / रहे (remained) / नयन (eyes) / पट (curtain, eyelids) / रोकी (stopped) / चितवहिं (they gaze) / सादर (with reverence) / रूप (form) / अनूपा (matchless) / तृप्ति (satisfaction) / न (not) / मानहिं (consider) / मनु (Manu) / सतरूपा (Shatarupa)
ramacharitamanas::825.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::825.essence: True beauty stills the eyes and leaves desire satisfied by seeing.
ramacharitamanas::825.simple_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa see Ram’s beautiful form and cannot look away. Their reverent gaze never feels complete.
ramacharitamanas::825.simple_insight: Some beauty does not distract you — it deepens attention until the heart feels full.
ramacharitamanas::825.detailed_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa stand before Ram in awe. His beauty holds their eyes still, and reverence keeps them looking without fatigue. This is not a passing glance but the beginning of devotion through direct seeing.
ramacharitamanas::825.modern_relevance: You open a photo and keep staring longer than you meant to. Not because it flatters you, but because something in it feels larger than ordinary seeing.
ramacharitamanas::825.insight: It shifts attention from consuming an image to reverently receiving presence.

ramacharitamanas::826.verse_sanskrit: हरष बिबस तन दसा भुलानी। परे दंड इव गहि पद पानी॥ सिर परसे प्रभु निज कर कंजा। तुरत उठाए करुनापुंजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::826.verse_hindi: आनंद के अधिक वश में हो जाने के कारण उन्हें अपने देह की सुधि भूल गई। वे हाथों से भगवान के चरण पकड़कर दण्ड की तरह (सीधे) भूमि पर गिर पड़े। कृपा की राशि प्रभु ने अपने करकमलों से उनके मस्तकों का स्पर्श किया और उन्हें तुरंत ही उठा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::826.english_translation: Overwhelmed with joy, they forgot their bodies. Grasping the Lord's feet, they fell like sticks. The Lord touched their heads with his lotus hands and lifted them up at once.
ramacharitamanas::826.translation_literal: हरष (joy) / बिबस (overpowered) / तन (body) / दसा (state) / भुलानी (forgot) / परे (fell) / दंड इव (like a stick) / गहि (grasping) / पद पानी (feet and hands) / सिर (head) / परसे (touched) / प्रभु (Lord) / निज (own) / कर कंजा (lotus hands) / तुरत (at once) / उठाए (lifted) / करुनापुंजा (mass of compassion)
ramacharitamanas::826.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::826.essence: Joy before Ram dissolves the self and draws forth instant compassion.
ramacharitamanas::826.simple_meaning: Overjoyed, they lost awareness of their bodies, fell at Ram's feet, and were gently lifted up by his compassionate touch.
ramacharitamanas::826.simple_insight: Deep devotion can make you forget yourself, and compassion meets that surrender immediately.
ramacharitamanas::826.detailed_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa stand before Ram in awe. Joy overwhelms them, their bodies go limp, and they fall at his feet. Ram responds not with distance, but with tenderness, lifting them at once.
ramacharitamanas::826.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you have admired for years, and your voice catches. In that moment, real warmth doesn't keep its distance — it reaches down and steadies you.
ramacharitamanas::826.insight: It shows how surrender is answered by immediate grace, not delay or judgment.

ramacharitamanas::827.verse_sanskrit: बोले कृपानिधान पुनि अति प्रसन्न मोहि जानि। मागहु बर जोइ भाव मन महादानि अनुमानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::827.verse_hindi: फिर कृपानिधान भगवान बोले- मुझे अत्यन्त प्रसन्न जानकर और बड़ा भारी दानी मानकर, जो मन को भाए वही वर माँग लो ॥
ramacharitamanas::827.english_translation: Then the Lord of compassion, knowing me to be greatly pleased, said: ask for whatever boon your heart desires, thinking me a great giver.
ramacharitamanas::827.translation_literal: बोले (spoke) / कृपानिधान (treasure of compassion) / पुनि (again) / अति (very) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / मोहि (me) / जानि (knowing) / मागहु (ask) / बर (boon) / जोइ (whatever) / भाव (desires) / मन (heart) / महादानि (great giver) / अनुमानि (thinking)
ramacharitamanas::827.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::827.simple_meaning: Ram, pleased by the sight of his devotees, invites them to ask for any boon their hearts want.
ramacharitamanas::827.simple_insight: Love opens the door before anyone even speaks.
ramacharitamanas::827.detailed_meaning: Manu and Shatarupa have just stood transfixed before Ram's radiant form. Seeing their devotion and joy, Ram speaks kindly and offers them any boon they wish. The moment turns wonder into intimate grace.
ramacharitamanas::827.modern_relevance: You finally hear praise from someone you deeply respect, and they ask what would make you happiest. The moment feels bigger than the request — it feels like being seen.
ramacharitamanas::827.insight: It shifts devotion from silent awe to open asking, showing that grace welcomes honest desire.

ramacharitamanas::828.verse_sanskrit: सुनि प्रभु बचन जोरि जुग पानी। धरि धीरजु बोली मृदु बानी॥ नाथ देखि पद कमल तुम्हारे। अब पूरे सब काम हमारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::828.verse_hindi: प्रभु के वचन सुनकर, दोनों हाथ जोड़कर और धीरज धरकर राजा ने कोमल वाणी कही- हे नाथ! आपके चरणकमलों को देखकर अब हमारी सारी मनःकामनाएँ पूरी हो गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::828.english_translation: Hearing the Lord's words, he folded both hands, gathered his courage, and spoke softly: "Lord, seeing your lotus feet, all our wishes are now fulfilled."
ramacharitamanas::828.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु (Lord) / बचन (words) / जोरि (joining) / जुग (both) / पानी (hands) / धरि (holding) / धीरजु (courage) / बोली (spoke) / मृदु (soft) / बानी (speech) / नाथ (Lord) / देखि (seeing) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / तुम्हारे (your) / अब (now) / पूरे (fulfilled) / सब (all) / काम (wishes) / हमारे (our)
ramacharitamanas::828.speaker: King Janaka
ramacharitamanas::828.essence: Seeing Ram is enough; every other wish falls away.
ramacharitamanas::828.simple_meaning: Janaka hears Ram's words, bows with folded hands, and says that simply seeing Ram's feet has fulfilled every desire.
ramacharitamanas::828.simple_insight: Real fulfillment arrives when reverence replaces craving.
ramacharitamanas::828.detailed_meaning: At the Sita-swayamvar, Janaka has just heard Ram speak. Overwhelmed, he folds his hands and answers gently. The sight of Ram's feet is enough for him; the moment turns from ceremony into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::828.modern_relevance: You finally meet the person you have admired from afar. The meeting itself feels complete — no extra reward, no bigger moment needed.
ramacharitamanas::828.insight: It shifts desire from getting something from the divine to being satisfied by presence alone.

ramacharitamanas::829.verse_sanskrit: एक लालसा बड़ि उर माहीं। सुगम अगम कहि जाति सो नाहीं॥ तुम्हहि देत अति सुगम गोसाईं। अगम लाग मोहि निज कृपनाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::829.verse_hindi: फिर भी मन में एक बड़ी लालसा है। उसका पूरा होना सहज भी है और अत्यन्त कठिन भी, इसी से उसे कहते नहीं बनता। हे स्वामी! आपके लिए तो उसका पूरा करना बहुत सहज है, पर मुझे अपनी कृपणता (दीनता) के कारण वह अत्यन्त कठिन मालूम होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::829.english_translation: Still, one great longing lives in my heart. It is called both easy and hard, so it cannot be spoken plainly. O Lord, for you it is very easy to grant, but my own meanness makes it seem very hard.
ramacharitamanas::829.translation_literal: एक (one) / लालसा (longing) / बड़ि (great) / उर (heart) / माहीं (within) / सुगम (easy) / अगम (hard-to-reach) / कहि (said) / जाति (goes) / सो (that) / नाहीं (not) / तुम्हहि (to you) / देत (giving) / अति (very) / सुगम (easy) / गोसाईं (O Lord) / अगम (hard) / लाग (seems) / मोहि (to me) / निज (own) / कृपनाईं (miserliness, smallness)
ramacharitamanas::829.speaker: King Janaka
ramacharitamanas::829.essence: Humility can make the easiest gift feel impossible to ask for.
ramacharitamanas::829.simple_meaning: The speaker has one deep wish, but feels too small to ask for it clearly. Ram could grant it easily; the obstacle is the speaker's own humility and hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::829.simple_insight: There is tenderness in wanting something deeply yet feeling unworthy to ask for it.
ramacharitamanas::829.detailed_meaning: Janaka stands before Ram after receiving permission to ask for a boon. He admits one deep desire has stayed in his heart, but his own modesty makes it hard to voice. The moment turns on the gap between Ram's generosity and the speaker's self-doubt.
ramacharitamanas::829.modern_relevance: You finally get a chance to ask for help from someone generous, but your throat tightens. The request feels simple, and your pride makes it impossible. This verse knows that hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::829.insight: It shifts the mind from entitlement to humble asking, while still trusting that the giver is able.

ramacharitamanas::830.verse_sanskrit: जथा दरिद्र बिबुधतरु पाई। बहु संपति मागत सकुचाई॥ तासु प्रभाउ जान नहिं सोई। तथा हृदयँ मम संसय होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::830.verse_hindi: जैसे कोई दरिद्र कल्पवृक्ष को पाकर भी अधिक द्रव्य माँगने में संकोच करता है, क्योंकि वह उसके प्रभाव को नहीं जानता, वैसे ही मेरे हृदय में संशय हो रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::830.english_translation: Like a poor man who finds a wish-fulfilling tree but still hesitates to ask for more, not knowing its power, so doubt has arisen in my heart.
ramacharitamanas::830.translation_literal: जथा (like) / दरिद्र (poor) / बिबुधतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / पाई (having found) / बहु (many) / संपति (wealth) / मागत (asking for) / सकुचाई (hesitates) / तासु (its) / प्रभाउ (power) / जान (knows) / नहिं (not) / सोई (that one) / तथा (so) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / मम (my) / संसय (doubt) / होई (arises)
ramacharitamanas::830.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::830.essence: Doubt makes even abundance feel inaccessible.
ramacharitamanas::830.simple_meaning: A person may stand before a source of limitless blessing and still hesitate, simply because the source is not fully understood. That hesitation is what is happening in the speaker’s heart.
