ramacharitamanas::830.simple_insight: Doubt often comes from underestimating what is already present.
ramacharitamanas::830.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the king is speaking to Ram with folded hands, overwhelmed by grace yet unsure how to ask for what he truly wants. He compares himself to a poor man before a wish-fulfilling tree, unable to trust its abundance enough to ask freely.
ramacharitamanas::830.modern_relevance: You sit across from someone who can help, but you keep shrinking your request because you do not want to seem greedy. The real barrier is not lack — it is doubt about generosity.
ramacharitamanas::830.insight: It shifts the mind from timid asking to trusting reception.

ramacharitamanas::831.verse_sanskrit: सो तुम्ह जानहु अंतरजामी। पुरवहु मोर मनोरथ स्वामी॥ सकुच बिहाइ मागु नृप मोही। मोरें नहिं अदेय कछु तोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::831.verse_hindi: हे स्वामी! आप अन्तरयामी हैं, इसलिए उसे जानते ही हैं। मेरा वह मनोरथ पूरा कीजिए। (भगवान ने कहा-) हे राजन् ! संकोच छोड़कर मुझसे माँगो। तुम्हें न दे सकूँ ऐसा मेरे पास कुछ भी नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::831.english_translation: You know the heart within all hearts, Lord. Fulfil my desire. Cast off hesitation and ask freely, king. Nothing I have is beyond your reach.
ramacharitamanas::831.translation_literal: सो (that) / तुम्ह (you) / जानहु (know) / अंतरजामी (inner-knower) / पुरवहु (fulfil) / मोर (my) / मनोरथ (wish) / स्वामी (Lord) / सकुच (hesitation) / बिहाइ (leaving aside) / मागु (ask) / नृप (king) / मोही (me) / मोरें (with me) / नहिं (not) / अदेय (un-givable) / कछु (anything) / तोही (to you)
ramacharitamanas::831.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::831.simple_meaning: The speaker trusts Ram to know the heart and fulfil the wish. Ram answers by asking for direct, fearless asking, promising that nothing is beyond his giving.
ramacharitamanas::831.simple_insight: You do not need to hide your longing from the divine. Honest asking is already part of devotion.
ramacharitamanas::831.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, a king stands before Ram with a desire he can barely voice. He feels unworthy even to ask, but Ram, who knows every heart, invites him to speak plainly. The moment turns private longing into trust.
ramacharitamanas::831.modern_relevance: You rehearse the request in your head, then delete the message before sending it. The real barrier is not lack — it is hesitation. This verse asks for directness.
ramacharitamanas::831.insight: It shifts the mind from guarded wanting to open, trusting request.

ramacharitamanas::832.verse_sanskrit: दानि सिरोमनि कृपानिधि नाथ कहउँ सतिभाउ। चाहउँ तुम्हहि समान सुत प्रभु सन कवन दुराउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::832.verse_hindi: (राजा ने कहा-) हे दानियों के शिरोमणि! हे कृपानिधान! हे नाथ! मैं अपने मन का सच्चा भाव कहता हूँ कि मैं आपके समान पुत्र चाहता हूँ। प्रभु से भला क्या छिपाना! ॥
ramacharitamanas::832.english_translation: The king said, "O crown jewel among givers, ocean of compassion, my lord, I speak my true heart: I want a son like you. What can be hidden from the lord?"
ramacharitamanas::832.translation_literal: दानि (giver) / सिरोमनि (crown jewel) / कृपानिधि (ocean of compassion) / नाथ (lord) / कहउँ (I speak) / सतिभाउ (true feeling) / चाहउँ (I desire) / तुम्हहि (you) / समान (like) / सुत (son) / प्रभु (lord) / सन (from) / कवन (what) / दुराउ (hiding)
ramacharitamanas::832.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::832.essence: Trust makes the deepest wish speakable.
ramacharitamanas::832.simple_meaning: Dasharath speaks with complete honesty. He asks for a son like Ram and admits that nothing can be hidden from the lord.
ramacharitamanas::832.simple_insight: There is relief in telling the deepest wish plainly, without performance or disguise.
ramacharitamanas::832.detailed_meaning: King Dasharath has already been encouraged to ask without hesitation. Now he opens his heart fully to Ram, praising him as giver and source of compassion, and reveals the wish behind all his longing: a son like Ram.
ramacharitamanas::832.modern_relevance: You sit across from someone who truly cares about you, and the words you have rehearsed finally feel unnecessary. The real request comes out plain, because trust has made honesty possible.
ramacharitamanas::832.insight: It shifts the mind from guarded asking to wholehearted truth-telling.

ramacharitamanas::833.verse_sanskrit: देखि प्रीति सुनि बचन अमोले। एवमस्तु करुनानिधि बोले॥ आपु सरिस खोजौं कहँ जाई। नृप तव तनय होब मैं आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::833.verse_hindi: राजा की प्रीति देखकर और उनके अमूल्य वचन सुनकर करुणानिधान भगवान बोले- ऐसा ही हो। हे राजन् ! मैं अपने समान (दूसरा) कहाँ जाकर खोजूँ! अतः स्वयं ही आकर तुम्हारा पुत्र बनूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::833.english_translation: Seeing his devotion and hearing those priceless words, the compassionate one said, "So be it. O king, where shall I go to find another like myself? I will come and be born as your son."
ramacharitamanas::833.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / प्रीति (devotion, affection) / सुनि (hearing) / बचन (words) / अमोले (priceless) / एवमस्तु (so be it) / करुनानिधि (ocean of compassion) / बोले (spoke) / आपु (myself) / सरिस (like) / खोजौं (search) / कहँ (where) / जाई (going) / नृप (king) / तव (your) / तनय (son) / होब (will become) / मैं (I) / आई (coming)
ramacharitamanas::833.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::833.essence: Sincere longing can bring the divine into your home.
ramacharitamanas::833.simple_meaning: Ram accepts the king's heartfelt wish and promises to be born as his son.
ramacharitamanas::833.simple_insight: Love is not ignored. Sincere longing can draw the divine close.
ramacharitamanas::833.detailed_meaning: King Dasharath has just confessed his deepest wish: he wants a son like Ram. Ram hears the king's devotion, accepts it without hesitation, and promises to enter his family as a child. The moment turns longing into grace.
ramacharitamanas::833.modern_relevance: You speak honestly to someone you trust, without polishing your words. They hear the truth beneath the request and meet you there — not with distance, but with presence.
ramacharitamanas::833.insight: It shifts the mind from asking for control to trusting that sincere devotion can be answered.

ramacharitamanas::834.verse_sanskrit: सतरूपहिं बिलोकि कर जोरें। देबि मागु बरु जो रुचि तोरें॥ जो बरु नाथ चतुर नृप मागा। सोइ कृपाल मोहि अति प्रिय लागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::834.verse_hindi: शतरूपाजी को हाथ जोड़े देखकर भगवान ने कहा- हे देवी! तुम्हारी जो इच्छा हो, सो वर माँग लो। (शतरूपा ने कहा-) हे नाथ! चतुर राजा ने जो वर माँगा, हे कृपालु! वह मुझे बहुत ही प्रिय लगा, ॥
ramacharitamanas::834.english_translation: Seeing Satarupa with folded hands, the Lord said, “O देवी, ask for whatever boon you wish.” Satarupa replied, “O Lord, the boon the wise king asked for is very dear to me, O merciful one.”
ramacharitamanas::834.translation_literal: सतरूपहिं (Satarupa) / बिलोकि (seeing) / कर जोरें (with hands folded) / देबि (O देवी) / मागु (ask) / बरु (boon) / जो (whatever) / रुचि (pleases) / तोरें (you) / जो (which) / बरु (boon) / नाथ (Lord) / चतुर (wise) / नृप (king) / मागा (asked) / सोइ (that same) / कृपाल (merciful one) / मोहि (to me) / अति (very) / प्रिय (dear) / लागा (seemed)
ramacharitamanas::834.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::834.essence: A wise wish feels dear because it matches what is already true.
ramacharitamanas::834.simple_meaning: Ram offers Satarupa any boon she wants. She says the boon asked by the wise king pleases her deeply.
ramacharitamanas::834.simple_insight: There is peace in wanting what a wise heart has already asked for.
ramacharitamanas::834.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, Ram has just agreed to fulfill the king's request for a son like himself. Now Satarupa stands before him with folded hands. Rather than asking for something separate, she delights in the king's wise boon and aligns her wish with it.
ramacharitamanas::834.modern_relevance: You hear a request that already feels right in your chest, even before you say yes. The relief is not in getting your own way, but in recognizing a wise desire and blessing it.
ramacharitamanas::834.insight: It shifts desire from personal preference to shared alignment with what is already right.

ramacharitamanas::835.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु परंतु सुठि होति ढिठाई। जदपि भगत हित तुम्हहि सोहाई॥ तुम्ह ब्रह्मादि जनक जग स्वामी। ब्रह्म सकल उर अंतरजामी ॥
ramacharitamanas::835.verse_hindi: परंतु हे प्रभु! बहुत ढिठाई हो रही है, यद्यपि हे भक्तों का हित करने वाले! वह ढिठाई भी आपको अच्छी ही लगती है। आप ब्रह्मा आदि के भी पिता (उत्पन्न करने वाले), जगत के स्वामी और सबके हृदय के भीतर की जानने वाले ब्रह्म हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::835.english_translation: Lord, this is certainly bold. Yet that boldness pleases You, since You are the benefactor of devotees. You are Brahma's source, the master of the world, and the all-knowing supreme reality within every heart.
ramacharitamanas::835.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / परंतु (but) / सुठि (very much) / होति (is) / ढिठाई (boldness) / जदपि (although) / भगत (devotees) / हित (for the good) / तुम्हहि (to you) / सोहाई (is pleasing) / तुम्ह (you) / ब्रह्मादि (Brahma and others) / जनक (source/father) / जग (world) / स्वामी (master) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / सकल (all) / उर (heart) / अंतरजामी (knower within)
ramacharitamanas::835.speaker: Shatarupa
ramacharitamanas::835.essence: Bold devotion is welcome before the one who knows every heart.
ramacharitamanas::835.simple_meaning: Shatarupa praises Ram as the source of all beings, the ruler of the world, and the one who knows every heart. She admits her request is bold, but says such boldness pleases him because he cares for devotees.
ramacharitamanas::835.simple_insight: You can speak boldly to the divine when your heart is sincere.
ramacharitamanas::835.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, Shatarupa speaks after hearing Ram's gracious reply. She bows with reverence, then gathers courage to ask for a boon. The verse deepens her praise of Ram's greatness before she makes her request.
ramacharitamanas::835.modern_relevance: You hesitate before asking for help from someone you deeply respect. Then you remember that real care makes honest asking possible, not shameful.
ramacharitamanas::835.insight: It shifts prayer from timid formality to sincere, trusting speech.

ramacharitamanas::836.verse_sanskrit: अस समुझत मन संसय होई। कहा जो प्रभु प्रवान पुनि सोई॥ जे निज भगत नाथ तव अहहीं। जो सुख पावहिं जो गति लहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::836.verse_hindi: ऐसा समझने पर मन में संदेह होता है, फिर भी प्रभु ने जो कहा वही प्रमाण (सत्य) है। (मैं तो यह माँगती हूँ कि) हे नाथ! आपके जो निज जन हैं, वे जो (अलौकिक, अखंड) सुख पाते हैं और जिस परम गति को प्राप्त होते हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::836.english_translation: Even so, my mind feels doubt. Still, what the Lord has said is true. I ask for the same bliss, the same state, and the same fate that belong to your own devotees.
ramacharitamanas::836.translation_literal: अस (thus) / समुझत (understanding) / मन (mind) / संसय (doubt) / होई (arises) । / कहा (said) / जो (what) / प्रभु (Lord) / प्रवान (true/approved) / पुनि (again) / सोई (that itself) ॥ / जे (who) / निज (own) / भगत (devotees) / नाथ (Lord) / तव (your) / अहहीं (are) । / जो (which) / सुख (bliss) / पावहिं (they obtain) / जो (which) / गति (state/fate) / लहहीं (they attain) ॥
ramacharitamanas::836.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::836.essence: Doubt can remain, but trust still asks for the Lord's own gift.
ramacharitamanas::836.simple_meaning: Parvati admits a lingering doubt, but accepts Ram's word as true. She asks to receive the same bliss and final state that Ram's own devotees receive.
ramacharitamanas::836.simple_insight: Faith can include honest doubt without breaking. The heart still turns toward the Lord's promise.
ramacharitamanas::836.detailed_meaning: Parvati is listening to Shiva explain the power of devotion. She hesitates for a moment, then sets aside her doubt and asks for the same blessed state enjoyed by Ram's own devotees. The verse deepens her longing and makes the next prayer possible.
ramacharitamanas::836.modern_relevance: You are unsure whether this path will really change anything, yet you keep listening because something in it feels true. That quiet willingness to trust is where devotion begins.
ramacharitamanas::836.insight: It shifts the mind from proof-seeking to receptive trust in the Lord's promise.

ramacharitamanas::837.verse_sanskrit: सोइ सुख सोइ गति सोइ भगति सोइ निज चरन सनेहु। सोइ बिबेक सोइ रहनि प्रभु हमहि कृपा करि देहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::837.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! वही सुख, वही गति, वही भक्ति, वही अपने चरणों में प्रेम, वही ज्ञान और वही रहन-सहन कृपा करके हमें दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::837.english_translation: O Lord, grant us only that: the same joy, the same state, the same devotion, the same love for your feet, the same discernment, and the same way of living.
ramacharitamanas::837.translation_literal: सोइ (that same) / सुख (joy) / सोइ (that same) / गति (state or destination) / सोइ (that same) / भगति (devotion) / सोइ (that same) / निज (own) / चरन (feet) / सनेहु (love) / सोइ (that same) / बिबेक (discernment) / सोइ (that same) / रहनि (way of living) / प्रभु (Lord) / हमहि (to us) / कृपा (grace) / करि (having done) / देहु (give)
ramacharitamanas::837.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::837.essence: True devotion asks for Ram himself, not separate rewards.
ramacharitamanas::837.simple_meaning: Parvati asks Ram for the same joy, devotion, love for his feet, discernment, and way of living that belong to true devotees.
ramacharitamanas::837.simple_insight: The heart relaxes when it stops asking for many things and asks for the one thing that matters.
ramacharitamanas::837.detailed_meaning: Parvati has been pressing Shiva’s question about what a devotee truly receives from Ram. Now she states her own wish plainly: not wealth or power, but the inner state of a true devotee. The verse becomes a prayer for Ram's grace itself.
ramacharitamanas::837.modern_relevance: You scroll through ten different goals at midnight, but none of them quiet the ache. Then one honest sentence appears in you: let my life be shaped by what is worth loving.
ramacharitamanas::837.insight: It shifts desire from scattered ambitions to a single request for inner alignment with Ram.

ramacharitamanas::838.verse_sanskrit: सुनि मृदु गूढ़ रुचिर बर रचना। कृपासिंधु बोले मृदु बचना॥ जो कछु रुचि तुम्हरे मन माहीं। मैं सो दीन्ह सब संसय नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::838.verse_hindi: (रानी की) कोमल, गूढ़ और मनोहर श्रेष्ठ वाक्य रचना सुनकर कृपा के समुद्र भगवान कोमल वचन बोले- तुम्हारे मन में जो कुछ इच्छा है, वह सब मैंने तुमको दिया, इसमें कोई संदेह न समझना ॥
ramacharitamanas::838.english_translation: Hearing the queen's soft, subtle, and lovely words, the Ocean of Compassion spoke gently: "Whatever your mind desires, I have already given. Doubt it not."
ramacharitamanas::838.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / मृदु (soft) / गूढ़ (subtle) / रुचिर (lovely) / बर (excellent) / रचना (composition) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / बोले (spoke) / मृदु (gentle) / बचना (words) ॥ / जो (whatever) / कछु (anything) / रुचि (desire) / तुम्हरे (your) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / मैं (I) / सो (that) / दीन्ह (have given) / सब (all) / संसय (doubt) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::838.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::838.essence: Grace answers before doubt can finish speaking.
ramacharitamanas::838.simple_meaning: Ram hears the queen's humble words and gently assures her that her wish has already been granted. He removes all doubt.
ramacharitamanas::838.simple_insight: Trust softens the heart when you realize what you needed has already been received.
ramacharitamanas::838.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, after the queen speaks with tenderness and hidden longing, Ram answers as the ocean of compassion. He does not argue or delay. He simply assures her that her wish is already fulfilled, and that no doubt need remain.
ramacharitamanas::838.modern_relevance: You finally send the message you've been rehearsing for an hour, then stare at the screen waiting for reassurance. The answer you needed may already be there — if you can trust it.
ramacharitamanas::838.insight: It teaches the mind to stop demanding extra proof once grace has already answered.

ramacharitamanas::839.verse_sanskrit: मातु बिबेक अलौकिक तोरें। कबहुँ न मिटिहि अनुग्रह मोरें॥ बंदि चरन मनु कहेउ बहोरी। अवर एक बिनती प्रभु मोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::839.verse_hindi: हे माता! मेरी कृपा से तुम्हारा अलौकिक ज्ञान कभी नष्ट न होगा। तब मनु ने भगवान के चरणों की वंदना करके फिर कहा- हे प्रभु! मेरी एक विनती और है- ॥
ramacharitamanas::839.english_translation: O Mother, my grace will never let your extraordinary understanding fade. Bowing to his feet, Manu said again, "Lord, I have one more request."
ramacharitamanas::839.translation_literal: मातु (Mother) / बिबेक (discriminating understanding) / अलौकिक (extraordinary) / तोरें (for you) / कबहुँ (ever) / न (not) / मिटिहि (will fade) / अनुग्रह (grace) / मोरें (mine)॥ / बंदि (bowing) / चरन (feet) / मनु (Manu) / कहेउ (said) / बहोरी (again) / अवर (another) / एक (one) / बिनती (request) / प्रभु (Lord) / मोरी (my) ॥
ramacharitamanas::839.speaker: Manu
ramacharitamanas::839.essence: Grace can preserve the insight it awakens.
ramacharitamanas::839.simple_meaning: Manu is assured that divine grace will preserve his special understanding, and he humbly asks for one more boon.
ramacharitamanas::839.simple_insight: Grace does not just answer requests; it also protects the clarity needed to ask well.
ramacharitamanas::839.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar setting, Manu has already been granted a profound vision of Ram's grace. Hearing this assurance, he bows again and asks for one more blessing. The verse keeps the dialogue moving toward his deeper wish in the next line.
ramacharitamanas::839.modern_relevance: You finally understand something important after a hard season, and then you fear losing that clarity. This verse feels like the reassurance that insight can be held, not just visited.
ramacharitamanas::839.insight: It shifts the mind from treating understanding as fragile to trusting grace as sustaining.

ramacharitamanas::840.verse_sanskrit: सुत बिषइक तव पद रति होऊ। मोहि बड़ मूढ़ कहे किन कोऊ॥ मनि बिनु फनि जिमि जल बिनु मीना। मम जीवन तिमि तुम्हहि अधीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::840.verse_hindi: आपके चरणों में मेरी वैसी ही प्रीति हो जैसी पुत्र के लिए पिता की होती है, चाहे मुझे कोई बड़ा भारी मूर्ख ही क्यों न कहे। जैसे मणि के बिना साँप और जल के बिना मछली (नहीं रह सकती), वैसे ही मेरा जीवन आपके अधीन रहे (आपके बिना न रह सके) ॥
ramacharitamanas::840.english_translation: May my love for your feet be like a father's love for his son. Let anyone call me a great fool. Like a serpent without its jewel and a fish without water, let my life remain dependent on you.
ramacharitamanas::840.translation_literal: सुत (son) / बिषइक (for the son) / तव (your) / पद (feet) / रति (love, attachment) / होऊ (may it be) । / मोहि (me) / बड़ (very) / मूढ़ (foolish) / कहे (called) / किन (who) / कोऊ (anyone) ॥ / मनि (jewel) / बिनु (without) / फनि (serpent) / जिमि (like) / जल (water) / बिनु (without) / मीना (fish) । / मम (my) / जीवन (life) / तिमि (thus) / तुम्हहि (to you) / अधीना (dependent) ॥
ramacharitamanas::840.speaker: Manu
ramacharitamanas::840.essence: True devotion is wanting only closeness, even at the cost of being misunderstood.
ramacharitamanas::840.simple_meaning: Manu asks for love of Ram's feet so deep that his life depends on Ram alone, even if others think him foolish.
ramacharitamanas::840.simple_insight: Real devotion does not care about appearances. It wants closeness more than approval.
ramacharitamanas::840.detailed_meaning: Manu, standing before Ram after being tested by the divine couple's grace, asks for one thing only: a heart that clings to Ram's feet as naturally as a parent loves a child. He is willing to be called foolish if that bond becomes his life.
ramacharitamanas::840.modern_relevance: You choose the harder, quieter loyalty and others call it naive. Still, you keep showing up for what you love because approval is not the point.
ramacharitamanas::840.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to dependence, making love for the divine the center of life.

ramacharitamanas::841.verse_sanskrit: अस बरु मागि चरन गहि रहेऊ। एवमस्तु करुनानिधि कहेऊ॥ अब तुम्ह मम अनुसासन मानी। बसहु जाइ सुरपति रजधानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::841.verse_hindi: ऐसा वर माँगकर राजा भगवान के चरण पकड़े रह गए। तब दया के निधान भगवान ने कहा- ऐसा ही हो। अब तुम मेरी आज्ञा मानकर देवराज इन्द्र की राजधानी (अमरावती) में जाकर वास करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::841.english_translation: Having asked for this boon, Manu held on to the Lord's feet. Then the ocean of compassion said, “So be it. Now, obey my instruction: go and dwell in the city of Indra, the king of the gods.”
ramacharitamanas::841.translation_literal: अस (such) / बरु (boon) / मागि (asking) / चरन (feet) / गहि (grasping) / रहेऊ (remained) / एवमस्तु (so be it) / करुनानिधि (ocean of compassion) / कहेऊ (said) / अब (now) / तुम्ह (you) / मम (my) / अनुसासन (instruction) / मानी (having obeyed) / बसहु (dwell) / जाइ (going) / सुरपति (lord of the gods) / रजधानी (capital city)
ramacharitamanas::841.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::841.essence: True devotion accepts the boon and the command together.
ramacharitamanas::841.simple_meaning: Manu asks for a blessing and stays at Ram's feet. Ram grants it and tells him to obey and live in Indra's city.
ramacharitamanas::841.simple_insight: Trust deepens when you accept the blessing and the instruction together.
ramacharitamanas::841.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, Manu has just asked for the deepest blessing: to remain devoted to Ram. Ram, moved by compassion, grants the boon and sends him to live in Indra's city for a time. The verse matters because devotion here includes obedience, not just longing.
ramacharitamanas::841.modern_relevance: You finally get the chance you prayed for, but it comes with a strange condition. The harder part is not receiving the gift — it's trusting the guidance that comes with it.
ramacharitamanas::841.insight: It shifts devotion from asking for what you want to accepting the divine instruction that follows.

ramacharitamanas::842.verse_sanskrit: तहँ करि भोग बिसाल तात गएँ कछु काल पुनि। होइहहु अवध भुआल तब मैं होब तुम्हार सुत ॥
ramacharitamanas::842.verse_hindi: हे तात! वहाँ (स्वर्ग के) बहुत से भोग भोगकर, कुछ काल बीत जाने पर, तुम अवध के राजा होंगे। तब मैं तुम्हारा पुत्र होऊँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::842.english_translation: Father, after enjoying abundant pleasures there for some time, you will become the king of Ayodhya. Then I will become your son.
ramacharitamanas::842.translation_literal: तहँ (there) / करि (having done) / भोग (enjoyments) / बिसाल (great, abundant) / तात (father) / गएँ (after passing) / कछु (some) / काल (time) / पुनि (again, then) / होइहहु (you will become) / अवध (Ayodhya) / भुआल (king) / तब (then) / मैं (I) / होब (will be) / तुम्हार (your) / सुत (son)
ramacharitamanas::842.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::842.essence: Delay is not denial; the promised return is already unfolding.
ramacharitamanas::842.simple_meaning: Dasharath will spend some time enjoying heavenly pleasures, then return to rule Ayodhya, and only after that will Ram be born as his son.
ramacharitamanas::842.simple_insight: Even delays are part of the larger order. What is meant to happen still arrives.
ramacharitamanas::842.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand frame, Ram is speaking to Dasharath after accepting the king's devotion. He first blesses him with heavenly enjoyment and later promises a return to Ayodhya, where Ram himself will be born as his son. The verse bridges devotion, reward, and the coming incarnation.
ramacharitamanas::842.modern_relevance: You keep thinking the delay means nothing is happening, but life is already arranging the next turn. What feels like waiting may be the path itself.
ramacharitamanas::842.insight: It shifts attention from immediate desire to the timing of dharma and divine grace.

ramacharitamanas::843.verse_sanskrit: इच्छामय नरबेष सँवारें। होइहउँ प्रगट निकेत तुम्हारें॥ अंसन्ह सहित देह धरि ताता। करिहउँ चरित भगत सुखदाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::843.verse_hindi: इच्छानिर्मित मनुष्य रूप सजकर मैं तुम्हारे घर प्रकट होऊँगा। हे तात! मैं अपने अंशों सहित देह धारण करके भक्तों को सुख देने वाले चरित्र करूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::843.english_translation: Taking on a human form by my own will, I will appear in your house. Father, I will assume a body with my aspects and perform deeds that bring joy to devotees.
ramacharitamanas::843.translation_literal: इच्छामय (of own will) / नरबेष (human form) / सँवारें (having adorned) / होइहउँ (I will become) / प्रगट (manifest) / निकेत (house) / तुम्हारें (in your)॥ / अंसन्ह (with aspects) / सहित (together with) / देह (body) / धरि (having taken) / ताता (father) / करिहउँ (I will do) / चरित (deeds, pastimes) / भगत (devotees) / सुखदाता (giver of joy)॥
ramacharitamanas::843.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::843.essence: The divine comes in human form to bless those who love.
ramacharitamanas::843.simple_meaning: Ram says he will appear in human form in Dasharath's house and live out divine deeds that delight devotees.
ramacharitamanas::843.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing the divine can enter ordinary life and make it sacred.
ramacharitamanas::843.detailed_meaning: After Dasharath asks for the boon of a son, Ram reveals the deeper promise behind it: he will be born in Ayodhya in human form. He will take a body with his aspects and act in ways that bless and delight devotees.
ramacharitamanas::843.modern_relevance: A child is born into a family, and only later do people see how that arrival changed everything. Some presences do not announce themselves with thunder; they enter quietly and transform a home from within.
ramacharitamanas::843.insight: It shifts devotion from distant worship to welcoming the divine in human life and action.

ramacharitamanas::844.verse_sanskrit: जे सुनि सादर नर बड़भागी। भव तरिहहिं ममता मद त्यागी॥ आदिसक्ति जेहिं जग उपजाया। सोउ अवतरिहि मोरि यह माया ॥
ramacharitamanas::844.verse_hindi: जिन (चरित्रों) को बड़े भाग्यशाली मनुष्य आदरसहित सुनकर, ममता और मद त्यागकर, भवसागर से तर जाएँगे। आदिशक्ति यह मेरी (स्वरूपभूता) माया भी, जिसने जगत को उत्पन्न किया है, अवतार लेगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::844.english_translation: Those fortunate people who listen to these stories with reverence, giving up attachment and pride, will cross the cycle of reactivity. The primal power that created the world will also descend in my form through this veil of appearance.
ramacharitamanas::844.translation_literal: जे (those) / सुनि (hearing) / सादर (with reverence) / नर (people) / बड़भागी (fortunate) / भव (cycle of reactivity) / तरिहहिं (will cross) / ममता (attachment) / मद (pride) / त्यागी (having given up) ॥ आदिसक्ति (primal power) / जेहिं (by whom) / जग (world) / उपजाया (was produced) / सोउ (that also) / अवतरिहि (will descend) / मोरि (my) / यह (this) / माया (veil of appearance) ॥
ramacharitamanas::844.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::844.essence: Reverent hearing can carry a person beyond ego.
ramacharitamanas::844.simple_meaning: Reverent listening can free a person from attachment and pride. The same primal power that brought forth the world will also appear here in a human form.
ramacharitamanas::844.simple_insight: Devotion can change how you listen: reverence opens the way out of ego.
ramacharitamanas::844.detailed_meaning: Ram is speaking to Dasharath in the Balkand, promising his own descent and the saving power of hearing his story. He says fortunate listeners who drop possessiveness and pride will cross beyond the cycle of reactivity, and that the primal power behind creation will also take birth in visible form.
ramacharitamanas::844.modern_relevance: You hear a story that strips away your ego instead of feeding it. Something in you loosens, and for a moment you stop needing to be the center.
ramacharitamanas::844.insight: It shifts the reader from consuming sacred story as information to receiving it as a force that dissolves ego.

ramacharitamanas::845.verse_sanskrit: पुरउब मैं अभिलाष तुम्हारा। सत्य सत्य पन सत्य हमारा॥ पुनि पुनि अस कहि कृपानिधाना। अंतरधान भए भगवाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::845.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार मैं तुम्हारी अभिलाषा पूरी करूँगा। मेरा प्रण सत्य है, सत्य है, सत्य है। कृपानिधान भगवान बार-बार ऐसा कहकर अन्तरधान हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::845.english_translation: I will fulfill your wish. My vow is true, true, true. Saying this again and again, the compassionate Lord disappeared.
ramacharitamanas::845.translation_literal: पुरउब (I will fulfill) / मैं (I) / अभिलाष (wish) / तुम्हारा (your) / सत्य (true) / सत्य (true) / पन (vow) / सत्य (true) / हमारा (our/my) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / कृपानिधाना (treasure of compassion) / अंतरधान (vanished) / भए (became) / भगवाना (the Lord)
ramacharitamanas::845.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::845.essence: Ram's promise is enough; his repeated vow makes doubt fall away.
ramacharitamanas::845.simple_meaning: Ram promises to fulfill the request and repeats that his vow is absolutely true. After speaking, he disappears.
ramacharitamanas::845.simple_insight: A divine promise does not need decoration. Repetition itself becomes reassurance.
ramacharitamanas::845.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, Ram has just answered the longing of the waiting couple. He promises to fulfill their wish, seals it with repeated assurance, and then vanishes. The moment matters because the blessing is not abstract — it is a direct vow from Ram himself.
ramacharitamanas::845.modern_relevance: Someone finally says, “I’ll be there,” and means it. The relief is not in the speech, but in the certainty behind it.
ramacharitamanas::845.insight: It teaches trust in a promise that is complete before the proof arrives.

ramacharitamanas::846.verse_sanskrit: दंपति उर धरि भगत कृपाला। तेहिं आश्रम निवसे कछु काला॥ समय पाइ तनु तजि अनयासा। जाइ कीन्ह अमरावति बासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::846.verse_hindi: वे स्त्री-पुरुष (राजा-रानी) भक्तों पर कृपा करने वाले भगवान को हृदय में धारण करके कुछ काल तक उस आश्रम में रहे। फिर उन्होंने समय पाकर, सहज ही (बिना किसी कष्ट के) शरीर छोड़कर, अमरावती (इन्द्र की पुरी) में जाकर वास किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::846.english_translation: The devoted royal couple kept the compassionate Lord in their hearts and lived in that hermitage for some time. Then, when the time came, they left the body effortlessly and took residence in Amaravati.
ramacharitamanas::846.translation_literal: दंपति (the couple) / उर (heart) / धरि (placing) / भगत कृपाला (the compassionate Lord for devotees) / तेहिं आश्रम (in that hermitage) / निवसे (lived) / कछु काला (for some time) ॥ / समय पाइ (when the time came) / तनु (body) / तजि (leaving) / अनयासा (effortlessly) / जाइ (going) / कीन्ह (made) / अमरावति (Amaravati) / बासा (residence) ॥
ramacharitamanas::846.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::846.essence: Devotion makes even leaving the body effortless.
ramacharitamanas::846.simple_meaning: The king and queen stayed in the hermitage while keeping the compassionate Lord in their hearts. When their time ended, they left the body without struggle and went to Amaravati.
ramacharitamanas::846.simple_insight: A life held by devotion can end without fear or resistance.
ramacharitamanas::846.detailed_meaning: Yajnavalkya is still recounting the sacred backstory to Bharadvaja. The royal couple live quietly in the hermitage after their devotion matures. This verse closes their earthly stay and shows that their final passing is gentle, not tragic.
ramacharitamanas::846.modern_relevance: An elderly parent slips away in sleep after years of steady prayer and quiet trust. There is no battle in the leaving, only completion.
ramacharitamanas::846.insight: It shifts attention from clinging to the body toward a peaceful release when the time is ripe.

ramacharitamanas::847.verse_sanskrit: यह इतिहास पुनीत अति उमहि कही बृषकेतु। भरद्वाज सुनु अपर पुनि राम जनम कर हेतु ॥
ramacharitamanas::847.verse_hindi: (याज्ञवल्क्यजी कहते हैं-) हे भरद्वाज! इस अत्यन्त पवित्र इतिहास को शिवजी ने पार्वती से कहा था। अब श्रीराम के अवतार लेने का दूसरा कारण सुनो ॥
ramacharitamanas::847.english_translation: O Bharadvaja, this most sacred history was told by Shiva to Parvati. Now hear the second reason for Ram's birth.
ramacharitamanas::847.translation_literal: यह (this) / इतिहास (history) / पुनीत (sacred) / अति (very) / उमहि (to Uma/Parvati) / कही (was told) / बृषकेतु (Shiva) / भरद्वाज (O Bharadvaja) / सुनु (listen) / अपर (another/second) / पुनि (again) / राम (Ram) / जनम (birth) / कर (of) / हेतु (reason)
ramacharitamanas::847.speaker: Yajnavalkya
ramacharitamanas::847.essence: A sacred story has more than one reason hidden inside it.
ramacharitamanas::847.simple_meaning: Yajnavalkya tells Bharadvaja that Shiva once narrated this holy story to Parvati, and now he should hear the second reason for Ram's birth.
ramacharitamanas::847.simple_insight: Some truths arrive in layers. One answer opens the door; another reveals why the story matters.
ramacharitamanas::847.detailed_meaning: Yajnavalkya is guiding Bharadvaja through a sacred frame story. He reminds him that Shiva already told this ancient account to Parvati, and now he is about to explain the second reason Ram came into the world. The verse functions as a bridge, not the main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::847.modern_relevance: Someone starts a family story with, 'There is more behind this than you know.' You lean in because the first explanation was only the beginning.
ramacharitamanas::847.insight: It prepares the listener to receive a deeper cause, shifting attention from the surface event to the larger divine purpose behind it.

ramacharitamanas::848.verse_sanskrit: सुनु मुनि कथा पुनीत पुरानी। जो गिरिजा प्रति संभु बखानी॥ बिस्व बिदित एक कैकय देसू। सत्यकेतु तहँ बसइ नरेसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::848.verse_hindi: हे मुनि! वह पवित्र और प्राचीन कथा सुनो, जो शिवजी ने पार्वती से कही थी। संसार में प्रसिद्ध एक कैकय देश है। वहाँ सत्यकेतु नाम का राजा रहता (राज्य करता) था ॥
ramacharitamanas::848.english_translation: Listen, sage, to the ancient sacred story that Shiva told Parvati. In the world-famous land of Kekaya, a king named Satyaketu ruled.
ramacharitamanas::848.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / मुनि (sage) / कथा (story) / पुनीत (pure, sacred) / पुरानी (ancient) / जो (which) / गिरिजा (Parvati) / प्रति (to) / संभु (Shiva) / बखानी (told) / बिस्व (world) / बिदित (well-known) / एक (one) / कैकय (Kekaya) / देसू (land) / सत्यकेतु (Satyaketu) / तहँ (there) / बसइ (dwells, rules) / नरेसू (king)
ramacharitamanas::848.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::848.essence: An old story begins with the king who will set it in motion.
ramacharitamanas::848.simple_meaning: Shiva is introducing an old sacred story about a king from the land of Kekaya.
ramacharitamanas::848.simple_insight: Some stories matter because they open the door to a larger turning point.
ramacharitamanas::848.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the frame story, preparing to tell an older sacred account. He names the land of Kekaya and its king, Satyaketu, setting up the family background for the coming events.
ramacharitamanas::848.modern_relevance: A conversation begins with a name, a place, and a memory that seem small at first. Later, you realise that this was the doorway to everything that followed.
ramacharitamanas::848.insight: It shifts attention from the headline event to the hidden family history beneath it.

ramacharitamanas::849.verse_sanskrit: धरम धुरंधर नीति निधाना। तेज प्रताप सील बलवाना॥ तेहि कें भए जुगल सुत बीरा। सब गुन धाम महा रनधीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::849.verse_hindi: वह धर्म की धुरी को धारण करने वाला, नीति की खान, तेजस्वी, प्रतापी, सुशील और बलवान था, उसके दो वीर पुत्र हुए, जो सब गुणों के भंडार और बड़े ही रणधीर थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::849.english_translation: He upheld righteousness, was a treasury of wise conduct, radiant, majestic, virtuous, and strong. He had two brave sons, both abodes of every good quality and great warriors.
ramacharitamanas::849.translation_literal: धरम (righteousness) / धुरंधर (bearer) / नीति (wise conduct) / निधाना (treasury) / तेज (radiance) / प्रताप (majesty) / सील (virtue) / बलवाना (strong) ॥ तेहि (to him) / कें (of) / भए (were born) / जुगल (pair) / सुत (sons) / बीरा (brave) / सब (all) / गुन (qualities) / धाम (abode) / महा (great) / रनधीरा (battle-heroes) ॥
ramacharitamanas::849.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::849.essence: A righteous ruler naturally gives rise to heroic sons.
ramacharitamanas::849.simple_meaning: The king is described as righteous, wise, radiant, virtuous, and strong. He has two heroic sons who possess every good quality.
ramacharitamanas::849.simple_insight: Character is shown first in the ruler, then echoed in the children he raises.
ramacharitamanas::849.detailed_meaning: In the kingdom of Kaikay, the narrator introduces King Satyaketu before the story moves to his sons. He is praised as a model ruler, and this verse prepares the ground for the birth of two heroic princes.
ramacharitamanas::849.modern_relevance: A child hears people speak about a parent before ever meeting them. The qualities that shape a home do not stay hidden for long; they show up in the next generation.
ramacharitamanas::849.insight: It sets up the family line by showing that noble rule and noble children belong together.

ramacharitamanas::850.verse_sanskrit: राज धनी जो जेठ सुत आही। नाम प्रतापभानु अस ताही॥ अपर सुतहि अरिमर्दन नामा। भुजबल अतुल अचल संग्रामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::850.verse_hindi: राज्य का उत्तराधिकारी जो बड़ा लड़का था, उसका नाम प्रतापभानु था। दूसरे पुत्र का नाम अरिमर्दन था, जिसकी भुजाओं में अपार बल था और जो युद्ध में (पर्वत के समान) अटल रहता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::850.english_translation: The elder son, heir to the throne, was named Pratapbhanu. The other son was named Arimardan, whose arms held immense strength and who stood firm in battle.
ramacharitamanas::850.translation_literal: राजधनी (heir to the throne) / जो (who) / जेठ सुत (elder son) / आही (was) / नाम (name) / प्रतापभानु (Pratapbhanu) / अस (thus) / ताही (his) / अपर सुतहि (other son) / अरिमर्दन (Arimardan) / नामा (named) / भुजबल (arm-strength) / अतुल (immeasurable) / अचल (unmoving) / संग्रामा (in battle)
ramacharitamanas::850.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::850.essence: Names can quietly prepare the ground for a whole life story.
ramacharitamanas::850.simple_meaning: The king’s elder son was Pratapbhanu, and his younger son was Arimardan, a warrior of great strength and steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::850.simple_insight: Some lives enter the story only by name, but those names already hint at character.
ramacharitamanas::850.detailed_meaning: In Kekaya, King Satyaketu’s family is being introduced before the story moves into conflict. His elder son is Pratapbhanu, and his younger son is Arimardan. This verse simply names them and marks the younger prince as strong in battle.
ramacharitamanas::850.modern_relevance: A family group chat is full of introductions before a wedding, and one name quietly carries the weight of a future role. Not every line announces a turning point; some just set the stage.
ramacharitamanas::850.insight: It frames character through naming, preparing the reader for the family drama that follows.

ramacharitamanas::851.verse_sanskrit: भाइहि भाइहि परम समीती। सकल दोष छल बरजित प्रीती॥ जेठे सुतहि राज नृप दीन्हा। हरि हित आपु गवन बन कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::851.verse_hindi: भाई-भाई में बड़ा मेल और सब प्रकार के दोषों और छलों से रहित (सच्ची) प्रीति थी। राजा ने जेठे पुत्र को राज्य दे दिया और आप भगवान (के भजन) के लिए वन को चल दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::851.english_translation: There was deep harmony between the brothers, and their love was free of faults and deceit. The king gave the throne to his eldest son and went to the forest for the divine.
ramacharitamanas::851.translation_literal: भाइहि भाइहि (between brother and brother) / परम समीती (complete harmony) / सकल दोष (all faults) / छल (deceit) / बरजित (free from) / प्रीती (love)॥ / जेठे सुतहि (to the eldest son) / राज (kingdom) / नृप (the king) / दीन्हा (gave) / हरि हित (for the divine's sake) / आपु (himself) / गवन (went) / बन (to the forest) / कीन्हा (did)॥
ramacharitamanas::851.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::851.essence: True affection gives up power without resentment.
ramacharitamanas::851.simple_meaning: The brothers lived in genuine harmony, and the king gave the kingdom to his eldest son before leaving for the forest in devotion.
ramacharitamanas::851.simple_insight: Real love does not cling to power; it makes room for duty and surrender.
ramacharitamanas::851.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the royal family is still whole. The brothers love one another without trickery, and Dasharath hands the throne to Ram, his eldest son. Then he leaves for the forest, choosing devotion over palace life.
ramacharitamanas::851.modern_relevance: A parent signs over the family business to the child best suited for it, then steps back instead of controlling everything. Love becomes visible when power is released cleanly.
ramacharitamanas::851.insight: It shifts attention from possession to rightful handoff: love proves itself by letting the next person lead.

ramacharitamanas::852.verse_sanskrit: जब प्रतापरबि भयउ नृप फिरी दोहाई देस। प्रजा पाल अति बेदबिधि कतहुँ नहीं अघ लेस ॥
ramacharitamanas::852.verse_hindi: जब प्रतापभानु राजा हुआ, देश में उसकी दुहाई फिर गई। वह वेद में बताई हुई विधि के अनुसार उत्तम रीति से प्रजा का पालन करने लगा। उसके राज्य में पाप का कहीं लेश भी नहीं रह गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::852.english_translation: When Pratapabhanu became king, his fame spread through the land. He ruled the people according to the Vedas, and not even a trace of wrongdoing remained anywhere.
ramacharitamanas::852.translation_literal: जब (when) प्रतापरबि/प्रतापभानु (Pratapabhanu) भयउ (became) नृप (king) फिरी (again/spread) दोहाई (proclamation/fame) देस (land/country) / प्रजा (people) पाल (protected/nourished) अति (very) बेदबिधि (according to Vedic method) कतहुँ (anywhere) नहीं (not) अघ (wrongdoing/sin) लेस (trace)
ramacharitamanas::852.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::852.essence: Power becomes worthy only when it protects people cleanly.
ramacharitamanas::852.simple_meaning: Pratapabhanu became king, and his rule was so just that the whole kingdom prospered and wrongdoing disappeared.
ramacharitamanas::852.simple_insight: Good rule is measured by how safely ordinary people can live.
ramacharitamanas::852.detailed_meaning: Pratapabhanu has just been given the throne. The story pauses to show what kind of king he became: celebrated across the land, careful in protecting his people, and so orderly that no wrongdoing was left. It sets up the court that follows.
ramacharitamanas::852.modern_relevance: A neighborhood feels different when the landlord is fair, the rules are clear, and no one has to fear being cheated. People relax because power is being used to protect, not exploit.
ramacharitamanas::852.insight: It shifts attention from royal status to the moral quality of rule.

ramacharitamanas::853.verse_sanskrit: नृप हितकारक सचिव सयाना। नाम धरमरुचि सुक्र समाना॥ सचिव सयान बंधु बलबीरा। आपु प्रतापपुंज रनधीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::853.verse_hindi: राजा का हित करने वाला और शुक्राचार्य के समान बुद्धिमान धर्मरुचि नामक उसका मंत्री था। इस प्रकार बुद्धिमान मंत्री और बलवान तथा वीर भाई के साथ ही स्वयं राजा भी बड़ा प्रतापी और रणधीर था ॥
ramacharitamanas::853.english_translation: The king had a wise minister who cared for his welfare, named Dharmaruchi, like Shukracharya. The wise minister and the strong, brave brother stood with him, and the king himself was full of splendor and fearless in battle.
ramacharitamanas::853.translation_literal: नृप (king) / हितकारक (benefit-giving) / सचिव (minister) / सयाना (wise) / नाम (named) / धरमरुचि (Dharmaruchi) / सुक्र (Shukra) / समाना (equal to)॥ / सचिव (minister) / सयान (wise) / बंधु (brother) / बलबीरा (strong and brave) / आपु (himself) / प्रतापपुंज (mass of splendor) / रनधीरा (battle-fearless)॥
ramacharitamanas::853.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::853.essence: Power holds when wisdom, loyalty, and courage stand together.
ramacharitamanas::853.simple_meaning: The king is supported by a wise minister, a strong brother, and his own courage. The verse is building the picture of his power and readiness for rule.
ramacharitamanas::853.simple_insight: Real strength is never just personal. It grows through wise counsel, loyal support, and steady courage.
ramacharitamanas::853.detailed_meaning: In Pratapbhanu’s court, Tulsidas is still setting the scene. Before the army is even described, he shows the king’s support system: a wise minister, a brave brother, and the king’s own valor. This verse prepares the rise of a powerful royal order.
ramacharitamanas::853.modern_relevance: Before a big launch, one person has strategy, another handles the pressure, and a third keeps morale steady. Success rarely comes from one strong figure alone.
ramacharitamanas::853.insight: It shifts attention from lone heroism to the network of wisdom, loyalty, and courage that makes leadership possible.

ramacharitamanas::854.verse_sanskrit: सेन संग चतुरंग अपारा। अमित सुभट सब समर जुझारा॥ सेन बिलोकि राउ हरषाना। अरु बाजे गहगहे निसाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::854.verse_hindi: साथ में अपार चतुरंगिणी सेना थी, जिसमें असंख्य योद्धा थे, जो सब के सब रण में जूझ मरने वाले थे। अपनी सेना को देखकर राजा बहुत प्रसन्न हुआ और घमाघम नगाड़े बजने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::854.english_translation: He had an immense fourfold army, with countless warriors ready for battle. Seeing his forces, the king rejoiced, and loud drums rang out.
ramacharitamanas::854.translation_literal: सेन (army) / संग (with) / चतुरंग (fourfold) / अपारा (vast) । अमित (countless) / सुभट (warriors) / सब (all) / समर (battle) / जुझारा (battle-ready) ॥ सेन (army) / बिलोकि (seeing) / राउ (king) / हरषाना (rejoiced) । अरु (and) / बाजे (were sounded) / गहगहे (thundering) / निसाना (drums) ॥
ramacharitamanas::854.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::854.essence: An army can inspire confidence before a single battle is fought.
ramacharitamanas::854.simple_meaning: The king's army was huge and battle-ready. He felt pleased when he saw its strength, and war drums sounded loudly.
ramacharitamanas::854.simple_insight: Power can look impressive, but it is still only the beginning of a larger story.
ramacharitamanas::854.detailed_meaning: Prataparbhu's campaign is being assembled. After naming his wise minister and strong allies, the narration turns to his vast army. The king looks at his forces with delight, and the drums announce a move toward conquest.
ramacharitamanas::854.modern_relevance: You open the campaign dashboard and see the numbers spike. The room feels electric, the team cheers, and the plan finally looks real.
ramacharitamanas::854.insight: It shifts attention from inner preparation to the outward display of force.

ramacharitamanas::855.verse_sanskrit: बिजय हेतु कटकई बनाई। सुदिन साधि नृप चलेउ बजाई॥ जहँ तहँ परीं अनेक लराईं। जीते सकल भूप बरिआईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::855.verse_hindi: दिग्विजय के लिए सेना सजाकर वह राजा शुभ दिन (मुहूर्त) साधकर और डंका बजाकर चला। जहाँ-तहाँ बहुतसी लड़ाइयाँ हुईं। उसने सब राजाओं को बलपूर्वक जीत लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::855.english_translation: He assembled an army for victory, chose an auspicious day, and marched with drums sounding. Battles broke out everywhere, and he conquered all kings by sheer force.
ramacharitamanas::855.translation_literal: बिजय (victory) / हेतु (for) / कटकई (army) / बनाई (was assembled) / सुदिन (auspicious day) / साधि (having chosen) / नृप (king) / चलेउ (marched) / बजाई (with drums sounding) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / परीं (fell / took place) / अनेक (many) / लराईं (battles) / जीते (conquered) / सकल (all) / भूप (kings) / बरिआईं (by strength)
ramacharitamanas::855.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::855.essence: Victory by force still arrives through many battles.
ramacharitamanas::855.simple_meaning: The king set out with a prepared army, picked an auspicious time, and won battles everywhere by force.
ramacharitamanas::855.simple_insight: Power looks impressive in motion, but it is still only power.
ramacharitamanas::855.detailed_meaning: The scene stays with the king’s military march. After gathering his army and sounding the drums, he moves out to conquer nearby rulers. This verse is still describing the expansion of royal power, not yet any moral turning point.
ramacharitamanas::855.modern_relevance: A campaign launches with banners, planning, and confidence. Then the real world hits back in fragments, and every win still depends on force.
ramacharitamanas::855.insight: It keeps attention on outward conquest, showing how quickly ambition turns into conflict.

ramacharitamanas::856.verse_sanskrit: सप्त दीप भुजबल बस कीन्हे। लै लै दंड छाड़ि नृप दीन्हे॥ सकल अवनि मंडल तेहि काला। एक प्रतापभानु महिपाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::856.verse_hindi: अपनी भुजाओं के बल से उसने सातों द्वीपों (भूमिखण्डों) को वश में कर लिया और राजाओं से दंड (कर) ले-लेकर उन्हें छोड़ दिया। सम्पूर्ण पृथ्वी मंडल का उस समय प्रतापभानु ही एकमात्र (चक्रवर्ती) राजा था ॥
ramacharitamanas::856.english_translation: By the strength of his arms, he brought the seven islands under control and made kings pay tribute before releasing them. In that time, only Pratapbhanu was the sole sovereign of the whole earth.
ramacharitamanas::856.translation_literal: सप्त (seven) / दीप (islands) / भुजबल (arm-strength) / बस (under control) / कीन्हे (made) / लै लै (taking repeatedly) / दंड (tribute, punishment) / छाड़ि (releasing) / नृप (kings) / दीन्हे (gave) / सकल (entire) / अवनि (earth) / मंडल (realm) / तेहि काला (at that time) / एक (only) / प्रतापभानु (Pratapbhanu) / महिपाला (earth-protector, king)
ramacharitamanas::856.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::856.essence: Worldly rule can stretch across everything and still last only for a moment.
ramacharitamanas::856.simple_meaning: Pratapbhanu conquered a vast realm, collected tribute from other kings, and ruled as the only emperor of the earth.
ramacharitamanas::856.simple_insight: Power can expand outward until one ruler seems to hold everything, yet it still remains temporary.
ramacharitamanas::856.detailed_meaning: The narration is describing King Pratapbhanu after his military victories. His armies have subdued many regions, and other kings now pay tribute. The point is not a teaching but a scene-setting detail: he stands at the height of worldly power before the story turns onward.
ramacharitamanas::856.modern_relevance: A leader wins one contract after another, the office celebrates, and every chart points upward. For a moment it feels like the whole field belongs to one name.
ramacharitamanas::856.insight: It frames success as expansion that can be recorded, admired, and still remain only a passing condition.

ramacharitamanas::857.verse_sanskrit: स्वबस बिस्व करि बाहुबल निज पुर कीन्ह प्रबेसु। अरथ धरम कामादि सुख सेवइ समयँ नरेसु ॥
ramacharitamanas::857.verse_hindi: संसारभर को अपनी भुजाओं के बल से वश में करके राजा ने अपने नगर में प्रवेश किया। राजा अर्थ, धर्म और काम आदि के सुखों का समयानुसार सेवन करता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::857.english_translation: Having brought the whole world under his control by his own arm-strength, the king entered his city. The king enjoyed wealth, duty, desire, and other pleasures at the proper time.
ramacharitamanas::857.translation_literal: स्वबस (under his own control) / बिस्व (the world) / करि (having made) / बाहुबल (arm-strength) / निज (his own) / पुर (city) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रबेसु (entry) / अरथ (wealth) / धरम (duty) / कामादि (desire and others) / सुख (pleasures) / सेवइ (enjoys) / समयँ (at the proper time) / नरेसु (king)
ramacharitamanas::857.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::857.essence: True strength includes knowing when to enjoy and when to hold back.
ramacharitamanas::857.simple_meaning: A powerful king conquered the world and returned to rule his city well, enjoying life’s aims in their proper place and time.
ramacharitamanas::857.simple_insight: Power is not only conquest; it is also knowing how to live with order and restraint.
ramacharitamanas::857.detailed_meaning: The story shifts from battlefield victories to the ruler’s return home. After subduing many lands, King Pratapbhanu enters his own city and governs a prosperous realm. The verse pauses on the image of balanced kingship before the next praise of his reign.
ramacharitamanas::857.modern_relevance: You finally finish the big project, win the argument, or get the promotion. The real test comes after: can you return home and live wisely, without letting victory turn into excess?
ramacharitamanas::857.insight: It shifts attention from winning alone to governing power with timing, balance, and restraint.

ramacharitamanas::858.verse_sanskrit: भूप प्रतापभानु बल पाई। कामधेनु भै भूमि सुहाई॥ सब दुख बरजित प्रजा सुखारी। धरमसील सुंदर नर नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::858.verse_hindi: राजा प्रतापभानु का बल पाकर भूमि सुंदर कामधेनु (मनचाही वस्तु देने वाली) हो गई। (उनके राज्य में) प्रजा सब (प्रकार के) दुःखों से रहित और सुखी थी और सभी स्त्री-पुरुष सुंदर और धर्मात्मा थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::858.english_translation: By the strength of King Pratapbhanu, the land became like a wish-fulfilling cow. All the people were free from suffering and lived in happiness; men and women were beautiful and righteous.
ramacharitamanas::858.translation_literal: भूप (king) / प्रतापभानु (Pratapbhanu) / बल (strength) / पाई (having obtained) / कामधेनु (wish-fulfilling cow) / भै (became) / भूमि (earth/land) / सुहाई (beautiful/pleasant) / सब (all) / दुख (sorrow) / बरजित (free from) / प्रजा (subjects/people) / सुखारी (happy) / धरमसील (righteous) / सुंदर (beautiful) / नर (men) / नारी (women)
ramacharitamanas::858.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::858.essence: True power shows up as a whole society becoming easier to live in.
ramacharitamanas::858.simple_meaning: King Pratapbhanu's rule made the land prosperous and pleasant. People lived without suffering, and society was orderly, happy, and righteous.
ramacharitamanas::858.simple_insight: Good leadership changes the whole atmosphere of a place, not just the throne.
ramacharitamanas::858.detailed_meaning: The story pauses to describe Pratapbhanu's kingdom at its height. His power has made the land feel abundant and easy, like a wish-fulfilling cow. The people are free from suffering, and the kingdom seems peaceful and morally healthy before the next turn in the tale.
ramacharitamanas::858.modern_relevance: A neighborhood feels different when the local leader is fair, calm, and dependable. People stop bracing for trouble and start living normally, because the atmosphere itself has changed.
ramacharitamanas::858.insight: It shifts attention from personal glory to the social conditions a ruler creates.

ramacharitamanas::859.verse_sanskrit: सचिव धरमरुचि हरि पद प्रीती। नृप हित हेतु सिखव नित नीती॥ गुर सुर संत पितर महिदेवा। करइ सदा नृप सब कै सेवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::859.verse_hindi: धर्मरुचि मंत्री का श्री हरि के चरणों में प्रेम था। वह राजा के हित के लिए सदा उसको नीति सिखाया करता था। राजा गुरु, देवता, संत, पितर और ब्राह्मण- इन सबकी सदा सेवा करता रहता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::859.english_translation: The minister Dharmaruchi loved the feet of Hari. For the king's welfare, he always taught policy and right conduct. The king always served the teacher, the radiant beings, saints, ancestors, and holy men.
ramacharitamanas::859.translation_literal: सचिव (minister) / धरमरुचि (Dharmaruchi) / हरि (Hari) / पद (feet) / प्रीती (love) / नृप (king) / हित (welfare) / हेतु (for the purpose of) / सिखव (taught) / नित (always) / नीती (policy, right conduct) / गुर (teacher) / सुर (radiant beings) / संत (saints) / पितर (ancestors) / महिदेवा (holy men, brahmins) / करइ (does) / सदा (always) / नृप (king) / सब कै (of all) / सेवा (service)
ramacharitamanas::859.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::859.essence: Power stays clean when counsel is given in love and received in humility.
ramacharitamanas::859.simple_meaning: A wise minister loved Ram and kept advising the king for his welfare. The king, in turn, respected and served teachers, saints, ancestors, and holy men.
ramacharitamanas::859.simple_insight: Good leadership grows from humility, service, and guidance that is meant for someone else's good.
ramacharitamanas::859.detailed_meaning: In Pratapbhanu's prosperous kingdom, the court is being shown as truly righteous. Dharmaruchi, the minister, loves Hari and gives the king practical counsel for his welfare. The king responds with service and respect to all worthy elders and holy beings.
ramacharitamanas::859.modern_relevance: A manager who tells the truth even when it is inconvenient, and a leader who listens instead of defending ego — that combination keeps a team healthy.
ramacharitamanas::859.insight: It shifts authority from pride to service, showing that real power listens, learns, and honors what is worthy.

ramacharitamanas::860.verse_sanskrit: भूप धरम जे बेद बखाने। सकल करइ सादर सुख माने॥ दिन प्रति देइ बिबिध बिधि दाना। सुनइ सास्त्र बर बेद पुराना ॥
ramacharitamanas::860.verse_hindi: वेदों में राजाओं के जो धर्म बताए गए हैं, राजा सदा आदरपूर्वक और सुख मानकर उन सबका पालन करता था। प्रतिदिन अनेक प्रकार के दान देता और उत्तम शास्त्र, वेद और पुराण सुनता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::860.english_translation: The duties of kings described in the Vedas were all performed with respect and joy. Each day he gave many kinds of charity and listened to excellent scriptures, the Vedas, and the Puranas.
ramacharitamanas::860.translation_literal: भूप (king) / धरम (duty) / जे (which) / बेद (Vedas) / बखाने (describe) / सकल (all) / करइ (does) / सादर (with respect) / सुख माने (with gladness) / दिन प्रति (every day) / देइ (gives) / बिबिध बिधि (various kinds) / दाना (charity) / सुनइ (he hears) / सास्त्र (scriptures) / बर (excellent) / बेद (Vedas) / पुराना (Puranas)
ramacharitamanas::860.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::860.essence: Righteous rule is daily discipline, generosity, and learning.
ramacharitamanas::860.simple_meaning: The king followed the duties laid out for rulers, gave charity every day, and regularly listened to sacred teachings.
ramacharitamanas::860.simple_insight: A good life is built through steady practice, not occasional grand gestures.
ramacharitamanas::860.detailed_meaning: Pratapbhanu's reign is being described as orderly and righteous. After the minister's guidance, the king does not merely rule; he lives by the duties set for rulers, gives daily charity, and keeps listening to sacred learning.
ramacharitamanas::860.modern_relevance: A manager who reads the same hard feedback every morning, gives credit freely, and keeps learning instead of coasting is doing this verse in modern form.
ramacharitamanas::860.insight: It shifts leadership from status to steady self-education and generous action.

ramacharitamanas::861.verse_sanskrit: नाना बापीं कूप तड़ागा। सुमन बाटिका सुंदर बागा॥ बिप्रभवन सुरभवन सुहाए। सब तीरथन्ह विचित्र बनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::861.verse_hindi: उसने बहुत सी बावलियाँ, कुएँ, तालाब, फुलवाड़ियाँ सुंदर बगीचे, ब्राह्मणों के लिए घर और देवताओं के सुंदर विचित्र मंदिर सब तीर्थों में बनवाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::861.english_translation: He built many wells, ponds, tanks, flower-gardens, beautiful parks, houses for priests, pleasing temples for the radiant beings, and all kinds of sacred places.
ramacharitamanas::861.translation_literal: नाना (many) / बापीं (wells) / कूप (wells) / तड़ागा (ponds, tanks) / सुमन (flowers) / बाटिका (gardens) / सुंदर (beautiful) / बागा (parks, gardens) / बिप्रभवन (houses for priests) / सुरभवन (houses of radiant beings, temples) / सुहाए (pleasing, beautiful) / सब (all) / तीरथन्ह (at sacred places) / विचित्र (varied, splendid) / बनाए (made, built)
ramacharitamanas::861.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::861.essence: Real rule shows itself in what it builds for others.
ramacharitamanas::861.simple_meaning: The king built wells, ponds, gardens, priestly homes, temples, and sacred sites everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::861.simple_insight: A good ruler leaves behind places that nourish both people and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::861.detailed_meaning: The narration is describing King Dasharath's generous rule in Ayodhya. After establishing that he followed righteous conduct and gave freely, this verse adds the public works he built: water sources, gardens, homes for priests, and temples.
ramacharitamanas::861.modern_relevance: A city block with no shade, no water, no quiet place to sit feels harsh. This verse imagines leadership that makes life easier, greener, and more livable for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::861.insight: It shifts leadership from display to service: build what sustains daily life and sacred life together.

ramacharitamanas::862.verse_sanskrit: जहँ लजि कहे पुरान श्रुति एक एक सब जाग। बार सहस्र सहस्र नृप किए सहित अनुराग ॥
ramacharitamanas::862.verse_hindi: वेद और पुराणों में जितने प्रकार के यज्ञ कहे गए हैं, राजा ने एक-एक करके उन सब यज्ञों को प्रेम सहित हजार-हजार बार किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::862.english_translation: The king performed every sacrifice described in the Vedas and Puranas, again and again, with love.
ramacharitamanas::862.translation_literal: जहँ (where) / लजि (with modesty) / कहे (were said) / पुरान (Puranas) / श्रुति (Vedas) / एक एक (one by one, each) / सब (all) / जाग (sacrifices) / बार (times) / सहस्र (thousand) / सहस्र (thousand) / नृप (king) / किए (did) / सहित (with) / अनुराग (love, devotion)
ramacharitamanas::862.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::862.essence: Love makes repeated sacred action feel natural, not heavy.
ramacharitamanas::862.simple_meaning: The king carried out every prescribed sacrifice many times, and he did it with devotion, not reluctance.
ramacharitamanas::862.simple_insight: True generosity is not mechanical; it is wholehearted and repeated.
ramacharitamanas::862.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, King Dasharath rules with rare splendor. The earlier verses describe his charity and sacred works; this line adds that he completed every Vedic sacrifice again and again, lovingly, showing a king whose piety matched his power.
ramacharitamanas::862.modern_relevance: A person quietly keeps showing up for the same responsibility year after year — the school fundraiser, the family ritual, the community duty — not for praise, but because the heart is in it.
ramacharitamanas::862.insight: It shifts attention from ritual performance to the spirit of loving consistency behind it.

ramacharitamanas::863.verse_sanskrit: हृदयँ न कछु फल अनुसंधाना। भूप बिबेकी परम सुजाना॥ करइ जे धरम करम मन बानी। बासुदेव अर्पित नृप ग्यानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::863.verse_hindi: (राजा के) हृदय में किसी फल की टोह (कामना) न थी। राजा बड़ा ही बुद्धिमान और ज्ञानी था। वह ज्ञानी राजा कर्म, मन और वाणी से जो कुछ भी धर्म करता था, सब भगवान वासुदेव को अर्पित करते रहता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::863.english_translation: The king sought no reward in his heart. He was wise, discerning, and supremely intelligent. Whatever he did in duty, thought, and speech, that king offered to Vasudeva.
ramacharitamanas::863.translation_literal: हृदयँ (in the heart) / न (not) / कछु (any) / फल (fruit, result) / अनुसंधाना (seeking, expectation) / भूप (king) / बिबेकी (discerning, wise) / परम (supreme) / सुजाना (very intelligent, well-knowing) / करइ (does) / जे (whatever) / धरम (duty, righteous action) / करम (action) / मन (mind) / बानी (speech) / बासुदेव (Vasudeva) / अर्पित (offered) / नृप (king) / ग्यानी (knowing, wise)
ramacharitamanas::863.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::863.simple_meaning: A wise king did his duties with no desire for reward. He offered every action, thought, and word to the divine.
ramacharitamanas::863.simple_insight: There is freedom in giving your best without clinging to what comes back.
ramacharitamanas::863.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, King Dasharath is shown as a ruler whose mind is free of reward-seeking. He performs righteous action with wisdom and offers his whole life — thought, speech, and deed — to Vasudeva. The verse defines royal greatness as inner renunciation.
ramacharitamanas::863.modern_relevance: You finish a hard task, send it out, and refuse to keep checking for praise. The cleanest work comes from giving fully without bargaining with the result.
ramacharitamanas::863.insight: It shifts action from self-benefit to offering, so work stays pure even when results are uncertain.

ramacharitamanas::864.verse_sanskrit: चढ़ि बर बाजि बार एक राजा। मृगया कर सब साजि समाजा॥ बिंध्याचल गभीर बन गयऊ। मृग पुनीत बहु मारत भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::864.verse_hindi: एक बार वह राजा एक अच्छे घोड़े पर सवार होकर, शिकार का सब सामान सजाकर विंध्याचल के घने जंगल में गया और वहाँ उसने बहुत से उत्तम-उत्तम हिरन मारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::864.english_translation: Once the king rode out on a fine horse with all his hunting gear and entered the deep forest of Vindhyachal, where he killed many noble deer.
ramacharitamanas::864.translation_literal: चढ़ि (mounted) / बर (fine) / बाजि (horse) / बार एक (one time) / राजा (king) / मृगया (hunt) / कर (doing) / सब (all) / साजि (arranged) / समाजा (equipment, attendants) / बिंध्याचल (Vindhyachal) / गभीर (deep) / बन (forest) / गयऊ (went) / मृग (deer) / पुनीत (noble, pure) / बहु (many) / मारत (killing) / भयऊ (became)
ramacharitamanas::864.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::864.essence: Power without restraint quickly turns into harm.
ramacharitamanas::864.simple_meaning: The king went into the deep forest with hunting gear and killed many deer.
ramacharitamanas::864.simple_insight: Some actions begin as sport and end as harm.
ramacharitamanas::864.detailed_meaning: The king has already been shown as wise and devoted in action. Now he rides into the Vindhyachal forest with a hunting party, and the scene turns from royal order to violence, setting up the next sight he will encounter.
ramacharitamanas::864.modern_relevance: You start the day treating something as harmless entertainment, and by noon you have hurt people or things you meant to overlook.
ramacharitamanas::864.insight: It shifts attention from royal display to the moral weight of casual violence.

ramacharitamanas::865.verse_sanskrit: फिरत बिपिन नृप दीख बराहू। जनु बन दुरेउ ससिहि ग्रसि राहू॥ बड़ बिधु नहिं समात मुख माहीं। मनहुँ क्रोध बस उगिलत नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::865.verse_hindi: राजा ने वन में फिरते हुए एक सूअर को देखा। (दाँतों के कारण वह ऐसा दिख पड़ता था) मानो चन्द्रमा को ग्रसकर (मुँह में पकड़कर) राहु वन में आ छिपा हो। चन्द्रमा बड़ा होने से उसके मुँह में समाता नहीं है और मानो क्रोधवश वह भी उसे उगलता नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::865.english_translation: While roaming the forest, the king saw a boar, as if Rahu had swallowed the moon and hidden in the woods. The moon was too large for its mouth, and in anger it seemed not to spit it out.
ramacharitamanas::865.translation_literal: फिरत (roaming) / बिपिन (forest) / नृप (king) / दीख (saw) / बराहू (boar) । जनु (as if) / बन (forest) / दुरेउ (hid) / ससिहि (the moon) / ग्रसि (having swallowed) / राहू (Rahu) ॥ बड़ (big) / बिधु (moon) / नहिं (not) / समात (fits) / मुख (mouth) / माहीं (in) । मनहुँ (as if) / क्रोध (anger) / बस (under control of) / उगिलत (spitting out) / नाहीं (not) ॥
ramacharitamanas::865.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::865.essence: A forest sight is made vast through cosmic imagery.
ramacharitamanas::865.simple_meaning: The king sees a huge boar in the forest, described with a vivid comparison to Rahu swallowing the moon. It is a visual description, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::865.simple_insight: Sometimes a scene is only a scene, but its imagery still makes the moment unforgettable.
ramacharitamanas::865.detailed_meaning: King Dasarath is roaming the forest on a hunt when he spots a massive boar. Tulsidas pauses the action to paint its strange, fearsome appearance with a celestial image. The verse sets up the next movement in the hunt.
ramacharitamanas::865.modern_relevance: You catch sight of something enormous moving through the trees on an early morning drive, and for a second the whole world narrows to that one shape. The verse does the same with the boar.
ramacharitamanas::865.insight: It slows the reader down to see the scene before the hunt continues.

ramacharitamanas::866.verse_sanskrit: कोल कराल दसन छबि गाई। तनु बिसाल पीवर अधिकाई॥ घुरुघुरात हय आरौ पाएँ। चकित बिलोकत कान उठाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::866.verse_hindi: यह तो सूअर के भयानक दाँतों की शोभा कही गई। (इधर) उसका शरीर भी बहुत विशाल और मोटा था। घोड़े की आहट पाकर वह घुरघुराता हुआ कान उठाए चौकन्ना होकर देख रहा था ॥
ramacharitamanas::866.english_translation: Its fearsome tusks were praised, and its body was huge and very stout. Hearing the horse’s sound, it grunted, lifted its ears, and stared in alert surprise.
ramacharitamanas::866.translation_literal: कोल (boar) / कराल (fearsome) / दसन (teeth) / छबि (beauty, form) / गाई (was praised) / तनु (body) / बिसाल (huge) / पीवर (stout, fat) / अधिकाई (excessively) / घुरुघुरात (grunting) / हय (horse) / आरौ (sound, noise) / पाएँ (on hearing) / चकित (startled) / बिलोकत (looking) / कान (ears) / उठाएँ (raised)
ramacharitamanas::866.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::866.essence: The boar’s size and vigilance heighten the chase.
ramacharitamanas::866.simple_meaning: The boar is described as huge, fierce, and alert. It hears the horse and reacts at once.
ramacharitamanas::866.simple_insight: Pure scene detail can build tension without saying anything directly.
ramacharitamanas::866.detailed_meaning: A king is hunting in the Vindhya forest and spots a massive boar. The poem lingers on its teeth, bulk, and sudden alertness before the chase continues. This verse is part of the scene-setting, not the teaching.
ramacharitamanas::866.insight: It slows the action to sharpen the threat before the pursuit begins.

ramacharitamanas::867.verse_sanskrit: नील महीधर सिखर सम देखि बिसाल बराहु। चपरि चलेउ हय सुटुकि नृप हाँकि न होइ निबाहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::867.verse_hindi: नील पर्वत के शिखर के समान विशाल (शरीर वाले) उस सूअर को देखकर राजा घोड़े को चाबुक लगाकर तेजी से चला और उसने सूअर को ललकारा कि अब तेरा बचाव नहीं हो सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::867.english_translation: Seeing the huge boar, as large as a mountain peak, the king urged his horse forward at once and challenged it, as if saying there would be no escape now.
ramacharitamanas::867.translation_literal: नील (blue) / महीधर (mountain) / सिखर (peak) / सम (like) / देखि (seeing) / बिसाल (huge) / बराहु (boar) / चपरि (urging on) / चलेउ (he moved) / हय (horse) / सुटुकि (swiftly) / नृप (king) / हाँकि (calling out) / न होइ (will not be) / निबाहु (escape)
ramacharitamanas::867.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::867.essence: The chase begins the instant fear is answered with speed.
ramacharitamanas::867.simple_meaning: The king sees the huge boar and rushes after it on horseback, challenging it to flee if it can.
ramacharitamanas::867.simple_insight: The moment demands action, not hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::867.detailed_meaning: A king is hunting in the forest and spots a massive boar. He spurs his horse forward and calls it out, turning the chase into a direct confrontation. The verse mainly advances the scene toward the shot that follows.
ramacharitamanas::867.modern_relevance: You spot the problem before everyone else does. Instead of circling it for an hour, you move straight toward it and deal with it now.
ramacharitamanas::867.insight: It shifts attention from observation to immediate pursuit.

ramacharitamanas::868.verse_sanskrit: आवत देखि अधिक रव बाजी। चलेउ बराह मरुत गति भाजी॥ तुरत कीन्ह नृप सर संधाना। महि मिलि गयउ बिलोकत बाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::868.verse_hindi: अधिक शब्द करते हुए घोड़े को (अपनी तरफ) आता देखकर सूअर पवन वेग से भाग चला। राजा ने तुरंत ही बाण को धनुष पर चढ़ाया। सूअर बाण को देखते ही धरती में दुबक गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::868.english_translation: Seeing the horse coming closer, the boar ran away at the speed of the wind. The king quickly fitted an arrow to his bow, and the boar, seeing the arrow, sank into the earth.
ramacharitamanas::868.translation_literal: आवत (coming) / देखि (seeing) / अधिक (greatly) / रव (noise) / बाजी (horse) / चलेउ (ran) / बराह (boar) / मरुत गति (wind-speed) / भाजी (fleeing) / तुरत (quickly) / कीन्ह (did) / नृप (king) / सर (arrow) / संधाना (fitted) / महि (earth) / मिलि (having met) / गयउ (went) / बिलोकत (seeing) / बाना (arrow)
ramacharitamanas::868.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::868.essence: The chase begins, and the boar slips from sight.
ramacharitamanas::868.simple_meaning: The boar flees when the horse nears. The king readies his arrow at once, and the boar hides itself in the ground.
ramacharitamanas::868.simple_insight: Pressure reveals instinct: one side charges, the other vanishes.
ramacharitamanas::868.detailed_meaning: In the hunt, the boar hears the horse drawing near and bolts. The king instantly nocks an arrow, but the creature drops into the earth to escape. The scene is still building toward the chase, not delivering its main lesson yet.
ramacharitamanas::868.modern_relevance: A tense conversation starts to turn serious, and the other person suddenly dodges the issue. You feel the chase begin before either side says the real thing.
ramacharitamanas::868.insight: It keeps the action moving by showing the boar’s evasive fear and the king’s immediate response.

ramacharitamanas::869.verse_sanskrit: तकि तकि तीर महीस चलावा। करि छल सुअर सरीर बचावा॥ प्रगटत दुरत जाइ मृग भागा। रिस बस भूप चलेउ सँग लागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::869.verse_hindi: राजा तक-तककर तीर चलाता है, परन्तु सूअर छल करके शरीर को बचाता जाता है। वह पशु कभी प्रकट होता और कभी छिपता हुआ भाग जाता था और राजा भी क्रोध के वश उसके साथ (पीछे) लगा चला जाता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::869.english_translation: The king shot arrows again and again, but the boar kept saving its body through trickery. Appearing and disappearing, it ran off like a deer, and the king, driven by anger, kept chasing after it.
ramacharitamanas::869.translation_literal: तकि तकि (again and again aiming) / तीर (arrow) / महीस (king) / चलावा (shot) / करि (doing) / छल (trickery) / सुअर (boar) / सरीर (body) / बचावा (saved) / प्रगटत (appearing) / दुरत (fleeing) / जाइ (going) / मृग (deer) / भागा (ran away) / रिस (anger) / बस (under control) / भूप (king) / चलेउ (went) / सँग (along) / लागा (attached, pursued)
ramacharitamanas::869.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::869.essence: Anger makes pursuit feel like purpose.
ramacharitamanas::869.simple_meaning: The king keeps shooting, but the boar dodges and runs off. Anger drives the king to keep chasing it deeper into the forest.
ramacharitamanas::869.simple_insight: Anger narrows attention until pursuit feels more important than wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::869.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the king has already been lured into a dangerous chase. The boar keeps slipping away through trickery, and the king, now caught in rising anger, follows it without pause. This verse shows the hunt turning into obsession.
ramacharitamanas::869.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing the message thread, trying to get the last word. The more they slip away, the more your temper pulls you forward.
ramacharitamanas::869.insight: It shows how anger can trap a person in reactive pursuit instead of clear judgment.

ramacharitamanas::870.verse_sanskrit: गयउ दूरि घन गहन बराहू। जहँ नाहिन गज बाजि निबाहू॥ अति अकेल बन बिपुल कलेसू। तदपि न मृग मग तजइ नरेसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::870.verse_hindi: सूअर बहुत दूर ऐसे घने जंगल में चला गया, जहाँ हाथी-घोड़े का निबाह (गमन) नहीं था। राजा बिलकुल अकेला था और वन में क्लेश भी बहुत था, फिर भी राजा ने उस पशु का पीछा नहीं छोड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::870.english_translation: The boar went far into a dense forest where elephants and horses could not follow. The king was utterly alone, the forest was full of hardship, yet he did not abandon the chase.
ramacharitamanas::870.translation_literal: गयउ (went) / दूरि (far) / घन (dense) / गहन (thick, deep) / बराहू (boar) / जहँ (where) / नाहिन (not) / गज (elephants) / बाजि (horses) / निबाहू (can proceed) / अति (very) / अकेल (alone) / बन (forest) / बिपुल (great, abundant) / कलेसू (hardship) / तदपि (still) / न (not) / मृग (animal) / मग (path) / तजइ (abandons) / नरेसू (king)
ramacharitamanas::870.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::870.simple_meaning: The king keeps chasing the boar even when the path becomes lonely and difficult. He does not give up just because the terrain is harsh.
ramacharitamanas::870.simple_insight: Steady resolve matters more than comfort. Hard conditions do not excuse quitting.
ramacharitamanas::870.detailed_meaning: In the forest hunt, the boar has led the king far from easy ground into thick wilderness. The king is alone now, with no support from elephants or horses, yet he keeps going. The verse highlights his persistence before the chase turns even deeper.
ramacharitamanas::870.modern_relevance: You are the last one still troubleshooting at midnight after the team has gone home. The problem is messy, the path is ugly, and quitting would be easier — but you keep going.
ramacharitamanas::870.insight: It teaches you to stay with a worthy task even when support disappears and conditions turn difficult.

ramacharitamanas::871.verse_sanskrit: कोल बिलोकि भूप बड़ धीरा। भागि पैठ गिरिगुहाँ गभीरा॥ अगम देखि नृप अति पछिताई। फिरेउ महाबन परेउ भुलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::871.verse_hindi: राजा को बड़ा धैर्यवान देखकर, सूअर भागकर पहाड़ की एक गहरी गुफा में जा घुसा। उसमें जाना कठिन देखकर राजा को बहुत पछताकर लौटना पड़ा, पर उस घोर वन में वह रास्ता भूल गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::871.english_translation: Seeing the king’s great patience, the boar ran into a deep mountain cave. Finding it impossible to enter, the king turned back in deep regret, but in that vast forest he lost his way.
ramacharitamanas::871.translation_literal: कोल (boar) / बिलोकि (seeing) / भूप (king) / बड़ (very) / धीरा (patient) / भागि (running) / पैठ (entered) / गिरिगुहाँ (mountain cave) / गभीरा (deep)॥ अगम (inaccessible) / देखि (seeing) / नृप (king) / अति (very) / पछिताई (regretted) / फिरेउ (turned back) / महाबन (great forest) / परेउ (fell) / भुलाई (into confusion, lost his way)॥
ramacharitamanas::871.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::871.essence: A hard chase can leave the pursuer more lost than the quarry.
ramacharitamanas::871.simple_meaning: The boar escapes into a deep cave, and the king cannot follow. Frustrated and lost, he turns back and loses his way in the forest.
ramacharitamanas::871.simple_insight: Pursuit can turn into confusion when the goal slips beyond reach.
ramacharitamanas::871.detailed_meaning: The king has chased the boar deep into the forest, but the animal slips into a mountain cave that is too difficult to enter. He turns back in frustration, only to become lost in the vast wilderness. The passage heightens the danger and futility of the chase.
ramacharitamanas::871.modern_relevance: You keep chasing a problem through endless tabs, calls, and dead ends. Then the trail goes cold, and suddenly you are the one who feels lost.
ramacharitamanas::871.insight: It shifts attention from pursuit to the cost of stubborn chasing when the situation has already slipped beyond control.

ramacharitamanas::872.verse_sanskrit: खेद खिन्न छुद्धित तृषित राजा बाजि समेत। खोजत ब्याकुल सरित सर जल बिनु भयउ अचेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::872.verse_hindi: बहुत परिश्रम करने से थका हुआ और घोड़े समेत भूख-प्यास से व्याकुल राजा नदी-तालाब खोजता-खोजता पानी बिना बेहाल हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::872.english_translation: The king, exhausted, hungry, and thirsty, wandered with his horse, searching for lakes and rivers. Finding no water, he fell senseless.
ramacharitamanas::872.translation_literal: खेद (weariness) / खिन्न (dejected) / छुद्धित (hungry) / तृषित (thirsty) / राजा (king) / बाजि (horse) / समेत (along with) / खोजत (searching) / ब्याकुल (restless, distressed) / सरित (river) / सर (lake) / जल (water) / बिनु (without) / भयउ (became) / अचेत (unconscious)
ramacharitamanas::872.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::872.essence: Pursuit without rest ends in collapse.
ramacharitamanas::872.simple_meaning: The king grows exhausted and desperate as he searches for water with his horse. With no water to be found, he collapses.
ramacharitamanas::872.simple_insight: Even strength fails when basic needs are unmet.
