ramacharitamanas::872.detailed_meaning: Pratapabhanu has wandered deep into the forest after chasing the boar. Tired, hungry, and thirsty, he searches for water with his horse, but finds none. This verse shows his physical collapse before the next turn of the story.
ramacharitamanas::872.modern_relevance: You keep circling the city after a long day, phone dying, throat dry, and every café is closed. At some point, effort alone cannot carry you further.
ramacharitamanas::872.insight: It shifts attention from heroic striving to bodily limits and vulnerability.

ramacharitamanas::873.verse_sanskrit: फिरत बिपिन आश्रम एक देखा। तहँ बस नृपति कपट मुनिबेषा॥ जासु देस नृप लीन्ह छड़ाई। समर सेन तजि गयउ पराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::873.verse_hindi: वन में फिरते-फिरते उसने एक आश्रम देखा, वहाँ कपट से मुनि का वेष बनाए एक राजा रहता था, जिसका देश राजा प्रतापभानु ने छीन लिया था और जो सेना को छोड़कर युद्ध से भाग गया था ॥
ramacharitamanas::873.english_translation: Roaming through the forest, he saw one hermitage. There lived a king disguised as a mendicant. He had lost his kingdom to King Pratapbhanu and had abandoned his army, fleeing the battle.
ramacharitamanas::873.translation_literal: फिरत (roaming) / बिपिन (forest) / आश्रम (hermitage) / एक (one) / देखा (saw) / तहँ (there) / बस (dwelt) / नृपति (king) / कपट (deceitfully) / मुनिबेषा (in sage's guise) / जासु (whose) / देस (kingdom) / नृप (king) / लीन्ह (took) / छड़ाई (away) / समर (battle) / सेन (army) / तजि (leaving) / गयउ (went) / पराई (away)
ramacharitamanas::873.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::873.essence: A false renunciate can still carry the wound of flight.
ramacharitamanas::873.simple_meaning: While wandering in the forest, the king saw a hermitage where a deposed ruler lived in disguise, having lost his kingdom and fled the battle.
ramacharitamanas::873.simple_insight: No throne or disguise can hide fear for long.
ramacharitamanas::873.detailed_meaning: Pratapbhanu keeps roaming the forest after losing his way. He comes upon a hermitage and finds a fallen king living there in a false ascetic disguise, a man who once abandoned his army and ran from battle. The scene sets up the next turn in the story.
ramacharitamanas::873.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a retreat who speaks softly, dresses simply, and seems transformed. Then you learn they are hiding from the very life they abandoned. The costume cannot erase the escape.
ramacharitamanas::873.insight: It prepares the reader for a hidden identity and shows how defeat can drive a person into disguise.

ramacharitamanas::874.verse_sanskrit: समय प्रतापभानु कर जानी। आपन अति असमय अनुमानी॥ गयउ न गृह मन बहुत गलानी। मिला न राजहि नृप अभिमानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::874.verse_hindi: प्रतापभानु का समय (अच्छे दिन) जानकर और अपना कुसमय (बुरे दिन) अनुमानकर उसके मन में बड़ी ग्लानि हुई। इससे वह न तो घर गया और न अभिमानी होने के कारण राजा प्रतापभानु से ही मिला (मेल किया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::874.english_translation: Knowing the time was favorable for King Pratapbhanu and sensing his own time was unfavorable, he felt deep shame. So he did not return home, and pride kept him from meeting the king.
ramacharitamanas::874.translation_literal: समय (time) / प्रतापभानु (Pratapbhanu) / कर (of) / जानी (knowing) / आपन (own) / अति (very) / असमय (bad time) / अनुमानी (sensing) / गयउ (went) / न (not) / गृह (home) / मन (mind) / बहुत (much) / गलानी (shame) / मिला (met) / न (not) / राजहि (the king) / नृप (king) / अभिमानी (proud)
ramacharitamanas::874.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::874.essence: Shame and pride can both keep a fallen person from seeking help.
ramacharitamanas::874.simple_meaning: He sees that the king’s fortune is rising while his own has fallen, and shame keeps him from going home or facing the king.
ramacharitamanas::874.simple_insight: Pride can trap a person between regret and avoidance.
ramacharitamanas::874.detailed_meaning: The disguised king, now living in the forest after losing his kingdom, reads the moment and feels his own ruin. Shame stops him from going home, and pride stops him from approaching Pratapbhanu. The scene pushes the story into another hidden meeting.
ramacharitamanas::874.modern_relevance: You get the message that someone else is moving ahead while you feel left behind. Shame says disappear; pride says don’t reach out. Both can keep you isolated.
ramacharitamanas::874.insight: It shows how status loss can turn into withdrawal instead of repair.

ramacharitamanas::875.verse_sanskrit: रिस उर मारि रंक जिमि राजा। बिपिन बसइ तापस कें साजा॥ तासु समीप गवन नृप कीन्हा। यह प्रतापरबि तेहिं तब चीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::875.verse_hindi: दरिद्र की भाँति मन ही में क्रोध को मारकर वह राजा तपस्वी के वेष में वन में रहता था। राजा (प्रतापभानु) उसी के पास गया। उसने तुरंत पहचान लिया कि यह प्रतापभानु है ॥
ramacharitamanas::875.english_translation: Having crushed anger within, the king lived in the forest like a beggar, dressed as a hermit. When Pratapbhanu approached him, he immediately recognized him.
ramacharitamanas::875.translation_literal: रिस (anger) / उर (heart) / मारि (having killed) / रंक (beggar) / जिमि (like) / राजा (king) / बिपिन (forest) / बसइ (lives) / तापस (ascetic) / कें (of) / साजा (dress) / तासु (his) / समीप (near) / गवन (approach) / नृप (king) / कीन्हा (did) / यह (this) / प्रतापरबि (Pratapbhanu) / तेहिं (by him) / तब (then) / चीन्हा (recognized)
ramacharitamanas::875.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::875.essence: Disguise can hide rank, not recognition.
ramacharitamanas::875.simple_meaning: A king hid his anger, lived in the forest as an ascetic, and recognized another king who came near him.
ramacharitamanas::875.simple_insight: Not every calm face is innocent. Clear seeing notices what disguise tries to hide.
ramacharitamanas::875.detailed_meaning: Pratapbhanu has wandered into the forest and found a hermitage where a fallen king lives in disguise. The man has mastered his anger and wears the clothes of a hermit, but he instantly sees who is approaching. This verse moves the story from disguise to recognition.
ramacharitamanas::875.modern_relevance: You walk into a room thinking no one knows what you are carrying. Someone with sharper attention notices the strain in your face before you speak.
ramacharitamanas::875.insight: It shows that outer roles can hide inner states, but careful awareness still reads the truth.

ramacharitamanas::876.verse_sanskrit: राउ तृषित नहिं सो पहिचाना। देखि सुबेष महामुनि जाना॥ उतरि तुरग तें कीन्ह प्रनामा। परम चतुर न कहेउ निज नामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::876.verse_hindi: राजा प्यासा होने के कारण (व्याकुलता में) उसे पहचान न सका। सुंदर वेष देखकर राजा ने उसे महामुनि समझा और घोड़े से उतरकर उसे प्रणाम किया, परन्तु बड़ा चतुर होने के कारण राजा ने उसे अपना नाम नहीं बताया ॥
ramacharitamanas::876.english_translation: The king, thirsty and distracted, did not recognize him. Seeing his fine disguise, the king took him for a great sage. He got down from the horse and bowed, but the clever king did not reveal his own name.
ramacharitamanas::876.translation_literal: राउ (king) / तृषित (thirsty) / नहिं (not) / सो (him) / पहिचाना (recognized) / देखि (seeing) / सुबेष (fine disguise) / महामुनि (great sage) / जाना (considered) / उतरि (getting down) / तुरग (horse) / तें (from) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रनामा (bowed) / परम (very) / चतुर (clever) / न (not) / कहेउ (said) / निज (own) / नामा (name)
ramacharitamanas::876.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::876.essence: Need makes pride pause, and courtesy remains.
ramacharitamanas::876.simple_meaning: The thirsty king mistakes the disguised man for a sage, bows to him, and keeps his own identity hidden.
ramacharitamanas::876.simple_insight: Pride softens when need appears. A person can still act respectfully even in uncertainty.
ramacharitamanas::876.detailed_meaning: King Pratapabhanu, hungry and thirsty in the forest, meets a man in a beautiful disguise. Unable to see through the appearance, he bows with respect but keeps his own name hidden. The scene prepares the next turn of the trick.
ramacharitamanas::876.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a difficult moment and cannot tell who they really are. You still choose courtesy, because humility matters more than control.
ramacharitamanas::876.insight: It shifts attention from status to conduct: even confusion can be met with respectful restraint.

ramacharitamanas::877.verse_sanskrit: भूपति तृषित बिलोकि तेहिं सरबरू दीन्ह देखाइ। मज्जन पान समेत हय कीन्ह नृपति हरषाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::877.verse_hindi: राजा को प्यासा देखकर उसने सरोवर दिखला दिया। हर्षित होकर राजा ने घोड़े सहित उसमें स्नान और जलपान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::877.english_translation: Seeing the king thirsty, he showed him a lake. Delighted, the king bathed and drank there with his horse.
ramacharitamanas::877.translation_literal: भूपति (the king) / तृषित (thirsty) / बिलोकि (seeing) / तेहिं (by him) / सरबरू (lake) / दीन्ह (was given) / देखाइ (showing) / मज्जन (bathing) / पान (drinking) / समेत (together with) / हय (horse) / कीन्ह (did) / नृपति (the king) / हरषाइ (delighted)
ramacharitamanas::877.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::877.essence: Kindness begins with noticing another’s need.
ramacharitamanas::877.simple_meaning: Seeing the king’s thirst, the ascetic showed him a lake. The king happily bathed and drank there with his horse.
ramacharitamanas::877.simple_insight: A small act of care can restore someone completely.
ramacharitamanas::877.detailed_meaning: King Pratapabhanu has reached the forest in disguise and met the ascetic. Seeing the king thirsty, the ascetic points out a lake. The king drinks, bathes, and feels relieved before the deeper exchange begins.
ramacharitamanas::877.modern_relevance: You hand someone a glass of water after a long, hot commute. It seems small, but that one gesture can change the whole mood of the day.
ramacharitamanas::877.insight: It highlights simple hospitality before the story turns to deeper instruction.

ramacharitamanas::878.verse_sanskrit: गै श्रम सकल सुखी नृप भयऊ। निज आश्रम तापस लै गयऊ॥ आसन दीन्ह अस्त रबि जानी। पुनि तापस बोलेउ मृदु बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::878.verse_hindi: सारी थकावट मिट गई, राजा सुखी हो गया। तब तपस्वी उसे अपने आश्रम में ले गया और सूर्यास्त का समय जानकर उसने (राजा को बैठने के लिए) आसन दिया। फिर वह तपस्वी कोमल वाणी से बोला- ॥
ramacharitamanas::878.english_translation: The king’s fatigue vanished. The ascetic took him to his own hermitage, gave him a seat when he saw the sun had set, and then spoke in a gentle voice.
ramacharitamanas::878.translation_literal: गै (went away) / श्रम (fatigue) / सकल (all) / सुखी (contented) / नृप (king) / भयऊ (became) / निज (own) / आश्रम (hermitage) / तापस (ascetic) / लै (taking) / गयऊ (went) / आसन (seat) / दीन्ह (gave) / अस्त (setting) / रबि (sun) / जानी (knowing) / पुनि (then) / तापस (ascetic) / बोलेउ (spoke) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (speech)
ramacharitamanas::878.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::878.essence: Gentle hospitality opens the way for honest speech.
ramacharitamanas::878.simple_meaning: The king rests at the ascetic’s hermitage, and the ascetic treats him kindly before asking anything.
ramacharitamanas::878.simple_insight: Kindness often begins with simple care: a place to sit, a pause, and a gentle voice.
ramacharitamanas::878.detailed_meaning: The king, weary from travel, has been guided by a strange ascetic who first helped him with water. Now the ascetic brings him to his hermitage, seats him before sunset, and prepares to speak. This is the calm before the real question begins.
ramacharitamanas::878.modern_relevance: After a long train ride, a stranger offers you a chair, water, and a quiet minute before asking who you are. That small care lowers the guard before any real conversation.
ramacharitamanas::878.insight: It shifts attention from the event to the atmosphere of trust being created.

ramacharitamanas::879.verse_sanskrit: को तुम्ह कस बन फिरहु अकेलें। सुंदर जुबा जीव परहेलें॥ चक्रबर्ति के लच्छन तोरें। देखत दया लागि अति मोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::879.verse_hindi: तुम कौन हो? सुंदर युवक होकर, जीवन की परवाह न करके वन में अकेले क्यों फिर रहे हो? तुम्हारे चक्रवर्ती राजा के से लक्षण देखकर मुझे बड़ी दया आती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::879.english_translation: Who are you, and why do you wander alone in the forest, handsome youth? Seeing the marks of a universal ruler in you, I feel great pity.
ramacharitamanas::879.translation_literal: को (who) / तुम्ह (you) / कस (why) / बन (forest) / फिरहु (wander) / अकेलें (alone) / सुंदर (beautiful) / जुबा (youth) / जीव (life) / परहेलें (without caring) / चक्रबर्ति (universal ruler) / के (of) / लच्छन (marks) / तोरें (your) / देखत (seeing) / दया (pity) / लागि (came) / अति (greatly) / मोरें (to me)
ramacharitamanas::879.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::879.essence: Royal bearing can still look like loneliness in the forest.
ramacharitamanas::879.simple_meaning: The speaker asks an unknown young man who he is, why he is alone in the forest, and says his royal bearing inspires pity.
ramacharitamanas::879.simple_insight: Even a stranger can recognize dignity, loss, and vulnerability at a glance.
ramacharitamanas::879.detailed_meaning: While wandering in the forest, the minister of King Pratapbhanu comes upon a solitary young man. His polished bearing suggests high birth, so the minister pauses and speaks with concern before the story turns to identity and circumstance.
ramacharitamanas::879.modern_relevance: You meet someone on a late train platform, dressed well but looking stranded. Before you know their story, you can still sense they have fallen far from where they belong.
ramacharitamanas::879.insight: It shifts attention from the surface encounter to the hidden story behind a person’s condition.

ramacharitamanas::880.verse_sanskrit: नाम प्रतापभानु अवनीसा। तासु सचिव मैं सुनहु मुनीसा॥ फिरत अहेरें परेउँ भुलाई। बड़ें भाग देखेउँ पद आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::880.verse_hindi: (राजा ने कहा-) हे मुनीश्वर! सुनिए, प्रतापभानु नाम का एक राजा है, मैं उसका मंत्री हूँ। शिकार के लिए फिरते हुए राह भूल गया हूँ। बड़े भाग्य से यहाँ आकर मैंने आपके चरणों के दर्शन पाए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::880.english_translation: I am a minister of King Pratapbhanu, lord of this land. While hunting, I lost my way. By great good fortune, I have come to your feet.
ramacharitamanas::880.translation_literal: नाम (named) / प्रतापभानु (Pratapbhanu) / अवनीसा (lord of the earth) / तासु (his) / सचिव (minister) / मैं (I) / सुनहु (listen) / मुनीसा (O sage) / फिरत (wandering) / अहेरें (while hunting) / परेउँ (I fell/lost) / भुलाई (in forgetting the way) / बड़ें (great) / भाग (fortune) / देखेउँ (I saw) / पद (feet) / आई (coming)
ramacharitamanas::880.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::880.essence: What looks like getting lost can be the start of grace.
ramacharitamanas::880.simple_meaning: The speaker introduces himself as King Pratapbhanu’s minister and says he lost his way while hunting. He feels fortunate to have reached the sage’s feet.
ramacharitamanas::880.simple_insight: A lost moment can become grace when it brings you to the right place.
ramacharitamanas::880.detailed_meaning: A stranger arrives at the sage’s hermitage after losing his way in the hunt. He politely explains who he is and why he is there. This is the opening of the encounter that will soon reveal a deeper turn of fate.
ramacharitamanas::880.modern_relevance: You take the wrong exit after a long drive and end up at a quiet house you never meant to visit. What felt like a mistake becomes the meeting that changes the day.
ramacharitamanas::880.insight: It frames an accidental meeting as fortunate, preparing the listener for a hidden turning point.

ramacharitamanas::881.verse_sanskrit: हम कहँ दुर्लभ दरस तुम्हारा। जानत हौं कछु भल होनिहारा॥ कह मुनि तात भयउ अँधिआरा। जोजन सत्तरि नगरु तुम्हारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::881.verse_hindi: हमें आपका दर्शन दुर्लभ था, इससे जान पड़ता है कुछ भला होने वाला है। मुनि ने कहा- हे तात! अँधेरा हो गया। तुम्हारा नगर यहाँ से सत्तर योजन पर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::881.english_translation: “Your sight is hard to obtain. I know that some good fortune is near.” The sage said, “Dear one, darkness has fallen. Your city is seventy leagues away.”
ramacharitamanas::881.translation_literal: हम (we) / कहँ (for me) / दुर्लभ (rare) / दरस (sight) / तुम्हारा (your) / जानत (knowing) / हौं (I am) / कछु (something) / भल (good) / होनिहारा (about to happen) / कह (said) / मुनि (sage) / तात (dear one) / भयउ (has become) / अँधिआरा (darkness) / जोजन (league) / सत्तरि (seventy) / नगरु (city) / तुम्हारा (your)
ramacharitamanas::881.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::881.essence: A fortunate meeting can arrive just as night makes action impossible.
ramacharitamanas::881.simple_meaning: The sage tells the traveler that meeting him is a good sign, then warns that night has fallen and the city is far away.
ramacharitamanas::881.simple_insight: A kind meeting can still end in practical limits. Warmth and realism can live together.
ramacharitamanas::881.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a sage speaks with a lost traveler who has appeared at an auspicious moment. He feels the meeting itself is a good sign, but he also warns that darkness has already fallen and the city is still far away.
ramacharitamanas::881.modern_relevance: You finally meet the right person after a long day, and the conversation feels meaningful. Still, the train is gone, the roads are dark, and you need to stay put tonight.
ramacharitamanas::881.insight: It teaches you to hold both intuition and reality at once: a hopeful sign does not cancel practical limits.

ramacharitamanas::882.verse_sanskrit: निसा घोर गंभीर बन पंथ न सुनहु सुजान। बसहु आजु अस जानि तुम्ह जाएहु होत बिहान ॥
ramacharitamanas::882.verse_hindi: हे सुजान! सुनो, घोर अँधेरी रात है, घना जंगल है, रास्ता नहीं है, ऐसा समझकर तुम आज यहीं ठहर जाओ, सबेरा होते ही चले जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::882.english_translation: O wise one, the night is deep and the forest path is dark. Stay here today, and go at dawn.
ramacharitamanas::882.translation_literal: निसा (night) / घोर (fierce, deep) / गंभीर (dense, profound) / बन (forest) / पंथ (path) / न (not) / सुनहु (listen) / सुजान (wise one) / बसहु (stay) / आजु (today) / अस (thus) / जानि (knowing) / तुम्ह (you) / जाएहु (go) / होत (becoming) / बिहान (dawn)
ramacharitamanas::882.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::882.essence: Wait for daylight before you move.
ramacharitamanas::882.simple_meaning: The night is too dark and the forest road is unsafe. Stay where you are and travel after sunrise.
ramacharitamanas::882.simple_insight: Sometimes wisdom is simply not forcing the next step before light arrives.
ramacharitamanas::882.detailed_meaning: A lost minister reaches a forest at night and is warned by a sage that the path is too dangerous to take now. The verse pauses the journey, showing that safety sometimes means waiting for dawn.
ramacharitamanas::882.modern_relevance: You are driving on an unfamiliar road after midnight, GPS drifting and fatigue rising. The smartest move is not courage; it is stopping and waiting for daylight.
ramacharitamanas::882.insight: It teaches you to delay action until conditions become clear and safe.

ramacharitamanas::883.verse_sanskrit: तुलसी जसि भवतब्यता तैसी मिलइ सहाइ। आपुनु आवइ ताहि पहिं ताहि तहाँ लै जाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::883.verse_hindi: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- जैसी भवितव्यता (होनहार) होती है, वैसी ही सहायता मिल जाती है। या तो वह आप ही उसके पास आती है या उसको वहाँ ले जाती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::883.english_translation: Tulsidas says: Whatever is meant to happen finds its own helper. Either it comes by itself, or it brings the person there.
ramacharitamanas::883.translation_literal: तुलसी (Tulsidas) / जसि (as) / भवतब्यता (what is destined to happen) / तैसी (that way) / मिलइ (meets) / सहाइ (helper) / आपुनु (itself) / आवइ (comes) / ताहि (to it) / पहिं (near) / ताहि (that) / तहाँ (there) / लै (taking) / जाइ (goes)
ramacharitamanas::883.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::883.essence: What is meant to happen brings its own help.
ramacharitamanas::883.simple_meaning: Whatever is truly meant to happen will find support. Sometimes help comes to you; sometimes life carries you to the right place.
ramacharitamanas::883.simple_insight: You can stop forcing every outcome. What is meant to unfold will find a way.
ramacharitamanas::883.detailed_meaning: A traveler has been told to stay the night because the forest is dark and the path is unsafe. Tulsidas pauses the scene to say that when something is meant to happen, the needed help appears on its own.
ramacharitamanas::883.modern_relevance: You missed the last train, then a friend called with a spare room. The plan looked broken, but life quietly rearranged itself around what needed to happen.
ramacharitamanas::883.insight: It shifts the mind from anxious control to trust in the unfolding of events.

ramacharitamanas::884.verse_sanskrit: भलेहिं नाथ आयसु धरि सीसा। बाँधि तुरग तरु बैठ महीसा॥ नृप बहु भाँति प्रसंसेउ ताही। चरन बंदि निज भाग्य सराही ॥
ramacharitamanas::884.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! बहुत अच्छा, ऐसा कहकर और उसकी आज्ञा सिर चढ़ाकर, घोड़े को वृक्ष से बाँधकर राजा बैठ गया। राजा ने उसकी बहुत प्रकार से प्रशंसा की और उसके चरणों की वंदना करके अपने भाग्य की सराहना की ॥
ramacharitamanas::884.english_translation: “Very well, Lord,” he said, taking the command on his head. He tied the horse to a tree and sat down. The king praised him in many ways, bowed at his feet, and blessed his own fortune.
ramacharitamanas::884.translation_literal: भलेहिं (very well) / नाथ (Lord) / आयसु (command) / धरि (placing) / सीसा (on the head) / बाँधि (tying) / तुरग (horse) / तरु (tree) / बैठ (sat) / महीसा (king) / नृप (king) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / प्रसंसेउ (praised) / ताही (that one) / चरन (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / निज (own) / भाग्य (fortune) / सराही (praised)
ramacharitamanas::884.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::884.essence: True nobility bows before wise guidance.
ramacharitamanas::884.simple_meaning: The king accepts the order, secures the horse, and praises the one who guided him. He bows in gratitude and feels blessed by the encounter.
ramacharitamanas::884.simple_insight: Humility turns a difficult moment into gratitude instead of resistance.
ramacharitamanas::884.detailed_meaning: On the forest road at night, the king is told to stop and wait. He obeys without argument, ties up the horse, sits down, and honors the one who advised him. The scene shows reverence, patience, and trust before the next instruction arrives.
ramacharitamanas::884.modern_relevance: Your plan gets interrupted on a dark road, and the person with more experience says, “Stop here.” You could bristle — or you could recognize protection in the delay.
ramacharitamanas::884.insight: It trains the mind to accept guidance quickly and respond with gratitude, not ego.

ramacharitamanas::885.verse_sanskrit: पुनि बोलेउ मृदु गिरा सुहाई। जानि पिता प्रभु करउँ ढिठाई॥ मोहि मुनीस सुत सेवक जानी। नाथ नाम निज कहहु बखानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::885.verse_hindi: फिर सुंदर कोमल वाणी से कहा- हे प्रभो! आपको पिता जानकर मैं ढिठाई करता हूँ। हे मुनीश्वर! मुझे अपना पुत्र और सेवक जानकर अपना नाम (धाम) विस्तार से बतलाइए ॥
ramacharitamanas::885.english_translation: Then he spoke again in a soft, pleasant voice: "Knowing you as my father, I am being bold. O sage, knowing me as your son and servant, please tell me your name and lineage in full."
ramacharitamanas::885.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / बोलेउ (spoke) / मृदु (soft) / गिरा (voice) / सुहाई (pleasant) / जानि (knowing) / पिता (father) / प्रभु (lord/master) / करउँ (I do) / ढिठाई (boldness) / मोहि (me) / मुनीस (sage among sages) / सुत (son) / सेवक (servant) / जानी (knowing) / नाथ (lord) / नाम (name) / निज (own) / कहहु (tell) / बखानी (explain in detail)
ramacharitamanas::885.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::885.essence: Respectful humility makes the right question possible.
ramacharitamanas::885.simple_meaning: A respectful stranger speaks gently to the sage, calling him father and asking him to identify himself and explain his name and lineage.
ramacharitamanas::885.simple_insight: Humility opens the door to real conversation.
ramacharitamanas::885.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a king has just been received with kindness by a learned sage. The stranger speaks softly, claiming a childlike closeness and asking the sage to introduce himself fully. The moment builds trust before the deeper exchange begins.
ramacharitamanas::885.modern_relevance: You meet someone generous at a retreat and, instead of rushing in, you ask who they are and how they came to be there. Respect first. Curiosity second. That order changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::885.insight: It teaches you to approach wisdom with humility before asking for answers.

ramacharitamanas::886.verse_sanskrit: तेहि न जान नृप नृपहि सो जाना। भूप सुहृद सो कपट सयाना॥ बैरी पुनि छत्री पुनि राजा। छल बल कीन्ह चहइ निज काजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::886.verse_hindi: राजा ने उसको नहीं पहचाना, पर वह राजा को पहचान गया था। राजा तो शुद्ध हृदय था और वह कपट करने में चतुर था। एक तो वैरी, फिर जाति का क्षत्रिय, फिर राजा। वह छल-बल से अपना काम बनाना चाहता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::886.english_translation: The king did not recognize him, but he recognized the king. The king had a pure heart, while he was clever in deceit. An enemy, yet a Kshatriya, yet a king, he wanted to get his way through trickery and force.
ramacharitamanas::886.translation_literal: तेहि (him) / न (not) / जान (know) / नृप (king) / नृपहि (the king) / सो (he) / जाना (knew) / भूप (king) / सुहृद (well-hearted) / सो (that one) / कपट (deceit) / सयाना (skilled) / बैरी (enemy) / पुनि (again) / छत्री (Kshatriya) / पुनि (again) / राजा (king) / छल (trickery) / बल (force) / कीन्ह (did) / चहइ (wants) / निज (his own) / काजा (work)
ramacharitamanas::886.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::886.essence: Pure hearts can be outmatched by cunning motives.
ramacharitamanas::886.simple_meaning: The king does not see the man’s true nature, but the man sees the king clearly. One is sincere; the other is skilled in deceit and wants to use trickery and force.
ramacharitamanas::886.simple_insight: Not everyone who approaches you is honest. Clear seeing matters when motives are hidden.
ramacharitamanas::886.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, a stranger stands before the king with a hidden agenda. Janak remains open-hearted, but the visitor is an enemy who knows exactly how to manipulate the moment. The verse exposes the contrast before the tension rises.
ramacharitamanas::886.modern_relevance: A smooth-talking person shows up in a meeting with a friendly smile and a hidden agenda. You feel the shift before anyone else does. This verse names that uneasy clarity.
ramacharitamanas::886.insight: It teaches you to notice hidden intent beneath polite words, and to value sincerity over clever manipulation.

ramacharitamanas::887.verse_sanskrit: समुझि राजसुख दुखित अराती। अवाँ अनल इव सुलगइ छाती॥ ससरल बचन नृप के सुनि काना। बयर सँभारि हृदयँ हरषाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::887.verse_hindi: वह शत्रु अपने राज्य सुख को समझ करके (स्मरण करके) दुःखी था। उसकी छाती (कुम्हार के) आँवे की आग की तरह (भीतर ही भीतर) सुलग रही थी। राजा के सरल वचन कान से सुनकर, अपने वैर को यादकर वह हृदय में हर्षित हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::887.english_translation: Remembering his royal comfort, the enemy burned with hidden anger. Hearing the king's plain words, he rejoiced inwardly at his old hatred.
ramacharitamanas::887.translation_literal: समुझि (remembering) / राजसुख (royal comfort) / दुखित (grieved) / अराती (enemy) / अवाँ (furnace) / अनल (fire) / इव (like) / सुलगइ (smolders) / छाती (chest)॥ / ससरल (plain) / बचन (words) / नृप (king) / के (of) / सुनि (hearing) / काना (ears) / बयर (hatred) / सँभारि (remembering) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / हरषाना (rejoiced)॥
ramacharitamanas::887.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::887.essence: Old hatred can smolder beneath polite words.
ramacharitamanas::887.simple_meaning: The enemy is still carrying old hatred. The king speaks simply, and that only makes the enemy's hidden anger flare up.
ramacharitamanas::887.simple_insight: Hidden resentment can turn even kind words into fuel for more bitterness.
ramacharitamanas::887.detailed_meaning: In the palace scene, a deceitful enemy stands before the king. He remembers the comfort he once enjoyed, feels the heat of loss, and hears the king's gentle words. Instead of softening, he secretly rejoices in his grudge and plans his next move.
ramacharitamanas::887.modern_relevance: Someone smiles at your apology, but their jaw stays tight. They say the right words, yet the old injury is still burning underneath, waiting for a chance to come back out.
ramacharitamanas::887.insight: It shows how unresolved resentment distorts hearing, so even plain speech gets filtered through old injury.

ramacharitamanas::888.verse_sanskrit: कपट बोरि बानी मृदल बोलेउ जुगुति समेत। नाम हमार भिखारि अब निर्धन रहित निकेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::888.verse_hindi: वह कपट में डुबोकर बड़ी युक्ति के साथ कोमल वाणी बोला- अब हमारा नाम भिखारी है, क्योंकि हम निर्धन और अनिकेत (घर-द्वारहीन) हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::888.english_translation: He spoke sweetly, masking deceit with cleverness: “Now my name is beggar, for I am poor and homeless.”
ramacharitamanas::888.translation_literal: कपट (deceit) / बोरि (drenched) / बानी (speech) / मृदल (soft, gentle) / बोलेउ (spoke) / जुगुति (clever strategy) / समेत (together with) / नाम (name) / हमार (my) / भिखारि (beggar) / अब (now) / निर्धन (poor) / रहित (without) / निकेत (home, dwelling)
ramacharitamanas::888.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::888.simple_meaning: He speaks softly and cleverly, hiding his deceit. He pretends to be a poor, homeless beggar.
ramacharitamanas::888.simple_insight: Sweet words can hide a selfish plan.
ramacharitamanas::888.detailed_meaning: In this scene, a cunning enemy approaches the king with a polished voice. He hides his true intent, calling himself a beggar and claiming poverty and homelessness. The verse shows the face of deception before the king answers.
ramacharitamanas::888.modern_relevance: Someone messages with perfect politeness, but every line is designed to get something from you. The tone feels kind; the motive is not.
ramacharitamanas::888.insight: It teaches you to look past soft language and notice the intent underneath.

ramacharitamanas::889.verse_sanskrit: कह नृप जे बिग्यान निधाना। तुम्ह सारिखे गलित अभिमाना॥ सदा रहहिं अपनपौ दुराएँ। सब बिधि कुसल कुबेष बनाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::889.verse_hindi: राजा ने कहा- जो आपके सदृश विज्ञान के निधान और सर्वथा अभिमानरहित होते हैं, वे अपने स्वरूप को सदा छिपाए रहते हैं, क्योंकि कुवेष बनाकर रहने में ही सब तरह का कल्याण है (प्रकट संत वेश में मान होने की सम्भावना है और मान से पतन की) ॥
ramacharitamanas::889.english_translation: The king said, 'Those who are like you are treasures of wisdom and free from pride. They always hide their true nature, because wearing a disguise brings safety in every way.'
ramacharitamanas::889.translation_literal: कह (said) / नृप (the king) / जे (those who) / बिग्यान निधाना (treasures of wisdom) / तुम्ह सारिखे (like you) / गलित अभिमाना (free from pride) / सदा (always) / रहहिं (remain) / अपनपौ (their own nature) / दुराएँ (hiding) / सब बिधि (in every way) / कुसल (safe / well) / कुबेष (disguise) / बनाएँ (by making)
ramacharitamanas::889.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::889.essence: Real wisdom hides itself and stays untouched by pride.
ramacharitamanas::889.simple_meaning: Truly wise people do not advertise themselves. They stay humble and often keep a low profile, because pride and display can lead to trouble.
ramacharitamanas::889.simple_insight: Humility protects what ego would expose.
ramacharitamanas::889.detailed_meaning: A king speaks to a disguised ascetic after sensing deep wisdom beneath the rough appearance. He praises the hidden, pride-free life: the truly wise do not seek display, because concealment guards them from vanity and harm.
ramacharitamanas::889.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a train platform in plain clothes who turns out to be far more accomplished than they look. The point is not image — it is the safety of staying unadvertised.
ramacharitamanas::889.insight: It shifts attention from self-display to quiet protection of character.

ramacharitamanas::890.verse_sanskrit: तेहि तें कहहिं संत श्रुति टेरें। परम अकिंचन प्रिय हरि केरें॥ तुम्ह सम अधन भिखारि अगेहा। होत बिरंचि सिवहि संदेहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::890.verse_hindi: इसी से तो संत और वेद पुकारकर कहते हैं कि परम अकिंचन (सर्वथा अहंकार, ममता और मानरहित) ही भगवान को प्रिय होते हैं। आप सरीखे निर्धन, भिखारी और गृहहीनों को देखकर ब्रह्मा और शिवजी को भी संदेह हो जाता है (कि वे वास्तविक संत हैं या भिखारी) ॥
ramacharitamanas::890.english_translation: Because of this, the saints and the Vedas cry out that the one who is utterly without possessions is dear to Hari. Seeing someone like you, so poor, a beggar, and without a home, even Brahma and Shiva would wonder whether he is a true saint or a beggar.
ramacharitamanas::890.translation_literal: तेहि तें (because of that) / कहहिं (say) / संत (the saints) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / टेरें (calling out) / परम (utterly) / अकिंचन (without possessions) / प्रिय (dear) / हरि (Hari) / केरें (of) / तुम्ह (you) / सम (like) / अधन (poor) / भिखारि (beggar) / अगेहा (without a home) / होत (becoming) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / सिवहि (to Shiva) / संदेहा (doubt)
ramacharitamanas::890.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::890.essence: Complete humility makes a person dear to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::890.simple_meaning: Saints and scripture praise the one who has no pride, no possessions, and no home of attachment. Such emptiness makes a person dear to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::890.simple_insight: There is dignity in having nothing to prove. Letting go can make you more lovable, not less.
ramacharitamanas::890.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, a disguised figure is speaking humbly while testing the court. The speaker praises the saintly ideal of utter non-possession, saying that true humility is so complete it can even confuse Brahma and Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::890.modern_relevance: You show up to a gathering with nothing to impress anyone: no status story, no polished performance, no need to be seen. That quiet simplicity can feel strangely powerful.
ramacharitamanas::890.insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to self-emptying, treating humility as spiritual strength rather than weakness.

ramacharitamanas::891.verse_sanskrit: जोसि सोसि तव चरन नमामी। मो पर कृपा करिअ अब स्वामी॥ सहज प्रीति भूपति कै देखी। आपु बिषय बिस्वास बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::891.verse_hindi: आप जो हों सो हों (अर्थात् जो कोई भी हों), मैं आपके चरणों में नमस्कार करता हूँ। हे स्वामी! अब मुझ पर कृपा कीजिए। अपने ऊपर राजा की स्वाभाविक प्रीति और अपने विषय में उसका अधिक विश्वास देखकर ॥
ramacharitamanas::891.english_translation: Whatever you are, I bow at your feet. Lord, now show me grace. Seeing the king's natural affection and his special trust in his own matter,
ramacharitamanas::891.translation_literal: जोसि (whatever) / सोसि (that you are) / तव (your) / चरन (feet) / नमामी (I bow) / मो (to me) / पर (on) / कृपा (grace) / करिअ (do) / अब (now) / स्वामी (lord) / सहज (natural) / प्रीति (affection) / भूपति (king) / कै (of) / देखी (seeing) / आपु (self) / बिषय (in the matter) / बिस्वास (trust) / बिसेषी (special)
ramacharitamanas::891.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::891.essence: Humility opens the way before words do.
ramacharitamanas::891.simple_meaning: The speaker bows respectfully and asks for mercy, noticing that the king feels especially trusting and affectionate.
ramacharitamanas::891.simple_insight: Courtesy can open the door before truth is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::891.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, a disguised figure approaches King Janak with humility. He bows first, asks for grace, and watches Janak’s natural warmth and confidence. That visible trust becomes the opening for the next move in the exchange.
ramacharitamanas::891.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where someone has already softened. A respectful opening lands differently when the other person’s guard is down.
ramacharitamanas::891.insight: It shows how humility and careful reading of another person can shape the next step in a conversation.

ramacharitamanas::892.verse_sanskrit: सब प्रकार राजहि अपनाई। बोलेउ अधिक सनेह जनाई॥ सुनु सतिभाउ कहउँ महिपाला। इहाँ बसत बीते बहु काला ॥
ramacharitamanas::892.verse_hindi: सब प्रकार से राजा को अपने वश में करके, अधिक स्नेह दिखाता हुआ वह (कपट-तपस्वी) बोला- हे राजन् ! सुनो, मैं तुमसे सत्य कहता हूँ, मुझे यहाँ रहते बहुत समय बीत गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::892.english_translation: Having won the king over in every way, he spoke, showing great affection: “Listen, O king, I speak truthfully. I have lived here for a long time.”
ramacharitamanas::892.translation_literal: सब प्रकार (in every way) / राजहि (the king) / अपनाई (having won over) / बोलेउ (he spoke) / अधिक (greatly) / सनेह (affection) / जनाई (showing) / सुनु (listen) / सति-भाउ (truthful intent) / कहउँ (I speak) / महिपाला (O king) / इहाँ (here) / बसत (living) / बीते (passed) / बहु (many) / काला (times)
ramacharitamanas::892.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::892.essence: Warm words can be a tool of control.
ramacharitamanas::892.simple_meaning: The disguised ascetic flatters the king and speaks gently, claiming he has lived there for a long time and is speaking honestly.
ramacharitamanas::892.simple_insight: Not every soft voice is sincere. Warmth can hide a motive.
ramacharitamanas::892.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the disguised ascetic has already drawn the king in with humility and praise. Now he deepens the charm with affectionate words and a claim of long residence, preparing the ground for his real purpose.
ramacharitamanas::892.modern_relevance: A stranger praises your judgment, lowers his voice, and says he only wants to be honest. The friendliness feels safe, but the real test is whether the words are meant to inform or to manipulate.
ramacharitamanas::892.insight: It trains you to notice charm as a tactic, not just a feeling.

ramacharitamanas::893.verse_sanskrit: अब लगि मोहि न मिलेउ कोउ मैं न जनावउँ काहु। लोकमान्यता अनल सम कर तप कानन दाहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::893.verse_hindi: अब तक न तो कोई मुझसे मिला और न मैं अपने को किसी पर प्रकट करता हूँ, क्योंकि लोक में प्रतिष्ठा अग्नि के समान है, जो तप रूपी वन को भस्म कर डालती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::893.english_translation: So far, no one has met me, and I do not reveal myself to anyone. Public reputation is like fire; it burns the forest of penance.
ramacharitamanas::893.translation_literal: अब लगि (until now) / मोहि (me) / न (not) / मिलेउ (met) / कोउ (anyone) / मैं (I) / न (not) / जनावउँ (reveal myself) / काहु (to anyone) / लोकमान्यता (public reputation / social esteem) / अनल (fire) / सम (like) / कर (doing) / तप (austerity / penance) / कानन (forest) / दाहु (burning)
ramacharitamanas::893.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::893.essence: Public admiration can destroy the very discipline it seems to honor.
ramacharitamanas::893.simple_meaning: A person says he stays hidden because public recognition can destroy inner discipline the way fire destroys a forest.
ramacharitamanas::893.simple_insight: It feels relieving to stop chasing visibility and protect the quiet work that actually changes you.
ramacharitamanas::893.detailed_meaning: A disguised ascetic is speaking to King Janaka in Mithila. He says he has remained unseen and unnamed because public admiration can consume hard-won discipline. The verse warns that praise itself can become a danger.
ramacharitamanas::893.modern_relevance: You post something vulnerable, and the applause starts coming in. Part of you wants more of it, but another part feels the practice slipping. This verse protects that second part.
ramacharitamanas::893.insight: It shifts attention from being seen to preserving the conditions that let character deepen.

ramacharitamanas::894.verse_sanskrit: तुलसी देखि सुबेषु भूलहिं मूढ़ न चतुर नर। सुंदर केकिहि पेखु बचन सुधा सम असन अहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::894.verse_hindi: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- सुंदर वेष देखकर मूढ़ नहीं (मूढ़ तो मूढ़ ही हैं), चतुर मनुष्य भी धोखा खा जाते हैं। सुंदर मोर को देखो, उसका वचन तो अमृत के समान है और आहार साँप का है ॥
ramacharitamanas::894.english_translation: Tulsidas says: Foolish people are deceived by a fine disguise, and even clever people can be fooled. Look at the peacock: its voice is sweet like nectar, but its food is a snake.
ramacharitamanas::894.translation_literal: तुलसी (Tulsidas) / देखि (seeing) / सुबेषु (fine disguise) / भूलहिं (are deceived) / मूढ़ (foolish) / न (not) / चतुर (clever) / नर (people) / सुंदर (beautiful) / केकिहि (peacock) / पेखु (look at) / बचन (voice) / सुधा (nectar) / सम (like) / असन (food) / अहि (snake)
ramacharitamanas::894.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::894.essence: Beauty can hide danger; clear seeing must go deeper than appearances.
ramacharitamanas::894.simple_meaning: A pleasing appearance can fool anyone, even intelligent people. The peacock looks beautiful and sounds sweet, but its food is a snake.
ramacharitamanas::894.simple_insight: Charm alone is not proof of goodness. Look deeper before you trust what shines.
ramacharitamanas::894.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas interrupts the story to warn the reader about appearances. A disguised trickster is speaking softly to King Janak, and the poet says that even smart people can be misled by beauty. The peacock image drives home the danger.
ramacharitamanas::894.modern_relevance: A polished profile, perfect smile, and calm voice can still hide selfish intent. The warning lands the moment you feel yourself trusting the packaging before the person.
ramacharitamanas::894.insight: It trains discernment: do not confuse attractive form with trustworthy nature.

ramacharitamanas::895.verse_sanskrit: तातें गुपुत रहउँ जग माहीं। हरि तजि किमपि प्रयोजन नाहीं॥ प्रभु जानत सब बिनहिं जनाए। कहहु कवनि सिधि लोक रिझाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::895.verse_hindi: (कपट-तपस्वी ने कहा-) इसी से मैं जगत में छिपकर रहता हूँ। श्री हरि को छोड़कर किसी से कुछ भी प्रयोजन नहीं रखता। प्रभु तो बिना जनाए ही सब जानते हैं। फिर कहो संसार को रिझाने से क्या सिद्धि मिलेगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::895.english_translation: That is why I remain hidden in the world. I seek nothing apart from Hari. The Lord knows everything without being told. So what gain comes from pleasing the crowd?
ramacharitamanas::895.translation_literal: तातें (therefore) / गुपुत (hidden) / रहउँ (I remain) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / हरि (Hari) / तजि (leaving) / किमपि (anything at all) / प्रयोजन (purpose, concern) / नाहीं (not) ॥ प्रभु (Lord) / जानत (knows) / सब (everything) / बिनहिं (without) / जनाए (being told) / कहहु (tell) / कवनि (what) / सिधि (success, gain) / लोक (world, people) / रिझाएँ (by pleasing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::895.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::895.essence: When Hari is enough, public approval loses its power.
ramacharitamanas::895.simple_meaning: The speaker says he stays hidden because only Ram matters to him. Since the Lord already knows everything, there is no need to impress people.
ramacharitamanas::895.simple_insight: It brings relief from performing for others. What matters most does not depend on public approval.
ramacharitamanas::895.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, a disguised ascetic speaks to a wise listener while testing trust and character. He says he lives hidden, cares only for Hari, and sees no value in trying to win the world’s praise because the Lord already knows all.
ramacharitamanas::895.modern_relevance: You draft the message ten times, wondering how it will sound to everyone else. Then you remember the one person who matters already sees your intent. That changes the whole tone.
ramacharitamanas::895.insight: It shifts attention from reputation management to sincere intention.

ramacharitamanas::896.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह सुचि सुमति परम प्रिय मोरें। प्रीति प्रतीति मोहि पर तोरें॥ अब जौं तात दुरावउँ तोही। दारुन दोष घटइ अति मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::896.verse_hindi: तुम पवित्र और सुंदर बुद्धि वाले हो, इससे मुझे बहुत ही प्यारे हो और तुम्हारी भी मुझ पर प्रीति और विश्वास है। हे तात! अब यदि मैं तुमसे कुछ छिपाता हूँ, तो मुझे बहुत ही भयानक दोष लगेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::896.english_translation: You are pure-minded and dear to me. You trust me, and I trust you. If I hide anything from you now, I will commit a grave fault.
ramacharitamanas::896.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / सुचि (pure) / सुमति (good mind) / परम (supremely) / प्रिय (dear) / मोरें (to me) / प्रीति (affection) / प्रतीति (trust) / मोहि (to me) / पर (toward) / तोरें (yours) / अब (now) / जौं (if) / तात (dear one) / दुरावउँ (I hide) / तोही (from you) / दारुन (terrible) / दोष (fault) / घटइ (falls) / अति (greatly) / मोही (on me)
ramacharitamanas::896.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::896.essence: Real trust makes hiding the truth feel like a moral wound.
ramacharitamanas::896.simple_meaning: The speaker says the listener is pure-minded, dear, and trusted. Hiding the truth now would be a serious wrong.
ramacharitamanas::896.simple_insight: Trust deepens when honesty is treated as a sacred duty.
ramacharitamanas::896.detailed_meaning: A disguised ascetic is speaking to King Janaka during the swayamvar scene. He wins the king’s confidence by praising Janaka’s purity and mutual trust, then says concealment would be a serious fault. The conversation is moving toward revelation.
ramacharitamanas::896.modern_relevance: A friend asks you a question you’ve been avoiding for weeks. You can feel the moment where politeness ends and honesty begins — and the relationship depends on crossing it cleanly.
ramacharitamanas::896.insight: It shifts the mind from strategic concealment to truthful disclosure.

ramacharitamanas::897.verse_sanskrit: जिमि जिमि तापसु कथइ उदासा। तिमि तिमि नृपहि उपज बिस्वासा॥ देखा स्वबस कर्म मन बानी। तब बोला तापस बगध्यानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::897.verse_hindi: ज्यों-ज्यों वह तपस्वी उदासीनता की बातें कहता था, त्यों ही त्यों राजा को विश्वास उत्पन्न होता जाता था। जब उस बगुले की तरह ध्यान लगाने वाले (कपटी) मुनि ने राजा को कर्म, मन और वचन से अपने वश में जाना, तब वह बोला- ॥
ramacharitamanas::897.english_translation: As the ascetic spoke more and more of detachment, the king's trust kept growing. When the deceitful, crane-like meditator saw the king under his control in body, mind, and speech, he began to speak.
ramacharitamanas::897.translation_literal: जिमि जिमि (as much as) / तापसु (the ascetic) / कथइ (speaks) / उदासा (of detachment) / तिमि तिमि (so much more) / नृपहि (in the king) / उपज (arises) / बिस्वासा (trust) ॥ देखा (seeing) / स्वबस (under his control) / कर्म (action) / मन (mind) / बानी (speech) / तब (then) / बोला (spoke) / तापस (the ascetic) / बगध्यानी (crane-minded, deceitful meditator) ॥
ramacharitamanas::897.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::897.essence: Polished detachment can be a mask for control.
ramacharitamanas::897.simple_meaning: The king grows more trusting as the ascetic speaks of detachment. Seeing the king fully under control, the deceitful holy man begins his next move.
ramacharitamanas::897.simple_insight: Charm can hide manipulation. Trust needs clear seeing, not just polished words.
ramacharitamanas::897.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, a disguised ascetic is speaking to King Dasharath with carefully chosen words about renunciation. Dasharath grows more trusting, unaware that the man is testing how fully he can be influenced before making his request.
ramacharitamanas::897.modern_relevance: A smooth-talking person keeps lowering your guard with just the right phrases about humility and good intentions. By the time you notice the pattern, you are already leaning toward their agenda.
ramacharitamanas::897.insight: It teaches you to watch whether words of virtue are matched by honest intent and steady conduct.

ramacharitamanas::898.verse_sanskrit: नाम हमार एकतनु भाई। सुनि नृप बोलेउ पुनि सिरु नाई॥ कहहु नाम कर अरथ बखानी। मोहि सेवक अति आपन जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::898.verse_hindi: हे भाई! हमारा नाम एकतनु है। यह सुनकर राजा ने फिर सिर नवाकर कहा- मुझे अपना अत्यन्त (अनुरागी) सेवक जानकर अपने नाम का अर्थ समझाकर कहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::898.english_translation: “My name is Ekatanu, brother.” Hearing this, the king bowed his head again and said, “Please tell me the meaning of your name and explain it. Regard me as your devoted servant.”
ramacharitamanas::898.translation_literal: नाम (name) / हमार (my) / एकतनु (Ekatanu) / भाई (brother) / सुनि (hearing) / नृप (king) / बोलेउ (spoke) / पुनि (again) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing) / कहहु (tell) / नाम (name) / कर (of) / अरथ (meaning) / बखानी (explain) / मोहि (me) / सेवक (servant) / अति (very) / आपन (your own) / जानी (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::898.speaker: Ekatanu
ramacharitamanas::898.essence: Humility opens the door to real inquiry.
ramacharitamanas::898.simple_meaning: The king humbly asks the sage to explain the meaning of his name, treating himself as the sage’s servant.
ramacharitamanas::898.simple_insight: Real learning begins when pride drops and questions become honest.
ramacharitamanas::898.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a king meets a strange ascetic and bows before him. The king’s curiosity is now sincere, not casual: he wants the meaning behind the name Ekatanu and speaks as a servant, ready to listen.
ramacharitamanas::898.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm feels deeper than your own. Instead of performing knowledge, you lower your head and ask the one question that can actually change you.
ramacharitamanas::898.insight: It shifts the mind from display to inquiry, making humility the doorway to understanding.

ramacharitamanas::899.verse_sanskrit: आदिसृष्टि उपजी जबहिं तब उतपति भै मोरि। नाम एकतनु हेतु तेहि देह न धरी बहोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::899.verse_hindi: (कपटी मुनि ने कहा-) जब सबसे पहले सृष्टि उत्पन्न हुई थी, तभी मेरी उत्पत्ति हुई थी। तबसे मैंने फिर दूसरी देह नहीं धारण की, इसी से मेरा नाम एकतनु है ॥
ramacharitamanas::899.english_translation: When the first creation arose, I arose then too. Since then I have not taken another body, so my name is Ekatanu.
ramacharitamanas::899.translation_literal: आदिसृष्टि (first creation) / उपजी (arose) / जबहिं (when) / तब (then) / उतपति (birth, arising) / भै (became) / मोरि (mine) / नाम (name) / एकतनु (one-bodied) / हेतु (because, for the reason) / तेहि (that) / देह (body) / न (not) / धरी (took) / बहोरि (again)
ramacharitamanas::899.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::899.simple_meaning: The speaker claims to have existed since the beginning of creation and says he has never taken another body, which is why he is called Ekatanu.
ramacharitamanas::899.simple_insight: A false story can sound holy when it is told with confidence.
ramacharitamanas::899.detailed_meaning: A disguised trickster is speaking to King Janaka in the opening of the Sita-swayamvar. He invents a grand origin story to gain trust, claiming he has existed since the first creation and never changed bodies. The line is part of his deception, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::899.modern_relevance: Someone in a meeting speaks with calm certainty, uses sacred-sounding language, and wins trust fast. The danger is not only lies — it is how easily confidence can masquerade as wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::899.insight: It trains the reader to question polished claims and look for consistency before believing them.

ramacharitamanas::900.verse_sanskrit: जनि आचरजु करहु मन माहीं। सुत तप तें दुर्लभ कछु नाहीं॥ तप बल तें जग सृजइ बिधाता। तप बल बिष्नु भए परित्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::900.verse_hindi: हे पुत्र! मन में आश्चर्य मत करो, तप से कुछ भी दुर्लभ नहीं है, तप के बल से ब्रह्मा जगत को रचते हैं। तप के ही बल से विष्णु संसार का पालन करने वाले बने हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::900.english_translation: O son, do not be surprised in your mind. Nothing is unattainable through tapas. By the power of tapas, Brahma creates the world, and by the power of tapas, Vishnu becomes its protector.
ramacharitamanas::900.translation_literal: जनि (do not) / आचरजु (wonder) / करहु (do) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / सुत (son) / तप (tapas) / तें (through) / दुर्लभ (hard to obtain) / कछु (anything) / नाहीं (is not) / तप (tapas) / बल (power) / तें (through) / जग (world) / सृजइ (creates) / बिधाता (the creator) / तप (tapas) / बल (power) / बिष्नु (Vishnu) / भए (became) / परित्राता (protector)
ramacharitamanas::900.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::900.simple_meaning: Serious discipline can accomplish what seems impossible. The verse says even the powers that create and protect the world arise from tapas.
ramacharitamanas::900.simple_insight: It replaces doubt with respect for sustained effort. Real transformation comes from steady inner heat, not wishful thinking.
ramacharitamanas::900.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar setting, the mysterious guest is explaining ancient power to the king. He says tapas is so strong that even Brahma's creation and Vishnu's protection come from it. The verse turns the conversation toward disciplined spiritual force.
ramacharitamanas::900.modern_relevance: You keep restarting the same habit on Monday morning, then quitting by Thursday. This verse says the missing ingredient is not talent — it is sustained inner discipline.
ramacharitamanas::900.insight: It shifts attention from what looks impossible to what consistent practice can build over time.

ramacharitamanas::901.verse_sanskrit: तपबल संभु करहिं संघारा। तप तें अगम न कछु संसारा॥ भयउ नृपहि सुनि अति अनुरागा। कथा पुरातन कहै सो लागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::901.verse_hindi: तप ही के बल से रुद्र संहार करते हैं। संसार में कोई ऐसी वस्तु नहीं जो तप से न मिल सके। यह सुनकर राजा को बड़ा अनुराग हुआ। तब वह (तपस्वी) पुरानी कथाएँ कहने लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::901.english_translation: By the power of tapas, Rudra brings destruction. Nothing in the world is beyond the reach of tapas. Hearing this, the king felt deep eagerness, and the ascetic began to tell the ancient story.
ramacharitamanas::901.translation_literal: तपबल (by the power of austerity) / संभु (Shambhu, Shiva) / करहिं (do) / संघारा (destruction) / तप (austerity) / तें (from/by) / अगम (unreachable) / न (not) / कछु (anything) / संसारा (in the world) / भयउ (became) / नृपहि (to the king) / सुनि (hearing) / अति (very) / अनुरागा (affection/eagerness) / कथा (story) / पुरातन (ancient) / कहै (to tell) / सो (he) / लागा (began)
ramacharitamanas::901.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::901.essence: Tapas can reach what ordinary effort cannot.
ramacharitamanas::901.simple_meaning: Tapsya is presented as so powerful that even Shiva's work of destruction happens through it. Hearing this, the king becomes eager to listen, and the old story continues.
ramacharitamanas::901.simple_insight: Great discipline can change even what seems impossible.
ramacharitamanas::901.detailed_meaning: The ascetic is still explaining the power of tapas to the king. He says that Shiva destroys through tapas and that nothing in the world lies beyond it. The king is captivated, and the telling moves deeper into the ancient story.
ramacharitamanas::901.modern_relevance: You keep practicing while everyone else calls it pointless. Months later, the habit has changed what used to feel impossible.
ramacharitamanas::901.insight: It shifts attention from quick results to the long power of disciplined effort.

ramacharitamanas::902.verse_sanskrit: करम धरम इतिहास अनेका। करइ निरूपन बिरति बिबेका॥ उदभव पालन प्रलय कहानी। कहेसि अमित आचरज बखानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::902.verse_hindi: कर्म, धर्म और अनेकों प्रकार के इतिहास कहकर वह वैराग्य और ज्ञान का निरूपण करने लगा। सृष्टि की उत्पत्ति, पालन (स्थिति) और संहार (प्रलय) की अपार आश्चर्यभरी कथाएँ उसने विस्तार से कही ॥
ramacharitamanas::902.english_translation: He explained many stories of action, duty, and history, and then taught renunciation and clear seeing. He told the wondrous tale of creation, preservation, and dissolution in great detail.
ramacharitamanas::902.translation_literal: करम (action) / धरम (duty) / इतिहास (histories) / अनेका (many) / करइ (does) / निरूपन (exposition) / बिरति (renunciation) / बिबेका (clear seeing) / उदभव (arising) / पालन (preservation) / प्रलय (dissolution) / कहानी (story) / कहेसि (he said) / अमित (immeasurable) / आचरज (wonder) / बखानी (described)
ramacharitamanas::902.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::902.essence: Stories of duty open into renunciation and the great cycle of change.
ramacharitamanas::902.simple_meaning: He taught many stories about action and duty, then explained renunciation and clear seeing. He also told the vast, wondrous story of how the world arises, lasts, and ends.
ramacharitamanas::902.simple_insight: Big truths can be taught through stories that widen the mind and loosen attachment.
ramacharitamanas::902.detailed_meaning: The king is listening to the ancient sage’s teaching. After hearing about discipline and tapas, the sage moves into deeper instruction: many stories of action, duty, renunciation, and the great cycle of creation, preservation, and dissolution.
ramacharitamanas::902.modern_relevance: A teacher finally stops giving rules and starts connecting the dots: why people act, why they cling, and how larger patterns shape a life. The room goes quiet because the story has become a mirror.
ramacharitamanas::902.insight: It shifts attention from isolated events to the larger pattern behind action, duty, and change.

ramacharitamanas::903.verse_sanskrit: सुनि महीप तापस बस भयऊ। आपन नाम कहन तब लयउ॥ कह तापस नृप जानउँ तोही। कीन्हेहु कपट लाग भल मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::903.verse_hindi: राजा सुनकर उस तपस्वी के वश में हो गया और तब वह उसे अपना नाम बताने लगा। तपस्वी ने कहा- राजन ! मैं तुमको जानता हूँ। तुमने कपट किया, वह मुझे अच्छा लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::903.english_translation: Hearing this, the king came under the ascetic's influence and then began to reveal his name. The ascetic said, 'King, I know you. You used a clever ruse, and that pleased me.'
ramacharitamanas::903.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / महीप (king) / तापस (ascetic) / बस (under control) / भयऊ (became) / आपन (own) / नाम (name) / कहन (saying) / तब (then) / लयउ (began) / कह (said) / तापस (ascetic) / नृप (king) / जानउँ (I know) / तोही (you) / कीन्हेहु (you did) / कपट (deception) / लाग (seemed) / भल (good) / मोही (to me)
ramacharitamanas::903.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::903.simple_meaning: The king is so impressed that he reveals his name. The ascetic already knows who he is and praises the king's cleverness.
ramacharitamanas::903.simple_insight: Being seen clearly can dissolve caution and open real connection.
ramacharitamanas::903.detailed_meaning: A king has been listening to a mysterious ascetic speak about deep truths. Moved and disarmed, he starts to reveal his identity. The ascetic immediately recognizes him and gently approves the king's clever concealment.
ramacharitamanas::903.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a retreat who seems to read you instantly. Instead of performing, you relax and speak honestly. Being understood can be more disarming than being praised.
ramacharitamanas::903.insight: It shifts the mind from guarded self-presentation to honest recognition.

ramacharitamanas::904.verse_sanskrit: सुनु महीस असि नीति जहँ तहँ नाम न कहहिं नृप। मोहि तोहि पर अति प्रीति सोइ चतुरता बिचारि तव ॥
ramacharitamanas::904.verse_hindi: हे राजन् ! सुनो, ऐसी नीति है कि राजा लोग जहाँ-तहाँ अपना नाम नहीं कहते। तुम्हारी वही चतुराई समझकर तुम पर मेरा बड़ा प्रेम हो गया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::904.english_translation: Listen, O king: there is a rule that kings do not reveal their names everywhere. Seeing that cleverness in you, I grew very fond of you.
ramacharitamanas::904.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / महीस (O king) / असि (such) / नीति (rule) / जहँ तहँ (everywhere) / नाम (name) / न कहहिं (do not say) / नृप (kings) / मोहि (to me) / तोहि (to you) / पर (upon) / अति (very) / प्रीति (affection) / सोइ (that) / चतुरता (cleverness) / बिचारि (considering) / तव (your)
ramacharitamanas::904.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::904.essence: Measured speech can create trust before full disclosure.
ramacharitamanas::904.simple_meaning: The speaker says kings do not casually reveal their names, and that your cleverness made me like you even more.
ramacharitamanas::904.simple_insight: Careful speech can build trust. A little restraint can make someone seem wiser and more worthy.
ramacharitamanas::904.detailed_meaning: In Vishvamitra’s testing of Ram and Lakshman, the disguised sage has already praised the king and drawn him in. Now he explains that a ruler does not casually give away his name, and that this guardedness made him trust the king’s intelligence and warmth.
ramacharitamanas::904.modern_relevance: At a first meeting, someone answers with just enough, not too much. That restraint feels confident, and it makes the other person lean in.
ramacharitamanas::904.insight: It shifts attention from oversharing to measured speech, showing that tact can deepen respect.

ramacharitamanas::905.verse_sanskrit: नाम तुम्हार प्रताप दिनेसा। सत्यकेतु तव पिता नरेसा॥ गुर प्रसाद सब जानिअ राजा। कहिअ न आपन जानि अकाजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::905.verse_hindi: तुम्हारा नाम प्रतापभानु है, महाराज सत्यकेतु तुम्हारे पिता थे। हे राजन् ! गुरु की कृपा से मैं सब जानता हूँ, पर अपनी हानि समझकर कहता नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::905.english_translation: Your name is Pratapbhanu, and your father was the king Satyaketu. By the guru's grace, I know everything, but I do not say it, knowing it would harm me.
ramacharitamanas::905.translation_literal: नाम (name) / तुम्हार (your) / प्रताप (splendor) / दिनेसा (sun) / सत्यकेतु (Satyaketu) / तव (your) / पिता (father) / नरेसा (king) / गुर (guru) / प्रसाद (grace) / सब (all) / जानिअ (known) / राजा (king) / कहिअ (say) / न (not) / आपन (own) / जानि (knowing) / अकाजा (harm)
ramacharitamanas::905.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::905.essence: Wisdom knows both what to say and what to hold back.
ramacharitamanas::905.simple_meaning: The teacher knows the king's identity and family, but speaks carefully because saying everything would bring harm.
ramacharitamanas::905.simple_insight: Not every truth should be spoken at once; wisdom also knows when silence protects.
ramacharitamanas::905.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the disguised king meets a learned ascetic who already knows who he is. The ascetic names his lineage and then holds back, showing that knowledge, tact, and restraint belong together in a wise exchange.
ramacharitamanas::905.modern_relevance: A colleague starts revealing private details in a meeting, then stops because the room has turned unsafe. Knowing something is not the same as saying it. Timing is part of wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::905.insight: It teaches restraint in speech: speak only when truth will help, not when it will wound.

ramacharitamanas::906.verse_sanskrit: देखि तात तव सहज सुधाई। प्रीति प्रतीति नीति निपुनाई॥ उपजि परी ममता मन मोरें। कहउँ कथा निज पूछे तोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::906.verse_hindi: हे तात! तुम्हारा स्वाभाविक सीधापन (सरलता), प्रेम, विश्वास और नीति में निपुणता देखकर मेरे मन में तुम्हारे ऊपर बड़ी ममता उत्पन्न हो गई है, इसीलिए मैं तुम्हारे पूछने पर अपनी कथा कहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::906.english_translation: Seeing your natural simplicity, affection, trust, and skill in conduct, affection arose in my heart. So I tell my own story because you asked.
ramacharitamanas::906.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / तात (dear one) / तव (your) / सहज (natural) / सुधाई (simplicity) / प्रीति (affection) / प्रतीति (trust) / नीति (right conduct) / निपुनाई (skillfulness) ॥ उपजि (having arisen) / परी (fell) / ममता (fondness) / मन (mind) / मोरें (in my) / कहउँ (I speak) / कथा (story) / निज (own) / पूछे (having asked) / तोरें (by you) ॥
ramacharitamanas::906.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::906.essence: Sincerity invites closeness, and closeness invites revelation.
ramacharitamanas::906.simple_meaning: Recognizing the king’s sincerity and good conduct, the speaker feels affection and answers his request by sharing his own story.
ramacharitamanas::906.simple_insight: Kindness and trust open the door to honest speech.
ramacharitamanas::906.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to King Janaka after noticing his natural simplicity, affection, trust, and wise conduct. That warmth creates a bond, and because Janaka has asked respectfully, Shiva begins to tell his own story.
ramacharitamanas::906.modern_relevance: A mentor listens to you differently when your questions come with humility and sincerity. Real trust changes the whole conversation before a single answer is given.
ramacharitamanas::906.insight: It shifts communication from formal exchange to earned intimacy and truthful sharing.

ramacharitamanas::907.verse_sanskrit: अब प्रसन्न मैं संसय नाहीं। मागु जो भूप भाव मन माहीं॥ सुनि सुबचन भूपति हरषाना। गहि पद बिनय कीन्हि बिधि नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::907.verse_hindi: अब मैं प्रसन्न हूँ, इसमें संदेह न करना। हे राजन् ! जो मन को भावे वही माँग लो। सुंदर (प्रिय) वचन सुनकर राजा हर्षित हो गया और (मुनि के) पैर पकड़कर उसने बहुत प्रकार से विनती की ॥
ramacharitamanas::907.english_translation: I am pleased now; have no doubt. Ask for whatever your heart desires, O king. Hearing those gracious words, the king rejoiced and bowed at the sage's feet in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::907.translation_literal: अब (now) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / मैं (I) / संसय (doubt) / नाहीं (not) / मागु (ask) / जो (whatever) / भूप (king) / भाव (desires) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / सुनि (having heard) / सुबचन (gracious words) / भूपति (the king) / हरषाना (rejoiced) / गहि (seizing) / पद (feet) / बिनय (humble request) / कीन्हि (made) / बिधि (in manner) / नाना (many)
ramacharitamanas::907.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::907.essence: True generosity removes doubt and invites the real request.
ramacharitamanas::907.simple_meaning: The sage tells the king he is pleased and should ask for any boon he wants. The king is overjoyed and falls at the sage's feet in gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::907.simple_insight: Kindness opens the heart faster than argument ever could.
ramacharitamanas::907.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, the sage has tested the king's sincerity and now relents. He tells him to ask freely. The king, relieved and delighted, bows at the sage's feet with repeated humility, setting up the deeper request that follows.
ramacharitamanas::907.modern_relevance: A mentor finally says, “Tell me what you really need.” The tension breaks, and gratitude rushes in before the request even comes out.
ramacharitamanas::907.insight: It shifts the moment from uncertainty to permission, showing how generosity makes honest asking possible.

ramacharitamanas::908.verse_sanskrit: कृपासिंधु मुनि दरसन तोरें। चारि पदारथ करतल मोरें॥ प्रभुहि तथापि प्रसन्न बिलोकी। मागि अगम बर होउँ असोकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::908.verse_hindi: हे दयासागर मुनि! आपके दर्शन से ही चारों पदार्थ (अर्थ, धर्म, काम और मोक्ष) मेरी मुट्ठी में आ गए। तो भी स्वामी को प्रसन्न देखकर मैं यह दुर्लभ वर माँगकर (क्यों न) शोकरहित हो जाऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::908.english_translation: O ocean of compassion, merely seeing the sage has placed the four aims of life in my hand. Yet, seeing the Lord pleased, I ask for this rare boon: let me become free of sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::908.translation_literal: कृपासिंधु (o ocean of compassion) / मुनि (sage) / दरसन (darshan, sacred sight) / तोरें (from you) / चारि (four) / पदारथ (aims of life) / करतल (in the palm of the hand) / मोरें (mine)॥ / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / तथापि (even then) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / बिलोकी (seeing) / मागि (asking) / अगम (hard to obtain) / बर (boon) / होउँ (may I become) / असोकी (free of sorrow)॥
ramacharitamanas::908.speaker: King Janaka
ramacharitamanas::908.essence: The highest boon is a heart that wants the Lord's pleasure, not its own prize.
ramacharitamanas::908.simple_meaning: Janaka says that even though meeting the sage has given him all four aims of life, he still asks for one rare blessing: to remain free from sorrow because the Lord is pleased.
ramacharitamanas::908.simple_insight: Real contentment is wanting less for yourself and more for the joy of the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::908.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's court during Sita's swayamvar, the king speaks to Vishvamitra after seeing Ram's greatness. He says that the sage's presence has already given him everything, but the deeper blessing is Ram's pleased face and a heart free from sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::908.modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the praise, the money — and still notice what matters most is whether the person you love is at peace. Some victories feel small beside that quiet relief.
ramacharitamanas::908.insight: It shifts desire from personal gain to the beloved's satisfaction.

ramacharitamanas::909.verse_sanskrit: जरा मरन दुख रहित तनु समर जितै जनि कोउ। एकछत्र रिपुहीन महि राज कलप सत होउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::909.verse_hindi: मेरा शरीर वृद्धावस्था, मृत्यु और दुःख से रहित हो जाए, मुझे युद्ध में कोई जीत न सके और पृथ्वी पर मेरा सौ कल्पतक एकछत्र अकण्टक राज्य हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::909.english_translation: May my body be free from old age, death, and sorrow; may no enemy defeat me in battle; may I rule the earth, unchallenged, for a hundred kalpas.
ramacharitamanas::909.translation_literal: जरा (old age) / मरन (death) / दुख (sorrow) / रहित (free from) / तनु (body) / समर (battle) / जितै (be defeated) / जनि (let not) / कोउ (anyone) / एकछत्र (under one umbrella, unchallenged) / रिपुहीन (without enemies) / महि (earth) / राज (rule) / कलप (kalpas) / सत (hundred) / होउ (may it be)
ramacharitamanas::909.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::909.essence: Worldly perfection still depends on what time and conflict can take away.
ramacharitamanas::909.simple_meaning: The king asks for a body free from aging, death, and suffering, invincibility in war, and a long, undisturbed reign over the earth.
ramacharitamanas::909.simple_insight: Power looks complete from the outside, yet it still cannot escape time, conflict, or loss.
ramacharitamanas::909.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the king is offered a blessing by the sage. He asks for the fullest possible worldly security: an ageless body, victory in war, and a long, enemy-free reign. The next line will reveal the hidden limit in that wish.
ramacharitamanas::909.modern_relevance: Someone wants the perfect job, perfect health, no rivals, and total control over the future. The wish sounds strong until you hear how fragile every part of it is.
ramacharitamanas::909.insight: It exposes the limits of worldly power and sets up the higher teaching that follows.

ramacharitamanas::910.verse_sanskrit: कह तापस नृप ऐसेइ होऊ। कारन एक कठिन सुनु सोऊ॥ कालउ तुअ पद नाइहि सीसा। एक बिप्रकुल छाड़ि महीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::910.verse_hindi: तपस्वी ने कहा- हे राजन् ! ऐसा ही हो, पर एक बात कठिन है, उसे भी सुन लो। हे पृथ्वी के स्वामी! केवल ब्राह्मण कुल को छोड़ काल भी तुम्हारे चरणों पर सिर नवाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::910.english_translation: The ascetic said, “So be it, O king. But hear one hard condition: even Time will bow his head at your feet, yet not one priestly lineage will be left out.”
ramacharitamanas::910.translation_literal: कह (said) / तापस (the ascetic) / नृप (O king) / ऐसेइ (just so) / होऊ (may it be) / कारन (reason) / एक (one) / कठिन (hard) / सुनु (listen) / सोऊ (that) / कालउ (even Time) / तुअ (your) / पद (feet) / नाइहि (will bow) / सीसा (head) / एक (one) / बिप्रकुल (priestly lineage) / छाड़ि (excepting) / महीसा (O lord of the earth)
ramacharitamanas::910.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::910.essence: Even granted power meets a law it cannot erase.
ramacharitamanas::910.simple_meaning: The ascetic grants the king’s wish, but adds one hard rule: even Time will bow to him, yet the priestly line will remain beyond his control.
ramacharitamanas::910.simple_insight: Power still has a boundary. Even the strongest wish cannot override every order in life.
ramacharitamanas::910.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, a king asks a sage for an impossible blessing: freedom from age, death, defeat, and sorrow. The sage agrees in principle, then warns that one thing cannot be bent — the authority of the priestly order. The blessing comes with a limit.
ramacharitamanas::910.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the raise, the title you wanted — and still one person can say no. This verse reminds you that no amount of ambition makes you master of everything.
ramacharitamanas::910.insight: It shifts the mind from total control to respectful limits: desire can be answered, but not without boundaries.

ramacharitamanas::911.verse_sanskrit: तपबल बिप्र सदा बरिआरा। तिन्ह के कोप न कोउ रखवारा॥ जौं बिप्रन्ह बस करहु नरेसा। तौ तुअ बस बिधि बिष्नु महेसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::911.verse_hindi: तप के बल से ब्राह्मण सदा बलवान रहते हैं। उनके क्रोध से रक्षा करने वाला कोई नहीं है। हे नरपति! यदि तुम ब्राह्मणों को वश में कर लो, तो ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और महेश भी तुम्हारे अधीन हो जाएँगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::911.english_translation: By the power of austerity, brahmins are always strong. No one can protect against their anger. O king, if you bring brahmins under your control, then Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh will also be under your control.
ramacharitamanas::911.translation_literal: तपबल (power of austerity) / बिप्र (brahmins) / सदा (always) / बरिआरा (strong) / तिन्ह के (their) / कोप (anger) / न कोउ (no one) / रखवारा (protector) / जौं (if) / बिप्रन्ह (brahmins) / बस (under control) / करहु (you bring) / नरेसा (O king) / तौ (then) / तुअ (your) / बस (under control) / बिधि (Brahma) / बिष्नु (Vishnu) / महेसा (Mahesh)
ramacharitamanas::911.speaker: Tapsi
ramacharitamanas::911.essence: A ruler who tries to control the righteous invites forces beyond control.
ramacharitamanas::911.simple_meaning: Austerity gives brahmins their strength, and no one can safely oppose them. If a king controls brahmins, even the highest powers would be forced under his influence.
ramacharitamanas::911.simple_insight: Power that ignores moral restraint invites forces it cannot manage.
ramacharitamanas::911.detailed_meaning: A tapasvi is warning the king after the earlier blessing request. He says brahmins draw strength from austerity, so their anger cannot be safely resisted. The point is to stop the king from imagining that raw power can dominate sacred authority.
ramacharitamanas::911.modern_relevance: A manager bullies the only person in the room who knows the system inside out. The shortcut looks strong for a day, then the whole structure starts to wobble.
ramacharitamanas::911.insight: It shifts the mind from domination to respect for moral and spiritual authority.

ramacharitamanas::912.verse_sanskrit: चल न ब्रह्मकुल सन बरिआई। सत्य कहउँ दोउ भुजा उठाई॥ बिप्र श्राप बिनु सुनु महिपाला। तोर नास नहिं कवनेहुँ काला ॥
ramacharitamanas::912.verse_hindi: ब्राह्मण कुल से जोर जबर्दस्ती नहीं चल सकती, मैं दोनों भुजा उठाकर सत्य कहता हूँ। हे राजन् ! सुनो, ब्राह्मणों के शाप बिना तुम्हारा नाश किसी काल में नहीं होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::912.english_translation: Force cannot prevail against the Brahmin lineage. I speak the truth with both arms raised: O ruler, without a Brahmin's curse, your destruction will not come at any time.
ramacharitamanas::912.translation_literal: चल (can go) / न (not) / ब्रह्मकुल (Brahmin lineage) / सन (with) / बरिआई (force) / सत्य (truth) / कहउँ (I say) / दोउ (both) / भुजा (arms) / उठाई (having raised) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / श्राप (curse) / बिनु (without) / सुनु (listen) / महिपाला (O ruler) / तोर (your) / नास (destruction) / नहिं (not) / कवनेहुँ (at any) / काला (time)
ramacharitamanas::912.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::912.essence: Force fails where moral authority stands.
ramacharitamanas::912.simple_meaning: Power cannot override the moral force of the Brahmin order. The speaker warns the king that his downfall will not come unless a Brahmin curses him.
ramacharitamanas::912.simple_insight: Some harms are not stopped by strength; they begin when moral order is ignored.
ramacharitamanas::912.detailed_meaning: In the court scene, a sage warns the king after the king has pressed too hard against Brahmin authority. He declares, with raised arms, that raw force cannot win here and that the king's ruin depends on provoking a curse.
ramacharitamanas::912.modern_relevance: You push your way through a dispute, sure that influence will protect you. Then one small act of disrespect turns the room against you. Some boundaries are not physical; they are moral.
ramacharitamanas::912.insight: It shifts the mind from brute confidence to respect for limits that power cannot erase.

ramacharitamanas::913.verse_sanskrit: हरषेउ राउ बचन सुनि तासू। नाथ न होइ मोर अब नासू॥ तव प्रसाद प्रभु कृपानिधाना। मो कहुँ सर्बकाल कल्याना ॥
ramacharitamanas::913.verse_hindi: राजा उसके वचन सुनकर बड़ा प्रसन्न हुआ और कहने लगा- हे स्वामी! मेरा नाश अब नहीं होगा। हे कृपानिधान प्रभु! आपकी कृपा से मेरा सब समय कल्याण होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::913.english_translation: The king was delighted to hear those words and said, “Lord, now my ruin will not come. By your grace, merciful one, may I always be blessed.”
ramacharitamanas::913.translation_literal: हरषेउ (was delighted) / राउ (the king) / बचन (words) / सुनि (having heard) / तासू (his) / नाथ (Lord) / न (not) / होइ (will be) / मोर (my) / अब (now) / नासू (ruin) / तव (your) / प्रसाद (grace) / प्रभु (Lord) / कृपानिधाना (treasure of mercy) / मो कहुँ (for me) / सर्बकाल (at all times) / कल्याना (well-being)
ramacharitamanas::913.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::913.essence: Relief arrives when fear gives way to trust in grace.
ramacharitamanas::913.simple_meaning: The king feels relieved and grateful after hearing the sage’s words. He believes divine grace will keep him safe and благословed.
ramacharitamanas::913.simple_insight: Relief deepens when fear is met with trust instead of resistance.
ramacharitamanas::913.detailed_meaning: A king has just been warned that Brahmin power and curses cannot be ignored. Hearing the sage’s words, he relaxes at once and thanks the merciful Lord, believing his danger has passed. The moment turns fear into gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::913.modern_relevance: After a tense call from someone who can change your plans, you finally hear a calm voice that steadies the room. The body unclenches before the mind can explain why.
ramacharitamanas::913.insight: It shifts the mind from panic to trust when danger feels near.

ramacharitamanas::914.verse_sanskrit: एवमस्तु कहि कपट मुनि बोला कुटिल बहोरि। मिलब हमार भुलाब निज कहहु त हमहि न खोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::914.verse_hindi: 'एवमस्तु' (ऐसा ही हो) कहकर वह कुटिल कपटी मुनि फिर बोला- (किन्तु) तुम मेरे मिलने तथा अपने राह भूल जाने की बात किसी से (कहना नहीं, यदि) कह दोगे, तो हमारा दोष नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::914.english_translation: “So be it,” said the crooked sage, and then spoke again: “If you mention our meeting or your losing the way, then the blame is not ours.”
ramacharitamanas::914.translation_literal: एवमस्तु (so be it) / कहि (having said) / कपट (deceitful) / मुनि (sage) / बोला (spoke) / कुटिल (crooked) / बहोरि (again) / मिलब (meeting) / हमार (our) / भुलाब (forgetting / losing the way) / निज (your own) / कहहु (say) / त (then) / हमहि (to us) / न (not) / खोरि (fault)
ramacharitamanas::914.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::914.essence: Agreement can still conceal fear of blame.
ramacharitamanas::914.simple_meaning: The deceitful sage agrees, but immediately warns the king not to reveal the meeting or the lost path. He wants to keep himself safe from blame.
ramacharitamanas::914.simple_insight: Not every agreement is honest. Some words are only a trap to protect the speaker.
ramacharitamanas::914.detailed_meaning: A crooked sage has just won the king's trust with a flattering assurance. Before the king can relax, he adds a warning: keep this meeting secret, or the fault will not be his. The passage shows manipulation hiding inside polite words.
ramacharitamanas::914.modern_relevance: Someone says, “Sure, do it my way,” then quietly adds, “And don’t tell anyone I advised this.” The smile is still there, but the self-protection is now obvious.
ramacharitamanas::914.insight: It trains the reader to notice manipulation wrapped in agreement and to watch for hidden self-interest.

ramacharitamanas::915.verse_sanskrit: तातें मैं तोहि बरजउँ राजा। कहें कथा तव परम अकाजा॥ छठें श्रवन यह परत कहानी। नास तुम्हार सत्य मम बानी ॥
