ramacharitamanas::915.verse_hindi: हे राजन् ! मैं तुमको इसलिए मना करता हूँ कि इस प्रसंग को कहने से तुम्हारी बड़ी हानि होगी। छठे कान में यह बात पड़ते ही तुम्हारा नाश हो जाएगा, मेरा यह वचन सत्य जानना ॥
ramacharitamanas::915.english_translation: O king, I warn you for this reason: telling this story will bring you great harm. The moment it reaches a sixth ear, your ruin will be certain; believe my words as true.
ramacharitamanas::915.translation_literal: तातें (therefore) / मैं (I) / तोहि (you) / बरजउँ (warn) / राजा (king) / कहें (speaking) / कथा (story) / तव (your) / परम (greatest) / अकाजा (harm) ॥ / छठें (to the sixth) / श्रवन (ear) / यह (this) / परत (falls) / कहानी (story) / नास (destruction) / तुम्हार (your) / सत्य (true) / मम (my) / बानी (speech) ॥
ramacharitamanas::915.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::915.essence: Some truths destroy the listener who hears them too soon.
ramacharitamanas::915.simple_meaning: The sage warns the king not to repeat the story, because hearing it by the wrong person will destroy him.
ramacharitamanas::915.simple_insight: Some truths are dangerous in the wrong place. Wisdom includes knowing when silence protects life.
ramacharitamanas::915.detailed_meaning: King Pratāpbhanu has just been drawn into a strange exchange with a deceptive sage. The sage now warns him that if this story is spoken aloud, it will bring disaster. The warning sets up the hidden trap that follows.
ramacharitamanas::915.modern_relevance: You almost repeat a private conversation in a group chat, then stop. Not every true thing belongs everywhere; some words become harmful the moment they leave the wrong room.
ramacharitamanas::915.insight: It teaches restraint in speech: not every truth should be repeated, and timing can matter as much as content.

ramacharitamanas::916.verse_sanskrit: यह प्रगटें अथवा द्विजश्रापा। नास तोर सुनु भानुप्रतापा॥ आन उपायँ निधन तव नाहीं। जौं हरि हर कोपहिं मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::916.verse_hindi: हे प्रतापभानु! सुनो, इस बात के प्रकट करने से अथवा ब्राह्मणों के शाप से तुम्हारा नाश होगा और किसी उपाय से, चाहे ब्रह्मा और शंकर भी मन में क्रोध करें, तुम्हारी मृत्यु नहीं होगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::916.english_translation: O glorious king, know this: if it becomes known, or if the brahmins curse you, your ruin will come. No other remedy exists, even if Brahma and Shiva become angry in their minds.
ramacharitamanas::916.translation_literal: यह (this) / प्रगटें (if revealed) / अथवा (or) / द्विजश्रापा (by brahmin curse) / नास (destruction) / तोर (your) / सुनु (listen) / भानुप्रतापा (O sun-glorious king) / आन (other) / उपायँ (by remedy) / निधन (death, ruin) / तव (your) / नाहीं (not) / जौं (if) / हरि (Brahma) / हर (Shiva) / कोपहिं (become angry) / मन माहीं (in the mind)
ramacharitamanas::916.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::916.essence: Fear can make a false warning feel unavoidable.
ramacharitamanas::916.simple_meaning: The disguised sage warns King Pratāpa Bhānu that revealing the secret or earning the brahmins’ curse will bring ruin, and no other escape exists.
ramacharitamanas::916.simple_insight: Some warnings are traps: they narrow your choices until fear feels like fate.
ramacharitamanas::916.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, the disguised sage presses Pratāpa Bhānu with a frightening claim: if the secret is exposed, or if the brahmins curse him, disaster will follow. The verse is part of the manipulation that pushes the king toward obedience.
ramacharitamanas::916.modern_relevance: A stranger in a polished office lowers their voice and says, “Don’t tell anyone this.” The threat is vague, but it grips you. Fear can make a lie feel like the only safe path.
ramacharitamanas::916.insight: It exposes how fear is used to control judgment by making every alternative seem fatal.

ramacharitamanas::917.verse_sanskrit: सत्य नाथ पद गहि नृप भाषा। द्विज गुर कोप कहहु को राखा॥ राखइ गुर जौं कोप बिधाता। गुर बिरोध नहिं कोउ जग त्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::917.verse_hindi: राजा ने मुनि के चरण पकड़कर कहा- हे स्वामी! सत्य ही है। ब्राह्मण और गुरु के क्रोध से, कहिए, कौन रक्षा कर सकता है? यदि ब्रह्मा भी क्रोध करें, तो गुरु बचा लेते हैं, पर गुरु से विरोध करने पर जगत में कोई भी बचाने वाला नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::917.english_translation: The king clasped the sage's feet and said, "Master, what you say is true. Who can protect anyone from the anger of a brahmin and a teacher? Even if Brahma grows angry, a teacher can still save one; but no one in the world can save against a teacher's opposition."
ramacharitamanas::917.translation_literal: सत्य (true) / नाथ (master) / पद (feet) / गहि (grasping) / नृप (king) / भाषा (spoke) / द्विज (brahmin) / गुर (teacher) / कोप (anger) / कहहु (tell) / को (who) / राखा (protects) / राखइ (protects) / गुर (teacher) / जौं (if) / कोप (anger) / बिधाता (Brahma) / गुर (teacher) / बिरोध (opposition) / नहिं (not) / कोउ (anyone) / जग (world) / त्राता (protector)
ramacharitamanas::917.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::917.essence: Teacherly opposition is treated as beyond ordinary protection.
ramacharitamanas::917.simple_meaning: The king admits the sage is right: a teacher's anger is dangerous, and no one can protect a person who opposes a teacher.
ramacharitamanas::917.simple_insight: Respect for the teacher is not optional; it is treated here as a force stronger than power.
ramacharitamanas::917.detailed_meaning: In the courtly exchange around Bhanupratap's warning, the king falls at the sage's feet and acknowledges the truth of the warning. The verse deepens the pressure of the moment: even divine power cannot override the authority of the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::917.modern_relevance: You argue with someone who has guided you for years, then realize the damage is already in the room. Some relationships carry a weight that pride cannot afford to ignore.
ramacharitamanas::917.insight: It shifts the mind from self-assertion to reverence for guidance and consequences.

ramacharitamanas::918.verse_sanskrit: जौं न चलब हम कहे तुम्हारें। होउ नास नहिं सोच हमारें॥ एकहिं डर डरपत मन मोरा। प्रभु महिदेव श्राप अति घोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::918.verse_hindi: यदि मैं आपके कथन के अनुसार नहीं चलूँगा, तो (भले ही) मेरा नाश हो जाए। मुझे इसकी चिन्ता नहीं है। मेरा मन तो हे प्रभो! (केवल) एक ही डर से डर रहा है कि ब्राह्मणों का शाप बड़ा भयानक होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::918.english_translation: If I do not follow your command, let me perish. I do not worry about that. My mind fears only one thing: the terrible curse of the Brahmins, O Lord.
ramacharitamanas::918.translation_literal: जौं (if) / न (not) / चलब (I will follow) / हम (I) / कहे (said) / तुम्हारें (your) / होउ (let it be) / नास (destruction) / नहिं (not) / सोच (worry) / हमारें (my) / एकहिं (only one) / डर (fear) / डरपत (fearing) / मन (mind) / मोरा (my) / प्रभु (Lord) / महिदेव (Brahmins) / श्राप (curse) / अति (very) / घोरा (terrible)
ramacharitamanas::918.speaker: Pratapbhanu
ramacharitamanas::918.essence: Death is bearable; breaking sacred order is not.
ramacharitamanas::918.simple_meaning: The king says he is willing to die rather than disobey, but he is terrified of the Brahmins' curse.
ramacharitamanas::918.simple_insight: Real fear is not death here, but the weight of violating sacred trust.
ramacharitamanas::918.detailed_meaning: Pratapbhanu stands before the sage after hearing that his hidden wrongdoing has brought a curse. He says he can accept death, but not the spiritual force of a Brahmin's curse. This keeps the scene moving toward his desperate search for a remedy.
ramacharitamanas::918.modern_relevance: You can face losing your reputation, your comfort, even your position. What shakes you more is the feeling that you have crossed a line you should never have crossed.
ramacharitamanas::918.insight: It shifts attention from physical loss to moral consequence and reverence for higher authority.

ramacharitamanas::919.verse_sanskrit: होहिं बिप्र बस कवन बिधि कहहु कृपा करि सोउ। तुम्ह तजि दीनदयाल निज हितू न देखउँ कोउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::919.verse_hindi: वे ब्राह्मण किस प्रकार से वश में हो सकते हैं, कृपा करके वह भी बताइए। हे दीनदयालु! आपको छोड़कर और किसी को मैं अपना हितू नहीं देखता ॥
ramacharitamanas::919.english_translation: Please tell me, by what means can the Brahmins be brought under control? O compassionate one, apart from you I see no helper who can truly protect me.
ramacharitamanas::919.translation_literal: होहिं (become) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / बस (under control) / कवन बिधि (by what means) / कहहु (tell) / कृपा करि (showing grace) / सोउ (that too) / तुम्ह (you) / तजि (leaving aside) / दीनदयाल (compassionate one) / निज (own) / हितू (helper) / न (not) / देखउँ (I see) / कोउ (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::919.speaker: King
ramacharitamanas::919.essence: True help begins when pride stops looking elsewhere.
ramacharitamanas::919.simple_meaning: The king asks how the Brahmins can be brought under control, and says he sees no protector except the compassionate one he is addressing.
ramacharitamanas::919.simple_insight: There is relief in asking for help instead of pretending to manage everything alone.
ramacharitamanas::919.detailed_meaning: The king is already afraid of the curse and has bowed in humility. He now asks the sage for the one thing he still lacks: a way to face the Brahmins. This line deepens his dependence and prepares the practical answer that follows.
ramacharitamanas::919.modern_relevance: You have exhausted every workaround, every apology, every clever plan. At last you admit, 'I need someone wiser than me to show the next step.'
ramacharitamanas::919.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance under pressure to humble dependence on a wiser guide.

ramacharitamanas::920.verse_sanskrit: सुनु नृप बिबिध जतन जग माहीं। कष्टसाध्य पुनि होहिं कि नाहीं॥ अहइ एक अति सुगम उपाई। तहाँ परन्तु एक कठिनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::920.verse_hindi: (तपस्वी ने कहा-) हे राजन् !सुनो, संसार में उपाय तो बहुत हैं, पर वे कष्ट साध्य हैं (बड़ी कठिनता से बनने में आते हैं) और इस पर भी सिद्ध हों या न हों (उनकी सफलता निश्चित नहीं है) हाँ, एक उपाय बहुत सहज है, परन्तु उसमें भी एक कठिनता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::920.english_translation: Hear, O king: there are many methods in the world, but they are hard to accomplish. Even then, success is uncertain. There is one very easy method, but it has one difficulty.
ramacharitamanas::920.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / नृप (king) / बिबिध (various) / जतन (methods, efforts) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / कष्टसाध्य (hard to accomplish) / पुनि (again, also) / होहिं (are) / कि (whether) / नाहीं (not) / अहइ (is) / एक (one) / अति (very) / सुगम (easy) / उपाई (method, means) / तहाँ (there) / परन्तु (but) / एक (one) / कठिनाई (difficulty)
ramacharitamanas::920.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::920.essence: The easiest solution is often blocked by one hard condition.
ramacharitamanas::920.simple_meaning: Many methods exist, but most are hard and uncertain. One method is easy, yet it has a single obstacle.
ramacharitamanas::920.simple_insight: Not every difficult problem needs a difficult answer.
ramacharitamanas::920.detailed_meaning: A sage speaks to a king about a problem that has resisted every ordinary solution. He admits there are many possible methods, but they are all hard and unreliable. Then he points toward one simple way, preparing the king for the one obstacle that remains.
ramacharitamanas::920.modern_relevance: You’ve tried five complicated fixes, and none of them held. Then someone suggests a simpler route — and you resist it because it feels too easy to be real.
ramacharitamanas::920.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing complexity to asking what simple obstacle remains.

ramacharitamanas::921.verse_sanskrit: मम आधीन जुगुति नृप सोई। मोर जाब तव नगर न होई॥ आजु लगें अरु जब तें भयऊँ। काहू के गृह ग्राम न गयऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::921.verse_hindi: हे राजन् ! वह युक्ति तो मेरे हाथ है, पर मेरा जाना तुम्हारे नगर में हो नहीं सकता। जब से पैदा हुआ हूँ, तब से आज तक मैं किसी के घर अथवा गाँव नहीं गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::921.english_translation: O king, that method is in my hands, but I cannot go to your city. Since I was born until today, I have never gone to anyone's house or village.
ramacharitamanas::921.translation_literal: मम (my) / आधीन (under my control) / जुगुति (method, means) / नृप (O king) / सोई (that) / मोर (my) / जाब (going) / तव (your) / नगर (city) / न (not) / होई (is possible) / आजु लगें (until today) / अरु (and) / जब तें (since) / भयऊँ (I was born) / काहू (anyone's) / के गृह (house) / ग्राम (village) / न (not) / गयऊँ (have gone)
ramacharitamanas::921.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::921.essence: Power stays clean when it refuses convenience.
ramacharitamanas::921.simple_meaning: The speaker says he knows the solution, but he will not enter the king's city or visit anyone's home. He has kept that rule his whole life.
ramacharitamanas::921.simple_insight: Some limits are not weakness. They are part of a life held together by principle.
ramacharitamanas::921.detailed_meaning: A king asks a sage how the brahmins can be won over. The sage offers a method, but immediately sets a boundary: he will not go to the king's city. He explains that he has never gone to anyone's house or village since birth.
ramacharitamanas::921.modern_relevance: A respected elder refuses a flattering dinner invitation because he will not trade his integrity for access. The answer is available, but not on borrowed terms.
ramacharitamanas::921.insight: It shows that real authority can include strict self-limitation. The method is offered without compromising the speaker's way of life.

ramacharitamanas::922.verse_sanskrit: जौं न जाउँ तव होइ अकाजू। बना आइ असमंजस आजू॥ सुनि महीस बोलेउ मृदु बानी। नाथ निगम असि नीति बखानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::922.verse_hindi: परन्तु यदि नहीं जाता हूँ, तो तुम्हारा काम बिगड़ता है। आज यह बड़ा असमंजस आ पड़ा है। यह सुनकर राजा कोमल वाणी से बोला, हे नाथ! वेदों में ऐसी नीति कही है कि- ॥
ramacharitamanas::922.english_translation: But if I do not go, your work will fail. A difficult dilemma has arisen today. Hearing this, the king spoke gently: "Master, the Vedas teach this policy..."
ramacharitamanas::922.translation_literal: जौं (if) / न (not) / जाउँ (I go) / तव (your) / होइ (becomes) / अकाजू (bad work, failure) / बना (made) / आइ (coming) / असमंजस (confusion, dilemma) / आजू (today) / सुनि (having heard) / महीस (the king) / बोलेउ (spoke) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (speech) / नाथ (master) / निगम (the Vedas) / असि (such) / नीति (policy, conduct) / बखानी (have described)
ramacharitamanas::922.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::922.essence: Refusing the task would harm others, so duty must answer the dilemma.
ramacharitamanas::922.simple_meaning: The speaker says that refusing to go would ruin the other person's task, so a painful dilemma has arisen. The king then replies gently, appealing to the moral guidance of the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::922.simple_insight: Sometimes duty leaves no comfortable choice, only the need to act without resentment.
ramacharitamanas::922.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, the king faces a binding obligation and a public crisis. The speaker points out that not going would cause harm, while the king responds with humility and scriptural restraint. The verse sits inside a larger negotiation, not as a complete teaching.
ramacharitamanas::922.modern_relevance: You’re on the phone at midnight, hearing that backing out will leave someone stranded. There’s no elegant option left — only the weight of showing up anyway.
ramacharitamanas::922.insight: It frames obligation as immediate and unavoidable, shifting attention from comfort to responsibility.

ramacharitamanas::923.verse_sanskrit: बड़े सनेह लघुन्ह पर करहीं। गिरि निज सिरनि सदा तृन धरहीं॥ जलधि अगाध मौलि बह फेनू। संतत धरनि धरत सिर रेनू ॥
ramacharitamanas::923.verse_hindi: बड़े लोग छोटों पर स्नेह करते ही हैं। पर्वत अपने सिरों पर सदा तृण (घास) को धारण किए रहते हैं। अगाध समुद्र अपने मस्तक पर फेन को धारण करता है और धरती अपने सिर पर सदा धूलि को धारण किए रहती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::923.english_translation: Great beings show affection to those below them. Mountains hold grass on their heads, the deep ocean holds foam on its crown, and the earth always bears dust upon its head.
ramacharitamanas::923.translation_literal: बड़े (great) / सनेह (affection) / लघुन्ह (toward the small) / पर (upon) / करहीं (do) / गिरि (mountain) / निज (own) / सिरनि (on the head) / सदा (always) / तृन (grass) / धरहीं (hold) / जलधि (ocean) / अगाध (deep, unfathomable) / मौलि (crown, head) / बह (much) / फेनू (foam) / संतत (continually) / धरनि (earth) / धरत (holding) / सिर (head) / रेनू (dust)
ramacharitamanas::923.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::923.essence: Greatness proves itself by carrying what is smaller.
ramacharitamanas::923.simple_meaning: Truly great people naturally treat those beneath them with care and humility. The mountain, ocean, and earth are used as examples of bearing what is small without pride.
ramacharitamanas::923.simple_insight: Real greatness lowers itself. It protects, carries, and makes room for others.
ramacharitamanas::923.detailed_meaning: A king is pleading with a sage for help. Before the request is answered, the poem explains the sage's nature: greatness does not boast, it shelters the small. This image prepares the king to approach with humility.
ramacharitamanas::923.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, and the new intern is terrified to ask questions. The way you answer them shows whether you rose in rank or in character.
ramacharitamanas::923.insight: It shifts status from dominance to responsibility: the higher one stands, the more gently one should hold others.

ramacharitamanas::924.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि गहे नरेस पद स्वामी होहु कृपाल। मोहि लागि दुख सहिअ प्रभु सज्जन दीनदयाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::924.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर राजा ने मुनि के चरण पकड़ लिए। (और कहा-) हे स्वामी! कृपा कीजिए। आप संत हैं। दीनदयालु हैं। (अतः) हे प्रभो! मेरे लिए इतना कष्ट (अवश्य) सहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::924.english_translation: Saying this, the king grasped the sage's feet: “Be gracious, my lord. You are kind to the lowly and distressed. Please bear this hardship for my sake.”
ramacharitamanas::924.translation_literal: अस कहि (saying thus) / गहे (grasped) / नरेस (the king) / पद (feet) / स्वामी (master) / होहु (be) / कृपाल (gracious) / मोहि लागि (for my sake) / दुख (hardship) / सहिअ (bear/endure) / प्रभु (lord) / सज्जन (good and noble one) / दीनदयाल (compassionate to the distressed)
ramacharitamanas::924.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::924.essence: True need bows first and asks with humility.
ramacharitamanas::924.simple_meaning: The king bows to the sage's feet and asks him to be kind, noble, and willing to bear hardship for his sake.
ramacharitamanas::924.simple_insight: Humility can turn a tense request into a plea that opens the heart.
ramacharitamanas::924.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, the king faces a sacred task he cannot complete alone. He falls at the sage's feet and asks for mercy, showing how quickly pride must give way when the moment demands help.
ramacharitamanas::924.modern_relevance: You are asking a senior colleague to cover for your mistake, and your voice softens before you finish the sentence. Real need sounds like this: respectful, direct, and unguarded.
ramacharitamanas::924.insight: It teaches you to ask for help without ego and to honour the one who can carry the burden with you.

ramacharitamanas::925.verse_sanskrit: जानि नृपहि आपन आधीना। बोला तापस कपट प्रबीना॥ सत्य कहउँ भूपति सुनु तोही। जग नाहिन दुर्लभ कछु मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::925.verse_hindi: राजा को अपने अधीन जानकर कपट में प्रवीण तपस्वी बोला- हे राजन् ! सुनो, मैं तुमसे सत्य कहता हूँ, जगत में मुझे कुछ भी दुर्लभ नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::925.english_translation: Seeing the king under his control, the skilled deceiver spoke: "Listen, king, I speak truthfully to you. In this world, nothing is beyond my reach."
ramacharitamanas::925.translation_literal: जानि (knowing) / नृपहि (the king) / आपन (own) / आधीना (under control) / बोला (spoke) / तापस (ascetic) / कपट (deception) / प्रबीना (skilled) / सत्य (truth) / कहउँ (I say) / भूपति (king) / सुनु (listen) / तोही (to you) / जग (world) / नाहिन (not) / दुर्लभ (hard to obtain) / कछु (anything) / मोही (for me)
ramacharitamanas::925.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::925.essence: Control makes deception sound like certainty.
ramacharitamanas::925.simple_meaning: The ascetic, skilled in deception, sees the king is now under his control and speaks confidently, claiming nothing in the world is beyond his reach.
ramacharitamanas::925.simple_insight: Charm can hide control. Confidence can be a mask for manipulation.
ramacharitamanas::925.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, the king has already been softened by respect and emotion. The ascetic notices this advantage and answers with polished confidence, preparing the ground for the promise he will make next.
ramacharitamanas::925.modern_relevance: A smooth speaker notices you are already leaning in and turns that opening into leverage. The danger is not loud force; it is a calm voice that knows exactly how to steer you.
ramacharitamanas::925.insight: It warns you to notice when persuasion is being used to create dependence before a request is made.

ramacharitamanas::926.verse_sanskrit: अवसि काज मैं करिहउँ तोरा। मन तन बचन भगत तैं मोरा॥ जोग जुगुति तप मंत्र प्रभाऊ। फलइ तबहिं जब करिअ दुराऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::926.verse_hindi: मैं तुम्हारा काम अवश्य करूँगा, (क्योंकि) तुम, मन, वाणी और शरीर (तीनों) से मेरे भक्त हो। पर योग, युक्ति, तप और मंत्रों का प्रभाव तभी फलीभूत होता है जब वे छिपाकर किए जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::926.english_translation: I will certainly do your work, because you are my devotee in mind, speech, and body. But the power of yoga, skill, austerity, and mantra bears fruit only when done in secret.
ramacharitamanas::926.translation_literal: अवसि (certainly) / काज (work) / मैं (I) / करिहउँ (will do) / तोरा (your) / मन (mind) / तन (body) / बचन (speech) / भगत (devotee) / तैं (you are) / मोरा (my) / जोग (yoga) / जुगुति (skill / method) / तप (austerity) / मंत्र (mantra) / प्रभाऊ (power / influence) / फलइ (bears fruit) / तबहिं (then only) / जब (when) / करिअ (is done) / दुराऊ (secretly)
ramacharitamanas::926.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::926.essence: Wholehearted devotion moves the divine; display is what weakens practice.
ramacharitamanas::926.simple_meaning: Ram says he will do the king's work because the king loves him with mind, speech, and body. He adds that spiritual practices work best when kept private.
ramacharitamanas::926.simple_insight: Devotion does not need an audience. Quiet sincerity carries more force than performance.
ramacharitamanas::926.detailed_meaning: A disguised sage has already won the king's trust. Now he reveals a deeper truth: Ram responds to wholehearted devotion, not status or show. The verse turns the conversation from cleverness to hidden love.
ramacharitamanas::926.modern_relevance: You help someone late at night, then resist posting about it. The act itself carries the weight. What is done quietly often has the deepest force.
ramacharitamanas::926.insight: It shifts the mind from performance to inward sincerity, showing that real practice matures away from applause.

ramacharitamanas::927.verse_sanskrit: जौं नरेस मैं करौं रसोई। तुम्ह परुसहु मोहि जान न कोई॥ अन्न सो जोइ जोइ भोजन करई। सोइ सोइ तव आयसु अनुसरई ॥
ramacharitamanas::927.verse_hindi: हे नरपति! मैं यदि रसोई बनाऊँ और तुम उसे परोसो और मुझे कोई जानने न पावे, तो उस अन्न को जो-जो खाएगा, सो-सो तुम्हारा आज्ञाकारी बन जाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::927.english_translation: O king, if I cook the meal and you serve it, and no one knows me, then whoever eats that food will become obedient to you.
ramacharitamanas::927.translation_literal: जौं (if) / नरेस (O king) / मैं (I) / करौं (do) / रसोई (cooking) / तुम्ह (you) / परुसहु (serve) / मोहि (me) / जान (know) / न (not) / कोई (anyone)॥ / अन्न (food) / सो (that) / जोइ जोइ (whoever) / भोजन (meal) / करई (eats) / सोइ सोइ (each one) / तव (your) / आयसु (command) / अनुसरई (follows) ॥
ramacharitamanas::927.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::927.essence: Quiet support can shape an entire crowd.
ramacharitamanas::927.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says that if the king serves food made by him without revealing him, everyone who eats it will come under the king's influence.
ramacharitamanas::927.simple_insight: Power can move quietly through trust, not just through force.
ramacharitamanas::927.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, a clever ascetic is bargaining with the king and testing royal confidence. He says he can prepare food so potent that anyone who eats it will obey the king, even without knowing the source. The verse advances his strange promise.
ramacharitamanas::927.modern_relevance: A team meeting ends, and one person quietly backs the decision so well that everyone leaves aligned. Influence often comes from invisible support, not public credit.
ramacharitamanas::927.insight: It shifts attention from visible control to the hidden causes that shape obedience and loyalty.

ramacharitamanas::928.verse_sanskrit: पुनि तिन्ह के गृह जेवँइ जोऊ। तव बस होइ भूप सुनु सोऊ॥ जाइ उपाय रचहु नृप एहू। संबत भरि संकलप करेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::928.verse_hindi: यही नहीं, उन (भोजन करने वालों) के घर भी जो कोई भोजन करेगा, हे राजन् ! सुनो, वह भी तुम्हारे अधीन हो जाएगा। हे राजन् ! जाकर यही उपाय करो और वर्षभर (भोजन कराने) का संकल्प कर लेना ॥
ramacharitamanas::928.english_translation: Not only that, whoever eats in the homes of those diners will also come under your control, O king. Go and arrange this remedy, and make the vow for a full year.
ramacharitamanas::928.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / तिन्ह के (their) / गृह (homes) / जेवँइ (eats) / जोऊ (whoever) / तव (your) / बस (under control) / होइ (becomes) / भूप (king) / सुनु (listen) / सोऊ (that too) / जाइ (go) / उपाय (remedy) / रचहु (devise) / नृप (king) / एहू (this) / संबत (year) / भरि (for the full) / संकलप (vow) / करेहू (make)
ramacharitamanas::928.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::928.essence: A single vow can shape lives beyond the people you directly serve.
ramacharitamanas::928.simple_meaning: The promise is widened: not only the guests, but even the people they feed will be influenced by the king's vow.
ramacharitamanas::928.simple_insight: Small acts of devotion can spread farther than you expect.
ramacharitamanas::928.detailed_meaning: A king has been told that feeding holy men can turn hearts. The teaching now expands the effect: even those who eat in those homes will come under the king's influence. The point is to show how one sincere vow can ripple outward.
ramacharitamanas::928.modern_relevance: You help one person, and they go home kinder to everyone they meet. A single generous act can keep moving long after you stop watching.
ramacharitamanas::928.insight: It shifts attention from one visible result to the wider ripple of a sincere act.

ramacharitamanas::929.verse_sanskrit: नित नूतन द्विज सहस सत बरेहु सहित परिवार। मैं तुम्हरे संकलप लगि दिनहिं करबि जेवनार ॥
ramacharitamanas::929.verse_hindi: नित्य नए एक लाख ब्राह्मणों को कुटुम्ब सहित निमंत्रित करना। मैं तुम्हारे सकंल्प (के काल अर्थात एक वर्ष) तक प्रतिदिन भोजन बना दिया करूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::929.english_translation: Invite one hundred thousand Brahmins each day, with their families. I will prepare meals daily for the full year of your vow.
ramacharitamanas::929.translation_literal: नित (daily) / नूतन (new) / द्विज (Brahmins) / सहस सत (hundred thousand) / बरेहु (invite) / सहित परिवार (with family) / मैं (I) / तुम्हरे (your) / संकलप (vow) / लगि (for) / दिनहिं (daily) / करबि (will do) / जेवनार (feast, meal)
ramacharitamanas::929.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::929.essence: Sustained service can gather what force cannot.
ramacharitamanas::929.simple_meaning: The plan is to invite huge numbers of Brahmins every day, and the speaker will cook for them throughout the vow period.
ramacharitamanas::929.simple_insight: Great service often begins with a practical promise, not a grand speech.
ramacharitamanas::929.detailed_meaning: A king is being advised on a ritual strategy. Instead of force, the plan is to win the Brahmins through daily hospitality. The speaker offers to cook for an entire year, turning service into influence.
ramacharitamanas::929.modern_relevance: A family gathering is spinning out of control, and one person quietly says, “I’ll handle the food every day.” That steady help changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::929.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to sustained service as the real power behind influence.

ramacharitamanas::930.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि भूप कष्ट अति थोरें। होइहहिं सकल बिप्र बस तोरें॥ करिहहिं बिप्र होममख सेवा। तेहिं प्रसंग सहजेहिं बस देवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::930.verse_hindi: हे राजन् ! इस प्रकार बहुत ही थोड़े परिश्रम से सब ब्राह्मण तुम्हारे वश में हो जाएँगे। ब्राह्मण हवन, यज्ञ और सेवा-पूजा करेंगे, तो उस प्रसंग (संबंध) से देवता भी सहज ही वश में हो जाएँगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::930.english_translation: In this way, O king, with very little effort all the priests will come under your control. The priests will perform homa, yajna, and service-worship, and through that connection the radiant beings will also naturally come under your control.
ramacharitamanas::930.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / भूप (king) / कष्ट (effort, hardship) / अति (very) / थोरें (little) / होइहहिं (will become) / सकल (all) / बिप्र (priests, learned Brahmins) / बस (under control) / तोरें (yours) / करिहहिं (will do) / बिप्र (priests) / होम (fire offering) / मख (sacrifice) / सेवा (service, worship) / तेहिं प्रसंग (through that connection) / सहजेहिं (naturally) / बस (under control) / देवा (radiant beings)
ramacharitamanas::930.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::930.essence: Gentle support can achieve what force cannot.
ramacharitamanas::930.simple_meaning: With little effort, the king will gain influence over the priests, and through their rituals even the radiant beings will be reached.
ramacharitamanas::930.simple_insight: It can feel reassuring to know that steady support and right relationships can open doors that force never could.
ramacharitamanas::930.detailed_meaning: A speaker is advising a king on how to gain influence without direct struggle. By supporting priests, sacrifices, and ritual service, the king can create a network that naturally extends even to the radiant beings. It is one step in a practical strategy, not the full teaching.
ramacharitamanas::930.modern_relevance: You help organize a community event, and suddenly people who never noticed your work start trusting your judgment. Influence often comes through service and alignment, not force.
ramacharitamanas::930.insight: It shifts the mind from brute control to indirect influence through support and ritual order.

ramacharitamanas::931.verse_sanskrit: और एक तोहि कहउँ लखाऊ। मैं एहिं बेष न आउब काऊ॥ तुम्हरे उपरोहित कहुँ राया। हरि आनब मैं करि निज माया ॥
ramacharitamanas::931.verse_hindi: मैं एक और पहचान तुमको बताए देता हूँ कि मैं इस रूप में कभी न आऊँगा। हे राजन् ! मैं अपनी माया से तुम्हारे पुरोहित को हर लाऊँगा ॥\
ramacharitamanas::931.english_translation: I will tell you one more thing: I will never come in this form. O king, I will use my power to take your priest away.
ramacharitamanas::931.translation_literal: और (and) / एक (one) / तोहि (to you) / कहउँ (I tell) / लखाऊ (make known) / मैं (I) / एहिं (this) / बेष (form/disguise) / न (not) / आउब (will come) / काऊ (at all)॥ / तुम्हरे (your) / उपरोहित (priest) / कहुँ (for) / राया (O king) / हरि (will take away) / आनब (I will bring) / मैं (I) / करि (doing) / निज (my own) / माया (power of illusion) ॥
ramacharitamanas::931.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::931.essence: The disguise is temporary; the real change is already underway.
ramacharitamanas::931.simple_meaning: The speaker says he will not appear in this disguise again and will use his power to remove the king’s priest.
ramacharitamanas::931.simple_insight: Not every promise is straightforward; some carry hidden force and change the whole situation.
ramacharitamanas::931.detailed_meaning: A disguised visitor is speaking to King Bali’s court in the middle of a clever divine test. After promising one thing, he adds a sharper warning: he will not return in this form and will use his power to remove the priest who is advising the king.
ramacharitamanas::931.modern_relevance: A person smiles politely in a meeting, then quietly rewrites the entire plan behind the scenes. The real move is not always the one announced first.
ramacharitamanas::931.insight: It prepares the reader for a strategic shift: what looks like a simple request is actually part of a larger divine intervention.

ramacharitamanas::932.verse_sanskrit: तपबल तेहि करि आपु समाना। रखिहउँ इहाँ बरष परवाना॥ मैं धरि तासु बेषु सुनु राजा। सब बिधि तोर सँवारब काजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::932.verse_hindi: तप के बल से उसे अपने समान बनाकर एक वर्ष यहाँ रखूँगा और हे राजन् ! सुनो, मैं उसका रूप बनाकर सब प्रकार से तुम्हारा काम सिद्ध करूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::932.english_translation: By the power of austerity, I will make him like myself and keep him here for a year. Listen, O king, I will take his form and accomplish all your work in every way.
ramacharitamanas::932.translation_literal: तपबल (by the power of austerity) / तेहि (him) / करि (making) / आपु (myself) / समाना (equal-like) / रखिहउँ (I will keep) / इहाँ (here) / बरष (year) / परवाना (duration)॥ / मैं (I) / धरि (taking) / तासु (his) / बेषु (form) / सुनु (listen) / राजा (O king) / सब बिधि (in every way) / तोर (your) / सँवारब (will arrange) / काजा (work)॥
ramacharitamanas::932.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::932.essence: Spiritual power can reshape events without public display.
ramacharitamanas::932.simple_meaning: The sage says he will use his spiritual power to keep a man in place for a year and take that man's form to handle the king's work.
ramacharitamanas::932.simple_insight: Power is shown not by force, but by the ability to quietly alter events for dharma.
ramacharitamanas::932.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the disguised sage is still speaking with the king. He has already promised to remove the ordinary priest and now explains the next step: through tapas, he will hold that man in one place and personally take his form to complete the king's plan.
ramacharitamanas::932.modern_relevance: A skilled fixer steps into a broken process, takes on someone else's role, and quietly makes the whole thing work while everyone else sleeps.
ramacharitamanas::932.insight: It shifts attention from visible effort to hidden power working behind events.

ramacharitamanas::933.verse_sanskrit: गै निसि बहुत सयन अब कीजे। मोहि तोहि भूप भेंट दिन तीजे॥ मैं तपबल तोहि तुरग समेता। पहुँचैहउँ सोवतहि निकेता ॥
ramacharitamanas::933.verse_hindi: हे राजन् ! रात बहुत बीत गई, अब सो जाओ। आज से तीसरे दिन मुझसे तुम्हारी भेंट होगी। तप के बल से मैं घोड़े सहित तुमको सोते ही में घर पहुँचा दूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::933.english_translation: O king, the night has passed. Now go to sleep. On the third day from today, you and I will meet. By the power of my austerity, I will carry you home along with your horse while you sleep.
ramacharitamanas::933.translation_literal: गै (has passed) / निसि (night) / बहुत (much) / सयन (sleep) / अब (now) / कीजे (do) / मोहि (me) / तोहि (you) / भूप (king) / भेंट (meeting) / दिन (day) / तीजे (third) / मैं (I) / तपबल (by the power of austerity) / तोहि (you) / तुरग (horse) / समेता (along with) / पहुँचैहउँ (I will bring) / सोवतहि (while sleeping) / निकेता (home)
ramacharitamanas::933.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::933.essence: True power can protect without being seen.
ramacharitamanas::933.simple_meaning: The speaker tells the king to sleep, promises a meeting in three days, and says he will carry the king and horse home while the king sleeps.
ramacharitamanas::933.simple_insight: Some help works quietly, without drama or effort from the one receiving it.
ramacharitamanas::933.detailed_meaning: In King Janaka’s court, Vishvamitra is speaking after revealing his power. He tells the king to rest, promises they will meet again in three days, and says he can return the king home effortlessly. The verse builds trust in the sage’s extraordinary ability.
ramacharitamanas::933.modern_relevance: You fall asleep after a long, exhausting day, trusting someone else has already handled the problem. Relief comes when control is no longer yours to carry.
ramacharitamanas::933.insight: It shifts attention from personal control to confident reliance on a capable guide.

ramacharitamanas::934.verse_sanskrit: मैं आउब सोइ बेषु धरि पहिचानेहु तब मोहि। जब एकांत बोलाइ सब कथा सुनावौं तोहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::934.verse_hindi: मैं वही (पुरोहित का) वेश धरकर आऊँगा। जब एकांत में तुमको बुलाकर सब कथा सुनाऊँगा, तब तुम मुझे पहचान लेना ॥
ramacharitamanas::934.english_translation: I will come in that same disguise. When I call you aside in private and tell you the whole story, then you will recognize me.
ramacharitamanas::934.translation_literal: मैं (I) / आउब (will come) / सोइ (that same) / बेषु (disguise/appearance) / धरि (wearing) / पहिचानेहु (recognize) / तब (then) / मोहि (me) / जब (when) / एकांत (private seclusion) / बोलाइ (calling) / सब (all) / कथा (story) / सुनावौं (I tell) / तोहि (to you)
ramacharitamanas::934.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::934.essence: Truth can wear a disguise until the right moment.
ramacharitamanas::934.simple_meaning: The speaker says he will return in disguise and reveal the full story only in private, so the king will know who he is.
ramacharitamanas::934.simple_insight: Not every truth arrives openly. Some things are revealed only when the moment is right.
ramacharitamanas::934.detailed_meaning: At night in Janak's court, the mysterious teacher is arranging a hidden plan. He has promised to return in disguise, speak privately, and guide the king through the next step. This verse keeps the suspense moving toward the secret meeting.
ramacharitamanas::934.modern_relevance: Someone texts, 'Can we talk in private?' and suddenly the whole tone changes. Some conversations need the right setting before the truth can land.
ramacharitamanas::934.insight: It teaches you to respect timing and context, not force revelation before trust is ready.

ramacharitamanas::935.verse_sanskrit: सयन कीन्ह नृप आयसु मानी। आसन जाइ बैठ छलग्यानी॥ श्रमित भूप निद्रा अति आई। सो किमि सोव सोच अधिकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::935.verse_hindi: राजा ने आज्ञा मानकर शयन किया और वह कपट-ज्ञानी आसन पर जा बैठा। राजा थका था, (उसे) खूब (गहरी) नींद आ गई। पर वह कपटी कैसे सोता। उसे तो बहुत चिन्ता हो रही थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::935.english_translation: The king obeyed and lay down to sleep. The deceiver sat on the seat. The weary king fell into deep sleep, but how could the deceiver sleep? His mind was full of worry.
ramacharitamanas::935.translation_literal: सयन (sleep) / कीन्ह (did) / नृप (king) / आयसु (command) / मानी (having obeyed) / आसन (seat) / जाइ (going) / बैठ (sat) / छलग्यानी (deceitful-knower) ॥ / श्रमित (tired) / भूप (king) / निद्रा (sleep) / अति (very) / आई (came) / सो (he) / किमि (how) / सोव (slept) / सोच (worry) / अधिकाई (greatly increased) ॥
ramacharitamanas::935.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::935.essence: A tired body can sleep; a scheming mind cannot.
ramacharitamanas::935.simple_meaning: The king goes to sleep, but the deceitful man cannot rest because he is full of worry and scheming.
ramacharitamanas::935.simple_insight: A guilty mind cannot settle, even in a quiet room.
ramacharitamanas::935.detailed_meaning: In the palace at night, the king follows the order to sleep while the disguised trickster takes the seat. The king is exhausted and drifts off, but the schemer stays awake, trapped in his own anxious plotting. The scene sets up the next act of deception.
ramacharitamanas::935.modern_relevance: You finally turn off the lights after a draining day, but your mind keeps replaying the conversation, the plan, the lie, the risk. The body wants rest; the restless mind refuses it.
ramacharitamanas::935.insight: It shows how inner agitation outlasts physical fatigue when the mind is caught in deceit.

ramacharitamanas::936.verse_sanskrit: कालकेतु निसिचर तहँ आवा। जेहिं सूकर होइ नृपहि भुलावा॥ परम मित्र तापस नृप केरा। जानइ सो अति कपट घनेरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::936.verse_hindi: (उसी समय) वहाँ कालकेतु राक्षस आया, जिसने सूअर बनकर राजा को भटकाया था। वह तपस्वी राजा का बड़ा मित्र था और खूब छल-प्रपंच जानता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::936.english_translation: At that very time, the demon Kalaketu arrived, the same one who had once misled the king in the form of a boar. He was the ascetic king's close friend and knew many tricks of deceit.
ramacharitamanas::936.translation_literal: कालकेतु (Kalaketu) / निसिचर (demon) / तहँ (there) / आवा (came) / जेहिं (who) / सूकर (boar) / होइ (becoming) / नृपहि (the king) / भुलावा (misled) / परम (great) / मित्र (friend) / तापस (ascetic) / नृप (king) / केरा (of) / जानइ (knows) / सो (he) / अति (very) / कपट (deceit) / घनेरा (much)
ramacharitamanas::936.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::936.essence: Deceit is most dangerous when it returns as a friend.
ramacharitamanas::936.simple_meaning: Kalaketu, a deceitful demon and close friend of the king, arrives. The verse reminds us that he is skilled in trickery and has already misled the king before.
ramacharitamanas::936.simple_insight: Not every friendly face is safe. Deceit often returns wearing familiarity.
ramacharitamanas::936.detailed_meaning: In this Ayodhyakand-style court intrigue, the king has already been softened by sleep and confusion. Now Kalaketu, the same trickster who once led him astray as a boar, appears again as a trusted friend. The scene deepens the danger before the next move.
ramacharitamanas::936.modern_relevance: A smooth-talking colleague shows up again right after you lowered your guard. The danger is not loud; it arrives wearing trust and old familiarity.
ramacharitamanas::936.insight: It trains you to notice repeated manipulation, especially when it comes disguised as friendship.

ramacharitamanas::937.verse_sanskrit: तेहि के सत सुत अरु दस भाई। खल अति अजय देव दुखदाई॥ प्रथमहिं भूप समर सब मारे। बिप्र संत सुर देखि दुखारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::937.verse_hindi: उसके सौ पुत्र और दस भाई थे, जो बड़े ही दुष्ट, किसी से न जीते जाने वाले और देवताओं को दुःख देने वाले थे। ब्राह्मणों, संतों और देवताओं को दुःखी देखकर राजा ने उन सबको पहले ही युद्ध में मार डाला था ॥
ramacharitamanas::937.english_translation: He had a hundred sons and ten brothers, all extremely wicked, unconquerable, and harmful to the radiant beings. Seeing the suffering of the learned, the holy, and the radiant beings, the king had already killed them in battle.
ramacharitamanas::937.translation_literal: तेहि (his) / के (of) / सत (hundred) / सुत (sons) / अरु (and) / दस (ten) / भाई (brothers) / खल (wicked) / अति (very) / अजय (unconquerable) / देव (radiant beings) / दुखदाई (pain-giving) / प्रथमहिं (first/earlier) / भूप (king) / समर (battle) / सब (all) / मारे (killed) / बिप्र (learned) / संत (holy ones) / सुर (radiant beings) / देखि (seeing) / दुखारे (grieved)
ramacharitamanas::937.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::937.essence: Protecting the vulnerable can create enemies among the cruel.
ramacharitamanas::937.simple_meaning: The verse describes the king's enemies: a huge family of wicked, powerful beings. It also says the king had already slain them because they caused suffering to the learned, holy, and radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::937.simple_insight: Some victories are not personal glory; they are protection for those who cannot protect themselves.
ramacharitamanas::937.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand story, the narration pauses to explain who the hostile force is. This king had once destroyed a terrible family of one hundred sons and ten brothers because they tormented the learned, the holy, and the radiant beings. The verse sets up the reason for the coming revenge.
ramacharitamanas::937.modern_relevance: A person who quietly protects a vulnerable community may later become the target of resentment from those who benefited from the harm. The earlier act of defense is what the next conflict is really about.
ramacharitamanas::937.insight: It frames conflict as a response to prior harm, not random hostility.

ramacharitamanas::938.verse_sanskrit: तेहिं खल पाछिल बयरु सँभारा। तापस नृप मिलि मंत्र बिचारा॥ जेहिं रिपु छय सोइ रचेन्हि उपाऊ। भावी बस न जान कछु राऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::938.verse_hindi: उस दुष्ट ने पिछला बैर याद करके तपस्वी राजा से मिलकर सलाह विचारी (षड्यंत्र किया) और जिस प्रकार शत्रु का नाश हो, वही उपाय रचा। भावीवश राजा (प्रतापभानु) कुछ भी न समझ सका ॥
ramacharitamanas::938.english_translation: That wicked one revived his old enmity. He met the ascetic king and plotted a strategy. He devised a way to destroy his enemy, but fate kept King Pratapbhanu unaware.
ramacharitamanas::938.translation_literal: तेहिं (that) / खल (wicked one) / पाछिल (previous) / बयरु (enmity) / सँभारा (remembered, revived) / तापस नृप (ascetic king) / मिलि (meeting) / मंत्र (counsel, plan) / बिचारा (considered, plotted)॥ / जेहिं (by which) / रिपु (enemy) / छय (destruction) / सोइ (that only) / रचेन्हि (he devised) / उपाऊ (means, strategy) / भावी (by fate) / बस (under control) / न (not) / जान (knew) / कछु (anything) / राऊ (the king) ॥
ramacharitamanas::938.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::938.essence: Old enmity quietly becomes a trap.
ramacharitamanas::938.simple_meaning: The enemy remembered an old grudge, planned in secret with the king, and set a trap. The king did not realize what was happening.
ramacharitamanas::938.simple_insight: Hidden resentment can shape a plan long before anyone sees the danger.
ramacharitamanas::938.detailed_meaning: In Pratapbhanu’s story, the deceitful ally Kalaketu revives an old grudge and joins the ascetic king in secret planning. The verse shows the trap being built before the king understands he is already caught.
ramacharitamanas::938.modern_relevance: A colleague smiles in the meeting, then quietly turns others against you after it ends. By the time the damage is visible, the plan was already in motion.
ramacharitamanas::938.insight: It trains the reader to notice how resentment and strategy can work together before harm becomes obvious.

ramacharitamanas::939.verse_sanskrit: रिपु तेजसी अकेल अपि लघु करि गनिअ न ताहु। अजहुँ देत दुख रबि ससिहि सिर अवसेषित राहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::939.verse_hindi: तेजस्वी शत्रु अकेला भी हो तो भी उसे छोटा नहीं समझना चाहिए। जिसका सिर मात्र बचा था, वह राहु आज तक सूर्य-चन्द्रमा को दुःख देता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::939.english_translation: A powerful enemy should not be underestimated, even when alone. Rahu, with only his head left, still troubles the sun and moon.
ramacharitamanas::939.translation_literal: रिपु (enemy) / तेजसी (powerful, radiant) / अकेल (alone) / अपि (even) / लघु (small) / करि (making) / गनिअ (should be considered) / न (not) / ताहु (that one) / अजहुँ (still) / देत (gives) / दुख (pain) / रबि (sun) / ससिहि (moon) / सिर (head) / अवसेषित (left over) / राहु (Rahu)
ramacharitamanas::939.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::939.essence: A weakened enemy can still strike hard.
ramacharitamanas::939.simple_meaning: A strong enemy must never be dismissed just because he stands alone. Even a defeated force can still cause harm.
ramacharitamanas::939.simple_insight: Stay alert to danger, even after it seems broken.
ramacharitamanas::939.detailed_meaning: The verse comes in a warning sequence about a wicked ruler and his allies. After describing their cruelty and plotting, the poet uses Rahu as an example: even a being with only a head left can still torment the sun and moon.
ramacharitamanas::939.modern_relevance: You think the conflict is over because one loud critic is gone. Then one message, one rumor, one stubborn person keeps the whole situation burning.
ramacharitamanas::939.insight: It teaches you not to mistake partial defeat for complete safety.

ramacharitamanas::940.verse_sanskrit: तापस नृप निज सखहि निहारी। हरषि मिलेउ उठि भयउ सुखारी॥ मित्रहि कहि सब कथा सुनाई। जातुधान बोला सुख पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::940.verse_hindi: तपस्वी राजा अपने मित्र को देख प्रसन्न हो उठकर मिला और सुखी हुआ। उसने मित्र को सब कथा कह सुनाई, तब राक्षस आनंदित होकर बोला ॥
ramacharitamanas::940.english_translation: The ascetic king saw his friend, rose joyfully, and embraced him. He told his friend the whole story, and the demon rejoiced.
ramacharitamanas::940.translation_literal: तापस (ascetic) / नृप (king) / निज (own) / सखहि (friend) / निहारी (seeing) / हरषि (rejoicing) / मिलेउ (met) / उठि (rising) / भयउ (became) / सुखारी (happy) / मित्रहि (to the friend) / कहि (telling) / सब (all) / कथा (story) / सुनाई (told) / जातुधान (demon) / बोला (spoke) / सुख पाई (having gained joy)
ramacharitamanas::940.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::940.essence: Joy can blind a person to danger standing right beside him.
ramacharitamanas::940.simple_meaning: The king greets his friend happily and shares everything with him. The demon listens and feels pleased.
ramacharitamanas::940.simple_insight: Not every warm welcome is trustworthy. The heart can open to the wrong person.
ramacharitamanas::940.detailed_meaning: A tapasvi king meets his old friend with joy and tells him everything that has happened. The friend is actually a demon, and the scene is part of a larger trap already forming around the king.
ramacharitamanas::940.modern_relevance: You call an old friend to vent, relieved to be understood. But the person smiling at your pain may be the one feeding it forward.
ramacharitamanas::940.insight: It warns you to test trust before disclosure, especially when someone is already aligned with harm.

ramacharitamanas::941.verse_sanskrit: अब साधेउँ रिपु सुनहु नरेसा। जौं तुम्ह कीन्ह मोर उपदेसा॥ परिहरि सोच रहहु तुम्ह सोई। बिनु औषध बिआधि बिधि खोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::941.verse_hindi: हे राजन् ! सुनो, जब तुमने मेरे कहने के अनुसार (इतना) काम कर लिया, तो अब मैंने शत्रु को काबू में कर ही लिया (समझो)। तुम अब चिन्ता त्याग सो रहो। विधाता ने बिना ही दवा के रोग दूर कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::941.english_translation: O king, listen. Since you have followed my instruction, the enemy has now been subdued. Let go of your worry and rest. Fate has removed the illness without medicine.
ramacharitamanas::941.translation_literal: अब (now) / साधेउँ (I have subdued) / रिपु (enemy) / सुनहु (listen) / नरेसा (O king) / जौं (since) / तुम्ह (you) / कीन्ह (did) / मोर (my) / उपदेसा (instruction) / परिहरि (casting off) / सोच (worry) / रहहु (remain) / तुम्ह (you) / सोई (at ease) / बिनु (without) / औषध (medicine) / बिआधि (illness) / बिधि (fate) / खोई (removed)
ramacharitamanas::941.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::941.essence: False reassurance can be the final step of a trap.
ramacharitamanas::941.simple_meaning: The speaker tells the king that following the advice has already defeated the enemy, so there is no need to worry anymore.
ramacharitamanas::941.simple_insight: Relief comes when you trust good guidance and stop feeding fear after the work is done.
ramacharitamanas::941.detailed_meaning: A tapasvi king has just heard a cunning enemy speak with false confidence. The enemy now pretends the danger is already handled and tells the king to stop worrying. The verse is part of a deceptive reassurance before the next move.
ramacharitamanas::941.modern_relevance: Someone says, “It’s all fine now,” right after you’ve been pushed into relaxing your guard. The calm tone itself is part of the trick.
ramacharitamanas::941.insight: It warns you not to mistake soothing words for real safety.

ramacharitamanas::942.verse_sanskrit: कुल समेत रिपु मूल बहाई। चौथें दिवस मिलब मैं आई॥ तापस नृपहि बहुत परितोषी। चला महाकपटी अतिरोषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::942.verse_hindi: कुल सहित शत्रु को जड़-मूल से उखाड़-बहाकर, (आज से) चौथे दिन मैं तुमसे आ मिलूँगा। (इस प्रकार) तपस्वी राजा को खूब दिलासा देकर वह महामायावी और अत्यन्त क्रोधी राक्षस चला ॥
ramacharitamanas::942.english_translation: After uprooting the enemy from the root along with his whole line, I will meet you on the fourth day. Giving the ascetic-king great comfort in this way, that great deceiver and furious demon went away.
ramacharitamanas::942.translation_literal: कुल समेत (along with the whole line) / रिपु (enemy) / मूल (root) / बहाई (uprooting and throwing away) / चौथें दिवस (on the fourth day) / मिलब (I will meet) / मैं (I) / आई (coming) / तापस नृपहि (to the ascetic king) / बहुत (greatly) / परितोषी (pleased/comforted) / चला (went) / महाकपटी (great deceiver) / अतिरोषी (very angry)
ramacharitamanas::942.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::942.essence: A lie can soothe before it strikes.
ramacharitamanas::942.simple_meaning: The deceiver promises to destroy the enemy and return in four days. He uses this promise to comfort the king, then leaves in anger.
ramacharitamanas::942.simple_insight: False reassurance can sound calm while hiding violent intent.
ramacharitamanas::942.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, the demon king Ravana is in disguise, manipulating King Pratapbhanu. He pretends to be helpful, promises swift victory, and wins the king’s trust. The verse shows the instant before his deception bears fruit.
ramacharitamanas::942.modern_relevance: A smooth-talking person says, “Leave it to me, I’ll fix everything by Thursday,” and you feel relieved for a second. The danger is in how comfort can be manufactured.
ramacharitamanas::942.insight: It trains you to notice reassurance that serves manipulation rather than truth.

ramacharitamanas::943.verse_sanskrit: भानुप्रतापहि बाजि समेता। पहुँचाएसि छन माझ निकेता॥ नृपहि नारि पहिं सयन कराई। हयगृहँ बाँधेसि बाजि बनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::943.verse_hindi: उसने प्रतापभानु राजा को घोड़े सहित क्षणभर में घर पहुँचा दिया। राजा को रानी के पास सुलाकर घोड़े को अच्छी तरह से घुड़साल में बाँध दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::943.english_translation: He carried King Bhanupratap home with his horse in an instant. He laid the king beside his queen and tied the horse securely in the stable.
ramacharitamanas::943.translation_literal: भानु-प्रतापहि (King Bhanupratap) / बाजि (horse) / समेता (together with) / पहुँचाएसि (he brought) / छन माझ (in a moment) / निकेता (home) ॥ / नृपहि (the king) / नारि पहिं (beside the queen) / सयन (sleeping) / कराई (made) / हय-गृहँ (in the horse-stable) / बाँधेसि (he tied) / बाजि (the horse) / बनाई (properly) ॥
ramacharitamanas::943.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::943.essence: Deception can arrive dressed as help and leave no alarm behind.
ramacharitamanas::943.simple_meaning: The disguised figure quickly brings the king home, settles him beside his wife, and secures the horse in the stable.
ramacharitamanas::943.simple_insight: Some power works quietly and completely, leaving no trace of effort behind.
ramacharitamanas::943.detailed_meaning: The trickster has already reassured King Pratāpabhanu that the enemy is defeated. Now, in a blink, he carries the king home, puts him to bed beside his queen, and hides the horse away. The deception is unfolding with perfect speed.
ramacharitamanas::943.modern_relevance: A problem seems solved in one smooth sweep, and everyone relaxes before noticing the trap was part of the solution. Quick relief can hide deeper manipulation.
ramacharitamanas::943.insight: It shows how illusion can move fast enough to feel like rescue.

ramacharitamanas::944.verse_sanskrit: राजा के उपरोहितहि हरि लै गयउ बहोरि। लै राखेसि गिरि खोह महुँ मायाँ करि मति भोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::944.verse_hindi: फिर वह राजा के पुरोहित को उठा ले गया और माया से उसकी बुद्धि को भ्रम में डालकर उसे उसने पहाड़ की खोह में ला रखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::944.english_translation: Then he carried off the king's priest again, and by illusion clouded his mind and left him in a mountain cave.
ramacharitamanas::944.translation_literal: राजा के (of the king's) उपरोहितहि (the priest) हरि (carried off) लै गयउ (went away taking) बहोरि (again) / लै (taking) राखेसि (kept) गिरि (mountain) खोह (cave) महुँ (in) मायाँ (illusion) करि (doing) मति (mind) भोरि (confused)
ramacharitamanas::944.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::944.essence: Illusion first clouds the mind, then moves the person.
ramacharitamanas::944.simple_meaning: The king's priest is taken away again and left confused in a mountain cave through illusion.
ramacharitamanas::944.simple_insight: Deception can trap a person by first clouding judgment.
ramacharitamanas::944.detailed_meaning: In the story of King Pratapbhanu, the deceptive figure is still at work. After misleading the king, he now removes the royal priest too, using illusion to cloud his mind and hide him in a mountain cave. The trick is tightening around the whole court.
ramacharitamanas::944.modern_relevance: Someone in a group chat keeps steering everyone off course, and by the time people notice, the damage is already done. Confusion spreads fastest when judgment is blurred.
ramacharitamanas::944.insight: It shows how manipulation works by isolating helpers and weakening clear thinking.

ramacharitamanas::945.verse_sanskrit: आपु बिरचि उपरोहित रूपा। परेउ जाइ तेहि सेज अनूपा॥ जागेउ नृप अनभएँ बिहाना। देखि भवन अति अचरजु माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::945.verse_hindi: वह आप पुरोहित का रूप बनाकर उसकी सुंदर सेज पर जा लेटा। राजा सबेरा होने से पहले ही जागा और अपना घर देखकर उसने बड़ा ही आश्चर्य माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::945.english_translation: He fashioned himself as the priest and lay down on the priest's beautiful bed. The king woke before dawn and, seeing his own palace, was filled with wonder.
ramacharitamanas::945.translation_literal: आपु (himself) / बिरचि (fashioning) / उपरोहित रूपा (in the form of the priest) / परेउ (lay down) / जाइ (going) / तेहि (that) / सेज (bed) / अनूपा (beautiful, unmatched) ॥ जागेउ (woke) / नृप (the king) / अनभएँ (before dawn) / बिहाना (morning) / देखि (seeing) / भवन (the house/palace) / अति (very) / अचरजु (wonder) / माना (felt) ॥
ramacharitamanas::945.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::945.essence: A disguise can reorder reality for a moment.
ramacharitamanas::945.simple_meaning: He took the priest's form and lay on the priest's bed. At daybreak, the king woke up in his own palace and was astonished.
ramacharitamanas::945.simple_insight: The scene turns on clever disguise and sudden confusion, not on a teaching about how to live.
ramacharitamanas::945.detailed_meaning: The hidden force behind the king's ordeal keeps working in the palace. Taking the priest's form, he lies down on the priest's bed, and before dawn the king wakes in confusion, staring at the palace with wonder. The verse advances the trick, not a doctrine.
ramacharitamanas::945.modern_relevance: You wake up in a hotel room after a long night and need a second to remember where you are. That brief confusion is all this verse holds.
ramacharitamanas::945.insight: It shows a story moving through disguise and disorientation, setting up the next step.

ramacharitamanas::946.verse_sanskrit: मुनि महिमा मन महुँ अनुमानी। उठेउ गवँहिं जेहिं जान न रानी॥ कानन गयउ बाजि चढ़ि तेहीं। पुर नर नारि न जानेउ केहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::946.verse_hindi: मन में मुनि की महिमा का अनुमान करके वह धीरे से उठा, जिसमें रानी न जान पावे। फिर उसी घोड़े पर चढ़कर वन को चला गया। नगर के किसी भी स्त्री-पुरुष ने नहीं जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::946.english_translation: Thinking of the sage's greatness in his heart, he rose quietly so the queen would not know. Then he mounted that same horse and rode into the forest. No man or woman in the city knew.
ramacharitamanas::946.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / महिमा (greatness) / मन महुँ (in the mind) / अनुमानी (having considered) / उठेउ (rose) / गवँहिं (quietly) / जेहिं (so that) / जान (know) / न (not) / रानी (queen) / कानन (forest) / गयउ (went) / बाजि (horse) / चढ़ि (mounted) / तेहीं (that same) / पुर (city) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / न (not) / जानेउ (knew) / केहीं (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::946.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::946.essence: Quiet action can carry the heaviest turning point.
ramacharitamanas::946.simple_meaning: He leaves quietly, without letting the queen or the city know, and rides into the forest.
ramacharitamanas::946.simple_insight: Some departures are carried by humility and silence, not announcement.
ramacharitamanas::946.detailed_meaning: The king has just been tricked into believing the priest’s absence is normal. Now the priest, moved by the sage’s hidden influence, rises without waking the queen, mounts the horse, and slips away toward the forest. The scene keeps the deception moving.
ramacharitamanas::946.modern_relevance: You slip out before dawn for a difficult conversation, hoping no one notices the weight you’re carrying. Some responsibilities are borne in silence.
ramacharitamanas::946.insight: It shows action without display: move decisively, but without stirring the whole house.

ramacharitamanas::947.verse_sanskrit: गएँ जाम जुग भूपति आवा। घर घर उत्सव बाज बधावा॥ उपरोहितहि देख जब राजा। चकित बिलोक सुमिरि सोइ काजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::947.verse_hindi: दो पहर बीत जाने पर राजा आया। घर-घर उत्सव होने लगे और बधावा बजने लगा। जब राजा ने पुरोहित को देखा, तब वह (अपने) उसी कार्य का स्मरणकर उसे आश्चर्य से देखने लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::947.english_translation: After half the day passed, the king returned. Every house filled with celebration and drums of welcome. When the king saw the priest, he stared in amazement, remembering that very deed.
ramacharitamanas::947.translation_literal: गएँ जाम (after half the day) / जुग (two) / भूपति (king) / आवा (came) / घर घर (in every house) / उत्सव (celebration) / बाज (drums) / बधावा (welcome songs) / उपरोहितहि (the priest) / देख (seeing) / जब (when) / राजा (the king) / चकित (astonished) / बिलोक (looked) / सुमिरि (remembering) / सोइ (that very) / काजा (deed)
ramacharitamanas::947.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::947.essence: Joy outside cannot erase the memory of a hidden deed.
ramacharitamanas::947.simple_meaning: The king comes home to a city full of celebration, then sees the priest and remembers the strange deed with surprise.
ramacharitamanas::947.simple_insight: A hidden act can return later and meet the doer with its own force.
ramacharitamanas::947.detailed_meaning: The king has returned after the priest’s secret act, and the whole city is celebrating. But when he sees the priest again, the memory of what happened rushes back, and surprise replaces ease. This verse keeps the scene moving toward the revelation.
ramacharitamanas::947.modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering after a private mistake, and someone’s face reminds you instantly. The room is cheerful, but your own memory is not.
ramacharitamanas::947.insight: It shows how a buried action can resurface the moment its witness appears.

ramacharitamanas::948.verse_sanskrit: जुग सम नृपहि गए दिन तीनी। कपटी मुनि पद रह मति लीनी॥ समय जान उपरोहित आवा। नृपहि मते सब कहि समुझावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::948.verse_hindi: राजा को तीन दिन युग के समान बीते। उसकी बुद्धि कपटी मुनि के चरणों में लगी रही। निश्चित समय जानकर पुरोहित (बना हुआ राक्षस) आया और राजा के साथ की हुई गुप्त सलाह के अनुसार (उसने अपने) सब विचार उसे समझाकर कह दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::948.english_translation: Three days passed for the king like ages. His mind stayed fixed at the feet of the deceitful ascetic. At the right time, the priest arrived and explained everything according to the secret plan agreed upon with the king.
ramacharitamanas::948.translation_literal: जुग (ages) / सम (like) / नृपहि (for the king) / गए (passed) / दिन (days) / तीनी (three) / कपटी (deceitful) / मुनि (ascetic) / पद (feet) / रह (stayed) / मति (mind) / लीनी (taken) / समय (time) / जान (knowing) / उपरोहित (the priest) / आवा (came) / नृपहि (to the king) / मते (according to the plan) / सब (all) / कहि (having said) / समुझावा (explained)
ramacharitamanas::948.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::948.essence: Uncertainty makes even a few days feel endless.
ramacharitamanas::948.simple_meaning: The king waited three days in anxious expectation, still trusting the disguised ascetic. Then the priest arrived at the appointed time and explained the agreed plan.
ramacharitamanas::948.simple_insight: Waiting can stretch time painfully when hope and uncertainty are mixed.
ramacharitamanas::948.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the king has been kept in suspense by the disguised ascetic's plan. Three days feel endless to him, and his attention remains trapped in that deception. At the appointed moment, the priest returns and quietly lays out the next step.
ramacharitamanas::948.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone after sending a message that matters. Every minute feels longer than it should, because your mind has already gone ahead of the answer.
ramacharitamanas::948.insight: It shows how expectation can distort time and hold the mind captive until the next instruction arrives.

ramacharitamanas::949.verse_sanskrit: नृप हरषेउ पहिचानि गुरु भ्रम बस रहा न चेत। बरे तुरत सत सहस बर बिप्र कुटुंब समेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::949.verse_hindi: (संकेत के अनुसार) गुरु को (उस रूप में) पहचानकर राजा प्रसन्न हुआ। भ्रमवश उसे चेत न रहा (कि यह तापस मुनि है या कालकेतु राक्षस)। उसने तुरंत एक लाख उत्तम ब्राह्मणों को कुटुम्ब सहित निमंत्रण दे दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::949.english_translation: The king rejoiced after recognizing the guru. Deluded by illusion, he did not realize what was happening, and at once invited one hundred thousand excellent Brahmins with their families.
ramacharitamanas::949.translation_literal: नृप (the king) / हरषेउ (rejoiced) / पहिचानि (having recognized) / गुरु (the teacher) / भ्रम (delusion) / बस (under) / रहा (remained) / न (not) / चेत (aware) / बरे (invited) / तुरत (immediately) / सत (hundred) / सहस (thousand) / बर (excellent) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / कुटुंब (families) / समेत (together with)
ramacharitamanas::949.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::949.essence: Recognition without clear seeing still leaves a person easy to mislead.
ramacharitamanas::949.simple_meaning: The king thinks he has recognized his teacher and feels happy, but illusion still clouds his mind. He quickly invites a huge number of Brahmins with their families.
ramacharitamanas::949.simple_insight: A mistaken certainty can make you act fast while still missing the truth.
ramacharitamanas::949.detailed_meaning: The king has been waiting in confusion while a deceptive plan unfolds around him. Seeing the disguised guru, he feels relieved and immediately orders a massive invitation for Brahmins and their households. His happiness is real, but his understanding is still trapped in delusion.
ramacharitamanas::949.modern_relevance: You finally get a reply from someone you trust, and relief makes you stop checking the details. One warm feeling can make you overlook the whole setup.
ramacharitamanas::949.insight: It shows how relief can deepen error when the mind stops questioning too soon.

ramacharitamanas::950.verse_sanskrit: उपरोहित जेवनार बनाई। छरस चारि बिधि जसि श्रुति गाई॥ मायामय तेहिं कीन्हि रसोई। बिंजन बहु गनि सकइ न कोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::950.verse_hindi: पुरोहित ने छह रस और चार प्रकार के भोजन, जैसा कि वेदों में वर्णन है, बनाए। उसने मायामयी रसोई तैयार की और इतने व्यंजन बनाए, जिन्हें कोई गिन नहीं सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::950.english_translation: The priest prepared a feast with six tastes and four kinds of food, as the Vedas describe. He set up an illusion-made kitchen and cooked countless dishes no one could number.
ramacharitamanas::950.translation_literal: उपरोहित (the priest) / जेवनार (feast) / बनाई (made) / छरस (six tastes) / चारि बिधि (four kinds) / जसि (as) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / गाई (sing)॥ / मायामय (illusory) / तेहिं (by him) / कीन्हि (made) / रसोई (kitchen/cooking) / बिंजन (dishes) / बहु (many) / गनि (count) / सकइ (can) / न (not) / कोई (anyone)॥
ramacharitamanas::950.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::950.essence: Illusion can dress itself as abundance and still carry harm.
ramacharitamanas::950.simple_meaning: The false priest prepares a lavish, magical feast with many kinds of food. It is part of his trick to deceive the king and the court.
ramacharitamanas::950.simple_insight: A beautiful setup can hide a dangerous lie. Appearances may be carefully built to mislead trust.
ramacharitamanas::950.detailed_meaning: The disguised demon has already won the king's trust. Now he prepares an impossible feast, using illusion to make the palace believe he is a holy priest. This lavish display is not generosity; it is the bait before the trap.
ramacharitamanas::950.modern_relevance: A polished presentation, a glossy deck, a perfect menu, a smooth voice — all of it can still be a setup. The danger often arrives dressed as refinement.
ramacharitamanas::950.insight: It trains attention to look past spectacle and ask what intention is being served.

ramacharitamanas::951.verse_sanskrit: बिबिध मृगन्ह कर आमिष राँधा। तेहि महुँ बिप्र माँसु खल साँधा॥ भोजन कहुँ सब बिप्र बोलाए। पद पखारि सादर बैठाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::951.verse_hindi: अनेक प्रकार के पशुओं का मांस पकाया और उसमें उस दुष्ट ने ब्राह्मणों का मांस मिला दिया। सब ब्राह्मणों को भोजन के लिए बुलाया और चरण धोकर आदर सहित बैठाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::951.english_translation: He cooked various kinds of animal meat and mixed in the flesh of the Brahmins. He invited all the Brahmins for food, washed their feet, and seated them with respect.
ramacharitamanas::951.translation_literal: बिबिध (various) / मृगन्ह (of animals) / कर (of) / आमिष (meat) / राँधा (cooked) / तेहि महुँ (in that) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / माँसु (flesh) / खल (wicked one) / साँधा (mixed) / भोजन (meal) / कहुँ (for) / सब (all) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / बोलाए (called) / पद (feet) / पखारि (washing) / सादर (respectfully) / बैठाए (seated)
ramacharitamanas::951.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::951.essence: Respect without sincerity becomes another form of harm.
ramacharitamanas::951.simple_meaning: The wicked man prepared meat, mixed in human flesh, and invited the Brahmins to eat after honoring them.
ramacharitamanas::951.simple_insight: Outward respect can hide cruelty. Polite gestures mean nothing when the heart is corrupt.
ramacharitamanas::951.detailed_meaning: In this Bala Kand scene, the false feast is being prepared by a deceitful enemy. After the previous verses describe the magical kitchen, this one reveals the horror inside it: meat is cooked, human flesh is mixed in, and the Brahmins are honored only to be deceived.
ramacharitamanas::951.modern_relevance: Someone smiles warmly in a meeting, offers tea, and signs off with perfect manners — while quietly setting a trap behind the scenes. This verse exposes that split between appearance and intent.
ramacharitamanas::951.insight: It trains you to judge conduct by motive, not ceremony.

ramacharitamanas::952.verse_sanskrit: परुसन जबहिं लाग महिपाला। भै अकासबानी तेहि काला॥ बिप्रबृंद उठि उठि गृह जाहू। है बड़ि हानि अन्न जनि खाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::952.verse_hindi: ज्यों ही राजा परोसने लगा, उसी काल (कालकेतुकृत) आकाशवाणी हुई- हे ब्राह्मणों! उठ-उठकर अपने घर जाओ, यह अन्न मत खाओ। इस (के खाने) में बड़ी हानि है ॥
ramacharitamanas::952.english_translation: As soon as the king began serving the food, a voice from the sky rang out: "Priests, rise and go home. Do not eat this food. It brings great harm."
ramacharitamanas::952.translation_literal: परुसन (serving) / जबहिं (as soon as) / लाग (began) / महिपाला (the king) / भै (became) / अकासबानी (voice from the sky) / तेहि (at that) / काला (time) / बिप्रबृंद (group of priests) / उठि उठि (rise up) / गृह (home) / जाहू (go) / है (is) / बड़ि (great) / हानि (loss) / अन्न (food) / जनि (do not) / खाहू (eat)
ramacharitamanas::952.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::952.essence: A clear warning can interrupt hidden harm before it is swallowed.
ramacharitamanas::952.simple_meaning: Just as the king starts serving the meal, a voice from the sky warns the priests to leave at once and not eat, because the food is dangerous.
ramacharitamanas::952.simple_insight: A warning can arrive in time to save people from harm.
ramacharitamanas::952.detailed_meaning: The king has prepared a grand meal for the priests, but the offering has been poisoned by hidden evil. As the serving begins, a voice from the sky interrupts the scene and warns the priests to leave before they eat.
ramacharitamanas::952.modern_relevance: You’re about to accept food at a gathering, but something feels off: the smell, the timing, the person insisting too hard. Sometimes caution arrives as a sudden inner alarm.
ramacharitamanas::952.insight: It shifts attention from ceremonial appearance to hidden danger, reminding you to pause before accepting what looks generous.

ramacharitamanas::953.verse_sanskrit: भयउ रसोईं भूसुर माँसू। सब द्विज उठे मानि बिस्वासू॥ भूप बिकल मति मोहँ भुलानी। भावी बस न आव मुख बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::953.verse_hindi: रसोई में ब्राह्मणों का मांस बना है। (आकाशवाणी का) विश्वास मानकर सब ब्राह्मण उठ खड़े हुए। राजा व्याकुल हो गया (परन्तु), उसकी बुद्धि मोह में भूली हुई थी। होनहारवश उसके मुँह से (एक) बात (भी) न निकली ॥
ramacharitamanas::953.english_translation: The kitchen had become a place of brahmin flesh. Trusting the warning, all the brahmins stood up. The king was distressed, his mind lost in delusion, and fate left him speechless.
ramacharitamanas::953.translation_literal: भयउ (became) / रसोईं (the kitchen) / भूसुर (brahmins) / माँसू (flesh) / सब (all) / द्विज (brahmins) / उठे (rose) / मानि (accepting) / बिस्वासू (trust) / भूप (the king) / बिकल (distressed) / मति (mind) / मोहँ (in delusion) / भुलानी (was lost) / भावी (fate) / बस (under control) / न (not) / आव (came) / मुख (mouth) / बानी (speech)
ramacharitamanas::953.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::953.essence: Delusion silences the wrongdoer; clear trust lets others walk away.
ramacharitamanas::953.simple_meaning: The brahmins realize the food is defiled and leave at once. The king is stunned, trapped in confusion, and cannot speak.
ramacharitamanas::953.simple_insight: Delusion can freeze even a powerful person, while clear warning lets others act at once.
ramacharitamanas::953.detailed_meaning: A cruel king has disguised a meal with forbidden meat. An unseen warning has just reached the brahmins, and they rise to leave. The king stands shaken, unable to think or speak as the truth collapses around him.
ramacharitamanas::953.modern_relevance: You open a group chat and see the warning you ignored ten minutes ago. Everyone else has already stepped back, but you are still staring at the screen, frozen by the mess you made.
ramacharitamanas::953.insight: It shows how confusion silences wrongdoing and how timely awareness lets others withdraw before harm deepens.

ramacharitamanas::954.verse_sanskrit: बोले बिप्र सकोप तब नहिं कछु कीन्ह बिचार। जाइ निसाचर होहु नृप मूढ़ सहित परिवार ॥
ramacharitamanas::954.verse_hindi: तब ब्राह्मण क्रोध सहित बोल उठे- उन्होंने कुछ भी विचार नहीं किया- अरे मूर्ख राजा! तू जाकर परिवार सहित राक्षस हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::954.english_translation: Then the angry Brahmins spoke: without thinking at all, "Go, O foolish king, and become a demon along with your family."
ramacharitamanas::954.translation_literal: बोले (spoke) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / सकोप (with anger) / तब (then) / नहिं (not) / कछु (anything) / कीन्ह (did) / बिचार (consideration) / जाइ (go) / निसाचर (demon-like being) / होहु (become) / नृप (king) / मूढ़ (foolish) / सहित (along with) / परिवार (family)
ramacharitamanas::954.speaker: Brahmins
ramacharitamanas::954.essence: Anger without reflection turns correction into destruction.
ramacharitamanas::954.simple_meaning: The Brahmins, angered by the king’s mistake, curse him and his family to become demons.
ramacharitamanas::954.simple_insight: Anger spoken without thought turns a wound into a curse.
ramacharitamanas::954.detailed_meaning: A royal meal has gone wrong, and the Brahmins have discovered the shocking truth. Still furious, they curse the king for his reckless act and condemn him along with his family. The verse sharpens the tension before the king’s fate unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::954.modern_relevance: A group chat explodes after one careless mistake, and the first angry reply makes everything worse. The damage is no longer the mistake itself, but the words thrown in heat.
ramacharitamanas::954.insight: It shows how unchecked anger hardens judgment and escalates conflict instead of resolving it.

ramacharitamanas::955.verse_sanskrit: छत्रबंधु तैं बिप्र बोलाई। घालै लिए सहित समुदाई॥ ईश्वर राखा धरम हमारा। जैहसि तैं समेत परिवारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::955.verse_hindi: रे नीच क्षत्रिय! तूने तो परिवार सहित ब्राह्मणों को बुलाकर उन्हें नष्ट करना चाहा था, ईश्वर ने हमारे धर्म की रक्षा की। अब तू परिवार सहित नष्ट होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::955.english_translation: You low-born warrior, you called the brahmins here with your family and tried to destroy them. The divine protected our way of life. Now you will perish with your family.
ramacharitamanas::955.translation_literal: छत्रबंधु (low-born warrior) / तैं (you) / बिप्र (brahmins) / बोलाई (having called) / घालै (to destroy) / लिए (took) / सहित (along with) / समुदाई (the whole group) ॥ / ईश्वर (the divine) / राखा (protected) / धरम (our way of life) / हमारा (our) ॥ / जैहसि (you will go) / तैं (you) / समेत (along with) / परिवारा (family) ॥
ramacharitamanas::955.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::955.essence: Harm aimed at others returns to the one who planned it.
ramacharitamanas::955.simple_meaning: The brahmins accuse the king of trying to destroy them. They say the divine protected them, and now the king and his family will be destroyed.
ramacharitamanas::955.simple_insight: Cruel intent does not disappear just because it failed once.
ramacharitamanas::955.detailed_meaning: The brahmins are still speaking after the king’s failed attempt to harm them. They blame him for inviting them only to destroy them, declare that their way of life was protected, and pronounce a curse on him and his household.
ramacharitamanas::955.modern_relevance: You set a trap in a group chat, expecting the other side to be cornered. Instead, the message thread exposes your intent, and the damage lands back on your own name.
ramacharitamanas::955.insight: It shows how violent intention rebounds, and how protection of the innocent becomes the basis for judgment.

ramacharitamanas::956.verse_sanskrit: संबत मध्य नास तव होऊ। जलदाता न रहिहि कुल कोऊ॥ नृप सुनि श्राप बिकल अति त्रासा। भै बहोरि बर गिरा अकासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::956.verse_hindi: एक वर्ष के भीतर तेरा नाश हो जाए, तेरे कुल में कोई पानी देने वाला तक न रहेगा। शाप सुनकर राजा भय के मारे अत्यन्त व्याकुल हो गया। फिर सुंदर आकाशवाणी हुई- ॥
ramacharitamanas::956.english_translation: May your line be destroyed within a year, and no one in your family remain to offer water. Hearing the curse, the king became extremely fearful and distressed. Then a beautiful voice came from the sky.
ramacharitamanas::956.translation_literal: संबत (year) / मध्य (within) / नास (destruction) / तव (your) / होऊ (may happen) । जलदाता (water-giver) / न रहिहि (will not remain) / कुल (family/lineage) / कोऊ (anyone) ॥ नृप (king) / सुनि (hearing) / श्राप (curse) / बिकल (distressed) / अति (very) / त्रासा (fear) । भै (became) / बहोरि (again) / बर (beautiful) / गिरा (voice) / अकासा (from the sky) ॥
ramacharitamanas::956.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::956.essence: Fear arrives before the sky has finished speaking.
ramacharitamanas::956.simple_meaning: The brahmin curses the king’s line to end within a year. The king is terrified, and then a voice from the sky speaks.
ramacharitamanas::956.simple_insight: A single harsh word can shatter a ruler’s confidence in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::956.detailed_meaning: The angry brahmins have just cursed the king after being insulted. They declare that his family will soon perish. The king is struck with terror, and the scene pauses as a mysterious voice from the sky interrupts the moment.
ramacharitamanas::956.modern_relevance: A message lands in your phone inbox and your stomach drops before you even finish reading it. One sentence can turn a whole day into fear.
ramacharitamanas::956.insight: It shifts attention from the curse itself to the king’s immediate collapse under fear.
