ramacharitamanas::957.verse_sanskrit: बिप्रहु श्राप बिचारि न दीन्हा। नहिं अपराध भूप कछु कीन्हा॥ चकित बिप्र सब सुनि नभबानी। भूप गयउ जहँ भोजन खानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::957.verse_hindi: हे ब्राह्मणों! तुमने विचार कर शाप नहीं दिया। राजा ने कुछ भी अपराध नहीं किया। आकाशवाणी सुनकर सब ब्राह्मण चकित हो गए। तब राजा वहाँ गया, जहाँ भोजन बना था ॥
ramacharitamanas::957.english_translation: O Brahmins, you did not think before cursing him. The king had done no wrong. Hearing the voice from the sky, all the Brahmins were stunned. Then the king went to the place where the food had been prepared.
ramacharitamanas::957.translation_literal: बिप्रहु (O Brahmins) / श्राप (curse) / बिचारि (after considering) / न दीन्हा (did not give) / नहिं (not) / अपराध (fault) / भूप (king) / कछु (any) / कीन्हा (did) / चकित (stunned) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / सब (all) / सुनि (hearing) / नभबानी (voice from the sky) / भूप (king) / गयउ (went) / जहँ (where) / भोजन खानी (food place)
ramacharitamanas::957.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::957.essence: Judgment softens when innocence becomes clear.
ramacharitamanas::957.simple_meaning: The Brahmins realize the curse was not justified, because the king had done nothing wrong. Shocked by the heavenly voice, they watch him go to the place where the meal was being prepared.
ramacharitamanas::957.simple_insight: A harsh reaction can collapse when the facts are finally seen clearly.
ramacharitamanas::957.detailed_meaning: The court scene has turned tense after the Brahmins' curse. An unseen voice corrects the moment: the king is innocent. The Brahmins are shaken, and the king quietly walks toward the cooking place, showing the scene is still unfolding, not resolved.
ramacharitamanas::957.modern_relevance: You fire off a furious message, then realize you misunderstood the whole situation. By the time the facts land, the damage is already moving.
ramacharitamanas::957.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional certainty to factual checking before judgment.

ramacharitamanas::958.verse_sanskrit: तहँ न असन नहिं बिप्र सुआरा। फिरेउ राउ मन सोच अपारा॥ सब प्रसंग महिसुरन्ह सुनाई। त्रसित परेउ अवनीं अकुलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::958.verse_hindi: (देखा तो) वहाँ न भोजन था, न रसोइया ब्राह्मण ही था। तब राजा मन में अपार चिन्ता करता हुआ लौटा। उसने ब्राह्मणों को सब वृत्तान्त सुनाया और (बड़ा ही) भयभीत और व्याकुल होकर वह पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::958.english_translation: There was no food there, and no Brahmin cook. The king returned with great worry in his mind. He told the Brahmins everything, then fell to the ground in fear and distress.
ramacharitamanas::958.translation_literal: तहँ (there) / न (not) / असन (food) / नहिं (not) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / सुआरा (cook) / फिरेउ (returned) / राउ (king) / मन (mind) / सोच (worry) / अपारा (boundless) / सब (all) / प्रसंग (account) / महिसुरन्ह (to the Brahmins) / सुनाई (told) / त्रसित (frightened) / परेउ (fell) / अवनीं (to the ground) / अकुलाई (distressed)
ramacharitamanas::958.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::958.essence: Fear can break a person before events do.
ramacharitamanas::958.simple_meaning: The king finds no meal and no Brahmin cook, so he returns in deep worry, explains the situation, and collapses in fear.
ramacharitamanas::958.simple_insight: Sometimes fear grows before any real disaster arrives.
ramacharitamanas::958.detailed_meaning: After the Brahmin's curse, the king searches for the promised meal and finds nothing arranged. He returns to the Brahmins, explains the whole matter, and collapses in fear. The scene shows panic spreading before the curse has even taken full effect.
ramacharitamanas::958.modern_relevance: You open the kitchen after a long day and realize nothing is ready, the deadline is still real, and your mind starts spiraling before anything has actually gone wrong.
ramacharitamanas::958.insight: It shows how anxiety magnifies a problem and makes a person collapse before the outcome is known.

ramacharitamanas::959.verse_sanskrit: भूपति भावी मिटइ नहिं जदपि न दूषन तोर। किएँ अन्यथा दोइ नहिं बिप्रश्राप अति घोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::959.verse_hindi: हे राजन! यद्यपि तुम्हारा दोष नहीं है, तो भी होनहार नहीं मिटता। ब्राह्मणों का शाप बहुत ही भयानक होता है, यह किसी तरह भी टाले टल नहीं सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::959.english_translation: O king, what is destined does not change, even though you are not at fault. A brahmin's curse is very terrible; it cannot be turned aside in any other way.
ramacharitamanas::959.translation_literal: भूपति (O king) / भावी (what is destined) / मिटइ (is erased) / नहिं (not) / जदपि (even though) / न (not) / दूषन (fault) / तोर (yours) / किएँ (by doing) / अन्यथा (otherwise) / दोइ (both) / नहिं (not) / बिप्रश्राप (brahmin's curse) / अति घोर (very terrible)
ramacharitamanas::959.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::959.essence: Faultlessness does not always prevent suffering.
ramacharitamanas::959.simple_meaning: Even without fault, the king must face what has already come. The curse is said to be unavoidable.
ramacharitamanas::959.simple_insight: Not every painful outcome comes from your mistake. Some moments must be endured, not argued with.
ramacharitamanas::959.detailed_meaning: The king returns from the empty kitchen in shock. The brahmins have already seen the larger pattern and now speak with finality: Dasharath is not guilty, yet the curse cannot be undone. This verse seals the tragedy.
ramacharitamanas::959.modern_relevance: You did everything right, and the project still collapsed. The apology is real, but so is the fact that some losses cannot be negotiated away.
ramacharitamanas::959.insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame and resistance toward sober acceptance of what cannot be reversed.

ramacharitamanas::960.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि सब महिदेव सिधाए। समाचार पुरलोगन्ह पाए॥ सोचहिं दूषन दैवहि देहीं। बिरचत हंस काग किए जेहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::960.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर सब ब्राह्मण चले गए। नगरवासियों ने (जब) यह समाचार पाया, तो वे चिन्ता करने और विधाता को दोष देने लगे, जिसने हंस बनाते-बनाते कौआ कर दिया (ऐसे पुण्यात्मा राजा को देवता बनाना चाहिए था, सो राक्षस बना दिया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::960.english_translation: After saying this, all the Brahmins departed. When the townspeople heard the news, they began to worry and blame fate, saying that the one who forms swans has made crows.
ramacharitamanas::960.translation_literal: अस कहि (saying this) / सब (all) / महिदेव (great divine-men, Brahmins) / सिधाए (departed) / समाचार (news) / पुरलोगन्ह (by the townspeople) / पाए (received) / सोचहिं (they worry) / दूषन (blame) / दैवहि (fate) / देहीं (they give) / बिरचत (while creating) / हंस (swans) / काग (crows) / किए (made) / जेहीं (who)
ramacharitamanas::960.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::960.essence: Grief turns into blame when people cannot undo what happened.
ramacharitamanas::960.simple_meaning: The Brahmins leave, and the town falls into grief and complaint. People blame fate for turning a noble ruler into a ruined one.
ramacharitamanas::960.simple_insight: Shock can turn into blame before anyone knows what to do next.
ramacharitamanas::960.detailed_meaning: The Brahmins have delivered their harsh judgment and gone. Word spreads through the city, and everyone reels at the loss of a just king. Instead of action, the townspeople sink into worry and blame the force that seems to have reversed what should have been good.
ramacharitamanas::960.modern_relevance: A family group chat blows up after bad news, and everyone starts asking who ruined everything. The first response is often blame, not clarity.
ramacharitamanas::960.insight: It shows how grief quickly becomes projection when people feel powerless.

ramacharitamanas::961.verse_sanskrit: उपरोहितहि भवन पहुँचाई। असुर तापसहि खबरि जनाई॥ तेहिं खल जहँ तहँ पत्र पठाए। सजि सजि सेन भूप सब धाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::961.verse_hindi: पुरोहित को उसके घर पहुँचाकर असुर (कालकेतु) ने (कपटी) तपस्वी को खबर दी। उस दुष्ट ने जहाँ-तहाँ पत्र भेजे, जिससे सब (बैरी) राजा सेना सजा-सजाकर (चढ़) दौड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::961.english_translation: After escorting the priest to his home, the demon informed the deceitful ascetic. That wicked one sent letters everywhere, and all the hostile kings hurried forth, arraying their armies.
ramacharitamanas::961.translation_literal: उपरोहितहि (the priest) / भवन (to the house) / पहुँचाई (having escorted) / असुर (the demon) / तापसहि (to the ascetic) / खबरि (news) / जनाई (made known) / तेहिं (that one) / खल (wicked) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / पत्र (letters) / पठाए (sent) / सजि सजि (having arrayed) / सेन (armies) / भूप (kings) / सब (all) / धाए (rushed)
ramacharitamanas::961.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::961.essence: False news can summon armies before anyone sees the truth.
ramacharitamanas::961.simple_meaning: The demon passes the message on, the deceitful ascetic spreads the word, and enemy kings rush out with their armies.
ramacharitamanas::961.simple_insight: Some conflicts begin with quiet messages before they become open war.
ramacharitamanas::961.detailed_meaning: The story has moved from a curse to its consequences. After the priest is sent home, the demon alerts the false ascetic, who sends letters across the land. Enemy kings respond at once, gathering their forces and rushing into battle.
ramacharitamanas::961.modern_relevance: A group chat turns one rumor into three meetings, then a full-blown crisis. One careless message can mobilize people faster than truth can catch up.
ramacharitamanas::961.insight: It shows how deception spreads conflict quickly by recruiting others before clarity can arrive.

ramacharitamanas::962.verse_sanskrit: घेरेन्हि नगर निसान बजाई। बिबिध भाँति नित होइ लराई॥ जूझे सकल सुभट करि करनी। बंधु समेत परेउ नृप धरनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::962.verse_hindi: और उन्होंने डंका बजाकर नगर को घेर लिया। नित्य प्रति अनेक प्रकार से लड़ाई होने लगी। (प्रताप भानु के) सब योद्धा (शूरवीरों की) करनी करके रण में जूझ मरे। राजा भी भाई सहित खेत रहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::962.english_translation: They surrounded the city and sounded the war drums. Battles raged there in many forms every day. All the warriors fought bravely and fell on the battlefield, and the king fell there with his brothers.
ramacharitamanas::962.translation_literal: घेरेन्हि (they surrounded) / नगर (the city) / निसान (war drum) / बजाई (sounding) / बिबिध भाँति (in many ways) / नित (every day) / होइ (being) / लराई (battle) / जूझे (fought) / सकल (all) / सुभट (warriors) / करि करनी (doing brave deeds) / बंधु (brothers) / समेत (together with) / परेउ (fell) / नृप (king) / धरनी (on the ground)
ramacharitamanas::962.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::962.essence: War closes in, and even kings fall.
ramacharitamanas::962.simple_meaning: The city is surrounded, fighting breaks out daily, and the king and his brothers die in battle.
ramacharitamanas::962.simple_insight: Violence consumes everyone equally; courage does not spare anyone from loss.
ramacharitamanas::962.detailed_meaning: After the earlier warning and mobilization, the enemy closes in on the city of Pratap Bhanu. War drums sound, fighting erupts again and again, and the king falls on the battlefield with his brothers. The verse is a battlefield report, not a teaching statement.
ramacharitamanas::962.modern_relevance: A neighborhood goes tense after days of threats, sirens keep sounding, and everyone is bracing for the next blow. In that atmosphere, even the strongest people can be swept into collapse.
ramacharitamanas::962.insight: It shifts attention from heroic display to the cost of conflict.

ramacharitamanas::963.verse_sanskrit: सत्यकेतु कुल कोउ नहिं बाँचा। बिप्रश्राप किमि होइ असाँचा॥ रिपु जिति सब नृप नगर बसाई। निज पुर गवने जय जसु पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::963.verse_hindi: सत्यकेतु के कुल में कोई नहीं बचा। ब्राह्मणों का शाप झूठा कैसे हो सकता था। शत्रु को जीतकर नगर को (फिर से) बसाकर सब राजा विजय और यश पाकर अपने-अपने नगर को चले गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::963.english_translation: No one in Satyaketu's line survived. How could the Brahmins' curse prove false? Defeating the enemy, the kings rebuilt the city, gained victory and fame, and returned to their own kingdoms.
ramacharitamanas::963.translation_literal: सत्यकेतु (Satyaketu) / कुल (lineage) / कोउ (anyone) / नहिं (not) / बाँचा (survived) / बिप्रश्राप (Brahmin curse) / किमि (how) / होइ (could be) / असाँचा (false) / रिपु (enemy) / जिति (having defeated) / सब (all) / नृप (kings) / नगर (city) / बसाई (rebuilt/settled) / निज (own) / पुर (city/kingdom) / गवने (went) / जय (victory) / जसु (fame) / पाई (having obtained)
ramacharitamanas::963.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::963.essence: Victory in the city cannot undo a curse already fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::963.simple_meaning: Satyaketu's family was wiped out because the curse had to come true. After defeating the enemy, the kings restored the city and went back home with victory.
ramacharitamanas::963.simple_insight: Some losses cannot be escaped once a wrong has ripened.
ramacharitamanas::963.detailed_meaning: The battle against the enemy has ended, and the kings have restored the city. But the larger story is still the collapse of Satyaketu's line under a Brahmin's curse. This verse closes that episode by showing victory in the city and ruin in the lineage.
ramacharitamanas::963.modern_relevance: A group finishes cleaning up the office after a scandal, and everyone wants to move on. But the damage that was set in motion earlier has already done its work.
ramacharitamanas::963.insight: It shifts attention from surface victory to the deeper consequences already unfolding beneath it.

ramacharitamanas::964.verse_sanskrit: भरद्वाज सुनु जाहि जब होई बिधाता बाम। धूरि मेरुसम जनक जम ताहि ब्यालसम दाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::964.verse_hindi: (याज्ञवल्क्यजी कहते हैं-) हे भरद्वाज! सुनो, विधाता जब जिसके विपरीत होते हैं, तब उसके लिए धूल सुमेरु पर्वत के समान (भारी और कुचल डालने वाली), पिता यम के समान (कालरूप) और रस्सी साँप के समान (काट खाने वाली) हो जाती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::964.english_translation: Bharadwaj, listen: when the creator turns against someone, dust becomes like Mount Meru, a father becomes like Yama, and a rope becomes like a snake.
ramacharitamanas::964.translation_literal: भरद्वाज (Bharadwaj) / सुनु (listen) / जाहि (for whom) / जब (when) / होई (becomes) / बिधाता (the creator) / बाम (opposed) / धूरि (dust) / मेरुसम (like Mount Meru) / जनक (father) / जम (Yama) / ताहि (for that one) / ब्यालसम (like a snake) / दाम (rope)
ramacharitamanas::964.speaker: Yajnavalkya
ramacharitamanas::964.essence: When life turns hostile, perception itself becomes heavy and dangerous.
ramacharitamanas::964.simple_meaning: When life turns against someone, even ordinary things feel unbearable: dust feels huge, a father feels like death, and a rope feels like a snake.
ramacharitamanas::964.simple_insight: It helps you notice how suffering can distort perception and make harmless things feel threatening.
ramacharitamanas::964.detailed_meaning: Yajnavalkya is explaining to Bharadwaj how the fallen king's life has changed. After victory and glory, the king's world will turn so harsh that even small things will feel crushing and dangerous. This verse marks the beginning of that tragic reversal.
ramacharitamanas::964.modern_relevance: You get one bad email, and suddenly every message feels hostile. The room, the tone, the silence — all of it seems heavier than it is. This verse names that warped seeing.
ramacharitamanas::964.insight: It trains the mind to recognize fear's exaggeration instead of accepting every impression as reality.

ramacharitamanas::965.verse_sanskrit: काल पाइ मुनि सुनु सोइ राजा। भयउ निसाचर सहित समाजा॥ दस सिर ताहि बीस भुजदंडा। रावन नाम बीर बरिबंडा ॥
ramacharitamanas::965.verse_hindi: हे मुनि! सुनो, समय पाकर वही राजा परिवार सहित रावण नामक राक्षस हुआ। उसके दस सिर और बीस भुजाएँ थीं और वह बड़ा ही प्रचण्ड शूरवीर था ॥
ramacharitamanas::965.english_translation: O sage, listen: in time, that very king became a demon along with his household. He was called Ravana, with ten heads, twenty arms, and immense heroic might.
ramacharitamanas::965.translation_literal: काल (in time) / पाइ (having obtained) / मुनि (sage) / सुनु (listen) / सोइ (that very) / राजा (king) / भयउ (became) / निसाचर (demon) / सहित (along with) / समाजा (household) / दस (ten) / सिर (heads) / ताहि (to him) / बीस (twenty) / भुजदंडा (arms) / रावन (Ravana) / नाम (named) / बीर (hero) / बरिबंडा (very mighty)
ramacharitamanas::965.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::965.essence: Great power, cut off from restraint, becomes a force of ruin.
ramacharitamanas::965.simple_meaning: That king and his household later became Ravana and his demon clan. He is described as a mighty warrior with ten heads and twenty arms.
ramacharitamanas::965.simple_insight: Power without restraint can harden into monstrous pride.
ramacharitamanas::965.detailed_meaning: The narration turns from a cursed royal line to Ravana's origin. The sage is told that the same king, in another turn of time, became Ravana with his whole household. The verse introduces the enemy before the larger story of his rise unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::965.modern_relevance: A person who keeps feeding pride, control, and resentment can slowly become unrecognizable to everyone around them.
ramacharitamanas::965.insight: It frames Ravana as a warning: greatness twisted by ego becomes destruction.

ramacharitamanas::966.verse_sanskrit: भूप अनुज अरिमर्दन नामा। भयउ सो कुंभकरन बलधामा॥ सचिव जो रहा धरमरुचि जासू। भयउ बिमात्र बंधु लघु तासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::966.verse_hindi: अरिमर्दन नामक जो राजा का छोटा भाई था, वह बल का धाम कुम्भकर्ण हुआ। उसका जो मंत्री था, जिसका नाम धर्मरुचि था, वह रावण का सौतेला छोटा भाई हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::966.english_translation: The king's younger brother, Arimardan, became Kumbhakarna, the strong one. The minister named Dharamaruchi became Ravana's younger half-brother.
ramacharitamanas::966.translation_literal: भूप (king) / अनुज (younger brother) / अरिमर्दन (Arimardan, crusher of enemies) / नामा (named) / भयउ (became) / सो (that) / कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / बलधामा (abode of strength) ॥ / सचिव (minister) / जो (who) / रहा (remained) / धरमरुचि (Dharamaruchi, one inclined to dharma) / जासू (whose) / भयउ (became) / बिमात्र (stepmother-born) / बंधु (brother) / लघु (younger) / तासू (his) ॥
ramacharitamanas::966.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::966.essence: Old relations return in new forms around Ravana.
ramacharitamanas::966.simple_meaning: Ravana's former allies and relatives are being identified by their later births in his family. The verse simply lists who became whom.
ramacharitamanas::966.simple_insight: Sometimes a whole life is shown through a single reappearance in a new role.
ramacharitamanas::966.detailed_meaning: Yajnavalkya continues explaining how the beings around Ravana were reborn into his own family. One became Kumbhakarna, another became a younger half-brother. The verse is a linking detail in a larger account of Ravana's household.
ramacharitamanas::966.modern_relevance: A family photo can hide a whole history of loyalty, resentment, and change. Later, the same people may return in roles no one expected.
ramacharitamanas::966.insight: It keeps the reader oriented in the genealogy, not the philosophy.

ramacharitamanas::967.verse_sanskrit: नाम बिभीषन जेहि जग जाना। बिष्नुभगत बिग्यान निधाना॥ रहे जे सुत सेवक नृप केरे। भए निसाचर घोर घनेरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::967.verse_hindi: उसका विभीषण नाम था, जिसे सारा जगत जानता है। वह विष्णुभक्त और ज्ञान-विज्ञान का भंडार था और जो राजा के पुत्र और सेवक थे, वे सभी बड़े भयानक राक्षस हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::967.english_translation: His name was Vibhishana, known throughout the world. He was a devotee of Vishnu and a treasury of wisdom and discernment, while the king's own sons and servants became fierce demons.
ramacharitamanas::967.translation_literal: नाम (name) / बिभीषन (Vibhishana) / जेहि (whom) / जग (world) / जाना (knew) / बिष्नुभगत (devotee of Vishnu) / बिग्यान (knowledge) / निधाना (treasury) / रहे (were) / जे (who) / सुत (sons) / सेवक (servants) / नृप (king) / केरे (of) / भए (became) / निसाचर (demons) / घोर (fierce) / घनेरे (many)
ramacharitamanas::967.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::967.essence: A corrupted house can still produce one clear-hearted devotee.
ramacharitamanas::967.simple_meaning: Vibhishana is remembered as a wise devotee of Vishnu, while the king's own sons and servants turned into terrible demons.
ramacharitamanas::967.simple_insight: Character is not inherited by status. Devotion and discernment can stand apart from family and power.
ramacharitamanas::967.detailed_meaning: The story pauses to contrast Ravana's household with one bright exception: Vibhishana. Though born in the same demonic line, he becomes known everywhere as a devotee of Vishnu and a storehouse of wisdom, while the rest of the royal family sinks deeper into cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::967.modern_relevance: You can grow up in a home full of noise, ego, or harm and still choose a cleaner way. Bloodline does not decide your character.
ramacharitamanas::967.insight: It shifts attention from family identity to moral choice and inner discernment.

ramacharitamanas::968.verse_sanskrit: कामरूप खल जिनस अनेका। कुटिल भयंकर बिगत बिबेका॥ कृपा रहित हिंसक सब पापी। बरनि न जाहिं बिस्व परितापी ॥
ramacharitamanas::968.verse_hindi: वे सब अनेकों जाति के, मनमाना रूप धारण करने वाले, दुष्ट, कुटिल, भयंकर, विवेकरहित, निर्दयी, हिंसक, पापी और संसार भर को दुःख देने वाले हुए, उनका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::968.english_translation: They were many kinds of shape-shifters: crooked, terrifying, and without discernment. Devoid of grace, violent, and full of wrongdoing, they brought suffering to the whole world; no one can fully describe them.
ramacharitamanas::968.translation_literal: कामरूप (shape-shifting) / खल (wicked) / जिनस (kinds) / अनेका (many) / कुटिल (crooked) / भयंकर (terrifying) / बिगत (without) / बिबेका (discernment) / कृपा (grace) / रहित (devoid of) / हिंसक (violent) / सब (all) / पापी (wrongdoers) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाहिं (can be) / बिस्व (world) / परितापी (causing suffering)
ramacharitamanas::968.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::968.essence: Cruelty without discernment spreads suffering wherever it goes.
ramacharitamanas::968.simple_meaning: Ravana's followers are described as many kinds of cruel, deceptive beings who lack discernment and bring suffering everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::968.simple_insight: Some forces harm not by accident, but by nature. Seeing that clearly helps you stop excusing them.
ramacharitamanas::968.detailed_meaning: The story has moved into Lanka's dark world. Tulsidas is describing Ravana's camp: beings shaped by cruelty, deceit, and violence. This line deepens the picture before the verse that explains how even their noble birth could not save them from a curse.
ramacharitamanas::968.modern_relevance: A workplace rumor spreads fast, and suddenly everyone is anxious, defensive, and mistrustful. One manipulative person can poison an entire room before lunch.
ramacharitamanas::968.insight: It trains the reader to recognise destructive character as a pattern, not a surprise.

ramacharitamanas::969.verse_sanskrit: उपजे जदपि पुलस्त्यकुल पावन अमल अनूप। तदपि महीसुर श्राप बस भए सकल अघरूप ॥
ramacharitamanas::969.verse_hindi: यद्यपि वे पुलस्त्य ऋषि के पवित्र, निर्मल और अनुपम कुल में उत्पन्न हुए, तथापि ब्राह्मणों के शाप के कारण वे सब पाप रूप हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::969.english_translation: Though they were born in the pure, flawless, incomparable line of Pulastya, the curse of the sages made them all wicked.
ramacharitamanas::969.translation_literal: उपजे (were born) / जदपि (although) / पुलस्त्यकुल (Pulastya's lineage) / पावन (pure) / अमल (flawless) / अनूप (incomparable) / तदपि (still) / महीसुर (sages / brahmins) / श्राप (curse) / बस (under the power of) / भए (became) / सकल (all) / अघरूप (of sinful form)
ramacharitamanas::969.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::969.essence: A noble birth can still end in ruin under the weight of a curse.
ramacharitamanas::969.simple_meaning: They came from a noble lineage, but a curse turned them into beings of wrongdoing.
ramacharitamanas::969.simple_insight: A good beginning does not guarantee a good life when pride and wrongdoing take over.
ramacharitamanas::969.detailed_meaning: The narration shifts to Ravana’s family line. Tulsidas reminds us that these beings were not born base; they came from the pure line of Pulastya. But a sage’s curse changed their course, and the story now moves toward the dark actions that follow.
ramacharitamanas::969.modern_relevance: Someone may grow up in a respected family, with every advantage and good example around them, yet still choose habits that ruin everything. Background helps, but it does not save a person from their own turning.
ramacharitamanas::969.insight: It shifts attention from lineage to conduct: what a person becomes matters more than where they began.

ramacharitamanas::970.verse_sanskrit: कीन्ह बिबिध तप तीनिहुँ भाई। परम उग्र नहिं बरनि सो जाई॥ गयउ निकट तप देखि बिधाता। मागहु बर प्रसन्न मैं ताता ॥
ramacharitamanas::970.verse_hindi: तीनों भाइयों ने अनेकों प्रकार की बड़ी ही कठिन तपस्या की, जिसका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता। (उनका उग्र) तप देखकर ब्रह्माजी उनके पास गए और बोले- हे तात! मैं प्रसन्न हूँ, वर माँगो ॥
ramacharitamanas::970.english_translation: The three brothers performed many kinds of severe austerity, beyond description. Seeing that fierce tapas, Brahma came near and said, 'Ask for a boon, dear sons; I am pleased.'
ramacharitamanas::970.translation_literal: कीन्ह (performed) / बिबिध (various) / तप (austerities) / तीनिहुँ भाई (the three brothers) / परम उग्र (extremely severe) / नहिं बरनि सो जाई (cannot be described) / गयउ (went) / निकट (near) / तप देखि (seeing the austerity) / बिधाता (Brahma) / मागहु बर (ask for a boon) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / मैं (I) / ताता (dear sons)
ramacharitamanas::970.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::970.essence: Severe discipline itself becomes a force that summons response.
ramacharitamanas::970.simple_meaning: The three brothers practiced intense austerity for so long and so seriously that Brahma himself came to offer them a boon.
ramacharitamanas::970.simple_insight: Deep discipline can draw even the highest recognition.
ramacharitamanas::970.detailed_meaning: The three brothers are in the middle of a punishing penance so intense that it cannot be fully described. Their austerity moves Brahma to come to them in person and invite them to ask for a boon.
ramacharitamanas::970.modern_relevance: You keep showing up before dawn, long after motivation fades. No applause arrives, but the work itself changes who you are — and eventually it is noticed.
ramacharitamanas::970.insight: It shifts attention from results to sustained practice that builds power over time.

ramacharitamanas::971.verse_sanskrit: करि बिनती पद गहि दससीसा। बोलेउ बचन सुनहु जगदीसा॥ हम काहू के मरहिं न मारें। बानर मनुज जाति दुइ बारें ॥
ramacharitamanas::971.verse_hindi: रावण ने विनय करके और चरण पकड़कर कहा- हे जगदीश्वर! सुनिए, वानर और मनुष्य- इन दो जातियों को छोड़कर हम और किसी के मारे न मरें। (यह वर दीजिए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::971.english_translation: Ravana bowed, held the Lord's feet, and said, 'Listen, Lord of the world. Let us be killed by no one except monkeys and humans.'
ramacharitamanas::971.translation_literal: करि (having done) / बिनती (request) / पद (feet) / गहि (grasping) / दससीसा (ten-headed one, Ravana) / बोलेउ (spoke) / बचन (words) / सुनहु (listen) / जगदीसा (Lord of the world) / हम (we) / काहू (by anyone) / के (of) / मरहिं (be killed) / न (not) / मारें (may kill) / बानर (monkeys) / मनुज (humans) / जाति (race, kind) / दुइ (two) / बारें (except)
ramacharitamanas::971.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::971.essence: The mind that feels invincible chooses the crack that ends it.
ramacharitamanas::971.simple_meaning: Ravana humbly asks for a boon that makes him vulnerable only to monkeys and humans.
ramacharitamanas::971.simple_insight: Pride can disguise itself as prayer, but the request still reveals the mind's blind spot.
ramacharitamanas::971.detailed_meaning: After severe penance, Ravana stands before Brahma and bows with apparent humility. He asks for a boon that no being except humans and monkeys can kill him, unknowingly setting the condition for his own defeat.
ramacharitamanas::971.modern_relevance: A person feels untouchable after years of success and quietly builds in one exception he thinks will never matter. That hidden exception becomes the opening that undoes everything.
ramacharitamanas::971.insight: It exposes how ego seeks protection in the very form that will later betray it.

ramacharitamanas::972.verse_sanskrit: एवमस्तु तुम्ह बड़ तप कीन्हा। मैं ब्रह्माँ मिलि तेहि बर दीन्हा॥ पुनि प्रभु कुंभकरन पहिं गयऊ। तेहि बिलोकि मन बिसमय भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::972.verse_hindi: (शिवजी कहते हैं कि-) मैंने और ब्रह्मा ने मिलकर उसे वर दिया कि ऐसा ही हो, तुमने बड़ा तप किया है। फिर ब्रह्माजी कुंभकर्ण के पास गए। उसे देखकर उनके मन में बड़ा आश्चर्य हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::972.english_translation: So be it. You have performed great austerity. Brahma and I granted that boon together. Then the Lord went to Kumbhakarna, and seeing him, his mind was filled with wonder.
ramacharitamanas::972.translation_literal: एवमस्तु (so be it) / तुम्ह (you) / बड़ (great) / तप (austerity) / कीन्हा (did) / मैं (I) / ब्रह्माँ (Brahma) / मिलि (together) / तेहि (that) / बर (boon) / दीन्हा (gave) / पुनि (then) / प्रभु (lord) / कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / पहिं (to) / गयऊ (went) / तेहि (him) / बिलोकि (seeing) / मन (mind) / बिसमय (wonder) / भयऊ (became)
ramacharitamanas::972.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::972.essence: A boon can carry its own warning.
ramacharitamanas::972.simple_meaning: Shiva confirms the boon was granted after Kumbhakarna's severe penance, then notes Brahma's astonishment at seeing him.
ramacharitamanas::972.simple_insight: Great power can come with a hidden cost that even the giver cannot fully foresee.
ramacharitamanas::972.detailed_meaning: After the demons' harsh austerities, the boon is granted. Shiva explains that Brahma and he approved it, then Brahma goes to Kumbhakarna and is startled by what he sees. The scene sets up the danger of a boon that has gone wrong.
ramacharitamanas::972.modern_relevance: A decision looks wise in the moment, then months later you see the side effect you never imagined. What seemed like a reward can become a burden.
ramacharitamanas::972.insight: It shifts attention from the request itself to the consequences hidden inside a granted wish.

ramacharitamanas::973.verse_sanskrit: जौं एहिं खल नित करब अहारू। होइहि सब उजारि संसारू॥ सारद प्रेरि तासु मति फेरी। मागेसि नीद मास षट केरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::973.verse_hindi: जो यह दुष्ट नित्य आहार करेगा, तो सारा संसार ही उजाड़ हो जाएगा। (ऐसा विचारकर) ब्रह्माजी ने सरस्वती को प्रेरणा करके उसकी बुद्धि फेर दी। (जिससे) उसने छह महीने की नींद माँगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::973.english_translation: If this wicked one kept eating every day, the whole world would be destroyed. So Brahma, moved by Saraswati, turned his mind. Then he asked for six months of sleep.
ramacharitamanas::973.translation_literal: जौं (if) / एहिं (this) / खल (wicked one) / नित (always, daily) / करब (will do) / अहारू (food, eating) / होइहि (will become) / सब (all) / उजारि (destroyed) / संसारू (world) / सारद (Saraswati) / प्रेरि (having prompted) / तासु (his) / मति (mind, intelligence) / फेरी (turned, changed) / मागेसि (asked for) / नीद (sleep) / मास (months) / षट (six) / केरी (of)
ramacharitamanas::973.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::973.essence: A harmful appetite can be neutralized by changing the mind that feeds it.
ramacharitamanas::973.simple_meaning: Brahma realizes this being would destroy everything if left to eat freely, so he changes the being's mind and makes him ask for six months of sleep.
ramacharitamanas::973.simple_insight: Even a destructive force can be redirected before it harms everyone.
ramacharitamanas::973.detailed_meaning: Brahma is dealing with a terrifying boon-giver's mistake in the background of the Lanka story. He sees that this being's hunger could ruin the world, so he quietly alters the mind through Saraswati and diverts the request into sleep instead.
ramacharitamanas::973.modern_relevance: A friend is spiraling into a choice that will wreck everyone around them. Before the damage spreads, someone wiser steps in and redirects the impulse toward rest instead of ruin.
ramacharitamanas::973.insight: It shows that wisdom sometimes works by redirecting a dangerous desire, not by fighting it head-on.

ramacharitamanas::974.verse_sanskrit: गए बिभीषन पास पुनि कहेउ पुत्र बर मागु। तेहिं मागेउ भगवंत पद कमल अमल अनुरागु ॥
ramacharitamanas::974.verse_hindi: फिर ब्रह्माजी विभीषण के पास गए और बोले- हे पुत्र! वर माँगो। उसने भगवान के चरणकमलों में निर्मल (निष्काम और अनन्य) प्रेम माँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::974.english_translation: Then Brahma went to Vibhishana and said, 'Son, ask for a boon.' He asked for pure, unbroken love for the lotus feet of the divine.
ramacharitamanas::974.translation_literal: गए (went) / बिभीषन पास (to Vibhishana) / पुनि (again) / कहेउ (said) / पुत्र (son) / बर (boon) / मागु (ask) / तेहिं (he) / मागेउ (asked for) / भगवंत (the divine lord) / पद कमल (lotus feet) / अमल (pure) / अनुरागु (love/attachment)
ramacharitamanas::974.speaker: Brahma
ramacharitamanas::974.essence: The highest boon is love for the divine feet.
ramacharitamanas::974.simple_meaning: Brahma offers Vibhishana a boon, and Vibhishana asks only for pure love for the divine feet.
ramacharitamanas::974.simple_insight: What you ask for reveals what you value most.
ramacharitamanas::974.detailed_meaning: Brahma comes to Vibhishana after the strange birth of the three brothers and invites him to choose a boon. Vibhishana does not ask for status, safety, or power. He asks only for pure love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::974.modern_relevance: Someone finally gives you a blank cheque: a promotion, a favor, a chance to ask for anything. The real test is not what you can get, but what your heart reaches for first.
ramacharitamanas::974.insight: It shifts desire from outer gain to inward devotion.

ramacharitamanas::975.verse_sanskrit: तिन्हहि देइ बर ब्रह्म सिधाए। हरषित ते अपने गृह आए॥ मय तनुजा मंदोदरि नामा। परम सुंदरी नारि ललामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::975.verse_hindi: उनको वर देकर ब्रह्माजी चले गए और वे (तीनों भाई) हर्षित हेकर अपने घर लौट आए। मय दानव की मंदोदरी नाम की कन्या परम सुंदरी और स्त्रियों में शिरोमणि थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::975.english_translation: Brahma gave them the boon and departed. Delighted, they returned home. Maya's daughter Mandodari by name was a supremely beautiful woman, foremost among women.
ramacharitamanas::975.translation_literal: तिन्हहि (to them) / देइ (giving) / बर (boon) / ब्रह्म (Brahma) / सिधाए (departed) / हरषित (delighted) / ते (they) / अपने (their own) / गृह (home) / आए (came) / मय (Maya) / तनुजा (daughter) / मंदोदरि (Mandodari) / नामा (named) / परम (supreme) / सुंदरी (beautiful) / नारि (woman) / ललामा (foremost)
ramacharitamanas::975.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::975.essence: A boon is granted, and the story quietly prepares its next turning point.
ramacharitamanas::975.simple_meaning: Brahma grants the boon and leaves. The brothers go home happily. Mandodari, Maya's daughter, is introduced as a beautiful and noble woman.
ramacharitamanas::975.simple_insight: Some verses simply move the story forward, setting up the next turn of fate.
ramacharitamanas::975.detailed_meaning: Brahma has just granted the boon requested by the brothers. He departs, and the brothers return home joyful. The verse then introduces Mandodari, daughter of Maya, whose beauty and status will matter in the next turn of Ravana's story.
ramacharitamanas::975.modern_relevance: A meeting ends, people stand up smiling, and one small introduction changes everything that follows. Some moments look like background until the story turns on them.
ramacharitamanas::975.insight: It shifts attention from the boon itself to the chain of consequences it sets in motion.

ramacharitamanas::976.verse_sanskrit: सोइ मयँ दीन्हि रावनहि आनी। होइहि जातुधानपति जानी॥ हरषित भयउ नारि भलि पाई। पुनि दोउ बंधु बिआहेसि जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::976.verse_hindi: मय ने उसे लाकर रावण को दिया। उसने जान लिया कि यह राक्षसों का राजा होगा। अच्छी स्त्री पाकर रावण प्रसन्न हुआ और फिर उसने जाकर दोनों भाइयों का विवाह कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::976.english_translation: Maya brought her to Ravana. He knew that this one would become the lord of the demons. Ravana was pleased to have a fine wife, and then he went and married the two brothers.
ramacharitamanas::976.translation_literal: सोइ (that very one) / मयँ (by Maya) / दीन्हि (gave) / रावनहि (to Ravana) / आनी (bringing) / होइहि (will become) / जातुधानपति (lord of the demons) / जानी (knowing) / हरषित (delighted) / भयउ (became) / नारि (wife) / भलि (good/fine) / पाई (having obtained) / पुनि (then) / दोउ (both) / बंधु (brothers) / बिआहेसि (he married) / जाई (going)
ramacharitamanas::976.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::976.essence: The story advances through a marriage that will shape Ravana’s rise.
ramacharitamanas::976.simple_meaning: Maya gives his daughter to Ravana, who is pleased to get a beautiful wife and then arranges the marriage of the two brothers.
ramacharitamanas::976.simple_insight: Some events are just the turning of a story’s wheel, not a lesson to be forced from them.
ramacharitamanas::976.detailed_meaning: Maya has just returned from Brahma’s blessing, and the family line now moves toward Ravana. He receives Mandodari, feels pleased by the match, and then completes the marriage of his two brothers. The verse simply carries the story forward.
ramacharitamanas::976.insight: It keeps the focus on narrative movement, not moral instruction.

ramacharitamanas::977.verse_sanskrit: गिरि त्रिकूट एक सिंधु मझारी। बिधि निर्मित दुर्गम अति भारी॥ सोइ मय दानवँ बहुरि सँवारा। कनक रचित मनि भवन अपारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::977.verse_hindi: समुद्र के बीच में त्रिकूट नामक पर्वत पर ब्रह्मा का बनाया हुआ एक बड़ा भारी किला था। (महान मायावी और निपुण कारीगर) मय दानव ने उसको फिर से सजा दिया। उसमें मणियों से जड़े हुए सोने के अनगिनत महल थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::977.english_translation: On Mount Trikuta in the middle of the ocean stood a huge, formidable fortress made by Brahma. Maya Danava later embellished it with countless golden palaces set with jewels.
ramacharitamanas::977.translation_literal: गिरि त्रिकूट (Trikuta mountain) / एक (one) / सिंधु (ocean) / मझारी (in the middle) / बिधि (Brahma) / निर्मित (made) / दुर्गम (hard to reach) / अति भारी (very huge) / सोइ (that same) / मय दानवँ (by Maya Danava) / बहुरि (again) / सँवारा (adorned) / कनक (gold) / रचित (made/arranged) / मनि (jewels) / भवन (palaces) / अपारा (countless, boundless)
ramacharitamanas::977.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::977.essence: Splendour can conceal the forces that built it.
ramacharitamanas::977.simple_meaning: A mighty fortress stood on Trikuta mountain in the ocean, later adorned by Maya Danava with countless golden, jewel-studded palaces.
ramacharitamanas::977.simple_insight: Power can build beauty, but it can also hide danger.
ramacharitamanas::977.detailed_meaning: The narration shifts to Lanka’s setting. Before Ravana’s story fully unfolds, Tulsidas describes the city’s impossible location and grandeur: a fortress in the sea, first shaped by Brahma and then ornamented by Maya Danava. The splendour itself foreshadows the pride inside it.
ramacharitamanas::977.modern_relevance: You walk into a gleaming building with marble floors, quiet elevators, and perfect lighting. Everything looks secure and impressive — but the real story of a place is never its polish alone.
ramacharitamanas::977.insight: It frames outer magnificence as a clue, not a guarantee, and prepares the mind to look beneath appearances.

ramacharitamanas::978.verse_sanskrit: भोगावति जसि अहिकुल बासा। अमरावति जसि सक्रनिवासा॥ तिन्ह तें अधिक रम्य अति बंका। जग बिख्यात नाम तेहि लंका ॥
ramacharitamanas::978.verse_hindi: जैसी नागकुल के रहने की (पाताल लोक में) भोगावती पुरी है और इन्द्र के रहने की (स्वर्गलोक में) अमरावती पुरी है, उनसे भी अधिक सुंदर और बाँका वह दुर्ग था। जगत में उसका नाम लंका प्रसिद्ध हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::978.english_translation: Like Bhogavati is the dwelling of the serpent clan, and like Amaravati is the abode of Indra, even more beautiful and splendid was that fortress. Its name became famous in the world as Lanka.
ramacharitamanas::978.translation_literal: भोगावति (Bhogavati) / जसि (like) / अहिकुल (serpent clan) / बासा (dwelling) / अमरावति (Amaravati) / जसि (like) / सक्रनिवासा (Indra's abode) / तिन्ह तें (than those) / अधिक (more) / रम्य (beautiful) / अति (very) / बंका (splendid/fair) / जग (world) / बिख्यात (famous) / नाम (name) / तेहि (that) / लंका (Lanka)
ramacharitamanas::978.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::978.essence: Even a fortress can feel like a rival to heaven.
ramacharitamanas::978.simple_meaning: Lanka is described as a famous, beautiful, and magnificent fortress, even grander than mythical heavenly cities.
ramacharitamanas::978.simple_insight: Some places are introduced with awe before any action begins.
ramacharitamanas::978.detailed_meaning: Maya has built Ravana's city on Trikuta Mountain in the middle of the sea. The narrator now pauses to describe Lanka itself: a world-famous fortress, more splendid than the legendary cities of the serpent realm and Indra's heaven.
ramacharitamanas::978.modern_relevance: You walk into a city at night and every tower, gate, and light feels unreal. Before any conflict starts, the place itself already carries power and menace.
ramacharitamanas::978.insight: It frames the setting as a force in the story, not just a backdrop.

ramacharitamanas::979.verse_sanskrit: खाईं सिंधु गभीर अति चारिहुँ दिसि फिरि आव। कनक कोट मनि खचित दृढ़ बरनि न जाइ बनाव ॥
ramacharitamanas::979.verse_hindi: उसे चारों ओर से समुद्र की अत्यन्त गहरी खाई घेरे हुए है। उस (दुर्ग) के मणियों से जड़ा हुआ सोने का मजबूत परकोटा है, जिसकी कारीगरी का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::979.english_translation: A very deep moat surrounds it on all four sides. Its golden rampart, studded with gems, is so strong and beautiful that no one can describe its design.
ramacharitamanas::979.translation_literal: खाईं (moat) / सिंधु (ocean) / गभीर (deep) / अति (very) / चारिहुँ दिसि (in all four directions) / फिरि (surrounding) / आव (is) / कनक (golden) / कोट (rampart) / मनि (gems) / खचित (studded) / दृढ़ (strong) / बरनि (to describe) / न जाइ (cannot be) / बनाव (design / workmanship)
ramacharitamanas::979.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::979.essence: Even a glittering fortress is only a fortress.
ramacharitamanas::979.simple_meaning: Lanka is protected by a deep moat on all sides and a golden wall set with gems. Its design is so impressive that words cannot fully describe it.
ramacharitamanas::979.simple_insight: Some things are built to look unbreakable, yet they still stand inside a larger story.
ramacharitamanas::979.detailed_meaning: The narration is describing Lanka, Ravana’s fortified city, after introducing its mountain setting and splendour. The focus is on its defenses: a deep surrounding moat and a gem-studded golden wall. This is scene-setting before the verse turns to Ravana’s power.
ramacharitamanas::979.modern_relevance: You look at a company, a house, or a reputation that seems sealed from every side — polished, expensive, untouchable. The verse reminds you that even the strongest-looking outer shell is only a setting, not the whole story.
ramacharitamanas::979.insight: It shifts attention from surface grandeur to the fragile structures that protect pride.

ramacharitamanas::980.verse_sanskrit: हरि प्रेरित जेहिं कलप जोइ जातुधानपति होइ। सूर प्रतापी अतुलबल दल समेत बस सोइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::980.verse_hindi: भगवान की प्रेरणा से जिस कल्प में जो राक्षसों का राजा (रावण) होता है, वही शूर, प्रतापी, अतुलित बलवान् अपनी सेना सहित उस पुरी में बसता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::980.english_translation: In whatever age the lord of the demons is born by Hari's prompting, that same brave, radiant, immeasurably strong one lives there with his army.
ramacharitamanas::980.translation_literal: हरि (Hari) / प्रेरित (prompted) / जेहिं (in which) / कलप (age) / जोइ (whoever) / जातुधानपति (lord of demons) / होइ (becomes) / सूर (brave) / प्रतापी (radiant, glorious) / अतुलबल (of unequalled strength) / दल (army) / समेत (together with) / बस (dwells) / सोइ (that same one)
ramacharitamanas::980.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::980.essence: Even a demon king's might appears only by Hari's prompting.
ramacharitamanas::980.simple_meaning: Hari's will places a mighty demon king in that city, along with his army. The verse describes the power and grandeur of Lanka's ruler.
ramacharitamanas::980.simple_insight: Power itself is not random; even fearsome strength appears within a larger order.
ramacharitamanas::980.detailed_meaning: The narration is describing Lanka, the fortress city of Ravana. After praising its beauty and defenses, the text says that in whatever age a demon king rises by Hari's prompting, that same formidable ruler lives there with his army. It sets up Ravana's presence as part of the city’s identity.
ramacharitamanas::980.modern_relevance: A company looks untouchable because one bold leader has built an empire around himself. The verse reminds you that even towering power is still temporary and placed within a larger design.
ramacharitamanas::980.insight: It shifts attention from human dominance to the force that allows dominance to appear at all.

ramacharitamanas::981.verse_sanskrit: रहे तहाँ निसिचर भट भारे। ते सब सुरन्ह समर संघारे॥ अब तहँ रहहिं सक्र के प्रेरे। रच्छक कोटि जच्छपति केरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::981.verse_hindi: (पहले) वहाँ बड़े-बड़े योद्धा राक्षस रहते थे। देवताओं ने उन सबको युद्द में मार डाला। अब इंद्र की प्रेरणा से वहाँ कुबेर के एक करोड़ रक्षक (यक्ष लोग) रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::981.english_translation: Great warrior demons once lived there. The radiant beings defeated them in battle. Now, by Indra's command, a crore guardians of Kubera live there.
ramacharitamanas::981.translation_literal: रहे (remained/lived) / तहाँ (there) / निसिचर (night-walkers; demons) / भट (warriors) / भारे (great, mighty) । ते (they) / सब (all) / सुरन्ह (by the radiant beings; gods) / समर (battle) / संघारे (were destroyed) ॥ अब (now) / तहँ (there) / रहहिं (remain) / सक्र (Indra) / के (of) / प्रेरे (by the prompting) । रच्छक (guardians) / कोटि (ten million) / जच्छपति (of Kubera) / केरे (belonging to) ॥
ramacharitamanas::981.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::981.essence: Even a mighty stronghold is only temporary in the face of changing power.
ramacharitamanas::981.simple_meaning: That place was once full of powerful demon warriors, but they were defeated in battle. Now it is guarded by a huge force of Kubera's attendants under Indra's order.
ramacharitamanas::981.simple_insight: Power shifts, and even the strongest stronghold can change hands.
ramacharitamanas::981.detailed_meaning: After the earlier description of Lanka's fortified walls, the narration turns to its defenders. Powerful demons once lived there, but the radiant beings killed them in war. Now a vast host of Kubera's guardians remains there under Indra's direction, showing how the fortress has changed hands over time.
ramacharitamanas::981.insight: It shifts attention from the fortress's beauty to the changing forces that hold it.

ramacharitamanas::982.verse_sanskrit: दसमुख कतहुँ खबरि असि पाई। सेन साजि गढ़ घेरेसि जाई॥ देखि बिकट भट बड़ि कटकाई। जच्छ जीव लै गए पराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::982.verse_hindi: रावण को कहीं ऐसी खबर मिली, तब उसने सेना सजाकर किले को जा घेरा। उस बड़े विकट योद्धा और उसकी बड़ी सेना को देखकर यक्ष अपने प्राण लेकर भाग गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::982.english_translation: Ravana heard news from somewhere, then gathered his army and went to besiege the fort. Seeing that terrible warrior and his huge force, the yakshas fled with their lives.
ramacharitamanas::982.translation_literal: दसमुख (ten-faced one, Ravana) / कतहुँ (somewhere) / खबरि (news) / असि (such) / पाई (having received) / सेना (army) / साजि (having arranged) / गढ़ (fort) / घेरेसि (besieged) / जाई (going) / देखि (seeing) / बिकट (terrible) / भट (warrior) / बड़ि (great) / कटकाई (army) / जच्छ (yakshas) / जीव (life) / लै (taking) / गए (went) / पराई (away)
ramacharitamanas::982.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::982.simple_meaning: Ravana hears the news, gathers his army, and surrounds the fort. The yakshas panic and flee when they see his terrifying force.
ramacharitamanas::982.simple_insight: Fear spreads fast when power arrives with force.
ramacharitamanas::982.detailed_meaning: Ravana has taken control of Lanka and is moving through the city with overwhelming force. When he hears news, he marshals his army and surrounds the fort. The yakshas, seeing his terrible might, run for their lives.
ramacharitamanas::982.modern_relevance: A rumour reaches the office before noon, and suddenly everyone is tense, watching the same powerful person walk in with a storm behind him.
ramacharitamanas::982.insight: It shows how intimidation works: the sight of raw force can drive people away before a word is spoken.

ramacharitamanas::983.verse_sanskrit: फिरि सब नगर दसानन देखा। गयउ सोच सुख भयउ बिसेषा॥ सुंदर सहज अगम अनुमानी। कीन्हि तहाँ रावन रजधानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::983.verse_hindi: तब रावण ने घूम-फिरकर सारा नगर देखा। उसकी (स्थान संबंधी) चिन्ता मिट गई और उसे बहुत ही सुख हुआ। उस पुरी को स्वाभाविक ही सुंदर और (बाहर वालों के लिए) दुर्गम अनुमान करके रावण ने वहाँ अपनी राजधानी कायम की ॥
ramacharitamanas::983.english_translation: Ravana looked around the whole city. His worry about the site vanished, and he felt great delight. Seeing it naturally beautiful and hard to approach from outside, he made it his capital.
ramacharitamanas::983.translation_literal: फिरि (having turned around) / सब (all) / नगर (city) / दसानन (Ravana) / देखा (saw) / गयउ (went away) / सोच (worry) / सुख (happiness) / भयउ (became) / बिसेषा (especially)॥ / सुंदर (beautiful) / सहज (natural) / अगम (hard to reach) / अनुमानी (having judged) / कीन्हि (made) / तहाँ (there) / रावन (Ravana) / रजधानी (capital) ॥
ramacharitamanas::983.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::983.essence: Power turns a conquered place into a home.
ramacharitamanas::983.simple_meaning: Ravana inspects the city, finds it beautiful and secure, and decides to make it his capital.
ramacharitamanas::983.simple_insight: A place can win the mind before it wins the body.
ramacharitamanas::983.detailed_meaning: Ravana is surveying the conquered city after the earlier fighting. He notices its beauty and natural security, loses his concern, and chooses it as his capital. The verse simply moves the story forward by showing how he settles into power.
ramacharitamanas::983.modern_relevance: You walk through a new apartment, checking the windows, the light, the quiet street. Once it feels safe and impressive, your mind has already moved in before you have.
ramacharitamanas::983.insight: It shows how conquest becomes possession when the mind decides a place is secure.

ramacharitamanas::984.verse_sanskrit: जेहि जस जोग बाँटि गृह दीन्हे। सुखी सकल रजनीचर कीन्हें॥ एक बार कुबेर पर धावा। पुष्पक जान जीति लै आवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::984.verse_hindi: योग्यता के अनुसार घरों को बाँटकर रावण ने सब राक्षसों को सुखी किया। एक बार वह कुबेर पर चढ़ दौड़ा और उससे पुष्पक विमान को जीतकर ले आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::984.english_translation: Ravana distributed houses according to each one's merit and made all the demons content. Once he attacked Kubera and seized the Pushpak chariot after defeating him.
ramacharitamanas::984.translation_literal: जेहि जस जोग (according to each one's merit) / बाँटि (having divided) / गृह (houses) / दीन्हे (gave) / सुखी (content) / सकल (all) / रजनीचर (night-walkers, demons) / कीन्हें (made) ॥ / एक बार (one time) / कुबेर (Kubera) / पर (upon) / धावा (attacked) / पुष्पक (Pushpak) / जान (chariot) / जीति (having won) / लै (taking) / आवा (brought) ॥
ramacharitamanas::984.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::984.essence: Great power still bows to pride.
ramacharitamanas::984.simple_meaning: Ravana is described as a strong ruler who organized his kingdom well and won Kubera's flying chariot in battle.
ramacharitamanas::984.simple_insight: Power can look orderly and impressive before its pride turns destructive.
ramacharitamanas::984.detailed_meaning: Ravana has just been shown surveying Lanka and taking pride in its strength. This verse adds how he governed his people and how far his ambition reached: he ruled efficiently, defeated Kubera, and brought home the Pushpak chariot. The scene builds his grandeur before the story turns darker.
ramacharitamanas::984.modern_relevance: A leader can build a polished, efficient system and still be driven by ego. The structure may work; the heart behind it can still be reckless.
ramacharitamanas::984.insight: It separates outward competence from inner wisdom, warning that success can feed arrogance.

ramacharitamanas::985.verse_sanskrit: कौतुकहीं कैलास पुनि लीन्हेसि जाइ उठाइ। मनहुँ तौलि निज बाहुबल चला बहुत सुख पाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::985.verse_hindi: फिर उसने जाकर (एक बार) खिलवाड़ ही में कैलास पर्वत को उठा लिया और मानो अपनी भुजाओं का बल तौलकर, बहुत सुख पाकर वह वहाँ से चला आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::985.english_translation: Then, just for sport, he lifted Mount Kailash and carried it away, as if weighing the strength of his own arms, and went off delighted.
ramacharitamanas::985.translation_literal: कौतुकहीं (just for sport) / कैलास (Kailash) / पुनि (again) / लीन्हेसि (he lifted) / जाइ (going) / उठाइ (lifting) / मनहुँ (as if) / तौलि (weighing) / निज (his own) / बाहुबल (arm-strength) / चला (he went) / बहुत (much) / सुख (delight) / पाइ (having obtained)
ramacharitamanas::985.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::985.essence: Power becomes vanity when it exists only to impress itself.
ramacharitamanas::985.simple_meaning: Ravana casually lifted Mount Kailash, almost as if testing his own strength, and left pleased with himself.
ramacharitamanas::985.simple_insight: Pride can turn even impossible acts into play.
ramacharitamanas::985.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already made Lanka secure and prosperous. Now the verse shows the scale of his arrogance: he lifts Kailash merely as sport, treating a sacred mountain like proof of his own power. It is a display, not a lesson.
ramacharitamanas::985.modern_relevance: Someone wins a little status and starts treating every room like a stage. The real danger is not strength itself, but the thrill of proving it to yourself.
ramacharitamanas::985.insight: It shows how ego turns power into self-admiration instead of service.

ramacharitamanas::986.verse_sanskrit: सुख संपति सुत सेन सहाई। जय प्रताप बल बुद्धि बड़ाई॥ नित नूतन सब बाढ़त जाई। जिमि प्रतिलाभ लोभ अधिकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::986.verse_hindi: सुख, सम्पत्ति, पुत्र, सेना, सहायक, जय, प्रताप, बल, बुद्धि और बड़ाई- ये सब उसके नित्य नए (वैसे ही) बढ़ते जाते थे, जैसे प्रत्येक लाभ पर लोभ बढ़ता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::986.english_translation: His happiness, wealth, sons, army, allies, victory, glory, strength, intelligence, and greatness kept increasing, just as greed increases with every gain.
ramacharitamanas::986.translation_literal: सुख (happiness) / संपति (wealth) / सुत (sons) / सेन (army) / सहाई (allies) / जय (victory) / प्रताप (glory) / बल (strength) / बुद्धि (intelligence) / बड़ाई (greatness) / नित (always) / नूतन (new) / सब (all) / बाढ़त (increasing) / जाई (goes) / जिमि (just as) / प्रतिलाभ (with each gain) / लोभ (greed) / अधिकाई (increases)
ramacharitamanas::986.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::986.essence: More power only enlarged his appetite.
ramacharitamanas::986.simple_meaning: Ravana's power and comforts kept growing without limit. Each success only made him want more, like greed that expands after every gain.
ramacharitamanas::986.simple_insight: Unchecked success can feed hunger instead of satisfaction.
ramacharitamanas::986.detailed_meaning: The narration is describing Ravana's rise before the war. He has wealth, power, family support, and growing fame, but none of it satisfies him. Every gain only makes his hunger larger, setting up the force that will later challenge Ram.
ramacharitamanas::986.modern_relevance: You hit one target, then immediately start chasing the next badge, the next raise, the next proof. Achievements pile up, but the appetite only gets louder.
ramacharitamanas::986.insight: It shifts attention from accumulation to the mind that cannot stop accumulating.

ramacharitamanas::987.verse_sanskrit: अतिबल कुंभकरन अस भ्राता। जेहि कहुँ नहिं प्रतिभट जग जाता॥ करइ पान सोवइ षट मासा। जागत होइ तिहूँ पुर त्रासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::987.verse_hindi: अत्यन्त बलवान् कुम्भकर्ण सा उसका भाई था, जिसके जोड़ का योद्धा जगत में पैदा ही नहीं हुआ। वह मदिरा पीकर छह महीने सोया करता था। उसके जागते ही तीनों लोकों में तहलका मच जाता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::987.english_translation: His brother was the mighty Kumbhakarna, for whom no equal warrior had ever been born in the world. He drank and slept for six months; when he woke, the three worlds trembled.
ramacharitamanas::987.translation_literal: अतिबल (extremely strong) / कुंभकरन (Kumbhakarna) / अस (like this) / भ्राता (brother) | जेहि कहुँ (for whom) / नहिं (not) / प्रतिभट (equal opponent) / जग (world) / जाता (born) | करइ (does) / पान (drinking) / सोवइ (sleeps) / षट (six) / मासा (months) | जागत (waking) / होइ (becomes) / तिहूँ (three) / पुर (worlds/cities) / त्रासा (terror)
ramacharitamanas::987.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::987.essence: Unrestrained strength turns sleep and waking alike into danger.
ramacharitamanas::987.simple_meaning: Ravana's brother Kumbhakarna is described as unimaginably strong, sleeping for six months at a time and frightening the three worlds whenever he wakes.
ramacharitamanas::987.simple_insight: Raw power without restraint becomes a threat, even before it is used.
ramacharitamanas::987.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Tulsidas pauses the story to describe Ravana's family. Kumbhakarna is not a thinker or devotee here, only a colossal force: unmatched in battle, drunk, asleep for months, and terrifying when awake. The verse builds Ravana's side as a world of excess.
ramacharitamanas::987.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when the one person who always dominates finally speaks. Everyone feels the pressure before a single word lands. Power like that changes the atmosphere before it changes anything else.
ramacharitamanas::987.insight: It shifts attention from admiration of strength to awareness of how ungoverned force affects everyone around it.

ramacharitamanas::988.verse_sanskrit: जौं दिन प्रति अहार कर सोई। बिस्व बेगि सब चौपट होई॥ समर धीर नहिं जाइ बखाना। तेहि सम अमित बीर बलवाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::988.verse_hindi: यदि वह प्रतिदिन भोजन करता, तब तो सम्पूर्ण विश्व शीघ्र ही चौपट (खाली) हो जाता। रणधीर ऐसा था कि जिसका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। (लंका में) उसके ऐसे असंख्य बलवान वीर थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::988.english_translation: If he ate every day, the whole world would quickly be laid waste. He was so valiant in battle that no one could describe him. Lanka had countless such mighty warriors.
ramacharitamanas::988.translation_literal: जौं (if) / दिन प्रति (every day) / अहार (food) / कर (doing) / सोई (he) / बिस्व (world) / बेगि (quickly) / सब (all) / चौपट (ruined) / होई (would become) ॥ / समर (battle) / धीर (valiant) / नहिं (not) / जाइ (can be) / बखाना (described) / तेहि (that) / सम (like) / अमित (countless) / बीर (warriors) / बलवाना (powerful) ॥
ramacharitamanas::988.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::988.essence: Unchecked power becomes ruin when nothing restrains it.
ramacharitamanas::988.simple_meaning: Kumbhakarna is described as so huge and powerful that even his normal appetite would destroy the world, and his battle courage is beyond description. Lanka is full of warriors like him.
ramacharitamanas::988.simple_insight: Some forces are so excessive they become their own danger.
ramacharitamanas::988.detailed_meaning: The narration continues in Lanka, describing Ravana's terrifying allies before the war intensifies. Kumbhakarna is presented as a being whose appetite and strength are both monstrous, and the verse widens the threat by saying Lanka contains many such warriors.
ramacharitamanas::988.modern_relevance: A room full of people keeps talking about one person who drains every resource and dominates every conflict. The problem is not just one giant appetite — it is a whole culture built around it.
ramacharitamanas::988.insight: It shifts attention from individual strength to the destructive scale of unchecked power.

ramacharitamanas::989.verse_sanskrit: बारिदनाद जेठ सुत तासू। भट महुँ प्रथम लीक जग जासू॥ जेहि न होइ रन सनमुख कोई। सुरपुर नितहिं परावन होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::989.verse_hindi: मेघनाद रावण का बड़ा लड़का था, जिसका जगत के योद्धाओं में पहला नंबर था। रण में कोई भी उसका सामना नहीं कर सकता था। स्वर्ग में तो (उसके भय से) नित्य भगदड़ मची रहती थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::989.english_translation: Meghanad was Ravana's eldest son. He ranked first among the warriors of the world. No one could face him in battle, and even the higher realm was thrown into panic by him every day.
ramacharitamanas::989.translation_literal: बारिदनाद (Meghanad) / जेठ सुत (eldest son) / तासू (of him) / भट महुँ (among warriors) / प्रथम लीक (first rank) / जग जासू (whose fame in the world)॥ / जेहि (whom) / न होइ (does not become) / रन सनमुख (face-to-face in battle) / कोई (anyone) / सुरपुर (higher realm) / नितहिं (every day) / परावन (panic / uproar) / होई (is)
ramacharitamanas::989.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::989.essence: Fear can make a warrior famous, but never secure.
ramacharitamanas::989.simple_meaning: Meghanad was Ravana's eldest and most feared son. No warrior could stand before him, and even the higher realm trembled at his power.
ramacharitamanas::989.simple_insight: Power without restraint makes every place feel unsafe.
ramacharitamanas::989.detailed_meaning: The narration continues listing Ravana's terrifying champions in Lanka. Meghanad stands out as the foremost warrior, so fierce that no one dares face him and even the higher realm is said to panic at his approach. The verse builds Ravana's side as a force of overwhelming threat.
ramacharitamanas::989.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when one person walks in because everyone knows they dominate the conversation. That kind of fear may look like strength, but it reveals a world ruled by intimidation.
ramacharitamanas::989.insight: It frames raw force as instability, not greatness.

ramacharitamanas::990.verse_sanskrit: कुमुख अकंपन कुलिसरद धूमकेतु अतिकाय। एक एक जग जीति सक ऐसे सुभट निकाय ॥
ramacharitamanas::990.verse_hindi: (इनके अतिरिक्त) दुर्मुख, अकम्पन, वज्रदन्त, धूमकेतु और अतिकाय आदि ऐसे अनेक योद्धा थे, जो अकेले ही सारे जगत को जीत सकते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::990.english_translation: Besides them were Durmukh, Akampan, Vajradanta, Dhumketu, and Atikaya—such warriors that each could conquer the whole world alone.
ramacharitamanas::990.translation_literal: कुमुख (Durmukh) / अकंपन (Akampan) / कुलिसरद (Vajradanta) / धूमकेतु (Dhumketu) / अतिकाय (Atikaya) / एक एक (each one) / जग (world) / जीति (conquering) / सक (could) / ऐसे (such) / सुभट (warriors) / निकाय (group)
ramacharitamanas::990.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::990.essence: Lanka's power is shown through warriors who seem unbeatable alone.
ramacharitamanas::990.simple_meaning: Ravana's side also had many more terrifying warriors, each powerful enough to conquer the world alone.
ramacharitamanas::990.simple_insight: Raw strength can look overwhelming, but it is still only force.
ramacharitamanas::990.detailed_meaning: The poem is listing Ravana's mighty commanders after describing Meghnad. It adds more names to show how fearsome Lanka's army seemed before the war fully unfolds. The point is scale, not teaching.
ramacharitamanas::990.modern_relevance: A meeting room fills with the names of the best people, the biggest budgets, the sharpest plans. The list itself is meant to intimidate before anything begins.
ramacharitamanas::990.insight: It sets the scale of the enemy force before the battle turns.

ramacharitamanas::991.verse_sanskrit: कामरूप जानहिं सब माया। सपनेहुँ जिन्ह कें धरम न दाया॥ दसमुख बैठ सभाँ एक बारा। देखि अमित आपन परिवारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::991.verse_hindi: सभी राक्षस मनमाना रूप बना सकते थे और (आसुरी) माया जानते थे। उनके दया-धर्म स्वप्न में भी नहीं था। एक बार सभा में बैठे हुए रावण ने अपने अगणित परिवार को देखा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::991.english_translation: All the demons could assume any form they wished and knew illusion. They had no trace of compassion or righteousness, even in dreams. Once, Ravana sat in his assembly and looked at his countless relatives.
ramacharitamanas::991.translation_literal: कामरूप (able to take any form) / जानहिं (they know) / सब (all) / माया (illusion) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / जिन्ह कें (for whom) / धरम (righteousness) / न (not) / दाया (compassion) / दसमुख (ten-faced one, Ravana) / बैठ (sitting) / सभाँ (in the assembly) / एक बारा (one time) / देखि (seeing) / अमित (countless) / आपन (his own) / परिवारा (family, retinue)
ramacharitamanas::991.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::991.essence: Illusion and strength mean little without compassion or righteousness.
ramacharitamanas::991.simple_meaning: The demons were skilled in illusion but lacked compassion and righteousness. Ravana sat in his court and looked over his huge family and followers.
ramacharitamanas::991.simple_insight: Power without compassion only multiplies emptiness.
ramacharitamanas::991.detailed_meaning: The scene stays in Lanka. After naming Ravana's great warriors, the narration turns to Ravana himself, seated in his court and surrounded by a vast demon family. The verse shows the scale of his power and the moral emptiness beneath it before he speaks in pride.
ramacharitamanas::991.modern_relevance: A leader scrolls through hundreds of names on a company roster, proud of how much control he has. The numbers look impressive, but the verse asks what kind of people fill that circle.
ramacharitamanas::991.insight: It shifts attention from sheer size and ability to the moral quality of the people and power you gather.

ramacharitamanas::992.verse_sanskrit: सुत समूह जन परिजन नाती। गनै को पार निसाचर जाती॥ सेन बिलोकि सहज अभिमानी। बोला बचन क्रोध मद सानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::992.verse_hindi: पुत्र-पौत्र, कुटुम्बी और सेवक ढेर-के-ढेर थे। (सारी) राक्षसों की जातियों को तो गिन ही कौन सकता था! अपनी सेना को देखकर स्वभाव से ही अभिमानी रावण क्रोध और गर्व में सनी हुई वाणी बोला- ॥
ramacharitamanas::992.english_translation: Sons, grandsons, relatives, and servants were countless. Who could even count the races of the night-dwellers? Seeing his army, the naturally arrogant Ravana spoke words soaked in anger and pride.
ramacharitamanas::992.translation_literal: सुत समूह (groups of sons) / जन परिजन (kinsmen and household) / नाती (grandsons) / गनै (to count) / को पार (what limit) / निसाचर जाती (races of night-dwellers) ॥ / सेन (army) / बिलोकि (seeing) / सहज (natural) / अभिमानी (arrogant) / बोला (spoke) / बचन (words) / क्रोध (anger) / मद (pride) / सानी (mixed with)
ramacharitamanas::992.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::992.essence: Power without humility turns into loud, self-feeding pride.
ramacharitamanas::992.simple_meaning: Ravana looks at his vast family and army and becomes even more arrogant. This is the moment before he boasts in anger to his forces.
ramacharitamanas::992.simple_insight: Pride grows louder when it is surrounded by numbers and power.
ramacharitamanas::992.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana sits before an enormous household and army of night-dwellers. Seeing his own strength, he becomes more arrogant, and anger mixes with pride as he begins to address his troops. The verse sets up his boastful speech.
ramacharitamanas::992.modern_relevance: You scroll through a group chat full of people cheering you on, and your judgment starts to blur. Approval can make pride sound like certainty.
ramacharitamanas::992.insight: It shows how power and crowd support can feed delusion instead of wisdom.

ramacharitamanas::993.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु सकल रजनीचर जूथा। हमरे बैरी बिबुध बरूथा॥ ते सनमुख नहिं करहिं लराई। देखि सबल रिपु जाहिं पराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::993.verse_hindi: हे समस्त राक्षसों के दलों! सुनो, देवतागण हमारे शत्रु हैं। वे सामने आकर युद्ध नहीं करते। बलवान शत्रु को देखकर भाग जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::993.english_translation: Listen, all you hosts of night-dwellers: the radiant beings are our enemies. They do not come forward to fight. They flee when they see a strong foe.
ramacharitamanas::993.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / सकल (all) / रजनीचर (night-walkers) / जूथा (hosts, groups) / हमरे (our) / बैरी (enemies) / बिबुध (radiant beings) / बरूथा (armies)॥ ते (they) / सनमुख (face-to-face) / नहिं (do not) / करहिं (do) / लराई (fight) / देखि (seeing) / सबल (strong) / रिपु (enemy) / जाहिं (go) / पराई (flee away)॥
ramacharitamanas::993.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::993.essence: Ego always claims the stronger side, even before the fight begins.
ramacharitamanas::993.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts to his forces that the radiant beings are afraid of direct battle and run from strength.
ramacharitamanas::993.simple_insight: Pride turns fear into a story of superiority.
ramacharitamanas::993.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana stands before his assembled forces, inflamed by his own power and the size of his army. He mocks the radiant beings as cowards, setting up the arrogant logic that will soon be shattered by war.
ramacharitamanas::993.modern_relevance: A leader in a meeting dismisses every critic as weak and scared, mistaking swagger for strength. That kind of confidence usually collapses the moment real resistance appears.
ramacharitamanas::993.insight: It exposes how ego rewrites fear as dominance and mistakes boasting for power.

ramacharitamanas::994.verse_sanskrit: तेन्ह कर मरन एक बिधि होई। कहउँ बुझाइ सुनहु अब सोई॥ द्विजभोजन मख होम सराधा। सब कै जाइ करहु तुम्ह बाधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::994.verse_hindi: उनका मरण एक ही उपाय से हो सकता है, मैं समझाकर कहता हूँ। अब उसे सुनो। (उनके बल को बढ़ाने वाले) ब्राह्मण भोजन, यज्ञ, हवन और श्राद्ध- इन सबमें जाकर तुम बाधा डालो ॥
ramacharitamanas::994.english_translation: There is only one way to kill them. Listen carefully now. Go and disrupt the Brahmin-feasts, sacrifices, fire offerings, and funeral rites that sustain their strength.
ramacharitamanas::994.translation_literal: तेन्ह कर (their) / मरन (death) / एक (one) / बिधि (way) / होई (is) / कहउँ (I say) / बुझाइ (explaining) / सुनहु (listen) / अब (now) / सोई (that only) / द्विजभोजन (feeding of Brahmins) / मख (sacrifice) / होम (fire offering) / सराधा (funeral rite) / सब कै (of all) / जाइ (go) / करहु (do) / तुम्ह (you) / बाधा (obstruction)
ramacharitamanas::994.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::994.essence: Destruction begins by cutting off what gives others strength.
ramacharitamanas::994.simple_meaning: Ravana says the only way to defeat the gods is to stop the rituals that strengthen them.
ramacharitamanas::994.simple_insight: It shows how hatred attacks the sources of another's strength, not just the person.
ramacharitamanas::994.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking to the demons after boasting about his army. He explains that the gods can be weakened only by blocking the rites that nourish them. The verse shifts from pride to strategy, showing the dark intelligence behind his aggression.
ramacharitamanas::994.modern_relevance: A group realizes it cannot win by direct force, so it sabotages the support system instead. The move is cold, strategic, and deeply destructive.
ramacharitamanas::994.insight: It shifts attention from open conflict to the hidden ways people undermine what sustains others.

ramacharitamanas::995.verse_sanskrit: छुधा छीन बलहीन सुर सहजेहिं मिलिहहिं आइ। तब मारिहउँ कि छाड़िहउँ भली भाँति अपनाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::995.verse_hindi: भूख से दुर्बल और बलहीन होकर देवता सहज ही में आ मिलेंगे। तब उनको मैं मार डालूँगा अथवा भलीभाँति अपने अधीन करके (सर्वथा पराधीन करके) छोड़ दूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::995.english_translation: The gods will come weakened by hunger. Then I will kill them or bring them fully under my control.
ramacharitamanas::995.translation_literal: छुधा (hunger) / छीन (weakened) / बलहीन (powerless) / सुर (devas) / सहजेहिं (easily) / मिलिहहिं (will come together) / आइ (coming) / तब (then) / मारिहउँ (I will kill) / कि (or) / छाड़िहउँ (I will release) / भली भाँति (well) / अपनाइ (taking under control)
ramacharitamanas::995.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::995.essence: Control begins by making others helpless.
ramacharitamanas::995.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that starving the gods will make them easy to overpower. He plans either to kill them or force them into submission.
ramacharitamanas::995.simple_insight: Pride looks for weakness to exploit, but it always reveals its own cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::995.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is plotting against the devas after learning how to weaken them through ritual disruption. He imagines that hunger will make them helpless, and that he can then destroy or subdue them. The verse shows his arrogant strategy taking shape.
ramacharitamanas::995.modern_relevance: A manager cuts every resource and then blames the team for failing. The move feels clever for a moment, but it is really just control dressed up as strategy.
ramacharitamanas::995.insight: It exposes the logic of ego: weaken others first, then claim victory over them.

ramacharitamanas::996.verse_sanskrit: मेघनाद कहूँ पुनि हँकरावा। दीन्हीं सिख बलु बयरु बढ़ावा॥ जे सुर समर धीर बलवाना। जिन्ह कें लरिबे कर अभिमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::996.verse_hindi: फिर उसने मेघनाद को बुलवाया और सिखा-पढ़ाकर उसके बल और देवताओं के प्रति बैरभाव को उत्तेजना दी। (फिर कहा-) हे पुत्र ! जो देवता रण में धीर और बलवान् हैं और जिन्हें लड़ने का अभिमान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::996.english_translation: Then he summoned Meghnad again and instructed him, stirring up his strength and hatred toward the devas. "Son, those devas are brave and mighty in battle, and they take pride in fighting."
ramacharitamanas::996.translation_literal: मेघनाद (Meghnad) / कहूँ (to) / पुनि (again) / हँकरावा (was summoned) / दीन्हीं (gave) / सिख (instruction) / बलु (strength) / बयरु (enmity) / बढ़ावा (increased) / जे (those who) / सुर (devas) / समर (battle) / धीर (steadfast) / बलवाना (powerful) / जिन्ह कें (in whom) / लरिबे (to fight) / कर (of) / अभिमाना (pride)
ramacharitamanas::996.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::996.essence: Strength becomes destructive when it is fed by pride and enmity.
ramacharitamanas::996.simple_meaning: Ravana calls Meghnad and urges him to grow stronger and more hostile toward the devas. He points out that the devas are brave fighters who take pride in battle.
ramacharitamanas::996.simple_insight: Pride and hatred can be taught, sharpened, and passed on.
ramacharitamanas::996.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is preparing his son Meghnad for war. He does not just give orders; he feeds Meghnad's anger and confidence, then points to the devas as worthy enemies. The scene shows how ego trains the next generation to fight.
ramacharitamanas::996.modern_relevance: A parent hypes up a child before a sports match, turning competition into contempt. The lesson is unsettling: the attitudes we repeat become the instincts we hand on.
ramacharitamanas::996.insight: It shows how leaders can weaponize pride, turning skill into aggression and conflict into identity.

ramacharitamanas::997.verse_sanskrit: तिन्हहि जीति रन आनेसु बाँधी। उठि सुत पितु अनुसासन काँघी॥ एहि बिधि सबही अग्या दीन्हीं। आपुनु चलेउ गदा कर लीन्ही ॥
ramacharitamanas::997.verse_hindi: उन्हें युद्ध में जीतकर बाँध लाना। बेटे ने उठकर पिता की आज्ञा को शिरोधार्य किया। इसी तरह उसने सबको आज्ञा दी और आप भी हाथ में गदा लेकर चल दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::997.english_translation: Capture them in battle and bring them bound. The son rose and placed his father's command upon his shoulder. In this way he gave orders to everyone, and then set out himself with mace in hand.
ramacharitamanas::997.translation_literal: तिन्हहि (them) / जीति (having defeated) / रन (in battle) / आनेसु (bring) / बाँधी (bound) / उठि (rising) / सुत (the son) / पितु (father's) / अनुसासन (command) / काँघी (on the shoulder) / एहि बिधि (in this way) / सबही (to everyone) / अग्या (orders) / दीन्हीं (gave) / आपुनु (himself) / चलेउ (went) / गदा (mace) / कर (in hand) / लीन्ही (took)
ramacharitamanas::997.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::997.essence: True obedience becomes action the moment it is heard.
ramacharitamanas::997.simple_meaning: The son accepts his father's order, gives commands to the others, and goes out to fight with his mace in hand.
ramacharitamanas::997.simple_insight: Duty is not only spoken; it is carried, commanded, and acted on without delay.
ramacharitamanas::997.detailed_meaning: After Ravana orders his son Megnada to strike fear into the gods, the son rises at once. He takes his father's command on his shoulder, sends out orders to the rest, and moves into battle with his mace. The scene shows obedience turning into action.
ramacharitamanas::997.modern_relevance: The message lands when a manager forwards a crisis at 9pm and you stop scrolling, assign the next steps, and get moving. Responsibility becomes real only when someone carries it.
ramacharitamanas::997.insight: It shifts attention from hearing instructions to embodying them immediately.

ramacharitamanas::998.verse_sanskrit: चलत दसानन डोलति अवनी। गर्जत गर्भ स्रवहिं सुर रवनी॥ रावन आवत सुनेउ सकोहा। देवन्ह तके मेरु गिरि खोहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::998.verse_hindi: रावण के चलने से पृथ्वी डगमगाने लगी और उसकी गर्जना से देवरमणियों के गर्भ गिरने लगे। रावण को क्रोध सहित आते हुए सुनकर देवताओं ने सुमेरु पर्वत की गुफाएँ तकीं (भागकर सुमेरु की गुफाओं का आश्रय लिया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::998.english_translation: As Ravana walked, the earth trembled. His roar made the celestial women miscarry. Hearing Ravana approach in fury, the gods looked to the caves of Mount Meru for refuge.
ramacharitamanas::998.translation_literal: चलत (walking) / दसानन (Ravana, the ten-faced one) / डोलति (trembled) / अवनी (earth) / गर्जत (roaring) / गर्भ (womb/pregnancy) / स्रवहिं (flow away / miscarry) / सुर (radiant beings) / रवनी (women/voices) / रावन (Ravana) / आवत (coming) / सुनेउ (heard) / सकोहा (angrily) / देवन्ह (the gods) / तके (sought) / मेरु गिरि (Mount Meru) / खोहा (caves)
ramacharitamanas::998.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::998.essence: Ravana's presence alone turns the world into a place of fear.
ramacharitamanas::998.simple_meaning: Ravana's power is so fearsome that the world shakes and the gods hide from him.
ramacharitamanas::998.simple_insight: Unchecked pride can make fear spread everywhere, even before a battle begins.
ramacharitamanas::998.detailed_meaning: Ravana advances in Lanka with overwhelming force. His presence shakes the earth, terrifies the heavenly beings, and sends the gods searching for shelter in Mount Meru. The stanza builds his menace before the next confrontation.
ramacharitamanas::998.modern_relevance: A room goes silent when one person storms in angry and untouchable. Everyone feels smaller, even before a word is spoken. This verse captures that kind of fear-made-power.
ramacharitamanas::998.insight: It shows how raw force can dominate a whole atmosphere before any action is taken.

ramacharitamanas::999.verse_sanskrit: दिगपालन्ह के लोक सुहाए। सूने सकल दसानन पाए॥ पुनि पुनि सिंघनाद करि भारी। देइ देवतन्ह गारि पचारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::999.verse_hindi: दिक्पालों के सारे सुंदर लोकों को रावण ने सूना पाया। वह बार-बार भारी सिंहगर्जना करके देवताओं को ललकार-ललकारकर गालियाँ देता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::999.english_translation: Ravana found the beautiful worlds of the guardians of the directions emptied. Again and again he roared fiercely, hurling abuse and taunts at the gods.
