ramacharitamanas::999.translation_literal: दिगपालन्ह (of the guardians of the directions) / के (of the) / लोक (worlds) / सुहाए (beautiful) / सूने (empty) / सकल (all) / दसानन (Ravana) / पाए (found) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / सिंघनाद (lion-roar) / करि (doing) / भारी (fierce, great) / देइ (giving) / देवतन्ह (to the gods) / गारि (abuse) / पचारी (taunted)
ramacharitamanas::999.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::999.essence: Unchecked pride fills empty space with noise.
ramacharitamanas::999.simple_meaning: Ravana swept through the heavenly realms and found them deserted. He kept roaring loudly and insulting the gods as he went.
ramacharitamanas::999.simple_insight: Power can become noise when it has no worthy match.
ramacharitamanas::999.detailed_meaning: Ravana has burst into the realms of the guardians of the directions. The once-beautiful worlds are empty before him, and his pride turns into loud taunts and roaring. This is scene-setting for his unchecked arrogance before the next challenge.
ramacharitamanas::999.modern_relevance: A person storms through a group chat, a meeting, or a family argument, dominating everything with volume. The room goes quiet, but not because they have won.
ramacharitamanas::999.insight: It frames arrogance as aggressive display, not real strength.

ramacharitamanas::1000.verse_sanskrit: रन मद मत्त फिरइ गज धावा। प्रतिभट खोजत कतहुँ न पावा॥ रबि ससि पवन बरुन धनधारी। अगिनि काल जम सब अधिकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1000.verse_hindi: रण के मद में मतवाला होकर वह अपनी जोड़ी का योद्धा खोजता हुआ जगत भर में दौड़ता फिरा, परन्तु उसे ऐसा योद्धा कहीं नहीं मिला। सूर्य, चन्द्रमा, वायु, वरुण, कुबेर, अग्नि, काल और यम आदि सब अधिकारी, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1000.english_translation: Drunk with the pride of battle, he roamed about like a charging elephant, searching for a worthy rival but finding none. The Sun, Moon, Wind, Varuna, Kubera, Fire, Time, and Yama all stood among the mighty.
ramacharitamanas::1000.translation_literal: रण (battle) / मद (intoxication, pride) / मत्त (drunk, maddened) / फिरइ (wanders) / गज (elephant) / धावा (charged) / प्रतिभट (worthy rival) / खोजत (searching) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / न (not) / पावा (found) / रबि (sun) / ससि (moon) / पवन (wind) / बरुन (Varuna) / धनधारी (Kubera) / अगिनि (fire) / काल (time) / जम (Yama) / सब (all) / अधिकारी (powerful ones)
ramacharitamanas::1000.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1000.essence: Pride keeps searching for rivals because it can never feel enough.
ramacharitamanas::1000.simple_meaning: Ravana, swollen with battle pride, roams everywhere looking for an equal opponent and finds none. Even the great cosmic powers are named as his peers in strength.
ramacharitamanas::1000.simple_insight: Pride makes a person feel untouchable, but it also leaves them empty and restless.
ramacharitamanas::1000.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already shaken the world, and the narration keeps building his menace. He storms around like a maddened elephant, hunting for someone who can match him, while even the great powers of the universe are listed to show the scale of his arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::1000.modern_relevance: Someone wins one argument and starts scanning every room for a challenge, hungry to prove they are unbeatable. The louder the ego gets, the less it can actually rest.
ramacharitamanas::1000.insight: It shifts the mind from admiring brute force to seeing how ego drives endless escalation.

ramacharitamanas::1001.verse_sanskrit: किंनर सिद्ध मनुज सुर नागा। हठि सबही के पंथहिं लागा॥ ब्रह्मसृष्टि जहँ लगि तनुधारी। दसमुख बसबर्ती नर नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1001.verse_hindi: किन्नर, सिद्ध, मनुष्य, देवता और नाग- सभी के पीछे वह हठपूर्वक पड़ गया (किसी को भी उसने शांतिपूर्वक नहीं बैठने दिया)। ब्रह्माजी की सृष्टि में जहाँ तक शरीरधारी स्त्री-पुरुष थे, सभी रावण के अधीन हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1001.english_translation: He relentlessly attacked kinnaras, siddhas, humans, gods, and serpents. Wherever Brahma's creation had embodied beings, men and women everywhere came under Ravana's control.
ramacharitamanas::1001.translation_literal: किंनर (kinnaras) / सिद्ध (accomplished beings) / मनुज (humans) / सुर (radiant beings) / नागा (serpents) / हठि (with force, stubbornly) / सबही (all) / के पंथहिं (on the path of) / लागा (attacked, fell upon) / ब्रह्मसृष्टि (Brahma's creation) / जहँ लगि (as far as) / तनुधारी (embodied beings) / दसमुख (ten-faced one, Ravana) / बसबर्ती (under control) / नर (men) / नारी (women)
ramacharitamanas::1001.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1001.essence: Power without restraint turns every world into a captive.
ramacharitamanas::1001.simple_meaning: Ravana used force against every kind of being and brought all embodied beings under his control.
ramacharitamanas::1001.simple_insight: Unchecked power spreads until nothing around it feels safe.
ramacharitamanas::1001.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already been shown raging through the worlds, seeking an equal and finding none. Now the scale of his domination is named: every class of being, and every embodied creature in creation, has been pressed beneath his will. The scene prepares the fear that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1001.modern_relevance: A powerful person in a workplace, family, or online space keeps pushing until everyone starts adjusting their tone, their choices, even their silence. The harm is not one blow — it is the climate of fear.
ramacharitamanas::1001.insight: It frames domination as a spreading force that bends whole communities, not just individuals.

ramacharitamanas::1002.verse_sanskrit: आयसु करहिं सकल भयभीता। नवहिं आइ नित चरन बिनीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1002.verse_hindi: डर के मारे सभी उसकी आज्ञा का पालन करते थे और नित्य आकर नम्रतापूर्वक उसके चरणों में सिर नवाते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1002.english_translation: All, terrified, obeyed his command and came daily to bow at his feet with humility.
ramacharitamanas::1002.translation_literal: आयसु (command) / करहिं (they do) / सकल (all) / भयभीता (fearful) / नवहिं (they bow) / आइ (coming) / नित (daily) / चरन (feet) / बिनीता (humble)
ramacharitamanas::1002.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1002.essence: Fear can force obedience, but it cannot create rightful respect.
ramacharitamanas::1002.simple_meaning: Everyone lived under Ravana's fear. They obeyed him and came daily to bow before him.
ramacharitamanas::1002.simple_insight: Power built on fear makes even respect feel forced.
ramacharitamanas::1002.detailed_meaning: Ravana has already been shown roaming the worlds in pride, seeking rivals and dominating every realm. This line shows the result: terrified beings obey him and bow before him daily. It sets up the larger claim that his rule rests on fear, not rightful order.
ramacharitamanas::1002.modern_relevance: A team keeps nodding in a meeting because one person always explodes when challenged. The room looks orderly, but the silence is fear, not respect.
ramacharitamanas::1002.insight: It exposes domination as a false kind of authority that silences others instead of earning trust.

ramacharitamanas::1003.verse_sanskrit: भुजबल बिस्व बस्य करि राखेसि कोउ न सुतंत्र। मंडलीक मनि रावन राज करइ निज मंत्र ॥
ramacharitamanas::1003.verse_hindi: उसने भुजाओं के बल से सारे विश्व को वश में कर लिया, किसी को स्वतंत्र नहीं रहने दिया। (इस प्रकार) मंडलीक राजाओं का शिरोमणि (सार्वभौम सम्राट) रावण अपनी इच्छानुसार राज्य करने लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1003.english_translation: He subdued the whole world by the strength of his arms and left no one free. Thus Ravana, the jewel among subordinate kings, ruled by his own command.
ramacharitamanas::1003.translation_literal: भुजबल (by arm-strength) / बिस्व (world) / बस्य (subdued) / करि (having done) / राखेसि (kept) / कोउ (anyone) / न (not) / सुतंत्र (free) / मंडलीक (subordinate kings) / मनि (jewel) / रावन (Ravana) / राज (rule) / करइ (does) / निज (own) / मंत्र (command)
ramacharitamanas::1003.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1003.essence: Dominion without restraint leaves no one free.
ramacharitamanas::1003.simple_meaning: Ravana conquered the world through force and kept everyone under his control. He ruled like the foremost king among lesser rulers.
ramacharitamanas::1003.simple_insight: Power without restraint turns into domination.
ramacharitamanas::1003.detailed_meaning: The narration is describing Ravana’s reach before the larger conflict begins. He has bent rulers and beings alike to his will, so that no one can act freely. This is part of the setup for why his pride has become unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::1003.modern_relevance: A boss who controls every decision in the room, checks every message, and leaves no room for initiative is living this verse in a modern form.
ramacharitamanas::1003.insight: It frames unchecked power as captivity, not greatness.

ramacharitamanas::1004.verse_sanskrit: देव जच्छ गंधर्ब नर किंनर नाग कुमारि। जीति बरीं निज बाहु बल बहु सुंदर बर नारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1004.verse_hindi: देवता, यक्ष, गंधर्व, मनुष्य, किन्नर और नागों की कन्याओं तथा बहुत सी अन्य सुंदरी और उत्तम स्त्रियों को उसने अपनी भुजाओं के बल से जीतकर ब्याह लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1004.english_translation: He won and married many beautiful women: daughters of devas, yakshas, gandharvas, humans, kinnaras, and nagas, by the strength of his arms.
ramacharitamanas::1004.translation_literal: देव (devas) / जच्छ (yakshas) / गंधर्ब (gandharvas) / नर (humans) / किंनर (kinnaras) / नाग (nagas) / कुमारि (maidens) / जीति (having conquered) / बरीं (he married) / निज (his own) / बाहु बल (arm-strength) / बहु (many) / सुंदर (beautiful) / बर (excellent) / नारि (women)
ramacharitamanas::1004.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1004.simple_meaning: Ravana used his power to conquer and marry many beautiful women from many kinds of beings.
ramacharitamanas::1004.simple_insight: Power without restraint turns people into trophies.
ramacharitamanas::1004.detailed_meaning: The narration is describing Ravana’s rise in Lanka. After subduing the world, he takes many women by force and pride. This verse adds to his image of domination, not wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::1004.modern_relevance: A powerful man boasts about every conquest as if possession proves worth. The applause is loud, but the emptiness behind it grows louder.
ramacharitamanas::1004.insight: It shows how domination expands greed instead of satisfaction.

ramacharitamanas::1005.verse_sanskrit: इंद्रजीत सन जो कछु कहेऊ। सो सब जनु पहिलेहिं करि रहेऊ॥ प्रथमहिं जिन्ह कहुँ आयसु दीन्हा। तिन्ह कर चरित सुनहु जो कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1005.verse_hindi: मेघनाद से उसने जो कुछ कहा, उसे उसने (मेघनाद ने) मानो पहले से ही कर रखा था (अर्थात् रावण के कहने भर की देर थी, उसने आज्ञापालन में तनिक भी देर नहीं की।) जिनको (रावण ने मेघनाद से) पहले ही आज्ञा दे रखी थी, उन्होंने जो करतूतें की उन्हें सुनो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1005.english_translation: Whatever he said to Indrajit, Indrajit had already done. Those who had been given orders earlier, listen to the deeds they carried out.
ramacharitamanas::1005.translation_literal: इंद्रजीत (Indrajit) / सन (with) / जो (whatever) / कछु (anything) / कहेऊ (said) / सो (that) / सब (all) / जनु (as if) / पहिलेहिं (already) / करि (having done) / रहेऊ (remained)॥ प्रथमहिं (earlier) / जिन्ह (those who) / कहुँ (to whom) / आयसु (order) / दीन्हा (gave) / तिन्ह (they) / कर (their) / चरित (deeds) / सुनहु (listen) / जो (which) / कीन्हा (did)॥
ramacharitamanas::1005.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1005.essence: Instant obedience becomes dangerous when the will behind it is corrupt.
ramacharitamanas::1005.simple_meaning: Ravana's commands were followed immediately. His officers had already carried out the tasks he mentioned, so the poem now turns to describe their actions.
ramacharitamanas::1005.simple_insight: Efficient obedience can also serve destruction. Speed means little when it is used without restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1005.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana's court is being shown as tightly controlled and fiercely active. Indrajit and the other commanders act the moment Ravana speaks, and the next lines begin listing the terrifying deeds of these forces. The verse is a transition, not the main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1005.modern_relevance: A manager sends one message and the whole team moves instantly, but the project itself is cruel or reckless. Fast execution is not the same as wise direction.
ramacharitamanas::1005.insight: It frames obedience as a tool: the same discipline that can build order can also amplify harm.

ramacharitamanas::1006.verse_sanskrit: देखत भीमरूप सब पापी। निसिचर निकर देव परितापी॥ करहिं उपद्रव असुर निकाया। नाना रूप धरहिं करि माया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1006.verse_hindi: सब राक्षसों के समूह देखने में बड़े भयानक, पापी और देवताओं को दुःख देने वाले थे। वे असुरों के समूह उपद्रव करते थे और माया से अनेकों प्रकार के रूप धरते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1006.english_translation: Seeing their terrible forms, all were sinners. The host of night-wanderers tormented the radiant beings. The demon ranks caused havoc and took many forms through illusion.
ramacharitamanas::1006.translation_literal: देखत (seeing) / भीमरूप (terrible forms) / सब (all) / पापी (sinners) / निसिचर (night-wanderers / demons) / निकर (host) / देव (radiant beings) / परितापी (tormenting) ॥ / करहिं (they do) / उपद्रव (havoc) / असुर (demons) / निकाया (ranks / groups) / नाना (many) / रूप (forms) / धरहिं (assume) / करि (by doing) / माया (illusion) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1006.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1006.essence: Many disguises can still hide one destructive intent.
ramacharitamanas::1006.simple_meaning: The demons were frightening, violent, and deceptive. They caused trouble and used illusion to change their forms.
ramacharitamanas::1006.simple_insight: Evil often looks many-faced, but its pattern is still the same.
ramacharitamanas::1006.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Tulsidas pauses over Ravana's world: the demon hosts are fearsome, cruel, and skilled at deception. This verse is not the lesson itself, but a vivid description that prepares the ground for the next line, where their actions are judged against dharma.
ramacharitamanas::1006.modern_relevance: A room full of fake profiles, burner accounts, and polished lies can feel overwhelming. The verse names that kind of chaos: many masks, one harmful intent.
ramacharitamanas::1006.insight: It trains the mind to see through changing appearances and notice the recurring pattern underneath.

ramacharitamanas::1007.verse_sanskrit: जेहि बिधि होइ धर्म निर्मूला। सो सब करहिं बेद प्रतिकूला॥ जेहिं जेहिं देस धेनु द्विज पावहिं। नगर गाउँ पुर आगि लगावहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1007.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार धर्म की जड़ कटे, वे वही सब वेदविरुद्ध काम करते थे। जिस-जिस स्थान में वे गो और ब्राह्मणों को पाते थे, उसी नगर, गाँव और पुरवे में आग लगा देते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1007.english_translation: Where the roots of dharma were cut, they acted against the Vedas. Wherever they found cows and learned priests, they set fire to towns, villages, and cities.
ramacharitamanas::1007.translation_literal: जेहि बिधि (in whatever way) / होइ (becomes) / धर्म (dharma) / निर्मूला (rootless, uprooted) / सो (that) / सब (all) / करहिं (do) / बेद (the Vedas) / प्रतिकूला (opposed to) ॥ / जेहिं जेहिं (wherever) / देस (place, country) / धेनु (cow) / द्विज (learned priest) / पावहिं (they find) / नगर (town) / गाउँ (village) / पुर (city) / आगि (fire) / लगावहिं (they set)
ramacharitamanas::1007.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1007.essence: When reverence dies, violence spreads everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::1007.simple_meaning: These beings opposed dharma and the Vedas. Wherever they found cows or learned priests, they burned the place.
ramacharitamanas::1007.simple_insight: Cruelty is not random here; it is a complete rejection of order, reverence, and restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1007.detailed_meaning: The narration describes Ravana’s side in Lanka: violent beings who hate dharma, ignore the Vedas, and attack sacred life wherever they find it. The verse is one step in a larger portrait of their corruption and terror.
ramacharitamanas::1007.modern_relevance: A mob arrives in a neighborhood and targets the temple, the school, and the people who keep the place steady. The point is not chaos alone, but contempt for every form of moral order.
ramacharitamanas::1007.insight: It teaches you to recognize when destruction is aimed at the roots, not just the surface.

ramacharitamanas::1008.verse_sanskrit: सुभ आचरन कतहुँ नहिं होई। देव बिप्र गुरु मान न कोई॥ नहिं हरिभगति जग्य तप ग्याना। सपनेहु सुनिअ न बेद पुराना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1008.verse_hindi: (उनके डर से) कहीं भी शुभ आचरण (ब्राह्मण भोजन, यज्ञ, श्राद्ध आदि) नहीं होते थे। देवता, ब्राह्मण और गुरु को कोई नहीं मानता था। न हरिभक्ति थी, न यज्ञ, तप और ज्ञान था। वेद और पुराण तो स्वप्न में भी सुनने को नहीं मिलते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1008.english_translation: No auspicious conduct happened anywhere. No one honored the gods, priests, or teachers. There was no devotion to Hari, no sacrifice, no austerity, no wisdom. Even the old Vedas and Puranas were unheard of in dreams.
ramacharitamanas::1008.translation_literal: सुभ (auspicious) / आचरन (conduct) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / नहिं (not) / होई (was) / देव (deities) / बिप्र (priests) / गुरु (teacher) / मान (respect) / न (not) / कोई (anyone) / नहिं (not) / हरिभगति (devotion to Hari) / जग्य (sacrifice) / तप (austerity) / ग्याना (wisdom) / सपनेहु (even in dream) / सुनिअ (heard) / न (not) / बेद (Vedas) / पुराना (Puranas)
ramacharitamanas::1008.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1008.essence: Ego-driven rule does not just harm people; it wipes out the habits of goodness.
ramacharitamanas::1008.simple_meaning: Ravana's rule had destroyed every sign of goodness. Respect, devotion, sacrifice, discipline, and learning had all disappeared.
ramacharitamanas::1008.simple_insight: A corrupt environment does not stay neutral; it erases the habits that keep people human.
ramacharitamanas::1008.detailed_meaning: The poem is describing Lanka under Ravana's fear. His power has made people abandon sacred conduct, respect for teachers, devotion, sacrifice, and study. It is a supporting detail that shows how deeply his rule has broken dharma.
ramacharitamanas::1008.modern_relevance: A workplace where everyone cuts corners slowly teaches you to stop caring about standards. Soon, even basic respect, honesty, and learning feel unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::1008.insight: It shows how a poisonous leader reshapes an entire culture by normalizing disregard.

ramacharitamanas::1009.verse_sanskrit: जप जोग बिरागा तप मख भागा श्रवन सुनइ दससीसा। आपुनु उठि धावइ रहै न पावइ धरि सब घालइ खीसा॥ अस भ्रष्ट अचारा भा संसारा धर्म सुनिअ नहिं काना। तेहि बहुबिधि त्रासइ देस निकासइ जो कह बेद पुराना॥
ramacharitamanas::1009.verse_hindi: जप, योग, वैराग्य, तप तथा यज्ञ में (देवताओं के) भाग पाने की बात रावण कहीं कानों से सुन पाता, तो (उसी समय) स्वयं उठ दौड़ता। कुछ भी रहने नहीं पाता, वह सबको पकड़कर विध्वंस कर डालता था। संसार में ऐसा भ्रष्ट आचरण फैल गया कि धर्म तो कानों में सुनने में नहीं आता था, जो कोई वेद और पुराण कहता, उसको बहुत तरह से त्रास देता और देश से निकाल देता था।
ramacharitamanas::1009.english_translation: If Ravana heard even a mention of japa, yoga, detachment, austerity, or sacrifice, he would leap up and destroy it all. Such corruption spread through the world that people could not even hear the word dharma; whoever spoke of the Vedas and Puranas was threatened and driven from the land.
ramacharitamanas::1009.translation_literal: जप (recitation) / जोग (yoga) / बिरागा (detachment) / तप (austerity) / मख (sacrifice) / भागा (share) / श्रवन (hearing) / सुनइ (hears) / दससीसा (ten-headed one) / आपुनु (himself) / उठि (rising) / धावइ (runs) / रहै (remain) / न (not) / पावइ (gets) / धरि (grabs) / सब (all) / घालइ (destroys) / खीसा (purse, possessions) / अस (such) / भ्रष्ट (corrupt) / अचारा (conduct) / भा (became) / संसारा (world) / धर्म (dharma) / सुनिअ (heard) / नहिं (not) / काना (ear) / तेहि (that) / बहुबिधि (many ways) / त्रासइ (frightens, troubles) / देस (country) / निकासइ (drives out) / जो (whoever) / कह (speaks) / बेद (Vedas) / पुराना (Puranas)
ramacharitamanas::1009.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1009.essence: Ego destroys goodness by making even its name unwelcome.
ramacharitamanas::1009.simple_meaning: Ravana cannot tolerate any trace of spiritual practice or right conduct. He attacks it wherever he finds it, and his rule makes even the word dharma unsafe to speak.
ramacharitamanas::1009.simple_insight: A corrupt mind does not just ignore goodness; it tries to erase it from public life.
ramacharitamanas::1009.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, Tulsidas describes Ravana's reign as a world turned upside down. Even hearing about discipline, detachment, or sacrifice makes him lash out. The verse shows how fear and ego spread until dharma itself becomes dangerous to mention.
ramacharitamanas::1009.modern_relevance: A workplace where honesty gets mocked, a family where kindness is treated as weakness, a group chat where decency is laughed out of the room — corruption rarely stays private. It tries to silence the very language of integrity.
ramacharitamanas::1009.insight: It trains the mind to recognize how ego attacks virtue first by suppressing speech, then by normalizing harm.

ramacharitamanas::1010.verse_sanskrit: बरनि न जाइ अनीति घोर निसाचर जो करहिं। हिंसा पर अति प्रीति तिन्ह के पापहि कवनि मिति ॥
ramacharitamanas::1010.verse_hindi: राक्षस लोग जो घोर अत्याचार करते थे, उसका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। हिंसा पर ही जिनकी प्रीति है, उनके पापों का क्या ठिकाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1010.english_translation: The cruel acts of the night-wandering beings cannot be described. Their love for violence has no measure.
ramacharitamanas::1010.translation_literal: बरनि न जाइ (cannot be described) / अनीति घोर (terrible injustice) / निसाचर (night-wandering beings) / जो करहिं (who do) / हिंसा (violence) / पर (for) / अति प्रीति (great love) / तिन्ह के (of those) / पापहि (sins) / कवनि मिति (what measure)
ramacharitamanas::1010.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1010.essence: When violence becomes beloved, wrongdoing loses all limit.
ramacharitamanas::1010.simple_meaning: The cruelty of the demons was beyond description. They loved violence so much that no limit could be placed on their wrongdoing.
ramacharitamanas::1010.simple_insight: Some harm becomes so habitual that it seems to erase all restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1010.detailed_meaning: The narration pauses to show how far Lanka has fallen under Ravana's rule. The night-wandering beings are not merely flawed; they are steeped in cruelty, and the next verse expands that social collapse into everyday vice.
ramacharitamanas::1010.modern_relevance: A workplace where bullying is shrugged off, a family where cruelty has become normal, a group chat where humiliation feels routine — violence grows when no one names it clearly.
ramacharitamanas::1010.insight: It shifts attention from isolated bad acts to a culture that rewards harm.

ramacharitamanas::1011.verse_sanskrit: बाढ़े खल बहु चोर जुआरा। जे लंपट परधन परदारा॥ मानहिं मातु पिता नहिं देवा। साधुन्ह सन करवावहिं सेवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1011.verse_hindi: पराए धन और पराई स्त्री पर मन चलाने वाले, दुष्ट, चोर और जुआरी बहुत बढ़ गए। लोग माता-पिता और देवताओं को नहीं मानते थे और साधुओं (की सेवा करना तो दूर रहा, उल्टे उन) से सेवा करवाते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1011.english_translation: Adulterers, thieves, gamblers, and the wicked multiplied. People no longer honored parents or the divine, and they made the holy serve them.
ramacharitamanas::1011.translation_literal: बाढ़े (increased) / खल (the wicked) / बहु (many) / चोर (thieves) / जुआरा (gamblers)। / जे (those who) / लंपट (debauched) / परधन (another's wealth) / परदारा (another's woman)॥ / मानहिं (honour) / मातु पिता (mother and father) / नहिं (not) / देवा (the divine) / सेवा (service)। / साधुन्ह (holy ones) / सन (from) / करवावहिं (make done) / सेवा (service)॥
ramacharitamanas::1011.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1011.essence: When greed rules, even reverence gets inverted.
ramacharitamanas::1011.simple_meaning: Corruption has spread so far that people chase others' wealth and partners, ignore parents and the divine, and even force holy people to serve them.
ramacharitamanas::1011.simple_insight: A society falls apart first in small acts of disrespect and greed.
ramacharitamanas::1011.detailed_meaning: In the opening Balkand description of the age of disorder, Tulsidas shows a world turned upside down. Thieves, gamblers, and the lustful multiply, family respect disappears, and holy people are no longer honoured. This sets up the need for Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::1011.modern_relevance: A group chat turns cruel, gossip spreads, and the person who tries to stay decent gets mocked for being naive. That reversal is exactly what this verse warns about.
ramacharitamanas::1011.insight: It shifts attention from private vice to social collapse: when greed and disrespect become normal, disorder spreads everywhere.

ramacharitamanas::1012.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह के यह आचरन भवानी। ते जानेहु निसिचर सब प्रानी॥ अतिसय देखि धर्म कै ग्लानी। परम सभीत धरा अकुलानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1012.verse_hindi: (श्री शिवजी कहते हैं कि-) हे भवानी! जिनके ऐसे आचरण हैं, उन सब प्राणियों को राक्षस ही समझना। इस प्रकार धर्म के प्रति (लोगों की) अतिशय ग्लानि (अरुचि, अनास्था) देखकर पृथ्वी अत्यन्त भयभीत एवं व्याकुल हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1012.english_translation: O Bhavani, understand all such beings as demons. Seeing such deep contempt for dharma, the earth grew utterly afraid and restless.
ramacharitamanas::1012.translation_literal: जिन्ह (those who) / के (whose) / यह (this) / आचरन (conduct) / भवानी (Bhavani) / ते (they) / जानेहु (know) / निसिचर (demons) / सब (all) / प्रानी (beings) ॥ अतिसय (extreme) / देखि (seeing) / धर्म (dharma) / कै (of) / ग्लानी (disdain) / परम (utterly) / सभीत (afraid) / धरा (earth) / अकुलानी (restless, distressed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1012.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::1012.essence: A society that mocks dharma turns human beings into demons.
ramacharitamanas::1012.simple_meaning: When people lose all respect for dharma and behave cruelly, they become like demons. The earth itself is shaken by that corruption.
ramacharitamanas::1012.simple_insight: Cruel habits do not stay private; they warp the whole atmosphere around them.
ramacharitamanas::1012.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati in the Balkand, describing the age of moral collapse before Ram's birth. After naming the greed and lawlessness spreading everywhere, he says such beings are no better than demons, and even the earth trembles under their contempt for dharma.
ramacharitamanas::1012.modern_relevance: A workplace where lying is normal, cruelty is rewarded, and everyone shrugs at it starts to feel poisonous. This verse names that decay before it becomes everyone’s new normal.
ramacharitamanas::1012.insight: It shifts attention from isolated bad acts to the social damage caused when respect for right conduct disappears.

ramacharitamanas::1013.verse_sanskrit: गिरि सरि सिंधु भार नहिं मोही। जस मोहि गरुअ एक परद्रोही। सकल धर्म देखइ बिपरीता। कहि न सकइ रावन भय भीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1013.verse_hindi: (वह सोचने लगी कि) पर्वतों, नदियों और समुद्रों का बोझ मुझे इतना भारी नहीं जान पड़ता, जितना भारी मुझे एक परद्रोही (दूसरों का अनिष्ट करने वाला) लगता है। पृथ्वी सारे धर्मों को विपरीत देख रही है, पर रावण से भयभीत हुई वह कुछ बोल नहीं सकती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1013.english_translation: The burden of mountains, rivers, and oceans does not trouble me. One traitor weighs heavier than all of them. The world has turned against every righteous way, and Earth cannot speak because Ravana frightens her.
ramacharitamanas::1013.translation_literal: गिरि (mountains) / सरि (rivers) / सिंधु (ocean) / भार (burden) / नहिं (not) / मोही (to me) / जस (as) / मोहि (to me) / गरुअ (heavy) / एक (one) / परद्रोही (traitor) / सकल (all) / धर्म (righteous ways) / देखइ (sees) / बिपरीता (reversed) / कहि (to say) / न सकइ (cannot) / रावन (Ravana) / भय (fear) / भीता (frightened)
ramacharitamanas::1013.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1013.essence: One corrupt presence can outweigh the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::1013.simple_meaning: Earth feels the weight of Ravana's wrongdoing more than the weight of mountains or oceans. His presence has reversed right conduct, and fear keeps her silent.
ramacharitamanas::1013.simple_insight: Some burdens are moral, not physical. A corrupt presence can feel heavier than the world itself.
ramacharitamanas::1013.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, the world has fallen out of order under Ravana's rule. Earth feels crushed not by stone or sea, but by the weight of one wrongdoer. She sees dharma overturned, yet fear leaves her unable to protest.
ramacharitamanas::1013.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where one person’s cruelty changes the air. No one names it, but everyone feels it. That heaviness is what this verse captures.
ramacharitamanas::1013.insight: It shifts attention from physical strain to the moral weight a harmful person can impose on everyone around them.

ramacharitamanas::1014.verse_sanskrit: धेनु रूप धरि हृदयँ बिचारी। गई तहाँ जहँ सुर मुनि झारी॥ निज संताप सुनाएसि रोई। काहू तें कछु काज न होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1014.verse_hindi: (अंत में) हृदय में सोच-विचारकर, गो का रूप धारण कर धरती वहाँ गई, जहाँ सब देवता और मुनि (छिपे) थे। पृथ्वी ने रोककर उनको अपना दुःख सुनाया, पर किसी से कुछ काम न बना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1014.english_translation: Thinking deeply in her heart, Earth took the form of a cow and went to the place where the gods and sages were hidden. She told them her suffering with tears, but nothing came of it.
ramacharitamanas::1014.translation_literal: धेनु रूप (cow-form) / धरि (having taken) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारी (having thought) / गई (went) / तहाँ (there) / जहँ (where) / सुर (gods) / मुनि (sages) / झारी (hidden group)॥ / निज (own) / संताप (sorrow) / सुनाएसि (told) / रोई (weeping) / काहू तें (from anyone) / कछु (some) / काज (work/help) / न होई (did not happen) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1014.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1014.essence: Despair becomes visible before help can arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1014.simple_meaning: Earth takes the form of a cow, seeks out the hidden gods and sages, and cries out her suffering. No one can help her.
ramacharitamanas::1014.simple_insight: Some burdens are so large that even pleading for help brings no relief.
ramacharitamanas::1014.detailed_meaning: Earth, overwhelmed by the burden of evil, thinks it over and takes the form of a cow. She goes to the hidden gods and sages and weeps out her pain. This is part of the larger appeal for help before Ram's descent.
ramacharitamanas::1014.modern_relevance: You’ve tried every group chat, every expert, every workaround, and the problem is still there. Sometimes the first honest act is simply naming the burden aloud.
ramacharitamanas::1014.insight: It frames suffering as something to be named clearly before rescue can begin.

ramacharitamanas::1015.verse_sanskrit: सुर मुनि गंधर्बा मिलि करि सर्बा गे बिरंचि के लोका। सँग गोतनुधारी भूमि बिचारी परम बिकल भय सोका॥ ब्रह्माँ सब जाना मन अनुमाना मोर कछू न बसाई। जा करि तैं दासी सो अबिनासी हमरेउ तोर सहाई॥
ramacharitamanas::1015.verse_hindi: तब देवता, मुनि और गंधर्व सब मिलकर ब्रह्माजी के लोक (सत्यलोक) को गए। भय और शोक से अत्यन्त व्याकुल बेचारी पृथ्वी भी गो का शरीर धारण किए हुए उनके साथ थी। ब्रह्माजी सब जान गए। उन्होंने मन में अनुमान किया कि इसमें मेरा कुछ भी वश नहीं चलने का। (तब उन्होंने पृथ्वी से कहा कि-) जिसकी तू दासी है, वही अविनाशी हमारा और तुम्हारा दोनों का सहायक है॥
ramacharitamanas::1015.english_translation: Then the gods, sages, and celestial singers all went together to Brahma's realm. Earth, in the form of a cow, went with them, overwhelmed by fear and sorrow. Brahma understood everything and reflected, "I have no power in this matter. The one you serve is the imperishable support of us both."
ramacharitamanas::1015.translation_literal: सुर (gods) / मुनि (sages) / गंधर्बा (celestial singers) / मिलि करि (having come together) / सर्बा (all) / गे (went) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / के लोका (to the realm) / सँग (with) / गोतनुधारी (cow-formed) / भूमि (Earth) / बिचारी (poor one) / परम (utterly) / बिकल (distressed) / भय (fear) / सोका (sorrow) / ब्रह्माँ (Brahma) / सब (everything) / जाना (knew) / मन (mind) / अनुमाना (concluded) / मोर (my) / कछू (anything) / न (not) / बसाई (in control) / जा (whose) / करि (having become) / तैं (you) / दासी (servant) / सो (that one) / अबिनासी (imperishable) / हमरेउ (our) / तोर (your) / सहाई (helper)
ramacharitamanas::1015.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1015.essence: Power ends where true support begins.
ramacharitamanas::1015.simple_meaning: The gods, sages, and Earth go to Brahma because the world is in distress. Brahma sees that he cannot solve it himself and points Earth toward the imperishable support beyond him.
ramacharitamanas::1015.simple_insight: When your own power ends, clarity begins. Real help starts by knowing who can actually carry the weight.
ramacharitamanas::1015.detailed_meaning: Earth, crushed by Ravana's burden, reaches Brahma's realm with the gods and sages. Brahma sees the limits of his own power and turns her toward the imperishable support who can end the crisis. This verse moves the story from complaint to divine intervention.
ramacharitamanas::1015.modern_relevance: A team meeting runs in circles while everyone waits for one person to fix a problem no one can solve. The honest moment is not louder effort — it's recognising where real authority and help actually lie.
ramacharitamanas::1015.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance in impossible situations to seeking the one source that can truly resolve them.

ramacharitamanas::1016.verse_sanskrit: धरनि धरहि मन धीर कह बिरंचि हरि पद सुमिरु। जानत जन की पीर प्रभु भंजिहि दारुन बिपति ॥
ramacharitamanas::1016.verse_hindi: ब्रह्माजी ने कहा- हे धरती! मन में धीरज धारण करके श्री हरि के चरणों का स्मरण करो। प्रभु अपने दासों की पीड़ा को जानते हैं, वे तुम्हारी कठिन विपत्ति का नाश करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1016.english_translation: Brahma said, “O Earth, hold your mind steady and remember Hari’s feet. The Lord knows the pain of his servants; he will end this terrible distress.”
ramacharitamanas::1016.translation_literal: धरनि (Earth) / धरहि (hold) / मन (mind) / धीर (steady) / कह (said) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / हरि (Hari) / पद (feet) / सुमिरु (remember) / जानत (knowing) / जन (servants) / की (of) / पीर (pain) / प्रभु (Lord) / भंजिहि (will destroy) / दारुन (terrible) / बिपति (distress)
ramacharitamanas::1016.speaker: Brahma
ramacharitamanas::1016.essence: Steady trust meets a Lord who already knows the pain.
ramacharitamanas::1016.simple_meaning: Brahma tells Earth to stay calm and remember Ram. Ram knows the suffering of his devotees and will remove the crisis.
ramacharitamanas::1016.simple_insight: You are not pleading into emptiness. The divine already sees the hurt and answers it.
ramacharitamanas::1016.detailed_meaning: Earth has gone in distress to Brahma, surrounded by the gods and sages. Brahma tells her not to panic, but to remember Hari, because Ram knows the pain of those who rely on him and will end the crisis.
ramacharitamanas::1016.modern_relevance: You are staring at a message that changes nothing yet, and your chest is tight. A wiser voice says: stay steady, remember what you trust, and do not assume you are unheard.
ramacharitamanas::1016.insight: It shifts the mind from panic to trust, and from private suffering to being held in Ram’s awareness.

ramacharitamanas::1017.verse_sanskrit: बैठे सुर सब करहिं बिचारा। कहँ पाइअ प्रभु करिअ पुकारा॥ पुर बैकुंठ जान कह कोई। कोउ कह पयनिधि बस प्रभु सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1017.verse_hindi: सब देवता बैठकर विचार करने लगे कि प्रभु को कहाँ पावें ताकि उनके सामने पुकार (फरियाद) करें। कोई बैकुंठपुरी जाने को कहता था और कोई कहता था कि वही प्रभु क्षीरसमुद्र में निवास करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1017.english_translation: All the devas sat and debated where to find the Lord so they could call out to Him. Some said He could be found in Vaikuntha; others said He dwells in the ocean of milk.
ramacharitamanas::1017.translation_literal: बैठे (sat) / सुर (devas) / सब (all) / करहिं (do) / बिचारा (deliberation) । / कहँ (where) / पाइअ (is found) / प्रभु (the Lord) / करिअ (should be made) / पुकारा (call) । / पुर (city) / बैकुंठ (Vaikuntha) / जान (know) / कह (says) / कोई (someone) । / कोउ (someone) / कह (says) / पयनिधि (ocean of milk) / बस (dwells) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सोई (that same)
ramacharitamanas::1017.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1017.essence: Searching for Ram begins with not knowing where He is.
ramacharitamanas::1017.simple_meaning: The devas are trying to figure out where to find Ram so they can pray to Him. Some think of Vaikuntha, others of the ocean of milk.
ramacharitamanas::1017.simple_insight: When you need help, the heart starts searching for the one place mercy can be reached.
ramacharitamanas::1017.detailed_meaning: The devas have gone to Brahma’s realm in distress over Earth’s suffering. Now they sit and debate where to find Ram, wondering whether He can be reached in Vaikuntha or in the ocean of milk. The verse shows their uncertainty before the deeper truth is revealed.
ramacharitamanas::1017.modern_relevance: You are desperate and start asking everyone the same question: where do I even go now? The mind keeps naming places, but what you really want is the one presence that can answer.
ramacharitamanas::1017.insight: It shifts the mind from ordinary location-thinking to seeking the presence that can actually respond.

ramacharitamanas::1018.verse_sanskrit: जाके हृदयँ भगति जसि प्रीती। प्रभु तहँ प्रगट सदा तेहिं रीती॥ तेहिं समाज गिरिजा मैं रहेऊँ। अवसर पाइ बचन एक कहेउँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1018.verse_hindi: जिसके हृदय में जैसी भक्ति और प्रीति होती है, प्रभु वहाँ (उसके लिए) सदा उसी रीति से प्रकट होते हैं। हे पार्वती! उस समाज में मैं भी था। अवसर पाकर मैंने एक बात कही- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1018.english_translation: Wherever there is devotion and love in the heart, the divine appears there in that very way. Parvati, I was also in that gathering. I took the chance to say one thing.
ramacharitamanas::1018.translation_literal: जाके (whose) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / भगति (devotion) / जसि (as much as) / प्रीती (love) / प्रभु (the divine / Lord) / तहँ (there) / प्रगट (manifest) / सदा (always) / तेहिं रीती (in that manner) / तेहिं (in that) / समाज (assembly) / गिरिजा (Parvati) / मैं (I) / रहेऊँ (was) / अवसर (opportunity) / पाइ (having found) / बचन (words) / एक (one) / कहेउँ (I said)
ramacharitamanas::1018.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::1018.essence: Devotion shapes the form in which the divine appears.
ramacharitamanas::1018.simple_meaning: The divine appears to each person in the form their devotion and love can receive. Shiva says he was present in that gathering and spoke when the moment came.
ramacharitamanas::1018.simple_insight: Love changes what you are able to meet. The heart's shape determines the presence it can receive.
ramacharitamanas::1018.detailed_meaning: Parvati has asked where the Lord can be found. Shiva answers from the gathering of sages, saying that Ram appears according to the devotee's devotion and love. He then places himself in the scene, showing that this teaching came from lived witness, not theory.
ramacharitamanas::1018.modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed, and one person feels only fear while another feels held by grace. The same room can feel empty or full, depending on the heart that enters it.
ramacharitamanas::1018.insight: It shifts attention from searching outward to preparing the heart that can recognise presence.

ramacharitamanas::1019.verse_sanskrit: हरि ब्यापक सर्बत्र समाना। प्रेम तें प्रगट होहिं मैं जाना॥ देस काल दिसि बिदिसिहु माहीं। कहहु सो कहाँ जहाँ प्रभु नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1019.verse_hindi: मैं तो यह जानता हूँ कि भगवान सब जगह समान रूप से व्यापक हैं, प्रेम से वे प्रकट हो जाते हैं, देश, काल, दिशा, विदिशा में बताओ, ऐसी जगह कहाँ है, जहाँ प्रभु न हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1019.english_translation: I know the divine is equally present everywhere. They appear through love. Tell me: in which place, in which time, in which direction, is there anywhere the divine is not?
ramacharitamanas::1019.translation_literal: हरि (the divine) / ब्यापक (all-pervading) / सर्बत्र (everywhere) / समाना (equally) / प्रेम (love) / तें (through) / प्रगट (manifest) / होहिं (appear) / मैं (I) / जाना (know)॥ देस (place) / काल (time) / दिसि (direction) / बिदिसिहु (and intermediate directions too) / माहीं (within) / कहहु (tell) / सो (that) / कहाँ (where) / जहाँ (where) / प्रभु (the divine) / नाहीं (is not) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1019.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::1019.essence: Love does not create presence; it reveals what was always everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::1019.simple_meaning: The divine is present everywhere, and love is what makes that presence felt. There is no place, time, or direction where the divine is absent.
ramacharitamanas::1019.simple_insight: You do not need to search far away; love changes what you can perceive right here.
ramacharitamanas::1019.detailed_meaning: Shiva is answering Parvati in the opening frame of the Ramcharitmanas. After the gods wonder where to find Ram, he explains that Ram is everywhere already, but becomes visible through love. This verse deepens that claim into a universal vision.
ramacharitamanas::1019.modern_relevance: You are sitting in a crowded train, feeling alone, while your phone keeps buzzing with what you lack. This verse says presence is not missing; love is what lets you notice it.
ramacharitamanas::1019.insight: It shifts the mind from searching for a distant presence to recognising the sacred already here.

ramacharitamanas::1020.verse_sanskrit: अग जगमय सब रहित बिरागी। प्रेम तें प्रभु प्रगटइ जिमि आगी॥ मोर बचन सब के मन माना। साधु-साधु करि ब्रह्म बखाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1020.verse_hindi: वे चराचरमय (चराचर में व्याप्त) होते हुए ही सबसे रहित हैं और विरक्त हैं (उनकी कहीं आसक्ति नहीं है), वे प्रेम से प्रकट होते हैं, जैसे अग्नि। (अग्नि अव्यक्त रूप से सर्वत्र व्याप्त है, परन्तु जहाँ उसके लिए अरणिमन्थनादि साधन किए जाते हैं, वहाँ वह प्रकट होती है। इसी प्रकार सर्वत्र व्याप्त भगवान भी प्रेम से प्रकट होते हैं।) मेरी बात सबको प्रिय लगी। ब्रह्माजी ने 'साधु-साधु' कहकर बड़ाई की ॥
ramacharitamanas::1020.english_translation: Though present in all moving and unmoving things, the Lord is detached from all. The Lord appears through love, like fire. Everyone approved my words, and Brahma praised them with "Well said, well said."
ramacharitamanas::1020.translation_literal: अग जगमय (filled with moving and unmoving beings) / सब रहित (free from all) / बिरागी (detached) / प्रेम तें (through love) / प्रभु (the Lord) / प्रगटइ (appears) / जिमि (like) / आगी (fire) / मोर (my) / बचन (words) / सब के (of everyone) / मन (mind) / माना (accepted) / साधु-साधु (well said) / करि (saying) / ब्रह्म (Brahma) / बखाना (praised)
ramacharitamanas::1020.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::1020.essence: Love makes the ever-present Lord visible.
ramacharitamanas::1020.simple_meaning: The divine is present everywhere, yet remains unattached. Love is what makes that presence show itself, just as fire appears when kindled.
ramacharitamanas::1020.simple_insight: Love is not just a feeling; it is the condition that lets you recognize what was always there.
ramacharitamanas::1020.detailed_meaning: Shiva is still explaining to Parvati how Ram appears to devotees. He says Ram is present in all beings and beyond attachment, but love brings that hidden presence into view, like fire emerging from wood. Brahma hears this and approves it.
ramacharitamanas::1020.modern_relevance: You can sit beside someone who is deeply hurt and still miss what they need most. The moment you meet them with real love, something hidden in them finally comes forward.
ramacharitamanas::1020.insight: It shifts attention from searching outward for proof to creating the inner condition that allows recognition.

ramacharitamanas::1021.verse_sanskrit: सुनि बिरंचि मन हरष तन पुलकि नयन बह नीर। अस्तुति करत जोरि कर सावधान मतिधीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::1021.verse_hindi: मेरी बात सुनकर ब्रह्माजी के मन में बड़ा हर्ष हुआ, उनका तन पुलकित हो गया और नेत्रों से (प्रेम के) आँसू बहने लगे। तब वे धीरबुद्धि ब्रह्माजी सावधान होकर हाथ जोड़कर स्तुति करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1021.english_translation: Hearing this, Brahma felt great joy in his mind. His body thrilled, tears flowed from his eyes, and with steady intelligence he began to praise, hands joined in reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1021.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / मन (mind) / हरष (joy) / तन (body) / पुलकि (thrilled) / नयन (eyes) / बह (flow) / नीर (water/tears) / अस्तुति (praise) / करत (doing) / जोरि (joining) / कर (hands) / सावधान (alert) / मतिधीर (steady-minded)
ramacharitamanas::1021.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1021.essence: Truth that is truly seen turns into reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1021.simple_meaning: Brahma hears the truth, feels joy, and responds with tears and praise.
ramacharitamanas::1021.simple_insight: Real understanding often ends in reverence, not argument.
ramacharitamanas::1021.detailed_meaning: Brahma has just heard that the supreme presence is everywhere and yet appears through love. The words strike him deeply: his mind rejoices, his body trembles, and he lifts his joined hands to praise.
ramacharitamanas::1021.modern_relevance: You hear something so true that you stop defending your old view. Your chest loosens, your eyes sting, and gratitude replaces debate.
ramacharitamanas::1021.insight: It shifts the mind from analysis to humble praise when truth lands fully.

ramacharitamanas::1022.verse_sanskrit: जय जय सुरनायक जन सुखदायक प्रनतपाल भगवंता। गो द्विज हितकारी जय असुरारी सिंधुसुता प्रिय कंता॥ पालन सुर धरनी अद्भुत करनी मरम न जानइ कोई। जो सहज कृपाला दीनदयाला करउ अनुग्रह सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1022.verse_hindi: हे देवताओं के स्वामी, सेवकों को सुख देने वाले, शरणागत की रक्षा करने वाले भगवान! आपकी जय हो! जय हो!! हे गो-ब्राह्मणों का हित करने वाले, असुरों का विनाश करने वाले, समुद्र की कन्या (श्री लक्ष्मीजी) के प्रिय स्वामी! आपकी जय हो! हे देवता और पृथ्वी का पालन करने वाले! आपकी लीला अद्भुत है, उसका भेद कोई नहीं जानता। ऐसे जो स्वभाव से ही कृपालु और दीनदयालु हैं, वे ही हम पर कृपा करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1022.english_translation: Victory, victory to the Lord of the devas, the giver of joy to all people, the protector of those who seek refuge! Victory to you! Victory to you! O friend of the cows and the twice-born, destroyer of the asuras, beloved lord of the daughter of the sea! You sustain the devas and the earth; your acts are wondrous, and no one knows their secret. May that naturally compassionate, kind to the humble, show mercy to us.
ramacharitamanas::1022.translation_literal: जय (victory) / जय (victory) / सुरनायक (lord of the devas) / जन सुखदायक (giver of joy to people) / प्रनतपाल (protector of the surrendered) / भगवंता (O blessed Lord) । / गो द्विज हितकारी (benefactor of cows and twice-born) / जय (victory) / असुरारी (enemy of the asuras) / सिंधुसुता प्रिय कंता (beloved consort of the daughter of the sea) ॥ / पालन (sustaining) / सुर (devas) / धरनी (earth) / अद्भुत करनी (wondrous acts) / मरम (secret) / न जानइ (does not know) / कोई (anyone) । / जो (who) / सहज (by nature) / कृपाला (compassionate) / दीनदयाला (kind to the humble) / करउ (may do) / अनुग्रह (mercy) / सोई (that one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1022.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1022.essence: Ram's greatness is hidden, but his mercy is natural.
ramacharitamanas::1022.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the protector of the surrendered, the friend of all, and the destroyer of harmful forces. His actions are mysterious, but his nature is naturally compassionate.
ramacharitamanas::1022.simple_insight: You do not need to force mercy from Ram; compassion is already his nature.
ramacharitamanas::1022.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is in a devotional flow, piling up praise for Ram after Brahma’s reverent response. The verse names Ram as protector, sustainer, and beloved lord, then admits that his ways are beyond human grasp. The prayer ends by asking for mercy from his own nature of compassion.
ramacharitamanas::1022.modern_relevance: You are exhausted after trying to explain yourself to everyone, and one person still sees your struggle without needing a perfect story. This verse turns toward that kind of mercy: not earned, simply given.
ramacharitamanas::1022.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to decode Ram to trusting his compassion directly.

ramacharitamanas::1023.verse_sanskrit: जय जय अबिनासी सब घट बासी ब्यापक परमानंदा। अबिगत गोतीतं चरित पुनीतं मायारहित मुकुंदा॥ जेहि लागि बिरागी अति अनुरागी बिगत मोह मुनिबृंदा। निसि बासर ध्यावहिं गुन गन गावहिं जयति सच्चिदानंदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1023.verse_hindi: हे अविनाशी, सबके हृदय में निवास करने वाले (अन्तर्यामी), सर्वव्यापक, परम आनंदस्वरूप, अज्ञेय, इन्द्रियों से परे, पवित्र चरित्र, माया से रहित मुकुंद (मोक्षदाता)! आपकी जय हो! जय हो!! (इस लोक और परलोक के सब भोगों से) विरक्त तथा मोह से सर्वथा छूटे हुए (ज्ञानी) मुनिवृन्द भी अत्यन्त अनुरागी (प्रेमी) बनकर जिनका रात-दिन ध्यान करते हैं और जिनके गुणों के समूह का गान करते हैं, उन सच्चिदानंद की जय हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1023.english_translation: Victory, victory to the imperishable one who dwells in every heart, who is all-pervading bliss, beyond speech and beyond the senses, pure in conduct, free from illusion, and the giver of liberation. Even renunciates, freed from delusion, meditate on you day and night and sing your countless qualities.
ramacharitamanas::1023.translation_literal: जय जय (victory, victory) / अबिनासी (imperishable) / सब घट बासी (dwelling in all hearts) / ब्यापक (all-pervading) / परमानंदा (supreme bliss) / अबिगत (beyond speech) / गोतीतं (beyond the senses) / चरित (conduct) / पुनीतं (pure) / मायारहित (free from illusion) / मुकुंदा (Mukunda, giver of liberation) / जेहि लागि (for whom) / बिरागी (renunciates) / अति अनुरागी (deeply devoted) / बिगत मोह (free from delusion) / मुनिबृंदा (assemblies of sages) / निसि बासर (night and day) / ध्यावहिं (meditate) / गुन गन (groups of qualities) / गावहिं (sing) / जयति (victory) / सच्चिदानंदा (being-consciousness-bliss)
ramacharitamanas::1023.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1023.essence: The one beyond words becomes the heart's nearest love.
ramacharitamanas::1023.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond words and senses, yet present in every heart. He is pure, free from illusion, and the source of liberation. Even great sages who have let go of worldly desire still love and praise him constantly.
ramacharitamanas::1023.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing the highest reality is also the closest presence.
ramacharitamanas::1023.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, the sages and gods are praising Ram after hearing Brahma's devotion. This verse lifts Ram beyond all limits: he is everywhere, yet beyond description, and even the most detached sages are drawn into loving remembrance of him.
ramacharitamanas::1023.modern_relevance: You sit in a silent room after a long day, and the mind still keeps reaching for words. This verse reminds you that what is deepest is not something you can fully explain — only recognize, remember, and love.
ramacharitamanas::1023.insight: It shifts devotion from ritual form to constant inward remembrance of the all-pervading presence.

ramacharitamanas::1024.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं सृष्टि उपाई त्रिबिध बनाई संग सहाय न दूजा। सो करउ अघारी चिंत हमारी जानिअ भगति न पूजा॥ जो भव भय भंजन मुनि मन रंजन गंजन बिपति बरूथा। मन बच क्रम बानी छाड़ि सयानी सरन सकल सुरजूथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1024.verse_hindi: जिन्होंने बिना किसी दूसरे संगी अथवा सहायक के अकेले ही (या स्वयं अपने को त्रिगुणरूप- ब्रह्मा, विष्णु, शिवरूप- बनाकर अथवा बिना किसी उपादान-कारण के अर्थात् स्वयं ही सृष्टि का अभिन्ननिमित्तोपादान कारण बनकर) तीन प्रकार की सृष्टि उत्पन्न की, वे पापों का नाश करने वाले भगवान हमारी सुधि लें। हम न भक्ति जानते हैं, न पूजा, जो संसार के (जन्म-मृत्यु के) भय का नाश करने वाले, मुनियों के मन को आनंद देने वाले और विपत्तियों के समूह को नष्ट करने वाले हैं। हम सब देवताओं के समूह, मन, वचन और कर्म से चतुराई करने की बान छोड़कर उन (भगवान) की शरण (आए) हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1024.english_translation: He who created the threefold world without any second companion or helper, let that destroyer of sin take care of us. We know neither devotion nor worship. He who ends the fear of worldly becoming, delights the minds of sages, and destroys every heap of trouble, we have abandoned cleverness in thought, speech, and action and taken refuge in the whole assembly of radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::1024.translation_literal: जेहिं (who) / सृष्टि (creation) / उपाई (created) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / बनाई (made) / संग (with) / सहाय (helper) / न (not) / दूजा (second) / सो (that one) / करउ (may do) / अघारी (destroyer of sins) / चिंत (care) / हमारी (our) / जानिअ (known) / भगति (devotion) / न (not) / पूजा (worship) / जो (who) / भव (worldly becoming) / भय (fear) / भंजन (breaker) / मुनि (sage) / मन (mind) / रंजन (delighter) / गंजन (destroyer) / बिपति (trouble) / बरूथा (heap) / मन (mind) / बच (speech) / क्रम (action) / बानी (way) / छाड़ि (leaving) / सयानी (cleverness) / सरन (refuge) / सकल (all) / सुरजूथा (assembly of radiant beings)
ramacharitamanas::1024.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1024.essence: True refuge begins where cleverness ends.
ramacharitamanas::1024.simple_meaning: Ram created the whole world alone, and the speaker admits there is no skill in him except surrender. He asks Ram to remember him and protect him from fear and trouble.
ramacharitamanas::1024.simple_insight: There is relief in dropping performance and coming honestly, empty-handed, to the divine.
ramacharitamanas::1024.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram at the start of Balkand, after describing his glory. Now he turns personal: the creator of the three worlds needs no help, while the devotee has no real offering except surrender. This verse is a direct plea for mercy.
ramacharitamanas::1024.modern_relevance: You open the message draft for the tenth time, trying to sound impressive, and finally realize honesty will do more than polish. The verse lets you stop performing and ask plainly for help.
ramacharitamanas::1024.insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to refuge, from trying to deserve grace to simply receiving it.

ramacharitamanas::1025.verse_sanskrit: सारद श्रुति सेषा रिषय असेषा जा कहुँ कोउ नहिं जाना। जेहि दीन पिआरे बेद पुकारे द्रवउ सो श्रीभगवाना॥ भव बारिधि मंदर सब बिधि सुंदर गुनमंदिर सुखपुंजा। मुनि सिद्ध सकल सुर परम भयातुर नमत नाथ पद कंजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1025.verse_hindi: सरस्वती, वेद, शेषजी और सम्पूर्ण ऋषि कोई भी जिनको नहीं जानते, जिन्हें दीन प्रिय हैं, ऐसा वेद पुकारकर कहते हैं, वे ही श्री भगवान हम पर दया करें। हे संसार रूपी समुद्र के (मथने के) लिए मंदराचल रूप, सब प्रकार से सुंदर, गुणों के धाम और सुखों की राशि नाथ! आपके चरण कमलों में मुनि, सिद्ध और सारे देवता भय से अत्यन्त व्याकुल होकर नमस्कार करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1025.english_translation: Saraswati, the Vedas, Shesha, and all the sages do not know You. Yet the Vedas proclaim that You are dear to the humble; so may the supreme Lord show mercy. O Lord, ocean-churner in the form of Mount Mandara, beautiful in every way, abode of virtues and a mass of joy, all sages, perfected beings, and radiant beings, overwhelmed by fear, bow at Your lotus feet.
ramacharitamanas::1025.translation_literal: सारद (Saraswati) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / सेषा (Shesha) / रिषय (sages) / असेषा (all) / जा कहुँ (whom) / कोउ (anyone) / नहिं (not) / जाना (know) / जेहि (whom) / दीन (the humble) / पिआरे (dear) / बेद (the Vedas) / पुकारे (proclaim) / द्रवउ (may show mercy) / सो (that) / श्रीभगवाना (the supreme Lord) / भव (worldly existence) / बारिधि (ocean) / मंदर (Mount Mandara) / सब बिधि (in every way) / सुंदर (beautiful) / गुनमंदिर (abode of virtues) / सुखपुंजा (mass of joy) / मुनि (sages) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / सकल (all) / सुर (radiant beings) / परम (supreme) / भयातुर (overcome by fear) / नमत (bow) / नाथ (Lord) / पद (feet) / कंजा (lotus)
ramacharitamanas::1025.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1025.essence: The highest wisdom bows, and the humble receive what knowing cannot.
ramacharitamanas::1025.simple_meaning: Even the greatest sages cannot fully know Ram, but the Vedas say he loves the humble and should be asked for mercy. All wise beings bow to his feet in fear and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1025.simple_insight: You do not need mastery to approach him — humility opens the door that intellect cannot.
ramacharitamanas::1025.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram before the story moves forward. He says that even Saraswati, the Vedas, Shesha, and all sages cannot fully know Ram, yet the scriptures still declare one thing clearly: the humble are dear to him. Fearful sages and radiant beings bow to his feet.
ramacharitamanas::1025.modern_relevance: You’ve read every article, rehearsed every argument, and still feel no closer to the answer. This verse says the door is not more cleverness — it is humility, reverence, and a willingness to bow before what exceeds you.
ramacharitamanas::1025.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to master the divine to approaching with humility and trust.

ramacharitamanas::1026.verse_sanskrit: जानि सभय सुर भूमि सुनि बचन समेत सनेह। गगनगिरा गंभीर भइ हरनि सोक संदेह ॥
ramacharitamanas::1026.verse_hindi: देवताओं और पृथ्वी को भयभीत जानकर और उनके स्नेहयुक्त वचन सुनकर शोक और संदेह को हरने वाली गंभीर आकाशवाणी हुई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1026.english_translation: Knowing the gods and the earth were afraid, and hearing their loving words, a grave voice from the sky arose, removing sorrow and doubt.
ramacharitamanas::1026.translation_literal: जानि (knowing) / सभय (fearful) / सुर (gods) / भूमि (earth) / सुनि (hearing) / बचन (words) / समेत (together with) / सनेह (love) / गगनगिरा (voice from the sky) / गंभीर (grave) / भइ (became) / हरनि (removing) / सोक (sorrow) / संदेह (doubt)
ramacharitamanas::1026.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1026.essence: Reassurance from above dissolves fear before the answer comes.
ramacharitamanas::1026.simple_meaning: The divine voice answered the frightened gods with reassurance, and their sorrow and doubt faded.
ramacharitamanas::1026.simple_insight: Fear eases when loving assurance arrives from beyond your own control.
ramacharitamanas::1026.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, the gods and the earth are anxious as they plead for relief. Their loving appeal is heard, and a solemn voice from above answers, clearing sorrow and doubt before Ram's promise of birth is announced.
ramacharitamanas::1026.modern_relevance: You are waiting for a message that could change everything. Your chest is tight, your mind is spinning, and then one calm reply arrives and steadies the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::1026.insight: It shifts attention from panic to reassurance, preparing the mind to receive Ram's promise.

ramacharitamanas::1027.verse_sanskrit: जनि डरपहु मुनि सिद्ध सुरेसा। तुम्हहि लागि धरिहउँ नर बेसा॥ अंसन्ह सहित मनुज अवतारा। लेहउँ दिनकर बंस उदारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1027.verse_hindi: हे मुनि, सिद्ध और देवताओं के स्वामियों! डरो मत। तुम्हारे लिए मैं मनुष्य का रूप धारण करूँगा और उदार (पवित्र) सूर्यवंश में अंशों सहित मनुष्य का अवतार लूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1027.english_translation: O sages, perfected beings, and lords of the radiant ones, do not fear. For your sake I will take a human form and descend as an incarnation, with my own portions, in the noble solar lineage.
ramacharitamanas::1027.translation_literal: जनि (do not) / डरपहु (fear) / मुनि (sages) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / सुरेसा (lords of the radiant ones) / तुम्हहि लागि (for your sake) / धरिहउँ (I will take) / नर बेसा (human form) / अंसन्ह सहित (with portions) / मनुज अवतारा (human incarnation) / लेहउँ (I will take) / दिनकर बंस (solar lineage) / उदारा (noble)
ramacharitamanas::1027.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1027.essence: The divine comes close enough to be met.
ramacharitamanas::1027.simple_meaning: The divine reassures the sages and promises to appear in human form in the noble solar lineage for their sake.
ramacharitamanas::1027.simple_insight: You are not abandoned by the divine; help can arrive in a form you can actually meet.
ramacharitamanas::1027.detailed_meaning: The heavenly beings and sages have just heard the cosmic promise and are still shaken. Ram answers them directly: do not fear. He will be born among humans, in the solar lineage, so the world can meet the divine face to face.
ramacharitamanas::1027.modern_relevance: When life feels too large to hold — a hospital corridor, a legal notice, a phone call you feared — relief comes from what can actually reach you. Help is real when it enters your world instead of staying distant.
ramacharitamanas::1027.insight: It shifts faith from abstract awe to personal nearness: the divine chooses a human scale to protect and guide.

ramacharitamanas::1028.verse_sanskrit: कस्यप अदिति महातप कीन्हा। तिन्ह कहुँ मैं पूरब बर दीन्हा॥ ते दसरथ कौसल्या रूपा। कोसलपुरीं प्रगट नर भूपा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1028.verse_hindi: कश्यप और अदिति ने बड़ा भारी तप किया था। मैं पहले ही उनको वर दे चुका हूँ। वे ही दशरथ और कौसल्या के रूप में मनुष्यों के राजा होकर श्री अयोध्यापुरी में प्रकट हुए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1028.english_translation: Kashyapa and Aditi performed great austerities. I had already granted them that boon. They have appeared as King Dasharatha and Queen Kaushalya in the city of Kosala.
ramacharitamanas::1028.translation_literal: कस्यप (Kashyapa) / अदिति (Aditi) / महातप (great austerity) / कीन्हा (performed) / तिन्ह कहुँ (for them) / मैं (I) / पूरब (earlier) / बर (boon) / दीन्हा (gave) / ते (they) / दसरथ (Dasharatha) / कौसल्या (Kaushalya) / रूपा (in the form of) / कोसलपुरीं (in Kosala city) / प्रगट (manifested) / नर भूपा (human king)
ramacharitamanas::1028.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1028.essence: Boons do not vanish; they return as the right birth at the right time.
ramacharitamanas::1028.simple_meaning: Kashyapa and Aditi’s long austerities had already been rewarded. They were born again as Dasharatha and Kaushalya, the royal parents in Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::1028.simple_insight: What looks like a birth is often the return of a long-earned blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1028.detailed_meaning: Shiva’s narration has reached the point where Ram explains why he will enter Dasharatha’s house. The verse identifies Dasharatha and Kaushalya as the rebirth of Kashyapa and Aditi, linking the coming incarnation to earlier devotion and divine promise.
ramacharitamanas::1028.modern_relevance: A family line can carry the result of years of unseen effort. The life you see today may be the flowering of prayers, discipline, and patience that began long before you arrived.
ramacharitamanas::1028.insight: It shifts attention from random birth to meaningful continuity across lives and vows.

ramacharitamanas::1029.verse_sanskrit: तिन्ह कें गृह अवतरिहउँ जाई। रघुकुल तिलक सो चारिउ भाई॥ नारद बचन सत्य सब करिहउँ। परम सक्ति समेत अवतरिहउँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1029.verse_hindi: उन्हीं के घर जाकर मैं रघुकुल में श्रेष्ठ चार भाइयों के रूप में अवतार लूँगा। नारद के सब वचन मैं सत्य करूँगा और अपनी पराशक्ति के सहित अवतार लूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1029.english_translation: I will go and take birth in their home as the ornament of the Raghu clan, the four brothers. I will make Narada's words come true and incarnate with my supreme power.
ramacharitamanas::1029.translation_literal: तिन्ह कें गृह (in their home) / अवतरिहउँ (I will incarnate) / जाई (going) / रघुकुल (the Raghu clan) / तिलक (ornament, mark of honor) / सो (that) / चारिउ (four) / भाई (brothers) / नारद (Narada) / बचन (words) / सत्य (true) / सब (all) / करिहउँ (I will make) / परम सक्ति (supreme power) / समेत (together with) / अवतरिहउँ (I will incarnate)
ramacharitamanas::1029.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1029.essence: Birth itself can be the answer to a promise.
ramacharitamanas::1029.simple_meaning: Ram says he will be born in the house of Dasharath and become the four celebrated brothers of the Raghu line, fulfilling Narada's words with his divine power.
ramacharitamanas::1029.simple_insight: A great life begins as a promise kept. Even birth itself can be an act of purpose.
ramacharitamanas::1029.detailed_meaning: In the opening of Balkand, the divine plan is being announced before Ram's birth. The supreme being chooses Dasharath and Kausalya's house, promises to appear as the four brothers, and confirms Narada's prophecy. This verse shows incarnation as a deliberate answer to a cosmic need.
ramacharitamanas::1029.modern_relevance: Before a child is born, a family already imagines a future for them. This verse carries a larger version of that feeling: a life can arrive with a clear calling, not by accident but by deliberate meaning.
ramacharitamanas::1029.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing existence as random to seeing it as purposeful and responsive.

ramacharitamanas::1030.verse_sanskrit: हरिहउँ सकल भूमि गरुआई। निर्भय होहु देव समुदाई॥ गगन ब्रह्मबानी सुनि काना। तुरत फिरे सुर हृदय जुड़ाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1030.verse_hindi: मैं पृथ्वी का सब भार हर लूँगा। हे देववृंद! तुम निर्भय हो जाओ। आकाश में ब्रह्म (भगवान) की वाणी को कान से सुनकर देवता तुरंत लौट गए। उनका हृदय शीतल हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1030.english_translation: I will lift the burden of the earth. Be fearless, hosts of radiant beings. Hearing the voice of the supreme being in the sky, they quickly returned, and their hearts were soothed.
ramacharitamanas::1030.translation_literal: हरिहउँ (I will remove) / सकल (all) / भूमि (earth) / गरुआई (burden) / निर्भय (fearless) / होहु (become) / देव (radiant beings) / समुदाई (assembly) / गगन (sky) / ब्रह्मबानी (voice of the supreme being) / सुनि (hearing) / काना (with ears) / तुरत (immediately) / फिरे (returned) / सुर (radiant beings) / हृदय (hearts) / जुड़ाना (became cool/soothed)
ramacharitamanas::1030.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1030.essence: The burden lifts when the divine takes it on.
ramacharitamanas::1030.simple_meaning: Ram promises to lift the earth’s burden and tells the radiant beings not to fear. After hearing the divine voice, they return with eased hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1030.simple_insight: Fear loosens when a greater power takes responsibility.
ramacharitamanas::1030.detailed_meaning: The gods have gathered because the earth is weighed down by Ravana’s rule. After the promise of Ram’s descent, a voice from the sky tells them to be unafraid. Their panic ends, and they return reassured.
ramacharitamanas::1030.modern_relevance: You get the message after a night of panic: the problem is real, but it is not yours alone to carry. Relief comes the moment responsibility is shared.
ramacharitamanas::1030.insight: It shifts attention from cosmic panic to trust in a larger restoring force.

ramacharitamanas::1031.verse_sanskrit: तब ब्रह्माँ धरनिहि समुझावा। अभय भई भरोस जियँ आवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1031.verse_hindi: तब ब्रह्माजी ने पृथ्वी को समझाया। वह भी निर्भय हुई और उसके जी में भरोसा (ढाढस) आ गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1031.english_translation: Then Brahma explained it to the earth. She became fearless, and trust arose in her heart.
ramacharitamanas::1031.translation_literal: तब (then) / ब्रह्माँ (Brahma) / धरनिहि (to the earth) / समुझावा (explained) / अभय (fearless) / भई (became) / भरोस (trust) / जियँ (in the heart) / आवा (came)
ramacharitamanas::1031.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1031.essence: Clear reassurance turns fear into trust.
ramacharitamanas::1031.simple_meaning: Brahma reassures the earth, and her fear turns into trust.
ramacharitamanas::1031.simple_insight: Fear softens when a greater order is made clear.
ramacharitamanas::1031.detailed_meaning: After the divine promise of Ram's birth, Brahma turns to the earth itself and reassures her. The burden she has carried eases, her fear disappears, and trust returns before the story moves on to the gods' next step.
ramacharitamanas::1031.modern_relevance: A child finally tells the truth after days of silence, and the whole room relaxes. Naming what is coming can turn panic into steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::1031.insight: It shows how reassurance restores courage when uncertainty has been weighing on the mind.

ramacharitamanas::1032.verse_sanskrit: निज लोकहि बिरंचि गे देवन्ह इहइ सिखाइ। बानर तनु धरि धरि महि हरि पद सेवहु जाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1032.verse_hindi: देवताओं को यही सिखाकर कि वानरों का शरीर धर-धरकर तुम लोग पृथ्वी पर जाकर भगवान के चरणों की सेवा करो, ब्रह्माजी अपने लोक को चले गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1032.english_translation: After teaching the gods this, Brahma returned to his own realm: take the form of monkeys and go to earth to serve the feet of Hari.
ramacharitamanas::1032.translation_literal: निज लोकहि (to his own realm) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / गे (went) / देवन्ह (to the gods) / इहइ (this only) / सिखाइ (having taught) / बानर तनु (monkey form) / धरि धरि (taking again and again) / महि (on earth) / हरि पद (Hari's feet) / सेवहु (serve) / जाइ (go)
ramacharitamanas::1032.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1032.essence: Service in humble form becomes the way the divine work unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::1032.simple_meaning: Brahma tells the gods to take monkey forms and go to earth to serve Hari. Then he returns to his own world.
ramacharitamanas::1032.simple_insight: Great help can begin with humble service, not status.
ramacharitamanas::1032.detailed_meaning: Brahma has just reassured the gods and arranged Ram's coming to earth. After giving them their instruction, he leaves for his own realm. This verse is a bridge, not the main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1032.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with panic about a crisis, and one clear voice cuts through the noise: stop worrying, start serving. The solution is not prestige; it is useful presence.
ramacharitamanas::1032.insight: It shifts attention from divine rescue as a miracle to divine rescue through willing service.

ramacharitamanas::1033.verse_sanskrit: गए देव सब निज निज धामा। भूमि सहित मन कहुँ बिश्रामा॥ जो कछु आयसु ब्रह्माँ दीन्हा। हरषे देव बिलंब न कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1033.verse_hindi: सब देवता अपने-अपने लोक को गए। पृथ्वी सहित सबके मन को शांति मिली। ब्रह्माजी ने जो कुछ आज्ञा दी, उससे देवता बहुत प्रसन्न हुए और उन्होंने (वैसा करने में) देर नहीं की ॥
ramacharitamanas::1033.english_translation: All the devas returned to their own abodes. Along with the earth, every mind found rest. Whatever command Brahma gave, the devas rejoiced and did not delay.
ramacharitamanas::1033.translation_literal: गए (went) / देव (devas) / सब (all) / निज निज (their own) / धामा (abodes) / भूमि (earth) / सहित (along with) / मन (mind) / कहुँ (for) / बिश्रामा (rest)॥ / जो (whatever) / कछु (some) / आयसु (command) / ब्रह्माँ (Brahma) / दीन्हा (gave) / हरषे (rejoiced) / देव (devas) / बिलंब (delay) / न (not) / कीन्हा (did)
ramacharitamanas::1033.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1033.essence: Clarity ends fear; obedience becomes joy.
ramacharitamanas::1033.simple_meaning: The devas returned to their own realms, and the earth was eased. Brahma's order was welcomed, and the devas acted without delay.
ramacharitamanas::1033.simple_insight: Peace returns when the right beings accept their role and move at once.
ramacharitamanas::1033.detailed_meaning: Brahma has just reassured the earth and sent the devas into action. Their fear lifts, their minds settle, and they leave without hesitation. This is the quiet turning point before the divine allies take birth on earth.
ramacharitamanas::1033.modern_relevance: After a tense family meeting, everyone finally agrees on the next step. The room softens, shoulders drop, and the plan starts moving the moment the decision is made.
ramacharitamanas::1033.insight: It shifts attention from anxiety to immediate, willing action once clarity arrives.

ramacharitamanas::1034.verse_sanskrit: बनचर देह धरी छिति माहीं। अतुलित बल प्रताप तिन्ह पाहीं॥ गिरि तरु नख आयुध सब बीरा। हरि मारग चितवहिं मतिधीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1034.verse_hindi: पृथ्वी पर उन्होंने वानरदेह धारण की। उनमें अपार बल और प्रताप था। सभी शूरवीर थे, पर्वत, वृक्ष और नख ही उनके शस्त्र थे। वे धीर बुद्धि वाले (वानर रूप देवता) भगवान के आने की राह देखने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1034.english_translation: They took monkey bodies on earth. They possessed immeasurable strength and splendor. Brave and wise, they used mountains, trees, and nails as weapons, and watched for the Lord's path.
ramacharitamanas::1034.translation_literal: बनचर (forest-dweller) / देह (body) / धरी (having taken) / छिति (earth) / माहीं (in) / अतुलित (immeasurable) / बल (strength) / प्रताप (splendor, valor) / तिन्ह (they) / पाहीं (had) / गिरि (mountain) / तरु (tree) / नख (nails) / आयुध (weapons) / सब (all) / बीरा (heroes) / हरि (Lord) / मारग (path) / चितवहिं (they watched) / मतिधीरा (steadfast-minded)
ramacharitamanas::1034.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1034.essence: Power becomes noble when it waits for the right call.
ramacharitamanas::1034.simple_meaning: The divine beings took monkey bodies on earth, became strong and heroic, and waited for Ram's arrival with calm minds.
ramacharitamanas::1034.simple_insight: Strength becomes sacred when it waits to serve something higher than itself.
ramacharitamanas::1034.detailed_meaning: After Brahma sends the gods to earth in monkey forms, they settle into their new bodies with joy. Tulsidas describes their power, courage, and readiness: these are not ordinary monkeys, but divine allies waiting for Ram's coming.
ramacharitamanas::1034.modern_relevance: A team gathers before a hard rescue, each person bringing different tools, skills, and courage. Nobody is trying to shine alone. Everyone is ready for the moment the call finally comes.
ramacharitamanas::1034.insight: It shifts attention from raw power to power held in readiness for service.

ramacharitamanas::1035.verse_sanskrit: गिरि कानन जहँ तहँ भरि पूरी। रहे निज निज अनीक रचि रूरी॥ यह सब रुचिर चरित मैं भाषा। अब सो सुनहु जो बीचहिं राखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1035.verse_hindi: वे (वानर) पर्वतों और जंगलों में जहाँ-तहाँ अपनी-अपनी सुंदर सेना बनाकर भरपूर छा गए। यह सब सुंदर चरित्र मैंने कहा। अब वह चरित्र सुनो जिसे बीच ही में छोड़ दिया था ॥
ramacharitamanas::1035.english_translation: The monkeys filled the hills and forests, spreading out in beautiful divisions everywhere. I have told this lovely tale. Now hear the part I had left in between.
ramacharitamanas::1035.translation_literal: गिरि (mountains) / कानन (forests) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / भरि पूरी (filled completely) / रहे (remained) / निज निज (their own) / अनीक (army divisions) / रचि (arranged) / रूरी (beautiful) / यह (this) / सब (all) / रुचिर (beautiful) / चरित (deeds/story) / मैं (I) / भाषा (have narrated) / अब (now) / सो (that) / सुनहु (listen) / जो (which) / बीचहिं (in the middle) / राखा (was kept/left)
ramacharitamanas::1035.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1035.essence: The poet pauses, then gathers the story back into motion.
ramacharitamanas::1035.simple_meaning: The monkeys spread through the hills and forests in well-formed groups. The narrator pauses, says the scene is beautiful, and returns to the story he interrupted.
ramacharitamanas::1035.simple_insight: A story can move in and out of scene without losing its thread.
ramacharitamanas::1035.detailed_meaning: After the vanara forces are formed, they spread across hills and forests in orderly divisions. Tulsidas pauses to admire the beauty of the scene, then signals that he is returning to the episode he had set aside before continuing the larger narrative.
ramacharitamanas::1035.modern_relevance: You’re reading a long message thread, and the speaker suddenly says, “Let me come back to the point I left earlier.” The story resumes cleanly, without losing momentum.
ramacharitamanas::1035.insight: It teaches the reader to follow a layered narrative without confusion and to notice how the poem moves between description and continuation.

ramacharitamanas::1036.verse_sanskrit: अवधपुरीं रघुकुलमनि राऊ। बेद बिदित तेहि दसरथ नाऊँ॥ धरम धुरंधर गुननिधि ग्यानी। हृदयँ भगति भति सारँगपानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1036.verse_hindi: अवधपुरी में रघुकुल शिरोमणि दशरथ नाम के राजा हुए, जिनका नाम वेदों में विख्यात है। वे धर्मधुरंधर, गुणों के भंडार और ज्ञानी थे। उनके हृदय में शांर्गधनुष धारण करने वाले भगवान की भक्ति थी और उनकी बुद्धि भी उन्हीं में लगी रहती थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1036.english_translation: In Ayodhya lived King Dasharath, the jewel of the Raghu line, famed in the Vedas. He was a pillar of dharma, a storehouse of virtues, and a wise man. His heart held devotion to the divine, and his mind remained fixed there.
ramacharitamanas::1036.translation_literal: अवधपुरीं (in Ayodhya city) / रघुकुलमनि (jewel of the Raghu line) / राऊ (king) / बेद बिदित (known in the Vedas) / तेहि (that) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / नाऊँ (name) / धरम धुरंधर (pillar of dharma) / गुननिधि (storehouse of virtues) / ग्यानी (wise) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / भगति (devotion) / भति (in the manner) / सारँगपानी (the bow-bearing divine one)
ramacharitamanas::1036.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1036.essence: True greatness joins rule, virtue, wisdom, and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1036.simple_meaning: Dasharath is introduced as a noble king of Ayodhya: righteous, virtuous, wise, and devoted to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1036.simple_insight: A good ruler is not just powerful; his inner life must also be anchored in devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1036.detailed_meaning: The story pauses in Ayodhya to introduce Dasharath, Ram's father. He is praised as the finest of the Raghu line, learned, virtuous, and devoted. This matters because the exile and family crisis that follow will test the very king whose heart is already turned toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1036.modern_relevance: A leader signs the final decision after a long day, but what matters most is not the title on the door. It is whether character, wisdom, and devotion guide the hand that signs.
ramacharitamanas::1036.insight: It shifts attention from public status to the inner qualities that make authority worthy.

ramacharitamanas::1037.verse_sanskrit: कौसल्यादि नारि प्रिय सब आचरन पुनीत। पति अनुकूल प्रेम दृढ़ हरि पद कमल बिनीत ॥
ramacharitamanas::1037.verse_hindi: उनकी कौसल्या आदि प्रिय रानियाँ सभी पवित्र आचरण वाली थीं। वे (बड़ी) विनीत और पति के अनुकूल (चलने वाली) थीं और श्री हरि के चरणकमलों में उनका दृढ़ प्रेम था ॥
ramacharitamanas::1037.english_translation: Kausalya and the other beloved queens were all pure in conduct. They were humble, devoted to their husband, and firmly devoted to the lotus feet of Hari.
ramacharitamanas::1037.translation_literal: कौसल्यादि (Kausalya and others) / नारि (women) / प्रिय (beloved) / सब (all) / आचरन (conduct) / पुनीत (pure) / पति (husband) / अनुकूल (favourable, devoted) / प्रेम (love) / दृढ़ (firm) / हरि (Hari) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / बिनीत (humble, obedient)
ramacharitamanas::1037.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1037.essence: Pure conduct and steady devotion make a household fit for grace.
ramacharitamanas::1037.simple_meaning: Dasharath’s queens are described as pure, humble, and deeply devoted to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1037.simple_insight: Devotion begins at home, in how love, humility, and conduct are lived every day.
ramacharitamanas::1037.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Tulsidas pauses to describe the royal household before the sorrow of childlessness unfolds. Dasharath’s queens, especially Kausalya, are shown as pure in conduct, gentle in marriage, and firmly devoted to Hari, setting the moral tone of the family.
ramacharitamanas::1037.modern_relevance: A home can look successful from outside and still be held together by quiet humility and shared devotion. The real strength of a family often lives in the way people speak, serve, and honor one another.
ramacharitamanas::1037.insight: It shifts attention from status to the quality of love and conduct inside the household.

ramacharitamanas::1038.verse_sanskrit: एक बार भूपति मन माहीं। भै गलानि मोरें सुत नाहीं॥ गुर गृह गयउ तुरत महिपाला। चरन लागि करि बिनय बिसाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::1038.verse_hindi: एक बार राजा के मन में बड़ी ग्लानि हुई कि मेरे पुत्र नहीं है। राजा तुरंत ही गुरु के घर गए और चरणों में प्रणाम कर बहुत विनय की ॥
