ramacharitamanas::1038.english_translation: Once, the king felt deep sorrow in his mind: "I have no son." At once the king went to his guru's house and bowed at his feet with great humility.
ramacharitamanas::1038.translation_literal: एक बार (once) / भूपति (king) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / भै (became) / गलानि (sorrow, regret) / मोरें (my) / सुत (son) / नाहीं (not) || गुर गृह (to the guru's house) / गयउ (went) / तुरत (at once) / महिपाला (the king) / चरन लागि (touching the feet) / करि (doing) / बिनय (humble request) / बिसाला (great, extensive)
ramacharitamanas::1038.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1038.essence: Pride softens when real pain is finally spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1038.simple_meaning: King Dasharath feels distressed that he has no son, so he immediately goes to his teacher and bows with great humility.
ramacharitamanas::1038.simple_insight: When helplessness becomes honest, pride can turn into prayer.
ramacharitamanas::1038.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, King Dasharath is troubled by the pain of childlessness. Instead of hiding it, he goes straight to Guru Vashistha, bows at his feet, and asks for guidance. This moment opens the path to the birth of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1038.modern_relevance: You sit alone after another failed test result or medical report and finally stop pretending you're fine. The next move is not performance — it's honest humility before someone wiser.
ramacharitamanas::1038.insight: It shifts the mind from private struggle to seeking wise help without ego.

ramacharitamanas::1039.verse_sanskrit: निज दुख सुख सब गुरहि सुनायउ। कहि बसिष्ठ बहुबिधि समुझायउ॥ धरहु धीर होइहहिं सुत चारी। त्रिभुवन बिदित भगत भय हारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1039.verse_hindi: राजा ने अपना सारा सुख-दुःख गुरु को सुनाया। गुरु वशिष्ठजी ने उन्हें बहुत प्रकार से समझाया (और कहा-) धीरज धरो, तुम्हारे चार पुत्र होंगे, जो तीनों लोकों में प्रसिद्ध और भक्तों के भय को हरने वाले होंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1039.english_translation: The king told the guru all his sorrow and joy. Vashishtha explained in many ways: "Take heart. You will have four sons, famous in the three worlds and remover of devotees' fear."
ramacharitamanas::1039.translation_literal: निज (own) / दुख (sorrow) / सुख (joy) / सब (all) / गुरहि (to the guru) / सुनायउ (told) / कहि (speaking) / बसिष्ठ (Vashishtha) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / समुझायउ (explained) / धरहु (hold) / धीर (courage) / होइहहिं (will become) / सुत (sons) / चारी (four) / त्रिभुवन (three worlds) / बिदित (known) / भगत (devotees') / भय (fear) / हारी (remover)
ramacharitamanas::1039.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1039.essence: Sorrow becomes bearable when it is spoken to wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::1039.simple_meaning: Dasharath shares his grief with Vashishtha, and the guru reassures him that he will have four sons who will become famous and remove fear from devotees.
ramacharitamanas::1039.simple_insight: Even private sorrow can be held safely when you bring it to a wise guide.
ramacharitamanas::1039.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has just confessed his childlessness and pain to Vashishtha. The guru answers with reassurance, not only promising sons but revealing their future greatness. This moment turns personal grief into the opening of Ram's divine arrival.
ramacharitamanas::1039.modern_relevance: You finally say out loud what has been hurting for months. A wise person hears the whole mess, steadies you, and shows that your fear is not the end of the story.
ramacharitamanas::1039.insight: It shifts the mind from private despair to trust in wise guidance and a larger unfolding.

ramacharitamanas::1040.verse_sanskrit: सृंगी रिषिहि बसिष्ठ बोलावा। पुत्रकाम सुभ जग्य करावा॥ भगति सहित मुनि आहुति दीन्हें। प्रगटे अगिनि चरू कर लीन्हें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1040.verse_hindi: वशिष्ठजी ने श्रृंगी ऋषि को बुलवाया और उनसे शुभ पुत्रकामेष्टि यज्ञ कराया। मुनि के भक्ति सहित आहुतियाँ देने पर अग्निदेव हाथ में चरु (हविष्यान्न खीर) लिए प्रकट हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1040.english_translation: Vasishtha summoned Shringi Rishi and arranged the auspicious Putrakameshti sacrifice. When the sage offered the oblations with devotion, the fire appeared holding the offering bowl in its hand.
ramacharitamanas::1040.translation_literal: सृंगी (Shringi) / रिषिहि (to the sage) / बसिष्ठ (Vasishtha) / बोलावा (called) / पुत्रकाम (for a son) / सुभ (auspicious) / जग्य (sacrifice) / करावा (caused to be performed) / भगति सहित (with devotion) / मुनि (the sage) / आहुति (oblations) / दीन्हें (gave) / प्रगटे (appeared) / अगिनि (fire) / चरू (offering bowl of cooked sacrificial food) / कर (hand) / लीन्हें (taking)
ramacharitamanas::1040.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1040.essence: Devotion makes the sacred act come alive.
ramacharitamanas::1040.simple_meaning: Vasishtha has Shringi Rishi perform the sacred sacrifice for a son. When the offerings are made with devotion, fire appears and takes the offering bowl.
ramacharitamanas::1040.simple_insight: Devotion turns ritual into a living encounter.
ramacharitamanas::1040.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath’s longing for a son has reached a decisive moment. Vasishtha calls Shringi Rishi and arranges the Putrakameshti sacrifice. The verse shows the ritual beginning to bear fruit as divine fire appears.
ramacharitamanas::1040.modern_relevance: You prepare carefully for something deeply wanted — a child, a reconciliation, a new beginning — and the moment finally feels charged with meaning.
ramacharitamanas::1040.insight: It shifts attention from mechanical ritual to the sincerity that animates it.

ramacharitamanas::1041.verse_sanskrit: जो बसिष्ठ कछु हृदयँ बिचारा। सकल काजु भा सिद्ध तुम्हारा॥ यह हबि बाँटि देहु नृप जाई। जथा जोग जेहि भाग बनाई ॥ तब अदृस्य भए पावक सकल सभहि समुझाइ। परमानंद मगन नृप हरष न हृदयँ समाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1041.verse_hindi: (और दशरथ से बोले-) वशिष्ठ ने हृदय में जो कुछ विचारा था, तुम्हारा वह सब काम सिद्ध हो गया। हे राजन् ! (अब) तुम जाकर इस हविष्यान्न (पायस) को, जिसको जैसा उचित हो, वैसा भाग बनाकर बाँट दो॥ तदनन्तर अग्निदेव सारी सभा को समझाकर अन्तर्धान हो गए। राजा परमानंद में मग्न हो गए, उनके हृदय में हर्ष समाता न था ॥
ramacharitamanas::1041.english_translation: Vashishtha had whatever he had thought in his heart fulfilled. O king, go and distribute this offering in proper shares as is fitting. Then the fire became invisible after instructing the whole assembly. The king was filled with supreme joy, and his heart could not contain its delight.
ramacharitamanas::1041.translation_literal: जो (whatever) / बसिष्ठ (Vashishtha) / कछु (something) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारा (thought) / सकल (all) / काजु (work) / भा (became) / सिद्ध (fulfilled) / तुम्हारा (your) / यह (this) / हबि (offering) / बाँटि (distribute) / देहु (give) / नृप (king) / जाई (going) / जथा (as) / जोग (proper) / जेहि (to whom) / भाग (share) / बनाई (making) / तब (then) / अदृस्य (invisible) / भए (became) / पावक (fire) / सकल (all) / सभहि (assembly) / समुझाइ (explaining) / परमानंद (supreme joy) / मगन (immersed) / नृप (king) / हरष (joy) / न हृदयँ (in the heart not) / समाइ (contained)
ramacharitamanas::1041.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1041.essence: A fulfilled prayer turns into a joy that cannot stay inside.
ramacharitamanas::1041.simple_meaning: The divine plan succeeds, the sacred offering is divided, and the king overflows with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1041.simple_insight: There is relief when a long prayer finally turns into action and blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1041.detailed_meaning: At Vashishtha's arranged sacrifice, the sacred offering is ready and the fire has delivered its message. The unseen force of the rite has worked; Dasharath is told to divide the offering properly. This is the moment before the queens receive their portions.
ramacharitamanas::1041.modern_relevance: A tense family dinner is finally over, and the news everyone has been waiting for arrives. The room changes at once: instructions are clear, relief breaks through, and hope becomes something you can actually act on.
ramacharitamanas::1041.insight: It shifts attention from waiting for a sign to receiving and acting on it with order.

ramacharitamanas::1042.verse_sanskrit: तबहिं रायँ प्रिय नारि बोलाईं। कौसल्यादि तहाँ चलि आईं॥ अर्ध भाग कौसल्यहि दीन्हा। उभय भाग आधे कर कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1042.verse_hindi: उसी समय राजा ने अपनी प्यारी पत्नियों को बुलाया। कौसल्या आदि सब (रानियाँ) वहाँ चली आईं। राजा ने (पायस का) आधा भाग कौसल्या को दिया, (और शेष) आधे के दो भाग किए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1042.english_translation: Then the king called his beloved queens. Kausalya and the others came there. He gave half the offering to Kausalya, and divided the remaining half into two parts.
ramacharitamanas::1042.translation_literal: तबहिं (then) / रायँ (the king) / प्रिय नारि (beloved wives) / बोलाईं (called) / कौसल्यादि (Kausalya and others) / तहाँ (there) / चलि आईं (came) / अर्ध भाग (half portion) / कौसल्यहि (to Kausalya) / दीन्हा (gave) / उभय भाग (the two portions) / आधे कर (into halves) / कीन्हा (made)
ramacharitamanas::1042.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1042.essence: Blessing grows when it is divided with love.
ramacharitamanas::1042.simple_meaning: Dasharath calls his queens and shares the sacred offering among them, giving the first portion to Kausalya and dividing the rest.
ramacharitamanas::1042.simple_insight: Sacred grace is shared, not hoarded.
ramacharitamanas::1042.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has just received the blessed offering from the sacrifice. He calls Kausalya and the other queens, and the portion is divided among them. This verse is a step in the larger sequence that will lead to Ram's birth.
ramacharitamanas::1042.modern_relevance: A family waits in the kitchen while one person brings home something precious. The way it is shared reveals the love, fairness, and tenderness in the house.
ramacharitamanas::1042.insight: It shifts attention from the object itself to the care shown in sharing it.

ramacharitamanas::1043.verse_sanskrit: कैकेई कहँ नृप सो दयऊ। रह्यो सो उभय भाग पुनि भयऊ॥ कौसल्या कैकेई हाथ धरि। दीन्ह सुमित्रहि मन प्रसन्न करि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1043.verse_hindi: वह (उनमें से एक भाग) राजा ने कैकेयी को दिया। शेष जो बच रहा उसके फिर दो भाग हुए और राजा ने उनको कौसल्या और कैकेयी के हाथ पर रखकर (अर्थात् उनकी अनुमति लेकर) और इस प्रकार उनका मन प्रसन्न करके सुमित्रा को दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1043.english_translation: The king gave one share to Kaikeyi. The remaining portion was again divided in two, and with Kaikeyi and Kaushalya’s hands upon it, he gave it to Sumitra, pleasing their minds.
ramacharitamanas::1043.translation_literal: कैकेई कहँ (to Kaikeyi) / नृप (the king) / सो (that) / दयऊ (gave) / रह्यो (remained) / सो (that which) / उभय भाग (two parts) / पुनि (again) / भयऊ (became) / कौसल्या (Kaushalya) / कैकेई (Kaikeyi) / हाथ धरि (placing in the hands) / दीन्ह (gave) / सुमित्रहि (to Sumitra) / मन प्रसन्न करि (making the mind pleased)
ramacharitamanas::1043.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1043.simple_meaning: Dasharath gives the sacred food fairly among his three queens, making sure each receives a share and feels respected.
ramacharitamanas::1043.simple_insight: Care and fairness can be shown in small, exact actions that leave no one feeling left out.
ramacharitamanas::1043.detailed_meaning: In Dasharath’s sacrificial ritual, the sacred food is being distributed to his queens. He first gives Kaikeyi her share, then divides the rest for Kaushalya and Sumitra with care, using their hands to show consent and goodwill. The scene shows harmony before the births of Ram and his brothers.
ramacharitamanas::1043.modern_relevance: At a family dinner, one parent notices the last serving and splits it carefully so no child feels overlooked. Small fairness can protect a whole home.
ramacharitamanas::1043.insight: It teaches you to distribute what matters with attention, so generosity also preserves dignity.

ramacharitamanas::1044.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि गर्भसहित सब नारी। भईं हृदयँ हरषित सुख भारी॥ जा दिन तें हरि गर्भहिं आए। सकल लोक सुख संपति छाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1044.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार सब स्त्रियाँ गर्भवती हुईं। वे हृदय में बहुत हर्षित हुईं। उन्हें बड़ा सुख मिला। जिस दिन से श्री हरि (लीला से ही) गर्भ में आए, सब लोकों में सुख और सम्पत्ति छा गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1044.english_translation: In this way, all the women became pregnant. Their hearts filled with great joy. Since the day Hari entered the womb, happiness and prosperity spread through all the worlds.
ramacharitamanas::1044.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / गर्भसहित (with pregnancy) / सब नारी (all women) / भईं (became) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / हरषित (delighted) / सुख भारी (great happiness) / जा दिन तें (from the day when) / हरि (Hari) / गर्भहिं (in the womb) / आए (came) / सकल लोक (all worlds) / सुख संपति (happiness and prosperity) / छाए (spread over)
ramacharitamanas::1044.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1044.essence: Hari's coming turns private joy into a blessing for the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::1044.simple_meaning: Queenly joy fills the palace as all the wives become pregnant. The arrival of Hari in the womb is described as bringing happiness and prosperity to the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::1044.simple_insight: When the divine presence enters life, even the world around it feels lighter.
ramacharitamanas::1044.detailed_meaning: After the sacred pudding is shared among Dasharath's queens, all of them conceive. The palace fills with joy, and Tulsidas marks this as the moment when Hari's coming begins to bless the entire world.
ramacharitamanas::1044.modern_relevance: A home feels different the moment hope returns after months of waiting. The same room, the same people, but something unseen has lifted everyone’s hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1044.insight: It shifts attention from private joy to the wider blessing that true presence brings.

ramacharitamanas::1045.verse_sanskrit: मंदिर महँ सब राजहिं रानीं। सोभा सील तेज की खानीं॥ सुख जुत कछुक काल चलि गयऊ। जेहिं प्रभु प्रगट सो अवसर भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1045.verse_hindi: शोभा, शील और तेज की खान (बनी हुई) सब रानियाँ महल में सुशोभित हुईं। इस प्रकार कुछ समय सुखपूर्वक बीता और वह अवसर आ गया, जिसमें प्रभु को प्रकट होना था ॥
ramacharitamanas::1045.english_translation: All the queens shone in the palace, treasures of beauty, character, and radiance. Thus some time passed in happiness, and the moment arrived for the Lord to appear.
ramacharitamanas::1045.translation_literal: मंदिर महँ (in the palace) / सब (all) / राजहिं (the queens) / रानीं (queens) / सोभा (beauty) / सील (character) / तेज (radiance) / की खानीं (mines/treasures) ॥ / सुख जुत (with happiness) / कछुक (some) / काल (time) / चलि गयऊ (passed) / जेहिं (in which) / प्रभु (the Lord) / प्रगट (manifested) / सो (that) / अवसर (moment) / भयऊ (became/arrived) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1045.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1045.essence: Peaceful time passes until the Lord's arrival.
ramacharitamanas::1045.simple_meaning: The queens lived happily in the palace, full of grace and virtue, until the time came for Ram to be born.
ramacharitamanas::1045.simple_insight: Even quiet, happy seasons can be the waiting room for something sacred.
ramacharitamanas::1045.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the queens live in beauty and ease, but this calm is only the pause before a greater event. Time ripens, and the palace becomes ready for Ram's appearance.
ramacharitamanas::1045.modern_relevance: A home feels ordinary for years — the same rooms, the same routines, the same laughter at dinner. Then one day everything changes, and you realise that the long calm was preparing you for that moment.
ramacharitamanas::1045.insight: It shifts attention from comfort itself to the hidden timing inside comfort.

ramacharitamanas::1046.verse_sanskrit: जोग लगन ग्रह बार तिथि सकल भए अनुकूल। चर अरु अचर हर्षजुत राम जनम सुखमूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1046.verse_hindi: योग, लग्न, ग्रह, वार और तिथि सभी अनुकूल हो गए। जड़ और चेतन सब हर्ष से भर गए। (क्योंकि) श्री राम का जन्म सुख का मूल है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1046.english_translation: All signs became favorable: the yoga, ascendant, planets, weekday, and date. All living and nonliving beings rejoiced, for Ram's birth is the root of joy.
ramacharitamanas::1046.translation_literal: जोग (auspicious alignment) / लगन (ascendant) / ग्रह (planets) / बार (weekday) / तिथि (lunar date) / सकल (all) / भए (became) / अनुकूल (favorable) / चर (living) / अरु (and) / अचर (nonliving) / हर्षजुत (filled with joy) / राम (Ram) / जनम (birth) / सुखमूल (root of joy)
ramacharitamanas::1046.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1046.essence: Ram's birth turns time itself into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1046.simple_meaning: The stars, time, and all conditions turned favorable. Everything rejoiced because Ram's birth brings joy to all existence.
ramacharitamanas::1046.simple_insight: When what matters most arrives, even the world seems to celebrate with you.
ramacharitamanas::1046.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the sacred moment before Ram's birth in Ayodhya. The heavens align, the calendar turns auspicious, and both living and nonliving creation seem to rejoice. The verse prepares the reader for a divine arrival.
ramacharitamanas::1046.modern_relevance: The room goes quiet before the baby cry, and everyone feels it: something sacred has arrived. Some moments change the mood of an entire home before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1046.insight: It shifts attention from event to atmosphere, showing that a truly blessed arrival transforms the whole world around it.

ramacharitamanas::1047.verse_sanskrit: नौमी तिथि मधु मास पुनीता। सुकल पच्छ अभिजित हरिप्रीता॥ मध्यदिवस अति सीत न घामा। पावन काल लोक बिश्रामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1047.verse_hindi: पवित्र चैत्र का महीना था, नवमी तिथि थी। शुक्ल पक्ष और भगवान का प्रिय अभिजित् मुहूर्त था। दोपहर का समय था। न बहुत सर्दी थी, न धूप (गरमी) थी। वह पवित्र समय सब लोकों को शांति देने वाला था ॥
ramacharitamanas::1047.english_translation: It was the sacred ninth day of the bright half of the month of Madhu. The auspicious Abhijit hour dear to the divine had arrived. It was midday. Neither cold nor heat was strong. That holy time brought peace to all worlds.
ramacharitamanas::1047.translation_literal: नौमी तिथि (ninth day) / मधु मास (month of Madhu) / पुनीता (sacred) / सुकल पच्छ (bright half) / अभिजित (Abhijit) / हरिप्रीता (dear to Hari) / मध्यदिवस (midday) / अति (very) / सीत (cold) / न (not) / घामा (heat/sun) / पावन (holy) / काल (time) / लोक (worlds) / बिश्रामा (rest/peace)
ramacharitamanas::1047.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1047.essence: The world itself pauses when the divine arrival is near.
ramacharitamanas::1047.simple_meaning: The birth moment is described as perfectly auspicious: a sacred day, a favorable hour, and a balanced midday that brings peace to the world.
ramacharitamanas::1047.simple_insight: Some moments feel prepared by the whole universe, as if life itself is holding still for something holy.
ramacharitamanas::1047.detailed_meaning: The story is preparing for Ram’s birth in Ayodhya. After the queens, stars, and timing have all been set in harmony, this verse fixes the exact sacred moment: the ninth day, bright fortnight, Abhijit hour, and a calm midday. It is the stillness before Ram appears.
ramacharitamanas::1047.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet before the announcement everyone has been waiting for. The clock, the air, and everyone’s nerves seem to line up at once. Some arrivals feel bigger than the moment that carries them.
ramacharitamanas::1047.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary clock time to the feeling of a moment charged with meaning.

ramacharitamanas::1048.verse_sanskrit: सीतल मंद सुरभि बह बाऊ। हरषित सुर संतन मन चाऊ॥ बन कुसुमित गिरिगन मनिआरा। स्रवहिं सकल सरिताऽमृतधारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1048.verse_hindi: शीतल, मंद और सुगंधित पवन बह रहा था। देवता हर्षित थे और संतों के मन में (बड़ा) चाव था। वन फूले हुए थे, पर्वतों के समूह मणियों से जगमगा रहे थे और सारी नदियाँ अमृत की धारा बहा रही थीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1048.english_translation: A cool, gentle, fragrant breeze blew. The radiant beings were delighted, and the saints felt deep joy. The forest bloomed, the mountains shone like jewels, and every river flowed like nectar.
ramacharitamanas::1048.translation_literal: सीतल (cool) / मंद (gentle) / सुरभि (fragrant) / बह (blew) / बाऊ (wind) / हरषित (delighted) / सुर (radiant beings) / संतन (saints) / मन (mind) / चाऊ (joy) / बन (forest) / कुसुमित (in bloom) / गिरिगन (mountain groups) / मनिआरा (jewel-like, shining) / स्रवहिं (flow) / सकल (all) / सरिताऽमृतधारा (rivers with nectar-streams)
ramacharitamanas::1048.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1048.essence: Ram's arrival makes the whole world feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1048.simple_meaning: Nature itself becomes joyful and beautiful at Ram's birth. The world feels purified, fragrant, and alive with celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1048.simple_insight: When the heart is right, even the world seems to celebrate with you.
ramacharitamanas::1048.detailed_meaning: As Ram's birth approaches in Ayodhya, the scene turns radiant: the air softens, forests bloom, mountains gleam, and rivers seem to flow with nectar. This is not action but atmosphere — creation itself responding to the coming of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1048.modern_relevance: You step outside after rain and the whole street feels washed clean. The air, the trees, even the puddles seem to carry relief — as if something good has just arrived.
ramacharitamanas::1048.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the way the whole world responds to it.

ramacharitamanas::1049.verse_sanskrit: सो अवसर बिरंचि जब जाना। चले सकल सुर साजि बिमाना॥ गगन बिमल संकुल सुर जूथा। गावहिं गुन गंधर्ब बरूथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1049.verse_hindi: जब ब्रह्माजी ने वह (भगवान के प्रकट होने का) अवसर जाना तब (उनके समेत) सारे देवता विमान सजा-सजाकर चले। निर्मल आकाश देवताओं के समूहों से भर गया। गंधर्वों के दल गुणों का गान करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1049.english_translation: When Brahma understood that sacred moment, all the radiant beings came with their flying chariots. The clear sky filled with groups of radiant beings, and the celestial singers sang of divine qualities.
ramacharitamanas::1049.translation_literal: सो (that) / अवसर (moment) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / जब (when) / जाना (knew) / चले (went) / सकल (all) / सुर (radiant beings) / साजि (having prepared) / बिमाना (flying chariots)॥ / गगन (sky) / बिमल (clear) / संकुल (filled) / सुर (radiant beings) / जूथा (groups)॥ / गावहिं (sing) / गुन (qualities) / गंधर्ब (celestial singers) / बरूथा (troops)॥
ramacharitamanas::1049.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1049.essence: Even the heavens gather when Ram appears.
ramacharitamanas::1049.simple_meaning: Brahma and the radiant beings arrive in the sky to witness Ram's birth, and the celestial singers begin praising him.
ramacharitamanas::1049.simple_insight: A sacred moment draws the whole cosmos into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1049.detailed_meaning: The signs of Ram's birth have appeared in Ayodhya. Brahma recognises the moment, and the radiant beings come down in flying chariots. The sky fills with heavenly hosts, and the singers begin praising the divine child.
ramacharitamanas::1049.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet just before the baby’s first cry. Everyone knows something precious has arrived, and the whole atmosphere seems to lean toward it.
ramacharitamanas::1049.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary time to a moment charged with wonder and blessing.

ramacharitamanas::1050.verse_sanskrit: बरषहिं सुमन सुअंजुलि साजी। गहगहि गगन दुंदुभी बाजी॥ अस्तुति करहिं नाग मुनि देवा। बहुबिधि लावहिं निज निज सेवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1050.verse_hindi: और सुंदर अंजलियों में सजा-सजाकर पुष्प बरसाने लगे। आकाश में घमाघम नगाड़े बजने लगे। नाग, मुनि और देवता स्तुति करने लगे और बहुत प्रकार से अपनी-अपनी सेवा (उपहार) भेंट करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1050.english_translation: They showered flowers from beautiful handfuls. Drums thundered in the sky. Nagas, sages, and devas offered praise and presented their many forms of service.
ramacharitamanas::1050.translation_literal: बरषहिं (they shower) / सुमन (flowers) / सुअंजुलि (beautiful handfuls) / साजी (arranged) / गहगहि (thundering) / गगन (sky) / दुंदुभी (drums) / बाजी (were sounded) / अस्तुति (praise) / करहिं (do) / नाग (serpents) / मुनि (sages) / देवा (devas) / बहुबिधि (many kinds) / लावहिं (offer) / निज निज (their own) / सेवा (service)
ramacharitamanas::1050.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1050.essence: Joy erupts when the divine presence appears.
ramacharitamanas::1050.simple_meaning: Flowers rain down, drums sound in the sky, and celestial beings praise Ram and offer their service.
ramacharitamanas::1050.simple_insight: Some moments are so sacred that praise becomes the only fitting response.
ramacharitamanas::1050.detailed_meaning: The heavens have recognised Ram's birth. Flowers fall, drums thunder, and snakes, sages, and devas fill the sky with praise and offerings. This is the joyful overflow before the final declaration that the Lord has appeared.
ramacharitamanas::1050.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after a long-awaited announcement, and everyone reacts at once — applause, tears, relief. The moment is bigger than words, so gratitude becomes the only language left.
ramacharitamanas::1050.insight: It turns reverence into action: praise, offering, and celebration become a single response to the sacred.

ramacharitamanas::1051.verse_sanskrit: सुर समूह बिनती करि पहुँचे निज निज धाम। जगनिवास प्रभु प्रगटे अखिल लोक बिश्राम॥191
ramacharitamanas::1051.verse_hindi: देवताओं के समूह विनती करके अपने-अपने लोक में जा पहुँचे। समस्त लोकों को शांति देने वाले, जगदाधार प्रभु प्रकट हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1051.english_translation: The gathered radiant beings returned to their own realms in prayer. The Lord of the worlds appeared, bringing rest to all worlds.
ramacharitamanas::1051.translation_literal: सुर समूह (gathered radiant beings) / बिनती करि (having prayed) / पहुँचे (reached) / निज निज (their own) / धाम (realms) / जगनिवास (abode of the world) / प्रभु (Lord) / प्रगटे (appeared) / अखिल (all) / लोक (worlds) / बिश्राम (rest)
ramacharitamanas::1051.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1051.essence: The world rests when Ram appears.
ramacharitamanas::1051.simple_meaning: The heavenly beings return home after praying, and Ram appears in the world to bring peace to all beings.
ramacharitamanas::1051.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that the one who comes is not distant, but arrives to steady everything.
ramacharitamanas::1051.detailed_meaning: After the gods finish their prayers and leave for their own realms, the story turns to the reason for their hope: Ram has appeared. This doha is a transition, not the full revelation, preparing for the next verse that describes his form.
ramacharitamanas::1051.modern_relevance: After a long night of worry, the room finally goes quiet and the person everyone was waiting for walks in. The tension eases before anyone even speaks.
ramacharitamanas::1051.insight: It shifts attention from heavenly anticipation to the arrival of the one who brings rest to all life.

ramacharitamanas::1052.verse_sanskrit: भए प्रगट कृपाला दीनदयाला कौसल्या हितकारी। हरषित महतारी मुनि मन हारी अद्भुत रूप बिचारी॥ लोचन अभिरामा तनु घनस्यामा निज आयुध भुजचारी। भूषन बनमाला नयन बिसाला सोभासिंधु खरारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1052.verse_hindi: दीनों पर दया करने वाले, कौसल्याजी के हितकारी कृपालु प्रभु प्रकट हुए। मुनियों के मन को हरने वाले उनके अद्भुत रूप का विचार करके माता हर्ष से भर गई। नेत्रों को आनंद देने वाला मेघ के समान श्याम शरीर था, चारों भुजाओं में अपने (खास) आयुध (धारण किए हुए) थे, (दिव्य) आभूषण और वनमाला पहने थे, बड़े-बड़े नेत्र थे। इस प्रकार शोभा के समुद्र तथा खर राक्षस को मारने वाले भगवान प्रकट हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1052.english_translation: The compassionate, merciful one appeared for Kaushalya's sake. His mother was overjoyed, and the sages' minds were captivated as they contemplated his wondrous form. His eyes delighted the gaze, his body was dark like a rain cloud, his four arms bore his own weapons, he wore ornaments and a forest garland, his eyes were wide, and the destroyer of Khara appeared as a sea of splendor.
ramacharitamanas::1052.translation_literal: भए (became/appeared) / प्रगट (manifest) / कृपाला (the compassionate one) / दीनदयाला (merciful to the humble) / कौसल्या हितकारी (benefactor of Kaushalya) / हरषित (delighted) / महतारी (mother) / मुनि मन हारी (captivating the minds of sages) / अद्भुत रूप (wondrous form) / बिचारी (having contemplated) ॥ लोचन अभिरामा (delighting the eyes) / तनु (body) / घनस्यामा (cloud-dark) / निज आयुध (his own weapons) / भुजचारी (bearing in the arms) / भूषन (ornaments) / बनमाला (forest garland) / नयन बिसाला (wide eyes) / सोभासिंधु (sea of splendor) / खरारी (destroyer of Khara)
ramacharitamanas::1052.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1052.essence: The divine arrives as beauty that comforts the humble.
ramacharitamanas::1052.simple_meaning: Ram appears in a beautiful divine form, and Kaushalya is filled with joy. His presence delights the sages and shows mercy to the humble.
ramacharitamanas::1052.simple_insight: There is comfort in seeing power arrive as tenderness, not threat.
ramacharitamanas::1052.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the long-awaited birth has finally happened. Ram appears before Kaushalya in his divine form, and the room changes completely. The mother is flooded with joy, and even the sages are awed into silence by his beauty and grace.
ramacharitamanas::1052.modern_relevance: After months of waiting in a hospital corridor, the doctor finally says the baby is healthy. Relief, wonder, and tears arrive together. Some arrivals do not just change a room — they transform the heart watching them.
ramacharitamanas::1052.insight: It shifts attention from abstract divinity to a form that can be loved, seen, and welcomed.

ramacharitamanas::1053.verse_sanskrit: कह दुइ कर जोरी अस्तुति तोरी केहि बिधि करौं अनंता। माया गुन ग्यानातीत अमाना बेद पुरान भनंता॥ करुना सुख सागर सब गुन आगर जेहि गावहिं श्रुति संता। सो मम हित लागी जन अनुरागी भयउ प्रगट श्रीकंता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1053.verse_hindi: दोनों हाथ जोड़कर माता कहने लगी- हे अनंत! मैं किस प्रकार तुम्हारी स्तुति करूँ। वेद और पुराण तुम को माया, गुण और ज्ञान से परे और परिमाण रहित बतलाते हैं। श्रुतियाँ और संतजन दया और सुख का समुद्र, सब गुणों का धाम कहकर जिनका गान करते हैं, वही भक्तों पर प्रेम करने वाले लक्ष्मीपति भगवान मेरे कल्याण के लिए प्रकट हुए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1053.english_translation: With both hands joined, Mother said, “How can I praise you, Infinite One? The Vedas and Puranas declare you beyond illusion, qualities, knowledge, and measure. The Vedas and saints sing of you as the ocean of compassion and joy, the treasury of all virtues. For my welfare, the Lord of Lakshmi has appeared, moved by love for his devotees.”
ramacharitamanas::1053.translation_literal: कह (said) / दुइ कर (both hands) / जोरी (joined) / अस्तुति (praise) / तोरी (your) / केहि बिधि (in what way) / करौं (shall I do) / अनंता (O Infinite One) / माया (illusion) / गुन (qualities) / ग्यानातीत (beyond knowledge) / अमाना (immeasurable) / बेद (Vedas) / पुरान (Puranas) / भनंता (declare) / करुना (compassion) / सुख सागर (ocean of joy) / सब गुन आगर (treasury of all virtues) / जेहि (whom) / गावहिं (sing) / श्रुति (Vedas) / संता (saints) / सो (that one) / मम (my) / हित (welfare) / लागी (for) / जन अनुरागी (loving toward devotees) / भयउ (became) / प्रगट (manifest) / श्रीकंता (Lord of Lakshmi)
ramacharitamanas::1053.speaker: Kaushalya
ramacharitamanas::1053.essence: The highest reality becomes near through love for devotees.
ramacharitamanas::1053.simple_meaning: Kaushalya cannot fully describe Ram, because he is beyond measurement and thought. She praises him as the source of compassion, joy, and every good quality, and says he has appeared out of love for devotees.
ramacharitamanas::1053.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing the highest reality is not distant — it comes close out of love.
ramacharitamanas::1053.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Ram’s divine birth, Kaushalya folds her hands before the newborn and tries to praise what cannot be fully praised. She moves from awe to gratitude: the Lord beyond measure has come close for the sake of her welfare and the love of devotees.
ramacharitamanas::1053.modern_relevance: You hold your sleeping child after a long night of fear, and the relief is bigger than words. Some gifts feel so immense that gratitude becomes the only honest prayer.
ramacharitamanas::1053.insight: It shifts praise from description to surrender, showing that devotion begins where language ends.

ramacharitamanas::1054.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मांड निकाया निर्मित माया रोम रोम प्रति बेद कहै। मम उर सो बासी यह उपहासी सुनत धीर मति थिर न रहै॥ उपजा जब ग्याना प्रभु मुसुकाना चरित बहुत बिधि कीन्ह चहै। कहि कथा सुहाई मातु बुझाई जेहि प्रकार सुत प्रेम लहै ॥
ramacharitamanas::1054.verse_hindi: वेद कहते हैं कि तुम्हारे प्रत्येक रोम में माया के रचे हुए अनेकों ब्रह्माण्डों के समूह (भरे) हैं। वे तुम मेरे गर्भ में रहे- इस हँसी की बात के सुनने पर धीर (विवेकी) पुरुषों की बुद्धि भी स्थिर नहीं रहती (विचलित हो जाती है)। जब माता को ज्ञान उत्पन्न हुआ, तब प्रभु मुस्कुराए। वे बहुत प्रकार के चरित्र करना चाहते हैं। अतः उन्होंने (पूर्व जन्म की) सुंदर कथा कहकर माता को समझाया, जिससे उन्हें पुत्र का (वात्सल्य) प्रेम प्राप्त हो (भगवान के प्रति पुत्र भाव हो जाए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1054.english_translation: The Vedas say countless universes are contained in every hair of your body. Hearing that you lived in my womb, even the steady mind cannot remain still. When knowledge arose in Mother, the Lord smiled. He wanted many kinds of divine play, so he told her a lovely story and gently explained things, so she could receive motherly love for the child.
ramacharitamanas::1054.translation_literal: ब्रह्मांड (universes) / निकाया (groups, heaps) / निर्मित (made, formed) / माया (by illusion) / रोम रोम प्रति (for every hair) / बेद (the Vedas) / कहै (say) । मम (my) / उर (womb, heart) / सो (that) / बासी (dweller) / यह (this) / उपहासी (laughable thing) / सुनत (hearing) / धीर (steady) / मति (mind, understanding) / थिर (steady) / न रहै (does not remain) ॥ उपजा (arose) / जब (when) / ग्याना (knowledge) / प्रभु (the Lord) / मुसुकाना (smiled) / चरित (divine play, deeds) / बहुत बिधि (in many ways) / कीन्ह चहै (wanted to do) । कहि (saying) / कथा (story) / सुहाई (lovely, pleasing) / मातु (to the mother) / बुझाई (explained, made understand) / जेहि प्रकार (in such a way that) / सुत (child) / प्रेम (love) / लहै (may receive)
ramacharitamanas::1054.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1054.essence: The immeasurable Lord becomes a child so love can hold him.
ramacharitamanas::1054.simple_meaning: The Lord is vast beyond measure, yet he comes close enough to live in a mother's womb. His greatness and tenderness appear together, and he gently leads Mother into loving him as her child.
ramacharitamanas::1054.simple_insight: Awe and intimacy can live together. The heart can bow to greatness without losing tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::1054.detailed_meaning: After Ram's birth, Kaushalya is overwhelmed by his divine form. She realizes he contains countless universes, yet he has also appeared as her child. Ram smiles and softens the moment, speaking in a way that lets her hold him with motherly love.
ramacharitamanas::1054.modern_relevance: You are holding a newborn and suddenly feel both wonder and protectiveness at once. Something greater than you has become deeply close, and your heart has to learn a new kind of love.
ramacharitamanas::1054.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing divinity as distant to seeing it as intimate and near.

ramacharitamanas::1055.verse_sanskrit: माता पुनि बोली सो मति डोली तजहु तात यह रूपा। कीजै सिसुलीला अति प्रियसीला यह सुख परम अनूपा॥ सुनि बचन सुजाना रोदन ठाना होइ बालक सुरभूपा। यह चरित जे गावहिं हरिपद पावहिं ते न परहिं भवकूपा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1055.verse_hindi: माता की वह बुद्धि बदल गई, तब वह फिर बोली- हे तात! यह रूप छोड़कर अत्यन्त प्रिय बाललीला करो, (मेरे लिए) यह सुख परम अनुपम होगा। (माता का) यह वचन सुनकर देवताओं के स्वामी सुजान भगवान ने बालक (रूप) होकर रोना शुरू कर दिया। (तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं-) जो इस चरित्र का गान करते हैं, वे श्री हरि का पद पाते हैं और (फिर) संसार रूपी कूप में नहीं गिरते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1055.english_translation: Mother spoke again, her mind changed: "Leave this form, dear one, and perform your beloved child-play. For me, this joy would be unmatched." Hearing these words, the wise Lord of the gods began to cry as a child. Tulsidas says: those who sing this story reach Hari's feet and do not fall into the well of worldly existence.
ramacharitamanas::1055.translation_literal: माता (mother) / पुनि (again) / बोली (spoke) / सो (that) / मति (mind) / डोली (changed) / तजहु (leave) / तात (dear one) / यह (this) / रूपा (form) / कीजै (do) / सिसुलीला (child-play) / अति (very) / प्रियसीला (dear-loving) / यह (this) / सुख (joy) / परम (supreme) / अनूपा (matchless) / सुनि (hearing) / बचन (words) / सुजाना (wise one) / रोदन (crying) / ठाना (began) / होइ (becoming) / बालक (child) / सुरभूपा (lord of the gods) / यह (this) / चरित (deed/story) / जे (who) / गावहिं (sing) / हरिपद (Hari's feet) / पावहिं (reach) / ते (they) / न (not) / परहिं (fall) / भवकूपा (well of worldly existence)
ramacharitamanas::1055.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1055.essence: Ram's child-play becomes a rescue for anyone who sings it with devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1055.simple_meaning: Mother asks the child to take up his playful form, and the child begins to cry. The verse ends by saying that singing this divine story leads to Hari and protects one from falling into worldly suffering.
ramacharitamanas::1055.simple_insight: Devotion turns even a story into a refuge. Repeating it with love becomes a way out of suffering.
ramacharitamanas::1055.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, the child form of Ram is being revealed to Mother Yashoda-like devotion in a moment of tenderness. She asks him to stay in child-play, and he responds like a real child. Tulsidas then lifts the scene into a promise: singing this leela carries the heart to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1055.modern_relevance: A parent watches a tired child laugh again after tears, and the whole room softens. Some stories do more than entertain — they steady the heart and keep it from sinking.
ramacharitamanas::1055.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the transforming power of remembering Ram with love.

ramacharitamanas::1056.verse_sanskrit: बिप्र धेनु सुर संत हित लीन्ह मनुज अवतार। निज इच्छा निर्मित तनु माया गुन गो पार ॥
ramacharitamanas::1056.verse_hindi: ब्राह्मण, गो, देवता और संतों के लिए भगवान ने मनुष्य का अवतार लिया। वे (अज्ञानमयी, मलिना) माया और उसके गुण (सत् , रज, तम) और (बाहरी तथा भीतरी) इन्द्रियों से परे हैं। उनका (दिव्य) शरीर अपनी इच्छा से ही बना है (किसी कर्म बंधन से परवश होकर त्रिगुणात्मक भौतिक पदार्थों के द्वारा नहीं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1056.english_translation: For the sake of Brahmins, cows, the radiant beings, and saints, the divine took a human birth. Beyond the veil of appearance and its three qualities, the divine body is formed by its own will.
ramacharitamanas::1056.translation_literal: बिप्र (brahmins) / धेनु (cows) / सुर (radiant beings) / संत (saints) / हित (for the good of) / लीन्ह (took) / मनुज (human) / अवतार (incarnation) / निज (own) / इच्छा (will) / निर्मित (made) / तनु (body) / माया (veil of appearance) / गुन (qualities) / गो (beyond) / पार (beyond)
ramacharitamanas::1056.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1056.essence: Ram enters human life freely, yet remains beyond what binds ordinary beings.
ramacharitamanas::1056.simple_meaning: Ram took a human birth for the good of brahmins, cows, radiant beings, and saints. His body is not bound by the veil of appearance or its three qualities.
ramacharitamanas::1056.simple_insight: You are meeting a presence that chooses to come near, not one forced into form.
ramacharitamanas::1056.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the child’s birth is being revealed as more than a royal event. Tulsidas explains that Ram has entered human life for the protection of the worthy and the devout, while remaining beyond the forces that bind ordinary beings.
ramacharitamanas::1056.modern_relevance: A child is born after years of waiting, and everyone sees only a family celebration. Then you notice how the whole room changes — gentler, brighter, steadier. Some arrivals feel like grace choosing a form.
ramacharitamanas::1056.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as merely human to seeing human form as a chosen act of compassion.

ramacharitamanas::1057.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सिसु रुदन परम प्रिय बानी। संभ्रम चलि आईं सब रानी॥ हरषित जहँ तहँ धाईं दासी। आनँद मगन सकल पुरबासी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1057.verse_hindi: बच्चे के रोने की बहुत ही प्यारी ध्वनि सुनकर सब रानियाँ उतावली होकर दौड़ी चली आईं। दासियाँ हर्षित होकर जहाँ-तहाँ दौड़ीं। सारे पुरवासी आनंद में मग्न हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1057.english_translation: Hearing the child’s cry, all the queens hurried over. The maids ran here and there with joy. All the people of the city were absorbed in delight.
ramacharitamanas::1057.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सिसु (child) / रुदन (crying) / परम प्रिय बानी (most beloved sound) / संभ्रम (in haste) / चलि आईं (came running) / सब (all) / रानी (queens)॥ / हरषित (joyful) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / धाईं (ran) / दासी (maids) / आनँद (delight) / मगन (absorbed) / सकल (all) / पुरबासी (city-dwellers)॥
ramacharitamanas::1057.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1057.essence: A child’s cry can awaken an entire city to joy.
ramacharitamanas::1057.simple_meaning: The newborn’s cry fills the palace with joy. The queens rush in, the servants run about happily, and the whole city rejoices.
ramacharitamanas::1057.simple_insight: A child’s arrival can turn an entire household into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1057.detailed_meaning: Ram has just been born in Ayodhya. The first sound of the baby’s cry reaches the palace, and the queens, maids, and townspeople all move at once in joy. This verse is a festive scene, not the main teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::1057.modern_relevance: A hospital hallway goes quiet, then someone hears the first cry of a newborn. Relief spreads instantly — through parents, relatives, nurses, everyone waiting outside.
ramacharitamanas::1057.insight: It frames a sacred arrival as shared public joy, not private news.

ramacharitamanas::1058.verse_sanskrit: दसरथ पुत्रजन्म सुनि काना। मानहु ब्रह्मानंद समाना॥ परम प्रेम मन पुलक सरीरा। चाहत उठन करत मति धीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1058.verse_hindi: राजा दशरथजी पुत्र का जन्म कानों से सुनकर मानो ब्रह्मानंद में समा गए। मन में अतिशय प्रेम है, शरीर पुलकित हो गया। (आनंद में अधीर हुई) बुद्धि को धीरज देकर (और प्रेम में शिथिल हुए शरीर को संभालकर) वे उठना चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1058.english_translation: Hearing that Dasharath's son was born, he felt as if immersed in Brahmananda. His heart overflowed with deep love; his body thrilled with delight, and he gathered his mind to rise.
ramacharitamanas::1058.translation_literal: दसरथ (Dasharath's) / पुत्रजन्म (son's birth) / सुनि (hearing) / काना (ears) / मानहु (as if) / ब्रह्मानंद (Brahmananda) / समाना (immersed) ॥ / परम (great) / प्रेम (love) / मन (mind) / पुलक (thrilled) / सरीरा (body) / चाहत (wishing) / उठन (to rise) / करत (doing) / मति (mind) / धीरा (steady) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1058.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1058.essence: True joy makes the body tremble before the mind can speak.
ramacharitamanas::1058.simple_meaning: Dasharath hears of his son's birth and is overwhelmed with joy. Love fills his mind, his body shivers with delight, and he gathers himself to rise.
ramacharitamanas::1058.simple_insight: Joy can be so full it moves the whole body before the mind catches up.
ramacharitamanas::1058.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath hears that a son has been born. The news hits him like a wave of sacred joy. Love, relief, and awe rise together, and even his body responds before he can stand.
ramacharitamanas::1058.modern_relevance: You get the message you have waited months for, and your chest tightens before you even smile. Some happiness arrives before language does.
ramacharitamanas::1058.insight: It shows how deep joy can overpower the body and then gather the mind into stillness.

ramacharitamanas::1059.verse_sanskrit: जाकर नाम सुनत सुभ होई। मोरें गृह आवा प्रभु सोई॥ परमानंद पूरि मन राजा। कहा बोलाइ बजावहु बाजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1059.verse_hindi: जिनका नाम सुनने से ही कल्याण होता है, वही प्रभु मेरे घर आए हैं। (यह सोचकर) राजा का मन परम आनंद से पूर्ण हो गया। उन्होंने बाजे वालों को बुलाकर कहा कि बाजा बजाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1059.english_translation: The one whose name brings blessing has come to my home. The king's mind overflowed with supreme joy, and he called for the musicians to play.
ramacharitamanas::1059.translation_literal: जाकर (whose) / नाम (name) / सुनत (hearing) / सुभ (auspicious) / होई (becomes) / मोरें (my) / गृह (home) / आवा (has come) / प्रभु (lord) / सोई (that same one) / परमानंद (supreme joy) / पूरि (filled) / मन (mind) / राजा (king) / कहा (said) / बोलाइ (calling) / बजावहु (play) / बाजा (musical instruments)
ramacharitamanas::1059.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1059.essence: Recognising the divine arrival turns longing into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1059.simple_meaning: The king realises that Ram has come to his home, and he is so overjoyed that he orders music to begin.
ramacharitamanas::1059.simple_insight: Joy becomes celebration the moment the heart recognises what it has received.
ramacharitamanas::1059.detailed_meaning: At Dasharath's palace in Ayodhya, the long-awaited child has been born. Hearing that the blessed one has arrived in his house, the king is flooded with joy and immediately calls for music. The scene turns private longing into public celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1059.modern_relevance: You get the message that the person you waited for has arrived at the hospital entrance. Relief hits first, then the urge to tell everyone. Joy wants sound.
ramacharitamanas::1059.insight: It shifts the mind from silent relief to active celebration when grace is recognised.

ramacharitamanas::1060.verse_sanskrit: गुर बसिष्ठ कहँ गयउ हँकारा। आए द्विजन सहित नृपद्वारा॥ अनुपम बालक देखेन्हि जाई। रूप रासि गुन कहि न सिराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1060.verse_hindi: गुरु वशिष्ठजी के पास बुलावा गया। वे ब्राह्मणों को साथ लिए राजद्वार पर आए। उन्होंने जाकर अनुपम बालक को देखा, जो रूप की राशि है और जिसके गुण कहने से समाप्त नहीं होते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1060.english_translation: A summons was sent to Guru Vashishtha. He came to the royal gate with the brahmins. There they saw the incomparable child; his beauty was a treasure, and his virtues could not be fully described.
ramacharitamanas::1060.translation_literal: गुरु (teacher) / बसिष्ठ कहँ (to Vashishtha) / गयउ (was sent) / हँकारा (summons) । / आए (came) / द्विजन (brahmins) / सहित (with) / नृपद्वारा (to the king's gate) ॥ / अनुपम (incomparable) / बालक (child) / देखेन्हि (they saw) / जाई (going) । / रूप (beauty) / रासि (heap/treasure) / गुन (virtues) / कहि (saying) / न (not) / सिराई (end) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1060.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1060.essence: Beauty and virtue can exceed every attempt to describe them.
ramacharitamanas::1060.simple_meaning: Vashishtha is called to the palace, comes with the brahmins, and sees the newborn child whose beauty and virtues seem beyond words.
ramacharitamanas::1060.simple_insight: Some moments feel too full for language. Wonder itself becomes the only honest response.
ramacharitamanas::1060.detailed_meaning: At Dasharath's palace, the celebration turns sacred. Vashishtha arrives with the brahmins to witness the newborn prince, and even the sight of the child overwhelms description. This verse prepares the rites that will follow.
ramacharitamanas::1060.modern_relevance: You step into a hospital room and see a newborn for the first time. Everyone lowers their voice, because the moment feels larger than speech.
ramacharitamanas::1060.insight: It shifts attention from explanation to reverence, letting wonder come before analysis.

ramacharitamanas::1061.verse_sanskrit: नंदीमुख सराध करि जातकरम सब कीन्ह। हाटक धेनु बसन मनि नृप बिप्रन्ह कहँ दीन्ह ॥
ramacharitamanas::1061.verse_hindi: फिर राजा ने नांदीमुख श्राद्ध करके सब जातकर्म-संस्कार आदि किए और ब्राह्मणों को सोना, गो, वस्त्र और मणियों का दान दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1061.english_translation: Then the king performed the nandi-mukha shraddha and all the birth rites, and gave gold, cows, clothes, and jewels to the Brahmins.
ramacharitamanas::1061.translation_literal: नंदीमुख (nandi-mukha rite) / सराध (shraddha offering) / करि (having done) / जातकरम (birth rites) / सब (all) / कीन्ह (performed) / हाटक (gold) / धेनु (cow) / बसन (clothes) / मनि (jewels) / नृप (king) / बिप्रन्ह कहँ (to the Brahmins) / दीन्ह (gave)
ramacharitamanas::1061.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1061.simple_meaning: King Dasharath completed the birth ceremonies and gave gifts to the Brahmins.
ramacharitamanas::1061.simple_insight: Joy becomes complete when it is expressed through gratitude and generosity.
ramacharitamanas::1061.detailed_meaning: Dasharath’s long-awaited joy over Ram’s birth now moves into ritual action. He completes the family ceremonies, honors the Brahmins, and gives generous gifts. The verse is part of the celebration, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1061.modern_relevance: A long-awaited baby arrives, and the house fills with guests, prayers, and gifts. The happiness is not kept private; it spills outward in thanks and sharing.
ramacharitamanas::1061.insight: It shifts celebration from private excitement to public gratitude and giving.

ramacharitamanas::1062.verse_sanskrit: ध्वज पताक तोरन पुर छावा। कहि न जाइ जेहि भाँति बनावा॥ सुमनबृष्टि अकास तें होई। ब्रह्मानंद मगन सब लोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1062.verse_hindi: ध्वजा, पताका और तोरणों से नगर छा गया। जिस प्रकार से वह सजाया गया, उसका तो वर्णन ही नहीं हो सकता। आकाश से फूलों की वर्षा हो रही है, सब लोग ब्रह्मानंद में मग्न हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1062.english_translation: The city was covered with banners, flags, and arches. No one could describe how it was decorated. Flowers rained from the sky, and everyone was immersed in bliss.
ramacharitamanas::1062.translation_literal: ध्वज (banners) / पताक (flags) / तोरन (arches) / पुर (city) / छावा (covered) / कहि (said) / न (not) / जाइ (can be told) / जेहि (which) / भाँति (manner) / बनावा (was made) / सुमनबृष्टि (rain of flowers) / अकास (sky) / तें (from) / होई (happened) / ब्रह्मानंद (supreme bliss) / मगन (immersed) / सब (all) / लोई (people)
ramacharitamanas::1062.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1062.essence: Beauty and joy can transform an entire city at once.
ramacharitamanas::1062.simple_meaning: The whole city is decorated for celebration, flowers fall from the sky, and everyone feels overwhelmed with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1062.simple_insight: Joy spreads through a whole community when something sacred and beautiful arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1062.detailed_meaning: Ram's homecoming celebrations are underway in Ayodhya. The city is dressed with banners, arches, and flags, and flowers fall from the sky. This is a scene of public joy, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::1062.modern_relevance: A neighborhood lights up for a wedding, balconies fill with garlands, and strangers smile at each other in the street. Some moments change the mood of an entire city.
ramacharitamanas::1062.insight: It shifts attention from private feeling to shared celebration.

ramacharitamanas::1063.verse_sanskrit: बृंद बृंद मिलि चलीं लोगाईं। सहज सिंगार किएँ उठि धाईं॥ कनक कलस मंगल भरि थारा। गावत पैठहिं भूप दुआरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1063.verse_hindi: स्त्रियाँ झुंड की झुंड मिलकर चलीं। स्वाभाविक श्रृंगार किए ही वे उठ दौड़ीं। सोने का कलश लेकर और थालों में मंगल द्रव्य भरकर गाती हुईं राजद्वार में प्रवेश करती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1063.english_translation: Groups of women came together and hurried out in natural adornment. Carrying golden vessels and trays filled with auspicious offerings, they entered the king's gate singing.
ramacharitamanas::1063.translation_literal: बृंद बृंद (groups and groups) / मिलि (together) / चलीं (went) / लोगाईं (women) / सहज (natural) / सिंगार (adornment) / किएँ (having done) / उठि (rising) / धाईं (hurried) / कनक (golden) / कलस (vessels) / मंगल (auspicious) / भरि (filled) / थारा (trays) / गावत (singing) / पैठहिं (enter) / भूप (king) / दुआरा (gate)
ramacharitamanas::1063.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1063.essence: Celebration spills outward and pulls everyone into it.
ramacharitamanas::1063.simple_meaning: Women gather quickly, dressed simply, carrying golden vessels and trays of auspicious offerings as they sing and enter the king's gate.
ramacharitamanas::1063.simple_insight: Joy becomes a shared movement here, where celebration itself feels alive and overflowing.
ramacharitamanas::1063.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is in festive uproar after the prince's birth. Women from the city gather in groups, dress quickly, take golden vessels and offering trays, and hurry toward the palace singing. This is one small living detail in the larger celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1063.modern_relevance: At a family celebration, people stop what they are doing, grab whatever offerings they have, and head out singing. The joy is so full it pulls everyone into motion.
ramacharitamanas::1063.insight: It shifts the scene from private happiness to communal celebration, showing joy as something shared in action.

ramacharitamanas::1064.verse_sanskrit: करि आरति नेवछावरि करहीं। बार बार सिसु चरनन्हि परहीं॥ मागध सूत बंदिगन गायक। पावन गुन गावहिं रघुनायक ॥
ramacharitamanas::1064.verse_hindi: वे आरती करके निछावर करती हैं और बार-बार बच्चे के चरणों पर गिरती हैं। मागध, सूत, वन्दीजन और गवैये रघुकुल के स्वामी के पवित्र गुणों का गान करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1064.english_translation: They perform the aarti and offer gifts, bowing again and again at the child's feet. Bards, heralds, praise-singers, and singers sing the pure virtues of the Lord of the Raghu clan.
ramacharitamanas::1064.translation_literal: करि (doing) / आरति (aarti) / नेवछावरि (offering gifts) / करहीं (they do) / बार बार (again and again) / सिसु (child) / चरनन्हि (at the feet) / परहीं (they fall) ॥ मागध (bards) / सूत (heralds) / बंदिगन (praise-singers) / गायक (singers) / पावन (pure) / गुन (virtues) / गावहिं (sing) / रघुनायक (Lord of the Raghu clan) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1064.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1064.essence: Love cannot stay private; it turns into worship and song.
ramacharitamanas::1064.simple_meaning: The people celebrate the child Ram with worship, gifts, bowing, and songs of praise.
ramacharitamanas::1064.simple_insight: Joy deepens when gratitude becomes action, song, and reverence all at once.
ramacharitamanas::1064.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is overflowing with celebration after Ram's birth. People worship the child, shower gifts, bow at his feet, and singers fill the streets with praise. This verse is part of the festival atmosphere, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1064.modern_relevance: A family gathers around a newborn, and everyone wants to hold, bless, photograph, and sing over the baby. The feeling is bigger than words, and devotion spills out naturally.
ramacharitamanas::1064.insight: It shows how love becomes public celebration: praise, gifts, and repeated bowing.

ramacharitamanas::1065.verse_sanskrit: सर्बस दान दीन्ह सब काहू। जेहिं पावा राखा नहिं ताहू॥ मृगमद चंदन कुंकुम कीचा। मची सकल बीथिन्ह बिच बीचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1065.verse_hindi: राजा ने सब किसी को भरपूर दान दिया। जिसने पाया उसने भी नहीं रखा (लुटा दिया)। (नगर की) सभी गलियों के बीच-बीच में कस्तूरी, चंदन और केसर की कीच मच गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1065.english_translation: The king gave gifts to everyone. Whoever received them did not keep them. Musk, sandalwood, and saffron were scattered through the streets.
ramacharitamanas::1065.translation_literal: सर्बस (all kinds of) / दान (gifts) / दीन्ह (gave) / सब (all) / काहू (to everyone) / जेहिं (whoever) / पावा (received) / राखा (kept) / नहिं (not) / ताहू (that too) / मृगमद (musk) / चंदन (sandalwood) / कुंकुम (saffron) / कीचा (paste) / मची (spread) / सकल (all) / बीथिन्ह (streets) / बिच बीचा (in the middle)
ramacharitamanas::1065.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1065.essence: Abundance spreads fastest when no one tries to keep it.
ramacharitamanas::1065.simple_meaning: Generosity filled the city so completely that gifts were immediately passed on, and fragrant substances were spread everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::1065.simple_insight: Joy becomes contagious when giving is abundant.
ramacharitamanas::1065.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is celebrating Ram's birth. The city overflows with gifts, and people do not hoard what they receive; they pass it along in delight. Even the streets are marked with fragrant offerings, showing a festival that spreads through everyone.
ramacharitamanas::1065.modern_relevance: A neighborhood wedding spills into the lane, and strangers are handed sweets, flowers, and folded notes. Nobody clutches anything. Celebration moves from hand to hand and becomes shared atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::1065.insight: It shows how true celebration dissolves possessiveness and turns receiving into sharing.

ramacharitamanas::1066.verse_sanskrit: गृह गृह बाज बधाव सुभ प्रगटे सुषमा कंद। हरषवंत सब जहँ तहँ नगर नारि नर बृंद ॥
ramacharitamanas::1066.verse_hindi: घर-घर मंगलमय बधावा बजने लगा, क्योंकि शोभा के मूल भगवान प्रकट हुए हैं। नगर के स्त्री-पुरुषों के झुंड के झुंड जहाँ-तहाँ आनंदमग्न हो रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1066.english_translation: Auspicious drums sounded in every home, for the source of beauty had appeared. Men and women throughout the city were filled with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1066.translation_literal: गृह (house) / गृह (house) / बाज (drums) / बधाव (auspicious welcome) / सुभ (auspicious) / प्रगटे (appeared) / सुषमा (beauty, splendor) / कंद (root, source) / हरषवंत (joyful) / सब (all) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / नगर (city) / नारि (women) / नर (men) / बृंद (groups)
ramacharitamanas::1066.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1066.essence: A true arrival makes an entire city rejoice.
ramacharitamanas::1066.simple_meaning: The city erupts in celebration because a beautiful, blessed birth has taken place. Everyone, everywhere, is overjoyed.
ramacharitamanas::1066.simple_insight: Joy spreads fastest when people feel something precious has arrived for the whole community.
ramacharitamanas::1066.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the long-awaited birth has finally happened. Drums sound in every house, and the whole city—women and men alike—breaks into celebration. This verse paints the public joy before the next details of the royal births unfold.
ramacharitamanas::1066.modern_relevance: A neighborhood group chat lights up after good news everyone has been waiting for. Strangers become neighbors for a moment, and shared relief turns into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1066.insight: It shifts attention from private happiness to a joy that belongs to everyone around you.

ramacharitamanas::1067.verse_sanskrit: कैकयसुता सुमित्रा दोऊ। सुंदर सुत जनमत भैं ओऊ॥ वह सुख संपति समय समाजा। कहि न सकइ सारद अहिराजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1067.verse_hindi: कैकेयी और सुमित्रा- इन दोनों ने भी सुंदर पुत्रों को जन्म दिया। उस सुख, सम्पत्ति, समय और समाज का वर्णन सरस्वती और सर्पों के राजा शेषजी भी नहीं कर सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1067.english_translation: Kaikeyi's daughter and Sumitra both gave birth to beautiful sons. Even Saraswati and Sheshanaga cannot describe that joy, wealth, season, and gathering.
ramacharitamanas::1067.translation_literal: कैकयसुता (Kaikeyi's daughter) / सुमित्रा (Sumitra) / दोऊ (both) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुत (sons) / जनमत (being born) / भैं (became) / ओऊ (those) ॥ / वह (that) / सुख (joy) / संपति (wealth) / समय (time/season) / समाजा (gathering) / कहि (to say) / न सकइ (cannot) / सारद (Saraswati) / अहिराजा (king of serpents, Sheshanaga) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1067.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1067.essence: Some births create a joy too vast for speech.
ramacharitamanas::1067.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi and Sumitra each gave birth to noble sons. The joy and grandeur of that moment were beyond words.
ramacharitamanas::1067.simple_insight: Some arrivals are so full of blessing that language itself feels too small.
ramacharitamanas::1067.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the royal family is overflowing with joy after Ram's birth. This verse widens the celebration to Kaikeyi and Sumitra, whose sons Bharata and Lakshman are also born. The scene is so rich that even divine speech cannot fully capture it.
ramacharitamanas::1067.modern_relevance: A hospital room fills with relieved laughter after a safe delivery, and everyone keeps repeating, 'He's here,' because the feeling is larger than the words.
ramacharitamanas::1067.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the sacred fullness surrounding it.

ramacharitamanas::1068.verse_sanskrit: अवधपुरी सोहइ एहि भाँती। प्रभुहि मिलन आई जनु राती॥ देखि भानु जनु मन सकुचानी। तदपि बनी संध्या अनुमानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1068.verse_hindi: अवधपुरी इस प्रकार सुशोभित हो रही है, मानो रात्रि प्रभु से मिलने आई हो और सूर्य को देखकर मानो मन में सकुचा गई हो, परन्तु फिर भी मन में विचार कर वह मानो संध्या बन (कर रह) गई हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1068.english_translation: Ayodhya shines like this: night has come to meet the Lord, and seeing the sun, it blushes and becomes dusk.
ramacharitamanas::1068.translation_literal: अवधपुरी (Ayodhya city) / सोहइ (shines) / एहि भाँती (in this way) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / मिलन (meeting) / आई (came) / जनु (as if) / राती (night) / देखि (seeing) / भानु (the sun) / जनु (as if) / मन (mind) / सकुचानी (became shy) / तदपि (even then) / बनी (became) / संध्या (dusk) / अनुमानी (by thinking)
ramacharitamanas::1068.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1068.essence: The whole city turns into a welcome for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1068.simple_meaning: Ayodhya is described like a bride at dusk: night seems to arrive to meet the Lord, and the fading day turns into evening out of shy beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1068.simple_insight: Beauty can be so complete that even time feels like it is bowing.
ramacharitamanas::1068.detailed_meaning: The city of Ayodhya is preparing for Ram's birth. Tulsidas paints the whole sky and city as if they are alive with longing: night arrives like a visitor, the sun withdraws, and dusk settles in as part of the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1068.modern_relevance: A house glows warm before the first guest arrives, and the whole street seems to soften with anticipation. Some moments change the atmosphere before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::1068.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary scenery to a world made sacred by expectation.

ramacharitamanas::1069.verse_sanskrit: अगर धूप बहु जनु अँधिआरी। उड़इ अबीर मनहुँ अरुनारी॥ मंदिर मनि समूह जनु तारा। नृप गृह कलस सो इंदु उदारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1069.verse_hindi: अगर की धूप का बहुत सा धुआँ मानो (संध्या का) अंधकार है और जो अबीर उड़ रहा है, वह उसकी ललाई है। महलों में जो मणियों के समूह हैं, वे मानो तारागण हैं। राज महल का जो कलश है, वही मानो श्रेष्ठ चन्द्रमा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1069.english_translation: The agarwood smoke is like deep twilight. The drifting vermilion is like the red glow of dusk. The jewels in the palace are like stars, and the royal finial is like a glorious moon.
ramacharitamanas::1069.translation_literal: अगर (agarwood) / धूप (incense smoke) / बहु (much) / जनु (as if) / अँधिआरी (darkness) / उड़इ (drifts) / अबीर (vermilion powder) / मनहुँ (as if) / अरुनारी (reddish dusk) / मंदिर (palace) / मनि (jewels) / समूह (cluster) / जनु (as if) / तारा (stars) / नृप गृह (king's house) / कलस (finial) / सो (that) / इंदु (moon) / उदारा (splendid)
ramacharitamanas::1069.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1069.essence: Even a palace can look like the sky when joy fills it.
ramacharitamanas::1069.simple_meaning: The palace is decorated so richly that incense smoke, red powder, jewels, and the finial all look like parts of the sky.
ramacharitamanas::1069.simple_insight: Beauty can be so complete that it turns a room into a world.
ramacharitamanas::1069.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is being prepared for Ram's arrival. Tulsidas lingers on the palace decorations: incense, vermilion, jewels, and the royal finial all become images of twilight, stars, and the moon. The verse is pure scene-painting, building wonder before the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1069.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall glowing with lamps, flowers, and music, and the whole place feels lifted out of ordinary time. That is the mood here.
ramacharitamanas::1069.insight: It teaches the mind to see ordinary objects as part of a larger sacred scene.

ramacharitamanas::1070.verse_sanskrit: भवन बेदधुनि अति मृदु बानी। जनु खग मुखर समयँ जनु सानी॥ कौतुक देखि पतंग भुलाना। एक मास तेइँ जात न जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1070.verse_hindi: राजभवन में जो अति कोमल वाणी से वेदध्वनि हो रही है, वही मानो समय से (समयानुकूल) सनी हुई पक्षियों की चहचहाहट है। यह कौतुक देखकर सूर्य भी (अपनी चाल) भूल गए। एक महीना उन्होंने जाता हुआ न जाना (अर्थात उन्हें एक महीना वहीं बीत गया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1070.english_translation: The palace echoed with very soft recitation of the Vedas, like birds singing in season. Watching this wonder, the sun forgot its course. One month passed without anyone noticing.
ramacharitamanas::1070.translation_literal: भवन (palace) / बेदधुनि (Veda-sound) / अति (very) / मृदु (soft) / बानी (speech, voice) / जनु (as if) / खग (birds) / मुखर (noisy, singing) / समयँ (in season, at the right time) / जनु (as if) / सानी (mixed, blended)॥ कौतुक (wonder, marvel) / देखि (seeing) / पतंग (sun) / भुलाना (forgot) / एक मास (one month) / तेइँ (there itself) / जात (passing) / न (not) / जाना (knew)
ramacharitamanas::1070.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1070.essence: Beauty so complete makes time disappear.
ramacharitamanas::1070.simple_meaning: The palace was filled with soft Vedic sound, like birds singing at the right season. The scene was so wondrous that even the sun seemed to lose track of time.
ramacharitamanas::1070.simple_insight: Wonder can make time feel suspended, as if the world itself is holding its breath.
ramacharitamanas::1070.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is being described in its perfect, dreamlike splendor around Ram's birth. The palace sounds, sights, and sacred rhythm are so beautiful that the sun itself seems to pause. This verse deepens the atmosphere, not the teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1070.modern_relevance: You walk into a temple courtyard at dawn and hear a chant rise through the air. For a moment, your phone, your schedule, and the clock all feel far away.
ramacharitamanas::1070.insight: It shifts attention from measurement to marvel, showing how sacred atmosphere can dissolve ordinary time.

ramacharitamanas::1071.verse_sanskrit: मास दिवस कर दिवस भा मरम न जानइ कोइ। रथ समेत रबि थाकेउ निसा कवन बिधि होइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1071.verse_hindi: महीने भर का दिन हो गया। इस रहस्य को कोई नहीं जानता। सूर्य अपने रथ सहित वहीं रुक गए, फिर रात किस तरह होती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1071.english_translation: A month-long day passed. No one understood the mystery. The sun, with its chariot, stood still—so how could night ever come?
ramacharitamanas::1071.translation_literal: मास (month) / दिवस (day) / कर (of) / दिवस (day) / भा (became) / मरम (mystery) / न (not) / जानइ (knows) / कोइ (anyone) / रथ (chariot) / समेत (along with) / रबि (sun) / थाकेउ (stopped) / निसा (night) / कवन (which) / बिधि (way) / होइ (happens)
ramacharitamanas::1071.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1071.essence: A sacred joy can make time itself seem to stop.
ramacharitamanas::1071.simple_meaning: Time seems to stop in wonder. The day stretches on so long that night cannot arrive, and no one can explain why.
ramacharitamanas::1071.simple_insight: Wonder can make even time feel suspended.
ramacharitamanas::1071.detailed_meaning: At King Janak’s palace, the wedding festivities around Ram and Sita become so radiant that the whole scene feels timeless. The narrator says the day lasted like a month, as if the sun itself had paused, because no one could grasp the mystery of the joy unfolding.
ramacharitamanas::1071.modern_relevance: You are at a wedding where the music, lights, and laughter make you lose track of hours. The night feels unreal because the moment is too full to measure.
ramacharitamanas::1071.insight: It shifts attention from clock-time to the felt fullness of an experience.

ramacharitamanas::1072.verse_sanskrit: यह रहस्य काहूँ नहिं जाना। दिनमनि चले करत गुनगाना॥ देखि महोत्सव सुर मुनि नागा। चले भवन बरनत निज भागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1072.verse_hindi: यह रहस्य किसी ने नहीं जाना। सूर्यदेव (भगवान श्री रामजी का) गुणगान करते हुए चले। यह महोत्सव देखकर देवता, मुनि और नाग अपने भाग्य की सराहना करते हुए अपने-अपने घर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1072.english_translation: No one understood this mystery. The sun moved on, singing Ram's praise. Seeing the great celebration, the gods, sages, and serpents returned home, praising their own good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::1072.translation_literal: यह (this) / रहस्य (mystery) / काहूँ (by anyone) / नहिं (not) / जाना (known) । / दिनमनि (the sun) / चले (moved) / करत (doing) / गुनगाना (singing praise) ॥ / देखि (seeing) / महोत्सव (great celebration) / सुर (gods) / मुनि (sages) / नागा (serpents) । / चले (went) / भवन (to their homes) / बरनत (praising) / निज (their own) / भागा (fortune) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1072.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1072.essence: Some mysteries are not solved; they are honored.
ramacharitamanas::1072.simple_meaning: No one could grasp the wonder of what happened. Even the sun moved on while praising Ram, and the gods, sages, and serpents went home delighted by the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1072.simple_insight: Some moments are too full for explanation; reverence is the only honest response.
ramacharitamanas::1072.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram's birth has turned time strange: the day has stretched beyond measure, and the mystery still cannot be explained. Even the sun resumes its course in praise, while gods, sages, and serpents leave, awed by the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1072.modern_relevance: You walk out of a wedding, a temple hall, or a hospital room where something larger than words just happened. Nobody can fully explain it, so everyone leaves quieter, kinder, and a little more grateful.
ramacharitamanas::1072.insight: It shifts attention from explanation to wonder, letting reverence close what the mind cannot solve.

ramacharitamanas::1073.verse_sanskrit: औरउ एक कहउँ निज चोरी। सुनु गिरिजा अति दृढ़ मति तोरी॥ काकभुसुंडि संग हम दोऊ। मनुजरूप जानइ नहिं कोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1073.verse_hindi: हे पार्वती! तुम्हारी बुद्धि (श्री रामजी के चरणों में) बहुत दृढ़ है, इसलिए मैं और भी अपनी एक चोरी (छिपाव) की बात कहता हूँ, सुनो। काकभुशुण्डि और मैं दोनों वहाँ साथ-साथ थे, परन्तु मनुष्य रूप में होने के कारण हमें कोई जान न सका ॥
ramacharitamanas::1073.english_translation: O Parvati, your mind is very firm, so I will tell you one more secret. Kakabhushundi and I were both there together, but in human form no one could recognize us.
ramacharitamanas::1073.translation_literal: औरउ (also) / एक (one) / कहउँ (I tell) / निज (my) / चोरी (secret) / सुनु (listen) / गिरिजा (Parvati) / अति (very) / दृढ़ (firm) / मति (mind) / तोरी (your) / काकभुसुंडि (Kakabhushundi) / संग (with) / हम (we) / दोऊ (both) / मनुजरूप (human form) / जानइ (knows) / नहिं (not) / कोऊ (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::1073.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::1073.essence: Presence can be real even when no one recognizes it.
ramacharitamanas::1073.simple_meaning: Shiva tells Parvati another hidden detail: he and Kakabhushundi were present together in human form, but nobody recognized them.
ramacharitamanas::1073.simple_insight: Some truths stay hidden even when they are right in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::1073.detailed_meaning: In Shiva’s telling to Parvati, he adds a private secret about the scene being described. He says he and Kakabhushundi were there together in human form, yet everyone failed to पहचान them. The line deepens the mystery, not the teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1073.modern_relevance: You sit in a room with people who know only your surface. The truest part of what is happening can be invisible to everyone present, even to the ones inside it.
ramacharitamanas::1073.insight: It shifts attention from outward appearance to hidden presence and deeper recognition.

ramacharitamanas::1074.verse_sanskrit: परमानंद प्रेम सुख फूले। बीथिन्ह फिरहिं मगन मन भूले॥ यह सुभ चरित जान पै सोई। कृपा राम कै जापर होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1074.verse_hindi: परम आनंद और प्रेम के सुख में फूले हुए हम दोनों मगन मन से (मस्त हुए) गलियों में (तन-मन की सुधि) भूले हुए फिरते थे, परन्तु यह शुभ चरित्र वही जान सकता है, जिस पर श्री रामजी की कृपा हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1074.english_translation: We were both blooming in the joy of supreme bliss and love, wandering through the streets with minds lost in ecstasy. Only one on whom Ram's grace has fallen can know this blessed story.
ramacharitamanas::1074.translation_literal: परमानंद (supreme bliss) / प्रेम (love) / सुख (joy) / फूले (bloomed) / बीथिन्ह (in the streets) / फिरहिं (wander) / मगन (absorbed) / मन (mind) / भूले (forgotten) / यह (this) / सुभ (auspicious) / चरित (deed/story) / जान (know) / पै (only) / सोई (that one) / कृपा (grace) / राम कै (of Ram) / जापर (on whom) / होई (happens)
ramacharitamanas::1074.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1074.essence: Ram's grace lets love become its own understanding.
ramacharitamanas::1074.simple_meaning: We were lost in the joy of love and bliss, walking through the streets without awareness of anything else. Only Ram's grace lets someone truly know this blessed story.
ramacharitamanas::1074.simple_insight: Some truths are understood only by hearts softened by grace, not by effort alone.
ramacharitamanas::1074.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's celebration, the narrator recalls moving through the streets with minds overwhelmed by love and joy. The scene is so radiant that ordinary awareness disappears. The verse closes by saying that only Ram's grace lets a person truly grasp this sacred event.
ramacharitamanas::1074.modern_relevance: You leave a wedding feeling strangely weightless, still smiling at nothing in particular. Later, you realise the day was not just beautiful — it changed how you see love, and only a softened heart can really understand why.
ramacharitamanas::1074.insight: It shifts the reader from trying to explain devotion to recognising that grace makes devotion intelligible.

ramacharitamanas::1075.verse_sanskrit: तेहि अवसर जो जेहि बिधि आवा। दीन्ह भूप जो जेहि मन भावा॥ गज रथ तुरग हेम गो हीरा। दीन्हे नृप नानाबिधि चीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1075.verse_hindi: उस अवसर पर जो जिस प्रकार आया और जिसके मन को जो अच्छा लगा, राजा ने उसे वही दिया। हाथी, रथ, घोड़े, सोना, गायें, हीरे और भाँति-भाँति के वस्त्र राजा ने दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1075.english_translation: At that time, whoever came in whatever way, the king gave them whatever pleased their heart. The king gave elephants, chariots, horses, gold, cows, diamonds, and many kinds of clothes.
ramacharitamanas::1075.translation_literal: तेहि अवसर (at that time) / जो (whoever) / जेहि बिधि (in whatever way) / आवा (came) / दीन्ह (gave) / भूप (the king) / जो (whatever) / जेहि मन भावा (pleased each heart) / गज (elephants) / रथ (chariots) / तुरग (horses) / हेम (gold) / गो (cows) / हीरा (diamonds) / दीन्हे (were given) / नृप (the king) / नानाबिधि (of many kinds) / चीरा (clothes)
ramacharitamanas::1075.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1075.essence: True generosity gives what each heart can receive.
ramacharitamanas::1075.simple_meaning: The king freely gave each visitor what suited them best: gifts, animals, wealth, and clothes.
ramacharitamanas::1075.simple_insight: Generosity becomes real when it meets people where they are, not where you wish they were.
ramacharitamanas::1075.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the celebration around Ram's story has drawn many people in. Raja Dasharath responds with open-handed generosity, giving each visitor what they most desire. The scene shows a kingdom flowing with joy, abundance, and goodwill.
ramacharitamanas::1075.modern_relevance: A wedding host notices one guest needs shade, another needs food, and a child wants water. Care is not one-size-fits-all; it notices each person and gives accordingly.
ramacharitamanas::1075.insight: It shifts attention from giving in general to giving what actually fits the person in front of you.

ramacharitamanas::1076.verse_sanskrit: मन संतोषे सबन्हि के जहँ तहँ देहिं असीस। सकल तनय चिर जीवहुँ तुलसिदास के ईस ॥
ramacharitamanas::1076.verse_hindi: राजा ने सबके मन को संतुष्ट किया। (इसी से) सब लोग जहाँ-तहाँ आशीर्वाद दे रहे थे कि तुलसीदास के स्वामी सब पुत्र (चारों राजकुमार) चिरजीवी (दीर्घायु) हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1076.english_translation: The king satisfied everyone’s hearts, and people everywhere blessed him: "May Tulsidas’s lord’s four sons live long."
ramacharitamanas::1076.translation_literal: मन (mind/heart) / संतोषे (was satisfied) / सबन्हि के (of all) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / देहिं (they give) / असीस (blessings) / सकल (all) / तनय (sons) / चिर (long) / जीवहुँ (may live) / तुलसिदास के (of Tulsidas's) / ईस (lord)
ramacharitamanas::1076.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1076.essence: When a home is truly content, blessing rises on its own.
ramacharitamanas::1076.simple_meaning: Everyone was pleased, and people blessed Ram’s four sons to live long.
ramacharitamanas::1076.simple_insight: Shared joy naturally turns into blessing when a home feels complete.
ramacharitamanas::1076.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the gifts have been given and every heart is content. The people, moved by the sight of the four princes, bless the king’s sons for long life. This verse closes the mood of celebration before the naming ceremony begins.
ramacharitamanas::1076.modern_relevance: At a family celebration, the room goes quiet after the gifts are opened and everyone smiles at once. The real wealth is not the objects — it is the goodwill filling the house.
ramacharitamanas::1076.insight: It shifts attention from royal display to the collective blessing that follows fulfilled joy.

ramacharitamanas::1077.verse_sanskrit: कछुक दिवस बीते एहि भाँती। जात न जानिअ दिन अरु राती॥ नामकरन कर अवसरु जानी। भूप बोलि पठए मुनि ग्यानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1077.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार कुछ दिन बीत गए। दिन और रात जाते हुए जान नहीं पड़ते। तब नामकरण संस्कार का समय जानकर राजा ने ज्ञानी मुनि श्री वशिष्ठजी को बुला भेजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1077.english_translation: Some days passed like this. Day and night went by unnoticed. Then, knowing the time for the naming ceremony had arrived, the king sent for the wise sage Vashishtha.
ramacharitamanas::1077.translation_literal: कछुक (some) / दिवस (days) / बीते (passed) / एहि भाँती (in this manner) / जात (going) / न जानिअ (not known) / दिन (day) / अरु (and) / राती (night) / नामकरन (naming) / कर (of) / अवसरु (occasion/time) / जानी (knowing) / भूप (king) / बोलि (calling) / पठए (sent) / मुनि (sage) / ग्यानी (wise)
ramacharitamanas::1077.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1077.essence: Joy can make days and nights feel nonexistent.
ramacharitamanas::1077.simple_meaning: A few days passed without anyone noticing day or night. When the naming ceremony time came, King Dasharath sent for the wise sage Vashishtha.
ramacharitamanas::1077.simple_insight: Some moments are so full of joy that time itself disappears.
ramacharitamanas::1077.detailed_meaning: After the gifts and blessings for the newborn princes, days slip by in delight at Ayodhya. No one feels the passing of day or night. When the naming ceremony approaches, Dasharath calls the wise sage Vashishtha to guide the rite.
ramacharitamanas::1077.modern_relevance: You’re in a house after a baby is born, and nobody checks the clock. Meals blur together, sleep disappears, and then someone says, ‘It’s time for the naming ceremony.’
ramacharitamanas::1077.insight: It shifts attention from routine timekeeping to the felt fullness of a joyful moment.
