ramacharitamanas::1078.verse_sanskrit: करि पूजा भूपति अस भाषा। धरिअ नाम जो मुनि गुनि राखा॥ इन्ह के नाम अनेक अनूपा। मैं नृप कहब स्वमति अनुरूपा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1078.verse_hindi: मुनि की पूजा करके राजा ने कहा- हे मुनि! आपने मन में जो विचार रखे हों, वे नाम रखिए। (मुनि ने कहा-) हे राजन् ! इनके अनुपम नाम हैं, फिर भी मैं अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार कहूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1078.english_translation: After worshipping the sage, the king said, "Please give the names that the sage has kept in mind. These children have many incomparable names, yet I will speak according to my own understanding."
ramacharitamanas::1078.translation_literal: करि (having done) / पूजा (worship) / भूपति (the king) / अस (thus) / भाषा (spoke) / धरिअ (let be placed/given) / नाम (names) / जो (which) / मुनि (the sage) / गुनि (having considered) / राखा (kept) / इन्ह (these) / के (of) / नाम (names) / अनेक (many) / अनूपा (matchless) / मैं (I) / नृप (king) / कहब (will say) / स्वमति (own understanding) / अनुरूपा (according to)
ramacharitamanas::1078.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::1078.essence: Humility makes space for the right names to appear.
ramacharitamanas::1078.simple_meaning: After honoring the sage, the king asks for the names the sage has chosen. He also says the children have many beautiful names, and he will speak according to his own judgment.
ramacharitamanas::1078.simple_insight: Respect opens the way for guidance. Humility makes room for wisdom to speak.
ramacharitamanas::1078.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the naming ceremony begins after the king has invited the wise sage. Dasharath first honors the sage, then asks him to give the names he has already considered. The scene prepares the joyful revelation of Ram's names.
ramacharitamanas::1078.modern_relevance: Before a family decision, someone pauses to listen to the elder who has thought carefully. The room softens when pride steps back and respect takes its place.
ramacharitamanas::1078.insight: It models deference before speech: honor the wise first, then let naming or decision emerge from that respect.

ramacharitamanas::1079.verse_sanskrit: जो आनंद सिंधु सुखरासी। सीकर तें त्रैलोक सुपासी॥ सो सुखधाम राम अस नामा। अखिल लोक दायक बिश्रामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1079.verse_hindi: ये जो आनंद के समुद्र और सुख की राशि हैं, जिस (आनंदसिंधु) के एक कण से तीनों लोक सुखी होते हैं, उन (आपके सबसे बड़े पुत्र) का नाम 'राम' है, जो सुख का भवन और सम्पूर्ण लोकों को शांति देने वाला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1079.english_translation: He is the ocean of bliss and the storehouse of joy; even a drop of him brings happiness to the three worlds. His name is Ram, the home of peace and the giver of rest to all beings.
ramacharitamanas::1079.translation_literal: जो (who) / आनंद-सिंधु (ocean of bliss) / सुख-रासी (storehouse of joy) / सीकर (drop) / तें (from) / त्रैलोक (three worlds) / सुपासी (made happy)॥ / सो (that) / सुख-धाम (abode of joy) / राम (Ram) / अस (such) / नामा (name) / अखिल (all) / लोक (worlds) / दायक (giver) / बिश्रामा (rest, peace)॥
ramacharitamanas::1079.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1079.essence: Ram's name carries the peace that all beings long for.
ramacharitamanas::1079.simple_meaning: Ram's name is described as pure joy and peace. Even a tiny taste of it brings happiness to all three worlds.
ramacharitamanas::1079.simple_insight: A sacred name can steady the whole heart, not just the mind.
ramacharitamanas::1079.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Vashishtha is naming Dasharath's sons. After naming the first child, he explains why the eldest is called Ram: his very name carries bliss, and even a drop of that bliss can delight all worlds.
ramacharitamanas::1079.modern_relevance: You hear a name that instantly softens you — the kind tied to safety, relief, and home. Some names do that because they carry a whole presence, not just a label.
ramacharitamanas::1079.insight: It shifts attention from the person as a figure to the name as a living source of peace.

ramacharitamanas::1080.verse_sanskrit: बिस्व भरन पोषन कर जोई। ताकर नाम भरत अस होई॥ जाके सुमिरन तें रिपु नासा। नाम सत्रुहन बेद प्रकासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1080.verse_hindi: जो संसार का भरण-पोषण करते हैं, उन (आपके दूसरे पुत्र) का नाम 'भरत' होगा, जिनके स्मरण मात्र से शत्रु का नाश होता है, उनका वेदों में प्रसिद्ध 'शत्रुघ्न' नाम है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1080.english_translation: He who sustains and nourishes the world shall be called Bharat. He whose remembrance destroys enemies is known in the Vedas as Shatrughna.
ramacharitamanas::1080.translation_literal: बिस्व (world) / भरन (sustaining) / पोषन (nourishing) / कर (doing) / जोई (who) / ताकर (his) / नाम (name) / भरत (Bharat) / अस (thus) / होई (becomes) ॥ / जाके (whose) / सुमिरन (remembrance) / तें (by) / रिपु (enemy) / नासा (destruction) / नाम (name) / सत्रुहन (Shatrughna) / बेद (Vedas) / प्रकासा (revealed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1080.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1080.essence: Their names are blessings that hint at their future roles.
ramacharitamanas::1080.simple_meaning: The sages give the king's second and third sons names that match their future qualities: one will sustain the world, and the other will destroy enemies.
ramacharitamanas::1080.simple_insight: Names can point toward a life of service and strength before that life is even lived.
ramacharitamanas::1080.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the first two princes are named, the naming continues. The sages explain Bharat and Shatrughna's names as signs of their roles in the royal family: one will nourish the world, and the other will overcome enemies. The scene is still the sacred naming ceremony.
ramacharitamanas::1080.modern_relevance: At a naming ceremony, everyone smiles at the baby while older relatives quietly imagine the life ahead. The verse carries that feeling: a name can be a blessing, a direction, and a hope.
ramacharitamanas::1080.insight: It shifts attention from a name as label to a name as an invitation to live well.

ramacharitamanas::1081.verse_sanskrit: लच्छन धाम राम प्रिय सकल जगत आधार। गुरु बसिष् ठ तेहि राखा लछिमन नाम उदार ॥
ramacharitamanas::1081.verse_hindi: जो शुभ लक्षणों के धाम, श्री रामजी के प्यारे और सारे जगत के आधार हैं, गुरु वशिष् ठजी ने उनका 'लक्ष्मण' ऐसा श्रेष् ठ नाम रखा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1081.english_translation: Guru Vashishtha named him Lakshman, the noble one, for he is the abode of auspicious marks, dear to Ram, and the support of the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::1081.translation_literal: लच्छन (auspicious marks) / धाम (abode) / राम (Ram) / प्रिय (dear) / सकल (all) / जगत (world) / आधार (support) / गुरु (teacher) / बसिष् ठ (Vashishtha) / तेहि (him) / राखा (named) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / नाम (name) / उदार (noble)
ramacharitamanas::1081.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1081.essence: A true name points to character, devotion, and service.
ramacharitamanas::1081.simple_meaning: Vashishtha gives the child a noble name: Lakshman. The name points to his auspicious nature, his love for Ram, and his role as support for the world.
ramacharitamanas::1081.simple_insight: A name can be a blessing and a direction, not just a label.
ramacharitamanas::1081.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Ram's brothers are described, Guru Vashishtha names the third son. He sees in the child auspicious qualities, deep love for Ram, and a life meant to support the world.
ramacharitamanas::1081.modern_relevance: A child is born and elders choose a name that carries hope, character, and responsibility. The right name can feel like a promise about who someone is meant to become.
ramacharitamanas::1081.insight: It shifts attention from a person's label to the qualities and duty the label is meant to nurture.

ramacharitamanas::1082.verse_sanskrit: धरे नाम गुर हृदयँ बिचारी। बेद तत्व नृप तव सुत चारी॥ मुनि धन जन सरबस सिव प्राना। बाल केलि रस तेहिं सुख माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1082.verse_hindi: गुरुजी ने हृदय में विचार कर ये नाम रखे (और कहा-) हे राजन् ! तुम्हारे चारों पुत्र वेद के तत्त्व (साक्षात् परात्पर भगवान) हैं। जो मुनियों के धन, भक्तों के सर्वस्व और शिवजी के प्राण हैं, उन्होंने (इस समय तुम लोगों के प्रेमवश) बाल लीला के रस में सुख माना है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1082.english_translation: The guru reflected in his heart and named them. He said: O king, your four sons are the essence of the Vedas. They are the wealth of sages, the treasure of devotees, and the breath of Shiva. Yet they delight in the sweetness of divine play as children.
ramacharitamanas::1082.translation_literal: धरे (placed) / नाम (names) / गुर (the guru) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारी (having reflected) / बेद (Vedas) / तत्व (essence) / नृप (king) / तव (your) / सुत (sons) / चारी (four) / मुनि (sages) / धन (wealth) / जन (devotees) / सरबस (all) / सिव (Shiva) / प्राना (breath/life) / बाल (childhood) / केलि (play) / रस (sweetness) / तेहिं (in that) / सुख (delight) / माना (considered)
ramacharitamanas::1082.speaker: Guru Vashistha
ramacharitamanas::1082.essence: The highest reality can arrive wearing a child's smile.
ramacharitamanas::1082.simple_meaning: Vashistha names Dasharath's four sons as divine in essence. They are revered by sages and devotees, yet they are also shown as delighting in childhood play.
ramacharitamanas::1082.simple_insight: Even the highest presence can arrive in a simple, lovable form.
ramacharitamanas::1082.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Guru Vashistha reflects on Dasharath's newborn sons and gives them names that reveal their nature. He says they are not ordinary children: they are the essence behind the Vedas, cherished by sages, devotees, and Shiva himself. The verse softens theology into tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::1082.modern_relevance: A family gathers around a newborn and tries to find the right name. The room is full of ordinary joy, yet everyone senses something larger is being welcomed in. This verse holds that feeling without making it loud.
ramacharitamanas::1082.insight: It shifts attention from the children’s smallness to their hidden greatness, while keeping their human sweetness intact.

ramacharitamanas::1083.verse_sanskrit: बारेहि ते निज हित पति जानी। लछिमन राम चरन रति मानी॥ भरत सत्रुहन दूनउ भाई। प्रभु सेवक जसि प्रीति बड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1083.verse_hindi: बचपन से ही श्री रामचन्द्रजी को अपना परम हितैषी स्वामी जानकर लक्ष्मणजी ने उनके चरणों में प्रीति जोड़ ली। भरत और शत्रुघ्न दोनों भाइयों में स्वामी और सेवक की जिस प्रीति की प्रशंसा है, वैसी प्रीति हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1083.english_translation: From childhood, Lakshman knew Ram as his own highest good and loved Ram's feet. The two brothers, Bharat and Shatrughna, shared the same praised bond of master and servant, with love greatly increased.
ramacharitamanas::1083.translation_literal: बारेहि (from childhood) / ते (from) / निज (own) / हित (welfare, highest good) / पति (lord, master) / जानी (knowing) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / रति (love, devotion) / मानी (held, took)॥ / भरत (Bharat) / सत्रुहन (Shatrughna) / दूनउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / प्रभु (master) / सेवक (servant) / जसि (like) / प्रीति (love) / बड़ाई (greatly increased)॥
ramacharitamanas::1083.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1083.essence: Real closeness looks like joyful service.
ramacharitamanas::1083.simple_meaning: Lakshman loved Ram as his highest good from childhood, and Bharat and Shatrughna also shared a deep master-servant love.
ramacharitamanas::1083.simple_insight: Love becomes strongest when service is freely chosen, not forced.
ramacharitamanas::1083.detailed_meaning: The four brothers are being introduced through their relationships, not just their names. Lakshman is already oriented toward Ram, and Bharat and Shatrughna are marked by the same spirit of loving service. This verse deepens the family ideal before the next description of their beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1083.modern_relevance: A younger sibling quietly rearranges life around an older brother's needs without resentment. No announcement, no self-importance — just a bond where serving feels natural.
ramacharitamanas::1083.insight: It shifts attention from possession to loving service as the measure of closeness.

ramacharitamanas::1084.verse_sanskrit: स्याम गौर सुंदर दोउ जोरी। निरखहिं छबि जननीं तृन तोरी॥ चारिउ सील रूप गुन धामा। तदपि अधिक सुखसागर रामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1084.verse_hindi: श्याम और गौर शरीर वाली दोनों सुंदर जोड़ियों की शोभा को देखकर माताएँ तृण तोड़ती हैं (जिसमें दीठ न लग जाए)। यों तो चारों ही पुत्र शील, रूप और गुण के धाम हैं, तो भी सुख के समुद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी सबसे अधिक हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1084.english_translation: The mothers gaze at the two lovely pairs, dark and fair, and ward off the evil eye with grass. All four sons are abodes of virtue, beauty, and good qualities, yet Ram is the ocean of bliss beyond the rest.
ramacharitamanas::1084.translation_literal: स्याम (dark) / गौर (fair) / सुंदर (beautiful) / दोउ (both) / जोरी (paired together) / निरखहिं (they behold) / छबि (beauty) / जननीं (the mothers) / तृन (grass) / तोरी (breaking) / चारिउ (all four) / सील (character) / रूप (beauty) / गुन (qualities) / धामा (abodes) / तदपि (even so) / अधिक (more) / सुखसागर (ocean of bliss) / रामा (Ram)
ramacharitamanas::1084.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1084.essence: All four sons shine, but Ram holds the deepest joy.
ramacharitamanas::1084.simple_meaning: The mothers delight in all four sons, but Ram stands above the rest as the deepest source of joy.
ramacharitamanas::1084.simple_insight: Love can be shared, yet one presence still feels like home.
ramacharitamanas::1084.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the queens watch their four sons growing in beauty and grace. They protect them from the evil eye and rejoice in all of them, yet this line quietly lifts Ram above the others as the fullest ocean of delight.
ramacharitamanas::1084.modern_relevance: You watch your child with the kind of tenderness that makes you almost afraid to praise them too much. Then one presence, one smile, still touches the heart more deeply than the others.
ramacharitamanas::1084.insight: It shifts attention from equal admiration to the unique sweetness Ram carries.

ramacharitamanas::1085.verse_sanskrit: हृदयँ अनुग्रह इंदु प्रकासा। सूचत किरन मनोहर हासा॥ कबहुँ उछंग कबहुँ बर पलना। मातु दुलारइ कहि प्रिय ललना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1085.verse_hindi: उनके हृदय में कृपा रूपी चन्द्रमा प्रकाशित है। उनकी मन को हरने वाली हँसी उस (कृपा रूपी चन्द्रमा) की किरणों को सूचित करती है। कभी गोद में (लेकर) और कभी उत्तम पालने में (लिटाकर) माता 'प्यारे ललना!' कहकर दुलार करती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1085.english_translation: A moon of grace shines in the heart. A charming smile shows its rays. Sometimes in the lap, sometimes in a fine cradle, the mother caresses him, calling him her dear child.
ramacharitamanas::1085.translation_literal: हृदयँ (in the heart) / अनुग्रह (grace) / इंदु (moon) / प्रकासा (shines) / सूचत (showing) / किरन (rays) / मनोहर (charming) / हासा (smile) / कबहुँ (sometimes) / उछंग (lap) / कबहुँ (sometimes) / बर (fine/good) / पलना (cradle) / मातु (mother) / दुलारइ (caresses) / कहि (saying) / प्रिय (dear) / ललना (child)
ramacharitamanas::1085.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1085.essence: Grace appears as a child that a mother can hold.
ramacharitamanas::1085.simple_meaning: Ram's face shines with a gentle grace, and his mother lovingly holds and spoils him, sometimes in her lap and sometimes in a cradle.
ramacharitamanas::1085.simple_insight: Even the supreme being appears here as a beloved child, making devotion feel tender and intimate.
ramacharitamanas::1085.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kaushalya is raising infant Ram. Tulsidas lingers on the tenderness of the scene: grace seems to shine through Ram's smile, and his mother alternates between holding him in her lap and laying him in a cradle, treating the supreme child with overflowing love.
ramacharitamanas::1085.modern_relevance: A parent rocks a child at 2 a.m., half-awake but completely devoted. In that ordinary tenderness, something vast feels near and human at once.
ramacharitamanas::1085.insight: It shifts the mind from distant awe to intimate love: the highest reality can be approached through simple affection.

ramacharitamanas::1086.verse_sanskrit: ब्यापक ब्रह्म निरंजन निर्गुन बिगत बिनोद। सो अज प्रेम भगति बस कौसल्या कें गोद ॥
ramacharitamanas::1086.verse_hindi: जो सर्वव्यापक, निरंजन (मायारहित), निर्गुण, विनोदरहित और अजन्मे ब्रह्म हैं, वही प्रेम और भक्ति के वश कौसल्याजी की गोद में (खेल रहे) हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1086.english_translation: The all-pervading, stainless, attributeless, joyless, unborn supreme reality lies in कौसल्या's lap, bound by love and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1086.translation_literal: ब्यापक (all-pervading) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / निरंजन (stainless, untouched by illusion) / निर्गुन (without attributes) / बिगत (without) / बिनोद (joy/play) / सो (that) / अज (unborn) / प्रेम (love) / भगति (devotion) / बस (under the power of) / कौसल्या कें गोद (Kausalya's lap)
ramacharitamanas::1086.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1086.essence: Love makes the infinite feel like a child in your arms.
ramacharitamanas::1086.simple_meaning: The limitless, formless supreme reality has become a child in कौसल्या's lap because of love and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1086.simple_insight: Devotion can make the impossible feel tender and near.
ramacharitamanas::1086.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the newborn Ram is being cradled by कौसल्या. Tulsidas pauses on the shock of it: the same reality that fills everything and has no form is now a child in a mother's arms, reached through love alone.
ramacharitamanas::1086.modern_relevance: You are holding a sleeping baby after a brutal day, and the room goes quiet. What felt vast and unreachable suddenly feels close enough to protect. Love does that.
ramacharitamanas::1086.insight: It shifts the mind from abstract distance to intimate presence.

ramacharitamanas::1087.verse_sanskrit: काम कोटि छबि स्याम सरीरा। नील कंज बारिद गंभीरा॥ नअरुन चरन पंकज नख जोती। कमल दलन्हि बैठे जनु मोती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1087.verse_hindi: उनके नीलकमल और गंभीर (जल से भरे हुए) मेघ के समान श्याम शरीर में करोड़ों कामदेवों की शोभा है। लाल-लाल चरण कमलों के नखों की (शुभ्र) ज्योति ऐसी मालूम होती है जैसे (लाल) कमल के पत्तों पर मोती स्थिर हो गए हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1087.english_translation: His dark body has the beauty of millions of love-gods. His red lotus feet shine like pearls resting on lotus petals.
ramacharitamanas::1087.translation_literal: काम कोटि (millions of love-gods) / छबि (beauty) / स्याम सरीरा (dark body) / नील कंज (blue lotus) / बारिद (rain cloud) / गंभीरा (deep)॥ / नअरुन (reddish) / चरन पंकज (lotus feet) / नख (nails) / जोती (light) / कमल दलन्हि (on lotus petals) / बैठे (resting) / जनु (as if) / मोती (pearls)
ramacharitamanas::1087.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1087.essence: Even the smallest features of Ram overflow with beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1087.simple_meaning: Ram's dark body is extraordinarily beautiful, and his red feet shine like pearls on lotus petals.
ramacharitamanas::1087.simple_insight: Beauty can feel sacred when the heart sees it as more than appearance.
ramacharitamanas::1087.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the child Ram lies in Kaushalya's lap while the poet lingers on his form. After describing the divine child as the supreme reality in human embrace, this verse dwells on his dark body and radiant feet to make devotion visible.
ramacharitamanas::1087.modern_relevance: A parent lifts a sleeping child and suddenly notices the tiny feet, the dark hair, the soft light on the skin. Ordinary tenderness can become overwhelming when love sees holiness in detail.
ramacharitamanas::1087.insight: It teaches attention to the sacred in physical form, not just abstract greatness.

ramacharitamanas::1088.verse_sanskrit: रेख कुलिस ध्वज अंकुस सोहे। नूपुर धुनि सुनि मुनि मन मोहे॥ कटि किंकिनी उदर त्रय रेखा। नाभि गभीर जान जेहिं देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1088.verse_hindi: (चरणतलों में) वज्र, ध्वजा और अंकुश के चिह्न शोभित हैं। नूपुर (पेंजनी) की ध्वनि सुनकर मुनियों का भी मन मोहित हो जाता है। कमर में करधनी और पेट पर तीन रेखाएँ (त्रिवली) हैं। नाभि की गंभीरता को तो वही जानते हैं, जिन्होंने उसे देखा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1088.english_translation: The soles shine with the marks of thunderbolt, flag, and goad. The sound of the ankle bells captivates even sages. A jeweled girdle rests at the waist, and three folds mark the belly. Only one who has seen it knows the depth of the navel.
ramacharitamanas::1088.translation_literal: रेख (marks) / कुलिस (thunderbolt) / ध्वज (flag) / अंकुस (goad) / सोहे (shine) । नूपुर (ankle bells) / धुनि (sound) / सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (sages) / मन (mind) / मोहे (captivate) ॥ कटि (waist) / किंकिनी (jeweled girdle) / उदर (belly) / त्रय (three) / रेखा (lines) । नाभि (navel) / गभीर (deep) / जान (knows) / जेहिं (who) / देखा (has seen) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1088.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1088.essence: Divine greatness appears as intimate, tender beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1088.simple_meaning: Ram's feet, ornaments, waist, and form are described in loving detail. Even sages are enchanted by the sound of his anklets.
ramacharitamanas::1088.simple_insight: Beauty itself becomes a form of grace when the mind is turned toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1088.detailed_meaning: In Kaushalya's lap, the unborn supreme being is being described as a tender child. Tulsidas lingers on Ram's divine body—his marked feet, anklets, waist, and navel—showing that even sages are drawn into wonder before this living beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1088.modern_relevance: You catch yourself staring at a child asleep in your arms, noticing details no one else would care about. Love makes the ordinary radiant, and attention becomes devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1088.insight: It shifts attention from abstract divinity to intimate, embodied wonder.

ramacharitamanas::1089.verse_sanskrit: भुज बिसाल भूषन जुत भूरी। हियँ हरि नख अति सोभा रूरी॥ उर मनिहार पदिक की सोभा। बिप्र चरन देखत मन लोभा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1089.verse_hindi: बहुत से आभूषणों से सुशोभित विशाल भुजाएँ हैं। हृदय पर बाघ के नख की बहुत ही निराली छटा है। छाती पर रत्नों से युक्त मणियों के हार की शोभा और ब्राह्मण (भृगु) के चरण चिह्न को देखते ही मन लुभा जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1089.english_translation: His broad arms are adorned with many ornaments. A tiger-claw mark shines beautifully on his chest. The necklace on his chest and the mark of the brahmin's feet delight the heart at once.
ramacharitamanas::1089.translation_literal: भुज (arms) / बिसाल (broad) / भूषन जुत (adorned with ornaments) / भूरी (many) / हियँ (on the heart/chest) / हरि नख (the divine's claw-mark) / अति (very) / सोभा (beauty) / रूरी (lovely) / उर (on the chest) / मनिहार (necklace) / पदिक (foot-mark) / की (of) / सोभा (beauty) / बिप्र (brahmin) / चरन (feet) / देखत (seeing) / मन (mind) / लोभा (is captivated)
ramacharitamanas::1089.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1089.essence: Sacred beauty draws the heart before the mind can speak.
ramacharitamanas::1089.simple_meaning: Ram's broad arms, chest marks, and sacred signs are being described in loving detail. The sight of his body fills the heart with delight.
ramacharitamanas::1089.simple_insight: Beauty becomes devotion when the heart recognises what it is seeing.
ramacharitamanas::1089.detailed_meaning: The Sita-swayamvar is unfolding, and the poet lingers over Ram's form. This verse is part of a continuous description of his body, not a separate teaching. The beauty of his arms and chest, along with sacred marks, draws the mind toward him.
ramacharitamanas::1089.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone who carries quiet grace into a room, and everything in you softens. Some presence needs no explanation; it simply draws the heart toward reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1089.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary appearance to sacred presence.

ramacharitamanas::1090.verse_sanskrit: कंबु कंठ अति चिबुक सुहाई। आनन अमित मदन छबि छाई॥ दुइ दुइ दसन अधर अरुनारे। नासा तिलक को बरनै पारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1090.verse_hindi: कंठ शंख के समान (उतार-चढ़ाव वाला, तीन रेखाओं से सुशोभित) है और ठोड़ी बहुत ही सुंदर है। मुख पर असंख्य कामदेवों की छटा छा रही है। दो-दो सुंदर दँतुलियाँ हैं, लाल-लाल होठ हैं। नासिका और तिलक (के सौंदर्य) का तो वर्णन ही कौन कर सकता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1090.english_translation: The neck is like a conch and the chin is beautiful. Countless forms of love’s beauty shine on the face. Two lovely rows of teeth, red lips, and who can describe the nose and mark on the forehead?
ramacharitamanas::1090.translation_literal: कंबु (conch-like) / कंठ (neck) / अति (very) / चिबुक (chin) / सुहाई (beautiful) / आनन (face) / अमित (countless) / मदन (love/desire) / छबि (beauty) / छाई (spread) / दुइ दुइ (two by two) / दसन (teeth) / अधर (lips) / अरुनारे (reddish) / नासा (nose) / तिलक (forehead mark) / को (of) / बरनै (to describe) / पारे (able)
ramacharitamanas::1090.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1090.simple_meaning: The verse keeps describing the baby’s beautiful face: conch-like neck, lovely chin, shining face, red lips, teeth, nose, and forehead mark.
ramacharitamanas::1090.simple_insight: Beauty can be so complete that language starts to fail.
ramacharitamanas::1090.detailed_meaning: In the opening of Balkand, the poet is lingering over baby Ram’s divine beauty. After describing his feet, legs, and chest, the verse moves upward to the neck, chin, mouth, and face, building wonder by piling image upon image.
ramacharitamanas::1090.modern_relevance: A parent keeps taking photos because the baby’s face seems impossible to capture. Every angle feels more beautiful than the last, and words suddenly feel too small.
ramacharitamanas::1090.insight: It trains attention to linger on beauty without rushing past it.

ramacharitamanas::1091.verse_sanskrit: सुंदर श्रवन सुचारु कपोला। अति प्रिय मधुर तोतरे बोला॥ चिक्कन कच कुंचित गभुआरे। बहु प्रकार रचि मातु सँवारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1091.verse_hindi: सुंदर कान और बहुत ही सुंदर गाल हैं। मधुर तोतले शब्द बहुत ही प्यारे लगते हैं। जन्म के समय से रखे हुए चिकने और घुँघराले बाल हैं, जिनको माता ने बहुत प्रकार से बनाकर सँवार दिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1091.english_translation: Beautiful ears and lovely cheeks; his sweet, childish speech is dear. His hair is soft and curly from birth, and his mother has carefully dressed and adorned him in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::1091.translation_literal: सुंदर (beautiful) / श्रवन (ears) / सुचारु (lovely) / कपोला (cheeks) / अति (very) / प्रिय (dear) / मधुर (sweet) / तोतरे (childish, lisping) / बोला (speech) / चिक्कन (soft, smooth) / कच (hair) / कुंचित (curly) / गभुआरे (from birth) / बहु प्रकार (many ways) / रचि (having arranged) / मातु (mother) / सँवारे (adorned, beautified)
ramacharitamanas::1091.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1091.essence: Love sees divinity in the smallest features.
ramacharitamanas::1091.simple_meaning: The child is described as beautifully made, with soft features, sweet speech, and lovingly arranged hair.
ramacharitamanas::1091.simple_insight: Love notices every detail and turns ordinary baby features into wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1091.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the child Ram is being admired piece by piece: ears, cheeks, speech, hair, and the motherly care that has dressed him. The verse continues the poetic portrait begun before it, adding more beauty rather than making a new claim.
ramacharitamanas::1091.modern_relevance: A parent keeps taking photos of a sleeping baby, unable to stop smiling at tiny cheeks and messy curls. The moment is ordinary, but love makes it feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::1091.insight: It trains attention toward tenderness, letting beauty be found in small, intimate details.

ramacharitamanas::1092.verse_sanskrit: पीत झगुलिआ तनु पहिराई। जानु पानि बिचरनि मोहि भाई॥ रूप सकहिं नहिं कहि श्रुति सेषा। सो जानइ सपनेहुँ जेहिं देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1092.verse_hindi: शरीर पर पीली झँगुली पहनाई हुई है। उनका घुटनों और हाथों के बल चलना मुझे बहुत ही प्यारा लगता है। उनके रूप का वर्णन वेद और शेषजी भी नहीं कर सकते। उसे वही जानता है, जिसने कभी स्वप्न में भी देखा हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1092.english_translation: He is dressed in a yellow little garment. His crawling on hands and knees is very dear to me. Even the Vedas and Shesha cannot describe his form. Only one who has seen him, even in a dream, can know him.
ramacharitamanas::1092.translation_literal: पीत (yellow) / झगुलिआ (little garment) / तनु (body) / पहिराई (dressed) / जानु (knees) / पानि (hands) / बिचरनि (moving about/crawling) / मोहि (to me) / भाई (dear) / रूप (form) / सकहिं (are able) / नहिं (not) / कहि (to describe) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / सेषा (Shesha) / सो (that one) / जानइ (knows) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / जेहिं (by whom) / देखा (was seen)
ramacharitamanas::1092.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1092.essence: Ram's beauty exceeds every description, and only love can recognize it.
ramacharitamanas::1092.simple_meaning: The child Ram is dressed in yellow and crawls on his hands and knees. His beauty is beyond words, beyond even the Vedas and Shesha.
ramacharitamanas::1092.simple_insight: Love sees what language cannot hold.
ramacharitamanas::1092.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, baby Ram is being dressed and watched with tender delight. The poet lingers on his crawling, his tiny yellow garment, and his indescribable beauty. The scene is not teaching a doctrine; it is overflowing with wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1092.modern_relevance: A parent watches a toddler wobble across the floor in a bright shirt and forgets every task on the list. Some moments are too tender to explain — they only need to be loved.
ramacharitamanas::1092.insight: It shifts attention from description to direct seeing, where devotion recognizes what words cannot capture.

ramacharitamanas::1093.verse_sanskrit: सुख संदोह मोह पर ग्यान गिरा गोतीत। दंपति परम प्रेम बस कर सिसुचरित पुनीत ॥
ramacharitamanas::1093.verse_hindi: जो सुख के पुंज, मोह से परे तथा ज्ञान, वाणी और इन्द्रियों से अतीत हैं, वे भगवान दशरथ-कौसल्या के अत्यन्त प्रेम के वश होकर पवित्र बाललीला करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1093.english_translation: A mass of bliss, beyond delusion, beyond thought, speech, and the senses, the pure child-acts are performed by the divine couple’s boundless love.
ramacharitamanas::1093.translation_literal: सुख-संदोह (a heap of bliss) / मोह (delusion) / पर (beyond) / ग्यान (knowledge) / गिरा (speech) / गोतीत (beyond the senses) / दंपति (the divine couple) / परम प्रेम (supreme love) / बस (under the influence) / कर (doing) / सिसुचरित (child-acts) / पुनीत (pure, sanctified)
ramacharitamanas::1093.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1093.essence: Love makes the beyond appear as a child.
ramacharitamanas::1093.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond delusion, knowledge, speech, and the senses, yet he performs pure childlike play out of the deep love of Dasharath and Kaushalya.
ramacharitamanas::1093.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing the highest reality can also be tender, playful, and close.
ramacharitamanas::1093.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after describing baby Ram’s beauty and sweetness, Tulsidas pauses to explain the mystery behind the scene. The child who is beyond mind and speech still becomes the beloved son of Dasharath and Kaushalya, and that love brings forth his holy play.
ramacharitamanas::1093.modern_relevance: You hold a sleeping child and forget every theory you ever had about control. In that moment, love is not an idea — it is the power that makes the sacred feel near.
ramacharitamanas::1093.insight: It shifts the mind from abstract greatness to intimate devotion: the highest can be approached through love, not analysis.

ramacharitamanas::1094.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि राम जगत पितु माता। कोसलपुर बासिन्ह सुखदाता॥ जिन्ह रघुनाथ चरन रति मानी। तिन्ह की यह गति प्रगट भवानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1094.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार (सम्पूर्ण) जगत के माता-पिता श्री रामजी अवधपुर के निवासियों को सुख देते हैं, जिन्होंने श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में प्रीति जोड़ी है, हे भवानी! उनकी यह प्रत्यक्ष गति है (कि भगवान उनके प्रेमवश बाललीला करके उन्हें आनंद दे रहे हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1094.english_translation: In this way, Ram is the father and mother of the world and the giver of joy to the people of Kosala. O Bhavani, for those who hold love for Raghunath’s feet, this visible grace is theirs.
ramacharitamanas::1094.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / राम (Ram) / जगत (world) / पितु (father) / माता (mother) / कोसलपुर (Kosala city / Ayodhya) / बासिन्ह (residents) / सुखदाता (giver of joy) / जिन्ह (those who) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath / Ram) / चरन (feet) / रति (love/attachment) / मानी (held) / तिन्ह (for them) / की (of) / यह (this) / गति (state / grace) / प्रगट (manifest) / भवानी (O Bhavani)
ramacharitamanas::1094.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1094.essence: Love for Ram makes his grace visible and immediate.
ramacharitamanas::1094.simple_meaning: Ram is the loving source of joy for the people of Ayodhya. Those who hold deep love for his feet receive his visible grace.
ramacharitamanas::1094.simple_insight: Love changes how grace is experienced: what feels distant becomes personal and present.
ramacharitamanas::1094.detailed_meaning: After describing Ram’s childhood delight, Tulsidas turns to Bhavani and says that Ram is the parent of the world and the joy of Ayodhya. For those who love his feet, his grace is no longer hidden — it becomes visible in their lives.
ramacharitamanas::1094.modern_relevance: A child runs into a room and the whole house softens. The one person everyone loves becomes the center of warmth. Devotion works like that: love makes presence feel immediate.
ramacharitamanas::1094.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract belief to lived closeness, where love itself reveals Ram’s grace.

ramacharitamanas::1095.verse_sanskrit: रघुपति बिमुख जतन कर कोरी। कवन सकइ भव बंधन छोरी॥ जीव चराचर बस कै राखे। सो माया प्रभु सों भय भाखे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1095.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी से विमुख रहकर मनुष्य चाहे करोड़ों उपाय करे, परन्तु उसका संसार बंधन कौन छुड़ा सकता है। जिसने सब चराचर जीवों को अपने वश में कर रखा है, वह माया भी प्रभु से भय खाती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1095.english_translation: Separated from Raghupati, no amount of effort can cut the bonds of worldly existence. The one who keeps all moving and unmoving beings under control, even Maya fears that Lord.
ramacharitamanas::1095.translation_literal: रघुपति (Lord of Raghu) / बिमुख (turned away) / जतन (effort, effortful means) / कर (doing) / कोरी (crores, countless) / कवन (who) / सकइ (can) / भव (worldly existence) / बंधन (bondage) / छोरी (to release) / जीव (living beings) / चराचर (moving and unmoving) / बस (under control) / कै (having) / राखे (kept) / सो (that) / माया (illusion) / प्रभु (Lord) / सों (from) / भय (fear) / भाखे (speaks, says)
ramacharitamanas::1095.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1095.essence: No amount of effort frees a heart turned away from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1095.simple_meaning: Turning away from Ram leaves a person trapped, no matter how many methods they try. Ram holds all beings in his power, and even Maya fears him.
ramacharitamanas::1095.simple_insight: Relief comes from knowing release is not a private achievement; it begins with turning back toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1095.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, Tulsidas is explaining why the people of Ayodhya find peace around Ram. He says that separation from Raghupati keeps a person bound, while Ram rules all living and non-living beings so completely that even Maya trembles before him.
ramacharitamanas::1095.modern_relevance: You can exhaust yourself with plans, therapy apps, and self-fixes, yet still feel stuck in the same loop. The verse says the real turning point is not more force, but a return of trust toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1095.insight: It shifts the mind from self-rescue to surrendering into the power that actually frees.

ramacharitamanas::1096.verse_sanskrit: भृकुटि बिलास नचावइ ताही। अस प्रभु छाड़ि भजिअ कहु काही॥ मन क्रम बचन छाड़ि चतुराई। भजत कृपा करिहहिं रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1096.verse_hindi: भगवान उस माया को भौंह के इशारे पर नचाते हैं। ऐसे प्रभु को छोड़कर कहो, (और) किसका भजन किया जाए। मन, वचन और कर्म से चतुराई छोड़कर भजते ही श्री रघुनाथजी कृपा करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1096.english_translation: That divine illusion dances at a mere flick of the brow. Why leave such a Lord and worship anyone else? Drop cleverness in mind, speech, and action; as soon as you worship, Raghuvir will show grace.
ramacharitamanas::1096.translation_literal: भृकुटि (brow) / बिलास (play, gesture) / नचावइ (makes dance) / ताही (that) / अस (such) / प्रभु (Lord) / छाड़ि (leaving) / भजिअ (should worship) / कहु (say) / काही (whom) / मन (mind) / क्रम (deed, action) / बचन (speech) / छाड़ि (leaving) / चतुराई (cleverness) / भजत (worshipping) / कृपा (grace) / करिहहिं (will do) / रघुराई (Raghuraj, Lord of Raghu)
ramacharitamanas::1096.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1096.essence: Cleverness falls away when you trust the one who rules illusion.
ramacharitamanas::1096.simple_meaning: Ram controls illusion effortlessly, so no other refuge makes sense. Worship him with a simple heart, without mental tricks, and his grace will come.
ramacharitamanas::1096.simple_insight: You do not need to outthink devotion. Sincere turning toward Ram is enough.
ramacharitamanas::1096.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Tulsidas pauses the child-Ram scenes to praise Ram’s power. He says even illusion dances to Ram’s brow, so there is no wiser refuge. The verse turns the reader from cleverness to wholehearted devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1096.modern_relevance: You keep rehearsing the perfect apology, the perfect plan, the perfect image. Then you realise the relationship does not need performance — it needs honesty, and a clean turn toward what is worthy.
ramacharitamanas::1096.insight: It shifts the mind from strategic self-protection to direct, trusting devotion.

ramacharitamanas::1097.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि सिसुबिनोद प्रभु कीन्हा। सकल नगरबासिन्ह सुख दीन्हा॥ लै उछंग कबहुँक हलरावै। कबहुँ पालने घालि झुलावै ॥
ramacharitamanas::1097.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार से प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने बालक्रीड़ा की और समस्त नगर निवासियों को सुख दिया। कौसल्याजी कभी उन्हें गोद में लेकर हिलाती-डुलाती और कभी पालने में लिटाकर झुलाती थीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1097.english_translation: In this way, the Lord played as a child and gave joy to all the city’s people. Sometimes Kaushalya held him in her lap and rocked him; sometimes she laid him in a cradle and swung him.
ramacharitamanas::1097.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / सिसु-बिनोद (child’s play) / प्रभु (the Lord) / कीन्हा (did) / सकल (all) / नगर-बासिन्ह (city dwellers) / सुख (joy) / दीन्हा (gave) / लै (taking) / उछंग (lap) / कबहुँक (sometimes) / हलरावै (rocked) / कबहुँ (sometimes) / पालने (in cradle) / घालि (placing) / झुलावै (swung)
ramacharitamanas::1097.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1097.essence: A child’s play can bless an entire city.
ramacharitamanas::1097.simple_meaning: Ram played like a child, and everyone in Ayodhya felt joy. Kaushalya lovingly rocked him in her lap and cradle.
ramacharitamanas::1097.simple_insight: Love can turn ordinary care into a whole city’s happiness.
ramacharitamanas::1097.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, baby Ram is growing up under Kaushalya’s care. His playful movements and her tender rocking bring delight not just to the palace, but to everyone in the city. This verse lingers on that shared joy before the next line deepens Kaushalya’s love.
ramacharitamanas::1097.modern_relevance: A mother rocks her child at 3 a.m. while the whole house finally goes quiet. The smallest act of care can change the feeling of an entire home.
ramacharitamanas::1097.insight: It shifts attention from grand events to the power of loving presence in daily life.

ramacharitamanas::1098.verse_sanskrit: प्रेम मगन कौसल्या निसि दिन जात न जान। सुत सनेह बस माता बालचरित कर गान ॥
ramacharitamanas::1098.verse_hindi: प्रेम में मग्न कौसल्याजी रात और दिन का बीतना नहीं जानती थीं। पुत्र के स्नेहवश माता उनके बालचरित्रों का गान किया करतीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1098.english_translation: Kausalya was so absorbed in love that she did not know day from night. Bound by motherly affection, she kept singing of her son's childhood deeds.
ramacharitamanas::1098.translation_literal: प्रेम (love) / मगन (immersed) / कौसल्या (Kausalya) / निसि (night) / दिन (day) / जात (passing) / न जान (did not know) / सुत (son) / सनेह (affection) / बस (under the power of) / माता (mother) / बालचरित (childhood deeds) / करि (doing) / गान (singing)
ramacharitamanas::1098.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1098.essence: Love makes time vanish and memory sing.
ramacharitamanas::1098.simple_meaning: Kausalya is so filled with love for Ram that she loses track of time and keeps singing about his childhood.
ramacharitamanas::1098.simple_insight: Love can make ordinary time disappear.
ramacharitamanas::1098.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram's childhood fills the house with joy. Kausalya, overwhelmed by motherly love, forgets day and night and keeps singing of his playful deeds. The verse lingers on her devotion rather than advancing the plot.
ramacharitamanas::1098.modern_relevance: You replay your child's first steps on your phone for the tenth time and still smile. Some loves do not move forward; they keep returning to the same precious moment.
ramacharitamanas::1098.insight: It shifts attention from clock time to lived affection.

ramacharitamanas::1099.verse_sanskrit: एक बार जननीं अन्हवाए। करि सिंगार पलनाँ पौढ़ाए॥ निज कुल इष्टदेव भगवाना। पूजा हेतु कीन्ह अस्नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1099.verse_hindi: एक बार माता ने श्री रामचन्द्रजी को स्नान कराया और श्रृंगार करके पालने पर पौढ़ा दिया। फिर अपने कुल के इष्टदेव भगवान की पूजा के लिए स्नान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1099.english_translation: Once, Mother bathed Ram, decorated him, and laid him in the cradle. Then, for worship of the family deity, she bathed herself.
ramacharitamanas::1099.translation_literal: एक बार (once) / जननीं (the mother) / अन्हवाए (bathed) / करि (doing) / सिंगार (adornment) / पलनाँ (cradle) / पौढ़ाए (laid down) / निज (own) / कुल (family) / इष्टदेव (chosen deity) / भगवाना (the divine lord) / पूजा (worship) / हेतु (for the purpose of) / कीन्ह (did) / अस्नाना (bathing)
ramacharitamanas::1099.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1099.essence: Care for the beloved comes before formal worship.
ramacharitamanas::1099.simple_meaning: Mother bathes and dresses Ram, then goes to bathe herself before worshipping the family deity.
ramacharitamanas::1099.simple_insight: Love becomes ritual when care for the child and reverence for the divine flow together.
ramacharitamanas::1099.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kaushalya finishes dressing little Ram and gently lays him in the cradle. Only then does she bathe herself to begin worship of her family deity. The verse pauses on her tenderness and her devotion in the same breath.
ramacharitamanas::1099.modern_relevance: You finish packing your child’s lunch, smooth their hair, and only then step into the shower before prayer or meditation. Care first, then worship — that order reveals what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::1099.insight: It teaches you to place loving responsibility before private ritual.

ramacharitamanas::1100.verse_sanskrit: करि पूजा नैबेद्य चढ़ावा। आपु गई जहँ पाक बनावा॥ बहुरि मातु तहवाँ चलि आई। भोजन करत देख सुत जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1100.verse_hindi: पूजा करके नैवेद्य चढ़ाया और स्वयं वहाँ गईं, जहाँ रसोई बनाई गई थी। फिर माता वहीं (पूजा के स्थान में) लौट आई और वहाँ आने पर पुत्र को (इष्टदेव भगवान के लिए चढ़ाए हुए नैवेद्य का) भोजन करते देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1100.english_translation: After offering the naivedya, she went to where the food had been prepared. Then Mother returned there and saw her son eating the offering made for the family deity.
ramacharitamanas::1100.translation_literal: करि (having done) / पूजा (worship) / नैबेद्य (offering of food) / चढ़ावा (offered) / आपु (herself) / गई (went) / जहँ (where) / पाक (cooking) / बनावा (was made) / बहुरि (again) / मातु (mother) / तहवाँ (there) / चलि (having gone) / आई (came) / भोजन (food/eating) / करत (doing) / देख (saw) / सुत (son) / जाई (went)
ramacharitamanas::1100.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1100.essence: The offering meant for worship is joyfully claimed by the child himself.
ramacharitamanas::1100.simple_meaning: Mother offers worship, then returns and finds the child eating the offering meant for the family deity.
ramacharitamanas::1100.simple_insight: Love for Ram turns ordinary household worship into a living, playful presence.
ramacharitamanas::1100.detailed_meaning: Kausalya has just bathed, dressed, and worshipped the family deity before placing baby Ram in the cradle. She steps away to the kitchen, then comes back and finds the child eating the very offering she had placed before the deity. The scene deepens her wonder and delight.
ramacharitamanas::1100.modern_relevance: You set aside food at a home altar, turn away for a moment, and come back to find a child reaching for it. The sacred no longer feels distant; it has entered the room.
ramacharitamanas::1100.insight: It shifts devotion from a ritual act to a felt relationship, where the divine is present inside the home itself.

ramacharitamanas::1101.verse_sanskrit: गै जननी सिसु पहिं भयभीता। देखा बाल तहाँ पुनि सूता॥ बहुरि आइ देखा सुत सोई। हृदयँ कंप मन धीर न होई॥3।
ramacharitamanas::1101.verse_hindi: माता भयभीत होकर (पालने में सोया था, यहाँ किसने लाकर बैठा दिया, इस बात से डरकर) पुत्र के पास गई, तो वहाँ बालक को सोया हुआ देखा। फिर (पूजा स्थान में लौटकर) देखा कि वही पुत्र वहाँ (भोजन कर रहा) है। उनके हृदय में कम्प होने लगा और मन को धीरज नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1101.english_translation: The mother, frightened, went to the child and saw him asleep there. She returned and saw the same son there again. Her heart trembled, and her mind could not stay calm.
ramacharitamanas::1101.translation_literal: गै (went) / जननी (mother) / सिसु (child) / पहिं (to) / भयभीता (frightened) / देखा (saw) / बाल (the child) / तहाँ (there) / पुनि (again) / सूता (asleep)॥ / बहुरि (again) / आइ (coming) / देखा (saw) / सुत (son) / सोई (the same) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / कंप (trembling) / मन (mind) / धीर (steady) / न (not) / होई (becomes)
ramacharitamanas::1101.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1101.essence: The familiar child suddenly reveals a mystery that the mind cannot hold.
ramacharitamanas::1101.simple_meaning: Yashoda is startled because she sees the child in two places at once. Her heart shakes, and she cannot make sense of what she is seeing.
ramacharitamanas::1101.simple_insight: Wonder can unsettle even a loving heart when the familiar suddenly becomes impossible.
ramacharitamanas::1101.detailed_meaning: Yashoda has just finished worship and returns to the child she left in the cradle. She finds him asleep there, then goes back and sees him again where she had placed food. The sight shakes her, because this ordinary moment begins to reveal Ram's mysterious nature.
ramacharitamanas::1101.modern_relevance: You check the baby monitor twice because something feels off, and the same impossible little detail appears again. The mind starts to wobble when reality refuses to stay ordinary.
ramacharitamanas::1101.insight: It turns a simple domestic scene into a glimpse of mystery, preparing the reader for Ram's divine play.

ramacharitamanas::1102.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ उहाँ दुइ बालक देखा। मतिभ्रम मोर कि आन बिसेषा॥ देखि राम जननी अकुलानी। प्रभु हँसि दीन्ह मधुर मुसुकानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1102.verse_hindi: (वह सोचने लगी कि) यहाँ और वहाँ मैंने दो बालक देखे। यह मेरी बुद्धि का भ्रम है या और कोई विशेष कारण है? प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी माता को घबड़ाई हुई देखकर मधुर मुस्कान से हँस दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1102.english_translation: She thought, “I have seen two boys here and there. Is this a confusion of my mind, or something else?” Seeing Mother Yashoda anxious, Lord Ram smiled gently and sweetly.
ramacharitamanas::1102.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / उहाँ (there) / दुइ (two) / बालक (boys/children) / देखा (saw) / मतिभ्रम (confusion of mind) / मोर (my) / कि (or) / आन (another/else) / बिसेषा (special cause) ॥ / देखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / जननी (mother) / अकुलानी (anxious/distressed) / प्रभु (Lord) / हँसि (smiling) / दीन्ह (gave) / मधुर (sweet) / मुसुकानी (smile) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1102.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1102.essence: Ram answers confusion with a smile before any explanation.
ramacharitamanas::1102.simple_meaning: Mother Yashoda becomes confused after seeing two boys, and Ram responds with a gentle smile to calm her fear.
ramacharitamanas::1102.simple_insight: Love can steady fear without a word.
ramacharitamanas::1102.detailed_meaning: In Yashoda’s home, she has just seen the child in two places and cannot make sense of it. Alarmed, she wonders whether her mind is deceiving her. Ram notices her distress and answers with a sweet smile before revealing his vast form.
ramacharitamanas::1102.modern_relevance: You glance at the crib, then the hallway, and panic because the child seems to be everywhere at once. The fear is real, but a calm presence can dissolve it before explanation does.
ramacharitamanas::1102.insight: It shifts attention from confusion to reassurance: presence matters more than argument when someone is frightened.

ramacharitamanas::1103.verse_sanskrit: देखरावा मातहि निज अद्भुत रूप अखंड। रोम रोम प्रति लागे कोटि कोटि ब्रह्मंड ॥
ramacharitamanas::1103.verse_hindi: फिर उन्होंने माता को अपना अखंड अद्भुत रूप दिखलाया, जिसके एक-एक रोम में करोड़ों ब्रह्माण्ड लगे हुए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1103.english_translation: Then he showed his mother his wondrous, undivided form, in whose every hair countless universes were contained.
ramacharitamanas::1103.translation_literal: देखरावा (showed) / मातहि (to the mother) / निज (own) / अद्भुत (wondrous) / रूप (form) / अखंड (undivided) / रोम रोम प्रति (in each and every hair) / लागे (were contained) / कोटि कोटि (countless millions) / ब्रह्मंड (universes)
ramacharitamanas::1103.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1103.essence: The child reveals infinity itself, and the mother is made to see.
ramacharitamanas::1103.simple_meaning: Ram reveals to his mother that his true form is vast and undivided, with countless universes contained in every hair.
ramacharitamanas::1103.simple_insight: What looked like a child is also the infinite. Love can suddenly open onto awe.
ramacharitamanas::1103.detailed_meaning: After Yashoda grows uneasy seeing two forms of the child, Ram smiles and reveals his cosmic form to her. In that moment, the mother who thought she knew her son is shown the infinite reality hidden within him.
ramacharitamanas::1103.modern_relevance: You think you know someone by their small daily habits, then one moment of crisis reveals a depth you never imagined. The familiar face can hold an entire universe.
ramacharitamanas::1103.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing only the visible person to recognising the vast reality beneath appearances.

ramacharitamanas::1104.verse_sanskrit: अगनित रबि ससि सिव चतुरानन। बहु गिरि सरित सिंधु महि कानन॥ काल कर्म गुन ग्यान सुभाऊ। सोउ देखा जो सुना न काऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1104.verse_hindi: अगणित सूर्य, चन्द्रमा, शिव, ब्रह्मा, बहुत से पर्वत, नदियाँ, समुद्र, पृथ्वी, वन, काल, कर्म, गुण, ज्ञान और स्वभाव देखे और वे पदार्थ भी देखे जो कभी सुने भी न थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1104.english_translation: She saw countless suns, moons, Shiva, Brahma, many mountains, rivers, oceans, earth, forests, time, action, qualities, knowledge, and nature, along with things never heard before.
ramacharitamanas::1104.translation_literal: अगनित (countless) / रबि (suns) / ससि (moons) / सिव (Shiva) / चतुरानन (four-faced Brahma) / बहु (many) / गिरि (mountains) / सरित (rivers) / सिंधु (oceans) / महि (earth) / कानन (forests) / काल (time) / कर्म (action) / गुन (qualities) / ग्यान (knowledge) / सुभाऊ (nature) / सोउ (also that) / देखा (saw) / जो (which) / सुना (heard) / न (not) / काऊ (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::1104.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1104.essence: The smallest form can hold the whole universe.
ramacharitamanas::1104.simple_meaning: She saw the whole universe inside Ram’s divine form: countless cosmic powers, the world of nature, and even realities beyond ordinary hearing.
ramacharitamanas::1104.simple_insight: A single moment of vision can overturn an entire lifetime of ordinary seeing.
ramacharitamanas::1104.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s palace, mother Yashoda’s vision opens into Ram’s boundless form. What looked like two children becomes a universe: suns, moons, Shiva, Brahma, mountains, rivers, time, karma, and all qualities appear within him.
ramacharitamanas::1104.modern_relevance: A child’s drawing on the fridge suddenly reveals a whole family history: the tiny mark holds memory, love, and meaning you never noticed at first glance.
ramacharitamanas::1104.insight: It shifts perception from seeing a person as small and separate to seeing the vast reality revealed through them.

ramacharitamanas::1105.verse_sanskrit: देखी माया सब बिधि गाढ़ी। अति सभीत जोरें कर ठाढ़ी॥ देखा जीव नचावइ जाही। देखी भगति जो छोरइ ताही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1105.verse_hindi: सब प्रकार से बलवती माया को देखा कि वह (भगवान के सामने) अत्यन्त भयभीत हाथ जोड़े खड़ी है। जीव को देखा, जिसे वह माया नचाती है और (फिर) भक्ति को देखा, जो उस जीव को (माया से) छुड़ा देती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1105.english_translation: He saw Maya in every way, powerful and fearful, standing with folded hands. He saw the jiva that Maya makes dance, and he saw bhakti that frees that jiva from Maya.
ramacharitamanas::1105.translation_literal: देखी (saw) / माया (the veil of appearance) / सब बिधि (in every way) / गाढ़ी (powerful, dense) / अति सभीत (very fearful) / जोरें कर (with joined hands) / ठाढ़ी (standing) / देखा (saw) / जीव (the living being) / नचावइ (makes dance) / जाही (which/whom) / देखी (saw) / भगति (devoted love) / जो (which) / छोरइ (frees) / ताही (that one)
ramacharitamanas::1105.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1105.essence: Devotion is stronger than the force that makes you forget yourself.
ramacharitamanas::1105.simple_meaning: Ram's presence reveals three things: Maya is frightened, the living being is controlled by Maya, and devotion is what breaks that control.
ramacharitamanas::1105.simple_insight: You are not trapped by what confuses you. Devotion gives you a way out.
ramacharitamanas::1105.detailed_meaning: After showing Sita his cosmic form, Ram reveals the deeper order behind existence. The narrator sees Maya standing afraid, the living being being pulled around by her, and bhakti as the power that cuts the bond.
ramacharitamanas::1105.modern_relevance: You know that moment when anxiety keeps spinning your mind, and every thought seems to pull you farther from yourself. Then one sincere act of devotion, trust, or remembrance breaks the loop.
ramacharitamanas::1105.insight: It shifts the mind from feeling helpless under illusion to trusting devotion as the liberating force.

ramacharitamanas::1106.verse_sanskrit: तन पुलकित मुख बचन न आवा। नयन मूदि चरननि सिरु नावा॥ बिसमयवंत देखि महतारी। भए बहुरि सिसुरूप खरारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1106.verse_hindi: (माता का) शरीर पुलकित हो गया, मुख से वचन नहीं निकलता। तब आँखें मूँदकर उसने श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में सिर नवाया। माता को आश्चर्यचकित देखकर खर के शत्रु श्री रामजी फिर बाल रूप हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1106.english_translation: Her body thrilled with devotion, and no words came to her mouth. Closing her eyes, she bowed her head at Ram's feet. Seeing her wonder, the destroyer of Khara returned again to his child form.
ramacharitamanas::1106.translation_literal: तन (body) / पुलकित (thrilled) / मुख (mouth) / बचन (words) / न आवा (did not come) / नयन (eyes) / मूदि (closing) / चरननि (at the feet) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / बिसमयवंत (wonder-filled) / देखि (seeing) / महतारी (mother) / भए (became) / बहुरि (again) / सिसुरूप (child form) / खरारी (enemy of Khara)
ramacharitamanas::1106.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1106.essence: Awe silences the mother, and Ram answers by becoming her child again.
ramacharitamanas::1106.simple_meaning: Mother's body shivers with awe and devotion. She cannot speak, so she bows to Ram's feet. Seeing her wonder, Ram returns to his child form.
ramacharitamanas::1106.simple_insight: Deep reverence can silence the mind before it can explain itself.
ramacharitamanas::1106.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Kaushalya sees the child before her is no ordinary boy. Her body trembles, her speech stops, and she bows in awe. Ram notices her wonder and returns to his child form so she can relate to him as her son.
ramacharitamanas::1106.modern_relevance: You are standing in front of someone you love deeply, and words fail. The heart knows before the mouth does, and reverence changes how you see them.
ramacharitamanas::1106.insight: It shows how awe can interrupt ordinary speech and how Ram meets devotion halfway by softening his form.

ramacharitamanas::1107.verse_sanskrit: अस्तुति करि न जाइ भय माना। जगत पिता मैं सुत करि जाना॥ हरि जननी बहुबिधि समुझाई। यह जनि कतहुँ कहसि सुनु माई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1107.verse_hindi: (माता से) स्तुति भी नहीं की जाती। वह डर गई कि मैंने जगत्पिता परमात्मा को पुत्र करके जाना। श्री हरि ने माता को बहुत प्रकार से समझाया (और कहा-) हे माता! सुनो, यह बात कहीं पर कहना नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1107.english_translation: Worship cannot reach it. She feared, "I have known the father of the world as my son." Hari gently explained to his mother in many ways, "Listen, mother, never speak this aloud."
ramacharitamanas::1107.translation_literal: अस्तुति (praise/worship) / करि (having done) / न जाइ (cannot be done) / भय माना (fear arose) / जगत पिता (father of the world) / मैं (I) / सुत करि (as son) / जाना (knew) / हरि (Hari) / जननी (mother) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / समुझाई (explained) / यह (this) / जनि (do not) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / कहसि (speak) / सुनु (listen) / माई (mother)
ramacharitamanas::1107.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1107.essence: Intimacy with the divine deepens reverence, not familiarity.
ramacharitamanas::1107.simple_meaning: Kausalya realizes that she has known the lord of the world as her son and feels overwhelmed. Ram gently tells her not to speak of it openly.
ramacharitamanas::1107.simple_insight: Even the closest love can tremble before the sacred. Reverence and intimacy can exist together.
ramacharitamanas::1107.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, Kausalya stands before Ram after seeing his divine nature. Overcome, she cannot even praise him properly and fears the weight of what she has understood. Ram comforts her and asks her to keep this realization private.
ramacharitamanas::1107.modern_relevance: You suddenly see a parent, teacher, or partner in a new light and go quiet. Some truths are too tender to parade; they are meant to be held with care.
ramacharitamanas::1107.insight: It teaches you to hold sacred realizations with humility, not display them carelessly.

ramacharitamanas::1108.verse_sanskrit: बार बार कौसल्या बिनय करइ कर जोरि। अब जनि कबहूँ ब्यापै प्रभु मोहि माया तोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1108.verse_hindi: कौसल्याजी बार-बार हाथ जोड़कर विनय करती हैं कि हे प्रभो! मुझे आपकी माया अब कभी न व्यापे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1108.english_translation: Kausalya repeatedly folded her hands and prayed, "Lord, may your veil of appearance never overcome me again."
ramacharitamanas::1108.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / कौसल्या (Kausalya) / बिनय करइ (makes a humble plea) / कर जोरि (with joined hands) / अब (now) / जनि (do not) / कबहूँ (ever) / ब्यापै (overcome) / प्रभु (Lord) / मोहि (me) / माया (the veil of appearance) / तोरि (of you / your)
ramacharitamanas::1108.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::1108.essence: Clear seeing begins when you ask not to be deceived again.
ramacharitamanas::1108.simple_meaning: Kausalya prays with folded hands that she never again be overcome by the veil of appearance and confusion.
ramacharitamanas::1108.simple_insight: There is relief in asking for clear seeing instead of being trapped by appearances.
ramacharitamanas::1108.detailed_meaning: Kausalya has just realised that the child before her is not an ordinary child but Ram himself. Overwhelmed, she bows and then prays for one thing: that Ram's veil of appearance never mislead her again. The moment turns wonder into surrender.
ramacharitamanas::1108.modern_relevance: You finally see a situation clearly after months of making excuses for it. The hardest part is not the truth itself — it is asking not to be fooled by the old story again.
ramacharitamanas::1108.insight: It shifts the mind from enchantment to clear seeing, and from confusion to humble prayer.

ramacharitamanas::1109.verse_sanskrit: बालचरित हरि बहुबिधि कीन्हा। अति अनंद दासन्ह कहँ दीन्हा॥ कछुक काल बीतें सब भाई। बड़े भए परिजन सुखदाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1109.verse_hindi: भगवान ने बहुत प्रकार से बाललीलाएँ कीं और अपने सेवकों को अत्यन्त आनंद दिया। कुछ समय बीतने पर चारों भाई बड़े होकर कुटुम्बियों को सुख देने वाले हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1109.english_translation: The divine performed many childhood pastimes and gave great joy to his devotees. In time, all four brothers grew up and became a source of happiness to their family.
ramacharitamanas::1109.translation_literal: बालचरित (childhood pastimes) / हरि (the divine Ram) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / कीन्हा (did) / अति अनंद (great joy) / दासन्ह (to devotees) / कहँ (for) / दीन्हा (gave) / कछुक (some) / काल (time) / बीतें (having passed) / सब (all) / भाई (brothers) / बड़े भए (became grown) / परिजन (family members) / सुखदाई (bringing happiness)
ramacharitamanas::1109.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1109.essence: Divine play matures into household joy.
ramacharitamanas::1109.simple_meaning: Ram spent his childhood in many playful ways, delighting his devotees. As time passed, the four brothers grew into young men who brought joy to their household.
ramacharitamanas::1109.simple_insight: Joy can be holy long before it becomes useful.
ramacharitamanas::1109.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram's childhood unfolds as sacred play, not ordinary growing up. The verse looks back on those early years and then moves forward: the four brothers mature, and the whole family feels the blessing of their presence.
ramacharitamanas::1109.modern_relevance: A house fills with noise as children grow, and one day you notice the chaos has become a comfort. What once looked like simple play has quietly become the memory that holds everyone together.
ramacharitamanas::1109.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic events to the quiet blessing of growth, family, and shared delight.

ramacharitamanas::1110.verse_sanskrit: चूड़ाकरन कीन्ह गुरु जाई। बिप्रन्ह पुनि दछिना बहु पाई॥ परम मनोहर चरित अपारा। करत फिरत चारिउ सुकुमारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1110.verse_hindi: तब गुरुजी ने जाकर चूड़ाकर्म-संस्कार किया। ब्राह्मणों ने फिर बहुत सी दक्षिणा पाई। चारों सुंदर राजकुमार बड़े ही मनोहर अपार चरित्र करते फिरते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1110.english_translation: Then the guru performed the tonsure ceremony, and the priests received many gifts. The four beautiful princes kept moving about in charming, wondrous ways.
ramacharitamanas::1110.translation_literal: चूड़ाकरन (tonsure ceremony) / कीन्ह (performed) / गुरु (the teacher) / जाई (going) / बिप्रन्ह (to the priests) / पुनि (again) / दछिना (gifts) / बहु (many) / पाई (received) / परम (supremely) / मनोहर (charming) / चरित (deeds) / अपारा (boundless) / करत (doing) / फिरत (moving about) / चारिउ (all four) / सुकुमारा (delicate princes)
ramacharitamanas::1110.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1110.essence: Blessed childhood makes even ritual feel beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::1110.simple_meaning: The boys undergo their ceremonial tonsure, the priests are honored with gifts, and the four princes continue their beautiful childhood activities.
ramacharitamanas::1110.simple_insight: Even ordinary rites and play become radiant when the divine child lives among people.
ramacharitamanas::1110.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the princes have grown past infancy. The family completes the tonsure ceremony, gifts are given to the priests, and Ram, Lakshman, Bharat, and Shatrughna continue their enchanting boyhood. The verse simply marks their blessed childhood moving forward.
ramacharitamanas::1110.modern_relevance: A family photo day turns into a blur of rituals, gifts, and children running everywhere. Some moments matter not because they are dramatic, but because they quietly mark a life being formed.
ramacharitamanas::1110.insight: It trains attention to see sacred significance inside ordinary family milestones.

ramacharitamanas::1111.verse_sanskrit: मन क्रम बचन अगोचर जोई। दसरथ अजिर बिचर प्रभु सोई॥ भोजन करत बोल जब राजा। नहिं आवत तजि बाल समाजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1111.verse_hindi: जो मन, वचन और कर्म से अगोचर हैं, वही प्रभु दशरथजी के आँगन में विचर रहे हैं। भोजन करने के समय जब राजा बुलाते हैं, तब वे अपने बाल सखाओं के समाज को छोड़कर नहीं आते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1111.english_translation: The Lord, beyond mind, speech, and action, roams in Dasharath's courtyard. When the king calls at mealtime, he does not leave his playmates.
ramacharitamanas::1111.translation_literal: मन (mind) / क्रम (action) / बचन (speech) / अगोचर (beyond perception) / जोई (who) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / अजिर (courtyard) / बिचर (roams) / प्रभु (Lord) / सोई (that same one) // भोजन (meal) / करत (doing) / बोल (call) / जब (when) / राजा (king) / नहिं (not) / आवत (comes) / तजि (leaving) / बाल (child) / समाजा (company)
ramacharitamanas::1111.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1111.essence: The ungraspable Lord lives as a playful child at home.
ramacharitamanas::1111.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond ordinary grasp, yet he plays in Dasharath's courtyard like an ordinary child. Even when called for meals, he stays with his boyhood companions.
ramacharitamanas::1111.simple_insight: The infinite can also be intimate. Love makes the ungraspable feel close.
ramacharitamanas::1111.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the divine child Ram has grown up among his brothers and friends. He is beyond ordinary understanding, yet he still runs and plays in Dasharath's courtyard. Even the king has to call him for meals, because the child is absorbed in play.
ramacharitamanas::1111.modern_relevance: A child is so deep in a game in the courtyard that a parent has to call twice for dinner. The scene feels ordinary, yet it carries wonder: the highest presence can live inside the simplest family moment.
ramacharitamanas::1111.insight: It shifts attention from remote divinity to accessible presence, showing that greatness can appear in ordinary affection and play.

ramacharitamanas::1112.verse_sanskrit: कौसल्या जब बोलन जाई। ठुमुकु ठुमुकु प्रभु चलहिं पराई॥ निगम नेति सिव अंत न पावा। ताहि धरै जननी हठि धावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1112.verse_hindi: कौसल्या जब बुलाने जाती हैं, तब प्रभु ठुमुक-ठुमुक भाग चलते हैं। जिनका वेद 'नेति' (इतना ही नहीं) कहकर निरूपण करते हैं और शिवजी ने जिनका अन्त नहीं पाया, माता उन्हें हठपूर्वक पकड़ने के लिए दौड़ती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1112.english_translation: When Kaushalya goes to call him, the Lord runs along in tiny, toddling steps. The one whom the Vedas describe as "not this, not that," and whose end even Shiva could not find, that same one the mother chases after in playful insistence.
ramacharitamanas::1112.translation_literal: कौसल्या (Kaushalya) / जब (when) / बोलन (to call) / जाई (goes) / ठुमुकु ठुमुकु (with toddling steps) / प्रभु (the Lord) / चलहिं (walks/runs) / पराई (away) ॥ / निगम (the Vedas) / नेति (not this, not this) / सिव (Shiva) / अंत (end) / न (not) / पावा (found) / ताहि (that one) / धरै (to catch/hold) / जननी (mother) / हठि (insistently) / धावा (runs) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1112.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1112.essence: The infinite becomes intimate when love calls.
ramacharitamanas::1112.simple_meaning: Kaushalya calls Ram, and he runs to her like a small child. The same one beyond all description becomes playfully reachable in a mother's love.
ramacharitamanas::1112.simple_insight: Love makes the immeasurable feel close, tender, and touchable.
ramacharitamanas::1112.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the child Ram is playing at home. Kaushalya calls him, and the cosmic Lord comes toddling toward her. Tulsidas contrasts Ram's boundlessness with a mother's intimate love, showing how devotion makes the infinite feel near.
ramacharitamanas::1112.modern_relevance: A child hears their mother's voice from another room and runs before thinking. That instinctive pull toward love is what this verse honors: the highest reality is not distant when the heart is open.
ramacharitamanas::1112.insight: It shifts reverence from awe alone to intimacy, showing that greatness and tenderness can live together.

ramacharitamanas::1113.verse_sanskrit: धूसर धूरि भरें तनु आए। भूपति बिहसि गोद बैठाए ॥।
ramacharitamanas::1113.verse_hindi: वे शरीर में धूल लपेटे हुए आए और राजा ने हँसकर उन्हें गोद में बैठा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1113.english_translation: Covered in dust, they came with their bodies smeared in dirt. The king laughed and seated them on his lap.
ramacharitamanas::1113.translation_literal: धूसर (dusty) / धूरि (dust) / भरें (filled with) / तनु (body) / आए (came) / भूपति (king) / बिहसि (laughing) / गोद (lap) / बैठाए (seated)
ramacharitamanas::1113.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1113.essence: Dust and delight meet in a king’s embrace.
ramacharitamanas::1113.simple_meaning: The children came back covered in dust, and King Dasharath smiled and lifted them into his lap.
ramacharitamanas::1113.simple_insight: Love notices the mess and welcomes it anyway.
ramacharitamanas::1113.detailed_meaning: In Dasharath's palace, the little princes return from play covered in dust. The king laughs and pulls them onto his lap, showing the warm, ordinary tenderness that surrounds Ram's childhood before the deeper divine meaning is revealed.
ramacharitamanas::1113.modern_relevance: A child runs in from the yard with scraped knees and a dirty shirt. Instead of scolding, a parent smiles and hugs them close. That small welcome is the whole mood here.
ramacharitamanas::1113.insight: It shifts attention from spotless appearance to affectionate acceptance.

ramacharitamanas::1114.verse_sanskrit: भोजन करत चपल चित इत उत अवसरु पाइ। भाजि चले किलकत मुख दधि ओदन लपटाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1114.verse_hindi: भोजन करते हैं, पर चित चंचल है। अवसर पाकर मुँह में दही-भात लपटाए किलकारी मारते हुए इधर-उधर भाग चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1114.english_translation: While eating, the mind stays playful and restless. At the first chance, he runs off with a mouthful of yogurt rice, laughing and scattering it about.
ramacharitamanas::1114.translation_literal: भोजन करत (while eating) / चपल चित (restless mind) / इत उत (here and there) / अवसरु (opportunity) / पाइ (having found) / भाजि चले (ran away) / किलकत (laughing/crying out) / मुख (mouth) / दधि ओदन (yogurt rice) / लपटाइ (smearing/holding on)
ramacharitamanas::1114.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1114.essence: Playfulness itself becomes sacred in Ram's childhood.
ramacharitamanas::1114.simple_meaning: Little Ram is so playful that even while eating, he slips away with food in his mouth as soon as he gets the chance.
ramacharitamanas::1114.simple_insight: There is delight in a child who cannot be contained, even for a meal.
ramacharitamanas::1114.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the child Ram is being lovingly fed after his dusty play. The moment is not teaching doctrine; it is a tender glimpse of his untamed childhood, where even eating turns into a game and the whole court watches his charm.
ramacharitamanas::1114.modern_relevance: A toddler grabs a bite, smears it across his face, and bolts from the chair before anyone can stop him. The scene makes everyone smile because joy refuses to sit still.
ramacharitamanas::1114.insight: It invites the reader to see divinity in ordinary, mischievous childhood play rather than only in solemn grandeur.

ramacharitamanas::1115.verse_sanskrit: बालचरित अति सरल सुहाए। सारद सेष संभु श्रुति गाए॥ जिन्ह कर मन इन्ह सन नहिं राता। ते जन बंचित किए बिधाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1115.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की बहुत ही सरल (भोली) और सुंदर (मनभावनी) बाललीलाओं का सरस्वती, शेषजी, शिवजी और वेदों ने गान किया है। जिनका मन इन लीलाओं में अनुरक्त नहीं हुआ, विधाता ने उन मनुष्यों को वंचित कर दिया (नितांत भाग्यहीन बनाया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1115.english_translation: Ram's childhood play is simple and beautiful. Saraswati, Shesha, Shiva, and the Vedas sing it. Whoever does not love these scenes is deprived by the creator.
ramacharitamanas::1115.translation_literal: बालचरित (childhood play) / अति (very) / सरल (simple) / सुहाए (beautiful, delightful) / सारद (Saraswati) / सेष (Shesha) / संभु (Shiva) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / गाए (sang, praised) / जिन्ह (those who) / कर (whose) / मन (mind) / इन्ह सन (in these) / नहिं राता (did not become absorbed) / ते (those) / जन (people) / बंचित (deprived) / किए (made) / बिधाता (the creator)
ramacharitamanas::1115.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1115.essence: Ram's childhood sweetness is so complete that indifference becomes a loss.
ramacharitamanas::1115.simple_meaning: Ram's childhood acts are so lovely that even great beings and sacred texts praise them. A person who feels no love for them misses something essential.
ramacharitamanas::1115.simple_insight: It invites warmth and reverence, not analysis — devotion begins with delight in Ram's sweetness.
ramacharitamanas::1115.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, the poem pauses over Ram's childhood as something even Saraswati, Shesha, Shiva, and the Vedas celebrate. Tulsidas says that a heart untouched by this sweetness is somehow left empty, because it has missed Ram's living charm.
ramacharitamanas::1115.modern_relevance: You scroll past a child's laughter because you're too busy, then later realize you missed the only thing that softened the whole day. This verse says that tenderness matters more than your schedule.
ramacharitamanas::1115.insight: It shifts attention from achievement to reverence, teaching the mind to cherish divine sweetness before it hardens.

ramacharitamanas::1116.verse_sanskrit: भए कुमार जबहिं सब भ्राता। दीन्ह जनेऊ गुरु पितु माता॥ गुरगृहँ गए पढ़न रघुराई। अलप काल बिद्या सब आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1116.verse_hindi: ज्यों ही सब भाई कुमारावस्था के हुए, त्यों ही गुरु, पिता और माता ने उनका यज्ञोपवीत संस्कार कर दिया। श्री रघुनाथजी (भाइयों सहित) गुरु के घर में विद्या पढ़ने गए और थोड़े ही समय में उनको सब विद्याएँ आ गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1116.english_translation: When all the brothers reached boyhood, their sacred thread ceremony was performed by the guru, father, and mother. Then the Raghu prince went to the guru's house to study, and in a short time all knowledge came to him.
ramacharitamanas::1116.translation_literal: भए (became) / कुमार (boys, youths) / जबहिं (when) / सब (all) / भ्राता (brothers)। / दीन्ह (gave) / जनेऊ (sacred thread ceremony) / गुरु (guru) / पितु (father) / माता (mother)॥ / गुरगृहँ (to the guru's house) / गए (went) / पढ़न (to study) / रघुराई (Raghuraj, Ram)। / अलप (little) / काल (time) / बिद्या (knowledge, learning) / सब (all) / आई (came) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1116.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1116.essence: Even the highest one learns through humility.
ramacharitamanas::1116.simple_meaning: The brothers grow up, receive their sacred thread ceremony, and go to study with the guru. Ram learns quickly and completely.
ramacharitamanas::1116.simple_insight: Real greatness begins with humility, learning, and respect for the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::1116.detailed_meaning: The four brothers have left childhood behind. Their family sends them through the sacred thread ceremony, and Ram goes with his brothers to the guru's house. Even though he is divine, he enters learning like an obedient student, and all knowledge comes easily.
ramacharitamanas::1116.modern_relevance: A gifted child still shows up on the first day, carrying a notebook and listening carefully while everyone else assumes talent is enough.
ramacharitamanas::1116.insight: It shifts admiration away from raw ability and toward disciplined learning and reverence for the teacher.

ramacharitamanas::1117.verse_sanskrit: जाकी सहज स्वास श्रुति चारी। सो हरि पढ़ यह कौतुक भारी॥ बिद्या बिनय निपुन गुन सीला। खेलहिंखेल सकल नृपलीला ॥
ramacharitamanas::1117.verse_hindi: चारों वेद जिनके स्वाभाविक श्वास हैं, वे भगवान पढ़ें, यह बड़ा कौतुक (अचरज) है। चारों भाई विद्या, विनय, गुण और शील में (बड़े) निपुण हैं और सब राजाओं की लीलाओं के ही खेल खेलते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1117.english_translation: The four Vedas are their natural breath, yet Hari studies them—what a wondrous play. The four brothers are skilled in learning, humility, virtue, and good conduct; they play at the sport of kings.
ramacharitamanas::1117.translation_literal: जाकी (whose) / सहज (natural) / स्वास (breath) / श्रुति (Vedas) / चारी (four) / सो (that) / हरि (Hari) / पढ़ (studies) / यह (this) / कौतुक (wonder) / भारी (great) / बिद्या (learning) / बिनय (humility) / निपुन (skilled) / गुन (virtues) / सीला (good conduct) / खेलहिं (they play) / खेल (play) / सकल (all) / नृपलीला (kings' play)
ramacharitamanas::1117.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1117.essence: Even the all-knowing can choose the path of learning with humility.
ramacharitamanas::1117.simple_meaning: Ram and his brothers are naturally perfect, yet they still learn like ordinary princes. Their learning, humility, virtues, and royal grace make their childhood feel wondrous.
ramacharitamanas::1117.simple_insight: Greatness can be humble. Real excellence does not need to announce itself.
ramacharitamanas::1117.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the boys' sacred thread ceremony, Ram and his brothers go to the teacher's house. Tulsidas pauses to marvel that the one whose breath is the Vedas still studies them, while the brothers grow into learning, humility, virtue, and royal ease.
ramacharitamanas::1117.modern_relevance: A child who already knows the answer still sits quietly and listens in class. That image of effortless greatness is what this verse celebrates: mastery without arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::1117.insight: It shifts admiration from flashy talent to graceful discipline and humility.

ramacharitamanas::1118.verse_sanskrit: करतल बान धनुष अति सोहा। देखत रूप चराचर मोहा॥ जिन्ह बीथिन्ह बिहरहिं सब भाई। थकित होहिं सब लोग लुगाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1118.verse_hindi: हाथों में बाण और धनुष बहुत ही शोभा देते हैं। रूप देखते ही चराचर (जड़-चेतन) मोहित हो जाते हैं। वे सब भाई जिन गलियों में खेलते (हुए निकलते) हैं, उन गलियों के सभी स्त्री-पुरुष उनको देखकर स्नेह से शिथिल हो जाते हैं अथवा ठिठककर रह जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1118.english_translation: The bow and arrows in their hands look beautiful. Just seeing their form enchants all that moves and all that does not. In whatever lanes the four brothers walk, every man and woman there pauses, delighted and spellbound.
ramacharitamanas::1118.translation_literal: करतल (in the hand) / बान (arrow) / धनुष (bow) / अति (very) / सोहा (looked beautiful) / देखत (seeing) / रूप (form/beauty) / चराचर (moving and unmoving beings) / मोहा (became enchanted) / जिन्ह (in which) / बीथिन्ह (lanes) / बिहरहिं (wander/walk) / सब (all) / भाई (brothers) / थकित (swayed/paused) / होहिं (become) / सब (all) / लोग (people) / लुगाई (women)
ramacharitamanas::1118.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1118.essence: Beauty so complete makes everyone pause.
ramacharitamanas::1118.simple_meaning: The four brothers are so beautiful with bow and arrows that everyone who sees them stops and feels delighted.
ramacharitamanas::1118.simple_insight: True grace quiets a crowd without effort.
ramacharitamanas::1118.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, Bharat, and Shatrughna have grown into radiant young princes. Their beauty and bearing are so striking that even the streets of Ayodhya fall silent when they pass. This verse shows how naturally they draw every heart.
ramacharitamanas::1118.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after months away, and the noise fades before anyone speaks. Not because you demand attention, but because your presence carries calm, grace, and warmth.
ramacharitamanas::1118.insight: It shifts attention from outward display to the quiet power of presence.
