ramacharitamanas::1119.verse_sanskrit: कोसलपुर बासी नर नारि बृद्ध अरु बाल। प्रानहु ते प्रिय लागत सब कहुँ राम कृपाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1119.verse_hindi: कोसलपुर के रहने वाले स्त्री, पुरुष, बूढ़े और बालक सभी को कृपालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी प्राणों से भी बढ़कर प्रिय लगते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1119.english_translation: The men, women, elders, and children of Kosalpur all hold compassionate Ram dearer than life itself.
ramacharitamanas::1119.translation_literal: कोसलपुर (of Kosalpur) / बासी (residents) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / बृद्ध (elders) / अरु (and) / बाल (children) / प्रानहु ते (than life itself) / प्रिय (dear) / लागत (seem) / सब कहुँ (to everyone) / राम (Ram) / कृपाल (compassionate)
ramacharitamanas::1119.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1119.essence: Love makes Ram dearer than breath.
ramacharitamanas::1119.simple_meaning: Everyone in Koshalpur, from children to elders, feels Ram is more precious than life itself.
ramacharitamanas::1119.simple_insight: Love can become so complete that even fear of loss disappears.
ramacharitamanas::1119.detailed_meaning: In Koshalpur, Ram's presence has transformed ordinary people into devotees. Men, women, elders, and children all feel that his compassion is worth more than their own lives. This verse shows the depth of public love around Ram before the next scene moves on.
ramacharitamanas::1119.modern_relevance: At a family gathering, one person walks in and the whole room softens. Nobody is performing, nobody is calculating—everyone simply feels safer, happier, more themselves. That is the kind of presence this verse celebrates.
ramacharitamanas::1119.insight: It shifts attention from admiration to belonging: Ram is not just respected, he is cherished as life itself.

ramacharitamanas::1120.verse_sanskrit: बंधु सखा सँग लेहिं बोलाई। बन मृगया नित खेलहिं जाई॥ पावन मृग मारहिं जियँ जानी। दिन प्रति नृपहि देखावहिं आनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1120.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी भाइयों और इष्ट मित्रों को बुलाकर साथ ले लेते हैं और नित्य वन में जाकर शिकार खेलते हैं। मन में पवित्र समझकर मृगों को मारते हैं और प्रतिदिन लाकर राजा (दशरथजी) को दिखलाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1120.english_translation: Ram called his brothers and friends to go with him, and they went daily into the forest to hunt. Knowing the deer to be pure, he would kill them and bring them each day to show King Dasharath.
ramacharitamanas::1120.translation_literal: बंधु (brothers) / सखा (friends) / सँग (with) / लेहिं (take) / बोलाई (calling) / बन (forest) / मृगया (hunting) / नित (daily) / खेलहिं (play) / जाई (going) / पावन (pure) / मृग (deer) / मारहिं (kill) / जियँ (in heart) / जानी (knowing) / दिन प्रति (every day) / नृपहि (to the king) / देखावहिं (show) / आनी (bringing)
ramacharitamanas::1120.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1120.essence: Peaceful days can be the ones you miss most after they pass.
ramacharitamanas::1120.simple_meaning: Ram goes into the forest with his brothers and friends, hunts deer, and brings them back to show Dasharath.
ramacharitamanas::1120.simple_insight: The scene matters more as a glimpse of Ram's life than as a teaching. It shows royal ease before exile.
ramacharitamanas::1120.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram spends his days with Lakshman and his companions, going into the forest for hunting and returning to show the slain deer to Dasharath. The verse paints the calm, beloved world before exile, not a lesson.
ramacharitamanas::1120.modern_relevance: A family remembers the ordinary days before everything changed — the shared outings, the easy laughter, the small rituals that later feel precious because they were never noticed then.
ramacharitamanas::1120.insight: It frames Ram's early life as lived harmony, making the coming break feel deeper.

ramacharitamanas::1121.verse_sanskrit: जे मृग राम बान के मारे। ते तनु तजि सुरलोक सिधारे॥ अनुज सखा सँग भोजन करहीं। मातु पिता अग्या अनुसरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1121.verse_hindi: जो मृग श्री रामजी के बाण से मारे जाते थे, वे शरीर छोड़कर देवलोक को चले जाते थे। श्री रामचन्द्रजी अपने छोटे भाइयों और सखाओं के साथ भोजन करते हैं और माता-पिता की आज्ञा का पालन करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1121.english_translation: The deer killed by Ram's arrows left their bodies and went to the higher realm. Ram ate with his younger brothers and friends, and obeyed his mother and father.
ramacharitamanas::1121.translation_literal: जे (those) / मृग (deer) / राम (Ram) / बान (arrow) / के (of) / मारे (struck-killed) / ते (they) / तनु (body) / तजि (leaving) / सुरलोक (higher realm) / सिधारे (departed) / अनुज (younger brothers) / सखा (friends) / सँग (with) / भोजन (meal) / करहीं (do) / मातु (mother) / पिता (father) / अग्या (command) / अनुसरहीं (follow)
ramacharitamanas::1121.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1121.essence: Strength becomes sacred when it remains gentle and obedient.
ramacharitamanas::1121.simple_meaning: Ram's arrows sent the deer to a higher realm, while Ram lived gently at home with his brothers and friends, always following his parents' commands.
ramacharitamanas::1121.simple_insight: Power can stay gentle. True greatness shows itself in kindness, not arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::1121.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Tulsidas paints Ram's daily life as both playful and pure. His arrows free the deer, then he returns to shared meals, brotherly company, and obedience to his parents. The scene shows divine power expressed as domestic grace.
ramacharitamanas::1121.modern_relevance: A person with real authority in the room does not need to dominate it. They can still eat with others, listen, and keep faith with family obligations.
ramacharitamanas::1121.insight: It shifts attention from force to character: power becomes noble when it serves harmony and duty.

ramacharitamanas::1122.verse_sanskrit: जेहि बिधि सुखी होहिं पुर लोगा। करहिं कृपानिधि सोइ संजोगा॥ बेद पुरान सुनहिं मन लाई। आपु कहहिं अनुजन्ह समुझाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1122.verse_hindi: जिस प्रकार नगर के लोग सुखी हों, कृपानिधान श्री रामचन्द्रजी वही संयोग (लीला) करते हैं। वे मन लगाकर वेद-पुराण सुनते हैं और फिर स्वयं छोटे भाइयों को समझाकर कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1122.english_translation: In whatever way the people of the city may be happy, the treasure of compassion arranges that very circumstance. He listens to the Vedas and Puranas with full attention, then explains them to his younger brothers himself.
ramacharitamanas::1122.translation_literal: जेहि बिधि (in whatever way) / सुखी (happy) / होहिं (become) / पुर (city) / लोगा (people) / करहिं (do) / कृपानिधि (treasure of compassion) / सोइ (that very) / संजोगा (circumstance) / बेद (Veda) / पुरान (Puranas) / सुनहिं (listen) / मन लाई (with mind applied) / आपु (himself) / कहहिं (says) / अनुजन्ह (to younger brothers) / समुझाई (explaining)
ramacharitamanas::1122.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1122.essence: Ram's care for others includes listening deeply and teaching gently.
ramacharitamanas::1122.simple_meaning: Ram arranges his life to bring happiness to the people of Ayodhya. He also listens carefully to sacred teachings and explains them to his brothers.
ramacharitamanas::1122.simple_insight: True leadership includes learning quietly and then passing wisdom on with care.
ramacharitamanas::1122.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram is already living as the ideal prince. He shapes his daily life for the people's well-being, listens deeply to sacred teachings, and then personally explains them to Lakshman and the other brothers. The verse shows his gentle discipline before the next scene of royal duty.
ramacharitamanas::1122.modern_relevance: You finish a long day, then still sit with a younger sibling or teammate and explain what you learned instead of showing off. Real care includes helping others understand.
ramacharitamanas::1122.insight: It connects public duty with private study: serve people, keep learning, and teach what you learn to those near you.

ramacharitamanas::1123.verse_sanskrit: प्रातकाल उठि कै रघुनाथा। मातु पिता गुरु नावहिं माथा॥ आयसु मागि करहिं पुर काजा। देखि चरित हरषइ मन राजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1123.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी प्रातःकाल उठकर माता-पिता और गुरु को मस्तक नवाते हैं और आज्ञा लेकर नगर का काम करते हैं। उनके चरित्र देख-देखकर राजा मन में बड़े हर्षित होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1123.english_translation: Raghunath rises at dawn, bows to his mother, father, and teacher, and asks permission before handling the city's affairs. Seeing his conduct, the king's heart fills with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1123.translation_literal: प्रातकाल (at dawn) / उठि कै (having risen) / रघुनाथा (Raghunath) / मातु (mother) / पिता (father) / गुरु (teacher) / नावहिं (they bow) / माथा (the head) / आयसु (permission / command) / मागि (asking) / करहिं (they do) / पुर (city) / काजा (work / affairs) / देखि (seeing) / चरित (conduct) / हरषइ (rejoices) / मन (the mind) / राजा (the king)
ramacharitamanas::1123.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1123.essence: True greatness bows before it acts.
ramacharitamanas::1123.simple_meaning: Ram begins the day with respect, asks permission before acting, and handles his duties well. His conduct delights the king.
ramacharitamanas::1123.simple_insight: A steady life begins with humility. Respect before action keeps power clean.
ramacharitamanas::1123.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram rises early, bows to Kaushalya, Dasharath, and his teacher, then asks leave before taking up the city's work. The sight of his disciplined conduct fills the king with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1123.modern_relevance: You wake before everyone else, check your phone, and still choose to greet the people who shaped you before touching the day's tasks. That small order changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::1123.insight: It teaches you to begin action with humility and permission, not ego and impulse.

ramacharitamanas::1124.verse_sanskrit: ब्यापक अकल अनीह अज निर्गुन नाम न रूप। भगत हेतु नाना बिधि करत चरित्र अनूप ॥
ramacharitamanas::1124.verse_hindi: जो व्यापक, अकल (निरवयव), इच्छारहित, अजन्मा और निर्गुण है तथा जिनका न नाम है न रूप, वही भगवान भक्तों के लिए नाना प्रकार के अनुपम (अलौकिक) चरित्र करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1124.english_translation: The all-pervading, uncreated, desireless, birthless, formless one performs many wondrous acts for devotees.
ramacharitamanas::1124.translation_literal: ब्यापक (all-pervading) / अकल (without parts) / अनीह (desireless) / अज (unborn) / निर्गुन (without qualities) / नाम (name) / न रूप (and no form) / भगत हेतु (for devotees) / नाना बिधि (in many ways) / करत (does) / चरित्र (acts, pastimes) / अनूप (matchless)
ramacharitamanas::1124.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1124.essence: The formless one becomes personally present for those who love him.
ramacharitamanas::1124.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond form, name, and desire, yet he still appears in countless beautiful ways for devotees.
ramacharitamanas::1124.simple_insight: Love makes the distant feel near. The divine is not less infinite for becoming personally present.
ramacharitamanas::1124.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas pauses after describing Ram's ideal conduct in Ayodhya and names the deepest paradox: the limitless, formless Ram still moves through the world in beautiful ways for those who love him. The verse turns story into theology.
ramacharitamanas::1124.modern_relevance: You can feel utterly unseen, then one small act of care changes everything. This verse says the deepest presence often arrives quietly, in a form you can actually meet.
ramacharitamanas::1124.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract belief to lived encounter: the infinite becomes relatable through loving action.

ramacharitamanas::1125.verse_sanskrit: यह सब चरित कहा मैं गाई। आगिलि कथा सुनहु मन लाई॥ बिस्वामित्र महामुनि ग्यानी। बसहिं बिपिन सुभ आश्रम जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1125.verse_hindi: यह सब चरित्र मैंने गाकर (बखानकर) कहा। अब आगे की कथा मन लगाकर सुनो। ज्ञानी महामुनि विश्वामित्रजी वन में शुभ आश्रम (पवित्र स्थान) जानकर बसते थे, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1125.english_translation: I have sung and told all these deeds. Now listen closely to the next part of the story. The wise great sage Vishwamitra lived in a beautiful hermitage in the forest.
ramacharitamanas::1125.translation_literal: यह (this) / सब (all) / चरित (deeds, story) / कहा (said, told) / मैं (I) / गाई (sung) / आगिलि (next, further) / कथा (story, account) / सुनहु (listen) / मन (mind) / लाई (applying, focusing) / बिस्वामित्र (Vishwamitra) / महामुनि (great sage) / ग्यानी (wise, knowledgeable) / बसहिं (dwelt, lived) / बिपिन (forest) / सुभ (auspicious, beautiful) / आश्रम (hermitage) / जानी (known, recognized)
ramacharitamanas::1125.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1125.essence: A new chapter begins when attention turns fully toward it.
ramacharitamanas::1125.simple_meaning: The narrator closes one section and asks the listener to pay attention to the next. Vishwamitra, a wise sage, lives in a holy forest hermitage.
ramacharitamanas::1125.simple_insight: The story slows down so attention can deepen before the next turning point.
ramacharitamanas::1125.detailed_meaning: The narration shifts from Ram's daily conduct to the next chapter of the story. Tulsidas invites the listener to lean in, then introduces Vishwamitra living in a blessed forest hermitage, setting up the crisis that will soon reach him.
ramacharitamanas::1125.modern_relevance: You finish one chapter of your life and sense the next one arriving. Before the next demand hits, the mind needs a pause so it can actually receive what comes.
ramacharitamanas::1125.insight: It teaches you to treat transitions as sacred attention points, not empty gaps.

ramacharitamanas::1126.verse_sanskrit: जहँ जप जग्य जोग मुनि करहीं। अति मारीच सुबाहुहि डरहीं॥ देखत जग्य निसाचर धावहिं। करहिं उपद्रव मुनि दुख पावहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1126.verse_hindi: जहाँ वे मुनि जप, यज्ञ और योग करते थे, परन्तु मारीच और सुबाहु से बहुत डरते थे। यज्ञ देखते ही राक्षस दौड़ पड़ते थे और उपद्रव मचाते थे, जिससे मुनि (बहुत) दुःख पाते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1126.english_translation: Where the sages performed chanting, sacrifice, and yoga, Maricha and Subahu feared them greatly. At the sight of a sacrifice, the demons would rush in and create trouble, and the sages suffered distress.
ramacharitamanas::1126.translation_literal: जहँ (where) / जप (chanting) / जग्य (sacrifice) / जोग (yoga) / मुनि (sages) / करहीं (were doing) / अति (very) / मारीच (Maricha) / सुबाहुहि (Subahu) / डरहीं (feared) / देखत (seeing) / जग्य (sacrifice) / निसाचर (demons) / धावहिं (ran) / करहिं (did) / उपद्रव (trouble) / मुनि (sages) / दुख (sorrow) / पावहिं (suffered)
ramacharitamanas::1126.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1126.essence: Sacred work collapses when disturbance is allowed to rule.
ramacharitamanas::1126.simple_meaning: The sages were trying to live in peace through chanting, sacrifice, and meditation, but demons kept attacking and disturbing their rites.
ramacharitamanas::1126.simple_insight: Even sincere practice can be interrupted by forces that thrive on disorder.
ramacharitamanas::1126.detailed_meaning: In the forest near Vishvamitra's hermitage, the sages are trying to keep their sacred fire rites alive. Maricha and Subahu keep terrorising them, turning holy practice into fear and exhaustion. This scene creates the need for Ram's intervention.
ramacharitamanas::1126.modern_relevance: You finally sit down to focus, and the phone keeps buzzing, the door keeps opening, and your attention keeps getting stolen. Some work cannot survive without protection.
ramacharitamanas::1126.insight: It shifts attention from the ritual itself to the conditions needed to protect it.

ramacharitamanas::1127.verse_sanskrit: गाधितनय मन चिंता ब्यापी। हरि बिनु मरहिं न निसिचर पापी॥ तब मुनिबर मन कीन्ह बिचारा। प्रभु अवतरेउ हरन महि भारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1127.verse_hindi: गाधि के पुत्र विश्वामित्रजी के मन में चिन्ता छा गई कि ये पापी राक्षस भगवान के (मारे) बिना न मरेंगे। तब श्रेष्ठ मुनि ने मन में विचार किया कि प्रभु ने पृथ्वी का भार हरने के लिए अवतार लिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1127.english_translation: A worry filled the mind of Gadhi's son: these sinful demons will not die without the divine. Then the great sage reflected: the Lord has incarnated to remove the burden of the earth.
ramacharitamanas::1127.translation_literal: गाधितनय (son of Gadhi) / मन (mind) / चिंता (worry) / ब्यापी (spread) / हरि (the divine) / बिनु (without) / मरहिं (will die) / न (not) / निसिचर (night-wanderers, demons) / पापी (sinful)॥ / तब (then) / मुनिबर (great sage) / मन (mind) / कीन्ह (made) / बिचारा (reflection) / प्रभु (Lord) / अवतरेउ (has incarnated) / हरन (to remove) / महि (earth) / भारा (burden)॥
ramacharitamanas::1127.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1127.essence: Some problems yield only to the force already sent to end them.
ramacharitamanas::1127.simple_meaning: विश्वामित्र को चिंता हुई कि ये राक्षस भगवान के बिना नहीं मरेंगे। तब उन्होंने सोचा कि प्रभु पृथ्वी का बोझ हरने के लिए अवतार ले चुके हैं।
ramacharitamanas::1127.simple_insight: When ordinary means fail, the mind turns toward a larger help already at work.
ramacharitamanas::1127.detailed_meaning: विश्वामित्र के आश्रम पर राक्षस बार-बार यज्ञ भंग कर रहे हैं. गाधि-पुत्र समझ जाते हैं कि केवल तप या मंत्र से यह संकट नहीं मिटेगा. उसी क्षण उन्हें राम के अवतार का बोध होता है, और वे आगे सहायता माँगने का निश्चय करते हैं.
ramacharitamanas::1127.modern_relevance: You have tried every practical fix, and the problem keeps returning. Then a quieter thought arrives: this is bigger than your control, and the right help already exists.
ramacharitamanas::1127.insight: It shifts the mind from helpless struggle to seeking the right support at the right level.

ramacharitamanas::1128.verse_sanskrit: एहूँ मिस देखौं पद जाई। करि बिनती आनौं दोउ भाई॥ ग्यान बिराग सकल गुन अयना। सो प्रभु मैं देखब भरि नयना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1128.verse_hindi: इसी बहाने जाकर मैं उनके चरणों का दर्शन करूँ और विनती करके दोनों भाइयों को ले आऊँ। (अहा!) जो ज्ञान, वैराग्य और सब गुणों के धाम हैं, उन प्रभु को मैं नेत्र भरकर देखूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1128.english_translation: Using this excuse, I will go and see his feet. After praying, I will bring both brothers back. The Lord who is the home of wisdom, non-attachment, and every virtue—I will behold him with these eyes full.
ramacharitamanas::1128.translation_literal: एहूँ मिस (using this excuse) / देखौं (I will see) / पद (feet) / जाई (going) / करि (doing) / बिनती (request) / आनौं (I will bring) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / ग्यान (wisdom) / बिराग (non-attachment) / सकल (all) / गुन (virtues) / अयना (abode/home) / सो (that) / प्रभु (lord) / मैं (I) / देखब (will see) / भरि (filled) / नयना (eyes)
ramacharitamanas::1128.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramacharitamanas::1128.essence: Even a mission can become a longing to behold the highest.
ramacharitamanas::1128.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra plans to visit Ram, bow before him, and bring the two brothers back. He longs to see Ram, who embodies wisdom, detachment, and every virtue.
ramacharitamanas::1128.simple_insight: Even a great seeker still longs to behold the source of all virtues.
ramacharitamanas::1128.detailed_meaning: After the forest sages describe the terror of Maricha and Subahu, Vishwamitra decides to go to King Dasharath. He hopes to bring Ram and Lakshman with him, but beneath the practical plan is devotion: he wants to see Ram, the home of wisdom and non-attachment.
ramacharitamanas::1128.modern_relevance: You make a practical visit for help, but your deeper reason is reverence. Beneath the errand, you are longing to be near what you admire most.
ramacharitamanas::1128.insight: It shifts action from mere strategy to pilgrimage, where even a task becomes a way to meet what is highest.

ramacharitamanas::1129.verse_sanskrit: बहुबिधि करत मनोरथ जात लागि नहिं बार। करि मज्जन सरऊ जल गए भूप दरबार ॥
ramacharitamanas::1129.verse_hindi: बहुत प्रकार से मनोरथ करते हुए जाने में देर नहीं लगी। सरयूजी के जल में स्नान करके वे राजा के दरवाजे पर पहुँचे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1129.english_translation: Thinking many thoughts along the way, he wasted no time. After bathing in the Saryu, he reached the king's court.
ramacharitamanas::1129.translation_literal: बहुबिधि (in many ways) / करत (doing) / मनोरथ (wishes, intentions) / जात (going) / लागि (for) / नहिं बार (no delay) / करि (having done) / मज्जन (bath) / सरऊ जल (Saryu water) / गए (went) / भूप दरबार (king's court)
ramacharitamanas::1129.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1129.essence: Thought becomes real only when it reaches the door.
ramacharitamanas::1129.simple_meaning: Visvamitra makes his way to the palace quickly, after bathing in the Saryu. The verse simply moves the story forward.
ramacharitamanas::1129.simple_insight: Sometimes a decisive step matters more than the long buildup before it.
ramacharitamanas::1129.detailed_meaning: Visvamitra has already decided that Ram must come to end the threat of the forest demons. After thinking through many possibilities, he does not linger; he bathes in the Saryu and goes straight to Dasharath's court.
ramacharitamanas::1129.modern_relevance: You finally stop rehearsing the conversation in your head, wash your face, and walk into the room. The real change begins when thought becomes movement.
ramacharitamanas::1129.insight: It shifts the mind from planning to arrival, showing that intention must become action.

ramacharitamanas::1130.verse_sanskrit: मुनि आगमन सुना जब राजा। मिलन गयउ लै बिप्र समाजा॥ करि दंडवत मुनिहि सनमानी। निज आसन बैठारेन्हि आनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1130.verse_hindi: राजा ने जब मुनि का आना सुना, तब वे ब्राह्मणों के समाज को साथ लेकर मिलने गए और दण्डवत् करके मुनि का सम्मान करते हुए उन्हें लाकर अपने आसन पर बैठाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1130.english_translation: When the king heard of the sage's arrival, he went to meet him with the company of brahmins. He bowed down, honored the sage, brought him in, and seated him on his own seat.
ramacharitamanas::1130.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / आगमन (arrival) / सुना (heard) / जब (when) / राजा (king) / मिलन (to meet) / गयउ (went) / लै (taking) / बिप्र (brahmin) / समाजा (company) / करि (doing) / दंडवत (prostration) / मुनिहि (to the sage) / सनमानी (honored) / निज (own) / आसन (seat) / बैठारेन्हि (seated) / आनी (bringing)
ramacharitamanas::1130.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1130.simple_meaning: The king hears that a sage has arrived, goes out with the brahmins, bows to him, honors him, and seats him on his own throne.
ramacharitamanas::1130.simple_insight: True respect shows itself in humble action, not status.
ramacharitamanas::1130.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, King Dasharath hears that the sage has arrived. He does not wait in pride; he goes out with the brahmins, bows fully, and offers his own seat. The scene shows royal humility before the sacred guest.
ramacharitamanas::1130.modern_relevance: You hear that a respected elder has come to visit. You stop what you are doing, walk out to greet them, and make room for them first. Honor is shown in how you receive people.
ramacharitamanas::1130.insight: It teaches you to meet wisdom with humility and visible respect.

ramacharitamanas::1131.verse_sanskrit: चरन पखारि कीन्हि अति पूजा। मो सम आजु धन्य नहिं दूजा॥ बिबिध भाँति भोजन करवावा। मुनिबर हृदयँ हरष अति पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1131.verse_hindi: चरणों को धोकर बहुत पूजा की और कहा- मेरे समान धन्य आज दूसरा कोई नहीं है। फिर अनेक प्रकार के भोजन करवाए, जिससे श्रेष्ठ मुनि ने अपने हृदय में बहुत ही हर्ष प्राप्त किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1131.english_translation: He washed the sage’s feet and offered great worship, saying, "No one is more blessed than I today." Then he served many kinds of food, and the best of sages felt great joy in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::1131.translation_literal: चरन (feet) / पखारि (washing) / कीन्हि (did) / अति (great) / पूजा (worship) । मो (I) / सम (like) / आजु (today) / धन्य (blessed) / नहिं (not) / दूजा (another) ॥ बिबिध (various) / भाँति (kinds) / भोजन (food) / करवावा (caused to be served) । मुनिबर (best of sages) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / हरष (joy) / अति (great) / पावा (received) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1131.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1131.essence: True honor is shown through humble service.
ramacharitamanas::1131.simple_meaning: The king honors the sage with foot-washing, worship, and a generous meal. The sage feels deep joy at the king’s respect.
ramacharitamanas::1131.simple_insight: Respect becomes real when it is shown in action, not just in words.
ramacharitamanas::1131.detailed_meaning: King Dasharath receives the visiting sage with full humility. He washes the sage’s feet, worships him deeply, and serves a lavish meal. This is the courtly devotion that sets the stage for the sage’s blessing and the arrival of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1131.modern_relevance: A guest arrives after a long journey, and you stop everything to care for them properly. No performance, no hurry — just real honor shown through service.
ramacharitamanas::1131.insight: It teaches that reverence must be embodied through concrete care and hospitality.

ramacharitamanas::1132.verse_sanskrit: पुनि चरननि मेले सुत चारी। राम देखि मुनि देह बिसारी॥ भए मगन देखत मुख सोभा। जनु चकोर पूरन ससि लोभा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1132.verse_hindi: फिर राजा ने चारों पुत्रों को मुनि के चरणों पर डाल दिया (उनसे प्रणाम कराया)। श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर मुनि अपनी देह की सुधि भूल गए। वे श्री रामजी के मुख की शोभा देखते ही ऐसे मग्न हो गए, मानो चकोर पूर्ण चन्द्रमा को देखकर लुभा गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1132.english_translation: Then the king had his four sons placed at the sage's feet. Seeing Ram, the sage forgot his body. He became so absorbed in Ram's beautiful face, like a chakor longing for the full moon.
ramacharitamanas::1132.translation_literal: पुनि (then again) / चरननि (at the feet) / मेले (placed) / सुत (sons) / चारी (four) / राम (Ram) / देखि (seeing) / मुनि (sage) / देह (body) / बिसारी (forgot) / भए (became) / मगन (absorbed) / देखत (seeing) / मुख (face) / सोभा (beauty) / जनु (as if) / चकोर (chakor bird) / पूरन (full) / ससि (moon) / लोभा (longing)
ramacharitamanas::1132.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1132.essence: Ram's beauty makes the seeker forget himself.
ramacharitamanas::1132.simple_meaning: The king brings his four sons before the sage. The sage sees Ram and becomes so absorbed in his beauty that he forgets his own body.
ramacharitamanas::1132.simple_insight: Deep reverence can make the self disappear for a moment, leaving only wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1132.detailed_meaning: King Dasharath has welcomed Vishvamitra with honor and hospitality. Now he brings his four sons forward. The sage sees Ram's face and loses all sense of his body, overwhelmed by devotion and delight.
ramacharitamanas::1132.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence instantly quiets the room. Your phone stays in your pocket, your thoughts stop racing, and for a moment attention becomes pure admiration.
ramacharitamanas::1132.insight: It shows how true beauty and reverence can pull the mind out of self-consciousness.

ramacharitamanas::1133.verse_sanskrit: तब मन हरषि बचन कह राऊ। मुनि अस कृपा न कीन्हिहु काऊ॥ केहि कारन आगमन तुम्हारा। कहहु सो करत न लावउँ बारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1133.verse_hindi: तब राजा ने मन में हर्षित होकर ये वचन कहे- हे मुनि! इस प्रकार कृपा तो आपने कभी नहीं की। आज किस कारण से आपका शुभागमन हुआ? कहिए, मैं उसे पूरा करने में देर नहीं लगाऊँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1133.english_translation: Then the king, delighted in his heart, said: "O sage, you have never shown such kindness to anyone. For what reason have you come? Tell me, and I will not delay doing it."
ramacharitamanas::1133.translation_literal: तब (then) / मन (mind) / हरषि (rejoicing) / बचन (words) / कह (spoke) / राऊ (the king) / मुनि (sage) / अस (such) / कृपा (kindness) / न (not) / कीन्हिहु (you have done) / काऊ (to anyone)॥ / केहि (what) / कारन (reason) / आगमन (arrival) / तुम्हारा (your) / कहहु (tell) / सो (that) / करत (doing) / न (not) / लावउँ (I delay) / बारा (time)॥
ramacharitamanas::1133.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1133.essence: True welcome offers help before the request is even spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1133.simple_meaning: King Dasharath welcomes the sage with joy and promises to do whatever he asks without delay.
ramacharitamanas::1133.simple_insight: A generous heart answers before fear or hesitation can rise.
ramacharitamanas::1133.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, King Dasharath has just honored the visiting sage Vishvamitra with great reverence. Still moved by the sage's presence, he asks why the sage has come and promises immediate help, not knowing the painful request that is about to follow.
ramacharitamanas::1133.modern_relevance: Someone you deeply respect asks for help, and your first response is not calculation. You listen fully, because trust moves faster than suspicion.
ramacharitamanas::1133.insight: It teaches readiness to serve before knowing the full demand.

ramacharitamanas::1134.verse_sanskrit: असुर समूह सतावहिं मोही। मैं जाचन आयउँ नृप तोही॥ अनुज समेत देहु रघुनाथा। निसिचर बध मैं होब सनाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1134.verse_hindi: (मुनि ने कहा-) हे राजन् ! राक्षसों के समूह मुझे बहुत सताते हैं, इसीलिए मैं तुमसे कुछ माँगने आया हूँ। छोटे भाई सहित श्री रघुनाथजी को मुझे दो। राक्षसों के मारे जाने पर मैं सनाथ (सुरक्षित) हो जाऊँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1134.english_translation: O king, the hosts of demons torment me. I have come asking you for a gift: give me Raghunath together with his younger brother. When the demons are slain, I will be safe.
ramacharitamanas::1134.translation_literal: असुर समूह (hosts of demons) / सतावहिं (torment) / मोही (me) / मैं (I) / जाचन (asking) / आयउँ (have come) / नृप (king) / तोही (to you) / अनुज (younger brother) / समेत (together with) / देहु (give) / रघुनाथा (Raghunatha) / निसिचर (demons/night-walkers) / बध (slaying) / मैं (I) / होब (will be) / सनाथा (protected/safe)
ramacharitamanas::1134.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1134.essence: True refuge may require giving up what you most want to keep.
ramacharitamanas::1134.simple_meaning: The sage says the demons trouble him and asks King Dasharath to give him Ram and Lakshman. He says their death will leave him safe.
ramacharitamanas::1134.simple_insight: Real help sometimes means surrendering what you love most to protect a greater good.
ramacharitamanas::1134.detailed_meaning: After seeing the king’s four sons, the sage speaks plainly: demons are harassing him, and only Ram and Lakshman can end that fear. This request begins the chain that leads to Ram’s exile and the destruction of evil.
ramacharitamanas::1134.modern_relevance: A parent is asked to let a gifted child leave home for something hard and dangerous. The instinct is to hold on, but the larger duty is to release them for the work only they can do.
ramacharitamanas::1134.insight: It shifts attention from possession to protection: what matters is not keeping the beloved close, but letting dharma move through them.

ramacharitamanas::1135.verse_sanskrit: देहु भूप मन हरषित तजहु मोह अग्यान। धर्म सुजस प्रभु तुम्ह कौं इन्ह कहँ अति कल्यान ॥
ramacharitamanas::1135.verse_hindi: हे राजन् ! प्रसन्न मन से इनको दो, मोह और अज्ञान को छोड़ दो। हे स्वामी! इससे तुमको धर्म और सुयश की प्राप्ति होगी और इनका परम कल्याण होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1135.english_translation: O king, give them with a joyful mind; abandon delusion and ignorance. O lord, this will bring you dharma and good fame, and bring great welfare to them.
ramacharitamanas::1135.translation_literal: देहु (give) / भूप (king) / मन हरषित (with a joyful mind) / तजहु (abandon) / मोह (delusion) / अग्यान (ignorance) / धर्म (righteous duty) / सुजस (good fame) / प्रभु (lord) / तुम्ह (to you) / कौं (to) / इन्ह कहँ (for these) / अति कल्यान (great welfare)
ramacharitamanas::1135.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1135.essence: Right giving requires dropping attachment first.
ramacharitamanas::1135.simple_meaning: The request is simple: give the boys willingly, drop confusion, and choose what is right. That choice will honour the king and help everyone involved.
ramacharitamanas::1135.simple_insight: Doing the hard right thing can protect both dignity and peace.
ramacharitamanas::1135.detailed_meaning: The sage has asked King Dasharath for Rama and Lakshman. Before the king can answer, the request is framed as a moral test: give them gladly, release attachment, and trust that dharma will be served.
ramacharitamanas::1135.modern_relevance: You are asked to let go of something you love because it is the right thing to do. Every instinct resists, but a clear mind knows that clinging can become its own kind of blindness.
ramacharitamanas::1135.insight: It shifts the mind from possessiveness to righteous release.

ramacharitamanas::1136.verse_sanskrit: सुनि राजा अति अप्रिय बानी। हृदय कंप मुख दुति कुमुलानी॥ चौथेंपन पायउँ सुत चारी। बिप्र बचन नहिं कहेहु बिचारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1136.verse_hindi: इस अत्यन्त अप्रिय वाणी को सुनकर राजा का हृदय काँप उठा और उनके मुख की कांति फीकी पड़ गई। (उन्होंने कहा-) हे ब्राह्मण! मैंने चौथेपन में चार पुत्र पाए हैं, आपने विचार कर बात नहीं कही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1136.english_translation: Hearing this very unpleasant speech, the king's heart trembled and the color left his face. He said, "O Brahmin, I have gained four sons only in old age; you have spoken without thinking."
ramacharitamanas::1136.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / राजा (the king) / अति (very) / अप्रिय (unpleasant) / बानी (speech) / हृदय (heart) / कंप (trembled) / मुख (face) / दुति (brightness) / कुमुलानी (faded) / चौथेंपन (old age) / पायउँ (I obtained) / सुत (sons) / चारी (four) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / बचन (words) / नहिं (not) / कहेहु (you spoke) / बिचारी (after thinking)
ramacharitamanas::1136.speaker: King Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::1136.essence: Grief makes the heart protest before it can understand.
ramacharitamanas::1136.simple_meaning: Dasharath is shaken by the sage's demand. He says the request is cruel because he has only just received four sons in old age.
ramacharitamanas::1136.simple_insight: Sudden loss hits hardest when it threatens what you waited your whole life to receive.
ramacharitamanas::1136.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath hears the sage's demand for Ram and Lakshman and is stunned. His body reacts before his mind can recover: his heart trembles, his face pales, and he protests that the request ignores the joy of his late fatherhood.
ramacharitamanas::1136.modern_relevance: You finally hear the words you were dreading after years of hoping for good news. Your chest tightens, and all you can say is, "Please think again."
ramacharitamanas::1136.insight: It shows how attachment makes even a generous person feel wounded before understanding the larger demand.

ramacharitamanas::1137.verse_sanskrit: मागहु भूमि धेनु धन कोसा। सर्बस देउँ आजु सहरोसा॥ देह प्रान तें प्रिय कछु नाहीं। सोउ मुनि देउँ निमिष एक माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1137.verse_hindi: हे मुनि! आप पृथ्वी, गो, धन और खजाना माँग लीजिए, मैं आज बड़े हर्ष के साथ अपना सर्वस्व दे दूँगा। देह और प्राण से अधिक प्यारा कुछ भी नहीं होता, मैं उसे भी एक पल में दे दूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1137.english_translation: Ask for land, cows, wealth, and treasure. Today I will give everything gladly. Nothing is dearer than body and life; I would give even that in a moment.
ramacharitamanas::1137.translation_literal: मागहु (ask for) / भूमि (land) / धेनु (cows) / धन (wealth) / कोसा (treasure) / सर्बस (everything) / देउँ (I give) / आजु (today) / सहरोसा (with joy)॥ / देह (body) / प्रान (life-breath) / तें (than) / प्रिय (dear) / कछु (anything) / नाहीं (not) / सोउ (that too) / मुनि (sage) / देउँ (I give) / निमिष (moment) / एक (one) / माहीं (within) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1137.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::1137.essence: Generosity fails when attachment reaches the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1137.simple_meaning: Dasharath offers everything he owns, even his own life, to honor the sage's request.
ramacharitamanas::1137.simple_insight: Sometimes the heart wants to give everything, even when the cost is unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::1137.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, King Dasharath is shaken by the sage's demand. He tries to buy time with land, cattle, wealth, and treasure, then goes further and offers even his own life. But this generosity cannot solve the deeper crisis now unfolding.
ramacharitamanas::1137.modern_relevance: You say, “Take whatever I have, just don’t ask for the one thing I cannot bear to lose.” That is the sound of love meeting a limit.
ramacharitamanas::1137.insight: It reveals the first crack in Dasharath’s resolve: he can offer possessions, but not what his heart clings to.

ramacharitamanas::1138.verse_sanskrit: सब सुत प्रिय मोहि प्रान की नाईं। राम देत नहिं बनइ गोसाईं॥ कहँ निसिचर अति घोर कठोरा। कहँ सुंदर सुत परम किसोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1138.verse_hindi: सभी पुत्र मुझे प्राणों के समान प्यारे हैं, उनमें भी हे प्रभो! राम को तो (किसी प्रकार भी) देते नहीं बनता। कहाँ अत्यन्त डरावने और क्रूर राक्षस और कहाँ परम किशोर अवस्था के (बिलकुल सुकुमार) मेरे सुंदर पुत्र! ॥
ramacharitamanas::1138.english_translation: All my sons are dear to me like my very life, but I cannot give Ram away, O Lord. How can I compare fierce, dreadful demons with my beautiful, tender young son?
ramacharitamanas::1138.translation_literal: सब (all) / सुत (sons) / प्रिय (dear) / मोहि (to me) / प्रान की नाईं (like life itself) / राम (Ram) / देत (giving) / नहिं बनइ (is not possible) / गोसाईं (O Lord) / कहँ (where) / निसिचर (demons) / अति घोर (very dreadful) / कठोरा (cruel) / कहँ (where) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुत (son) / परम (extremely) / किसोरा (young)
ramacharitamanas::1138.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::1138.essence: A father’s love trembles when duty asks for his child.
ramacharitamanas::1138.simple_meaning: Dasharath says all his sons are precious, but he cannot bear to give Ram away. Ram is gentle and beautiful, while the demons sound terrifying and cruel.
ramacharitamanas::1138.simple_insight: Love makes sacrifice feel unbearable, even when duty demands it.
ramacharitamanas::1138.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Vishwamitra has asked for Ram and Lakshman to protect his sacrifice. Dasharath has already offered wealth, land, and even his life, but this request cuts deeper. He speaks from a father's heart, unable to imagine handing over his tender son to danger.
ramacharitamanas::1138.modern_relevance: A parent watches a child pack for a risky move, a harsh job, or a dangerous city. The mind knows courage matters; the heart still resists letting go.
ramacharitamanas::1138.insight: It reveals the clash between parental attachment and the demands of dharma.

ramacharitamanas::1139.verse_sanskrit: सुनि नृप गिरा प्रेम रस सानी। हृदयँ हरष माना मुनि ग्यानी॥ तब बसिष्ट बहुबिधि समुझावा। नृप संदेह नास कहँ पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1139.verse_hindi: प्रेम रस में सनी हुई राजा की वाणी सुनकर ज्ञानी मुनि विश्वामित्रजी ने हृदय में बड़ा हर्ष माना। तब वशिष्ठजी ने राजा को बहुत प्रकार से समझाया, जिससे राजा का संदेह नाश को प्राप्त हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1139.english_translation: Hearing the king's words soaked in the nectar of love, the wise sage felt great joy in his heart. Then Vasishtha explained many things to the king, and the king's doubt was removed.
ramacharitamanas::1139.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / नृप (king's) / गिरा (words) / प्रेम रस सानी (soaked in love's nectar) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / हरष (joy) / माना (felt) / मुनि (sage) / ग्यानी (wise) / तब (then) / बसिष्ट (Vasishtha) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / समुझावा (explained) / नृप (king's) / संदेह (doubt) / नास (destruction) / कहँ (for) / पावा (was obtained)
ramacharitamanas::1139.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1139.essence: Love-filled speech opens the heart to understanding.
ramacharitamanas::1139.simple_meaning: The king speaks with loving sincerity, and the sage feels joy. Then Vasishtha explains things clearly, and the king's doubt disappears.
ramacharitamanas::1139.simple_insight: Sincere love softens resistance, and clear guidance can then reach the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1139.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, King Dasharath has just offered everything except Ram. His voice is full of love and pain, and the sage feels that sincerity. Vasishtha then patiently explains, until the king's confusion begins to clear.
ramacharitamanas::1139.modern_relevance: You finally tell the truth in a voice that shakes a little. The other person stops arguing and starts listening. Honest feeling opens the door that force never could.
ramacharitamanas::1139.insight: It shows that heartfelt honesty can make guidance effective and dissolve confusion.

ramacharitamanas::1140.verse_sanskrit: अति आदर दोउ तनय बोलाए। हृदयँ लाइ बहु भाँति सिखाए॥ मेरे प्रान नाथ सुत दोऊ। तुम्ह मुनि पिता आन नहिं कोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1140.verse_hindi: राजा ने बड़े ही आदर से दोनों पुत्रों को बुलाया और हृदय से लगाकर बहुत प्रकार से उन्हें शिक्षा दी। (फिर कहा-) हे नाथ! ये दोनों पुत्र मेरे प्राण हैं। हे मुनि! (अब) आप ही इनके पिता हैं, दूसरा कोई नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1140.english_translation: With great respect, the king called both sons and embraced them, instructing them in many ways. He said, "These two sons are my very life, O sage; now you are their father, and no one else."
ramacharitamanas::1140.translation_literal: अति आदर (with great respect) / दोउ (both) / तनय (sons) / बोलाए (called) / हृदयँ लाइ (embracing to the heart) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / सिखाए (instructed) / मेरे (my) / प्रान नाथ (life-lord) / सुत (sons) / दोऊ (both) / तुम्ह (you) / मुनि (sage) / पिता (father) / आन (other) / नहिं (not) / कोऊ (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::1140.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1140.essence: True care can mean handing your most beloved over with trust.
ramacharitamanas::1140.simple_meaning: Dasharath lovingly brings both sons close, teaches them carefully, and entrusts them to Vishvamitra as their true guide and father for the journey ahead.
ramacharitamanas::1140.simple_insight: Love can release what it cannot keep, and that release can still be tender.
ramacharitamanas::1140.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has accepted Vishvamitra's request, though it breaks his heart. Before the boys leave, he gathers Ram and Lakshman close, instructs them with affection, and formally places them under the sage's care.
ramacharitamanas::1140.modern_relevance: A parent walks a child to the first day at a new school, smiling through the ache. Love is not always holding on; sometimes it is handing over with trust.
ramacharitamanas::1140.insight: It teaches you to bless the next step even when it hurts to let go.

ramacharitamanas::1141.verse_sanskrit: सौंपे भूप रिषिहि सुत बहुबिधि देइ असीस। जननी भवन गए प्रभु चले नाइ पद सीस॥208 क ॥
ramacharitamanas::1141.verse_hindi: राजा ने बहुत प्रकार से आशीर्वाद देकर पुत्रों को ऋषि के हवाले कर दिया। फिर प्रभु माता के महल में गए और उनके चरणों में सिर नवाकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1141.english_translation: The king handed the sons over to the sage with many blessings. Then the Lord went to his mother's chamber, bowed his head at her feet, and departed.
ramacharitamanas::1141.translation_literal: सौंपे (handed over) / भूप (the king) / रिषिहि (to the sage) / सुत (sons) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / देइ (giving) / असीस (blessings) / जननी (mother) / भवन (chamber/house) / गए (went) / प्रभु (the Lord) / चले (departed) / नाइ (bowing) / पद (feet) / सीस (head)
ramacharitamanas::1141.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1141.essence: Duty can be tender, not cold.
ramacharitamanas::1141.simple_meaning: Dasharath gives Ram and Lakshman to Vishwamitra with blessings. Ram then bows to Kaushalya and leaves.
ramacharitamanas::1141.simple_insight: Even the hardest departure can be made sacred by respect, blessing, and obedience.
ramacharitamanas::1141.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has agreed to send his sons with Vishwamitra. After blessing them, he entrusts them to the sage. Ram then goes to his mother's chamber, bows at her feet, and leaves. The moment marks the beginning of a duty that will carry him away from home.
ramacharitamanas::1141.modern_relevance: You pack your child’s bag for the first day away from home, then watch them walk out the door. Love does not stop the leaving; it blesses it.
ramacharitamanas::1141.insight: It teaches you to honour duty without bitterness, even when it separates you from what you love.

ramacharitamanas::1142.verse_sanskrit: पुरुष सिंह दोउ बीर हरषि चले मुनि भय हरन। कृपासिंधु मतिधीर अखिल बिस्व कारन करन ॥
ramacharitamanas::1142.verse_hindi: पुरुषों में सिंह रूप दोनों भाई (राम-लक्ष्मण) मुनि का भय हरने के लिए प्रसन्न होकर चले। वे कृपा के समुद्र, धीर बुद्धि और सम्पूर्ण विश्व के कारण के भी कारण हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1142.english_translation: The two lion-like brothers went happily to remove the sage's fear. They are oceans of grace, steady in mind, and the cause behind the cause of the entire universe.
ramacharitamanas::1142.translation_literal: पुरुष सिंह (lion among men) / दोउ (both) / बीर (heroes) / हरषि (joyfully) / चले (went) / मुनि (sage) / भय (fear) / हरन (removing) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of grace) / मतिधीर (steady-minded) / अखिल (entire) / बिस्व (universe) / कारन (cause) / करन (cause of)
ramacharitamanas::1142.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1142.essence: Real greatness walks in gladly to remove another's fear.
ramacharitamanas::1142.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman go joyfully to protect the sage and remove his fear. The verse also praises Ram as compassionate, steady, and the source behind all existence.
ramacharitamanas::1142.simple_insight: Strength becomes holy when it protects the fearful.
ramacharitamanas::1142.detailed_meaning: After Dasharath sends Ram and Lakshman away with the sage, the two brothers leave happily. The scene shifts from royal farewell to sacred protection: the boys are not just walking into the forest, but into their first great act of service.
ramacharitamanas::1142.modern_relevance: You walk into a difficult room with someone who feels unsafe. Your calm changes the atmosphere before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1142.insight: It links courage with protection and reminds the reader that true power steadies others, not intimidates them.

ramacharitamanas::1143.verse_sanskrit: अरुन नयन उर बाहु बिसाला। नील जलज तनु स्याम तमाला॥ कटि पट पीत कसें बर भाथा। रुचिर चाप सायक दुहुँ हाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1143.verse_hindi: भगवान के लाल नेत्र हैं, चौड़ी छाती और विशाल भुजाएँ हैं, नील कमल और तमाल के वृक्ष की तरह श्याम शरीर है, कमर में पीताम्बर (पहने) और सुंदर तरकस कसे हुए हैं। दोनों हाथों में (क्रमशः) सुंदर धनुष और बाण हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1143.english_translation: His eyes are red, his chest broad, his arms vast. His body is dark like a blue lotus and tamal tree. A yellow garment is tied at his waist, a beautiful quiver is strapped on, and a lovely bow and arrows are in both hands.
ramacharitamanas::1143.translation_literal: अरुन (red) / नयन (eyes) / उर (chest) / बाहु (arms) / बिसाला (vast) / नील (blue) / जलज (lotus) / तनु (body) / स्याम (dark) / तमाला (tamal tree) / कटि (waist) / पट (cloth) / पीत (yellow) / कसें (fastened) / बर (beautiful) / भाथा (quiver) / रुचिर (lovely) / चाप (bow) / सायक (arrows) / दुहुँ (both) / हाथा (hands)
ramacharitamanas::1143.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1143.essence: Beauty and strength meet in one armed presence.
ramacharitamanas::1143.simple_meaning: Ram is described as beautifully radiant, dark-complexioned, and fully armed, with a bow and arrows in his hands.
ramacharitamanas::1143.simple_insight: The divine appears not as abstraction, but as a vivid, protective presence you can picture and trust.
ramacharitamanas::1143.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra has brought Ram and Lakshman into the forest, and the poet pauses to paint Ram's form before the next turn of the story. The verse is a visual portrait: beauty, strength, and readiness gathered into one figure.
ramacharitamanas::1143.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone entering a room and everything changes — calm, strength, and readiness all arrive together. That kind of presence needs no introduction.
ramacharitamanas::1143.insight: It shifts attention from abstract reverence to embodied presence: the divine is seen as beautiful, strong, and ready to act.

ramacharitamanas::1144.verse_sanskrit: स्याम गौर सुंदर दोउ भाई। बिस्वामित्र महानिधि पाई॥ प्रभु ब्रह्मन्यदेव मैं जाना। मोहि निति पिता तजेउ भगवाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1144.verse_hindi: श्याम और गौर वर्ण के दोनों भाई परम सुंदर हैं। विश्वामित्रजी को महान निधि प्राप्त हो गई। (वे सोचने लगे-) मैं जान गया कि प्रभु ब्रह्मण्यदेव (ब्राह्मणों के भक्त) हैं। मेरे लिए भगवान ने अपने पिता को भी छोड़ दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1144.english_translation: Both brothers, dark and fair, are beautifully radiant. Vishwamitra has found a great treasure. He thought, "I know the Lord is devoted to the righteous and the learned; for my sake, the Blessed One even left his father."
ramacharitamanas::1144.translation_literal: स्याम (dark) / गौर (fair) / सुंदर (beautiful) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / बिस्वामित्र (Vishwamitra) / महानिधि (great treasure) / पाई (found) / प्रभु (Lord) / ब्रह्मन्यदेव (devoted to the righteous and learned) / मैं (I) / जाना (knew) / मोहि (for me) / निति (always) / पिता (father) / तजेउ (left) / भगवाना (the Blessed One)
ramacharitamanas::1144.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1144.essence: True greatness shows itself in the willingness to leave comfort for duty.
ramacharitamanas::1144.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra sees Ram and Lakshman as a priceless blessing. He realises Ram protects those devoted to dharma and has already chosen to leave his father for this higher calling.
ramacharitamanas::1144.simple_insight: Grace often appears as a person who is willing to leave comfort for what is right.
ramacharitamanas::1144.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra is walking with Ram and Lakshman after meeting them in the forest. Looking at the two radiant brothers, he feels he has found a treasure. In that moment he understands Ram's greatness: the prince has already given up his father to uphold a higher duty.
ramacharitamanas::1144.modern_relevance: You watch someone step away from family expectations to do what they know is right. The choice looks costly from outside, but it reveals a steadier kind of greatness.
ramacharitamanas::1144.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to the moral courage behind a person's choices.

ramacharitamanas::1145.verse_sanskrit: चले जात मुनि दीन्हि देखाई। सुनि ताड़का क्रोध करि धाई॥ एकहिं बान प्रान हरि लीन्हा। दीन जानि तेहि निज पद दीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1145.verse_hindi: मार्ग में चले जाते हुए मुनि ने ताड़का को दिखलाया। शब्द सुनते ही वह क्रोध करके दौड़ी। श्री रामजी ने एक ही बाण से उसके प्राण हर लिए और दीन जानकर उसको निजपद (अपना दिव्य स्वरूप) दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1145.english_translation: Walking along, the sage showed her. Hearing this, Tadka rushed in anger. Ram took her life with a single arrow and, seeing her as helpless, granted her his own divine state.
ramacharitamanas::1145.translation_literal: चले (went) / जात (going) / मुनि (sage) / दीन्हि (showed) / देखाई (having shown) / सुनि (hearing) / ताड़का (Tadaka) / क्रोध (anger) / करि (doing) / धाई (rushed) / एकहिं (only one) / बान (arrow) / प्रान (life-breath) / हरि (taking away) / लीन्हा (took) / दीन (helpless) / जानि (knowing) / तेहि (her) / निज (own) / पद (state/feet) / दीन्हा (gave)
ramacharitamanas::1145.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1145.essence: Power becomes righteous when it protects the helpless.
ramacharitamanas::1145.simple_meaning: Ram ends Tadka's threat with one arrow, then shows mercy by giving her release.
ramacharitamanas::1145.simple_insight: Strength without mercy is incomplete; true power knows when to end harm and when to spare.
ramacharitamanas::1145.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra leads Ram and Lakshman through the forest and points out Tadka, whose fury blocks the sages' path. Ram ends the danger instantly, then responds to her helplessness with compassion. The scene shows divine action joined to mercy.
ramacharitamanas::1145.modern_relevance: A bully corners the weakest person in the room, and everyone waits. Someone steps in firmly, stops the harm, and does not keep hatred after the danger ends.
ramacharitamanas::1145.insight: It teaches you to meet threat decisively, without losing compassion once the threat is ended.

ramacharitamanas::1146.verse_sanskrit: तब रिषि निज नाथहि जियँ चीन्ही। बिद्यानिधि कहुँ बिद्या दीन्ही॥ जाते लाग न छुधा पिपासा। अतुलित बल तनु तेज प्रकासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1146.verse_hindi: तब ऋषि विश्वामित्र ने प्रभु को मन में विद्या का भंडार समझते हुए भी (लीला को पूर्ण करने के लिए) ऐसी विद्या दी, जिससे भूख-प्यास न लगे और शरीर में अतुलित बल और तेज का प्रकाश हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1146.english_translation: Then the sage recognized his Lord in his heart and gave the treasure of knowledge the knowledge that prevents hunger and thirst and reveals incomparable strength and radiance in the body.
ramacharitamanas::1146.translation_literal: तब (then) / रिषि (sage) / निज नाथहि (his own lord) / जियँ (in the heart) / चीन्ही (recognized) / बिद्यानिधि (treasure of knowledge) / कहुँ (for) / बिद्या (knowledge) / दीन्ही (gave) / जाते (by which) / लाग (attaches) / न (not) / छुधा (hunger) / पिपासा (thirst) / अतुलित (incomparable) / बल (strength) / तनु (body) / तेज (radiance) / प्रकासा (shines)
ramacharitamanas::1146.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1146.essence: True recognition gives the right knowledge at the right moment.
ramacharitamanas::1146.simple_meaning: विश्वामित्र ने मन में राम को अपना प्रभु पहचानकर उन्हें ऐसी विद्या दी, जिससे भूख-प्यास न लगे और शरीर में असाधारण बल और तेज प्रकट हो।
ramacharitamanas::1146.simple_insight: Recognition changes everything: once the teacher sees Ram, he gives not just instruction but protection and power.
ramacharitamanas::1146.detailed_meaning: विश्वामित्र ताड़का-वध के बाद राम की असली महिमा समझ चुके हैं। अब वे अपने आश्रम-जीवन के लिए राम को ऐसी विद्या देते हैं जो भूख-प्यास से बचाए और उनके शरीर में अपार बल-तेज जगाए।
ramacharitamanas::1146.modern_relevance: A mentor sees your potential before you do and gives you exactly what you need to keep going through the hard stretch.
ramacharitamanas::1146.insight: It shifts the reader from thinking of knowledge as information to seeing it as support that sustains action.

ramacharitamanas::1147.verse_sanskrit: आयुध सर्ब समर्पि कै प्रभु निज आश्रम आनि। कंद मूल फल भोजन दीन्ह भगति हित जानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1147.verse_hindi: सब अस्त्र-शस्त्र समर्पण करके मुनि प्रभु श्री रामजी को अपने आश्रम में ले आए और उन्हें परम हितू जानकर भक्तिपूर्वक कंद, मूल और फल का भोजन कराया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1147.english_translation: After surrendering all weapons, the Lord brought him to his own hermitage and, knowing him to be devoted, gave him roots, fruits, and forest food.
ramacharitamanas::1147.translation_literal: आयुध (weapons) / सर्ब (all) / समर्पि कै (having offered up) / प्रभु (the Lord) / निज (own) / आश्रम (hermitage) / आनि (bringing) / कंद (roots) / मूल (tubers/roots) / फल (fruits) / भोजन (food) / दीन्ह (gave) / भगति (devotion) / हित (for the good) / जानि (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::1147.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1147.essence: Devotion turns simple hospitality into an offering.
ramacharitamanas::1147.simple_meaning: The sage brings Ram to his hermitage, offers food, and receives him with devotion, seeing him as supremely worthy.
ramacharitamanas::1147.simple_insight: Hospitality becomes worship when it is offered with devotion, not obligation.
ramacharitamanas::1147.detailed_meaning: After Ram has freed the way by killing Tadka, Vishwamitra brings him to the hermitage. The sage lays down all weapons, welcomes Ram inside, and serves simple forest food with reverence. This is the quiet bond of trust before the next task begins.
ramacharitamanas::1147.modern_relevance: A host clears the table, sets aside the phone, and serves a tired guest without making a show of it. Care becomes sacred in that small, unforced gesture.
ramacharitamanas::1147.insight: It shifts attention from the food itself to the spirit in which service is given.

ramacharitamanas::1148.verse_sanskrit: प्रात कहा मुनि सन रघुराई। निर्भय जग्य करहु तुम्ह जाई॥ होम करन लागे मुनि झारी। आपु रहे मख कीं रखवारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1148.verse_hindi: सबेरे श्री रघुनाथजी ने मुनि से कहा- आप जाकर निडर होकर यज्ञ कीजिए। यह सुनकर सब मुनि हवन करने लगे। आप (श्री रामजी) यज्ञ की रखवाली पर रहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1148.english_translation: In the morning, Raghurai said to the sage, “Go and perform the sacrifice without fear.” The sage began the rite, while Ram himself stood guard over the sacrifice.
ramacharitamanas::1148.translation_literal: प्रात (in the morning) / कहा (said) / मुनि (sage) / सन (to) / रघुराई (Raghurai) / निर्भय (fearlessly) / जग्य (sacrifice) / करहु (do) / तुम्ह (you) / जाई (go) / होम (ritual fire-offering) / करन (to do) / लागे (began) / मुनि (sage) / झारी (sprinkled/began) / आपु (himself) / रहे (remained) / मख (sacrifice) / कीं (of) / रखवारी (guarding)
ramacharitamanas::1148.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1148.essence: Protection becomes real when Ram stands beside the work.
ramacharitamanas::1148.simple_meaning: Ram tells the sage to perform the sacrifice without fear, then stands guard while the ritual begins.
ramacharitamanas::1148.simple_insight: Real protection is not talk. It is staying present so the work can be done safely.
ramacharitamanas::1148.detailed_meaning: In Vishwamitra’s forest sacrifice, Ram has already agreed to protect the sages. At dawn, he tells the sage to proceed without fear. The ritual begins, and Ram himself guards the sacrifice, making safety real through action.
ramacharitamanas::1148.modern_relevance: You finally start the presentation after weeks of tension, and the one person you trusted stays beside you while you speak. Fear drops when support becomes visible.
ramacharitamanas::1148.insight: It teaches that duty is not only promise but presence: protect the task by standing with it.

ramacharitamanas::1149.verse_sanskrit: सुनि मारीच निसाचर क्रोही। लै सहाय धावा मुनिद्रोही॥ बिनु फर बान राम तेहि मारा। सत जोजन गा सागर पारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1149.verse_hindi: यह समाचार सुनकर मुनियों का शत्रु कोरथी राक्षस मारीच अपने सहायकों को लेकर दौड़ा। श्री रामजी ने बिना फल वाला बाण उसको मारा, जिससे वह सौ योजन के विस्तार वाले समुद्र के पार जा गिरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1149.english_translation: Hearing this, Maricha, the enemy of sages, rushed forward with his allies. Ram struck him with an arrow that bore no fruit, and he was hurled across the ocean of a hundred yojanas.
ramacharitamanas::1149.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / मारीच (Maricha) / निसाचर (night-dweller, demon) / क्रोही (angry) / लै (taking) / सहाय (helpers) / धावा (rushed) / मुनिद्रोही (enemy of sages)॥ / बिनु (without) / फर (fruit) / बान (arrow) / राम (Ram) / तेहि (him) / मारा (struck) / सत (hundred) / जोजन (yojanas) / गा (went) / सागर (ocean) / पारा (across)॥
ramacharitamanas::1149.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1149.essence: One clear strike can silence a whole assault.
ramacharitamanas::1149.simple_meaning: Maricha, angry and backed by helpers, attacked the sages. Ram answered with one arrow and sent him flying far across the ocean.
ramacharitamanas::1149.simple_insight: Evil rushes in with force; a single steady response can end the threat.
ramacharitamanas::1149.detailed_meaning: In Vishvamitra's sacrifice, the forest danger finally arrives. Maricha, the sage-hating demon, charges in with reinforcements. Ram meets him with one decisive arrow, driving him far beyond the sea so the ritual can continue.
ramacharitamanas::1149.modern_relevance: A chaotic message thread explodes with blame and panic, but one calm reply cuts through the noise. Not every attack deserves a long reaction.
ramacharitamanas::1149.insight: It shows force used without hesitation, so protection comes before drama.

ramacharitamanas::1150.verse_sanskrit: पावक सर सुबाहु पुनि मारा। अनुज निसाचर कटकु सँघारा॥ मारि असुर द्विज निर्भयकारी। अस्तुति करहिं देव मुनि झारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1150.verse_hindi: फिर सुबाहु को अग्निबाण मारा। इधर छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी ने राक्षसों की सेना का संहार कर डाला। इस प्रकार श्री रामजी ने राक्षसों को मारकर ब्राह्मणों को निर्भय कर दिया। तब सारे देवता और मुनि स्तुति करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1150.english_translation: Then Ram struck Subahu with a fire-arrow. Lakshman destroyed the army of demons. By killing the demons, Ram made the priests fearless, and the gods and sages began to praise him.
ramacharitamanas::1150.translation_literal: पावक (fire) / सर (arrow) / सुबाहु (Subahu) / पुनि (again) / मारा (struck) / अनुज (younger brother) / निसाचर (night-dwelling demon) / कटकु (army) / सँघारा (destroyed) / मारि (having killed) / असुर (demon) / द्विज (twice-born priest) / निर्भयकारी (making fearless) / अस्तुति (praise) / करहिं (they do) / देव (gods) / मुनि (sages) / झारी (in a group)
ramacharitamanas::1150.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1150.essence: True protection ends fear, and fearless people naturally praise what saved them.
ramacharitamanas::1150.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman defeat the demons, and the priests are left safe. The gods and sages respond with praise.
ramacharitamanas::1150.simple_insight: Protection is part of righteousness. When fear is removed, gratitude naturally follows.
ramacharitamanas::1150.detailed_meaning: At Vishvamitra’s sacrifice, Ram has already begun clearing the field of danger. Subahu falls, Lakshman cuts down the demon army, and the priests can finally continue without fear. The scene closes with the gods and sages praising Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1150.modern_relevance: A room finally goes quiet after one person stands up and stops the chaos. Everyone else can breathe again, and the relief itself feels like praise.
ramacharitamanas::1150.insight: It shifts attention from heroic force to the peace that force makes possible.

ramacharitamanas::1151.verse_sanskrit: तहँ पुनि कछुक दिवस रघुराया। रहे कीन्हि बिप्रन्ह पर दाया॥ भगति हेतु बहुत कथा पुराना। कहे बिप्र जद्यपि प्रभु जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1151.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी ने वहाँ कुछ दिन और रहकर ब्राह्मणों पर दया की। भक्ति के कारण ब्राह्मणों ने उन्हें पुराणों की बहुत सी कथाएँ कहीं, यद्यपि प्रभु सब जानते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1151.english_translation: Raghunath stayed there for some more days and showed kindness to the Brahmins. Out of devotion, the Brahmins told many ancient stories, even though the Lord already knew them.
ramacharitamanas::1151.translation_literal: तहँ (there) / पुनि (again) / कछुक (some) / दिवस (days) / रघुराया (Raghunath, the lord) / रहे (remained) / कीन्हि (showed) / बिप्रन्ह (to the Brahmins) / पर (upon) / दाया (compassion) ॥ भगति (devotion) / हेतु (for the sake of) / बहुत (many) / कथा (stories) / पुराना (ancient) / कहे (told) / बिप्र (the Brahmins) / जद्यपि (although) / प्रभु (the Lord) / जाना (knew) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1151.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1151.essence: Love turns familiar stories into sacred listening.
ramacharitamanas::1151.simple_meaning: Ram stayed a little longer, treated the Brahmins kindly, and listened as they shared old stories out of devotion, even though he already knew them.
ramacharitamanas::1151.simple_insight: Real reverence does not need to impress. It simply offers what is already known with love.
ramacharitamanas::1151.detailed_meaning: After the demons are slain, Ram remains with the Brahmins in the forest. He treats them kindly, and they respond by telling ancient stories with devotion. The moment shows how sacred attention flows both ways: Ram gives grace, and the wise answer with loving remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::1151.modern_relevance: A guest sits in your kitchen and listens to your parents repeat stories you have heard a hundred times. No one is bored. That is what love does to ordinary conversation.
ramacharitamanas::1151.insight: It shifts attention from information to reverent presence, where hearing itself becomes an act of devotion.

ramacharitamanas::1152.verse_sanskrit: तब मुनि सादर कहा बुझाई। चरित एक प्रभु देखिअ जाई॥ धनुषजग्य सुनि रघुकुल नाथा। हरषि चले मुनिबर के साथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1152.verse_hindi: तदन्तर मुनि ने आदरपूर्वक समझाकर कहा- हे प्रभो! चलकर एक चरित्र देखिए। रघुकुल के स्वामी श्री रामचन्द्रजी धनुषयज्ञ (की बात) सुनकर मुनिश्रेष्ठ विश्वामित्रजी के साथ प्रसन्न होकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1152.english_translation: Then the sage respectfully explained and said, "Come and see a wondrous event." Hearing of the bow sacrifice, the Lord of Raghu joyfully went with the great sage.
ramacharitamanas::1152.translation_literal: तब (then) / मुनि (sage) / सादर (respectfully) / कहा (said) / बुझाई (explaining) / चरित (event, deed) / एक (one) / प्रभु (Lord) / देखिअ (let [it] be seen) / जाई (go) ॥ / धनुषजग्य (bow-sacrifice) / सुनि (hearing) / रघुकुल नाथा (Lord of the Raghu clan) / हरषि (rejoicing) / चले (went) / मुनिबर (great sage) / के साथा (with) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1152.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1152.essence: The worthy invitation is answered with joyful readiness.
ramacharitamanas::1152.simple_meaning: Viswamitra invites Ram to witness the bow sacrifice. Ram hears the news and goes joyfully with him.
ramacharitamanas::1152.simple_insight: Joy grows when you move toward what is worthy.
ramacharitamanas::1152.detailed_meaning: Viswamitra speaks to young Ram with respect and urgency, inviting him to see the bow sacrifice in Mithila. Ram, hearing of it, goes gladly with the sage. The verse moves the story from forest protection to the larger destiny that will lead to Sita's swayamvar.
ramacharitamanas::1152.modern_relevance: A mentor says, "Come with me, you need to see this," and you go without hesitation. Some moments are not chores; they are doorways into a larger life.
ramacharitamanas::1152.insight: It shifts the mind from passive listening to willing participation in dharma's unfolding.

ramacharitamanas::1153.verse_sanskrit: आश्रम एक दीख मग माहीं। खग मृग जीव जंतु तहँ नाहीं॥ पूछा मुनिहि सिला प्रभु देखी। सकल कथा मुनि कहा बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1153.verse_hindi: मार्ग में एक आश्रम दिखाई पड़ा। वहाँ पशु-पक्षी, को भी जीव-जन्तु नहीं था। पत्थर की एक शिला को देखकर प्रभु ने पूछा, तब मुनि ने विस्तारपूर्वक सब कथा कही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1153.english_translation: On the road, they saw an ashram. There were no birds, beasts, or living creatures there. The Lord saw a stone slab and asked the sage about it. The sage then told the whole story in detail.
ramacharitamanas::1153.translation_literal: आश्रम (hermitage) / एक (one) / दीख (was seen) / मग माहीं (on the road) / खग (birds) / मृग (beasts) / जीव (living beings) / जंतु (creatures) / तहँ (there) / नाहीं (were not) ॥ पूछा (asked) / मुनिहि (the sage) / सिला (stone slab) / प्रभु (the Lord) / देखी (having seen) / सकल (all) / कथा (story) / मुनि (the sage) / कहा (told) / बिसेषी (in detail) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1153.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1153.essence: One question can uncover a forgotten past.
ramacharitamanas::1153.simple_meaning: They come to a deserted hermitage where no creatures live. Ram notices a stone slab and asks about it, prompting the sage to tell its story.
ramacharitamanas::1153.simple_insight: A single question can open a hidden history that changes how you see a place.
ramacharitamanas::1153.detailed_meaning: Ram and the sage are walking toward the bow sacrifice when they reach a strange, empty hermitage on the road. Ram notices a stone slab and asks why it is there. That question leads into Ahilya's story, which the next verse reveals.
ramacharitamanas::1153.modern_relevance: You walk into an old house and notice one cracked wall everyone else ignores. You ask about it, and suddenly a family story, a wound, or a truth comes back into view.
ramacharitamanas::1153.insight: It shifts attention from the surface of a place to the story buried inside it.

ramacharitamanas::1154.verse_sanskrit: गौतम नारि श्राप बस उपल देह धरि धीर। चरन कमल रज चाहति कृपा करहु रघुबीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::1154.verse_hindi: गौतम मुनि की स्त्री अहल्या शापवश पत्थर की देह धारण किए बड़े धीरज से आपके चरणकमलों की धूलि चाहती है। हे रघुवीर! इस पर कृपा कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1154.english_translation: Gautama's wife, bound by a curse, has taken a stone body. With patient longing, she seeks the dust of your lotus feet. O Raghuvir, show her grace.
ramacharitamanas::1154.translation_literal: गौतम (of Gautama) / नारि (wife) / श्राप बस (by the power of a curse) / उपल (stone) / देह (body) / धरि (having taken) / धीर (patient, steadfast) / चरन कमल (lotus feet) / रज (dust) / चाहति (desires) / कृपा (grace) / करहु (do) / रघुबीर (Raghuvir)
ramacharitamanas::1154.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1154.essence: Patient longing can still draw grace.
ramacharitamanas::1154.simple_meaning: Ahalya has been turned to stone by a curse, yet she still waits with patience for Ram's grace and the dust of his feet.
ramacharitamanas::1154.simple_insight: Deep waiting is not passive when it is held by trust.
ramacharitamanas::1154.detailed_meaning: At the hermitage, Ram has been led to a stone figure hidden in plain sight. The sage reveals that this is Ahalya, Gautama's wife, cursed and waiting in stillness for Ram's mercy. Her release is about to begin.
ramacharitamanas::1154.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone who cannot yet respond — a parent in recovery, a friend in silence, a relationship under strain. This verse honors the dignity of waiting without losing hope.
ramacharitamanas::1154.insight: It shifts attention from helplessness to receptive trust: grace can meet patient longing.

ramacharitamanas::1155.verse_sanskrit: परसत पद पावन सोकनसावन प्रगट भई तपपुंज सही। देखत रघुनायक जन सुखदायक सनमुख होइ कर जोरि रही॥ अति प्रेम अधीरा पुलक शरीरा मुख नहिं आवइ बचन कही। अतिसय बड़भागी चरनन्हि लागी जुगल नयन जलधार बही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1155.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के पवित्र और शोक को नाश करने वाले चरणों का स्पर्श पाते ही सचमुच वह तपोमूर्ति अहल्या प्रकट हो गई। भक्तों को सुख देने वाले श्री रघुनाथजी को देखकर वह हाथ जोड़कर सामने खड़ी रह गई। अत्यन्त प्रेम के कारण वह अधीर हो गई। उसका शरीर पुलकित हो उठा, मुख से वचन कहने में नहीं आते थे। वह अत्यन्त बड़भागिनी अहल्या प्रभु के चरणों से लिपट गई और उसके दोनों नेत्रों से जल (प्रेम और आनंद के आँसुओं) की धारा बहने लगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1155.english_translation: Touching Ram's holy feet, Ahalya rose from her long penance. Seeing Raghunath, the giver of joy to all beings, she stood before him with folded hands. Overcome by love, her body thrilled, words failed her, and she clung to his feet as tears flowed from both eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1155.translation_literal: परसत (touching) / पद (feet) / पावन (holy) / सोकनसावन (destroyer of sorrow) / प्रगट (manifested) / भई (became) / तपपुंज (mass of penance) / सही (indeed) / देखत (seeing) / रघुनायक (Lord of the Raghu clan) / जन (beings) / सुखदायक (giver of joy) / सनमुख (facing) / होइ (having become) / कर (hands) / जोरि (folding) / रही (remained) / अति (very) / प्रेम (love) / अधीरा (restless) / पुलक (thrilled) / शरीरा (body) / मुख (mouth) / नहिं (not) / आवइ (comes) / बचन (words) / कही (to say) / अतिसय (extremely) / बड़भागी (fortunate) / चरनन्हि (to the feet) / लागी (attached herself) / जुगल (both) / नयन (eyes) / जलधार (stream of water) / बही (flowed)
ramacharitamanas::1155.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1155.essence: Ram's touch restores what suffering had frozen.
ramacharitamanas::1155.simple_meaning: Ahalya is restored by Ram's touch. Overwhelmed with love, she stands before him, cannot speak, and weeps at his feet.
ramacharitamanas::1155.simple_insight: Grace can arrive so completely that gratitude becomes tears.
ramacharitamanas::1155.detailed_meaning: At Gautama's old hermitage, the cursed Ahalya has just been touched by Ram's feet and awakened from her stone-like state. She sees Ram, folds her hands, loses all composure in love, and falls at his feet in tears.
ramacharitamanas::1155.modern_relevance: After months of feeling numb, you finally meet the person who helped you heal. You cannot explain it cleanly. You just stand there, overwhelmed and grateful.
ramacharitamanas::1155.insight: It shifts attention from the miracle itself to the surrender and gratitude it awakens.

ramacharitamanas::1156.verse_sanskrit: धीरजु मन कीन्हा प्रभु कहुँ चीन्हा रघुपति कृपाँ भगति पाई। अति निर्मल बानी अस्तुति ठानी ग्यानगम्य जय रघुराई॥ मैं नारि अपावन प्रभु जग पावन रावन रिपु जन सुखदाई। राजीव बिलोचन भव भय मोचन पाहि पाहि सरनहिं आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1156.verse_hindi: फिर उसने मन में धीरज धरकर प्रभु को पहचाना और श्री रघुनाथजी की कृपा से भक्ति प्राप्त की। तब अत्यन्त निर्मल वाणी से उसने (इस प्रकार) स्तुति प्रारंभ की- हे ज्ञान से जानने योग्य श्री रघुनाथजी! आपकी जय हो! मैं (सहज ही) अपवित्र स्त्री हूँ, और हे प्रभो! आप जगत को पवित्र करने वाले, भक्तों को सुख देने वाले और रावण के शत्रु हैं। हे कमलनयन! हे संसार (जन्म-मृत्यु) के भय से छुड़ाने वाले! मैं आपकी शरण आई हूँ, (मेरी) रक्षा कीजिए, रक्षा कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1156.english_translation: She steadied her mind, recognized the Lord, and by Raghu's grace received devotion. Then, in utterly pure words, she began to praise: "Victory to you, Raghu's lord, known only through wisdom! I am an impure woman, and you are the purifier of the world, the delight of your devotees, the foe of Ravana. Lotus-eyed one, remover of the fear of worldly existence, I have come to your refuge. Protect me, protect me."
ramacharitamanas::1156.translation_literal: धीरजु (steadiness) / मन (mind) / कीन्हा (made) / प्रभु (Lord) / कहुँ (for) / चीन्हा (recognized) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu) / कृपाँ (by grace) / भगति (devotion) / पाई (received) / अति (very) / निर्मल (pure) / बानी (speech) / अस्तुति (praise) / ठानी (began) / ग्यानगम्य (reachable through knowledge) / जय (victory) / रघुराई (Raghu's lord) / मैं (I) / नारि (woman) / अपावन (impure) / प्रभु (Lord) / जग (world) / पावन (purifying) / रावन (Ravana) / रिपु (enemy) / जन (devotees) / सुखदाई (giver of joy) / राजीव (lotus) / बिलोचन (eyed) / भव (worldly existence) / भय (fear) / मोचन (remover) / पाहि (protect) / पाहि (protect) / सरनहिं (to refuge) / आई (came)
ramacharitamanas::1156.speaker: Ahalya
ramacharitamanas::1156.essence: Recognition becomes devotion, and devotion becomes shelter.
ramacharitamanas::1156.simple_meaning: Ahalya regains composure, recognizes Ram, and praises him with pure devotion. She admits her own impurity and asks the lotus-eyed Lord to protect her from fear.
ramacharitamanas::1156.simple_insight: Grace can turn shame into devotion and fear into surrender.
ramacharitamanas::1156.detailed_meaning: Ahalya has just been released from her long curse and stands before Ram. The shock gives way to steadiness, recognition, and praise. In this moment, her gratitude becomes surrender, and her first prayer asks for protection.
ramacharitamanas::1156.modern_relevance: After a mistake you thought would define you, you finally meet someone who sees past it. Your voice shakes at first, then steadies. What comes out is not explanation, but gratitude and a plea for mercy.
ramacharitamanas::1156.insight: It turns self-condemnation into refuge-seeking, showing that humility can become prayer.

ramacharitamanas::1157.verse_sanskrit: मुनि श्राप जो दीन्हा अति भल कीन्हा परम अनुग्रह मैं माना। देखेउँ भरि लोचन हरि भव मोचन इहइ लाभ संकर जाना॥ बिनती प्रभु मोरी मैं मति भोरी नाथ न मागउँ बर आना। पद कमल परागा रस अनुरागा मम मन मधुप करै पाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1157.verse_hindi: मुनि ने जो मुझे शाप दिया, सो बहुत ही अच्छा किया। मैं उसे अत्यन्त अनुग्रह (करके) मानती हूँ कि जिसके कारण मैंने संसार से छुड़ाने वाले श्री हरि (आप) को नेत्र भरकर देखा। इसी (आपके दर्शन) को शंकरजी सबसे बड़ा लाभ समझते हैं। हे प्रभो! मैं बुद्धि की बड़ी भोली हूँ, मेरी एक विनती है। हे नाथ ! मैं और कोई वर नहीं माँगती, केवल यही चाहती हूँ कि मेरा मन रूपी भौंरा आपके चरण-कमल की रज के प्रेमरूपी रस का सदा पान करता रहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1157.english_translation: The sage's curse did me great good; I count it as supreme grace, for it let me behold Hari, the liberator from worldly bondage, with my own eyes. Even Shankar knows that this is the highest gain. Lord, I am foolish in mind and ask for no other boon: let my bee-like mind drink forever the love-rasa of the dust of your lotus feet.
ramacharitamanas::1157.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / श्राप (curse) / जो (which) / दीन्हा (gave) / अति (very) / भल (good) / कीन्हा (did) / परम (supreme) / अनुग्रह (grace) / मैं (I) / माना (consider) । / देखेउँ (I saw) / भरि (filled) / लोचन (eyes) / हरि (Hari) / भव (worldly existence) / मोचन (liberator) / इहइ (this only) / लाभ (gain) / संकर (Shankar) / जाना (knows) । / बिनती (request) / प्रभु (Lord) / मोरी (my) / मैं (I) / मति (mind) / भोरी (foolish) / नाथ (Lord) / न (not) / मागउँ (ask) / बर (boon) / आना (other) । / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / परागा (dust/pollen) / रस (nectar) / अनुरागा (love) / मम (my) / मन (mind) / मधुप (bee) / करै (does) / पाना (drinking) ।
ramacharitamanas::1157.speaker: Ahalya
ramacharitamanas::1157.essence: Even suffering can become grace when it leads to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1157.simple_meaning: Ahalya says the curse was a blessing because it gave her Ram's darshan. She asks for nothing else except a mind forever devoted to his feet.
ramacharitamanas::1157.simple_insight: Pain can become the doorway to devotion, and devotion can make the heart feel richly fed.
ramacharitamanas::1157.detailed_meaning: Ahalya, just awakened by Ram's touch, speaks with wonder and gratitude. The curse that once seemed cruel now feels like the very path that brought her to the liberating sight of Ram. She asks only for endless love at his feet.
ramacharitamanas::1157.modern_relevance: A setback that once felt humiliating can later reveal the one meeting that changed everything. You look back and realize the detour was the doorway.
ramacharitamanas::1157.insight: It shifts the mind from resenting hardship to seeing how hardship can deepen longing and surrender.

ramacharitamanas::1158.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं पद सुरसरिता परम पुनीता प्रगट भई सिव सीस धरी। सोई पद पंकज जेहि पूजत अज मम सिर धरेउ कृपाल हरी॥ एहि भाँति सिधारी गौतम नारी बार बार हरि चरन परी। जो अति मन भावा सो बरु पावा गै पति लोक अनंद भरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1158.verse_hindi: जिन चरणों से परमपवित्र देवनदी गंगाजी प्रकट हुईं, जिन्हें शिवजी ने सिर पर धारण किया और जिन चरणकमलों को ब्रह्माजी पूजते हैं, कृपालु हरि (आप) ने उन्हीं को मेरे सिर पर रखा। इस प्रकार (स्तुति करती हुई) बार-बार भगवान के चरणों में गिरकर, जो मन को बहुत ही अच्छा लगा, उस वर को पाकर गौतम की स्त्री अहल्या आनंद में भरी हुई पतिलोक को चली गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1158.english_translation: The feet from which the sacred Ganga emerged, which Shiva bears on his head, and which Brahma worships, those same lotus feet compassionate Hari placed on my head. In this way, Gautama's wife Ahalya, again and again falling at Hari's feet, received the boon that pleased her mind and went, filled with joy, to her husband's realm.
ramacharitamanas::1158.translation_literal: जेहिं (by which) / पद (feet) / सुरसरिता (the river of the gods, Ganga) / परम पुनीता (most pure) / प्रगट भई (became manifest) / सिव (Shiva) / सीस (head) / धरी (placed) / सोई (those same) / पद पंकज (lotus feet) / जेहि (which) / पूजत (worshipping) / अज (Brahma) / मम (my) / सिर (head) / धरेउ (placed) / कृपाल हरी (compassionate Hari) / एहि भाँति (in this way) / सिधारी (departed, went forth) / गौतम नारी (Gautama's wife) / बार बार (again and again) / हरि चरन (Hari's feet) / परी (fell) / जो (that which) / अति मन भावा (greatly pleased the mind) / सो बरु (that boon) / पावा (received) / गै (went) / पति लोक (husband's realm) / अनंद भरी (filled with joy)
ramacharitamanas::1158.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1158.essence: The feet worshipped by the highest beings redeem the one who bows.
ramacharitamanas::1158.simple_meaning: Ram places his sacred feet on Ahalya's head, and the same feet are honored by Shiva and Brahma. Ahalya keeps bowing again and again, receives the blessing she longs for, and leaves in joy.
ramacharitamanas::1158.simple_insight: Reverence opens the door to grace. Humble surrender matters more than status or effort.
ramacharitamanas::1158.detailed_meaning: In the Gautama-Ahalya episode of Balkand, Ahalya finally meets Ram after long suffering and repentance.
