Tulsidas lingers on Ram's feet as the highest sacred object: the Ganga comes from them, Shiva bears them, Brahma worships them. Ahalya's repeated bowing becomes the moment that releases her.
ramacharitamanas::1158.modern_relevance: You finally apologize after carrying guilt for years. The other person doesn't need a perfect speech — they need sincerity, humility, and the courage to bow without defending yourself.
ramacharitamanas::1158.insight: It shifts the reader from self-justification to reverent surrender, showing that grace meets the one who yields.

ramacharitamanas::1159.verse_sanskrit: अस प्रभु दीनबंधु हरि कारन रहित दयाल। तुलसिदास सठ तेहि भजु छाड़ि कपट जंजाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1159.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ऐसे दीनबंधु और बिना ही कारण दया करने वाले हैं। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं, हे शठ (मन)! तू कपट-जंजाल छोड़कर उन्हीं का भजन कर ॥
ramacharitamanas::1159.english_translation: Ram is the friend of the humble and merciful without cause. Tulsidas says: O foolish mind, abandon deceit and worship him.
ramacharitamanas::1159.translation_literal: अस (such) / प्रभु (Lord) / दीनबंधु (friend of the humble) / हरि (Ram) / कारन (cause) / रहित (without) / दयाल (merciful) / तुलसिदास (Tulsidas) / सठ (foolish) / तेहि (him) / भजु (worship) / छाड़ि (abandon) / कपट (deceit) / जंजाल (tangle)
ramacharitamanas::1159.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1159.essence: Ram meets humility with mercy, not with conditions.
ramacharitamanas::1159.simple_meaning: Ram is merciful to the humble without needing a reason. Tulsidas tells the mind to stop pretending and turn toward him sincerely.
ramacharitamanas::1159.simple_insight: You do not have to earn grace by being perfect. Honest devotion is enough.
ramacharitamanas::1159.detailed_meaning: After hearing how the sacred river came to earth and how Shiva revered Ram's feet, Tulsidas turns inward. He calls Ram the friend of the humble and the merciful one who needs no cause, then urges his own restless mind to abandon deceit and worship sincerely.
ramacharitamanas::1159.modern_relevance: You catch yourself performing sincerity in a prayer room, a meeting, or even a private apology. The verse cuts through the performance and asks for one clean thing: stop pretending and come honestly.
ramacharitamanas::1159.insight: It shifts devotion from appearance to sincerity, and from self-protection to direct turning toward Ram.

ramacharitamanas::1160.verse_sanskrit: चले राम लछिमन मुनि संगा। गए जहाँ जग पावनि गंगा॥ गाधिसूनु सब कथा सुनाई। जेहि प्रकार सुरसरि महि आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1160.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी और लक्ष्मणजी मुनि के साथ चले। वे वहाँ गए, जहाँ जगत को पवित्र करने वाली गंगाजी थीं। महाराज गाधि के पुत्र विश्वामित्रजी ने वह सब कथा कह सुनाई जिस प्रकार देवनदी गंगाजी पृथ्वी पर आई थीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1160.english_translation: Ram and Lakshman walked with the sage to the Ganga, the purifier of the world. Gadhi's son then told the whole story of how the river Ganga came to earth.
ramacharitamanas::1160.translation_literal: चले (walked) / राम (Ram) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / मुनि (sage) / संगा (with) / गए (went) / जहाँ (where) / जग (world) / पावनि (purifying) / गंगा (Ganga) / गाधिसूनु (son of Gadhi) / सब (all) / कथा (story) / सुनाई (told) / जेहि प्रकार (in which way) / सुरसरि (river of the divine beings) / महि (to earth) / आई (came)
ramacharitamanas::1160.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1160.essence: A journey becomes sacred when the teacher begins the story.
ramacharitamanas::1160.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman go with Vishwamitra to the Ganga, and Vishwamitra explains how the river came down to earth.
ramacharitamanas::1160.simple_insight: Sacred stories can turn a journey into remembrance. The path itself becomes part of the teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1160.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman travel with Vishwamitra to the holy Ganga. There, the sage begins recounting the river's descent to earth. The verse is a transition in the journey, not the teaching's climax.
ramacharitamanas::1160.modern_relevance: You are walking somewhere ordinary with someone who knows the whole backstory. A simple stop becomes a lesson, and the conversation changes the mood of the entire day.
ramacharitamanas::1160.insight: It frames movement and place as part of spiritual instruction, not just travel.

ramacharitamanas::1161.verse_sanskrit: तब प्रभु रिषिन्ह समेत नहाए। बिबिध दान महिदेवन्हि पाए॥ हरषि चले मुनि बृंद सहाया। बेगि बिदेह नगर निअराया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1161.verse_hindi: तब प्रभु ने ऋषियों सहित (गंगाजी में) स्नान किया। ब्राह्मणों ने भाँति-भाँति के दान पाए। फिर मुनिवृन्द के साथ वे प्रसन्न होकर चले और शीघ्र ही जनकपुर के निकट पहुँच गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1161.english_translation: Then the Lord bathed with the sages, and the holy men received many gifts. Joyfully, He went on with the band of ascetics and quickly reached near the city of Videha.
ramacharitamanas::1161.translation_literal: तब (then) / प्रभु (the Lord) / रिषिन्ह समेत (together with the sages) / नहाए (bathed) / बिबिध (various) / दान (gifts) / महिदेवन्हि (to the holy men / brahmins) / पाए (were received) / हरषि (joyfully) / चले (went) / मुनि बृंद (the group of sages) / सहाया (with company) / बेगि (quickly) / बिदेह नगर (the city of Videha) / निअराया (came near)
ramacharitamanas::1161.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1161.essence: Sacred action does not stop the journey; it makes the next step joyful.
ramacharitamanas::1161.simple_meaning: Ram bathes with the sages, gives gifts, and then travels on cheerfully toward Janakpur.
ramacharitamanas::1161.simple_insight: Even sacred moments stay rooted in movement, generosity, and shared company.
ramacharitamanas::1161.detailed_meaning: Ram has just reached the Ganga with the sages. After bathing and giving gifts to the holy men, He continues onward in joy with the ascetics. The journey now brings Him close to Videha, where Sita's story is waiting.
ramacharitamanas::1161.modern_relevance: You finish a meaningful ritual, thank the people who helped, and keep moving without fuss. The day stays clean because gratitude and progress travel together.
ramacharitamanas::1161.insight: It keeps the focus on graceful transition: receive, give, and move on without delay.

ramacharitamanas::1162.verse_sanskrit: पुर रम्यता राम जब देखी। हरषे अनुज समेत बिसेषी॥ बापीं कूप सरित सर नाना। सलिल सुधासम मनि सोपाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1162.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने जब जनकपुर की शोभा देखी, तब वे छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण सहित अत्यन्त हर्षित हुए। वहाँ अनेकों बावलियाँ, कुएँ, नदी और तालाब हैं, जिनमें अमृत के समान जल है और मणियों की सीढ़ियाँ (बनी हुई) हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1162.english_translation: When Ram saw the beauty of Janakpur, he and Lakshman were greatly delighted. There were many wells, ponds, rivers, and lakes, with water sweet as nectar and stairways made of gems.
ramacharitamanas::1162.translation_literal: पुर (city) / रम्यता (beauty) / राम (Ram) / जब (when) / देखी (saw) / हरषे (were delighted) / अनुज (younger brother) / समेत (together with) / बिसेषी (especially) ॥ / बापीं (wells) / कूप (wells) / सरित (rivers) / सर (lakes) / नाना (many) / सलिल (water) / सुधासम (like nectar) / मनि (jewel) / सोपाना (stairways) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1162.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1162.essence: Wonder begins when the heart actually sees beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1162.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman admire the beauty of Janakpur, with its many wells, rivers, ponds, and gem-studded steps filled with sweet water.
ramacharitamanas::1162.simple_insight: Beauty can soften the heart and open it to wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1162.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have reached Janakpur on the way to Sita's swayamvar. Seeing the city's beauty, the brothers feel joy. The verse pauses the journey to paint the sacred, welcoming splendour of the place before the deeper meeting begins.
ramacharitamanas::1162.modern_relevance: You step into a city after a long train ride, exhausted and dusty, and suddenly the streets open into trees, water, and light. The body relaxes before the mind even knows why.
ramacharitamanas::1162.insight: It slows the reader into attention, teaching that reverence begins by truly seeing what is before you.

ramacharitamanas::1163.verse_sanskrit: गुंजत मंजु मत्त रस भृंगा। कूजत कल बहुबरन बिहंगा॥ बरन बरन बिकसे बनजाता। त्रिबिध समीर सदा सुखदाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1163.verse_hindi: मकरंद रस से मतवाले होकर भौंरे सुंदर गुंजार कर रहे हैं। रंग-बिरंगे (बहुत से) पक्षी मधुर शब्द कर रहे हैं। रंग-रंग के कमल खिले हैं। सदा (सब ऋतुओं में) सुख देने वाला शीतल, मंद, सुगंध पवन बह रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1163.english_translation: Bees hum softly drunk on nectar. Birds sing in many sweet colors. Lotuses bloom in many hues. A cool, gentle breeze gives steady delight in every season.
ramacharitamanas::1163.translation_literal: गुंजत (humming) / मंजु (sweetly) / मत्त (intoxicated) / रस (nectar) / भृंगा (bees) / कूजत (chirping) / कल (sweet) / बहुबरन (many-colored) / बिहंगा (birds) / बरन बरन (of many colors) / बिकसे (bloomed) / बनजाता (lotuses) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / समीर (breeze) / सदा (always) / सुखदाता (giver of delight)
ramacharitamanas::1163.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1163.essence: A blessed setting announces the sacred moment before it arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1163.simple_meaning: The garden around Janakpur is full of life, color, flowers, birds, and a pleasant breeze.
ramacharitamanas::1163.simple_insight: Beauty can prepare the heart before anything important is said.
ramacharitamanas::1163.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have reached Janakpur, and the scene is being set before the wedding festivities. The garden is alive with bees, birds, lotuses, and cool air, creating the calm, auspicious atmosphere that surrounds Sita’s world.
ramacharitamanas::1163.modern_relevance: You walk into a courtyard before a family wedding: flowers arranged, music drifting, everyone suddenly softer. The setting itself tells you something sacred is about to happen.
ramacharitamanas::1163.insight: It shifts attention from event to atmosphere, showing how place can carry meaning before action begins.

ramacharitamanas::1164.verse_sanskrit: सुमन बाटिका बाग बन बिपुल बिहंग निवास। फूलत फलत सुपल्लवत सोहत पुर चहुँ पास॥212।
ramacharitamanas::1164.verse_hindi: पुष्प वाटिका (फुलवारी), बाग और वन, जिनमें बहुत से पक्षियों का निवास है, फूलते, फलते और सुंदर पत्तों से लदे हुए नगर के चारों ओर सुशोभित हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1164.english_translation: Flower gardens, groves, and forests with many birds dwell around the city, blooming and fruiting, beautiful with tender leaves on all four sides.
ramacharitamanas::1164.translation_literal: सुमन (flowers) / बाटिका (gardens) / बाग (groves) / बन (forests) / बिपुल (many) / बिहंग (birds) / निवास (dwelling) / फूलत (blooming) / फलत (fruiting) / सुपल्लवत (with tender leaves) / सोहत (shining, looking beautiful) / पुर (city) / चहुँ पास (on all four sides)
ramacharitamanas::1164.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1164.essence: The city’s beauty surrounds you before anyone even enters it.
ramacharitamanas::1164.simple_meaning: Gardens, groves, forests, and birds make the city beautiful on every side.
ramacharitamanas::1164.simple_insight: Beauty can be felt as a whole atmosphere, not just seen in one object.
ramacharitamanas::1164.detailed_meaning: As Ram and Lakshman enter Janakpur, the city opens around them in layers of gardens, groves, forests, flowers, fruit, and birds. Tulsidas is painting the setting before the swayamvar, letting the reader feel the city’s living beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1164.modern_relevance: You step into a neighborhood at dusk and notice jasmine on a wall, trees overhanging the lane, birds settling in the branches. The place feels alive before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::1164.insight: It shifts attention from isolated details to the living harmony of a place.

ramacharitamanas::1165.verse_sanskrit: बनइ न बरनत नगर निकाई। जहाँ जाइ मन तहँइँ लोभाई॥ चारु बजारु बिचित्र अँबारी। मनिमय बिधि जनु स्वकर सँवारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1165.verse_hindi: नगर की सुंदरता का वर्णन करते नहीं बनता। मन जहाँ जाता है, वहीं लुभा जाता (रम जाता) है। सुंदर बाजार है, मणियों से बने हुए विचित्र छज्जे हैं, मानो ब्रह्मा ने उन्हें अपने हाथों से बनाया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1165.english_translation: The city's beauty cannot be described. Wherever the mind goes, it is drawn in. Beautiful markets and wondrous balconies stand there, as if the creator shaped them by hand.
ramacharitamanas::1165.translation_literal: बनइ न (is not possible) / बरनत (describing) / नगर (city) / निकाई (beauty) / जहाँ (where) / जाइ (goes) / मन (mind) / तहँइँ (there itself) / लोभाई (is enticed) / चारु (beautiful) / बजारु (market) / बिचित्र (wondrous) / अँबारी (balconies/overhangs) / मनिमय (made of jewels) / बिधि (the creator) / जनु (as if) / स्वकर (own hand) / सँवारी (decorated)
ramacharitamanas::1165.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1165.essence: Ayodhya is so beautiful that the mind cannot keep its distance.
ramacharitamanas::1165.simple_meaning: The city is so beautiful that words fail to capture it. Every part of it attracts the mind, from the markets to the jeweled balconies.
ramacharitamanas::1165.simple_insight: Beauty can be so complete that attention stops wandering and simply rests there.
ramacharitamanas::1165.detailed_meaning: The poem is still describing Ayodhya before Ram's return. After the gardens and birds, the narrator turns to the city's streets, markets, and jeweled architecture. The point is not doctrine but wonder: this is a place so perfectly ordered that it seems crafted by the creator's own hand.
ramacharitamanas::1165.modern_relevance: You walk into a festival street at dusk, with lights strung above stalls and music drifting from every corner. For a moment, you stop scrolling, stop planning, and simply look.
ramacharitamanas::1165.insight: It shifts attention from analysis to wonder, letting the mind receive beauty without needing to control it.

ramacharitamanas::1166.verse_sanskrit: धनिक बनिक बर धनद समाना। बैठे सकल बस्तु लै नाना। चौहट सुंदर गलीं सुहाई। संतत रहहिं सुगंध सिंचाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1166.verse_hindi: कुबेर के समान श्रेष्ठ धनी व्यापारी सब प्रकार की अनेक वस्तुएँ लेकर (दुकानों में) बैठे हैं। सुंदर चौराहे और सुहावनी गलियाँ सदा सुगंध से सिंची रहती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1166.english_translation: Wealthy merchants, like Kubera, sat with many kinds of goods. Beautiful crossroads and pleasant lanes were always sprinkled with fragrance.
ramacharitamanas::1166.translation_literal: धनिक (wealthy) / बनिक (merchant) / बर (excellent) / धनद (Kubera, giver of wealth) / समाना (like) / बैठे (sat) / सकल (all) / बस्तु (goods) / लै (taking) / नाना (many kinds) / चौहट (crossroads) / सुंदर (beautiful) / गलीं (lanes) / सुहाई (pleasant) / संतत (continually) / रहहिं (remain) / सुगंध (fragrance) / सिंचाई (sprinkled)
ramacharitamanas::1166.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1166.essence: A blessed city makes abundance visible in every street.
ramacharitamanas::1166.simple_meaning: Wealthy merchants fill the city with many goods, while its crossroads and lanes stay fragrant and beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::1166.simple_insight: Some places feel alive because abundance is shared openly, not hidden away.
ramacharitamanas::1166.detailed_meaning: The description of Ayodhya continues. Merchants sit in their shops with rich wares, and the streets stay scented and lovely. This is part of the larger picture of a city so complete that every detail seems blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1166.modern_relevance: You walk into a market where every stall is full, the alleys are clean, and the air smells of flowers and spice. The place itself feels cared for.
ramacharitamanas::1166.insight: It shifts attention from isolated riches to a whole culture of beauty, order, and plenty.

ramacharitamanas::1167.verse_sanskrit: मंगलमय मंदिर सब केरें। चित्रित जनु रतिनाथ चितेरें॥ पुर नर नारि सुभग सुचि संता। धरमसील ग्यानी गुनवंता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1167.verse_hindi: सबके घर मंगलमय हैं और उन पर चित्र कढ़े हुए हैं, जिन्हें मानो कामदेव रूपी चित्रकार ने अंकित किया है। नगर के (सभी) स्त्री-पुरुष सुंदर, पवित्र, साधु स्वभाव वाले, धर्मात्मा, ज्ञानी और गुणवान हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1167.english_translation: All the houses are filled with auspicious beauty, as if painted by Cupid himself. The men and women of the city are handsome, pure, gentle, righteous, wise, and virtuous.
ramacharitamanas::1167.translation_literal: मंगलमय (full of auspiciousness) / मंदिर (houses, dwellings) / सब (all) / केरें (of them) / चित्रित (painted, decorated) / जनु (as if) / रतिनाथ (lord of desire, Cupid) / चितेरें (by a painter) // पुर (city) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / सुभग (beautiful, fortunate) / सुचि (pure) / संता (gentle, saintly) / धरमसील (righteous) / ग्यानी (wise) / गुनवंता (virtuous)
ramacharitamanas::1167.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1167.essence: A truly beautiful city is made by both its homes and its people.
ramacharitamanas::1167.simple_meaning: The city is so beautiful that every house seems blessed and artist-made. Its people are also pure, righteous, wise, and full of good qualities.
ramacharitamanas::1167.simple_insight: Beauty feels complete when the place and the people both shine.
ramacharitamanas::1167.detailed_meaning: The narration has entered Janakpur, where even the streets, homes, and people seem perfected. Tulsidas is not teaching a doctrine here; he is building wonder before Janaka's palace appears, so the reader feels the city's sacred splendor in advance.
ramacharitamanas::1167.modern_relevance: You walk into a home where everything is clean, calm, and thoughtfully placed, and then the people greet you with the same warmth. The whole place feels blessed because character matches beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1167.insight: It trains the eye to notice that true grandeur includes moral beauty, not just decoration.

ramacharitamanas::1168.verse_sanskrit: अति अनूप जहँ जनक निवासू। बिथकहिं बिबुध बिलोकि बिलासू॥ होत चकित चित कोट बिलोकी। सकल भुवन सोभा जनु रोकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1168.verse_hindi: जहाँ जनकजी का अत्यन्त अनुपम (सुंदर) निवास स्थान (महल) है, वहाँ के विलास (ऐश्वर्य) को देखकर देवता भी थकित (स्तम्भित) हो जाते हैं (मनुष्यों की तो बात ही क्या!)। कोट (राजमहल के परकोटे) को देखकर चित्त चकित हो जाता है, (ऐसा मालूम होता है) मानो उसने समस्त लोकों की शोभा को रोक (घेर) रखा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1168.english_translation: Janak's residence is uniquely beautiful. Even the radiant beings are stunned by its splendor. Seeing the fort walls, the mind is amazed, as if all the world's beauty were gathered there.
ramacharitamanas::1168.translation_literal: अति अनूप (extremely incomparable) / जहँ (where) / जनक (Janak) / निवासू (residence) / बिथकहिं (are amazed) / बिबुध (radiant beings) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बिलासू (splendor, luxury)॥ / होत (becoming) / चकित (stunned) / चित (mind) / कोट (fort wall, fortress) / बिलोकी (seeing) / सकल (all) / भुवन (worlds) / सोभा (beauty, splendor) / जनु (as if) / रोकी (stopped, held back) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1168.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1168.essence: Beauty here is so complete it seems to contain the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::1168.simple_meaning: Janak's palace is so beautiful that even the radiant beings are amazed by it. Its walls seem to hold all beauty inside them.
ramacharitamanas::1168.simple_insight: Some places feel so complete they silence the mind for a moment.
ramacharitamanas::1168.detailed_meaning: The story has reached Mithila, where Janak's palace and city are being described in rich detail before Sita's swayamvar. The verse lingers on the palace's beauty to build awe, not to teach a doctrine.
ramacharitamanas::1168.modern_relevance: You walk into a home so carefully kept that conversation stops for a second. The light, the order, the elegance — everything feels gathered into one place.
ramacharitamanas::1168.insight: It slows the reader into wonder before the meeting of Ram and Sita.

ramacharitamanas::1169.verse_sanskrit: धवल धाम मनि पुरट पट सुघटित नाना भाँति। सिय निवास सुंदर सदन सोभा किमि कहि जाति ॥
ramacharitamanas::1169.verse_hindi: उज्ज्वल महलों में अनेक प्रकार के सुंदर रीति से बने हुए मणि जटित सोने की जरी के परदे लगे हैं। सीताजी के रहने के सुंदर महल की शोभा का वर्णन किया ही कैसे जा सकता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1169.english_translation: The bright palace has many kinds of finely fitted curtains of gems and gold. How can the beauty of Sita’s lovely dwelling even be described?
ramacharitamanas::1169.translation_literal: धवल (bright/white) / धाम (dwelling, palace) / मनि (gems) / पुरट (gold) / पट (curtains, cloths) / सुघटित (well-fitted, finely made) / नाना भाँति (in many ways) / सिय निवास (Sita’s dwelling) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सदन (house, mansion) / सोभा (beauty, splendor) / किमि (how) / कहि (spoken, described) / जाति (can be gone, can be described)
ramacharitamanas::1169.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1169.essence: Beauty beyond measure leaves language behind.
ramacharitamanas::1169.simple_meaning: Sita’s palace is so beautiful and richly decorated that words cannot fully describe it.
ramacharitamanas::1169.simple_insight: Some beauty is too complete for language; it simply overwhelms the mind.
ramacharitamanas::1169.detailed_meaning: The narration lingers inside Janak’s palace, moving from one exquisite detail to the next. After describing the splendor of the city and the royal residence, this line pauses on Sita’s own chambers, showing that even divine-style grandeur feels inadequate before her beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1169.modern_relevance: You walk into a room prepared with such care that you stop speaking for a moment. The attention in the space says more than any explanation could.
ramacharitamanas::1169.insight: It shifts attention from naming beauty to receiving it fully without trying to contain it in words.

ramacharitamanas::1170.verse_sanskrit: सुभग द्वार सब कुलिस कपाटा। भूप भीर नट मागध भाटा॥ बनी बिसाल बाजि गज साला। हय गय रख संकुल सब काला ॥
ramacharitamanas::1170.verse_hindi: राजमहल के सब दरवाजे (फाटक) सुंदर हैं, जिनमें वज्र के (मजबूत अथवा हीरों के चमकते हुए) किवाड़ लगे हैं। वहाँ (मातहत) राजाओं, नटों, मागधों और भाटों की भीड़ लगी रहती है। घोड़ों और हाथियों के लिए बहुत बड़ी-बड़ी घुड़सालें और गजशालाएँ (फीलखाने) बनी हुई हैं, जो सब समय घोड़े, हाथी और रथों से भरी रहती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1170.english_translation: All the gates are beautiful, with iron-clad doors. Kings, dancers, heralds, and bards crowd the court. Great stables and elephant houses stand ready, always packed with horses and elephants.
ramacharitamanas::1170.translation_literal: सुभग (beautiful) / द्वार (gates) / सब (all) / कुलिस (diamond/iron) / कपाटा (doors, shutters) / भूप (kings) / भीर (crowd) / नट (dancers, actors) / मागध (court bards, heralds) / भाटा (praisers, minstrels) / बनी (made, built) / बिसाल (vast, large) / बाजि (horses) / गज (elephants) / साला (stables, sheds) / हय (horses) / गय (elephants) / रख (kept) / संकुल (crowded, packed) / सब (all) / काला (at all times)
ramacharitamanas::1170.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1170.essence: Grandeur is revealed by the order it can sustain.
ramacharitamanas::1170.simple_meaning: Janak's palace is described as richly built, with strong doors, many visitors, and huge stables full of horses and elephants.
ramacharitamanas::1170.simple_insight: Sometimes a place's grandeur is shown through the life moving through it, not just through its walls.
ramacharitamanas::1170.detailed_meaning: The scene is still inside Janak's dazzling palace complex before Sita's swayamvar. After praising its beauty, the narration turns to its gates, courtyards, and stables, showing that this is not a quiet home but a living royal center filled with power and movement.
ramacharitamanas::1170.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding venue where security, guests, staff, and vehicles all move at once. The building matters, but the real impression is the scale of life it can hold.
ramacharitamanas::1170.insight: It shifts attention from decorative beauty to the social and material order that supports it.

ramacharitamanas::1171.verse_sanskrit: सूर सचिव सेनप बहुतेरे। नृपगृह सरिस सदन सब केरे॥ पुर बाहेर सर सरित समीपा। उतरे जहँ तहँ बिपुल महीपा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1171.verse_hindi: बहुत से शूरवीर, मंत्री और सेनापति हैं। उन सबके घर भी राजमहल सरीखे ही हैं। नगर के बाहर तालाब और नदी के निकट जहाँ-तहाँ बहुत से राजा लोग उतरे हुए (डेरा डाले हुए) हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1171.english_translation: There are many brave warriors, ministers, and commanders. Their homes are like royal palaces. Outside the city, near ponds and rivers, many kings have camped here and there.
ramacharitamanas::1171.translation_literal: सूर (brave men) / सचिव (ministers) / सेनप (commanders) / बहुतेरे (many) / नृपगृह (king's house) / सरिस (like) / सदन (homes) / सब (all) / केरे (of them)॥ / पुर (city) / बाहेर (outside) / सर (ponds) / सरित (rivers) / समीपा (near) / उतरे (camped) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / बिपुल (many) / महीपा (kings)॥
ramacharitamanas::1171.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1171.essence: Power surrounds the moment, but the real turning point has not arrived.
ramacharitamanas::1171.simple_meaning: The city is full of powerful people and their grand homes. Many kings have set up camp around it near water.
ramacharitamanas::1171.simple_insight: The scene feels crowded with power, but nothing here is yet the point.
ramacharitamanas::1171.detailed_meaning: The narration is still describing Mithila’s splendor before the swayamvar. Warriors, ministers, commanders, and visiting kings fill the city and its outskirts. The verse builds the setting, not the teaching, so it supports the next arrival of Vishwamitra and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1171.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding venue and see VIP cars, security, and grand decorations everywhere. The room is impressive, but it is still only the backdrop before the real moment begins.
ramacharitamanas::1171.insight: It trains attention to notice scene-setting without mistaking it for the message.

ramacharitamanas::1172.verse_sanskrit: देखि अनूप एक अँवराई। सब सुपास सब भाँति सुहाई। कौसिक कहेउ मोर मनु माना। इहाँ रहिअ रघुबीर सुजाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1172.verse_hindi: (वहीं) आमों का एक अनुपम बाग देखकर, जहाँ सब प्रकार के सुभीते थे और जो सब तरह से सुहावना था, विश्वामित्रजी ने कहा- हे सुजान रघुवीर! मेरा मन कहता है कि यहीं रहा जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1172.english_translation: Seeing a unique mango grove there, pleasant in every way and full of conveniences, Vishwamitra said, “O wise Raghubir, my mind says we should stay here.”
ramacharitamanas::1172.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / अनूप (unique) / एक (one) / अँवराई (mango grove) / सब (all) / सुपास (convenient) / सब (all) / भाँति (ways) / सुहाई (pleasant) / कौसिक (Vishwamitra) / कहेउ (said) / मोर (my) / मनु (mind) / माना (has decided) / इहाँ (here) / रहिअ (stay) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / सुजाना (wise)
ramacharitamanas::1172.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1172.essence: A wise traveler knows when a place is fit to stop.
ramacharitamanas::1172.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra sees a beautiful mango grove and decides it is a good place to stop and stay.
ramacharitamanas::1172.simple_insight: Sometimes the next right step is simple: notice a fitting place and let the mind settle there.
ramacharitamanas::1172.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Vishwamitra are traveling toward Mithila. They come upon a lovely mango grove with everything needed for rest. Vishwamitra decides this is the right place to halt before the journey continues.
ramacharitamanas::1172.modern_relevance: After hours on the road, you finally spot a quiet grove, a water tap, and shade. The body knows before the mind does: this is where you stop.
ramacharitamanas::1172.insight: It shifts attention from pushing onward to recognizing the right place to pause and rest.

ramacharitamanas::1173.verse_sanskrit: भलेहिं नाथ कहि कृपानिकेता। उतरे तहँ मुनि बृंद समेता॥ बिस्वामित्र महामुनि आए। समाचार मिथिलापति पाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1173.verse_hindi: कृपा के धाम श्री रामचन्द्रजी 'बहुत अच्छा स्वामिन् !' कहकर वहीं मुनियों के समूह के साथ ठहर गए। मिथिलापति जनकजी ने जब यह समाचार पाया कि महामुनि विश्वामित्र आए हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1173.english_translation: Saying, “Very well, Lord,” the shelter of grace settled there with the sages. When the great sage Vishvamitra arrived, King Janaka learned the news.
ramacharitamanas::1173.translation_literal: भलेहिं (very well) / नाथ (Lord) / कहि (saying) / कृपानिकेता (abode of grace) / उतरे (descended / settled) / तहँ (there) / मुनि (sage) / बृंद (group) / समेता (together with)॥ / बिस्वामित्र (Vishvamitra) / महामुनि (great sage) / आए (came) / समाचार (news) / मिथिलापति (king of Mithila) / पाए (received)
ramacharitamanas::1173.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1173.essence: The meeting begins before the people meet.
ramacharitamanas::1173.simple_meaning: Ram agrees to stay there with the sages. Then Vishvamitra arrives, and King Janaka hears the news.
ramacharitamanas::1173.simple_insight: Some moments simply unfold in the right order: welcome, arrival, and the stir of meeting.
ramacharitamanas::1173.detailed_meaning: Ram has accepted Vishvamitra’s choice of resting place and settled there with the sages. At the same time, Vishvamitra reaches Mithila, and Janaka receives word of his arrival. The scene is setting up the first meeting between the two great figures.
ramacharitamanas::1173.modern_relevance: A host points you to a quiet room, you settle in, and then the message comes that the person you were waiting for has arrived. The whole atmosphere changes in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::1173.insight: It shifts attention from action to arrival: the verse prepares the meeting by showing both parties in motion.

ramacharitamanas::1174.verse_sanskrit: संग सचिव सुचि भूरि भट भूसुर बर गुर ग्याति। चले मिलन मुनिनायकहि मुदित राउ एहि भाँति ॥
ramacharitamanas::1174.verse_hindi: तब उन्होंने पवित्र हृदय के (ईमानदार, स्वामिभक्त) मंत्री बहुत से योद्धा, श्रेष्ठ ब्राह्मण, गुरु (शतानंदजी) और अपनी जाति के श्रेष्ठ लोगों को साथ लिया और इस प्रकार प्रसन्नता के साथ राजा मुनियों के स्वामी विश्वामित्रजी से मिलने चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1174.english_translation: Then the king, with pure ministers, many warriors, excellent brahmins, the teacher, and noble kinsmen, went joyfully to meet the sage chief.
ramacharitamanas::1174.translation_literal: संग (with) / सचिव (ministers) / सुचि (pure) / भूरि (many) / भट (warriors) / भूसुर (brahmins) / बर (excellent) / गुर (teacher) / ग्याति (kinsmen) / चले (went) / मिलन (to meet) / मुनिनायकहि (the sage chief) / मुदित (joyful) / राउ (the king) / एहि भाँति (in this manner)
ramacharitamanas::1174.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1174.essence: Joyful respect makes room for a worthy arrival.
ramacharitamanas::1174.simple_meaning: King Janak goes out joyfully with his trusted court and respected elders to greet Vishwamitra.
ramacharitamanas::1174.simple_insight: Respectful meeting begins with the right company and a willing heart.
ramacharitamanas::1174.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, King Janak hears that Vishwamitra has arrived. He leaves with ministers, warriors, brahmins, his teacher, and kinsmen, all in a spirit of joy. The verse simply sets up the formal welcome.
ramacharitamanas::1174.modern_relevance: A senior leader walks into a room with the people who hold the organization together, not for show, but to greet an important guest properly.
ramacharitamanas::1174.insight: It shifts attention to the dignity of welcome and the social harmony behind it.

ramacharitamanas::1175.verse_sanskrit: कीन्ह प्रनामु चरन धरि माथा। दीन्हि असीस मुदित मुनिनाथा॥ बिप्रबृंद सब सादर बंदे। जानि भाग्य बड़ राउ अनंदे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1175.verse_hindi: राजा ने मुनि के चरणों पर मस्तक रखकर प्रणाम किया। मुनियों के स्वामी विश्वामित्रजी ने प्रसन्न होकर आशीर्वाद दिया। फिर सारी ब्राह्मणमंडली को आदर सहित प्रणाम किया और अपना बड़ा भाग्य जानकर राजा आनंदित हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1175.english_translation: The king bowed with his head at the sage's feet. The lord of the sages, pleased, gave his blessing. He then honored all the learned Brahmins with respect, and the king rejoiced, knowing his great good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::1175.translation_literal: कीन्ह (did) / प्रनामु (bowed) / चरन (feet) / धरि (placing) / माथा (head) / दीन्हि (gave) / असीस (blessing) / मुदित (pleased) / मुनिनाथा (lord of sages) / बिप्रबृंद (assembly of Brahmins) / सब (all) / सादर (with respect) / बंदे (he bowed) / जानि (knowing) / भाग्य (fortune) / बड़ (great) / राउ (king) / अनंदे (rejoiced)
ramacharitamanas::1175.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1175.essence: True greatness begins with humility before wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::1175.simple_meaning: King Janaka bows to Vishwamitra, receives his blessing, honors the Brahmins, and feels joy at the good fortune of this visit.
ramacharitamanas::1175.simple_insight: Respect opens the heart. When humility leads, even a royal welcome becomes a moment of joy.
ramacharitamanas::1175.detailed_meaning: Janaka has come out to meet Vishwamitra in Mithila. He bows low, receives the sage's blessing, and then honors the gathered Brahmins with care. This is a scene of courtly respect, not a teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::1175.modern_relevance: You enter a room where everyone is waiting for your answer, and you choose respect first. That small bow changes the whole atmosphere before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1175.insight: It shows how humility and honor create a dignified meeting before any discussion begins.

ramacharitamanas::1176.verse_sanskrit: कुसल प्रस्न कहि बारहिं बारा। बिस्वामित्र नृपहि बैठारा॥ तेहि अवसर आए दोउ भाई। गए रहे देखन फुलवाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1176.verse_hindi: बार-बार कुशल प्रश्न करके विश्वामित्रजी ने राजा को बैठाया। उसी समय दोनों भाई आ पहुँचे, जो फुलवाड़ी देखने गए थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1176.english_translation: विश्वामित्र repeatedly asked after the king's welfare and seated him. At that moment the two brothers arrived; they had gone to see the flower garden.
ramacharitamanas::1176.translation_literal: कुसल (well-being) / प्रस्न (questions) / कहि (having said) / बारहिं बारा (again and again) / बिस्वामित्र (Vishwamitra) / नृपहि (the king) / बैठारा (seated) / तेहि अवसर (at that moment) / आए (came) / दोउ भाई (both brothers) / गए रहे (had gone) / देखन (to see) / फुलवाई (flower garden)
ramacharitamanas::1176.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1176.essence: A calm welcome makes room for the arrival that matters.
ramacharitamanas::1176.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra warmly seated King Janak and kept asking after his well-being. At that moment Rama and Lakshman arrived from the flower garden.
ramacharitamanas::1176.simple_insight: Sometimes the most important meeting begins with simple courtesy and perfect timing.
ramacharitamanas::1176.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Vishwamitra finishes greeting the king and settles him in place. Just then Rama and Lakshman return from seeing the flower garden, setting up the first face-to-face moment of this section.
ramacharitamanas::1176.modern_relevance: You are deep in small talk at a family gathering when the one person everyone has been waiting for walks in. The room shifts before anyone says a word.
ramacharitamanas::1176.insight: It sets the scene for a decisive meeting by showing how ordinary courtesy can frame a moment of destiny.

ramacharitamanas::1177.verse_sanskrit: स्याम गौर मृदु बयस किसोरा। लोचन सुखद बिस्व चित चोरा॥ उठे सकल जब रघुपति आए। बिस्वामित्र निकट बैठाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1177.verse_hindi: सुकुमार किशोर अवस्था वाले श्याम और गौर वर्ण के दोनों कुमार नेत्रों को सुख देने वाले और सारे विश्व के चित्त को चुराने वाले हैं। जब रघुनाथजी आए तब सभी (उनके रूप एवं तेज से प्रभावित होकर) उठकर खड़े हो गए। विश्वामित्रजी ने उनको अपने पास बैठा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1177.english_translation: The dark and fair youths were tender in age, pleasing to the eyes, and stealing the hearts of the world. When Raghunath arrived, everyone stood up, and Vishwamitra seated them near himself.
ramacharitamanas::1177.translation_literal: स्याम (dark) / गौर (fair) / मृदु (soft, tender) / बयस (age) / किसोरा (young boys) / लोचन (eyes) / सुखद (pleasing) / बिस्व (world) / चित (mind) / चोरा (thieves) / उठे (stood up) / सकल (all) / जब (when) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / आए (came) / बिस्वामित्र (Vishvamitra) / निकट (near) / बैठाए (made sit)
ramacharitamanas::1177.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1177.essence: Their presence alone makes the whole assembly rise.
ramacharitamanas::1177.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman arrive as beautiful young boys. Their presence delights everyone, and Vishvamitra makes them sit beside him.
ramacharitamanas::1177.simple_insight: Some presences need no introduction. Their arrival changes the room before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1177.detailed_meaning: In Vishvamitra’s presence, the two brothers return from the flower garden. Their youthful beauty silences the assembly, and everyone rises at once. Vishvamitra seats them close, marking this as a moment of reverence before the next part of the story begins.
ramacharitamanas::1177.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the conversation stops for a second. Not because you demanded attention, but because your presence carried something unmistakable.
ramacharitamanas::1177.insight: It shows how Ram’s presence naturally draws respect and tenderness without force.

ramacharitamanas::1178.verse_sanskrit: भए सब सुखी देखि दोउ भ्राता। बारि बिलोचन पुलकित गाता॥ मूरति मधुर मनोहर देखी भयउ बिदेहु बिदेहु बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1178.verse_hindi: दोनों भाइयों को देखकर सभी सुखी हुए। सबके नेत्रों में जल भर आया (आनंद और प्रेम के आँसू उमड़ पड़े) और शरीर रोमांचित हो उठे। रामजी की मधुर मनोहर मूर्ति को देखकर विदेह (जनक) विशेष रूप से विदेह (देह की सुध-बुध से रहित) हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1178.english_translation: Seeing the two brothers, everyone became happy. Their eyes filled with tears and their bodies thrilled with joy. Seeing Ram's sweet, beautiful form, Janak became especially lost beyond bodily awareness.
ramacharitamanas::1178.translation_literal: भए (became) / सब (all) / सुखी (happy) / देखि (seeing) / दोउ (both) / भ्राता (brothers) / बारि (water) / बिलोचन (eyes) / पुलकित (thrilled) / गाता (body) / मूरति (form) / मधुर (sweet) / मनोहर (beautiful) / देखी (seeing) / भयउ (became) / बिदेहु (Janak) / बिदेहु (beyond bodily awareness) / बिसेषी (especially)
ramacharitamanas::1178.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1178.essence: Ram's presence turns sight into joy and self-forgetting.
ramacharitamanas::1178.simple_meaning: Everyone feels joy on seeing Ram and Lakshman. Janak is especially overwhelmed by Ram's beautiful form and forgets his body.
ramacharitamanas::1178.simple_insight: Real devotion can make joy physical — tears, goosebumps, and a mind that forgets itself.
ramacharitamanas::1178.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, after the prince brothers arrive, the whole gathering softens with delight. Tears rise, bodies shiver, and Janak is especially struck by Ram's beauty. The scene shows how Ram's presence moves a room before any words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1178.modern_relevance: You catch sight of someone you have waited weeks to meet, and your chest loosens before you can speak. Some presences arrive before language does.
ramacharitamanas::1178.insight: It shifts attention from explanation to direct experience: the sight of the beloved can transform the whole body at once.

ramacharitamanas::1179.verse_sanskrit: प्रेम मगन मनु जानि नृपु करि बिबेकु धरि धीर। बोलेउ मुनि पद नाइ सिरु गदगद गिरा गभीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::1179.verse_hindi: मन को प्रेम में मग्न जान राजा जनक ने विवेक का आश्रय लेकर धीरज धारण किया और मुनि के चरणों में सिर नवाकर गद् गद् (प्रेमभरी) गंभीर वाणी से कहा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1179.english_translation: Knowing his mind was overwhelmed by love, the king gathered himself with discernment and calm. Bowing his head at the sage's feet, he spoke in a choked, deep voice.
ramacharitamanas::1179.translation_literal: प्रेम (love) / मगन (immersed) / मनु (mind) / जानि (knowing) / नृपु (king) / करि (having done) / बिबेकु (discernment) / धरि (having held) / धीर (calm) / बोलेउ (spoke) / मुनि (sage) / पद (feet) / नाइ (bowing) / सिरु (head) / गदगद (choked with emotion) / गिरा (voice) / गभीर (deep)
ramacharitamanas::1179.speaker: Janak
ramacharitamanas::1179.essence: Love can overwhelm the heart without overthrowing composure.
ramacharitamanas::1179.simple_meaning: Janak is overwhelmed by love, but he steadies himself, bows to the sage, and speaks calmly through tears.
ramacharitamanas::1179.simple_insight: Strong feeling does not have to become confusion. You can feel deeply and still respond with dignity.
ramacharitamanas::1179.detailed_meaning: Janak sees Ram and Lakshman and is flooded with love. Before he asks who these beautiful boys are, he gathers himself, bows to Vishwamitra, and speaks with reverence. The verse shows emotion held by discernment.
ramacharitamanas::1179.modern_relevance: You see someone you love walk into the room and your chest tightens. You still lower your voice, breathe, and speak with care instead of spilling everything at once.
ramacharitamanas::1179.insight: It teaches you to let feeling be real without letting it seize control of your speech or conduct.

ramacharitamanas::1180.verse_sanskrit: कहहु नाथ सुंदर दोउ बालक। मुनिकुल तिलक कि नृपकुल पालक॥ ब्रह्म जो निगम नेति कहि गावा। उभय बेष धरि की सोइ आवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1180.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! कहिए, ये दोनों सुंदर बालक मुनिकुल के आभूषण हैं या किसी राजवंश के पालक? अथवा जिसका वेदों ने 'नेति' कहकर गान किया है कहीं वह ब्रह्म तो युगल रूप धरकर नहीं आया है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1180.english_translation: O Lord, tell me: are these two beautiful boys ornaments of the sage's line, or protectors of the king's line? Or has the same supreme reality, praised in the Vedas as beyond all description, come here wearing two forms?
ramacharitamanas::1180.translation_literal: कहहु (tell) / नाथ (lord) / सुंदर (beautiful) / दोउ (both) / बालक (boys) / मुनिकुल (sage-line) / तिलक (ornament) / कि (or) / नृपकुल (king-line) / पालक (protector) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / जो (which) / निगम (the Vedas) / नेति (not this, not this) / कहि (saying) / गावा (sung) / उभय (both) / बेष (forms) / धरि (having taken) / की (did) / सोइ (the same) / आवा (came)
ramacharitamanas::1180.speaker: Janaka
ramacharitamanas::1180.essence: Beauty can reveal the supreme reality before words can explain it.
ramacharitamanas::1180.simple_meaning: Janaka is overwhelmed by Rama and Lakshmana's beauty and wonders who they really are. He suspects they may be the supreme reality itself appearing in human form.
ramacharitamanas::1180.simple_insight: A pure heart can look at beauty and feel reverence before it can name it.
ramacharitamanas::1180.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court at Sita's swayamvar, Rama and Lakshmana enter and everyone is stunned by their radiance. Janaka, moved beyond ordinary speech, asks whether these boys are royal protectors or the supreme reality itself come in two forms.
ramacharitamanas::1180.modern_relevance: You meet someone and their calm, dignity, and grace stop your mind cold. Before you can categorize them, something in you recognizes depth and bows.
ramacharitamanas::1180.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to sacred presence, teaching the mind to recognize greatness before analysis.

ramacharitamanas::1181.verse_sanskrit: सहज बिरागरूप मनु मोरा। थकित होत जिमि चंद चकोरा॥ ताते प्रभु पूछउँ सतिभाऊ। कहहु नाथ जनि करहु दुराऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1181.verse_hindi: मेरा मन जो स्वभाव से ही वैराग्य रूप (बना हुआ) है, (इन्हें देखकर) इस तरह मुग्ध हो रहा है, जैसे चन्द्रमा को देखकर चकोर। हे प्रभो! इसलिए मैं आपसे सत्य (निश्छल) भाव से पूछता हूँ। हे नाथ! बताइए, छिपाव न कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1181.english_translation: My mind is naturally turned toward detachment, yet it becomes captivated like a chakora before the moon. Therefore, Lord, I ask you with complete sincerity. O Master, do not hide the truth.
ramacharitamanas::1181.translation_literal: सहज (natural) / बिरागरूप (in the form of detachment) / मनु (mind) / मोरा (my) / थकित होत (becomes weary/captivated) / जिमि (like) / चंद (moon) / चकोरा (chakora bird) / ताते (therefore) / प्रभु (Lord) / पूछउँ (I ask) / सतिभाऊ (with true sincerity) / कहहु (tell) / नाथ (Master) / जनि (do not) / करहु (do) / दुराऊ (concealment)
ramacharitamanas::1181.speaker: Janaka
ramacharitamanas::1181.essence: Detachment can still bow before what is truly radiant.
ramacharitamanas::1181.simple_meaning: Janaka says his mind is usually detached, yet the sight of the two boys has overwhelmed him. He asks the teacher to answer honestly and without hiding anything.
ramacharitamanas::1181.simple_insight: Even a disciplined mind can be moved by wonder. Honest questioning is part of wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::1181.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court at the Sita swayamvar, the king has just seen the two extraordinary boys. His normally detached mind is shaken by their beauty and presence, so he asks the sage plainly to tell the truth. This is the moment when reverence turns into inquiry.
ramacharitamanas::1181.modern_relevance: You thought you had a situation figured out, then one unexpected encounter unsettles everything. Instead of pretending certainty, you ask the hard question directly.
ramacharitamanas::1181.insight: It shifts the mind from polished certainty to sincere inquiry when experience breaks the old frame.

ramacharitamanas::1182.verse_sanskrit: इन्हहि बिलोकत अति अनुरागा। बरबस ब्रह्मसुखहि मन त्यागा॥ कह मुनि बिहसि कहेहु नृप नीका। बचन तुम्हार न होइ अलीका ॥
ramacharitamanas::1182.verse_hindi: इनको देखते ही अत्यन्त प्रेम के वश होकर मेरे मन ने जबर्दस्ती ब्रह्मसुख को त्याग दिया है। मुनि ने हँसकर कहा- हे राजन् ! आपने ठीक (यथार्थ ही) कहा। आपका वचन मिथ्या नहीं हो सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1182.english_translation: Looking at them, my heart was overwhelmed with love and forcibly gave up the bliss of Brahman. The sage laughed and said, "You speak rightly, O king. Your words cannot be false."
ramacharitamanas::1182.translation_literal: इन्हहि (these) / बिलोकत (seeing) / अति (greatly) / अनुरागा (filled with love) / बरबस (forcibly) / ब्रह्मसुखहि (the bliss of Brahman) / मन (mind) / त्यागा (gave up) ॥ कह (said) / मुनि (the sage) / बिहसि (smiling) / कहेहु (you said) / नृप (O king) / नीका (well/rightly) / बचन (words) / तुम्हार (your) / न (not) / होइ (be) / अलीका (false) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1182.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1182.essence: Love for Ram can outweigh even the bliss of Brahman.
ramacharitamanas::1182.simple_meaning: Seeing the two boys, the sage becomes so moved by love that even the highest spiritual bliss feels secondary. He confirms that the king has spoken truly.
ramacharitamanas::1182.simple_insight: Love can be so complete that even the highest inner peace no longer feels separate from it.
ramacharitamanas::1182.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the sage sees Ram and Lakshman and is overwhelmed. Their presence pulls his heart beyond abstract spiritual stillness into living love. He smiles and tells King Janak that such a response is natural and true.
ramacharitamanas::1182.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence makes the room feel different, and all your polished detachment suddenly looks thin. Some recognitions are stronger than theory.
ramacharitamanas::1182.insight: It shifts devotion from an idea into an experience that can outshine even spiritual achievement.

ramacharitamanas::1183.verse_sanskrit: ए प्रिय सबहि जहाँ लगि प्रानी। मन मुसुकाहिं रामु सुनि बानी॥ रघुकुल मनि दसरथ के जाए। मम हित लागि नरेस पठाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1183.verse_hindi: जगत में जहाँ तक (जितने भी) प्राणी हैं, ये सभी को प्रिय हैं। मुनि की (रहस्य भरी) वाणी सुनकर श्री रामजी मन ही मन मुस्कुराते हैं (हँसकर मानो संकेत करते हैं कि रहस्य खोलिए नहीं)। (तब मुनि ने कहा-) ये रघुकुल मणि महाराज दशरथ के पुत्र हैं। मेरे हित के लिए राजा ने इन्हें मेरे साथ भेजा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1183.english_translation: All beings in the world are dear to him. Hearing the sage's veiled words, Ram smiles inwardly. Then the sage says, "He is the jewel of Raghu's line, the son of King Dasharath. The king has sent him with me for my welfare."
ramacharitamanas::1183.translation_literal: ए (these) / प्रिय (dear) / सबहि (to all) / जहाँ लगि (as far as) / प्रानी (living beings) / मन (mind) / मुसुकाहिं (smile) / रामु (Ram) / सुनि (hearing) / बानी (speech) / रघुकुल मनि (jewel of Raghu's clan) / दसरथ के जाए (born to Dasharath) / मम हित लागि (for my welfare) / नरेस (king) / पठाए (sent)
ramacharitamanas::1183.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1183.essence: Recognition turns an ordinary meeting into a sacred unveiling.
ramacharitamanas::1183.simple_meaning: Ram is dear to every living being. The sage then identifies him as Dasharath's son, sent for the sage's welfare.
ramacharitamanas::1183.simple_insight: There is quiet joy in being recognized for what you truly are.
ramacharitamanas::1183.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sage first hints at Ram's hidden identity and Ram smiles at the playful secrecy. Then the sage openly names him: the jewel of Raghu's line, Dasharath's son, sent here for the sage's welfare. The moment confirms Ram's presence without yet revealing his full divinity.
ramacharitamanas::1183.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a gathering who seems ordinary, then a shared friend quietly reveals who they are. The room changes, but the person has not.
ramacharitamanas::1183.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to recognition, showing how a name can uncover hidden stature.

ramacharitamanas::1184.verse_sanskrit: रामु लखनु दोउ बंधुबर रूप सील बल धाम। मख राखेउ सबु साखि जगु जिते असुर संग्राम ॥
ramacharitamanas::1184.verse_hindi: ये राम और लक्ष्मण दोनों श्रेष्ठ भाई रूप, शील और बल के धाम हैं। सारा जगत (इस बात का) साक्षी है कि इन्होंने युद्ध में असुरों को जीतकर मेरे यज्ञ की रक्षा की है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1184.english_translation: Ram and Lakshman, the two noble brothers, are abodes of beauty, character, and strength. The whole world is witness that they protected my sacrifice and defeated the demons in battle.
ramacharitamanas::1184.translation_literal: रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / दोउ (both) / बंधुबर (noble brothers) / रूप (beauty) / सील (character) / बल (strength) / धाम (abode) / मख (sacrifice) / राखेउ (protected) / सबु (all) / साखि (witness) / जगु (world) / जिते (defeated) / असुर (demons) / संग्राम (battle)
ramacharitamanas::1184.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1184.essence: Their beauty matters because it is backed by courage and protection.
ramacharitamanas::1184.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are praised as noble, beautiful, strong brothers who protected the sage's sacrifice and defeated hostile forces.
ramacharitamanas::1184.simple_insight: True greatness shows itself by protecting what is sacred and standing firm under pressure.
ramacharitamanas::1184.detailed_meaning: At the sage's sacrifice, the king speaks after seeing Ram and Lakshman. He praises them as the finest of brothers and points to a public fact: they defended the ritual and overcame the hostile forces that threatened it.
ramacharitamanas::1184.modern_relevance: A parent watches two siblings quietly step in when a family crisis hits. No speech is needed — everyone sees who protected the home when it mattered.
ramacharitamanas::1184.insight: It shifts attention from appearance alone to the proof of character found in action.

ramacharitamanas::1185.verse_sanskrit: मुनि तव चरन देखि कह राऊ। कहि न सकउँ निज पुन्य प्रभाऊ॥ सुंदर स्याम गौर दोउ भ्राता। आनँदहू के आनँद दाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1185.verse_hindi: राजा ने कहा- हे मुनि! आपके चरणों के दर्शन कर मैं अपना पुण्य प्रभाव कह नहीं सकता। ये सुंदर श्याम और गौर वर्ण के दोनों भाई आनंद को भी आनंद देने वाले हैं।
ramacharitamanas::1185.english_translation: The king said, “O sage, seeing your feet, I cannot describe the power of my own merit. These beautiful dark and fair brothers are givers of joy even to joy itself.”
ramacharitamanas::1185.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / तव (your) / चरन (feet) / देखि (seeing) / कह (said) / राऊ (the king) / कहि (to say) / न (not) / सकउँ (I can) / निज (my own) / पुन्य (merit) / प्रभाऊ (power, influence) / सुंदर (beautiful) / स्याम (dark-blue) / गौर (fair) / दोउ (both) / भ्राता (brothers) / आनँदहू (even of joy) / के (of) / आनँद (joy) / दाता (givers)
ramacharitamanas::1185.speaker: Janak
ramacharitamanas::1185.essence: Their presence makes joy feel larger than joy.
ramacharitamanas::1185.simple_meaning: Janak bows before the sage and praises Ram and Lakshman as brothers whose presence deepens joy itself.
ramacharitamanas::1185.simple_insight: Real reverence sees greatness in others and becomes quieter, softer, and more grateful.
ramacharitamanas::1185.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, King Janak stands before the sage and speaks with humility. Looking at the two brothers, Ram and Lakshman, he feels that even joy is heightened by their presence. The scene builds devotion before the marriage of Sita.
ramacharitamanas::1185.modern_relevance: You meet someone so steady and gracious that your own pride drops away. Around them, even a happy room feels more alive.
ramacharitamanas::1185.insight: It shifts attention from self-importance to reverent recognition of true greatness.

ramacharitamanas::1186.verse_sanskrit: इन्ह कै प्रीति परसपर पावनि। कहि न जाइ मन भाव सुहावनि॥ सुनहु नाथ कह मुदित बिदेहू। ब्रह्म जीव इव सहज सनेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1186.verse_hindi: इनकी आपस की प्रीति बड़ी पवित्र और सुहावनी है, वह मन को बहुत भाती है, पर (वाणी से) कही नहीं जा सकती। विदेह (जनकजी) आनंदित होकर कहते हैं- हे नाथ! सुनिए, ब्रह्म और जीव की तरह इनमें स्वाभाविक प्रेम है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1186.english_translation: Their mutual love is pure and delightful. It cannot be spoken; it pleases the mind deeply. Listen, lord, says Janaka joyfully: their natural affection is like Brahman and the individual being.
ramacharitamanas::1186.translation_literal: इन्ह कै (of these) / प्रीति (love) / परसपर (mutual) / पावनि (pure, purifying) / कहि न जाइ (cannot be said) / मन (mind) / भाव (pleasing) / सुहावनि (delightful) / सुनहु (listen) / नाथ (lord) / कह (said) / मुदित (joyful) / बिदेहू (Janaka) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / जीव (individual being) / इव (like) / सहज (natural) / सनेहू (affection)
ramacharitamanas::1186.speaker: Janaka
ramacharitamanas::1186.essence: True affection needs no explanation; it reveals a deeper unity already there.
ramacharitamanas::1186.simple_meaning: Janaka says Ram and Lakshman share a love that is pure, beautiful, and beyond words. He compares their natural bond to the relation between the supreme reality and the individual being.
ramacharitamanas::1186.simple_insight: Some bonds feel so complete that language can only point at them, not contain them.
ramacharitamanas::1186.detailed_meaning: Janaka stands before Ram and Lakshman after seeing their grace and brotherly closeness. Overjoyed, he says their affection is pure, pleasing, and impossible to describe, then lifts the moment into a spiritual comparison: their bond is as natural as Brahman and the individual being.
ramacharitamanas::1186.modern_relevance: You watch two siblings protect each other at a family wedding, without a single dramatic speech. Everyone feels it. Some loyalties are so natural they make explanation unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::1186.insight: It shifts attention from spoken sentiment to the quiet evidence of a bond that needs no performance.

ramacharitamanas::1187.verse_sanskrit: पुनि पुनि प्रभुहि चितव नरनाहू। पुलक गात उर अधिक उछाहू॥ मुनिहि प्रसंसि नाइ पद सीसू। चलेउ लवाइ नगर अवनीसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1187.verse_hindi: राजा बार-बार प्रभु को देखते हैं (दृष्टि वहाँ से हटना ही नहीं चाहती)। (प्रेम से) शरीर पुलकित हो रहा है और हृदय में बड़ा उत्साह है। (फिर) मुनि की प्रशंसा करके और उनके चरणों में सिर नवाकर राजा उन्हें नगर में लिवा चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1187.english_translation: The king kept looking at the Lord again and again. His body thrilled with joy, and his heart overflowed with eagerness. Then he praised the sage, bowed his head at the sage's feet, and led him toward the city.
ramacharitamanas::1187.translation_literal: पुनि पुनि (again and again) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / चितव (looked at) / नरनाहू (the king) / पुलक (goosebumps, thrill) / गात (body) / उर (heart) / अधिक (more) / उछाहू (eagerness, joy) / मुनिहि (the sage) / प्रसंसि (praising) / नाइ (bowing) / पद (feet) / सीसू (head) / चलेउ (went) / लवाइ (leading along) / नगर (city) / अवनीसू (the king of the earth)
ramacharitamanas::1187.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1187.essence: True admiration keeps returning to its source.
ramacharitamanas::1187.simple_meaning: The king cannot stop looking at Ram. Joy rises in his body and heart, and after honoring the sage, he leads him toward the city.
ramacharitamanas::1187.simple_insight: Love makes reverence natural. The heart bows first, and the body follows.
ramacharitamanas::1187.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, King Janaka is still overwhelmed after seeing Ram and Lakshman. He keeps turning back to look at Ram, then honors the sage who brought them, bows low, and escorts him into the city. The scene shows devotion overflowing into action.
ramacharitamanas::1187.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence changes the room, and you keep glancing back even after the conversation ends. Respect turns into hospitality before you even plan it.
ramacharitamanas::1187.insight: It shifts attention from formal duty to heartfelt welcome and visible reverence.

ramacharitamanas::1188.verse_sanskrit: सुंदर सदनु सुखद सब काला। तहाँ बासु लै दीन्ह भुआला॥ करि पूजा सब बिधि सेवकाई। गयउ राउ गृह बिदा कराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1188.verse_hindi: एक सुंदर महल जो सब समय (सभी ऋतुओं में) सुखदायक था, वहाँ राजा ने उन्हें ले जाकर ठहराया। तदनन्तर सब प्रकार से पूजा और सेवा करके राजा विदा माँगकर अपने घर गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1188.english_translation: A beautiful hall, pleasant in every season, was arranged for them there. The king offered every kind of worship and service, then took leave and returned home.
ramacharitamanas::1188.translation_literal: सुंदर (beautiful) / सदनु (dwelling, hall) / सुखद (pleasant) / सब (all) / काला (times, seasons) / तहाँ (there) / बासु (residence) / लै (taking) / दीन्ह (gave) / भुआला (the king) / करि (doing) / पूजा (worship) / सब बिधि (in every way) / सेवकाई (service) / गयउ (went) / राउ (king) / गृह (home) / बिदा (leave) / कराई (having asked for)
ramacharitamanas::1188.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1188.essence: True honor serves completely and then withdraws gracefully.
ramacharitamanas::1188.simple_meaning: The king arranged comfortable lodging for Ram and Lakshman, honored them properly, and then left after asking permission.
ramacharitamanas::1188.simple_insight: Respect is shown through care, not just words.
ramacharitamanas::1188.detailed_meaning: Janak has brought Ram and Lakshman into a beautiful residence suited for every season. He serves them with full honor, then asks leave and returns home. The verse is a courteous transition, not the main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1188.modern_relevance: A host sets out clean sheets, water, and food before guests arrive, then steps back without making a scene. Real respect knows when to serve and when to leave space.
ramacharitamanas::1188.insight: It models dignified hospitality: provide fully, honor properly, and do not cling to attention.

ramacharitamanas::1189.verse_sanskrit: रिषय संग रघुबंस मनि करि भोजनु बिश्रामु। बैठे प्रभु भ्राता सहित दिवसु रहा भरि जामु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1189.verse_hindi: रघुकुल के शिरोमणि प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ऋषियों के साथ भोजन और विश्राम करके भाई लक्ष्मण समेत बैठे। उस समय पहरभर दिन रह गया था ॥
ramacharitamanas::1189.english_translation: Rama, jewel of the Raghu line, ate and rested with the sages. He sat with Lakshmana, and then a quarter of the day remained.
ramacharitamanas::1189.translation_literal: रिषय (with the sages) / संग (together) / रघुबंस मनि (jewel of the Raghu line) / करि (having done) / भोजनु (food) / बिश्रामु (rest) / बैठे (sat) / प्रभु (the Lord) / भ्राता (brother) / सहित (together with) / दिवसु (the day) / रहा (remained) / भरि जामु (a quarter of the day)
ramacharitamanas::1189.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1189.essence: Peace can live inside the simplest shared meal.
ramacharitamanas::1189.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshmana eat, rest, and sit with the sages. The day is already passing, so the scene pauses before the next event.
ramacharitamanas::1189.simple_insight: Even a brief rest can carry quiet dignity when it is shared in the right company.
ramacharitamanas::1189.detailed_meaning: After the sages host Ram and Lakshmana, the two brothers eat and rest among them. The day is moving on, and the poem lingers on this peaceful pause before the next turn in the journey.
ramacharitamanas::1189.modern_relevance: After a long drive, you finally sit down at a friend's house, eat something simple, and let the noise of the day fall away. Not every sacred moment is dramatic.
ramacharitamanas::1189.insight: It teaches you to notice the holiness of ordinary rest and companionship before the next demand arrives.

ramacharitamanas::1190.verse_sanskrit: लखन हृदयँ लालसा बिसेषी। जाइ जनकपुर आइअ देखी॥ प्रभु भय बहुरि मुनिहि सकुचाहीं। प्रगट न कहहिं मनहिं मुसुकाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1190.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी के हृदय में विशेष लालसा है कि जाकर जनकपुर देख आवें, परन्तु प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी का डर है और फिर मुनि से भी सकुचाते हैं, इसलिए प्रकट में कुछ नहीं कहते, मन ही मन मुस्कुरा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1190.english_translation: Lakshman has a strong desire in his heart to go see Janakpur, but he feels shy before Lord Ram and even before the sage, so he says nothing openly and smiles to himself.
ramacharitamanas::1190.translation_literal: लखन (Lakshman) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / लालसा (desire, longing) / बिसेषी (great, special) / जाइ (going) / जनकपुर (Janakpur) / आइअ (coming) / देखी (to see)॥ प्रभु (the Lord) / भय (fear) / बहुरि (again) / मुनिहि (before the sage) / सकुचाहीं (they feel shy) / प्रगट (openly) / न (not) / कहहिं (say) / मनहिं (in the mind) / मुसुकाहीं (they smile) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1190.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1190.essence: Desire can remain alive even when respect keeps it silent.
ramacharitamanas::1190.simple_meaning: Lakshman wants to see Janakpur, but he is too shy to ask openly. He keeps the wish in his heart and smiles quietly.
ramacharitamanas::1190.simple_insight: Some desires stay unspoken because respect is stronger than impulse.
ramacharitamanas::1190.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and the sages are staying near Janakpur during the Sita-swayamvar period. Lakshman feels a strong wish to see the city, but he hesitates out of reverence for Ram and modesty before the sage. The verse simply shows that quiet inner restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1190.modern_relevance: You want to ask for the extra day off, but your manager is already overloaded and you hold back. The wish is real; the restraint is real too.
ramacharitamanas::1190.insight: It shows a feeling being contained by reverence, not erased by it.

ramacharitamanas::1191.verse_sanskrit: राम अनुज मन की गति जानी। भगत बछलता हियँ हुलसानी॥ परम बिनीत सकुचि मुसुकाई। बोले गुर अनुसासन पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1191.verse_hindi: (अन्तर्यामी) श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने छोटे भाई के मन की दशा जान ली, (तब) उनके हृदय में भक्तवत्सलता उमड़ आई। वे गुरु की आज्ञा पाकर बहुत ही विनय के साथ सकुचाते हुए मुस्कुराकर बोले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1191.english_translation: Ram knew his younger brother's wish. His heart overflowed with love for a devotee. With deep humility, he smiled shyly and spoke after receiving the teacher's permission.
ramacharitamanas::1191.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / अनुज (younger brother) / मन (mind) / की गति (the movement/state of) / जानी (knew) / भगत बछलता (devotion-loving tenderness) / हियँ (in the heart) / हुलसानी (overflowed with joy) / परम (very) / बिनीत (humble) / सकुचि (with modest hesitation) / मुसुकाई (smiled) / बोले (spoke) / गुर (the teacher) / अनुसासन (permission/instruction) / पाई (having received)
ramacharitamanas::1191.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1191.essence: True love notices desire before it becomes speech.
ramacharitamanas::1191.simple_meaning: Ram understands Lakshman's unspoken wish and responds with affectionate humility. He smiles gently and speaks only after receiving his teacher's permission.
ramacharitamanas::1191.simple_insight: Being deeply attentive lets love answer before words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1191.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Lakshman longs to see Janakpur, but he hesitates to ask. Ram notices the wish in his younger brother's heart. Moved by devotion and guided by the teacher's order, he answers with gentle humility.
ramacharitamanas::1191.modern_relevance: A younger sibling keeps hinting they want something but won't ask directly. You notice, soften first, and respond without making them feel small.
ramacharitamanas::1191.insight: It teaches you to notice unspoken needs and answer with humility instead of self-importance.

ramacharitamanas::1192.verse_sanskrit: नाथ लखनु पुरु देखन चहहीं। प्रभु सकोच डर प्रगट न कहहीं॥ जौं राउर आयसु मैं पावौं। नगर देखाइ तुरत लै आवौं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1192.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! लक्ष्मण नगर देखना चाहते हैं, किन्तु प्रभु (आप) के डर और संकोच के कारण स्पष्ट नहीं कहते। यदि आपकी आज्ञा पाऊँ, तो मैं इनको नगर दिखलाकर तुरंत ही (वापस) ले आऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1192.english_translation: Lord, Lakshman wants to see the city, but out of respect and fear of you, he does not say it openly. If I receive your order, I will show him the city and bring him back at once.
ramacharitamanas::1192.translation_literal: नाथ (lord) / लखनु (Lakshman) / पुरु (city) / देखन (to see) / चहहीं (wants) / प्रभु (lord) / सकोच (hesitation) / डर (fear) / प्रगट (openly) / न (not) / कहहीं (says) / जौं (if) / राउर (your) / आयसु (order) / मैं (I) / पावौं (receive) / नगर (city) / देखाइ (showing) / तुरत (at once) / लै (taking) / आवौं (bring back)
ramacharitamanas::1192.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1192.essence: True service notices the wish before it is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1192.simple_meaning: Lakshman wants to see the city, but he is too respectful to ask directly. The speaker offers to take him there only if ordered to do so.
ramacharitamanas::1192.simple_insight: Care can be quiet and obedient. Even a small wish waits for the right permission.
ramacharitamanas::1192.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the moment is delicate. Lakshman wants to see the city, but he will not speak boldly before Ram. The speaker steps in with humility, offering to arrange it only if Ram permits.
ramacharitamanas::1192.modern_relevance: You want to ask for something simple, but you hesitate because the room feels too formal. A respectful person notices the need and makes space for it without forcing the issue.
ramacharitamanas::1192.insight: It shows how service listens for unspoken needs and waits for permission before acting.

ramacharitamanas::1193.verse_sanskrit: सुनि मुनीसु कह बचन सप्रीती। कस न राम तुम्ह राखहु नीती॥ धरम सेतु पालक तुम्ह ताता। प्रेम बिबस सेवक सुखदाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1193.verse_hindi: यह सुनकर मुनीश्वर विश्वामित्रजी ने प्रेम सहित वचन कहे- हे राम! तुम नीति की रक्षा कैसे न करोगे, हे तात! तुम धर्म की मर्यादा का पालन करने वाले और प्रेम के वशीभूत होकर सेवकों को सुख देने वाले हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1193.english_translation: Hearing this, the sage Vishvamitra spoke with affection: “Why would you not uphold righteous conduct, Ram? You are the guardian of dharma, dear one, and you are bound by love to give joy to your servants.”
ramacharitamanas::1193.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / मुनीसु (the sage) / कह (said) / बचन (words) / सप्रीती (with affection) / कस (how) / न (not) / राम (Ram) / तुम्ह (you) / राखहु (uphold/keep) / नीती (righteous conduct)॥ / धरम (dharma) / सेतु (bridge) / पालक (guardian) / तुम्ह (you) / ताता (dear one) / प्रेम (love) / बिबस (under the power of) / सेवक (servants/devotees) / सुखदाता (giver of joy) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1193.speaker: Vishvamitra
ramacharitamanas::1193.essence: True righteousness protects others and still remains tender.
ramacharitamanas::1193.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra praises Ram as someone who naturally protects righteousness and brings happiness to those who serve him.
ramacharitamanas::1193.simple_insight: It feels safe to trust a presence that never bends away from what is right.
ramacharitamanas::1193.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has just seen the tenderness between Ram and Lakshman. Moved by that scene, he speaks with affection, praising Ram as the protector of righteous conduct and the one who gives comfort to devoted servants.
ramacharitamanas::1193.modern_relevance: A younger colleague quietly covers for everyone, refuses shortcuts, and still treats the team kindly. You notice that real strength is not coldness — it is the steadiness to do right while staying warm.
ramacharitamanas::1193.insight: It shifts respect toward people whose kindness does not weaken their standards.

ramacharitamanas::1194.verse_sanskrit: जाइ देखि आवहु नगरु सुख निधान दोउ भाइ। करहु सुफल सब के नयन सुंदर बदन देखाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1194.verse_hindi: सुख के निधान दोनों भाई जाकर नगर देख आओ। अपने सुंदर मुख दिखलाकर सब (नगर निवासियों) के नेत्रों को सफल करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1194.english_translation: Go and see the city, both brothers, treasure of joy. Show your beautiful faces and make everyone's eyes fruitful.
ramacharitamanas::1194.translation_literal: जाइ (going) / देखि (seeing) / आवहु (come back) / नगरु (city) / सुख निधान (treasure of joy) / दोउ (both) / भाइ (brothers) / करहु (do) / सुफल (fruitful, fulfilled) / सब (all) / के (of) / नयन (eyes) / सुंदर (beautiful) / बदन (faces) / देखाइ (showing)
ramacharitamanas::1194.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1194.essence: Their beauty blesses every pair of eyes that sees them.
ramacharitamanas::1194.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman should go into the city, let people see them, and feel their eyes fulfilled by the sight of their beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1194.simple_insight: Some presence itself is a blessing. Beauty and goodness can quiet a whole crowd without a single speech.
ramacharitamanas::1194.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Vishwamitra has brought Ram and Lakshman to the city before the swayamvar. After asking them to walk through and be seen, he frames their presence as a gift to everyone watching. This verse simply invites that public viewing.
ramacharitamanas::1194.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after months away, and the whole place turns to look. Sometimes the kindest thing you can do is simply arrive fully and let people feel your presence.
ramacharitamanas::1194.insight: It shifts attention from performing to appearing fully, letting goodness be received rather than announced.

ramacharitamanas::1195.verse_sanskrit: मुनि पद कमल बंदि दोउ भ्राता। चले लोक लोचन सुख दाता॥ बालक बृंद देखि अति सोभा। लगे संग लोचन मनु लोभा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1195.verse_hindi: सब लोकों के नेत्रों को सुख देने वाले दोनों भाई मुनि के चरणकमलों की वंदना करके चले। बालकों के झुंड इन (के सौंदर्य) की अत्यन्त शोभा देखकर साथ लग गए। उनके नेत्र और मन (इनकी माधुरी पर) लुभा गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1195.english_translation: After bowing to the sage’s lotus feet, the two brothers set out. Seeing the beauty of the children, the boys gathered around, and eyes and minds were drawn to them.
ramacharitamanas::1195.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / बंदि (bowing) / दोउ (both) / भ्राता (brothers) / चले (went) / लोक (world) / लोचन (eyes) / सुख (joy) / दाता (giver) / बालक (children) / बृंद (group) / देखि (seeing) / अति (very) / सोभा (beauty) / लगे (began) / संग (together) / लोचन (eyes) / मनु (mind) / लोभा (attracted)
ramacharitamanas::1195.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1195.essence: Beauty grounded in humility quietly gathers every eye.
ramacharitamanas::1195.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman bow to the sage and walk on. Their beauty is so striking that children gather around them, unable to look away.
ramacharitamanas::1195.simple_insight: True presence draws people naturally. You do not need to announce beauty when it is already alive.
ramacharitamanas::1195.detailed_meaning: Worlds of forest and court have met around Vishwamitra’s guidance. Ram and Lakshman leave after bowing to the sage, and their grace is so radiant that even children are pulled toward them. This is scene-setting before the next movement.
ramacharitamanas::1195.modern_relevance: You walk into a crowded station, and the noise shifts for a second because someone calm and kind has entered. No speech, no performance — just a presence people trust.
ramacharitamanas::1195.insight: It keeps attention on the brothers’ visible grace, not on any teaching. The verse functions as a bridge into the next scene.

ramacharitamanas::1196.verse_sanskrit: पीत बसन परिकर कटि भाथा। चारु चाप सर सोहत हाथा॥ तन अनुहरत सुचंदन खोरी। स्यामल गौर मनोहर जोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1196.verse_hindi: (दोनों भाइयों के) पीले रंग के वस्त्र हैं, कमर के (पीले) दुपट्टों में तरकस बँधे हैं। हाथों में सुंदर धनुष-बाण सुशोभित हैं। (श्याम और गौर वर्ण के) शरीरों के अनुकूल (अर्थात् जिस पर जिस रंग का चंदन अधिक फबे उस पर उसी रंग के) सुंदर चंदन की खौर लगी है। साँवरे और गोरे (रंग) की मनोहर जोड़ी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1196.english_translation: They wear yellow garments, with quivers tied at their waists. Beautiful bows and arrows shine in their hands. Their bodies are adorned with sandal paste suited to their complexions. Dark and fair, they form a lovely pair.
ramacharitamanas::1196.translation_literal: पीत (yellow) / बसन (garments) / परिकर (waist-belt, quiver support) / कटि (waist) / भाथा (quiver) / चारु (beautiful) / चाप (bow) / सर (arrows) / सोहत (shining) / हाथा (hands)॥ / तन (body) / अनुहरत (suited to, fitting) / सुचंदन (fine sandal paste) / खोरी (mark, paste) / स्यामल (dark-complexioned) / गौर (fair-complexioned) / मनोहर (lovely) / जोरी (pair)॥
ramacharitamanas::1196.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1196.essence: Their beauty is inseparable from their readiness.
ramacharitamanas::1196.simple_meaning: The two brothers are dressed beautifully, armed with bows and arrows, and marked with sandal paste that suits their dark and fair complexions.
ramacharitamanas::1196.simple_insight: Beauty and readiness can live together. Even in calm grace, they are prepared for duty.
ramacharitamanas::1196.detailed_meaning: The two brothers have just entered the city after bowing to the sage. The crowd is drinking in their beauty. This verse lingers on their appearance — yellow clothes, quivers, bows, arrows, sandal paste, dark and fair forms — before the people’s wonder turns into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1196.modern_relevance: You see two siblings step out together before a ceremony, one in deep blue, one in light cream, both composed and ready. The room notices their presence before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1196.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary appearance to embodied readiness — grace that is already armed for action.

ramacharitamanas::1197.verse_sanskrit: केहरि कंधर बाहु बिसाला। उर अति रुचिर नागमनि माला॥ सुभग सोन सरसीरुह लोचन। बदन मयंक तापत्रय मोचन ॥
ramacharitamanas::1197.verse_hindi: सिंह के समान (पुष्ट) गर्दन (गले का पिछला भाग) है, विशाल भुजाएँ हैं। (चौड़ी) छाती पर अत्यन्त सुंदर गजमुक्ता की माला है। सुंदर लाल कमल के समान नेत्र हैं। तीनों तापों से छुड़ाने वाला चन्द्रमा के समान मुख है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1197.english_translation: His neck is strong like a lion's, and his arms are broad. A splendid pearl necklace rests on his chest. His eyes are beautiful like red lotuses, and his face is like the moon that removes the threefold suffering.
ramacharitamanas::1197.translation_literal: केहरि (lion) / कंधर (neck) / बाहु (arms) / बिसाला (broad, विशाल) / उर (chest) / अति (very) / रुचिर (beautiful) / नागमनि (pearl / gem) / माला (garland) / सुभग (lovely) / सोन (golden, red-gold) / सरसीरुह (lotus) / लोचन (eyes) / बदन (face) / मयंक (moon) / तापत्रय (threefold suffering) / मोचन (remover, liberator)
ramacharitamanas::1197.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1197.essence: Ram's beauty is strength that soothes suffering.
ramacharitamanas::1197.simple_meaning: Ram's body is described as noble and radiant, with a strong neck, broad arms, lotus-like eyes, and a moonlike face that brings relief from suffering.
ramacharitamanas::1197.simple_insight: Beauty here is not decoration; it carries comfort, dignity, and mercy.
ramacharitamanas::1197.detailed_meaning: The poet is still describing Ram and Lakshman as they move through the scene after honoring the sage. This verse lingers on Ram's physical radiance—his strength, beauty, and soothing presence—before the next verse turns to the charm of his glance.
ramacharitamanas::1197.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm presence changes the whole room before they even speak. Their steadiness feels like relief, not performance.
ramacharitamanas::1197.insight: It shifts attention from mere appearance to presence that heals and steadies others.

ramacharitamanas::1198.verse_sanskrit: कानन्हि कनक फूल छबि देहीं। चितवत चितहि चोरि जनु लेहीं॥ चितवनि चारु भृकुटि बर बाँकी। तिलक रेख सोभा जनु चाँकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1198.verse_hindi: कानों में सोने के कर्णफूल (अत्यन्त) शोभा दे रहे हैं और देखते ही (देखने वाले के) चित्त को मानो चुरा लेते हैं। उनकी चितवन (दृष्टि) बड़ी मनोहर है और भौंहें तिरछी एवं सुंदर हैं। (माथे पर) तिलक की रेखाएँ ऐसी सुंदर हैं, मानो (मूर्तिमती) शोभा पर मुहर लगा दी गई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1198.english_translation: Gold earrings brighten their beauty and seem to steal the viewer’s mind. Their gaze is lovely, their brows are gracefully curved, and the tilak on their foreheads seems to seal their beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1198.translation_literal: कानन्हि (in the ears) / कनक (gold) / फूल (flowers; earrings) / छबि (beauty) / देहीं (give) / चितवत (while looking) / चितहि (the mind) / चोरि (stealing) / जनु (as if) / लेहीं (take away) / चितवनि (gaze) / चारु (beautiful) / भृकुटि (eyebrows) / बर (excellent) / बाँकी (curved) / तिलक रेख (tilak line) / सोभा (beauty) / जनु (as if) / चाँकी (sealed; stamped)
ramacharitamanas::1198.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1198.essence: Beauty can seize the mind before the mind knows what happened.
ramacharitamanas::1198.simple_meaning: The brothers are described as breathtakingly beautiful. Their ornaments, gaze, brows, and forehead mark all heighten their charm.
ramacharitamanas::1198.simple_insight: Some beauty does not just please the eye; it quietly takes hold of the mind.
ramacharitamanas::1198.detailed_meaning: In Sita’s swayamvar scene, the two brothers stand out in full royal splendor. Their earrings, gaze, brows, and tilak are described one by one, not to teach a doctrine, but to deepen the reader’s sense of their radiant presence before the contest begins.
ramacharitamanas::1198.modern_relevance: You notice someone walk into a room and the whole atmosphere shifts before a word is spoken. The details are small, but the presence is unmistakable.
ramacharitamanas::1198.insight: It slows the mind down to notice how form, posture, and expression carry meaning before speech begins.

ramacharitamanas::1199.verse_sanskrit: रुचिर चौतनीं सुभग सिर मेचक कुंचित केस। नख सिख सुंदर बंधु दोउ सोभा सकल सुदेस ॥
ramacharitamanas::1199.verse_hindi: सिर पर सुंदर चौकोनी टोपियाँ (दिए) हैं, काले और घुँघराले बाल हैं। दोनों भाई नख से लेकर शिखा तक (एड़ी से चोटी तक) सुंदर हैं और सारी शोभा जहाँ जैसी चाहिए वैसी ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1199.english_translation: Both brothers are beautiful from head to toe, with dark curly hair and lovely square caps on their heads. Their beauty fits every place perfectly.
ramacharitamanas::1199.translation_literal: रुचिर (beautiful) / चौतनीं (square caps) / सुभग (lovely) / सिर (head) / मेचक (dark) / कुंचित (curly) / केस (hair) / नख (nails) / सिख (top / crown) / सुंदर (beautiful) / बंधु (brothers) / दोउ (both) / सोभा (beauty) / सकल (all) / सुदेस (fit each place well)
ramacharitamanas::1199.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1199.essence: Complete beauty needs no extra ornament.
