ramacharitamanas::1199.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are described as beautiful from head to toe. Their appearance is graceful, complete, and fitting in every way.
ramacharitamanas::1199.simple_insight: A truly noble presence needs no introduction. Beauty, when complete, speaks for itself.
ramacharitamanas::1199.detailed_meaning: The two princes have entered the scene in Ayodhya, and the poet pauses to describe them before the city reacts. Their dark curls, fine caps, and flawless beauty are part of the wonder that will draw everyone toward them.
ramacharitamanas::1199.modern_relevance: You notice someone walk into a room and the whole atmosphere changes before they speak. Their calm, complete presence makes everyone look up.
ramacharitamanas::1199.insight: It shifts attention from action to presence, showing how wholeness can command attention without effort.

ramacharitamanas::1200.verse_sanskrit: देखन नगरु भूपसुत आए। समाचार पुरबासिन्ह पाए॥ धाए धाम काम सब त्यागी। मनहुँ रंक निधि लूटन लागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1200.verse_hindi: जब पुरवासियों ने यह समाचार पाया कि दोनों राजकुमार नगर देखने के लिए आए हैं, तब वे सब घर-बार और सब काम-काज छोड़कर ऐसे दौड़े मानो दरिद्री (धन का) खजाना लूटने दौड़े हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1200.english_translation: When the townspeople heard that the two princes had come to see the city, they left home and work and rushed out like poor people running to seize a treasure.
ramacharitamanas::1200.translation_literal: देखन (to see) / नगरु (the city) / भूपसुत (king's sons, princes) / आए (came) / समाचार (news) / पुरबासिन्ह (of the townspeople) / पाए (received) / धाए (ran) / धाम (home) / काम (work) / सब (all) / त्यागी (leaving) / मनहुँ (as if) / रंक (poor people) / निधि (treasure) / लूटन (to loot) / लागी (ran)
ramacharitamanas::1200.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1200.essence: True beauty makes ordinary life stop and run toward it.
ramacharitamanas::1200.simple_meaning: The whole city drops its work and rushes out just to see the two princes. Their arrival creates a wave of joy and excitement.
ramacharitamanas::1200.simple_insight: Some presences pull people out of routine without effort. Real beauty makes attention gather on its own.
ramacharitamanas::1200.detailed_meaning: The princes have entered the city, and word spreads fast. The townspeople abandon their homes and tasks to catch a glimpse of Ram and Lakshman. This verse shows how deeply their beauty and presence stir the city.
ramacharitamanas::1200.modern_relevance: A street vendor leaves his stall half-open because word spreads that someone extraordinary has arrived nearby. People stop ordinary life for a moment when presence feels rare and precious.
ramacharitamanas::1200.insight: It shows how genuine radiance interrupts habit and draws people toward it before they even decide.

ramacharitamanas::1201.verse_sanskrit: निरखि सहज सुंदर दोउ भाई। होहिं सुखी लोचन फल पाई॥ जुबतीं भवन झरोखन्हि लागीं। निरखहिं राम रूप अनुरागीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1201.verse_hindi: स्वभाव ही से सुंदर दोनों भाइयों को देखकर वे लोग नेत्रों का फल पाकर सुखी हो रहे हैं। युवती स्त्रियाँ घर के झरोखों से लगी हुई प्रेम सहित श्री रामचन्द्रजी के रूप को देख रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1201.english_translation: Seeing the two brothers, beautiful by nature, they became joyful as if their eyes had found their reward. Young women leaned from the windows of their houses, gazing lovingly at Ram's form.
ramacharitamanas::1201.translation_literal: निरखि (seeing) / सहज (natural) / सुंदर (beautiful) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / होहिं (become) / सुखी (happy) / लोचन (eyes) / फल (fruit, reward) / पाई (having obtained) / जुबतीं (young women) / भवन (houses) / झरोखन्हि (from windows) / लागीं (leaned) / निरखहिं (they behold) / राम (Ram) / रूप (form) / अनुरागीं (with love)
ramacharitamanas::1201.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1201.essence: Ram's presence makes seeing itself feel fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::1201.simple_meaning: People feel complete just by seeing Ram and Lakshman. Young women lean from their windows, lovingly watching Ram's beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1201.simple_insight: Some presences satisfy the heart before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1201.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya has opened its streets to the sight of Ram and Lakshman. The city is caught in wonder: people feel their eyes have found their reward, and young women lean from windows to drink in Ram's beauty. This verse lingers on that shared enchantment.
ramacharitamanas::1201.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone walking into a room and the whole atmosphere changes. No announcement, no performance — just a presence that makes people look up and feel glad to be there.
ramacharitamanas::1201.insight: It shifts attention from what is said to the effect a noble presence has on others.

ramacharitamanas::1202.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं परसपर बचन सप्रीती। सखि इन्ह कोटि काम छबि जीती॥ सुर नर असुर नाग मुनि माहीं। सोभा असि कहुँ सुनिअति नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1202.verse_hindi: वे आपस में बड़े प्रेम से बातें कर रही हैं- हे सखी! इन्होंने करोड़ों कामदेवों की छबि को जीत लिया है। देवता, मनुष्य, असुर, नाग और मुनियों में ऐसी शोभा तो कहीं सुनने में भी नहीं आती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1202.english_translation: They speak to one another with deep affection: “Sakhi, these two have conquered the beauty of millions of Cupids. Among gods, humans, demons, serpents, and sages, no such splendor has ever been heard of.”
ramacharitamanas::1202.translation_literal: कहहिं (they speak) / परसपर (to one another) / बचन (words) / सप्रीती (with affection) / सखि (friend) / इन्ह (these) / कोटि (crores, millions) / काम (of desire) / छबि (beauty) / जीती (conquered) / सुर (gods) / नर (humans) / असुर (demons) / नाग (serpents) / मुनि (sages) / माहीं (among) / सोभा (splendor) / असि (such) / कहुँ (anywhere) / सुनिअति (is heard) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::1202.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1202.essence: Their beauty silences comparison and turns strangers into witnesses.
ramacharitamanas::1202.simple_meaning: The women speak lovingly among themselves, saying that the two brothers are more beautiful than millions of love-gods and unlike anyone else in all worlds.
ramacharitamanas::1202.simple_insight: A shared moment of beauty can stop a whole crowd and leave only wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1202.detailed_meaning: As Ram and Lakshman walk through Ayodhya, the women watching from homes and windows whisper to one another in delight. Their praise rises naturally from sight itself: the brothers’ beauty overwhelms every comparison, and the scene builds toward a fuller description of that divine splendor.
ramacharitamanas::1202.modern_relevance: You catch sight of someone walking into a room and the whole atmosphere changes. People stop talking, lean closer, and share the same stunned thought before they even know why.
ramacharitamanas::1202.insight: It turns admiration into a collective act, showing how beauty creates instant reverence and shared speech.

ramacharitamanas::1203.verse_sanskrit: बिष्नु चारि भुज बिधि मुख चारी। बिकट बेष मुख पंच पुरारी॥ अपर देउ अस कोउ ना आही। यह छबि सखी पटतरिअ जाही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1203.verse_hindi: भगवान विष्णु के चार भुजाएँ हैं, ब्रह्माजी के चार मुख हैं, शिवजी का विकट (भयानक) वेष है और उनके पाँच मुँह हैं। हे सखी! दूसरा देवता भी कोई ऐसा नहीं है, जिसके साथ इस छबि की उपमा दी जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1203.english_translation: Vishnu has four arms, Brahma has four faces, and Shiva has a fierce form with five mouths. O friend, no other deity exists whose beauty can be compared to this one.
ramacharitamanas::1203.translation_literal: बिष्नु (Vishnu) / चारि भुज (four-armed) / बिधि (Brahma) / मुख चारी (four-faced) / बिकट बेष (fierce form) / मुख पंच (five-faced) / पुरारी (Shiva) / अपर (other) / देउ (deity) / अस (such) / कोउ (anyone) / ना आही (does not exist) / यह (this) / छबि (beauty, form) / सखी (friend) / पटतरिअ (compared) / जाही (goes, is compared)
ramacharitamanas::1203.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1203.simple_meaning: The women say that even the great deities of the world cannot match Ram and Lakshman's beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1203.simple_insight: Some presence is so complete that comparison itself feels too small.
ramacharitamanas::1203.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the women keep watching the two princes as they move through the court. They try to measure their beauty against Vishnu, Brahma, and Shiva, but the comparison fails. This verse heightens the wonder before the bow contest begins.
ramacharitamanas::1203.modern_relevance: You see someone enter a room and every other conversation quietly stops. People reach for comparisons, but nothing fits. The moment feels larger than language.
ramacharitamanas::1203.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary description to reverent astonishment.

ramacharitamanas::1204.verse_sanskrit: बय किसोर सुषमा सदन स्याम गौर सुख धाम। अंग अंग पर वारिअहिं कोटि कोटि सत काम ॥
ramacharitamanas::1204.verse_hindi: इनकी किशोर अवस्था है, ये सुंदरता के घर, साँवले और गोरे रंग के तथा सुख के धाम हैं। इनके अंग-अंग पर करोड़ों-अरबों कामदेवों को निछावर कर देना चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1204.english_translation: Their youth is a home of beauty, dark and fair, a dwelling of bliss. On every limb, millions and billions of Kamas should be offered up.
ramacharitamanas::1204.translation_literal: बय (age) / किसोर (youthful) / सुषमा (beauty) / सदन (dwelling) / स्याम (dark-complexioned) / गौर (fair-complexioned) / सुख (bliss) / धाम (abode) / अंग अंग (every limb) / पर (upon) / वारिअहिं (should be offered) / कोटि कोटि (millions and billions) / सत (hundreds) / काम (Kama)
ramacharitamanas::1204.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1204.essence: Their beauty makes even desire look small.
ramacharitamanas::1204.simple_meaning: Ram and Sita are being praised as radiantly beautiful in their youth. Their beauty is so overwhelming that even countless Kamas seem small beside it.
ramacharitamanas::1204.simple_insight: Some beauty does not just attract attention; it overwhelms the mind and leaves only reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1204.detailed_meaning: In the swayamvar gathering, the women are comparing every possible measure of beauty and finding it inadequate. After describing the unmatched charm in the previous lines, this couplet crowns the praise of Ram's youthful form.
ramacharitamanas::1204.modern_relevance: You catch yourself staring at someone across a crowded room, then realize the feeling is not desire alone. It is awe — the mind quietly admitting it has met something greater than its usual standards.
ramacharitamanas::1204.insight: It shifts the mind from ordinary attraction to reverent wonder before beauty.

ramacharitamanas::1205.verse_sanskrit: कहहु सखी अस को तनु धारी। जो न मोह यह रूप निहारी॥ कोउ सप्रेम बोली मृदु बानी। जो मैं सुना सो सुनहु सयानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1205.verse_hindi: हे सखी! (भला) कहो तो ऐसा कौन शरीरधारी होगा, जो इस रूप को देखकर मोहित न हो जाए (अर्थात यह रूप जड़-चेतन सबको मोहित करने वाला है)। (तब) कोई दूसरी सखी प्रेम सहित कोमल वाणी से बोली- हे सयानी! मैंने जो सुना है उसे सुनो- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1205.english_translation: Tell me, dear friend, who could wear a body and not be charmed by this form? Then another friend spoke lovingly and softly: "Listen, wise one, to what I have heard."
ramacharitamanas::1205.translation_literal: कहहु (tell) / सखी (friend) / अस (such) / को (who) / तनु (body) / धारी (bearing) / जो (who) / न (not) / मोह (is enchanted) / यह (this) / रूप (form) / निहारी (having seen) ॥ / कोउ (someone) / सप्रेम (with love) / बोली (spoke) / मृदु (soft) / बानी (speech) / जो (what) / मैं (I) / सुना (heard) / सो (that) / सुनहु (listen) / सयानी (wise one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1205.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1205.essence: Ram's beauty first disarms the mind, then opens the door to devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1205.simple_meaning: The women are marveling at Ram and asking who could see such beauty without being moved. One of them then begins to answer gently.
ramacharitamanas::1205.simple_insight: Beauty can stop the mind before it starts judging.
ramacharitamanas::1205.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the women have just seen Ram and Lakshman. Their wonder spills out in speech: this form is so beautiful that no embodied being could remain unmoved. One friend then leans in to explain what she has heard about them.
ramacharitamanas::1205.modern_relevance: You catch sight of someone entering a room and the whole conversation changes. Before anyone names what happened, everyone already feels it: presence can silence the mind.
ramacharitamanas::1205.insight: It prepares the reader for a revelation by showing how Ram's form naturally draws devotion.

ramacharitamanas::1206.verse_sanskrit: ए दोऊ दसरथ के ढोटा। बाल मरालन्हि के कल जोटा॥ मुनि कौसिक मख के रखवारे। जिन्ह रन अजिर निसाचर मारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1206.verse_hindi: ये दोनों (राजकुमार) महाराज दशरथजी के पुत्र हैं! बाल राजहंसों का सा सुंदर जोड़ा है। ये मुनि विश्वामित्र के यज्ञ की रक्षा करने वाले हैं, इन्होंने युद्ध के मैदान में राक्षसों को मारा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1206.english_translation: These two are King Dasharath's sons, a beautiful pair like young swans. They protect Sage Vishwamitra's sacrifice and have killed demons on the battlefield.
ramacharitamanas::1206.translation_literal: ए (these) / दोऊ (both) / दसरथ के ढोटा (Dasharath's sons) / बाल मरालन्हि के कल जोटा (a beautiful pair like young swans) / मुनि कौसिक मख के रखवारे (protectors of Sage Kaushik's sacrifice) / जिन्ह (who) / रन अजिर (battlefield) / निसाचर (demons) / मारे (killed)
ramacharitamanas::1206.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1206.essence: True beauty shows itself in protection and courage.
ramacharitamanas::1206.simple_meaning: The verse praises Ram and Lakshman as Dasharath's handsome sons. It also recalls how they protected Vishvamitra's sacrifice and defeated demons in battle.
ramacharitamanas::1206.simple_insight: Some introductions are not idle praise; they reveal what kind of people these two truly are.
ramacharitamanas::1206.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the princes are being described before the swayamvar. The speaker names Ram and Lakshman as Dasharath's sons, beautiful like swans, and reminds everyone that they already guarded Vishwamitra's sacrifice and destroyed demons. It is praise, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1206.modern_relevance: At a family gathering, someone introduces two siblings with pride: not just how they look, but what they have already done for others. The introduction itself carries their character.
ramacharitamanas::1206.insight: It frames identity through service and courage, not appearance alone.

ramacharitamanas::1207.verse_sanskrit: स्याम गात कल कंज बिलोचन। जो मारीच सुभुज मदु मोचन॥ कौसल्या सुत सो सुख खानी। नामु रामु धनु सायक पानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1207.verse_hindi: जिनका श्याम शरीर और सुंदर कमल जैसे नेत्र हैं, जो मारीच और सुबाहु के मद को चूर करने वाले और सुख की खान हैं और जो हाथ में धनुष-बाण लिए हुए हैं, वे कौसल्याजी के पुत्र हैं, इनका नाम राम है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1207.english_translation: They have a dark complexion and lovely lotus-like eyes. They humbled Maricha and Subahu. They are a source of joy. The one with bow and arrows in hand is Kaushalya's son, Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1207.translation_literal: स्याम (dark) / गात (body) / कल (lovely) / कंज (lotus) / बिलोचन (eyes) / जो (who) / मारीच (Maricha) / सुभुज (Subahu) / मदु (pride) / मोचन (one who releases) / कौसल्या (Kaushalya) / सुत (son) / सो (that) / सुख (joy) / खानी (mine/source) / नामु (name) / रामु (Ram) / धनु (bow) / सायक (arrows) / पानी (in hand)
ramacharitamanas::1207.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1207.essence: Ram's beauty is inseparable from his strength.
ramacharitamanas::1207.simple_meaning: Ram is described as dark-complexioned, lotus-eyed, joyful to behold, and armed with bow and arrows. He is identified as Kaushalya's son.
ramacharitamanas::1207.simple_insight: The mind settles when beauty and strength appear together in one person.
ramacharitamanas::1207.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, the onlookers are identifying the princes one by one. This verse turns fully toward Ram: dark-complexioned, lotus-eyed, radiant, and already known for defeating Maricha and Subahu. The crowd is naming the one who has entered the assembly.
ramacharitamanas::1207.modern_relevance: You spot someone in a crowded room and know, before words, that they carry calm strength. Their presence feels steady, not flashy — and everyone notices.
ramacharitamanas::1207.insight: It shifts attention from mere appearance to the combination of grace, power, and proven courage.

ramacharitamanas::1208.verse_sanskrit: गौर किसोर बेषु बर काछें। कर सर चाप राम के पाछें॥ लछिमनु नामु राम लघु भ्राता। सुनु सखि तासु सुमित्रा माता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1208.verse_hindi: जिनका रंग गोरा और किशोर अवस्था है और जो सुंदर वेष बनाए और हाथ में धनुष-बाण लिए श्री रामजी के पीछे-पीछे चल रहे हैं, वे इनके छोटे भाई हैं, उनका नाम लक्ष्मण है। हे सखी! सुनो, उनकी माता सुमित्रा हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1208.english_translation: Fair and youthful in appearance, handsome in dress, with bow and arrows in hand, Lakshman walks behind Ram. Listen, friend: his name is Lakshman, and his mother is Sumitra.
ramacharitamanas::1208.translation_literal: गौर (fair) / किसोर (youthful) / बेषु (appearance, dress) / बर (beautiful) / काछें (wearing) / कर (in hand) / सर (arrows) / चाप (bow) / राम के पाछें (behind Ram) / लछिमनु (Lakshman) / नामु (name) / राम लघु भ्राता (Ram's younger brother) / सुनु (listen) / सखि (friend) / तासु (his) / सुमित्रा माता (mother Sumitra)
ramacharitamanas::1208.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1208.essence: True support stays close and never competes for the front.
ramacharitamanas::1208.simple_meaning: Lakshman is introduced as Ram's younger brother, walking behind Ram with bow and arrows in hand.
ramacharitamanas::1208.simple_insight: Loyalty can be seen in how someone stands, not just what they say.
ramacharitamanas::1208.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the onlookers are taking in Ram's arrival for the bow ceremony. This verse pauses to identify Lakshman: young, radiant, armed, and always at Ram's side. The scene deepens the sense that Ram's journey is never alone.
ramacharitamanas::1208.modern_relevance: You notice the friend who never steps in front, only beside or behind, ready before anyone asks. That quiet loyalty changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::1208.insight: It trains attention toward faithful presence and self-effacing service.

ramacharitamanas::1209.verse_sanskrit: बिप्रकाजु करि बंधु दोउ मग मुनिबधू उधारि। आए देखन चापमख सुनि हरषीं सब नारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1209.verse_hindi: दोनों भाई ब्राह्मण विश्वामित्र का काम करके और रास्ते में मुनि गौतम की स्त्री अहल्या का उद्धार करके यहाँ धनुषयज्ञ देखने आए हैं। यह सुनकर सब स्त्रियाँ प्रसन्न हुईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1209.english_translation: After serving the priest's purpose and redeeming Ahalya on the way, both brothers have come to see the bow sacrifice. Hearing this, all the women rejoiced.
ramacharitamanas::1209.translation_literal: बिप्रकाजु (priest's work) / करि (having done) / बंधु (brothers) / दोउ (both) / मग (on the way) / मुनिबधू (sage's wife) / उधारि (having rescued) / आए (came) / देखन (to see) / चापमख (bow-sacrifice) / सुनि (hearing) / हरषीं (rejoiced) / सब (all) / नारि (women)
ramacharitamanas::1209.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1209.essence: Good action announces itself before the person does.
ramacharitamanas::1209.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have arrived after helping Vishwamitra and rescuing Ahalya. The women hear this and feel joy at the sight of them coming to the bow sacrifice.
ramacharitamanas::1209.simple_insight: A noble act creates its own welcome. People recognize goodness before they even know its full story.
ramacharitamanas::1209.detailed_meaning: At Janak's bow sacrifice, Ram and Lakshman arrive not as strangers but as the brothers who have already served Vishwamitra and freed Ahalya. The women hearing of their deeds rejoice, and the scene turns toward Ram's first public admiration.
ramacharitamanas::1209.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after helping someone quietly on the way there. Before you say a word, the atmosphere changes — people already feel your character.
ramacharitamanas::1209.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to reputation earned through action.

ramacharitamanas::1210.verse_sanskrit: देखि राम छबि कोउ एक कहई। जोगु जानकिहि यह बरु अहई॥ जौं सखि इन्हहि देख नरनाहू। पन परिहरि हठि करइ बिबाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1210.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की छबि देखकर कोई एक (दूसरी सखी) कहने लगी- यह वर जानकी के योग्य है। हे सखी! यदि कहीं राजा इन्हें देख ले, तो प्रतिज्ञा छोड़कर हठपूर्वक इन्हीं से विवाह कर देगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1210.english_translation: Seeing Rama's radiance, one lady said, “He is fit for Janaki. O friend, if the king sees him, he will abandon his vow and insist on this marriage.”
ramacharitamanas::1210.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / राम (Rama) / छबि (radiance, beauty) / कोउ एक (someone, one lady) / कहई (said) / जोगु (fit, worthy) / जानकिहि (for Janaki) / यह (this) / बरु (bridegroom) / अहई (is) ॥ / जौं (if) / सखि (friend) / इन्हहि (these) / देख (seeing) / नरनाहू (the king) / पन (vow) / परिहरि (abandoning) / हठि (stubbornly) / करइ (does) / बिबाहू (marriage) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1210.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1210.essence: True fit can make even a vow feel small.
ramacharitamanas::1210.simple_meaning: A woman sees Rama and says he is the right bridegroom for Janaki. She adds that even the king would forget his vow if he saw Rama.
ramacharitamanas::1210.simple_insight: Beauty can overturn rigid plans when it reveals what truly belongs together.
ramacharitamanas::1210.detailed_meaning: At Janak's bow ceremony in Mithila, the women watching Rama are struck by his presence. One of them says he is exactly right for Sita, and even the king would be tempted to break his own vow after seeing him.
ramacharitamanas::1210.modern_relevance: At a wedding venue, the room goes quiet when one person walks in and everyone feels the match before any words are spoken. Some recognitions are instant and undeniable.
ramacharitamanas::1210.insight: It shows how true suitability can feel self-evident, stronger than rules or formal plans.

ramacharitamanas::1211.verse_sanskrit: कोउ कह ए भूपति पहिचाने। मुनि समेत सादर सनमाने॥ सखि परंतु पनु राउ न तजई। बिधि बस हठि अबिबेकहि भजई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1211.verse_hindi: किसी ने कहा- राजा ने इन्हें पहचान लिया है और मुनि के सहित इनका आदरपूर्वक सम्मान किया है, परंतु हे सखी! राजा अपना प्रण नहीं छोड़ता। वह होनहार के वशीभूत होकर हठपूर्वक अविवेक का ही आश्रय लिए हुए हैं (प्रण पर अड़े रहने की मूर्खता नहीं छोड़ता) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1211.english_translation: Someone said, "The king has recognized them and honored them respectfully along with the sage. Yet, O friend, the king will not let go of his vow. Driven by fate, he clings stubbornly to foolishness."
ramacharitamanas::1211.translation_literal: कोउ (someone) / कह (said) / ए (these) / भूपति (king) / पहिचाने (has recognized) / मुनि (sage) / समेत (together with) / सादर (respectfully) / सनमाने (has honored) / सखि (O friend) / परंतु (but) / पनु (vow) / राउ (king) / न (not) / तजई (lets go) / बिधि (fate) / बस (under the control) / हठि (stubbornly) / अबिबेकहि (foolishness) / भजई (takes refuge in)
ramacharitamanas::1211.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1211.essence: Seeing clearly changes nothing if pride keeps the vow.
ramacharitamanas::1211.simple_meaning: The women see that the king understands who Rama is, yet he still refuses to release his vow and act wisely.
ramacharitamanas::1211.simple_insight: Recognition is not enough if pride keeps the heart closed.
ramacharitamanas::1211.detailed_meaning: At Janak's bow ceremony, the women watching Rama and Lakshman can see the king's reaction. He has honored them and seems to know their worth, yet he remains bound by his vow. The scene shows insight trapped inside stubbornness.
ramacharitamanas::1211.modern_relevance: You know your partner is right in the middle of an argument, but you keep defending your position anyway. Clear seeing means nothing if pride keeps steering.
ramacharitamanas::1211.insight: It shifts attention from what is understood to what stubbornness still refuses to release.

ramacharitamanas::1212.verse_sanskrit: कोउ कह जौं भल अहइ बिधाता। सब कहँ सुनिअ उचित फल दाता॥ तौ जानकिहि मिलिहि बरु एहू। नाहिन आलि इहाँ संदेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1212.verse_hindi: कोई कहती है- यदि विधाता भले हैं और सुना जाता है कि वे सबको उचित फल देते हैं, तो जानकीजी को यही वर मिलेगा। हे सखी! इसमें संदेह नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1212.english_translation: If the creator is kind and gives each person the right result, then Janaki will surely get this groom. O friend, there is no doubt.
ramacharitamanas::1212.translation_literal: कोउ (someone) / कह (says) / जौं (if) / भल (good) / अहइ (is) / बिधाता (the creator) / सब कहँ (for everyone) / सुनिअ (it is heard) / उचित (right) / फल (result) / दाता (giver) / तौ (then) / जानकिहि (to Janaki) / मिलिहि (will be obtained) / बरु (groom) / एहू (this) / नाहिन (no) / आलि (friend) / इहाँ (here) / संदेहू (doubt)
ramacharitamanas::1212.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1212.essence: What fits rightly will find its place.
ramacharitamanas::1212.simple_meaning: If the creator truly gives each person the fitting result, then Janaki will surely receive this groom. The women watching the swayamvar feel certain about Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1212.simple_insight: Hope becomes calm when the heart trusts that what is right will arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1212.detailed_meaning: In the swayamvar hall, the watching women compare Ram's beauty with Janaki's worth. One of them says that if the creator is just and gives fitting results, then Ram must be the bridegroom. Their excitement is building toward certainty.
ramacharitamanas::1212.modern_relevance: You watch two people in a room and know, without forcing it, that the right match is already obvious. The heart stops bargaining and simply recognises what fits.
ramacharitamanas::1212.insight: It shifts the mind from anxious wishing to trusting what aligns naturally.

ramacharitamanas::1213.verse_sanskrit: जौं बिधि बस अस बनै सँजोगू। तौ कृतकृत्य होइ सब लोगू॥ सखि हमरें आरति अति तातें। कबहुँक ए आवहिं एहि नातें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1213.verse_hindi: जो दैवयोग से ऐसा संयोग बन जाए, तो हम सब लोग कृतार्थ हो जाएँ। हे सखी! मेरे तो इसी से इतनी अधिक आतुरता हो रही है कि इसी नाते कभी ये यहाँ आवेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1213.english_translation: If fate arranges such a meeting, everyone will be fulfilled. O friend, my longing is so intense that perhaps they will come here through this bond.
ramacharitamanas::1213.translation_literal: जौं (if) / बिधि (fate) / बस (under the control) / अस (such) / बनै (is formed) / सँजोगू (meeting, union) / तौ (then) / कृतकृत्य (fulfilled, accomplished) / होइ (become) / सब (all) / लोगू (people) / सखि (O friend) / हमरें (my) / आरति (longing, distress) / अति (very much) / तातें (therefore) / कबहुँक (sometime, perhaps) / ए (these) / आवहिं (come) / एहि (this) / नातें (through this bond, for this reason)
ramacharitamanas::1213.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1213.essence: Hope turns a possible meeting into a whole world.
ramacharitamanas::1213.simple_meaning: If destiny brings this meeting about, everyone will feel fulfilled. The speaker longs so deeply that even a small bond feels like a possible path to that meeting.
ramacharitamanas::1213.simple_insight: Longing can make even a tiny possibility feel sacred and enough to hold onto.
ramacharitamanas::1213.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the women speak about the prince's identity and Sita's possible marriage. One speaker imagines that if fate allows this union, everyone will be fulfilled. Her own longing makes her hope that the men may come again through this connection.
ramacharitamanas::1213.modern_relevance: You keep replaying a message, a meeting, a chance encounter, because one small opening feels like it could change everything. Hope makes even uncertainty feel alive.
ramacharitamanas::1213.insight: It shifts the mind from certainty to hopeful waiting, where desire reads meaning into every possible sign.

ramacharitamanas::1214.verse_sanskrit: नाहिं त हम कहुँ सुनहु सखि इन्ह कर दरसनु दूरि। यह संघटु तब होइ जब पुन्य पुराकृत भूरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1214.verse_hindi: नहीं तो (विवाह न हुआ तो) हे सखी! सुनो, हमको इनके दर्शन दुर्लभ हैं। यह संयोग तभी हो सकता है, जब हमारे पूर्वजन्मों के बहुत पुण्य हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1214.english_translation: Otherwise, listen, dear friend: seeing them is hard for us. This union can happen only if our past lives hold great merit.
ramacharitamanas::1214.translation_literal: नाहिं (otherwise) / त (then) / हम कहुँ (for us) / सुनहु सखि (listen, dear friend) / इन्ह कर (of these) / दरसनु (seeing) / दूरि (far, difficult) / यह संघटु (this union) / तब होइ (then happens) / जब (when) / पुन्य पुराकृत (past-acquired merit) / भूरि (great, abundant)
ramacharitamanas::1214.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1214.essence: Rare meetings feel like the fruit of deep merit.
ramacharitamanas::1214.simple_meaning: The women say that meeting Ram is rare and can happen only through great past merit.
ramacharitamanas::1214.simple_insight: Longing becomes humble when it recognizes that some blessings feel earned across time.
ramacharitamanas::1214.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur before the swayamvar, the women are speaking quietly about Ram and the chance of Sita's marriage. One says their sight of him is rare and such a union would require immense merit from past lives.
ramacharitamanas::1214.modern_relevance: You meet someone and feel, almost instantly, that this connection is not ordinary. The mind calls it chance, but the heart feels the weight of everything that led here.
ramacharitamanas::1214.insight: It shifts desire from entitlement to reverence, making the reader see precious meetings as earned, not owed.

ramacharitamanas::1215.verse_sanskrit: बोली अपर कहेहु सखि नीका। एहिं बिआह अति हित सबही का। कोउ कह संकर चाप कठोरा। ए स्यामल मृदु गात किसोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1215.verse_hindi: दूसरी ने कहा- हे सखी! तुमने बहुत अच्छा कहा। इस विवाह से सभी का परम हित है। किसी ने कहा- शंकरजी का धनुष कठोर है और ये साँवले राजकुमार कोमल शरीर के बालक हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1215.english_translation: Another said, “Sakhi, you spoke well. This marriage is for everyone’s highest good. Someone said, “Shankar’s bow is hard, and these dark, tender-bodied youths are boys.”
ramacharitamanas::1215.translation_literal: बोली (spoke) / अपर (another) / कहेहु (you said) / सखि (friend) / नीका (well) / एहिं (this) / बिआह (marriage) / अति (very) / हित (benefit) / सबही (of everyone) / का (of) / कोउ (someone) / कह (said) / संकर (Shankar) / चाप (bow) / कठोरा (hard) / ए (these) / स्यामल (dark) / मृदु (soft) / गात (body) / किसोरा (youths)
ramacharitamanas::1215.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1215.essence: Hope and doubt can stand side by side before the same impossible task.
ramacharitamanas::1215.simple_meaning: One woman agrees that this marriage would bless everyone. Another points out the obstacle: Shiva’s bow is hard to bend, while the princes look young and delicate.
ramacharitamanas::1215.simple_insight: Big hopes can sit beside real doubt in the same room.
ramacharitamanas::1215.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, the women watching Sita’s swayamvar weigh the same moment differently. One sees a blessed union for all; another sees the impossible contrast between Shiva’s mighty bow and the princes’ youthful bodies. The tension builds before the test.
ramacharitamanas::1215.modern_relevance: A family chat fills with excitement about a wedding, then someone quietly names the practical problem no one wants to say aloud. Hope and doubt are both speaking at once.
ramacharitamanas::1215.insight: It shows how a hopeful vision can coexist with clear-eyed recognition of difficulty.

ramacharitamanas::1216.verse_sanskrit: सबु असमंजस अहइ सयानी। यह सुनि अपर कहइ मृदु बानी॥ सखि इन्ह कहँ कोउ कोउ अस कहहीं। बड़ प्रभाउ देखत लघु अहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1216.verse_hindi: हे सयानी! सब असमंजस ही है। यह सुनकर दूसरी सखी कोमल वाणी से कहने लगी- हे सखी! इनके संबंध में कोई-कोई ऐसा कहते हैं कि ये देखने में तो छोटे हैं, पर इनका प्रभाव बहुत बड़ा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1216.english_translation: O wise one, everything is bewildering. Hearing this, another spoke gently: "Sister, some say this about them: they look small, yet their power is great."
ramacharitamanas::1216.translation_literal: सबु (all) / असमंजस (confusion, uncertainty) / अहइ (is) / सयानी (wise woman) / यह (this) / सुनि (hearing) / अपर (another) / कहइ (speaks) / मृदु बानी (gentle words) / सखि (sister-friend) / इन्ह कहँ (about them) / कोउ कोउ (some people) / अस (thus) / कहहीं (say) / बड़ प्रभाउ (great power) / देखत (seeing) / लघु (small) / अहहीं (are)
ramacharitamanas::1216.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1216.essence: True power can hide behind a modest appearance.
ramacharitamanas::1216.simple_meaning: The women are unsure about the match, but one of them says the prince may look young while still carrying great power.
ramacharitamanas::1216.simple_insight: Greatness is not always visible at first glance.
ramacharitamanas::1216.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the maidens are discussing Ram before the bow ceremony. One says the situation is confusing, then another gently reminds the group that appearances deceive: the boy who seems slight may still hold immense power.
ramacharitamanas::1216.modern_relevance: At a job interview, the quiet candidate speaks softly and looks unassuming. Then one answer changes the room. People often mistake calm presence for weakness.
ramacharitamanas::1216.insight: It shifts attention from outward size to hidden capacity.

ramacharitamanas::1217.verse_sanskrit: परसि जासु पद पंकज धूरी। तरी अहल्या कृत अघ भूरी॥ सो कि रहिहि बिनु सिव धनु तोरें। यह प्रतीति परिहरिअ न भोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1217.verse_hindi: जिनके चरणकमलों की धूलि का स्पर्श पाकर अहल्या तर गई, जिसने बड़ा भारी पाप किया था, वे क्या शिवजी का धनुष बिना तोड़े रहेंगे। इस विश्वास को भूलकर भी नहीं छोड़ना चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1217.english_translation: The dust from whose lotus feet redeemed Ahalya, burdened with grave wrongdoing, can such a one fail to break Shiva's bow? Never let go of this faith, even for a moment.
ramacharitamanas::1217.translation_literal: परसि (touching) / जासु (whose) / पद-पंकज (lotus feet) / धूरी (dust) / तरी (was saved) / अहल्या (Ahalya) / कृत (done) / अघ (wrongdoing) / भूरी (great) / सो (that one) / कि (how) / रहिहि (will remain) / बिनु (without) / सिव-धनु (Shiva's bow) / तोरें (breaking) / यह (this) / प्रतीति (trust) / परिहरिअ (should be abandoned) / न (not) / भोरें (even in the morning)
ramacharitamanas::1217.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1217.essence: Past grace is reason enough for trust.
ramacharitamanas::1217.simple_meaning: Ram's feet have already shown their power by redeeming Ahalya. That same power makes it unthinkable that he will fail to break Shiva's bow.
ramacharitamanas::1217.simple_insight: Faith grows stronger when you remember what has already been made possible.
ramacharitamanas::1217.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the women are debating whether the dark-complexioned youth can lift Shiva's bow and win Sita. One voice answers with a memory of Ahalya: the same feet that lifted her burden can surely complete this marriage test.
ramacharitamanas::1217.modern_relevance: You are doubting whether a hard conversation will work, then remember every time this person has already shown up for you. Past grace becomes present confidence.
ramacharitamanas::1217.insight: It shifts the mind from present doubt to remembered proof.

ramacharitamanas::1218.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं बिरंचि रचि सीय सँवारी। तेहिं स्यामल बरु रचेउ बिचारी॥ तासु बचन सुनि सब हरषानीं। ऐसेइ होउ कहहिं मृदु बानीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1218.verse_hindi: जिस ब्रह्मा ने सीता को सँवारकर (बड़ी चतुराई से) रचा है, उसी ने विचार कर साँवला वर भी रच रखा है। उसके ये वचन सुनकर सब हर्षित हुईं और कोमल वाणी से कहने लगीं- ऐसा ही हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1218.english_translation: The one who fashioned Sita with care also fashioned the dark-hued groom with thought. Hearing this, everyone rejoiced and softly said, "So be it."
ramacharitamanas::1218.translation_literal: जेहिं (who) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / रचि (having fashioned) / सीय (Sita) / सँवारी (beautifully adorned) / तेहिं (that same one) / स्यामल (dark-hued) / बरु (groom) / रचेउ (fashioned) / बिचारी (with thought) / तासु (his) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / सब (all) / हरषानीं (rejoiced) / ऐसेइ (just so) / होउ (may it be so) / कहहिं (they say) / मृदु (gentle) / बानीं (words)
ramacharitamanas::1218.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1218.essence: What is truly matched needs no argument.
ramacharitamanas::1218.simple_meaning: The women agree that Sita and Ram are perfectly matched, as if both were fashioned with the same care. Their doubt turns into joy and acceptance.
ramacharitamanas::1218.simple_insight: Some recognitions arrive as relief: what seemed uncertain suddenly feels obviously right.
ramacharitamanas::1218.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the women are still weighing who can truly win her hand. One speaker says Brahma himself has shaped both Sita and the dark-hued groom with matching care. The room softens into delight and agreement.
ramacharitamanas::1218.modern_relevance: At a wedding when everyone is still measuring the match, one quiet comment can dissolve the tension. Suddenly the choice feels not forced, but beautifully obvious.
ramacharitamanas::1218.insight: It turns hesitation into assent by framing the union as already rightly made.

ramacharitamanas::1219.verse_sanskrit: हियँ हरषहिं बरषहिं सुमन सुमुखि सुलोचनि बृंद। जाहिं जहाँ जहँ बंधु दोउ तहँ तहँ परमानंद ॥
ramacharitamanas::1219.verse_hindi: सुंदर मुख और सुंदर नेत्रों वाली स्त्रियाँ समूह की समूह हृदय में हर्षित होकर फूल बरसा रही हैं। जहाँ-जहाँ दोनों भाई जाते हैं, वहाँ-वहाँ परम आनंद छा जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1219.english_translation: Women with lovely faces and beautiful eyes felt joy in their hearts and showered flowers. Wherever the two brothers went, there was supreme delight.
ramacharitamanas::1219.translation_literal: हियँ (in the heart) / हरषहिं (they rejoice) / बरषहिं (they shower) / सुमन (flowers) / सुमुखि (beautiful-faced) / सुलोचनि (beautiful-eyed) / बृंद (groups) / जाहिं (go) / जहाँ जहाँ (wherever) / बंधु (brothers) / दोउ (both) / तहँ तहँ (there) / परमानंद (supreme delight)
ramacharitamanas::1219.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1219.essence: Their presence turns an ordinary path into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1219.simple_meaning: As Ram and Lakshman walk through the crowd, the women around them feel joy and shower flowers. Their presence fills every place with delight.
ramacharitamanas::1219.simple_insight: Some people bring joy simply by entering a space.
ramacharitamanas::1219.detailed_meaning: The two brothers have just accepted the bow challenge in Mithila. As they move toward the arena, the city responds with flowers, smiles, and rising joy. This verse paints the atmosphere before the bow is lifted.
ramacharitamanas::1219.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the mood changes before you speak. Some people carry that kind of quiet grace, and everyone around them feels it.
ramacharitamanas::1219.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the living presence that makes the event feel blessed.

ramacharitamanas::1220.verse_sanskrit: पुर पूरब दिसि गे दोउ भाई। जहँ धनुमख हित भूमि बनाई॥ अति बिस्तार चारु गच ढारी। बिमल बेदिका रुचिर सँवारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1220.verse_hindi: दोनों भाई नगर के पूरब ओर गए, जहाँ धनुषयज्ञ के लिए (रंग) भूमि बनाई गई थी। बहुत लंबा-चौड़ा सुंदर ढाला हुआ पक्का आँगन था, जिस पर सुंदर और निर्मल वेदी सजाई गई थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1220.english_translation: The two brothers went to the eastern side of the city, where the ground had been prepared for the bow sacrifice. It was a broad, beautifully arranged courtyard, with a pure and lovely altar set in place.
ramacharitamanas::1220.translation_literal: पुर (city) / पूरब दिसि (eastern side) / गे (went) / दोउ भाई (both brothers) / जहँ (where) / धनुमख (bow sacrifice) / हित (for the purpose of) / भूमि (ground) / बनाई (made/prepared) / अति (very) / बिस्तार (broad/expansive) / चारु (beautiful) / गच (paved platform/courtyard) / ढारी (laid/arranged) / बिमल (pure/clear) / बेदिका (altar/platform) / रुचिर (lovely) / सँवारी (decorated/arranged)
ramacharitamanas::1220.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1220.essence: A sacred event begins with a carefully prepared space.
ramacharitamanas::1220.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman walk to the prepared site for the bow sacrifice. The verse simply describes the sacred space set up for the event.
ramacharitamanas::1220.simple_insight: Sometimes the moment before a great event is just a quiet, careful arrangement.
ramacharitamanas::1220.detailed_meaning: At King Janak's city, Ram and Lakshman move toward the eastern side where the bow sacrifice ground has been prepared. The verse lingers on the wide courtyard and the pure altar, building the stage for the coming swayamvar.
ramacharitamanas::1220.modern_relevance: Before a wedding, the hall is being decorated, chairs aligned, flowers placed, and the altar set. The verse captures that charged stillness just before everything begins.
ramacharitamanas::1220.insight: It shifts attention from the drama to the sacred preparation that makes the drama possible.

ramacharitamanas::1221.verse_sanskrit: चहुँ दिसि कंचन मंच बिसाला। रचे जहाँ बैठहिं महिपाला॥ तेहि पाछें समीप चहुँ पासा। अपर मंच मंडली बिलासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1221.verse_hindi: चारों ओर सोने के बड़े-बड़े मंच बने थे, जिन पर राजा लोग बैठेंगे। उनके पीछे समीप ही चारों ओर दूसरे मचानों का मंडलाकार घेरा सुशोभित था ॥
ramacharitamanas::1221.english_translation: All around stood broad golden platforms where the kings would sit. Behind them, close on every side, another circular array of elegant platforms was set.
ramacharitamanas::1221.translation_literal: चहुँ दिसि (on four sides) / कंचन (golden) / मंच (platforms) / बिसाला (broad, विशाल) / रचे (were arranged) / जहाँ (where) / बैठहिं (would sit) / महिपाला (kings) / तेहि पाछें (behind that) / समीप (near) / चहुँ पासा (on four sides) / अपर (other) / मंच (platforms) / मंडली (circular array) / बिलासा (splendor)
ramacharitamanas::1221.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1221.essence: Royal splendor is carefully arranged before the moment begins.
ramacharitamanas::1221.simple_meaning: Golden platforms were arranged for the kings, with another ring of platforms set just behind them. The verse is describing the ceremonial seating area.
ramacharitamanas::1221.simple_insight: Grandeur can be built with care, but it is still only a setting.
ramacharitamanas::1221.detailed_meaning: At the bow sacrifice in Mithila, the chosen ground is being prepared for the royal assembly. After the central platform, the poet turns to the surrounding seats for the kings and nobles, showing the full ceremonial order before the contest begins.
ramacharitamanas::1221.modern_relevance: A wedding hall is set before the guests arrive: chairs aligned, lights tested, stage polished. The verse lingers on the arrangement itself, because the event’s importance is already visible in the space.
ramacharitamanas::1221.insight: It shifts attention from the event to the order and dignity built around it.

ramacharitamanas::1222.verse_sanskrit: कछुक ऊँचि सब भाँति सुहाई। बैठहिं नगर लोग जहँ जाई॥ तिन्ह के निकट बिसाल सुहाए। धवल धाम बहुबरन बनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1222.verse_hindi: वह कुछ ऊँचा था और सब प्रकार से सुंदर था, जहाँ जाकर नगर के लोग बैठेंगे। उन्हीं के पास विशाल एवं सुंदर सफेद मकान अनेक रंगों के बनाए गए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1222.english_translation: It was somewhat raised and beautiful in every way, where the city people would sit and watch. Beside it stood large, lovely white buildings made in many colors.
ramacharitamanas::1222.translation_literal: कछुक (somewhat) / ऊँचि (raised/high) / सब भाँति (in every way) / सुहाई (beautiful) / बैठहिं (will sit) / नगर लोग (city people) / जहँ (where) / जाई (going) / तिन्ह के निकट (near them) / बिसाल (large) / सुहाए (beautiful) / धवल (white) / धाम (houses/buildings) / बहुबरन (many-colored) / बनाए (made)
ramacharitamanas::1222.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1222.essence: The ceremony’s beauty begins with the space built around it.
ramacharitamanas::1222.simple_meaning: The viewing area was built higher and made beautiful, with large white buildings nearby for the people of the city.
ramacharitamanas::1222.simple_insight: Even a public gathering can be shaped with care, dignity, and beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1222.detailed_meaning: At the Sita-swayamvar, the arena is being prepared in Mithila. After the raised stage and royal seats, the builders add elevated places for the townspeople and handsome white halls nearby. The scene is still being arranged before the ceremony begins.
ramacharitamanas::1222.modern_relevance: A wedding hall is being decorated before guests arrive, and every chair, curtain, and walkway is placed with care. The beauty of the space already signals the importance of what is about to happen.
ramacharitamanas::1222.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the careful creation of a worthy setting for it.

ramacharitamanas::1223.verse_sanskrit: जहँ बैठें देखहिं सब नारी। जथाजोगु निज कुल अनुहारी॥ पुर बालक कहि कहि मृदु बचना। सादर प्रभुहि देखावहिं रचना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1223.verse_hindi: जहाँ अपने-अपने कुल के अनुसार सब स्त्रियाँ यथायोग्य (जिसको जहाँ बैठना उचित है) बैठकर देखेंगी। नगर के बालक कोमल वचन कह-कहकर आदरपूर्वक प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को (यज्ञशाला की) रचना दिखला रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1223.english_translation: Where all the women will sit and watch according to their family rank. The boys of the city, speaking gently, respectfully show Lord Ram the arrangement.
ramacharitamanas::1223.translation_literal: जहँ (where) / बैठें (sit) / देखहिं (will see) / सब (all) / नारी (women) / जथाजोगु (as appropriate) / निज (their own) / कुल (family rank) / अनुहारी (in accordance with)॥ / पुर (city) / बालक (boys) / कहि कहि (speaking repeatedly) / मृदु (gentle) / बचना (words) / सादर (respectfully) / प्रभुहि (to the Lord) / देखावहिं (show) / रचना (arrangement)
ramacharitamanas::1223.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1223.essence: Order and tenderness can make even a public gathering feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::1223.simple_meaning: The verse describes the arranged seating at the ceremony and the city boys politely showing Ram around. It is a scene of order, respect, and joyful attention.
ramacharitamanas::1223.simple_insight: Respect can be shown through small, careful gestures that make everyone feel included.
ramacharitamanas::1223.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the hall has been arranged for kings, women, and citizens. In this verse, the city boys gently guide Ram through the decorated space, showing him the setup with affection and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1223.modern_relevance: At a wedding venue, volunteers quietly guide guests to their seats while children point out the decorations with pride. The atmosphere feels orderly because everyone is being treated with care.
ramacharitamanas::1223.insight: It highlights how devotion and respect can appear as simple, courteous conduct in public spaces.

ramacharitamanas::1224.verse_sanskrit: सब सिसु एहि मिस प्रेमबस परसि मनोहर गात। तन पुलकहिं अति हरषु हियँ देखि देखि दोउ भ्रात ॥
ramacharitamanas::1224.verse_hindi: सब बालक इसी बहाने प्रेम के वश में होकर श्री रामजी के मनोहर अंगों को छूकर शरीर से पुलकित हो रहे हैं और दोनों भाइयों को देख-देखकर उनके हृदय में अत्यन्त हर्ष हो रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1224.english_translation: All the children, under the pretext of this, touched the lovely limbs of Ram in love. Their bodies thrilled with joy as they kept looking at the two brothers.
ramacharitamanas::1224.translation_literal: सब (all) / सिसु (children) / एहि मिस (by this pretext) / प्रेमबस (under the control of love) / परसि (touching) / मनोहर (beautiful) / गात (limbs, body) / तन (bodies) / पुलकहिं (thrill) / अति (greatly) / हरषु (joy) / हियँ (in the heart) / देखि देखि (seeing again and again) / दोउ भ्रात (both brothers)
ramacharitamanas::1224.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1224.essence: Love makes even touch feel like blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1224.simple_meaning: The children use the moment to touch Ram and Lakshman lovingly, and seeing them fills everyone with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1224.simple_insight: Love naturally moves toward what is beautiful and pure; joy deepens when it is shared openly.
ramacharitamanas::1224.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the city is being prepared for public viewing, and the children gather near Ram and Lakshman. They touch Ram’s lovely form in affection, and their bodies tremble with delight as they keep looking at both brothers.
ramacharitamanas::1224.modern_relevance: A child reaches for a beloved teacher at a school event, then beams just from standing nearby. Some presence makes people soften without effort.
ramacharitamanas::1224.insight: It shows how genuine beauty and goodness draw spontaneous affection, not forced respect.

ramacharitamanas::1225.verse_sanskrit: सिसु सब राम प्रेमबस जाने। प्रीति समेत निकेत बखाने॥ निज निज रुचि सब लेहिं बोलाई। सहित सनेह जाहिं दोउ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1225.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सब बालकों को प्रेम के वश जानकर (यज्ञभूमि के) स्थानों की प्रेमपूर्वक प्रशंसा की। (इससे बालकों का उत्साह, आनंद और प्रेम और भी बढ़ गया, जिससे) वे सब अपनी-अपनी रुचि के अनुसार उन्हें बुला लेते हैं और (प्रत्येक के बुलाने पर) दोनों भाई प्रेम सहित उनके पास चले जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1225.english_translation: Ram knew all the children were moved by love. He described the sacred place with affection. Each one called them over as they wished, and the two brothers went along lovingly.
ramacharitamanas::1225.translation_literal: सिसु (children) / सब (all) / राम (Ram) / प्रेमबस (under the sway of love) / जाने (knew) । / प्रीति (affection) / समेत (together with) / निकेत (place) / बखाने (described) ॥ / निज निज (each one's own) / रुचि (choice) / सब (all) / लेहिं (they take/call) / बोलाई (having called) । / सहित (with) / सनेह (love) / जाहिं (go) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1225.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1225.essence: Love turns public gathering into personal welcome.
ramacharitamanas::1225.simple_meaning: Ram understood that the children were acting out of loving excitement. They admired the place, called the brothers over, and the brothers went with affection.
ramacharitamanas::1225.simple_insight: Love makes even a simple encounter feel intimate and alive.
ramacharitamanas::1225.detailed_meaning: At the sacrificial gathering in Balkand, the children around Ram and Lakshman are already enchanted. Ram notices their loving excitement, speaks gently about the place, and the boys keep drawing the brothers toward them. The scene builds the tenderness of the swayamvar before the main event.
ramacharitamanas::1225.modern_relevance: At a wedding hall before the ceremony, cousins keep pulling the groom aside just to admire his clothes, tease him, and bring him to different groups. The room feels warm because everyone is moved by affection, not formality.
ramacharitamanas::1225.insight: It shows how presence can create warmth without effort; the brothers move through the crowd as beloved guests, not distant figures.

ramacharitamanas::1226.verse_sanskrit: राम देखावहिं अनुजहि रचना। कहि मृदु मधुर मनोहर बचना॥ लव निमेष महुँ भुवन निकाया। रचइ जासु अनुसासन माया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1226.verse_hindi: कोमल, मधुर और मनोहर वचन कहकर श्री रामजी अपने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण को (यज्ञभूमि की) रचना दिखलाते हैं। जिनकी आज्ञा पाकर माया लव निमेष (पलक गिरने के चौथाई समय) में ब्रह्माण्डों के समूह रच डालती है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1226.english_translation: Ram shows the arrangement to Lakshman, speaking soft, sweet, and lovely words. By whose command Maya creates countless worlds in a moment of a blink,
ramacharitamanas::1226.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / देखावहिं (show) / अनुजहि (to the younger brother) / रचना (arrangement, structure) / कहि (speaking) / मृदु (soft) / मधुर (sweet) / मनोहर (lovely) / बचना (words) / लव (fraction of time) / निमेष (blink) / महुँ (in) / भुवन (worlds) / निकाया (groups, multitudes) / रचइ (creates) / जासु (whose) / अनुसासन (command, instruction) / माया (illusion, creative power)
ramacharitamanas::1226.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1226.essence: True greatness can speak in the softest voice.
ramacharitamanas::1226.simple_meaning: Ram gently shows Lakshman the sacred arrangement and speaks to him with tender words. The verse also points to Ram's command over the power that creates worlds in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::1226.simple_insight: Even cosmic power can speak with tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::1226.detailed_meaning: In the yajna grounds, Ram is walking with Lakshman and pointing out the sacred layout. The mood is playful and gentle, but the verse suddenly lifts from scene to cosmic scale: the same one who speaks softly is the source whose command lets Maya create worlds in a blink.
ramacharitamanas::1226.modern_relevance: You are explaining something ordinary to a younger sibling, calm and patient, while carrying a depth they cannot yet see. The verse holds both the gentle human moment and the vast power behind it.
ramacharitamanas::1226.insight: It teaches you to hold strength without hardness, letting power remain warm and approachable.

ramacharitamanas::1227.verse_sanskrit: भगति हेतु सोइ दीनदयाला। चितवत चकित धनुष मखसाला॥ कौतुक देखि चले गुरु पाहीं। जानि बिलंबु त्रास मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1227.verse_hindi: वही दीनों पर दया करने वाले श्री रामजी भक्ति के कारण धनुष यज्ञ शाला को चकित होकर (आश्चर्य के साथ) देख रहे हैं। इस प्रकार सब कौतुक (विचित्र रचना) देखकर वे गुरु के पास चले। देर हुई जानकर उनके मन में डर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1227.english_translation: The Lord of the humble, moved by devotion, gazed in wonder at the sacrificial hall. Seeing all the marvels, he went to the teacher, fearing delay in his mind.
ramacharitamanas::1227.translation_literal: भगति हेतु (for devotion's sake) / सोइ (that very) / दीनदयाला (compassionate to the humble) / चितवत (gazing) / चकित (astonished) / धनुष (bow) / मखसाला (sacrificial hall) / कौतुक (wonder) / देखि (having seen) / चले (went) / गुरु पाहीं (to the teacher) / जानि (knowing) / बिलंबु (delay) / त्रास (fear) / मन माहीं (in the mind)
ramacharitamanas::1227.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1227.essence: True greatness can look like wonder and hurry to serve.
ramacharitamanas::1227.simple_meaning: Ram looks with childlike wonder at the sacrificial hall, then quickly goes to his teacher, afraid of being late.
ramacharitamanas::1227.simple_insight: Even the highest presence moves with humility, wonder, and care.
ramacharitamanas::1227.detailed_meaning: At Janak's sacrifice, young Ram is walking with Lakshman through the ceremonial space. He pauses to admire the strange, beautiful setup, then hurries to Vishvamitra, worried that delay may be disrespectful. The scene shows divine grace wearing the gentleness of a child.
ramacharitamanas::1227.modern_relevance: You enter a grand hall for an interview, a wedding, or a formal meeting and still feel small enough to look around with wonder. Respect and humility can coexist with confidence.
ramacharitamanas::1227.insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing that dignity can include childlike curiosity.

ramacharitamanas::1228.verse_sanskrit: जासु त्रास डर कहुँ डर होई। भजन प्रभाउ देखावत सोई॥ कहि बातें मृदु मधुर सुहाईं। किए बिदा बालक बरिआईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1228.verse_hindi: जिनके भय से डर को भी डर लगता है, वही प्रभु भजन का प्रभाव (जिसके कारण ऐसे महान प्रभु भी भय का नाट्य करते हैं) दिखला रहे हैं। उन्होंने कोमल, मधुर और सुंदर बातें कहकर बालकों को जबर्दस्ती विदा किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1228.english_translation: By whose fear even fear itself becomes afraid, he now displays the power of devotion. Speaking gently, sweetly, and beautifully, he sent the boys away by force.
ramacharitamanas::1228.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / त्रास (fear) / डर कहुँ (to fear) / डर होई (becomes fear) / भजन प्रभाउ (power/effect of devotion) / देखावत (showing) / सोई (that very one) / कहि (saying) / बातें (words) / मृदु (gentle) / मधुर (sweet) / सुहाईं (beautiful) / किए (did) / बिदा (farewell/send-off) / बालक (boys/children) / बरिआईं (by force)
ramacharitamanas::1228.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1228.essence: True greatness can choose gentleness without losing power.
ramacharitamanas::1228.simple_meaning: Ram, who makes fear itself tremble, is showing the power of devotion by gently sending the boys away.
ramacharitamanas::1228.simple_insight: Even the highest power bows to loving devotion, not force.
ramacharitamanas::1228.detailed_meaning: At the yajna arena, Ram has already shown the boys the sacred arrangement and now turns them back with soft, loving words. The scene reveals something startling: the one before whom fear itself is afraid chooses tenderness and devotion over display of power.
ramacharitamanas::1228.modern_relevance: You have every reason to dominate the room, but you choose a gentle tone instead. That restraint often carries more strength than pressure ever could.
ramacharitamanas::1228.insight: It shifts attention from outward authority to the quiet force of loving conduct.

ramacharitamanas::1229.verse_sanskrit: सभय सप्रेम बिनीत अति सकुच सहित दोउ भाइ। गुर पद पंकज नाइ सिर बैठे आयसु पाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1229.verse_hindi: फिर भय, प्रेम, विनय और बड़े संकोच के साथ दोनों भाई गुरु के चरण कमलों में सिर नवाकर आज्ञा पाकर बैठे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1229.english_translation: Then, with fear, love, humility, and deep modesty, both brothers bowed their heads at the guru's lotus feet and sat down after receiving permission.
ramacharitamanas::1229.translation_literal: सभय (with reverence and fear) / सप्रेम (with love) / बिनीत (humble) / अति (very) / सकुच सहित (with deep modesty) / दोउ भाइ (both brothers) / गुर पद पंकज (the guru's lotus feet) / नाइ (bowing) / सिर (heads) / बैठे (sat) / आयसु (permission/command) / पाइ (having received)
ramacharitamanas::1229.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1229.simple_meaning: Both brothers bow to their teacher with love and humility, then sit only after receiving permission.
ramacharitamanas::1229.simple_insight: Respect begins with restraint. Even greatness softens before the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::1229.detailed_meaning: In Janak's sacrificial hall, Ram and Lakshman have just drawn the bow and stirred wonder. Before anything else, they bow to Vishvamitra, wait for his permission, and sit quietly. The moment shows how power stays disciplined by reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1229.modern_relevance: You finish presenting your work and still wait for your mentor's nod before speaking again. Confidence without humility feels loud; confidence with restraint feels complete.
ramacharitamanas::1229.insight: It teaches you to pause, bow, and receive direction before acting further.

ramacharitamanas::1230.verse_sanskrit: निसि प्रबेस मुनि आयसु दीन्हा। सबहीं संध्याबंदनु कीन्हा॥ कहत कथा इतिहास पुरानी। रुचिर रजनि जुग जाम सिरानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1230.verse_hindi: रात्रि का प्रवेश होते ही (संध्या के समय) मुनि ने आज्ञा दी, तब सबने संध्यावंदन किया। फिर प्राचीन कथाएँ तथा इतिहास कहते-कहते सुंदर रात्रि दो पहर बीत गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1230.english_translation: As night fell, the sage gave the order, and everyone performed the evening worship. Then they spent two watches of the beautiful night telling old stories and histories.
ramacharitamanas::1230.translation_literal: निसि (night) / प्रबेस (entry) / मुनि (sage) / आयसु (order) / दीन्हा (gave) / सबहीं (everyone) / संध्याबंदनु (evening worship) / कीन्हा (did) / कहत (telling) / कथा (stories) / इतिहास (histories) / पुरानी (old) / रुचिर (beautiful) / रजनि (night) / जुग (two) / जाम (watches) / सिरानी (passed)
ramacharitamanas::1230.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1230.essence: Evening worship and shared stories make the night sacred.
ramacharitamanas::1230.simple_meaning: Night falls, the sage gives the order, and everyone does evening worship. After that, they spend the night listening to old stories until two watches pass.
ramacharitamanas::1230.simple_insight: A sacred evening can turn into gentle companionship, worship, and shared remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::1230.detailed_meaning: In the forest hermitage, the day closes and the sage sets the evening discipline. Ram and Lakshman, with the others, complete their worship, then sit through the night listening to ancient stories. The verse simply marks this peaceful pause in the larger journey.
ramacharitamanas::1230.modern_relevance: The house goes quiet after dinner, phones are set aside, and an elder begins telling family stories no one wants to end. The evening becomes a small sanctuary.
ramacharitamanas::1230.insight: It shifts attention from action to shared rhythm, showing how discipline and story can steady a night.

ramacharitamanas::1231.verse_sanskrit: मुनिबर सयन कीन्हि तब जाई। लगे चरन चापन दोउ भाई॥ जिन्ह के चरन सरोरुह लागी। करत बिबिध जप जोग बिरागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1231.verse_hindi: तब श्रेष्ठ मुनि ने जाकर शयन किया। दोनों भाई उनके चरण दबाने लगे, जिनके चरण कमलों के (दर्शन एवं स्पर्श के) लिए वैराग्यवान् पुरुष भी भाँति-भाँति के जप और योग करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1231.english_translation: Then the great sage went to sleep. The two brothers began massaging his feet. Even renunciates perform many chants and disciplines to reach the lotus feet that bear his touch.
ramacharitamanas::1231.translation_literal: मुनिबर (great sage) / सयन (sleep) / कीन्हि (did) / तब (then) / जाई (going) / लगे (began) / चरन (feet) / चापन (to press/massage) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / जिन्ह (whose) / के (of) / चरन (feet) / सरोरुह (lotus) / लागी (for the sake of) / करत (doing) / बिबिध (various) / जप (chants) / जोग (yoga) / बिरागी (renunciates)
ramacharitamanas::1231.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1231.essence: Love kneels where pride would hesitate.
ramacharitamanas::1231.simple_meaning: The sage goes to sleep, and both brothers massage his feet. The verse praises those feet so highly that even renunciates seek them through chant and yoga.
ramacharitamanas::1231.simple_insight: Service becomes sacred when it is offered with love, not calculation.
ramacharitamanas::1231.detailed_meaning: In Vishvamitra’s camp, the evening has settled and the brothers have already taken their place beside their guru. After the sage lies down, Rama and Lakshmana quietly massage his feet. The verse pauses on the holiness of the guru’s feet, showing why even renunciates seek such nearness.
ramacharitamanas::1231.modern_relevance: You stay up beside an exhausted mentor after a long day, quietly helping however you can. No applause, no spotlight — just the dignity of serving well.
ramacharitamanas::1231.insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing that real devotion is expressed through humble service.

ramacharitamanas::1232.verse_sanskrit: तेइ दोउ बंधु प्रेम जनु जीते। गुर पद कमल पलोटत प्रीते॥ बार बार मुनि अग्या दीन्ही। रघुबर जाइ सयन तब कीन्ही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1232.verse_hindi: वे ही दोनों भाई मानो प्रेम से जीते हुए प्रेमपूर्वक गुरुजी के चरण कमलों को दबा रहे हैं। मुनि ने बार-बार आज्ञा दी, तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने जाकर शयन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1232.english_translation: Those two brothers were as if conquered by love, tenderly massaging the guru's lotus feet. Again and again the sage gave the command, and then Raghubar went to sleep.
ramacharitamanas::1232.translation_literal: तेइ (those) / दोउ (both) / बंधु (brothers) / प्रेम (love) / जनु (as if) / जीते (conquered) / गुर (guru's) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / पलोटत (massaging) / प्रीते (with affection) / बार बार (again and again) / मुनि (sage) / अग्या (command) / दीन्ही (gave) / रघुबर (Raghubar) / जाइ (going) / सयन (sleep) / तब (then) / कीन्ही (did)
ramacharitamanas::1232.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1232.essence: Love obeys through service and rests only when asked.
ramacharitamanas::1232.simple_meaning: The two brothers lovingly serve their teacher by massaging his feet. Only after the sage insists does Ram go to sleep.
ramacharitamanas::1232.simple_insight: Love shows itself in service, not in words.
ramacharitamanas::1232.detailed_meaning: At the sage's hermitage, both brothers stay awake to honor their teacher. They keep massaging his feet until he repeatedly tells them to rest. Only then does Ram finally lie down, showing reverence through action.
ramacharitamanas::1232.modern_relevance: You keep helping a mentor pack up after the workshop ends, even when they tell you to stop. Respect can look like quiet service, not grand speech.
ramacharitamanas::1232.insight: It shifts attention from claiming closeness to expressing it through humble care.

ramacharitamanas::1233.verse_sanskrit: चापत चरन लखनु उर लाएँ। सभय सप्रेम परम सचु पाएँ॥ पुनि पुनि प्रभु कह सोवहु ताता। पौढ़े धरि उर पद जलजाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1233.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के चरणों को हृदय से लगाकर भय और प्रेम सहित परम सुख का अनुभव करते हुए लक्ष्मणजी उनको दबा रहे हैं। प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने बार-बार कहा- हे तात! (अब) सो जाओ। तब वे उन चरण कमलों को हृदय में धरकर लेटे रहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1233.english_translation: Laxman pressed Ram's feet, holding them to his heart, and felt fearless, loving, and utterly fulfilled. Again and again, the Lord said, 'Sleep now, dear one.' Then he lay down with those lotus feet kept in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::1233.translation_literal: चापत (pressing) / चरन (feet) / लखनु (Laxman) / उर (heart/chest) / लाएँ (having brought) / सभय (fearless? with awe) / सप्रेम (with love) / परम (supreme) / सचु (truth / fulfillment) / पाएँ (having attained) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / प्रभु (Lord) / कह (said) / सोवहु (sleep) / ताता (dear one) / पौढ़े (lay down) / धरि (holding) / उर (heart/chest) / पद (feet) / जलजाता (lotus-born feet)
ramacharitamanas::1233.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1233.essence: Closeness to Ram makes even exhaustion feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::1233.simple_meaning: Laxman holds Ram's feet to his heart and feels complete. Ram keeps telling him to rest, but Laxman stays lying with those feet in his chest.
ramacharitamanas::1233.simple_insight: Love makes service feel like rest, not burden.
ramacharitamanas::1233.detailed_meaning: In the quiet after the guru has gone to sleep, Laxman keeps massaging Ram's feet with reverence. Ram gently tells him to sleep, but Laxman cannot let go of that closeness. The moment shows devotion so deep that service itself becomes fulfillment.
ramacharitamanas::1233.modern_relevance: You stay awake beside a loved one in the hospital, ignoring your own fatigue because caring for them feels more real than sleep. That is Laxman's tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::1233.insight: It shifts attention from self-care alone to the joy of devoted service.

ramacharitamanas::1234.verse_sanskrit: उठे लखनु निसि बिगत सुनि अरुनसिखा धुनि कान। गुर तें पहिलेहिं जगतपति जागे रामु सुजान ॥
ramacharitamanas::1234.verse_hindi: रात बीतने पर, मुर्गे का शब्द कानों से सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी उठे। जगत के स्वामी सुजान श्री रामचन्द्रजी भी गुरु से पहले ही जाग गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1234.english_translation: When night had passed and the rooster's cry was heard, Lakshman rose. Lord of the world, wise Ram awoke even before the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::1234.translation_literal: उठे (rose) / लखनु (Lakshman) / निसि (night) / बिगत (ended, passed) / सुनि (having heard) / अरुनसिखा (the red-combed rooster) / धुनि (sound) / कान (ears) / गुर तें (from the teacher) / पहिलेहिं (even before) / जगतपति (lord of the world) / जागे (awoke) / रामु (Ram) / सुजान (wise, all-knowing)
ramacharitamanas::1234.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1234.essence: True greatness wakes before everyone else.
ramacharitamanas::1234.simple_meaning: Lakshman rises at dawn, and Ram is already awake before the teacher. The verse shows their disciplined, attentive routine.
ramacharitamanas::1234.simple_insight: Quiet readiness is its own kind of strength.
ramacharitamanas::1234.detailed_meaning: At the teacher's hermitage, night has ended and the rooster calls. Lakshman rises first, and Ram, though the lord of the world, is already awake before the guru. The verse sets up their disciplined morning practice.
ramacharitamanas::1234.modern_relevance: The alarm goes off before sunrise, and you get up before the second snooze. No one is watching, but the day already belongs to your discipline.
ramacharitamanas::1234.insight: It shifts attention from sleep and comfort to alertness, readiness, and respect for order.

ramacharitamanas::1235.verse_sanskrit: सकल सौच करि जाइ नहाए। नित्य निबाहि मुनिहि सिर नाए॥ समय जानि गुर आयसु पाई। लेन प्रसून चले दोउ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1235.verse_hindi: सब शौचक्रिया करके वे जाकर नहाए। फिर (संध्या-अग्निहोत्रादि) नित्यकर्म समाप्त करके उन्होंने मुनि को मस्तक नवाया। (पूजा का) समय जानकर, गुरु की आज्ञा पाकर दोनों भाई फूल लेने चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1235.english_translation: After completing all cleansing rites, they bathed. After finishing their daily duties, they bowed to the sage. Knowing the proper time and receiving the teacher’s permission, both brothers went to gather flowers.
ramacharitamanas::1235.translation_literal: सकल (all) / सौच (purification) / करि (doing) / जाइ (going) / नहाए (bathed) / नित्य (daily) / निबाहि (having completed) / मुनिहि (to the sage) / सिर (head) / नाए (bowed) / समय (time) / जानि (knowing) / गुर (teacher) / आयसु (command) / पाई (having received) / लेन (to take) / प्रसून (flowers) / चले (went) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::1235.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1235.essence: Right action begins with cleansing, respect, and proper timing.
ramacharitamanas::1235.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman finish their morning cleansing, bow to the sage, wait for the proper time, receive permission from their teacher, and then go to gather flowers.
ramacharitamanas::1235.simple_insight: Order, respect, and timing matter. Even simple tasks become meaningful when done with discipline and permission.
ramacharitamanas::1235.detailed_meaning: At the sage’s hermitage, Ram and Lakshman begin the day with cleansing, bathing, and their regular duties. They bow before the sage, wait for the right moment, and only then go out to gather flowers. The scene shows their disciplined reverence before the next event unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::1235.modern_relevance: You finish your shower, silence your phone, and check in with the person guiding the project before starting. Even a small task goes better when you enter it with respect.
ramacharitamanas::1235.insight: It shifts action from impulse to disciplined timing and deference to guidance.

ramacharitamanas::1236.verse_sanskrit: भूप बागु बर देखेउ जाई। जहँ बसंत रितु रही लोभाई॥ लागे बिटप मनोहर नाना। बरन बरन बर बेलि बिताना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1236.verse_hindi: उन्होंने जाकर राजा का सुंदर बाग देखा, जहाँ वसंत ऋतु लुभाकर रह गई है। मन को लुभाने वाले अनेक वृक्ष लगे हैं। रंग-बिरंगी उत्तम लताओं के मंडप छाए हुए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1236.english_translation: They went and saw the king's beautiful garden, where spring itself seemed to linger in delight. Many charming trees stood there, and trellises of many-colored, excellent vines spread everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::1236.translation_literal: भूप (king's) / बागु (garden) / बर (beautiful) / देखेउ (saw) / जाई (going) / जहँ (where) / बसंत (spring) / रितु (season) / रही (remained) / लोभाई (alluring) / लागे (were placed) / बिटप (trees) / मनोहर (charming) / नाना (many) / बरन बरन (various colors) / बर (excellent) / बेलि (vines) / बिताना (trellises/canopies)
ramacharitamanas::1236.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1236.essence: Beauty fills the world before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::1236.simple_meaning: They entered a royal garden full of beautiful trees and colorful vines, so lovely that spring itself seemed to stay there.
ramacharitamanas::1236.simple_insight: Sometimes beauty is so complete it feels alive around you.
ramacharitamanas::1236.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have gone to fetch flowers for their teacher. Before any meeting or blessing, the story pauses on the royal garden they enter: a place overflowing with trees, vines, and springlike beauty. The scene prepares the mood for what follows.
ramacharitamanas::1236.modern_relevance: You step into a public garden at dawn, and everything looks almost unreal — the trees, the vines, the light. Before any task begins, the world itself seems to breathe.
ramacharitamanas::1236.insight: It slows the mind enough to notice sacred beauty before the next action begins.

ramacharitamanas::1237.verse_sanskrit: नव पल्लव फल सुमन सुहाए। निज संपति सुर रूख लजाए॥ चातक कोकिल कीर चकोरा। कूजत बिहग नटत कल मोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1237.verse_hindi: नए, पत्तों, फलों और फूलों से युक्त सुंदर वृक्ष अपनी सम्पत्ति से कल्पवृक्ष को भी लजा रहे हैं। पपीहे, कोयल, तोते, चकोर आदि पक्षी मीठी बोली बोल रहे हैं और मोर सुंदर नृत्य कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1237.english_translation: Fresh leaves, fruits, and flowers made the trees beautiful. Their abundance put even the wish-fulfilling tree to shame. Cuckoos, parrots, chakoras, and other birds sang sweetly, while peacocks danced gracefully.
ramacharitamanas::1237.translation_literal: नव (new) / पल्लव (young leaves) / फल (fruits) / सुमन (flowers) / सुहाए (became beautiful) / निज (own) / संपति (abundance) / सुर (divine) / रूख (tree) / लजाए (felt ashamed) / चातक (rain-bird) / कोकिल (cuckoo) / कीर (parrot) / चकोरा (chakora bird) / कूजत (singing) / बिहग (birds) / नटत (dancing) / कल (gracefully) / मोरा (peacocks)
ramacharitamanas::1237.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1237.essence: Nature’s abundance fills the garden with song and dance.
ramacharitamanas::1237.simple_meaning: The garden is overflowing with fresh beauty, sweet birdsong, and peacocks dancing. It is a rich, festive scene.
ramacharitamanas::1237.simple_insight: Beauty becomes most alive when it naturally overflows into sound, color, and movement.
ramacharitamanas::1237.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have entered a royal garden while gathering flowers for their teacher. The scene pauses on the garden itself: trees heavy with blossoms, birds singing, peacocks dancing. It is a lush description, not a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::1237.modern_relevance: You step into a quiet park after rain and notice everything seems to be showing off — the leaves, the flowers, the birds, even the air. The world can feel like that for a moment.
ramacharitamanas::1237.insight: It invites attention to abundance and sensory wonder before the story moves on.

ramacharitamanas::1238.verse_sanskrit: मध्य बाग सरु सोह सुहावा। मनि सोपान बिचित्र बनावा॥ बिमल सलिलु सरसिज बहुरंगा। जलखग कूजत गुंजत भृंगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1238.verse_hindi: बाग के बीचोंबीच सुहावना सरोवर सुशोभित है, जिसमें मणियों की सीढ़ियाँ विचित्र ढंग से बनी हैं। उसका जल निर्मल है, जिसमें अनेक रंगों के कमल खिले हुए हैं, जल के पक्षी कलरव कर रहे हैं और भ्रमर गुंजार कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1238.english_translation: In the middle of the garden stands a lovely lake, with wondrous stairways made of gems. Its water is clear, with many-colored lotuses blooming; water birds call, and bees hum.
ramacharitamanas::1238.translation_literal: मध्य (middle) / बाग (garden) / सरु (lake) / सोह (shines) / सुहावा (beautiful) / मनि (jewel) / सोपान (steps) / बिचित्र (wondrous) / बनावा (made) / बिमल (clear) / सलिलु (water) / सरसिज (lotus) / बहुरंगा (many-colored) / जलखग (water-birds) / कूजत (calling) / गुंजत (humming) / भृंगा (bees)
ramacharitamanas::1238.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1238.essence: The setting itself becomes part of the wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1238.simple_meaning: A beautiful lake sits in the center of the garden, with gem-like steps, clear water, colorful lotuses, birds, and bees all adding to its charm.
ramacharitamanas::1238.simple_insight: Beauty deepens when every part of a place feels alive and in harmony.
ramacharitamanas::1238.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are walking through a royal garden before the swayamvar. The scene lingers on the lake at its center: jeweled steps, clear water, lotuses, birds, and bees. It is vivid setting, building wonder before the next verse reveals Ram's delight.
ramacharitamanas::1238.modern_relevance: You step into a quiet public garden after a noisy commute and suddenly notice the pond, the lilies, the birds, the hum. The mind softens before it even tries.
ramacharitamanas::1238.insight: It trains attention to notice atmosphere, not just objects.

ramacharitamanas::1239.verse_sanskrit: बागु तड़ागु बिलोकि प्रभु हरषे बंधु समेत। परम रम्य आरामु यहु जो रामहि सुख देत ॥
ramacharitamanas::1239.verse_hindi: बाग और सरोवर को देखकर प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी भाई लक्ष्मण सहित हर्षित हुए। यह बाग (वास्तव में) परम रमणीय है, जो (जगत को सुख देने वाले) श्री रामचन्द्रजी को सुख दे रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1239.english_translation: Seeing the garden and lake, Lord Ram rejoiced with Lakshman. This garden is truly beautiful, bringing delight even to Ram, who gives delight to the world.
ramacharitamanas::1239.translation_literal: बागु (garden) / तड़ागु (lake) / बिलोकि (seeing) / प्रभु (Lord) / हरषे (rejoiced) / बंधु (brother) / समेत (together with) / परम (supreme) / रम्य (beautiful) / आरामु (garden) / यहु (this) / जो (which) / रामहि (to Ram) / सुख (joy) / देत (giving)
ramacharitamanas::1239.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1239.essence: Even Ram is delighted by beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1239.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman feel happy seeing the beautiful garden and lake. The place is so lovely that it seems to give joy even to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1239.simple_insight: Beauty can soften the heart and invite wonder before anything else happens.
ramacharitamanas::1239.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have entered the garden near the lake. The scene is lush, bright, and carefully prepared, and their delight shows the calm before Sita appears. This verse simply pauses to let the beauty of the place be felt.
ramacharitamanas::1239.modern_relevance: You walk into a quiet public garden after a long week and feel your shoulders drop. Before any conversation begins, the place itself has already changed your mood.
ramacharitamanas::1239.insight: It shifts attention from plot to atmosphere, showing how setting can prepare the mind for the next encounter.

ramacharitamanas::1240.verse_sanskrit: चहुँ दिसि चितइ पूँछि मालीगन। लगे लेन दल फूल मुदित मन॥ तेहि अवसर सीता तहँ आई। गिरिजा पूजन जननि पठाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1240.verse_hindi: चारों ओर दृष्टि डालकर और मालियों से पूछकर वे प्रसन्न मन से पत्र-पुष्प लेने लगे। उसी समय सीताजी वहाँ आईं। माता ने उन्हें गिरिजाजी (पार्वती) की पूजा करने के लिए भेजा था ॥
ramacharitamanas::1240.english_translation: Looking all around and asking the gardeners, they happily began gathering leaves and flowers. At that moment Sita arrived there, sent by her mother to worship Girija.
ramacharitamanas::1240.translation_literal: चहुँ दिसि (in all directions) / चितइ (looking) / पूँछि (asking) / मालीगन (the gardeners) / लगे (began) / लेन (to take) / दल (leaves) / फूल (flowers) / मुदित मन (with a joyful mind) / तेहि अवसर (at that moment) / सीता (Sita) / तहँ (there) / आई (came) / गिरिजा (Girija) / पूजन (worship) / जननि (mother) / पठाई (sent)
ramacharitamanas::1240.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1240.essence: A simple errand opens the door to a sacred meeting.
ramacharitamanas::1240.simple_meaning: The people gather flowers and leaves for worship, and Sita arrives at the same time, sent by her mother to honor Girija.
ramacharitamanas::1240.simple_insight: Small preparations can become sacred when the heart is already ready.
