ramacharitamanas::1240.detailed_meaning: In the garden by the lake, the gathering is still in motion. The people are asking the gardeners for flowers and leaves when Sita arrives, sent by her mother to worship Parvati. The verse simply moves the scene into the next sacred moment.
ramacharitamanas::1240.modern_relevance: You are hurrying to collect flowers before a family ritual begins, and someone you love walks in at the exact right moment. Ordinary errands can suddenly feel charged with meaning.
ramacharitamanas::1240.insight: It shifts attention from the task itself to the timing and grace woven through it.

ramacharitamanas::1241.verse_sanskrit: संग सखीं सब सुभग सयानीं। गावहिं गीत मनोहर बानीं॥ सर समीप गिरिजा गृह सोहा। बरनि न जाइ देखि मनु मोहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1241.verse_hindi: साथ में सब सुंदरी और सयानी सखियाँ हैं, जो मनोहर वाणी से गीत गा रही हैं। सरोवर के पास गिरिजाजी का मंदिर सुशोभित है, जिसका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता, देखकर मन मोहित हो जाता है॥।2॥
ramacharitamanas::1241.english_translation: All her beautiful, wise companions sang sweet songs. Near the lake, Girija's shrine shone; its beauty cannot be described, and the mind was enchanted at the sight.
ramacharitamanas::1241.translation_literal: संग (with) / सखीं (female companions) / सब (all) / सुभग (beautiful) / सयानीं (wise, grown) / गावहिं (sing) / गीत (songs) / मनोहर (lovely) / बानीं (words, voice) / सर (lake) / समीप (near) / गिरिजा (Girija) / गृह (house, shrine) / सोहा (shone, was beautiful) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाइ (can be) / देखि (seeing) / मनु (mind) / मोहा (was enchanted)
ramacharitamanas::1241.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1241.essence: A holy place can enchant the mind before any prayer begins.
ramacharitamanas::1241.simple_meaning: Sita arrives with her companions singing sweet songs. Near the lake, Girija's shrine is so beautiful that it leaves the mind spellbound.
ramacharitamanas::1241.simple_insight: Beauty can quiet the mind before a sacred moment begins.
ramacharitamanas::1241.detailed_meaning: Sita comes to the lake with her companions, all singing as they walk. The shrine of Girija near the water is glowing with beauty. This verse lingers on the setting, preparing the way for Sita's worship.
ramacharitamanas::1241.modern_relevance: You walk into a temple courtyard at dusk, and the lamps, flowers, and singing change your mood before you speak a word. The place itself prepares the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1241.insight: It shifts attention from action to atmosphere, showing how sacred space shapes the mind before prayer.

ramacharitamanas::1242.verse_sanskrit: मज्जनु करि सर सखिन्ह समेता। गई मुदित मन गौरि निकेता॥ पूजा कीन्हि अधिक अनुरागा। निज अनुरूप सुभग बरु मागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1242.verse_hindi: सखियों सहित सरोवर में स्नान करके सीताजी प्रसन्न मन से गिरिजाजी के मंदिर में गईं। उन्होंने बड़े प्रेम से पूजा की और अपने योग्य सुंदर वर माँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1242.english_translation: After bathing in the lake with her companions, Sita went joyfully to the shrine of Gauri. With deep love, she worshipped and asked for a beautiful bridegroom suited to her own nature.
ramacharitamanas::1242.translation_literal: मज्जनु (bathing) / करि (having done) / सर (lake) / सखिन्ह (with companions) / समेता (together) / गई (went) / मुदित (joyful) / मन (mind) / गौरि (Gauri) / निकेता (dwelling/shrine) / पूजा (worship) / कीन्हि (did) / अधिक (greatly) / अनुरागा (with love) / निज (own) / अनुरूप (suited) / सुभग (beautiful) / बरु (bridegroom) / मागा (asked)
ramacharitamanas::1242.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1242.essence: Pure prayer asks for what matches one’s nature.
ramacharitamanas::1242.simple_meaning: Sita bathes with her friends, goes happily to Gauri's shrine, worships with great love, and asks for a husband suited to her nature.
ramacharitamanas::1242.simple_insight: A sincere heart can ask for what it truly needs without shame.
ramacharitamanas::1242.detailed_meaning: At the shrine near the lake, Sita arrives with her companions during the Sita-swayamvar scene. She bathes, prays with deep feeling, and asks Gauri for a worthy husband. The moment quietly reveals her devotion, purity, and inner readiness.
ramacharitamanas::1242.modern_relevance: You light a candle before a big decision, not to control the future, but to ask for the right path with a steady heart.
ramacharitamanas::1242.insight: It frames desire through reverence, not grasping, and teaches the mind to ask cleanly for what aligns with dharma.

ramacharitamanas::1243.verse_sanskrit: एक सखी सिय संगु बिहाई। गई रही देखन फुलवाई॥ तेहिं दोउ बंधु बिलोके जाई। प्रेम बिबस सीता पहिं आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1243.verse_hindi: एक सखी सीताजी का साथ छोड़कर फुलवाड़ी देखने चली गई थी। उसने जाकर दोनों भाइयों को देखा और प्रेम में विह्वल होकर वह सीताजी के पास आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1243.english_translation: One companion left Sita's side and went to see the flower garden. There she saw the two brothers, and overwhelmed by love, she returned to Sita.
ramacharitamanas::1243.translation_literal: एक (one) / सखी (female companion) / सिय (Sita) / संगु (with) / बिहाई (leaving) / गई (went) / रही (having remained) / देखन (to see) / फुलवाई (flower garden) / तेहिं (that) / दोउ (both) / बंधु (brothers) / बिलोके (saw) / जाई (going) / प्रेम (love) / बिबस (overpowered) / सीता (Sita) / पहिं (to) / आई (came)
ramacharitamanas::1243.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1243.essence: A glimpse of Ram's grace can overwhelm the heart at once.
ramacharitamanas::1243.simple_meaning: A companion briefly leaves Sita, sees the two brothers, and returns overwhelmed with love.
ramacharitamanas::1243.simple_insight: A single glimpse can turn curiosity into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1243.detailed_meaning: At the flower garden near the swayamvar grounds, one of Sita's companions wanders off and sees the two brothers. Their presence strikes her so strongly that she cannot stay away and returns to Sita in a state of love-struck wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1243.modern_relevance: You walk into a room planning to stay detached, then one unexpected presence changes your whole mood. Some encounters do that instantly.
ramacharitamanas::1243.insight: It shows how presence can move the heart before thought has a chance to speak.

ramacharitamanas::1244.verse_sanskrit: तासु दसा देखी सखिन्ह पुलक गात जलु नैन। कहु कारनु निज हरष कर पूछहिं सब मृदु बैन ॥
ramacharitamanas::1244.verse_hindi: सखियों ने उसकी दशा देखी कि उसका शरीर पुलकित है और नेत्रों में जल भरा है। सब कोमल वाणी से पूछने लगीं कि अपनी प्रसन्नता का कारण बता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1244.english_translation: Seeing her condition, the friends saw her body thrill and tears fill her eyes. In soft words they asked, "Tell us the cause of your joy."
ramacharitamanas::1244.translation_literal: तासु (her) / दसा (condition) / देखी (seeing) / सखिन्ह (the friends) / पुलक (goosebumps, thrill) / गात (body) / जलु (water, tears) / नैन (eyes) / कहु (tell) / कारनु (cause) / निज (own) / हरष (joy) / कर (of) / पूछहिं (they ask) / सब (all) / मृदु (soft) / बैन (words)
ramacharitamanas::1244.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1244.essence: Love reveals itself before speech can catch up.
ramacharitamanas::1244.simple_meaning: Her friends notice her body trembling and her eyes filling with tears, and they gently ask what has made her so joyful.
ramacharitamanas::1244.simple_insight: Joy can be so full it spills into the body before words arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1244.detailed_meaning: In the flower garden at the swayamvar, Sita has just seen Ram and Lakshman. Her companions notice her trembling, tearful joy and softly press her to explain what has happened inside her.
ramacharitamanas::1244.modern_relevance: Your friend notices the sudden shine in your eyes after one glance across the room. Before you can hide it, they already know something has changed.
ramacharitamanas::1244.insight: It shows emotion becoming visible before explanation, preparing the scene for Sita's confession of love.

ramacharitamanas::1245.verse_sanskrit: देखन बागु कुअँर दुइ आए। बय किसोर सब भाँति सुहाए॥ स्याम गौर किमि कहौं बखानी। गिरा अनयन नयन बिनु बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1245.verse_hindi: (उसने कहा-) दो राजकुमार बाग देखने आए हैं। किशोर अवस्था के हैं और सब प्रकार से सुंदर हैं। वे साँवले और गोरे (रंग के) हैं, उनके सौंदर्य को मैं कैसे बखानकर कहूँ। वाणी बिना नेत्र की है और नेत्रों के वाणी नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1245.english_translation: Two princes have come to see the garden. They are young and beautiful in every way. How can I describe their beauty? Speech has no eyes, and eyes have no speech.
ramacharitamanas::1245.translation_literal: देखन (to see) / बागु (garden) / कुअँर (princes) / दुइ (two) / आए (came) / बय (age) / किसोर (youthful) / सब भाँति (in every way) / सुहाए (beautiful) / स्याम (dark-complexioned) / गौर (fair-complexioned) / किमि (how) / कहौं (shall I say) / बखानी (describe) / गिरा (speech) / अनयन (without eyes) / नयन (eyes) / बिनु (without) / बानी (speech)
ramacharitamanas::1245.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1245.essence: Beauty beyond words leaves only wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1245.simple_meaning: Two young princes have entered the garden, and their beauty is beyond description. The speaker can only say that words cannot fully capture what the eyes have seen.
ramacharitamanas::1245.simple_insight: Some beauty is so complete that language fails and wonder begins.
ramacharitamanas::1245.detailed_meaning: In the flower garden at Janakpur, a sakhi sees two young princes arrive. Their beauty overwhelms her, and she struggles to describe them to Sita and the other women. The verse pauses on that stunned admiration before the next revelation.
ramacharitamanas::1245.modern_relevance: You spot someone across a crowded station and forget your sentence halfway through. The mind goes quiet because the sight itself says more than language can hold.
ramacharitamanas::1245.insight: It shifts attention from explanation to direct seeing, letting wonder come before analysis.

ramacharitamanas::1246.verse_sanskrit: सुनि हरषीं सब सखीं सयानी। सिय हियँ अति उतकंठा जानी॥ एक कहइ नृपसुत तेइ आली। सुने जे मुनि सँग आए काली ॥
ramacharitamanas::1246.verse_hindi: यह सुनकर और सीताजी के हृदय में बड़ी उत्कंठा जानकर सब सयानी सखियाँ प्रसन्न हुईं। तब एक सखी कहने लगी- हे सखी! ये वही राजकुमार हैं, जो सुना है कि कल विश्वामित्र मुनि के साथ आए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1246.english_translation: Hearing this, all the wise companions were delighted and sensed Sita's intense eagerness. Then one companion said, 'O friend, these are the same princes said to have come yesterday with the sage Vishvamitra.'
ramacharitamanas::1246.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / हरषीं (became joyful) / सब (all) / सखीं (companions) / सयानी (wise) / सिय (Sita's) / हियँ (in the heart) / अति (very) / उतकंठा (eagerness) / जानी (known)॥ / एक (one) / कहइ (says) / नृपसुत (king's sons) / तेइ (those) / आली (friend) / सुने (heard) / जे (who) / मुनि (sage) / सँग (with) / आए (came) / काली (yesterday)॥
ramacharitamanas::1246.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1246.essence: Longing becomes visible to those who know how to look.
ramacharitamanas::1246.simple_meaning: The companions realize Sita is longing deeply, and one of them identifies the princes as the same boys who arrived yesterday with Vishvamitra.
ramacharitamanas::1246.simple_insight: Shared excitement can notice what private longing is trying to say.
ramacharitamanas::1246.detailed_meaning: In Janak's garden, Sita has just seen the princes and fallen into silent longing. Her wise companions read her heart at once. They gently confirm that these are the same royal boys who came with Vishvamitra yesterday.
ramacharitamanas::1246.modern_relevance: You glance at a friend across the room and instantly know something has changed in them. A close companion notices before words arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1246.insight: It shows how devotion often begins as recognition: the heart knows before the mouth speaks.

ramacharitamanas::1247.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह निज रूप मोहनी डारी। कीन्हे स्वबस नगर नर नारी॥ बरनत छबि जहँ तहँ सब लोगू। अवसि देखिअहिं देखन जोगू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1247.verse_hindi: और जिन्होंने अपने रूप की मोहिनी डालकर नगर के स्त्री-पुरुषों को अपने वश में कर लिया है। जहाँ-तहाँ सब लोग उन्हीं की छबि का वर्णन कर रहे हैं। अवश्य (चलकर) उन्हें देखना चाहिए, वे देखने ही योग्य हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1247.english_translation: Those who have cast the spell of their own beauty over the city have brought the men and women under their sway. Everyone everywhere is speaking of their radiance; surely they are worth seeing.
ramacharitamanas::1247.translation_literal: जिन्ह (those who) / निज रूप (their own form) / मोहनी (spell of beauty) / डारी (cast) / कीन्हे (made) / स्वबस (under their control) / नगर (city) / नर (men) / नारी (women) ॥ / बरनत (describing) / छबि (beauty, radiance) / जहँ तहँ (here and there, everywhere) / सब लोगू (all people) / अवसि (certainly) / देखिअहिं (should be seen) / देखन जोगू (worthy of seeing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1247.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1247.essence: True radiance draws people in before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1247.simple_meaning: Their beauty has captivated the whole city. Everyone is talking about them, and all agree they must be seen.
ramacharitamanas::1247.simple_insight: Some presence is so compelling that people move toward it before they even know why.
ramacharitamanas::1247.detailed_meaning: At Mithila, Sita’s friends hear that two radiant princes have entered the city. Their beauty has already stirred everyone’s attention, and the women around Sita are urging her to go see them. This verse builds the anticipation before the first direct glimpse.
ramacharitamanas::1247.modern_relevance: You hear a room go quiet when someone rare walks in. No one needs to explain why they matter; the atmosphere already knows.
ramacharitamanas::1247.insight: It heightens anticipation by showing that true presence announces itself before words do.

ramacharitamanas::1248.verse_sanskrit: तासु बचन अति सियहि सोहाने। दरस लागि लोचन अकुलाने॥ चली अग्र करि प्रिय सखि सोई। प्रीति पुरातन लखइ न कोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1248.verse_hindi: उसके वचन सीताजी को अत्यन्त ही प्रिय लगे और दर्शन के लिए उनके नेत्र अकुला उठे। उसी प्यारी सखी को आगे करके सीताजी चलीं। पुरानी प्रीति को कोई लख नहीं पाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1248.english_translation: Her words delighted Sita deeply, and her eyes grew restless to see him. She moved forward with that dear friend leading the way. No one can fully trace an old, hidden love.
ramacharitamanas::1248.translation_literal: तासु (of that) / बचन (words) / अति (very) / सियहि (to Sita) / सोहाने (became pleasing) / दरस (for sight) / लागि (for) / लोचन (eyes) / अकुलाने (became restless) / चली (she went) / अग्र (ahead) / करि (making) / प्रिय (dear) / सखि (friend) / सोई (that same) / प्रीति (love) / पुरातन (ancient) / लखइ (sees) / न (not) / कोई (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::1248.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1248.essence: Love moves first in the heart, long before anyone else can name it.
ramacharitamanas::1248.simple_meaning: Sita feels deep joy at those words and becomes eager to see Ram. She walks forward with her dear friend leading, moved by an old love that no one else can fully understand.
ramacharitamanas::1248.simple_insight: Real devotion often begins as a quiet, private recognition before it becomes visible to others.
ramacharitamanas::1248.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, after Narad's hint and the maidens' excited talk, Sita hears words that awaken something ancient in her heart. She cannot stay still. Guided by a trusted friend, she moves toward the sight of Ram, while the depth of her feeling remains hidden from everyone else.
ramacharitamanas::1248.modern_relevance: You hear a name, a song, or a voice message and something in you instantly leans forward. No one else sees why, but your heart already knows.
ramacharitamanas::1248.insight: It shifts attention from public explanation to the private pull of devotion.

ramacharitamanas::1249.verse_sanskrit: सुमिरि सीय नारद बचन उपजी प्रीति पुनीत। चकित बिलोकति सकल दिसि जनु सिसु मृगी सभीत ॥
ramacharitamanas::1249.verse_hindi: नारदजी के वचनों का स्मरण करके सीताजी के मन में पवित्र प्रीति उत्पन्न हुई। वे चकित होकर सब ओर इस तरह देख रही हैं, मानो डरी हुई मृगछौनी इधर-उधर देख रही हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1249.english_translation: Remembering Narad's words, Sita's heart filled with pure love. She looked in every direction in astonishment, like a frightened fawn glancing around.
ramacharitamanas::1249.translation_literal: सुमिरि (remembering) / सीय (Sita) / नारद (Narad) / बचन (words) / उपजी (arose) / प्रीति (love) / पुनीत (pure) / चकित (astonished) / बिलोकति (looking) / सकल (all) / दिसि (directions) / जनु (as if) / सिसु (fawn) / मृगी (doe) / सभीत (afraid)
ramacharitamanas::1249.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1249.essence: Pure love makes the heart both fearless and shy.
ramacharitamanas::1249.simple_meaning: Sita remembers Narad's words, and pure love rises in her heart. She looks around in startled wonder, like a frightened young deer.
ramacharitamanas::1249.simple_insight: Love can make the heart alert, tender, and beautifully uncertain all at once.
ramacharitamanas::1249.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Sita has just heard words that awaken her devotion and longing. Narad's reminder stirs her heart so deeply that she turns in wonder, searching the world with the innocence of a deer.
ramacharitamanas::1249.modern_relevance: You reread a message that changed everything, then stare out the window before answering. The heart knows before the mind does.
ramacharitamanas::1249.insight: It shows how devotion begins as a startled, tender attentiveness rather than a settled certainty.

ramacharitamanas::1250.verse_sanskrit: कंकन किंकिनि नूपुर धुनि सुनि। कहत लखन सन रामु हृदयँ गुनि॥ मानहुँ मदन दुंदुभी दीन्ही। मनसा बिस्व बिजय कहँ कीन्ही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1250.verse_hindi: कंकण (हाथों के कड़े), करधनी और पायजेब के शब्द सुनकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी हृदय में विचार कर लक्ष्मण से कहते हैं- (यह ध्वनि ऐसी आ रही है) मानो कामदेव ने विश्व को जीतने का संकल्प करके डंके पर चोट मारी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1250.english_translation: Hearing the sound of bracelets, anklets, and waist-bells, Ram thought in his heart and said to Lakshman: it is as if Cupid has sounded his drum, declaring a vow to conquer the world.
ramacharitamanas::1250.translation_literal: कंकन (bracelets) / किंकिनि (small bells) / नूपुर (anklets) / धुनि (sound) / सुनि (hearing) / कहत (saying) / लखन सन (to Lakshman) / रामु (Ram) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / गुनि (having thought) / मानहुँ (as if) / मदन (Cupid) / दुंदुभी (drum) / दीन्ही (gave) / मनसा (with intention) / बिस्व (world) / बिजय (victory) / कहँ (for) / कीन्ही (made)
ramacharitamanas::1250.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1250.essence: Desire announces itself before the eyes ever meet it.
ramacharitamanas::1250.simple_meaning: Ram hears the ornaments before he sees anyone, and he recognizes the approach of beauty. He compares the sound to Cupid announcing his aim to conquer the world.
ramacharitamanas::1250.simple_insight: Even a small sound can stir the heart before the eyes see anything.
ramacharitamanas::1250.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the women of the palace are approaching for the swayamvar. Ram hears their ornaments first and quietly remarks to Lakshman on the power of that sound. The verse builds the mood before Ram turns to see Sita.
ramacharitamanas::1250.modern_relevance: You hear someone laughing in the next room before you walk in, and your attention shifts instantly. The mind knows desire and beauty by sound before reason catches up.
ramacharitamanas::1250.insight: It sharpens attention to the mind's quick response to attraction before full sight or judgment arrives.

ramacharitamanas::1251.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि फिरि चितए तेहि ओरा। सिय मुख ससि भए नयन चकोरा॥ भए बिलोचन चारु अचंचल। मनहुँ सकुचि निमि तजे दिगंचल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1251.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर श्री रामजी ने फिर कर उस ओर देखा। श्री सीताजी के मुख रूपी चन्द्रमा (को निहारने) के लिए उनके नेत्र चकोर बन गए। सुंदर नेत्र स्थिर हो गए (टकटकी लग गई)। मानो निमि (जनकजी के पूर्वज) ने (जिनका सबकी पलकों में निवास माना गया है, लड़की-दामाद के मिलन-प्रसंग को देखना उचित नहीं, इस भाव से) सकुचाकर पलकें छोड़ दीं, (पलकों में रहना छोड़ दिया, जिससे पलकों का गिरना रुक गया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1251.english_translation: After saying this, Ram looked back toward her. Sita's face became a moon, and his eyes became chakoras for that moon. His lovely eyes stayed still, as if Nimi, ashamed, had left the eyelids.
ramacharitamanas::1251.translation_literal: अस कहि (saying thus) / फिरि (again) / चितए (looked) / तेहि ओरा (toward that side) । सिय (Sita's) / मुख (face) / ससि (moon) / भए (became) / नयन (eyes) / चकोरा (chakora birds) । भए (became) / बिलोचन (eyes) / चारु (beautiful) / अचंचल (unmoving) । मनहुँ (as if) / सकुचि (having shied away) / निमि (Nimi) / तजे (left) / दिगंचल (eyelids)
ramacharitamanas::1251.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1251.essence: True seeing holds still when love is present.
ramacharitamanas::1251.simple_meaning: Ram turns to look at Sita again, and both are lost in each other’s beauty. His eyes do not move, as if even blinking has stopped out of reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1251.simple_insight: Love can quiet the whole body until only attention remains.
ramacharitamanas::1251.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court after the bow-breaking, Ram looks back toward Sita. Her face is compared to the moon, his eyes to chakoras that live for moonlight. The moment is not action but mutual wonder, and the scene pauses in silence before words return.
ramacharitamanas::1251.modern_relevance: You catch someone across a crowded room and forget the noise around you. For one suspended second, attention itself becomes devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1251.insight: It shifts attention from outer activity to inward absorption, where seeing itself becomes an act of reverence.

ramacharitamanas::1252.verse_sanskrit: देखि सीय शोभा सुखु पावा। हृदयँ सराहत बचनु न आवा॥ जनु बिरंचि सब निज निपुनाई। बिरचि बिस्व कहँ प्रगटि देखाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1252.verse_hindi: सीताजी की शोभा देखकर श्री रामजी ने बड़ा सुख पाया। हृदय में वे उसकी सराहना करते हैं, किन्तु मुख से वचन नहीं निकलते। (वह शोभा ऐसी अनुपम है) मानो ब्रह्मा ने अपनी सारी निपुणता को मूर्तिमान कर संसार को प्रकट करके दिखा दिया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1252.english_translation: Seeing Sita's beauty, Ram felt deep joy. He praised her inwardly, but no words came to his lips. Her beauty seemed like Brahma had displayed all his skill by revealing the world itself.
ramacharitamanas::1252.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / सीय (Sita) / शोभा (beauty, grace) / सुखु (joy) / पावा (received) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / सराहत (praising) / बचनु (words) / न (not) / आवा (came) / जनु (as if) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / सब (all) / निज (own) / निपुनाई (skill, mastery) / बिरचि (creating) / बिस्व (world) / कहँ (for) / प्रगटि (manifested) / देखाई (showed)
ramacharitamanas::1252.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1252.essence: True beauty leaves even praise speechless.
ramacharitamanas::1252.simple_meaning: Ram is overwhelmed by Sita's beauty and can only admire her inwardly. Her grace is compared to the creator's finest work made visible in the world.
ramacharitamanas::1252.simple_insight: Some beauty is so complete that praise falls silent.
ramacharitamanas::1252.detailed_meaning: In the swayamvar hall, Ram has just turned to look at Sita. Her presence fills him with delight so deep that speech stops. The verse pauses on that silent wonder before the next line expands her beauty into a cosmic comparison.
ramacharitamanas::1252.modern_relevance: You catch sight of someone across a crowded room and forget your sentence mid-thought. Some moments do that: they leave admiration too full for language.
ramacharitamanas::1252.insight: It shifts attention from speaking about beauty to feeling its power directly.

ramacharitamanas::1253.verse_sanskrit: सुंदरता कहुँ सुंदर करई। छबिगृहँ दीपसिखा जनु बरई॥ सब उपमा कबि रहे जुठारी। केहिं पटतरौं बिदेहकुमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1253.verse_hindi: वह (सीताजी की शोभा) सुंदरता को भी सुंदर करने वाली है। (वह ऐसी मालूम होती है) मानो सुंदरता रूपी घर में दीपक की लौ जल रही हो। (अब तक सुंदरता रूपी भवन में अँधेरा था, वह भवन मानो सीताजी की सुंदरता रूपी दीपशिखा को पाकर जगमगा उठा है, पहले से भी अधिक सुंदर हो गया है)। सारी उपमाओं को तो कवियों ने जूँठा कर रखा है। मैं जनकनन्दिनी श्री सीताजी की किससे उपमा दूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1253.english_translation: Beauty itself becomes more beautiful. Like a lamp flame burning in a house of beauty. Poets have exhausted every comparison. What can compare with Janak's daughter?
ramacharitamanas::1253.translation_literal: सुंदरता (beauty) / कहुँ (for) / सुंदर (beautiful) / करई (makes) / छबिगृहँ (in the house of beauty) / दीपसिखा (lamp-flame) / जनु (like) / बरई (burns) / सब (all) / उपमा (comparisons) / कबि (poets) / रहे (have remained) / जुठारी (left-over, exhausted) / केहिं (to whom) / पटतरौं (comparison) / बिदेहकुमारी (Janak's daughter)
ramacharitamanas::1253.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1253.essence: Sita's presence makes every comparison collapse.
ramacharitamanas::1253.simple_meaning: Sita's beauty outshines every comparison. It makes beauty itself seem more beautiful, and language runs out trying to describe her.
ramacharitamanas::1253.simple_insight: Some things exceed description. You stop analyzing and simply stand in awe.
ramacharitamanas::1253.detailed_meaning: At the Sita-swayamvar, Ram has just seen Sita and fallen into silent wonder. This verse is the poet's overflow: even beauty seems transformed by her presence, and every comparison fails before Janak's daughter.
ramacharitamanas::1253.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence makes the whole room feel different. Your usual words feel thin, and for once the right response is silence, not explanation.
ramacharitamanas::1253.insight: It shifts attention from naming beauty to feeling its power directly.

ramacharitamanas::1254.verse_sanskrit: सिय शोभा हियँ बरनि प्रभु आपनि दसा बिचारि॥ बोले सुचि मन अनुज सन बचन समय अनुहारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1254.verse_hindi: (इस प्रकार) हृदय में सीताजी की शोभा का वर्णन करके और अपनी दशा को विचारकर प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी पवित्र मन से अपने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण से समयानुकूल वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1254.english_translation: After praising Sita's beauty in his heart and considering his own situation, the Lord spoke to his younger brother Lakshman with a pure mind, in words suited to the moment.
ramacharitamanas::1254.translation_literal: सिय (Sita) / शोभा (beauty, splendor) / हियँ (in the heart) / बरनि (describing, praising) / प्रभु (the Lord) / आपनि (his own) / दसा (condition, situation) / बिचारि (having considered) / बोले (spoke) / सुचि (pure) / मन (mind) / अनुज (younger brother) / सन (to) / बचन (words) / समय (time, moment) / अनुहारि (suited to)
ramacharitamanas::1254.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1254.essence: Feeling deeply and speaking rightly can happen in the same breath.
ramacharitamanas::1254.simple_meaning: Ram quietly reflects on Sita and on his own position, then speaks to Lakshman with a calm, fitting response.
ramacharitamanas::1254.simple_insight: A steady mind can meet a charged moment without losing its purity.
ramacharitamanas::1254.detailed_meaning: At the swayamvar, Ram has just seen Sita and feels her beauty deeply. He pauses, takes in his own situation, and then turns to Lakshman. The verse shows the inward composure that precedes his first spoken response.
ramacharitamanas::1254.modern_relevance: You notice something beautiful, feel the pull of it, and still choose your words carefully. That pause before speaking can keep a moment from becoming chaos.
ramacharitamanas::1254.insight: It teaches you to let feeling settle before responding, so your words match the moment instead of your impulse.

ramacharitamanas::1255.verse_sanskrit: तात जनकतनया यह सोई। धनुषजग्य जेहि कारन होई॥ पूजन गौरि सखीं लै आईं। करत प्रकासु फिरइ फुलवाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1255.verse_hindi: हे तात! यह वही जनकजी की कन्या है, जिसके लिए धनुषयज्ञ हो रहा है। सखियाँ इसे गौरी पूजन के लिए ले आई हैं। यह फुलवाड़ी में प्रकाश करती हुई फिर रही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1255.english_translation: O father, this is the same daughter of Janaka for whom the bow sacrifice is being held. The maidens brought her for the worship of Gauri, and she moves through the flower-grove like light itself.
ramacharitamanas::1255.translation_literal: तात (father) / जनकतनया (daughter of Janaka) / यह (this) / सोई (the same) / धनुषजग्य (bow-sacrifice) / जेहि (for whom) / कारन (cause) / होई (is happening)॥ / पूजन (worship) / गौरि (Gauri) / सखीं (maidens) / लै (taking) / आईं (brought)॥ / करत (doing) / प्रकासु (light) / फिरइ (moves around) / फुलवाईं (flower-grove)॥
ramacharitamanas::1255.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1255.essence: Beauty becomes clear when it is seen with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1255.simple_meaning: Ram recognizes Sita as Janaka’s daughter and explains why she is there: the bow ceremony and the Gauri worship. He sees her moving through the flower-grove like radiant light.
ramacharitamanas::1255.simple_insight: A single glimpse can stop the mind. Beauty becomes clearer when it is seen with reverence, not possession.
ramacharitamanas::1255.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s flower-grove, Ram sees Sita among the maidens. He tells Lakshman that she is the princess for whom the bow-sacrifice is being held and that she has come for Gauri worship. The moment matters because his first sight of her becomes recognition, not mere admiration.
ramacharitamanas::1255.modern_relevance: You spot someone across a crowded temple courtyard and everything else blurs. The mind does not just notice beauty; it searches for meaning, reverence, and the story behind the face.
ramacharitamanas::1255.insight: It shifts attention from surface attraction to sacred recognition.

ramacharitamanas::1256.verse_sanskrit: जासु बिलोकि अलौकिक सोभा। सहज पुनीत मोर मनु छोभा॥ सो सबु कारन जान बिधाता। फरकहिं सुभद अंग सुनु भ्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1256.verse_hindi: जिसकी अलौकिक सुंदरता देखकर स्वभाव से ही पवित्र मेरा मन क्षुब्ध हो गया है। वह सब कारण (अथवा उसका सब कारण) तो विधाता जानें, किन्तु हे भाई! सुनो, मेरे मंगलदायक (दाहिने) अंग फड़क रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1256.english_translation: Seeing her wondrous beauty, my naturally pure mind was stirred. The cause of it all only the Creator knows, brother; listen, my auspicious right limbs are twitching.
ramacharitamanas::1256.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / बिलोकि (seeing) / अलौकिक (unworldly) / सोभा (beauty) / सहज (natural) / पुनीत (pure) / मोर (my) / मनु (mind) / छोभा (was stirred) / सो (that) / सबु (all) / कारन (cause) / जान (knows) / बिधाता (the Creator) / फरकहिं (twitch) / सुभद (auspicious) / अंग (limbs) / सुनु (listen) / भ्राता (brother)
ramacharitamanas::1256.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1256.essence: Pure seeing can still shake the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1256.simple_meaning: Ram sees Sita’s extraordinary beauty and feels his pure mind stirred. He says the cause is known only to the Creator and notices auspicious signs in his body.
ramacharitamanas::1256.simple_insight: Even a steady heart can be moved by beauty without losing its purity.
ramacharitamanas::1256.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s swayamvar, Ram has just seen Sita. Her beauty shakes him, yet his mind remains naturally pure. He tells Lakshman that only the Creator knows why this happens, while his right limbs twitch with an auspicious omen.
ramacharitamanas::1256.modern_relevance: You meet someone and feel your composure break for a moment. The feeling is real, but it does not have to make you careless or confused.
ramacharitamanas::1256.insight: It shifts attention from control to reverent recognition: some encounters move you before you can explain them.

ramacharitamanas::1257.verse_sanskrit: रघुबंसिन्ह कर सहज सुभाऊ। मनु कुपंथ पगु धरइ न काऊ॥ मोहि अतिसय प्रतीति मन केरी। जेहिं सपनेहुँ परनारि न हेरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1257.verse_hindi: रघुवंशियों का यह सहज (जन्मगत) स्वभाव है कि उनका मन कभी कुमार्ग पर पैर नहीं रखता। मुझे तो अपने मन का अत्यन्त ही विश्वास है कि जिसने (जाग्रत की कौन कहे) स्वप्न में भी पराई स्त्री पर दृष्टि नहीं डाली है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1257.english_translation: The natural nature of Raghu's line is this: the mind never steps onto the wrong path. I trust my own mind completely, for it has never looked at another man's wife even in a dream.
ramacharitamanas::1257.translation_literal: रघुबंसिन्ह (of Raghu's line) / कर (of) / सहज सुभाऊ (natural nature) / मनु (mind) / कुपंथ (wrong path) / पगु (foot) / धरइ (places) / न (not) / काऊ (anyone)॥ / मोहि (to me) / अतिसय (great) / प्रतीति (trust) / मन केरी (of the mind) / जेहिं (which) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / परनारि (another man's wife) / न (not) / हेरी (looked at)
ramacharitamanas::1257.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::1257.simple_meaning: Ravana says that the people of Raghu's line naturally avoid wrongdoing, and he trusts his own mind because it has never even glanced at another man's wife in a dream.
ramacharitamanas::1257.simple_insight: Pride can sound like self-knowledge, even while it blinds a person to his own weakness.
ramacharitamanas::1257.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Ravana has come in disguise to judge Sita's beauty and speak of himself. He praises the noble discipline of Raghu's line and claims his own mind is pure, even as the scene quietly exposes the arrogance that will lead him astray.
ramacharitamanas::1257.modern_relevance: Someone says, "I know myself too well to fall for that," right before making the exact mistake they swore they would avoid. Confidence can hide the blind spot.
ramacharitamanas::1257.insight: It shifts attention from declared self-control to the deeper question of whether the mind is actually clear.

ramacharitamanas::1258.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह कै लहहिं न रिपु रन पीठी। नहिं पावहिं परतिय मनु डीठी॥ मंगन लहहिं न जिन्ह कै नाहीं। ते नरबर थोरे जग माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1258.verse_hindi: रण में शत्रु जिनकी पीठ नहीं देख पाते (अर्थात् जो लड़ाई के मैदान से भागते नहीं), पराई स्त्रियाँ जिनके मन और दृष्टि को नहीं खींच पातीं और भिखारी जिनके यहाँ से 'नाहीं' नहीं पाते (खाली हाथ नहीं लौटते), ऐसे श्रेष्ठ पुरुष संसार में थोड़े हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1258.english_translation: Rare in the world are noble men whom enemies cannot see fleeing from battle, whose minds and eyes are not drawn to another man's wife, and whose doors never send a beggar away empty-handed.
ramacharitamanas::1258.translation_literal: जिन्ह कै (whose) / लहहिं न (do not get) / रिपु (enemy) / रन (battle) / पीठी (back) / नहिं (not) / पावहिं (obtain) / परतिय (another man's wife) / मनु (mind) / डीठी (sight) / मंगन (beggar) / लहहिं न (do not get) / जिन्ह कै (whose) / नाहीं (no / not) / ते (those) / नरबर (noble men) / थोरे (few) / जग (world) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::1258.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1258.essence: Nobility shows itself in courage, purity, and generosity.
ramacharitamanas::1258.simple_meaning: Truly noble people do not run from battle, do not chase another man's wife, and do not send beggars away empty-handed.
ramacharitamanas::1258.simple_insight: Honor is measured by courage, restraint, and generosity together.
ramacharitamanas::1258.detailed_meaning: Ram speaks with Lakshman while Sita's beauty still stirs his mind. He names the qualities of a truly noble person: steady in danger, pure in desire, and open-handed toward the needy. The verse sets a moral standard, not a battle report.
ramacharitamanas::1258.modern_relevance: You see someone panic under pressure, flirt where they shouldn't, and ignore the person asking for help at the door. This verse cuts through that mess and names real character: steadiness, self-control, and generosity.
ramacharitamanas::1258.insight: It trains the mind to judge character by conduct under pressure, not by status or talk.

ramacharitamanas::1259.verse_sanskrit: करत बतकही अनुज सन मन सिय रूप लोभान। मुख सरोज मकरंद छबि करइ मधुप इव पान ॥
ramacharitamanas::1259.verse_hindi: यों श्री रामजी छोटे भाई से बातें कर रहे हैं, पर मन सीताजी के रूप में लुभाया हुआ उनके मुखरूपी कमल के छबि रूप मकरंद रस को भौंरे की तरह पी रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1259.english_translation: While talking with his younger brother, Ram's mind is captivated by Sita's beauty. Like a bee, he drinks the nectar of his lotus-like face.
ramacharitamanas::1259.translation_literal: करत (doing) / बतकही (conversation) / अनुज सन (with the younger brother) / मन (mind) / सिय रूप (Sita's form) / लोभान (was captivated) / मुख (face) / सरोज (lotus) / मकरंद (nectar) / छबि (beauty) / करइ (does) / मधुप इव (like a bee) / पान (drinking)
ramacharitamanas::1259.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1259.essence: The heart drinks beauty even while the mouth speaks elsewhere.
ramacharitamanas::1259.simple_meaning: Ram is speaking with Lakshman, but his attention keeps drifting to Sita's beauty. The image compares his gaze to a bee drawn to nectar.
ramacharitamanas::1259.simple_insight: Love can split attention without breaking devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1259.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, Ram is speaking casually with Lakshman while Sita is nearby. The poet quietly reveals that even in conversation, Ram's heart is drawn to her beauty. The verse captures the first tender pull between them.
ramacharitamanas::1259.modern_relevance: You are answering someone politely, but your eyes keep drifting to the person across the room. The body stays in the moment; the mind has already fallen elsewhere.
ramacharitamanas::1259.insight: It shows how attraction can shape attention before any words are spoken.

ramacharitamanas::1260.verse_sanskrit: चितवति चकित चहूँ दिसि सीता। कहँ गए नृप किसोर मनु चिंता॥ जहँ बिलोक मृग सावक नैनी। जनु तहँ बरिस कमल सित श्रेनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1260.verse_hindi: सीताजी चकित होकर चारों ओर देख रही हैं। मन इस बात की चिन्ता कर रहा है कि राजकुमार कहाँ चले गए। बाल मृगनयनी (मृग के छौने की सी आँख वाली) सीताजी जहाँ दृष्टि डालती हैं, वहाँ मानो श्वेत कमलों की कतार बरस जाती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1260.english_translation: Sita, startled, looks in all directions. Her mind wonders where the prince has gone. Wherever the doe-eyed maiden looks, it is as if rows of white lotuses rain down there.
ramacharitamanas::1260.translation_literal: चितवति (looking) / चकित (startled) / चहूँ दिसि (in all four directions) / सीता (Sita) / कहँ (where) / गए (went) / नृप किसोर (prince) / मनु (mind) / चिंता (anxious thought)॥ / जहँ (where) / बिलोक (she sees) / मृग सावक (deer-calf) / नैनी (eyed one) / जनु (as if) / तहँ (there) / बरिस (rain) / कमल (lotus) / सित (white) / श्रेनी (rows)
ramacharitamanas::1260.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1260.essence: Longing sharpens sight, and absence becomes the strongest presence.
ramacharitamanas::1260.simple_meaning: Sita looks around in surprise and worries about where Ram has gone. Her beauty is so gentle that wherever she looks, it seems to bloom with white lotuses.
ramacharitamanas::1260.simple_insight: Love makes absence feel immediate, and even a glance can seem to brighten the world.
ramacharitamanas::1260.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, Sita stands among the gathering and suddenly cannot see Ram nearby. She looks around anxiously, and Tulsidas lingers on her beauty: her deer-like eyes seem to make white lotuses fall wherever they rest.
ramacharitamanas::1260.modern_relevance: You scan a crowded wedding hall for one face and feel the room tighten when you do not find it. The mind goes to the missing person first; everything else fades.
ramacharitamanas::1260.insight: It shifts attention from the crowd to the ache of separation, making longing the center of the scene.

ramacharitamanas::1261.verse_sanskrit: लता ओट तब सखिन्ह लखाए। स्यामल गौर किसोर सुहाए॥ देखि रूप लोचन ललचाने। हरषे जनु निज निधि पहिचाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1261.verse_hindi: तब सखियों ने लता की ओट में सुंदर श्याम और गौर कुमारों को दिखलाया। उनके रूप को देखकर नेत्र ललचा उठे, वे ऐसे प्रसन्न हुए मानो उन्होंने अपना खजाना पहचान लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1261.english_translation: Then the maidens showed them from behind the vines: the handsome dark-complexioned and fair-complexioned princes. Seeing their beauty, their eyes were captivated; they rejoiced as if they had recognized their own treasure.
ramacharitamanas::1261.translation_literal: लता (vine) / ओट (cover) / तब (then) / सखिन्ह (by the maidens) / लखाए (were shown) / स्यामल (dark-complexioned) / गौर (fair-complexioned) / किसोर (princes/youths) / सुहाए (beautiful) ॥ देखि (seeing) / रूप (beauty) / लोचन (eyes) / ललचाने (became eager/captivated) / हरषे (rejoiced) / जनु (as if) / निज (own) / निधि (treasure) / पहिचाने (recognized) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1261.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1261.essence: True beauty feels like finding what was already yours.
ramacharitamanas::1261.simple_meaning: The maidens point out Ram and Lakshman hiding behind the vines. Sita sees their beauty and feels instant joy, as if she has found something precious she already knew.
ramacharitamanas::1261.simple_insight: Recognition can feel like joy before words arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1261.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the maidens guide Sita's gaze through the vines to the two princes, Ram and Lakshman. She sees their beauty and is struck with delight, as if her heart has found its own long-sought treasure. This moment deepens her silent attraction before the swayamvar unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::1261.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone across a crowded room and feel an instant certainty before you can explain it. The heart sometimes recognizes what the mind has not yet named.
ramacharitamanas::1261.insight: It shifts attention from looking to recognizing, showing how love can feel like recovery rather than discovery.

ramacharitamanas::1262.verse_sanskrit: थके नयन रघुपति छबि देखें। पलकन्हिहूँ परिहरीं निमेषें॥ अधिक सनेहँ देह भै भोरी। सरद ससिहि जनु चितव चकोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1262.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी की छबि देखकर नेत्र थकित (निश्चल) हो गए। पलकों ने भी गिरना छोड़ दिया। अधिक स्नेह के कारण शरीर विह्वल (बेकाबू) हो गया। मानो शरद ऋतु के चन्द्रमा को चकोरी (बेसुध हुई) देख रही हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1262.english_translation: Seeing Ram's beauty, the eyes grew tired and the eyelids stopped blinking. Love overwhelmed the body, like a chakori gazing at the autumn moon.
ramacharitamanas::1262.translation_literal: थके (grew tired) / नयन (eyes) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / छबि (beauty, radiance) / देखें (having seen) / पलकन्हिहूँ (even the eyelids) / परिहरीं (gave up) / निमेषें (blinking) / अधिक (excessive) / सनेहँ (with love) / देह (body) / भै (became) / भोरी (overwhelmed, bewildered) / सरद (autumn) / ससिहि (moon) / जनु (like) / चितव (looks at) / चकोरी (chakori bird)
ramacharitamanas::1262.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1262.essence: Ram's beauty stops the body before the mind can move.
ramacharitamanas::1262.simple_meaning: Ram's beauty is so overwhelming that the eyes stop blinking and the body goes weak with love. The sight leaves the viewer absorbed and spellbound.
ramacharitamanas::1262.simple_insight: Some experiences are so beautiful they quiet the body before the mind can speak.
ramacharitamanas::1262.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, Sita and the women around her have just glimpsed Ram and Lakshman. The sight is so overwhelming that their eyes freeze and their bodies lose composure. This verse lingers on the first shock of divine beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1262.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone you love across a crowded station, and for a second everything else disappears. The body knows before the mind can explain.
ramacharitamanas::1262.insight: It shifts attention from looking at beauty to being overtaken by it, showing devotion as physical absorption.

ramacharitamanas::1263.verse_sanskrit: लोचन मग रामहि उर आनी। दीन्हे पलक कपाट सयानी॥ जब सिय सखिन्ह प्रेमबस जानी। कहि न सकहिं कछु मन सकुचानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1263.verse_hindi: नेत्रों के रास्ते श्री रामजी को हृदय में लाकर चतुरशिरोमणि जानकीजी ने पलकों के किवाड़ लगा दिए (अर्थात नेत्र मूँदकर उनका ध्यान करने लगीं)। जब सखियों ने सीताजी को प्रेम के वश जाना, तब वे मन में सकुचा गईं, कुछ कह नहीं सकती थीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1263.english_translation: With the eyes, Sita brought Ram into her heart and shut the eyelids as gates. When the companions saw Sita overwhelmed by love, they fell silent, shy and unable to speak.
ramacharitamanas::1263.translation_literal: लोचन (eyes) / मग (path) / रामहि (Ram) / उर (heart) / आनी (bringing) / दीन्हे (gave) / पलक (eyelids) / कपाट (gates) / सयानी (wise) / जब (when) / सिय (Sita) / सखिन्ह (companions) / प्रेमबस (under the sway of love) / जानी (knew) / कहि न सकहिं (could not speak) / कछु (anything) / मन (mind) / सकुचानी (became shy)
ramacharitamanas::1263.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1263.essence: Love closes the eyes and keeps Ram within.
ramacharitamanas::1263.simple_meaning: Sita drew Ram into her heart through her gaze and closed her eyes in loving meditation. Her companions saw that love and became too shy to speak.
ramacharitamanas::1263.simple_insight: Love can become so complete that even silence feels reverent.
ramacharitamanas::1263.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, the girls have just pointed out Ram and Lakshman hidden among the vines. Sita takes Ram into her heart through her eyes, closes them like doors, and the companions instantly recognize the depth of her love.
ramacharitamanas::1263.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone who matters and everything else goes quiet. Even the people beside you can tell: your attention has already gone somewhere deeper.
ramacharitamanas::1263.insight: It shifts attention from outward seeing to inward holding, where love becomes steady and private.

ramacharitamanas::1264.verse_sanskrit: लताभवन तें प्रगट भे तेहि अवसर दोउ भाइ। तकिसे जनु जुग बिमल बिधु जलद पटल बिलगाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1264.verse_hindi: उसी समय दोनों भाई लता मंडप (कुंज) में से प्रकट हुए। मानो दो निर्मल चन्द्रमा बादलों के परदे को हटाकर निकले हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1264.english_translation: At that moment, the two brothers emerged from the bower. It was as if two pure moons had come out, parting a screen of clouds.
ramacharitamanas::1264.translation_literal: लताभवन (bower) / तें (from) / प्रगट भे (appeared) / तेहि अवसर (at that moment) / दोउ भाइ (both brothers) / तकिसे (as if) / जनु (like) / जुग (pair) / बिमल (pure) / बिधु (moons) / जलद पटल (cloud screen) / बिलगाई (parting, separating)
ramacharitamanas::1264.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1264.essence: Their appearance turns the whole scene luminous.
ramacharitamanas::1264.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshman stepped out of the bower together, shining like two full moons emerging from behind clouds.
ramacharitamanas::1264.simple_insight: Beauty can arrive so fully that it feels like the world has been cleared for it.
ramacharitamanas::1264.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s court, after Sita has been overwhelmed by Ram’s sight, the two brothers appear from the flower bower together. Tulsidas pauses on their radiance before the swayamvar moves forward, turning the scene into a vision of divine beauty rather than action.
ramacharitamanas::1264.modern_relevance: You look up from a crowded room and see two people enter with such calm presence that the noise seems to fall away. Some arrivals change the atmosphere before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1264.insight: It shifts attention from event to radiance, asking the reader to notice presence itself.

ramacharitamanas::1265.verse_sanskrit: सोभा सीवँ सुभग दोउ बीरा। नील पीत जलजाभ सरीरा॥ मोरपंख सिर सोहत नीके। गुच्छ बीच बिच कुसुम कली के ॥
ramacharitamanas::1265.verse_hindi: दोनों सुंदर भाई शोभा की सीमा हैं। उनके शरीर की आभा नीले और पीले कमल की सी है। सिर पर सुंदर मोरपंख सुशोभित हैं। उनके बीच-बीच में फूलों की कलियों के गुच्छे लगे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1265.english_translation: Both brothers were the height of beauty. Their bodies shone like blue and yellow lotuses. Fine peacock feathers adorned their heads, with clusters of flowers and buds placed between them.
ramacharitamanas::1265.translation_literal: सोभा (beauty) / सीवँ (limit, boundary) / सुभग (beautiful, auspicious) / दोउ (both) / बीरा (brothers, heroes) / नील (blue) / पीत (yellow) / जलजाभ (lotus-like) / सरीरा (bodies) / मोरपंख (peacock feathers) / सिर (head) / सोहत (adorned) / नीके (beautifully) / गुच्छ (clusters) / बीच बिच (here and there, between) / कुसुम (flowers) / कली के (of buds)
ramacharitamanas::1265.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1265.essence: Their beauty is revealed as part of their divine presence.
ramacharitamanas::1265.simple_meaning: Both brothers are described as stunningly beautiful, with lotus-like bodies and peacock feathers and flowers adorning them.
ramacharitamanas::1265.simple_insight: Beauty here feels sacred and alive, not decorative.
ramacharitamanas::1265.detailed_meaning: Sita has just seen Ram and Lakshman emerge from the bow-garden. The poem now lingers on their appearance: both brothers shine like lotus blooms, crowned with peacock feathers and flowers. The scene slows so devotion can drink in their beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1265.modern_relevance: You catch someone in a rare, unguarded moment and realize the room has changed. The details — a tilt of the head, a simple ornament, a calm face — suddenly feel unforgettable.
ramacharitamanas::1265.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary appearance to the charged beauty of presence.

ramacharitamanas::1266.verse_sanskrit: भाल तिलक श्रम बिन्दु सुहाए। श्रवन सुभग भूषन छबि छाए॥ बिकट भृकुटि कच घूघरवारे। नव सरोज लोचन रतनारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1266.verse_hindi: माथे पर तिलक और पसीने की बूँदें शोभायमान हैं। कानों में सुंदर भूषणों की छबि छाई है। टेढ़ी भौंहें और घुँघराले बाल हैं। नए लाल कमल के समान रतनारे (लाल) नेत्र हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1266.english_translation: A tilak and beads of sweat adorn the forehead. Lovely ornaments shine on the ears. Strong brows, curly hair, and fresh red lotus eyes complete the beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1266.translation_literal: भाल (forehead) / तिलक (tilak mark) / श्रम (exertion) / बिन्दु (drops) / सुहाए (look lovely) / श्रवन (ears) / सुभग (beautiful) / भूषन (ornaments) / छबि (radiance) / छाए (spread) / बिकट (strong/arched) / भृकुटि (eyebrows) / कच (hair) / घूघरवारे (curly) / नव (new) / सरोज (lotus) / लोचन (eyes) / रतनारे (red, jewel-like)
ramacharitamanas::1266.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1266.essence: Even exertion becomes ornament in Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::1266.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are described in detail: their foreheads, ornaments, brows, curls, and red lotus-like eyes all add to their beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1266.simple_insight: Beauty here feels alive and human, not distant. Even a few drops of sweat only deepen the radiance.
ramacharitamanas::1266.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have just emerged in the swayamvar hall, and the poet lingers on their appearance before the bow is even addressed. Their beauty is so complete that even sweat becomes ornament, preparing the reader for the wonder that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1266.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone after a long, intense effort — hair slightly undone, face marked by strain — and the whole presence becomes more compelling, not less.
ramacharitamanas::1266.insight: It turns strain into grace, showing that effort can heighten presence instead of diminishing it.

ramacharitamanas::1267.verse_sanskrit: चारु चिबुक नासिका कपोला। हास बिलास लेत मनु मोला॥ मुखछबि कहि न जाइ मोहि पाहीं। जो बिलोकि बहु काम लजाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1267.verse_hindi: ठोड़ी नाक और गाल बड़े सुंदर हैं और हँसी की शोभा मन को मोल लिए लेती है। मुख की छबि तो मुझसे कही ही नहीं जाती, जिसे देखकर बहुत से कामदेव लजा जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1267.english_translation: The chin, nose, and cheeks are beautiful, and the charm of the smile steals the mind. I cannot describe the beauty of the face, before which many Cupids grow ashamed.
ramacharitamanas::1267.translation_literal: चारु (beautiful) / चिबुक (chin) / नासिका (nose) / कपोला (cheeks) / हास (smile) / बिलास (playful charm) / लेत (taking) / मनु (mind) / मोला (price, as if purchased) / मुखछबि (beauty of the face) / कहि (said) / न जाइ (cannot be told) / मोहि (by me) / पाहीं (to, before me) / जो (which) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बहु (many) / काम (Cupids) / लजाहीं (are ashamed)
ramacharitamanas::1267.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1267.essence: Ram's beauty defeats description and humbles desire itself.
ramacharitamanas::1267.simple_meaning: Ram's face is so beautiful that words cannot capture it. Even the god of desire would feel humbled before it.
ramacharitamanas::1267.simple_insight: Some beauty cannot be measured; it simply overwhelms the mind and leaves reverence in its place.
ramacharitamanas::1267.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, the assembly is seeing Ram and Lakshman in their full splendour. After describing their bodies and ornaments, the poet lingers on Ram's face, saying its beauty defeats comparison itself. The verse deepens the devotional wonder before Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1267.modern_relevance: You catch someone smiling across a crowded room, and the whole noise of the day drops away. Some presence does not ask to be explained; it simply rearranges your attention.
ramacharitamanas::1267.insight: It shifts attention from analysis to wonder, letting beauty be received instead of reduced.

ramacharitamanas::1268.verse_sanskrit: उर मनि माल कंबु कल गीवा। काम कलभ कर भुज बलसींवा॥ सुमन समेत बाम कर दोना। सावँर कुअँर सखी सुठि लोना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1268.verse_hindi: वक्षःस्थल पर मणियों की माला है। शंख के सदृश सुंदर गला है। कामदेव के हाथी के बच्चे की सूँड के समान (उतार-चढ़ाव वाली एवं कोमल) भुजाएँ हैं, जो बल की सीमा हैं। जिसके बाएँ हाथ में फूलों सहित दोना है, हे सखि! वह साँवला कुँअर तो बहुत ही सलोना है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1268.english_translation: His chest wears a jewel garland. His neck is beautiful like a conch. His arms, soft and powerful like a baby elephant’s trunk, hold strength itself. In his left hand he carries a flower-filled bowl. O friend, that dark prince is truly lovely.
ramacharitamanas::1268.translation_literal: उर (chest) / मनि माल (jewel garland) / कंबु (conch) / कल (beautiful) / गीवा (neck) / काम (desire) / कलभ (baby elephant) / कर (hand/trunk) / भुज (arms) / बलसींवा (strength-limit) / सुमन (flowers) / समेत (together with) / बाम कर (left hand) / दोना (bowl) / सावँर (dark-complexioned) / कुअँर (prince) / सखी (friend) / सुठि (very) / लोना (lovely)
ramacharitamanas::1268.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1268.essence: Ram’s beauty overwhelms thought and leaves only admiration.
ramacharitamanas::1268.simple_meaning: The verse keeps describing Ram’s beauty: jeweled chest, graceful neck, strong arms, flowers in his left hand, and a dark, lovely form.
ramacharitamanas::1268.simple_insight: Beauty can feel so complete that it stops the mind and leaves only wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1268.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, the narrator continues painting Ram’s form for the women watching him. After the face, the description moves to his chest, neck, arms, and hand, building the overwhelming charm that makes the onlookers lose themselves.
ramacharitamanas::1268.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone across a crowded room and forget your train of thought. The mind goes quiet before beauty that feels larger than language.
ramacharitamanas::1268.insight: It teaches attention to move from analysis to reverent seeing.

ramacharitamanas::1269.verse_sanskrit: केहरि कटि पट पीत धर सुषमा सील निधान। देखि भानुकुलभूषनहि बिसरा सखिन्ह अपान ॥
ramacharitamanas::1269.verse_hindi: सिंह की सी (पतली, लचीली) कमर वाले, पीताम्बर धारण किए हुए, शोभा और शील के भंडार, सूर्यकुल के भूषण श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर सखियाँ अपने आपको भूल गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1269.english_translation: Seeing the ornament of the solar line, the companions forgot themselves.
ramacharitamanas::1269.translation_literal: केहरि (lion-like) / कटि (waist) / पट (garment) / पीत (yellow) / धर (wearing) / सुषमा (beauty) / सील (virtue) / निधान (treasure) / देखि (seeing) / भानुकुलभूषनहि (the ornament of the solar lineage) / बिसरा (forgot) / सखिन्ह (the companions) / अपान (themselves)
ramacharitamanas::1269.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1269.essence: Ram's presence makes even the observer disappear.
ramacharitamanas::1269.simple_meaning: Ram's beauty and grace are so striking that the women around him lose awareness of themselves while looking at him.
ramacharitamanas::1269.simple_insight: A moment of beauty can quiet self-consciousness and leave only wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1269.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the marriage hall is alive with admiring eyes. The young prince of Ayodhya stands before the gathered women, and even the companions around Sita are overwhelmed by his form, grace, and character. Their attention is so complete that they forget themselves.
ramacharitamanas::1269.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone in a crowded wedding hall and stop mid-step, forgetting the message in your hand. Some presence is so complete it erases self-consciousness.
ramacharitamanas::1269.insight: It shifts attention from self-display to pure, wordless admiration.

ramacharitamanas::1270.verse_sanskrit: धरि धीरजु एक आलि सयानी। सीता सन बोली गहि पानी॥ बहुरि गौरि कर ध्यान करेहू। भूपकिसोर देखि किन लेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1270.verse_hindi: एक चतुर सखी धीरज धरकर, हाथ पकड़कर सीताजी से बोली- गिरिजाजी का ध्यान फिर कर लेना, इस समय राजकुमार को क्यों नहीं देख लेतीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1270.english_translation: A clever companion, steadying herself, took Sita's hand and said, "Remember Gauri later; why not look at the prince now?"
ramacharitamanas::1270.translation_literal: धरि (holding) / धीरजु (patience, composure) / एक (one) / आलि (companion) / सयानी (wise, clever) / सीता सन (to Sita) / बोली (spoke) / गहि (holding) / पानी (hand) / बहुरि (again) / गौरि कर (of Gauri) / ध्यान (attention, remembrance) / करेहू (do) / भूपकिसोर (prince) / देखि (seeing) / किन (why not) / लेहू (take, behold)
ramacharitamanas::1270.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1270.essence: A gentle nudge can open the heart to what it already seeks.
ramacharitamanas::1270.simple_meaning: A wise companion gently urges Sita to look at Ram now and remember Gauri later.
ramacharitamanas::1270.simple_insight: Sometimes a small nudge is enough to move the heart toward what it already longs for.
ramacharitamanas::1270.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the wedding assembly has brought Sita face to face with Ram for the first time. A clever friend takes her hand and quietly encourages her to look at the prince now, before turning back to Gauri. The moment is delicate and full of anticipation.
ramacharitamanas::1270.modern_relevance: At a crowded engagement ceremony, your friend squeezes your hand and points toward the person you came to see. One gentle cue can open the heart faster than a thousand thoughts.
ramacharitamanas::1270.insight: It shows how one careful companion can help someone cross from hesitation into direct seeing.

ramacharitamanas::1271.verse_sanskrit: सकुचि सीयँ तब नयन उघारे। सनमुख दोउ रघुसिंघ निहारे॥ नख सिख देखि राम कै सोभा। सुमिरि पिता पनु मनु अति छोभा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1271.verse_hindi: तब सीताजी ने सकुचाकर नेत्र खोले और रघुकुल के दोनों सिंहों को अपने सामने (खड़े) देखा। नख से शिखा तक श्री रामजी की शोभा देखकर और फिर पिता का प्रण याद करके उनका मन बहुत क्षुब्ध हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1271.english_translation: Then Sita, shyly, opened her eyes and saw the two lions of the Raghu line before her. Seeing Ram's beauty from head to toe, and remembering her father's vow, her mind became deeply agitated.
ramacharitamanas::1271.translation_literal: सकुचि (with shyness) / सीयँ (Sita) / तब (then) / नयन (eyes) / उघारे (opened) / सनमुख (facing) / दोउ (both) / रघुसिंघ (lions of Raghu) / निहारे (saw) / नख सिख (from nails to crest) / देखि (seeing) / राम कै (of Ram) / सोभा (beauty) / सुमिरि (remembering) / पिता पनु (father's vow) / मनु (mind) / अति (very) / छोभा (agitated)
ramacharitamanas::1271.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1271.essence: Beauty can stir the heart and disturb it at once.
ramacharitamanas::1271.simple_meaning: Sita finally looks at Ram, sees his full beauty, and remembers the vow her father made. That mixture of joy and duty shakes her heart.
ramacharitamanas::1271.simple_insight: Love and obligation can collide in one glance.
ramacharitamanas::1271.detailed_meaning: At Janak's swayamvar, Sita is standing before the assembled kings and the bow of Shiva. Shy and overwhelmed, she opens her eyes, sees Ram face to face, and is struck both by his beauty and by the weight of her father's vow. The moment is emotionally charged, not complete in itself.
ramacharitamanas::1271.modern_relevance: You meet someone who feels unmistakably right, then remember the promise, the family expectation, the consequences. One look can carry delight and pressure at once.
ramacharitamanas::1271.insight: It shows how attraction, memory, and duty can all seize the mind together.

ramacharitamanas::1272.verse_sanskrit: परबस सखिन्ह लखी जब सीता। भयउ गहरु सब कहहिं सभीता॥ पुनि आउब एहि बेरिआँ काली। अस कहि मन बिहसी एक आली ॥
ramacharitamanas::1272.verse_hindi: जब सखियों ने सीताजी को परवश (प्रेम के वश) देखा, तब सब भयभीत होकर कहने लगीं- बड़ी देर हो गई। (अब चलना चाहिए)। कल इसी समय फिर आएँगी, ऐसा कहकर एक सखी मन में हँसी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1272.english_translation: When the friends saw Sita overcome by love, they all grew uneasy and said, "It is already very late. We should go now." Then one friend laughed inwardly and said, "We will come again at this same time tomorrow."
ramacharitamanas::1272.translation_literal: परबस (overcome / under another's control) / सखिन्ह (by the friends) / लखी (saw) / जब (when) / सीता (Sita) / भयउ (became) / गहरु (late / delay) / सब (all) / कहहिं (say) / सभीता (uneasy / afraid) / पुनि (again) / आउब (will come) / एहि (this) / बेरिआँ (time) / काली (tomorrow) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / मन (in the mind) / बिहसी (smiled / laughed) / एक (one) / आली (friend)
ramacharitamanas::1272.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1272.essence: Love makes even restraint look obvious.
ramacharitamanas::1272.simple_meaning: Sita’s love is so visible that her friends become flustered and quickly try to end the meeting, though one friend secretly smiles at the situation.
ramacharitamanas::1272.simple_insight: Love can make even the bystanders nervous. What is felt deeply in one heart changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::1272.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s palace, the friends see Sita overwhelmed by longing after Ram’s presence. They realize the moment has gone too far and try to cover it with polite urgency, while one of them quietly enjoys the tenderness of it all.
ramacharitamanas::1272.modern_relevance: You notice the room change when someone’s feelings become impossible to hide. A friend clears her throat, checks the time, and suddenly everyone knows something real has happened.
ramacharitamanas::1272.insight: It shifts attention from public composure to the quiet power of love to expose the heart.

ramacharitamanas::1273.verse_sanskrit: गूढ़ गिरा सुनि सिय सकुचानी। भयउ बिलंबु मातु भय मानी॥ धरि बड़ि धीर रामु उर आने। फिरी अपनपउ पितुबस जाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1273.verse_hindi: सखी की यह रहस्यभरी वाणी सुनकर सीताजी सकुचा गईं। देर हो गई जान उन्हें माता का भय लगा। बहुत धीरज धरकर वे श्री रामचन्द्रजी को हृदय में ले आईं और (उनका ध्यान करती हुई) अपने को पिता के अधीन जानकर लौट चलीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1273.english_translation: Hearing the mysterious words, Sita became shy. Thinking of her mother’s warning, she felt the delay. Gathering great courage, she brought Ram into her heart and, feeling herself under her father’s command, turned back.
ramacharitamanas::1273.translation_literal: गूढ़ (mysterious) / गिरा (speech) / सुनि (hearing) / सिय (Sita) / सकुचानी (became shy) / भयउ (became) / बिलंबु (delay) / मातु (mother) / भय (fear) / मानी (considered) / धरि (holding) / बड़ि (great) / धीर (courage) / रामु (Ram) / उर (in the heart) / आने (brought) / फिरी (turned back) / अपनपउ (own state / self-possession) / पितुबस (under father’s control) / जाने (considered)
ramacharitamanas::1273.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1273.essence: Deep feeling can bow to restraint without losing its force.
ramacharitamanas::1273.simple_meaning: Sita feels shy and delays, then gathers herself, holds Ram in her heart, and returns with a sense of duty and restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1273.simple_insight: Love can be deep and still remain restrained. Real feeling does not always rush forward.
ramacharitamanas::1273.detailed_meaning: At the swayamvar, Sita has seen Ram and is drawn toward him, but the moment is delicate. A veiled warning from her companions and her sense of propriety make her pause. She steadies herself, keeps Ram in her heart, and returns.
ramacharitamanas::1273.modern_relevance: You almost send the message, then stop and breathe. The feeling is real, but so is the boundary. Not every strong pull should be followed immediately.
ramacharitamanas::1273.insight: It shows how devotion can coexist with self-control, turning longing into disciplined restraint.

ramacharitamanas::1274.verse_sanskrit: देखन मिस मृग बिहग तरु फिरइ बहोरि बहोरि। निरखि निरखि रघुबीर छबि बाढ़इ प्रीति न थोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1274.verse_hindi: मृग, पक्षी और वृक्षों को देखने के बहाने सीताजी बार-बार घूम जाती हैं और श्री रामजी की छबि देख-देखकर उनका प्रेम कम नहीं बढ़ रहा है। (अर्थात् बहुत ही बढ़ता जाता है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1274.english_translation: Again and again, under the pretext of looking at deer, birds, and trees, Sita keeps circling back; each sight of Ram's radiance only deepens her love.
ramacharitamanas::1274.translation_literal: देखन (for seeing) / मिस (as a pretext) / मृग (deer) / बिहग (birds) / तरु (trees) / फिरइ (circles/goes again) / बहोरि बहोरि (again and again) / निरखि निरखि (seeing repeatedly) / रघुबीर (Ram, hero of the Raghu clan) / छबि (beauty/radiance) / बाढ़इ (increases) / प्रीति (love) / न थोरि (not a little)
ramacharitamanas::1274.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1274.essence: True love keeps returning and grows stronger each time it looks.
ramacharitamanas::1274.simple_meaning: Sita keeps finding excuses to look around so she can keep seeing Ram. The more she sees him, the more her love grows.
ramacharitamanas::1274.simple_insight: Love keeps finding a way back to what it longs for.
ramacharitamanas::1274.detailed_meaning: In the swayamvar hall, Sita has just glimpsed Ram and feels her heart pulled toward him. She pretends to look at deer, birds, and trees, but keeps turning back to his beauty. This verse shows her love quietly overflowing before the bow is even lifted.
ramacharitamanas::1274.modern_relevance: You pretend to check your phone, then glance up just to see one person across the room again. The excuse changes; the pull does not.
ramacharitamanas::1274.insight: It reveals how devotion redirects attention toward the beloved, even through ordinary gestures.

ramacharitamanas::1275.verse_sanskrit: जानि कठिन सिवचाप बिसूरति। चली राखि उर स्यामल मूरति॥ प्रभु जब जात जानकी जानी। सुख सनेह सोभा गुन खानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1275.verse_hindi: शिवजी के धनुष को कठोर जानकर वे विसूरती (मन में विलाप करती) हुई हृदय में श्री रामजी की साँवली मूर्ति को रखकर चलीं। (शिवजी के धनुष की कठोरता का स्मरण आने से उन्हें चिंता होती थी कि ये सुकुमार रघुनाथजी उसे कैसे तोड़ेंगे, पिता के प्रण की स्मृति से उनके हृदय में क्षोभ था ही, इसलिए मन में विलाप करने लगीं। प्रेमवश ऐश्वर्य की विस्मृति हो जाने से ही ऐसा हुआ, फिर भगवान के बल का स्मरण आते ही वे हर्षित हो गईं और साँवली छबि को हृदय में धारण करके चलीं।) प्रभु श्री रामजी ने जब सुख, स्नेह, शोभा और गुणों की खान श्री जानकीजी को जाती हुई जाना, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1275.english_translation: Knowing Shiva's bow to be hard, she walked on, keeping Ram's dark image in her heart. When the Lord saw Janaki depart, he knew her as a treasure-house of joy, love, beauty, and virtue.
ramacharitamanas::1275.translation_literal: जानि (knowing) / कठिन (hard) / सिवचाप (Shiva's bow) / बिसूरति (lamenting) / चली (walked) / राखि (keeping) / उर (in heart) / स्यामल (dark) / मूरति (image) / प्रभु (Lord) / जब (when) / जात (going) / जानकी (Janaki) / जानी (knew) / सुख (joy) / सनेह (love) / सोभा (beauty) / गुन (virtue) / खानी (treasure-house)
ramacharitamanas::1275.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1275.essence: Fear yields when the heart stays fixed on Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1275.simple_meaning: Sita worries that Shiva's bow is too hard, but she keeps Ram in her heart and continues forward. Ram sees her leave and knows her as full of joy, love, beauty, and virtue.
ramacharitamanas::1275.simple_insight: Love can carry you through doubt. Even fear softens when the heart stays fixed on what it trusts.
ramacharitamanas::1275.detailed_meaning: At Janak's swayamvar, Sita has already chosen Ram inwardly, but the sight of Shiva's impossible bow makes her tremble. She walks on with Ram's image in her heart, while Ram sees her and recognises her true worth.
ramacharitamanas::1275.modern_relevance: You are about to walk into a room where one obstacle looks impossible. Your chest tightens, then you remember who you are doing it for and keep going.
ramacharitamanas::1275.insight: It shifts attention from the obstacle to the beloved presence held within the heart.

ramacharitamanas::1276.verse_sanskrit: परम प्रेममय मृदु मसि कीन्ही। चारु चित्त भीतीं लिखि लीन्ही॥ गई भवानी भवन बहोरी। बंदि चरन बोली कर जोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1276.verse_hindi: तब परमप्रेम की कोमल स्याही बनाकर उनके स्वरूप को अपने सुंदर चित्त रूपी भित्ति पर चित्रित कर लिया। सीताजी पुनः भवानीजी के मंदिर में गईं और उनके चरणों की वंदना करके हाथ जोड़कर बोलीं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1276.english_translation: Then she made her form into a soft ink of pure love and wrote it on the beautiful wall of her heart. She returned to Parvati's shrine, bowed at her feet, and spoke with joined palms.
ramacharitamanas::1276.translation_literal: परम (supreme) / प्रेममय (full of love) / मृदु (soft) / मसि (ink) / कीन्ही (made) / चारु (beautiful) / चित्त (mind/heart) / भीतीं (wall) / लिखि (having written) / लीन्ही (took) / गई (went) / भवानी (Parvati) / भवन (shrine/home) / बहोरी (again) / बंदि (bowing) / चरन (feet) / बोली (spoke) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined)
ramacharitamanas::1276.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1276.essence: True love writes the beloved into the heart forever.
ramacharitamanas::1276.simple_meaning: Sita holds Ram's form in her heart with the deepest love, then returns to Parvati and bows before speaking.
ramacharitamanas::1276.simple_insight: Love becomes a lasting imprint when the heart itself is the page.
ramacharitamanas::1276.detailed_meaning: Sita has just seen Ram and cannot stop cherishing his image. In the middle of the Sita-Parvati exchange, she carries that love inward, then returns to Parvati's shrine and speaks with reverence. The scene shows devotion becoming inner memory.
ramacharitamanas::1276.modern_relevance: You leave a room after meeting someone who changed you, and their presence stays with you all day. The mind keeps replaying the moment because the heart has already made its choice.
ramacharitamanas::1276.insight: It shifts devotion from a passing feeling into an inner imprint that guides speech and action.

ramacharitamanas::1277.verse_sanskrit: जय जय गिरिबरराज किसोरी। जय महेस मुख चंद चकोरी॥ जय गजबदन षडानन माता। जगत जननि दामिनि दुति गाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1277.verse_hindi: हे श्रेष्ठ पर्वतों के राजा हिमाचल की पुत्री पार्वती! आपकी जय हो, जय हो, हे महादेवजी के मुख रूपी चन्द्रमा की (ओर टकटकी लगाकर देखने वाली) चकोरी! आपकी जय हो, हे हाथी के मुख वाले गणेशजी और छह मुख वाले स्वामिकार्तिकजी की माता! हे जगज्जननी! हे बिजली की सी कान्तियुक्त शरीर वाली! आपकी जय हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::1277.english_translation: Victory, victory to the daughter of the king of mountains. Victory to the moon-like face of Mahesh. Victory to the mother of Ganesha and Kartikeya. Victory to the world-mother, whose body shines like lightning.
ramacharitamanas::1277.translation_literal: जय (victory) / जय (victory) / गिरिबरराज (king of great mountains) / किसोरी (daughter) / जय (victory) / महेस (Mahesh) / मुख (face) / चंद (moon) / चकोरी (chakori bird) / जय (victory) / गजबदन (elephant-faced) / षडानन (six-faced) / माता (mother) / जगत (world) / जननि (mother) / दामिनि (lightning) / दुति (radiance) / गाता (body)
ramacharitamanas::1277.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1277.essence: Praise reveals Parvati as beloved, mother, and radiant source at once.
ramacharitamanas::1277.simple_meaning: Parvati is praised as the daughter of the mountain king, Shiva’s beloved, the mother of Ganesha and Kartikeya, and the radiant mother of the world.
ramacharitamanas::1277.simple_insight: Reverence can honor many roles at once: daughter, beloved, mother, and cosmic presence.
ramacharitamanas::1277.detailed_meaning: In the Shiva-Parvati frame of Balkand, the poet turns from Sita’s inner devotion to praise Parvati directly. She is honored as mountain-born, Shiva’s beloved, and the mother of Ganesha and Kartikeya. The hymn prepares for a deeper description of her limitless nature.
ramacharitamanas::1277.modern_relevance: At a family ceremony, one person is seen only as a mother, another only as a spouse, another only as a daughter. This verse widens the frame and says a person can hold all those identities at once, with sacred dignity.
ramacharitamanas::1277.insight: It trains the mind to see a person’s fullness instead of reducing them to one role.

ramacharitamanas::1278.verse_sanskrit: नहिं तव आदि मध्य अवसाना। अमित प्रभाउ बेदु नहिं जाना॥ भव भव बिभव पराभव कारिनि। बिस्व बिमोहनि स्वबस बिहारिनि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1278.verse_hindi: आपका न आदि है, न मध्य है और न अंत है। आपके असीम प्रभाव को वेद भी नहीं जानते। आप संसार को उत्पन्न, पालन और नाश करने वाली हैं। विश्व को मोहित करने वाली और स्वतंत्र रूप से विहार करने वाली हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1278.english_translation: You have no beginning, middle, or end. Even the Vedas do not know your limitless power. You create, sustain, and dissolve the world. You enchant the universe and move freely by your own will.
ramacharitamanas::1278.translation_literal: नहिं (not) / तव (your) / आदि (beginning) / मध्य (middle) / अवसाना (end) / अमित (limitless) / प्रभाउ (power) / बेदु (the Vedas) / नहिं (do not) / जाना (know) / भव (world/existence) / भव (world/existence) / बिभव (sustenance/power) / पराभव (dissolution/undoing) / कारिनि (doer) / बिस्व (universe) / बिमोहनि (enchanting) / स्वबस (by your own will) / बिहारिनि (moving freely)
ramacharitamanas::1278.speaker: Parvati
ramacharitamanas::1278.essence: What has no beginning or end cannot be fully known by words.
ramacharitamanas::1278.simple_meaning: Parvati is praised as beyond beginning, middle, and end. Her power is beyond even the Vedas, and she is described as the force behind creation, preservation, dissolution, and the world's enchantment.
ramacharitamanas::1278.simple_insight: Some presence is so vast that even sacred learning cannot contain it.
ramacharitamanas::1278.detailed_meaning: Shiva is answering Parvati within the opening frame of Ramcharitmanas. As the praise rises, her nature is described as beyond time, beyond measurement, and beyond ordinary understanding. The verse deepens the devotion before the next line crowns her as the foremost ideal wife.
ramacharitamanas::1278.modern_relevance: A person can spend years trying to explain a mother, a teacher, or a beloved mentor — and still fail. Some forms of power are known only by their effects, not by definition.
ramacharitamanas::1278.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to fully define greatness to revering what exceeds language.

ramacharitamanas::1279.verse_sanskrit: पतिदेवता सुतीय महुँ मातु प्रथम तव रेख। महिमा अमित न सकहिं कहि सहस सारदा सेष ॥
ramacharitamanas::1279.verse_hindi: पति को इष्टदेव मानने वाली श्रेष्ठ नारियों में हे माता! आपकी प्रथम गणना है। आपकी अपार महिमा को हजारों सरस्वती और शेषजी भी नहीं कह सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1279.english_translation: Among noble women who regard their husband as their highest deity, you, O Mother, are foremost. Your immeasurable greatness cannot be fully described even by thousands of Saraswatis and Sheshas.
ramacharitamanas::1279.translation_literal: पतिदेवता (husband as deity) / सुतीय (among noble women) / महुँ (among) / मातु (Mother) / प्रथम (first) / तव (your) / रेख (line, rank) / महिमा (greatness) / अमित (immeasurable) / न (not) / सकहिं (can) / कहि (say) / सहस (thousands) / सारदा (Saraswati) / सेष (Shesha)
ramacharitamanas::1279.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::1279.essence: Steadfast devotion makes a person greater than praise can hold.
ramacharitamanas::1279.simple_meaning: Among devoted wives, Sita stands first. Her greatness is beyond speech, beyond even the reach of countless divine tongues.
ramacharitamanas::1279.simple_insight: True devotion is not small or passive; it becomes a greatness that speech cannot contain.
ramacharitamanas::1279.detailed_meaning: Shiva is praising Parvati by drawing a sacred comparison to Sita, the model of devoted wifehood. The verse sits inside a flowing hymn: first Sita is honored as foremost among faithful women, then her greatness is declared beyond all description.
ramacharitamanas::1279.modern_relevance: At a wedding where everyone praises the couple, one quiet person sees the deeper standard: love that keeps faith under pressure. Some forms of devotion are so complete they outgrow language.
ramacharitamanas::1279.insight: It shifts attention from outward praise to the depth of steadfast, relational devotion.

ramacharitamanas::1280.verse_sanskrit: सेवत तोहि सुलभ फल चारी। बरदायनी पुरारि पिआरी॥ देबि पूजि पद कमल तुम्हारे। सुर नर मुनि सब होहिं सुखारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1280.verse_hindi: हे (भक्तों को मुँहमाँगा) वर देने वाली! हे त्रिपुर के शत्रु शिवजी की प्रिय पत्नी! आपकी सेवा करने से चारों फल सुलभ हो जाते हैं। हे देवी! आपके चरण कमलों की पूजा करके देवता, मनुष्य और मुनि सभी सुखी हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1280.english_translation: O giver of boons, beloved wife of the enemy of Tripura, serving you makes the four aims of life easy to attain. O देवी, by worshipping your lotus feet, gods, humans, and sages all become joyful.
ramacharitamanas::1280.translation_literal: सेवत (serving) / तोहि (you) / सुलभ (easy to attain) / फल (fruits) / चारी (four) / बरदायनी (giver of boons) / पुरारि (enemy of Tripura; Shiva) / पिआरी (beloved) / देबि (devi) / पूजि (worshipping) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / तुम्हारे (your) / सुर (gods) / नर (humans) / मुनि (sages) / सब (all) / होहिं (become) / सुखारे (happy)
ramacharitamanas::1280.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1280.essence: Serving the divine feminine makes life’s four aims easy to attain.
ramacharitamanas::1280.simple_meaning: Worshipping Sita is said to bring the four aims of life easily, and honoring her feet brings joy to gods, humans, and sages.
ramacharitamanas::1280.simple_insight: Devotion to Sita is presented as a direct source of wholeness, not a distant reward.
ramacharitamanas::1280.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, Tulsidas is praising Sita after describing her limitless greatness. He says that serving her makes all four aims of life easy to attain, and that worshipping her lotus feet brings joy to every kind of being.
ramacharitamanas::1280.modern_relevance: You light a candle before leaving for a hard day, not because the day becomes easy, but because devotion steadies everything you touch.
ramacharitamanas::1280.insight: It shifts devotion from ritual to relationship: honoring the divine presence becomes the source of ease and joy.

ramacharitamanas::1281.verse_sanskrit: मोर मनोरथु जानहु नीकें। बसहु सदा उर पुर सबही कें॥ कीन्हेउँ प्रगट न कारन तेहीं। अस कहि चरन गहे बैदेहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1281.verse_hindi: मेरे मनोरथ को आप भलीभाँति जानती हैं, क्योंकि आप सदा सबके हृदय रूपी नगरी में निवास करती हैं। इसी कारण मैंने उसको प्रकट नहीं किया। ऐसा कहकर जानकीजी ने उनके चरण पकड़ लिए ॥
