ramacharitamanas::1281.english_translation: You know my heart’s desire well. You live in every heart, so I did not speak it aloud. Saying this, Janaki held her feet.
ramacharitamanas::1281.translation_literal: मोर (my) / मनोरथु (heart’s desire) / जानहु (you know) / नीकें (well) / बसहु (you dwell) / सदा (always) / उर (heart) / पुर (city) / सबही (of all) / कें (in) / कीन्हेउँ (I made) / प्रगट (manifest) / न (not) / कारन (reason) / तेहीं (therefore) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / चरन (feet) / गहे (held) / बैदेहीं (Vaidehi, Sita)
ramacharitamanas::1281.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::1281.essence: The deepest wish needs no announcement before the one who already knows the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1281.simple_meaning: Sita tells Parvati that she already knows her heart’s wish because she lives in every heart. So Sita does not need to say it openly, and she bows at Parvati’s feet.
ramacharitamanas::1281.simple_insight: Real reverence does not need performance. The heart is understood before words arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1281.detailed_meaning: Sita is speaking to Parvati after praising her greatness. She says Parvati already knows every heart’s wish because she dwells within all hearts, so there is no need to state it directly. This quiet humility deepens the bond between devotee and divine mother.
ramacharitamanas::1281.modern_relevance: You sit across from someone who knows your pain before you can explain it. The relief is immediate: you do not have to perform your feelings to be understood.
ramacharitamanas::1281.insight: It shifts the mind from explaining itself to bowing in trust.

ramacharitamanas::1282.verse_sanskrit: बिनय प्रेम बस भई भवानी। खसी माल मूरति मुसुकानी॥ सादर सियँ प्रसादु सिर धरेऊ। बोली गौरि हरषु हियँ भरेऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1282.verse_hindi: गिरिजाजी सीताजी के विनय और प्रेम के वश में हो गईं। उन (के गले) की माला खिसक पड़ी और मूर्ति मुस्कुराई। सीताजी ने आदरपूर्वक उस प्रसाद (माला) को सिर पर धारण किया। गौरीजी का हृदय हर्ष से भर गया और वे बोलीं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1282.english_translation: Parvati was overcome by devotion and love. The garland slipped and the image smiled. Sita respectfully placed the blessing on her head, and Gauri's heart filled with joy as she spoke.
ramacharitamanas::1282.translation_literal: बिनय (humility) / प्रेम (love) / बस (under the control of) / भई (became) / भवानी (Parvati) / खसी (slipped down) / माल (garland) / मूरति (image) / मुसुकानी (smiled) / सादर (respectfully) / सियँ (by Sita) / प्रसादु (blessing/offering) / सिर (head) / धरेऊ (placed) / बोली (spoke) / गौरि (Gauri/Parvati) / हरषु (joy) / हियँ (in the heart) / भरेऊ (became filled)
ramacharitamanas::1282.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1282.essence: Humility and love make blessing itself come alive.
ramacharitamanas::1282.simple_meaning: Parvati is moved by Sita's humility and love. Sita accepts the blessing with respect, and Parvati responds with joy and approval.
ramacharitamanas::1282.simple_insight: True devotion softens even the one who receives it. Humility and reverence create joy on both sides.
ramacharitamanas::1282.detailed_meaning: At the Sita-Swayamvar, Parvati sees Sita's humble devotion and is overcome. Her garland slips, the image seems to smile, and Sita places the blessing on her head. The moment confirms Sita's worthiness before the marriage choice unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::1282.modern_relevance: You watch someone receive praise without showing off, and the whole room changes. Their humility makes the respect feel real, not ceremonial.
ramacharitamanas::1282.insight: It shows that reverent humility can awaken grace and mutual joy, not just private virtue.

ramacharitamanas::1283.verse_sanskrit: सुनु सिय सत्य असीस हमारी। पूजिहि मन कामना तुम्हारी॥ नारद बचन सदा सुचि साचा। सो बरु मिलिहि जाहिं मनु राचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1283.verse_hindi: हे सीता! हमारी सच्ची आसीस सुनो, तुम्हारी मनःकामना पूरी होगी। नारदजी का वचन सदा पवित्र (संशय, भ्रम आदि दोषों से रहित) और सत्य है। जिसमें तुम्हारा मन अनुरक्त हो गया है, वही वर तुमको मिलेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1283.english_translation: Listen, Sita, to our true blessing: your wish will be fulfilled. Narada's word is always pure and true. The one your mind loves will surely be the bridegroom you receive.
ramacharitamanas::1283.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / सिय (Sita) / सत्य (true) / असीस (blessing) / हमारी (our) / पूजिहि (will be fulfilled) / मन (mind) / कामना (wish) / तुम्हारी (your)॥ / नारद (Narada) / बचन (word) / सदा (always) / सुचि (pure) / साचा (true) / सो (that) / बरु (bridegroom) / मिलिहि (will be received) / जाहिं (whom) / मनु (mind) / राचा (has become pleased/loved) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1283.speaker: Gauri
ramacharitamanas::1283.essence: A pure wish, once blessed, moves toward its rightful fulfillment.
ramacharitamanas::1283.simple_meaning: Gauri blesses Sita that her wish will come true, and says Narada's words are always pure and true. The bridegroom Sita loves in her heart will be the one she gets.
ramacharitamanas::1283.simple_insight: A longing held with purity is not dismissed. The heart’s true desire is being honored.
ramacharitamanas::1283.detailed_meaning: After Sita's devotion and humility, Gauri answers her with reassurance. She declares that Narada's words are trustworthy and that Sita's heartfelt wish will be fulfilled. This moment prepares the revelation that Ram himself is the chosen bridegroom.
ramacharitamanas::1283.modern_relevance: You finally admit what you want, half afraid it sounds foolish. A trusted elder hears it, blesses it, and says the wish is not too much.
ramacharitamanas::1283.insight: It shifts attention from doubt to trust in a sincere longing already moving toward fulfillment.

ramacharitamanas::1284.verse_sanskrit: मनु जाहिं राचेउ मिलिहि सो बरु सहज सुंदर साँवरो। करुना निधान सुजान सीलु सनेहु जानत रावरो॥ एहि भाँति गौरि असीस सुनि सिय सहित हियँ हरषीं अली। तुलसी भवानिहि पूजि पुनि पुनि मुदित मन मंदिर चली॥
ramacharitamanas::1284.verse_hindi: जिसमें तुम्हारा मन अनुरक्त हो गया है, वही स्वभाव से ही सुंदर साँवला वर (श्री रामचन्द्रजी) तुमको मिलेगा। वह दया का खजाना और सुजान (सर्वज्ञ) है, तुम्हारे शील और स्नेह को जानता है। इस प्रकार श्री गौरीजी का आशीर्वाद सुनकर जानकीजी समेत सब सखियाँ हृदय में हर्षित हुईं। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- भवानीजी को बार-बार पूजकर सीताजी प्रसन्न मन से राजमहल को लौट चलीं॥
ramacharitamanas::1284.english_translation: The one your mind has chosen will surely be your husband: the naturally beautiful dark one, a treasure of compassion, wise, and aware of your character and love. Hearing this blessing from Gauri, Sita and her companions rejoiced, and Tulsidas says Sita worshipped Bhavani again and again and returned to the palace with a glad heart.
ramacharitamanas::1284.translation_literal: मनु (mind) / जाहिं राचेउ (has become fixed upon) / मिलिहि (will obtain) / सो बरु (that bridegroom) / सहज (naturally) / सुंदर (beautiful) / साँवरो (dark-complexioned one) / करुना (compassion) / निधान (treasure) / सुजान (wise) / सीलु (character) / सनेहु (love) / जानत (knowing) / रावरो (your)॥ / एहि भाँति (in this way) / गौरि (Gauri) / असीस (blessing) / सुनि (hearing) / सिय सहित (with Sita) / हियँ (in the heart) / हरषीं (rejoiced) / अली (companions) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / भवानिहि (Bhavani) / पूजि (having worshipped) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / मुदित (glad) / मन (mind) / मंदिर (palace) / चली (went)॥
ramacharitamanas::1284.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1284.essence: The heart’s chosen one is also the one the blessing confirms.
ramacharitamanas::1284.simple_meaning: Sita is told that the husband her mind has chosen will indeed be hers: Ram, beautiful, compassionate, wise, and attentive to her love. Hearing this, she and her companions rejoice and return happily.
ramacharitamanas::1284.simple_insight: It feels like being seen by the right love before the meeting even happens.
ramacharitamanas::1284.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, Gauri blesses her in front of the gathered women. The blessing confirms what Sita already feels in her heart: Ram is the one meant for her. The moment turns private longing into public joy.
ramacharitamanas::1284.modern_relevance: You finally hear someone name the choice your heart has been carrying all along. The relief is not just getting an answer — it is being told your deepest longing was never foolish.
ramacharitamanas::1284.insight: It shifts the mind from doubt about love to trust in the heart’s clarity.

ramacharitamanas::1285.verse_sanskrit: जानि गौरि अनुकूल सिय हिय हरषु न जाइ कहि। मंजुल मंगल मूल बाम अंग फरकन लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1285.verse_hindi: गौरीजी को अनुकूल जानकर सीताजी के हृदय को जो हर्ष हुआ, वह कहा नहीं जा सकता। सुंदर मंगलों के मूल उनके बाएँ अंग फड़कने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1285.english_translation: Seeing that Gauri favored her, Sita's heart filled with joy beyond words. Her left limbs began to twitch, a sign of auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::1285.translation_literal: जानि (knowing) / गौरि (Gauri) / अनुकूल (favorable) / सिय (Sita) / हिय (heart) / हरषु (joy) / न जाइ (cannot go) / कहि (to say) / मंजुल (beautiful) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मूल (root) / बाम (left) / अंग (limbs) / फरकन (to twitch) / लगे (began)
ramacharitamanas::1285.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1285.essence: Joy becomes visible when the body answers blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1285.simple_meaning: Sita felt immense joy when she knew Gauri was pleased with her. Her left limbs twitched, which was taken as an auspicious sign.
ramacharitamanas::1285.simple_insight: Joy can arrive so fully that even the body seems to answer it.
ramacharitamanas::1285.detailed_meaning: After the blessing for Sita's marriage is spoken, the scene turns inward for a moment. Sita understands that Gauri is favorable to her, and her heart overflows with joy. The body follows with auspicious signs, showing that the moment is blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1285.modern_relevance: You get a message saying the job you hoped for is yours, and before you even speak, your body reacts. Relief, joy, and disbelief all arrive at once.
ramacharitamanas::1285.insight: It shifts attention from spoken blessing to the body's quiet confirmation of it.

ramacharitamanas::1286.verse_sanskrit: हृदयँ सराहत सीय लोनाई। गुर समीप गवने दोउ भाई॥ राम कहा सबु कौसिक पाहीं। सरल सुभाउ छुअत छल नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1286.verse_hindi: हृदय में सीताजी के सौंदर्य की सराहना करते हुए दोनों भाई गुरुजी के पास गए। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने विश्वामित्र से सब कुछ कह दिया, क्योंकि उनका सरल स्वभाव है, छल तो उसे छूता भी नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1286.english_translation: Keeping Sita’s beauty in their hearts, the two brothers went to their teacher. Ram told Vishwamitra everything, because his nature is simple and deceit never touches him.
ramacharitamanas::1286.translation_literal: हृदयँ (in the heart) / सराहत (praising) / सीय (Sita) / लोनाई (beauty) / गुर (teacher) / समीप (near) / गवने (went) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers)॥ राम (Ram) / कहा (said) / सबु (everything) / कौसिक पाहीं (to Vishvamitra) / सरल (simple) / सुभाउ (nature) / छुअत (touching) / छल (deceit) / नाहीं (not)॥
ramacharitamanas::1286.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1286.essence: Simple hearts speak plainly and need no disguise.
ramacharitamanas::1286.simple_meaning: The two brothers return to their teacher, still admiring Sita in their hearts. Ram speaks openly to Vishvamitra because his nature is straight and free of deceit.
ramacharitamanas::1286.simple_insight: There is strength in being open. A clean heart does not need masks.
ramacharitamanas::1286.detailed_meaning: After Sita’s swayamvar, Ram and Lakshman walk back to Vishvamitra. Ram quietly admires Sita, then speaks plainly to the sage about what has happened. The moment shows his natural honesty before the blessing that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1286.modern_relevance: You sit across from someone who can help you, and you stop performing. You tell the truth plainly, without polishing it for approval. That kind of honesty changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::1286.insight: It shifts the mind from guarded self-presentation to direct, unforced speech.

ramacharitamanas::1287.verse_sanskrit: सुमन पाइ मुनि पूजा कीन्ही। पुनि असीस दुहु भाइन्ह दीन्ही॥ सुफल मनोरथ होहुँ तुम्हारे। रामु लखनु सुनि भय सुखारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1287.verse_hindi: फूल पाकर मुनि ने पूजा की। फिर दोनों भाइयों को आशीर्वाद दिया कि तुम्हारे मनोरथ सफल हों। यह सुनकर श्री राम-लक्ष्मण सुखी हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1287.english_translation: The sage accepted the flowers as worship and blessed both brothers: may your wishes come true. Hearing this, Ram and Lakshman felt glad.
ramacharitamanas::1287.translation_literal: सुमन (flowers) / पाइ (having received) / मुनि (the sage) / पूजा (worship) / कीन्ही (did) / पुनि (then) / असीस (blessing) / दुहु (both) / भाइन्ह (brothers) / दीन्ही (gave) / सुफल (fruitful) / मनोरथ (wishes) / होहुँ (may become) / तुम्हारे (yours) / रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / सुनि (hearing) / भय (became) / सुखारे (glad)
ramacharitamanas::1287.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1287.essence: A true blessing makes both giver and receiver glad.
ramacharitamanas::1287.simple_meaning: The sage receives the flowers, offers a blessing, and Ram and Lakshman feel happy when they hear it.
ramacharitamanas::1287.simple_insight: Blessing softens the moment. A sincere wish for someone’s good can lift both giver and receiver.
ramacharitamanas::1287.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar setting, Vishwamitra receives flowers offered in worship and blesses Ram and Lakshman. His words of goodwill please both brothers, showing a brief moment of grace before the next turn in the journey.
ramacharitamanas::1287.modern_relevance: A respected elder smiles after your small gesture of respect, then quietly wishes you well. The room changes. Sometimes one sincere blessing steadies everyone more than a long speech.
ramacharitamanas::1287.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the warmth and goodwill carried through it.

ramacharitamanas::1288.verse_sanskrit: करि भोजनु मुनिबर बिग्यानी। लगे कहन कछु कथा पुरानी॥ बिगत दिवसु गुरु आयसु पाई। संध्या करन चले दोउ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1288.verse_hindi: श्रेष्ठ विज्ञानी मुनि विश्वामित्रजी भोजन करके कुछ प्राचीन कथाएँ कहने लगे। (इतने में) दिन बीत गया और गुरु की आज्ञा पाकर दोनों भाई संध्या करने चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1288.english_translation: The wise sage ate, then began telling old tales. As the day passed, both brothers went to perform evening worship on the teacher's command.
ramacharitamanas::1288.translation_literal: करि (having done) / भोजनु (meal) / मुनिबर (best of sages) / बिग्यानी (knowing, wise) / लगे (began) / कहन (to speak) / कछु (some) / कथा (stories) / पुरानी (old) / बिगत (passed) / दिवसु (day) / गुरु (teacher) / आयसु (command) / पाई (having received) / संध्या (evening worship) / करन (to do) / चले (went) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::1288.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1288.essence: Even in rest, the brothers move when the teacher calls.
ramacharitamanas::1288.simple_meaning: After eating, Vishwamitra began telling old stories. When evening came and their teacher ordered it, both brothers went to do their evening worship.
ramacharitamanas::1288.simple_insight: Even sacred conversation gives way to discipline. The day is not complete until the teacher’s command is fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::1288.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra has finished his meal and starts speaking of old matters. Time has passed in the forest camp, and Ram and Lakshman do not linger in comfort. They rise at their guru's command and go for evening worship.
ramacharitamanas::1288.modern_relevance: You are midway through a warm conversation when the clock changes and your child needs help with homework, prayer, or bedtime. The moment asks for obedience, not delay.
ramacharitamanas::1288.insight: It shifts attention from pleasant conversation to the duty that structures the day.

ramacharitamanas::1289.verse_sanskrit: प्राची दिसि ससि उयउ सुहावा। सिय मुख सरिस देखि सुखु पावा॥ बहुरि बिचारु कीन्ह मन माहीं। सीय बदन सम हिमकर नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1289.verse_hindi: (उधर) पूर्व दिशा में सुंदर चन्द्रमा उदय हुआ। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने उसे सीता के मुख के समान देखकर सुख पाया। फिर मन में विचार किया कि यह चन्द्रमा सीताजी के मुख के समान नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1289.english_translation: The lovely moon rose in the eastern sky. Seeing it like Sita's face, Ram felt joy. Then he thought in his mind: this moon is not equal to Sita's face.
ramacharitamanas::1289.translation_literal: प्राची दिसि (in the eastern direction) / ससि (moon) / उयउ (rose) / सुहावा (lovely) / सिय मुख (Sita's face) / सरिस (like) / देखि (seeing) / सुखु (joy) / पावा (obtained) / बहुरि (again) / बिचारु (thought) / कीन्ह (made) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / सीय बदन (Sita's face) / सम (equal to) / हिमकर (moon) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::1289.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1289.essence: The beloved makes even the moon feel inadequate.
ramacharitamanas::1289.simple_meaning: The moon rises beautifully, and Ram compares it to Sita's face. He feels delight, then decides even the moon cannot match her beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1289.simple_insight: Love changes what beauty means. Everything else becomes smaller beside the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::1289.detailed_meaning: After the sages' meal, evening falls and the moon rises. Ram looks at it and first feels joy, then privately judges that even the moon cannot equal Sita's face. The verse captures his tender longing before the swayamvar scene deepens.
ramacharitamanas::1289.modern_relevance: You step outside after a long day and see a full moon over the rooftops. For a second it calms you, but then one person you miss makes every other beauty feel secondary.
ramacharitamanas::1289.insight: It shifts attention from general beauty to personal devotion, showing how love reorders perception.

ramacharitamanas::1290.verse_sanskrit: जनमु सिंधु पुनि बंधु बिषु दिन मलीन सकलंक। सिय मुख समता पाव किमि चंदु बापुरो रंक ॥
ramacharitamanas::1290.verse_hindi: खारे समुद्र में तो इसका जन्म, फिर (उसी समुद्र से उत्पन्न होने के कारण) विष इसका भाई, दिन में यह मलिन (शोभाहीन, निस्तेज) रहता है, और कलंकी (काले दाग से युक्त) है। बेचारा गरीब चन्द्रमा सीताजी के मुख की बराबरी कैसे पा सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1290.english_translation: The moon is born from the salty sea, its brother is poison, it is dim and blemished by day. How can that poor, lowly moon match Sita's face?
ramacharitamanas::1290.translation_literal: जनमु (birth) / सिंधु (sea) / पुनि (again) / बंधु (brother) / बिषु (poison) / दिन (day) / मलीन (dull, dim) / सकलंक (blemished) / सिय (Sita's) / मुख (face) / समता (equality) / पाव (can attain) / किमि (how) / चंदु (moon) / बापुरो (poor, helpless) / रंक (pauper)
ramacharitamanas::1290.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1290.essence: Comparison fails when real radiance appears.
ramacharitamanas::1290.simple_meaning: The moon is being compared and found wanting next to Sita's face. The speaker says the moon is dim, flawed, and too poor to match her beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1290.simple_insight: Some beauty feels beyond comparison. The mind bows when it meets something truly radiant.
ramacharitamanas::1290.detailed_meaning: After seeing Sita's face, Ram's mind turns to comparison. The moon, born from the sea and marked by flaws, feels unfit beside her radiance. This doha sharpens the contrast before the praise continues.
ramacharitamanas::1290.modern_relevance: You scroll past polished images all day, then see one face in a crowded room and every comparison collapses. Some presence makes your usual standards feel small.
ramacharitamanas::1290.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary beauty standards to the shock of encountering something incomparable.

ramacharitamanas::1291.verse_sanskrit: घटइ बढ़इ बिरहिनि दुखदाई। ग्रसइ राहु निज संधिहिं पाई॥ कोक सोकप्रद पंकज द्रोही। अवगुन बहुत चंद्रमा तोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1291.verse_hindi: फिर यह घटता-बढ़ता है और विरहिणी स्त्रियों को दुःख देने वाला है, राहु अपनी संधि में पाकर इसे ग्रस लेता है। चकवे को (चकवी के वियोग का) शोक देने वाला और कमल का बैरी (उसे मुरझा देने वाला) है। हे चन्द्रमा! तुझमें बहुत से अवगुण हैं (जो सीताजी में नहीं हैं।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1291.english_translation: It waxes and wanes, bringing sorrow to separated lovers. Rahu swallows it when the time is right. It brings grief to the chakora bird and enemies to the lotus. Moon, you have many flaws.
ramacharitamanas::1291.translation_literal: घटइ (it decreases) / बढ़इ (it increases) / बिरहिनि (for separated women) / दुखदाई (pain-giving) / ग्रसइ (swallows) / राहु (Rahu) / निज (its own) / संधिहिं (at the junction/time) / पाई (having found) / कोक (chakora bird) / सोकप्रद (grief-giving) / पंकज (lotus) / द्रोही (enemy) / अवगुन (faults) / बहुत (many) / चंद्रमा (moon) / तोही (to you)
ramacharitamanas::1291.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1291.essence: The moon fails as a measure because its beauty is mixed with flaw.
ramacharitamanas::1291.simple_meaning: The moon keeps changing, harms lovers in separation, is swallowed by Rahu, troubles the chakora bird, and hurts the lotus. It is not fit to compare with Sita.
ramacharitamanas::1291.simple_insight: Comparison can reveal flaws as clearly as praise reveals beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1291.detailed_meaning: Ram is praising Sita's face by first exposing the moon's defects. The moon grows and shrinks, darkens separated lovers, is eclipsed by Rahu, and even troubles the chakora and lotus. This is part of his argument that no earthly image truly matches Sita.
ramacharitamanas::1291.modern_relevance: You think a perfect photo will capture someone you love, then the lighting changes and everything falls flat. Some beauty cannot be reduced to a comparison.
ramacharitamanas::1291.insight: It shifts attention from borrowed comparisons to the uniqueness of what is being praised.

ramacharitamanas::1292.verse_sanskrit: बैदेही मुख पटतर दीन्हे। होइ दोषु बड़ अनुचित कीन्हे॥ सिय मुख छबि बिधु ब्याज बखानी। गुर पहिं चले निसा बड़ि जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1292.verse_hindi: अतः जानकीजी के मुख की तुझे उपमा देने में बड़ा अनुचित कर्म करने का दोष लगेगा। इस प्रकार चन्द्रमा के बहाने सीताजी के मुख की छबि का वर्णन करके, बड़ी रात हो गई जान, वे गुरुजी के पास चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1292.english_translation: It would be a great impropriety to compare her face to the moon. So, praising Sita's face through the moon's beauty, they went to the guru when night had grown deep.
ramacharitamanas::1292.translation_literal: बैदेही (Sita) / मुख (face) / पटतर (comparison) / दीन्हे (given) / होइ (becoming) / दोषु (fault) / बड़ (great) / अनुचित (improper) / कीन्हे (done) / सिय (Sita) / मुख (face) / छबि (beauty) / बिधु (moon) / ब्याज (pretext) / बखानी (described) / गुर (guru) / पहिं (to) / चले (went) / निसा (night) / बड़ि (great/deep) / जानी (having known)
ramacharitamanas::1292.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1292.essence: True praise knows when comparison itself becomes disrespect.
ramacharitamanas::1292.simple_meaning: Sita's face is beyond comparison, so the poet avoids direct comparison and uses the moon only as a pretext. The verse ends by saying they went to the teacher late at night.
ramacharitamanas::1292.simple_insight: Some beauty is too great for direct comparison; reverence shows itself by restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1292.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still in the Sita-swayamvar scene, praising Sita's unmatched beauty. After saying even the moon falls short, he warns that comparing her face directly would be improper. He then uses the moon only as a respectful device and turns to the guru.
ramacharitamanas::1292.modern_relevance: You try to describe someone you love and keep failing, because plain comparison feels too small. The best praise is often humble enough to admit it cannot fully capture what it sees.
ramacharitamanas::1292.insight: It shifts attention from clever description to reverent restraint.

ramacharitamanas::1293.verse_sanskrit: करि मुनि चरन सरोज प्रनामा। आयसु पाइ कीन्ह बिश्रामा॥ बिगत निसा रघुनायक जागे। बंधु बिलोकि कहन अस लागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1293.verse_hindi: मुनि के चरण कमलों में प्रणाम करके, आज्ञा पाकर उन्होंने विश्राम किया, रात बीतने पर श्री रघुनाथजी जागे और भाई को देखकर ऐसा कहने लगे- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1293.english_translation: After bowing to the sage's lotus feet and receiving permission, they rested. When the night passed, Raghunath woke and, seeing his brother, began to speak.
ramacharitamanas::1293.translation_literal: करि (having done) / मुनि (sage) / चरन (feet) / सरोज (lotus) / प्रनामा (salutation) / आयसु (permission) / पाइ (having received) / कीन्ह (did) / बिश्रामा (rest) / बिगत (passed) / निसा (night) / रघुनायक (Raghunath) / जागे (woke) / बंधु (brother) / बिलोकि (seeing) / कहन (to speak) / अस (thus) / लागे (began)
ramacharitamanas::1293.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1293.essence: Rest comes before the next teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1293.simple_meaning: They bow to the sage, rest for the night, and wake at dawn. Ram then sees Lakshman and begins to speak.
ramacharitamanas::1293.simple_insight: Even sacred journeys still pause for rest before the next step begins.
ramacharitamanas::1293.detailed_meaning: After honoring the sage and taking his leave, Ram and Lakshman rest for the night. At dawn, Ram wakes first, sees his brother beside him, and begins the day's teaching. The scene quietly prepares the next instruction.
ramacharitamanas::1293.modern_relevance: You finally sit down after a long day, shoes off, phone face down. The real work can wait until morning; even Ram rested before speaking.
ramacharitamanas::1293.insight: It slows the reader into the rhythm of pause, rest, and then instruction.

ramacharitamanas::1294.verse_sanskrit: उयउ अरुन अवलोकहु ताता। पंकज कोक लोक सुखदाता॥ बोले लखनु जोरि जुग पानी। प्रभु प्रभाउ सूचक मृदु बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1294.verse_hindi: हे तात! देखो, कमल, चक्रवाक और समस्त संसार को सुख देने वाला अरुणोदय हुआ है। लक्ष्मणजी दोनों हाथ जोड़कर प्रभु के प्रभाव को सूचित करने वाली कोमल वाणी बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1294.english_translation: Look, dear brother, dawn has risen, bringing joy to the lotus, the cakravaka bird, and the whole world. Lakshmana then joined his palms and spoke gently, revealing the Lord's greatness.
ramacharitamanas::1294.translation_literal: उयउ (has risen) / अरुन (reddish dawn) / अवलोकहु (look) / ताता (dear brother) / पंकज (lotus) / कोक (cakravaka bird) / लोक (world) / सुखदाता (giver of joy) / बोले (spoke) / लखनु (Lakshmana) / जोरि (joining) / जुग (both) / पानी (hands) / प्रभु (Lord's) / प्रभाउ (greatness) / सूचक (indicating) / मृदु (soft) / बानी (speech)
ramacharitamanas::1294.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1294.essence: Even dawn becomes sacred when spoken with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1294.simple_meaning: Dawn arrives, and Lakshmana speaks softly to draw attention to it. The verse mainly sets the scene and shows his respectful manner.
ramacharitamanas::1294.simple_insight: Small moments can carry reverence. Even a sunrise becomes a way to speak with care.
ramacharitamanas::1294.detailed_meaning: After resting through the night, Ram wakes and Lakshmana sees the dawn. He points out the red sky, the lotus, and the cakravaka bird, then speaks with folded hands. The verse gently prepares the next exchange by showing his devotion and awareness.
ramacharitamanas::1294.modern_relevance: You step outside before sunrise, coffee still warm in your hand, and someone quietly points to the sky. A simple moment suddenly feels respectful, awake, and full of meaning.
ramacharitamanas::1294.insight: It trains attention to notice beauty first and to speak with humility.

ramacharitamanas::1295.verse_sanskrit: अरुनोदयँ सकुचे कुमुद उडगन जोति मलीन। जिमि तुम्हार आगमन सुनि भए नृपति बलहीन ॥
ramacharitamanas::1295.verse_hindi: अरुणोदय होने से कुमुदिनी सकुचा गई और तारागणों का प्रकाश फीका पड़ गया, जिस प्रकार आपका आना सुनकर सब राजा बलहीन हो गए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1295.english_translation: At sunrise, the lilies close and the stars fade. So too, hearing your arrival, the kings became powerless.
ramacharitamanas::1295.translation_literal: अरुनोदयँ (at sunrise) / सकुचे (withered/closed) / कुमुद (night-lilies) / उडगन (stars) / जोति (light) / मलीन (dimmed) / जिमि (just as) / तुम्हार (your) / आगमन (arrival) / सुनि (hearing) / भए (became) / नृपति (kings) / बलहीन (powerless)
ramacharitamanas::1295.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1295.essence: Real power makes lesser power fade on its own.
ramacharitamanas::1295.simple_meaning: At dawn, night flowers close and stars lose their shine. In the same way, the kings lose strength when you arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1295.simple_insight: True greatness makes lesser power fade without effort.
ramacharitamanas::1295.detailed_meaning: As dawn breaks in Ayodhya, the scene shifts from night to morning. The poet compares the fading stars and closing lilies to the kings gathered around Rama and Lakshmana: their pride and force shrink naturally in his presence.
ramacharitamanas::1295.modern_relevance: A room full of confident voices goes quiet when one person with real authority walks in. Some presence does not need to announce itself; it simply changes the field.
ramacharitamanas::1295.insight: It shifts attention from outward status to the quiet force that outshines it.

ramacharitamanas::1296.verse_sanskrit: नृप सब नखत करहिं उजिआरी। टारि न सकहिं चाप तम भारी॥ कमल कोक मधुकर खग नाना। हरषे सकल निसा अवसाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1296.verse_hindi: सब राजा रूपी तारे उजाला (मंद प्रकाश) करते हैं, पर वे धनुष रूपी महान अंधकार को हटा नहीं सकते। रात्रि का अंत होने से जैसे कमल, चकवे, भौंरे और नाना प्रकार के पक्षी हर्षित हो रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1296.english_translation: All the kings shine like stars, but they cannot remove the great darkness of the bow. As night ends, the lotus, chakor, bees, and many birds rejoice.
ramacharitamanas::1296.translation_literal: नृप (kings) / सब (all) / नखत (stars) / करहिं (make) / उजिआरी (light) / टारि (remove) / न सकहिं (cannot) / चाप (bow) / तम (darkness) / भारी (heavy, great) / कमल (lotus) / कोक (chakor bird) / मधुकर (bees) / खग (birds) / नाना (various) / हरषे (rejoiced) / सकल (all) / निसा (night) / अवसाना (at end)
ramacharitamanas::1296.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1296.essence: Brightness without power cannot clear the darkness.
ramacharitamanas::1296.simple_meaning: Many kings can shine with power, but none can remove the great obstacle before them. When night ends, all living things rejoice.
ramacharitamanas::1296.simple_insight: Some problems are bigger than status or pride. Relief comes when the right force finally arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1296.detailed_meaning: At the Sita-swayamvar, the gathered kings are compared to stars: bright in their own right, but powerless before Shiva's great bow. The night-like tension is ending, and the scene turns toward Ram's arrival, which will change everything.
ramacharitamanas::1296.modern_relevance: A room full of confident people can still freeze when the real challenge appears. Titles look bright until one person quietly does what none of them can do.
ramacharitamanas::1296.insight: It shifts attention from appearance and rank to actual capacity. The verse prepares the mind to see who can truly act.

ramacharitamanas::1297.verse_sanskrit: ऐसेहिं प्रभु सब भगत तुम्हारे। होइहहिं टूटें धनुष सुखारे॥ उयउ भानु बिनु श्रम तम नासा। दुरे नखत जग तेजु प्रकासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1297.verse_hindi: वैसे ही हे प्रभो! आपके सब भक्त धनुष टूटने पर सुखी होंगे। सूर्य उदय हुआ, बिना ही परिश्रम अंधकार नष्ट हो गया। तारे छिप गए, संसार में तेज का प्रकाश हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1297.english_translation: In the same way, O Lord, all your devotees will rejoice when the bow is broken. The sun has risen, and without effort the darkness is destroyed. The stars hide, and the world is filled with radiance.
ramacharitamanas::1297.translation_literal: ऐसेहिं (in the same way) / प्रभु (Lord) / सब (all) / भगत (devotees) / तुम्हारे (your) / होइहहिं (will become) / टूटें (when broken) / धनुष (bow) / सुखारे (happy)॥ / उयउ (has risen) / भानु (sun) / बिनु (without) / श्रम (effort) / तम (darkness) / नासा (destroyed)॥ / दुरे (hidden) / नखत (stars) / जग (world) / तेजु (radiance) / प्रकासा (became manifest)॥
ramacharitamanas::1297.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1297.essence: Ram’s rise ends resistance without strain.
ramacharitamanas::1297.simple_meaning: The broken bow is compared to sunrise: once the obstacle falls, joy and clarity spread everywhere without strain.
ramacharitamanas::1297.simple_insight: Relief comes when the barrier finally breaks; what felt impossible suddenly feels natural.
ramacharitamanas::1297.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, the assembled kings have failed before Shiva’s bow. Tulsidas compares their defeat to night ending at sunrise: Ram’s effortless power will break the bow, expose the others’ weakness, and make his devotees rejoice.
ramacharitamanas::1297.modern_relevance: You’ve been staring at the same impossible problem for weeks. Then one clean decision cuts through it, and everything around it suddenly makes sense.
ramacharitamanas::1297.insight: It shifts attention from struggling against darkness to recognising the force that ends it.

ramacharitamanas::1298.verse_sanskrit: रबि निज उदय ब्याज रघुराया। प्रभु प्रतापु सब नृपन्ह दिखाया॥ तव भुज बल महिमा उदघाटी। प्रगटी धनु बिघटन परिपाटी।3॥
ramacharitamanas::1298.verse_hindi: हे रघुनाथजी! सूर्य ने अपने उदय के बहाने सब राजाओं को प्रभु (आप) का प्रताप दिखलाया है। आपकी भुजाओं के बल की महिमा को उद्घाटित करने (खोलकर दिखाने) के लिए ही धनुष तोड़ने की यह पद्धति प्रकट हुई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1298.english_translation: O Raghunath, the sun has risen to reveal your glory to all the kings. This breaking of the bow has appeared to display the greatness of your arm-strength.
ramacharitamanas::1298.translation_literal: रबि (sun) / निज (own) / उदय (rise) / ब्याज (pretext) / रघुराया (Raghuraja, Ram) / प्रभु (lord) / प्रतापु (glory) / सब (all) / नृपन्ह (kings) / दिखाया (showed)॥ / तव (your) / भुज (arm) / बल (strength) / महिमा (greatness) / उदघाटी (revealed) / प्रगटी (appeared) / धनु (bow) / बिघटन (breaking) / परिपाटी (method, occasion)॥
ramacharitamanas::1298.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1298.essence: True strength reveals itself without needing to boast.
ramacharitamanas::1298.simple_meaning: The bow-breaking scene is showing Ram's strength to all the kings, just as sunrise reveals everything.
ramacharitamanas::1298.simple_insight: Real power does not announce itself; it becomes undeniable when the moment arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1298.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the kings have gathered around Shiva's great bow. The previous verse likened them to stars before sunrise; now Tulsidas says the breaking of the bow exists to reveal Ram's strength and glory to everyone present.
ramacharitamanas::1298.modern_relevance: A room full of confident people goes quiet when the least-showy person solves the problem no one else could. The moment exposes what was real all along.
ramacharitamanas::1298.insight: It shifts attention from public display to the quiet proof of capability under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::1299.verse_sanskrit: बंधु बचन सुनि प्रभु मुसुकाने। होइ सुचि सहज पुनीत नहाने॥ कनित्यक्रिया करि गरु पहिं आए। चरन सरोज सुभग सिर नाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1299.verse_hindi: भाई के वचन सुनकर प्रभु मुस्कुराए। फिर स्वभाव से ही पवित्र श्री रामजी ने शौच से निवृत्त होकर स्नान किया और नित्यकर्म करके वे गुरुजी के पास आए। आकर उन्होंने गुरुजी के सुंदर चरण कमलों में सिर नवाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1299.english_translation: Hearing his brother's words, the Lord smiled. Then, naturally pure, Ram bathed, performed his daily rites, and came to the guru. Arriving, he bowed his head at the guru's lovely lotus feet.
ramacharitamanas::1299.translation_literal: बंधु बचन (brother's words) / सुनि (having heard) / प्रभु (the Lord) / मुसुकाने (smiled) / होइ (being) / सुचि (pure) / सहज (naturally) / पुनीत (purified) / नहाने (bathed) / कनित्यक्रिया (daily rites) / करि (having done) / गरु पहिं (to the guru) / आए (came) / चरन सरोज (lotus feet) / सुभग (beautiful) / सिर (head) / नाए (bowed)
ramacharitamanas::1299.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1299.essence: Victory never excuses forgetting the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::1299.simple_meaning: Ram smiles, completes his daily purification, and goes to bow before his teacher.
ramacharitamanas::1299.simple_insight: Even the highest dignity bends easily before the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::1299.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, after the bow has broken and the scene is still charged with wonder, Ram hears his brother's words with a smile. He remains calm, keeps ritual order, and goes first to honor his guru before anything else.
ramacharitamanas::1299.modern_relevance: A room is buzzing after a big win, and everyone wants applause. You quietly wash up, steady yourself, and go thank the person who trained you.
ramacharitamanas::1299.insight: It shifts attention from celebration to reverence, showing that achievement still begins with humility.

ramacharitamanas::1300.verse_sanskrit: सतानंदु तब जनक बोलाए। कौसिक मुनि पहिं तुरत पठाए॥ जनक बिनय तिन्ह आइ सुनाई। हरषे बोलि लिए दोउ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1300.verse_hindi: तब जनकजी ने शतानंदजी को बुलाया और उन्हें तुरंत ही विश्वामित्र मुनि के पास भेजा। उन्होंने आकर जनकजी की विनती सुनाई। विश्वामित्रजी ने हर्षित होकर दोनों भाइयों को बुलाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1300.english_translation: Then Janaka called Shatananda and quickly sent him to Sage Vishvamitra. He came and conveyed Janaka's request. Vishvamitra was delighted and called both brothers.
ramacharitamanas::1300.translation_literal: सतानंदु (Shatananda) / तब (then) / जनक (Janaka) / बोलाए (called) / कौसिक मुनि (Sage Vishvamitra) / पहिं (to) / तुरत (quickly) / पठाए (sent)॥ / जनक (Janaka) / बिनय (request) / तिन्ह (he) / आइ (coming) / सुनाई (told) / हरषे (delighted) / बोलि लिए (called) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1300.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1300.essence: A respectful request moves the story forward.
ramacharitamanas::1300.simple_meaning: Janaka sends Shatananda to Vishvamitra with a request, and Vishvamitra happily calls the two brothers.
ramacharitamanas::1300.simple_insight: Right timing and respectful mediation can open the way forward.
ramacharitamanas::1300.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's court, Shatananda is sent to Vishvamitra as a messenger. He returns with Janaka's request, and the sage responds with joy by summoning Ram and Lakshman. The verse simply moves the wedding story forward.
ramacharitamanas::1300.modern_relevance: A message finally reaches the right person after days of waiting. One calm messenger, one respectful request, and suddenly the room opens again.
ramacharitamanas::1300.insight: It shows how courteous communication can clear a path for action.

ramacharitamanas::1301.verse_sanskrit: सतानंद पद बंदि प्रभु बैठे गुर पहिं जाइ। चलहु तात मुनि कहेउ तब पठवा जनक बोलाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1301.verse_hindi: शतानन्दजी के चरणों की वंदना करके प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी गुरुजी के पास जा बैठे। तब मुनि ने कहा- हे तात! चलो, जनकजी ने बुला भेजा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1301.english_translation: After bowing to Shatanand, Lord Ram went and sat near the guru. Then the sage said, “Come, dear one. Janak has sent for you.”
ramacharitamanas::1301.translation_literal: सतानंद (Shatanand) / पद (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / प्रभु (Lord) / बैठे (sat) / गुरु (teacher) / पहिं (to) / जाइ (going) / चलहु (come/go) / तात (dear one) / मुनि (sage) / कहेउ (said) / तब (then) / पठवा (sent) / जनक (Janak) / बोलाइ (calling)
ramacharitamanas::1301.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1301.simple_meaning: Ram bows to Shatanand and sits near the teacher. The sage then calls him to come because Janak has sent for him.
ramacharitamanas::1301.simple_insight: Respect comes before the next step. Even the divine prince moves with humility.
ramacharitamanas::1301.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the formalities before Sita's swayamvar are unfolding. Ram first bows to Shatanand, then goes to sit near the guru. Only after that does the sage call him onward, saying Janak has summoned him.
ramacharitamanas::1301.modern_relevance: You enter a room full of important people and still greet the oldest person first. The moment stays clean because pride never gets to lead.
ramacharitamanas::1301.insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing that true dignity begins with humility.

ramacharitamanas::1302.verse_sanskrit: सीय स्वयंबरू देखिअ जाई। ईसु काहि धौं देइ बड़ाई॥ लखन कहा जस भाजनु सोई। नाथ कृपा तव जापर होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1302.verse_hindi: चलकर सीताजी के स्वयंवर को देखना चाहिए। देखें ईश्वर किसको बड़ाई देते हैं। लक्ष्मणजी ने कहा- हे नाथ! जिस पर आपकी कृपा होगी, वही बड़ाई का पात्र होगा (धनुष तोड़ने का श्रेय उसी को प्राप्त होगा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1302.english_translation: Let us go and see Sita's swayamvara. Let us see whom the divine will honor. Lakshman said, "O Lord, the one on whom your grace falls becomes worthy of honor."
ramacharitamanas::1302.translation_literal: सीय (of Sita) / स्वयंबरू (swayamvara) / देखिअ (let us see) / जाई (go) / ईसु (the divine) / काहि (whom) / धौं (indeed) / देइ (gives) / बड़ाई (honor) / लखन (Lakshman) / कहा (said) / जस (as) / भाजनु (worthy recipient) / सोई (that one) / नाथ (Lord) / कृपा (grace) / तव (your) / जापर (on whom) / होई (is)
ramacharitamanas::1302.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::1302.essence: Grace, not display, decides who is truly honored.
ramacharitamanas::1302.simple_meaning: Lakshman says they should go see Sita's swayamvara, and that real honor will go to the one chosen by Ram's grace.
ramacharitamanas::1302.simple_insight: Praise belongs to grace, not to ego or effort alone.
ramacharitamanas::1302.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the guests are being led toward Sita's swayamvara. Lakshman speaks with quiet certainty: the real winner will not be the loudest or strongest, but the one on whom Ram's grace rests. The moment prepares the way for the bow challenge.
ramacharitamanas::1302.modern_relevance: You watch a room full of people trying to impress the panel, polish their answers, and claim the spotlight. One calm voice cuts through the noise: real worth is not self-made theater.
ramacharitamanas::1302.insight: It shifts attention from public display to the quiet source of true honor.

ramacharitamanas::1303.verse_sanskrit: हरषे मुनि सब सुनि बर बानी। दीन्हि असीस सबहिं सुखु मानी॥ पुनि मुनिबृंद समेत कृपाला। देखन चले धनुषमख साला ॥
ramacharitamanas::1303.verse_hindi: इस श्रेष्ठ वाणी को सुनकर सब मुनि प्रसन्न हुए। सभी ने सुख मानकर आशीर्वाद दिया। फिर मुनियों के समूह सहित कृपालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी धनुष यज्ञशाला देखने चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1303.english_translation: Hearing this noble speech, all the sages rejoiced and gave blessings, finding peace in it. Then the compassionate Ram, with the gathered sages, went to see the hall of the bow sacrifice.
ramacharitamanas::1303.translation_literal: हरषे (rejoiced) / मुनि (sages) / सब (all) / सुनि (hearing) / बर (excellent) / बानी (speech) / दीन्हि (gave) / असीस (blessings) / सबहिं (to all) / सुखु (peace) / मानी (considered)॥ / पुनि (then) / मुनिबृंद (group of sages) / समेत (together with) / कृपाला (the compassionate one) / देखन (to see) / चले (went) / धनुषमख (bow sacrifice) / साला (hall) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1303.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1303.essence: Graceful words clear the path for what comes next.
ramacharitamanas::1303.simple_meaning: The sages are pleased by the exchange and bless everyone. Then Ram goes with them to see the bow-sacrifice hall.
ramacharitamanas::1303.simple_insight: A calm blessing can open the way for the next step.
ramacharitamanas::1303.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, the sages hear Ram’s gracious words and feel reassured. They bless the gathering, and Ram, accompanied by them, walks toward the bow-sacrifice hall. The verse simply moves the story forward.
ramacharitamanas::1303.modern_relevance: A tense room softens after one respectful sentence, and everyone can finally move. Sometimes the right words do not solve the moment; they make the next step possible.
ramacharitamanas::1303.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic action to the quiet power of courtesy and blessing.

ramacharitamanas::1304.verse_sanskrit: रंगभूमि आए दोउ भाई। असि सुधि सब पुरबासिन्ह पाई॥ चले सकल गृह काज बिसारी। बाल जुबान जरठ नर नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1304.verse_hindi: दोनों भाई रंगभूमि में आए हैं, ऐसी खबर जब सब नगर निवासियों ने पाई, तब बालक, जवान, बूढ़े, स्त्री, पुरुष सभी घर और काम-काज को भुलाकर चल दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1304.english_translation: When the two brothers arrived at the arena, the whole city heard. Men and women, young and old, forgot their homes and work and rushed out.
ramacharitamanas::1304.translation_literal: रंगभूमि (arena) / आए (came) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / असि (such) / सुधि (news) / सब (all) / पुरबासिन्ह (city-dwellers) / पाई (having received) / चले (went) / सकल (all) / गृह (home) / काज (work) / बिसारी (forgetting) / बाल (children) / जुबान (young) / जरठ (old) / नर (men) / नारी (women)
ramacharitamanas::1304.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1304.essence: Their arrival makes ordinary life disappear.
ramacharitamanas::1304.simple_meaning: News of the two brothers reaching the arena spread through the city, and everyone left home at once to see them.
ramacharitamanas::1304.simple_insight: A moment of arrival can pull an entire city out of its routine.
ramacharitamanas::1304.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have entered the arena for Sita's swayamvar. The news spreads through Mithila, and the people abandon their homes and work to see them. The verse builds the public excitement before Janak notices the crowd.
ramacharitamanas::1304.modern_relevance: A message hits the family group chat: the person everyone has been waiting for is finally here. Dinner is forgotten, chores are dropped, and everyone heads out at once.
ramacharitamanas::1304.insight: It shows how presence can outweigh routine, drawing attention away from ordinary obligations.

ramacharitamanas::1305.verse_sanskrit: देखी जनक भीर भै भारी। सुचि सेवक सब लिए हँकारी॥ तुरत सकल लोगन्ह पहिं जाहू। आसन उचित देहु सब काहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1305.verse_hindi: जब जनकजी ने देखा कि बड़ी भीड़ हो गई है, तब उन्होंने सब विश्वासपात्र सेवकों को बुलवा लिया और कहा- तुम लोग तुरंत सब लोगों के पास जाओ और सब किसी को यथायोग्य आसन दो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1305.english_translation: Seeing the crowd become very large, Janaka called his trusted servants and said, "Go at once to everyone and give each person a proper seat."
ramacharitamanas::1305.translation_literal: देखी (seeing) / जनक (Janaka) / भीर (crowd) / भै (became) / भारी (large) / सुचि (trustworthy) / सेवक (servants) / सब (all) / लिए (having taken/called) / हँकारी (called out) / तुरत (immediately) / सकल (all) / लोगन्ह (people) / पहिं (to) / जाहू (go) / आसन (seat) / उचित (proper) / देहु (give) / सब (to everyone) / काहू (each one)
ramacharitamanas::1305.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1305.essence: True hospitality begins when everyone is given their rightful place.
ramacharitamanas::1305.simple_meaning: Janaka sees the gathering grow too large, so he instructs his trusted servants to go at once and seat everyone properly.
ramacharitamanas::1305.simple_insight: Respect is shown in small, immediate acts that make room for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::1305.detailed_meaning: At the bow sacrifice in Janakpur, the crowd has swelled around Ram and Lakshman. Janaka notices the disorder and quickly sends trusted servants to seat every visitor with care, showing royal grace before the swayamvar begins.
ramacharitamanas::1305.modern_relevance: At a packed wedding hall, guests are standing near the entrance while the family rushes to find chairs and guide people in. Order begins with noticing who has been left waiting.
ramacharitamanas::1305.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle to the dignity of each person present.

ramacharitamanas::1306.verse_sanskrit: कहि मृदु बचन बिनीत तिन्ह बैठारे नर नारि। उत्तम मध्यम नीच लघु निज निज थल अनुहारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1306.verse_hindi: उन सेवकों ने कोमल और नम्र वचन कहकर उत्तम, मध्यम, नीच और लघु (सभी श्रेणी के) स्त्री-पुरुषों को अपने-अपने योग्य स्थान पर बैठाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1306.english_translation: The servants spoke gently and respectfully, seating men and women of every rank in their proper places.
ramacharitamanas::1306.translation_literal: कहि (speaking) / मृदु (gentle) / बचन (words) / बिनीत (humble) / तिन्ह (they) / बैठारे (seated) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / उत्तम (excellent) / मध्यम (middle) / नीच (low) / लघु (small) / निज निज (each one’s own) / थल (place) / अनुहारि (according to)
ramacharitamanas::1306.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1306.essence: Respectful order makes space for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::1306.simple_meaning: The servants politely arranged everyone according to rank and gave each person a fitting seat.
ramacharitamanas::1306.simple_insight: Order can be created without force when respect leads the way.
ramacharitamanas::1306.detailed_meaning: Janak has ordered his attendants to make room for the great crowd gathered for the swayamvar. The servants respond with gentle speech, seating everyone properly by rank so the gathering stays orderly before Ram and Lakshman arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1306.modern_relevance: At a packed wedding hall, one calm coordinator quietly guides elders, friends, and strangers to their seats. No shouting, no chaos — just respect doing the work.
ramacharitamanas::1306.insight: It shows how humility and clear order can hold a crowd together before a major event.

ramacharitamanas::1307.verse_sanskrit: राजकुअँर तेहि अवसर आए। मनहुँ मनोहरता तन छाए॥ गुन सागर नागर बर बीरा। सुंदर स्यामल गौर सरीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1307.verse_hindi: उसी समय राजकुमार (राम और लक्ष्मण) वहाँ आए। (वे ऐसे सुंदर हैं) मानो साक्षात मनोहरता ही उनके शरीरों पर छा रही हो। सुंदर साँवला और गोरा उनका शरीर है। वे गुणों के समुद्र, चतुर और उत्तम वीर हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1307.english_translation: At that moment, the princes arrived. Beauty itself seemed to rest upon their bodies. Their forms were lovely, dark and fair; they were oceans of virtue, polished and noble warriors.
ramacharitamanas::1307.translation_literal: राजकुअँर (princes) / तेहि अवसर (at that moment) / आए (came) / मनहुँ (as if) / मनोहरता (beauty, loveliness) / तन (body) / छाए (covered, spread over) ॥ / गुन (virtues) / सागर (ocean) / नागर (polished, refined) / बर (excellent) / बीरा (warriors) / सुंदर (beautiful) / स्यामल (dark-complexioned) / गौर (fair-complexioned) / सरीरा (bodies) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1307.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1307.essence: True nobility announces itself before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1307.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman arrive at the gathering, and their beauty, virtue, and noble strength immediately stand out.
ramacharitamanas::1307.simple_insight: Some presences need no introduction; their character is visible the moment they enter.
ramacharitamanas::1307.detailed_meaning: Janak's court has filled with nobles and onlookers for the swayamvar. Just as the crowd is being arranged, Ram and Lakshman enter. Their arrival changes the whole atmosphere, and the poet pauses to describe their radiance before the bow contest begins.
ramacharitamanas::1307.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when two people walk in and carry themselves with ease, restraint, and unmistakable character. Before they speak, everyone already senses who they are.
ramacharitamanas::1307.insight: It shifts attention from appearance alone to beauty joined with virtue and composure.

ramacharitamanas::1308.verse_sanskrit: राज समाज बिराजत रूरे। उडगन महुँ जनु जुग बिधु पूरे॥ जिन्ह कें रही भावना जैसी। प्रभु मूरति तिन्ह देखी तैसी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1308.verse_hindi: वे राजाओं के समाज में ऐसे सुशोभित हो रहे हैं, मानो तारागणों के बीच दो पूर्ण चन्द्रमा हों। जिनकी जैसी भावना थी, प्रभु की मूर्ति उन्होंने वैसी ही देखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1308.english_translation: They shine in the assembly of kings like two full moons among the stars. Each person saw the Lord in the form shaped by their own feeling.
ramacharitamanas::1308.translation_literal: राज समाज (assembly of kings) / बिराजत (shining) / रूरे (beautiful) / उडगन (stars) / महुँ (among) / जनु (as if) / जुग (two) / बिधु (moons) / पूरे (full) ॥ / जिन्ह कें (for whom) / रही (remained) / भावना (feeling) / जैसी (as) / प्रभु (Lord) / मूरति (form) / तिन्ह (they) / देखी (saw) / तैसी (that same) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1308.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1308.essence: Ram appears differently to each heart.
ramacharitamanas::1308.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman stand out in the royal assembly like two full moons among stars. People see Ram according to the feeling already in their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1308.simple_insight: What you bring inside shapes what you recognize outside.
ramacharitamanas::1308.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have entered the gathering of kings at Sita’s swayamvar. Their beauty fills the hall, but the deeper point is subtler: each observer sees Ram through the lens of their own inner state. This moment prepares the reactions that follow.
ramacharitamanas::1308.modern_relevance: At a crowded wedding, one person sees only the decorations, another feels the tension, and another notices a single face that changes everything. The same room meets three different hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1308.insight: It shifts attention from the object alone to the observer’s inner condition.

ramacharitamanas::1309.verse_sanskrit: देखहिं रूप महा रनधीरा। मनहुँ बीर रसु धरें सरीरा॥ डरे कुटिल नृप प्रभुहि निहारी। मनहुँ भयानक मूरति भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1309.verse_hindi: महान रणधीर (राजा लोग) श्री रामचन्द्रजी के रूप को ऐसा देख रहे हैं, मानो स्वयं वीर रस शरीर धारण किए हुए हों। कुटिल राजा प्रभु को देखकर डर गए, मानो बड़ी भयानक मूर्ति हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1309.english_translation: The great warriors saw Ram's form as if heroic power itself had taken shape. The crooked kings feared him, as if a terrible image stood before them.
ramacharitamanas::1309.translation_literal: देखहिं (they see) / रूप (form) / महा (great) / रनधीरा (warriors) / मनहुँ (as if) / बीर रसु (heroic essence) / धरें (having taken) / सरीरा (body) ॥ डरे (were afraid) / कुटिल (crooked) / नृप (kings) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / निहारी (seeing) / मनहुँ (as if) / भयानक (terrible) / मूरति (form) / भारी (great) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1309.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1309.essence: A pure presence inspires the upright and unsettles the crooked.
ramacharitamanas::1309.simple_meaning: The brave see Ram and feel courage itself made visible. The crooked kings see him and feel fear instead.
ramacharitamanas::1309.simple_insight: The same presence can awaken courage in the honest and fear in the crooked.
ramacharitamanas::1309.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, kings fill the hall and Ram enters with Lakshman. The noble feel inspired by his presence, but the scheming kings sense danger. This verse shows how one form is received differently by different hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1309.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and some people relax while others stiffen. The same calm, honest presence can feel welcoming to one person and threatening to another.
ramacharitamanas::1309.insight: It shifts attention from Ram's appearance to the viewer's own character.

ramacharitamanas::1310.verse_sanskrit: रहे असुर छल छोनिप बेषा। तिन्ह प्रभु प्रगट कालसम देखा। पुरबासिन्ह देखे दोउ भाई। नरभूषन लोचन सुखदाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1310.verse_hindi: छल से जो राक्षस वहाँ राजाओं के वेष में (बैठे) थे, उन्होंने प्रभु को प्रत्यक्ष काल के समान देखा। नगर निवासियों ने दोनों भाइयों को मनुष्यों के भूषण रूप और नेत्रों को सुख देने वाला देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1310.english_translation: The disguised demons saw the Lord as time itself. The people of the city saw the two brothers as the ornament of humankind and a delight to the eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1310.translation_literal: रहे (remained) / असुर (demons) / छल (deception) / छोनिप (royal) / बेषा (disguise) / तिन्ह (they) / प्रभु (the Lord) / प्रगट (manifest) / कालसम (like time/death) / देखा (saw) / पुरबासिन्ह (townspeople) / देखे (saw) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / नरभूषन (ornament of men) / लोचन (eyes) / सुखदाई (giving delight)
ramacharitamanas::1310.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1310.essence: One form brings dread to the crooked and joy to the pure.
ramacharitamanas::1310.simple_meaning: The hidden enemies saw Ram as a terrifying force, while the city people saw Ram and Lakshman as graceful and beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::1310.simple_insight: The same presence can reveal fear in one heart and joy in another.
ramacharitamanas::1310.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the royal gathering is watching Ram and Lakshman after the swayamvar. The disguised demons still seated among the kings feel the Lord as death itself, while the townspeople behold the two brothers as the finest ornament of human form.
ramacharitamanas::1310.modern_relevance: In a crowded room, one person feels threatened by your calm while another feels comforted by it. The same presence exposes the state of each observer.
ramacharitamanas::1310.insight: It shows that perception depends on the viewer's inner state, not only on what is seen.

ramacharitamanas::1311.verse_sanskrit: नारि बिलोकहिं हरषि हियँ निज-निज रुचि अनुरूप। जनु सोहत सिंगार धरि मूरति परम अनूप ॥
ramacharitamanas::1311.verse_hindi: स्त्रियाँ हृदय में हर्षित होकर अपनी-अपनी रुचि के अनुसार उन्हें देख रही हैं। मानो श्रृंगार रस ही परम अनुपम मूर्ति धारण किए सुशोभित हो रहा हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1311.english_translation: The women look at him with joy, each according to her own liking. It is as if beauty itself has taken a most incomparable form.
ramacharitamanas::1311.translation_literal: नारि (women) / बिलोकहिं (look) / हरषि (with joy) / हियँ (in the heart) / निज-निज (each one’s own) / रुचि (liking) / अनुरूप (according to) / जनु (as if) / सोहत (shining, beautifying) / सिंगार (beauty, adornment) / धरि (having taken) / मूरति (form) / परम (supreme) / अनूप (matchless)
ramacharitamanas::1311.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1311.essence: Ram's beauty is so complete that every heart sees its own delight in him.
ramacharitamanas::1311.simple_meaning: The women in the crowd are delighted by Ram's presence, and each sees him in her own way. His beauty seems beyond comparison.
ramacharitamanas::1311.simple_insight: True beauty meets each heart differently and still leaves everyone quietly amazed.
ramacharitamanas::1311.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the assembly is reacting to Ram's arrival. After kings and even hidden enemies have looked on him with fear, the women see him with delighted hearts, each through her own tender taste. Tulsidas pauses to show how Ram's form awakens joy rather than alarm.
ramacharitamanas::1311.modern_relevance: At a wedding, one person notices the groom's calm, another his grace, another his kindness. The same presence lands differently in each heart, yet all feel the pull of something rare.
ramacharitamanas::1311.insight: It shifts attention from one fixed description to the many ways a noble presence is received.

ramacharitamanas::1312.verse_sanskrit: बिदुषन्ह प्रभु बिराटमय दीसा। बहु मुख कर पग लोचन सीसा॥ जनक जाति अवलोकहिं कैसें। सजन सगे प्रिय लागहिं जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1312.verse_hindi: विद्वानों को प्रभु विराट रूप में दिखाई दिए, जिसके बहुत से मुँह, हाथ, पैर, नेत्र और सिर हैं। जनकजी के सजातीय (कुटुम्बी) प्रभु को किस तरह (कैसे प्रिय रूप में) देख रहे हैं, जैसे सगे सजन (संबंधी) प्रिय लगते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1312.english_translation: To the learned, the Lord appeared as the cosmic form, with many mouths, hands, feet, eyes, and heads. How the people of Janaka's line saw him, they loved him like dear relatives.
ramacharitamanas::1312.translation_literal: बिदुषन्ह (to the learned) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बिराटमय (filled with the cosmic form) / दीसा (appeared) । / बहु (many) / मुख (mouths) / कर (hands) / पग (feet) / लोचन (eyes) / सीसा (heads) ॥ / जनक जाति (Janaka's lineage) / अवलोकहिं (see) / कैसें (how) / सजन (dear relatives) / सगे (related) / प्रिय (beloved) / लागहिं (appear) / जैसें (as if) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1312.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1312.essence: Ram is seen through the heart that looks at him.
ramacharitamanas::1312.simple_meaning: Different people saw Ram in different ways. Scholars saw his vast cosmic form, while Janaka's people saw him as a beloved relative.
ramacharitamanas::1312.simple_insight: The same presence meets each heart differently, and every sincere vision is a true one.
ramacharitamanas::1312.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the wedding scene opens into wonder. Ram stands before the crowd, and the same presence is received in many ways: scholars behold the cosmic form, while Janaka's people feel the warmth of family. The verse shows how devotion and understanding shape vision.
ramacharitamanas::1312.modern_relevance: In a crowded temple hall, one person feels awe, another feels comfort, and another sees only ceremony. The moment is the same; the heart decides what it receives.
ramacharitamanas::1312.insight: It shifts attention from one fixed meaning to many valid ways of seeing the divine presence.

ramacharitamanas::1313.verse_sanskrit: सहित बिदेह बिलोकहिं रानी। सिसु सम प्रीति न जाति बखानी॥ जोगिन्ह परम तत्वमय भासा। सांत सुद्ध सम सहज प्रकासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1313.verse_hindi: जनक समेत रानियाँ उन्हें अपने बच्चे के समान देख रही हैं, उनकी प्रीति का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। योगियों को वे शांत, शुद्ध, सम और स्वतः प्रकाश परम तत्व के रूप में दिखे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1313.english_translation: With Janaka present, the queens looked upon them as their own children; their love cannot be described. Yogis saw them as the supreme reality, peaceful, pure, equal, and naturally radiant.
ramacharitamanas::1313.translation_literal: सहित (along with) / बिदेह (Janaka, king of Videha) / बिलोकहिं (they behold) / रानी (the queens) / सिसु (child) / सम (like) / प्रीति (affection) / न (not) / जाति (can be) / बखानी (described) / जोगिन्ह (for yogis) / परम (supreme) / तत्वमय (made of ultimate reality) / भासा (appeared) / सांत (peaceful) / सुद्ध (pure) / सम (equal) / सहज (natural) / प्रकासा (radiance)
ramacharitamanas::1313.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1313.essence: One presence can awaken tender love and deep realization at once.
ramacharitamanas::1313.simple_meaning: The queens saw Ram and Lakshman with motherly love, while yogis saw them as the supreme reality itself — peaceful, pure, equal, and self-luminous.
ramacharitamanas::1313.simple_insight: The same presence can meet different hearts in different ways, yet all of them feel something sacred.
ramacharitamanas::1313.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, after the first sight of Ram and Lakshman, the crowd is not seeing them in one single way. The queens feel tender, parental love; yogis see the deepest reality shining through them. This verse widens the scene into devotion and realization.
ramacharitamanas::1313.modern_relevance: At a wedding, one grandmother sees a beloved child, a monk sees stillness, and a friend sees grace. The same person can awaken different forms of love and understanding.
ramacharitamanas::1313.insight: It teaches you that true presence is received according to the heart that meets it.

ramacharitamanas::1314.verse_sanskrit: हरिभगतन्ह देखे दोउ भ्राता। इष्टदेव इव सब सुख दाता॥ रामहि चितव भायँ जेहि सीया। सो सनेहु सुखु नहिं कथनीया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1314.verse_hindi: हरि भक्तों ने दोनों भाइयों को सब सुखों के देने वाले इष्ट देव के समान देखा। सीताजी जिस भाव से श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देख रही हैं, वह स्नेह और सुख तो कहने में ही नहीं आता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1314.english_translation: Devotees of Hari saw the two brothers as the giver of all joy, like their chosen deity. The love with which Sita looked at Ram cannot be described.
ramacharitamanas::1314.translation_literal: हरिभगतन्ह (devotees of Hari) / देखे (saw) / दोउ भ्राता (both brothers) / इष्टदेव (chosen deity) / इव (like) / सब सुख दाता (giver of all joy)॥ / रामहि (Ram) / चितव (looked at) / भायँ (with feeling) / जेहि (with which) / सीया (Sita) / सो (that) / सनेहु (love) / सुखु (joy) / नहिं (not) / कथनीया (describable)॥
ramacharitamanas::1314.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1314.essence: Love makes the beloved look like the source of all joy.
ramacharitamanas::1314.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman appear to the devotees as the source of all joy. Sita's loving gaze toward Ram is beyond words.
ramacharitamanas::1314.simple_insight: Love changes how you see someone: ordinary presence becomes a source of joy and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1314.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court during the swayamvar, the onlookers do not see two ordinary princes. Ram and Lakshman appear as the beloved form of the divine, and Sita's gaze toward Ram carries a love too deep for speech.
ramacharitamanas::1314.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love walk into a room, and the whole atmosphere changes. The verse captures that quiet transformation: affection makes the ordinary feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::1314.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to recognition, showing how devotion reveals hidden greatness in another.

ramacharitamanas::1315.verse_sanskrit: उर अनुभवति न कहि सक सोऊ। कवन प्रकार कहै कबि कोऊ॥ एहि बिधि रहा जाहि जस भाऊ। तेहिं तस देखेउ कोसलराऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1315.verse_hindi: उस (स्नेह और सुख) का वे हृदय में अनुभव कर रही हैं, पर वे भी उसे कह नहीं सकतीं। फिर कोई कवि उसे किस प्रकार कह सकता है। इस प्रकार जिसका जैसा भाव था, उसने कोसलाधीश श्री रामचन्द्रजी को वैसा ही देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1315.english_translation: They feel it in the heart but cannot say it. How could any poet describe it? In this way, each person saw the king of Kosala according to the feeling within.
ramacharitamanas::1315.translation_literal: उर (heart) / अनुभवति (experiences) / न (not) / कहि (to say) / सक (able) / सोऊ (that) / कवन (which) / प्रकार (manner) / कहै (says) / कबि (poet) / कोऊ (anyone) / एहि बिधि (in this way) / रहा (remained) / जाहि (whoever) / जस (as) / भाऊ (feeling) / तेहिं (by that) / तस (thus) / देखेउ (saw) / कोसलराऊ (king of Kosala)
ramacharitamanas::1315.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1315.essence: Ram is seen through the feeling already living in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1315.simple_meaning: The feeling in the heart is beyond words. People saw Ram according to their own inner mood and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1315.simple_insight: Some experiences are too full for language; the heart understands before the mind can explain.
ramacharitamanas::1315.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the gathered people are beholding Ram and Lakshman. The joy is so deep that even the witnesses cannot put it into words. Each person receives Ram through their own inner feeling, and that feeling shapes what they see.
ramacharitamanas::1315.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone you love after a long separation, and no sentence feels adequate. The real meeting happens before words arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1315.insight: It shifts attention from explaining devotion to receiving it directly, as a lived inner experience.

ramacharitamanas::1316.verse_sanskrit: राजत राज समाज महुँ कोसलराज किसोर। सुंदर स्यामल गौर तन बिस्व बिलोचन चोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::1316.verse_hindi: सुंदर साँवले और गोरे शरीर वाले तथा विश्वभर के नेत्रों को चुराने वाले कोसलाधीश के कुमार राज समाज में (इस प्रकार) सुशोभित हो रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1316.english_translation: The prince of Kosala shines in the royal assembly, with a beautiful dark-and-light body that steals the eyes of the world.
ramacharitamanas::1316.translation_literal: राजत (shines) / राज समाज महुँ (in the royal assembly) / कोसलराज (king of Kosala) / किसोर (young prince) / सुंदर (beautiful) / स्यामल (dark-complexioned) / गौर तन (fair body) / बिस्व बिलोचन (world's eyes) / चोर (stealer)
ramacharitamanas::1316.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1316.essence: Ram’s beauty silently takes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::1316.simple_meaning: Ram appears as a radiant young prince in the royal court, so beautiful that everyone’s gaze is drawn to him.
ramacharitamanas::1316.simple_insight: Some presence needs no announcement. It simply captures every eye in the room.
ramacharitamanas::1316.detailed_meaning: In King Janak’s royal assembly, the young prince of Kosala stands among the gathered crowd. His dark-and-light radiance and irresistible beauty make everyone look toward him, setting up the deeper praise that follows in the next lines.
ramacharitamanas::1316.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the conversation shifts before you speak. Some people carry a presence that settles attention instantly.
ramacharitamanas::1316.insight: It shifts attention from the crowd to the one who naturally commands it, preparing the mind for reverence.

ramacharitamanas::1317.verse_sanskrit: सहज मनोहर मूरति दोऊ। कोटि काम उपमा लघु सोऊ॥ सरद चंद निंदक मुख नीके। नीरज नयन भावते जी के ॥
ramacharitamanas::1317.verse_hindi: दोनों मूर्तियाँ स्वभाव से ही (बिना किसी बनाव-श्रृंगार के) मन को हरने वाली हैं। करोड़ों कामदेवों की उपमा भी उनके लिए तुच्छ है। उनके सुंदर मुख शरद् (पूर्णिमा) के चन्द्रमा की भी निंदा करने वाले (उसे नीचा दिखाने वाले) हैं और कमल के समान नेत्र मन को बहुत ही भाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1317.english_translation: Both forms are naturally enchanting. Even millions of Kamadevas are small beside them. Their lovely faces outshine the autumn moon, and their lotus eyes delight the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1317.translation_literal: सहज (natural) / मनोहर (enchanting) / मूरति (forms) / दोऊ (both) । / कोटि (crores/millions) / काम (Kamadeva) / उपमा (comparison) / लघु (small) / सोऊ (that also) ॥ / सरद (autumn) / चंद (moon) / निंदक (surpassing/putting to shame) / मुख (faces) / नीके (beautiful) । / नीरज (lotus) / नयन (eyes) / भावते (please/delight) / जी (heart) / के (of) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1317.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1317.simple_meaning: Both princes are naturally beautiful. Their faces are more lovely than the autumn moon, and their lotus eyes delight the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1317.simple_insight: Beauty can feel effortless when it is complete.
ramacharitamanas::1317.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya’s royal court, the two princes sit in splendour, and the people cannot stop looking. Tulsidas lingers on their beauty before the swayamvar, showing that their presence already moves hearts before any action begins.
ramacharitamanas::1317.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence feels effortless — no performance, no polish, yet everyone turns to look. Some kinds of beauty need no decoration at all.
ramacharitamanas::1317.insight: It shifts attention from ornament to innate radiance.

ramacharitamanas::1318.verse_sanskrit: चितवनि चारु मार मनु हरनी। भावति हृदय जाति नहिं बरनी॥ कल कपोल श्रुति कुंडल लोला। चिबुक अधर सुंदर मृदु बोला ॥
ramacharitamanas::1318.verse_hindi: सुंदर चितवन (सारे संसार के मन को हरने वाले) कामदेव के भी मन को हरने वाली है। वह हृदय को बहुत ही प्यारी लगती है, पर उसका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। सुंदर गाल हैं, कानों में चंचल (झूमते हुए) कुंडल हैं। ठोड़ और अधर (होठ) सुंदर हैं, कोमल वाणी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1318.english_translation: Their charming glance steals even the mind of love itself. It delights the heart, yet cannot be described. Beautiful cheeks, playful earrings, a lovely chin and lips, and a soft, graceful voice.
ramacharitamanas::1318.translation_literal: चितवनि (glance) / चारु (beautiful) / मार (of love) / मनु (mind) / हरनी (stealing) / भावति (pleases) / हृदय (heart) / जाति (kind) / नहिं (not) / बरनी (described) / कल (beautiful) / कपोल (cheeks) / श्रुति (ears) / कुंडल (earrings) / लोला (playful, swinging) / चिबुक (chin) / अधर (lips) / सुंदर (beautiful) / मृदु (soft) / बोला (speech)
ramacharitamanas::1318.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1318.essence: Beauty beyond words steals the mind before speech can begin.
ramacharitamanas::1318.simple_meaning: The prince’s face is so beautiful that it captivates the mind, yet words fail to capture it. Every feature—cheeks, earrings, chin, lips, and voice—adds to that charm.
ramacharitamanas::1318.simple_insight: Some beauty is so complete that language only circles it, never contains it.
ramacharitamanas::1318.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya’s royal gathering, the young prince sits radiant among the court. The poet lingers on his face and features, showing that even before action begins, Ram’s presence overwhelms everyone with effortless beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1318.modern_relevance: You catch someone’s face in a crowded train and lose your train of thought for a second. Some presence doesn’t need explanation; it simply stops the mind.
ramacharitamanas::1318.insight: It shifts attention from argument to presence, showing that some truths are felt before they can be named.

ramacharitamanas::1319.verse_sanskrit: कुमुदबंधु कर निंदक हाँसा। भृकुटी बिकट मनोहर नासा॥ भाल बिसाल तिलक झलकाहीं। कच बिलोकि अलि अवलि लजाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1319.verse_hindi: हँसी, चन्द्रमा की किरणों का तिरस्कार करने वाली है। भौंहें टेढ़ी और नासिका मनोहर है। (ऊँचे) चौड़े ललाट पर तिलक झलक रहे हैं (दीप्तिमान हो रहे हैं)। (काले घुँघराले) बालों को देखकर भौंरों की पंक्तियाँ भी लजा जाती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1319.english_translation: Their smile mocks the moonlight. Their eyebrows are striking, and their nose is beautiful. On the broad forehead, the tilak shines. Seeing the dark curls, even lines of bees feel shy.
ramacharitamanas::1319.translation_literal: कुमुदबंधु (moon) / कर (of the hand; here, rays) / निंदक (mocking) / हाँसा (smile, laughter) / भृकुटी (eyebrows) / बिकट (striking, fierce) / मनोहर (beautiful) / नासा (nose) / भाल (forehead) / बिसाल (broad) / तिलक (tilak mark) / झलकाहीं (shine) / कच (hair) / बिलोकि (seeing) / अलि (bees) / अवलि (row, line) / लजाहीं (feel shy)
ramacharitamanas::1319.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1319.essence: Their beauty overwhelms every measure and leaves comparison embarrassed.
ramacharitamanas::1319.simple_meaning: The verse praises the beauty of the two forms: their smile outshines the moon, their features are graceful, and even bees seem ashamed beside their dark hair.
ramacharitamanas::1319.simple_insight: Beauty can feel so complete that ordinary comparisons collapse.
ramacharitamanas::1319.detailed_meaning: Ram and Sita are being described in the middle of the Sita-swayamvar scene. The poet lingers on their faces, brows, forehead, and hair, building a visual hymn of beauty before the ceremony moves forward.
ramacharitamanas::1319.modern_relevance: You catch someone smiling under warm lights at a wedding, and the room seems to pause. Some presences do not just look beautiful; they make every comparison feel small.
ramacharitamanas::1319.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary comparison to reverent seeing.

ramacharitamanas::1320.verse_sanskrit: पीत चौतनीं सिरन्हि सुहाईं। कुसुम कलीं बिच बीच बनाईं॥ रेखें रुचिर कंबु कल गीवाँ। जनु त्रिभुवन सुषमा की सीवाँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1320.verse_hindi: पीली चौकोनी टोपियाँ सिरों पर सुशोभित हैं, जिनके बीच-बीच में फूलों की कलियाँ बनाई (काढ़ी) हुई हैं। शंख के समान सुंदर (गोल) गले में मनोहर तीन रेखाएँ हैं, जो मानो तीनों लोकों की सुंदरता की सीमा (को बता रही) हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1320.english_translation: Yellow pointed caps adorn their heads, decorated between with flower buds. Three lovely lines mark their graceful necks, as if setting the boundary of beauty across the three worlds.
ramacharitamanas::1320.translation_literal: पीत (yellow) / चौतनीं (pointed caps) / सिरन्हि (on the heads) / सुहाईं (adorned beautifully) / कुसुम (flowers) / कलीं (buds) / बिच बीच (here and there, between) / बनाईं (made, decorated) / रेखें (lines) / रुचिर (beautiful) / कंबु (conch-shell) / कल (soft, graceful) / गीवाँ (necks) / जनु (as if) / त्रिभुवन (three worlds) / सुषमा (beauty) / की (of) / सीवाँ (boundary, limit)
ramacharitamanas::1320.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1320.essence: Grace is revealed in the smallest details of form.
ramacharitamanas::1320.simple_meaning: The verse describes the princes’ dress and features: bright caps, flower decorations, and graceful necks with three beautiful lines.
ramacharitamanas::1320.simple_insight: Beauty here is not random; it is carefully shaped, harmonious, and complete.
ramacharitamanas::1320.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, the poet keeps painting the gathered princes in vivid detail. This verse lingers on their ornaments and bodily grace, building the festive atmosphere before the contest begins.
ramacharitamanas::1320.modern_relevance: You notice the careful outfit before a wedding or ceremony: the folded cap, the neat collar, the final touch that makes everything feel complete. The verse lingers on that polished presence.
ramacharitamanas::1320.insight: It shifts attention from action to atmosphere, letting appearance build the emotional weight of the scene.

ramacharitamanas::1321.verse_sanskrit: कुंजर मनि कंठा कलित उरन्हि तुलसिका माल। बृषभ कंध केहरि ठवनि बल निधि बाहु बिसाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1321.verse_hindi: हृदयों पर गजमुक्ताओं के सुंदर कंठे और तुलसी की मालाएँ सुशोभित हैं। उनके कंधे बैलों के कंधे की तरह (ऊँचे तथा पुष्ट) हैं, ऐंड़ (खड़े होने की शान) सिंह की सी है और भुजाएँ विशाल एवं बल की भंडार हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1321.english_translation: Their chests are adorned with elephant-pearls and garlands of tulsi. Their shoulders are broad like bulls, their bearing proud like lions, and their arms are vast with strength.
ramacharitamanas::1321.translation_literal: कुंजर (elephant) / मनि (pearls) / कंठा (necklace) / कलित (adorned) / उरन्हि (on the chests) / तुलसिका (of tulsi) / माल (garland) / बृषभ (bull) / कंध (shoulder) / केहरि (lion) / ठवनि (bearing/stance) / बल (strength) / निधि (storehouse) / बाहु (arms) / बिसाल (vast)
ramacharitamanas::1321.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1321.essence: Beauty and strength appear together in the same form.
ramacharitamanas::1321.simple_meaning: The princes are described as richly adorned, strong, and majestic. Their bodies show both beauty and power.
ramacharitamanas::1321.simple_insight: True presence is not just ornament or strength, but both together, carried with ease.
ramacharitamanas::1321.detailed_meaning: The wedding scene in Mithila is still unfolding. After describing their faces and crowns, the narrator moves to their chests, shoulders, and arms, building the full image of Ram and Lakshman before the swayamvar. This is part of the visual praise, not the main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1321.modern_relevance: At a ceremony, someone walks in with calm confidence — not flashy, not weak, just fully composed. You notice that real dignity comes from both grace and grounded strength.
ramacharitamanas::1321.insight: It trains attention to read character through posture, bearing, and presence, not just appearance.

ramacharitamanas::1322.verse_sanskrit: कटि तूनीर पीत पट बाँधें। कर सर धनुष बाम बर काँधें॥ पीत जग्य उपबीत सुहाए। नख सिख मंजु महाछबि छाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1322.verse_hindi: कमर में तरकस और पीताम्बर बाँधे हैं। (दाहिने) हाथों में बाण और बाएँ सुंदर कंधों पर धनुष तथा पीले यज्ञोपवीत (जनेऊ) सुशोभित हैं। नख से लेकर शिखा तक सब अंग सुंदर हैं, उन पर महान शोभा छाई हुई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1322.english_translation: A quiver is tied at the waist, and a yellow upper cloth is wrapped around the body. Arrows rest in the right hand, and a fine bow rests on the left shoulder. A yellow sacred thread shines, and beauty covers every limb from head to toe.
ramacharitamanas::1322.translation_literal: कटि (waist) / तूनीर (quiver) / पीत पट (yellow cloth) / बाँधें (tied) / कर (hand) / सर (arrows) / धनुष (bow) / बाम (left) / बर (excellent) / काँधें (shoulder) / पीत (yellow) / जग्य उपबीत (sacred thread) / सुहाए (adorned) / नख (nails) / सिख (hair-tuft / head) / मंजु (lovely) / महाछबि (great beauty) / छाए (covered)
ramacharitamanas::1322.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1322.essence: Their presence announces strength before they speak.
ramacharitamanas::1322.simple_meaning: The two brothers are fully armed and beautifully dressed, with sacred signs of their noble status visible on every part of their bodies.
