ramacharitamanas::1322.simple_insight: True dignity can look powerful and graceful at the same time.
ramacharitamanas::1322.detailed_meaning: The crowd is watching Ram and Lakshman approach for Sita's swayamvar. Before anyone speaks, their appearance itself announces courage, royalty, and sacred duty. This verse simply paints that radiant presence.
ramacharitamanas::1322.modern_relevance: You see someone walk into a room and everything about them is settled: prepared, composed, unmistakably ready. Before a word is spoken, their presence has already changed the atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::1322.insight: It shifts attention from what they say to the authority carried in their bearing and appearance.

ramacharitamanas::1323.verse_sanskrit: देखि लोग सब भए सुखारे। एकटक लोचन चलत न तारे॥ हरषे जनकु देखि दोउ भाई। मुनि पद कमल गहे तब जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1323.verse_hindi: उन्हें देखकर सब लोग सुखी हुए। नेत्र एकटक (निमेष शून्य) हैं और तारे (पुतलियाँ) भी नहीं चलते। जनकजी दोनों भाइयों को देखकर हर्षित हुए। तब उन्होंने जाकर मुनि के चरण कमल पकड़ लिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1323.english_translation: Seeing them, everyone felt delighted. Eyes stayed fixed without blinking, and even the pupils did not move. King Janaka rejoiced on seeing the two brothers, and then went to bow at the sage's lotus feet.
ramacharitamanas::1323.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / भए (became) / सुखारे (delighted) / एकटक (fixed in one gaze) / लोचन (eyes) / चलत (moving) / न (not) / तारे (pupils) / हरषे (rejoiced) / जनकु (Janaka) / देखि (seeing) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / मुनि (sage) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / गहे (held) / तब (then) / जाई (going)
ramacharitamanas::1323.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1323.essence: Presence alone can quiet a crowd and lift the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1323.simple_meaning: The crowd is so struck by the sight of the two brothers that everyone watches without blinking. Janaka is overjoyed and bows to the sage.
ramacharitamanas::1323.simple_insight: A beautiful presence can still the whole room and soften even a king's heart.
ramacharitamanas::1323.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's sacrifice hall, the two princes have just appeared in full splendour. The crowd falls silent in wonder, and Janaka's joy rises at once. This verse shows the first wave of awe before the formal meeting begins.
ramacharitamanas::1323.modern_relevance: You catch sight of someone entering a room, and every conversation stops for a second. The whole atmosphere changes before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1323.insight: It shifts attention from speech to presence: some moments announce themselves before anyone explains them.

ramacharitamanas::1324.verse_sanskrit: करि बिनती निज कथा सुनाई। रंग अवनि सब मुनिहि देखाई॥ जहँ जहँ जाहिं कुअँर बर दोऊ। तहँ तहँ चकित चितव सबु कोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1324.verse_hindi: विनती करके अपनी कथा सुनाई और मुनि को सारी रंगभूमि (यज्ञशाला) दिखलाई। (मुनि के साथ) दोनों श्रेष्ठ राजकुमार जहाँ-जहाँ जाते हैं, वहाँ-वहाँ सब कोई आश्चर्यचकित हो देखने लगते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1324.english_translation: After offering respect, he told his own story and showed the sage the whole arena. Wherever the two noble princes went, everyone stared in amazement.
ramacharitamanas::1324.translation_literal: करि (having done) / बिनती (respectful request) / निज (own) / कथा (story) / सुनाई (told) / रंग अवनि (arena-ground) / सब (all) / मुनिहि (to the sage) / देखाई (showed) / जहँ जहँ (wherever) / जाहिं (go) / कुअँर (princes) / बर (excellent) / दोऊ (both) / तहँ तहँ (there there) / चकित (astonished) / चितव (looked) / सबु (everyone) / कोऊ (someone/everyone)
ramacharitamanas::1324.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1324.essence: Their presence turns an ordinary gathering into astonishment.
ramacharitamanas::1324.simple_meaning: He respectfully explains the situation to the sage, and the two princes draw amazed attention everywhere they go.
ramacharitamanas::1324.simple_insight: Some presence is so complete that it changes the whole room without a word.
ramacharitamanas::1324.detailed_meaning: In Janak's sacrificial arena, the sage is being guided through the scene after the princes arrive. The focus is still on setting up the moment: the brothers move through the space, and every eye turns toward them in wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1324.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the conversation quietly stops. No announcement is needed; people feel something important has arrived.
ramacharitamanas::1324.insight: It frames the princes as figures whose presence itself commands attention, before any action begins.

ramacharitamanas::1325.verse_sanskrit: निज निज रुख रामहि सबु देखा। कोउ न जान कछु मरमु बिसेषा॥ भलि रचना मुनि नृप सन कहेऊ। राजाँ मुदित महासुख लहेऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1325.verse_hindi: सबने रामजी को अपनी-अपनी ओर ही मुख किए हुए देखा, परन्तु इसका कुछ भी विशेष रहस्य कोई नहीं जान सका। मुनि ने राजा से कहा- रंगभूमि की रचना बड़ी सुंदर है (विश्वामित्र- जैसे निःस्पृह, विरक्त और ज्ञानी मुनि से रचना की प्रशंसा सुनकर) राजा प्रसन्न हुए और उन्हें बड़ा सुख मिला ॥
ramacharitamanas::1325.english_translation: Everyone saw Ram with their own eyes turned toward him, yet no one understood any special mystery. The sage spoke to the king and praised the beautiful arrangement, and the king became delighted and felt great joy.
ramacharitamanas::1325.translation_literal: निज निज (each one's own) / रुख (face, direction) / रामहि (toward Ram) / सबु (everyone) / देखा (saw) / कोउ (someone) / न (not) / जान (know) / कछु (anything) / मरमु (secret, mystery) / बिसेषा (special) / भलि (good, beautiful) / रचना (arrangement, construction) / मुनि (sage) / नृप (king) / सन (to, from) / कहेऊ (said) / राजाँ (king) / मुदित (delighted) / महासुख (great joy) / लहेऊ (received)
ramacharitamanas::1325.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1325.essence: Presence can be obvious long before its meaning is understood.
ramacharitamanas::1325.simple_meaning: Everyone looked at Ram, but no one could grasp the deeper mystery. The sage then praised the beautiful arrangement, and the king felt great joy.
ramacharitamanas::1325.simple_insight: Some moments are felt before they are understood.
ramacharitamanas::1325.detailed_meaning: At Janak's wedding arena, everyone turns toward Ram and Lakshman, sensing something extraordinary without fully naming it. Vishwamitra praises the setting to King Janak, and Janak's heart fills with joy before the ceremony moves forward.
ramacharitamanas::1325.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and feel the shift before anyone speaks. Something important is present, but the meaning arrives later, after the first stunned silence.
ramacharitamanas::1325.insight: It teaches you to notice significance before analysis catches up.

ramacharitamanas::1326.verse_sanskrit: सब मंचन्ह तें मंचु एक सुंदर बिसद बिसाल। मुनि समेत दोउ बंधु तहँ बैठारे महिपाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1326.verse_hindi: सब मंचों से एक मंच अधिक सुंदर, उज्ज्वल और विशाल था। (स्वयं) राजा ने मुनि सहित दोनों भाइयों को उस पर बैठाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1326.english_translation: Of all the platforms, one was more beautiful, bright, and vast. The king seated the sage and both brothers upon it.
ramacharitamanas::1326.translation_literal: सब (all) / मंचन्ह तें (from the platforms) / मंचु (platform) / एक (one) / सुंदर (beautiful) / बिसद (bright, clear) / बिसाल (vast) / मुनि (sage) / समेत (together with) / दोउ (both) / बंधु (brothers) / तहँ (there) / बैठारे (seated) / महिपाल (king)
ramacharitamanas::1326.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1326.essence: Honor is shown first in where you seat someone.
ramacharitamanas::1326.simple_meaning: One platform in the wedding hall stood out as the most beautiful and spacious. The king seated the sage and both princes there.
ramacharitamanas::1326.simple_insight: Even a small gesture of honor can reveal deep respect.
ramacharitamanas::1326.detailed_meaning: At Janak's swayamvar, the hall is being arranged for the arrival of Ram and Lakshman. Among all the platforms, one special seat is chosen, and King Janak places the sage and both brothers upon it. The scene quietly prepares the moment of revelation.
ramacharitamanas::1326.modern_relevance: A host notices the quiet elder in the room and chooses the best seat for him, then makes space for the guests beside him. Respect is shown before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1326.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to reverent placement: who is honored, where, and by whose hand.

ramacharitamanas::1327.verse_sanskrit: प्रभुहि देखि सब नृप हियँ हारे। जनु राकेश उदय भएँ तारे॥ असि प्रतीति सब के मन माहीं। राम चाप तोरब सक नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1327.verse_hindi: प्रभु को देखकर सब राजा हृदय में ऐसे हार गए (निराश एवं उत्साहहीन हो गए) जैसे पूर्ण चन्द्रमा के उदय होने पर तारे प्रकाशहीन हो जाते हैं। (उनके तेज को देखकर) सबके मन में ऐसा विश्वास हो गया कि रामचन्द्रजी ही धनुष को तोड़ेंगे, इसमें संदेह नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1327.english_translation: Seeing the Lord, all the kings felt defeated, like stars fading when the full moon rises. Everyone’s mind became certain: Ram alone would break the bow.
ramacharitamanas::1327.translation_literal: प्रभुहि (the Lord) / देखि (having seen) / सब (all) / नृप (kings) / हियँ (in heart) / हारे (were defeated) / जनु (as if) / राकेश (full moon) / उदय भएँ (upon rising) / तारे (stars) / असि (such) / प्रतीति (certainty) / सब के (of all) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / राम चाप (Ram's bow) / तोरब (to break) / सक नाहीं (cannot be able)
ramacharitamanas::1327.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1327.essence: True strength ends rivalry before the first move.
ramacharitamanas::1327.simple_meaning: The kings lose confidence when they see Ram. His presence makes it clear that only he can break the bow.
ramacharitamanas::1327.simple_insight: Some people do not need to announce their strength. Their presence itself ends the doubt.
ramacharitamanas::1327.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, the assembled kings have come to win her hand. Then Ram enters, and their pride collapses before his presence. The comparison to stars and the full moon shows that this is not a contest anymore; the result already feels decided.
ramacharitamanas::1327.modern_relevance: You walk into a room for an interview or a final presentation, and someone else’s calm changes the whole atmosphere. The competition does not always fail by argument; sometimes it fades in the light of clear presence.
ramacharitamanas::1327.insight: It shifts attention from competing loudly to embodying quiet authority.

ramacharitamanas::1328.verse_sanskrit: बिनु भंजेहुँ भव धनुषु बिसाला। मेलिहि सीय राम उर माला॥ अस बिचारि गवनहु घर भाई। जसु प्रतापु बलु तेजु गवाँई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1328.verse_hindi: (इधर उनके रूप को देखकर सबके मन में यह निश्चय हो गया कि) शिवजी के विशाल धनुष को (जो संभव है न टूट सके) बिना तोड़े भी सीताजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी के ही गले में जयमाला डालेंगी (अर्थात दोनों तरह से ही हमारी हार होगी और विजय रामचन्द्रजी के हाथ रहेगी)। (यों सोचकर वे कहने लगे) हे भाई! ऐसा विचारकर यश, प्रताप, बल और तेज गँवाकर अपने-अपने घर चलो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1328.english_translation: Without breaking the great bow of the world, Sita will still place the garland around Ram's neck. Thinking this, go home, brothers, and give up your fame, power, strength, and pride.
ramacharitamanas::1328.translation_literal: बिनु (without) / भंजेहुँ (breaking) / भव (world) / धनुषु (bow) / बिसाला (great, विशाल) / मेलिहि (will place) / सीय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / उर (neck, heart) / माला (garland)॥ / अस (thus) / बिचारि (thinking) / गवनहु (go) / घर (home) / भाई (brothers) / जसु (fame) / प्रतापु (glory) / बलु (strength) / तेजु (splendour) / गवाँई (having lost)
ramacharitamanas::1328.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1328.essence: Some contests end before the first move.
ramacharitamanas::1328.simple_meaning: The kings realise Ram has already won Sita, whether the bow is broken or not. Their pride, power, and reputation are already slipping away.
ramacharitamanas::1328.simple_insight: Pride fades fastest when you can see the outcome is already decided.
ramacharitamanas::1328.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the assembled kings stare at Ram and lose heart. They sense that victory has slipped away before the bow is even touched. The verse captures their private surrender to defeat.
ramacharitamanas::1328.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and instantly know the promotion is not yours. The sharpest move is not to cling harder, but to leave with dignity intact.
ramacharitamanas::1328.insight: It shifts the mind from competitive grasping to graceful withdrawal when the moment is already lost.

ramacharitamanas::1329.verse_sanskrit: बिहसे अपर भूप सुनि बानी। जे अबिबेक अंध अभिमानी॥ तोरेहुँ धनुषु ब्याहु अवगाहा। बिनु तोरें को कुअँरि बिआहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1329.verse_hindi: दूसरे राजा, जो अविवेक से अंधे हो रहे थे और अभिमानी थे, यह बात सुनकर बहुत हँसे। (उन्होंने कहा) धनुष तोड़ने पर भी विवाह होना कठिन है (अर्थात सहज ही में हम जानकी को हाथ से जाने नहीं देंगे), फिर बिना तोड़े तो राजकुमारी को ब्याह ही कौन सकता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1329.english_translation: The other kings, blind with folly and swollen with pride, laughed at this saying. “Even after breaking the bow, the marriage is difficult; without breaking it, who can marry the princess?”
ramacharitamanas::1329.translation_literal: बिहसे (laughed) / अपर भूप (the other kings) / सुनि (hearing) / बानी (the words) / जे (who) / अबिबेक (without discernment) / अंध (blind) / अभिमानी (proud)॥ / तोरेहुँ (even after breaking) / धनुषु (the bow) / ब्याहु (marriage) / अवगाहा (is difficult / hard to accomplish) / बिनु (without) / तोरें (breaking) / को (who) / कुअँरि (princess) / बिआहा (can marry)॥
ramacharitamanas::1329.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1329.essence: Pride laughs at what it cannot yet face.
ramacharitamanas::1329.simple_meaning: The proud kings mock the idea that anyone can win Sita easily. They think even breaking the bow may not be enough to secure the marriage.
ramacharitamanas::1329.simple_insight: Pride laughs first and understands last.
ramacharitamanas::1329.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s court, the assembled kings have already felt Rama’s presence and seen their confidence begin to fail. Now some of them, still blinded by ego, laugh at the idea that the bow test can be won and Sita claimed.
ramacharitamanas::1329.modern_relevance: A room full of experts smirks when one quiet person speaks with confidence. They think they already know the limits. Pride often mistakes its own fear for realism.
ramacharitamanas::1329.insight: It shows how ego dismisses what it cannot match, turning insecurity into mockery.

ramacharitamanas::1330.verse_sanskrit: एक बार कालउ किन होऊ। सिय हित समर जितब हम सोऊ॥ यह सुनि अवर महिप मुसुकाने। धरमसील हरिभगत सयाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1330.verse_hindi: काल ही क्यों न हो, एक बार तो सीता के लिए उसे भी हम युद्ध में जीत लेंगे। यह घमंड की बात सुनकर दूसरे राजा, जो धर्मात्मा, हरिभक्त और सयाने थे, मुस्कुराए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1330.english_translation: Even Time itself, if it must be, we will conquer in battle for Sita. Hearing this, the other kings, who were righteous, devoted to Hari, and wise, smiled.
ramacharitamanas::1330.translation_literal: एक बार (once) / कालउ (even Time) / किन होऊ (if it should be) / सिय हित (for Sita's sake) / समर (battle) / जितब (we will conquer) / हम (we) / सोऊ (that too) ॥ / यह (this) / सुनि (hearing) / अवर (other) / महिप (kings) / मुसुकाने (smiled) / धरमसील (righteous) / हरिभगत (devoted to Hari) / सयाने (wise) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1330.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1330.essence: Boasting about greatness only reveals how little strength remains.
ramacharitamanas::1330.simple_meaning: The proud kings boast that they would even defeat Time itself for Sita, and the wiser kings smile at their arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::1330.simple_insight: Pride sounds loud, but wisdom often answers with a quiet smile.
ramacharitamanas::1330.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, boastful kings are testing the impossible bow and inflating their own power. One of them claims they would even conquer Time for Sita. The righteous and wise kings smile, seeing empty pride before the real challenge begins.
ramacharitamanas::1330.modern_relevance: In a group chat before a high-stakes event, one person starts promising the impossible. The others smile, already knowing bravado is easier than doing the work.
ramacharitamanas::1330.insight: It shifts attention from grand claims to the character of the people making them.

ramacharitamanas::1331.verse_sanskrit: सीय बिआहबि राम गरब दूरि करि नृपन्ह के। जीति को सक संग्राम दसरथ के रन बाँकुरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1331.verse_hindi: (उन्होंने कहा-) राजाओं के गर्व दूर करके (जो धनुष किसी से नहीं टूट सकेगा उसे तोड़कर) श्री रामचन्द्रजी सीताजी को ब्याहेंगे। (रही युद्ध की बात, सो) महाराज दशरथ के रण में बाँके पुत्रों को युद्ध में तो जीत ही कौन सकता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1331.english_translation: They said, "Ram will marry Sita and strip away the kings' pride. Who can defeat the brave sons of Dasharath in battle?"
ramacharitamanas::1331.translation_literal: सीय (Sita) / बिआहबि (will marry) / राम (Ram) / गरब (pride) / दूरि करि (removing) / नृपन्ह के (of the kings) / जीति (defeat) / को (who) / सक (can) / संग्राम (battle) / दसरथ के (of Dasharath) / रन बाँकुरे (brave warriors in war)
ramacharitamanas::1331.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1331.essence: Boasting grows loud when people cannot see their own limits.
ramacharitamanas::1331.simple_meaning: The boastful kings claim Ram will win Sita and no one can defeat Dasharath's brave sons in battle.
ramacharitamanas::1331.simple_insight: Pride speaks loudly before reality answers it.
ramacharitamanas::1331.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the proud kings keep mocking and measuring strength. They dismiss the challenge, saying Ram will win Sita and Dasharath's sons cannot be beaten. The verse is part of their arrogance, not the teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::1331.modern_relevance: A room full of confident people starts talking too soon, each trying to sound strongest. Their certainty says more about their ego than about what will actually happen.
ramacharitamanas::1331.insight: It shows how arrogance turns a sacred contest into a display of ego.

ramacharitamanas::1332.verse_sanskrit: ब्यर्थ मरहु जनि गाल बजाई। मन मोदकन्हि कि भूख बुताई॥ सिख हमारि सुनि परम पुनीता। जगदंबा जानहु जियँ सीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1332.verse_hindi: गाल बजाकर व्यर्थ ही मत मरो। मन के लड्डुओं से भी कहीं भूख बुझती है? हमारी परम पवित्र (निष्कपट) सीख को सुनकर सीताजी को अपने जी में साक्षात जगज्जननी समझो (उन्हें पत्नी रूप में पाने की आशा एवं लालसा छोड़ दो), ॥
ramacharitamanas::1332.english_translation: Do not die boasting in vain. Can hunger be satisfied with sweet dumplings? Hear our pure teaching: know Sita in your heart as the Mother of the world.
ramacharitamanas::1332.translation_literal: ब्यर्थ (in vain) / मरहु (die) / जनि (do not) / गाल (boasting) / बजाई (by beating) / मन (mind) / मोदकन्हि (with sweet dumplings) / कि (does) / भूख (hunger) / बुताई (be quenched) / सिख (teaching) / हमारि (our) / सुनि (hearing) / परम (supremely) / पुनीता (pure) / जगदंबा (Mother of the world) / जानहु (know) / जियँ (in the heart) / सीता (Sita)
ramacharitamanas::1332.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1332.essence: Pride cannot grasp what reverence alone can honour.
ramacharitamanas::1332.simple_meaning: Empty boasting will not win Sita. Desire alone cannot be fed by pretending. The right response is to drop pride and see her as the Mother of the world.
ramacharitamanas::1332.simple_insight: Pride gets quieter when you stop feeding fantasy and face what is real.
ramacharitamanas::1332.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, proud kings have been boasting about winning her. This verse cuts through that arrogance: the contest is not about swagger or craving. Sita is to be honoured as the Mother of the world, not treated as a prize.
ramacharitamanas::1332.modern_relevance: You keep rehearsing what you'll say to impress someone, but the room will not be won by swagger. The moment you drop the performance, you see the person clearly.
ramacharitamanas::1332.insight: It shifts desire away from conquest and toward reverence, making pride impossible to sustain.

ramacharitamanas::1333.verse_sanskrit: जगत पिता रघुपतिहि बिचारी। भरि लोचन छबि लेहु निहारी॥ सुंदर सुखद सकल गुन रासी। ए दोउ बंधु संभु उर बासी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1333.verse_hindi: और श्री रघुनाथजी को जगत का पिता (परमेश्वर) विचार कर, नेत्र भरकर उनकी छबि देख लो (ऐसा अवसर बार-बार नहीं मिलेगा)। सुंदर, सुख देने वाले और समस्त गुणों की राशि ये दोनों भाई शिवजी के हृदय में बसने वाले हैं (स्वयं शिवजी भी जिन्हें सदा हृदय में छिपाए रखते हैं, वे तुम्हारे नेत्रों के सामने आ गए हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1333.english_translation: Consider Raghunath as the father of the world, and fill your eyes with his beauty. Beautiful, bliss-giving, and a treasury of every virtue, these two brothers dwell in Shiva’s heart.
ramacharitamanas::1333.translation_literal: जगत (world) / पिता (father) / रघुपतिहि (Raghupati) / बिचारी (considering) / भरि (filling) / लोचन (eyes) / छबि (beauty) / लेहु (take) / निहारी (seeing) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुखद (giving joy) / सकल (all) / गुन (virtues) / रासी (heap/treasury) / ए (these) / दोउ (two) / बंधु (brothers) / संभु (Shiva) / उर (heart) / बासी (dwelling)
ramacharitamanas::1333.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1333.essence: Beauty becomes devotion when the heart truly sees.
ramacharitamanas::1333.simple_meaning: Look at Ram and Lakshman with full attention. They are beautiful, full of goodness, and beloved even in Shiva’s heart.
ramacharitamanas::1333.simple_insight: A sacred moment is passing; devotion asks you to receive it fully before it slips away.
ramacharitamanas::1333.detailed_meaning: At the Swayamvar, the princesses and onlookers are being urged to stop wasting the moment. Ram and Lakshman stand before them, radiant and calm, and even Shiva is said to keep them in his heart. The verse turns sight itself into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1333.modern_relevance: You meet someone who changes the atmosphere of the room, and you almost look away out of habit. This verse says: stay. See clearly. Some moments are not ordinary, and some people carry a quiet greatness you miss if you rush past.
ramacharitamanas::1333.insight: It shifts attention from casual looking to reverent seeing.

ramacharitamanas::1334.verse_sanskrit: सुधा समुद्र समीप बिहाई। मृगजलु निरखि मरहु कत धाई॥ करहु जाइ जा कहुँ जोइ भावा। हम तौ आजु जनम फलु पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1334.verse_hindi: समीप आए हुए (भगवत् दर्शन रूप) अमृत के समुद्र को छोड़कर तुम (जगज्जननी जानकी को पत्नी रूप में पाने की दुराशा रूप मिथ्या) मृगजल को देखकर दौड़कर क्यों मरते हो? फिर (भाई!) जिसको जो अच्छा लगे, वही जाकर करो। हमने तो (श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन करके) आज जन्म लेने का फल पा लिया (जीवन और जन्म को सफल कर लिया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1334.english_translation: Why run toward a mirage and die, leaving the ocean of nectar nearby? Go and do whatever you please. We have already gained the fruit of life today.
ramacharitamanas::1334.translation_literal: सुधा (nectar) / समुद्र (ocean) / समीप (nearby) / बिहाई (leaving behind) / मृगजलु (mirage-water) / निरखि (seeing) / मरहु (die) / कत (why) / धाई (running) / करहु (do) / जाइ (going) / जा (that which) / कहुँ (to whom) / जोइ (whatever) / भावा (pleases) / हम तौ (we indeed) / आजु (today) / जनम (birth) / फलु (fruit) / पावा (have obtained)
ramacharitamanas::1334.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1334.essence: The real treasure is present; chasing illusion only wastes a life.
ramacharitamanas::1334.simple_meaning: Do not abandon the real blessing that is already present in order to chase an illusion. True fulfillment has already arrived through Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::1334.simple_insight: The ache of wanting eases when you recognize what is already enough.
ramacharitamanas::1334.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar, the gathered kings are dazzled by Sita's beauty and the contest around her. One voice cuts through the crowd: Ram is the ocean of nectar already before you, and chasing lesser desire is like running after a mirage.
ramacharitamanas::1334.modern_relevance: You scroll past the message from someone who truly matters because a shinier option is calling. Later, you realize you ignored the one presence that could have made the whole day complete.
ramacharitamanas::1334.insight: It shifts attention from restless pursuit to recognizing the fulfillment already within reach.

ramacharitamanas::1335.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि भले भूप अनुरागे। रूप अनूप बिलोकन लागे॥ देखहिं सुर नभ चढ़े बिमाना। बरषहिं सुमन करहिं कल गाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1335.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर अच्छे राजा प्रेम मग्न होकर श्री रामजी का अनुपम रूप देखने लगे। (मनुष्यों की तो बात ही क्या) देवता लोग भी आकाश से विमानों पर चढ़े हुए दर्शन कर रहे हैं और सुंदर गान करते हुए फूल बरसा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1335.english_translation: Having said this, the noble king, filled with love, began to behold Rama's incomparable beauty. Even the gods rose in their flying chariots in the sky to watch, showering flowers and singing sweet songs.
ramacharitamanas::1335.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (having said) / भले (noble) / भूप (king) / अनुरागे (filled with love) / रूप (form, beauty) / अनूप (matchless) / बिलोकन (to behold) / लागे (began) ॥ / देखहिं (they see) / सुर (the gods) / नभ (sky) / चढ़े (having ascended) / बिमाना (flying chariots) / बरषहिं (they shower) / सुमन (flowers) / करहिं (they do) / कल (sweet) / गाना (songs) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1335.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1335.essence: True beauty stops the crowd and lifts the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1335.simple_meaning: King Janak, moved by love, gazes at Rama's unmatched beauty. Even the gods come in their heavenly chariots to watch, singing and showering flowers.
ramacharitamanas::1335.simple_insight: Love sharpens the eyes. What is truly sacred draws both human longing and higher attention.
ramacharitamanas::1335.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the king has just praised Rama and turned fully toward him. Overcome with love, he cannot look away. Above the assembly, the gods descend in their chariots, raining flowers and singing, as the wedding scene becomes a celebration beyond earth.
ramacharitamanas::1335.modern_relevance: At a concert, everyone in the room goes quiet when the singer begins the first note. Some moments do that: they pull attention upward, and even the crowd feels reverent.
ramacharitamanas::1335.insight: It shifts attention from the surrounding event to the living presence at its center.

ramacharitamanas::1336.verse_sanskrit: जानि सुअवसरु सीय तब पठई जनक बोलाइ। चतुर सखीं सुंदर सकल सादर चलीं िलवाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1336.verse_hindi: तब सुअवसर जानकर जनकजी ने सीताजी को बुला भेजा। सब चतुर और सुंदर सखियाँ आरदपूर्वक उन्हें लिवा चलीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1336.english_translation: Then, seeing the right moment, Janaka sent for Sita. All the clever, graceful companions went respectfully to bring her.
ramacharitamanas::1336.translation_literal: जानि (knowing) / सुअवसरु (the right moment) / सीय (Sita) / तब (then) / पठई (sent) / जनक (Janaka) / बोलाइ (calling) / चतुर (clever) / सखीं (companions) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सकल (all) / सादर (respectfully) / चलीं (went) / िलवाइ (to bring)
ramacharitamanas::1336.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1336.essence: Right action begins with knowing the moment.
ramacharitamanas::1336.simple_meaning: Janaka chose the proper moment and sent for Sita. Her graceful companions went respectfully to bring her.
ramacharitamanas::1336.simple_insight: Some moments need timing and grace, not force.
ramacharitamanas::1336.detailed_meaning: At Janaka’s court during the Sita-swayamvar, the king sees the moment has arrived. He sends for Sita, and her graceful companions go with respect to bring her forward for the gathering.
ramacharitamanas::1336.modern_relevance: You wait outside the room while everyone prepares the announcement. Then the signal comes, and the people closest to you quietly step in to guide you forward.
ramacharitamanas::1336.insight: It teaches you to recognize the right moment and move with dignity, not haste.

ramacharitamanas::1337.verse_sanskrit: सिय सोभा नहिं जाइ बखानी। जगदंबिका रूप गुन खानी॥ उपमा सकल मोहि लघु लागीं। प्राकृत नारि अंग अनुरागीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1337.verse_hindi: रूप और गुणों की खान जगज्जननी जानकीजी की शोभा का वर्णन नहीं हो सकता। उनके लिए मुझे (काव्य की) सब उपमाएँ तुच्छ लगती हैं, क्योंकि वे लौकिक स्त्रियों के अंगों से अनुराग रखने वाली हैं (अर्थात् वे जगत की स्त्रियों के अंगों को दी जाती हैं)। (काव्य की उपमाएँ सब त्रिगुणात्मक, मायिक जगत से ली गई हैं, उन्हें भगवान की स्वरूपा शक्ति श्री जानकीजी के अप्राकृत, चिन्मय अंगों के लिए प्रयुक्त करना उनका अपमान करना और अपने को उपहासास्पद बनाना है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1337.english_translation: Sita's beauty cannot be described. She is the world-mother, a treasury of form and qualities. All comparisons seem small to me, for they belong to ordinary women of the world.
ramacharitamanas::1337.translation_literal: सिय (Sita) / सोभा (beauty, splendor) / नहिं (not) / जाइ (can go, can be) / बखानी (described) । / जगदंबिका (world-mother) / रूप (form) / गुन (qualities) / खानी (treasury, mine) ॥ / उपमा (comparison) / सकल (all) / मोहि (to me) / लघु (small) / लागीं (seem) । / प्राकृत (ordinary, worldly) / नारि (woman) / अंग (limbs, form) / अनुरागीं (loving, attached to) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1337.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1337.essence: True beauty outgrows every worldly comparison.
ramacharitamanas::1337.simple_meaning: Sita's beauty and qualities cannot be captured by ordinary comparison. Any image drawn from worldly women feels too small for her divine nature.
ramacharitamanas::1337.simple_insight: Some realities are too pure for neat comparison. Reverence begins where language admits its limits.
ramacharitamanas::1337.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the assembled kings have come to see Sita at the swayamvar. Tulsidas pauses the scene to praise her as the world-mother, saying ordinary poetic comparisons fail before her divine radiance. The next verse extends that warning against shallow description.
ramacharitamanas::1337.modern_relevance: You try to explain someone who changed your life, and every sentence feels thin. Some people cannot be reduced to a flattering comparison; they have to be honoured directly.
ramacharitamanas::1337.insight: It shifts the mind from describing holiness as an object to approaching it with humility and restraint.

ramacharitamanas::1338.verse_sanskrit: सिय बरनिअ तेइ उपमा देई। कुकबि कहाइ अजसु को लेई॥ जौं पटतरिअ तीय सम सीया। जग असि जुबति कहाँ कमनीया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1338.verse_hindi: सीताजी के वर्णन में उन्हीं उपमाओं को देकर कौन कुकवि कहलाए और अपयश का भागी बने (अर्थात सीताजी के लिए उन उपमाओं का प्रयोग करना सुकवि के पद से च्युत होना और अपकीर्ति मोल लेना है, कोई भी सुकवि ऐसी नादानी एवं अनुचित कार्य नहीं करेगा।) यदि किसी स्त्री के साथ सीताजी की तुलना की जाए तो जगत में ऐसी सुंदर युवती है ही कहाँ (जिसकी उपमा उन्हें दी जाए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1338.english_translation: Who would be called a bad poet and earn infamy by using those comparisons for Sita? If Sita is compared with any woman, where in the world is there a lovely woman like her?
ramacharitamanas::1338.translation_literal: सिय (Sita) / बरनिअ (to describe) / तेइ (those only) / उपमा (comparisons) / देई (giving) / कुकबि (bad poet) / कहाइ (called) / अजसु (infamy) / को (who) / लेई (takes) ॥ / जौं (if) / पटतरिअ (compared) / तीय (woman) / सम (equal to) / सीया (Sita) / जग (world) / असि (such) / जुबति (young woman) / कहाँ (where) / कमनीया (lovely one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1338.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1338.essence: Sita cannot be measured against ordinary comparisons.
ramacharitamanas::1338.simple_meaning: Sita is beyond ordinary comparison. Any attempt to measure her against other women falls short and feels disrespectful.
ramacharitamanas::1338.simple_insight: Some greatness cannot be flattened into comparison. Reverence begins where ordinary language ends.
ramacharitamanas::1338.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the praise of Sita is rising beyond ordinary poetry. The speaker says that using common comparisons for her would make a poet foolish and bring shame, because no woman in the world can truly match her.
ramacharitamanas::1338.modern_relevance: You try to explain someone you love to a friend, and every comparison feels cheap. Some people are not best understood by ranking them — only by honoring what makes them singular.
ramacharitamanas::1338.insight: It shifts the mind from comparing beauty by scale to recognising uniqueness with reverence.

ramacharitamanas::1339.verse_sanskrit: गिरा मुखर तन अरध भवानी। रति अति दुखित अतनु पति जानी॥ बिष बारुनी बंधु प्रिय जेही। कहिअ रमासम किमि बैदेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1339.verse_hindi: (पृथ्वी की स्त्रियों की तो बात ही क्या, देवताओं की स्त्रियों को भी यदि देखा जाए तो हमारी अपेक्षा कहीं अधिक दिव्य और सुंदर हैं, तो उनमें) सरस्वती तो बहुत बोलने वाली हैं, पार्वती अंर्द्धांगिनी हैं (अर्थात अर्ध-नारीनटेश्वर के रूप में उनका आधा ही अंग स्त्री का है, शेष आधा अंग पुरुष-शिवजी का है), कामदेव की स्त्री रति पति को बिना शरीर का (अनंग) जानकर बहुत दुःखी रहती है और जिनके विष और मद्य-जैसे (समुद्र से उत्पन्न होने के नाते) प्रिय भाई हैं, उन लक्ष्मी के समान तो जानकीजी को कहा ही कैसे जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1339.english_translation: How can Janaki be compared to Rama's Lakshmi? Saraswati is talkative, Parvati is only half-woman, Rati grieves over her bodiless husband, and Lakshmi has brothers born of poison and wine.
ramacharitamanas::1339.translation_literal: गिरा (speech/Saraswati) / मुखर (very talkative) / तन (body) / अरध (half) / भवानी (Parvati) / रति (Rati) / अति (very) / दुखित (grieved) / अतनु (bodiless) / पति (husband) / जानी (having known) / बिष (poison) / बारुनी (wine) / बंधु (brothers) / प्रिय (dear) / जेही (whose) / कहिअ (how can one say) / रमासम (equal to Lakshmi) / किमि (how) / बैदेही (Janaki)
ramacharitamanas::1339.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1339.essence: Janaki exceeds every measure, even the highest ones.
ramacharitamanas::1339.simple_meaning: No comparison fits Janaki. Even famous celestial women fall short in different ways, so Lakshmi herself cannot measure her.
ramacharitamanas::1339.simple_insight: Some beauty is beyond comparison. The mind has to stop ranking and simply bow.
ramacharitamanas::1339.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar section, Tulsidas has already said ordinary comparisons fail. He now pushes further: even the most celebrated women of the higher worlds cannot match Janaki. The verse deepens the praise by showing that every standard is too small.
ramacharitamanas::1339.modern_relevance: You try to explain someone you love to a friend, then realise every comparison cheapens them. Some presence is not meant to be measured against a list.
ramacharitamanas::1339.insight: It shifts the mind from comparison to reverence, teaching that some excellence must be acknowledged without ranking.

ramacharitamanas::1340.verse_sanskrit: जौं छबि सुधा पयोनिधि होई। परम रूपमय कच्छपु सोई॥ सोभा रजु मंदरु सिंगारू। मथै पानि पंकज निज मारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1340.verse_hindi: (जिन लक्ष्मीजी की बात ऊपर कही गई है, वे निकली थीं खारे समुद्र से, जिसको मथने के लिए भगवान ने अति कर्कश पीठ वाले कच्छप का रूप धारण किया, रस्सी बनाई गई महान विषधर वासुकि नाग की, मथानी का कार्य किया अतिशय कठोर मंदराचल पर्वत ने और उसे मथा सारे देवताओं और दैत्यों ने मिलकर। जिन लक्ष्मी को अतिशय शोभा की खान और अनुपम सुंदरी कहते हैं, उनको प्रकट करने में हेतु बने ये सब असुंदर एवं स्वाभाविक ही कठोर उपकरण। ऐसे उपकरणों से प्रकट हुई लक्ष्मी श्री जानकीजी की समता को कैसे पा सकती हैं। हाँ, (इसके विपरीत) यदि छबि रूपी अमृत का समुद्र हो, परम रूपमय कच्छप हो, शोभा रूप रस्सी हो, श्रृंगार (रस) पर्वत हो और (उस छबि के समुद्र को) स्वयं कामदेव अपने ही करकमल से मथे, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1340.english_translation: If beauty were the ocean of nectar, the tortoise its perfect form, splendor the rope, Mount Mandara ornament, and Cupid himself the churning hand, even then such beauty could not match Sita.
ramacharitamanas::1340.translation_literal: जौं (if) / छबि (beauty) / सुधा (nectar) / पयोनिधि (ocean) / होई (were) / परम (supreme) / रूपमय (full of form) / कच्छपु (tortoise) / सोई (that) / सोभा (splendor) / रजु (rope) / मंदरु (Mandara) / सिंगारू (ornament) / मथै (churns) / पानि (hand) / पंकज (lotus) / निज (own) / मारू (Cupid)
ramacharitamanas::1340.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1340.essence: Even the highest beauty remains inadequate before Sita.
ramacharitamanas::1340.simple_meaning: Even the most beautiful imaginable scene would still fall short of Sita’s beauty. Tulsidas uses the churning of the ocean as a comparison and then says the comparison itself is not enough.
ramacharitamanas::1340.simple_insight: Some things are so radiant that ordinary language breaks down before them.
ramacharitamanas::1340.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is still praising Sita in the Swayamvar section of Balkand. After rejecting ordinary comparisons, he imagines the ocean of beauty itself being churned by the most perfect, elegant, and divine elements — yet even that would not equal Sita.
ramacharitamanas::1340.modern_relevance: You try to describe someone who changed the room the moment they entered, and every comparison feels clumsy. The feeling is simple: some presence cannot be reduced to metaphor.
ramacharitamanas::1340.insight: It trains the mind to stop measuring sacred beauty by ordinary standards and instead meet it with reverence.

ramacharitamanas::1341.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि उपजै लच्छि जब सुंदरता सुख मूल। तदपि सकोच समेत कबि कहहिं सीय समतूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1341.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार (का संयोग होने से) जब सुंदरता और सुख की मूल लक्ष्मी उत्पन्न हो, तो भी कवि लोग उसे (बहुत) संकोच के साथ सीताजी के समान कहेंगे ॥ (जिस सुंदरता के समुद्र को कामदेव मथेगा वह सुंदरता भी प्राकृत, लौकिक सुंदरता ही होगी, क्योंकि कामदेव स्वयं भी त्रिगुणमयी प्रकृति का ही विकार है। अतः उस सुंदरता को मथकर प्रकट की हुई लक्ष्मी भी उपर्युक्त लक्ष्मी की अपेक्षा कहीं अधिक सुंदर और दिव्य होने पर भी होगी प्राकृत ही, अतः उसके साथ भी जानकीजी की तुलना करना कवि के लिए बड़े संकोच की बात होगी। जिस सुंदरता से जानकीजी का दिव्यातिदिव्य परम दिव्य विग्रह बना है, वह सुंदरता उपर्युक्त सुंदरता से भिन्न अप्राकृत है- वस्तुतः लक्ष्मीजी का अप्राकृत रूप भी यही है। वह कामदेव के मथने में नहीं आ सकती और वह जानकीजी का स्वरूप ही है, अतः उनसे भिन्न नहीं और उपमा दी जाती है भिन्न वस्तु के साथ। इसके अतिरिक्त जानकीजी प्रकट हुई हैं स्वयं अपनी महिमा से, उन्हें प्रकट करने के लिए किसी भिन्न उपकरण की अपेक्षा नहीं है। अर्थात शक्ति शक्तिमान से अभिन्न, अद्वैत तत्व है, अतएव अनुपमेय है, यही गूढ़ दार्शनिक तत्व भक्त शिरोमणि कवि ने इस अभूतोपमालंकार के द्वारा बड़ी सुंदरता से व्यक्त किया है।)
ramacharitamanas::1341.english_translation: In this way, when beauty arises as the source of delight, even then poets speak of it as equal to Sita, with great hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::1341.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / उपजै (arises) / लच्छि (Lakshmi) / जब (when) / सुंदरता (beauty) / सुख मूल (source of delight) / तदपि (even then) / सकोच समेत (with hesitation) / कबि (poets) / कहहिं (say) / सीय (Sita) / समतूल (equal)
ramacharitamanas::1341.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1341.essence: Sita is so radiant that comparison itself becomes reverent hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::1341.simple_meaning: Even the highest beauty can only be compared to Sita with hesitation. Her form is beyond ordinary standards and cannot be measured by them.
ramacharitamanas::1341.simple_insight: Some things are so complete that comparison itself feels clumsy.
ramacharitamanas::1341.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, the poet has just described an ideal, radiant beauty and then pulls back. Even if a new form of Lakshmi were born from that beauty, the poet says, it would still be awkward to compare it with Sita. Her radiance belongs to a higher order.
ramacharitamanas::1341.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence makes every flattering description sound cheap. You start a sentence with praise, then stop, because the person is already beyond the language you brought.
ramacharitamanas::1341.insight: It shifts the mind from measuring holiness or beauty by standards to recognising what cannot be reduced to comparison.

ramacharitamanas::1342.verse_sanskrit: चलीं संग लै सखीं सयानी। गावत गीत मनोहर बानी॥ सोह नवल तनु सुंदर सारी। जगत जननि अतुलित छबि भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1342.verse_hindi: सयानी सखियाँ सीताजी को साथ लेकर मनोहर वाणी से गीत गाती हुई चलीं। सीताजी के नवल शरीर पर सुंदर साड़ी सुशोभित है। जगज्जननी की महान छबि अतुलनीय है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1342.english_translation: The wise companions walked along with her, singing in sweet voices. Sita's fresh form was adorned with a beautiful sari; the mother of the world shone with unmatched splendor.
ramacharitamanas::1342.translation_literal: चलीं (walked) / संग (together) / लै (taking) / सखीं (companions) / सयानी (wise) / गावत (singing) / गीत (songs) / मनोहर (lovely) / बानी (speech) / सोह (shone) / नवल (fresh) / तनु (body) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सारी (sari) / जगत जननि (mother of the world) / अतुलित (matchless) / छबि (beauty) / भारी (great)
ramacharitamanas::1342.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1342.essence: Sita's presence turns a simple procession into something unforgettable.
ramacharitamanas::1342.simple_meaning: Wise companions escort Sita while singing. She is dressed beautifully, and her unmatched radiance fills the scene.
ramacharitamanas::1342.simple_insight: Beauty here is not decoration alone; it feels like a presence that changes the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::1342.detailed_meaning: Sita is being led forward by her elder companions in the wedding procession. They sing as they walk, and Tulsidas pauses to linger on her youthful form, sari, and unmatched radiance before the swayamvar scene unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::1342.modern_relevance: A bride steps out of the dressing room, and everyone falls quiet for a second. The room changes before she even speaks.
ramacharitamanas::1342.insight: It shifts attention from movement to presence, showing how grace can transform an entire gathering.

ramacharitamanas::1343.verse_sanskrit: भूषन सकल सुदेस सुहाए। अंग अंग रचि सखिन्ह बनाए॥ रंगभूमि जब सिय पगु धारी। देखि रूप मोहे नर नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1343.verse_hindi: सब आभूषण अपनी-अपनी जगह पर शोभित हैं, जिन्हें सखियों ने अंग-अंग में भलीभाँति सजाकर पहनाया है। जब सीताजी ने रंगभूमि में पैर रखा, तब उनका (दिव्य) रूप देखकर स्त्री, पुरुष सभी मोहित हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1343.english_translation: All ornaments shone in their proper places, arranged beautifully on each limb by the companions. When Sita stepped into the arena, men and women alike were enchanted by her form.
ramacharitamanas::1343.translation_literal: भूषन (ornaments) / सकल (all) / सुदेस (proper places) / सुहाए (looked beautiful) / अंग अंग (each limb) / रचि (arranged) / सखिन्ह (by the companions) / बनाए (made) / रंगभूमि (arena) / जब (when) / सिय (Sita) / पगु (foot) / धारी (placed) / देखि (seeing) / रूप (form/beauty) / मोहे (were enchanted) / नर नारी (men and women)
ramacharitamanas::1343.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1343.essence: Her arrival alone silences the crowd.
ramacharitamanas::1343.simple_meaning: Sita is beautifully adorned by her companions, and when she enters the arena, everyone is captivated by her beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1343.simple_insight: Some presences need no introduction; they change the mood of a whole room the moment they arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1343.detailed_meaning: Sita, dressed and adorned by her companions, steps into the marriage arena. The sight of her beauty is so overwhelming that men and women alike are spellbound. This verse simply carries the moment of arrival before the garland contest begins.
ramacharitamanas::1343.modern_relevance: A bride walks into the hall and every conversation stops for a second. No announcement is needed; the room itself knows something important has arrived.
ramacharitamanas::1343.insight: It turns attention from the event to the power of presence, showing how beauty can command an entire gathering.

ramacharitamanas::1344.verse_sanskrit: हरषि सुरन्ह दुंदुभीं बजाईं। बरषि प्रसून अपछरा गाईं॥ पानि सरोज सोह जयमाला। अवचट चितए सकल भुआला ॥
ramacharitamanas::1344.verse_hindi: देवताओं ने हर्षित होकर नगाड़े बजाए और पुष्प बरसाकर अप्सराएँ गाने लगीं। सीताजी के करकमलों में जयमाला सुशोभित है। सब राजा चकित होकर अचानक उनकी ओर देखने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1344.english_translation: The gods beat drums in joy, and the celestial nymphs sang while showering flowers. The garland of victory shone in Sita's lotus hands. All the kings turned to look in sudden wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1344.translation_literal: हरषि (rejoicing) / सुरन्ह (the gods) / दुंदुभीं (drums) / बजाईं (beat) / बरषि (showering) / प्रसून (flowers) / अपछरा (celestial nymphs) / गाईं (sang) / पानि (hands) / सरोज (lotus) / सोह (shone) / जयमाला (victory garland) / अवचट (suddenly) / चितए (looked) / सकल (all) / भुआला (kings)
ramacharitamanas::1344.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1344.essence: A rightful choice makes the whole world pause.
ramacharitamanas::1344.simple_meaning: The heavens celebrate as Sita receives the victory garland, and every king turns to stare in amazement.
ramacharitamanas::1344.simple_insight: Some moments are so complete that even the world seems to applaud them.
ramacharitamanas::1344.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Sita has just chosen Ram. The heavens respond with drums, flowers, and song, while the kings stand stunned. This verse paints the instant before their attention shifts fully to Ram and Sita together.
ramacharitamanas::1344.modern_relevance: You watch a room go quiet after someone makes a choice everyone felt but no one expected. The air changes before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::1344.insight: It turns a wedding scene into a cosmic affirmation, showing that true choice can command universal attention.

ramacharitamanas::1345.verse_sanskrit: सीय चकित चित रामहि चाहा। भए मोहबस सब नरनाहा॥ मुनि समीप देखे दोउ भाई। लगे ललकि लोचन निधि पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1345.verse_hindi: सीताजी चकित चित्त से श्री रामजी को देखने लगीं, तब सब राजा लोग मोह के वश हो गए। सीताजी ने मुनि के पास (बैठे हुए) दोनों भाइयों को देखा तो उनके नेत्र अपना खजाना पाकर ललचाकर वहीं (श्री रामजी में) जा लगे (स्थिर हो गए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1345.english_translation: Sita, startled, longed to look at Ram. All the kings fell under illusion. Seeing the two brothers near the sage, her eyes clung to the treasure they had found.
ramacharitamanas::1345.translation_literal: सीय (Sita) / चकित (startled) / चित (mind) / रामहि (to Ram) / चाहा (wanted to see) / भए (became) / मोहबस (under the power of illusion) / सब (all) / नरनाहा (kings) / मुनि (sage) / समीप (near) / देखे (saw) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / लगे (became attached) / ललकि (longing greedily) / लोचन (eyes) / निधि (treasure) / पाई (having found)
ramacharitamanas::1345.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1345.essence: The heart knows its treasure before the mind can explain it.
ramacharitamanas::1345.simple_meaning: Sita is drawn to Ram at first sight, while the assembled kings lose their composure. Seeing the two brothers near the sage, her eyes fix on them with sudden longing.
ramacharitamanas::1345.simple_insight: True beauty pulls the heart without effort; the rest of the crowd fades into the background.
ramacharitamanas::1345.detailed_meaning: At the Sita-swayamvar, the hall is full of kings and spectacle. Sita sees Ram and Lakshman near the sage and is instantly captivated, while the other kings fall into confusion. The moment shows how the right heart recognizes its treasure at once.
ramacharitamanas::1345.modern_relevance: You walk into a crowded room and everything blurs except one face. The mind does not choose that recognition; it happens before thought can interfere.
ramacharitamanas::1345.insight: It shifts attention from social noise to the immediate pull of what truly matters.

ramacharitamanas::1346.verse_sanskrit: गुरजन लाज समाजु बड़ देखि सीय सकुचानि। लागि बिलोकन सखिन्ह तन रघुबीरहि उर आनि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1346.verse_hindi: परन्तु गुरुजनों की लाज से तथा बहुत बड़े समाज को देखकर सीताजी सकुचा गईं। वे श्री रामचन्द्रजी को हृदय में लाकर सखियों की ओर देखने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1346.english_translation: But seeing the elders and the large gathering, Sita became shy. She brought Ram into her heart and looked toward her companions.
ramacharitamanas::1346.translation_literal: गुरजन (elders) / लाज (shame, modesty) / समाजु (gathering) / बड़ (great, large) / देखि (seeing) / सीय (Sita) / सकुचानि (became shy) / लागि (applied, turned) / बिलोकन (to look) / सखिन्ह (to the companions) / तन (body) / रघुबीरहि (Ram) / उर (heart) / आनि (bringing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1346.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1346.essence: Love can be inwardly certain and outwardly restrained.
ramacharitamanas::1346.simple_meaning: Sita feels shy in front of the elders and the large crowd. She turns her attention to Ram in her heart and glances toward her friends instead.
ramacharitamanas::1346.simple_insight: Even deep love can become quiet and modest in public.
ramacharitamanas::1346.detailed_meaning: At the swayamvar, the hall is full and every eye is fixed on Sita. She has chosen Ram inwardly, but the presence of elders and the crowd makes her lower her gaze and turn to her companions. The verse shows her graceful restraint in a charged moment.
ramacharitamanas::1346.modern_relevance: You know the feeling of wanting to meet someone's eyes, then suddenly becoming aware of everyone watching. The heart moves first, but dignity still shapes the moment.
ramacharitamanas::1346.insight: It shows how devotion can remain inward while outward conduct stays modest and composed.

ramacharitamanas::1347.verse_sanskrit: राम रूपु अरु सिय छबि देखें। नर नारिन्ह परिहरीं निमेषें॥ सोचहिं सकल कहत सकुचाहीं। बिधि सन बिनय करहिं मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1347.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का रूप और सीताजी की छबि देखकर स्त्री-पुरुषों ने पलक मारना छोड़ दिया (सब एकटक उन्हीं को देखने लगे)। सभी अपने मन में सोचते हैं, पर कहते सकुचाते हैं। मन ही मन वे विधाता से विनय करते हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1347.english_translation: Seeing the beauty of Ram's form and Sita's radiance, men and women forgot to blink. Everyone thought silently, spoke with hesitation, and prayed inwardly to fate.
ramacharitamanas::1347.translation_literal: राम रूपु (Ram's form) / अरु (and) / सिय छबि (Sita's radiance) / देखें (having seen) / नर (men) / नारिन्ह (women) / परिहरीं (gave up) / निमेषें (blinking)॥ / सोचहिं (they think) / सकल (all) / कहत (speaking) / सकुचाहीं (feel shy) / बिधि (fate) / सन (to) / बिनय (prayer) / करहिं (they do) / मन माहीं (in the mind)॥
ramacharitamanas::1347.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1347.essence: Beauty can still a crowd before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1347.simple_meaning: Everyone is so struck by Ram and Sita's beauty that they stare without blinking. They think their feelings privately, but stay too shy to speak them aloud.
ramacharitamanas::1347.simple_insight: Some moments are so luminous they leave people silent, inwardly overwhelmed, and unable to act like themselves.
ramacharitamanas::1347.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the assembly has gathered to witness the swayamvar. Ram and Sita's beauty stops the crowd in its tracks. Men and women stare without blinking, each person inwardly moved but too awed to speak.
ramacharitamanas::1347.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the whole conversation dies for a second. Everyone notices something beautiful, but no one knows how to say it out loud.
ramacharitamanas::1347.insight: It captures how awe can silence speech and turn attention inward before action begins.

ramacharitamanas::1348.verse_sanskrit: हरु बिधि बेगि जनक जड़ताई। मति हमारि असि देहि सुहाई॥ बिनु बिचार पनु तजि नरनाहू। सीय राम कर करै बिबाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1348.verse_hindi: हे विधाता! जनक की मूढ़ता को शीघ्र हर लीजिए और हमारी ही ऐसी सुंदर बुद्धि उन्हें दीजिए कि जिससे बिना ही विचार किए राजा अपना प्रण छोड़कर सीताजी का विवाह रामजी से कर दें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1348.english_translation: O Creator, quickly remove Janak's stubbornness and give him our own pleasing wisdom, so that without further thought the king may break his vow and give Sita in marriage to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1348.translation_literal: हरु (remove) / बिधि (O Creator) / बेगि (quickly) / जनक (Janak's) / जड़ताई (stubbornness, dullness) / मति (wisdom) / हमारि (our) / असि (such) / देहि (give) / सुहाई (pleasing) / बिनु (without) / बिचार (thought) / पनु (vow) / तजि (giving up) / नरनाहू (king) / सीय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / कर (of) / करै (may do) / बिबाहू (marriage)
ramacharitamanas::1348.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1348.essence: Hesitation must give way when dharma is already visible.
ramacharitamanas::1348.simple_meaning: The speakers pray that King Janak will abandon hesitation and fulfill the vow by marrying Sita to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1348.simple_insight: Sometimes the right act is already clear; the only obstacle is delay.
ramacharitamanas::1348.detailed_meaning: At Janak's swayamvar, everyone has seen Ram and Sita and feels the moment has come. The crowd waits in breathless hope, and this verse captures the prayer that Janak will stop hesitating and complete the marriage.
ramacharitamanas::1348.modern_relevance: You know the answer in the meeting, but the room keeps circling the same hesitation. Sometimes the kindest thing is to stop overthinking and let the right decision happen.
ramacharitamanas::1348.insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to decisive fulfillment of what has already become clear.

ramacharitamanas::1349.verse_sanskrit: जगु भल कहिहि भाव सब काहू। हठ कीन्हें अंतहुँ उर दाहू॥ एहिं लालसाँ मगन सब लोगू। बरु साँवरो जानकी जोगू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1349.verse_hindi: संसार उन्हें भला कहेगा, क्योंकि यह बात सब किसी को अच्छी लगती है। हठ करने से अंत में भी हृदय जलेगा। सब लोग इसी लालसा में मग्न हो रहे हैं कि जानकीजी के योग्य वर तो यह साँवला ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1349.english_translation: The world will call this good, because everyone likes it. Stubbornness will end in a burning heart. Everyone is absorbed in this longing: the dark one alone is fit for Janaki.
ramacharitamanas::1349.translation_literal: जगु (the world) / भल (good) / कहिहि (will say) / भाव (pleasing) / सब (all) / काहू (to everyone) / हठ (stubbornness) / कीन्हें (by doing) / अंतहुँ (in the end also) / उर (heart) / दाहू (burning) ॥ एहिं (in this) / लालसाँ (longing) / मगन (absorbed) / सब (all) / लोगू (people) / बरु (better) / साँवरो (the dark one) / जानकी (Janaki) / जोगू (fit, worthy) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1349.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1349.essence: Forcing the wrong choice leaves only inner fire.
ramacharitamanas::1349.simple_meaning: People will praise what seems pleasing, but stubbornness still burns the heart. Here, everyone is caught in the longing that only the dark one is worthy of Janaki.
ramacharitamanas::1349.simple_insight: Public approval does not end inner conflict. Only a choice aligned with what is truly fitting brings peace.
ramacharitamanas::1349.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the crowd is already leaning toward Ram as Sita's worthy match. The verse pauses the scene to show how collective desire and inner resistance clash: pleasing appearances may win praise, but stubbornness only leaves the heart scorched.
ramacharitamanas::1349.modern_relevance: You keep arguing for your preference in a family decision, but everyone already feels the fit. The longer you force it, the more you burn yourself out.
ramacharitamanas::1349.insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to personal insistence toward recognizing what is naturally right.

ramacharitamanas::1350.verse_sanskrit: तब बंदीजन जनक बोलाए। बिरिदावली कहत चलि आए॥ कह नृपु जाइ कहहु पन मोरा। चले भाट हियँ हरषु न थोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1350.verse_hindi: तब राजा जनक ने वंदीजनों (भाटों) को बुलाया। वे विरुदावली (वंश की कीर्ति) गाते हुए चले आए। राजा ने कहा- जाकर मेरा प्रण सबसे कहो। भाट चले, उनके हृदय में कम आनंद न था ॥
ramacharitamanas::1350.english_translation: Then King Janak called the bards. They came singing praises of the royal line. The king said, "Go and tell my vow." The bards departed, no less joyful in their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1350.translation_literal: तब (then) / बंदीजन (bards) / जनक (Janak) / बोलाए (called) / बिरिदावली (praise of lineage) / कहत (saying) / चलि आए (came walking)॥ / कह (say) / नृपु (king) / जाइ (going) / कहहु (tell) / पन (vow) / मोरा (my) / चले (went) / भाट (bards) / हियँ (in heart) / हरषु (joy) / न (not) / थोरा (little)
ramacharitamanas::1350.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1350.essence: A vow travels farther when the messenger's heart is glad.
ramacharitamanas::1350.simple_meaning: Janak calls the court bards and sends them out to announce his vow. They leave happily, carrying his message to everyone.
ramacharitamanas::1350.simple_insight: A public vow becomes a living message when it is carried with joy, not pressure.
ramacharitamanas::1350.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court in Mithila, the bards are summoned after the king's vow about Sita's marriage is set in motion. They sing the family's glory, then go out to announce Janak's resolve, carrying not duty alone but real delight.
ramacharitamanas::1350.modern_relevance: A founder gathers the team after making a hard announcement and asks them to spread it clearly. The message lands because they believe in it, not because they were forced.
ramacharitamanas::1350.insight: It shows how a noble message moves through people best when they carry it with inner gladness.

ramacharitamanas::1351.verse_sanskrit: बोले बंदी बचन बर सुनहु सकल महिपाल। पन बिदेह कर कहहिं हम भुजा उठाइ बिसाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1351.verse_hindi: भाटों ने श्रेष्ठ वचन कहा- हे पृथ्वी की पालना करने वाले सब राजागण! सुनिए। हम अपनी भुजा उठाकर जनकजी का विशाल प्रण कहते हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1351.english_translation: The heralds said, “Listen, all noble kings. We proclaim King Janaka’s great vow with raised arms.”
ramacharitamanas::1351.translation_literal: बोले (spoke) / बंदी (heralds) / बचन (words) / बर (excellent) / सुनहु (listen) / सकल (all) / महिपाल (kings) / पन (vow) / बिदेह (of Videha, Janaka) / कर (hand) / कहहिं (say) / हम (we) / भुजा (arm) / उठाइ (raising) / बिसाल (great)
ramacharitamanas::1351.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1351.essence: A royal vow is being formally declared before the contest begins.
ramacharitamanas::1351.simple_meaning: The royal heralds announce Janaka’s vow to the gathered kings and invite everyone to listen.
ramacharitamanas::1351.simple_insight: Some moments are only the announcement before the real test begins.
ramacharitamanas::1351.detailed_meaning: At Janaka’s court, the heralds step forward before the assembled kings and begin reciting the king’s vow. Their announcement prepares the whole gathering for the challenge of Shiva’s bow, but this verse itself is only the formal introduction.
ramacharitamanas::1351.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet before an announcement that changes everything. The tension is not in the words alone, but in what everyone knows is coming next.
ramacharitamanas::1351.insight: It frames the scene as a public challenge, not a private thought.

ramacharitamanas::1352.verse_sanskrit: नृप भुजबल बिधु सिवधनु राहू। गरुअ कठोर बिदित सब काहू॥ रावनु बानु महाभट भारे। देखि सरासन गवँहिं सिधारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1352.verse_hindi: राजाओं की भुजाओं का बल चन्द्रमा है, शिवजी का धनुष राहु है, वह भारी है, कठोर है, यह सबको विदित है। बड़े भारी योद्धा रावण और बाणासुर भी इस धनुष को देखकर गौं से (चुपके से) चलते बने (उसे उठाना तो दूर रहा, छूने तक की हिम्मत न हुई) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1352.english_translation: The bow of Shiva is as hard and terrible as Rahu to the moon of kings' arm-strength. It is heavy, rigid, and known by all. Even the great warriors Ravana and Banasura turned away on seeing that bow and its bowstring.
ramacharitamanas::1352.translation_literal: नृप (kings) / भुजबल (arm-strength) / बिधु (moon) / सिवधनु (Shiva's bow) / राहू (Rahu) / गरुअ (heavy) / कठोर (hard) / बिदित (known) / सब (all) / काहू (to anyone) / रावनु (Ravana) / बानु (Bana) / महाभट (great warriors) / भारे (mighty) / देखि (seeing) / सरासन (bow and string) / गवँहिं (turned away) / सिधारे (went away)
ramacharitamanas::1352.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1352.essence: Even the proud turn back before a challenge beyond their strength.
ramacharitamanas::1352.simple_meaning: Shiva's bow is so heavy and hard that even famous warriors like Ravana and Banasura backed away from it.
ramacharitamanas::1352.simple_insight: Some challenges are so great that pride alone cannot face them.
ramacharitamanas::1352.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the kings' strength is being compared and tested before Sita's swayamvar. The bow of Shiva stands like an impossible challenge. Even Ravana and Banasura, famous for power, lose confidence at the sight of it.
ramacharitamanas::1352.modern_relevance: You open the box in the gym and see a weight you cannot even imagine lifting. A room full of strong people goes quiet. The first test is not strength — it is whether ego can stay in the room.
ramacharitamanas::1352.insight: It frames the bow as a threshold that exposes limits before the real contest begins.

ramacharitamanas::1353.verse_sanskrit: सोइ पुरारि कोदंडु कठोरा। राज समाज आजु जोइ तोरा॥ त्रिभुवन जय समेत बैदेही। बिनहिं बिचार बरइ हठि तेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1353.verse_hindi: उसी शिवजी के कठोर धनुष को आज इस राज समाज में जो भी तोड़ेगा, तीनों लोकों की विजय के साथ ही उसको जानकीजी बिना किसी विचार के हठपूर्वक वरण करेंगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1353.english_translation: Whoever breaks Lord Shiva's hard bow in this royal assembly today, Sita will choose him without hesitation, along with victory over the three worlds.
ramacharitamanas::1353.translation_literal: सोइ (that same) / पुरारि (of Shiva, enemy of the cities) / कोदंडु (bow) / कठोरा (hard, कठor) । / राज समाज (royal assembly) / आजु (today) / जोइ (whoever) / तोरा (breaks) ॥ / त्रिभुवन (three worlds) / जय (victory) / समेत (along with) / बैदेही (Sita) । / बिनहिं (without) / बिचार (thought, consideration) / बरइ (chooses) / हठि (firmly, insistently) / तेही (that one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1353.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1353.essence: Only the one who breaks the impossible test wins the bride.
ramacharitamanas::1353.simple_meaning: Shiva's bow is so hard that only the one who breaks it will win Sita's hand and gain great honor.
ramacharitamanas::1353.simple_insight: Real worth is proven by action, not by boasting.
ramacharitamanas::1353.detailed_meaning: In Janak's royal court, the bow of Shiva stands as the test for Sita's swayamvar. The earlier challenge has been announced; now this verse sharpens the promise: the man who can break it will win Sita and the world's acclaim.
ramacharitamanas::1353.modern_relevance: A room full of confident people goes quiet when the real test appears. The prize goes not to the loudest voice, but to the one who can actually do the hard thing.
ramacharitamanas::1353.insight: It shifts attention from pride and talk to proven capacity under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::1354.verse_sanskrit: सुनि पन सकल भूप अभिलाषे। भटमानी अतिसय मन माखे॥ परिकर बाँधि उठे अकुलाई। चले इष्ट देवन्ह सिर नाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1354.verse_hindi: प्रण सुनकर सब राजा ललचा उठे। जो वीरता के अभिमानी थे, वे मन में बहुत ही तमतमाए। कमर कसकर अकुलाकर उठे और अपने इष्टदेवों को सिर नवाकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1354.english_translation: Hearing the challenge, all the kings longed to try. The proud warriors grew furious in their hearts. They tightened their belts, rose in agitation, and went forward bowing to their chosen deities.
ramacharitamanas::1354.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / पन (pledge, challenge) / सकल (all) / भूप (kings) / अभिलाषे (desired, longed) / भटमानी (warrior-proud) / अतिसय (greatly) / मन (mind) / माखे (grew heated, enraged) / परिकर (waistband, belt) / बाँधि (tying) / उठे (rose) / अकुलाई (in agitation) / चले (went) / इष्ट (chosen) / देवन्ह (deities) / सिर (head) / नाई (bowing)
ramacharitamanas::1354.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1354.essence: Pride leaps up first, and reason is already behind it.
ramacharitamanas::1354.simple_meaning: The kings hear the challenge and become eager to prove themselves. Their pride flares up, so they rise, bow to their chosen deities, and move toward the contest.
ramacharitamanas::1354.simple_insight: Pride rushes in before wisdom can speak.
ramacharitamanas::1354.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the challenge to lift Shiva's bow has stirred the court. The kings, swollen with martial pride, cannot stay seated. They rise in haste, salute their chosen deities, and prepare to test themselves, setting up the next failure.
ramacharitamanas::1354.modern_relevance: You see the group chat light up with a dare, and suddenly everyone wants to prove something. The body moves before the mind asks why.
ramacharitamanas::1354.insight: It shows how ego turns a sacred test into a contest for status.

ramacharitamanas::1355.verse_sanskrit: तमकि ताकि तकि सिवधनु धरहीं। उठइ न कोटि भाँति बलु करहीं॥ जिन्ह के कछु बिचारु मन माहीं। चाप समीप महीप न जाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1355.verse_hindi: वे तमककर (बड़े ताव से) शिवजी के धनुष की ओर देखते हैं और फिर निगाह जमाकर उसे पकड़ते हैं, करोड़ों भाँति से जोर लगाते हैं, पर वह उठता ही नहीं। जिन राजाओं के मन में कुछ विवेक है, वे तो धनुष के पास ही नहीं जाते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1355.english_translation: They glare at Shiva's bow, grab it, and strain in countless ways, but it will not rise. Kings with any sense do not even approach the bow.
ramacharitamanas::1355.translation_literal: तमकि (glaring) / ताकि (looking) / तकि (staring) / सिवधनु (Shiva's bow) / धरहीं (they grasp) / उठइ (it rises) / न (not) / कोटि भाँति (in countless ways) / बलु (strength) / करहीं (they do) / जिन्ह के (whose) / कछु (some) / बिचारु (discernment) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / चाप (bow) / समीप (near) / महीप (kings) / न जाहीं (do not go)
ramacharitamanas::1355.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1355.simple_meaning: The proud kings try again and again to lift Shiva's bow, but it does not move. Only the thoughtful kings keep away from it.
ramacharitamanas::1355.simple_insight: Pride pushes people into impossible tests; clear judgment knows when not to force what cannot be forced.
ramacharitamanas::1355.detailed_meaning: At Janak's assembly, the kings have already heard the challenge to win Sita by lifting Shiva's bow. Some rush forward in pride and strain with all their strength, but the bow stays unmoved. Others, wiser in that moment, do not even step closer.
ramacharitamanas::1355.modern_relevance: You walk into a room determined to prove yourself, then realize the task is not for display. The wise choice is not to force the moment just to protect your ego.
ramacharitamanas::1355.insight: It shifts attention from proving strength to recognizing limits before humiliation does.

ramacharitamanas::1356.verse_sanskrit: तमकि धरहिं धनु मूढ़ नृप उठइ न चलहिं लजाइ॥ मनहुँ पाइ भट बाहुबलु अधिकु अधिकु गरुआइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1356.verse_hindi: वे मूर्ख राजा तमककर (किटकिटाकर) धनुष को पकड़ते हैं, परन्तु जब नहीं उठता तो लजाकर चले जाते हैं, मानो वीरों की भुजाओं का बल पाकर वह धनुष अधिक-अधिक भारी होता जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1356.english_translation: The foolish kings grab the bow in anger, but when it will not lift, they leave in shame, as if the bow grows heavier and heavier with the strength of proud warriors.
ramacharitamanas::1356.translation_literal: तमकि (with anger) / धरहिं (they grasp) / धनु (the bow) / मूढ़ (foolish) / नृप (kings) / उठइ (does not rise) / न चलहिं (they do not move) / लजाइ (in shame) / मनहुँ (as if) / पाइ (having obtained) / भट (warriors) / बाहुबलु (arm-strength) / अधिकु अधिकु (more and more) / गरुआइ (becomes heavy)
ramacharitamanas::1356.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1356.essence: Pride makes even strength feel like weight.
ramacharitamanas::1356.simple_meaning: The proud kings try to lift Shiva's bow, but they cannot. Ashamed, they step back, as if their own pride makes the bow seem even heavier.
ramacharitamanas::1356.simple_insight: Pride can turn effort into failure. The harder ego pushes, the more impossible the task feels.
ramacharitamanas::1356.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, many kings have already failed to lift Shiva's bow. Some rush at it in anger, grab it, and then retreat in embarrassment when it will not move. Their pride itself becomes part of the failure.
ramacharitamanas::1356.modern_relevance: You force open a stuck lid in front of everyone, then pretend you never cared. The embarrassment is not from the lid — it is from the ego that demanded to win.
ramacharitamanas::1356.insight: It shows how ego magnifies resistance and makes defeat feel heavier than the task itself.

ramacharitamanas::1357.verse_sanskrit: भूप सहस दस एकहि बारा। लगे उठावन टरइ न टारा॥ डगइ न संभु सरासनु कैसें। कामी बचन सती मनु जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1357.verse_hindi: तब दस हजार राजा एक ही बार धनुष को उठाने लगे, तो भी वह उनके टाले नहीं टलता। शिवजी का वह धनुष कैसे नहीं डिगता था, जैसे कामी पुरुष के वचनों से सती का मन (कभी) चलायमान नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1357.english_translation: Ten thousand kings tried at once to lift it, but it would not budge. Shiva's bow stood unmoved, like Sati's mind before a lover's words.
ramacharitamanas::1357.translation_literal: भूप (kings) / सहस दस (ten thousand) / एकहि बारा (at one time) / लगे (began) / उठावन (to lift) / टरइ न (did not move away) / टारा (moved) / डगइ न (did not stir) / संभु (Shiva) / सरासनु (bow) / कैसें (how) / कामी (lustful man) / बचन (words) / सती (Sati) / मनु (mind) / जैसें (like)
ramacharitamanas::1357.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1357.essence: True steadiness cannot be moved by force or persuasion.
ramacharitamanas::1357.simple_meaning: Ten thousand kings try together, but Shiva's bow still does not move. The verse compares that unmoving bow to Sati's mind, which cannot be swayed by a lustful man's words.
ramacharitamanas::1357.simple_insight: Some things cannot be forced. Real steadiness does not yield to pressure.
ramacharitamanas::1357.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the assembled kings have already failed. Now ten thousand of them strain together, yet Shiva's bow still will not move. The verse uses that stubborn stillness to show the depth of Sati's unwavering mind.
ramacharitamanas::1357.modern_relevance: A whole room piles on pressure, votes, and arguments, but your decision stays unchanged. Some commitments are not moved by noise, only by inner steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::1357.insight: It shifts attention from force to constancy: what is truly settled cannot be shaken by display or persuasion.

ramacharitamanas::1358.verse_sanskrit: सब नृप भए जोगु उपहासी। जैसें बिनु बिराग संन्यासी॥ कीरति बिजय बीरता भारी। चले चाप कर बरबस हारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1358.verse_hindi: सब राजा उपहास के योग्य हो गए, जैसे वैराग्य के बिना संन्यासी उपहास के योग्य हो जाता है। कीर्ति, विजय, बड़ी वीरता- इन सबको वे धनुष के हाथों बरबस हारकर चले गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1358.english_translation: All the kings became a joke, like renunciates without detachment. Their fame, victory, and great valor all went away, defeated by the bow.
ramacharitamanas::1358.translation_literal: सब (all) / नृप (kings) / भए (became) / जोगु (fit) / उपहासी (a laughingstock) / जैसें (like) / बिनु (without) / बिराग (detachment) / संन्यासी (renunciate) / कीरति (fame) / बिजय (victory) / बीरता (valor) / भारी (great) / चले (went away) / चाप (bow) / कर (in the hand) / बरबस (helplessly) / हारी (defeated)
ramacharitamanas::1358.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1358.essence: Pride becomes ridicule when it cannot carry the weight.
ramacharitamanas::1358.simple_meaning: The kings fail so completely that they become a laughingstock. Their pride, fame, and strength collapse before the bow.
ramacharitamanas::1358.simple_insight: Pride looks impressive until it meets something it cannot move.
ramacharitamanas::1358.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s swayamvar, thousands of kings have already strained and failed before Shiva’s bow. This verse sums up their humiliation: all their fame and valor end in helpless defeat, setting up the contrast with the one who can truly lift it.
ramacharitamanas::1358.modern_relevance: You walk into the room certain you will handle it, then one question exposes how fragile your confidence was. The humiliation is sharp, but it reveals the difference between image and real strength.
ramacharitamanas::1358.insight: It shifts attention from public status to actual capacity under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::1359.verse_sanskrit: श्रीहत भए हारि हियँ राजा। बैठे निज निज जाइ समाजा॥ नृपन्ह बिलोकि जनकु अकुलाने। बोले बचन रोष जनु साने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1359.verse_hindi: राजा लोग हृदय से हारकर श्रीहीन (हतप्रभ) हो गए और अपने-अपने समाज में जा बैठे। राजाओं को (असफल) देखकर जनक अकुला उठे और ऐसे वचन बोले जो मानो क्रोध में सने हुए थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1359.english_translation: The kings were defeated and sat down in their own assemblies. Seeing the kings fail, Janaka grew anxious and spoke words steeped in anger.
ramacharitamanas::1359.translation_literal: श्रीहत (deprived of glory) / भए (became) / हारि (having lost) / हियँ (in heart) / राजा (the kings) / बैठे (sat) / निज निज (their own) / जाइ (going) / समाजा (assemblies)॥ / नृपन्ह (the kings) / बिलोकि (seeing) / जनकु (Janaka) / अकुलाने (became distressed) / बोले (spoke) / बचन (words) / रोष (anger) / जनु (as if) / साने (smeared)
ramacharitamanas::1359.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1359.essence: Public defeat leaves pride speechless and the host uneasy.
ramacharitamanas::1359.simple_meaning: The kings could not lift Shiva's bow and sat down in shame. Janaka saw their failure and spoke in rising distress.
ramacharitamanas::1359.simple_insight: Failure can turn a proud scene into silence and pressure. Even a king feels the weight when hope starts slipping away.
ramacharitamanas::1359.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's great swayamvar in Mithila, the assembled kings have failed to lift Shiva's bow. Defeated and humiliated, they return to their seats. Janaka watches the promise of the contest collapse before his eyes and speaks out in agitation.
ramacharitamanas::1359.modern_relevance: You watch a room full of capable people go quiet after the pitch falls flat. The host's smile tightens, and everyone feels the embarrassment before anyone says a word.
ramacharitamanas::1359.insight: It shifts attention from triumph to the emotional cost of public failure.

ramacharitamanas::1360.verse_sanskrit: दीप दीप के भूपति नाना। आए सुनिहम जो पनु ठाना॥ देव दनुज धरि मनुज सरीरा। बिपुल बीर आए रनधीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1360.verse_hindi: मैंने जो प्रण ठाना था, उसे सुनकर द्वीप-द्वीप के अनेकों राजा आए। देवता और दैत्य भी मनुष्य का शरीर धारण करके आए तथा और भी बहुत से रणधीर वीर आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1360.english_translation: Many kings from island to island came, hearing of the vow I had made. Gods and demons, taking human form, also came, along with many other fearless warriors.
ramacharitamanas::1360.translation_literal: दीप (island) / दीप (island) / के (of) / भूपति (kings) / नाना (many) / आए (came) / सुनिहम (hearing) / जो (which) / पनु (vow) / ठाना (was made)॥ / देव (gods) / दनुज (demons) / धरि (taking) / मनुज (human) / सरीरा (bodies) / बिपुल (many) / बीर (warriors) / आए (came) / रनधीरा (battle-brave)
ramacharitamanas::1360.speaker: Janaka
ramacharitamanas::1360.essence: Janaka's vow draws every kind of challenger into one place.
ramacharitamanas::1360.simple_meaning: Kings from many lands came after hearing Janaka's vow. Even beings of power and fear came in human form, along with many brave warriors.
ramacharitamanas::1360.simple_insight: A public vow can draw every kind of contender into one place.
ramacharitamanas::1360.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's swayamvar in Mithila, the hall fills with rulers from across the world. His impossible vow has drawn not just kings, but also beings of power disguised as humans and countless warriors. The scene builds the scale of the challenge before Ram steps forward.
ramacharitamanas::1360.modern_relevance: You announce a standard that actually matters, and suddenly everyone shows up to test it. The room changes the moment the challenge becomes real.
ramacharitamanas::1360.insight: It frames the swayamvar as a magnet for ambition, pride, and courage before the decisive test begins.

ramacharitamanas::1361.verse_sanskrit: कुअँरि मनोहर बिजय बड़ि कीरतिअति कमनीय। पावनिहार बिरंचि जनु रचेउ न धनु दमनीय ॥
ramacharitamanas::1361.verse_hindi: परन्तु धनुष को तोड़कर मनोहर कन्या, बड़ी विजय और अत्यन्त सुंदर कीर्ति को पाने वाला मानो ब्रह्मा ने किसी को रचा ही नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1361.english_translation: But the prince who broke the bow won the lovely maiden, great victory, and a supremely beautiful fame. It was as if Brahma had not created anyone fit to bend that bow.
ramacharitamanas::1361.translation_literal: कुअँरि (maiden) / मनोहर (beautiful) / बिजय (victory) / बड़ि (great) / कीरतिअति (fame, exceedingly) / कमनीय (lovely) / पावनिहार (purifying, one who makes sacred) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / जनु (as if) / रचेउ (created) / न (not) / धनु (bow) / दमनीय (fit to be bent)
ramacharitamanas::1361.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1361.essence: The impossible bow reveals the one worthy to break it.
ramacharitamanas::1361.simple_meaning: Rama's bow-breaking won Sita, glorious victory, and lasting fame. The bow was so hard that it seemed no one had been made to bend it.
ramacharitamanas::1361.simple_insight: Some victories feel impossible until they happen.
ramacharitamanas::1361.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, kings from many lands have failed to lift Shiva's bow. The contest is collapsing into shame and silence. This line celebrates the one who will break that impossible bow and win Sita.
ramacharitamanas::1361.modern_relevance: You watch everyone else fail at the task, and the room has already decided it cannot be done. Then one person steps forward and changes the meaning of impossible.
ramacharitamanas::1361.insight: It frames success as meeting the one challenge no one else could bear.

ramacharitamanas::1362.verse_sanskrit: कहहु काहि यहु लाभु न भावा। काहुँ न संकर चाप चढ़ावा॥ रहउ चढ़ाउब तोरब भाई। तिलु भरि भूमि न सके छड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1362.verse_hindi: कहिए, यह लाभ किसको अच्छा नहीं लगता, परन्तु किसी ने भी शंकरजी का धनुष नहीं चढ़ाया। अरे भाई! चढ़ाना और तोड़ना तो दूर रहा, कोई तिल भर भूमि भी छुड़ा न सका ॥
ramacharitamanas::1362.english_translation: Tell me, who would not want this prize? Yet no one could lift Shiva's bow. Brother, lifting it or breaking it was not even possible; no one could move it by even a tiny grain of earth.
ramacharitamanas::1362.translation_literal: कहहु (tell) / काहि (for whom) / यहु (this) / लाभु (gain, prize) / न (not) / भावा (pleased) / काहुँ (to anyone) / न (not) / संकर (Shiva's) / चाप (bow) / चढ़ावा (was lifted)॥ / रहउ (to remain) / चढ़ाउब (to lift) / तोरब (to break) / भाई (brother) / तिलु (sesame-grain) / भरि (full) / भूमि (earth) / न (not) / सके (was able) / छड़ाई (to move, to dislodge) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1362.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1362.essence: Wanting the prize is easy; lifting the bow is not.
ramacharitamanas::1362.simple_meaning: No one could lift or break Shiva's bow, not even move it a little. The prize was there, but no one could claim it.
ramacharitamanas::1362.simple_insight: Sometimes the desire is common, but the ability is absent.
ramacharitamanas::1362.detailed_meaning: At Janak's swayamvar, kings from many lands have gathered to win Sita. The challenge is Shiva's bow, and the room has already filled with failure. This verse underlines the impossible standard before Ram is revealed.
ramacharitamanas::1362.modern_relevance: A room full of qualified applicants goes silent when the task gets real. Everyone wanted the role; almost no one could actually do what it demanded.
ramacharitamanas::1362.insight: It frames the contest as a test of true power, not public ambition.
