ramacharitamanas::1363.verse_sanskrit: अब जनि कोउ भाखे भट मानी। बीर बिहीन मही मैं जानी॥ तजहु आस निज निज गृह जाहू। लिखा न बिधि बैदेहि बिबाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1363.verse_hindi: अब कोई वीरता का अभिमानी नाराज न हो। मैंने जान लिया, पृथ्वी वीरों से खाली हो गई। अब आशा छोड़कर अपने-अपने घर जाओ, ब्रह्मा ने सीता का विवाह लिखा ही नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1363.english_translation: Now let no one boast as a hero. I have seen that the earth is empty of warriors. Give up hope and go back to your homes. Brahma has not written Sita's marriage.
ramacharitamanas::1363.translation_literal: अब (now) / जनि (do not) / कोउ (anyone) / भाखे (speak) / भट (hero/warrior) / मानी (thinking oneself) / बीर (warrior) / बिहीन (without) / मही (earth) / मैं (I) / जानी (have known)॥ / तजहु (give up) / आस (hope) / निज (own) / निज (own) / गृह (home) / जाहू (go) / लिखा (written) / न (not) / बिधि (Brahma/fate) / बैदेहि (Sita) / बिबाहू (marriage) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1363.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1363.essence: False courage falls away when reality refuses to support it.
ramacharitamanas::1363.simple_meaning: The suitor's pride is cut down: he says no warrior has proved himself, so everyone should stop hoping and go home because Sita's marriage seems unwritten.
ramacharitamanas::1363.simple_insight: Pride collapses when reality refuses to match it. Sometimes the hardest wisdom is accepting that a door is not open.
ramacharitamanas::1363.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the crowd has watched impossible attempts fail. After the boastful claims around Shiva's bow, the speaker dismisses heroic pride and declares the earth empty of true warriors. The moment turns the contest into a crisis of hope itself.
ramacharitamanas::1363.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing the application portal after every rejection, then finally admit it: the path you wanted may not open. The brave move is to stop posturing and face what is actually there.
ramacharitamanas::1363.insight: It shifts the mind from wounded pride to clear acceptance of limits and reality.

ramacharitamanas::1364.verse_sanskrit: सुकृतु जाइ जौं पनु परिहरऊँ। कुअँरि कुआँरि रहउ का करऊँ॥ जौं जनतेउँ बिनु भट भुबि भाई। तौ पनु करि होतेउँ न हँसाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1364.verse_hindi: यदि प्रण छोड़ता हूँ, तो पुण्य जाता है, इसलिए क्या करूँ, कन्या कुँआरी ही रहे। यदि मैं जानता कि पृथ्वी वीरों से शून्य है, तो प्रण करके उपहास का पात्र न बनता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1364.english_translation: If I abandon my vow, my merit is lost. Then the princess must remain unmarried—what should I do? If I had known there were no heroes on earth, I would not have made a vow and become a laughingstock.
ramacharitamanas::1364.translation_literal: सुकृतु (merit) / जाइ (goes) / जौं (if) / पनु (vow) / परिहरऊँ (I abandon) / कुअँरि (princess) / कुआँरि (unmarried) / रहउ (remain) / का (what) / करऊँ (shall I do) / जौं (if) / जनतेउँ (I had known) / बिनु (without) / भट (heroes) / भुबि (earth) / भाई (brother) / तौ (then) / पनु (vow) / करि (making) / होतेउँ (I would have become) / न (not) / हँसाई (a laughingstock)
ramacharitamanas::1364.speaker: Janaka
ramacharitamanas::1364.essence: A vow can trap pride, but breaking it traps character more deeply.
ramacharitamanas::1364.simple_meaning: Janaka says he cannot back away from his vow, even though the result is painful. He would rather bear the shame than break his word and leave Sita unmarried.
ramacharitamanas::1364.simple_insight: Keeping your word can cost you pride, but breaking it costs your character.
ramacharitamanas::1364.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, Janaka has challenged the strongest princes to lift Shiva’s bow and win Sita’s hand. No one has succeeded. Now he stands before the court, wounded by the failure yet bound by his promise, speaking with regret and resolve.
ramacharitamanas::1364.modern_relevance: You promised a deadline, but the work is harder than anyone admitted. Backing out would save face for a moment; keeping the promise protects the trust people placed in you.
ramacharitamanas::1364.insight: It teaches you to value integrity over embarrassment, even when the vow becomes costly.

ramacharitamanas::1365.verse_sanskrit: जनक बचन सुनि सब नर नारी। देखि जानकिहि भए दुखारी॥ माखे लखनु कुटिल भइँ भौंहें। रदपट फरकत नयन रिसौंहें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1365.verse_hindi: जनक के वचन सुनकर सभी स्त्री-पुरुष जानकीजी की ओर देखकर दुःखी हुए, परन्तु लक्ष्मणजी तमतमा उठे, उनकी भौंहें टेढ़ी हो गईं, होठ फड़कने लगे और नेत्र क्रोध से लाल हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1365.english_translation: Hearing Janak's words, all the men and women looked at Janaki and felt sorrow. Lakshman grew angry: his eyebrows knit, his lips trembled, and his eyes reddened with rage.
ramacharitamanas::1365.translation_literal: जनक बचन (Janak's words) / सुनि (hearing) / सब (all) / नर नारी (men and women) / देखि (seeing) / जानकिहि (Janaki) / भए (became) / दुखारी (sorrowful) / माखे (became angry) / लखनु (Lakshman) / कुटिल (crooked) / भइँ (became) / भौंहें (eyebrows) / रदपट (lips) / फरकत (trembling) / नयन (eyes) / रिसौंहें (reddened with anger)
ramacharitamanas::1365.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1365.essence: Humiliation spreads through the room; loyal love reacts before speech can.
ramacharitamanas::1365.simple_meaning: Janak's words make everyone sad, and Lakshman reacts with visible anger at the insult to Janaki.
ramacharitamanas::1365.simple_insight: Some words wound a whole room, and loyal love can flare instantly into anger.
ramacharitamanas::1365.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the failed swayamvar has left everyone tense. When Janak speaks, the crowd looks at Sita with sorrow. Lakshman cannot stay quiet; his body shows his outrage at the humiliation.
ramacharitamanas::1365.modern_relevance: A family dinner goes silent after one cutting remark. Everyone feels the sting, but the person who loves most visibly bristles first.
ramacharitamanas::1365.insight: It shows how public humiliation spreads instantly, and how protective loyalty can turn into anger before words are spoken.

ramacharitamanas::1366.verse_sanskrit: कहि न सकत रघुबीर डर लगे बचन जनु बान। नाइ राम पद कमल सिरु बोले गिरा प्रमान ॥
ramacharitamanas::1366.verse_hindi: श्री रघुवीरजी के डर से कुछ कह तो सकते नहीं, पर जनक के वचन उन्हें बाण से लगे। (जब न रह सके तब) श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरण कमलों में सिर नवाकर वे यथार्थ वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1366.english_translation: Afraid of Raghuvir, they could not speak; Janak's words struck them like arrows. Then, bowing their head at Ram's lotus feet, they spoke truthfully.
ramacharitamanas::1366.translation_literal: कहि (speaking) / न सकत (not able) / रघुबीर (Raghuvir) / डर लगे (fear arose) / बचन (words) / जनु (as if) / बान (arrows) / नाइ (bowing) / राम पद कमल (Ram's lotus feet) / सिरु (head) / बोले (spoke) / गिरा (speech) / प्रमान (true / proper)
ramacharitamanas::1366.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1366.essence: Pride blocks speech; reverence restores truth.
ramacharitamanas::1366.simple_meaning: Janak's words left them speechless. They bowed to Ram and then spoke honestly.
ramacharitamanas::1366.simple_insight: Respect softens the heart enough for truth to come out.
ramacharitamanas::1366.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the assembled kings and princes are stunned by the challenge over Sita's swayamvar. The words feel like arrows to their pride, and only after bowing to Ram do they answer with honesty.
ramacharitamanas::1366.modern_relevance: You freeze in a tense room after someone says exactly what everyone feared. Only after you lower your pride can you answer plainly.
ramacharitamanas::1366.insight: It shows that humility clears the throat of fear and makes truthful speech possible.

ramacharitamanas::1367.verse_sanskrit: रघुबंसिन्ह महुँ जहँ कोउ होई। तेहिं समाज अस कहइ न कोई॥ कही जनक जसि अनुचित बानी। बिद्यमान रघुकुल मनि जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1367.verse_hindi: रघुवंशियों में कोई भी जहाँ होता है, उस समाज में ऐसे वचन कोई नहीं कहता, जैसे अनुचित वचन रघुकुल शिरोमणि श्री रामजी को उपस्थित जानते हुए भी जनकजी ने कहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1367.english_translation: Among the descendants of Raghu, no one would speak such words in such an assembly. Janaka has spoken an improper thing while knowing Ram, the jewel of the Raghu line, is present.
ramacharitamanas::1367.translation_literal: रघुबंसिन्ह (among the descendants of Raghu) / महुँ (among) / जहँ (where) / कोउ (anyone) / होई (is) / तेहिं (in that) / समाज (assembly) / अस (such) / कहइ (speaks) / न (not) / कोई (anyone) ॥ कही (spoken) / जनक (Janaka) / जसि (such as) / अनुचित (improper) / बानी (speech) / बिद्यमान (present) / रघुकुल (Raghu clan) / मनि (jewel) / जानी (knowing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1367.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1367.essence: True conduct speaks differently in the presence of greatness.
ramacharitamanas::1367.simple_meaning: In a gathering of Raghu's descendants, no one would speak like this. Janaka has spoken words that do not fit the presence of Ram, the jewel of Raghu's line.
ramacharitamanas::1367.simple_insight: Respect changes what can be said. Presence itself calls for greater care.
ramacharitamanas::1367.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, after Janaka's troubling words, the court feels the sting of impropriety. Tulsidas pauses the scene to note that in the presence of Ram, the jewel of Raghu's line, such speech should never have been spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1367.modern_relevance: You make a cutting remark in a room where everyone can feel the tension. Later, you realize the issue was not just what you said, but the dignity of the moment you ignored.
ramacharitamanas::1367.insight: It teaches you to match your speech to the dignity of the setting and the people before you.

ramacharitamanas::1368.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु भानुकुल पंकज भानू। कहउँ सुभाउ न कछु अभिमानू॥ जौं तुम्हारि अनुसासन पावौं। कंदुक इव ब्रह्मांड उठावौं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1368.verse_hindi: हे सूर्य कुल रूपी कमल के सूर्य! सुनिए, मैं स्वभाव ही से कहता हूँ, कुछ अभिमान करके नहीं, यदि आपकी आज्ञा पाऊँ, तो मैं ब्रह्माण्ड को गेंद की तरह उठा लूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1368.english_translation: Listen, O sun of the solar clan. I speak from my nature, not from pride. If I receive your command, I could lift the universe like a ball.
ramacharitamanas::1368.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / भानुकुल (solar clan) / पंकज (lotus) / भानू (sun) / कहउँ (I speak) / सुभाउ (nature) / न (not) / कछु (any) / अभिमानू (pride) / जौं (if) / तुम्हारि (your) / अनुसासन (command) / पावौं (I receive) / कंदुक इव (like a ball) / ब्रह्मांड (universe) / उठावौं (I lift)
ramacharitamanas::1368.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::1368.essence: Pride can speak in the language of humility.
ramacharitamanas::1368.simple_meaning: Ravana flatters Ram while boasting of his own power. He says he is not speaking out of pride, and that with Ram's command he could lift the universe like a ball.
ramacharitamanas::1368.simple_insight: Pride can wear the mask of humility. Real strength does not need to announce itself.
ramacharitamanas::1368.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the tension is rising after the failed breaking of Shiva's bow. Ravana steps forward and speaks with grand self-confidence, claiming immense power while pretending modesty. This verse reveals his ego before the challenge deepens.
ramacharitamanas::1368.modern_relevance: Someone says, “I’m not bragging, but…” and then spends two minutes proving how exceptional they are. The verse catches that instant when confidence quietly turns into self-display.
ramacharitamanas::1368.insight: It exposes how the sense of separate self inflates even a humble-sounding claim.

ramacharitamanas::1369.verse_sanskrit: काचे घट जिमि डारौं फोरी। सकउँ मेरु मूलक जिमि तोरी॥ तव प्रताप महिमा भगवाना। को बापुरो पिनाक पुराना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1369.verse_hindi: और उसे कच्चे घड़े की तरह फोड़ डालूँ। मैं सुमेरु पर्वत को मूली की तरह तोड़ सकता हूँ, हे भगवन् ! आपके प्रताप की महिमा से यह बेचारा पुराना धनुष तो कौन चीज है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1369.english_translation: I could smash it like a clay pot and break Mount Meru like a radish. By your power and glory, what is this old bow?
ramacharitamanas::1369.translation_literal: काचे (of clay / fragile) / घट (pot) / जिमि (like) / डारौं (I would throw) / फोरी (breaking) / सकउँ (I can) / मेरु (Mount Meru) / मूलक (radish) / जिमि (like) / तोरी (I would break) / तव (your) / प्रताप (power / splendor) / महिमा (glory) / भगवाना (O Lord) / को (what) / बापुरो (poor / helpless) / पिनाक (Pinaka bow) / पुराना (old)
ramacharitamanas::1369.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1369.essence: Divine power makes even the impossible look fragile.
ramacharitamanas::1369.simple_meaning: The speaker says the bow is nothing compared with divine power and could be broken as easily as a clay pot.
ramacharitamanas::1369.simple_insight: Real strength makes obstacles look small, not the other way around.
ramacharitamanas::1369.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the challenge of Shiva's bow is about to be tested. The speaker dismisses the ancient weapon as fragile beside divine power, setting up the moment that will reveal Ram's true greatness.
ramacharitamanas::1369.modern_relevance: You stare at a problem that everyone else treats like a wall. Then someone with calm confidence handles it as if it were light enough to lift with one hand.
ramacharitamanas::1369.insight: It shifts attention from the object's size to the power behind the one who acts.

ramacharitamanas::1370.verse_sanskrit: नाथ जानि अस आयसु होऊ। कौतुकु करौं बिलोकिअ सोऊ॥ कमल नाल जिमि चाप चढ़ावौं। जोजन सत प्रमान लै धावौं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1370.verse_hindi: ऐसा जानकर हे नाथ! आज्ञा हो तो कुछ खेल करूँ, उसे भी देखिए। धनुष को कमल की डंडी की तरह चढ़ाकर उसे सौ योजन तक दौड़ा लिए चला जाऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1370.english_translation: Knowing this, O Lord, if you command it, I will perform a little feat and let you see it. I will string the bow like a lotus stalk and run with it for a hundred yojanas.
ramacharitamanas::1370.translation_literal: नाथ (O Lord) / जानि (knowing) / अस (thus) / आयसु (command) / होऊ (may it be) / कौतुकु (play/feat) / करौं (I do) / बिलोकिअ (watch) / सोऊ (that) / कमल (lotus) / नाल (stalk) / जिमि (like) / चाप (bow) / चढ़ावौं (I string/lift) / जोजन (yojana) / सत (hundred) / प्रमान (measure) / लै (taking) / धावौं (I run)
ramacharitamanas::1370.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::1370.essence: Pride turns strength into a display.
ramacharitamanas::1370.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that, if allowed, he can string the bow easily and carry it far, as if it were nothing more than a toy.
ramacharitamanas::1370.simple_insight: Pride makes strength feel effortless, but it also makes a person blind to what truly matters.
ramacharitamanas::1370.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s court, the bow of Shiva stands before the assembled kings. Ravana steps forward, speaking with swagger, asking permission to show off his strength. His boast only deepens the contrast before Ram’s own quiet act.
ramacharitamanas::1370.modern_relevance: A person in a group chat keeps escalating: “Give me the task, I’ll handle it.” The confidence sounds impressive until the moment arrives and everyone sees whether it was skill or noise.
ramacharitamanas::1370.insight: It reveals how ego turns ability into performance, not service.

ramacharitamanas::1371.verse_sanskrit: तोरौं छत्रक दंड जिमि तव प्रताप बल नाथ। जौं न करौं प्रभु पद सपथ कर न धरौं धनु भाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1371.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! आपके प्रताप के बल से धनुष को कुकुरमुत्ते (बरसाती छत्ते) की तरह तोड़ दूँ। यदि ऐसा न करूँ तो प्रभु के चरणों की शपथ है, फिर मैं धनुष और तरकस को कभी हाथ में भी न लूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1371.english_translation: By your power, Lord, I will break the bow like a mushroom. If I do not, I swear by the Lord's feet that I will never again take up bow and quiver.
ramacharitamanas::1371.translation_literal: तोरौं (I will break) / छत्रक (mushroom) / दंड (stem) / जिमि (like) / तव (your) / प्रताप (splendor) / बल (power) / नाथ (Lord) / जौं (if) / न (not) / करौं (I do) / प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / सपथ (oath) / कर (hand) / न (not) / धरौं (I place) / धनु (bow) / भाथ (quiver)
ramacharitamanas::1371.speaker: Rama
ramacharitamanas::1371.essence: True confidence makes the impossible sound simple.
ramacharitamanas::1371.simple_meaning: The speaker vows to break the bow easily, and says that if he fails, he will never touch a bow again.
ramacharitamanas::1371.simple_insight: Bold confidence can be tested without fear when the task is truly yours to prove.
ramacharitamanas::1371.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the bow of Shiva has become the test for winning Sita. Ram speaks with calm certainty before the assembled kings, promising to break it as easily as a mushroom stem. This verse heightens the challenge just before the bow is lifted.
ramacharitamanas::1371.modern_relevance: You stand before a task everyone says is impossible. Instead of shrinking, you name the challenge plainly and commit yourself fully before the room.
ramacharitamanas::1371.insight: It frames difficult action as a direct vow: either do it completely or give up the claim.

ramacharitamanas::1372.verse_sanskrit: लखन सकोप बचन जे बोले। डगमगानि महि दिग्गज डोले॥ सकल लोग सब भूप डेराने। सिय हियँ हरषु जनकु सकुचाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1372.verse_hindi: ज्यों ही लक्ष्मणजी क्रोध भरे वचन बोले कि पृथ्वी डगमगा उठी और दिशाओं के हाथी काँप गए। सभी लोग और सब राजा डर गए। सीताजी के हृदय में हर्ष हुआ और जनकजी सकुचा गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1372.english_translation: As Lakshman spoke angry words, the earth shook and the elephants of the directions trembled. All the people and all the kings were frightened. Sita's heart filled with joy, and Janak felt bashful.
ramacharitamanas::1372.translation_literal: लखन (Lakshman) / सकोप (with anger) / बचन (words) / जे (which) / बोले (spoke) / डगमगानि (shaking) / महि (earth) / दिग्गज (elephants of the directions) / डोले (trembled) / सकल (all) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / भूप (kings) / डेराने (were frightened) / सिय (Sita) / हियँ (in heart) / हरषु (joy) / जनकु (Janak) / सकुचाने (felt bashful)
ramacharitamanas::1372.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1372.essence: Anger from loyalty can shake a whole court.
ramacharitamanas::1372.simple_meaning: Lakshman speaks in anger, and the whole assembly reacts. The crowd is afraid, while Sita feels joy and Janak feels shy.
ramacharitamanas::1372.simple_insight: Strong feeling changes the room instantly. One voice can shake fear, joy, and pride at once.
ramacharitamanas::1372.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court during Sita's swayamvar, Lakshman flashes with anger after the bow challenge. His words shake the assembly: kings fear, Sita feels delight, and Janak grows bashful. The scene heightens the tension before Ram's turn.
ramacharitamanas::1372.modern_relevance: A tense room goes silent after one sharp remark. Some people flinch, one person smiles, and the host suddenly wishes the floor would swallow him.
ramacharitamanas::1372.insight: It shows how public emotion spreads fast, and how one charged voice can expose courage, fear, and embarrassment in the same moment.

ramacharitamanas::1373.verse_sanskrit: गुर रघुपति सब मुनि मन माहीं। मुदित भए पुनि पुनि पुलकाहीं॥ सयनहिं रघुपति लखनु नेवारे। प्रेम समेत निकट बैठारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1373.verse_hindi: गुरु विश्वामित्रजी, श्री रघुनाथजी और सब मुनि मन में प्रसन्न हुए और बार-बार पुलकित होने लगे। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने इशारे से लक्ष्मण को मना किया और प्रेम सहित अपने पास बैठा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1373.english_translation: Guru Vishwamitra, Ram, and all the sages rejoiced in their hearts and again and again shivered with delight. Shri Ramchandra signaled Lakshman to stop and lovingly seated him close beside himself.
ramacharitamanas::1373.translation_literal: गुर (teacher) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan, Ram) / सब (all) / मुनि (sages) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / मुदित (glad) / भए (became) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / पुलकाहीं (they thrilled) / सयनहिं (by gesture) / रघुपति (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / नेवारे (stopped) / प्रेम समेत (with love) / निकट (near) / बैठारे (seated)
ramacharitamanas::1373.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1373.essence: True strength can be gentle enough to seat love beside itself.
ramacharitamanas::1373.simple_meaning: Everyone feels joy at the moment, and Ram lovingly keeps Lakshman close by his side.
ramacharitamanas::1373.simple_insight: Joy deepens when love is shown through small, gentle gestures.
ramacharitamanas::1373.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the bow challenge has reached its turning point. Vishwamitra, Ram, and the sages feel delight rising in them, and Ram gently draws Lakshman back to his side. The scene prepares for the next command to break the bow.
ramacharitamanas::1373.modern_relevance: In a tense family gathering, one person’s small calming gesture can settle the whole room. A hand on the shoulder can speak louder than a speech.
ramacharitamanas::1373.insight: It shifts attention from drama to tenderness, showing leadership through affection and restraint.

ramacharitamanas::1374.verse_sanskrit: बिस्वामित्र समय सुभ जानी। बोले अति सनेहमय बानी॥ उठहु राम भंजहु भवचापा। मेटहु तात जनक परितापा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1374.verse_hindi: विश्वामित्रजी शुभ समय जानकर अत्यन्त प्रेमभरी वाणी बोले- हे राम! उठो, शिवजी का धनुष तोड़ो और हे तात! जनक का संताप मिटाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1374.english_translation: Knowing the auspicious moment, Vishwamitra spoke with great affection: "Rise, Ram. Break the bow of Shiva, and, dear child, end Janak's sorrow."
ramacharitamanas::1374.translation_literal: बिस्वामित्र (Vishwamitra) / समय (time) / सुभ (auspicious) / जानी (having known) / बोले (spoke) / अति (very) / सनेहमय (full of affection) / बानी (speech) / उठहु (rise) / राम (Ram) / भंजहु (break) / भवचापा (Shiva's bow) / मेटहु (remove) / तात (dear child) / जनक (Janak's) / परितापा (sorrow)
ramacharitamanas::1374.speaker: Vishwamitra
ramacharitamanas::1374.essence: Right timing and loving guidance turn readiness into action.
ramacharitamanas::1374.simple_meaning: Vishwamitra sees the right moment and gently urges Ram to rise, break Shiva's bow, and relieve Janak's sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::1374.simple_insight: A true teacher knows when to call you forward, and does it with care, not pressure.
ramacharitamanas::1374.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the bow contest has reached its decisive moment. Vishwamitra sees that the time is ripe and, with loving urgency, asks Ram to step forward. This is the prompt that turns readiness into action.
ramacharitamanas::1374.modern_relevance: Your mentor texts you one line before the interview: "Go in now." The timing matters, but so does the warmth behind the push. The right nudge can unlock courage.
ramacharitamanas::1374.insight: It teaches you to recognize the moment and act without hesitation when the path is clear.

ramacharitamanas::1375.verse_sanskrit: सुनि गुरु बचन चरन सिरु नावा। हरषु बिषादु न कछु उर आवा॥ ठाढ़े भए उठि सहज सुभाएँ। ठवनि जुबा मृगराजु लजाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1375.verse_hindi: गुरु के वचन सुनकर श्री रामजी ने चरणों में सिर नवाया। उनके मन में न हर्ष हुआ, न विषाद और वे अपनी ऐंड़ (खड़े होने की शान) से जवान सिंह को भी लजाते हुए सहज स्वभाव से ही उठ खड़े हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1375.english_translation: Hearing the guru's words, Ram bowed his head to his feet. No joy or sorrow arose in his heart, and he rose naturally, with a bearing that would shame even a young lion.
ramacharitamanas::1375.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / गुरु (teacher) / बचन (words) / चरन (feet) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / हरषु (joy) / बिषादु (sorrow) / न (not) / कछु (anything) / उर (heart) / आवा (came) / ठाढ़े (standing) / भए (became) / उठि (rising) / सहज (natural) / सुभाएँ (by nature) / ठवनि (bearing/stance) / जुबा (young) / मृगराजु (lion) / लजाएँ (would be ashamed)
ramacharitamanas::1375.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1375.essence: True strength stays calm, respectful, and ready to act.
ramacharitamanas::1375.simple_meaning: Ram honors his teacher, stays beyond excitement or fear, and rises with calm dignity.
ramacharitamanas::1375.simple_insight: Steady respect does not need drama. Real strength can be quiet, obedient, and unshaken.
ramacharitamanas::1375.detailed_meaning: विश्वामित्र has just asked Ram to rise and break Shiva's bow. Ram hears the command, bows to the teacher's feet, and stands without excitement or fear. The verse shows his composed readiness before the great test.
ramacharitamanas::1375.modern_relevance: You get a difficult message from a mentor, then feel the urge to overreact, defend yourself, or freeze. Ram's response is simpler: hear fully, bow in respect, and stand up steady.
ramacharitamanas::1375.insight: It teaches you to receive instruction without emotional noise and respond with poised action.

ramacharitamanas::1376.verse_sanskrit: उदित उदयगिरि मंच पर रघुबर बालपतंग। बिकसे संत सरोज सब हरषे लोचन भृंग ॥
ramacharitamanas::1376.verse_hindi: मंच रूपी उदयाचल पर रघुनाथजी रूपी बाल सूर्य के उदय होते ही सब संत रूपी कमल खिल उठे और नेत्र रूपी भौंरे हर्षित हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1376.english_translation: As the young sun-like Raghuvar rose on the horizon-like stage, all the saints' lotus-hearts bloomed and their bee-like eyes rejoiced.
ramacharitamanas::1376.translation_literal: उदित (having risen) / उदयगिरि (eastern mountain) / मंच (stage) / पर (on) / रघुबर (Raghubar) / बालपतंग (young sun) / बिकसे (bloomed) / संत (saints) / सरोज (lotuses) / सब (all) / हरषे (rejoiced) / लोचन (eyes) / भृंग (bees)
ramacharitamanas::1376.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1376.essence: Ram's arrival makes the heart bloom before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1376.simple_meaning: Ram is compared to the rising sun. His arrival fills the saints with joy, like lotuses opening to light.
ramacharitamanas::1376.simple_insight: True presence changes the whole atmosphere. What was waiting in darkness suddenly opens.
ramacharitamanas::1376.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, just before the bow-breaking moment, Ram steps onto the stage like the morning sun. The saints respond instantly with joy, while the scene prepares for the pride of kings to fade in the next line.
ramacharitamanas::1376.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the tension shifts before anyone speaks. The people who were braced and guarded suddenly soften, because something steady has arrived.
ramacharitamanas::1376.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to presence: one pure arrival can transform the whole field around it.

ramacharitamanas::1377.verse_sanskrit: नृपन्ह केरि आसा निसि नासी। बचन नखत अवली न प्रकासी॥ मानी महिप कुमुद सकुचाने। कपटी भूप उलूक लुकाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1377.verse_hindi: राजाओं की आशा रूपी रात्रि नष्ट हो गई। उनके वचन रूपी तारों के समूह का चमकना बंद हो गया। (वे मौन हो गए)। अभिमानी राजा रूपी कुमुद संकुचित हो गए और कपटी राजा रूपी उल्लू छिप गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1377.english_translation: The night of kings' hopes was destroyed. The stars of their words no longer shone. Proud rulers shrank like lotuses, and deceitful kings hid like owls.
ramacharitamanas::1377.translation_literal: नृपन्ह (of kings) / केरि (of) / आसा (hope) / निसि (night) / नासी (destroyed) / बचन (words) / नखत (stars) / अवली (row/group) / न (not) / प्रकासी (shone) / मानी (proud) / महिप (kings) / कुमुद (lotuses) / सकुचाने (shrunk/shy) / कपटी (deceitful) / भूप (rulers/kings) / उलूक (owls) / लुकाने (hid)
ramacharitamanas::1377.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1377.essence: Pride goes silent when it meets real majesty.
ramacharitamanas::1377.simple_meaning: The arrival of Ram makes proud and deceitful rulers lose their confidence. Their hopes fade, their voices fall silent, and they hide themselves.
ramacharitamanas::1377.simple_insight: False power cannot stay bright when real greatness appears.
ramacharitamanas::1377.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar gathering, Ram has just risen in calm majesty. The watching kings feel the change at once: proud ones shrink, cunning ones go silent, and the whole room shifts under his presence.
ramacharitamanas::1377.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where one person carries real authority without trying. The loudest people suddenly soften, and the ones performing confidence start looking for the exit.
ramacharitamanas::1377.insight: It shows how ego reacts when it meets true worth: it either shrinks or hides.

ramacharitamanas::1378.verse_sanskrit: भए बिसोक कोक मुनि देवा। बरिसहिं सुमन जनावहिं सेवा॥ गुर पद बंदि सहित अनुरागा। राम मुनिन्हसन आयसु मागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1378.verse_hindi: मुनि और देवता रूपी चकवे शोकरहित हो गए। वे फूल बरसाकर अपनी सेवा प्रकट कर रहे हैं। प्रेम सहित गुरु के चरणों की वंदना करके श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने मुनियों से आज्ञा माँगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1378.english_translation: The sages and the radiant beings became free of sorrow. They showered flowers to show their service. Bowing to the guru's feet with love, Ram asked the sages for permission.
ramacharitamanas::1378.translation_literal: भए (became) / बिसोक (free from sorrow) / कोक (sages) / मुनि (ascetics) / देवा (radiant beings) / बरिसहिं (they shower) / सुमन (flowers) / जनावहिं (show) / सेवा (service) / गुर (teacher) / पद (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / सहित (together with) / अनुरागा (love) / राम (Ram) / मुनिन्हसन (from the sages) / आयसु (permission) / मागा (asked)
ramacharitamanas::1378.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1378.essence: Power stays pure when it bows before acting.
ramacharitamanas::1378.simple_meaning: The sages and celestial beings rejoice and honor Ram with flowers. Ram first bows to his teacher, then asks the sages for permission before moving on.
ramacharitamanas::1378.simple_insight: True greatness still bows first. Respect keeps power clean.
ramacharitamanas::1378.detailed_meaning: Ram has reached the sacred assembly after the bow challenge. The sages and celestial beings rejoice at his presence, showering flowers in service. Yet Ram does not rush ahead; he bows to his teacher and asks the sages' permission before acting.
ramacharitamanas::1378.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is waiting for you to take charge. Before speaking, you acknowledge the person who taught you and the people already holding the space.
ramacharitamanas::1378.insight: It teaches that authority becomes noble when it begins with humility and consent.

ramacharitamanas::1379.verse_sanskrit: सहजहिं चले सकल जग स्वामी। मत्त मंजु बर कुंजर गामी॥ चलत राम सब पुर नर नारी। पुलक पूरि तन भए सुखारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1379.verse_hindi: समस्त जगत के स्वामी श्री रामजी सुंदर मतवाले श्रेष्ठ हाथी की सी चाल से स्वाभाविक ही चले। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चलते ही नगर भर के सब स्त्री-पुरुष सुखी हो गए और उनके शरीर रोमांच से भर गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1379.english_translation: Lord of the world Rama walked naturally, like a splendid intoxicated elephant. As Rama moved through the city, every man and woman became joyful, and their bodies thrilled with goosebumps.
ramacharitamanas::1379.translation_literal: सहजहिं (naturally) / चले (walked) / सकल जग स्वामी (lord of the whole world) / मत्त (intoxicated) / मंजु (graceful) / बर (excellent) / कुंजर (elephant) / गामी (moving) ॥ / चलत (while walking) / राम (Rama) / सब (all) / पुर (city) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / पुलक (goosebumps) / पूरि (filled) / तन (body) / भए (became) / सुखारी (happy) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1379.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1379.essence: Rama's presence itself turns the whole city joyful.
ramacharitamanas::1379.simple_meaning: Rama walked through the city with effortless grace, and everyone who saw him felt joy and bodily thrill.
ramacharitamanas::1379.simple_insight: Presence can bless a whole crowd without a single word.
ramacharitamanas::1379.detailed_meaning: The wedding city is overflowing with anticipation as Rama moves through it. His graceful walk alone fills every man and woman with delight. This is a scene of public joy before the great bow contest.
ramacharitamanas::1379.modern_relevance: A beloved teacher enters a crowded hall, and the whole room changes before they speak. Some people carry a calm that reaches everyone around them.
ramacharitamanas::1379.insight: It shows how noble presence can transform a space without effort or speech.

ramacharitamanas::1380.verse_sanskrit: बंदि पितर सुर सुकृत सँभारे। जौं कछु पुन्य प्रभाउ हमारे॥ तौ सिवधनु मृनाल की नाईं। तोरहुँ रामु गनेस गोसाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1380.verse_hindi: उन्होंने पितर और देवताओं की वंदना करके अपने पुण्यों का स्मरण किया। यदि हमारे पुण्यों का कुछ भी प्रभाव हो, तो हे गणेश गोसाईं! रामचन्द्रजी शिवजी के धनुष को कमल की डंडी की भाँति तोड़ डालें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1380.english_translation: After honoring the ancestors and the radiant beings, he recalled his own merit. "If any merit of ours has power, O Ganesh, may Ram break Shiva's bow as easily as a lotus stem."
ramacharitamanas::1380.translation_literal: बंदि (having bowed to) / पितर (ancestors) / सुर (radiant beings) / सुकृत (merit) / सँभारे (remembered) / जौं (if) / कछु (some) / पुन्य (merit) / प्रभाउ (power/effect) / हमारे (our) / तौ (then) / सिवधनु (Shiva's bow) / मृनाल (lotus stem) / की नाईं (like) / तोरहुँ (may break) / रामु (Ram) / गनेस गोसाईं (O Ganesh, lord)
ramacharitamanas::1380.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1380.essence: A hard task becomes light when merit and faith are on its side.
ramacharitamanas::1380.simple_meaning: The bride's side prays and remembers their good deeds, hoping Ram can break Shiva's bow easily.
ramacharitamanas::1380.simple_insight: Faith can turn a terrifying test into a hopeful prayer.
ramacharitamanas::1380.detailed_meaning: At King Janak's court, the assembly is waiting for Ram to lift and break Shiva's bow before Sita's marriage can happen. The family quietly invokes ancestors, divine beings, and their own merit, asking Ganesh to make the impossible effortless.
ramacharitamanas::1380.modern_relevance: You stand outside a hospital room, hoping a loved one gets through surgery. All you can do is whisper, remember every blessing, and ask for a mercy bigger than your fear.
ramacharitamanas::1380.insight: It shifts the mind from dread to trust in a larger grace.

ramacharitamanas::1381.verse_sanskrit: रामहि प्रेम समेत लखि सखिन्ह समीप बोलाइ। सीता मातु सनेह बस बचन कहइ बिलखाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1381.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी को (वात्सल्य) प्रेम के साथ देखकर और सखियों को समीप बुलाकर सीताजी की माता स्नेहवश बिलखकर (विलाप करती हुई सी) ये वचन बोलीं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1381.english_translation: Seeing Ram with loving tenderness, Sita's mother called the maids close and, overwhelmed by affection, spoke these words in tears.
ramacharitamanas::1381.translation_literal: रामहि (Ram) / प्रेम समेत (with love) / लखि (seeing) / सखिन्ह (maids, companions) / समीप (near) / बोलाइ (calling) / सीता मातु (Sita's mother) / सनेह बस (under the sway of affection) / बचन (words) / कहइ (speaks) / बिलखाइ (weeping)
ramacharitamanas::1381.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1381.essence: Affection speaks first in tears, not in polished words.
ramacharitamanas::1381.simple_meaning: Sita's mother sees Ram lovingly, calls the maids close, and speaks while crying from affection.
ramacharitamanas::1381.simple_insight: Love can be so full it turns into tears before words arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1381.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the wedding preparations are alive with joy and tension. Sita's mother looks at Ram with deep affection, gathers the women around her, and begins speaking through tears. The verse is a tender reaction, not the main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1381.modern_relevance: You catch sight of your child's partner and suddenly your throat tightens. The feeling is too full for a neat sentence, so you call someone closer and speak through tears.
ramacharitamanas::1381.insight: It shifts attention from the ceremony itself to the human tenderness it awakens.

ramacharitamanas::1382.verse_sanskrit: सखि सब कौतुक देख निहारे। जेउ कहावत हितू हमारे॥ कोउ न बुझाइ कहइ गुर पाहीं। ए बालक असि हठ भलि नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1382.verse_hindi: हे सखी! ये जो हमारे हितू कहलाते हैं, वे भी सब तमाशा देखने वाले हैं। कोई भी (इनके) गुरु विश्वामित्रजी को समझाकर नहीं कहता कि ये (रामजी) बालक हैं, इनके लिए ऐसा हठ अच्छा नहीं। (जो धनुष रावण और बाण- जैसे जगद्विजयी वीरों के हिलाए न हिल सका, उसे तोड़ने के लिए मुनि विश्वामित्रजी का रामजी को आज्ञा देना और रामजी का उसे तोड़ने के लिए चल देना रानी को हठ जान पड़ा, इसलिए वे कहने लगीं कि गुरु विश्वामित्रजी को कोई समझाता भी नहीं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1382.english_translation: O friend, everyone stands here just to watch. No one even tells the teacher, “This is only a child; such stubbornness is not good.”
ramacharitamanas::1382.translation_literal: सखि (friend) / सब (all) / कौतुक (spectacle, amusement) / देख (seeing) / निहारे (look on) / जेउ (those who) / कहावत (called) / हितू (well-wishers) / हमारे (our) / कोउ (someone) / न (not) / बुझाइ (making understand) / कहइ (says) / गुर (teacher) / पाहीं (near) / ए (these) / बालक (child) / असि (such) / हठ (insistence) / भलि (good) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::1382.speaker: Sita's mother
ramacharitamanas::1382.essence: A mother sees the strain behind everyone else's excitement.
ramacharitamanas::1382.simple_meaning: Sita’s mother sees everyone watching silently as Ram is being asked to lift Shiva’s bow. She feels no one is protecting the boy from what looks like an unreasonable test.
ramacharitamanas::1382.simple_insight: Love notices when a child is being pushed too hard, even by well-meaning people.
ramacharitamanas::1382.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s court, Ram has been called to lift Shiva’s bow. Sita’s mother watches the scene with anxious affection. She sees only a tender boy being pressed into a task that looks too severe, and she wonders why no one stops it.
ramacharitamanas::1382.modern_relevance: You watch a quiet teenager being pushed into the spotlight by adults who call it 'character-building.' Everyone smiles, but one person in the room can feel the strain.
ramacharitamanas::1382.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle to the human cost of public pressure.

ramacharitamanas::1383.verse_sanskrit: रावन बान छुआ नहिं चापा। हारे सकल भूप करि दापा॥ सो धनु राजकुअँर कर देहीं। बाल मराल कि मंदर लेहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1383.verse_hindi: रावण और बाणासुर ने जिस धनुष को छुआ तक नहीं और सब राजा घमंड करके हार गए, वही धनुष इस सुकुमार राजकुमार के हाथ में दे रहे हैं। हंस के बच्चे भी कहीं मंदराचल पहाड़ उठा सकते हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1383.english_translation: Ravana and Banasura never even touched the bow, and all the kings were defeated in pride. And now they give that bow to the young prince. Can a baby swan lift Mount Mandara?
ramacharitamanas::1383.translation_literal: रावन (Ravana) / बान (Banasura) / छुआ (touched) / नहिं (not) / चापा (bow) / हारे (were defeated) / सकल (all) / भूप (kings) / करि (doing) / दापा (pride) / सो (that) / धनु (bow) / राजकुअँर (prince) / कर (hand) / देहीं (they give) / बाल (young) / मराल (swan) / कि (can) / मंदर (Mandara) / लेहीं (lift)
ramacharitamanas::1383.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1383.essence: Apperance can mislead; true strength may arrive in a gentle form.
ramacharitamanas::1383.simple_meaning: The bow defeated mighty kings, so the queen’s fear makes sense. It seems impossible that such a delicate prince could lift what powerful warriors could not.
ramacharitamanas::1383.simple_insight: Doubt often comes from appearances. What looks fragile may carry a strength others missed.
ramacharitamanas::1383.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s court, Sita’s mother watches the swayamvar with alarm. The bow has humbled proud kings, and now it is being placed before Ram, who looks like a tender boy. Her fear turns the scene into a test of seeming versus true strength.
ramacharitamanas::1383.modern_relevance: You watch a quiet new hire walk into the room while everyone else doubts them. They look too young, too soft, too untested — until they do what the loudest people could not.
ramacharitamanas::1383.insight: It shifts the mind from judging by appearance to waiting for revealed capacity.

ramacharitamanas::1384.verse_sanskrit: भूप सयानप सकल सिरानी। सखि बिधि गति कछु जाति न जानी॥ बोली चतुर सखी मृदु बानी। तेजवंत लघु गनिअ न रानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1384.verse_hindi: (और तो कोई समझाकर कहे या नहीं, राजा तो बड़े समझदार और ज्ञानी हैं, उन्हें तो गुरु को समझाने की चेष्टा करनी चाहिए थी, परन्तु मालूम होता है-) राजा का भी सारा सयानापन समाप्त हो गया। हे सखी! विधाता की गति कुछ जानने में नहीं आती (यों कहकर रानी चुप हो रहीं)। तब एक चतुर (रामजी के महत्व को जानने वाली) सखी कोमल वाणी से बोली- हे रानी! तेजवान को (देखने में छोटा होने पर भी) छोटा नहीं गिनना चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1384.english_translation: The king's cleverness was exhausted. "Sakhi, I cannot understand the ways of fate." Then a wise friend spoke gently: "Do not judge the powerful as small just because they seem young."
ramacharitamanas::1384.translation_literal: भूप (king) / सयानप (cleverness, wisdom) / सकल (all) / सिरानी (was exhausted) / सखि (friend) / बिधि (fate, the divine order) / गति (movement, ways) / कछु (anything) / जाति (known, understood) / न जानी (not known) / बोली (spoke) / चतुर (wise, clever) / सखी (friend) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (speech) / तेजवंत (powerful, radiant) / लघु (small) / गनिअ (count, judge) / न (not) / रानी (queen)
ramacharitamanas::1384.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1384.essence: Do not mistake outward smallness for real power.
ramacharitamanas::1384.simple_meaning: The king's confidence breaks, and a wise friend reminds the queen not to judge power by outward size or youth.
ramacharitamanas::1384.simple_insight: Real strength is often hidden at first glance.
ramacharitamanas::1384.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, everyone is stunned that the great bow is being offered to young Ram. The king's certainty falters, and a sharp-eyed friend gently corrects the room: outward size means nothing when true power is present.
ramacharitamanas::1384.modern_relevance: You dismiss the quiet intern in the meeting because she looks nervous. Then she names the flaw everyone missed. Wisdom often arrives in a soft voice.
ramacharitamanas::1384.insight: It trains the mind to stop confusing appearance with capacity.

ramacharitamanas::1385.verse_sanskrit: कहँ कुंभज कहँ सिंधु अपारा। सोषेउ सुजसु सकल संसारा॥ रबि मंडल देखत लघु लागा। उदयँ तासु तिभुवन तम भागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1385.verse_hindi: कहाँ घड़े से उत्पन्न होने वाले (छोटे से) मुनि अगस्त्य और कहाँ समुद्र? किन्तु उन्होंने उसे सोख लिया, जिसका सुयश सारे संसार में छाया हुआ है। सूर्यमंडल देखने में छोटा लगता है, पर उसके उदय होते ही तीनों लोकों का अंधकार भाग जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1385.english_translation: Where is sage Agastya, born from a pot, and where is the vast ocean? Yet he drank it dry, though the ocean’s fame fills the world. The sun may seem small to the eye, but when it rises, the darkness of the three worlds flees.
ramacharitamanas::1385.translation_literal: कहँ (where) / कुंभज (pot-born one, Agastya) / कहँ (where) / सिंधु (ocean) / अपारा (boundless) / सोषेउ (he drank up, absorbed) / सुजसु (good fame) / सकल (all) / संसारा (world) / रबि (sun) / मंडल (disc) / देखत (seeing) / लघु (small) / लागा (seemed) / उदयँ (at rising) / तासु (its) / तिभुवन (three worlds) / तम (darkness) / भागा (fled)
ramacharitamanas::1385.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1385.essence: True power can live in a form that seems small.
ramacharitamanas::1385.simple_meaning: Great power can hide in a small form. Agastya is tiny compared with the ocean, yet he drank it dry. The sun looks small, yet its rise ends darkness everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::1385.simple_insight: What looks small can still be stronger than what looks vast.
ramacharitamanas::1385.detailed_meaning: The sages and kings are still circling the wonder of Shiva’s bow and the bridegroom’s worth. Tulsidas pauses to remind the reader that size means nothing: Agastya humbled the ocean, and the sun’s rise wipes out darkness across the worlds.
ramacharitamanas::1385.modern_relevance: A quiet person walks into the room with no show at all, then says one sentence that changes everything. The room was measuring appearances; reality was never doing that.
ramacharitamanas::1385.insight: It shifts attention from outward scale to actual power and effect.

ramacharitamanas::1386.verse_sanskrit: मंत्र परम लघु जासु बस बिधि हरि हर सुर सर्ब। महामत्त गजराज कहुँ बस कर अंकुस खर्ब ॥
ramacharitamanas::1386.verse_hindi: जिसके वश में ब्रह्मा, विष्णु, शिव और सभी देवता हैं, वह मंत्र अत्यन्त छोटा होता है। महान मतवाले गजराज को छोटा सा अंकुश वश में कर लेता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1386.english_translation: The highest mantra is very small. Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, and all radiant beings are controlled by it. A tiny goad controls a mighty intoxicated elephant.
ramacharitamanas::1386.translation_literal: मंत्र (mantra) / परम (highest) / लघु (small) / जासु (whose) / बस (under control) / बिधि (Brahma) / हरि (Vishnu) / हर (Shiva) / सुर (radiant beings) / सर्ब (all) / महामत्त (greatly intoxicated) / गजराज (king elephant) / कहुँ (for) / बस (control) / कर (hand) / अंकुस (goad) / खर्ब (small)
ramacharitamanas::1386.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1386.essence: The smallest tool can master the greatest force.
ramacharitamanas::1386.simple_meaning: A mantra may look tiny, yet it can hold immense power. Even the greatest beings and the strongest forces can be guided by something small and precise.
ramacharitamanas::1386.simple_insight: Size is not the measure of power. What matters is the force hidden inside the right form.
ramacharitamanas::1386.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the sages and women are explaining why a divine task can be accomplished by something that seems too small to matter. The verse compares a mantra to a goad: brief, sharp, and able to guide even the strongest elephant.
ramacharitamanas::1386.modern_relevance: A few calm words from a mentor can stop a room full of panic. A short reminder on your phone can redirect an entire day. Small, well-placed guidance often does what force cannot.
ramacharitamanas::1386.insight: It shifts attention from visible size to hidden efficacy: the right phrase, practice, or instruction can steer overwhelming power.

ramacharitamanas::1387.verse_sanskrit: काम कुसुम धनु सायक लीन्हे। सकल भुवन अपनें बस कीन्हे॥ देबि तजिअ संसउ अस जानी। भंजब धनुषु राम सुनु रानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1387.verse_hindi: कामदेव ने फूलों का ही धनुष-बाण लेकर समस्त लोकों को अपने वश में कर रखा है। हे देवी! ऐसा जानकर संदेह त्याग दीजिए। हे रानी! सुनिए, रामचन्द्रजी धनुष को अवश्य ही तोड़ेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1387.english_translation: Kama, the flower-bow wielder, has already brought all worlds under control. O queen, cast away doubt. Listen, Ram will surely break the bow.
ramacharitamanas::1387.translation_literal: काम (desire) / कुसुम (flower) / धनु (bow) / सायक (arrow) / लीन्हे (took) / सकल (all) / भुवन (worlds) / अपनें (own) / बस (control) / कीन्हे (made) / देबि (O queen) / तजिअ (give up) / संसउ (doubt) / अस (thus) / जानी (knowing) / भंजब (will break) / धनुषु (bow) / राम (Ram) / सुनु (listen) / रानी (queen)
ramacharitamanas::1387.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1387.essence: Doubt falls when trust sees the outcome clearly.
ramacharitamanas::1387.simple_meaning: The speaker says even desire has conquered the world, so the queen should drop her doubt. Ram will certainly break the bow.
ramacharitamanas::1387.simple_insight: Confidence can arrive before proof. Doubt softens when trust sees what fear cannot.
ramacharitamanas::1387.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, the contest bow stands before the assembled kings. A speaker reassures Queen Sunaina that even desire can rule the world, so Ram’s victory is not in question. This verse builds the queen’s confidence before the bow is lifted.
ramacharitamanas::1387.modern_relevance: You are staring at the final interview round, and everyone else seems larger than life. One calm voice says, 'Stop doubting. The one you’re rooting for can do this.'
ramacharitamanas::1387.insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to trust in the strength already present.

ramacharitamanas::1388.verse_sanskrit: सखी बचन सुनि भै परतीती। मिटा बिषादु बढ़ी अति प्रीती॥ तब रामहि बिलोकि बैदेही। सभय हृदयँ बिनवति जेहि तेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1388.verse_hindi: सखी के वचन सुनकर रानी को (श्री रामजी के सामर्थ्य के संबंध में) विश्वास हो गया। उनकी उदासी मिट गई और श्री रामजी के प्रति उनका प्रेम अत्यन्त बढ़ गया। उस समय श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर सीताजी भयभीत हृदय से जिस-तिस (देवता) से विनती कर रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1388.english_translation: Hearing her companion's words, she gained faith. Her sorrow faded and her love for Ram grew greatly. Then, seeing Ram, Vaidehi prayed in fear to one and another with a trembling heart.
ramacharitamanas::1388.translation_literal: सखी (companion) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / भै (became) / परतीती (faith) / मिटा (was removed) / बिषादु (sorrow) / बढ़ी (grew) / अति (very) / प्रीती (love) / तब (then) / रामहि (to Ram) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बैदेही (Vaidehi) / सभय (fearful) / हृदयँ (with heart) / बिनवति (prays) / जेहि तेही (to one and another)
ramacharitamanas::1388.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1388.essence: Trust arrives first; fear lingers, but love already deepens.
ramacharitamanas::1388.simple_meaning: Sita hears her companion, believes Ram's power, and her sorrow falls away. Seeing Ram, she feels afraid and starts praying in her heart to anyone who might help.
ramacharitamanas::1388.simple_insight: Faith can quiet sorrow before the moment is fully safe.
ramacharitamanas::1388.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Sita has just heard a companion explain Ram's strength. Her doubt breaks, her sadness lifts, and love rushes in. But when she finally sees Ram, her heart still trembles, and she begins praying inwardly for protection.
ramacharitamanas::1388.modern_relevance: A friend sends one voice note and suddenly your panic eases. You still don't know what will happen, but something in you trusts again and can breathe.
ramacharitamanas::1388.insight: It shifts the mind from doubt and grief toward trusting love, even before certainty arrives.

ramacharitamanas::1389.verse_sanskrit: मनहीं मन मनाव अकुलानी। होहु प्रसन्न महेस भवानी॥ करहु सफल आपनि सेवकाई। करि हितु हरहु चाप गरुआई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1389.verse_hindi: वे व्याकुल होकर मन ही मन मना रही हैं- हे महेश-भवानी! मुझ पर प्रसन्न होइए, मैंने आपकी जो सेवा की है, उसे सुफल कीजिए और मुझ पर स्नेह करके धनुष के भारीपन को हर लीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1389.english_translation: She pleaded inwardly in distress: “O Mahesh and Bhavani, be pleased with me. Make my service fruitful, and out of compassion remove the heaviness of the bow.”
ramacharitamanas::1389.translation_literal: मनहीं मन (within the mind) / मनाव (she pleads) / अकुलानी (distressed) / होहु (be) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / महेस (Mahesh) / भवानी (Bhavani) / करहु (make) / सफल (fruitful) / आपनि (your own) / सेवकाई (service) / करि (doing) / हितु (kindness) / हरहु (remove) / चाप (bow) / गरुआई (heaviness)
ramacharitamanas::1389.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1389.essence: Devotion asks for help without losing dignity.
ramacharitamanas::1389.simple_meaning: Sita prays inwardly to Shiva and Parvati, asking them to bless her service and lighten the bow.
ramacharitamanas::1389.simple_insight: When pressure rises, devotion becomes a quiet plea for help, not a demand for control.
ramacharitamanas::1389.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s swayamvar, Sita watches Ram and the impossible bow. Her heart turns inward in anxiety, and she silently appeals to Mahesh and Bhavani, asking that her long service bear fruit by easing the bow’s weight.
ramacharitamanas::1389.modern_relevance: You stand in a crowded hall, watching someone you care about struggle under a burden you cannot lift. All you can do is pray, soften inwardly, and hope grace makes room.
ramacharitamanas::1389.insight: It shifts the mind from anxious strain to humble request for grace.

ramacharitamanas::1390.verse_sanskrit: गननायक बरदायक देवा। आजु लगें कीन्हिउँ तुअ सेवा॥ बार बार बिनती सुनि मोरी। करहु चाप गुरुता अति थोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1390.verse_hindi: हे गणों के नायक, वर देने वाले देवता गणेशजी! मैंने आज ही के लिए तुम्हारी सेवा की थी। बार-बार मेरी विनती सुनकर धनुष का भारीपन बहुत ही कम कर दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1390.english_translation: O leader of the ganas, giver of boons, divine Ganesh, I have served you for this very day. Hear my repeated plea and make the great weight of the bow very light.
ramacharitamanas::1390.translation_literal: गननायक (leader of the ganas) / बरदायक (giver of boons) / देवा (divine one) / आजु लगें (until today) / कीन्हिउँ (I have done) / तुअ (your) / सेवा (service) / बार बार (again and again) / बिनती (plea) / सुनि (hearing) / मोरी (my) / करहु (do) / चाप (bow) / गुरुता (heaviness) / अति (very) / थोरी (little)
ramacharitamanas::1390.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::1390.essence: Devotion asks for help without arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::1390.simple_meaning: Sita prays to Ganesh, reminding him of her devotion and asking him to lessen the bow's weight so she can succeed.
ramacharitamanas::1390.simple_insight: A sincere plea can come from trust, not force.
ramacharitamanas::1390.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, Sita stands before Shiva’s great bow and silently appeals to Ganesh, the remover of obstacles. After her earlier prayers to Shiva and Parvati, she now asks for help in the final moment before Ram’s test.
ramacharitamanas::1390.modern_relevance: You have done everything you could, and the last step still feels impossible. In that moment, prayer can be the calm request that steadies your hands.
ramacharitamanas::1390.insight: It shifts the mind from self-pressure to humble asking for help.

ramacharitamanas::1391.verse_sanskrit: देखि देखि रघुबीर तन सुर मनाव धरि धीर। भरे बिलोचन प्रेम जल पुलकावली सरीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::1391.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी की ओर देख-देखकर सीताजी धीरज धरकर देवताओं को मना रही हैं। उनके नेत्रों में प्रेम के आँसू भरे हैं और शरीर में रोमांच हो रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1391.english_translation: Sita keeps looking at Raghubir and, with steady mind, pleads with the radiant beings. Her eyes brim with tears of love, and her body shivers with delight.
ramacharitamanas::1391.translation_literal: देखि देखि (seeing again and again) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / तन (body) / सुर (radiant beings) / मनाव (appeals, pleads) / धरि (holding) / धीर (steadiness) / भरे (filled) / बिलोचन (eyes) / प्रेम (love) / जल (water) / पुलकावली (hairs standing on end) / सरीर (body)
ramacharitamanas::1391.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1391.essence: True devotion stays composed even while it overflows.
ramacharitamanas::1391.simple_meaning: Sita keeps looking at Ram with steady composure while her eyes fill with tears and her body shivers with love.
ramacharitamanas::1391.simple_insight: Love can be overwhelming and still deeply steady.
ramacharitamanas::1391.detailed_meaning: At the swayamvar, Sita stands before Ram and the impossible bow. She keeps glancing at him, trying to steady herself while the emotion in her body gives her away. This verse shows her inner devotion before the decisive moment.
ramacharitamanas::1391.modern_relevance: You spot someone across a crowded room and try to stay composed, but your face and body already know what your mind is hiding.
ramacharitamanas::1391.insight: It shows devotion as both restraint and overflow: the heart stays steady while the body reveals the truth.

ramacharitamanas::1392.verse_sanskrit: नीकें निरखि नयन भरि सोभा। पितु पनु सुमिरि बहुरि मनु छोभा॥ अहह तात दारुनि हठ ठानी। समुझत नहिं कछु लाभु न हानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1392.verse_hindi: अच्छी तरह नेत्र भरकर श्री रामजी की शोभा देखकर, फिर पिता के प्रण का स्मरण करके सीताजी का मन क्षुब्ध हो उठा। (वे मन ही मन कहने लगीं-) अहो! पिताजी ने बड़ा ही कठिन हठ ठाना है, वे लाभ-हानि कुछ भी नहीं समझ रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1392.english_translation: Looking closely and filling her eyes with Ram's beauty, Sita remembered her father's vow and became troubled again. "Ah, father has taken a harsh and stubborn stand. He does not see gain or loss at all."
ramacharitamanas::1392.translation_literal: नीकें (well) / निरखि (having looked) / नयन भरि (filling the eyes) / सोभा (beauty) / पितु पनु (father's vow) / सुमिरि (remembering) / बहुरि (again) / मनु (mind) / छोभा (troubled) / अहह (ah) / तात (father) / दारुनि (harsh) / हठ (stubborn resolve) / ठानी (has taken) / समुझत (understanding) / नहिं (not) / कछु (any) / लाभु (gain) / न (not) / हानी (loss)
ramacharitamanas::1392.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::1392.essence: Beauty can awaken joy and grief in the same breath.
ramacharitamanas::1392.simple_meaning: Sita sees Ram's beauty, then remembers her father's promise and feels torn again. She sees that her father is holding to a hard decision without weighing the cost.
ramacharitamanas::1392.simple_insight: Love can be clear-eyed and wounded at once; seeing the truth does not always stop the ache.
ramacharitamanas::1392.detailed_meaning: At the swayamvar, Sita has already fallen into Ram's beauty. Then memory returns: her father Janak's vow has set the whole scene in motion, and that vow now feels severe. Her heart wavers between delight and sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::1392.modern_relevance: You finally see the person you love across the room, and then the family rule, the timing, the old promise, all rush back. The heart knows one thing; the situation says another.
ramacharitamanas::1392.insight: It shows how desire, duty, and family obligation can collide in a single mind.

ramacharitamanas::1393.verse_sanskrit: सचिव सभय सिख देइ न कोई। बुध समाज बड़ अनुचित होई॥ कहँ धनु कुलिसहु चाहि कठोरा। कहँ स्यामल मृदुगात किसोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1393.verse_hindi: मंत्री डर रहे हैं, इसलिए कोई उन्हें सीख भी नहीं देता, पंडितों की सभा में यह बड़ा अनुचित हो रहा है। कहाँ तो वज्र से भी बढ़कर कठोर धनुष और कहाँ ये कोमल शरीर किशोर श्यामसुंदर! ॥
ramacharitamanas::1393.english_translation: The ministers are afraid, so no one dares to advise. In the assembly of scholars, this is deeply improper. Where is a bow, hard as thunderbolt, and where is this dark, tender-bodied youth?
ramacharitamanas::1393.translation_literal: सचिव (ministers) / सभय (fearful) / सिख (advice) / देइ (give) / न (not) / कोई (anyone) । / बुध (wise) / समाज (assembly) / बड़ (very) / अनुचित (improper) / होई (is) ॥ / कहँ (where) / धनु (bow) / कुलिसहु (even thunderbolt) / चाहि (like) / कठोरा (hard) । / कहँ (where) / स्यामल (dark) / मृदुगात (soft-bodied) / किसोरा (youth) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1393.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1393.essence: The court sees a gentle youth and an impossible bow.
ramacharitamanas::1393.simple_meaning: The court is too frightened to speak honestly. The contrast between the hard bow and Ram's tender youth makes the marriage demand seem impossible.
ramacharitamanas::1393.simple_insight: Sometimes the mind freezes before a demand that feels too large to hold.
ramacharitamanas::1393.detailed_meaning: In Janak's assembly, the ministers and scholars see Ram's gentle youth and the terrifyingly hard bow set before him. No one dares speak plainly. This verse deepens the court's collective doubt before Sita's swayamvar turns toward crisis.
ramacharitamanas::1393.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when the task feels absurdly beyond the person in front of it. Everyone senses the mismatch, but no one wants to say it aloud.
ramacharitamanas::1393.insight: It frames the scene as social hesitation before an impossible challenge, sharpening the tension that follows.

ramacharitamanas::1394.verse_sanskrit: बिधि केहि भाँति धरौं उर धीरा। सिरस सुमन कन बेधिअ हीरा॥ सकल सभा कै मति भै भोरी। अब मोहि संभुचाप गति तोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1394.verse_hindi: हे विधाता! मैं हृदय में किस तरह धीरज धरूँ, सिरस के फूल के कण से कहीं हीरा छेदा जाता है। सारी सभा की बुद्धि भोली (बावली) हो गई है, अतः हे शिवजी के धनुष! अब तो मुझे तुम्हारा ही आसरा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1394.english_translation: O Fate, how can I keep my heart steady? A lotus stalk can pierce a diamond. The whole assembly has gone mad, so now, O Shiva's bow, you alone are my support.
ramacharitamanas::1394.translation_literal: बिधि (fate) / केहि भाँति (in what way) / धरौं (I hold) / उर (in heart) / धीरा (steadiness) / सिरस सुमन (lotus flower) / कन (particle) / बेधिअ (pierce) / हीरा (diamond) / सकल (entire) / सभा (assembly) / कै (of) / मति (mind) / भै (became) / भोरी (deluded) / अब (now) / मोहि (to me) / संभुचाप (Shiva's bow) / गति (support/refuge) / तोरी (your)
ramacharitamanas::1394.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::1394.essence: Impossible pressure makes the heart seek one true support.
ramacharitamanas::1394.simple_meaning: Sita feels overwhelmed by the impossible task before her. The court has lost its sense, and she turns to Shiva's bow as the only remaining support.
ramacharitamanas::1394.simple_insight: When everything around you feels impossible, the mind looks for one steady anchor.
ramacharitamanas::1394.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, Sita has just seen Ram's gentle form and then remembered the vow tied to the bow contest. The assembly is confused, and the task seems impossible. In that pressure, she turns inward and calls on fate and Shiva's bow.
ramacharitamanas::1394.modern_relevance: You are standing in front of a task that feels absurdly beyond reach: the deadline, the exam, the conversation you cannot control. In that moment, panic shrinks when you find one solid thing to hold.
ramacharitamanas::1394.insight: It shifts the mind from confusion to refuge, showing that steadiness can come from surrendering to one clear support.

ramacharitamanas::1395.verse_sanskrit: निज जड़ता लोगन्ह पर डारी। होहि हरुअ रघुपतिहि निहारी॥ अति परिताप सीय मन माहीं। लव निमेष जुग सय सम जाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1395.verse_hindi: तुम अपनी जड़ता लोगों पर डालकर, श्री रघुनाथजी (के सुकुमार शरीर) को देखकर (उतने ही) हल्के हो जाओ। इस प्रकार सीताजी के मन में बड़ा ही संताप हो रहा है। निमेष का एक लव (अंश) भी सौ युगों के समान बीत रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1395.english_translation: Cast your heaviness onto others and become light by beholding Raghupati. Sita's heart burns with intense anguish; even a fraction of a blink feels like hundreds of ages.
ramacharitamanas::1395.translation_literal: निज (one's own) / जड़ता (heaviness, dullness) / लोगन्ह (on the people) / डारी (cast) / होहि (become) / हरुअ (light) / रघुपतिहि (Raghupati) / निहारी (beholding) / अति (very) / परिताप (pain, anguish) / सीय (Sita) / मन (mind, heart) / माहीं (in) / लव (a blink's fraction) / निमेष (blink) / जुग (ages) / सय (hundreds) / सम (like) / जाहीं (go)
ramacharitamanas::1395.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1395.essence: Longing makes a blink feel like ages.
ramacharitamanas::1395.simple_meaning: Sita feels unbearable pain while looking at Ram. Even a tiny moment apart from him feels endlessly long.
ramacharitamanas::1395.simple_insight: Love changes time itself: a moment stretches when the heart is aching.
ramacharitamanas::1395.detailed_meaning: In Mithila's assembly, Sita has just seen Ram after the bow-breaking contest. Her heart is overwhelmed, and the poet shows how longing distorts time: a blink feels like centuries while she tries to hold herself steady before him.
ramacharitamanas::1395.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after sending one message that matters too much. The minutes crawl, and every silence feels louder than it should.
ramacharitamanas::1395.insight: It shifts attention from outer time to inner longing, showing how desire can make a moment feel infinite.

ramacharitamanas::1396.verse_sanskrit: प्रभुहि चितइ पुनि चितव महि राजत लोचन लोल। खेलत मनसिज मीन जुग जनु बिधु मंडल डोल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1396.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर फिर पृथ्वी की ओर देखती हुई सीताजी के चंचल नेत्र इस प्रकार शोभित हो रहे हैं, मानो चन्द्रमंडल रूपी डोल में कामदेव की दो मछलियाँ खेल रही हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1396.english_translation: Looking at Lord Ram and then glancing down at the ground, Sita's restless eyes shine like two fish of desire playing in the moonlike bowl of her gaze.
ramacharitamanas::1396.translation_literal: प्रभुहि (the Lord) / चितइ (having looked at) / पुनि (again) / चितव (looks) / महि (toward the ground) / राजत (shining) / लोचन (eyes) / लोल (restless) / खेलत (playing) / मनसिज (of desire) / मीन (fish) / जुग (pair) / जनु (as if) / बिधु (moon) / मंडल (circle/bowl) / डोल (swinging bowl)
ramacharitamanas::1396.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1396.essence: Shy love speaks first through the eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1396.simple_meaning: Sita glances at Ram, then lowers her eyes in shy longing. Her restless eyes are compared to playful fish moving in a moonlike bowl.
ramacharitamanas::1396.simple_insight: Love can make even silence and lowered eyes feel vivid.
ramacharitamanas::1396.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Sita has just seen Ram at the swayamvar. She cannot speak openly, so her eyes do the talking: they rise toward him, then fall in shy restraint. Tulsidas lingers on that charged, wordless moment.
ramacharitamanas::1396.modern_relevance: You catch someone's eyes across a crowded room, then look away too quickly. Nothing is said, but the whole moment changes shape.
ramacharitamanas::1396.insight: It trains attention on the body’s quiet signals of longing and restraint.

ramacharitamanas::1397.verse_sanskrit: गिरा अलिनि मुख पंकज रोकी। प्रगट न लाज निसा अवलोकी॥ लोचन जलु रह लोचन कोना। जैसें परम कृपन कर सोना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1397.verse_hindi: सीताजी की वाणी रूपी भ्रमरी को उनके मुख रूपी कमल ने रोक रखा है। लाज रूपी रात्रि को देखकर वह प्रकट नहीं हो रही है। नेत्रों का जल नेत्रों के कोने (कोये) में ही रह जाता है। जैसे बड़े भारी कंजूस का सोना कोने में ही गड़ा रह जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1397.english_translation: Sita's speech stays back like a bee held by a lotus. Shame stands like night before her, so her words do not appear. Tears remain in the corners of her eyes, like gold hoarded by a miser.
ramacharitamanas::1397.translation_literal: गिरा (speech) / अलिनि (bee) / मुख पंकज (lotus-face) / रोकी (held back) / प्रगट न (does not appear) / लाज (shame) / निसा (night) / अवलोकी (seeing) / लोचन जलु (tears) / रह (remains) / लोचन कोना (corner of the eyes) / जैसें (just as) / परम कृपन (very miserly) / कर (hand) / सोना (gold)
ramacharitamanas::1397.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1397.essence: Deep feeling can silence speech and hide tears.
ramacharitamanas::1397.simple_meaning: Sita is so overwhelmed by seeing Ram that her words stop, her shame deepens, and tears stay hidden in her eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1397.simple_insight: Some feelings are too full for speech; devotion can make silence more honest than words.
ramacharitamanas::1397.detailed_meaning: Sita has just seen Ram at the swayamvar. Her heart is flooded, but her shyness and longing hold her back. Tulsidas compares her speech to a bee trapped at a lotus and her tears to hidden gold, showing how devotion can become quiet, trembling, and wordless.
ramacharitamanas::1397.modern_relevance: You open a message from someone you care about deeply, then stare at it for a minute before typing anything. The feeling is too real, and your words arrive late.
ramacharitamanas::1397.insight: It shifts attention from spoken response to the inner pressure that makes silence meaningful.

ramacharitamanas::1398.verse_sanskrit: सकुची ब्याकुलता बड़ि जानी। धरि धींरजु प्रतीति उर आनी॥ तन मन बचन मोर पनु साचा। रघुपति पद सरोज चितु राचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1398.verse_hindi: अपनी बढ़ी हुई व्याकुलता जानकर सीताजी सकुचा गईं और धीरज धरकर हृदय में विश्वास ले आईं कि यदि तन, मन और वचन से मेरा प्रण सच्चा है और श्री रघुनाथजी के चरण कमलों में मेरा चित्त वास्तव में अनुरक्त है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1398.english_translation: Realising the depth of her agitation, Sita steadied herself and brought trust into her heart: if my vow in body, mind, and speech is true, and my mind truly rests at the lotus feet of Raghupati, ...
ramacharitamanas::1398.translation_literal: सकुची (having become shy/embarrassed) / ब्याकुलता (agitation) / बड़ि (great) / जानी (known) / धरि (holding) / धींरजु (patience/steadiness) / प्रतीति (trust) / उर (in the heart) / आनी (brought) / तन (body) / मन (mind) / बचन (speech) / मोर (my) / पनु (vow) / साचा (true) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu) / पद (feet) / सरोज (lotus) / चितु (mind) / राचा (absorbed)
ramacharitamanas::1398.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::1398.essence: Steady trust turns agitation into hope.
ramacharitamanas::1398.simple_meaning: Sita gathers herself, steadies her heart, and trusts that her vow is true: body, mind, and speech are fixed on Ram’s lotus feet.
ramacharitamanas::1398.simple_insight: Trust can quiet agitation and restore inner steadiness when longing feels overwhelming.
ramacharitamanas::1398.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-Ram sighting at Mithila, Sita feels her longing rising too strongly. She checks herself, regains composure, and turns inward to trust. Her private vow becomes the basis for hope that Ram will answer her devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1398.modern_relevance: You reread the message for the tenth time before sending it, heart racing. Then you stop, breathe, and remember what you already know is true.
ramacharitamanas::1398.insight: It shifts attention from emotional panic to the steadiness of a vow kept honestly.

ramacharitamanas::1399.verse_sanskrit: तौ भगवानु सकल उर बासी। करिहि मोहि रघुबर कै दासी॥ जेहि कें जेहि पर सत्य सनेहू। सो तेहि मिलइ न कछु संदेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1399.verse_hindi: तो सबके हृदय में निवास करने वाले भगवान मुझे रघुश्रेष्ठ श्री रामचन्द्रजी की दासी अवश्य बनाएँगे। जिसका जिस पर सच्चा स्नेह होता है, वह उसे मिलता ही है, इसमें कुछ भी संदेह नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1399.english_translation: Then the divine one who lives in every heart will surely make me the servant of Raghubar. Whoever holds true love for someone will surely meet that beloved, without doubt.
ramacharitamanas::1399.translation_literal: तौ (then) / भगवानु (the divine one) / सकल (all) / उर (heart) / बासी (dwelling) / करिहि (will make) / मोहि (me) / रघुबर कै (of Raghubar's) / दासी (servant)॥ / जेहि कें (for whom) / जेहि पर (toward whom) / सत्य (true) / सनेहू (love) / सो (that one) / तेहि (to that one) / मिलइ (meets) / न (not) / कछु (any) / संदेहू (doubt)॥
ramacharitamanas::1399.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::1399.essence: True love does not remain unanswered; it draws the beloved near.
ramacharitamanas::1399.simple_meaning: Sita trusts that sincere love never fails. Because her love is true, she believes Ram will surely make her his own devotee.
ramacharitamanas::1399.simple_insight: Love is not wasted when it is real. It creates a bond that life itself cannot undo.
ramacharitamanas::1399.detailed_meaning: In Janak's assembly, Sita has just steadied her heart before the bow. She tells herself that the divine one who lives in every heart will surely make her Ram's servant, because true love never goes unanswered.
ramacharitamanas::1399.modern_relevance: You send one honest message and wait, unsure whether it will land. This verse says real love is never random noise; it has a way of finding the heart it belongs to.
ramacharitamanas::1399.insight: It shifts the mind from fear of rejection to trust in the power of sincere love.

ramacharitamanas::1400.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु तन चितइ प्रेम तन ठाना। कृपानिधान राम सबु जाना॥ सियहि बिलोकि तकेउ धनु कैसें। चितव गरुरु लघु ब्यालहि जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1400.verse_hindi: प्रभु की ओर देखकर सीताजी ने शरीर के द्वारा प्रेम ठान लिया (अर्थात् यह निश्चय कर लिया कि यह शरीर इन्हीं का होकर रहेगा या रहेगा ही नहीं) कृपानिधान श्री रामजी सब जान गए। उन्होंने सीताजी को देखकर धनुष की ओर कैसे ताका, जैसे गरुड़जी छोटे से साँप की ओर देखते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1400.english_translation: Sita looked toward the Lord and resolved with her whole body in love. Compassionate Ram understood everything. Seeing Sita, he looked at the bow as Garuda looks at a small snake.
ramacharitamanas::1400.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / तन (body) / चितइ (looking) / प्रेम (love) / तन (body) / ठाना (resolved) / कृपानिधान (treasure of compassion) / राम (Ram) / सबु (everything) / जाना (knew)॥ / सियहि (Sita) / बिलोकि (seeing) / तकेउ (looked at) / धनु (bow) / कैसें (how) / चितव (looked) / गरुरु (Garuda) / लघु (small) / ब्यालहि (snake) / जैसें (as)॥
ramacharitamanas::1400.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1400.essence: True devotion is seen before it is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1400.simple_meaning: Sita looks at Ram and silently commits herself to him with her whole being. Ram understands her heart at once and then looks toward the bow with calm certainty.
ramacharitamanas::1400.simple_insight: Love does not need long explanations. The heart can be seen before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1400.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, Sita has already made her inward choice. She stands before Ram with steady devotion, and Ram instantly recognises her resolve. His glance shifts to the bow, showing the fearless calm that will soon break the contest.
ramacharitamanas::1400.modern_relevance: In a room where everyone is pretending to be composed, one person’s eyes reveal everything. You feel the shift before any announcement is made: the decision has already happened inside.
ramacharitamanas::1400.insight: It teaches you to recognise the moment when inward commitment becomes outward action.

ramacharitamanas::1401.verse_sanskrit: लखन लखेउ रघुबंसमनि ताकेउ हर कोदंडु। पुलकि गात बोले बचन चरन चापि ब्रह्मांडु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1401.verse_hindi: इधर जब लक्ष्मणजी ने देखा कि रघुकुल मणि श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने शिवजी के धनुष की ओर ताका है, तो वे शरीर से पुलकित हो ब्रह्माण्ड को चरणों से दबाकर निम्नलिखित वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1401.english_translation: When Lakshman saw the Lord of Raghu glance toward Shiva’s bow, his body thrilled with joy, and he spoke, pressing the universe beneath his feet.
ramacharitamanas::1401.translation_literal: लखन (Lakshman) / लखेउ (saw) / रघुबंसमनि (jewel of the Raghu line) / ताकेउ (looked toward) / हर (Shiva) / कोदंडु (bow) / पुलकि (with thrill) / गात (body) / बोले (spoke) / बचन (words) / चरन (feet) / चापि (pressing down) / ब्रह्मांडु (the universe)
ramacharitamanas::1401.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1401.essence: Joy rises before the bow is even lifted.
ramacharitamanas::1401.simple_meaning: Lakshman sees Ram looking at Shiva’s bow and feels intense joy. He speaks with such devotion that the verse pictures him pressing the universe under his feet.
ramacharitamanas::1401.simple_insight: Pure devotion can make even a small moment feel cosmic.
ramacharitamanas::1401.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the swayamvar has reached its decisive moment. Ram looks toward Shiva’s bow, and Lakshman, watching beside him, overflows with excitement. His words prepare the ground for Ram to act.
ramacharitamanas::1401.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love step toward the one thing they were made to do, and your whole body goes alert. That is Lakshman here — joy before the action even begins.
ramacharitamanas::1401.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the devotional energy surrounding it.

ramacharitamanas::1402.verse_sanskrit: दिसिकुंजरहु कमठ अहि कोला। धरहु धरनि धरि धीर न डोला॥ रामु चहहिं संकर धनु तोरा। होहु सजग सुनि आयसु मोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1402.verse_hindi: हे दिग्गजो! हे कच्छप! हे शेष! हे वाराह! धीरज धरकर पृथ्वी को थामे रहो, जिससे यह हिलने न पावे। श्री रामचन्द्रजी शिवजी के धनुष को तोड़ना चाहते हैं। मेरी आज्ञा सुनकर सब सावधान हो जाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1402.english_translation: O elephants of the directions, tortoise, serpent, boar, hold up the earth steadily so it does not tremble. Ram wants to break Shiva's bow. Hearing my command, be alert.
ramacharitamanas::1402.translation_literal: दिसिकुंजरहु (O elephants of the directions) / कमठ (tortoise) / अहि (serpent) / कोला (boar) / धरहु (hold) / धरनि (the earth) / धरि (holding) / धीर (steadily) / न डोला (does not shake) / रामु (Ram) / चहहिं (want) / संकर (Shiva's) / धनु (bow) / तोरा (to break) / होहु (be) / सजग (alert) / सुनि (hearing) / आयसु (command) / मोरा (my)
ramacharitamanas::1402.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1402.essence: The next action is so vast that even the earth must steady itself.
ramacharitamanas::1402.simple_meaning: The scene is so intense that the speaker calls on cosmic beings to steady the earth while Ram prepares to break Shiva's bow.
ramacharitamanas::1402.simple_insight: Great moments make the whole world feel like it is holding its breath.
ramacharitamanas::1402.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the hall is tense as Ram steps toward Shiva's bow. The speaker imagines cosmic supports beneath the earth, then orders everyone to stay alert, because the decisive moment is about to begin.
ramacharitamanas::1402.modern_relevance: In a room before a final announcement, everyone goes quiet and even small movements feel loud. A single action is about to change everything.
ramacharitamanas::1402.insight: It turns a private act into a world-shifting moment, heightening the sense of sacred anticipation.

ramacharitamanas::1403.verse_sanskrit: चाप समीप रामु जब आए। नर नारिन्ह सुर सुकृत मनाए॥ सब कर संसउ अरु अग्यानू। मंद महीपन्ह कर अभिमानू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1403.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी जब धनुष के समीप आए, तब सब स्त्री-पुरुषों ने देवताओं और पुण्यों को मनाया। सबका संदेह और अज्ञान, नीच राजाओं का अभिमान, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1403.english_translation: When Ram came near the bow, men and women remembered the gods and their good deeds. Doubt and ignorance vanished; the pride of petty kings remained.
ramacharitamanas::1403.translation_literal: चाप (bow) / समीप (near) / रामु (Ram) / जब (when) / आए (came) / नर (men) / नारिन्ह (women) / सुर (radiant beings, gods) / सुकृत (good deeds, merit) / मनाए (remembered) / सब (all) / कर (of) / संसउ (doubt) / अरु (and) / अग्यानू (ignorance) / मंद (lowly) / महीपन्ह (kings) / कर (of) / अभिमानू (pride)
ramacharitamanas::1403.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1403.essence: True presence dissolves doubt and exposes pride.
ramacharitamanas::1403.simple_meaning: Ram's arrival near the bow changes the whole atmosphere. People feel reverence, while doubt, ignorance, and pride are exposed.
ramacharitamanas::1403.simple_insight: Presence can quiet confusion and reveal what was hiding underneath.
ramacharitamanas::1403.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, Ram steps toward Shiva's bow and the room shifts. Men and women feel reverence; doubt and ignorance weaken; proud kings stand exposed. This verse shows the emotional turning point before the bow-breaking moment.
ramacharitamanas::1403.modern_relevance: A room goes silent when the person everyone has been waiting for finally walks in. The nervous chatter drops away, and the people trying to look important suddenly feel small.
ramacharitamanas::1403.insight: It shifts attention from social performance to the force of real presence.

ramacharitamanas::1404.verse_sanskrit: भृगुपति केरि गरब गरुआई। सुर मुनिबरन्ह केरि कदराई॥ सिय कर सोचु जनक पछितावा। रानिन्ह कर दारुन दुख दावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1404.verse_hindi: परशुरामजी के गर्व की गुरुता, देवता और श्रेष्ठ मुनियों की कातरता (भय), सीताजी का सोच, जनक का पश्चाताप और रानियों के दारुण दुःख का दावानल, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1404.english_translation: Parashurama's pride, the fear of the gods and great sages, Sita's worry, Janaka's regret, and the royal women’s terrible suffering all flared up together.
ramacharitamanas::1404.translation_literal: भृगुपति केरि (of the lord of Bhrigu, Parashurama) / गरब (pride) / गरुआई (heaviness, intensity) / सुर (devas, radiant beings) / मुनिबरन्ह (great sages) / केरि (of) / कदराई (fear, anxious cry) / सिय (Sita) / कर (of) / सोचु (worry) / जनक (Janaka) / पछितावा (regret) / रानिन्ह (of the queens) / कर (of) / दारुन (terrible) / दुख (sorrow) / दावा (blaze, wildfire)
ramacharitamanas::1404.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1404.essence: One turning point can expose every hidden fear in the room.
ramacharitamanas::1404.simple_meaning: Parashurama's pride, the sages' fear, Sita's worry, Janaka's regret, and the queens' grief all rose together in one charged moment.
ramacharitamanas::1404.simple_insight: A single public moment can hold many private storms at once.
