ramacharitamanas::1404.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's court, just as Ram stands near Shiva's bow, the room fills with tension. Parashurama's pride, the sages' fear, Sita's worry, Janaka's regret, and the queens' grief all surge together before the decisive turning point.
ramacharitamanas::1404.modern_relevance: A wedding hall goes silent after one remark, and suddenly everyone's face tells a different story. One moment can carry pride, fear, hope, and heartbreak at once.
ramacharitamanas::1404.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the hidden emotions it exposes in everyone present.

ramacharitamanas::1405.verse_sanskrit: संभुचाप बड़ बोहितु पाई। चढ़े जाइ सब संगु बनाई॥ राम बाहुबल सिंधु अपारू। चहत पारु नहिं कोउ कड़हारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1405.verse_hindi: ये सब शिवजी के धनुष रूपी बड़े जहाज को पाकर, समाज बनाकर उस पर जा चढ़े। ये श्री रामचन्द्रजी की भुजाओं के बल रूपी अपार समुद्र के पार जाना चाहते हैं, परन्तु कोई केवट नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1405.english_translation: They found Shiva's great bow like a large boat and climbed aboard together. They wish to cross the boundless sea of Ram's arm-strength, but there is no boatman.
ramacharitamanas::1405.translation_literal: संभुचाप (Shiva's bow) / बड़ (great) / बोहितु (boat) / पाई (having found) / चढ़े (they climbed) / जाइ (going) / सब (all) / संगु (together) / बनाई (having made a group) / राम (Ram's) / बाहुबल (arm-strength) / सिंधु (sea) / अपारू (boundless) / चहत (wish) / पारु (crossing) / नहिं (not) / कोउ (any) / कड़हारू (boatman)
ramacharitamanas::1405.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1405.essence: Even the finest boat cannot cross Ram's boundless strength alone.
ramacharitamanas::1405.simple_meaning: The people treat Shiva's bow like a boat and gather around it, but Ram's strength is still an ocean no one can cross without help.
ramacharitamanas::1405.simple_insight: Even sacred power can only carry you so far; real crossing needs grace.
ramacharitamanas::1405.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the crowd watches Ram approach Shiva's bow. The bow becomes a symbolic boat, but the deeper truth is that Ram's greatness is still beyond ordinary reach. The verse heightens the tension before the bow is lifted.
ramacharitamanas::1405.modern_relevance: You have the right tools, the right team, and all the confidence in the room — yet the hardest part still feels impossible. Some crossings need more than effort.
ramacharitamanas::1405.insight: It shifts attention from visible supports to the hidden force that actually makes passage possible.

ramacharitamanas::1406.verse_sanskrit: राम बिलोके लोग सब चित्र लिखे से देखि। चितई सीय कृपायतन जानी बिकल बिसेषि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1406.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने सब लोगों की ओर देखा और उन्हें चित्र में लिखे हुए से देखकर फिर कृपाधाम श्री रामजी ने सीताजी की ओर देखा और उन्हें विशेष व्याकुल जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1406.english_translation: Ram looked at everyone as if they were painted figures, then the abode of compassion looked at Sita and saw her especially distressed.
ramacharitamanas::1406.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बिलोके (looked) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / चित्र (picture) / लिखे (drawn) / से (like) / देखि (seeing) / चितई (looked) / सीय (Sita) / कृपायतन (abode of compassion) / जानी (knowing) / बिकल (distressed) / बिसेषि (especially)
ramacharitamanas::1406.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1406.essence: Compassion sees the hidden pain everyone else misses.
ramacharitamanas::1406.simple_meaning: Ram first saw the crowd as still and lifeless, then turned to Sita and understood her deep distress.
ramacharitamanas::1406.simple_insight: A truly loving gaze notices the one person who is suffering most.
ramacharitamanas::1406.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, the hall is full of stunned onlookers after Ram breaks Shiva’s bow. Ram scans the crowd, then turns to Sita and immediately sees her special anguish. The verse sets up the compassion that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1406.modern_relevance: In a crowded room after bad news, everyone may look composed except one person whose face has gone quiet. Real care notices that one person first.
ramacharitamanas::1406.insight: It trains attention toward the most vulnerable person in the room, not the loudest or most visible.

ramacharitamanas::1407.verse_sanskrit: देखी बिपुल बिकल बैदेही। निमिष बिहात कलप सम तेही। तृषित बारि बिनु जो तनु त्यागा। मुएँ करइ का सुधा तड़ागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1407.verse_hindi: उन्होंने जानकीजी को बहुत ही विकल देखा। उनका एक-एक क्षण कल्प के समान बीत रहा था। यदि प्यासा आदमी पानी के बिना शरीर छोड़ दे, तो उसके मर जाने पर अमृत का तालाब भी क्या करेगा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1407.english_translation: He saw Vaidehi deeply distraught. For her, each moment passed like an age. What use is a pool of nectar to one who has died of thirst?
ramacharitamanas::1407.translation_literal: देखी (saw) / बिपुल (greatly) / बिकल (distressed) / बैदेही (Vaidehi) / निमिष (moment) / बिहात (passing) / कलप (an age) / सम (like) / तेही (for her) / तृषित (thirsty) / बारि (water) / बिनु (without) / जो (who) / तनु (body) / त्यागा (gave up) / मुएँ (after dying) / करइ (does) / का (what) / सुधा (nectar) / तड़ागा (pool)
ramacharitamanas::1407.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1407.essence: Delayed help cannot undo suffering already endured.
ramacharitamanas::1407.simple_meaning: Sita is in such deep pain that every moment feels endless. Relief offered too late cannot help someone who is already overwhelmed by loss.
ramacharitamanas::1407.simple_insight: Some remedies arrive after the heart has already broken open.
ramacharitamanas::1407.detailed_meaning: In the swayamvar hall, Ram sees Sita’s distress after the bow is won and the crowd surges around her. Her suffering is so intense that even a future rescue feels meaningless if it comes too late.
ramacharitamanas::1407.modern_relevance: You finally call back after days of silence, but the hurt was already there in the waiting. Some gestures matter only before the wound deepens.
ramacharitamanas::1407.insight: It shifts attention from delayed comfort to timely care, where presence matters more than repair.

ramacharitamanas::1408.verse_sanskrit: का बरषा सब कृषी सुखानें। समय चुकें पुनि का पछितानें॥ अस जियँ जानि जानकी देखी। प्रभु पुलके लखि प्रीति बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1408.verse_hindi: सारी खेती के सूख जाने पर वर्षा किस काम की? समय बीत जाने पर फिर पछताने से क्या लाभ? जी में ऐसा समझकर श्री रामजी ने जानकीजी की ओर देखा और उनका विशेष प्रेम लखकर वे पुलकित हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1408.english_translation: What use is rain after all the crops have dried? What benefit is regret after the right moment has passed? Knowing this in his heart, Ram looked at Janaki and, seeing her deep love, was filled with delight.
ramacharitamanas::1408.translation_literal: का (what) / बरषा (rain) / सब (all) / कृषी (crops) / सुखानें (after drying) / समय (time, right moment) / चुकें (having missed) / पुनि (again) / का (what) / पछितानें (regret) / अस (thus) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानि (knowing) / जानकी (Janaki) / देखी (saw) / प्रभु (the Lord) / पुलके (was thrilled) / लखि (seeing) / प्रीति (love) / बिसेषी (special)
ramacharitamanas::1408.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1408.essence: Miss the moment, and regret cannot restore it.
ramacharitamanas::1408.simple_meaning: Ram sees Sita's love and feels joy. The verse says that once the right moment has passed, regret cannot help.
ramacharitamanas::1408.simple_insight: Love recognized at the right moment brings joy; missed timing only brings sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::1408.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, Ram sees Janaki's distress and devotion before the bow test begins. He understands that a missed moment cannot be repaired later, and her special love moves him deeply.
ramacharitamanas::1408.modern_relevance: You notice the person you care about is finally open, but hesitation could ruin everything. The verse reminds you that timing matters, and love must be met while it is alive.
ramacharitamanas::1408.insight: It shifts attention from delayed regret to immediate response when a meaningful moment arrives.

ramacharitamanas::1409.verse_sanskrit: गुरहि प्रनामु मनहिं मन कीन्हा। अति लाघवँ उठाइ धनु लीन्हा॥ दमकेउ दामिनि जिमि जब लयऊ। पुनि नभ धनु मंडल सम भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1409.verse_hindi: मन ही मन उन्होंने गुरु को प्रणाम किया और बड़ी फुर्ती से धनुष को उठा लिया। जब उसे (हाथ में) लिया, तब वह धनुष बिजली की तरह चमका और फिर आकाश में मंडल जैसा (मंडलाकार) हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1409.english_translation: He mentally bowed to his teacher and quickly lifted the bow. When he took it in hand, it flashed like lightning, then became like a circle in the sky.
ramacharitamanas::1409.translation_literal: गुरहि (to the teacher) / प्रनामु (bowed) / मनहिं मन (in the mind) / कीन्हा (did) / अति (very) / लाघवँ (lightly, swiftly) / उठाइ (lifting) / धनु (the bow) / लीन्हा (took) / दमकेउ (flashed) / दामिनि (lightning) / जिमि (like) / जब (when) / लयऊ (he took) / पुनि (then) / नभ (sky) / धनु (bow) / मंडल (circle) / सम (like) / भयऊ (became)
ramacharitamanas::1409.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1409.essence: Reverence and readiness make the impossible feel light.
ramacharitamanas::1409.simple_meaning: Ram bows to his teacher in his heart and lifts Shiva’s bow with ease. The bow flashes brilliantly in his hands, showing its power and his speed.
ramacharitamanas::1409.simple_insight: Great strength can look effortless when it comes from complete readiness.
ramacharitamanas::1409.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s court, after Sita has been seen and the bow is brought forward, Ram moves without hesitation. He first honors his teacher inwardly, then lifts the great bow so swiftly that its brilliance and shape seem almost unreal.
ramacharitamanas::1409.modern_relevance: You finally open the heavy file everyone feared, and the task that looked impossible becomes simple in your hands. Calm readiness changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::1409.insight: It shifts attention from the object’s size to the steadiness of the one who handles it.

ramacharitamanas::1410.verse_sanskrit: लेत चढ़ावत खैंचत गाढ़ें। काहुँ न लखा देख सबु ठाढ़ें॥ तेहि छन राम मध्य धनु तोरा। भरे भुवन धुनि घोर कठोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1410.verse_hindi: लेते, चढ़ाते और जोर से खींचते हुए किसी ने नहीं लखा (अर्थात ये तीनों काम इतनी फुर्ती से हुए कि धनुष को कब उठाया, कब चढ़ाया और कब खींचा, इसका किसी को पता नहीं लगा), सबने श्री रामजी को (धनुष खींचे) खड़े देखा। उसी क्षण श्री रामजी ने धनुष को बीच से तोड़ डाला। भयंकर कठोर ध्वनि से (सब) लोक भर गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1410.english_translation: No one saw the lifting, placing, and pulling; everyone saw Ram standing there. In that instant, Ram broke the bow in the middle, and the fierce sound filled all the worlds.
ramacharitamanas::1410.translation_literal: लेत (taking) / चढ़ावत (lifting up) / खैंचत (pulling) / गाढ़ें (forcefully) / काहुँ (by anyone) / न (not) / लखा (seen) / देख (seeing) / सबु (all) / ठाढ़ें (standing) / तेहि छन (that instant) / राम (Ram) / मध्य (middle) / धनु (bow) / तोरा (broke) / भरे (filled) / भुवन (worlds) / धुनि (sound) / घोर (fierce) / कठोरा (hard, harsh)
ramacharitamanas::1410.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1410.essence: True force acts so cleanly that even the effort vanishes.
ramacharitamanas::1410.simple_meaning: Ram broke the bow so quickly that no one saw the action itself, only the result and the thunderous sound.
ramacharitamanas::1410.simple_insight: Some moments happen so completely that effort disappears and only the result remains.
ramacharitamanas::1410.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the assembled kings watch Ram after he has lifted Shiva's bow. The movement is so swift that no one can even track the strain. Then the bow snaps in the middle, shaking the whole gathering.
ramacharitamanas::1410.modern_relevance: You finally make the call, send the message, or cut the knot — and everyone only notices the outcome. The decisive act was over before doubt could catch it.
ramacharitamanas::1410.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic struggle to clean, decisive action.

ramacharitamanas::1411.verse_sanskrit: भे भुवन घोर कठोर रव रबि बाजि तजि मारगु चले। चिक्करहिं दिग्गज डोल महि अहि कोल कूरुम कलमले॥ सुर असुर मुनि कर कान दीन्हें सकल बिकल बिचारहीं। कोदंड खंडेउ राम तुलसी जयति बचन उचारहीं॥
ramacharitamanas::1411.verse_hindi: घोर, कठोर शब्द से (सब) लोक भर गए, सूर्य के घोड़े मार्ग छोड़कर चलने लगे। दिग्गज चिग्घाड़ने लगे, धरती डोलने लगी, शेष, वाराह और कच्छप कलमला उठे। देवता, राक्षस और मुनि कानों पर हाथ रखकर सब व्याकुल होकर विचारने लगे। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं (जब सब को निश्चय हो गया कि) श्री रामजी ने धनुष को तोड़ डाला, तब सब 'श्री रामचन्द्र की जय' बोलने लगे।
ramacharitamanas::1411.english_translation: The worlds filled with a terrible, harsh sound; the sun's horses left the road. The elephant guardians roared, the earth shook, and serpents, boars, and tortoises trembled. Devas, asuras, and sages covered their ears and grew bewildered. Tulsidas says the moment Ram broke the bow, all cried, "Victory to Ram."
ramacharitamanas::1411.translation_literal: भे (became) / भुवन (worlds) / घोर (terrible) / कठोर (harsh) / रव (sound) / रबि (sun) / बाजि (horses) / तजि (leaving) / मारगु (road) / चले (went) / चिक्करहिं (roared) / दिग्गज (elephant guardians) / डोल (shook) / महि (earth) / अहि (serpents) / कोल (boars) / कूरुम (tortoises) / कलमले (trembled) / सुर (devas) / असुर (asuras) / मुनि (sages) / कर (hands) / कान (ears) / दीन्हें (placed) / सकल (all) / बिकल (bewildered) / बिचारहीं (considered) / कोदंड (bow) / खंडेउ (broke) / राम (Ram) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / जयति (victory) / बचन (words) / उचारहीं (uttered)
ramacharitamanas::1411.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1411.essence: Reality announces itself before people are ready to praise it.
ramacharitamanas::1411.simple_meaning: Ram breaks Shiva's bow, and the whole cosmos reacts with shock. Only after the break does everyone realise what has happened and begin praising Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1411.simple_insight: Sometimes the true turning point is obvious only after the silence breaks.
ramacharitamanas::1411.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Ram has just broken Shiva's bow. The sound shakes the whole world: beings, sages, and even cosmic creatures react in stunned fear. Only then does the assembly understand that Ram has won, and praise rises everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::1411.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after one sentence lands harder than anyone expected. People stop pretending, look at each other, and finally admit the moment has changed everything.
ramacharitamanas::1411.insight: It marks the instant when hidden truth becomes undeniable and collective doubt turns into recognition.

ramacharitamanas::1412.verse_sanskrit: संकर चापु जहाजु सागरु रघुबर बाहुबलु। बूड़ सो सकल समाजु चढ़ा जो प्रथमहिं मोह बस ॥
ramacharitamanas::1412.verse_hindi: शिवजी का धनुष जहाज है और श्री रामचन्द्रजी की भुजाओं का बल समुद्र है। (धनुष टूटने से) वह सारा समाज डूब गया, जो मोहवश पहले इस जहाज पर चढ़ा था। (जिसका वर्णन ऊपर आया है।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1412.english_translation: Shiva's bow is a ship, and the strength of Raghubar's arms is the sea. The whole company sank who first boarded that ship through delusion.
ramacharitamanas::1412.translation_literal: संकर (of Shiva) / चापु (bow) / जहाजु (ship) / सागरु (sea) / रघुबर (Raghubar, Ram) / बाहुबलु (arm-strength) / बूड़ (sank) / सो (that) / सकल (whole) / समाजु (company) / चढ़ा (boarded) / जो (who) / प्रथमहिं (first) / मोह बस (under delusion)
ramacharitamanas::1412.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1412.essence: Delusion boards first and sinks first.
ramacharitamanas::1412.simple_meaning: The bow is compared to a ship and Ram's strength to the sea. Those who approached the contest out of pride and confusion were the ones who fell away first.
ramacharitamanas::1412.simple_insight: Pride can make a person step into danger before they even understand it.
ramacharitamanas::1412.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, Shiva's great bow has become the test of every king present. Ram's effortless power shatters it, and the gathering that came in pride is exposed as helpless. The verse turns that moment into a vivid image of delusion sinking itself.
ramacharitamanas::1412.modern_relevance: You walk into a room sure you can handle the challenge, but your confidence is built on ego. The moment pressure rises, that false footing gives way.
ramacharitamanas::1412.insight: It shifts attention from outward display to the hidden weakness of ego-driven action.

ramacharitamanas::1413.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु दोउ चापखंड महि डारे। देखि लोग सब भए सुखारे॥ कौसिकरूप पयोनिधि पावन। प्रेम बारि अवगाहु सुहावन ॥
ramacharitamanas::1413.verse_hindi: प्रभु ने धनुष के दोनों टुकड़े पृथ्वी पर डाल दिए। यह देखकर सब लोग सुखी हुए। विश्वामित्र रूपी पवित्र समुद्र में, जिसमें प्रेम रूपी सुंदर अथाह जल भरा है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1413.english_translation: The Lord put the two broken halves of the bow on the ground. Everyone felt relieved. In the pure ocean-like form of Vishwamitra, the beautiful, unfathomable water of love invited a joyful plunge.
ramacharitamanas::1413.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / दोउ (both) / चापखंड (bow-halves) / महि (on the ground) / डारे (threw, placed) / देखि (seeing) / लोग (the people) / सब (all) / भए (became) / सुखारे (relieved, happy) / कौसिकरूप (in Vishwamitra's form) / पयोनिधि (ocean) / पावन (pure) / प्रेम (love) / बारि (water) / अवगाहु (a plunge, immersion) / सुहावन (pleasant, delightful)
ramacharitamanas::1413.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1413.essence: Breaking the bow releases the crowd into relief and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1413.simple_meaning: Ram breaks the bow and sets the two pieces down. The crowd feels relieved, and the scene shifts into a joyful, devotional image of Vishwamitra as a pure ocean of love.
ramacharitamanas::1413.simple_insight: Relief can arrive when tension breaks and the heart opens into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1413.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, Ram has just broken Shiva’s bow and ended the contest. The broken pieces hit the ground, the crowd exhales, and the verse turns from public tension to the devotional presence of Vishwamitra, whose role is now to receive this moment in purity and love.
ramacharitamanas::1413.modern_relevance: The room goes quiet after the announcement nobody dared to hear. Then the pressure lifts, and everyone suddenly knows the worst has passed.
ramacharitamanas::1413.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to the deeper emotional release that follows fulfilled dharma.

ramacharitamanas::1414.verse_sanskrit: रामरूप राकेसु निहारी। बढ़त बीचि पुलकावलि भारी॥ बाजे नभ गहगहे निसाना। देवबधू नाचहिं करि गाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1414.verse_hindi: राम रूपी पूर्णचन्द्र को देखकर पुलकावली रूपी भारी लहरें बढ़ने लगीं। आकाश में बड़े जोर से नगाड़े बजने लगे और देवांगनाएँ गान करके नाचने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1414.english_translation: Seeing Ram as the full moon, waves of goosebumps rose high. Loud drums sounded in the sky, and divine women danced and sang.
ramacharitamanas::1414.translation_literal: रामरूप (in the form of Ram) / राकेसु (the full moon) / निहारी (having seen) / बढ़त (rising) / बीचि (waves) / पुलकावलि (a line of goosebumps) / भारी (great) / बाजे (sounded) / नभ (in the sky) / गहगहे (loudly) / निसाना (drums) / देवबधू (divine women) / नाचहिं (dance) / करि (doing) / गाना (singing)
ramacharitamanas::1414.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1414.essence: Ram's presence turns tension into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1414.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram fills everyone with joy. The whole scene turns festive, with heavenly drums and dancing celestial women.
ramacharitamanas::1414.simple_insight: True beauty does not stay private; it ripples outward and makes the whole world rejoice.
ramacharitamanas::1414.detailed_meaning: After the bow breaks in Janakpur, the crowd has shifted from tension to wonder. Ram's radiant presence is compared to a full moon, and the joy spreads so strongly that even the heavens respond with music and dance.
ramacharitamanas::1414.modern_relevance: A room goes silent when someone finally walks in with calm, steady presence after hours of strain. Nobody has to explain the relief. Their very presence changes the atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::1414.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the transforming presence behind it.

ramacharitamanas::1415.verse_sanskrit: ब्रह्मादिक सुर सिद्ध मुनीसा। प्रभुहि प्रसंसहिं देहिं असीसा॥ बरिसहिं सुमन रंग बहु माला। गावहिं किंनर गीत रसाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::1415.verse_hindi: ब्रह्मा आदि देवता, सिद्ध और मुनीश्वर लोग प्रभु की प्रशंसा कर रहे हैं और आशीर्वाद दे रहे हैं। वे रंग-बिरंगे फूल और मालाएँ बरसा रहे हैं। किन्नर लोग रसीले गीत गा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1415.english_translation: Brahma, the radiant beings, perfected ones, and sages praised the Lord and offered blessings. They showered flowers and garlands, and the celestial singers sang sweet songs.
ramacharitamanas::1415.translation_literal: ब्रह्मादिक (Brahma and others) / सुर (radiant beings) / सिद्ध (perfected ones) / मुनीसा (great sages) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / प्रसंसहिं (praise) / देहिं (give) / असीसा (blessings) / बरिसहिं (shower) / सुमन (flowers) / रंग बहु (many colors) / माला (garlands) / गावहिं (sing) / किंनर (celestial singers) / गीत रसाला (sweet songs)
ramacharitamanas::1415.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1415.essence: Ram's victory draws praise from every higher being.
ramacharitamanas::1415.simple_meaning: All the great beings praise Ram, bless him, and shower flowers as the celebration spreads through the heavens.
ramacharitamanas::1415.simple_insight: True victory feels larger than one person; the whole world seems to sing with it.
ramacharitamanas::1415.detailed_meaning: After Ram breaks Shiva's bow at Sita's swayamvar, the celebration rises beyond the court. Brahma, sages, perfected beings, and celestial singers join the praise, turning the moment into a heavenly festival before the crowd below even fully absorbs it.
ramacharitamanas::1415.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after the final result appears, then erupts into applause and relief. The moment is bigger than the winner — everyone feels the lift of it.
ramacharitamanas::1415.insight: It shifts attention from the feat itself to the shared joy it awakens around it.

ramacharitamanas::1416.verse_sanskrit: रही भुवन भरि जय जय बानी। धनुषभंग धुनिजात न जानी॥ मुदित कहहिं जहँ तहँ नर नारी। भंजेउ राम संभुधनु भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1416.verse_hindi: सारे ब्रह्माण्ड में जय-जयकार की ध्वनि छा गई, जिसमें धनुष टूटने की ध्वनि जान ही नहीं पड़ती। जहाँ-तहाँ स्त्री-पुरुष प्रसन्न होकर कह रहे हैं कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने शिवजी के भारी धनुष को तोड़ डाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::1416.english_translation: The whole world rang with cries of victory, and the sound of the bow breaking was lost. Men and women everywhere rejoiced, saying, "Ram has broken Shiva's mighty bow."
ramacharitamanas::1416.translation_literal: रही (remained) / भुवन भरि (filling the worlds) / जय जय (victory, victory) / बानी (sound, voice) / धनुषभंग (bow-breaking) / धुनि (sound) / जात (being) / न जानी (not known)॥ / मुदित (joyful) / कहहिं (say) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / नर नारी (men and women) / भंजेउ (broke) / राम (Ram) / संभुधनु (Shiva's bow) / भारी (mighty) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1416.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1416.essence: A true victory makes the whole world sing at once.
ramacharitamanas::1416.simple_meaning: Victory fills the world as people celebrate Ram breaking Shiva's mighty bow.
ramacharitamanas::1416.simple_insight: Joy spreads instantly when a true act of strength and grace is witnessed.
ramacharitamanas::1416.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Ram has just lifted and broken Shiva's great bow. The shock of the feat gives way to a wave of celebration, and the whole gathering erupts in praise before the next verse turns to public offerings and honor.
ramacharitamanas::1416.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after someone nails the one task everyone thought impossible. Then the tension breaks, and relief turns into applause.
ramacharitamanas::1416.insight: It shifts attention from the feat itself to the shared joy it awakens in others.

ramacharitamanas::1417.verse_sanskrit: बंदी मागध सूतगन बिरुद बदहिं मतिधीर। करहिं निछावरि लोग सब हय गय धन मनि चीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::1417.verse_hindi: धीर बुद्धि वाले, भाट, मागध और सूत लोग विरुदावली (कीर्ति) का बखान कर रहे हैं। सब लोग घोड़े, हाथी, धन, मणि और वस्त्र निछावर कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1417.english_translation: Bards, heralds, and minstrels of steady mind sing the heroes’ praises. Everyone offers horses, elephants, wealth, jewels, and garments in tribute.
ramacharitamanas::1417.translation_literal: बंदी (bards / praise-singers) / मागध (heralds) / सूतगन (minstrels) / बिरुद (praise / heroic praise) / बदहिं (sing) / मतिधीर (steady-minded) / करहिं (do) / निछावरि (offering / tribute) / लोग सब (all people) / हय (horses) / गय (elephants) / धन (wealth) / मनि (jewels) / चीर (garments)
ramacharitamanas::1417.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1417.essence: Praise and generosity rise together when awe fills a crowd.
ramacharitamanas::1417.simple_meaning: The crowd celebrates the event with praise and gifts. Bards sing, and everyone offers valuable things in joy.
ramacharitamanas::1417.simple_insight: Joy becomes generous when the heart is overwhelmed.
ramacharitamanas::1417.detailed_meaning: After Ram breaks Shiva’s bow in Janakpur, the whole court erupts in celebration. Bards and heralds sing his praise while people shower gifts of horses, elephants, wealth, jewels, and cloth. The verse shows the public outpouring before the wedding music begins.
ramacharitamanas::1417.modern_relevance: A room erupts after the announcement lands, and people start clapping, cheering, and sending flowers. Some moments are too full for words alone.
ramacharitamanas::1417.insight: It shifts attention from private achievement to shared celebration and public gratitude.

ramacharitamanas::1418.verse_sanskrit: झाँझि मृदंग संख सहनाई। भेरि ढोल दुंदुभी सुहाई॥ बाजहिं बहु बाजने सुहाए। जहँ तहँ जुबतिन्ह मंगल गाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1418.verse_hindi: झाँझ, मृदंग, शंख, शहनाई, भेरी, ढोल और सुहावने नगाड़े आदि बहुत प्रकार के सुंदर बाजे बज रहे हैं। जहाँ-तहाँ युवतियाँ मंगल गीत गा रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1418.english_translation: Jhanjh, mridang, conch, and shehnai sounded. Bheri, dhol, and auspicious drums were played. Many lovely instruments resounded, and everywhere young women sang मंगल songs.
ramacharitamanas::1418.translation_literal: झाँझि (cymbals) / मृदंग (mridang) / संख (conch) / सहनाई (shehnai) / भेरि (war drum) / ढोल (drum) / दुंदुभी (kettle drum) / सुहाई (pleasing) / बाजहिं (are played) / बहु (many) / बाजने (instruments) / सुहाए (lovely) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / जुबतिन्ह (by young women) / मंगल (auspicious) / गाए (sang)
ramacharitamanas::1418.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1418.essence: Celebration spreads through sound before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::1418.simple_meaning: The wedding celebration is in full swing. Many instruments are playing, and young women are singing auspicious songs everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::1418.simple_insight: Joy can fill a whole place at once, turning a single moment into shared celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1418.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the bow has been broken and the wedding mood has burst open. Drums, conches, and flutes sound everywhere, and the young women sing blessings as the whole scene turns into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1418.modern_relevance: A wedding hall erupts just after the good news lands. Drums start, voices rise, and strangers smile at each other because the moment has become bigger than any one person.
ramacharitamanas::1418.insight: It turns the scene from tension to collective joy, showing that victory ripples outward through the whole community.

ramacharitamanas::1419.verse_sanskrit: सखिन्ह सहित हरषी अति रानी। सूखत धान परा जनु पानी॥ जनक लहेउ सुखु सोचु बिहाई। तैरत थकें थाह जनु पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1419.verse_hindi: सखियों सहित रानी अत्यन्त हर्षित हुईं, मानो सूखते हुए धान पर पानी पड़ गया हो। जनकजी ने सोच त्याग कर सुख प्राप्त किया। मानो तैरते-तैरते थके हुए पुरुष ने थाह पा ली हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1419.english_translation: The queens, with their companions, were overjoyed, like water falling on dry grain. Janaka found happiness and let go of sorrow, like a tired swimmer reaching the far bank.
ramacharitamanas::1419.translation_literal: सखिन्ह (with companions) / सहित (together with) / हरषी (became joyful) / अति (very) / रानी (the queen) / सूखत (drying) / धान (paddy grain) / परा (fell) / जनु (as if) / पानी (water) / जनक (Janaka) / लहेउ (found) / सुखु (happiness) / सोचु (sorrow) / बिहाई (having left) / तैरत (while swimming) / थकें (tired) / थाह (the bank / bottom / depth) / जनु (as if) / पाई (found)
ramacharitamanas::1419.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1419.essence: Joy can end sorrow as suddenly as water revives dry grain.
ramacharitamanas::1419.simple_meaning: The queens and their companions feel sudden joy. Janaka also feels relief, as if a long struggle has finally ended.
ramacharitamanas::1419.simple_insight: Relief can arrive all at once, after a long stretch of strain.
ramacharitamanas::1419.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court at the Sita-swayamvar, the queens and their companions burst into joy as the scene turns toward celebration. Janaka's own worry falls away too, because the long tension of waiting has finally broken.
ramacharitamanas::1419.modern_relevance: You hold your breath through a tense family meeting, then one sentence changes everything. The room softens at once, and everyone can finally exhale.
ramacharitamanas::1419.insight: It shows how a shared moment of release can dissolve private worry instantly.

ramacharitamanas::1420.verse_sanskrit: श्रीहत भए भूप धनु टूटे। जैसें दिवस दीप छबि छूटे॥ सीय सुखहि बरनिअ केहि भाँती। जनु चातकी पाइ जलु स्वाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1420.verse_hindi: धनुष टूट जाने पर राजा लोग ऐसे श्रीहीन (निस्तेज) हो गए, जैसे दिन में दीपक की शोभा जाती रहती है। सीताजी का सुख किस प्रकार वर्णन किया जाए, जैसे चातकी स्वाती का जल पा गई हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1420.english_translation: When the bow broke, the kings lost their radiance, like a lamp in daylight. Sita's joy cannot be described; she was like a chatak bird finding rain from the Swati star.
ramacharitamanas::1420.translation_literal: श्रीहत (deprived of splendour) / भए (became) / भूप (kings) / धनु (bow) / टूटे (broke) / जैसें (as) / दिवस (day) / दीप (lamp) / छबि (radiance) / छूटे (left)॥ / सीय (Sita's) / सुखहि (happiness) / बरनिअ (describe) / केहि (how) / भाँती (manner) / जनु (as if) / चातकी (chatak bird) / पाइ (having obtained) / जलु (water) / स्वाती (Swati star)
ramacharitamanas::1420.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1420.essence: One broken bow, two opposite hearts: shame for some, overflowing joy for Sita.
ramacharitamanas::1420.simple_meaning: The broken bow leaves the kings stunned, while Sita feels the joy of a bird finally reaching rain after a long wait.
ramacharitamanas::1420.simple_insight: Some moments are so overwhelming that words fail; joy and loss can strike the room at once.
ramacharitamanas::1420.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Shiva's bow has just snapped before everyone. The proud kings are stripped of their shine, and Sita's heart leaps in a joy too large to measure. The scene sets up the moment before Ram is called forward.
ramacharitamanas::1420.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after the final interview question. One person realizes they have failed; another realizes the door they longed for has opened. The same moment can flatten one life and lift another.
ramacharitamanas::1420.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle of victory to the inner change the event creates in each person.

ramacharitamanas::1421.verse_sanskrit: रामहि लखनु बिलोकत कैसें। ससिहि चकोर किसोरकु जैसें॥ सतानंद तब आयसु दीन्हा। सीताँ गमनु राम पहिं कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1421.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी को लक्ष्मणजी किस प्रकार देख रहे हैं, जैसे चन्द्रमा को चकोर का बच्चा देख रहा हो। तब शतानंदजी ने आज्ञा दी और सीताजी ने श्री रामजी के पास गमन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1421.english_translation: How Lakshman watched Ram, like a young chakor bird watching the moon. Then Shatanand gave the order, and Sita went toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1421.translation_literal: रामहि (to Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / बिलोकत (watching) / कैसें (how) / ससिहि (the moon) / चकोर (chakor bird) / किसोरकु (young one) / जैसें (like) / सतानंद (Shatanand) / तब (then) / आयसु (command) / दीन्हा (gave) / सीताँ (Sita) / गमनु (going) / राम पहिं (toward Ram) / कीन्हा (did)
ramacharitamanas::1421.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1421.essence: Devotion fixes the gaze and draws the beloved near.
ramacharitamanas::1421.simple_meaning: Lakshman gazes at Ram with complete devotion, like a young bird gazing at the moon. Then Shatanand gives the command, and Sita walks toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1421.simple_insight: Love makes the eyes steady and the steps certain.
ramacharitamanas::1421.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the bow has been broken and the wedding moment has arrived. Lakshman cannot look away from Ram, while Shatanand gives the signal for Sita to move toward him. The scene glows with devotion and sacred union.
ramacharitamanas::1421.modern_relevance: In a crowded wedding hall, one person keeps looking only at the one they trust most. The noise fades. The whole room narrows to that one steady gaze.
ramacharitamanas::1421.insight: It shifts attention from the crowd to the one presence that matters.

ramacharitamanas::1422.verse_sanskrit: संग सखीं सुंदर चतुर गावहिं मंगलचार। गवनी बाल मराल गति सुषमा अंग अपार ॥
ramacharitamanas::1422.verse_hindi: साथ में सुंदर चतुर सखियाँ मंगलाचार के गीत गा रही हैं, सीताजी बालहंसिनी की चाल से चलीं। उनके अंगों में अपार शोभा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1422.english_translation: Beautiful, clever companions sing auspicious songs. Sita walks with the graceful gait of a young swan, her body radiant beyond measure.
ramacharitamanas::1422.translation_literal: संग (with) / सखीं (companions) / सुंदर (beautiful) / चतुर (clever) / गावहिं (sing) / मंगलचार (auspicious songs) / गवनी (walked) / बाल (young) / मराल (swan) / गति (gait) / सुषमा (beauty) / अंग (limbs/body) / अपार (boundless)
ramacharitamanas::1422.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1422.essence: Grace can turn a procession into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1422.simple_meaning: Sita is escorted by lovely companions singing blessings, and she walks with extraordinary grace and beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1422.simple_insight: Some moments are so full of grace that the whole scene feels blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1422.detailed_meaning: Sita is being led forward after the bow has been broken and the wedding scene is unfolding. Around her, the companions sing auspicious songs, and her movement is described as delicate and radiant. The verse lingers on the beauty of the procession, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1422.modern_relevance: At a wedding procession, the music rises and everyone turns to watch one person walk in with quiet grace. The room changes before anyone says a word.
ramacharitamanas::1422.insight: It trains attention on sacred beauty in ordinary movement and ceremony.

ramacharitamanas::1423.verse_sanskrit: सखिन्ह मध्य सिय सोहति कैसें। छबिगन मध्य महाछबि जैसें॥ कर सरोज जयमाल सुहाई। बिस्व बिजय सोभा जेहिं छाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1423.verse_hindi: सखियों के बीच में सीताजी कैसी शोभित हो रही हैं, जैसे बहुत सी छवियों के बीच में महाछवि हो। करकमल में सुंदर जयमाला है, जिसमें विश्व विजय की शोभा छाई हुई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1423.english_translation: How beautifully Sita shines among the companions, like a supreme radiance among many lights. In her lotus hand rests a lovely garland of victory, covered with the glory of world-conquest.
ramacharitamanas::1423.translation_literal: सखिन्ह (among the companions) / मध्य (in the middle) / सिय (Sita) / सोहति (shines beautifully) / कैसें (how) / छबिगन (among beauties/radiances) / मध्य (in the middle) / महाछबि (great radiance) / जैसें (like) // कर (hand) / सरोज (lotus) / जयमाल (victory garland) / सुहाई (beautiful) / बिस्व (world) / बिजय (victory) / सोभा (splendor) / जेहिं (in which) / छाई (is spread)
ramacharitamanas::1423.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1423.essence: Sita outshines every surrounding beauty by simply being herself.
ramacharitamanas::1423.simple_meaning: Sita stands out among the maidens like a brilliant radiance among lesser lights. Her hand holds the victory garland, glowing with the splendor of triumph.
ramacharitamanas::1423.simple_insight: Grace can outshine every surrounding beauty without trying to compete.
ramacharitamanas::1423.detailed_meaning: At Janak's swayamvar, the maidens gather around Sita as she moves forward with the garland. Tulsidas pauses on her radiance itself: she is not just beautiful, but the brightest presence in the whole scene, already carrying the sign of Ram's victory.
ramacharitamanas::1423.modern_relevance: At a wedding hall full of glittering clothes, cameras, and noise, one person enters with such natural grace that everyone else fades into the background. Real beauty does not strain to be seen.
ramacharitamanas::1423.insight: It shifts attention from decoration to presence, showing that true radiance needs no display.

ramacharitamanas::1424.verse_sanskrit: तन सकोचु मन परम उछाहू। गूढ़ प्रेमु लखि परइ न काहू॥ जाइ समीप राम छबि देखी। रहि जनु कुअँरि चित्र अवरेखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1424.verse_hindi: सीताजी के शरीर में संकोच है, पर मन में परम उत्साह है। उनका यह गुप्त प्रेम किसी को जान नहीं पड़ रहा है। समीप जाकर, श्री रामजी की शोभा देखकर राजकुमारी सीताजी जैसे चित्र में लिखी सी रह गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1424.english_translation: Her body grew shy, but her mind was full of joy. No one could see the depth of her hidden love. Near Ram, seeing his radiant form, the princess stood like a picture come to life.
ramacharitamanas::1424.translation_literal: तन (body) / सकोचु (shyness) / मन (mind) / परम (supreme) / उछाहू (joy) / गूढ़ (hidden) / प्रेमु (love) / लखि (seeing) / परइ (is known) / न (not) / काहू (to anyone) ॥ / जाइ (going) / समीप (near) / राम (Ram) / छबि (radiance) / देखी (saw) / रहि (remained) / जनु (as if) / कुअँरि (princess) / चित्र (picture) / अवरेखी (drawn)
ramacharitamanas::1424.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1424.essence: Love becomes stillness when the beloved is near.
ramacharitamanas::1424.simple_meaning: Sita feels shy outwardly but intensely joyful भीतर. Her hidden love is invisible to others. When she comes close and sees Ram, she stands still as if painted in place.
ramacharitamanas::1424.simple_insight: Deep love can make you quiet, still, and wordless before the one you long for.
ramacharitamanas::1424.detailed_meaning: At the swayamvar, Sita moves toward Ram while the court watches. Her face shows restraint, but her heart is overflowing. Seeing Ram's beauty up close, she becomes motionless, absorbed in love before the next decisive moment.
ramacharitamanas::1424.modern_relevance: You finally walk into the room where someone you deeply admire is standing. Your face stays composed, but inside everything is shaking. Love can make even confidence go silent.
ramacharitamanas::1424.insight: It shows how devotion can freeze speech and movement, replacing performance with pure absorption.

ramacharitamanas::1425.verse_sanskrit: चतुर सखीं लखि कहा बुझाई। पहिरावहु जयमाल सुहाई॥ सुनत जुगल कर माल उठाई। प्रेम बिबस पहिराइ न जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1425.verse_hindi: चतुर सखी ने यह दशा देखकर समझाकर कहा- सुहावनी जयमाला पहनाओ। यह सुनकर सीताजी ने दोनों हाथों से माला उठाई, पर प्रेम में विवश होने से पहनाई नहीं जाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1425.english_translation: The wise companion saw her state and said, “Place the lovely garland on him.” Hearing this, Sita lifted the garland with both hands, but love made her unable to place it.
ramacharitamanas::1425.translation_literal: चतुर (wise) / सखीं (female companion) / लखि (seeing) / कहा (said) / बुझाई (explaining) / पहिरावहु (make wear / place on) / जयमाल (victory garland) / सुहाई (lovely) ॥ सुनत (hearing) / जुगल (both) / कर (hands) / माल (garland) / उठाई (lifted) / प्रेम (love) / बिबस (powerless, compelled) / पहिराइ (to place / make wear) / न जाई (cannot be done) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1425.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1425.essence: Love can overwhelm the very act it longs to perform.
ramacharitamanas::1425.simple_meaning: A thoughtful friend urges Sita to place the garland, but love overwhelms her and she cannot do it.
ramacharitamanas::1425.simple_insight: Love can make even a simple gesture feel impossible.
ramacharitamanas::1425.detailed_meaning: At Janak's swayamvar, Sita stands before Ram with the garland in her hands. Her clever companion tries to guide the moment forward, but Sita's love is so strong that even lifting the garland becomes an act of trembling hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::1425.modern_relevance: You know the moment when your heart is already decided, but your hands still hesitate. A text message, a confession, a first move — love can make action feel weightless and impossible at once.
ramacharitamanas::1425.insight: It shows how feeling can delay action even when the heart has already chosen.

ramacharitamanas::1426.verse_sanskrit: सोहत जनु जुग जलज सनाला। ससिहि सभीत देत जयमाला॥ गावहिं छबि अवलोकि सहेली। सियँ जयमाल राम उर मेली ॥
ramacharitamanas::1426.verse_hindi: (उस समय उनके हाथ ऐसे सुशोभित हो रहे हैं) मानो डंडियों सहित दो कमल चन्द्रमा को डरते हुए जयमाला दे रहे हों। इस छवि को देखकर सखियाँ गाने लगीं। तब सीताजी ने श्री रामजी के गले में जयमाला पहना दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1426.english_translation: Her hands shone like two lotus stalks offering a garland to the moon. The maids sang at the sight, and Sita placed the victory garland around Ram's neck.
ramacharitamanas::1426.translation_literal: सोहत (shone) / जनु (as if) / जुग (two) / जलज (lotuses) / सनाला (with stalks) / ससिहि (to the moon) / सभीत (fearfully) / देत (giving) / जयमाला (victory garland) / गावहिं (they sing) / छबि (beauty) / अवलोकि (seeing) / सहेली (maidens) / सियँ (Sita) / जयमाल (garland) / राम (Ram) / उर (neck/chest) / मेली (placed)
ramacharitamanas::1426.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1426.essence: Love recognizes its own place and moves without delay.
ramacharitamanas::1426.simple_meaning: Sita’s hands look like lotus stems offering a garland, and the maids sing as she places it around Ram’s neck.
ramacharitamanas::1426.simple_insight: Love becomes graceful when fear disappears and the heart acts on its own.
ramacharitamanas::1426.detailed_meaning: At the swayamvar, Sita has already gathered herself after her inward hesitation. The maids watch her beauty and courage as she lifts the garland and places it on Ram, completing the moment everyone has been waiting for.
ramacharitamanas::1426.modern_relevance: Your hands shake before the text you have been meaning to send for weeks. Then you do it anyway, and the whole room inside you changes.
ramacharitamanas::1426.insight: It shifts attention from hesitation to the clean act that seals commitment.

ramacharitamanas::1427.verse_sanskrit: रघुबर उर जयमाल देखि देव बरिसहिं सुमन। सकुचे सकल भुआल जनु बिलोकि रबि कुमुदगन ॥
ramacharitamanas::1427.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी के हृदय पर जयमाला देखकर देवता फूल बरसाने लगे। समस्त राजागण इस प्रकार सकुचा गए मानो सूर्य को देखकर कुमुदों का समूह सिकुड़ गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1427.english_translation: Seeing the garland on Raghubar's chest, the divine beings showered flowers. All the kings grew shy, like a cluster of water lilies shrinking before the sun.
ramacharitamanas::1427.translation_literal: रघुबर (Raghubar) / उर (chest) / जयमाल (garland of victory) / देखि (seeing) / देव (divine beings) / बरिसहिं (shower) / सुमन (flowers) / सकुचे (grew shy) / सकल (all) / भुआल (kings) / जनु (as if) / बिलोकि (seeing) / रबि (sun) / कुमुदगन (cluster of water lilies)
ramacharitamanas::1427.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1427.essence: Real greatness makes pride fall silent.
ramacharitamanas::1427.simple_meaning: The moment Ram receives the garland, heaven rejoices and the gathered kings lose their confidence.
ramacharitamanas::1427.simple_insight: True radiance needs no announcement; it naturally humbles pride and draws celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1427.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, Ram has just received the victory garland. The court watches in stunned silence while the divine beings shower flowers from above. The kings, who had come with pride and ambition, suddenly shrink before Ram's quiet greatness.
ramacharitamanas::1427.modern_relevance: At a wedding, the room goes still when the right person is chosen. The loudest people suddenly have nothing to say, and everyone can feel what is real without a speech.
ramacharitamanas::1427.insight: It shifts attention from human competition to the quiet authority of earned worth.

ramacharitamanas::1428.verse_sanskrit: पुर अरु ब्योम बाजने बाजे। खल भए मलिन साधु सब राजे॥ सुर किंनर नर नाग मुनीसा। जय जय जय कहि देहिं असीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1428.verse_hindi: नगर और आकाश में बाजे बजने लगे। दुष्ट लोग उदास हो गए और सज्जन लोग सब प्रसन्न हो गए। देवता, किन्नर, मनुष्य, नाग और मुनीश्वर जय-जयकार करके आशीर्वाद दे रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1428.english_translation: The drums sounded in the city and in the sky. The wicked grew sullen, and all the good were delighted. Devas, celestial singers, humans, serpents, and sages cried victory and gave blessings.
ramacharitamanas::1428.translation_literal: पुर (city) / अरु (and) / ब्योम (sky) / बाजने (drums) / बाजे (sounded) / खल (wicked) / भए (became) / मलिन (sullen) / साधु (good) / सब (all) / राजे (delighted) / सुर (devas) / किंनर (celestial singers) / नर (humans) / नाग (serpents) / मुनीसा (sages) / जय जय जय (victory, victory, victory) / कहि (saying) / देहिं (give) / असीसा (blessings)
ramacharitamanas::1428.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1428.essence: Right action makes the whole world sing.
ramacharitamanas::1428.simple_meaning: The whole world rejoices at the wedding. Even the heavens join in, while those opposed to Ram and Sita feel troubled.
ramacharitamanas::1428.simple_insight: When the right thing happens, joy spreads beyond one room. Even the atmosphere feels it.
ramacharitamanas::1428.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, Ram has just won the garland and the hall is overflowing with celebration. The drums sound in earth and sky, the righteous rejoice, and every class of beings joins the blessing. This is a scene of cosmic approval, not private joy.
ramacharitamanas::1428.modern_relevance: A wedding hall erupts when the couple finally meets at the center. Even the people who came to judge can feel the shift: something true has happened, and the room knows it.
ramacharitamanas::1428.insight: It turns a personal victory into a cosmic affirmation, showing that dharma draws universal support.

ramacharitamanas::1429.verse_sanskrit: नाचहिं गावहिं बिबुध बधूटीं। बार बार कुसुमांजलि छूटीं॥ जहँ तहँ बिप्र बेदधुनि करहीं। बंदी बिरिदावलि उच्चरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1429.verse_hindi: देवताओं की स्त्रियाँ नाचती-गाती हैं। बार-बार हाथों से पुष्पों की अंजलियाँ छूट रही हैं। जहाँ-तहाँ ब्रह्म वेदध्वनि कर रहे हैं और भाट लोग विरुदावली (कुलकीर्ति) बखान रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1429.english_translation: The divine women dance and sing. Again and again, flower offerings spill from their hands. Everywhere, priests chant the Vedic sound, and bards recite lines of praise.
ramacharitamanas::1429.translation_literal: नाचहिं (dance) / गावहिं (sing) / बिबुध बधूटीं (the wives of the radiant beings) / बार बार (again and again) / कुसुमांजलि (flower-offering) / छूटीं (spill, slip away) / जहँ तहँ (here and there, everywhere) / बिप्र (priests) / बेदधुनि (Vedic sound) / करहीं (make, chant) / बंदी (bards) / बिरिदावलि (line of praise, genealogy of glory) / उच्चरहीं (recite)
ramacharitamanas::1429.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1429.essence: A true union makes the whole world sing.
ramacharitamanas::1429.simple_meaning: The whole world rejoices at Ram and Sita's wedding. Celestial women dance, flowers fall from every hand, priests chant, and praise fills every direction.
ramacharitamanas::1429.simple_insight: Joy becomes collective when a moment is truly blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1429.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar in Mithila, Ram has just won the bow and the celebration spills beyond the court. Celestial beings, priests, and bards all join the jubilation, showing that this union is being honored across every level of creation.
ramacharitamanas::1429.modern_relevance: A wedding hall erupts when the couple finally takes each other's hands. Strangers smile, elders chant blessings, and even the air feels changed. Some moments make celebration feel bigger than the room.
ramacharitamanas::1429.insight: It shifts attention from the private event to its cosmic recognition.

ramacharitamanas::1430.verse_sanskrit: महिं पाताल नाक जसु ब्यापा। राम बरी सिय भंजेउ चापा॥ करहिं आरती पुर नर नारी। देहिं निछावरि बित्त बिसारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1430.verse_hindi: पृथ्वी, पाताल और स्वर्ग तीनों लोकों में यश फैल गया कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने धनुष तोड़ दिया और सीताजी को वरण कर लिया। नगर के नर-नारी आरती कर रहे हैं और अपनी पूँजी (हैसियत) को भुलाकर (सामर्थ्य से बहुत अधिक) निछावर कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1430.english_translation: Fame spread through earth, the lower realms, and the heavens: Ram broke the bow and won Sita. Men and women in the city performed aarti and offered everything they had, forgetting their wealth.
ramacharitamanas::1430.translation_literal: महिं (on the earth) / पाताल (the lower realms) / नाक (heavenly realms) / जसु (fame) / ब्यापा (spread) / राम (Ram) / बरी (chose as bride) / सिय (Sita) / भंजेउ (broke) / चापा (the bow) / करहिं (they do) / आरती (aarti) / पुर (in the city) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / देहिं (give) / निछावरि (offering) / बित्त (wealth) / बिसारी (forgetting)
ramacharitamanas::1430.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1430.essence: Ram's victory makes the whole world celebrate and give.
ramacharitamanas::1430.simple_meaning: News of Ram breaking the bow and winning Sita spreads everywhere. The city erupts in celebration, and people offer whatever they have in joy.
ramacharitamanas::1430.simple_insight: Joy makes people generous. When the heart is full, giving feels natural.
ramacharitamanas::1430.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the bow has been broken and Sita has chosen Ram. The news rushes through earth, the lower realms, and the heavens. The whole city responds with aarti, celebration, and offerings, because the long-awaited union has finally happened.
ramacharitamanas::1430.modern_relevance: A wedding crowd hears the announcement and the room changes at once. Strangers smile, elders bless, and even careful people reach into their pockets. Some moments make generosity feel effortless.
ramacharitamanas::1430.insight: It shows how sacred joy turns spectators into participants.

ramacharitamanas::1431.verse_sanskrit: सोहति सीय राम कै जोरी। छबि सिंगारु मनहुँ एक ठोरी॥ सखीं कहहिं प्रभु पद गहु सीता। करति न चरन परस अति भीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1431.verse_hindi: श्री सीता-रामजी की जोड़ी ऐसी सुशोभित हो रही है मानो सुंदरता और श्रृंगार रस एकत्र हो गए हों। सखियाँ कह रही हैं- सीते! स्वामी के चरण छुओ, किन्तु सीताजी अत्यन्त भयभीत हुई उनके चरण नहीं छूतीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1431.english_translation: Sita and Ram shine together like beauty and adornment gathered into one place. The companions say, "Sita, touch your lord's feet," but Sita is so shy she does not touch them.
ramacharitamanas::1431.translation_literal: सोहति (shines) / सीय राम कै (of Sita and Ram) / जोरी (pair) / छबि (beauty) / सिंगारु (adornment) / मनहुँ (as if) / एक ठोरी (one place, gathered together)॥ / सखीं (companions) / कहहिं (say) / प्रभु (lord) / पद (feet) / गहु (touch/hold) / सीता (Sita) / करति (doing) / न (not) / चरन (feet) / परस (touch) / अति (very) / भीता (afraid)
ramacharitamanas::1431.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1431.essence: Reverence can make even love feel shy.
ramacharitamanas::1431.simple_meaning: Ram and Sita look beautifully matched, like beauty itself has become a pair. The companions urge Sita to touch Ram's feet, but she feels too shy to do it.
ramacharitamanas::1431.simple_insight: Love can be so reverent that even closeness feels overwhelming.
ramacharitamanas::1431.detailed_meaning: After Ram breaks Shiva's bow and wins Sita, the wedding scene turns tender. Sita and Ram stand together in radiant splendor, and the companions gently urge Sita to touch Ram's feet. Her shyness shows the depth of reverence in their bond.
ramacharitamanas::1431.modern_relevance: At a wedding, everyone is smiling while the bride's hands tremble before the first blessing. The moment is beautiful not because it is polished, but because reverence makes even simple closeness feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::1431.insight: It shifts attention from outward ceremony to the inward humility that makes true union beautiful.

ramacharitamanas::1432.verse_sanskrit: गौतम तिय गति सुरति करि नहिं परसति पग पानि। मन बिहसे रघुबंसमनि प्रीति अलौकिक जानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1432.verse_hindi: गौतमजी की स्त्री अहल्या की गति का स्मरण करके सीताजी श्री रामजी के चरणों को हाथों से स्पर्श नहीं कर रही हैं। सीताजी की अलौकिक प्रीति जानकर रघुकुल मणि श्री रामचन्द्रजी मन में हँसे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1432.english_translation: Remembering Ahilya's state, Sita did not touch Ram's feet with her hands. Seeing her extraordinary love, Ram, jewel of the Raghu line, smiled within.
ramacharitamanas::1432.translation_literal: गौतम तिय (Gautam's wife) / गति (state, fate) / सुरति (remembering) / करि (doing) / नहिं (not) / परसति (touching) / पग (feet) / पानि (hands) / मन (mind) / बिहसे (smiled) / रघुबंसमनि (jewel of the Raghu line) / प्रीति (love) / अलौकिक (unworldly, extraordinary) / जानि (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::1432.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1432.essence: True love can be so reverent that even touch feels too bold.
ramacharitamanas::1432.simple_meaning: Sita, remembering Ahilya's story, hesitates to touch Ram's feet with her hands. Ram sees that her love is beyond ordinary and smiles inwardly.
ramacharitamanas::1432.simple_insight: Love can be so reverent that even closeness feels like awe.
ramacharitamanas::1432.detailed_meaning: After Ram breaks Shiva's bow and Sita accepts him, the wedding scene turns tender. Sita remembers Ahilya and feels too humble to touch Ram's feet directly. Ram notices the depth of her love and smiles.
ramacharitamanas::1432.modern_relevance: You stand beside someone you deeply respect and suddenly your hands feel awkward, almost too human for the moment. Reverence can make love gentler, not smaller.
ramacharitamanas::1432.insight: It shifts attention from physical contact to the quality of reverence behind the gesture.

ramacharitamanas::1433.verse_sanskrit: तब सिय देखि भूप अभिलाषे। कूर कपूत मूढ़ मन माखे॥ उठि उठि पहिरि सनाह अभागे। जहँ तहँ गाल बजावन लागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1433.verse_hindi: उस समय सीताजी को देखकर कुछ राजा लोग ललचा उठे। वे दुष्ट, कुपूत और मूढ़ राजा मन में बहुत तमतमाए। वे अभागे उठ-उठकर, कवच पहनकर, जहाँ-तहाँ गाल बजाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1433.english_translation: Then, seeing Sita, the kings grew covetous. Wicked, foolish, and base-minded, they burned with anger. Rising again and again, they put on armor and began shouting everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::1433.translation_literal: तब (then) / सिय (Sita) / देखि (seeing) / भूप (kings) / अभिलाषे (desired, became covetous) / कूर (wicked) / कपूत (bad-born, base) / मूढ़ (foolish) / मन (mind) / माखे (burned, flared up) / उठि उठि (rising again and again) / पहिरि (wearing) / सनाह (armor) / अभागे (unlucky, wretched) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / गाल (shouts, boasts) / बजावन (to sound, to boast) / लागे (began)
ramacharitamanas::1433.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1433.essence: Desire makes proud men loud before it makes them strong.
ramacharitamanas::1433.simple_meaning: The sight of Sita makes the kings greedy and angry. They rush about in armor, boasting loudly like fools.
ramacharitamanas::1433.simple_insight: Unchecked desire turns status into noise and courage into bluster.
ramacharitamanas::1433.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the assembled kings see her and lose their composure. Their pride turns to greed, then to anger. Instead of wisdom or restraint, they arm themselves and start boasting, setting up the clash that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1433.modern_relevance: A room full of polished people can change in a second when envy enters. Smiles tighten, voices get louder, and someone starts performing strength instead of showing it.
ramacharitamanas::1433.insight: It exposes how desire can strip away judgment and turn confidence into empty display.

ramacharitamanas::1434.verse_sanskrit: लेहु छड़ाइ सीय कह कोऊ। धरि बाँधहु नृप बालक दोऊ॥ तोरें धनुषु चाड़ नहिं सरई। जीवत हमहि कुअँरि को बरई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1434.verse_hindi: कोई कहते हैं, सीता को छीन लो और दोनों राजकुमारों को पकड़कर बाँध लो। धनुष तोड़ने से ही चाह नहीं सरेगी (पूरी होगी)। हमारे जीते-जी राजकुमारी को कौन ब्याह सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1434.english_translation: Some cried, "Snatch Sita away. Seize and bind the two princes. Breaking the bow will not satisfy desire. While we live, who can marry the princess?"
ramacharitamanas::1434.translation_literal: लेहु (take) / छड़ाइ (snatching away) / सीय (Sita) / कह (saying) / कोऊ (someone) / धरि (seizing) / बाँधहु (bind) / नृप (king) / बालक (young princes) / दोऊ (both) / तोरें (breaking) / धनुषु (bow) / चाड़ (desire) / नहिं (not) / सरई (be satisfied) / जीवत (while alive) / हमहि (us) / कुअँरि (princess) / को (of whom) / बरई (marry)
ramacharitamanas::1434.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1434.essence: Wounded pride reaches for force when it cannot win fairly.
ramacharitamanas::1434.simple_meaning: The arrogant kings want to seize Sita and bind the princes, because they think only force can win the contest.
ramacharitamanas::1434.simple_insight: Desire makes people lose all dignity and reason.
ramacharitamanas::1434.detailed_meaning: At Janak's swayamvar, the princes have failed to lift Shiva's bow, and the court's pride is turning ugly. Enraged kings speak of violence, not honour, showing how quickly wounded ego becomes cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::1434.modern_relevance: A room full of people starts posturing after someone else gets chosen. The jokes turn sharp, the smiles harden, and wounded pride begins looking for a target.
ramacharitamanas::1434.insight: It exposes how ego turns competition into aggression when admiration is denied.

ramacharitamanas::1435.verse_sanskrit: जौं बिदेहु कछु करै सहाई। जीतहु समर सहित दोउ भाई॥ साधु भूप बोले सुनि बानी। राजसमाजहि लाज लजानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1435.verse_hindi: यदि जनक कुछ सहायता करें, तो युद्ध में दोनों भाइयों सहित उसे भी जीत लो। ये वचन सुनकर साधु राजा बोले- इस (निर्लज्ज) राज समाज को देखकर तो लाज भी लजा गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1435.english_translation: If King Janaka gives any help, then defeat both brothers in battle. Hearing these words, the noble king said, "Looking at this shameless royal assembly, even shame itself feels ashamed."
ramacharitamanas::1435.translation_literal: जौं (if) / बिदेहु (Janaka of Videha) / कछु (some) / करै (does) / सहाई (help) / जीतहु (defeat) / समर (battle) / सहित (together with) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) ॥ / साधु (noble) / भूप (king) / बोले (spoke) / सुनि (hearing) / बानी (words) / राजसमाजहि (the royal assembly) / लाज (shame) / लजानी (was ashamed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1435.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1435.essence: Pride becomes ridiculous when it has no restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1435.simple_meaning: The kings are so shameless that one noble king says even shame would feel ashamed watching them.
ramacharitamanas::1435.simple_insight: Empty pride collapses when someone honest names it clearly.
ramacharitamanas::1435.detailed_meaning: At Janak's swayamvar, the gathered kings are furious that they may lose Sita. One noble king, disgusted by their arrogance, says their conduct is so disgraceful that even shame itself seems humiliated.
ramacharitamanas::1435.modern_relevance: A group chat turns ugly the moment ego takes over, and one calm person finally says what everyone feels: this is beneath us.
ramacharitamanas::1435.insight: It exposes how collective arrogance destroys dignity, and how one clear voice can puncture it.

ramacharitamanas::1436.verse_sanskrit: बलु प्रतापु बीरता बड़ाई। नाक पिनाकहि संग सिधाई॥ सोइ सूरता कि अब कहुँ पाई। असि बुधि तौ बिधि मुँह मसि लाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1436.verse_hindi: अरे! तुम्हारा बल, प्रताप, वीरता, बड़ाई और नाक (प्रतिष्ठा) तो धनुष के साथ ही चली गई। वही वीरता थी कि अब कहीं से मिली है? ऐसी दुष्ट बुद्धि है, तभी तो विधाता ने तुम्हारे मुखों पर कालिख लगा दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1436.english_translation: Ah! Your strength, glory, bravery, and pride went away with the bow. Was that real courage at all? Such foolish thinking has only blackened your face.
ramacharitamanas::1436.translation_literal: बलु (strength) / प्रतापु (glory) / बीरता (bravery) / बड़ाई (greatness) / नाक (honour) / पिनाकहि (with the bow) / संग (with) / सिधाई (went away) ॥ / सोइ (that same) / सूरता (courage) / कि (indeed?) / अब (now) / कहुँ (anywhere) / पाई (found) ॥ / असि (such) / बुधि (intelligence) / तौ (then) / बिधि (the creator) / मुँह (face) / मसि (ink/blackness) / लाई (applied) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1436.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1436.essence: Pride disappears the moment real test arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1436.simple_meaning: The speaker mocks the boastful men, saying their pride and courage vanished with the broken bow. Their foolishness has brought shame upon them.
ramacharitamanas::1436.simple_insight: Boasting collapses instantly when skill fails. Real strength does not need swagger.
ramacharitamanas::1436.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the bow has been broken and the boastful kings are exposed. Someone taunts them for losing all honour with the bow itself, turning their failed pride into public shame. The verse sharpens the humiliation before the next challenge.
ramacharitamanas::1436.modern_relevance: You talk big in the group chat, then the moment comes and everything goes quiet. The room remembers the gap between swagger and substance.
ramacharitamanas::1436.insight: It exposes false confidence and shifts attention from reputation to real capability under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::1437.verse_sanskrit: देखहु रामहि नयन भरि तजि इरिषा मदु कोहु॥ लखन रोषु पावकु प्रबल जानि सलभ जनि होहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1437.verse_hindi: ईर्षा, घमंड और क्रोध छोड़कर नेत्र भरकर श्री रामजी (की छबि) को देख लो। लक्ष्मण के क्रोध को प्रबल अग्नि जानकर उसमें पतंगे मत बनो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1437.english_translation: See Ram with full eyes, and leave aside jealousy, pride, and anger. Know Lakshman's wrath to be a fierce fire; do not become a moth in it.
ramacharitamanas::1437.translation_literal: देखहु (see) / रामहि (Ram) / नयन भरि (with filled eyes) / तजि (leaving) / इरिषा (jealousy) / मदु (pride/intoxication) / कोहु (anger) ॥ / लखन (Lakshman) / रोषु (wrath) / पावकु (fire) / प्रबल (fierce) / जानि (knowing) / सलभ (moth) / जनि (do not) / होहु (be)
ramacharitamanas::1437.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1437.essence: Humility lets you see Ram; ego walks straight into fire.
ramacharitamanas::1437.simple_meaning: Look at Ram with complete attention and let go of jealousy, pride, and anger. Lakshman's anger is dangerous, so do not rush into it blindly.
ramacharitamanas::1437.simple_insight: There is relief in stepping back from ego before it turns a moment into a fire.
ramacharitamanas::1437.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the proud men mock the broken bow and stir tension. Tulsidas interrupts the scene with a warning: look at Ram with humility, and do not rush into Lakshman's blazing anger like a moth to flame.
ramacharitamanas::1437.modern_relevance: A group chat turns sharp, and you can feel your own pride rising with every reply. One more message and the whole thing may catch fire. Step back before you become part of the blaze.
ramacharitamanas::1437.insight: It teaches you to pause before reacting, and to see anger as something to avoid, not join.

ramacharitamanas::1438.verse_sanskrit: बैनतेय बलि जिमि चह कागू। जिमि ससु चहै नाग अरि भागू॥ जिमि चह कुसल अकारन कोही। सब संपदा चहै सिवद्रोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1438.verse_hindi: जैसे गरुड़ का भाग कौआ चाहे, सिंह का भाग खरगोश चाहे, बिना कारण ही क्रोध करने वाला अपनी कुशल चाहे, शिवजी से विरोध करने वाला सब प्रकार की सम्पत्ति चाहे, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1438.english_translation: Like a crow wanting Garuda's strength, like a rabbit wanting a lion's place, like an angry man wanting welfare for himself, like one opposed to Shiva wanting every kind of wealth.
ramacharitamanas::1438.translation_literal: बैनतेय (Garuda) / बलि (strength) / जिमि (like) / चह (wants) / कागू (crow) / जिमि (like) / ससु (rabbit) / चहै (wants) / नाग अरि (enemy of serpents, Garuda) / भागू (share/place) / जिमि (like) / चह (wants) / कुसल (well-being) / अकारन (without cause) / कोही (angry one) / सब (all) / संपदा (wealth, prosperity) / चहै (wants) / सिवद्रोही (one hostile to Shiva)
ramacharitamanas::1438.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1438.essence: Unfit desires cannot deliver the good you claim to want.
ramacharitamanas::1438.simple_meaning: A person cannot sincerely want good fortune while living in anger, hostility, or the wrong nature. Desire must match character.
ramacharitamanas::1438.simple_insight: It feels sobering: some desires fail because the heart asking for them is already misaligned.
ramacharitamanas::1438.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar crowd, the poet turns from praise to warning. After the broken pride of the kings, he says a hostile or angry person cannot claim the blessings he wants. The inner nature must fit the outer wish.
ramacharitamanas::1438.modern_relevance: You want a calm relationship, but your messages are sharp and defensive. You want respect, but you keep poisoning the room. The verse says the mismatch is the problem.
ramacharitamanas::1438.insight: It shifts attention from chasing outcomes to correcting the character that is asking for them.

ramacharitamanas::1439.verse_sanskrit: लोभी लोलुप कल कीरति चहई। अकलंकता कि कामी लहई॥ हरि पद बिमुख परम गति चाहा। तस तुम्हार लालचु नरनाहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1439.verse_hindi: लोभी-लालची सुंदर कीर्ति चाहे, कामी मनुष्य निष्कलंकता (चाहे तो) क्या पा सकता है? और जैसे श्री हरि के चरणों से विमुख मनुष्य परमगति (मोक्ष) चाहे, हे राजाओं! सीता के लिए तुम्हारा लालच भी वैसा ही व्यर्थ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1439.english_translation: A greedy person may desire fame; can a lustful person gain spotless purity? And can one turned away from Hari's feet attain the highest state? O kings, your greed for Sita is just as futile.
ramacharitamanas::1439.translation_literal: लोभी (greedy person) / लोलुप (greedy, craving) / कल कीरति (beautiful fame) / चहई (desires) / अकलंकता (spotless purity) / कि (whether) / कामी (lustful person) / लहई (obtains) / हरि (Hari) / पद (feet) / बिमुख (turned away) / परम गति (highest state) / चाहा (desires) / तस (so) / तुम्हार (your) / लालचु (greed) / नरनाहा (O kings)
ramacharitamanas::1439.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1439.essence: Greed disqualifies the very thing it chases.
ramacharitamanas::1439.simple_meaning: A greedy or lustful mind cannot gain what requires purity. Likewise, someone turned away from Hari cannot reach the highest state. The kings' desire for Sita is therefore pointless.
ramacharitamanas::1439.simple_insight: Not every desire can be satisfied by wanting harder. Some aims collapse the moment greed enters them.
ramacharitamanas::1439.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the challenge around Sita's swayamvar exposes the kings' motives. Tulsidas cuts through their pride: a mind driven by greed or desire cannot claim purity or the highest release. Their longing for Sita is not noble aspiration, but distortion.
ramacharitamanas::1439.modern_relevance: You want recognition, but the need to be praised is exactly what makes your work feel hollow. The more you chase validation, the less clean your effort becomes.
ramacharitamanas::1439.insight: It shifts the mind from craving outcomes to seeing whether the craving itself has already spoiled the aim.

ramacharitamanas::1440.verse_sanskrit: कोलाहलु सुनि सीय सकानी। सखीं लवाइ गईं जहँ रानी॥ रामु सुभायँ चले गुरु पाहीं। सिय सनेहु बरनत मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1440.verse_hindi: कोलाहल सुनकर सीताजी शंकित हो गईं। तब सखियाँ उन्हें वहाँ ले गईं, जहाँ रानी (सीताजी की माता) थीं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी मन में सीताजी के प्रेम का बखान करते हुए स्वाभाविक चाल से गुरुजी के पास चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1440.english_translation: Hearing the uproar, Sita became alarmed. Her companions took her to where the queen was. Ram then naturally went to the teacher, while thinking of Sita's love in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::1440.translation_literal: कोलाहलु (uproar/noise) / सुनि (hearing) / सीय (Sita) / सकानी (became alarmed) / सखीं (companions) / लवाइ (taking along) / गईं (went) / जहँ (where) / रानी (the queen) / रामु (Ram) / सुभायँ (naturally) / चले (went) / गुरु पाहीं (to the teacher) / सिय (Sita) / सनेहु (love) / बरनत (describing) / मन माहीं (in the mind)
ramacharitamanas::1440.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1440.essence: Outward calm can hold deep feeling without losing direction.
ramacharitamanas::1440.simple_meaning: Sita is startled by the commotion and taken to the queen. Ram quietly goes to his teacher, carrying Sita's love in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::1440.simple_insight: Love and duty can move at once, each in its own way.
ramacharitamanas::1440.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the hall erupts with noise and tension. Sita grows uneasy and is guided to the queen's side. At the same time, Ram walks calmly to his teacher, inwardly holding Sita in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::1440.modern_relevance: In a crowded wedding hall, everyone is whispering about what just happened. One person panics, another steadies the room, and the one at the center keeps moving with quiet grace.
ramacharitamanas::1440.insight: It separates outward action from inward feeling: Ram stays composed while love remains alive within him.

ramacharitamanas::1441.verse_sanskrit: रानिन्ह सहित सोच बस सीया। अब धौं बिधिहि काह करनीया॥ भूप बचन सुनि इत उत तकहीं। लखनु राम डर बोलि न सकहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1441.verse_hindi: रानियों सहित सीताजी (दुष्ट राजाओं के दुर्वचन सुनकर) सोच के वश हैं कि न जाने विधाता अब क्या करने वाले हैं। राजाओं के वचन सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी इधर-उधर ताकते हैं, किन्तु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के डर से कुछ बोल नहीं सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1441.english_translation: Sita, along with the queens, is overcome with worry: what will fate do now? Hearing the kings' words, Lakshman looks here and there, but out of fear of Ram he cannot speak.
ramacharitamanas::1441.translation_literal: रानिन्ह (with the queens) / सहित (together with) / सोच (worry) / बस (under control) / सीया (Sita) / अब (now) / धौं (indeed/then) / बिधिहि (fate) / काह (what) / करनीया (to be done) / भूप (kings) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / इत (here) / उत (there) / तकहीं (they look) / लखनु (Lakshman) / रामु (Ram) / डर (fear) / बोलि (speaking) / न (not) / सकहीं (are able)
ramacharitamanas::1441.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1441.essence: Anxious hearts and restrained speech sharpen the moment before action.
ramacharitamanas::1441.simple_meaning: Sita and the queens are anxious about what will happen next. Lakshman, hearing the kings, keeps looking around but stays silent because he fears Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::1441.simple_insight: Tension can freeze even the boldest person. Fear of a higher authority can hold back speech.
ramacharitamanas::1441.detailed_meaning: At the swayamvar, the kings' harsh words and the rising tension unsettle the women nearby, including Sita. Lakshman is stirred too, but he restrains himself because Ram is present. The scene builds pressure before the decisive response.
ramacharitamanas::1441.modern_relevance: You sit in a room where someone says something insulting, and everyone feels the air tighten. You want to speak, but the presence of one respected person keeps you controlled.
ramacharitamanas::1441.insight: It shows how social pressure and reverence can silence reaction, even when anger is rising.

ramacharitamanas::1442.verse_sanskrit: अरुन नयन भृकुटी कुटिल चितवत नृपन्ह सकोप। मनहुँ मत्त गजगन निरखि सिंघकिसोरहि चोप ॥
ramacharitamanas::1442.verse_hindi: उनके नेत्र लाल और भौंहें टेढ़ी हो गईं और वे क्रोध से राजाओं की ओर देखने लगे, मानो मतवाले हाथियों का झुंड देखकर सिंह के बच्चे को जोश आ गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1442.english_translation: Their eyes turned red, their brows twisted in anger, and they stared fiercely at the kings, like a lion cub facing a herd of drunk elephants.
ramacharitamanas::1442.translation_literal: अरुन (red) / नयन (eyes) / भृकुटी (brows) / कुटिल (crooked) / चितवत (gazing) / नृपन्ह (at the kings) / सकोप (with anger) / मनहुँ (as if) / मत्त (drunken) / गजगन (herd of elephants) / निरखि (seeing) / सिंघकिसोरहि (lion cub) / चोप (agitation / fierce spirit)
ramacharitamanas::1442.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1442.essence: Fierce anger rises when pride meets a real challenge.
ramacharitamanas::1442.simple_meaning: The kings' fierce challenge fills the scene with anger and tension. Their look is compared to a lion cub bristling at a herd of elephants.
ramacharitamanas::1442.simple_insight: Some moments do not invite calm. They wake up raw courage and sharpen the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::1442.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the kings' noisy arrogance has pushed the gathering to the edge. The room tightens as their faces harden with anger. This verse paints that rising heat just before the bow of Shiva is broken.
ramacharitamanas::1442.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where someone has just spoken too boldly. The air changes instantly; everyone feels the challenge before a single reply is made.
ramacharitamanas::1442.insight: It frames conflict as a visible surge of force, not just a private feeling.

ramacharitamanas::1443.verse_sanskrit: खरभरु देखि बिकल पुर नारीं। सब मिलि देहिं महीपन्ह गारीं॥ तेहिं अवसर सुनि सिवधनु भंगा। आयउ भृगुकुल कमल पतंगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1443.verse_hindi: खलबली देखकर जनकपुरी की स्त्रियाँ व्याकुल हो गईं और सब मिलकर राजाओं को गालियाँ देने लगीं। उसी मौके पर शिवजी के धनुष का टूटना सुनकर भृगुकुल रूपी कमल के सूर्य परशुरामजी आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1443.english_translation: Seeing the uproar, the women of Janakpur became agitated and all together began to curse the kings. At that moment, hearing that Shiva's bow had been broken, Parashuram came like the sun to the lotus of Bhrigu's line.
ramacharitamanas::1443.translation_literal: खरभरु (uproar) / देखि (seeing) / बिकल (agitated) / पुर (of the city) / नारीं (women) / सब (all) / मिलि (together) / देहिं (give) / महीपन्ह (to the kings) / गारीं (curses) / तेहिं (that) / अवसर (moment) / सुनि (hearing) / सिवधनु (Shiva's bow) / भंगा (broken) / आयउ (came) / भृगुकुल (Bhrigu line) / कमल (lotus) / पतंगा (sun)
ramacharitamanas::1443.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1443.essence: One broken bow brings a new storm into the court.
ramacharitamanas::1443.simple_meaning: The crowd in Janakpur is shaken, the women curse the kings, and Parashuram arrives after hearing that Shiva's bow has been broken.
ramacharitamanas::1443.simple_insight: A single event can turn celebration into danger in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::1443.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the wedding assembly has turned chaotic after Shiva's bow is broken. The women of the city react in alarm and anger, while the news reaches Parashuram, whose arrival signals that the contest has crossed into a far more dangerous moment.
ramacharitamanas::1443.modern_relevance: A room that was cheering a minute ago goes silent after one bad headline. Joy can flip into tension before anyone has time to breathe.
ramacharitamanas::1443.insight: It shifts attention from the wedding's success to the immediate threat the broken bow now creates.

ramacharitamanas::1444.verse_sanskrit: देखि महीप सकल सकुचाने। बाज झपट जनु लवा लुकाने॥ गौरि सरीर भूति भल भ्राजा। भाल बिसाल त्रिपुंड बिराजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1444.verse_hindi: इन्हें देखकर सब राजा सकुचा गए, मानो बाज के झपटने पर बटेर लुक (छिप) गए हों। गोरे शरीर पर विभूति (भस्म) बड़ी फब रही है और विशाल ललाट पर त्रिपुण्ड्र विशेष शोभा दे रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1444.english_translation: Seeing him, all the kings grew uneasy, like quails hiding when a hawk swoops down. Sacred ash shone beautifully on his fair body, and the triple mark on his broad forehead stood out with special grace.
ramacharitamanas::1444.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / महीप (kings) / सकल (all) / सकुचाने (became uneasy) / बाज (hawk) / झपट (swoop) / जनु (as if) / लवा (quails) / लुकाने (hid) / गौरि (fair/white) / सरीर (body) / भूति (ash) / भल (well/beautifully) / भ्राजा (shone) / भाल (forehead) / बिसाल (broad) / त्रिपुंड (triple mark) / बिराजा (shone beautifully)
ramacharitamanas::1444.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1444.essence: True presence makes pride shrink before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1444.simple_meaning: The kings felt shaken at his sight. His ash-covered body and sacred forehead markings stood out with striking grace.
ramacharitamanas::1444.simple_insight: Sometimes presence alone changes the room before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1444.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the assembled kings are already rattled after Shiva's bow has broken. Now they see the fierce, ash-marked ascetic before them, and their confidence collapses even further. The verse pauses on his appearance before the next movement of the scene.
ramacharitamanas::1444.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the mood shifts before you speak. Everyone senses steadiness, or fear, or power — and reacts instantly.
ramacharitamanas::1444.insight: It shows how embodied presence can unsettle pride and command attention without argument.

ramacharitamanas::1445.verse_sanskrit: सीस जटा ससिबदनु सुहावा। रिस बस कछुक अरुन होइ आवा॥ भृकुटी कुटिल नयन रिस राते। सहजहुँ चितवत मनहुँ रिसाते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1445.verse_hindi: सिर पर जटा है, सुंदर मुखचन्द्र क्रोध के कारण कुछ लाल हो आया है। भौंहें टेढ़ी और आँखें क्रोध से लाल हैं। सहज ही देखते हैं, तो भी ऐसा जान पड़ता है मानो क्रोध कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1445.english_translation: His hair is matted, his face is moon-like and lovely, but anger has made it slightly red. His brows are crooked, his eyes are red with fury, and even his calm glance seems full of anger.
ramacharitamanas::1445.translation_literal: सीस (head) / जटा (matted hair) / ससिबदनु (moon-faced) / सुहावा (lovely) / रिस बस (under the sway of anger) / कछुक (somewhat) / अरुन (red) / होइ आवा (has become) ॥ भृकुटी (brows) / कुटिल (crooked) / नयन (eyes) / रिस राते (reddened by anger) / सहजहुँ (even naturally) / चितवत (while looking) / मनहुँ (as if) / रिसाते (angry)
ramacharitamanas::1445.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1445.essence: Beauty and anger can live in the same face.
ramacharitamanas::1445.simple_meaning: The man is described as outwardly beautiful but visibly angered, with red eyes and a tense face.
ramacharitamanas::1445.simple_insight: Even a calm presence can feel fierce when justice is at stake.
ramacharitamanas::1445.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, the kings have just failed to lift Shiva’s bow. The crowd is tense, and the poem pauses to describe the fierce, ascetic figure who has arrived. His beauty remains, but anger has sharpened his face.
ramacharitamanas::1445.modern_relevance: You see someone quiet at a family gathering, but their jaw is tight and their eyes are fixed. The silence is not emptiness; it is pressure before speech.
ramacharitamanas::1445.insight: It teaches you to read the emotional charge beneath a composed exterior.

ramacharitamanas::1446.verse_sanskrit: बृषभ कंध उर बाहु बिसाला। चारु जनेउ माल मृगछाला॥ कटि मुनिबसन तून दुइ बाँधें। धनु सर कर कुठारु कल काँधें ॥
