ramacharitamanas::1446.verse_hindi: बैल के समान (ऊँचे और पुष्ट) कंधे हैं, छाती और भुजाएँ विशाल हैं। सुंदर यज्ञोपवीत धारण किए, माला पहने और मृगचर्म लिए हैं। कमर में मुनियों का वस्त्र (वल्कल) और दो तरकस बाँधे हैं। हाथ में धनुष-बाण और सुंदर कंधे पर फरसा धारण किए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1446.english_translation: His shoulders are like a bull's, with broad chest and arms. He wears the sacred thread, a garland, and deer skin. Around his waist are tied a hermit's cloth and two quivers; in his hands are a bow, arrows, and an axe on his graceful shoulder.
ramacharitamanas::1446.translation_literal: बृषभ (bull) / कंध (shoulders) / उर (chest) / बाहु (arms) / बिसाला (broad) / चारु (beautiful) / जनेउ (sacred thread) / माल (garland) / मृगछाला (deer skin) / कटि (waist) / मुनिबसन (hermit's cloth) / तून (quivers) / दुइ (two) / बाँधें (tied) / धनु (bow) / सर (arrows) / कर (in hand) / कुठारु (axe) / कल (graceful) / काँधें (on the shoulder)
ramacharitamanas::1446.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1446.essence: True strength can wear the clothes of simplicity.
ramacharitamanas::1446.simple_meaning: The figure is dressed like a hermit but armed like a warrior. His body, clothes, and weapons all show a strange mix of restraint and power.
ramacharitamanas::1446.simple_insight: Outward simplicity can hold enormous strength.
ramacharitamanas::1446.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the assembled kings see a remarkable figure enter in a hermit's dress. His body is strong, his weapons are ready, and the contrast unsettles everyone. This verse completes that startling appearance.
ramacharitamanas::1446.modern_relevance: Someone walks into the room in plain clothes, carrying no ego, yet everyone feels the weight of their presence. The strongest person is not always the loudest one.
ramacharitamanas::1446.insight: It shifts attention from appearance alone to the disciplined power hidden beneath restraint.

ramacharitamanas::1447.verse_sanskrit: सांत बेषु करनी कठिन बरनि न जाइ सरूप। धरि मुनितनु जनु बीर रसु आयउ जहँ सब भूप ॥
ramacharitamanas::1447.verse_hindi: शांत वेष है, परन्तु करनी बहुत कठोर हैं, स्वरूप का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। मानो वीर रस ही मुनि का शरीर धारण करके, जहाँ सब राजा लोग हैं, वहाँ आ गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1447.english_translation: His dress is calm, but his deeds are severe; his form cannot be described. It is as if heroic energy itself has taken a sage’s body and come among all the kings.
ramacharitamanas::1447.translation_literal: सांत (calm) / बेषु (dress) / करनी (deeds, conduct) / कठिन (severe, hard) / बरनि (described) / न जाइ (cannot be) / सरूप (form) / धरि (having taken) / मुनितनु (sage-body) / जनु (as if) / बीर रसु (heroic sentiment) / आयउ (came) / जहँ (where) / सब (all) / भूप (kings)
ramacharitamanas::1447.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1447.essence: A peaceful appearance can hide overwhelming force.
ramacharitamanas::1447.simple_meaning: He looks like a calm sage, but his actions are fierce and powerful. He seems like heroic force itself has taken a saint’s body and entered the royal gathering.
ramacharitamanas::1447.simple_insight: Appearances can mislead; a quiet exterior may hide immense force.
ramacharitamanas::1447.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, the kings are waiting for the bow contest. Parashurama arrives with the calm look of a sage, but everyone senses his fierce power. Tulsidas paints him as heroic energy in a saint’s body, heightening the fear before he speaks.
ramacharitamanas::1447.modern_relevance: A soft-spoken person walks into the room wearing simple clothes, and the whole atmosphere changes. You realize calmness is not weakness, and restraint can carry real force.
ramacharitamanas::1447.insight: It trains you to read character beyond appearance and respect power that does not advertise itself.

ramacharitamanas::1448.verse_sanskrit: देखत भृगुपति बेषु कराला। उठे सकल भय बिकल भुआला॥ पितु समेत कहि कहि निज नामा। लगे करन सब दंड प्रनामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1448.verse_hindi: परशुरामजी का भयानक वेष देखकर सब राजा भय से व्याकुल हो उठ खड़े हुए और पिता सहित अपना नाम कह-कहकर सब दंडवत प्रणाम करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1448.english_translation: Seeing Parashurama's terrible form, all the kings rose in fear and became agitated. Naming themselves and their fathers again and again, they all bowed down flat in reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1448.translation_literal: देखत (seeing) / भृगुपति (lord of the Bhrigu line, Parashurama) / बेषु (form/appearance) / कराला (terrible, fierce) / उठे (rose) / सकल (all) / भय (fear) / बिकल (disturbed, agitated) / भुआला (kings) / पितु (father) / समेत (along with) / कहि कहि (saying again and again) / निज (own) / नामा (names) / लगे (began) / करन (to do) / सब (all) / दंड प्रनामा (full prostrating bows)
ramacharitamanas::1448.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1448.essence: Pride dissolves when fear enters the room.
ramacharitamanas::1448.simple_meaning: The kings see Parashurama's fierce appearance and are shaken. They stand up, state their names and fathers, and bow fully in fear.
ramacharitamanas::1448.simple_insight: Fear can strip away pride in an instant and make even kings humble.
ramacharitamanas::1448.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's court during Sita's swayamvar, Parashurama arrives in a fierce form. The assembled kings, already tense, are startled into submission and begin bowing and identifying themselves. The scene shows how fragile royal pride is before overwhelming force.
ramacharitamanas::1448.modern_relevance: A room goes silent when the senior judge walks in and everyone straightens their papers. Status vanishes in a second; the body tells the truth before the mouth does.
ramacharitamanas::1448.insight: It shows how power can collapse self-importance and force immediate humility.

ramacharitamanas::1449.verse_sanskrit: जेहि सुभायँ चितवहिं हितु जानी। सो जानइ जनु आइ खुटानी॥ जनक बहोरि आइ सिरु नावा। सीय बोलाइ प्रनामु करावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1449.verse_hindi: परशुरामजी हित समझकर भी सहज ही जिसकी ओर देख लेते हैं, वह समझता है मानो मेरी आयु पूरी हो गई। फिर जनकजी ने आकर सिर नवाया और सीताजी को बुलाकर प्रणाम कराया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1449.english_translation: Whoever Parashurama looks at with goodwill feels as if his life has reached its end. Then King Janaka came and bowed his head, and he called Sita forward to offer salutations.
ramacharitamanas::1449.translation_literal: जेहि (to whom) / सुभायँ (by good nature) / चितवहिं (he looks) / हितु (for welfare) / जानी (knowing) / सो (that one) / जानइ (knows) / जनु (as if) / आइ (came) / खुटानी (the end of life) / जनक (Janaka) / बहोरि (again) / आइ (came) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / सीय (Sita) / बोलाइ (calling) / प्रनामु (salutation) / करावा (made do)
ramacharitamanas::1449.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1449.essence: Humility is the only safe response to overwhelming force.
ramacharitamanas::1449.simple_meaning: Parashurama's gaze is so fierce that even a kind look from him feels like death. Janaka returns, bows again, and brings Sita forward to salute him.
ramacharitamanas::1449.simple_insight: Some presences are so intense that even kindness feels overwhelming.
ramacharitamanas::1449.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, Parashurama has just arrived in his terrifying form and the kings are shaken. Even a glance from him feels fatal. Janaka returns, bows again, and brings Sita to offer respect before the tense meeting continues.
ramacharitamanas::1449.modern_relevance: A room goes silent when the senior partner walks in after the failed presentation. Everyone straightens up, rereads the mood, and lowers their voice before speaking again.
ramacharitamanas::1449.insight: It shows how to respond to overwhelming authority with humility instead of resistance.

ramacharitamanas::1450.verse_sanskrit: आसिष दीन्हि सखीं हरषानीं। निज समाज लै गईं सयानीं॥ बिस्वामित्रु मिले पुनि आई। पद सरोज मेले दोउ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1450.verse_hindi: परशुरामजी ने सीताजी को आशीर्वाद दिया। सखियाँ हर्षित हुईं और (वहाँ अब अधिक देर ठहरना ठीक न समझकर) वे सयानी सखियाँ उनको अपनी मंडली में ले गईं। फिर विश्वामित्रजी आकर मिले और उन्होंने दोनों भाइयों को उनके चरण कमलों पर गिराया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1450.english_translation: The wise companions, delighted, gave blessings and took Sita back into their group. Then Vishvamitra came again and made both brothers bow at his lotus feet.
ramacharitamanas::1450.translation_literal: आसिष (blessings) / दीन्हि (gave) / सखीं (companions) / हरषानीं (delighted) / निज (own) / समाज (group) / लै (taking) / गईं (went) / सयानीं (wise women) ॥ / बिस्वामित्रु (Vishvamitra) / मिले (met) / पुनि (again) / आई (came) / पद (feet) / सरोज (lotus) / मेले (placed) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1450.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1450.essence: Blessing and bowing keep sacred moments in motion.
ramacharitamanas::1450.simple_meaning: Sita receives blessings, and her companions take her back with them. Then Vishvamitra arrives and both brothers bow at his feet.
ramacharitamanas::1450.simple_insight: Some moments are not for lingering. Blessing, reunion, and respect each have their own place.
ramacharitamanas::1450.detailed_meaning: After Sita’s swayamvar, the joyful women bless her and guide her back into their circle. Vishvamitra then returns and the two brothers bow to him. The verse simply moves the scene forward between the wedding joy and the next exchange.
ramacharitamanas::1450.modern_relevance: At a wedding, the elders finish their blessings, the bride is led away, and the next greeting begins. Not every beautiful moment is meant to be held onto.
ramacharitamanas::1450.insight: It keeps the scene moving from celebration to reverence, showing social grace and order.

ramacharitamanas::1451.verse_sanskrit: रामु लखनु दसरथ के ढोटा। दीन्हि असीस देखि भल जोटा॥ रामहि चितइ रहे थकि लोचन। रूप अपार मार मद मोचन ॥
ramacharitamanas::1451.verse_hindi: (विश्वामित्रजी ने कहा-) ये राम और लक्ष्मण राजा दशरथ के पुत्र हैं। उनकी सुंदर जोड़ी देखकर परशुरामजी ने आशीर्वाद दिया। कामदेव के भी मद को छुड़ाने वाले श्री रामचन्द्रजी के अपार रूप को देखकर उनके नेत्र थकित (स्तम्भित) हो रहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1451.english_translation: These are Ram and Lakshman, the sons of King Dasharath. Seeing the beautiful pair, Parashurama gave his blessing. His eyes grew fixed, gazing at Ram's boundless form, the one who removes even Cupid's pride.
ramacharitamanas::1451.translation_literal: रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / के (of) / ढोटा (sons) / दीन्हि (gave) / असीस (blessing) / देखि (seeing) / भल (beautiful) / जोटा (pair)॥ / रामहि (at Ram) / चितइ (gazing) / रहे (remained) / थकि (fatigued/fixed) / लोचन (eyes) / रूप (form) / अपार (boundless) / मार (Cupid) / मद (pride/intoxication) / मोचन (remover) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1451.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1451.essence: Ram's presence stops pride before it can speak.
ramacharitamanas::1451.simple_meaning: Parashurama sees Ram and Lakshman together, blesses them, and becomes absorbed in Ram's extraordinary beauty and power.
ramacharitamanas::1451.simple_insight: Some presence is so complete that even an angry mind falls silent before it.
ramacharitamanas::1451.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the marriage gathering is still tense after Parashurama's arrival. He looks at the two princes, blesses them, and then cannot look away from Ram's incomparable form. This pause before his next outburst heightens the drama.
ramacharitamanas::1451.modern_relevance: You enter a room already charged with tension, and one person's calm presence changes the whole atmosphere. Before anyone speaks, the mood has already shifted.
ramacharitamanas::1451.insight: It shifts attention from conflict to the quiet authority that can hold conflict without flinching.

ramacharitamanas::1452.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि बिलोकि बिदेह सन कहहु काह अति भीर। पूँछत जानि अजान जिमि ब्यापेउ कोपु सरीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::1452.verse_hindi: फिर सब देखकर, जानते हुए भी अनजान की तरह जनकजी से पूछते हैं कि कहो, यह बड़ी भारी भीड़ कैसी है? उनके शरीर में क्रोध छा गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1452.english_translation: Then, looking around, he asked Janaka, “Why is there such a great crowd here?” Though he knew, he asked as if unaware, and anger filled his body.
ramacharitamanas::1452.translation_literal: बहुरि (again) / बिलोकि (looking) / बिदेह सन (to Janaka of Videha) / कहहु (say) / काह (what) / अति (very) / भीर (crowd) / पूँछत (asking) / जानि (knowing) / अजान (unaware) / जिमि (as if) / ब्यापेउ (spread) / कोपु (anger) / सरीर (body)
ramacharitamanas::1452.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1452.essence: Knowing the answer, he still asks — and anger is already in control.
ramacharitamanas::1452.simple_meaning: Parashurama asks Janaka about the crowd, though he already knows the answer. His anger is already rising.
ramacharitamanas::1452.simple_insight: A person can ask a question while already burning inside.
ramacharitamanas::1452.detailed_meaning: At Janaka’s court, Parashurama has just arrived after seeing Ram and Lakshman. He looks around and asks about the huge gathering, even though he understands the situation. The line shows anger gathering before the confrontation begins.
ramacharitamanas::1452.modern_relevance: You walk into a room already tense, then ask a question you know will expose the problem. Everyone can feel the heat before anyone speaks plainly.
ramacharitamanas::1452.insight: It shows how pride can turn a simple question into a warning sign of conflict.

ramacharitamanas::1453.verse_sanskrit: समाचार कहि जनक सुनाए। जेहि कारन महीप सब आए॥ सुनत बचन फिरि अनत निहारे। देखे चापखंड महि डारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1453.verse_hindi: जिस कारण सब राजा आए थे, राजा जनक ने वे सब समाचार कह सुनाए। जनक के वचन सुनकर परशुरामजी ने फिरकर दूसरी ओर देखा तो धनुष के टुकड़े पृथ्वी पर पड़े हुए दिखाई दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1453.english_translation: Janaka explained the situation and told why all the kings had come. Hearing him, Parashurama looked elsewhere and saw the broken pieces of the bow lying on the ground.
ramacharitamanas::1453.translation_literal: समाचार (news / account) / कहि (having told) / जनक (Janaka) / सुनाए (made heard, explained) / जेहि कारन (for which reason) / महीप (kings) / सब (all) / आए (came) ॥ / सुनत (hearing) / बचन (words) / फिरि (turning back) / अनत (elsewhere) / निहारे (looked) / देखे (saw) / चापखंड (pieces of the bow) / महि (on the ground) / डारे (thrown, lying) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1453.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1453.essence: The broken bow is seen before the anger is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1453.simple_meaning: Janaka explains why the kings have gathered. Parashurama turns and sees the shattered bow on the ground.
ramacharitamanas::1453.simple_insight: Sometimes the truth is already visible before anger fully speaks.
ramacharitamanas::1453.detailed_meaning: In Janaka’s hall at the swayamvar, the kings have gathered around the broken bow. Janaka explains the reason for the assembly, and Parashurama, still simmering, turns and notices the shattered pieces. The sight sets up his furious response.
ramacharitamanas::1453.modern_relevance: You finally look up from the argument and see the broken object on the floor, the silence in the room, the damage already done. The facts are there before the shouting starts.
ramacharitamanas::1453.insight: It shifts attention from the explanation to the visible evidence that will trigger the next conflict.

ramacharitamanas::1454.verse_sanskrit: अति रिस बोले बचन कठोरा। कहु जड़ जनक धनुष कै तोरा॥ बेगि देखाउ मूढ़ न त आजू। उलटउँ महि जहँ लहि तव राजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1454.verse_hindi: अत्यन्त क्रोध में भरकर वे कठोर वचन बोले- रे मूर्ख जनक! बता, धनुष किसने तोड़ा? उसे शीघ्र दिखा, नहीं तो अरे मूढ़! आज मैं जहाँ तक तेरा राज्य है, वहाँ तक की पृथ्वी उलट दूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1454.english_translation: In great rage, he spoke harsh words: "Tell me, foolish Janak, who broke the bow? Show me quickly, fool, or today I will overturn the earth as far as your kingdom extends."
ramacharitamanas::1454.translation_literal: अति (very) / रिस (rage) / बोले (spoke) / बचन (words) / कठोरा (harsh) / कहु (tell) / जड़ (foolish) / जनक (Janak) / धनुष (bow) / कै (of) / तोरा (broke) / बेगि (quickly) / देखाउ (show) / मूढ़ (fool) / न (not) / त (then) / आजू (today) / उलटउँ (I will overturn) / महि (earth) / जहँ लहि (as far as) / तव (your) / राजू (kingdom)
ramacharitamanas::1454.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1454.essence: Anger makes even power speak like a threat.
ramacharitamanas::1454.simple_meaning: Parashurama, furious, insults Janak and demands to know who broke the bow. He threatens to destroy the kingdom if he is not shown immediately.
ramacharitamanas::1454.simple_insight: Unchecked anger turns power into a threat instead of wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::1454.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court after the bow is broken, Parashurama turns in fury and demands an answer. The king is stunned, the assembly falls silent, and the moment becomes dangerous because one man's rage can unmake the entire wedding scene.
ramacharitamanas::1454.modern_relevance: A senior manager slams a report on the table and asks who ruined it, not really listening for an answer. The room freezes because anger has already taken over the conversation.
ramacharitamanas::1454.insight: It shows how anger seeks domination first and truth second.

ramacharitamanas::1455.verse_sanskrit: अति डरु उतरु देत नृपु नाहीं। कुटिल भूप हरषे मन माहीं॥ सुर मुनि नाग नगर नर नारी। सोचहिं सकल त्रास उर भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1455.verse_hindi: राजा को अत्यन्त डर लगा, जिसके कारण वे उत्तर नहीं देते। यह देखकर कुटिल राजा मन में बड़े प्रसन्न हुए। देवता, मुनि, नाग और नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष सभी सोच करने लगे, सबके हृदय में बड़ा भय है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1455.english_translation: The king was so afraid that he could not answer. The crooked king was pleased in his heart. Devas, sages, serpents, and all men and women in the city were filled with fear.
ramacharitamanas::1455.translation_literal: अति (very) / डरु (fear) / उतरु (answer) / देत (giving) / नृपु (king) / नाहीं (not) / कुटिल (crooked) / भूप (king) / हरषे (rejoiced) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / सुर (devas) / मुनि (sages) / नाग (serpents) / नगर (city) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / सोचहिं (are worried) / सकल (all) / त्रास (fear) / उर (heart) / भारी (heavy)
ramacharitamanas::1455.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1455.essence: Fear can silence a king and spread through an entire city.
ramacharitamanas::1455.simple_meaning: King Janak cannot answer because he is terrified. Parashurama feels pleased, while everyone in the city is shaken with fear.
ramacharitamanas::1455.simple_insight: Fear spreads fast when power turns hostile. One person’s silence can make an entire room hold its breath.
ramacharitamanas::1455.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s court, Parashurama’s anger has frozen the king and shaken everyone present. Janak cannot speak, Parashurama enjoys the fear, and devas, sages, serpents, and townspeople all feel the pressure of the moment.
ramacharitamanas::1455.modern_relevance: You are in a meeting when one senior voice turns sharp and nobody dares respond. The whole room tightens, and even the confident people start thinking twice.
ramacharitamanas::1455.insight: It shows how intimidation silences action and how fear becomes collective in a charged atmosphere.

ramacharitamanas::1456.verse_sanskrit: मन पछिताति सीय महतारी। बिधि अब सँवरी बात बिगारी॥ भृगुपति कर सुभाउ सुनि सीता। अरध निमेष कलप सम बीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1456.verse_hindi: सीताजी की माता मन में पछता रही हैं कि हाय! विधाता ने अब बनी-बनाई बात बिगाड़ दी। परशुरामजी का स्वभाव सुनकर सीताजी को आधा क्षण भी कल्प के समान बीतते लगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1456.english_translation: Sita's mother regretted in her heart: "Alas, fate has spoiled what was already settled." Hearing Parashurama's fierce nature, Sita felt even half a moment stretch like a cosmic age.
ramacharitamanas::1456.translation_literal: मन (mind) / पछिताति (regrets) / सीय (Sita's) / महतारी (mother) / बिधि (fate) / अब (now) / सँवरी (settled) / बात (matter) / बिगारी (spoiled) / भृगुपति (lord of the Bhrigu clan, Parashurama) / कर (of) / सुभाउ (nature) / सुनि (hearing) / सीता (Sita) / अरध (half) / निमेष (moment) / कलप (cosmic age) / सम (like) / बीता (passed)
ramacharitamanas::1456.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1456.essence: Fear can make a single moment feel like an age.
ramacharitamanas::1456.simple_meaning: Sita's mother feels regret as the marriage situation turns tense, and Sita becomes so afraid of Parashurama that even a moment feels endless.
ramacharitamanas::1456.simple_insight: Fear stretches time and makes a settled moment feel fragile.
ramacharitamanas::1456.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the broken bow has brought Parashurama into the scene, and the whole court is shaken. Sita's mother regrets how quickly joy has turned to danger, while Sita herself trembles before Parashurama's fierce presence. The verse holds that tense pause before Ram speaks.
ramacharitamanas::1456.modern_relevance: You are waiting outside a room while a hard conversation unfolds inside. Every second feels longer than it should, and one wrong word could change everything.
ramacharitamanas::1456.insight: It captures how anxiety distorts time and makes calm situations feel unstable.

ramacharitamanas::1457.verse_sanskrit: सभय बिलोके लोग सब जानि जानकी भीरु। हृदयँ न हरषु बिषादु कछु बोले श्रीरघुबीरु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1457.verse_hindi: तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी सब लोगों को भयभीत देखकर और सीताजी को डरी हुई जानकर बोले- उनके हृदय में न कुछ हर्ष था न विषाद- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1457.english_translation: Then Shri Ramchandra saw everyone frightened and Sita afraid, yet his own heart held neither joy nor sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::1457.translation_literal: सभय (fearful) / बिलोके (looked) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / जानि (knowing) / जानकी (Janaki, Sita) / भीरु (afraid) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / न (not) / हरषु (joy) / बिषादु (sorrow) / कछु (any) / बोले (spoke) / श्रीरघुबीरु (Shri Raghuvir, Ram)
ramacharitamanas::1457.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1457.essence: True composure stays untouched by fear or excitement.
ramacharitamanas::1457.simple_meaning: Ram sees the crowd frightened and Sita afraid, but he stays beyond both excitement and distress before speaking.
ramacharitamanas::1457.simple_insight: Calm presence can steady a room more than any argument.
ramacharitamanas::1457.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, Parashuram's anger has frozen everyone in fear. Sita is shaken, the crowd is tense, and Ram remains inwardly unmoved. His next words come from that unruffled center.
ramacharitamanas::1457.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after a harsh email lands on the screen. Everyone is bracing for the worst, but one person reads it, breathes, and answers without panic. That steadiness changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::1457.insight: It teaches you to answer pressure without being pulled into its mood.

ramacharitamanas::1458.verse_sanskrit: नाथ संभुधनु भंजनिहारा। होइहि केउ एक दास तुम्हारा॥ आयसु काह कहिअ किन मोही। सुनि रिसाइ बोले मुनि कोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1458.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! शिवजी के धनुष को तोड़ने वाला आपका कोई एक दास ही होगा। क्या आज्ञा है, मुझसे क्यों नहीं कहते? यह सुनकर क्रोधी मुनि रिसाकर बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1458.english_translation: O Lord, the one who broke Shiva's bow will be your servant. Why not tell me your command? Hearing this, the angry sage spoke in fury.
ramacharitamanas::1458.translation_literal: नाथ (lord) / संभु-धनु (Shiva's bow) / भंजनिहारा (breaker) / होइहि (will be) / केउ (someone) / एक (one) / दास (servant) / तुम्हारा (your) / आयसु (command) / काह (why) / कहिअ (should be said) / किन (why not) / मोही (to me) / सुनि (hearing) / रिसाइ (angrily) / बोले (spoke) / मुनि (sage) / कोही (angry)
ramacharitamanas::1458.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1458.essence: Pride hears service as insult and answers with anger.
ramacharitamanas::1458.simple_meaning: Parashurama says the bow-breaker must be Ram's servant, and asks why Ram has not given him orders. Hearing this, he grows angry.
ramacharitamanas::1458.simple_insight: Pride can mistake itself for service and turn instantly into anger.
ramacharitamanas::1458.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, after Shiva's bow is broken, Parashurama confronts Ram. He assumes the archer must be a servant and demands to be addressed. The moment is tense: one proud sage stands before the calm prince, and the next line reveals his fury.
ramacharitamanas::1458.modern_relevance: Someone corrects you in public and you feel your face heat up before you even think. The ego wants status, not truth.
ramacharitamanas::1458.insight: It exposes how quickly wounded pride turns a conversation into conflict.

ramacharitamanas::1459.verse_sanskrit: सेवकु सो जो करै सेवकाई। अरि करनी करि करिअ लराई॥ सुनहु राम जेहिं सिवधनु तोरा। सहसबाहु सम सो रिपु मोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1459.verse_hindi: सेवक वह है जो सेवा का काम करे। शत्रु का काम करके तो लड़ाई ही करनी चाहिए। हे राम! सुनो, जिसने शिवजी के धनुष को तोड़ा है, वह सहस्रबाहु के समान मेरा शत्रु है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1459.english_translation: A servant is one who does a servant’s work. If someone does an enemy’s deed, then only battle remains. Listen, Ram: the one who broke Shiva’s bow is my enemy, equal to Sahasrabahu.
ramacharitamanas::1459.translation_literal: सेवकु (servant) / सो (that one) / जो (who) / करै (does) / सेवकाई (service) / अरि (enemy) / करनी (deed) / करि (doing) / करिअ (should be done) / लराई (fight) / सुनहु (listen) / राम (Ram) / जेहिं (who) / सिवधनु (Shiva’s bow) / तोरा (broke) / सहसबाहु (Sahasrabahu) / सम (equal to) / सो (that one) / रिपु (enemy) / मोरा (my)
ramacharitamanas::1459.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1459.essence: A servant cannot act like an enemy and still claim service.
ramacharitamanas::1459.simple_meaning: A true servant acts in service, not in opposition. Parashurama sees the bow-breaker as an enemy and prepares for conflict.
ramacharitamanas::1459.simple_insight: Service and hostility cannot be mixed. The mind must know which role it is playing.
ramacharitamanas::1459.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, Parashurama has just heard that Shiva’s bow was broken. He reacts like a warrior-sage whose honor has been struck. In this tense exchange, he defines service and enemy action before confronting Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1459.modern_relevance: A team member says they will help, then quietly blocks the project in meetings. Everyone feels the split immediately. This verse names that fracture: service cannot wear the mask of sabotage.
ramacharitamanas::1459.insight: It separates loyal action from hostile action, making the conflict explicit instead of hidden.

ramacharitamanas::1460.verse_sanskrit: सो बिलगाउ बिहाइ समाजा। न त मारे जैहहिं सब राजा॥ सुनि मुनि बचन लखन मुसुकाने। बोले परसुधरहि अपमाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1460.verse_hindi: वह इस समाज को छोड़कर अलग हो जाए, नहीं तो सभी राजा मारे जाएँगे। मुनि के वचन सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी मुस्कुराए और परशुरामजी का अपमान करते हुए बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1460.english_translation: Let him step away from this assembly; otherwise all the kings will be slain. Hearing the sage's words, Lakshman smiled and spoke in insult to Parashurama.
ramacharitamanas::1460.translation_literal: सो (that) / बिलगाउ (let him move aside) / बिहाइ (leaving) / समाजा (the assembly) / न (otherwise) / त (then) / मारे (killed) / जैहहिं (will go) / सब (all) / राजा (kings) // सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (the sage's) / बचन (words) / लखन (Lakshman) / मुसुकाने (smiled) / बोले (spoke) / परसुधरहि (to Parashurama) / अपमाने (in insult)
ramacharitamanas::1460.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1460.essence: Mockery turns a warning into a clash.
ramacharitamanas::1460.simple_meaning: Parashurama demands that the challenger step aside or all the kings will die. Lakshman hears this and smiles, answering with sharp disrespect.
ramacharitamanas::1460.simple_insight: Pride escalates conflict faster than weapons do.
ramacharitamanas::1460.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, Parashurama has arrived furious after Shiva's bow is broken. He warns the gathered kings to step aside or face death. Lakshman smiles instead of bowing, and the confrontation hardens into a dangerous exchange.
ramacharitamanas::1460.modern_relevance: A tense room goes quiet after one person makes a threat. Another person smirks instead of softening the moment, and suddenly everyone can feel the conflict sharpen.
ramacharitamanas::1460.insight: It shows how a single mocking response can turn warning into open confrontation.

ramacharitamanas::1461.verse_sanskrit: बहु धनुहीं तोरीं लरिकाईं। कबहुँ न असि रिस कीन्हि गोसाईं॥ एहि धनु पर ममता केहि हेतू। सुनि रिसाइ कह भृगुकुलकेतू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1461.verse_hindi: हे गोसाईं! लड़कपन में हमने बहुत सी धनुहियाँ तोड़ डालीं, किन्तु आपने ऐसा क्रोध कभी नहीं किया। इसी धनुष पर इतनी ममता किस कारण से है? यह सुनकर भृगुवंश की ध्वजा स्वरूप परशुरामजी कुपित होकर कहने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1461.english_translation: O noble one, in childhood I broke many bows, yet you never became angry. Why do you cherish this bow so much? Hearing this, the banner of Bhrigu's line grew furious and spoke.
ramacharitamanas::1461.translation_literal: बहु (many) / धनुहीं (bows) / तोरीं (I broke) / लरिकाईं (in childhood) / कबहुँ (ever) / न (not) / असि (such) / रिस (anger) / कीन्हि (did) / गोसाईं (noble one) / एहि (this) / धनु (bow) / पर (on) / ममता (attachment) / केहि हेतू (for what reason) / सुनि (hearing) / रिसाइ (becoming angry) / कह (spoke) / भृगुकुलकेतू (banner of the Bhrigu line)
ramacharitamanas::1461.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1461.essence: Attachment flares when calm truth touches it.
ramacharitamanas::1461.simple_meaning: Ram reminds Parashurama that he broke many bows as a child and asks why this one bow is so precious. The question triggers Parashurama’s anger.
ramacharitamanas::1461.simple_insight: Some questions expose attachment so sharply that they provoke the very pride they reveal.
ramacharitamanas::1461.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, Ram has already broken Shiva’s bow. Parashurama arrives furious, and Ram calmly points out that many bows were broken in childhood without offense. The verse sets up Parashurama’s wounded pride before his angry reply.
ramacharitamanas::1461.modern_relevance: You ask one honest question in a tense room, and the real issue surfaces at once. The volume rises because the attachment was never really about the object.
ramacharitamanas::1461.insight: It shows how calm truth can expose hidden attachment and inflate wounded ego.

ramacharitamanas::1462.verse_sanskrit: रे नृप बालक काल बस बोलत तोहि न सँभार। धनुही सम तिपुरारि धनु बिदित सकल संसार ॥
ramacharitamanas::1462.verse_hindi: अरे राजपुत्र! काल के वश होने से तुझे बोलने में कुछ भी होश नहीं है। सारे संसार में विख्यात शिवजी का यह धनुष क्या धनुही के समान है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1462.english_translation: O prince, under time's power you speak without restraint. Is Shiva's bow merely like a toy bow? The whole world knows that bow.
ramacharitamanas::1462.translation_literal: रे (O) / नृप (king, prince) / बालक काल बस (under time's control, like a child) / बोलत (speaking) / तोहि (to you) / न (not) / सँभार (restraint, control) / धनुही (toy bow, small bow) / सम (like) / तिपुरारि (Shiva, destroyer of the three cities) / धनु (bow) / बिदित (known) / सकल (entire) / संसार (world)
ramacharitamanas::1462.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1462.essence: Pride talks first and sees last.
ramacharitamanas::1462.simple_meaning: Parashurama scolds the prince for speaking carelessly and mocks the sacred bow by comparing it to a child's toy bow.
ramacharitamanas::1462.simple_insight: Pride makes a person speak before seeing clearly.
ramacharitamanas::1462.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, Parashurama has been enraged by the breaking of Shiva's bow. He turns on the young prince and dismisses him as reckless and childish, setting up the confrontation that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1462.modern_relevance: In a tense room, someone snaps before checking the facts. The harshest words often come from wounded pride, not clear seeing.
ramacharitamanas::1462.insight: It exposes how insult and ego can distort judgment, turning a sacred object into something to belittle.

ramacharitamanas::1463.verse_sanskrit: लखन कहा हँसि हमरें जाना। सुनहु देव सब धनुष समाना॥ का छति लाभु जून धनु तोरें। देखा राम नयन के भोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1463.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी ने हँसकर कहा- हे देव! सुनिए, हमारे जान में तो सभी धनुष एक से ही हैं। पुराने धनुष के तोड़ने में क्या हानि-लाभ! श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने तो इसे नवीन के धोखे से देखा था ॥
ramacharitamanas::1463.english_translation: Lakshman laughed and said, “O noble one, hear me: in our view, all bows are the same. What loss or gain is there in breaking an old bow? Ram saw it as a new one in the morning light.”
ramacharitamanas::1463.translation_literal: लखन (Lakshman) / कहा (said) / हँसि (laughing) / हमरें (in our view) / जाना (known) / सुनहु (listen) / देव (noble one) / सब (all) / धनुष (bows) / समाना (equal)॥ / का (what) / छति (loss) / लाभु (gain) / जून (old) / धनु (bow) / तोरें (breaking) / देखा (saw) / राम (Ram) / नयन (eyes) / के (of) / भोरें (in the morning light) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1463.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::1463.essence: Sacred objects lose power when pride inflates them.
ramacharitamanas::1463.simple_meaning: Lakshman says the bow is just an old bow, so breaking it brings no real loss. Ram had seen it as ordinary, not special.
ramacharitamanas::1463.simple_insight: Status loses its grip when you see objects for what they are.
ramacharitamanas::1463.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, Parashuram has erupted in anger over Shiva's bow being broken. Lakshman answers with a laugh, refusing the bow's sacred prestige and exposing the absurdity of outrage over an object.
ramacharitamanas::1463.modern_relevance: Someone gets furious because a family heirloom cracked at a wedding, while everyone else sees only wood and metal. Lakshman's tone cuts through the drama and asks what, exactly, is being protected.
ramacharitamanas::1463.insight: It shifts attention from symbolic pride to plain reality, making inflated anger look unnecessary.

ramacharitamanas::1464.verse_sanskrit: छुअत टूट रघुपतिहु न दोसू। मुनि बिनु काज करिअ कत रोसू॥ बोले चितइ परसु की ओरा। रे सठ सुनेहि सुभाउ न मोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1464.verse_hindi: फिर यह तो छूते ही टूट गया, इसमें रघुनाथजी का भी कोई दोष नहीं है। मुनि! आप बिना ही कारण किसलिए क्रोध करते हैं? परशुरामजी अपने फरसे की ओर देखकर बोले- अरे दुष्ट! तूने मेरा स्वभाव नहीं सुना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1464.english_translation: The bow broke on mere touch, and Raghunath bears no fault. Why do you rage without cause, sage? Parashuram looked toward his axe and said, "Wretch, you have not heard my nature."
ramacharitamanas::1464.translation_literal: छुअत (touching) / टूट (broke) / रघुपतिहु (of Raghupati too) / न (not) / दोसू (fault) / मुनि (sage) / बिनु (without) / काज (cause, reason) / करिअ (is done) / कत (why) / रोसू (anger) / बोले (spoke) / चितइ (looking toward) / परसु (axe) / की ओर (toward) / रे (hey) / सठ (fool) / सुनेहि (have you heard) / सुभाउ (nature, disposition) / न (not) / मोरा (my)
ramacharitamanas::1464.speaker: Parashuram
ramacharitamanas::1464.essence: Pride can survive even when blame disappears.
ramacharitamanas::1464.simple_meaning: Parashuram says the bow broke by itself and Ram is not at fault, but he still turns angry and warns that his true nature is fierce.
ramacharitamanas::1464.simple_insight: Even after a fair explanation, pride can still flare up and refuse peace.
ramacharitamanas::1464.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Ram has just broken Shiva's bow. The tension should end with a simple explanation, but Parashuram's pride is still burning. He admits the bow broke on touch and Ram is not to blame, yet his anger rises anyway.
ramacharitamanas::1464.modern_relevance: You get a calm explanation in the group chat, but someone still snaps back as if being right matters more than being fair.
ramacharitamanas::1464.insight: It shows how wounded ego can keep fighting even after the facts are clear.

ramacharitamanas::1465.verse_sanskrit: बालकु बोलि बधउँ नहिं तोही। केवल मुनि जड़ जानहि मोही॥ बाल ब्रह्मचारी अति कोही। बिस्व बिदित छत्रियकुल द्रोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1465.verse_hindi: मैं तुझे बालक जानकर नहीं मारता हूँ। अरे मूर्ख! क्या तू मुझे निरा मुनि ही जानता है। मैं बालब्रह्मचारी और अत्यन्त क्रोधी हूँ। क्षत्रियकुल का शत्रु तो विश्वभर में विख्यात हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1465.english_translation: I do not kill you because you are a child. Fool, do you think I am merely a hermit? I am a lifelong celibate and fiercely angry. I am known everywhere as the enemy of the warrior clan.
ramacharitamanas::1465.translation_literal: बालकु (as a child) / बोलि (calling) / बधउँ (I kill) / नहिं (not) / तोही (you) / केवल (only) / मुनि (sage) / जड़ (foolish) / जानहि (you know) / मोही (me) / बाल ब्रह्मचारी (lifelong celibate) / अति (very) / कोही (angry) / बिस्व बिदित (world-famous) / छत्रियकुल (warrior clan) / द्रोही (enemy)
ramacharitamanas::1465.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1465.essence: Do not mistake a calm face for harmlessness.
ramacharitamanas::1465.simple_meaning: Parashurama says he is not harmless just because he looks like a sage. He warns that he is fierce, celibate, and famous for opposing the warrior clan.
ramacharitamanas::1465.simple_insight: Outer appearance can hide real force. Misjudging someone can bring instant consequences.
ramacharitamanas::1465.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, Ram has just broken Shiva's bow. Parashurama steps forward in anger, feeling insulted. He tells Lakshman that he is no soft hermit, but a fierce ascetic known for destroying warrior pride.
ramacharitamanas::1465.modern_relevance: Someone smiles calmly in a tense room, and the whole atmosphere shifts because the calm is not weakness. A quiet person can still carry force, boundaries, and memory.
ramacharitamanas::1465.insight: It warns against confusing gentleness with powerlessness and teaches respect for hidden strength.

ramacharitamanas::1466.verse_sanskrit: भुजबल भूमि भूप बिनु कीन्ही। बिपुल बार महिदेवन्ह दीन्ही॥ सहसबाहु भुज छेदनिहारा। परसु बिलोकु महीपकुमारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1466.verse_hindi: अपनी भुजाओं के बल से मैंने पृथ्वी को राजाओं से रहित कर दिया और बहुत बार उसे ब्राह्मणों को दे डाला। हे राजकुमार! सहस्रबाहु की भुजाओं को काटने वाले मेरे इस फरसे को देख! ॥
ramacharitamanas::1466.english_translation: By the strength of my arms, I emptied the earth of kings and gave it away many times to the priests. O prince, behold my axe, the one that cut off Sahasrabahu's arms!
ramacharitamanas::1466.translation_literal: भुजबल (by arm-strength) / भूमि (earth) / भूप (kings) / बिनु (without) / कीन्ही (made) / बिपुल (many) / बार (times) / महिदेवन्ह (to priests) / दीन्ही (gave) / सहसबाहु (Sahasrabahu) / भुज (arms) / छेदनिहारा (the one who cuts) / परसु (axe) / बिलोकु (behold) / महीपकुमारा (prince)
ramacharitamanas::1466.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1466.essence: Old victories become threats when pride takes over.
ramacharitamanas::1466.simple_meaning: Parashurama boasts that he cleared the earth of kings and gave it to priests, then points to the axe that cut Sahasrabahu's arms.
ramacharitamanas::1466.simple_insight: Power can harden into pride when it starts speaking for itself.
ramacharitamanas::1466.detailed_meaning: Parashurama stands before Ram at the Sita swayamvar, furious over the broken bow. He reminds the prince of his own violent past: kings destroyed, land gifted away, Sahasrabahu defeated. The threat is meant to terrify Ram into silence.
ramacharitamanas::1466.modern_relevance: Someone in an argument starts listing old wins, old fights, old favors, as if history alone should end the discussion. The room gets smaller when pride begins to speak in trophies.
ramacharitamanas::1466.insight: It shows how ego uses past strength as a weapon in the present.

ramacharitamanas::1467.verse_sanskrit: मातु पितहि जनि सोचबस करसि महीसकिसोर। गर्भन्ह के अर्भक दलन परसु मोर अति घोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::1467.verse_hindi: अरे राजा के बालक! तू अपने माता-पिता को सोच के वश न कर। मेरा फरसा बड़ा भयानक है, यह गर्भों के बच्चों का भी नाश करने वाला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1467.english_translation: Do not make your parents suffer, prince. My axe is terrible; it can destroy even the children in the womb.
ramacharitamanas::1467.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / पितहि (father) / जनि (do not) / सोचबस (under the control of grief) / करसि (make) / महीसकिसोर (prince) / गर्भन्ह (of wombs) / के (of) / अर्भक (children) / दलन (destroying) / परसु (axe) / मोर (my) / अति घोर (very terrible)
ramacharitamanas::1467.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1467.essence: Pride in anger turns warning into a weapon.
ramacharitamanas::1467.simple_meaning: Parashurama warns the prince not to cause his parents grief and boasts that his axe is so fierce it can even destroy unborn children.
ramacharitamanas::1467.simple_insight: Anger can turn warning into cruelty, and pride can make mercy disappear.
ramacharitamanas::1467.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, Parashurama confronts Lakshman after Rama has broken Shiva’s bow. Still burning with fury, he threatens the young prince and claims his axe is so terrible it can destroy even unborn children. The line intensifies the standoff before Lakshman answers.
ramacharitamanas::1467.modern_relevance: A furious senior keeps escalating a family argument until the words become more dangerous than the problem. The threat sounds strong, but it only exposes how quickly anger loses proportion.
ramacharitamanas::1467.insight: It shows how threatened ego speaks in extremes, trying to dominate instead of resolve.

ramacharitamanas::1468.verse_sanskrit: बिहसि लखनु बोले मृदु बानी। अहो मुनीसु महा भटमानी॥ पुनि पुनि मोहि देखाव कुठारू। चहत उड़ावन फूँकि पहारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1468.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी हँसकर कोमल वाणी से बोले- अहो, मुनीश्वर तो अपने को बड़ा भारी योद्धा समझते हैं। बार-बार मुझे कुल्हाड़ी दिखाते हैं। फूँक से पहाड़ उड़ाना चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1468.english_translation: Lakshman smiled and spoke gently: "Ah, great ascetic, you think yourself a mighty warrior. Again and again you show me your axe, as if you could blow away a mountain with a puff."
ramacharitamanas::1468.translation_literal: बिहसि (smiling) / लखनु (Lakshman) / बोले (spoke) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (speech) / अहो (ah) / मुनीसु (great sage) / महा (great) / भटमानी (one who considers himself a warrior) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / मोहि (to me) / देखाव (show) / कुठारू (axe) / चहत (you wish) / उड़ावन (to blow away) / फूँकि (with a puff) / पहारू (mountain)
ramacharitamanas::1468.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::1468.essence: Bluster loses power when met by steady calm.
ramacharitamanas::1468.simple_meaning: Lakshman answers the sage’s threat with calm mockery. He says the axe is no match for him, and the boast sounds empty.
ramacharitamanas::1468.simple_insight: A calm mind can meet bluster without flinching.
ramacharitamanas::1468.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar, Parashuram has stormed in after seeing his broken bow and is threatening the court. Lakshman smiles and replies with gentle irony, refusing to be intimidated. The moment tests whether he can hold his tongue, or his nerve, before a furious sage.
ramacharitamanas::1468.modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in a meeting and starts talking like they own the room. You can feel the heat rise, or you can answer with steady wit and not hand them your fear.
ramacharitamanas::1468.insight: It teaches you to stay unshaken under intimidation and answer from composure, not panic.

ramacharitamanas::1469.verse_sanskrit: इहाँ कुम्हड़बतिया कोउ नाहीं। जे तरजनी देखि मरि जाहीं॥ देखि कुठारु सरासन बाना। मैं कछु कहा सहित अभिमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1469.verse_hindi: यहाँ कोई कुम्हड़े की बतिया (छोटा कच्चा फल) नहीं है, जो तर्जनी (सबसे आगे की) अँगुली को देखते ही मर जाती हैं। कुठार और धनुष-बाण देखकर ही मैंने कुछ अभिमान सहित कहा था ॥
ramacharitamanas::1469.english_translation: There is no weak pumpkin here, one that dies at the sight of a raised finger. I spoke with some pride only after seeing the axe, bow, and arrows.
ramacharitamanas::1469.translation_literal: इहाँ (here) / कुम्हड़बतिया (pumpkin-vine seedling; weak little gourd) / कोउ (anyone) / नाहीं (not) / जे (who) / तरजनी (raised finger; pointing finger) / देखि (seeing) / मरि जाहीं (die away; perish)॥ / देखि (seeing) / कुठारु (axe) / सरासन (bow) / बाना (arrows) / मैं (I) / कछु (something) / कहा (said) / सहित (with) / अभिमाना (pride) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1469.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::1469.essence: True courage does not wilt before threats.
ramacharitamanas::1469.simple_meaning: Lakshman says he is not fragile or easily frightened. He only spoke boldly because he saw the weapons and felt confident enough to answer back.
ramacharitamanas::1469.simple_insight: Courage is not bluster. It is the steadiness to answer fear without shrinking.
ramacharitamanas::1469.detailed_meaning: At Vishvamitra's command, Lakshman has already bristled at Parashurama's threats. Seeing the axe, bow, and arrows, he refuses to act like a tender plant that withers at a finger-point. This line shows his fearless pride before the real clash begins.
ramacharitamanas::1469.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a meeting, trying to make you fold with a sharp tone and a glare. You do not need to become small just because they sound large.
ramacharitamanas::1469.insight: It teaches you to recognize intimidation and answer it without collapsing into fear.

ramacharitamanas::1470.verse_sanskrit: भृगुसुत समुझि जनेउ बिलोकी। जो कछु कहहु सहउँ रिस रोकी॥ सुर महिसुर हरिजन अरु गाई। हमरें कुल इन्ह पर न सुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1470.verse_hindi: भृगुवंशी समझकर और यज्ञोपवीत देखकर तो जो कुछ आप कहते हैं, उसे मैं क्रोध को रोककर सह लेता हूँ। देवता, ब्राह्मण, भगवान के भक्त और गो- इन पर हमारे कुल में वीरता नहीं दिखाई जाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1470.english_translation: Recognizing you as a descendant of Bhrigu and seeing the sacred thread, I can bear whatever you say by restraining my anger. Gods, priests, devotees of the Lord, and cows are not met with valor in our line.
ramacharitamanas::1470.translation_literal: भृगुसुत (descendant of Bhrigu) / समुझि (recognizing) / जनेउ (sacred thread) / बिलोकी (seeing) / जो कछु (whatever) / कहहु (you say) / सहउँ (I bear) / रिस (anger) / रोकी (restrained) / सुर (gods) / महिसुर (priests) / हरिजन (devotees of the Lord) / अरु (and) / गाई (cows) / हमरें (our) / कुल (lineage) / इन्ह पर (toward these) / न (not) / सुराई (valor)
ramacharitamanas::1470.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1470.essence: Restraint can coexist with a warrior's pride.
ramacharitamanas::1470.simple_meaning: Parashurama says he can tolerate Lakshman's words because he sees his lineage and sacred thread. He also says his family does not show aggression toward the divine, priests, devotees, or cows.
ramacharitamanas::1470.simple_insight: Respect can soften anger, but pride still speaks through it.
ramacharitamanas::1470.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Lakshman has just mocked Parashurama's threat. Parashurama answers with controlled anger, naming Lakshman’s lineage and sacred thread, then drawing a line around whom his warrior code will not attack. The exchange is tightening toward conflict.
ramacharitamanas::1470.modern_relevance: Someone cuts you down in front of everyone, and you answer with a smile that still carries a warning. You are trying to stay restrained, but the old pride is still standing guard.
ramacharitamanas::1470.insight: It shows how social respect can delay anger without dissolving ego.

ramacharitamanas::1471.verse_sanskrit: बधें पापु अपकीरति हारें। मारतहूँ पा परिअ तुम्हारें॥ कोटि कुलिस सम बचनु तुम्हारा। ब्यर्थ धरहु धनु बान कुठारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1471.verse_hindi: क्योंकि इन्हें मारने से पाप लगता है और इनसे हार जाने पर अपकीर्ति होती है, इसलिए आप मारें तो भी आपके पैर ही पड़ना चाहिए। आपका एक-एक वचन ही करोड़ों वज्रों के समान है। धनुष-बाण और कुठार तो आप व्यर्थ ही धारण करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1471.english_translation: Because killing them brings sin and being defeated by them brings disgrace, even if you strike, I should fall at your feet. Your words alone are worth millions of thunderbolts; you wear bow, arrows, and axe in vain.
ramacharitamanas::1471.translation_literal: बधें (by killing) / पापु (sin) / अपकीरति (disgrace) / हारें (by being defeated) / मारतहूँ (even by striking) / पा परिअ (fall at the feet) / तुम्हारें (of yours) / कोटि (crores/millions) / कुलिस (thunderbolts) / सम (like) / बचनु (words) / तुम्हारा (yours) / ब्यर्थ (vainly) / धरहु (you wear/hold) / धनु (bow) / बान (arrows) / कुठारा (axe)
ramacharitamanas::1471.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1471.essence: True strength makes violence and humiliation equally impossible.
ramacharitamanas::1471.simple_meaning: Parashurama says that fighting this opponent brings shame either way, so the only proper response is reverence. He also says the other man's words are as powerful as thunderbolts and that weapons are unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::1471.simple_insight: Pride softens when raw force meets true authority.
ramacharitamanas::1471.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, Parashurama has just challenged the bow-breaker. Seeing Ram's calm, he admits the trap of violence: to kill him is sinful, to lose to him is disgraceful. The confrontation turns from threat into reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1471.modern_relevance: You are ready to snap back in a meeting, then the other person speaks with such calm authority that your anger collapses. The fight was never equal.
ramacharitamanas::1471.insight: It shifts the mind from confrontation to recognition of higher strength.

ramacharitamanas::1472.verse_sanskrit: जो बिलोकि अनुचित कहेउँ छमहु महामुनि धीर। सुनि सरोष भृगुबंसमनि बोले गिरा गभीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::1472.verse_hindi: इन्हें (धनुष-बाण और कुठार को) देखकर मैंने कुछ अनुचित कहा हो, तो उसे हे धीर महामुनि! क्षमा कीजिए। यह सुनकर भृगुवंशमणि परशुरामजी क्रोध के साथ गंभीर वाणी बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1472.english_translation: If I spoke improperly after seeing these, forgive me, O patient great sage. Hearing this, the jewel of Bhrigu's line spoke in a grave, angry voice.
ramacharitamanas::1472.translation_literal: जो (if) / बिलोकि (seeing) / अनुचित (improper) / कहेउँ (I spoke) / छमहु (forgive) / महामुनि (great sage) / धीर (patient, steadfast) / सुनि (hearing) / सरोष (with anger) / भृगुबंसमनि (jewel of the Bhrigu line) / बोले (spoke) / गिरा (voice) / गभीर (grave, deep)
ramacharitamanas::1472.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1472.essence: A polite apology can stand right before a storm of anger.
ramacharitamanas::1472.simple_meaning: Parashuram apologizes for any disrespect in his words, then the narration says he answered in an angry, serious tone.
ramacharitamanas::1472.simple_insight: Even a tense exchange can begin with humility before pride erupts.
ramacharitamanas::1472.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, Parashuram has just seen Shiva's bow and the broken pieces. Before his anger fully explodes, he offers a formal apology for any improper words. The couplet marks the turning point from restraint into confrontation.
ramacharitamanas::1472.modern_relevance: You realize you overstepped in the middle of a heated argument and try to soften it — but the room is already charged, and the next words can still cut.
ramacharitamanas::1472.insight: It shows the instant before conflict hardens, when courtesy still exists but barely holds.

ramacharitamanas::1473.verse_sanskrit: कौसिक सुनहु मंद यहु बालकु। कुटिल कालबस निज कुल घालकु॥ भानु बंस राकेस कलंकू। निपट निरंकुस अबुध असंकू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1473.verse_hindi: हे विश्वामित्र! सुनो, यह बालक बड़ा कुबुद्धि और कुटिल है, काल के वश होकर यह अपने कुल का घातक बन रहा है। यह सूर्यवंश रूपी पूर्ण चन्द्र का कलंक है। यह बिल्कुल उद्दण्ड, मूर्ख और निडर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1473.english_translation: O Kaushik, listen: this boy is foolish and crooked. Under the grip of fate, he is destroying his own lineage. He is a stain on the Sun dynasty, utterly unruly, ignorant, and fearless.
ramacharitamanas::1473.translation_literal: कौसिक (O Kaushik) / सुनहु (listen) / मंद (foolish) / यहु (this) / बालकु (boy) / कुटिल (crooked) / कालबस (under the grip of fate) / निज (own) / कुल (lineage) / घालकु (destroyer) / भानु (sun) / बंस (dynasty) / राकेस (moon) / कलंकू (stain) / निपट (utterly) / निरंकुस (unruly) / अबुध (ignorant) / असंकू (fearless)
ramacharitamanas::1473.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1473.essence: Anger sees a child as a threat and mistakes contempt for insight.
ramacharitamanas::1473.simple_meaning: Parashurama insults the boy in front of Vishwamitra, calling him foolish, crooked, and a disgrace to his lineage.
ramacharitamanas::1473.simple_insight: Pride speaks in labels; it cannot see the larger truth in front of it.
ramacharitamanas::1473.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, Parashurama has just been provoked by the breaking of Shiva's bow. Facing Vishwamitra, he turns his anger on Ram, calling the young prince a ruin to his own clan. The scene is tightening toward confrontation, and this verse is part of that threat.
ramacharitamanas::1473.modern_relevance: A heated group chat makes someone the villain before anyone asks what actually happened. The loudest voice can sound certain and still be blind.
ramacharitamanas::1473.insight: It shows how anger reduces a person to insults instead of seeing character or context.

ramacharitamanas::1474.verse_sanskrit: काल कवलु होइहि छन माहीं। कहउँ पुकारि खोरि मोहि नाहीं॥ तुम्ह हटकहु जौं चहहु उबारा। कहि प्रतापु बलु रोषु हमारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1474.verse_hindi: अभी क्षण भर में यह काल का ग्रास हो जाएगा। मैं पुकारकर कहे देता हूँ, फिर मुझे दोष नहीं है। यदि तुम इसे बचाना चाहते हो, तो हमारा प्रताप, बल और क्रोध बतलाकर इसे मना कर दो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1474.english_translation: It will be swallowed by death in a moment. I warn you openly; blame me not later. If you want to save it, stop it by speaking of my power, strength, and anger.
ramacharitamanas::1474.translation_literal: काल कवलु (the mouth of death) / होइहि (will become) / छन माहीं (within a moment) / कहउँ (I say) / पुकारि (aloud) / खोरि (blame) / मोहि (me) / नाहीं (not) / तुम्ह (you) / हटकहु (restrain) / जौं (if) / चहहु (you wish) / उबारा (to save) / कहि (saying) / प्रतापु (power) / बलु (strength) / रोषु (anger) / हमारा (our)
ramacharitamanas::1474.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::1474.essence: Arrogance mistakes loudness for power and walks straight into ruin.
ramacharitamanas::1474.simple_meaning: Ravana warns that the bow will be destroyed immediately and says no one can blame him. If anyone wants to save it, they must stop him by showing his power and fury.
ramacharitamanas::1474.simple_insight: Pride speaks as certainty. It announces its own downfall before it happens.
ramacharitamanas::1474.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, before the swayamvar, Ravana has mocked Shiva's bow. Now the boast hardens into a threat: he says the bow will be finished in a moment, and only someone who can match his force should stop him. The scene exposes his arrogance just before Lakshman answers.
ramacharitamanas::1474.modern_relevance: A person in a meeting laughs too loudly, daring anyone to challenge them. Everyone can hear the insecurity under the volume. Ravana's voice is what unchecked ego sounds like.
ramacharitamanas::1474.insight: It shows how ego turns a simple challenge into a public display of force.

ramacharitamanas::1475.verse_sanskrit: लखन कहेउ मुनि सुजसु तुम्हारा। तुम्हहि अछत को बरनै पारा॥ अपने मुँह तुम्ह आपनि करनी। बार अनेक भाँति बहु बरनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1475.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी ने कहा- हे मुनि! आपका सुयश आपके रहते दूसरा कौन वर्णन कर सकता है? आपने अपने ही मुँह से अपनी करनी अनेकों बार बहुत प्रकार से वर्णन की है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1475.english_translation: Lakshman said, "O sage, who else can describe your fame while you are still alive? You have often spoken of your own deeds in many ways."
ramacharitamanas::1475.translation_literal: लखन (Lakshman) / कहेउ (said) / मुनि (sage) / सुजसु (fame) / तुम्हारा (your) / तुम्हहि (you yourself) / अछत (while alive) / को (who) / बरनै (to describe) / पारा (able) ॥ / अपने (own) / मुँह (mouth) / तुम्ह (you) / आपनि (own) / करनी (deeds) / बार (many times) / अनेक (many) / भाँति (ways) / बहु (much) / बरनी (described) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1475.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::1475.essence: Self-praise loses force when it is named aloud.
ramacharitamanas::1475.simple_meaning: Lakshman answers the sage sharply, saying that the sage has already praised his own deeds many times, so no one else needs to describe his fame.
ramacharitamanas::1475.simple_insight: Pride can be exposed with a single honest line.
ramacharitamanas::1475.detailed_meaning: At Vishwamitra's harsh warning about the boy, Lakshman replies with biting confidence. He turns the sage's own words back on him, mocking self-praise and refusing to be intimidated. The exchange keeps the tension alive before the next rebuke.
ramacharitamanas::1475.modern_relevance: Someone keeps listing their achievements in a meeting, waiting for applause. One calm sentence can cut through the performance and bring the room back to reality.
ramacharitamanas::1475.insight: It shows how to answer arrogance without losing composure: name the self-praise plainly and move the exchange forward.

ramacharitamanas::1476.verse_sanskrit: नहिं संतोषु त पुनि कछु कहहू। जनि रिस रोकि दुसह दुख सहहू॥ बीरब्रती तुम्ह धीर अछोभा। गारी देत न पावहु सोभा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1476.verse_hindi: इतने पर भी संतोष न हुआ हो तो फिर कुछ कह डालिए। क्रोध रोककर असह्य दुःख मत सहिए। आप वीरता का व्रत धारण करने वाले, धैर्यवान और क्षोभरहित हैं। गाली देते शोभा नहीं पाते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1476.english_translation: If that still does not satisfy you, say more. Do not swallow unbearable pain by holding back anger. You are vowed to heroic conduct, steady and unshaken. Insults do not suit you.
ramacharitamanas::1476.translation_literal: नहिं (not) / संतोषु (satisfaction) / त (then) / पुनि (again) / कछु (something) / कहहू (say) / जनि (do not) / रिस (anger) / रोकि (holding back) / दुसह (unbearable) / दुख (pain) / सहहू (bear) / बीरब्रती (vowed to heroic conduct) / तुम्ह (you) / धीर (steady) / अछोभा (unshaken) / गारी (insult) / देत (giving) / न (not) / पावहु (obtain) / सोभा (honour)
ramacharitamanas::1476.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::1476.essence: Heroic steadiness does not need insults to prove itself.
ramacharitamanas::1476.simple_meaning: Lakshman tells the sage to speak plainly if he is still unhappy, but not to endure terrible pain by suppressing anger. A heroic person should stay steady, not answer with abuse.
ramacharitamanas::1476.simple_insight: Strength is not the same as swallowing hurt. Real steadiness keeps dignity without becoming abusive.
ramacharitamanas::1476.detailed_meaning: At the hermitage, Lakshman has already answered the sage sharply. The tension is still alive, so he pushes back again: speak out, but do not pretend that restraint means silent suffering. He reminds the sage that true courage stays steady and does not gain honour through insults.
ramacharitamanas::1476.modern_relevance: Someone keeps provoking you in a group chat, and you feel the heat rising in your chest. The verse points to a harder choice: stay composed, but do not confuse dignity with self-erasure.
ramacharitamanas::1476.insight: It teaches you to hold firm without collapsing into either silence or abuse.

ramacharitamanas::1477.verse_sanskrit: सूर समर करनी करहिं कहि न जनावहिं आपु। बिद्यमान रन पाइ रिपु कायर कथहिं प्रतापु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1477.verse_hindi: शूरवीर तो युद्ध में करनी (शूरवीरता का कार्य) करते हैं, कहकर अपने को नहीं जनाते। शत्रु को युद्ध में उपस्थित पाकर कायर ही अपने प्रताप की डींग मारा करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1477.english_translation: The brave do their work in battle and do not advertise themselves. The cowardly, when they meet an enemy face to face, boast of their own valor.
ramacharitamanas::1477.translation_literal: सूर (brave) / समर (battle) / करनी (deeds) / करहिं (do) / कहि (saying) / न (not) / जनावहिं (make known) / आपु (oneself) । / बिद्यमान (present) / रन (battlefield) / पाइ (having found) / रिपु (enemy) / कायर (cowardly) / कथहिं (speak of) / प्रतापु (valor, glory)
ramacharitamanas::1477.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1477.essence: Bravery proves itself in action, not in claims.
ramacharitamanas::1477.simple_meaning: Real courage shows itself through action, not self-praise. Only cowards talk about their greatness when an enemy is right there.
ramacharitamanas::1477.simple_insight: Quiet strength needs no announcement. The urge to brag often hides fear.
ramacharitamanas::1477.detailed_meaning: Laxman has just mocked Parashurama’s boasting, and this doha sharpens that rebuke. In the middle of their heated exchange, Tulsidas contrasts true bravery with empty self-display: the brave act, while the fearful talk.
ramacharitamanas::1477.modern_relevance: A colleague keeps talking about how indispensable they are, right when the actual crisis is in front of everyone. The people who matter are already fixing the problem.
ramacharitamanas::1477.insight: It shifts attention from self-promotion to visible action under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::1478.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह तौ कालु हाँक जनु लावा। बार बार मोहि लागि बोलावा॥ सुनत लखन के बचन कठोरा। परसु सुधारि धरेउ कर घोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1478.verse_hindi: आप तो मानो काल को हाँक लगाकर बार-बार उसे मेरे लिए बुलाते हैं। लक्ष्मणजी के कठोर वचन सुनते ही परशुरामजी ने अपने भयानक फरसे को सुधारकर हाथ में ले लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1478.english_translation: You seem to be summoning Death itself again and again for me. Hearing Lakshman's harsh words, Parashurama adjusted his terrible axe and took it in hand.
ramacharitamanas::1478.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / तौ (indeed) / कालु (death) / हाँक (call) / जनु (as if) / लावा (have brought) / बार बार (again and again) / मोहि (for me) / लागि (for) / बोलावा (called) ॥ / सुनत (hearing) / लखन (Lakshman) / के (of) / बचन (words) / कठोरा (harsh) / परसु (axe) / सुधारि (adjusted) / धरेउ (took/held) / कर (in hand) / घोरा (terrible) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1478.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1478.essence: Pride hears insult and reaches for force.
ramacharitamanas::1478.simple_meaning: Parashurama feels Lakshman's words are so sharp they are like calling death itself. He immediately grips his axe, ready to respond.
ramacharitamanas::1478.simple_insight: Sharp words can turn a tense moment into open danger in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::1478.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, Lakshman has just spoken boldly to Parashurama. The sage takes the insult as a challenge, saying it is as if death itself has been summoned for him, and he lifts his axe in anger. The scene is about to tip from verbal heat into violence.
ramacharitamanas::1478.modern_relevance: One cutting sentence in a family argument can change the whole room. A voice rises, hands clench, and suddenly everyone can feel the danger in the air.
ramacharitamanas::1478.insight: It shows how quickly pride can convert words into confrontation.

ramacharitamanas::1479.verse_sanskrit: अब जनि देइ दोसु मोहि लोगू। कटुबादी बालकु बधजोगू॥ बाल बिलोकि बहुत मैं बाँचा। अब यहु मरनिहार भा साँचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1479.verse_hindi: (और बोले-) अब लोग मुझे दोष न दें। यह कडुआ बोलने वाला बालक मारे जाने के ही योग्य है। इसे बालक देखकर मैंने बहुत बचाया, पर अब यह सचमुच मरने को ही आ गया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1479.english_translation: “Do not let people blame me now. This sharp-tongued boy deserves death. I spared him because he was only a child, but now he has truly become fit to die.”
ramacharitamanas::1479.translation_literal: अब (now) / जनि (do not) / देइ (give) / दोसु (blame) / मोहि (me) / लोगू (people) / कटुबादी (sharp-tongued) / बालकु (boy/child) / बधजोगू (fit for killing) / बाल (child) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बहुत (much) / मैं (I) / बाँचा (spared) / अब (now) / यहु (this) / मरनिहार (fit to die) / भा (has become) / साँचा (truly)
ramacharitamanas::1479.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1479.essence: Anger always finds a reason once pride feels insulted.
ramacharitamanas::1479.simple_meaning: Parashurama says he should not be blamed for wanting to kill Lakshman, because Lakshman has spoken harshly and now seems truly deserving of death.
ramacharitamanas::1479.simple_insight: Pride turns patience into anger. Once respect is broken, the mind starts justifying harm.
ramacharitamanas::1479.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, Lakshman’s sharp words have pushed Parashurama to the edge. He says he spared the boy because of his age, but now sees him as fully deserving punishment. The tension rises before Vishwamitra steps in.
ramacharitamanas::1479.modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in a meeting, then smirks like nothing happened. You feel the heat rise and start building a case in your head for why they deserve a harsh reply.
ramacharitamanas::1479.insight: It shows how wounded pride turns into moral justification, making anger feel righteous.

ramacharitamanas::1480.verse_sanskrit: कौसिक कहा छमिअ अपराधू। बाल दोष गुन गनहिं न साधू॥ खर कुठार मैं अकरुन कोही। आगें अपराधी गुरुद्रोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1480.verse_hindi: विश्वामित्रजी ने कहा- अपराध क्षमा कीजिए। बालकों के दोष और गुण को साधु लोग नहीं गिनते। (परशुरामजी बोले-) तीखी धार का कुठार, मैं दयारहित और क्रोधी और यह गुरुद्रोही और अपराधी मेरे सामने- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1480.english_translation: Kausika said, “Forgive the offense. Noble people do not count the faults and merits of a child.” Parashurama said, “My sharp axe, I am merciless and angry; before me stands a culprit and a betrayer of his teacher.”
ramacharitamanas::1480.translation_literal: कौसिक (Kausika/Visvamitra) / कहा (said) / छमिअ (forgive) / अपराधू (offense) / बाल (child) / दोष (faults) / गुन (virtues) / गनहिं (count) / न (not) / साधू (noble people)॥ / खर (sharp) / कुठार (axe) / मैं (I) / अकरुन (merciless) / कोही (angry one) / आगें (before) / अपराधी (culprit) / गुरुद्रोही (betrayer of teacher) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1480.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1480.essence: Anger turns a child into a criminal.
ramacharitamanas::1480.simple_meaning: Visvamitra asks for forgiveness and says noble people do not judge a child by faults. Parashurama answers with anger, calling himself fierce and the boy guilty.
ramacharitamanas::1480.simple_insight: Anger narrows vision; compassion widens it, even in a tense confrontation.
ramacharitamanas::1480.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, Parashurama confronts Ram and Lakshman after the bow is broken. Visvamitra tries to calm the moment by asking for forgiveness, but Parashurama still speaks from fury, seeing insult and guilt instead of youth and innocence.
ramacharitamanas::1480.modern_relevance: A teenager snaps back in a family argument, and the room instantly shrinks into blame. One person sees a child; another sees an offense. The verse captures how anger turns a moment into a verdict.
ramacharitamanas::1480.insight: It shows how perception changes with temper: the same person can be seen as a child or as a threat.

ramacharitamanas::1481.verse_sanskrit: उतर देत छोड़उँ बिनु मारें। केवल कौसिक सील तुम्हारें॥ न त एहि काटि कुठार कठोरें। गुरहि उरिन होतेउँ श्रम थोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1481.verse_hindi: उत्तर दे रहा है। इतने पर भी मैं इसे बिना मारे छोड़ रहा हूँ, सो हे विश्वामित्र! केवल तुम्हारे शील (प्रेम) से। नहीं तो इसे इस कठोर कुठार से काटकर थोड़े ही परिश्रम से गुरु से उऋण हो जाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1481.english_translation: I am answering. Even so, I am leaving him alive without killing him, only because of your gentleness, O Vishvamitra. Otherwise, I would have cut him down with this hard axe and repaid my teacher with little effort.
ramacharitamanas::1481.translation_literal: उतर (reply) / देत (giving) / छोड़उँ (I leave) / बिनु (without) / मारें (killing) / केवल (only) / कौसिक (O Kaushika/Vishvamitra) / सील (gentleness / good conduct) / तुम्हारें (because of yours) / न (not) / त (then) / एहि (this) / काटि (cutting) / कुठार (axe) / कठोरें (hard) / गुरहि (to the teacher) / उरिन (debt-free / repaid) / होतेउँ (I would become) / श्रम (effort) / थोरें (small)
ramacharitamanas::1481.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1481.essence: Strength proves itself by not striking.
ramacharitamanas::1481.simple_meaning: Parashurama says he is sparing the boy only out of respect for Vishvamitra. He claims he could have killed him easily and still settled his debt to his teacher.
ramacharitamanas::1481.simple_insight: Power feels different when it is restrained by respect.
ramacharitamanas::1481.detailed_meaning: Parashurama has just been angered by Lakshman’s sharp words in Vishvamitra’s sacrificial arena. Now, with his axe raised, he says he is letting the boy live only because Vishvamitra’s gentleness has stayed his hand. The scene is a tense pause before the next blow.
ramacharitamanas::1481.modern_relevance: You’re furious in a meeting and ready to humiliate someone back. Then a senior person’s presence or a deeper respect stops you. The strongest response is sometimes the one you do not use.
ramacharitamanas::1481.insight: It teaches restraint under anger: even justified power can be held back by reverence.

ramacharitamanas::1482.verse_sanskrit: गाधिसूनु कह हृदयँ हँसि मुनिहि हरिअरइ सूझ। अयमय खाँड़ न ऊखमय अजहुँ न बूझ अबूझ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1482.verse_hindi: विश्वामित्रजी ने हृदय में हँसकर कहा- मुनि को हरा ही हरा सूझ रहा है (अर्थात सर्वत्र विजयी होने के कारण ये श्री राम-लक्ष्मण को भी साधारण क्षत्रिय ही समझ रहे हैं), किन्तु यह लोहमयी (केवल फौलाद की बनी हुई) खाँड़ (खाँड़ा-खड्ग) है, ऊख की (रस की) खाँड़ नहीं है (जो मुँह में लेते ही गल जाए। खेद है,) मुनि अब भी बेसमझ बने हुए हैं, इनके प्रभाव को नहीं समझ रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1482.english_translation: Gadhi's son smiled inwardly: the sage sees only green everywhere. This is an iron blade, not a sugar blade; even now he does not understand.
ramacharitamanas::1482.translation_literal: गाधिसूनु (Gadhi's son) / कह (said) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / हँसि (smiling) / मुनिहि (the sage) / हरिअरइ (green everywhere) / सूझ (appears) / अयमय (iron-made) / खाँड़ (blade) / न (not) / ऊखमय (sugar-made) / अजहुँ (even now) / न (not) / बूझ (understand) / अबूझ (uncomprehending)
ramacharitamanas::1482.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1482.essence: What looks harmless may be far harder than it seems.
ramacharitamanas::1482.simple_meaning: विश्वामित्र मन ही मन सोचते हैं कि परशुराम राम-लक्ष्मण की असली शक्ति नहीं समझ रहे। वे उन्हें साधारण मान रहे हैं, जबकि सामने लोहे जैसी कठोर शक्ति है, कोई मीठी चीज़ नहीं।
ramacharitamanas::1482.simple_insight: Overconfidence blinds you to what is actually in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::1482.detailed_meaning: परशुराम के तीखे वचनों के बाद विश्वामित्र भीतर ही भीतर मुस्कराते हैं। वे देखते हैं कि परशुराम राम-लक्ष्मण को साधारण समझ रहे हैं, जबकि उनकी शक्ति कठोर और वास्तविक है। यह क्षण तनाव को और गहरा करता है।
ramacharitamanas::1482.modern_relevance: You dismiss the quiet person in the room, assuming they will fold. Then they speak once, cleanly, and the whole atmosphere changes.
ramacharitamanas::1482.insight: It shifts the mind from surface appearance to hidden force.

ramacharitamanas::1483.verse_sanskrit: कहेउ लखन मुनि सीलु तुम्हारा। को नहिं जान बिदित संसारा॥ माता पितहि उरिन भए नीकें। गुर रिनु रहा सोचु बड़ जीकें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1483.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी ने कहा- हे मुनि! आपके शील को कौन नहीं जानता? वह संसार भर में प्रसिद्ध है। आप माता-पिता से तो अच्छी तरह उऋण हो ही गए, अब गुरु का ऋण रहा, जिसका जी में बड़ा सोच लगा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1483.english_translation: Lakshman said, "O sage, everyone in the world knows your noble conduct. You have already repaid your debt to mother and father. Only the guru's debt remains, and that weighs heavily on my heart."
ramacharitamanas::1483.translation_literal: कहेउ (said) / लखन (Lakshman) / मुनि (sage) / सीलु (noble conduct) / तुम्हारा (your) / को नहिं (who not) / जान (knows) / बिदित (known) / संसारा (world) / माता (mother) / पितहि (father) / उरिन (debt-free) / भए (became) / नीकें (well) / गुर (guru) / रिनु (debt) / रहा (remains) / सोचु (worry) / बड़ (great) / जीकें (in the heart)
ramacharitamanas::1483.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::1483.essence: Honor is incomplete until the remaining debt is repaid.
ramacharitamanas::1483.simple_meaning: Lakshman praises the sage's character and says the sage has already settled his debts to his parents. Only the teacher's debt remains, and that still troubles him.
ramacharitamanas::1483.simple_insight: A person of honour is never finished until every obligation is met.
ramacharitamanas::1483.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, Lakshman speaks sharply but respectfully to Vishwamitra after the tension around Parashuram. He acknowledges the sage's greatness, then points to one remaining obligation: the debt to the teacher. The moment turns on duty and unfinished responsibility.
ramacharitamanas::1483.modern_relevance: You’ve cleared your parents’ calls, your deadlines, your obligations — but one promise still sits in the back of your mind. Until that’s handled, you feel it.
ramacharitamanas::1483.insight: It shifts attention from public praise to the unfinished obligation that still needs care.

ramacharitamanas::1484.verse_sanskrit: सो जनु हमरेहि माथे काढ़ा। दिन चलि गए ब्याज बड़ बाढ़ा॥ अब आनिअ ब्यवहरिआ बोली। तुरत देउँ मैं थैली खोली ॥
ramacharitamanas::1484.verse_hindi: वह मानो हमारे ही मत्थे काढ़ा था। बहुत दिन बीत गए, इससे ब्याज भी बहुत बढ़ गया होगा। अब किसी हिसाब करने वाले को बुला लाइए, तो मैं तुरंत थैली खोलकर दे दूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1484.english_translation: It was as if he had been set on our own head. So much time has passed that the interest has grown greatly. Now call a moneylender, and I will open my bag at once.
ramacharitamanas::1484.translation_literal: सो (that) / जनु (as if) / हमरेहि (our own) / माथे (head) / काढ़ा (placed) । / दिन (days) / चलि गए (have passed) / ब्याज (interest) / बड़ (greatly) / बाढ़ा (grown) ॥ / अब (now) / आनिअ (bring) / ब्यवहरिआ (moneylender/account-settler) / बोली (speaking/call) । / तुरत (immediately) / देउँ (I will give) / मैं (I) / थैली (bag/purse) / खोली (opening) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1484.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::1484.essence: Bold wit can puncture pride before force is needed.
ramacharitamanas::1484.simple_meaning: Lakshman says the burden has sat on their heads for a long time, so the debt has grown huge. He asks for someone to settle accounts and says he will pay immediately.
ramacharitamanas::1484.simple_insight: Sharp wit can deflate arrogance without breaking your composure.
ramacharitamanas::1484.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur’s court, Parashuram has challenged the assembly after Ram breaks Shiva’s bow. Lakshman answers with mocking confidence, treating the long delay like an unpaid debt with rising interest. His words are a spark before the confrontation erupts.
ramacharitamanas::1484.modern_relevance: Someone corners you in a group chat, acting as if you owe them obedience. You answer calmly, with enough edge to expose the bluff without losing your footing.
ramacharitamanas::1484.insight: It shows how fearless speech can cut through intimidation and shift the balance of power.

ramacharitamanas::1485.verse_sanskrit: सुनि कटु बचन कुठार सुधारा। हाय हाय सब सभा पुकारा॥ भृगुबर परसु देखावहु मोही। बिप्र बिचारि बचउँ नृपदोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1485.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी के कडुए वचन सुनकर परशुरामजी ने कुठार सम्हाला। सारी सभा हाय-हाय! करके पुकार उठी। (लक्ष्मणजी ने कहा-) हे भृगुश्रेष्ठ! आप मुझे फरसा दिखा रहे हैं? पर हे राजाओं के शत्रु! मैं ब्राह्मण समझकर बचा रहा हूँ (तरह दे रहा हूँ) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1485.english_translation: Hearing the bitter words, Parashurama raised his axe. The whole assembly cried out, “Alas, alas!” “O best of the Bhargavas, you show me your axe? But I spare you only because you are a Brahmin, O enemy of kings.”
ramacharitamanas::1485.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / कटु (bitter) / बचन (words) / कुठार (axe) / सुधारा (raised, readied) / हाय हाय (alas, alas) / सब (all) / सभा (assembly) / पुकारा (cried out) / भृगुबर (best of the Bhargavas) / परसु (axe) / देखावहु (show) / मोही (to me) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / बिचारि (considering) / बचउँ (I spare) / नृपदोही (enemy of kings)
ramacharitamanas::1485.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1485.essence: One sharp word can turn a public gathering into a crisis.
ramacharitamanas::1485.simple_meaning: Parashurama lifts his axe after Lakshman’s sharp words, and the crowd panics. Lakshman answers with a taunt, saying he is being spared only because he is a Brahmin.
ramacharitamanas::1485.simple_insight: Pride and restraint collide in one charged moment.
ramacharitamanas::1485.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s assembly, Lakshman’s sharp teasing has pushed Parashurama to the edge. He raises his axe, the crowd cries out, and the exchange becomes a public test of temper, status, and power.
ramacharitamanas::1485.modern_relevance: A tense group chat turns into a live wire after one cutting reply. Everyone can feel the room tighten before anyone even types again.
ramacharitamanas::1485.insight: It shows how a single insult can escalate a whole room, and how status can become a weapon.

ramacharitamanas::1486.verse_sanskrit: मिले न कबहुँ सुभट रन गाढ़े। द्विज देवता घरहि के बा़ढ़े॥ अनुचित कहि सब लोग पुकारे। रघुपति सयनहिं लखनु नेवारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1486.verse_hindi: आपको कभी रणधीर बलवान् वीर नहीं मिले हैं। हे ब्राह्मण देवता ! आप घर ही में बड़े हैं। यह सुनकर 'अनुचित है, अनुचित है' कहकर सब लोग पुकार उठे। तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने इशारे से लक्ष्मणजी को रोक दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1486.english_translation: You have never met a true warrior in battle. You have grown up only at home, Brahmin deity. Hearing this, everyone cried out, "This is improper!" Then Lord Raghunath signaled Lakshman to stop.
ramacharitamanas::1486.translation_literal: मिले (met) / न (not) / कबहुँ (ever) / सुभट (valiant warrior) / रन (battle) / गाढ़े (in the thick of) / द्विज (twice-born, Brahmin) / देवता (deity) / घरहि (at home itself) / के (of) / बा़ढ़े (grown up) / अनुचित (improper) / कहि (saying) / सब (all) / लोग (people) / पुकारे (cried out) / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu) / सयनहिं (by sign) / लखनु (Lakshman) / नेवारे (restrained)
ramacharitamanas::1486.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::1486.essence: A heated exchange ends when Ram restrains Lakshman before pride can spread.
ramacharitamanas::1486.simple_meaning: Lakshman taunts Parashurama, saying he has only grown strong at home, not in battle. The assembly protests, and Ram quietly stops Lakshman from continuing.
ramacharitamanas::1486.simple_insight: Even sharp speech can be held back when a greater harmony is at stake.
ramacharitamanas::1486.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, after Parashurama's fury rises over Shiva's bow, Lakshman answers with cutting words. The court recoils. Ram, seeing the danger, stops his brother with a signal before the argument turns into bloodshed.
ramacharitamanas::1486.modern_relevance: A group chat is heating up, and one reply could humiliate everyone. You type it anyway, then catch yourself. The wiser move is the one that prevents the room from breaking.
ramacharitamanas::1486.insight: It teaches restraint in the middle of provocation, especially when pride could escalate conflict.

ramacharitamanas::1487.verse_sanskrit: लखन उतर आहुति सरिस भृगुबर कोपु कृसानु। बढ़त देखि जल सम बचन बोले रघुकुलभानु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1487.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी के उत्तर से, जो आहुति के समान थे, परशुरामजी के क्रोध रूपी अग्नि को बढ़ते देखकर रघुकुल के सूर्य श्री रामचंद्रजी जल के समान (शांत करने वाले) वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1487.english_translation: Seeing Parashurama's anger rise, Ram of the Raghu line spoke words that were cooling like water.
ramacharitamanas::1487.translation_literal: लखन (Lakshman) / उतर (reply) / आहुति (offering) / सरिस (like) / भृगुबर (Bhrigu's श्रेष्ठ, Parashurama) / कोपु (anger) / कृसानु (fire) / बढ़त (growing) / देखि (seeing) / जल (water) / सम (like) / बचन (words) / बोले (spoke) / रघुकुलभानु (sun of the Raghu line, Ram)
ramacharitamanas::1487.speaker: Narrator
