ramacharitamanas::1487.essence: Cooling words can stop a blaze of anger.
ramacharitamanas::1487.simple_meaning: Ram responds to rising anger with calming words. He does not meet fire with fire.
ramacharitamanas::1487.simple_insight: A tense moment can be defused by choosing a steady response instead of matching heat with heat.
ramacharitamanas::1487.detailed_meaning: Parashurama has arrived furious after Lakshman’s sharp reply, and the whole assembly is trembling. Ram steps in before the conflict can explode further. His words are meant to cool the anger, not feed it.
ramacharitamanas::1487.modern_relevance: A group chat is spiraling after one rude message, and everyone is ready to strike back. One calm reply can stop the whole fire before it spreads.
ramacharitamanas::1487.insight: It teaches you to interrupt escalation with restraint and soothing speech.

ramacharitamanas::1488.verse_sanskrit: नाथ करहु बालक पर छोहु। सूध दूधमुख करिअ न कोहू॥ जौं पै प्रभु प्रभाउ कछु जाना। तौ कि बराबरि करत अयाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1488.verse_hindi: हे नाथ ! बालक पर कृपा कीजिए। इस सीधे और दूधमुँहे बच्चे पर क्रोध न कीजिए। यदि यह प्रभु का (आपका) कुछ भी प्रभाव जानता, तो क्या यह बेसमझ आपकी बराबरी करता ? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1488.english_translation: O Lord, show kindness to the child. Do not be angry with this simple, milk-mouthed boy. If he knew even a little of your power, would this fool dare compare himself with you?
ramacharitamanas::1488.translation_literal: नाथ (lord) / करहु (do) / बालक (child) / पर (on) / छोहु (kindness) / सूध (straight) / दूधमुख (milk-faced; very young) / करिअ (do) / न (not) / कोहू (anger) / जौं (if) / पै (indeed) / प्रभु (lord's) / प्रभाउ (power, influence) / कछु (some) / जाना (knew) / तौ (then) / कि (would) / बराबरि (equal) / करत (doing) / अयाना (fool, ignorant one)
ramacharitamanas::1488.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::1488.essence: Power should answer childish provocation with mercy, not force.
ramacharitamanas::1488.simple_meaning: Lakshman asks Parashurama to spare the boy and not stay angry. He says the child is innocent and foolish enough not to understand Parashurama's greatness.
ramacharitamanas::1488.simple_insight: Mercy becomes the wiser response when power meets innocence.
ramacharitamanas::1488.detailed_meaning: Parashurama has risen in anger after Lakshman’s sharp words. Seeing the danger, Lakshman steps in and softens the moment, asking him to treat the boy like a child, not an enemy. The verse turns a confrontation into a plea for restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1488.modern_relevance: A teenager snaps in a family argument, and the room heats up fast. Someone older steps in and says, 'He doesn't know what he's doing.' That pause can save the whole relationship.
ramacharitamanas::1488.insight: It shifts the response from punishment to proportion, reminding you to read immaturity before reacting to insult.

ramacharitamanas::1489.verse_sanskrit: जौं लरिका कछु अचगरि करहीं। गुर पितु मातु मोद मन भरहीं॥ करिअ कृपा सिसु सेवक जानी। तुम्ह सम सील धीर मुनि ग्यानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1489.verse_hindi: बालक यदि कुछ चपलता भी करते हैं, तो गुरु, पिता और माता मन में आनंद से भर जाते हैं। अतः इसे छोटा बच्चा और सेवक जानकर कृपा कीजिए। आप तो समदर्शी, सुशील, धीर और ज्ञानी मुनि हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1489.english_translation: If children show a little mischief, teachers, fathers, and mothers are filled with joy. So please show mercy, knowing him as a child and servant. You are a sage—equal-minded, virtuous, patient, and wise.
ramacharitamanas::1489.translation_literal: जौं (if) / लरिका (child) / कछु (some) / अचगरि (mischief) / करहीं (do) / गुर (teacher) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / मोद (joy) / मन (mind) / भरहीं (be filled)॥ / करिअ (do) / कृपा (mercy) / सिसु (child) / सेवक (servant) / जानी (knowing) / तुम्ह (you) / सम (like) / सील (virtuous) / धीर (patient) / मुनि (sage) / ग्यानी (wise) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1489.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1489.essence: Mercy grows when strength sees innocence.
ramacharitamanas::1489.simple_meaning: Children’s small mischief can delight the adults who care for them. Ram asks Parashurama to show mercy, seeing the boy as a child and servant, while honoring Parashurama’s calm wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::1489.simple_insight: Gentleness becomes natural when strength looks at another with care instead of threat.
ramacharitamanas::1489.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar, Parashurama’s anger has risen after Lakshman’s sharp words. Ram steps in quietly and asks him to treat the boy like a child and servant, not an enemy. He softens the moment by appealing to Parashurama’s own wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::1489.modern_relevance: A teenager snaps back in a family argument, and the room tightens. The most powerful response is not to escalate, but to remember the person in front of you is still learning.
ramacharitamanas::1489.insight: It shifts the response from punishment to compassionate understanding, especially when someone is immature or reactive.

ramacharitamanas::1490.verse_sanskrit: राम बचन सुनि कछुक जुड़ाने। कहि कछु लखनु बहुरि मुसुकाने॥ हँसत देखि नख सिख रिस ब्यापी। राम तोर भ्राता बड़ पापी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1490.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी के वचन सुनकर वे कुछ ठंडे पड़े। इतने में लक्ष्मणजी कुछ कहकर फिर मुस्कुरा दिए। उनको हँसते देखकर परशुरामजी के नख से शिखा तक (सारे शरीर में) क्रोध छा गया। उन्होंने कहा- हे राम! तेरा भाई बड़ा पापी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1490.english_translation: Hearing Ram's words, he calmed somewhat. Then Lakshman said something and smiled again. Seeing him laugh, anger spread through Parashuram from head to toe. He said, “Ram, your brother is very sinful.”
ramacharitamanas::1490.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / कछुक (somewhat) / जुड़ाने (became calmed) / कहि (saying) / कछु (something) / लखनु (Lakshman) / बहुरि (again) / मुसुकाने (smiled) / हँसत (laughing) / देखि (seeing) / नख (nail) / सिख (crest/head) / रिस (anger) / ब्यापी (spread) / राम (Ram) / तोर (your) / भ्राता (brother) / बड़ (very) / पापी (sinful)
ramacharitamanas::1490.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1490.essence: A single smile can bring anger roaring back.
ramacharitamanas::1490.simple_meaning: Ram speaks, Lakshman smiles, and Parashuram's anger flares again. The scene turns from brief calm to open insult.
ramacharitamanas::1490.simple_insight: A small smile can reopen a conflict that words had only briefly softened.
ramacharitamanas::1490.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Ram has just answered Parashuram with calm dignity. Lakshman cannot resist a sharp reply and a smile. That spark makes Parashuram's anger surge back, setting up the clash that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1490.modern_relevance: You finally calm a tense room, then one sarcastic grin undoes everything. A tiny reaction can revive an argument everyone thought was settling.
ramacharitamanas::1490.insight: It shows how fragile peace is when pride is still active. One mocking response can reignite the whole conflict.

ramacharitamanas::1491.verse_sanskrit: गौर सरीर स्याम मन माहीं। कालकूट मुख पयमुख नाहीं॥ सहज टेढ़ अनुहरइ न तोही। नीचु मीचु सम देख न मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1491.verse_hindi: यह शरीर से गोरा, पर हृदय का बड़ा काला है। यह विषमुख है, दूधमुँहा नहीं। स्वभाव ही टेढ़ा है, तेरा अनुसरण नहीं करता (तेरे जैसा शीलवान नहीं है)। यह नीच मुझे काल के समान नहीं देखता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1491.english_translation: This body is fair, but the mind is dark. It has a poison mouth, not a milk mouth. Its nature is crooked, and it does not follow you. It does not see me, lowly and mortal, as death itself.
ramacharitamanas::1491.translation_literal: गौर (fair) / सरीर (body) / स्याम (dark) / मन (mind) / माहीं (within) / कालकूट (poison) / मुख (mouth) / पयमुख (milk-mouth) / नाहीं (not) / सहज (natural) / टेढ़ (crooked) / अनुहरइ (follows) / न (not) / तोही (you) / नीचु (lowly) / मीचु (death) / सम (like) / देख (sees) / न (not) / मोही (me)
ramacharitamanas::1491.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1491.essence: Anger makes the mind crooked and the other person look monstrous.
ramacharitamanas::1491.simple_meaning: Parashurama is insulting Lakshman, saying his appearance is fair but his mind is harsh and crooked. He sees Lakshman as disrespectful and dangerous.
ramacharitamanas::1491.simple_insight: Anger turns another person into an enemy before the truth is seen.
ramacharitamanas::1491.detailed_meaning: After Ram answers Parashurama, Lakshman smiles and speaks back. Parashurama, already burning with rage, lashes out and judges Lakshman's character by his own wounded pride. The scene shows how anger distorts perception before the peace-making reply arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1491.modern_relevance: You read a sharp text at midnight and decide the other person is cruel. The mind fills in poison before it checks the facts.
ramacharitamanas::1491.insight: It shows how anger projects darkness onto others and blinds the speaker to reality.

ramacharitamanas::1492.verse_sanskrit: लखन कहेउ हँसि सुनहु मुनि क्रोधु पाप कर मूल। जेहि बस जन अनुचित करहिं चरहिं बिस्व प्रतिकूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1492.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी ने हँसकर कहा- हे मुनि! सुनिए, क्रोध पाप का मूल है, जिसके वश में होकर मनुष्य अनुचित कर्म कर बैठते हैं और विश्वभर के प्रतिकूल चलते (सबका अहित करते) हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1492.english_translation: Lakshman said with a smile, "Listen, sage: anger is the root of wrongdoing. Under its control, people do what is improper and act against the whole world."
ramacharitamanas::1492.translation_literal: लखन (Lakshman) / कहेउ (said) / हँसि (smiling) / सुनहु (listen) / मुनि (sage) / क्रोधु (anger) / पाप (wrongdoing) / कर (of) / मूल (root) / जेहि (whose) / बस (control) / जन (people) / अनुचित (improper) / करहिं (do) / चरहिं (walk/act) / बिस्व (world) / प्रतिकूल (against)
ramacharitamanas::1492.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::1492.essence: Anger is the first wrong move; everything else follows it.
ramacharitamanas::1492.simple_meaning: Anger is the source of bad actions. Once anger takes control, people do things that hurt others and go against what is right.
ramacharitamanas::1492.simple_insight: You can catch the harm at its source, before anger turns into action.
ramacharitamanas::1492.detailed_meaning: In the heat of the argument, Lakshman answers Parashurama with a smile. Instead of escalating, he names the real enemy: anger itself. The verse turns the scene from insult to self-control.
ramacharitamanas::1492.modern_relevance: You are one sharp reply away from ruining a family dinner, a team chat, or a friendship. Lakshman names the moment before damage becomes irreversible.
ramacharitamanas::1492.insight: It shifts attention from the outer conflict to the inner trigger, so restraint begins earlier.

ramacharitamanas::1493.verse_sanskrit: मैं तुम्हार अनुचर मुनिराया। परिहरि कोपु करिअ अब दाया॥ टूट चाप नहिं जुरिहि रिसाने। बैठिअ होइहिं पाय पिराने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1493.verse_hindi: हे मुनिराज! मैं आपका दास हूँ। अब क्रोध त्यागकर दया कीजिए। टूटा हुआ धनुष क्रोध करने से जुड़ नहीं जाएगा। खड़े-खड़े पैर दुःखने लगे होंगे, बैठ जाइए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1493.english_translation: O great sage, I am your servant. Now leave anger and show mercy. A broken bow will not be mended by rage. Sit down; your feet must be aching from standing.
ramacharitamanas::1493.translation_literal: मैं (I) / तुम्हार (your) / अनुचर (servant) / मुनिराया (O king of sages) / परिहरि (leaving aside) / कोपु (anger) / करिअ (do) / अब (now) / दाया (mercy) / टूट (broken) / चाप (bow) / नहिं (not) / जुरिहि (will be mended) / रिसाने (by anger) / बैठिअ (sit down) / होइहिं (will become) / पाय (feet) / पिराने (painful)
ramacharitamanas::1493.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::1493.essence: Anger cannot repair what only skill and calm can mend.
ramacharitamanas::1493.simple_meaning: Lakshman speaks respectfully to the sage and asks him to stop being angry. He says anger will not fix the broken bow, and the sage should sit down if standing is tiring.
ramacharitamanas::1493.simple_insight: Force cannot repair what patience and skill must mend.
ramacharitamanas::1493.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the bow has been broken and tension is rising. Lakshman, sharp but respectful, tells the sage that anger will not solve anything. The moment turns from insult to practical restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1493.modern_relevance: A meeting is going sideways, and one person keeps escalating the room. Lakshman’s words cut through the heat: anger does not repair what already broke.
ramacharitamanas::1493.insight: It shifts the mind from reacting with force to responding with calm usefulness.

ramacharitamanas::1494.verse_sanskrit: जौं अति प्रिय तौ करिअ उपाई। जोरिअ कोउ बड़ गुनी बोलाई॥ बोलत लखनहिं जनकु डेराहीं। मष्ट करहु अनुचित भल नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1494.verse_hindi: यदि धनुष अत्यन्त ही प्रिय हो, तो कोई उपाय किया जाए और किसी बड़े गुणी (कारीगर) को बुलाकर जुड़वा दिया जाए। लक्ष्मणजी के बोलने से जनकजी डर जाते हैं और कहते हैं- बस, चुप रहिए, अनुचित बोलना अच्छा नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1494.english_translation: If the bow is very dear, then have it repaired. Call a skilled craftsman to join it again. Janaka grows afraid at Lakshmana's words and says, "Enough—do not speak improperly."
ramacharitamanas::1494.translation_literal: जौं (if) / अति (very) / प्रिय (dear) / तौ (then) / करिअ (do) / उपाई (a remedy) / जोरिअ (join again) / कोउ (some) / बड़ (great) / गुनी (skilled) / बोलाई (calling) / बोलत (speaking) / लखनहिं (to Lakshmana) / जनकु (Janaka) / डेराहीं (becomes afraid) / मष्ट (enough) / करहु (do) / अनुचित (improper) / भल (good) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::1494.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1494.essence: A wise response can calm anger before it becomes damage.
ramacharitamanas::1494.simple_meaning: Janaka tries to defuse Lakshmana's sharp words by suggesting the bow could simply be repaired. He then asks him to stop speaking in a way that feels improper.
ramacharitamanas::1494.simple_insight: Not every sharp moment needs a sharper reply. Sometimes restraint keeps the room from breaking.
ramacharitamanas::1494.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, Lakshmana has just spoken boldly about the broken bow. Janaka, startled and uneasy, tries to calm the situation by suggesting a practical fix and warning him to stop speaking harshly. The scene shows tension rising before Sita's swayamvar can move forward.
ramacharitamanas::1494.modern_relevance: Someone makes a cutting remark in a family meeting, and the room tightens instantly. You can feel the urge to answer harder, but the wiser move is to slow the spiral before it becomes a fight.
ramacharitamanas::1494.insight: It teaches you to interrupt escalation and return the exchange to a workable level.

ramacharitamanas::1495.verse_sanskrit: थर थर काँपहिं पुर नर नारी। छोट कुमार खोट बड़ भारी॥ भृगुपति सुनि सुनि निरभय बानी। रिस तन जरइ होई बल हानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1495.verse_hindi: जनकपुर के स्त्री-पुरुष थर-थर काँप रहे हैं (और मन ही मन कह रहे हैं कि) छोटा कुमार बड़ा ही खोटा है। लक्ष्मणजी की निर्भय वाणी सुन-सुनकर परशुरामजी का शरीर क्रोध से जला जा रहा है और उनके बल की हानि हो रही है (उनका बल घट रहा है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1495.english_translation: The people of Janakpur trembled. They called the young prince deeply rude. Hearing Lakshman's fearless words again and again, Parashurama burned with rage and his strength began to fail.
ramacharitamanas::1495.translation_literal: थर थर (trembling) / काँपहिं (tremble) / पुर (city) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / छोट (small, young) / कुमार (prince) / खोट (bad, rude) / बड़ (very) / भारी (great, severe) / भृगुपति (lord of Bhrigu) / सुनि सुनि (hearing again and again) / निरभय (fearless) / बानी (speech) / रिस (anger) / तन (body) / जरइ (burns) / होई (becomes) / बल (strength) / हानी (loss)
ramacharitamanas::1495.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1495.essence: Rage looks powerful, but it burns away its own strength.
ramacharitamanas::1495.simple_meaning: The people of Janakpur are frightened by Lakshman's bold words. Parashurama's anger keeps rising, and that anger weakens him.
ramacharitamanas::1495.simple_insight: Bold speech can shake a room, but rage also drains the one who holds it.
ramacharitamanas::1495.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the wedding hall has turned tense after the broken bow. The people tremble, Lakshman speaks sharply, and Parashurama's fury rises. This verse shows the crowd's fear and the saint-warrior's growing loss of composure.
ramacharitamanas::1495.modern_relevance: A family dinner turns silent after one cutting remark. Everyone feels the temperature drop, and the angriest person in the room is also the one losing control fastest.
ramacharitamanas::1495.insight: It shifts attention from the force of angry speech to the self-damage anger creates.

ramacharitamanas::1496.verse_sanskrit: बोले रामहि देइ निहोरा। बचउँ बिचारि बंधु लघु तोरा॥ मनु मलीन तनु सुंदर कैसें। बिष रस भरा कनक घटु जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1496.verse_hindi: तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी पर एहसान जनाकर परशुरामजी बोले- तेरा छोटा भाई समझकर मैं इसे बचा रहा हूँ। यह मन का मैला और शरीर का कैसा सुंदर है, जैसे विष के रस से भरा हुआ सोने का घड़ा! ॥
ramacharitamanas::1496.english_translation: Parashurama said, "I grant this favor to Ram: I spare you because you are your younger brother. How can a mind be impure and a body beautiful? It is like a golden pot filled with poison."
ramacharitamanas::1496.translation_literal: बोले (said) / रामहि (to Ram) / देइ (giving) / निहोरा (request/favor) / बचउँ (I spare) / बिचारि (considering) / बंधु (brother) / लघु (younger) / तोरा (your) / मनु (mind) / मलीन (polluted) / तनु (body) / सुंदर (beautiful) / कैसें (how) / बिष (poison) / रस (essence/liquid) / भरा (filled) / कनक (gold) / घटु (pot) / जैसें (like)
ramacharitamanas::1496.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1496.essence: A beautiful exterior means nothing when the mind is poisoned.
ramacharitamanas::1496.simple_meaning: Parashurama says he is sparing Lakshman because Ram is his elder brother. Then he insults Lakshman, saying a beautiful body means nothing if the mind is corrupt.
ramacharitamanas::1496.simple_insight: Outward grace cannot hide inner corruption. What matters most is the quality of the mind.
ramacharitamanas::1496.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the broken bow has turned into a clash of pride. Lakshman’s sharp words provoke Parashurama, who now stands before Ram and Lakshman in fierce judgment, claiming restraint while exposing the danger he sees in Lakshman’s inner state.
ramacharitamanas::1496.modern_relevance: Someone looks polished in a meeting, speaks smoothly, and still leaves a sour feeling behind. The verse cuts through appearances: a refined exterior cannot cover a bitter, reckless mind.
ramacharitamanas::1496.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to character, warning that beauty without inner purity is fragile and misleading.

ramacharitamanas::1497.verse_sanskrit: सुनि लछिमन बिहसे बहुरि नयन तरेरे राम। गुर समीप गवने सकुचि परिहरि बानी बाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::1497.verse_hindi: यह सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी फिर हँसे। तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने तिरछी नजर से उनकी ओर देखा, जिससे लक्ष्मणजी सकुचाकर, विपरीत बोलना छोड़कर, गुरुजी के पास चले गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1497.english_translation: Hearing this, Lakshman laughed again. Then Ram gave him a sidelong look, and Lakshman, embarrassed, stopped speaking harshly and went near the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::1497.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / बिहसे (laughed) / बहुरि (again) / नयन (eyes) / तरेरे (cast sideways) / राम (Ram) / गुर (teacher) / समीप (near) / गवने (went) / सकुचि (with embarrassment) / परिहरि (having छोड़ा) / बानी (speech) / बाम (harsh/contrary)
ramacharitamanas::1497.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1497.essence: Ram's glance is enough to turn pride into restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1497.simple_meaning: Lakshman laughs again, Ram silences him with a look, and Lakshman stops his sharp words and returns to the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::1497.simple_insight: A single look can end a quarrel before it grows louder.
ramacharitamanas::1497.detailed_meaning: After Parashuram's sharp exchange in Janakpur, Lakshman keeps provoking with a laugh. Ram answers only with a sideways glance. Lakshman immediately feels the correction, drops the harsh words, and moves back toward the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::1497.modern_relevance: You make a cutting joke in a tense room, and one calm look from someone you respect tells you to stop. No speech is needed; the correction lands instantly.
ramacharitamanas::1497.insight: It shows how restraint can restore order faster than argument.

ramacharitamanas::1498.verse_sanskrit: अति बिनीत मृदु सीतल बानी। बोले रामु जोरि जुग पानी॥ सुनहु नाथ तुम्ह सहज सुजाना। बालक बचनु करिअ नहिं काना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1498.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी दोनों हाथ जोड़कर अत्यन्त विनय के साथ कोमल और शीतल वाणी बोले- हे नाथ! सुनिए, आप तो स्वभाव से ही सुजान हैं। आप बालक के वचन पर कान न दीजिए (उसे सुना-अनसुना कर दीजिए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1498.english_translation: With extreme humility, soft and cooling words, Rama spoke with both hands joined: "Listen, lord, you are naturally wise. Do not heed a child's words."
ramacharitamanas::1498.translation_literal: अति (very) / बिनीत (humble) / मृदु (soft) / सीतल (cooling) / बानी (speech) / बोले (spoke) / रामु (Rama) / जोरि (joining) / जुग (both) / पानी (hands) / सुनहु (listen) / नाथ (lord) / तुम्ह (you) / सहज (naturally) / सुजाना (wise) / बालक (child) / बचनु (words) / करिअ (do) / नहिं (not) / काना (ear)
ramacharitamanas::1498.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1498.essence: Gentleness can disarm anger before it grows teeth.
ramacharitamanas::1498.simple_meaning: Rama speaks with humility and asks the elder to ignore a child's harsh words.
ramacharitamanas::1498.simple_insight: A calm response can stop pride from turning a small insult into a bigger wound.
ramacharitamanas::1498.detailed_meaning: In the bow-breaking assembly, Parashurama stands offended and ready to strike. Rama answers not with force, but with folded hands and gentle respect, trying to cool the moment before it erupts into violence.
ramacharitamanas::1498.modern_relevance: Someone snaps at you in a group chat, and every instinct says to clap back. Instead, you answer softly, lower the temperature, and refuse to let one sharp remark become a bigger fire.
ramacharitamanas::1498.insight: It teaches restraint before reaction, using humility to defuse conflict.

ramacharitamanas::1499.verse_sanskrit: बररै बालकु एकु सुभाऊ। इन्हहि न संत बिदूषहिं काऊ ॥ तेहिं नाहीं कछु काज बिगारा। अपराधी मैं नाथ तुम्हारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1499.verse_hindi: बर्रै और बालक का एक स्वभाव है। संतजन इन्हें कभी दोष नहीं लगाते। फिर उसने (लक्ष्मण ने) तो कुछ काम भी नहीं बिगाड़ा है, हे नाथ! आपका अपराधी तो मैं हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1499.english_translation: A child and a wild horse share one nature. The wise never blame them. He has ruined nothing, O Lord. I alone am at fault.
ramacharitamanas::1499.translation_literal: बररै (wild horse / child) / बालकु (child) / एकु (one) / सुभाऊ (nature) । इन्हहि (these) / न (not) / संत (wise) / बिदूषहिं (blame) / काऊ (anyone) ॥ तेहिं (by him) / नाहीं (not) / कछु (anything) / काज (work) / बिगारा (spoiled) । अपराधी (guilty one) / मैं (I) / नाथ (O Lord) / तुम्हारा (yours) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1499.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1499.essence: Real strength takes responsibility before it takes offense.
ramacharitamanas::1499.simple_meaning: Ram says Lakshman is only acting like a child and has done no real harm. The fault is his alone.
ramacharitamanas::1499.simple_insight: A mature heart protects the weaker one and takes the blame itself.
ramacharitamanas::1499.detailed_meaning: In the court at Janakpur, Lakshman has spoken sharply. Ram gently steps in before the tension grows. He excuses Lakshman as someone naturally impulsive, says no work has been spoiled, and takes responsibility himself to calm the moment.
ramacharitamanas::1499.modern_relevance: A younger sibling snaps at dinner, and the room tightens. Instead of escalating it, someone wiser lowers the heat, protects the vulnerable one, and takes responsibility for peace.
ramacharitamanas::1499.insight: It shifts you from defending ego to absorbing blame for the sake of harmony.

ramacharitamanas::1500.verse_sanskrit: कृपा कोपु बधु बँधब गोसाईं। मो पर करिअ दास की नाईं॥ कहिअ बेगि जेहि बिधि रिस जाई। मुनिनायक सोइ करौं उपाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1500.verse_hindi: अतः हे स्वामी! कृपा, क्रोध, वध और बंधन, जो कुछ करना हो, दास की तरह (अर्थात दास समझकर) मुझ पर कीजिए। जिस प्रकार से शीघ्र आपका क्रोध दूर हो। हे मुनिराज! बताइए, मैं वही उपाय करूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1500.english_translation: O master, do whatever you wish—grace, anger, punishment, or bondage. Treat me like a servant. Tell me quickly how your anger may be removed, and I will do that remedy, O sage.
ramacharitamanas::1500.translation_literal: कृपा (grace) / कोपु (anger) / बधु (binding) / बँधब (to bind) / गोसाईं (master) / मो पर (on me) / करिअ (do) / दास की नाईं (like a servant)॥ / कहिअ (tell) / बेगि (quickly) / जेहि बिधि (by which way) / रिस (anger) / जाई (goes away) / मुनिनायक (leader of sages) / सोइ (that) / करौं (I will do) / उपाई (remedy)॥
ramacharitamanas::1500.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1500.essence: Humility asks for correction before asking for pardon.
ramacharitamanas::1500.simple_meaning: Ram offers himself completely to the sage, even accepting punishment, and asks for the quickest way to remove the sage's anger.
ramacharitamanas::1500.simple_insight: Real humility listens first, even when it must accept blame.
ramacharitamanas::1500.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar, Ram has already spoken gently to the angry sage. The moment is tense: a broken bow, a proud assembly, and a saint's anger hanging over the scene. Ram lowers himself fully and asks what must be done to restore peace.
ramacharitamanas::1500.modern_relevance: A meeting goes sideways, and you know your tone made it worse. Before defending yourself, you ask what would repair the damage.
ramacharitamanas::1500.insight: It teaches you to prioritize repair over self-protection when conflict has already begun.

ramacharitamanas::1501.verse_sanskrit: कह मुनि राम जाइ रिस कैसें। अजहुँ अनुज तव चितव अनैसें॥ एहि कें कंठ कुठारु न दीन्हा। तौ मैं कहा कोपु करि कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1501.verse_hindi: मुनि ने कहा- हे राम! क्रोध कैसे जाए, अब भी तेरा छोटा भाई टेढ़ा ही ताक रहा है। इसकी गर्दन पर मैंने कुठार न चलाया, तो क्रोध करके किया ही क्या? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1501.english_translation: The sage said, "How can anger leave when your younger brother still looks at me so crookedly? If I did not strike off his head, what did I accomplish by being angry?"
ramacharitamanas::1501.translation_literal: कह (said) / मुनि (sage) / राम (Ram) / जाइ (go) / रिस (anger) / कैसें (how) / अजहुँ (still) / अनुज (younger brother) / तव (your) / चितव (looks) / अनैसें (crookedly) / एहि (this) / कें (of) / कंठ (neck) / कुठारु (axe) / न (not) / दीन्हा (given) / तौ (then) / मैं (I) / कहा (what) / कोपु (anger) / करि (doing) / कीन्हा (did)
ramacharitamanas::1501.speaker: Muni
ramacharitamanas::1501.essence: Anger survives as long as pride still wants a wound repaid.
ramacharitamanas::1501.simple_meaning: The sage says his anger cannot calm down because Lakshman is still glaring at him. He feels that if he did not retaliate, his anger had no real force behind it.
ramacharitamanas::1501.simple_insight: Anger clings when the ego still feels challenged.
ramacharitamanas::1501.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Parashuram is furious after Lakshman’s sharp words. Ram tries to soften the moment, but the sage keeps defending his rage. This verse shows the last resistance before his anger begins to break.
ramacharitamanas::1501.modern_relevance: You replay a rude reply in your head long after the conversation ends. The body wants payback, not peace. Until the insult loses its grip, anger keeps finding reasons to stay.
ramacharitamanas::1501.insight: It exposes how pride feeds anger, and how retaliation becomes the ego’s proof of power.

ramacharitamanas::1502.verse_sanskrit: गर्भ स्रवहिं अवनिप रवनि सुनि कुठार गति घोर। परसु अछत देखउँ जिअत बैरी भूपकिसोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::1502.verse_hindi: मेरे जिस कुठार की घोर करनी सुनकर राजाओं की स्त्रियों के गर्भ गिर पड़ते हैं, उसी फरसे के रहते मैं इस शत्रु राजपुत्र को जीवित देख रहा हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1502.english_translation: The cruel force of my axe is such that, hearing of it, queens miscarry. Yet with that axe in hand, I still see this enemy prince alive.
ramacharitamanas::1502.translation_literal: गर्भ (wombs) / स्रवहिं (fall away) / अवनिप (earth-lords, kings) / रवनि (hearing) / सुनि (having heard) / कुठार (axe) / गति (power, force) / घोर (terrible) / परसु (axe) / अछत (present, remaining) / देखउँ (I see) / जिअत (alive) / बैरी (enemy) / भूपकिसोर (young prince, royal youth)
ramacharitamanas::1502.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1502.essence: Raw power becomes humiliation when it cannot control the moment.
ramacharitamanas::1502.simple_meaning: The speaker says his axe is so feared that even hearing of it makes queens miscarry, yet this enemy prince still lives in front of him.
ramacharitamanas::1502.simple_insight: Pride can make even strength feel useless when it cannot end what it wants to end.
ramacharitamanas::1502.detailed_meaning: In the confrontation with Parashuram, the furious warrior boasts of his terrible axe and its fearsome reputation. He is shocked that the young prince before him is still alive, and that shock feeds the next surge of anger.
ramacharitamanas::1502.modern_relevance: You bring every argument, every fact, every sharp line you have prepared — and still the other person stands there unchanged. That helplessness can turn power into rage.
ramacharitamanas::1502.insight: It shows how wounded ego reacts when its force meets resistance it cannot instantly break.

ramacharitamanas::1503.verse_sanskrit: बहइ न हाथु दहइ रिस छाती। भा कुठारु कुंठित नृपघाती॥ भयउ बाम बिधि फिरेउ सुभाऊ। मोरे हृदयँ कृपा कसि काऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1503.verse_hindi: हाथ चलता नहीं, क्रोध से छाती जली जाती है। (हाय!) राजाओं का घातक यह कुठार भी कुण्ठित हो गया। विधाता विपरीत हो गया, इससे मेरा स्वभाव बदल गया, नहीं तो भला, मेरे हृदय में किसी समय भी कृपा कैसी? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1503.english_translation: My hand will not strike, and anger burns my chest. This king-slayer's axe has become dull. Fate has turned against me, and my nature has changed; otherwise, how could compassion ever live in my heart?
ramacharitamanas::1503.translation_literal: बहइ (moves) / न (not) / हाथु (hand) / दहइ (burns) / रिस (anger) / छाती (chest) / भा (became) / कुठारु (axe) / कुंठित (blunted) / नृपघाती (king-slayer) / भयउ (became) / बाम (adverse) / बिधि (fate) / फिरेउ (turned) / सुभाऊ (nature) / मोरे (my) / हृदयँ (in heart) / कृपा (compassion) / कसि (how) / काऊ (ever)
ramacharitamanas::1503.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1503.essence: Violence weakens when compassion unexpectedly enters the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1503.simple_meaning: Parashurama admits his hand cannot strike, his anger is burning, and even his axe has lost its force. He blames adverse fate for changing his nature and making compassion arise in him.
ramacharitamanas::1503.simple_insight: Even fierce pride can be interrupted by a force bigger than ego.
ramacharitamanas::1503.detailed_meaning: Parashurama has confronted Ram and then noticed Lakshman’s fearless challenge. The warrior-sage, once known for rage and destruction, suddenly feels his violence failing him. He speaks in frustration, sensing that something has changed in him.
ramacharitamanas::1503.modern_relevance: You are ready to lash out in a group chat, then notice your fingers hovering over the screen. The heat is still there, but the impulse to strike has lost its power.
ramacharitamanas::1503.insight: It shows how anger can be exposed as unstable the moment it meets a stronger presence.

ramacharitamanas::1504.verse_sanskrit: आजु दया दुखु दुसह सहावा। सुनि सौमित्रि बिहसि सिरु नावा॥ बाउ कृपा मूरति अनुकूला। बोलत बचन झरत जनु फूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::1504.verse_hindi: आज दया मुझे यह दुःसह दुःख सहा रही है। यह सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी ने मुस्कुराकर सिर नवाया (और कहा-) आपकी कृपा रूपी वायु भी आपकी मूर्ति के अनुकूल ही है, वचन बोलते हैं, मानो फूल झड़ रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1504.english_translation: Today, compassion has made me bear unbearable pain. Hearing this, Lakshman smiled and bowed his head. Your grace, like the wind, is always in harmony with your form. Your words fall like flowers.
ramacharitamanas::1504.translation_literal: आजु (today) / दया (compassion) / दुखु (pain) / दुसह (unbearable) / सहावा (made bear) / सुनि (hearing) / सौमित्रि (Lakshman) / बिहसि (smiling) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / बाउ (wind) / कृपा (grace) / मूरति (form) / अनुकूला (in harmony) / बोलत (speaking) / बचन (words) / झरत (falling) / जनु (as if) / फूला (flowers)
ramacharitamanas::1504.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1504.essence: Grace can meet anger without losing its softness.
ramacharitamanas::1504.simple_meaning: Parashurama says that compassion has made him suffer unbearable pain. Lakshman responds with calm respect, praising the gentleness in his words.
ramacharitamanas::1504.simple_insight: Even in tension, grace can soften the room instead of hardening it.
ramacharitamanas::1504.detailed_meaning: In the Sita swayamvar, Parashurama is furious after his bow is broken and boasts of his power. Lakshman answers lightly but respectfully, smiling and bowing. This verse captures that strange moment when rage meets grace and the clash is still not yet over.
ramacharitamanas::1504.modern_relevance: Someone snaps at you in a meeting, and you answer without matching their heat. The room changes before anyone notices — not because you won, but because you stayed gentle.
ramacharitamanas::1504.insight: It teaches you to answer hostility with composed respect instead of reflexive anger.

ramacharitamanas::1505.verse_sanskrit: जौं पै कृपाँ जरिहिं मुनि गाता। क्रोध भएँ तनु राख बिधाता॥ देखु जनक हठि बालकु एहू। कीन्ह चहत जड़ जमपुर गेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1505.verse_hindi: हे मुनि ! यदि कृपा करने से आपका शरीर जला जाता है, तो क्रोध होने पर तो शरीर की रक्षा विधाता ही करेंगे। (परशुरामजी ने कहा-) हे जनक! देख, यह मूर्ख बालक हठ करके यमपुरी में घर (निवास) करना चाहता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1505.english_translation: O sage, if kindness can burn your body, then anger can surely protect it by the Creator's will. Look, Janak, this stubborn boy wants to make his home in the city of death.
ramacharitamanas::1505.translation_literal: जौं (if) / पै (indeed) / कृपाँ (by kindness) / जरिहिं (burn) / मुनि (sage) / गाता (body) / क्रोध (anger) / भएँ (having become) / तनु (body) / राख (protect) / बिधाता (the Creator) / देखु (look) / जनक (Janak) / हठि (stubborn) / बालकु (boy) / एहू (this) / कीन्ह (made) / चहत (wants) / जड़ (foolish) / जमपुर (city of death) / गेहू (home)
ramacharitamanas::1505.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1505.simple_meaning: Parashurama mocks the boy's stubbornness and warns Janak that this child is inviting death by his arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::1505.simple_insight: Pride makes a person blind to danger before danger ever arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1505.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Parashurama is furious after the bow-breaking incident. He turns his anger toward the young challenger, calling him stubborn and foolish, and warns Janak that this boy is courting death. The tension is at its peak before Lakshman answers.
ramacharitamanas::1505.modern_relevance: A senior in the room dismisses a younger person's confidence as arrogance. The atmosphere tightens before anyone even speaks back.
ramacharitamanas::1505.insight: It shows how anger quickly turns into contempt and how contempt inflates a small conflict into a life-or-death challenge.

ramacharitamanas::1506.verse_sanskrit: बेगि करहु किन आँखिन्ह ओटा। देखत छोट खोट नृपु ढोटा॥ बिहसे लखनु कहा मन माहीं। मूदें आँखि कतहुँ कोउ नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1506.verse_hindi: इसको शीघ्र ही आँखों की ओट क्यों नहीं करते? यह राजपुत्र देखने में छोटा है, पर है बड़ा खोटा। लक्ष्मणजी ने हँसकर मन ही मन कहा- आँख मूँद लेने पर कहीं कोई नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1506.english_translation: Why not quickly move him out of sight? He looks small, but he is very wicked. Lakshman smiled and thought to himself, "If eyes are closed, nowhere is anyone seen."
ramacharitamanas::1506.translation_literal: बेगि (quickly) / करहु (do) / किन (why not) / आँखिन्ह (of the eyes) / ओटा (out of sight) / देखत (seeing) / छोट (small) / खोट (crooked/wicked) / नृपु (king) / ढोटा (prince/young fellow) / बिहसे (smiled) / लखनु (Lakshman) / कहा (said) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / मूदें (closed) / आँखि (eyes) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / कोउ (someone) / नाहीं (is not)
ramacharitamanas::1506.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1506.essence: A closed mind sees no one; Lakshman answers insult with inward ease.
ramacharitamanas::1506.simple_meaning: Parashuram wants the boy removed from sight, calling him small but deceitful. Lakshman quietly thinks that if the eyes are shut, nothing is seen anywhere.
ramacharitamanas::1506.simple_insight: A sharp insult can be met with a lighter mind that refuses to be shaken.
ramacharitamanas::1506.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, Parashuram is angered by the broken bow and turns his harsh attention toward Ram. Lakshman answers with a private, teasing thought that undercuts the insult without open defiance. The verse keeps the tension moving toward Parashuram's next outburst.
ramacharitamanas::1506.modern_relevance: Someone snaps at a teenager in front of a crowd, expecting fear. Instead, the teenager stays inwardly amused, untouched by the glare. That calm humor can be stronger than a fight.
ramacharitamanas::1506.insight: It shows how to keep inner ease when another person tries to provoke shame or fear.

ramacharitamanas::1507.verse_sanskrit: परसुरामु तब राम प्रति बोले उर अति क्रोधु। संभु सरासनु तोरि सठ करसि हमार प्रबोधु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1507.verse_hindi: तब परशुरामजी हृदय में अत्यन्त क्रोध भरकर श्री रामजी से बोले- अरे शठ! तू शिवजी का धनुष तोड़कर उलटा हमीं को ज्ञान सिखाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1507.english_translation: Then Parashurama, filled with intense anger in his heart, said to Ram: "You fool, you broke Shiva's bow and now you are trying to instruct me!"
ramacharitamanas::1507.translation_literal: परसुरामु (Parashurama) / तब (then) / राम प्रति (toward Ram) / बोले (spoke) / उर (heart) / अति (very) / क्रोधु (anger) / संभु (Shiva) / सरासनु (bow) / तोरि (breaking) / सठ (fool) / करसि (you do) / हमार (my) / प्रबोधु (instruction / awakening)
ramacharitamanas::1507.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1507.essence: Pride hears insult where wisdom is being offered.
ramacharitamanas::1507.simple_meaning: Parashurama, furious, accuses Ram of breaking Shiva's bow and then lecturing him.
ramacharitamanas::1507.simple_insight: Anger narrows vision until even humility looks like insult.
ramacharitamanas::1507.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Ram has broken Shiva's bow, and Parashurama rises in fury. Instead of seeing Ram's greatness, he sees only challenge and disrespect. This line begins the clash that tests whether power can recognise divinity.
ramacharitamanas::1507.modern_relevance: Someone corrects you in front of others, and your chest tightens before you even hear the words. In that second, pride turns a simple moment into a fight.
ramacharitamanas::1507.insight: It shows how ego turns guidance into offense and blocks clear seeing.

ramacharitamanas::1508.verse_sanskrit: बंधु कहइ कटु संमत तोरें। तू छल बिनय करसि कर जोरें॥ करु परितोषु मोर संग्रामा। नाहिं त छाड़ कहाउब रामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1508.verse_hindi: तेरा यह भाई तेरी ही सम्मति से कटु वचन बोलता है और तू छल से हाथ जोड़कर विनय करता है। या तो युद्ध में मेरा संतोष कर, नहीं तो राम कहलाना छोड़ दे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1508.english_translation: Your brother speaks harsh words with your approval. You fold your hands and speak with deceit. Satisfy me in battle, or stop calling yourself Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1508.translation_literal: बंधु (brother) / कहइ (speaks) / कटु (harsh) / संमत (with approval) / तोरें (of yours) / तू (you) / छल (deceit) / बिनय (humble request) / करसि (do) / कर (hands) / जोरें (joined) / करु (do) / परितोषु (satisfy) / मोर (my) / संग्रामा (battle) / नाहिं (otherwise not) / त (then) / छाड़ (leave) / कहाउब (calling) / रामा (Ram)
ramacharitamanas::1508.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1508.essence: Pride sees deceit where humility stands.
ramacharitamanas::1508.simple_meaning: Parashurama accuses Ram of hidden disrespect. He demands either a real fight or that Ram stop claiming his name.
ramacharitamanas::1508.simple_insight: Some anger only wants proof. It forces a confrontation where politeness no longer counts.
ramacharitamanas::1508.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, Parashurama has already erupted after Shiva's bow is broken. Now he turns on Ram, reading Ram's calm courtesy as deception and demanding either combat or a renunciation of Ram's claim to honour.
ramacharitamanas::1508.modern_relevance: A senior keeps pressing you after you apologize politely, convinced your calm tone is fake. The room tightens because the issue is no longer the mistake — it is whether your sincerity will be believed.
ramacharitamanas::1508.insight: It shows how wounded pride turns every gesture into suspicion and demands a public test of worth.

ramacharitamanas::1509.verse_sanskrit: छलु तजि करहि समरु सिवद्रोही। बंधु सहित न त मारउँ तोही॥ भृगुपति बकहिं कुठार उठाएँ। मन मुसुकाहिं रामु सिर नाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1509.verse_hindi: अरे शिवद्रोही! छल त्यागकर मुझसे युद्ध कर। नहीं तो भाई सहित तुझे मार डालूँगा। इस प्रकार परशुरामजी कुठार उठाए बक रहे हैं और श्री रामचन्द्रजी सिर झुकाए मन ही मन मुस्कुरा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1509.english_translation: “O enemy of Shiva, give up deceit and fight me in battle. Otherwise I will kill you along with your brother.” Thus Parashurama raised his axe and spoke harshly, while Ram Chandr bowed his head and smiled inwardly.
ramacharitamanas::1509.translation_literal: छलु (deceit) / तजि (having given up) / करहि (do) / समरु (battle) / सिवद्रोही (enemy of Shiva) / बंधु (brother) / सहित (together with) / न (not) / त मारउँ (I will kill) / तोही (you) / भृगुपति (lord of Bhrigu, Parashurama) / बकहिं (speaks) / कुठार (axe) / उठाएँ (raising) / मन (mind) / मुसुकाहिं (smiles) / रामु (Ram) / सिर (head) / नाएँ (bowing)
ramacharitamanas::1509.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1509.essence: True strength stays calm while pride rages.
ramacharitamanas::1509.simple_meaning: Parashurama, still furious, demands honest combat and threatens to kill Ram and Lakshman. Ram stays calm, bows respectfully, and smiles inwardly.
ramacharitamanas::1509.simple_insight: Calm can stand untouched in the middle of someone else’s rage.
ramacharitamanas::1509.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, Parashurama has erupted after the breaking of Shiva’s bow. He lifts his axe and threatens Ram and Lakshman, but Ram remains bowed, composed, and inwardly amused. The scene shows the contrast between wounded pride and unshaken restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1509.modern_relevance: Someone is shouting in the meeting, trying to provoke you into matching their heat. You stay quiet, respectful, and untouched. That restraint changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::1509.insight: It teaches you to hold your center when anger demands a reaction.

ramacharitamanas::1510.verse_sanskrit: गुनह लखन कर हम पर रोषू। कतहुँ सुधाइहु ते बड़ दोषू॥ टेढ़ जानि सब बंदइ काहू। बक्र चंद्रमहि ग्रसइ न राहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1510.verse_hindi: (श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने मन ही मन कहा-) गुनाह (दोष) तो लक्ष्मण का और क्रोध मुझ पर करते हैं। कहीं-कहीं सीधेपन में भी बड़ा दोष होता है। टेढ़ा जानकर सब लोग किसी की भी वंदना करते हैं, टेढ़े चन्द्रमा को राहु भी नहीं ग्रसता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1510.english_translation: Laxmana is at fault, yet people blame me. Straightness itself can become a great flaw. Everyone bows to what is bent; even Rahu does not swallow the curved moon.
ramacharitamanas::1510.translation_literal: गुनह (fault) / लखन (Laxmana) / कर (of) / हम (me) / पर (on) / रोषू (anger) / कतहुँ (somehow) / सुधाइहु (straightness) / तोरें (of yours) / ते (than) / बड़ (great) / दोषू (fault)॥ टेढ़ (crooked) / जानि (knowing) / सब (all) / बंदइ (bow to) / काहू (someone) / बक्र (curved) / चंद्रमहि (moon) / ग्रसइ (swallows) / न (not) / राहू (Rahu) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1510.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1510.essence: Even truth needs flexibility to be received.
ramacharitamanas::1510.simple_meaning: Ram says that people often blame him for Laxmana's fault. He adds that being too straight can itself be a weakness, while the world often bows to what is bent or flexible.
ramacharitamanas::1510.simple_insight: Sometimes firmness backfires; wisdom also knows when to bend.
ramacharitamanas::1510.detailed_meaning: At Parashurama's angry challenge in Balkand, Ram stands calm while the tension could turn violent. In his inward response, he reflects on how the world judges strength and softness, preparing the ground for a wiser, less combative answer.
ramacharitamanas::1510.modern_relevance: You keep insisting on being perfectly direct in a tense family argument, and the room only hardens. Sometimes the person who bends slightly keeps the whole relationship from breaking.
ramacharitamanas::1510.insight: It shifts the mind from rigid self-assertion to strategic humility and social intelligence.

ramacharitamanas::1511.verse_sanskrit: राम कहेउ रिस तजिअ मुनीसा। कर कुठारु आगें यह सीसा॥ जेहिं रिस जाइ करिअ सोइ स्वामी। मोहि जानिअ आपन अनुगामी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1511.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने (प्रकट) कहा- हे मुनीश्वर! क्रोध छोड़िए। आपके हाथ में कुठार है और मेरा यह सिर आगे है, जिस प्रकार आपका क्रोध जाए, हे स्वामी! वही कीजिए। मुझे अपना अनुचर (दास) जानिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1511.english_translation: Rama said, 'O sage, give up anger. My head is before your axe. Let your anger go as it will, lord. Know me as your servant.'
ramacharitamanas::1511.translation_literal: राम (Rama) / कहेउ (said) / रिस (anger) / तजिअ (give up) / मुनीसा (O sage) / कर (in hand) / कुठारु (axe) / आगें (before) / यह (this) / सीसा (head) / जेहिं (by which) / रिस (anger) / जाइ (goes) / करिअ (do) / सोइ (that) / स्वामी (lord/master) / मोहि (me) / जानिअ (know) / आपन (your own) / अनुगामी (follower/servant)
ramacharitamanas::1511.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1511.essence: True authority can offer itself before force.
ramacharitamanas::1511.simple_meaning: Rama asks the sage to drop his anger and do what he must, while placing himself completely in the sage's hands as a servant.
ramacharitamanas::1511.simple_insight: Real strength can kneel without losing dignity.
ramacharitamanas::1511.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, Parashurama stands furious with his axe raised after Lakshman’s sharp words. Rama steps forward calmly, offers his own head, and asks the sage to release his anger. The moment tests whether power will answer pride or restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1511.modern_relevance: Someone is ready to explode in a family argument, and you choose the harder move: lowering your voice, taking responsibility, and refusing to escalate the room.
ramacharitamanas::1511.insight: It teaches you to absorb hostility without mirroring it, turning confrontation into restraint.

ramacharitamanas::1512.verse_sanskrit: प्रभुहि सेवकहि समरु कस तजहु बिप्रबर रोसु। बेषु बिलोकें कहेसि कछु बालकहू नहिं दोसु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1512.verse_hindi: स्वामी और सेवक में युद्ध कैसा? हे ब्राह्मण श्रेष्ठ! क्रोध का त्याग कीजिए। आपका (वीरों का सा) वेष देखकर ही बालक ने कुछ कह डाला था, वास्तव में उसका भी कोई दोष नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1512.english_translation: What war can there be between a master and a servant? O best of brahmins, give up anger. Seeing your warrior-like appearance, the boy said something; he too is not at fault.
ramacharitamanas::1512.translation_literal: प्रभुहि (to the master) / सेवकहि (to the servant) / समरु (war) / कस (how) / तजहु (give up) / बिप्रबर (O best of brahmins) / रोसु (anger) / बेषु (appearance/attire) / बिलोकें (on seeing) / कहेसि (he said) / कछु (something) / बालकहू (the boy also) / नहिं (not) / दोसु (fault)
ramacharitamanas::1512.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1512.essence: Real authority does not need to turn anger into punishment.
ramacharitamanas::1512.simple_meaning: A master and servant should not treat each other as enemies. The boy reacted to the priest’s warrior-like appearance, so the priest should let go of anger.
ramacharitamanas::1512.simple_insight: It softens blame and restores dignity to both sides.
ramacharitamanas::1512.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Parashurama stands furious before Ram and Lakshman after the broken bow. Ram steps in to calm him, saying the boy only reacted to the priest’s fierce, warrior-like appearance. The moment turns conflict into restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1512.modern_relevance: A teacher snaps at a student for speaking too quickly, but the student was only reacting to the teacher’s harsh tone. This verse asks you to lower the temperature before you assign blame.
ramacharitamanas::1512.insight: It shifts the mind from punishment to understanding the cause of reaction.

ramacharitamanas::1513.verse_sanskrit: देखि कुठार बान धनु धारी। भै लरिकहि रिस बीरु बिचारी॥ नामु जान पै तुम्हहि न चीन्हा। बंस सुभायँ उतरु तेहिं दीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1513.verse_hindi: आपको कुठार, बाण और धनुष धारण किए देखकर और वीर समझकर बालक को क्रोध आ गया। वह आपका नाम तो जानता था, पर उसने आपको पहचाना नहीं। अपने वंश (रघुवंश) के स्वभाव के अनुसार उसने उत्तर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1513.english_translation: Seeing the axe, arrows, and bow in his hands, the boy grew angry, thinking him a warrior. He knew your name, but did not recognize you. According to the nature of his lineage, he gave that reply.
ramacharitamanas::1513.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / कुठार (axe) / बान (arrows) / धनु (bow) / धारी (holder) / भै (became) / लरिकहि (to the boy) / रिस (anger) / बीरु (warrior) / बिचारी (thinking) / नामु (name) / जान (knowing) / पै (but) / तुम्हहि (you) / न (not) / चीन्हा (recognized) / बंस (lineage) / सुभायँ (by nature) / उतरु (reply) / तेहिं (he) / दीन्हा (gave)
ramacharitamanas::1513.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1513.essence: Anger begins when appearance is mistaken for identity.
ramacharitamanas::1513.simple_meaning: The boy mistook the sage for a warrior because of his weapons and answered in anger. He knew the man's name, but not his identity.
ramacharitamanas::1513.simple_insight: First impressions can trigger conflict before understanding has a chance to enter.
ramacharitamanas::1513.detailed_meaning: Parashurama stands before the bow-breaking crowd, still armed and fierce. Young Lakshman sees the weapons, assumes warrior pride, and answers hotly. The verse explains the misunderstanding that deepens the tension before Ram's calm can soften it.
ramacharitamanas::1513.modern_relevance: You read a harsh text message and answer in the same tone. Later you learn the person was tired, not hostile. One wrong reading can turn a small moment into a fight.
ramacharitamanas::1513.insight: It shows how appearance can distort response, and how pride reacts before recognition.

ramacharitamanas::1514.verse_sanskrit: जौं तुम्ह औतेहु मुनि की नाईं। पद रज सिर सिसु धरत गोसाईं॥ छमहु चूक अनजानत केरी। चहिअ बिप्र उर कृपा घनेरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1514.verse_hindi: यदि आप मुनि की तरह आते, तो हे स्वामी! बालक आपके चरणों की धूलि सिर पर रखता। अनजाने की भूल को क्षमा कर दीजिए। ब्राह्मणों के हृदय में बहुत अधिक दया होनी चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1514.english_translation: If you had come like a sage, the child would have placed the dust of your feet on his head. Forgive the mistake made in ignorance. A Brahmin’s heart should hold abundant compassion.
ramacharitamanas::1514.translation_literal: जौं (if) / तुम्ह (you) / औतेहु (had come) / मुनि (sage) / की नाईं (like) / पद रज (dust of the feet) / सिर (head) / सिसु (child) / धरत (would place) / गोसाईं (lord) / छमहु (forgive) / चूक (mistake) / अनजानत (in ignorance) / केरी (of) / चहिअ (should be) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / उर (heart) / कृपा (compassion) / घनेरी (very abundant)
ramacharitamanas::1514.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1514.essence: Humility invites reverence; ignorance calls for mercy.
ramacharitamanas::1514.simple_meaning: The child says he would have shown respect if the visitor had come humbly. Since the mistake was made in ignorance, he asks for forgiveness and says a Brahmin should have great compassion.
ramacharitamanas::1514.simple_insight: Respect grows where humility meets mercy.
ramacharitamanas::1514.detailed_meaning: In the bow-breaking scene at Janakpur, Parashurama has arrived in anger after seeing Shiva’s bow broken. The child speaks gently but firmly: if the visitor had come like a sage, he would have bowed; since the mistake was unintentional, forgiveness and compassion are needed.
ramacharitamanas::1514.modern_relevance: Someone snaps at you in a meeting because they misunderstood your tone. The real test is whether you answer with pride or with mercy.
ramacharitamanas::1514.insight: It shifts the response from retaliation to dignified forgiveness, while still asking for respect.

ramacharitamanas::1515.verse_sanskrit: हमहि तुम्हहि सरिबरि कसि नाथा। कहहु न कहाँ चरन कहँ माथा॥ राम मात्र लघुनाम हमारा। परसु सहित बड़ नाम तोहारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1515.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! हमारी और आपकी बराबरी कैसी? कहिए न, कहाँ चरण और कहाँ मस्तक! कहाँ मेरा राम मात्र छोटा सा नाम और कहाँ आपका परशुसहित बड़ा नाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::1515.english_translation: O Lord, how can we compare ourselves? Tell me, where are your feet and where is my head? My Ram is only a small name; your name is great, with the axe.
ramacharitamanas::1515.translation_literal: हमहि (us) / तुम्हहि (you) / सरिबरि (equal) / कसि (how) / नाथा (O lord) / कहहु (say) / न (not) / कहाँ (where) / चरन (feet) / कहँ (where) / माथा (head) / राम (Ram) / मात्र (only) / लघु (small) / नामु (name) / हमारा (our) / परसु (axe) / सहित (with) / बड़ (great) / नाम (name) / तोहारा (your)
ramacharitamanas::1515.speaker: Parasurama
ramacharitamanas::1515.essence: Real greatness makes comparison feel foolish.
ramacharitamanas::1515.simple_meaning: Parasurama admits that he and Ram are not equal. He bows to Ram's feet and says his own name is only a small one beside Ram's greater name.
ramacharitamanas::1515.simple_insight: Pride loosens when someone sees a greater presence clearly.
ramacharitamanas::1515.detailed_meaning: After seeing Parasurama's anger, the child speaker answers with humility. He says there is no comparison between them: one is only a boy with a small name, the other is a mighty warrior with an axe. The exchange softens the tension before the next test of Ram's bow.
ramacharitamanas::1515.modern_relevance: You walk into a room ready to prove yourself, then meet someone whose presence makes boasting feel childish. The wiser move is to bow internally and speak cleanly.
ramacharitamanas::1515.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to reverence before strength and grace.

ramacharitamanas::1516.verse_sanskrit: देव एकु गुनु धनुष हमारें। नव गुन परम पुनीत तुम्हारें॥ सब प्रकार हम तुम्ह सन हारे। छमहु बिप्र अपराध हमारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1516.verse_hindi: हे देव! हमारे तो एक ही गुण धनुष है और आपके परम पवित्र (शम, दम, तप, शौच, क्षमा, सरलता, ज्ञान, विज्ञान और आस्तिकता ये) नौ गुण हैं। हम तो सब प्रकार से आपसे हारे हैं। हे विप्र! हमारे अपराधों को क्षमा कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1516.english_translation: O divine one, we have only one quality: the bow. Your qualities are nine and supremely pure. In every way, we have been defeated by you. O learned one, forgive our offense.
ramacharitamanas::1516.translation_literal: देव (divine one) / एकु (one) / गुनु (quality) / धनुष (bow) / हमारें (in our case) / नव (nine) / गुन (qualities) / परम (supreme) / पुनीत (pure) / तुम्हारें (yours) / सब (all) / प्रकार (ways) / हम (we) / तुम्ह सन (from you) / हारे (defeated) / छमहु (forgive) / बिप्र (learned one) / अपराध (offense) / हमारे (our)
ramacharitamanas::1516.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1516.essence: True strength can begin by admitting defeat.
ramacharitamanas::1516.simple_meaning: Ram admits defeat before Parashurama and asks forgiveness for any offense. He contrasts his single strength with the sage's many pure qualities.
ramacharitamanas::1516.simple_insight: Humility can be stronger than force. Bowing first often ends what pride would prolong.
ramacharitamanas::1516.detailed_meaning: In the Sita swayamvar, Ram has just broken Shiva's bow. Parashurama steps forward in anger, and Ram answers without pride. He lowers himself, praises the sage's virtues, and asks forgiveness before the confrontation can harden.
ramacharitamanas::1516.modern_relevance: A tense argument is about to explode in a family group chat. Instead of defending every word, you say, 'I may have missed something. Please forgive me.' The temperature drops instantly.
ramacharitamanas::1516.insight: It teaches you to defuse conflict with humility rather than ego-driven defense.

ramacharitamanas::1517.verse_sanskrit: बार बार मुनि बिप्रबर कहा राम सन राम। बोले भृगुपति सरुष हसि तहूँ बंधू सम बाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::1517.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने परशुरामजी को बार-बार 'मुनि' और 'विप्रवर' कहा। तब भृगुपति (परशुरामजी) कुपित होकर (अथवा क्रोध की हँसी हँसकर) बोले- तू भी अपने भाई के समान ही टेढ़ा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1517.english_translation: Ram kept calling Parashurama “sage” and “best of the learned.” Bhargupati then laughed in anger and said, “You are crooked like your brother.”
ramacharitamanas::1517.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / मुनि (sage) / बिप्रबर (best of the learned) / कहा (said) / राम सन (to Ram) / राम (Ram) / बोले (spoke) / भृगुपति (lord of Bhrigu) / सरुष (angrily) / हसि (laughing) / तहूँ (then) / बंधू (brother) / सम (like) / बाम (crooked)
ramacharitamanas::1517.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1517.essence: Courtesy can meet anger and still not stop it.
ramacharitamanas::1517.simple_meaning: Ram keeps addressing Parashurama respectfully, but Parashurama answers with angry mockery, accusing Ram of being crooked like his brother.
ramacharitamanas::1517.simple_insight: Respect does not always soften pride. Sometimes it only exposes how little the other side is willing to bend.
ramacharitamanas::1517.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, Ram has just broken Shiva’s bow and Parashurama has entered in fury. Ram keeps speaking gently and honorifically, trying to calm him. Instead, Parashurama turns sharp and insulting, setting up the confrontation that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1517.modern_relevance: You keep speaking calmly in a tense room, calling the other person with respect. They answer with sarcasm anyway, and the atmosphere hardens one degree more.
ramacharitamanas::1517.insight: It shows how one person’s humility can meet another person’s wounded pride without immediately resolving it.

ramacharitamanas::1518.verse_sanskrit: निपटहिं द्विज करि जानहि मोही। मैं जस बिप्र सुनावउँ तोही॥ चाप सुवा सर आहुति जानू। कोपु मोर अति घोर कृसानू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1518.verse_hindi: तू मुझे निरा ब्राह्मण ही समझता है? मैं जैसा विप्र हूँ, तुझे सुनाता हूँ। धनुष को सु्रवा, बाण को आहुति और मेरे क्रोध को अत्यन्त भयंकर अग्नि जान ॥
ramacharitamanas::1518.english_translation: Do you take me for an ordinary brahmin? I will show you what kind of brahmin I am. Take the bow as a parrot, the arrows as offerings, and my anger as a fierce fire.
ramacharitamanas::1518.translation_literal: निपटहिं (entirely/just) / द्विज (brahmin) / करि (as) / जानहि (you know) / मोही (me) / मैं (I) / जस (as) / बिप्र (brahmin) / सुनावउँ (I tell/show) / तोही (to you) / चाप (bow) / सुवा (parrot) / सर (arrows) / आहुति (offering) / जानू (know) / कोपु (anger) / मोर (my) / अति (very) / घोर (fierce) / कृसानू (fire)
ramacharitamanas::1518.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1518.essence: Pride turns even a priestly voice into a weapon.
ramacharitamanas::1518.simple_meaning: Parashurama warns Ram not to mistake him for a harmless priest. He says his bow is a parrot, his arrows are offerings, and his anger is a blazing fire.
ramacharitamanas::1518.simple_insight: Anger can turn ritual language into threat when pride takes over.
ramacharitamanas::1518.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, Ram has already broken Shiva's bow. Parashurama arrives furious, and the tension spikes into a clash of pride and power. This line is his warning before he tests Ram's restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1518.modern_relevance: A senior colleague smiles through clenched teeth after being corrected in public. The words sound polished, but the heat underneath is real. Pride can make even restraint feel like a weapon.
ramacharitamanas::1518.insight: It shows how wounded ego speaks in symbols of force, turning sacred language into intimidation.

ramacharitamanas::1519.verse_sanskrit: समिधि सेन चतुरंग सुहाई। महा महीप भए पसु आई॥ मैं एहिं परसु काटि बलि दीन्हे। समर जग्य जप कोटिन्ह कीन्हे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1519.verse_hindi: चतुरंगिणी सेना सुंदर समिधाएँ (यज्ञ में जलाई जाने वाली लकड़ियाँ) हैं। बड़े-बड़े राजा उसमें आकर बलि के पशु हुए हैं, जिनको मैंने इसी फरसे से काटकर बलि दिया है। ऐसे करोड़ों जपयुक्त रणयज्ञ मैंने किए हैं (अर्थात जैसे मंत्रोच्चारण पूर्वक 'स्वाहा' शब्द के साथ आहुति दी जाती है, उसी प्रकार मैंने पुकार-पुकार कर राजाओं की बलि दी है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1519.english_translation: The splendid fourfold army is my sacrificial fuel. Great kings have come into it like sacrificial animals. I have cut them down with this axe and offered them up. I have performed millions of battle-sacrifices.
ramacharitamanas::1519.translation_literal: समिधि (sacrificial fuel) / सेन (army) / चतुरंग (fourfold) / सुहाई (beautiful) / महा (great) / महीप (kings) / भए (became) / पसु (animals) / आई (coming) ॥ मैं (I) / एहिं (this) / परसु (axe) / काटि (cutting) / बलि (offering) / दीन्हे (gave) ॥ समर (battle) / जग्य (sacrifice) / जप (chanting) / कोटिन्ह (millions) / कीन्हे (made) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1519.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1519.essence: Violence feels holy when ego is the priest.
ramacharitamanas::1519.simple_meaning: Parashurama boasts that he has turned armies and kings into sacrificial offerings through battle, comparing war to ritual sacrifice.
ramacharitamanas::1519.simple_insight: Pride turns violence into a sacred story in the speaker’s mind.
ramacharitamanas::1519.detailed_meaning: Parashurama is confronting Ram after the bow is broken. Inflamed by insult, he describes his lifelong fury as if it were holy ritual: kings become offerings, war becomes sacrifice, and his axe becomes the priest’s tool. He is defending his power before the next challenge lands.
ramacharitamanas::1519.modern_relevance: Someone who always frames their anger as justified starts sounding noble to themselves. The story reveals how easily force can dress itself up as principle.
ramacharitamanas::1519.insight: It exposes how ego can sanctify aggression and mistake domination for righteousness.

ramacharitamanas::1520.verse_sanskrit: मोर प्रभाउ बिदित नहिं तोरें। बोलसि निदरि बिप्र के भोरें॥ भंजेउ चापु दापु बड़ बाढ़ा। अहमिति मनहुँ जीति जगु ठाढ़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1520.verse_hindi: मेरा प्रभाव तुझे मालूम नहीं है, इसी से तू ब्राह्मण के धोखे मेरा निरादर करके बोल रहा है। धनुष तोड़ डाला, इससे तेरा घमंड बहुत बढ़ गया है। ऐसा अहंकार है, मानो संसार को जीतकर खड़ा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1520.english_translation: My power is unknown to you, so you speak with disrespect, taking me for a mere Brahmin. You broke the bow, and that has swelled your pride greatly. Your arrogance stands there as if it has conquered the world.
ramacharitamanas::1520.translation_literal: मोर (my) / प्रभाउ (power) / बिदित (known) / नहिं (not) / तोरें (to you) / बोलसि (you speak) / निदरि (disrespectfully) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / के (of) / भोरें (mistakenly) / भंजेउ (broke) / चापु (the bow) / दापु (pride) / बड़ (great) / बाढ़ा (has increased) / अहमिति (ego) / मनहुँ (as if) / जीति (having conquered) / जगु (the world) / ठाढ़ा (standing)
ramacharitamanas::1520.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1520.essence: Pride after victory blinds the mind to its own excess.
ramacharitamanas::1520.simple_meaning: Parashurama says that the young man has become arrogant after breaking the bow and is now speaking carelessly, not knowing Parashurama's power.
ramacharitamanas::1520.simple_insight: Pride makes a person misread the room and speak beyond wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::1520.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the bow has been broken and Parashurama rises in fury. He sees the young prince's boldness as disrespect and reads the moment as swollen ego, not innocence. This verse shows the clash before Ram answers calmly.
ramacharitamanas::1520.modern_relevance: You finally win the argument in the group chat, then your tone turns sharp. The real danger is not victory — it is the pride that follows it.
ramacharitamanas::1520.insight: It exposes how achievement can inflate the sense of separate self and distort speech.

ramacharitamanas::1521.verse_sanskrit: राम कहा मुनि कहहु बिचारी। रिस अति बड़ि लघु चूक हमारी॥ छुअतहिं टूट पिनाक पुराना। मैं केहि हेतु करौं अभिमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1521.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने कहा- हे मुनि! विचारकर बोलिए। आपका क्रोध बहुत बड़ा है और मेरी भूल बहुत छोटी है। पुराना धनुष था, छूते ही टूट गया। मैं किस कारण अभिमान करूँ? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1521.english_translation: Ram said, “O sage, speak after reflection. Your anger is very great, and my fault is very small. The old bow broke as soon as it was touched. Why should I feel proud?”
ramacharitamanas::1521.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / कहा (said) / मुनि (sage) / कहहु (speak) / बिचारी (after reflection) / रिस (anger) / अति बड़ि (very great) / लघु (small) / चूक (fault) / हमारी (my) / छुअतहिं (on touching) / टूट (broke) / पिनाक (bow) / पुराना (old) / मैं (I) / केहि हेतु (for what reason) / करौं (should do) / अभिमाना (pride)
ramacharitamanas::1521.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1521.essence: Greatness needs no pride; it speaks with humility.
ramacharitamanas::1521.simple_meaning: Ram answers calmly after the bow breaks. He asks the sage to judge fairly, saying his own fault is small and there is no reason for pride.
ramacharitamanas::1521.simple_insight: Humility stays intact even in victory. Calm speech can dissolve conflict faster than force.
ramacharitamanas::1521.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the bow has just broken and the tension is rising. Ram does not boast. He tells the sage to think clearly, calls his mistake minor, and refuses pride over an old bow that broke on touch.
ramacharitamanas::1521.modern_relevance: You fix a problem in front of everyone, and the room waits for you to gloat. Instead, you lower your voice, name the mistake honestly, and let pride die there.
ramacharitamanas::1521.insight: It teaches you to answer success with restraint, not self-importance.

ramacharitamanas::1522.verse_sanskrit: जौं हम निदरहिं बिप्र बदि सत्य सुनहु भृगुनाथ। तौ अस को जग सुभटु जेहि भय बस नावहिं माथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1522.verse_hindi: हे भृगुनाथ! यदि हम सचमुच ब्राह्मण कहकर निरादर करते हैं, तो यह सत्य सुनिए, फिर संसार में ऐसा कौन योद्धा है, जिसे हम डरके मारे मस्तक नवाएँ? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1522.english_translation: O Lord of the Bhṛgu lineage, if we truly insult Brahmins, then tell us: which warrior in the world can make us bow in fear?
ramacharitamanas::1522.translation_literal: जौं (if) / हम (we) / निदरहिं (insult) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / बदि (calling) / सत्य (truth) / सुनहु (listen) / भृगुनाथ (O Lord of Bhṛgu) / तौ (then) / अस (such) / को (which) / जग (world) / सुभटु (warrior) / जेहि (whom) / भय (fear) / बस (under) / नावहिं (we bow) / माथ (head)
ramacharitamanas::1522.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1522.essence: Fear cannot command a heart grounded in truth.
ramacharitamanas::1522.simple_meaning: Ram says that if he truly treated Brahmins with contempt, then no warrior in the world could make him bow out of fear.
ramacharitamanas::1522.simple_insight: Real strength does not need to prove itself through intimidation.
ramacharitamanas::1522.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Ram has just broken Shiva's bow. Parashurama arrives furious, testing Ram's composure and worth. Ram answers without fear, saying that if he were truly disrespectful, no warrior anywhere could frighten him into bowing.
ramacharitamanas::1522.modern_relevance: Someone challenges you in front of a room, trying to make you shrink. You answer calmly, not to win applause, but because fear no longer gets to steer your posture.
ramacharitamanas::1522.insight: It shifts the mind from defensive posturing to steady self-possession under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::1523.verse_sanskrit: देव दनुज भूपति भट नाना। समबल अधिक होउ बलवाना॥ जौं रन हमहि पचारै कोऊ। लरहिं सुखेन कालु किन होऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1523.verse_hindi: देवता, दैत्य, राजा या और बहुत से योद्धा, वे चाहे बल में हमारे बराबर हों चाहे अधिक बलवान हों, यदि रण में हमें कोई भी ललकारे तो हम उससे सुखपूर्वक लड़ेंगे, चाहे काल ही क्यों न हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1523.english_translation: Devas, demons, kings, and many warriors: whether they are equal to us in strength or stronger, if anyone challenges us in battle, we will fight with ease, even if Death itself comes.
ramacharitamanas::1523.translation_literal: देव (devas) / दनुज (demons) / भूपति (kings) / भट (warriors) / नाना (many) / समबल (equal in strength) / अधिक (greater) / होउ (be) / बलवाना (strong) / जौं (if) / रन (battle) / हमहि (us) / पचारै (challenges) / कोऊ (someone) / लरहिं (we fight) / सुखेन (easily) / कालु (Death) / किन (even if not) / होऊ (be)
ramacharitamanas::1523.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1523.essence: Strength is proven by calmness before a stronger challenger.
ramacharitamanas::1523.simple_meaning: Ram says that a true warrior does not fear any opponent. He will face challengers calmly, even if they are stronger or seem as unstoppable as death.
ramacharitamanas::1523.simple_insight: Courage becomes simple when fear of loss no longer rules the mind.
ramacharitamanas::1523.detailed_meaning: In the bow-breaking contest at Janakpur, Parashurama is confronting Ram after the broken pinak. Ram answers without flinching, saying that devas, demons, kings, and warriors may be equal or greater in strength, yet he will meet any challenger calmly, even death itself.
ramacharitamanas::1523.modern_relevance: You’re cornered in a tense meeting, and the other person is louder, older, and clearly trying to intimidate you. Ram’s answer is the opposite of panic: meet challenge steadily, without shrinking.
ramacharitamanas::1523.insight: It shifts the mind from intimidation to fearless readiness.

ramacharitamanas::1524.verse_sanskrit: छत्रिय तनु धरि समर सकाना। कुल कलंकु तेहिं पावँर आना॥ कहउँ सुभाउ न कुलहि प्रसंसी। कालहु डरहिं न रन रघुबंसी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1524.verse_hindi: क्षत्रिय का शरीर धरकर जो युद्ध में डर गया, उस नीच ने अपने कुल पर कलंक लगा दिया। मैं स्वभाव से ही कहता हूँ, कुल की प्रशंसा करके नहीं, कि रघुवंशी रण में काल से भी नहीं डरते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1524.english_translation: One who takes a warrior's body and then fears battle brings shame on the line. I speak from nature, not praise: the descendants of Raghu do not fear death in war.
ramacharitamanas::1524.translation_literal: छत्रिय (warrior) / तनु (body) / धरि (having taken) / समर (battle) / सकाना (became afraid) / कुल (lineage) / कलंकु (shame) / तेहिं (that one) / पावँर (base) / आना (brought) / कहउँ (I speak) / सुभाउ (nature) / न (not) / कुलहि (the lineage) / प्रसंसी (in praise) / कालहु (even death) / डरहिं (fear) / न (not) / रन (battle) / रघुबंसी (descendants of Raghu)
ramacharitamanas::1524.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::1524.essence: A warrior dishonours his line by fearing the fight.
ramacharitamanas::1524.simple_meaning: A warrior who runs from battle dishonours his own lineage. Raghu's descendants are naturally fearless in war, even before death.
ramacharitamanas::1524.simple_insight: Courage is not decoration. It is the standard that protects a person's name and role.
ramacharitamanas::1524.detailed_meaning: Ravana is speaking in the middle of the Lanka war, trying to shame an opponent by measuring courage against lineage. He says a warrior who fears battle stains his own house, while Raghu's line is known for fearlessness. The verse sharpens the insult before the next reply.
ramacharitamanas::1524.modern_relevance: You back out at the last minute from the hard conversation you promised to have. The issue is bigger than discomfort now — your name, role, and word are all on the line.
ramacharitamanas::1524.insight: It pushes action toward bravery under pressure, not self-protection when stakes rise.

ramacharitamanas::1525.verse_sanskrit: बिप्रबंस कै असि प्रभुताई। अभय होइ जो तुम्हहि डेराई॥ सुनि मृदु गूढ़ बचन रघुपत के। उघरे पटल परसुधर मति के ॥
ramacharitamanas::1525.verse_hindi: ब्राह्मणवंश की ऐसी ही प्रभुता (महिमा) है कि जो आपसे डरता है, वह सबसे निर्भय हो जाता है (अथवा जो भयरहित होता है, वह भी आपसे डरता है) श्री रघुनाथजी के कोमल और रहस्यपूर्ण वचन सुनकर परशुरामजी की बुद्धि के परदे खुल गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1525.english_translation: Such is the majesty of a Brahmin line: whoever fears you becomes fearless. Hearing the gentle, hidden words of Raghupati, the veils over Parashurama's mind were lifted.
ramacharitamanas::1525.translation_literal: बिप्रबंस (Brahmin line) / कै (of) / असि (such) / प्रभुताई (majesty, lordship) / अभय (fearless) / होइ (becomes) / जो (whoever) / तुम्हहि (you) / डेराई (fears)॥ / सुनि (hearing) / मृदु (gentle) / गूढ़ (hidden, profound) / बचन (words) / रघुपत (of Raghupati) / के (of) / उघरे (opened) / पटल (veils) / परसुधर (Parashurama) / मति (mind, understanding) / के (of) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1525.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1525.essence: Gentle truth can dissolve even a hardened mind.
ramacharitamanas::1525.simple_meaning: Ram's gentle but hidden words break through Parashurama's pride and confusion. The fear that once ruled the moment turns into clarity.
ramacharitamanas::1525.simple_insight: A calm, truthful word can dissolve hardness faster than force.
ramacharitamanas::1525.detailed_meaning: Parashurama has come to challenge Ram after the breaking of Shiva's bow. Ram answers without aggression, and his soft, layered speech cuts through Parashurama's forceful mind. In that instant, Parashurama sees clearly and his anger loosens.
ramacharitamanas::1525.modern_relevance: Someone sends you a sharp text, and you almost fire back. Then one careful, honest reply changes the whole tone. Not louder force — clearer speech — ends the spiral.
ramacharitamanas::1525.insight: It shifts the response from confrontation to lucid speech that reveals rather than attacks.

ramacharitamanas::1526.verse_sanskrit: राम रमापति कर धनु लेहू। खैंचहु मिटै मोर संदेहू॥ देत चापु आपुहिं चलि गयऊ। परसुराम मन बिसमय भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1526.verse_hindi: (परशुरामजी ने कहा-) हे राम! हे लक्ष्मीपति! धनुष को हाथ में (अथवा लक्ष्मीपति विष्णु का धनुष) लीजिए और इसे खींचिए, जिससे मेरा संदेह मिट जाए। परशुरामजी धनुष देने लगे, तब वह आप ही चला गया। तब परशुरामजी के मन में बड़ा आश्चर्य हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1526.english_translation: Parashurama said, "Ram, lord of Lakshmi, take this bow in your hand and draw it, so my doubt will be removed." As he handed over the bow, it moved by itself. Parashurama was filled with wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1526.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / रमापति (lord of Lakshmi) / कर (hand) / धनु (bow) / लेहू (take) / खैंचहु (draw) / मिटै (may be removed) / मोर (my) / संदेहू (doubt) / देत (giving) / चापु (the bow) / आपुहिं (by itself) / चलि गयऊ (moved away) / परसुराम (Parashurama) / मन (mind) / बिसमय (wonder) / भयऊ (became)
ramacharitamanas::1526.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1526.essence: True power needs no strain to reveal itself.
ramacharitamanas::1526.simple_meaning: Parashurama asks Ram to lift and draw the bow so his doubt will be cleared. When the bow moves easily, he is astonished and realizes Ram's extraordinary power.
ramacharitamanas::1526.simple_insight: Real recognition begins when pride gives way to wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1526.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, Parashurama has just challenged Ram after the bow-breaking contest. He asks Ram to lift the bow again, and the bow yields effortlessly. This moment breaks Parashurama's suspicion and prepares him to see Ram's true stature.
ramacharitamanas::1526.modern_relevance: You keep insisting you need proof, then someone does the hard thing without strain. The argument stops. Your certainty gives way to awe.
ramacharitamanas::1526.insight: It shifts the mind from testing power to recognizing it.

ramacharitamanas::1527.verse_sanskrit: जाना राम प्रभाउ तब पुलक प्रफुल्लित गात। जोरि पानि बोले बचन हृदयँ न प्रेमु अमात ॥
ramacharitamanas::1527.verse_hindi: तब उन्होंने श्री रामजी का प्रभाव जाना, (जिसके कारण) उनका शरीर पुलकित और प्रफुल्लित हो गया। वे हाथ जोड़कर वचन बोले- प्रेम उनके हृदय में समाता न था- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1527.english_translation: Then he understood Ram's power. His body thrilled with joy, and with folded hands he spoke, his heart overflowing with love.
ramacharitamanas::1527.translation_literal: जाना (understood) / राम (Ram) / प्रभाउ (power, influence) / तब (then) / पुलक (thrilled) / प्रफुल्लित (blossoming, joyful) / गात (body) / जोरि (joining) / पानि (hands) / बोले (spoke) / बचन (words) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / न (not) / प्रेमु (love) / अमात (did not fit, was overflowing)
ramacharitamanas::1527.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1527.essence: Seeing Ram rightly turns force into reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1527.simple_meaning: Parashurama finally recognizes Ram's power. That recognition fills him with joy, and he bows with folded hands because his heart overflows with love.
ramacharitamanas::1527.simple_insight: Real recognition softens pride. When the heart sees greatness clearly, reverence rises on its own.
ramacharitamanas::1527.detailed_meaning: After seeing Ram lift and break Shiva's bow, Parashurama's anger dissolves into awe. He understands who stands before him, his body shivers with delight, and he speaks with folded hands. The moment turns confrontation into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1527.modern_relevance: You meet someone you had judged too quickly, and one honest moment changes everything. The tension leaves your body before your words do.
ramacharitamanas::1527.insight: It shifts the mind from testing others to recognising their true stature and responding with respect.

ramacharitamanas::1528.verse_sanskrit: जय रघुबंस बनज बन भानू। गहन दनुज कुल दहन कृसानू॥ जय सुर बिप्र धेनु हितकारी। जय मद मोह कोह भ्रम हारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1528.verse_hindi: हे रघुकुल रूपी कमल वन के सूर्य! हे राक्षसों के कुल रूपी घने जंगल को जलाने वाले अग्नि! आपकी जय हो! हे देवता, ब्राह्मण और गो का हित करने वाले! आपकी जय हो। हे मद, मोह, क्रोध और भ्रम के हरने वाले! आपकी जय हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1528.english_translation: Victory to the sun of the Raghu clan’s lotus-grove, the fire that burns the dense forest of demon clans. Victory to the benefactor of the radiant beings, the learned, and the cows. Victory to the remover of pride, delusion, anger, and confusion.
ramacharitamanas::1528.translation_literal: जय (victory) / रघुबंस (Raghu clan) / बनज (lotus) / बन (forest) / भानू (sun) / गहन (dense) / दनुज (demon) / कुल (clan) / दहन (burning) / कृसानू (fire) / जय (victory) / सुर (radiant beings) / बिप्र (learned ones) / धेनु (cow) / हितकारी (benefactor) / जय (victory) / मद (pride) / मोह (delusion) / कोह (anger) / भ्रम (confusion) / हारी (remover)
ramacharitamanas::1528.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1528.essence: Ram burns away what distorts the mind and protects what is worth keeping.
ramacharitamanas::1528.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the light of Raghu’s line, the destroyer of evil, and the remover of pride, confusion, and anger. He protects the good and blesses all who live rightly.
ramacharitamanas::1528.simple_insight: Praise can steady the mind by placing strength, protection, and clarity outside the ego.
