ramacharitamanas::1528.detailed_meaning: After Parashuram’s anger softens and Ram’s greatness is recognized, the praise rises naturally from the scene. Tulsidas hails Ram as the light of Raghu’s line, the force that burns down evil, and the one who protects the worthy and clears away inner poison.
ramacharitamanas::1528.modern_relevance: After a tense family argument, someone finally speaks the name of what is good instead of feeding the fight. The room changes. Praise for what is steady and clear can cut through heat faster than argument.
ramacharitamanas::1528.insight: It shifts attention from conflict to the qualities that dissolve conflict: clarity, restraint, and protection of the good.

ramacharitamanas::1529.verse_sanskrit: बिनय सील करुना गुन सागर। जयति बचन रचना अति नागर॥ सेवक सुखद सुभग सब अंगा। जय सरीर छबि कोटि अनंगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1529.verse_hindi: हे विनय, शील, कृपा आदि गुणों के समुद्र और वचनों की रचना में अत्यन्त चतुर! आपकी जय हो। हे सेवकों को सुख देने वाले, सब अंगों से सुंदर और शरीर में करोड़ों कामदेवों की छबि धारण करने वाले! आपकी जय हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1529.english_translation: You are an ocean of humility, virtue, and compassion, and masterful in speech. You delight your devotees, beautiful in every limb, with the radiance of countless love-gods.
ramacharitamanas::1529.translation_literal: बिनय (humility) / सील (virtue) / करुना (compassion) / गुन (qualities) / सागर (ocean) / जयति (victorious) / बचन (speech) / रचना (composition) / अति (very) / नागर (skilled) / सेवक (devotees/servants) / सुखद (giver of joy) / सुभग (beautiful/auspicious) / सब (all) / अंगा (limbs) / जय (victory) / सरीर (body) / छबि (beauty/radiance) / कोटि (crores/millions) / अनंगा (love-gods)
ramacharitamanas::1529.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1529.essence: True greatness shines as humility, grace, and delight for others.
ramacharitamanas::1529.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as full of humility, goodness, compassion, and graceful speech. His beauty and presence bring joy to devotees.
ramacharitamanas::1529.simple_insight: There is comfort in meeting power that is gentle, beautiful, and kind.
ramacharitamanas::1529.detailed_meaning: At the Sita-swayamvar, the praise continues after the crowd has recognised Ram's greatness. Tulsidas now turns from strength to tenderness, calling Ram an ocean of humility, virtue, compassion, and beauty — the kind of greatness that serves others.
ramacharitamanas::1529.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose talent never turns sharp, whose words calm a room, and whose presence makes others feel included. That rare combination feels almost unreal.
ramacharitamanas::1529.insight: It shifts admiration away from raw power toward character that blesses others.

ramacharitamanas::1530.verse_sanskrit: करौं काह मुख एक प्रसंसा। जय महेस मन मानस हंसा॥ अनुचित बहुत कहेउँ अग्याता। छमहु छमा मंदिर दोउ भ्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1530.verse_hindi: मैं एक मुख से आपकी क्या प्रशंसा करूँ? हे महादेवजी के मन रूपी मानसरोवर के हंस! आपकी जय हो। मैंने अनजाने में आपको बहुत से अनुचित वचन कहे। हे क्षमा के मंदिर दोनों भाई! मुझे क्षमा कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1530.english_translation: How can I praise you with one mouth? Victory to Mahesh, the swan on the lake of his own mind. I have spoken many improper words in ignorance. Forgive me, both brothers, temples of forgiveness.
ramacharitamanas::1530.translation_literal: करौं (shall I do) / काह (what) / मुख (mouth) / एक (one) / प्रसंसा (praise) / जय (victory) / महेस (Mahesh/Shiva) / मन (mind) / मानस (lake) / हंसा (swan) / अनुचित (improper) / बहुत (many) / कहेउँ (I said) / अग्याता (in ignorance) / छमहु (forgive) / छमा (forgiveness) / मंदिर (temple) / दोउ (both) / भ्राता (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::1530.speaker: Parashurama
ramacharitamanas::1530.essence: Pride ends when a person asks forgiveness.
ramacharitamanas::1530.simple_meaning: Parashurama admits he has spoken wrongly and asks Ram and Lakshman for forgiveness. He also offers praise to Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::1530.simple_insight: Even a fierce mind can bow down. Humility turns conflict into reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1530.detailed_meaning: After the tense exchange with Ram, Parashurama’s anger collapses into shame and respect. He praises Shiva, admits his mistake, and asks forgiveness from the two brothers, showing that even pride can soften before grace.
ramacharitamanas::1530.modern_relevance: After a heated argument, you replay your sharp words and feel the sting. The real strength is not winning the exchange — it is returning, admitting fault, and asking to be forgiven.
ramacharitamanas::1530.insight: It shifts the mind from self-justification to humble repair.

ramacharitamanas::1531.verse_sanskrit: कहि जय जय जय रघुकुलकेतू। भृगुपति गए बनहि तप हेतू॥ अपभयँ कुटिल महीप डेराने। जहँ तहँ कायर गवँहिं पराने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1531.verse_hindi: हे रघुकुल के पताका स्वरूप श्री रामचन्द्रजी! आपकी जय हो, जय हो, जय हो। ऐसा कहकर परशुरामजी तप के लिए वन को चले गए। (यह देखकर) दुष्ट राजा लोग बिना ही कारण के (मनः कल्पित) डर से (रामचन्द्रजी से तो परशुरामजी भी हार गए, हमने इनका अपमान किया था, अब कहीं ये उसका बदला न लें, इस व्यर्थ के डर से डर गए) वे कायर चुपके से जहाँ-तहाँ भाग गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1531.english_translation: Saying, “Victory, victory, victory to the banner of the Raghu clan,” Parashurama went to the forest for austerity. Frightened by false fear, crooked kings ran away in every direction.
ramacharitamanas::1531.translation_literal: कहि (saying) / जय जय जय (victory, victory, victory) / रघुकुलकेतू (banner of the Raghu clan) / भृगुपति (lord of the Bhrigu line, Parashurama) / गए (went) / बनहि (to the forest) / तप हेतू (for austerity) / अपभयँ (through false fear) / कुटिल (crooked) / महीप (kings) / डेराने (were frightened) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / कायर (cowardly) / गवँहिं (went away) / पराने (fled)
ramacharitamanas::1531.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1531.simple_meaning: Parashurama praises Ram, then leaves for the forest to continue his austerity. The sight frightens weak kings, who flee in panic.
ramacharitamanas::1531.simple_insight: Fear spreads fast when pride is already guilty.
ramacharitamanas::1531.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, Parashurama has just faced Ram and backed down. He now blesses Ram, turns away, and returns to the forest for austerity. The petty kings watching are shaken by their own shame and run off in fear.
ramacharitamanas::1531.modern_relevance: You watch someone handle a tense room with complete calm, and your own bluster collapses. The loudest people often flee first when real steadiness appears.
ramacharitamanas::1531.insight: It shifts attention from public bravado to the fear hidden beneath it.

ramacharitamanas::1532.verse_sanskrit: देवन्ह दीन्हीं दुंदुभीं प्रभु पर बरषहिं फूल। हरषे पुर नर नारि सब मिटी मोहमय सूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1532.verse_hindi: देवताओं ने नगाड़े बजाए, वे प्रभु के ऊपर फूल बरसाने लगे। जनकपुर के स्त्री-पुरुष सब हर्षित हो गए। उनका मोहमय (अज्ञान से उत्पन्न) शूल मिट गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1532.english_translation: The radiant beings beat drums and showered flowers on the Lord. All the men and women of the city rejoiced; the thorn of delusion vanished.
ramacharitamanas::1532.translation_literal: देवन्ह (the radiant beings) / दीन्हीं (gave) / दुंदुभीं (drums) / प्रभु (Lord) / पर (on) / बरषहिं (shower) / फूल (flowers) / हरषे (rejoiced) / पुर (city) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / सब (all) / मिटी (was removed) / मोहमय (full of delusion) / सूल (thorn)
ramacharitamanas::1532.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1532.essence: Joy around Ram dissolves the thorn of delusion.
ramacharitamanas::1532.simple_meaning: The divine beings celebrated Ram with drums and flowers, and the people of the city felt deep joy. Their confusion and sorrow disappeared.
ramacharitamanas::1532.simple_insight: Joy can arrive so fully that confusion loses its grip.
ramacharitamanas::1532.detailed_meaning: After Parashurama has left, the scene in Janakpur opens into celebration. The radiant beings beat drums and shower flowers on Ram, and the whole city — men and women alike — feels the relief of a burden lifted.
ramacharitamanas::1532.modern_relevance: The room goes quiet after the hard conversation ends, and then everyone exhales at once. The tension you were carrying was real, but it was never permanent.
ramacharitamanas::1532.insight: It shifts attention from conflict to release, showing how a shared moment of grace can dissolve mental heaviness.

ramacharitamanas::1533.verse_sanskrit: अति गहगहे बाजने बाजे। सबहिं मनोहर मंगल साजे॥ जूथ जूथ मिलि सुमुखि सुनयनीं। करहिं गान कल कोकिलबयनीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1533.verse_hindi: खूब जोर से बाजे बजने लगे। सभी ने मनोहर मंगल साज साजे। सुंदर मुख और सुंदर नेत्रों वाली तथा कोयल के समान मधुर बोलने वाली स्त्रियाँ झुंड की झुंड मिलकर सुंदरगान करने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1533.english_translation: The drums thundered loudly. All the beautiful wedding arrangements were made. Women with lovely faces and sweet voices sang in joyful groups.
ramacharitamanas::1533.translation_literal: अति (very much) / गहगहे (thundering loudly) / बाजने (instruments) / बाजे (were played) / सबहिं (all) / मनोहर (beautiful) / मंगल (auspicious) / साजे (arrangements) / जूथ जूथ (group by group) / मिलि (together) / सुमुखि (lovely-faced) / सुनयनीं (beautiful-eyed women) / करहिं (do) / गान (singing) / कल (sweet) / कोकिलबयनीं (with cuckoo-like voices)
ramacharitamanas::1533.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1533.essence: Celebration fills the whole world when joy finally arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1533.simple_meaning: The wedding scene bursts into music, decoration, and joyful singing by the women gathered there.
ramacharitamanas::1533.simple_insight: Joy becomes communal when celebration fills the whole space.
ramacharitamanas::1533.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur after the tension of the bow contest, the wedding atmosphere breaks open into sound and color. Drums thunder, auspicious decorations appear, and groups of women sing sweetly. It is a pure scene of celebration, not a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::1533.modern_relevance: A wedding hall suddenly wakes up when the music starts, the lights warm the room, and the relatives begin to sing together. The moment belongs to shared joy, not to explanation.
ramacharitamanas::1533.insight: It shifts attention from the individual event to the collective happiness it creates.

ramacharitamanas::1534.verse_sanskrit: सुखु बिदेह कर बरनि न जाई। जन्मदरिद्र मनहुँ निधि पाई॥ बिगत त्रास भइ सीय सुखारी। जनु बिधु उदयँ चकोरकुमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1534.verse_hindi: जनकजी के सुख का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता, मानो जन्म का दरिद्री धन का खजाना पा गया हो! सीताजी का भय जाता रहा, वे ऐसी सुखी हुईं जैसे चन्द्रमा के उदय होने से चकोर की कन्या सुखी होती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1534.english_translation: Janak's joy cannot be described, as if a born pauper had found a treasury. Sita's fear vanished; she became happy like a female chakor at the moon's rise.
ramacharitamanas::1534.translation_literal: सुखु (joy) / बिदेह (of Janak) / कर (of) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाई (can be done) / जन्मदरिद्र (born poor) / मनहुँ (as if) / निधि (treasure) / पाई (having found) / बिगत (gone) / त्रास (fear) / भइ (became) / सीय (Sita) / सुखारी (happy) / जनु (like) / बिधु (moon) / उदयँ (at rising) / चकोरकुमारी (female chakor)
ramacharitamanas::1534.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1534.essence: Relief can feel like finding a treasure you never expected.
ramacharitamanas::1534.simple_meaning: Janak is overwhelmed with joy, like a poor person suddenly finding treasure. Sita's fear disappears, and her happiness blooms at the sight of the rising moon.
ramacharitamanas::1534.simple_insight: Joy can arrive so fully that words fail, and fear can dissolve in a single moment of relief.
ramacharitamanas::1534.detailed_meaning: Janak's court is still alive with celebration after the sacred victory. In that charged moment, Tulsidas pauses to show two hearts at once: the king's overflowing joy and Sita's sudden release from fear. The scene prepares for the next step in the wedding story.
ramacharitamanas::1534.modern_relevance: You wait outside a hospital room, then hear the doctor say the test is clear. The fear drops away so fast it feels unreal, and relief becomes its own kind of celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1534.insight: It shifts attention from event to emotional release: the real miracle is fear ending and joy taking over.

ramacharitamanas::1535.verse_sanskrit: जनक कीन्ह कौसिकहि प्रनामा। प्रभु प्रसाद धनु भंजेउ रामा॥ मोहि कृतकृत्य कीन्ह दुहुँ भाईं। अब जो उचित सो कहिअ गोसाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1535.verse_hindi: जनकजी ने विश्वामित्रजी को प्रणाम किया (और कहा-) प्रभु ही की कृपा से श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने धनुष तोड़ा है। दोनों भाइयों ने मुझे कृतार्थ कर दिया। हे स्वामी! अब जो उचित हो सो कहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1535.english_translation: Janaka bowed to Vishvamitra and said, “By the Lord’s grace, Rama has broken the bow. Both brothers have fulfilled my purpose. Now, my lord, please say what is proper.”
ramacharitamanas::1535.translation_literal: जनक (Janaka) / कीन्ह (did) / कौसिकहि (to Vishvamitra) / प्रनामा (salutation) / प्रभु (lord) / प्रसाद (grace) / धनु (bow) / भंजेउ (broke) / रामा (Rama) / मोहि (me) / कृतकृत्य (fulfilled) / कीन्ह (made) / दुहुँ (both) / भाईं (brothers) / अब (now) / जो (what) / उचित (proper) / सो (that) / कहिअ (say) / गोसाईं (my lord)
ramacharitamanas::1535.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1535.essence: Grace has done the impossible; now only the proper next step remains.
ramacharitamanas::1535.simple_meaning: Janaka thanks Vishvamitra and credits Rama’s success to divine grace. He feels fully fulfilled and asks what should happen next.
ramacharitamanas::1535.simple_insight: Fulfillment comes before the next step. When a heart is satisfied, it can ask wisely.
ramacharitamanas::1535.detailed_meaning: At Janaka’s court in Mithila, Rama has just broken Shiva’s bow. Janaka bows to Vishvamitra, overwhelmed with relief and gratitude. The impossible condition for Sita’s marriage has been met, and now he asks what is proper to do next.
ramacharitamanas::1535.modern_relevance: You finish the hardest part of a project and feel the room exhale. Before rushing ahead, you pause, grateful that the crucial thing is already done.
ramacharitamanas::1535.insight: It shifts attention from strain to completion, then from completion to the right next action.

ramacharitamanas::1536.verse_sanskrit: कह मुनि सुनु नरनाथ प्रबीना। रहा बिबाहु चाप आधीना॥ टूटतहीं धनु भयउ बिबाहू। सुर नर नाग बिदित सब काहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1536.verse_hindi: मुनि ने कहा- हे चतुर नरेश ! सुनो यों तो विवाह धनुष के अधीन था, धनुष के टूटते ही विवाह हो गया। देवता, मनुष्य और नाग सब किसी को यह मालूम है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1536.english_translation: The sage said, “Listen, wise king. The wedding depended on the bow. The moment the bow broke, the marriage was accomplished. All the gods, humans, and serpents know this.”
ramacharitamanas::1536.translation_literal: कह (said) / मुनि (sage) / सुनु (listen) / नरनाथ (king) / प्रबीना (wise) / रहा (was) / बिबाहु (marriage) / चाप (bow) / आधीना (dependent) / टूटतहीं (the very moment breaking) / धनु (bow) / भयउ (became) / बिबाहू (the marriage) / सुर (gods) / नर (humans) / नाग (serpents) / बिदित (known) / सब (all) / काहू (to whom)
ramacharitamanas::1536.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1536.essence: The marriage is settled the moment the bow breaks.
ramacharitamanas::1536.simple_meaning: The sage explains that Sita’s marriage was tied to the bow: once Ram broke it, the wedding was settled, and everyone knew it.
ramacharitamanas::1536.simple_insight: Some moments are already decided by the act itself; after that, the rest is only formal.
ramacharitamanas::1536.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s court, after Ram has broken Shiva’s bow, the sage turns to the wise king and clarifies the situation. The marriage is no longer in doubt; the bow’s breaking has already sealed it, and the whole world knows the result.
ramacharitamanas::1536.modern_relevance: You sign the contract, and the room changes. The negotiation is over; now everyone is just completing the paperwork.
ramacharitamanas::1536.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to decisive action: one fulfilled condition can settle an entire future.

ramacharitamanas::1537.verse_sanskrit: तदपि जाइ तुम्ह करहु अब जथा बंस ब्यवहारु। बूझि बिप्र कुलबृद्ध गुर बेद बिदित आचारु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1537.verse_hindi: तथापि तुम जाकर अपने कुल का जैसा व्यवहार हो, ब्राह्मणों, कुल के बूढ़ों और गुरुओं से पूछकर और वेदों में वर्णित जैसा आचार हो वैसा करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1537.english_translation: Still, go and do what is proper for your family line. Ask the learned Brahmins, the elders of your clan, the guru, and the conduct laid down in the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::1537.translation_literal: तदपि (still / nevertheless) / जाइ (go) / तुम्ह (you) / करहु (do) / अब (now) / जथा (as) / बंस (family line) / ब्यवहारु (custom / conduct) / बूझि (asking / inquiring) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / कुलबृद्ध (elders of the clan) / गुर (guru) / बेद (Veda) / बिदित (known) / आचारु (conduct / practice)
ramacharitamanas::1537.speaker: Janaka
ramacharitamanas::1537.essence: Right action begins with consulting wisdom older than your impulse.
ramacharitamanas::1537.simple_meaning: Janaka tells them to act according to family custom, after consulting learned Brahmins, elders, the guru, and the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::1537.simple_insight: Good action is not impulsive. It is checked against wisdom, tradition, and right conduct.
ramacharitamanas::1537.detailed_meaning: After Ram breaks Shiva's bow, Janaka does not rush. He tells the assembly to proceed according to family custom, guided by Brahmins, elders, the guru, and Vedic conduct. The marriage moment is too important for haste.
ramacharitamanas::1537.modern_relevance: You are about to make a huge family decision and everyone is emotional. Instead of reacting, you pause, ask the elders, and choose what is proper, not merely what is exciting.
ramacharitamanas::1537.insight: It shifts action from impulse to disciplined consultation with wise authority.

ramacharitamanas::1538.verse_sanskrit: दूत अवधपुर पठवहु जाई। आनहिं नृप दसरथहिं बोलाई॥ मुदित राउ कहि भलेहिं कृपाला। पठए दूत बोलि तेहि काला ॥
ramacharitamanas::1538.verse_hindi: जाकर अयोध्या को दूत भेजो, जो राजा दशरथ को बुला लावें। राजा ने प्रसन्न होकर कहा- हे कृपालु! बहुत अच्छा! और उसी समय दूतों को बुलाकर भेज दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1538.english_translation: Send messengers to Ayodhya and invite King Dasharath here. The king gladly said, 'Very well, gracious one,' and immediately sent the messengers.
ramacharitamanas::1538.translation_literal: दूत (messengers) / अवधपुर (to Ayodhya city) / पठवहु (send) / जाई (going) / आनहिं (bring) / नृप (king) / दसरथहिं (Dasharath) / बोलाई (calling) / मुदित (pleased) / राउ (king) / कहि (saying) / भलेहिं (well) / कृपाला (gracious one) / पठए (sent) / दूत (messengers) / बोलि (calling) / तेहि काला (at that time)
ramacharitamanas::1538.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1538.essence: Right action begins with respectful invitation and timely response.
ramacharitamanas::1538.simple_meaning: Messengers are sent to Ayodhya to bring King Dasharath. The king agrees happily and sends them at once.
ramacharitamanas::1538.simple_insight: Some moments move forward because everyone involved is ready to honor the right order.
ramacharitamanas::1538.detailed_meaning: After the bow is broken and the marriage is secured, the next step is formal and royal. The sage advises sending messengers to Ayodhya for Dasharath. The king agrees joyfully and dispatches them at once.
ramacharitamanas::1538.modern_relevance: A family wedding is finally settled, and now someone has to make the respectful calls, invite the elders, and do things properly. The celebration begins with honor, not haste.
ramacharitamanas::1538.insight: It shows how sacred moments still need proper social order, timing, and consent.

ramacharitamanas::1539.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि महाजन सकल बोलाए। आइ सबन्हि सादर सिर नाए॥ हाट बाट मंदिर सुरबासा। नगरु सँवारहु चारिहुँ पासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1539.verse_hindi: फिर सब महाजनों को बुलाया और सबने आकर राजा को आदरपूर्वक सिर नवाया। (राजा ने कहा-) बाजार, रास्ते, घर, देवालय और सारे नगर को चारों ओर से सजाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1539.english_translation: Then he called all the great merchants. They came and bowed their heads respectfully. "Decorate the markets, roads, temples, and the whole city on every side."
ramacharitamanas::1539.translation_literal: बहुरि (then) / महाजन (great merchants) / सकल (all) / बोलाए (called) / आइ (coming) / सबन्हि (all) / सादर (respectfully) / सिर (head) / नाए (bowed) / हाट (markets) / बाट (roads) / मंदिर (temples) / सुरबासा (abodes of the divine) / नगरु (city) / सँवारहु (decorate) / चारिहुँ पासा (on all four sides)
ramacharitamanas::1539.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1539.essence: Joy becomes real when the whole city prepares for it.
ramacharitamanas::1539.simple_meaning: The king summons the city’s merchants and orders the whole city to be decorated for the occasion.
ramacharitamanas::1539.simple_insight: Big moments are prepared through shared effort, not private excitement.
ramacharitamanas::1539.detailed_meaning: King Janak has already sent for Ayodhya’s messengers and received Dasharath’s welcome. Now he calls the city’s merchants and instructs them to beautify the streets, temples, and neighborhoods. The wedding preparations are moving from announcement to action.
ramacharitamanas::1539.modern_relevance: A family hears guests are coming for a once-in-years celebration, and suddenly everyone is cleaning, hanging lights, and fixing what they usually ignore. A joyful event changes the whole town’s rhythm.
ramacharitamanas::1539.insight: It shifts attention from the announcement of joy to the work that makes joy visible.

ramacharitamanas::1540.verse_sanskrit: हरषि चले निज निज गृह आए। पुनि परिचारक बोलि पठाए॥ रचहु बिचित्र बितान बनाई। सिर धरि बचन चले सचु पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1540.verse_hindi: महाजन प्रसन्न होकर चले और अपने-अपने घर आए। फिर राजा ने नौकरों को बुला भेजा (और उन्हें आज्ञा दी कि) विचित्र मंडप सजाकर तैयार करो। यह सुनकर वे सब राजा के वचन सिर पर धरकर और सुख पाकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1540.english_translation: The merchants returned home delighted. Then the king summoned the attendants and ordered them to prepare a splendid pavilion. They took his command to heart and departed gladly.
ramacharitamanas::1540.translation_literal: हरषि (delighted) / चले (went) / निज निज (each their own) / गृह (home) / आए (came) / पुनि (again) / परिचारक (attendants) / बोलि (calling) / पठाए (sent) / रचहु (prepare) / बिचित्र (splendid/varied) / बितान (pavilion/canopy) / बनाई (making) / सिर (head) / धरि (placing) / बचन (word/command) / चले (went) / सचु (true) / पाई (having obtained)
ramacharitamanas::1540.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1540.essence: Joy becomes action when people carry the command gladly.
ramacharitamanas::1540.simple_meaning: The merchants went home happily, and the king sent for his attendants to prepare a beautiful pavilion. Everyone accepted the order gladly and got to work.
ramacharitamanas::1540.simple_insight: A clear command, given with goodwill, can turn effort into shared joy.
ramacharitamanas::1540.detailed_meaning: After the merchants are invited, they leave in happiness. King Dasharath then calls his attendants and asks them to ready a splendid pavilion for the coming ceremony. The verse shows the city moving from celebration into careful preparation.
ramacharitamanas::1540.modern_relevance: A wedding text thread lights up, then everyone starts arranging chairs, lights, and flowers without complaint. A good plan becomes real because people treat the request as an honour.
ramacharitamanas::1540.insight: It shifts attention from excitement to execution: a joyful order still needs willing hands.

ramacharitamanas::1541.verse_sanskrit: पठए बोलि गुनी तिन्ह नाना। जे बितान बिधि कुसल सुजाना॥ बिधिहि बंदि तिन्ह कीन्ह अरंभा। बिरचे कनक कदलि के खंभा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1541.verse_hindi: उन्होंने अनेक कारीगरों को बुला भेजा, जो मंडप बनाने में कुशल और चतुर थे। उन्होंने ब्रह्मा की वंदना करके कार्य आरंभ किया और (पहले) सोने के केले के खंभे बनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1541.english_translation: They summoned many skilled craftsmen, expert and wise in building the pavilion. Worshipping Brahma, they began the work and made golden banana-pillars.
ramacharitamanas::1541.translation_literal: पठए (sent for) / बोलि (calling) / गुनी (skilled) / तिन्ह (those) / नाना (many) / जे (who) / बितान (pavilion) / बिधि (method) / कुसल (skilled) / सुजाना (wise) / बिधिहि (to Brahma) / बंदि (bowing) / तिन्ह (they) / कीन्ह (did) / अरंभा (beginning) / बिरचे (made) / कनक (golden) / कदलि (banana) / के (of) / खंभा (pillars)
ramacharitamanas::1541.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1541.essence: Beauty begins with skilled hands and reverent beginnings.
ramacharitamanas::1541.simple_meaning: Skilled craftsmen were called in to build the wedding pavilion. They began by honoring Brahma and made golden banana pillars.
ramacharitamanas::1541.simple_insight: Even a celebration begins with order, skill, and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1541.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the king has ordered the city prepared for Ram's wedding. Skilled builders are summoned, they honor Brahma, and the pavilion begins to take shape with ornate golden pillars.
ramacharitamanas::1541.modern_relevance: A wedding venue is still empty at dawn. By noon, electricians, decorators, and carpenters are moving with quiet precision. A beautiful event begins long before anyone arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1541.insight: It shifts attention from the finished spectacle to the disciplined, reverent work that makes it possible.

ramacharitamanas::1542.verse_sanskrit: हरित मनिन्ह के पत्र फल पदुमराग के फूल। रचना देखि बिचित्र अति मनु बिरंचि कर भूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1542.verse_hindi: हरी-हरी मणियों (पन्ने) के पत्ते और फल बनाए तथा पद्मराग मणियों (माणिक) के फूल बनाए। मंडप की अत्यन्त विचित्र रचना देखकर ब्रह्मा का मन भी भूल गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1542.english_translation: The leaves and fruits were made of emeralds, and the flowers of ruby. Seeing the wondrous design, even Brahma's mind was bewildered.
ramacharitamanas::1542.translation_literal: हरित (green) / मनिन्ह (of jewels) / के (of) / पत्र (leaves) / फल (fruits) / पदुमराग (ruby) / के (of) / फूल (flowers) / रचना (design) / देखि (seeing) / बिचित्र (wondrous) / अति (very) / मनु (mind) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / कर (of) / भूल (bewilderment)
ramacharitamanas::1542.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1542.essence: The beauty is so complete it outshines the mind that made worlds.
ramacharitamanas::1542.simple_meaning: The pavilion was decorated so beautifully with jewel-like leaves, fruits, and flowers that even Brahma would be amazed by it.
ramacharitamanas::1542.simple_insight: Beauty can be so complete that it overwhelms even the mind that imagines worlds.
ramacharitamanas::1542.detailed_meaning: The kings have ordered a grand wedding pavilion for Sita's swayamvar. Skilled builders now decorate it with jewel-made leaves, fruits, and flowers. The scene is still only preparation, so the verse lingers on dazzling craftsmanship rather than a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1542.modern_relevance: You step into a wedding hall after hours of setup and stop in silence. The lights, colors, and details feel almost unreal, as if the room itself has been enchanted.
ramacharitamanas::1542.insight: It shifts attention from function to wonder, showing how form itself can carry meaning.

ramacharitamanas::1543.verse_sanskrit: बेनु हरित मनिमय सब कीन्हे। सरल सपरब परहिं नहिं चीन्हे॥ कनक कलित अहिबेलि बनाई। लखि नहिं परइ सपरन सुहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1543.verse_hindi: बाँस सब हरी-हरी मणियों (पन्ने) के सीधे और गाँठों से युक्त ऐसे बनाए जो पहचाने नहीं जाते थे (कि मणियों के हैं या साधारण)। सोने की सुंदर नागबेली (पान की लता) बनाई, जो पत्तों सहित ऐसी भली मालूम होती थी कि पहचानी नहीं जाती थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1543.english_translation: All the bamboo was made of green gems, straight and jointed, yet impossible to recognize. A beautiful golden vine was made, so lovely with its leaves that it could not be told apart.
ramacharitamanas::1543.translation_literal: बेनु (bamboo) / हरित (green) / मनिमय (gem-made) / सब (all) / कीन्हे (were made) / सरल (straight) / सपरब (jointed) / परहिं (appear) / नहिं (not) / चीन्हे (recognized)॥ / कनक (golden) / कलित (adorned) / अहिबेलि (snake-vine) / बनाई (was made) / लखि (seeing) / नहिं (not) / परइ (is possible) / सपरन (with leaves) / सुहाई (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::1543.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1543.essence: Perfect craft makes the ordinary look enchanted.
ramacharitamanas::1543.simple_meaning: The wedding pavilion was decorated so skillfully that ordinary bamboo and vines looked like jeweled art.
ramacharitamanas::1543.simple_insight: Beauty can be so complete that it hides the labor behind it.
ramacharitamanas::1543.detailed_meaning: The wedding pavilion for Sita’s swayamvar is being built in Ayodhya. Skilled artisans turn bamboo into gem-like forms and a vine into gold-like ornamentation. This verse continues the lavish scene-setting, showing the care and wonder poured into the setting.
ramacharitamanas::1543.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and only notice the elegance, not the hours of careful work behind every detail. That hidden craft is what makes the whole space feel effortless.
ramacharitamanas::1543.insight: It trains attention toward craftsmanship, where excellence disappears into appearance.

ramacharitamanas::1544.verse_sanskrit: तेहि के रचि पचि बंध बनाए। बिच बिच मुकुता दाम सुहाए॥ मानिक मरकत कुलिस पिरोजा। चीरि कोरि पचि रचे सरोजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1544.verse_hindi: उसी नागबेली के रचकर और पच्चीकारी करके बंधन (बाँधने की रस्सी) बनाए। बीच-बीच में मोतियों की सुंदर झालरें हैं। माणिक, पन्ने, हीरे और िफरोजे, इन रत्नों को चीरकर, कोरकर और पच्चीकारी करके, इनके (लाल, हरे, सफेद और फिरोजी रंग के) कमल बनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1544.english_translation: They fashioned bindings from that vine, with strings of pearls hanging beautifully between them. Rubies, emeralds, diamonds, and turquoise were cut, carved, and inlaid into lotuses of red, green, white, and blue.
ramacharitamanas::1544.translation_literal: तेहि के (of that) / रचि पचि (fashioned with intricate inlay) / बंध (bindings) / बनाए (made) / बिच बिच (here and there) / मुकुता (pearls) / दाम (garlands/strings) / सुहाए (beautiful) / मानिक (rubies) / मरकत (emeralds) / कुलिस (diamonds) / पिरोजा (turquoise) / चीरि (cutting) / कोरि (carving) / पचि रचे (intricately fashioned) / सरोजा (lotuses)
ramacharitamanas::1544.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1544.essence: Splendor is made in the smallest details.
ramacharitamanas::1544.simple_meaning: The pavilion is decorated with intricate vine-like bindings, pearl strings, and lotus shapes made from precious stones.
ramacharitamanas::1544.simple_insight: Beauty can be built with patient craftsmanship, not just wealth.
ramacharitamanas::1544.detailed_meaning: The Sita-swayamvar pavilion is being described in lavish detail. After the gem-studded pillars and walls, this verse adds the decorative bindings and lotus forms, showing how every surface has been shaped into splendor before the contest begins.
ramacharitamanas::1544.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where every corner has been thought through: the drapes, the lights, the flowers, the tiny details no guest will name. That care itself changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::1544.insight: It shifts attention from the finished display to the disciplined artistry behind it.

ramacharitamanas::1545.verse_sanskrit: किए भृंग बहुरंग बिहंगा। गुंजहिं कूजहिं पवन प्रसंगा॥ सुर प्रतिमा खंभन गढ़ि काढ़ीं। मंगल द्रब्य लिएँ सब ठाढ़ीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1545.verse_hindi: भौंरे और बहुत रंगों के पक्षी बनाए, जो हवा के सहारे गूँजते और कूजते थे। खंभों पर देवताओं की मूर्तियाँ गढ़कर निकालीं, जो सब मंगल द्रव्य लिए खड़ी थीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1545.english_translation: They made bees and many-colored birds that hummed and sang with the breeze. They carved divine figures on the pillars, each standing with auspicious offerings in hand.
ramacharitamanas::1545.translation_literal: किए (made) / भृंग (bees) / बहुरंग (many-colored) / बिहंगा (birds) / गुंजहिं (hum) / कूजहिं (sing) / पवन (wind) / प्रसंगा (with the movement/occasion of) / सुर (divine beings) / प्रतिमा (images) / खंभन (on pillars) / गढ़ि (carving) / काढ़ीं (were made to emerge) / मंगल (auspicious) / द्रब्य (offerings) / लिएँ (holding) / सब (all) / ठाढ़ीं (standing)
ramacharitamanas::1545.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1545.essence: Even carved figures and painted birds can make a place feel alive.
ramacharitamanas::1545.simple_meaning: The decorations were made to look alive: bees, colorful birds, and carved divine figures holding auspicious offerings.
ramacharitamanas::1545.simple_insight: Beauty can feel alive when every detail is made with care.
ramacharitamanas::1545.detailed_meaning: The verse continues the description of a richly decorated ceremonial space in Balkand. Craftsmen have shaped pillars, birds, bees, and divine figures so the whole setting seems vibrant and sacred. It is a visual detail, not a teaching point.
ramacharitamanas::1545.modern_relevance: A wedding hall, temple stage, or festival pandal can feel transformed when every small detail is arranged with care. The atmosphere itself begins to sing.
ramacharitamanas::1545.insight: It trains attention toward crafted atmosphere, where decoration becomes part of the experience.

ramacharitamanas::1546.verse_sanskrit: चौकें भाँति अनेक पुराईं। सिंधुर मनिमय सहज सुहाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1546.verse_hindi: गजमुक्ताओं के सहज ही सुहावने अनेकों तरह के चौक पुराए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1546.english_translation: Many kinds of auspicious designs were made naturally beautiful with pearl-like elephant motifs.
ramacharitamanas::1546.translation_literal: चौकें (decorative floor designs) / भाँति अनेक (many kinds) / पुराईं (were made) / सिंधुर (elephant) / मनिमय (jewel-made) / सहज (naturally) / सुहाईं (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::1546.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1546.essence: A sacred welcome is made through beautiful, careful detail.
ramacharitamanas::1546.simple_meaning: The verse describes decorative floor patterns made in many forms, with elephant figures that looked naturally beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::1546.simple_insight: Beauty can be built into the smallest details of a welcome.
ramacharitamanas::1546.detailed_meaning: The scene is a royal decoration being prepared for a sacred celebration. After the pillars, garlands, and carved figures, the floor itself is adorned with many auspicious designs. This verse simply adds another layer of that festive splendor.
ramacharitamanas::1546.modern_relevance: You walk into a home before a wedding and notice the rangoli, the lights, the careful arrangement of every corner. The welcome is not accidental; it is made with devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1546.insight: It shifts attention to the care hidden inside preparation, not just the final event.

ramacharitamanas::1547.verse_sanskrit: सौरभ पल्लव सुभग सुठि किए नीलमनि कोरि। हेम बौर मरकत घवरि लसत पाटमय डोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1547.verse_hindi: नील मणि को कोरकर अत्यन्त सुंदर आम के पत्ते बनाए। सोने के बौर (आम के फूल) और रेशम की डोरी से बँधे हुए पन्ने के बने फलों के गुच्छे सुशोभित हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1547.english_translation: Beautiful fragrant leaves were made from sapphire, with golden blossoms and emerald clusters tied by silken cords.
ramacharitamanas::1547.translation_literal: सौरभ (fragrance) / पल्लव (leaf-buds, leaves) / सुभग (beautiful) / सुठि (very) / किए (made) / नीलमनि (sapphire) / कोरि (carved) / हेम (gold) / बौर (blossoms) / मरकत (emerald) / घवरि (clusters) / लसत (shining) / पाटमय (silken) / डोरि (cord)
ramacharitamanas::1547.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1547.essence: Even decoration becomes sacred when made with loving care.
ramacharitamanas::1547.simple_meaning: The verse describes decorative festival ornaments made to look like mango leaves, blossoms, and fruit clusters using precious materials.
ramacharitamanas::1547.simple_insight: Beauty can be created with care and devotion, turning ordinary celebration into something radiant.
ramacharitamanas::1547.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the wedding preparations for Ram and Sita are in full bloom. Artisans are crafting every detail of the festive decoration, from carved leaves to jeweled fruit clusters. This verse adds one more ornament to the scene.
ramacharitamanas::1547.modern_relevance: You watch someone spend hours hanging lights, arranging flowers, and fixing every detail before a wedding. The care itself becomes part of the blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1547.insight: It shifts attention from the object to the devotion behind the making.

ramacharitamanas::1548.verse_sanskrit: रचे रुचिर बर बंदनिवारे। मनहुँ मनोभवँ फंद सँवारे॥ मंगल कलश अनेक बनाए। ध्वज पताक पट चमर सुहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1548.verse_hindi: ऐसे सुंदर और उत्तम बंदनवार बनाए मानो कामदेव ने फंदे सजाए हों। अनेकों मंगल कलश और सुंदर ध्वजा, पताका, परदे और चँवर बनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1548.english_translation: Beautiful and auspicious festoons were made, like Cupid had arranged his nets. Many sacred pots, banners, flags, curtains, and fly-whisks were also set up.
ramacharitamanas::1548.translation_literal: रचे (were made) / रुचिर (beautiful) / बर (excellent) / बंदनिवारे (festoons) / मनहुँ (as if) / मनोभवँ (by Cupid) / फंद (nets) / सँवारे (arranged)॥ / मंगल (auspicious) / कलश (pots) / अनेक (many) / बनाए (made) / ध्वज (banners) / पताका (flags) / पट (curtains) / चमर (fly-whisks) / सुहाए (looked beautiful) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1548.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1548.essence: The wedding hall is dressed like a celebration before the bride appears.
ramacharitamanas::1548.simple_meaning: The wedding pavilion was decorated with beautiful festoons, sacred pots, banners, flags, curtains, and fly-whisks.
ramacharitamanas::1548.simple_insight: The scene is being prepared for a sacred celebration, with every detail made beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::1548.detailed_meaning: The wedding pavilion for Sita’s swayamvar is being dressed with rich decorations. Festoons, auspicious pots, banners, flags, curtains, and fly-whisks are arranged to create the splendor of the coming ceremony.
ramacharitamanas::1548.modern_relevance: You walk into a hall before a wedding and see every corner being dressed with care — flowers tied, lights hung, fabric smoothed. The room itself announces that something precious is about to happen.
ramacharitamanas::1548.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the sacred preparation that makes the event feel worthy.

ramacharitamanas::1549.verse_sanskrit: दीप मनोहर मनिमय नाना। जाइ न बरनि बिचित्र बिताना॥ जेहिं मंडप दुलहिनि बैदेही। सो बरनै असि मति कबि केही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1549.verse_hindi: जिसमें मणियों के अनेकों सुंदर दीपक हैं, उस विचित्र मंडप का तो वर्णन ही नहीं किया जा सकता, जिस मंडप में श्री जानकीजी दुलहिन होंगी, किस कवि की ऐसी बुद्धि है जो उसका वर्णन कर सके ॥
ramacharitamanas::1549.english_translation: The many jeweled lamps are beautiful, but this strange pavilion cannot be described. What poet has the mind to describe the pavilion where Janaki will be the bride?
ramacharitamanas::1549.translation_literal: दीप (lamps) / मनोहर (beautiful) / मनिमय (made of jewels) / नाना (many) / जाइ (can) / न बरनि (not be described) / बिचित्र (strange, wondrous) / बिताना (pavilion, canopy) / जेहिं (in which) / मंडप (pavilion, marriage hall) / दुलहिनि (bride) / बैदेही (Janaki, daughter of King Janak) / सो (that) / बरनै (describe) / असि (such) / मति (mind, intelligence) / कबि (poet) / केही (whose)
ramacharitamanas::1549.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1549.essence: A sacred moment can exceed the poet's own language.
ramacharitamanas::1549.simple_meaning: The wedding pavilion is so beautiful and wondrous that no poet can fully describe it, especially because it will hold Janaki as the bride.
ramacharitamanas::1549.simple_insight: Some moments feel too full for language. Beauty can make words feel small.
ramacharitamanas::1549.detailed_meaning: The wedding decorations in Janak's palace are being prepared for Sita's marriage. After the garlands, banners, and jeweled ornaments, the poet pauses at the pavilion itself and admits its beauty is beyond description, because it is the place where Janaki will stand as bride.
ramacharitamanas::1549.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall before the guests arrive, lights still being adjusted, every corner glowing. For a moment, the room feels bigger than the words you could use to praise it.
ramacharitamanas::1549.insight: It shifts attention from description to reverence, letting awe remain larger than explanation.

ramacharitamanas::1550.verse_sanskrit: दूलहु रामु रूप गुन सागर। सो बितानु तिहुँ लोग उजागर॥ जनक भवन कै सोभा जैसी। गृह गृह प्रति पुर देखिअ तैसी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1550.verse_hindi: जिस मंडप में रूप और गुणों के समुद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी दूल्हे होंगे, वह मंडप तीनों लोकों में प्रसिद्ध होना ही चाहिए। जनकजी के महल की जैसी शोभा है, वैसी ही शोभा नगर के प्रत्येक घर की दिखाई देती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1550.english_translation: The bridegroom Ram, ocean of beauty and virtues, made that canopy radiant through all three worlds. The splendor of Janak's palace was matched in every house of the city.
ramacharitamanas::1550.translation_literal: दूलहु (bridegroom) / रामु (Ram) / रूप (beauty, form) / गुन (virtues) / सागर (ocean) / सो (that) / बितानु (canopy, pavilion) / तिहुँ (three) / लोग (worlds) / उजागर (bright, renowned)॥ / जनक (Janak) / भवन (house, palace) / कै (of) / सोभा (splendor) / जैसी (as) / गृह (house) / गृह (house) / प्रति (each) / पुर (city) / देखिअ (is seen) / तैसी (so, like that)॥
ramacharitamanas::1550.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1550.essence: Ram's presence makes even ordinary places feel radiant.
ramacharitamanas::1550.simple_meaning: Ram's wedding canopy is glorious enough to be known in all three worlds. Janak's palace is so radiant that the whole city seems equally splendid.
ramacharitamanas::1550.simple_insight: True greatness makes the whole surrounding world feel elevated.
ramacharitamanas::1550.detailed_meaning: The wedding preparations in Janakpur have reached their peak. Ram, the bridegroom, is described as an ocean of beauty and virtue, and his presence makes the ceremonial canopy famous across the three worlds. His radiance spills into the whole city.
ramacharitamanas::1550.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall and the whole room changes because one person arrives with grace. Real presence doesn't just stand out — it transforms everything around it.
ramacharitamanas::1550.insight: It shifts attention from decoration alone to the presence that gives a place its shine.

ramacharitamanas::1551.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं तेरहुति तेहि समय निहारी। तेहि लघु लगहिं भुवन दस चारी॥ जो संपदा नीच गृह सोहा। सो बिलोकि सुरनायक मोहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1551.verse_hindi: उस समय जिसने तिरहुत को देखा, उसे चौदह भुवन तुच्छ जान पड़े। जनकपुर में नीच के घर भी उस समय जो सम्पदा सुशोभित थी, उसे देखकर इन्द्र भी मोहित हो जाता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::1551.english_translation: Whoever saw Tirhut at that time found the fourteen worlds small. The wealth shining even in humble homes in Janakpur would fascinate Indra himself.
ramacharitamanas::1551.translation_literal: जेहिं (whoever) / तेरहुति (Tirhut) / तेहि समय (at that time) / निहारी (having seen) / तेहि (that) / लघु (small) / लगहिं (seem) / भुवन (worlds) / दस चारी (fourteen) / जो (which) / संपदा (wealth) / नीच गृह (humble houses) / सोहा (shone beautifully) / सो (that) / बिलोकि (seeing) / सुरनायक (lord of the gods) / मोहा (was enchanted)
ramacharitamanas::1551.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1551.essence: Janakpur’s splendor makes even heaven seem small.
ramacharitamanas::1551.simple_meaning: Janakpur’s splendor was so great that even the whole world seemed small beside it. Its beauty and wealth amazed even Indra.
ramacharitamanas::1551.simple_insight: Some places announce a turning point before anyone speaks. Their atmosphere alone tells you something extraordinary is about to happen.
ramacharitamanas::1551.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the wedding preparations for Sita and Ram have made the city dazzling beyond measure. Tulsidas pauses on the setting itself: the grandeur is so overwhelming that even Indra would be stunned. It prepares the mind for the marriage to come.
ramacharitamanas::1551.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall lit like a palace, and the air changes before the ceremony begins. Everyone feels it: this is not an ordinary gathering; something unforgettable is unfolding.
ramacharitamanas::1551.insight: It shifts attention from the event to the atmosphere it creates, showing how setting can carry meaning before action begins.

ramacharitamanas::1552.verse_sanskrit: बसइ नगर जेहिं लच्छि करि कपट नारि बर बेषु। तेहि पुर कै सोभा कहत सकुचहिं सारद सेषु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1552.verse_hindi: जिस नगर में साक्षात् लक्ष्मीजी कपट से स्त्री का सुंदर वेष बनाकर बसती हैं, उस पुर की शोभा का वर्णन करने में सरस्वती और शेष भी सकुचाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1552.english_translation: In the city where Lakshmi herself lives, disguised as a beautiful woman, even Saraswati and Shesha grow shy describing its splendor.
ramacharitamanas::1552.translation_literal: बसइ (dwells) / नगर (city) / जेहिं (in which) / लच्छि (Lakshmi) / करि (having done) / कपट (deception, disguise) / नारि (woman) / बर (beautiful, excellent) / बेषु (form, dress) / तेहि (that) / पुर (city) / कै (of) / सोभा (beauty, splendor) / कहत (while speaking) / सकुचहिं (feel shy) / सारद (Saraswati) / सेषु (Shesha)
ramacharitamanas::1552.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1552.essence: Some beauty is so complete that language itself bows.
ramacharitamanas::1552.simple_meaning: Ayodhya is so magnificent that even the goddess of speech and the cosmic serpent hesitate to describe it fully.
ramacharitamanas::1552.simple_insight: Some places feel larger than language. Their beauty makes even praise seem too small.
ramacharitamanas::1552.detailed_meaning: Janak's messengers have entered the world of Ram's future bride and are seeing Ayodhya in its glory. Tulsidas pauses the action to say that the city's splendor is beyond ordinary description, setting up the sacred scale of the meeting to come.
ramacharitamanas::1552.modern_relevance: You walk into a home after years of care, light, and welcome have shaped every corner. For a moment, even the best words feel clumsy.
ramacharitamanas::1552.insight: It shifts attention from literal description to reverent witnessing, letting grandeur be felt before it is explained.

ramacharitamanas::1553.verse_sanskrit: पहुँचे दूत राम पुर पावन। हरषे नगर बिलोकि सुहावन॥ भूप द्वार तिन्ह खबरि जनाई। दसरथ नृप सुनि लिए बोलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1553.verse_hindi: जनकजी के दूत श्री रामचन्द्रजी की पवित्र पुरी अयोध्या में पहुँचे। सुंदर नगर देखकर वे हर्षित हुए। राजद्वार पर जाकर उन्होंने खबर भेजी, राजा दशरथजी ने सुनकर उन्हें बुला लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1553.english_translation: The envoys reached Ram's sacred city and rejoiced at its beauty. At the palace gate they sent word, and King Dasharath, hearing it, called them in.
ramacharitamanas::1553.translation_literal: पहुँचे (reached) / दूत (envoys) / राम पुर (Ram's city) / पावन (sacred) / हरषे (rejoiced) / नगर (city) / बिलोकि (seeing) / सुहावन (beautiful) / भूप (king) / द्वार (gate) / तिन्ह (they) / खबरि (news) / जनाई (made known) / दसरथ नृप (King Dasharath) / सुनि (hearing) / लिए (took) / बोलाई (called in)
ramacharitamanas::1553.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1553.essence: The city welcomes the message before the king does.
ramacharitamanas::1553.simple_meaning: Janak's envoys arrive in Ayodhya, admire the city's beauty, and are summoned by Dasharath after sending word at the palace gate.
ramacharitamanas::1553.simple_insight: A meeting is about to change everything, and even the city itself feels alive with it.
ramacharitamanas::1553.detailed_meaning: Janak's messengers arrive in Ayodhya, the sacred city of Ram, and are struck by its beauty. They announce themselves at the palace gate, and Dasharath immediately calls them in. The scene prepares the meeting that will carry Janak's message into the royal house.
ramacharitamanas::1553.modern_relevance: You arrive at a house where something important is about to be decided. The gate opens, the message is sent, and everyone feels the shift before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1553.insight: It frames a turning point through atmosphere, not argument: the city, the gate, and the summons all signal importance.

ramacharitamanas::1554.verse_sanskrit: करि प्रनामु तिन्ह पाती दीन्ही। मुदित महीप आपु उठि लीन्ही॥ बारि बिलोचन बाँचत पाती। पुलक गात आई भरि छाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1554.verse_hindi: दूतों ने प्रणाम करके चिट्ठी दी। प्रसन्न होकर राजा ने स्वयं उठकर उसे लिया। चिट्ठी बाँचते समय उनके नेत्रों में जल (प्रेम और आनंद के आँसू) छा गया, शरीर पुलकित हो गया और छाती भर आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1554.english_translation: The messengers bowed and gave the letter. The king rose joyfully and took it himself. As he read, tears filled his eyes, his body thrilled, and his chest swelled with emotion.
ramacharitamanas::1554.translation_literal: करि (having done) / प्रनामु (bowing) / तिन्ह (they) / पाती (letter) / दीन्ही (gave) / मुदित (joyful) / महीप (king) / आपु (himself) / उठि (rising) / लीन्ही (took) / बारि (water) / बिलोचन (eyes) / बाँचत (reading) / पाती (letter) / पुलक (horripilation) / गात (body) / आई (came) / भरि (filled) / छाती (chest)
ramacharitamanas::1554.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1554.essence: Love makes even a king rise to receive a letter.
ramacharitamanas::1554.simple_meaning: The messengers respectfully hand over the letter, and the king receives it himself with joy. Reading it fills him with tears, trembling, and a heart too full to hold itself.
ramacharitamanas::1554.simple_insight: Warmth can arrive through a single letter. Respect opens the door, and love floods the body before the mind can speak.
ramacharitamanas::1554.detailed_meaning: Janak's messengers have reached Ayodhya and stand before Dasharath. They bow, hand over the message, and the king rises to take it himself. As he reads, joy and tenderness overwhelm him before the next exchange begins.
ramacharitamanas::1554.modern_relevance: You open a message from someone you love after a long wait. Before you even finish reading, your eyes sting and your chest tightens with feeling.
ramacharitamanas::1554.insight: It shows how sincere contact changes posture, speech, and body at once. Reverence and affection become visible before any reply is made.

ramacharitamanas::1555.verse_sanskrit: रामु लखनु उर कर बर चीठी। रहि गए कहत न खाटी मीठी॥ पुनि धरि धीर पत्रिका बाँची। हरषी सभा बात सुनि साँची ॥
ramacharitamanas::1555.verse_hindi: हृदय में राम और लक्ष्मण हैं, हाथ में सुंदर चिट्ठी है, राजा उसे हाथ में लिए ही रह गए, खट्टी-मीठी कुछ भी कह न सके। फिर धीरज धरकर उन्होंने पत्रिका पढ़ी। सारी सभा सच्ची बात सुनकर हर्षित हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1555.english_translation: Ram and Lakshman were in the king's heart, and the beautiful letter was in his hand. He could not say anything, neither bitter nor sweet. Then, gathering himself, he read the letter. The whole assembly rejoiced to hear the true news.
ramacharitamanas::1555.translation_literal: रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / उर (heart) / कर (hand) / बर (beautiful) / चीठी (letter) / रहि गए (remained) / कहत (saying) / न (not) / खाटी (bitter) / मीठी (sweet) / पुनि (again) / धरि (gathering) / धीर (composure) / पत्रिका (letter) / बाँची (read) / हरषी (rejoiced) / सभा (assembly) / बात (news) / सुनि (hearing) / साँची (true)
ramacharitamanas::1555.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1555.essence: True news can leave the heart speechless before it makes the whole room rejoice.
ramacharitamanas::1555.simple_meaning: Dasharath is so moved by the letter about Ram and Lakshman that he cannot speak at first. After steadying himself, he reads it, and everyone feels joy at the true news.
ramacharitamanas::1555.simple_insight: Sometimes joy arrives so suddenly that the heart has to catch up before the mind can speak.
ramacharitamanas::1555.detailed_meaning: At the royal court in Ayodhya, Dasharath receives the message from Janak's envoys. The names of Ram and Lakshman overwhelm him before he can respond. He steadies himself, reads the letter, and the court brightens with relief and happiness.
ramacharitamanas::1555.modern_relevance: Your phone buzzes with the message you have been waiting for, and for a second you just stare at it. Relief is so strong it steals your words before it gives them back.
ramacharitamanas::1555.insight: It shows how overwhelming good news can pause speech, then restore composure and shared joy.

ramacharitamanas::1556.verse_sanskrit: खेलत रहे तहाँ सुधि पाई। आए भरतु सहित हित भाई॥ पूछत अति सनेहँ सकुचाई। तात कहाँ तें पाती आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1556.verse_hindi: भरतजी अपने मित्रों और भाई शत्रुघ्न के साथ जहाँ खेलते थे, वहीं समाचार पाकर वे आ गए। बहुत प्रेम से सकुचाते हुए पूछते हैं- पिताजी! चिट्ठी कहाँ से आई है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1556.english_translation: When Bharata heard the news, he came with his dear brother and friends. Asking with great affection and modesty, he said, “Father, where did the letter come from?”
ramacharitamanas::1556.translation_literal: खेलत रहे (were playing) / तहाँ (there) / सुधि (news, remembrance) / पाई (having received) / आए (came) / भरतु (Bharata) / सहित (together with) / हित (dear) / भाई (brother) / पूछत (asking) / अति (very) / सनेहँ (with affection) / सकुचाई (with modest modesty) / तात (father) / कहाँ तें (from where) / पाती (letter) / आई (came)
ramacharitamanas::1556.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1556.essence: Affection moves first, before the mind even asks why.
ramacharitamanas::1556.simple_meaning: Bharata stops playing and comes at once when he hears the news. With loving modesty, he asks his father where the letter came from.
ramacharitamanas::1556.simple_insight: Love makes him attentive before he even knows the message.
ramacharitamanas::1556.detailed_meaning: Bharata is in Ayodhya, playing with his friends and brother Shatrughna, when news arrives. He comes immediately, gentle and respectful, and asks Dasharath where the letter came from. The moment shows his affectionate nature before the bigger news is revealed.
ramacharitamanas::1556.modern_relevance: You are in the middle of a game or a conversation when a message about family arrives. Without drama, you leave everything and ask carefully what happened. That instinct reveals your heart before your words do.
ramacharitamanas::1556.insight: It shifts attention from play to relationship, showing how affection responds before analysis.

ramacharitamanas::1557.verse_sanskrit: कुसल प्रानप्रिय बंधु दोउ अहहिं कहहु केहिं देस। सुनि सनेह साने बचन बाची बहुरि नरेस ॥
ramacharitamanas::1557.verse_hindi: हमारे प्राणों से प्यारे दोनों भाई, कहिए सकुशल तो हैं और वे किस देश में हैं? स्नेह से सने ये वचन सुनकर राजा ने फिर से चिट्ठी पढ़ी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1557.english_translation: Are the two brothers, dearer than life, well? In which land do they dwell? Hearing these loving words, the king read the letter again.
ramacharitamanas::1557.translation_literal: कुसल (well) / प्रानप्रिय (dearer than life) / बंधु (brothers) / दोउ (both) / अहहिं (are) / कहहु (tell) / केहिं (which) / देस (land) / सुनि (hearing) / सनेह साने (saturated with affection) / बचन (words) / बाची (read) / बहुरि (again) / नरेस (king)
ramacharitamanas::1557.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::1557.essence: Tender concern can make a question feel like a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1557.simple_meaning: Bharat asks whether Ram and Lakshman are safe and where they are. The king, moved by the tender words, reads the letter again.
ramacharitamanas::1557.simple_insight: Love makes even a simple question feel sacred and unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::1557.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat has just received news of Ram and Lakshman. He asks with deep tenderness whether his life-breath brothers are well and where they are. The king, overwhelmed by the letter's affection, reads it again.
ramacharitamanas::1557.modern_relevance: You reread a message from someone you miss because one line carries their whole heart. The words are simple, but the feeling behind them changes your breathing.
ramacharitamanas::1557.insight: It shifts attention from the literal question to the devotion inside it.

ramacharitamanas::1558.verse_sanskrit: सुनि पाती पुलके दोउ भ्राता। अधिन सनेहु समात न गाता॥ प्रीति पुनीत भरत कै देखी। सकल सभाँ सुखु लहेउ बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1558.verse_hindi: चिट्ठी सुनकर दोनों भाई पुलकित हो गए। स्नेह इतना अधिक हो गया कि वह शरीर में समाता नहीं। भरतजी का पवित्र प्रेम देखकर सारी सभा ने विशेष सुख पाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1558.english_translation: Hearing the letter, both brothers were filled with delight. Their love grew so great it could not fit in the body. Seeing Bharat's pure love, the whole assembly felt a special joy.
ramacharitamanas::1558.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / पाती (letter) / पुलके (were thrilled) / दोउ (both) / भ्राता (brothers) / अधिन (excessive) / सनेहु (love) / समात (fits) / न (not) / गाता (body) / प्रीति (love) / पुनीत (pure) / भरत कै (of Bharat) / देखी (seeing) / सकल (all) / सभाँ (assembly) / सुखु (joy) / लहेउ (received) / बिसेषी (special)
ramacharitamanas::1558.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1558.essence: Pure love overflows and blesses everyone nearby.
ramacharitamanas::1558.simple_meaning: The brothers rejoice on hearing the letter, and Bharat's pure love fills everyone present with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1558.simple_insight: Pure love spreads. When affection is sincere, it lifts everyone around it.
ramacharitamanas::1558.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyā, news arrives about Ram and Lakshman. Bharat and Shatrughna are overwhelmed with love, and the court itself softens. Their devotion is so visible that the whole assembly feels blessed by it.
ramacharitamanas::1558.modern_relevance: A message finally arrives from someone you miss deeply. You read it, your chest loosens, and everyone nearby feels the warmth too. Love does not stay private when it is real.
ramacharitamanas::1558.insight: It shows how sincere affection becomes contagious and transforms a whole room without argument.

ramacharitamanas::1559.verse_sanskrit: तब नृप दूत निकट बैठारे। मधुर मनोहर बचन उचारे॥ भैया कहहु कुसल दोउ बारे। तुम्ह नीकें निज नयन निहारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1559.verse_hindi: तब राजा दूतों को पास बैठाकर मन को हरने वाले मीठे वचन बाले- भैया! कहो, दोनों बच्चे कुशल से तो हैं? तुमने अपनी आँखों से उन्हें अच्छी तरह देखा है न? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1559.english_translation: Then the king seated the messengers nearby and spoke sweet, charming words: "Brother, tell me, are both boys well? You have seen them clearly with your own eyes, haven't you?"
ramacharitamanas::1559.translation_literal: तब (then) / नृप (king) / दूत (messengers) / निकट (near) / बैठारे (had seated) / मधुर (sweet) / मनोहर (charming) / बचन (words) / उचारे (spoke) / भैया (brother) / कहहु (tell) / कुसल (well) / दोउ (both) / बारे (boys/children) / तुम्ह (you) / नीकें (well) / निज (own) / नयन (eyes) / निहारे (seen)
ramacharitamanas::1559.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1559.essence: Love wants facts, not comforting guesses.
ramacharitamanas::1559.simple_meaning: The king gently questions the messengers about the two boys, asking whether they are safe and whether the messengers truly saw them.
ramacharitamanas::1559.simple_insight: Careful love asks for direct witness, not vague reassurance.
ramacharitamanas::1559.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the king receives the messengers and draws them close with gentle words. He is not asking casually; his heart is fixed on the two boys he longs for. Their answer will either confirm his hope or deepen his ache.
ramacharitamanas::1559.modern_relevance: You refresh the chat thread for the fifth time, then call someone who was supposed to arrive hours ago. You do not want guesses. You want a clear, honest answer.
ramacharitamanas::1559.insight: It shifts attention from rumor to firsthand confirmation before the heart settles.

ramacharitamanas::1560.verse_sanskrit: स्यामल गौर धरें धनु भाथा। बय किसोर कौसिक मुनि साथा॥ पहिचानहु तुम्ह कहहु सुभाऊ। प्रेम बिबस पुनि पुनि कह राऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1560.verse_hindi: साँवले और गोरे शरीर वाले वे धनुष और तरकस धारण किए रहते हैं, किशोर अवस्था है, विश्वामित्र मुनि के साथ हैं। तुम उनको पहचानते हो तो उनका स्वभाव बताओ। राजा प्रेम के विशेष वश होने से बार-बार इस प्रकार कह (पूछ) रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1560.english_translation: Dark and fair, they carry bow and quiver, young in age, and with the sage Vishwamitra. If you recognize them, tell me their nature. The king, overcome by love, asks this again and again.
ramacharitamanas::1560.translation_literal: स्यामल (dark) / गौर (fair) / धरें (wearing) / धनु (bow) / भाथा (quiver) / बय (age) / किसोर (young) / कौसिक मुनि (sage Vishvamitra) / साथा (with) / पहिचानहु (recognize) / तुम्ह (you) / कहहु (tell) / सुभाऊ (nature) / प्रेम (love) / बिबस (overcome) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / कह (says) / राऊ (king)
ramacharitamanas::1560.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1560.essence: Love keeps returning to the same beloved face.
ramacharitamanas::1560.simple_meaning: The king asks the messengers to identify the two young boys with bows and quivers who are with Vishvamitra, because love makes him ask repeatedly.
ramacharitamanas::1560.simple_insight: Love makes a person keep asking the same question until the heart is satisfied.
ramacharitamanas::1560.detailed_meaning: Janak’s messengers have returned from the sacrifice hall, and the king is stunned by what they describe: two radiant boys with Vishvamitra. He is so moved by affection and curiosity that he keeps asking who they are and what kind of boys they are.
ramacharitamanas::1560.modern_relevance: You hear a name from someone you trust, and suddenly you want every detail — how they look, how they speak, what kind of person they are. Love turns curiosity into longing.
ramacharitamanas::1560.insight: It shows how affection sharpens attention and makes the mind return to one beloved subject.

ramacharitamanas::1561.verse_sanskrit: जा दिन तें मुनि गए लवाई। तब तें आजु साँचि सुधि पाई॥ कहहु बिदेह कवन बिधि जाने। सुनि प्रिय बचन दूत मुसुकाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1561.verse_hindi: (भैया!) जिस दिन से मुनि उन्हें लिवा ले गए, तब से आज ही हमने सच्ची खबर पाई है। कहो तो महाराज जनक ने उन्हें कैसे पहचाना? ये प्रिय (प्रेम भरे) वचन सुनकर दूत मुस्कुराए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1561.english_translation: “From the day the sage took them away, only today have we received the true news. Tell us, Janaka, how did you recognize them?” Hearing these loving words, the messengers smiled.
ramacharitamanas::1561.translation_literal: जा दिन तें (from the day) / मुनि (the sage) / गए (went) / लवाई (taking away) / तब तें (since then) / आजु (today) / साँचि (true) / सुधि (news/knowledge) / पाई (received) / कहहु (tell) / बिदेह (Janaka) / कवन बिधि (by what manner) / जाने (recognized) / सुनि (hearing) / प्रिय बचन (loving words) / दूत (messengers) / मुसुकाने (smiled)
ramacharitamanas::1561.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1561.essence: Kind words reveal what uncertainty could not.
ramacharitamanas::1561.simple_meaning: The messengers tell Janaka they have finally heard the truth about the boys and ask how he recognized them. Their loving words make the messengers smile.
ramacharitamanas::1561.simple_insight: Warm speech opens trust. Even a hard search softens when the heart feels welcomed.
ramacharitamanas::1561.detailed_meaning: Janaka’s messengers have been sent to identify the two princes with Vishvamitra. They finally learn the truth from Janaka’s tender reply, and his affectionate tone makes them smile. The scene turns from uncertainty to recognition.
ramacharitamanas::1561.modern_relevance: You finally reach the parent of the missing child, and instead of suspicion, you hear warmth. The tension drops at once because kindness has answered the question first.
ramacharitamanas::1561.insight: It shifts the moment from doubt to recognition through respectful, affectionate speech.

ramacharitamanas::1562.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु महीपति मुकुट मनि तुम्ह सम धन्य न कोउ। रामु लखनु जिन्ह के तनय बिस्व बिभूषन दोउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1562.verse_hindi: (दूतों ने कहा-) हे राजाओं के मुकुटमणि! सुनिए, आपके समान धन्य और कोई नहीं है, जिनके राम-लक्ष्मण जैसे पुत्र हैं, जो दोनों विश्व के विभूषण हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1562.english_translation: Listen, jewel among kings, no one is more blessed than you. You have Ram and Lakshman as your sons, both ornaments of the world.
ramacharitamanas::1562.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / महीपति (lord of the earth, king) / मुकुट मनि (jewel of the crown) / तुम्ह सम (like you) / धन्य (blessed) / न कोउ (no one) / रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / जिन्ह के (whose) / तनय (sons) / बिस्व (world) / बिभूषन (ornaments) / दोउ (both)
ramacharitamanas::1562.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1562.essence: Having Ram close is the highest blessing any house can receive.
ramacharitamanas::1562.simple_meaning: The messengers tell Janak that no ruler is more fortunate than he is, because Ram and Lakshman are his sons and the glory of the world.
ramacharitamanas::1562.simple_insight: Real honor is not status. It is being entrusted with what is most radiant.
ramacharitamanas::1562.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the messengers finally confirm what everyone longs to hear: the two princes with bows are Ram and Lakshman. They praise Janak as the luckiest of kings, because such sons make his house blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1562.modern_relevance: You hear your child praised by a teacher after years of worry, and the relief hits first: not your achievement, but your blessing. Some honors cannot be bought.
ramacharitamanas::1562.insight: It shifts attention from royal rank to the grace of having Ram in one's family.

ramacharitamanas::1563.verse_sanskrit: पूछन जोगु न तनय तुम्हारे। पुरुषसिंघ तिहु पुर उजिआरे॥ जिन्ह के जस प्रताप कें आगे। ससि मलीन रबि सीतल लागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1563.verse_hindi: आपके पुत्र पूछने योग्य नहीं हैं। वे पुरुषसिंह तीनों लोकों के प्रकाश स्वरूप हैं। जिनके यश के आगे चन्द्रमा मलिन और प्रताप के आगे सूर्य शीतल लगता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1563.english_translation: Your sons are beyond question. They are lion-like men, the light of all three worlds. Before their fame, the moon looks dim; before their brilliance, the sun feels cool.
ramacharitamanas::1563.translation_literal: पूछन जोगु (fit to be asked about) / न (not) / तनय (sons) / तुम्हारे (your) / पुरुषसिंघ (lion among men) / तिहु पुर (three worlds) / उजिआरे (radiance)॥ / जिन्ह (whose) / के (of) / जस (fame) / प्रताप (splendor, power) / कें आगे (before) / ससि (moon) / मलीन (dim) / रबि (sun) / सीतल (cool) / लागे (seems)॥
ramacharitamanas::1563.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1563.simple_meaning: King Janak's sons are so extraordinary that they hardly need to be identified. Their fame outshines the moon, and their power makes even the sun seem cool.
ramacharitamanas::1563.simple_insight: Some greatness is so clear that explanation becomes unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::1563.detailed_meaning: Janak's messengers are speaking in Mithila after hearing that Ram and Lakshman have arrived. They answer with praise, saying these princes are so radiant and famous that no further identification is needed. The verse lifts the scene from simple inquiry into reverent recognition.
ramacharitamanas::1563.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose work has already changed the room before they speak. No introduction feels needed, because their presence has done the explaining.
ramacharitamanas::1563.insight: It shifts attention from asking who they are to recognising what their presence reveals.

ramacharitamanas::1564.verse_sanskrit: तिन्ह कहँ कहिअ नाथ किमि चीन्हे। देखिअ रबि कि दीप कर लीन्हे॥ सीय स्वयंबर भूप अनेका। समिटे सुभट एक तें एका ॥
ramacharitamanas::1564.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! उनके लिए आप कहते हैं कि उन्हें कैसे पहचाना! क्या सूर्य को हाथ में दीपक लेकर देखा जाता है? सीताजी के स्वयंवर में अनेकों राजा और एक से एक बढ़कर योद्धा एकत्र हुए थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1564.english_translation: O Lord, how can they be recognized? Can the sun be seen with a lamp in hand? At Sita's swayamvar, many kings and warriors of every rank had gathered.
ramacharitamanas::1564.translation_literal: तिन्ह (those) / कहँ (for them) / कहिअ (is it said) / नाथ (O Lord) / किमि (how) / चीन्हे (to be recognized) / देखिअ (is seen) / रबि (sun) / कि (with?) / दीप (lamp) / कर (hand) / लीन्हे (taken) / सीय (Sita's) / स्वयंबर (swayamvar) / भूप (kings) / अनेका (many) / समिटे (assembled) / सुभट (warriors) / एक तें एका (one greater than another)
ramacharitamanas::1564.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1564.essence: Greatness cannot be judged by ordinary measures.
ramacharitamanas::1564.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana are so radiant that ordinary praise cannot measure them. The verse compares trying to identify the sun with a lamp, then shifts to the crowded swayamvar where many kings and warriors had gathered.
ramacharitamanas::1564.simple_insight: Some presence is too great to be measured by ordinary standards.
ramacharitamanas::1564.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Rama and Lakshmana have already been praised as unmatched. The messenger pushes the praise further: how can such men even be described? He then recalls the Sita swayamvar, where countless kings and warriors assembled to test themselves.
ramacharitamanas::1564.modern_relevance: You try to explain a leader, teacher, or parent who changed your life, and ordinary words feel too small. Some people are not measured by comparison; they make comparison look foolish.
ramacharitamanas::1564.insight: It shifts the mind from ranking greatness to recognising that true excellence outshines the usual scale.

ramacharitamanas::1565.verse_sanskrit: संभु सरासनु काहुँ न टारा। हारे सकल बीर बरिआरा॥ तीनि लोक महँ जे भटमानी। सभ कै सकति संभु धनु भानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1565.verse_hindi: परंतु शिवजी के धनुष को कोई भी नहीं हटा सका। सारे बलवान वीर हार गए। तीनों लोकों में जो वीरता के अभिमानी थे, शिवजी के धनुष ने सबकी शक्ति तोड़ दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1565.english_translation: No one could move Shiva's bow. All the mighty warriors were defeated. The proud fighters in the three worlds had their strength broken by Shiva's bow.
ramacharitamanas::1565.translation_literal: संभु (Shiva) / सरासनु (bow) / काहुँ (by anyone) / न (not) / टारा (moved) / हारे (defeated) / सकल (all) / बीर (warriors) / बरिआरा (mighty)॥ / तीनि (three) / लोक (worlds) / महँ (in) / जे (who) / भटमानी (proud fighters) / सभ (all) / कै (of) / सकति (strength) / संभु (Shiva's) / धनु (bow) / भानी (broke)॥
ramacharitamanas::1565.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1565.essence: Pride breaks before a power it cannot move.
ramacharitamanas::1565.simple_meaning: No warrior could lift or move Shiva's bow. The strongest fighters failed, and their pride was broken by it.
ramacharitamanas::1565.simple_insight: Pride collapses when it meets a force greater than itself.
ramacharitamanas::1565.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, kings and warriors from across the three worlds have gathered to win the contest. One by one, the proud and powerful fail before Shiva's bow. This verse records their defeat before Ram's arrival.
ramacharitamanas::1565.modern_relevance: A room full of confident people tries the same impossible task and then falls silent. The thing that looked like status reveals who can actually act.
ramacharitamanas::1565.insight: It shifts attention from brute confidence to real capacity under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::1566.verse_sanskrit: सकइ उठाइ सरासुर मेरू। सोउ हियँ हारि गयउ करि फेरू॥ जेहिं कौतुक सिवसैलु उठावा। सोउ तेहि सभाँ पराभउ पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1566.verse_hindi: बाणासुर, जो सुमेरु को भी उठा सकता था, वह भी हृदय में हारकर परिक्रमा करके चला गया और जिसने खेल से ही कैलास को उठा लिया था, वह रावण भी उस सभा में पराजय को प्राप्त हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1566.english_translation: Banaasura, who could lift Mount Meru, also turned back defeated in his heart. Ravana, who had once lifted Kailash in sport, was defeated in that assembly.
ramacharitamanas::1566.translation_literal: सकइ (was able) / उठाइ (to lift) / सरासुर (with gods and demons) / मेरू (Meru) / सोउ (he also) / हियँ (in heart) / हारि (defeated) / गयउ (went) / करि (doing) / फेरू (turning back) / जेहिं (by whom) / कौतुक (in play) / सिवसैलु (Shiva's mountain) / उठावा (was lifted) / सोउ (he also) / तेहि (that) / सभाँ (in the assembly) / पराभउ (defeat) / पावा (got)
ramacharitamanas::1566.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1566.essence: Great strength still bows before the moment that reveals its limit.
ramacharitamanas::1566.simple_meaning: Even the mightiest warriors failed before Shiva's bow. Their strength and pride could not carry them through that assembly.
ramacharitamanas::1566.simple_insight: Outer power means little when pride meets a test it cannot control.
ramacharitamanas::1566.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, famous warriors have already come and failed. Tulsidas now names two legendary strongmen, Banaasura and Ravana, to show how completely the contest humbled even the greatest powers before Ram's future bow-breaking moment.
ramacharitamanas::1566.modern_relevance: You walk into the room knowing you are the best prepared person there, and still the challenge exposes a limit you did not expect. Skill alone does not guarantee mastery.
ramacharitamanas::1566.insight: It shifts attention from raw strength to the humbling force of true testing.

ramacharitamanas::1567.verse_sanskrit: तहाँ राम रघुबंसमनि सुनिअ महा महिपाल। भंजेउ चाप प्रयास बिनु जिमि गज पंकज नाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1567.verse_hindi: हे महाराज! सुनिए, वहाँ (जहाँ ऐसे-ऐसे योद्धा हार मान गए) रघुवंशमणि श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने बिना ही प्रयास शिवजी के धनुष को वैसे ही तोड़ डाला जैसे हाथी कमल की डंडी को तोड़ डालता है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::1567.english_translation: There, O great king, hear of Ram, jewel of the Raghu line: without effort he broke Shiva's bow, just as an elephant breaks a lotus stalk.
ramacharitamanas::1567.translation_literal: तहाँ (there) / राम (Ram) / रघुबंसमनि (jewel of the Raghu line) / सुनिअ (hear) / महा महिपाल (great king) / भंजेउ (broke) / चाप (bow) / प्रयास बिनु (without effort) / जिमि (like) / गज (elephant) / पंकज नाल (lotus stalk)
ramacharitamanas::1567.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1567.simple_meaning: Ram broke Shiva's bow effortlessly, astonishing everyone who had failed before him.
ramacharitamanas::1567.simple_insight: Real strength does not strain to prove itself.
ramacharitamanas::1567.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, mighty warriors have already failed to lift Shiva's bow. Then Ram steps forward and breaks it without effort. The line heightens the wonder of his feat before Parashurama arrives in the next verse.
ramacharitamanas::1567.modern_relevance: Everyone else has already overcomplicated the problem. Then one calm person walks in, does the thing cleanly, and changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::1567.insight: It shifts attention from display of force to effortless mastery.

ramacharitamanas::1568.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सरोष भृगुनायकु आए। बहुत भाँति तिन्ह आँखि देखाए॥ देखि राम बलु निज धनु दीन्हा। करिबहु बिनय गवनु बन कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1568.verse_hindi: धनुष टूटने की बात सुनकर परशुरामजी क्रोध में भरे आए और उन्होंने बहुत प्रकार से आँखें दिखलाईं। अंत में उन्होंने भी श्री रामचन्द्रजी का बल देखकर उन्हें अपना धनुष दे दिया और बहुत प्रकार से विनती करके वन को गमन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1568.english_translation: Hearing that the bow had been broken, Parashurama came in fury and glared in many ways. Seeing Ram's strength, he handed over his own bow and, after much pleading, went back to the forest.
ramacharitamanas::1568.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सरोष (furious) / भृगुनायकु (leader of the Bhrigu line, Parashurama) / आए (came) / बहुत भाँति (in many ways) / तिन्ह (they) / आँखि देखाए (showed their eyes, glared) / देखि (seeing) / राम बलु (Ram's strength) / निज धनु (his own bow) / दीन्हा (gave) / करिबहु (having done much) / बिनय (pleading) / गवनु (departure) / बन (forest) / कीन्हा (made, went)
ramacharitamanas::1568.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1568.essence: True strength can end anger without becoming angry itself.
ramacharitamanas::1568.simple_meaning: Parashurama arrives angry after the bow is broken, but Ram's strength makes him yield. He gives up his bow, speaks respectfully, and leaves for the forest.
ramacharitamanas::1568.simple_insight: Real strength does not need to dominate. It can quiet anger without fighting it.
ramacharitamanas::1568.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the broken bow has drawn Parashurama into the scene. He comes blazing with pride and threat, but when he sees Ram's power, the confrontation ends differently than expected: the furious warrior softens, offers his bow, and withdraws.
ramacharitamanas::1568.modern_relevance: A tense room goes silent after one person speaks with calm authority. The argument does not need a winner; the strongest presence can end the fight by refusing to escalate it.
ramacharitamanas::1568.insight: It shifts the mind from proving power through aggression to recognizing power through restraint.

ramacharitamanas::1569.verse_sanskrit: राजन रामु अतुलबल जैसें। तेज निधान लखनु पुनि तैसें॥ कंपहिं भूप बिलोकत जाकें। जिमि गज हरि किसोर के ताकें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1569.verse_hindi: हे राजन् ! जैसे श्री रामचन्द्रजी अतुलनीय बली हैं, वैसे ही तेज निधान फिर लक्ष्मणजी भी हैं, जिनके देखने मात्र से राजा लोग ऐसे काँप उठते थे, जैसे हाथी सिंह के बच्चे के ताकने से काँप उठते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1569.english_translation: O king, Rama is immeasurably powerful, and Lakshmana too is a treasury of radiance. Kings tremble just by seeing them, like elephants trembling before a lion cub.
ramacharitamanas::1569.translation_literal: राजन (O king) / रामु (Rama) / अतुलबल (of immeasurable strength) / जैसें (just as) / तेज निधान (treasury of radiance) / लखनु (Lakshmana) / पुनि (also) / तैसें (likewise) / कंपहिं (tremble) / भूप (kings) / बिलोकत (seeing) / जाकें (whom) / जिमि (like) / गज (elephant) / हरि (lion) / किसोर (cub) / के (of) / ताकें (seeing)
ramacharitamanas::1569.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1569.essence: Their presence alone makes power tremble.
ramacharitamanas::1569.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana are so powerful that kings tremble just by looking at them. Their presence alone commands fear and respect.
ramacharitamanas::1569.simple_insight: Real strength needs no display. Its presence changes the room before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1569.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, after Ram has broken Shiva's bow, the assembly is still reeling. This verse pauses the action to describe the two brothers' overwhelming presence: Ram's unmatched strength and Lakshmana's blazing force make even kings tremble.
ramacharitamanas::1569.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting and nobody interrupts you, not because you spoke loudly, but because your calm is unmistakable. Some presence is stronger than force.
ramacharitamanas::1569.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic action to embodied authority: power can be felt before it is explained.

ramacharitamanas::1570.verse_sanskrit: देव देखि तव बालक दोऊ। अब न आँखि तर आवत कोऊ ॥ दूत बचन रचना प्रिय लागी। प्रेम प्रताप बीर रस पागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1570.verse_hindi: हे देव! आपके दोनों बालकों को देखने के बाद अब आँखों के नीचे कोई आता ही नहीं (हमारी दृष्टि पर कोई चढ़ता ही नहीं)। प्रेम, प्रताप और वीर रस में पगी हुई दूतों की वचन रचना सबको बहुत प्रिय लगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1570.english_translation: O divine one, after seeing your two boys, no one else now rises before our eyes. The envoys' words, woven with love, dignity, and heroic spirit, became dear to all.
