ramacharitamanas::1570.translation_literal: देव (divine one) / देखि (seeing) / तव (your) / बालक (boys/children) / दोऊ (both) / अब (now) / न (not) / आँखि (eye) / तर (under) / आवत (comes/rises) / कोऊ (anyone) / दूत (envoys) / बचन (words) / रचना (composition/weaving) / प्रिय (dear) / लागी (became) / प्रेम (love) / प्रताप (dignity/power) / बीर रस (heroic flavor) / पागी (saturated)
ramacharitamanas::1570.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1570.essence: Words filled with love and courage can disarm pride.
ramacharitamanas::1570.simple_meaning: The envoys speak so beautifully and forcefully that everyone is won over. After seeing Ram and Lakshman, no one dares to look down on them.
ramacharitamanas::1570.simple_insight: Respect changes the room faster than force. Clear, loving speech can soften even proud hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1570.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court after the bow has been broken, the envoys speak about Ram and Lakshman with grace, pride, and warmth. Their words carry such force that even the assembled kings are disarmed and moved.
ramacharitamanas::1570.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting where everyone is ready to argue. Then someone speaks with confidence, warmth, and precision, and the whole room relaxes. Strong words can change the atmosphere before any debate begins.
ramacharitamanas::1570.insight: It shifts attention from confrontation to persuasive presence, showing how speech can carry both dignity and affection.

ramacharitamanas::1571.verse_sanskrit: सभा समेत राउ अनुरागे। दूतन्ह देन निछावरि लागे॥ कहि अनीति ते मूदहिं काना। धरमु बिचारि सबहिं सुखु माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1571.verse_hindi: सभा सहित राजा प्रेम में मग्न हो गए और दूतों को निछावर देने लगे। (उन्हें निछावर देते देखकर) यह नीति विरुद्ध है, ऐसा कहकर दूत अपने हाथों से कान मूँदने लगे। धर्म को विचारकर (उनका धर्मयुक्त बर्ताव देखकर) सभी ने सुख माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1571.english_translation: The king and his assembled court were filled with affection and began offering gifts to the messengers. The messengers covered their ears, saying it was against custom. Thinking of righteousness, everyone felt pleased.
ramacharitamanas::1571.translation_literal: सभा समेत (with the court) / राउ (the king) / अनुरागे (filled with affection) / दूतन्ह (to the messengers) / देन (to give) / निछावरि (offerings) / लागे (began) / कहि (saying) / अनीति (against custom / improper) / ते (that) / मूदहिं (they cover) / काना (ears) / धरमु (righteousness) / बिचारि (considering) / सबहिं (everyone) / सुखु (happiness / contentment) / माना (felt)
ramacharitamanas::1571.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1571.essence: Affection becomes beautiful when it is guided by righteousness.
ramacharitamanas::1571.simple_meaning: The king and his court were so pleased that they wanted to honor the messengers. The messengers politely resisted, and everyone felt that the proper thing had been done.
ramacharitamanas::1571.simple_insight: Respect feels best when it stays within right conduct.
ramacharitamanas::1571.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the king and the assembled nobles are moved by the messengers' words and try to honor them with gifts. The messengers refuse excess as improper, and the room settles into the satisfaction of conduct that stays within dharma.
ramacharitamanas::1571.modern_relevance: At a wedding reception, someone tries to shower a guest with expensive gifts, but the guest gently refuses because it feels too much. The room relaxes when generosity and restraint stay in balance.
ramacharitamanas::1571.insight: It shows that even gratitude needs discernment, not impulse.

ramacharitamanas::1572.verse_sanskrit: तब उठि भूप बसिष्ट कहुँ दीन्हि पत्रिका जाई। कथा सुनाई गुरहि सब सादर दूत बोलाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1572.verse_hindi: तब राजा ने उठकर वशिष्ठजी के पास जाकर उन्हें पत्रिका दी और आदरपूर्वक दूतों को बुलाकर सारी कथा गुरुजी को सुना दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1572.english_translation: Then the king rose, went to Vashishtha, handed him the letter, and respectfully called the envoys to tell the whole story to the guru.
ramacharitamanas::1572.translation_literal: तब (then) / उठि (rising) / भूप (the king) / बसिष्ट कहुँ (to Vashishtha) / दीन्हि (gave) / पत्रिका (the letter) / जाई (going) / कथा (story) / सुनाई (told) / गुरहि (to the guru) / सब (all) / सादर (respectfully) / दूत (envoys) / बोलाइ (calling)
ramacharitamanas::1572.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1572.essence: Respectful order turns confusion into clarity.
ramacharitamanas::1572.simple_meaning: The king stands up, gives Vashishtha the message, and respectfully has the envoys explain everything to the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::1572.simple_insight: Respectful action keeps the whole situation clear and orderly.
ramacharitamanas::1572.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the king rises in the middle of the gathered court, takes the message to Vashishtha, and asks the envoys to explain the full matter. It is a brief scene of protocol and deference, not the verse's main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1572.modern_relevance: In a tense family group chat, you stop arguing, call the elder who can calm things, and let the facts be heard cleanly.
ramacharitamanas::1572.insight: It shifts attention from the heat of the moment to proper communication through the right channel.

ramacharitamanas::1573.verse_sanskrit: सुनि बोले गुर अति सुखु पाई। पुन्य पुरुष कहुँ महि सुख छाई॥ जिमि सरिता सागर महुँ जाहीं। जद्यपि ताहि कामना नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1573.verse_hindi: सब समाचार सुनकर और अत्यन्त सुख पाकर गुरु बोले- पुण्यात्मा पुरुष के लिए पृथ्वी सुखों से छाई हुई है। जैसे नदियाँ समुद्र में जाती हैं, यद्यपि समुद्र को नदी की कामना नहीं होती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1573.english_translation: Hearing this, the guru spoke with great joy: "For a virtuous person, the earth is filled with happiness. Like rivers going into the ocean, though the ocean does not desire them."
ramacharitamanas::1573.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / बोले (spoke) / गुर (the guru) / अति (greatly) / सुखु (joy) / पाई (having received) / पुन्य (virtuous) / पुरुष (person) / कहुँ (for) / महि (earth) / सुखु (happiness) / छाई (spread) / जिमि (like) / सरिता (rivers) / सागर (ocean) / महुँ (into) / जाहीं (go) / जद्यपि (although) / ताहि (to it) / कामना (desire) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::1573.speaker: Vasishtha
ramacharitamanas::1573.essence: Virtue draws its own abundance, without chasing it.
ramacharitamanas::1573.simple_meaning: The guru says that goodness draws happiness naturally, just as rivers flow into the ocean without the ocean asking for them.
ramacharitamanas::1573.simple_insight: You do not have to chase what is meant for a steady, righteous life.
ramacharitamanas::1573.detailed_meaning: After hearing the news, Vasishtha is delighted. He tells the gathered court that a life rooted in virtue naturally attracts good fortune, just as rivers flow toward the ocean without being summoned. The verse prepares the praise of Kaushalya and the blessing of righteous conduct.
ramacharitamanas::1573.modern_relevance: You stop forcing every outcome and notice how respect, support, and opportunities often gather around people who live cleanly and consistently.
ramacharitamanas::1573.insight: It shifts attention from grasping for results to becoming the kind of person to whom good things naturally come.

ramacharitamanas::1574.verse_sanskrit: तिमि सुख संपति बिनहिं बोलाएँ। धरमसील पहिं जाहिं सुभाएँ॥ तुम्ह गुर बिप्र धेनु सुर सेबी। तसि पुनीत कौसल्या देबी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1574.verse_hindi: वैसे ही सुख और सम्पत्ति बिना ही बुलाए स्वाभाविक ही धर्मात्मा पुरुष के पास जाती है। तुम जैसे गुरु, ब्राह्मण, गाय और देवता की सेवा करने वाले हो, वैसी ही पवित्र कौसल्यादेवी भी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1574.english_translation: Wealth and happiness come uncalled to the righteous. Pure Kaushalya is like the guru, the learned, the cow, and the radiant beings she serves.
ramacharitamanas::1574.translation_literal: तिमि (thus) / सुख (happiness) / संपति (wealth) / बिनहिं बोलाएँ (without being called) / धरमसील (righteous) / पहिं (to) / जाहिं (go) / सुभाएँ (by nature) ॥ / तुम्ह (you) / गुर (guru) / बिप्र (learned priest) / धेनु (cow) / सुर (radiant beings) / सेबी (serving) / तसि (like that) / पुनीत (pure) / कौसल्या (Kaushalya) / देबी (queen, revered lady) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1574.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1574.essence: Virtue draws its own rewards, and service makes a person pure.
ramacharitamanas::1574.simple_meaning: Good fortune naturally comes to people who live rightly. Kaushalya is praised as pure because she serves the teacher, the learned, cows, and radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::1574.simple_insight: A life shaped by service draws honour without chasing it.
ramacharitamanas::1574.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the king and his family are being praised for their virtue. The speaker says that prosperity naturally follows the righteous, then singles out Kaushalya as pure because her life is devoted to serving the guru, priests, cows, and radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::1574.modern_relevance: A family member quietly cares for elders, feeds guests, and never asks for credit. Years later, everyone trusts her first. Respect gathers around a life that serves well.
ramacharitamanas::1574.insight: It shifts attention from chasing status to becoming worthy of it through steady service.

ramacharitamanas::1575.verse_sanskrit: सुकृती तुम्ह समान जग माहीं। भयउ न है कोउ होनेउ नाहीं॥ तुम्ह ते अधिक पुन्य बड़ काकें। राजन राम सरिस सुत जाकें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1575.verse_hindi: तुम्हारे समान पुण्यात्मा जगत में न कोई हुआ, न है और न होने का ही है। हे राजन् ! तुमसे अधिक पुण्य और किसका होगा, जिसके राम सरीखे पुत्र हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1575.english_translation: There has been no one like you in the world, nor is there, nor will there be. O king, who could be more blessed than you, whose son is Ram himself?
ramacharitamanas::1575.translation_literal: सुकृती (virtuous/blessed) / तुम्ह (you) / समान (like) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / भयउ (was) / न (not) / है (is) / कोउ (anyone) / होनेउ (has been) / नाहीं (not) / तुम्ह (you) / ते (than) / अधिक (more) / पुन्य (merit) / बड़ (great) / काकें (whose) / राजन (O king) / राम (Ram) / सरिस (like) / सुत (son) / जाकें (whose)
ramacharitamanas::1575.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1575.essence: Having Ram as your son is the highest blessing imaginable.
ramacharitamanas::1575.simple_meaning: No one has ever been as blessed as you. Your great merit is shown by having Ram as your son.
ramacharitamanas::1575.simple_insight: Some blessings are so complete they make comparison feel impossible.
ramacharitamanas::1575.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the praise keeps building around Dasharath’s good fortune. The speaker declares that no one in the world matches his merit, because Ram himself has been born as his son. This verse crowns that blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1575.modern_relevance: A parent watches a child become the kind of person others trust instantly. The pride is not in achievement alone, but in the character that shines through them.
ramacharitamanas::1575.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary success to the deeper blessing of having children of noble character.

ramacharitamanas::1576.verse_sanskrit: बीर बिनीत धरम ब्रत धारी। गुन सागर बर बालक चारी॥ तुम्ह कहुँ सर्ब काल कल्याना। सजहु बरात बजाइ निसाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1576.verse_hindi: और जिसके चारों बालक वीर, विनम्र, धर्म का व्रत धारण करने वाले और गुणों के सुंदर समुद्र हैं। तुम्हारे लिए सभी कालों में कल्याण है। अतएव डंका बजवाकर बारात सजाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1576.english_translation: And whose four sons are brave, humble, bound to righteousness, and oceans of noble qualities. For you, all times are auspicious. So prepare the wedding procession and have the drums beaten.
ramacharitamanas::1576.translation_literal: बीर (brave) / बिनीत (humble) / धरम (righteousness) / ब्रत धारी (vow-holders) / गुन सागर (oceans of qualities) / बर बालक चारी (four excellent boys) / तुम्ह कहुँ (for you) / सर्ब काल (all times) / कल्याना (auspiciousness) / सजहु (prepare) / बरात (wedding procession) / बजाइ (beating) / निसाना (drums, battle-signal drums)
ramacharitamanas::1576.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1576.essence: Character itself makes the moment auspicious.
ramacharitamanas::1576.simple_meaning: The king's four sons are praised as brave, humble, righteous, and full of virtues. Because of that, the wedding is declared fully auspicious and ready to begin.
ramacharitamanas::1576.simple_insight: Real honor comes from character so complete that even celebration feels blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1576.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the marriage negotiations for Ram and his brothers are reaching their peak. The speaker praises Dasharath's four sons as brave, humble, disciplined, and rich in virtue, then announces that the moment is entirely auspicious and the wedding procession should be prepared.
ramacharitamanas::1576.modern_relevance: A parent hears strangers speak with admiration about a child who has grown steady, kind, and reliable. The praise is not for talent alone, but for a character that makes every next step feel right.
ramacharitamanas::1576.insight: It shifts attention from appearance or status to the deeper qualities that make a life fit for sacred commitment.

ramacharitamanas::1577.verse_sanskrit: चलहु बेगि सुनि गुर बचन भलेहिं नाथ सिरु नाई। भूपति गवने भवन तब दूतन्ह बासु देवाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1577.verse_hindi: और जल्दी चलो। गुरुजी के ऐसे वचन सुनकर, हे नाथ! बहुत अच्छा कहकर और सिर नवाकर तथा दूतों को डेरा दिलवाकर राजा महल में गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1577.english_translation: Then the king said, 'Depart at once.' Hearing the guru's gracious words, he bowed his head, praised them, and returned to the palace after arranging lodging for the messengers.
ramacharitamanas::1577.translation_literal: चलहु (go) / बेगि (quickly) / सुनि (hearing) / गुर (guru's) / बचन (words) / भलेहिं (graciously) / नाथ (lord) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing) / भूपति (the king) / गवने (went) / भवन (to the palace) / तब (then) / दूतन्ह (for the messengers) / बासु (lodging) / देवाइ (having arranged)
ramacharitamanas::1577.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1577.essence: True courtesy turns hearing into immediate, orderly action.
ramacharitamanas::1577.simple_meaning: The king accepts the guru's words, bows respectfully, makes arrangements for the messengers, and returns to the palace.
ramacharitamanas::1577.simple_insight: Respect does not stay in the heart alone; it shows up in action.
ramacharitamanas::1577.detailed_meaning: Janak has just heard the praise of Dasharath's family and the promise of Ram's marriage. He responds with humility, bows to the guru's words, and sends the messengers back with proper care before returning inside. The scene moves the wedding preparations forward.
ramacharitamanas::1577.modern_relevance: A message arrives that changes everything, and you do not rush to perform. You listen fully, bow to what is wise, handle the practical details, and only then move on.
ramacharitamanas::1577.insight: It teaches respectful response: hear well, act properly, and do not let excitement replace etiquette.

ramacharitamanas::1578.verse_sanskrit: राजा सबु रनिवास बोलाई। जनक पत्रिका बाचि सुनाई॥ सुनि संदेसु सकल हरषानीं। अपर कथा सब भूप बखानीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1578.verse_hindi: राजा ने सारे रनिवास को बुलाकर जनकजी की पत्रिका बाँचकर सुनाई। समाचार सुनकर सब रानियाँ हर्ष से भर गईं। राजा ने फिर दूसरी सब बातों का (जो दूतों के मुख से सुनी थीं) वर्णन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1578.english_translation: The king called all the queens and read Janak's letter aloud. Hearing the message, all were filled with joy. Then the king recounted the rest of what the messengers had said.
ramacharitamanas::1578.translation_literal: राजा (the king) / सबु (all) / रनिवास (the inner palace women) / बोलाई (called) / जनक (Janak's) / पत्रिका (letter) / बाचि (reading) / सुनाई (made heard)॥ / सुनि (hearing) / संदेसु (message) / सकल (all) / हरषानीं (rejoiced)॥ / अपर (other) / कथा (talks) / सब (all) / भूप (the king) / बखानीं (described) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1578.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1578.essence: Good news becomes fuller when it is spoken aloud.
ramacharitamanas::1578.simple_meaning: The king shares Janak's letter with the queens, and they all rejoice at the good news.
ramacharitamanas::1578.simple_insight: Joy grows when good news is shared with everyone at once.
ramacharitamanas::1578.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyā, King Dasharath gathers the queens and reads Janak's letter aloud. The message confirms the marriage arrangements, and the whole inner palace fills with happiness. This verse simply shows the news spreading through the royal household.
ramacharitamanas::1578.modern_relevance: You open the family group chat and read out the message everyone was waiting for. The room changes instantly — shoulders drop, faces brighten, and relief becomes shared.
ramacharitamanas::1578.insight: It shows how a single clear message can turn private relief into collective joy.

ramacharitamanas::1579.verse_sanskrit: प्रेम प्रफुल्लित राजहिं रानी। मनहुँ सिखिनि सुनि बारिद बानी॥ मुदित असीस देहिं गुर नारीं। अति आनंद मगन महतारीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1579.verse_hindi: प्रेम में प्रफुल्लित हुई रानियाँ ऐसी सुशोभित हो रही हैं, जैसे मोरनी बादलों की गरज सुनकर प्रफुल्लित होती हैं। बड़ी-बूढ़ी (अथवा गुरुओं की) स्त्रियाँ प्रसन्न होकर आशीर्वाद दे रही हैं। माताएँ अत्यन्त आनंद में मग्न हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1579.english_translation: The queens, filled with love, bloom with joy like peahens hearing the sound of rain. The elder women give cheerful blessings, and the mothers are lost in delight.
ramacharitamanas::1579.translation_literal: प्रेम (love) / प्रफुल्लित (blooming with joy) / राजहिं (the queens) / रानी (queens) / मनहुँ (as if) / सिखिनि (peahens) / सुनि (hearing) / बारिद (rain cloud) / बानी (sound/voice) / मुदित (happy) / असीस (blessings) / देहिं (give) / गुर (elders/teachers) / नारीं (women) / अति (very) / आनंद (joy) / मगन (immersed) / महतारीं (mothers)
ramacharitamanas::1579.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1579.essence: Love makes the whole house bloom at once.
ramacharitamanas::1579.simple_meaning: The queens and older women are overjoyed at the news. They bless the event and celebrate together like peahens delighting in rain.
ramacharitamanas::1579.simple_insight: Joy spreads instantly when hope becomes real.
ramacharitamanas::1579.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath’s household has just heard Janak’s message about the marriage proposal. The queens, elder women, and mothers overflow with delight, blessing the news before the next line shows them embracing the letter itself.
ramacharitamanas::1579.modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with the message you were waiting for, and the whole room changes. Relief, laughter, and blessing rush out before anyone can even sit down.
ramacharitamanas::1579.insight: It shows how hopeful news can turn a household into shared celebration.

ramacharitamanas::1580.verse_sanskrit: लेहिं परस्पर अति प्रिय पाती। हृदयँ लगाई जुड़ावहिं छाती॥ राम लखन कै कीरति करनी। बारहिं बार भूपबर बरनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1580.verse_hindi: उस अत्यन्त प्रिय पत्रिका को आपस में लेकर सब हृदय से लगाकर छाती शीतल करती हैं। राजाओं में श्रेष्ठ दशरथजी ने श्री राम-लक्ष्मण की कीर्ति और करनी का बारंबार वर्णन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1580.english_translation: They take the dear letter from one another, press it to their hearts, and soothe their chests. King Dasharath again and again describes the fame and deeds of Ram and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::1580.translation_literal: लेहिं (they take) / परस्पर (from one another) / अति प्रिय (very dear) / पाती (letter) / हृदयँ लगाई (having pressed to the heart) / जुड़ावहिं (they soothe) / छाती (chest) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / कै (of) / कीरति (fame) / करनी (deeds) / बारहिं बार (again and again) / भूपबर (best among kings) / बरनी (described)
ramacharitamanas::1580.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1580.essence: A beloved message can steady the heart more than presence.
ramacharitamanas::1580.simple_meaning: The queens cherish Janak's message and calm their hearts with it. Dasharath keeps praising Ram and Lakshman's virtues and renown.
ramacharitamanas::1580.simple_insight: Love makes a message feel like a presence, not just words.
ramacharitamanas::1580.detailed_meaning: After hearing Janak's message, the queens hold the letter close and feel their hearts cool. In the palace, Dasharath keeps speaking of Ram and Lakshman's fame, while everyone waits in rising joy for what comes next.
ramacharitamanas::1580.modern_relevance: You reread a message from someone you love, holding the phone to your chest for a second. The words are simple, but they steady you anyway.
ramacharitamanas::1580.insight: It shows how devotion can turn a message into emotional nourishment.

ramacharitamanas::1581.verse_sanskrit: मुनि प्रसादु कहि द्वार सिधाए। रानिन्ह तब महिदेव बोलाए॥ दिए दान आनंद समेता। चले बिप्रबर आसिष देता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1581.verse_hindi: 'यह सब मुनि की कृपा है' ऐसा कहकर वे बाहर चले आए। तब रानियों ने ब्राह्मणों को बुलाया और आनंद सहित उन्हें दान दिए। श्रेष्ठ ब्राह्मण आशीर्वाद देते हुए चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1581.english_translation: Saying, “This is the grace of the sage,” they went out. Then the queens called the Brahmins and gave gifts with joy. The best Brahmins departed, giving blessings.
ramacharitamanas::1581.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / प्रसादु (grace) / कहि (saying) / द्वार (door) / सिधाए (went out) / रानिन्ह (by the queens) / तब (then) / महिदेव (Brahmins, revered ones) / बोलाए (were called) / दिए (gave) / दान (gifts) / आनंद (joy) / समेता (together with) / चले (went) / बिप्रबर (best Brahmins) / आसिष (blessings) / देता (giving)
ramacharitamanas::1581.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1581.essence: Joy becomes complete when it is shared as generosity.
ramacharitamanas::1581.simple_meaning: The queens thank the sage, call the Brahmins, and give generous gifts with joy. The Brahmins leave after blessing them.
ramacharitamanas::1581.simple_insight: Gratitude becomes giving. Joy deepens when it is shared through generosity and blessings.
ramacharitamanas::1581.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the queens are overflowing with happiness after the holy news. They step out, credit the sage’s grace, summon the Brahmins, and give gifts with delight. Their joy turns immediately into honour and charity.
ramacharitamanas::1581.modern_relevance: You get the good news, and your first impulse is not to hoard the happiness. You call the people who helped, feed them, thank them, and let the joy move outward.
ramacharitamanas::1581.insight: It shifts celebration from private pleasure to grateful giving.

ramacharitamanas::1582.verse_sanskrit: जाचक लिए हँकारि दीन्हि निछावरि कोटि बिधि। चिरु जीवहुँ सुत चारि चक्रबर्ति दसरत्थ के ॥
ramacharitamanas::1582.verse_hindi: फिर भिक्षुकों को बुलाकर करोड़ों प्रकार की निछावरें उनको दीं। 'चक्रवर्ती महाराज दशरथ के चारों पुत्र चिरंजीवी हों' ॥
ramacharitamanas::1582.english_translation: They called the beggars and gave them countless gifts. “May the four sons of Emperor Dasharath live long!”
ramacharitamanas::1582.translation_literal: जाचक (beggars) / लिए (having called) / हँकारि (summoned) / दीन्हि (gave) / निछावरि (gifts offered in blessing) / कोटि बिधि (in millions of ways) / चिरु (long) / जीवहुँ (may live) / सुत (sons) / चारि (four) / चक्रबर्ति (emperor) / दसरत्थ के (of Dasharath)
ramacharitamanas::1582.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1582.essence: True joy gives first and blesses others freely.
ramacharitamanas::1582.simple_meaning: The royal family gives lavish gifts to beggars and blesses Dasharath’s four sons with long life.
ramacharitamanas::1582.simple_insight: Joy becomes generous here. Celebration is not just felt; it is shared outward in gifts and blessings.
ramacharitamanas::1582.detailed_meaning: Dasharath’s house overflows with happiness after the princes’ birth. The queens call in beggars and give generous gifts, then bless all four sons to live long. The scene shows how a king’s joy spills into public celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1582.modern_relevance: A family announces a long-awaited baby and the whole house turns festive: sweets, gifts, blessings, phone calls. The happiness feels too big to keep inside, so it becomes shared abundance.
ramacharitamanas::1582.insight: It shifts celebration from private pleasure to generous blessing.

ramacharitamanas::1583.verse_sanskrit: कहत चले पहिरें पट नाना। हरषि हने गहगहे निसाना॥ समाचार सब लोगन्ह पाए। लागे घर-घर होन बधाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1583.verse_hindi: यों कहते हुए वे अनेक प्रकार के सुंदर वस्त्र पहन-पहनकर चले। आनंदित होकर नगाड़े वालों ने बड़े जोर से नगाड़ों पर चोट लगाई। सब लोगों ने जब यह समाचार पाया, तब घर-घर बधावे होने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1583.english_translation: Saying this, they walked on in many kinds of fine clothes. Joyful drummers struck the drums with great force. When all the people heard the news, celebrations began in every home.
ramacharitamanas::1583.translation_literal: कहत (saying) / चले (went) / पहिरें (wearing) / पट (cloths) / नाना (many kinds) / हरषि (joyfully) / हने (struck) / गहगहे (loudly) / निसाना (drums) / समाचार (news) / सब (all) / लोगन्ह (people) / पाए (received) / लागे (began) / घर-घर (in every house) / होन (to happen) / बधाए (celebrations)
ramacharitamanas::1583.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1583.essence: Joy announces itself before the wedding even begins.
ramacharitamanas::1583.simple_meaning: The people dress up, drums sound loudly, and the whole city starts celebrating the news.
ramacharitamanas::1583.simple_insight: Joy spreads outward fast when something truly wonderful arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1583.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the wedding news has already begun to spread. People put on fine clothes, drums thunder through the streets, and every household starts celebrating before the full event is even announced.
ramacharitamanas::1583.modern_relevance: A message hits the family group chat, and within minutes everyone is calling relatives, changing plans, and smiling at their phones. Some news turns a whole neighborhood alive at once.
ramacharitamanas::1583.insight: It shifts attention from private excitement to collective joy that reshapes an entire community.

ramacharitamanas::1584.verse_sanskrit: भुवन चारिदस भरा उछाहू। जनकसुता रघुबीर बिआहू॥ सुनि सुभ कथा लोग अनुरागे। मग गृह गलीं सँवारन लागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1584.verse_hindi: चौदहों लोकों में उत्साह भर गया कि जानकीजी और श्री रघुनाथजी का विवाह होगा। यह शुभ समाचार पाकर लोग प्रेममग्न हो गए और रास्ते, घर तथा गलियाँ सजाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1584.english_translation: The fourteen worlds filled with joy: Janaki and Raghubir were to be married. Hearing this auspicious news, people fell in love with the moment and began decorating roads, homes, and lanes.
ramacharitamanas::1584.translation_literal: भुवन (worlds) / चारिदस (fourteen) / भरा (filled) / उछाहू (joy) / जनकसुता (daughter of Janak) / रघुबीर (Raghu's hero, Ram) / बिआहू (marriage) / सुनि (hearing) / सुभ (auspicious) / कथा (news/story) / लोग (people) / अनुरागे (became loving/devoted) / मग (roads) / गृह (homes) / गलीं (lanes) / सँवारन (to decorate) / लागे (began)
ramacharitamanas::1584.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1584.essence: Joy spreads so widely that the whole city starts to celebrate.
ramacharitamanas::1584.simple_meaning: News of Ram and Sita’s wedding spreads everywhere. Everyone feels joy and starts decorating the city.
ramacharitamanas::1584.simple_insight: Shared joy makes even streets and homes feel alive.
ramacharitamanas::1584.detailed_meaning: As Ram and Sita's wedding draws near in Mithila, the news ripples through the whole world. People are so delighted that they begin decorating roads, houses, and lanes, turning the city itself into a celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1584.modern_relevance: A wedding invitation hits the family group chat, and suddenly cousins, neighbors, and friends are rearranging chairs, hanging lights, and smiling for no reason. Joy becomes collective before the event even begins.
ramacharitamanas::1584.insight: It turns a private union into a shared celebration that transforms the whole environment.

ramacharitamanas::1585.verse_sanskrit: जद्यपि अवध सदैव सुहावनि। रामपुरी मंगलमय पावनि॥ तदपि प्रीति कै प्रीति सुहाई। मंगल रचना रची बनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1585.verse_hindi: यद्यपि अयोध्या सदा सुहावनी है, क्योंकि वह श्री रामजी की मंगलमयी पवित्र पुरी है, तथापि प्रीति पर प्रीति होने से वह सुंदर मंगल रचना से सजाई गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1585.english_translation: Although Ayodhya is always lovely, for it is Ram's auspicious and purifying city, it was decorated with even more beauty out of love for love.
ramacharitamanas::1585.translation_literal: जद्यपि (although) / अवध (Ayodhya) / सदैव (always) / सुहावनि (beautiful) / रामपुरी (Ram's city) / मंगलमय (full of auspiciousness) / पावनि (purifying) / तदपि (still) / प्रीति (love) / कै (of) / प्रीति (love) / सुहाई (pleasing) / मंगल (auspicious) / रचना (arrangement) / रची (made) / बनाई (formed)
ramacharitamanas::1585.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1585.essence: Love makes even perfection feel worth beautifying again.
ramacharitamanas::1585.simple_meaning: Ayodhya is already holy and beautiful because of Ram, yet the wedding joy makes people decorate it even more lavishly.
ramacharitamanas::1585.simple_insight: Love does not settle for enough; it keeps expressing itself in beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1585.detailed_meaning: The wedding of Sita and Ram is being prepared in Ayodhya. Even though the city already shines as Ram's sacred home, the people add fresh decorations everywhere. Their joy keeps multiplying into more joy.
ramacharitamanas::1585.modern_relevance: You clean the house before guests arrive, then still add flowers, lights, and fresh cloth because the occasion matters. Love turns a good setting into a memorable one.
ramacharitamanas::1585.insight: It shifts attention from mere usefulness to joyful abundance in how love is expressed.

ramacharitamanas::1586.verse_sanskrit: ध्वज पताक पट चामर चारू। छावा परम बिचित्र बजारू॥ कनक कलस तोरन मनि जाला। हरद दूब दधि अच्छत माला ॥
ramacharitamanas::1586.verse_hindi: ध्वजा, पताका, परदे और सुंदर चँवरों से सारा बाजा बहुत ही अनूठा छाया हुआ है। सोने के कलश, तोरण, मणियों की झालरें, हलदी, दूब, दही, अक्षत और मालाओं से- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1586.english_translation: Flags, banners, silk canopies, and beautiful fly-whisks covered the whole market. Golden pots, arches of leaves, garlands of jewels, turmeric, durva grass, curd, rice, and flower garlands adorned it all.
ramacharitamanas::1586.translation_literal: ध्वज (flags) / पताक (banners) / पट (cloths, silk hangings) / चामर (fly-whisks) / चारू (beautiful) / छावा (covered) / परम (very) / बिचित्र (wonderful, varied) / बजारू (market) / कनक (gold) / कलस (pots) / तोरन (arches, festoons) / मनि (jewels) / जाला (net, lattice, garlands) / हरद (turmeric) / दूब (durva grass) / दधि (curd) / अच्छत (unbroken rice) / माला (garlands)
ramacharitamanas::1586.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1586.essence: A wedding can make an entire city shine with auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::1586.simple_meaning: The marketplace is richly decorated with flags, banners, canopies, gold pots, garlands, turmeric, durva grass, curd, rice, and flowers for the wedding celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1586.simple_insight: Joy becomes visible when people turn an ordinary place into a sacred celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1586.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is preparing for Ram and Sita's wedding. The streets, market, and entrances are dressed in festive symbols and auspicious offerings. This verse adds the visual richness of the city-wide celebration before the actual marriage begins.
ramacharitamanas::1586.modern_relevance: A neighborhood strings lights across the lane for a wedding, and even the smallest shopfront looks transformed. Shared joy changes the whole atmosphere before a single ritual starts.
ramacharitamanas::1586.insight: It shows how collective celebration can sanctify a whole city, not just a single house.

ramacharitamanas::1587.verse_sanskrit: मंगलमय निज निज भवन लोगन्ह रचे बनाइ। बीथीं सींचीं चतुरसम चौकें चारु पुराइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1587.verse_hindi: लोगों ने अपने-अपने घरों को सजाकर मंगलमय बना लिया। गलियों को चतुर सम से सींचा और (द्वारों पर) सुंदर चौक पुराए। (चंदन, केशर, कस्तूरी और कपूर से बने हुए एक सुगंधित द्रव को चतुरसम कहते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1587.english_translation: People decorated their own homes and made them auspicious. They sprinkled the streets with fragrant water and filled the doorways with beautiful designs.
ramacharitamanas::1587.translation_literal: मंगलमय (auspicious) / निज निज (each one's own) / भवन (home) / लोगन्ह (by the people) / रचे बनाइ (made and arranged) / बीथीं (streets) / सींचीं (sprinkled) / चतुरसम (fragrant mixture) / चौकें (courtyard designs) / चारु (beautifully) / पुराइ (filled)
ramacharitamanas::1587.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1587.essence: Joy makes even streets and homes feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::1587.simple_meaning: The city is being decorated everywhere. People are preparing their homes and streets with beauty and fragrance.
ramacharitamanas::1587.simple_insight: Shared joy can transform an ordinary street into something luminous.
ramacharitamanas::1587.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is preparing for Ram's return. People are beautifying their homes, sprinkling the streets, and decorating every doorway. The verse lingers on the atmosphere of collective celebration before the next scene unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::1587.modern_relevance: A neighborhood hangs lights before a festival, and even the quietest house feels included. Beauty spreads fastest when everyone joins in.
ramacharitamanas::1587.insight: It shifts attention from private celebration to a whole community lifted by one arrival.

ramacharitamanas::1588.verse_sanskrit: जहँ तहँ जूथ जूथ मिलि भामिनि। सजि नव सप्त सकल दुति दामिनि॥ बिधुबदनीं मृग सावक लोचनि। निज सरूप रति मानु बिमोचनि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1588.verse_hindi: बिजली की सी कांति वाली चन्द्रमुखी, हरिन के बच्चे के से नेत्र वाली और अपने सुंदर रूप से कामदेव की स्त्री रति के अभिमान को छुड़ाने वाली सुहागिनी स्त्रियाँ सभी सोलहों श्रृंगार सजकर, जहाँ-तहाँ झुंड की झुंड मिलकर, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1588.english_translation: Wherever one looked, married women gathered in groups, adorned with the sixteen ornaments, shining like lightning. Their moon-like faces, deer-calf eyes, and beauty seemed to humble even Rati's pride in her own form.
ramacharitamanas::1588.translation_literal: जहँ तहँ (here and there) / जूथ जूथ (group by group) / मिलि (having gathered) / भामिनि (married women) / सजि (adorned) / नव सप्त (nine and seven; sixteen) / सकल (all) / दुति (radiance) / दामिनि (lightning) / बिधुबदनीं (moon-faced women) / मृग सावक (deer cub) / लोचनि (eyes) / निज सरूप (their own beauty/form) / रति (Rati) / मानु (pride) / बिमोचनि (removing, humbling)
ramacharitamanas::1588.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1588.essence: The whole city glows with the expectancy of a sacred celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1588.simple_meaning: The city is full of beautifully dressed married women gathered everywhere, glowing like lightning. Their faces, eyes, and grace are so striking that even the pride of beauty itself seems defeated.
ramacharitamanas::1588.simple_insight: Beauty can fill a place so completely that it feels almost sacred and unreal.
ramacharitamanas::1588.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the wedding celebration has begun. Women across the city gather in decorated groups, fully adorned for the auspicious event. Tulsidas lingers on their beauty to build the atmosphere before the songs and praises of the palace appear.
ramacharitamanas::1588.modern_relevance: A wedding venue before the guests arrive: lights strung up, relatives in bright clothes, everyone moving in little clusters. The scene itself announces that something blessed and unforgettable is about to happen.
ramacharitamanas::1588.insight: It teaches you to see how setting and mood prepare the heart before the main event arrives.

ramacharitamanas::1589.verse_sanskrit: गावहिं मंगल मंजुल बानीं। सुनि कल रव कलकंठि लजानीं॥ भूप भवन किमि जाइ बखाना। बिस्व बिमोहन रचेउ बिताना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1589.verse_hindi: मनोहर वाणी से मंगल गीत गा रही हैं, जिनके सुंदर स्वर को सुनकर कोयलें भी लजा जाती हैं। राजमहल का वर्णन कैसे किया जाए, जहाँ विश्व को विमोहित करने वाला मंडप बनाया गया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1589.english_translation: They sing auspicious songs in lovely voices; even the cuckoo is shamed by their sweet sound. How can one describe the royal palace, where a canopy has been raised to enchant the world?
ramacharitamanas::1589.translation_literal: गावहिं (they sing) / मंगल (auspicious) / मंजुल (lovely) / बानीं (voices) / सुनि (hearing) / कल (sweet) / रव (sound) / कलकंठि (cuckoos) / लजानीं (are shamed) / भूप (king's) / भवन (palace) / किमि (how) / जाइ (can be gone) / बखाना (described) / बिस्व (world) / बिमोहन (enchanting) / रचेउ (made) / बिताना (canopy)
ramacharitamanas::1589.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1589.essence: A celebration so beautiful it outshines comparison.
ramacharitamanas::1589.simple_meaning: Women sing auspicious songs so beautifully that even cuckoos seem inferior. The palace is so splendid that it seems made to enchant the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::1589.simple_insight: Beauty can be so complete that ordinary comparison falls away.
ramacharitamanas::1589.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is being prepared for Ram's wedding. Women sing auspicious songs, the palace glows with festive splendor, and the scene keeps building toward the ceremony. This verse is part of the vivid setting, not the main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1589.modern_relevance: A home is being dressed for a wedding, and every corner feels alive with music, color, and anticipation. Some moments are too full to summarize; they can only be entered.
ramacharitamanas::1589.insight: It invites the reader to feel the atmosphere before the event itself arrives.

ramacharitamanas::1590.verse_sanskrit: मंगल द्रब्य मनोहर नाना। राजत बाजत बिपुल निसाना॥ कतहुँ बिरिद बंदी उच्चरहीं। कतहुँ बेद धुनि भूसुर करहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1590.verse_hindi: अनेकों प्रकार के मनोहर मांगलिक पदार्थ शोभित हो रहे हैं और बहुत से नगाड़े बज रहे हैं। कहीं भाट विरुदावली (कुलकीर्ति) का उच्चारण कर रहे हैं और कहीं ब्राह्मण वेदध्वनि कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1590.english_translation: Many kinds of auspicious offerings shone there, and many drums resounded. Somewhere bards recited praises, and somewhere Brahmins chanted the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::1590.translation_literal: मंगल (auspicious) / द्रब्य (offerings) / मनोहर (beautiful) / नाना (many kinds) / राजत (shining) / बाजत (resounding) / बिपुल (many) / निसाना (drums) / कतहुँ (somewhere) / बिरिद (praise) / बंदी (bards) / उच्चरहीं (were reciting) / कतहुँ (somewhere) / बेद (Vedas) / धुनि (chant) / भूसुर (Brahmins) / करहीं (were doing)
ramacharitamanas::1590.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1590.essence: Celebration fills the palace before the decisive moment arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1590.simple_meaning: The palace is filled with auspicious gifts, drumbeats, praise-singers, and Vedic chants. It is a scene of celebration, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1590.simple_insight: Some moments are meant to be entered with wonder, not analyzed.
ramacharitamanas::1590.detailed_meaning: The Sita-swayamvar celebration is swelling inside Janak's palace. Beautiful offerings, drums, praise-singers, and Brahmins chanting fill every corner. Tulsidas is still painting the festive atmosphere before the decisive moment arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1590.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall before the ceremony begins. Music, flowers, voices, and ritual fill the room before anyone speaks a word. The atmosphere itself tells you something important is about to happen.
ramacharitamanas::1590.insight: It trains attention on atmosphere and ritual detail, preparing the reader for the coming turning point.

ramacharitamanas::1591.verse_sanskrit: गावहिं सुंदरि मंगल गीता। लै लै नामु रामु अरु सीता॥ बहुत उछाहु भवनु अति थोरा। मानहुँ उमगि चला चहु ओरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1591.verse_hindi: सुंदरी स्त्रियाँ श्री रामजी और श्री सीताजी का नाम ले-लेकर मंगलगीत गा रही हैं। उत्साह बहुत है और महल अत्यन्त ही छोटा है। इससे (उसमें न समाकर) मानो वह उत्साह (आनंद) चारों ओर उमड़ चला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1591.english_translation: Beautiful women sing auspicious songs, taking the names of Ram and Sita again and again. Joy is so great that the palace feels too small, as if that joy is spilling out in every direction.
ramacharitamanas::1591.translation_literal: गावहिं (sing) / सुंदरि (beautiful women) / मंगल (auspicious) / गीता (songs) / लै लै (taking again and again) / नामु (name) / रामु (Ram) / अरु (and) / सीता (Sita) / बहुत (much) / उछाहु (joy) / भवनु (house/palace) / अति (very) / थोरा (small) / मानहुँ (as if) / उमगि (surging) / चला (moved) / चहु ओरा (in all four directions)
ramacharitamanas::1591.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1591.essence: Joy in Ram and Sita spills beyond every boundary.
ramacharitamanas::1591.simple_meaning: Women in the palace sing Ram and Sita's names with great joy. The celebration feels so full that the whole palace seems to overflow with it.
ramacharitamanas::1591.simple_insight: Joy becomes larger than the room that holds it.
ramacharitamanas::1591.detailed_meaning: In Dasharath's palace, the wedding celebration is in full bloom. Women sing auspicious songs for Ram and Sita, and the happiness is so intense that the palace itself seems too small for it.
ramacharitamanas::1591.modern_relevance: At a wedding hall packed with music, flowers, and laughter, the feeling is bigger than the venue. Some joy does not fit inside walls; it spills into everyone present.
ramacharitamanas::1591.insight: It turns a festive scene into a picture of overflowing joy, not private emotion.

ramacharitamanas::1592.verse_sanskrit: सोभा दसरथ भवन कइ को कबि बरनै पार। जहाँ सकल सुर सीस मनि राम लीन्ह अवतार ॥
ramacharitamanas::1592.verse_hindi: दशरथ के महल की शोभा का वर्णन कौन कवि कर सकता है, जहाँ समस्त देवताओं के शिरोमणि रामचन्द्रजी ने अवतार लिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1592.english_translation: Who can describe the splendour of Dasharath's palace, where Ram, the crown jewel of all radiant beings, took birth?
ramacharitamanas::1592.translation_literal: सोभा (splendour) / दसरथ भवन (Dasharath's palace) / कइ (of) / को (who) / कबि (poet) / बरनै (can describe) / पार (fully) / जहाँ (where) / सकल (all) / सुर (radiant beings) / सीस मनि (crown jewel) / राम (Ram) / लीन्ह (took) / अवतार (incarnation)
ramacharitamanas::1592.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1592.essence: Ram's arrival makes even a palace beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::1592.simple_meaning: Dasharath's palace is beyond description because Ram has taken birth there, making it supremely blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1592.simple_insight: Some places become unforgettable because of who enters them.
ramacharitamanas::1592.detailed_meaning: The birth celebration is underway in Dasharath's palace. Music, songs, and auspicious signs fill the air. Tulsidas pauses to say that no poet can fully describe its splendour, because Ram himself has appeared there.
ramacharitamanas::1592.modern_relevance: A hospital room feels different the moment a child is born there. The walls are the same, but one arrival turns an ordinary place into a lifelong memory.
ramacharitamanas::1592.insight: It shifts attention from the setting itself to the sacred meaning created by Ram's presence.

ramacharitamanas::1593.verse_sanskrit: भूप भरत पुनि लिए बोलाई। हय गयस्यंदन साजहु जाई॥ चलहु बेगि रघुबीर बराता। सुनत पुलक पूरे दोउ भ्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1593.verse_hindi: फिर राजा ने भरतजी को बुला लिया और कहा कि जाकर घोड़े, हाथी और रथ सजाओ, जल्दी रामचन्द्रजी की बारात में चलो। यह सुनते ही दोनों भाई (भरतजी और शत्रुघ्नजी) आनंदवश पुलक से भर गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1593.english_translation: King Bharata was called again and told, "Go and prepare the horses, elephants, and chariots. Quickly set out for Raghuvir's wedding procession." Hearing this, both brothers were filled with delight and thrilled with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1593.translation_literal: भूप (king) / भरत (Bharata) / पुनि (again) / लिए (called) / बोलाई (having called) / हय (horses) / गय (elephants) / स्यंदन (chariots) / साजहु (prepare) / जाई (go) / चलहु (go) / बेगि (quickly) / रघुबीर (Raghuvir) / बराता (wedding procession) / सुनत (hearing) / पुलक (thrilled) / पूरे (filled) / दोउ (both) / भ्राता (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::1593.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1593.essence: Service becomes celebration when Ram is the one being honored.
ramacharitamanas::1593.simple_meaning: Bharata is told to prepare the wedding procession for Ram, and both brothers become overjoyed at the news.
ramacharitamanas::1593.simple_insight: Joy rises instantly when duty becomes service to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1593.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, preparations for Ram's wedding are underway. Bharata is summoned and asked to arrange horses, elephants, and chariots at once. The news fills Bharata and Shatrughna with delight, showing how naturally their hearts move toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1593.insight: It shows that real devotion turns preparation itself into joy and swift action.

ramacharitamanas::1594.verse_sanskrit: भरत सकल साहनी बोलाए। आयसु दीन्ह मुदित उठि धाए॥ रचि रुचि जीन तुरग तिन्ह साजे। बरन बरन बर बाजि बिराजे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1594.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने सब साहनी (घुड़साल के अध्यक्ष) बुलाए और उन्हें (घोड़ों को सजाने की) आज्ञा दी, वे प्रसन्न होकर उठ दौड़े। उन्होंने रुचि के साथ (यथायोग्य) जीनें कसकर घोड़े सजाए। रंग-रंग के उत्तम घोड़े शोभित हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1594.english_translation: Bharat called all the stable masters and gave them orders. They sprang up gladly. With care and skill, they fitted the saddles and decorated the horses in many colors.
ramacharitamanas::1594.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / सकल (all) / साहनी (stable masters) / बोलाए (called) / आयसु (order) / दीन्ह (gave) / मुदित (gladly) / उठि (rising) / धाए (rushed) / रचि (arranged) / रुचि (with care) / जीन (saddles) / तुरग (horses) / तिन्ह (they) / साजे (decorated) / बरन बरन (many-colored) / बर (excellent) / बाजि (horses) / बिराजे (shone)
ramacharitamanas::1594.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1594.essence: Joyful service makes preparation itself shine.
ramacharitamanas::1594.simple_meaning: Bharat quickly organizes the horsekeepers and has the horses prepared for the journey. It is a scene of cheerful, careful readiness.
ramacharitamanas::1594.simple_insight: Readiness becomes beautiful when service is done gladly.
ramacharitamanas::1594.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat is preparing the bridal procession for Ram. He calls the stable masters, gives instructions, and they rush to dress the horses with care. The verse shows a kingdom moving in joyful service.
ramacharitamanas::1594.modern_relevance: A wedding morning turns hectic, but one person quietly coordinates the details, checks the saddles, and keeps everyone moving. That calm, cheerful efficiency is what makes the whole event feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1594.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the loving care that makes ceremony possible.

ramacharitamanas::1595.verse_sanskrit: सुभग सकल सुठि चंचल करनी। अय इव जरत धरत पग धरनी॥ नाना जाति न जाहिं बखाने। निदरि पवनु जनु चहत उड़ाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1595.verse_hindi: सब घोड़े बड़े ही सुंदर और चंचल करनी (चाल) के हैं। वे धरती पर ऐसे पैर रखते हैं जैसे जलते हुए लोहे पर रखते हों। अनेकों जाति के घोड़े हैं, जिनका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता। (ऐसी तेज चाल के हैं) मानो हवा का निरादर करके उड़ना चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1595.english_translation: The horses are beautiful, restless, and swift. They seem to place their feet on burning ground. Their many breeds cannot be fully described. They look as if they want to outrun the wind itself.
ramacharitamanas::1595.translation_literal: सुभग (beautiful) / सकल (all) / सुठि (very) / चंचल (restless, swift) / करनी (gait, movement) / अय (horses) / इव (like) / जरत (burning) / धरत (placing) / पग (feet) / धरनी (ground) / नाना (many) / जाति (kinds, breeds) / न जाहिं (cannot be) / बखाने (described) / निदरि (disregarding) / पवनु (wind) / जनु (as if) / चहत (want) / उड़ाने (to fly, to race away)
ramacharitamanas::1595.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1595.essence: Speed and beauty announce the grandeur before anyone rides.
ramacharitamanas::1595.simple_meaning: The horses are finely bred, fast, and so lively they seem to barely touch the ground.
ramacharitamanas::1595.simple_insight: Some scenes are built on pure motion and beauty, with no need for explanation.
ramacharitamanas::1595.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharata is preparing Rama’s wedding procession. The stable hands have already been called, and now the text lingers on the horses themselves: beautiful, numerous, and almost airborne. It is a vivid scene-setting detail before the riders mount.
ramacharitamanas::1595.modern_relevance: A wedding garage door opens and the cars gleam in a row, polished for the procession. Before anyone speaks, the scene already tells you this day is important.
ramacharitamanas::1595.insight: It shifts attention from meaning to atmosphere, letting the scene carry the emotion.

ramacharitamanas::1596.verse_sanskrit: तिन्ह सब छयल भए असवारा। भरत सरिस बय राजकुमारा॥ सब सुंदर सब भूषनधारी। कर सर चाप तून कटि भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1596.verse_hindi: उन सब घोड़ों पर भरतजी के समान अवस्था वाले सब छैल-छबीले राजकुमार सवार हुए। वे सभी सुंदर हैं और सब आभूषण धारण किए हुए हैं। उनके हाथों में बाण और धनुष हैं तथा कमर में भारी तरकस बँधे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1596.english_translation: All those riders were handsome young princes like Bharat. All were adorned with ornaments, with bows and arrows in hand and heavy quivers at their waists.
ramacharitamanas::1596.translation_literal: तिन्ह (those) / सब (all) / छयल (handsome young men) / भए (were) / असवारा (horsemen, riders) / भरत सरिस (like Bharat) / बय (young) / राजकुमारा (princes) / सब (all) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सब (all) / भूषनधारी (wearing ornaments) / कर (in hand) / सर (arrow) / चाप (bow) / तून (quiver) / कटि (at the waist) / भारी (heavy)
ramacharitamanas::1596.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1596.essence: Royal splendour and battle readiness fill the scene.
ramacharitamanas::1596.simple_meaning: The mounted princes are all young, handsome, richly adorned, and armed for battle.
ramacharitamanas::1596.simple_insight: Sometimes a scene is meant to show readiness and splendour, not explain anything deeper.
ramacharitamanas::1596.detailed_meaning: The horses have just been prepared, and now the riders are shown: young princes, handsome like Bharat, decked in ornaments, bows, arrows, and quivers. The verse adds vivid detail to the royal procession before it moves on.
ramacharitamanas::1596.modern_relevance: A wedding convoy pulls up with polished cars, matching outfits, and armed security in perfect formation. The point is not one person, but the full display of readiness and rank.
ramacharitamanas::1596.insight: It shifts attention from the individual rider to the collective image of royal preparedness.

ramacharitamanas::1597.verse_sanskrit: छरे छबीले छयल सब सूर सुजान नबीन। जुग पदचर असवार प्रति जे असिकला प्रबीन ॥
ramacharitamanas::1597.verse_hindi: सभी चुने हुए छबीले छैल, शूरवीर, चतुर और नवयुवक हैं। प्रत्येक सवार के साथ दो पैदल सिपाही हैं, जो तलवार चलाने की कला में बड़े निपुण हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1597.english_translation: All are chosen, handsome, brave, clever, and youthful. Each rider has two foot soldiers, skilled in swordsmanship.
ramacharitamanas::1597.translation_literal: छरे (chosen) / छबीले (handsome, dashing) / छयल (youthful gallants) / सब (all) / सूर (brave) / सुजान (clever, well-informed) / नबीन (new, youthful) / जुग (pair of) / पदचर (foot soldiers) / असवार (horsemen) / प्रति (each) / जे (who) / असिकला (sword-art) / प्रबीन (skilled)
ramacharitamanas::1597.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1597.essence: A disciplined force becomes visible before it moves.
ramacharitamanas::1597.simple_meaning: The army is made of handsome young warriors, each rider supported by two skilled foot soldiers.
ramacharitamanas::1597.simple_insight: The scene builds momentum through disciplined, ready forces.
ramacharitamanas::1597.detailed_meaning: The royal host is assembling for the march. Tulsidas lingers on the look and readiness of the warriors: mounted fighters, foot soldiers, and sword experts moving as one. It is vivid scene-setting, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::1597.modern_relevance: A stadium tunnel fills before the match: jerseys straightened, shoes laced, everyone waiting for the signal. The energy is in the formation itself.
ramacharitamanas::1597.insight: It shifts attention from individual glamour to coordinated readiness.

ramacharitamanas::1598.verse_sanskrit: बाँधें बिरद बीर रन गाढ़े। निकसि भए पुर बाहेर ठाढ़े॥ फेरहिं चतुर तुरग गति नाना। हरषहिं सुनि सुनि पनव निसाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1598.verse_hindi: शूरता का बाना धारण किए हुए रणधीर वीर सब निकलकर नगर के बाहर आ खड़े हुए। वे चतुर अपने घोड़ों को तरह-तरह की चालों से फेर रहे हैं और भेरी तथा नगाड़े की आवाज सुन-सुनकर प्रसन्न हो रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1598.english_translation: Clad in the garb of valor, the brave warriors stood outside the city. They twirled their fine horses in many ways and rejoiced at the sound of drums and kettledrums.
ramacharitamanas::1598.translation_literal: बाँधें (bound/clad) / बिरद (valor, fame of heroism) / बीर (brave warriors) / रन (battle) / गाढ़े (firm, intense) / निकसि (having come out) / भए (became) / पुर (city) / बाहेर (outside) / ठाढ़े (standing) / फेरहिं (they turn) / चतुर (skilled, clever) / तुरग (horses) / गति (movement) / नाना (many) / हरषहिं (rejoice) / सुनि सुनि (again and again hearing) / पनव (drums) / निसाना (kettledrums)
ramacharitamanas::1598.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1598.essence: Battle spirit rises before the first blow is struck.
ramacharitamanas::1598.simple_meaning: The warriors ride out of the city, full of battle spirit, showing off their horses and enjoying the war drums.
ramacharitamanas::1598.simple_insight: Excitement can fill a crowd before a battle, even before anyone has fought.
ramacharitamanas::1598.detailed_meaning: The princes and warriors have gathered for Sita's swayamvar in Mithila. After the earlier descriptions of their horses and arms, this verse shows them already outside the city, eager and proud, displaying their horsemanship as the drums sound.
ramacharitamanas::1598.modern_relevance: At a stadium tunnel before the final match, players bounce on their toes, adjusting gloves, grinning at the roar outside. The noise itself lifts their courage.
ramacharitamanas::1598.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle to the charged mood before action begins.

ramacharitamanas::1599.verse_sanskrit: रथ सारथिन्ह बिचित्र बनाए। ध्वज पताक मनि भूषन लाए॥ चवँर चारु किंकिनि धुनि करहीं। भानु जान सोभा अपहरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1599.verse_hindi: सारथियों ने ध्वजा, पताका, मणि और आभूषणों को लगाकर रथों को बहुत विलक्षण बना दिया है। उनमें सुंदर चँवर लगे हैं और घंटियाँ सुंदर शब्द कर रही हैं। वे रथ इतने सुंदर हैं, मानो सूर्य के रथ की शोभा को छीने लेते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1599.english_translation: The charioteers made the chariots wondrous, adorning them with flags, pennants, jewels, and ornaments. Beautiful fly-whisks and tinkling bells made them shine so brightly they seemed to rival the sun’s splendor.
ramacharitamanas::1599.translation_literal: रथ (chariots) / सारथिन्ह (by the charioteers) / बिचित्र (wonderfully varied) / बनाए (made) / ध्वज (flags) / पताक (pennants) / मनि (jewels) / भूषन (ornaments) / लाए (brought) / चवँर (fly-whisks) / चारु (beautiful) / किंकिनि (little bells) / धुनि (sound) / करहीं (make) / भानु (sun) / जान (like) / सोभा (splendor) / अपहरहीं (carry away)
ramacharitamanas::1599.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1599.essence: Splendour itself becomes part of the procession.
ramacharitamanas::1599.simple_meaning: The chariots are richly decorated with flags, jewels, fly-whisks, and bells. They shine so brightly that they seem to outshine the sun.
ramacharitamanas::1599.simple_insight: Beauty here is public, ceremonial, and overwhelming — a whole kingdom is preparing to be seen.
ramacharitamanas::1599.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, the wedding procession is being readied in full splendour. Charioteers dress the chariots with flags, jewels, ornaments, fly-whisks, and bells, turning the scene into a dazzling royal display before the journey begins.
ramacharitamanas::1599.modern_relevance: A wedding convoy rolls out with lights, ribbons, and music, and everyone pauses to look. The moment feels larger than the people inside it — a whole world announcing itself.
ramacharitamanas::1599.insight: It shifts attention from the riders to the atmosphere they create: form, ceremony, and collective awe.

ramacharitamanas::1600.verse_sanskrit: सावँकरन अगनित हय होते। ते तिन्ह रथन्ह सारथिन्ह जोते॥ सुंदर सकल अलंकृत सोहे। जिन्हहि बिलोकत मुनि मन मोहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1600.verse_hindi: अगणित श्यामवर्ण घोड़े थे। उनको सारथियों ने उन रथों में जोत दिया है, जो सभी देखने में सुंदर और गहनों से सजाए हुए सुशोभित हैं और जिन्हें देखकर मुनियों के मन भी मोहित हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1600.english_translation: There were countless dark horses. The charioteers yoked them to the chariots, all beautifully adorned, so lovely that even sages were enchanted at the sight.
ramacharitamanas::1600.translation_literal: सावँकरन (dark-colored) / अगनित (countless) / हय (horses) / होते (were) / ते (those) / तिन्ह (those) / रथन्ह (to the chariots) / सारथिन्ह (charioteers) / जोते (yoked)॥ / सुंदर (beautiful) / सकल (all) / अलंकृत (adorned) / सोहे (shone) / जिन्हहि (which) / बिलोकत (seeing) / मुनि (sages) / मन (mind) / मोहे (were enchanted)॥
ramacharitamanas::1600.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1600.essence: Splendour itself can announce a turning point.
ramacharitamanas::1600.simple_meaning: Countless dark horses are yoked to beautifully decorated chariots. The sight is so splendid that even sages are captivated.
ramacharitamanas::1600.simple_insight: Greatness is made visible through order, beauty, and readiness.
ramacharitamanas::1600.detailed_meaning: The armies are gathering for the great contest in Mithila. Chariots are being prepared, horses yoked, and every detail made splendid. This verse lingers on the magnificence of the war assembly before the contest begins.
ramacharitamanas::1600.modern_relevance: A wedding hall fills with polished cars, bright fabric, and restless guests before the ceremony begins. The atmosphere itself signals that something important is about to unfold.
ramacharitamanas::1600.insight: It shifts attention from the fighters to the charged atmosphere of preparation and grandeur.

ramacharitamanas::1601.verse_sanskrit: जे जल चलहिं थलहि की नाईं। टाप न बूड़ बेग अधिकाईं॥ अस्त्र सस्त्र सबु साजु बनाई। रथी सारथिन्ह लिए बोलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1601.verse_hindi: जो जल पर भी जमीन की तरह ही चलते हैं। वेग की अधिकता से उनकी टाप पानी में नहीं डूबती। अस्त्र-शस्त्र और सब साज सजाकर सारथियों ने रथियों को बुला लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1601.english_translation: Those who move on water as if on land. Their hoofprints do not sink in the water because of their great speed. After preparing all weapons and gear, the charioteers called the warriors to the chariots.
ramacharitamanas::1601.translation_literal: जे (who) / जल (water) / चलहिं (move) / थलहि (on land) / की नाईं (like) / टाप (hoofprints) / न बूड़ (do not sink) / बेग (speed) / अधिकाईं (greatly) / अस्त्र सस्त्र (weapons and arms) / सबु (all) / साजु (equipment/array) / बनाई (having prepared) / रथी (warriors/charioteers) / सारथिन्ह (by the charioteers) / लिए (taken) / बोलाई (called)
ramacharitamanas::1601.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1601.essence: Speed and splendor signal that the procession has fully begun.
ramacharitamanas::1601.simple_meaning: The army’s horses are so swift that they seem to run on water like they run on land. The chariots are fully armed and the warriors are being called to mount them.
ramacharitamanas::1601.simple_insight: Some moments are pure momentum: preparation is complete, and action is about to begin.
ramacharitamanas::1601.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, the royal procession is being readied in full splendor. Horses, chariots, weapons, and warriors are all set in motion, creating the sense of a vast, unstoppable arrival rather than a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::1601.modern_relevance: You hear the elevator ding, grab your bag, and step into the hallway already moving. Everything has been arranged; now the day is about to carry you forward.
ramacharitamanas::1601.insight: It shifts attention from meaning to motion, showing how a scene can build force through detail alone.

ramacharitamanas::1602.verse_sanskrit: चढ़ि चढ़ि रथ बाहेर नगर लागी जुरन बरात। होत सगुन सुंदर सबहि जो जेहि कारज जात ॥
ramacharitamanas::1602.verse_hindi: रथों पर चढ़-चढ़कर बारात नगर के बाहर जुटने लगी, जो जिस काम के लिए जाता है, सभी को सुंदर शकुन होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1602.english_translation: The wedding party climbed onto the chariots and gathered outside the city. For every person going to a worthy task, good omens appear.
ramacharitamanas::1602.translation_literal: चढ़ि चढ़ि (climbing up and up) / रथ (chariots) / बाहेर नगर (outside the city) / लागी जुरन (began to gather) / बरात (wedding party) / होत (happening) / सगुन (omens) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सबहि (for everyone) / जो जेहि (whoever) / कारज (task) / जात (goes)
ramacharitamanas::1602.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1602.essence: A sacred journey begins with auspicious signs.
ramacharitamanas::1602.simple_meaning: The wedding procession gathers outside the city on decorated chariots, and the scene is marked by good omens.
ramacharitamanas::1602.simple_insight: A major moment can feel blessed before it even begins.
ramacharitamanas::1602.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession is assembling outside the city of Mithila. Chariots are ready, people are moving, and the whole scene feels auspicious. This verse simply marks the joyful beginning of the journey before the grand procession continues.
ramacharitamanas::1602.modern_relevance: You step out of the house before dawn for a day that matters. The air feels charged, and even small signs seem to bless the road ahead.
ramacharitamanas::1602.insight: It keeps the mind on the unfolding scene rather than forcing a lesson from it.

ramacharitamanas::1603.verse_sanskrit: कलित करिबरन्हि परीं अँबारीं। कहि न जाहिं जेहि भाँति सँवारीं॥ चले मत्त गज घंट बिराजी। मनहुँ सुभग सावन घन राजी॥1।
ramacharitamanas::1603.verse_hindi: श्रेष्ठ हाथियों पर सुंदर अंबारियाँ पड़ी हैं। वे जिस प्रकार सजाई गई थीं, सो कहा नहीं जा सकता। मतवाले हाथी घंटों से सुशोभित होकर (घंटे बजाते हुए) चले, मानो सावन के सुंदर बादलों के समूह (गरते हुए) जा रहे हों॥
ramacharitamanas::1603.english_translation: Beautiful palanquins were placed upon noble elephants, so finely adorned that their arrangement cannot be described. The intoxicated elephants, bright with bells, moved like lovely monsoon clouds drifting across the sky.
ramacharitamanas::1603.translation_literal: कलित (adorned) / करिबरन्हि (on elephants) / परीं (placed) / अँबारीं (palanquins) / कहि न जाहिं (cannot be said) / जेहि भाँति (in what way) / सँवारीं (decorated) / चले (moved) / मत्त (intoxicated) / गज (elephants) / घंट (bells) / बिराजी (shining) / मनहुँ (as if) / सुभग (beautiful) / सावन (monsoon) / घन (clouds) / राजी (rows, groups)
ramacharitamanas::1603.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1603.essence: Splendor turns a procession into a moving festival.
ramacharitamanas::1603.simple_meaning: The wedding procession is richly decorated, with elephants carrying beautiful palanquins and moving like monsoon clouds.
ramacharitamanas::1603.simple_insight: Beauty can become a form of celebration, where even movement feels festive and alive.
ramacharitamanas::1603.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession is assembling for Sita’s swayamvar. Noble elephants carry ornate palanquins, and their bells ring as the crowd moves toward Janakpur. The verse lingers on the splendor of the scene before the great contest begins.
ramacharitamanas::1603.modern_relevance: A wedding convoy rolls past your window at dusk, lights strung across every vehicle, drums echoing down the street. The whole city seems to breathe in rhythm with the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1603.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the atmosphere it creates around everyone present.

ramacharitamanas::1604.verse_sanskrit: बाहन अपर अनेक बिधाना। सिबिका सुभग सुखासन जाना॥ तिन्ह चढ़ि चले बिप्रबर बृंदा। जनु तनु धरें सकल श्रुति छंदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1604.verse_hindi: सुंदर पालकियाँ, सुख से बैठने योग्य तामजान (जो कुर्सीनुमा होते हैं) और रथ आदि और भी अनेकों प्रकार की सवारियाँ हैं। उन पर श्रेष्ठ ब्राह्मणों के समूह चढ़कर चले, मानो सब वेदों के छन्द ही शरीर धारण किए हुए हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1604.english_translation: There were many kinds of beautiful rides: palanquins, comfortable seats, and chariots. The finest Brahmins rode on them, as if all the Vedic hymns had taken bodily form.
ramacharitamanas::1604.translation_literal: बाहन (vehicles/rides) / अपर (other) / अनेक (many) / बिधाना (kinds) / सिबिका (palanquins) / सुभग (beautiful) / सुखासन (comfortable seats) / जाना (chariots) / तिन्ह (on those) / चढ़ि (riding) / चले (went) / बिप्रबर (best Brahmins) / बृंदा (groups) / जनु (as if) / तनु (body) / धरें (having taken) / सकल (all) / श्रुति (Veda) / छंदा (hymns/metres)
ramacharitamanas::1604.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1604.essence: The procession carries not just people, but living sacred order.
ramacharitamanas::1604.simple_meaning: Many kinds of decorated vehicles carried the Brahmin groups in the procession, and they looked like the Vedic hymns themselves taking form.
ramacharitamanas::1604.simple_insight: Great occasions can make even a procession feel sacred and alive.
ramacharitamanas::1604.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession is moving through the city of Mithila. After the elephants and chariots, more vehicles follow, carrying groups of learned Brahmins. Their presence makes the celebration feel not just royal, but ritually radiant.
ramacharitamanas::1604.modern_relevance: A wedding convoy rolls past with music, flowers, and elders in every car. The scene feels bigger than transport alone — it feels like tradition itself has entered the street.
ramacharitamanas::1604.insight: It turns a festive procession into a sacred public event, where learning and ritual travel together.

ramacharitamanas::1605.verse_sanskrit: मागध सूत बंधि गुनगायक। चले जान चढ़ि जो जेहि लायक॥ बेसर ऊँट बृषभ बहु जाती। चले बस्तु भरि अगनित भाँती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1605.verse_hindi: मागध, सूत, भाट और गुण गाने वाले सब, जो जिस योग्य थे, वैसी सवारी पर चढ़कर चले। बहुत जातियों के खच्चर, ऊँट और बैल असंख्यों प्रकार की वस्तुएँ लाद-लादकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1605.english_translation: The bards, singers, and praise-singers set out on whatever mounts suited them. Countless mules, camels, and bullocks went along, laden with goods of every kind.
ramacharitamanas::1605.translation_literal: मागध (bards) / सूत (charioteer-singers) / बंधि (praise-singers) / गुनगायक (singers of virtues) / चले (went) / जान (on mounts) / चढ़ि (riding) / जो (whatever) / जेहि (to whichever) / लायक (suited) / बेसर (mules) / ऊँट (camels) / बृषभ (bullocks) / बहु जाती (many kinds) / चले (went) / बस्तु (goods) / भरि (loaded with) / अगनित (countless) / भाँती (kinds)
ramacharitamanas::1605.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1605.essence: A grand journey depends on every kind of helper, rider, and load-bearer.
ramacharitamanas::1605.simple_meaning: The procession includes singers, praise-singers, and many kinds of animals carrying goods and supplies.
ramacharitamanas::1605.simple_insight: Great gatherings are built by many roles, not just the visible leaders.
ramacharitamanas::1605.detailed_meaning: As the wedding procession moves forward in Balkand, not only nobles and priests travel with it. Bards, singers, and praise-singers ride on suitable mounts, while mules, camels, and bullocks carry endless supplies. The scene shows the scale and richness of the journey.
ramacharitamanas::1605.modern_relevance: A wedding convoy, moving trucks, and family helpers all arrive at once. The event feels grand only because many unseen hands and vehicles make it possible.
ramacharitamanas::1605.insight: It shifts attention from a single hero to the many supporting roles that make a celebration possible.

ramacharitamanas::1606.verse_sanskrit: कोटिन्ह काँवरि चले कहारा। बिबिध बस्तु को बरनै पारा॥ चले सकल सेवक समुदाई। निज निज साजु समाजु बनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1606.verse_hindi: कहार करोड़ों काँवरें लेकर चले। उनमें अनेकों प्रकार की इतनी वस्तुएँ थीं कि जिनका वर्णन कौन कर सकता है। सब सेवकों के समूह अपना-अपना साज-समाज बनाकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1606.english_translation: Porters walked carrying millions of canopies and loads. Who can describe the countless kinds of goods they bore? All the servants marched together, arranging their own gear and procession.
ramacharitamanas::1606.translation_literal: कोटिन्ह (millions) / काँवरि (canopies or shoulder-borne loads) / चले (walked) / कहारा (porters) / बिबिध (various) / बस्तु (things, goods) / को (of) / बरनै (to describe) / पारा (able) / चले (walked) / सकल (all) / सेवक (servants) / समुदाई (in groups) / निज निज (each one's own) / साजु (equipment, gear) / समाजु (procession, arrangement) / बनाई (making, arranging)
ramacharitamanas::1606.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1606.essence: A royal celebration moves on the shoulders of unseen workers.
ramacharitamanas::1606.simple_meaning: The people traveling with the wedding procession carried huge amounts of goods and supplies, each group arranging its own transport.
ramacharitamanas::1606.simple_insight: Great occasions are built by many hands, each quietly carrying a share.
ramacharitamanas::1606.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession is already in motion. Porters, servants, and attendants move with endless loads, canopies, and supplies, each group organized in its own way. The verse lingers on the scale of the scene, not on a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1606.modern_relevance: At a wedding, the back room is crowded with boxes, folded chairs, flowers, and people hurrying with lists in hand. The celebration only exists because many unseen helpers keep moving.
ramacharitamanas::1606.insight: It shifts attention from the grand event to the collective labor that makes it possible.

ramacharitamanas::1607.verse_sanskrit: सब कें उर निर्भर हरषु पूरित पुलक सरीर। कबहिं देखिबे नयन भरि रामु लखनु दोउ बीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::1607.verse_hindi: सबके हृदय में अपार हर्ष है और शरीर पुलक से भरे हैं। (सबको एक ही लालसा लगी है कि) हम श्री राम-लक्ष्मण दोनों भाइयों को नेत्र भरकर कब देखेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1607.english_translation: Everyone's heart overflows with joy, and their bodies are covered in goosebumps: When will we behold Ram and Lakshman with our own eyes?
ramacharitamanas::1607.translation_literal: सब कें (for everyone) / उर (heart) / निर्भर (full, overflowing) / हरषु (joy) / पूरित (filled) / पुलक (goosebumps) / सरीर (body) / कबहिं (when) / देखिबे (to see) / नयन (eyes) / भरि (full) / रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / दोउ (both) / बीर (heroes)
ramacharitamanas::1607.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1607.essence: Joy swells when the beloved is about to appear.
ramacharitamanas::1607.simple_meaning: Everyone is thrilled and physically moved with joy, eagerly waiting to see Ram and Lakshman with their own eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1607.simple_insight: Longing can fill a whole crowd at once, turning anticipation into shared delight.
ramacharitamanas::1607.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession is arriving in Mithila. All the attendants, singers, and servants are swept up in one feeling: eager joy at the thought of seeing Ram and Lakshman. This is a moment of collective anticipation, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::1607.modern_relevance: You wait at the edge of a crowded platform, craning for one person who matters more than the rest. The whole room feels charged with the same hope.
ramacharitamanas::1607.insight: It captures shared anticipation before a moment everyone has been waiting for.

ramacharitamanas::1608.verse_sanskrit: गरजहिं गज घंटा धुनि घोरा। रथ रव बाजि हिंस चहु ओरा॥ निदरि घनहि घुर्म्मरहिं निसाना। निज पराइ कछु सुनिअ न काना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1608.verse_hindi: हाथी गरज रहे हैं, उनके घंटों की भीषण ध्वनि हो रही है। चारों ओर रथों की घरघराहट और घोड़ों की हिनहिनाहट हो रही है। बादलों का निरादर करते हुए नगाड़े घोर शब्द कर रहे हैं। किसी को अपनी-पराई कोई बात कानों से सुनाई नहीं देती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1608.english_translation: Elephants roar, their bells thunder loudly. All around, the rumble of chariots and the neighing of horses rise. Drums beat so fiercely they seem to defy the clouds. No ear can tell one side from another.
ramacharitamanas::1608.translation_literal: गरजहिं (roar) / गज (elephants) / घंटा (bells) / धुनि (sound) / घोरा (fierce) / रथ (chariots) / रव (rumble) / बाजि (horses) / हिंस (neighing) / चहु ओर (on all sides) / निदरि (disregarding) / घनहि (clouds) / घुर्म्मरहिं (boom) / निसाना (drums) / निज (own) / पराइ (other) / कछु (anything) / सुनिअ (is heard) / न (not) / काना (ears)
ramacharitamanas::1608.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1608.essence: The arrival is so grand that sound itself becomes the announcement.
ramacharitamanas::1608.simple_meaning: The whole scene is filled with loud celebration and movement. The noise is so overwhelming that nothing else can be heard clearly.
ramacharitamanas::1608.simple_insight: Sometimes a moment is so full of life that the world becomes only sound and motion.
ramacharitamanas::1608.detailed_meaning: The people are gathering at Dasharath’s palace to see Ram and Lakshman. Elephants, chariots, horses, and drums fill the air with noise. This verse only paints the overwhelming arrival scene before the crowd reaches full sight of the princes.
ramacharitamanas::1608.modern_relevance: A wedding procession turns the street into thunder: horns, drums, engines, shouting, all at once. You cannot hear your own thoughts, only the fact that something important is arriving.
ramacharitamanas::1608.insight: It turns the moment into pure atmosphere, preparing the reader for the royal gathering that follows.

ramacharitamanas::1609.verse_sanskrit: महा भीर भूपति के द्वारें। रज होइ जाइ पषान पबारें॥ चढ़ी अटारिन्ह देखहिं नारीं। लिएँ आरती मंगल थारीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1609.verse_hindi: राजा दशरथ के दरवाजे पर इतनी भारी भीड़ हो रही है कि वहाँ पत्थर फेंका जाए तो वह भी पिसकर धूल हो जाए। अटारियों पर चढ़ी स्त्रियाँ मंगल थालों में आरती लिए देख रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1609.english_translation: At the king's gate, the crowd was so immense that even a thrown stone would be ground to dust. Women climbed the terraces, holding lamps and auspicious plates for the aarti.
ramacharitamanas::1609.translation_literal: महा भीर (great crowd) / भूपति (of the king) / के द्वारें (at the gate) / रज (dust) / होइ जाइ (would become) / पषान (stone) / पबारें (if thrown and crushed) / चढ़ी (having climbed) / अटारिन्ह (terraces) / देखहिं (see) / नारीं (women) / लिएँ (holding) / आरती (aarti lamp) / मंगल थारीं (auspicious plates)
ramacharitamanas::1609.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1609.essence: The king's gate overflows with joy before the brothers appear.
ramacharitamanas::1609.simple_meaning: The king's palace is packed with people, and women on the terraces watch the scene with lamps and auspicious offerings.
ramacharitamanas::1609.simple_insight: Joy can become so full that the whole city feels lifted together.
ramacharitamanas::1609.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are arriving at Dasharath's court, and the whole palace is overflowing with excitement. The crowd is so dense that women on the terraces watch with aarti plates, turning the moment into a public celebration before the brothers even appear.
ramacharitamanas::1609.modern_relevance: You stand outside a wedding hall while relatives crowd the steps, phones in hand, waiting for the bride and groom. The building itself seems to vibrate with expectation before the doors open.
ramacharitamanas::1609.insight: It turns a private arrival into a shared festival, showing how devotion can fill an entire place.

ramacharitamanas::1610.verse_sanskrit: गावहिं गीत मनोहर नाना। अति आनंदु न जाइ बखाना॥ तब सुमंत्र दुइ स्यंदन साजी। जोते रबि हय निंदक बाजी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1610.verse_hindi: और नाना प्रकार के मनोहर गीत गा रही हैं। उनके अत्यन्त आनंद का बखान नहीं हो सकता। तब सुमन्त्रजी ने दो रथ सजाकर उनमें सूर्य के घोड़ों को भी मात करने वाले घोड़े जोते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1610.english_translation: And they sang many lovely songs. Their joy was beyond description. Then Sumantra prepared two chariots and yoked horses that could outmatch the sun’s own steeds.
ramacharitamanas::1610.translation_literal: गावहिं (they sing) / गीत (songs) / मनोहर (lovely) / नाना (many kinds) / अति (very) / आनंदु (joy) / न जाइ (cannot be) / बखाना (described) / तब (then) / सुमंत्र (Sumantra) / दुइ (two) / स्यंदन (chariots) / साजी (having prepared) / जोते (yoked) / रबि (sun) / हय (horses) / निंदक (surpassing) / बाजी (horses)
ramacharitamanas::1610.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1610.essence: Joy rises, and the journey is set in motion.
ramacharitamanas::1610.simple_meaning: The people sing with great joy while Sumantra gets two chariots ready and harnesses excellent horses.
ramacharitamanas::1610.simple_insight: Joy can fill a moment before a journey begins, even when the road ahead is uncertain.
ramacharitamanas::1610.detailed_meaning: At Dasharath’s palace in Ayodhya, the celebration is overflowing. Women sing from the balconies, and Sumantra prepares the royal chariots for the next movement in the story. This is a scene of motion, pageantry, and rising anticipation.
ramacharitamanas::1610.modern_relevance: A house is buzzing before dawn, phones are ringing, clothes are being packed, and everyone is half-excited, half-nervous. The day has already begun moving before anyone is ready.
ramacharitamanas::1610.insight: It keeps attention on atmosphere and preparation, not on private feeling or inner debate.

ramacharitamanas::1611.verse_sanskrit: दोउ रथ रुचिर भूप पहिं आने। नहिं सारद पहिं जाहिं बखाने॥ राज समाजु एक रथ साजा। दूसर तेज पुंज अति भ्राजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1611.verse_hindi: दोनों सुंदर रथ वे राजा दशरथ के पास ले आए, जिनकी सुंदरता का वर्णन सरस्वती से भी नहीं हो सकता। एक रथ पर राजसी सामान सजाया गया और दूसरा जो तेज का पुंज और अत्यन्त ही शोभायमान था, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1611.english_translation: They brought two beautiful chariots to the king, beyond even Sarada's power to describe. One chariot was decked for royal use; the other shone like a blazing mass of light.
ramacharitamanas::1611.translation_literal: दोउ (both) / रथ (chariots) / रुचिर (beautiful) / भूप (king) / पहिं (to) / आने (brought) / नहिं (not) / सारद (Saraswati) / पहिं (to) / जाहिं (go) / बखाने (described) / राज (royal) / समाजु (arrangement) / एक (one) / रथ (chariot) / साजा (adorned) / दूसर (second) / तेज (radiance) / पुंज (mass) / अति (very) / भ्राजा (shone)
ramacharitamanas::1611.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1611.essence: Preparation itself can carry the dignity of the moment.
ramacharitamanas::1611.simple_meaning: Two splendid chariots are brought for King Dasharath. One is prepared for royal display, and the other shines with extraordinary brilliance.
ramacharitamanas::1611.simple_insight: Great moments deserve careful preparation before anyone moves forward.
ramacharitamanas::1611.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the crowd is gathered and Sumantra has prepared two chariots for Dasharath. One is fitted for courtly travel, while the other gleams with special radiance. This is the quiet moment before Vasishtha and the king set out.
