ramacharitamanas::1611.modern_relevance: Before a wedding procession, someone is still fastening the flowers on the car while everyone waits in bright, nervous excitement. The visible preparation matters because a sacred moment is about to begin.
ramacharitamanas::1611.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the care that makes the event worthy.

ramacharitamanas::1612.verse_sanskrit: तेहिं रथ रुचिर बसिष्ठ कहुँ हरषि चढ़ाई नरेसु। आपु चढ़ेउ स्यंदन सुमिरि हर गुर गौरि गनेसु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1612.verse_hindi: उस सुंदर रथ पर राजा वशिष्ठजी को हर्ष पूर्वक चढ़ाकर फिर स्वयं शिव, गुरु, गौरी (पार्वती) और गणेशजी का स्मरण करके (दूसरे) रथ पर चढ़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::1612.english_translation: He joyfully seated Vashishtha on the beautiful chariot. Then he himself boarded the chariot, remembering Shiva, the guru, Gauri, and Ganesha.
ramacharitamanas::1612.translation_literal: तेहिं (on that) / रथ (chariot) / रुचिर (beautiful) / बसिष्ठ कहुँ (for Vashishtha) / हरषि (joyfully) / चढ़ाई (made to ascend) / नरेसु (the king) / आपु (himself) / चढ़ेउ (ascended) / स्यंदन (chariot) / सुमिरि (remembering) / हर (Shiva) / गुर (the teacher) / गौरि (Gauri) / गनेसु (Ganesha)
ramacharitamanas::1612.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1612.essence: True action begins with remembrance, not self-assertion.
ramacharitamanas::1612.simple_meaning: King Dasharath seats Vashishtha on one chariot and then gets on another after remembering Shiva, the teacher, Parvati, and Ganesha.
ramacharitamanas::1612.simple_insight: Even a king begins a journey with humility and remembrance, not self-importance.
ramacharitamanas::1612.detailed_meaning: Dasharath is preparing to leave for Sita's swayamvar with Vashishtha beside him. Before the journey begins, he honors the teacher and remembers the sacred powers he trusts. The scene shows royal action grounded in reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1612.modern_relevance: Before a big presentation, you pause, breathe, and silently remember the people and values that steadied you. The move is not empty ritual; it keeps pride from taking over.
ramacharitamanas::1612.insight: It teaches you to begin important action with reverence, not ego.

ramacharitamanas::1613.verse_sanskrit: सहित बसिष्ठ सोह नृप कैसें। सुर गुर संग पुरंदर जैसें॥ करि कुल रीति बेद बिधि राऊ। देखि सबहि सब भाँति बनाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1613.verse_hindi: वशिष्ठजी के साथ (जाते हुए) राजा दशरथजी कैसे शोभित हो रहे हैं, जैसे देव गुरु बृहस्पतिजी के साथ इन्द्र हों। वेद की विधि से और कुल की रीति के अनुसार सब कार्य करके तथा सबको सब प्रकार से सजे देखकर, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1613.english_translation: How splendid King Dasharath looked with Vashishtha, like Indra with Brihaspati. He completed every act by Vedic rule and family custom, and saw that everything was fully arranged.
ramacharitamanas::1613.translation_literal: सहित (together with) / बसिष्ठ (Vashishtha) / सोह (shone) / नृप (king) / कैसें (how) / सुर (devas) / गुर (teacher) / संग (with) / पुरंदर (Indra) / जैसें (like) / करि (doing) / कुल रीति (family custom) / बेद बिधि (Vedic method) / राऊ (king Dasharath) / देखि (seeing) / सबहि (all) / सब भाँति (in every way) / बनाऊ (arranged, prepared)
ramacharitamanas::1613.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1613.essence: True dignity comes from doing every detail in the right order.
ramacharitamanas::1613.simple_meaning: Dasharath appears radiant beside Vashishtha, like Indra with his teacher. He follows sacred rules and family custom carefully, making sure everything is properly prepared.
ramacharitamanas::1613.simple_insight: Order, reverence, and preparation can make even a royal moment feel complete.
ramacharitamanas::1613.detailed_meaning: Dasharath is preparing for Ram's wedding procession. With Vashishtha beside him, he moves with dignity and exactness, following both Vedic rule and family tradition. The scene shows a king who honors every detail before setting out.
ramacharitamanas::1613.modern_relevance: Before a wedding procession, a family checks every garland, seat, and timing detail. The calm dignity comes from care done properly, not from rushing or improvising.
ramacharitamanas::1613.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to disciplined preparation and respectful order.

ramacharitamanas::1614.verse_sanskrit: सुमिरि रामु गुर आयसु पाई। चले महीपति संख बजाई॥ हरषे बिबुध बिलोकि बराता। बरषहिं सुमन सुमंगल दाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1614.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का स्मरण करके, गुरु की आज्ञा पाकर पृथ्वी पति दशरथजी शंख बजाकर चले। बारात देखकर देवता हर्षित हुए और सुंदर मंगलदायक फूलों की वर्षा करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1614.english_translation: Remembering Ram and receiving the guru's command, the king set out with a conch blast. The radiant beings rejoiced at the wedding procession and showered auspicious flowers.
ramacharitamanas::1614.translation_literal: सुमिरि (remembering) / रामु (Ram) / गुर (guru) / आयसु (command) / पाई (having received) / चले (went) / महीपति (earth-lord, king) / संख (conch) / बजाई (blowing) / हरषे (rejoiced) / बिबुध (radiant beings) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बराता (wedding procession) / बरषहिं (they shower) / सुमन (flowers) / सुमंगल (most auspicious) / दाता (giver)
ramacharitamanas::1614.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1614.essence: Guided action becomes sacred the moment it leaves the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1614.simple_meaning: King Dasharath remembers Ram, follows his guru's instruction, and sets out with the wedding procession. The radiant beings celebrate and shower flowers.
ramacharitamanas::1614.simple_insight: Right action can feel blessed before anyone else understands it.
ramacharitamanas::1614.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has received Vashistha's guidance and is leading the wedding procession for Ram. As he moves forward, the radiant beings in the sky rejoice and shower flowers, marking this as an auspicious turning point in the story.
ramacharitamanas::1614.modern_relevance: You finally get the message that changes everything, and you move. The room may still be ordinary, but the step you take has already been blessed by clarity.
ramacharitamanas::1614.insight: It shows how obedience to right guidance turns an ordinary departure into an auspicious beginning.

ramacharitamanas::1615.verse_sanskrit: भयउ कोलाहल हय गय गाजे। ब्योम बरात बाजने बाजे॥ सुर नर नारि सुमंगल गाईं। सरस राग बाजहिं सहनाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1615.verse_hindi: बड़ा शोर मच गया, घोड़े और हाथी गरजने लगे। आकाश में और बारात में (दोनों जगह) बाजे बजने लगे। देवांगनाएँ और मनुष्यों की स्त्रियाँ सुंदर मंगलगान करने लगीं और रसीले राग से शहनाइयाँ बजने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1615.english_translation: A great uproar arose. Horses and elephants roared; drums and trumpets sounded in the sky and in the wedding procession. Celestial beings, men, and women sang auspicious songs, and sweet shawms played melodious tunes.
ramacharitamanas::1615.translation_literal: भयउ (became) / कोलाहल (uproar) / हय (horses) / गय (elephants) / गाजे (roared, sounded) / ब्योम (sky) / बरात (wedding procession) / बाजने (sounding) / बाजे (instruments) / सुर (devas, radiant beings) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / सुमंगल (auspicious) / गाईं (sang) / सरस (sweet, melodious) / राग (song, tune) / बाजहिं (are played) / सहनाईं (shawms)
ramacharitamanas::1615.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1615.essence: Joy spills outward until the whole world seems to join it.
ramacharitamanas::1615.simple_meaning: The wedding procession becomes loud and festive, with animals, instruments, and singing filling the air.
ramacharitamanas::1615.simple_insight: Joy can be so full that the whole world seems to ring with it.
ramacharitamanas::1615.detailed_meaning: Dasharath’s wedding procession for Ram moves forward in Ayodhya with overwhelming celebration. Horses, elephants, instruments, singers, and heavenly beings all join the scene. The verse simply paints the rising festival before the next moment unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::1615.modern_relevance: A neighborhood lane fills with music, laughter, and the clatter of guests arriving for a wedding. For a moment, the whole street feels lifted by one shared joy.
ramacharitamanas::1615.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the atmosphere it creates around everyone.

ramacharitamanas::1616.verse_sanskrit: घंट घंटि धुनि बरनि न जाहीं। सरव करहिं पाइक फहराहीं॥ करहिं बिदूषक कौतुक नाना। हास कुसल कल गान सुजाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1616.verse_hindi: घंटे-घंटियों की ध्वनि का वर्णन नहीं हो सकता। पैदल चलने वाले सेवकगण अथवा पट्टेबाज कसरत के खेल कर रहे हैं और फहरा रहे हैं (आकाश में ऊँचे उछलते हुए जा रहे हैं।) हँसी करने में निपुण और सुंदर गाने में चतुर विदूषक (मसखरे) तरह-तरह के तमाशे कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1616.english_translation: The sound of bells cannot be described. Foot soldiers and attendants leap and wave flags. Jokers perform many amusements, skilled in laughter and sweet song.
ramacharitamanas::1616.translation_literal: घंट (bells) / घंटि (bells) / धुनि (sound) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाहीं (can go) / सरव (soldiers/footmen) / करहिं (do) / पाइक (foot soldiers/attendants) / फहराहीं (wave/leap) / करहिं (do) / बिदूषक (jokers/clowns) / कौतुक (amusements) / नाना (many) / हास (laughter) / कुसल (skilled) / कल (sweet) / गान (song) / सुजाना (clever/skillful)
ramacharitamanas::1616.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1616.essence: The procession is so alive that words fall short.
ramacharitamanas::1616.simple_meaning: The wedding procession is overflowing with noise, movement, jokes, and music. It is a lively scene, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::1616.simple_insight: Sometimes joy is so full it cannot be neatly described.
ramacharitamanas::1616.detailed_meaning: Dasharath’s wedding procession is moving toward Janakpur. Bells ring, attendants surge forward, and entertainers fill the air with song and laughter. Tulsidas is painting the festive scene before the next movement of the journey.
ramacharitamanas::1616.modern_relevance: You reach a wedding baraat and the whole street is alive with drums, shouting, dancing, and people making each other laugh. The moment is bigger than description.
ramacharitamanas::1616.insight: It sets the scene with sensory abundance, preparing the reader for the procession’s grandeur.

ramacharitamanas::1617.verse_sanskrit: तुरग नचावहिं कुअँर बर अकनि मृदंग निसान। नागर नट चितवहिं चकित डगहिं न ताल बँधान ॥
ramacharitamanas::1617.verse_hindi: सुंदर राजकुमार मृदंग और नगाड़े के शब्द सुनकर घोड़ों को उन्हीं के अनुसार इस प्रकार नचा रहे हैं कि वे ताल के बंधान से जरा भी डिगते नहीं हैं। चतुर नट चकित होकर यह देख रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1617.english_translation: The handsome princes make the horses dance to the beat of the drum and kettledrum. Even skilled acrobats watch in wonder, unable to keep time without faltering.
ramacharitamanas::1617.translation_literal: तुरग (horses) / नचावहिं (make dance) / कुअँर बर (handsome princes) / अकनि (to the sound) / मृदंग (drum) / निसान (kettledrum) / नागर नट (skilled acrobats) / चितवहिं (watch) / चकित (amazed) / डगहिं (falter) / न (not) / ताल (rhythm) / बँधान (binding)
ramacharitamanas::1617.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1617.essence: True skill stays steady even under a roaring rhythm.
ramacharitamanas::1617.simple_meaning: The princes ride so skillfully to the beat of the drums that even expert performers are amazed by their control.
ramacharitamanas::1617.simple_insight: Real grace is effortless control, not forced display.
ramacharitamanas::1617.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession is in full motion. Drums thunder, horses move in rhythm, and the princes handle them with such ease that even seasoned performers stare in surprise. This line adds to the festive grandeur before the next auspicious signs appear.
ramacharitamanas::1617.modern_relevance: At a crowded arena, someone handles pressure so smoothly that the experts in the stands go quiet. Skill like that doesn't announce itself; it simply holds the room.
ramacharitamanas::1617.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to mastery under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::1618.verse_sanskrit: बनइ न बरनत बनी बराता। होहिं सगुन सुंदर सुभदाता॥ चारा चाषु बाम दिसि लेई। मनहुँ सकल मंगल कहि देई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1618.verse_hindi: बारात ऐसी बनी है कि उसका वर्णन करते नहीं बनता। सुंदर शुभदायक शकुन हो रहे हैं। नीलकंठ पक्षी बाईं ओर चारा ले रहा है, मानो सम्पूर्ण मंगलों की सूचना दे रहा हो॥।1॥
ramacharitamanas::1618.english_translation: The wedding procession was so splendid it could not be described. Auspicious signs appeared everywhere, and the blue-necked bird on the left seemed to announce good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::1618.translation_literal: बनइ न (cannot be made) / बरनत (while describing) / बनी (splendid) / बराता (wedding procession) / होहिं (are happening) / सगुन (auspicious signs) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुभदाता (giver of good fortune) / चारा (food) / चाषु (blue-necked bird) / बाम दिसि (left side) / लेई (taking) / मनहुँ (as if) / सकल (all) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / कहि देई (saying, gives)
ramacharitamanas::1618.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1618.essence: A blessed moment makes even nature seem to speak.
ramacharitamanas::1618.simple_meaning: The wedding procession is overflowing with beauty and good omens. Even the birds and signs around it seem to announce blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1618.simple_insight: Some moments feel so right that the whole world seems to agree.
ramacharitamanas::1618.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the wedding procession for Ram has arrived in full splendour. The scene is packed with music, movement, and auspicious signs. This verse pauses to show that the marriage is not ordinary; nature itself seems to bless it.
ramacharitamanas::1618.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall and feel the air change before anyone speaks. The lights, the music, the smiles, even the smallest details seem to say: something sacred is beginning.
ramacharitamanas::1618.insight: It trains attention to notice harmony and blessing in the atmosphere around an event.

ramacharitamanas::1619.verse_sanskrit: दाहिन काग सुखेत सुहावा। नकुल दरसु सब काहूँ पावा॥ सानुकूल बह त्रिबिध बयारी। सघट सबाल आव बर नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1619.verse_hindi: दाहिनी ओर कौआ सुंदर खेत में शोभा पा रहा है। नेवले का दर्शन भी सब किसी ने पाया। तीनों प्रकार की (शीतल, मंद, सुगंधित) हवा अनुकूल दिशा में चल रही है। श्रेष्ठ (सुहागिनी) स्त्रियाँ भरे हुए घड़े और गोद में बालक लिए आ रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1619.english_translation: A crow appears auspiciously on the right. A mongoose is seen by everyone. Three kinds of favorable breeze blow. Married women come carrying full pots and infants in their laps.
ramacharitamanas::1619.translation_literal: दाहिनि (on the right) / काग (crow) / सुखेत (in a pleasant field) / सुहावा (beautiful, auspicious) / नकुल (mongoose) / दरसु (sight, appearance) / सब काहूँ (to everyone) / पावा (was found) / सानुकूल (favorable, auspicious) / बह (blows) / त्रिबिध (three kinds) / बयारी (breeze) / सघट (full, filled) / सबाल (with child in lap) / आव (come) / बर (married, excellent) / नारी (women)
ramacharitamanas::1619.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1619.essence: The world itself seems to bless the marriage before it begins.
ramacharitamanas::1619.simple_meaning: A series of auspicious signs appears around the wedding procession: crows, mongooses, gentle winds, and married women carrying pots and children.
ramacharitamanas::1619.simple_insight: Some moments arrive wrapped in favor, as if the world itself is blessing the event.
ramacharitamanas::1619.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession for Ram and Sita is moving forward, and the scene is thick with good omens. Birds, animals, winds, and women with full pots all appear in fortunate ways, building the sense that this marriage is blessed from every direction.
ramacharitamanas::1619.modern_relevance: You step outside on a day that suddenly feels unusually gentle: the air is soft, people smile without reason, and everything seems to line up. Some days seem to welcome what is about to happen.
ramacharitamanas::1619.insight: It trains attention to read the atmosphere of a moment, not just its facts.

ramacharitamanas::1620.verse_sanskrit: लोवा फिरि फिरि दरसु देखावा। सुरभी सनमुख सिसुहि पिआवा॥ मृगमाला फिरि दाहिनि आई। मंगल गन जनु दीन्हि देखाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1620.verse_hindi: लोमड़ी फिर-फिरकर (बार-बार) दिखाई दे जाती है। गायें सामने खड़ी बछड़ों को दूध पिलाती हैं। हरिनों की टोली (बाईं ओर से) घूमकर दाहिनी ओर को आई, मानो सभी मंगलों का समूह दिखाई दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1620.english_translation: The fox kept appearing again and again. Cows stood facing their calves and fed them milk. A herd of deer came around to the right, as if a whole cluster of auspicious signs had appeared.
ramacharitamanas::1620.translation_literal: लोवा (fox) / फिरि फिरि (again and again) / दरसु (sight) / देखावा (showed)। / सुरभी (cows) / सनमुख (facing) / सिसुहि (to the calf) / पिआवा (made drink milk)॥ / मृगमाला (herd of deer) / फिरि (turning) / दाहिनि (to the right) / आई (came)। / मंगल (auspiciousness) / गन (group) / जनु (as if) / दीन्हि (gave) / देखाई (showing)॥
ramacharitamanas::1620.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1620.essence: The world itself seems to bless the procession.
ramacharitamanas::1620.simple_meaning: More auspicious signs appear as the wedding procession moves forward: animals and birds behave in fortunate ways, suggesting everything is going well.
ramacharitamanas::1620.simple_insight: A good beginning can feel supported by the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::1620.detailed_meaning: As Ram’s wedding procession advances in Balkand, everyone watches for signs of blessing. Foxes, cows, and deer appear in patterns read as auspicious. This verse continues the scene-setting, building the feeling that the marriage is under divine favor.
ramacharitamanas::1620.modern_relevance: You leave home for a big family ceremony, and every small detail feels meaningful — the traffic clears, a child smiles, the day seems to open. This verse lives in that feeling of being gently blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1620.insight: It trains attention to read the moment as favorable and aligned, not random.

ramacharitamanas::1621.verse_sanskrit: छेमकरी कह छेम बिसेषी। स्यामा बाम सुतरु पर देखी॥ सनमुख आयउ दधि अरु मीना। कर पुस्तक दुइ बिप्र प्रबीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1621.verse_hindi: क्षेमकरी (सफेद सिरवाली चील) विशेष रूप से क्षेम (कल्याण) कह रही है। श्यामा बाईं ओर सुंदर पेड़ पर दिखाई पड़ी। दही, मछली और दो विद्वान ब्राह्मण हाथ में पुस्तक लिए हुए सामने आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1621.english_translation: The auspicious bird called Khemkari gave a special sign of well-being. The dark one appeared on the left in a beautiful tree. Curds, fish, and two learned Brahmins with books came into view ahead.
ramacharitamanas::1621.translation_literal: छेमकरी (auspicious bird) / कह (said) / छेम (well-being) / बिसेषी (special) / स्यामा (the dark one) / बाम (left) / सुतरु (beautiful tree) / पर (on) / देखी (seen) / सनमुख (in front) / आयउ (came) / दधि (curds) / अरु (and) / मीना (fish) / कर (in hand) / पुस्तक (book) / दुइ (two) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / प्रबीना (learned)
ramacharitamanas::1621.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1621.essence: A blessed moment seems to announce itself from every direction.
ramacharitamanas::1621.simple_meaning: A series of auspicious signs appears together, pointing toward success and blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1621.simple_insight: Hope gathers when many small signs all lean in the same direction.
ramacharitamanas::1621.detailed_meaning: As the wedding signs gather around the moment of Sita's swayamvar, the scene fills with favorable omens: birds, directions, food symbols, and learned Brahmins. The verse adds more signs to show that the coming event is fully blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1621.modern_relevance: Before a big interview, you notice every small thing seems to go right — the train is on time, your notes are ready, the room feels calm. The mind starts reading the day as favorable.
ramacharitamanas::1621.insight: It trains attention to notice a pattern of blessing rather than random fragments.

ramacharitamanas::1622.verse_sanskrit: मंगलमय कल्यानमय अभिमत फल दातार। जनु सब साचे होन हित भए सगुन एक बार ॥
ramacharitamanas::1622.verse_hindi: सभी मंगलमय, कल्याणमय और मनोवांछित फल देने वाले शकुन मानो सच्चे होने के लिए एक ही साथ हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1622.english_translation: All auspicious, all beneficial, and all desired omens seemed to become true at once.
ramacharitamanas::1622.translation_literal: मंगलमय (auspicious) / कल्यानमय (beneficial) / अभिमत (desired) / फल (fruit) / दातार (giver) / जनु (as if) / सब (all) / साचे (true) / होन (to become) / हित (for good) / भए (became) / सगुन (omens) / एक बार (at once)
ramacharitamanas::1622.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1622.essence: A blessed moment makes even signs seem to speak in one voice.
ramacharitamanas::1622.simple_meaning: Every good sign appeared together, as if the whole world was confirming that this moment would bring blessing and the desired result.
ramacharitamanas::1622.simple_insight: It feels like life itself is giving a green light.
ramacharitamanas::1622.detailed_meaning: In the lead-up to Ram and Sita’s marriage, the omens around them turn overwhelmingly favorable. The scene is not teaching a doctrine; it is building a sacred atmosphere, showing that the moment is being blessed from every side.
ramacharitamanas::1622.modern_relevance: You are already nervous before a big decision, then everything seems to line up at once: the call comes through, the timing works, the signs feel unmistakable. This verse captures that rare feeling of life opening its hand.
ramacharitamanas::1622.insight: It shifts attention from uncertainty to the felt sense that a moment is being quietly affirmed.

ramacharitamanas::1623.verse_sanskrit: मंगल सगुन सुगम सब ताकें। सगुन ब्रह्म सुंदर सुत जाकें॥ राम सरिस बरु दुलहिनि सीता। समधी दसरथु जनकु पुनीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1623.verse_hindi: स्वयं सगुण ब्रह्म जिसके सुंदर पुत्र हैं, उसके लिए सब मंगल शकुन सुलभ हैं। जहाँ श्री रामचन्द्रजी सरीखे दूल्हा और सीताजी जैसी दुलहिन हैं तथा दशरथजी और जनकजी जैसे पवित्र समधी हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1623.english_translation: For that one, all auspicious signs come easily. The supreme reality has a beautiful son. Ram is the bridegroom, Sita the bride, and pure Dasharath and Janak are the noble fathers-in-law.
ramacharitamanas::1623.translation_literal: मंगल (auspicious) / सगुन (auspicious signs) / सुगम (easy) / सब (all) / ताकें (for that one) / सगुन (with form) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुत (son) / जाकें (whose) / राम (Ram) / सरिस (like) / बरु (bridegroom) / दुलहिनि (bride) / सीता (Sita) / समधी (fathers-in-law) / दसरथु (Dasharath) / जनकु (Janak) / पुनीता (pure)
ramacharitamanas::1623.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1623.essence: Purity at the center makes every sign turn auspicious.
ramacharitamanas::1623.simple_meaning: A house blessed by Ram and Sita needs no effort for good signs. The wedding is holy because the bridegroom, bride, and both fathers are all pure and noble.
ramacharitamanas::1623.simple_insight: When life is rooted in what is pure, even the signs around it feel naturally blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1623.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the wedding of Ram and Sita is approaching. Tulsidas pauses to show that this is no ordinary marriage: Ram is the supreme reality in human form, Sita is his radiant bride, and Dasharath and Janak are both righteous fathers. The whole scene overflows with auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::1623.modern_relevance: A wedding hall fills with noise, relatives, and last-minute chaos, yet one simple thing changes everything: the people at the center are good, steady, and sincere. Then even the disorder feels blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1623.insight: It shifts attention from lucky signs to the moral purity that makes a moment truly auspicious.

ramacharitamanas::1624.verse_sanskrit: सुनि अस ब्याहु सगुन सब नाचे। अब कीन्हे बिरंचि हम साँचे॥ एहि बिधि कीन्ह बरात पयाना। हय गय गाजहिं हने निसाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1624.verse_hindi: ऐसा ब्याह सुनकर मानो सभी शकुन नाच उठे (और कहने लगे-) अब ब्रह्माजी ने हमको सच्चा कर दिया। इस तरह बारात ने प्रस्थान किया। घोड़े, हाथी गरज रहे हैं और नगाड़ों पर चोट लग रही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1624.english_translation: Hearing of such a wedding, all the auspicious signs seemed to dance. "Now Brahma himself has made us true." In this way the wedding procession set out; horses and elephants roared, and the drums were struck.
ramacharitamanas::1624.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / अस (such) / ब्याहु (wedding) / सगुन (auspicious signs) / सब (all) / नाचे (danced) / अब (now) / कीन्हे (made) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / हम (us) / साँचे (true) / एहि बिधि (in this manner) / कीन्ह (made) / बरात (wedding procession) / पयाना (departure) / हय (horses) / गय (elephants) / गाजहिं (roar) / हने (struck) / निसाना (drums)
ramacharitamanas::1624.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1624.essence: A blessed beginning moves like the whole world agrees.
ramacharitamanas::1624.simple_meaning: The wedding procession begins amid joy and celebration. Horses, elephants, and drums announce the start of Ram and Sita's marriage journey.
ramacharitamanas::1624.simple_insight: Some moments feel so right that even the world seems to celebrate with you.
ramacharitamanas::1624.detailed_meaning: After the auspicious signs announce Ram and Sita's union, the wedding procession finally moves out from Janakpur. Horses, elephants, and drums fill the air. This verse simply marks the grand departure, carrying the joy into the next stage of the marriage.
ramacharitamanas::1624.modern_relevance: The car pulls away from the house after the ceremony, and everyone on the street turns to look. The noise, the movement, the relief — a long-awaited beginning is finally underway.
ramacharitamanas::1624.insight: It shifts attention from the ceremony itself to the living momentum that follows a fulfilled blessing.

ramacharitamanas::1625.verse_sanskrit: आवत जानि भानुकुल केतू। सरितन्हि जनक बँधाए सेतू॥ बीच-बीच बर बास बनाए। सुरपुर सरिस संपदा छाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1625.verse_hindi: सूर्यवंश के पताका स्वरूप दशरथजी को आते हुए जानकर जनकजी ने नदियों पर पुल बँधवा दिए। बीच-बीच में ठहरने के लिए सुंदर घर (पड़ाव) बनवा दिए, जिनमें देवलोक के समान सम्पदा छाई है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1625.english_translation: Knowing that the Sun-line prince was coming, King Janak had bridges built over the rivers. At intervals he had beautiful rest houses made, filled with wealth like the realm of the radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::1625.translation_literal: आवत (coming) / जानि (knowing) / भानुकुल केतू (banner of the Sun-line) / सरितन्हि (on the rivers) / जनक (Janak) / बँधाए (had built) / सेतू (bridges) / बीच-बीच (at intervals) / बर (excellent) / बास (lodgings) / बनाए (had made) / सुरपुर (realm of the radiant beings) / सरिस (like) / संपदा (wealth, splendour) / छाए (spread)
ramacharitamanas::1625.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1625.essence: True welcome builds the road before the guest arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1625.simple_meaning: Janak prepares the route for Dasharath's arrival by building bridges and rest houses along the way.
ramacharitamanas::1625.simple_insight: Care becomes visible in practical preparation, not just in feeling welcome.
ramacharitamanas::1625.detailed_meaning: Dasharath's wedding procession is on the way to Mithila. Janak does not merely wait; he prepares the roads, bridges, and resting places so the guests travel in comfort. The verse shows royal hospitality before the great wedding begins.
ramacharitamanas::1625.modern_relevance: A guest is arriving after a long drive, and you clear the path, set up water, and make the rooms ready before they knock. Real welcome is built in advance.
ramacharitamanas::1625.insight: It shifts respect from words and ceremony to concrete preparation that eases another person's journey.

ramacharitamanas::1626.verse_sanskrit: असन सयन बर बसन सुहाए। पावहिं सब निज निज मन भाए॥ नित नूतन सुख लखि अनुकूले। सकल बरातिन्ह मंदिर भूले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1626.verse_hindi: और जहाँ बारात के सब लोग अपने-अपने मन की पसंद के अनुसार सुहावने उत्तम भोजन, बिस्तर और वस्त्र पाते हैं। मन के अनुकूल नित्य नए सुखों को देखकर सभी बारातियों को अपने घर भूल गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1626.english_translation: And there, all the wedding guests received pleasing food, beds, and clothes suited to their own taste. Seeing new delights each day in perfect comfort, all the guests forgot their homes.
ramacharitamanas::1626.translation_literal: असन (food) / सयन (sleeping place) / बर (excellent) / बसन (clothes) / सुहाए (pleasant) / पावहिं (they receive) / सब (all) / निज निज (each one's own) / मन (mind) / भाए (pleased)॥ / नित (daily) / नूतन (new) / सुख (comforts) / लखि (seeing) / अनुकूले (favourable) / सकल (all) / बरातिन्ह (wedding guests) / मंदिर (home) / भूले (forgot)
ramacharitamanas::1626.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1626.essence: True hospitality makes people forget the road home.
ramacharitamanas::1626.simple_meaning: The wedding guests are treated so well that they get exactly what they like, and the comfort makes them forget their homes.
ramacharitamanas::1626.simple_insight: Care that truly fits people makes them feel at ease so quickly that distance and homesickness disappear.
ramacharitamanas::1626.detailed_meaning: At Janak's city, Ram's wedding procession is being hosted with extraordinary warmth. Guests receive fine food, beds, and clothes exactly as they prefer. The comfort is so complete that everyone forgets the journey and their own homes.
ramacharitamanas::1626.modern_relevance: You arrive tired at a host's house after a long train ride, and they notice everything — the tea you like, the blanket you need, the silence you need. That kind of welcome makes a stranger feel instantly held.
ramacharitamanas::1626.insight: It shifts attention from grand display to precise hospitality: real care means meeting each person's actual need.

ramacharitamanas::1627.verse_sanskrit: आवत जानि बरात बर सुनि गहगहे निसान। सजि गज रथ पदचर तुरग लेन चले अगवान ॥
ramacharitamanas::1627.verse_hindi: बड़े जोर से बजते हुए नगाड़ों की आवाज सुनकर श्रेष्ठ बारात को आती हुई जानकर अगवानी करने वाले हाथी, रथ, पैदल और घोड़े सजाकर बारात लेने चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1627.english_translation: Hearing the splendid wedding procession approach, the welcoming party set out with decorated elephants, chariots, foot soldiers, and horses to receive it.
ramacharitamanas::1627.translation_literal: आवत (coming) / जानि (knowing) / बरात (wedding procession) / बर (splendid) / सुनि (hearing) / गहगहे (loudly resounding) / निसान (drums) / सजि (decorated) / गज (elephants) / रथ (chariots) / पदचर (foot soldiers) / तुरग (horses) / लेन (to receive) / चले (went) / अगवान (welcoming party)
ramacharitamanas::1627.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1627.essence: Joy is revealed by how carefully it receives what it loves.
ramacharitamanas::1627.simple_meaning: The wedding party is arriving, and the welcoming group goes out with elephants, chariots, foot soldiers, and horses to receive it.
ramacharitamanas::1627.simple_insight: Big moments are met with full respect. The welcome itself becomes part of the joy.
ramacharitamanas::1627.detailed_meaning: Janak’s city is preparing for Ram’s wedding procession. As the drums thunder in the distance, the welcome party sets out in ceremonial splendour with elephants, chariots, horses, and foot soldiers. The verse is a scene of arrival, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1627.modern_relevance: A long-awaited guest is finally near, and the whole house changes at once — shoes lined up, lights switched on, everyone moving faster because something precious is about to arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1627.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the honour shown in receiving it well.

ramacharitamanas::1628.verse_sanskrit: कनक कलस भरि कोपर थारा। भाजन ललित अनेक प्रकारा॥ भरे सुधा सम सब पकवाने। नाना भाँति न जाहिं बखाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1628.verse_hindi: (दूध, शर्बत, ठंडाई, जल आदि से) भरकर सोने के कलश तथा जिनका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता ऐसे अमृत के समान भाँति-भाँति के सब पकवानों से भरे हुए परात, थाल आदि अनेक प्रकार के सुंदर बर्तन, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1628.english_translation: Golden pitchers, trays, and many beautiful vessels were filled; the dishes were like nectar, beyond counting in variety.
ramacharitamanas::1628.translation_literal: कनक (golden) / कलस (pitchers) / भरि (filled) / कोपर (trays) / थारा (platters) / भाजन (vessels) / ललित (beautiful) / अनेक (many) / प्रकारा (kinds) / भरे (filled) / सुधा (nectar) / सम (like) / सब (all) / पकवाने (cooked dishes) / नाना (various) / भाँति (ways) / न जाहिं (cannot be) / बखाने (described)
ramacharitamanas::1628.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1628.essence: Honor becomes visible in the way people are fed and received.
ramacharitamanas::1628.simple_meaning: The wedding welcome is lavish: golden vessels, beautiful trays, and many kinds of food and drink are prepared in abundance.
ramacharitamanas::1628.simple_insight: A grand welcome can be felt in the details. Care shown through abundance becomes its own language.
ramacharitamanas::1628.detailed_meaning: At Janak's palace, the bridal feast and reception are being prepared for the arriving wedding party. Golden vessels, trays, and countless dishes fill the scene, showing royal honor before any deeper teaching begins.
ramacharitamanas::1628.modern_relevance: You walk into a home where every dish is set out before you speak. The welcome is already doing the talking.
ramacharitamanas::1628.insight: It shifts attention from abstract celebration to concrete hospitality and generosity.

ramacharitamanas::1629.verse_sanskrit: फल अनेक बर बस्तु सुहाईं। हरषि भेंट हित भूप पठाईं॥ भूषन बसन महामनि नाना। खग मृग हय गय बहुबिधि जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1629.verse_hindi: उत्तम फल तथा और भी अनेकों सुंदर वस्तुएँ राजा ने हर्षित होकर भेंट के लिए भेजीं। गहने, कपड़े, नाना प्रकार की मूल्यवान मणियाँ (रत्न), पक्षी, पशु, घोड़े, हाथी और बहुत तरह की सवारियाँ, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1629.english_translation: The king joyfully sent gifts of fine fruits and many beautiful things. He also sent ornaments, clothes, priceless jewels, birds, animals, horses, elephants, and many kinds of mounts.
ramacharitamanas::1629.translation_literal: फल (fruits) / अनेक (many) / बर (excellent) / बस्तु (things) / सुहाईं (beautiful) / हरषि (joyfully) / भेंट (gifts) / हित (for the sake of) / भूप (king) / पठाईं (sent) / भूषन (ornaments) / बसन (clothes) / महामनि (great jewels) / नाना (many kinds of) / खग (birds) / मृग (animals) / हय (horses) / गय (elephants) / बहुबिधि (various) / जाना (sent)
ramacharitamanas::1629.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1629.essence: Welcome becomes real through generous preparation.
ramacharitamanas::1629.simple_meaning: The king sends many fine gifts, including fruit, clothes, jewels, animals, horses, and elephants, to welcome the arriving wedding party.
ramacharitamanas::1629.simple_insight: Generosity becomes visible in what you send out before anyone asks.
ramacharitamanas::1629.detailed_meaning: As the wedding procession approaches Janakpur, King Janak has gifts prepared in abundance. This verse lists the welcome offerings—fruits, ornaments, clothes, jewels, birds, animals, horses, and elephants—showing the scale of honor and joy surrounding the arrival.
ramacharitamanas::1629.modern_relevance: A home fills with boxes, flowers, sweets, and last-minute gifts before guests arrive for a wedding. The care is in the details, and everyone can feel it before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1629.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to the lived act of welcoming with abundance.

ramacharitamanas::1630.verse_sanskrit: मंगल सगुन सुगंध सुहाए। बहुत भाँति महिपाल पठाए॥ दधि चिउरा उपहार अपारा। भरि भरि काँवरि चले कहारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1630.verse_hindi: तथा बहुत प्रकार के सुगंधित एवं सुहावने मंगल द्रव्य और शगुन के पदार्थ राजा ने भेजे। दही, चिउड़ा और अगणित उपहार की चीजें काँवरों में भर-भरकर कहार चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1630.english_translation: The king sent many auspicious gifts and fragrant offerings. Bearers loaded baskets with curd, flattened rice, and countless presents.
ramacharitamanas::1630.translation_literal: मंगल (auspicious) / सगुन (good omens) / सुगंध (fragrant) / सुहाए (pleasant) / बहुत भाँति (many kinds) / महिपाल (the king) / पठाए (sent)॥ / दधि (curd) / चिउरा (flattened rice) / उपहार (gifts) / अपारा (immeasurable) / भरि भरि (filled to the brim) / काँवरि (baskets) / चले (went) / कहारा (bearers)॥
ramacharitamanas::1630.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1630.essence: Generous giving turns preparation into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1630.simple_meaning: The king sends many auspicious gifts, and the bearers carry them in baskets.
ramacharitamanas::1630.simple_insight: Small offerings can carry great joy when they are given with care.
ramacharitamanas::1630.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the wedding preparations are in full flow. King Janak sends fragrant, auspicious gifts, curd, flattened rice, and many other offerings ahead of the bridegroom party. The verse simply shows the abundance and excitement building before the wedding.
ramacharitamanas::1630.modern_relevance: You’re packing gifts before a wedding and checking every box twice. The point is not the size of the present, but the warmth carried in its careful sending.
ramacharitamanas::1630.insight: It shifts attention from the objects themselves to the intention and joy behind the offering.

ramacharitamanas::1631.verse_sanskrit: अगवानन्ह जब दीखि बराता। उर आनंदु पुलक भर गाता॥ देखि बनाव सहित अगवाना। मुदित बरातिन्ह हने निसाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1631.verse_hindi: अगवानी करने वालों को जब बारात दिखाई दी, तब उनके हृदय में आनंद छा गया और शरीर रोमांच से भर गया। अगवानों को सज-धज के साथ देखकर बारातियों ने प्रसन्न होकर नगाड़े बजाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1631.english_translation: When the welcoming party saw the wedding procession, joy rose in their hearts and their bodies thrilled. Seeing the greeters dressed in splendor, the wedding guests happily beat the drums.
ramacharitamanas::1631.translation_literal: अगवानन्ह (the greeters) / जब (when) / दीखि (saw) / बराता (the wedding procession) / उर (in the heart) / आनंदु (joy) / पुलक (horripilation) / भर (filled) / गाता (body) / देखि (seeing) / बनाव (splendor) / सहित (with) / अगवाना (the greeters) / मुदित (delighted) / बरातिन्ह (the wedding guests) / हने (struck) / निसाना (drums)
ramacharitamanas::1631.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1631.simple_meaning: The greeters and the wedding guests are overjoyed when they see each other. Their happiness shows in tears, thrills, and drumbeats.
ramacharitamanas::1631.simple_insight: Shared joy becomes visible. Even a meeting can feel like celebration before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1631.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession has arrived, and the welcoming party finally sees it. Both sides are dressed for honor and joy, so the sight itself breaks open delight. This is a scene of festive arrival, not instruction.
ramacharitamanas::1631.modern_relevance: You spot your family at the airport after months apart, and before anyone speaks, everyone is already smiling, waving, and rushing forward.
ramacharitamanas::1631.insight: It simply shows joy spreading between two groups at first sight.

ramacharitamanas::1632.verse_sanskrit: हरषि परसपर मिलन हित कछुक चले बगमेल। जनु आनंद समुद्र दुइ मिलत बिहाइ सुबेल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1632.verse_hindi: (बाराती तथा अगवानों में से) कुछ लोग परस्पर मिलने के लिए हर्ष के मारे बाग छोड़कर (सरपट) दौड़ चले और ऐसे मिले मानो आनंद के दो समुद्र मर्यादा छोड़कर मिलते हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1632.english_translation: Some people, overjoyed to meet each other, ran out of the garden. It was like two oceans of joy meeting and overflowing their banks.
ramacharitamanas::1632.translation_literal: हरषि (rejoicing) / परसपर (one another) / मिलन (meeting) / हित (for the sake of) / कछुक (some) / चले (went) / बगमेल (out of the garden) / जनु (as if) / आनंद (joy) / समुद्र (oceans) / दुइ (two) / मिलत (meeting) / बिहाइ (leaving) / सुबेल (their banks)
ramacharitamanas::1632.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1632.essence: True joy cannot stay contained; it rushes toward meeting.
ramacharitamanas::1632.simple_meaning: People were so happy to meet that they rushed out to greet one another. Their joy felt vast, like two oceans overflowing together.
ramacharitamanas::1632.simple_insight: Joy can become so full that it spills into movement and greeting.
ramacharitamanas::1632.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession has arrived, and the welcoming party sees it from afar. Overcome with delight, some rush forward to meet the guests. Tulsidas compares their meeting to two oceans of joy overflowing at once.
ramacharitamanas::1632.modern_relevance: You spot someone you have not seen in years at a train platform, and before you even think, you are already walking fast. Some happiness is too large to sit still.
ramacharitamanas::1632.insight: It turns emotion into vivid movement, showing joy as something that naturally seeks connection.

ramacharitamanas::1633.verse_sanskrit: बरषि सुमन सुर सुंदरि गावहिं। मुदित देव दुंदुभीं बजावहिं॥ बस्तु सकल राखीं नृप आगें। बिनय कीन्हि तिन्ह अति अनुरागें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1633.verse_hindi: देवसुंदरियाँ फूल बरसाकर गीत गा रही हैं और देवता आनंदित होकर नगाड़े बजा रहे हैं। (अगवानी में आए हुए) उन लोगों ने सब चीजें दशरथजी के आगे रख दीं और अत्यन्त प्रेम से विनती की ॥
ramacharitamanas::1633.english_translation: The divine maidens shower flowers and sing, while the radiant beings joyfully beat drums. They placed all gifts before King Dasharatha and bowed with deep affection.
ramacharitamanas::1633.translation_literal: बरषि (showering) / सुमन (flowers) / सुर (radiant beings) / सुंदरि (maidens) / गावहिं (sing) / मुदित (joyful) / देव (divine beings) / दुंदुभीं (drums) / बजावहिं (beat) / बस्तु (things) / सकल (all) / राखीं (placed) / नृप (king) / आगें (before) / बिनय (humble request) / कीन्हि (made) / तिन्ह (they) / अति (very) / अनुरागें (with love)
ramacharitamanas::1633.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1633.essence: True festivity bows before what it honors.
ramacharitamanas::1633.simple_meaning: Heavenly beings celebrate the wedding procession, place gifts before Dasharatha, and greet him with loving respect.
ramacharitamanas::1633.simple_insight: Joy feels complete when it is shared with humility and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1633.detailed_meaning: The marriage procession has arrived in Mithila, and the city is alive with welcome. Divine beings shower flowers, sing, and beat drums while the hosts offer gifts and respectful words before King Dasharatha. The verse lingers on the beauty of honored arrival.
ramacharitamanas::1633.modern_relevance: A bride’s family opens the door, the guests step in, and the room fills with music, gifts, and bowed heads. The moment becomes sacred because everyone enters with respect.
ramacharitamanas::1633.insight: It turns celebration into reverence, showing that joy deepens when pride steps aside.

ramacharitamanas::1634.verse_sanskrit: प्रेम समेत रायँ सबु लीन्हा। भै बकसीस जाचकन्हि दीन्हा॥ करि पूजा मान्यता बड़ाई। जनवासे कहुँ चले लवाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1634.verse_hindi: राजा दशरथजी ने प्रेम सहित सब वस्तुएँ ले लीं, फिर उनकी बख्शीशें होने लगीं और वे याचकों को दे दी गईं। तदनन्तर पूजा, आदर-सत्कार और बड़ाई करके अगवान लोग उनको जनवासे की ओर लिवा ले चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1634.english_translation: With affection, the king received everything. Gifts were then handed to the petitioners. After worship, honor, and praise, the escorts led them toward the guest quarters.
ramacharitamanas::1634.translation_literal: प्रेम समेत (with affection) / रायँ (the king) / सबु (all) / लीन्हा (took/received) / भै (became) / बकसीस (gifts) / जाचकन्हि (to the petitioners) / दीन्हा (given) / करि (doing) / पूजा (worship) / मान्यता (respect) / बड़ाई (praise) / जनवासे (to the guest quarters) / कहुँ (toward) / चले (went) / लवाई (caused to be led)
ramacharitamanas::1634.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1634.essence: Honor is complete only when it flows onward.
ramacharitamanas::1634.simple_meaning: King Dasharath receives the offerings with affection, gives gifts to those who ask, and is then escorted with honor to the guest quarters.
ramacharitamanas::1634.simple_insight: Respect becomes real when it is shared generously, not just displayed.
ramacharitamanas::1634.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the wedding guests are being honored after the swayamvar. Dasharath accepts the offerings warmly, gives gifts to the needy, and is escorted with ceremony toward the guest quarters. The verse keeps the procession moving, showing the abundance and courtesy of the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1634.modern_relevance: You arrive at a ceremony where every gesture matters: the welcome, the gifts, the walk to the room. The point is not status, but graciousness.
ramacharitamanas::1634.insight: It shifts attention from receiving honor to returning honor through generosity.

ramacharitamanas::1635.verse_sanskrit: बसन बिचित्र पाँवड़े परहीं। देखि धनदु धन मदु परिहरहीं॥ अति सुंदर दीन्हेउ जनवासा। जहँ सब कहुँ सब भाँति सुपासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1635.verse_hindi: विलक्षण वस्त्रों के पाँवड़े पड़ रहे हैं, जिन्हें देखकर कुबेर भी अपने धन का अभिमान छोड़ देते हैं। बड़ा सुंदर जनवासा दिया गया, जहाँ सबको सब प्रकार का सुभीता था ॥
ramacharitamanas::1635.english_translation: There were exquisite carpets underfoot; even Kubera would give up pride in wealth at the sight. A beautiful guest-house was provided, where everyone had every comfort.
ramacharitamanas::1635.translation_literal: बसन (cloths) / बिचित्र (wonderful, varied) / पाँवड़े (carpets, floor coverings) / परहीं (were laid) / देखि (seeing) / धनद (Kubera, lord of wealth) / दु (even) / धन (wealth) / मदु (pride) / परिहरहीं (would give up, abandon) / अति (very) / सुंदर (beautiful) / दीन्हेउ (was given) / जनवासा (guest-house, lodging for the wedding party) / जहँ (where) / सब कहुँ (for everyone) / सब भाँति (in every way) / सुपासा (comfortable, easy, well-arranged)
ramacharitamanas::1635.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1635.essence: Wealth becomes humble when it serves everyone well.
ramacharitamanas::1635.simple_meaning: The wedding arrangements were lavish and welcoming. The carpets, lodging, and comfort were so fine that even the lord of wealth would lose his pride.
ramacharitamanas::1635.simple_insight: True abundance is not showing off wealth; it is making everyone feel fully cared for.
ramacharitamanas::1635.detailed_meaning: Janakpur is preparing for Sita’s wedding, and the welcome for the arriving guests is overflowing with beauty and care. The carpets, lodging, and hospitality are so splendid that the poet says even Kubera would drop his pride.
ramacharitamanas::1635.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where every detail has been thought through — the seating, the food, the shade, the welcome. Nobody feels like a burden. That kind of care is its own wealth.
ramacharitamanas::1635.insight: It shifts attention from display to hospitality: the measure of prosperity is how completely others are at ease.

ramacharitamanas::1636.verse_sanskrit: जानी सियँ बरात पुर आई। कछु निज महिमा प्रगटि जनाई॥ हृदयँ सुमिरि सब सिद्धि बोलाईं। भूप पहुनई करन पठाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1636.verse_hindi: सीताजी ने बारात जनकपुर में आई जानकर अपनी कुछ महिमा प्रकट करके दिखलाई। हृदय में स्मरणकर सब सिद्धियों को बुलाया और उन्हें राजा दशरथजी की मेहमानी करने के लिए भेजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1636.english_translation: Knowing that the wedding procession had arrived in Janakpur, Sita revealed a little of her own splendor. Remembering it in her heart, she called all powers and sent them to honor King Dasharath.
ramacharitamanas::1636.translation_literal: जानी (knowing) / सियँ (Sita) / बरात (wedding procession) / पुर (city) / आई (arrived) / कछु (some) / निज (own) / महिमा (glory) / प्रगटि (revealing) / जनाई (showed) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / सुमिरि (remembering) / सब (all) / सिद्धि (powers/perfections) / बोलाईं (called) / भूप (king) / पहुनई (hospitality) / करन (to do) / पठाईं (sent)
ramacharitamanas::1636.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1636.essence: Greatness becomes real when it serves without announcing itself.
ramacharitamanas::1636.simple_meaning: Sita notices the wedding procession has arrived and, with quiet power, arranges a grand welcome for Dasharath. Her inner greatness appears through service and hospitality.
ramacharitamanas::1636.simple_insight: True greatness does not announce itself loudly; it shows up in how generously it welcomes others.
ramacharitamanas::1636.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the wedding procession has arrived. Sita quietly reveals her hidden splendor, gathers her powers in remembrance, and sends them to serve King Dasharath. The scene shows her divine grace expressed as honour and hospitality.
ramacharitamanas::1636.modern_relevance: You hear guests are coming, and suddenly the whole house comes alive — cleaning, cooking, arranging, welcoming. The best host does not make a speech; the care is visible in every detail.
ramacharitamanas::1636.insight: It shifts attention from status to gracious action: power becomes visible through service, not display.

ramacharitamanas::1637.verse_sanskrit: सिधि सब सिय आयसु अकनि गईं जहाँ जनवास। लिएँ संपदा सकल सुख सुरपुर भोग बिलास ॥
ramacharitamanas::1637.verse_hindi: सीताजी की आज्ञा सुनकर सब सिद्धियाँ जहाँ जनवासा था, वहाँ सारी सम्पदा, सुख और इंद्रपुरी के भोग-विलास को लिए हुए गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1637.english_translation: When Sita gave the order, all the siddhis went to the guest quarters carrying wealth, comfort, and the pleasures of the gods' city.
ramacharitamanas::1637.translation_literal: सिधि सब (all siddhis) / सिय (Sita) / आयसु (order) / अकनि (hearing) / गईं (went) / जहाँ (where) / जनवास (guest quarters) / लिएँ (carrying) / संपदा (wealth) / सकल (all) / सुख (comforts) / सुरपुर (city of the gods) / भोग (enjoyments) / बिलास (luxury)
ramacharitamanas::1637.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1637.essence: Sita's command turns hospitality into abundance.
ramacharitamanas::1637.simple_meaning: Sita's command sends all divine powers to the guest quarters with every kind of wealth and delight.
ramacharitamanas::1637.simple_insight: True honor draws abundance without effort or display.
ramacharitamanas::1637.detailed_meaning: Janak's city is receiving Ram's wedding party. After Sita's subtle display of majesty, the siddhis obey her command and bring every comfort to the guests' lodging. The scene shows how fully Janakpur welcomes the divine marriage.
ramacharitamanas::1637.modern_relevance: A home opens for guests, and everything feels quietly ready: extra bedding, food, warmth, care. Real hospitality does not brag; it makes people feel richly received.
ramacharitamanas::1637.insight: It shifts attention from showing wealth to creating welcome.

ramacharitamanas::1638.verse_sanskrit: निज निज बास बिलोकि बराती। सुर सुख सकल सुलभ सब भाँती॥ बिभव भेद कछु कोउ न जाना। सकल जनक कर करहिं बखाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1638.verse_hindi: बारातियों ने अपने-अपने ठहरने के स्थान देखे तो वहाँ देवताओं के सब सुखों को सब प्रकार से सुलभ पाया। इस ऐश्वर्य का कुछ भी भेद कोई जान न सका। सब जनकजी की बड़ाई कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1638.english_translation: The wedding guests saw their own places and found every pleasure of the higher realm available in every way. No one could understand the details of this splendor. Everyone praised King Janaka.
ramacharitamanas::1638.translation_literal: निज निज (each one's own) / बास (lodging, place of stay) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बराती (wedding guests) / सुर (radiant beings, higher realm) / सुख (pleasures) / सकल (all) / सुलभ (easily available) / सब भाँती (in every way) / बिभव (splendor, wealth) / भेद (details, distinctions) / कछु (some) / कोउ (anyone) / न (not) / जाना (knew) / सकल (all) / जनक (Janaka) / कर (of) / करहिं (they do) / बखाना (praise)
ramacharitamanas::1638.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1638.essence: Real magnificence makes everyone feel at home.
ramacharitamanas::1638.simple_meaning: The wedding guests found their lodging filled with heavenly comfort and unmatched splendour, beyond anyone's full understanding. Everyone praised Janaka for it.
ramacharitamanas::1638.simple_insight: A generous host makes others feel held, honoured, and at ease.
ramacharitamanas::1638.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the wedding guests arrive for Sita's swayamvar and find their own lodgings transformed with effortless abundance. The splendour is so complete that no one can even grasp its full extent, and all of them praise Janaka.
ramacharitamanas::1638.modern_relevance: You walk into a home where every detail has been thought through before you arrived. The room is ready, the water is poured, the welcome is already there — and you feel cared for before saying a word.
ramacharitamanas::1638.insight: It shifts attention from display to hospitality: true greatness makes others comfortable, not impressed.

ramacharitamanas::1639.verse_sanskrit: सिय महिमा रघुनायक जानी। हरषे हृदयँ हेतु पहिचानी॥ पितु आगमनु सुनत दोउ भाई। हृदयँ न अति आनंदु अमाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1639.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी यह सब सीताजी की महिमा जानकर और उनका प्रेम पहचानकर हृदय में हर्षित हुए। पिता दशरथजी के आने का समाचार सुनकर दोनों भाइयों के हृदय में महान आनंद समाता न था ॥
ramacharitamanas::1639.english_translation: Raghunath understood Sita's greatness and rejoiced, recognizing her love. Hearing of Father Dasharath's arrival, both brothers felt such joy that their hearts could not contain it.
ramacharitamanas::1639.translation_literal: सिय (Sita) / महिमा (greatness) / रघुनायक (Lord of the Raghu clan) / जानी (having known) / हरषे (rejoiced) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / हेतु (cause) / पहिचानी (having recognized) / पितु (father) / आगमनु (arrival) / सुनत (hearing) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / न (not) / अति (very) / आनंदु (joy) / अमाई (did not fit / could not be contained)
ramacharitamanas::1639.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1639.essence: True joy comes from recognizing love and longing for what is coming.
ramacharitamanas::1639.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are filled with joy. Ram sees Sita's worth and love clearly, and both brothers overflow with happiness at hearing their father is coming.
ramacharitamanas::1639.simple_insight: Love deepens when it is recognized; joy also rises when a longed-for presence is near.
ramacharitamanas::1639.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the bridal celebration is unfolding in splendour. Ram sees Sita's greatness and responds with gladness; Lakshman and Ram then hear that King Dasharath is arriving, and their joy becomes too large to hold.
ramacharitamanas::1639.modern_relevance: You spot someone’s care in the smallest gesture and feel your own heart open. Then you hear a parent is on the way, and the whole room suddenly feels brighter.
ramacharitamanas::1639.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to recognition: real joy comes from seeing love clearly and welcoming family.

ramacharitamanas::1640.verse_sanskrit: सकुचन्ह कहि न सकत गुरु पाहीं। पितु दरसन लालचु मन माहीं॥ बिस्वामित्र बिनय बड़ि देखी। उपजा उर संतोषु बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1640.verse_hindi: संकोचवश वे गुरु विश्वामित्रजी से कह नहीं सकते थे, परन्तु मन में पिताजी के दर्शनों की लालसा थी। विश्वामित्रजी ने उनकी बड़ी नम्रता देखी, तो उनके हृदय में बहुत संतोष उत्पन्न हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1640.english_translation: Out of shyness, they could not speak to the guru, yet their minds longed to see their father. Seeing Vishvamitra's great humility, a deep satisfaction arose in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::1640.translation_literal: सकुचन्ह (out of shyness) / कहि (speaking) / न सकत (could not) / गुरु पाहीं (before the guru) / पितु (father) / दरसन (darshan, sight) / लालचु (longing) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / बिस्वामित्र (Vishvamitra) / बिनय (humility) / बड़ि (great) / देखी (seeing) / उपजा (arose) / उर (in the heart) / संतोषु (contentment) / बिसेषी (great)
ramacharitamanas::1640.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1640.essence: Shyness can still reveal the heart clearly.
ramacharitamanas::1640.simple_meaning: They feel shy before the teacher, but their hearts long to see their father. Vishvamitra notices their humility and feels pleased.
ramacharitamanas::1640.simple_insight: Quiet respect and modesty can move a wise teacher more than words.
ramacharitamanas::1640.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, the two brothers are caught between reverence for Vishvamitra and longing for Dasharath’s arrival. They cannot bring themselves to speak openly, but their restraint reveals their tenderness. Vishvamitra sees this and feels deep satisfaction.
ramacharitamanas::1640.modern_relevance: You sit across from a mentor, wanting to ask about family news but holding back out of respect. The silence itself reveals your heart, and the elder understands anyway.
ramacharitamanas::1640.insight: It shows that humility can communicate more than direct speech.

ramacharitamanas::1641.verse_sanskrit: हरषि बंधु दोउ हृदयँ लगाए। पुलक अंग अंबक जल छाए॥ चले जहाँ दसरथु जनवासे। मनहुँ सरोबर तकेउ पिआसे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1641.verse_hindi: प्रसन्न होकर उन्होंने दोनों भाइयों को हृदय से लगा लिया। उनका शरीर पुलकित हो गया और नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया। वे उस जनवासे को चले, जहाँ दशरथजी थे। मानो सरोवर प्यासे की ओर लक्ष्य करके चला हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1641.english_translation: Delighted, he embraced both brothers to his heart. His body thrilled, and his eyes filled with tears. He went to the camp where Dasharath was, like a thirsty one moving toward a lake.
ramacharitamanas::1641.translation_literal: हरषि (delighted) / बंधु (brothers) / दोउ (both) / हृदयँ (to the heart) / लगाए (embraced) / पुलक (hairs standing on end) / अंग (body) / अंबक (eyes) / जल (water/tears) / छाए (covered) / चले (went) / जहाँ (where) / दसरथु (Dasharath) / जनवासे (at the camp) / मनहुँ (as if) / सरोबर (lake) / तकेउ (went toward) / पिआसे (thirsty one)
ramacharitamanas::1641.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1641.essence: Longing turns the heart toward its beloved like thirst toward water.
ramacharitamanas::1641.simple_meaning: Dasharath joyfully hugs both sons, his body trembles with emotion, and he rushes to meet them, longing for their sight.
ramacharitamanas::1641.simple_insight: Love can make even a king move like a thirsty person toward water.
ramacharitamanas::1641.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has arrived at the tournament grounds and sees his sons after a long wait. Overcome with affection, he embraces both of them, trembles, and walks toward the camp where they are staying. The moment is about a father’s longing finally finding its object.
ramacharitamanas::1641.modern_relevance: You spot your child across a crowded station after days away. Your body moves before your thoughts do. This is what love looks like when it finally reaches what it has been missing.
ramacharitamanas::1641.insight: It turns reunion into a bodily event, showing how longing becomes immediate action.

ramacharitamanas::1642.verse_sanskrit: भूप बिलोके जबहिं मुनि आवत सुतन्ह समेत। उठे हरषि सुखसिंधु महुँ चले थाह सी लेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::1642.verse_hindi: जब राजा दशरथजी ने पुत्रों सहित मुनि को आते देखा, तब वे हर्षित होकर उठे और सुख के समुद्र में थाह सी लेते हुए चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1642.english_translation: When King Dasharath saw the sage arrive with his sons, he rose joyfully and walked as if measuring the depths of a sea of bliss.
ramacharitamanas::1642.translation_literal: भूप (king) / बिलोके (saw) / जबहिं (when) / मुनि (sage) / आवत (coming) / सुतन्ह (with sons) / समेत (together) / उठे (rose) / हरषि (joyfully) / सुखसिंधु (sea of bliss) / महुँ (in) / चले (walked) / थाह (depth) / सी (like) / लेत (taking/measuring)
ramacharitamanas::1642.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1642.essence: Long-awaited presence turns joy into motion.
ramacharitamanas::1642.simple_meaning: Dasharath sees Vishwamitra arrive with the princes and rises with great joy.
ramacharitamanas::1642.simple_insight: Joy makes even a king move like a child running to welcome what he loves.
ramacharitamanas::1642.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has been waiting for this moment in Ayodhya. When Vishwamitra arrives with Ram and Lakshman, the king rises at once, overflowing with delight. The verse simply shows the warmth of that reunion before the formal greeting begins.
ramacharitamanas::1642.modern_relevance: You spot someone you’ve been waiting for at the station, and your whole body lifts before your mind catches up. Some arrivals speak before any words do.
ramacharitamanas::1642.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to emotion: the heart moves first, and the body follows.

ramacharitamanas::1643.verse_sanskrit: मुनिहि दंडवत कीन्ह महीसा। बार बार पद रज धरि सीसा॥ कौसिक राउ लिए उर लाई। कहि असीस पूछी कुसलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1643.verse_hindi: पृथ्वीपति दशरथजी ने मुनि की चरणधूलि को बारंबार सिर पर चढ़ाकर उनको दण्डवत् प्रणाम किया। विश्वामित्रजी ने राजा को उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया और आशीर्वाद देकर कुशल पूछी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1643.english_translation: King Dasharath bowed to the sage again and again, pressing the sage's dust to his head. Kaushik raised him into his arms, gave blessings, and asked after his welfare.
ramacharitamanas::1643.translation_literal: मुनिहि (to the sage) / दंडवत (full prostration) / कीन्ह (did) / महीसा (lord of the earth) / बार बार (again and again) / पद रज (dust of the feet) / धरि (placing) / सीसा (on the head)॥ / कौसिक (Kaushik) / राउ (king) / लिए (took) / उर लाई (into the chest) / कहि (speaking) / असीस (blessings) / पूछी (asked) / कुसलाई (welfare)॥
ramacharitamanas::1643.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1643.essence: Humility opens the door before any request is made.
ramacharitamanas::1643.simple_meaning: King Dasharath bows fully to the sage, touching the sage's feet dust to his head. The sage lifts him up, blesses him, and asks how he is.
ramacharitamanas::1643.simple_insight: Respect softens pride. A true meeting begins when both sides meet with humility.
ramacharitamanas::1643.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has come to receive Vishwamitra with his sons. The king falls at the sage's feet again and again, and Vishwamitra responds with warmth, blessing him and drawing him close. Their meeting sets the tone for the sacred request that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1643.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where someone older, wiser, or more experienced is waiting. Instead of performing confidence, you lower your guard first — and the whole conversation changes.
ramacharitamanas::1643.insight: It teaches you to begin important relationships with humility, not status.

ramacharitamanas::1644.verse_sanskrit: पुनि दंडवत करत दोउ भाई। देखि नृपति उर सुखु न समाई॥ सुत हियँ लाइ दुसह दुख मेटे। मृतक सरीर प्रान जनु भेंटे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1644.verse_hindi: फिर दोनों भाइयों को दण्डवत् प्रणाम करते देखकर राजा के हृदय में सुख समाया नहीं। पुत्रों को (उठाकर) हृदय से लगाकर उन्होंने अपने (वियोगजनित) दुःसह दुःख को मिटाया। मानो मृतक शरीर को प्राण मिल गए हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1644.english_translation: Seeing both brothers bow again, the king could not contain his joy. He drew his sons to his heart and the unbearable pain of separation vanished, as if life had returned to a dead body.
ramacharitamanas::1644.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / दंडवत करत (bowing down) / दोउ भाई (both brothers) / देखि (seeing) / नृपति (the king) / उर (in the heart) / सुखु (joy) / न समाई (did not fit) ॥ / सुत (sons) / हियँ (to the heart) / लाइ (embracing) / दुसह (unbearable) / दुख (pain) / मेटे (was removed) ॥ / मृतक (dead) / सरीर (body) / प्रान (life-breath) / जनु (as if) / भेंटे (met) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1644.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1644.essence: Separation ends, and the heart feels life return.
ramacharitamanas::1644.simple_meaning: Dasharath sees both sons bow again, overflows with joy, and hugs them close. The pain of separation briefly disappears, like life returning to a lifeless body.
ramacharitamanas::1644.simple_insight: Love can feel like breath returning after a long absence.
ramacharitamanas::1644.detailed_meaning: After Dasharath welcomes Vishvamitra and the boys, he sees Rama and Lakshmana bow once more. The sight overwhelms him. He pulls both sons to his chest, and the grief of separation lifts for a moment in pure parental relief.
ramacharitamanas::1644.modern_relevance: You spot your child across the platform after days apart, and your chest loosens before you even speak. Some joy is so physical it feels like breath returning.
ramacharitamanas::1644.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to reunion: the body remembers love before words do.

ramacharitamanas::1645.verse_sanskrit: पुनि बसिष्ठ पद सिर तिन्ह नाए। प्रेम मुदित मुनिबर उर लाए॥ बिप्र बृंद बंदे दुहुँ भाईं। मनभावती असीसें पाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1645.verse_hindi: फिर उन्होंने वशिष्ठजी के चरणों में सिर नवाया। मुनि श्रेष्ठ ने प्रेम के आनंद में उन्हें हृदय से लगा लिया। दोनों भाइयों ने सब ब्राह्मणों की वंदना की और मनभाए आशीर्वाद पाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1645.english_translation: Then they bowed their heads at Vashishtha's feet. The great sage, filled with love, embraced them. Both brothers bowed to the Brahmins and received blessings that pleased their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1645.translation_literal: पुनि (then) / बसिष्ठ (Vashishtha) / पद (feet) / सिर (head) / तिन्ह (they) / नाए (bowed) / प्रेम (love) / मुदित (filled with joy) / मुनिबर (great sage) / उर (chest) / लाए (embraced) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / बृंद (group) / बंदे (bowed to) / दुहुँ (both) / भाईं (brothers) / मनभावती (heart-pleasing) / असीसें (blessings) / पाईं (received)
ramacharitamanas::1645.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1645.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman bow to Vashishtha and the Brahmins. The sage embraces them with affection, and they receive blessings that delight the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1645.simple_insight: Respect softens everyone in the room. Humility opens the door to warmth, blessing, and belonging.
ramacharitamanas::1645.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, after the great bow is won, the two brothers move through the court with reverence. They bow first to Vashishtha, then to the Brahmins. The sage and the priests respond with affection and blessings, showing the ideal order of honour and grace.
ramacharitamanas::1645.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a big win and choose humility over display. The people around you feel the difference immediately, and the atmosphere turns warm.
ramacharitamanas::1645.insight: It teaches you to meet honour with humility, and to let respect create connection instead of pride.

ramacharitamanas::1646.verse_sanskrit: भरत सहानुज कीन्ह प्रनामा। लिए उठाइ लाइ उर रामा॥ हरषे लखन देखि दोउ भ्राता। मिले प्रेम परिपूरित गाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1646.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न सहित श्री रामचन्द्रजी को प्रणाम किया। श्री रामजी ने उन्हें उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया। लक्ष्मणजी दोनों भाइयों को देखकर हर्षित हुए और प्रेम से परिपूर्ण हुए शरीर से उनसे मिले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1646.english_translation: Bharat, with Shatrughna beside him, bowed to Ram. Ram lifted him up and embraced him. Lakshman rejoiced at seeing both brothers and met them with a body full of love.
ramacharitamanas::1646.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / सहानुज (with younger brother) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रनामा (salutation) / लिए (took) / उठाइ (lifting up) / लाइ (bringing) / उर (to the chest) / रामा (Ram) / हरषे (rejoiced) / लखन (Lakshman) / देखि (seeing) / दोउ (both) / भ्राता (brothers) / मिले (met) / प्रेम (with love) / परिपूरित (filled completely) / गाता (body)
ramacharitamanas::1646.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1646.essence: Respect and love erase the distance between brothers.
ramacharitamanas::1646.simple_meaning: Bharat and Shatrughna bow to Ram. Ram lifts Bharat up and embraces him. Lakshman is overjoyed to see the brothers and welcomes them with love.
ramacharitamanas::1646.simple_insight: Love becomes visible when respect, welcome, and joy move through the body.
ramacharitamanas::1646.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat arrives with Shatrughna and bows before Ram. Ram immediately lifts him into an embrace, while Lakshman is moved with joy at the reunion. The verse captures the warmth of a family restored before the public gathering begins.
ramacharitamanas::1646.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after months apart, unsure whether anyone still feels the same. Then someone stands, pulls you close, and all the distance disappears in one embrace.
ramacharitamanas::1646.insight: It shifts attention from formal greeting to the healing power of affectionate recognition.

ramacharitamanas::1647.verse_sanskrit: पुरजन परिजन जातिजन जाचक मंत्री मीत। मिले जथाबिधि सबहि प्रभु परम कृपाल बिनीत ॥
ramacharitamanas::1647.verse_hindi: तदन्तर परम कृपालु और विनयी श्री रामचन्द्रजी अयोध्यावासियों, कुटुम्बियों, जाति के लोगों, याचकों, मंत्रियों और मित्रों सभी से यथा योग्य मिले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1647.english_translation: Then the supremely compassionate and humble Lord met all properly: the townspeople, relatives, people of his caste, petitioners, ministers, and friends.
ramacharitamanas::1647.translation_literal: पुरजन (townspeople) / परिजन (relatives) / जातिजन (people of the same community) / जाचक (petitioners) / मंत्री (ministers) / मीत (friends) / मिले (met) / जथाबिधि (according to proper manner) / सबहि (all) / प्रभु (Lord) / परम कृपाल (supremely compassionate) / बिनीत (humble)
ramacharitamanas::1647.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1647.essence: Greatness is proved by equal warmth toward everyone.
ramacharitamanas::1647.simple_meaning: Ram meets everyone in the right way, from relatives and citizens to petitioners, ministers, and friends. He does it with humility and kindness.
ramacharitamanas::1647.simple_insight: True greatness shows itself in how gently someone treats every person, not just the important ones.
ramacharitamanas::1647.detailed_meaning: After the wedding, Ram returns to the people of Ayodhya. The celebration is not only for nobles and family; he meets everyone properly, from townspeople to petitioners. The moment shows his humility and the breadth of his grace.
ramacharitamanas::1647.modern_relevance: At a family gathering, you notice the person everyone admires also remembers the server, the driver, and the shy cousin. That small equality reveals the character more than any speech.
ramacharitamanas::1647.insight: It shifts attention from status to respect, showing that dignity must be distributed, not reserved.

ramacharitamanas::1648.verse_sanskrit: रामहि देखि बरात जुड़ानी। प्रीति कि रीति न जाति बखानी॥ नृप समीप सोहहिं सुत चारी। जनु धन धरमादिक तनुधारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1648.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर बारात शीतल हुई (राम के वियोग में सबके हृदय में जो आग जल रही थी, वह शांत हो गई)। प्रीति की रीति का बखान नहीं हो सकता। राजा के पास चारों पुत्र ऐसी शोभा पा रहे हैं, मानो अर्थ, धर्म, काम और मोक्ष शरीर धारण किए हुए हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1648.english_translation: Seeing Ram, the wedding party became calm. Love's way cannot be described. The king's four sons shone beside him, like embodied wealth, duty, desire, and freedom.
ramacharitamanas::1648.translation_literal: रामहि (Ram) / देखि (seeing) / बरात (wedding party) / जुड़ानी (became soothed) / प्रीति (love) / कि (of) / रीति (way) / न (not) / जाति (goes) / बखानी (described) / नृप (king) / समीप (near) / सोहहिं (shone) / सुत (sons) / चारी (four) / जनु (as if) / धन (wealth) / धरमादिक (duty and the rest) / तनुधारी (having bodies)
ramacharitamanas::1648.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1648.essence: Ram's presence soothes, and love itself becomes impossible to explain.
ramacharitamanas::1648.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram calmed the whole wedding party. His presence creates a love that words cannot fully explain. The four princes beside Dasharath shine like wealth, duty, desire, and freedom made visible.
ramacharitamanas::1648.simple_insight: Some presences quiet the heart before any words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1648.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the wedding procession reaches the king's side and Ram stands before everyone. His presence cools the crowd's longing and wonder. The poet then lifts the scene into symbol, showing the four brothers as living forms of human aims.
ramacharitamanas::1648.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a tense family argument, and one person’s calm changes everything. No speech fixes it. Their presence does the work first.
ramacharitamanas::1648.insight: It shifts attention from explanation to presence: some qualities are felt before they are understood.

ramacharitamanas::1649.verse_sanskrit: सुतन्ह समेत दसरथहि देखी। मुदित नगर नर नारि बिसेषी॥ सुमन बरिसि सुर हनहिं निसाना। नाकनटीं नाचहिं करि गाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1649.verse_hindi: पुत्रों सहित दशरथजी को देखकर नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष बहुत ही प्रसन्न हो रहे हैं। (आकाश में) देवता फूलों की वर्षा करके नगाड़े बजा रहे हैं और अप्सराएँ गा-गाकर नाच रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1649.english_translation: Seeing Dasharatha together with his sons, the people of the city—men and women—were especially delighted. The deities showered flowers, beat drums, and celestial singers danced and sang.
ramacharitamanas::1649.translation_literal: सुतन्ह समेत (together with sons) / दसरथहि (Dasharatha) / देखी (seeing) / मुदित (delighted) / नगर (city) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / बिसेषी (especially) ॥ / सुमन (flowers) / बरिसि (showering) / सुर (deities) / हनहिं (beating) / निसाना (drums) / नाकनटीं (celestial women) / नाचहिं (dance) / करि (doing) / गाना (singing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1649.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1649.essence: Arrival itself can make a city feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::1649.simple_meaning: The city rejoices at Dasharatha’s arrival with his sons, while the heavenly beings celebrate above with flowers, music, and dance.
ramacharitamanas::1649.simple_insight: Joy deepens when a home’s long-awaited return becomes visible to everyone.
ramacharitamanas::1649.detailed_meaning: Dasharatha arrives in Ayodhya with his sons after the wedding celebration. The whole city lights up with happiness, and even the heavens join in with flowers, drums, singing, and dancing. This is a scene of public joy, not a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::1649.modern_relevance: A father walks in after a long trip, and the whole house changes at once. The relief is not private anymore—faces soften, voices rise, and the room feels blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1649.insight: It frames reunion as something larger than one family, turning private happiness into shared celebration.

ramacharitamanas::1650.verse_sanskrit: सतानंद अरु बिप्र सचिव गन। मागध सूत बिदुष बंदीजन॥ सहित बरात राउ सनमाना। आयसु मागि फिरे अगवाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1650.verse_hindi: अगवानी में आए हुए शतानंदजी, अन्य ब्राह्मण, मंत्रीगण, मागध, सूत, विद्वान और भाटों ने बारात सहित राजा दशरथजी का आदर-सत्कार किया। फिर आज्ञा लेकर वे वापस लौटे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1650.english_translation: Shatananda, the other brahmins, ministers, bards, singers, scholars, and praise-speakers honoured King Dasharatha along with the wedding party. Taking permission, they returned to lead the procession onward.
ramacharitamanas::1650.translation_literal: सतानंद (Shatananda) / अरु (and) / बिप्र (brahmins) / सचिव गन (groups of ministers) / मागध (bards) / सूत (singers) / बिदुष (scholars) / बंदीजन (praise-speakers) / सहित (together with) / बरात (wedding party) / राउ (king) / सनमाना (honoured) / आयसु (permission) / मागि (asking) / फिरे (returned) / अगवाना (those who had come to welcome)
ramacharitamanas::1650.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1650.essence: True welcome respects, then steps aside.
ramacharitamanas::1650.simple_meaning: The welcoming party honours Dasharatha and the wedding procession, then asks permission to go back and continue leading them.
ramacharitamanas::1650.simple_insight: Respect can be active and orderly. Even celebration moves forward through courtesy.
ramacharitamanas::1650.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur’s gate, Shatananda arrives with brahmins, ministers, singers, scholars, and praise-speakers to receive Dasharatha’s wedding party. They honour the king properly, then ask leave to return and guide the procession onward. The verse keeps the festive movement flowing.
ramacharitamanas::1650.modern_relevance: A host greets arriving guests, handles the introductions, and then steps back so the event can continue smoothly. Good hospitality knows when to lead and when to let the moment move on.
ramacharitamanas::1650.insight: It shows that grace includes both honouring others and knowing when to withdraw.

ramacharitamanas::1651.verse_sanskrit: प्रथम बरात लगन तें आई। तातें पुर प्रमोदु अधिकाई॥ ब्रह्मानंदु लोग सब लहहीं। बढ़हुँ दिवस निसि बिधि सन कहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1651.verse_hindi: बारात लग्न के दिन से पहले आ गई है, इससे जनकपुर में अधिक आनंद छा रहा है। सब लोग ब्रह्मानंद प्राप्त कर रहे हैं और विधाता से मनाकर कहते हैं कि दिन-रात बढ़ जाएँ (बड़े हो जाएँ) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1651.english_translation: The wedding procession arrived before the auspicious day, so the city’s joy grew even greater. Everyone felt overwhelming delight and begged time itself to stretch longer.
ramacharitamanas::1651.translation_literal: प्रथम (first) / बरात (wedding procession) / लगन (auspicious wedding day) / तें (from) / आई (came) / तातें (therefore) / पुर (city) / प्रमोदु (joy) / अधिकाई (greater)॥ / ब्रह्मानंदु (supreme bliss) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / लहहीं (receive) / बढ़हुँ (increase) / दिवस (days) / निसि (nights) / बिधि (fate/order) / सन (to) / कहहीं (say) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1651.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1651.essence: Joy makes people ask time to slow down.
ramacharitamanas::1651.simple_meaning: The wedding party arrives early, and the whole city becomes even happier. People feel such joy that they wish time would move more slowly.
ramacharitamanas::1651.simple_insight: Some moments feel so full that even waiting becomes sweet.
ramacharitamanas::1651.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, Dasharath’s wedding procession has arrived ahead of the appointed day. The whole city is overflowing with joy at Ram and Sita’s coming union, and the people long for the days and nights to last longer.
ramacharitamanas::1651.modern_relevance: You get the message that the guests have arrived early, and suddenly the whole house feels brighter. No one wants the evening to end because something beloved is already here.
ramacharitamanas::1651.insight: It captures how joy can make time feel too small for what the heart is receiving.

ramacharitamanas::1652.verse_sanskrit: रामु सीय सोभा अवधि सुकृत अवधि दोउ राज। जहँ तहँ पुरजन कहहिं अस मिलि नर नारि समाज ॥
ramacharitamanas::1652.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी और सीताजी सुंदरता की सीमा हैं और दोनों राजा पुण्य की सीमा हैं, जहाँ-तहाँ जनकपुरवासी स्त्री-पुरुषों के समूह इकट्ठे हो-होकर यही कह रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1652.english_translation: Ram and Sita are the limit of beauty, and both are the limit of merit. Wherever people gather, men and women of the city say this.
ramacharitamanas::1652.translation_literal: रामु (Ram) / सीय (Sita) / सोभा (beauty) / अवधि (limit) / सुकृत (merit) / अवधि (limit) / दोउ (both) / राज (kings) / जहँ तहँ (wherever) / पुरजन (city people) / कहहिं (say) / अस (thus) / मिलि (gathering) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / समाज (assembly)
ramacharitamanas::1652.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1652.essence: Beauty and virtue seem complete when Ram and Sita arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1652.simple_meaning: The people of Janakpur see Ram and Sita as the highest expression of beauty and virtue, and they keep saying so to one another.
ramacharitamanas::1652.simple_insight: Some moments are so full of grace that a whole city can only speak in praise.
ramacharitamanas::1652.detailed_meaning: Janakpur is alive with wedding excitement. As the people gather, they look at Ram and Sita and feel that beauty and merit have reached their limit in these two. This verse captures the public wonder before the next praise deepens it.
ramacharitamanas::1652.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and everyone goes quiet for a second because something rare has arrived. Some presences do not need an introduction; they change the atmosphere by being there.
