ramacharitamanas::1652.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary admiration to recognising a presence that feels complete and unsurpassable.

ramacharitamanas::1653.verse_sanskrit: जनक सुकृत मूरति बैदेही। दसरथ सुकृत रामु धरें देही॥ इन्ह सम काहुँ न सिव अवराधे। काहुँ न इन्ह समान फल लाधे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1653.verse_hindi: जनकजी के सुकृत (पुण्य) की मूर्ति जानकीजी हैं और दशरथजी के सुकृत देह धारण किए हुए श्री रामजी हैं। इन (दोनों राजाओं) के समान किसी ने शिवजी की आराधना नहीं की और न इनके समान किसी ने फल ही पाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1653.english_translation: Janak's accumulated merit has become Vaidehi, and Dasharath's accumulated merit has taken bodily form as Ram. No one has worshipped Shiva like these two, and no one has received such fruits.
ramacharitamanas::1653.translation_literal: जनक (Janak) / सुकृत (merit) / मूरति (embodiment) / बैदेही (Vaidehi, Sita) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / सुकृत (merit) / रामु (Ram) / धरें (having taken) / देही (body) / इन्ह (these) / सम (like) / काहुँ (anyone) / न (not) / सिव (Shiva) / अवराधे (worshipped) / काहुँ (anyone) / न (not) / इन्ह (these) / समान (equal) / फल (fruit) / लाधे (received)
ramacharitamanas::1653.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1653.essence: True devotion returns as living blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1653.simple_meaning: Janak and Dasharath’s good deeds have taken form as Sita and Ram. Their devotion to Shiva brought incomparable results.
ramacharitamanas::1653.simple_insight: Deep devotion is not wasted; it can ripen into a life of sacred beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1653.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the wedding celebration has turned into praise. Tulsidas pauses the scene to say that Janak’s merit became Sita and Dasharath’s merit became Ram. Their devotion to Shiva bore the highest possible fruit.
ramacharitamanas::1653.modern_relevance: You spend years doing quiet, unglamorous good while no one notices. Then one day you see the shape it made: trust, character, and a life that blesses others.
ramacharitamanas::1653.insight: It shifts attention from effort as expense to effort as seed, showing that devotion can mature into visible grace.

ramacharitamanas::1654.verse_sanskrit: इन्ह सम कोउ न भयउ जग माहीं। है नहिं कतहूँ होनेउ नाहीं॥ हम सब सकल सुकृत कै रासी। भए जग जनमि जनकपुर बासी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1654.verse_hindi: इनके समान जगत में न कोई हुआ, न कहीं है, न होने का ही है। हम सब भी सम्पूर्ण पुण्यों की राशि हैं, जो जगत में जन्म लेकर जनकपुर के निवासी हुए, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1654.english_translation: No one in the world was like them, is like them, or will ever be like them. We too are a heap of good deeds, born into the world and living in Janakpur.
ramacharitamanas::1654.translation_literal: इन्ह सम (like them) / कोउ (anyone) / न (not) / भयउ (was) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / है (is) / नहिं (not) / कतहूँ (anywhere) / होनेउ (will be) / नाहीं (not) / हम (we) / सब (all) / सकल (all) / सुकृत (good deeds) / कै (of) / रासी (heap) / भए (became) / जग (world) / जनमि (having been born) / जनकपुर (Janakpur) / बासी (residents)
ramacharitamanas::1654.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1654.essence: Some presences are so rare they make comparison fail.
ramacharitamanas::1654.simple_meaning: No one compares to Ram and Sita. The people of Janakpur feel blessed just to have been born there and to witness them.
ramacharitamanas::1654.simple_insight: Some moments make ordinary life feel sacred just by proximity.
ramacharitamanas::1654.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the wedding crowd is overwhelmed by Ram and Sita's beauty and grace. The people speak with wonder, saying no one like them has ever existed and calling themselves fortunate simply to live in the city where this sight unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::1654.modern_relevance: You stand in a crowded temple courtyard, and for a moment everyone falls silent at the sight of a bride and groom who seem made for each other. The room knows it has witnessed something rare.
ramacharitamanas::1654.insight: It shifts attention from comparison to reverent recognition of extraordinary grace.

ramacharitamanas::1655.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह जानकी राम छबि देखी। को सुकृती हम सरिस बिसेषी॥ पुनि देखब रघुबीर बिआहू। लेब भली बिधि लोचन लाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1655.verse_hindi: और जिन्होंने जानकीजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी की छबि देखी है। हमारे सरीखा विशेष पुण्यात्मा कौन होगा! और अब हम श्री रघुनाथजी का विवाह देखेंगे और भलीभाँति नेत्रों का लाभ लेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1655.english_translation: Those who have seen the beauty of Janaki and Ram are the most fortunate. Now we will see Raghubir's wedding and gain the true reward of our eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1655.translation_literal: जिन्ह (those who) / जानकी (Janaki) / राम (Ram) / छबि (beauty) / देखी (have seen) / को (who) / सुकृती (fortunate, virtuous) / हम (we) / सरिस (like, equal to) / बिसेषी (especially, श्रेष्ठ)॥ / पुनि (again, now) / देखब (will see) / रघुबीर (Raghubir, Ram) / बिआहू (wedding) / लेब (will take) / भली बिधि (in a good way, properly) / लोचन (eyes) / लाहू (profit, reward) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1655.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1655.essence: Seeing Ram and Janaki is itself the reward.
ramacharitamanas::1655.simple_meaning: The speaker says that anyone who has seen Ram and Janaki is truly blessed, and that watching their wedding will be the eyes' greatest reward.
ramacharitamanas::1655.simple_insight: Some sights feel like a blessing in themselves. Beauty can become a form of reward.
ramacharitamanas::1655.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the wedding scene is about to unfold. The onlookers, especially the women, feel overwhelmed by the sight of Janaki and Ram and speak in joyful wonder. This verse is part of that shared excitement, not the passage’s final teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1655.modern_relevance: You finally reach the temple festival after months of waiting, and the first glimpse of the procession makes the whole journey feel worthwhile.
ramacharitamanas::1655.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary seeing to reverent witnessing of what is precious.

ramacharitamanas::1656.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं परसपर कोकिलबयनीं। एहि बिआहँ बड़ लाभु सुनयनीं॥ बड़ें भाग बिधि बात बनाई। नयन अतिथि होइहहिं दोउ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1656.verse_hindi: कोयल के समान मधुर बोलने वाली स्त्रियाँ आपस में कहती हैं कि हे सुंदर नेत्रों वाली! इस विवाह में बड़ा लाभ है। बड़े भाग्य से विधाता ने सब बात बना दी है, ये दोनों भाई हमारे नेत्रों के अतिथि हुआ करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1656.english_translation: Women with cuckoo-like sweet voices speak among themselves: “O beautiful-eyed one, this wedding brings great fortune. By great luck, the creator has arranged everything; these two brothers will become guests for our eyes.”
ramacharitamanas::1656.translation_literal: कहहिं (they say) / परसपर (to one another) / कोकिलबयनीं (with cuckoo-like voices) / एहि (in this) / बिआहँ (wedding) / बड़ (great) / लाभु (gain, fortune) / सुनयनीं (beautiful-eyed women) / बड़ें (great) / भाग (luck, fortune) / बिधि (the creator) / बात (arrangement, matter) / बनाई (made, arranged) / नयन (eyes) / अतिथि (guest) / होइहहिं (will become) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::1656.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1656.essence: A blessed meeting turns everyone into a witness of joy.
ramacharitamanas::1656.simple_meaning: The women praise the wedding as a great blessing. They feel fortunate that the two beautiful brothers will be present before their eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1656.simple_insight: Beauty and blessing can feel like a gift to the whole community, not just to the couple.
ramacharitamanas::1656.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the wedding preparations are overflowing with joy. Women with sweet voices speak to one another, marveling that destiny has arranged this moment. They see Rama and Lakshman as a rare sight that will delight everyone watching.
ramacharitamanas::1656.modern_relevance: You arrive at a wedding hall where everyone keeps turning to look at the groom’s entrance. The room feels lighter because beauty, joy, and blessing are being shared by all.
ramacharitamanas::1656.insight: It frames a sacred celebration as a communal delight, not a private event.

ramacharitamanas::1657.verse_sanskrit: बारहिं बार सनेह बस जनक बोलाउब सीय। लेन आइहहिं बंधु दोउ कोटि काम कमनीय ॥
ramacharitamanas::1657.verse_hindi: जनकजी स्नेहवश बार-बार सीताजी को बुलावेंगे और करोड़ों कामदेवों के समान सुंदर दोनों भाई सीताजी को लेने (विदा कराने) आया करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1657.english_translation: Again and again, out of affection, Janak will call Sita; the two brothers, beautiful like millions of Cupids, will come to escort her.
ramacharitamanas::1657.translation_literal: बारहिं बार (again and again) / सनेह बस (under the power of affection) / जनक (Janak) / बोलाउब (will call) / सीय (Sita) / लेन (to take) / आइहहिं (will come) / बंधु दोउ (both brothers) / कोटि (crore / millions) / काम (Cupid) / कमनीय (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::1657.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1657.essence: Affection turns farewell into a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1657.simple_meaning: Janak will keep calling Sita with affection, and Ram and Lakshman will come to take her away in beauty and honour.
ramacharitamanas::1657.simple_insight: Love makes even a farewell feel tender, not painful.
ramacharitamanas::1657.detailed_meaning: At Sita's wedding in Mithila, the guests are already imagining the farewell. Janak's affection for his daughter and the radiant arrival of Ram and Lakshman create a scene of joyful sending-off, not loss.
ramacharitamanas::1657.modern_relevance: You keep walking your daughter to the car, then calling her back for one more hug. The parting hurts, but love keeps turning it into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1657.insight: It frames separation as an act of affection, not abandonment.

ramacharitamanas::1658.verse_sanskrit: बिबिध भाँति होइहि पहुनाई। प्रिय न काहि अस सासुर माई॥ तब तब राम लखनहि निहारी। होइहहिं सब पुर लोग सुखारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1658.verse_hindi: तब उनकी अनेकों प्रकार से पहुनाई होगी। सखी! ऐसी ससुराल किसे प्यारी न होगी! तब-तब हम सब नगर निवासी श्री राम-लक्ष्मण को देख-देखकर सुखी होंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1658.english_translation: She will be welcomed in many ways. Who would not love such a home? Then all the people of the city will feel happy just seeing Ram and Lakshman again and again.
ramacharitamanas::1658.translation_literal: बिबिध भाँति (in various ways) / होइहि (will happen) / पहुनाई (hospitality, welcoming) / प्रिय (dear, beloved) / न (not) / काहि (to whom) / अस (such) / सासुर (in-laws' home) / माई (mother) / तब (then) / तब (again and again) / राम (Ram) / लखनहि (Lakshman) / निहारी (seeing) / होइहहिं (will become) / सब (all) / पुर (city) / लोग (people) / सुखारी (happy)
ramacharitamanas::1658.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1658.essence: A noble union makes an entire city rejoice.
ramacharitamanas::1658.simple_meaning: Sita’s new home will welcome her warmly, and the city will rejoice whenever Ram and Lakshman are seen.
ramacharitamanas::1658.simple_insight: Joy deepens when a home, a marriage, and a whole city all feel blessed together.
ramacharitamanas::1658.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the wedding celebration is being imagined before it fully unfolds. The women speak of Sita’s honourable reception and of the delight the whole city will feel whenever Ram and Lakshman are seen. It is a scene of shared joy, not teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1658.modern_relevance: At a wedding hall, relatives keep stepping aside just to catch another glimpse of the couple. The happiness is bigger than the ceremony itself; everyone feels it in the room.
ramacharitamanas::1658.insight: It turns a private marriage into a public blessing and a shared delight.

ramacharitamanas::1659.verse_sanskrit: सखि जस राम लखन कर जोटा। तैसेइ भूप संग हुइ ढोटा॥ स्याम गौर सब अंग सुहाए। ते सब कहहिं देखि जे आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1659.verse_hindi: हे सखी! जैसा श्री राम-लक्ष्मण का जोड़ा है, वैसे ही दो कुमार राजा के साथ और भी हैं। वे भी एक श्याम और दूसरे गौर वर्ण के हैं, उनके भी सब अंग बहुत सुंदर हैं। जो लोग उन्हें देख आए हैं, वे सब यही कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1659.english_translation: O friend, just as Ram and Lakshman are a pair, so are the two princes with the king. One is dark, the other fair, and all their limbs are lovely. Everyone who has seen them says the same.
ramacharitamanas::1659.translation_literal: सखि (O friend) / जस (just as) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / कर (of) / जोटा (pair) / तैसेइ (just so) / भूप (king) / संग (with) / हुइ (being) / ढोटा (princes) / स्याम (dark) / गौर (fair) / सब (all) / अंग (limbs) / सुहाए (beautiful) / ते (they) / सब (all) / कहहिं (say) / देखि (having seen) / जे (who) / आए (came)
ramacharitamanas::1659.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1659.essence: Beauty becomes unforgettable when two forms belong together.
ramacharitamanas::1659.simple_meaning: The two princes are described as a beautiful pair, one dark and one fair, and everyone who sees them praises their beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1659.simple_insight: Some presence is so striking that people agree without argument.
ramacharitamanas::1659.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court during Sita's swayamvar preparations, the people keep comparing every noble pair to Ram and Lakshman. Now they notice the king's two princes too, and their beauty becomes part of the same excited, admiring atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::1659.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the whole mood changes before anyone speaks. People notice not just appearance, but the rare harmony between two people standing together.
ramacharitamanas::1659.insight: It shifts attention from isolated beauty to the power of a matching pair.

ramacharitamanas::1660.verse_sanskrit: कहा एक मैं आजु निहारे। जनु बिरंचि निज हाथ सँवारे॥ भरतु राम ही की अनुहारी। सहसा लखि न सकहिं नर नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1660.verse_hindi: एक ने कहा- मैंने आज ही उन्हें देखा है, इतने सुंदर हैं, मानो ब्रह्माजी ने उन्हें अपने हाथों सँवारा है। भरत तो श्री रामचन्द्रजी की ही शकल-सूरत के हैं। स्त्री-पुरुष उन्हें सहसा पहचान नहीं सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1660.english_translation: One person said, “I saw them today. They are so beautiful, as if Brahma shaped them with his own hands.” Bharat resembles Ram so closely that men and women cannot recognize him at once.
ramacharitamanas::1660.translation_literal: कहा (said) / एक (one) / मैं (I) / आजु (today) / निहारे (saw) / जनु (as if) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / निज (own) / हाथ (hands) / सँवारे (shaped)॥ / भरतु (Bharat) / राम (Ram) / ही (only) / की (of) / अनुहारी (resembling) / सहसा (suddenly/at once) / लखि (to recognize) / न (not) / सकहिं (can) / नर (men) / नारी (women)॥
ramacharitamanas::1660.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1660.essence: Bharat’s face carries Ram’s likeness so fully that recognition lags behind wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1660.simple_meaning: Someone says Bharat looks so much like Ram that people cannot recognize him immediately. His beauty seems divinely crafted.
ramacharitamanas::1660.simple_insight: Sometimes a presence is so striking that words fail before it.
ramacharitamanas::1660.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyā, people are speaking about Ram, Lakshman, Bharat, and Shatrughna as the brothers appear together. One observer is stunned by Bharat’s likeness to Ram and says he seems fashioned by Brahma himself. The verse heightens the wonder of the brothers before the wedding scene continues.
ramacharitamanas::1660.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a family gathering and stop mid-sentence because they carry the same face as someone you deeply miss. Recognition arrives late, but the resemblance lands instantly.
ramacharitamanas::1660.insight: It trains attention toward likeness, beauty, and the quiet wonder of seeing kinship in another face.

ramacharitamanas::1661.verse_sanskrit: लखनु सत्रुसूदनु एकरूपा। नख सिख ते सब अंग अनूपा॥ मन भावहिं मुख बरनि न जाहीं। उपमा कहुँ त्रिभुवन कोउ नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1661.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मण और शत्रुघ्न दोनों का एक रूप है। दोनों के नख से शिखा तक सभी अंग अनुपम हैं। मन को बड़े अच्छे लगते हैं, पर मुख से उनका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता। उनकी उपमा के योग्य तीनों लोकों में कोई नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1661.english_translation: Lakshman and Shatrughna are one in form. From head to toe, every limb is incomparable. The mind delights in them, but the mouth cannot describe them. In the three worlds, no one is their equal.
ramacharitamanas::1661.translation_literal: लखनु (Lakshman) / सत्रुसूदनु (Shatrughna) / एकरूपा (of one form) / नख (nails) / सिख (head-top) / ते (from) / सब (all) / अंग (limbs) / अनूपा (matchless) / मन (mind) / भावहिं (delight) / मुख (mouth) / बरनि (describing) / न जाहीं (cannot go) / उपमा (comparison) / कहुँ (for) / त्रिभुवन (three worlds) / कोउ (anyone) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::1661.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1661.essence: Some forms of grace can only be witnessed, never fully said.
ramacharitamanas::1661.simple_meaning: Lakshman and Shatrughna are perfectly beautiful and beyond comparison. Their charm is so great that words fail to describe it.
ramacharitamanas::1661.simple_insight: Some presence is felt more deeply than it can be explained.
ramacharitamanas::1661.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the crowd is still taking in the sight of Ram, Lakshman, Bharat, and Shatrughna. After praising Ram and Bharat, the speaker turns to Lakshman and Shatrughna, saying their beauty and grace cannot be matched or fully spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1661.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm, grace, and presence stop the room. Everyone tries to explain it, but the real experience is simpler: some people are beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::1661.insight: It shifts attention from analysis to direct appreciation of rare excellence.

ramacharitamanas::1662.verse_sanskrit: उपमा न कोउ कह दास तुलसी कतहुँ कबि कोबिद कहैं। बल बिनय बिद्या सील सोभा सिंधु इन्ह से एइ अहैं॥ पुर नारि सकल पसारि अंचल बिधिहि बचन सुनावहीं॥ ब्याहिअहुँ चारिउ भाइ एहिं पुर हम सुमंगल गावहीं॥
ramacharitamanas::1662.verse_hindi: दास तुलसी कहता है कवि और कोविद (विद्वान) कहते हैं, इनकी उपमा कहीं कोई नहीं है। बल, विनय, विद्या, शील और शोभा के समुद्र इनके समान ये ही हैं। जनकपुर की सब स्त्रियाँ आँचल फैलाकर विधाता को यह वचन (विनती) सुनाती हैं कि चारों भाइयों का विवाह इसी नगर में हो और हम सब सुंदर मंगल गावें।
ramacharitamanas::1662.english_translation: I, Tulsidas the servant, say that no comparison exists anywhere; even poets and scholars cannot find one. Their strength, humility, learning, virtue, and beauty are like oceans, and the women of the city spread their veils before the Creator, praying that all four brothers be married here so this town may sing auspicious songs.
ramacharitamanas::1662.translation_literal: उपमा (comparison) / न (not) / कोउ (anyone) / कह (say) / दास तुलसी (servant Tulsidas) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / कबि (poet) / कोबिद (wise one) / कहैं (say) / बल (strength) / बिनय (humility) / बिद्या (learning) / सील (virtue) / सोभा (beauty) / सिंधु (ocean) / इन्ह (these) / से (like) / एइ (these) / अहैं (are)॥ पुर (city) / नारि (women) / सकल (all) / पसारि (spreading) / अंचल (veils) / बिधिहि (to the Creator) / बचन (words) / सुनावहीं (speak, make heard)॥ ब्याहिअहुँ (may they be married) / चारिउ (all four) / भाइ (brothers) / एहिं (this) / पुर (city) / हम (we) / सुमंगल (auspicious songs) / गावहीं (sing)॥
ramacharitamanas::1662.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1662.essence: True greatness draws praise, humility, and shared celebration at once.
ramacharitamanas::1662.simple_meaning: No one can compare these four brothers to anything else. Their strength, humility, learning, virtue, and beauty seem unmatched, and the women of Janakpur pray that the wedding happen there.
ramacharitamanas::1662.simple_insight: A whole city recognizes rare greatness and responds with joy, reverence, and a wish to bless it.
ramacharitamanas::1662.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the wedding scene is building around Ram and his brothers. Tulsidas steps in to praise their unmatched qualities, while the women of the city lift their veils and pray that all four marriages be completed here in an atmosphere of celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1662.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone quietly feels the same thing: this moment is special. No one is trying to own it; they just want to bless it before it passes.
ramacharitamanas::1662.insight: It shifts attention from judging greatness to reverently receiving it and helping it unfold.

ramacharitamanas::1663.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं परस्पर नारि बारि बिलोचन पुलक तन। सखि सबु करब पुरारि पुन्य पयोनिधि भूप दोउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1663.verse_hindi: नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भरकर पुलकित शरीर से स्त्रियाँ आपस में कह रही हैं कि हे सखी! दोनों राजा पुण्य के समुद्र हैं, त्रिपुरारी शिवजी सब मनोरथ पूर्ण करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1663.english_translation: With eyes full of tears and bodies thrilled with joy, the women say to one another, "Sakhi, both kings are oceans of merit; Tripurari Shiva will fulfill every wish."
ramacharitamanas::1663.translation_literal: कहहिं (they say) / परस्पर (to one another) / नारि (women) / बारि (water) / बिलोचन (eyes) / पुलक (goosebumps, thrill) / तन (body) / सखि (friend) / सबु (all) / करब (will do) / पुरारि (Shiva, destroyer of the triple city) / पुन्य (merit) / पयोनिधि (ocean) / भूप (kings) / दोउ (both)
ramacharitamanas::1663.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1663.essence: Wonder makes the heart trust before the outcome arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1663.simple_meaning: The women at Sita's swayamvar are so moved that they weep and thrill with joy. They praise both kings as highly virtuous and trust Shiva to fulfill their hopes.
ramacharitamanas::1663.simple_insight: Joy and devotion can spill over together, making hope feel alive before anything has happened.
ramacharitamanas::1663.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the women watching Sita's swayamvar are overcome by the sight of the two kings. Their eyes fill with tears, their bodies tremble with delight, and they speak to each other in wonder, praising the scene and placing their hopes in Shiva's grace.
ramacharitamanas::1663.modern_relevance: You sit in a crowded hall watching two people step forward for a life-changing choice, and the whole room leans in. Everyone can feel that something sacred is about to happen.
ramacharitamanas::1663.insight: It turns attention from dry observation to shared wonder and hopeful reverence.

ramacharitamanas::1664.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि सकल मनोरथ करहीं। आनँद उमगि उमगि उर भरहीं॥ जे नृप सीय स्वयंबर आए। देखि बंधु सब तिन्ह सुख पाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1664.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार सब मनोरथ कर रही हैं और हृदय को उमंग-उमंगकर (उत्साहपूर्वक) आनंद से भर रही हैं। सीताजी के स्वयंवर में जो राजा आए थे, उन्होंने भी चारों भाइयों को देखकर सुख पाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1664.english_translation: In this way, everyone was making their hearts' wishes come true, their hearts overflowing with joy. The kings who had come to Sita's swayamvar also felt delight on seeing the four brothers.
ramacharitamanas::1664.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / सकल (all) / मनोरथ (wishes) / करहीं (were making) / आनँद (joy) / उमगि उमगि (surging again and again) / उर (heart) / भरहीं (were filling) / जे (those who) / नृप (kings) / सीय स्वयंबर (Sita's swayamvar) / आए (came) / देखि (seeing) / बंधु (brothers) / सब (all) / तिन्ह (they) / सुख (happiness) / पाए (found)
ramacharitamanas::1664.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1664.essence: Noble presence can quiet rivalry before it starts.
ramacharitamanas::1664.simple_meaning: Everyone at the swayamvar feels joy. The kings are pleased just seeing Ram and his brothers.
ramacharitamanas::1664.simple_insight: Some moments lift everyone at once, even rivals.
ramacharitamanas::1664.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur's swayamvar, the gathered kings are not yet in conflict; they are still caught in the shared wonder of the scene. Seeing Ram and his brothers, they feel a spontaneous joy before the contest begins.
ramacharitamanas::1664.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where even strangers soften for a moment. Before anyone competes, the room itself seems to bless certain people with presence.
ramacharitamanas::1664.insight: It shifts attention from rivalry to shared delight in noble presence.

ramacharitamanas::1665.verse_sanskrit: कहत राम जसु बिसद बिसाला। निज निज भवन गए महिपाला॥ गए बीति कछु दिन एहि भाँती। प्रमुदित पुरजन सकल बराती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1665.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का निर्मल और महान यश कहते हुए राजा लोग अपने-अपने घर गए। इस प्रकार कुछ दिन बीत गए। जनकपुर निवासी और बाराती सभी बड़े आनंदित हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1665.english_translation: The kings returned to their own homes while speaking of Ram's pure, vast glory. In this way, some days passed. The people of Janakpur and all the wedding guests remained delighted.
ramacharitamanas::1665.translation_literal: कहत (saying) / राम जसु (Ram's glory) / बिसद (pure) / बिसाला (vast) / निज निज (each one's own) / भवन (home) / गए (went) / महिपाला (kings)॥ / गए (passed) / बीति (having passed) / कछु (some) / दिन (days) / एहि भाँती (in this manner)॥ / प्रमुदित (delighted) / पुरजन (townspeople) / सकल (all) / बराती (wedding guests)॥
ramacharitamanas::1665.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1665.essence: Ram's glory leaves people joyful even after they go home.
ramacharitamanas::1665.simple_meaning: The kings went home praising Ram, and the wedding party stayed joyful as days passed.
ramacharitamanas::1665.simple_insight: Joy lingers when an event is touched by reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1665.detailed_meaning: After the kings arrive for Sita's swayamvar, the scene settles into celebration. They return home speaking of Ram's glorious name, while Janakpur's people and the wedding guests remain happily absorbed in the moment.
ramacharitamanas::1665.modern_relevance: You leave a ceremony still talking about one person’s grace, and the whole group feels brighter for it. Some moments keep their glow long after the crowd disperses.
ramacharitamanas::1665.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the atmosphere devotion creates around it.

ramacharitamanas::1666.verse_sanskrit: मंगल मूल लगन दिनु आवा। हिम रितु अगहनु मासु सुहावा॥ ग्रह तिथि नखतु जोगु बर बारू। लगन सोधि बिधि कीन्ह बिचारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1666.verse_hindi: मंगलों का मूल लग्न का दिन आ गया। हेमंत ऋतु और सुहावना अगहन का महीना था। ग्रह, तिथि, नक्षत्र, योग और वार श्रेष्ठ थे। लग्न (मुहूर्त) शोधकर ब्रह्माजी ने उस पर विचार किया, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1666.english_translation: The auspicious wedding day arrived. It was the pleasant winter month of Magha. The planets, date, star, yoga, and weekday were all favorable. After checking the auspicious time, Brahma considered the match.
ramacharitamanas::1666.translation_literal: मंगल (auspicious) / मूल (root) / लगन (auspicious time) / दिनु (day) / आवा (arrived) / हिम (cool) / रितु (season) / अगहनु (Magha-like winter month) / मासु (month) / सुहावा (pleasant) / ग्रह (planet) / तिथि (lunar day) / नखतु (star) / जोगु (yoga) / बर (excellent) / बारू (weekday) / लगन (auspicious time) / सोधि (having checked) / बिधि (Brahma) / कीन्ह (did) / बिचारू (consideration)
ramacharitamanas::1666.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1666.essence: A sacred moment arrives when every sign is in harmony.
ramacharitamanas::1666.simple_meaning: The wedding day arrives at the right season and under the right stars. Everything is arranged for the ceremony to begin.
ramacharitamanas::1666.simple_insight: Some moments feel fully aligned, as if life itself has cleared the path.
ramacharitamanas::1666.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, preparations for Sita's swayamvar have reached their peak. The chosen day arrives with every sign favorable, and the court treats the timing itself as blessed. This verse simply marks that auspicious threshold before the next ritual step.
ramacharitamanas::1666.modern_relevance: The room is finally ready, the guests are seated, and the one person you were waiting for has arrived. Before the ceremony begins, you feel that rare sense that everything has come together.
ramacharitamanas::1666.insight: It shifts attention from human planning to the feeling of perfect timing before an important event.

ramacharitamanas::1667.verse_sanskrit: पठै दीन्हि नारद सन सोई। गनी जनक के गनकन्ह जोई॥ सुनी सकल लोगन्ह यह बाता। कहहिं जोतिषी आहिं बिधाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1667.verse_hindi: और उस (लग्न पत्रिका) को नारदजी के हाथ (जनकजी के यहाँ) भेज दिया। जनकजी के ज्योतिषियों ने भी वही गणना कर रखी थी। जब सब लोगों ने यह बात सुनी तब वे कहने लगे- यहाँ के ज्योतिषी भी ब्रह्मा ही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1667.english_translation: He sent that horoscope through Narada. Janaka's astrologers had made the same calculation. When everyone heard this, they said, "The astrologers here are like Brahma himself."
ramacharitamanas::1667.translation_literal: पठै (sent) / दीन्हि (gave) / नारद सन (through Narada) / सोई (that very one) / गनी (calculated) / जनक के (of Janaka) / गनकन्ह (astrologers) / जोई (the same) / सुनी (hearing) / सकल (all) / लोगन्ह (people) / यह बाता (this matter) / कहहिं (they say) / जोतिषी (astrologers) / आहिं (are) / बिधाता (Brahma / the creator)
ramacharitamanas::1667.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1667.essence: Perfect timing is confirmed when careful minds arrive at the same answer.
ramacharitamanas::1667.simple_meaning: Janak sent the horoscope through Narada, and his own astrologers reached the same conclusion. Everyone was amazed by their accuracy.
ramacharitamanas::1667.simple_insight: Careful preparation earns trust when the moment arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1667.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the wedding arrangements are being confirmed. The horoscope is sent through Narada, and Janak's astrologers independently match the same calculation. The crowd marvels at their skill, seeing the timing as perfectly set.
ramacharitamanas::1667.modern_relevance: You double-check the numbers before a major launch, and your team arrives at the same answer from different angles. That quiet agreement builds confidence before the big moment.
ramacharitamanas::1667.insight: It highlights verified timing and shared confidence, not personal opinion.

ramacharitamanas::1668.verse_sanskrit: धेनुधूरि बेला बिमल सकल सुमंगल मूल। बिप्रन्ह कहेउ बिदेह सन जानि सगुन अनुकूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1668.verse_hindi: निर्मल और सभी सुंदर मंगलों की मूल गोधूलि की पवित्र बेला आ गई और अनुकूल शकुन होने लगे, यह जानकर ब्राह्मणों ने जनकजी से कहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1668.english_translation: The pure dusk hour arrived, the source of all auspiciousness. Seeing favorable omens, the Brahmins told King Janaka.
ramacharitamanas::1668.translation_literal: धेनुधूरि बेला (dusk hour) / बिमल (pure) / सकल (all) / सुमंगल (most auspicious) / मूल (source) / बिप्रन्ह (by the Brahmins) / कहेउ (said) / बिदेह सन (to the king of Videha, Janaka) / जानि (knowing) / सगुन (omens) / अनुकूल (favorable)
ramacharitamanas::1668.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1668.essence: Favorable timing announces what should happen next.
ramacharitamanas::1668.simple_meaning: The auspicious dusk hour arrived, and the Brahmins saw that the signs were favorable, so they informed Janaka.
ramacharitamanas::1668.simple_insight: Some moments feel ready before anyone speaks. The right timing can be felt in the air.
ramacharitamanas::1668.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's palace, the wedding preparations for Sita and Ram are reaching their decisive moment. The Brahmins observe the auspicious dusk and favorable signs, then report this to Janaka, prompting the final arrangements to move forward.
ramacharitamanas::1668.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet before the ceremony begins. The planner checks the sky, the clock, the faces in the crowd — and knows the moment has come to proceed.
ramacharitamanas::1668.insight: It shifts attention from forcing events to recognizing when conditions are ready.

ramacharitamanas::1669.verse_sanskrit: उपरोहितहि कहेउ नरनाहा। अब बिलंब कर कारनु काहा॥ सतानंद तब सचिव बोलाए। मंगल सकल साजि सब ल्याए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1669.verse_hindi: तब राजा जनक ने पुरोहित शतानंदजी से कहा कि अब देरी का क्या कारण है। तब शतानंदजी ने मंत्रियों को बुलाया। वे सब मंगल का सामान सजाकर ले आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1669.english_translation: Then King Janak said to the priest, “Why is there still delay?” Shatanand then called the ministers, and they brought all the auspicious preparations.
ramacharitamanas::1669.translation_literal: उपरोहितहि (to the priest) / कहेउ (said) / नरनाहा (the king) / अब (now) / बिलंब (delay) / कर (of) / कारनु (cause) / काहा (what) / सतानंद (Shatanand) / तब (then) / सचिव (ministers) / बोलाए (called) / मंगल (auspicious) / सकल (all) / साजि (arranging) / सब (all) / ल्याए (brought)
ramacharitamanas::1669.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1669.essence: A sacred event still depends on practical readiness.
ramacharitamanas::1669.simple_meaning: Janak asks why the ceremony is delayed, and Shatanand calls the ministers to bring the auspicious items.
ramacharitamanas::1669.simple_insight: Even sacred moments need clear coordination; devotion also shows up as timely preparation.
ramacharitamanas::1669.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s court, the wedding preparations are finally moving. He asks Shatanand why there is any delay, and the priest immediately calls the ministers to arrange everything needed for the auspicious rite.
ramacharitamanas::1669.modern_relevance: The guests are waiting, the room is set, and one missing detail keeps the whole event on hold. Someone has to notice, speak up, and get the preparations moving.
ramacharitamanas::1669.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the discipline of making readiness happen.

ramacharitamanas::1670.verse_sanskrit: संख निसान पनव बहु बाजे। मंगल कलस सगुन सुभ साजे॥ सुभग सुआसिनि गावहिं गीता। करहिं बेद धुनि बिप्र पुनीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1670.verse_hindi: शंख, नगाड़े, ढोल और बहुत से बाजे बजने लगे तथा मंगल कलश और शुभ शकुन की वस्तुएँ (दधि, दूर्वा आदि) सजाई गईं। सुंदर सुहागिन स्त्रियाँ गीत गा रही हैं और पवित्र ब्राह्मण वेद की ध्वनि कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1670.english_translation: Conches, drums, and many other instruments began to sound. Auspicious pots and other good omens were arranged. Beautiful married women sang songs, and pure Brahmins chanted the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::1670.translation_literal: संख (conch) / निसान (drums and battle-kettledrums) / पनव (tambourines) / बहु (many) / बाजे (were played) / मंगल (auspicious) / कलस (pots) / सगुन (omens) / सुभ (good) / साजे (were arranged) / सुभग (fortunate, beautiful) / सुआसिनि (married women) / गावहिं (sing) / गीता (songs) / करहिं (perform) / बेद (Veda) / धुनि (sound) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / पुनीता (pure, holy)
ramacharitamanas::1670.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1670.essence: A sacred occasion is announced by music, ritual, and shared joy.
ramacharitamanas::1670.simple_meaning: The wedding preparations are in full swing: music, auspicious symbols, women singing, and Brahmins chanting sacred sounds.
ramacharitamanas::1670.simple_insight: Some moments are made holy by collective joy, not by private effort.
ramacharitamanas::1670.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, the wedding procession is being prepared with full ceremonial splendor. Conches, drums, women’s songs, and Brahmin chants fill the air. The verse deepens the scene before the bridegroom’s party is formally received.
ramacharitamanas::1670.insight: It frames a sacred occasion as something carried by community, ritual, and shared anticipation.

ramacharitamanas::1671.verse_sanskrit: लेन चले सादर एहि भाँती। गए जहाँ जनवास बराती॥ कोसलपति कर देखि समाजू। अति लघु लाग तिन्हहि सुरराजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1671.verse_hindi: सब लोग इस प्रकार आदरपूर्वक बारात को लेने चले और जहाँ बारातियों का जनवासा था, वहाँ गए। अवधपति दशरथजी का समाज (वैभव) देखकर उनको देवराज इन्द्र भी बहुत ही तुच्छ लगने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1671.english_translation: They went forth respectfully to receive the wedding party and reached the place where the guests were staying. Seeing the assembly of King of Kosala, even Indra seemed very small to them.
ramacharitamanas::1671.translation_literal: लेन चले (went to receive) / सादर (with respect) / एहि भाँती (in this manner) / गए (went) / जहाँ (where) / जनवास (guest quarters) / बराती (wedding guests) / कोसलपति (lord of Kosala) / कर (of) / देखि (seeing) / समाजू (assembly) / अति (very) / लघु (small) / लाग (seemed) / तिन्हहि (to them) / सुरराजू (king of the gods)
ramacharitamanas::1671.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1671.essence: True dignity can make even heaven's king seem small.
ramacharitamanas::1671.simple_meaning: The wedding party is formally received and brought to the guest area. Janak's court is so grand that even Indra seems insignificant beside it.
ramacharitamanas::1671.simple_insight: Greatness can make even the mighty feel small. Awe quiets comparison.
ramacharitamanas::1671.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the marriage preparations are in full motion. The hosts go respectfully to receive the wedding guests and bring them from the lodging area. As the guests see King Janak's magnificent assembly, even Indra's glory feels minor.
ramacharitamanas::1671.modern_relevance: You walk into a hall dressed for a family wedding and stop for a second — the lights, the flowers, the order, the dignity. Some spaces announce respect before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::1671.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary comparison to the felt grandeur of a properly honoured gathering.

ramacharitamanas::1672.verse_sanskrit: भयउ समउ अब धारिअ पाऊ। यह सुनि परा निसानहिं घाऊ ॥ गुरहि पूछि करि कुल बिधि राजा। चले संग मुनि साधु समाजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1672.verse_hindi: (उन्होंने जाकर विनती की-) समय हो गया, अब पधारिए। यह सुनते ही नगाड़ों पर चोट पड़ी। गुरु वशिष्ठजी से पूछकर और कुल की सब रीतियों को करके राजा दशरथजी मुनियों और साधुओं के समाज को साथ लेकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1672.english_translation: “The time has come; please come now.” Hearing this, the drums were struck. After consulting Guru Vashistha and following the family rites, King Dasharath set out with the sages and holy men.
ramacharitamanas::1672.translation_literal: भयउ (has become) / समउ (time) / अब (now) / धारिअ (please hold/come) / पाऊ (feet, come) / यह (this) / सुनि (hearing) / परा (fell/struck) / निसानहिं (on the drums) / घाऊ (blow, strike) / गुरहि (to the guru) / पूछि (asking) / करि (doing) / कुल (family) / बिधि (rites) / राजा (king) / चले (went) / संग (with) / मुनि (sages) / साधु (holy men) / समाजा (assembly)
ramacharitamanas::1672.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1672.essence: Right action moves with guidance and timing.
ramacharitamanas::1672.simple_meaning: The wedding procession is set in motion. Dasharath follows the proper rites, consults his teacher, and goes forward with sages and holy men.
ramacharitamanas::1672.simple_insight: Proper action begins with respect, guidance, and timing.
ramacharitamanas::1672.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the wedding preparations are complete. When the call comes to proceed, drums sound and Dasharath first checks with Vashistha, then follows the family customs. This verse simply moves the marriage scene forward.
ramacharitamanas::1672.modern_relevance: A family gathering is ready, the elders are waiting, and you do not rush ahead on impulse. You pause, ask the right person, and move in the right order.
ramacharitamanas::1672.insight: It teaches that important action should be guided by counsel and custom, not haste.

ramacharitamanas::1673.verse_sanskrit: भाग्य बिभव अवधेस कर देखि देव ब्रह्मादि। लगे सराहन सहस मुख जानि जनम निज बादि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1673.verse_hindi: अवध नरेश दशरथजी का भाग्य और वैभव देखकर और अपना जन्म व्यर्थ समझकर, ब्रह्माजी आदि देवता हजारों मुखों से उसकी सराहना करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1673.english_translation: Seeing the fortune and splendor of the king of Ayodhya, Brahma and the other radiant beings praised him with a thousand mouths, considering their own births wasted.
ramacharitamanas::1673.translation_literal: भाग्य (fortune) / बिभव (splendor) / अवधेस (king of Ayodhya) / कर (of) / देखि (seeing) / देव (radiant beings) / ब्रह्मादि (Brahma and others) / लगे (began) / सराहन (to praise) / सहस (thousand) / मुख (mouths) / जानि (knowing) / जनम (birth) / निज (own) / बादि (wasted)
ramacharitamanas::1673.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1673.essence: Great fortune can make even the radiant beings feel small.
ramacharitamanas::1673.simple_meaning: The heavenly beings see Dasharath's good fortune and greatness and praise him intensely, feeling their own births were less fruitful by comparison.
ramacharitamanas::1673.simple_insight: True greatness can make even the proud feel humbled.
ramacharitamanas::1673.detailed_meaning: At Dasharath's palace in Ayodhya, the wedding atmosphere has become so splendid that even Brahma and the other radiant beings look on with wonder. They praise the king and feel their own existence falls short beside such fortune.
ramacharitamanas::1673.modern_relevance: You walk into a celebration where everything is effortless, warm, and full of grace. The room itself seems to honor someone’s character, not just their status.
ramacharitamanas::1673.insight: It shifts attention from status alone to the virtue and fortune that make a life worthy of praise.

ramacharitamanas::1674.verse_sanskrit: सुरन्ह सुमंगल अवसरु जाना। बरषहिं सुमन बजाइ निसाना॥ सिव ब्रह्मादिक बिबुध बरूथा। चढ़े बिमानन्हि नाना जूथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1674.verse_hindi: देवगण सुंदर मंगल का अवसर जानकर, नगाड़े बजा-बजाकर फूल बरसाते हैं। शिवजी, ब्रह्माजी आदि देववृन्द यूथ (टोलियाँ) बना-बनाकर विमानों पर जा चढ़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::1674.english_translation: The radiant beings knew the moment was auspicious. They showered flowers and beat their drums. Shiva, Brahma, and other exalted hosts rose in many groups aboard their celestial vehicles.
ramacharitamanas::1674.translation_literal: सुरन्ह (radiant beings) / सुमंगल (highly auspicious) / अवसरु (occasion) / जाना (knew) / बरषहिं (they shower) / सुमन (flowers) / बजाइ (beating) / निसाना (drums, battle-drums) / सिव (Shiva) / ब्रह्मादिक (Brahma and others) / बिबुध (deities) / बरूथा (hosts, troops) / चढ़े (mounted, ascended) / बिमानन्हि (on aerial vehicles) / नाना (various) / जूथा (groups)
ramacharitamanas::1674.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1674.essence: A truly blessed moment draws even the heavens into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1674.simple_meaning: The heavenly beings recognize the wedding time as deeply auspicious, so they celebrate with flowers, drums, and celestial processions.
ramacharitamanas::1674.simple_insight: Some moments feel so right that even the heavens seem to celebrate them.
ramacharitamanas::1674.detailed_meaning: As Ram’s wedding approaches in Janakpur, the scene widens beyond the human court. Shiva, Brahma, and other radiant beings gather in festive groups and descend in their celestial vehicles, marking the occasion as sacred and joyful.
ramacharitamanas::1674.modern_relevance: A wedding hall falls quiet for a second, then erupts in cheers as the couple enters. Everyone can feel it: this is one of those rare moments that carries its own blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1674.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary ceremony to the sense that some events reveal a larger order.

ramacharitamanas::1675.verse_sanskrit: प्रेम पुलक तन हृदयँ उछाहू। चले बिलोकन राम बिआहू॥ देखि जनकपुरु सुर अनुरागे। निज निज लोक सबहिं लघु लागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1675.verse_hindi: और प्रेम से पुलकित शरीर हो तथा हृदय में उत्साह भरकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी का विवाह देखने चले। जनकपुर को देखकर देवता इतने अनुरक्त हो गए कि उन सबको अपने-अपने लोक बहुत तुच्छ लगने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1675.english_translation: Filled with love, their bodies thrilled and hearts joyful, they went to behold Ram's wedding. Seeing Janakpur, the radiant beings became so enamored that all their own realms seemed small.
ramacharitamanas::1675.translation_literal: प्रेम (love) / पुलक (thrilled) / तन (body) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / उछाहू (joy) / चले (went) / बिलोकन (to behold) / राम (Ram) / बिआहू (wedding)॥ / देखि (seeing) / जनकपुरु (Janakpur) / सुर (radiant beings) / अनुरागे (became enamored) / निज निज (their own) / लोक (realms) / सबहिं (to all) / लघु (small) / लागे (seemed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1675.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1675.essence: Beauty so complete makes even paradise feel small.
ramacharitamanas::1675.simple_meaning: The radiant beings go joyfully to see Ram's wedding. Janakpur's beauty makes even their own heavenly realms feel small.
ramacharitamanas::1675.simple_insight: Wonder can make even the greatest comforts feel ordinary.
ramacharitamanas::1675.detailed_meaning: The wedding feast in Janakpur is underway, and the radiant beings descend in delight to witness Ram's marriage. Overwhelmed by the beauty before them, they forget the greatness of their own realms.
ramacharitamanas::1675.modern_relevance: You step into a wedding hall glowing with flowers, music, and faces lit by joy. For a moment, every other place you know feels dull beside it.
ramacharitamanas::1675.insight: It shifts attention from possession to wonder, showing how beauty can dissolve pride in status.

ramacharitamanas::1676.verse_sanskrit: चितवहिं चकित बिचित्र बिताना। रचना सकल अलौकिक नाना। नगर नारि नर रूप निधाना। सुघर सुधरम सुसील सुजाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1676.verse_hindi: विचित्र मंडप को तथा नाना प्रकार की सब अलौकिक रचनाओं को वे चकित होकर देख रहे हैं। नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष रूप के भंडार, सुघड़, श्रेष्ठ धर्मात्मा, सुशील और सुजान हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1676.english_translation: They gaze in wonder at the wondrous pavilion and all its many otherworldly designs. The men and women of the city are treasures of beauty, well-formed, virtuous, gentle, and wise.
ramacharitamanas::1676.translation_literal: चितवहिं (they gaze) / चकित (astonished) / बिचित्र (wondrous) / बिताना (pavilion) / रचना (designs) / सकल (all) / अलौकिक (otherworldly) / नाना (various) / नगर (city) / नारि (women) / नर (men) / रूप (beauty/form) / निधाना (treasures) / सुघर (well-formed) / सुधरम (virtuous) / सुसील (gentle) / सुजाना (wise)
ramacharitamanas::1676.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1676.essence: A sacred scene can make even the divine pause in wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1676.simple_meaning: The heavenly visitors are amazed by the wedding pavilion, the many strange decorations, and the beauty and goodness of the city’s people.
ramacharitamanas::1676.simple_insight: Wonder opens the heart before words can.
ramacharitamanas::1676.detailed_meaning: The gods have arrived in Janakpur for Ram’s wedding. They look around at the dazzling pavilion and the city’s people, struck by beauty, virtue, and grace. This verse simply paints the scene before the deeper praise that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1676.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall lit like a dream, and for a second everyone falls quiet. Beauty, order, and kindness can still stop the mind.
ramacharitamanas::1676.insight: It slows the reader into attentive wonder before the celebration’s meaning is revealed.

ramacharitamanas::1677.verse_sanskrit: तिन्हहि देखि सब सुर सुरनारीं। भए नखत जनु बिधु उजिआरीं॥ बिधिहि भयउ आचरजु बिसेषी। निज करनी कछु कतहुँ न देखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1677.verse_hindi: उन्हें देखकर सब देवता और देवांगनाएँ ऐसे प्रभाहीन हो गए जैसे चन्द्रमा के उजियाले में तारागण फीके पड़ जाते हैं। ब्रह्माजी को विशेष आश्चर्य हुआ, क्योंकि वहाँ उन्होंने अपनी कोई करनी (रचना) तो कहीं देखी ही नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1677.english_translation: Seeing them, all the devas and celestial women shone like stars in moonlight. Brahma felt a special wonder, for he could not see his own handiwork there.
ramacharitamanas::1677.translation_literal: तिन्हहि (them) / देखि (seeing) / सब (all) / सुर (devas) / सुरनारीं (celestial women) / भए (became) / नखत (stars) / जनु (as if) / बिधु (moon) / उजिआरीं (in brightness) / बिधिहि (to Brahma) / भयउ (became) / आचरजु (wonder) / बिसेषी (special) / निज (own) / करनी (work/creation) / कछु (some) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / न (not) / देखी (saw)
ramacharitamanas::1677.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1677.essence: Creation falls silent before a beauty it cannot explain.
ramacharitamanas::1677.simple_meaning: The divine beings are overwhelmed by what they see, and even Brahma is astonished because his own creation cannot account for it.
ramacharitamanas::1677.simple_insight: Some moments exceed explanation. Even the maker stands speechless before what has come alive beyond his design.
ramacharitamanas::1677.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the gods and celestial women look on as Rama's wedding draws near. Their own radiance seems dim beside what they witness, and Brahma himself is astonished because this beauty is beyond any ordinary created order.
ramacharitamanas::1677.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and realise the atmosphere is larger than the decorations, larger than the plan. Something has happened there that no spreadsheet or blueprint could have predicted.
ramacharitamanas::1677.insight: It shifts attention from human design to a reality that can surpass design itself.

ramacharitamanas::1678.verse_sanskrit: सिवँ समुझाए देव सब जनि आचरज भुलाहु। हृदयँ बिचारहु धीर धरि सिय रघुबीर बिआहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1678.verse_hindi: तब शिवजी ने सब देवताओं को समझाया कि तुम लोग आश्चर्य में मत भूलो। हृदय में धीरज धरकर विचार तो करो कि यह (भगवान की महामहिमामयी निजशक्ति) श्री सीताजी का और (अखिल ब्रह्माण्डों के परम ईश्वर साक्षात् भगवान) श्री रामचन्द्रजी का विवाह है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1678.english_translation: Then Shiva explained to all the gods: do not lose yourselves in wonder. Hold your mind steady and reflect that this is the marriage of Sita and Raghuvir.
ramacharitamanas::1678.translation_literal: सिवँ (Shiva) / समुझाए (explained) / देव (the gods) / सब (all) / जनि (do not) / आचरज (wonder) / भुलाहु (forget/lose yourselves) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारहु (reflect) / धीर (steady) / धरि (holding) / सिय (Sita) / रघुबीर (Raghuvir) / बिआहु (marriage)
ramacharitamanas::1678.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::1678.essence: Wonder must give way to clear seeing.
ramacharitamanas::1678.simple_meaning: Shiva tells the gods not to be dazzled by the sight. They should steady themselves and understand that they are witnessing the sacred marriage of Sita and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1678.simple_insight: A stunning moment becomes clear when the mind stops trembling and looks again.
ramacharitamanas::1678.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the gods are overwhelmed by the wonder of the scene. Shiva gently corrects them: do not lose your wits in amazement. Look steadily, and see the deeper reality of Sita and Ram's divine union.
ramacharitamanas::1678.modern_relevance: You are watching something beautiful unfold and your mind starts racing with awe, comparison, and noise. Shiva's reminder is simple: settle yourself first, then understand what you are actually seeing.
ramacharitamanas::1678.insight: It shifts attention from dazzlement to steady recognition of what is sacred.

ramacharitamanas::1679.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह कर नामु लेत जग माहीं। सकल अमंगल मूल नसाहीं॥ करतल होहिं पदारथ चारी। तेइ सिय रामु कहेउ कामारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1679.verse_hindi: जिनका नाम लेते ही जगत में सारे अमंगलों की जड़ कट जाती है और चारों पदार्थ (अर्थ, धर्म, काम, मोक्ष) मुट्ठी में आ जाते हैं, ये वही (जगत के माता-पिता) श्री सीतारामजी हैं, काम के शत्रु शिवजी ने ऐसा कहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1679.english_translation: Those whose name, spoken in the world, destroys the root of all inauspiciousness, and whose hands hold all four aims of life—Shiva, enemy of desire, spoke thus of Sita and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1679.translation_literal: जिन्ह (whose) / कर नामु (name) / लेत (taking, speaking) / जग माहीं (in the world) / सकल (all) / अमंगल (inauspiciousness) / मूल (root) / नसाहीं (destroyed) / करतल (in the palm of the hand) / होहिं (become) / पदारथ (aims, attainments) / चारी (four) / तेइ (they only) / सिय रामु (Sita and Ram) / कहेउ (said) / कामारी (enemy of desire, Shiva)
ramacharitamanas::1679.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::1679.essence: Ram's name removes harm and contains every fulfillment.
ramacharitamanas::1679.simple_meaning: Speaking Ram and Sita's name removes the root of all badness. Shiva says that through them, the four aims of life are fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::1679.simple_insight: There is relief in trusting a name that steadies everything before you can fix it yourself.
ramacharitamanas::1679.detailed_meaning: Shiva is explaining the wonder of Ram and Sita to the gods after their amazement at the wedding scene. He says their name itself clears away inauspiciousness, and that the four aims of human life are already held by them.
ramacharitamanas::1679.modern_relevance: You are spiraling before a difficult call, and one steady reminder cuts through the noise. A single sacred word, repeated with trust, can reset the whole mind.
ramacharitamanas::1679.insight: It shifts attention from fear and fragmentation to refuge in Ram's presence and name.

ramacharitamanas::1680.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि संभु सुरन्ह समुझावा। पुनि आगें बर बसह चलावा॥ देवन्ह देखे दसरथु जाता। महामोद मन पुलकित गाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1680.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार शिवजी ने देवताओं को समझाया और फिर अपने श्रेष्ठ बैल नंदीश्वर को आगे बढ़ाया। देवताओं ने देखा कि दशरथजी मन में बड़े ही प्रसन्न और शरीर से पुलकित हुए चले जा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1680.english_translation: In this way Shiva explained the matter to the gods, and then led his noble bull forward. The gods saw Dasharath walking ahead, filled with great joy and his body thrilled with delight.
ramacharitamanas::1680.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / संभु (Shiva) / सुरन्ह (to the gods) / समुझावा (explained) / पुनि (then) / आगें (forward) / बर (noble) / बसह (bull) / चलावा (led)॥ / देवन्ह (the gods) / देखे (saw) / दसरथु (Dasharath) / जाता (going) / महामोद (great joy) / मन (mind) / पुलकित (thrilled) / गाता (body)॥
ramacharitamanas::1680.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1680.essence: Joy shows itself in the body before words arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1680.simple_meaning: Shiva finishes explaining the situation to the gods, and the scene shifts to Dasharath moving forward in joy, his body filled with delight.
ramacharitamanas::1680.simple_insight: Even a sacred gathering is made vivid by the human pulse of joy and motion.
ramacharitamanas::1680.detailed_meaning: Shiva has just reassured the gods about the wedding of Ram and Sita. The procession now moves on, with Dasharath walking ahead in visible bliss. This verse simply carries the scene forward, showing the happiness surrounding the sacred event.
ramacharitamanas::1680.modern_relevance: You catch a parent walking ahead of a wedding procession, smiling before anyone else can. The day is not just ceremony; it is relief, blessing, and shared joy moving together.
ramacharitamanas::1680.insight: It keeps attention on the living emotion inside a public event, not just the event itself.

ramacharitamanas::1681.verse_sanskrit: साधु समाज संग महिदेवा। जनु तनु धरें करहिं सुख सेवा॥ सोहत साथ सुभग सुत चारी। जनु अपबरग सकल तनुधारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1681.verse_hindi: उनके साथ (परम हर्षयुक्त) साधुओं और ब्राह्मणों की मंडली ऐसी शोभा दे रही है, मानो समस्त सुख शरीर धारण करके उनकी सेवा कर रहे हों। चारों सुंदर पुत्र साथ में ऐसे सुशोभित हैं, मानो सम्पूर्ण मोक्ष (सालोक्य, सामीप्य, सारूप्य, सायुज्य) शरीर धारण किए हुए हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1681.english_translation: The company of holy people and priests shone around him, as if joy itself had taken form to serve him. The four beautiful sons beside him shone like freedom itself in embodied form.
ramacharitamanas::1681.translation_literal: साधु समाज (company of holy people) / संग (with) / महिदेवा (great lord) / जनु (as if) / तनु (body) / धरें (having taken) / करहिं (do) / सुख (joy) / सेवा (service)॥ / सोहत (shining) / साथ (with) / सुभग (beautiful) / सुत (sons) / चारी (four) / जनु (as if) / अपबरग (freedom) / सकल (all) / तनुधारी (embodied) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1681.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1681.essence: Holy company makes joy and freedom seem tangible.
ramacharitamanas::1681.simple_meaning: The king is surrounded by holy people and his four beautiful sons. The scene is so radiant that joy and freedom seem to have taken visible form.
ramacharitamanas::1681.simple_insight: Some moments feel blessed simply because the right company is present.
ramacharitamanas::1681.detailed_meaning: Dasharath arrives in a scene already filled with divine attention. Holy people stand around him, and his four sons shine beside him. Tulsidas pauses on the radiance of that gathering before the gods respond with delight.
ramacharitamanas::1681.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where a family is gathered after a long wait, and everyone suddenly seems lighter. No speech is needed — the right presence itself changes the air.
ramacharitamanas::1681.insight: It frames auspicious company as something that visibly transforms a space and makes joy feel embodied.

ramacharitamanas::1682.verse_sanskrit: मरकत कनक बरन बर जोरी। देखि सुरन्ह भै प्रीति न थोरी॥ पुनि रामहि बिलोकि हियँ हरषे। नृपहि सराहि सुमन तिन्ह बरषे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1682.verse_hindi: मरकतमणि और सुवर्ण के रंग की सुंदर जोड़ियों को देखकर देवताओं को कम प्रीति नहीं हुई (अर्थात् बहुत ही प्रीति हुई)। फिर रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर वे हृदय में (अत्यन्त) हर्षित हुए और राजा की सराहना करके उन्होंने फूल बरसाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1682.english_translation: Seeing the beautiful pair in emerald and gold, the gods felt deep delight. Then, beholding Rama, their hearts filled with joy; they praised the king and showered flowers.
ramacharitamanas::1682.translation_literal: मरकत (emerald) / कनक (gold) / बरन (color) / बर (beautiful) / जोरी (pair) / देखि (seeing) / सुरन्ह (the gods) / भै (became) / प्रीति (delight) / न थोरी (not little) / पुनि (then) / रामहि (Rama) / बिलोकि (beholding) / हियँ (in the heart) / हरषे (rejoiced) / नृपहि (the king) / सराहि (praising) / सुमन (flowers) / तिन्ह (they) / बरषे (showered)
ramacharitamanas::1682.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1682.essence: Rama's presence turns beauty into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1682.simple_meaning: The gods admire the royal family and feel even greater joy when they see Rama. They praise Dasharath and shower flowers in blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1682.simple_insight: Joy deepens when the heart recognises what it has been waiting to see.
ramacharitamanas::1682.detailed_meaning: Shiva has led the gods to watch Dasharath's procession in Ayodhya. They first admire the royal splendour, then their joy rises further when Rama appears. Their praise and flower-rain mark the moment as sacred.
ramacharitamanas::1682.modern_relevance: You spot a family arriving at a ceremony, dressed with quiet grace. Then one face in the group stops you cold — the whole room seems brighter because of that presence.
ramacharitamanas::1682.insight: It shifts attention from surface splendour to the presence that gives splendour meaning.

ramacharitamanas::1683.verse_sanskrit: राम रूपु नख सिख सुभग बारहिं बार निहारि। पुलक गात लोचन सजल उमा समेत पुरारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1683.verse_hindi: नख से शिखा तक श्री रामचन्द्रजी के सुंदर रूप को बार-बार देखते हुए पार्वतीजी सहित श्री शिवजी का शरीर पुलकित हो गया और उनके नेत्र (प्रेमाश्रुओं के) जल से भर गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1683.english_translation: Shiva, together with Parvati, kept beholding Ram’s beautiful form from head to toe again and again. Their bodies thrilled with delight and their eyes filled with tears.
ramacharitamanas::1683.translation_literal: राम रूपु (Ram’s form) / नख सिख (from nail to head, from toe to crown) / सुभग (beautiful) / बारहिं बार (again and again) / निहारि (seeing) / पुलक (horripilation, thrill) / गात (body) / लोचन (eyes) / सजल (moist, filled with tears) / उमा समेत (together with Uma/Parvati) / पुरारि (Shiva, enemy of the three cities)
ramacharitamanas::1683.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1683.essence: Repeated seeing turns beauty into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1683.simple_meaning: Shiva and Parvati keep looking at Ram’s beautiful form, and devotion makes their bodies thrill and their eyes fill with tears.
ramacharitamanas::1683.simple_insight: Love changes the body before the mind can explain it.
ramacharitamanas::1683.detailed_meaning: In the Balkand, the divine marriage scene opens into a vision of Ram’s beauty. Shiva and Parvati do not just see him once; they keep looking, overwhelmed. Their tears and trembling bodies show devotion becoming visible.
ramacharitamanas::1683.modern_relevance: You catch a photo of someone you love and stare at it longer than you meant to. Your chest tightens, your eyes soften, and for a moment nothing else matters.
ramacharitamanas::1683.insight: It shifts attention from description to reverent seeing, where repeated remembrance deepens devotion.

ramacharitamanas::1684.verse_sanskrit: केकि कंठ दुति स्यामल अंगा। तड़ित बिनिंदक बसन सुरंगा॥ ब्याह बिभूषन बिबिध बनाए। मंगल सब सब भाँति सुहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1684.verse_hindi: रामजी का मोर के कंठ की सी कांतिवाला (हरिताभ) श्याम शरीर है। बिजली का अत्यन्त निरादर करने वाले प्रकाशमय सुंदर (पीत) रंग के वस्त्र हैं। सब मंगल रूप और सब प्रकार के सुंदर भाँति-भाँति के विवाह के आभूषण शरीर पर सजाए हुए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1684.english_translation: Ram's body is dark like a peacock's neck, with garments bright as lightning. He wears many wedding ornaments, all auspicious and beautiful in every way.
ramacharitamanas::1684.translation_literal: केकि (peacock) / कंठ (neck) / दुति (lustre) / स्यामल (dark) / अंगा (body) / तड़ित (lightning) / बिनिंदक (outshining, putting to shame) / बसन (garments) / सुरंगा (brightly colored) / ब्याह (wedding) / बिभूषन (ornaments) / बिबिध (various) / बनाए (made) / मंगल (auspicious) / सब (all) / सब भाँति (in every way) / सुहाए (beautiful, pleasing)
ramacharitamanas::1684.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1684.essence: Auspicious beauty can make the ordinary world feel consecrated.
ramacharitamanas::1684.simple_meaning: Ram is dressed for the wedding in bright, auspicious ornaments. His dark body and shining clothes make him look beautiful beyond compare.
ramacharitamanas::1684.simple_insight: Beauty can feel sacred when it is aligned with joy, dignity, and readiness.
ramacharitamanas::1684.detailed_meaning: The wedding scene is unfolding in Mithila. Ram stands adorned for marriage, his dark body and bright garments glowing with beauty. This verse lingers on his appearance before the next verse completes the portrait of his face and eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1684.modern_relevance: You see someone dressed for a once-in-a-lifetime ceremony, and everything about them feels composed and radiant. The outer form is not vanity here; it carries meaning, blessing, and joy.
ramacharitamanas::1684.insight: It trains attention to see sacred beauty in form, color, and ceremonial order.

ramacharitamanas::1685.verse_sanskrit: सरद बिमल बिधु बदनु सुहावन। नयन नवल राजीव लजावन॥ सकल अलौकिक सुंदरताई। कहि न जाई मनहीं मन भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1685.verse_hindi: उनका सुंदर मुख शरत्पूर्णिमा के निर्मल चन्द्रमा के समान और (मनोहर) नेत्र नवीन कमल को लजाने वाले हैं। सारी सुंदरता अलौकिक है। (माया की बनी नहीं है, दिव्य सच्चिदानन्दमयी है) वह कहीं नहीं जा सकती, मन ही मन बहुत प्रिय लगती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1685.english_translation: His lovely face is like a clear autumn moon, and his fresh eyes shame newly opened lotuses. All beauty there is beyond the world, beyond speech, and dear to the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1685.translation_literal: सरद (autumn) / बिमल (pure) / बिधु (moon) / बदनु (face) / सुहावन (lovely) / नयन (eyes) / नवल (new) / राजीव (lotus) / लजावन (shaming) / सकल (all) / अलौकिक (otherworldly) / सुंदरताई (beauty) / कहि न जाई (cannot be spoken) / मनहीं मन (in the mind itself) / भाई (became dear)
ramacharitamanas::1685.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1685.essence: Ram's beauty is so complete that words fail before the heart does.
ramacharitamanas::1685.simple_meaning: Ram's face is like a clear autumn moon, and his eyes outshine fresh lotuses. His beauty is beyond ordinary words and wins the heart inwardly.
ramacharitamanas::1685.simple_insight: Some beauty does not just please the eye; it settles the heart before language can catch up.
ramacharitamanas::1685.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar setting, the assembled eyes are fixed on Ram as his bridal splendor is described. Tulsidas lingers on his face and eyes to show that Ram's beauty is not ordinary charm but a divine radiance that leaves everyone wordless.
ramacharitamanas::1685.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone walking into a room and the noise inside you goes quiet. Some presence cannot be explained; it is simply felt first.
ramacharitamanas::1685.insight: It shifts attention from physical description to reverent recognition of a presence that exceeds speech.

ramacharitamanas::1686.verse_sanskrit: बंधु मनोहर सोहहिं संगा। जात नचावत चपल तुरंगा। राजकुअँर बर बाजि देखावहिं। बंस प्रसंसक बिरिद सुनावहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1686.verse_hindi: साथ में मनोहर भाई शोभित हैं, जो चंचल घोड़ों को नचाते हुए चले जा रहे हैं। राजकुमार श्रेष्ठ घोड़ों को (उनकी चाल को) दिखला रहे हैं और वंश की प्रशंसा करने वाले (मागध भाट) विरुदावली सुना रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1686.english_translation: The handsome brothers ride together, guiding their restless horses. Royal princes display fine steeds, while bards sing praises of the dynasty.
ramacharitamanas::1686.translation_literal: बंधु (brothers) / मनोहर (beautiful) / सोहहिं (shine) / संगा (together) / जात (going) / नचावत (making dance) / चपल (restless) / तुरंगा (horses) / राजकुअँर (princes) / बर (excellent) / बाजि (horses) / देखावहिं (show) / बंस (dynasty) / प्रसंसक (praisers) / बिरिद (praise-song) / सुनावहिं (make hear)
ramacharitamanas::1686.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1686.essence: Royal splendor becomes visible in motion and song.
ramacharitamanas::1686.simple_meaning: The princes ride out together on lively horses, looking splendid as bards sing their praises.
ramacharitamanas::1686.simple_insight: Sometimes the moment is simply radiant: grace, motion, and honour all moving together.
ramacharitamanas::1686.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession is in motion. Ram and his brothers ride out as royal princes, their horses prancing while court bards sing of the Raghu line. The verse paints the pageant before Ram’s own horse becomes the focus.
ramacharitamanas::1686.modern_relevance: A wedding convoy rolls past with music, polished cars, and relatives calling out blessings. The scene itself feels complete before anyone even speaks.
ramacharitamanas::1686.insight: It shifts attention from plot to atmosphere, letting the grandeur of the moment carry the meaning.

ramacharitamanas::1687.verse_sanskrit: जेहि तुरंग पर रामु बिराजे। गति बिलोकि खगनायकु लाजे॥ कहि न जाइ सब भाँति सुहावा। बाजि बेषु जनु काम बनावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1687.verse_hindi: जिस घोड़े पर श्री रामजी विराजमान हैं, उसकी (तेज) चाल देखकर गरुड़ भी लजा जाते हैं, उसका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता, वह सब प्रकार से सुंदर है। मानो कामदेव ने ही घोड़े का वेष धारण कर लिया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1687.english_translation: On the horse where Ram is seated, even Garuda would feel shy at its speed. It cannot be fully described; it is beautiful in every way, as if Cupid himself had taken the form of a horse.
ramacharitamanas::1687.translation_literal: जेहि (on which) / तुरंग (horse) / पर (upon) / रामु (Ram) / बिराजे (are seated) / गति (speed, gait) / बिलोकि (seeing) / खगनायकु (Garuda, lord of birds) / लाजे (is ashamed) / कहि (said) / न (not) / जाइ (can be told) / सब भाँति (in every way) / सुहावा (beautiful) / बाजि (horse) / बेषु (form, guise) / जनु (as if) / काम (Cupid) / बनावा (made)
ramacharitamanas::1687.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1687.essence: Even the horse seems divine when Ram sits upon it.
ramacharitamanas::1687.simple_meaning: Ram rides a horse so splendid and swift that even Garuda would be humbled. Its beauty is beyond description, like Cupid himself has taken the horse's form.
ramacharitamanas::1687.simple_insight: A sacred presence can make even an ordinary ride feel radiant and unforgettable.
ramacharitamanas::1687.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar procession, Ram sits on a magnificent horse while the royal assembly looks on. The poet pauses on the horse’s beauty and speed, using this image to heighten Ram’s grandeur before the contest begins.
ramacharitamanas::1687.modern_relevance: You catch one glimpse of someone entering a room with total ease, and everything feels elevated. The clothes, the posture, the movement — all of it carries a presence that cannot be faked.
ramacharitamanas::1687.insight: It shifts attention from the object itself to the radiance that dignity and presence give it.

ramacharitamanas::1688.verse_sanskrit: जनु बाजि बेषु बनाइ मनसिजु राम हित अति सोहई। आपनें बय बल रूप गुन गति सकल भुवन बिमोहई॥ जगमगत जीनु जराव जोति सुमोति मनि मानिक लगे। किंकिनि ललाम लगामु ललित बिलोकिसुर नर मुनि ठगे॥
ramacharitamanas::1688.verse_hindi: मानो श्री रामचन्द्रजी के लिए कामदेव घोड़े का वेश बनाकर अत्यन्त शोभित हो रहा है। वह अपनी अवस्था, बल, रूप, गुण और चाल से समस्त लोकों को मोहित कर रहा है। उसकी सुंदर घुँघरू लगी ललित लगाम को देखकर देवता, मनुष्य और मुनि सभी ठगे जाते हैं।
ramacharitamanas::1688.english_translation: It was as if Cupid himself had taken the form of a horse for Ram, and shone with great beauty. Its age, strength, form, qualities, and gait enchanted all the worlds. The glittering saddle, bright ornaments, and jeweled trappings looked like stars on a glowing body. Its charming reins and bells left gods, humans, and sages stunned.
ramacharitamanas::1688.translation_literal: जनु (as if) / बाजि बेषु (horse-form) / बनाइ (having made) / मनसिजु (Cupid) / राम हित (for Ram's sake) / अति सोहई (shone greatly) / आपनें (its own) / बय (age) / बल (strength) / रूप (form) / गुन (qualities) / गति (gait) / सकल भुवन (all worlds) / बिमोहई (enchanted) / जगमगत (shining) / जीनु (saddle) / जराव (ornamented) / जोति (light) / सुमोति (fine jewels) / मनि (gems) / मानिक (rubies) / लगे (seemed placed) / किंकिनि (bells) / ललाम (beautiful) / लगामु (reins) / ललित (lovely) / बिलोकि (seeing) / सुर (gods) / नर (humans) / मुनि (sages) / ठगे (stunned)
ramacharitamanas::1688.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1688.essence: Beauty can overwhelm even the wise.
ramacharitamanas::1688.simple_meaning: A horse so beautiful appears before Ram that it seems like Cupid himself has taken that form. Its beauty, strength, and ornaments amaze everyone who sees it.
ramacharitamanas::1688.simple_insight: Some moments are so vivid that attention stops and wonder takes over.
ramacharitamanas::1688.detailed_meaning: The horse procession continues at Sita's swayamvar, and this verse lingers on one horse's impossible beauty. Tulsidas pauses the action to show how even gods, humans, and sages are caught by its splendour before Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1688.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of a perfectly prepared wedding car, a stage entrance, or a restored classic and everyone falls quiet for a second. Beauty can still stop a room.
ramacharitamanas::1688.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the power of form, movement, and ornament to overwhelm the mind.

ramacharitamanas::1689.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु मनसहिं लयलीन मनु चलत बाजि छबि पाव। भूषित उड़गन तड़ित घनु जनु बर बरहि नचाव ॥
ramacharitamanas::1689.verse_hindi: प्रभु की इच्छा में अपने मन को लीन किए चलता हुआ वह घोड़ा बड़ी शोभा पा रहा है। मानो तारागण तथा बिजली से अलंकृत मेघ सुंदर मोर को नचा रहा हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1689.english_translation: The horse, with its mind absorbed in the Lord's will, moved in such beauty. Adorned with stars and lightning, it seemed like a cloud making a noble peacock dance.
ramacharitamanas::1689.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / मनसहिं (in the mind/will) / लयलीन (absorbed) / मनु (mind) / चलत (moving) / बाजि (horse) / छबि (beauty) / पाव (found/received) / भूषित (adorned) / उड़गन (stars) / तड़ित (lightning) / घनु (cloud) / जनु (as if) / बर (noble) / बरहि (peacock) / नचाव (makes dance)
ramacharitamanas::1689.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1689.essence: Grace becomes visible when everything moves in harmony.
ramacharitamanas::1689.simple_meaning: The horse is moving in perfect beauty, as if the sky itself is decorating and animating it.
ramacharitamanas::1689.simple_insight: Beauty can feel alive when movement, grace, and wonder come together.
ramacharitamanas::1689.detailed_meaning: Ram sits on a magnificent horse during the Sita swayamvar procession. The poet stops on the horse itself, describing its grace as almost impossible to capture. This verse is part of the visual celebration, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1689.modern_relevance: A wedding procession passes under bright lights, and everyone pauses at one stunning detail — the way movement, color, and music suddenly feel larger than life.
ramacharitamanas::1689.insight: It invites attention to beauty as an experience, not just an object to describe.

ramacharitamanas::1690.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं बर बाजि रामु असवारा। तेहि सारदउ न बरनै पारा॥ संकरु राम रूप अनुरागे। नयन पंचदस अति प्रिय लागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1690.verse_hindi: जिस श्रेष्ठ घोड़े पर श्री रामचन्द्रजी सवार हैं, उसका वर्णन सरस्वतीजी भी नहीं कर सकतीं। शंकरजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी के रूप में ऐसे अनुरक्त हुए कि उन्हें अपने पंद्रह नेत्र इस समय बहुत ही प्यारे लगने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1690.english_translation: On the splendid horse that Ram rides, even Saraswati cannot fully describe it. Shiva became so absorbed in Ram's form that his fifteen eyes felt especially dear to him.
ramacharitamanas::1690.translation_literal: जेहिं (which) / बर (excellent) / बाजि (horse) / रामु (Ram) / असवारा (rider) / तेहि (that) / सारदउ (even Saraswati) / न (not) / बरनै (to describe) / पारा (was able)॥ / संकरु (Shiva) / राम रूप (Ram's form) / अनुरागे (became absorbed in love) / नयन (eyes) / पंचदस (fifteen) / अति (very) / प्रिय (dear) / लागे (became)
ramacharitamanas::1690.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1690.essence: Ram's presence is so radiant that even divine sight falls silent.
ramacharitamanas::1690.simple_meaning: Ram's horse is so splendid that even Saraswati cannot fully describe it. Shiva becomes so absorbed in Ram's beauty that his many eyes feel precious.
ramacharitamanas::1690.simple_insight: A beautiful thing can draw even the greatest minds into wonder and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1690.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, Ram arrives on a magnificent horse. The poet says its beauty defeats description itself, then shifts to Shiva, who is so taken by Ram's form that even his extra eyes feel dear. The moment magnifies Ram's radiance through divine awe.
ramacharitamanas::1690.modern_relevance: You see someone walk into a room and the whole atmosphere changes. Words fail first, then admiration takes over. Some presence is felt before it is understood.
ramacharitamanas::1690.insight: It shifts attention from description to direct awe, showing that devotion begins where language ends.

ramacharitamanas::1691.verse_sanskrit: हरि हित सहित रामु जब जोहे। रमा समेत रमापति मोहे॥ निरखि राम छबि बिधि हरषाने। आठइ नयन जानि पछिताने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1691.verse_hindi: भगवान विष्णु ने जब प्रेम सहित श्री राम को देखा, तब वे (रमणीयता की मूर्ति) श्री लक्ष्मीजी के पति श्री लक्ष्मीजी सहित मोहित हो गए। श्री रामचन्द्रजी की शोभा देखकर ब्रह्माजी बड़े प्रसन्न हुए, पर अपने आठ ही नेत्र जानकर पछताने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1691.english_translation: When Hari saw Ram with loving delight, Lakshmi's lord became enchanted along with Lakshmi. Seeing Ram's beauty, Brahma was delighted, then regretted having only eight eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1691.translation_literal: हरि (Ram/Hari) / हित सहित (with affection) / रामु (Ram) / जब (when) / जोहे (saw) / रमा (Lakshmi) / समेत (along with) / रमापति (Lakshmi's lord) / मोहे (became enchanted) / निरखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / छबि (beauty) / बिधि (Brahma) / हरषाने (was delighted) / आठइ (eight) / नयन (eyes) / जानि (knowing) / पछिताने (regretted)
ramacharitamanas::1691.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1691.essence: Ram's beauty overwhelms even the highest beings.
ramacharitamanas::1691.simple_meaning: Ram's beauty delights even the highest beings. Brahma rejoices at seeing him, then regrets having only eight eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1691.simple_insight: Even the greatest powers feel small before beauty that exceeds their reach.
ramacharitamanas::1691.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, the divine assembly watches Ram's splendour on the royal stage. Hari and Lakshmi are drawn toward him, and Brahma himself is overcome with joy. The verse deepens the wonder by showing that even cosmic beings cannot fully take in Ram's form.
ramacharitamanas::1691.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm and grace make the whole room soften. You smile, then realise you do not have enough attention, enough words, enough of anything to hold that presence.
ramacharitamanas::1691.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary admiration to reverent astonishment before Ram's form.

ramacharitamanas::1692.verse_sanskrit: सुर सेनप उर बहुत उछाहू। बिधि ते डेवढ़ लोचन लाहू॥ रामहि चितव सुरेस सुजाना। गौतम श्रापु परम हित माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1692.verse_hindi: देवताओं के सेनापति स्वामि कार्तिक के हृदय में बड़ा उत्साह है, क्योंकि वे ब्रह्माजी से ड्योढ़े अर्थात बारह नेत्रों से रामदर्शन का सुंदर लाभ उठा रहे हैं। सुजान इन्द्र (अपने हजार नेत्रों से) श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देख रहे हैं और गौतमजी के शाप को अपने लिए परम हितकर मान रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1692.english_translation: The commander of the gods feels great joy in his heart, for he gains the blessed sight of Ram with twelve eyes instead of one pair. Wise Indra gazes at Ram and counts Gautama's curse as a supreme blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1692.translation_literal: सुर सेनप (commander of the gods) / उर (heart) / बहुत (great) / उछाहू (joy) / बिधि (Brahma) / ते (than) / डेवढ़ (one and a half times) / लोचन (eyes) / लाहू (gain)॥ / रामहि (Ram) / चितव (gazes at) / सुरेस (lord of the gods, Indra) / सुजाना (wise) / गौतम (Gautama) / श्रापु (curse) / परम (supreme) / हित (benefit) / माना (considered)
ramacharitamanas::1692.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1692.essence: A setback becomes a blessing when it brings you closer to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1692.simple_meaning: Indra and other heavenly beings are overjoyed to behold Ram. Even a curse is seen as a blessing because it led to this sight.
ramacharitamanas::1692.simple_insight: What looked like punishment can become grace when it leads you to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1692.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar, the gods are watching Ram reveal his divine splendour. Indra, the king of the gods, feels fortunate beyond measure because he can behold Ram with a thousand eyes. Even Gautama's curse now seems like a gift.
ramacharitamanas::1692.modern_relevance: You miss a train, then meet the person who changes your life on the platform. Later, the delay stops looking like bad luck and starts looking like grace.
ramacharitamanas::1692.insight: It shifts the mind from resenting setbacks to recognising how they can open a better sightline.

ramacharitamanas::1693.verse_sanskrit: देव सकल सुरपतिहि सिहाहीं। आजु पुरंदर सम कोउ नाहीं॥ मुदित देवगन रामहि देखी। नृपसमाज दुहुँ हरषु बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1693.verse_hindi: सभी देवता देवराज इन्द्र से ईर्षा कर रहे हैं (और कह रहे हैं) कि आज इन्द्र के समान भाग्यवान दूसरा कोई नहीं है। श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर देवगण प्रसन्न हैं और दोनों राजाओं के समाज में विशेष हर्ष छा रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1693.english_translation: All the gods envy Indra, saying, “Today no one is as fortunate as he.” Seeing Ram, the hosts of gods rejoice, and special joy fills both royal assemblies.
ramacharitamanas::1693.translation_literal: देव (gods) / सकल (all) / सुरपतिहि (to Indra, lord of the gods) / सिहाहीं (envy) / आजु (today) / पुरंदर (Indra) / सम (like) / कोउ (anyone) / नाहीं (is not) / मुदित (glad) / देवगन (hosts of gods) / रामहि (Ram) / देखी (seeing) / नृपसमाज (royal assembly) / दुहुँ (both) / हरषु (joy) / बिसेषी (special, great)
ramacharitamanas::1693.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1693.essence: Ram's presence turns envy into joy.
ramacharitamanas::1693.simple_meaning: The gods feel joy at Ram's presence, and both the divine and royal gatherings are filled with special happiness.
