ramacharitamanas::1693.simple_insight: Real joy spreads outward; when the right presence arrives, even the crowd changes.
ramacharitamanas::1693.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the hall is filling with kings, gods, and expectation. The gods look at Indra with envy, then turn to Ram and rejoice. His arrival lifts the whole assembly into a rare, shared delight.
ramacharitamanas::1693.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when the person everyone was waiting for finally walks in. The mood changes before anyone speaks. Presence itself can settle a crowd and lift its heart.
ramacharitamanas::1693.insight: It shifts attention from status and comparison to the transforming power of a worthy presence.

ramacharitamanas::1694.verse_sanskrit: अति हरषु राजसमाज दुहु दिसि दुंदुभीं बाजहिं घनी। बरषहिं सुमन सुर हरषि कहि जय जयति जय रघुकुलमनी॥ एहि भाँति जानि बरात आवत बाजने बहु बाजहीं। रानी सुआसिनि बोलि परिछनि हेतु मंगल साजहीं॥
ramacharitamanas::1694.verse_hindi: दोनों ओर से राजसमाज में अत्यन्त हर्ष है और बड़े जोर से नगाड़े बज रहे हैं। देवता प्रसन्न होकर और 'रघुकुलमणि श्री राम की जय हो, जय हो, जय हो' कहकर फूल बरसा रहे हैं। इस प्रकार बारात को आती हुई जानकर बहुत प्रकार के बाजे बजने लगे और रानी सुहागिन स्त्रियों को बुलाकर परछन के लिए मंगल द्रव्य सजाने लगीं॥
ramacharitamanas::1694.english_translation: The royal assembly rejoices on both sides; drums thunder loudly. The radiant beings, delighted, shower flowers and cry, "Victory, victory, victory to the jewel of the Raghu clan!" Knowing the wedding procession is arriving, many instruments sound, and the queens call auspicious married women to prepare the ceremonial welcome.
ramacharitamanas::1694.translation_literal: अति (very) / हरषु (joy) / राजसमाज (royal assembly) / दुहु दिसि (on both sides) / दुंदुभीं (drums) / बाजहिं (sound) / घनी (loudly) / बरषहिं (shower) / सुमन (flowers) / सुर (radiant beings) / हरषि (rejoicing) / कहि (saying) / जय जयति जय (victory, victory, victory) / रघुकुलमनी (jewel of the Raghu clan) / एहि भाँति (in this way) / जानि (knowing) / बरात (wedding procession) / आवत (coming) / बाजने (instruments) / बहु (many) / बाजहीं (sound) / रानी (queens) / सुआसिनि (married women) / बोलि (calling) / परिछनि (ceremonial welcome) / हेतु (for) / मंगल (auspicious) / साजहीं (prepare)
ramacharitamanas::1694.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1694.essence: Joy prepares itself before the beloved arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1694.simple_meaning: Everyone rejoices as the wedding procession arrives. Drums sound, flowers fall, and the queens prepare the ceremonial welcome.
ramacharitamanas::1694.simple_insight: Joy becomes visible when people prepare to honour what they love.
ramacharitamanas::1694.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is alive with anticipation as Ram's wedding procession approaches. The royal household, the women of the palace, and even the radiant beings above share the same delight. This verse paints the gathering excitement before the formal welcome begins.
ramacharitamanas::1694.modern_relevance: A house fills with noise before the first guest arrives: cousins rushing, aunties setting trays, someone checking the flowers again. The happiness is not private anymore; it spreads through every room.
ramacharitamanas::1694.insight: It turns arrival into a shared celebration and shows reverence through preparation.

ramacharitamanas::1695.verse_sanskrit: सजि आरती अनेक बिधि मंगल सकल सँवारि। चलीं मुदित परिछनि करन गजगामिनि बर नारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1695.verse_hindi: अनेक प्रकार से आरती सजकर और समस्त मंगल द्रव्यों को यथायोग्य सजाकर गजगामिनी (हाथी की सी चाल वाली) उत्तम स्त्रियाँ आनंदपूर्वक परछन के लिए चलीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1695.english_translation: Women of noble bearing, having arranged the auspicious offerings in many ways, joyfully went out to perform the welcoming ritual.
ramacharitamanas::1695.translation_literal: सजि (having arranged) / आरती (welcoming lamp-offering) / अनेक बिधि (in many ways) / मंगल (auspicious items) / सकल (all) / सँवारि (having arranged) / चलीं (went) / मुदित (joyful) / परिछनि (welcoming ritual) / करन (to do) / गजगामिनि (elephant-gaited) / बर (noble) / नारि (women)
ramacharitamanas::1695.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1695.essence: Welcome itself becomes auspicious when done with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1695.simple_meaning: The noble women prepared the welcoming lamps and all auspicious items, then went joyfully to greet the arriving guests.
ramacharitamanas::1695.simple_insight: Joy can be expressed through careful welcome, not just words.
ramacharitamanas::1695.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the wedding celebration is in full bloom. The noble women of the household prepare the aarti and other auspicious offerings, then move out together to greet the procession with delight. The verse is part of the festive scene, not a teaching statement.
ramacharitamanas::1695.modern_relevance: You are rushing to greet guests before the doorbell rings, straightening the tray, lighting the lamp, making the room feel ready. Careful welcome becomes its own joy.
ramacharitamanas::1695.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony as duty to ceremony as shared delight.

ramacharitamanas::1696.verse_sanskrit: बिधुबदनीं सब सब मृगलोचनि। सब निज तन छबि रति मदु मोचनि॥ पहिरें बरन बरन बर चीरा। सकल बिभूषन सजें सरीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1696.verse_hindi: सभी स्त्रियाँ चन्द्रमुखी (चन्द्रमा के समान मुख वाली) और सभी मृगलोचनी (हरिण की सी आँखों वाली) हैं और सभी अपने शरीर की शोभा से रति के गर्व को छुड़ाने वाली हैं। रंग-रंग की सुंदर साड़ियाँ पहने हैं और शरीर पर सब आभूषण सजे हुए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1696.english_translation: All the women have moon-like faces and deer-like eyes, and their beauty makes even Rati's pride fall away. They wear garments of many colors, and their bodies are adorned with every ornament.
ramacharitamanas::1696.translation_literal: बिधुबदनीं (moon-faced) / सब (all) / सब (all) / मृगलोचनि (deer-eyed) / सब (all) / निज (own) / तन (body) / छबि (beauty) / रति (Rati) / मदु (pride/intoxication) / मोचनि (causing to lose) / पहिरें (wearing) / बरन बरन (many-colored) / बर (excellent) / चीरा (garments) / सकल (all) / बिभूषन (ornaments) / सजें (adorned) / सरीरा (bodies)
ramacharitamanas::1696.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1696.essence: Celebration itself becomes sacred when every detail shines.
ramacharitamanas::1696.simple_meaning: The women are richly dressed and beautifully adorned, with faces and eyes compared to the moon and deer. Their beauty is so striking that it outshines even legendary beauty itself.
ramacharitamanas::1696.simple_insight: Beauty can be shared, festive, and radiant without needing to compete.
ramacharitamanas::1696.detailed_meaning: As Ram's wedding procession arrives in Mithila, the city women come out to welcome the groom. Tulsidas lingers on their beauty, clothing, and ornaments to build the scene of celebration before the formal reception begins.
ramacharitamanas::1696.modern_relevance: A wedding hall fills with color, perfume, silk, and laughter before the first ritual begins. Everyone is dressed to honor the moment, and the whole room feels lifted by shared joy.
ramacharitamanas::1696.insight: It shifts attention from plot to atmosphere, letting the reader feel the grandeur of the celebration.

ramacharitamanas::1697.verse_sanskrit: सकल सुमंगल अंग बनाएँ। करहिं गान कलकंठि लजाएँ॥ कंकन किंकिनि नूपुर बाजहिं। चालि बिलोकि काम गज लाजहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1697.verse_hindi: समस्त अंगों को सुंदर मंगल पदार्थों से सजाए हुए वे कोयल को भी लजाती हुई (मधुर स्वर से) गान कर रही हैं। कंगन, करधनी और नूपुर बज रहे हैं। स्त्रियों की चाल देखकर कामदेव के हाथी भी लजा जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1697.english_translation: With every limb adorned in auspicious beauty, they sing so sweetly that even the cuckoo is humbled. Bracelets, waist-bells, and anklets ring; their graceful walk shames even Cupid's elephant.
ramacharitamanas::1697.translation_literal: सकल (all) / सुमंगल (most auspicious) / अंग (limbs) / बनाएँ (made adorned) / करहिं (they do) / गान (singing) / कलकंठि (cuckoo-throated women) / लजाएँ (put to shame) / कंकन (bracelets) / किंकिनि (waist-bells) / नूपुर (anklets) / बाजहिं (ring) / चालि (walking) / बिलोकि (seeing) / काम (Cupid) / गज (elephant) / लाजहिं (are shamed)
ramacharitamanas::1697.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1697.essence: Grace makes even sound and movement feel auspicious.
ramacharitamanas::1697.simple_meaning: The women are beautifully dressed, singing sweetly, and moving so gracefully that their ornaments ring as they walk.
ramacharitamanas::1697.simple_insight: Beauty can be so complete that it feels alive in sound, movement, and presence.
ramacharitamanas::1697.detailed_meaning: In Janak's palace during the swayamvar preparations, the women of the court move forward for the auspicious welcome. Tulsidas lingers on their dress, song, and graceful walk, building the festive atmosphere before Sita's great moment.
ramacharitamanas::1697.modern_relevance: A wedding hall is filling up, bangles clinking, music rising, everyone moving with that special careful joy. The scene matters before anyone even speaks.
ramacharitamanas::1697.insight: It shifts attention from plot to atmosphere, letting the reader feel the sacred celebration taking shape.

ramacharitamanas::1698.verse_sanskrit: बाजहिं बाजने बिबिध प्रकारा। नभ अरु नगर सुमंगलचारा॥ सची सारदा रमा भवानी। जे सुरतिय सुचि सजह सयानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1698.verse_hindi: अनेक प्रकार के बाजे बज रहे हैं, आकाश और नगर दोनों स्थानों में सुंदर मंगलाचार हो रहे हैं। शची (इन्द्राणी), सरस्वती, लक्ष्मी, पार्वती और जो स्वभाव से ही पवित्र और सयानी देवांगनाएँ थीं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1698.english_translation: Various kinds of musical instruments are sounding. Auspicious celebrations fill the sky and the city. Shachi, Saraswati, Lakshmi, Parvati, and other pure, wise celestial women...
ramacharitamanas::1698.translation_literal: बाजहिं (are sounding) / बाजने (musical instruments) / बिबिध प्रकारा (of various kinds) / नभ (sky) / अरु (and) / नगर (city) / सुमंगलचारा (auspicious celebrations) / सची (Shachi) / सारदा (Saraswati) / रमा (Lakshmi) / भवानी (Parvati) / जे (who) / सुरतिय (celestial women) / सुचि (pure) / सजह (well-adorned) / सयानी (wise)
ramacharitamanas::1698.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1698.essence: Auspicious joy announces a moment before words do.
ramacharitamanas::1698.simple_meaning: The celebration is in full swing. Music fills the sky and the city, while divine women arrive beautifully dressed and ready for the auspicious event.
ramacharitamanas::1698.simple_insight: Joy can be shared so fully that even the atmosphere feels transformed.
ramacharitamanas::1698.detailed_meaning: The Sita-swayamvar is underway in Mithila. Music rises everywhere, and celestial women like Shachi, Saraswati, Lakshmi, and Parvati appear in festive splendor. This verse adds to the growing sense that something sacred and extraordinary is unfolding.
ramacharitamanas::1698.modern_relevance: A wedding hall hums before the ceremony begins: drums, flowers, silk, and a room charged with anticipation. The moment feels larger than the people inside it.
ramacharitamanas::1698.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the sacred atmosphere surrounding it.

ramacharitamanas::1699.verse_sanskrit: कपट नारि बर बेष बनाई। मिली सकल रनिवासहिं जाई॥ करहिं गान कल मंगल बानीं। हरष बिबस सब काहुँ न जानीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1699.verse_hindi: वे सब कपट से सुंदर स्त्री का वेश बनाकर रनिवास में जा मिलीं और मनोहर वाणी से मंगलगान करने लगीं। सब कोई हर्ष के विशेष वश थे, अतः किसी ने उन्हें पहचाना नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1699.english_translation: They disguised themselves as beautiful women and went into the royal women's quarters. They sang auspicious songs in sweet voices, and everyone was so overjoyed that no one recognized them.
ramacharitamanas::1699.translation_literal: कपट (deception) / नारि (woman) / बर (beautiful) / बेष (disguise) / बनाई (having made) / मिली (met) / सकल (all) / रनिवासहिं (to the royal women's quarters) / जाई (going) / करहिं (they sing) / गान (songs) / कल (sweet) / मंगल (auspicious) / बानीं (words/voices) / हरष (joy) / बिबस (overpowered) / सब (all) / काहुँ (anyone) / न (not) / जानीं (knew/recognized)
ramacharitamanas::1699.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1699.essence: Delight can hide what fear would instantly notice.
ramacharitamanas::1699.simple_meaning: They enter the royal women’s quarters in disguise and sing auspicious songs. Everyone is so delighted that nobody notices who they really are.
ramacharitamanas::1699.simple_insight: Joy can make even the obvious go unseen.
ramacharitamanas::1699.detailed_meaning: At the wedding festivities in Mithila, the divine women arrive disguised as ordinary women and slip into the royal women’s quarters. Their singing fills the scene with delight, and the joy is so complete that no one recognizes them.
ramacharitamanas::1699.modern_relevance: At a crowded wedding, everyone is swept up in music, color, and laughter. In that kind of joy, even the most unlikely presence can pass unnoticed.
ramacharitamanas::1699.insight: It shows how collective joy can dissolve suspicion and blur identity.

ramacharitamanas::1700.verse_sanskrit: को जान केहि आनंद बस सब ब्रह्मु बर परिछन चली। कल गान मधुर निसान बरषहिं सुमन सुर सोभा भली॥ आनंदकंदु बिलोकि दूलहु सकलहियँ हरषित भई। अंभोज अंबक अंबु उमगि सुअंग पुलकावलि छई॥
ramacharitamanas::1700.verse_hindi: कौन किसे जाने-पहिचाने! आनंद के वश हुई सब दूल्हे बने हुए ब्रह्म का परछन करने चलीं। मनोहर गान हो रहा है। मधुर-मधुर नगाड़े बज रहे हैं, देवता फूल बरसा रहे हैं, बड़ी अच्छी शोभा है। आनंदकन्द दूल्हे को देखकर सब स्त्रियाँ हृदय में हर्षित हुईं। उनके कमल सरीखे नेत्रों में प्रेमाश्रुओं का जल उमड़ आया और सुंदर अंगों में पुलकावली छा गई॥
ramacharitamanas::1700.english_translation: Who can know whom? Overcome by bliss, all went to behold the bridegroom Brahma. Sweet songs rose, drums rained, and the gods showered flowers in fine splendour. Seeing the joy-filled bridegroom, all the women’s hearts overflowed with delight. Tears of love filled their lotus-like eyes, and goosebumps covered their lovely bodies.
ramacharitamanas::1700.translation_literal: को (who) / जान (know) / केहि (whom) / आनंद बस (under the sway of joy) / सब ब्रह्मु बर (all, the bridegroom Brahma) / परिछन (to behold / perform auspicious viewing) / चली (went) / कल गान (sweet songs) / मधुर (sweet) / निसान (drums) / बरषहिं (are showering) / सुमन (flowers) / सुर (gods) / सोभा (splendour) / भली (beautiful)॥ / आनंदकंदु (root of bliss) / बिलोकि (seeing) / दूलहु (the bridegroom) / सकलहियँ (in all hearts) / हरषित (delighted) / भई (became) / अंभोज अंबक (lotus eyes) / अंबु (water) / उमगि (overflowing) / सुअंग (beautiful bodies) / पुलकावलि (goosebumps) / छई (spread)॥
ramacharitamanas::1700.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1700.essence: Joy at Ram’s sight overflows into tears, music, and trembling delight.
ramacharitamanas::1700.simple_meaning: The wedding scene overflows with joy, music, flowers, and wonder. Everyone is so moved by the sight of the bridegroom that tears, delight, and goosebumps appear together.
ramacharitamanas::1700.simple_insight: Some moments are so beautiful they move the body before the mind can speak.
ramacharitamanas::1700.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, the women of the palace and the gathered beings are swept into celebration as Ram appears in bridegroom form. Music, flowers, and radiant joy fill the scene, and the sight of him stirs love so deeply that tears and shivers break out at once.
ramacharitamanas::1700.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall and the room changes before anyone speaks. Music starts, people smile through tears, and one sight makes the whole crowd feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1700.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to presence: the sight of what is sacred makes joy physical.

ramacharitamanas::1701.verse_sanskrit: जो सुखु भा सिय मातु मन देखि राम बर बेषु। सो न सकहिं कहि कलप सत सहस सारदा सेषु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1701.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का वर वेश देखकर सीताजी की माता सुनयनाजी के मन में जो सुख हुआ, उसे हजारों सरस्वती और शेषजी सौ कल्पों में भी नहीं कह सकते (अथवा लाखों सरस्वती और शेष लाखों कल्पों में भी नहीं कह सकते) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1701.english_translation: The joy that Sita's mother felt upon seeing Ram in bridegroom's dress cannot be told even by a hundred thousand Saraswatis or Sheshas over countless ages.
ramacharitamanas::1701.translation_literal: जो (which) / सुखु (joy) / भा (became) / सिय मातु (Sita's mother) / मन (mind) / देखि (seeing) / राम बर बेषु (Ram's bridegroom form) / सो (that) / न सकहिं (cannot) / कहि (say) / कलप सत सहस (hundreds and thousands of ages) / सारदा सेषु (Saraswati and Shesha)
ramacharitamanas::1701.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1701.essence: Some joy is too vast for language to hold.
ramacharitamanas::1701.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram dressed as the bridegroom filled Sita's mother with joy beyond words. Even endless time and countless voices could not describe it.
ramacharitamanas::1701.simple_insight: Some moments are too full for language. Joy can be so complete that silence feels truer than speech.
ramacharitamanas::1701.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the bridegroom procession has arrived and Ram appears in royal wedding dress. Sita's mother, Sunayana, sees him and is overwhelmed with joy. Tulsidas says even divine speech cannot fully capture that feeling.
ramacharitamanas::1701.modern_relevance: You catch sight of your child in a graduation gown, and your chest tightens before any words come. Some pride and tenderness are bigger than explanation.
ramacharitamanas::1701.insight: It shifts attention from describing joy to feeling its fullness directly.

ramacharitamanas::1702.verse_sanskrit: नयन नीरु हटि मंगल जानी। परिछनि करहिं मुदित मन रानी॥ बेद बिहित अरु कुल आचारू। कीन्ह भली बिधि सब ब्यवहारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1702.verse_hindi: मंगल अवसर जानकर नेत्रों के जल को रोके हुए रानी प्रसन्न मन से परछन कर रही हैं। वेदों में कहे हुए तथा कुलाचार के अनुसार सभी व्यवहार रानी ने भलीभाँति किए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1702.english_translation: The queens, knowing this was an auspicious moment, held back their tears and joyfully performed the welcoming rites. They carried out every formality properly, according to the Vedas and family custom.
ramacharitamanas::1702.translation_literal: नयन (eyes) / नीरु (water, tears) / हटि (holding back) / मंगल (auspicious) / जानी (knowing) / परिछनि (welcoming rite) / करहिं (do) / मुदित (joyful) / मन (mind) / रानी (queens) ॥ / बेद (Vedas) / बिहित (prescribed) / अरु (and) / कुल (family) / आचारू (custom) / कीन्ह (did) / भली बिधि (properly) / सब (all) / ब्यवहारू (formal acts) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1702.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1702.essence: Joy becomes complete when it is expressed through rightful action.
ramacharitamanas::1702.simple_meaning: The queens suppress their tears, feel joy, and perform the welcoming ritual properly, following sacred law and family custom.
ramacharitamanas::1702.simple_insight: Even joy has a right form. Grace shows up in how carefully you honor a sacred moment.
ramacharitamanas::1702.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s house, the wedding welcome is in motion as Sita’s family receives Ram in his bridegroom form. The queens are overwhelmed, but they hold back tears and complete the rites exactly as tradition requires.
ramacharitamanas::1702.modern_relevance: You are smiling through tears at your child’s wedding, doing the ritual steps one by one because love needs form, not just feeling.
ramacharitamanas::1702.insight: It teaches that devotion can be both emotional and exact, with feeling guided by right conduct.

ramacharitamanas::1703.verse_sanskrit: पंच सबद धुनि मंगल गाना। पट पाँवड़े परहिं बिधि नाना॥ करि आरती अरघु तिन्ह दीन्हा। राम गमनु मंडप तब कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1703.verse_hindi: पंचशब्द (तंत्री, ताल, झाँझ, नगारा और तुरही- इन पाँच प्रकार के बाजों के शब्द), पंचध्वनि (वेदध्वनि, वन्दिध्वनि, जयध्वनि, शंखध्वनि और हुलूध्वनि) और मंगलगान हो रहे हैं। नाना प्रकार के वस्त्रों के पाँवड़े पड़ रहे हैं। उन्होंने (रानी ने) आरती करके अर्घ्य दिया, तब श्री रामजी ने मंडप में गमन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1703.english_translation: The sounds of five kinds of instruments and five sacred cries rose with auspicious songs. Fine cloths were laid down in many ways. They performed aarti and offered arghya, then Ram entered the wedding pavilion.
ramacharitamanas::1703.translation_literal: पंच सबद (five sounds) / धुनि (sound) / मंगल गाना (auspicious singing) / पट पाँवड़े (cloth carpets) / परहिं (are laid) / बिधि नाना (in many ways) / करि (doing) / आरती (aarti) / अरघु (ritual offering) / तिन्ह (they) / दीन्हा (gave) / राम गमनु (Ram's entry) / मंडप (wedding pavilion) / तब (then) / कीन्हा (made)
ramacharitamanas::1703.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1703.essence: Reverence prepares the way before joy enters.
ramacharitamanas::1703.simple_meaning: The wedding pavilion fills with music, ritual offerings, and celebration as Ram enters.
ramacharitamanas::1703.simple_insight: Joy becomes visible when reverence turns into action.
ramacharitamanas::1703.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the wedding rites are underway. Music, cloth pathways, aarti, and offerings prepare the sacred space. Only after all this welcome does Ram step into the मंडप, marking the threshold of the marriage scene.
ramacharitamanas::1703.modern_relevance: A home fills with music, flowers, and careful preparation before a loved one arrives. The welcome itself becomes part of the joy.
ramacharitamanas::1703.insight: It shifts attention from the arrival alone to the care that makes arrival sacred.

ramacharitamanas::1704.verse_sanskrit: दसरथु सहित समाज बिराजे। बिभव बिलोकि लोकपति लाजे॥ समयँ समयँ सुर बरषहिं फूला। सांति पढ़हिं महिसुर अनुकूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::1704.verse_hindi: दशरथजी अपनी मंडली सहित विराजमान हुए। उनके वैभव को देखकर लोकपाल भी लजा गए। समय-समय पर देवता फूल बरसाते हैं और भूदेव ब्राह्मण समयानुकूल शांति पाठ करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1704.english_translation: Dasharath sat there with his assembled company. Seeing his splendor, the guardians of the world felt humbled. At intervals, the radiant beings showered flowers, and the learned priests recited peace chants in fitting sequence.
ramacharitamanas::1704.translation_literal: दसरथु (Dasharath) / सहित (together with) / समाज (assembly, company) / बिराजे (sat in splendour) / बिभव (splendor, wealth, grandeur) / बिलोकि (seeing) / लोकपति (guardians of the world) / लाजे (felt ashamed/humbled) / समयँ समयँ (at intervals) / सुर (radiant beings) / बरषहिं (rain) / फूला (flowers) / सांति (peace) / पढ़हिं (recite) / महिसुर (learned priests, brahmins) / अनुकूला (in proper order, suitably)
ramacharitamanas::1704.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1704.essence: Royal splendour and sacred ceremony announce the coming of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1704.simple_meaning: Dasharath sits in royal splendour while flowers fall from above and priests recite blessings in order.
ramacharitamanas::1704.simple_insight: A sacred moment can feel larger than power itself.
ramacharitamanas::1704.detailed_meaning: At the swayamvar gathering, Dasharath sits with his retinue in full royal dignity. The scene overflows with ceremony: flowers from the radiant beings, peace chants from the priests, and a court so grand that even the guardians of the world are humbled.
ramacharitamanas::1704.modern_relevance: You walk into a hall before the ceremony begins, and every detail is already arranged: the flowers, the chants, the waiting crowd. The room itself seems to know something important is about to happen.
ramacharitamanas::1704.insight: It shifts attention from the king to the charged atmosphere surrounding Ram's arrival.

ramacharitamanas::1705.verse_sanskrit: नभ अरु नगर कोलाहल होई। आपनि पर कछु सुनइ न कोई॥ एहि बिधि रामु मंडपहिं आए। अरघु देइ आसन बैठाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1705.verse_hindi: आकाश और नगर में शोर मच रहा है। अपनी-पराई कोई कुछ भी नहीं सुनता। इस प्रकार श्री रामचन्द्रजी मंडप में आए और अर्घ्य देकर आसन पर बैठाए गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1705.english_translation: There was uproar in the sky and the city. No one heard anything else. In this way, Ram entered the wedding pavilion, was honored with offerings, and seated.
ramacharitamanas::1705.translation_literal: नभ (sky) / अरु (and) / नगर (city) / कोलाहल (uproar) / होई (was) / आपनि (one's own) / पर (other) / कछु (anything) / सुनइ (hears) / न (not) / कोई (anyone) / एहि बिधि (in this way) / रामु (Ram) / मंडपहिं (to the pavilion) / आए (came) / अरघु (offering) / देइ (having given) / आसन (seat) / बैठाए (was seated)
ramacharitamanas::1705.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1705.essence: Ram's arrival turns the whole city into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1705.simple_meaning: The whole city is filled with celebration as Ram enters the wedding pavilion and is seated with honor.
ramacharitamanas::1705.simple_insight: Joy can be so complete that the whole world seems to ring with it.
ramacharitamanas::1705.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the wedding celebration is at its peak. The sky and city resound with noise as Ram arrives at the pavilion. He is welcomed with offerings and seated for the ceremony, a moment of public joy before the marriage rites begin.
ramacharitamanas::1705.modern_relevance: A wedding hall erupts when the bridegroom finally walks in. Music, voices, footsteps, and laughter blur together — the kind of moment where celebration itself becomes the message.
ramacharitamanas::1705.insight: It turns attention to the sacred arrival itself, not the details around it.

ramacharitamanas::1706.verse_sanskrit: बैठारि आसन आरती करि निरखि बरु सुखु पावहीं। मनि बसन भूषन भूरि वारहिं नारि मंगल गावहीं॥ ब्रह्मादि सुरबर बिप्र बेष बनाइ कौतुक देखहीं। अवलोकि रघुकुल कमल रबि छबि सुफल जीवन लेखहीं॥
ramacharitamanas::1706.verse_hindi: आसन पर बैठाकर, आरती करके दूल्हे को देखकर स्त्रियाँ सुख पा रही हैं। वे ढेर के ढेर मणि, वस्त्र और गहने निछावर करके मंगल गा रही हैं। ब्रह्मा आदि श्रेष्ठ देवता ब्राह्मण का वेश बनाकर कौतुक देख रहे हैं। वे रघुकुल रूपी कमल को प्रफुल्लित करने वाले सूर्य श्री रामचन्द्रजी की छबि देखकर अपना जीवन सफल जान रहे हैं।
ramacharitamanas::1706.english_translation: Having seated him, the women perform the aarti and feel joy at seeing the groom. They shower heaps of jewels, clothes, and ornaments, singing auspicious songs. Brahma and the other radiant beings, disguised as Brahmins, watch the spectacle. Seeing the beauty of Ram, the sun of the Raghu clan, they feel their lives have become fruitful.
ramacharitamanas::1706.translation_literal: बैठारि (having seated) / आसन (seat) / आरती (aarti) / करि (doing) / निरखि (seeing) / बरु (groom) / सुखु (joy) / पावहीं (they obtain) / मनि (jewels) / बसन (clothes) / भूषन (ornaments) / भूरि (many) / वारहिं (they offer/sacrifice) / नारि (women) / मंगल (auspicious songs) / गावहीं (they sing) / ब्रह्मादि (Brahma and others) / सुरबर (radiant beings) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / बेष (disguise) / बनाइ (making) / कौतुक (wonder/spectacle) / देखहीं (they see) / अवलोकि (seeing) / रघुकुल (Raghu clan) / कमल (lotus) / रबि (sun) / छबि (beauty) / सुफल (fruitful) / जीवन (life) / लेखहीं (they consider)
ramacharitamanas::1706.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1706.essence: Ram’s presence turns celebration into fulfillment.
ramacharitamanas::1706.simple_meaning: The wedding hall overflows with joy. Women sing, offer gifts, and celebrate Ram’s beauty, while even the radiant beings in disguise watch in wonder and feel their lives are fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::1706.simple_insight: Joy deepens when beauty is recognized as sacred. Even the watchers feel transformed by simply seeing Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1706.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur’s wedding hall, Ram has just been seated as the groom. Women sing auspicious songs and offer gifts in delight. Even Brahma and other radiant beings, hidden as Brahmins, come to witness the moment and see Ram’s beauty as life’s fulfillment.
ramacharitamanas::1706.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where everyone has paused mid-conversation, not from etiquette but awe. The room feels larger because one presence has made ordinary celebration feel holy.
ramacharitamanas::1706.insight: It shifts attention from the ceremony itself to the presence that gives the ceremony meaning.

ramacharitamanas::1707.verse_sanskrit: नाऊ बारी भाट नट राम निछावरि पाइ। मुदित असीसहिं नाइ सिर हरषु न हृदयँ समाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1707.verse_hindi: नाई, बारी, भाट और नट श्री रामचन्द्रजी की निछावर पाकर आनंदित हो सिर नवाकर आशीष देते हैं, उनके हृदय में हर्ष समाता नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1707.english_translation: The barber, washerman, bard, and dancers receive Ram's gifts, bow their heads, and offer blessings. Their hearts overflow with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1707.translation_literal: नाऊ (barber) / बारी (washerman) / भाट (bard) / नट (dancers) / राम (Ram) / निछावरि (gift offered in reverence) / पाइ (receiving) / मुदित (joyful) / असीसहिं (they bless) / नाइ (bowing) / सिर (head) / हरषु (joy) / न (not) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / समाइ (fits)
ramacharitamanas::1707.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1707.essence: Honor given freely returns as joy.
ramacharitamanas::1707.simple_meaning: The people serving the wedding receive gifts from Ram and feel so happy that they bow and bless him with overflowing joy.
ramacharitamanas::1707.simple_insight: Joy deepens when respect is mutual and everyone is honoured.
ramacharitamanas::1707.detailed_meaning: At Sita's wedding in Mithila, the celebration has moved from ritual to shared delight. Ordinary workers and performers receive Ram's gifts, bow their heads, and bless him back. The scene shows how his presence fills even the smallest roles with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1707.modern_relevance: At a wedding, the caterer, musician, and driver are all treated with real warmth. The event feels different because no one is invisible.
ramacharitamanas::1707.insight: It shifts attention from the main ceremony to the dignity of every person who helps hold it together.

ramacharitamanas::1708.verse_sanskrit: मिले जनकु दसरथु अति प्रीतीं। करि बैदिक लौकिक सब रीतीं॥ मिलत महा दोउ राज बिराजे। उपमा खोजि खोजि कबि लाजे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1708.verse_hindi: वैदिक और लौकिक सब रीतियाँ करके जनकजी और दशरथजी बड़े प्रेम से मिले। दोनों महाराज मिलते हुए बड़े ही शोभित हुए, कवि उनके लिए उपमा खोज-खोजकर लजा गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1708.english_translation: Janak and Dasharath met with great affection, following all Vedic and worldly customs. As the two royal fathers met in splendor, poets searched for a comparison and then felt ashamed.
ramacharitamanas::1708.translation_literal: मिले (met) / जनकु (Janak) / दसरथु (Dasharath) / अति (greatly) / प्रीतीं (with affection) / करि (doing) / बैदिक (Vedic) / लौकिक (worldly) / सब (all) / रीतीं (customs) / मिलत (meeting) / महा (great) / दोउ (both) / राज (kings) / बिराजे (shone splendidly) / उपमा (comparison) / खोजि खोजि (searching again and again) / कबि (poets) / लाजे (were ashamed)
ramacharitamanas::1708.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1708.essence: Greatness can be so graceful that comparison fails.
ramacharitamanas::1708.simple_meaning: Janak and Dasharath meet with deep affection and full ceremony. Their royal dignity is so great that poets cannot find a fitting comparison.
ramacharitamanas::1708.simple_insight: Some moments are too full for language. Respect and grace can make even poetry fall silent.
ramacharitamanas::1708.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, Janak receives Dasharath with full ritual and warmth. The two kings stand together in splendor, and even the poets feel embarrassed searching for a comparison. The verse slows the story to honor the meeting before the marriage.
ramacharitamanas::1708.modern_relevance: At a wedding where two families meet with folded hands, careful rituals, and quiet pride, you can feel the room change. Some encounters carry a dignity that no caption can fully hold.
ramacharitamanas::1708.insight: It shifts attention from event to reverence, showing that form and courtesy can reveal true greatness.

ramacharitamanas::1709.verse_sanskrit: लही न कतहुँ हारि हियँ मानी। इन्ह सम एइ उपमा उर आनी॥ सामध देखि देव अनुरागे। सुमन बरषि जसु गावन लागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1709.verse_hindi: जब कहीं भी उपमा नहीं मिली, तब हृदय में हार मानकर उन्होंने मन में यही उपमा निश्चित की कि इनके समान ये ही हैं। समधियों का मिलाप या परस्पर संबंध देखकर देवता अनुरक्त हो गए और फूल बरसाकर उनका यश गाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1709.english_translation: No comparison could be found, so they accepted in their hearts: these two are equal. Seeing the union of the families, the radiant beings grew delighted, showered flowers, and began singing their praise.
ramacharitamanas::1709.translation_literal: लही (was found) / न (not) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / हारि (defeat) / हियँ (in the heart) / मानी (accepted) / इन्ह (these) / सम (equal to) / एइ (this) / उपमा (comparison) / उर (in the heart) / आनी (bringing) || सामध (the in-laws) / देखि (seeing) / देव (radiant beings) / अनुरागे (became delighted) / सुमन (flowers) / बरषि (showering) / जसु (praise) / गावन (to sing) / लागे (began)
ramacharitamanas::1709.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1709.essence: Some unions are so perfect that praise itself becomes celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1709.simple_meaning: No one could find a comparison equal to this royal match, so they settled on one: these two are alike. The heavenly beings rejoiced, showered flowers, and sang their praise.
ramacharitamanas::1709.simple_insight: Some unions feel beyond comparison. When harmony is complete, even admiration turns into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1709.detailed_meaning: Janak and Dasharath have met for Sita and Ram's wedding. After formal greetings, the poet says no comparison could capture their splendour, so the heart accepts only this: they are equal. Even the radiant beings respond with joy, flowers, and praise.
ramacharitamanas::1709.modern_relevance: At a wedding where both families are equally gracious, everyone falls quiet for a moment. No compliment feels large enough, and the room itself seems to bless the match.
ramacharitamanas::1709.insight: It shifts attention from measuring people to recognising a rare, complete harmony.

ramacharitamanas::1710.verse_sanskrit: जगु बिरंचि उपजावा जब तें। देखे सुने ब्याह बहु तब तें॥ सकल भाँति सम साजु समाजू। सम समधी देखे हम आजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1710.verse_hindi: (वे कहने लगे-) जबसे ब्रह्माजी ने जगत को उत्पन्न किया, तब से हमने बहुत विवाह देखे- सुने, परन्तु सब प्रकार से समान साज-समाज और बराबरी के (पूर्ण समतायुक्त) समधी तो आज ही देखे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1710.english_translation: Since Brahma created the world, we have seen and heard many weddings, but only today have we seen a match so perfectly equal in every respect.
ramacharitamanas::1710.translation_literal: जगु (world) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / उपजावा (created) / जब तें (since then) / देखे (seen) / सुने (heard) / ब्याह (weddings) / बहु (many) / तब तें (since then) / सकल (all) / भाँति (kinds) / सम (equal) / साजु (arrangement) / समाजू (assembly) / सम (equal) / समधी (in-laws) / देखे (seen) / हम (we) / आजू (today)
ramacharitamanas::1710.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1710.essence: Even the oldest witnesses find no comparison for this perfect union.
ramacharitamanas::1710.simple_meaning: The assembled kings say they have seen many weddings since the world began, but never one as perfectly matched and splendid as this one.
ramacharitamanas::1710.simple_insight: Some moments feel so complete that even experience runs out of comparison.
ramacharitamanas::1710.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s palace, after the perfect match between Ram and Sita is recognised, the assembled kings and guests marvel at the wedding arrangements. They admit that no earlier marriage they have ever seen can compare with this one.
ramacharitamanas::1710.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding where every detail feels strangely right — the families, the timing, the atmosphere. Everyone knows they are witnessing something rare before a single ceremony begins.
ramacharitamanas::1710.insight: It frames the marriage as a once-in-a-lifetime harmony, not just a social event.

ramacharitamanas::1711.verse_sanskrit: देव गिरा सुनि सुंदर साँची। प्रीति अलौकिक दुहु दिसि माची॥ देत पाँवड़े अरघु सुहाए। सादर जनकु मंडपहिं ल्याए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1711.verse_hindi: देवताओं की सुंदर सत्यवाणी सुनकर दोनों ओर अलौकिक प्रीति छा गई। सुंदर पाँवड़े और अर्घ्य देते हुए जनकजी दशरथजी को आदरपूर्वक मंडप में ले आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1711.english_translation: Hearing the gods’ beautiful and true words, both sides were filled with extraordinary affection. Offering graceful steps and respectful gifts, Janaka ceremoniously led Dasharatha into the pavilion.
ramacharitamanas::1711.translation_literal: देव (gods) / गिरा (speech) / सुनि (hearing) / सुंदर (beautiful) / साँची (true) / प्रीति (affection) / अलौकिक (extraordinary) / दुहु दिसि (on both sides) / माची (spread) / देत (giving) / पाँवड़े (steps/stairs) / अरघु (respectful offering) / सुहाए (graceful/beautiful) / सादर (with respect) / जनकु (Janaka) / मंडपहिं (to the pavilion) / ल्याए (brought)
ramacharitamanas::1711.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1711.essence: Honor given sincerely turns ceremony into affection.
ramacharitamanas::1711.simple_meaning: The gods’ blessing and praise fill both sides with affection, and Janaka respectfully escorts Dasharatha into the wedding pavilion.
ramacharitamanas::1711.simple_insight: Respect softens pride. When honor is given sincerely, even a formal ceremony becomes warm and alive.
ramacharitamanas::1711.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s wedding pavilion in Mithila, the gods’ praise has already lifted the mood. Janaka now receives Dasharatha with ritual honor, and the whole gathering turns tender and joyous before the marriage rites begin.
ramacharitamanas::1711.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where two families once felt like strangers. A warm welcome, a seat offered with care, and the whole room changes before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1711.insight: It shows how reverent hospitality can transform a public event into shared affection.

ramacharitamanas::1712.verse_sanskrit: मंडपु बिलोकि बिचित्र रचनाँ रुचिरताँ मुनि मन हरे। निज पानि जनक सुजान सब कहुँ आनि सिंघासन धरे॥ कुल इष्ट सरिस बसिष्ट पूजे बिनय करि आसिष लही। कौसिकहि पूजन परम प्रीति कि रीति तौ न परै कही॥
ramacharitamanas::1712.verse_hindi: मंडप को देखकर उसकी विचित्र रचना और सुंदरता से मुनियों के मन भी हरे गए (मोहित हो गए)। सुजान जनकजी ने अपने हाथों से ला-लाकर सबके लिए सिंहासन रखे। उन्होंने अपने कुल के इष्टदेवता के समान वशिष्ठजी की पूजा की और विनय करके आशीर्वाद प्राप्त किया। विश्वामित्रजी की पूजा करते समय की परम प्रीति की रीति तो कहते ही नहीं बनती॥
ramacharitamanas::1712.english_translation: Seeing the pavilion, its strange design and beauty captivated even the sages. Wise Janak personally brought and placed seats for everyone. He honored Vashishtha as his family deity and received blessings with humility. The warmth with which he worshiped Vishvamitra cannot even be fully described.
ramacharitamanas::1712.translation_literal: मंडपु (pavilion) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बिचित्र (wonderful, varied) / रचनाँ (design) / रुचिरताँ (beauty) / मुनि (sages) / मन (mind) / हरे (captivated) / निज (own) / पानि (hand) / जनक (Janak) / सुजान (wise) / सब कहुँ (for everyone) / आनि (bringing) / सिंघासन (seats, thrones) / धरे (placed) / कुल (family) / इष्ट (chosen deity) / सरिस (like) / बसिष्ट (Vashishtha) / पूजे (worshiped) / बिनय करि (with humility) / आसिष (blessings) / लही (received) / कौसिकहि (Vishvamitra) / पूजन (worship) / परम (supreme) / प्रीति (love) / कि रीति (manner) / तौ (then) / न परै कही (cannot be said)
ramacharitamanas::1712.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1712.essence: Honor becomes real when pride gives way to humble service.
ramacharitamanas::1712.simple_meaning: Janak welcomes the sages with great honor, placing seats for them himself and worshiping Vashishtha and Vishvamitra with deep respect and love.
ramacharitamanas::1712.simple_insight: True greatness shows itself in humble hospitality, not in status.
ramacharitamanas::1712.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the wedding pavilion itself amazes the gathered sages. Janak does not stand on royal pride; he personally arranges seats, bows to Vashishtha like a family deity, and honors Vishvamitra with overflowing warmth. The scene reveals the grace of the court before the marriage begins.
ramacharitamanas::1712.modern_relevance: A host who is already exhausted still pulls out chairs, pours water, and greets the elders first. That quiet care makes the whole room feel respected.
ramacharitamanas::1712.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony as display to ceremony as reverent welcome.

ramacharitamanas::1713.verse_sanskrit: बामदेव आदिक रिषय पूजे मुदित महीस॥ दिए दिब्य आसन सबहि सब सन लही असीस ॥
ramacharitamanas::1713.verse_hindi: राजा ने वामदेव आदि ऋषियों की प्रसन्न मन से पूजा की। सभी को दिव्य आसन दिए और सबसे आशीर्वाद प्राप्त किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1713.english_translation: The king joyfully honored Vamadeva and the other sages. He gave each a divine seat and received blessings from all.
ramacharitamanas::1713.translation_literal: बामदेव (Vamadeva) / आदिक (and others) / रिषय (sages) / पूजे (honored) / मुदित (joyful) / महीस (the king)॥ / दिए (gave) / दिब्य (divine) / आसन (seats) / सबहि (to everyone) / सब (all) / सन (from) / लही (received) / असीस (blessings)॥
ramacharitamanas::1713.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1713.essence: Honor the wise first; blessings follow naturally.
ramacharitamanas::1713.simple_meaning: King Janak respectfully welcomes the sages, seats them with honor, and receives their blessings in return.
ramacharitamanas::1713.simple_insight: True respect creates a sacred exchange: honor given freely returns as blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1713.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s grand wedding hall in Mithila, the sages arrive before the marriage rites begin. The king greets Vamadeva and the others with delight, gives them honored seats, and receives their blessings as the gathering deepens in sanctity.
ramacharitamanas::1713.modern_relevance: You welcome elders into your home, pull out the best chairs, and listen before speaking. That simple respect changes the whole atmosphere of the room.
ramacharitamanas::1713.insight: It teaches you to honor wisdom before asking for anything from it.

ramacharitamanas::1714.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि कीन्हि कोसलपति पूजा। जानि ईस सम भाउ न दूजा॥ कीन्हि जोरि कर बिनय बड़ाई। कहि निज भाग्य बिभव बहुताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1714.verse_hindi: फिर उन्होंने कोसलाधीश राजा दशरथजी की पूजा उन्हें ईश (महादेवजी) के समान जानकर की, कोई दूसरा भाव न था। तदन्तर (उनके संबंध से) अपने भाग्य और वैभव के विस्तार की सराहना करके हाथ जोड़कर विनती और बड़ाई की ॥
ramacharitamanas::1714.english_translation: Then Janaka honored the king of Kosala, knowing him as equal to Shiva and feeling no other regard. He joined his hands, offered praise, and spoke of his own fortune and greatness.
ramacharitamanas::1714.translation_literal: बहुरि (again) / कीन्हि (did) / कोसलपति (lord of Kosala) / पूजा (worship, honor) । जानि (knowing) / ईस (Shiva, the Lord) / सम (equal) / भाउ (feeling, regard) / न (not) / दूजा (other) ॥ कीन्हि (did) / जोरि (joining) / कर (hands) / बिनय (humble request, praise) / बड़ाई (glorification) । कहि (speaking) / निज (own) / भाग्य (fortune) / बिभव (splendor, wealth) / बहुताई (abundance, greatness) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1714.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1714.essence: Honor becomes sacred when pride is absent.
ramacharitamanas::1714.simple_meaning: Janaka honors King Dasharath with deep respect, seeing him as equal to Shiva. He then folds his hands and praises the good fortune and grandeur that have come to his house.
ramacharitamanas::1714.simple_insight: True honor is humble. It lifts the guest without lowering the host.
ramacharitamanas::1714.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, Janaka receives Dasharath and the wedding party with full royal courtesy. He does not treat the king as an ordinary guest, but as one worthy of the highest reverence. The scene shows the dignity and grace that surround this alliance.
ramacharitamanas::1714.modern_relevance: You meet your child’s future in-laws at the door, and the room is tense. One person’s humility can soften everything, turning formality into warmth.
ramacharitamanas::1714.insight: It teaches respect that is wholehearted, not performative, and praise that comes from genuine gratitude.

ramacharitamanas::1715.verse_sanskrit: पूजे भूपति सकल बराती। समधी सम सादर सब भाँती॥ आसन उचित दिए सब काहू। कहौं काह मुख एक उछाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1715.verse_hindi: राजा जनकजी ने सब बारातियों का समधी दशरथजी के समान ही सब प्रकार से आदरपूर्वक पूजन किया और सब किसी को उचित आसन दिए। मैं एक मुख से उस उत्साह का क्या वर्णन करूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1715.english_translation: King Janak honored all the wedding guests in every proper way, as a father-in-law honors a son-in-law. He gave everyone fitting seats. How can I describe that joy in a single mouth?
ramacharitamanas::1715.translation_literal: पूजे (honored) / भूपति (the king) / सकल (all) / बराती (wedding guests) / समधी (as a father-in-law) / सम (like) / सादर (respectfully) / सब भाँती (in every manner) ॥ / आसन (seats) / उचित (fitting) / दिए (gave) / सब काहू (to everyone) / कहौं (I say) / काह (what) / मुख (mouth) / एक (single) / उछाहू (joy, excitement) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1715.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1715.essence: Honor becomes visible in the way every guest is received.
ramacharitamanas::1715.simple_meaning: Janak welcomed every guest with full respect and gave each person a proper seat. The joy of the scene is so great it feels impossible to describe fully.
ramacharitamanas::1715.simple_insight: True hospitality sees everyone and makes room for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::1715.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s palace during Sita’s wedding, the king receives Dasharath and the entire marriage party with generous honor. The scene is overflowing with celebration, and the narrator pauses to say the joy is beyond words.
ramacharitamanas::1715.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where the host remembers every name, every seat, every elder’s comfort. No one feels like an extra. That is the kind of welcome Janak gives.
ramacharitamanas::1715.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the dignity shown through how each guest is received.

ramacharitamanas::1716.verse_sanskrit: सकल बरात जनक सनमानी। दान मान बिनती बर बानी॥ बिधि हरि हरु दिसिपति दिनराऊ। जे जानहिं रघुबीर प्रभाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1716.verse_hindi: राजा जनक ने दान, मान-सम्मान, विनय और उत्तम वाणी से सारी बारात का सम्मान किया। ब्रह्मा, विष्णु, शिव, दिक्पाल और सूर्य जो श्री रघुनाथजी का प्रभाव जानते हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1716.english_translation: Janak honored the whole wedding party with gifts, respect, humility, and gracious speech. Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, the guardians of directions, and the sun know the power of Raghubir.
ramacharitamanas::1716.translation_literal: सकल (entire) / बरात (wedding party) / जनक (Janak) / सनमानी (honored) / दान (gifts) / मान (respect) / बिनती (humility, request) / बर (excellent) / बानी (speech) / बिधि (Brahma) / हरि (Vishnu) / हरु (Shiva) / दिसिपति (lords of the directions) / दिनराऊ (sun) / जे (those who) / जानहिं (know) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / प्रभाऊ (power, influence)
ramacharitamanas::1716.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1716.essence: Honor becomes sacred when it reaches everyone without pride.
ramacharitamanas::1716.simple_meaning: Janak welcomes every guest with gifts, respect, humility, and kind words. Even the highest beings know Ram's power.
ramacharitamanas::1716.simple_insight: True honour is generous, humble, and wide enough for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::1716.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court during Sita's wedding, the king treats the entire bridal procession with gifts and courtesy. The verse then widens the scene: even Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, the guardians of the directions, and the sun recognize Ram's greatness. It is a moment of royal hospitality inside a divine wedding.
ramacharitamanas::1716.modern_relevance: A host notices the shy cousin at the edge of the room and makes space for him first. That small act of grace says more than the decorations ever could.
ramacharitamanas::1716.insight: It shifts attention from status display to generous conduct that makes others feel seen.

ramacharitamanas::1717.verse_sanskrit: कपट बिप्र बर बेष बनाएँ। कौतुक देखहिं अति सचु पाएँ॥ पूजे जनक देव सम जानें। दिए सुआसन बिनु पहिचानें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1717.verse_hindi: वे कपट से ब्राह्मणों का सुंदर वेश बनाए बहुत ही सुख पाते हुए सब लीला देख रहे थे। जनकजी ने उनको देवताओं के समान जानकर उनका पूजन किया और बिना पहिचाने भी उन्हें सुंदर आसन दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1717.english_translation: They had disguised themselves as clever Brahmins and watched the whole spectacle with delight. Janak honored them as though they were divine beings and gave them fine seats without recognizing them.
ramacharitamanas::1717.translation_literal: कपट (deceitfully) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / बर (excellent) / बेष (disguise) / बनाएँ (having made) / कौतुक (the spectacle) / देखहिं (they see) / अति (greatly) / सचु (joy) / पाएँ (having obtained) / पूजे (worshiped/honored) / जनक (Janak) / देव (divine beings) / सम (like) / जानें (having known) / दिए (gave) / सुआसन (fine seats) / बिनु (without) / पहिचानें (recognizing)
ramacharitamanas::1717.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1717.essence: Honor first; recognition can come later.
ramacharitamanas::1717.simple_meaning: The disguised men enjoyed the ceremony, and Janak honored them generously without knowing who they were.
ramacharitamanas::1717.simple_insight: Respect can be given before recognition. True courtesy does not wait for certainty.
ramacharitamanas::1717.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s wedding hall in Mithila, the disguised gods arrive as Brahmins to witness the swayamvar. Janak, full of generosity and reverence, welcomes them properly and gives them seats even without knowing their true identity.
ramacharitamanas::1717.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a crowded function and they seem ordinary, but you still offer warmth, water, and a seat. Later you learn you treated them with dignity before knowing anything about them.
ramacharitamanas::1717.insight: It shifts attention from status and recognition to immediate, respectful conduct.

ramacharitamanas::1718.verse_sanskrit: पहिचान को केहि जान सबहि अपान सुधि भोरी भई। आनंद कंदु बिलोकि दूलहु उभय दिसि आनँदमई॥ सुर लखे राम सुजान पूजे मानसिक आसन दए। अवलोकि सीलु सुभाउ प्रभु को बिबुध मन प्रमुदित भए॥
ramacharitamanas::1718.verse_hindi: कौन किसको जाने-पहिचाने! सबको अपनी ही सुध भूली हुई है। आनंदकन्द दूल्हे को देखकर दोनों ओर आनंदमयी स्थिति हो रही है। सुजान (सर्वज्ञ) श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने देवताओं को पहिचान लिया और उनकी मानसिक पूजा करके उन्हें मानसिक आसन दिए। प्रभु का शील-स्वभाव देखकर देवगण मन में बहुत आनंदित हुए।
ramacharitamanas::1718.english_translation: Who knows who here? Everyone has forgotten their own identity. Seeing the source of joy, the bridegroom, both sides are filled with joy. Wise Ram recognised the devas and honoured them with mental worship and seats in the mind. Seeing the Lord's noble conduct and nature, the devas became delighted in their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1718.translation_literal: पहिचान (recognition) / को (who) / केहि (whom) / जान (knows) / सबहि (everyone) / अपान (one's own) / सुधि (awareness) / भोरी (lost) / भई (became) / आनंद कंदु (source of joy) / बिलोकि (seeing) / दूलहु (bridegroom) / उभय दिसि (on both sides) / आनँदमई (filled with joy) / सुर (devas) / लखे (saw) / राम (Ram) / सुजान (all-knowing) / पूजे (honoured) / मानसिक (mental) / आसन (seat) / दए (gave) / अवलोकि (seeing) / सीलु (noble conduct) / सुभाउ (nature) / प्रभु (Lord) / को (of) / बिबुध (devas) / मन (mind) / प्रमुदित (delighted) / भए (became)
ramacharitamanas::1718.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1718.essence: True greatness honours others without losing its own radiance.
ramacharitamanas::1718.simple_meaning: At Ram and Sita's wedding, everyone is so absorbed in joy that they forget themselves. Ram notices the visiting devas, honours them inwardly, and their hearts fill with delight at his noble nature.
ramacharitamanas::1718.simple_insight: Real greatness notices others first. Reverence flows both ways when the heart is humble.
ramacharitamanas::1718.detailed_meaning: In Janak's wedding hall, the whole assembly is swept up in the sight of the bridegroom. The devas are present among the guests, and Ram, though all-knowing, recognises them, honours them inwardly, and reveals a gentleness that deepens their joy.
ramacharitamanas::1718.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the person at the center of attention still notices the quiet guest near the wall. That small act of recognition changes the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::1718.insight: It shifts admiration from appearance alone to the humility that makes true dignity visible.

ramacharitamanas::1719.verse_sanskrit: रामचन्द्र मुख चंद्र छबि लोचन चारु चकोर। करत पान सादर सकल प्रेमु प्रमोदु न थोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::1719.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के मुख रूपी चन्द्रमा की छबि को सभी के सुंदर नेत्र रूपी चकोर आदरपूर्वक पान कर रहे हैं, प्रेम और आनंद कम नहीं है (अर्थात बहुत है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1719.english_translation: The moon-like face of Ramchandra is beautiful; all the lovely eyes drink it like chakors. Love and delight do not lessen at all.
ramacharitamanas::1719.translation_literal: रामचन्द्र (Ramchandra) / मुख (face) / चंद्र (moon) / छबि (beauty) / लोचन (eyes) / चारु (lovely) / चकोर (chakor bird) / करत (doing) / पान (drinking) / सादर (with reverence) / सकल (all) / प्रेमु (love) / प्रमोदु (delight) / न थोर (not little)
ramacharitamanas::1719.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1719.essence: Ram's beauty feeds the gaze without ever being exhausted.
ramacharitamanas::1719.simple_meaning: Ram's face is so beautiful that everyone keeps looking at it with love and delight, and that joy never runs out.
ramacharitamanas::1719.simple_insight: Some beauty does not fade with attention; it deepens the more sincerely you behold it.
ramacharitamanas::1719.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the wedding scene is unfolding and everyone is already spellbound by Ram. This couplet pauses on the shared wonder: all eyes rest on him like birds drinking moonlight, while love and joy keep overflowing.
ramacharitamanas::1719.modern_relevance: You catch yourself staring at a bride and groom during the ceremony, smiling without meaning to. Some presence makes the whole room soften, and no one wants to look away.
ramacharitamanas::1719.insight: It shifts attention from the event around Ram to the transforming effect of beholding him.

ramacharitamanas::1720.verse_sanskrit: समउ बिलोकि बसिष्ठ बोलाए। सादर सतानंदु सुनि आए॥ बेगि कुअँरि अब आनहु जाई। चले मुदित मुनि आयसु पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1720.verse_hindi: समय देखकर वशिष्ठजी ने शतानंदजी को आदरपूर्वक बुलाया। वे सुनकर आदर के साथ आए। वशिष्ठजी ने कहा- अब जाकर राजकुमारी को शीघ्र ले आइए। मुनि की आज्ञा पाकर वे प्रसन्न होकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1720.english_translation: Vashishtha saw the right moment and called Shatananda with respect. Hearing him, Shatananda came reverently. Vashishtha said, "Go quickly and bring the princess here." Receiving the sage's command, he left happily.
ramacharitamanas::1720.translation_literal: समउ (right time) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बसिष्ठ (Vashishtha) / बोलाए (called) / सादर (with respect) / सतानंदु (Shatananda) / सुनि (hearing) / आए (came) / बेगि (quickly) / कुअँरि (princess) / अब (now) / आनहु (bring) / जाई (going) / चले (went) / मुदित (joyful) / मुनि (sage) / आयसु (command) / पाई (having received)
ramacharitamanas::1720.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1720.essence: The right moment moves forward through respectful, joyful obedience.
ramacharitamanas::1720.simple_meaning: Vashishtha notices the right moment, respectfully calls Shatananda, and sends him to bring the princess. Shatananda obeys gladly.
ramacharitamanas::1720.simple_insight: Right action begins with timing, respect, and cheerful obedience.
ramacharitamanas::1720.detailed_meaning: At the swayamvar scene, Vashishtha sees the moment has arrived. He calls Shatananda with honor and sends him to fetch the princess. The verse quietly moves the ceremony forward, showing how sacred events unfold through proper timing and orderly conduct.
ramacharitamanas::1720.modern_relevance: A family gathering is already humming with anticipation, and one person quietly notices the exact moment to speak. The right instruction, given respectfully, can move everything forward without strain.
ramacharitamanas::1720.insight: It teaches that even major turning points depend on calm timing and dignified coordination.

ramacharitamanas::1721.verse_sanskrit: रानी सुनि उपरोहित बानी। प्रमुदित सखिन्ह समेत सयानी॥ बिप्र बधू कुल बृद्ध बोलाईं। करि कुल रीति सुमंगल गाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1721.verse_hindi: बुद्धिमती रानी पुरोहित की वाणी सुनकर सखियों समेत बड़ी प्रसन्न हुईं। ब्राह्मणों की स्त्रियों और कुल की बूढ़ी स्त्रियों को बुलाकर उन्होंने कुलरीति करके सुंदर मंगल गीत गाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1721.english_translation: Hearing the priest's words, the wise queen rejoiced with her companions. She called the wives of the Brahmins and the elder women of the household, and they sang auspicious songs according to family custom.
ramacharitamanas::1721.translation_literal: रानी (queen) / सुनि (hearing) / उपरोहित (priest's) / बानी (words) / प्रमुदित (delighted) / सखिन्ह (with companions) / समेत (together with) / सयानी (wise) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / बधू (wives) / कुल (family) / बृद्ध (elders) / बोलाईं (called) / करि (doing) / कुल रीति (family custom) / सुमंगल (auspicious) / गाईं (sang)
ramacharitamanas::1721.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1721.essence: Joy becomes complete when it is prepared with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1721.simple_meaning: The queen hears the priest's instruction, feels joyful, gathers the women of the household, and has auspicious songs sung in the proper family way.
ramacharitamanas::1721.simple_insight: Right timing and shared ritual can turn an important moment into joy instead of anxiety.
ramacharitamanas::1721.detailed_meaning: Vashistha has just sent word to bring Sita. The wise queen hears the priest's message, rejoices with her companions, and calls the women of the household together. The palace prepares for a sacred family moment with song and custom.
ramacharitamanas::1721.modern_relevance: A family gets the call that the ceremony can begin. Instead of panic, someone steady starts gathering the right people, setting the mood, and making the room ready. Calm leadership can bless the whole moment.
ramacharitamanas::1721.insight: It shifts attention from private excitement to shared preparation and reverent action.

ramacharitamanas::1722.verse_sanskrit: नारि बेष जे सुर बर बामा। सकल सुभायँ सुंदरी स्यामा॥ तिन्हहि देखि सुखु पावहिं नारी। बिनु पहिचानि प्रानहु ते प्यारीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1722.verse_hindi: श्रेष्ठ देवांगनाएँ, जो सुंदर मनुष्य-स्त्रियों के वेश में हैं, सभी स्वभाव से ही सुंदरी और श्यामा (सोलह वर्ष की अवस्था वाली) हैं। उनको देखकर रनिवास की स्त्रियाँ सुख पाती हैं और बिना पहिचान के ही वे सबको प्राणों से भी प्यारी हो रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1722.english_translation: The celestial women, appearing in the form of beautiful human women, are all naturally lovely and youthful. The women of the palace feel joy at seeing them, and without knowing who they are, they become dearer than life itself.
ramacharitamanas::1722.translation_literal: नारि बेष (in women’s form) / जे (who) / सुर बर (excellent celestial beings) / बामा (beautiful women) / सकल (all) / सुभायँ (by nature) / सुंदरी (beautiful) / स्यामा (dark-hued, youthful) / तिन्हहि (them) / देखि (seeing) / सुखु (joy) / पावहिं (receive) / नारी (women) / बिनु (without) / पहिचानि (recognizing) / प्रानहु ते (than life) / प्यारीं (dear)
ramacharitamanas::1722.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1722.essence: Grace is recognized before identity is known.
ramacharitamanas::1722.simple_meaning: Beautiful celestial women appear among the palace women, and everyone feels joy simply by seeing them. Their grace is so natural that they are loved before anyone even knows who they are.
ramacharitamanas::1722.simple_insight: True charm needs no introduction; presence itself can soften a room.
ramacharitamanas::1722.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra has brought Rama and Lakshmana to King Janaka's court for Sita's swayamvar. The palace women, seeing the disguised celestial visitors, feel delighted and drawn to them. This is a scene of gathering, admiration, and quiet wonder before Sita enters.
ramacharitamanas::1722.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone seems instantly at ease around one person you barely know. No performance, no introduction — just a presence that makes others smile before they can explain why.
ramacharitamanas::1722.insight: It shifts attention from outward status to the natural warmth that makes people feel safe and happy.

ramacharitamanas::1723.verse_sanskrit: बार बार सनमानहिं रानी। उमा रमा सारद सम जानी॥ सीय सँवारि समाजु बनाई। मुदित मंडपहिं चलीं लवाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1723.verse_hindi: उन्हें पार्वती, लक्ष्मी और सरस्वती के समान जानकर रानी बार-बार उनका सम्मान करती हैं। (रनिवास की स्त्रियाँ और सखियाँ) सीताजी का श्रृंगार करके, मंडली बनाकर, प्रसन्न होकर उन्हें मंडप में लिवा चलीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1723.english_translation: The queen repeatedly honored them, knowing them to be like Uma, Rama, and Saraswati. After adorning Sita and arranging the wedding party, the joyful women led her to the pavilion.
ramacharitamanas::1723.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / सनमानहिं (honor) / रानी (the queen) / उमा (Uma) / रमा (Rama/Lakshmi) / सारद (Saraswati) / सम (like) / जानी (having known) ॥ / सीय (Sita) / सँवारि (after adorning) / समाजु (the wedding assembly) / बनाई (having arranged) / मुदित (joyful) / मंडपहिं (to the pavilion) / चलीं (went) / लवाई (led along) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1723.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1723.essence: Honor deepens when every woman is seen as sacred presence.
ramacharitamanas::1723.simple_meaning: The queen treats the visiting women with great respect, seeing them as divine figures. Then Sita is dressed beautifully and taken joyfully to the wedding pavilion.
ramacharitamanas::1723.simple_insight: Respect becomes natural when you see the sacred in others.
ramacharitamanas::1723.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court before Sita's wedding, the queen and attendants welcome the visiting women with repeated honor. Seeing them as like Uma, Lakshmi, and Saraswati, they dress Sita and guide her happily toward the pavilion.
ramacharitamanas::1723.modern_relevance: A bride’s room is full of careful hands fixing her veil, jewelry, and confidence before she walks out. The mood is reverent, not rushed.
ramacharitamanas::1723.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony as display to ceremony as reverent welcome.

ramacharitamanas::1724.verse_sanskrit: चलि ल्याइ सीतहि सखीं सादर सजि सुमंगल भामिनीं। नवसप्त साजें सुंदरी सब मत्त कुंजर गामिनीं॥ कल गान सुनि मुनि ध्यान त्यागहिं काम कोकिल लाजहीं। मंजीर नूपुर कलित कंकन ताल गति बर बाजहीं॥
ramacharitamanas::1724.verse_hindi: सुंदर मंगल का साज सजकर (रनिवास की) स्त्रियाँ और सखियाँ आदर सहित सीताजी को लिवा चलीं। सभी सुंदरियाँ सोलहों श्रृंगार किए हुए मतवाले हाथियों की चाल से चलने वाली हैं। उनके मनोहर गान को सुनकर मुनि ध्यान छोड़ देते हैं और कामदेव की कोयलें भी लजा जाती हैं। पायजेब, पैंजनी और सुंदर कंकण ताल की गति पर बड़े सुंदर बज रहे हैं।
ramacharitamanas::1724.english_translation: The women and companions, adorned with auspicious finery, respectfully led Sita forward. All the beautiful women, dressed in sixteen ornaments, moved like intoxicated elephants. Hearing their sweet songs, sages abandon meditation; even the cuckoos of desire are shamed. Anklets, toe-rings, and bracelets ring beautifully in time with the rhythm.
ramacharitamanas::1724.translation_literal: चलि (walking) / ल्याइ (bringing) / सीतहि (Sita) / सखीं (companions) / सादर (with respect) / सजि (having adorned) / सुमंगल (auspicious) / भामिनीं (women) / नवसप्त (newly-seven / sixteen) / साजें (ornaments) / सुंदरी (beautiful women) / सब (all) / मत्त (intoxicated) / कुंजर (elephants) / गामिनीं (walking like) / कल (sweet) / गान (song) / सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (sages) / ध्यान (meditation) / त्यागहिं (abandon) / काम (desire) / कोकिल (cuckoos) / लाजहीं (are ashamed) / मंजीर (anklets) / नूपुर (toe-rings) / कलित (adorned) / कंकन (bracelets) / ताल (rhythm) / गति (movement) / बर (excellent) / बाजहीं (resound)
ramacharitamanas::1724.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1724.essence: Grace enters before the bride does.
ramacharitamanas::1724.simple_meaning: Sita is led forward in a grand, festive procession. The women around her are beautifully dressed, their songs and ornaments creating a scene of overflowing grace and celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1724.simple_insight: Beauty can be so complete that it changes the whole atmosphere around it.
ramacharitamanas::1724.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the women of the palace and Sita's companions escort her toward the marriage pavilion. The verse lingers on their ornaments, music, and graceful movement, building the splendour of the moment before Sita appears among them.
ramacharitamanas::1724.modern_relevance: A wedding aisle, a room full of relatives, the sound of bangles and soft laughter before the first entrance — some moments carry their own sacred electricity.
ramacharitamanas::1724.insight: It turns attention from the individual object to the whole atmosphere a person creates.

ramacharitamanas::1725.verse_sanskrit: सोहति बनिता बृंद महुँ सहज सुहावनि सीय। छबि ललना गन मध्य जनु सुषमा तिय कमनीय ॥
ramacharitamanas::1725.verse_hindi: सहज ही सुंदरी सीताजी स्त्रियों के समूह में इस प्रकार शोभा पा रही हैं, मानो छबि रूपी ललनाओं के समूह के बीच साक्षात परम मनोहर शोभा रूपी स्त्री सुशोभित हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1725.english_translation: Sita shines among the women like natural beauty itself among beautiful ladies.
ramacharitamanas::1725.translation_literal: सोहति (shines) / बनिता बृंद (group of women) / महुँ (among) / सहज (natural, innate) / सुहावनि (lovely) / सीय (Sita) / छबि (beauty, radiance) / ललना गन (group of women) / मध्य (in the midst) / जनु (as if) / सुषमा (beauty, grace) / तिय (woman) / कमनीय (lovely, charming)
ramacharitamanas::1725.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1725.simple_meaning: Sita stands out among the women because her beauty is effortless and naturally radiant.
ramacharitamanas::1725.simple_insight: True grace does not compete; it simply reveals itself.
ramacharitamanas::1725.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the women lead Sita toward the wedding pavilion with reverence. Amid the finely dressed crowd, her beauty does not look arranged or forced. Tulsidas pauses on that quiet radiance before the larger praise of her form begins.
ramacharitamanas::1725.modern_relevance: You walk into a room full of polished, carefully styled people, and one person quietly changes the atmosphere without trying. Their ease makes everyone else look like they are performing.
ramacharitamanas::1725.insight: It shifts attention from decoration to natural presence, showing that real charm needs no display.

ramacharitamanas::1726.verse_sanskrit: सिय सुंदरता बरनि न जाई। लघु मति बहुत मनोहरताई॥ आवत दीखि बरातिन्ह सीता। रूप रासि सब भाँति पुनीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1726.verse_hindi: सीताजी की सुंदरता का वर्णन नहीं हो सकता, क्योंकि बुद्धि बहुत छोटी है और मनोहरता बहुत बड़ी है। रूप की राशि और सब प्रकार से पवित्र सीताजी को बारातियों ने आते देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1726.english_translation: Sita's beauty cannot be described. The mind is too small to grasp her charm. The wedding party saw Sita arrive, a treasure of form, pure in every way.
ramacharitamanas::1726.translation_literal: सिय (Sita) / सुंदरता (beauty) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाई (can be done) । / लघु (small) / मति (intellect) / बहुत (very) / मनोहरताई (charm, loveliness) ॥ / आवत (coming) / दीखि (saw) / बरातिन्ह (by the wedding party) / सीता (Sita) । / रूप (form, beauty) / रासि (heap, treasure) / सब (all) / भाँति (ways) / पुनीता (pure) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1726.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1726.essence: Some radiance cannot be put into words.
ramacharitamanas::1726.simple_meaning: Sita's beauty is beyond description, and the wedding guests see her arriving as pure, radiant, and complete in every way.
ramacharitamanas::1726.simple_insight: Some presence is felt more deeply than it can be explained.
ramacharitamanas::1726.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the wedding procession is arriving and everyone is waiting to see Sita. Tulsidas pauses the scene to say that her beauty cannot be captured by ordinary speech or thought, because the moment itself exceeds description.
ramacharitamanas::1726.modern_relevance: You see someone enter a room and the whole atmosphere changes before anyone speaks. Some moments are understood first by the heart, and only later, imperfectly, by words.
ramacharitamanas::1726.insight: It shifts attention from trying to explain beauty to simply recognizing its overwhelming presence.

ramacharitamanas::1727.verse_sanskrit: सबहिं मनहिं मन किए प्रनामा। देखि राम भए पूरनकामा॥ हरषे दसरथ सुतन्ह समेता। कहि न जाइ उर आनँदु जेता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1727.verse_hindi: सभी ने उन्हें मन ही मन प्रणाम किया। श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर तो सभी पूर्णकाम (कृतकृत्य) हो गए। राजा दशरथजी पुत्रों सहित हर्षित हुए। उनके हृदय में जितना आनंद था, वह कहा नहीं जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1727.english_translation: Everyone bowed to him in their hearts. Seeing Ram, they felt fully fulfilled. King Dasharath rejoiced with his sons. The joy in his heart cannot be spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1727.translation_literal: सबहिं (everyone) / मनहिं मन (in the mind) / किए (made) / प्रनामा (salutations) / देखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / भए (became) / पूरनकामा (fully fulfilled in desire) / हरषे (rejoiced) / दसरथ सुतन्ह समेता (Dasharath with his sons) / कहि न जाइ (cannot be said) / उर (in the heart) / आनँदु (joy) / जेता (as much as)
ramacharitamanas::1727.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1727.essence: Ram’s presence alone makes everyone feel complete.
ramacharitamanas::1727.simple_meaning: Everyone silently bowed as Ram arrived. Seeing him, they felt complete, and Dasharath rejoiced with his sons beyond words.
ramacharitamanas::1727.simple_insight: Some presences do not need explanation; they make the heart feel complete at once.
ramacharitamanas::1727.detailed_meaning: The marriage hall has filled, and Sita has already been seen. Now Ram appears, and the whole gathering responds inwardly before any words are spoken. Dasharath stands with his sons, overwhelmed by joy as the moment finally becomes real.
ramacharitamanas::1727.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after months apart, and the tension drops before anyone speaks. Some arrivals settle every heart at once.
ramacharitamanas::1727.insight: It shifts attention from outward ceremony to the inner recognition that true presence creates.

ramacharitamanas::1728.verse_sanskrit: सुर प्रनामु करि बरिसहिं फूला। मुनि असीस धुनि मंगल मूला॥ गान निसान कोलाहलु भारी। प्रेम प्रमोद मगन नर नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1728.verse_hindi: देवता प्रणाम करके फूल बरसा रहे हैं। मंगलों की मूल मुनियों के आशीर्वादों की ध्वनि हो रही है। गानों और नगाड़ों के शब्द से बड़ा शोर मच रहा है। सभी नर-नारी प्रेम और आनंद में मग्न हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1728.english_translation: The radiant beings bow and shower flowers. The sages' blessings sound, source of all auspiciousness. Drums and songs rise in a great uproar. Men and women are lost in love and joy.
ramacharitamanas::1728.translation_literal: सुर (radiant beings) / प्रनामु करि (having bowed) / बरिसहिं (shower) / फूला (flowers) / मुनि (sages) / असीस (blessings) / धुनि (sound) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मूल (root/source) / गान (songs) / निसान (drums) / कोलाहलु (uproar) / भारी (great) / प्रेम (love) / प्रमोद (joy) / मगन (immersed) / नर (men) / नारी (women)
ramacharitamanas::1728.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1728.essence: A sacred moment makes even the crowd feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1728.simple_meaning: Heavenly beings bow and shower flowers while sages bless the scene. Drums, songs, and joyful noise fill the air as everyone is swept up in love and delight.
ramacharitamanas::1728.simple_insight: Some moments feel so sacred that even the crowd becomes part of the blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1728.detailed_meaning: At Sita's wedding pavilion, the celebration swells beyond human scale. Radiant beings bow from above, sages bless the moment, and the whole gathering of men and women is carried into joy. This verse paints the sacred atmosphere before the ceremony continues.
ramacharitamanas::1728.modern_relevance: A wedding hall goes silent for one breath, then erupts as the couple appears. The noise, the flowers, the tears — everyone knows they are witnessing something larger than the room.
ramacharitamanas::1728.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the shared reverence it awakens.

ramacharitamanas::1729.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि सीय मंडपहिं आई। प्रमुदित सांति पढ़हिं मुनिराई॥ तेहि अवसर कर बिधि ब्यवहारू। दुहुँ कुलगुर सब कीन्ह अचारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1729.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार सीताजी मंडप में आईं। मुनिराज बहुत ही आनंदित होकर शांतिपाठ पढ़ रहे हैं। उस अवसर की सब रीति, व्यवहार और कुलाचार दोनों कुलगुरुओं ने किए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1729.english_translation: In this way Sita entered the pavilion. The great sages, filled with joy, recited auspicious prayers. At that moment, both family teachers performed all the proper rites and customs.
ramacharitamanas::1729.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / सीय (Sita) / मंडपहिं (to the pavilion) / आई (came) / प्रमुदित (joyful) / सांति (auspicious peace-prayer) / पढ़हिं (recite) / मुनिराई (great sages) / तेहि अवसर (at that moment) / कर (of) / बिधि (proper) / ब्यवहारू (rites and conduct) / दुहुँ (both) / कुलगुर (family teachers) / सब (all) / कीन्ह (performed) / अचारू (customs)
ramacharitamanas::1729.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1729.essence: A holy occasion becomes complete through proper rite and blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1729.simple_meaning: Sita enters the wedding pavilion, while the sages recite blessings and both family teachers carry out the proper rituals and customs.
ramacharitamanas::1729.simple_insight: Sacred moments are held together by order, blessing, and care.
ramacharitamanas::1729.detailed_meaning: Sita arrives at the wedding pavilion in Mithila. The sages chant auspicious prayers, and both family teachers oversee every rite and custom. The verse is scene-setting, showing the ceremony moving forward in a sacred, orderly way.
ramacharitamanas::1729.modern_relevance: A wedding hall goes quiet as the elders begin the ritual and everyone finds their place. The beauty of the moment comes not from spectacle, but from the care that holds it together.
ramacharitamanas::1729.insight: It shifts attention from the main event to the sacred discipline that makes the event complete.

ramacharitamanas::1730.verse_sanskrit: आचारु करि गुर गौरि गनपति मुदित बिप्र पुजावहीं। सुर प्रगटि पूजा लेहिं देहिं असीस अति सुखु पावहीं॥ मधुपर्क मंगल द्रब्य जो जेहि समय मुनि मन महुँ चहें। भरे कनक कोपर कलस सो तब लिएहिं परिचारक रहैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1730.verse_hindi: कुलाचार करके गुरुजी प्रसन्न होकर गौरीजी, गणेशजी और ब्राह्मणों की पूजा करा रहे हैं (अथवा ब्राह्मणों के द्वारा गौरी और गणेश की पूजा करवा रहे हैं)। देवता प्रकट होकर पूजा ग्रहण करते हैं, आशीर्वाद देते हैं और अत्यन्त सुख पा रहे हैं। मधुपर्क आदि जिस किसी भी मांगलिक पदार्थ की मुनि जिस समय भी मन में चाह मात्र करते हैं, सेवकगण उसी समय सोने की परातों में और कलशों में भरकर उन पदार्थों को लिए तैयार रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1730.english_translation: Following the family customs, the teacher joyfully had Gauri, Ganapati, and the Brahmins worshipped. The radiant beings appeared, accepted the worship, gave blessings, and felt great delight. Whatever auspicious drink or offering the sages desired in their minds, servants immediately brought it in golden plates and vessels.
ramacharitamanas::1730.translation_literal: आचारु (custom/ritual) / करि (having done) / गुर (teacher) / गौरि (Gauri) / गनपति (Ganapati) / मुदित (joyful) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / पुजावहीं (caused to be worshipped) / सुर (radiant beings) / प्रगटि (appearing) / पूजा (worship) / लेहिं (receive) / देहिं (give) / असीस (blessings) / अति (greatly) / सुखु (joy) / पावहीं (they obtain) / मधुपर्क (honour-offering) / मंगल (auspicious) / द्रब्य (articles) / जो (which) / जेहि (whichever) / समय (time) / मुनि (sages) / मन (mind) / महुँ (in) / चहें (desire) / भरे (filled) / कनक (gold) / कोपर (platters) / कलस (vessels) / सो (those) / तब (then) / लिएहिं (bring) / परिचारक (attendants) / रहैं (remain)
ramacharitamanas::1730.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1730.essence: True reverence makes every needed offering appear at once.
ramacharitamanas::1730.simple_meaning: The wedding ceremony is being carried out with perfect ritual care. Even the radiant beings and sages are honored immediately, and every needed offering appears without delay.
ramacharitamanas::1730.simple_insight: When reverence is complete, everything needed seems to arrive at the right moment.
ramacharitamanas::1730.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s wedding in Mithila, the sacred order is exact and overflowing with joy. The teacher, the sages, the Brahmins, and even the radiant beings are honored properly, while attendants stand ready with every offering the ritual requires.
ramacharitamanas::1730.modern_relevance: A wedding hall is buzzing, and the family keeps moving before anyone asks. Flowers, water, food, seating — everything is ready because everyone is serving the moment, not themselves.
ramacharitamanas::1730.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony as performance to ceremony as wholehearted service.

ramacharitamanas::1731.verse_sanskrit: कुल रीति प्रीति समेत रबि कहि देत सबु सादर कियो। एहि भाँति देव पुजाइ सीतहि सुभग सिंघासनु दियो॥ सिय राम अवलोकनि परसपर प्रेमु काहुँ न लखि परै। मन बुद्धि बर बानी अगोचर प्रगट कबि कैसें करै ॥
ramacharitamanas::1731.verse_hindi: स्वयं सूर्यदेव प्रेम सहित अपने कुल की सब रीतियाँ बता देते हैं और वे सब आदरपूर्वक की जा रही हैं। इस प्रकार देवताओं की पूजा कराके मुनियों ने सीताजी को सुंदर सिंहासन दिया। श्री सीताजी और श्री रामजी का आपस में एक-दूसरे को देखना तथा उनका परस्पर का प्रेम किसी को लख नहीं पड़ रहा है, जो बात श्रेष्ठ मन, बुद्धि और वाणी से भी परे है, उसे कवि क्यों कर प्रकट करे? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1731.english_translation: With love and due respect, the Sun himself speaks of all the family customs. In this way, after the divine beings were worshipped, a beautiful throne was given to Sita. The mutual sight of Sita and Ram, and their love for each other, cannot be seen by anyone; how can a poet reveal what lies beyond the best mind, intellect, and speech?
ramacharitamanas::1731.translation_literal: कुल (family) / रीति (custom) / प्रीति (love) / समेत (together with) / रबि (the Sun) / कहि (saying) / देत (giving) / सबु (all) / सादर (with respect) / कियो (done) / एहि भाँति (in this way) / देव (divine beings) / पुजाइ (having worshipped) / सीतहि (to Sita) / सुभग (beautiful) / सिंघासनु (throne) / दियो (gave) / सिय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / अवलोकनि (looking upon) / परसपर (mutually) / प्रेमु (love) / काहुँ (to anyone) / न (not) / लखि (seen) / परै (can be seen) / मन (mind) / बुद्धि (discerning mind) / बर (best) / बानी (speech) / अगोचर (beyond reach) / प्रगट (manifest) / कबि (poet) / कैसें (how) / करै (can make)
ramacharitamanas::1731.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1731.essence: True love between Ram and Sita cannot be captured by speech.
ramacharitamanas::1731.simple_meaning: The wedding hall is full of reverence and ritual, but the deepest thing there is the silent love between Sita and Ram. That love is beyond ordinary seeing or describing.
ramacharitamanas::1731.simple_insight: Some truths are felt most clearly when language falls away.
