ramacharitamanas::1731.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, the rites are being completed with great care and honor. The gods are worshipped, Sita is seated on a splendid throne, and the real wonder is the unspoken love between Sita and Ram — too deep for ordinary speech.
ramacharitamanas::1731.modern_relevance: You watch two people at a wedding glance at each other across a crowded room, and the whole noise of the event fades. What matters most is not what gets announced, but what is quietly recognized.
ramacharitamanas::1731.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to the invisible bond that ceremony only points toward.

ramacharitamanas::1732.verse_sanskrit: होम समय तनु धरि अनलु अति सुख आहुति लेहिं। बिप्र बेष धरि बेद सब कहि बिबाह बिधि देहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1732.verse_hindi: हवन के समय अग्निदेव शरीर धारण करके बड़े ही सुख से आहुति ग्रहण करते हैं और सारे वेद ब्राह्मण वेष धरकर विवाह की विधियाँ बताए देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1732.english_translation: At the time of the fire ritual, the fire deity took a body and gladly accepted the offerings. The Vedas, dressed as priests, explained the rites of the wedding.
ramacharitamanas::1732.translation_literal: होम (fire ritual) / समय (time) / तनु (body) / धरि (taking) / अनलु (fire) / अति (very) / सुख (with joy) / आहुति (offering) / लेहिं (receive) / बिप्र (priestly) / बेष (disguise) / धरि (taking) / बेद (Vedas) / सब (all) / कहि (speaking) / बिबाह (wedding) / बिधि (rites) / देहिं (give)
ramacharitamanas::1732.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1732.essence: Sacred rites become alive when the whole world seems to bless them.
ramacharitamanas::1732.simple_meaning: At the wedding fire ritual, the sacred fire seemed to take form and gladly receive the offerings, while the Vedas appeared as priests and taught the marriage rites.
ramacharitamanas::1732.simple_insight: The whole ceremony is shown as divinely approved, complete, and alive with blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1732.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s grand wedding preparations, the ritual itself becomes wondrous. Fire seems to take a body and accept the offerings with delight, while the Vedas appear in priestly form to guide the marriage rites. The scene prepares the sacred fulfillment of Sita and Ram’s union.
ramacharitamanas::1732.modern_relevance: A wedding hall is full, the chants begin, and every detail suddenly feels larger than ceremony. The moment carries the sense that something sacred is being formally welcomed into ordinary life.
ramacharitamanas::1732.insight: It shifts attention from ritual as performance to ritual as living blessing.

ramacharitamanas::1733.verse_sanskrit: जनक पाटमहिषी जग जानी। सीय मातु किमि जाइ बखानी॥॥ सुजसु सुकृत सुख सुंदरताई। सब समेटि बिधि रची बनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1733.verse_hindi: जनकजी की जगविख्यात पटरानी और सीताजी की माता का बखान तो हो ही कैसे सकता है। सुयश, सुकृत (पुण्य), सुख और सुंदरता सबको बटोरकर विधाता ने उन्हें सँवारकर तैयार किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1733.english_translation: Janaka's queen, known throughout the world, and Sita's mother—how can anyone describe her? The creator shaped her by gathering fame, virtue, joy, and beauty together.
ramacharitamanas::1733.translation_literal: जनक (Janaka) / पाटमहिषी (chief queen) / जग (world) / जानी (known) / सीय (Sita's) / मातु (mother) / किमि (how) / जाइ (can be) / बखानी (described)॥ / सुजसु (good fame) / सुकृत (good deeds) / सुख (joy) / सुंदरताई (beauty) / सब (all) / समेटि (gathering together) / बिधि (the creator) / रची (fashioned) / बनाई (made)
ramacharitamanas::1733.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1733.essence: Grace can be so complete that words fall short.
ramacharitamanas::1733.simple_meaning: Sita's mother is beyond ordinary description. She is presented as someone fashioned from fame, virtue, joy, and beauty themselves.
ramacharitamanas::1733.simple_insight: Some people are so complete that language feels too small for them.
ramacharitamanas::1733.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's court, the wedding preparations continue. Before the sacred gathering begins, the narrator pauses to honor Sita's mother, the famous queen of Mithila. Her grace is so complete that even praise feels inadequate.
ramacharitamanas::1733.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose kindness, dignity, and warmth make everyone softer around them. Later, you try to describe them and fail. Some presence is larger than description.
ramacharitamanas::1733.insight: It shifts attention from events to the quiet radiance that makes the whole scene sacred.

ramacharitamanas::1734.verse_sanskrit: समउ जानि मुनिबरन्ह बोलाईं। सुनत सुआसिनि सादर ल्याईं॥ जनक बाम दिसि सोह सुनयना। हिमगिरि संग बनी जनु मयना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1734.verse_hindi: समय जानकर श्रेष्ठ मुनियों ने उनको बुलवाया। यह सुनते ही सुहागिनी स्त्रियाँ उन्हें आदरपूर्वक ले आईं। सुनयनाजी (जनकजी की पटरानी) जनकजी की बाईं ओर ऐसी सोह रही हैं, मानो हिमाचल के साथ मैनाजी शोभित हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1734.english_translation: Knowing the right moment, the sages called them. Hearing this, the married women respectfully brought them in. Sunayana shone on Janak's left side, like Maina beside the Himavan.
ramacharitamanas::1734.translation_literal: समउ (the proper time) / जानि (having known) / मुनिबरन्ह (the best sages) / बोलाईं (called) / सुनत (hearing) / सुआसिनि (married women) / सादर (with respect) / ल्याईं (brought) / जनक (of Janak) / बाम दिसि (left side) / सोह (shone) / सुनयना (Sunayana) / हिमगिरि (Himavan) / संग (with) / बनी (adorned) / जनु (as if) / मयना (Maina)
ramacharitamanas::1734.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1734.essence: Dignity itself becomes visible when a house is ready for blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1734.simple_meaning: At the proper moment, the sages summoned the women. The married women brought Sunayana respectfully, and she stood beside Janak like Maina beside Himavan.
ramacharitamanas::1734.simple_insight: Reverence can be seen in the smallest gestures of welcome.
ramacharitamanas::1734.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court during the wedding preparations, the sages give the signal and the married women lead Sunayana forward with honor. Tulsidas pauses to praise her beauty and dignity, setting a sacred, graceful mood before the ritual offerings begin.
ramacharitamanas::1734.modern_relevance: A family room falls quiet when the bride’s mother enters with that steady, proud dignity. Everyone knows the day is bigger because she is there.
ramacharitamanas::1734.insight: It turns a ceremonial arrival into an image of honor, grace, and auspicious order.

ramacharitamanas::1735.verse_sanskrit: कनक कलस मनि कोपर रूरे। सुचि सुगंध मंगल जल पूरे॥ निज कर मुदित रायँ अरु रानी। धरे राम के आगें आनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1735.verse_hindi: पवित्र, सुगंधित और मंगल जल से भरे सोने के कलश और मणियों की सुंदर परातें राजा और रानी ने आनंदित होकर अपने हाथों से लाकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी के आगे रखीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1735.english_translation: The king and queen, delighted, brought golden vessels and jeweled trays filled with pure, fragrant, auspicious water and placed them before Ram with their own hands.
ramacharitamanas::1735.translation_literal: कनक (golden) / कलस (vessels) / मनि (jewels) / कोपर (trays) / रूरे (beautiful) / सुचि (pure) / सुगंध (fragrant) / मंगल (auspicious) / जल (water) / पूरे (filled) / निज (own) / कर (hands) / मुदित (delighted) / रायँ (king) / अरु (and) / रानी (queen) / धरे (placed) / राम के (of Ram) / आगें (in front) / आनी (bringing)
ramacharitamanas::1735.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1735.essence: True reverence shows itself in what you place before the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::1735.simple_meaning: The king and queen joyfully place ceremonial vessels of pure, fragrant water before Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1735.simple_insight: Love becomes visible in small, careful acts of welcome.
ramacharitamanas::1735.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the wedding preparations are in full bloom. The king and queen themselves bring golden vessels and jeweled trays filled with sacred water and place them before Ram. The scene shows honor turning into action.
ramacharitamanas::1735.modern_relevance: You set out the best cups before a guest arrives, then realize the care matters more than the display. Respect becomes real only when your hands do the welcoming.
ramacharitamanas::1735.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to a deliberate act of honoring someone with care.

ramacharitamanas::1736.verse_sanskrit: पढ़हिं बेद मुनि मंगल बानी। गगन सुमन झरि अवसरु जानी॥ बरु बिलोकि दंपति अनुरागे। पाय पुनीत पखारन लागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1736.verse_hindi: मुनि मंगलवाणी से वेद पढ़ रहे हैं। सुअवसर जानकर आकाश से फूलों की झड़ी लग गई है। दूल्हे को देखकर राजा-रानी प्रेममग्न हो गए और उनके पवित्र चरणों को पखारने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1736.english_translation: The sages recite the Vedas with auspicious words. Knowing the moment, flowers rain down from the sky. Seeing the groom, the king and queen are filled with love and begin washing his sacred feet.
ramacharitamanas::1736.translation_literal: पढ़हिं (recite) / बेद (the Vedas) / मुनि (sages) / मंगल बानी (auspicious words) / गगन (sky) / सुमन (flowers) / झरि (showering) / अवसरु (the moment) / जानी (knowing) / बरु (the groom) / बिलोकि (seeing) / दंपति (the royal couple) / अनुरागे (filled with love) / पाय (feet) / पुनीत (sacred) / पखारन (to wash) / लागे (began)
ramacharitamanas::1736.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1736.essence: True honour begins when love bows before greatness.
ramacharitamanas::1736.simple_meaning: The wedding moment turns sacred: sages chant, flowers fall, and the king and queen lovingly wash Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::1736.simple_insight: Love becomes worship when the heart recognises what stands before it.
ramacharitamanas::1736.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the marriage rite has reached its holy moment. The sages chant, the sky showers flowers, and King Janak and Queen Sunayana, overwhelmed by devotion, wash Ram's feet before the wedding proceeds.
ramacharitamanas::1736.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence changes the whole room. The conversation stops, the noise drops away, and even ordinary gestures feel reverent.
ramacharitamanas::1736.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to recognition: the deepest response is humble devotion.

ramacharitamanas::1737.verse_sanskrit: लागे पखारन पाय पंकज प्रेम तन पुलकावली। नभ नगर गान निसान जय धुनि उमगि जनु चहुँ दिसि चली॥ जे पद सरोज मनोज अरि उर सर सदैव बिराजहीं। जे सुकृत सुमिरत बिमलता मन सकल कलि मल भाजहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1737.verse_hindi: वे श्री रामजी के चरण कमलों को पखारने लगे, प्रेम से उनके शरीर में पुलकावली छा रही है। आकाश और नगर में होने वाली गान, नगाड़े और जय-जयकार की ध्वनि मानो चारों दिशाओं में उमड़ चली, जो चरण कमल कामदेव के शत्रु श्री शिवजी के हृदय रूपी सरोवर में सदा ही विराजते हैं, जिनका एक बार भी स्मरण करने से मन में निर्मलता आ जाती है और कलियुग के सारे पाप भाग जाते हैं,॥1।
ramacharitamanas::1737.english_translation: They began washing Ram's lotus feet, their bodies trembling with love. Songs, drums, and cries of victory surged through heaven and the city. Those lotus feet always rest in Shiva's heart, and even a single remembrance of them brings purity while all stains of Kali-yuga fall away.
ramacharitamanas::1737.translation_literal: लागे (began) / पखारन (to wash) / पाय (feet) / पंकज (lotus) / प्रेम (love) / तन (body) / पुलकावली (goosebumps, thrill) / नभ (sky) / नगर (city) / गान (songs) / निसान (drums) / जय धुनि (victory cries) / उमगि (surging) / जनु (as if) / चहुँ दिसि (to the four directions) / चली (went) / जे (those) / पद (feet) / सरोज (lotus) / मनोज अरि (enemy of desire, Shiva) / उर (heart) / सर (lake) / सदैव (always) / बिराजहीं (abide) / जे (those) / सुकृत (good deeds, merit) / सुमिरत (remembering) / बिमलता (purity) / मन (mind) / सकल (all) / कलि (Kali-yuga) / मल (stains) / भाजहीं (flee, depart)
ramacharitamanas::1737.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1737.essence: Ram's feet purify the one who remembers them with love.
ramacharitamanas::1737.simple_meaning: Ram's feet are washed with love, and that same remembrance is said to purify the mind and drive away all darkness.
ramacharitamanas::1737.simple_insight: Reverence is not passive here; it cleans the mind and turns devotion into inner clarity.
ramacharitamanas::1737.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the wedding celebration has reached its most sacred moment. King and queen wash Ram's feet themselves, overcome with love. The verse widens from the ritual to Ram's divine power: even remembering those feet purifies the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1737.modern_relevance: You pause before a wedding ceremony, hands shaking as you help someone you deeply respect. The gesture feels small, but your whole body knows it is not small at all.
ramacharitamanas::1737.insight: It shifts devotion from a feeling into an act that transforms the one who offers it.

ramacharitamanas::1738.verse_sanskrit: जे परसि मुनिबनिता लही गति रही जो पातकमई। मकरंदु जिन्ह को संभु सिर सुचिता अवधि सुर बरनई॥ करि मधुप मन मुनि जोगिजन जे सेइ अभिमत गति लहैं। ते पद पखारत भाग्यभाजनु जनकु जय जय सब कहैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1738.verse_hindi: जिनका स्पर्श पाकर गौतम मुनि की स्त्री अहल्या ने, जो पापमयी थी, परमगति पाई, जिन चरणकमलों का मकरन्द रस (गंगाजी) शिवजी के मस्तक पर विराजमान है, जिसको देवता पवित्रता की सीमा बताते हैं, मुनि और योगीजन अपने मन को भौंरा बनाकर जिन चरणकमलों का सेवन करके मनोवांछित गति प्राप्त करते हैं, उन्हीं चरणों को भाग्य के पात्र (बड़भागी) जनकजी धो रहे हैं, यह देखकर सब जय-जयकार कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1738.english_translation: Those feet transformed Ahalya, the wife of Gautama, who had fallen into sin. Their pollen-rasa is praised by Shiva, the limit of purity. The sages and yogis worship those feet in their minds and attain the state they seek. Janak, fortunate among men, washes those feet, and all cry victory.
ramacharitamanas::1738.translation_literal: जे (those who) / परसि (touching) / मुनिबनिता (the wife of the sage) / लही (attained) / गति (state, liberation) / रही (remained) / जो (who) / पातकमई (full of sin) / मकरंदु (pollen-nectar) / जिन्ह (whose) / को (of) / संभु (Shiva) / सिर (head) / सुचिता (purity) / अवधि (limit) / सुर (devas) / बरनई (praise) / करि (making) / मधुप (bee) / मन (mind) / मुनि (sages) / जोगिजन (yogis) / जे (who) / सेइ (serving) / अभिमत (desired) / गति (state) / लहैं (attain) / ते (those) / पद (feet) / पखारत (washing) / भाग्यभाजनु (fortunate one) / जनकु (Janak) / जय जय (victory, victory) / सब (all) / कहैं (say)
ramacharitamanas::1738.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1738.essence: The purest feet are washed by the fortunate.
ramacharitamanas::1738.simple_meaning: Ram's feet are so holy that they lifted Ahalya, are praised by Shiva, and are sought by sages and yogis. Now King Janak washes those same feet in joy.
ramacharitamanas::1738.simple_insight: Greatness bows before what it reveres. Even the highest honor becomes beautiful when offered with love.
ramacharitamanas::1738.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the ceremony has reached a sacred peak. Janak, the wise king, is washing Ram's feet while the assembled court watches in wonder. The verse recalls why those feet are worthy of such honor: they redeemed Ahalya, are praised by Shiva, and are sought by sages and yogis.
ramacharitamanas::1738.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose quiet integrity changes the room, and even the most accomplished people lower their heads. Real reverence feels natural when character is unmistakable.
ramacharitamanas::1738.insight: It shifts status from social rank to spiritual worth, showing that true honor belongs to what transforms others.

ramacharitamanas::1739.verse_sanskrit: बर कुअँरि करतल जोरि साखोचारु दोउ कुलगुर करैं। भयो पानिगहनु बिलोकि बिधि सुर मनुज मुनि आनँद भरैं॥ सुखमूल दूलहु देखि दंपति पुलक तन हुलस्यो हियो। करि लोक बेद बिधानु कन्यादानु नृपभूषन कियो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1739.verse_hindi: दोनों कुलों के गुरु वर और कन्या की हथेलियों को मिलाकर शाखोच्चार करने लगे। पाणिग्रहण हुआ देखकर ब्रह्मादि देवता, मनुष्य और मुनि आनंद में भर गए। सुख के मूल दूल्हे को देखकर राजा-रानी का शरीर पुलकित हो गया और हृदय आनंद से उमंग उठा। राजाओं के अलंकार स्वरूप महाराज जनकजी ने लोक और वेद की रीति को करके कन्यादान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1739.english_translation: The family priests joined the bride and groom’s hands and began the wedding rites. Seeing the marriage complete, Brahma, the gods, humans, and sages were filled with joy. The king and queen’s bodies thrilled with delight at the blessed bridegroom, and Janak, ornament of kings, gave Sita in marriage according to worldly custom and Vedic law.
ramacharitamanas::1739.translation_literal: बर कुअँरि (bride and prince) / करतल (palms) / जोरि (joining) / साखोचारु (wedding rites) / दोउ (both) / कुलगुर (family priests) / करैं (do) ॥ भयो (became) / पानिगहनु (marriage-hand-taking) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बिधि (Brahma) / सुर (gods) / मनुज (humans) / मुनि (sages) / आनँद (joy) / भरैं (fill) ॥ सुखमूल (root of joy) / दूलहु (bridegroom) / देखि (seeing) / दंपति (the royal couple) / पुलक (hairs standing on end) / तन (body) / हुलस्यो (thrilled) / हियो (heart) / भयो (became) ॥ करि (doing) / लोक (worldly) / बेद (Vedic) / बिधानु (law/ritual) / कन्यादानु (gift of the daughter) / नृपभूषन (ornament of kings, Janak) / कियो (did) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1739.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1739.essence: A true marriage blesses everyone who sees it.
ramacharitamanas::1739.simple_meaning: The wedding begins, everyone rejoices, and Janak gives Sita away in the proper ritual way.
ramacharitamanas::1739.simple_insight: A rightful union can make an entire world feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1739.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the marriage of Ram and Sita is underway. The family priests join their hands, the heavens and earth rejoice, and King Janak completes the sacred gift of his daughter. This verse is a ceremonial bridge into the marriage itself.
ramacharitamanas::1739.modern_relevance: At a wedding, the room goes quiet as the hands are joined and the vows begin. Even the people who came only to witness feel the weight of something holy and complete.
ramacharitamanas::1739.insight: It frames marriage as a shared sacred event, not a private transaction.

ramacharitamanas::1740.verse_sanskrit: हिमवंत जिमि गिरिजा महेसहि हरिहि श्री सागर दई। तिमि जनक रामहि सिय समरपी बिस्व कल कीरति नई॥ क्यों करै बिनय बिदेहु कियो बिदेहु मूरति सावँरीं। करि होमु बिधिवत गाँठि जोरी होन लागीं भावँरीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1740.verse_hindi: जैसे हिमवान ने शिवजी को पार्वतीजी और सागर ने भगवान विष्णु को लक्ष्मीजी दी थीं, वैसे ही जनकजी ने श्री रामचन्द्रजी को सीताजी समर्पित कीं, जिससे विश्व में सुंदर नवीन कीर्ति छा गई। विदेह (जनकजी) कैसे विनती करें! उस साँवली मूर्ति ने तो उन्हें सचमुच विदेह (देह की सुध-बुध से रहित) ही कर दिया। विधिपूर्वक हवन करके गठजोड़ी की गई और भाँवरें होने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1740.english_translation: Just as Himavan gave Parvati to Shiva and the ocean gave Lakshmi to Vishnu, so Janak gave Sita to Ram, and a new glory spread through the world. How can Videha make an offering? That dark beauty had made him truly beyond the body. After the fire ritual, the sacred knot was tied and the wedding rounds began.
ramacharitamanas::1740.translation_literal: हिमवंत (Himavan) / जिमि (as) / गिरिजा (Parvati) / महेसहि (to Shiva) / हरिहि (to Hari/Vishnu) / श्री (Lakshmi) / सागर (ocean) / दई (gave) / तिमि (thus) / जनक (Janak) / रामहि (to Ram) / सिय (Sita) / समरपी (offered) / बिस्व (world) / कल (beautiful) / कीरति (glory) / नई (new) / क्यों (how) / करै (does/make) / बिनय (request) / बिदेहु (Videha/Janak) / कियो (made) / बिदेहु (beyond the body) / मूरति (form) / सावँरीं (dark-hued) / करि (having done) / होमु (fire offering) / बिधिवत (according to rule) / गाँठि (knot) / जोरी (joined) / होन (becoming) / लागीं (began) / भावँरीं (wedding rounds)
ramacharitamanas::1740.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1740.essence: Their union is shown as the world's ancient pattern returning in human form.
ramacharitamanas::1740.simple_meaning: Janak gives Sita to Ram just as sacred cosmic unions are given in the world of the divine. The marriage is performed with ritual fire, the knot is tied, and the wedding rounds begin.
ramacharitamanas::1740.simple_insight: Some unions feel larger than a family event. They seem to restore order to the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::1740.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the swayamvar has ended and the marriage is being sealed. Tulsidas lifts the scene into cosmic scale: Janak gives Sita to Ram as if repeating the ancient unions of Shiva-Parvati and Vishnu-Lakshmi. The ritual begins, and the wedding becomes world-making.
ramacharitamanas::1740.modern_relevance: A wedding hall goes quiet as the sacred knot is tied, and everyone feels it: this is not just two people starting a life. The room senses a larger order settling into place.
ramacharitamanas::1740.insight: It frames a marriage as a cosmic alignment, not a private transaction.

ramacharitamanas::1741.verse_sanskrit: जय धुनि बंदी बेद धुनि मंगल गान निसान। सुनि हरषहिं बरषहिं बिबुध सुरतरु सुमन सुजान ॥
ramacharitamanas::1741.verse_hindi: जय ध्वनि, वन्दी ध्वनि, वेद ध्वनि, मंगलगान और नगाड़ों की ध्वनि सुनकर चतुर देवगण हर्षित हो रहे हैं और कल्पवृक्ष के फूलों को बरसा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1741.english_translation: Hail cries, praise cries, Vedic chants, auspicious songs, and drumbeats rise. Hearing them, the wise radiant beings rejoice and shower celestial flowers.
ramacharitamanas::1741.translation_literal: जय धुनि (shouts of victory) / बंदी धुनि (praise cries) / बेद धुनि (Vedic chants) / मंगल गान (auspicious songs) / निसान (drums) / सुनि (hearing) / हरषहिं (they rejoice) / बरषहिं (they shower) / बिबुध (radiant beings) / सुरतरु (celestial tree) / सुमन (flowers) / सुजान (the wise)
ramacharitamanas::1741.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1741.essence: Joy in the marriage spills into heaven and earth alike.
ramacharitamanas::1741.simple_meaning: The wedding ceremony fills the air with victory cries, praise, sacred chants, songs, and drums. The radiant beings in the higher realm rejoice and shower flowers.
ramacharitamanas::1741.simple_insight: Joy becomes public here. The whole celebration seems to rise beyond the earth.
ramacharitamanas::1741.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, Ram and Sita have just been joined in marriage. As the ceremony reaches its peak, the hall erupts in cries, chants, songs, and drums, and even the radiant beings above respond with delight and flowers.
ramacharitamanas::1741.insight: It shifts attention from the private ritual to the shared joy it creates around it.

ramacharitamanas::1742.verse_sanskrit: कुअँरु कुअँरि कल भावँरि देहीं। नयन लाभु सब सादर लेहीं॥ जाइ न बरनि मनोहर जोरी। जो उपमा कछु कहौं सो थोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1742.verse_hindi: वर और कन्या सुंदर भाँवरें दे रहे हैं। सब लोग आदरपूर्वक (उन्हें देखकर) नेत्रों का परम लाभ ले रहे हैं। मनोहर जोड़ी का वर्णन नहीं हो सकता, जो कुछ उपमा कहूँ वही थोड़ी होगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1742.english_translation: The prince and princess are exchanging graceful rounds. Everyone watches with reverence and drinks in the sight. The beautiful pair cannot be described; any comparison would fall short.
ramacharitamanas::1742.translation_literal: कुअँरु (prince) / कुअँरि (princess) / कल (graceful) / भावँरि (rounds of marriage) / देहीं (give) / नयन (eyes) / लाभु (gain) / सब (all) / सादर (with reverence) / लेहीं (take) / जाइ (go) / न (not) / बरनि (describe) / मनोहर (beautiful) / जोरी (pair) / जो (which) / उपमा (comparison) / कछु (some) / कहौं (I say) / सो (that) / थोरी (insufficient)
ramacharitamanas::1742.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1742.essence: Perfect union can be seen, but never fully said.
ramacharitamanas::1742.simple_meaning: Ram and Sita are circling the sacred fire as bride and groom. Everyone watches with deep joy, but their beauty is beyond full description.
ramacharitamanas::1742.simple_insight: Some moments are so complete that words can only bow to them.
ramacharitamanas::1742.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, Ram and Sita begin the marriage rounds after the swayamvar. The celebration has turned into a vision of perfect union, and the poet pauses because even praise feels too small for what everyone is seeing.
ramacharitamanas::1742.modern_relevance: You stand at the back of a wedding hall, phone forgotten in your hand, watching two people move through a moment that feels larger than language. You do not need commentary; the beauty is enough.
ramacharitamanas::1742.insight: It shifts attention from explanation to reverent seeing, letting beauty be witnessed without being reduced.

ramacharitamanas::1743.verse_sanskrit: राम सीय सुंदर प्रतिछाहीं। जगमगात मनि खंभन माहीं मनहुँ मदन रति धरि बहु रूपा। देखत राम बिआहु अनूपा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1743.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी और श्री सीताजी की सुंदर परछाहीं मणियों के खम्भों में जगमगा रही हैं, मानो कामदेव और रति बहुत से रूप धारण करके श्री रामजी के अनुपम विवाह को देख रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1743.english_translation: The beautiful reflections of Ram and Sita shimmer in the jeweled pillars, as if Kama and Rati have taken many forms to witness Ram's incomparable wedding.
ramacharitamanas::1743.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सीय (Sita) / सुंदर (beautiful) / प्रतिछाहीं (reflections) / जगमगात (shimmering) / मनि (jewel) / खंभन (pillars) / माहीं (in) / मनहुँ (as if) / मदन (Kama) / रति (Rati) / धरि (taking) / बहु (many) / रूपा (forms) / देखत (seeing) / राम (Ram) / बिआहु (wedding) / अनूपा (incomparable)
ramacharitamanas::1743.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1743.essence: Beauty becomes so complete it seems to invite divine witnesses.
ramacharitamanas::1743.simple_meaning: Ram and Sita's reflections shine in the jewel pillars, and the scene is so beautiful it seems even Kama and Rati have come to watch.
ramacharitamanas::1743.simple_insight: Beauty can make the whole world feel attentive.
ramacharitamanas::1743.detailed_meaning: At Janak's wedding hall, Ram and Sita stand in the glittering setting of their marriage. Their reflections shine in the jeweled pillars so vividly that the poet imagines Kama and Rati themselves watching the scene.
ramacharitamanas::1743.modern_relevance: You catch your reflection in a glass lobby before a wedding, and for a second everything feels arranged around one perfect moment. Beauty can make even a room feel alive.
ramacharitamanas::1743.insight: It turns a wedding scene into a vision of overwhelming beauty, making the surroundings feel conscious of the moment.

ramacharitamanas::1744.verse_sanskrit: दरस लालसा सकुच न थोरी। प्रगटत दुरत बहोरि बहोरी॥ भए मगन सब देखनिहारे। जनक समान अपान बिसारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1744.verse_hindi: उन्हें (कामदेव और रति को) दर्शन की लालसा और संकोच दोनों ही कम नहीं हैं (अर्थात बहुत हैं), इसीलिए वे मानो बार-बार प्रकट होते और छिपते हैं। सब देखने वाले आनंदमग्न हो गए और जनकजी की भाँति सभी अपनी सुध भूल गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1744.english_translation: The longing to behold them and the shyness to reveal themselves were both strong, so they kept appearing and disappearing again and again. All the onlookers became absorbed, and like King Janaka, they forgot themselves.
ramacharitamanas::1744.translation_literal: दरस (seeing / sight) / लालसा (longing) / सकुच (shyness) / न (not) / थोरी (small, little) / प्रगटत (appearing) / दुरत (hiding, receding) / बहोरि बहोरी (again and again) / भए (became) / मगन (absorbed) / सब (all) / देखनिहारे (those who were watching) / जनक (Janaka) / समान (like) / अपान (themselves) / बिसारे (forgot)
ramacharitamanas::1744.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1744.simple_meaning: The crowd is so overwhelmed by Ram and Sita's beauty that they keep losing themselves in wonder, just like Janaka.
ramacharitamanas::1744.simple_insight: Beauty can be so complete that the watcher disappears into it.
ramacharitamanas::1744.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's court, Ram and Sita are circling in the swayamvar, and the whole assembly is stunned. Their beauty is so intense that people keep staring, then losing themselves, as if Janaka's own awareness has dissolved in awe.
ramacharitamanas::1744.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone walking onto the stage and forget your own script for a moment. Some moments are so full they erase self-consciousness.
ramacharitamanas::1744.insight: It shifts attention from managing your image to being fully present in wonder.

ramacharitamanas::1745.verse_sanskrit: प्रमुदित मुनिन्ह भावँरीं फेरीं। नेगसहित सब रीति निवेरीं॥ राम सीय सिर सेंदुर देहीं। सोभा कहि न जाति बिधि केहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1745.verse_hindi: मुनियों ने आनंदपूर्वक भाँवरें फिराईं और नेग सहित सब रीतियों को पूरा किया। श्री रामचन्द्रजी सीताजी के सिर में सिंदूर दे रहे हैं, यह शोभा किसी प्रकार भी कही नहीं जाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1745.english_translation: The sages joyfully completed the wedding rites and gifts. Ram places vermilion on Sita's head, and no one can describe the beauty of that sight.
ramacharitamanas::1745.translation_literal: प्रमुदित (joyful) / मुनिन्ह (by the sages) / भावँरीं (wedding circumambulations) / फेरीं (completed) / नेगसहित (with gifts and customary offerings) / सब रीति (all rites) / निवेरीं (were completed) / राम (Ram) / सीय (Sita) / सिर (head) / सेंदुर (vermilion) / देहीं (give/placing) / सोभा (beauty) / कहि (speak) / न जाति (cannot be) / बिधि (by Brahma / fate) / केहीं (by anyone)
ramacharitamanas::1745.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1745.essence: Marriage becomes sacred when beauty outgrows speech.
ramacharitamanas::1745.simple_meaning: The wedding rituals are completed, and Ram places vermilion on Sita's head. The scene is so beautiful that words fail.
ramacharitamanas::1745.simple_insight: Some moments are too full for language; they only ask for reverent witnessing.
ramacharitamanas::1745.detailed_meaning: At Janak's grand wedding, the sages finish the sacred rites with delight. Ram and Sita are now joined in the most auspicious moment of the ceremony, and the poet pauses because the beauty before him feels beyond speech.
ramacharitamanas::1745.modern_relevance: You watch two people you care about complete a ceremony that changes everything. Everyone is smiling, but what you really feel is the hush that comes when a life reaches a sacred turning point.
ramacharitamanas::1745.insight: It teaches you to recognize certain moments as beyond commentary and meet them with awe.

ramacharitamanas::1746.verse_sanskrit: अरुन पराग जलजु भरि नीकें। ससिहि भूष अहि लोभ अमी कें॥ बहुरि बसिष्ठ दीन्हि अनुसासन। बरु दुलहिनि बैठे एक आसन ॥
ramacharitamanas::1746.verse_hindi: मानो कमल को लाल पराग से अच्छी तरह भरकर अमृत के लोभ से साँप चन्द्रमा को भूषित कर रहा है। (यहाँ श्री राम के हाथ को कमल की, सेंदूर को पराग की, श्री राम की श्याम भुजा को साँप की और सीताजी के मुख को चन्द्रमा की उपमा दी गई है।) फिर वशिष्ठजी ने आज्ञा दी, तब दूल्हे और दुलहिन एक आसन पर बैठे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1746.english_translation: Like red pollen filling a lotus, and a serpent adorning the moon for the sake of nectar, Vashishtha then gave the order, and the bride and groom sat on one seat.
ramacharitamanas::1746.translation_literal: अरुन (red) / पराग (pollen) / जलजु (lotus) / भरि (filled) / नीकें (well) / ससिहि (the moon) / भूष (ornament) / अहि (serpent) / लोभ (greed/desire) / अमी कें (for nectar) / बहुरि (then again) / बसिष्ठ (Vashishtha) / दीन्हि (gave) / अनुसासन (instruction/order) / बरु (the bridegroom) / दुलहिनि (the bride) / बैठे (sat) / एक (one) / आसन (seat)
ramacharitamanas::1746.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1746.essence: Sacred union deserves both beauty and order.
ramacharitamanas::1746.simple_meaning: The verse uses poetic images to describe the beauty of the wedding, then says Vashishtha instructed Ram and Sita to sit together on one seat.
ramacharitamanas::1746.simple_insight: Some moments are too sacred for plain speech; poetry carries their weight.
ramacharitamanas::1746.detailed_meaning: At Sita's wedding in Mithila, the ceremony has reached its most tender point. Tulsidas lingers on ornate imagery, then shows Vashishtha giving the final instruction for Ram and Sita to sit together as bride and groom.
ramacharitamanas::1746.modern_relevance: You watch two people walk to the front of the hall, and the room goes quiet. The formality, the beauty, the pause before the vows — all of it matters because a life is being joined.
ramacharitamanas::1746.insight: It turns a ceremony into a moment of reverence, showing how ritual gives shape to love.

ramacharitamanas::1747.verse_sanskrit: बैठे बरासन रामु जानकि मुदित मन दसरथु भए। तनु पुलक पुनि पुनि देखि अपनें सुकृत सुरतरु पल नए॥ भरि भुवन रहा उछाहु राम बिबाहु भा सबहीं कहा। केहि भाँति बरनि सिरात रसना एक यहु मंगलु महा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1747.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी और जानकीजी श्रेष्ठ आसन पर बैठे, उन्हें देखकर दशरथजी मन में बहुत आनंदित हुए। अपने सुकृत रूपी कल्प वृक्ष में नए फल (आए) देखकर उनका शरीर बार-बार पुलकित हो रहा है। चौदहों भुवनों में उत्साह भर गया, सबने कहा कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी का विवाह हो गया। जीभ एक है और यह मंगल महान है, फिर भला, वह वर्णन करके किस प्रकार समाप्त किया जा सकता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1747.english_translation: Ram and Janaki sat on the royal seat. Dasharath was filled with joy, and his body thrilled again and again, seeing the new fruit of his merit tree. Joy filled the whole world as everyone said, “Sri Ramchandra has been married.” How can such a great blessing be described and ended with one tongue?
ramacharitamanas::1747.translation_literal: बैठे (sat) / बरासन (royal seat) / रामु (Ram) / जानकि (Janaki) / मुदित (joyful) / मन (mind) / दसरथु (Dasharath) / भए (became) / तनु (body) / पुलक (goosebumps) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / देखि (seeing) / अपनें (own) / सुकृत (merit) / सुरतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / पल (fruit) / नए (new) / भरि (filled) / भुवन (world) / रहा (remained) / उछाहु (joy) / राम बिबाहु (Ram’s marriage) / भा (happened) / सबहीं (everyone) / कहा (said) / केहि भाँति (in what way) / बरनि (describe) / सिरात (be ended) / रसना (tongue) / एक (one) / यहु (this) / मंगलु (auspiciousness) / महा (great)
ramacharitamanas::1747.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1747.essence: Joy can overflow beyond the reach of speech.
ramacharitamanas::1747.simple_meaning: Ram and Janaki are seated in marriage, Dasharath overflows with joy, and the whole world celebrates this great blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1747.simple_insight: Some moments are too full for words. Joy itself becomes the only honest response.
ramacharitamanas::1747.detailed_meaning: The wedding has been completed, and Ram and Janaki sit together on the royal seat. Dasharath, seeing the marriage of his son, trembles with delight. The whole world joins in celebration, and the poet admits that this blessing is too vast to finish describing.
ramacharitamanas::1747.modern_relevance: You watch your child step into a new life, and your chest tightens with pride you cannot explain. The room feels larger, brighter, almost sacred, and words suddenly seem too small.
ramacharitamanas::1747.insight: It shifts attention from narration to gratitude: some joys are meant to be witnessed, not contained.

ramacharitamanas::1748.verse_sanskrit: तब जनक पाइ बसिष्ठ आयसु ब्याह साज सँवारि कै। मांडवी श्रुतकीरति उरमिला कुअँरि लईं हँकारि कै॥ कुसकेतु कन्या प्रथम जो गुन सील सुख सोभामई। सब रीति प्रीति समेत करि सो ब्याहि नृप भरतहि दई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1748.verse_hindi: तब वशिष्ठजी की आज्ञा पाकर जनकजी ने विवाह का सामान सजाकर माण्डवीजी, श्रुतकीर्तिजी और उर्मिलाजी इन तीनों राजकुमारियों को बुला लिया। कुश ध्वज की बड़ी कन्या माण्डवीजी को, जो गुण, शील, सुख और शोभा की रूप ही थीं, राजा जनक ने प्रेमपूर्वक सब रीतियाँ करके भरतजी को ब्याह दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1748.english_translation: Then, having received Vashishtha's command, Janaka prepared the wedding arrangements and summoned Mandavi, Shrutakirti, and Urmila. He gave Mandavi, the eldest daughter of Kushadhvaja, who was full of virtue, conduct, joy, and beauty, to Bharat in marriage with full rites and affection.
ramacharitamanas::1748.translation_literal: तब (then) / जनक (Janaka) / पाइ (having received) / बसिष्ठ (Vashishtha) / आयसु (command) / ब्याह (wedding) / साज (arrangements) / सँवारि कै (having prepared) / मांडवी (Mandavi) / श्रुतकीरति (Shrutakirti) / उरमिला (Urmila) / कुअँरि (princesses) / लईं (brought) / हँकारि कै (having called) / कुसकेतु (of Kushadhvaja) / कन्या (daughter) / प्रथम (first/eldest) / जो (who) / गुन (virtue) / सील (conduct) / सुख (joy) / सोभामई (beautiful) / सब रीति (all rites) / प्रीति समेत (with affection) / करि (having done) / सो (that) / ब्याहि (married) / नृप (king) / भरतहि (to Bharat) / दई (gave)
ramacharitamanas::1748.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1748.essence: Sacred unions are completed through care, not haste.
ramacharitamanas::1748.simple_meaning: Janaka, following Vashishtha's instruction, arranges the wedding and gives Mandavi to Bharat with full ceremony and love.
ramacharitamanas::1748.simple_insight: A right marriage is not rushed or casual; it is honored with care, consent, and dignity.
ramacharitamanas::1748.detailed_meaning: The wedding at Mithila is moving from one match to the next. After Ram and Sita, Vashishtha directs Janaka to complete the remaining alliances. Janaka prepares everything properly and gives Mandavi to Bharat, keeping the whole royal family joined in harmony.
ramacharitamanas::1748.modern_relevance: A family meeting turns into a careful planning session, and every detail matters because two lives are being joined. The verse carries the quiet dignity of doing something sacred with full attention.
ramacharitamanas::1748.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to proper conduct, showing that important bonds deserve complete care.

ramacharitamanas::1749.verse_sanskrit: जानकी लघु भगिनी सकल सुंदरि सिरोमनि जानि कै। सो तनय दीन्ही ब्याहि लखनहि सकल बिधि सनमानि कै॥ जेहि नामु श्रुतकीरति सुलोचनि सुमुखि सब गुन आगरी। सो दई रिपुसूदनहि भूपति रूप सील उजागरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1749.verse_hindi: जानकीजी की छोटी बहिन उर्मिलाजी को सब सुंदरियों में शिरोमणि जानकर उस कन्या को सब प्रकार से सम्मान करके, लक्ष्मणजी को ब्याह दिया और जिनका नाम श्रुतकीर्ति है और जो सुंदर नेत्रों वाली, सुंदर मुखवाली, सब गुणों की खान और रूप तथा शील में उजागर हैं, उनको राजा ने शत्रुघ्न को ब्याह दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1749.english_translation: Knowing Janaki's younger sister Urmila as the foremost of all beautiful women, Janak honored the marriage in every way and gave her to Lakshman. He then gave Shrutakirti, lovely-eyed, sweet-faced, full of virtues, radiant in beauty and character, to Shatrughna.
ramacharitamanas::1749.translation_literal: जानकी (Janaki) / लघु (younger) / भगिनी (sister) / सकल (all) / सुंदरि (beautiful women) / सिरोमनि (crest-jewel) / जानि कै (having known) / सो (that) / तनय (daughter) / दीन्ही (gave) / ब्याहि (in marriage) / लखनहि (to Lakshman) / सकल बिधि (in every way) / सनमानि कै (having honored) / जेहि (whose) / नामु (name) / श्रुतकीरति (Shrutakirti) / सुलोचनि (lovely-eyed) / सुमुखि (sweet-faced) / सब (all) / गुन (virtues) / आगरी (mine/treasure) / सो (that) / दई (gave) / रिपुसूदनहि (to Shatrughna) / भूपति (the king) / रूप (beauty) / सील (character) / उजागरी (radiant)
ramacharitamanas::1749.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1749.essence: Marriage becomes complete when each match is honored with equal care.
ramacharitamanas::1749.simple_meaning: Janak gives the two younger princesses in marriage with full honor: Urmila to Lakshman and Shrutakirti to Shatrughna.
ramacharitamanas::1749.simple_insight: Right union is shown through respect, not display.
ramacharitamanas::1749.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, after Ram and Sita are joined, King Janak completes the wedding by arranging the remaining two marriages with care and honor. Urmila is matched with Lakshman, and Shrutakirti with Shatrughna. The verse keeps the scene moving toward harmony.
ramacharitamanas::1749.modern_relevance: A family wedding where every detail is handled with dignity, not hurry, feels like this. The care given to each person says as much as the ceremony itself.
ramacharitamanas::1749.insight: It shifts attention from the main event to the equal dignity given to every relationship in the family.

ramacharitamanas::1750.verse_sanskrit: अनुरूप बर दुलहिनि परस्पर लखि सकुच हियँ हरषहीं। सब मुदित सुंदरता सराहहिं सुमन सुर गन बरषहीं॥ सुंदरीं सुंदर बरन्ह सह सब एक मंडप राजहीं। जनु जीव उर चारिउ अवस्था बिभुन सहित बिराजहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1750.verse_hindi: दूल्हे और दुलहिनें परस्पर अपने-अपने अनुरूप जोड़ी को देखकर सकुचाते हुए हृदय में हर्षित हो रही हैं। सब लोग प्रसन्न होकर उनकी सुंदरता की सराहना करते हैं और देवगण फूल बरसा रहे हैं। सब सुंदरी दुलहिनें सुंदर दूल्हों के साथ एक ही मंडप में ऐसी शोभा पा रही हैं, मानो जीव के हृदय में चारों अवस्थाएँ (जाग्रत, स्वप्न, सुषुप्ति और तुरीय) अपने चारों स्वामियों (विश्व, तैजस, प्राज्ञ और ब्रह्म) सहित विराजमान हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1750.english_translation: The brides and grooms, suited to one another, shyly rejoice in their hearts. Everyone is delighted, praising their beauty, and the gods shower flowers. The lovely brides and handsome grooms stand together in one pavilion, like the four states of consciousness with their lords enthroned in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1750.translation_literal: अनुरूप (suited, fitting) / बर (grooms) / दुलहिनि (brides) / परस्पर (one another) / लखि (seeing) / सकुच (shy, modest) / हियँ (in the heart) / हरषहीं (rejoice) / सब (all) / मुदित (happy) / सुंदरता (beauty) / सराहहिं (praise) / सुमन (flowers) / सुर गन (groups of gods) / बरषहीं (shower) / सुंदरीं (beautiful women) / सुंदर (beautiful) / बरन्ह (grooms) / सह (with) / सब (all) / एक (one) / मंडप (pavilion) / राजहीं (shine, are resplendent) / जनु (as if) / जीव (the individual being) / उर (in the heart) / चारिउ (four) / अवस्था (states) / बिभुन (with their lords) / सहित (together with) / बिराजहीं (reign, are seated)
ramacharitamanas::1750.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1750.essence: Perfect pairing makes the whole scene feel like inner harmony made visible.
ramacharitamanas::1750.simple_meaning: The wedding pavilion is full of matched couples, quiet joy, praise, and celebration. The poet compares that harmony to the four states of consciousness shining together in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1750.simple_insight: Beauty feels complete when everything belongs in its proper place.
ramacharitamanas::1750.detailed_meaning: At Janak's grand wedding, the brides and grooms stand together in perfect pairings while the whole assembly rejoices. Flowers fall from above. Tulsidas turns the scene into a spiritual image, comparing the harmony of the pavilion to the ordered states within the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1750.modern_relevance: At a wedding where everyone keeps pausing to look at the couples, the room itself feels arranged by grace. The verse notices that rare moment when outer harmony and inner delight seem to mirror each other.
ramacharitamanas::1750.insight: It turns a wedding scene into a vision of inner order and completeness.

ramacharitamanas::1751.verse_sanskrit: मुदित अवधपति सकल सुत बधुन्ह समेत निहारि। जनु पाए महिपाल मनि क्रियन्ह सहित फल चारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1751.verse_hindi: सब पुत्रों को बहुओं सहित देखकर अवध नरेश दशरथजी ऐसे आनंदित हैं, मानो वे राजाओं के शिरोमणि क्रियाओं (यज्ञक्रिया, श्रद्धाक्रिया, योगक्रिया और ज्ञानक्रिया) सहित चारों फल (अर्थ, धर्म, काम और मोक्ष) पा गए हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1751.english_translation: Seeing all his sons and daughters-in-law together, the king of Ayodhya was delighted, as if a ruler of kings had obtained the four aims of life along with the four kinds of sacred acts.
ramacharitamanas::1751.translation_literal: मुदित (delighted) / अवधपति (king of Ayodhya) / सकल (all) / सुत (sons) / बधुन्ह (daughters-in-law) / समेत (together with) / निहारि (seeing) / जनु (as if) / पाए (obtained) / महिपाल (ruler of kings) / मनि (jewel) / क्रियन्ह (with rites/acts) / सहित (together with) / फल (fruits) / चारि (four)
ramacharitamanas::1751.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1751.essence: True fulfillment can look like everyone you love gathered in one place.
ramacharitamanas::1751.simple_meaning: Dasharath feels deep joy seeing all his sons and daughters-in-law together. It feels to him like a king has gained the four aims of life and the four sacred acts.
ramacharitamanas::1751.simple_insight: Family harmony can feel like life’s highest success.
ramacharitamanas::1751.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath looks at all four sons with their brides after the weddings. The joy is not just fatherly; it feels complete, as if every blessing a ruler could hope for has arrived at once.
ramacharitamanas::1751.modern_relevance: You stand at the wedding reception watching both families laugh across one long table. For one quiet minute, the years of worry, planning, and longing feel worth it.
ramacharitamanas::1751.insight: It turns achievement into gratitude, showing that wholeness can be felt in family togetherness.

ramacharitamanas::1752.verse_sanskrit: जसि रघुबीर ब्याह बिधि बरनी। सकल कुअँर ब्याहे तेहिं करनी॥ कहि न जा कछु दाइज भूरी। रहा कनक मनि मंडपु पूरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1752.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विवाह की जैसी विधि वर्णन की गई, उसी रीति से सब राजकुमार विवाहे गए। दहेज की अधिकता कुछ कही नहीं जाती, सारा मंडप सोने और मणियों से भर गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1752.english_translation: The wedding of Ram was arranged in that same manner, and all the princes were married likewise. The gifts were beyond counting; the marriage pavilion was filled with gold and jewels.
ramacharitamanas::1752.translation_literal: जसि (as) / रघुबीर (Ram, hero of the Raghu clan) / ब्याह (marriage) / बिधि (method, manner) / बरनी (described) / सकल (all) / कुअँर (princes) / ब्याहे (were married) / तेहिं (that) / करनी (manner, way) / कहि (said) / न (not) / जा (can be) / कछु (anything) / दाइज (dowry, gifts) / भूरी (great, abundant) / रहा (remained) / कनक (gold) / मनि (jewels) / मंडपु (marriage pavilion) / पूरी (filled)
ramacharitamanas::1752.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1752.essence: Blessing becomes visible when joy fills every detail.
ramacharitamanas::1752.simple_meaning: The princes were all married in the same grand way as Ram, with an enormous amount of gifts and a pavilion full of gold and jewels.
ramacharitamanas::1752.simple_insight: Some moments are too abundant to measure. Joy, honor, and blessing overflow beyond ordinary counting.
ramacharitamanas::1752.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, after Ram’s marriage is described, the celebration spreads to the other princes as well. The scene lingers on the lavish gifts and the gold-filled pavilion, showing a wedding that feels like a royal blessing made visible.
ramacharitamanas::1752.modern_relevance: A wedding hall glows under chandeliers, gifts stacked to the ceiling, relatives smiling through tears. The event feels bigger than expense — it feels like shared joy made tangible.
ramacharitamanas::1752.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony as cost to ceremony as overflowing blessing.

ramacharitamanas::1753.verse_sanskrit: कंबल बसन बिचित्र पटोरे। भाँति भाँति बहु मोल न थोरे॥ गज रथ तुरगदास अरु दासी। धेनु अलंकृत कामदुहा सी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1753.verse_hindi: बहुत से कम्बल, वस्त्र और भाँति-भाँति के विचित्र रेशमी कपड़े, जो थोड़ी कीमत के न थे (अर्थात बहुमूल्य थे) तथा हाथी, रथ, घोड़े, दास-दासियाँ और गहनों से सजी हुई कामधेनु सरीखी गायें- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1753.english_translation: Blankets, garments, and many kinds of rich silk cloths; elephants, chariots, horses, servants, maidservants, and a cow adorned like wish-fulfilling Kamadhenu.
ramacharitamanas::1753.translation_literal: कंबल (blankets) / बसन (clothes) / बिचित्र (varied, beautiful) / पटोरे (silk cloths) / भाँति भाँति (of many kinds) / बहु (many) / मोल (price, value) / न थोरे (not small) / गज (elephants) / रथ (chariots) / तुरग (horses) / दास (servants) / अरु (and) / दासी (maidservants) / धेनु (cow) / अलंकृत (adorned) / कामदुहा (wish-fulfilling, like Kamadhenu) / सी (like)
ramacharitamanas::1753.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1753.essence: Abundance becomes visible through the list itself.
ramacharitamanas::1753.simple_meaning: The wedding gifts were lavish: fine cloth, animals, servants, and richly adorned cows. The list is part of a scene showing overwhelming abundance.
ramacharitamanas::1753.simple_insight: Sometimes generosity is so large it can only be shown by overflowing detail.
ramacharitamanas::1753.detailed_meaning: After the grand weddings in Ayodhya, the narrator begins listing the gifts and treasures given in celebration. This verse is not the main teaching; it is part of the overflowing display of royal abundance that surrounds Ram's marriage.
ramacharitamanas::1753.modern_relevance: A wedding hall filled with stacked gift boxes, silk bags, and flower-covered trays tells its own story before anyone speaks. Some moments are so full that listing the details becomes the point.
ramacharitamanas::1753.insight: It shifts attention from the single object to the sheer scale of giving.

ramacharitamanas::1754.verse_sanskrit: बस्तु अनेक करिअ किमि लेखा। कहि न जाइ जानहिं जिन्ह देखा॥ लोकपाल अवलोकि सिहाने। लीन्ह अवधपति सबु सुखु माने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1754.verse_hindi: (आदि) अनेकों वस्तुएँ हैं, जिनकी गिनती कैसे की जाए। उनका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता, जिन्होंने देखा है, वही जानते हैं। उन्हें देखकर लोकपाल भी सिहा गए। अवधराज दशरथजी ने सुख मानकर प्रसन्नचित्त से सब कुछ ग्रहण किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1754.english_translation: Countless gifts cannot be numbered or fully described. Even the guardians of the worlds were astonished, and King Dasharatha accepted everything with delight.
ramacharitamanas::1754.translation_literal: बस्तु अनेक (many things) / करिअ (to be done) / किमि (how) / लेखा (count, reckoning) / कहि न जाइ (cannot be spoken) / जानहिं (know) / जिन्ह (those who) / देखा (saw) / लोकपाल (guardians of the worlds) / अवलोकि (seeing) / सिहाने (were astonished) / लीन्ह (took) / अवधपति (lord of Ayodhya, Dasharatha) / सबु (all) / सुखु माने (with delight, as joy)
ramacharitamanas::1754.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1754.simple_meaning: The wedding gifts were so many they could not be counted or fully described. Even the guardians of the worlds were amazed, and Dasharatha gladly accepted everything.
ramacharitamanas::1754.simple_insight: Some moments overflow measure. When joy is complete, even abundance feels natural.
ramacharitamanas::1754.detailed_meaning: At Sita and Ram’s wedding in Mithila, the gifts are piled beyond counting. The scene is so overflowing that even the guardians of the worlds are stunned. Dasharatha receives it all happily, as the celebration reaches its peak.
ramacharitamanas::1754.modern_relevance: You open the wedding hall door and see gifts stacked to the ceiling, relatives buzzing, and nothing left to explain. Some joy is too full for accounting.
ramacharitamanas::1754.insight: It shifts attention from tallying possessions to recognizing the fullness of a blessed moment.

ramacharitamanas::1755.verse_sanskrit: दीन्ह जाचकन्हि जो जेहि भावा। उबरा सो जनवासेहिं आवा॥ तब कर जोरि जनकु मृदु बानी। बोले सब बरात सनमानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1755.verse_hindi: उन्होंने वह दहेज का सामान याचकों को, जो जिसे अच्छा लगा, दे दिया। जो बच रहा, वह जनवासे में चला आया। तब जनकजी हाथ जोड़कर सारी बारात का सम्मान करते हुए कोमल वाणी से बोले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1755.english_translation: They gave away whatever each beggar desired, and what remained went to the bridal lodging. Then Janak folded his hands and, honoring the whole wedding party, spoke gently.
ramacharitamanas::1755.translation_literal: दीन्ह (gave) / जाचकन्हि (to the beggars) / जो (whatever) / जेहि (whichever) / भावा (pleased) / उबरा (what remained) / सो (that) / जनवासेहिं (to the bridal lodging) / आवा (came) / तब (then) / कर जोरि (with folded hands) / जनकु (Janak) / मृदु बानी (soft words) / बोले (spoke) / सब (all) / बरात (the wedding party) / सनमानी (honoring)
ramacharitamanas::1755.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1755.essence: Generosity and courtesy turn abundance into grace.
ramacharitamanas::1755.simple_meaning: Janak gives away the wedding gifts freely, then welcomes the whole wedding party with respectful, gentle words.
ramacharitamanas::1755.simple_insight: True generosity leaves no need to guard what remains.
ramacharitamanas::1755.detailed_meaning: At Sita's wedding in Mithila, Janak has already displayed great wealth. Now he gives gifts to beggars, sends the rest to the bridal lodging, and turns to honor Ram's wedding party with humility. The moment shows royal abundance joined to grace.
ramacharitamanas::1755.modern_relevance: After a big family celebration, you notice the leftovers, the gifts, the extra plates, the last details. Someone still makes sure every guest leaves feeling honored. That quiet dignity is the point here.
ramacharitamanas::1755.insight: It shifts attention from possession to hospitality, showing that wealth becomes meaningful only when shared and offered with respect.

ramacharitamanas::1756.verse_sanskrit: सनमानि सकल बरात आदर दान बिनय बड़ाइ कै। प्रमुदित महामुनि बृंद बंदे पूजि प्रेम लड़ाइ कै॥ सिरु नाइ देव मनाइ सब सन कहत कर संपुट किएँ। सुर साधु चाहत भाउ सिंधु कि तोष जल अंजलि दिएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1756.verse_hindi: आदर, दान, विनय और बड़ाई के द्वारा सारी बारात का सम्मान कर राजा जनक ने महान आनंद के साथ प्रेमपूर्वक लड़ाकर (लाड़ करके) मुनियों के समूह की पूजा एवं वंदना की। सिर नवाकर, देवताओं को मनाकर, राजा हाथ जोड़कर सबसे कहने लगे कि देवता और साधु तो भाव ही चाहते हैं, (वे प्रेम से ही प्रसन्न हो जाते हैं, उन पूर्णकाम महानुभावों को कोई कुछ देकर कैसे संतुष्ट कर सकता है), क्या एक अंजलि जल देने से कहीं समुद्र संतुष्ट हो सकता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1756.english_translation: King Janaka honored the entire wedding party with respect, gifts, humility, and praise. The delighted sages were bowed to and worshiped with loving affection. Bowing his head, pleasing the devas, and joining his palms, he said to all that devas and saints desire only devotion; how could a handful of water satisfy the ocean?
ramacharitamanas::1756.translation_literal: सनमानि (honoring) / सकल (all) / बरात (wedding party) / आदर (respect) / दान (gift-giving) / बिनय (humility) / बड़ाइ (praise) / कै (with) / प्रमुदित (delighted) / महामुनि बृंद (group of great sages) / बंदे (bowed to) / पूजि (worshiped) / प्रेम (love) / लड़ाइ कै (with affection) / सिरु नाइ (bowing the head) / देव (devas) / मनाइ (pleasing) / सब सन (to all) / कहत (saying) / कर संपुट किएँ (with joined palms) / सुर (devas) / साधु (saints) / चाहत (desire) / भाउ (devotion) / सिंधु (ocean) / कि (how) / तोष (satisfaction) / जल अंजलि (handful of water) / दिएँ (by giving)
ramacharitamanas::1756.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1756.essence: Devotion, not display, reaches what offerings cannot.
ramacharitamanas::1756.simple_meaning: Janaka honors the whole wedding party and says that saints and radiant beings want loving devotion, not material offerings.
ramacharitamanas::1756.simple_insight: Relief comes from knowing that sincerity matters more than display.
ramacharitamanas::1756.detailed_meaning: At Janaka’s palace, the wedding celebration is in full flow. He greets Ram’s party with gifts, respect, and warmth, then bows before the sages and speaks from humble understanding: the highest beings are pleased by devotion, not by things.
ramacharitamanas::1756.modern_relevance: You bring expensive flowers to a teacher’s farewell, but what they remember is your honest gratitude and steady care. Janaka’s insight cuts through performance: heartfelt reverence matters more than impressive giving.
ramacharitamanas::1756.insight: It shifts attention from external generosity to the quality of feeling behind it.

ramacharitamanas::1757.verse_sanskrit: कर जोरि जनकु बहोरि बंधु समेत कोसलराय सों। बोले मनोहर बयन सानि सनेह सील सुभाय सों॥ संबंध राजन रावरें हम बड़े अब सब बिधि भए। एहि राज साज समेत सेवक जानिबे बिनु गथ लए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1757.verse_hindi: फिर जनकजी भाई सहित हाथ जोड़कर कोसलाधीश दशरथजी से स्नेह, शील और सुंदर प्रेम में सानकर मनोहर वचन बोले- हे राजन् ! आपके साथ संबंध हो जाने से अब हम सब प्रकार से बड़े हो गए। इस राज-पाट सहित हम दोनों को आप बिना दाम के लिए हुए सेवक ही समझिएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1757.english_translation: Then Janak, with his brothers, joined his hands and spoke charming words to the king of Kosala, sweetened by affection, gentleness, and grace: “Our relation with you has made us great in every way. Regard us, along with this royal wealth, as your servants taken without payment.”
ramacharitamanas::1757.translation_literal: कर जोरि (joining hands) / जनकु (Janak) / बहोरि (again) / बंधु समेत (together with brothers) / कोसलराय सों (to the king of Kosala) / बोले (spoke) / मनोहर बयन (charming words) / सानि (smeared / blended) / सनेह (affection) / सील (gentleness / good conduct) / सुभाय सों (with noble nature) / संबंध (relation) / राजन (O king) / रावरें (with you / your) / हम (we) / बड़े (great) / अब (now) / सब बिधि (in every way) / भए (have become) / एहि (this) / राज साज (royal wealth and splendour) / समेत (along with) / सेवक (servants) / जानिबे (to be regarded) / बिनु (without) / गथ लए (payment taken)
ramacharitamanas::1757.speaker: Janak
ramacharitamanas::1757.essence: True dignity bows and calls itself a servant.
ramacharitamanas::1757.simple_meaning: Janak greets Dasharath with humility and says their new bond has made them greater, not lesser. He asks to be treated as servants, not as owners of the royal gifts.
ramacharitamanas::1757.simple_insight: Real greatness can sound like humility. The heart that bows freely is already above pride.
ramacharitamanas::1757.detailed_meaning: After the wedding gifts are distributed, Janak stands with his brothers before Dasharath in Janakpur. Instead of boasting about his power or wealth, he bows and calls the new family bond a blessing. This verse shows the tenderness and humility sealing the alliance.
ramacharitamanas::1757.modern_relevance: At a wedding, one family tries to outdo the other with status and expense. Janak does the opposite: he lowers himself, honors the bond, and makes generosity feel sacred instead of transactional.
ramacharitamanas::1757.insight: It teaches you to meet honor with humility, and to treat relationship as a gift rather than a bargain.

ramacharitamanas::1758.verse_sanskrit: ए दारिका परिचारिका करि पालिबीं करुना नई। अपराधु छमिबो बोलि पठए बहुत हौं ढीट्यो कई॥ पुनि भानुकुलभूषन सकल सनमान निधि समधी किए। कहि जाति नहिं बिनती परस्पर प्रेम परिपूरन हिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1758.verse_hindi: इन लड़कियों को टहलनी मानकर, नई-नई दया करके पालन कीजिएगा। मैंने बड़ी ढिठाई की कि आपको यहाँ बुला भेजा, अपराध क्षमा कीजिएगा। फिर सूर्यकुल के भूषण दशरथजी ने समधी जनकजी को सम्पूर्ण सम्मान का निधि कर दिया (इतना सम्मान किया कि वे सम्मान के भंडार ही हो गए)। उनकी परस्पर की विनय कही नहीं जाती, दोनों के हृदय प्रेम से परिपूर्ण हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1758.english_translation: Please treat these girls as attendants and raise them with fresh compassion. Forgive my boldness in having sent for you. Then the jewel of the solar line, Dasharatha, made King Janaka a treasury of honor. Their mutual humility cannot be described; both hearts were filled with love.
ramacharitamanas::1758.translation_literal: ए (these) / दारिका (girls) / परिचारिका (attendants) / करि (having made) / पालिबीं (you will raise) / करुना (compassion) / नई (new) / अपराधु (offense) / छमिबो (forgive) / बोलि (speaking) / पठए (sent) / बहुत (much) / हौं (I) / ढीट्यो (bold) / कई (done) / पुनि (then) / भानुकुलभूषन (ornament of the solar line) / सकल (all) / सनमान (honor) / निधि (treasury) / समधी (father-in-law) / किए (made) / कहि (saying) / जाति (goes) / नहिं (not) / बिनती (humble request) / परस्पर (mutual) / प्रेम (love) / परिपूरन (full) / हिए (hearts)
ramacharitamanas::1758.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1758.simple_meaning: Janaka humbly asks Dasharatha to care for the girls with kindness and forgive his boldness. Dasharatha responds with such honor that both families overflow with mutual love.
ramacharitamanas::1758.simple_insight: Real respect makes family larger, softer, and more loving.
ramacharitamanas::1758.detailed_meaning: At Janaka’s court in Mithila, the formal wedding exchange turns tender. Janaka speaks with humility to Dasharatha, asking that the girls be cared for gently. Dasharatha answers with such honor that the two houses meet in love, not ceremony.
ramacharitamanas::1758.modern_relevance: At a wedding dinner, two families keep apologizing for small inconveniences and thanking each other for everything. The real gift is not the event itself — it is the tenderness that makes strangers feel like kin.
ramacharitamanas::1758.insight: It shifts attention from social formality to the quality of humility that creates genuine closeness.

ramacharitamanas::1759.verse_sanskrit: बृंदारका गन सुमन बरिसहिं राउ जनवासेहि चले। दुंदुभी जय धुनि बेद धुनि नभ नगर कौतूहल भले॥ तब सखीं मंगल गान करत मुनीस आयसु पाइ कै। दूल्हे दुलहिनिन्ह सहित सुंदरि चलीं कोहबर ल्याइ कै ॥
ramacharitamanas::1759.verse_hindi: देवतागण फूल बरसा रहे हैं, राजा जनवासे को चले। नगाड़े की ध्वनि, जयध्वनि और वेद की ध्वनि हो रही है, आकाश और नगर दोनों में खूब कौतूहल हो रहा है (आनंद छा रहा है), तब मुनीश्वर की आज्ञा पाकर सुंदरी सखियाँ मंगलगान करती हुई दुलहिनों सहित दूल्हों को लिवाकर कोहबर को चलीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1759.english_translation: The divine beings shower flowers. The king goes to the wedding pavilion. Drumbeats, victory cries, and Vedic chants fill the sky and the city with joy. Then, after receiving the sage's command, the beautiful bridesmaids sing auspicious songs and lead the brides and grooms to the wedding chamber.
ramacharitamanas::1759.translation_literal: बृंदारका गन (hosts of the divine beings) / सुमन (flowers) / बरिसहिं (shower) / राउ (the king) / जनवासेहि (to the wedding pavilion) / चले (went) / दुंदुभी (drums) / जय धुनि (victory cry) / बेद धुनि (Vedic chant) / नभ (sky) / नगर (city) / कौतूहल (joyful excitement) / भले (well, greatly) / तब (then) / सखीं (bridesmaids) / मंगल गान (auspicious songs) / करत (singing) / मुनीस (sage) / आयसु (command) / पाइ कै (having received) / दूल्हे (grooms) / दुलहिनिन्ह (brides) / सहित (together with) / सुंदरि (beautiful) / चलीं (went) / कोहबर (wedding chamber) / ल्याइ कै (bringing, leading)
ramacharitamanas::1759.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1759.essence: Joy spills outward when a holy union begins.
ramacharitamanas::1759.simple_meaning: The wedding procession moves forward in celebration. Flowers fall from above, drums and chants fill the air, and the bridesmaids lead the couples toward the wedding chamber.
ramacharitamanas::1759.simple_insight: A sacred moment can fill an entire city with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1759.detailed_meaning: Janak's court is alive with celebration as Ram and Sita's wedding procession moves toward the pavilion. The divine beings shower flowers, the city rings with drums and Vedic chants, and the bridesmaids lead the couples onward. This is a scene of public joy before the private meeting in the wedding chamber.
ramacharitamanas::1759.modern_relevance: You arrive at a wedding hall before the ceremony, and every corridor hums with music, perfume, and anticipation. Even strangers smile. Some moments make an entire place feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1759.insight: It shifts attention from the couple alone to the shared joy that surrounds a sacred union.

ramacharitamanas::1760.verse_sanskrit: पुनि पुनि रामहि चितव सिय सकुचति मनु सकुचै न। हरत मनोहर मीन छबि प्रेम पिआसे नैन ॥
ramacharitamanas::1760.verse_hindi: सीताजी बार-बार रामजी को देखती हैं और सकुचा जाती हैं, पर उनका मन नहीं सकुचाता। प्रेम के प्यासे उनके नेत्र सुंदर मछलियों की छबि को हर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1760.english_translation: Sita looks at Ram again and again and grows shy; her mind does not grow shy. Her eyes, thirsty for love, keep drinking in his beautiful fish-like eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1760.translation_literal: पुनि पुनि (again and again) / रामहि (Ram) / चितव (looks at) / सिय (Sita) / सकुचति (grows shy) / मनु (mind) / सकुचै न (does not grow shy) / हरत (stealing/captivating) / मनोहर (beautiful) / मीन (fish) / छबि (beauty/form) / प्रेम (love) / पिआसे (thirsty) / नैन (eyes)
ramacharitamanas::1760.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1760.essence: Shyness can hide a heart already surrendered.
ramacharitamanas::1760.simple_meaning: Sita keeps looking at Ram and feels shy, but her mind is fully drawn to him. Her eyes cannot stop drinking in his beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1760.simple_insight: Love can make the body hesitate while the heart stays completely open.
ramacharitamanas::1760.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, after the marriage arrangements, Sita sees Ram again and again. Her outward shyness remains, but her inward pull is unmistakable. This couplet captures the first blush of devoted love before the fuller praise of Ram's beauty that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1760.modern_relevance: You catch yourself glancing at someone across a crowded room, then looking away too quickly. The face goes shy; the attention does not. That split is human.
ramacharitamanas::1760.insight: It shows how devotion can be hidden in restraint: outward modesty, inward absorption.

ramacharitamanas::1761.verse_sanskrit: स्याम सरीरु सुभायँ सुहावन। सोभा कोटि मनोज लजावन॥ जावक जुत पद कमल सुहाए। मुनि मन मधुप रहत जिन्ह छाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1761.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का साँवला शरीर स्वभाव से ही सुंदर है। उसकी शोभा करोड़ों कामदेवों को लजाने वाली है। महावर से युक्त चरण कमल बड़े सुहावने लगते हैं, जिन पर मुनियों के मन रूपी भौंरे सदा छाए रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1761.english_translation: Ram's dark body is naturally beautiful. Its splendor shames millions of Cupids. His lovely lotus feet, adorned with red dye, are where the minds of sages stay like bees.
ramacharitamanas::1761.translation_literal: स्याम (dark) / सरीरु (body) / सुभायँ (by nature) / सुहावन (beautiful) / सोभा (splendor) / कोटि (crores/millions) / मनोज (Cupid) / लजावन (shaming) / जावक (red dye / lacquer) / जुत (joined with) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / सुहाए (beautiful) / मुनि (sage) / मन (mind) / मधुप (bee) / रहत (remain) / जिन्ह (on whom) / छाए (hovering)
ramacharitamanas::1761.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1761.essence: Ram's beauty silences every lesser charm and holds the heart still.
ramacharitamanas::1761.simple_meaning: Ram's dark form is naturally beautiful, and even the most enchanting beauty seems small beside it. His feet draw the minds of sages the way bees gather around flowers.
ramacharitamanas::1761.simple_insight: True beauty doesn't shout. It quietly holds the mind and makes everything else feel lesser.
ramacharitamanas::1761.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, Sita has just seen Ram for the first time. Tulsidas pauses the marriage scene to dwell on Ram's form: dark, radiant, and irresistibly beautiful. The verse turns outward admiration into devotion, showing how sages cling to his feet.
ramacharitamanas::1761.modern_relevance: You scroll past polished faces, curated profiles, and perfect lighting, then meet someone whose calm presence stops you cold. Real beauty doesn't need performance; it quietly commands attention.
ramacharitamanas::1761.insight: It shifts attention from surface glamour to the kind of beauty that naturally draws devotion.

ramacharitamanas::1762.verse_sanskrit: पीत पुनीत मनोहर धोती। हरति बाल रबि दामिनि जोती॥ कल किंकिनि कटि सूत्र मनोहर। बाहु बिसाल बिभूषन सुंदर ॥
ramacharitamanas::1762.verse_hindi: पवित्र और मनोहर पीली धोती प्रातःकाल के सूर्य और बिजली की ज्योति को हरे लेती है। कमर में सुंदर किंकिणी और कटिसूत्र हैं। विशाल भुजाओं में सुंदर आभूषण सुशोभित हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1762.english_translation: The pure yellow cloth is beautiful and radiant, outshining the morning sun and lightning. Lovely bells and a waist cord adorn the waist. Beautiful ornaments shine on the broad arms.
ramacharitamanas::1762.translation_literal: पीत (yellow) / पुनीत (pure) / मनोहर (beautiful) / धोती (cloth) / हरति (takes away) / बाल (morning) / रबि (sun) / दामिनि (lightning) / जोती (light) / कल (lovely) / किंकिनि (small bells) / कटि-सूत्र (waist cord) / मनोहर (beautiful) / बाहु (arms) / बिसाल (broad) / बिभूषन (ornaments) / सुंदर (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::1762.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1762.essence: Radiant adornment turns a moment into a sacred event.
ramacharitamanas::1762.simple_meaning: Ram's wedding attire is described in vivid detail: a bright yellow cloth, ornaments, bells, and a beautiful waist cord all add to his splendor.
ramacharitamanas::1762.simple_insight: Beauty here is not decoration alone; it reveals the joy and dignity of the moment.
ramacharitamanas::1762.detailed_meaning: The swayamvar scene is unfolding, and attention shifts from Sita's shy glance to Ram's wedding adornments. Tulsidas lingers on the yellow cloth, ornaments, and bright details to build the sacred mood before the marriage.
ramacharitamanas::1762.modern_relevance: You see someone dressed for a once-in-a-lifetime ceremony, and every detail feels charged. The clothes are not just clothing anymore; they carry the weight of the moment.
ramacharitamanas::1762.insight: It trains the eye to notice how outer form can express inner significance.

ramacharitamanas::1763.verse_sanskrit: पीत जनेउ महाछबि देई। कर मुद्रिका चोरि चितु लेई॥ सोहत ब्याह साज सब साजे। उर आयत उरभूषन राजे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1763.verse_hindi: पीला जनेऊ महान शोभा दे रहा है। हाथ की अँगूठी चित्त को चुरा लेती है। ब्याह के सब साज सजे हुए वे शोभा पा रहे हैं। चौड़ी छाती पर हृदय पर पहनने के सुंदर आभूषण सुशोभित हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1763.english_translation: The yellow sacred thread adds great beauty. The ring steals the mind. Every wedding ornament shines on the broad chest.
ramacharitamanas::1763.translation_literal: पीत (yellow) / जनेउ (sacred thread) / महाछबि (great beauty) / देई (gives) / कर (hand) / मुद्रिका (ring) / चोरि (steals) / चितु (mind) / लेई (takes) / सोहत (shining) / ब्याह साज (wedding adornments) / सब (all) / साजे (adorned) / उर (chest) / आयत (broad) / उरभूषन (chest-ornament) / राजे (shine)
ramacharitamanas::1763.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1763.essence: Every ornament on Ram deepens the spell of his presence.
ramacharitamanas::1763.simple_meaning: Ram's wedding ornaments make him look even more radiant: the sacred thread, ring, and chest ornaments all add to his beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1763.simple_insight: Beauty becomes unforgettable when every detail feels alive and intentional.
ramacharitamanas::1763.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, Ram is being described as he appears in full wedding adornment. The sacred thread, ring, and chest ornaments are not separate details; they build the image of his overwhelming, royal beauty before Sita and the gathered assembly.
ramacharitamanas::1763.modern_relevance: You see someone walk into a wedding hall, and the room shifts before they even speak. The right details do that: a thread, a ring, a necklace, all quietly announcing presence.
ramacharitamanas::1763.insight: It trains attention on the harmony of small details that create an unforgettable whole.

ramacharitamanas::1764.verse_sanskrit: पिअर उपरना काखासोती। दुहुँ आँचरन्हि लगे मनि मोती॥ नयन कमल कल कुंडल काना। बदनु सकल सौंदर्ज निदाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1764.verse_hindi: पीला दुपट्टा काँखासोती (जनेऊ की तरह) शोभित है, जिसके दोनों छोरों पर मणि और मोती लगे हैं। कमल के समान सुंदर नेत्र हैं, कानों में सुंदर कुंडल हैं और मुख तो सारी सुंदरता का खजाना ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1764.english_translation: A yellow shawl shines on the shoulder, its two ends set with gems and pearls. Eyes are like lotuses, ears wear lovely earrings, and the face is the treasure-house of all beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1764.translation_literal: पिअर (yellow) / उपरना (upper cloth/shawl) / काखासोती (shoulder-cloth) / दुहुँ (both) / आँचरन्हि (ends/edges) / लगे (attached) / मनि (gems) / मोती (pearls)॥ नयन (eyes) / कमल (lotuses) / कल (beautiful) / कुंडल (earrings) / काना (ears) / बदनु (face) / सकल (all) / सौंदर्ज (beauty) / निदाना (treasure-house/end)॥
ramacharitamanas::1764.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1764.essence: Ram's beauty is calm, complete, and impossible to overlook.
ramacharitamanas::1764.simple_meaning: Ram is described as beautifully dressed and adorned, with a radiant face, lotus eyes, and earrings. The verse is pure praise of his appearance.
ramacharitamanas::1764.simple_insight: Beauty here is not decoration alone; it feels complete, calm, and naturally radiant.
ramacharitamanas::1764.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar scene, the narrator keeps describing Ram’s royal beauty piece by piece. This verse adds his shawl, earrings, eyes, and face, building the full image of the bridegroom before the gathering.
ramacharitamanas::1764.modern_relevance: You notice someone enter a room and the whole atmosphere changes. Nothing flashy, nothing forced — just a quiet radiance that makes everyone look twice.
ramacharitamanas::1764.insight: It trains attention toward grace, poise, and inner composure expressed through form.

ramacharitamanas::1765.verse_sanskrit: सुंदर भृकुटि मनोहर नासा। भाल तिलकु रुचिरता निवासा॥ सोहत मौरु मनोहर माथे। मंगलमय मुकुता मनि गाथे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1765.verse_hindi: सुंदर भौंहें और मनोहर नासिका है। ललाट पर तिलक तो सुंदरता का घर ही है, जिसमें मंगलमय मोती और मणि गुँथे हुए हैं, ऐसा मनोहर मौर माथे पर सोह रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1765.english_translation: Beautiful eyebrows and a lovely nose. The tilak on the forehead seems like a home of beauty, with auspicious pearls and gems woven into the graceful crown on the head.
ramacharitamanas::1765.translation_literal: सुंदर (beautiful) / भृकुटि (eyebrows) / मनोहर (charming) / नासा (nose) / भाल (forehead) / तिलकु (tilak mark) / रुचिरता (beauty) / निवासा (dwelling) / सोहत (is shining) / मौरु (crown of flowers and peacock feathers) / मनोहर (charming) / माथे (on the head) / मंगलमय (auspicious) / मुकुता (pearls) / मनि (gems) / गाथे (woven)
ramacharitamanas::1765.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1765.essence: Beauty here is not decoration; it announces sacred presence.
ramacharitamanas::1765.simple_meaning: The groom is described as dazzlingly beautiful, with lovely features, a bright tilak, and an ornamented crown.
ramacharitamanas::1765.simple_insight: Some moments are meant to be admired, not explained.
ramacharitamanas::1765.detailed_meaning: At Sita's swayamvar, the wedding assembly is already awed by Ram's appearance. The poet lingers on his face and crown, building the scene's splendor before the crowd's fuller reaction in the next verse.
ramacharitamanas::1765.modern_relevance: You catch someone across a crowded room and every detail feels radiant at once. The mind stops arguing and simply sees beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1765.insight: It slows the reader down to notice how form itself can carry reverence.

ramacharitamanas::1766.verse_sanskrit: गाथे महामनि मौर मंजुल अंग सब चित चोरहीं। पुर नारि सुर सुंदरीं बरहि बिलोकि सब तिन तोरहीं॥ मनि बसन भूषन वारि आरति करहिं मंगल गावहीं। सुर सुमन बरिसहिं सूत मागध बंदि सुजसु सुनावहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1766.verse_hindi: सुंदर मौर में बहुमूल्य मणियाँ गुँथी हुई हैं, सभी अंग चित्त को चुराए लेते हैं। सब नगर की स्त्रियाँ और देवसुंदरियाँ दूल्हे को देखकर तिनका तोड़ रही हैं (उनकी बलैयाँ ले रही हैं) और मणि, वस्त्र तथा आभूषण निछावर करके आरती उतार रही और मंगलगान कर रही हैं। देवता फूल बरसा रहे हैं और सूत, मागध तथा भाट सुयश सुना रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1766.english_translation: The groom’s jeweled crest and graceful limbs steal every heart. Townswomen and celestial beauties gaze at him, offer worship, sing blessings, shower gifts, and proclaim his fame.
ramacharitamanas::1766.translation_literal: गाथे (woven) / महामनि (great jewels) / मौर (crest) / मंजुल (graceful) / अंग (limbs) / सब (all) / चित (mind) / चोरहीं (steal) । पुर (town) / नारि (women) / सुर (divine beings) / सुंदरीं (beautiful women) / बरहि (seeing) / बिलोकि (gazing) / सब (all) / तिन (their) / तोरहीं (tear up / offer blessings) । मनि (jewels) / बसन (clothes) / भूषन (ornaments) / वारि (water) / आरति (worship) / करहिं (do) / मंगल (auspicious) / गावहीं (sing) । सुर (divine beings) / सुमन (flowers) / बरिसहिं (rain down) / सूत (bards) / मागध (panegyrists) / बंदि (praise) / सुजसु (good fame) / सुनावहीं (make heard)
ramacharitamanas::1766.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1766.essence: Ram’s presence draws worship before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::1766.simple_meaning: Ram appears so beautiful at the wedding that everyone is captivated. Women, celestial beings, and singers all honor him with gifts, songs, flowers, and praise.
ramacharitamanas::1766.simple_insight: Beauty can become worship when the heart recognizes what it is seeing.
ramacharitamanas::1766.detailed_meaning: At Sita’s swayamvar, Ram stands adorned like the perfect groom. His beauty overwhelms the crowd: women, divine beings, singers, and bards respond at once with offerings, blessings, flowers, and praise. The scene is celebration, not argument.
ramacharitamanas::1766.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the mood changes before you say a word. Not because you demanded attention, but because your presence carried something worth honoring.
ramacharitamanas::1766.insight: It shifts attention from performance to presence: when character is radiant, recognition follows naturally.

ramacharitamanas::1767.verse_sanskrit: कोहबरहिं आने कुअँर कुअँरि सुआसिनिन्ह सुख पाइ कै। अति प्रीति लौकिक रीति लागीं करन मंगल गाइ कै॥ लहकौरि गौरि सिखाव रामहि सीय सन सारद कहैं। रनिवासु हास बिलास रस बस जन्म को फलु सब लहैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1767.verse_hindi: सुहागिनी स्त्रियाँ सुख पाकर कुँअर और कुमारियों को कोहबर (कुलदेवता के स्थान) में लाईं और अत्यन्त प्रेम से मंगल गीत गा-गाकर लौकिक रीति करने लगीं। पार्वतीजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी को लहकौर (वर-वधू का परस्पर ग्रास देना) सिखाती हैं और सरस्वतीजी सीताजी को सिखाती हैं। रनिवास हास-विलास के आनंद में मग्न है, (श्री रामजी और सीताजी को देख-देखकर) सभी जन्म का परम फल प्राप्त कर रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1767.english_translation: The married women brought the prince and princess into the wedding chamber, singing auspicious songs with deep affection and following the customary rites. Parvati teaches Ram the bride-groom’s first morsel, Saraswati teaches Sita, and the palace women, lost in laughter and delight, feel they have gained the fruit of all their births by seeing Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::1767.translation_literal: कोहबरहिं (to the wedding chamber) / आने (brought) / कुअँर (prince) / कुअँरि (princess) / सुआसिनिन्ह (married women) / सुख पाइ कै (having obtained joy) / अति प्रीति (with great affection) / लौकिक रीति (customary worldly rite) / लागीं (began) / करन (to do) / मंगल (auspicious songs) / गाइ कै (singing) / लहकौरि (first morsel for bride and groom) / गौरि (Parvati) / सिखाव (teaches) / रामहि (to Ram) / सीय (to Sita) / सन (to) / सारद (Saraswati) / कहैं (they say) / रनिवासु (the palace women) / हास बिलास रस (in the joy of laughter and play) / बस (absorbed) / जन्म को फलु (fruit of birth) / सब (all) / लहैं (receive)
ramacharitamanas::1767.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1767.essence: Seeing Ram and Sita makes life feel complete.
ramacharitamanas::1767.simple_meaning: The wedding chamber fills with joy, songs, and ritual. Everyone feels that seeing Ram and Sita is the highest blessing of life.
ramacharitamanas::1767.simple_insight: Some moments feel so complete that ordinary joy turns into reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1767.detailed_meaning: Ram and Sita have entered the wedding chamber, and the palace women are carrying out the marriage rites with delight. Parvati and Saraswati are imagined guiding the ritual, while the women feel that simply witnessing this union has fulfilled their lives.
ramacharitamanas::1767.modern_relevance: At a wedding where the room goes quiet the moment the couple enters, everyone feels it: this is more than ceremony. The joy in the room becomes its own blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1767.insight: It shifts attention from ritual as form to ritual as shared wonder and fulfillment.

ramacharitamanas::1768.verse_sanskrit: निज पानि मनि महुँ देखिअति मूरति सुरूपनिधान की। चालति न भुजबल्ली बिलोकनि बिरह भय बस जानकी॥ कौतुक बिनोद प्रमोदु प्रेमु न जाइ कहि जानहिं अलीं। बर कुअँरि सुंदर सकल सखीं लवाइ जनवासेहि चलीं ॥
