ramacharitamanas::1768.verse_hindi: 'अपने हाथ की मणियों में सुंदर रूप के भण्डार श्री रामचन्द्रजी की परछाहीं दिख रही है। यह देखकर जानकीजी दर्शन में वियोग होने के भय से बाहु रूपी लता को और दृष्टि को हिलाती-डुलाती नहीं हैं। उस समय के हँसी-खेल और विनोद का आनंद और प्रेम कहा नहीं जा सकता, उसे सखियाँ ही जानती हैं। तदनन्तर वर-कन्याओं को सब सुंदर सखियाँ जनवासे को लिवा चलीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1768.english_translation: In the jewels in her hand, Janaki sees the beautiful form of Ram. Fearful of separation, she does not move her arms or her gaze. The laughter, play, delight, and love of that moment cannot be described; only the companions know it. Then the beautiful attendants led the bride and groom to the marriage pavilion.
ramacharitamanas::1768.translation_literal: निज (own) / पानि (hand) / मनि (jewel) / महुँ (in) / देखिअति (is seen) / मूरति (form) / सुरूपनिधान (treasure of beauty) / की (of) / चालति (moves) / न (not) / भुजबल्ली (arm-vine) / बिलोकनि (gaze) / बिरह (separation) / भय (fear) / बस (under) / जानकी (Janaki) / कौतुक (playfulness) / बिनोद (delight) / प्रमोदु (joy) / प्रेमु (love) / न (not) / जाइ (can be) / कहि (said) / जानहिं (know) / अलीं (companions) / बर (groom) / कुअँरि (bride) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सकल (all) / सखीं (companions) / लवाइ (leading) / जनवासेहि (to the marriage pavilion) / चलीं (went)
ramacharitamanas::1768.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1768.essence: A single glimpse of Ram makes the heart afraid to blink.
ramacharitamanas::1768.simple_meaning: Janaki sees Ram’s image reflected in her jewels and becomes afraid of losing that sight. She stays still, while the wedding party moves the bride and groom toward the marriage pavilion.
ramacharitamanas::1768.simple_insight: Love makes even a glance feel precious. When the heart is full, it wants to hold still.
ramacharitamanas::1768.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, the wedding preparations are in full joy. Janaki catches Ram’s reflection in her jewel and, afraid of losing that vision, stops even the smallest movement. The verse lingers on her shy devotion before the procession moves on.
ramacharitamanas::1768.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone you love across a crowded room and suddenly everything else fades. You do not want the moment to end; you want to keep looking.
ramacharitamanas::1768.insight: It shifts attention from the ceremony itself to the intensity of seeing Ram, where devotion freezes motion.

ramacharitamanas::1769.verse_sanskrit: तेहि समय सुनिअ असीस जहँ तहँ नगर नभ आनँदु महा। चिरु जिअहुँ जोरीं चारु चार् यो मुदित मन सबहीं कहा॥ जोगींद्र सिद्ध मुनीस देव बिलोकि प्रभु दुंदुभि हनी। चले हरषि बरषि प्रसून निज निज लोक जय जय जय भनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1769.verse_hindi: उस समय नगर और आकाश में जहाँ सुनिए, वहीं आशीर्वाद की ध्वनि सुनाई दे रही है और महान आनंद छाया है। सभी ने प्रसन्न मन से कहा कि सुंदर चारों जोड़ियाँ चिरंजीवी हों। योगीराज, सिद्ध, मुनीश्वर और देवताओं ने प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर दुन्दुभी बजाई और हर्षित होकर फूलों की वर्षा करते हुए तथा 'जय हो, जय हो, जय हो' कहते हुए वे अपने-अपने लोक को चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1769.english_translation: At that time, blessings were heard everywhere in the city and the sky was filled with great joy. Everyone, delighted, said, "May the four beautiful couples live long." The lords of yoga, the perfected sages, the great seers, and the radiant beings saw Lord Ram, beat their drums, showered flowers, and returned to their own realms crying, "Victory, victory, victory."
ramacharitamanas::1769.translation_literal: तेहि समय (at that time) / सुनिअ (is heard) / असीस (blessings) / जहँ तहँ (everywhere) / नगर (city) / नभ (sky) / आनँदु (joy) / महा (great) / चिरु (long) / जिअहुँ (may live) / जोरीं (pairs) / चारु (beautiful) / चार् यो (four) / मुदित (delighted) / मन (mind) / सबहीं (everyone) / कहा (said) / जोगींद्र (lord of yogis) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / मुनीस (great sages) / देव (radiant beings) / बिलोकि (seeing) / प्रभु (the Lord) / दुंदुभि (drum) / हनी (struck) / चले (went) / हरषि (rejoicing) / बरषि (showering) / प्रसून (flowers) / निज निज (their own) / लोक (realms) / जय जय जय (victory, victory, victory) / भनी (said)
ramacharitamanas::1769.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1769.essence: Ram's presence makes even the heavens rejoice.
ramacharitamanas::1769.simple_meaning: The whole city and sky overflow with blessings and joy. Sages and radiant beings rejoice at Ram's sight, shower flowers, and return praising him.
ramacharitamanas::1769.simple_insight: Some moments are so full of grace that even the unseen world seems to celebrate with you.
ramacharitamanas::1769.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur after the wedding, the whole city is swept into celebration. Blessings rise everywhere, the sages and radiant beings witness Ram, beat their drums, and shower flowers before returning to their own realms. The scene is pure overflow, not argument.
ramacharitamanas::1769.modern_relevance: At a wedding when the room suddenly goes quiet and then erupts into blessings, you feel it: some joy is bigger than the people in the room. This verse lives in that overflowing moment.
ramacharitamanas::1769.insight: It turns the wedding into a cosmic celebration, showing Ram's presence as something the whole world recognizes.

ramacharitamanas::1770.verse_sanskrit: सहित बधूटिन्ह कुअँर सब तब आए पितु पास। सोभा मंगल मोद भरि उमगेउ जनु जनवास ॥
ramacharitamanas::1770.verse_hindi: तब सब (चारों) कुमार बहुओं सहित पिताजी के पास आए। ऐसा मालूम होता था मानो शोभा, मंगल और आनंद से भरकर जनवासा उमड़ पड़ा हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1770.english_translation: Then all the princes, along with their brides, came to their father. It seemed as if the bridal pavilion itself overflowed with beauty, auspiciousness, and joy.
ramacharitamanas::1770.translation_literal: सहित (along with) / बधूटिन्ह (with the brides) / कुअँर (princes) / सब (all) / तब (then) / आए (came) / पितु (father) / पास (near) / सोभा (beauty) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मोद (joy) / भरि (filled with) / उमगेउ (overflowed) / जनु (as if) / जनवास (bridal pavilion)
ramacharitamanas::1770.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1770.essence: Joy becomes visible when a family comes together in harmony.
ramacharitamanas::1770.simple_meaning: The princes return with their brides to their father, and the whole wedding pavilion feels full of beauty and joy.
ramacharitamanas::1770.simple_insight: Shared joy can make an ordinary gathering feel alive and radiant.
ramacharitamanas::1770.detailed_meaning: After the wedding, the four princes come back to King Dasharath with their brides. The scene is overflowing with festive happiness, and the bridal pavilion feels so full of splendour that it seems to swell with life.
ramacharitamanas::1770.modern_relevance: After a wedding, the whole house is still buzzing — relatives moving through rooms, laughter spilling into the hallway, everyone carrying the glow of something just completed.
ramacharitamanas::1770.insight: It turns a family reunion into a picture of collective blessing and celebration.

ramacharitamanas::1771.verse_sanskrit: पुनि जेवनार भई बहु भाँती। पठए जनक बोलाइ बराती॥ परत पाँवड़े बसन अनूपा। सुतन्ह समेत गवन कियो भूपा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1771.verse_hindi: फिर बहुत प्रकार की रसोई बनी। जनकजी ने बारातियों को बुला भेजा। राजा दशरथजी ने पुत्रों सहित गमन किया। अनुपम वस्त्रों के पाँवड़े पड़ते जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1771.english_translation: Then many kinds of food were prepared. Janak sent word to invite the wedding guests. King Dasharath set out with his sons, while splendid cloths were laid beneath their feet.
ramacharitamanas::1771.translation_literal: पुनि (then again) / जेवनार (feast) / भई (was prepared) / बहु भाँती (in many kinds) / पठए (sent) / जनक (Janak) / बोलाइ (having called) / बराती (wedding guests) / परत (while falling) / पाँवड़े (carpets / cloths laid for walking) / बसन (cloths) / अनूपा (beautiful, incomparable) / सुतन्ह (with sons) / समेत (together with) / गवन (departure / going) / कियो (made) / भूपा (the king)
ramacharitamanas::1771.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1771.essence: Honor turns celebration into something larger than celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1771.simple_meaning: A grand feast was prepared, the wedding guests were invited, and Dasharath departed with his sons on beautifully laid cloths.
ramacharitamanas::1771.simple_insight: Great occasions are marked by care, honor, and shared joy.
ramacharitamanas::1771.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the wedding celebration moves into its next stage. Janak arranges the feast and calls the guests, while Dasharath arrives with his sons in royal splendor. The verse paints the dignity and abundance surrounding Ram and Sita's union.
ramacharitamanas::1771.modern_relevance: A wedding hall fills with fragrance, relatives bustle through the rooms, and every detail is arranged to honor the moment. Some occasions become sacred simply because everyone present chooses care.
ramacharitamanas::1771.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the reverence shown through preparation and welcome.

ramacharitamanas::1772.verse_sanskrit: सादर सब के पाय पखारे। जथाजोगु पीढ़न्ह बैठारे॥ धोए जनक अवधपति चरना। सीलु सनेहु जाइ नहिं बरना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1772.verse_hindi: आदर के साथ सबके चरण धोए और सबको यथायोग्य पीढ़ों पर बैठाया। तब जनकजी ने अवधपति दशरथजी के चरण धोए। उनका शील और स्नेह वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1772.english_translation: With respect, everyone’s feet were washed and everyone was seated according to rank. Then Janaka washed the feet of the king of Ayodhya. His nobility and affection cannot be described.
ramacharitamanas::1772.translation_literal: सादर (with respect) / सब (all) / के (of) / पाय (feet) / पखारे (washed) / जथाजोगु (as appropriate) / पीढ़न्ह (on seats) / बैठारे (seated) / धोए (washed) / जनक (Janaka) / अवधपति (lord of Ayodhya) / चरना (feet) / सीलु (nobility) / सनेहु (affection) / जाइ (go) / नहिं (not) / बरना (described)
ramacharitamanas::1772.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1772.essence: Honor becomes real when pride kneels before service.
ramacharitamanas::1772.simple_meaning: Janaka honors every guest properly, then personally washes Dasharath’s feet. The verse highlights his noble manners and heartfelt affection.
ramacharitamanas::1772.simple_insight: True respect is shown in humble actions, not just polite words.
ramacharitamanas::1772.detailed_meaning: At Janaka’s court after the wedding, the guests are being received with full honor. Janaka seats everyone properly, then bows even lower to wash Dasharath’s feet himself. The scene reveals the dignity and warmth of the hosts before the celebration moves on.
ramacharitamanas::1772.modern_relevance: You welcome guests into your home, then notice the oldest person at the table and quietly bring water yourself. No speech can match that kind of respect.
ramacharitamanas::1772.insight: It teaches that status is not lost by humility; it is revealed through it.

ramacharitamanas::1773.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि राम पद पंकज धोए। जे हर हृदय कमल महुँ गोए॥ तीनिउ भाइ राम सम जानी। धोए चरन जनक निज पानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1773.verse_hindi: फिर श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणकमलों को धोया, जो श्री शिवजी के हृदय कमल में छिपे रहते हैं। तीनों भाइयों को श्री रामचन्द्रजी के समान जानकर जनकजी ने उनके भी चरण अपने हाथों से धोए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1773.english_translation: Then Janaka washed Ram's lotus feet, the feet that dwell in Shiva's lotus heart. Seeing all three brothers as equal to Ram, Janaka washed their feet with his own hands.
ramacharitamanas::1773.translation_literal: बहुरि (again) / राम (Ram) / पद पंकज (lotus feet) / धोए (washed) / जे (which) / हर (Shiva) / हृदय (heart) / कमल महुँ (in the lotus) / गोए (hidden, gone) ॥ / तीनिउ (all three) / भाइ (brothers) / राम (Ram) / सम (equal) / जानी (knowing) / धोए (washed) / चरन (feet) / जनक (Janaka) / निज (own) / पानी (water, hands) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1773.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1773.essence: Reverence becomes complete when it honors Ram in every brother.
ramacharitamanas::1773.simple_meaning: Janaka honors Ram by washing his feet, then does the same for Ram's brothers, seeing all three as equal in dignity.
ramacharitamanas::1773.simple_insight: True reverence does not stop at ceremony. It sees sacred worth and responds with humble care.
ramacharitamanas::1773.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's court after the wedding, the king receives Dasharath and his sons with deep reverence. He washes Ram's feet first, then treats Lakshman, Bharat, and Shatrughna with the same honor, showing devotion that recognizes Ram in all three brothers.
ramacharitamanas::1773.modern_relevance: You meet someone famous at a family gathering, but you still make tea for their quieter sibling and ask their opinion too. Respect is real when it is not selective.
ramacharitamanas::1773.insight: It shifts reverence from status to recognition: honor the divine presence, not just the most visible one.

ramacharitamanas::1774.verse_sanskrit: आसन उचित सबहि नृप दीन्हे। बोलि सूपकारी सब लीन्हे॥ सादर लगे परन पनवारे। कनक कील मनि पान सँवारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1774.verse_hindi: राजा जनकजी ने सभी को उचित आसन दिए और सब परसने वालों को बुला लिया। आदर के साथ पत्तलें पड़ने लगीं, जो मणियों के पत्तों से सोने की कील लगाकर बनाई गई थीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1774.english_translation: King Janaka gave everyone fitting seats and called the servers. Respectfully, leaf-plates were set out, adorned with jewels and fastened with golden pegs.
ramacharitamanas::1774.translation_literal: आसन (seats) / उचित (proper, fitting) / सबहि (to everyone) / नृप (king) / दीन्हे (gave) / बोलि (calling) / सूपकारी (servants, caterers) / सब (all) / लीन्हे (brought) / सादर (respectfully) / लगे (were set) / परन (leaf-plates) / पनवारे (servers, arrangers) / कनक (gold) / कील (pegs) / मनि (jewel) / पान (leaf) / सँवारे (adorned)
ramacharitamanas::1774.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1774.essence: Respect becomes visible in the smallest arrangements.
ramacharitamanas::1774.simple_meaning: Janaka arranges the feast with care and respect. Everyone is seated properly, and the serving plates are beautifully prepared.
ramacharitamanas::1774.simple_insight: True hospitality notices every person and makes room for them with dignity.
ramacharitamanas::1774.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's palace after the ritual welcome, the guests are being honored properly. The king seats everyone according to rank and calls the servers. This verse pauses on the careful arrangement before the meal begins.
ramacharitamanas::1774.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where the hosts have already noticed who needs a chair, who needs water, and who should be seated together. That quiet attention makes people feel seen before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1774.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to care: dignity is shown through how people are seated and served.

ramacharitamanas::1775.verse_sanskrit: सूपोदन सुरभी सरपि सुंदर स्वादु पुनीत। छन महुँ सब कें परुसि गे चतुर सुआर बिनीत ॥
ramacharitamanas::1775.verse_hindi: चतुर और विनीत रसोइए सुंदर, स्वादिष्ट और पवित्र दाल-भात और गाय का (सुगंधित) घी क्षण भर में सबके सामने परस गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1775.english_translation: The wise and courteous cooks quickly served everyone with fragrant rice, lentils, ghee, and pure, delicious food.
ramacharitamanas::1775.translation_literal: सूपोदन (rice and food) / सुरभी (fragrant) / सरपि (ghee) / सुंदर (beautiful) / स्वादु (tasty) / पुनीत (pure) / छन महुँ (in a moment) / सब कें (to everyone) / परुसि गे (served) / चतुर (skilled) / सुआर (cooks) / बिनीत (courteous)
ramacharitamanas::1775.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1775.essence: True honour is served as quickly as it is felt.
ramacharitamanas::1775.simple_meaning: The cooks served the meal quickly and respectfully, with fine food and ghee for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::1775.simple_insight: Care shows itself in small, timely acts that make everyone feel welcomed.
ramacharitamanas::1775.detailed_meaning: At Janak's feast after the sacred washing of Ram's feet, the household moves with graceful order. Skilled cooks serve the assembled guests immediately, turning hospitality into a visible act of honour.
ramacharitamanas::1775.modern_relevance: A host notices the plates are still empty while guests keep glancing around the room. The meal arrives fast, warm, and thoughtful — and everyone feels seen before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1775.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to care: real respect is making others comfortable without delay.

ramacharitamanas::1776.verse_sanskrit: पंच कवल करि जेवन लागे। गारि गान सुनि अति अनुरागे। भाँति अनेक परे पकवाने। सुधा सरिस नहिं जाहिं बखाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1776.verse_hindi: सब लोग पंचकौर करके (अर्थात 'प्राणाय स्वाहा, अपानाय स्वाहा, व्यानाय स्वाहा, उदानाय स्वाहा और समानाय स्वाहा' इन मंत्रों का उच्चारण करते हुए पहले पाँच ग्रास लेकर) भोजन करने लगे। गाली का गाना सुनकर वे अत्यन्त प्रेममग्न हो गए। अनेकों तरह के अमृत के समान (स्वादिष्ट) पकवान परसे गए, जिनका बखान नहीं हो सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1776.english_translation: They began eating after taking the five mouthfuls. Hearing songs of abuse, they became deeply delighted. Many kinds of dishes were served; they were like nectar and beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::1776.translation_literal: पंच कवल (five mouthfuls) / करि (having done) / जेवन (eating) / लागे (began) / गारि (abuse) / गान (song) / सुनि (hearing) / अति (very) / अनुरागे (filled with love) / भाँति (ways/kinds) / अनेक (many) / परे (were served) / पकवाने (cooked dishes) / सुधा (nectar) / सरिस (like) / नहिं (not) / जाहिं (can be) / बखाने (described)
ramacharitamanas::1776.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1776.essence: Abundance becomes memorable when it is offered with delight.
ramacharitamanas::1776.simple_meaning: Everyone started eating, delighted by the festive singing and the many dishes served. The food was so varied and exquisite that it could not be fully described.
ramacharitamanas::1776.simple_insight: Joy multiplies ordinary things. Even a meal becomes unforgettable when it is offered with warmth and celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1776.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s grand feast during Sita’s swayamvar, the guests are seated and served with royal care. The cooks bring out countless delicacies, and the whole hall is alive with music and delight. This verse lingers on the abundance and beauty of that welcome.
ramacharitamanas::1776.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall where the air is full of laughter, music, and the smell of fresh food. The details blur because the feeling is larger than the menu.
ramacharitamanas::1776.insight: It shifts attention from the meal itself to the atmosphere of generous hospitality that surrounds it.

ramacharitamanas::1777.verse_sanskrit: परुसन लगे सुआर सुजाना। बिंजन बिबिध नाम को जाना॥ चारि भाँति भोजन बिधि गाई। एक एक बिधि बरनि न जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1777.verse_hindi: चतुर रसोइए नाना प्रकार के व्यंजन परसने लगे, उनका नाम कौन जानता है। चार प्रकार के (चर्व्य, चोष्य, लेह्य, पेय अर्थात चबाकर, चूसकर, चाटकर और पीना-खाने योग्य) भोजन की विधि कही गई है, उनमें से एक-एक विधि के इतने पदार्थ बने थे कि जिनका वर्ण नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1777.english_translation: Skilled cooks began serving the dishes. Who could even name the many kinds of food? Four kinds of food were prepared, and each kind had so many varieties that they could not be fully described.
ramacharitamanas::1777.translation_literal: परुसन (to serve) / लगे (began) / सुआर (cooks) / सुजाना (skilled) । / बिंजन (dishes) / बिबिध (various) / नाम (names) / को (who) / जाना (knows) ॥ / चारि (four) / भाँति (kinds) / भोजन (food) / बिधि (method) / गाई (was described) । / एक एक (one by one) / बिधि (kind) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाई (can be) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1777.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1777.essence: Some abundance is too rich to be fully named.
ramacharitamanas::1777.simple_meaning: The cooks served many kinds of food, and the variety was beyond counting or description.
ramacharitamanas::1777.simple_insight: Abundance can be so complete that language runs out.
ramacharitamanas::1777.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s grand feast during the Balkand, the cooks begin serving an astonishing spread. The verse does not teach a doctrine; it lingers on the overflowing richness of the meal, preparing the scene for the celebration that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1777.modern_relevance: You open a festival menu and freeze for a second, smiling at how much care went into every dish. Some moments are so full that listing them feels smaller than simply receiving them.
ramacharitamanas::1777.insight: It shifts attention from counting details to feeling the fullness of the offering.

ramacharitamanas::1778.verse_sanskrit: छरस रुचिर बिंजन बहु जाती। एक एक रस अगनित भाँती॥ जेवँत देहिं मधुर धुनि गारी। लै लै नाम पुरुष अरु नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1778.verse_hindi: छहों रसों के बहुत तरह के सुंदर (स्वादिष्ट) व्यंजन हैं। एक-एक रस के अनगिनत प्रकार के बने हैं। भोजन के समय पुरुष और स्त्रियों के नाम ले-लेकर स्त्रियाँ मधुर ध्वनि से गाली दे रही हैं (गाली गा रही हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1778.english_translation: There are many kinds of beautiful dishes, each taste in countless forms. As they eat, women sing playful scoldings in sweet voices, calling out the names of men and women.
ramacharitamanas::1778.translation_literal: छरस (six tastes) / रुचिर (beautiful) / बिंजन (dishes) / बहु जाती (many kinds) / एक एक (each one) / रस (taste) / अगनित (countless) / भाँती (forms) / जेवँत (while eating) / देहिं (give) / मधुर (sweet) / धुनि (voice/sound) / गारी (playful scolding song) / लै लै (taking, calling) / नाम (names) / पुरुष (men) / अरु (and) / नारी (women)
ramacharitamanas::1778.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1778.essence: Delight multiplies when abundance is joined by playful song.
ramacharitamanas::1778.simple_meaning: The feast is overflowing with many kinds of delicious food, and the women add playful singing and teasing as everyone eats.
ramacharitamanas::1778.simple_insight: Joy becomes richer when food, music, and shared laughter fill the same moment.
ramacharitamanas::1778.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya’s feast scene, cooks have already set out endless dishes. Now the women begin sweet teasing songs while everyone eats. This verse is not teaching a doctrine; it simply deepens the festive, overflowing atmosphere before the meal continues.
ramacharitamanas::1778.modern_relevance: A family gathering comes alive when the table is full, someone starts joking, and the room loosens into laughter. The memory is not just the food — it is the warmth around it.
ramacharitamanas::1778.insight: It keeps the focus on atmosphere, showing how celebration is made complete by shared sound and social ease.

ramacharitamanas::1779.verse_sanskrit: समय सुहावनि गारि बिराजा। हँसत राउ सुनि सहित समाजा॥ एहि बिधि सबहीं भोजनु कीन्हा। आदर सहित आचमनु दीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1779.verse_hindi: समय की सुहावनी गाली शोभित हो रही है। उसे सुनकर समाज सहित राजा दशरथजी हँस रहे हैं। इस रीति से सभी ने भोजन किया और तब सबको आदर सहित आचमन (हाथ-मुँह धोने के लिए जल) दिया गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1779.english_translation: A pleasant jest adorned the moment. King Dasharath laughed with the assembled company upon hearing it. In this way everyone ate, and then water was respectfully given for rinsing the mouth.
ramacharitamanas::1779.translation_literal: समय (occasion) / सुहावनि (pleasant) / गारि (jest) / बिराजा (adorned) / हँसत (laughing) / राउ (king) / सुनि (having heard) / सहित (along with) / समाजा (assembly) / एहि बिधि (in this manner) / सबहीं (everyone) / भोजनु (food) / कीन्हा (did) / आदर सहित (with respect) / आचमनु (mouth-rinsing water) / दीन्हा (gave)
ramacharitamanas::1779.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1779.essence: A joyful meal becomes memorable through laughter and respect.
ramacharitamanas::1779.simple_meaning: The feast was cheerful and respectful. Dasharath laughed with the gathered people, everyone ate, and water was served afterward.
ramacharitamanas::1779.simple_insight: Shared joy and good manners can make even a royal meal feel warm and human.
ramacharitamanas::1779.detailed_meaning: At Janak's feast, the guests are already enjoying the many dishes. A light joke brings laughter from Dasharath and the whole assembly. The verse simply completes the scene: the meal is finished with proper honor and care.
ramacharitamanas::1779.modern_relevance: At a family wedding table, someone cracks a harmless joke and the whole room loosens at once. The best gatherings are remembered not just for food, but for ease, laughter, and respect.
ramacharitamanas::1779.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony alone to the human warmth that makes ceremony alive.

ramacharitamanas::1780.verse_sanskrit: देइ पान पूजे जनक दसरथु सहित समाज। जनवासेहि गवने मुदित सकल भूप सिरताज ॥
ramacharitamanas::1780.verse_hindi: फिर पान देकर जनकजी ने समाज सहित दशरथजी का पूजन किया। सब राजाओं के सिरमौर (चक्रवर्ती) श्री दशरथजी प्रसन्न होकर जनवासे को चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1780.english_translation: Then Janaka offered betel leaf and honored Dasharatha with the assembled kings. Delighted, the crowned king Dasharatha went to the guest quarters.
ramacharitamanas::1780.translation_literal: देइ (giving) / पान (betel leaf) / पूजे (honored) / जनक (Janaka) / दसरथु (Dasharatha) / सहित (along with) / समाज (assembly) / जनवासेहि (to the guest quarters) / गवने (went) / मुदित (delighted) / सकल (all) / भूप (kings) / सिरताज (crowned head)
ramacharitamanas::1780.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1780.essence: Honor turns a visit into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1780.simple_meaning: Janaka honors Dasharatha and the gathered kings, then Dasharatha happily goes to the guest quarters.
ramacharitamanas::1780.simple_insight: Respect and hospitality can make a formal visit feel warm and dignified.
ramacharitamanas::1780.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, after the feast and royal gathering, King Janaka formally honors Dasharatha in front of the assembled rulers. The mood is gracious and celebratory, and Dasharatha leaves for the guest quarters pleased.
ramacharitamanas::1780.modern_relevance: After a long wedding function, the host walks over with a respectful gesture, and the whole room softens. Small acts of honour can change the atmosphere instantly.
ramacharitamanas::1780.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the dignity created by respectful welcome.

ramacharitamanas::1781.verse_sanskrit: नित नूतन मंगल पुर माहीं। निमिष सरिस दिन जामिनि जाहीं॥ बड़े भोर भूपतिमनि जागे। जाचक गुन गन गावन लागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1781.verse_hindi: जनकपुर में नित्य नए मंगल हो रहे हैं। दिन और रात पल के समान बीत जाते हैं। बड़े सबेरे राजाओं के मुकुटमणि दशरथजी जागे। याचक उनके गुण समूह का गान करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1781.english_translation: In Janakpur, new auspiciousness arose each day. Day and night passed like a moment. At dawn, king Dasharath awoke, and the supplicants began singing his many virtues.
ramacharitamanas::1781.translation_literal: नित (ever) / नूतन (new) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / पुर (city) / माहीं (in) / निमिष (moment) / सरिस (like) / दिन (day) / जामिनि (night) / जाहीं (go) / बड़े (great) / भोर (dawn) / भूपतिमनि (jewel among kings) / जागे (awoke) / जाचक (supplicants) / गुन (virtues) / गन (groups) / गावन (to sing) / लागे (began)
ramacharitamanas::1781.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1781.essence: Joy makes a whole day feel like a moment.
ramacharitamanas::1781.simple_meaning: Janakpur is full of festive joy, time seems to fly, and Dasharath wakes at dawn while people praise him.
ramacharitamanas::1781.simple_insight: Some moments feel so blessed that even time seems to hurry.
ramacharitamanas::1781.detailed_meaning: After the banquet and welcome in Janakpur, the scene settles into a night of overflowing celebration. The city feels newly blessed, Dasharath rises early, and the people around him begin praising his virtues as the wedding joy continues to build.
ramacharitamanas::1781.modern_relevance: After a wedding feast that runs past midnight, the house is still glowing at dawn. Nobody wants the night to end, and even the early hours feel too brief.
ramacharitamanas::1781.insight: It frames the scene as festive atmosphere, not teaching, and carries the story forward into the next morning.

ramacharitamanas::1782.verse_sanskrit: देखि कुअँर बर बधुन्ह समेता। किमि कहि जात मोदु मन जेता॥ प्रातक्रिया करि गे गुरु पाहीं। महाप्रमोदु प्रेमु मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1782.verse_hindi: चारों कुमारों को सुंदर वधुओं सहित देखकर उनके मन में जितना आनंद है, वह किस प्रकार कहा जा सकता है? वे प्रातः क्रिया करके गुरु वशिष्ठजी के पास गए। उनके मन में महान आनंद और प्रेम भरा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1782.english_translation: Seeing the four princes together with their beautiful brides, their joy cannot be described. After their morning rites, they went to Guru Vashistha, filled with great delight and love.
ramacharitamanas::1782.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / कुअँर (princes) / बर (excellent) / बधुन्ह (with brides) / समेता (together) / किमि (how) / कहि (said) / जात (is able to be) / मोदु (joy) / मन (mind) / जेता (as much) / प्रातक्रिया (morning rites) / करि (having done) / गे (went) / गुरु (teacher) / पाहीं (to) / महाप्रमोदु (great delight) / प्रेमु (love) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::1782.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1782.essence: Joy becomes speechless when life finally feels complete.
ramacharitamanas::1782.simple_meaning: The fathers see all four princes with their brides and feel overwhelming joy. After their morning duties, the princes go to their teacher, full of love and happiness.
ramacharitamanas::1782.simple_insight: Some moments are too full for words. Joy itself becomes the only honest response.
ramacharitamanas::1782.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the wedding celebrations have reached their peak. Dasharath and the others see Ram, Lakshman, Bharat, and Shatrughna standing with their brides, and their hearts overflow. After morning rites, the princes go to Vashistha, carrying that joy with them.
ramacharitamanas::1782.modern_relevance: You look across the room at your children standing beside the people they chose, and something in you softens. The day feels complete before anyone says a word.
ramacharitamanas::1782.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to the emotional fullness that ceremony reveals.

ramacharitamanas::1783.verse_sanskrit: करि प्रनामु पूजा कर जोरी। बोले गिरा अमिअँ जनु बोरी॥ तुम्हरी कृपाँ सुनहु मुनिराजा। भयउँ आजु मैं पूरन काजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1783.verse_hindi: राजा प्रणाम और पूजन करके, फिर हाथ जोड़कर मानो अमृत में डुबोई हुई वाणी बोले- हे मुनिराज! सुनिए, आपकी कृपा से आज मैं पूर्णकाम हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1783.english_translation: After bowing and worshipping with joined hands, the king spoke in words like nectar: “By your grace, O great sage, today I have accomplished my purpose.”
ramacharitamanas::1783.translation_literal: करि (having done) / प्रनामु (salutation) / पूजा (worship) / कर (with the hands) / जोरी (joined) / बोले (spoke) / गिरा (speech) / अमिअँ (nectar) / जनु (as if) / बोरी (dipped) / तुम्हरी (your) / कृपाँ (by grace) / सुनहु (listen) / मुनिराजा (O king of sages) / भयउँ (I became) / आजु (today) / मैं (I) / पूरन (complete) / काजा (task)
ramacharitamanas::1783.speaker: Janaka
ramacharitamanas::1783.essence: Completion becomes sweeter when it is offered back as gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::1783.simple_meaning: Janaka bows to the sage and says he has completed his task through the sage's grace.
ramacharitamanas::1783.simple_insight: Gratitude feels deepest when success is received, not claimed.
ramacharitamanas::1783.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur after the wedding, King Janaka bows before the sage and speaks with overflowing humility. The great assembly has been fulfilled, and he credits the completion not to his own power but to the sage's grace.
ramacharitamanas::1783.modern_relevance: You finish a project, but the mentor who shaped you is the first person you call. The achievement feels real only when pride gives way to gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::1783.insight: It shifts success from self-ownership to humble acknowledgment of help received.

ramacharitamanas::1784.verse_sanskrit: अब सब बिप्र बोलाइ गोसाईं। देहु धेनु सब भाँति बनाईं॥ सुनि गुर करि महिपाल बड़ाई। पुनि पठए मुनिबृंद बोलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1784.verse_hindi: हे स्वामिन् ! अब सब ब्राह्मणों को बुलाकर उनको सब तरह (गहनों-कपड़ों) से सजी हुई गायें दीजिए। यह सुनकर गुरुजी ने राजा की बड़ाई करके फिर मुनिगणों को बुलवा भेजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1784.english_translation: O Lord, now call all the brahmins and give away cows, fully adorned in every way. Hearing this, the guru praised the king and then sent word to summon the host of sages.
ramacharitamanas::1784.translation_literal: अब (now) / सब (all) / बिप्र (brahmins) / बोलाइ (having called) / गोसाईं (lord) / देहु (give) / धेनु (cows) / सब भाँति (in every way) / बनाईं (adorned, prepared) / सुनि (hearing) / गुर (the guru) / करि (having done) / महिपाल (king) / बड़ाई (praise) / पुनि (again) / पठए (sent) / मुनिबृंद (host of sages) / बोलाई (having called)
ramacharitamanas::1784.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1784.essence: Joy becomes complete when it is given away.
ramacharitamanas::1784.simple_meaning: The king is told to honor the brahmins with decorated cows, and the guru responds by praising him and calling the sages.
ramacharitamanas::1784.simple_insight: True celebration includes generosity, respect, and shared blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1784.detailed_meaning: After the princes’ marriages, the king is overflowing with joy. The guru instructs him to summon the brahmins and give richly adorned cows. The response turns celebration into public reverence, drawing the sages into the auspicious moment.
ramacharitamanas::1784.modern_relevance: A family finishes a wedding and everyone wants photos, applause, and speeches. One elder quietly says: feed people first, honor them properly, and let gratitude lead the day.
ramacharitamanas::1784.insight: It shifts celebration from display to offering, making joy communal instead of private.

ramacharitamanas::1785.verse_sanskrit: बामदेउ अरु देवरिषि बालमीकि जाबालि। आए मुनिबर निकर तब कौसिकादि तपसालि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1785.verse_hindi: तब वामदेव, देवर्षि नारद, वाल्मीकि, जाबालि और विश्वामित्र आदि तपस्वी श्रेष्ठ मुनियों के समूह के समूह आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1785.english_translation: Then Vamadeva, the divine sage Narada, Valmiki, Jabali, and the great ascetics led by Vishvamitra came in a group of sages.
ramacharitamanas::1785.translation_literal: बामदेउ (Vamadeva) / अरु (and) / देवरिषि (divine sage) / बालमीकि (Valmiki) / जाबालि (Jabali) / आए (came) / मुनिबर (great sages) / निकर (group) / तब (then) / कौसिकादि (led by Vishvamitra and others) / तपसालि (ascetics)
ramacharitamanas::1785.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1785.essence: A sacred gathering grows as revered sages arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1785.simple_meaning: Many respected sages arrived together, including Vamadeva, Narada, Valmiki, Jabali, and Vishvamitra.
ramacharitamanas::1785.simple_insight: Great moments draw great witnesses. Reverence gathers the wise around what matters.
ramacharitamanas::1785.detailed_meaning: After the king has honored the teacher and completed the rite, a larger assembly of sages arrives at the scene. The verse simply names the revered guests, showing the gathering growing before the next act of worship and giving.
ramacharitamanas::1785.modern_relevance: A formal ceremony is underway, and the room suddenly fills with elders, teachers, and respected guests. Their arrival signals that something important is about to be witnessed, honored, and remembered.
ramacharitamanas::1785.insight: It shifts attention from the ritual itself to the sacred company gathered around it.

ramacharitamanas::1786.verse_sanskrit: दंड प्रनाम सबहि नृप कीन्हे। पूजि सप्रेम बरासन दीन्हे॥ चारि लच्छ बर धेनु मगाईं। काम सुरभि सम सील सुहाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1786.verse_hindi: राजा ने सबको दण्डवत् प्रणाम किया और प्रेम सहित पूजन करके उन्हें उत्तम आसन दिए। चार लाख उत्तम गायें मँगवाईं, जो कामधेनु के समान अच्छे स्वभाव वाली और सुहावनी थीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1786.english_translation: The king bowed to everyone with full prostration, honored them with loving hospitality, and brought four hundred thousand excellent cows—gentle and beautiful like Kamadhenu.
ramacharitamanas::1786.translation_literal: दंड प्रनाम (full prostration) / सबहि (everyone) / नृप (king) / कीन्हे (did) / पूजि (honoring) / सप्रेम (with love) / बरासन (excellent seats) / दीन्हे (gave) / चारि लच्छ (four lakhs) / बर (excellent) / धेनु (cows) / मगाईं (had brought) / काम सुरभि (Kamadhenu) / सम (like) / सील (gentle nature) / सुहाईं (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::1786.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1786.essence: Honor becomes real when it is given as service.
ramacharitamanas::1786.simple_meaning: The king shows complete respect to the gathered sages, welcomes them warmly, and gives away huge numbers of fine cows.
ramacharitamanas::1786.simple_insight: Real honour is shown through generosity, not just polite words.
ramacharitamanas::1786.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the sages have arrived for the great gathering. The king does not treat them as guests to impress, but as holy people to serve. He bows, seats them with love, and gives lavish gifts before the next exchange begins.
ramacharitamanas::1786.modern_relevance: You greet the elder who came to your home with a quick nod, then stop and bring a chair, water, and real attention. Respect becomes visible the moment you make room for someone.
ramacharitamanas::1786.insight: It shifts respect from performance to concrete hospitality.

ramacharitamanas::1787.verse_sanskrit: सब बिधि सकल अलंकृत कीन्हीं। मुदित महिप महिदेवन्ह दीन्हीं॥ करत बिनय बहु बिधि नरनाहू। लहेउँ आजु जग जीवन लाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1787.verse_hindi: उन सबको सब प्रकार से (गहनों-कपड़ों से) सजाकर राजा ने प्रसन्न होकर भूदेव ब्राह्मणों को दिया। राजा बहुत तरह से विनती कर रहे हैं कि जगत में मैंने आज ही जीने का लाभ पाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1787.english_translation: He had them adorned in every way and gave them away joyfully to the Brahmins. The king kept bowing in many ways and said, "Today I have found the true benefit of living in the world."
ramacharitamanas::1787.translation_literal: सब बिधि (in every way) / सकल (all) / अलंकृत (adorned) / कीन्हीं (made) / मुदित (joyful) / महिप (the king) / महिदेवन्ह (to the Brahmins) / दीहीं (gave) / करत (doing) / बिनय (humble request) / बहु बिधि (in many ways) / नरनाहू (the king) / लहेउँ (I have found) / आजु (today) / जग (world) / जीवन (living) / लाहू (benefit)
ramacharitamanas::1787.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1787.essence: True gain comes from giving without holding back.
ramacharitamanas::1787.simple_meaning: The king honors the Brahmins with gifts, ornaments, and repeated bows, and feels that serving them is the true value of his life.
ramacharitamanas::1787.simple_insight: Generosity stops feeling like loss when service becomes the measure of a good life.
ramacharitamanas::1787.detailed_meaning: After honoring the gathered sages, the king keeps offering gifts with delight and humility. He dresses them richly, gives them away, and bows again and again. In that moment, giving itself becomes his reward.
ramacharitamanas::1787.modern_relevance: You stay after the ceremony to thank the people who made it possible, even though no one is watching. Something in you knows that recognition is small compared with sincere giving.
ramacharitamanas::1787.insight: It shifts the mind from keeping score to finding fulfillment in service itself.

ramacharitamanas::1788.verse_sanskrit: पाइ असीस महीसु अनंदा। लिए बोलि पुनि जाचक बृंदा॥ कनक बसन मनि हय गय स्यंदन। दिए बूझि रुचि रबिकुलनंदन ॥
ramacharitamanas::1788.verse_hindi: (ब्राह्मणों से) आशीर्वाद पाकर राजा आनंदित हुए। फिर याचकों के समूहों को बुलवा लिया और सबको उनकी रुचि पूछकर सोना, वस्त्र, मणि, घोड़ा, हाथी और रथ (जिसने जो चाहा सो) सूर्यकुल को आनंदित करने वाले दशरथजी ने दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1788.english_translation: After receiving blessings, the king was filled with joy. He then called the groups of petitioners and, asking each what they desired, gave gold, clothes, jewels, horses, elephants, and chariots to the delight of the Solar dynasty's lord.
ramacharitamanas::1788.translation_literal: पाइ (having received) / असीस (blessings) / महीसु (the king) / अनंदा (rejoiced) / लिए (called) / बोलि (having called) / पुनि (again) / जाचक बृंदा (groups of petitioners) / कनक (gold) / बसन (clothes) / मनि (jewels) / हय (horses) / गय (elephants) / स्यंदन (chariots) / दिए (gave) / बूझि (asking) / रुचि (desire) / रबिकुलनंदन (the delight of the Solar dynasty)
ramacharitamanas::1788.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1788.essence: True giving asks what each person needs.
ramacharitamanas::1788.simple_meaning: King Dasharath, happy after receiving blessings, called the beggars and gave each person what they wanted: wealth, clothes, jewels, horses, elephants, and chariots.
ramacharitamanas::1788.simple_insight: Generosity becomes complete when it listens first and gives second.
ramacharitamanas::1788.detailed_meaning: The marriage celebration is underway in Ayodhya. After honoring the Brahmins, Dasharath turns to the petitioners and gives generously according to each person's wish. The scene shows royal abundance, public joy, and the festive overflow surrounding Ram's wedding.
ramacharitamanas::1788.modern_relevance: At a wedding feast, the host notices what each guest actually needs instead of handing out the same gift to everyone. Real generosity pays attention before it gives.
ramacharitamanas::1788.insight: It shifts giving from display to responsiveness.

ramacharitamanas::1789.verse_sanskrit: चले पढ़त गावत गुन गाथा। जय जय जय दिनकर कुल नाथा॥ एहि बिधि राम बिआह उछाहू। सकइ न बरनि सहस मुख जाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1789.verse_hindi: वे सब गुणानुवाद गाते और 'सूर्यकुल के स्वामी की जय हो, जय हो, जय हो' कहते हुए चले। इस प्रकार श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विवाह का उत्सव हुआ, जिन्हें सहस्र मुख हैं, वे शेषजी भी उसका वर्णन नहीं कर सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1789.english_translation: They walked along singing praises of his virtues, crying, 'Victory, victory, victory to the lord of the solar race!' In this way the joy of Ram's wedding unfolded, a joy that even a thousand-mouthed being cannot describe.
ramacharitamanas::1789.translation_literal: चले (went) / पढ़त (reciting) / गावत (singing) / गुन गाथा (praise-stories of virtues) / जय जय जय (victory, victory, victory) / दिनकर कुल नाथा (lord of the solar race)॥ / एहि बिधि (in this way) / राम बिआह (Ram's wedding) / उछाहू (joy, celebration) / सकइ न (cannot) / बरनि (describe) / सहस मुख (thousand mouths) / जाहू (even Shesha) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1789.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1789.essence: Joy around Ram exceeds every attempt to describe it.
ramacharitamanas::1789.simple_meaning: The wedding celebration fills everyone with praise and joy, and its greatness feels beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::1789.simple_insight: Some moments are so full they turn speech into song.
ramacharitamanas::1789.detailed_meaning: The wedding of Ram and Sita is underway in Mithila. People walk away singing Ram's virtues and cheering his name. The scene is overflowing with joy, but this verse mainly paints the atmosphere rather than delivering a new teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1789.modern_relevance: A wedding crowd spills out into the street, still humming the same name, still smiling at nothing and everything. Some happiness is too large to fit into a sentence.
ramacharitamanas::1789.insight: It turns attention from explanation to celebration, showing that some truths are best carried in praise.

ramacharitamanas::1790.verse_sanskrit: बार बार कौसिक चरन सीसु नाइ कह राउ। यह सबु सुखु मुनिराज तव कृपा कटाच्छ पसाउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1790.verse_hindi: बार-बार विश्वामित्रजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर राजा कहते हैं- हे मुनिराज! यह सब सुख आपके ही कृपाकटाक्ष का प्रसाद है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1790.english_translation: Again and again, the king bowed his head to Kaushika’s feet and said, "All this joy is the gift of your grace, O great sage."
ramacharitamanas::1790.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / कौसिक (Kaushika, Vishwamitra) / चरन (feet) / सीसु (head) / नाइ (bowing) / कह (said) / राउ (the king) / यह (this) / सबु (all) / सुखु (joy) / मुनिराज (king of sages) / तव (your) / कृपा (grace) / कटाच्छ (glance) / पसाउ (gift, favor)
ramacharitamanas::1790.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::1790.essence: True joy remembers the hands that made it possible.
ramacharitamanas::1790.simple_meaning: King Dasharath bows repeatedly to Vishwamitra and credits him for all the joy of the wedding, calling it the result of the sage’s gracious glance.
ramacharitamanas::1790.simple_insight: Gratitude deepens joy. The heart sees blessing more clearly when it bows.
ramacharitamanas::1790.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s wedding celebration, Dasharath bows again and again before Vishwamitra. The king’s happiness is overflowing, and he openly says that the whole joy of this moment has come through the sage’s grace.
ramacharitamanas::1790.modern_relevance: After a long ceremony ends perfectly, you thank the person who quietly made it possible. The spotlight may land elsewhere, but your heart knows who held the whole thing together.
ramacharitamanas::1790.insight: It teaches you to name the people whose grace made your success possible.

ramacharitamanas::1791.verse_sanskrit: जनक सनेहु सीलु करतूती। नृपु सब भाँति सराह बिभूती॥ दिन उठि बिदा अवधपति मागा। राखहिं जनकु सहित अनुरागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1791.verse_hindi: राजा दशरथजी जनकजी के स्नेह, शील, करनी और ऐश्वर्य की सब प्रकार से सराहना करते हैं। प्रतिदिन (सबेरे) उठकर अयोध्या नरेश विदा माँगते हैं। पर जनकजी उन्हें प्रेम से रख लेते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1791.english_translation: King Dasharath praises Janak's affection, gentleness, conduct, and splendour in every way. Each morning the lord of Ayodhya asks to depart, but Janak keeps him there with loving warmth.
ramacharitamanas::1791.translation_literal: जनक (Janak) / सनेहु (affection) / सीलु (gentleness, virtue) / करतूती (conduct, deeds) / नृपु (king) / सब भाँति (in every way) / सराह (praises) / बिभूती (splendour, prosperity)॥ / दिन (day) / उठि (rising) / बिदा (leave-taking) / अवधपति (lord of Ayodhya) / मागा (asked) / राखहिं (kept) / जनकु (Janak) / सहित (with) / अनुरागा (loving attachment)॥
ramacharitamanas::1791.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1791.essence: Respect deepens into affection, and departure keeps getting delayed.
ramacharitamanas::1791.simple_meaning: Dasharath admires Janak's character and wealth, and keeps asking to leave, but Janak lovingly continues to host him.
ramacharitamanas::1791.simple_insight: Warm hospitality can turn duty-bound departure into shared affection.
ramacharitamanas::1791.detailed_meaning: After Sita and Ram's marriage, Dasharath stays in Mithila as a honoured guest. He repeatedly asks to return to Ayodhya, but Janak keeps him back with affection. The verse shows two royal households joined not just by marriage, but by mutual respect and love.
ramacharitamanas::1791.modern_relevance: You stand at the door after a wedding weekend, still being fed tea and stories while everyone delays goodbye. The leaving matters, but the warmth matters more.
ramacharitamanas::1791.insight: It shifts attention from formal farewell to the human bond that makes parting difficult.

ramacharitamanas::1792.verse_sanskrit: नित नूतन आदरु अधिकाई। दिन प्रति सहस भाँति पहुनाई॥ नित नव नगर अनंद उछाहू। दसरथ गवनु सोहाइ न काहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1792.verse_hindi: आदर नित्य नया बढ़ता जाता है। प्रतिदिन हजारों प्रकार से मेहमानी होती है। नगर में नित्य नया आनंद और उत्साह रहता है, दशरथजी का जाना किसी को नहीं सुहाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1792.english_translation: Respect grew anew each day. Every day brought a thousand kinds of hospitality. New joy and excitement filled the city each day, and no one liked Dasharath's departure.
ramacharitamanas::1792.translation_literal: नित (constantly) / नूतन (new) / आदरु (respect) / अधिकाई (increased) / दिन प्रति (day by day) / सहस भाँति (in a thousand ways) / पहुनाई (hospitality) / नित (constantly) / नव (new) / नगर (city) / अनंद (joy) / उछाहू (enthusiasm) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / गवनु (departure) / सोहाइ (is pleasing) / न काहू (to no one)
ramacharitamanas::1792.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1792.essence: True welcome makes even leaving feel like loss.
ramacharitamanas::1792.simple_meaning: King Dasharath is honored more and more each day in Mithila. The city keeps celebrating him with endless hospitality, and no one wants him to leave.
ramacharitamanas::1792.simple_insight: Warm welcome can turn a formal visit into a bond nobody wants to break.
ramacharitamanas::1792.detailed_meaning: Dasharath stays in Mithila after the swayamvar, and King Janak’s city keeps showering him with respect and hospitality. Each day brings fresh joy, so the time to depart feels painful for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::1792.modern_relevance: You stay a few extra days at a house where every meal feels like love and every goodbye keeps getting delayed. Leaving starts to feel like breaking a shared heartbeat.
ramacharitamanas::1792.insight: It shows how genuine hospitality can deepen attachment and make departure feel wrong even when it is necessary.

ramacharitamanas::1793.verse_sanskrit: बहुत दिवस बीते एहि भाँती। जनु सनेह रजु बँधे बराती॥ कौसिक सतानंद तब जाई। कहा बिदेह नृपहि समुझाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1793.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार बहुत दिन बीत गए, मानो बाराती स्नेह की रस्सी से बँध गए हैं। तब विश्वामित्रजी और शतानंदजी ने जाकर राजा जनक को समझाकर कहा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1793.english_translation: Many days passed in this way, as if the wedding guests were bound by the rope of affection. Then Vishvamitra and Shatananda went and spoke to King Janaka, explaining the matter.
ramacharitamanas::1793.translation_literal: बहुत दिवस (many days) / बीते (passed) / एहि भाँती (in this way) / जनु (as if) / सनेह (affection) / रजु (rope) / बँधे (bound) / बराती (wedding guests) / कौसिक (Vishvamitra) / सतानंद (Shatananda) / तब (then) / जाई (going) / कहा (spoke) / बिदेह नृपहि (to King Janaka) / समुझाई (explaining)
ramacharitamanas::1793.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1793.essence: Affection can hold people together longer than ceremony itself.
ramacharitamanas::1793.simple_meaning: The wedding guests stayed on for many days, held there by mutual affection. Then Vishvamitra and Shatananda went to Janaka and explained the situation.
ramacharitamanas::1793.simple_insight: Warm bonds can make even delay feel natural.
ramacharitamanas::1793.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the wedding celebrations have stretched on because everyone is reluctant to part. Vishvamitra and Shatananda finally go to Janaka and prepare to move the story forward, showing how affection has softened the whole gathering.
ramacharitamanas::1793.modern_relevance: A house full of relatives stays lively long after the ceremony ends. Nobody wants to be the first to leave, because the connection itself has become the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1793.insight: It frames delay as a sign of shared affection, not inconvenience.

ramacharitamanas::1794.verse_sanskrit: अब दसरथ कहँ आयसु देहू। जद्यपि छाड़ि न सकहु सनेहू॥ भलेहिं नाथ कहि सचिव बोलाए। कहि जय जीव सीस तिन्ह नाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1794.verse_hindi: यद्यपि आप स्नेह (वश उन्हें) नहीं छोड़ सकते, तो भी अब दशरथजी को आज्ञा दीजिए। 'हे नाथ! बहुत अच्छा' कहकर जनकजी ने मंत्रियों को बुलवाया। वे आए और 'जय जीव' कहकर उन्होंने मस्तक नवाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1794.english_translation: Though you cannot bear to part from them, now give King Dasharatha his leave. Janaka said, "Very well, my lord," and called his ministers. They came and bowed their heads, saying, "Victory and long life."
ramacharitamanas::1794.translation_literal: अब (now) / दसरथ कहँ (to Dasharatha) / आयसु (permission, leave) / देहू (give) / जद्यपि (although) / छाड़ि (to leave) / न सकहु (you cannot) / सनेहू (affection) / भलेहिं (well indeed) / नाथ (lord) / कहि (saying) / सचिव (ministers) / बोलाए (called) / कहि (saying) / जय जीव (victory and long life) / सीस (heads) / तिन्ह (they) / नाए (bowed)
ramacharitamanas::1794.speaker: Janaka
ramacharitamanas::1794.essence: Affection need not erase proper farewell.
ramacharitamanas::1794.simple_meaning: Janaka asks that Dasharatha be formally given permission to depart, even though affection makes parting hard. He then calls his ministers, who come and bow respectfully.
ramacharitamanas::1794.simple_insight: Even deep affection still makes room for proper conduct and respectful farewell.
ramacharitamanas::1794.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the wedding celebrations are ending and the guests are preparing to leave. Janaka, still moved by affection, asks that Dasharatha be formally released. He then summons his ministers, and the court responds with honor and ceremony.
ramacharitamanas::1794.modern_relevance: You know the moment when a long, warm visit is ending and nobody wants to say goodbye. Still, someone has to make the departure graceful, not awkward.
ramacharitamanas::1794.insight: It shows how tenderness and formality can coexist, so separation is handled with dignity instead of clinging.

ramacharitamanas::1795.verse_sanskrit: अवधनाथु चाहत चलन भीतर करहु जनाउ। भए प्रेमबस सचिव सुनि बिप्र सभासद राउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1795.verse_hindi: (जनकजी ने कहा-) अयोध्यानाथ चलना चाहते हैं, भीतर (रनिवास में) खबर कर दो। यह सुनकर मंत्री, ब्राह्मण, सभासद और राजा जनक भी प्रेम के वश हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1795.english_translation: Janak said, "The lord of Ayodhya wants to depart; go and inform the inner quarters." Hearing this, the ministers, priests, courtiers, and King Janak himself were overcome by love.
ramacharitamanas::1795.translation_literal: अवधनाथु (the lord of Ayodhya) / चाहत (wants) / चलन (to depart) / भीतर (inside) / करहु (do) / जनाउ (inform) / भए (became) / प्रेमबस (under the power of love) / सचिव (ministers) / सुनि (hearing) / बिप्र (priests) / सभासद (courtiers) / राउ (king)
ramacharitamanas::1795.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1795.essence: Love remains present even as departure begins.
ramacharitamanas::1795.simple_meaning: Janak asks that Rama's departure be announced inside the palace. The news moves everyone so deeply that even Janak and his court are overcome with love.
ramacharitamanas::1795.simple_insight: Love can make parting painful without making it wrong.
ramacharitamanas::1795.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the wedding celebration is ending and the moment of separation has arrived. Janak sends word that Rama wants to leave, and the whole court — ministers, priests, nobles, and Janak himself — is softened by love.
ramacharitamanas::1795.modern_relevance: The guest is already at the door with his bag in hand, and no one wants the evening to end. Everyone smiles, but the room has gone quiet because goodbye has already begun.
ramacharitamanas::1795.insight: It shows how devotion deepens even ordinary parting, turning a departure into a shared ache.

ramacharitamanas::1796.verse_sanskrit: पुरबासी सुनि चलिहि बराता। बूझत बिकल परस्पर बाता॥ सत्य गवनु सुनि सब बिलखाने। मनहुँ साँझ सरसिज सकुचाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::1796.verse_hindi: जनकपुरवासियों ने सुना कि बारात जाएगी, तब वे व्याकुल होकर एक-दूसरे से बात पूछने लगे। जाना सत्य है, यह सुनकर सब ऐसे उदास हो गए मानो संध्या के समय कमल सकुचा गए हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1796.english_translation: Hearing that the wedding procession would leave, the people of Janakpur grew restless and asked each other what was happening. When they heard the departure was certain, everyone became sorrowful, like lotuses shrinking at dusk.
ramacharitamanas::1796.translation_literal: पुरबासी (city-dwellers) / सुनि (hearing) / चलिहि (will depart) / बराता (wedding procession) / बूझत (asking) / बिकल (agitated) / परस्पर (mutually, one another) / बाता (words, matter) ॥ सत्य (true) / गवनु (departure) / सुनि (hearing) / सब (all) / बिलखाने (became sorrowful) / मनहुँ (as if) / साँझ (evening) / सरसिज (lotuses) / सकुचाने (shrunk, closed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1796.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1796.essence: Even happy news can sting when separation is certain.
ramacharitamanas::1796.simple_meaning: The people of Janakpur hear that the wedding procession is leaving, and they become anxious and sad. The certainty of departure makes them feel the loss before it happens.
ramacharitamanas::1796.simple_insight: Love makes even a joyful departure feel like a wound.
ramacharitamanas::1796.detailed_meaning: Janakpur has just learned that the wedding procession will leave. The city people, already attached to the moment, turn restless and question one another. When the departure becomes certain, their joy collapses into grief.
ramacharitamanas::1796.modern_relevance: You hear the flight is booked, and the house goes quiet. The visit is still happening, but everyone already feels the ending.
ramacharitamanas::1796.insight: It shows how attachment turns anticipation into sorrow before the event even arrives.

ramacharitamanas::1797.verse_sanskrit: जहँ जहँ आवत बसे बराती। तहँ तहँ सिद्ध चला बहु भाँती॥ बिबिध भाँति मेवा पकवाना। भोजन साजु न जाइ बखाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1797.verse_hindi: आते समय जहाँ-जहाँ बाराती ठहरे थे, वहाँ-वहाँ बहुत प्रकार का सीधा (रसोई का सामान) भेजा गया। अनेकों प्रकार के मेवे, पकवान और भोजन की सामग्री जो बखानी नहीं जा सकती- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1797.english_translation: Wherever the wedding party had stayed, food and supplies were sent there in many ways. Countless kinds of sweets, cooked dishes, and feast items cannot be described.
ramacharitamanas::1797.translation_literal: जहँ जहँ (wherever) / आवत (coming) / बसे (stayed) / बराती (wedding guests) / तहँ तहँ (there, there) / सिद्ध (supplies, provisions) / चला (sent) / बहु भाँती (in many ways)॥ / बिबिध (various) / भाँति (kinds) / मेवा (dry fruits, sweets) / पकवाना (cooked foods) / भोजन (meal, food) / साजु (arrangement, supplies) / न जाइ (cannot be) / बखाना (described) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1797.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1797.simple_meaning: Every place the wedding guests stopped received food and supplies. The arrangements were so abundant that no one could fully describe them.
ramacharitamanas::1797.simple_insight: Generosity can be so complete that it turns into a blessing everyone remembers.
ramacharitamanas::1797.detailed_meaning: The wedding procession has reached Janakpur, and the city is pouring out hospitality. Wherever the guests have rested, provisions are sent in abundance. This verse is part of the celebration, showing the scale of welcome before the marriage itself.
ramacharitamanas::1797.modern_relevance: A house fills with relatives before a wedding, and someone keeps bringing more trays, more mats, more water, more care. The joy is not in show — it is in making every guest feel held.
ramacharitamanas::1797.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the sacredness of generous preparation.

ramacharitamanas::1798.verse_sanskrit: भरि भरि बसहँ अपार कहारा। पठईं जनक अनेक सुसारा॥ तुरग लाख रथ सहस पचीसा। सकल सँवारे नख अरु सीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1798.verse_hindi: अनगिनत बैलों और कहारों पर भर-भरकर (लाद-लादकर) भेजी गई। साथ ही जनकजी ने अनेकों सुंदर शय्याएँ (पलंग) भेजीं। एक लाख घोड़े और पचीस हजार रथ सब नख से शिखा तक (ऊपर से नीचे तक) सजाए हुए, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1798.english_translation: Countless bearers and carriers were loaded to the brim and sent by Janak. One hundred thousand horses and twenty-five thousand chariots were all made ready, polished from hoof to head.
ramacharitamanas::1798.translation_literal: भरि भरि (to the brim) / बसहँ (bearers) / अपार (countless) / कहारा (carriers) / पठईं (sent) / जनक (Janak) / अनेक (many) / सुसारा (beautiful beds) / तुरग (horses) / लाख (hundred thousand) / रथ (chariots) / सहस (thousand) / पचीसा (twenty-five thousand) / सकल (all) / सँवारे (made ready, adorned) / नख (hoof) / अरु (and) / सीसा (head)
ramacharitamanas::1798.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1798.essence: Grandeur is only the visible edge of careful preparation.
ramacharitamanas::1798.simple_meaning: Janak sends out huge quantities of transport, beds, horses, and chariots, all fully prepared for the wedding procession.
ramacharitamanas::1798.simple_insight: Great occasions are carried by unseen labor. Splendor is built from careful preparation.
ramacharitamanas::1798.detailed_meaning: Janak’s court is preparing the wedding procession for Ram and Sita. After the news spreads through Janakpur, this verse lists the vast, carefully arranged transport and supplies being sent out, showing the scale and honor of the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1798.modern_relevance: A wedding hall looks effortless only because dozens of people have worked all night. The beauty you see is the result of meticulous, invisible care.
ramacharitamanas::1798.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle to the disciplined preparation that makes the spectacle possible.

ramacharitamanas::1799.verse_sanskrit: मत्त सहस दस सिंधुर साजे। जिन्हहि देखि दिसिकुंजर लाजे॥ कनक बसन मनि भरि भरि जाना। महिषीं धेनु बस्तु बिधि नाना ॥ दाइज अमित न सकिअ कहि दीन्ह बिदेहँ बहोरि। जो अवलोकत लोकपति लोक संपदा थोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1799.verse_hindi: दस हजार सजे हुए मतवाले हाथी, जिन्हें देखकर दिशाओं के हाथी भी लजा जाते हैं, गाड़ियों में भर-भरकर सोना, वस्त्र और रत्न (जवाहरात) और भैंस, गाय तथा और भी नाना प्रकार की चीजें दीं ॥ (इस प्रकार) जनकजी ने फिर से अपरिमित दहेज दिया, जो कहा नहीं जा सकता और जिसे देखकर लोकपालों के लोकों की सम्पदा भी थोड़ी जान पड़ती थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1799.english_translation: Ten thousand decorated elephants were prepared; even elephants of the directions felt ashamed to see them. Carts were filled again and again with gold, cloth, and jewels, and with buffaloes, cows, and many other things. Janak gave limitless gifts beyond speech; the wealth of the world seemed small beside what he sent.
ramacharitamanas::1799.translation_literal: मत्त (intoxicated / spirited) / सहस दस (ten thousand) / सिंधुर (elephants) / साजे (decorated, prepared) / जिन्हहि (whom) / देखि (seeing) / दिसिकुंजर (elephants of the directions) / लाजे (felt ashamed) / कनक (gold) / बसन (cloth) / मनि (jewels) / भरि भरि (again and again, full to the brim) / जाना (carts, loads) / महिषीं (buffaloes) / धेनु (cows) / बस्तु (things, goods) / बिधि नाना (many kinds) / दाइज (dowry, gifts) / अमित (immeasurable) / न सकिअ (cannot) / कहि (say, describe) / दीन्ह (gave) / बिदेहँ (Janak of Videha) / बहोरि (again) / जो (which) / अवलोकत (seeing) / लोकपति (lords of the worlds) / लोक (worlds) / संपदा (wealth, splendor) / थोरि (small, lesser)
ramacharitamanas::1799.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1799.essence: True giving feels infinite because it is unstinting.
ramacharitamanas::1799.simple_meaning: Janak sends an enormous bridal gift with the wedding procession: elephants, gold, cloth, jewels, cattle, and countless other riches. The gift is so vast that even heavenly wealth seems small beside it.
ramacharitamanas::1799.simple_insight: Some generosity is so complete it makes abundance itself feel modest.
ramacharitamanas::1799.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, the wedding preparations for Ram and Sita are overflowing. Janak sends carts of treasure, animals, and gifts to Ayodhya. The verse pauses on the sheer scale of his offering before the procession moves on.
ramacharitamanas::1799.modern_relevance: You pack a moving truck for someone you love and keep adding more than seems necessary. The point is not display. It is the fullness of a heart that gives without measuring.
ramacharitamanas::1799.insight: It shifts attention from the objects given to the abundance of the giver's heart.

ramacharitamanas::1800.verse_sanskrit: सबु समाजु एहि भाँति बनाई। जनक अवधपुर दीन्ह पठाई॥ चलिहि बरात सुनत सब रानीं। बिकल मीनगन जनु लघु पानीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1800.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार सब सामान सजाकर राजा जनक ने अयोध्यापुरी को भेज दिया। बारात चलेगी, यह सुनते ही सब रानियाँ ऐसी विकल हो गईं, मानो थोड़े जल में मछलियाँ छटपटा रही हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::1800.english_translation: In this way, the entire wedding procession was prepared and sent to Ayodhya by King Janak. Hearing that the procession would set out, all the queens became agitated like fish in shallow water.
ramacharitamanas::1800.translation_literal: सबु (all) / समाजु (assembly, entire arrangement) / एहि भाँति (in this manner) / बनाई (having made ready) / जनक (Janak) / अवधपुर (to Ayodhya city) / दीन्ह (gave, sent) / पठाई (having sent) / चलिहि (will depart) / बरात (wedding procession) / सुनत (hearing) / सब (all) / रानीं (queens) / बिकल (agitated, distressed) / मीनगन (fish-groups) / जनु (as if) / लघु (little, shallow) / पानीं (water)
ramacharitamanas::1800.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1800.essence: Even a joyful departure can make the heart tremble.
ramacharitamanas::1800.simple_meaning: Janak sends the wedding procession to Ayodhya, and the queens are overwhelmed with emotion when they hear it is about to leave.
ramacharitamanas::1800.simple_insight: Love can be so intense that even a joyful departure feels like loss.
ramacharitamanas::1800.detailed_meaning: Janak has finished preparing the wedding gifts and procession for Ayodhya. As news spreads that the barat will depart, the queens of Mithila are overcome with grief and longing. The scene shows how celebration and separation arrive together.
ramacharitamanas::1800.modern_relevance: You watch your daughter leave after the wedding, and the house suddenly feels too quiet. Joy is there, but it hurts too.
ramacharitamanas::1800.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to the emotional cost of transition.

ramacharitamanas::1801.verse_sanskrit: पुनि पुनि सीय गोद करि लेहीं। देह असीस सिखावनु देहीं॥ होएहु संतत पियहि पिआरी। चिरु अहिबात असीस हमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1801.verse_hindi: वे बार-बार सीताजी को गोद कर लेती हैं और आशीर्वाद देकर सिखावन देती हैं- तुम सदा अपने पति की प्यारी होओ, तुम्हारा सोहाग अचल हो, हमारी यही आशीष है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1801.english_translation: They repeatedly take Sita into their laps, blessing and instructing her: “May you always be dear to your husband. May your married bond remain unbroken. This is our blessing.”
ramacharitamanas::1801.translation_literal: पुनि पुनि (again and again) / सीय (Sita) / गोद करि (having taken into the lap) / लेहीं (they take) / देह (giving) / असीस (blessings) / सिखावनु (instruction) / देहीं (they give) / होएहु (may you be) / संतत (always) / पियहि (to the husband) / पिआरी (dear) / चिरु (long-lasting) / अहिबात (married bond) / असीस (blessing) / हमारी (our)
ramacharitamanas::1801.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1801.essence: Affection can teach the shape of a life.
ramacharitamanas::1801.simple_meaning: The women lovingly bless Sita and teach her the ideals expected of a married woman in their world.
ramacharitamanas::1801.simple_insight: Love can also carry guidance, especially when it comes from those who want your life to flourish.
ramacharitamanas::1801.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s palace, the women gather around Sita before the wedding procession. They hold her close, bless her, and gently teach her the duties and blessings of married life. This is part of the larger farewell scene before her departure.
ramacharitamanas::1801.modern_relevance: At a family gathering before a wedding, older relatives pull the bride close, adjust her veil, and whisper advice she may remember for years. Care and guidance arrive together.
ramacharitamanas::1801.insight: It shows how elders pass on values through tenderness, not just instruction.

ramacharitamanas::1802.verse_sanskrit: सासु ससुर गुर सेवा करेहू। पति रुख लखि आयसु अनुसरेहू॥ अति सनेह बस सखीं सयानी। नारि धरम सिखवहिं मृदु बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1802.verse_hindi: सास, ससुर और गुरु की सेवा करना। पति का रुख देखकर उनकी आज्ञा का पालन करना। सयानी सखियाँ अत्यन्त स्नेह के वश कोमल वाणी से स्त्रियों के धर्म सिखलाती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1802.english_translation: Serve your mother-in-law, father-in-law, and teacher. Read your husband's mood and follow his wishes. Wise friends, moved by affection, gently teach women their duty in soft words.
ramacharitamanas::1802.translation_literal: सासु (mother-in-law) / ससुर (father-in-law) / गुर (teacher) / सेवा (service) / करेहू (do) / पति (husband) / रुख (inclination) / लखि (seeing) / आयसु (order) / अनुसरेहू (follow) / अति (very) / सनेह (affection) / बस (under the sway of) / सखीं (friends) / सयानी (wise) / नारि धरम (women's duty) / सिखवहिं (teach) / मृदु (soft) / बानी (speech)
ramacharitamanas::1802.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1802.essence: Family duty begins with service, attentiveness, and gentle speech.
ramacharitamanas::1802.simple_meaning: Women are advised to serve elders, notice their husband's wishes, and learn their role through gentle guidance from wise friends.
ramacharitamanas::1802.simple_insight: Care and respect can be taught without harshness.
ramacharitamanas::1802.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the women are preparing Sita for marriage and married life. The elders and friends give her practical guidance about family service, attentiveness, and gentle conduct, showing the social ideal expected of a bride.
ramacharitamanas::1802.modern_relevance: Before a wedding, an older aunt pulls you aside and says, 'Learn the family, watch the room, speak softly.' The verse carries that same lived advice about entering a new home with care.
ramacharitamanas::1802.insight: It shifts attention from personal preference to respectful participation in family life.

ramacharitamanas::1803.verse_sanskrit: सादर सकल कुअँरि समुझाईं। रानिन्ह बार बार उर लाईं॥ बहुरि बहुरि भेटहिं महतारीं। कहहिं बिरंचि रचीं कत नारीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1803.verse_hindi: आदर के साथ सब पुत्रियों को (स्त्रियों के धर्म) समझाकर रानियों ने बार-बार उन्हें हृदय से लगाया। माताएँ फिर-फिर भेंटती और कहती हैं कि ब्रह्मा ने स्त्री जाति को क्यों रचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1803.english_translation: With respect, the queens explained everything to the brides and embraced them again and again. The mothers came again and again to meet them, saying, "Why did Brahma create women at all?"
ramacharitamanas::1803.translation_literal: सादर (with respect) / सकल (all) / कुअँरि (maidens, brides) / समुझाईं (explained) / रानिन्ह (by the queens) / बार बार (again and again) / उर (to the chest/heart) / लाईं (brought, embraced) ॥ / बहुरि बहुरि (again and again) / भेटहिं (they meet) / महतारीं (the mothers) / कहहिं (they say) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / रचीं (created) / कत (why) / नारीं (women) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1803.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1803.essence: Parting is softened by love, but love cannot stop the ache.
ramacharitamanas::1803.simple_meaning: The queens lovingly instruct the brides and keep embracing them, while the mothers keep returning to see them and speak in sorrowful wonder about the lot of women.
ramacharitamanas::1803.simple_insight: Love can carry grief, pride, and tenderness all at once.
ramacharitamanas::1803.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, the brides are being prepared to leave. The queens explain a woman’s duties with care, then keep pulling the girls close. Their mothers cannot stop returning, overwhelmed by affection and the pain of separation.
ramacharitamanas::1803.modern_relevance: A mother keeps smoothing her daughter's hair before the wedding procession leaves. She smiles, gives advice, then turns away and comes back again because letting go hurts more than she can say.
ramacharitamanas::1803.insight: It shows how farewell becomes a ritual of repeated embrace and repeated release.

ramacharitamanas::1804.verse_sanskrit: तेहि अवसर भाइन्ह सहित रामु भानु कुल केतु। चले जनक मंदिर मुदित बिदा करावन हेतु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1804.verse_hindi: उसी समय सूर्यवंश के पताका स्वरूप श्री रामचन्द्रजी भाइयों सहित प्रसन्न होकर विदा कराने के लिए जनकजी के महल को चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1804.english_translation: At that moment, Ram, the banner of the solar dynasty, went with his brothers to Janak's palace, pleased to take leave.
ramacharitamanas::1804.translation_literal: तेहि अवसर (at that time) / भाइन्ह सहित (with the brothers) / रामु (Ram) / भानु कुल केतु (banner of the solar dynasty) / चले (went) / जनक मंदिर (Janak's palace) / मुदित (pleased) / बिदा करावन हेतु (for the purpose of taking leave)
ramacharitamanas::1804.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1804.essence: Leave with joy, even at the moment of departure.
ramacharitamanas::1804.simple_meaning: Ram goes with his brothers to Janak's palace to take leave, and he does so gladly.
ramacharitamanas::1804.simple_insight: Even a farewell can be graceful when the heart is steady.
ramacharitamanas::1804.detailed_meaning: The wedding festivities are ending, and Ram leaves with Lakshman and the other brothers to visit Janak's palace for farewell. The scene simply moves the story forward, showing the family preparing to depart.
ramacharitamanas::1804.modern_relevance: The event is over, the guests are still chatting, and you walk back in to say goodbye properly. Small departures still matter when they are done with grace.
ramacharitamanas::1804.insight: It keeps attention on the dignity of transition, not on drama.

ramacharitamanas::1805.verse_sanskrit: चारिउ भाइ सुभायँ सुहाए। नगर नारि नर देखन धाए॥ कोउ कह चलन चहत हहिं आजू। कीन्ह बिदेह बिदा कर साजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1805.verse_hindi: स्वभाव से ही सुंदर चारों भाइयों को देखने के लिए नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष दौड़े। कोई कहता है- आज ये जाना चाहते हैं। विदेह ने विदाई का सब सामान तैयार कर लिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1805.english_translation: The four brothers were naturally beautiful. Men and women in the city rushed out to see them. Some said, “Today they are leaving.” “King Janaka has arranged the farewell.”
ramacharitamanas::1805.translation_literal: चारिउ (four) / भाइ (brothers) / सुभायँ (by nature) / सुहाए (beautiful) / नगर (city) / नारि (women) / नर (men) / देखन (to see) / धाए (ran) / कोउ (someone) / कह (says) / चलन (to leave) / चहत (wanting) / हहिं (are) / आजू (today) / कीन्ह (made) / बिदेह (Janaka) / बिदा (farewell) / कर साजू (arrangement made)
ramacharitamanas::1805.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1805.essence: Their beauty makes the whole city stop and look.
ramacharitamanas::1805.simple_meaning: The four brothers are so beautiful that the whole city rushes out to see them and talk about their departure.
ramacharitamanas::1805.simple_insight: Some arrivals are so radiant they turn a city into one shared moment of wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1805.detailed_meaning: The people of Mithila have gathered around Janaka's palace for Ram's farewell. When the four brothers appear, their beauty draws men and women into the streets, and the city buzzes with excited guesses about their departure.
ramacharitamanas::1805.modern_relevance: You catch sight of a family stepping out of a car at a wedding, and everyone on the street turns to look. Some presences need no announcement; they draw attention by their very nature.
ramacharitamanas::1805.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the living presence that makes the event unforgettable.

ramacharitamanas::1806.verse_sanskrit: लेहु नयन भरि रूप निहारी। प्रिय पाहुने भूप सुत चारी॥ को जानै केहिं सुकृत सयानी। नयन अतिथि कीन्हे बिधि आनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1806.verse_hindi: राजा के चारों पुत्र, इन प्यारे मेहमानों के (मनोहर) रूप को नेत्र भरकर देख लो। हे सयानी! कौन जाने, किस पुण्य से विधाता ने इन्हें यहाँ लाकर हमारे नेत्रों का अतिथि किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1806.english_translation: Look at the beauty with full eyes, dear guests, the four sons of the king. Wise lady, who knows by what merit Fate has brought them here and made them the guests of our eyes?
ramacharitamanas::1806.translation_literal: लेहु (take) / नयन (eyes) / भरि (full) / रूप (beauty, form) / निहारी (having seen) / प्रिय (dear) / पाहुने (guests) / भूप सुत (king's sons) / चारी (four) / को (who) / जानै (knows) / केहिं (by what) / सुकृत (merit, good deed) / सयानी (wise woman) / नयन (eyes) / अतिथि (guest) / कीन्हे (made) / बिधि (Fate) / आनी (having brought)
ramacharitamanas::1806.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1806.essence: Beauty has arrived as a guest, and the eyes are blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1806.simple_meaning: The women of Mithila are told to look fully at Ram and his brothers, and to wonder what merit brought such beauty to their sight.
ramacharitamanas::1806.simple_insight: Some encounters feel like a gift you did nothing to deserve.
ramacharitamanas::1806.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, Bharat, and Shatrughna are walking into Janak’s palace after the swayamvar. The women of Mithila stop and stare, struck by their beauty. The verse pauses the scene to frame the brothers as rare guests sent by fate.
ramacharitamanas::1806.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone entering a room and the whole mood changes. Before anyone speaks, you already know something precious has arrived.
ramacharitamanas::1806.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary seeing to reverent noticing.

ramacharitamanas::1807.verse_sanskrit: मरनसीलु जिमि पाव पिऊषा। सुरतरु लहै जनम कर भूखा॥ पाव नार की हरिपदु जैसें। इन्ह कर दरसनु हम कहँ तैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1807.verse_hindi: मरने वाला जिस तरह अमृत पा जाए, जन्म का भूखा कल्पवृक्ष पा जाए और नरक में रहने वाला (या नरक के योग्य) जीव जैसे भगवान के परमपद को प्राप्त हो जाए, हमारे लिए इनके दर्शन वैसे ही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1807.english_translation: For the dying, it is like nectar; for the hungry, like the wish-fulfilling tree; for one fit for the lower realm, like reaching the supreme abode. For us, seeing them is exactly like that.
ramacharitamanas::1807.translation_literal: मरनसीलु (dying one) / जिमि (like) / पाव (gets) / पिऊषा (nectar) / सुरतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / लहै (gets) / जनम कर भूखा (hungry for birth) / पाव (gets) / नार की (of the lower realm) / हरिपदु (the supreme abode of Hari) / जैसें (as) / इन्ह कर (of these) / दरसनु (seeing) / हम कहँ (for us) / तैसें (like that)
ramacharitamanas::1807.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1807.essence: Ram's presence feels like rescue to every kind of longing.
ramacharitamanas::1807.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram and his brothers feels like receiving nectar, a wish-fulfilling tree, and the highest refuge all at once.
ramacharitamanas::1807.simple_insight: Some meetings are so precious they feel like a rescue.
ramacharitamanas::1807.detailed_meaning: The four brothers have entered Mithila, and the city has rushed out just to see them. The sight is so overwhelming that the speaker says it is like nectar for the dying and the highest refuge for the fallen.
ramacharitamanas::1807.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone who changes the whole room — and suddenly your tiredness, hunger, and worry all loosen at once.
ramacharitamanas::1807.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary admiration to the sense that true presence can restore a person completely.

ramacharitamanas::1808.verse_sanskrit: निरखि राम सोभा उर धरहू। निज मन फनि मूरति मनि करहू॥ एहि बिधि सबहि नयन फलु देता। गए कुअँर सब राज निकेता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1808.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की शोभा को निरखकर हृदय में धर लो। अपने मन को साँप और इनकी मूर्ति को मणि बना लो। इस प्रकार सबको नेत्रों का फल देते हुए सब राजकुमार राजमहल में गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1808.english_translation: Keep Ram's beauty in your heart. Make your mind the serpent and his image the jewel. In this way, giving everyone's eyes their reward, the princes went to the royal palace.
ramacharitamanas::1808.translation_literal: निरखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / सोभा (beauty, splendour) / उर (heart) / धरहू (place, hold) / निज (own) / मन (mind) / फनि (serpent) / मूरति (form, image) / मनि (jewel) / करहू (make) / एहि बिधि (in this way) / सबहि (to everyone) / नयन (eyes) / फलु (fruit, reward) / देता (giving) / गए (went) / कुअँर (princes) / सब (all) / राज निकेता (royal palace)
ramacharitamanas::1808.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1808.essence: Beauty should be held inwardly, not just glanced at and forgotten.
ramacharitamanas::1808.simple_meaning: Hold Ram's beauty in your heart and let your mind become a fitting vessel for it. The princes then go to the palace after blessing everyone with their sight.
