ramacharitamanas::1808.simple_insight: There is a quiet joy in receiving beauty fully instead of rushing past it.
ramacharitamanas::1808.detailed_meaning: At King Janak's palace in Mithila, the four princes enter like a blessing. The women of the inner quarters urge everyone to drink in Ram's beauty, and the scene becomes one of shared wonder before the princes move on to the royal residence.
ramacharitamanas::1808.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone who changes the mood of the whole room, and everyone stops talking for a second. Some moments are meant to be taken in, not merely passed through.
ramacharitamanas::1808.insight: It trains attention to receive beauty with reverence before moving on.

ramacharitamanas::1809.verse_sanskrit: रूप सिंधु सब बंधु लखि हरषि उठा रनिवासु। करहिं निछावरि आरती महा मुदित मन सासु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1809.verse_hindi: रूप के समुद्र सब भाइयों को देखकर सारा रनिवास हर्षित हो उठा। सासुएँ महान प्रसन्न मन से निछावर और आरती करती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1809.english_translation: Seeing the ocean of beauty in all the brothers, the whole women’s quarters burst into joy. The mothers, delighted, offered lamps and waved blessings with glad hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1809.translation_literal: रूप (beauty/form) / सिंधु (ocean) / सब (all) / बंधु (brothers) / लखि (seeing) / हरषि (rejoiced) / उठा (rose up) / रनिवासु (women’s quarters) / करहिं (do) / निछावरि (offering) / आरती (lamp-waving worship) / महा (greatly) / मुदित (delighted) / मन (mind/heart) / सासु (mothers/in-laws)
ramacharitamanas::1809.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1809.essence: Beauty becomes sacred when it is met with devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1809.simple_meaning: The royal household is overjoyed when it sees Ram and his brothers. The mothers respond with loving worship and blessings.
ramacharitamanas::1809.simple_insight: Joy deepens when beauty is met with reverence, not just admiration.
ramacharitamanas::1809.detailed_meaning: Ram and his brothers have entered the royal house in Ayodhya. Their beauty fills everyone with delight, and the women’s quarters responds at once. The mothers do not merely look; they honor the moment with lamps and blessings.
ramacharitamanas::1809.modern_relevance: A family gathers at the doorway after a long separation. Before anyone speaks, someone lights a lamp, someone smiles through tears, and the whole room softens into gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::1809.insight: It shifts attention from passive seeing to active welcome and blessing.

ramacharitamanas::1810.verse_sanskrit: देखि राम छबि अति अनुरागीं। प्रेमबिबस पुनि पुनि पद लागीं॥ रही न लाज प्रीति उर छाई। सहज सनेहु बरनि किमि जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1810.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की छबि देखकर वे प्रेम में अत्यन्त मग्न हो गईं और प्रेम के विशेष वश होकर बार-बार चरणों लगीं। हृदय में प्रीति छा गई, इससे लज्जा नहीं रह गई। उनके स्वाभाविक स्नेह का वर्णन किस तरह किया जा सकता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1810.english_translation: Seeing Ram's beauty, they became utterly absorbed in love. Overcome by love, they fell at his feet again and again. Shame disappeared as affection filled the heart. How can such natural tenderness be described?
ramacharitamanas::1810.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / छबि (beauty, radiance) / अति (very) / अनुरागीं (deeply loving, absorbed in love) / प्रेमबिबस (overpowered by love) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / पद (feet) / लागीं (they fell at, touched) / रही (remained) / न (not) / लाज (shame, reserve) / प्रीति (affection, love) / उर (heart) / छाई (spread, filled) / सहज (natural) / सनेहु (affection, tenderness) / बरनि (to describe) / किमि (how) / जाई (can it be done)
ramacharitamanas::1810.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1810.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram's beauty, the women are swept into loving devotion. Their affection becomes so natural and complete that self-consciousness disappears.
ramacharitamanas::1810.simple_insight: Love can be so full that hesitation falls away on its own.
ramacharitamanas::1810.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the royal women behold Ram and his brothers after the wedding gathering. Ram's beauty overwhelms them, and even their social reserve melts into repeated acts of reverence. The scene pauses to show how love itself erases shame.
ramacharitamanas::1810.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence makes you forget to perform. The careful mask drops, and what remains is simple, unguarded warmth.
ramacharitamanas::1810.insight: It shifts attention from social restraint to spontaneous reverence when the heart is fully moved.

ramacharitamanas::1811.verse_sanskrit: भाइन्ह सहित उबटि अन्हवाए। छरस असन अति हेतु जेवाँए॥ बोले रामु सुअवसरु जानी। सील सनेह सकुचमय बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1811.verse_hindi: उन्होंने भाइयों सहित श्री रामजी को उबटन करके स्नान कराया और बड़े प्रेम से षट्रस भोजन कराया। सुअवसर जानकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी शील, स्नेह और संकोचभरी वाणी बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1811.english_translation: They anointed and bathed Ram and his brothers, then lovingly served a six-flavoured meal. Ram, seeing the right moment, spoke with gentle, affectionate modesty.
ramacharitamanas::1811.translation_literal: भाइन्ह सहित (with the brothers) / उबटि (anointed with oil and paste) / अन्हवाए (bathed) / छरस (six-flavoured) / असन (meal) / अति हेतु (with great love) / जेवाँए (served food) / बोले (spoke) / रामु (Ram) / सुअवसरु (the right occasion) / जानी (having known) / सील (gentleness/modesty) / सनेह (affection) / सकुचमय (full of modesty) / बानी (speech)
ramacharitamanas::1811.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1811.essence: Grace is proven by humility, not display.
ramacharitamanas::1811.simple_meaning: The household welcomes Ram and his brothers with bathing, food, and loving care. Ram then speaks at the proper moment with gentle humility.
ramacharitamanas::1811.simple_insight: Even in honor, Ram stays modest. True grace does not need to announce itself.
ramacharitamanas::1811.detailed_meaning: In the royal household, Ram and his brothers are treated with loving ceremony: anointed, bathed, and served a rich meal. Then Ram, perfectly aware of the moment, answers with soft, respectful words. The scene shows his natural gentleness.
ramacharitamanas::1811.modern_relevance: A family has gone all out for a guest, and the most impressive person in the room still speaks softly, thanks everyone, and never acts entitled.
ramacharitamanas::1811.insight: It teaches you to receive honor without losing humility, and to speak only when the moment is right.

ramacharitamanas::1812.verse_sanskrit: राउ अवधपुर चहत सिधाए। बिदा होन हम इहाँ पठाए॥ मातु मुदित मन आयसु देहू। बालक जानि करब नित नेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1812.verse_hindi: महाराज अयोध्यापुरी को चलाना चाहते हैं, उन्होंने हमें विदा होने के लिए यहाँ भेजा है। हे माता! प्रसन्न मन से आज्ञा दीजिए और हमें अपने बालक जानकर सदा स्नेह बनाए रखिएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1812.english_translation: The king of Ayodhya wants to depart. He has sent us here to take leave. Mother, grant your blessing with a glad heart and keep loving us as your children.
ramacharitamanas::1812.translation_literal: राउ (the king) / अवधपुर (Ayodhya city) / चहत (wants) / सिधाए (to depart) / बिदा (farewell) / होन (to be) / हम (we) / इहाँ (here) / पठाए (sent) / मातु (mother) / मुदित (glad) / मन (mind) / आयसु (permission/blessing) / देहू (give) / बालक (children) / जानि (knowing as) / करब (will do) / नित (always) / नेहू (affection)
ramacharitamanas::1812.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1812.essence: Even departure can ask for blessing and keep affection alive.
ramacharitamanas::1812.simple_meaning: The king’s party is preparing to leave, and they ask the mothers to bless them and keep loving them like children.
ramacharitamanas::1812.simple_insight: Love can be humble and formal at the same time; asking for blessing is its own kind of closeness.
ramacharitamanas::1812.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the royal women are being told that the king wants to depart and the visitors have come to take leave. They ask the mothers to bless them gladly and to continue loving them as children, setting up the emotional break that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1812.modern_relevance: You stand at the door after a family visit, shoes on, bags in hand, not wanting the moment to end. The hardest goodbye is the one that still asks for blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1812.insight: It shifts farewell from a cold exit into a sacred exchange of respect, blessing, and ongoing care.

ramacharitamanas::1813.verse_sanskrit: सुनत बचन बिलखेउ रनिवासू। बोलि न सकहिं प्रेमबस सासू॥ हृदयँ लगाई कुअँरि सब लीन्ही। पतिन्ह सौंपि बिनती अति कीन्ही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1813.verse_hindi: इन वचनों को सुनते ही रनिवास उदास हो गया। सासुएँ प्रेमवश बोल नहीं सकतीं। उन्होंने सब कुमारियों को हृदय से लगा लिया और उनके पतियों को सौंपकर बहुत विनती की ॥
ramacharitamanas::1813.english_translation: On hearing these words, the women of the palace grew distressed. The mothers-in-law could not speak, overwhelmed by love. They embraced all the princesses and, entrusting them to their husbands, offered many prayers.
ramacharitamanas::1813.translation_literal: सुनत (on hearing) / बचन (words) / बिलखेउ (became distressed) / रनिवासू (the palace women) । / बोलि (speaking) / न सकहिं (could not) / प्रेमबस (under the control of love) / सासू (mothers-in-law) ॥ / हृदयँ (to the heart) / लगाई (embracing) / कुअँरि (princesses) / सब (all) / लीन्ही (took) । / पतिन्ह (to their husbands) / सौंपि (entrusting) / बिनती (prayer) / अति (greatly) / कीन्ही (made) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1813.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1813.essence: Love lets go by blessing, not by speaking.
ramacharitamanas::1813.simple_meaning: The palace women are overcome with emotion. They embrace the princesses, hand them to their husbands, and pray deeply.
ramacharitamanas::1813.simple_insight: Love can be so full that words fail and only blessing remains.
ramacharitamanas::1813.detailed_meaning: At Ayodhya, the marriage celebrations are ending and the women of the palace hear the farewell words. Overwhelmed, they cannot speak clearly. They embrace the young brides, place them with their husbands, and send them off with heartfelt prayers.
ramacharitamanas::1813.modern_relevance: At a wedding farewell, the room goes quiet. The aunt who joked all evening suddenly cannot speak, and the hug says everything her voice cannot.
ramacharitamanas::1813.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to surrender, showing how love expresses itself through blessing, not possession.

ramacharitamanas::1814.verse_sanskrit: करि बिनय सिय रामहि समरपी जोरि कर पुनि पुनि कहै। बलि जाउँ तात सुजान तुम्ह कहुँ बिदित गति सब की अहै॥ परिवार पुरजन मोहि राजहि प्रानप्रिय सिय जानिबी। तुलसीस सीलु सनेहु लखि निज किंकरी करि मानिबी॥
ramacharitamanas::1814.verse_hindi: विनती करके उन्होंने सीताजी को श्री रामचन्द्रजी को समर्पित किया और हाथ जोड़कर बार-बार कहा- हे तात! हे सुजान! मैं बलि जाती हूँ, तुमको सबकी गति (हाल) मालूम है। परिवार को, पुरवासियों को, मुझको और राजा को सीता प्राणों के समान प्रिय है, ऐसा जानिएगा। हे तुलसी के स्वामी! इसके शील और स्नेह को देखकर इसे अपनी दासी करके मानिएगा।
ramacharitamanas::1814.english_translation: After making a humble request, she surrendered Sita to Ram and, joining her hands, said again and again: "I sacrifice myself to you, wise one; you know the condition of everyone. Family, citizens, myself, and the king all hold Sita dear as life. O lord of Tulsidas, seeing her character and affection, please accept her as your own servant."
ramacharitamanas::1814.translation_literal: करि (having done) / बिनय (humble request) / सिय (Sita) / रामहि (to Ram) / समरपी (surrendered) / जोरि कर (joining hands) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / कहै (says) / बलि जाउँ (I sacrifice myself) / तात (O dear one) / सुजान (wise one) / तुम्ह कहुँ (to you) / बिदित (known) / गति (condition) / सब की (of all) / अहै (is) / परिवार (family) / पुरजन (citizens) / मोहि (to me) / राजहि (to the king) / प्रानप्रिय (dear as life) / सिय (Sita) / जानिबी (know) / तुलसीस (O lord of Tulsidas) / सीलु (character) / सनेहु (affection) / लखि (seeing) / निज (own) / किंकरी (servant) / करि (making) / मानिबी (please accept)
ramacharitamanas::1814.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1814.essence: True love offers what it cherishes without trying to keep it.
ramacharitamanas::1814.simple_meaning: Sita is formally offered to Ram with deep humility. The speaker asks Ram to see her character, her affection, and the love everyone already has for her.
ramacharitamanas::1814.simple_insight: There is peace in offering someone precious without clinging to possession.
ramacharitamanas::1814.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the women of the household are sending Sita toward Ram with reverence and emotion. This is not a casual introduction but a sacred offering: they ask Ram to receive her not as property, but as one whose character and love deserve honor.
ramacharitamanas::1814.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love step into a new life, and your only honest response is blessing, not control. You want their goodness to be seen, not owned.
ramacharitamanas::1814.insight: It shifts the mind from possession to reverent offering, asking that worth be recognized rather than claimed.

ramacharitamanas::1815.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह परिपूरन काम जान सिरोमनि भावप्रिय। जन गुन गाहक राम दोष दलन करुनायतन ॥
ramacharitamanas::1815.verse_hindi: तुम पूर्ण काम हो, सुजान शिरोमणि हो और भावप्रिय हो (तुम्हें प्रेम प्यारा है)। हे राम! तुम भक्तों के गुणों को ग्रहण करने वाले, दोषों को नाश करने वाले और दया के धाम हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1815.english_translation: You are complete in every way, the wisest among the wise, and beloved of loving hearts. O Ram, you accept your devotees' virtues, destroy their faults, and are the home of compassion.
ramacharitamanas::1815.translation_literal: तुम (you) / परिपूरन (complete) / काम (fulfilled) / जान (knower) / सिरोमनि (crest-jewel) / भावप्रिय (dear to devotion) / जन (people/devotees) / गुन (virtues) / गाहक (receiver) / राम (Ram) / दोष (faults) / दलन (destroyer) / करुनायतन (abode of compassion)
ramacharitamanas::1815.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1815.essence: Ram receives loving hearts and remakes them from within.
ramacharitamanas::1815.simple_meaning: Ram is perfect, wise, and dear to loving hearts. He welcomes a devotee's good qualities, removes faults, and rests as compassion itself.
ramacharitamanas::1815.simple_insight: You do not need to be flawless to be held by Ram's grace.
ramacharitamanas::1815.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar, the queens and women of the palace have just surrendered Sita to Ram. This verse becomes their praise of Ram: he is complete, tender toward devotion, and able to transform both virtue and weakness in those who approach him.
ramacharitamanas::1815.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone who has disappointed you, yet you still see the good in them. This verse names that rare kind of love: one that notices faults without being ruled by them.
ramacharitamanas::1815.insight: It shifts devotion from earning approval to offering a heart that can be transformed.

ramacharitamanas::1816.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि रही चरन गहि रानी। प्रेम पंक जनु गिरा समानी॥ सुनि सनेहसानी बर बानी। बहुबिधि राम सासु सनमानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1816.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर रानी चरणों को पकड़कर (चुप) रह गईं। मानो उनकी वाणी प्रेम रूपी दलदल में समा गई हो। स्नेह से सनी हुई श्रेष्ठ वाणी सुनकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सास का बहुत प्रकार से सम्मान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1816.english_translation: Having said this, the queen remained holding his feet. Her speech seemed to sink into the mud of love. Hearing the noble words soaked in affection, Ram honored his mother-in-law in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::1816.translation_literal: अस कहि (having said this) / रही (remained) / चरन गहि (holding the feet) / रानी (the queen) / प्रेम (love) / पंक (mud) / जनु (as if) / गिरा (speech) / समानी (merged)॥ / सुनि (hearing) / सनेहसानी (soaked in affection) / बर (noble) / बानी (words) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / राम (Ram) / सासु (mother-in-law) / सनमानी (honored)॥
ramacharitamanas::1816.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1816.essence: Love can silence speech and still be fully answered.
ramacharitamanas::1816.simple_meaning: The queen falls silent in devotion and holds Ram's feet. Ram responds by honoring his mother-in-law with great respect.
ramacharitamanas::1816.simple_insight: Love can leave you wordless, and respect can answer it beautifully.
ramacharitamanas::1816.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the marriage has been completed and the family is gathered around Ram and Sita. The queen is overcome with feeling and can only cling to Ram's feet. Ram receives her words tenderly and returns that love with deep respect.
ramacharitamanas::1816.modern_relevance: A parent watches their child leave home after the wedding and cannot quite speak. The goodbye is too full for words, and the most loving response is simple respect.
ramacharitamanas::1816.insight: It shows that devotion need not be loud; it can be met with humble honor.

ramacharitamanas::1817.verse_sanskrit: राम बिदा मागत कर जोरी। कीन्ह प्रनामु बहोरि बहोरी॥ पाइ असीस बहुरि सिरु नाई। भाइन्ह सहित चले रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1817.verse_hindi: तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने हाथ जोड़कर विदा माँगते हुए बार-बार प्रणाम किया। आशीर्वाद पाकर और फिर सिर नवाकर भाइयों सहित श्री रघुनाथजी चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1817.english_translation: Then Shri Ramchandra, with joined hands, asked for leave and bowed again and again. After receiving blessings and bowing his head once more, Raghurai departed with his brothers.
ramacharitamanas::1817.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बिदा (leave-taking) / मागत (asking) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रनामु (bowing) / बहोरि (again) / बहोरी (again and again) / पाइ (having received) / असीस (blessings) / बहुरि (again) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing) / भाइन्ह (with brothers) / सहित (together) / चले (went) / रघुराई (Raghurai)
ramacharitamanas::1817.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1817.essence: True greatness leaves with humility, not entitlement.
ramacharitamanas::1817.simple_meaning: Ram respectfully asks permission to leave, bows for blessings, and departs with his brothers.
ramacharitamanas::1817.simple_insight: Even in departure, dignity stays joined with humility.
ramacharitamanas::1817.detailed_meaning: At the end of the exchange with the queens, Ram stands before his family, asks for leave with folded hands, receives blessings, bows again, and walks out with Lakshman and the others. The scene shows the grace of a prince who never stops honouring those he loves.
ramacharitamanas::1817.modern_relevance: You finish a difficult family visit, stand at the doorway, and still make time for one more thank-you, one more bow of respect. Leaving well can be its own form of love.
ramacharitamanas::1817.insight: It teaches graceful exit: honour others fully before moving on.

ramacharitamanas::1818.verse_sanskrit: मंजु मधुर मूरति उर आनी। भईं सनेह सिथिल सब रानी॥ पुनि धीरजु धरि कुअँरि हँकारीं। बार बार भेटहि महतारीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1818.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी की सुंदर मधुर मूर्ति को हृदय में लाकर सब रानियाँ स्नेह से शिथिल हो गईं। फिर धीरज धारण करके कुमारियों को बुलाकर माताएँ बारंबार उन्हें (गले लगाकर) भेंटने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1818.english_translation: Bringing Ram's sweet, beautiful form into their hearts, all the queens were overcome with affection. Then they steadied themselves, called the young women, and the mothers embraced them again and again.
ramacharitamanas::1818.translation_literal: मंजु (lovely) / मधुर (sweet) / मूरति (form) / उर (heart) / आनी (bringing) / भईं (became) / सनेह (affection) / सिथिल (weakened, overcome) / सब (all) / रानी (queens)॥ / पुनि (again) / धीरजु (steadiness) / धरि (holding) / कुअँरि (young women) / हँकारीं (called) / बार बार (again and again) / भेटहि (embrace) / महतारीं (mothers)॥
ramacharitamanas::1818.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1818.essence: Love makes farewell linger in the body.
ramacharitamanas::1818.simple_meaning: The queens think of Ram with love and become overwhelmed. After calming themselves, they call the young women and keep embracing them.
ramacharitamanas::1818.simple_insight: Love softens the heart so completely that even parting becomes tender.
ramacharitamanas::1818.detailed_meaning: Ram has just taken leave of the palace. The queens hold his beautiful form in their hearts and are nearly undone by love. Gathering themselves, they call the young women close and keep embracing them, stretching the farewell with affection.
ramacharitamanas::1818.modern_relevance: You watch someone leave after a family visit, and nobody wants to be the first to let go. The goodbye keeps turning into one more hug, one more look, one more second together.
ramacharitamanas::1818.insight: It shows how love can make parting gentle instead of abrupt, and how people prolong closeness through repeated embrace.

ramacharitamanas::1819.verse_sanskrit: पहुँचावहिं फिरि मिलहिं बहोरी। बढ़ी परस्पर प्रीति न थोरी॥ पुनि पुनि मिलत सखिन्ह बिलगाई। बाल बच्छ जिमि धेनु लवाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1819.verse_hindi: पुत्रियों को पहुँचाती हैं, फिर लौटकर मिलती हैं। परस्पर में कुछ थोड़ी प्रीति नहीं बढ़ी (अर्थात बहुत प्रीति बढ़ी)। बार-बार मिलती हुई माताओं को सखियों ने अलग कर दिया। जैसे हाल की ब्यायी हुई गाय को कोई उसके बालक बछड़े (या बछिया) से अलग कर दे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1819.english_translation: They escort them and then come back to meet again. Their mutual love only grows. Again and again the mothers meet, and the companions separate them, like a cow newly calved being pulled away from her calf.
ramacharitamanas::1819.translation_literal: पहुँचावहिं (they escort) / फिरि (again) / मिलहिं (they meet) / बहोरी (again) / बढ़ी (increased) / परस्पर (mutual) / प्रीति (love) / न थोरी (not little) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / मिलत (meeting) / सखिन्ह (by the companions) / बिलगाई (separated) / बाल बच्छ (young calf) / जिमि (like) / धेनु (cow) / लवाई (newly calved)
ramacharitamanas::1819.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1819.essence: Parting hurts most when love is deepest.
ramacharitamanas::1819.simple_meaning: The mothers keep returning to see the daughters they love, and the friends keep separating them. Their affection grows so strong it feels like a mother cow being torn from her calf.
ramacharitamanas::1819.simple_insight: Love makes parting painful, even when everyone knows the separation is temporary.
ramacharitamanas::1819.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the women of the household cannot bear to let Ram, Sita, and the others go. They escort the departing party, return to meet them again, and are pulled apart by their own companions. The scene shows love overflowing beyond restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1819.modern_relevance: At a train platform, your mother keeps stepping forward for one more hug while friends gently pull her back. Nobody is dramatic; everyone is simply unable to let go.
ramacharitamanas::1819.insight: It turns a departure into a shared act of tenderness, not a clean farewell.

ramacharitamanas::1820.verse_sanskrit: प्रेमबिबस नर नारि सब सखिन्ह सहित रनिवासु। मानहुँ कीन्ह बिदेहपुर करुनाँ बिरहँ निवासु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1820.verse_hindi: सब स्त्री-पुरुष और सखियों सहित सारा रनिवास प्रेम के विशेष वश हो रहा है। (ऐसा लगता है) मानो जनकपुर में करुणा और विरह ने डेरा डाल दिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1820.english_translation: All the men and women, along with the maids, were overcome by love. It seemed as if Janakpur itself had become the home of compassion and separation.
ramacharitamanas::1820.translation_literal: प्रेमबिबस (overcome by love) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / सब (all) / सखिन्ह (with companions) / सहित (together with) / रनिवासु (women's quarters) / मानहुँ (as if) / कीन्ह (made) / बिदेहपुर (Janakpur) / करुनाँ (compassion) / बिरहँ (separation) / निवासु (dwelling)
ramacharitamanas::1820.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1820.essence: Love turns an entire place into longing.
ramacharitamanas::1820.simple_meaning: Everyone in the palace is so overwhelmed by love and longing that the whole city feels filled with compassion and separation.
ramacharitamanas::1820.simple_insight: Love can spread through a whole place and turn private longing into a shared atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::1820.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the women of the palace have just been meeting and parting from the princesses in waves of affection. The mood has become so intense that Tulsidas says the whole city now feels like a dwelling place of longing.
ramacharitamanas::1820.modern_relevance: A house after a farewell can feel strangely silent, as if the rooms themselves are grieving. One person's departure can change the emotional weather for everyone left behind.
ramacharitamanas::1820.insight: It shifts attention from individual feeling to the way love and loss shape an entire community.

ramacharitamanas::1821.verse_sanskrit: सुक सारिका जानकी ज्याए। कनक पिंजरन्हि राखि पढ़ाए॥ ब्याकुल कहहिं कहाँ बैदेही। सुनि धीरजु परिहरइ न केही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1821.verse_hindi: जानकी ने जिन तोता और मैना को पाल-पोसकर बड़ा किया था और सोने के पिंजड़ों में रखकर पढ़ाया था, वे व्याकुल होकर कह रहे हैं- वैदेही कहाँ हैं। उनके ऐसे वचनों को सुनकर धीरज किसको नहीं त्याग देगा (अर्थात सबका धैर्य जाता रहा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1821.english_translation: Sita had raised the parrots and mynas, keeping them in golden cages and teaching them. They cry out in distress, “Where is Vaidehi?” Hearing such words, who could keep composure?
ramacharitamanas::1821.translation_literal: सुक (parrot) / सारिका (myna) / जानकी (Sita) / ज्याए (raised) / कनक (golden) / पिंजरन्हि (in cages) / राखि (keeping) / पढ़ाए (taught) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / कहहिं (they say) / कहाँ (where) / बैदेही (Vaidehi) / सुनि (hearing) / धीरजु (composure) / परिहरइ (gives up) / न (not) / केही (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::1821.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1821.essence: Absence is so strong it reaches the birds Sita raised.
ramacharitamanas::1821.simple_meaning: Sita's trained birds cry out for her, and their grief shakes everyone nearby.
ramacharitamanas::1821.simple_insight: Love so deep can make even the smallest voices carry unbearable longing.
ramacharitamanas::1821.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, Sita's absence has already unsettled the whole household. Even the parrots and mynas she raised in golden cages cry out for Vaidehi. Their distress becomes another proof of how completely the palace is pierced by separation.
ramacharitamanas::1821.modern_relevance: You open a voice note from a pet sitter, and your cat keeps waiting by the door. Even the animals notice the absence before the people do.
ramacharitamanas::1821.insight: It turns grief into a shared atmosphere, not a private feeling.

ramacharitamanas::1822.verse_sanskrit: भए बिकल खग मृग एहि भाँती। मनुज दसा कैसें कहि जाती॥ बंधु समेत जनकु तब आए। प्रेम उमगि लोचन जल छाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1822.verse_hindi: जब पक्षी और पशु तक इस तरह विकल हो गए, तब मनुष्यों की दशा कैसे कही जा सकती है! तब भाई सहित जनकजी वहाँ आए। प्रेम से उमड़कर उनके नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1822.english_translation: Even birds and animals were distraught like this; how can the condition of human beings be described? Then King Janaka came with his brothers, and love welled up so strongly that tears filled his eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1822.translation_literal: भए (became) / बिकल (distressed) / खग (birds) / मृग (animals) / एहि भाँती (in this manner) / मनुज (humans) / दसा (condition) / कैसें (how) / कहि जाती (can be described) / बंधु (brothers) / समेत (together with) / जनकु (Janaka) / तब (then) / आए (came) / प्रेम (love) / उमगि (surged) / लोचन (eyes) / जल (water/tears) / छाए (covered, filled)
ramacharitamanas::1822.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1822.essence: Love can make even the whole world seem distressed.
ramacharitamanas::1822.simple_meaning: Even the birds and animals are shaken by this separation. Janaka arrives with his brothers, overwhelmed with love and tears.
ramacharitamanas::1822.simple_insight: Grief can be so deep that even the natural world seems to feel it with you.
ramacharitamanas::1822.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the wedding celebration has turned into a scene of separation and longing. Even birds and animals appear disturbed. Janaka comes with his brothers, and his love for Sita overflows into tears.
ramacharitamanas::1822.modern_relevance: You walk into a quiet house after everyone has left, and the silence feels alive. Some losses are so large that even the room seems to know them.
ramacharitamanas::1822.insight: It shifts attention from public ceremony to private grief, showing how deeply love can unsettle composure.

ramacharitamanas::1823.verse_sanskrit: सीय बिलोकि धीरता भागी। रहे कहावत परम बिरागी॥ लीन्हि रायँ उर लाइ जानकी। मिटी महामरजाद ग्यान की ॥
ramacharitamanas::1823.verse_hindi: वे परम वैराग्यवान कहलाते थे, पर सीताजी को देखकर उनका भी धीरज भाग गया। राजा ने जानकीजी को हृदय से लगा लिया। (प्रेम के प्रभाव से) ज्ञान की महान मर्यादा मिट गई (ज्ञान का बाँध टूट गया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1823.english_translation: Seeing Sita, his composure fled. The one called utterly detached lost all restraint. The king embraced Janaki to his heart, and the great boundary of knowledge dissolved.
ramacharitamanas::1823.translation_literal: सीय (Sita) / बिलोकि (seeing) / धीरता (composure) / भागी (ran away) / रहे (remained) / कहावत (called) / परम (supreme) / बिरागी (detached) / लीन्हि (took) / रायँ (the king) / उर (to the heart) / लाइ (bringing) / जानकी (Janaki) / मिटी (dissolved) / महामरजाद (great boundary) / ग्यान (of knowledge) / की (of)
ramacharitamanas::1823.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1823.essence: True love can break the rules of restraint without becoming weakness.
ramacharitamanas::1823.simple_meaning: The sight of Sita overwhelms even the most detached mind. Love breaks through restraint, and the usual limits of reason fall away.
ramacharitamanas::1823.simple_insight: Love can undo the pride of self-control and make the heart honest.
ramacharitamanas::1823.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Sita's presence stirs everyone deeply. Even the king, famed for detachment, loses his composure, embraces her, and shows that love can break the proud boundary of learned restraint.
ramacharitamanas::1823.modern_relevance: You walk into a room planning to stay cool, but one look at someone you love changes everything. The body knows what the mind tries to manage.
ramacharitamanas::1823.insight: It shifts attention from polished control to the force of genuine feeling.

ramacharitamanas::1824.verse_sanskrit: समुझावत सब सचिव सयाने। कीन्ह बिचारु न अवसर जाने॥ बारहिं बार सुता उर लाईं। सजि सुंदर पालकीं मगाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1824.verse_hindi: सब बुद्धिमान मंत्री उन्हें समझाते हैं। तब राजा ने विषाद करने का समय न जानकर विचार किया। बारंबार पुत्रियों को हृदय से लगाकर सुंदर सजी हुई पालकियाँ मँगवाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1824.english_translation: The wise ministers tried to console him. Then the king, seeing no time for grief, made a decision. He kept embracing his daughters again and again and ordered beautiful palanquins to be brought.
ramacharitamanas::1824.translation_literal: समुझावत (consoling) / सब (all) / सचिव (ministers) / सयाने (wise) / कीन्ह (made) / बिचारु (decision) / न (not) / अवसर (occasion/time) / जाने (knowing) / बारहिं बार (again and again) / सुता (daughters) / उर (to the chest) / लाईं (embracing) / सजि (decorated) / सुंदर (beautiful) / पालकीं (palanquins) / मगाईं (had brought)
ramacharitamanas::1824.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1824.essence: Grief can coexist with clear action.
ramacharitamanas::1824.simple_meaning: The king is overwhelmed, but the ministers steady him. He gathers himself, hugs his daughters again and again, and arranges for the palanquins.
ramacharitamanas::1824.simple_insight: Even in grief, a person still has to make the next careful choice.
ramacharitamanas::1824.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, after Sita's swayamvar, King Janak is flooded with emotion as the wedding arrangements move forward. His wise ministers try to steady him. He pauses, embraces his daughters, and orders the palanquins, because the moment cannot wait.
ramacharitamanas::1824.modern_relevance: You are wiping your eyes in the hallway before your daughter's wedding, then checking the guest list one more time. Love and responsibility do not cancel each other.
ramacharitamanas::1824.insight: It shifts the mind from being swallowed by feeling to acting with care despite feeling.

ramacharitamanas::1825.verse_sanskrit: प्रेमबिबस परिवारु सबु जानि सुलगन नरेस। कुअँरि चढ़ाईं पालकिन्ह सुमिरे सिद्धि गनेस ॥
ramacharitamanas::1825.verse_hindi: सारा परिवार प्रेम में विवश है। राजा ने सुंदर मुहूर्त जानकर सिद्धि सहित गणेशजी का स्मरण करके कन्याओं को पालकियों पर चढ़ाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1825.english_translation: The whole family was overcome by love. The king, choosing an auspicious moment and remembering Ganesh for success, placed the princesses in palanquins.
ramacharitamanas::1825.translation_literal: प्रेमबिबस (overcome by love) / परिवारु (family) / सबु (all) / जानि (knowing) / सुलगन (auspicious time) / नरेस (king) / कुअँरि (princesses) / चढ़ाईं (had placed) / पालकिन्ह (in palanquins) / सुमिरे (remembered) / सिद्धि (success) / गनेस (Ganesh)
ramacharitamanas::1825.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1825.essence: Love moves the family, but order still carries the moment.
ramacharitamanas::1825.simple_meaning: Everyone is swept up in love, and the king arranges the princesses’ departure at an auspicious time after remembering Ganesh.
ramacharitamanas::1825.simple_insight: Love can make a family tremble, yet ceremony still gives grief a place to move forward.
ramacharitamanas::1825.detailed_meaning: At King Janak’s court, the wedding joy has turned tender and heavy. The family is overwhelmed by love, so Janak carefully sends the princesses off in palanquins at an auspicious moment, remembering Ganesh as the journey begins.
ramacharitamanas::1825.modern_relevance: A family gathers at a train platform, trying not to cry as the youngest leaves home. Someone still checks the clock, adjusts the bags, and makes sure the goodbye is done properly.
ramacharitamanas::1825.insight: It shows how devotion, custom, and tenderness can coexist even in a painful farewell.

ramacharitamanas::1826.verse_sanskrit: बहुबिधि भूप सुता समुझाईं। नारिधरमु कुलरीति सिखाईं॥ दासीं दास दिए बहुतेरे। सुचि सेवक जे प्रिय सिय केरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1826.verse_hindi: राजा ने पुत्रियों को बहुत प्रकार से समझाया और उन्हें स्त्रियों का धर्म और कुल की रीति सिखाई। बहुत से दासी-दास दिए, जो सीताजी के प्रिय और विश्वास पात्र सेवक थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1826.english_translation: The king instructed his daughters in many ways, teaching them the duties of women and the customs of the family line. He gave them many maidservants and servants, all pure and trusted attendants dear to Sita.
ramacharitamanas::1826.translation_literal: बहुबिधि (in many ways) / भूप (king) / सुता (daughters) / समुझाईं (explained) / नारिधरमु (women's duty) / कुलरीति (family custom) / सिखाईं (taught) / दासीं (maidservants) / दास (servants) / दिए (gave) / बहुतेरे (many) / सुचि (pure) / सेवक (attendants) / जे (who) / प्रिय (dear) / सिय (to Sita) / केरे (belonging to)
ramacharitamanas::1826.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1826.essence: Love prepares others before letting them go.
ramacharitamanas::1826.simple_meaning: King Janak prepares his daughters for marriage by teaching them proper conduct and sending trusted servants with them.
ramacharitamanas::1826.simple_insight: Care is practical, not sentimental. Real love prepares people for the life they are entering.
ramacharitamanas::1826.detailed_meaning: Janak is sending Sita away from her childhood home after the swayamvar. Before the journey, he instructs the daughters in family conduct and arranges trusted attendants for Sita, showing both affection and responsibility at a painful threshold.
ramacharitamanas::1826.modern_relevance: A parent packing a child for a new city does more than say goodbye. They teach, prepare, and quietly place support in the child's hands before the door closes.
ramacharitamanas::1826.insight: It shifts love from emotion alone to preparation, guidance, and dependable support.

ramacharitamanas::1827.verse_sanskrit: सीय चलत ब्याकुल पुरबासी। होहिं सगुन सुभ मंगल रासी॥ भूसुर सचिव समेत समाजा। संग चले पहुँचावन राजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1827.verse_hindi: सीताजी के चलते समय जनकपुरवासी व्याकुल हो गए। मंगल की राशि शुभ शकुन हो रहे हैं। ब्राह्मण और मंत्रियों के समाज सहित राजा जनकजी उन्हें पहुँचाने के लिए साथ चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1827.english_translation: As Sita set out, the people of Janakpur grew restless. Auspicious signs and blessings appeared. King Janak, with brahmins, ministers, and the whole assembly, went along to escort her.
ramacharitamanas::1827.translation_literal: सीय (Sita) / चलत (while going) / ब्याकुल (restless) / पुरबासी (city dwellers) / होहिं (become) / सगुन (auspicious signs) / सुभ (good) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / रासी (mass) / भूसुर (brahmins) / सचिव (ministers) / समेत (together with) / समाजा (assembly) / संग (with) / चले (went) / पहुँचावन (to escort) / राजा (king)
ramacharitamanas::1827.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1827.essence: A blessed farewell can carry an entire city’s love.
ramacharitamanas::1827.simple_meaning: The people of Janakpur feel emotional as Sita leaves, and everyone sees this moment as blessed. King Janak escorts her with his court.
ramacharitamanas::1827.simple_insight: A sacred departure can move an entire city. Love, honor, and blessing all travel with it.
ramacharitamanas::1827.detailed_meaning: Sita is leaving Janakpur, and the whole city feels the ache of that moment. King Janak does not send her away coldly; he walks with her, surrounded by brahmins and ministers, as if the entire kingdom is blessing her journey.
ramacharitamanas::1827.modern_relevance: At a train platform, everyone goes quiet when the bride steps forward and her family walks beside her. The goodbye hurts, but the escort itself becomes love made visible.
ramacharitamanas::1827.insight: It turns departure into a shared act of honor, not a private loss.

ramacharitamanas::1828.verse_sanskrit: समय बिलोकि बाजने बाजे। रथ गज बाजि बरातिन्ह साजे॥ दसरथ बिप्र बोलि सब लीन्हे। दान मान परिपूरन कीन्हे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1828.verse_hindi: समय देखकर बाजे बजने लगे। बारातियों ने रथ, हाथी और घोड़े सजाए। दशरथजी ने सब ब्राह्मणों को बुला लिया और उन्हें दान और सम्मान से परिपूर्ण कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1828.english_translation: At the right time, the drums began to sound. The wedding party readied chariots, elephants, and horses. Dasharath called all the brahmins and fulfilled them with gifts and honour.
ramacharitamanas::1828.translation_literal: समय (time) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बाजने (instruments of music) / बाजे (were played) / रथ (chariots) / गज (elephants) / बाजि (horses) / बरातिन्ह (for the wedding party) / साजे (were prepared) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / बिप्र (brahmins) / बोलि (calling) / सब (all) / लीन्हे (took) / दान (gifts) / मान (honour) / परिपूरन (fully) / कीन्हे (did)
ramacharitamanas::1828.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1828.essence: Sacred occasions begin with order, timing, and honour.
ramacharitamanas::1828.simple_meaning: The wedding procession is getting ready. Drums sound, vehicles and animals are prepared, and Dasharath honours the brahmins with gifts.
ramacharitamanas::1828.simple_insight: Great moments begin with careful timing and generous respect.
ramacharitamanas::1828.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the wedding celebration is moving forward. The music starts, the procession is readied, and Dasharath makes sure the brahmins are honoured before departure. The scene builds the sacred, festive atmosphere around Sita and Ram's marriage.
ramacharitamanas::1828.modern_relevance: The hall is buzzing before the ceremony begins. Someone checks the guest list, someone else adjusts the decorations, and the host quietly makes sure every elder is welcomed properly.
ramacharitamanas::1828.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle to the care that prepares it.

ramacharitamanas::1829.verse_sanskrit: चरन सरोज धूरि धरि सीसा। मुदित महीपति पाइ असीसा॥ सुमिरि गजाननु कीन्ह पयाना। मंगल मूल सगुन भए नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1829.verse_hindi: उनके चरण कमलों की धूलि सिर पर धरकर और आशीष पाकर राजा आनंदित हुए और गणेशजी का स्मरण करके उन्होंने प्रस्थान किया। मंगलों के मूल अनेकों शकुन हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1829.english_translation: Placing the dust of the lotus feet on his head, the king departed delighted after receiving blessings. Remembering Ganesha, many auspicious signs appeared.
ramacharitamanas::1829.translation_literal: चरन (feet) / सरोज (lotus) / धूरि (dust) / धरि (placing) / सीसा (head) / मुदित (delighted) / महीपति (king) / पाइ (having received) / असीसा (blessings) / सुमिरि (remembering) / गजाननु (Ganesha) / कीन्ह (did) / पयाना (departure) / मंगल (auspicious) / मूल (source) / सगुन (omens) / भए (became) / नाना (many)
ramacharitamanas::1829.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1829.essence: Blessed beginnings turn movement into auspicious momentum.
ramacharitamanas::1829.simple_meaning: The king leaves joyfully after bowing to holy feet and receiving blessings. He remembers Ganesha, and many good omens appear.
ramacharitamanas::1829.simple_insight: A humble start changes the whole journey. Reverence turns departure into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1829.detailed_meaning: Janakpur has just sent Sita off. In the next moment, King Dasharath bows, receives blessings, remembers Ganesha, and sets out with his wedding procession. The scene is full of good signs, but it mainly carries the movement of the story forward.
ramacharitamanas::1829.modern_relevance: Before a big family event, someone touches the feet of elders, gets their blessing, and finally steps out with a lighter heart. The day feels protected before it even begins.
ramacharitamanas::1829.insight: It frames a major departure as an act of reverence, not mere travel.

ramacharitamanas::1830.verse_sanskrit: सुर प्रसून बरषहिं हरषि करहिं अपछरा गान। चले अवधपति अवधपुर मुदित बजाइ निसान ॥
ramacharitamanas::1830.verse_hindi: देवता हर्षित होकर फूल बरसा रहे हैं और अप्सराएँ गान कर रही हैं। अवधपति दशरथजी नगाड़े बजाकर आनंदपूर्वक अयोध्यापुरी चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1830.english_translation: The radiant beings shower flowers in delight, and the celestial dancers sing. The lord of Ayodhya returned to Ayodhya with drums sounding in joy.
ramacharitamanas::1830.translation_literal: सुर (radiant beings) / प्रसून (flowers) / बरषहिं (shower) / हरषि (in delight) / करहिं (do) / अपछरा (celestial dancers) / गान (song) / चले (went) / अवधपति (lord of Ayodhya) / अवधपुर (to Ayodhya city) / मुदित (joyful) / बजाइ (sounding) / निसान (drums)
ramacharitamanas::1830.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1830.essence: A blessed return makes the whole world seem to rejoice.
ramacharitamanas::1830.simple_meaning: The city welcomes Dasharath's return with joy from the heavens and music all around. This is a celebratory scene, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::1830.simple_insight: Joy can feel so complete that even the world seems to celebrate with you.
ramacharitamanas::1830.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has completed the wedding arrangements and is returning to Ayodhya in triumph. The heavens join the celebration: flowers fall, celestial singers sing, and drums sound as the king rides home.
ramacharitamanas::1830.modern_relevance: You finally leave the hospital after hearing good news, and the whole ride home feels lighter. Even the traffic seems less harsh because your chest is full of relief.
ramacharitamanas::1830.insight: It frames a joyful turning point as a public celebration, not a private feeling.

ramacharitamanas::1831.verse_sanskrit: नृप करि बिनय महाजन फेरे। सादर सकल मागने टेरे॥ भूषन बसन बाजि गज दीन्हे। प्रेम पोषि ठाढ़े सब कीन्हे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1831.verse_hindi: राजा दशरथजी ने विनती करके प्रतिष्ठित जनों को लौटाया और आदर के साथ सब मँगनों को बुलवाया। उनको गहने-कपड़े, घोड़े-हाथी दिए और प्रेम से पुष्ट करके सबको सम्पन्न अर्थात बलयुक्त कर दिया ॥।
ramacharitamanas::1831.english_translation: King Dasharath respectfully sent the honored guests away, then called all the beggars and gave them ornaments, clothes, horses, and elephants. He filled them with love and made them prosperous.
ramacharitamanas::1831.translation_literal: नृप (king) / करि (doing) / बिनय (humble request) / महाजन (respected people) / फेरे (sent back) / सादर (with respect) / सकल (all) / मागने (beggars, those who ask) / टेरे (called) / भूषन (ornaments) / बसन (clothes) / बाजि (horses) / गज (elephants) / दीन्हे (gave) / प्रेम (love) / पोषि (nourishing) / ठाढ़े (standing) / सब (all) / कीन्हे (made)
ramacharitamanas::1831.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1831.essence: Joy becomes complete only when it feeds everyone nearby.
ramacharitamanas::1831.simple_meaning: Dasharath honors the guests, then gives gifts generously to everyone who asks. He sends them away satisfied and strengthened.
ramacharitamanas::1831.simple_insight: True generosity does not merely give things; it makes people feel seen, welcomed, and uplifted.
ramacharitamanas::1831.detailed_meaning: At Dasharath’s court in Ayodhya, the celebration for Ram’s wedding is overflowing. The king sends away the honored guests with courtesy, then calls in the needy and gives them wealth, clothes, animals, and honor. The scene shows a ruler whose joy becomes open-handed giving.
ramacharitamanas::1831.modern_relevance: After a family celebration, you notice the leftovers, the extra chairs, the unopened gifts, and the people waiting quietly near the gate. The real test is whether joy stays private or becomes sharing.
ramacharitamanas::1831.insight: It shifts the mind from ceremonial celebration to practical generosity toward those who need support.

ramacharitamanas::1832.verse_sanskrit: बार बार बिरिदावलि भाषी। फिरे सकल रामहि उर राखी॥ बहुरि बहुरि कोसलपति कहहीं। जनकु प्रेमबस फिरै न चहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1832.verse_hindi: वे सब बारंबार विरुदावली (कुलकीर्ति) बखानकर और श्री रामचन्द्रजी को हृदय में रखकर लौटे। कोसलाधीश दशरथजी बार-बार लौटने को कहते हैं, परन्तु जनकजी प्रेमवश लौटना नहीं चाहते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1832.english_translation: They praised the family glory again and again, keeping Ram in their hearts as they returned. The king of Kosala kept asking them to return, but Janaka, moved by love, did not want to turn back.
ramacharitamanas::1832.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / बिरिदावलि (list of family glory) / भाषी (speaking) / फिरे (returned) / सकल (all) / रामहि (Ram) / उर (heart) / राखी (keeping) / बहुरि बहुरि (again and again) / कोसलपति (lord of Kosala) / कहहीं (kept saying) / जनकु (Janaka) / प्रेमबस (under the power of love) / फिरै (to return) / न चहहीं (did not wish)
ramacharitamanas::1832.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1832.essence: Love lingers longer than the journey home.
ramacharitamanas::1832.simple_meaning: Everyone kept praising Ram and returned with him in their hearts. King Dasharath kept asking Janaka to turn back, but Janaka, full of love, did not want to leave.
ramacharitamanas::1832.simple_insight: Love makes leaving harder than arriving. The heart keeps holding on even after the journey should end.
ramacharitamanas::1832.detailed_meaning: After the wedding celebrations in Mithila, Dasharath and Janaka part with deep affection. The guests praise Ram's glory as they return, but Janaka cannot bear to turn back. This verse lingers on the ache of separation after joy.
ramacharitamanas::1832.modern_relevance: You leave a wedding hall after midnight, still looking back at the people you love. The car starts, but your heart stays behind in the light and music.
ramacharitamanas::1832.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the emotional cost of parting from what the heart has held dear.

ramacharitamanas::1833.verse_sanskrit: पुनि कह भूपत बचन सुहाए। फिरिअ महीस दूरि बड़ि आए॥ राउ बहोरि उतरि भए ठाढ़े। प्रेम प्रबाह बिलोचन बाढ़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::1833.verse_hindi: दशरथजी ने फिर सुहावने वचन कहे- हे राजन् ! बहुत दूर आ गए, अब लौटिए। फिर राजा दशरथजी रथ से उतरकर खड़े हो गए। उनके नेत्रों में प्रेम का प्रवाह बढ़ आया (प्रेमाश्रुओं की धारा बह चली) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1833.english_translation: King Dasharatha spoke gently again: "Turn back, O king. You have come very far." Then the king stepped down from the chariot and stood there, while tears of love rose in his eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1833.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / कह (said) / भूपत (the king) / बचन (words) / सुहाए (sweet, pleasing) / फिरिअ (turn back) / महीस (O king) / दूरि (far) / बड़ि (very) / आए (have come) / राउ (the king) / बहोरि (again) / उतरि (stepped down) / भए (became) / ठाढ़े (standing) / प्रेम (love) / प्रबाह (flow) / बिलोचन (eyes) / बाढ़े (swelled, increased)
ramacharitamanas::1833.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1833.simple_meaning: Dasharatha gently asks the king to turn back. He gets down from the chariot and stands there, overwhelmed with love and tears.
ramacharitamanas::1833.simple_insight: Love can make even a king forget formality and stand exposed.
ramacharitamanas::1833.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court during the Sita-swayamvar, King Dasharatha keeps trying to honor his guest and send him back with affection. The moment is full of royal courtesy and tenderness, not teaching, as his love overflows into tears.
ramacharitamanas::1833.modern_relevance: You walk your guest to the door, then keep talking because neither of you wants the moment to end. Sometimes affection makes simple goodbyes impossible.
ramacharitamanas::1833.insight: It shows how deep affection softens pride and turns etiquette into tenderness.

ramacharitamanas::1834.verse_sanskrit: तब बिदेह बोले कर जोरी। बचन सनेह सुधाँ जनु बोरी॥ करौं कवन बिधि बिनय बनाई। महाराज मोहि दीन्हि बड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1834.verse_hindi: तब जनकजी हाथ जोड़कर मानो स्नेह रूपी अमृत में डुबोकर वचन बोले- मैं किस तरह बनाकर (किन शब्दों में) विनती करूँ। हे महाराज! आपने मुझे बड़ी बड़ाई दी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1834.english_translation: Then the King of Videha folded his hands and spoke, as if pouring his words into nectar of affection: “How should I frame my thanks? O great king, you have shown me great honor.”
ramacharitamanas::1834.translation_literal: तब (then) बिदेह (the king of Videha) बोले (spoke) कर जोरी (with folded hands) / बचन (words) सनेह (of affection) सुधाँ (nectar) जनु (as if) बोरी (poured)॥ / करौं (how should I do) कवन बिधि (what manner) बिनय (humble request) बनाई (having made) / महाराज (great king) मोहि (to me) दीन्हि (you gave) बड़ाई (honor, greatness)॥
ramacharitamanas::1834.speaker: Janak
ramacharitamanas::1834.essence: Honor is best received with folded hands and a smaller ego.
ramacharitamanas::1834.simple_meaning: Janak greets Dasharath with folded hands and speaks humbly, saying he cannot even find the right words to thank him for the honor shown.
ramacharitamanas::1834.simple_insight: True greatness shows itself in humility. The more honored he is, the more gently Janak bows.
ramacharitamanas::1834.detailed_meaning: Janak has just welcomed Dasharath, who came so far with love and respect. Now Janak folds his hands and answers with deep humility, feeling that Dasharath has already honored him beyond measure. The meeting is rich with affection and formal courtesy.
ramacharitamanas::1834.modern_relevance: You receive a call from someone you deeply respect, and they speak to you with warmth you did not expect. Your first response is not performance, but humility and gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::1834.insight: It shifts the reader from self-importance to gracious receiving, showing how honor is answered with modesty.

ramacharitamanas::1835.verse_sanskrit: कोसलपति समधी सजन सनमाने सब भाँति। मिलनि परसपर बिनय अति प्रीति न हृदयँ समाति ॥
ramacharitamanas::1835.verse_hindi: अयोध्यानाथ दशरथजी ने अपने स्वजन समधी का सब प्रकार से सम्मान किया। उनके आपस के मिलने में अत्यन्त विनय थी और इतनी प्रीति थी जो हृदय में समाती न थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1835.english_translation: The lord of Kosala honored his in-laws in every way. Their meeting was full of humility and such love that it could not fit in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1835.translation_literal: कोसलपति (lord of Kosala) / समधी (in-laws) / सजन (relatives, loved ones) / सनमाने (honored) / सब भाँति (in every way) / मिलनि (meeting) / परसपर (mutual) / बिनय (humility) / अति (great) / प्रीति (love) / न (not) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / समाति (fits, contained)
ramacharitamanas::1835.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1835.essence: Honor can carry more love than words can hold.
ramacharitamanas::1835.simple_meaning: Dasharath welcomed Janak and his family with full respect. Their meeting overflowed with humility and affection.
ramacharitamanas::1835.simple_insight: Real greatness shows itself in how warmly you honor others.
ramacharitamanas::1835.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, Dasharath has come as a father-in-law, not just a king. He and Janak meet with deep courtesy, each honoring the other’s side. The verse lingers on the tenderness of that royal family reunion before the wedding rites continue.
ramacharitamanas::1835.modern_relevance: You meet your child’s in-laws for the first time, and every gesture matters: the seat you offer, the tone you use, the respect you show. This verse remembers that dignity can feel like love.
ramacharitamanas::1835.insight: It shifts attention from status to gracious conduct in relationships.

ramacharitamanas::1836.verse_sanskrit: मुनि मंडलिहि जनक सिरु नावा। आसिरबादु सबहि सन पावा॥ सादर पुनि भेंटे जामाता। रूप सील गुन निधि सब भ्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::1836.verse_hindi: जनकजी ने मुनि मंडली को सिर नवाया और सभी से आशीर्वाद पाया। फिर आदर के साथ वे रूप, शील और गुणों के निधान सब भाइयों से, अपने दामादों से मिले, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1836.english_translation: Janak bowed his head to the assembly of sages and received blessings from all. Then, with respect, he greeted his sons-in-law, treasures of beauty, character, and virtue, along with all the brothers.
ramacharitamanas::1836.translation_literal: मुनि मंडलिहि (the assembly of sages) / जनक (Janak) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / आसिरबादु (blessings) / सबहि सन (from all) / पावा (received)॥ / सादर (respectfully) / पुनि (then) / भेंटे (greeted/met) / जामाता (sons-in-law) / रूप (beauty) / सील (character) / गुन (virtues) / निधि (treasures) / सब भ्राता (all the brothers) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1836.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1836.essence: Humility opens the door to blessing and affectionate welcome.
ramacharitamanas::1836.simple_meaning: Janak first bows to the sages and receives their blessings. Then he respectfully greets his sons-in-law and the brothers gathered there.
ramacharitamanas::1836.simple_insight: Respect moves outward first to wisdom, then to family. Humility makes every meeting graceful.
ramacharitamanas::1836.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court during Sita's swayamvar, the formal meeting turns warm and sacred. Janak honors the gathered sages, receives their blessings, and then greets Ram and his brothers as beloved sons-in-law. The scene shows dignity joined with affection.
ramacharitamanas::1836.modern_relevance: You enter a room where elders, in-laws, and guests are all watching. The way you bow, greet, and honor each person quietly sets the tone for everything that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1836.insight: It teaches that reverence is not separate from family warmth; proper respect creates harmony in public and private life.

ramacharitamanas::1837.verse_sanskrit: जोरि पंकरुह पानि सुहाए। बोले बचन प्रेम जनु जाए॥ राम करौं केहि भाँति प्रसंसा। मुनि महेस मन मानस हंसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1837.verse_hindi: और सुंदर कमल के समान हाथों को जोड़कर ऐसे वचन बोले जो मानो प्रेम से ही जन्मे हों। हे रामजी! मैं किस प्रकार आपकी प्रशंसा करूँ! आप मुनियों और महादेवजी के मन रूपी मानसरोवर के हंस हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1837.english_translation: Joining his beautiful lotus-like hands, he spoke words born from love: "How can I praise Ram? He is the swan in the mind-lake of sages and Mahadev."
ramacharitamanas::1837.translation_literal: जोरि (joining) / पंकरुह (lotus-like) / पानि (hands) / सुहाए (beautiful) / बोले (spoke) / बचन (words) / प्रेम (love) / जनु (as if) / जाए (born) / राम (Ram) / करौं (do I make) / केहि भाँति (in what manner) / प्रसंसा (praise) / मुनि (sages) / महेस (Mahadev) / मन (mind) / मानस (mind-lake) / हंसा (swan)
ramacharitamanas::1837.speaker: Janak
ramacharitamanas::1837.essence: True praise ends in humility before Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1837.simple_meaning: Janak bows with love and says Ram cannot be praised enough. Even sages and Shiva hold Ram in the deepest place of their minds.
ramacharitamanas::1837.simple_insight: Praise becomes humble when the heart knows the divine is greater than words.
ramacharitamanas::1837.detailed_meaning: After welcoming Dasharath and the guests, Janak turns to Ram with folded hands. In front of sages, kings, and Shiva's great name, he admits that ordinary praise is too small for Ram. The moment shifts the scene from ceremony to devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1837.modern_relevance: You try to thank someone who changed your life, and every sentence feels too small. Janak's response is that feeling made sacred: words bow before what the heart already knows.
ramacharitamanas::1837.insight: It teaches reverence without performance: let praise become surrender when language runs out.

ramacharitamanas::1838.verse_sanskrit: करहिं जोग जोगी जेहि लागी। कोहु मोहु ममता मदु त्यागी॥ ब्यापकु ब्रह्मु अलखु अबिनासी। चिदानंदु निरगुन गुनरासी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1838.verse_hindi: योगी लोग जिनके लिए क्रोध, मोह, ममता और मद को त्यागकर योग साधन करते हैं, जो सर्वव्यापक, ब्रह्म, अव्यक्त, अविनाशी, चिदानंद, निर्गुण और गुणों की राशि हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1838.english_translation: Yogis practice yoga for the one who is free of anger, delusion, attachment, and pride: the all-pervading Brahman, unseen, imperishable, consciousness-bliss, without qualities, yet the storehouse of all qualities.
ramacharitamanas::1838.translation_literal: करहिं (do) / जोग (yoga) / जोगी (yogis) / जेहि लागी (for whom) / कोहु (anger) / मोहु (delusion) / ममता (possessiveness) / मदु (pride) / त्यागी (having abandoned) / ब्यापकु (all-pervading) / ब्रह्मु (Brahman) / अलखु (unseen) / अबिनासी (imperishable) / चिदानंदु (consciousness-bliss) / निरगुनु (without qualities) / गुनरासी (storehouse of qualities)
ramacharitamanas::1838.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1838.essence: What yogis seek is beyond anger, form, and decay.
ramacharitamanas::1838.simple_meaning: The yogis seek the supreme reality by dropping anger, delusion, possessiveness, and pride. That reality fills everything, cannot be seen directly, never perishes, and is beyond ordinary qualities.
ramacharitamanas::1838.simple_insight: The mind quiets when it stops chasing forms and starts resting in what never changes.
ramacharitamanas::1838.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, after the respectful greetings, the praise turns upward. The speaker is no longer describing the guests in the hall but the reality behind all appearances: the supreme reality that yogis seek by renouncing inner agitation.
ramacharitamanas::1838.modern_relevance: You sit in a silent room after a fight, replaying every sharp word. Beneath the noise, something in you knows that anger and possessiveness are not the whole of you.
ramacharitamanas::1838.insight: It shifts attention from emotional clutter to the unchanging reality that underlies it.

ramacharitamanas::1839.verse_sanskrit: मन समेत जेहि जान न बानी। तरकि न सकहिं सकल अनुमानी॥ महिमा निगमु नेति कहि कहई। जो तिहुँ काल एकरस रहई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1839.verse_hindi: जिनको मन सहित वाणी नहीं जानती और सब जिनका अनुमान ही करते हैं, कोई तर्कना नहीं कर सकते, जिनकी महिमा को वेद 'नेति' कहकर वर्णन करता है और जो (सच्चिदानंद) तीनों कालों में एकरस (सर्वदा और सर्वथा निर्विकार) रहते हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1839.english_translation: The mind and speech cannot know him. All reasoning falls short. The Vedas describe his greatness by saying, “not this, not this.” He remains unchanged through all three times.
ramacharitamanas::1839.translation_literal: मन (mind) / समेत (along with) / जेहि (whom) / जान (know) / न (not) / बानी (speech) / तरकि (by reasoning) / न (not) / सकहिं (are able) / सकल (all) / अनुमानि (by inference) / महिमा (greatness) / निगमु (the Veda) / नेति (not this) / कहि (saying) / कहई (says) / जो (who) / तिहुँ (three) / काल (times) / एकरस (unchanged, of one taste) / रहई (remains)
ramacharitamanas::1839.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1839.essence: The highest reality cannot be captured, only recognised.
ramacharitamanas::1839.simple_meaning: Ram's true nature cannot be fully grasped by mind, speech, or logic. Even the Vedas point to him by saying he is beyond all descriptions and remains unchanged through past, present, and future.
ramacharitamanas::1839.simple_insight: Not everything real can be captured by thought. Some truths are known by reverence, not argument.
ramacharitamanas::1839.detailed_meaning: In the Sita-swayamvar, the sages have already praised Ram's glory. Tulsidas now lifts the vision higher: Ram is beyond mind, speech, and logic, yet fully present and unchanged in every age. This is the climax of praise before the final blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1839.modern_relevance: You keep trying to explain a loss, a love, or a calling to yourself late at night, and the words keep failing. Some realities are too vast for analysis; they ask for humility instead.
ramacharitamanas::1839.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to define the highest reality to bowing before what cannot be reduced.

ramacharitamanas::1840.verse_sanskrit: नयन बिषय मो कहुँ भयउ सो समस्त सुख मूल। सबइ लाभु जग जीव कहँ भएँ ईसु अनुकूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::1840.verse_hindi: वे ही समस्त सुखों के मूल (आप) मेरे नेत्रों के विषय हुए। ईश्वर के अनुकूल होने पर जगत में जीव को सब लाभ ही लाभ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1840.english_translation: Your form, which my eyes behold, has become the root of all happiness. When the divine is favorable, every gain comes to the living being in the world.
ramacharitamanas::1840.translation_literal: नयन (eyes) / बिषय (object of sight) / मो (to me) / कहुँ (for) / भयउ (became) / सो (that) / समस्त (all) / सुख (happiness) / मूल (root) / सबइ (all) / लाभु (gain) / जग (world) / जीव (living being) / कहँ (for) / भएँ (when becoming) / ईसु (the divine) / अनुकूल (favorable)
ramacharitamanas::1840.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1840.essence: Seeing Ram turns ordinary life into abundance.
ramacharitamanas::1840.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram has become the source of all joy. When life is aligned with the divine, nothing is truly lacking.
ramacharitamanas::1840.simple_insight: Relief comes from knowing that grace changes everything, even ordinary seeing.
ramacharitamanas::1840.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, the speaker is overwhelmed by Ram's presence after describing the supreme, formless reality. Now that same greatness appears before the eyes as Ram's visible form, and the heart realises that divine favor turns life itself into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1840.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone who steadied your whole life, and suddenly the room feels different. What once felt ordinary now feels like grace showing up in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::1840.insight: It shifts attention from chasing gains to recognising that alignment with the divine is the real gain.

ramacharitamanas::1841.verse_sanskrit: सबहि भाँति मोहि दीन्हि बड़ाई। निज जन जानि लीन्ह अपनाई॥ होहिं सहस दस सारद सेषा। करहिं कलप कोटिक भरि लेखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1841.verse_hindi: आपने मुझे सभी प्रकार से बड़ाई दी और अपना जन जानकर अपना लिया। यदि दस हजार सरस्वती और शेष हों और करोड़ों कल्पों तक गणना करते रहें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1841.english_translation: You have honored me in every way and accepted me as your own. Even ten thousand Saraswatis and Shesha, counting for countless ages, could not finish the account.
ramacharitamanas::1841.translation_literal: सबहि भाँति (in every way) / मोहि (me) / दीन्हि (gave) / बड़ाई (honor, greatness) / निज जन (your own person, your own devotee) / जानि (knowing) / लीन्ह (took) / अपनाई (as one’s own) / होहिं (would become) / सहस दस (ten thousand) / सारद (Saraswati) / सेषा (Shesha) / करहिं (would do) / कलप कोटिक (crores of kalpas) / भरि (filling) / लेखा (counting, account)
ramacharitamanas::1841.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1841.essence: Ram's grace is so complete that praise itself runs out.
ramacharitamanas::1841.simple_meaning: Ram has shown full grace by honoring the speaker and taking him as his own. That kindness is too vast for endless counting to describe.
ramacharitamanas::1841.simple_insight: Being accepted by the divine can feel larger than language itself.
ramacharitamanas::1841.detailed_meaning: In the middle of Tulsidas's praise, he turns from describing Ram's greatness to his own amazement. Ram has not merely listened; he has claimed the devotee as his own. The poet says even endless divine speech and cosmic memory could not measure that favor.
ramacharitamanas::1841.modern_relevance: You finally get a message from someone you admire: not a polite reply, but real warmth, real welcome. The relief is bigger than the words themselves.
ramacharitamanas::1841.insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to belonging: the devotee is not outside Ram's care, but counted as one of his own.

ramacharitamanas::1842.verse_sanskrit: मोर भाग्य राउर गुन गाथा। कहि न सिराहिं सुनहु रघुनाथा॥ मैं कछु कहउँ एक बल मोरें। तुम्ह रीझहु सनेह सुठि थोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1842.verse_hindi: तो भी हे रघुनाजी! सुनिए, मेरे सौभाग्य और आपके गुणों की कथा कहकर समाप्त नहीं की जा सकती। मैं जो कुछ कह रहा हूँ, वह अपने इस एक ही बल पर कि आप अत्यन्त थोड़े प्रेम से प्रसन्न हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1842.english_translation: Even so, O Raghunath, the story of my good fortune and your virtues cannot be finished. I speak only on the strength that you are pleased by even a little affection.
ramacharitamanas::1842.translation_literal: मोर (my) / भाग्य (fortune) / राउर (your) / गुन (virtues) / गाथा (story, praise) / कहि (saying) / न (not) / सिराहिं (comes to an end) / सुनहु (listen) / रघुनाथा (Raghunath) / मैं (I) / कछु (something) / कहउँ (say) / एक (one) / बल (strength) / मोरें (in me) / तुम्ह (you) / रीझहु (are pleased) / सनेह (affection, love) / सुठि (very) / थोरें (little)
ramacharitamanas::1842.speaker: Janak
ramacharitamanas::1842.essence: A little true love is enough to please Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1842.simple_meaning: Janak says he can never finish praising Ram's virtues, but he dares to speak because Ram is pleased even by a little love.
ramacharitamanas::1842.simple_insight: You do not need perfection to approach Ram; sincere affection is enough to open the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1842.detailed_meaning: In Janak's wedding court, the king is speaking to Ram after the swayamvar. Overwhelmed by Ram's grace, he admits that Ram's virtues cannot be fully described. Yet he continues, because Ram responds to even a small amount of loving devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1842.modern_relevance: You rehearse what to say before sending the message, afraid it won't be enough. Then you remember that real closeness is not built on polished words, but on honest affection.
ramacharitamanas::1842.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to sincerity: the smallest true offering can be enough.

ramacharitamanas::1843.verse_sanskrit: बार बार मागउँ कर जोरें। मनु परिहरै चरन जनि भोरें॥ सुनि बर बचन प्रेम जनु पोषे। पूरनकाम रामु परितोषे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1843.verse_hindi: मैं बार-बार हाथ जोड़कर यह माँगता हूँ कि मेरा मन भूलकर भी आपके चरणों को न छोड़े। जनकजी के श्रेष्ठ वचनों को सुनकर, जो मानो प्रेम से पुष्ट किए हुए थे, पूर्ण काम श्री रामचन्द्रजी संतुष्ट हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1843.english_translation: Again and again, with hands joined, I ask that my mind never turn away from your feet. Hearing Janak's noble words, lovingly nourished, Ram was delighted, the fulfilled one pleased completely.
ramacharitamanas::1843.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / मागउँ (I ask) / कर जोरें (with joined hands) / मनु (mind) / परिहरै (may abandon) / चरन (feet) / जनि (never) / भोरें (by mistake) || सुनि (hearing) / बर (excellent) / बचन (words) / प्रेम (love) / जनु (as if) / पोषे (nourished) / पूरनकाम (fully fulfilled) / रामु (Ram) / परितोषे (was pleased)
ramacharitamanas::1843.speaker: Janak
ramacharitamanas::1843.essence: True devotion asks only to remain at Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::1843.simple_meaning: Janak humbly asks Ram not to let his mind ever stray from Ram's feet. Ram hears these loving words and feels fully pleased.
ramacharitamanas::1843.simple_insight: Deep devotion can be a request for constancy, not just a moment of feeling.
ramacharitamanas::1843.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the wedding blessings are being exchanged. Janak speaks with folded hands, asking for one thing above all: that his mind never forget Ram's feet. Ram hears this love-filled humility and is completely pleased.
ramacharitamanas::1843.modern_relevance: At a wedding, someone speaks not about gifts or status, but about never letting love become casual. That kind of devotion still lands with force.
ramacharitamanas::1843.insight: It shifts devotion from ceremony to inner loyalty, showing that love is proven by remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::1844.verse_sanskrit: करि बर बिनय ससुर सनमाने। पितु कौसिक बसिष्ठ सम जाने॥ बिनती बहुरि भरत सन कीन्ही। मिलि सप्रेमु पुनि आसिष दीन्ही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1844.verse_hindi: उन्होंने सुंदर विनती करके पिता दशरथजी, गुरु विश्वामित्रजी और कुलगुरु वशिष्ठजी के समान जानकर ससुर जनकजी का सम्मान किया। फिर जनकजी ने भरतजी से विनती की और प्रेम के साथ मिलकर फिर उन्हें आशीर्वाद दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1844.english_translation: After offering respectful greetings, he honored his father-in-law as he would his father, Kaushika, and Vasistha. Then he again made a request to Bharat, met him with affection, and gave blessings.
ramacharitamanas::1844.translation_literal: करि (doing) / बर (excellent) / बिनय (humble request) / ससुर (father-in-law) / सनमाने (honored) / पितु (father) / कौसिक (Kaushika) / बसिष्ठ (Vasistha) / सम (equal to) / जाने (considered) / बिनती (request) / बहुरि (again) / भरत (Bharat) / सन (with) / कीन्ही (did) / मिलि (meeting) / सप्रेमु (with love) / पुनि (again) / आसिष (blessings) / दीन्ही (gave)
ramacharitamanas::1844.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1844.essence: Honor creates family before blood does.
ramacharitamanas::1844.simple_meaning: Janak honors his in-laws and treats them like his own family. He then meets Bharat with affection, asks again, and gives blessings.
ramacharitamanas::1844.simple_insight: Respect deepens when it is extended beyond blood ties. Love becomes visible in how you greet, honor, and bless others.
ramacharitamanas::1844.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the wedding meeting continues after Sita's swayamvar. Janak receives Dasharath's side not as strangers but as his own kin, honoring them with full warmth. The scene shows royal courtesy becoming genuine family affection.
ramacharitamanas::1844.modern_relevance: At a wedding dinner, two families who barely knew each other start speaking with real warmth. No one is performing. Everyone feels the bridge being built in real time.
ramacharitamanas::1844.insight: It shifts attention from formal relations to shared regard, showing how affection can turn ceremony into kinship.

ramacharitamanas::1845.verse_sanskrit: मिले लखन रिपुसूदनहि दीन्हि असीस महीस। भए परसपर प्रेमबस फिरि फिरि नावहिं सीस ॥
ramacharitamanas::1845.verse_hindi: फिर राजा ने लक्ष्मणजी और शत्रुघ्नजी से मिलकर उन्हें आशीर्वाद दिया। वे परस्पर प्रेम के वश होकर बार-बार आपस में सिर नवाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1845.english_translation: Then the king met Lakshman and Shatrughna and gave them blessings. Overcome by mutual love, they bowed again and again to one another.
ramacharitamanas::1845.translation_literal: मिले (met) / लखन (Lakshman) / रिपुसूदनहि (to the foe-slayer) / दीन्हि (gave) / असीस (blessings) / महीस (the king) / भए (became) / परसपर (mutual) / प्रेमबस (under the sway of love) / फिरि फिरि (again and again) / नावहिं (bow) / सीस (heads)
ramacharitamanas::1845.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1845.essence: Love makes even formal bows feel endless.
ramacharitamanas::1845.simple_meaning: The king blesses Lakshman and Shatrughna, and everyone keeps bowing to one another out of affection.
ramacharitamanas::1845.simple_insight: Love softens rank and turns formal meeting into warmth.
ramacharitamanas::1845.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court after the wedding, the greetings continue. King Janak meets Lakshman and Shatrughna, blesses them, and the family keeps bowing again and again in mutual affection. It is a gentle bridge before Ram and his brothers depart.
ramacharitamanas::1845.modern_relevance: After a wedding dinner, two families stand at the doorway refusing to leave, each one bowing, blessing, and smiling through the goodbye. No one wants the moment to end.
ramacharitamanas::1845.insight: It shows how respect deepens when affection is real, not forced by status.

ramacharitamanas::1846.verse_sanskrit: बार बार करि बिनय बड़ाई। रघुपति चले संग सब भाई॥ जनक गहे कौसिक पद जाई। चरन रेनु सिर नयनन्ह लाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1846.verse_hindi: जनकजी की बार-बार विनती और बड़ाई करके श्री रघुनाथजी सब भाइयों के साथ चले। जनकजी ने जाकर विश्वामित्रजी के चरण पकड़ लिए और उनके चरणों की रज को सिर और नेत्रों में लगाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1846.english_translation: After repeatedly offering praise and respect, Lord Raghunath set out with all his brothers. Janak went and clasped Vishwamitra's feet, then placed the dust of those feet on his head and eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1846.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / करि (having done) / बिनय (humble request) / बड़ाई (praise) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / चले (went) / संग (with) / सब (all) / भाई (brothers)॥ / जनक (Janak) / गहे (grasped) / कौसिक (Vishwamitra) / पद (feet) / जाई (going) / चरन (feet) / रेनु (dust) / सिर (head) / नयनन्ह (eyes) / लाई (applied)॥
ramacharitamanas::1846.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1846.essence: True honour is shown by bowing, not by words alone.
ramacharitamanas::1846.simple_meaning: Ram leaves with his brothers after honoring Janak. Janak bows to Vishwamitra and places the dust of the guru's feet on his head and eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1846.simple_insight: Respect can be shown without words alone; the body itself can become prayer.
ramacharitamanas::1846.detailed_meaning: The wedding celebration is ending, and the two great families are parting with warmth. Ram leaves with his brothers after honoring Janak, while Janak humbly bows to Vishwamitra and touches his feet-dust to his head and eyes. The scene shows mutual reverence, not just farewell.
ramacharitamanas::1846.modern_relevance: At the end of a wedding, everyone is smiling for photos, but one elder still bends fully to touch a teacher's feet. The gesture says what the celebration cannot: gratitude is real when it becomes action.
ramacharitamanas::1846.insight: It shifts respect from polite feeling to embodied humility and gratitude.

ramacharitamanas::1847.verse_sanskrit: सुनु मुनीस बर दरसन तोरें। अगमु न कछु प्रतीति मन मोरें॥ जो सुखु सुजसु लोकपति चहहीं। करत मनोरथ सकुचत अहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1847.verse_hindi: (उन्होंने कहा-) हे मुनीश्वर! सुनिए, आपके सुंदर दर्शन से कुछ भी दुर्लभ नहीं है, मेरे मन में ऐसा विश्वास है, जो सुख और सुयश लोकपाल चाहते हैं, परन्तु (असंभव समझकर) जिसका मनोरथ करते हुए सकुचाते हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::1847.english_translation: Listen, sage lord: by your sight, nothing is impossible to me. My mind believes that the joy and fame even the rulers of the world desire, yet hesitate to seek, are within reach.
ramacharitamanas::1847.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / मुनीस (sage-lord) / बर (excellent) / दरसन (sight) / तोरें (by your) / अगमु (inaccessible) / न (not) / कछु (anything) / प्रतीति (trust/conviction) / मन (mind) / मोरें (my)॥ / जो (which) / सुखु (joy) / सुजसु (fame) / लोकपति (rulers of the world) / चहहीं (desire)॥ / करत (doing) / मनोरथ (wish/desire) / सकुचत (hesitate) / अहहीं (they are)
ramacharitamanas::1847.speaker: Janaka
ramacharitamanas::1847.essence: True presence makes the impossible feel ordinary.
ramacharitamanas::1847.simple_meaning: Janaka says that seeing the sage has removed all doubt from his mind. Even the highest joys and honors now seem attainable.
ramacharitamanas::1847.simple_insight: Faith can shrink fear until the impossible feels reachable.
ramacharitamanas::1847.detailed_meaning: In Janaka’s court, the king bows before Vishwamitra after Ram’s arrival. Overwhelmed, he says the sage’s presence has erased hesitation from his mind. What even rulers long for but fear to ask now feels possible.
ramacharitamanas::1847.modern_relevance: You walk into a room expecting rejection, but one person’s calm welcome changes everything. Suddenly the conversation you were afraid to start feels easy.
ramacharitamanas::1847.insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to confidence through the power of sacred presence.

ramacharitamanas::1848.verse_sanskrit: सो सुखु सुजसु सुलभ मोहि स्वामी। सब सिधि तव दरसन अनुगामी॥ कीन्हि बिनय पुनि पुनि सिरु नाई। फिरे महीसु आसिषा पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1848.verse_hindi: हे स्वामी! वही सुख और सुयश मुझे सुलभ हो गया, सारी सिद्धियाँ आपके दर्शनों की अनुगामिनी अर्थात पीछे-पीछे चलने वाली हैं। इस प्रकार बार-बार विनती की और सिर नवाकर तथा उनसे आशीर्वाद पाकर राजा जनक लौटे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1848.english_translation: O Lord, that very happiness and fame have become easy for me to attain. All powers follow after your sight. Thus the king bowed his head again and again, offered repeated prayers, and returned after receiving blessings.
ramacharitamanas::1848.translation_literal: सो (that) / सुखु (happiness) / सुजसु (good fame) / सुलभ (easy to attain) / मोहि (for me) / स्वामी (lord) / सब (all) / सिधि (powers, attainments) / तव (your) / दरसन (sight, vision) / अनुगामी (following) / कीन्हि (did) / बिनय (request, prayer) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing) / फिरे (returned) / महीसु (king) / आसिषा (blessings) / पाई (having received)
ramacharitamanas::1848.speaker: Janaka
ramacharitamanas::1848.essence: Humility makes even honor and success feel effortless.
ramacharitamanas::1848.simple_meaning: Janaka tells Vishwamitra that true happiness and honour come easily through his sight. He bows again and again, asks for blessings, and then leaves.
ramacharitamanas::1848.simple_insight: Respect and humility open the door to blessings that pride cannot reach.
ramacharitamanas::1848.detailed_meaning: Janaka has just welcomed Ram, Lakshman, and Vishwamitra with deep honor. Overwhelmed by the sage's presence, he bows repeatedly, speaks with reverence, and receives blessings before returning. The scene shows royal dignity turning into humble devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1848.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence quietly changes the room. Instead of performing, you soften, listen, and let respect replace self-importance.
ramacharitamanas::1848.insight: It shifts the response from status-protection to humble receptivity, where blessing becomes possible.

ramacharitamanas::1849.verse_sanskrit: चली बरात निसान बजाई। मुदित छोट बड़ सब समुदाई॥ रामहि निरखि ग्राम नर नारी। पाइ नयन फलु होहिं सुखारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1849.verse_hindi: डंका बजाकर बारात चली। छोटे-बड़े सभी समुदाय प्रसन्न हैं। (रास्ते के) गाँव के स्त्री-पुरुष श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर नेत्रों का फल पाकर सुखी होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1849.english_translation: The wedding procession set out with drums beating. Small and large alike in the whole assembly were delighted. Seeing Ram, the men and women of the villages felt their eyes had found their true reward and became joyful.
