ramacharitamanas::1890.detailed_meaning: The wedding celebration in Ayodhya is ending in joy. King Dasharath is not holding back; he gives beggars what they ask and honors the servants and musicians with gifts. The scene shows abundance expressed as cheerful giving.
ramacharitamanas::1890.modern_relevance: At the end of a wedding, someone quietly makes sure the caterers, drivers, and helpers leave with extra envelopes and full stomachs. Real gratitude shows up as generous, specific giving.
ramacharitamanas::1890.insight: It shifts attention from celebrating the event to honoring everyone who made it possible.

ramacharitamanas::1891.verse_sanskrit: देहिं असीस जोहारि सब गावहिं गुन गन गाथ। तब गुर भूसुर सहित गृहँ गवनु कीन्ह नरनाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1891.verse_hindi: सब जोहार (वंदन) करके आशीष देते हैं और गुण समूहों की कथा गाते हैं। तब गुरु और ब्राह्मणों सहित राजा दशरथजी ने महल में गमन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1891.english_translation: Everyone bowed, gave blessings, and sang praises of his virtues. Then the king entered the palace with the guru and the brahmins.
ramacharitamanas::1891.translation_literal: देहिं (give) / असीस (blessings) / जोहारि (bowing respectfully) / सब (all) / गावहिं (sing) / गुन गन (clusters of virtues) / गाथ (songs, praises) / तब (then) / गुर (guru) / भूसुर (brahmins) / सहित (together with) / गृहँ (to the house/palace) / गवनु (going) / कीन्ह (did, made) / नरनाथ (king)
ramacharitamanas::1891.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1891.essence: Public joy fades into a dignified return home.
ramacharitamanas::1891.simple_meaning: People bowed, blessed the king, and sang his praises. Then Dasharath returned to the palace with the guru and the brahmins.
ramacharitamanas::1891.simple_insight: A good moment ends in gratitude, not applause. Respect flows naturally when conduct has been right.
ramacharitamanas::1891.detailed_meaning: The wedding atmosphere settles after the ceremony. The people bless Dasharath, praise his virtues, and he returns home with Vashishtha and the brahmins. The verse simply closes the scene before the next household events begin.
ramacharitamanas::1891.modern_relevance: After a long ceremony, the guests linger by the gate, smiling, offering blessings, and slowly drifting home. The big moment is over; what remains is quiet respect.
ramacharitamanas::1891.insight: It closes the scene with honor and transition, not a new teaching.

ramacharitamanas::1892.verse_sanskrit: जो बसिष्ट अनुसासन दीन्ही। लोक बेद बिधि सादर कीन्ही॥ भूसुर भीर देखि सब रानी। सादर उठीं भाग्य बड़ जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1892.verse_hindi: वशिष्ठजी ने जो आज्ञा दी, उसे लोक और वेद की विधि के अनुसार राजा ने आदरपूर्वक किया। ब्राह्मणों की भीड़ देखकर अपना बड़ा भाग्य जानकर सब रानियाँ आदर के साथ उठीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1892.english_translation: Vashishtha's instructions were carried out with reverence according to worldly custom and Vedic rule. Seeing the crowd of brahmins, all the queens rose respectfully, knowing their great good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::1892.translation_literal: जो (which) / बसिष्ट (Vashishtha) / अनुसासन (instruction) / दीन्ही (given) / लोक (worldly custom) / बेद (Veda) / बिधि (rule) / सादर (respectfully) / कीन्ही (done)॥ / भूसुर (brahmins) / भीर (crowd) / देखि (seeing) / सब (all) / रानी (queens) / सादर (respectfully) / उठीं (rose) / भाग्य (fortune) / बड़ (great) / जानी (knowing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1892.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1892.essence: Respect is proved by how you rise for others.
ramacharitamanas::1892.simple_meaning: Vashishtha's instructions are followed with respect, and the queens rise when they see the gathered brahmins, feeling blessed by the honor.
ramacharitamanas::1892.simple_insight: Respect becomes visible in small gestures: rising, receiving, and honoring the people in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::1892.detailed_meaning: At Dasharath's palace celebration, Vashishtha gives the order for the ceremony. The king and queens respond exactly as tradition requires. This verse shows the reverence that frames the feast before the real honoring begins.
ramacharitamanas::1892.modern_relevance: A respected elder enters the room, and everyone quietly stands. No speech is needed — the room itself shows who is being honored.
ramacharitamanas::1892.insight: It teaches deference through action: honor is not felt privately, but enacted in public conduct.

ramacharitamanas::1893.verse_sanskrit: पाय पखारि सकल अन्हवाए। पूजि भली बिधि भूप जेवाँए॥ आदर दान प्रेम परिपोषे। देत असीस चले मन तोषे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1893.verse_hindi: चरण धोकर उन्होंने सबको स्नान कराया और राजा ने भली-भाँति पूजन करके उन्हें भोजन कराया! आदर, दान और प्रेम से पुष्ट हुए वे संतुष्ट मन से आशीर्वाद देते हुए चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::1893.english_translation: He washed their feet, bathed them all, worshipped them properly, and fed them. Honored with gifts and loved deeply, they left content, giving blessings.
ramacharitamanas::1893.translation_literal: पाय (feet) / पखारि (washing) / सकल (all) / अन्हवाए (bade bathe) / पूजि (worshipping) / भली बिधि (in proper manner) / भूप (the king) / जेवाँए (fed, caused to eat) / आदर (respect) / दान (gifts) / प्रेम (love) / परिपोषे (nourished, cherished) / देत (giving) / असीस (blessings) / चले (left, went) / मन तोषे (with contented mind)
ramacharitamanas::1893.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1893.essence: Honor becomes complete when care is made visible.
ramacharitamanas::1893.simple_meaning: King Dasharath honors the guests with foot-washing, bathing, worship, food, gifts, and loving respect. The guests leave pleased and blessing him.
ramacharitamanas::1893.simple_insight: True honor is shown through care, generosity, and humility.
ramacharitamanas::1893.detailed_meaning: At Dasharath's court in Ayodhya, the guests have arrived after Vashishtha's instruction. The king receives them not as burdens but as sacred visitors: washing their feet, serving food, giving gifts, and sending them away with blessings.
ramacharitamanas::1893.modern_relevance: Someone comes to your home tired from travel, and you stop everything to make them comfortable. No performance, no display — just wholehearted hospitality that leaves both people lighter.
ramacharitamanas::1893.insight: It shifts attention from status to service, showing that respect becomes real only when it is enacted.

ramacharitamanas::1894.verse_sanskrit: बहु बिधि कीन्हि गाधिसुत पूजा। नाथ मोहि सम धन्य न दूजा॥ कीन्हि प्रसंसा भूपति भूरी। रानिन्ह सहित लीन्हि पग धूरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1894.verse_hindi: राजा ने गाधि पुत्र विश्वामित्रजी की बहुत तरह से पूजा की और कहा- हे नाथ! मेरे समान धन्य दूसरा कोई नहीं है। राजा ने उनकी बहुत प्रशंसा की और रानियों सहित उनकी चरणधूलि को ग्रहण किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1894.english_translation: The king honored Vishwamitra, son of Gadhi, in many ways and said, “O Lord, no one is as blessed as I am.” He praised him greatly and, with the queens, took the dust of his feet.
ramacharitamanas::1894.translation_literal: बहु बिधि (in many ways) / कीन्हि (did) / गाधिसुत (son of Gadhi) / पूजा (honor, worship) / नाथ (Lord) / मोहि (me) / सम (like, equal to) / धन्य (blessed) / न दूजा (no second) / कीन्हि (did) / प्रसंसा (praise) / भूपति (king) / भूरी (greatly, abundantly) / रानिन्ह (with the queens) / सहित (together with) / लीन्हि (took) / पग धूरी (dust of the feet)
ramacharitamanas::1894.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1894.essence: True honor begins when pride is willing to bow.
ramacharitamanas::1894.simple_meaning: King Dasharath honors Vishwamitra with gifts, praise, and humility. He even takes the dust from Vishwamitra’s feet along with the queens.
ramacharitamanas::1894.simple_insight: Respect becomes complete when pride disappears.
ramacharitamanas::1894.detailed_meaning: At Dasharath’s court in Balkand, Vishwamitra has arrived as a revered guest. The king does not merely greet him; he worships him, praises him, and humbly takes the dust of his feet with the queens present. The scene shows royal humility before the sage.
ramacharitamanas::1894.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose experience dwarfs your own, and you stop performing. You listen, thank them properly, and let your pride kneel first.
ramacharitamanas::1894.insight: It teaches the reader to honor genuine greatness without self-importance.

ramacharitamanas::1895.verse_sanskrit: भीतर भवन दीन्ह बर बासू। मन जोगवत रह नृपु रनिवासू॥ पूजे गुर पद कमल बहोरी। कीन्हि बिनय उर प्रीति न थोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1895.verse_hindi: उन्हें महल के भीतर ठहरने को उत्तम स्थान दिया, जिसमें राजा और सब रनिवास उनका मन जोहता रहे (अर्थात जिसमें राजा और महल की सारी रानियाँ स्वयं उनकी इच्छानुसार उनके आराम की ओर दृष्टि रख सकें) फिर राजा ने गुरु वशिष्ठजी के चरणकमलों की पूजा और विनती की। उनके हृदय में कम प्रीति न थी (अर्थात बहुत प्रीति थी) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1895.english_translation: A fine residence was given inside the palace. The king and the queens kept watch over their comfort. Then the king worshiped the guru's lotus feet and bowed with deep love in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::1895.translation_literal: भीतर (inside) / भवन (house, palace) / दीन्ह (gave) / बर (excellent) / बासू (dwelling) / मन (mind) / जोगवत (watching over, attending) / रह (remained) / नृपु (king) / रनिवासू (women's quarters, queens) / पूजे (worshiped) / गुर (teacher) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / बहोरी (again) / कीन्हि (did) / बिनय (humble request, bowing) / उर (heart) / प्रीति (love) / न (not) / थोरी (little)
ramacharitamanas::1895.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1895.essence: True honor is shown through care and humility, not rank.
ramacharitamanas::1895.simple_meaning: The king gave the visitors a good place to stay, made sure they were cared for, and bowed to his guru with deep respect and love.
ramacharitamanas::1895.simple_insight: Respect becomes real when it shows up as care, not just words.
ramacharitamanas::1895.detailed_meaning: At King Janak's court, the honored guests are settled inside the palace with careful attention from the king and queens. After arranging their comfort, Janak turns to Vashistha, worships his feet, and offers heartfelt humility. The moment shows royal hospitality joined to reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1895.modern_relevance: A guest arrives after a long journey, and you make sure the room is ready before you ask anything of them. Then you thank the mentor who made the meeting possible. Care and humility together change the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::1895.insight: It shifts attention from status to service: first care for others, then bow to the source of guidance.

ramacharitamanas::1896.verse_sanskrit: बधुन्ह समेत कुमार सब रानिन्ह सहित महीसु। पुनि पुनि बंदत गुर चरन देत असीस मुनीसु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1896.verse_hindi: बहुओं सहित सब राजकुमार और सब रानियों समेत राजा बार-बार गुरुजी के चरणों की वंदना करते हैं और मुनीश्वर आशीर्वाद देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1896.english_translation: With the princes, their wives, and the queens together, the king repeatedly bowed at the guru's feet, and the sage gave his blessings.
ramacharitamanas::1896.translation_literal: बधुन्ह (with daughters-in-law) / समेत (together with) / कुमार (princes) / सब (all) / रानिन्ह (queens) / सहित (along with) / महीसु (king) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / बंदत (bowing) / गुर (guru's) / चरन (feet) / देत (giving) / असीस (blessings) / मुनीसु (sage)
ramacharitamanas::1896.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1896.essence: Humility becomes complete when an entire household bows together.
ramacharitamanas::1896.simple_meaning: The king, his sons, their wives, and the queens all bow again and again to the guru, and the sage blesses them.
ramacharitamanas::1896.simple_insight: Respect deepens when an entire family bows together.
ramacharitamanas::1896.detailed_meaning: After welcoming Vishwamitra with honor, King Dasharath brings his whole household before the sage. The princes, queens, and daughters-in-law bow repeatedly at his feet, and Vishwamitra responds with blessings. It is a ceremonial moment of reverence, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::1896.modern_relevance: A family gathers before an elder who has shaped their lives. No one performs for show; everyone simply bows, listens, and receives blessing with humility.
ramacharitamanas::1896.insight: It highlights reverence as a shared family act, not a private gesture.

ramacharitamanas::1897.verse_sanskrit: बिनय कीन्हि उर अति अनुरागें। सुत संपदा राखि सब आगें॥ नेगु मागि मुनिनायक लीन्हा। आसिरबादु बहुत बिधि दीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1897.verse_hindi: राजा ने अत्यन्त प्रेमपूर्ण हृदय से पुत्रों को और सारी सम्पत्ति को सामने रखकर (उन्हें स्वीकार करने के लिए) विनती की, परन्तु मुनिराज ने (पुरोहित के नाते) केवल अपना नेग माँग लिया और बहुत तरह से आशीर्वाद दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1897.english_translation: With great affection in his heart, the king placed his sons and all his wealth before the sage and made his request. The sage accepted only the customary honor-gift and gave blessings in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::1897.translation_literal: बिनय (humble request) / कीन्हि (made) / उर (heart) / अति अनुरागें (with great affection) / सुत (sons) / संपदा (wealth) / राखि (placing) / सब (all) / आगें (before) / नेगु (customary honor-gift) / मागि (asking) / मुनिनायक (leader of sages) / लीन्हा (took) / आसिरबादु (blessings) / बहुत बिधि (in many ways) / दीन्हा (gave)
ramacharitamanas::1897.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1897.essence: Honor matters more than wealth when reverence is real.
ramacharitamanas::1897.simple_meaning: Dasharath respectfully offers his sons and wealth to the sage, but the sage asks only for the customary honor-gift and blesses them generously.
ramacharitamanas::1897.simple_insight: True respect is shown by humility, not by trying to buy favor.
ramacharitamanas::1897.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court during the Sita swayamvar, King Dasharath greets Sage Vishvamitra with deep affection. He offers his sons and riches in welcome, but the sage accepts only the formal honor-gift and then blesses everyone before moving on.
ramacharitamanas::1897.modern_relevance: You meet someone important and start offering favors, gifts, and leverage. They do not want your display of abundance — only sincerity and the right gesture.
ramacharitamanas::1897.insight: It shifts attention from material display to proper respect and simple generosity.

ramacharitamanas::1898.verse_sanskrit: उर धरि रामहि सीय समेता। हरषि कीन्ह गुर गवनु निकेता॥ बिप्रबधू सब भूप बोलाईं। चैल चारु भूषन पहिराईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1898.verse_hindi: फिर सीताजी सहित श्री रामचन्द्रजी को हृदय में रखकर गुरु वशिष्ठजी हर्षित होकर अपने स्थान को गए। राजा ने सब ब्राह्मणों की स्त्रियों को बुलवाया और उन्हें सुंदर वस्त्र तथा आभूषण पहनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1898.english_translation: Holding Ram and Sita in his heart, the teacher returned home with joy. The king called all the wives of the Brahmins and dressed them in fine clothes and ornaments.
ramacharitamanas::1898.translation_literal: उर धरि (placing in the heart) / रामहि (Ram) / सीय समेता (together with Sita) / हरषि (rejoicing) / कीन्ह (did) / गुर (the teacher) / गवनु (return) / निकेता (to home) ॥ / बिप्रबधू (wives of Brahmins) / सब (all) / भूप (the king) / बोलाईं (called) / चैल (cloths) / चारु (beautiful) / भूषन (ornaments) / पहिराईं (had them wear) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1898.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1898.essence: Joy becomes complete when it turns into honoring others.
ramacharitamanas::1898.simple_meaning: Vashishtha leaves happily with Ram and Sita in his heart. King Janaka then calls the Brahmin women and honors them with beautiful clothes and ornaments.
ramacharitamanas::1898.simple_insight: True joy shows itself in blessing others, not just in receiving blessings.
ramacharitamanas::1898.detailed_meaning: The wedding ceremony is ending in Janakpur. Vashishtha departs, carrying Ram and Sita in his heart, while King Janaka turns to the Brahmin women and honors them with gifts. The scene shows gratitude, reverence, and generous hospitality after the sacred union.
ramacharitamanas::1898.modern_relevance: After a long family ceremony ends, the host does not rush to collapse. He thanks the guests, honors the elders, and sends everyone home with care. That is the dignity of a generous heart.
ramacharitamanas::1898.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony itself to the grace shown in how people are treated afterward.

ramacharitamanas::1899.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि बोलाइ सुआसिनि लीन्हीं। रुचि बिचारि पहिरावनि दीन्हीं॥ नेगी नेग जोग जब लेहीं। रुचि अनुरूप भूपमनि देहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1899.verse_hindi: फिर अब सुआसिनियों को (नगर की सौभाग्यवती बहिन, बेटी, भानजी आदि को) बुलवा लिया और उनकी रुचि समझकर (उसी के अनुसार) उन्हें पहिरावनी दी। नेगी लोग सब अपना-अपना नेग-जोग लेते और राजाओं के शिरोमणि दशरथजी उनकी इच्छा के अनुसार देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1899.english_translation: Then he called the married women and, understanding what each liked, gave them gifts and garments accordingly. The recipients took their customary gifts, and King Dasharath gave each one according to her wish.
ramacharitamanas::1899.translation_literal: बहुरि (again/then) / बोलाइ (having called) / सुआसिनि (married women) / लीन्हीं (he took/called them) / रुचि (preference/taste) / बिचारि (considering) / पहिरावनि (gifts of clothing) / दीन्हीं (gave) ॥ नेगी (customary gift-takers) / नेग (customary gift) / जोग (proper/fit) / जब (when) / लेहीं (they take) / रुचि (according to preference) / अनुरूप (matching) / भूपमनि (jewel among kings) / देहीं (gives) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1899.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1899.essence: True generosity meets each person where their heart already is.
ramacharitamanas::1899.simple_meaning: Dasharath honors the women at the wedding by giving each one gifts suited to her liking.
ramacharitamanas::1899.simple_insight: Respect grows when you notice what people actually value, not just what is convenient to give.
ramacharitamanas::1899.detailed_meaning: At Ram and Sita’s wedding in Mithila, King Dasharath is hosting guests with generous care. He calls the married women, considers their preferences, and gives each one fitting gifts. The scene shows royal hospitality before the marriage celebration continues.
ramacharitamanas::1899.modern_relevance: At a family wedding, one aunt loves silver bangles, another prefers a shawl, and a child only wants sweets. Real generosity notices the person, not just the price tag.
ramacharitamanas::1899.insight: It shifts giving from routine charity to attentive, person-shaped care.

ramacharitamanas::1900.verse_sanskrit: प्रिय पाहुने पूज्य जे जाने। भूपति भली भाँति सनमाने॥ देव देखि रघुबीर बिबाहू। बरषि प्रसून प्रसंसि उछाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1900.verse_hindi: जिन मेहमानों को प्रिय और पूजनीय जाना, उनका राजा ने भलीभाँति सम्मान किया। देवगण श्री रघुनाथजी का विवाह देखकर, उत्सव की प्रशंसा करके फूल बरसाते हुए- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1900.english_translation: The king honored the guests he regarded as dear and worthy of reverence. Seeing Raghubir's wedding, the divine beings praised the celebration and showered flowers.
ramacharitamanas::1900.translation_literal: प्रिय (dear) / पाहुने (guests) / पूज्य (worthy of reverence) / जे (who) / जाने (considered) / भूपति (the king) / भली भाँति (well) / सनमाने (honored) / देव (divine beings) / देखि (seeing) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / बिबाहू (wedding) / बरषि (showering) / प्रसून (flowers) / प्रसंसि (praising) / उछाहू (celebration)
ramacharitamanas::1900.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1900.essence: Honor the guests; the sacred joy answers with flowers.
ramacharitamanas::1900.simple_meaning: The king treated honored guests with respect. The divine beings rejoiced at Ram's wedding and showered flowers.
ramacharitamanas::1900.simple_insight: Joy becomes fuller when respect and celebration meet each other.
ramacharitamanas::1900.detailed_meaning: At Janak's wedding court, the formal honors continue after Ram and Sita's marriage. Guests are received with care, and the divine beings look on from above, praising the sacred joy and showering flowers on the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1900.modern_relevance: At a wedding reception, the host notices the elderly aunt, the quiet teacher, the distant cousin, and makes each one feel seen. That kind of grace turns a gathering into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1900.insight: It turns ceremony into reverence, showing that celebration and hospitality belong together.

ramacharitamanas::1901.verse_sanskrit: चले निसान बजाइ सुर निज निज पुर सुख पाइ। कहत परसपर राम जसु प्रेम न हृदयँ समाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1901.verse_hindi: नगाड़े बजाकर और (परम) सुख प्राप्त कर अपने-अपने लोकों को चले। वे एक-दूसरे से श्री रामजी का यश कहते जाते हैं। हृदय में प्रेम समाता नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1901.english_translation: The gods departed to their own abodes, beating drums in joy. They spoke among themselves of Ram's glory, and love would not fit within their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1901.translation_literal: चले (departed) / निसान (drums) / बजाइ (beating) / सुर (the radiant beings) / निज निज (their own) / पुर (abodes) / सुख पाइ (having found joy) / कहत (speaking) / परसपर (to one another) / राम जसु (Ram's glory) / प्रेम (love) / न हृदयँ (not in the heart) / समाइ (fits)
ramacharitamanas::1901.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1901.essence: True joy keeps turning into praise.
ramacharitamanas::1901.simple_meaning: The radiant beings left joyfully after the wedding, praising Ram among themselves. Their hearts were so full of love that it could not be contained.
ramacharitamanas::1901.simple_insight: When joy is real, praise spills out naturally and the heart feels too full to hold it all.
ramacharitamanas::1901.detailed_meaning: After Ram and Sita's wedding, the radiant beings return to their own realms beating drums. The celebration is so overwhelming that they keep speaking of Ram's glory to one another, unable to contain their love.
ramacharitamanas::1901.modern_relevance: You leave a wedding, still buzzing, and keep replaying the best moments with the friend beside you. The joy is so full it keeps turning into praise.
ramacharitamanas::1901.insight: It shows how devotion expresses itself as shared remembrance, not private feeling.

ramacharitamanas::1902.verse_sanskrit: सब बिधि सबहि समदि नरनाहू। रहा हृदयँ भरि पूरि उछाहू॥ जहँ रनिवासु तहाँ पगु धारे। सहित बहूटिन्ह कुअँर निहारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1902.verse_hindi: सब प्रकार से सबका प्रेमपूर्वक भली-भाँति आदर-सत्कार कर लेने पर राजा दशरथजी के हृदय में पूर्ण उत्साह (आनंद) भर गया। जहाँ रनिवास था, वे वहाँ पधारे और बहुओं समेत उन्होंने कुमारों को देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1902.english_translation: After honoring everyone properly, the king’s heart filled with joy. He then went to the queens’ residence and looked upon the princes with his daughters-in-law.
ramacharitamanas::1902.translation_literal: सब बिधि (in every way) / सबहि (everyone) / समदि (properly honored) / नरनाहू (king) / रहा (remained) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / भरि (filled) / पूरि (completely) / उछाहू (joy) / जहँ (where) / रनिवासु (women’s quarters) / तहाँ (there) / पगु (foot) / धारे (placed) / सहित (along with) / बहूटिन्ह (daughters-in-law) / कुअँर (princes) / निहारे (looked upon)
ramacharitamanas::1902.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1902.essence: Honor everyone first; joy naturally fills the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1902.simple_meaning: King Dasharath, full of joy after honoring his guests, goes to the queens’ quarters and looks at the princes with their wives.
ramacharitamanas::1902.simple_insight: Joy deepens when everyone has been respected and included.
ramacharitamanas::1902.detailed_meaning: The wedding feast has ended, and King Dasharath is overflowing with happiness. After sending the guests off with full honor, he walks into the queens’ residence and sees the princes with their wives. This is a quiet moment of family fullness before the next turn in the story.
ramacharitamanas::1902.modern_relevance: After hosting a wedding, you finally walk into the quiet house and see your family gathered, laughing in the kitchen. The relief is not in the event itself, but in everyone being safely together.
ramacharitamanas::1902.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to the human warmth that remains after ceremony ends.

ramacharitamanas::1903.verse_sanskrit: लिए गोद करि मोद समेता। को कहि सकइ भयउ सुखु जेता॥ बधू सप्रेम गोद बैठारीं। बार बार हियँ हरषि दुलारीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1903.verse_hindi: राजा ने आनंद सहित पुत्रों को गोद में ले लिया। उस समय राजा को जितना सुख हुआ उसे कौन कह सकता है? फिर पुत्रवधुओं को प्रेम सहित गोदी में बैठाकर, बार-बार हृदय में हर्षित होकर उन्होंने उनका दुलार (लाड़-चाव) किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1903.english_translation: The king joyfully took the sons into his lap. Who can describe the happiness he felt? Then he lovingly seated the daughters-in-law on his lap and, again and again delighted in his heart, caressed them tenderly.
ramacharitamanas::1903.translation_literal: लिए (took) / गोद (lap) / करि (doing) / मोद समेता (with joy) / को (who) / कहि (say) / सकइ (can) / भयउ (became) / सुखु (happiness) / जेता (as much as) / बधू (daughters-in-law) / सप्रेम (with love) / गोद (lap) / बैठारीं (seated) / बार बार (again and again) / हियँ (in heart) / हरषि (rejoicing) / दुलारीं (caressed, cherished)
ramacharitamanas::1903.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1903.essence: Joy becomes complete when it is shared through loving touch.
ramacharitamanas::1903.simple_meaning: Dasharath overflows with joy as he embraces his sons and lovingly welcomes the daughters-in-law.
ramacharitamanas::1903.simple_insight: Family love can be so full it becomes wordless.
ramacharitamanas::1903.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the wedding celebrations have just ended and Dasharath is surrounded by his sons and their brides. He lifts the sons into his lap, then seats the daughters-in-law with affection, unable to contain his happiness.
ramacharitamanas::1903.modern_relevance: You finally get everyone under one roof after a long wedding weekend. The noise is exhausting, the room is crowded, and yet one embrace makes the whole house feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::1903.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to tenderness, showing that affection is the real celebration.

ramacharitamanas::1904.verse_sanskrit: देखि समाजु मुदित रनिवासू। सब कें उर अनंद कियो बासू॥ कहेउ भूप जिमि भयउ बिबाहू। सुनि सुनि हरषु होत सब काहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1904.verse_hindi: यह समाज (समारोह) देखकर रनिवास प्रसन्न हो गया। सबके हृदय में आनंद ने निवास कर लिया। तब राजा ने जिस तरह विवाह हुआ था, वह सब कहा। उसे सुन-सुनकर सब किसी को हर्ष होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1904.english_translation: Seeing the gathering, the women in the inner chambers were delighted. Joy settled in every heart. Then the king told how the marriage had happened, and hearing it again and again, everyone felt happiness.
ramacharitamanas::1904.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / समाजु (gathering) / मुदित (delighted) / रनिवासू (inner chambers) / सब कें (in everyone) / उर (heart) / अनंद (joy) / कियो (made) / बासू (dwelling) / कहेउ (told) / भूप (king) / जिमि (how) / भयउ (happened) / बिबाहू (marriage) / सुनि सुनि (hearing again and again) / हरषु (happiness) / होत (happens) / सब (all) / काहू (to everyone)
ramacharitamanas::1904.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1904.essence: Joy multiplies when a beloved story is retold.
ramacharitamanas::1904.simple_meaning: The whole household feels joy as the king recounts the wedding, and everyone keeps listening with happiness.
ramacharitamanas::1904.simple_insight: Shared joy deepens when a loving story is told again.
ramacharitamanas::1904.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the wedding celebration has filled the palace with delight. Dasharath speaks about how the marriage took place, and the queens and attendants listen with growing happiness. This verse simply shows the joy spreading through the household.
ramacharitamanas::1904.modern_relevance: A family sits around the dinner table after a wedding, retelling the same beautiful moment from different angles. Nobody is bored; everyone keeps smiling because love becomes richer when it is remembered together.
ramacharitamanas::1904.insight: It shows how joyful memory can renew a whole room, turning narration itself into celebration.

ramacharitamanas::1905.verse_sanskrit: जनक राज गुन सीलु बड़ाई। प्रीति रीति संपदा सुहाई॥ बहुबिधि भूप भाट जिमि बरनी। रानीं सब प्रमुदित सुनि करनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1905.verse_hindi: राजा जनक के गुण, शील, महत्व, प्रीति की रीति और सुहावनी सम्पत्ति का वर्णन राजा ने भाट की तरह बहुत प्रकार से किया। जनकजी की करनी सुनकर सब रानियाँ बहुत प्रसन्न हुईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1905.english_translation: The king described Janak's virtues, noble character, loving conduct, and splendid wealth in many ways, like a bard. Hearing of Janak's deeds, all the queens were greatly pleased.
ramacharitamanas::1905.translation_literal: जनक राज (King Janak) / गुन (virtues) / सीलु (good character) / बड़ाई (greatness) / प्रीति (loving affection) / रीति (custom, conduct) / संपदा (wealth, prosperity) / सुहाइ (beautiful, pleasing)॥ / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / भूप (the king) / भाट जिमि (like a bard) / बरनी (described) / रानीं (the queens) / सब (all) / प्रमुदित (delighted) / सुनि (hearing) / करनी (deeds, conduct)॥
ramacharitamanas::1905.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1905.essence: True greatness is the kind that delights others when spoken aloud.
ramacharitamanas::1905.simple_meaning: Janak's virtues, conduct, love, and prosperity are praised at length, and the queens feel delighted hearing about him.
ramacharitamanas::1905.simple_insight: Good character can make a stranger feel like family.
ramacharitamanas::1905.detailed_meaning: At the wedding celebration in Ayodhya, the king speaks admiringly about Janak, praising his virtue, dignity, loving conduct, and grace. The queens listen and are pleased, showing how Janak's character has already won hearts before the feast continues.
ramacharitamanas::1905.modern_relevance: At a wedding dinner, someone tells stories about the bride's father — how steady, generous, and respected he is. The table softens. People who never met him feel warmth just hearing his name.
ramacharitamanas::1905.insight: It shifts attention from status to character, showing how conduct creates trust and joy.

ramacharitamanas::1906.verse_sanskrit: सुतन्ह समेत नहाइ नृप बोलि बिप्र गुर ग्याति। भोजन कीन्ह अनेक बिधि घरी पंच गइ राति॥।354॥
ramacharitamanas::1906.verse_hindi: पुत्रों सहित स्नान करके राजा ने ब्राह्मण, गुरु और कुटुम्बियों को बुलाकर अनेक प्रकार के भोजन किए। (यह सब करते-करते) पाँच घड़ी रात बीत गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1906.english_translation: After bathing with his sons, the king called the priests, the teacher, and his relatives, and they ate many kinds of food. Five watches of the night passed in this way.
ramacharitamanas::1906.translation_literal: सुतन्ह (with sons) / समेत (together) / नहाइ (having bathed) / नृप (the king) / बोलि (calling) / बिप्र (priests) / गुर (teacher) / ग्याति (relatives) / भोजन (food) / कीन्ह (did) / अनेक बिधि (in many ways) / घरी पंच (five watches) / गइ (passed) / राति (night)
ramacharitamanas::1906.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1906.essence: Joy ripens when the whole household is gathered.
ramacharitamanas::1906.simple_meaning: The king, his sons, priests, teacher, and relatives shared a festive meal after bathing. Time passed into the night as the celebration continued.
ramacharitamanas::1906.simple_insight: Shared joy deepens a sacred occasion. Celebration becomes complete when everyone is included.
ramacharitamanas::1906.detailed_meaning: At Janak's palace, after the wedding festivities, the king bathes with his sons and invites the priests, teacher, and relatives to feast. The night keeps moving as the celebration of Ram and Sita's union continues.
ramacharitamanas::1906.modern_relevance: A family reunion runs late after a wedding, with elders, cousins, and teachers all still gathered around the table. No one wants the evening to end.
ramacharitamanas::1906.insight: It keeps the focus on communal celebration, not private emotion, showing how joy is shared through ritual and hospitality.

ramacharitamanas::1907.verse_sanskrit: मंगलगान करहिं बर भामिनि। भै सुखमूल मनोहर जामिनि॥ अँचइ पान सब काहूँ पाए। स्रग सुगंध भूषित छबि छाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1907.verse_hindi: सुंदर स्त्रियाँ मंगलगान कर रही हैं। वह रात्रि सुख की मूल और मनोहारिणी हो गई। सबने आचमन करके पान खाए और फूलों की माला, सुगंधित द्रव्य आदि से विभूषित होकर सब शोभा से छा गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1907.english_translation: Beautiful women sang auspicious songs. The night became the very source of delight, lovely and sweet. Everyone received betel leaf and wereca nut, and they shone with garlands, fragrance, and adornment.
ramacharitamanas::1907.translation_literal: मंगलगान (auspicious songs) / करहिं (they sing) / बर भामिनि (beautiful women) / भै (became) / सुखमूल (source of delight) / मनोहर (lovely) / जामिनि (night) / अँचइ (having offered/received) / पान (betel leaf) / सब (all) / काहूँ (to everyone) / पाए (received) / स्रग (garlands) / सुगंध (fragrance) / भूषित (adorned) / छबि (beauty) / छाए (were covered/shone)
ramacharitamanas::1907.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1907.essence: Joy can turn even night into ornament.
ramacharitamanas::1907.simple_meaning: The celebration is in full swing. Women sing auspicious songs, everyone is adorned, and the whole night feels joyful and beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::1907.simple_insight: Some moments are meant to be received, not analysed.
ramacharitamanas::1907.detailed_meaning: Janak’s court is still in celebration after the bridegroom has been honored. Women sing auspicious songs, guests are given betel and flowers, and the whole night glows with festive beauty. This verse simply paints the atmosphere before the gathering disperses.
ramacharitamanas::1907.modern_relevance: At a wedding reception, the music keeps rising, trays keep moving, and every face looks softened by celebration. Nothing is being argued here — only joy filling the room.
ramacharitamanas::1907.insight: It shifts attention from event to atmosphere, letting the reader feel the fullness of the moment.

ramacharitamanas::1908.verse_sanskrit: रामहि देखि रजायसु पाई। निज निज भवन चले सिर नाई॥ प्रेम प्रमोदु बिनोदु बड़ाई। समउ समाजु मनोहरताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1908.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर और आज्ञा पाकर सब सिर नवाकर अपने-अपने घर को चले। वहाँ के प्रेम, आनंद, विनोद, महत्व, समय, समाज और मनोहरता को- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1908.english_translation: Seeing Ram and receiving his leave, everyone bowed their heads and returned to their own homes. The love, joy, delight, greatness, occasion, gathering, and beauty of that moment were beyond measure.
ramacharitamanas::1908.translation_literal: रामहि (Ram) / देखि (having seen) / रजायसु (leave, permission) / पाई (having received) / निज निज (each one's own) / भवन (home) / चले (went) / सिर (head) / नाई (bowing) / प्रेम (love) / प्रमोदु (joy) / बिनोदु (delight) / बड़ाई (greatness) / समउ (occasion, time) / समाजु (gathering) / मनोहरताई (beauty, charm)
ramacharitamanas::1908.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1908.essence: Ram's presence turns an ordinary departure into a scene of grace.
ramacharitamanas::1908.simple_meaning: After seeing Ram and receiving permission, everyone bowed and went home. The scene was full of love, joy, and beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1908.simple_insight: Some moments are so full of grace that even leaving them feels sacred.
ramacharitamanas::1908.detailed_meaning: The guests have honored Ram, eaten, sung, and shared the joy of his presence. Now, after receiving his permission, they bow and return home. Tulsidas pauses to show that the whole gathering has been transformed by love and beauty.
ramacharitamanas::1908.modern_relevance: The wedding ends, the last guest steps into the night, and no one wants the evening to break. You leave carrying the warmth of a room where everyone felt held.
ramacharitamanas::1908.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the atmosphere of love it creates.

ramacharitamanas::1909.verse_sanskrit: कहि न सकहिं सतसारद सेसू। बेद बिरंचि महेस गनेसू॥ सो मैं कहौं कवन बिधि बरनी। भूमिनागु सिर धरइ कि धरनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1909.verse_hindi: सैकड़ों सरस्वती, शेष, वेद, ब्रह्मा, महादेवजी और गणेशजी भी नहीं कह सकते। फिर भला मैं उसे किस प्रकार से बखानकर कहूँ? कहीं केंचुआ भी धरती को सिर पर ले सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1909.english_translation: Even a hundred Saraswatis, Shesha, the Vedas, Brahma, Mahesh, and Ganesha cannot describe it. How can I, then, tell it fully? Can an earthworm carry the earth on its head?
ramacharitamanas::1909.translation_literal: कहि (say) / न (not) / सकहिं (are able) / सतसारद (hundreds of Saraswati) / सेसू (Shesha) / बेद (Vedas) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / महेस (Mahesh) / गनेसू (Ganesha)॥ / सो (that) / मैं (I) / कहौं (say) / कवन (which) / बिधि (way) / बरनी (described) / भूमिनागु (earthworm) / सिर (head) / धरइ (carries) / कि (or) / धरनी (earth) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1909.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1909.essence: Greatness outruns speech; humility is the only faithful response.
ramacharitamanas::1909.simple_meaning: No one can fully describe what happened, not even the greatest beings and sages. The poet says he cannot carry the whole weight of it in words.
ramacharitamanas::1909.simple_insight: Some experiences are too vast for language; humility is the honest response.
ramacharitamanas::1909.detailed_meaning: The wedding hall has just emptied after Rama's swayamvar. The poet pauses before the next scene and bows to the limit of speech itself. Even cosmic powers cannot contain this glory, so the narration turns humble before moving on.
ramacharitamanas::1909.modern_relevance: You try to explain a moment that changed your life, and every sentence feels flat. Some things deserve reverence more than explanation.
ramacharitamanas::1909.insight: It teaches the reader to honor what exceeds description instead of forcing a neat summary.

ramacharitamanas::1910.verse_sanskrit: नृप सब भाँति सबहि सनमानी। कहि मृदु बचन बोलाईं रानी॥ बधू लरिकनीं पर घर आईं। राखेहु नयन पलक की नाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1910.verse_hindi: राजा ने सबका सब प्रकार से सम्मान करके, कोमल वचन कहकर रानियों को बुलाया और कहा- बहुएँ अभी बच्ची हैं, पराए घर आई हैं। इनको इस तरह से रखना जैसे नेत्रों को पलकें रखती हैं (जैसे पलकें नेत्रों की सब प्रकार से रक्षा करती हैं और उन्हें सुख पहुँचाती हैं, वैसे ही इनको सुख पहुँचाना) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1910.english_translation: The king honored everyone in every way, spoke gently, and called the queens, saying: "The daughters-in-law are still children and have come to another home. Care for them as the eyelids care for the eyes."
ramacharitamanas::1910.translation_literal: नृप (the king) / सब भाँति (in every way) / सबहि (everyone) / सनमानी (having honored) / कहि (saying) / मृदु (gentle) / बचन (words) / बोलाईं (called) / रानी (the queens) / बधू (daughters-in-law) / लरिकनीं (little girls/children) / पर घर (another home) / आईं (have come) / राखेहु (keep/care for) / नयन (eyes) / पलक की नाई (like the eyelids)
ramacharitamanas::1910.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1910.essence: Care for newcomers like eyes are guarded by eyelids.
ramacharitamanas::1910.simple_meaning: The king tells the queens to treat the young daughters-in-law with gentle care, like eyelids protect eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1910.simple_insight: Tenderness is not weakness. It is how a home protects what is precious and new.
ramacharitamanas::1910.detailed_meaning: After the wedding scene in Mithila, the king turns to the queens and speaks with warmth and respect. He asks them to shelter the young brides, who are still like children in a new home. The verse shows the household ideal of loving protection.
ramacharitamanas::1910.modern_relevance: A new daughter-in-law arrives with awkward silence, folded hands, and a heart trying not to show fear. The right response is not scrutiny, but care that makes her feel safe.
ramacharitamanas::1910.insight: It shifts attention from judging newcomers to protecting their dignity and ease.

ramacharitamanas::1911.verse_sanskrit: लरिका श्रमित उनीद बस सयन करावहु जाइ। अस कहि गे बिश्रामगृहँ राम चरन चितु लाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1911.verse_hindi: लड़के थके हुए नींद के वश हो रहे हैं, इन्हें ले जाकर शयन कराओ। ऐसा कहकर राजा श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में मन लगाकर विश्राम भवन में चले गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1911.english_translation: The children are tired and falling asleep. Take them and put them to bed. Saying this, he went to the rest house, fixing his mind on Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::1911.translation_literal: लरिका (children) / श्रमित (tired) / उनीद (sleepy) / बस (under the control of) / सयन (sleep) / करावहु (make to sleep) / जाइ (go) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / गे (went) / बिश्रामगृहँ (to the rest house) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / चितु (mind) / लाइ (fixing)
ramacharitamanas::1911.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1911.essence: Tender duty and inward devotion move together.
ramacharitamanas::1911.simple_meaning: The king tells the women to put the sleepy children to bed, then leaves for the rest house with his mind fixed on Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1911.simple_insight: Even in a royal household, care and reverence belong together.
ramacharitamanas::1911.detailed_meaning: The king has just welcomed everyone with gentle words. Now he notices the children are exhausted and asks that they be put to sleep. After speaking, he withdraws to the rest house, inwardly absorbed in Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1911.modern_relevance: A parent notices the kids nodding off after a long family gathering, quietly gets them settled, and then slips away without fuss. Care can be tender and inwardly devoted at the same time.
ramacharitamanas::1911.insight: It models calm responsibility: attend to practical needs first, then return the mind to what is sacred.

ramacharitamanas::1912.verse_sanskrit: भूप बचन सुनि सहज सुहाए। जरित कनक मनि पलँग डसाए॥ सुभग सुरभि पय फेन समाना। कोमल कलित सुपेतीं नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1912.verse_hindi: राजा के स्वाभव से ही सुंदर वचन सुनकर (रानियों ने) मणियों से जड़े सुवर्ण के पलँग बिछवाए। (गद्दों पर) गो के फेन के समान सुंदर एवं कोमल अनेकों सफेद चादरें बिछाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1912.english_translation: Hearing the king's gentle words, they spread jewel-studded golden beds. On them they laid many soft white coverings, beautiful like foaming milk.
ramacharitamanas::1912.translation_literal: भूप (king) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / सहज (naturally) / सुहाए (pleasing, beautiful) / जरित (studded, adorned) / कनक (gold) / मनि (jewels) / पलँग (beds) / डसाए (spread, laid out) / सुभग (beautiful) / सुरभि (fragrant, gentle) / पय (milk) / फेन (foam) / समाना (like) / कोमल (soft) / कलित (adorned) / सुपेतीं (white coverings) / नाना (various, many)
ramacharitamanas::1912.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1912.essence: Kind authority creates care without force.
ramacharitamanas::1912.simple_meaning: The royal women prepare luxurious beds and soft white coverings for the children after hearing the king's kind instructions.
ramacharitamanas::1912.simple_insight: Gentle words can turn a household from confusion into care.
ramacharitamanas::1912.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Dasharath asks the queens to look after the children, they immediately prepare rich beds and soft coverings. The verse lingers on the beauty of the room, showing the tenderness of a royal household responding to duty.
ramacharitamanas::1912.modern_relevance: A parent comes home exhausted after a hard day, and the family quietly sets out food, water, and a clean bed before a single complaint is spoken. Care begins with how you respond.
ramacharitamanas::1912.insight: It shifts attention from grand gestures to the quiet, immediate acts that make others feel protected.

ramacharitamanas::1913.verse_sanskrit: उपबरहन बर बरनि न जाहीं। स्रग सुगंध मनिमंदिर माहीं॥ रतनदीप सुठि चारु चँदोवा। कहत न बनइ जान जेहिं जोवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1913.verse_hindi: सुंदर तकियों का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। मणियों के मंदिर में फूलों की मालाएँ और सुगंध द्रव्य सजे हैं। सुंदर रत्नों के दीपकों और सुंदर चँदोवे की शोभा कहते नहीं बनती। जिसने उन्हें देखा हो, वही जान सकता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1913.english_translation: The cushions cannot be described. In the jeweled palace, garlands and fragrant offerings were arranged. The glow of jeweled lamps and the beauty of the canopy cannot be told; only one who has seen it knows.
ramacharitamanas::1913.translation_literal: उपबरहन (cushions / bedding) / बर बरनि न जाहीं (cannot be properly described) / स्रग (garland) / सुगंध (fragrance) / मनि-मंदिर (jeweled palace) / माहीं (within) / रतन-दीप (jeweled lamps) / सुठि (very) / चारु (beautiful) / चँदोवा (canopy) / कहत न बनइ (cannot be spoken of) / जान (one who knows / has seen) / जेहिं (by whom) / जोवा (seen)
ramacharitamanas::1913.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1913.essence: Some forms of care can only be felt, not fully described.
ramacharitamanas::1913.simple_meaning: The palace room is so beautifully arranged with cushions, flowers, fragrance, lamps, and a canopy that words cannot fully capture it.
ramacharitamanas::1913.simple_insight: Some beauty is beyond description; it must be directly experienced.
ramacharitamanas::1913.detailed_meaning: Inside Dasharath’s palace in Balkand, the women prepare a lavish resting place for Ram and his brothers. The verse lingers on the jeweled room, but only as a prelude to Ram being lovingly put to rest in the next line.
ramacharitamanas::1913.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after someone quietly prepared it for you: clean sheets, soft light, flowers, and everything in place. The care is obvious before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1913.insight: It shifts attention from the objects themselves to the love that arranged them.

ramacharitamanas::1914.verse_sanskrit: सेज रुचिर रचि रामु उठाए। प्रेम समेत पलँग पौढ़ाए॥ अग्या पुनि पुनि भाइन्ह दीन्ही। निज निज सेज सयन तिन्ह कीन्ही ॥
ramacharitamanas::1914.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार सुंदर शय्या सजाकर (माताओं ने) श्री रामचन्द्रजी को उठाया और प्रेम सहित पलँग पर पौढ़ाया। श्री रामजी ने बार-बार भाइयों को आज्ञा दी। तब वे भी अपनी-अपनी शय्याओं पर सो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1914.english_translation: After arranging a lovely bed, they laid Ram down on the couch with love. Again and again, he instructed his brothers, and then they all lay down in their own beds.
ramacharitamanas::1914.translation_literal: सेज (bed) / रुचिर (beautiful) / रचि (having arranged) / रामु (Ram) / उठाए (was lifted) / प्रेम समेत (with love) / पलँग (couch/bed) / पौढ़ाए (was laid down) / अग्या (instruction) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / भाइन्ह (to the brothers) / दीन्ही (gave) / निज निज (each one's own) / सेज (bed) / सयन (sleep) / तिन्ह (they) / कीन्ही (did)
ramacharitamanas::1914.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1914.essence: Ram's care reaches his brothers before his own rest.
ramacharitamanas::1914.simple_meaning: Ram is lovingly put to rest, and he makes sure his brothers also sleep in their own beds.
ramacharitamanas::1914.simple_insight: Care includes everyone. Even in comfort, Ram remains attentive to the people beside him.
ramacharitamanas::1914.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the mothers have prepared a beautiful resting place for Ram after the day's events. Ram is placed on the couch with affection, but he still turns to his brothers and gives them repeated instructions before they all sleep. The scene shows his loving care and household order, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1914.modern_relevance: After a long family gathering, everyone is tired and drifting toward bed. One person still checks that the younger siblings are settled, lights are off, and everyone is comfortable before resting.
ramacharitamanas::1914.insight: It shifts attention from private comfort to shared responsibility, even in small domestic moments.

ramacharitamanas::1915.verse_sanskrit: देखि स्याम मृदु मंजुल गाता। कहहिं सप्रेम बचन सब माता॥ मारग जात भयावनि भारी। केहि बिधि तात ताड़का मारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1915.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के साँवले सुंदर कोमल अँगों को देखकर सब माताएँ प्रेम सहित वचन कह रही हैं- हे तात! मार्ग में जाते हुए तुमने बड़ी भयावनी ताड़का राक्षसी को किस प्रकार से मारा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1915.english_translation: Seeing Ram's soft, beautiful dark form, all the mothers speak with love: "Dear son, while traveling on the road, how did you kill the dreadful Tadka?"
ramacharitamanas::1915.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / स्याम (dark-complexioned) / मृदु (soft) / मंजुल (beautiful) / गाता (body) / कहहिं (speak) / सप्रेम (with love) / बचन (words) / सब (all) / माता (mothers) / मारग (road) / जात (going) / भयावनि (frightening) / भारी (very great) / केहि बिधि (by what means) / तात (dear son) / ताड़का (Tadka) / मारी (killed)
ramacharitamanas::1915.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1915.essence: His gentleness and strength are seen as one.
ramacharitamanas::1915.simple_meaning: The mothers look at young Ram's gentle, beautiful form and lovingly ask how he killed the terrible Tadka on the road.
ramacharitamanas::1915.simple_insight: Love is so close here that even fear becomes a question of wonder.
ramacharitamanas::1915.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, the mothers are admiring young Ram after the wedding preparations. His dark, tender beauty moves them so deeply that they ask about his earlier deed on the road: how he killed Tadka, the terrifying demoness. Their love turns his strength into something intimate and dear.
ramacharitamanas::1915.modern_relevance: A child comes home with scraped knees after handling a bully at school, and the family keeps asking the same thing: how did you do that? The question is really admiration.
ramacharitamanas::1915.insight: It shifts attention from the violence of the act to the tenderness of the one who acted.

ramacharitamanas::1916.verse_sanskrit: घोर निसाचर बिकट भट समर गनहिं नहिं काहु। मारे सहित सहाय किमि खल मारीच सुबाहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1916.verse_hindi: बड़े भयानक राक्षस, जो विकट योद्धा थे और जो युद्ध में किसी को कुछ नहीं गिनते थे, उन दुष्ट मारीच और सुबाहु को सहायकों सहित तुमने कैसे मारा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::1916.english_translation: How did you kill the terrible night-rangers, fierce warriors who counted no one in battle, Maricha and Subahu, along with their helpers?
ramacharitamanas::1916.translation_literal: घोर (terrible) / निसाचर (night-rangers) / बिकट (fierce) / भट (warriors) / समर (battle) / गनहिं (count) / नहिं (not) / काहु (anyone) / मारे (killed) / सहित (along with) / सहाय (helpers) / किमि (how) / खल (wicked) / मारीच (Maricha) / सुबाहु (Subahu)
ramacharitamanas::1916.speaker: Mothers
ramacharitamanas::1916.simple_meaning: The mothers ask how Ram managed to defeat the fierce demons Maricha and Subahu, along with their allies.
ramacharitamanas::1916.simple_insight: A child’s hidden strength can astonish even the people closest to him.
ramacharitamanas::1916.detailed_meaning: After Ram is laid on the bed, the mothers look at his gentle form and begin to remember his childhood feats. One asks how this soft-bodied boy could destroy the fierce demons Maricha and Subahu when even warriors feared them. The verse supports their wonder, not a standalone teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1916.modern_relevance: A parent watches a quiet teenager and remembers the day that same child stood up to a bully everyone else avoided. The memory makes ordinary strength look almost miraculous.
ramacharitamanas::1916.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to hidden capacity.

ramacharitamanas::1917.verse_sanskrit: मुनि प्रसाद बलि तात तुम्हारी। ईस अनेक करवरें टारी॥ मख रखवारी करि दुहुँ भाईं। गुरु प्रसाद सब बिद्या पाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1917.verse_hindi: हे तात! मैं बलैया लेती हूँ, मुनि की कृपा से ही ईश्वर ने तुम्हारी बहुत सी बलाओं को टाल दिया। दोनों भाइयों ने यज्ञ की रखवाली करके गुरुजी के प्रसाद से सब विद्याएँ पाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1917.english_translation: By the sage's grace, dear son, your many dangers were averted. Both brothers guarded the sacrifice, and by the teacher's grace they received all knowledge.
ramacharitamanas::1917.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / प्रसाद (grace) / बलि (I offer myself) / तात (dear son) / तुम्हारी (your) / ईस (the divine) / अनेक (many) / करवरें (dangers) / टारी (removed) / मख (sacrifice) / रखवारी (guarding) / करि (having done) / दुहुँ (both) / भाईं (brothers) / गुरु (teacher) / प्रसाद (grace) / सब (all) / बिद्या (knowledge) / पाईं (received)
ramacharitamanas::1917.speaker: Mothers
ramacharitamanas::1917.essence: Grace protects, service teaches, and learning arrives through the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::1917.simple_meaning: The mothers bless Ram and Lakshman, saying their dangers were removed by the sage's grace. They also praise how both brothers guarded the sacrifice and gained all learning through their teacher's blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1917.simple_insight: Real protection and real learning come through grace, discipline, and service.
ramacharitamanas::1917.detailed_meaning: In Balkand, the mothers look at the young brothers and bless them with love. They recall how Vishvamitra's grace protected them from danger, how Ram and Lakshman guarded the sacrificial rite, and how they received every skill through their teacher.
ramacharitamanas::1917.modern_relevance: A parent watches a child leave for a hard school, a first job, or a risky city, and can only bless them inwardly. Some protection comes from unseen help, and some learning comes from serving a larger purpose.
ramacharitamanas::1917.insight: It shifts attention from raw talent to the quiet forces that shape a life: blessing, guidance, and faithful duty.

ramacharitamanas::1918.verse_sanskrit: मुनितिय तरी लगत पग धूरी। कीरति रही भुवन भरि पूरी॥ कमठ पीठि पबि कूट कठोरा। नृप समाज महुँ सिव धनु तोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1918.verse_hindi: चरणों की धूलि लगते ही मुनि पत्नी अहल्या तर गई। विश्वभर में यह कीर्ति पूर्ण रीति से व्याप्त हो गई। कच्छप की पीठ, वज्र और पर्वत से भी कठोर शिवजी के धनुष को राजाओं के समाज में तुमने तोड़ दिया! ॥
ramacharitamanas::1918.english_translation: The moment the dust of your feet touched her, Ahalya was redeemed. That fame spread fully across the worlds. You broke Shiva’s bow in the assembly of kings, though it was harder than a tortoise’s back, thunderbolt, and mountain.
ramacharitamanas::1918.translation_literal: मुनितिय (sage's wife) / तरी (crossed, redeemed) / लगत (touching) / पग (feet) / धूरी (dust) / कीरति (fame) / रही (remained) / भुवन (worlds) / भरि (filled) / पूरी (complete) / कमठ (tortoise) / पीठि (back) / पबि (thunderbolt) / कूट (mountain) / कठोरा (hard) / नृप (king) / समाज (assembly) / महुँ (in) / सिव (Shiva) / धनु (bow) / तोरा (broke)
ramacharitamanas::1918.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1918.essence: His touch restores, and his power shatters what none else could.
ramacharitamanas::1918.simple_meaning: Ahalya is freed by the touch of Ram’s feet, and his fame spreads everywhere. In the kings’ assembly, he breaks Shiva’s bow, proving his unmatched strength.
ramacharitamanas::1918.simple_insight: Grace and greatness arrive together: one touch restores, one act reveals power.
ramacharitamanas::1918.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, the broken Ahalya is restored by Ram’s feet, and that mercy becomes famous everywhere. Soon after, in Janaka’s royal assembly, Ram breaks Shiva’s bow and wins the right to Sita. This verse joins compassion and heroic power.
ramacharitamanas::1918.modern_relevance: You walk into a room carrying shame, and one person treats you with dignity instead of suspicion. That can change a life. Then comes the harder test: can you still act with strength?
ramacharitamanas::1918.insight: It links mercy and strength, showing that true greatness heals first and proves itself without boasting.

ramacharitamanas::1919.verse_sanskrit: बिस्व बिजय जसु जानकि पाई। आए भवन ब्याहि सब भाई॥ सकल अमानुष करम तुम्हारे। केवल कौसिक कृपाँ सुधारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1919.verse_hindi: विश्वविजय के यश और जानकी को पाया और सब भाइयों को ब्याहकर घर आए। तुम्हारे सभी कर्म अमानुषी हैं (मनुष्य की शक्ति के बाहर हैं), जिन्हें केवल विश्वामित्रजी की कृपा ने सुधारा है (सम्पन्न किया है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1919.english_translation: You won the world and won Janaki, then returned home with all your brothers married. All your deeds are beyond ordinary human power; only Vishwamitra's grace brought them to completion.
ramacharitamanas::1919.translation_literal: बिस्व (world) / बिजय (victory) / जसु (fame) / जानकि (Janaki) / पाई (having obtained) / आए (came) / भवन (home) / ब्याहि (having married) / सब (all) / भाई (brothers)॥ / सकल (all) / अमानुष (beyond human) / करम (deeds) / तुम्हारे (your) / केवल (only) / कौसिक (Vishvamitra) / कृपाँ (by grace) / सुधारे (were brought to completion)॥
ramacharitamanas::1919.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1919.essence: Even victory becomes humble when grace is remembered.
ramacharitamanas::1919.simple_meaning: The brothers return home with Janaki after winning her hand. Their achievements are described as beyond ordinary human power and made complete by Vishvamitra's grace.
ramacharitamanas::1919.simple_insight: Great achievement still carries humility when grace is named first.
ramacharitamanas::1919.detailed_meaning: The wedding has been won, Janaki has been obtained, and the brothers have returned home together. The verse pauses the celebration to say that such feats are not merely human skill; Vishvamitra's blessing made them possible.
ramacharitamanas::1919.modern_relevance: You finally close the deal, get the offer, and come home to celebrate. But one honest glance back tells you how many hands, chances, and blessings carried you there.
ramacharitamanas::1919.insight: It shifts credit away from personal mastery and toward the grace that made success possible.

ramacharitamanas::1920.verse_sanskrit: आजु सुफल जग जनमु हमारा। देखि तात बिधुबदन तुम्हारा॥ जे दिन गए तुम्हहि बिनु देखें। ते बिरंचि जनि पारहिं लेखें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1920.verse_hindi: हे तात! तुम्हारा चन्द्रमुख देखकर आज हमारा जगत में जन्म लेना सफल हुआ। तुमको बिना देखे जो दिन बीते हैं, उनको ब्रह्मा गिनती में न लावें (हमारी आयु में शामिल न करें) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1920.english_translation: O dear one, seeing your moon-like face, our life feels fulfilled today. The days spent without seeing you should not even be counted by Brahma.
ramacharitamanas::1920.translation_literal: आजु (today) / सुफल (fruitful, fulfilled) / जग (world, life) / जनमु (birth) / हमारा (our) / देखि (seeing) / तात (dear one) / बिधुबदन (moon-faced) / तुम्हारा (your) / जे (those) / दिन (days) / गए (passed) / तुम्हहि (you) / बिनु (without) / देखें (seeing) / ते (those) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / जनि (do not) / पारहिं (count/include) / लेखें (in account)
ramacharitamanas::1920.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::1920.essence: Presence with Ram makes every other day feel incomplete.
ramacharitamanas::1920.simple_meaning: The speaker says that seeing Ram's face makes life feel fulfilled, and the days spent without his sight feel unworthy of counting.
ramacharitamanas::1920.simple_insight: Love changes time itself: presence makes life meaningful, absence makes even days feel unreal.
ramacharitamanas::1920.detailed_meaning: After the wedding and the victory, someone close to Ram looks at his moon-like face and feels that life has finally become fruitful. The verse turns devotion into a measure of time: only moments with Ram truly count.
ramacharitamanas::1920.modern_relevance: You finally see someone you have waited months to meet, and the whole room changes. The long wait vanishes the moment they arrive, because presence matters more than the calendar.
ramacharitamanas::1920.insight: It shifts attention from counting days to valuing presence. What matters is not duration, but contact with what you love most.

ramacharitamanas::1921.verse_sanskrit: राम प्रतोषीं मातु सब कहि बिनीत बर बैन। सुमिरि संभु गुरु बिप्र पद किए नीदबस नैन ॥
ramacharitamanas::1921.verse_hindi: विनय भरे उत्तम वचन कहकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सब माताओं को संतुष्ट किया। फिर शिवजी, गुरु और ब्राह्मणों के चरणों का स्मरण कर नेत्रों को नींद के वश किया। (अर्थात वे सो रहे) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1921.english_translation: Ram satisfied all the mothers with humble and gracious words. Then, remembering Shiva, the teacher, and the Brahmins, he let sleep take his eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1921.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / प्रतोषीं (satisfied, pleased) / मातु (mothers) / सब (all) / कहि (speaking) / बिनीत (humble) / बर (excellent) / बैन (words) / सुमिरि (remembering) / संभु (Shiva) / गुरु (teacher) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / पद (feet) / किए (made) / नीदबस (under sleep's control) / नैन (eyes)
ramacharitamanas::1921.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1921.essence: Greatness stays gentle when it remembers whom to honor.
ramacharitamanas::1921.simple_meaning: Ram speaks gently to the mothers, then remembers Shiva, his teacher, and the learned Brahmins before falling asleep.
ramacharitamanas::1921.simple_insight: Even after greatness, he stays humble and grateful.
ramacharitamanas::1921.detailed_meaning: After the wedding and the praise of the gathered people, Ram returns home. He answers the mothers with respectful words, then bows inwardly to Shiva, his teacher, and the Brahmins before resting. The scene shows how grace and humility remain intact even at the height of joy.
ramacharitamanas::1921.modern_relevance: You finally finish the big event everyone praised, then still thank the people who made it possible. The real mark of maturity is not the applause — it is the humility that follows it.
ramacharitamanas::1921.insight: It shifts attention from achievement to reverence, showing that success should end in gratitude, not self-importance.

ramacharitamanas::1922.verse_sanskrit: नीदउँ बदन सोह सुठि लोना। मनहुँ साँझ सरसीरुह सोना॥ घर घर करहिं जागरन नारीं। देहिं परसपर मंगल गारीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1922.verse_hindi: नींद में भी उनका अत्यन्त सलोना मुखड़ा ऐसा सोह रहा था, मानो संध्या के समय का लाल कमल सोह रहा हो। स्त्रियाँ घर-घर जागरण कर रही हैं और आपस में (एक-दूसरी को) मंगलमयी गालियाँ दे रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1922.english_translation: Even in sleep, his lovely face shone so beautifully, like a red lotus at dusk. Women held wakeful celebrations from house to house and exchanged blessings in the form of playful scolding.
ramacharitamanas::1922.translation_literal: नीदउँ (even in sleep) / बदन (face) / सोह (shone) / सुठि (very) / लोना (lovely) / मनहुँ (as if) / साँझ (evening) / सरसीरुह (lotus) / सोना (golden) // घर घर (from house to house) / करहिं (they do) / जागरन (wakeful celebration) / नारीं (women) / देहिं (give) / परसपर (to one another) / मंगल (auspicious) / गारीं (playful scolding)
ramacharitamanas::1922.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1922.essence: Presence makes even sleep radiant, and celebration becomes blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1922.simple_meaning: Ram's face was so beautiful even in sleep that it looked like a glowing lotus. In Ayodhya, women stayed awake in celebration and greeted each other with affectionate teasing.
ramacharitamanas::1922.simple_insight: Joy spills into ordinary life when a beloved presence fills the home.
ramacharitamanas::1922.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is celebrating Ram's return. Even while he sleeps, his beauty fills the city, and the women keep vigil from house to house, turning their teasing into blessings. The scene shows a household and a kingdom relieved into joy.
ramacharitamanas::1922.modern_relevance: A home after a long-awaited reunion feels different: people stay up late, talk over each other, and laugh at small things because the person they missed is finally there.
ramacharitamanas::1922.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the atmosphere devotion creates around it.

ramacharitamanas::1923.verse_sanskrit: पुरी बिराजति राजति रजनी। रानीं कहहिं बिलोकहु सजनी॥ सुंदर बधुन्ह सासु लै सोईं। फनिकन्ह जनु सिरमनि उर गोईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1923.verse_hindi: रानियाँ कहती हैं- हे सजनी! देखो, (आज) रात्रि की कैसी शोभा है, जिससे अयोध्यापुरी विशेष शोभित हो रही है! (यों कहती हुई) सासुएँ सुंदर बहुओं को लेकर सो गईं, मानो सर्पों ने अपने सिर की मणियों को हृदय में छिपा लिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1923.english_translation: The city shone in the night. The queens said, “Look, dear friend, how beautiful the night is.” The graceful daughters-in-law took their mothers-in-law to sleep, like snakes hiding their jewels in their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1923.translation_literal: पुरी (city) / बिराजति (is shining) / राजति (is glorious) / रजनी (night) / रानीं (queens) / कहहिं (say) / बिलोकहु (look) / सजनी (dear friend) / सुंदर (beautiful) / बधुन्ह (daughters-in-law) / सासु (mothers-in-law) / लै (taking) / सोईं (slept) / फनिकन्ह (snakes) / जनु (as if) / सिरमनि (jewels on the head) / उर (heart) / गोईं (hid)
ramacharitamanas::1923.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1923.essence: Peaceful order makes a city glow from within.
ramacharitamanas::1923.simple_meaning: Ayodhya is so peaceful and beautiful at night that even the queens admire it. The household settles into sleep, with the younger women gently attending to the older women.
ramacharitamanas::1923.simple_insight: A calm home can make even ordinary night feel sacred and complete.
ramacharitamanas::1923.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Ram has rested the royal household, the city settles into a gentle night. Queens admire the beauty around them, and the women of the palace tuck one another into sleep. The verse lingers on quiet domestic harmony before dawn arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1923.modern_relevance: A house finally goes quiet after a long family gathering. The dishes are done, the elders are settled, and the whole place feels held. That soft order is its own kind of blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1923.insight: It shifts attention from action to atmosphere, showing how harmony itself becomes a sign of grace.

ramacharitamanas::1924.verse_sanskrit: प्रात पुनीत काल प्रभु जागे। अरुनचूड़ बर बोलन लागे॥ बंदि मागधन्हि गुनगन गाए। पुरजन द्वार जोहारन आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1924.verse_hindi: प्रातःकाल पवित्र ब्रह्म मुहूर्त में प्रभु जागे। मुर्गे सुंदर बोलने लगे। भाट और मागधों ने गुणों का गान किया तथा नगर के लोग द्वार पर जोहार करने को आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1924.english_translation: At the sacred dawn, the Lord awoke. The red-crested roosters began to crow. Bards and minstrels sang his praises, and the townspeople came to the door to pay respects.
ramacharitamanas::1924.translation_literal: प्रात (morning) / पुनीत (pure, sacred) / काल (time) / प्रभु (Lord) / जागे (awoke) / अरुनचूड़ (red-crested) / बर (roosters) / बोलन (to crow) / लागे (began) / बंदि (bards) / मागधन्हि (minstrels) / गुनगन (praise-songs) / गाए (sang) / पुरजन (townspeople) / द्वार (door) / जोहारन (to pay respects) / आए (came)
ramacharitamanas::1924.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1924.essence: Dawn itself seems to rise in reverence around Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1924.simple_meaning: Ram wakes at dawn, the birds crow, singers praise him, and the townspeople gather to honor him.
ramacharitamanas::1924.simple_insight: A blessed morning begins with reverence before action.
ramacharitamanas::1924.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is alive with celebration after the night’s joy. At sacred dawn, Ram wakes, the roosters crow, singers praise him, and townspeople arrive at the palace door. The verse simply sets the morning scene before the family’s formal greetings begin.
ramacharitamanas::1924.modern_relevance: You wake before sunrise and the house is still quiet, but the day already feels charged. Before anyone asks anything of you, the morning itself seems to bow.
ramacharitamanas::1924.insight: It frames ordinary morning activity as an atmosphere of honor and blessing, not just routine.

ramacharitamanas::1925.verse_sanskrit: बंदि बिप्र सुर गुर पितु माता। पाइ असीस मुदित सब भ्राता॥ जननिन्ह सादर बदन निहारे। भूपति संग द्वार पगु धारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1925.verse_hindi: ब्राह्मणों, देवताओं, गुरु, पिता और माताओं की वंदना करके आशीर्वाद पाकर सब भाई प्रसन्न हुए। माताओं ने आदर के साथ उनके मुखों को देखा। फिर वे राजा के साथ दरवाजे (बाहर) पधारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1925.english_translation: Having bowed to the brahmins, the radiant beings, the teacher, father, and mother, all the brothers rejoiced after receiving blessings. The mothers looked upon their faces with reverence. Then they went out through the doorway with the king.
ramacharitamanas::1925.translation_literal: बंदि (bowing to) / बिप्र (brahmins) / सुर (radiant beings) / गुर (teacher) / पितु (father) / माता (mother) / पाइ (having received) / असीस (blessings) / मुदित (joyful) / सब (all) / भ्राता (brothers) / जननिन्ह (the mothers) / सादर (with reverence) / बदन (faces) / निहारे (looked upon) / भूपति (the king) / संग (with) / द्वार (doorway) / पगु (feet) / धारे (placed/stepped)
ramacharitamanas::1925.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1925.simple_meaning: The brothers bow to elders and receive blessings before leaving with the king. Their mothers watch them with loving respect.
ramacharitamanas::1925.simple_insight: Respect for elders becomes the first step of the day.
ramacharitamanas::1925.detailed_meaning: At dawn in Ayodhya, the four brothers rise in a household shaped by devotion and duty. They first honor the brahmins, teachers, parents, and elders, receive blessings, and only then step out with the king. The scene shows the family order that supports Ram's life.
ramacharitamanas::1925.modern_relevance: Before a child leaves for an exam, a parent quietly touches their forehead and blesses them. Before the day begins, respect and blessing come first.
ramacharitamanas::1925.insight: It places humility before action and shows that strength begins with honoring those who raised and guided you.

ramacharitamanas::1926.verse_sanskrit: कीन्हि सौच सब सहज सुचि सरित पुनीत नहाइ। प्रातक्रिया करि तात पहिं आए चारिउ भाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1926.verse_hindi: स्वभाव से ही पवित्र चारों भाइयों ने सब शौचादि से निवृत्त होकर पवित्र सरयू नदी में स्नान किया और प्रातःक्रिया (संध्या वंदनादि) करके वे पिता के पास आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1926.english_translation: The four brothers, naturally pure, completed their cleansing, bathed in the sacred Sarayu, performed their morning rites, and then came to their father.
ramacharitamanas::1926.translation_literal: कीन्हि (did) / सौच (cleansing) / सब (all) / सहज (naturally) / सुचि (pure) / सरित (river) / पुनीत (sacred) / नहाइ (bathed) / प्रातक्रिया (morning rites) / करि (having done) / तात (father) / पहिं (to) / आए (came) / चारिउ (four) / भाइ (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::1926.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1926.essence: Purity and routine come before action.
ramacharitamanas::1926.simple_meaning: The four brothers bathe, complete their morning duties, and go to their father. It is a calm, orderly morning scene.
ramacharitamanas::1926.simple_insight: Small acts of purity and routine prepare the mind for the day ahead.
ramacharitamanas::1926.detailed_meaning: After the dawn prayers, Ram, Lakshman, Bharat, and Shatrughna cleanse themselves in the sacred Sarayu and complete their morning observances. This is not a teaching moment but a quiet scene of royal discipline before they return to Dasharath.
ramacharitamanas::1926.modern_relevance: You finish your morning shower, prayers, and a quiet walk before the house wakes up. The day feels steadier because you began it clean and composed.
ramacharitamanas::1926.insight: It shifts attention from rushing into the day to beginning with order and care.

ramacharitamanas::1927.verse_sanskrit: भूप बिलोकि लिए उर लाई। बैठे हरषि रजायसु पाई॥ देखि रामु सब सभा जुड़ानी। लोचन लाभ अवधि अनुमानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1927.verse_hindi: राजा ने देखते ही उन्हें हृदय से लगा लिया। तदनन्तर वे आज्ञा पाकर हर्षित होकर बैठ गए। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन कर और नेत्रों के लाभ की बस यही सीमा है, ऐसा अनुमान कर सारी सभा शीतल हो गई। (अर्थात सबके तीनों प्रकार के ताप सदा के लिए मिट गए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1927.english_translation: The king embraced them at once and seated them with joy. Seeing Ram, the whole assembly felt cooled, as if the eyes had reached their limit.
ramacharitamanas::1927.translation_literal: भूप (the king) / बिलोकि (seeing) / लिए (took) / उर (to chest) / लाई (brought) / बैठे (sat) / हरषि (joyfully) / रजायसु (permission) / पाई (having received) / देखि (seeing) / रामु (Ram) / सब (all) / सभा (assembly) / जुड़ानी (became cool) / लोचन (eyes) / लाभ (gain) / अवधि (limit) / अनुमानी (having judged)
ramacharitamanas::1927.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1927.essence: Ram’s presence cools what the world has heated.
ramacharitamanas::1927.simple_meaning: The king hugs the brothers and seats them happily. Seeing Ram makes everyone feel complete and deeply soothed.
ramacharitamanas::1927.simple_insight: Recognition can be a kind of relief. A single true sight can settle a whole room.
ramacharitamanas::1927.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, King Dasharath receives the four brothers after their ritual bath and morning duties. He embraces them, seats them with delight, and the whole court is calmed by Ram’s presence. The verse pauses on that shared joy before the sages arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1927.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after weeks away, and one familiar face changes everything. The tension drops, shoulders loosen, and everyone knows they are safe again.
ramacharitamanas::1927.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to presence: Ram’s arrival itself restores the whole gathering.

ramacharitamanas::1928.verse_sanskrit: पुनि बसिष्टु मुनि कौसिकु आए। सुभग आसनन्हि मुनि बैठाए॥ सुतन्ह समेत पूजि पद लागे। निरखि रामु दोउ गुर अनुरागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1928.verse_hindi: फिर मुनि वशिष्ठजी और विश्वामित्रजी आए। राजा ने उनको सुंदर आसनों पर बैठाया और पुत्रों समेत उनकी पूजा करके उनके चरणों लगे। दोनों गुरु श्री रामजी को देखकर प्रेम में मुग्ध हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1928.english_translation: Then the sage Vashishtha and sage Kaushika arrived. The king seated the sages on fine seats, worshipped them with his sons, and bowed at their feet. Seeing Ram, both teachers were filled with love.
ramacharitamanas::1928.translation_literal: पुनि (then) / बसिष्टु (Vashishtha) / मुनि (sage) / कौसिकु (Kaushika) / आए (came) / सुभग (beautiful) / आसनन्हि (on seats) / मुनि (sages) / बैठाए (seated) / सुतन्ह (with sons) / समेत (together) / पूजि (worshipping) / पद (feet) / लागे (touched/bowed) / निरखि (seeing) / रामु (Ram) / दोउ (both) / गुर (teachers) / अनुरागे (became loving)
ramacharitamanas::1928.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1928.essence: True honor turns arrival into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1928.simple_meaning: King Janak honors Vashishtha and Vishwamitra, seats them well, bows with his sons, and both teachers are moved with love on seeing Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1928.simple_insight: Respect opens the heart. A humble welcome can turn a formal meeting into living devotion.
ramacharitamanas::1928.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, Vashishtha and Vishwamitra arrive and are received with full honor. Janak bows with his sons before them. The moment both sages see Ram, their hearts melt into love, preparing the scene for the sacred dialogue that follows.
ramacharitamanas::1928.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet when someone greets elders with real humility, not performance. The atmosphere changes before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1928.insight: It shifts attention from status and ceremony to reverence that softens everyone present.

ramacharitamanas::1929.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं बसिष्टु धरम इतिहासा। सुनहिं महीसु सहित रनिवासा॥ मुनि मन अगम गाधिसुत करनी। मुदित बसिष्ठ बिपुल बिधि बरनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1929.verse_hindi: वशिष्ठजी धर्म के इतिहास कह रहे हैं और राजा रनिवास सहित सुन रहे हैं, जो मुनियों के मन को भी अगम्य है, ऐसी विश्वामित्रजी की करनी को वशिष्ठजी ने आनंदित होकर बहुत प्रकार से वर्णन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1929.english_translation: Vashishtha speaks of the histories of dharma, and the king with the royal women listens. The deeds of Vishvamitra are beyond even a sage's mind, and Vashishtha joyfully describes them in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::1929.translation_literal: कहहिं (speak) / बसिष्टु (Vashishtha) / धरम (dharma) / इतिहासा (histories) / सुनहिं (listen) / महीसु (king) / सहित (together with) / रनिवासा (the royal women of the palace) / मुनि (sage) / मन (mind) / अगम (unreachable) / गाधिसुत (son of Gadhi, Vishvamitra) / करनी (deeds) / मुदित (joyful) / बसिष्ठ (Vashishtha) / बिपुल (many) / बिधि (ways) / बरनी (described)
ramacharitamanas::1929.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1929.essence: A saint's life becomes living instruction when told with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1929.simple_meaning: Vashishtha recounts the sacred history of Vishvamitra's life while the king and the palace women listen with attention.
ramacharitamanas::1929.simple_insight: Great lives become teachings when they are remembered with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1929.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, after the elders are seated and Ram has been seen, Vashishtha begins telling the story of Vishvamitra's dharmic life. The king and the women of the palace listen as a saint joyfully praises another sage's impossible transformation.
ramacharitamanas::1929.modern_relevance: At a family gathering, an elder tells the story of someone who changed completely through discipline and courage. Everyone falls quiet, not for entertainment, but because the story itself carries authority.
ramacharitamanas::1929.insight: It shifts attention from the present scene to the moral power of remembered example.

ramacharitamanas::1930.verse_sanskrit: बोले बामदेउ सब साँची। कीरति कलित लोक तिहुँ माची॥ सुनि आनंदु भयउ सब काहू। राम लखन उर अधिक उछाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1930.verse_hindi: वामदेवजी बोले- ये सब बातें सत्य हैं। विश्वामित्रजी की सुंदर कीर्ति तीनों लोकों में छाई हुई है। यह सुनकर सब किसी को आनंद हुआ। श्री राम-लक्ष्मण के हृदय में अधिक उत्साह (आनंद) हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1930.english_translation: Vamadeva said, “All of this is true. Vishvamitra's splendid fame has spread through all three worlds.” Hearing this, everyone felt joy, and Ram and Lakshman felt even greater delight in their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1930.translation_literal: बोले (spoke) / बामदेउ (Vamadeva) / सब (all) / साँची (true) / कीरति (fame) / कलित (adorned, splendid) / लोक (worlds) / तिहुँ (three) / माची (spread) / सुनि (hearing) / आनंदु (joy) / भयउ (became) / सब (all) / काहू (everyone) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / उर (heart) / अधिक (more) / उछाहू (joy, enthusiasm)
ramacharitamanas::1930.speaker: Vamadeva
ramacharitamanas::1930.essence: True greatness needs no defence; it is already known.
ramacharitamanas::1930.simple_meaning: Vamadeva confirms that Vishvamitra's fame is truly widespread. Everyone feels happy hearing it, and Ram and Lakshman feel especially glad.
ramacharitamanas::1930.simple_insight: Recognition of a worthy teacher naturally lifts the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::1930.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the sages are being honoured and their greatness is being spoken of openly. Vamadeva confirms Vishvamitra's reputation, and the whole gathering brightens. Ram and Lakshman feel the joy most deeply because they are listening with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1930.modern_relevance: A respected mentor walks into the room and someone finally names what everyone already felt: this person has earned it. The mood changes instantly, and the people who listen with humility feel it most.
ramacharitamanas::1930.insight: It shifts attention from private opinion to public recognition of earned greatness.

ramacharitamanas::1931.verse_sanskrit: मंगल मोद उछाह नित जाहिं दिवस एहि भाँति। उमगी अवध अनंद भरि अधिक अधिक अधिकाति ॥
ramacharitamanas::1931.verse_hindi: नित्य ही मंगल, आनंद और उत्सव होते हैं, इस तरह आनंद में दिन बीतते जाते हैं। अयोध्या आनंद से भरकर उमड़ पड़ी, आनंद की अधिकता अधिक-अधिक बढ़ती ही जा रही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1931.english_translation: Auspiciousness, delight, and festivity pass every day in this way. Ayodhya swells with joy, and its joy keeps growing and growing.
ramacharitamanas::1931.translation_literal: मंगल (auspiciousness) / मोद (joy) / उछाह (festivity, enthusiasm) / नित (always) / जाहिं (go) / दिवस (days) / एहि (this) / भाँति (way) / उमगी (overflowed) / अवध (Ayodhya) / अनंद (joy) / भरि (filled) / अधिक (more) / अधिक (more) / अधिकाति (greatly increasing)
