ramacharitamanas::1931.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1931.essence: Joy multiplies until the whole city overflows.
ramacharitamanas::1931.simple_meaning: Ayodhya is overflowing with joy, and each day brings more celebration and delight.
ramacharitamanas::1931.simple_insight: Joy can become contagious, turning an entire home into a living celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1931.detailed_meaning: The sages and royal household have just heard Vishwamitra's wondrous story, and the mood in Ayodhya lifts higher and higher. This line simply lingers on the city’s overflowing happiness before the next auspicious moment arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1931.modern_relevance: A house after good news feels different: people move lighter, speak softer, and keep smiling at nothing in particular. Happiness spreads through shared space before anyone names it.
ramacharitamanas::1931.insight: It shifts attention from a single happy event to the way joy can saturate an entire atmosphere.

ramacharitamanas::1932.verse_sanskrit: सुदिन सोधि कल कंकन छोरे। मंगल मोद बिनोद न थोरे॥ नित नव सुखु सुर देखि सिहाहीं। अवध जन्म जाचहिं बिधि पाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1932.verse_hindi: अच्छा दिन (शुभ मुहूर्त) शोधकर सुंदर कंकण खोले गए। मंगल, आनंद और विनोद कुछ कम नहीं हुए (अर्थात बहुत हुए)। इस प्रकार नित्य नए सुख को देखकर देवता सिहाते हैं और अयोध्या में जन्म पाने के लिए ब्रह्माजी से याचना करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1932.english_translation: After choosing an auspicious day, the ceremonial bracelets were removed. Joy, delight, and festivity did not lessen. Seeing the ever-new happiness, the radiant beings long to take birth in Ayodhya and beg Brahma for that fate.
ramacharitamanas::1932.translation_literal: सुदिन (auspicious day) / सोधि (having chosen) / कल (ceremonial bracelet) / कंकन (bracelets) / छोरे (were removed) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मोद (joy) / बिनोद (festivity) / न (not) / थोरे (less) / नित (daily) / नव (new) / सुखु (happiness) / सुर (radiant beings) / देखि (seeing) / सिहाहीं (are envious) / अवध (Ayodhya) / जन्म (birth) / जाचहिं (ask for) / बिधि (Brahma) / पाहीं (from)
ramacharitamanas::1932.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1932.essence: Ram's arrival makes even the radiant beings long for Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::1932.simple_meaning: The auspicious birth rituals begin, and the joy in Ayodhya keeps growing. Even the radiant beings envy that happiness and long to be born there.
ramacharitamanas::1932.simple_insight: Some moments feel so blessed that even the heavens seem to lean toward them.
ramacharitamanas::1932.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the birth celebrations are underway after the right auspicious moment is chosen. The bracelets are removed, the joy keeps swelling, and the scene is so radiant that even the radiant beings look on with longing.
ramacharitamanas::1932.modern_relevance: A home fills with laughter before a newborn arrives. The room feels larger than itself, and everyone present knows they are standing inside a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1932.insight: It frames Ram's birth as a joy so complete that it draws longing even from the radiant beings.

ramacharitamanas::1933.verse_sanskrit: बिस्वामित्रु चलन नित चहहीं। राम सप्रेम बिनय बस रहहीं॥ दिन दिन सयगुन भूपति भाऊ। देखि सराह महामुनिराऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1933.verse_hindi: विश्वामित्रजी नित्य ही चलना (अपने आश्रम जाना) चाहते हैं, पर रामचन्द्रजी के स्नेह और विनयवश रह जाते हैं। दिनोंदिन राजा का सौ गुना भाव (प्रेम) देखकर महामुनिराज विश्वामित्रजी उनकी सराहना करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1933.english_translation: Vishvamitra kept wanting to leave, but Ram's affection and humility kept him there. Day by day, the great sage praised the king more and more for his hundredfold love.
ramacharitamanas::1933.translation_literal: बिस्वामित्रु (Vishvamitra) / चलन (to depart) / नित (always) / चहहीं (wanted) / राम (Ram) / सप्रेम (with affection) / बिनय (humility) / बस (because of) / रहहीं (remained) ॥ / दिन दिन (day by day) / सयगुन (hundredfold) / भूपति (king) / भाऊ (feeling/love) / देखि (seeing) / सराह (praised) / महामुनिराऊ (the great sage king) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1933.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1933.essence: Affection and humility can keep a blessing from leaving.
ramacharitamanas::1933.simple_meaning: Vishvamitra keeps trying to depart, but Ram's loving humility makes him stay. Watching the king's love grow stronger each day, the great sage keeps praising him.
ramacharitamanas::1933.simple_insight: Love and humility can hold a relationship together more powerfully than obligation.
ramacharitamanas::1933.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Vishvamitra has finished his purpose and wants to leave, but Ram's affectionate respect keeps him from going. The king's devotion deepens each day, and the sage recognises and praises that rare bond.
ramacharitamanas::1933.modern_relevance: A mentor packs up after the work is done, but the family keeps insisting he stay for dinner. What holds him there is not duty, but the warmth of being genuinely valued.
ramacharitamanas::1933.insight: It shifts attention from formal duty to the living force of affectionate respect.

ramacharitamanas::1934.verse_sanskrit: मागत बिदा राउ अनुरागे। सुतन्ह समेत ठाढ़ भे आगे॥ नाथ सकल संपदा तुम्हारी। मैं सेवकु समेत सुत नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1934.verse_hindi: अंत में जब विश्वामित्रजी ने विदा माँगी, तब राजा प्रेममग्न हो गए और पुत्रों सहित आगे खड़े हो गए। (वे बोले-) हे नाथ! यह सारी सम्पदा आपकी है। मैं तो स्त्री-पुत्रों सहित आपका सेवक हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1934.english_translation: When Vishvamitra asked to leave, King Dasharath stood forward in love with his sons. He said, “O lord, all this wealth is yours. I am your servant, with my sons and wife.”
ramacharitamanas::1934.translation_literal: मागत (asking) / बिदा (leave-taking) / राउ (the king) / अनुरागे (filled with love) / सुतन्ह (with sons) / समेत (together with) / ठाढ़ (standing) / भे (became) / आगे (in front) || नाथ (lord) / सकल (all) / संपदा (wealth, possessions) / तुम्हारी (yours) / मैं (I) / सेवकु (servant) / समेत (together with) / सुत (sons) / नारी (wife)
ramacharitamanas::1934.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1934.simple_meaning: Dasharath responds to Vishvamitra with loving humility. He offers his wealth, family, and himself in service.
ramacharitamanas::1934.simple_insight: Real devotion makes status feel small and service feel natural.
ramacharitamanas::1934.detailed_meaning: Vishvamitra is ready to depart after receiving Ram and Lakshman. Dasharath, still overwhelmed by affection and reverence, steps forward with his sons and declares everything his. The moment reveals how completely he places himself in the sage's service.
ramacharitamanas::1934.modern_relevance: A respected guest is about to leave after helping your family, and you find yourself offering more than thanks. You offer food, time, help, and your full respect without calculating what it costs.
ramacharitamanas::1934.insight: It shifts the mind from ownership to offering, turning possession into service.

ramacharitamanas::1935.verse_sanskrit: करब सदा लरिकन्ह पर छोहू। दरसनु देत रहब मुनि मोहू॥ अस कहि राउ सहित सुत रानी। परेउ चरन मुख आव न बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1935.verse_hindi: हे मुनि! लड़कों पर सदा स्नेह करते रहिएगा और मुझे भी दर्शन देते रहिएगा। ऐसा कहकर पुत्रों और रानियों सहित राजा दशरथजी विश्वामित्रजी के चरणों पर गिर पड़े, (प्रेमविह्वल हो जाने के कारण) उनके मुँह से बात नहीं निकलती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1935.english_translation: “Always show affection to the boys and keep giving me your darshan, O sage.” Saying this, King Dasharath fell at the sage's feet with his sons and queens, too moved to speak.
ramacharitamanas::1935.translation_literal: करब (do) / सदा (always) / लरिकन्ह (to the boys) / पर (upon) / छोहू (affection) / दरसनु (darshan, sight) / देत (giving) / रहब (keep staying) / मुनि (sage) / मोहू (to me) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / राउ (the king) / सहित (along with) / सुत (sons) / रानी (queens) / परेउ (fell) / चरन (feet) / मुख (mouth) / आव (comes) / न (not) / बानी (speech)
ramacharitamanas::1935.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::1935.simple_meaning: Dasharath, overwhelmed with love, asks Vishwamitra to keep blessing his sons and to keep visiting him. Then he falls at the sage's feet, unable to speak.
ramacharitamanas::1935.simple_insight: Love can be so full that it leaves no words at all.
ramacharitamanas::1935.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has just begged Vishwamitra not to leave. Now, with his sons and queens beside him, he collapses at the sage's feet in gratitude and tenderness. The scene is about overflowing affection, not instruction.
ramacharitamanas::1935.modern_relevance: You try to thank someone who changed your life, but the words vanish. Your chest tightens, your eyes fill, and all you can do is bow your head.
ramacharitamanas::1935.insight: It shifts attention from speaking well to expressing love directly, even when language fails.

ramacharitamanas::1936.verse_sanskrit: दीन्हि असीस बिप्र बहु भाँति। चले न प्रीति रीति कहि जाती॥ रामु सप्रेम संग सब भाई। आयसु पाइ फिरे पहुँचाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1936.verse_hindi: ब्राह्मण विश्वमित्रजी ने बहुत प्रकार से आशीर्वाद दिए और वे चल पड़े। प्रीति की रीति कही नहीं जीती। सब भाइयों को साथ लेकर श्री रामजी प्रेम के साथ उन्हें पहुँचाकर और आज्ञा पाकर लौटे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1936.english_translation: The Brahmin gave many blessings and departed, but affection could not be expressed in the proper way. Ram went with loving care, took leave, and returned after escorting him with all his brothers.
ramacharitamanas::1936.translation_literal: दीन्हि (gave) / असीस (blessings) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / चले (departed) / न (not) / प्रीति (affection) / रीति (proper way) / कहि (saying) / जाती (could be expressed)॥ / रामु (Ram) / सप्रेम (with love) / संग (with) / सब (all) / भाई (brothers) / आयसु (permission) / पाइ (having obtained) / फिरे (returned) / पहुँचाई (after escorting)
ramacharitamanas::1936.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1936.essence: Love is proven by how you part, not by how you greet.
ramacharitamanas::1936.simple_meaning: विश्वामित्रजी ने आशीर्वाद देकर विदा ली। राम अपने भाइयों के साथ प्रेम से उन्हें छोड़ने गए और अनुमति लेकर लौट आए।
ramacharitamanas::1936.simple_insight: True respect shows itself in how you send someone off, not just in what you say.
ramacharitamanas::1936.detailed_meaning: विश्वामित्रजी अब विदा ले रहे हैं. दशरथ के घर का तनाव शांति में बदल गया है, और राम अपने भाइयों के साथ गुरु को प्रेमपूर्वक छोड़ने जाते हैं. यह दृश्य औपचारिक विदाई से अधिक, सम्मान और स्नेह की पूरी रीति दिखाता है.
ramacharitamanas::1936.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to care: real courtesy follows someone all the way out.

ramacharitamanas::1937.verse_sanskrit: राम रूपु भूपति भगति ब्याहु उछाहु अनंदु। जात सराहत मनहिं मन मुदित गाधिकुलचंदु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1937.verse_hindi: गाधिकुल के चन्द्रमा विश्वामित्रजी बड़े हर्ष के साथ श्री रामचन्द्रजी के रूप, राजा दशरथजी की भक्ति, (चारों भाइयों के) विवाह और (सबके) उत्साह और आनंद को मन ही मन सराहते जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1937.english_translation: The sage from the Gadhi line kept admiring Ram's beauty, King Dasharath's devotion, the wedding, and everyone's joy as he went along.
ramacharitamanas::1937.translation_literal: राम रूपु (Ram's form) / भूपति (king) / भगति (devotion) / ब्याहु (wedding) / उछाहु (enthusiasm) / अनंदु (joy) / जात (going) / सराहत (praising) / मनहिं मन (in his own mind) / मुदित (delighted) / गाधिकुलचंदु (moon of the Gadhi line)
ramacharitamanas::1937.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1937.essence: True joy keeps itself alive by remembering what is beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::1937.simple_meaning: Worldly and spiritual joy meet here: Vishwamitra walks on, quietly admiring Ram's beauty, Dasharath's devotion, and the wedding festivities.
ramacharitamanas::1937.simple_insight: Some moments are so full they leave you smiling inwardly, without needing to say a word.
ramacharitamanas::1937.detailed_meaning: Vishwamitra has just blessed the family and is departing after seeing Ram and the wedding preparations. As he walks away, he keeps recalling Ram's beauty, Dasharath's devotion, and the happiness around him. The verse lingers on his inward delight.
ramacharitamanas::1937.modern_relevance: You leave a family gathering and keep replaying one small moment of grace — a parent’s pride, a child’s smile, a room suddenly softened by love.
ramacharitamanas::1937.insight: It shifts attention from outer ceremony to the quiet joy that devotion and harmony create.

ramacharitamanas::1938.verse_sanskrit: बामदेव रघुकुल गुर ग्यानी। बहुरि गाधिसुत कथा बखानी॥ सुनि मुनि सुजसु मनहिं मन राऊ। बरनत आपन पुन्य प्रभाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1938.verse_hindi: वामदेवजी और रघुकुल के गुरु ज्ञानी वशिष्ठजी ने फिर विश्वामित्रजी की कथा बखानकर कही। मुनि का सुंदर यश सुनकर राजा मन ही मन अपने पुण्यों के प्रभाव का बखान करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1938.english_translation: Vamadeva and Vashistha, the wise teachers of the Raghu line, again recounted the story of Vishvamitra. Hearing the sage's fame, the king quietly began praising his own past merit.
ramacharitamanas::1938.translation_literal: बामदेव (Vamadeva) / रघुकुल गुर (teacher of the Raghu line) / ग्यानी (wise) / बहुरि (again) / गाधिसुत (son of Gadhi, Vishvamitra) / कथा (story) / बखानी (described) / सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (sage) / सुजसु (good fame) / मनहिं मन (within the mind) / राऊ (king) / बरनत (describing) / आपन (own) / पुन्य (merit) / प्रभाऊ (power, influence)
ramacharitamanas::1938.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1938.essence: Sacred praise can still awaken the king's hidden pride.
ramacharitamanas::1938.simple_meaning: The sages retell Vishvamitra's story, and King Dasharath privately feels proud of the merit that brought this blessing to him.
ramacharitamanas::1938.simple_insight: Pride can hide inside gratitude, even in a sacred moment.
ramacharitamanas::1938.detailed_meaning: After Vishvamitra's blessed visit and the wedding celebrations, the court is still alive with reverence. Vamadeva and Vashistha recount Vishvamitra's greatness, and Dasharath inwardly reflects on the merit that drew such a sage to his house.
ramacharitamanas::1938.modern_relevance: At a family gathering, everyone praises the guest of honour, and you quietly think, 'I must have done something right.' The moment is grateful, but the ego slips in unnoticed.
ramacharitamanas::1938.insight: It reveals how admiration can turn inward into self-congratulation, even when the heart is meant to be humble.

ramacharitamanas::1939.verse_sanskrit: बहुरे लोग रजायसु भयऊ। सुतन्ह समेत नृपति गृहँ गयऊ॥ जहँ तहँ राम ब्याहु सबु गावा। सुजसु पुनीत लोक तिहुँ छावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1939.verse_hindi: आज्ञा हुई तब सब लोग (अपने-अपने घरों को) लौटे। राजा दशरथजी भी पुत्रों सहित महल में गए। जहाँ-तहाँ सब श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विवाह की गाथाएँ गा रहे हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी का पवित्र सुयश तीनों लोकों में छा गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1939.english_translation: Then everyone received permission and returned home. King Dasharath went to the palace with his sons. Everywhere people sang of Ram's wedding, and Ram's pure fame spread through the three worlds.
ramacharitamanas::1939.translation_literal: बहुरे (returned) / लोग (people) / रजायसु (permission) / भयऊ (became) / सुतन्ह (with sons) / समेत (together) / नृपति (king) / गृहँ (home/palace) / गयऊ (went) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / राम (Ram) / ब्याहु (wedding) / सबु (all) / गावा (sang) / सुजसु (good fame) / पुनीत (pure) / लोक (world) / तिहुँ (three) / छावा (spread)
ramacharitamanas::1939.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1939.essence: Ram's wedding leaves no one unchanged; even the air carries its joy.
ramacharitamanas::1939.simple_meaning: The wedding is over, and everyone goes home. Ram's marriage becomes the talk of the land, and his holy fame spreads everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::1939.simple_insight: Joy shared widely becomes its own kind of blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1939.detailed_meaning: The wedding of Ram and Sita has just ended in Mithila. The guests receive permission to leave, and Dasharath returns with his sons. The celebration does not stop at the palace; Ram's marriage becomes a song across the world.
ramacharitamanas::1939.modern_relevance: After a family wedding, relatives are still replaying the best moments in group chats, voice notes, and dinner tables. Some events don't end when the ceremony ends; they keep spreading joy.
ramacharitamanas::1939.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the way joy travels through a community.

ramacharitamanas::1940.verse_sanskrit: आए ब्याहि रामु घर जब तें। बसइ अनंद अवध सब तब तें॥ प्रभु बिबाहँ जस भयउ उछाहू। सकहिं न बरनि गिरा अहिनाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1940.verse_hindi: जब से श्री रामचन्द्रजी विवाह करके घर आए, तब से सब प्रकार का आनंद अयोध्या में आकर बसने लगा। प्रभु के विवाह में आनंद-उत्साह हुआ, उसे सरस्वती और सर्पों के राजा शेषजी भी नहीं कह सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1940.english_translation: From the moment Ram came home after the wedding, all joy came to dwell in Ayodhya. The delight and excitement of the Lord's marriage cannot be described even by Saraswati or Shesha.
ramacharitamanas::1940.translation_literal: आए (came) / ब्याहि (having married) / रामु (Ram) / घर (home) / जब तें (from when) / बसइ (dwells) / अनंद (joy) / अवध (Ayodhya) / सब (all) / तब तें (from then) / प्रभु (Lord's) / बिबाहँ (in marriage) / जस (as) / भयउ (became) / उछाहू (excitement) / सकहिं (can) / न (not) / बरनि (describe) / गिरा (speech) / अहिनाहू (Shesha)
ramacharitamanas::1940.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1940.essence: Ram's presence turns a city into joy.
ramacharitamanas::1940.simple_meaning: Ram's return home after marriage fills Ayodhya with joy. The celebration is so great that even divine speech cannot fully describe it.
ramacharitamanas::1940.simple_insight: Some arrivals change a whole place. When Ram comes home, joy itself seems to settle in.
ramacharitamanas::1940.detailed_meaning: After the wedding, Ram returns to Ayodhya with Sita. The city is no longer just relieved; it feels blessed and overflowing with celebration. The poet says the joy is beyond full description, marking this as the emotional crest of the marriage episode.
ramacharitamanas::1940.modern_relevance: The house feels different the moment someone you love walks back in after a long absence. The tension drops, voices soften, and the whole room seems to breathe again.
ramacharitamanas::1940.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the transforming presence that makes a whole place feel alive.

ramacharitamanas::1941.verse_sanskrit: कबिकुल जीवनु पावन जानी। राम सीय जसु मंगल खानी॥ तेहि ते मैं कछु कहा बखानी। करन पुनीत हेतु निज बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1941.verse_hindi: श्री सीतारामजी के यश को कविकुल के जीवन को पवित्र करने वाला और मंगलों की खान जानकर, इससे मैंने अपनी वाणी को पवित्र करने के लिए कुछ (थोड़ा सा) बखानकर कहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1941.english_translation: Knowing the glory of Ram and Sita as the life of poets and a source of blessings, I have spoken a little to purify my own speech.
ramacharitamanas::1941.translation_literal: कबिकुल (poets' line) / जीवनु (life) / पावन (purifying) / जानी (knowing) / राम (Ram) / सीय (Sita) / जसु (glory) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / खानी (mine/source)॥ / तेहि ते (because of that) / मैं (I) / कछु (something a little) / कहा (said) / बखानी (described) / करन (to make) / पुनीत (pure) / हेतु (for the purpose) / निज (my own) / बानी (speech)॥
ramacharitamanas::1941.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1941.essence: Praise of Ram and Sita purifies the one who speaks it.
ramacharitamanas::1941.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he speaks about Ram and Sita to make his own speech pure, because their glory brings blessings and ennobles poets.
ramacharitamanas::1941.simple_insight: Speaking about what is sacred can change the speaker first.
ramacharitamanas::1941.detailed_meaning: At the end of the marriage celebration in Balkand, Tulsidas steps out of the story and explains why he is singing at all. Ram and Sita's glory is so purifying that even his own words become cleaner by touching it.
ramacharitamanas::1941.modern_relevance: You open a notebook after a messy day and write about the one person or moment that still feels clean. The act of speaking about what is noble steadies your own mind.
ramacharitamanas::1941.insight: It shifts expression from self-display to self-purification.

ramacharitamanas::1942.verse_sanskrit: निज गिरा पावनि करन कारन राम जसु तुलसीं कह्यो। रघुबीर चरित अपार बारिधि पारु कबि कौनें लह्यो॥ उपबीत ब्याह उछाह मंगल सुनि जे सादर गावहीं। बैदेहि राम प्रसाद ते जन सर्बदा सुखु पावहीं॥
ramacharitamanas::1942.verse_hindi: अपनी वाणी को पवित्र करने के लिए तुलसी ने राम का यश कहा है। (नहीं तो) श्री रघुनाथजी का चरित्र अपार समुद्र है, किस कवि ने उसका पार पाया है? जो लोग यज्ञोपवीत और विवाह के मंगलमय उत्सव का वर्णन आदर के साथ सुनकर गावेंगे, वे लोग श्री जानकीजी और श्री रामजी की कृपा से सदा सुख पावेंगे।
ramacharitamanas::1942.english_translation: Tulsidas has spoken Ram's glory to purify his own speech. Raghubir's life is an endless ocean; which poet has ever crossed its far shore? Those who listen with reverence and sing the auspicious celebration of the sacred thread and the wedding will always receive happiness by the grace of Sita and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1942.translation_literal: निज (one's own) / गिरा (speech) / पावनि (purifying) / करन (to do) / कारन (for the reason) / राम जसु (Ram's glory) / तुलसीं (by Tulsidas) / कह्यो (was spoken) / रघुबीर चरित (the deeds of Raghubir) / अपार (endless) / बारिधि (ocean) / पारु (far shore) / कबि (poet) / कौनें (which) / लह्यो (found) / उपबीत (sacred thread) / ब्याह (wedding) / उछाह (celebration) / मंगल (auspicious) / सुनि (hearing) / जे (those who) / सादर (with reverence) / गावहीं (sing) / बैदेहि (Sita) / राम प्रसाद (Ram's grace) / ते (those) / जन (people) / सर्बदा (always) / सुखु (happiness) / पावहीं (receive)
ramacharitamanas::1942.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1942.essence: Ram's glory is too vast to finish, yet singing it purifies the singer.
ramacharitamanas::1942.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he sings Ram's glory to purify his own speech, because Ram's life is too vast for any poet to fully describe. Anyone who reverently sings of Ram and Sita's wedding receives lasting happiness.
ramacharitamanas::1942.simple_insight: Praise becomes purification, not performance. The heart that sings with reverence is already being transformed.
ramacharitamanas::1942.detailed_meaning: At the end of Balkand, Tulsidas steps forward and explains why he has been singing at all. Ram's life is an endless ocean, yet he offers this verse as worship, saying that even hearing the wedding celebration with reverence brings blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1942.modern_relevance: You open a notebook before writing about someone you love and realize no sentence will be enough. Still, the act of speaking with reverence changes you first.
ramacharitamanas::1942.insight: It shifts expression from cleverness to worship, and from description to blessing.

ramacharitamanas::1943.verse_sanskrit: सिय रघुबीर बिबाहु जे सप्रेम गावहिं सुनहिं। तिन्ह कहुँ सदा उछाहु मंगलायतन राम जसु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1943.verse_hindi: श्री सीताजी और श्री रघुनाथजी के विवाह प्रसंग को जो लोग प्रेमपूर्वक गाएँ-सुनेंगे, उनके लिए सदा उत्साह (आनंद) ही उत्साह है, क्योंकि श्री रामचन्द्रजी का यश मंगल का धाम है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1943.english_translation: Those who lovingly sing and hear the wedding of Sita and Raghubir will always know joy upon joy, for Ram’s glory is the home of auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::1943.translation_literal: सिय (Sita) / रघुबीर (Lord of the Raghu clan) / बिबाहु (wedding) / जे (who) / सप्रेम (with love) / गावहिं (sing) / सुनहिं (hear) / तिन्ह (for them) / कहुँ (for) / सदा (always) / उछाहु (joy) / मंगलायतन (abode of auspiciousness) / राम जसु (Ram's glory)
ramacharitamanas::1943.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1943.essence: Love-filled hearing of Ram’s story turns life into celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1943.simple_meaning: People who lovingly sing or hear Ram and Sita’s wedding story will always feel joy, because Ram’s fame itself is a source of blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1943.simple_insight: Devotion changes listening into celebration. The heart becomes lighter just by entering Ram’s story.
ramacharitamanas::1943.detailed_meaning: After praising Ram’s story as the purifier of poetry, Tulsidas closes with a blessing: anyone who lovingly sings or hears the wedding of Sita and Ram will keep finding joy. The marriage scene itself becomes the seal of auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::1943.modern_relevance: You put on a song that reminds you of someone you love, and the whole room softens. Some stories do that too — they don’t just entertain, they change the atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::1943.insight: It teaches you to treat sacred stories as living nourishment, not information.

ramacharitamanas::1944.verse_sanskrit: यस्यांके च विभाति भूधरसुता देवापगा मस्तके भाले बालविधुर्गले च गरलं यस्योरसि व्यालराट्। सोऽयं भूतिविभूषणः सुरवरः सर्वाधिपः सर्वदा शर्वः सर्वगतः शिवः शशिनिभः श्री शंकरः पातु माम् ॥
ramacharitamanas::1944.verse_hindi: जिनकी गोद में हिमाचलसुता पार्वतीजी, मस्तक पर गंगाजी, ललाट पर द्वितीया का चन्द्रमा, कंठ में हलाहल विष और वक्षःस्थल पर सर्पराज शेषजी सुशोभित हैं, वे भस्म से विभूषित, देवताओं में श्रेष्ठ, सर्वेश्वर, संहारकर्ता (या भक्तों के पापनाशक), सर्वव्यापक, कल्याण रूप, चन्द्रमा के समान शुभ्रवर्ण श्री शंकरजी सदा मेरी रक्षा करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1944.english_translation: May Shri Shankar, adorned with ash, the best among the radiant beings, lord of all, ever-present, all-pervading, auspicious, moon-like, protect me forever. On his lap shines Parvati, on his head the Ganga, on his forehead the crescent moon, around his neck the poison, and on his chest the king of serpents.
ramacharitamanas::1944.translation_literal: यस्यांके (on whose lap) / च (and) / विभाति (shines) / भूधरसुता (the daughter of the mountain) / देवापगा (the river of the divine beings) / मस्तके (on the head) / भाले (on the forehead) / बालविधुः (the young moon / crescent moon) / गले (in the neck) / च (and) / गरलम् (poison) / यस्य (whose) / उरसि (on the chest) / व्यालराट् (king of serpents) / सः अयम् (that very one) / भूतिविभूषणः (adorned with ash) / सुरवरः (best among the radiant beings) / सर्वाधिपः (lord of all) / सर्वदा (always) / शर्वः (Shiva) / सर्वगतः (all-pervading) / शिवः (auspicious) / शशिनिभः (moon-like) / श्रीशंकरः (Shri Shankar) / पातु (may protect) / माम् (me)
ramacharitamanas::1944.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1944.essence: Shiva’s vast presence is invoked as shelter before the sorrow begins.
ramacharitamanas::1944.simple_meaning: A prayer to Shiva describes his cosmic form and asks for his protection.
ramacharitamanas::1944.simple_insight: It leaves you with reverence and the feeling of being held by a vast, protective presence.
ramacharitamanas::1944.detailed_meaning: At the opening of Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas begins with a mangal verse to Shiva before the exile story unfolds. He praises Shiva’s cosmic form, then asks for protection, setting a sacred tone for the grief and dharma to come.
ramacharitamanas::1944.modern_relevance: Before a hard conversation, you pause and steady yourself. A few words of reverence can turn fear into composure before the day begins.
ramacharitamanas::1944.insight: It shifts attention from personal anxiety to a larger, stabilizing presence.

ramacharitamanas::1945.verse_sanskrit: प्रसन्नतां या न गताभिषेकतस्तथा न मम्ले वनवासदुःखतः। मुखाम्बुजश्री रघुनन्दनस्य मे सदास्तु सा मंजुलमंगलप्रदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1945.verse_hindi: रघुकुल को आनंद देने वाले श्री रामचन्द्रजी के मुखारविंद की जो शोभा राज्याभिषेक से (राज्याभिषेक की बात सुनकर) न तो प्रसन्नता को प्राप्त हुई और न वनवास के दुःख से मलिन ही हुई, वह (मुखकमल की छबि) मेरे लिए सदा सुंदर मंगलों की देने वाली हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1945.english_translation: May the beauty of Ram's lotus face, which did not swell with joy at coronation nor fade in the sorrow of exile, always bring me auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::1945.translation_literal: प्रसन्नताम् (joy) / या (which) / न (not) / गताभिषेकतः (from the coronation) / तथा (also) / न (not) / मम्ले (faded) / वनवासदुःखतः (from the sorrow of forest-exile) / मुखाम्बुजश्री (the beauty of the lotus-face) / रघुनन्दनस्य (of the delight of Raghu's line) / मे (for me) / सदा (always) / अस्तु (may it be) / सा (that) / मंजुलमंगलप्रदा (beautiful giver of auspiciousness)
ramacharitamanas::1945.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1945.essence: Joy and exile cannot disturb the one who is inwardly whole.
ramacharitamanas::1945.simple_meaning: Ram's face remained beautiful and unchanged whether he was about to be crowned king or sent into exile. Tulsidas asks that this sight always bless him.
ramacharitamanas::1945.simple_insight: Real greatness does not depend on winning or losing. It stays whole through both.
ramacharitamanas::1945.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court's joy is about to turn into exile and grief. Tulsidas pauses to praise Ram's face as unmoved by both coronation and loss. That steady beauty becomes the blessing he wants to carry forever.
ramacharitamanas::1945.modern_relevance: You get the promotion email, then the project is cancelled two days later. Your mood swings with both. This verse points to a steadier way to live: let success and setback pass without changing your face.
ramacharitamanas::1945.insight: It shifts attention from external outcomes to inner steadiness under changing circumstances.

ramacharitamanas::1946.verse_sanskrit: नीलाम्बुजश्यामलकोमलांग सीतासमारोपितवामभागम् । पाणौ महासायकचारुचापं नमामि रामं रघुवंशनाथम् ॥
ramacharitamanas::1946.verse_hindi: नीले कमल के समान श्याम और कोमल जिनके अंग हैं, श्री सीताजी जिनके वाम भाग में विराजमान हैं और जिनके हाथों में (क्रमशः) अमोघ बाण और सुंदर धनुष है, उन रघुवंश के स्वामी श्री रामचन्द्रजी को मैं नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1946.english_translation: I bow to Rama, lord of the Raghu line, whose body is dark as a blue lotus, tender-limbed, with Sita on his left side, and with a mighty arrow and beautiful bow in his hands.
ramacharitamanas::1946.translation_literal: नीलाम्बुजश्यामलकोमलांगम् (having limbs soft and dark like blue lotus) / सीतासमारोपितवामभागम् (with Sita placed on the left side) / पाणौ (in the hand) / महासायकचारुचापम् (mighty arrow and beautiful bow) / नमामि (I bow) / रामम् (to Rama) / रघुवंशनाथम् (lord of the Raghu line)
ramacharitamanas::1946.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1946.essence: Beauty, tenderness, and strength meet in Rama.
ramacharitamanas::1946.simple_meaning: Rama is praised as beautiful, tender, and royal, with Sita beside him and bow and arrow in his hands.
ramacharitamanas::1946.simple_insight: Reverence can hold beauty, power, and tenderness in one gaze.
ramacharitamanas::1946.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas begins his praise of Rama in Ayodhyakand by bowing to the lord of Raghu, visualising him with Sita at his side and weapons in hand. The verse is an opening salutation, not a standalone teaching.
ramacharitamanas::1946.modern_relevance: Before a speech, a meeting, or a hard conversation, you pause and remember who you are answering to: not ego, but what is worthy. That changes your posture.
ramacharitamanas::1946.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary description to worshipful seeing.

ramacharitamanas::1947.verse_sanskrit: श्री गुरु चरन सरोज रज निज मनु मुकुरु सुधारि। बरनउँ रघुबर बिमल जसु जो दायकु फल चारि॥
ramacharitamanas::1947.verse_hindi: श्री गुरुजी के चरण कमलों की रज से अपने मन रूपी दर्पण को साफ करके मैं श्री रघुनाथजी के उस निर्मल यश का वर्णन करता हूँ, जो चारों फलों को (धर्म, अर्थ, काम, मोक्ष को) देने वाला है।
ramacharitamanas::1947.english_translation: By cleansing my mind-mirror with the dust of my guru's lotus feet, I sing the spotless glory of Raghubar, who grants the four aims of life.
ramacharitamanas::1947.translation_literal: श्री गुरु (holy teacher) / चरन (feet) / सरोज (lotus) / रज (dust) / निज (own) / मनु (mind) / मुकुरु (mirror) / सुधारि (having cleansed) / बरनउँ (I describe) / रघुबर (Raghubar, Ram) / बिमल (pure) / जसु (glory) / जो (which) / दायकु (giver) / फल (fruits) / चारि (four)
ramacharitamanas::1947.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1947.essence: Purify the mind first; only then does Ram's glory become visible.
ramacharitamanas::1947.simple_meaning: The poet says he first purifies his own mind by honoring the guru, and only then can he speak about Ram's pure glory, which gives the four goals of human life.
ramacharitamanas::1947.simple_insight: Reverence and inner cleanliness change what you are able to recognize.
ramacharitamanas::1947.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas opens his retelling by bowing to the guru and cleansing his own mind before speaking. He is not just introducing Ram; he is showing that Ram's glory can be described properly only from a purified inner state.
ramacharitamanas::1947.modern_relevance: You open a book after a chaotic morning, and nothing lands until you sit still for a minute. The same words feel different once the mind stops smudging everything.
ramacharitamanas::1947.insight: It shifts attention from raw information to the condition of the mind receiving it.

ramacharitamanas::1948.verse_sanskrit: जब तें रामु ब्याहि घर आए। नित नव मंगल मोद बधाए॥ भुवन चारिदस भूधर भारी। सुकृत मेघ बरषहिं सुख बारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1948.verse_hindi: जब से श्री रामचन्द्रजी विवाह करके घर आए, तब से (अयोध्या में) नित्य नए मंगल हो रहे हैं और आनंद के बधावे बज रहे हैं। चौदहों लोक रूपी बड़े भारी पर्वतों पर पुण्य रूपी मेघ सुख रूपी जल बरसा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1948.english_translation: Since Ram came home after marriage, every day in Ayodhya brought new auspiciousness and joy. Across the fourteen worlds, heavy mountains of merit rained down waters of happiness.
ramacharitamanas::1948.translation_literal: जब तें (since) / रामु (Ram) / ब्याहि (having married) / घर आए (came home) / नित (daily) / नव (new) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मोद (joy) / बधाए (festivals were proclaimed) / भुवन (worlds) / चारिदस (fourteen) / भूधर (mountains) / भारी (great/heavy) / सुकृत (merit) / मेघ (clouds) / बरषहिं (rain) / सुख (happiness) / बारी (water)
ramacharitamanas::1948.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1948.essence: Ram's arrival turns the whole world festive.
ramacharitamanas::1948.simple_meaning: Ram's return after marriage fills Ayodhya with constant celebration, as if merit itself is raining happiness across the world.
ramacharitamanas::1948.simple_insight: Joy multiplies when life is aligned with what is right and beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::1948.detailed_meaning: Ram has returned to Ayodhya after marrying Sita. The city is overflowing with celebration, and Tulsidas paints that joy as something so vast it seems to bless the whole world. This verse opens the atmosphere before the exile begins.
ramacharitamanas::1948.modern_relevance: A house feels different the day someone beloved returns. The air is lighter, the routines soften, and even ordinary tasks seem blessed with meaning.
ramacharitamanas::1948.insight: It shifts attention from private happiness to the way one noble event can lift an entire community.

ramacharitamanas::1949.verse_sanskrit: रिधि सिधि संपति नदीं सुहाई। उमगि अवध अंबुधि कहुँ आई॥ मनिगन पुर नर नारि सुजाती। सुचि अमोल सुंदर सब भाँती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1949.verse_hindi: ऋद्धि-सिद्धि और सम्पत्ति रूपी सुहावनी नदियाँ उमड़-उमड़कर अयोध्या रूपी समुद्र में आ मिलीं। नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष अच्छी जाति के मणियों के समूह हैं, जो सब प्रकार से पवित्र, अमूल्य और सुंदर हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1949.english_translation: Rivers of prosperity and accomplishment flowed into Ayodhya like lovely streams. The men and women of the city were like fine jewels—pure, priceless, and beautiful in every way.
ramacharitamanas::1949.translation_literal: रिधि (prosperity) / सिधि (accomplishment) / संपति (wealth) / नदीं (rivers) / सुहाई (beautiful) / उमगि (surging) / अवध (Ayodhya) / अंबुधि (ocean) / कहुँ (into) / आई (came) / मनिगन (group of jewels) / पुर (city) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / सुजाती (well-born) / सुचि (pure) / अमोल (priceless) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सब भाँती (in every way)
ramacharitamanas::1949.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1949.essence: Ram's presence turns a city into a field of abundance and purity.
ramacharitamanas::1949.simple_meaning: Ayodhya is overflowing with prosperity, and its people are pure, precious, and beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::1949.simple_insight: A blessed life is not just wealth; it is a whole community shining with goodness.
ramacharitamanas::1949.detailed_meaning: Ram has returned home after marriage, and Ayodhya is swelling with joy. The city seems flooded with prosperity, and its people appear like priceless jewels. This verse deepens the picture of a kingdom made radiant by Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::1949.modern_relevance: A neighborhood feels different after one family brings warmth, generosity, and steadiness to it. The change is not only in money or comfort, but in the quality of everyone who lives there.
ramacharitamanas::1949.insight: It shifts attention from material abundance to the moral beauty of a whole community.

ramacharitamanas::1950.verse_sanskrit: कहि न जाइ कछु नगर बिभूती। जनु एतनिअ बिरंचि करतूती॥ सब बिधि सब पुर लोग सुखारी। रामचंद मुख चंदु निहारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1950.verse_hindi: नगर का ऐश्वर्य कुछ कहा नहीं जाता। ऐसा जान पड़ता है, मानो ब्रह्माजी की कारीगरी बस इतनी ही है। सब नगर निवासी श्री रामचन्द्रजी के मुखचन्द्र को देखकर सब प्रकार से सुखी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1950.english_translation: The city's splendor cannot be described. It seems as if Brahma's craftsmanship has reached its limit. Everyone in the city is happy in every way, gazing upon Ramchandra's moonlike face.
ramacharitamanas::1950.translation_literal: कहि न जाइ (cannot be said) / कछु (some) / नगर बिभूती (city splendor) / जनु (as if) / एतनिअ (this much) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / करतूती (craftsmanship) / सब बिधि (in every way) / सब पुर (all city) / लोग (people) / सुखारी (happy) / रामचंद (Ramchandra) / मुख चंदु (moon-face) / निहारी (gazing upon)
ramacharitamanas::1950.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1950.essence: Ram's presence turns a city into joy.
ramacharitamanas::1950.simple_meaning: Ayodhya's beauty is beyond description, and everyone there is joyful because they keep looking at Ram's radiant face.
ramacharitamanas::1950.simple_insight: Beauty becomes complete when the people who see it are at peace.
ramacharitamanas::1950.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya has just welcomed Ram home after his marriage. The city overflows with wealth, beauty, and celebration, yet the real source of its joy is simpler: everyone keeps looking at Ram's face and feels fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::1950.modern_relevance: A home after a wedding feels different when everyone keeps stealing glances at the person who returned with love intact. The room itself is full, but the real brightness is in the faces around it.
ramacharitamanas::1950.insight: It shifts attention from external splendor to the presence that makes a place feel blessed.

ramacharitamanas::1951.verse_sanskrit: मुदित मातु सब सखीं सहेली। फलित बिलोकि मनोरथ बेली॥ राम रूपु गुन सीलु सुभाऊ। प्रमुदित होइ देखि सुनि राऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1951.verse_hindi: सब माताएँ और सखी-सहेलियाँ अपनी मनोरथ रूपी बेल को फली हुई देखकर आनंदित हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के रूप, गुण, शील और स्वभाव को देख-सुनकर राजा दशरथजी बहुत ही आनंदित होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1951.english_translation: All the mothers and their female companions are delighted, seeing the vine of their wish bear fruit. Seeing and hearing Ram's form, virtues, conduct, and nature, King Dasharath is filled with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1951.translation_literal: मुदित (delighted) / मातु (mothers) / सब (all) / सखीं (female companions) / सहेली (friends) / फलित (fruited) / बिलोकि (seeing) / मनोरथ (wish) / बेली (vine) / राम (Ram) / रूपु (form) / गुन (virtues) / सीलु (conduct) / सुभाऊ (nature) / प्रमुदित (filled with joy) / होइ (becoming) / देखि (seeing) / सुनि (hearing) / राऊ (king)
ramacharitamanas::1951.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1951.essence: A noble life makes everyone else's hope bloom.
ramacharitamanas::1951.simple_meaning: The women of Ayodhya are overjoyed because their wish is coming true. Dasharath is equally delighted as he sees Ram's noble qualities.
ramacharitamanas::1951.simple_insight: Joy deepens when a long-held hope starts taking shape in real life.
ramacharitamanas::1951.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the court and the women of the palace are alive with hope. The mothers and their companions feel their long wish beginning to bloom, and Dasharath, seeing Ram's beauty and character, is filled with delight. This verse shows the city leaning toward Ram's coronation.
ramacharitamanas::1951.modern_relevance: You watch someone you've raised finally step into the role they were meant for. Pride, relief, and hope all arrive at once.
ramacharitamanas::1951.insight: It shifts attention from private wishing to the visible ripening of a worthy life.

ramacharitamanas::1952.verse_sanskrit: सब कें उर अभिलाषु अस कहहिं मनाइ महेसु। आप अछत जुबराज पद रामहि देउ नरेसु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1952.verse_hindi: सबके हृदय में ऐसी अभिलाषा है और सब महादेवजी को मनाकर (प्रार्थना करके) कहते हैं कि राजा अपने जीते जी श्री रामचन्द्रजी को युवराज पद दे दें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1952.english_translation: Everyone in their hearts wished that the king, after consulting Mahesh, would give the crown prince's seat to Ram while he was still alive.
ramacharitamanas::1952.translation_literal: सब कें (for everyone) / उर (heart) / अभिलाषु (wish) / अस (thus) / कहहिं (they say) / मनाइ (having pleased) / महेसु (Mahesh) / आप (self) / अछत (while alive) / जुबराज पद (prince's seat) / रामहि (to Ram) / देउ (should give) / नरेसु (the king)
ramacharitamanas::1952.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1952.essence: Ram's worth is so clear that even the city hopes for it.
ramacharitamanas::1952.simple_meaning: Everyone hopes the king will give Ram the crown prince's seat while he is still alive.
ramacharitamanas::1952.simple_insight: A whole city can quietly agree on who is worthy before the official decision is made.
ramacharitamanas::1952.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is overflowing with love for Ram. The people, already delighted by his presence, pray to Mahesh and hope Dasharath will name Ram crown prince while he still lives. This verse gathers the city's hidden wish before the public announcement.
ramacharitamanas::1952.modern_relevance: A room full of people senses who is ready for the promotion before the email is sent. The decision is still pending, but the recognition has already spread.
ramacharitamanas::1952.insight: It shifts attention from private ambition to communal recognition of worth.

ramacharitamanas::1953.verse_sanskrit: एक समय सब सहित समाजा। राजसभाँ रघुराजु बिराजा॥ सकल सुकृत मूरति नरनाहू। राम सुजसु सुनि अतिहि उछाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1953.verse_hindi: एक समय रघुकुल के राजा दशरथजी अपने सारे समाज सहित राजसभा में विराजमान थे। महाराज समस्त पुण्यों की मूर्ति हैं, उन्हें श्री रामचन्द्रजी का सुंदर यश सुनकर अत्यन्त आनंद हो रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1953.english_translation: At one time, King Dasharath sat in the royal assembly with all his attendants. The lord of the people, a treasury of all good deeds, felt great delight hearing Ram's beautiful fame.
ramacharitamanas::1953.translation_literal: एक समय (at one time) / सब सहित समाजा (with all the attendants) / राजसभाँ (in the royal assembly) / रघुराजु (the king of Raghu's line) / बिराजा (was seated) ॥ सकल (all) / सुकृत (good deeds, merit) / मूरति (embodiment) / नरनाहू (lord of men, king) / राम सुजसु (Ram's good fame) / सुनि (hearing) / अतिहि (very much) / उछाहू (delight, enthusiasm) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1953.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1953.essence: Love rejoices when the beloved is praised.
ramacharitamanas::1953.simple_meaning: King Dasharath sits in his court with his attendants and feels deep joy hearing Ram's praise.
ramacharitamanas::1953.simple_insight: A father's happiness can rise simply from hearing his son praised.
ramacharitamanas::1953.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's royal court, Dasharath sits surrounded by his assembly. He is described as the embodiment of good deeds, and the reason for his joy is simple: he hears Ram's fame and feels uplifted by it. This verse sets the emotional stage for the coming decision.
ramacharitamanas::1953.modern_relevance: You hear your child praised at a school event, and your chest loosens before you even speak. Some joy arrives just from seeing someone you love reflected well.
ramacharitamanas::1953.insight: It shifts attention from status to love: a king's delight comes from Ram's reputation, not his own power.

ramacharitamanas::1954.verse_sanskrit: नृप सब रहहिं कृपा अभिलाषें। लोकप करहिं प्रीति रुख राखें॥ वन तीनि काल जग माहीं। भूरिभाग दसरथ सम नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1954.verse_hindi: सब राजा उनकी कृपा चाहते हैं और लोकपालगण उनके रुख को रखते हुए (अनुकूल होकर) प्रीति करते हैं। (पृथ्वी, आकाश, पाताल) तीनों भुवनों में और (भूत, भविष्य, वर्तमान) तीनों कालों में दशरथजी के समान बड़भागी (और) कोई नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1954.english_translation: All kings seek his grace, and the guardians of the worlds stay aligned with his will. In the three worlds and the three times, no one is more fortunate than Dasharath.
ramacharitamanas::1954.translation_literal: नृप (kings) / सब (all) / रहहिं (remain) / कृपा (grace) / अभिलाषें (desiring) / लोकप (guardians of the worlds) / करहिं (do) / प्रीति (affection) / रुख (inclination/will) / राखें (keeping) / वन (worlds) / तीनि (three) / काल (times) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / भूरिभाग (great fortune) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / सम (like) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::1954.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1954.essence: Even the most fortunate ruler still stands inside time.
ramacharitamanas::1954.simple_meaning: Dasharath is so fortunate that every king wants his favor, and even the guardians of the worlds stay in harmony with him.
ramacharitamanas::1954.simple_insight: Some lives seem blessed from every direction, yet that blessing can still be fragile.
ramacharitamanas::1954.detailed_meaning: In Dasharath's court, the narrator pauses to praise his worldly greatness before the deeper turn of the story. Kings seek his favor, the guardians of the worlds favor him, and he seems unmatched in fortune across time and space.
ramacharitamanas::1954.modern_relevance: A person walks into a room and every senior voice bends toward them. The praise feels absolute — until the story reminds you that status can vanish in a single breath.
ramacharitamanas::1954.insight: It frames success as visible alignment from others, not just private achievement.

ramacharitamanas::1955.verse_sanskrit: मंगलमूल रामु सुत जासू। जो कछु कहिअ थोर सबु तासू॥ रायँ सुभायँ मुकुरु कर लीन्हा। बदनु बिलोकि मुकुटु सम कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1955.verse_hindi: मंगलों के मूल श्री रामचन्द्रजी जिनके पुत्र हैं, उनके लिए जो कुछ कहा जाए सब थोड़ा है। राजा ने स्वाभाविक ही हाथ में दर्पण ले लिया और उसमें अपना मुँह देखकर मुकुट को सीधा किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1955.english_translation: Ram, the source of all auspiciousness, is his son; whatever can be said about him is only a little. The king naturally took a mirror in hand, looked at his face, and straightened his crown.
ramacharitamanas::1955.translation_literal: मंगलमूल (root of auspiciousness) / रामु (Ram) / सुत (son) / जासू (whose) / जो (whatever) / कछु (a little) / कहिअ (is said) / थोर (small) / सबु (all) / तासू (his) / रायँ (the king) / सुभायँ (naturally) / मुकुरु (mirror) / कर (hand) / लीन्हा (took) / बदनु (face) / बिलोकि (seeing) / मुकुटु (crown) / सम (straight) / कीन्हा (made)
ramacharitamanas::1955.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1955.essence: Even a king becomes small before Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1955.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond full praise, and King Dasharath adjusts his crown after seeing his reflection.
ramacharitamanas::1955.simple_insight: Even greatness can be met with humility when the heart remembers who stands above it.
ramacharitamanas::1955.detailed_meaning: In Dasharath's court in Ayodhya, the king sits in royal splendour while praise of Ram fills the hall. The verse pauses on a simple gesture: Dasharath looks into a mirror and straightens his crown, a quiet sign that his honour comes second to his son.
ramacharitamanas::1955.modern_relevance: You catch your reflection before a big family gathering and fix your collar, then remember the child who makes your name matter more than your title. Pride softens into reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1955.insight: It shifts attention from self-display to honouring the higher presence in one's life.

ramacharitamanas::1956.verse_sanskrit: श्रवन समीप भए सित केसा। मनहुँ जरठपनु अस उपदेसा॥ नृप जुबराजु राम कहुँ देहू। जीवन जनम लाहु किन लेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1956.verse_hindi: (देखा कि) कानों के पास बाल सफेद हो गए हैं, मानो बुढ़ापा ऐसा उपदेश कर रहा है कि हे राजन् ! श्री रामचन्द्रजी को युवराज पद देकर अपने जीवन और जन्म का लाभ क्यों नहीं लेते ॥
ramacharitamanas::1956.english_translation: His hair near the ears had turned white, as if old age itself were advising him: "O king, give Rama the crown prince's seat. Why not take the true benefit of your life and birth?"
ramacharitamanas::1956.translation_literal: श्रवन (ears) / समीप (near) / भए (became) / सित केसा (white hair) / मनहुँ (as if) / जरठपनु (old age) / अस (such) / उपदेसा (advice) / नृप (king) / जुबराजु (crown prince) / राम कहुँ (for Rama) / देहू (give) / जीवन (life) / जनम (birth) / लाहु (benefit) / किन (why) / लेहू (take)
ramacharitamanas::1956.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1956.essence: Time itself urges the right decision before it slips away.
ramacharitamanas::1956.simple_meaning: Old age seems to advise Dasharath to give Rama the crown prince's seat and make his life truly worthwhile.
ramacharitamanas::1956.simple_insight: Sometimes the clearest guidance comes as a quiet reminder that time is moving, and the right act is already obvious.
ramacharitamanas::1956.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath sees his hair has gone white near the ears. That sight feels like old age itself speaking. The moment pushes him toward the one duty that gives meaning to his life: placing Rama on the throne.
ramacharitamanas::1956.modern_relevance: You catch your reflection in the bathroom mirror and notice the first silver hairs. The question changes: will you keep postponing the hard, right decision, or finally make the call that matters?
ramacharitamanas::1956.insight: It shifts attention from delay to decisive obligation: do the rightful act while the moment is still open.

ramacharitamanas::1957.verse_sanskrit: यह बिचारु उर आनि नृप सुदिनु सुअवसरु पाइ। प्रेम पुलकि तन मुदित मन गुरहि सुनायउ जाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1957.verse_hindi: हृदय में यह विचार लाकर (युवराज पद देने का निश्चय कर) राजा दशरथजी ने शुभ दिन और सुंदर समय पाकर, प्रेम से पुलकित शरीर हो आनंदमग्न मन से उसे गुरु वशिष्ठजी को जा सुनाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1957.english_translation: Having brought this thought into his heart, the king found an auspicious day and fitting moment. His body thrilled with love, his mind filled with joy, and he went to tell Guru Vashishtha.
ramacharitamanas::1957.translation_literal: यह (this) / बिचारु (thought) / उर (heart) / आनि (bringing) / नृप (king) / सुदिनु (auspicious day) / सुअवसरु (good opportunity) / पाइ (having found) / प्रेम (love) / पुलकि (thrilled) / तन (body) / मुदित (delighted) / मन (mind) / गुरहि (to the guru) / सुनायउ (told) / जाइ (going)
ramacharitamanas::1957.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1957.essence: A loving decision ripens before it is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1957.simple_meaning: King Dasharath held the decision in his heart, waited for the right moment, and then joyfully told Guru Vashishtha.
ramacharitamanas::1957.simple_insight: A right decision becomes lighter when it is shared with reverence and care.
ramacharitamanas::1957.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has already resolved to give Ram the throne. With love surging through him, he waits for an auspicious moment and then goes to Vashishtha to announce it. This verse is the quiet step before the royal declaration.
ramacharitamanas::1957.modern_relevance: You finally know the hard thing you need to say. Before sending the message, you wait for the right time, steady yourself, and speak with care.
ramacharitamanas::1957.insight: It teaches you to honor important decisions by timing and sharing them well, not blurting them out in haste.

ramacharitamanas::1958.verse_sanskrit: कहइ भुआलु सुनिअ मुनिनायक। भए राम सब बिधि सब लायक॥ सेवक सचिव सकल पुरबासी। जे हमार अरि मित्र उदासी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1958.verse_hindi: राजा ने कहा- हे मुनिराज! (कृपया यह निवेदन) सुनिए। श्री रामचन्द्रजी अब सब प्रकार से सब योग्य हो गए हैं। सेवक, मंत्री, सब नगर निवासी और जो हमारे शत्रु, मित्र या उदासीन हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1958.english_translation: The king said, "Listen, sage leader. Ram is now fit in every way, for every role. Servants, ministers, all the people of the city, and even those who are our enemies, friends, or indifferent."
ramacharitamanas::1958.translation_literal: कहइ (said) / भुआलु (the king) / सुनिअ (listen) / मुनिनायक (leader of sages) / भए (has become) / राम (Ram) / सब बिधि (in every way) / सब लायक (fully fit) / सेवक (servants) / सचिव (ministers) / सकल (all) / पुरबासी (city-dwellers) / जे (who) / हमार (our) / अरि (enemies) / मित्र (friends) / उदासी (indifferent)
ramacharitamanas::1958.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::1958.essence: Ram is ready because his whole life has already trained him for the throne.
ramacharitamanas::1958.simple_meaning: Dasharath tells the sage that Ram is fully ready for kingship, and that everyone in the kingdom sees it too.
ramacharitamanas::1958.simple_insight: Readiness is not private; a life’s fitness becomes visible to everyone around it.
ramacharitamanas::1958.detailed_meaning: Dasharath speaks to the sage after deciding to crown Ram. He is not praising Ram lightly; he is presenting him as ready in every way, with the whole city as witness. The moment turns personal love into a public declaration.
ramacharitamanas::1958.modern_relevance: You watch someone step into a role after years of quiet responsibility — and everyone who has worked with them knows it before the title arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1958.insight: It shifts attention from ambition to earned readiness, showing that true calling is confirmed by character and community.

ramacharitamanas::1959.verse_sanskrit: सबहि रामु प्रिय जेहि बिधि मोही। प्रभु असीस जनु तनु धरि सोही॥ बिप्र सहित परिवार गोसाईं। करहिं छोहु सब रौरिहि नाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1959.verse_hindi: सभी को श्री रामचन्द्र वैसे ही प्रिय हैं, जैसे वे मुझको हैं। (उनके रूप में) आपका आशीर्वाद ही मानो शरीर धारण करके शोभित हो रहा है। हे स्वामी! सारे ब्राह्मण, परिवार सहित आपके ही समान उन पर स्नेह करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1959.english_translation: Ram is dear to everyone just as he is dear to me. Your blessing seems to have taken form in him. O lord, all the Brahmins and the whole family love him as you do.
ramacharitamanas::1959.translation_literal: सबहि (to everyone) / रामु (Ram) / प्रिय (dear) / जेहि बिधि (in the same way) / मोही (to me) / प्रभु (lord/blessing) / असीस (blessing) / जनु (as if) / तनु धरि (taking a body) / सोही (shines) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / सहित (along with) / परिवार (family) / गोसाईं (lord) / करहिं (do) / छोहु (affection) / सब (all) / रौरिहि (to your own) / नाईं (like)
ramacharitamanas::1959.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::1959.essence: True worth wins the same love from everyone.
ramacharitamanas::1959.simple_meaning: Dasharath says Ram is loved by everyone, just as he loves Ram. He sees Ram as a living blessing, and says even the Brahmins and family feel affection for him.
ramacharitamanas::1959.simple_insight: Love for the worthy person becomes a shared bond, not a private feeling.
ramacharitamanas::1959.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has just decided to honor Ram. Speaking warmly to the sage and court, he says Ram is dear to all in the same way he is dear to him. This is part of his joyful announcement, not the full teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::1959.modern_relevance: You introduce someone at a family gathering and every room softens at once. Their kindness is obvious before anyone explains it.
ramacharitamanas::1959.insight: It frames Ram’s worth as publicly visible, not merely a father’s bias.

ramacharitamanas::1960.verse_sanskrit: जे गुर चरन रेनु सिर धरहीं। ते जनु सकल बिभव बस करहीं॥ मोहि सम यहु अनुभयउ न दूजें। सबु पायउँ रज पावनि पूजें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1960.verse_hindi: जो लोग गुरु के चरणों की रज को मस्तक पर धारण करते हैं, वे मानो समस्त ऐश्वर्य को अपने वश में कर लेते हैं। इसका अनुभव मेरे समान दूसरे किसी ने नहीं किया। आपकी पवित्र चरण रज की पूजा करके मैंने सब कुछ पा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1960.english_translation: Those who place the dust of the teacher's feet on their heads seem to bring all prosperity under their control. No one has had this experience like I have. By worshipping your sacred foot-dust, I have attained everything.
ramacharitamanas::1960.translation_literal: जे (those who) / गुर (teacher) / चरन (feet) / रेनु (dust) / सिर (head) / धरहीं (place) / ते (they) / जनु (as if) / सकल (all) / बिभव (prosperity, wealth) / बस (under control) / करहीं (make)॥ मोहि (to me) / सम (like) / यहु (this) / अनुभयउ (was experienced) / न (not) / दूजें (by another) / सबु (everything) / पायउँ (I obtained) / रज (dust) / पावनि (sacred, purifying) / पूजें (by worshipping)॥
ramacharitamanas::1960.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1960.essence: Humility before the teacher opens what pride cannot reach.
ramacharitamanas::1960.simple_meaning: Honouring the teacher with complete humility brings real abundance. The speaker says that worshipping the teacher's sacred foot-dust gave him everything he needed.
ramacharitamanas::1960.simple_insight: Humility stops feeling like loss and starts feeling like access.
ramacharitamanas::1960.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, King Dasharath speaks with the sages about Ram and his own heart. He says that those who place the teacher's dust on their head gain all prosperity, and he speaks from personal experience after worshipping that sacred dust himself.
ramacharitamanas::1960.modern_relevance: You sit across from a mentor who has seen your excuses before. You stop performing, listen properly, and something in you opens. Respect becomes the doorway, not the price.
ramacharitamanas::1960.insight: It shifts reverence from ceremony to a practical source of transformation.

ramacharitamanas::1961.verse_sanskrit: अब अभिलाषु एकु मन मोरें। पूजिहि नाथ अनुग्रह तोरें॥ मुनि प्रसन्न लखि सहज सनेहू। कहेउ नरेस रजायसु देहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1961.verse_hindi: अब मेरे मन में एक ही अभिलाषा है। हे नाथ! वह भी आप ही के अनुग्रह से पूरी होगी। राजा का सहज प्रेम देखकर मुनि ने प्रसन्न होकर कहा- नरेश! आज्ञा दीजिए (कहिए, क्या अभिलाषा है?) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1961.english_translation: Now my mind has only one desire. O Lord, it will be fulfilled by your grace. Seeing the king's natural affection, the sage grew pleased and said, 'O king, speak your wish.'
ramacharitamanas::1961.translation_literal: अब (now) / अभिलाषु (desire) / एकु (one) / मन (mind) / मोरें (in my) / पूजिहि (will be fulfilled) / नाथ (Lord) / अनुग्रह (grace) / तोरें (your) / मुनि (sage) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / लखि (seeing) / सहज (natural) / सनेहू (affection) / कहेउ (said) / नरेस (king) / रजायसु (command) / देहू (give)
ramacharitamanas::1961.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1961.essence: One true wish becomes enough when it rests on grace.
ramacharitamanas::1961.simple_meaning: The king has one sincere wish, and he trusts it will be fulfilled only through grace. The sage, seeing this natural affection, invites him to speak freely.
ramacharitamanas::1961.simple_insight: Pure desire becomes peaceful when it rests in grace, not control.
ramacharitamanas::1961.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, a king stands before a sage with humility and warmth. He says he has only one wish, and even that depends on the sage's grace. The sage, moved by this simple affection, asks him to speak.
ramacharitamanas::1961.modern_relevance: You finally sit across from someone who can help, but you stop performing and speak plainly. The pressure drops the moment you trust that sincerity matters more than control.
ramacharitamanas::1961.insight: It shifts the mind from grasping for outcomes to offering one honest request with trust.

ramacharitamanas::1962.verse_sanskrit: राजन राउर नामु जसु सब अभिमत दातार। फल अनुगामी महिप मनि मन अभिलाषु तुम्हार ॥
ramacharitamanas::1962.verse_hindi: हे राजन! आपका नाम और यश ही सम्पूर्ण मनचाही वस्तुओं को देने वाला है। हे राजाओं के मुकुटमणि! आपके मन की अभिलाषा फल का अनुगमन करती है (अर्थात आपके इच्छा करने के पहले ही फल उत्पन्न हो जाता है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1962.english_translation: O king, your very name and fame grant everything desired. Jewel among rulers, your wish is followed by its fruit.
ramacharitamanas::1962.translation_literal: राजन (O king) / राउर (your) / नामु (name) / जसु (fame) / सब (all) / अभिमत (desired) / दातार (giver) / फल (fruit) / अनुगामी (following) / महिप मनि (jewel among kings) / मन (mind) / अभिलाषु (wish) / तुम्हार (your)
ramacharitamanas::1962.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1962.essence: True greatness makes good things arrive before they are asked for.
ramacharitamanas::1962.simple_meaning: The king’s name is praised as one that fulfills every wish, and his desire is said to bear fruit even before it is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1962.simple_insight: Being in the presence of a noble ruler feels like standing near abundance itself.
ramacharitamanas::1962.detailed_meaning: In Ajodhyakand, the sage has been won over by Dasharath’s humility and devotion. He praises the king’s name and fame as wish-granting, and says even his desire seems to summon results. This prepares the way for the request about Ram’s coronation.
ramacharitamanas::1962.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence changes the room before they speak. Their calm, integrity, and goodwill make everything feel possible, as if good things gather around them naturally.
ramacharitamanas::1962.insight: It shifts attention from power as control to power as blessing others effortlessly.

ramacharitamanas::1963.verse_sanskrit: सब बिधि गुरु प्रसन्न जियँ जानी। बोलेउ राउ रहँसि मृदु बानी॥ नाथ रामु करिअहिं जुबराजू। कहिअ कृपा करि करिअ समाजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1963.verse_hindi: अपने जी में गुरुजी को सब प्रकार से प्रसन्न जानकर, हर्षित होकर राजा कोमल वाणी से बोले- हे नाथ! श्री रामचन्द्र को युवराज कीजिए। कृपा करके कहिए (आज्ञा दीजिए) तो तैयारी की जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1963.english_translation: Having seen the teacher fully pleased in his heart, the king spoke with a smile in gentle words: “O lord, let Ram be crowned prince. Kindly give the order, and preparations will be made.”
ramacharitamanas::1963.translation_literal: सब बिधि (in every way) / गुरु (teacher) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानी (having known) / बोलेउ (spoke) / राउ (king) / रहँसि (smilingly) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (speech) ॥ नाथ (lord) / रामु (Ram) / करिअहिं (may be made) / जुबराजू (crown prince) / कहिअ (say) / कृपा (grace) / करि (doing) / करिअ (let be done) / समाजू (preparations) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1963.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::1963.essence: The king asks for Ram's rightful place with humility, not force.
ramacharitamanas::1963.simple_meaning: Dasharath, seeing his teacher pleased, gently asks that Ram be made crown prince and the preparations begin.
ramacharitamanas::1963.simple_insight: A rightful request can be soft. Strength does not need harshness.
ramacharitamanas::1963.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, King Dasharath has gone to his teacher with a heart full of hope. Seeing the teacher pleased, he speaks gently and asks for Ram's coronation as crown prince. The moment is quiet, but it carries the future of Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::1963.modern_relevance: You finally get a chance to ask for what matters after sensing the other person is open. The right timing makes even a big request feel simple and respectful.
ramacharitamanas::1963.insight: It teaches you to ask directly, but with humility and good timing.

ramacharitamanas::1964.verse_sanskrit: मोहि अछत यहु होइ उछाहू। लहहिं लोग सब लोचन लाहू॥ प्रभु प्रसाद सिव सबइ निबाहीं। यह लालसा एक मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1964.verse_hindi: मेरे जीते जी यह आनंद उत्सव हो जाए, (जिससे) सब लोग अपने नेत्रों का लाभ प्राप्त करें। प्रभु (आप) के प्रसाद से शिवजी ने सब कुछ निबाह दिया (सब इच्छाएँ पूर्ण कर दीं), केवल यही एक लालसा मन में रह गई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1964.english_translation: May this celebration happen while I am still alive, so everyone can behold it with their own eyes. By the divine grace, Shiva has fulfilled everything; only this one longing remains in my mind.
ramacharitamanas::1964.translation_literal: मोहि (to me) / अछत (while alive) / यहु (this) / होइ (may happen) / उछाहू (celebration)॥ लहहिं (may receive) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / लोचन (eyes) / लाहू (benefit)॥ प्रभु (lord) / प्रसाद (grace) / सिव (Shiva) / सबइ (all) / निबाहीं (fulfilled/completed)॥ यह (this) / लालसा (longing) / एक (one) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in)॥
ramacharitamanas::1964.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::1964.essence: A fulfilled life can still ache for one last sight.
ramacharitamanas::1964.simple_meaning: Dasharath wants to live long enough to see Ram's joyful coronation. He says everything else has been fulfilled; only this one wish remains.
ramacharitamanas::1964.simple_insight: Love can narrow a whole life down to one final wish.
ramacharitamanas::1964.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath thinks the long-awaited coronation of Ram is finally near. He feels every other desire has been met and asks only to live long enough to witness this joy with his own eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1964.modern_relevance: You keep one photo on your phone because it holds the moment you most want to see happen. Dasharath's heart is like that: everything else can wait, but not this.
ramacharitamanas::1964.insight: It shifts attention from private satisfaction to witnessing a loved one's fulfillment.

ramacharitamanas::1965.verse_sanskrit: पुनि न सोच तनु रहउ कि जाऊ। जेहिं न होइ पाछें पछिताऊ॥ सुनि मुनि दसरथ बचन सुहाए। मंगल मोद मूल मन भाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1965.verse_hindi: (इस लालसा के पूर्ण हो जाने पर) फिर सोच नहीं, शरीर रहे या चला जाए, जिससे मुझे पीछे पछतावा न हो। दशरथजी के मंगल और आनंद के मूल सुंदर वचन सुनकर मुनि मन में बहुत प्रसन्न हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1965.english_translation: Then I will have no more worry, whether this body remains or departs, so that I do not regret it later. Hearing King Dasharath's lovely words, rooted in auspiciousness and joy, the sage was delighted in his mind.
ramacharitamanas::1965.translation_literal: पुनि (then again) / न (not) / सोच (worry) / तनु (body) / रहउ (remain) / कि (or) / जाऊ (depart) / जेहिं (so that) / न (not) / होइ (becomes) / पाछें (later) / पछिताऊ (regret) / सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (sage) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / बचन (words) / सुहाए (lovely) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मोद (joy) / मूल (root) / मन (mind) / भाए (pleased)
ramacharitamanas::1965.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::1965.essence: Choose so completely that regret has nowhere to enter.
ramacharitamanas::1965.simple_meaning: Dasharath says he wants the blessing fulfilled so completely that he will have no regret, even if his body must go. The sage listening is filled with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1965.simple_insight: A settled mind wants no second-guessing later. It chooses the path that leaves no inner remorse.
ramacharitamanas::1965.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is speaking with the sage after asking for Ram's coronation. He says he wants the wish fulfilled so fully that he will not be left with regret, even if it costs him his life. The sage hears the sincerity and rejoices.
ramacharitamanas::1965.modern_relevance: You sign the form, send the message, and know there is no clean way back. What matters now is choosing so clearly that you can live with it tomorrow.
ramacharitamanas::1965.insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to clean commitment: act in a way that leaves no later remorse.

ramacharitamanas::1966.verse_sanskrit: सुनु नृप जासु बिमुख पछिताहीं। जासु भजन बिनु जरनि न जाहीं॥ भयउ तुम्हार तनय सोइ स्वामी। रामु पुनीत प्रेम अनुगामी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1966.verse_hindi: (वशिष्ठजी ने कहा-) हे राजन् ! सुनिए, जिनसे विमुख होकर लोग पछताते हैं और जिनके भजन बिना जी की जलन नहीं जाती, वही स्वामी (सर्वलोक महेश्वर) श्री रामजी आपके पुत्र हुए हैं, जो पवित्र प्रेम के अनुगामी हैं। (श्री रामजी पवित्र प्रेम के पीछे-पीछे चलने वाले हैं, इसी से तो प्रेमवश आपके पुत्र हुए हैं।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1966.english_translation: Listen, king: people regret turning away from the one whose worship ends the burning in the heart. That same Lord has become your son, Ram, who follows pure love.
ramacharitamanas::1966.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / नृप (king) / जासु (whose) / बिमुख (turned away) / पछिताहीं (regret) / जासु (whose) / भजन (worship) / बिनु (without) / जरनि (burning) / न (not) / जाहीं (go away) / भयउ (became) / तुम्हार (your) / तनय (son) / सोइ (that same) / स्वामी (lord) / रामु (Ram) / पुनीत (pure) / प्रेम (love) / अनुगामी (follower)
ramacharitamanas::1966.speaker: Vashishtha
ramacharitamanas::1966.essence: Ram is the one whose nearness ends regret and inner burning.
ramacharitamanas::1966.simple_meaning: Turning away from Ram brings regret, and devotion to him ends the inner burning. Vashishtha says this same Ram has been born as Dasharath's son and follows pure love.
ramacharitamanas::1966.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing the heart's restlessness has a true home.
ramacharitamanas::1966.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Vashishtha speaks to Dasharath after the king has longed for Ram's coronation. He reminds the king that Ram is not an ordinary prince: people regret losing connection with him, and devotion to him ends inner torment. That same Ram has now come as Dasharath's son.
ramacharitamanas::1966.modern_relevance: You finally meet the person who makes your mind quiet after months of chasing noise. The relief is not that they changed your life, but that your heart recognized its own home.
ramacharitamanas::1966.insight: It shifts attention from temporary relief to the one presence that truly ends restlessness.

ramacharitamanas::1967.verse_sanskrit: बेगि बिलंबु न करिअ नृप साजिअ सबुइ समाजु। सुदिन सुमंगलु तबहिं जब रामु होहिं जुबराजु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1967.verse_hindi: हे राजन् ! अब देर न कीजिए, शीघ्र सब सामान सजाइए। शुभ दिन और सुंदर मंगल तभी है, जब श्री रामचन्द्रजी युवराज हो जाएँ (अर्थात उनके अभिषेक के लिए सभी दिन शुभ और मंगलमय हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1967.english_translation: O king, do not delay. Prepare everything at once. The day is truly auspicious only when Ram becomes crown prince.
ramacharitamanas::1967.translation_literal: बेगि (quickly) / बिलंबु (delay) / न करिअ (do not do) / नृप (O king) / साजिअ (prepare) / सबुइ (all) / समाजु (arrangements) / सुदिनु (auspicious day) / सुमंगलु (most auspicious) / तबहिं (then only) / जब (when) / रामु (Ram) / होहिं (becomes) / जुबराजु (crown prince)
ramacharitamanas::1967.speaker: Vasistha
ramacharitamanas::1967.essence: The right day is the one that places Ram first.
ramacharitamanas::1967.simple_meaning: Vasistha urges King Dasharath to stop delaying and arrange the coronation immediately. The real blessing of the day is Ram becoming crown prince.
ramacharitamanas::1967.simple_insight: Right timing is not about the calendar; it is about aligning action with what is truly worthy.
ramacharitamanas::1967.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Vasistha is pressing Dasharath to begin Ram's coronation without hesitation. The court is ready, the king is swayed by joy, and this moment turns from private happiness into a public promise.
ramacharitamanas::1967.modern_relevance: You finally have everyone's agreement, but the room still drags its feet. This verse cuts through the hesitation: stop polishing the plan and do the thing that matters.
ramacharitamanas::1967.insight: It shifts attention from procedural delay to immediate alignment with dharma.

ramacharitamanas::1968.verse_sanskrit: मुदित महीपति मंदिर आए। सेवक सचिव सुमंत्रु बोलाए॥ कहि जयजीव सीस तिन्ह नाए। भूप सुमंगल बचन सुनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1968.verse_hindi: राजा आनंदित होकर महल में आए और उन्होंने सेवकों को तथा मंत्री सुमंत्र को बुलवाया। उन लोगों ने 'जय-जीव' कहकर सिर नवाए। तब राजा ने सुंदर मंगलमय वचन (श्री रामजी को युवराज पद देने का प्रस्ताव) सुनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1968.english_translation: The king returned to the palace in joy, summoned his servants and the minister Sumantra, and they bowed their heads saying, 'Victory and long life.' Then the king spoke auspicious words.
ramacharitamanas::1968.translation_literal: मुदित (glad) / महीपति (king) / मंदिर (palace) / आए (came) / सेवक (servants) / सचिव (minister) / सुमंत्रु (Sumantra) / बोलाए (called) / कहि (saying) / जयजीव (victory and long life) / सीस (heads) / तिन्ह (they) / नाए (bowed) / भूप (king) / सुमंगल (auspicious) / बचन (words) / सुनाए (spoke)
ramacharitamanas::1968.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1968.essence: Joy gathers in the palace before the decisive words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1968.simple_meaning: King Dasharath returns happily to the palace, calls his attendants and Sumantra, and speaks in a joyful, formal way.
ramacharitamanas::1968.simple_insight: A moment of celebration can still carry a turning point inside it.
ramacharitamanas::1968.detailed_meaning: Dasharath returns to the palace pleased, with Sumantra and the court around him. The atmosphere is respectful and bright, but this is only the opening movement before he announces Ram's coronation.
ramacharitamanas::1968.modern_relevance: You walk into a family room smiling, and everyone straightens up because they sense news is coming. The mood is warm, but the real change is still just about to be spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1968.insight: It sets the scene for the announcement, showing how public joy can hide a coming fracture.

ramacharitamanas::1969.verse_sanskrit: जौं पाँचहि मत लागै नीका। करहु हरषि हियँ रामहि टीका ॥
ramacharitamanas::1969.verse_hindi: (और कहा-) यदि पंचों को (आप सबको) यह मत अच्छा लगे, तो हृदय में हर्षित होकर आप लोग श्री रामचन्द्र का राजतिलक कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1969.english_translation: If the council approves, then gladly crown Ram in your hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1969.translation_literal: जौं (if) / पाँचहि (five; the council of five) / मत (opinion) / लागै (seems) / नीका (good) / करहु (do) / हरषि (joyfully) / हियँ (in the heart) / रामहि (Ram) / टीका (coronation)
ramacharitamanas::1969.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::1969.essence: A good act should be welcomed openly, not imposed in haste.
ramacharitamanas::1969.simple_meaning: If the ministers agree, then Ram should be crowned with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1969.simple_insight: A rightful decision becomes lighter when everyone stands behind it.
ramacharitamanas::1969.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has returned to the palace and called his ministers and counselors. After announcing Ram's consecration, he asks for their approval, turning a royal decision into a shared moment of joy before the ceremony begins.
ramacharitamanas::1969.modern_relevance: You have the plan ready, but the room still needs to be brought with you. A leader speaks plainly, checks alignment, and then moves forward without forcing the moment.
ramacharitamanas::1969.insight: It models leadership that seeks consent before action, not ego before approval.

ramacharitamanas::1970.verse_sanskrit: मंत्री मुदित सुनत प्रिय बानी। अभिमत बिरवँ परेउ जनु पानी॥ बिनती सचिव करहिं कर जोरी। जिअहु जगतपति बरिस करोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1970.verse_hindi: इस प्रिय वाणी को सुनते ही मंत्री ऐसे आनंदित हुए मानो उनके मनोरथ रूपी पौधे पर पानी पड़ गया हो। मंत्री हाथ जोड़कर विनती करते हैं कि हे जगत्पति! आप करोड़ों वर्ष जिएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1970.english_translation: The ministers were delighted to hear the beloved words, as if water had fallen on a wished-for plant. With folded hands, the ministers prayed: "May you live for millions of years, lord of the world."
ramacharitamanas::1970.translation_literal: मंत्री (ministers) / मुदित (delighted) / सुनत (hearing) / प्रिय बानी (beloved words) / अभिमत (desired) / बिरवँ (plant) / परेउ (fell) / जनु (as if) / पानी (water) / बिनती (request/prayer) / सचिव (ministers) / करहिं (do) / कर जोरी (with joined hands) / जिअहु (may you live) / जगतपति (lord of the world) / बरिस (years) / करोरी (millions)
ramacharitamanas::1970.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1970.essence: Delighted support rises when words match hidden hopes.
ramacharitamanas::1970.simple_meaning: The ministers are overjoyed by the king’s words and respectfully pray for his long life.
ramacharitamanas::1970.simple_insight: Warm approval can turn hesitation into wholehearted support.
ramacharitamanas::1970.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath has just spoken of crowning Ram. The ministers, relieved and delighted, respond with folded hands and blessings. Their joy shows that the court is ready to welcome Ram’s rise.
ramacharitamanas::1970.modern_relevance: A team hears the plan they had secretly hoped for, and the whole room changes at once. Relief makes people generous, respectful, and eager to support what was just announced.
ramacharitamanas::1970.insight: It shows how shared joy can quickly transform a group from passive listeners into active supporters.

ramacharitamanas::1971.verse_sanskrit: जग मंगल भल काजु बिचारा। बेगिअ नाथ न लाइअ बारा॥ नृपहि मोदु सुनि सचिव सुभाषा। बढ़त बौंड़ जनु लही सुसाखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1971.verse_hindi: आपने जगतभर का मंगल करने वाला भला काम सोचा है। हे नाथ! शीघ्रता कीजिए, देर न लगाइए। मंत्रियों की सुंदर वाणी सुनकर राजा को ऐसा आनंद हुआ मानो बढ़ती हुई बेल सुंदर डाली का सहारा पा गई हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1971.english_translation: You have planned a deed that will bring auspiciousness to the whole world. Lord, do not delay. Hearing the ministers' gracious words, the king felt such joy, like a growing vine finding a lovely support.
ramacharitamanas::1971.translation_literal: जग (world) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / भल (good) / काजु (work, deed) / बिचारा (considered, thought) । / बेगिअ (quickly) / नाथ (lord) / न (not) / लाइअ (put, delay) / बारा (delay) ॥ / नृपहि (to the king) / मोदु (joy) / सुनि (hearing) / सचिव (ministers) / सुभाषा (good speech) / बढ़त (growing) / बौंड़ (vine) / जनु (as if) / लही (found) / सुसाखा (good support, branch) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1971.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1971.essence: A right deed gains force when everyone helps it move quickly.
ramacharitamanas::1971.simple_meaning: The ministers praise the plan to crown Ram and urge the king to act quickly. The king is so pleased that his joy is compared to a vine finding a strong branch.
ramacharitamanas::1971.simple_insight: Good plans need swift support. Shared approval can turn hesitation into glad action.
ramacharitamanas::1971.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the ministers hear the proposal for Ram's coronation and instantly recognize it as a blessing for the world. They urge Dasharath not to delay. The king's heart rises with joy as the plan begins to take shape.
ramacharitamanas::1971.modern_relevance: A team finally agrees on the right decision in a tense meeting, and relief floods the room. The hardest part is over: everyone can feel the work moving forward.
ramacharitamanas::1971.insight: It shifts attention from private hesitation to timely support for the right action.

ramacharitamanas::1972.verse_sanskrit: कहेउ भूप मुनिराज कर जोइ जोइ आयसु होइ। राम राज अभिषेक हित बेगि करहु सोइ सोइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1972.verse_hindi: राजा ने कहा- श्री रामचन्द्र के राज्याभिषेक के लिए मुनिराज वशिष्ठजी की जो-जो आज्ञा हो, आप लोग वही सब तुरंत करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1972.english_translation: The king said, "Whatever command the sage-king gives, do it all at once for Rama's coronation."
