ramacharitamanas::1972.translation_literal: कहेउ (said) / भूप (the king) / मुनिराज (sage-king) / कर जोइ जोइ (whatever, whatever) / आयसु (command) / होइ (is) / राम राज अभिषेक (Rama's royal consecration) / हित (for the sake of) / बेगि (quickly) / करहु (do) / सोइ सोइ (that, that)
ramacharitamanas::1972.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::1972.essence: True readiness obeys the right command without delay.
ramacharitamanas::1972.simple_meaning: Dasharath tells his ministers to carry out every order of Vashishtha quickly for Rama's coronation.
ramacharitamanas::1972.simple_insight: Real devotion shows up as immediate obedience, not hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::1972.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace has just turned joyful after the ministers hear of Rama's coronation. Dasharath, eager and obedient, tells them to follow Vashishtha's every instruction at once. The scene moves the story from intention into action.
ramacharitamanas::1972.modern_relevance: Your team finally agrees on the plan, and the room fills with relief. The next step is not debate but clean execution.
ramacharitamanas::1972.insight: It shifts attention from wishing for a good outcome to carrying out the needed steps without delay.

ramacharitamanas::1973.verse_sanskrit: हरषि मुनीस कहेउ मृदु बानी। आनहु सकल सुतीरथ पानी॥ औषध मूल फूल फल पाना। कहे नाम गनि मंगल नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::1973.verse_hindi: मुनिराज ने हर्षित होकर कोमल वाणी से कहा कि सम्पूर्ण श्रेष्ठ तीर्थों का जल ले आओ। फिर उन्होंने औषधि, मूल, फूल, फल और पत्र आदि अनेकों मांगलिक वस्तुओं के नाम गिनकर बताए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1973.english_translation: The sage spoke joyfully in a gentle voice: "Bring water from all sacred places. Gather medicines, roots, flowers, fruits, leaves, and many other auspicious items."
ramacharitamanas::1973.translation_literal: हरषि (joyfully) / मुनीस (the great sage) / कहेउ (said) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (speech) / आनहु (bring) / सकल (all) / सुतीरथ (excellent sacred places) / पानी (water) / औषध (medicines) / मूल (roots) / फूल (flowers) / फल (fruits) / पाना (leaves) / कहे (said) / नाम (names) / गनि (counting) / मंगल (auspicious) / नाना (various)
ramacharitamanas::1973.speaker: Vashistha
ramacharitamanas::1973.simple_meaning: Vashistha calmly gives practical instructions for the coronation ritual: bring sacred water and gather auspicious plants and offerings.
ramacharitamanas::1973.simple_insight: Sacred moments still need careful preparation. Reverence shows up in exact, humble work.
ramacharitamanas::1973.detailed_meaning: Ram's coronation is being arranged in Ayodhya. Vashistha, delighted, speaks gently and begins ordering the ritual materials: sacred water, herbs, roots, flowers, fruits, and leaves. The joy of the moment becomes concrete through precise preparation.
ramacharitamanas::1973.modern_relevance: Before a wedding, a memorial, or a major family ceremony, someone has to make the lists, gather the items, and keep the atmosphere steady. Reverence is often hidden inside those small exact tasks.
ramacharitamanas::1973.insight: It shifts attention from grand intention to the disciplined gathering that makes a holy event possible.

ramacharitamanas::1974.verse_sanskrit: चामर चरम बसन बहु भाँती। रोम पाट पट अगनित जाती॥ मनिगन मंगल बस्तु अनेका। जो जग जोगु भूप अभिषेका ॥
ramacharitamanas::1974.verse_hindi: चँवर, मृगचर्म, बहुत प्रकार के वस्त्र, असंख्यों जातियों के ऊनी और रेशमी कपड़े, (नाना प्रकार की) मणियाँ (रत्न) तथा और भी बहुत सी मंगल वस्तुएँ, जो जगत में राज्याभिषेक के योग्य होती हैं, (सबको मँगाने की उन्होंने आज्ञा दी) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1974.english_translation: Many kinds of fans, deer skins, many kinds of garments, countless kinds of wool and silk cloth, many jewels, and many auspicious items fit for a king's consecration in the world.
ramacharitamanas::1974.translation_literal: चामर (fans) / चरम (deer skin) / बसन (garments) / बहु भाँती (many kinds) / रोम पाट पट (wool and silk cloth) / अगनित जाती (countless kinds) / मनिगन (groups of jewels) / मंगल बस्तु (auspicious items) / अनेका (many) / जो जग जोगु (fit for the world) / भूप अभिषेका (king's consecration)
ramacharitamanas::1974.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1974.essence: Great occasions are honored through careful gathering, not haste.
ramacharitamanas::1974.simple_meaning: The preparations for Ram's coronation include many fine cloths, jewels, and auspicious items suitable for a royal consecration.
ramacharitamanas::1974.simple_insight: Some moments call for full preparation, because what is sacred deserves care in every detail.
ramacharitamanas::1974.detailed_meaning: Vashishtha is organizing Ram's coronation in Ayodhya. After asking for sacred water, herbs, flowers, fruits, and leaves, he now calls for royal fabrics, jewels, and other ceremonial items. The verse is part of the practical preparation, not the emotional climax.
ramacharitamanas::1974.modern_relevance: A wedding hall is being set before dawn: flowers, lights, fabrics, and utensils arrive in careful piles. The moment matters, so every detail is gathered with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::1974.insight: It shifts attention from grand intention to exact preparation. Sacred or important work is completed through disciplined attention to detail.

ramacharitamanas::1975.verse_sanskrit: बेद बिदित कहि सकल बिधाना। कहेउ रचहु पुर बिबिध बिताना॥ सफल रसाल पूगफल केरा। रोपहु बीथिन्ह पुर चहुँ फेरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1975.verse_hindi: मुनि ने वेदों में कहा हुआ सब विधान बताकर कहा- नगर में बहुत से मंडप (चँदोवे) सजाओ। फलों समेत आम, सुपारी और केले के वृक्ष नगर की गलियों में चारों ओर रोप दो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1975.english_translation: Having explained all the rites known in the Vedas, he said, "Set up many canopies throughout the city. Plant fruitful mango, areca, and banana trees along the streets on all four sides."
ramacharitamanas::1975.translation_literal: बेद बिदित (known in the Vedas) / कहि (having said) / सकल (all) / बिधाना (rites, arrangements) / कहेउ (he said) / रचहु (arrange, set up) / पुर (city) / बिबिध (many, various) / बिताना (canopies, awnings) / सफल (fruit-bearing) / रसाल (mango) / पूगफल (areca fruit) / केरा (banana) / रोपहु (plant) / बीथिन्ह (in the streets) / पुर (city) / चहुँ फेरा (on all four sides)
ramacharitamanas::1975.speaker: Muni
ramacharitamanas::1975.essence: A sacred event begins with careful order.
ramacharitamanas::1975.simple_meaning: The sage instructs the city to be decorated for the coming ceremony with canopies and rows of fruit trees along the streets.
ramacharitamanas::1975.simple_insight: Preparation can be sacred. Even a city becomes worthy when every detail is arranged with care.
ramacharitamanas::1975.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the sage has already gathered the materials for the royal rite. Now he gives the next instructions: cover the city with canopies and line the streets with fruit trees. The whole city is being made fit for a solemn sacred event.
ramacharitamanas::1975.modern_relevance: You are setting up chairs before dawn, hanging lights, and placing flowers where people will walk in silence. The work is ordinary, but the care makes it feel holy.
ramacharitamanas::1975.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony as spectacle to ceremony as disciplined preparation.

ramacharitamanas::1976.verse_sanskrit: रचहु मंजु मनि चौकें चारू। कहहु बनावन बेगि बजारू॥ पूजहु गनपति गुर कुलदेवा। सब बिधि करहु भूमिसुर सेवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1976.verse_hindi: सुंदर मणियों के मनोहर चौक पुरवाओ और बाजार को तुरंत सजाने के लिए कह दो। श्री गणेशजी, गुरु और कुलदेवता की पूजा करो और भूदेव ब्राह्मणों की सब प्रकार से सेवा करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::1976.english_translation: Have beautiful jewel-studded courtyards laid out and quickly prepare the market. Worship Ganesha, the teacher, and the family deities, and serve the learned brahmins in every way.
ramacharitamanas::1976.translation_literal: रचहु (arrange) / मंजु (beautiful) / मनि (jewel) / चौकें (courtyards) / चारू (lovely) / कहहु (say) / बनावन (to prepare) / बेगि (quickly) / बजारू (the market) / पूजहु (worship) / गनपति (Ganesha) / गुर (teacher) / कुलदेवा (family deities) / सब बिधि (in every way) / करहु (do) / भूमिसुर (learned brahmins) / सेवा (service)
ramacharitamanas::1976.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1976.essence: A worthy welcome begins with reverence, service, and careful preparation.
ramacharitamanas::1976.simple_meaning: The city is being prepared for a great welcome. Beautiful decorations are put up, sacred worship is performed, and respected brahmins are served with care.
ramacharitamanas::1976.simple_insight: Big moments begin with humble preparation, respect, and attention to every detail.
ramacharitamanas::1976.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, preparations for Ram's return are underway. Courtyards, shops, and decorations are being arranged, while worship and service to brahmins are ordered first. The scene shows a kingdom making itself worthy of a sacred homecoming.
ramacharitamanas::1976.modern_relevance: Before a wedding, a housewarming, or a family reunion, someone is still sweeping the floor, arranging flowers, and making sure elders are welcomed first. Great joy is built through careful, respectful preparation.
ramacharitamanas::1976.insight: It shifts attention from celebration alone to the discipline of preparing well and honoring what is sacred in the moment.

ramacharitamanas::1977.verse_sanskrit: ध्वज पताक तोरन कलस सजहु तुरग रथ नाग। सिर धरि मुनिबर बचन सबु निज निज काजहिं लाग ॥
ramacharitamanas::1977.verse_hindi: ध्वजा, पताका, तोरण, कलश, घोड़े, रथ और हाथी सबको सजाओ! मुनि श्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी के वचनों को शिरोधार्य करके सब लोग अपने-अपने काम में लग गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1977.english_translation: Decorate the banners, flags, arches, pots, horses, chariots, and elephants. Holding the sage's words on their heads, everyone set to their own tasks.
ramacharitamanas::1977.translation_literal: ध्वज (banner) / पताक (flag) / तोरन (archway) / कलस (sacred pot) / सजहु (decorate) / तुरग (horse) / रथ (chariot) / नाग (elephant) / सिर (head) / धरि (placing) / मुनिबर (best sage) / बचन (words) / सबु (all) / निज निज (each one's own) / काजहिं (tasks) / लाग (engaged)
ramacharitamanas::1977.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1977.essence: Order appears when everyone takes up their own task.
ramacharitamanas::1977.simple_meaning: The city is being prepared for a great celebration. Everyone follows Vashistha's instructions and gets to work at once.
ramacharitamanas::1977.simple_insight: Big moments begin with orderly action. Respect for guidance turns chaos into readiness.
ramacharitamanas::1977.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Vashistha is arranging the royal preparations. He orders the city decorated with banners, arches, pots, horses, chariots, and elephants. The people immediately obey, showing the discipline and unity behind the coming event.
ramacharitamanas::1977.modern_relevance: A wedding hall is half-finished, guests are arriving, and everyone suddenly knows their role. The whole scene works because people stop debating and start doing exactly what needs doing.
ramacharitamanas::1977.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to coordinated action under wise direction.

ramacharitamanas::1978.verse_sanskrit: जो मुनीस जेहि आयसु दीन्हा। सो तेहिं काजु प्रथम जनु कीन्हा॥ बिप्र साधु सुर पूजत राजा। करत राम हित मंगल काजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1978.verse_hindi: मुनीश्वर ने जिसको जिस काम के लिए आज्ञा दी, उसने वह काम (इतनी शीघ्रता से कर डाला कि) मानो पहले से ही कर रखा था। राजा ब्राह्मण, साधु और देवताओं को पूज रहे हैं और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के लिए सब मंगल कार्य कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1978.english_translation: Whatever task the sage assigned to each person, each completed it as if it had already been done first. The king honored Brahmins, saints, and radiant beings, and carried out every auspicious act for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1978.translation_literal: जो (whatever) / मुनीस (sage) / जेहि (to whom) / आयसु (order) / दीन्हा (gave) / सो (that one) / तेहिं (that) / काजु (task) / प्रथम (first) / जनु (as if) / कीन्हा (did)॥ / बिप्र (Brahmins) / साधु (saints) / सुर (radiant beings) / पूजत (honoring) / राजा (king) / करत (doing) / राम (Ram) / हित (for the good of) / मंगल (auspicious) / काजा (acts) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1978.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1978.essence: Shared devotion makes many hands move as one.
ramacharitamanas::1978.simple_meaning: Everyone obeyed the sage's instructions at once. The king was busy honoring holy people and arranging auspicious rites for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1978.simple_insight: Order becomes harmony when everyone serves the same sacred purpose.
ramacharitamanas::1978.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the preparations for Ram's coronation are underway. Vashishtha has given each person a task, and the whole city responds instantly. King Dasharath is honoring priests and saints while every action is directed toward Ram's auspicious consecration.
ramacharitamanas::1978.modern_relevance: A wedding venue before sunrise: florists, cooks, relatives, and priests all move without confusion because one clear purpose holds them together. When everyone knows what matters, effort stops scattering.
ramacharitamanas::1978.insight: It shows how shared purpose turns many separate actions into one coordinated act.

ramacharitamanas::1979.verse_sanskrit: सुनत राम अभिषेक सुहावा। बाज गहागह अवध बधावा॥ राम सीय तन सगुन जनाए। फरकहिं मंगल अंग सुहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1979.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के राज्याभिषेक की सुहावनी खबर सुनते ही अवधभर में बड़ी धूम से बधावे बजने लगे। श्री रामचन्द्रजी और सीताजी के शरीर में भी शुभ शकुन सूचित हुए। उनके सुंदर मंगल अंग फड़कने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1979.english_translation: As soon as the happy news of Ram's coronation was heard, Ayodhya rang with loud celebrations. Auspicious signs appeared in Ram and Sita's bodies, and their beautiful limbs trembled with joy.
ramacharitamanas::1979.translation_literal: सुनत (on hearing) / राम (Ram's) / अभिषेक (coronation) / सुहावा (pleasant, delightful) / बाज (were sounded) / गहागह (with great clamour) / अवध (Ayodhya) / बधावा (congratulatory rejoicing) / राम (Ram) / सीय (Sita's) / तन (bodies) / सगुन (auspicious signs) / जनाए (appeared) / फरकहिं (tremble) / मंगल (auspicious) / अंग (limbs) / सुहाए (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::1979.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1979.essence: Joy in the city and joy in the body rise together.
ramacharitamanas::1979.simple_meaning: Ayodhya erupts in celebration at the news of Ram's coronation, and Ram and Sita themselves show joyful auspicious signs.
ramacharitamanas::1979.simple_insight: Joy can spread through an entire city, then show itself in the body before words arrive.
ramacharitamanas::1979.detailed_meaning: Vashishtha's preparations have reached the point of Ram's coronation. The news sweeps through Ayodhya like a wave, drums and cheers rising everywhere. In the same moment, Ram and Sita's bodies show joyful omens, hinting that the celebration has already entered their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::1979.modern_relevance: Your phone lights up with the message you were waiting for, and before you even speak, your body changes—shoulders loosen, breath deepens, a smile comes. Some happiness arrives before language.
ramacharitamanas::1979.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the visible signs of shared joy.

ramacharitamanas::1980.verse_sanskrit: पुलकि सप्रेम परसपर कहहीं। भरत आगमनु सूचक अहहीं॥ भए बहुत दिन अति अवसेरी। सगुन प्रतीति भेंट प्रिय केरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1980.verse_hindi: पुलकित होकर वे दोनों प्रेम सहित एक-दूसरे से कहते हैं कि ये सब शकुन भरत के आने की सूचना देने वाले हैं। (उनको मामा के घर गए) बहुत दिन हो गए, बहुत ही अवसेर आ रही है (बार-बार उनसे मिलने की मन में आती है) शकुनों से प्रिय (भरत) के मिलने का विश्वास होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1980.english_translation: With joy and love, they tell one another that these omens point to Bharat's arrival. He has been away for many days, and every sign now feels like the beloved's meeting is near.
ramacharitamanas::1980.translation_literal: पुलकि (with thrill) / सप्रेम (with love) / परसपर (one another) / कहहीं (say) / भरत आगमनु (Bharat's arrival) / सूचक (indicating) / अहहीं (are) / भए (have been) / बहुत दिन (many days) / अति अवसेरी (very long delayed) / सगुन (omens) / प्रतीति (confidence) / भेंट (meeting) / प्रिय केरी (of the beloved)
ramacharitamanas::1980.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1980.essence: Love turns even omens into messages of return.
ramacharitamanas::1980.simple_meaning: The people around Ram read the omens as signs that Bharat is coming. Their hearts have waited so long that every sign now feels like hope fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::1980.simple_insight: Longing can sharpen the heart until even small signs feel like relief.
ramacharitamanas::1980.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, news and omens are moving through Ayodhya as everyone waits for Bharat. The verse shows the tenderness of that waiting: people thrill at the thought that the beloved brother may be near, and hope itself becomes visible in the signs.
ramacharitamanas::1980.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after a long silence from someone you love. A tiny message, a typing bubble, even a delayed reply starts to feel like a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::1980.insight: It trains the mind to notice hope in small signs instead of collapsing into doubt.

ramacharitamanas::1981.verse_sanskrit: भरत सरिस प्रिय को जग माहीं। इहइ सगुन फलु दूसर नाहीं॥ रामहि बंधु सोच दिन राती। अंडन्हि कमठ हृदय जेहि भाँती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1981.verse_hindi: और भरत के समान जगत में (हमें) कौन प्यारा है! शकुन का बस, यही फल है, दूसरा नहीं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी को (अपने) भाई भरत का दिन-रात ऐसा सोच रहता है जैसा कछुए का हृदय अंडों में रहता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1981.english_translation: Who in the world is dear like Bharat? This is the only fruit of the omen, nothing else. Ram thinks of his brother Bharat day and night, like a turtle guarding its eggs in its heart.
ramacharitamanas::1981.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / सरिस (like) / प्रिय (dear) / को (who) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / इहइ (this only) / सगुन (omen) / फलु (fruit/result) / दूसर (other) / नाहीं (not) / रामहि (to Ram) / बंधु (brother) / सोच (thought/worry) / दिन राती (day and night) / अंडन्हि (eggs) / कमठ (turtle) / हृदय (heart) / जेहि भाँती (in the manner that)
ramacharitamanas::1981.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1981.essence: True love keeps the absent beloved alive in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1981.simple_meaning: Bharat is described as the dearest person in the world, and Ram keeps thinking of him constantly, with deep protective concern.
ramacharitamanas::1981.simple_insight: Being loved like this feels like belonging completely — you matter enough to live in someone’s heart.
ramacharitamanas::1981.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace has just erupted with joy over Ram’s return and coronation. Amid that celebration, Tulsidas pauses to say that Bharat is the dearest being in the world and that Ram thinks of him day and night, with a protective love that never lets go.
ramacharitamanas::1981.modern_relevance: You are halfway through a crowded family wedding when one person keeps scanning the entrance, not for attention but for someone they love. That quiet loyalty is what this verse honors.
ramacharitamanas::1981.insight: It shifts attention from public celebration to the private bond that gives the celebration its heart.

ramacharitamanas::1982.verse_sanskrit: एहि अवसर मंगलु परम सुनि रहँसेउ रनिवासु। सोभत लखि बिधु बढ़त जनु बारिधि बीचि बिलासु ॥
ramacharitamanas::1982.verse_hindi: इसी समय यह परम मंगल समाचार सुनकर सारा रनिवास हर्षित हो उठा। जैसे चन्द्रमा को बढ़ते देखकर समुद्र में लहरों का विलास (आनंद) सुशोभित होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1982.english_translation: At this moment, hearing this most auspicious news, the whole inner palace rejoiced. Like waves dancing in the sea when the moon grows brighter, it became beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::1982.translation_literal: एहि अवसर (at this moment) / मंगलु (auspiciousness) / परम (highest) / सुनि (having heard) / रहँसेउ (rejoiced) / रनिवासु (the inner palace) / सोभत (shining) / लखि (seeing) / बिधु (the moon) / बढ़त (growing) / जनु (as if) / बारिधि (sea) / बीचि (waves) / बिलासु (playful delight)
ramacharitamanas::1982.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1982.essence: Hope arriving at last makes even waiting feel beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::1982.simple_meaning: The royal women hear the news and become joyful at once. Their delight is compared to sea waves brightening under the rising moon.
ramacharitamanas::1982.simple_insight: Joy spreads instantly when hope finally arrives.
ramacharitamanas::1982.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the inner palace has been waiting for Bharat's return. When the auspicious news is heard, the queens burst into joy. Tulsidas uses the image of moonlit waves to show how hope makes the whole palace come alive.
ramacharitamanas::1982.modern_relevance: You see a message from someone you've been waiting for all week, and your whole body loosens before you even open it. Relief can feel like light returning to a room.
ramacharitamanas::1982.insight: It turns waiting into visible joy and shows how hope animates an entire household.

ramacharitamanas::1983.verse_sanskrit: प्रथम जाइ जिन्ह बचन सुनाए। भूषन बसन भूरि तिन्ह पाए॥ प्रेम पुलकि तन मन अनुरागीं। मंगल कलस सजन सब लागीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1983.verse_hindi: सबसे पहले (रनिवास में) जाकर जिन्होंने ये वचन (समाचार) सुनाए, उन्होंने बहुत से आभूषण और वस्त्र पाए। रानियों का शरीर प्रेम से पुलकित हो उठा और मन प्रेम में मग्न हो गया। वे सब मंगल कलश सजाने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1983.english_translation: Those who first went and told the news received many ornaments and garments. The queens' bodies thrilled with love, and their minds were absorbed in affection. They all began arranging the auspicious pots.
ramacharitamanas::1983.translation_literal: प्रथम (first) / जाइ (going) / जिन्ह (those who) / बचन (words) / सुनाए (told) / भूषन (ornaments) / बसन (garments) / भूरि (many) / तिन्ह (they) / पाए (received) / प्रेम (love) / पुलकि (thrilled) / तन (body) / मन (mind) / अनुरागीं (loving, devoted) / मंगल (auspicious) / कलस (pots) / सजन (arranging) / सब (all) / लागीं (began)
ramacharitamanas::1983.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1983.essence: Good news turns sorrow into celebration before anything else changes.
ramacharitamanas::1983.simple_meaning: The messengers who brought the good news were rewarded. The queens overflowed with joy and began preparing for celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1983.simple_insight: Joy spreads fast when hope returns. Even a house in grief can suddenly become alive again.
ramacharitamanas::1983.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace has just heard that Bharat is returning. The first messengers who carried the news are rewarded, and the queens burst into delighted activity, dressing the house for welcome before the deeper grief and reunion fully unfold.
ramacharitamanas::1983.modern_relevance: A text message finally arrives after hours of silence, and the whole room changes. Relief turns into motion: calls, plans, food, clothes, everything suddenly has purpose again.
ramacharitamanas::1983.insight: It shows how hope instantly reorganizes behavior, turning waiting into preparation.

ramacharitamanas::1984.verse_sanskrit: चौकें चारु सुमित्राँ पूरी। मनिमय बिबिध भाँति अति रूरी॥ आनँद मगन राम महतारी। दिए दान बहु बिप्र हँकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1984.verse_hindi: सुमित्राजी ने मणियों (रत्नों) के बहुत प्रकार के अत्यन्त सुंदर और मनोहर चौक पूरे। आनंद में मग्न हुई श्री रामचन्द्रजी की माता कौसल्याजी ने ब्राह्मणों को बुलाकर बहुत दान दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1984.english_translation: Sumitra filled the courtyards with many kinds of beautiful jeweled designs. In joy, Ram's mother Kaushalya, absorbed in bliss, called the Brahmins and gave many gifts.
ramacharitamanas::1984.translation_literal: चौकें (courtyards / decorated spaces) / चारु (beautiful) / सुमित्राँ (by Sumitra) / पूरी (filled) / मनिमय (made of jewels) / बिबिध (various) / भाँति (kinds) / अति (very) / रूरी (lovely) ॥ / आनँद (joy) / मगन (immersed) / राम (Ram's) / महतारी (mother) / दिए (gave) / दान (gifts) / बहु (many) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / हँकारी (calling out)
ramacharitamanas::1984.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1984.essence: Joy does not stay still; it becomes giving.
ramacharitamanas::1984.simple_meaning: The palace is being decorated for a joyful celebration, and Kaushalya gives gifts to Brahmins in her happiness.
ramacharitamanas::1984.simple_insight: Joy naturally turns outward. When the heart is full, it wants to decorate, give, and bless others.
ramacharitamanas::1984.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace is alive with news of Ram's return. Sumitra decorates the courtyards with jeweled patterns, and Kaushalya, overflowing with joy, calls the Brahmins and gives gifts. The verse shows celebration spilling into ritual generosity.
ramacharitamanas::1984.modern_relevance: You get the message that someone you love is safe, and suddenly you start tidying the house, buying sweets, calling relatives. Happiness wants to become action, not stay private.
ramacharitamanas::1984.insight: It shifts emotion into offering: delight becomes visible through generosity and care.

ramacharitamanas::1985.verse_sanskrit: पूजीं ग्रामदेबि सुर नागा। कहेउ बहोरि देन बलिभागा॥ जेहि बिधि होइ राम कल्यानू। देहु दया करि सो बरदानू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1985.verse_hindi: उन्होंने ग्रामदेवियों, देवताओं और नागों की पूजा की और फिर बलि भेंट देने को कहा (अर्थात कार्य सिद्ध होने पर फिर पूजा करने की मनौती मानी) और प्रार्थना की कि जिस प्रकार से श्री रामचन्द्रजी का कल्याण हो, दया करके वही वरदान दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1985.english_translation: They worshipped the village deities, the radiant beings, and the serpents, and promised offerings of thanks. Then they prayed, “Grant that whatever brings Ram’s welfare may be given with compassion.”
ramacharitamanas::1985.translation_literal: पूजीं (they worshipped) / ग्रामदेबि (village deities) / सुर (radiant beings) / नागा (serpents) / कहेउ (said) / बहोरि (again) / देन (to give) / बलिभागा (offering share) / जेहि बिधि (in whatever way) / होइ (happens) / राम (Ram) / कल्यानू (well-being) / देहु (give) / दया करि (with compassion) / सो (that) / बरदानू (boon)
ramacharitamanas::1985.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1985.essence: True devotion asks only for what helps Ram.
ramacharitamanas::1985.simple_meaning: The people made offerings and prayed only for Ram’s well-being.
ramacharitamanas::1985.simple_insight: Devotion becomes simple when every prayer bends toward one beloved aim.
ramacharitamanas::1985.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the household is preparing with joy for Ram’s return and blessing. The people honor local powers, promise offerings, and ask only for the kind of boon that will protect Ram and bring him welfare.
ramacharitamanas::1985.modern_relevance: Before a long-awaited family reunion, someone quietly says, “Let whatever helps her be the thing that happens.” That is a heart no longer bargaining for itself.
ramacharitamanas::1985.insight: It shifts prayer from asking for personal gain to asking for what serves Ram’s welfare.

ramacharitamanas::1986.verse_hindi: कोयल की सी मीठी वाणी वाली, चन्द्रमा के समान मुख वाली और हिरन के बच्चे के से नेत्रों वाली स्त्रियाँ मंगलगान करने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1986.english_translation: Women with honey-sweet voices, moonlike faces, and deer-like eyes began singing auspicious songs.
ramacharitamanas::1986.translation_literal: गावहिं (are singing) / मंगल (auspicious songs) / कोकिलबयनीं (with cuckoo-like voices) / बिधुबदनीं (moon-faced) / मृगसावकनयनीं (with deer-calf eyes)
ramacharitamanas::1986.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1986.essence: Auspicious news makes the whole city sing.
ramacharitamanas::1986.simple_meaning: Women sing auspicious songs, and the verse describes their sweet voices, lovely faces, and gentle eyes.
ramacharitamanas::1986.simple_insight: Joy often arrives first as song before it becomes a public celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1986.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the news of Ram's coronation is spreading. Women begin singing mangal songs, and the poet lingers on their beauty and grace as the whole city fills with festive anticipation.
ramacharitamanas::1986.modern_relevance: A neighborhood hears good news before dawn, and windows open one by one. Someone starts humming, someone else smiles, and the whole street feels lighter.
ramacharitamanas::1986.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the shared joy it awakens in a community.

ramacharitamanas::1987.verse_sanskrit: राम राज अभिषेकु सुनि हियँ हरषे नर नारि। लगे सुमंगल सजन सब बिधि अनुकूल बिचारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::1987.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का राज्याभिषेक सुनकर सभी स्त्री-पुरुष हृदय में हर्षित हो उठे और विधाता को अपने अनुकूल समझकर सब सुंदर मंगल साज सजाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1987.english_translation: Hearing of Ram's coronation, men and women rejoiced in their hearts. Seeing every sign as favorable, everyone began arranging auspicious celebrations.
ramacharitamanas::1987.translation_literal: राम राज अभिषेकु (Ram's coronation) / सुनि (hearing) / हियँ (in the heart) / हरषे (rejoiced) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / लगे (began) / सुमंगल (auspicious) / सजन (arrangements) / सब (all) / बिधि (fate / the divine order) / अनुकूल (favorable) / बिचारि (considering)
ramacharitamanas::1987.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1987.essence: Joy makes an entire city move as one.
ramacharitamanas::1987.simple_meaning: Everyone in Ayodhya feels joy at Ram's coronation and starts preparing for the celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1987.simple_insight: Shared joy can turn an entire city into one moving heart.
ramacharitamanas::1987.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya has just heard that Ram will be crowned. Men and women alike are overjoyed, and the whole city begins preparing auspicious decorations and ceremonies. This is the people’s first wave of happiness before the deeper drama unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::1987.modern_relevance: A family group chat lights up when good news finally arrives after weeks of worry. Suddenly everyone is calling, planning, and making room for celebration before the moment even comes.
ramacharitamanas::1987.insight: It shifts attention from private feeling to collective preparation for a blessing.

ramacharitamanas::1988.verse_sanskrit: तब नरनाहँ बसिष्ठु बोलाए। रामधाम सिख देन पठाए॥ गुर आगमनु सुनत रघुनाथा। द्वार आइ पद नायउ माथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1988.verse_hindi: तब राजा ने वशिष्ठजी को बुलाया और शिक्षा (समयोचित उपदेश) देने के लिए श्री रामचन्द्रजी के महल में भेजा। गुरु का आगमन सुनते ही श्री रघुनाथजी ने दरवाजे पर आकर उनके चरणों में मस्तक नवाया।1॥
ramacharitamanas::1988.english_translation: Then the king summoned Vashishtha and sent him to give instruction at Ram's abode. Hearing of the guru's arrival, Raghunath came to the door and bowed his head at his feet.
ramacharitamanas::1988.translation_literal: तब (then) / नरनाहँ (the king) / बसिष्ठु (Vashishtha) / बोलाए (called) / रामधाम (Ram's abode) / सिख (instruction) / देन (to give) / पठाए (sent) ॥ / गुर (guru) / आगमनु (arrival) / सुनत (hearing) / रघुनाथा (Raghunath) / द्वार (door) / आइ (coming) / पद (feet) / नायउ (bowed) / माथा (head) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1988.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1988.simple_meaning: The king sends Vashishtha to instruct Ram, and Ram immediately greets his teacher with a bow.
ramacharitamanas::1988.simple_insight: Even the highest honor begins with humility before the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::1988.detailed_meaning: At Ayodhya, the king arranges Ram's instruction and sends Vashishtha to Ram's home. The moment Ram hears his teacher is coming, he steps out to the door and bows his head, showing the reverence that shapes the whole scene.
ramacharitamanas::1988.modern_relevance: Your mentor arrives for a difficult conversation, and you do not wait to be called. You meet them at the door, attentive before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::1988.insight: It shifts respect from a formal duty into an immediate, embodied response.

ramacharitamanas::1989.verse_sanskrit: सादर अरघ देइ घर आने। सोरह भाँति पूजि सनमाने॥ गहे चरन सिय सहित बहोरी। बोले रामु कमल कर जोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::1989.verse_hindi: आदरपूर्वक अर्घ्य देकर उन्हें घर में लाए और षोडशोपचार से पूजा करके उनका सम्मान किया। फिर सीताजी सहित उनके चरण स्पर्श किए और कमल के समान दोनों हाथों को जोड़कर श्री रामजी बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1989.english_translation: With reverence, he offered water and brought him home. He honored him with sixteenfold worship. Then, along with Sita, he bowed at his feet again. Rama, with lotus-like hands joined, spoke.
ramacharitamanas::1989.translation_literal: सादर (with reverence) / अरघ (offering of water) / देइ (giving) / घर (home) / आने (brought) / सोरह (sixteen) / भाँति (ways) / पूजि (worshipping) / सनमाने (honored) / गहे (held) / चरन (feet) / सिय (Sita) / सहित (together with) / बहोरी (again) / बोले (spoke) / रामु (Rama) / कमल (lotus) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined)
ramacharitamanas::1989.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1989.essence: Honor becomes highest when the honored one bows first.
ramacharitamanas::1989.simple_meaning: The host welcomes the guest with water, worship, and honor. Then Rama and Sita bow at the guest's feet before speaking.
ramacharitamanas::1989.simple_insight: True greatness makes room for humility. Honor deepens when the highest person bows first.
ramacharitamanas::1989.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Vashishtha has arrived to guide the ceremony for Rama's coronation. Dasharath receives the teacher with full ceremony, and Rama himself bows with Sita beside him. The scene shows royal respect before the crisis of exile begins.
ramacharitamanas::1989.modern_relevance: A respected elder walks into your home, and you stop everything to greet them properly. Before any request or conversation, respect comes first. That simple act can change the whole tone of a room.
ramacharitamanas::1989.insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing that dignity grows through humility.

ramacharitamanas::1990.verse_sanskrit: सेवक सदन स्वामि आगमनू। मंगल मूल अमंगल दमनू॥ तदपि उचित जनु बोलि सप्रीती। पठइअ काज नाथ असि नीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::1990.verse_hindi: यद्यपि सेवक के घर स्वामी का पधारना मंगलों का मूल और अमंगलों का नाश करने वाला होता है, तथापि हे नाथ! उचित तो यही था कि प्रेमपूर्वक दास को ही कार्य के लिए बुला भेजते, ऐसी ही नीति है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1990.english_translation: Although a master’s arrival at a servant’s home is the root of all auspiciousness and the destroyer of all misfortune, still, my lord, proper conduct is to call the servant for the task with affection.
ramacharitamanas::1990.translation_literal: सेवक (servant) / सदन (home) / स्वामि (master) / आगमनू (arrival) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मूल (root) / अमंगल (inauspiciousness) / दमनू (destroyer) / तदपि (still) / उचित (proper) / जनु (indeed) / बोलि (calling) / सप्रीती (with affection) / पठइअ (should be sent) / काज (task) / नाथ (lord) / असि (such) / नीती (conduct)
ramacharitamanas::1990.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::1990.essence: Honor is deepest when power speaks with humility.
ramacharitamanas::1990.simple_meaning: A master coming to a servant’s home is an auspicious honor, but respect also means calling the servant kindly when there is work to do.
ramacharitamanas::1990.simple_insight: True respect does not erase service; it makes service gentle and mutual.
ramacharitamanas::1990.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Vashishtha has come to Ram’s home with counsel. Ram receives him with full honor, then speaks with humility: a master’s visit blesses the house, yet proper conduct would have been to summon the servant instead. The moment reveals Ram’s tenderness beneath his royal dignity.
ramacharitamanas::1990.modern_relevance: A respected mentor shows up at your door for a project discussion, and you feel both honored and slightly overwhelmed. You still remember: real courtesy does not depend on rank; it shows in how gently you ask for help.
ramacharitamanas::1990.insight: It shifts the mind from status to relationship, showing that dignity and service can coexist.

ramacharitamanas::1991.verse_sanskrit: प्रभुता तजि प्रभु कीन्ह सनेहू। भयउ पुनीत आजु यहु गेहू॥ आयसु होइ सो करौं गोसाईं। सेवकु लइह स्वामि सेवकाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1991.verse_hindi: परन्तु प्रभु (आप) ने प्रभुता छोड़कर (स्वयं यहाँ पधारकर) जो स्नेह किया, इससे आज यह घर पवित्र हो गया! हे गोसाईं! (अब) जो आज्ञा हो, मैं वही करूँ। स्वामी की सेवा में ही सेवक का लाभ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::1991.english_translation: But You set aside majesty and showed affection; today this home has become pure. O Lord, whatever command You give, I will do. A servant finds gain only in serving the master.
ramacharitamanas::1991.translation_literal: प्रभुता (majesty) / तजि (leaving aside) / प्रभु (the Lord) / कीन्ह (did) / सनेहू (affection) / भयउ (became) / पुनीत (pure) / आजु (today) / यहु (this) / गेहू (home) / आयसु (command) / होइ (becomes) / सो (that) / करौं (I do) / गोसाईं (O Lord) / सेवकु (servant) / लइह (finds) / स्वामि (master) / सेवकाईं (service)
ramacharitamanas::1991.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1991.essence: Majesty becomes sacred when it bends into affection.
ramacharitamanas::1991.simple_meaning: Ram has set aside royal distance and shown affection, and that alone makes the house sacred. The servant now waits only for his command, because serving the master is the servant’s true gain.
ramacharitamanas::1991.simple_insight: Real greatness feels like warmth, not distance. When respect becomes love, service becomes joy.
ramacharitamanas::1991.detailed_meaning: In Vishwamitra’s hermitage, Ram has arrived as a guest but behaves like a beloved family member. The host is overwhelmed: the prince’s humility makes the whole home feel purified, and he answers with complete readiness to serve.
ramacharitamanas::1991.modern_relevance: A senior leader sits beside the new intern, asks about their family, and listens without performing power. The room changes. People serve more willingly when authority becomes care.
ramacharitamanas::1991.insight: It shifts reverence from formality to loving service, showing that true status deepens humility.

ramacharitamanas::1992.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सनेह साने बचन मुनि रघुबरहि प्रसंस। राम कस न तुम्ह कहहु अस हंस बंस अवतंस ॥
ramacharitamanas::1992.verse_hindi: (श्री रामचन्द्रजी के) प्रेम में सने हुए वचनों को सुनकर मुनि वशिष्ठजी ने श्री रघुनाथजी की प्रशंसा करते हुए कहा कि हे राम! भला आप ऐसा क्यों न कहें। आप सूर्यवंश के भूषण जो हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1992.english_translation: Hearing those affectionate words, the sage praised Raghubar: “Why would you not speak like this, O ornament of the solar line?”
ramacharitamanas::1992.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सनेह साने (soaked in affection) / बचन (words) / मुनि (sage) / रघुबरहि (to Raghubar) / प्रसंस (praising) / राम (Ram) / कस (why) / न (not) / तुम्ह (you) / कहहु (speak) / अस (thus) / हंस बंस (solar line) / अवतंस (ornament)
ramacharitamanas::1992.speaker: Vashistha
ramacharitamanas::1992.essence: Graceful speech reveals the highest lineage.
ramacharitamanas::1992.simple_meaning: Vashistha hears Ram's tender words and praises him warmly, calling him the ornament of the solar lineage.
ramacharitamanas::1992.simple_insight: True nobility shows itself in gentle speech, not in rank.
ramacharitamanas::1992.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Vashistha hears Ram answer with affection instead of pride. Moved by that humility, he praises Ram as the jewel of the solar line. The verse is a bridge between the king's offer and Ram's gracious response.
ramacharitamanas::1992.modern_relevance: Someone apologizes to you with real softness, not defensiveness. You feel the difference immediately — dignity can sound like warmth, not authority.
ramacharitamanas::1992.insight: It shifts attention from status to the quality of speech and character.

ramacharitamanas::1993.verse_sanskrit: बरनि राम गुन सीलु सुभाऊ। बोले प्रेम पुलकि मुनिराऊ॥ भूप सजेउ अभिषेक समाजू। चाहत देन तुम्हहि जुबराजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::1993.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुण, शील और स्वभाव का बखान कर, मुनिराज प्रेम से पुलकित होकर बोले- (हे रामचन्द्रजी!) राजा (दशरथजी) ने राज्याभिषेक की तैयारी की है। वे आपको युवराज पद देना चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1993.english_translation: After praising Ram's virtues, character, and nature, the sage, trembling with love, said: "The king has prepared the coronation. He wants to make you crown prince."
ramacharitamanas::1993.translation_literal: बरनि (praising) / राम (Ram) / गुन (virtues) / सीलु (character) / सुभाऊ (nature) / बोले (spoke) / प्रेम (with love) / पुलकि (thrilled) / मुनिराऊ (the sage-king) ॥ / भूप (king) / सजेउ (has prepared) / अभिषेक (coronation) / समाजू (arrangement) / चाहत (wants) / देन (to give) / तुम्हहि (to you) / जुबराजू (crown prince) ॥
ramacharitamanas::1993.speaker: Vashistha
ramacharitamanas::1993.essence: Honor arrives as duty, not just celebration.
ramacharitamanas::1993.simple_meaning: Vashistha praises Ram's virtues and tells him that King Dasharath has arranged the coronation and wants to make him crown prince.
ramacharitamanas::1993.simple_insight: A life can change in one sentence, even before the celebration begins.
ramacharitamanas::1993.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Vashistha speaks to Ram after praising his character. He announces that Dasharath has prepared the coronation and intends to place the crown prince's duty on Ram. The joy is real, but the coming turn of events will test that honor.
ramacharitamanas::1993.modern_relevance: A parent finally says, “We’re proud of you,” and then adds a responsibility that changes everything. The praise is warm, but the real weight is the role being handed over.
ramacharitamanas::1993.insight: It frames recognition as a transfer of responsibility, not just a reward.

ramacharitamanas::1994.verse_sanskrit: राम करहु सब संजम आजू। जौं बिधि कुसल निबाहै काजू॥ गुरु सिख देइ राय पहिं गयऊ। राम हृदयँ अस बिसमउ भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::1994.verse_hindi: (इसलिए) हे रामजी! आज आप (उपवास, हवन आदि विधिपूर्वक) सब संयम कीजिए, जिससे विधाता कुशलपूर्वक इस काम को निबाह दें (सफल कर दें)। गुरुजी शिक्षा देकर राजा दशरथजी के पास चले गए। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के हृदय में (यह सुनकर) इस बात का खेद हुआ कि- ॥
ramacharitamanas::1994.english_translation: O Ram, now observe all restraints, so that fate may bring this task to success. The teacher gave his instruction and went to the king. Hearing this, sorrow arose in Ram's heart.
ramacharitamanas::1994.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / करहु (do) / सब (all) / संजम (restraint) / आजू (today) / जौं (if) / बिधि (fate) / कुसल (well) / निबाहै (carries through) / काजू (task) // गुरु (teacher) / सिख (instruction) / देइ (having given) / राय (king) / पहिं (to) / गयऊ (went) / राम (Ram) / हृदयँ (in heart) / अस (thus) / बिसमउ (sorrow) / भयऊ (became)
ramacharitamanas::1994.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1994.essence: A joyful ceremony can carry a hidden break in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::1994.simple_meaning: The teacher asks Ram to observe the needed rites so the wedding can proceed well. After the teacher leaves, Ram feels troubled in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::1994.simple_insight: Even a joyful turning point can carry a hidden ache when the outcome is not fully in your hands.
ramacharitamanas::1994.detailed_meaning: Vashishtha has just praised Ram and begun preparations for the coronation. He tells Ram to complete the required rites and then goes to Dasharath. The celebration is still being arranged, but Ram senses something unsettling beneath the surface.
ramacharitamanas::1994.modern_relevance: You hear the polite instructions before a major family event, but something in the room feels off. Everyone keeps moving forward, while you sense the shift before anyone names it.
ramacharitamanas::1994.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to the emotional weight behind it, showing how intuition notices what words have not yet said.

ramacharitamanas::1995.verse_sanskrit: जनमे एक संग सब भाई। भोजन सयन केलि लरिकाई॥ करनबेध उपबीत बिआहा। संग संग सब भए उछाहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1995.verse_hindi: हम सब भाई एक ही साथ जन्मे, खाना, सोना, लड़कपन के खेल-कूद, कनछेदन, यज्ञोपवीत और विवाह आदि उत्सव सब साथ-साथ ही हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::1995.english_translation: We four brothers were born together. We ate, slept, played, and grew up together. We shared the sacred thread ceremony, weddings, and every joy together.
ramacharitamanas::1995.translation_literal: जनमे (were born) / एक संग (together as one) / सब भाई (all brothers) / भोजन (eating) / सयन (sleeping) / केलि (play) / लरिकाई (childhood) / करनबेध (ear-piercing ceremony) / उपबीत (sacred thread) / बिआहा (marriage) / संग संग (together together) / सब भए (all became) / उछाहा (joys, celebrations)
ramacharitamanas::1995.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::1995.essence: A shared life makes separation unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::1995.simple_meaning: The brothers grew up sharing every stage of life together, from childhood games to major family ceremonies.
ramacharitamanas::1995.simple_insight: Shared joy makes separation feel sharper.
ramacharitamanas::1995.detailed_meaning: Bharat is speaking in Ayodhyakand, remembering how he, Ram, Lakshman, and Shatrughna moved through life as one family. He lists every shared milestone to show why Ram’s exile and the coming coronation feel so painfully wrong.
ramacharitamanas::1995.modern_relevance: You and your siblings once shared one table, one roof, one childhood. Then life split you into separate paths, and every family decision started to ache differently.
ramacharitamanas::1995.insight: It turns the reader toward the emotional cost of breaking a bond that was once complete.

ramacharitamanas::1996.verse_sanskrit: बिमल बंस यहु अनुचित एकू। बंधु बिहाइ बड़ेहि अभिषेकू॥ प्रभु सप्रेम पछितानि सुहाई। हरउ भगत मन कै कुटिलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::1996.verse_hindi: पर इस निर्मल वंश में यही एक अनुचित बात हो रही है कि और सब भाइयों को छोड़कर राज्याभिषेक एक बड़े का ही (मेरा ही) होता है। (तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि) प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी का यह सुंदर प्रेमपूर्ण पछतावा भक्तों के मन की कुटिलता को हरण करे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1996.english_translation: In this pure lineage, one thing feels wrong: the elder alone receives the coronation. May Lord Ram's loving regret remove the crookedness from devotees' minds.
ramacharitamanas::1996.translation_literal: बिमल (pure) / बंस (lineage) / यहु (this) / अनुचित (improper) / एकू (one) / बंधु (brothers) / बिहाइ (leaving aside) / बड़ेहि (to the elder) / अभिषेकू (coronation) / प्रभु (Lord) / सप्रेम (with love) / पछितानि (regret) / सुहाई (beautiful) / हरउ (may remove) / भगत (devotees) / मन (minds) / कै (of) / कुटिलाई (crookedness)
ramacharitamanas::1996.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::1996.essence: Love makes even victory feel incomplete when others are left behind.
ramacharitamanas::1996.simple_meaning: Ram feels it is not right that only the eldest brother should receive the coronation while the others are left out. His loving regret shows a heart free of pride.
ramacharitamanas::1996.simple_insight: Real nobility feels the pain of unfairness, even when the advantage is its own.
ramacharitamanas::1996.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the royal family is moving toward Ram's coronation. But Ram, seeing the other brothers' love and shared life, feels a gentle regret that the honor falls only to one. Tulsidas turns that moment into a prayer for the reader's heart.
ramacharitamanas::1996.modern_relevance: You get the promotion everyone expected, but your teammate did the same work and gets nothing. That quiet discomfort in your chest is what this verse honors.
ramacharitamanas::1996.insight: It teaches you to notice when success for one person feels like a wound to shared belonging.

ramacharitamanas::1997.verse_sanskrit: तेहि अवसर आए लखन मगन प्रेम आनंद। सनमाने प्रिय बचन कहि रघुकुल कैरव चंद ॥
ramacharitamanas::1997.verse_hindi: उसी समय प्रेम और आनंद में मग्न लक्ष्मणजी आए। रघुकुल रूपी कुमुद के खिलाने वाले चन्द्रमा श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने प्रिय वचन कहकर उनका सम्मान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::1997.english_translation: At that moment Lakshman arrived, absorbed in love and joy. Ram, the moon of the Raghu clan, honored him with affectionate words.
ramacharitamanas::1997.translation_literal: तेहि अवसर (at that moment) / आए (arrived) / लखन (Lakshman) / मगन (absorbed) / प्रेम (love) / आनंद (joy) / सनमाने (honored) / प्रिय बचन (affectionate words) / कहि (speaking) / रघुकुल कैरव चंद (moon of the Raghu clan, lotus-blooming moon)
ramacharitamanas::1997.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1997.essence: Love becomes visible in the way one greets another.
ramacharitamanas::1997.simple_meaning: Lakshman arrives full of love and joy, and Ram greets him warmly with kind words.
ramacharitamanas::1997.simple_insight: Love is shown through respect. True closeness still remembers honor.
ramacharitamanas::1997.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the family gathers around the coming coronation and the strain beneath it. Lakshman arrives joyful and absorbed in devotion, and Ram receives him with loving, dignified words. The verse adds tenderness to the larger drama.
ramacharitamanas::1997.modern_relevance: Your sibling walks in after a long day, and you can tell they are carrying more than they say. A warm welcome, a few careful words, can soften an entire room.
ramacharitamanas::1997.insight: It shifts attention from status to tenderness in relationships.

ramacharitamanas::1998.verse_sanskrit: बाजहिं बाजने बिबिध बिधाना। पुर प्रमोदु नहिं जाइ बखाना॥ भरत आगमनु सकल मनावहिं। आवहुँ बेगि नयन फलु पावहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::1998.verse_hindi: बहुत प्रकार के बाजे बज रहे हैं। नगर के अतिशय आनंद का वर्णन नहीं हो सकता। सब लोग भरतजी का आगमन मना रहे हैं और कह रहे हैं कि वे भी शीघ्र आवें और (राज्याभिषेक का उत्सव देखकर) नेत्रों का फल प्राप्त करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::1998.english_translation: Many kinds of musical instruments were playing. The city's joy cannot be described. Everyone was celebrating Bharata's arrival, saying, 'Come quickly and let our eyes be fulfilled.'
ramacharitamanas::1998.translation_literal: बाजहिं (are sounding) / बाजने (instruments) / बिबिध (various) / बिधाना (kinds) / पुर (city) / प्रमोदु (joy) / नहिं (not) / जाइ (can be told) / बखाना (description) / भरत (Bharata) / आगमनु (arrival) / सकल (all) / मनावहिं (are celebrating) / आवहुँ (come) / बेगि (quickly) / नयन (eyes) / फलु (fruit/fulfillment) / पावहिं (may obtain)
ramacharitamanas::1998.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1998.essence: Joy swells when a beloved presence is near.
ramacharitamanas::1998.simple_meaning: The city is overflowing with joy and music as everyone celebrates Bharata's arrival and longs to see him soon.
ramacharitamanas::1998.simple_insight: Shared joy can fill a whole city when love is waiting at the gate.
ramacharitamanas::1998.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is alive with music and excitement as the people celebrate Bharata's return. They are not just welcoming a prince; they are longing to see him with their own eyes, before the coronation scene unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::1998.modern_relevance: A train platform packed with families, flowers, and phones held high feels this same pulse: people are not just waiting for someone to arrive, they are waiting to finally see a beloved face.
ramacharitamanas::1998.insight: It turns public celebration into a sign of collective longing, not just festivity.

ramacharitamanas::1999.verse_sanskrit: हाट बाट घर गलीं अथाईं। कहहिं परसपर लोग लोगाईं॥ कालि लगन भलि केतिक बारा। पूजिहि बिधि अभिलाषु हमारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::1999.verse_hindi: बाजार, रास्ते, घर, गली और चबूतरों पर (जहाँ-तहाँ) पुरुष और स्त्री आपस में यही कहते हैं कि कल वह शुभ लग्न (मुहूर्त) कितने समय है, जब विधाता हमारी अभिलाषा पूरी करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::1999.english_translation: In markets, roads, homes, and lanes, men and women keep asking each other, “How long until tomorrow’s auspicious moment, when the creator fulfills our wish?”
ramacharitamanas::1999.translation_literal: हाट (market) / बाट (road) / घर (home) / गलीं (lanes) / अथाईं (everywhere) / कहहिं (say) / परसपर (to one another) / लोग लोगाईं (men and women) / कालि (tomorrow) / लगन (auspicious moment) / भलि (good) / केतिक (how much) / बारा (time) / पूजिहि (will fulfill) / बिधि (the creator) / अभिलाषु (wish) / हमारा (our)
ramacharitamanas::1999.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::1999.essence: Hope turns the whole city into a single waiting heart.
ramacharitamanas::1999.simple_meaning: Everyone in Ayodhya is restless with hope. They keep asking when the auspicious moment will arrive and their wish will be fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::1999.simple_insight: Anticipation can fill an entire city. Hope spreads faster than noise.
ramacharitamanas::1999.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is alive with excitement for Bharat’s arrival. In markets, streets, homes, and lanes, people keep repeating the same question: when will the blessed hour come? The whole city is waiting for a joy it believes is near.
ramacharitamanas::1999.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing the tracking page for a package that matters more than it should. The whole day is shaped by one hoped-for arrival.
ramacharitamanas::1999.insight: It captures collective expectancy, turning waiting into a shared atmosphere rather than a private feeling.

ramacharitamanas::2000.verse_sanskrit: कनक सिंघासन सीय समेता। बैठहिं रामु होइ चित चेता॥ सकल कहहिं कब होइहि काली। बिघन मनावहिं देव कुचाली ॥
ramacharitamanas::2000.verse_hindi: जब सीताजी सहित श्री रामचन्द्रजी सुवर्ण के सिंहासन पर विराजेंगे और हमारा मनचीता होगा (मनःकामना पूरी होगी)। इधर तो सब यह कह रहे हैं कि कल कब होगा, उधर कुचक्री देवता विघ्न मना रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2000.english_translation: When Ram sits on the golden throne with Sita beside him, every wish will be fulfilled. People keep asking when tomorrow will come, while scheming radiant beings plot obstacles.
ramacharitamanas::2000.translation_literal: कनक (golden) / सिंघासन (throne) / सीय समेता (together with Sita) / बैठहिं (will sit) / रामु (Ram) / होइ (becomes) / चित (mind) / चेता (desired, intended) ॥ सकल (all) / कहहिं (say) / कब (when) / होइहि (will happen) / काली (tomorrow) / बिघन (obstacles) / मनावहिं (are plotting) / देव (radiant beings) / कुचाली (crooked, scheming)
ramacharitamanas::2000.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2000.essence: Ram's coronation is so certain that even delay feels temporary.
ramacharitamanas::2000.simple_meaning: The people long for Ram and Sita to sit on the throne, but unseen forces try to block that hope.
ramacharitamanas::2000.simple_insight: Hope can be communal, and resistance can be invisible.
ramacharitamanas::2000.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ayodhya is alive with expectation for Bharat's return and Ram's rightful restoration. The city imagines the moment Ram and Sita will sit on the golden throne, while even the higher beings are said to be arranging obstacles. The scene builds the tension before the coronation is delayed.
ramacharitamanas::2000.modern_relevance: You finally see the plan coming together: the room booked, the family informed, the promotion almost announced. Then one strange delay appears from nowhere, and everyone feels the same ache — why can't the good thing simply arrive?
ramacharitamanas::2000.insight: It trains the mind to hold joy and resistance together without losing sight of the larger unfolding.

ramacharitamanas::2001.verse_sanskrit: तिन्हहि सोहाइ न अवध बधावा। चोरहि चंदिनि राति न भावा॥ सारद बोलि बिनय सुर करहीं। बारहिं बार पाय लै परहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2001.verse_hindi: उन्हें (देवताओं को) अवध के बधावे नहीं सुहाते, जैसे चोर को चाँदनी रात नहीं भाती। सरस्वतीजी को बुलाकर देवता विनय कर रहे हैं और बार-बार उनके पैरों को पकड़कर उन पर गिरते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2001.english_translation: The gods do not delight in Ayodhya's celebration, just as a thief dislikes moonlit night. They summon Saraswati and bow again and again, pleading.
ramacharitamanas::2001.translation_literal: तिन्हहि (to them) / सोहाइ (is pleasing) / न (not) / अवध (Ayodhya) / बधावा (rejoicing, celebration) / चोरहि (to a thief) / चंदिनि राति (moonlit night) / न (not) / भावा (is liked) / सारद (Saraswati) / बोलि (calling) / बिनय (humble request) / सुर (the gods) / करहीं (do) / बारहिं बार (again and again) / पाय (feet) / लै (taking) / परहीं (fall)
ramacharitamanas::2001.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2001.essence: Joy can turn bitter when hidden forces are already moving.
ramacharitamanas::2001.simple_meaning: The gods feel no joy at Ayodhya's celebration because they know it will lead to Ram's exile. They keep pleading to Saraswati and bowing again and again.
ramacharitamanas::2001.simple_insight: Even a joyful moment can hide a coming loss. Not every celebration is innocent.
ramacharitamanas::2001.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is preparing for Ram's coronation, but the gods see the hidden turn of fate. They are uneasy, because the celebration will soon be undone. In desperation, they beg Saraswati to bend events toward exile.
ramacharitamanas::2001.modern_relevance: Everyone in the room is cheering a promotion, a wedding, a move to a bigger house — but one person sees the bill coming due. This verse knows that some gains carry a shadow.
ramacharitamanas::2001.insight: It shifts attention from surface celebration to the forces shaping what happens next.

ramacharitamanas::2002.verse_sanskrit: बिपति हमारि बिलोकि बड़ि मातु करिअ सोइ आजु। रामु जाहिं बन राजु तजि होइ सकल सुरकाजु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2002.verse_hindi: (वे कहते हैं-) हे माता! हमारी बड़ी विपत्ति को देखकर आज वही कीजिए जिससे श्री रामचन्द्रजी राज्य त्यागकर वन को चले जाएँ और देवताओं का सब कार्य सिद्ध हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2002.english_translation: Seeing our great distress, Mother, do the one thing today that will make Ram leave the kingdom and go to the forest, and all the radiant beings' work will be fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::2002.translation_literal: बिपति (distress) / हमारि (our) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बड़ि (great) / मातु (Mother) / करिअ (do) / सोइ (that very thing) / आजु (today) / रामु (Ram) / जाहिं (go) / बन (forest) / राजु (kingdom) / तजि (leaving) / होइ (becomes) / सकल (all) / सुरकाजु (work of the radiant beings)
ramacharitamanas::2002.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2002.essence: One hidden nudge can overturn a kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::2002.simple_meaning: The radiant beings ask Mother Saraswati to cause Ram to leave the kingdom and go into exile, because that will fulfill their purpose.
ramacharitamanas::2002.simple_insight: A hidden turn can redirect an entire life.
ramacharitamanas::2002.detailed_meaning: The radiant beings are alarmed by Ram's impending coronation. In their fear, they appeal to Saraswati to create the condition that will send Ram to the forest instead. This verse is one step in the chain of divine intervention, not the final teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::2002.modern_relevance: A plan seems perfect until one small decision changes everything. A single conversation, made at the wrong moment, can reroute a family, a career, or a whole future.
ramacharitamanas::2002.insight: It shows how the larger story can turn on one subtle intervention.

ramacharitamanas::2003.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुर बिनय ठाढ़ि पछिताती। भइउँ सरोज बिपिन हिमराती॥ देखि देव पुनि कहहिं निहोरी। मातु तोहि नहिं थोरिउ खोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2003.verse_hindi: देवताओं की विनती सुनकर सरस्वतीजी खड़ी-खड़ी पछता रही हैं कि (हाय!) मैं कमलवन के लिए हेमंत ऋतु की रात हुई। उन्हें इस प्रकार पछताते देखकर देवता विनय करके कहने लगे- हे माता! इसमें आपको जरा भी दोष न लगेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2003.english_translation: Hearing the gods' plea, Saraswati stood there regretting it: "I have become a winter night for the lotus grove." Seeing her regret, the gods humbly said, "Mother, no fault lies with you."
ramacharitamanas::2003.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुर (gods) / बिनय (plea) / ठाढ़ि (standing) / पछिताती (regretting) / भइउँ (I became) / सरोज (lotus) / बिपिन (grove) / हिमराती (winter night)॥ / देखि (seeing) / देव (gods) / पुनि (again) / कहहिं (say) / निहोरी (humbly) / मातु (mother) / तोहि (to you) / नहिं (not) / थोरिउ (even a little) / खोरी (fault) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2003.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2003.essence: A difficult outcome can come through you without being your fault.
ramacharitamanas::2003.simple_meaning: Saraswati regrets helping the gods, and the gods reassure her that she is not at fault.
ramacharitamanas::2003.simple_insight: Sometimes even a wise choice can feel painful in the moment, and not every painful result is blame.
ramacharitamanas::2003.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the gods have asked for Ram's exile, and Saraswati has helped shape the words that make it happen. Now she stands uneasy, seeing the consequence of that divine request, while the gods gently tell her she bears no blame.
ramacharitamanas::2003.modern_relevance: You said the honest thing in a tense family conversation, and the room went silent. Later, you wonder whether you caused the hurt — even when the truth had to be spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2003.insight: It separates responsibility from guilt: not every role in a difficult outcome is a moral fault.

ramacharitamanas::2004.verse_sanskrit: बिसमय हरष रहित रघुराऊ। तुम्ह जानहु सब राम प्रभाऊ॥ जीव करम बस सुख दुख भागी। जाइअ अवध देव हित लागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2004.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी विषाद और हर्ष से रहित हैं। आप तो श्री रामजी के सब प्रभाव को जानती ही हैं। जीव अपने कर्मवश ही सुख-दुःख का भागी होता है। अतएव देवताओं के हित के लिए आप अयोध्या जाइए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2004.english_translation: Raghu's lord is beyond sorrow and joy. You know Ram's full power. A being receives pleasure and pain according to its own actions. Go to Ayodhya for the gods' welfare.
ramacharitamanas::2004.translation_literal: बिसमय (wonder) / हरष (joy) / रहित (free from) / रघुराऊ (lord of Raghu) / तुम्ह (you) / जानहु (know) / सब (all) / राम (Ram) / प्रभाऊ (power, glory) / जीव (being) / करम (action, consequence) / बस (under the control of) / सुख (pleasure) / दुख (pain) / भागी (one who receives) / जाइअ (go) / अवध (Ayodhya) / देव (for the gods) / हित (welfare) / लागी (for the sake of)
ramacharitamanas::2004.speaker: Saraswati
ramacharitamanas::2004.essence: Joy and sorrow belong to action, not to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2004.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond ordinary emotion. Every being experiences joy and sorrow according to its own actions, so Saraswati is urged to return to Ayodhya for the gods' benefit.
ramacharitamanas::2004.simple_insight: Pain feels personal, but the verse reminds you that action shapes experience more than mood does.
ramacharitamanas::2004.detailed_meaning: Saraswati has been blamed for the turmoil around Ram's exile. Here she is reminded that Ram himself remains untouched by sorrow and joy, and that beings taste results according to their own karma. The verse gently redirects her back toward Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::2004.modern_relevance: You replay one harsh message all night and assume it defines you. This verse pulls you back: not every feeling is a verdict, and not every outcome is yours to own.
ramacharitamanas::2004.insight: It shifts attention from emotional reaction to the law of consequence shaping experience.

ramacharitamanas::2005.verse_sanskrit: बार बार गहि चरन सँकोची। चली बिचारि बिबुध मति पोची॥ ऊँच निवासु नीचि करतूती। देखि न सकहिं पराइ बिभूती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2005.verse_hindi: बार-बार चरण पकड़कर देवताओं ने सरस्वती को संकोच में डाल दिया। तब वे यह विचारकर चलीं कि देवताओं की बुद्धि ओछी है। इनका निवास तो ऊँचा है, पर इनकी करनी नीची है। ये दूसरे का ऐश्वर्य नहीं देख सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::2005.english_translation: Again and again they held her feet, and she withdrew in embarrassment. Thinking, she left, knowing the gods' minds were petty. Their dwelling is high, but their conduct is low. They cannot bear to see another's splendor.
ramacharitamanas::2005.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / गहि (holding) / चरन (feet) / सँकोची (withdrew in embarrassment) / चली (went) / बिचारि (thinking) / बिबुध (gods) / मति (mind) / पोची (petty)॥ / ऊँच (high) / निवासु (dwelling) / नीचि (low) / करतूती (conduct) / देखि (seeing) / न सकहिं (cannot) / पराइ (another's) / बिभूती (splendor)
ramacharitamanas::2005.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2005.essence: High status means little when envy cannot bear another's rise.
ramacharitamanas::2005.simple_meaning: The gods keep pleading with Saraswati, but she leaves, seeing their small-mindedness. They may live in a high place, yet their actions are low, and they cannot tolerate another's greatness.
ramacharitamanas::2005.simple_insight: Status means little when the mind is jealous. Real nobility shows in how you respond to another person's excellence.
ramacharitamanas::2005.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the gods have been pressing Saraswati to shape events, but their repeated pleading only makes her withdraw in embarrassment. The verse turns sharp: high status means nothing if conduct is petty and envy cannot bear another's glory.
ramacharitamanas::2005.modern_relevance: A senior manager smiles in the meeting while quietly resenting the junior who solved the problem first. The title is high, but the reaction gives the mind away.
ramacharitamanas::2005.insight: It shifts attention from outer rank to inner conduct, exposing envy as a sign of weakness rather than power.

ramacharitamanas::2006.verse_sanskrit: आगिल काजु बिचारि बहोरी। करिहहिं चाह कुसल कबि मोरी॥ हरषि हृदयँ दसरथ पुर आई। जनु ग्रह दसा दुसह दुखदाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2006.verse_hindi: परन्तु आगे के काम का विचार करके (श्री रामजी के वन जाने से राक्षसों का वध होगा, जिससे सारा जगत सुखी हो जाएगा) चतुर कवि (श्री रामजी के वनवास के चरित्रों का वर्णन करने के लिए) मेरी चाह (कामना) करेंगे। ऐसा विचार कर सरस्वती हृदय में हर्षित होकर दशरथजी की पुरी अयोध्या में आईं, मानो दुःसह दुःख देने वाली कोई ग्रहदशा आई हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2006.english_translation: Thinking ahead, the wise poet will later praise my wish. Rejoicing, Saraswati entered Dasharath's city, like a cruel planetary affliction bringing unbearable sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2006.translation_literal: आगिल (future) / काजु (matter, task) / बिचारि (having considered) / बहोरी (again, thereafter) / करिहहिं (will do) / चाह (wish, desire) / कुसल (skilled, wise) / कबि (poet) / मोरी (my) / हरषि (rejoicing) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / पुर (city) / आई (came) / जनु (as if) / ग्रह-दसा (planetary affliction, bad period) / दुसह (unbearable) / दुखदाई (pain-giving)
ramacharitamanas::2006.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2006.essence: Joy can arrive carrying the shape of grief.
ramacharitamanas::2006.simple_meaning: Saraswati enters Ayodhya with joy, but her arrival will lead to sorrow for Dasharath. The poet hints that future events will later be described with skill.
ramacharitamanas::2006.simple_insight: Even a joyful turn can hide the seed of grief.
ramacharitamanas::2006.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Saraswati comes into Dasharath's heart and city just before the exile begins to unfold. Tulsidas hints that the coming events will be worth a poet's praise, even though they will bring unbearable sorrow to the king.
ramacharitamanas::2006.modern_relevance: A message arrives that seems harmless, even bright, but you can already feel the family tension underneath it. One small shift in tone can carry a whole future of pain.
ramacharitamanas::2006.insight: It prepares the reader for a tragic reversal, where apparent blessing becomes the doorway to loss.

ramacharitamanas::2007.verse_sanskrit: नामु मंथरा मंदमति चेरी कैकइ केरि। अजस पेटारी ताहि करि गई गिरा मति फेरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2007.verse_hindi: मन्थरा नाम की कैकेई की एक मंदबुद्धि दासी थी, उसे अपयश की पिटारी बनाकर सरस्वती उसकी बुद्धि को फेरकर चली गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2007.english_translation: Manthara, Kaikeyi's dull-witted maid, became a vessel of disgrace; Saraswati turned her mind and departed.
ramacharitamanas::2007.translation_literal: नामु (name) / मंथरा (Manthara) / मंदमति (dull-witted) / चेरी (maid) / कैकइ केरि (of Kaikeyi) / अजस (disgrace) / पेटारी (box/vessel) / ताहि (her) / करि (making) / गई (went) / गिरा (speech) / मति (mind) / फेरि (turning)
ramacharitamanas::2007.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2007.essence: A twisted mind turns blessing into disgrace.
ramacharitamanas::2007.simple_meaning: Manthara, Kaikeyi's maid, is described as a carrier of disgrace. Saraswati then turns her mind and leaves.
ramacharitamanas::2007.simple_insight: A mind twisted by desire can become the tool of harm without seeing it.
ramacharitamanas::2007.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court is preparing for Ram's coronation. Before Manthara even speaks, the narration marks her as the seed of coming ruin: Kaikeyi's maid, already bent toward mischief, is shown as a vessel for disgrace, with divine speech itself turning her mind.
ramacharitamanas::2007.modern_relevance: A person hears one rumor in a crowded kitchen, and suddenly every detail feels charged with insult. The mind can be turned before it knows what happened.
ramacharitamanas::2007.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the distorted mind that interprets it.

ramacharitamanas::2008.verse_sanskrit: दीख मंथरा नगरु बनावा। मंजुल मंगल बाज बधावा॥ पूछेसि लोगन्ह काह उछाहू। राम तिलकु सुनि भा उर दाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2008.verse_hindi: मंथरा ने देखा कि नगर सजाया हुआ है। सुंदर मंगलमय बधावे बज रहे हैं। उसने लोगों से पूछा कि कैसा उत्सव है? (उनसे) श्री रामचन्द्रजी के राजतिलक की बात सुनते ही उसका हृदय जल उठा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2008.english_translation: Manthara saw the city beautifully decorated. Auspicious drums and cheers were sounding. She asked the people what the celebration was about. Hearing that Ram was to be crowned, her heart burned with jealousy.
ramacharitamanas::2008.translation_literal: दीख (saw) / मंथरा (Manthara) / नगरु (the city) / बनावा (made decorated) / मंजुल (beautiful) / मंगल (auspicious) / बाज (drums) / बधावा (congratulatory songs) / पूछेसि (she asked) / लोगन्ह (the people) / काह (what) / उछाहू (celebration) / राम (Ram) / तिलकु (coronation) / सुनि (hearing) / भा (became) / उर (heart) / दाहू (burning)
ramacharitamanas::2008.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2008.essence: Jealousy makes another person's joy feel unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2008.simple_meaning: The city is celebrating Ram's coronation, and Manthara reacts with burning jealousy instead of joy.
ramacharitamanas::2008.simple_insight: Envy can turn another person's happiness into your own pain.
ramacharitamanas::2008.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is decorated for Ram's coronation. Manthara sees the celebration, asks what is happening, and hears the news. Instead of delight, she feels her heart burn. This moment sets her scheming in motion.
ramacharitamanas::2008.modern_relevance: You open a group chat and see everyone congratulating someone you secretly resent. Their win should be harmless, but your mind turns it into a wound.
ramacharitamanas::2008.insight: It exposes how envy distorts perception and pushes the mind toward harmful planning.

ramacharitamanas::2009.verse_sanskrit: करइ बिचारु कुबुद्धि कुजाती। होइ अकाजु कवनि बिधि राती॥ देखि लागि मधु कुटिल किराती। जिमि गवँ तकइ लेउँ केहि भाँती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2009.verse_hindi: वह दुर्बुद्धि, नीच जाति वाली दासी विचार करने लगी कि किस प्रकार से यह काम रात ही रात में बिगड़ जाए, जैसे कोई कुटिल भीलनी शहद का छत्ता लगा देखकर घात लगाती है कि इसको किस तरह से उखाड़ लूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2009.english_translation: That evil-minded, low-born maid thought of how to ruin the matter by night. Like a crafty bee-keeper seeing honey, like a cunning hill-woman watching a hive, she schemed how to tear it down.
ramacharitamanas::2009.translation_literal: करइ (does) / बिचारु (thought) / कुबुद्धि (evil-minded) / कुजाती (of low birth) / होइ (becomes) / अकाजु (harmful deed) / कवनि बिधि (by what means) / राती (at night) / देखि (seeing) / लागि (attached) / मधु (honey) / कुटिल (cunning) / किराती (hill-woman) / जिमि (as) / गवँ (hive) / तकइ (watches) / लेउँ (to take) / केहि भाँती (by what means)
ramacharitamanas::2009.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2009.essence: A crooked mind turns someone else's joy into a target.
ramacharitamanas::2009.simple_meaning: Manthara starts plotting how to ruin the happy news before morning, like a crafty hunter watching for a chance to strike.
ramacharitamanas::2009.simple_insight: A twisted mind does not rest when goodness appears; it immediately looks for a way to spoil it.
ramacharitamanas::2009.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Manthara has just seen Ayodhya glowing with joy at Ram's coronation preparations. Instead of sharing the happiness, she begins plotting through the night, searching for a way to turn celebration into disaster.
ramacharitamanas::2009.modern_relevance: You hear good news in a family group chat, and one person instantly starts looking for what could go wrong. The verse captures that reflex to spoil joy before it can settle.
ramacharitamanas::2009.insight: It exposes how envy works: first it watches, then it schemes, then it acts.

ramacharitamanas::2010.verse_sanskrit: भरत मातु पहिं गइ बिलखानी। का अनमनि हसि कह हँसि रानी॥ ऊतरु देइ न लेइ उसासू। नारि चरित करि ढारइ आँसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2010.verse_hindi: वह उदास होकर भरतजी की माता कैकेयी के पास गई। रानी कैकेयी ने हँसकर कहा- तू उदास क्यों है? मंथरा कुछ उत्तर नहीं देती, केवल लंबी साँस ले रही है और त्रियाचरित्र करके आँसू ढरका रही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2010.english_translation: Manthara went sadly to Queen Kaikeyi. The queen laughed and said, “Why are you so downcast?” Manthara gave no answer, only sighed deeply and shed tears like a woman acting a part.
ramacharitamanas::2010.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / मातु (mother) / पहिं (to) / गइ (went) / बिलखानी (sorrowful) / का (why) / अनमनि (listless) / हसि (laughing) / कह (said) / हँसि (laughing) / रानी (queen) / ऊतरु (answer) / देइ (giving) / न (not) / लेइ (taking) / उसासू (sighs) / नारि (woman) / चरित (behavior) / करि (doing) / ढारइ (sheds) / आँसू (tears)
ramacharitamanas::2010.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2010.essence: Deception often begins with tears, not words.
ramacharitamanas::2010.simple_meaning: Manthara, upset and pretending to be innocent, goes to Kaikeyi. Kaikeyi laughs and asks why she is sad, while Manthara only sighs and cries without speaking plainly.
ramacharitamanas::2010.simple_insight: Hidden motives often speak through silence, sighs, and performance.
ramacharitamanas::2010.detailed_meaning: Manthara reaches Kaikeyi’s chamber in Ayodhya after seeing the city celebrate Ram’s coming coronation. Kaikeyi greets her with a smile, but Manthara refuses direct speech, acting distressed instead. The scene shows the first poison of the exile plot spreading quietly.
ramacharitamanas::2010.modern_relevance: A friend says, “Nothing’s wrong,” but their silence is heavy and theatrical. You can feel the manipulation before a single accusation is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2010.insight: It trains attention toward indirect signals, helping you notice when emotion is being used to steer another person.

ramacharitamanas::2011.verse_sanskrit: हँसि कह रानि गालु बड़ तोरें। दीन्ह लखन सिख अस मन मोरें॥ तबहुँ न बोल चेरि बड़ि पापिनि। छाड़इ स्वास कारि जनु साँपिनि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2011.verse_hindi: रानी हँसकर कहने लगी कि तेरे बड़े गाल हैं (तू बहुत बढ़-बढ़कर बोलने वाली है)। मेरा मन कहता है कि लक्ष्मण ने तुझे कुछ सीख दी है (दण्ड दिया है)। तब भी वह महापापिनी दासी कुछ भी नहीं बोलती। ऐसी लंबी साँस छोड़ रही है, मानो काली नागिन (फुफकार छोड़ रही) हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2011.english_translation: The queen laughed and said, “Your words are too bold. I think Lakshman has taught you a lesson.” Still the wicked maid said nothing, breathing hard like a snake woman hissing.”
ramacharitamanas::2011.translation_literal: हँसि (laughing) / कह (said) / रानि (queen) / गालु (abuse, taunt) / बड़ (big, excessive) / तोरें (your) / दीन्ह (gave) / लखन (Lakshman) / सिख (lesson) / अस (like, thus) / मन (mind) / मोरें (my) / तबहुँ (even then) / न (not) / बोल (spoke) / चेरि (maidservant) / बड़ि (great) / पापिनि (sinful woman) / छाड़इ (releasing) / स्वास (breath) / कारि (black) / जनु (as if) / साँपिनि (female snake)
ramacharitamanas::2011.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2011.essence: Cruel speech deepens fear and turns silence into menace.
ramacharitamanas::2011.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi taunts the maid for speaking boldly, then notices she still stays silent and breathes like an angry snake. The verse shows mockery, suspicion, and the maid’s stubborn silence.
ramacharitamanas::2011.simple_insight: A cruel mind keeps looking for weakness in others, even while fear is already rising inside it.
ramacharitamanas::2011.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi faces Manthara after the poisonous counsel has begun to work. She mocks the maid’s boldness and assumes Lakshman has already punished her. Manthara stays silent, breathing like a snake, and the tension keeps building toward disaster.
ramacharitamanas::2011.modern_relevance: You catch the sharp tone in a group chat and answer with a jab, trying to stay in control. But the silence on the other side already tells you the conversation has turned toxic.
ramacharitamanas::2011.insight: It shows how suspicion and insult escalate a broken exchange instead of calming it.

ramacharitamanas::2012.verse_sanskrit: सभय रानि कह कहसि किन कुसल रामु महिपालु। लखनु भरतु रिपुदमनु सुनि भा कुबरी उर सालु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2012.verse_hindi: तब रानी ने डरकर कहा- अरी! कहती क्यों नहीं? श्री रामचन्द्र, राजा, लक्ष्मण, भरत और शत्रुघ्न कुशल से तो हैं? यह सुनकर कुबरी मंथरा के हृदय में बड़ी ही पीड़ा हुई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2012.english_translation: The queen, frightened, said, “Why do you not say whether Ram, the king, Lakshman, Bharat, and Shatrughna are well?” Hearing this, a deep ache rose in Manthara’s heart.
ramacharitamanas::2012.translation_literal: सभय (frightened) / रानि (queen) / कह (said) / कहसि (why do you say) / किन (why not) / कुसल (well) / रामु (Ram) / महिपालु (king) / लखनु (Lakshman) / भरतु (Bharat) / रिपुदमनु (subduer of enemies) / सुनि (hearing) / भा (became) / कुबरी (Manthara) / उर (heart) / सालु (ache/pain)
ramacharitamanas::2012.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2012.essence: A sincere concern for Ram wounds the heart of manipulation.
ramacharitamanas::2012.simple_meaning: Queen Kaikeyi, suddenly uneasy, asks whether Ram, Lakshman, Bharat, and Shatrughna are all well. Manthara feels a sharp pain in her heart.
ramacharitamanas::2012.simple_insight: A single honest question can expose hidden motives and disturb a plotted mind.
ramacharitamanas::2012.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has been drawn into Manthara’s scheme. Now, startled by fear, she asks after the well-being of Ram and his brothers. The question stings Manthara, because her plan depends on Kaikeyi forgetting that love.
ramacharitamanas::2012.modern_relevance: You’re halfway into a manipulative conversation, and one sincere question breaks the spell. The person steering the room suddenly feels exposed.
ramacharitamanas::2012.insight: It shifts attention from plotting to the human bond that plotting tries to erase.

ramacharitamanas::2013.verse_sanskrit: कत सिख देइ हमहि कोउ माई। गालु करब केहि कर बलु पाई॥ रामहि छाड़ि कुसल केहि आजू। जेहि जनेसु देइ जुबराजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2013.verse_hindi: (वह कहने लगी-) हे माई! हमें कोई क्यों सीख देगा और मैं किसका बल पाकर गाल करूँगी (बढ़-बढ़कर बोलूँगी)। रामचन्द्र को छोड़कर आज और किसकी कुशल है, जिन्हें राजा युवराज पद दे रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2013.english_translation: She said, “Mother, who could teach me now? And whose strength would I have to speak harshly? Except for Ram, whose welfare matters today, when he is being made crown prince?”
ramacharitamanas::2013.translation_literal: कत (who) / सिख (instruction) / देइ (would give) / हमहि (to us) / कोउ (anyone) / माई (mother) / गालु (insulting words) / करब (to speak) / केहि (whose) / कर (hand/strength) / बलु (strength) / पाई (having obtained) / रामहि (Ram) / छाड़ि (except) / कुसल (well-being) / केहि (whose) / आजू (today) / जेहि (to whom) / जनेसु (gave birth to) / देइ (gives) / जुबराजू (crown prince)
ramacharitamanas::2013.speaker: Kaikeyi
