ramacharitamanas::2054.verse_hindi: मन्थरा की बातें सुनने में तो कोमल हैं, पर परिणाम में कठोर (भयानक) हैं। मानो वह शहद में घोलकर जहर पिला रही हो। दासी कहती है- हे स्वामिनि! तुमने मुझको एक कथा कही थी, उसकी याद है कि नहीं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2054.english_translation: Manthara's words sound soft at first, but they are hard in the end. It is as if she is pouring poison mixed with honey. The maid says, "Mistress, do you remember the story you told me or not?"
ramacharitamanas::2054.translation_literal: सुनत (on hearing) / बात (words) / मृदु (soft) / अंत (in the end) / कठोरी (hard) / देति (giving) / मनहुँ (as if) / मधु (honey) / माहुर (poison) / घोरी (mixed) / कहइ (says) / चेरि (maid) / सुधि (memory) / अहइ (is) / कि (or) / नाहीं (not) / स्वामिनि (mistress) / कहिहु (tell) / कथा (story) / मोहि (to me) / पाहीं (to me)
ramacharitamanas::2054.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2054.essence: Soft words can carry the hardest harm.
ramacharitamanas::2054.simple_meaning: Manthara speaks in a sweet way, but her words are meant to bring harm. The maid then reminds Kaikeyi of an old promise or story.
ramacharitamanas::2054.simple_insight: Sweet words can hide a destructive intention. Clear seeing matters before you trust the voice in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::2054.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Manthara has begun steering Kaikeyi toward disaster. Her speech sounds gentle, but it carries poison. The maid then prods Kaikeyi's memory, preparing her to demand the boons that will exile Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2054.modern_relevance: A friend texts you in a calm tone, but every line nudges you toward a choice you already know will cost you. The danger is not the volume — it is the hidden intent.
ramacharitamanas::2054.insight: It trains attention on motive, not just tone, so manipulation is seen before it takes hold.

ramacharitamanas::2055.verse_sanskrit: दुइ बरदान भूप सन थाती। मागहु आजु जुड़ावहु छाती॥ सुतहि राजु रामहि बनबासू। देहु लेहु सब सवति हुलासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2055.verse_hindi: तुम्हारे दो वरदान राजा के पास धरोहर हैं। आज उन्हें राजा से माँगकर अपनी छाती ठंडी करो। पुत्र को राज्य और राम को वनवास दो और सौत का सारा आनंद तुम ले लो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2055.english_translation: Your two boons are still with the king. Today, ask for them and cool your heart: give the son the kingdom, give Ram exile, and let the other queen keep all her joy.
ramacharitamanas::2055.translation_literal: दुइ (two) / बरदान (boons) / भूप (king) / सन (with) / थाती (stored treasure) / मागहु (ask) / आजु (today) / जुड़ावहु (cool) / छाती (heart/chest) / सुतहि (to the son) / राजु (kingdom) / रामहि (to Ram) / बनबासू (forest exile) / देहु (give) / लेहु (take) / सब (all) / सवति (co-wife) / हुलासू (joy)
ramacharitamanas::2055.speaker: Manthara
ramacharitamanas::2055.essence: Resentment becomes disaster the moment it is given a voice.
ramacharitamanas::2055.simple_meaning: Manthara urges Kaikeyi to use her two boons right away: ask for her son to become king and send Ram into exile.
ramacharitamanas::2055.simple_insight: Manipulation often sounds like advice. The danger is not only in the demand, but in the timing.
ramacharitamanas::2055.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Manthara has poisoned Kaikeyi’s mind and now pushes her toward action. She tells Kaikeyi to claim the two boons from Dasharath immediately, making Bharata king and sending Ram to the forest. This is the decisive nudge before the tragedy unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::2055.modern_relevance: A friend texts you late at night, framing revenge as self-respect and urging you to act before morning. The pressure feels urgent because it is designed to be urgent.
ramacharitamanas::2055.insight: It teaches you to notice how fear and resentment can be turned into a plan before you have time to think.

ramacharitamanas::2056.verse_sanskrit: भूपति राम सपथ जब करई। तब मागेहु जेहिं बचनु न टरई॥ होइ अकाजु आजु निसि बीतें। बचनु मोर प्रिय मानेहु जी तें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2056.verse_hindi: जब राजा राम की सौगंध खा लें, तब वर माँगना, जिससे वचन न टलने पावे। आज की रात बीत गई, तो काम बिगड़ जाएगा। मेरी बात को हृदय से प्रिय (या प्राणों से भी प्यारी) समझना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2056.english_translation: When the king has sworn by Ram, then ask for the boon, so his word cannot fail. If tonight passes, the plan will be ruined. Take my words as dear to your heart.
ramacharitamanas::2056.translation_literal: भूपति (king) / राम (Ram) / सपथ (oath) / जब (when) / करई (does) / तब (then) / मागेहु (ask) / जेहिं (so that) / बचनु (word) / न (not) / टरई (fails)॥ / होइ (becomes) / अकाजु (ruin) / आजु (today) / निसि (night) / बीतें (having passed) / बचनु (word) / मोर (my) / प्रिय (dear) / मानेहु (consider) / जी (heart) / तें (from)
ramacharitamanas::2056.speaker: Manthara
ramacharitamanas::2056.essence: Haste can be used to trap a promise before reason returns.
ramacharitamanas::2056.simple_meaning: Manthara tells Kaikeyi to wait for the right moment and make sure Ram's father's promise cannot be broken. She pushes urgency and secrecy to get the result she wants.
ramacharitamanas::2056.simple_insight: Manipulation thrives on timing, pressure, and fear of delay.
ramacharitamanas::2056.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Manthara has already poisoned Kaikeyi's mind. Now she sharpens the plot: wait until Dasharath has sworn by Ram, then ask for the boon before the night ends. The whole exile scheme depends on trapping the king's word.
ramacharitamanas::2056.modern_relevance: A text message lands at midnight: "Reply now or the offer is gone." The pressure is the point. This verse shows how fear of delay can be used to steer a decision.
ramacharitamanas::2056.insight: It exposes how urgency can be weaponized to bypass reflection.

ramacharitamanas::2057.verse_sanskrit: बड़ कुघातु करि पातकिनि कहेसि कोपगृहँ जाहु। काजु सँवारेहु सजग सबु सहसा जनि पतिआहु ॥॥
ramacharitamanas::2057.verse_hindi: पापिनी मन्थरा ने बड़ी बुरी घात लगाकर कहा- कोपभवन में जाओ। सब काम बड़ी सावधानी से बनाना, राजा पर सहसा विश्वास न कर लेना (उनकी बातों में न आ जाना) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2057.english_translation: The wicked Manthara, after striking a cruel blow, said, "Go to the anger chamber. Handle everything carefully, and do not trust the king suddenly."
ramacharitamanas::2057.translation_literal: बड़ (great) / कुघातु (evil blow) / करि (having done) / पातकिनि (sinful woman) / कहेसि (she said) / कोपगृहँ (to the anger chamber) / जाहु (go) / काजु (matter) / सँवारेहु (arrange carefully) / सजग (alert) / सबु (all) / सहसा (suddenly) / जनि (do not) / पतिआहु (trust)
ramacharitamanas::2057.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2057.essence: Manipulation begins by making caution feel like wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::2057.simple_meaning: Manthara, after plotting against Kaikeyi, tells her to go to the anger chamber and be careful. She warns her not to trust the king too quickly.
ramacharitamanas::2057.simple_insight: A manipulative mind survives by planting fear and urgency before reason can speak.
ramacharitamanas::2057.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Manthara has already poisoned Kaikeyi's mind. Now she pushes her toward the anger chamber and tells her to act carefully, not to trust Dasharath's words. This is the moment the scheme is sealed.
ramacharitamanas::2057.modern_relevance: A friend texts at midnight: "Don’t tell anyone yet. Act fast." The message feels urgent, but urgency is often how manipulation wins before clarity arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2057.insight: It shows how fear and haste can be used to control another person's judgment.

ramacharitamanas::2058.verse_sanskrit: कुबरिहि रानि प्रानप्रिय जानी। बार बार बुद्धि बखानी॥ तोहि सम हित न मोर संसारा। बहे जात कई भइसि अधारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2058.verse_hindi: कुबरी को रानी ने प्राणों के समान प्रिय समझकर बार-बार उसकी बड़ी बुद्धि का बखान किया और बोली- संसार में मेरा तेरे समान हितकारी और कोई नहीं है। तू मुझे बही जाती हुई के लिए सहारा हुई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2058.english_translation: The queen regarded Manthara as dear as her own life and praised her wisdom again and again: "No one in the world is as helpful to me as you. You have become a support for me as I am being carried away."
ramacharitamanas::2058.translation_literal: कुबरिहि (Manthara) / रानि (the queen) / प्रानप्रिय (dear as life) / जानी (knowing) / बार बार (again and again) / बुद्धि (wisdom) / बखानी (praised) / तोहि (you) / सम (equal) / हित (beneficial) / न (not) / मोर (my) / संसारा (world) / बहे जात (being carried away) / कई (for me) / भइसि (you became) / अधारा (support)
ramacharitamanas::2058.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2058.essence: Desire turns warning into wisdom and harm into help.
ramacharitamanas::2058.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi flatters Manthara and treats her like a lifesaving helper, not seeing the harm being fed into her mind.
ramacharitamanas::2058.simple_insight: Praise can become blindness when desire is steering the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2058.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Manthara has begun planting fear and ambition in Kaikeyi's mind. Kaikeyi, still unaware of the trap, calls her dear as life and credits her with saving her from being swept away. The moment shows how manipulation works before the damage becomes visible.
ramacharitamanas::2058.modern_relevance: A friend keeps repeating, “I’m just being honest,” while quietly pushing you toward a bad choice. You start calling it help because it flatters what you already want.
ramacharitamanas::2058.insight: It shows how the mind mistakes reinforcement for guidance and loses the ability to judge what is harmful.

ramacharitamanas::2059.verse_sanskrit: जौं बिधि पुरब मनोरथु काली। करौं तोहि चख पूतरि आली॥ बहुबिधि चेरिहि आदरु देई। कोपभवन गवनी कैकेई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2059.verse_hindi: यदि विधाता कल मेरा मनोरथ पूरा कर दें तो हे सखी! मैं तुझे आँखों की पुतली बना लूँ। इस प्रकार दासी को बहुत तरह से आदर देकर कैकेयी कोपभवन में चली गई॥।2॥
ramacharitamanas::2059.english_translation: If fate fulfills my wish tomorrow, I will keep you as the pupil of my eye, dear friend. Giving the maid many kinds of honor, Kaikeyi went to the chamber of anger.
ramacharitamanas::2059.translation_literal: जौं (if) / बिधि (fate) / पुरब (tomorrow) / मनोरथु (wish) / काली (tomorrow) / करौं (I do) / तोहि (you) / चख (eye) / पूतरि (pupil) / आली (friend) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / चेरिहि (to the maid) / आदरु (honor) / देई (giving) / कोपभवन (anger chamber) / गवनी (went) / कैकेई (Kaikeyi)
ramacharitamanas::2059.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2059.essence: Sweet words can escort a mind straight into ruin.
ramacharitamanas::2059.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi flatters Manthara and promises special favor if her wish comes true. Then she goes to the chamber of anger.
ramacharitamanas::2059.simple_insight: Praise can hide a mind already leaning toward harm.
ramacharitamanas::2059.detailed_meaning: Kaikeyi has already been stirred by Manthara's words. Now she sweetens the maid with affection and promises, then walks toward the chamber where resentment will harden into action. The scene shows manipulation taking shape before the demand is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2059.modern_relevance: You smile warmly at the person feeding your worst suspicion. The kindness looks real, but your mind has already chosen the darker story.
ramacharitamanas::2059.insight: It exposes how flattery can become the cover for a decision already made.

ramacharitamanas::2060.verse_sanskrit: बिपति बीजु बरषा रितु चेरी। भुइँ भइ कुमति कैकई केरी॥ पाइ कपट जलु अंकुर जामा। बर दोउ दल दुख फल परिनामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2060.verse_hindi: विपत्ति (कलह) बीज है, दासी वर्षा ऋतु है, कैकेयी की कुबुद्धि (उस बीज के बोने के लिए) जमीन हो गई। उसमें कपट रूपी जल पाकर अंकुर फूट निकला। दोनों वरदान उस अंकुर के दो पत्ते हैं और अंत में इसके दुःख रूपी फल होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2060.english_translation: The seed of disaster was sown. Manthara's counsel was the rain, and Kaikeyi's bad judgment became the ground. With deceit as water, the sprout rose. The two boons were its two leaves, and sorrow would be its fruit.
ramacharitamanas::2060.translation_literal: बिपति (disaster) / बीजु (seed) / बरषा रितु (rainy season) / चेरी (servant) / भुइँ (ground) / भइ (became) / कुमति (bad judgment) / कैकई केरी (of Kaikeyi) / पाइ (having received) / कपट (deceit) / जलु (water) / अंकुर (sprout) / जामा (sprang up) / बर (boons) / दोउ (two) / दल (leaves) / दुख (sorrow) / फल (fruit) / परिनामा (result)
ramacharitamanas::2060.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2060.essence: Disaster grows first as a seed, then as a fruit.
ramacharitamanas::2060.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi's poor judgment, fed by Manthara's deceit, grew into a disaster that would end in sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2060.simple_insight: A small wrong choice can grow quietly until it becomes a life-shaping loss.
ramacharitamanas::2060.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has already been swayed by Manthara's praise and manipulation. Tulsidas compares that influence to rain falling on bad ground: deceit takes root, the boons become visible, and the coming grief is already planted.
ramacharitamanas::2060.modern_relevance: One careless conversation in a kitchen late at night can become the argument that breaks a family. The damage often begins long before anyone admits it.
ramacharitamanas::2060.insight: It shifts attention to the hidden seed of a crisis, not just its final explosion.

ramacharitamanas::2061.verse_sanskrit: कोप समाजु साजि सबु सोई। राजु करत निज कुमति बिगोई॥ राउर नगर कोलाहलु होई। यह कुचालि कछु जान न कोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2061.verse_hindi: कैकेयी कोप का सब साज सजकर (कोपभवन में) जा सोई। राज्य करती हुई वह अपनी दुष्ट बुद्धि से नष्ट हो गई। राजमहल और नगर में धूम-धाम मच रही है। इस कुचाल को कोई कुछ नहीं जानता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2061.english_translation: Kaikeyi arranged the whole scene of anger and lay there. While ruling, she was ruined by her own bad judgment. The royal palace and the city were in uproar, and no one understood this plot.
ramacharitamanas::2061.translation_literal: कोप (anger) / समाजु (assembly; arrangement) / साजि (having prepared) / सबु (all) / सोई (that very one) / राजु (kingdom; rule) / करत (doing; ruling) / निज (own) / कुमति (bad judgment) / बिगोई (ruined)॥ / राउर (royal) / नगर (city) / कोलाहलु (uproar) / होई (is; happened)॥ / यह (this) / कुचालि (bad plot; foul scheme) / कछु (anything) / जान (know) / न (not) / कोई (anyone) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2061.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2061.essence: A private bad choice can quietly ruin an entire kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::2061.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi has set her anger in motion, and that very choice is ruining her. The palace and city are in confusion, while no one yet sees the hidden plot.
ramacharitamanas::2061.simple_insight: A hidden decision can spread chaos long before anyone understands it.
ramacharitamanas::2061.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has already entered the chamber of anger and set her scheme in motion. The palace is busy and noisy, but underneath that normal activity her bad judgment is quietly unmaking the kingdom, and no one around her sees it yet.
ramacharitamanas::2061.modern_relevance: A family group chat looks normal while one message has already poisoned the room. Everyone keeps talking, laughing, planning — and nobody sees the fracture that is about to split everything open.
ramacharitamanas::2061.insight: It shifts attention from outward normalcy to the hidden cause already shaping events.

ramacharitamanas::2062.verse_sanskrit: प्रमुदित पुर नर नारि सब सजहिं सुमंगलचार। एक प्रबिसहिं एक निर्गमहिं भीर भूप दरबार॥23।
ramacharitamanas::2062.verse_hindi: बड़े ही आनन्दित होकर नगर के सब स्त्री-पुरुष शुभ मंगलाचार के साथ सज रहे हैं। कोई भीतर जाता है, कोई बाहर निकलता है, राजद्वार में बड़ी भीड़ हो रही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2062.english_translation: The people of the city, men and women alike, are delighted and busy with auspicious preparations. Some go in, some come out; the king’s gate is crowded.
ramacharitamanas::2062.translation_literal: प्रमुदित (delighted) / पुर (city) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / सब (all) / सजहिं (prepare) / सुमंगलचार (auspicious observances) / एक (one) / प्रबिसहिं (enter) / एक (one) / निर्गमहिं (exit) / भीर (crowd) / भूप (king) / दरबार (court)
ramacharitamanas::2062.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2062.essence: A whole city rises together for an auspicious turning point.
ramacharitamanas::2062.simple_meaning: The whole city is joyful and preparing for an auspicious event. People are moving in and out of the royal court in a crowd.
ramacharitamanas::2062.simple_insight: Shared joy can fill an entire city before a great moment arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2062.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is alive with excitement. Men and women prepare for an auspicious royal event, while crowds move in and out of the king’s court. The verse sets the scene before the news reaches Ram’s childhood friends.
ramacharitamanas::2062.modern_relevance: Outside a wedding hall, relatives keep arriving with flowers, gifts, and folded clothes. No one is still; everyone feels the day is larger than themselves.
ramacharitamanas::2062.insight: It shifts attention from private feeling to a community carried by one hopeful event.

ramacharitamanas::2063.verse_sanskrit: बाल सखा सुनि हियँ हरषाहीं। मिलि दस पाँच राम पहिं जाहीं॥ प्रभु आदरहिं प्रेमु पहिचानी। पूँछहिं कुसल खेम मृदु बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2063.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के बाल सखा राजतिलक का समाचार सुनकर हृदय में हर्षित होते हैं। वे दस-पाँच मिलकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी के पास जाते हैं। प्रेम पहचानकर प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी उनका आदर करते हैं और कोमल वाणी से कुशल क्षेम पूछते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2063.english_translation: Hearing of the coronation, Ram's childhood friends rejoice in their hearts. Ten or five of them go together to meet Ram. Ram recognises their love, honours them, and asks after their well-being in gentle words.
ramacharitamanas::2063.translation_literal: बाल सखा (childhood friends) / सुनि (hearing) / हियँ (in the heart) / हरषाहीं (rejoice) / मिलि (together) / दस पाँच (ten or five) / राम पहिं (to Ram) / जाहीं (go) / प्रभु (the Lord) / आदरहिं (honour) / प्रेमु (love) / पहिचानी (recognising) / पूँछहिं (ask) / कुसल खेम (well-being and safety) / मृदु बानी (gentle words)
ramacharitamanas::2063.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2063.essence: Love keeps friendship equal, even when one friend becomes king.
ramacharitamanas::2063.simple_meaning: Ram's childhood friends hear about his coronation, come to see him, and are welcomed with warmth and respect.
ramacharitamanas::2063.simple_insight: Real love shows up as warmth, not status. Old friendship stays alive even when a friend becomes king.
ramacharitamanas::2063.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, news of Ram's coronation spreads through the city. His childhood friends hear it, feel joy, and come together to meet him. Ram receives them with affection, recognising their bond before rank, and speaks to them kindly.
ramacharitamanas::2063.modern_relevance: Your oldest friend finally gets the promotion everyone expected. You still speak to them like the person who knew your worst days, not the title on their door.
ramacharitamanas::2063.insight: It shifts attention from hierarchy to human bond, showing that honour begins with recognising love.

ramacharitamanas::2064.verse_sanskrit: फिरहिं भवन प्रिय आयसु पाई। करत परसपर राम बड़ाई॥ को रघुबीर सरिस संसारा। सीलु सनेहु निबाहनिहारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2064.verse_hindi: अपने प्रिय सखा श्री रामचन्द्रजी की आज्ञा पाकर वे आपस में एक-दूसरे से श्री रामचन्द्रजी की बड़ाई करते हुए घर लौटते हैं और कहते हैं- संसार में श्री रघुनाथजी के समान शील और स्नेह को निबाहने वाला कौन है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2064.english_translation: They return to their homes after receiving Ram's kind permission, praising Ram to one another. "Who in the world is like the Lord of the Raghu clan, who keeps both character and affection?"
ramacharitamanas::2064.translation_literal: फिरहिं (they return) / भवन (to homes) / प्रिय (dear) / आयसु (permission, command) / पाई (having received) / करत (doing) / परसपर (mutually, to one another) / राम (Ram) / बड़ाई (praise) / को (who) / रघुबीर (Lord of the Raghu clan) / सरिस (like) / संसारा (world) / सीलु (character, gentleness) / सनेहु (affection, love) / निबाहनिहारा (one who upholds, one who keeps)
ramacharitamanas::2064.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2064.essence: Character and affection make Ram unforgettable.
ramacharitamanas::2064.simple_meaning: Ram's friends go home after his permission, praising him among themselves. They see him as unmatched in keeping both character and affection.
ramacharitamanas::2064.simple_insight: Real greatness is steady conduct that never breaks trust or warmth.
ramacharitamanas::2064.detailed_meaning: Ram's childhood friends have come with joy for his coronation, but this moment is not about celebration alone. After meeting him, they leave with his permission, still speaking of his unmatched gentleness and loyalty. Their praise becomes its own teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2064.modern_relevance: You leave a reunion still talking about the one person who treated everyone with rare steadiness. No performance, no sharp edges — just the kind of respect that makes people remember you on the drive home.
ramacharitamanas::2064.insight: It shifts admiration from status to character, showing that true authority is measured by how faithfully someone treats others.

ramacharitamanas::2065.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं-जेहिं जोनि करम बस भ्रमहीं। तहँ तहँ ईसु देउ यह हमहीं॥ सेवक हम स्वामी सियनाहू। होउ नात यह ओर निबाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2065.verse_hindi: भगवान हमें यही दें कि हम अपने कर्मवश भ्रमते हुए जिस-जिस योनि में जन्में, वहाँ-वहाँ (उस-उस योनि में) हम तो सेवक हों और सीतापति श्री रामचन्द्रजी हमारे स्वामी हों और यह नाता अन्त तक निभ जाए॥
ramacharitamanas::2065.english_translation: May the divine grant that, wherever we are driven by the force of our actions in any birth, we remain servants there, and Ram, Lord of Sita, remains our master. May this bond endure to the end.
ramacharitamanas::2065.translation_literal: जेहिं-जेहिं (in whichever) / जोनि (birth-form) / करम बस (by the force of action) / भ्रमहीं (we wander) / तहँ तहँ (there, there) / ईसु (the divine) / देउ (may give) / यह (this) / हमहीं (to us) / सेवक (servant) / हम (we) / स्वामी (master) / सियनाहू (of Sita's lord) / होउ (may it be) / नात (bond) / यह (this) / ओर (end) / निबाहू (be upheld)
ramacharitamanas::2065.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2065.essence: True freedom is to belong to Ram in every life.
ramacharitamanas::2065.simple_meaning: No matter where karma sends us in future births, let us remain servants and let Ram remain our master forever.
ramacharitamanas::2065.simple_insight: There is peace in choosing belonging over control.
ramacharitamanas::2065.detailed_meaning: The villagers have been praising Ram's qualities, and the speaker turns that admiration into a prayer. He asks that, through every birth and every change, the relationship remain fixed: we serve, and Ram rules our heart.
ramacharitamanas::2065.modern_relevance: After a long career change, a family move, or a season of uncertainty, you may not know what role life will give you next. This prayer says identity can stay steady even when circumstances do not.
ramacharitamanas::2065.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing status to preserving devotion through every change.

ramacharitamanas::2066.verse_sanskrit: अस अभिलाषु नगर सब काहू। कैकयसुता हृदयँ अति दाहू॥ को न कुसंगति पाइ नसाई। रहइ न नीच मतें चतुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2066.verse_hindi: नगर में सबकी ऐसी ही अभिलाषा है, परन्तु कैकेयी के हृदय में बड़ी जलन हो रही है। कुसंगति पाकर कौन नष्ट नहीं होता। नीच के मत के अनुसार चलने से चतुराई नहीं रह जाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2066.english_translation: Everyone in the city has the same wish, but Kaikeyi's heart burns with intense jealousy. Who does not get ruined by bad company? Wisdom does not remain when one follows the counsel of the base.
ramacharitamanas::2066.translation_literal: अस (such) / अभिलाषु (wish) / नगर (city) / सब (all) / काहू (of everyone) / कैकयसुता (daughter of Kaikeyi) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / अति (very) / दाहू (burning) / को (who) / न (not) / कुसंगति (bad company) / पाइ (having obtained) / नसाई (is ruined) / रहइ (remains) / न (not) / नीच (base) / मतें (in the counsel) / चतुराई (wisdom, discernment)
ramacharitamanas::2066.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2066.essence: Bad company burns away clear judgment before a person notices.
ramacharitamanas::2066.simple_meaning: The whole city wants one thing, but Kaikeyi is burning inside. Bad company ruins people, and following base advice destroys good judgment.
ramacharitamanas::2066.simple_insight: It warns how quickly a mind can be bent when it stays too close to the wrong influence.
ramacharitamanas::2066.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is calm on the surface, but Kaikeyi's heart is already inflamed by Manthara's influence. Tulsidas pauses the story to show a larger rule: bad company can twist judgment so completely that even intelligence disappears.
ramacharitamanas::2066.modern_relevance: You leave a conversation feeling oddly smaller, then realise someone has been feeding your worst suspicion for weeks. This verse names that slow corruption before it becomes your own voice.
ramacharitamanas::2066.insight: It shifts attention from the outward event to the hidden influence shaping the mind.

ramacharitamanas::2067.verse_sanskrit: साँझ समय सानंद नृपु गयउ कैकई गेहँ। गवनु निठुरता निकट किय जनु धरि देह सनेहँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2067.verse_hindi: संध्या के समय राजा दशरथ आनंद के साथ कैकेयी के महल में गए। मानो साक्षात स्नेह ही शरीर धारण कर निष्ठुरता के पास गया हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2067.english_translation: At dusk, King Dasharath went joyfully to Kaikeyi's palace. It was as if affection itself had taken a body and walked toward cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::2067.translation_literal: साँझ समय (at dusk) / सानंद (with joy) / नृपु (the king) / गयउ (went) / कैकई गेहँ (to Kaikeyi's house) / गवनु (going) / निठुरता (cruelty) / निकट (near) / किय (made) / जनु (as if) / धरि (having taken) / देह (body) / सनेहँ (affection)
ramacharitamanas::2067.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2067.essence: Affection can walk straight into cruelty without noticing the trap.
ramacharitamanas::2067.simple_meaning: Dasharath walks happily into Kaikeyi's palace, unaware that affection is entering the place where cruelty waits.
ramacharitamanas::2067.simple_insight: Trust can walk straight into betrayal and still not see it coming.
ramacharitamanas::2067.detailed_meaning: Dasharath goes to Kaikeyi's palace in the evening, still warm with trust. The couplet turns that innocent approach into a tragic image: love itself seems to be stepping toward hard-heartedness, just before the crisis of the exile begins.
ramacharitamanas::2067.modern_relevance: You walk into a familiar house smiling, carrying good news, and the room changes before you understand why. Sometimes the heart arrives before the danger does.
ramacharitamanas::2067.insight: It prepares the mind for betrayal by showing how trust can be blind to its own vulnerability.

ramacharitamanas::2068.verse_sanskrit: कोपभवन सुनि सकुचेउ राऊ। भय बस अगहुड़ परइ न पाऊ॥ सुरपति बसइ बाहँबल जाकें। नरपति सकल रहहिं रुख ताकें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2068.verse_hindi: कोप भवन का नाम सुनकर राजा सहम गए। डर के मारे उनका पाँव आगे को नहीं पड़ता। स्वयं देवराज इन्द्र जिनकी भुजाओं के बल पर (राक्षसों से निर्भय होकर) बसता है और सम्पूर्ण राजा लोग जिनका रुख देखते रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2068.english_translation: Hearing of the anger chamber, the king grew timid. In fear, his feet would not move forward. Even Indra lives by the strength of his arms, and all kings keep watching his face.
ramacharitamanas::2068.translation_literal: कोपभवन (anger chamber) / सुनि (hearing) / सकुचेउ (grew timid) / राऊ (the king) । भय (fear) / बस (under the control of) / अगहुड़ (forward) / परइ (falls) / न (not) / पाऊ (foot) ॥ सुरपति (lord of the gods, Indra) / बसइ (dwells) / बाहँबल (arm-strength) / जाकें (whose) / नरपति (kings) / सकल (all) / रहहिं (remain) / रुख (face/look) / ताकें (watching) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2068.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2068.essence: Fear can stop even the powerful before they speak.
ramacharitamanas::2068.simple_meaning: Dasharath hears of the anger chamber and loses his courage. Fear stops him, even though he is a powerful king.
ramacharitamanas::2068.simple_insight: Power means little when fear has already entered the mind.
ramacharitamanas::2068.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has gone to Kaikeyi’s chamber, and the atmosphere has turned tense. The king who commands others now hesitates at the doorway, while the narration reminds us that even great rulers depend on his strength. The scene prepares the emotional collapse that follows.
ramacharitamanas::2068.modern_relevance: You stand outside a room where a hard conversation is waiting. Your body knows before your mind admits it: one sentence inside could change everything.
ramacharitamanas::2068.insight: It shows how fear can shrink even the strongest person before any words are spoken.

ramacharitamanas::2069.verse_sanskrit: सो सुनि तिय रिस गयउ सुखाई। देखहु काम प्रताप बड़ाई॥ सूल कुलिस असि अँगवनिहारे। ते रतिनाथ सुमन सर मारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2069.verse_hindi: वही राजा दशरथ स्त्री का क्रोध सुनकर सूख गए। कामदेव का प्रताप और महिमा तो देखिए। जो त्रिशूल, वज्र और तलवार आदि की चोट अपने अंगों पर सहने वाले हैं, वे रतिनाथ कामदेव के पुष्पबाण से मारे गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2069.english_translation: Hearing her anger, King Dasharath withered away. See the greatness of Kamadeva's power. Those who bear tridents, thunderbolts, and swords on their bodies are struck by the flower-arrows of the lord of passion.
ramacharitamanas::2069.translation_literal: सो (that) / सुनि (hearing) / तिय (woman's) / रिस (anger) / गयउ (went) / सुखाई (withered) / देखहु (see) / काम (desire) / प्रताप (power) / बड़ाई (greatness) / सूल (trident) / कुलिस (thunderbolt) / असि (sword) / अँगवनिहारे (bearing on the body) / ते (those) / रतिनाथ (lord of desire) / सुमन (flower) / सर (arrows) / मारे (struck)
ramacharitamanas::2069.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2069.essence: Even the strongest body falls before an unsettled mind.
ramacharitamanas::2069.simple_meaning: Dasharath weakens at the sound of Kaikeyi's anger. The verse marvels that even the strongest beings can be pierced by desire's softest arrows.
ramacharitamanas::2069.simple_insight: Outer strength means little when the mind is already vulnerable.
ramacharitamanas::2069.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has entered Kaikeyi's chamber, and the air has turned dangerous. Hearing her anger, he loses his strength at once. Tulsidas pauses the scene to show a larger truth: even those hardened by battle can be overcome by desire.
ramacharitamanas::2069.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense conversation already tired, already hoping to keep the peace. One sharp tone from the other person and your resolve collapses before the real argument even begins.
ramacharitamanas::2069.insight: It shifts attention from physical strength to the mind's hidden weakness before desire and fear.

ramacharitamanas::2070.verse_sanskrit: सभय नरेसु प्रिया पहिं गयऊ। देखि दसा दुखु दारुन भयऊ॥ भूमि सयन पटु मोट पुराना। दिए डारि तन भूषन नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2070.verse_hindi: राजा डरते-डरते अपनी प्यारी कैकेयी के पास गए। उसकी दशा देखकर उन्हें बड़ा ही दुःख हुआ। कैकेयी जमीन पर पड़ी है। पुराना मोटा कपड़ा पहने हुए है। शरीर के नाना आभूषणों को उतारकर फेंक दिया है।
ramacharitamanas::2070.english_translation: The frightened king went to his beloved Kaikeyi. Seeing her condition, he was deeply grieved. Kaikeyi lay on the ground, wearing an old coarse cloth, having cast off all her ornaments.
ramacharitamanas::2070.translation_literal: सभय (fearfully) / नरेसु (the king) / प्रिया पहिं (to his beloved) / गयऊ (went) / देखि (seeing) / दसा (condition) / दुखु (grief) / दारुन (terrible) / भयऊ (became) / भूमि (ground) / सयन (lying) / पटु (cloth) / मोट (coarse) / पुराना (old) / दिए डारि (having thrown away) / तन (body) / भूषन (ornaments) / नाना (various)
ramacharitamanas::2070.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2070.essence: Fear and love meet in a single wounded glance.
ramacharitamanas::2070.simple_meaning: Dasharath goes anxiously to Kaikeyi and is pained by her miserable appearance. She lies on the floor in plain clothes, having removed her ornaments.
ramacharitamanas::2070.simple_insight: A loved one’s suffering can disarm even a powerful heart.
ramacharitamanas::2070.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has been shaken by Kaikeyi’s withdrawal into the anger chamber. He approaches her fearfully, and the sight of her on the ground in rough clothes deepens his distress. The scene prepares the next exchange of wounded words.
ramacharitamanas::2070.modern_relevance: You walk into a bedroom after an argument and find the other person curled on the floor, silent and wrecked. Your anger drops before the sight of their pain.
ramacharitamanas::2070.insight: It shifts attention from accusation to the raw human cost of conflict.

ramacharitamanas::2071.verse_sanskrit: कुमतिहि कसि कुबेषता फाबी। अनअहिवातु सूच जनु भाबी॥ जाइ निकट नृपु कह मृदु बानी। प्रानप्रिया केहि हेतु रिसानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2071.verse_hindi: उस दुर्बुद्धि कैकेयी को यह कुवेषता (बुरा वेष) कैसी फब रही है, मानो भावी विधवापन की सूचना दे रही हो। राजा उसके पास जाकर कोमल वाणी से बोले- हे प्राणप्रिये! किसलिए रिसाई (रूठी) हो? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2071.english_translation: Why does this ugly disguise suit the foolish-minded Kaikeyi so well, as if it were a sign of coming widowhood? The king went near her and spoke gently: "Beloved, why are you angry?"
ramacharitamanas::2071.translation_literal: कुमतिहि (to the foolish-minded one) / कसि (how) / कुबेषता (ugly disguise) / फाबी (suits well) / अनअहिवातु (widowhood-to-come) / सूच (sign) / जनु (as if) / भाबी (appeared) / जाइ (going) / निकट (near) / नृपु (the king) / कह (said) / मृदु बानी (gentle words) / प्रानप्रिया (beloved) / केहि हेतु (for what reason) / रिसानी (angry)
ramacharitamanas::2071.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2071.essence: Gentle speech can enter even a poisoned room.
ramacharitamanas::2071.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi’s harsh appearance seems like a bad omen, and Dasharath approaches her softly, asking why she is angry.
ramacharitamanas::2071.simple_insight: Even in hurt and confusion, gentleness is the first response.
ramacharitamanas::2071.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has gone to Kaikeyi’s chamber and found her lying in harsh, strange dress after her anger has taken hold. Seeing her, he is shaken and speaks tenderly, trying to understand what has upset her. This moment opens the door to the demand that will shatter his life.
ramacharitamanas::2071.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and instantly feel something is wrong. Instead of snapping back, you soften your voice and ask what hurt them. That is the king’s instinct here.
ramacharitamanas::2071.insight: It teaches you to meet conflict with calm speech before the damage deepens.

ramacharitamanas::2072.verse_sanskrit: केहि हेतु रानि रिसानि परसत पानि पतिहि नेवारई। मानहुँ सरोष भुअंग भामिनि बिषम भाँति निहारई॥ दोउ बासना रसना दसन बर मरम ठाहरु देखई। तुलसी नृपति भवतब्यता बस काम कौतुक लेखई॥
ramacharitamanas::2072.verse_hindi: 'हे रानी! किसलिए रूठी हो?' यह कहकर राजा उसे हाथ से स्पर्श करते हैं, तो वह उनके हाथ को (झटककर) हटा देती है और ऐसे देखती है मानो क्रोध में भरी हुई नागिन क्रूर दृष्टि से देख रही हो। दोनों (वरदानों की) वासनाएँ उस नागिन की दो जीभें हैं और दोनों वरदान दाँत हैं, वह काटने के लिए मर्मस्थान देख रही है। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि राजा दशरथ होनहार के वश में होकर इसे (इस प्रकार हाथ झटकने और नागिन की भाँति देखने को) कामदेव की क्रीड़ा ही समझ रहे हैं।
ramacharitamanas::2072.english_translation: “Why are you angry, queen?” When the king touches her hand, she pushes his hand away and looks at him like an enraged serpent. Her two desires are like that serpent’s two tongues, its two boons like its fangs, searching for a vital spot to strike. Tulsidas says the king, trapped by fate, mistakes this as a play of desire.
ramacharitamanas::2072.translation_literal: केहि हेतु (for what reason) / रानि (queen) / रिसानि (angry) / परसत (touching) / पानि (hand) / पतिहि (the husband/king) / नेवारई (pushes away) / मानहुँ (as if) / सरोष (full of anger) / भुअंग (serpent) / भामिनि (woman) / बिषम भाँति (strange manner) / निहारई (looks) / दोउ (both) / बासना (desires) / रसना (tongues) / दसन (teeth) / बर (boons) / मरम (vital spot) / ठाहरु (place) / देखई (sees) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / नृपति (king) / भवतब्यता (fate) / बस (under) / काम (desire) / कौतुक (play) / लेखई (considers)
ramacharitamanas::2072.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2072.essence: Blind trust turns a warning into a joke.
ramacharitamanas::2072.simple_meaning: Dasharath thinks Kaikeyi is merely angry, but her mind is already set on the two boons that will wound him. He cannot see the danger because desire has clouded his judgment.
ramacharitamanas::2072.simple_insight: It is painful to watch someone miss the warning signs because love or hope blinds them.
ramacharitamanas::2072.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath approaches Kaikeyi after finding her upset, still believing this is a small domestic quarrel. But Kaikeyi’s anger hides a deadly purpose: the two boons that will force Ram’s exile. The tragedy begins because the king cannot read what is in front of him.
ramacharitamanas::2072.modern_relevance: You keep reassuring yourself that a tense conversation is only moodiness, while the other person has already decided the outcome. The cost of misreading intention is often paid too late.
ramacharitamanas::2072.insight: It teaches you to notice when emotion is masking a deeper agenda, instead of assuming goodwill will explain everything.

ramacharitamanas::2073.verse_sanskrit: बार बार कह राउ सुमुखि सुलोचनि पिकबचनि। कारन मोहि सुनाउ गजगामिनि निज कोप कर ॥
ramacharitamanas::2073.verse_hindi: राजा बार-बार कह रहे हैं- हे सुमुखी! हे सुलोचनी! हे कोकिलबयनी! हे गजगामिनी! मुझे अपने क्रोध का कारण तो बताओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2073.english_translation: Again and again the king said, 'O fair-faced one, lovely-eyed one, voice like a cuckoo, graceful one, tell me the reason for your anger.'
ramacharitamanas::2073.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / कह (said) / राउ (the king) / सुमुखि (fair-faced one) / सुलोचनि (lovely-eyed one) / पिकबचनि (cuckoo-voiced one) / कारन (reason) / मोहि (to me) / सुनाउ (tell) / गजगामिनि (graceful one, with elephant-like gait) / निज (your own) / कोप (anger) / कर (of)
ramacharitamanas::2073.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2073.essence: Tender words cannot reach a heart already closed.
ramacharitamanas::2073.simple_meaning: Dasharath keeps gently asking Kaikeyi why she is angry and wants her to explain herself.
ramacharitamanas::2073.simple_insight: A soft voice can still stand helpless before a wall of anger.
ramacharitamanas::2073.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has come to Kaikeyi's chamber, unaware that her demand will destroy his world. He speaks to her with tenderness and repeated endearments, trying to understand her anger before the hidden crisis is revealed.
ramacharitamanas::2073.modern_relevance: You keep asking, softly, what went wrong in the conversation, while the other person stays cold and silent. The heartbreak is not the shouting; it is the refusal to explain.
ramacharitamanas::2073.insight: It shows a helpless attempt to restore intimacy by appealing to tenderness instead of force.

ramacharitamanas::2074.verse_sanskrit: अनहित तोर प्रिया केइँ कीन्हा। केहि दुइ सिर केहि जमु चह लीन्हा॥ कहु केहि रंकहि करौं नरेसू। कहु केहि नृपहि निकासौं देसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2074.verse_hindi: हे प्रिये! किसने तेरा अनिष्ट किया? किसके दो सिर हैं? यमराज किसको लेना (अपने लोक को ले जाना) चाहते हैं? कह, किस कंगाल को राजा कर दूँ या किस राजा को देश से निकाल दूँ? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2074.english_translation: Beloved, who has wronged you? Who has two heads? Which Yama wants to take away? Tell me, which beggar should I make king, or which king should I drive from the land?
ramacharitamanas::2074.translation_literal: अनहित (harm) / तोर (your) / प्रिया (beloved) / केइँ (who) / कीन्हा (did) / केहि (whom) / दुइ (two) / सिर (heads) / केहि (whom) / जमु (Yama) / चह (wants) / लीन्हा (to take) // कहु (tell) / केहि (which) / रंकहि (beggar) / करौं (shall I make) / नरेसू (king) / कहु (tell) / केहि (which) / नृपहि (king) / निकासौं (shall I expel) / देसू (from the land)
ramacharitamanas::2074.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2074.essence: Love, once shaken, can make a king beg like a child.
ramacharitamanas::2074.simple_meaning: Dasharath begs Kaikeyi to explain her anger and offers impossible rewards to whoever she names. He is trying to calm her, not teaching a principle by itself.
ramacharitamanas::2074.simple_insight: Desperation can make a person promise anything just to restore love.
ramacharitamanas::2074.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath stands before Kaikeyi after her sudden anger. He pleads, flatters, and offers absurd bargains to win back her favor, not yet knowing that her demand will send Ram into exile and break the kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::2074.modern_relevance: Someone you love goes cold for reasons you cannot understand. You start bargaining, apologising, promising anything — because the silence feels unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2074.insight: It shows how attachment can make power look helpless and turn speech into pleading.

ramacharitamanas::2075.verse_sanskrit: सकउँ तोर अरि अमरउ मारी। काह कीट बपुरे नर नारी॥ जानसि मोर सुभाउ बरोरू। मनु तव आनन चंद चकोरू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2075.verse_hindi: तेरा शत्रु अमर (देवता) भी हो, तो मैं उसे भी मार सकता हूँ। बेचारे कीड़े-मकोड़े सरीखे नर-नारी तो चीज ही क्या हैं। हे सुंदरी! तू तो मेरा स्वभाव जानती ही है कि मेरा मन सदा तेरे मुख रूपी चन्द्रमा का चकोर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2075.english_translation: I could even kill your enemy if he were immortal. What are mere human beings? You know my nature well, fair one: my mind is always a chakora bird to your moonlike face.
ramacharitamanas::2075.translation_literal: सकउँ (I could) / तोर (your) / अरि (enemy) / अमरउ (even immortal) / मारी (kill) / काह (what) / कीट (insects) / बपुरे (poor wretches) / नर नारी (men and women) / जानसि (you know) / मोर (my) / सुभाउ (nature) / बरोरू (fair one) / मनु (mind) / तव (your) / आनन (face) / चंद (moon) / चकोरू (chakora bird)
ramacharitamanas::2075.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::2075.simple_meaning: Ravana boasts that he could kill even an immortal enemy, dismisses ordinary people as insignificant, and says his mind is fixed on Mandodari’s face like a bird on the moon.
ramacharitamanas::2075.simple_insight: Pride makes everything smaller except the self-image it feeds.
ramacharitamanas::2075.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trying to placate and impress Mandodari after his harsh words. Instead of softening, he inflates his power, mocks human life, and turns his desire into poetry. The scene reveals his ego before the collapse that follows.
ramacharitamanas::2075.modern_relevance: A person in a heated argument starts talking like no one else matters and every problem is beneath them. The louder the boasting gets, the more fragile the ego underneath it looks.
ramacharitamanas::2075.insight: It exposes how desire and arrogance can dress themselves up as confidence.

ramacharitamanas::2076.verse_sanskrit: प्रिया प्रान सुत सरबसु मोरें। परिजन प्रजा सकल बस तोरें॥ जौं कछु कहौं कपटु करि तोही। भामिनि राम सपथ सत मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2076.verse_hindi: हे प्रिये! मेरी प्रजा, कुटम्बी, सर्वस्व (सम्पत्ति), पुत्र, यहाँ तक कि मेरे प्राण भी, ये सब तेरे वश में (अधीन) हैं। यदि मैं तुझसे कुछ कपट करके कहता होऊँ तो हे भामिनी! मुझे सौ बार राम की सौगंध है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2076.english_translation: My beloved, my life, my son, my everything, my family, my people, and all my wealth are under your control. If I speak deceitfully to you, then, O beautiful one, may I be struck a hundred times by Ram's oath.
ramacharitamanas::2076.translation_literal: प्रिया (beloved) / प्रान (life) / सुत (son) / सरबसु (everything, all wealth) / मोरें (of mine) / परिजन (family) / प्रजा (subjects, people) / सकल (all) / बस (under control) / तोरें (of yours) / जौं (if) / कछु (something) / कहौं (I say) / कपटु (deceit) / करि (doing) / तोही (to you) / भामिनि (beautiful one) / राम (Ram) / सपथ (oath) / सत (hundred) / मोही (to me)
ramacharitamanas::2076.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::2076.essence: Flattery can wear the mask of devotion while hiding coercion.
ramacharitamanas::2076.simple_meaning: Ravana claims that everything he values is under Sita's control, and he swears by Ram that he is not lying.
ramacharitamanas::2076.simple_insight: Charm can sound like surrender while still hiding control.
ramacharitamanas::2076.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana keeps flattering Sita while trying to soften her resistance. He says his life, family, subjects, and wealth are all hers, then swears by Ram to sound sincere. The verse is part of his manipulative persuasion, not a true confession.
ramacharitamanas::2076.modern_relevance: Someone floods your inbox with praise, then asks for a favor that crosses a line. The warmth is real in the words, but the pressure underneath is the point.
ramacharitamanas::2076.insight: It exposes how language can be used to disarm judgment before a harmful demand.

ramacharitamanas::2077.verse_sanskrit: बिहसि मागु मनभावति बाता। भूषन सजहि मनोहर गाता॥। घरी कुघरी समुझि जियँ देखू। बेगि प्रिया परिहरहि कुबेषू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2077.verse_hindi: तू हँसकर (प्रसन्नतापूर्वक) अपनी मनचाही बात माँग ले और अपने मनोहर अंगों को आभूषणों से सजा। मौका-बेमौका तो मन में विचार कर देख। हे प्रिये! जल्दी इस बुरे वेष को त्याग दे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2077.english_translation: Smilingly ask for whatever pleases your mind, and adorn your beautiful body with ornaments. Consider the right and wrong time in your heart. Dear one, quickly give up this ugly disguise.
ramacharitamanas::2077.translation_literal: बिहसि (smilingly) / मागु (ask) / मनभावति (pleasing to the mind) / बाता (thing, request) / भूषन (ornaments) / सजहि (adorn) / मनोहर (beautiful, charming) / गाता (body) / घरी (time) / कुघरी (bad time, wrong time) / समुझि (understanding) / जियँ (in the heart) / देखू (see, consider) / बेगि (quickly) / प्रिया (dear one) / परिहरहि (give up, abandon) / कुबेषू (ugly disguise)
ramacharitamanas::2077.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2077.essence: Love can make a person bless the very harm that will destroy him.
ramacharitamanas::2077.simple_meaning: Dasharath, still under Kaikeyi's influence, speaks gently and tells her to ask for what she wants, dress well, and quickly drop the harsh disguise she has worn.
ramacharitamanas::2077.simple_insight: A tender tone can hide a devastating mistake.
ramacharitamanas::2077.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is speaking to Kaikeyi as her demands begin to unfold. He still thinks he is soothing his beloved queen, not realizing that her request will break his family and send Ram into exile.
ramacharitamanas::2077.modern_relevance: You smile at someone you trust, trying to keep the mood light, while missing the damage already taking shape in the room.
ramacharitamanas::2077.insight: It shows how affection and blindness can coexist, making a person unable to see danger even while naming it.

ramacharitamanas::2078.verse_sanskrit: यह सुनि मन गुनि सपथ बड़ि बिहसि उठी मतिमंद। भूषन सजति बिलोकिमृगु मनहुँ किरातिनि फंद ॥
ramacharitamanas::2078.verse_hindi: यह सुनकर और मन में रामजी की बड़ी सौंगंध को विचारकर मंदबुद्धि कैकेयी हँसती हुई उठी और गहने पहनने लगी, मानो कोई भीलनी मृग को देखकर फंदा तैयार कर रही हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2078.english_translation: Hearing this and reflecting on Ram's great oath in her mind, the foolish Kaikeyi rose laughing and began putting on ornaments, like a hunter-woman setting a snare after seeing a deer.
ramacharitamanas::2078.translation_literal: यह (this) / सुनि (hearing) / मन (mind) / गुनि (reflecting) / सपथ (oath) / बड़ि (great) / बिहसि (laughing) / उठी (rose) / मतिमंद (foolish, dull-witted) / भूषन (ornaments) / सजति (adorning) / बिलोकिमृगु (seeing the deer) / मनहुँ (as if) / किरातिनि (hunter-woman) / फंद (snare)
ramacharitamanas::2078.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2078.essence: A trapped mind can hear honesty and still prepare betrayal.
ramacharitamanas::2078.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi hears Ram's oath, thinks about it, and laughs as she puts on ornaments. The verse compares her to a hunter preparing a trap.
ramacharitamanas::2078.simple_insight: A mind ruled by desire can turn even trust into a weapon.
ramacharitamanas::2078.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has just heard Dasharath speak with great confidence and oath-bound sincerity. Instead of softening, she smiles and dresses herself, already preparing the trap that will break the royal family.
ramacharitamanas::2078.modern_relevance: Someone hears a sincere apology, nods, and quietly plans the next move anyway. The face is calm, but the mind is already loading the trap.
ramacharitamanas::2078.insight: It exposes how cunning works: hearing truth without being changed by it.

ramacharitamanas::2079.verse_sanskrit: पुनि कह राउ सुहृद जियँ जानी। प्रेम पुलकि मृदु मंजुल बानी॥ भामिनि भयउ तोर मनभावा। घर घर नगर अनंद बधावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2079.verse_hindi: अपने जी में कैकेयी को सुहृद् जानकर राजा दशरथजी प्रेम से पुलकित होकर कोमल और सुंदर वाणी से फिर बोले- हे भामिनि! तेरे मन का ही होगा। नगर में घर-घर आनंद के बधावे बज रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2079.english_translation: King Dasharath, seeing Kaikeyi as a friend in his heart, spoke again with love, his body thrilled, in soft and lovely words: “O beautiful one, whatever is in your heart will happen. In every house of the city, songs of joy are being sung.”
ramacharitamanas::2079.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / कह (spoke) / राउ (the king) / सुहृद (friend) / जियँ (in heart) / जानी (knowing) / प्रेम (love) / पुलकि (thrilled) / मृदु (soft) / मंजुल (lovely) / बानी (speech) / भामिनि (O beautiful one) / भयउ (became) / तोर (your) / मनभावा (heart's wish) / घर घर (house by house) / नगर (city) / अनंद (joy) / बधावा (songs of celebration)
ramacharitamanas::2079.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2079.essence: Warm trust can make a king blind to danger.
ramacharitamanas::2079.simple_meaning: Dasharath speaks gently to Kaikeyi, trusting her as a friend and saying he will grant what she wants. He believes the city is already celebrating.
ramacharitamanas::2079.simple_insight: Trust can make a person speak with complete softness right before tragedy begins.
ramacharitamanas::2079.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is still unaware of the trap closing around him. He sees Kaikeyi as dear and trustworthy, speaks affectionately, and assumes the city’s joy is shared by his household. The next verse reveals how badly he misreads the moment.
ramacharitamanas::2079.modern_relevance: You’re speaking warmly to someone you trust, unaware they are about to ask for something that will split your life open. The heartbreak is not in the shouting; it begins in the softness.
ramacharitamanas::2079.insight: It shows how affection without discernment can leave a person exposed to manipulation.

ramacharitamanas::2080.verse_sanskrit: रामहि देउँ कालि जुबराजू। सजहि सुलोचनि मंगल साजू॥ दलकि उठेउ सुनि हृदउ कठोरू। जनु छुइ गयउ पाक बरतोरू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2080.verse_hindi: मैं कल ही राम को युवराज पद दे रहा हूँ, इसलिए हे सुनयनी! तू मंगल साज सज। यह सुनते ही उसका कठोर हृदय दलक उठा (फटने लगा)। मानो पका हुआ बालतोड़ (फोड़ा) छू गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2080.english_translation: I will give Ram the crown prince’s seat tomorrow. O beautiful-eyed one, prepare the auspicious ornaments. Hearing this, her hard heart split open, like a ripe boil touched by a hand.
ramacharitamanas::2080.translation_literal: रामहि (to Ram) / देउँ (I will give) / कालि (tomorrow) / जुबराजू (crown princehood) / सजहि (prepare) / सुलोचनि (beautiful-eyed one) / मंगल (auspicious) / साजू (ornaments / preparations) / दलकि (split open) / उठेउ (rose up) / सुनि (having heard) / हृदउ (heart) / कठोरू (hard) / जनु (as if) / छुइ (touched) / गयउ (went) / पाक (ripe) / बरतोरू (boil / swelling)
ramacharitamanas::2080.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2080.simple_meaning: Dasharath announces that Ram will be crowned tomorrow. Kaikeyi’s heart, hardened by desire, breaks open in pain and shock.
ramacharitamanas::2080.simple_insight: A hidden demand can shatter the very person who made it.
ramacharitamanas::2080.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath, still speaking warmly to Kaikeyi, says he will crown Ram the next day and asks her to prepare for celebration. The news strikes her like a wound opening, revealing how far her mind has already turned.
ramacharitamanas::2080.modern_relevance: You hear a promotion, a wedding plan, or a family decision and realize someone in the room is not celebrating. Their silence suddenly feels dangerous.
ramacharitamanas::2080.insight: It exposes how a heart hardened by craving can react violently to joy it does not want.

ramacharitamanas::2081.verse_sanskrit: ऐसिउ पीर बिहसि तेहिं गोई। चोर नारि जिमि प्रगटि न रोई॥ लखहिं न भूप कपट चतुराई। कोटि कुटिल मनि गुरू पढ़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2081.verse_hindi: ऐसी भारी पीड़ा को भी उसने हँसकर छिपा लिया, जैसे चोर की स्त्री प्रकट होकर नहीं रोती (जिसमें उसका भेद न खुल जाए)। राजा उसकी कपट-चतुराई को नहीं लख रहे हैं, क्योंकि वह करोड़ों कुटिलों की शिरोमणि गुरु मंथरा की पढ़ाई हुई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2081.english_translation: She hid even that intense pain with a smile, like a thief's wife who does not cry in public so her secret is not exposed. The king does not see her deceitful cunning, because she was taught by Manthara, the teacher of millions of crooked minds.
ramacharitamanas::2081.translation_literal: ऐसिउ (even such) / पीर (pain) / बिहसि (smiling) / तेहिं (she) / गोई (hid) / चोर (thief) / नारि (wife) / जिमि (like) / प्रगटि (appearing) / न (not) / रोई (cries)॥ / लखहिं (perceives) / न (not) / भूप (king) / कपट (deceit) / चतुराई (cunning) / कोटि (millions) / कुटिल (crooked) / मनि (mind) / गुरू (teacher) / पढ़ाई (taught)॥
ramacharitamanas::2081.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2081.essence: A smiling face can conceal a mind already captured by deceit.
ramacharitamanas::2081.simple_meaning: She hides her pain behind a smile so her deceit is not exposed. The king still cannot see her cunning.
ramacharitamanas::2081.simple_insight: A polished face can hide a restless mind. Not everything that smiles is honest.
ramacharitamanas::2081.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has already been stirred by Manthara's scheme. Dasharath speaks kindly, unaware that her grief and ambition are being masked by a careful smile. The verse shows deception working beneath family intimacy.
ramacharitamanas::2081.modern_relevance: Someone laughs at the dinner table after a harsh text just arrived, then keeps the conversation moving. Everyone sees calm; no one sees the plan forming underneath.
ramacharitamanas::2081.insight: It trains attention on hidden motive, not visible politeness. The mind learns to look beneath performance.

ramacharitamanas::2082.verse_sanskrit: जद्यपि नीति निपुन नरनाहू। नारिचरित जलनिधि अवगाहू॥ कपट सनेहु बढ़ाई बहोरी। बोली बिहसि नयन मुहु मोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2082.verse_hindi: यद्यपि राजा नीति में निपुण हैं, परन्तु त्रियाचरित्र अथाह समुद्र है। फिर वह कपटयुक्त प्रेम बढ़ाकर (ऊपर से प्रेम दिखाकर) नेत्र और मुँह मोड़कर हँसती हुई बोली- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2082.english_translation: Although the king is skilled in policy, a woman's conduct is an unfathomable sea. She then increased her pretended affection and, turning her eyes and face away, spoke with a smile.
ramacharitamanas::2082.translation_literal: जद्यपि (although) / नीति (policy, conduct) / निपुन (skilled) / नरनाहू (king) / नारिचरित (woman's conduct) / जलनिधि (ocean) / अवगाहू (unfathomable) / कपट (deceitful) / सनेहु (affection) / बढ़ाई (increased) / बहोरी (again) / बोली (spoke) / बिहसि (smiling) / नयन (eyes) / मुहु (face) / मोरी (turned away)
ramacharitamanas::2082.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2082.essence: Charm can conceal intention better than force.
ramacharitamanas::2082.simple_meaning: Even a wise king can be fooled when deceit is wrapped in a smile. The verse shows a hidden intention behind outward affection.
ramacharitamanas::2082.simple_insight: A polished face can hide a dangerous motive. Clear seeing matters more than charm.
ramacharitamanas::2082.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has already been wounded by the news of Ram's coronation. The court still sees a queen speaking sweetly, but behind that smile she is preparing the demand that will shatter Dasharath's house.
ramacharitamanas::2082.modern_relevance: Someone says, “Of course I’m happy for you,” while their jaw is tight and their eyes won’t meet yours. The words sound gentle, but the room has already changed.
ramacharitamanas::2082.insight: It trains the mind to look past performance and notice the motive underneath.

ramacharitamanas::2083.verse_sanskrit: मागु मागु पै कहहु पिय कबहुँ न देहु न लेहु। देन कहेहु बरदान दुइ तेउ पावत संदेहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2083.verse_hindi: हे प्रियतम! आप माँग-माँग तो कहा करते हैं, पर देते-लेते कभी कुछ भी नहीं। आपने दो वरदान देने को कहा था, उनके भी मिलने में संदेह है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2083.english_translation: Beloved, you keep saying, “Ask, ask,” yet you never truly give or take. You spoke of granting two boons, but even that seems uncertain.
ramacharitamanas::2083.translation_literal: मागु (ask) / मागु (ask) / पै (indeed) / कहहु (you say) / पिय (beloved) / कबहुँ (ever) / न (not) / देहु (give) / न (not) / लेहु (take) / देन (giving) / कहेहु (you said) / बरदान (boons) / दुइ (two) / तेउ (those too) / पावत (getting) / संदेहु (doubt)
ramacharitamanas::2083.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2083.essence: Empty offers breed suspicion, not peace.
ramacharitamanas::2083.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi speaks bitterly to Dasharath, saying he keeps urging her to ask, yet never truly gives anything. Even the promised two boons now feel doubtful to her.
ramacharitamanas::2083.simple_insight: Desire makes the mind suspicious, even of what it was promised.
ramacharitamanas::2083.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi turns from soft words to complaint. She accuses Dasharath of saying “ask” while withholding true giving, and she doubts even the two boons he once promised. The exchange reveals how distrust has already poisoned the royal household.
ramacharitamanas::2083.modern_relevance: A partner says, “Tell me what you need,” but every time you do, they change the subject. After a while, even their promises start to sound empty.
ramacharitamanas::2083.insight: It exposes a mind that can no longer trust words, only motives.

ramacharitamanas::2084.verse_sanskrit: जानेउँ मरमु राउ हँसि कहई। तुम्हहि कोहाब परम प्रिय अहई॥ थाती राखि न मागिहु काऊ। बिसरि गयउ मोहि भोर सुभाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2084.verse_hindi: राजा ने हँसकर कहा कि अब मैं तुम्हारा मर्म (मतलब) समझा। मान करना तुम्हें परम प्रिय है। तुमने उन वरों को थाती (धरोहर) रखकर फिर कभी माँगा ही नहीं और मेरा भूलने का स्वभाव होने से मुझे भी वह प्रसंग याद नहीं रहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2084.english_translation: The king laughed and said, 'Now I understand your meaning. Pride is what you love most. You kept those boons as a stored treasure and never asked for them again, and because I forget easily, I also forgot that matter.'
ramacharitamanas::2084.translation_literal: जानेउँ (I understood) / मरमु (the meaning, the hidden point) / राउ (the king) / हँसि (laughing) / कहई (said) / तुम्हहि (you) / कोहाब (pride, anger) / परम प्रिय (most प्रिय, most beloved) / अहई (is) ॥ थाती (stored treasure) / राखि (having kept) / न मागिहु (you did not ask) / काऊ (at all) / बिसरि (forgotten) / गयउ (went) / मोहि (to me) / भोर (morning / early) / सुभाऊ (nature) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2084.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2084.essence: Silence can hide pride until it becomes a wound.
ramacharitamanas::2084.simple_meaning: The king says he now sees the other person’s real intention: they value pride most, kept the boons unused, and never brought them up again. He also says he forgot about them because of his own forgetful nature.
ramacharitamanas::2084.simple_insight: Hidden motives surface when patience runs out. What was left unspoken begins to shape the whole exchange.
ramacharitamanas::2084.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi’s old boons have come back into play, and Dasharath is trying to make sense of the conversation that led to Ram’s exile. Here he speaks with bitter irony, reading her silence as pride and realizing too late how the forgotten promise has trapped everyone.
ramacharitamanas::2084.modern_relevance: A family argument suddenly turns cold: one person says, 'So that’s what this was really about.' The hurt is not just the request — it is the years of silence that made the request feel like a trap.
ramacharitamanas::2084.insight: It shifts attention from the spoken demand to the motive beneath it, showing how unspoken pride can harden into conflict.

ramacharitamanas::2085.verse_sanskrit: झूठेहुँ हमहि दोषु जनि देहू। दुइ कै चारि मागि मकु लेहू॥ रघुकुल रीति सदा चलि आई। प्रान जाहुँ परु बचनु न जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2085.verse_hindi: मुझे झूठ-मूठ दोष मत दो। चाहे दो के बदले चार माँग लो। रघुकुल में सदा से यह रीति चली आई है कि प्राण भले ही चले जाएँ, पर वचन नहीं जाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2085.english_translation: Do not wrongly blame me. Ask for four instead of two if you wish. The Raghus have always kept this rule: life may go, but a promise does not.
ramacharitamanas::2085.translation_literal: झूठेहुँ (even falsely) / हमहि (to me) / दोषु (blame) / जनि (do not) / देहू (give) / दुइ (two) / कै (instead of) / चारि (four) / मागि (ask) / मकु (perhaps) / लेहू (take) / रघुकुल (the Raghu clan) / रीति (custom) / सदा (always) / चलि आई (has continued) / प्रान (life) / जाहुँ (may go) / परु (but) / बचनु (promise/word) / न (not) / जाई (goes)
ramacharitamanas::2085.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2085.essence: A true promise is kept even when it costs everything.
ramacharitamanas::2085.simple_meaning: A promise matters more than life itself. The royal line of Raghu is defined by keeping one’s word, even at the highest cost.
ramacharitamanas::2085.simple_insight: Integrity feels costly here, but it also feels clean. A kept promise can be heavier than survival and still be worth it.
ramacharitamanas::2085.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is trapped by his own past promise and Kaikeyi's demand. He insists that the Raghu line never breaks its word, even if it costs life itself. This verse turns royal duty into a moral law.
ramacharitamanas::2085.modern_relevance: You told your child you'd show up, then the meeting ran late and the excuse came easily. This verse remembers the cost of saying yes and the dignity of still arriving.
ramacharitamanas::2085.insight: It shifts the mind from convenience to covenant: what you promised becomes more important than what is easiest now.

ramacharitamanas::2086.verse_sanskrit: नहिं असत्य सम पातक पुंजा। गिरि सम होहिं कि कोटिक गुंजा॥ सत्यमूल सब सुकृत सुहाए। बेद पुरान बिदित मनु गाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2086.verse_hindi: असत्य के समान पापों का समूह भी नहीं है। क्या करोड़ों घुँघचियाँ मिलकर भी कहीं पहाड़ के समान हो सकती हैं। 'सत्य' ही समस्त उत्तम सुकृतों (पुण्यों) की जड़ है। यह बात वेद-पुराणों में प्रसिद्ध है और मनुजी ने भी यही कहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2086.english_translation: No heap of sins is equal to falsehood. Can millions of tiny shells ever become a mountain? Truth is the root of all noble deeds. The Vedas, Puranas, and Manu declare this.
ramacharitamanas::2086.translation_literal: नहिं (not) / असत्य (falsehood) / सम (equal to) / पातक पुंजा (heap of sins) / गिरि (mountain) / सम (like) / होहिं (become) / कि (whether) / कोटिक (millions) / गुंजा (tiny shells) / सत्यमूल (rooted in truth) / सब (all) / सुकृत (noble deeds) / सुहाए (beautiful) / बेद (Vedas) / पुरान (Puranas) / बिदित (known) / मनु (Manu) / गाए (have said)
ramacharitamanas::2086.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2086.essence: Falsehood corrupts everything; truth gives every good act its root.
ramacharitamanas::2086.simple_meaning: Falsehood is the worst corruption, and truth is the source of every good action. The verse says this is a timeless principle taught by tradition.
ramacharitamanas::2086.simple_insight: It leaves you with respect for honesty as a foundation, not just a rule.
ramacharitamanas::2086.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is pressing Kaikeyi’s side of the crisis, and the argument has reached a moral edge. The verse steps back from the drama and declares that falsehood ruins everything, while truth is the source of every worthy act.
ramacharitamanas::2086.modern_relevance: You are about to send a message that hides the real reason, hoping it will make things easier. The verse cuts through that impulse: once truth is bent, the whole act is weakened from the root.
ramacharitamanas::2086.insight: It shifts the mind from treating honesty as optional to seeing it as the base of all right action.

ramacharitamanas::2087.verse_sanskrit: तेहि पर राम सपथ करि आई। सुकृत सनेह अवधि रघुराई॥ बाद दृढ़ाइ कुमति हँसि बोली। कुमत कुबिहग कुलह जनु खोली ॥
ramacharitamanas::2087.verse_hindi: उस पर मेरे द्वारा श्री रामजी की शपथ करने में आ गई (मुँह से निकल पड़ी)। श्री रघुनाथजी मेरे सुकृत (पुण्य) और स्नेह की सीमा हैं। इस प्रकार बात पक्की कराके दुर्बुद्धि कैकेयी हँसकर बोली, मानो उसने कुमत (बुरे विचार) रूपी दुष्ट पक्षी (बाज) (को छोड़ने के लिए उस) की कुलही (आँखों पर की टोपी) खोल दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2087.english_translation: Then, by invoking Ram's name, she spoke. Raghunath is the limit of my merit and affection. Having firmly fixed the matter, the foolish woman laughed, as if she had opened the hood to release a cruel hawk of evil intent.
ramacharitamanas::2087.translation_literal: तेहि पर (then, upon that) / राम (Ram) / सपथ करि (having sworn by) / आई (came out, spoke) / सुकृत (merit, good deed) / सनेह (affection, love) / अवधि (limit, boundary) / रघुराई (Raghunath) / बाद (then, afterward) / दृढ़ाइ (having made firm) / कुमति (foolish intent) / हँसि (laughing) / बोली (spoke) / कुमत (bad thought) / कुबिहग (evil bird, hawk) / कुलह (hood, covering) / जनु (as if) / खोली (opened)
ramacharitamanas::2087.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2087.essence: A corrupted mind can use sacred words to fasten its own harm.
ramacharitamanas::2087.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi brings Ram's name into her oath, then laughs after securing her demand. Her hardened mind is shown as if it has opened a hood and released a dangerous bird of bad intent.
ramacharitamanas::2087.simple_insight: A fixed mind can turn sacred words into a tool for harm.
ramacharitamanas::2087.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has already been pulled into Manthara's scheme. She uses Ram's name to seal the demand that will exile him, then laughs as the plan locks into place. The verse shows the moment her bad judgment fully opens.
ramacharitamanas::2087.modern_relevance: You say a promise is for the best, but some hidden part of you is already smiling at the damage it will do. The harm begins the moment you stop questioning your own motive.
ramacharitamanas::2087.insight: It exposes how self-deception can dress itself in noble language and still push a harmful decision forward.

ramacharitamanas::2088.verse_sanskrit: भूप मनोरथ सुभग बनु सुख सुबिहंग समाजु। भिल्लिनि जिमि छाड़न चहति बचनु भयंकरु बाजु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2088.verse_hindi: राजा का मनोरथ सुंदर वन है, सुख सुंदर पक्षियों का समुदाय है। उस पर भीलनी की तरह कैकेयी अपना वचन रूपी भयंकर बाज छोड़ना चाहती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2088.english_translation: The king's wish is a beautiful forest, and the company of joy is like lovely birds. Yet Kaikeyi, like a huntress, wants to release the terrible arrow of her vow.
ramacharitamanas::2088.translation_literal: भूप (king) / मनोरथ (wish) / सुभग (beautiful) / बनु (forest) / सुख (joy) / सुबिहंग (beautiful birds) / समाजु (assembly) / भिल्लिनि (huntress woman) / जिमि (like) / छाड़न (to release) / चहति (wants) / बचनु (word/vow) / भयंकरु (terrible) / बाजु (arrow)
ramacharitamanas::2088.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2088.essence: A beautiful order can be broken by one spoken vow.
ramacharitamanas::2088.simple_meaning: Dasharath's hopes are pictured as a peaceful forest full of beauty and joy, but Kaikeyi is about to unleash a cruel promise like a deadly arrow.
ramacharitamanas::2088.simple_insight: A single vow can turn a whole life from harmony into ruin.
ramacharitamanas::2088.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath's court seems full of beauty and order, but Kaikeyi is preparing to speak the demand that will shatter it. Tulsidas compares her vow to a hunter's arrow, showing how one sentence can wound an entire family.
ramacharitamanas::2088.modern_relevance: A quiet dinner can change in one sentence. Someone says the thing they've been holding back, and the room goes cold. You can feel the moment before the damage lands.
ramacharitamanas::2088.insight: It shows how hidden intention can sit inside calm appearances until one decisive word releases it.

ramacharitamanas::2089.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु प्रानप्रिय भावत जी का। देहु एक बर भरतहि टीका॥ मागउँ दूसर बर कर जोरी। पुरवहु नाथ मनोरथ मोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2089.verse_hindi: (वह बोली-) हे प्राण प्यारे! सुनिए, मेरे मन को भाने वाला एक वर तो दीजिए, भरत को राजतिलक और हे नाथ! दूसरा वर भी मैं हाथ जोड़कर माँगती हूँ, मेरा मनोरथ पूरा कीजिए- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2089.english_translation: “Listen, my dear life, grant one boon that pleases me: give the coronation to Bharata. And, my lord, I ask for a second boon with folded hands: fulfill my wish.”
ramacharitamanas::2089.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / प्रानप्रिय (dear to life) / भावत (pleasing) / जी (my lord) / का (what) / देहु (give) / एक (one) / बर (boon) / भरतहि (to Bharata) / टीका (coronation)॥ / मागउँ (I ask) / दूसर (second) / बर (boon) / कर (hand) / जोरी (joined) / पुरवहु (fulfill) / नाथ (lord) / मनोरथ (wish) / मोरी (my) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2089.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2089.essence: A gentle request can conceal a devastating demand.
ramacharitamanas::2089.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi asks Dasharath to give Bharata the coronation and to fulfill a second wish she is about to name.
ramacharitamanas::2089.simple_insight: A wish can sound gentle and still carry a whole disaster inside it.
ramacharitamanas::2089.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi stands before Dasharath after her mind has been turned by Manthara. With folded hands and a sweet voice, she asks for Bharata's coronation and prepares to reveal the second boon that will drive Ram into exile.
ramacharitamanas::2089.modern_relevance: A message sounds polite, almost tender, but the real demand is hidden beneath it. The calm tone makes the blow harder when it lands.
ramacharitamanas::2089.insight: It shows how desire can wear a soft face while setting tragedy in motion.

ramacharitamanas::2090.verse_sanskrit: तापस बेष बिसेषि उदासी। चौदह बरिस रामु बनबासी॥ सुनि मृदु बचन भूप हियँ सोकू। ससि कर छुअत बिकल जिमि कोकू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2090.verse_hindi: तपस्वियों के वेष में विशेष उदासीन भाव से (राज्य और कुटुम्ब आदि की ओर से भलीभाँति उदासीन होकर विरक्त मुनियों की भाँति) राम चौदह वर्ष तक वन में निवास करें। कैकेयी के कोमल (विनययुक्त) वचन सुनकर राजा के हृदय में ऐसा शोक हुआ जैसे चन्द्रमा की किरणों के स्पर्श से चकवा विकल हो जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2090.english_translation: Ram will live in the forest for fourteen years, dressed like an ascetic and turned away from home and kingdom. Hearing Kaikeyi's gentle words, the king's heart filled with sorrow, like a chakravak bird struck by moonlight.
ramacharitamanas::2090.translation_literal: तापस (ascetic) / बेष (dress) / बिसेषि (especially) / उदासी (detached) / चौदह (fourteen) / बरिस (years) / रामु (Ram) / बनबासी (forest-dweller) / सुनि (hearing) / मृदु (gentle) / बचन (words) / भूप (king) / हियँ (in the heart) / सोकू (sorrow) / ससि (moon) / कर (ray) / छुअत (touching) / बिकल (distressed) / जिमि (like) / कोकू (chakravak bird)
ramacharitamanas::2090.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2090.essence: A spoken boon becomes a king's deepest grief.
ramacharitamanas::2090.simple_meaning: Ram is to live in the forest for fourteen years, dressed like an ascetic and detached from royal life. Hearing this, Dasharath is overwhelmed with grief.
ramacharitamanas::2090.simple_insight: A promise can cost everything, and the cost is felt most by the one who must keep it.
ramacharitamanas::2090.detailed_meaning: Kaikeyi has just asked for her boons. One boon sends Ram into exile for fourteen years, dressed as a forest ascetic. The other crowns Bharat. Dasharath hears the demand and collapses inward, struck by grief before he can even respond.
ramacharitamanas::2090.modern_relevance: You read a message that changes a family forever. One sentence redirects a whole life, and the person who must honor it feels the blow first.
ramacharitamanas::2090.insight: It shifts attention from the words spoken to the life-altering duty those words impose.

ramacharitamanas::2091.verse_sanskrit: गयउ सहमि नहिं कछु कहि आवा। जनु सचान बन झपटेउ लावा॥ बिबरन भयउ निपट नरपालू। दामिनि हनेउ मनहुँ तरु तालू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2091.verse_hindi: राजा सहम गए, उनसे कुछ कहते न बना मानो बाज वन में बटेर पर झपटा हो। राजा का रंग बिलकुल उड़ गया, मानो ताड़ के पेड़ को बिजली ने मारा हो (जैसे ताड़ के पेड़ पर बिजली गिरने से वह झुलसकर बदरंगा हो जाता है, वही हाल राजा का हुआ) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2091.english_translation: The king was stunned and could say nothing, as if a hawk had pounced on a quail in the forest. His face turned completely pale, like a palm tree struck by lightning.
ramacharitamanas::2091.translation_literal: गयउ (went) / सहमि (in shock) / नहिं (not) / कछु (anything) / कहि (saying) / आवा (came) / जनु (as if) / सचान (hawk) / बन (forest) / झपटेउ (pounced) / लावा (quail) / बिबरन (pale) / भयउ (became) / निपट (completely) / नरपालू (king) / दामिनि (lightning) / हनेउ (struck) / मनहुँ (as if) / तरु (tree) / तालू (palm tree)
ramacharitamanas::2091.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2091.essence: Grief can strike faster than thought and leave no words behind.
ramacharitamanas::2091.simple_meaning: The king is so shocked by the news that he cannot speak. His face loses all color, and he looks stricken and helpless.
ramacharitamanas::2091.simple_insight: Shock can empty a person before the mind even forms a response.
ramacharitamanas::2091.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has just asked for the boons that will send Ram into exile and raise Bharat to the throne. Dasharath hears it and collapses inward. This verse captures the instant his body registers what his heart cannot bear.
ramacharitamanas::2091.modern_relevance: You read a message that changes everything, and your hands go cold before you can reply. The mind has not caught up, but the body already knows.
ramacharitamanas::2091.insight: It shows how overwhelming grief can silence speech and drain the body at once.

ramacharitamanas::2092.verse_sanskrit: माथें हाथ मूदि दोउ लोचन। तनु धरि सोचु लाग जनु सोचन॥ मोर मनोरथु सुरतरु फूला। फरत करिनि जिमि हतेउ समूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::2092.verse_hindi: माथे पर हाथ रखकर, दोनों नेत्र बंद करके राजा ऐसे सोच करने लगे, मानो साक्षात् सोच ही शरीर धारण कर सोच कर रहा हो। (वे सोचते हैं- हाय!) मेरा मनोरथ रूपी कल्पवृक्ष फूल चुका था, परन्तु फलते समय कैकेयी ने हथिनी की तरह उसे जड़ समेत उखाड़कर नष्ट कर डाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::2092.english_translation: Placing his hand on his head and closing both eyes, the king sank into grief, as if grief itself had taken bodily form. 'My wish was a flowering wish-tree; just as it was bearing fruit, Kaikeyi uprooted it completely like an elephant uprooting a tree.'
ramacharitamanas::2092.translation_literal: माथें (on the head) / हाथ (hand) / मूदि (closing) / दोउ (both) / लोचन (eyes) / तनु (body) / धरि (having taken) / सोचु (grief) / लाग (became) / जनु (as if) / सोचन (grief itself) / मोर (my) / मनोरथु (wish) / सुरतरु (wish-tree) / फूला (flowered) / फरत (bearing fruit) / करिनि (elephant) / जिमि (like) / हतेउ (uprooted) / समूला (from the root)
ramacharitamanas::2092.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2092.essence: Hope can flower fully and still be torn out at the root.
ramacharitamanas::2092.simple_meaning: Dasharath collapses into grief and says his long-cherished wish was ruined just as it was about to bear fruit.
ramacharitamanas::2092.simple_insight: Some losses hurt because they arrive just when hope finally feels safe.
ramacharitamanas::2092.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has just heard that Ram must go to the forest for fourteen years. He closes his eyes, grips his head, and speaks from shock and heartbreak, comparing his ruined hope to a wish-tree torn up at the roots.
ramacharitamanas::2092.modern_relevance: You finally see the future you worked for — the offer, the wedding, the home, the breakthrough — and then one call changes everything. The grief is not just loss; it's the timing.
ramacharitamanas::2092.insight: It shows how quickly hope can turn into collapse when the thing you built your life around is cut off at the root.

ramacharitamanas::2093.verse_sanskrit: अवध उजारि कीन्हि कैकेईं। दीन्हिसि अचल बिपति कै नेईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2093.verse_hindi: कैकेयी ने अयोध्या को उजाड़ कर दिया और विपत्ति की अचल (सुदृढ़) नींव डाल दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2093.english_translation: Kaikeyi laid waste to Ayodhya and set the firm foundation of calamity.
ramacharitamanas::2093.translation_literal: अवध (Ayodhya) / उजारि (having laid waste) / कीन्हि (did) / कैकेईं (Kaikeyi) । / दीन्हिसि (she gave) / अचल (firm, unmoving) / बिपति (calamity) / कै (of) / नेईं (foundation)
ramacharitamanas::2093.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2093.essence: A selfish demand can turn a home into ruin.
ramacharitamanas::2093.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi's action brought ruin to Ayodhya and made disaster feel permanent.
ramacharitamanas::2093.simple_insight: One impulsive demand can break an entire household and make harm feel settled.
ramacharitamanas::2093.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath has just been struck silent by Kaikeyi's demand. The palace is turning from joy to grief. This line names the cost: her choice does not just wound one person; it lays waste to the whole kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::2093.modern_relevance: A single text message sent in anger can change a family group forever. One demand, one lie, one reckless choice can become the thing everyone has to live around.
ramacharitamanas::2093.insight: It shifts attention from private desire to the wider damage a choice can leave behind.

ramacharitamanas::2094.verse_sanskrit: कवनें अवसर का भयउ गयउँ नारि बिस्वास। जोग सिद्धि फल समय जिमि जतिहि अबिद्या नास ॥
ramacharitamanas::2094.verse_hindi: किस अवसर पर क्या हो गया! स्त्री का विश्वास करके मैं वैसे ही मारा गया, जैसे योग की सिद्धि रूपी फल मिलने के समय योगी को अविद्या नष्ट कर देती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2094.english_translation: At what moment did this happen? Trusting a woman, I was ruined, just as ignorance vanishes for a yogi when the fruit of yoga is reached.
ramacharitamanas::2094.translation_literal: कवनें अवसर (at what moment) / का (what) / भयउ (happened) / गयउँ (I was ruined) / नारि (woman) / बिस्वास (trust) / जोग (yoga) / सिद्धि (attainment) / फल (fruit) / समय (time) / जिमि (just as) / जतिहि (for the yogi) / अबिद्या (ignorance) / नास (destruction)
ramacharitamanas::2094.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2094.essence: Trust can become the very thing that undoes you.
ramacharitamanas::2094.simple_meaning: Dasharath laments that trusting Kaikeyi has destroyed him, comparing his ruin to the moment a yogi's ignorance disappears at the end of practice.
ramacharitamanas::2094.simple_insight: Broken trust can collapse an entire life in a single moment.
ramacharitamanas::2094.detailed_meaning: Dasharath sits in Ayodhya, stunned by Kaikeyi's demand and the exile of Ram. His grief turns into a bitter comparison: the very trust he placed in his queen has brought him down at the worst possible moment.
