ramacharitamanas::2094.modern_relevance: You open a message and realise the person you trusted has already made the decision without you. The shock is not just betrayal — it's the sudden collapse of the world you thought was secure.
ramacharitamanas::2094.insight: It shows how misplaced trust can turn a decisive moment into a catastrophe.

ramacharitamanas::2095.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि राउ मनहिं मन झाँखा। देखि कुभाँति कुमति मन माखा॥ भरतु कि राउर पूत न होंही। आनेहु मोल बेसाहि कि मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2095.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार राजा मन ही मन झींख रहे हैं। राजा का ऐसा बुरा हाल देखकर दुर्बुद्धि कैकेयी मन में बुरी तरह से क्रोधित हुई। (और बोली-) क्या भरत आपके पुत्र नहीं हैं? क्या मुझे आप दाम देकर खरीद लाए हैं? (क्या मैं आपकी विवाहिता पत्नी नहीं हूँ?) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2095.english_translation: In this way, the king kept churning his mind in silence. Seeing his cruel state, wicked Kaikeyi grew furious in her mind and said, “Is Bharata not your son? Did you buy me with money? Am I not your lawful wife?”
ramacharitamanas::2095.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / राउ (the king) / मनहिं मन (within the mind) / झाँखा (kept churning, fretted) / देखि (seeing) / कुभाँति (bad condition, cruel state) / कुमति (evil-minded, perverse) / मन (mind) / माखा (became angry) / भरतु (Bharata) / कि (is) / राउर (your) / पूत (son) / न (not) / होंही (is) / आनेहु (brought) / मोल (for price) / बेसाहि (bought) / कि (or) / मोही (me)
ramacharitamanas::2095.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2095.simple_meaning: Dasharath is inwardly tormented, and Kaikeyi reacts with anger, challenging his claim to Bharata and to her place as his wife.
ramacharitamanas::2095.simple_insight: Unchecked hurt turns quickly into accusation.
ramacharitamanas::2095.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath sits trapped in grief after Kaikeyi's demand has shattered the royal family. He turns the pain over in his mind, and Kaikeyi, seeing his distress, hardens further and lashes back, questioning Bharata, marriage, and belonging.
ramacharitamanas::2095.modern_relevance: A tense conversation at midnight can turn one wounded silence into three new accusations. Nobody is listening anymore; each person is defending a wound.
ramacharitamanas::2095.insight: It shows how a mind caught in hurt stops seeing clearly and starts striking back.

ramacharitamanas::2096.verse_sanskrit: जो सुनि सरु अस लाग तुम्हारें। काहे न बोलहु बचनु सँभारें॥ देहु उतरु अनु करहु कि नाहीं। सत्यसंध तुम्ह रघुकुल माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2096.verse_hindi: जो मेरा वचन सुनते ही आपको बाण सा लगा तो आप सोच-समझकर बात क्यों नहीं कहते? उत्तर दीजिए- हाँ कीजिए, नहीं तो नाहीं कर दीजिए। आप रघुवंश में सत्य प्रतिज्ञा वाले (प्रसिद्ध) हैं! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2096.english_translation: If my words struck you like an arrow, why not speak carefully? Give a clear answer: yes or no. You are famed in the Raghu line for keeping truth.
ramacharitamanas::2096.translation_literal: जो (which) / सुनि (hearing) / सरु (arrow) / अस (like) / लाग (struck) / तुम्हारें (to you) / काहे (why) / न (not) / बोलहु (do you speak) / बचनु (speech) / सँभारें (carefully) / देहु (give) / उतरु (answer) / अनु (yes) / करहु (do) / कि (or) / नाहीं (no) / सत्यसंध (bound to truth) / तुम्ह (you) / रघुकुल (Raghu line) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::2096.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2096.essence: Truthfulness means answering clearly, even when the answer hurts.
ramacharitamanas::2096.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi urges the king to answer clearly instead of reacting in pain. She reminds him that truthfulness is his family’s honor.
ramacharitamanas::2096.simple_insight: A hard conversation asks for clarity, not wounded silence.
ramacharitamanas::2096.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath has just been shaken by Kaikeyi's demand. Seeing his distress, Kaikeyi pushes him to answer plainly and invokes the Raghu line’s reputation for truthfulness. The moment exposes how a vow, once spoken, now binds the whole kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::2096.modern_relevance: A tense family conversation goes sideways because one person feels hurt and stops answering directly. The other person demands a clear yes or no, because half-spoken words only deepen the damage.
ramacharitamanas::2096.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional recoil to direct accountability in speech.

ramacharitamanas::2097.verse_sanskrit: देन कहेहु अब जनि बरु देहू। तजहु सत्य जग अपजसु लेहू॥ सत्य सराहि कहेहु बरु देना। जानेहु लेइहि मागि चबेना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2097.verse_hindi: आपने ही वर देने को कहा था, अब भले ही न दीजिए। सत्य को छोड़ दीजिए और जगत में अपयश लीजिए। सत्य की बड़ी सराहना करके वर देने को कहा था। समझा था कि यह चबेना ही माँग लेगी! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2097.english_translation: You asked for a boon, so now do not give it. Abandon truth and accept disgrace in the world. You praised truth and said to grant the boon. You thought I was only asking for a small snack.
ramacharitamanas::2097.translation_literal: देन (to give) / कहेहु (you said) / अब (now) / जनि (do not) / बरु (boon) / देहू (give) / तजहु (abandon) / सत्य (truth) / जग (world) / अपजसु (disgrace) / लेहू (accept) / सत्य (truth) / सराहि (praising) / कहेहु (you said) / बरु (boon) / देना (to give) / जानेहु (you knew) / लेइहि (would take) / मागि (asking) / चबेना (snack)
ramacharitamanas::2097.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2097.essence: A promise becomes a weapon when desire speaks through it.
ramacharitamanas::2097.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi taunts Dasharath: he promised a boon, so he should either give it or lose his good name. She says he praised truth, yet now acts as if her request was harmless.
ramacharitamanas::2097.simple_insight: A manipulative mind twists promises and then blames others for the damage.
ramacharitamanas::2097.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi presses Dasharath after his promise has trapped him. She turns his own words against him, acting as if the demand was small and ordinary. The verse exposes how desire can speak with cold logic.
ramacharitamanas::2097.modern_relevance: Someone says, “You agreed to this,” after hiding the real cost until the last second. The room goes quiet, and you see how a promise can be used like a knife.
ramacharitamanas::2097.insight: It reveals how self-justifying speech can weaponize another person's vow.

ramacharitamanas::2098.verse_sanskrit: सिबि दधीचि बलि जो कछु भाषा। तनु धनु तजेउ बचन पनु राखा॥ अति कटु बचन कहति कैकेई। मानहुँ लोन जरे पर देई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2098.verse_hindi: राजा शिबि, दधीचि और बलि ने जो कुछ कहा, शरीर और धन त्यागकर भी उन्होंने अपने वचन की प्रतिज्ञा को निबाहा। कैकेयी बहुत ही कड़ुवे वचन कह रही है, मानो जले पर नमक छिड़क रही हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2098.english_translation: Shibi, Dadhichi, and Bali gave up body and wealth, yet kept their word. Kaikeyi speaks with such bitter words, it is like salt on a wound.
ramacharitamanas::2098.translation_literal: सिबि (Shibi) / दधीचि (Dadhichi) / बलि (Bali) / जो (whatever) / कछु (something) / भाषा (said) / तनु (body) / धनु (wealth) / तजेउ (gave up) / बचन (word) / पनु (pledge) / राखा (kept) / अति (very) / कटु (bitter) / बचन (words) / कहति (speaking) / कैकेई (Kaikeyi) / मानहुँ (as if) / लोन (salt) / जरे (burned) / पर (on) / देई (sprinkled)
ramacharitamanas::2098.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2098.essence: Keeping a vow can cost everything; bitter speech can cut like fire on a wound.
ramacharitamanas::2098.simple_meaning: Great figures like Shibi, Dadhichi, and Bali gave up everything to keep their word. Kaikeyi’s harsh speech feels like salt poured on a burn.
ramacharitamanas::2098.simple_insight: Words can wound as deeply as loss, and a vow can be worth more than body or wealth.
ramacharitamanas::2098.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi is pressing her demand and speaking cruelly to Dasharath. Tulsidas recalls Shibi, Dadhichi, and Bali as examples of rulers who surrendered body and wealth rather than break their word, sharpening the contrast with Kaikeyi’s bitter insistence.
ramacharitamanas::2098.modern_relevance: A family argument turns vicious, and one sentence lands like acid on an old bruise. In that moment, you remember that some people would lose everything before they would break a promise.
ramacharitamanas::2098.insight: It shifts attention from the heat of the insult to the moral weight of keeping one’s word.

ramacharitamanas::2099.verse_sanskrit: धरम धुरंधर धीर धरि नयन उघारे रायँ। सिरु धुनि लीन्हि उसास असि मारेसि मोहि कुठायँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2099.verse_hindi: धर्म की धुरी को धारण करने वाले राजा दशरथ ने धीरज धरकर नेत्र खोले और सिर धुनकर तथा लंबी साँस लेकर इस प्रकार कहा कि इसने मुझे बड़े कुठौर मारा (ऐसी कठिन परिस्थिति उत्पन्न कर दी, जिससे बच निकलना कठिन हो गया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2099.english_translation: King Dasharath, bearer of dharma, opened his eyes with composure, shook his head, and sighed, saying, 'This has struck me in a terrible place.'
ramacharitamanas::2099.translation_literal: धरम धुरंधर (bearer of dharma) / धीर धरि (holding composure) / नयन (eyes) / उघारे (opened) / रायँ (the king) / सिरु (head) / धुनि (shaking) / लीन्हि (took) / उसास (sigh) / असि (thus) / मारेसि (struck) / मोहि (me) / कुठायँ (in a terrible place / hard-pressed)
ramacharitamanas::2099.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2099.essence: Composure can remain even when a promise turns into pain.
ramacharitamanas::2099.simple_meaning: Dasharath opens his eyes, stays composed, and admits that the situation has struck him painfully and left him trapped.
ramacharitamanas::2099.simple_insight: Sometimes dignity is just enduring the blow without pretending it did not hurt.
ramacharitamanas::2099.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has just been cornered by Kaikeyi’s demand after the earlier praise of truth and fulfilled promises. He opens his eyes, holds himself together, and quietly admits that this has placed him in an unbearable bind.
ramacharitamanas::2099.modern_relevance: You read the message that changes everything, then sit still for a long second before replying. The body knows before the mind can argue: this has landed badly.
ramacharitamanas::2099.insight: It shifts attention from outward control to the inward fact of being cornered by one’s own promise.

ramacharitamanas::2100.verse_sanskrit: आगें दीखि जरत सिर भारी। मनहुँ रोष तरवारि उघारी॥ मूठि कुबुद्धि धार निठुराई। धरी कूबरीं सान बनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2100.verse_hindi: प्रचंड क्रोध से जलती हुई कैकेयी सामने इस प्रकार दिखाई पड़ी, मानो क्रोध रूपी तलवार नंगी (म्यान से बाहर) खड़ी हो। कुबुद्धि उस तलवार की मूठ है, निष्ठुरता धार है और वह कुबरी (मंथरा) रूपी सान पर धरकर तेज की हुई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2100.english_translation: Kaikeyi appeared before him like a blazing sword of rage, unsheathed. Wrong understanding was its hilt, cruelty its blade, and Manthara's counsel had sharpened it on the whetstone.
ramacharitamanas::2100.translation_literal: आगें (in front) / दीखि (appeared) / जरत (burning) / सिर (head) / भारी (intensely) / मनहुँ (as if) / रोष (rage) / तरवारि (sword) / उघारी (unsheathed) / मूठि (hilt) / कुबुद्धि (wrong understanding) / धार (edge) / निठुराई (cruelty) / धरी (placed) / कूबरीं (on Manthara) / सान (whetstone) / बनाई (made sharp)
ramacharitamanas::2100.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2100.essence: Anger becomes deadly when wrong counsel sharpens it.
ramacharitamanas::2100.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi appears to Dasharath as a weapon of rage, sharpened by bad counsel and cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::2100.simple_insight: A mind fed by bad counsel can feel like a weapon turned inward.
ramacharitamanas::2100.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has just been confronted by Kaikeyi’s demand, and the king sees her not as a wife but as a force of destruction. Tulsidas turns her anger into a sharpened sword to show how desire, cruelty, and manipulation have taken over the moment.
ramacharitamanas::2100.modern_relevance: A family conversation turns cold in seconds. One harsh voice, one toxic influence, and suddenly the room feels armed. This verse names how manipulation sharpens anger.
ramacharitamanas::2100.insight: It shifts attention from the person alone to the chain of influence that armed the anger.

ramacharitamanas::2101.verse_sanskrit: लखी महीप कराल कठोरा। सत्य कि जीवनु लेइहि मोरा॥ बोले राउ कठिन करि छाती। बानी सबिनय तासु सोहाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2101.verse_hindi: राजा ने देखा कि यह (तलवार) बड़ी ही भयानक और कठोर है (और सोचा-) क्या सत्य ही यह मेरा जीवन लेगी? राजा अपनी छाती कड़ी करके, बहुत ही नम्रता के साथ उसे (कैकेयी को) प्रिय लगने वाली वाणी बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2101.english_translation: The king saw the cruel, hard blade and wondered, "Will truth itself take my life?" Then the king hardened his chest and spoke gently, in words pleasing to her.
ramacharitamanas::2101.translation_literal: लखी (seeing) / महीप (the king) / कराल (fierce) / कठोरा (hard) / सत्य (truth) / कि (whether) / जीवनु (life) / लेइहि (will take) / मोरा (mine)॥ / बोले (spoke) / राउ (the king) / कठिन (hard) / करि (making) / छाती (chest) / बानी (speech) / सबिनय (humble) / तासु (to her) / सोहाती (pleasing)॥
ramacharitamanas::2101.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2101.essence: Pain can be met with gentleness, even at the edge of collapse.
ramacharitamanas::2101.simple_meaning: Dasharath sees the harshness of the moment and speaks with outward gentleness, even while his heart is breaking.
ramacharitamanas::2101.simple_insight: Even in shock, dignity can remain. Pain does not have to make speech cruel.
ramacharitamanas::2101.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has just seen the terrible force of Kaikeyi's demand. He feels death approaching, yet he still answers with restraint. This verse shows the king's wounded dignity before the collapse becomes complete.
ramacharitamanas::2101.modern_relevance: Your throat tightens when someone you love says something unforgivable. You still choose not to throw the wound back at them. That restraint is its own courage.
ramacharitamanas::2101.insight: It teaches emotional control under extreme hurt: respond with measured speech instead of immediate retaliation.

ramacharitamanas::2102.verse_sanskrit: प्रिया बचन कस कहसि कुभाँती। भीर प्रतीति प्रीति करि हाँती॥ मोरें भरतु रामु दुइ आँखी। सत्य कहउँ करि संकरु साखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2102.verse_hindi: हे प्रिये! हे भीरु! विश्वास और प्रेम को नष्ट करके ऐसे बुरी तरह के वचन कैसे कह रही हो। मेरे तो भरत और रामचन्द्र दो आँखें (अर्थात एक से) हैं, यह मैं शंकरजी की साक्षी देकर सत्य कहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2102.english_translation: My dear, why do you speak such harsh words? You are ruining trust and love. For me, Bharata and Rama are like two eyes. I speak truth, with Shiva as witness.
ramacharitamanas::2102.translation_literal: प्रिया (dear) / बचन (words) / कस (why) / कहसि (do you speak) / कुभाँती (harshly, badly) / भीर (gentle one, timid one) / प्रतीति (trust) / प्रीति (love) / करि (having made) / हाँती (destroying) / मोरें (for me) / भरतु (Bharata) / रामु (Rama) / दुइ (two) / आँखी (eyes) / सत्य (truth) / कहउँ (I speak) / करि (having made) / संकरु (Shiva) / साखी (witness)
ramacharitamanas::2102.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2102.essence: True love refuses to choose between two beloveds.
ramacharitamanas::2102.simple_meaning: Dasharath gently rebukes Kaikeyi for speaking harshly and says Bharata and Rama are equally dear to him, like two eyes. He swears this truth before Shiva.
ramacharitamanas::2102.simple_insight: Love can hold more than one beloved without dividing itself.
ramacharitamanas::2102.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath faces Kaikeyi after her demand has shattered the royal household. Instead of anger, he answers with wounded tenderness, pleading that Bharata and Rama are both precious to him. His words show how deeply the coming exile will tear the family apart.
ramacharitamanas::2102.modern_relevance: A spouse says something cruel in the middle of a fight, and you feel the room split open. In that moment, the deepest response is not winning — it is protecting the trust that still remains.
ramacharitamanas::2102.insight: It shifts conflict from accusation to tenderness, reminding you to defend love before you defend yourself.

ramacharitamanas::2103.verse_sanskrit: अवसि दूतु मैं पठइब प्राता। ऐहहिं बेगि सुनत दोउ भ्राता॥ सुदिन सोधि सबु साजु सजाई। देउँ भरत कहुँ राजु बजाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2103.verse_hindi: मैं अवश्य सबेरे ही दूत भेजूँगा। दोनों भाई (भरत-शत्रुघ्न) सुनते ही तुरंत आ जाएँगे। अच्छा दिन (शुभ मुहूर्त) शोधवाकर, सब तैयारी करके डंका बजाकर मैं भरत को राज्य दे दूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2103.english_translation: I will surely send a messenger at dawn. Both brothers will come at once when they hear it. After choosing an auspicious day and arranging everything, I will publicly give the kingdom to Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::2103.translation_literal: अवसि (surely) / दूतु (messenger) / मैं (I) / पठइब (will send) / प्राता (at dawn) / ऐहहिं (will come) / बेगि (quickly) / सुनत (on hearing) / दोउ (both) / भ्राता (brothers) / सुदिन (auspicious day) / सोधि (choosing) / सबु (all) / साजु (arrangements) / सजाई (having arranged) / देउँ (I will give) / भरत कहुँ (to Bharat) / राजु (the kingdom) / बजाई (with proclamation / by beating the drum)
ramacharitamanas::2103.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2103.simple_meaning: Dasharath decides to send a messenger at dawn, call his sons quickly, and formally hand the kingdom to Bharat on an auspicious day.
ramacharitamanas::2103.simple_insight: A delayed promise becomes a public act. The heart wants relief, but duty still needs ceremony.
ramacharitamanas::2103.detailed_meaning: Dasharath, shaken by Kaikeyi's demands, tries to steady the moment by speaking of a swift, formal transfer of power. He imagines calling Bharat and Shatrughna back, choosing an auspicious day, and proclaiming Bharat's kingship.
ramacharitamanas::2103.modern_relevance: You finally decide to make the call you have avoided for days: to tell your family, your team, or your partner the hard decision. The relief is real, but the consequences are still waiting.
ramacharitamanas::2103.insight: It turns private intention into public responsibility, showing that important choices must be made clearly and openly.

ramacharitamanas::2104.verse_sanskrit: लोभु न रामहि राजु कर बहुत भरत पर प्रीति। मैं बड़ छोट बिचारि जियँ करत रहेउँ नृपनीति ॥
ramacharitamanas::2104.verse_hindi: राम को राज्य का लोभ नहीं है और भरत पर उनका बड़ा ही प्रेम है। मैं ही अपने मन में बड़े-छोटे का विचार करके राजनीति का पालन कर रहा था (बड़े को राजतिलक देने जा रहा था) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2104.english_translation: Ram has no desire for the throne, and he loves Bharat deeply. I was only following royal custom, thinking in terms of senior and junior.
ramacharitamanas::2104.translation_literal: लोभु (greed/desire) / न (not) / रामहि (for Ram) / राजु (kingdom) / कर (of) / बहुत (great) / भरत (Bharat) / पर (for/toward) / प्रीति (love) / मैं (I) / बड़ (big) / छोट (small) / बिचारि (having considered) / जियँ (in the mind) / करत रहेउँ (was doing) / नृपनीति (royal policy)
ramacharitamanas::2104.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2104.essence: Rank disappears when love is seen clearly.
ramacharitamanas::2104.simple_meaning: Dasharath admits that Ram does not want the kingdom and loves Bharat deeply. The mistake was his own, thinking in terms of rank and royal custom.
ramacharitamanas::2104.simple_insight: Status looks important until love makes it small.
ramacharitamanas::2104.detailed_meaning: Dasharath is explaining his own confusion as the exile crisis unfolds in Ayodhyakand. He sees that Ram has no hunger for power and that Bharat is dear to him. The tragedy came from Dasharath's attempt to judge his sons by rank instead of love.
ramacharitamanas::2104.modern_relevance: You assume the promotion matters most, then discover the person you admire never cared about the title. The real error was reading a relationship like a hierarchy.
ramacharitamanas::2104.insight: It shifts the mind from measuring people by position to seeing what they actually value and love.

ramacharitamanas::2105.verse_sanskrit: राम सपथ सत कहउँ सुभाऊ। राममातु कछु कहेउ न काऊ॥ मैं सबु कीन्ह तोहि बिनु पूँछें। तेहि तें परेउ मनोरथु छूछें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2105.verse_hindi: राम की सौ बार सौगंध खाकर मैं स्वभाव से ही कहता हूँ कि राम की माता (कौसल्या) ने (इस विषय में) मुझसे कभी कुछ नहीं कहा। अवश्य ही मैंने तुमसे बिना पूछे यह सब किया। इसी से मेरा मनोरथ खाली गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2105.english_translation: I swear by Ram a hundred times: by nature I say that Ram's mother never said anything to me about this. I did everything without asking you. Because of that, my wish has become empty.
ramacharitamanas::2105.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सपथ (oath) / सत (hundred) / कहउँ (I say) / सुभाऊ (by nature) / राममातु (Ram's mother) / कछु (anything) / कहेउ (said) / न (not) / काऊ (to me) / मैं (I) / सबु (all) / कीन्ह (did) / तोहि (you) / बिनु (without) / पूँछें (asking) / तेहि तें (because of that) / परेउ (fell) / मनोरथु (wish) / छूछें (empty)
ramacharitamanas::2105.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2105.essence: A decision made without asking can hollow out the heart that made it.
ramacharitamanas::2105.simple_meaning: Dasharath insists he acted without consulting Bharata and that no one else pushed him into it. He admits the result has left his wish empty.
ramacharitamanas::2105.simple_insight: A rushed choice can leave even a king with nothing but regret.
ramacharitamanas::2105.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath is trying to explain the broken succession decision to Bharata. He swears that Kaushalya never urged him, and admits he acted without asking Bharata. The verse exposes his guilt and the collapse of his hope.
ramacharitamanas::2105.modern_relevance: You send the message, make the decision, and only later realize you never checked with the person most affected. The damage is done before the explanation begins.
ramacharitamanas::2105.insight: It shows how acting without consultation can turn intention into regret.

ramacharitamanas::2106.verse_sanskrit: रिस परिहरु अब मंगल साजू। कछु दिन गएँ भरत जुबराजू॥ एकहि बात मोहि दुखु लागा। बर दूसर असमंजस मागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2106.verse_hindi: अब क्रोध छोड़ दे और मंगल साज सज। कुछ ही दिनों बाद भरत युवराज हो जाएँगे। एक ही बात का मुझे दुःख लगा कि तूने दूसरा वरदान बड़ी अड़चन का माँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2106.english_translation: Leave anger now and prepare for auspiciousness. In a few days, Bharata will be crowned crown prince. Only one thing caused me sorrow: you asked for the second boon in a way that created such trouble.
ramacharitamanas::2106.translation_literal: रिस (anger) / परिहरु (give up) / अब (now) / मंगल (auspicious) / साजू (prepare) / कछु दिन (a few days) / गएँ (after) / भरत (Bharata) / जुबराजू (crown prince) / एकहि बात (one thing only) / मोहि (to me) / दुखु (sorrow) / लागा (came) / बर (boon) / दूसर (second) / असमंजस (trouble / confusion) / मागा (asked)
ramacharitamanas::2106.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2106.essence: A single strained request can poison an entire household.
ramacharitamanas::2106.simple_meaning: Dasharath tells Kaikeyi to drop her anger and get ready for the celebration, saying Bharata will soon become crown prince. He also says her second boon caused him pain because it created this crisis.
ramacharitamanas::2106.simple_insight: Anger can turn a small request into a family-breaking wound.
ramacharitamanas::2106.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is still trying to steady Kaikeyi after her demand has trapped him. He asks her to put aside anger and accept the coming coronation of Bharata, while admitting that her second boon has already wounded him deeply.
ramacharitamanas::2106.modern_relevance: A parent hears one more impossible demand in the middle of a family argument, and knows the damage is already done. The real pain is not the request itself, but the confusion it creates.
ramacharitamanas::2106.insight: It shifts attention from the demand to the emotional fallout that follows it.

ramacharitamanas::2107.verse_sanskrit: अजहूँ हृदय जरत तेहि आँचा। रिस परिहास कि साँचेहुँ साँचा॥ कहु तजि रोषु राम अपराधू। सबु कोउ कहइ रामु सुठि साधू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2107.verse_hindi: उसकी आँच से अब भी मेरा हृदय जल रहा है। यह दिल्लगी में, क्रोध में अथवा सचमुच ही (वास्तव में) सच्चा है? क्रोध को त्यागकर राम का अपराध तो बता। सब कोई तो कहते हैं कि राम बड़े ही साधु हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2107.english_translation: My heart still burns from that sting. Was it a joke, anger, or truly real? Set aside your rage and tell me Ram’s fault. Everyone says Ram is very noble.
ramacharitamanas::2107.translation_literal: अजहूँ (still yet) / हृदय (heart) / जरत (burning) / तेहि (that) / आँचा (sting, heat) / रिस (anger) / परिहास (jest, mockery) / कि (or) / साँचेहुँ (truly) / साँचा (true) / कहु (say) / तजि (leaving) / रोषु (rage) / राम (Ram) / अपराधू (fault) / सबु कोउ (everyone) / कहइ (says) / रामु (Ram) / सुठि (very) / साधू (noble, virtuous)
ramacharitamanas::2107.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2107.essence: Hurt mind makes suspicion feel like proof.
ramacharitamanas::2107.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is still hurt and asks whether the earlier words were a joke or truly meant. She tells Manthara to drop the anger and explain what fault Ram has, since everyone praises him as noble.
ramacharitamanas::2107.simple_insight: A mind driven by hurt keeps asking for reasons after it has already chosen its story.
ramacharitamanas::2107.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Manthara keeps pressing Kaikeyi after the king’s promise has been twisted. Kaikeyi’s heart is still burning, yet she cannot quite tell whether the provocation was real or imagined. She is pulled into suspicion even as Ram’s goodness is publicly known.
ramacharitamanas::2107.modern_relevance: You replay a text message for the tenth time, trying to decide whether it was careless or cruel. The hurt becomes its own evidence, and suspicion starts writing the story for you.
ramacharitamanas::2107.insight: It shows how wounded attention turns into doubt and searches for fault even where none is clear.

ramacharitamanas::2108.verse_sanskrit: तुहूँ सराहसि करसि सनेहू। अब सुनि मोहि भयउ संदेहू॥ जासु सुभाउ अरिहि अनूकूला। सो किमि करिहि मातु प्रतिकूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::2108.verse_hindi: तू स्वयं भी राम की सराहना करती और उन पर स्नेह किया करती थी। अब यह सुनकर मुझे संदेह हो गया है (कि तुम्हारी प्रशंसा और स्नेह कहीं झूठे तो न थे?) जिसका स्वभाव शत्रु को भी अनूकल है, वह माता के प्रतिकूल आचरण क्यों कर करेगा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2108.english_translation: You yourself used to praise Ram and love him. Hearing this now, I have begun to doubt you. How could one whose nature is kind even to an enemy act against his mother?
ramacharitamanas::2108.translation_literal: तुहूँ (you yourself) / सराहसि (used to praise) / करसि (did) / सनेहू (love) / अब (now) / सुनि (hearing) / मोहि (in me) / भयउ (arose) / संदेहू (doubt) / जासु (whose) / सुभाउ (nature) / अरिहि (to an enemy) / अनूकूला (kindly favorable) / सो (he) / किमि (how) / करिहि (would do) / मातु (to mother) / प्रतिकूला (opposite, hostile)
ramacharitamanas::2108.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2108.essence: Kindness to all makes betrayal harder to believe.
ramacharitamanas::2108.simple_meaning: Dasharath remembers Kaikeyi's earlier love for Ram and cannot reconcile it with her present demand. He reasons that someone naturally kind, even to enemies, would not act against her own family.
ramacharitamanas::2108.simple_insight: A person’s true nature is revealed by consistency, not by one dramatic demand.
ramacharitamanas::2108.detailed_meaning: Dasharath, shaken by Kaikeyi’s sudden request, tries to understand how the wife who once praised Ram could now oppose him. In this moment of shock, he measures character by nature, not by the crisis in front of him.
ramacharitamanas::2108.modern_relevance: Someone who once stood by you now speaks coldly in a family group chat. You replay every kind moment and wonder which version was real. The verse catches that painful disbelief.
ramacharitamanas::2108.insight: It shifts judgment from the latest outburst to the deeper pattern of a person’s conduct.

ramacharitamanas::2109.verse_sanskrit: प्रिया हास रिस परिहरहि मागु बिचारि बिबेकु। जेहिं देखौं अब नयन भरि भरत राज अभिषेकु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2109.verse_hindi: हे प्रिये! हँसी और क्रोध छोड़ दे और विवेक (उचित-अनुचित) विचारकर वर माँग, जिससे अब मैं नेत्र भरकर भरत का राज्याभिषेक देख सकूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2109.english_translation: Beloved, set aside laughter and anger. Think with discernment and ask for a boon so that I may see Bharata's coronation with my own eyes.
ramacharitamanas::2109.translation_literal: प्रिया (beloved) / हास (laughter) / रिस (anger) / परिहरहि (set aside) / मागु (ask for) / बिचारि (having considered) / बिबेकु (discernment) / जेहिं (so that) / देखौं (I may see) / अब (now) / नयन भरि (with eyes full) / भरत (Bharata's) / राज अभिषेकु (coronation)
ramacharitamanas::2109.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2109.essence: Discernment should guide desire before desire becomes damage.
ramacharitamanas::2109.simple_meaning: Dasharath asks Kaikeyi to stop joking or getting angry and to think carefully before asking for a boon. He wants to witness Bharata's coronation with joy.
ramacharitamanas::2109.simple_insight: Real love asks for clarity, not impulse. It wants what truly supports the family, not what feeds a moment.
ramacharitamanas::2109.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is speaking to Kaikeyi after sensing her mood has turned strange. He asks her to drop anger and speak with discernment, still believing he is about to see Bharata crowned. The irony is sharp: the request comes just before the disaster that will shatter the kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::2109.modern_relevance: You can feel a conversation turning wrong before the words land. One person asks for calm and clarity, not knowing the request itself will change everything.
ramacharitamanas::2109.insight: It teaches you to choose discernment over emotional heat before making a life-altering request.

ramacharitamanas::2110.verse_sanskrit: जिऐ मीन बरु बारि बिहीना। मनि बिनु फनिकु जिऐ दुख दीना॥ कहउँ सुभाउ न छलु मन माहीं। जीवनु मोर राम बिनु नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2110.verse_hindi: मछली चाहे बिना पानी के जीती रहे और साँप भी चाहे बिना मणि के दीन-दुःखी होकर जीता रहे, परन्तु मैं स्वभाव से ही कहता हूँ, मन में (जरा भी) छल रखकर नहीं कि मेरा जीवन राम के बिना नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2110.english_translation: A fish may live without water, and a serpent may live miserably without its jewel; I speak my nature without any deceit in my mind: my life cannot exist without Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2110.translation_literal: जिऐ (may live) / मीन (fish) / बरु (perhaps) / बारि (water) / बिहीना (without) / मनि (jewel) / बिनु (without) / फनिकु (serpent) / जिऐ (may live) / दुख (pain) / दीना (wretched) / कहउँ (I say) / सुभाउ (nature) / न (not) / छलु (deceit) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / जीवनु (life) / मोर (my) / राम (Ram) / बिनु (without) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::2110.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2110.essence: Ram is not an ornament to life; he is the life that remains.
ramacharitamanas::2110.simple_meaning: Dasharath says that just as some beings cannot live without what sustains them, he cannot live without Ram. He speaks plainly, without deceit, from his true feeling.
ramacharitamanas::2110.simple_insight: Love can become so deep that separation feels like the end of life itself.
ramacharitamanas::2110.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is speaking to Kaikeyi as the demand for Ram's exile hangs over the palace. He tries to explain that Ram is not just a son to him; Ram is the center of his life, and losing Ram would be unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2110.modern_relevance: You watch someone leave the house after a fight, and the room feels hollow. Some bonds are not optional comforts; they are the shape of your whole day.
ramacharitamanas::2110.insight: It shifts devotion from idea to dependence: Ram is not praised from a distance, but felt as necessary for life.

ramacharitamanas::2111.verse_sanskrit: समुझि देखु जियँ प्रिया प्रबीना। जीवनु राम दरस आधीना॥ सुनि मृदु बचन कुमति अति जरई। मनहुँ अनल आहुति घृत परई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2111.verse_hindi: हे चतुर प्रिये! जी में समझ देख, मेरा जीवन श्री राम के दर्शन के अधीन है। राजा के कोमल वचन सुनकर दुर्बुद्धि कैकेयी अत्यन्त जल रही है। मानो अग्नि में घी की आहुतियाँ पड़ रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2111.english_translation: “Understand this, wise one, in your heart: my life depends on seeing Ram. Hearing the king’s gentle words, Kaikeyi’s bad sense burned fiercely, as if ghee were poured into a fire.”
ramacharitamanas::2111.translation_literal: समुझि (understanding) / देखु (see) / जियँ (in the heart) / प्रिया (beloved) / प्रबीना (wise one) / जीवनु (life) / राम (Ram) / दरस (sight) / आधीना (dependent) ॥ / सुनि (hearing) / मृदु (gentle) / बचन (words) / कुमति (bad sense) / अति (very) / जरई (burned) ॥ / मनहुँ (as if) / अनल (fire) / आहुति (offering) / घृत (ghee) / परई (falls) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2111.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2111.essence: A heart ruled by craving burns brighter when touched by tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::2111.simple_meaning: Dasharath tells Kaikeyi that his life depends on seeing Ram. Her hearing his gentle words only makes her selfish thinking burn hotter.
ramacharitamanas::2111.simple_insight: Love and attachment can coexist in one room, but only one can steer the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2111.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is trying to soften Kaikeyi and explain his longing for Ram. But the king’s tender words do the opposite: they inflame Kaikeyi’s poisoned resolve. This moment deepens the crisis that will force Ram into exile.
ramacharitamanas::2111.modern_relevance: A parent speaks gently, hoping to calm a tense home. Instead, the wrong desire in one person flares up harder. Not every soft word soothes; some only expose what is already burning.
ramacharitamanas::2111.insight: It shows how a mind ruled by craving turns even kindness into fuel for harm.

ramacharitamanas::2112.verse_sanskrit: कहइ करहु किन कोटि उपाया। इहाँ न लागिहि राउरि माया॥ देहु कि लेहु अजसु करि नाहीं। मोहि न बहुत प्रपंच सोहाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2112.verse_hindi: (कैकेयी कहती है-) आप करोड़ों उपाय क्यों न करें, यहाँ आपकी माया (चालबाजी) नहीं लगेगी। या तो मैंने जो माँगा है सो दीजिए, नहीं तो 'नाहीं' करके अपयश लीजिए। मुझे बहुत प्रपंच (बखेड़े) नहीं सुहाते ॥
ramacharitamanas::2112.english_translation: (Kaikeyi said:) You may try millions of tricks, but your magic will not work here. Give me what I asked for, or take the shame of refusal. I do not like endless scheming.
ramacharitamanas::2112.translation_literal: कहइ (says) / करहु (do) / किन (why) / कोटि (millions) / उपाया (means, tricks) / इहाँ (here) / न (not) / लागिहि (will work) / राउरि (your) / माया (magic, illusion, trickery)॥ / देहु (give) / कि (or) / लेहु (take) / अजसु (dishonour, shame) / करि (doing) / नाहीं (not) / मोहि (to me) / न (not) / बहुत (much) / प्रपंच (scheming, complication) / सोहाहीं (please, suit)॥
ramacharitamanas::2112.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2112.essence: Demand without reflection turns into hard refusal.
ramacharitamanas::2112.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi refuses delay and manipulation. She wants the demand fulfilled now, or she wants the shame of refusal openly accepted.
ramacharitamanas::2112.simple_insight: Some conflicts cannot be softened with cleverness. Clarity arrives when the demand is named plainly.
ramacharitamanas::2112.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kaikeyi has already been pulled into the bargain that will exile Ram. Dasharath is pleading, and she cuts through every attempt to persuade her. This verse shows her hardening into a demand that leaves no room for compromise.
ramacharitamanas::2112.modern_relevance: You are in a tense family argument and someone keeps changing the subject, hoping the storm will pass. Kaikeyi’s voice is the opposite of that drift: name the demand, face the cost, stop hiding behind words.
ramacharitamanas::2112.insight: It exposes how desire becomes rigid when it refuses reflection and only wants immediate satisfaction.

ramacharitamanas::2113.verse_sanskrit: रामु साधु तुम्ह साधु सयाने। राममातु भलि सब पहिचाने॥ जस कौसिलाँ मोर भल ताका। तस फलु उन्हहि देउँ करि साका ॥
ramacharitamanas::2113.verse_hindi: राम साधु हैं, आप सयाने साधु हैं और राम की माता भी भली है, मैंने सबको पहचान लिया है। कौसल्या ने मेरा जैसा भला चाहा है, मैं भी साका करके (याद रखने योग्य) उन्हें वैसा ही फल दूँगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2113.english_translation: Ram is noble; you are a wise noble woman. Ram's mother is also good, and I have understood all of you. Kaushalya wished me well, so I will repay her with the same kindness, in a memorable way.
ramacharitamanas::2113.translation_literal: रामु (Ram) / साधु (noble) / तुम्ह (you) / साधु (noble) / सयाने (wise) / राममातु (Ram's mother) / भलि (good) / सब (all) / पहिचाने (recognized)॥ / जस (as) / कौसिलाँ (Kaushalya) / मोर (my) / भल (good) / ताका (desired) / तस (that way) / फलु (result) / उन्हहि (to her) / देउँ (I will give) / करि (doing) / साका (memorable / fitting) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2113.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2113.essence: Kind words can conceal a binding demand.
ramacharitamanas::2113.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi flatters Ram, Sita? No—she speaks of Ram, the wise listener, and Kaushalya, saying she has understood everyone and will answer good with good.
ramacharitamanas::2113.simple_insight: Good intentions can still hide a hard bargain. Polite words do not always mean a peaceful heart.
ramacharitamanas::2113.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has already pressed her demand on Dasharath. She now speaks smoothly, naming Ram, the wise listener, and Kaushalya, as if all is well. But her words sit inside a tense bargain that is about to force Ram into exile.
ramacharitamanas::2113.modern_relevance: Someone smiles warmly in a family meeting while quietly keeping score. The room feels civil, but every sentence is carrying a hidden invoice.
ramacharitamanas::2113.insight: It teaches you to notice when courtesy is being used to mask leverage and emotional pressure.

ramacharitamanas::2114.verse_sanskrit: होत प्रात मुनिबेष धरि जौं न रामु बन जाहिं। मोर मरनु राउर अजस नृप समुझिअ मन माहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2114.verse_hindi: (सबेरा होते ही मुनि का वेष धारण कर यदि राम वन को नहीं जाते, तो हे राजन् ! मन में (निश्चय) समझ लीजिए कि मेरा मरना होगा और आपका अपयश! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2114.english_translation: If, by dawn, Rama does not leave for the forest in the guise of a sage, then understand in your heart that I will die and you will be disgraced.
ramacharitamanas::2114.translation_literal: होत प्रात (at dawn) / मुनिबेष (sage-disguise) धरि (wearing) / जौं (if) / न (not) / रामु (Rama) / बन (forest) / जाहिं (go) / मोर (my) / मरनु (death) / राउर (your) / अजस (disgrace) / नृप (king) / समुझिअ (understand) / मन (mind) / माहिं (within)
ramacharitamanas::2114.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2114.essence: Urgency turns a demand into a trap.
ramacharitamanas::2114.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi sets a deadline: if Rama does not go to the forest by dawn, she says she will die and the king will be shamed.
ramacharitamanas::2114.simple_insight: A demand becomes a crisis when it is tied to pride, fear, and urgency.
ramacharitamanas::2114.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has already pressed Dasharath with her demand. Now she sharpens it into a final ultimatum: by dawn, Rama must leave in sage's dress. Her words trap the king between family love and royal shame.
ramacharitamanas::2114.modern_relevance: A tense conversation turns into a deadline at midnight: either the decision happens now, or consequences follow by morning. Pressure can make a request feel like a threat.
ramacharitamanas::2114.insight: It shows how coercion works: urgency, shame, and emotional blackmail narrow another person's choices.

ramacharitamanas::2115.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि कुटिल भई उठि ठाढ़ी। मानहुँ रोष तरंगिनि बाढ़ी॥ पाप पहार प्रगट भइ सोई। भरी क्रोध जल जाइ न जोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2115.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर कुटिल कैकेयी उठ खड़ी हुई, मानो क्रोध की नदी उमड़ी हो। वह नदी पाप रूपी पहाड़ से प्रकट हुई है और क्रोध रूपी जल से भरी है, (ऐसी भयानक है कि) देखी नहीं जाती! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2115.english_translation: After saying this, crooked Kaikeyi stood up, as if a river of anger had swelled. It seemed to rise from a mountain of sin, full of the water of rage, too dreadful to look at.
ramacharitamanas::2115.translation_literal: अस कहि (having said this) / कुटिल (crooked) / भई (became) / उठि (rising) / ठाढ़ी (standing) / मानहुँ (as if) / रोष (anger) / तरंगिनि (river) / बाढ़ी (swelled)॥ / पाप (sin) / पहार (mountain) / प्रगट (manifest) / भइ (became) / सोई (that) / भरी (filled) / क्रोध (rage) / जल (water) / जाइ (goes) / न (not) / जोई (seen) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2115.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2115.essence: Anger can rise so fully that it takes a person over.
ramacharitamanas::2115.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi rises in a surge of anger, and the poet compares her fury to a terrifying river born from a mountain of wrongdoing.
ramacharitamanas::2115.simple_insight: Unchecked anger can make a person look like a force of nature, not a chooser.
ramacharitamanas::2115.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kaikeyi has just spoken the words that will shatter Dasharath’s household. Tulsidas does not pause for argument; he shows her rising in rage, as if anger itself has taken form. This is the moment her demand becomes a catastrophe.
ramacharitamanas::2115.modern_relevance: You hit send on the message while your chest is still hot. Ten minutes later, you can already see the damage. Anger feels powerful right before it becomes irreversible.
ramacharitamanas::2115.insight: It teaches you to notice rage before it becomes action and starts reshaping everything around it.

ramacharitamanas::2116.verse_sanskrit: दोउ बर कूल कठिन हठ धारा। भवँर कूबरी बचन प्रचारा॥ ढाहत भूपरूप तरु मूला। चली बिपति बारिधि अनूकूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::2116.verse_hindi: दोनों वरदान उस नदी के दो किनारे हैं, कैकेयी का कठिन हठ ही उसकी (तीव्र) धारा है और कुबरी (मंथरा) के वचनों की प्रेरणा ही भँवर है। (वह क्रोध रूपी नदी) राजा दशरथ रूपी वृक्ष को जड़-मूल से ढहाती हुई विपत्ति रूपी समुद्र की ओर (सीधी) चली है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2116.english_translation: The two boons are the river's two banks; Kaikeyi's hard stubbornness is its current, and Manthara's words are its whirlpool. That river of disaster rushes straight on, uprooting King Dasharath like a tree and flowing toward the sea of calamity.
ramacharitamanas::2116.translation_literal: दोउ (both) / बर (boons) / कूल (banks) / कठिन (hard) / हठ (stubbornness) / धारा (current) / भवँर (whirlpool) / कूबरी (hunchbacked woman, Manthara) / बचन (words) / प्रचारा (spread, urged) / ढाहत (uprooting, toppling) / भूपरूप (in the form of a king) / तरु (tree) / मूला (from the root) / चली (went) / बिपति (calamity) / बारिधि (ocean) / अनूकूला (toward, aligned with)
ramacharitamanas::2116.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2116.essence: Stubborn desire plus bad counsel can uproot even a king.
ramacharitamanas::2116.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi's stubbornness and Manthara's urging are pictured as a river of disaster. Together they are pulling Dasharath toward ruin.
ramacharitamanas::2116.simple_insight: Small manipulations can become a force strong enough to uproot an entire life.
ramacharitamanas::2116.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has already turned from affection to demand. Tulsidas turns her anger into a flooding river: her stubborn will is the current, Manthara's words are the whirlpool, and Dasharath is the tree about to be torn out by the roots.
ramacharitamanas::2116.modern_relevance: A friend keeps feeding your worst suspicion, and suddenly a simple disagreement becomes a family rupture. This verse shows how repeated pressure can carry a person straight into disaster.
ramacharitamanas::2116.insight: It teaches you to see how obsession and outside prompting can combine into irreversible harm.

ramacharitamanas::2117.verse_sanskrit: लखी नरेस बात फुरि साँची। तिय मिस मीचु सीस पर नाची॥ गहि पद बिनय कीन्ह बैठारी। जनि दिनकर कुल होसि कुठारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2117.verse_hindi: राजा ने समझ लिया कि बात सचमुच (वास्तव में) सच्ची है, स्त्री के बहाने मेरी मृत्यु ही सिर पर नाच रही है। (तदनन्तर राजा ने कैकेयी के) चरण पकड़कर उसे बिठाकर विनती की कि तू सूर्यकुल (रूपी वृक्ष) के लिए कुल्हाड़ी मत बन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2117.english_translation: The king understood the truth was real: death itself was dancing over his head because of a woman. He held her feet, made her sit down, and pleaded, "Do not become the axe for the solar dynasty."
ramacharitamanas::2117.translation_literal: लखी (saw) / नरेस (the king) / बात (the matter) / फुरि (truly) / साँची (true) / तिय (woman) / मिस (under the pretext) / मीचु (death) / सीस (head) / पर (on) / नाची (danced) / गहि (grasping) / पद (feet) / बिनय (humble plea) / कीन्ह (made) / बैठारी (to sit down) / जनि (do not) / दिनकर (sun) / कुल (dynasty) / होसि (become) / कुठारी (axe)
ramacharitamanas::2117.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2117.essence: Denial breaks, and the full cost becomes visible.
ramacharitamanas::2117.simple_meaning: Dasharath realizes Kaikeyi's demand is truly deadly for his family. He begs her not to become the instrument that cuts down the solar dynasty.
ramacharitamanas::2117.simple_insight: Grief becomes clearer when denial ends. The mind finally names what it has been trying not to see.
ramacharitamanas::2117.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has heard Kaikeyi's demand and understands the blow is real. The king who once ruled a great line now pleads at her feet, trying to stop the ruin of his house and the exile of Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2117.modern_relevance: You read the text message twice, then a third time. The meaning finally lands, and your stomach drops because the damage is no longer hypothetical.
ramacharitamanas::2117.insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to clear-eyed recognition of loss.

ramacharitamanas::2118.verse_sanskrit: मागु माथ अबहीं देउँ तोही। राम बिरहँ जनि मारसि मोही॥ राखु राम कहुँ जेहि तेहि भाँती। नाहिं त जरिहि जनम भरि छाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2118.verse_hindi: तू मेरा मस्तक माँग ले, मैं तुझे अभी दे दूँ। पर राम के विरह में मुझे मत मार। जिस किसी प्रकार से हो तू राम को रख ले। नहीं तो जन्मभर तेरी छाती जलेगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2118.english_translation: Take my head right now, and I will give it to you. But do not kill me with separation from Ram. Keep Ram somehow, any way you can. Otherwise your chest will burn for this whole birth.
ramacharitamanas::2118.translation_literal: मागु (ask for) / माथ (head) / अबहीं (right now) / देउँ (I give) / तोही (to you) / राम (Ram) / बिरहँ (in separation) / जनि (do not) / मारसि (kill) / मोही (me) / राखु (keep) / राम कहुँ (for Ram) / जेहि तेहि भाँती (by any means) / नाहिं (otherwise) / त (then) / जरिहि (will burn) / जनम भरि (for a whole birth) / छाती (chest)
ramacharitamanas::2118.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2118.essence: Separation from Ram burns more than death itself.
ramacharitamanas::2118.simple_meaning: Dasharath offers his head, but begs not to be destroyed by separation from Ram. He wants Ram preserved by any means, or the pain will last his whole life.
ramacharitamanas::2118.simple_insight: Love can make loss feel physically unbearable, and that pain reveals what mattered most.
ramacharitamanas::2118.detailed_meaning: Dasharath, crushed by Kaikeyi's demand and the thought of Ram's exile, speaks in helpless anguish. He offers anything except the one thing that truly matters to him: Ram's presence. This is grief before the final collapse.
ramacharitamanas::2118.modern_relevance: You stare at a hospital corridor, ready to trade anything for one more hour with someone you love. Some losses cannot be negotiated with; they only expose the depth of attachment.
ramacharitamanas::2118.insight: It shifts attention from bargaining with pain to seeing how completely love has anchored the heart.

ramacharitamanas::2119.verse_sanskrit: देखी ब्याधि असाध नृपु परेउ धरनि धुनि माथ। कहत परम आरत बचन राम राम रघुनाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2119.verse_hindi: राजा ने देखा कि रोग असाध्य है, तब वे अत्यन्त आर्तवाणी से 'हा राम! हा राम! हा रघुनाथ!' कहते हुए सिर पीटकर जमीन पर गिर पड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::2119.english_translation: Seeing the incurable illness, the king fell to the ground, striking his head, and cried out in utter distress, 'Ram, Ram, Raghunath!'
ramacharitamanas::2119.translation_literal: देखी (seeing) / ब्याधि (illness) / असाध (incurable) / नृपु (king) / परेउ (fell) / धरनि (on the ground) / धुनि (shaking) / माथ (head) / कहत (saying) / परम (utter) / आरत (distressed) / बचन (words) / राम (Ram) / राम (Ram) / रघुनाथ (Lord of Raghu)
ramacharitamanas::2119.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2119.essence: Grief strips away power and leaves only the name the heart can hold.
ramacharitamanas::2119.simple_meaning: The king sees that the illness cannot be cured and collapses in grief, crying out Ram's name again and again.
ramacharitamanas::2119.simple_insight: When helplessness becomes complete, the heart reaches for the name it trusts most.
ramacharitamanas::2119.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has just realised that the wound before him cannot be healed. In that instant, the king loses all strength, falls to the ground, and cries out Ram's name in unbearable anguish. The verse shows grief breaking the body before the next verse shows it draining away.
ramacharitamanas::2119.modern_relevance: You get a call from the hospital and suddenly the room goes silent. In that instant, the mind drops its arguments and reaches for the one presence it trusts.
ramacharitamanas::2119.insight: It shifts attention from control to refuge when suffering becomes unbearable.

ramacharitamanas::2120.verse_sanskrit: ब्याकुल राउ सिथिल सब गाता। करिनि कलपतरु मनहुँ निपाता॥ कंठु सूख मुख आव न बानी। जनु पाठीनु दीन बिनु पानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2120.verse_hindi: राजा व्याकुल हो गए, उनका सारा शरीर शिथिल पड़ गया, मानो हथिनी ने कल्पवृक्ष को उखाड़ फेंका हो। कंठ सूख गया, मुख से बात नहीं निकलती, मानो पानी के बिना पहिना नामक मछली तड़प रही हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2120.english_translation: King Dasharath became distressed; his whole body went limp, as if a female elephant had uprooted a wish-fulfilling tree. His throat dried up and no words came from his mouth, like a fish gasping without water.
ramacharitamanas::2120.translation_literal: ब्याकुल (distressed) / राउ (king) / सिथिल (limp, weak) / सब (all) / गाता (body) / करिनि (female elephant) / कलपतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / मनहुँ (as if) / निपाता (uprooted, thrown down) ॥ कंठु (throat) / सूख (dried) / मुख (mouth) / आव (came) / न (not) / बानी (speech, words) / जनु (as if) / पाठीनु (fish) / दीन (wretched) / बिनु (without) / पानी (water) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2120.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2120.essence: Grief can leave even a king wordless and weak.
ramacharitamanas::2120.simple_meaning: Dasharath is overcome with grief. His body weakens, his throat dries, and he cannot speak.
ramacharitamanas::2120.simple_insight: Deep grief can empty the body before the mind can explain it.
ramacharitamanas::2120.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has just been struck by the pain of Ram's exile and the collapse of his hopes. Tulsidas shows grief as physical ruin: the king cannot stand, breathe, or speak clearly.
ramacharitamanas::2120.modern_relevance: You get the message late at night and just sit on the edge of the bed, unable to answer anyone. Grief can make the body fail before the words arrive.
ramacharitamanas::2120.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic reaction to the bodily reality of sorrow.

ramacharitamanas::2121.verse_sanskrit: पुनि कह कटु कठोर कैकेई। मनहुँ घाय महुँ माहुर देई॥ जौं अंतहुँ अस करतबु रहेऊ। मागु मागु तुम्ह केहिं बल कहेऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2121.verse_hindi: कैकेयी फिर कड़वे और कठोर वचन बोली, मानो घाव में जहर भर रही हो। (कहती है-) जो अंत में ऐसा ही करना था, तो आपने 'माँग, माँग' किस बल पर कहा था? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2121.english_translation: Kaikeyi spoke again with bitter, harsh words, as if pouring poison into a wound. She said, "If you meant to do this in the end, on what strength did you say, 'Ask, ask'?"
ramacharitamanas::2121.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / कह (spoke) / कटु (bitter) / कठोर (harsh) / कैकेई (Kaikeyi) / मनहुँ (as if) / घाय (wound) / महुँ (in) / माहुर (poison) / देई (giving) / जौं (if) / अंतहुँ (at the end) / अस (such) / करतबु (deed) / रहेऊ (remained) / मागु (ask) / मागु (ask) / तुम्ह (you) / केहिं (what) / बल (strength) / कहेऊ (said)
ramacharitamanas::2121.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2121.essence: Cruel speech can make a wound deeper than the wound itself.
ramacharitamanas::2121.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi speaks cruelly to Dasharath, accusing him of weakness and hypocrisy after his promise to grant her boons.
ramacharitamanas::2121.simple_insight: Words spoken in anger can deepen a wound instead of healing it.
ramacharitamanas::2121.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath lies broken on the floor after realizing the cost of Kaikeyi's boons. Instead of softening, Kaikeyi answers with sharp blame, turning his suffering into an accusation. The scene shows how desire and resentment can harden the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2121.modern_relevance: A family argument reaches the point where one person is already hurting and the other keeps pressing harder. At that moment, the issue is no longer the problem itself — it is the cruelty of how it is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2121.insight: It shifts attention from the content of blame to the damage caused by a hardened mind.

ramacharitamanas::2122.verse_sanskrit: दुइ कि होइ एक समय भुआला। हँसब ठठाइ फुलाउब गाला॥ दानि कहाउब अरु कृपनाई। होइ कि खेम कुसल रौताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2122.verse_hindi: हे राजा! ठहाका मारकर हँसना और गाल फुलाना- क्या ये दोनों एक साथ हो सकते हैं? दानी भी कहाना और कंजूसी भी करना। क्या रजपूती में क्षेम-कुशल भी रह सकती है?(लड़ाई में बहादुरी भी दिखावें और कहीं चोट भी न लगे!) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2122.english_translation: Can two opposite things happen at the same time? Can one laugh loudly and still puff out the cheeks? Can one claim generosity and still be stingy? Can royal courage remain intact while fear and harm are both avoided?
ramacharitamanas::2122.translation_literal: दुइ (two) / कि (whether) / होइ (happen) / एक समय (at one time) / भुआला (confused, foolish) / हँसब (laughing) / ठठाइ (loudly) / फुलाउब (to puff up) / गाला (cheeks) / दानि (generous) / कहाउब (to be called) / अरु (and) / कृपनाई (stinginess) / होइ कि (can there be) / खेम (safety, well-being) / कुसल (welfare) / रौताई (royal courage, warrior spirit)
ramacharitamanas::2122.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2122.essence: Contradictory claims collapse when conduct reveals the truth.
ramacharitamanas::2122.simple_meaning: A person cannot claim opposite qualities at the same time. The verse warns that courage, generosity, and dignity must be real, not just spoken about.
ramacharitamanas::2122.simple_insight: It clears away self-deception and asks for one honest, consistent stance.
ramacharitamanas::2122.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has pushed Dasharath into a crisis, and the argument is turning moral. The speaker challenges her contradictions directly: a ruler cannot pretend to be both bold and afraid, generous and miserly, composed and shaken at once.
ramacharitamanas::2122.modern_relevance: A manager says she values honesty, then hides the real reason for a layoff. The room feels the split instantly. This verse cuts through that kind of double speech and demands one clean position.
ramacharitamanas::2122.insight: It pushes the mind toward consistency: say what you mean, and let conduct match the claim.

ramacharitamanas::2123.verse_sanskrit: छाड़हु बचनु कि धीरजु धरहू। जनि अबला जिमि करुना करहू॥ तनु तिय तनय धामु धनु धरनी। सत्यसंध कहुँ तृन सम बरनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2123.verse_hindi: या तो वचन (प्रतिज्ञा) ही छोड़ दीजिए या धैर्य धारण कीजिए। यों असहाय स्त्री की भाँति रोइए-पीटिए नहीं। सत्यव्रती के लिए तो शरीर, स्त्री, पुत्र, घर, धन और पृथ्वी- सब तिनके के बराबर कहे गए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2123.english_translation: Either give up your promise or hold your composure. Do not cry and lament like a helpless woman. For one who keeps truth, body, wife, son, home, wealth, and land are all as small as blades of grass.
ramacharitamanas::2123.translation_literal: छाड़हु (give up) / बचनु (promise, word) / कि (or) / धीरजु (composure, patience) / धरहू (hold) / जनि (do not) / अबला (helpless woman) / जिमि (like) / करुना (lamentation, pity) / करहू (do) / तनु (body) / तिय (wife) / तनय (son) / धामु (home) / धनु (wealth) / धरनी (earth, land) / सत्यसंध (one bound to truth) / कहुँ (for) / तृन (blade of grass) / सम (equal) / बरनी (described, counted)
ramacharitamanas::2123.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2123.essence: Truth demands steadiness, not sentimental collapse.
ramacharitamanas::2123.simple_meaning: Keep your promise or keep your composure. A person bound to truth must treat body, family, wealth, and land as small as grass.
ramacharitamanas::2123.simple_insight: It asks for a hard honesty: either stand by your word or stop pretending you can.
ramacharitamanas::2123.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi presses Dasharath after his vows have trapped him. She demands that he either abandon his promise or endure it with steadiness, while reminding him that truthfulness is greater than attachment to body, family, possessions, and kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::2123.modern_relevance: You promised something in a meeting, then panic hit the moment it became costly. This verse cuts through the drama: either own the promise or admit you will not keep it.
ramacharitamanas::2123.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional collapse to moral consistency under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::2124.verse_sanskrit: मरम बचन सुनि राउ कह कहु कछु दोषु न तोर। लागेउ तोहि पिसाच जिमि कालु कहावत मोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::2124.verse_hindi: कैकेयी के मर्मभेदी वचन सुनकर राजा ने कहा कि तू जो चाहे कह, तेरा कुछ भी दोष नहीं है। मेरा काल तुझे मानो पिशाच होकर लग गया है, वही तुझसे यह सब कहला रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2124.english_translation: Hearing Kaikeyi's piercing words, the king said, “Say what you wish; no fault is yours. My death itself has come upon you like a demon, making you speak like this.”
ramacharitamanas::2124.translation_literal: मरम (piercing) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / राउ (the king) / कह (said) / कहु (say) / कछु (some) / दोषु (fault) / न (not) / तोर (yours) / लागेउ (has come upon) / तोहि (you) / पिसाच जिमि (like a demon) / कालु (death) / कहावत (called) / मोर (mine)
ramacharitamanas::2124.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2124.essence: Grief can silence blame and make death feel present.
ramacharitamanas::2124.simple_meaning: Dasharath hears Kaikeyi's cruel demand and refuses to blame her. He says his own death has overtaken him, as if a dark force has possessed the moment.
ramacharitamanas::2124.simple_insight: Grief can make a person stop arguing and see only the wound.
ramacharitamanas::2124.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi's demand has shattered Dasharath's world. After her cutting words, he does not fight back or accuse her. He collapses inward, seeing the disaster as his own end and the result of a force beyond ordinary blame.
ramacharitamanas::2124.modern_relevance: You get the message that changes everything, and your first reaction is not anger but stunned surrender. The argument is over before it begins.
ramacharitamanas::2124.insight: It shifts the mind from blame to helpless recognition of a loss already in motion.

ramacharitamanas::2125.verse_sanskrit: चहत न भरत भूपतहि भोरें। बिधि बस कुमति बसी जिय तोरें॥ सो सबु मोर पाप परिनामू। भयउ कुठाहर जेहिं बिधि बामू॥
ramacharitamanas::2125.verse_hindi: भरत तो भूलकर भी राजपद नहीं चाहते। होनहारवश तेरे ही जी में कुमति आ बसी। यह सब मेरे पापों का परिणाम है, जिससे कुसमय (बेमौके) में विधाता विपरीत हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2125.english_translation: Bharat does not want kingship, not even in his sleep. Fate placed crooked thinking in your heart. All this is the result of my own sins, by which the times turned against me.
ramacharitamanas::2125.translation_literal: चहत (desire) / न (not) / भरत (Bharat) / भूपतहि (the kingly throne) / भोरें (even in sleep, by mistake) / बिधि बस (by fate's power) / कुमति (crooked thinking) / बसी (entered, dwelt) / जिय (in the heart) / तोरें (in your) ॥ / सो (that) / सबु (all) / मोर (my) / पाप (sins) / परिनामू (result) / भयउ (became) / कुठाहर (bad time, misfortune) / जेहिं (by which) / बिधि (fate) / बामू (crooked, adverse) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2125.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2125.essence: Bharat never wanted power; the disaster came from crooked desire.
ramacharitamanas::2125.simple_meaning: Bharat does not want the throne at all. The queen sees the disaster as the result of her own wrongdoing and says fate has turned against her.
ramacharitamanas::2125.simple_insight: Regret sharpens when you see your own choices as the source of harm.
ramacharitamanas::2125.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi looks at the ruin her demand has caused. She admits Bharat never wanted the throne and blames her own past actions for the disaster that has fallen on Ayodhya and the royal family.
ramacharitamanas::2125.modern_relevance: After the argument is over, you replay every sentence and realise the damage came from one selfish decision. The shame is not abstract anymore; it has a name and a face.
ramacharitamanas::2125.insight: It shifts blame inward and exposes how desire can distort judgment and invite regret.

ramacharitamanas::2126.verse_sanskrit: सुबस बसिहि फिरि अवध सुहाई। सब गुन धाम राम प्रभुताई॥ करिहहिं भाइ सकल सेवकाई। होइहि तिहुँ पुर राम बड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2126.verse_hindi: (तेरी उजाड़ी हुई) यह सुंदर अयोध्या फिर भलीभाँति बसेगी और समस्त गुणों के धाम श्री राम की प्रभुता भी होगी। सब भाई उनकी सेवा करेंगे और तीनों लोकों में श्री राम की बड़ाई होगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2126.english_translation: Beautiful Ayodhya will be restored again, and Ram, the abode of all virtues, will reign there. All the brothers will serve him, and Ram's glory will spread through the three worlds.
ramacharitamanas::2126.translation_literal: सुबस (beautiful) / बसिहि (will dwell / be settled) / फिरि (again) / अवध (Ayodhya) / सुहाई (beautiful) / सब (all) / गुन (virtues) / धाम (abode) / राम (Ram) / प्रभुताई (lordship / sovereignty) / करिहहिं (will do) / भाइ (brothers) / सकल (all) / सेवकाई (service) / होइहि (will be) / तिहुँ (three) / पुर (worlds / cities) / राम (Ram) / बड़ाई (greatness / glory)
ramacharitamanas::2126.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2126.essence: Ram's rightful presence restores the home and gives every brother a place in service.
ramacharitamanas::2126.simple_meaning: Ayodhya will be restored under Ram's rule. His brothers will serve him, and his greatness will be known everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::2126.simple_insight: Even after collapse, a life can be set right by service and rightful rule.
ramacharitamanas::2126.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kaikeyi tries to justify the exile she has caused by pointing to a future she imagines. She says the city will become beautiful again under Ram, his brothers will serve him, and his glory will fill the three worlds. The words sit inside a wounded family argument.
ramacharitamanas::2126.modern_relevance: A family home after a bitter fight can feel ruined. Then one person starts cleaning, another starts cooking, and slowly the place feels livable again. Order returns when everyone gives themselves to the right center.
ramacharitamanas::2126.insight: It shifts attention from personal gain to restored harmony around a worthy center.

ramacharitamanas::2127.verse_sanskrit: तोर कलंकु मोर पछिताऊ। मुएहुँ न मिटिहि न जाइहि काऊ॥ अब तोहि नीक लाग करु सोई। लोचन ओट बैठु मुहु गोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2127.verse_hindi: केवल तेरा कलंक और मेरा पछतावा मरने पर भी नहीं मिटेगा, यह किसी तरह नहीं जाएगा। अब तुझे जो अच्छा लगे वही कर। मुँह छिपाकर मेरी आँखों की ओट जा बैठ (अर्थात मेरे सामने से हट जा, मुझे मुँह न दिखा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2127.english_translation: Your disgrace and my regret will not disappear, even in death. Do what you think best now. Hide your face and sit out of my sight.
ramacharitamanas::2127.translation_literal: तोर (your) / कलंकु (disgrace) / मोर (my) / पछिताऊ (regret) / मुएहुँ (even after dying) / न (not) / मिटिहि (will be erased) / न (nor) / जाइहि (will go) / काऊ (at all)॥ / अब (now) / तोहि (to you) / नीक (good) / लाग (seems) / करु (do) / सोई (that) / लोचन (eyes) / ओट (out of sight) / बैठु (sit) / मुहु (face) / गोई (hide)॥
ramacharitamanas::2127.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2127.essence: Some pain cannot be repaired; it can only be faced and endured.
ramacharitamanas::2127.simple_meaning: The speaker says this shame and regret can never be undone. So the other person should do whatever seems best and leave the speaker's sight.
ramacharitamanas::2127.simple_insight: Some wounds are so deep that words can only ask for distance, not repair.
ramacharitamanas::2127.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the family rupture has already happened, and the grief is now turning inward. The speaker, overwhelmed by shame and remorse, tells the other person that this stain cannot be erased even by death and asks to be left alone.
ramacharitamanas::2127.modern_relevance: After a family argument, one person sits in the kitchen long after midnight, unable to fix what was said. The only honest thing left is to ask for space before more damage is done.
ramacharitamanas::2127.insight: It shifts the mind from arguing for repair to acknowledging irreversible hurt and creating distance.

ramacharitamanas::2128.verse_sanskrit: जब लगि जिऔं कहउँ कर जोरी। तब लगि जनि कछु कहसि बहोरी॥ फिरि पछितैहसि अंत अभागी। मारसि गाइ नहारू लागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2128.verse_hindi: मैं हाथ जोड़कर कहता हूँ कि जब तक मैं जीता रहूँ, तब तक फिर कुछ न कहना (अर्थात मुझसे न बोलना)। अरी अभागिनी! फिर तू अन्त में पछताएगी जो तू नहारू (ताँत) के लिए गाय को मार रही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2128.english_translation: As long as I live, I beg you with folded hands, do not say another word. You wretched woman will regret it in the end, killing a cow for the sake of a thread.
ramacharitamanas::2128.translation_literal: जब लगि (as long as) जिऔं (I live) कहउँ (I say) कर जोरी (with folded hands) / तब लगि (until then) जनि (do not) कछु (anything) कहसि (say) बहोरी (again)॥ / फिरि (later) पछितैहसि (you will regret) अंत (at the end) अभागी (wretched one) / मारसि (you kill) गाइ (cow) नहारू (for thread) लागी (for the sake of) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2128.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::2128.essence: Small gain, ignored warning, lasting regret.
ramacharitamanas::2128.simple_meaning: Ravana begs the other person to stop speaking and warns that this harmful choice will bring regret later.
ramacharitamanas::2128.simple_insight: Pride can make a person dismiss wise warning until the damage is already done.
ramacharitamanas::2128.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana is trapped in a moment of rage and helplessness. He pleads for silence, then lashes out with a bitter warning: a foolish, harmful act done for a trivial gain will end in regret. The verse deepens the collapse already unfolding around him.
ramacharitamanas::2128.modern_relevance: You are one message away from saying something irreversible, but your anger is louder than your judgment. Later, the cost will feel much bigger than the victory.
ramacharitamanas::2128.insight: It shows how ego refuses correction and turns a small desire into a destructive choice.

ramacharitamanas::2129.verse_sanskrit: परेउ राउ कहि कोटि बिधि काहे करसि निदानु। कपट सयानि न कहति कछु जागति मनहुँ मसानु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2129.verse_hindi: राजा करोड़ों प्रकार से (बहुत तरह से) समझाकर (और यह कहकर) कि तू क्यों सर्वनाश कर रही है, पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े। पर कपट करने में चतुर कैकेयी कुछ बोलती नहीं, मानो (मौन होकर) मसान जगा रही हो (श्मशान में बैठकर प्रेतमंत्र सिद्ध कर रही हो) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2129.english_translation: King Dasharath fell to the ground, saying, “Why are you bringing ruin?” Cunning Kaikeyi said nothing, as if she sat in a cremation ground, awakening dark rites.
ramacharitamanas::2129.translation_literal: परेउ (fell) / राउ (the king) / कहि (saying) / कोटि बिधि (in countless ways) / काहे (why) / करसि (are you doing) / निदानु (ruin, final destruction) / कपट (deceit) / सयानि (clever) / न कहति (does not say) / कछु (anything) / जागति (awakening) / मनहुँ (as if) / मसानु (cremation ground)
ramacharitamanas::2129.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2129.essence: Some silences confirm ruin more clearly than words.
ramacharitamanas::2129.simple_meaning: Dasharath collapses, pleading with Kaikeyi to stop the destruction, but she stays silent and unmoved.
ramacharitamanas::2129.simple_insight: Silence can be as devastating as speech when a heart has already chosen its wound.
ramacharitamanas::2129.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has already been shattered by Kaikeyi’s demand. He falls to the ground, begging her to stop this ruin, but she remains cold and silent. The scene freezes the instant when family love gives way to irreversible loss.
ramacharitamanas::2129.modern_relevance: You are pleading in a kitchen at midnight, asking someone not to say the thing that will break everyone. They go quiet, and that silence says the decision is already made.
ramacharitamanas::2129.insight: It shows how to recognize a moment when persuasion has ended and damage has begun.

ramacharitamanas::2130.verse_sanskrit: राम राम रट बिकल भुआलू। जनु बिनु पंख बिहंग बेहालू॥ हृदयँ मनाव भोरु जनि होई। रामहि जाइ कहै जनि कोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2130.verse_hindi: राजा 'राम-राम' रट रहे हैं और ऐसे व्याकुल हैं, जैसे कोई पक्षी पंख के बिना बेहाल हो। वे अपने हृदय में मनाते हैं कि सबेरा न हो और कोई जाकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी से यह बात न कहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2130.english_translation: King Dasharath cries, "Ram, Ram," and is as helpless as a bird without wings. In his heart he begs that dawn not come, so no one goes to tell Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2130.translation_literal: राम राम (Ram, Ram) / रट (repeating) / बिकल (distressed) / भुआलू (the king) / जनु (as if) / बिनु (without) / पंख (wings) / बिहंग (bird) / बेहालू (helpless) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / मनाव (he begs) / भोरु (dawn) / जनि (do not) / होई (happen) / रामहि (to Ram) / जाइ (going) / कहै (say) / जनि (do not) / कोई (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::2130.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2130.essence: Grief clings to the beloved's name and fears the coming day.
ramacharitamanas::2130.simple_meaning: Dasharath is overwhelmed with grief. He keeps repeating Ram's name and fears the morning, because dawn would bring the news to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2130.simple_insight: Some grief is so deep it wants to stop time itself.
ramacharitamanas::2130.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has just collapsed under the pain of Kaikeyi's demand and Ram's impending exile. Now he sits in helpless anguish, crying Ram's name, afraid of dawn because dawn means the world will move forward and Ram will be told.
ramacharitamanas::2130.modern_relevance: You stare at your phone before sunrise, dreading the message that will change everything. Part of you wants the morning to stay away a little longer.
ramacharitamanas::2130.insight: It shows grief as helplessness, not drama, and reveals how love can make even morning feel threatening.

ramacharitamanas::2131.verse_sanskrit: उदउ करहु जनि रबि रघुकुल गुर। अवध बिलोकि सूल होइहि उर॥ भूप प्रीति कैकइ कठिनाई। उभय अवधि बिधि रची बनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2131.verse_hindi: हे रघुकुल के गुरु (बड़ेरे, मूलपुरुष) सूर्य भगवान् ! आप अपना उदय न करें। अयोध्या को (बेहाल) देखकर आपके हृदय में बड़ी पीड़ा होगी। राजा की प्रीति और कैकेयी की निष्ठुरता दोनों को ब्रह्मा ने सीमा तक रचकर बनाया है (अर्थात राजा प्रेम की सीमा है और कैकेयी निष्ठुरता की) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2131.english_translation: O sun, guru of the Raghu clan, do not rise. If you look upon Ayodhya, grief will fill your heart. The king's love and Kaikeyi's harshness were both fashioned by fate to their limit.
ramacharitamanas::2131.translation_literal: उदउ (rise) / करहु (do) / जनि (do not) / रबि (sun) / रघुकुल (Raghu clan) / गुर (guru) / अवध (Ayodhya) / बिलोकि (seeing) / सूल (pain) / होइहि (will become) / उर (heart) / भूप (king) / प्रीति (love) / कैकइ (Kaikeyi) / कठिनाई (harshness) / उभय (both) / अवधि (limit) / बिधि (fate) / रची (fashioned) / बनाई (made)
ramacharitamanas::2131.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2131.essence: Even sunrise feels painful when grief has taken over the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2131.simple_meaning: The poet begs the sun not to rise, because dawn will only deepen the king's grief over Ayodhya, love, and Kaikeyi's cruelty.
ramacharitamanas::2131.simple_insight: Some mornings do not feel like relief. They feel like the start of a grief you cannot stop.
ramacharitamanas::2131.detailed_meaning: Dasharath lies in Ayodhya, shattered by Ram's exile and Kaikeyi's demand. As dawn approaches, the poet imagines even the sun as a compassionate witness who should delay rising, because the city itself has become unbearable to see.
ramacharitamanas::2131.modern_relevance: You wake before sunrise after a night of bad news, staring at the ceiling because morning means facing the same wound again. The day arrives, but your heart is not ready.
ramacharitamanas::2131.insight: It turns dawn into a measure of grief, showing how the world can feel cruel when the heart is broken.

ramacharitamanas::2132.verse_sanskrit: बिलपत नृपहि भयउ भिनुसारा। बीना बेनु संख धुनि द्वारा॥ पढ़हिं भाट गुन गावहिं गायक। सुनत नृपहि जनु लागहिं सायक ॥
ramacharitamanas::2132.verse_hindi: विलाप करते-करते ही राजा को सबेरा हो गया! राज द्वार पर वीणा, बाँसुरी और शंख की ध्वनि होने लगी। भाट लोग विरुदावली पढ़ रहे हैं और गवैये गुणों का गान कर रहे हैं। सुनने पर राजा को वे बाण जैसे लगते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2132.english_translation: Wailing, the king was overtaken by dawn. At the gate, the sounds of veena, flute, and conch arose. Bards recited praises and singers sang his virtues. Hearing them, the king felt as if arrows struck him.
ramacharitamanas::2132.translation_literal: बिलपत (wailing) / नृपहि (to the king) / भयउ (became) / भिनुसारा (dawn) / बीना (veena) / बेनु (flute) / संख (conch) / धुनि (sound) / द्वारा (at the gate) / पढ़हिं (recite) / भाट (bards) / गुन (virtues) / गावहिं (sing) / गायक (singers) / सुनत (hearing) / नृपहि (to the king) / जनु (as if) / लागहिं (strike) / सायक (arrows)
ramacharitamanas::2132.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2132.essence: Joy becomes an arrow when the heart is already wounded.
ramacharitamanas::2132.simple_meaning: The king keeps grieving until morning arrives. Festive sounds and praise at the palace gate only deepen his pain, because everything reminds him of Ram's exile.
ramacharitamanas::2132.simple_insight: Grief can turn even celebration into pain when the heart is fixed on loss.
ramacharitamanas::2132.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath lies shattered by Ram's exile. Dawn comes, and the palace fills with music, praise, and ritual sounds at the gate. Instead of comfort, each sound pierces him like an arrow because his heart is already broken.
ramacharitamanas::2132.modern_relevance: You hear wedding drums from the next street while sitting in a silent room after bad news. The world keeps celebrating, but your chest cannot join it.
ramacharitamanas::2132.insight: It shows how sorrow can make ordinary joy feel painful and intrusive.

ramacharitamanas::2133.verse_sanskrit: मंगल सकल सोहाहिं न कैसें। सहगामिनिहि बिभूषन जैसें॥ तेहि निसि नीद परी नहिं काहू। राम दरस लालसा उछाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2133.verse_hindi: राजा को ये सब मंगल साज कैसे नहीं सुहा रहे हैं, जैसे पति के साथ सती होने वाली स्त्री को आभूषण! श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन की लालसा और उत्साह के कारण उस रात्रि में किसी को भी नींद नहीं आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2133.english_translation: How can all these auspicious decorations please the king, like ornaments on a woman going with her husband onto the funeral pyre? That night no one slept, because longing to see Ram and excitement kept everyone awake.
ramacharitamanas::2133.translation_literal: मंगल (auspicious things) / सकल (all) / सोहाहिं (look beautiful, please) / न (not) / कैसें (how) / सहगामिनिहि (for the woman going with her husband) / बिभूषन (ornaments) / जैसें (like) / तेहि (that) / निसि (night) / नीद (sleep) / परी (fell) / नहिं (not) / काहू (to anyone) / राम (Ram) / दरस (sight) / लालसा (longing) / उछाहू (joy, eagerness)
ramacharitamanas::2133.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2133.essence: Longing for Ram turns celebration into wakeful waiting.
ramacharitamanas::2133.simple_meaning: The usual signs of celebration do not feel festive here. Everyone stays awake through the night, held by longing and excitement for Ram's sight.
ramacharitamanas::2133.simple_insight: Deep longing can make even celebration feel like waiting.
ramacharitamanas::2133.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya has dressed itself for Ram's return, but the city feels more like a house holding its breath. The decorations, the sleepless night, and the rising anticipation all show how completely Ram's presence has taken over the moment.
ramacharitamanas::2133.modern_relevance: You refresh your phone all night before someone you love arrives at the airport. The room is ready, the bags are packed, but sleep won't come because the waiting itself has become alive.
ramacharitamanas::2133.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the emotional charge of anticipation.

ramacharitamanas::2134.verse_sanskrit: द्वार भीर सेवक सचिव कहहिं उदित रबि देखि। जागेउ अजहुँ न अवधपति कारनु कवनु बिसेषि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2134.verse_hindi: राजद्वार पर मंत्रियों और सेवकों की भीड़ लगी है। वे सब सूर्य को उदय हुआ देखकर कहते हैं कि ऐसा कौन सा विशेष कारण है कि अवधपति दशरथजी अभी तक नहीं जागे? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2134.english_translation: The ministers and servants crowd the palace gate, and seeing the sun rise, they wonder what special reason keeps the king of Ayodhya from waking.
ramacharitamanas::2134.translation_literal: द्वार (at the gate) / भीर (crowd) / सेवक (servants) / सचिव (ministers) / कहहिं (say) / उदित (risen) / रबि (sun) / देखि (seeing) / जागेउ (has awakened) / अजहुँ (still) / न (not) / अवधपति (lord of Ayodhya) / कारनु (reason) / कवनु (what) / बिसेषि (special)
ramacharitamanas::2134.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2134.essence: A broken routine can announce hidden grief.
ramacharitamanas::2134.simple_meaning: The ministers and servants gather at the palace gate and notice that Dasharath has not woken up, which is unusual for him.
ramacharitamanas::2134.simple_insight: Even ordinary routines can signal that something is deeply wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2134.detailed_meaning: At Ayodhya’s palace gate, ministers and servants stand in a crowd as dawn breaks. Dasharath normally rises before this, so his continued sleep feels ominous. The verse builds quiet suspense before the news of his grief is faced.
ramacharitamanas::2134.modern_relevance: You check your phone at sunrise and see no reply from the person who always answers by dawn. The silence itself becomes the warning.
ramacharitamanas::2134.insight: It trains attention on small disruptions that reveal larger emotional or physical crisis.

ramacharitamanas::2135.verse_sanskrit: पछिले पहर भूपु नित जागा। आजु हमहि बड़ अचरजु लागा॥ जाहु सुमंत्र जगावहु जाई। कीजिअ काजु रजायसु पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2135.verse_hindi: राजा नित्य ही रात के पिछले पहर जाग जाया करते हैं, किन्तु आज हमें बड़ा आश्चर्य हो रहा है। हे सुमंत्र! जाओ, जाकर राजा को जगाओ। उनकी आज्ञा पाकर हम सब काम करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2135.english_translation: The king always woke in the last watch of the night, but today we are greatly surprised. Go, Sumantra, wake him and return. We will do the work after receiving his command.
