ramacharitamanas::2135.translation_literal: पछिले (later) / पहर (watch of the night) / भूपु (king) / नित (always) / जागा (woke) / आजु (today) / हमहि (to us) / बड़ (great) / अचरजु (surprise) / लागा (seemed) / जाहु (go) / सुमंत्र (Sumantra) / जगावहु (wake) / जाई (going) / कीजिअ (let be done) / काजु (work) / रजायसु (command) / पाई (having received)
ramacharitamanas::2135.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2135.essence: A ruler’s missing morning breaks the rhythm of the whole kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::2135.simple_meaning: The king usually woke before dawn, so everyone is shocked that he has not risen. They ask Sumantra to wake him so they can begin their work only after his command.
ramacharitamanas::2135.simple_insight: A small delay reveals something is deeply wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2135.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace is already uneasy after the night’s grief. The ministers and servants notice that Dasharath has not risen at his usual hour, and that absence itself feels alarming. They send Sumantra to wake him, still assuming the king will issue orders as always.
ramacharitamanas::2135.modern_relevance: You open the office chat and see the one person who always replies first has gone silent. The whole team feels it at once: something is off before anyone says a word.
ramacharitamanas::2135.insight: It turns ordinary routine into a signal that the household’s order has begun to break.

ramacharitamanas::2136.verse_sanskrit: गए सुमंत्रु तब राउर माहीं। देखि भयावन जात डेराहीं॥ धाइ खाई जनु जाइ न हेरा। मानहुँ बिपति बिषाद बसेरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2136.verse_hindi: तब सुमंत्र रावले (राजमहल) में गए, पर महल को भयानक देखकर वे जाते हुए डर रहे हैं। (ऐसा लगता है) मानो दौड़कर काट खाएगा, उसकी ओर देखा भी नहीं जाता। मानो विपत्ति और विषाद ने वहाँ डेरा डाल रखा हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2136.english_translation: Then Sumantra entered the royal palace, but the sight of it was so fearsome that he went in trembling. It was as if something would bite him if he rushed forward; no one could even bear to look at it. It seemed as though disaster and sorrow had made their home there.
ramacharitamanas::2136.translation_literal: गए (went) / सुमंत्रु (Sumantra) / तब (then) / राउर (royal) / माहीं (inside) / देखि (seeing) / भयावन (fearsome) / जात (going) / डेराहीं (they feared) / धाइ (rushing) / खाई (bite) / जनु (as if) / जाइ (going) / न (not) / हेरा (seen) / मानहुँ (as if) / बिपति (disaster) / बिषाद (sorrow) / बसेरा (dwelling-place)
ramacharitamanas::2136.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2136.essence: Grief can make a home feel uninhabitable.
ramacharitamanas::2136.simple_meaning: Sumantra enters the palace and feels fear and heaviness everywhere. The place itself seems filled with disaster and grief.
ramacharitamanas::2136.simple_insight: Some places carry sorrow so strongly that even entering them feels тяжёлым and unsafe.
ramacharitamanas::2136.detailed_meaning: Sumantra goes into Dasharath's palace in Ayodhya, but the atmosphere has turned ominous. The royal home no longer feels like a place of order or joy; grief seems to have taken over before anyone even speaks.
ramacharitamanas::2136.modern_relevance: You walk into a house after a family argument and feel the silence before anyone says a word. The room itself seems to hold the hurt.
ramacharitamanas::2136.insight: It turns emotional atmosphere into something visible, showing how grief can change a place before any conversation begins.

ramacharitamanas::2137.verse_sanskrit: पूछें कोउ न ऊतरु देई। गए जेहिं भवन भूप कैकेई॥ कहि जयजीव बैठ सिरु नाई। देखि भूप गति गयउ सुखाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2137.verse_hindi: पूछने पर कोई जवाब नहीं देता। वे उस महल में गए, जहाँ राजा और कैकेयी थे 'जय जीव' कहकर सिर नवाकर (वंदना करके) बैठे और राजा की दशा देखकर तो वे सूख ही गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2137.english_translation: No one answers when asked. He entered the chamber where King Dasharath and Kaikeyi sat. Saying "Victory and long life," he bowed his head, and seeing the king's condition, he was dried up with shock.
ramacharitamanas::2137.translation_literal: पूछें (on asking) / कोउ (someone) / न (not) / ऊतरु (answer) / देई (gives) / गए (went) / जेहिं (in which) / भवन (palace/chamber) / भूप (king) / कैकेई (Kaikeyi) / कहि (saying) / जयजीव (victory and long life) / बैठ (sat) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing) / देखि (seeing) / भूप (king) / गति (condition) / गयउ (went) / सुखाई (dried up)
ramacharitamanas::2137.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2137.essence: Silence and a broken face reveal the truth before speech does.
ramacharitamanas::2137.simple_meaning: No one gives Sumantra an answer. He enters the royal chamber, bows respectfully, and is stunned by the king's condition.
ramacharitamanas::2137.simple_insight: Some sights need no explanation. Grief can be recognized before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2137.detailed_meaning: Sumantra enters Dasharath's chamber in Ayodhya and finds silence instead of welcome. He greets the king and Kaikeyi with respect, but Dasharath's ruined state shocks him before anyone speaks. This is the moment the hidden disaster begins to show itself.
ramacharitamanas::2137.modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room and the air tells you everything before the family speaks. The face on the bed explains what no one is ready to say.
ramacharitamanas::2137.insight: It shifts attention from words to visible suffering, teaching the reader to read a room with compassion.

ramacharitamanas::2138.verse_sanskrit: सोच बिकल बिबरन महि परेऊ। मानहु कमल मूलु परिहरेऊ॥ सचिउ सभीत सकइ नहिं पूँछी। बोली असुभ भरी सुभ छूँछी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2138.verse_hindi: (देखा कि-) राजा सोच से व्याकुल हैं, चेहरे का रंग उड़ गया है। जमीन पर ऐसे पड़े हैं, मानो कमल जड़ छोड़कर (जड़ से उखड़कर) (मुर्झाया) पड़ा हो। मंत्री मारे डर के कुछ पूछ नहीं सकते। तब अशुभ से भरी हुई और शुभ से विहीन कैकेयी बोली- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2138.english_translation: The king lay on the ground, pale and bewildered, like a lotus torn from its root. The ministers, afraid, could not ask anything. Then Kaikeyi, full of ill omen and empty of goodness, spoke.
ramacharitamanas::2138.translation_literal: सोच (grief/thought) / बिकल (agitated) / बिबरन (colorless/pale) / महि परेऊ (fell on the ground) / मानहु (as if) / कमल (lotus) / मूलु (root) / परिहरेऊ (left/abandoned) / सचिउ (minister) / सभीत (fearful) / सकइ नहिं (cannot) / पूँछी (ask) / बोली (spoke) / असुभ (inauspicious) / भरी (filled) / सुभ (auspiciousness/goodness) / छूँछी (empty)
ramacharitamanas::2138.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2138.essence: Grief can strip a king down to helplessness.
ramacharitamanas::2138.simple_meaning: Dasharath lies collapsed in grief, drained of life. His ministers are too frightened to speak, and Kaikeyi begins to talk with a dark, joyless heart.
ramacharitamanas::2138.simple_insight: Grief can make power look fragile, and fear can silence everyone around it.
ramacharitamanas::2138.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sumantra has entered the palace and found King Dasharath shattered by the shock of Ram’s exile. The king lies pale on the ground, unable to steady himself. The ministers stand frozen, and Kaikeyi is about to speak again, deepening the family’s ruin.
ramacharitamanas::2138.modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room and see the strongest person in your family suddenly collapsed, unable to answer simple questions. Everyone lowers their voice because the room itself feels broken.
ramacharitamanas::2138.insight: It shifts attention from outward authority to the inner collapse that fear and grief can cause.

ramacharitamanas::2139.verse_sanskrit: परी न राजहि नीद निसि हेतु जान जगदीसु। रामु रामु रटि भोरु किय कहइ ना मरमु महीसु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2139.verse_hindi: राजा को रातभर नींद नहीं आई, इसका कारण जगदीश्वर ही जानें। इन्होंने 'राम राम' रटकर सबेरा कर दिया, परन्तु इसका भेद राजा कुछ भी नहीं बतलाते ॥
ramacharitamanas::2139.english_translation: The king did not sleep through the night; only the lord of the world knows why. He kept chanting "Ram, Ram" until dawn, yet the king revealed no secret.
ramacharitamanas::2139.translation_literal: परी (fell) / न (not) / राजहि (to the king) / नीद (sleep) / निसि (night) / हेतु (cause) / जान (know) / जगदीसु (the lord of the world) / रामु (Ram) / रामु (Ram) / रटि (chanting) / भोरु (dawn) / किय (made) / कहइ (says) / ना (not) / मरमु (secret) / महीसु (king)
ramacharitamanas::2139.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2139.essence: Grief can wake the whole night and still hide its cause.
ramacharitamanas::2139.simple_meaning: The king stayed awake all night, chanting Ram's name, but he would not reveal what was wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2139.simple_insight: Some pain is so deep it can only be carried, not yet spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2139.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath lies broken after hearing the news of Ram's exile. The palace is tense, and the king spends the night sleepless, repeating Ram's name. Yet he still does not speak the reason for his collapse.
ramacharitamanas::2139.modern_relevance: You lie awake after a message that changed everything, staring at the ceiling and repeating one name in your head. The truth is there, but you cannot say it yet.
ramacharitamanas::2139.insight: It captures grief before confession: the body shows the wound before words do.

ramacharitamanas::2140.verse_sanskrit: आनहु रामहि बेगि बोलाई। समाचार तब पूँछेहु आई॥ चलेउ सुमंत्रु राय रुख जानी। लखी कुचालि कीन्हि कछु रानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2140.verse_hindi: तुम जल्दी राम को बुला लाओ। तब आकर समाचार पूछना। राजा का रुख जानकर सुमंत्रजी चले, समझ गए कि रानी ने कुछ कुचाल की है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2140.english_translation: Bring Ram quickly. Then come back and ask about the news. Sumantra went, reading the king's mood, and realized the queen had done some mischief.
ramacharitamanas::2140.translation_literal: आनहु (bring) / रामहि (Ram) / बेगि (quickly) / बोलाई (having called) / समाचार (news) / तब (then) / पूँछेहु (ask) / आई (coming) / चलेउ (went) / सुमंत्रु (Sumantra) / राय (king's) / रुख (mood/face) / जानी (having known) / लखी (saw) / कुचालि (mischief) / कीन्हि (did) / कछु (some) / रानी (queen)
ramacharitamanas::2140.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2140.essence: Trouble is often visible before the truth is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2140.simple_meaning: The king orders Ram to be called at once, and Sumantra notices that the queen has caused trouble.
ramacharitamanas::2140.simple_insight: A tense situation often reveals itself before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::2140.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, King Dasharath is already shaken. He sends for Ram immediately, but says the news should be asked later. Sumantra reads the king's strained mood and suspects Kaikeyi has engineered something harmful.
ramacharitamanas::2140.modern_relevance: A manager says, “Bring her in now, ask questions later,” and the room goes quiet. Everyone can feel something is wrong before the explanation arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2140.insight: It trains attention to read tension and recognize hidden conflict early.

ramacharitamanas::2141.verse_sanskrit: सोच बिकल मग परइ न पाऊ। रामहि बोलि कहिहि का राऊ॥ उर धरि धीरजु गयउ दुआरें। पूँछहिं सकल देखि मनु मारें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2141.verse_hindi: सुमंत्र सोच से व्याकुल हैं, रास्ते पर पैर नहीं पड़ता (आगे बढ़ा नहीं जाता), (सोचते हैं-) रामजी को बुलाकर राजा क्या कहेंगे? किसी तरह हृदय में धीरज धरकर वे द्वार पर गए। सब लोग उनको मन मारे (उदास) देखकर पूछने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2141.english_translation: Sumantra was overwhelmed with worry and could not step forward. He thought, "What will the king say after calling Ram?" Holding his courage in his heart, he went to the door. Seeing him downcast, everyone began to ask him questions.
ramacharitamanas::2141.translation_literal: सोच (worry) / बिकल (disturbed) / मग (road) / परइ (falls) / न (not) / पाऊ (foot) / रामहि (Ram) / बोलि (calling) / कहिहि (will say) / का (what) / राऊ (king)॥ / उर (heart) / धरि (placing) / धीरजु (courage) / गयउ (went) / दुआरें (to the door)॥ / पूँछहिं (ask) / सकल (all) / देखि (seeing) / मनु (mind) / मारें (downcast)॥
ramacharitamanas::2141.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2141.essence: Worry can stop the feet before the truth is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2141.simple_meaning: Sumantra is so troubled that he cannot even walk properly. He gathers himself, goes to the door, and everyone notices his sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2141.simple_insight: Some grief is visible before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2141.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has just been sent to bring Ram. He already senses that Kaikeyi’s demand has poisoned the palace, and he walks toward the door with dread in his chest. His face reveals enough for everyone to question him.
ramacharitamanas::2141.modern_relevance: You get the call from a family member and already know bad news is waiting. Your steps slow before you even open the message. The body often knows the burden before the mind admits it.
ramacharitamanas::2141.insight: It shows how inner distress leaks into movement and expression, even before explanation begins.

ramacharitamanas::2142.verse_sanskrit: समाधानु करि सो सबही का। गयउ जहाँ दिनकर कुल टीका॥ राम सुमंत्रहि आवत देखा। आदरु कीन्ह पिता सम लेखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2142.verse_hindi: सब लोगों का समाधान करके (किसी तरह समझा-बुझाकर) सुमंत्र वहाँ गए, जहाँ सूर्यकुल के तिलक श्री रामचन्द्रजी थे। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सुमंत्र को आते देखा तो पिता के समान समझकर उनका आदर किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2142.english_translation: After reassuring everyone, Sumantra went to where Ram, the jewel of the सूर्यवंश, was. Ram saw Sumantra arrive and honored him as a father.
ramacharitamanas::2142.translation_literal: समाधानु (reassurance) / करि (having done) / सो (that) / सबही (everyone's) / का (of) / गयउ (went) / जहाँ (where) / दिनकर (sun) / कुल (clan) / टीका (tilak/jewel) / राम (Ram) / सुमंत्रहि (Sumantra) / आवत (coming) / देखा (saw) / आदरु (respect) / कीन्ह (did) / पिता (father) / सम (like) / लेखा (considering)
ramacharitamanas::2142.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2142.simple_meaning: Sumantra calms everyone down and goes to Ram. Ram welcomes him with the respect due to a father.
ramacharitamanas::2142.simple_insight: Respect can move both ways: the messenger carries duty, and the receiver meets him with honor.
ramacharitamanas::2142.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has just been sent to bring Ram. After calming the household, he reaches Ram. Ram, seeing him arrive, treats the royal messenger like a father, showing the tenderness and dignity that define this exile scene.
ramacharitamanas::2142.modern_relevance: You walk into a room carrying bad news, and the person you feared most greets you with warmth. That unexpected respect can steady an entire crisis.
ramacharitamanas::2142.insight: It shifts attention from rank to character, showing how dignity can survive even in painful moments.

ramacharitamanas::2143.verse_sanskrit: निरखि बदनु कहि भूप रजाई। रघुकुलदीपहि चलेउ लेवाई॥ रामु कुभाँति सचिव सँग जाहीं। देखि लोग जहँ तहँ बिलखाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2143.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के मुख को देखकर और राजा की आज्ञा सुनाकर वे रघुकुल के दीपक श्री रामचन्द्रजी को (अपने साथ) लिवा चले। श्री रामचन्द्रजी मंत्री के साथ बुरी तरह से (बिना किसी लवाजमे के) जा रहे हैं, यह देखकर लोग जहाँ-तहाँ विषाद कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2143.english_translation: Seeing his face and obeying the king's order, he led Raghu's lamp away. Rama, going with the minister in a humble way, made people everywhere grieve as they watched.
ramacharitamanas::2143.translation_literal: निरखि (seeing) / बदनु (face) / कहि (saying) / भूप (king) / रजाई (order) / रघुकुलदीपहि (Raghu-clan lamp) / चलेउ (went) / लेवाई (to take along)॥ / रामु (Rama) / कुभाँति (in a poor/humble manner) / सचिव (minister) / सँग (with) / जाहीं (goes) / देखि (seeing) / लोग (people) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / बिलखाहीं (grieve)
ramacharitamanas::2143.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2143.essence: Rama's humble departure turns the whole city to grief.
ramacharitamanas::2143.simple_meaning: Sumantra takes Rama away after obeying the king's order, and everyone who sees it feels deep sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2143.simple_insight: Some departures hurt so much that even bystanders feel the loss.
ramacharitamanas::2143.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has come to take Rama from Ayodhya under Dasharath's command. Rama leaves with him in plain, unroyal simplicity, and the sight of that humble departure makes people everywhere break into grief.
ramacharitamanas::2143.modern_relevance: You watch someone leave a family gathering with one small bag and no ceremony, and the room goes quiet. Everyone knows something precious is being taken away.
ramacharitamanas::2143.insight: It frames exile as a public wound, not a private errand.

ramacharitamanas::2144.verse_sanskrit: जाइ दीख रघुबंसमनि नरपति निपट कुसाजु। सहमि परेउ लखि सिंघिनिहि मनहुँ बृद्ध गजराजु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2144.verse_hindi: रघुवंशमणि श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने जाकर देखा कि राजा अत्यन्त ही बुरी हालत में पड़े हैं, मानो सिंहनी को देखकर कोई बूढ़ा गजराज सहमकर गिर पड़ा हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2144.english_translation: Ram, jewel of Raghu's line, went and saw the king in a miserable state, trembling and falling like an old elephant before a lioness.
ramacharitamanas::2144.translation_literal: जाइ (having gone) / दीख (saw) / रघुबंसमनि (jewel of the Raghu line) / नरपति (king) / निपट (utterly) / कुसाजु (bad condition) / सहमि (in fear) / परेउ (fell) / लखि (seeing) / सिंघिनिहि (lioness) / मनहुँ (as if) / बृद्ध (old) / गजराजु (elephant king)
ramacharitamanas::2144.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2144.essence: Grief can bring a king down to helplessness.
ramacharitamanas::2144.simple_meaning: Ram sees King Dasharath collapsed in deep distress. The king’s fear and weakness are compared to an old elephant stunned by a lioness.
ramacharitamanas::2144.simple_insight: Some grief is so heavy it makes even a king look helpless.
ramacharitamanas::2144.detailed_meaning: Ram has just come to see Dasharath after Sumantra brings him from the palace. What he finds is not a king in command, but a father crushed by sorrow and fear. The simile shows how completely Dasharath has been broken.
ramacharitamanas::2144.modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room and the strongest person in your family can barely meet your eyes. Power, status, and age all vanish in the face of grief.
ramacharitamanas::2144.insight: It shifts attention from outward rank to inner collapse, showing how sorrow can strip away all dignity and control.

ramacharitamanas::2145.verse_sanskrit: सूखहिं अधर जरइ सबु अंगू। मनहुँ दीन मनिहीन भुअंगू॥ सरुष समीप दीखि कैकेई। मानहुँ मीचु घरीं गनि लेई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2145.verse_hindi: राजा के होठ सूख रहे हैं और सारा शरीर जल रहा है, मानो मणि के बिना साँप दुःखी हो रहा हो। पास ही क्रोध से भरी कैकेयी को देखा, मानो (साक्षात) मृत्यु ही बैठी (राजा के जीवन की अंतिम) घड़ियाँ गिन रही हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2145.english_translation: His lips dried up and his whole body burned, as if a snake without its jewel were suffering. Nearby stood angry Kaikeyi, like death itself counting the king’s final hours.
ramacharitamanas::2145.translation_literal: सूखहिं (dry up) / अधर (lips) / जरइ (burns) / सबु (whole) / अंगू (body) / मनहुँ (as if) / दीन (poor, bereft) / मनिहीन (without a jewel) / भुअंगू (snake) / सरुष (angry) / समीप (near) / दीखि (seeing) / कैकेई (Kaikeyi) / मानहुँ (as if) / मीचु (death) / घरीं (hours) / गनि (counting) / लेई (takes)
ramacharitamanas::2145.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2145.essence: Grief and anger together can feel like death arriving early.
ramacharitamanas::2145.simple_meaning: Dasharath is in unbearable distress, and Kaikeyi stands nearby like death waiting to finish the work.
ramacharitamanas::2145.simple_insight: Some moments feel like the end before the end has happened.
ramacharitamanas::2145.detailed_meaning: Dasharath lies in agony after hearing the blow that has shattered his household. His body is failing, and Kaikeyi stands near him in anger and tension. The scene deepens the king’s collapse before the next verse turns to Ram’s response.
ramacharitamanas::2145.modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed after a family argument has already done its damage. No one speaks the real sentence aloud, but everyone feels it: something precious is slipping away.
ramacharitamanas::2145.insight: It frames emotional collapse as visible, bodily, and unavoidable, preparing the reader for the consequence of broken trust.

ramacharitamanas::2146.verse_sanskrit: करुनामय मृदु राम सुभाऊ। प्रथम दीख दुखु सुना न काऊ॥ तदपि धीर धरि समउ बिचारी। पूँछी मधुर बचन महतारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2146.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का स्वभाव कोमल और करुणामय है। उन्होंने (अपने जीवन में) पहली बार यह दुःख देखा, इससे पहले कभी उन्होंने दुःख सुना भी न था। तो भी समय का विचार करके हृदय में धीरज धरकर उन्होंने मीठे वचनों से माता कैकेयी से पूछा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2146.english_translation: Compassionate and gentle by nature, Ram had never seen grief before. Still, he held steady, judged the moment, and spoke softly to his mother.
ramacharitamanas::2146.translation_literal: करुनामय (full of compassion) / मृदु (gentle) / राम (Ram) / सुभाऊ (nature) / प्रथम (first) / दीख (saw) / दुखु (grief) / सुना (heard) / न (not) / काऊ (any) / तदपि (still) / धीर (steady) / धरि (holding) / समउ (the moment) / बिचारी (considered) / पूँछी (asked) / मधुर (sweet) / बचन (words) / महतारी (mother)
ramacharitamanas::2146.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2146.essence: Gentle strength stays calm inside grief.
ramacharitamanas::2146.simple_meaning: Ram’s nature is gentle and compassionate. Even in a painful moment, he stays calm, thinks carefully, and speaks kindly to Kaikeyi.
ramacharitamanas::2146.simple_insight: Kindness is strongest when pain is highest.
ramacharitamanas::2146.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram enters Dasharath’s chamber and finds suffering everywhere. Kaikeyi stands nearby, and the air is heavy with grief and tension. Even then, Ram does not react sharply; he steadies himself and speaks with tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::2146.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is tense, and your first impulse is to snap back. Ram shows another way: notice the moment, hold yourself steady, and speak gently anyway.
ramacharitamanas::2146.insight: It teaches you to pause before reacting and answer pain without adding more pain.

ramacharitamanas::2147.verse_sanskrit: मोहि कहु मातु तात दुख कारन। करिअ जतन जेहिं होइ निवारन॥ सुनहु राम सबु कारनु एहू। राजहि तुम्ह पर बहुत सनेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2147.verse_hindi: हे माता! मुझे पिताजी के दुःख का कारण कहो, ताकि उसका निवारण हो (दुःख दूर हो) वह यत्न किया जाए। (कैकेयी ने कहा-) हे राम! सुनो, सारा कारण यही है कि राजा का तुम पर बहुत स्नेह है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2147.english_translation: Mother, father, tell me the cause of his sorrow, so I may work to remove it. Hear, Rama: the whole reason is that the king loves you deeply.
ramacharitamanas::2147.translation_literal: मोहि (to me) / कहु (tell) / मातु (mother) / तात (father) / दुख (sorrow) / कारन (cause) / करिअ (let be done) / जतन (effort, remedy) / जेहिं (by which) / होइ (becomes) / निवारन (removal)॥ सुनहु (listen) / राम (Rama) / सबु (all) / कारनु (cause) / एहू (this) / राजहि (to the king) / तुम्ह पर (on you) / बहुत (great) / सनेहू (affection, love)॥
ramacharitamanas::2147.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2147.essence: Love itself can become the wound that cannot be named.
ramacharitamanas::2147.simple_meaning: Rama asks what caused his father's pain so it can be fixed. Kaikeyi answers that Dasharath's sorrow comes from his deep love for Rama.
ramacharitamanas::2147.simple_insight: Even a loving bond can become the source of unbearable pain.
ramacharitamanas::2147.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Rama has just seen Dasharath stricken with grief and turns to Kaikeyi, asking what has happened and how the pain can be removed. Kaikeyi replies with the truth that will soon break the family: the king loves Rama deeply, and that love is the root of his sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2147.modern_relevance: You hear a parent go quiet after a family conversation, and you ask what went wrong. The answer is often not hatred, but love tangled with fear, duty, and loss.
ramacharitamanas::2147.insight: It shifts attention from the visible pain to the hidden attachment underneath it.

ramacharitamanas::2148.verse_sanskrit: देन कहेन्हि मोहि दुइ बरदाना। मागेउँ जो कछु मोहि सोहाना॥ सो सुनि भयउ भूप उर सोचू। छाड़ि न सकहिं तुम्हार सँकोचू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2148.verse_hindi: इन्होंने मुझे दो वरदान देने को कहा था। मुझे जो कुछ अच्छा लगा, वही मैंने माँगा। उसे सुनकर राजा के हृदय में सोच हो गया, क्योंकि ये तुम्हारा संकोच नहीं छोड़ सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::2148.english_translation: They had promised me two boons. I asked for whatever pleased me. Hearing that, the king's heart fell into worry, for you cannot shake off your hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::2148.translation_literal: देन कहेन्हि (they had said to give) / मोहि (to me) / दुइ बरदाना (two boons) / मागेउँ (I asked for) / जो कछु (whatever) / मोहि सोहाना (seemed pleasing to me) / तदपि (then) / सुनि (hearing) / भयउ (became) / भूप (the king) / उर (in the heart) / सोचू (worry) / छाड़ि (leaving) / न सकहिं (cannot) / तुम्हार सँकोचू (your hesitation)
ramacharitamanas::2148.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2148.essence: A promise spoken lightly can turn into a king's ruin.
ramacharitamanas::2148.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi says she used the two boons she was promised, and she asked for what she wanted. Hearing this, Dasharath becomes deeply troubled because he cannot overcome his own hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::2148.simple_insight: A hidden demand can trap everyone in grief. One private choice can become a public burden.
ramacharitamanas::2148.detailed_meaning: Kaikeyi reveals to Ram that she claimed the two boons long ago promised to her and asked for what she desired. Dasharath hears the demand and sinks into worry, already unable to undo the promise or face the cost of his hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::2148.modern_relevance: A family meeting starts with one person calmly saying, “You said I could ask for anything.” The room changes at once, because everyone knows a promise is about to become a wound.
ramacharitamanas::2148.insight: It shifts attention to the binding force of promises and the damage caused when duty is delayed until it becomes unbearable.

ramacharitamanas::2149.verse_sanskrit: सुत सनेहु इत बचनु उत संकट परेउ नरेसु। सकहु त आयसु धरहु सिर मेटहु कठिन कलेसु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2149.verse_hindi: इधर तो पुत्र का स्नेह है और उधर वचन (प्रतिज्ञा), राजा इसी धर्मसंकट में पड़ गए हैं। यदि तुम कर सकते हो, तो राजा की आज्ञा शिरोधार्य करो और इनके कठिन क्लेश को मिटाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2149.english_translation: One side is a son's love, the other a king's vow. If you can, uphold the order and end this hard suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2149.translation_literal: सुत सनेहु (son's love) / इत (here, on this side) / बचनु (word, vow) / उत (there, on that side) / संकट (crisis, dilemma) / परेउ (has fallen) / नरेसु (king) / सकहु (if able) / त (then) / आयसु (command, order) / धरहु (hold, bear) / सिर (on the head) / मेटहु (remove) / कठिन (hard) / कलेसु (suffering)
ramacharitamanas::2149.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2149.essence: A vow can split the heart in two.
ramacharitamanas::2149.simple_meaning: Dasharath is trapped between love for his son and the promise he already made. Kaikeyi urges obedience to that promise, saying it will end his suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2149.simple_insight: A promise can become heavier than desire, and keeping it can hurt most when it matters most.
ramacharitamanas::2149.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kaikeyi presses her demand while Dasharath is torn apart by love for Ram and the vow he once gave. This line names the crisis plainly: a king must choose between affection and his word.
ramacharitamanas::2149.modern_relevance: You promised your child you'd be there, but a prior commitment is pulling you elsewhere. The room goes quiet because both choices hurt, and everyone can feel the cost.
ramacharitamanas::2149.insight: It teaches you to see duty as a binding force that can override personal attachment.

ramacharitamanas::2150.verse_sanskrit: निधरक बैठि कहइ कटु बानी। सुनत कठिनता अति अकुलानी॥ जीभ कमान बचन सर नाना। मनहुँ महिप मृदु लच्छ समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2150.verse_hindi: कैकेयी बेधड़क बैठी ऐसी कड़वी वाणी कह रही है, जिसे सुनकर स्वयं कठोरता भी अत्यन्त व्याकुल हो उठी। जीभ धनुष है, वचन बहुत से तीर हैं और मानो राजा ही कोमल निशाने के समान हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2150.english_translation: Kaikeyi sat boldly and spoke harsh words. Hearing them, even hardness became deeply agitated. Her tongue was a bow, her words were many arrows, and the king seemed like a soft target.
ramacharitamanas::2150.translation_literal: निधरक (boldly / without fear) / बैठि (sitting) / कहइ (speaks) / कटु (bitter / harsh) / बानी (speech) / सुनत (hearing) / कठिनता (hardness) / अति (greatly) / अकुलानी (agitated) / जीभ (tongue) / कमान (bow) / बचन (words) / सर (arrows) / नाना (many) / मनहुँ (as if) / महिप (king) / मृदु (soft / tender) / लच्छ (target) / समाना (like / comparable)
ramacharitamanas::2150.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2150.essence: Words can strike like arrows and leave no shield.
ramacharitamanas::2150.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi speaks harshly and without hesitation. Her words land on Dasharath like arrows, leaving him shaken and exposed.
ramacharitamanas::2150.simple_insight: Harsh speech can wound more deeply than any weapon.
ramacharitamanas::2150.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi sits before Dasharath and begins the demand that will break the kingdom's heart. Tulsidas paints her speech as a bow and her words as arrows, showing how completely the king is trapped.
ramacharitamanas::2150.modern_relevance: A single cold message can turn a calm evening into a crisis. The tone is the weapon, and the person receiving it feels every word.
ramacharitamanas::2150.insight: It shows how speech can become attack, and how powerlessness feels when the mind is already pierced.

ramacharitamanas::2151.verse_sanskrit: जनु कठोरपनु धरें सरीरू। सिखइ धनुषबिद्या बर बीरू॥ सबु प्रसंगु रघुपतिहि सुनाई। बैठि मनहुँ तनु धरि निठुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2151.verse_hindi: (इस सारे साज-समान के साथ) मानो स्वयं कठोरपन श्रेष्ठ वीर का शरीर धारण करके धनुष विद्या सीख रहा है। श्री रघुनाथजी को सब हाल सुनाकर वह ऐसे बैठी है, मानो निष्ठुरता ही शरीर धारण किए हुए हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2151.english_translation: As if harshness itself had taken a body, she learned the art of the bow like a mighty warrior. After telling Raghunath the whole matter, she sat there as though cruelty itself had taken form.
ramacharitamanas::2151.translation_literal: जनु (as if) / कठोरपनु (harshness) / धरें (having taken) / सरीरू (body) / सिखइ (learns) / धनुषबिद्या (archery) / बर (excellent) / बीरू (warrior) / सबु (all) / प्रसंगु (matter) / रघुपतिहि (to Raghupati) / सुनाई (having told) / बैठि (having sat) / मनहुँ (as if) / तनु (body) / धरि (having taken) / निठुराई (cruelty, hardness)
ramacharitamanas::2151.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2151.essence: Cruelty can become a person's whole posture.
ramacharitamanas::2151.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is described as the very embodiment of harshness: she speaks like a warrior learning archery, then sits as if cruelty itself has taken shape.
ramacharitamanas::2151.simple_insight: Some people do not merely act harshly; they seem to become harshness itself.
ramacharitamanas::2151.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has already cornered Dasharath with her demands. She now lays out the full plot to Ram and sits unmoved, and Tulsidas paints her as cruelty made visible so the shock of her betrayal lands fully.
ramacharitamanas::2151.modern_relevance: You recognize the person who has rehearsed their coldness so long that it feels natural. The room goes quiet, and everyone can tell this is not a momentary mood.
ramacharitamanas::2151.insight: It shifts attention from a bad action to the character state that produces it.

ramacharitamanas::2152.verse_sanskrit: मन मुसुकाइ भानुकुल भानू। रामु सहज आनंद निधानू॥ बोले बचन बिगत सब दूषन। मृदु मंजुल जनु बाग बिभूषन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2152.verse_hindi: सूर्यकुल के सूर्य, स्वाभाविक ही आनंदनिधान श्री रामचन्द्रजी मन में मुस्कुराकर सब दूषणों से रहित ऐसे कोमल और सुंदर वचन बोले जो मानो वाणी के भूषण ही थे- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2152.english_translation: Smiling inwardly, the Sun of Raghu's line, Ram, the natural treasury of joy, spoke words free of every fault—soft, beautiful words that seemed like ornaments of speech.
ramacharitamanas::2152.translation_literal: मन (mind) / मुसुकाइ (smiling) / भानुकुल (sun-clan) / भानू (sun) / रामु (Ram) / सहज (natural) / आनंद (joy) / निधानू (treasury) / बोले (spoke) / बचन (words) / बिगत (free from) / सब (all) / दूषन (faults) / मृदु (soft) / मंजुल (beautiful) / जनु (as if) / बाग (speech) / बिभूषन (ornament)
ramacharitamanas::2152.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2152.essence: Gentleness can stand firm without losing strength.
ramacharitamanas::2152.simple_meaning: Ram smiles inwardly and answers gently, with words free of fault and full of beauty.
ramacharitamanas::2152.simple_insight: Strength does not need harshness. A calm mind can answer with grace.
ramacharitamanas::2152.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has just spoken harshly and shaken the royal household. Ram does not react with anger. He smiles inwardly and answers with faultless gentleness, showing the steady conduct that will carry the exile story forward.
ramacharitamanas::2152.modern_relevance: Someone snaps at you in front of everyone, and your first impulse is to strike back. Instead, you pause, smile inwardly, and answer so gently that the tension breaks.
ramacharitamanas::2152.insight: It teaches you to meet pressure with composed speech, not reflexive force.

ramacharitamanas::2153.verse_sanskrit: सुनु जननी सोइ सुतु बड़भागी। जो पितु मातु बचन अनुरागी॥ तनय मातु पितु तोषनिहारा। दुर्लभ जननि सकल संसारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2153.verse_hindi: हे माता! सुनो, वही पुत्र बड़भागी है, जो पिता-माता के वचनों का अनुरागी (पालन करने वाला) है। (आज्ञा पालन द्वारा) माता-पिता को संतुष्ट करने वाला पुत्र, हे जननी! सारे संसार में दुर्लभ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2153.english_translation: Listen, mother: the truly fortunate son is the one devoted to his father and mother’s words. A son who pleases his parents, mother, is rare in the whole world.
ramacharitamanas::2153.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / जननी (mother) / सोइ (that only) / सुतु (son) / बड़भागी (fortunate) / जो (who) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / बचन (words) / अनुरागी (attached with love) / तनय (son) / मातु (mother) / पितु (father) / तोषनिहारा (one who gives delight) / दुर्लभ (rare) / जननि (mother) / सकल (all) / संसारा (world)
ramacharitamanas::2153.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2153.essence: True greatness lies in lovingly honoring one’s parents.
ramacharitamanas::2153.simple_meaning: A truly blessed son is one who lovingly follows his parents' words and brings them joy. Such a child is rare in the world.
ramacharitamanas::2153.simple_insight: There is dignity in making your parents feel respected, seen, and at peace.
ramacharitamanas::2153.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram speaks to mother Kaikeyi before leaving for exile. He defines true worth not by power or success, but by loving obedience to father and mother. The verse becomes a quiet moral standard for the whole exile.
ramacharitamanas::2153.modern_relevance: You answer your mother’s call while standing in a crowded station, even though you are late and tired. No one sees the choice, but it reveals who you are.
ramacharitamanas::2153.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to filial responsibility and respectful action.

ramacharitamanas::2154.verse_sanskrit: मुनिगन मिलनु बिसेषि बन सबहि भाँति हित मोर। तेहि महँ पितु आयसु बहुरि संमत जननी तोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::2154.verse_hindi: वन में विशेष रूप से मुनियों का मिलाप होगा, जिसमें मेरा सभी प्रकार से कल्याण है। उसमें भी, फिर पिताजी की आज्ञा और हे जननी! तुम्हारी सम्मति है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2154.english_translation: In the forest, meeting the sages will be especially beneficial to me in every way. Above all, there is my father's command, and, mother, your approval too.
ramacharitamanas::2154.translation_literal: मुनिगन (the sages) / मिलनु (meeting) / बिसेषि (especially) / बन (forest) / सबहि भाँति (in every way) / हित (beneficial) / मोर (my) / तेहि महँ (in that too) / पितु (father's) / आयसु (command) / बहुरि (again / above all) / संमत (approved) / जननी (mother) / तोर (your)
ramacharitamanas::2154.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2154.essence: Right action includes both obligation and willing assent.
ramacharitamanas::2154.simple_meaning: Ram says that going to the forest will benefit him in every way, and he also counts his father's command and his mother's approval as reasons to go.
ramacharitamanas::2154.simple_insight: Duty becomes clearer when it is seen as both right and lovingly accepted.
ramacharitamanas::2154.detailed_meaning: Ram is speaking to Kaushalya in Ayodhya after Dasharath's command has sealed his exile. He explains that the forest will bring him the company of sages and that his father's order, along with his mother's consent, makes the path right.
ramacharitamanas::2154.modern_relevance: You are weighing a hard move that affects everyone you love. The facts are not all comfortable, but the decision feels clean because it honors both obligation and care.
ramacharitamanas::2154.insight: It teaches you to see duty as something that can be embraced, not merely endured.

ramacharitamanas::2155.verse_sanskrit: भरतु प्रानप्रिय पावहिं राजू। बिधि सब बिधि मोहि सनमुख आजू॥ जौं न जाउँ बन ऐसेहु काजा। प्रथम गनिअ मोहि मूढ़ समाजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2155.verse_hindi: और प्राण प्रिय भरत राज्य पावेंगे। (इन सभी बातों को देखकर यह प्रतीत होता है कि) आज विधाता सब प्रकार से मुझे सम्मुख हैं (मेरे अनुकूल हैं)। यदि ऐसे काम के लिए भी मैं वन को न जाऊँ तो मूर्खों के समाज में सबसे पहले मेरी गिनती करनी चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2155.english_translation: Bharat will receive the kingdom, and fate stands fully before me today. If I do not go to the forest for such a task, I should be counted first among fools.
ramacharitamanas::2155.translation_literal: भरतु (Bharat) / प्रानप्रिय (dear as life) / पावहिं (will receive) / राजू (kingdom) / बिधि (fate) / सब बिधि (in every way) / मोहि (to me) / सनमुख (facing) / आजू (today) / जौं (if) / न (not) / जाउँ (go) / बन (to the forest) / ऐसेहु (such) / काजा (task) / प्रथम (first) / गनिअ (be counted) / मोहि (me) / मूढ़ (foolish) / समाजा (among the assembly)
ramacharitamanas::2155.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2155.essence: Taking the easy reward becomes foolish when duty points elsewhere.
ramacharitamanas::2155.simple_meaning: Bharat sees that the kingdom will go to him, but he treats the forest exile as the only right choice. Refusing it would make him foolish.
ramacharitamanas::2155.simple_insight: Real duty is clear when comfort and status stop mattering.
ramacharitamanas::2155.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands in the middle of Ayodhya's crisis, speaking to his mother after Ram's exile has been set in motion. He sees that the throne is coming to him, but he rejects that gain and accepts the forest path as the only honorable response.
ramacharitamanas::2155.modern_relevance: Your promotion finally arrives, but it comes only because someone better was pushed aside. The title looks shiny for a moment, then Bharat's voice cuts through: taking what should not be yours is shame, not success.
ramacharitamanas::2155.insight: It shifts the mind from personal gain to the right action, even when the reward is obvious.

ramacharitamanas::2156.verse_sanskrit: सेवहिं अरँडु कलपतरु त्यागी। परिहरि अमृत लेहिं बिषु मागी॥ तेउ न पाइ अस समउ चुकाहीं। देखु बिचारि मातु मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2156.verse_hindi: जो कल्पवृक्ष को छोड़कर रेंड की सेवा करते हैं और अमृत त्याग कर विष माँग लेते हैं, हे माता! तुम मन में विचार कर देखो, वे (महामूर्ख) भी ऐसा मौका पाकर कभी न चूकेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2156.english_translation: Those who abandon the wish-fulfilling tree and serve a castor plant, who give up nectar and ask for poison, never miss such a chance. Mother, think carefully in your mind.
ramacharitamanas::2156.translation_literal: सेवहिं (serve) / अरँडु (castor plant) / कलपतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / त्यागी (having abandoned) / परिहरि (leaving aside) / अमृत (nectar) / लेहिं (take) / बिषु (poison) / मागी (asking for) / तेउ (those also) / न पाइ (not getting) / अस समउ (such an opportunity) / चुकाहीं (miss) / देखु (look) / बिचारि (consider) / मातु (mother) / मन माहीं (in the mind)
ramacharitamanas::2156.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2156.essence: A hard duty can be the greatest gift, not the worst loss.
ramacharitamanas::2156.simple_meaning: Choosing exile over the chance to rule is like rejecting a wish-fulfilling tree and asking for poison instead. Ram says such a chance should never be wasted.
ramacharitamanas::2156.simple_insight: Some duties feel like loss, but refusing them can be the real mistake.
ramacharitamanas::2156.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is speaking to Kaikeyi after learning he must leave for the forest. He compares rejecting exile's hard duty to foolishly abandoning a priceless gift and choosing harm instead.
ramacharitamanas::2156.modern_relevance: You get the promotion that could change your career, but it would mean breaking a promise you made quietly years ago. The easier gain is not always the better one.
ramacharitamanas::2156.insight: It reframes hardship as a rare duty that should not be dodged when it arrives.

ramacharitamanas::2157.verse_sanskrit: अंब एक दुखु मोहि बिसेषी। निपट बिकल नरनायकु देखी॥ थोरिहिं बात पितहि दुख भारी। होति प्रतीति न मोहि महतारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2157.verse_hindi: हे माता! मुझे एक ही दुःख विशेष रूप से हो रहा है, वह महाराज को अत्यन्त व्याकुल देखकर। इस थोड़ी सी बात के लिए ही पिताजी को इतना भारी दुःख हो, हे माता! मुझे इस बात पर विश्वास नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2157.english_translation: Mother, one grief troubles me most: seeing the king utterly distraught. I cannot believe that for so small a matter my father should suffer such deep pain.
ramacharitamanas::2157.translation_literal: अंब (mother) / एक (one) / दुखु (grief) / मोहि (to me) / बिसेषी (especially) / निपट (utterly) / बिकल (distressed) / नरनायकु (king, leader of men) / देखी (seeing) / थोरिहिं (for a little) / बात (matter) / पितहि (father) / दुख (pain) / भारी (heavy, great) / होति (becomes) / प्रतीति (belief) / न (not) / मोहि (to me) / महतारी (mother)
ramacharitamanas::2157.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2157.essence: A small cause becomes unbearable when it breaks a noble heart.
ramacharitamanas::2157.simple_meaning: Bharat says his deepest pain is seeing his father in extreme distress. He cannot accept that such a small matter could cause Dasharath such heavy sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2157.simple_insight: Love notices suffering first, especially in the one you revere most.
ramacharitamanas::2157.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before his mother and speaks of Dasharath's collapse. The king's anguish over Ram's exile has shaken the whole family, and Bharat cannot bear the sight of his father broken by what feels like a small cause.
ramacharitamanas::2157.modern_relevance: You see your parent trying to stay composed after bad news, but their voice cracks anyway. That moment hurts more than the problem itself, because their pain feels bigger than the event.
ramacharitamanas::2157.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the hidden cost of suffering on a loved one.

ramacharitamanas::2158.verse_sanskrit: राउ धीर गुन उदधि अगाधू। भा मोहि तें कछु बड़ अपराधू॥ जातें मोहि न कहत कछु राऊ। मोरि सपथ तोहि कहु सतिभाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2158.verse_hindi: क्योंकि महाराज तो बड़े ही धीर और गुणों के अथाह समुद्र हैं। अवश्य ही मुझसे कोई बड़ा अपराध हो गया है, जिसके कारण महाराज मुझसे कुछ नहीं कहते। तुम्हें मेरी सौगंध है, माता! तुम सच-सच कहो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2158.english_translation: The king is an unfathomable ocean of patience and virtue. I must have committed some great offense, because the king speaks to me no more. By my oath, mother, tell me the truth.
ramacharitamanas::2158.translation_literal: राउ (the king) / धीर (patient, steady) / गुन (virtues) / उदधि (ocean) / अगाधू (unfathomable) / भा (became) / मोहि (to me) / तें (than) / कछु (some) / बड़ (great) / अपराधू (offense) / जातें (because of which) / मोहि (to me) / न (not) / कहत (speaks) / कछु (anything) / राऊ (the king) / मोरि (my) / सपथ (oath) / तोहि (to you) / कहु (tell) / सतिभाऊ (truthfully)
ramacharitamanas::2158.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2158.essence: Silence from the beloved feels like proof of your own fault.
ramacharitamanas::2158.simple_meaning: Bharat feels the king must be deeply hurt by him, because the king is silent. He begs his mother to tell him the truth.
ramacharitamanas::2158.simple_insight: Love becomes self-blame when the person you honor falls silent.
ramacharitamanas::2158.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Kaikeyi and tries to understand why Dasharath will not speak to him. Seeing the king's grief and silence, he assumes he must be at fault and urgently asks his mother to tell him the truth.
ramacharitamanas::2158.modern_relevance: You text someone you deeply respect and get no reply. The silence feels louder than any accusation, and you start searching your own heart for what went wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2158.insight: It turns the reader from suspicion outward to humble self-examination before reacting.

ramacharitamanas::2159.verse_sanskrit: सहज सकल रघुबर बचन कुमति कुटिल करि जान। चलइ जोंक जल बक्रगति जद्यपि सलिलु समान ॥
ramacharitamanas::2159.verse_hindi: रघुकुल में श्रेष्ठ श्री रामचन्द्रजी के स्वभाव से ही सीधे वचनों को दुर्बुद्धि कैकेयी टेढ़ा ही करके जान रही है, जैसे यद्यपि जल समान ही होता है, परन्तु जोंक उसमें टेढ़ी चाल से ही चलती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2159.english_translation: Queen Kaikeyi, with a crooked mind, twists Ram's simple words. A leech moves crookedly through water, though water itself is straight and even.
ramacharitamanas::2159.translation_literal: सहज (natural / simple) / सकल (all) / रघुबर (best of the Raghu clan, Ram) / बचन (words) / कुमति (crooked understanding) / कुटिल करि (making crooked) / जान (knows / takes) / चलइ (moves) / जोंक (leech) / जल (water) / बक्रगति (crooked motion) / जद्यपि (although) / सलिलु (water) / समान (equal / alike)
ramacharitamanas::2159.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2159.essence: Crooked minds bend even the straightest words.
ramacharitamanas::2159.simple_meaning: Ram's words are simple, but Kaikeyi's twisted mind interprets them crookedly. The fault is not in the words; it is in the mind that distorts them.
ramacharitamanas::2159.simple_insight: You stop blaming reality for what your own distorted mind has bent out of shape.
ramacharitamanas::2159.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi is already trapped in suspicion and desire. Even Ram's plain, gentle speech cannot reach her clearly. Tulsidas compares her crooked reading of truth to a leech's uneven movement through water.
ramacharitamanas::2159.modern_relevance: Someone sends a calm text, and your anxious mind turns it into rejection. The message was plain; the distortion came from inside your own fear.
ramacharitamanas::2159.insight: It shifts attention from the speaker's words to the listener's interpretation.

ramacharitamanas::2160.verse_sanskrit: रहसी रानि राम रुख पाई। बोली कपट सनेहु जनाई॥ सपथ तुम्हार भरत कै आना। हेतु न दूसर मैं कछु जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2160.verse_hindi: रानी कैकेयी श्री रामचन्द्रजी का रुख पाकर हर्षित हो गई और कपटपूर्ण स्नेह दिखाकर बोली- तुम्हारी शपथ और भरत की सौगंध है, मुझे राजा के दुःख का दूसरा कुछ भी कारण विदित नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2160.english_translation: Queen Kaikeyi, seeing Ram's expression, became pleased and spoke with false affection: “By your vow and by Bharata's oath, I know no other reason for the king's sorrow.”
ramacharitamanas::2160.translation_literal: रहसी (became pleased) / रानि (queen) / राम रुख (Ram's expression) / पाई (having seen) / बोली (spoke) / कपट (deceitful) / सनेहु (affection) / जनाई (showed)॥ / सपथ (oath) / तुम्हार (your) / भरत कै (of Bharata) / आना (by the oath) / हेतु (cause) / न (not) / दूसर (other) / मैं (I) / कछु (anything) / जाना (know)॥
ramacharitamanas::2160.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2160.essence: False affection hides a motive that has already decided.
ramacharitamanas::2160.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi pretends affection and uses Ram's and Bharata's oaths to hide her real intention. She speaks as if she knows nothing else about Dasharath's sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2160.simple_insight: A mind bent on deception can sound loving while staying blind to its own motive.
ramacharitamanas::2160.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has already set the exile in motion. Seeing Ram's response, she quickly softens her face and speaks with false tenderness, trying to keep her demand covered. The scene shows how manipulation protects itself with words.
ramacharitamanas::2160.modern_relevance: A person smiles in the meeting, says “I only want what’s best,” and quietly steers everything toward their own agenda. The mask can be polished; the motive still leaks through.
ramacharitamanas::2160.insight: It exposes how self-deception dresses itself as care, and teaches the reader to notice motive beneath polite speech.

ramacharitamanas::2161.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह अपराध जोगु नहिं ताता। जननी जनक बंधु सुखदाता॥ राम सत्य सबु जो कछु कहहू। तुम्ह पितु मातु बचन रत अहहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2161.verse_hindi: हे तात! तुम अपराध के योग्य नहीं हो (तुमसे माता-पिता का अपराध बन पड़े यह संभव नहीं)। तुम तो माता-पिता और भाइयों को सुख देने वाले हो। हे राम! तुम जो कुछ कह रहे हो, सब सत्य है। तुम पिता-माता के वचनों (के पालन) में तत्पर हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2161.english_translation: O dear one, you are not fit for blame. You are the giver of joy to mother, father, and brothers. O Ram, whatever you say is true. You are devoted to your parents' words.
ramacharitamanas::2161.translation_literal: तुम (you) / अपराध (blame, fault) / जोगु (fit, worthy) / नहिं (not) / ताता (dear one) । जननी (mother) / जनक (father) / बंधु (brothers) / सुखदाता (giver of joy) ॥ राम (Ram) / सत्य (true) / सबु (all) / जो (whatever) / कछु (something, anything) / कहहू (you say) । तुम्ह (you) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / बचन (words) / रत (devoted, absorbed) / अहहू (you are) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2161.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2161.essence: Blame can hide inside praise when a request is already loaded.
ramacharitamanas::2161.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi flatters Ram while admitting he is blameless, loving, and obedient to his parents. She is steering him toward a request that will trap him in exile.
ramacharitamanas::2161.simple_insight: Not every gentle word is honest. A caring tone can still be used to push someone into harm.
ramacharitamanas::2161.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has already turned against Ram under Manthara's influence. Now she speaks sweetly to him, praising his goodness and his obedience to his parents. The praise is part of her manipulation, setting up the demand that will send Ram into exile.
ramacharitamanas::2161.modern_relevance: Someone praises your character too warmly before asking for something unreasonable. The kindness feels real, but the direction is already set. This verse catches the moment before the trap closes.
ramacharitamanas::2161.insight: It teaches you to hear praise and pressure separately, and to notice when affection is being used as leverage.

ramacharitamanas::2162.verse_sanskrit: पितहि बुझाइ कहहु बलि सोई। चौथेंपन जेहिं अजसु न होई॥ तुम्ह सम सुअन सुकृत जेहिं दीन्हे। उचित न तासु निरादरु कीन्हे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2162.verse_hindi: मैं तुम्हारी बलिहारी जाती हूँ, तुम पिता को समझाकर वही बात कहो, जिससे चौथेपन (बुढ़ापे) में इनका अपयश न हो। जिस पुण्य ने इनको तुम जैसे पुत्र दिए हैं, उसका निरादर करना उचित नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2162.english_translation: I bow to you. Speak to your father so that his old age is not stained with dishonor. It is not right to show disrespect to the great merit that gave him sons like you.
ramacharitamanas::2162.translation_literal: पितहि (to the father) / बुझाइ (persuading, explaining) / कहहु (speak) / बलि (I am devoted to you, I bow) / सोई (that only) / चौथेंपन (in old age) / जेहिं (by which) / अजसु (dishonor, infamy) / न (not) / होई (happens) / तुम्ह (your) / सम (like) / सुअन (good sons) / सुकृत (merit, good fortune) / जेहिं (by which) / दीन्हे (were given) / उचित (proper) / न (not) / तासु (that) / निरादरु (disrespect) / कीन्हे (to do)
ramacharitamanas::2162.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2162.essence: Soft words can carry a hard demand.
ramacharitamanas::2162.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi urges Ram to persuade Dasharath, saying his old age should not be disgraced and that the merit which gave him such sons deserves respect.
ramacharitamanas::2162.simple_insight: Flattery can hide a demand. The verse shows how words can be dressed as care while pushing someone toward harm.
ramacharitamanas::2162.detailed_meaning: Kaikeyi has already turned the moment with hidden intent. Now she speaks sweetly to Ram, asking him to talk to Dasharath so the king's old age will not be shamed. Beneath the softness is the pressure that will force exile.
ramacharitamanas::2162.modern_relevance: Someone starts with praise before asking for something they know will hurt another person. The smile feels warm, but the request is already a trap.
ramacharitamanas::2162.insight: It trains you to hear manipulation beneath affectionate language and to notice when concern is being used as leverage.

ramacharitamanas::2163.verse_sanskrit: लागहिं कुमुख बचन सुभ कैसे। मगहँ गयादिक तीरथ जैसे॥ रामहि मातु बचन सब भाए। जिमि सुरसरि गत सलिल सुहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2163.verse_hindi: कैकेयी के बुरे मुख में ये शुभ वचन कैसे लगते हैं जैसे मगध देश में गया आदिक तीर्थ! श्री रामचन्द्रजी को माता कैकेयी के सब वचन ऐसे अच्छे लगे जैसे गंगाजी में जाकर (अच्छे-बुरे सभी प्रकार के) जल शुभ, सुंदर हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2163.english_translation: How can these auspicious words fit such a wicked mouth, like holy pilgrimage sites in Magadha and Gaya? Yet all of Mother Kaikeyi's words seemed pleasing to Ram, just as water becomes pure and lovely in the Ganga.
ramacharitamanas::2163.translation_literal: लागहिं (fit/appear) / कुमुख (evil mouth) / बचन (words) / सुभ (auspicious) / कैसे (how) / मगहँ (in Magadha) / गयादिक (Gaya and others) / तीरथ (pilgrimage sites) / जैसे (like) / रामहि (to Ram) / मातु (mother's) / बचन (words) / सब (all) / भाए (were pleasing) / जिमि (just as) / सुरसरि (Ganga) / गत (gone to) / सलिल (water) / सुहाए (beautiful/auspicious)
ramacharitamanas::2163.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2163.essence: A pure heart can receive bitter words without becoming bitter.
ramacharitamanas::2163.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi’s words seem out of place coming from her mouth, yet Ram receives them as pleasing and pure, like water in the Ganga.
ramacharitamanas::2163.simple_insight: Love can purify what would otherwise feel bitter. The same words land differently when the heart receiving them is free of resentment.
ramacharitamanas::2163.detailed_meaning: Kaikeyi has spoken the words that will send Ram into exile, and the court is still reeling. Tulsidas pauses on the strange contrast: her speech is harsh in source, yet Ram hears it without bitterness, as if impurity itself had become sacred.
ramacharitamanas::2163.modern_relevance: Someone sends a message that should sting, but you read it after a long walk and a deep breath. The words are unchanged; your heart is not.
ramacharitamanas::2163.insight: It shifts attention from the speaker’s tone to the listener’s inner purity and steadiness.

ramacharitamanas::2164.verse_sanskrit: गइ मुरुछा रामहि सुमिरि नृप फिरि करवट लीन्ह। सचिव राम आगमन कहि बिनय समय सम कीन्ह ॥
ramacharitamanas::2164.verse_hindi: इतने में राजा की मूर्छा दूर हुई, उन्होंने राम का स्मरण करके ('राम! राम!' कहकर) फिरकर करवट ली। मंत्री ने श्री रामचन्द्रजी का आना कहकर समयानुकूल विनती की ॥
ramacharitamanas::2164.english_translation: The king's fainting passed as he remembered Ram and turned over. The minister then spoke of Ram's arrival and made a timely request.
ramacharitamanas::2164.translation_literal: गइ (went away) / मुरुछा (fainting) / रामहि (Ram) / सुमिरि (remembering) / नृप (king) / फिरि (again/turning) / करवट (side/turn) / लीन्ह (took) / सचिव (minister) / राम (Ram) / आगमन (arrival) / कहि (saying) / बिनय (humble request) / समय (time) / सम (appropriate) / कीन्ह (did/made)
ramacharitamanas::2164.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2164.essence: Remembering Ram brings the mind back from collapse.
ramacharitamanas::2164.simple_meaning: The king comes out of his fainting spell when he remembers Ram. Then the minister announces Ram's arrival and speaks at the right moment.
ramacharitamanas::2164.simple_insight: Even in collapse, remembering Ram brings a person back to awareness.
ramacharitamanas::2164.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has been overwhelmed by grief and shock. As he comes back to himself, he remembers Ram and turns over. At that exact moment, the minister speaks of Ram's arrival, setting up the next emotional turn in the scene.
ramacharitamanas::2164.modern_relevance: You wake from a panic blur, reach for your phone, and see the message you feared and hoped for. In that fragile second, memory and timing decide what you can bear next.
ramacharitamanas::2164.insight: It shifts attention from physical collapse to the restoring power of remembrance and right timing.

ramacharitamanas::2165.verse_sanskrit: अवनिप अकनि रामु पगु धारे। धरि धीरजु तब नयन उघारे॥ सचिवँ सँभारि राउ बैठारे। चरन परत नृप रामु निहारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2165.verse_hindi: जब राजा ने सुना कि श्री रामचन्द्र पधारे हैं तो उन्होंने धीरज धरके नेत्र खोले। मंत्री ने संभालकर राजा को बैठाया। राजा ने श्री रामचन्द्रजी को अपने चरणों में पड़ते (प्रणाम करते) देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2165.english_translation: When the king heard that Ram had arrived, he steadied himself and opened his eyes. The minister helped the king sit up. The king saw Ram bowing at his feet.
ramacharitamanas::2165.translation_literal: अवनिप (king) / अकनि (hearing) / रामु (Ram) / पगु (feet) / धारे (placed) / धरि (having held) / धीरजु (patience, composure) / तब (then) / नयन (eyes) / उघारे (opened) ॥ / सचिवँ (by the minister) / सँभारि (supporting) / राउ (the king) / बैठारे (was seated) ॥ / चरन (feet) / परत (falling) / नृप (king) / रामु (Ram) / निहारे (saw) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2165.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2165.essence: Composure returns only so the father can see his son bow.
ramacharitamanas::2165.simple_meaning: Dasharath regains enough composure to see Ram arrive, and he watches Ram bow at his feet.
ramacharitamanas::2165.simple_insight: Love can return a shattered heart to awareness, even for one brief, trembling moment.
ramacharitamanas::2165.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has been broken by the news of Ram's exile. Hearing that Ram has come, he gathers himself, opens his eyes, and is helped upright by the minister. The sight of Ram bowing before him deepens the father's grief and love at once.
ramacharitamanas::2165.modern_relevance: You are lying awake after a fight, too drained to speak, when the person you longed for finally walks in. The body lifts before the heart can explain why.
ramacharitamanas::2165.insight: It shifts attention from royal power to filial tenderness and the pain of separation.

ramacharitamanas::2166.verse_sanskrit: लिए सनेह बिकल उर लाई। गै मनि मनहुँ फनिक फिरि पाई॥ रामहि चितइ रहेउ नरनाहू। चला बिलोचन बारि प्रबाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2166.verse_hindi: स्नेह से विकल राजा ने रामजी को हृदय से लगा लिया। मानो साँप ने अपनी खोई हुई मणि फिर से पा ली हो। राजा दशरथजी श्री रामजी को देखते ही रह गए। उनके नेत्रों से आँसुओं की धारा बह चली ॥
ramacharitamanas::2166.english_translation: Filled with love, the king drew Ram to his heart. It was like a snake finding its lost jewel again. The king kept gazing at Ram, and a stream of tears flowed from his eyes.
ramacharitamanas::2166.translation_literal: लिए (having taken) / सनेह (with love) / बिकल (overwhelmed) / उर (to the heart) / लाई (brought) / गै (went) / मनि (jewel) / मनहुँ (as if) / फनिक (snake) / फिरि (again) / पाई (found) / रामहि (Ram) / चितइ (gazing at) / रहेउ (remained) / नरनाहू (the king) / चला (flowed) / बिलोचन (eyes) / बारि (water) / प्रबाहू (stream)
ramacharitamanas::2166.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2166.essence: Love returns what grief had taken, and tears answer first.
ramacharitamanas::2166.simple_meaning: Dasharath holds Ram close, unable to let go. Seeing Ram again overwhelms him with love and tears.
ramacharitamanas::2166.simple_insight: Love can make grief and joy arrive together in the same breath.
ramacharitamanas::2166.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has finally heard that Ram has come. He pulls Ram to his chest like someone recovering what was lost, but the reunion only deepens his overwhelm. The king can only stare and weep.
ramacharitamanas::2166.modern_relevance: You see someone you love after a long absence, and your chest tightens before you can speak. Relief, grief, and gratitude all hit at once.
ramacharitamanas::2166.insight: It shifts attention from speaking to feeling: some reunions are too full for words.

ramacharitamanas::2167.verse_sanskrit: सोक बिबस कछु कहै न पारा। हृदयँ लगावत बारहिं बारा॥ बिधिहि मनाव राउ मन माहीं। जेहिं रघुनाथ न कानन जाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2167.verse_hindi: शोक के विशेष वश होने के कारण राजा कुछ कह नहीं सकते। वे बार-बार श्री रामचन्द्रजी को हृदय से लगाते हैं और मन में ब्रह्माजी को मनाते हैं कि जिससे श्री राघुनाथजी वन को न जाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2167.english_translation: Overcome by grief, the king could not speak. Again and again he clasped Ram to his heart and prayed inwardly to Brahma that Raghunath would not go to the forest.
ramacharitamanas::2167.translation_literal: सोक (grief) / बिबस (overcome) / कछु (anything) / कहै (speak) / न (not) / पारा (was able) / हृदयँ (to the heart) / लगावत (clasping) / बारहिं बार (again and again) / बिधिहि (to Brahma) / मनाव (appealed) / राउ (the king) / मन (mind) / माहीं (within) / जेहिं (so that) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / न (not) / कानन (forest) / जाहीं (go)
ramacharitamanas::2167.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2167.essence: Grief silences him; love keeps pulling Ram back to the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2167.simple_meaning: Grief leaves Dasharath speechless. He keeps holding Ram close and prays that Ram will not have to leave for the forest.
ramacharitamanas::2167.simple_insight: Love can make a person wordless, reaching for the beloved instead of explanations.
ramacharitamanas::2167.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has just embraced Ram after years of separation, and the joy is already breaking into fear. He cannot even speak through grief and affection. Clinging to Ram, he silently begs the higher power to stop the exile that has begun to crush his heart.
ramacharitamanas::2167.modern_relevance: You hold someone’s hand in the hospital corridor and cannot find the right words. Love becomes a silent plea: please let this not be the moment of loss.
ramacharitamanas::2167.insight: It shows grief as helpless attachment, and prayer as the only remaining language.

ramacharitamanas::2168.verse_sanskrit: सुमिरि महेसहि कहइ निहोरी। बिनती सुनहु सदासिव मोरी॥ आसुतोष तुम्ह अवढर दानी। आरति हरहु दीन जनु जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2168.verse_hindi: फिर महादेवजी का स्मरण करके उनसे निहोरा करते हुए कहते हैं- हे सदाशिव! आप मेरी विनती सुनिए। आप आशुतोष (शीघ्र प्रसन्न होने वाले) और अवढरदानी (मुँहमाँगा दे डालने वाले) हैं। अतः मुझे अपना दीन सेवक जानकर मेरे दुःख को दूर कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2168.english_translation: Remembering Mahesh, he pleaded, "Hear my prayer, Sadashiv. You are quick to please and generous beyond measure. Know me as your humble servant and remove my suffering."
ramacharitamanas::2168.translation_literal: सुमिरि (remembering) / महेसहि (Mahesh/Shiva) / कहइ (said) / निहोरी (humble plea) / बिनती (request) / सुनहु (listen) / सदासिव (Sadashiv) / मोरी (my) ॥ / आसुतोष (quick to please) / तुम्ह (you) / अवढरदानी (generous giver) / दानी (giver) / । / आरति (suffering) / हरहु (remove) / दीन (humble) / जनु (servant/person) / जानी (knowing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2168.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2168.essence: Grief becomes prayer when control finally ends.
ramacharitamanas::2168.simple_meaning: Dasharath remembers Shiva and humbly asks him to hear his plea and remove his suffering. He appeals to Shiva's kindness and generosity as a humble servant in pain.
ramacharitamanas::2168.simple_insight: Even in grief, the heart reaches upward first. Need can become prayer before it becomes despair.
ramacharitamanas::2168.detailed_meaning: Dasharath, crushed by Ram's departure, turns from raw grief to prayer. He remembers Shiva and begs Sadashiv to listen, praising him as quick to please and endlessly generous. In this moment, sorrow becomes surrender.
ramacharitamanas::2168.modern_relevance: You sit alone after a terrible phone call, unable to fix anything. Before you spiral, you whisper the only honest sentence left: help me, because I cannot carry this alone.
ramacharitamanas::2168.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance in pain to humble asking for help.

ramacharitamanas::2169.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह प्रेरक सब के हृदयँ सो मति रामहि देहु। बचनु मोर तजि रहहिं घर परिहरि सीलु सनेहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2169.verse_hindi: आप प्रेरक रूप से सबके हृदय में हैं। आप श्री रामचन्द्र को ऐसी बुद्धि दीजिए, जिससे वे मेरे वचन को त्यागकर और शील-स्नेह को छोड़कर घर ही में रह जाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2169.english_translation: You move within every heart. Grant Ram the understanding to abandon my word and stay home, leaving aside duty and affection.
ramacharitamanas::2169.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / प्रेरक (the mover) / सब के (of all) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / सो (thus) / मति (understanding) / रामहि (to Ram) / देहु (give) / बचनु (word) / मोर (my) / तजि (abandoning) / रहहिं (may remain) / घर (at home) / परिहरि (leaving aside) / सीलु (duty / righteous conduct) / सनेहु (affection)
ramacharitamanas::2169.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2169.essence: Grief begs even the rightful word to be withdrawn.
ramacharitamanas::2169.simple_meaning: Dasharath begs for Ram to stay home instead of keeping the promise that will send him into exile.
ramacharitamanas::2169.simple_insight: Love can ache so deeply that it asks for the impossible.
ramacharitamanas::2169.detailed_meaning: King Dasharath, crushed by grief in Ayodhya, turns from helpless lament to prayer. He asks the power moving every heart to change Ram's mind so his son will ignore the exile vow and remain at home.
ramacharitamanas::2169.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love pack a bag for a move that will break your family rhythm. Part of you wants reality to bend, just this once, so they stay.
ramacharitamanas::2169.insight: It reveals the human wish to override duty when love is too painful to bear.

ramacharitamanas::2170.verse_sanskrit: अजसु होउ जग सुजसु नसाऊ। नरक परौं बरु सुरपुरु जाऊ॥ सब दुख दुसह सहावहु मोही। लोचन ओट रामु जनि होंही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2170.verse_hindi: जगत में चाहे अपयश हो और सुयश नष्ट हो जाए। चाहे (नया पाप होने से) मैं नरक में गिरूँ, अथवा स्वर्ग चला जाए (पूर्व पुण्यों के फलस्वरूप मिलने वाला स्वर्ग चाहे मुझे न मिले)। और भी सब प्रकार के दुःसह दुःख आप मुझसे सहन करा लें। पर श्री रामचन्द्र मेरी आँखों की ओट न हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::2170.english_translation: Let my reputation be lost in the world and my good name vanish. Let me fall into hell, or even go to heaven. Let me endure every unbearable sorrow, but let Ram not be hidden from my sight.
ramacharitamanas::2170.translation_literal: अजसु (disgrace) / होउ (let it be) / जग (world) / सुजसु (good name) / नसाऊ (let it vanish) / नरक (hell) / परौं (I fall) / बरु (rather) / सुरपुरु (heavenly realm) / जाऊ (I go) / सब (all) / दुख (sorrows) / दुसह (unbearable) / सहावहु (let [them] be borne) / मोही (by me) / लोचन (eyes) / ओट (cover) / रामु (Ram) / जनि (do not) / होंही (be)
ramacharitamanas::2170.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2170.essence: All losses are bearable except being cut off from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2170.simple_meaning: Fame, comfort, even afterlife rewards do not matter here. The only unbearable thing is being separated from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2170.simple_insight: Devotion becomes so complete that every other loss feels small beside separation from the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::2170.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is overwhelmed by grief and surrender. He would rather lose reputation, comfort, and even endure harsh suffering than let Ram disappear from his sight. This is the depth of his love.
ramacharitamanas::2170.modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the praise, the clean record — and still feel hollow because one person’s trust is missing. Bharat shows what matters when love becomes the real measure.
ramacharitamanas::2170.insight: It shifts value from status and comfort to presence itself. The mind stops bargaining for rewards and asks only for nearness.

ramacharitamanas::2171.verse_sanskrit: अस मन गुनइ राउ नहिं बोला। पीपर पात सरिस मनु डोला॥ रघुपति पितहि प्रेमबस जानी। पुनि कछु कहिहि मातु अनुमानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2171.verse_hindi: राजा मन ही मन इस प्रकार विचार कर रहे हैं, बोलते नहीं। उनका मन पीपल के पत्ते की तरह डोल रहा है। श्री रघुनाथजी ने पिता को प्रेम के वश जानकर और यह अनुमान करके कि माता फिर कुछ कहेगी (तो पिताजी को दुःख होगा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2171.english_translation: The king thought silently and did not speak. His mind trembled like a peepal leaf. Lord Raghunath saw that his father was overwhelmed by love and guessed that if the mother spoke again, the father would be hurt.
ramacharitamanas::2171.translation_literal: अस (thus) / मन (mind) / गुनइ (thought) / राउ (the king) / नहिं (not) / बोला (spoke)। / पीपर (peepal) / पात (leaf) / सरिस (like) / मनु (mind) / डोला (trembled)॥ / रघुपति (Lord of Raghu) / पितहि (father) / प्रेमबस (under the sway of love) / जानी (knowing)। / पुनि (again) / कछु (something) / कहिहि (will say) / मातु (mother) / अनुमानि (guessing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2171.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2171.essence: Love notices pain before words can.
ramacharitamanas::2171.simple_meaning: The king is too shaken to speak. Ram understands that his father is ruled by love and worries that more words from the mother will only deepen his pain.
ramacharitamanas::2171.simple_insight: Silence can carry more grief than speech. Love can make even a strong person tremble.
ramacharitamanas::2171.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is crushed by the exile crisis. He sits silent, mind shaking like a leaf, while Ram reads his state with painful tenderness. Ram sees that another plea from Kaikeyi would only wound his father further.
ramacharitamanas::2171.modern_relevance: You watch a parent go quiet after bad news, and you know not to push for explanations. Sometimes care means reading the room and protecting someone from one more blow.
ramacharitamanas::2171.insight: It teaches you to notice when another person is too overwhelmed for more words and to respond with restraint.

ramacharitamanas::2172.verse_sanskrit: देस काल अवसर अनुसारी। बोले बचन बिनीत बिचारी॥ तात कहउँ कछु करउँ ढिठाई। अनुचितु छमब जानि लरिकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2172.verse_hindi: देश, काल और अवसर के अनुकूल विचार कर विनीत वचन कहे- हे तात! मैं कुछ कहता हूँ, यह ढिठाई करता हूँ। इस अनौचित्य को मेरी बाल्यावस्था समझकर क्षमा कीजिएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2172.english_translation: Speaking according to time, place, and occasion, he said in a humble, thoughtful voice: “Father, I say something now; it may seem rude. Please forgive this impropriety as the folly of my youth.”
ramacharitamanas::2172.translation_literal: देस (place) / काल (time) / अवसर (occasion) / अनुसारी (according to) / बोले (spoke) / बचन (words) / बिनीत (humble) / बिचारी (thoughtful) / तात (father) / कहउँ (I say) / कछु (something) / करउँ (I do) / ढिठाई (rudeness) / अनुचितु (improper thing) / छमब (forgive) / जानि (knowing) / लरिकाई (childhood)
ramacharitamanas::2172.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2172.essence: Respectful speech can carry even painful truth.
ramacharitamanas::2172.simple_meaning: Bharat speaks gently and carefully to his father, asking forgiveness for saying something that may sound improper.
ramacharitamanas::2172.simple_insight: Even difficult truths can be spoken with humility. Respect does not require silence.
ramacharitamanas::2172.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Dasharath while grief and duty press on the whole family. He chooses his words with care, matching time, place, and feeling, and asks his father to forgive any boldness as childishness.
ramacharitamanas::2172.modern_relevance: You need to say something hard to an elder, manager, or partner, and your pulse is racing. Bharat shows how honesty can still arrive wrapped in respect.
ramacharitamanas::2172.insight: It teaches you to speak truth without aggression, so the message lands without adding extra wound.

ramacharitamanas::2173.verse_sanskrit: अति लघु बात लागि दुखु पावा। काहुँ न मोहि कहि प्रथम जनावा॥ देखि गोसाइँहि पूँछिउँ माता। सुनि प्रसंगु भए सीतल गाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2173.verse_hindi: इस अत्यन्त तुच्छ बात के लिए आपने इतना दुःख पाया। मुझे किसी ने पहले कहकर यह बात नहीं जनाई। स्वामी (आप) को इस दशा में देखकर मैंने माता से पूछा। उनसे सारा प्रसंग सुनकर मेरे सब अंग शीतल हो गए (मुझे बड़ी प्रसन्नता हुई) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2173.english_translation: You suffered over such a small matter. No one told me first. Seeing you in this state, I asked Mother. Hearing the whole matter from her, my whole body became calm and glad.
ramacharitamanas::2173.translation_literal: अति लघु (very small) / बात (matter) / लागि (for) / दुखु (pain) / पावा (felt) / काहुँ (by anyone) / न (not) / मोहि (to me) / कहि (telling) / प्रथम (first) / जनावा (made known) / देखि (seeing) / गोसाइँहि (the lord/master) / पूँछिउँ (I asked) / माता (mother) / सुनि (hearing) / प्रसंगु (the matter/story) / भए (became) / सीतल (cool/calm) / गाता (limbs/body)
ramacharitamanas::2173.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2173.essence: Clarity calms pain faster than fear can spread it.
ramacharitamanas::2173.simple_meaning: Ram says the matter was very small, yet his father suffered deeply because no one explained it to him first. After hearing the full story from Mother, Ram feels relieved.
ramacharitamanas::2173.simple_insight: A hidden explanation can cool a heart that is burning with confusion.
ramacharitamanas::2173.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is shaken by the exile crisis and Ram sees his father’s suffering. Ram realizes the pain came from not knowing the full story, so he asks Kaushalya and hears what happened. Understanding the situation brings him calm.
ramacharitamanas::2173.modern_relevance: You hear half a conversation and spend the whole night spiraling. Then one clear explanation arrives, and the tightness in your chest finally loosens.
ramacharitamanas::2173.insight: It shifts the mind from reacting to fragments toward seeking the full context before judging.

ramacharitamanas::2174.verse_sanskrit: मंगल समय सनेह बस सोच परिहरिअ तात। आयसु देइअ हरषि हियँ कहि पुलके प्रभु गात ॥
ramacharitamanas::2174.verse_hindi: हे पिताजी! इस मंगल के समय स्नेहवश होकर सोच करना छोड़ दीजिए और हृदय में प्रसन्न होकर मुझे आज्ञा दीजिए। यह कहते हुए प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी सर्वांग पुलकित हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2174.english_translation: Father, in this auspicious moment, let go of sorrow and give me your command with joy. As he spoke, Lord Ram's body thrilled with delight.
ramacharitamanas::2174.translation_literal: मंगल (auspicious) / समय (time) / सनेह (affection, love) / बस (because of) / सोच (worry, sorrow) / परिहरिअ (give up) / तात (father) / आयसु (command) / देइअ (give) / हरषि (with joy) / हियँ (in the heart) / कहि (saying) / पुलके (thrilled, bristled with joy) / प्रभु (Lord) / गात (body)
ramacharitamanas::2174.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2174.essence: Duty can be joyful when it is offered in love.
ramacharitamanas::2174.simple_meaning: Ram asks Dasharath to set aside sorrow and give him his command with a joyful heart. He speaks with such love that his body shivers with delight.
ramacharitamanas::2174.simple_insight: Love does not weaken duty; it makes obedience radiant.
ramacharitamanas::2174.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has just been shaken by the painful turn of events around Ram's exile. Ram responds not with protest, but with tenderness: he asks his father to cast off grief and speak the command that must be obeyed. This is the moment his filial duty becomes visible.
ramacharitamanas::2174.modern_relevance: Your parent is upset, the room is heavy, and everyone waits for you to defend yourself. Instead, you soften your voice, accept the hard instruction, and keep the relationship intact.
ramacharitamanas::2174.insight: It teaches you to meet obligation with warmth, not resentment, even when the cost is personal.

ramacharitamanas::2175.verse_sanskrit: धन्य जनमु जगतीतल तासू। पितहि प्रमोदु चरित सुनि जासू॥ चारि पदारथ करतल ताकें। प्रिय पितु मातु प्रान सम जाकें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2175.verse_hindi: (उन्होंने फिर कहा-) इस पृथ्वीतल पर उसका जन्म धन्य है, जिसके चरित्र सुनकर पिता को परम आनंद हो, जिसको माता-पिता प्राणों के समान प्रिय हैं, चारों पदार्थ (अर्थ, धर्म, काम, मोक्ष) उसके करतलगत (मुट्ठी में) रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2175.english_translation: Blessed is the birth of the one whose character brings a father great joy when heard. Blessed is the one whose mother and father are dear as life, and for whom the four aims of life lie in the palm of the hand.
ramacharitamanas::2175.translation_literal: धन्य (blessed) / जनमु (birth) / जगतीतल (on the earth) / तासू (of that one) / पितहि (to the father) / प्रमोदु (great joy) / चरित (character/deeds) / सुनि (hearing) / जासू (whose) / चारि (four) / पदारथ (aims/ends) / करतल (palm of the hand) / ताकें (for that one) / प्रिय (dear) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / प्रान (life/breath) / सम (like) / जाकें (whose)
ramacharitamanas::2175.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2175.essence: A blessed life makes parents rejoice and keeps purpose within reach.
ramacharitamanas::2175.simple_meaning: A truly blessed life is one that makes parents happy, treats them as dearly as life itself, and keeps the four aims of life within reach.
ramacharitamanas::2175.simple_insight: You feel that a worthy life is measured by love, gratitude, and fulfilled purpose — not just personal success.
ramacharitamanas::2175.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram stands before Dasharath and speaks with perfect filial tenderness. He says a life is blessed when a father rejoices at hearing of it, when parents are cherished like breath, and when the four aims of life are naturally in hand.
ramacharitamanas::2175.modern_relevance: You call your mother after a long week, and her voice softens the moment she hears you are well. That small relief is part of what this verse calls a blessed life.
ramacharitamanas::2175.insight: It shifts success from private achievement to a life that honors parents and fulfills human purpose.

ramacharitamanas::2176.verse_sanskrit: आयसु पालि जनम फलु पाई। ऐहउँ बेगिहिं होउ रजाई॥ बिदा मातु सन आवउँ मागी। चलिहउँ बनहि बहुरि पग लागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2176.verse_hindi: आपकी आज्ञा पालन करके और जन्म का फल पाकर मैं जल्दी ही लौट आऊँगा, अतः कृपया आज्ञा दीजिए। माता से विदा माँग आता हूँ। फिर आपके पैर लगकर (प्रणाम करके) वन को चलूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2176.english_translation: By obeying your command, I will have gained the fruit of life. I will return quickly, so please give me your permission. I will go ask Mother for leave, then bow at your feet again and go to the forest.
