ramacharitamanas::2176.translation_literal: आयसु (command) / पालि (having obeyed) / जनम (birth) / फलु (fruit) / पाई (having gained) / ऐहउँ (I will come) / बेगिहिं (quickly) / होउ (be) / रजाई (permission) / बिदा (leave) / मातु (mother) / सन (from) / आवउँ (I will come) / मागी (having asked) / चलिहउँ (I will go) / बनहि (to the forest) / बहुरि (again) / पग (feet) / लागी (bowing)
ramacharitamanas::2176.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2176.essence: Obedience itself becomes the fruit of a human life.
ramacharitamanas::2176.simple_meaning: Ram says he will obey his father's command, ask his mother for leave, and then go to the forest after bowing again.
ramacharitamanas::2176.simple_insight: Real loyalty is shown in the willingness to leave what you love without argument.
ramacharitamanas::2176.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram stands before Dasharath and accepts exile without resistance. He says obedience to his father's command is the true fruit of life, asks permission to see Kaushalya, and prepares to leave again after bowing.
ramacharitamanas::2176.modern_relevance: You get the call you never wanted: a parent’s illness, a family duty, a move that changes everything. Ram shows that dignity is not in refusing the burden, but in carrying it cleanly.
ramacharitamanas::2176.insight: It shifts duty from burden to fulfillment, making obedience an act of wholeness rather than loss.

ramacharitamanas::2177.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि राम गवनु तब कीन्हा। भूप सोक बस उतरु न दीन्हा॥ नगर ब्यापि गइ बात सुतीछी। छुअत चढ़ी जनु सब तन बीछी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2177.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी वहाँ से चल दिए। राजा ने शोकवश कोई उत्तर नहीं दिया। वह बहुत ही तीखी (अप्रिय) बात नगर भर में इतनी जल्दी फैल गई, मानो डंक मारते ही बिच्छू का विष सारे शरीर में चढ़ गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2177.english_translation: Saying this, Ram departed. The king, overcome with grief, gave no reply. The harsh news spread through the city so fast it felt like scorpion venom racing through every body.
ramacharitamanas::2177.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / राम (Ram) / गवनु (departure) / तब (then) / कीन्हा (did) / भूप (king) / सोक (grief) / बस (under the control of) / उतरु (reply) / न (not) / दीन्हा (gave) / नगर (city) / ब्यापि (spread through) / गइ (went) / बात (news) / सुतीछी (sharp/harsh) / छुअत (touching) / चढ़ी (rose) / जनु (as if) / सब (all) / तन (bodies) / बीछी (scorpion) /
ramacharitamanas::2177.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2177.essence: A ruler’s silence turns private grief into public pain.
ramacharitamanas::2177.simple_meaning: Ram left after speaking, and the king could not answer because of grief. The painful news spread through the whole city instantly, striking everyone like poison.
ramacharitamanas::2177.simple_insight: Grief can silence a ruler and spread through a community like a shockwave.
ramacharitamanas::2177.detailed_meaning: Ram has just asked permission to go. Dasharath, crushed by sorrow, cannot answer. Ram leaves, and the court’s private pain becomes public disaster as the news races through Ayodhya, stinging every household before anyone can recover.
ramacharitamanas::2177.modern_relevance: You hear the message and freeze before you can even reply. By the time you put the phone down, the whole family group chat has caught the shock too.
ramacharitamanas::2177.insight: It shows how one painful moment can paralyze speech and spread distress through an entire community.

ramacharitamanas::2178.verse_sanskrit: सुनि भए बिकल सकल नर नारी। बेलि बिटप जिमि देखि दवारी॥ जो जहँ सुनइ धुनइ सिरु सोई। बड़ बिषादु नहिं धीरजु होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2178.verse_hindi: इस बात को सुनकर सब स्त्री-पुरुष ऐसे व्याकुल हो गए जैसे दावानल (वन में आग लगी) देखकर बेल और वृक्ष मुरझा जाते हैं। जो जहाँ सुनता है, वह वहीं सिर धुनने (पीटने) लगता है! बड़ा विषाद है, किसी को धीरज नहीं बँधता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2178.english_translation: Hearing this, all men and women became distraught, like vines and trees before a forest fire. Whoever heard it, struck his head in grief; no one could hold steady.
ramacharitamanas::2178.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / भए (became) / बिकल (distressed) / सकल (all) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / बेलि (vines) / बिटप (trees) / जिमि (like) / देखि (seeing) / दवारी (forest fire) / जो (whoever) / जहँ (where) / सुनइ (hears) / धुनइ (strikes) / सिरु (head) / सोई (that one) / बड़ (great) / बिषादु (grief) / नहिं (not) / धीरजु (steadiness) / होई (is)
ramacharitamanas::2178.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2178.essence: Grief can move through a whole city like fire through dry grass.
ramacharitamanas::2178.simple_meaning: The news throws the whole city into grief and panic. Everyone reacts at once, and no one can stay composed.
ramacharitamanas::2178.simple_insight: Shared sorrow can spread fast and overwhelm even steady people.
ramacharitamanas::2178.detailed_meaning: After Ram leaves, the news spreads through Ayodhya. Men and women everywhere collapse into grief, as if a wildfire has swept through the city. This verse shows the public shock before the deeper mourning that follows.
ramacharitamanas::2178.modern_relevance: A message lands in the family group chat: the job is gone, the wedding is off, the diagnosis is confirmed. Before anyone can think, the whole room changes shape.
ramacharitamanas::2178.insight: It shows how collective shock can erase composure and spread through an entire community.

ramacharitamanas::2179.verse_sanskrit: मुख सुखाहिं लोचन स्रवहिं सोकु न हृदयँ समाइ। मनहुँ करुन रस कटकई उतरी अवध बजाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2179.verse_hindi: सबके मुख सूखे जाते हैं, आँखों से आँसू बहते हैं, शोक हृदय में नहीं समाता। मानो करुणा रस की सेना अवध पर डंका बजाकर उतर आई हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2179.english_translation: Mouths go dry, tears flow from the eyes, and sorrow cannot fit in the heart. It is as if an army of grief has marched into Ayodhya, beating its drums.
ramacharitamanas::2179.translation_literal: मुख (mouths) / सुखाहिं (become dry) / लोचन (eyes) / स्रवहिं (flow) / सोकु (sorrow) / न (not) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / समाइ (fits) / मनहुँ (as if) / करुन रस (the rasa of compassion/grief) / कटकई (army) / उतरी (descended) / अवध (Ayodhya) / बजाइ (beating)
ramacharitamanas::2179.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2179.essence: Grief can occupy a whole city like an invading army.
ramacharitamanas::2179.simple_meaning: Ayodhya is so overwhelmed by grief that people cannot speak, only cry. The sorrow feels like a whole army has entered the city.
ramacharitamanas::2179.simple_insight: Some pain is so large it spreads through everyone at once.
ramacharitamanas::2179.detailed_meaning: After Ram leaves, Ayodhya cannot hold itself together. The people stand stunned, unable to answer or even speak clearly. This line shows grief spreading through the whole city like a marching force.
ramacharitamanas::2179.modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after one message changes everything. No one knows what to say, and the quiet itself feels heavy.
ramacharitamanas::2179.insight: It turns private grief into a shared atmosphere, showing how loss can overtake an entire community.

ramacharitamanas::2180.verse_sanskrit: मिलेहि माझ बिधि बात बेगारी। जहँ तहँ देहिं कैकइहि गारी॥ एहि पापिनिहि बूझि का परेऊ। छाइ भवन पर पावकु धरेऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2180.verse_hindi: सब मेल मिल गए थे (सब संयोग ठीक हो गए थे), इतने में ही विधाता ने बात बिगाड़ दी! जहाँ-तहाँ लोग कैकेयी को गाली दे रहे हैं! इस पापिन को क्या सूझ पड़ा जो इसने छाए घर पर आग रख दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2180.english_translation: Among people who had been united, fate suddenly spoiled everything. Everywhere, people cursed Kaikeyi. What madness seized this sinner, who set fire to a house already covered with shade?
ramacharitamanas::2180.translation_literal: मिलेहि (had met / were united) / माझ (middle / among) / बिधि (fate / the arranger) / बात (matter / affair) / बेगारी (spoiled, ruined) / जहँ तहँ (here and there / everywhere) / देहिं (give) / कैकइहि (to Kaikeyi) / गारी (abuse, curses) / एहि (this) / पापिनिहि (sinner woman) / बूझि (understanding / thinking) / का (what) / परेऊ (came over / fell upon) / छाइ (shade / cover) / भवन (house / palace) / पर (upon) / पावकु (fire) / धरेऊ (set)
ramacharitamanas::2180.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2180.essence: A single ruinous choice can set a whole home ablaze.
ramacharitamanas::2180.simple_meaning: What was once harmonious has been shattered, and Kaikeyi is blamed everywhere for bringing ruin into a peaceful home.
ramacharitamanas::2180.simple_insight: Some choices split a family so deeply that everyone feels the burn.
ramacharitamanas::2180.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya has just collapsed into grief after the exile decree. The people who were united a moment ago now curse Kaikeyi in shock and anger, seeing her as the one who turned a sheltered home into a blaze.
ramacharitamanas::2180.modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after one message, then explodes with blame. One decision has changed the whole atmosphere, and everyone can feel the damage.
ramacharitamanas::2180.insight: It shows how one destructive impulse can overturn trust and make a whole community turn on one person.

ramacharitamanas::2181.verse_sanskrit: निज कर नयन काढ़ि चह दीखा। डारि सुधा बिषु चाहत चीखा॥ कुटिल कठोर कुबुद्धि अभागी। भइ रघुबंस बेनु बन आगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2181.verse_hindi: यह अपने हाथ से अपनी आँखों को निकालकर (आँखों के बिना ही) देखना चाहती है और अमृत फेंककर विष चखना चाहती है! यह कुटिल, कठोर, दुर्बुद्धि और अभागिनी कैकेयी रघुवंश रूपी बाँस के वन के लिए अग्नि हो गई! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2181.english_translation: She wants to tear out her own eyes just to see, and to drink poison after throwing away nectar. Crooked, harsh, foolish, and unlucky, Kaikeyi has become the fire for the bamboo forest of Raghu's line.
ramacharitamanas::2181.translation_literal: निज कर (with her own hand) / नयन (eyes) / काढ़ि (pulling out) / चह (wants) / दीखा (to see) / डारि (throwing away) / सुधा (nectar) / बिषु (poison) / चाहत (desiring) / चीखा (cried out) / कुटिल (crooked) / कठोर (harsh) / कुबुद्धि (poor-minded) / अभागी (unlucky) / भइ (became) / रघुबंस (Raghu's line) / बेनु (bamboo) / बन (forest) / आगी (fire)
ramacharitamanas::2181.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2181.essence: Foolish desire can burn down the very family that nourished you.
ramacharitamanas::2181.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is being described as acting against her own good, as if she rejected nectar and chose poison. Her actions are said to have set the Raghu family ablaze.
ramacharitamanas::2181.simple_insight: Desire can make a person attack what once gave them joy.
ramacharitamanas::2181.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace has turned into a house of grief after Kaikeyi's demand sends Ram into exile. Tulsidas condemns her choice with fierce images: rejecting nectar, choosing poison, and burning the Raghu family from within.
ramacharitamanas::2181.modern_relevance: You know that moment when someone throws away a loving relationship for a petty advantage, then watches everything collapse. The damage feels self-inflicted because it is.
ramacharitamanas::2181.insight: It exposes how craving and poor judgment can make a person destroy their own source of happiness.

ramacharitamanas::2182.verse_sanskrit: पालव बैठि पेड़ु एहिं काटा। सुख महुँ सोक ठाटु धरि ठाटा॥ सदा रामु एहि प्रान समाना। कारन कवन कुटिलपनु ठाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2182.verse_hindi: पत्ते पर बैठकर इसने पेड़ को काट डाला। सुख में शोक का ठाट ठटकर रख दिया! श्री रामचन्द्रजी इसे सदा प्राणों के समान प्रिय थे। फिर भी न जाने किस कारण इसने यह कुटिलता ठानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2182.english_translation: She sat on a leaf and cut down the tree beneath her. She placed grief in the midst of happiness. Ram was always as dear to her as life itself, yet for what reason did she choose such crookedness?
ramacharitamanas::2182.translation_literal: पालव (leaf) / बैठि (having sat) / पेड़ु (tree) / एहिं (this) / काटा (cut) / सुख (happiness) / महुँ (in) / सोक (sorrow) / ठाटु (array) / धरि (having placed) / ठाटा (stood) / सदा (always) / रामु (Ram) / एहि (this) / प्रान (life-breath) / समाना (equal) / कारन (reason) / कवन (what) / कुटिलपनु (crookedness) / ठाना (undertook)
ramacharitamanas::2182.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2182.essence: A heart can destroy what it loves most.
ramacharitamanas::2182.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi destroyed her own happiness by choosing a harmful act. Ram had always been as dear to her as life, yet she still turned against him.
ramacharitamanas::2182.simple_insight: A single twisted choice can overturn a whole life of affection.
ramacharitamanas::2182.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court’s peace has already broken over Kaikeyi’s demand. Tulsidas now laments the mystery of her choice: Ram was as dear to her as breath, yet she still helped cut down her own joy and the kingdom’s future.
ramacharitamanas::2182.modern_relevance: You know the feeling of making one cold decision in a heated moment and watching months of trust collapse. What hurts most is that the bond was real before the damage began.
ramacharitamanas::2182.insight: It shifts attention from the act itself to the inner contradiction that made it possible.

ramacharitamanas::2183.verse_sanskrit: सत्य कहहिं कबि नारि सुभाऊ। सब बिधि अगहु अगाध दुराऊ॥ निज प्रतिबिंबु बरुकु गहि जाई। जानि न जाइ नारि गति भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2183.verse_hindi: कवि सत्य ही कहते हैं कि स्त्री का स्वभाव सब प्रकार से पकड़ में न आने योग्य, अथाह और भेदभरा होता है। अपनी परछाहीं भले ही पकड़ जाए, पर भाई! स्त्रियों की गति (चाल) नहीं जानी जाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2183.english_translation: Poets say a woman’s nature is hard to grasp, deep, and hidden. You may catch your own reflection, but you cannot know a woman’s way, brother.
ramacharitamanas::2183.translation_literal: सत्य (truth) / कहहिं (say) / कबि (poets) / नारि (woman) / सुभाऊ (nature) / सब बिधि (in every way) / अगहु (ungraspable) / अगाध (bottomless) / दुराऊ (hidden) / निज (own) / प्रतिबिंबु (reflection) / बरुकु (perhaps) / गहि (grasping) / जाई (can be taken) / जानि (known) / न (not) / जाइ (is possible) / नारि (woman) / गति (way) / भाई (brother)
ramacharitamanas::2183.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2183.essence: Another person’s inner movement cannot be mastered by quick judgment.
ramacharitamanas::2183.simple_meaning: Poets describe a woman’s nature as hard to fully understand or predict. You may catch a reflection, but not her inner movement.
ramacharitamanas::2183.simple_insight: Some people cannot be reduced to a simple reading; humility is wiser than certainty.
ramacharitamanas::2183.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the poet pauses amid Kaikeyi’s terrible turn and reflects on how concealed a woman’s nature can seem. The verse is not advancing the plot so much as sharpening the warning around the queen’s unreadable actions.
ramacharitamanas::2183.modern_relevance: You replay a text thread for the tenth time and still cannot tell what someone meant. The urge to label them quickly feels strong, but certainty can be a trap.
ramacharitamanas::2183.insight: It cautions against overconfidence in judging another person’s motives from the outside.

ramacharitamanas::2184.verse_sanskrit: काह न पावकु जारि सक का न समुद्र समाइ। का न करै अबला प्रबल केहि जग कालु न खाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2184.verse_hindi: आग क्या नहीं जला सकती! समुद्र में क्या नहीं समा सकता! अबला कहाने वाली प्रबल स्त्री (जाति) क्या नहीं कर सकती! और जगत में काल किसको नहीं खाता! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2184.english_translation: What cannot fire burn? What cannot the ocean contain? What cannot a woman, called weak, do when she is strong? And whom in this world does Time not consume?
ramacharitamanas::2184.translation_literal: काह (what) / न (not) / पावकु (fire) / जारि (burn) / सक (can) / का (what) / न (not) / समुद्र (ocean) / समाइ (fit in, contain) / का (what) / न (not) / करै (can do) / अबला (woman, weak one) / प्रबल (strong, powerful) / केहि (whom) / जग (world) / कालु (Time) / न (not) / खाइ (devours)
ramacharitamanas::2184.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2184.essence: Power and Time can overturn anything.
ramacharitamanas::2184.simple_meaning: Nothing is beyond fire, the ocean, a strong woman, or Time. The verse stresses how powerful forces can overcome almost anything.
ramacharitamanas::2184.simple_insight: It leaves a sober feeling: human plans are fragile before larger powers.
ramacharitamanas::2184.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the story has turned toward grief and blame. After the earlier lines about hidden motives, this couplet widens the frame: fire, ocean, women’s power, and Time itself can overwhelm anything. It prepares the argument that follows.
ramacharitamanas::2184.modern_relevance: A plan collapses, a message gets misread, and suddenly the whole day is out of your hands. This line reminds you that stronger forces can upend even careful intentions.
ramacharitamanas::2184.insight: It shifts attention from control to the limits of control, making the reader see how easily events exceed personal intention.

ramacharitamanas::2185.verse_sanskrit: का सुनाइ बिधि काह सुनावा। का देखाइ चह काह देखावा॥ एक कहहिं भल भूप न कीन्हा। बरु बिचारि नहिं कुमतिहि दीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2185.verse_hindi: विधाता ने क्या सुनाकर क्या सुना दिया और क्या दिखाकर अब वह क्या दिखाना चाहता है! एक कहते हैं कि राजा ने अच्छा नहीं किया, दुर्बुद्धि कैकेयी को विचारकर वर नहीं दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2185.english_translation: What did fate make heard, what did it make heard? What did it show, and what does it still want to show? Some say the king did wrong, because he did not think and give the boon to the foolish mind.
ramacharitamanas::2185.translation_literal: का (what) / सुनाइ (having caused to hear) / बिधि (fate) / काह (what) / सुनावा (caused to hear) / का (what) / देखाइ (having shown) / चह (wants) / काह (what) / देखावा (shown) / एक (some) / कहहिं (say) / भल (good) / भूप (king) / न (not) / कीन्हा (did) / बरु (boon) / बिचारि (thinking) / नहिं (not) / कुमतिहि (to the foolish mind) / दीन्हा (gave)
ramacharitamanas::2185.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2185.essence: Blame is easy when the larger design is still hidden.
ramacharitamanas::2185.simple_meaning: The verse wonders what destiny has revealed and what it is still revealing. It also notes that some people blame the king for not carefully giving Kaikeyi the boon.
ramacharitamanas::2185.simple_insight: Not every painful event is simple enough for blame. Sometimes people are only seeing part of a much larger turn.
ramacharitamanas::2185.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court’s disaster is unfolding through Kaikeyi’s demand and Dasharath’s helplessness. The narrator pauses to question what larger force is at work, while also noting that some judge the king harshly for not refusing Kaikeyi’s request.
ramacharitamanas::2185.modern_relevance: A family argument explodes after one rushed decision, and everyone starts assigning blame within minutes. This verse slows that rush and asks whether anyone is seeing the whole picture.
ramacharitamanas::2185.insight: It shifts the mind from quick judgment to wider seeing, especially when events are still unfolding.

ramacharitamanas::2186.verse_sanskrit: जो हठि भयउ सकल दुख भाजनु। अबला बिबस ग्यानु गुनु गा जनु॥ एक धरम परमिति पहिचाने। नृपहि दोसु नहिं देहिं सयाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::2186.verse_hindi: जो हठ करके (कैकेयी की बात को पूरा करने में अड़े रहकर) स्वयं सब दुःखों के पात्र हो गए। स्त्री के विशेष वश होने के कारण मानो उनका ज्ञान और गुण जाता रहा। एक (दूसरे) जो धर्म की मर्यादा को जानते हैं और सयाने हैं, वे राजा को दोष नहीं देते ॥
ramacharitamanas::2186.english_translation: Some say Dasharath, driven by stubbornness, became the source of all sorrow. Overpowered by Kaikeyi's demand, his wisdom and virtues seemed to fail. Others, knowing the limits of dharma, do not blame the king.
ramacharitamanas::2186.translation_literal: जो (who) / हठि (through stubbornness) / भयउ (became) / सकल (all) / दुख (sorrow) / भाजनु (a vessel) / अबला (a woman) / बिबस (helplessly controlled) / ग्यानु (wisdom) / गुनु (virtue) / गा (went) / जनु (as if) ॥ एक (some) / धरम (dharma) / परमिति (limits/measure) / पहिचाने (knowing) / नृपहि (the king) / दोसु (fault) / नहिं (not) / देहिं (give) / सयाने (the wise) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2186.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2186.essence: Wisdom sees the trap before it assigns blame.
ramacharitamanas::2186.simple_meaning: Some blame Dasharath for the tragedy, saying he was trapped by stubbornness and lost his judgment. Others, wiser about dharma, do not place the blame on him alone.
ramacharitamanas::2186.simple_insight: It is easier to judge a broken person than to see how grief and duty can trap them.
ramacharitamanas::2186.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court and the people are reeling after Kaikeyi's demand and Ram's exile. Some accuse Dasharath of stubborn weakness; others, seeing the limits of human duty and pressure, refuse to condemn him outright.
ramacharitamanas::2186.modern_relevance: A family argument leaves one parent silent, one child furious, and everyone else ready with a verdict. This verse asks for something harder than blame: the ability to see how pain narrows a person's choices.
ramacharitamanas::2186.insight: It shifts the mind from quick judgment to compassionate discernment about responsibility.

ramacharitamanas::2187.verse_sanskrit: सिबि दधीचि हरिचंद कहानी। एक एक सन कहहिं बखानी॥ एक भरत कर संमत कहहीं। एक उदास भायँ सुनि रहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2187.verse_hindi: वे शिबि, दधीचि और हरिश्चन्द्र की कथा एक-दूसरे से बखानकर कहते हैं। कोई एक इसमें भरतजी की सम्मति बताते हैं। कोई एक सुनकर उदासीन भाव से रह जाते हैं (कुछ बोलते नहीं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2187.english_translation: They recount the stories of Shibi, Dadhichi, and Harishchandra to one another. Some speak of Bharat's approval; some listen in silence, dejected.
ramacharitamanas::2187.translation_literal: सिबि (Shibi) / दधीचि (Dadhichi) / हरिचंद (Harishchandra) / कहानी (stories) / एक एक सन (with one another) / कहहिं (they tell) / बखानी (describing) ॥ / एक (some) / भरत कर (Bharat's) / संमत (approval) / कहहीं (say) / एक (some) / उदास भायँ (with dejected mind) / सुनि (hearing) / रहहीं (remain) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2187.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2187.essence: Sacrifice invites praise, but grief still has the final word.
ramacharitamanas::2187.simple_meaning: People compare old stories of sacrifice and debate Bharat's role. Some approve, while others fall silent and saddened.
ramacharitamanas::2187.simple_insight: Great sacrifice can stir admiration, doubt, and grief all at once.
ramacharitamanas::2187.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court and citizens are still shaken by Ram's exile. They invoke Shibi, Dadhichi, and Harishchandra as examples, then turn to Bharat's response. The verse captures a crowd divided between praise, silence, and sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2187.modern_relevance: At a family gathering after a painful decision, everyone retells the same event differently. Some defend it, some refuse to speak, and the room itself feels heavy.
ramacharitamanas::2187.insight: It shows how one painful event can split public judgment into praise, silence, and grief.

ramacharitamanas::2188.verse_sanskrit: कान मूदि कर रद गहि जीहा। एक कहहिं यह बात अलीहा॥ सुकृत जाहिं अस कहत तुम्हारे। रामु भरत कहुँ प्रानपिआरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2188.verse_hindi: कोई हाथों से कान मूँदकर और जीभ को दाँतों तले दबाकर कहते हैं कि यह बात झूठ है, ऐसी बात कहने से तुम्हारे पुण्य नष्ट हो जाएँगे। भरतजी को तो श्री रामचन्द्रजी प्राणों के समान प्यारे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2188.english_translation: Some cover their ears and bite their tongues, saying, 'That is false. Speaking so will destroy your merit.' Bharat is as dear to Ram as life itself.
ramacharitamanas::2188.translation_literal: कान (ears) / मूदि (covering) / कर (with hands) / रद (teeth) / गहि (grasping) / जीहा (tongue) / एक (some) / कहहिं (say) / यह (this) / बात (matter) / अलीहा (false) / सुकृत (merit) / जाहिं (go away) / अस (such) / कहत (saying) / तुम्हारे (your) / रामु (Ram) / भरत (Bharat) / कहुँ (to) / प्रानपिआरे (dear as life)
ramacharitamanas::2188.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2188.essence: Bharat's devotion is so complete that even doubting it feels wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2188.simple_meaning: People refuse to believe anyone could say Bharat is false to Ram. They insist such a claim would ruin their merit, because Bharat is utterly dear to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2188.simple_insight: Love can be so pure that even doubt feels like a kind of disrespect.
ramacharitamanas::2188.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, people are arguing over Bharat's devotion after Ram's exile. Some cannot bear the idea that Bharat could ever oppose Ram, and they reject the thought as offensive. The verse deepens Bharat's reputation before the next line seals it.
ramacharitamanas::2188.modern_relevance: You hear a friend being unfairly judged in a group chat, and you almost speak up before the message finishes loading. Real loyalty refuses easy suspicion.
ramacharitamanas::2188.insight: It shifts the reader from casual doubt to reverence for proven devotion.

ramacharitamanas::2189.verse_sanskrit: चंदु चवै बरु अनल कन सुधा होइ बिषतूल। सपनेहुँ कबहुँ न करहिं किछु भरतु राम प्रतिकूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::2189.verse_hindi: चन्द्रमा चाहे (शीतल किरणों की जगह) आग की चिनगारियाँ बरसाने लगे और अमृत चाहे विष के समान हो जाए, परन्तु भरतजी स्वप्न में भी कभी श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विरुद्ध कुछ नहीं करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2189.english_translation: Even if the moon were to rain sparks of fire and nectar were to turn into poison, Bharat would never oppose Ram, even in a dream.
ramacharitamanas::2189.translation_literal: चंदु (the moon) / चवै (may rain) / बरु (even if) / अनल (fire) / कन (sparks) / सुधा (nectar) / होइ (becomes) / बिषतूल (poison) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / कबहुँ न (never) / करहिं (would do) / किछु (anything) / भरतु (Bharat) / राम (Ram) / प्रतिकूल (opposed)
ramacharitamanas::2189.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2189.simple_meaning: Bharat's loyalty to Ram is so complete that nothing could turn him against Ram, not even in imagination.
ramacharitamanas::2189.simple_insight: Deep loyalty makes betrayal unthinkable, not merely avoided.
ramacharitamanas::2189.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the people of Ayodhya are arguing over Bharat's intentions after Ram's exile. This line settles the matter: Bharat's heart is fixed on Ram so completely that opposition is impossible.
ramacharitamanas::2189.modern_relevance: When everyone around you assumes you will choose convenience, you quietly keep the promise that matters most. That kind of loyalty does not need applause to stay firm.
ramacharitamanas::2189.insight: It shifts the mind from wavering loyalty to a settled allegiance that cannot be bought or shaken.

ramacharitamanas::2190.verse_sanskrit: एक बिधातहि दूषनु देहीं। सुधा देखाइ दीन्ह बिषु जेहीं॥ खरभरु नगर सोचु सब काहू। दुसह दाहु उर मिटा उछाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2190.verse_hindi: कोई एक विधाता को दोष देते हैं, जिसने अमृत दिखाकर विष दे दिया। नगर भर में खलबली मच गई, सब किसी को सोच हो गया। हृदय में दुःसह जलन हो गई, आनंद-उत्साह मिट गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2190.english_translation: Some blamed fate itself, saying it showed nectar and then gave poison. Confusion spread through the city; everyone was troubled. A painful fire burned in every heart, and joy vanished.
ramacharitamanas::2190.translation_literal: एक (one) / बिधातहि (to fate / the ordainer) / दूषनु (blame) / देहीं (they give) / सुधा (nectar) / देखाइ (showing) / दीन्ह (gave) / बिषु (poison) / जेहीं (who) ॥ खरभरु (commotion) / नगर (city) / सोचु (grief, worry) / सब काहू (for everyone) / दुसह (unbearable) / दाहु (burning) / उर (heart) / मिटा (was erased) / उछाहू (joy, enthusiasm) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2190.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2190.essence: A sweet promise can turn a whole city bitter in one moment.
ramacharitamanas::2190.simple_meaning: People in the city felt betrayed and blamed fate itself. What looked sweet had turned bitter, and the whole place fell into grief.
ramacharitamanas::2190.simple_insight: When hope turns into shock, even a whole city can feel emotionally scorched.
ramacharitamanas::2190.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the news of Ram's exile has spread through Ayodhya. People cannot make sense of it, so they blame fate for showing them sweetness and then handing them poison. The verse captures the city's collective shock before the grief deepens further.
ramacharitamanas::2190.modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after one message changes everything. People reread the words, blame bad timing, and feel the warmth drain out of the room.
ramacharitamanas::2190.insight: It shifts attention from private disappointment to shared shock and helplessness.

ramacharitamanas::2191.verse_sanskrit: बिप्रबधू कुलमान्य जठेरी। जे प्रिय परम कैकई केरी॥ लगीं देन सिख सीलु सराही। बचन बानसम लागहिं ताहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2191.verse_hindi: ब्राह्मणों की स्त्रियाँ, कुल की माननीय बड़ी-बूढ़ी और जो कैकेयी की परम प्रिय थीं, वे उसके शील की सराहना करके उसे सीख देने लगीं। पर उसको उनके वचन बाण के समान लगते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2191.english_translation: The wives of learned Brahmins, respected elder women of the clan, and those especially dear to Kaikeyi praised her virtue and tried to advise her. Their words struck her like arrows.
ramacharitamanas::2191.translation_literal: बिप्रबधू (wives of Brahmins) / कुलमान्य (respected by the clan) / जठेरी (elder women) / जे (who) / प्रिय (dear) / परम (most) / कैकई केरी (of Kaikeyi) / लगीं (began) / देन (to give) / सिख (advice) / सीलु (virtue) / सराही (praising) / बचन (words) / बान (arrows) / सम (like) / लागहिं (they strike) / ताहीं (her)
ramacharitamanas::2191.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2191.essence: A closed heart hears advice as harm.
ramacharitamanas::2191.simple_meaning: Respectable women praise Kaikeyi and try to guide her, but their advice feels painful to her.
ramacharitamanas::2191.simple_insight: When a mind is already bent by desire, even gentle advice can feel like an attack.
ramacharitamanas::2191.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has already been pulled into the trap of her own demand. Now respected women around her praise her character and try to correct her, but their kindness cannot reach her. The verse shows how distorted desire turns even loving words into wounds.
ramacharitamanas::2191.modern_relevance: A friend calmly points out what you already know you should fix, and you bristle instantly. The message is gentle, but your defensiveness makes it sting.
ramacharitamanas::2191.insight: It shows how inner resistance can turn guidance into pain and block honest correction.

ramacharitamanas::2192.verse_sanskrit: भरतु न मोहि प्रिय राम समाना। सदा कहहु यहु सबु जगु जाना॥ करहु राम पर सहज सनेहू। केहिं अपराध आजु बनु देहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2192.verse_hindi: (वे कहती हैं-) तुम तो सदा कहा करती थीं कि श्री रामचंद्र के समान मुझको भरत भी प्यारे नहीं हैं, इस बात को सारा जगत् जानता है। श्री रामचंद्रजी पर तो तुम स्वाभाविक ही स्नेह करती रही हो। आज किस अपराध से उन्हें वन देती हो? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2192.english_translation: You always said Bharat is not dear to me like Ram; the whole world knows it. You have always loved Ram naturally. What offence has he committed today that you send him to the forest?
ramacharitamanas::2192.translation_literal: भरतु (Bharat) / न (not) / मोहि (to me) / प्रिय (dear) / राम (Ram) / समाना (equal) / सदा (always) / कहहु (you say) / यहु (this) / सबु (all) / जगु (world) / जाना (knows)॥ / करहु (you do) / राम (Ram) / पर (toward) / सहज (natural) / सनेहू (affection) / केहिं (what) / अपराध (fault) / आजु (today) / बनु (forest) / देहू (give/send)॥
ramacharitamanas::2192.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2192.essence: Love remembered makes betrayal impossible to hide.
ramacharitamanas::2192.simple_meaning: The speaker reminds Kaikeyi of her love for Ram and Bharat, then asks why she is now sending Ram into exile.
ramacharitamanas::2192.simple_insight: A loving bond can be betrayed by one sudden decision, and the wound is deeper because everyone remembers the truth.
ramacharitamanas::2192.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace is reeling after Kaikeyi demands Ram's exile. The elder women of the court confront her gently but firmly, recalling her own words of affection for Ram and Bharat. Their question exposes the cruelty of the moment.
ramacharitamanas::2192.modern_relevance: A family gathering turns silent when one person makes a choice everyone knows cuts against years of love. The sharpest pain is not the decision itself, but the memory of what was once said and meant.
ramacharitamanas::2192.insight: It shifts attention from private desire to public accountability, showing that words of love create a standard the heart must answer to.

ramacharitamanas::2193.verse_sanskrit: कबहुँ न कियहु सवति आरेसू। प्रीति प्रतीति जान सबु देसू॥ कौसल्याँ अब काह बिगारा। तुम्ह जेहि लागि बज्र पुर पारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2193.verse_hindi: तुमने कभी सौतियाडाह नहीं किया। सारा देश तुम्हारे प्रेम और विश्वास को जानता है। अब कौसल्या ने तुम्हारा कौन सा बिगाड़ कर दिया, जिसके कारण तुमने सारे नगर पर वज्र गिरा दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2193.english_translation: You never showed jealousy toward your co-wife. The whole land knew your love and trust. What wrong has Kaushalya done to you that you struck the whole city with thunder?
ramacharitamanas::2193.translation_literal: कबहुँ (ever) / न (not) / कियहु (you did) / सवति (co-wife) / आरेसू (jealousy) / प्रीति (love) / प्रतीति (trust) / जान (knows) / सबु (all) / देसू (land) / कौसल्याँ (Kaushalya) / अब (now) / काह (what) / बिगारा (wrong) / तुम्ह (you) / जेहि लागि (for which reason) / बज्र (thunderbolt) / पुर (city) / पारा (struck down)
ramacharitamanas::2193.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2193.essence: Love once trusted can become the sharpest wound.
ramacharitamanas::2193.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is reminded that she was once known for love, trust, and freedom from jealousy. Now her actions have shattered the city and brought suffering on Kaushalya.
ramacharitamanas::2193.simple_insight: A trusted heart can wound more deeply than an enemy ever could.
ramacharitamanas::2193.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi is being confronted by the women of the palace. They remind her that she was never jealous and was once loved for her warmth. Now her demand has thrown Ayodhya into grief, and even Kaushalya is caught in the ruin.
ramacharitamanas::2193.modern_relevance: A family group chat turns cold after one bitter message. Everyone remembers how kind you used to be, which makes the sudden cruelty hurt even more.
ramacharitamanas::2193.insight: It shifts the mind from defending a grievance to seeing the damage created by one impulsive demand.

ramacharitamanas::2194.verse_sanskrit: सीय कि पिय सँगु परिहरिहि लखनु करहिहहिं धाम। राजु कि भूँजब भरत पुर नृपु कि जिइहि बिनु राम ॥
ramacharitamanas::2194.verse_hindi: क्या सीताजी अपने पति (श्री रामचंद्रजी) का साथ छोड़ देंगी? क्या लक्ष्मणजी श्री रामचंद्रजी के बिना घर रह सकेंगे? क्या भरतजी श्री रामचंद्रजी के बिना अयोध्यापुरी का राज्य भोग सकेंगे? और क्या राजा श्री रामचंद्रजी के बिना जीवित रह सकेंगे? (अर्थात् न सीताजी यहाँ रहेंगी, न लक्ष्मणजी रहेंगे, न भरतजी राज्य करेंगे और न राजा ही जीवित रहेंगे, सब उजाड़ हो जाएगा।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2194.english_translation: Will Sita leave her husband’s side? Will Lakshman stay at home without Ram? Will Bharat enjoy Ayodhya’s throne without Ram? And can the king live without Ram?
ramacharitamanas::2194.translation_literal: सीय (Sita) / कि (whether) / पिय (husband) / सँगु (with) / परिहरिहि (will leave) / लखनु (Lakshman) / करहिहहिं (will do) / धाम (home) / राजु (rule) / कि (whether) / भूँजब (will enjoy) / भरत (Bharat) / पुर (city) / नृपु (king) / कि (whether) / जिइहि (will live) / बिनु (without) / राम (Ram)
ramacharitamanas::2194.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2194.essence: Without Ram, every other role collapses into emptiness.
ramacharitamanas::2194.simple_meaning: Sita will not stay without Ram, Lakshman will not remain at home without him, Bharat will not enjoy the throne without him, and the king cannot live without him.
ramacharitamanas::2194.simple_insight: Some bonds are so strong that life itself feels incomplete without them.
ramacharitamanas::2194.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the queen is defending Ram’s place in the family while courtly tension rises around the exile. She points to Sita, Lakshman, Bharat, and Dasharath to show that Ram is the center holding every life together.
ramacharitamanas::2194.modern_relevance: A parent watches an adult child pack a bag after a painful argument and suddenly knows: no one in this house can pretend the bond is ordinary anymore. Some absences reorganize an entire family.
ramacharitamanas::2194.insight: It shifts attention from possession and status to the living force of relationship.

ramacharitamanas::2195.verse_sanskrit: अस बिचारि उर छाड़हु कोहू। सोक कलंक कोठि जनि होहू॥ भरतहि अवसि देहु जुबराजू। कानन काह राम कर काजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2195.verse_hindi: हृदय में ऐसा विचार कर क्रोध छोड़ दो, शोक और कलंक की कोठी मत बनो। भरत को अवश्य युवराजपद दो, पर श्री रामचंद्रजी का वन में क्या काम है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2195.english_translation: Thinking this through, let go of anger. Do not become a house of grief and disgrace. Surely give Bharat the crown prince’s seat; what business does Ram have in the forest?
ramacharitamanas::2195.translation_literal: अस (thus) / बिचारि (having considered) / उर (in the heart) / छाड़हु (let go) / कोहू (anger) / सोक (grief) / कलंक (disgrace) / कोठि (house/storehouse) / जनि (do not) / होहू (become)॥ भरतहि (to Bharat) / अवसि (surely) / देहु (give) / जुबराजू (crown princehood) / कानन (forest) / काह (what) / राम (Ram) / कर (of) / काजू (business/purpose) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2195.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2195.essence: Anger only multiplies disgrace; right action is to restore the proper role.
ramacharitamanas::2195.simple_meaning: Let go of anger and do what is proper: give Bharat the crown prince’s seat. Ram has no reason to be sent into the forest.
ramacharitamanas::2195.simple_insight: Clinging to resentment only deepens the wound. Clear duty is to stop the harm and restore what is right.
ramacharitamanas::2195.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the family crisis has already begun. The speaker tries to calm the court, urging everyone to drop anger and shame, and to place Bharat on the throne. The verse is part of the argument around Ram’s exile and the struggle over rightful duty.
ramacharitamanas::2195.modern_relevance: A family meeting is going badly, and every sentence adds another layer of hurt. Someone has to stop the spiral, name the right next step, and not feed the fire with pride.
ramacharitamanas::2195.insight: It shifts attention from emotional retaliation to the immediate obligation of restoring order and fairness.

ramacharitamanas::2196.verse_sanskrit: नाहिन रामु राज के भूखे। धरम धुरीन बिषय रस रूखे॥ गुर गृह बसहुँ रामु तजि गेहू। नृप सन अस बरु दूसर लेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2196.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी राज्य के भूखे नहीं हैं। वे धर्म की धुरी को धारण करने वाले और विषय रस से रूखे हैं (अर्थात् उनमें विषयासक्ति है ही नहीं), इसलिए तुम यह शंका न करो कि श्री रामजी वन न गए तो भरत के राज्य में विघ्न करेंगे, इतने पर भी मन न माने तो) तुम राजा से दूसरा ऐसा (यह) वर ले लो कि श्री राम घर छोड़कर गुरु के घर रहें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2196.english_translation: Ram is not hungry for a kingdom. He is firm in dharma and dry toward worldly taste. Even if you still doubt, ask the king for another boon: let Ram live in the guru's house, leaving his own home.
ramacharitamanas::2196.translation_literal: नाहिन (not) / रामु (Ram) / राज (kingdom) / के भूखे (hungry for) / धरम धुरीन (the pillar of dharma) / बिषय रस (worldly taste) / रूखे (dry, indifferent)॥ / गुर गृह (guru's house) / बसहुँ (let him live) / रामु (Ram) / तजि (leaving) / गेहू (home) / नृप सन (from the king) / अस (such) / बरु (boon) / दूसर (another) / लेहू (take) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2196.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2196.essence: Power means nothing to one who is rooted in dharma.
ramacharitamanas::2196.simple_meaning: Ram does not want the throne. He stands for dharma, not pleasure. If anyone still doubts, let Ram live in the guru's house instead of ruling.
ramacharitamanas::2196.simple_insight: Real duty does not chase power. It stays clean even when power is offered.
ramacharitamanas::2196.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court is still trembling over Bharat's claim and Ram's exile. This verse answers the suspicion that Ram might covet the throne. Tulsidas makes Ram's nature clear: he seeks dharma, not rule.
ramacharitamanas::2196.modern_relevance: A family business hands you the keys, and everyone watches to see whether you want control or just want peace. The verse separates ambition from right action.
ramacharitamanas::2196.insight: It teaches you to test motives: true duty does not need status, comfort, or possession.

ramacharitamanas::2197.verse_sanskrit: जौं नहिं लगिहहु कहें हमारे। नहिं लागिहि कछु हाथ तुम्हारे॥ जौं परिहास कीन्हि कछु होई। तौ कहि प्रगट जनावहु सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2197.verse_hindi: जो तुम हमारे कहने पर न चलोगी तो तुम्हारे हाथ कुछ भी न लगेगा। यदि तुमने कुछ हँसी की हो तो उसे प्रकट में कहकर जना दो (कि मैंने दिल्लगी की है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2197.english_translation: If you do not obey what I say, nothing will come into your hands. If this was only a joke, then say so openly and make it clear.
ramacharitamanas::2197.translation_literal: जौं (if) / नहिं (not) / लगिहहु (you will follow) / कहें (by saying) / हमारे (our) / नहिं (not) / लागिहि (will come) / कछु (anything) / हाथ (into hand) / तुम्हारे (your)॥ / जौं (if) / परिहास (joking) / कीन्हि (did) / कछु (some) / होई (was) / तौ (then) / कहि (saying) / प्रगट (openly) / जनावहु (make known) / सोई (that)॥
ramacharitamanas::2197.speaker: Manthara
ramacharitamanas::2197.essence: Manipulation thrives on urgency and shame.
ramacharitamanas::2197.simple_meaning: Manthara pushes Kaikeyi to obey her plan, warning that hesitation will cost her everything. She demands that Kaikeyi either act openly or admit the whole thing was a joke.
ramacharitamanas::2197.simple_insight: Pressure can make a mind surrender its own judgment.
ramacharitamanas::2197.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Manthara is hardening Kaikeyi's resolve against Ram. She warns that if Kaikeyi does not follow her advice, she will gain nothing, and if she was only joking, she should admit it plainly. This keeps the manipulation moving.
ramacharitamanas::2197.modern_relevance: A friend keeps texting, “Are you in or not?” and the pressure starts shrinking your own judgment. The demand is not for truth — it is for compliance.
ramacharitamanas::2197.insight: It shows how manipulation works by forcing a quick yes-or-no before reflection can return.

ramacharitamanas::2198.verse_sanskrit: राम सरिस सुत कानन जोगू। काह कहिहि सुनि तुम्ह कहुँ लोगू॥ उठहु बेगि सोइ करहु उपाई। जेहि बिधि सोकु कलंकु नसाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2198.verse_hindi: राम सरीखा पुत्र क्या वन के योग्य है? यह सुनकर लोग तुम्हें क्या कहेंगे! जल्दी उठो और वही उपाय करो जिस उपाय से इस शोक और कलंक का नाश हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2198.english_translation: Is a son like Ram fit for the forest? What will people say when they hear this? Rise quickly and do whatever will erase this sorrow and shame.
ramacharitamanas::2198.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सरिस (like) / सुत (son) / कानन (forest) / जोगू (fit) / काह (what) / कहिहि (will say) / सुनि (hearing) / तुम्ह (you) / कहुँ (to) / लोगू (people) / उठहु (rise) / बेगि (quickly) / सोइ (that) / करहु (do) / उपाई (remedy) / जेहि (by which) / बिधि (way) / सोकु (sorrow) / कलंकु (shame) / नसाई (may be erased)
ramacharitamanas::2198.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2198.essence: Shame-driven urgency can hide a deeper wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2198.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi urges a quick fix to remove the grief and public shame caused by Ram's exile.
ramacharitamanas::2198.simple_insight: Panic narrows the mind until image matters more than what is right.
ramacharitamanas::2198.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has already demanded Ram's exile. Now she presses for an immediate remedy that will remove the sorrow and disgrace from the palace. Her concern is not Ram's pain, but how the situation appears to others.
ramacharitamanas::2198.modern_relevance: A family argument explodes, and the first instinct is not repair but damage control: delete the messages, calm the relatives, save face. The verse exposes that reflex before it hardens into harm.
ramacharitamanas::2198.insight: It shifts attention from reputation management to the deeper cause of the crisis.

ramacharitamanas::2199.verse_sanskrit: जेहि भाँति सोकु कलंकु जाइ उपाय करि कुल पालही। हठि फेरु रामहि जात बन जनि बात दूसरि चालही॥ जिमि भानु बिनु दिनु प्रान बिनु तनु चंद बिनु जिमि जामिनी। तिमि अवध तुलसीदास प्रभु बिन समुझि धौं जियँ भामनी॥
ramacharitamanas::2199.verse_hindi: जिस तरह (नगरभर का) शोक और (तुम्हारा) कलंक मिटे, वही उपाय करके कुल की रक्षा कर। वन जाते हुए श्री रामजी को हठ करके लौटा ले, दूसरी कोई बात न चला। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- जैसे सूर्य के बिना दिन, प्राण के बिना शरीर और चंद्रमा के बिना रात (निर्जीव तथा शोभाहीन हो जाती है), वैसे ही श्री रामचंद्रजी के बिना अयोध्या हो जाएगी, हे भामिनी! तू अपने हृदय में इस बात को समझ (विचारकर देख) तो सही।
ramacharitamanas::2199.english_translation: Find whatever remedy removes the grief and the stain on the family. Force Ram back from the forest and do not follow any other course. Just as day without the sun, a body without breath, and night without the moon lose their life and beauty, so Ayodhya without Ram is nothing, O woman—understand this in your heart.
ramacharitamanas::2199.translation_literal: जेहि भाँति (in whichever way) / सोकु (grief) / कलंकु (stain) / जाइ (goes away) / उपाय करि (having made a remedy) / कुल (family) / पालही (protect) / हठि (by force) / फेरु (turn back) / रामहि (Ram) / जात बन (going to the forest) / जनि (do not) / बात (matter) / दूसरि (other) / चालही (follow) / जिमि (just as) / भानु (sun) / बिनु (without) / दिनु (day) / प्रान (breath/life) / बिनु (without) / तनु (body) / चंद (moon) / बिनु (without) / जिमि (just as) / जामिनी (night) / तिमि (so) / अवध (Ayodhya) / तुलसीदास (Tulsidas) / प्रभु (lord) / बिन (without) / समुझि (understand) / धौं (indeed) / जियँ (in the heart) / भामनी (O noble woman)
ramacharitamanas::2199.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2199.essence: A kingdom without Ram is lifeless; save the family by stopping the exile.
ramacharitamanas::2199.simple_meaning: The family elders urge Kaikeyi to stop Ram's exile, saying Ayodhya cannot live without him and the kingdom must be saved from shame and grief.
ramacharitamanas::2199.simple_insight: When a wrong choice starts harming everyone, courage means stopping it before it hardens into tragedy.
ramacharitamanas::2199.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kaikeyi is being pressed by her attendants to undo the damage she has set in motion. They beg her to find any remedy, protect the family line, and force Ram back from the forest, because the city itself feels lifeless without him.
ramacharitamanas::2199.modern_relevance: A family argument has gone too far, and everyone can feel the damage spreading through the house. Someone has to stop defending pride and choose the repair that saves what still can be saved.
ramacharitamanas::2199.insight: It shifts attention from winning the argument to preserving what the whole family cannot afford to lose.

ramacharitamanas::2200.verse_sanskrit: सखिन्ह सिखावनु दीन्ह सुनत मधुर परिनाम हित। तेइँ कछु कान न कीन्ह कुटिल प्रबोधी कूबरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2200.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार सखियों ने ऐसी सीख दी जो सुनने में मीठी और परिणाम में हितकारी थी। पर कुटिला कुबरी की सिखाई-पढ़ाई हुई कैकेयी ने इस पर जरा भी कान नहीं दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2200.english_translation: The handmaids gave advice that sounded sweet and would have led to a good result, but the crooked Kaikeyi, taught by Manthara, paid no heed.
ramacharitamanas::2200.translation_literal: सखिन्ह (by the handmaids) / सिखावनु (advice) / दीन्ह (given) / सुनत (while hearing) / मधुर (sweet) / परिनाम (result) / हित (beneficial) / तेइँ (she) / कछु (some) / कान (ear) / न (not) / कीन्ह (did) / कुटिल (crooked) / प्रबोधी (instructed) / कूबरी (Manthara)
ramacharitamanas::2200.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2200.essence: A twisted mind rejects even the advice meant to save it.
ramacharitamanas::2200.simple_meaning: The handmaids offered gentle advice that would have helped everyone, but Kaikeyi ignored it because Manthara had already twisted her mind.
ramacharitamanas::2200.simple_insight: A mind captured by resentment cannot hear even kind counsel.
ramacharitamanas::2200.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi is already under Manthara's influence. The palace women speak softly and try to guide her toward a better choice, but her mind is closed. This verse shows the tragedy beginning before the demand is even spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2200.modern_relevance: A friend texts you a careful message after a fight, but you read it through the filter of anger and miss the care inside it.
ramacharitamanas::2200.insight: It shows how inner distortion blocks good advice, even when the advice is gentle and useful.

ramacharitamanas::2201.verse_sanskrit: उतरु न देइ दुसह रिस रूखी। मृगिन्ह चितव जनु बाघिनि भूखी॥ ब्याधि असाधि जानि तिन्ह त्यागी। चलीं कहत मतिमंद अभागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2201.verse_hindi: कैकेयी कोई उत्तर नहीं देती, वह दुःसह क्रोध के मारे रूखी (बेमुरव्वत) हो रही है। ऐसे देखती है मानो भूखी बाघिन हरिनियों को देख रही हो। तब सखियों ने रोग को असाध्य समझकर उसे छोड़ दिया। सब उसको मंदबुद्धि, अभागिनी कहती हुई चल दीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2201.english_translation: Kaikeyi gives no reply. Overcome by unbearable anger, she grows harsh and cold, like a hungry tigress staring at deer. Seeing the disease as incurable, the attendants leave her, calling her foolish and unfortunate.
ramacharitamanas::2201.translation_literal: उतरु (reply) / न देइ (does not give) / दुसह (unbearable) / रिस (anger) / रूखी (harsh, cold) / मृगिन्ह (deer) / चितव (looks) / जनु (as if) / बाघिनि (tigress) / भूखी (hungry) / ब्याधि (disease) / असाधि (incurable) / जानि (knowing) / तिन्ह (them) / त्यागी (left) / चलीं (went away) / कहत (saying) / मतिमंद (foolish) / अभागी (unfortunate)
ramacharitamanas::2201.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2201.essence: Anger can become so rigid that even help cannot reach it.
ramacharitamanas::2201.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi stays silent in furious stubbornness. The attendants see that her condition cannot be cured and leave, condemning her as foolish and unlucky.
ramacharitamanas::2201.simple_insight: Unchecked anger isolates a person until even help gives up.
ramacharitamanas::2201.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has already been captured by Manthara's poison and the palace women can no longer reach her. Her silence is not peace; it is rage turned rigid. The attendants realise this wound has become untreatable and walk away in despair.
ramacharitamanas::2201.modern_relevance: A family argument turns cold, and one person stops answering every question with a hard stare. The room knows the conversation is over, not because the issue is solved, but because anger has shut the door.
ramacharitamanas::2201.insight: It shows how resentment can harden into a state where advice no longer enters.

ramacharitamanas::2202.verse_sanskrit: राजु करत यह दैअँ बिगोई। कीन्हेसि अस जस करइ न कोई॥ एहि बिधि बिलपहिं पुर नर नारीं। देहिं कुचालिहि कोटिक गारीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2202.verse_hindi: राज्य करते हुए इस कैकेयी को दैव ने नष्ट कर दिया। इसने जैसा कुछ किया, वैसा कोई भी न करेगा! नगर के सब स्त्री-पुरुष इस प्रकार विलाप कर रहे हैं और उस कुचाली कैकेयी को करोड़ों गालियाँ दे रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2202.english_translation: The divine ruined Kaikeyi while she was ruling. No one has ever done such a deed. In this way, the people of the city wept and hurled millions of curses at the wicked woman.
ramacharitamanas::2202.translation_literal: राजु (kingdom/rule) / करत (while doing) / यह (this) / दैअँ (by fate/divine will) / बिगोई (ruined) / कीन्हेसि (she did) / जस (as) / करइ (does) / न कोई (no one) / एहि बिधि (in this way) / बिलपहिं (they wept) / पुर (city) / नर नारीं (men and women) / देहिं (give) / कुचालिहि (to the wicked one) / कोटिक (millions of) / गारीं (abuses/curses)
ramacharitamanas::2202.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2202.essence: Selfish rule turns a whole city into mourners.
ramacharitamanas::2202.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi’s choice has shattered the city. People are grieving loudly and blaming her for a deed they see as unforgivable.
ramacharitamanas::2202.simple_insight: A single selfish act can wound an entire community and leave everyone mourning together.
ramacharitamanas::2202.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya has just learned that Kaikeyi’s demand will drive Ram into exile. The city is not calm or neutral; men and women are openly weeping, cursing her, and reacting as if the moral order itself has been broken.
ramacharitamanas::2202.modern_relevance: A family group chat explodes after one person makes a cruel decision that affects everyone. The anger is not abstract — it is the sound of trust breaking in real time.
ramacharitamanas::2202.insight: It shows how private desire can become public grief when a leader’s choice harms the whole community.

ramacharitamanas::2203.verse_sanskrit: जरहिं बिषम जर लेहिं उसासा। कवनि राम बिनु जीवन आसा॥ बिपुल बियोग प्रजा अकुलानी। जनु जलचर गन सूखत पानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2203.verse_hindi: लोग विषम ज्वर (भयानक दुःख की आग) से जल रहे हैं। लंबी साँसें लेते हुए वे कहते हैं कि श्री रामचंद्रजी के बिना जीने की कौन आशा है। महान् वियोग (की आशंका) से प्रजा ऐसी व्याकुल हो गई है मानो पानी सूखने के समय जलचर जीवों का समुदाय व्याकुल हो!॥3
ramacharitamanas::2203.english_translation: People burn in unbearable grief, gasping, "What hope of life remains without Ram?" The people are overwhelmed by great separation, like water creatures struggling as water dries up.
ramacharitamanas::2203.translation_literal: जरहिं (are burning) / बिषम जर (severe fever) / लेहिं (take) / उसासा (sighs) / कवनि (what) / राम बिनु (without Ram) / जीवन आसा (hope of life)॥ / बिपुल (great) / बियोग (separation) / प्रजा (people) / अकुलानी (restless, distressed) / जनु (as if) / जलचर गन (groups of water-creatures) / सूखत (drying) / पानी (water) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2203.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2203.essence: Absence of Ram feels like life draining away.
ramacharitamanas::2203.simple_meaning: The whole city is in deep grief. People feel life has no value without Ram, and their distress is compared to fish losing water.
ramacharitamanas::2203.simple_insight: When what you love feels absent, even breathing can feel heavy.
ramacharitamanas::2203.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya has just been shattered by Ram’s exile. The people are not debating it; they are suffering it physically, as if grief itself has become a fever. Their fear of life without Ram gives the scene its unbearable weight.
ramacharitamanas::2203.modern_relevance: A house goes quiet after someone leaves for good. The chairs are still there, the meals still happen, but the room feels airless. That is the kind of absence this verse knows.
ramacharitamanas::2203.insight: It shifts attention from public events to the human cost of separation.

ramacharitamanas::2204.verse_sanskrit: अति बिषाद बस लोग लोगाईं। गए मातु पहिं रामु गोसाईं॥ मुख प्रसन्न चित चौगुन चाऊ। मिटा सोचु जनि राखै राऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2204.verse_hindi: सभी पुरुष और स्त्रियाँ अत्यंत विषाद के वश हो रहे हैं। स्वामी श्री रामचंद्रजी माता कौसल्या के पास गए। उनका मुख प्रसन्न है और चित्त में चौगुना चाव (उत्साह) है। यह सोच मिट गया है कि राजा कहीं रख न लें। (श्री रामजी को राजतिलक की बात सुनकर विषाद हुआ था कि सब भाइयों को छोड़कर बड़े भाई मुझको ही राजतिलक क्यों होता है। अब माता कैकेयी की आज्ञा और पिता की मौन सम्मति पाकर वह सोच मिट गया।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2204.english_translation: The people were overwhelmed with grief. Lord Ram went to Mother Kausalya. His face was cheerful and his heart was full of joy. His worry that the king might keep him back had vanished.
ramacharitamanas::2204.translation_literal: अति बिषाद (great grief) / बस (under the control of) / लोग (the people) / लोगाईं (men and women) / गए (went) / मातु (mother) / पहिं (to the presence of) / रामु (Ram) / गोसाईं (lord) // मुख (face) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / चित (mind) / चौगुन चाऊ (fourfold joy) / मिटा (was removed) / सोचु (worry) / जनि (lest) / राखै (keep back) / राऊ (the king)
ramacharitamanas::2204.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2204.essence: Clear duty removes inner conflict, even when everyone else is grieving.
ramacharitamanas::2204.simple_meaning: The city is drowning in grief, but Ram is calm and happy. The fear that his father might refuse to let him go has disappeared.
ramacharitamanas::2204.simple_insight: Even in a broken moment, duty can bring a strange calm.
ramacharitamanas::2204.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is reeling from the exile order. While the citizens collapse into grief, Ram goes to Kausalya with a bright face. The king's silence has confirmed what Ram must do, and his inner conflict is gone.
ramacharitamanas::2204.modern_relevance: Your family is panicking over a sudden decision, but you already know what you have to do. The room is heavy, yet your mind is clear because the next step is no longer yours to debate.
ramacharitamanas::2204.insight: It shifts attention from public sorrow to private resolve: once duty is clear, hesitation falls away.

ramacharitamanas::2205.verse_sanskrit: नव गयंदु रघुबीर मनु राजु अलान समान। छूट जानि बन गवनु सुनि उर अनंदु अधिकान ॥
ramacharitamanas::2205.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी का मन नए पकड़े हुए हाथी के समान और राजतिलक उस हाथी के बाँधने की काँटेदार लोहे की बेड़ी के समान है। 'वन जाना है' यह सुनकर, अपने को बंधन से छूटा जानकर, उनके हृदय में आनंद बढ़ गया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2205.english_translation: Ram’s mind is like a young elephant, and the kingdom like a tethering stake. Hearing that he must go to the forest, his heart swells with joy, as if freed from bondage.
ramacharitamanas::2205.translation_literal: नव (young/new) / गयंदु (elephant) / रघुबीर (Ram) / मनु (mind) / राजु (kingdom) / अलान (tethering stake) / समान (like) / छूट (released) / जानि (knowing) / बन (forest) / गवनु (going) / सुनि (hearing) / उर (heart) / अनंदु (joy) / अधिकान (increased)
ramacharitamanas::2205.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2205.essence: True freedom can feel like losing the very thing others celebrate.
ramacharitamanas::2205.simple_meaning: Ram sees the kingdom as a binding chain, not a prize. Hearing that he will go to the forest, he feels joy because the pressure of rule is gone.
ramacharitamanas::2205.simple_insight: Relief can arrive when you stop clinging to what others call success.
ramacharitamanas::2205.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the exile order has already broken the court’s heart. But Ram’s own heart responds differently: the throne feels like a restraint, and the forest feels like freedom. This verse reveals his inner non-attachment before he leaves Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::2205.modern_relevance: You get the promotion everyone wanted, but your chest tightens instead of opening. The role looks glorious from outside, yet inside you feel the weight of a chain. Ram’s response shows another way to see it.
ramacharitamanas::2205.insight: It shifts the mind from craving status to recognizing freedom in release.

ramacharitamanas::2206.verse_sanskrit: रघुकुलतिलक जोरि दोउ हाथा। मुदित मातु पद नायउ माथा॥ दीन्हि असीस लाइ उर लीन्हे। भूषन बसन निछावरि कीन्हे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2206.verse_hindi: रघुकुल तिलक श्री रामचंद्रजी ने दोनों हाथ जोड़कर आनंद के साथ माता के चरणों में सिर नवाया। माता ने आशीर्वाद दिया, अपने हृदय से लगा लिया और उन पर गहने तथा कपड़े निछावर किए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2206.english_translation: Ram, the jewel of the Raghu clan, folded both hands and bowed his head joyfully at his mother’s feet. She blessed him, embraced him to her heart, and showered him with ornaments and clothes.
ramacharitamanas::2206.translation_literal: रघुकुल-तिलक (ornament of the Raghu clan) / जोरि (joining) / दोउ (both) / हाथा (hands) / मुदित (joyful) / मातु (mother) / पद (feet) / नायउ (bowed) / माथा (head)॥ दीन्हि (gave) / असीस (blessing) / लाइ (embracing) / उर (chest/heart) / लीन्हे (took) / भूषन (ornaments) / बसन (clothes) / निछावरि (offered as a gift) / कीन्हे (did)
ramacharitamanas::2206.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2206.essence: Even farewell becomes sacred when duty bows before a mother’s love.
ramacharitamanas::2206.simple_meaning: Ram bows to his mother with joy. She blesses him, embraces him, and gives him gifts with love.
ramacharitamanas::2206.simple_insight: Love stays tender even in loss. A blessing and an embrace can hold a whole family together.
ramacharitamanas::2206.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace is grieving as Ram prepares to leave. Before the separation deepens, Ram bows at Kaushalya’s feet with folded hands. She blesses him, holds him close, and offers ornaments and clothes in one last burst of motherly love.
ramacharitamanas::2206.modern_relevance: You leave for a long trip after a fight with your mother, and neither of you can say everything. A folded hand, a blessing, or a hug can carry what words cannot.
ramacharitamanas::2206.insight: It shifts attention from departure itself to the dignity and tenderness with which separation is met.

ramacharitamanas::2207.verse_sanskrit: बार-बार मुख चुंबति माता। नयन नेह जलु पुलकित गाता॥ गोद राखि पुनि हृदयँ लगाए। स्रवत प्रेमरस पयद सुहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2207.verse_hindi: माता बार-बार श्री रामचंद्रजी का मुख चूम रही हैं। नेत्रों में प्रेम का जल भर आया है और सब अंग पुलकित हो गए हैं। श्री राम को अपनी गोद में बैठाकर फिर हृदय से लगा लिया। सुंदर स्तन प्रेमरस (दूध) बहाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2207.english_translation: Mother kissed Ram's face again and again. Her eyes filled with tears of love, and her whole body trembled with joy. She placed Ram in her lap and held Him to her heart. Her breasts flowed with the milk of love.
ramacharitamanas::2207.translation_literal: बार-बार (again and again) / मुख (face) / चुंबति (kissing) / माता (mother) / नयन (eyes) / नेह (love) / जलु (water/tears) / पुलकित (thrilled) / गाता (body) / गोद (lap) / राखि (placing) / पुनि (again) / हृदयँ (to the heart) / लगाए (embraced) / स्रवत (flowing) / प्रेमरस (nectar of love) / पयद (breasts) / सुहाए (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::2207.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2207.essence: Love that cannot speak becomes tears, touch, and embrace.
ramacharitamanas::2207.simple_meaning: Kaushalya overflows with love as she kisses Ram, holds Him in her lap, and embraces Him to her heart.
ramacharitamanas::2207.simple_insight: Love becomes physical here — tears, trembling, and embrace all say what words cannot.
ramacharitamanas::2207.detailed_meaning: After Ram accepts exile, Kaushalya cannot hold back her motherly love. She kisses His face, weeps, lifts Him into her lap, and presses Him to her heart. The scene is not teaching a doctrine; it is showing the ache of separation and devotion in the royal household.
ramacharitamanas::2207.modern_relevance: You hug your child after bad news and realize comfort needs no speech. The body says what the mind cannot: stay close, stay loving, stay present.
ramacharitamanas::2207.insight: It shifts attention from explanation to embodied care — love is shown through touch, tears, and holding close.

ramacharitamanas::2208.verse_sanskrit: प्रेमु प्रमोदु न कछु कहि जाई। रंक धनद पदबी जनु पाई॥ सादर सुंदर बदनु निहारी। बोली मधुर बचन महतारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2208.verse_hindi: उनका प्रेम और महान् आनंद कुछ कहा नहीं जाता। मानो कंगाल ने कुबेर का पद पा लिया हो। बड़े आदर के साथ सुंदर मुख देखकर माता मधुर वचन बोलीं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2208.english_translation: Their love and joy could not be described. It was as if a poor man had gained Kubera's rank. With reverence she gazed at the beautiful face and spoke sweetly.
ramacharitamanas::2208.translation_literal: प्रेमु (love) / प्रमोदु (joy) / न (not) / कछु (anything) / कहि (said) / जाई (can be spoken) / रंक (poor man) / धनद (Kubera, giver of wealth) / पदबी (rank, position) / जनु (as if) / पाई (having obtained) / सादर (with reverence) / सुंदर (beautiful) / बदनु (face) / निहारी (having seen) / बोली (spoke) / मधुर (sweet) / बचन (words) / महतारी (mother)
ramacharitamanas::2208.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2208.essence: Love makes reunion feel like sudden riches.
ramacharitamanas::2208.simple_meaning: Mother's joy at seeing Ram cannot be described. It feels like a beggar suddenly becoming immensely wealthy.
ramacharitamanas::2208.simple_insight: Love can make ordinary reunion feel like a treasure beyond measure.
ramacharitamanas::2208.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaushalya welcomes Ram after the exile news has torn the family apart. Seeing his face again floods her with joy so vast it cannot be spoken; the moment feels like a beggar receiving a king's fortune.
ramacharitamanas::2208.modern_relevance: You finally see your child after weeks apart at the train platform, and the whole room disappears. Relief and love arrive so fully that language feels too small.
ramacharitamanas::2208.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the emotional abundance it awakens.

ramacharitamanas::2209.verse_sanskrit: कहहु तात जननी बलिहारी। कबहिं लगन मुद मंगलकारी॥ सुकृत सील सुख सीवँ सुहाई। जनम लाभ कइ अवधि अघाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2209.verse_hindi: हे तात! माता बलिहारी जाती है, कहो, वह आनंद- मंगलकारी लग्न कब है, जो मेरे पुण्य, शील और सुख की सुंदर सीमा है और जन्म लेने के लाभ की पूर्णतम अवधि है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2209.english_translation: Tell me, dear son, when is that auspicious wedding moment? It is the beautiful limit of my merit, virtue, and joy, and the full reward of birth.
ramacharitamanas::2209.translation_literal: कहहु (tell) / तात (dear son) / जननी (mother) / बलिहारी (devotedly grateful) / कबहिं (when) / लगन (auspicious moment) / मुद (joy) / मंगलकारी (auspicious) / सुकृत (merit) / सील (virtue) / सुख (happiness) / सीवँ (limit) / सुहाई (beautiful) / जनम (birth) / लाभ (gain) / कइ (of) / अवधि (limit) / अघाई (completely filled)
ramacharitamanas::2209.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2209.essence: A blessed moment can feel like the completion of a whole life.
ramacharitamanas::2209.simple_meaning: Mother asks when the auspicious wedding moment will come, calling it the beautiful completion of her merit, virtue, and joy.
ramacharitamanas::2209.simple_insight: Longing becomes sweetest when it is tied to blessing, not anxiety.
ramacharitamanas::2209.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaushalya is overwhelmed with love as she looks at Ram. She calls him dear son and asks when the blessed wedding moment will arrive, seeing it as the full fruit of her life.
ramacharitamanas::2209.modern_relevance: You keep checking the calendar for the day everything finally comes together — the ceremony, the reunion, the moment your waiting has meant something.
ramacharitamanas::2209.insight: It turns longing into sacred anticipation, where waiting itself feels fruitful.

ramacharitamanas::2210.verse_sanskrit: जेहि चाहत नर नारि सब अति आरत एहि भाँति। जिमि चातक चातकि तृषित बृष्टि सरद रितु स्वाति ॥
ramacharitamanas::2210.verse_hindi: तथा जिस (लग्न) को सभी स्त्री-पुरुष अत्यंत व्याकुलता से इस प्रकार चाहते हैं जिस प्रकार प्यास से चातक और चातकी शरद् ऋतु के स्वाति नक्षत्र की वर्षा को चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2210.english_translation: All men and women long for this time with deep urgency, as the thirsty chatak and chataki long for rain from Swati in autumn.
ramacharitamanas::2210.translation_literal: जेहि (which) / चाहत (desire) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / सब (all) / अति (very) / आरत (anxious) / एहि भाँति (in this way) / जिमि (as) / चातक (chatak bird) / चातकि (chataki bird) / तृषित (thirsty) / बृष्टि (rain) / सरद रितु (autumn season) / स्वाति (Swati)
ramacharitamanas::2210.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2210.essence: A blessed moment can be wanted like rain in drought.
ramacharitamanas::2210.simple_meaning: Everyone is eagerly waiting for this auspicious moment, just as thirsty birds wait for rain in the Swati season.
ramacharitamanas::2210.simple_insight: Longing can make a moment feel sacred before it even arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2210.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaushalya is speaking tenderly to Ram before his exile begins. She says the whole world waits for this blessed moment with the same thirst that chatak birds feel for rain. The line heightens the emotional weight of the farewell.
ramacharitamanas::2210.modern_relevance: You are waiting outside the exam hall, phone in hand, heart racing before the results open. The waiting itself has become its own kind of devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2210.insight: It turns ordinary waiting into intense expectation and shows how desire magnifies time.

ramacharitamanas::2211.verse_sanskrit: तात जाउँ बलि बेगि नाहाहू। जो मन भाव मधुर कछु खाहू॥ पितु समीप तब जाएहु भैआ। भइ बड़ि बार जाइ बलि मैआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2211.verse_hindi: हे तात! मैं बलैया लेती हूँ, तुम जल्दी नहा लो और जो मन भावे, कुछ मिठाई खा लो। भैया! तब पिता के पास जाना। बहुत देर हो गई है, माता बलिहारी जाती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2211.english_translation: Mother says: "Dear child, hurry and bathe. Eat whatever sweets you like. Then go to your father, son. It is already very late, my blessing is with you."
ramacharitamanas::2211.translation_literal: तात (dear child) / जाउँ (go) / बलि (blessed) / बेगि (quickly) / नाहाहू (bathe) / जो (whatever) / मन (mind) / भाव (likes) / मधुर (sweet) / कछु (some) / खाहू (eat) / पितु (father) / समीप (near) / तब (then) / जाएहु (go) / भैआ (son/brother) / भइ (became) / बड़ि (very) / बार (late) / जाइ (gone) / बलि (blessed) / मैआ (mother)
ramacharitamanas::2211.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2211.simple_meaning: The mother lovingly urges her child to bathe, eat something sweet, and then go to his father because it is already late.
ramacharitamanas::2211.simple_insight: Love can sound simple and practical: care for the body, then move toward what matters.
ramacharitamanas::2211.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the family mood is tender and domestic, not grand. A mother speaks gently to her child, telling him to bathe, eat, and then go to his father because time has slipped away. The scene deepens the warmth of home before the coming fracture.
ramacharitamanas::2211.modern_relevance: A parent calls from the kitchen while a child is still half-dressed, reminding them to eat before leaving for school. Small instructions carry real love when they are spoken with care.
ramacharitamanas::2211.insight: It teaches you that affection often appears as ordinary guidance, not dramatic emotion.

ramacharitamanas::2212.verse_sanskrit: मातु बचन सुनि अति अनुकूला। जनु सनेह सुरतरु के फूला॥ सुख मकरंद भरे श्रियमूला। निरखि राम मनु भवँरु न भूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::2212.verse_hindi: माता के अत्यंत अनुकूल वचन सुनकर- जो मानो स्नेह रूपी कल्पवृक्ष के फूल थे, जो सुख रूपी मकरन्द (पुष्परस) से भरे थे और श्री (राजलक्ष्मी) के मूल थे- ऐसे वचन रूपी फूलों को देकर श्री रामचंद्रजी का मन रूपी भौंरा उन पर नहीं भूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::2212.english_translation: Hearing his mother's affectionate words, Ram's mind did not wander from them, like a bee that stays on a flower filled with nectar.
ramacharitamanas::2212.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / अति (very) / अनुकूला (pleasant, agreeable) / जनु (as if) / सनेह (affection) / सुरतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / के (of) / फूला (flowers) / सुख (happiness) / मकरंद (nectar) / भरे (filled) / श्रियमूला (root of prosperity) / निरखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / मनु (mind) / भवँरु (bee) / न (not) / भूला (wandered away)
ramacharitamanas::2212.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2212.essence: Affection can hold the mind more firmly than force.
ramacharitamanas::2212.simple_meaning: Ram listens to his mother's loving words and stays completely absorbed in them, like a bee resting on a nectar-filled flower.
ramacharitamanas::2212.simple_insight: Love holds attention without force. What is cherished naturally becomes the mind's resting place.
ramacharitamanas::2212.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has just spoken gently to Ram, and the scene is still tender before the exile's pain fully unfolds. Her words, though part of a larger family rupture, land on Ram as sweet and affectionate, and his mind remains fixed on her.
ramacharitamanas::2212.modern_relevance: Your phone is buzzing, the room is loud, but one kind message from your mother cuts through everything. Some words do not just reach you — they hold you.
ramacharitamanas::2212.insight: It shows how affection can steady the mind, turning attention from restlessness to quiet absorption.

ramacharitamanas::2213.verse_sanskrit: धरम धुरीन धरम गति जानी। कहेउ मातु सन अति मृदु बानी॥ पिताँ दीन्ह मोहि कानन राजू। जहँ सब भाँति मोर बड़ काजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2213.verse_hindi: धर्मधुरीण श्री रामचंद्रजी ने धर्म की गति को जानकर माता से अत्यंत कोमल वाणी से कहा- हे माता! पिताजी ने मुझको वन का राज्य दिया है, जहाँ सब प्रकार से मेरा बड़ा काम बनने वाला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2213.english_translation: Ram, who fully knows the course of dharma, spoke to his mother in very gentle words: “Father has given me the kingdom of the forest, where my great work lies in every way.”
ramacharitamanas::2213.translation_literal: धरम धुरीन (steadfast in dharma) / धरम गति (the course of dharma) / जानी (knowing) / कहेउ (spoke) / मातु सन (to mother) / अति मृदु बानी (very gentle words)॥ / पिताँ (by father) / दीन्ह (given) / मोहि (to me) / कानन राजू (the kingdom of the forest) / जहँ (where) / सब भाँति (in every way) / मोर (my) / बड़ काजू (great work) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2213.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2213.essence: Dharma is honored when the hardest assignment is accepted gently.
ramacharitamanas::2213.simple_meaning: Ram speaks gently to his mother and accepts the forest exile as the place where his duty now lies.
ramacharitamanas::2213.simple_insight: There is dignity in accepting the hard task without complaint.
ramacharitamanas::2213.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram stands before his mother after Dasarath has sent him away. He does not resist or argue. Knowing dharma, he answers with tenderness and treats the forest exile as the work he must now fulfill.
ramacharitamanas::2213.modern_relevance: You get the call that changes everything: the promotion is gone, the move is fixed, the plan has already shifted. Ram shows how to answer without bitterness, and still stand upright.
ramacharitamanas::2213.insight: It teaches you to meet unavoidable duty with calm speech and inward steadiness.

ramacharitamanas::2214.verse_sanskrit: आयसु देहि मुदित मन माता। जेहिं मुद मंगल कानन जाता॥ जनि सनेह बस डरपसि भोरें। आनँदु अंब अनुग्रह तोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2214.verse_hindi: हे माता! तू प्रसन्न मन से मुझे आज्ञा दे, जिससे मेरी वन यात्रा में आनंद-मंगल हो। मेरे स्नेहवश भूलकर भी डरना नहीं। हे माता! तेरी कृपा से आनंद ही होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2214.english_translation: Mother, give me your blessing with a glad heart, so my journey to the forest may be full of auspiciousness. Do not let affection make you fearful. Through your grace, only joy will remain.
ramacharitamanas::2214.translation_literal: आयसु (permission / blessing) / देहि (give) / मुदित मन (with glad mind) / माता (mother) / जेहिं (by which) / मुद मंगल (auspicious joy) / कानन (forest) / जाता (going) / जनि (do not) / सनेह (affection) / बस (under the sway of) / डरपसि (fear) / भोरें (in confusion / by mistake) / आनँदु (joy) / अंब (mother) / अनुग्रह (grace) / तोरें (yours)
ramacharitamanas::2214.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2214.essence: True affection blesses the path instead of blocking it.
ramacharitamanas::2214.simple_meaning: Ram asks his mother to bless his journey to the forest with a joyful heart. He tells her not to let love turn into fear, because her grace should bring only blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2214.simple_insight: Love does not have to become panic. Blessing someone well can be an act of courage.
ramacharitamanas::2214.detailed_meaning: Ram has already accepted exile and is speaking gently to his mother before leaving Ayodhya. He asks for her cheerful permission, not sorrowful resistance, so the forest journey begins under blessing rather than grief.
ramacharitamanas::2214.modern_relevance: You are about to leave for a hard move, a risky surgery, or a painful goodbye. The person who loves you most can either tighten the fear or bless the step forward.
ramacharitamanas::2214.insight: It shifts family love from clinging to brave blessing.

ramacharitamanas::2215.verse_sanskrit: बरष चारिदस बिपिन बसि करि पितु बचन प्रमान। आइ पाय पुनि देखिहउँ मनु जनि करसि मलान ॥
ramacharitamanas::2215.verse_hindi: चौदह वर्ष वन में रहकर, पिताजी के वचन को प्रमाणित (सत्य) कर, फिर लौटकर तेरे चरणों का दर्शन करूँगा, तू मन को म्लान (दुःखी) न कर ॥
ramacharitamanas::2215.english_translation: Living in the forest for fourteen years, I will prove my father's word true and then return to see your feet. Do not let your mind grow sad.
ramacharitamanas::2215.translation_literal: बरष (years) / चारिदस (fourteen) / बिपिन (forest) / बसि (dwelling) / करि (having done) / पितु (father's) / बचन (word) / प्रमान (proof) / आइ (coming) / पाय (feet) / पुनि (again) / देखिहउँ (I will see) / मनु (mind) / जनि (do not) / करसि (make) / मलान (withered/sad)
ramacharitamanas::2215.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2215.essence: Keeping a father's word matters more than keeping a throne.
ramacharitamanas::2215.simple_meaning: Ram says he will spend fourteen years in the forest, make his father's word come true, and return to see his mother. He asks her not to grieve.
ramacharitamanas::2215.simple_insight: Love can be steady without clinging. Keeping a hard promise becomes its own comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2215.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram stands before his mother after accepting exile. He does not argue with fate or soften the promise. He turns his father's command into a vow, and his mother's sorrow into something he must carry with care.
ramacharitamanas::2215.modern_relevance: You leave home for a difficult posting, a family promise still hanging in the air. You cannot erase the pain, but you can keep the word that gives it meaning.
ramacharitamanas::2215.insight: It teaches you to treat a painful obligation as sacred, not merely unfortunate.

ramacharitamanas::2216.verse_sanskrit: बचन बिनीत मधुर रघुबर के। सर सम लगे मातु उर करके॥ सहमि सूखि सुनि सीतलि बानी। जिमि जवास परें पावस पानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2216.verse_hindi: रघुकुल में श्रेष्ठ श्री रामजी के ये बहुत ही नम्र और मीठे वचन माता के हृदय में बाण के समान लगे और कसकने लगे। उस शीतल वाणी को सुनकर कौसल्या वैसे ही सहमकर सूख गईं जैसे बरसात का पानी पड़ने से जवासा सूख जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2216.english_translation: The humble, sweet words of Raghubar pierced Mother Kaushalya's heart like arrows. Hearing that cooling speech, she trembled and withered, like javasa plants after rain.
ramacharitamanas::2216.translation_literal: बचन (words) / बिनीत (humble) / मधुर (sweet) / रघुबर के (of Raghubar) / सर (arrows) / सम (like) / लगे (struck) / मातु (mother) / उर (heart) / करके (doing) / सहमि (trembling) / सूखि (withered) / सुनि (hearing) / सीतलि (cooling) / बानी (speech) / जिमि (like) / जवास (javasa plant) / परें (falling) / पावस (rainy season) / पानी (water)
ramacharitamanas::2216.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2216.essence: Gentle words can wound more deeply than harsh ones.
ramacharitamanas::2216.simple_meaning: Ram speaks gently, but his words pierce Kaushalya's heart. Her body and mind react as if struck by sudden grief.
ramacharitamanas::2216.simple_insight: Even kind words can carry unbearable pain when they reveal a separation you cannot bear.
ramacharitamanas::2216.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is preparing to leave for exile and speaks tenderly to Kaushalya. His humility and sweetness do not comfort her; they cut deeper because they confirm what is about to be lost.
