ramacharitamanas::2216.modern_relevance: You hear a loving voice note from someone leaving town, and the softness makes it harder, not easier. Sometimes gentleness carries the full weight of goodbye.
ramacharitamanas::2216.insight: It shows how tenderness can intensify grief when the heart already knows what it is losing.

ramacharitamanas::2217.verse_sanskrit: कहि न जाइ कछु हृदय बिषादू। मनहुँ मृगी सुनि केहरि नादू॥ नयन सजल तन थर थर काँपी। माजहि खाइ मीन जनु मापी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2217.verse_hindi: हृदय का विषाद कुछ कहा नहीं जाता। मानो सिंह की गर्जना सुनकर हिरनी विकल हो गई हो। नेत्रों में जल भर आया, शरीर थर-थर काँपने लगा। मानो मछली माँजा (पहली वर्षा का फेन) खाकर बदहवास हो गई हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2217.english_translation: The grief in her heart cannot be spoken. She trembled like a doe hearing a lion's roar. Tears filled her eyes and her body shook. Like a fish stunned by the first monsoon foam, she lost all composure.
ramacharitamanas::2217.translation_literal: कहि न जाइ (cannot be said) / कछु (any) / हृदय (heart) / बिषादू (grief) / मनहुँ (as if) / मृगी (doe) / सुनि (hearing) / केहरि (lion) / नादू (roar) / नयन (eyes) / सजल (filled with water) / तन (body) / थर थर (trembling) / काँपी (shook) / माजहि (in the middle) / खाइ (eating) / मीन (fish) / जनु (as if) / मापी (measured / lost composure)
ramacharitamanas::2217.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2217.essence: Deep sorrow can silence speech and shake the body itself.
ramacharitamanas::2217.simple_meaning: Her sorrow is so deep that it cannot be put into words. She trembles, cries, and loses composure at the sight and sound before her.
ramacharitamanas::2217.simple_insight: Some pain hits so hard that the body speaks before the mind can.
ramacharitamanas::2217.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaushalya has just heard Ram's gentle but devastating vow to leave for exile. The room turns into a scene of shock: her grief is too large for speech, her body reacts before she can gather herself.
ramacharitamanas::2217.modern_relevance: You read a message that changes everything, and for a moment your hands go cold. Before you can think, your body already knows the news is too heavy.
ramacharitamanas::2217.insight: It shows grief as a full-body collapse, not just a private feeling.

ramacharitamanas::2218.verse_sanskrit: धरि धीरजु सुत बदनु निहारी। गदगद बचन कहति महतारी॥ तात पितहि तुम्ह प्रानपिआरे। देखि मुदित नित चरित तुम्हारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2218.verse_hindi: धीरज धरकर, पुत्र का मुख देखकर माता गदगद वचन कहने लगीं- हे तात! तुम तो पिता को प्राणों के समान प्रिय हो। तुम्हारे चरित्रों को देखकर वे नित्य प्रसन्न होते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2218.english_translation: Gathering her composure, she looked at her son’s face and spoke in a choked voice: “My dear child, you were as dear to your father as life itself. Seeing your conduct always made him glad.”
ramacharitamanas::2218.translation_literal: धरि (having held) / धीरजु (composure) / सुत (son) / बदनु (face) / निहारी (having looked at) / गदगद (choked, faltering) / बचन (words) / कहति (speaking) / महतारी (mother) / तात (dear child) / पितहि (to father) / तुम्ह (you) / प्रानपिआरे (dear as life) / देखि (seeing) / मुदित (glad) / नित (always) / चरित (conduct, deeds) / तुम्हारे (your)
ramacharitamanas::2218.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2218.essence: Grief remembers love before it can speak blame.
ramacharitamanas::2218.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi steadies herself, looks at Ram’s face, and says he was Dasharath’s dearest child. She remembers that Dasharath was always happy to see Ram’s conduct.
ramacharitamanas::2218.simple_insight: Love can speak even through grief, and memory can soften a breaking heart.
ramacharitamanas::2218.detailed_meaning: After Dasharath’s death, Kaikeyi faces Ram and tries to speak through tears. She remembers how deeply Dasharath loved him and how his good conduct always pleased the king. The scene turns from accusation toward aching remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::2218.modern_relevance: You finally sit beside someone after a family loss, and the first thing you can manage is a memory: how much the absent person loved them. Grief often speaks that way, in fragments of tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::2218.insight: It shifts attention from blame to remembrance, letting grief speak in a gentler, truer register.

ramacharitamanas::2219.verse_sanskrit: राजु देन कहुँ सुभ दिन साधा। कहेउ जान बन केहिं अपराधा॥ तात सुनावहु मोहि निदानू। को दिनकर कुल भयउ कृसानू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2219.verse_hindi: राज्य देने के लिए उन्होंने ही शुभ दिन शोधवाया था। फिर अब किस अपराध से वन जाने को कहा? हे तात! मुझे इसका कारण सुनाओ! सूर्यवंश (रूपी वन) को जलाने के लिए अग्नि कौन हो गया? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2219.english_translation: They had chosen an auspicious day for giving the kingdom. Then, by what fault is he sent to the forest? Mother, tell me the reason. Who has become the fire to burn the sun-born line?
ramacharitamanas::2219.translation_literal: राजु (kingdom) / देन (to give) / कहुँ (for) / सुभ (auspicious) / दिन (day) / साधा (chosen)। / कहेउ (said) / जान (to go) / बन (to forest) / केहिं (by what) / अपराधा (fault)॥ / तात (mother/father) / सुनावहु (tell) / मोहि (to me) / निदानू (the reason)। / को (who) / दिनकर (sun) / कुल (lineage) / भयउ (became) / कृसानू (fire) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2219.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2219.essence: A planned coronation turns into exile, and the heart demands a reason.
ramacharitamanas::2219.simple_meaning: The speaker is confused and hurt: if the kingdom was meant to be handed over on an auspicious day, why is exile being ordered now? She asks who has caused such ruin to the solar lineage.
ramacharitamanas::2219.simple_insight: Pain sharpens into a question when injustice arrives without warning.
ramacharitamanas::2219.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court's joy has turned to grief. The auspicious day for Ram's coronation was already fixed, yet exile has been announced instead. A distressed mother asks how such a reversal happened and who has brought fire into the solar line.
ramacharitamanas::2219.modern_relevance: You prepare for a promotion, the date is set, the family is relieved — and then one sudden decision tears everything apart. The mind asks the same question: how did this happen?
ramacharitamanas::2219.insight: It captures the shock of a promised future collapsing into betrayal and grief.

ramacharitamanas::2220.verse_sanskrit: निरखि राम रुख सचिवसुत कारनु कहेउ बुझाइ। सुनि प्रसंगु रहि मूक जिमि दसा बरनि नहिं जाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2220.verse_hindi: तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी का रुख देखकर मन्त्री के पुत्र ने सब कारण समझाकर कहा। उस प्रसंग को सुनकर वे गूँगी जैसी (चुप) रह गईं, उनकी दशा का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2220.english_translation: Then, seeing Ram's expression, the minister's son explained the reason. Hearing the whole matter, she became silent as if mute; her condition cannot be described.
ramacharitamanas::2220.translation_literal: निरखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / रुख (expression) / सचिवसुत (minister's son) / कारनु (reason) / कहेउ (said) / बुझाइ (explaining clearly) / सुनि (hearing) / प्रसंगु (the matter) / रहि (remained) / मूक (mute) / जिमि (like) / दसा (state) / बरनि (described) / नहिं (not) / जाइ (can be done)
ramacharitamanas::2220.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2220.essence: Some grief leaves no room for words.
ramacharitamanas::2220.simple_meaning: Hearing the explanation, she fell silent and was overwhelmed. Her pain was so deep that words could not capture it.
ramacharitamanas::2220.simple_insight: Some grief is too large for speech. Silence can be the only honest response.
ramacharitamanas::2220.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the minister's son explains the reason Ram is being sent away. The mother looks at Ram's face, hears the full story, and is struck mute. This verse captures the instant her shock turns into unbearable sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2220.modern_relevance: You finally hear the full reason behind a decision that changes everything — a move, a breakup, a family choice. The explanation helps, but it does not soften the ache.
ramacharitamanas::2220.insight: It shifts attention from argument to emotional reality: some truths are understood only as pain, not as debate.

ramacharitamanas::2221.verse_sanskrit: राखि न सकइ न कहि सक जाहू। दुहूँ भाँति उर दारुन दाहू॥ लिखत सुधाकर गा लिखि राहू। बिधि गति बाम सदा सब काहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2221.verse_hindi: न रख ही सकती हैं, न यह कह सकती हैं कि वन चले जाओ। दोनों ही प्रकार से हृदय में बड़ा भारी संताप हो रहा है। (मन में सोचती हैं कि देखो-) विधाता की चाल सदा सबके लिए टेढ़ी होती है। लिखने लगे चन्द्रमा और लिखा गया राहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2221.english_translation: She cannot keep him, and she cannot tell him to go to the forest. Both ways, her heart burns with terrible pain. Fate is always crooked for everyone: the moon was written, and Rahu came out.
ramacharitamanas::2221.translation_literal: राखि (to keep) / न (not) / सकइ (is able) / न (not) / कहि (to say) / सक जाहू (go to the forest) / दुहूँ भाँति (in both ways) / उर (heart) / दारुन (terrible) / दाहू (burning) / लिखत (while writing) / सुधाकर (moon) / गा (became) / लिखि (written) / राहू (Rahu) / बिधि (fate) / गति (course) / बाम (crooked) / सदा (always) / सब काहू (for everyone)
ramacharitamanas::2221.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2221.essence: Love and duty can burn the heart from opposite sides.
ramacharitamanas::2221.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is trapped between two impossible choices. She cannot hold on to Ram, and she cannot bear to send him away. Her heart burns with grief and confusion.
ramacharitamanas::2221.simple_insight: Some choices hurt no matter what you do. The mind can be torn apart by duty, love, and consequence at once.
ramacharitamanas::2221.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has learned the truth behind Ram's exile and feels the full weight of it. She cannot undo what has begun, yet she cannot emotionally accept it either. This verse captures her inner torment before the grief turns into open moral conflict.
ramacharitamanas::2221.modern_relevance: You are holding a phone after sending a message you cannot take back. One reply will wound someone, the other will wound you. The body knows what the mind cannot resolve.
ramacharitamanas::2221.insight: It names the paralysis that comes when every option carries loss, and no choice feels clean.

ramacharitamanas::2222.verse_sanskrit: धरम सनेह उभयँ मति घेरी। भइ गति साँप छुछुंदरि केरी॥ राखउँ सुतहि करउँ अनुरोधू। धरमु जाइ अरु बंधु बिरोधू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2222.verse_hindi: धर्म और स्नेह दोनों ने कौसल्याजी की बुद्धि को घेर लिया। उनकी दशा साँप-छछूँदर की सी हो गई। वे सोचने लगीं कि यदि मैं अनुरोध (हठ) करके पुत्र को रख लेती हूँ तो धर्म जाता है और भाइयों में विरोध होता है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2222.english_translation: Dharma and affection both surrounded Kaushalya's mind. She was in the state of a snake and a mongoose. If I insist and keep my son, duty is lost and there will be conflict among brothers.
ramacharitamanas::2222.translation_literal: धरम (dharma) / सनेह (affection) / उभयँ (both) / मति (mind) / घेरी (surrounded) / भइ (became) / गति (state) / साँप (snake) / छुछुंदरि (mongoose) / केरी (of) / राखउँ (I keep) / सुतहि (son) / करउँ (I do) / अनुरोधू (insistence) / धरमु (duty) / जाइ (goes away) / अरु (and) / बंधु (brother) / बिरोधू (conflict)
ramacharitamanas::2222.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2222.essence: Love and duty can pull so hard that the mind freezes.
ramacharitamanas::2222.simple_meaning: Kaushalya feels torn between duty and love. Keeping her son would break dharma and create conflict among the brothers.
ramacharitamanas::2222.simple_insight: Love becomes painful when it cannot find the right action.
ramacharitamanas::2222.detailed_meaning: Kaushalya stands between Ram's exile and her own maternal love. She cannot ask him to stay, yet she cannot bear to send him away. The verse captures her inner knot before she finally reasons through it.
ramacharitamanas::2222.modern_relevance: You hold your phone after reading a message that could change everything. Replying honestly may hurt someone you love, but avoiding it would also be wrong. That split feeling is Kaushalya's moment.
ramacharitamanas::2222.insight: It shifts the mind from choosing by emotion alone to weighing the deeper cost of each choice.

ramacharitamanas::2223.verse_sanskrit: कहउँ जान बन तौ बड़ि हानी। संकट सोच बिबस भइ रानी॥ बहुरि समुझि तिय धरमु सयानी। रामु भरतु दोउ सुत सम जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2223.verse_hindi: और यदि वन जाने को कहती हूँ तो बड़ी हानि होती है। इस प्रकार के धर्मसंकट में पड़कर रानी विशेष रूप से सोच के वश हो गईं। फिर बुद्धिमती कौसल्याजी स्त्री धर्म (पातिव्रत धर्म) को समझकर और राम तथा भरत दोनों पुत्रों को समान जानकर- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2223.english_translation: If I tell him to go to the forest, it will be a great loss. Caught in this crisis of duty, the queen became helpless with thought. Then wise Kausalya reflected on a wife's duty and saw Ram and Bharat as equal sons.
ramacharitamanas::2223.translation_literal: कहउँ (if I say) / जान (to the forest) / बन (forest) / तौ (then) / बड़ि (great) / हानी (loss) / संकट (crisis) / सोच (thought) / बिबस (helpless) / भइ (became) / रानी (queen) / बहुरि (again) / समुझि (understanding) / तिय धरमु (wife’s duty) / सयानी (wise) / रामु (Ram) / भरतु (Bharat) / दोउ (both) / सुत (sons) / सम (equal) / जानी (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::2223.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2223.essence: Wisdom begins when you stop demanding a choice without loss.
ramacharitamanas::2223.simple_meaning: Kausalya is torn between two harms: sending Ram away or keeping him back. She pauses, remembers her duty as a wife, and sees both Ram and Bharat as equally her sons.
ramacharitamanas::2223.simple_insight: Some choices hurt either way. Wisdom begins when the heart stops demanding a painless answer.
ramacharitamanas::2223.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kausalya stands at the edge of a family ruin. If she asks Ram to leave, she loses him; if she asks him to stay, she blocks his father's command. The verse shows her caught in a painful dharma conflict before she steadies herself.
ramacharitamanas::2223.modern_relevance: You’re on a call where either answer wounds someone you love. One option protects one relationship, the other protects another. The mind freezes until it can hold both losses without panic.
ramacharitamanas::2223.insight: It shifts the mind from seeking a perfect outcome to facing a painful duty clearly.

ramacharitamanas::2224.verse_sanskrit: सरल सुभाउ राम महतारी। बोली बचन धीर धरि भारी॥ तात जाउँ बलि कीन्हेहु नीका। पितु आयसु सब धरमक टीका ॥
ramacharitamanas::2224.verse_hindi: सरल स्वभाव वाली श्री रामचन्द्रजी की माता बड़ा धीरज धरकर वचन बोलीं- हे तात! मैं बलिहारी जाती हूँ, तुमने अच्छा किया। पिता की आज्ञा का पालन करना ही सब धर्मों का शिरोमणि धर्म है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2224.english_translation: With a simple nature, Ram's mother spoke with great composure: "Dear son, I bless you. You have done well. Obeying a father's command is the crown of all righteousness."
ramacharitamanas::2224.translation_literal: सरल (simple) / सुभाउ (nature) / राम (Ram) / महतारी (mother) / बोली (spoke) / बचन (words) / धीर (calm) / धरि (holding) / भारी (great) / तात (dear son) / जाउँ (I go) / बलि (offering myself) / कीन्हेहु (you did) / नीका (well) / पितु (father) / आयसु (command) / सब (all) / धरमक (of righteousness) / टीका (crown)
ramacharitamanas::2224.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::2224.essence: True duty can cost everything and still remain right.
ramacharitamanas::2224.simple_meaning: Kausalya praises Ram for obeying his father's command and says that keeping a parent's word is the highest duty.
ramacharitamanas::2224.simple_insight: Love does not always resist sacrifice; sometimes it blesses the hard choice that keeps a promise intact.
ramacharitamanas::2224.detailed_meaning: Kausalya has been torn between love for Ram and the pain of exile. After weighing both sides, she steadies herself and blesses him. In this moment, she names obedience to a father's word as the highest standard of right conduct.
ramacharitamanas::2224.modern_relevance: Your parent asks for something that costs you dearly, and every part of you wants to refuse. Kausalya's answer is the opposite of convenience: some promises matter more than comfort, and keeping them can be an act of love.
ramacharitamanas::2224.insight: It shifts duty from burden to sacred priority, showing that obedience can be a conscious moral choice.

ramacharitamanas::2225.verse_sanskrit: राजु देन कहिदीन्ह बनु मोहि न सो दुख लेसु। तुम्ह बिनु भरतहि भूपतिहि प्रजहि प्रचंड कलेसु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2225.verse_hindi: राज्य देने को कहकर वन दे दिया, उसका मुझे लेशमात्र भी दुःख नहीं है। (दुःख तो इस बात का है कि) तुम्हारे बिना भरत को, महाराज को और प्रजा को बड़ा भारी क्लेश होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2225.english_translation: I gave up the kingdom and sent myself to the forest; I feel no grief at all. The real pain is that, without you, Bharata, the king, and the people will suffer terribly.
ramacharitamanas::2225.translation_literal: राजु (kingdom) / देन (to give) / कहिदीन्ह (having said, gave) / बनु (forest) / मोहि (to me) / न (not) / सो (that) / दुख (grief) / लेसु (even a little) / तुम्ह (you) / बिनु (without) / भरतहि (to Bharata) / भूपतिहि (to the king) / प्रजहि (to the people) / प्रचंड (severe) / कलेसु (distress)
ramacharitamanas::2225.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2225.essence: The loss is not the throne; it is the suffering left behind.
ramacharitamanas::2225.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi says she does not grieve losing the kingdom. Her deeper sorrow is that Bharata, the king, and the people will suffer without Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2225.simple_insight: A choice can feel right in the moment and still wound everyone around it.
ramacharitamanas::2225.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi defends the bargain that sent Ram away. She says the kingdom itself does not pain her; what troubles her is the suffering that will fall on Bharata, Dasharath, and the people once Ram is gone.
ramacharitamanas::2225.modern_relevance: You make a decision in a tense family meeting and feel certain at first. Later you realize the real cost was not your own comfort, but the strain it placed on everyone else.
ramacharitamanas::2225.insight: It shifts attention from personal gain to the wider damage a decision can cause.

ramacharitamanas::2226.verse_sanskrit: जौं केवल पितु आयसु ताता। तौ जनि जाहु जानि बड़ि माता॥ जौं पितु मातु कहेउ बन जाना। तौ कानन सत अवध समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2226.verse_hindi: हे तात! यदि केवल पिताजी की ही आज्ञा, हो तो माता को (पिता से) बड़ी जानकर वन को मत जाओ, किन्तु यदि पिता-माता दोनों ने वन जाने को कहा हो, तो वन तुम्हारे लिए सैकड़ों अयोध्या के समान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2226.english_translation: O dear son, if only your father has commanded it, then do not go, regarding your mother as greater. But if both father and mother have told you to go to the forest, then the forest is as good as hundreds of Ayodhyas for you.
ramacharitamanas::2226.translation_literal: जौं (if) / केवल (only) / पितु (father) / आयसु (command) / ताता (dear son) / तौ (then) / जनि (do not) / जाहु (go) / जानि (knowing) / बड़ि (greater) / माता (mother)॥ / जौं (if) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / कहेउ (said) / बन (forest) / जाना (to go) / तौ (then) / कानन (forest) / सत (hundreds) / अवध (Ayodhya) / समाना (equal) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2226.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::2226.essence: A rightful command can turn exile into home.
ramacharitamanas::2226.simple_meaning: Kausalya tells Ram that if only his father ordered exile, he should stay for his mother’s sake. But if both parents agreed, the forest becomes as welcome as Ayodhya itself.
ramacharitamanas::2226.simple_insight: Love does not erase duty; it clarifies it. A hard path becomes bearable when it is fully right.
ramacharitamanas::2226.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kausalya speaks to Ram as the exile decision settles over the family. She distinguishes between a single command and a shared parental will, showing Ram that obedience is not blind but rooted in right order.
ramacharitamanas::2226.modern_relevance: Your parent says one thing, your other parent another, and you stand frozen between loyalty and obligation. This verse knows that ache: the right choice becomes easier when the whole family’s truth is clear.
ramacharitamanas::2226.insight: It teaches you to weigh obligation by the full moral context, not by a single voice. Duty becomes steadier when it is confirmed from all sides.

ramacharitamanas::2227.verse_sanskrit: पितु बनदेव मातु बनदेवी। खग मृग चरन सरोरुह सेवी॥ अंतहुँ उचित नृपहि बनबासू। बय बिलोकि हियँ होइ हराँसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2227.verse_hindi: वन के देवता तुम्हारे पिता होंगे और वनदेवियाँ माता होंगी। वहाँ के पशु-पक्षी तुम्हारे चरणकमलों के सेवक होंगे। राजा के लिए अंत में तो वनवास करना उचित ही है। केवल तुम्हारी (सुकुमार) अवस्था देखकर हृदय में दुःख होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2227.english_translation: The forest would have your father as its deity and your mother as its goddess. The birds and animals there would serve your lotus feet. For a king, living in the forest is fitting in the end. Only your tender age makes my heart ache.
ramacharitamanas::2227.translation_literal: पितु (father) / बनदेव (forest-deity) / मातु (mother) / बनदेवी (forest-goddess) / खग (birds) / मृग (deer/animals) / चरन (feet) / सरोरुह (lotus) / सेवी (servants) / अंतहुँ (even at the end) / उचित (fit/proper) / नृपहि (for a king) / बनबासू (forest-exile) / बय (age/youth) / बिलोकि (seeing) / हियँ (in the heart) / होइ (becomes) / हराँसू (pain/sorrow)
ramacharitamanas::2227.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2227.essence: The right path can still break the heart that loves you.
ramacharitamanas::2227.simple_meaning: The forest would welcome Ram like a royal home, and even its creatures would serve him. Yet Dasharath still grieves because Ram is so young.
ramacharitamanas::2227.simple_insight: Sometimes the right path still hurts, because love can see what duty ignores.
ramacharitamanas::2227.detailed_meaning: Dasharath continues pleading with Ram to stay. He imagines the forest itself honoring Ram, as if exile could become a royal welcome. But the king cannot hide the real wound: Ram is still too tender for such hardship.
ramacharitamanas::2227.modern_relevance: You tell yourself, "This will be good for me," while packing a child’s bag for a hard move. The decision may be right, and the ache may still be real.
ramacharitamanas::2227.insight: It separates what is fitting from what is emotionally bearable, showing that duty and tenderness can coexist.

ramacharitamanas::2228.verse_sanskrit: बड़भागी बनु अवध अभागी। जो रघुबंसतिलक तुम्ह त्यागी॥ जौं सुत कहौं संग मोहि लेहू। तुम्हरे हृदयँ होइ संदेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2228.verse_hindi: हे रघुवंश के तिलक! वन बड़ा भाग्यवान है और यह अवध अभागा है, जिसे तुमने त्याग दिया। हे पुत्र! यदि मैं कहूँ कि मुझे भी साथ ले चलो तो तुम्हारे हृदय में संदेह होगा (कि माता इसी बहाने मुझे रोकना चाहती हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2228.english_translation: O jewel of the Raghu line, the forest is fortunate and Ayodhya is unfortunate, for you have left it. If I say, 'Son, take me with you,' your heart will doubt me.
ramacharitamanas::2228.translation_literal: बड़भागी (most fortunate) / बनु (the forest) / अवध (Ayodhya) / अभागी (unfortunate) / जो (which) / रघुबंसतिलक (jewel of the Raghu line) / तुम्ह (you) / त्यागी (have left)॥ / जौं (if) / सुत (son) / कहौं (I say) / संग (with) / मोहि (me) / लेहू (take) / तुम्हरे (your) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / होइ (will be) / संदेहू (doubt)॥
ramacharitamanas::2228.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2228.essence: Even a mother's plea can sound like a trap after trust breaks.
ramacharitamanas::2228.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi says the forest is blessed because Ram will live there, while Ayodhya is unfortunate because it will lose him. She also says Ram may doubt her if she asks to go with him.
ramacharitamanas::2228.simple_insight: Love can be so wounded that even a mother fears being misunderstood.
ramacharitamanas::2228.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi speaks to Ram as exile is being forced on him. She calls the forest fortunate because it will receive him, and Ayodhya unfortunate because it loses him. Then she admits that if she asks to go along, Ram may suspect her intent.
ramacharitamanas::2228.modern_relevance: You want to say, 'Let me come too,' but you already know the request will sound like control. Sometimes care arrives too late, after trust has cracked.
ramacharitamanas::2228.insight: It reveals how broken trust makes even loving words sound suspicious.

ramacharitamanas::2229.verse_sanskrit: पूत परम प्रिय तुम्ह सबही के। प्रान प्रान के जीवन जी के॥ ते तुम्ह कहहु मातु बन जाऊँ। मैं सुनि बचन बैठि पछिताऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2229.verse_hindi: हे पुत्र! तुम सभी के परम प्रिय हो। प्राणों के प्राण और हृदय के जीवन हो। वही (प्राणाधार) तुम कहते हो कि माता! मैं वन को जाऊँ और मैं तुम्हारे वचनों को सुनकर बैठी पछताती हूँ! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2229.english_translation: O son, you are the dearest of all. You are the life of life, the very breath of our breath. And yet you say, “Mother, I must go to the forest,” and I sit here grieving after hearing your words.
ramacharitamanas::2229.translation_literal: पूत (son) / परम प्रिय (most dear) / तुम्ह (you) / सबही के (of everyone) / प्रान (life-breath) / प्रान के (of breath) / जीवन (life) / जी के (of the heart) / ते (therefore/then) / तुम्ह (you) / कहहु (say) / मातु (mother) / बन (forest) / जाऊँ (I should go) / मैं (I) / सुनि (hearing) / बचन (words) / बैठि (sitting) / पछिताऊँ (grieve/repent)
ramacharitamanas::2229.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2229.essence: The dearest person can still be the hardest to let go.
ramacharitamanas::2229.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi calls Ram the dearest life of everyone, then laments that he is still choosing exile. Her words carry both love and pain.
ramacharitamanas::2229.simple_insight: Love can become unbearable when it must bless the loss it fears most.
ramacharitamanas::2229.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi speaks to Ram while the exile is being accepted. She calls him the breath of everyone’s life, then breaks under the thought of losing him to the forest. Her words deepen the family’s wound.
ramacharitamanas::2229.modern_relevance: You watch your child pack a bag for a long move, and every blessing feels like a small tear. Love does not always soften pain; sometimes it makes goodbye sharper.
ramacharitamanas::2229.insight: It shows how affection can coexist with helpless grief, without turning into resistance or cruelty.

ramacharitamanas::2230.verse_sanskrit: यह बिचारि नहिं करउँ हठ झूठ सनेहु बढ़ाइ। मानि मातु कर नात बलि सुरति बिसरि जनि जाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2230.verse_hindi: यह सोचकर झूठा स्नेह बढ़ाकर मैं हठ नहीं करती! बेटा! मैं बलैया लेती हूँ, माता का नाता मानकर मेरी सुध भूल न जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2230.english_translation: Thinking thus, I will not fake affection by stubbornness. Son, I bow to you; remembering your mother's bond, do not forget me.
ramacharitamanas::2230.translation_literal: यह (this) / बिचारि (thinking) / नहिं (not) / करउँ (I do) / हठ (stubbornness) / झूठ (false) / सनेहु (affection) / बढ़ाइ (increasing) / मानि (accepting) / मातु (mother) / कर (of) / नात (bond) / बलि (I bow) / सुरति (memory) / बिसरि (forget) / जनि (do not) / जाइ (go)
ramacharitamanas::2230.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2230.essence: False affection cannot heal what truth must face.
ramacharitamanas::2230.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi says she will not pretend affection or cling stubbornly. She accepts the bond of a mother and asks Ram not to forget her.
ramacharitamanas::2230.simple_insight: Real love stops demanding a performance and speaks honestly, even when the heart is breaking.
ramacharitamanas::2230.detailed_meaning: Kaikeyi is speaking after Ram's exile has been set in motion. Faced with the cost of her own demand, she drops the mask of false tenderness and addresses Ram as a mother who still longs to be remembered.
ramacharitamanas::2230.modern_relevance: You realize a relationship is damaged, and the urge is to over-explain, over-text, and force warmth back into place. Sometimes the truest thing is a plain admission, without pretending everything is fine.
ramacharitamanas::2230.insight: It shifts the reader from possessive attachment to honest acceptance of what has already been set in motion.

ramacharitamanas::2231.verse_sanskrit: देव पितर सब तुम्हहि गोसाईं। राखहुँ पलक नयन की नाईं॥ अवधि अंबु प्रिय परिजन मीना। तुम्ह करुनाकर धरम धुरीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2231.verse_hindi: हे गोसाईं! सब देव और पितर तुम्हारी वैसी ही रक्षा करें, जैसे पलकें आँखों की रक्षा करती हैं। तुम्हारे वनवास की अवधि (चौदह वर्ष) जल है, प्रियजन और कुटुम्बी मछली हैं। तुम दया की खान और धर्म की धुरी को धारण करने वाले हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2231.english_translation: May all the devas and ancestors protect you, O lord, as eyelids protect the eyes. Your exile is water; your loved ones and kin are fish in it. You are a mine of compassion and the bearer of dharma.
ramacharitamanas::2231.translation_literal: देव (devas) / पितर (ancestors) / सब (all) / तुम्हहि (you) / गोसाईं (lord) / राखहुँ (may protect) / पलक (eyelids) / नयन (eyes) / की नाईं (like)॥ / अवधि (period) / अंबु (water) / प्रिय (loved) / परिजन (kin) / मीना (fish) / तुम्ह (you) / करुनाकर (mine of compassion) / धरम (dharma) / धुरीना (pillar-bearer) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2231.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2231.essence: Love blesses even the exile it cannot stop.
ramacharitamanas::2231.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi blesses Ram and says his exile is like water, with his loved ones as fish in it. She calls him compassionate and steadfast in dharma.
ramacharitamanas::2231.simple_insight: Even in sorrow, love speaks in images of protection and care.
ramacharitamanas::2231.detailed_meaning: Kaikeyi is speaking to Ram after the exile has been set in motion. She blesses him, compares his fourteen-year exile to a watery world, and calls him the bearer of dharma. Her words carry both pain and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2231.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love pack a bag for a long separation, and the room feels too small to hold it. What you offer is not logic, but blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2231.insight: It shifts attention from the loss itself to the care that still surrounds it.

ramacharitamanas::2232.verse_sanskrit: अस बिचारि सोइ करहु उपाई। सबहि जिअत जेहिं भेंटहु आई॥ जाहु सुखेन बनहि बलि जाऊँ। करि अनाथ जन परिजन गाऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2232.verse_hindi: ऐसा विचारकर वही उपाय करना, जिसमें सबके जीते जी तुम आ मिलो। मैं बलिहारी जाती हूँ, तुम सेवकों, परिवार वालों और नगर भर को अनाथ करके सुखपूर्वक वन को जाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2232.english_translation: Think of the way that lets everyone meet while still alive. I bless you: go peacefully to the forest, leaving your servants, family, and city orphaned.
ramacharitamanas::2232.translation_literal: अस (thus) / बिचारि (having thought) / सोइ (that very) / करहु (do) / उपाई (measure, way) / सबहि (everyone) / जिअत (while living) / जेहिं (by which) / भेंटहु (you meet) / आई (coming) ॥ / जाहु (go) / सुखेन (peacefully) / बनहि (to the forest) / बलि जाऊँ (I offer myself, I am devoted) / करि (making) / अनाथ (orphaned) / जन (people) / परिजन (relatives, attendants) / गाऊँ (city) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2232.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2232.essence: Love can release what it cannot keep.
ramacharitamanas::2232.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi asks Ram to choose the path where everyone can meet while still alive, then sends him to the forest with painful resignation.
ramacharitamanas::2232.simple_insight: Sometimes love speaks through loss, not possession.
ramacharitamanas::2232.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi faces the cost of her own demand. She tells Ram to choose the course that allows a living reunion, then urges him to go to the forest, leaving the household and city bereft. The verse carries the ache of separation before the full grief arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2232.modern_relevance: You finally tell someone to take the job abroad, even though the house will feel empty without them. Love can bless the departure and still feel the loss.
ramacharitamanas::2232.insight: It shifts the mind from clinging to closeness toward allowing the harder path that must unfold.

ramacharitamanas::2233.verse_sanskrit: सब कर आजु सुकृत फल बीता। भयउ कराल कालु बिपरीता॥ बहुबिधि बिलपि चरन लपटानी। परम अभागिनि आपुहि जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2233.verse_hindi: आज सबके पुण्यों का फल पूरा हो गया। कठिन काल हमारे विपरीत हो गया। (इस प्रकार) बहुत विलाप करके और अपने को परम अभागिनी जानकर माता श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में लिपट गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2233.english_translation: Today the fruit of everyone's merit has been exhausted. Hard time has turned against us. After crying in many ways and seeing herself as most unfortunate, she clung to Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::2233.translation_literal: सब (all) / कर (of all) / आजु (today) / सुकृत (merit) / फल (fruit) / बीता (spent) / भयउ (became) / कराल (fierce) / कालु (time) / बिपरीता (opposite) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / बिलपि (lamenting) / चरन (feet) / लपटानी (clung) / परम (supreme) / अभागिनि (unfortunate woman) / आपुहि (herself) / जानी (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::2233.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2233.essence: Regret strips away excuses and leaves only remorse.
ramacharitamanas::2233.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi feels that all good fortune has ended and disaster has turned against the family. In grief and self-blame, she clings to Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::2233.simple_insight: Grief can make a person see only loss and their own fault.
ramacharitamanas::2233.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace has already been shattered by Kaikeyi's demand and Dasharath's collapse. Now Kaikeyi looks at the ruin around her, weeps, and throws herself at Ram's feet, calling herself the most unfortunate one.
ramacharitamanas::2233.modern_relevance: A message arrives and you instantly know your words, not the event, helped cause the damage. The stomach drops. Before any explanation, there is only regret and the need to face it.
ramacharitamanas::2233.insight: It turns regret into self-recognition: the mind stops defending itself and sees the cost of its own choices.

ramacharitamanas::2234.verse_sanskrit: दारुन दुसह दाहु उर ब्यापा। बरनि न जाहिं बिलाप कलापा॥ राम उठाइ मातु उर लाई। कहि मृदु बचन बहुरि समुझाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2234.verse_hindi: हृदय में भयानक दुःसह संताप छा गया। उस समय के बहुविध विलाप का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने माता को उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया और फिर कोमल वचन कहकर उन्हें समझाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2234.english_translation: A terrible, unbearable grief seized the heart. No one could describe the many cries of mourning. Ram lifted his mother into his arms and gently comforted her with tender words.
ramacharitamanas::2234.translation_literal: दारुन (terrible) / दुसह (unbearable) / दाहु (burning pain) / उर (heart) / ब्यापा (spread) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाहिं (can go) / बिलाप (lamentation) / कलापा (groups, kinds) / राम (Ram) / उठाइ (lifting) / मातु (mother) / उर (to chest) / लाई (brought) / कहि (speaking) / मृदु (soft, gentle) / बचन (words) / बहुरि (again) / समुझाई (consoled, explained)
ramacharitamanas::2234.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2234.simple_meaning: Grief fills the heart so completely that words fail. Ram responds by holding his mother close and soothing her with gentle speech.
ramacharitamanas::2234.simple_insight: In the middle of loss, comfort can begin with simple presence.
ramacharitamanas::2234.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has died, and the palace is drowning in grief. Kaushalya’s sorrow becomes almost unbearable, too deep for speech to capture. In that raw moment, Ram does not stand apart; he lifts his mother close and steadies her with tender words.
ramacharitamanas::2234.modern_relevance: When a family member breaks down in the kitchen after bad news, you do not need a perfect speech. Sometimes the healing starts when you hold them, stay near, and speak softly.
ramacharitamanas::2234.insight: It teaches you to meet grief with physical closeness and calm words instead of distance or analysis.

ramacharitamanas::2235.verse_sanskrit: समाचार तेहि समय सुनि सीय उठी अकुलाइ। जाइ सासु पद कमल जुग बंदि बैठि सिरु नाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2235.verse_hindi: उसी समय यह समाचार सुनकर सीताजी अकुला उठीं और सास के पास जाकर उनके दोनों चरणकमलों की वंदना कर सिर नीचा करके बैठ गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2235.english_translation: Hearing the news at that moment, Sita was overcome with anxiety. She went to her mother-in-law, bowed to her lotus feet, and sat with her head lowered.
ramacharitamanas::2235.translation_literal: समाचार (news) / तेहि समय (at that time) / सुनि (hearing) / सीय (Sita) / उठी (rose) / अकुलाइ (in distress) / जाइ (going) / सासु (mother-in-law) / पद कमल जुग (pair of lotus-feet) / बंदि (bowing) / बैठि (sat) / सिरु नाइ (lowering the head)
ramacharitamanas::2235.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2235.simple_meaning: Hearing the news, Sita became distressed and immediately went to her mother-in-law, bowed respectfully, and sat down with her head lowered.
ramacharitamanas::2235.simple_insight: Even in shock, respect and humility can still guide the next move.
ramacharitamanas::2235.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace is already drowning in grief. Hearing the news, Sita rises in alarm, goes straight to her mother-in-law, bows to her feet, and sits silently. The verse shows her composed reverence inside a moment of panic.
ramacharitamanas::2235.modern_relevance: You get a message that shakes you, but you still walk into the room, greet the elder properly, and hold yourself together before speaking.
ramacharitamanas::2235.insight: It teaches grace under distress: respond first with respect, not impulse.

ramacharitamanas::2236.verse_sanskrit: दीन्हि असीस सासु मृदु बानी। अति सुकुमारि देखि अकुलानी॥ बैठि नमित मुख सोचति सीता। रूप रासि पति प्रेम पुनीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2236.verse_hindi: सास ने कोमल वाणी से आशीर्वाद दिया। वे सीताजी को अत्यन्त सुकुमारी देखकर व्याकुल हो उठीं। रूप की राशि और पति के साथ पवित्र प्रेम करने वाली सीताजी नीचा मुख किए बैठी सोच रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2236.english_translation: Sita's mother-in-law gave her a gentle blessing. Seeing the very delicate Sita, she became distressed. Sita sat with her face lowered, thinking, a treasure of beauty and pure love for her husband.
ramacharitamanas::2236.translation_literal: दीन्हि (gave) / असीस (blessing) / सासु (mother-in-law) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (speech) / अति (very) / सुकुमारि (delicate) / देखि (seeing) / अकुलानी (distressed)॥ / बैठि (sitting) / नमित (lowered) / मुख (face) / सोचति (thinking) / सीता (Sita) / रूप (beauty) / रासि (treasure) / पति (husband) / प्रेम (love) / पुनीता (pure)॥
ramacharitamanas::2236.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2236.essence: Love can sit quietly even when the world is breaking.
ramacharitamanas::2236.simple_meaning: Sita's mother-in-law blesses her gently, but worries when she sees how delicate Sita is. Sita sits quietly, bowed down, thinking of her pure love for her husband.
ramacharitamanas::2236.simple_insight: Tenderness and worry can coexist in the same room.
ramacharitamanas::2236.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace is already trembling with the news of Ram's exile. Sita has just come to her mother-in-law, and the older woman blesses her with affection while feeling anxious at her fragility. Sita sits silently, absorbed in her love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2236.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone you love after bad news, trying to stay composed while your concern shows in every glance. Care and fear often speak at once.
ramacharitamanas::2236.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic action to the quiet emotional weight carried in a family.

ramacharitamanas::2237.verse_sanskrit: चलन चहत बन जीवननाथू। केहि सुकृती सन होइहि साथू॥ की तनु प्रान कि केवल प्राना। बिधि करतबु कछु जाइ न जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2237.verse_hindi: जीवननाथ (प्राणनाथ) वन को चलना चाहते हैं। देखें किस पुण्यवान से उनका साथ होगा- शरीर और प्राण दोनों साथ जाएँगे या केवल प्राण ही से इनका साथ होगा? विधाता की करनी कुछ जानी नहीं जाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2237.english_translation: The lord of my life wants to go to the forest. Who will be fortunate enough to go with him? Will both body and breath go together, or only breath? No one can know the workings of fate.
ramacharitamanas::2237.translation_literal: चलन (to go) / चहत (wants) / बन (forest) / जीवननाथू (lord of life) / केहि (with whom) / सुकृती (fortunate one) / सन (with) / होइहि (will be) / साथू (companion) / की (whether) / तनु (body) / प्रान (life-breath) / कि (or) / केवल (only) / प्राना (breaths) / बिधि (fate) / करतबु (workings) / कछु (something) / जाइ (goes) / न (not) / जाना (known)
ramacharitamanas::2237.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2237.essence: Separation turns even breath into a question.
ramacharitamanas::2237.simple_meaning: Sita wonders who will accompany Ram into exile and whether she will go with both body and breath, or only her breath if she cannot follow.
ramacharitamanas::2237.simple_insight: Love makes separation feel like a question of survival, not comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2237.detailed_meaning: Sita has just bowed to Kaushalya and received her blessing. Now she sits trembling, hearing that Ram is leaving for the forest. Her heart turns to one question: will she go with him, or will fate leave her behind?
ramacharitamanas::2237.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love pack for a move you did not choose. Your mind races ahead of the goodbye, trying to measure how much of you can go with them.
ramacharitamanas::2237.insight: It shifts attention from logistics to the ache of devotion under uncertainty.

ramacharitamanas::2238.verse_sanskrit: चारु चरन नख लेखति धरनी। नूपुर मुखर मधुर कबि बरनी॥ मनहुँ प्रेम बस बिनती करहीं। हमहि सीय पद जनि परिहरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2238.verse_hindi: सीताजी अपने सुंदर चरणों के नखों से धरती कुरेद रही हैं। ऐसा करते समय नूपुरों का जो मधुर शब्द हो रहा है, कवि उसका इस प्रकार वर्णन करते हैं कि मानो प्रेम के वश होकर नूपुर यह विनती कर रहे हैं कि सीताजी के चरण कभी हमारा त्याग न करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2238.english_translation: Sita scratches the earth with her lovely toenails. The poet says the anklets sound sweet, as if moved by love they are pleading, “Do not leave Sita’s feet.”
ramacharitamanas::2238.translation_literal: चारु (beautiful) / चरन (feet) / नख (nails) / लेखति (scratches, traces) / धरनी (earth) / नूपुर (anklets) / मुखर (melodious) / मधुर (sweet) / कबि (poet) / बरनी (described)॥ / मनहुँ (as if) / प्रेम (love) / बस (under the power) / बिनती (request, plea) / करहीं (they do)॥ / हमहि (us) / सीय (Sita) / पद (feet) / जनि (do not) / परिहरहीं (abandon, leave) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2238.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2238.essence: Love makes even footsteps feel unwilling to part.
ramacharitamanas::2238.simple_meaning: Sita stands so delicately that even her anklets seem to beg not to be left behind by her feet.
ramacharitamanas::2238.simple_insight: Tender love can make even small details feel alive and pleading.
ramacharitamanas::2238.detailed_meaning: Sita is preparing to leave Ayodhya for the forest with Ram. The poet lingers on her delicate feet and the soft sound of her anklets, turning a simple movement into a moment of aching tenderness before exile begins.
ramacharitamanas::2238.modern_relevance: You pack a bag before a hard goodbye and notice the smallest things: a shoe by the door, a bracelet on the table. Ordinary objects suddenly feel like they are asking not to be left behind.
ramacharitamanas::2238.insight: It teaches the mind to notice how love charges even ordinary movement with grief and devotion.

ramacharitamanas::2239.verse_sanskrit: मंजु बिलोचन मोचति बारी। बोली देखि राम महतारी॥ तात सुनहु सिय अति सुकुमारी। सास ससुर परिजनहि पिआरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2239.verse_hindi: सीताजी सुंदर नेत्रों से जल बहा रही हैं। उनकी यह दशा देखकर श्री रामजी की माता कौसल्याजी बोलीं- हे तात! सुनो, सीता अत्यन्त ही सुकुमारी हैं तथा सास, ससुर और कुटुम्बी सभी को प्यारी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2239.english_translation: Sita's beautiful eyes spill tears. Seeing this, Rama's mother Kaushalya said, “Listen, dear child: Sita is extremely delicate and beloved by her parents-in-law and family.”
ramacharitamanas::2239.translation_literal: मंजु (beautiful) / बिलोचन (eyes) / मोचति (releases) / बारी (water, tears) / बोली (spoke) / देखि (seeing) / राम (Rama) / महतारी (mother) / तात (dear child) / सुनहु (listen) / सिय (Sita) / अति (very) / सुकुमारी (delicate) / सास (mother-in-law) / ससुर (father-in-law) / परिजनहि (family members) / पिआरी (beloved)
ramacharitamanas::2239.speaker: Kaushalya
ramacharitamanas::2239.simple_meaning: Sita is weeping softly, and Kaushalya comforts her by praising her gentle nature and her place in the family.
ramacharitamanas::2239.simple_insight: Tenderness is seen and answered with tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::2239.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the family stands at the edge of separation. Sita is crying, and Kaushalya, Rama's mother, responds with warmth rather than distance. She reminds everyone that Sita is delicate and deeply loved in the household.
ramacharitamanas::2239.modern_relevance: You see someone trying not to cry at a family gathering, and the room goes quiet. One gentle sentence can hold them together better than advice ever could.
ramacharitamanas::2239.insight: It shifts attention from the tears themselves to the care that meets them.

ramacharitamanas::2240.verse_sanskrit: पिता जनक भूपाल मनि ससुर भानुकुल भानु। पति रबिकुल कैरव बिपिन बिधु गुन रूप निधानु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2240.verse_hindi: इनके पिता जनकजी राजाओं के शिरोमणि हैं, ससुर सूर्यकुल के सूर्य हैं और पति सूर्यकुल रूपी कुमुदवन को खिलाने वाले चन्द्रमा तथा गुण और रूप के भंडार हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2240.english_translation: Janaka, the father, is the jewel among kings; the father-in-law is the sun of the solar line; the husband is the moon that makes the lotus grove of the solar line bloom, a storehouse of virtues and beauty.
ramacharitamanas::2240.translation_literal: पिता (father) / जनक (Janaka) / भूपाल (king) / मनि (jewel) / ससुर (father-in-law) / भानुकुल (solar line) / भानु (sun) / पति (husband) / रबिकुल (solar line) / कैरव (white lotus) / बिपिन (forest/grove) / बिधु (moon) / गुन (virtues) / रूप (beauty) / निधानु (storehouse)
ramacharitamanas::2240.speaker: Kaushalya
ramacharitamanas::2240.essence: Honor surrounds the one who marries into a noble home.
ramacharitamanas::2240.simple_meaning: Kaushalya praises Janak, his lineage, and Ram as the perfect husband, full of virtues and beauty.
ramacharitamanas::2240.simple_insight: Love speaks by seeing the beloved’s whole world as blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2240.detailed_meaning: Kaushalya is speaking to Sita in Ayodhyakand, trying to comfort her as she faces exile. She praises Janak, the royal family, and Ram’s noble qualities, showing that Sita has come from honor and entered an even greater home.
ramacharitamanas::2240.modern_relevance: You meet your partner’s parents for the first time and feel the quiet pressure to belong. A kind elder names the family with respect, and the room softens. Recognition can be its own blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2240.insight: It shifts attention from loss to the dignity already surrounding the relationship.

ramacharitamanas::2241.verse_sanskrit: मैं पुनि पुत्रबधू प्रिय पाई। रूप रासि गुन सील सुहाई॥ नयन पुतरि करि प्रीति बढ़ाई। राखेउँ प्रान जानकिहिं लाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2241.verse_hindi: फिर मैंने रूप की राशि, सुंदर गुण और शीलवाली प्यारी पुत्रवधू पाई है। मैंने इन (जानकी) को आँखों की पुतली बनाकर इनसे प्रेम बढ़ाया है और अपने प्राण इनमें लगा रखे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2241.english_translation: I have also gained a beloved daughter-in-law, full of beauty, virtues, and gentle character. I have cherished Janaki like the pupil of my eye and placed my life in her.
ramacharitamanas::2241.translation_literal: मैं (I) / पुनि (also) / पुत्रबधू (daughter-in-law) / प्रिय (beloved) / पाई (have obtained) / रूप (beauty) / रासि (heap, abundance) / गुन (virtues) / सील (gentle character) / सुहाई (lovely) / नयन (eye) / पुतरि (pupil) / करि (as) / प्रीति (love) / बढ़ाई (increased) / राखेउँ (I have kept) / प्रान (life) / जानकिहिं (in Janaki) / लाई (placed)
ramacharitamanas::2241.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::2241.essence: Love makes a daughter-in-law feel like the heart’s own child.
ramacharitamanas::2241.simple_meaning: Kausalya says she has gained a beloved daughter-in-law, and she has loved Janaki like the pupil of her eye, placing her whole heart in her.
ramacharitamanas::2241.simple_insight: Deep affection makes someone feel like family before they even speak.
ramacharitamanas::2241.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kausalya sees Sita weeping and speaks tenderly to her. She praises Janaki as a beautiful, virtuous daughter-in-law and reveals how completely she has already embraced her as her own, heightening the grief of the exile scene.
ramacharitamanas::2241.modern_relevance: You meet your partner’s mother and she instantly treats you like one of her own. That kind of welcome can soften even the hardest family rupture.
ramacharitamanas::2241.insight: It shifts attention from formal family roles to the felt reality of belonging and care.

ramacharitamanas::2242.verse_sanskrit: कलपबेलि जिमि बहुबिधि लाली। सींचि सनेह सलिल प्रतिपाली॥ फूलत फलत भयउ बिधि बामा। जानि न जाइ काह परिनामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2242.verse_hindi: इन्हें कल्पलता के समान मैंने बहुत तरह से बड़े लाड़-चाव के साथ स्नेह रूपी जल से सींचकर पाला है। अब इस लता के फूलने-फलने के समय विधाता वाम हो गए। कुछ जाना नहीं जाता कि इसका क्या परिणाम होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2242.english_translation: I have nurtured her like a wish-fulfilling vine with many kinds of affection and care. Now, just as she is flowering and fruiting, fate has turned against me. I cannot know what will happen next.
ramacharitamanas::2242.translation_literal: कलपबेलि (wish-fulfilling vine) / जिमि (like) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / लाली (fondly nurtured) / सींचि (watering) / सनेह (affection) / सलिल (water) / प्रतिपाली (raised, protected) / फूलत (flowering) / फलत (fruiting) / भयउ (became) / बिधि (fate) / बामा (adverse, crooked) / जानि (knowing) / न जाइ (cannot be known) / काह (what) / परिनामा (result, outcome)
ramacharitamanas::2242.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2242.simple_meaning: Dasharath says he has raised Sita with great love, like a precious vine. Now that her life is reaching fullness, he fears something has gone wrong and cannot see what comes next.
ramacharitamanas::2242.simple_insight: Love can make loss feel sharper, because you have cared so deeply for what is now uncertain.
ramacharitamanas::2242.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath looks back on how gently he and Kaikeyi have cherished Sita, almost like a treasured plant. Just as her life seems ready to bloom, the king feels an ominous turn and cannot see what fate will bring.
ramacharitamanas::2242.modern_relevance: You watch someone you’ve protected for years step into a new phase of life, and your chest tightens. Pride and fear arrive together, because love always includes the risk of not knowing.
ramacharitamanas::2242.insight: It shifts attention from possession to vulnerability: what is deeply loved is never fully controllable.

ramacharitamanas::2243.verse_sanskrit: पलँग पीठ तजि गोद हिंडोरा। सियँ न दीन्ह पगु अवनि कठोरा॥ जिअनमूरि जिमि जोगवत रहउँ। दीप बाति नहिं टारन कहऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2243.verse_hindi: सीता ने पर्यंकपृष्ठ (पलंग के ऊपर), गोद और हिंडोले को छोड़कर कठोर पृथ्वी पर कभी पैर नहीं रखा। मैं सदा संजीवनी जड़ी के समान (सावधानी से) इनकी रखवाली करती रही हूँ। कभी दीपक की बत्ती हटाने को भी नहीं कहती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2243.english_translation: Sita never set her foot on the hard earth, even leaving the bed, seat, lap, and swing. I cared for her like a life-saving herb, never even asking that the lamp’s wick be moved.
ramacharitamanas::2243.translation_literal: पलँग (bed) / पीठ (seat/backrest) / तजि (leaving) / गोद (lap) / हिंडोरा (swing) / सियँ (for Sita) / न दीन्ह (did not give) / पगु (foot) / अवनि (earth) / कठोरा (hard) / जिअनमूरि (life-saving herb) / जिमि (like) / जोगवत (carefully guarding) / रहउँ (I kept) / दीप (lamp) / बाति (wick) / नहिं (not) / टारन (to move away) / कहऊँ (I would say)
ramacharitamanas::2243.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2243.essence: Tender care makes exile feel even harsher.
ramacharitamanas::2243.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi says Sita was raised in great comfort and care, never even touching the hard ground, and was watched over with extreme tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::2243.simple_insight: Care can be so devoted that even small discomfort feels unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2243.detailed_meaning: Kaikeyi is speaking in Ayodhyakand, recalling how tenderly she once protected Sita in the palace. The memory heightens the coming separation: the beloved daughter-in-law who never touched rough ground is now about to leave for the forest.
ramacharitamanas::2243.modern_relevance: You tuck a child into bed, adjust the blanket, and quietly check the lamp before leaving the room. That instinct to protect without being asked is what this verse remembers.
ramacharitamanas::2243.insight: It highlights the contrast between royal comfort and the harsh exile that follows.

ramacharitamanas::2244.verse_sanskrit: सोइ सिय चलन चहति बन साथा। आयसु काह होइ रघुनाथा॥ चंद किरन रस रसिक चकोरी। रबि रुखनयन सकइ किमि जोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2244.verse_hindi: वही सीता अब तुम्हारे साथ वन चलना चाहती है। हे रघुनाथ! उसे क्या आज्ञा होती है? चन्द्रमा की किरणों का रस (अमृत) चाहने वाली चकोरी सूर्य की ओर आँख किस तरह मिला सकती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2244.english_translation: Sita now wants to go to the forest with you. O Raghunath, what command would she need? How can a chakor, longing for moonlight, turn its eyes toward the sun?
ramacharitamanas::2244.translation_literal: सोइ (that very) / सिय (Sita) / चलन (to go) / चहति (wants) / बन (forest) / साथा (with) / आयसु (command) / काह (what) / होइ (would be) / रघुनाथा (O Raghunath) / चंद (moon) / किरन (rays) / रस (nectar) / रसिक (delighting in) / चकोरी (chakor bird) / रबि (sun) / रुखनयन (toward the sun, with eyes turned) / सकइ (can) / किमि (how) / जोरी (join)
ramacharitamanas::2244.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2244.essence: Devotion needs no command; it follows love naturally.
ramacharitamanas::2244.simple_meaning: Sita wants to go to the forest with Ram, and no command is needed for her. Her love naturally turns toward him, just as a chakor turns toward the moon, not the sun.
ramacharitamanas::2244.simple_insight: Love does not need pressure. It moves toward its own source on its own.
ramacharitamanas::2244.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the exile is tearing the family apart. Sita is ready to leave with Ram, and the poet says her devotion needs no order. Her longing naturally follows him, the way a bird seeks the moon.
ramacharitamanas::2244.modern_relevance: Someone you love is moving through a hard season, and you do not ask, “Should I come?” You already know where your heart belongs.
ramacharitamanas::2244.insight: It shifts the mind from obligation to natural devotion: true love follows without being ordered.

ramacharitamanas::2245.verse_sanskrit: करि केहरि निसिचर चरहिं दुष्ट जंतु बन भूरि। बिष बाटिकाँ कि सोह सुत सुभग सजीवनि मूरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2245.verse_hindi: हाथी, सिंह, राक्षस आदि अनेक दुष्ट जीव-जन्तु वन में विचरते रहते हैं। हे पुत्र! क्या विष की वाटिका में सुंदर संजीवनी बूटी शोभा पा सकती है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2245.english_translation: Elephants, lions, and wicked forest beings roam there in great numbers. Son, can a beautiful healing herb flourish in a garden of poison?
ramacharitamanas::2245.translation_literal: करि (elephants) / केहरि (lions) / निसिचर (night-roamers, demons) / चरहिं (roam) / दुष्ट (wicked) / जंतु (creatures) / बन (forest) / भूरि (in great number) / बिष (poison) / बाटिकाँ (in a garden) / कि (can) / सोह (shine, flourish) / सुत (son) / सुभग (beautiful) / सजीवनि (healing herb) / मूरि (plant, root)
ramacharitamanas::2245.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2245.essence: A tender life cannot bloom in a poisonous place.
ramacharitamanas::2245.simple_meaning: A harsh forest full of dangerous creatures is no place for something delicate and life-giving. The setting itself makes the point: this environment cannot support tender beauty.
ramacharitamanas::2245.simple_insight: Not every place can hold what is gentle. Some environments simply crush what is precious.
ramacharitamanas::2245.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the speaker is describing the forest where Sita would have to live with Ram and Lakshman. The woods are full of wild beasts and hostile forces, so the image of a healing herb in a poison garden shows how unsuitable that life would be for her.
ramacharitamanas::2245.modern_relevance: You try to keep a calm heart in a room where sarcasm, gossip, and cruelty are normal. The problem is not your effort — it is the climate around you.
ramacharitamanas::2245.insight: It shifts attention from blaming the fragile thing to recognizing the toxicity of the setting.

ramacharitamanas::2246.verse_sanskrit: बन हित कोल किरात किसोरी। रचीं बिरंचि बिषय सुख भोरी॥ पाहन कृमि जिमि कठिन सुभाऊ। तिन्हहि कलेसु न कानन काऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2246.verse_hindi: वन के लिए तो ब्रह्माजी ने विषय सुख को न जानने वाली कोल और भीलों की लड़कियों को रचा है, जिनका पत्थर के कीड़े जैसा कठोर स्वभाव है। उन्हें वन में कभी क्लेश नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2246.english_translation: For the forest, Brahma created the girls of the Kol and Kirat tribes, who know nothing of worldly pleasures. Their nature is hard like stone or a worm in stone, so the forest gives them no distress.
ramacharitamanas::2246.translation_literal: बन (forest) / हित (for the welfare) / कोल (Kol) / किरात (Kirat) / किसोरी (girls) / रचीं (were created) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / बिषय सुख (worldly pleasure) / भोरी (not knowing)॥ / पाहन (stone) / कृमि (worm) / जिमि (like) / कठिन (hard) / सुभाऊ (nature) / तिन्हहि (to them) / कलेसु (distress) / न (not) / कानन (forest) / काऊ (at all) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2246.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2246.essence: Hard places do not trouble the one shaped for them.
ramacharitamanas::2246.simple_meaning: Some people are naturally fit for forest life because they are not attached to comfort. Their hardiness means the forest does not trouble them.
ramacharitamanas::2246.simple_insight: Not everyone suffers the same way. What feels unbearable to one person can feel natural to another.
ramacharitamanas::2246.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram and Sita are being weighed against the hardships of exile. Tulsidas notes that some forest-born girls are made for that life, unlike Sita, whose delicate upbringing makes the exile painful. It is a supporting argument in the larger plea.
ramacharitamanas::2246.modern_relevance: A friend who grew up hiking rough trails moves through a monsoon trek with ease while you struggle for every step. The same place can be home to one person and hardship to another.
ramacharitamanas::2246.insight: It shifts judgment away from universal assumptions and toward the actual nature and capacity of each person.

ramacharitamanas::2247.verse_sanskrit: कै तापस तिय कानन जोगू। जिन्ह तप हेतु तजा सब भोगू॥ सिय बन बसिहि तात केहि भाँती। चित्रलिखित कपि देखि डेराती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2247.verse_hindi: अथवा तपस्वियों की स्त्रियाँ वन में रहने योग्य हैं, जिन्होंने तपस्या के लिए सब भोग तज दिए हैं। हे पुत्र! जो तसवीर के बंदर को देखकर डर जाती हैं, वे सीता वन में किस तरह रह सकेंगी? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2247.english_translation: Or are the wives of ascetics fit for the forest, having given up all pleasures for penance? O son, how could Sita live in the forest when she trembles at seeing a painted monkey?
ramacharitamanas::2247.translation_literal: कै (or) / तापस (ascetics) / तिय (wives) / कानन (forest) / जोगू (fit) / जिन्ह (who) / तप (austerity) / हेतु (for the sake of) / तजा (gave up) / सब (all) / भोगू (pleasures)॥ / सिय (Sita) / बन (forest) / बसिहि (will live) / तात (son) / केहि भाँती (how) / चित्रलिखित (painted) / कपि (monkey) / देखि (seeing) / डेराती (is frightened)॥
ramacharitamanas::2247.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2247.essence: Hardship fits only where the heart and habits can bear it.
ramacharitamanas::2247.simple_meaning: A forest is easier for people already used to austerity. Sita, who is delicate and frightened even by a painted monkey, would find forest life extremely hard.
ramacharitamanas::2247.simple_insight: Some lives are not prepared for hardship, and pretending otherwise only deepens the suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2247.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the discussion turns to Sita’s exile. The speaker argues from common sense: women of ascetics can endure the forest because they have already renounced comfort, but Sita has lived in royal ease and is easily startled. The point is to show how severe the coming exile will be.
ramacharitamanas::2247.modern_relevance: You ask someone raised in comfort to sleep on a bare floor, eat little, and face constant uncertainty. The body may comply for a day, but the shock is real.
ramacharitamanas::2247.insight: It shifts the mind from romanticizing hardship to seeing the actual human cost of forcing it on someone unprepared.

ramacharitamanas::2248.verse_sanskrit: सुरसर सुभग बनज बन चारी। डाबर जोगु कि हंसकुमारी॥ अस बिचारि जस आयसु होई। मैं सिख देउँ जानकिहि सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2248.verse_hindi: देवसरोवर के कमल वन में विचरण करने वाली हंसिनी क्या गड़ैयों (तलैयों) में रहने के योग्य है? ऐसा विचार कर जैसी तुम्हारी आज्ञा हो, मैं जानकी को वैसी ही शिक्षा दूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2248.english_translation: A swan belongs among lotus-filled lakes, not in a muddy pond. Thinking this over, I will teach Janaki according to your wish.
ramacharitamanas::2248.translation_literal: सुरसर (of the heavenly lake) / सुभग (beautiful) / बनज (lotus) / बन (forest) / चारी (one who moves around) / डाबर (muddy pond) / जोगु (fit) / कि (or) / हंसकुमारी (swan-maiden) / अस (thus) / बिचारि (thinking) / जस (as) / आयसु (command) / होई (is) / मैं (I) / सिख (instruction) / देउँ (give) / जानकिहि (to Janaki) / सोई (that same)
ramacharitamanas::2248.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2248.essence: What is fitting preserves dignity; what is harsh must not be mistaken for care.
ramacharitamanas::2248.simple_meaning: A noble woman belongs in a fitting, beautiful place, not in a harsh one. So the speaker says he will teach Sita according to what is appropriate.
ramacharitamanas::2248.simple_insight: Right care means matching the person to the setting, not forcing them into what is merely convenient.
ramacharitamanas::2248.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the discussion turns to Sita’s life in exile. The speaker compares her to a swan that belongs among lotus lakes, not muddy ponds, and says he will guide her according to what is proper and loving.
ramacharitamanas::2248.modern_relevance: Someone asks you to adapt to a cramped, stressful situation that clearly does not suit you. You realize kindness is not forcing endurance; it is choosing what preserves dignity and well-being.
ramacharitamanas::2248.insight: It shifts attention from bare survival to fitting care and appropriate conditions.

ramacharitamanas::2249.verse_sanskrit: जौं सिय भवन रहै कह अंबा। मोहि कहँ होइ बहुत अवलंबा॥ सुनि रघुबीर मातु प्रिय बानी। सील सनेह सुधाँ जनु सानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2249.verse_hindi: माता कहती हैं- यदि सीता घर में रहें तो मुझको बहुत सहारा हो जाए। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने माता की प्रिय वाणी सुनकर, जो मानो शील और स्नेह रूपी अमृत से सनी हुई थी, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2249.english_translation: Mother said, "If Sita stays in the house, she will be a great support to me." Hearing his mother's dear words, Raghubir, as if soaked in the nectar of character and affection, ...
ramacharitamanas::2249.translation_literal: जौं (if) / सिय (Sita) / भवन (house) / रहै (stays) / कह (said) / अंबा (mother) / मोहि (to me) / कहँ (for) / होइ (becomes) / बहुत (much) / अवलंबा (support) ॥ / सुनि (hearing) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / मातु (mother's) / प्रिय (dear) / बानी (words) / सील (character) / सनेह (affection) / सुधाँ (nectar) / जनु (as if) / सानी (mixed/soaked) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2249.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2249.essence: Tender words can carry a hidden turning point.
ramacharitamanas::2249.simple_meaning: Mother says Sita would be a great comfort if she stayed at home. Ram hears this loving, gentle request, which feels soaked in kindness and affection.
ramacharitamanas::2249.simple_insight: A loving request can soften even a painful moment.
ramacharitamanas::2249.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the family is already under strain from exile. Mother speaks tenderly, saying Sita at home would support her. Ram hears the request with warmth, not resistance. The verse prepares the move from affection to the harder task of sending Sita away.
ramacharitamanas::2249.modern_relevance: A parent asks for help in a voice too gentle to refuse. You hear the need beneath the words, even when the request will cost you something.
ramacharitamanas::2249.insight: It shifts attention from the literal request to the emotional weight behind it.

ramacharitamanas::2250.verse_sanskrit: कहि प्रिय बचन बिबेकमय कीन्हि मातु परितोष। लगे प्रबोधन जानकिहि प्रगटि बिपिन गुन दोष ॥
ramacharitamanas::2250.verse_hindi: विवेकमय प्रिय वचन कहकर माता को संतुष्ट किया। फिर वन के गुण-दोष प्रकट करके वे जानकीजी को समझाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2250.english_translation: He spoke loving, wise words and satisfied his mother. Then he began instructing Janaki, openly describing the merits and faults of forest life.
ramacharitamanas::2250.translation_literal: कहि (saying) / प्रिय (loving) / बचन (words) / बिबेकमय (full of discernment) / कीन्हि (did) / मातु (mother) / परितोष (satisfaction) । / लगे (began) / प्रबोधन (instruction) / जानकिहि (to Janaki) / प्रगटि (openly) / बिपिन (forest) / गुन (virtues) / दोष (faults) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2250.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2250.essence: Kind words can carry hard truth without losing tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::2250.simple_meaning: Ram reassures his mother with thoughtful words, then gently explains to Sita what forest life will be like.
ramacharitamanas::2250.simple_insight: Care can be honest. Comfort does not require hiding the hard parts.
ramacharitamanas::2250.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram stands between his grieving mother and Sita as exile becomes real. He soothes Kaushalya first, then turns to Janaki and speaks plainly about the forest ahead. The moment matters because love must now carry truth.
ramacharitamanas::2250.modern_relevance: You are trying to calm a parent while also telling your partner the move will be hard. Ram shows how to be tender without being vague.
ramacharitamanas::2250.insight: It teaches you to speak with kindness and clarity when others need both reassurance and reality.

ramacharitamanas::2251.verse_sanskrit: मातु समीप कहत सकुचाहीं। बोले समउ समुझि मन माहीं॥ राजकुमारि सिखावनु सुनहू। आन भाँति जियँ जनि कछु गुनहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2251.verse_hindi: माता के सामने सीताजी से कुछ कहने में सकुचाते हैं। पर मन में यह समझकर कि यह समय ऐसा ही है, वे बोले- हे राजकुमारी! मेरी सिखावन सुनो। मन में कुछ दूसरी तरह न समझ लेना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2251.english_translation: Near his mother, he hesitated to speak. Then, understanding the moment in his heart, he said, “Princess, listen to my counsel. Do not take my words in any other way.”
ramacharitamanas::2251.translation_literal: मातु समीप (near the mother) / कहत (speaking) / सकुचाहीं (they hesitate) / बोले (spoke) / समउ (the time) / समुझि (understanding) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / राजकुमारि (princess) / सिखावनु (instruction) / सुनहू (listen) / आन भाँति (in another way) / जियँ (in the heart) / जनि (do not) / कछु (anything) / गुनहू (take/understand)
ramacharitamanas::2251.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2251.essence: Hard truth can be delivered without hardening the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2251.simple_meaning: Ram gently prepares Sita for the hard truth he must give her. He speaks carefully, so she does not misunderstand his counsel.
ramacharitamanas::2251.simple_insight: Even painful truth can be spoken with tenderness and timing.
ramacharitamanas::2251.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is trying to explain the coming separation to Sita while Mother Kaushalya stands nearby. He feels hesitation, then chooses his words carefully, because this moment requires both honesty and compassion.
ramacharitamanas::2251.modern_relevance: You know the conversation will hurt, but silence would hurt more. So you choose your words carefully, with respect, before the room hardens.
ramacharitamanas::2251.insight: It teaches you to speak difficult truth with tact, not bluntness.

ramacharitamanas::2252.verse_sanskrit: आपन मोर नीक जौं चहहू। बचनु हमार मानि गृह रहहू॥ आयसु मोर सासु सेवकाई। सब बिधि भामिनि भवन भलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2252.verse_hindi: जो अपना और मेरा भला चाहती हो, तो मेरा वचन मानकर घर रहो। हे भामिनी! मेरी आज्ञा का पालन होगा, सास की सेवा बन पड़ेगी। घर रहने में सभी प्रकार से भलाई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2252.english_translation: If you want what is best for both of us, obey my word and stay in the house. O gentle one, following my command will make service to the mother-in-law possible in every way, and staying at home is best in all respects.
ramacharitamanas::2252.translation_literal: आपन (one's own) / मोर (my) / नीक (good) / जौं (if) / चहहू (you want) / बचनु (word) / हमार (my) / मानि (having obeyed) / गृह (house) / रहहू (stay) ॥ / आयसु (command) / मोर (my) / सासु (mother-in-law) / सेवकाई (service) / सब बिधि (in every way) / भामिनि (gentle woman) / भवन (house) / भलाई (welfare) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2252.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2252.essence: True welfare can begin with obeying what preserves harmony.
ramacharitamanas::2252.simple_meaning: Ram tells Sita that staying in the house and obeying him will bring the best outcome for everyone, including service to her elders.
ramacharitamanas::2252.simple_insight: Love sometimes asks for restraint, not display.
ramacharitamanas::2252.detailed_meaning: In the exile conversation, Ram is gently instructing Sita before sending her back toward the house and family duties. He frames obedience and domestic service as the right path for her welfare, turning a painful separation into a lesson in dharma and care.
ramacharitamanas::2252.modern_relevance: You want to leave the argument, send the text, and prove your point. But sometimes the wiser move is to stay, listen, and do the unglamorous work of keeping the home steady.
ramacharitamanas::2252.insight: It shifts the mind from personal impulse to responsible restraint and care for family order.

ramacharitamanas::2253.verse_sanskrit: एहि ते अधिक धरमु नहिं दूजा। सादर सासु ससुर पद पूजा॥ जब जब मातु करिहि सुधि मोरी। होइहि प्रेम बिकल मति भोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2253.verse_hindi: आदरपूर्वक सास-ससुर के चरणों की पूजा (सेवा) करने से बढ़कर दूसरा कोई धर्म नहीं है। जब-जब माता मुझे याद करेंगी और प्रेम से व्याकुल होने के कारण उनकी बुद्धि भोली हो जाएगी (वे अपने-आपको भूल जाएँगी) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2253.english_translation: No duty is greater than this: reverently serve the feet of your parents-in-law. Whenever your mother remembers me, she will be overwhelmed with love and lose herself in tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::2253.translation_literal: एहि ते (than this) / अधिक (greater) / धरमु (duty) / नहिं (not) / दूजा (another) / सादर (with reverence) / सासु (mother-in-law) / ससुर (father-in-law) / पद (feet) / पूजा (worship/service) ॥ / जब जब (whenever) / मातु (mother) / करिहि (will do) / सुधि (remembrance) / मोरी (of me) / होइहि (will become) / प्रेम (love) / बिकल (overwhelmed) / मति (mind) / भोरी (naive/forgetful) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2253.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2253.essence: Reverent service to elders is the highest duty.
ramacharitamanas::2253.simple_meaning: Respectful service to one's parents-in-law is presented as the highest duty. Sita also says that when her mother thinks of her, love will overwhelm her.
ramacharitamanas::2253.simple_insight: Care for family can be sacred, not burdensome.
ramacharitamanas::2253.detailed_meaning: Sita is explaining how she will live in Rama's household after exile. She tells Rama that serving her parents-in-law with respect is the highest duty, and that her mother will remember her with such love that grief will soften her mind.
ramacharitamanas::2253.modern_relevance: You move into a new home and quietly learn the rhythms of an older generation: tea at the right time, the right tone, the right respect. Love shows up as careful service, not big speeches.
ramacharitamanas::2253.insight: It shifts duty from self-expression to reverent care for family roles.

ramacharitamanas::2254.verse_sanskrit: तब तब तुम्ह कहि कथा पुरानी। सुंदरि समुझाएहु मृदु बानी॥ कहउँ सुभायँ सपथ सत मोही। सुमुखि मातु हित राखउँ तोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2254.verse_hindi: हे सुंदरी! तब-तब तुम कोमल वाणी से पुरानी कथाएँ कह-कहकर इन्हें समझाना। हे सुमुखि! मुझे सैकड़ों सौगंध हैं, मैं यह स्वभाव से ही कहता हूँ कि मैं तुम्हें केवल माता के लिए ही घर पर रखता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2254.english_translation: Then, gently remind them with old stories, dear one. I speak this from my own nature and with many vows: fair-faced one, I keep you at home only for my mother’s sake.
ramacharitamanas::2254.translation_literal: तब तब (then, again and again) / तुम्ह (you) / कहि (telling) / कथा पुरानी (old stories) / सुंदरि (dear one) / समुझाएहु (make understand) / मृदु बानी (gentle words) / कहउँ (I say) / सुभायँ (by nature) / सपथ सत (hundreds of vows) / मोही (to me) / सुमुखि (fair-faced one) / मातु हित (for mother’s sake) / राखउँ (I keep) / तोही (you)
ramacharitamanas::2254.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2254.essence: Firm duty can still be spoken with tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::2254.simple_meaning: Ram tells Sita to use gentle words and old stories to explain why she must stay home. He says he keeps her there only because of his mother’s welfare.
ramacharitamanas::2254.simple_insight: Love can still speak with firmness. Kindness does not erase duty.
ramacharitamanas::2254.detailed_meaning: Sita has been asked to remain in the house, and Ram is explaining the reason with tenderness. He tells her to soften the message with old stories and gentle speech, while making clear that this decision serves his mother’s good.
ramacharitamanas::2254.modern_relevance: You have to tell someone a painful family decision and you choose your words carefully, not to hide the truth but to keep the relationship intact.
ramacharitamanas::2254.insight: It teaches you to hold duty and tenderness together, so hard choices do not become harsh speech.

ramacharitamanas::2255.verse_sanskrit: गुर श्रुति संमत धरम फलु पाइअ बिनहिं कलेस। हठ बस सब संकट सहे गालव नहुष नरेस ॥
ramacharitamanas::2255.verse_hindi: (मेरी आज्ञा मानकर घर पर रहने से) गुरु और वेद के द्वारा सम्मत धर्म (के आचरण) का फल तुम्हें बिना ही क्लेश के मिल जाता है, किन्तु हठ के वश होकर गालव मुनि और राजा नहुष आदि सब ने संकट ही सहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2255.english_translation: By following the Dharma approved by the teacher and the Vedas, one receives its fruit without hardship; but under stubbornness, Gālava, Nahuṣa, and other kings suffered only trouble.
ramacharitamanas::2255.translation_literal: गुर (teacher) / श्रुति (Veda) / संमत (approved) / धरम (dharma) / फलु (fruit) / पाइअ (is obtained) / बिनहिं (without) / कलेस (hardship) / हठ (stubbornness) / बस (under the control of) / सब (all) / संकट (troubles) / सहे (suffered) / गालव (Gālava) / नहुष (Nahuṣa) / नरेस (king)
ramacharitamanas::2255.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2255.essence: Right conduct yields its fruit cleanly; stubbornness turns duty into suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2255.simple_meaning: Follow the guidance of the teacher and the Vedas, and dharma bears fruit without suffering. Stubbornness only brings trouble, as Gālava and Nahuṣa learned.
ramacharitamanas::2255.simple_insight: You save yourself needless pain when you stop forcing your own way.
ramacharitamanas::2255.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita is being gently instructed about staying at home and accepting the family duty before exile. The speaker points to old examples like Gālava and Nahuṣa: stubbornness against right guidance leads to suffering, while dharma done properly brings its fruit smoothly.
ramacharitamanas::2255.modern_relevance: You keep arguing with the experienced person in the room, then spend three weeks cleaning up the mess. The verse says the hard lesson was avoidable: listen, align, and spare yourself the extra suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2255.insight: It shifts the mind from self-willed pushing to disciplined obedience to right guidance.

ramacharitamanas::2256.verse_sanskrit: मैं पुनि करि प्रवान पितु बानी। बेगि फिरब सुनु सुमुखि सयानी॥ दिवस जात नहिं लागिहि बारा। सुंदरि सिखवनु सुनहु हमारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2256.verse_hindi: हे सुमुखि! हे सयानी! सुनो, मैं भी पिता के वचन को सत्य करके शीघ्र ही लौटूँगा। दिन जाते देर नहीं लगेगी। हे सुंदरी! हमारी यह सीख सुनो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2256.english_translation: I will also fulfill my father's word and return soon, O wise and gentle one. Days will pass quickly; listen to my counsel, dear lady.
ramacharitamanas::2256.translation_literal: मैं (I) / पुनि (also) / करि (having done) / प्रवान (fulfilled) / पितु बानी (father's word) / बेगि (quickly) / फिरब (will return) / सुनु (listen) / सुमुखि (gentle-faced one) / सयानी (wise one) / दिवस (days) / जात (passing) / नहिं (not) / लागिहि (will take) / बारा (time) / सुंदरि (beautiful one) / सिखवनु (instruction) / सुनहु (listen) / हमारा (our/my)
ramacharitamanas::2256.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2256.essence: A promise kept is more important than a promise that comforts.
ramacharitamanas::2256.simple_meaning: Ram promises to fulfill his father's word and return soon. He tries to reassure Sita that the time apart will feel short.
ramacharitamanas::2256.simple_insight: Keeping a promise matters more than easing the moment with words.
ramacharitamanas::2256.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is preparing to leave for the forest after accepting exile. He speaks gently to Sita, promising that he will honor Dasharath's word and come back quickly, even as the separation begins to feel real.
ramacharitamanas::2256.modern_relevance: You leave for a long trip and promise you'll be back soon, even though both of you know the house will feel empty. A real promise steadies the heart before distance does.
ramacharitamanas::2256.insight: It shifts attention from comforting delay to honoring a binding promise.

ramacharitamanas::2257.verse_sanskrit: जौं हठ करहु प्रेम बस बामा। तौ तुम्ह दुखु पाउब परिनामा॥ काननु कठिन भयंकरु भारी। घोर घामु हिम बारि बयारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2257.verse_hindi: हे वामा! यदि प्रेमवश हठ करोगी, तो तुम परिणाम में दुःख पाओगी। वन बड़ा कठिन (क्लेशदायक) और भयानक है। वहाँ की धूप, जाड़ा, वर्षा और हवा सभी बड़े भयानक हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2257.english_translation: O lovely one, if you insist out of love, you will suffer in the end. The forest is very harsh and frightening. Its heat, cold, rain, and wind are all terrible.
ramacharitamanas::2257.translation_literal: जौं (if) / हठ (insistence) / करहु (you do) / प्रेम बस (under the force of love) / बामा (lovely one) / तौ (then) / तुम्ह (you) / दुखु (pain) / पाउब (will get) / परिनामा (in the end) / काननु (forest) / कठिन (hard) / भयंकरु (frightening) / भारी (very great) / घोर (fierce) / घामु (heat) / हिम (cold) / बारि (water) / बयारी (wind)
ramacharitamanas::2257.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2257.essence: Love can be sincere and still need to say no.
ramacharitamanas::2257.simple_meaning: Sita is warned that insisting on going will only bring suffering, because the forest is dangerous and full of harsh weather.
ramacharitamanas::2257.simple_insight: Love does not erase reality; sometimes care means naming the cost honestly.
