ramacharitamanas::2257.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita is determined to follow Ram into exile. The speaker tries to stop her by describing the forest’s dangers: heat, cold, rain, wind, and hardship. The verse is part of a compassionate warning, not the final argument.
ramacharitamanas::2257.modern_relevance: Someone you love wants to join you on a hard road, and you can already see the toll it will take. Honest care sometimes sounds like refusal, not encouragement.
ramacharitamanas::2257.insight: It teaches you to separate affection from denial and speak plainly about risk.

ramacharitamanas::2258.verse_sanskrit: कुस कंटक मग काँकर नाना। चलब पयादेहिं बिनु पदत्राना॥ चरन कमल मृदु मंजु तुम्हारे। मारग अगम भूमिधर भारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2258.verse_hindi: रास्ते में कुश, काँटे और बहुत से कंकड़ हैं। उन पर बिना जूते के पैदल ही चलना होगा। तुम्हारे चरणकमल कोमल और सुंदर हैं और रास्ते में बड़े-बड़े दुर्गम पर्वत हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2258.english_translation: The path is strewn with kusha grass, thorns, and stones. You will have to walk barefoot. Your lotus feet are soft and beautiful, and the road is full of high, impassable mountains.
ramacharitamanas::2258.translation_literal: कुस (kusha grass) / कंटक (thorns) / मग (path) / काँकर (pebbles, stones) / नाना (many kinds) / चलब (to walk) / पयादेहिं (on foot, barefoot) / बिनु (without) / पदत्राना (shoes, footwear) // चरन (feet) / कमल (lotus) / मृदु (soft) / मंजु (beautiful) / तुम्हारे (your) / मारग (road, path) / अगम (impassable) / भूमिधर (mountains) / भारे (heavy, great)
ramacharitamanas::2258.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2258.essence: Devotion must walk through pain, not around it.
ramacharitamanas::2258.simple_meaning: The road is rough, sharp, and full of obstacles. Walking it means going barefoot over painful ground and through hard mountain terrain.
ramacharitamanas::2258.simple_insight: Love can ask for a hard journey, not a comfortable one.
ramacharitamanas::2258.detailed_meaning: Ram is still speaking to Sita as he explains the exile ahead. He describes the forest path in plain, painful detail: thorns, stones, bare feet, and steep mountains. The warning deepens the emotional weight of her choice.
ramacharitamanas::2258.modern_relevance: You agree to a trip, then realise it means broken roads, no comfort, and a body that will feel every mile. Love sometimes asks for that kind of honesty.
ramacharitamanas::2258.insight: It shifts the mind from romantic longing to the physical cost of commitment.

ramacharitamanas::2259.verse_sanskrit: कंदर खोह नदीं नद नारे। अगम अगाध न जाहिं निहारे॥ भालु बाघ बृक केहरि नागा। करहिं नाद सुनि धीरजु भागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2259.verse_hindi: पर्वतों की गुफाएँ, खोह (दर्रे), नदियाँ, नद और नाले ऐसे अगम्य और गहरे हैं कि उनकी ओर देखा तक नहीं जाता। रीछ, बाघ, भेड़िये, सिंह और हाथी ऐसे (भयानक) शब्द करते हैं कि उन्हें सुनकर धीरज भाग जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2259.english_translation: Caves, ravines, rivers, and streams are so impassable and deep that no one even dares look at them. Bears, tigers, wolves, lions, and elephants roar there, and the sound drives courage away.
ramacharitamanas::2259.translation_literal: कंदर (caves) / खोह (ravines) / नदीं (rivers) / नद (rivers) / नारे (streams) / अगम (impassable) / अगाध (bottomless) / न जाहिं (do not go) / निहारे (to be seen) / भालु (bears) / बाघ (tigers) / बृक (wolves) / केहरि (lions) / नागा (elephants) / करहिं (make) / नाद (roars) / सुनि (hearing) / धीरजु (courage) / भागा (flees)
ramacharitamanas::2259.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2259.essence: The forest is so severe that even courage starts to run.
ramacharitamanas::2259.simple_meaning: The forest route is terrifying and nearly impossible. Caves, ravines, deep waters, and wild animals make even brave people lose courage.
ramacharitamanas::2259.simple_insight: Some journeys are hard before they are heroic. Fear is real, and pretending otherwise helps no one.
ramacharitamanas::2259.detailed_meaning: Kaikeyi is still pressing the case for exile, and the harshness of the forest is being laid out in full. Tulsidas describes cliffs, water, and wild beasts to show what Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are being sent into.
ramacharitamanas::2259.modern_relevance: You open the map for a night drive and see a route through empty hills, no signal, no shops, no comfort. The mind tightens before the road even begins.
ramacharitamanas::2259.insight: It shifts attention from romance to reality: the exile is not symbolic; it is physically dangerous.

ramacharitamanas::2260.verse_sanskrit: भूमि सयन बलकल बसन असनु कंद फल मूल। ते कि सदा सब दिन मिलहिं सबुइ समय अनुकूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::2260.verse_hindi: जमीन पर सोना, पेड़ों की छाल के वस्त्र पहनना और कंद, मूल, फल का भोजन करना होगा। और वे भी क्या सदा सब दिन मिलेंगे? सब कुछ अपने-अपने समय के अनुकूल ही मिल सकेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2260.english_translation: You will sleep on the ground, wear bark clothes, and live on roots, fruits, and tubers. Even those will not come every day; everything comes only in its proper season.
ramacharitamanas::2260.translation_literal: भूमि (ground) / सयन (sleeping) / बलकल (bark-cloth) / बसन (garments) / असनु (food) / कंद (roots) / फल (fruits) / मूल (tubers) / ते (those) / कि (indeed) / सदा (always) / सब दिन (every day) / मिलहिं (will be available) / सबुइ (all) / समय (time) / अनुकूल (favourable)
ramacharitamanas::2260.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2260.essence: Comfort is seasonal; endurance must be steady.
ramacharitamanas::2260.simple_meaning: Forest life will be hard. Even basic food and comfort will come only when nature allows.
ramacharitamanas::2260.simple_insight: It softens the need for constant comfort and teaches you to live with what arrives on time.
ramacharitamanas::2260.detailed_meaning: As Ram prepares for exile, the path ahead is described in plain, severe terms: no bed, no fine clothes, no guaranteed food. The forest will give only what it gives, when it gives it. This line deepens the warning before the journey begins.
ramacharitamanas::2260.modern_relevance: You pack for a long trek and realize the weather, the path, and even the meal stop are out of your control. The trip still happens, but on nature's terms, not yours.
ramacharitamanas::2260.insight: It trains the mind to expect irregularity without complaint and to prepare for hardship without panic.

ramacharitamanas::2261.verse_sanskrit: नर अहार रजनीचर चरहीं। कपट बेष बिधि कोटिक करहीं॥ लागइ अति पहार कर पानी। बिपिन बिपति नहिं जाइ बखानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2261.verse_hindi: मनुष्यों को खाने वाले निशाचर (राक्षस) फिरते रहते हैं। वे करोड़ों प्रकार के कपट रूप धारण कर लेते हैं। पहाड़ का पानी बहुत ही लगता है। वन की विपत्ति बखानी नहीं जा सकती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2261.english_translation: Man-eating night-wanderers roam there. They assume countless disguises of deceit. Even mountain water is hard to find. The dangers of the forest cannot be fully told.
ramacharitamanas::2261.translation_literal: नर (human) / अहार (food) / रजनीचर (night-wanderers) / चरहीं (wander) / कपट (deceit) / बेष (disguise) / बिधि (manner) / कोटिक (millions) / करहीं (make) / लागइ (seems) / अति (very) / पहार (mountain) / कर (of) / पानी (water) / बिपिन (forest) / बिपति (danger) / नहिं (not) / जाइ (can be) / बखानी (described)
ramacharitamanas::2261.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2261.essence: The forest is dangerous in ways words cannot hold.
ramacharitamanas::2261.simple_meaning: The forest is full of danger: man-eating beings, disguises, scarce water, and hardships that cannot be fully described.
ramacharitamanas::2261.simple_insight: Some places test your courage before they test your strength.
ramacharitamanas::2261.detailed_meaning: As Ram, Sita, and Lakshman move deeper into exile, the forest is no longer just wild land but a place of constant threat. The narrator lists the hidden dangers to show how harsh their path has become.
ramacharitamanas::2261.modern_relevance: You enter a new city at night with no contacts, no clear map, and every alley feels uncertain. The verse understands that feeling of being small inside a place that does not welcome you.
ramacharitamanas::2261.insight: It trains the mind to see the real cost of exile, not romanticize hardship.

ramacharitamanas::2262.verse_sanskrit: ब्याल कराल बिहग बन घोरा। निसिचर निकर नारि नर चोरा॥ डरपहिं धीर गहन सुधि आएँ। मृगलोचनि तुम्ह भीरु सुभाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2262.verse_hindi: वन में भीषण सर्प, भयानक पक्षी और स्त्री-पुरुषों को चुराने वाले राक्षसों के झुंड के झुंड रहते हैं। वन की (भयंकरता) याद आने मात्र से धीर पुरुष भी डर जाते हैं। फिर हे मृगलोचनि! तुम तो स्वभाव से ही डरपोक हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2262.english_translation: The forest holds terrible serpents, fierce birds, and bands of kidnappers. Even brave men tremble when they remember the forest. O lotus-eyed one, you are timid by nature.
ramacharitamanas::2262.translation_literal: ब्याल (serpents) / कराल (terrible) / बिहग (birds) / बन (forest) / घोरा (fierce) / निसिचर (night-dwelling beings) / निकर (groups) / नारि (women) / नर (men) / चोरा (kidnappers) ॥ / डरपहिं (tremble) / धीर (brave) / गहन (forest-depth) / सुधि (memory) / आएँ (on coming) ॥ / मृगलोचनि (deer-eyed one) / तुम्ह (you) / भीरु (timid) / सुभाएँ (by nature) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2262.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2262.essence: Fear makes the forest larger than it is.
ramacharitamanas::2262.simple_meaning: The forest is described as full of danger, and the speaker says even brave people fear it. The final line is a teasing warning that the listener is naturally timid.
ramacharitamanas::2262.simple_insight: Fear grows when the mind pictures danger before it arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2262.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the speaker is trying to dissuade Sita from going into exile by painting the forest as terrifying. He lists serpents, wild birds, and kidnappers, then claims that even brave people lose courage when they remember such dangers.
ramacharitamanas::2262.modern_relevance: You imagine the worst before a difficult move, and the whole situation starts feeling impossible. A single fearful picture can make a normal challenge seem like a threat.
ramacharitamanas::2262.insight: It shows how fear persuades through vivid images, not facts, and how warning can become pressure.

ramacharitamanas::2263.verse_sanskrit: हंसगवनि तुम्ह नहिं बन जोगू। सुनि अपजसु मोहि देइहि लोगू॥ मानस सलिल सुधाँ प्रतिपाली। जिअइ कि लवन पयोधि मराली ॥
ramacharitamanas::2263.verse_hindi: हे हंसगमनी! तुम वन के योग्य नहीं हो। तुम्हारे वन जाने की बात सुनकर लोग मुझे अपयश देंगे (बुरा कहेंगे)। मानसरोवर के अमृत के समान जल से पाली हुई हंसिनी कहीं खारे समुद्र में जी सकती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2263.english_translation: O swan-gaited one, you are not fit for the forest. Hearing of your going there, people will blame me. Can the swan, raised on the nectar-like waters of Manasarovar, live in the salty ocean?
ramacharitamanas::2263.translation_literal: हंसगवनि (swan-gaited one) / तुम्ह (you) / नहिं (not) / बन (forest) / जोगू (fit) / सुनि (hearing) / अपजसु (disgrace/blame) / मोहि (to me) / देइहि (will give) / लोगू (people) / मानस (Manasarovar) / सलिल (water) / सुधाँ (nectar-like) / प्रतिपाली (raised/fed) / जिअइ (live) / कि (can) / लवन (salty) / पयोधि (ocean) / मराली (swan)
ramacharitamanas::2263.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2263.essence: Real care knows when tenderness should not be tested by hardship.
ramacharitamanas::2263.simple_meaning: Sita is too delicate and refined for forest life, and Ram says her going there would bring him blame. The image compares her to a swan raised on sweet lake water, unable to live in the salty ocean.
ramacharitamanas::2263.simple_insight: Love sometimes protects by refusing to force someone into suffering they were never made for.
ramacharitamanas::2263.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is preparing for exile and speaking to Sita about the harsh forest ahead. He tries to keep her back by saying the wilderness is no place for her, and that public blame would fall on him if she came.
ramacharitamanas::2263.modern_relevance: You see someone you love packing for a situation that will grind them down, and your first instinct is to shield them, not prove a point.
ramacharitamanas::2263.insight: It frames care as discernment: not every hardship should be shared, and not every beloved person should be dragged into danger.

ramacharitamanas::2264.verse_sanskrit: नव रसाल बन बिहरनसीला। सोह कि कोकिल बिपिन करीला॥ रहहु भवन अस हृदयँ बिचारी। चंदबदनि दुखु कानन भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2264.verse_hindi: नवीन आम के वन में विहार करने वाली कोयल क्या करील के जंगल में शोभा पाती है? हे चन्द्रमुखी! हृदय में ऐसा विचारकर तुम घर ही पर रहो। वन में बड़ा कष्ट है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2264.english_translation: Does a cuckoo that belongs in fresh mango groves belong in a forest of karil thorns? O moon-faced one, think this through in your heart and stay at home. The forest is full of hardship.
ramacharitamanas::2264.translation_literal: नव रसाल (new mango) / बन (forest) / बिहरनसीला (fond of roaming) / सोह (look beautiful) / कि (whether) / कोकिल (cuckoo) / बिपिन (forest) / करीला (karil-thorn grove) ॥ / रहहु (stay) / भवन (home) / अस (thus) / हृदयँ (in heart) / बिचारी (having considered) / चंदबदनि (moon-faced one) / दुखु (hardship) / कानन (forest) / भारी (great) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2264.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2264.essence: Tenderness does not belong in every place.
ramacharitamanas::2264.simple_meaning: A tender, beautiful bird does not fit a harsh thorn forest. The speaker urges the listener to stay home because the forest is full of suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2264.simple_insight: Love sometimes protects by refusing what it cannot bear to lose.
ramacharitamanas::2264.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the conversation turns to the pain of exile. The speaker tries to keep the beloved woman from following Ram into the forest, comparing her delicate nature to a cuckoo that belongs in mango groves, not thorn thickets. The verse softens into warning: stay at home, because the forest will hurt you.
ramacharitamanas::2264.modern_relevance: You want to follow someone into a situation you know will break you — a move, a crisis, a rough season. Love can be real and still admit: this place is not built for your tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::2264.insight: It shifts the mind from romantic impulse to honest discernment about what a person can endure.

ramacharitamanas::2265.verse_sanskrit: सहज सुहृद गुर स्वामि सिख जो न करइ सिर मानि। सो पछिताइ अघाइ उर अवसि होइ हित हानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2265.verse_hindi: स्वाभाविक ही हित चाहने वाले गुरु और स्वामी की सीख को जो सिर चढ़ाकर नहीं मानता, वह हृदय में भरपेट पछताता है और उसके हित की हानि अवश्य होती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2265.english_translation: One who does not hold in the head the advice of a natural friend, guru, and master will later regret it deeply, and his own good will surely be harmed.
ramacharitamanas::2265.translation_literal: सहज (natural) / सुहृद (well-wisher) / गुर (guru) / स्वामि (master) / सिख (advice) / जो (who) / न (not) / करइ (does) / सिर (head) / मानि (placing) / सो (that one) / पछिताइ (regrets) / अघाइ (fully) / उर (in the heart) / अवसि (certainly) / होइ (becomes) / हित (good) / हानि (loss)
ramacharitamanas::2265.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2265.essence: Pride turns good counsel into future regret.
ramacharitamanas::2265.simple_meaning: A true well-wisher's advice should be taken seriously. Ignoring it leads to regret and damages your own good.
ramacharitamanas::2265.simple_insight: There is relief in listening early, before pride turns a warning into pain.
ramacharitamanas::2265.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi’s pride and resistance are already setting the exile in motion. This line warns that a person who refuses the counsel of a natural friend, guru, or master will later suffer regret and lose what was meant for their good.
ramacharitamanas::2265.modern_relevance: Your friend, mentor, or parent sees the pattern before you do. You brush them off because you want your own way, then spend weeks cleaning up the mess they warned about.
ramacharitamanas::2265.insight: It teaches you to treat wise counsel as protection, not interference.

ramacharitamanas::2266.verse_sanskrit: सुनि मृदु बचन मनोहर पिय के। लोचन ललित भरे जल सिय के॥ सीतल सिख दाहक भइ कैसें। चकइहि सरद चंद निसि जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2266.verse_hindi: प्रियतम के कोमल तथा मनोहर वचन सुनकर सीताजी के सुंदर नेत्र जल से भर गए। श्री रामजी की यह शीतल सीख उनको कैसी जलाने वाली हुई, जैसे चकवी को शरद ऋतु की चाँदनी रात होती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2266.english_translation: Hearing her beloved's gentle, beautiful words, Sita's lovely eyes filled with tears. How could this cooling advice burn her like a night of autumn moonlight burns a chakravaki bird?
ramacharitamanas::2266.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / मृदु (gentle) / बचन (words) / मनोहर (beautiful) / पिय के (of the beloved) / लोचन (eyes) / ललित (lovely) / भरे (filled) / जल (with water/tears) / सिय के (of Sita)॥ सीतल (cooling) / सिख (advice) / दाहक (burning) / भइ (became) / कैसें (how) / चकइहि (to the chakravaki bird) / सरद (autumn) / चंद (moon) / निसि (night) / जैसें (like)
ramacharitamanas::2266.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2266.essence: Tender words can still wound a heart that senses separation.
ramacharitamanas::2266.simple_meaning: Sita hears Ram's gentle words and cries. His soft advice feels painful to her, like a cold autumn moonlit night that hurts a chakravaki bird.
ramacharitamanas::2266.simple_insight: Love can make even kind words feel unbearable when separation is near.
ramacharitamanas::2266.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is preparing to leave, and Sita is already feeling the cut of separation. He speaks gently, but her heart hears loss. Her tears show that love can turn comfort into pain.
ramacharitamanas::2266.modern_relevance: You get a calm, careful message from someone you love, but your chest tightens anyway because you know it means distance. The words are soft; the grief underneath is not.
ramacharitamanas::2266.insight: It shows how attachment changes perception, making even kindness feel like sorrow.

ramacharitamanas::2267.verse_sanskrit: उतरु न आव बिकल बैदेही। तजन चहत सुचि स्वामि सनेही॥ बरबस रोकि बिलोचन बारी। धरि धीरजु उर अवनिकुमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2267.verse_hindi: जानकीजी से कुछ उत्तर देते नहीं बनता, वे यह सोचकर व्याकुल हो उठीं कि मेरे पवित्र और प्रेमी स्वामी मुझे छोड़ जाना चाहते हैं। नेत्रों के जल (आँसुओं) को जबर्दस्ती रोककर वे पृथ्वी की कन्या सीताजी हृदय में धीरज धरकर, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2267.english_translation: Janaki could not answer. She grew restless, thinking, “My pure and loving husband wants to leave me.” Forcing back her tears, Sita, daughter of the earth, held courage in her heart.
ramacharitamanas::2267.translation_literal: उतरु (answer) / न (not) / आव (came) / बिकल (distressed) / बैदेही (Sita) / तजन (to leave) / चहत (wants) / सुचि (pure) / स्वामि (husband/master) / सनेही (loving)॥ / बरबस (forcibly) / रोकि (stopping) / बिलोचन (eyes) / बारी (water/tears) / धरि (holding) / धीरजु (patience/courage) / उर (heart) / अवनिकुमारी (daughter of the earth)
ramacharitamanas::2267.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2267.essence: Love can tremble and still remain steady.
ramacharitamanas::2267.simple_meaning: Sita cannot speak at first. She feels distressed that her loving husband wants to leave her, so she holds back her tears and steadies herself.
ramacharitamanas::2267.simple_insight: Love can shake you so deeply that even silence becomes a struggle.
ramacharitamanas::2267.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram has just given Sita a gentle but painful instruction about separation. Hearing it, Sita is overwhelmed. She cannot answer at once; she fights back tears and gathers courage, showing the ache of devotion before she speaks to Kaikeyi.
ramacharitamanas::2267.modern_relevance: You hear a message from someone you love that changes everything, and your throat tightens before you can reply. The body feels the loss before the mind finds words.
ramacharitamanas::2267.insight: It shows how devotion can hold grief without collapsing into it.

ramacharitamanas::2268.verse_sanskrit: लागि सासु पग कह कर जोरी। छमबि देबि बड़ि अबिनय मोरी। दीन्हि प्रानपति मोहि सिख सोई। जेहि बिधि मोर परम हित होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2268.verse_hindi: सास के पैर लगकर, हाथ जोड़कर कहने लगीं- हे देवि! मेरी इस बड़ी भारी ढिठाई को क्षमा कीजिए। मुझे प्राणपति ने वही शिक्षा दी है, जिससे मेरा परम हित हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2268.english_translation: Sita bowed at her mother-in-law's feet and said, "Forgive my great boldness. My lord has taught me only what is for my highest good."
ramacharitamanas::2268.translation_literal: लागि (bowing) / सासु पग (mother-in-law's feet) / कह (said) / कर जोरी (with joined hands) / छमबि देबि (forgive, lady) / बड़ि अबिनय (great boldness) / मोरी (my) / दीन्हि (gave) / प्रानपति (lord of life) / मोहि (to me) / सिख (teaching) / सोई (that) / जेहि बिधि (in the way that) / मोर (my) / परम हित (highest good) / होई (happens)
ramacharitamanas::2268.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2268.essence: True care can arrive as a painful instruction.
ramacharitamanas::2268.simple_meaning: Sita apologizes respectfully to her mother-in-law and says that Ram's teaching is meant for her highest good, even though it is painful.
ramacharitamanas::2268.simple_insight: Real love can accept a hard instruction without resentment.
ramacharitamanas::2268.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita stands before her mother-in-law after hearing that she must leave with Ram. She bows, asks forgiveness for her boldness, and accepts Ram's teaching as her own welfare, even before the full pain of separation is spoken aloud.
ramacharitamanas::2268.modern_relevance: You get a message that changes everything, and your first instinct is to argue. Then you remember the person who loves you most may be asking for your deeper good, not your immediate comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2268.insight: It shifts the mind from defending comfort to trusting a painful correction.

ramacharitamanas::2269.verse_sanskrit: मैं पुनि समुझि दीखि मन माहीं। पिय बियोग सम दुखु जग नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2269.verse_hindi: परन्तु मैंने मन में समझकर देख लिया कि पति के वियोग के समान जगत में कोई दुःख नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2269.english_translation: But I have understood in my heart that no sorrow in the world equals separation from a husband.
ramacharitamanas::2269.translation_literal: मैं (I) / पुनि (again) / समुझि (understanding) / दीखि (saw) / मन (mind) / माहीं (within) / पिय (beloved husband) / बियोग (separation) / सम (equal) / दुखु (sorrow) / जग (world) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::2269.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2269.essence: Separation from the beloved becomes the heaviest sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2269.simple_meaning: Sita realises that no pain in the world is as great as being separated from her husband.
ramacharitamanas::2269.simple_insight: Love’s absence can feel larger than every other pain.
ramacharitamanas::2269.detailed_meaning: Sita, standing before her mother-in-law after Ram’s departure, gathers herself and speaks from lived grief. She has already been told to stay composed, but her heart knows one thing clearly: separation from her beloved is the deepest sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2269.modern_relevance: You can lose sleep over a message left unread, a call not returned, or a partner leaving the room after a fight. Some absences hurt more than any argument.
ramacharitamanas::2269.insight: It names emotional separation as a real wound, not a minor inconvenience.

ramacharitamanas::2270.verse_sanskrit: प्राननाथ करुनायतन सुंदर सुखद सुजान। तुम्ह बिनु रघुकुल कुमुद बिधु सुरपुर नरक समान ॥
ramacharitamanas::2270.verse_hindi: हे प्राणनाथ! हे दया के धाम! हे सुंदर! हे सुखों के देने वाले! हे सुजान! हे रघुकुल रूपी कुमुद के खिलाने वाले चन्द्रमा! आपके बिना स्वर्ग भी मेरे लिए नरक के समान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2270.english_translation: O lord of life, ocean of compassion, beautiful, giver of joy, all-knowing! Without you, O moon of the Raghu clan, even heaven feels like hell.
ramacharitamanas::2270.translation_literal: प्राननाथ (lord of life) / करुनायतन (abode of compassion) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुखद (giver of joy) / सुजान (all-knowing) / तुम्ह बिनु (without you) / रघुकुल (Raghu clan) / कुमुद (white lotus) / बिधु (moon) / सुरपुर (realm of the radiant beings) / नरक (lower realm) / समान (equal)
ramacharitamanas::2270.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2270.essence: Without Ram, even paradise becomes unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2270.simple_meaning: The speaker says Ram is the source of life, compassion, beauty, joy, and wisdom. Without Ram, even the highest place feels unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2270.simple_insight: Real peace comes from closeness to Ram, not from changing the outer situation.
ramacharitamanas::2270.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the women of the palace are grieving Ram's exile. One voice turns to him in longing, praising his tenderness and saying that without him, even the best life feels empty. The verse deepens the pain of separation.
ramacharitamanas::2270.modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the nicer apartment, the trip everyone envied — and still feel hollow because the one presence that mattered is missing. This verse names that ache exactly.
ramacharitamanas::2270.insight: It shifts attention from external comfort to the presence that makes life feel alive.

ramacharitamanas::2271.verse_sanskrit: मातु पिता भगिनी प्रिय भाई। प्रिय परिवारु सुहृदय समुदाई॥ सासु ससुर गुर सजन सहाई। सुत सुंदर सुसील सुखदाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2271.verse_hindi: माता, पिता, बहिन, प्यारा भाई, प्यारा परिवार, मित्रों का समुदाय, सास, ससुर, गुरु, स्वजन (बन्धु-बांधव), सहायक और सुंदर, सुशील और सुख देने वाला पुत्र- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2271.english_translation: Mother, father, sister, dear brother, beloved family, a circle of friends, mother-in-law, father-in-law, teacher, kin, helpers, and a handsome, well-mannered, joy-giving son.
ramacharitamanas::2271.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / पिता (father) / भगिनी (sister) / प्रिय (dear) / भाई (brother) / प्रिय (beloved) / परिवारु (family) / सुहृदय (good-hearted) / समुदाई (group) / सासु (mother-in-law) / ससुर (father-in-law) / गुर (teacher) / सजन (kinsmen) / सहाई (helpers) / सुत (son) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुसील (well-mannered) / सुखदाई (joy-giving)
ramacharitamanas::2271.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2271.essence: Separation turns every loving bond into pain.
ramacharitamanas::2271.simple_meaning: Every close relationship and every source of support becomes painful in separation from the husband.
ramacharitamanas::2271.simple_insight: Grief feels larger when it touches every bond at once.
ramacharitamanas::2271.detailed_meaning: Sita is speaking in Ayodhyakand, listing the whole web of family and support that a married woman lives within. The verse is not a standalone teaching; it is part of her grief as she explains how separation from Ram makes every relationship feel wounded.
ramacharitamanas::2271.modern_relevance: You get one message after another while someone you love is gone, and even the kindest voices start to hurt. Loss does not stay in one corner; it spreads through every relationship.
ramacharitamanas::2271.insight: It shifts attention from one missing person to the way their absence unsettles an entire life.

ramacharitamanas::2272.verse_sanskrit: जहँ लगिनाथ नेह अरु नाते। पिय बिनु तियहि तरनिहु ते ताते॥ तनु धनु धामु धरनि पुर राजू। पति बिहीन सबु सोक समाजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2272.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! जहाँ तक स्नेह और नाते हैं, पति के बिना स्त्री को सूर्य से भी बढ़कर तपाने वाले हैं। शरीर, धन, घर, पृथ्वी, नगर और राज्य, पति के बिना स्त्री के लिए यह सब शोक का समाज है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2272.english_translation: As long as love and relationships exist, a husbandless woman is scorched even more than by the sun. Body, wealth, home, land, city, and kingdom—all become a gathering of sorrow without a husband.
ramacharitamanas::2272.translation_literal: जहँ (where) / लगिनाथ (until then, lord) / नेह (affection) / अरु (and) / नाते (relations) / पिय (beloved husband) / बिनु (without) / तियहि (for the woman) / तरनिहु (the sun) / ते (than) / ताते (hotter, more scorching)॥ तनु (body) / धनु (wealth) / धामु (home) / धरनि (land) / पुर (city) / राजू (kingdom) / पति (husband) / बिहीन (without) / सबु (all) / सोक (sorrow) / समाजू (assembly, gathering)॥
ramacharitamanas::2272.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2272.essence: Without the beloved, even abundance becomes sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2272.simple_meaning: A wife without her husband feels every part of life as pain. Even the things that should support her—home, wealth, and status—turn into sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2272.simple_insight: Loss can make even a full life feel barren.
ramacharitamanas::2272.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the grief of separation is spreading through the household after Ram’s exile. The poet describes how a woman’s world collapses when the beloved husband is absent: affection itself burns, and every possession becomes a reminder of loss.
ramacharitamanas::2272.modern_relevance: You walk into an empty apartment after a breakup and see the same chair, the same cup, the same walls. Nothing changed, yet everything feels wounded.
ramacharitamanas::2272.insight: It shifts attention from outward comfort to the emotional center that gives life meaning.

ramacharitamanas::2273.verse_sanskrit: भोग रोगसम भूषन भारू। जम जातना सरिस संसारू॥ प्राननाथ तुम्ह बिनु जग माहीं। मो कहुँ सुखद कतहुँ कछु नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2273.verse_hindi: भोग रोग के समान हैं, गहने भार रूप हैं और संसार यम यातना (नरक की पीड़ा) के समान है। हे प्राणनाथ! आपके बिना जगत में मुझे कहीं कुछ भी सुखदायी नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2273.english_translation: Pleasures are like illness, ornaments are a burden, and the world is like Yama's torment. O Lord of my life, without you in this world I find nothing pleasant anywhere.
ramacharitamanas::2273.translation_literal: भोग (pleasures) / रोगसम (like illness) / भूषन (ornaments) / भारू (burden) / जम (Yama) / जातना (torment) / सरिस (like) / संसारू (world) / प्राननाथ (lord of life) / तुम्ह बिनु (without you) / जग माहीं (in the world) / मो कहुँ (for me) / सुखद (pleasant) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / कछु नाहीं (nothing)
ramacharitamanas::2273.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2273.essence: Without Ram, even pleasure becomes pain.
ramacharitamanas::2273.simple_meaning: Worldly pleasures feel like illness, ornaments feel heavy, and life without Ram feels unbearable. Nothing in the world can comfort the one who is separated from him.
ramacharitamanas::2273.simple_insight: Real relief comes when you stop expecting comfort from things that cannot truly hold you.
ramacharitamanas::2273.detailed_meaning: In the pain of separation, Sita speaks as if every pleasure has turned bitter. She sees ornaments as a burden and the world itself as torture. This moment deepens her longing for Ram and shows how complete her devotion is.
ramacharitamanas::2273.modern_relevance: You get dressed for the party, check the mirror, and still feel strangely empty. The things meant to make life feel rich can feel heavy when the one thing you love is missing.
ramacharitamanas::2273.insight: It shifts attention away from outer comfort and toward the one presence that makes life feel whole.

ramacharitamanas::2274.verse_sanskrit: जिय बिनु देह नदी बिनु बारी। तैसिअ नाथ पुरुष बिनु नारी॥ नाथ सकल सुख साथ तुम्हारें। सरद बिमल बिधु बदनु निहारें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2274.verse_hindi: जैसे बिना जीव के देह और बिना जल के नदी, वैसे ही हे नाथ! बिना पुरुष के स्त्री है। हे नाथ! आपके साथ रहकर आपका शरद्-(पूर्णिमा) के निर्मल चन्द्रमा के समान मुख देखने से मुझे समस्त सुख प्राप्त होंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2274.english_translation: As a body is nothing without life and a river is nothing without water, so a woman is nothing without her husband. O Lord, all happiness is with you; seeing your face, pure as the autumn full moon, brings every joy.
ramacharitamanas::2274.translation_literal: जिय (life) / बिनु (without) / देह (body) / नदी (river) / बिनु (without) / बारी (water) / तैसिअ (likewise) / नाथ (O Lord) / पुरुष (man) / बिनु (without) / नारी (woman)॥ / नाथ (O Lord) / सकल (all) / सुख (happiness) / साथ (with) / तुम्हारें (with you) / सरद (autumn) / बिमल (pure) / बिधु (moon) / बदनु (face) / निहारें (seeing)॥
ramacharitamanas::2274.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2274.essence: Presence with Ram makes every hardship feel like home.
ramacharitamanas::2274.simple_meaning: Life gives the body meaning, water gives the river life, and the husband gives the wife her place in the world. Being with Ram brings complete joy, like seeing the bright moon.
ramacharitamanas::2274.simple_insight: Love feels complete when presence itself becomes enough.
ramacharitamanas::2274.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita is speaking to Ram before exile. She explains that life without him would be empty, like a body without breath or a river without water. Her joy is simply to stay near him and behold his face.
ramacharitamanas::2274.modern_relevance: You pack a suitcase for a move and realize the apartment, the city, even the future feel secondary. What matters is who you are carrying your life toward.
ramacharitamanas::2274.insight: It shifts attention from comfort and setting to presence and companionship.

ramacharitamanas::2275.verse_sanskrit: खग मृग परिजन नगरु बनु बलकल बिमल दुकूल। नाथ साथ सुरसदन सम परनसाल सुख मूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::2275.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! आपके साथ पक्षी और पशु ही मेरे कुटुम्बी होंगे, वन ही नगर और वृक्षों की छाल ही निर्मल वस्त्र होंगे और पर्णकुटी (पत्तों की बनी झोपड़ी) ही स्वर्ग के समान सुखों की मूल होगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2275.english_translation: Birds and deer will be my kin, the forest my city, bark my clean clothing, and a leaf-hut the root of heavenly comfort, if I am with you, Lord.
ramacharitamanas::2275.translation_literal: खग (birds) / मृग (deer) / परिजन (family) / नगरु (city) / बनु (forest) / बलकल (bark-cloth) / बिमल (pure) / दुकूल (garment) / नाथ (Lord) / साथ (with) / सुरसदन (the abode of the radiant beings) / सम (like) / परनसाल (leaf-hut) / सुख (comfort) / मूल (root)
ramacharitamanas::2275.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2275.essence: Presence with Ram makes exile feel like home.
ramacharitamanas::2275.simple_meaning: With Ram beside her, Sita says the forest feels like home. Even simple things become enough when love is present.
ramacharitamanas::2275.simple_insight: Love can turn hardship into shelter. Presence matters more than comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2275.detailed_meaning: In the forest exile, Sita speaks to Ram about life away from palace comfort. She says birds and deer will be family, the forest a city, bark-cloth fine clothing, and a leaf-hut a place of joy if he is with her.
ramacharitamanas::2275.modern_relevance: You move into a small rented room after leaving a bigger life behind. The walls are bare, the furniture is cheap, but the place feels livable because the person you love is there.
ramacharitamanas::2275.insight: It shifts attention from external luxury to the quality of companionship.

ramacharitamanas::2276.verse_sanskrit: बनदेबीं बनदेव उदारा। करिहहिं सासु ससुर सम सारा॥ कुस किसलय साथरी सुहाई। प्रभु सँग मंजु मनोज तुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2276.verse_hindi: उदार हृदय के वनदेवी और वनदेवता ही सास-ससुर के समान मेरी सार-संभार करेंगे और कुशा और पत्तों की सुंदर साथरी (बिछौना) ही प्रभु के साथ कामदेव की मनोहर तोशक के समान होगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2276.english_translation: The benevolent forest deities will care for me like parents and in-laws. A bed of kusa grass and tender leaves will be a lovely couch beside my lord, as charming as Cupid's own bed.
ramacharitamanas::2276.translation_literal: बनदेबीं (forest goddesses) / बनदेव (forest gods) / उदारा (generous, noble) / करिहहिं (will do) / सासु (mother-in-law) / ससुर (father-in-law) / सम (like) / सारा (care, support) ॥ / कुस (kusa grass) / किसलय (tender leaves) / साथरी (bed, bedding) / सुहाई (beautiful) / प्रभु (lord) / सँग (with) / मंजु (lovely) / मनोज (Cupid) / तुराई (bed, cushion)
ramacharitamanas::2276.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2276.simple_meaning: Sita says the forest itself will become her family and home. Even a bed of grass and leaves will feel beautiful because Ram will be beside her.
ramacharitamanas::2276.simple_insight: Love can turn hardship into shelter when the beloved is present.
ramacharitamanas::2276.detailed_meaning: In the exile scene, Sita is answering the pain of leaving palace life behind. She imagines the forest as a new household, with nature itself serving as kin. Her comfort comes not from luxury, but from Ram's company.
ramacharitamanas::2276.modern_relevance: You move into a tiny rented room with a thin mat, no furniture, and boxes for tables. Still, the place feels bearable because the person you love is there with you.
ramacharitamanas::2276.insight: It shifts attention from what is missing to who is present.

ramacharitamanas::2277.verse_sanskrit: कंद मूल फल अमिअ अहारू। अवध सौध सत सरिस पहारू॥ छिनु-छिनु प्रभु पद कमल बिलोकी। रहिहउँ मुदित दिवस जिमि कोकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2277.verse_hindi: कन्द, मूल और फल ही अमृत के समान आहार होंगे और (वन के) पहाड़ ही अयोध्या के सैकड़ों राजमहलों के समान होंगे। क्षण-क्षण में प्रभु के चरण कमलों को देख-देखकर मैं ऐसी आनंदित रहूँगी जैसे दिन में चकवी रहती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2277.english_translation: Roots, bulbs, and fruits will be like nectar for food, and the hills of the forest will be like hundreds of palaces in Ayodhya. Moment by moment, I will keep looking at the lotus feet of the Lord and remain joyful like a chakravaki in daylight.
ramacharitamanas::2277.translation_literal: कंद (roots/tubers) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruits) / अमिअ (nectar) / अहारू (food) / अवध (Ayodhya) / सौध (palaces) / सत (hundreds) / सरिस (like) / पहारू (mountains/hills) / छिनु-छिनु (moment by moment) / प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / बिलोकी (seeing) / रहिहउँ (I will remain) / मुदित (joyful) / दिवस (day) / जिमि (like) / कोकी (chakravaki bird)
ramacharitamanas::2277.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2277.essence: Presence can turn exile into a palace.
ramacharitamanas::2277.simple_meaning: Life in the forest will feel sweet and beautiful because Ram is there. Seeing his feet again and again will keep Sita joyful even in exile.
ramacharitamanas::2277.simple_insight: Love can transform hardship into home.
ramacharitamanas::2277.detailed_meaning: Sita is imagining exile beside Ram. After leaving Ayodhya, she does not complain about the forest; she turns roots, fruits, and rough hills into comfort because Ram will be near. Her joy comes from his presence, not from luxury.
ramacharitamanas::2277.modern_relevance: You move into a tiny rented room after losing the apartment you loved. The walls are thin, the furniture is borrowed, but the person you love is beside you — and suddenly the place feels livable.
ramacharitamanas::2277.insight: It shifts the mind from measuring comfort by objects to measuring it by presence.

ramacharitamanas::2278.verse_sanskrit: बन दुख नाथ कहे बहुतेरे। भय बिषाद परिताप घनेरे॥ प्रभु बियोग लवलेस समाना। सब मिलि होहिं न कृपानिधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2278.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! आपने वन के बहुत से दुःख और बहुत से भय, विषाद और सन्ताप कहे, परन्तु हे कृपानिधान! वे सब मिलकर भी प्रभु (आप) के वियोग (से होने वाले दुःख) के लवलेश के समान भी नहीं हो सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::2278.english_translation: O Lord, you have spoken of many forest hardships—fear, grief, and deep suffering. Yet all of them together are not even a tiny fraction of the pain of being separated from the Lord.
ramacharitamanas::2278.translation_literal: बन (forest) / दुख (sorrows) / नाथ (Lord) / कहे (spoken) / बहुतेरे (many) / भय (fear) / बिषाद (grief) / परिताप (burning pain) / घनेरे (many, intense) / प्रभु (Lord) / बियोग (separation) / लवलेस (tiny fraction) / समाना (equal) / सब (all) / मिलि (together) / होहिं (become) / न (not) / कृपानिधाना (treasure of compassion)
ramacharitamanas::2278.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2278.essence: Separation from Ram outweighs every other suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2278.simple_meaning: Forest hardships can be endured, but separation from Ram feels far worse than all of them combined.
ramacharitamanas::2278.simple_insight: Love makes every outer hardship smaller than the ache of absence.
ramacharitamanas::2278.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the exile has already begun to feel unbearable. The speaker says that even fear, grief, and burning pain in the forest are small compared with the pain of being away from Ram. The real wound is separation, not hardship itself.
ramacharitamanas::2278.modern_relevance: You can survive a hard move, a messy job, even loneliness in a new city. What hurts most is not the inconvenience — it is being cut off from the person or presence that gives life meaning.
ramacharitamanas::2278.insight: It shifts attention from external discomfort to the deeper pain of separation and longing.

ramacharitamanas::2279.verse_sanskrit: अस जियँ जानि सुजान सिरोमनि। लेइअ संग मोहि छाड़िअ जनि॥ बिनती बहुत करौं का स्वामी। करुनामय उर अंतरजामी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2279.verse_hindi: ऐसा जी में जानकर, हे सुजान शिरोमणि! आप मुझे साथ ले लीजिए, यहाँ न छोड़िए। हे स्वामी! मैं अधिक क्या विनती करूँ? आप करुणामय हैं और सबके हृदय के अंदर की जानने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2279.english_translation: Knowing this in my heart, O most wise one, take me along and do not leave me here. What more pleading can I make, my lord? You are full of compassion and know the heart within every heart.
ramacharitamanas::2279.translation_literal: अस (thus) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानि (knowing) / सुजान (most wise) / सिरोमनि (crest-jewel) / लेइअ (take) / संग (along) / मोहि (me) / छाड़िअ (do not leave) / जनि (not) / बिनती (pleading) / बहुत (much) / करौं (I make) / का (what) / स्वामी (lord) / करुनामय (full of compassion) / उर (heart) / अंतरजामी (inner-knower)
ramacharitamanas::2279.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2279.essence: Love asks to be taken along, not merely understood.
ramacharitamanas::2279.simple_meaning: Bharat begs Ram to take him along and not leave him behind. He trusts Ram's compassion and inner knowledge, so he does not need to argue further.
ramacharitamanas::2279.simple_insight: Real love does not demand control; it asks to be held by trust.
ramacharitamanas::2279.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram at the edge of exile and pleads to go with him. He knows Ram already understands his heart, so his request becomes a surrender of ego, not a negotiation.
ramacharitamanas::2279.modern_relevance: You send one last message after a painful goodbye, not to persuade, but to be known. The deepest plea is simple: don't leave me outside your care.
ramacharitamanas::2279.insight: It shifts the mind from bargaining to surrender, trusting that love already sees what words cannot prove.

ramacharitamanas::2280.verse_sanskrit: राखिअ अवध जो अवधि लगि रहत न जनिअहिं प्रान। दीनबंधु सुंदर सुखद सील सनेह निधान ॥
ramacharitamanas::2280.verse_hindi: हे दीनबन्धु! हे सुंदर! हे सुख देने वाले! हे शील और प्रेम के भंडार! यदि अवधि (चौदह वर्ष) तक मुझे अयोध्या में रखते हैं, तो जान लीजिए कि मेरे प्राण नहीं रहेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2280.english_translation: O friend of the poor, O beautiful one, O giver of joy, O treasure of character and love! If you keep me in Ayodhya for fourteen years, know that my life will not remain.
ramacharitamanas::2280.translation_literal: राखिअ (keep) / अवध (Ayodhya) / जो (if) / अवधि (period) / लगि (until) / रहत (staying) / न (not) / जनिअहिं (should be known) / प्रान (life-breath) / दीनबंधु (friend of the poor) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुखद (giver of joy) / सील (character) / सनेह (love) / निधान (treasure)
ramacharitamanas::2280.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2280.essence: Separation from Ram is unbearable for the one who truly belongs to him.
ramacharitamanas::2280.simple_meaning: Bharat says he cannot live if Ram is kept in Ayodhya for the full exile period. He pleads with Ram as the source of kindness, beauty, joy, character, and love.
ramacharitamanas::2280.simple_insight: Love can become unbearable when separation lasts too long.
ramacharitamanas::2280.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands before Ram in Ayodhya, refusing any comfort that comes without Ram. After pleading to go with him and serve him, he says that if Ram remains away for fourteen years, his own life will not survive. The verse carries the ache of loyal love at the edge of separation.
ramacharitamanas::2280.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after the one person you trust leaves the room. Work and noise continue, but your attention stays with the absence. Bharat knows that kind of devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2280.insight: It shifts loyalty from convenience to life-or-death belonging.

ramacharitamanas::2281.verse_sanskrit: मोहि मग चलत न होइहि हारी। छिनु छिनु चरन सरोज निहारी॥ सबहि भाँति पिय सेवा करिहौं। मारग जनित सकल श्रम हरिहौं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2281.verse_hindi: क्षण-क्षण में आपके चरण कमलों को देखते रहने से मुझे मार्ग चलने में थकावट न होगी। हे प्रियतम! मैं सभी प्रकार से आपकी सेवा करूँगी और मार्ग चलने से होने वाली सारी थकावट को दूर कर दूँगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2281.english_translation: Looking at your lotus feet every moment, I will not tire on the road. Beloved, I will serve you in every way and remove all weariness from the journey.
ramacharitamanas::2281.translation_literal: मोहि (to me) / मग (on the road) / चलत (while walking) / न (not) / होइहि (will be) / हारी (tired) / छिनु छिनु (moment by moment) / चरन (feet) / सरोज (lotus) / निहारी (seeing) / सबहि भाँति (in every way) / पिय (beloved) / सेवा (service) / करिहौं (I will do) / मारग (path/journey) / जनित (caused by) / सकल (all) / श्रम (fatigue) / हरिहौं (I will remove)
ramacharitamanas::2281.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2281.essence: Love makes the hard road lighter through service.
ramacharitamanas::2281.simple_meaning: Sita says she will keep looking at Ram’s feet as they travel, serve him in every way, and ease the fatigue of the journey.
ramacharitamanas::2281.simple_insight: Love becomes practical when it notices what the other person needs and quietly helps.
ramacharitamanas::2281.detailed_meaning: Sita is leaving Ayodhya with Ram and Lakshman. On the road into exile, she offers not speeches but care: she will keep her eyes on Ram, serve him in every way, and relieve the strain of travel. This is love expressed as service.
ramacharitamanas::2281.modern_relevance: You’re on a long train ride with someone carrying more than they admit. You stop talking about yourself, notice their tired shoulders, and quietly make the trip easier. That is the kind of care Sita models.
ramacharitamanas::2281.insight: It shifts devotion into concrete help: attention, service, and relief of burden.

ramacharitamanas::2282.verse_sanskrit: पाय पखारि बैठि तरु छाहीं। करिहउँ बाउ मुदित मन माहीं॥ श्रम कन सहित स्याम तनु देखें। कहँ दुख समउ प्रानपति पेखें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2282.verse_hindi: आपके पैर धोकर, पेड़ों की छाया में बैठकर, मन में प्रसन्न होकर हवा करूँगी (पंखा झलूँगी)। पसीने की बूँदों सहित श्याम शरीर को देखकर प्राणपति के दर्शन करते हुए दुःख के लिए मुझे अवकाश ही कहाँ रहेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2282.english_translation: After washing your feet, I will sit in the shade of a tree and gladly fan you. Seeing your dark body covered with beads of sweat, where will sorrow find room when I behold my beloved lord?
ramacharitamanas::2282.translation_literal: पाय (feet) / पखारि (washing) / बैठि (sitting) / तरु (tree) / छाहीं (shade) / करिहउँ (I will do) / बाउ (fanning with a fan) / मुदित मन माहीं (with a joyful mind) / श्रम (sweat / fatigue) / कन (drops) / सहित (with) / स्याम (dark) / तनु (body) / देखें (seeing) / कहँ (where) / दुख (sorrow) / समउ (place / room) / प्रानपति (lord of life) / पेखें (seeing)
ramacharitamanas::2282.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2282.essence: Love makes service feel like rest.
ramacharitamanas::2282.simple_meaning: Sita says she will serve Ram lovingly by washing his feet, fanning him in the shade, and finding joy in caring for him. Seeing his tired body brings her no sorrow, only devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2282.simple_insight: Love turns service into joy, even in hardship.
ramacharitamanas::2282.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita speaks with deep tenderness about life beside Ram in exile. She imagines washing his feet, sitting under a tree, and fanning him with a happy heart. His sweat and fatigue only increase her devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2282.modern_relevance: You wipe the sweat from someone’s forehead after a long hospital visit, and the fatigue disappears from your own body. Care stops feeling like sacrifice when love is real.
ramacharitamanas::2282.insight: It shifts service from obligation to delight, showing that devotion can erase the sense of burden.

ramacharitamanas::2283.verse_sanskrit: सम महि तृन तरुपल्लव डासी। पाय पलोटिहि सब निसि दासी॥ बार बार मृदु मूरति जोही। लागिहि तात बयारि न मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2283.verse_hindi: समतल भूमि पर घास और पेड़ों के पत्ते बिछाकर यह दासी रातभर आपके चरण दबावेगी। बार-बार आपकी कोमल मूर्ति को देखकर मुझको गरम हवा भी न लगेगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2283.english_translation: I will spread grass, leaves, and tender shoots on the ground. This servant will massage your feet all night. Looking again and again at your gentle form, even hot wind will not touch me.
ramacharitamanas::2283.translation_literal: सम (level) / महि (earth) / तृन (grass) / तरुपल्लव (tree-leaves and tender shoots) / डासी (servant) / पाय (feet) / पलोटिहि (will massage) / सब (all) / निसि (night) / दासी (servant-woman)॥ बार बार (again and again) / मृदु (soft) / मूरति (form) / जोही (seeing) / लागिहि (will feel) / तात (father/Beloved) / बयारि (wind) / न (not) / मोही (to me)॥
ramacharitamanas::2283.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2283.essence: Devotion turns hardship into service and nearness into comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2283.simple_meaning: Sita offers to make the ground soft, massage Ram's feet all night, and stay comforted just by seeing his gentle form.
ramacharitamanas::2283.simple_insight: Love becomes service when comfort matters less than closeness.
ramacharitamanas::2283.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita is speaking to Ram as exile begins. She imagines the forest not as hardship but as a place to serve him directly: soften the ground, tend his feet, and endure the night by keeping sight of him.
ramacharitamanas::2283.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone in a hospital corridor, folding a jacket into a pillow and forgetting your own discomfort. Love stops asking for ease and starts asking, 'What do you need right now?'
ramacharitamanas::2283.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling to action: closeness is proven by care, not sentiment.

ramacharitamanas::2284.verse_sanskrit: को प्रभु सँग मोहि चितवनिहारा। सिंघबधुहि जिमि ससक सिआरा॥ मैं सुकुमारि नाथ बन जोगू। तुम्हहि उचित तप मो कहुँ भोगू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2284.verse_hindi: प्रभु के साथ (रहते) मेरी ओर (आँख उठाकर) देखने वाला कौन है (अर्थात कोई नहीं देख सकता)! जैसे सिंह की स्त्री (सिंहनी) को खरगोश और सियार नहीं देख सकते। मैं सुकुमारी हूँ और नाथ वन के योग्य हैं? आपको तो तपस्या उचित है और मुझको विषय भोग? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2284.english_translation: Who can look at me with the Lord present? A hare and a jackal cannot face a lioness. I am delicate, my lord belongs in the forest. You are fit for austerity; I am fit for comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2284.translation_literal: को (who) प्रभु (lord) सँग (with) मोहि (me) चितवनिहारा (one who looks) / सिंघबधुहि (lioness) जिमि (like) ससक (hare) सिआरा (jackal) / मैं (I) सुकुमारि (delicate) नाथ (lord) बन (forest) जोगू (fit) / तुम्हहि (to you) उचित (proper) तप (austerity) मो कहुँ (for me) भोगू (comfort, enjoyment)
ramacharitamanas::2284.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2284.essence: Love makes itself small so the beloved can bear the harder road.
ramacharitamanas::2284.simple_meaning: Sita says she is too delicate for forest hardship and that Ram belongs in the forest life, while she belongs to comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2284.simple_insight: Love can speak by shrinking the self and lifting the other person’s burden.
ramacharitamanas::2284.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita pleads to accompany Ram into exile. She insists that no one can even look at her properly in his presence, and that her soft life suits comfort, not forest austerity. Her words are a loving attempt to make the separation easier.
ramacharitamanas::2284.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love pack for a hard move, a risky job, or a long sacrifice, and your first instinct is to downplay yourself so they can go lighter.
ramacharitamanas::2284.insight: It shifts the mind from claiming closeness to offering support without self-importance.

ramacharitamanas::2285.verse_sanskrit: ऐसेउ बचन कठोर सुनि जौं न हृदउ बिलगान। तौ प्रभु बिषम बियोग दुख सहिहहिं पावँर प्रान ॥
ramacharitamanas::2285.verse_hindi: ऐसे कठोर वचन सुनकर भी जब मेरा हृदय न फटा तो, हे प्रभु! (मालूम होता है) ये पामर प्राण आपके वियोग का भीषण दुःख सहेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2285.english_translation: Even after hearing such harsh words, if my heart did not break, then, O Lord, these worthless breaths will surely endure the terrible pain of separation from you.
ramacharitamanas::2285.translation_literal: ऐसेउ (even so) / बचन (words) / कठोर (harsh) / सुनि (having heard) / जौं (if) / न (not) / हृदउ (heart) / बिलगान (broke apart) / तौ (then) / प्रभु (Lord) / बिषम (terrible) / बियोग (separation) / दुख (pain) / सहिहहिं (will bear) / पावँर (worthless) / प्रान (breaths)
ramacharitamanas::2285.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2285.essence: If the smaller wound holds, the greater sorrow can also be borne.
ramacharitamanas::2285.simple_meaning: Sita says that if harsh words did not break her heart, then she can endure the far greater pain of being separated from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2285.simple_insight: Love becomes steadier when it has already survived hurt.
ramacharitamanas::2285.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita is pleading to go with Ram into exile. She has just heard painful objections, yet her resolve does not collapse. She measures her strength against the greater suffering ahead: separation from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2285.modern_relevance: You were misunderstood in the meeting, and it stung. But the deeper test is whether you can still stay loyal to what matters when the cost gets heavier.
ramacharitamanas::2285.insight: It shifts the mind from fearing discomfort to trusting endurance born of love.

ramacharitamanas::2286.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि सीय बिकल भइ भारी। बचन बियोगु न सकी सँभारी॥ देखि दसा रघुपति जियँ जाना। हठि राखें नहिं राखिहि प्राना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2286.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर सीताजी बहुत ही व्याकुल हो गईं। वे वचन के वियोग को भी न सम्हाल सकीं। (अर्थात शरीर से वियोग की बात तो अलग रही, वचन से भी वियोग की बात सुनकर वे अत्यन्त विकल हो गईं।) उनकी यह दशा देखकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने अपने जी में जान लिया कि हठपूर्वक इन्हें यहाँ रखने से ये प्राणों को न रखेंगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2286.english_translation: Sita became deeply distressed after speaking. She could not bear even the thought of separation. Seeing her condition, Raghupati understood in his heart that if he kept her there by force, she would not keep her life.
ramacharitamanas::2286.translation_literal: अस कहि (thus speaking) / सीय (Sita) / बिकल भइ (became distressed) / भारी (greatly) / बचन (word) / बियोगु (separation) / न (not) / सकी (could) / सँभारी (bear)॥ / देखि (seeing) / दसा (condition) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / जियँ (in heart) / जाना (understood) / हठि (by force) / राखें (keeping) / नहिं (not) / राखिहि (will keep) / प्राना (life-breaths) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2286.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2286.essence: Forcing love destroys the one you mean to keep.
ramacharitamanas::2286.simple_meaning: Sita is overwhelmed by the pain of separation. Ram sees that forcing her to stay would cost her life.
ramacharitamanas::2286.simple_insight: Love can be so complete that separation feels unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2286.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita has just spoken of going into exile with Ram and the pain of separation. Her distress becomes so intense that Ram immediately sees the truth: if he forces her to remain behind, she will not survive it.
ramacharitamanas::2286.modern_relevance: You watch someone go quiet after bad news, and you know the argument is over. Some bonds are so deep that force only breaks what love is trying to protect.
ramacharitamanas::2286.insight: It shifts attention from obedience to compassion: Ram reads Sita’s state and responds to what preserves life.

ramacharitamanas::2287.verse_sanskrit: कहेउ कृपाल भानुकुलनाथा। परिहरि सोचु चलहु बन साथा॥ नहिं बिषाद कर अवसरु आजू। बेगि करहु बन गवन समाजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2287.verse_hindi: तब कृपालु, सूर्यकुल के स्वामी श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने कहा कि सोच छोड़कर मेरे साथ वन को चलो। आज विषाद करने का अवसर नहीं है। तुरंत वनगमन की तैयारी करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2287.english_translation: Then the compassionate Lord of the Sun dynasty said, "Set aside sorrow and come with me to the forest. Today is no time for grief. Quickly make ready for the journey into the forest."
ramacharitamanas::2287.translation_literal: कहेउ (said) / कृपाल (the compassionate one) / भानुकुलनाथा (lord of the Sun dynasty) / परिहरि (setting aside) / सोचु (sorrow) / चलहु (come/go) / बन (forest) / साथा (with me) ॥ / नहिं (not) / बिषाद (grief) / कर (of) / अवसरु (occasion/time) / आजू (today) / बेगि (quickly) / करहु (do/make) / बन गवन (forest-going) / समाजू (preparations) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2287.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2287.essence: Grief must wait when dharma calls you forward.
ramacharitamanas::2287.simple_meaning: Ram asks everyone to drop sorrow, come with him to the forest, and prepare quickly. The moment calls for action, not grief.
ramacharitamanas::2287.simple_insight: When life demands a hard step, clarity is kinder than collapse.
ramacharitamanas::2287.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, exile has been spoken and the family is reeling. Ram, calm and compassionate, refuses to let the moment dissolve into despair. He tells Sita and the others to set sorrow aside and prepare at once for the forest journey.
ramacharitamanas::2287.modern_relevance: The house is quiet after bad news, and everyone is frozen in shock. One person still has to pack the bag, call the driver, and keep the next step moving.
ramacharitamanas::2287.insight: It shifts attention from emotional paralysis to the next necessary act.

ramacharitamanas::2288.verse_sanskrit: कहि प्रिय बचन प्रिया समुझाई। लगे मातु पद आसिष पाई॥ बेगि प्रजा दुख मेटब आई। जननी निठुर बिसरि जनि जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2288.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने प्रिय वचन कहकर प्रियतमा सीताजी को समझाया। फिर माता के पैरों लगकर आशीर्वाद प्राप्त किया। (माता ने कहा-) बेटा! जल्दी लौटकर प्रजा के दुःख को मिटाना और यह निठुर माता तुम्हें भूल न जाए! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2288.english_translation: Speaking tender words, Ram comforted Sita. Then he bowed at his mother's feet and received her blessing. "Return quickly and remove the people's sorrow, and may this harsh mother not be forgotten by you."
ramacharitamanas::2288.translation_literal: कहि (speaking) / प्रिय (loving) / बचन (words) / प्रिया (beloved) / समुझाई (having comforted) / लगे (began) / मातु (mother's) / पद (feet) / आसिष (blessing) / पाई (having received) / बेगि (quickly) / प्रजा (people) / दुख (sorrow) / मेटब (to remove) / आई (come) / जननी (mother) / निठुर (harsh) / बिसरि (forgot) / जनि (do not) / जाई (go)
ramacharitamanas::2288.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2288.essence: Love speaks softly, but duty still sends him back.
ramacharitamanas::2288.simple_meaning: Ram comforts Sita, bows to his mother, and receives a blessing to return quickly and relieve the people's suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2288.simple_insight: Even in grief, duty remains clear: comfort the loved ones, honor the elders, and return to serve.
ramacharitamanas::2288.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is leaving for exile and the family is breaking apart. He reassures Sita, then touches his mother's feet for blessing. Kausalya blesses him to come back soon and ease the people's sorrow, turning private pain into public duty.
ramacharitamanas::2288.modern_relevance: You leave the hospital after saying goodbye to your mother, then still have to show up for the work that cannot wait. Grief does not cancel responsibility.
ramacharitamanas::2288.insight: It teaches you to honor love and obligation at the same time, without letting emotion erase action.

ramacharitamanas::2289.verse_sanskrit: फिरिहि दसा बिधि बहुरि कि मोरी। देखिहउँ नयन मनोहर जोरी। सुदिन सुघरी तात कब होइहि। जननी जिअत बदन बिधु जोइहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2289.verse_hindi: हे विधाता! क्या मेरी दशा भी फिर पलटेगी? क्या अपने नेत्रों से मैं इस मनोहर जोड़ी को फिर देख पाऊँगी? हे पुत्र! वह सुंदर दिन और शुभ घड़ी कब होगी जब तुम्हारी जननी जीते जी तुम्हारा चाँद सा मुखड़ा फिर देखेगी! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2289.english_translation: O Fate, will my condition ever change again? Will I see that lovely pair again with my own eyes? O son, when will that beautiful day and fortunate hour come when your mother, while still alive, sees your moonlike face again?
ramacharitamanas::2289.translation_literal: फिरिहि (will return) / दसा (condition, fate) / बिधि (fate, divine order) / बहुरि (again) / कि (whether) / मोरी (my) / देखिहउँ (I will see) / नयन (with eyes) / मनोहर (lovely) / जोरी (pair, together) / सुदिन (auspicious day) / सुघरी (good, fortunate) / तात (son) / कब (when) / होइहि (will it be) / जननी (mother) / जिअत (while living) / बदन (face) / बिधु (moon) / जोइहि (will see)
ramacharitamanas::2289.speaker: Kaushalya
ramacharitamanas::2289.essence: Separation turns even hope into a prayer for one more sight.
ramacharitamanas::2289.simple_meaning: Kaushalya longs to see Ram and Sita together again. She wonders if her own fate will ever turn, and if she will live to see Ram's face again.
ramacharitamanas::2289.simple_insight: Love can make waiting feel sacred, even when it hurts.
ramacharitamanas::2289.detailed_meaning: Kaushalya, just after Ram has been sent into exile, pours out her grief at the sight of her son and daughter-in-law leaving. She is not debating doctrine; she is a mother fearing she may never see Ram's beautiful face again.
ramacharitamanas::2289.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love pack a bag for a long absence, and the room suddenly feels too quiet. Kaushalya's words carry that ache of not knowing when, or whether, the reunion will come.
ramacharitamanas::2289.insight: It shifts attention from political loss to the intimate cost of separation.

ramacharitamanas::2290.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि बच्छ कहि लालु कहि रघुपति रघुबर तात। कबहिं बोलाइ लगाइ हियँ हरषि निरखिहउँ गात ॥
ramacharitamanas::2290.verse_hindi: हे तात! 'वत्स' कहकर, 'लाल' कहकर, 'रघुपति' कहकर, 'रघुवर' कहकर, मैं फिर कब तुम्हें बुलाकर हृदय से लगाऊँगी और हर्षित होकर तुम्हारे अंगों को देखूँगी! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2290.english_translation: Mother says, 'Beloved son, when will I again call you by these names, hold you to my heart, and joyfully behold your body?'
ramacharitamanas::2290.translation_literal: बहुरि (again) / बच्छ (son) / कहि (saying) / लालु (dear child) / कहि (saying) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu line) / रघुबर (best of the Raghu line) / तात (dear son) / कबहिं (when) / बोलाइ (calling) / लगाइ (embracing) / हियँ (to the heart) / हरषि (with joy) / निरखिहउँ (I will behold) / गात (body)
ramacharitamanas::2290.speaker: Kaushalya
ramacharitamanas::2290.essence: Separation turns ordinary affection into aching devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2290.simple_meaning: Kaushalya longs to call Ram by affectionate names, hold him close, and see him again. Her love is so deep that separation feels unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2290.simple_insight: Love becomes most visible when it has to wait.
ramacharitamanas::2290.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is preparing to leave Ayodhya, and Kaushalya cannot stop herself from grieving. She imagines the simple acts of motherly love she may no longer get to do: calling him, embracing him, looking at him with joy.
ramacharitamanas::2290.modern_relevance: You stand at the airport watching someone you love walk toward security, and suddenly the ordinary words you used every day feel sacred. Distance makes affection audible.
ramacharitamanas::2290.insight: It shifts the mind from taking closeness for granted to feeling its preciousness before it is gone.

ramacharitamanas::2291.verse_sanskrit: लखि सनेह कातरि महतारी। बचनु न आव बिकल भइ भारी॥ राम प्रबोधु कीन्ह बिधि नाना। समउ सनेहु न जाइ बखाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2291.verse_hindi: यह देखकर कि माता स्नेह के मारे अधीर हो गई हैं और इतनी अधिक व्याकुल हैं कि मुँह से वचन नहीं निकलता। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने अनेक प्रकार से उन्हें समझाया। वह समय और स्नेह वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2291.english_translation: Seeing his mother overcome with love and unable to speak, Ram comforted her in many ways. That moment and that affection cannot be described.
ramacharitamanas::2291.translation_literal: लखि (seeing) / सनेह (love) / कातरि (helpless, overwhelmed) / महतारी (mother) / बचनु (words) / न (not) / आव (come) / बिकल (distressed) / भइ (became) / भारी (greatly) / राम (Ram) / प्रबोधु (comfort, counsel) / कीन्ह (did) / बिधि (ways) / नाना (many) / समउ (moment, occasion) / सनेहु (love) / न (not) / जाइ (can be) / बखाना (described)
ramacharitamanas::2291.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2291.essence: Love can leave even comfort speechless.
ramacharitamanas::2291.simple_meaning: Ram sees his mother so overwhelmed with love that she cannot speak, and he comforts her in many ways. The depth of that moment is beyond words.
ramacharitamanas::2291.simple_insight: Some love is too full for language. Presence and comfort matter more than explanation.
ramacharitamanas::2291.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the family is breaking under the pain of separation. Kaushalya is so overcome by love for Ram that she cannot speak. Ram responds with gentle reassurance, but even the poet admits the feeling in that room cannot be fully described.
ramacharitamanas::2291.modern_relevance: You stand at a train platform watching a parent try not to cry, and no perfect sentence appears. In some moments, the kindest thing is not explanation but steady presence.
ramacharitamanas::2291.insight: It teaches you to meet overwhelming emotion with calm reassurance instead of forcing words.

ramacharitamanas::2292.verse_sanskrit: तब जानकी सासु पग लागी। सुनिअ माय मैं परम अभागी॥ सेवा समय दैअँ बनु दीन्हा। मोर मनोरथु सफल न कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2292.verse_hindi: तब जानकीजी सास के पाँव लगीं और बोलीं- हे माता! सुनिए, मैं बड़ी ही अभागिनी हूँ। आपकी सेवा करने के समय दैव ने मुझे वनवास दे दिया। मेरा मनोरथ सफल न किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2292.english_translation: Then Janaki touched her mother-in-law's feet and said, "Listen, Mother, I am utterly unfortunate. Fate gave me exile just when I could serve you. It did not fulfill my wish."
ramacharitamanas::2292.translation_literal: तब (then) / जानकी (Janaki) / सासु (mother-in-law) / पग (feet) / लागी (touched) / सुनिअ (listen) / माय (Mother) / मैं (I) / परम (utterly) / अभागी (unfortunate) / सेवा (service) / समय (time) / दैअँ (by fate) / बनु (forest exile) / दीन्हा (given) / मोर (my) / मनोरथु (wish) / सफल (fulfilled) / न (not) / कीन्हा (made)
ramacharitamanas::2292.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2292.essence: Blocked service becomes its own grief.
ramacharitamanas::2292.simple_meaning: Sita bows to her mother-in-law and says she feels unlucky because exile stopped her from serving properly.
ramacharitamanas::2292.simple_insight: Even sorrow can be shaped by humility when service is what you wanted most.
ramacharitamanas::2292.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita stands before Kaushalya after Ram's exile has torn the family apart. She bows at her mother-in-law's feet and speaks with aching respect, grieving that the forest took away her chance to serve in the house she had entered as a daughter-in-law.
ramacharitamanas::2292.modern_relevance: You finally get the chance to care for an elder, a parent-in-law, or a mentor — then distance, illness, or family conflict blocks it. The grief is not only loss; it is the frustration of unspent love.
ramacharitamanas::2292.insight: It shifts the mind from self-pity to service: the pain is not about status, but about blocked duty.

ramacharitamanas::2293.verse_sanskrit: तजब छोभु जनि छाड़िअ छोहू। करमु कठिन कछु दोसु न मोहू॥ सुनिसिय बचन सासु अकुलानी। दसा कवनि बिधि कहौं बखानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2293.verse_hindi: आप क्षोभ का त्याग कर दें, परन्तु कृपा न छोड़िएगा। कर्म की गति कठिन है, मुझे भी कुछ दोष नहीं है। सीताजी के वचन सुनकर सास व्याकुल हो गईं। उनकी दशा को मैं किस प्रकार बखान कर कहूँ! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2293.english_translation: Please do not let distress drive you away from affection. Fate is hard; I bear no blame. Hearing Sita’s words, her mother-in-law became distraught. How can I even describe her condition?
ramacharitamanas::2293.translation_literal: तजब (then) / छोभु (distress) / जनि (do not) / छाड़िअ (leave) / छोहू (affection, tenderness) / करमु (fate, the force of action) / कठिन (hard) / कछु (some) / दोसु (fault) / न (not) / मोहू (mine) / सुनिसिय (hearing) / बचन (words) / सासु (mother-in-law) / अकुलानी (became agitated) / दसा (condition) / कवनि (which) / बिधि (way) / कहौं (shall I say) / बखानी (describe)
ramacharitamanas::2293.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2293.simple_meaning: Sita asks her mother-in-law not to let pain destroy affection. She accepts that fate is difficult and says she is not at fault. The mother-in-law is overwhelmed by emotion.
ramacharitamanas::2293.simple_insight: Even in painful separation, love can stay intact without blame.
ramacharitamanas::2293.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita stands before Kaushalya after being told she must leave for the forest. She speaks gently, refusing anger or self-pity, and tries to protect family love even as exile tears the household apart.
ramacharitamanas::2293.modern_relevance: You are packing a bag in silence after a family argument, trying not to turn hurt into hatred. Sita shows how to keep tenderness alive even when life feels unfair.
ramacharitamanas::2293.insight: It teaches you to separate suffering from blame, so affection can survive hardship.

ramacharitamanas::2294.verse_sanskrit: बारहिं बार लाइ उर लीन्ही। धरि धीरजु सिख आसिष दीन्ही॥ अचल होउ अहिवातु तुम्हारा। जब लगि गंग जमुन जल धारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2294.verse_hindi: उन्होंने सीताजी को बार-बार हृदय से लगाया और धीरज धरकर शिक्षा दी और आशीर्वाद दिया कि जब तक गंगाजी और यमुनाजी में जल की धारा बहे, तब तक तुम्हारा सुहाग अचल रहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2294.english_translation: She drew Sita into her heart again and again, gave her counsel with patience, and blessed her: may your married bond remain unbroken as long as the Ganga and Yamuna keep flowing.
ramacharitamanas::2294.translation_literal: बारहिं बार (again and again) / लाइ (bringing) / उर (heart/chest) / लीन्ही (took) / धरि (holding) / धीरजु (patience) / सिख (instruction) / आसिष (blessing) / दीन्ही (gave) / अचल (unshaken) / होउ (may it be) / अहिवातु (married bond) / तुम्हारा (your) / जब लगि (as long as) / गंग (Ganga) / जमुन (Yamuna) / जल (water) / धारा (stream/flow)
ramacharitamanas::2294.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2294.essence: Tender blessing can hold a person steady when separation begins.
ramacharitamanas::2294.simple_meaning: Sita's mother-in-law embraced her repeatedly, steadied her with kind words, and blessed her long married life.
ramacharitamanas::2294.simple_insight: Love can be steady, tender, and protective even in grief.
ramacharitamanas::2294.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Sita is leaving for the forest and her mother-in-law cannot stop the pain. She holds Sita to her chest again and again, then gives her calm counsel and a blessing for enduring marital union.
ramacharitamanas::2294.modern_relevance: At an airport gate, your mother keeps pulling you into one last hug before you leave for a hard move. She cannot remove the pain, but she can steady you for the road.
ramacharitamanas::2294.insight: It shifts attention from loss to blessing, showing how care can strengthen someone before separation.

ramacharitamanas::2295.verse_sanskrit: सीतहि सासु आसीस सिख दीन्हि अनेक प्रकार। चली नाइ पद पदुम सिरु अति हित बारहिं बार ॥
ramacharitamanas::2295.verse_hindi: सीताजी को सास ने अनेकों प्रकार से आशीर्वाद और शिक्षाएँ दीं और वे (सीताजी) बड़े ही प्रेम से बार-बार चरणकमलों में सिर नवाकर चलीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2295.english_translation: Sita's mother-in-law gave her many blessings and teachings. Sita bowed her head again and again to the lotus feet and departed with deep affection.
ramacharitamanas::2295.translation_literal: सीतहि (to Sita) / सासु (mother-in-law) / आसीस (blessings) / सिख (teachings) / दीन्हि (gave) / अनेक प्रकार (many kinds) / चली (departed) / नाइ (bowing) / पद पदुम (lotus feet) / सिरु (head) / अति हित (with deep affection) / बारहिं बार (again and again)
ramacharitamanas::2295.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2295.essence: Deep affection bows before it walks away.
ramacharitamanas::2295.simple_meaning: Sita receives blessings and guidance from her mother-in-law, then leaves with repeated bows and deep affection.
ramacharitamanas::2295.simple_insight: Respect can be tender, not stiff. Love often shows itself in repeated small acts of reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2295.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita is leaving behind the women of the household as exile begins. Her mother-in-law blesses and instructs her, and Sita responds with repeated bows, showing the tenderness and dignity of this painful departure.
ramacharitamanas::2295.modern_relevance: You leave your childhood home after one last meal, and every goodbye feels heavier than the last. Quiet respect and repeated gratitude can hold a painful departure together.
ramacharitamanas::2295.insight: It teaches you to leave with humility, carrying love in your conduct rather than in words alone.

ramacharitamanas::2296.verse_sanskrit: समाचार जब लछिमन पाए। ब्याकुल बिलख बदन उठि धाए॥ कंप पुलक तन नयन सनीरा। गहे चरन अति प्रेम अधीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2296.verse_hindi: जब लक्ष्मणजी ने समाचार पाए, तब वे व्याकुल होकर उदास मुँह उठ दौड़े। शरीर काँप रहा है, रोमांच हो रहा है, नेत्र आँसुओं से भरे हैं। प्रेम से अत्यन्त अधीर होकर उन्होंने श्री रामजी के चरण पकड़ लिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2296.english_translation: When Lakshman heard the news, he rushed up in anguish, face clouded with grief. His body trembled, his hair stood on end, his eyes filled with tears. Overcome by love, he seized Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::2296.translation_literal: समाचार (news) / जब (when) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / पाए (received) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / बिलख (grieving) / बदन (face) / उठि (rising) / धाए (ran) / कंप (trembling) / पुलक (horripilation) / तन (body) / नयन (eyes) / सनीरा (full of water/tears) / गहे (grasped) / चरन (feet) / अति (very) / प्रेम (love) / अधीरा (restless/impatient)
ramacharitamanas::2296.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2296.essence: Love for Ram makes Lakshman rush forward in helpless grief.
ramacharitamanas::2296.simple_meaning: Lakshman hears the news and runs to Ram in grief and love, unable to stay still. His body shows his emotion before he can speak.
ramacharitamanas::2296.simple_insight: Love can make grief physical. The heart moves the body before words arrive.
ramacharitamanas::2296.detailed_meaning: Lakshman has just heard the news in Ayodhyakand, and his first response is not speech but motion. He rushes to Ram with trembling limbs and tears, showing how deeply he is bound to Ram and how powerless he feels before the coming loss.
ramacharitamanas::2296.modern_relevance: You read a message that changes everything, and your hands start shaking before you even understand it. Some bonds hit the body first, then the mind.
ramacharitamanas::2296.insight: It shows devotion as an immediate bodily response, not a polished emotion. Grief and loyalty arrive together and drive action.

ramacharitamanas::2297.verse_sanskrit: कहि न सकत कछु चितवत ठाढ़े। मीनु दीन जनु जल तें काढ़े॥ सोचु हृदयँ बिधि का होनिहारा। सबु सुखु सुकृतु सिरान हमारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2297.verse_hindi: वे कुछ कह नहीं सकते, खड़े-खड़े देख रहे हैं। (ऐसे दीन हो रहे हैं) मानो जल से निकाले जाने पर मछली दीन हो रही हो। हृदय में यह सोच है कि हे विधाता! क्या होने वाला है? क्या हमारा सब सुख और पुण्य पूरा हो गया? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2297.english_translation: They cannot say anything; they stand there staring. They are helpless like a fish taken out of water. Their hearts worry: what will fate bring now? Has all our happiness and merit been spent?
ramacharitamanas::2297.translation_literal: कहि (saying) / न (not) / सकत (able) / कछु (anything) / चितवत (staring) / ठाढ़े (standing) / मीनु (fish) / दीन (helpless) / जनु (as if) / जल (water) / तें (from) / काढ़े (pulled out) / सोचु (worry) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिधि (fate) / का (what) / होनिहारा (about to happen) / सबु (all) / सुखु (happiness) / सुकृतु (merit) / सिरान (finished) / हमारा (our)
ramacharitamanas::2297.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2297.essence: Sudden grief leaves people speechless and afraid of what comes next.
ramacharitamanas::2297.simple_meaning: They stand frozen, unable to speak, overwhelmed by dread. Their hearts fear that everything good has run out and something painful is about to happen.
ramacharitamanas::2297.simple_insight: Shock can leave even strong people wordless, with only fear and helplessness left.
ramacharitamanas::2297.detailed_meaning: Laxman has just rushed in after hearing the news, and the household is stunned. People stand speechless, staring, feeling as helpless as a fish out of water. In that charged silence, fear rises: what will happen next, and has all their good fortune ended?
ramacharitamanas::2297.modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after one message changes everything. Nobody knows what to say, but everyone feels the same knot in the chest: something has broken, and the next moment may hurt.
ramacharitamanas::2297.insight: It captures the freeze that follows sudden loss and the mind’s rush to fear the worst.

ramacharitamanas::2298.verse_sanskrit: मो कहुँ काह कहब रघुनाथा। रखिहहिं भवन कि लेहहिं साथा॥ राम बिलोकि बंधु कर जोरें। देह गेहसब सन तृनु तोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2298.verse_hindi: मुझको श्री रघुनाथजी क्या कहेंगे? घर पर रखेंगे या साथ ले चलेंगे? श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने भाई लक्ष्मण को हाथ जोड़े और शरीर तथा घर सभी से नाता तोड़े हुए खड़े देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2298.english_translation: What will Ragunath say to me? Will he keep me at home or take me along? Ram saw his brother with folded hands, standing free of body, home, and all possessions.
ramacharitamanas::2298.translation_literal: मो कहुँ (to me) / काह (what) / कहब (will say) / रघुनाथा (Raghunatha) / रखिहहिं (will keep) / भवन (home) / कि (or) / लेहहिं (will take) / साथा (along) ॥ राम (Ram) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बंधु (brother) / कर जोरें (with hands joined) / देह (body) / गेह (house) / सब (all) / सन (with) / तृनु (straw) / तोरें (broken off) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2298.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2298.essence: True loyalty drops body and home without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::2298.simple_meaning: Lakshman wonders whether Ram will keep him at home or take him along. He stands ready to give up body, house, and everything else for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2298.simple_insight: Love becomes clear when nothing is held back.
ramacharitamanas::2298.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Lakshman is shaken by the exile crisis and stands before Ram in complete readiness. He has already cut loose from comfort, home, and even his own body’s claims. The moment shows devotion turning into total duty.
ramacharitamanas::2298.modern_relevance: You are packing a bag for someone you love and realize you would go wherever they need you. No bargaining, no conditions — just readiness.
ramacharitamanas::2298.insight: It shifts loyalty from comfort and possession to complete readiness for service.

ramacharitamanas::2299.verse_sanskrit: बोले बचनु राम नय नागर। सील सनेह सरल सुख सागर॥ तात प्रेम बस जनि कदराहू। समुझि हृदयँ परिनाम उछाहू ॥
