ramacharitamanas::2299.verse_hindi: तब नीति में निपुण और शील, स्नेह, सरलता और सुख के समुद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी वचन बोले- हे तात! परिणाम में होने वाले आनंद को हृदय में समझकर तुम प्रेमवश अधीर मत होओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2299.english_translation: Then Ram, skilled in wise conduct, spoke. He was an ocean of character, affection, simplicity, and joy: “Father, do not be distressed by love. Understand in your heart the joy that will come at the end, and do not lose heart.”
ramacharitamanas::2299.translation_literal: बोले (spoke) / बचनु (words) / राम (Ram) / नय (wise conduct) / नागर (skilled) / सील (character) / सनेह (affection) / सरल (simple) / सुख (joy) / सागर (ocean) / तात (father) / प्रेम (love) / बस (under the power of) / जनि (do not) / कदराहू (be distressed) / समुझि (understanding) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / परिनाम (result/end) / उछाहू (joy/excitement)
ramacharitamanas::2299.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2299.essence: Affection stays clear when it remembers the good ahead.
ramacharitamanas::2299.simple_meaning: Ram tells his father not to panic in love-driven distress. He asks him to remember the good that will come in the end and stay steady.
ramacharitamanas::2299.simple_insight: Love does not have to become panic. Steadiness can protect tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::2299.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is shattered by the exile crisis, and the family stands frozen in grief. Ram answers with calm tenderness, urging his father not to be overwhelmed by emotion but to hold the larger good in mind.
ramacharitamanas::2299.modern_relevance: You get the message that your family group chat has gone silent after bad news. Before replying in fear, you breathe and remember that love can stay steady without collapsing.
ramacharitamanas::2299.insight: It teaches you to hold emotion without letting it overturn judgment.

ramacharitamanas::2300.verse_sanskrit: मातु पिता गुरु स्वामि सिख सिर धरि करहिं सुभायँ। लहेउ लाभु तिन्ह जनम कर नतरु जनमु जग जायँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2300.verse_hindi: जो लोग माता, पिता, गुरु और स्वामी की शिक्षा को स्वाभाविक ही सिर चढ़ाकर उसका पालन करते हैं, उन्होंने ही जन्म लेने का लाभ पाया है, नहीं तो जगत में जन्म व्यर्थ ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2300.english_translation: Those who naturally place the teachings of their mother, father, teacher, and master above their own head truly gain the value of birth; otherwise, life in the world is wasted.
ramacharitamanas::2300.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / पिता (father) / गुरु (teacher) / स्वामि (master) / सिख (teaching) / सिर धरि (placing on the head) / करहिं (they do) / सुभायँ (naturally) / लहेउ (obtained) / लाभु (benefit) / तिन्ह (those) / जनम कर (of birth) / नतरु (otherwise) / जनमु (birth) / जग (world) / जायँ (goes/wasted)
ramacharitamanas::2300.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2300.essence: Life becomes worthwhile when guidance is placed above pride.
ramacharitamanas::2300.simple_meaning: A person gains real value from life by naturally honoring the guidance of mother, father, teacher, and master. Without that, simply being born achieves nothing.
ramacharitamanas::2300.simple_insight: Respecting guidance turns life into something meaningful instead of merely lived.
ramacharitamanas::2300.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is teaching Lakshman before exile. He says that a child who naturally follows the guidance of mother, father, teacher, and master has truly benefited from birth. The point is not ritual obedience, but living with humility and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2300.modern_relevance: Your mother repeats the same warning, your mentor gives one hard truth, and your first impulse is to dismiss both. This verse asks you to pause and treat guidance as a gift, not an interruption.
ramacharitamanas::2300.insight: It shifts the mind from self-will to disciplined receptivity toward rightful guidance.

ramacharitamanas::2301.verse_sanskrit: अस जियँ जानि सुनहु सिख भाई। करहु मातु पितु पद सेवकाई॥ भवन भरतु रिपुसूदनु नाहीं। राउ बृद्ध मम दुखु मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2301.verse_hindi: हे भाई! हृदय में ऐसा जानकर मेरी सीख सुनो और माता-पिता के चरणों की सेवा करो। भरत और शत्रुघ्न घर पर नहीं हैं, महाराज वृद्ध हैं और उनके मन में मेरा दुःख है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2301.english_translation: Knowing this in your heart, listen to my counsel, brother: serve your mother and father. Bharat and Shatrughna are not at home, and the old king grieves for my absence in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::2301.translation_literal: अस (thus) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानि (knowing) / सुनहु (listen) / सिख (instruction) / भाई (brother) / करहु (do) / मातु (mother) / पितु (father) / पद (feet) / सेवकाई (service) / भवन (at home) / भरतु (Bharat) / रिपुसूदनु (Shatrughna) / नाहीं (not) / राउ (king) / बृद्ध (old) / मम (my) / दुखु (sorrow) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::2301.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2301.essence: Service to parents becomes urgent when they are left carrying grief alone.
ramacharitamanas::2301.simple_meaning: Ram tells Lakshman to serve their parents and stay with them, because the old king is suffering from Ram's exile and the brothers are not at home.
ramacharitamanas::2301.simple_insight: Love sometimes means staying behind and carrying someone else's burden with care.
ramacharitamanas::2301.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is preparing to leave for the forest, and Lakshman wants to follow him. Ram gently redirects him: the parents need service now, Bharat and Shatrughna are away, and Dasharath is already broken by grief. This verse grounds duty in family pain.
ramacharitamanas::2301.modern_relevance: Your father is unwell, your sibling is away, and everyone expects you to chase your own plans. Ram's words cut through that pressure: some moments ask for presence, not ambition.
ramacharitamanas::2301.insight: It shifts action from self-directed desire to immediate responsibility toward family.

ramacharitamanas::2302.verse_sanskrit: मैं बन जाउँ तुम्हहि लेइ साथा। होइ सबहि बिधि अवध अनाथा॥ गुरु पितु मातु प्रजा परिवारू। सब कहुँ परइ दुसह दुख भारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2302.verse_hindi: इस अवस्था में मैं तुमको साथ लेकर वन जाऊँ तो अयोध्या सभी प्रकार से अनाथ हो जाएगी। गुरु, पिता, माता, प्रजा और परिवार सभी पर दुःख का दुःसह भार आ पड़ेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2302.english_translation: If I take you with me to the forest, Ayodhya will be left orphaned in every way. Guru, father, mother, subjects, and family would all bear unbearable sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2302.translation_literal: मैं (I) / बन (forest) / जाउँ (go) / तुम्हहि (you) / लेइ (taking) / साथा (along) / होइ (becomes) / सबहि बिधि (in every way) / अवध (Ayodhya) / अनाथा (orphaned) / गुरु (teacher) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / प्रजा (subjects) / परिवारू (family) / सब कहुँ (for all) / परइ (falls) / दुसह (unbearable) / दुख (sorrow) / भारू (burden)
ramacharitamanas::2302.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2302.essence: True love sometimes stays behind to carry everyone else.
ramacharitamanas::2302.simple_meaning: Ram says he cannot take Bharat into exile, because Ayodhya would then be left helpless and grieving. He sees the duty of king, family, and people all at once.
ramacharitamanas::2302.simple_insight: Love can still choose the burden that protects others from pain.
ramacharitamanas::2302.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram is explaining why Bharat must stay behind. If Bharat leaves with him, the whole kingdom loses its support: parents, teacher, subjects, and family all suffer. Ram chooses responsibility over personal closeness.
ramacharitamanas::2302.modern_relevance: You want to drop everything and follow the person you love, but your home is already depending on you. Sometimes devotion means staying put so others do not collapse.
ramacharitamanas::2302.insight: It shifts loyalty from private feeling to public responsibility, showing that care must include the people who rely on you.

ramacharitamanas::2303.verse_sanskrit: रहहु करहु सब कर परितोषू। नतरु तात होइहि बड़ दोषू॥ जासु राज प्रिय प्रजा दुखारी। सो नृपु अवसि नरक अधिकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2303.verse_hindi: अतः तुम यहीं रहो और सबका संतोष करते रहो। नहीं तो हे तात! बड़ा दोष होगा। जिसके राज्य में प्यारी प्रजा दुःखी रहती है, वह राजा अवश्य ही नरक का अधिकारी होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2303.english_translation: So remain here and keep everyone satisfied. Otherwise, dear one, a great fault will follow. A king whose people suffer in his reign is surely fit for lower realms.
ramacharitamanas::2303.translation_literal: रहहु (remain) / करहु (do) / सब (all) / कर (by hand) / परितोषू (satisfaction) / नतरु (otherwise) / तात (dear one) / होइहि (will be) / बड़ (great) / दोषू (fault) / जासु (whose) / राज (rule/kingdom) / प्रिय (dear) / प्रजा (subjects) / दुखारी (suffering) / सो (that) / नृपु (king) / अवसि (certainly) / नरक (lower realm) / अधिकारी (fit/deserving)
ramacharitamanas::2303.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2303.essence: A ruler who lets people suffer has already failed.
ramacharitamanas::2303.simple_meaning: Bharat says a ruler must stay and care for everyone’s wellbeing. If the people suffer, that ruler has failed badly.
ramacharitamanas::2303.simple_insight: Leadership is measured by the comfort of the weakest, not the pride of the throne.
ramacharitamanas::2303.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat refuses power for himself and speaks as a guardian of the kingdom. He tells the others to remain and keep everyone content, warning that a ruler whose subjects suffer is morally ruined.
ramacharitamanas::2303.modern_relevance: You run a team meeting while one quiet person has stopped speaking entirely. The project may look fine, but the room is not. Bharat would call that a leadership failure.
ramacharitamanas::2303.insight: It shifts attention from authority to responsibility: a leader is judged by the people’s lived experience.

ramacharitamanas::2304.verse_sanskrit: रहहु तात असि नीति बिचारी। सुनत लखनु भए ब्याकुल भारी॥ सिअरें बचन सूखि गए कैसें। परसत तुहिन तामरसु जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2304.verse_hindi: हे तात! ऐसी नीति विचारकर तुम घर रह जाओ। यह सुनते ही लक्ष्मणजी बहुत ही व्याकुल हो गए! इन शीतल वचनों से वे कैसे सूख गए, जैसे पाले के स्पर्श से कमल सूख जाता है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2304.english_translation: “Considering such policy, stay here, dear brother.” Hearing this, Lakshman became deeply agitated. Those cooling words dried him out, like frost withering a lotus.
ramacharitamanas::2304.translation_literal: रहहु (stay) / तात (dear brother) / असि (such) / नीति (policy, wise course) / बिचारी (having considered) / सुनत (hearing) / लखनु (Lakshman) / भए (became) / ब्याकुल (agitated) / भारी (greatly) / सिअरें (frosty/cold) / बचन (words) / सूखि गए (dried up) / कैसें (how) / परसत (touching) / तुहिन (frost) / तामरसु (lotus) / जैसें (like)
ramacharitamanas::2304.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2304.essence: Tender counsel can feel like a wound to loyal love.
ramacharitamanas::2304.simple_meaning: Ram asks Lakshman to stay home after weighing what is right. Lakshman's heart breaks at hearing it, as if a lotus were shriveled by frost.
ramacharitamanas::2304.simple_insight: Love can make even gentle words feel unbearable when separation is near.
ramacharitamanas::2304.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram is trying to calm Lakshman and keep him from following into exile. The words are tender, but Lakshman hears them as rejection. His devotion is so intense that even kindness wounds him.
ramacharitamanas::2304.modern_relevance: You tell someone you care about to stay back for their own good, and they go quiet in a way that hurts. Sometimes protection feels like abandonment to a loyal heart.
ramacharitamanas::2304.insight: It shows how devotion can turn restraint into pain, and how careful words still carry emotional force.

ramacharitamanas::2305.verse_sanskrit: उतरु न आवत प्रेम बस गहे चरन अकुलाइ। नाथ दासु मैं स्वामि तुम्ह तजहु त काह बसाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2305.verse_hindi: प्रेमवश लक्ष्मणजी से कुछ उत्तर देते नहीं बनता। उन्होंने व्याकुल होकर श्री रामजी के चरण पकड़ लिए और कहा- हे नाथ! मैं दास हूँ और आप स्वामी हैं, अतः आप मुझे छोड़ ही दें तो मेरा क्या वश है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2305.english_translation: Overcome by love, he could not answer. He clutched Rama's feet in distress and said, "Lord, I am your servant and you are my master. If you abandon me, what power is left to me?"
ramacharitamanas::2305.translation_literal: उतरु (answer) / न (not) / आवत (comes) / प्रेम बस (under the control of love) / गहे (grasped) / चरन (feet) / अकुलाइ (in distress) / नाथ (Lord) / दासु (servant) / मैं (I) / स्वामि (master) / तुम्ह (you) / तजहु (abandon) / त (then) / काह (what) / बसाइ (power/control) / ॥
ramacharitamanas::2305.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::2305.essence: Surrender is not weakness; it is freedom from false control.
ramacharitamanas::2305.simple_meaning: Lakshman, overwhelmed with love, cannot argue back. He holds Ram's feet and admits complete dependence: Ram is the master, and without Ram he has no control.
ramacharitamanas::2305.simple_insight: There is relief in stopping the struggle and admitting dependence on what truly holds you.
ramacharitamanas::2305.detailed_meaning: Lakshman has just been urged to stay back for the good of Ayodhya. Instead of defending himself, he breaks under love, falls at Ram's feet, and confesses that his will means nothing apart from Ram's guidance.
ramacharitamanas::2305.modern_relevance: You finally admit to the friend, mentor, or partner that you cannot carry this alone. The relief is immediate: the burden gets lighter the moment control stops pretending to be strength.
ramacharitamanas::2305.insight: It shifts the mind from self-reliance to willing dependence on what is greater and steadier.

ramacharitamanas::2306.verse_sanskrit: दीन्हि मोहि सिख नीकि गोसाईं। लागि अगम अपनी कदराईं॥ नरबर धीर धरम धुर धारी। निगम नीति कहुँ ते अधिकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2306.verse_hindi: हे स्वामी! आपने मुझे सीख तो बड़ी अच्छी दी है, पर मुझे अपनी कायरता से वह मेरे लिए अगम (पहुँच के बाहर) लगी। शास्त्र और नीति के तो वे ही श्रेष्ठ पुरुष अधिकारी हैं, जो धीर हैं और धर्म की धुरी को धारण करने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2306.english_translation: O lord, you have given me a good teaching, but my own weakness made it hard for me to grasp. Only noble, steady people who bear the weight of dharma are fit for the scriptures and moral law.
ramacharitamanas::2306.translation_literal: दीन्हि (gave) / मोहि (to me) / सिख (teaching) / नीकि (good) / गोसाईं (lord) / लागि (because of) / अगम (hard to reach) / अपनी (my own) / कदराईं (weakness)॥ / नरबर (best among men) / धीर (steady) / धरम (dharma) / धुर (burden/pillar) / धारी (bearer) / निगम (scriptures) / नीति (moral order) / कहुँ (for) / ते (those) / अधिकारी (fit/qualified) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2306.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::2306.essence: Good teaching still feels far away to the unsteady.
ramacharitamanas::2306.simple_meaning: Lakshman admits the teaching is good, but says his own weakness makes it hard to hold. He says only steady, noble people who carry dharma well are fit for scripture and moral discipline.
ramacharitamanas::2306.simple_insight: Humility makes room for learning. Self-knowledge is the first step before discipline can take root.
ramacharitamanas::2306.detailed_meaning: Lakshman, still shaken by Ram’s call to stay behind, answers with humility instead of pride. He praises the teaching, but confesses that his own weakness makes it feel unreachable. In this family moment, the real issue is not knowledge but readiness to live it.
ramacharitamanas::2306.modern_relevance: You hear solid advice from someone you trust, then realise you are too reactive to follow it cleanly. The first honest move is admitting that gap instead of pretending mastery.
ramacharitamanas::2306.insight: It shifts the mind from defensiveness to self-honesty, so learning begins with admitting where you are not yet steady.

ramacharitamanas::2307.verse_sanskrit: मैं सिसु प्रभु सनेहँ प्रतिपाला। मंदरु मेरु कि लेहिं मराला॥ गुर पितु मातु न जानउँ काहू। कहउँ सुभाउ नाथ पतिआहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2307.verse_hindi: मैं तो प्रभु (आप) के स्नेह में पला हुआ छोटा बच्चा हूँ! कहीं हंस भी मंदराचल या सुमेरु पर्वत को उठा सकते हैं! हे नाथ! स्वभाव से ही कहता हूँ, आप विश्वास करें, मैं आपको छोड़कर गुरु, पिता, माता किसी को भी नहीं जानता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2307.english_translation: I have been raised in your affection like a child. Can a swan lift Mount Mandara or Mount Meru? I know no guru, father, or mother. I speak from my nature, Lord; trust me.
ramacharitamanas::2307.translation_literal: मैं (I) / सिसु (child) / प्रभु (Lord) / सनेहँ (in affection) / प्रतिपाला (raised, nurtured) / मंदरु (Mandara) / मेरु (Meru) / कि (can) / लेहिं (lift) / मराला (swan) / गुर (guru) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / न (not) / जानउँ (I know) / काहू (any) / कहउँ (I say) / सुभाउ (nature) / नाथ (Lord) / पतिआहू (trust, believe)
ramacharitamanas::2307.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::2307.essence: Belonging to Ram makes every other tie secondary.
ramacharitamanas::2307.simple_meaning: Lakshman says he has been raised in Ram's affection and speaks from his true nature, asking Ram to trust him. He knows no other master, parent, or guide.
ramacharitamanas::2307.simple_insight: Love creates loyalty so deep that it needs no explanation.
ramacharitamanas::2307.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Lakshman begs Ram not to doubt him after being gently corrected. He says he has grown up in Ram's care and belongs only to him, using the impossible image of a swan lifting great mountains to show how unnatural separation would be.
ramacharitamanas::2307.modern_relevance: A younger sibling stands in the kitchen after a harsh family argument, voice shaking, saying, 'I was raised by you. You know me.' The verse carries that raw plea to be seen through love, not suspicion.
ramacharitamanas::2307.insight: It shifts loyalty from formal duty to lived belonging, where trust matters more than proof.

ramacharitamanas::2308.verse_sanskrit: जहँ लगि जगत सनेह सगाई। प्रीति प्रतीति निगम निजु गाई॥ मोरें सबइ एक तुम्ह स्वामी। दीनबंधु उर अंतरजामी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2308.verse_hindi: जगत में जहाँ तक स्नेह का संबंध, प्रेम और विश्वास है, जिनको स्वयं वेद ने गाया है- हे स्वामी! हे दीनबन्धु! हे सबके हृदय के अंदर की जानने वाले! मेरे तो वे सब कुछ केवल आप ही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2308.english_translation: Wherever there is affection, love, and trust in the world, the Vedas themselves sing of them. For me, all of that is only you, my Lord, friend of the helpless, knower within every heart.
ramacharitamanas::2308.translation_literal: जहँ लगि (as far as) / जगत (world) / सनेह (affection) / सगाई (bond) / प्रीति (love) / प्रतीति (trust) / निगम (the Vedas) / निजु (themselves) / गाई (sang) / मोरें (for me) / सबइ (all) / एक (one) / तुम्ह (you) / स्वामी (lord) / दीनबंधु (friend of the helpless) / उर (heart) / अंतरजामी (knower within)
ramacharitamanas::2308.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2308.essence: Every true bond finds its completion in Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2308.simple_meaning: All affection, trust, and true connection in the world are gathered in Ram alone. For the speaker, Ram is the one source and meaning of every bond.
ramacharitamanas::2308.simple_insight: Love becomes simpler when every real bond is seen as a doorway to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2308.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the speaker turns from argument to surrender. After admitting his weakness, he says that every form of love, trust, and belonging praised by the Vedas is fulfilled in Ram alone. The verse shifts the whole discussion from social duty to total devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2308.modern_relevance: You keep looking for one person, one group, or one approval that will finally make you feel held. Then you realise the ache was never about possession — it was about where you place your deepest loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::2308.insight: It redirects attachment from scattered human bonds to a single, wholehearted devotion.

ramacharitamanas::2309.verse_sanskrit: धरम नीति उपदेसिअ ताही। कीरति भूति सुगति प्रिय जाही॥ मन क्रम बचन चरन रत होई। कृपासिंधु परिहरिअ कि सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2309.verse_hindi: धर्म और नीति का उपदेश तो उसको करना चाहिए, जिसे कीर्ति, विभूति (ऐश्वर्य) या सद्गति प्यारी हो, किन्तु जो मन, वचन और कर्म से चरणों में ही प्रेम रखता हो, हे कृपासिन्धु! क्या वह भी त्यागने के योग्य है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2309.english_translation: Teach duty and discipline to the one who wants fame, wealth, or a good afterlife. But should the compassionate one abandon the person who loves the feet with mind, speech, and body?
ramacharitamanas::2309.translation_literal: धरम (duty) / नीति (right conduct) / उपदेसिअ (should be taught) / ताही (to that one) / कीरति (fame) / भूति (wealth, splendor) / सुगति (good destination) / प्रिय (dear) / जाही (to whom) ॥ / मन (mind) / क्रम (action) / बचन (speech) / चरन (feet) / रत (attached, devoted) / होई (is) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / परिहरिअ (should be abandoned) / कि (or) / सोई (that one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2309.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2309.essence: Complete devotion is not a candidate for rejection.
ramacharitamanas::2309.simple_meaning: Rules and moral discipline suit people who still want worldly gain or a better future. But someone who loves Ram with complete devotion should not be pushed away.
ramacharitamanas::2309.simple_insight: Love is not a transaction. Genuine devotion deserves welcome, not conditions.
ramacharitamanas::2309.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat speaks with humility and fear before Ram. He says moral instruction suits those still chasing fame, wealth, or comfort, but a person already devoted in thought, word, and deed should never be rejected by the ocean of compassion.
ramacharitamanas::2309.modern_relevance: Someone finally opens up in therapy, not asking for advice, just wanting to be held without judgment. You can correct a performance; you should not dismiss a heart that is already surrendered.
ramacharitamanas::2309.insight: It shifts the mind from judging devotion by usefulness to honoring it as its own completion.

ramacharitamanas::2310.verse_sanskrit: करुनासिंधु सुबंधु के सुनि मृदु बचन बिनीत। समुझाए उर लाइ प्रभु जानि सनेहँ सभीत ॥
ramacharitamanas::2310.verse_hindi: दया के समुद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने भले भाई के कोमल और नम्रतायुक्त वचन सुनकर और उन्हें स्नेह के कारण डरे हुए जानकर, हृदय से लगाकर समझाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2310.english_translation: The ocean of compassion, the noble brother, heard his gentle and humble words, and, knowing his love and fear, the Lord took him to his heart and reassured him.
ramacharitamanas::2310.translation_literal: करुनासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / सुबंधु (noble brother) / के (of) / सुनि (hearing) / मृदु (gentle) / बचन (words) / बिनीत (humble) / समुझाए (explained/reassured) / उर (heart) / लाइ (placing) / प्रभु (Lord) / जानि (knowing) / सनेहँ (love) / सभीत (fearful)
ramacharitamanas::2310.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2310.essence: Gentle love can calm fear without dismissing it.
ramacharitamanas::2310.simple_meaning: Ram hears Lakshman’s gentle, respectful words and, seeing his loving fear, pulls him close and comforts him.
ramacharitamanas::2310.simple_insight: Love becomes safe when it is met with tenderness instead of force.
ramacharitamanas::2310.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Lakshman speaks softly to Ram after hearing the command to leave for the forest. Ram, already moved by his brother’s devotion, understands that the fear comes from love, not weakness, and answers by embracing and reassuring him.
ramacharitamanas::2310.modern_relevance: A younger sibling finally says what they’re afraid to say: “I don’t want to lose you.” Instead of brushing it off, you soften, listen, and make room for the fear beneath the words.
ramacharitamanas::2310.insight: It teaches you to meet another person’s hesitation with warmth, not pressure.

ramacharitamanas::2311.verse_sanskrit: मागहु बिदा मातु सन जाई। आवहु बेगि चलहु बन भाई॥ मुदित भए सुनि रघुबर बानी। भयउ लाभ बड़ गइ बड़ि हानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2311.verse_hindi: (और कहा-) हे भाई! जाकर माता से विदा माँग आओ और जल्दी वन को चलो! रघुकुल में श्रेष्ठ श्री रामजी की वाणी सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी आनंदित हो गए। बड़ी हानि दूर हो गई और बड़ा लाभ हुआ!॥1।
ramacharitamanas::2311.english_translation: “Go ask Mother for permission. Come quickly, brother; let us go to the forest.” Hearing the noble words of Raghubar, Lakshman rejoiced. A great loss was removed, and a great gain had come.
ramacharitamanas::2311.translation_literal: मागहु (ask for) / बिदा (permission to leave) / मातु सन (from Mother) / जाई (go) / आवहु (come) / बेगि (quickly) / चलहु (let us go) / बन (to the forest) / भाई (brother) / मुदित (joyful) / भए (became) / सुनि (hearing) / रघुबर (Raghubar, Ram) / बानी (words) / भयउ (became) / लाभ (gain) / बड़ (great) / गइ (went away) / बड़ि (great) / हानी (loss)
ramacharitamanas::2311.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2311.essence: Clear duty turns hardship into relief.
ramacharitamanas::2311.simple_meaning: Ram tells Lakshman to ask their mother for permission and come quickly to the forest. Lakshman feels joy, because the painful delay has finally ended.
ramacharitamanas::2311.simple_insight: Relief arrives when the right action finally becomes clear.
ramacharitamanas::2311.detailed_meaning: Ram, already accepting exile, sends Lakshman to seek Sumitra's permission before leaving. Lakshman hears the command and feels uplifted, because the hesitation and confusion around departure are over. The moment is about duty becoming clear.
ramacharitamanas::2311.modern_relevance: You finally make the call you've been avoiding: leave the job, start the move, tell your family. The fear doesn't vanish, but the next step becomes clean.
ramacharitamanas::2311.insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to immediate, rightful action.

ramacharitamanas::2312.verse_sanskrit: हरषित हृदयँ मातु पहिं आए। मनहुँ अंध फिरि लोचन पाए॥ जाइ जननि पग नायउ माथा। मनु रघुनंदन जानकि साथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2312.verse_hindi: वे हर्षित हृदय से माता सुमित्राजी के पास आए, मानो अंधा फिर से नेत्र पा गया हो। उन्होंने जाकर माता के चरणों में मस्तक नवाया, किन्तु उनका मन रघुकुल को आनंद देने वाले श्री रामजी और जानकीजी के साथ था ॥
ramacharitamanas::2312.english_translation: Laxman returned to his mother with a joyful heart, as if a blind man had regained sight. He bowed his head at her feet, yet his mind stayed with Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2312.translation_literal: हरषित (joyful) / हृदयँ (heart) / मातु (mother) / पहिं (to, near) / आए (came) / मनहुँ (as if) / अंध (blind) / फिरि (again) / लोचन (eyes, sight) / पाए (got, received) / जाइ (going) / जननि (mother) / पग (feet) / नायउ (bowed) / माथा (head) / मनु (mind) / रघुनंदन (Ram, delight of Raghu) / जानकि (Sita) / साथा (with)
ramacharitamanas::2312.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2312.essence: True devotion keeps the heart with Ram even while honoring the mother.
ramacharitamanas::2312.simple_meaning: Laxman returns to his mother with joy and bows to her feet, but his heart remains with Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2312.simple_insight: Love can honor family without leaving devotion behind.
ramacharitamanas::2312.detailed_meaning: Laxman has just been sent to seek permission from his mother before going into the forest with Ram. He comes back joyful, bows at Sumitra's feet, and shows that his deepest allegiance is still with Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2312.modern_relevance: You call your mother after making a hard choice, and she hears respect in your voice even when your life is pulling elsewhere. That split loyalty feels familiar.
ramacharitamanas::2312.insight: It shows how duty to family and devotion to Ram can coexist without conflict.

ramacharitamanas::2313.verse_sanskrit: पूँछे मातु मलिन मन देखी। लखन कही सब कथा बिसेषी। गई सहमि सुनि बचन कठोरा। मृगी देखि दव जनु चहुँ ओरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2313.verse_hindi: माता ने उदास मन देखकर उनसे (कारण) पूछा। लक्ष्मणजी ने सब कथा विस्तार से कह सुनाई। सुमित्राजी कठोर वचनों को सुनकर ऐसी सहम गईं जैसे हिरनी चारों ओर वन में आग लगी देखकर सहम जाती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2313.english_translation: Seeing her sad face, the mother asked the reason. Lakshman told her the whole story in full. Hearing the harsh words, Sumitra trembled like a deer that sees fire all around the forest.
ramacharitamanas::2313.translation_literal: पूँछे (asked) / मातु (mother) / मलिन (sad, clouded) / मन (mind, face) / देखी (seeing) / लखन (Lakshman) / कही (told) / सब (all) / कथा (story) / बिसेषी (in detail) / गई (went) / सहमि (trembling) / सुनि (hearing) / बचन (words) / कठोरा (harsh) / मृगी (deer) / देखि (seeing) / दव (fire) / जनु (as if) / चहुँ ओर (on all four sides)
ramacharitamanas::2313.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2313.essence: Pain becomes real the moment it is spoken aloud.
ramacharitamanas::2313.simple_meaning: Sumitra sees Lakshman’s sadness, asks why, and hears the whole terrible news. The harsh words shake her like a deer surrounded by fire.
ramacharitamanas::2313.simple_insight: Love does not protect you from pain. Sometimes it makes the pain sharper.
ramacharitamanas::2313.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Lakshman has returned from Rama’s side with a heavy face. Sumitra asks what has happened, and he tells her everything. Her body reacts before her mind can recover, because the exile has become real.
ramacharitamanas::2313.modern_relevance: You notice your mother’s face change the moment she reads your message. Before she says a word, she already knows something is wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2313.insight: It shows how grief lands first in the body, then in speech, before understanding can catch up.

ramacharitamanas::2314.verse_sanskrit: लखन लखेउ भा अनरथ आजू। एहिं सनेह सब करब अकाजू॥ मागत बिदा सभय सकुचाहीं। जाइ संग बिधि कहिहि कि नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2314.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मण ने देखा कि आज (अब) अनर्थ हुआ। ये स्नेह वश काम बिगाड़ देंगी! इसलिए वे विदा माँगते हुए डर के मारे सकुचाते हैं (और मन ही मन सोचते हैं) कि हे विधाता! माता साथ जाने को कहेंगी या नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2314.english_translation: Lakshman saw that disaster had come today. This affection will ruin everything. So, asking for leave, he hesitated in fear, wondering, "Will Mother let me go with them, or not?"
ramacharitamanas::2314.translation_literal: लखन (Lakshman) / लखेउ (saw) / भा (became) / अनरथ (disaster) / आजू (today) / एहिं (this) / सनेह (affection) / सब (all) / करब (doing) / अकाजू (harmful, ruinous) / मागत (asking) / बिदा (leave) / सभय (fearful) / सकुचाहीं (hesitate, shrink back) / जाइ (going) / संग (with) / बिधि (fate, providence) / कहिहि (will say) / कि (whether) / नाहीं (or not)
ramacharitamanas::2314.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::2314.essence: Affection can become harmful when it ignores duty.
ramacharitamanas::2314.simple_meaning: Lakshman sees that affection can create a mess, so he becomes shy and fearful about asking permission to go with Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2314.simple_insight: Love is not always enough; sometimes care must bow to what is right.
ramacharitamanas::2314.detailed_meaning: Lakshman has just heard the news from Sumitra and feels the weight of Ram and Sita's exile. He sees that family affection could now pull everyone into confusion, so he hesitates before asking permission to accompany them.
ramacharitamanas::2314.modern_relevance: You want to say yes to a friend’s request, but you can already see it will complicate a fragile family situation. Caring deeply does not remove the need for clear judgment.
ramacharitamanas::2314.insight: It teaches you to notice when affection is about to override sound action.

ramacharitamanas::2315.verse_sanskrit: समुझि सुमित्राँ राम सिय रूपु सुसीलु सुभाउ। नृप सनेहु लखि धुनेउ सिरु पापिनि दीन्ह कुदाउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2315.verse_hindi: सुमित्राजी ने श्री रामजी और श्री सीताजी के रूप, सुंदर शील और स्वभाव को समझकर और उन पर राजा का प्रेम देखकर अपना सिर धुना (पीटा) और कहा कि पापिनी कैकेयी ने बुरी तरह घात लगाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2315.english_translation: Understanding the beauty, virtue, and nature of Ram and Sita, and seeing the king's love, Sumitra shook her head and said, "Wicked Kaikeyi has struck a cruel blow."
ramacharitamanas::2315.translation_literal: समुझि (understanding) / सुमित्राँ (Sumitra) / राम (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / रूपु (form, beauty) / सुसीलु (good character) / सुभाउ (nature) / नृप (king) / सनेहु (love) / लखि (seeing) / धुनेउ (shook) / सिरु (head) / पापिनि (wicked woman) / दीन्ह (dealt) / कुदाउ (cruel blow)
ramacharitamanas::2315.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2315.essence: Seeing love clearly makes betrayal unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2315.simple_meaning: Sumitra sees Ram, Sita, and Dasharath's love clearly, and realizes Kaikeyi has caused terrible harm.
ramacharitamanas::2315.simple_insight: Clear seeing makes the wound impossible to deny.
ramacharitamanas::2315.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sumitra hears Lakshman’s account and finally understands what is being lost: Ram, Sita, and the king’s love for them. Her grief turns into recognition that Kaikeyi’s demand has cut deep into the family.
ramacharitamanas::2315.modern_relevance: You hear the whole story after the argument is already over. Then the pattern becomes obvious, and the person who caused it can no longer hide behind excuses.
ramacharitamanas::2315.insight: It shifts the mind from confusion to moral clarity about who has caused harm.

ramacharitamanas::2316.verse_sanskrit: धीरजु धरेउ कुअवसर जानी। सहज सुहृद बोली मृदु बानी॥ तात तुम्हारि मातु बैदेही। पिता रामु सब भाँति सनेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2316.verse_hindi: परन्तु कुसमय जानकर धैर्य धारण किया और स्वभाव से ही हित चाहने वाली सुमित्राजी कोमल वाणी से बोलीं- हे तात! जानकीजी तुम्हारी माता हैं और सब प्रकार से स्नेह करने वाले श्री रामचन्द्रजी तुम्हारे पिता हैं! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2316.english_translation: But knowing the moment was inauspicious, she held her composure and spoke with gentle words, true to her kind nature: "Child, Janaki is your mother, and Ram is your father in every way."
ramacharitamanas::2316.translation_literal: धीरजु (composure) / धरेउ (held) / कुअवसर (inauspicious moment) / जानी (knowing) / सहज (by nature) / सुहृद (well-wishing) / बोली (spoke) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (words) / तात (child) / तुम्हारि (your) / मातु (mother) / बैदेही (Vaidehi/Janaki) / पिता (father) / रामु (Ram) / सब भाँति (in every way) / सनेही (affectionate, loving)
ramacharitamanas::2316.speaker: Sumitra
ramacharitamanas::2316.essence: Composure and gentle speech can hold a family together in crisis.
ramacharitamanas::2316.simple_meaning: Sumitra stays calm in a tense moment and speaks gently to Lakshman. She reminds him that Sita is like his mother and Ram like his father.
ramacharitamanas::2316.simple_insight: Careful words can steady a crisis better than panic ever could.
ramacharitamanas::2316.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the family is being torn by Ram's exile. Lakshman is ready to react, but Sumitra sees the danger of the moment. She answers with calm affection, guiding him toward patience and duty.
ramacharitamanas::2316.modern_relevance: Your sibling is spiraling before a hard conversation, and you can feel the room tighten. One calm sentence from someone steady can stop the whole situation from breaking apart.
ramacharitamanas::2316.insight: It teaches you to answer crisis with composure and relational clarity, not emotional heat.

ramacharitamanas::2317.verse_sanskrit: अवध तहाँ जहँ राम निवासू। तहँइँ दिवसु जहँ भानु प्रकासू॥ जौं पै सीय रामु बन जाहीं। अवध तुम्हार काजु कछु नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2317.verse_hindi: जहाँ श्री रामजी का निवास हो वहीं अयोध्या है। जहाँ सूर्य का प्रकाश हो वहीं दिन है। यदि निश्चय ही सीता-राम वन को जाते हैं, तो अयोध्या में तुम्हारा कुछ भी काम नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2317.english_translation: Ayodhya is wherever Ram lives. Day is wherever the sun shines. If Sita and Ram truly go to the forest, then Ayodhya has no work left for you.
ramacharitamanas::2317.translation_literal: अवध (Ayodhya) / तहाँ (there) / जहँ (where) / राम (Ram) / निवासू (residence) / तहँइँ (there itself) / दिवसु (day) / जहँ (where) / भानु (sun) / प्रकासू (light) / जौं (if) / पै (indeed) / सीय (Sita) / रामु (Ram) / बन (forest) / जाहीं (go) / अवध (Ayodhya) / तुम्हार (your) / काजु (work) / कछु (some) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::2317.speaker: Sumitra
ramacharitamanas::2317.essence: Ram's presence makes a place complete; without him, even Ayodhya is empty.
ramacharitamanas::2317.simple_meaning: A city only feels complete when Ram is there. Without him, even Ayodhya loses its purpose.
ramacharitamanas::2317.simple_insight: The heart can stop treating status and place as enough. Presence matters more than location.
ramacharitamanas::2317.detailed_meaning: Sumitra is speaking in Ayodhya as exile looms. She tells the others that Ram's presence makes a place truly Ayodhya, just as sunlight makes day. If Ram and Sita go to the forest, the city's role for them is over.
ramacharitamanas::2317.modern_relevance: You move into the perfect apartment, but the room still feels wrong without the person you love. This verse reminds you that meaning comes from presence, not address.
ramacharitamanas::2317.insight: It shifts attention from geography and status to what truly makes a place whole: the presence of what you love and serve.

ramacharitamanas::2318.verse_sanskrit: गुर पितु मातु बंधु सुर साईं। सेइअहिं सकल प्रान की नाईं॥ रामु प्रानप्रिय जीवन जी के। स्वारथ रहित सखा सबही के ॥
ramacharitamanas::2318.verse_hindi: गुरु, पिता, माता, भाई, देवता और स्वामी, इन सबकी सेवा प्राण के समान करनी चाहिए। फिर श्री रामचन्द्रजी तो प्राणों के भी प्रिय हैं, हृदय के भी जीवन हैं और सभी के स्वार्थरहित सखा हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2318.english_translation: Guru, father, mother, brother, radiant beings, and master should all be served like life itself. Shri Ram is even more dear than life, the very life of the heart, and the selfless friend of everyone.
ramacharitamanas::2318.translation_literal: गुर (teacher) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / बंधु (brother) / सुर (radiant beings) / साईं (master) / सेइअहिं (should be served) / सकल (all) / प्रान (life) / की नाईं (like) ॥ / रामु (Ram) / प्रानप्रिय (dearer than life) / जीवन (life) / जी (of the heart) / के (of) / स्वारथ (self-interest) / रहित (free from) / सखा (friend) / सबही (of everyone) / के (of) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2318.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2318.essence: Serve the worthy deeply; Ram is dearer still and asks for nothing in return.
ramacharitamanas::2318.simple_meaning: Serve teachers, parents, siblings, radiant beings, and masters as dearly as your own life. Ram is even more precious: the life of the heart and the friend of all without selfishness.
ramacharitamanas::2318.simple_insight: Real devotion makes service feel natural, and Ram feel closer than breath.
ramacharitamanas::2318.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the exile has become a moral test. The teaching widens from family duty to reverence for all worthy relationships, then lifts higher: Ram is not just another person to honour, but the dearest presence and the friend who asks nothing for himself.
ramacharitamanas::2318.modern_relevance: You keep helping the mentor who shaped you, the parent who worries for you, the friend who never asks for credit. Then one relationship rises above them all: the one that asks for no payment, only love.
ramacharitamanas::2318.insight: It shifts devotion from social respect to wholehearted inward belonging.

ramacharitamanas::2319.verse_sanskrit: पूजनीय प्रिय परम जहाँ तें। सब मानिअहिं राम के नातें॥ अस जियँ जानि संग बन जाहू। लेहु तात जग जीवन लाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2319.verse_hindi: जगत में जहाँ तक पूजनीय और परम प्रिय लोग हैं, वे सब रामजी के नाते से ही (पूजनीय और परम प्रिय) मानने योग्य हैं। हृदय में ऐसा जानकर, हे तात! उनके साथ वन जाओ और जगत में जीने का लाभ उठाओ! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2319.english_translation: Whatever is revered and dearly loved in the world should be regarded as belonging to Ram. Knowing this in your heart, dear son, go into the forest with them and gain the true benefit of life.
ramacharitamanas::2319.translation_literal: पूजनीय (revered) / प्रिय (dear) / परम (supreme) / जहाँ तें (wherever) / सब (all) / मानिअहिं (should be regarded) / राम के नातें (because of Ram's relation) / अस (thus) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानि (knowing) / संग (with) / बन (forest) / जाहू (go) / लेहु (take/gain) / तात (dear son) / जग (world) / जीवन (life) / लाहू (profit/benefit)
ramacharitamanas::2319.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2319.essence: Honor every bond by placing Ram first.
ramacharitamanas::2319.simple_meaning: All people and things that seem most worthy of love are to be seen through Ram. With that understanding, the son should go to the forest and live rightly.
ramacharitamanas::2319.simple_insight: Love becomes clearer when it is placed in a larger devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2319.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the family crisis has already pushed Ram toward exile. The speaker urges that every honoured bond in life must now be understood through Ram's place in it, and that the son should go with Ram into the forest rather than cling to comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2319.modern_relevance: You are torn between staying home for comfort and leaving to support someone you love through a hard season. This verse says loyalty is not loss when it is rooted in what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::2319.insight: It shifts attachment from social approval and comfort toward faithful companionship in hardship.

ramacharitamanas::2320.verse_sanskrit: भूरि भाग भाजनु भयहु मोहि समेत बलि जाउँ। जौं तुम्हरें मन छाड़ि छलु कीन्ह राम पद ठाउँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2320.verse_hindi: मैं बलिहारी जाती हूँ, (हे पुत्र!) मेरे समेत तुम बड़े ही सौभाग्य के पात्र हुए, जो तुम्हारे चित्त ने छल छोड़कर श्री राम के चरणों में स्थान प्राप्त किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2320.english_translation: I am blessed beyond measure, and I offer myself to you, my son. You and I are truly fortunate, because your mind has abandoned deceit and found a place at Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::2320.translation_literal: भूरि (greatly) / भाग (fortune) / भाजनु (recipient) / भयहु (you became) / मोहि (to me) / समेत (together with) / बलि जाउँ (I offer myself) / जौं (if) / तुम्हरें (your) / मन (mind) / छाड़ि (leaving) / छलु (deceit) / कीन्ह (made) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / ठाउँ (place)
ramacharitamanas::2320.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2320.essence: True fortune is a mind that leaves deceit and rests in Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2320.simple_meaning: Real blessing is when the mind gives up deceit and settles at Ram's feet. The speaker celebrates a son who has found that place.
ramacharitamanas::2320.simple_insight: There is relief in becoming sincere enough to belong to something higher.
ramacharitamanas::2320.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, a mother speaks with gratitude about her son. After teaching that family members are honored through Ram, she rejoices that the boy's mind has dropped deceit and taken refuge at Ram's feet. That devotion is the real fortune.
ramacharitamanas::2320.modern_relevance: A parent watches a grown child stop pretending, stop performing, and finally choose what is true. The relief is not success or status — it is sincerity.
ramacharitamanas::2320.insight: It shifts attention from outward achievement to inward honesty and devotion.

ramacharitamanas::2321.verse_sanskrit: पुत्रवती जुबती जग सोई। रघुपति भगतु जासु सुतु होई॥ नतरु बाँझ भलि बादि बिआनी। राम बिमुख सुत तें हित जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2321.verse_hindi: संसार में वही युवती स्त्री पुत्रवती है, जिसका पुत्र श्री रघुनाथजी का भक्त हो। नहीं तो जो राम से विमुख पुत्र से अपना हित जानती है, वह तो बाँझ ही अच्छी। पशु की भाँति उसका ब्याना (पुत्र प्रसव करना) व्यर्थ ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2321.english_translation: The only truly blessed woman in the world is the one whose son is devoted to Raghupati. Otherwise, a barren woman is better than one who has given birth in vain, thinking a son who turns away from Ram is a source of benefit.
ramacharitamanas::2321.translation_literal: पुत्रवती (having a son) / जुबती (young woman) / जग (world) / सोई (that alone) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / भगतु (devotee) / जासु (whose) / सुतु (son) / होई (is) / नतरु (otherwise) / बाँझ (barren) / भलि (better) / बादि (in vain) / बिआनी (having given birth) / राम (Ram) / बिमुख (turned away) / सुत (son) / तें (than) / हित (benefit) / जानी (thinking/knowing)
ramacharitamanas::2321.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2321.essence: Birth means little unless it turns toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2321.simple_meaning: A son only truly blesses a mother if he loves Ram. A child who turns away from Ram brings no real benefit.
ramacharitamanas::2321.simple_insight: Love is measured by what the child becomes, not by birth itself.
ramacharitamanas::2321.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi is speaking to Bharata as the exile unfolds. She measures motherhood by devotion to Ram, not by biology alone, and pushes the shocking idea that birth without dharma is empty.
ramacharitamanas::2321.modern_relevance: A parent watches a child win trophies, but the real question is whether character is forming. Achievement without devotion to what is right feels hollow.
ramacharitamanas::2321.insight: It shifts the focus from producing success to nurturing devotion and character.

ramacharitamanas::2322.verse_sanskrit: तुम्हरेहिं भाग रामु बन जाहीं। दूसर हेतु तात कछु नाहीं॥ सकल सुकृत कर बड़ फलु एहू। राम सीय पद सहज सनेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2322.verse_hindi: तुम्हारे ही भाग्य से श्री रामजी वन को जा रहे हैं। हे तात! दूसरा कोई कारण नहीं है। सम्पूर्ण पुण्यों का सबसे बड़ा फल यही है कि श्री सीतारामजी के चरणों में स्वाभाविक प्रेम हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2322.english_translation: By your own good fortune, Ram is going to the forest. Son, there is no other reason. The greatest fruit of all merit is a natural love for the feet of Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2322.translation_literal: तुम्हरेहिं (by your own) / भाग (fortune) / रामु (Ram) / बन (forest) / जाहीं (go) / दूसर (other) / हेतु (reason) / तात (son) / कछु (anything) / नाहीं (not)॥ / सकल (all) / सुकृत (merit) / कर (of) / बड़ (great) / फलु (fruit) / एहू (this) / राम (Ram) / सीय (Sita) / पद (feet) / सहज (natural) / सनेहू (love) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2322.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2322.essence: Grace looks like exile; the highest reward is natural love for Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2322.simple_meaning: Ram’s exile is not random; it comes by fate and blessing. The highest reward of good deeds is an effortless love for Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2322.simple_insight: What seems like loss can actually be grace, and the deepest reward is love that arises on its own.
ramacharitamanas::2322.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the family’s grief is turning into a spiritual lesson. The speaker tells the listening mother that Ram’s going to the forest is not a mistake or accident, and that the real fruit of all good deeds is simple love for Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2322.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love lose a job, a home, or a plan they counted on. Later, you realise the break opened a deeper loyalty and a softer heart than success ever did.
ramacharitamanas::2322.insight: It shifts attention from outer success to inward devotion, teaching that the best outcome is spontaneous love for Ram and Sita.

ramacharitamanas::2323.verse_sanskrit: रागु रोषु इरिषा मदु मोहू। जनि सपनेहुँ इन्ह के बस होहू॥ सकल प्रकार बिकार बिहाई। मन क्रम बचन करेहु सेवकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2323.verse_hindi: राग, रोष, ईर्षा, मद और मोह- इनके वश स्वप्न में भी मत होना। सब प्रकार के विकारों का त्याग कर मन, वचन और कर्म से श्री सीतारामजी की सेवा करना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2323.english_translation: Do not ever fall under the sway of desire, anger, jealousy, pride, or delusion, even in a dream. Give up all forms of corruption and serve Sita and Ram with mind, speech, and action.
ramacharitamanas::2323.translation_literal: रागु (desire) / रोषु (anger) / इरिषा (jealousy) / मदु (pride) / मोहू (delusion) / जनि (do not) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / इन्ह के (of these) / बस (under control) / होहू (be) / सकल (all) / प्रकार (kinds) / बिकार (corruption) / बिहाई (leaving behind) / मन (mind) / क्रम (speech) / बचन (word) / करेहु (do) / सेवकाई (service)
ramacharitamanas::2323.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2323.essence: Clean service begins where ego's noise ends.
ramacharitamanas::2323.simple_meaning: Do not let desire, anger, jealousy, pride, or delusion control you. Leave all inner corruption behind and serve Sita and Ram with your whole being.
ramacharitamanas::2323.simple_insight: Real service begins when the mind is clean enough to obey without ego.
ramacharitamanas::2323.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the family is preparing for Ram's exile. As the pain rises, the teaching turns practical: Bharat must stay untouched by jealousy, pride, and confusion, and serve Ram and Sita with complete purity of thought, speech, and action.
ramacharitamanas::2323.modern_relevance: You are about to send a message while angry, jealous, or trying to prove yourself. Stop. The next move matters less than the state of mind behind it.
ramacharitamanas::2323.insight: It shifts action from ego-driven reaction to clean, disciplined service.

ramacharitamanas::2324.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह कहुँ बन सब भाँति सुपासू। सँग पितु मातु रामु सिय जासू॥ जेहिं न रामु बन लहहिं कलेसू। सुत सोइ करेहु इहइ उपदेसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2324.verse_hindi: तुमको वन में सब प्रकार से आराम है, जिसके साथ श्री रामजी और सीताजी रूप पिता-माता हैं। हे पुत्र! तुम वही करना जिससे श्री रामचन्द्रजी वन में क्लेश न पावें, मेरा यही उपदेश है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2324.english_translation: For you, the forest is comfortable in every way, with Ram and Sita as father and mother. Son, do only what keeps Ram free from hardship in the forest; this is my instruction.
ramacharitamanas::2324.translation_literal: तुम्ह कहुँ (for you) / बन (forest) / सब भाँति (in every way) / सुपासू (comfortable, easy) / सँग (with) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / रामु (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / जासू (whose, with whom) / जेहिं (by which) / न (not) / रामु (Ram) / बन (forest) / लहहिं (should suffer) / कलेसू (hardship, distress) / सुत (son) / सोइ (that very) / करेहु (do) / इहइ (this) / उपदेसू (instruction)
ramacharitamanas::2324.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2324.essence: Real care asks what eases Ram's path, not your own.
ramacharitamanas::2324.simple_meaning: Bharat tells his son that the forest will be easy for him if Ram and Sita are with him like parents. He should act in whatever way keeps Ram from suffering there.
ramacharitamanas::2324.simple_insight: Love shows itself by making another person's burden lighter, not by protecting your own comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2324.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is teaching his son how to live during Ram's exile. He says the forest is no hardship if Ram and Sita are present, and the real duty is to ensure Ram suffers no distress there. Bharat's love becomes instruction.
ramacharitamanas::2324.modern_relevance: You are packing for a difficult trip to help someone you love. Your own inconvenience stops mattering the moment you ask, 'What will make their day easier?'
ramacharitamanas::2324.insight: It shifts duty from self-protection to service: measure choices by the other person's ease, not your own.

ramacharitamanas::2325.verse_sanskrit: उपदेसु यहु जेहिं तात तुम्हरे राम सिय सुख पावहीं। पितु मातु प्रिय परिवार पुर सुख सुरति बन बिसरावहीं॥ तुलसी प्रभुहि सिख देइ आयसु दीन्ह पुनि आसिष दई। रति होउ अबिरल अमल सिय रघुबीर पद नित-नित नई॥
ramacharitamanas::2325.verse_hindi: हे तात! मेरा यही उपदेश है (अर्थात तुम वही करना), जिससे वन में तुम्हारे कारण श्री रामजी और सीताजी सुख पावें और पिता, माता, प्रिय परिवार तथा नगर के सुखों की याद भूल जाएँ। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि सुमित्राजी ने इस प्रकार हमारे प्रभु (श्री लक्ष्मणजी) को शिक्षा देकर (वन जाने की) आज्ञा दी और फिर यह आशीर्वाद दिया कि श्री सीताजी और श्री रघुवीरजी के चरणों में तुम्हारा निर्मल (निष्काम और अनन्य) एवं प्रगाढ़ प्रेम नित-नित नया हो!
ramacharitamanas::2325.english_translation: Mother Sumitra said: "My counsel is this—go so that Rama and Sita may find comfort in the forest, and so that you forget the comforts of father, mother, loved ones, family, and city. May your pure, unwavering love for the feet of Sita and Raghubir grow ever fresh, day by day."
ramacharitamanas::2325.translation_literal: उपदेसु (counsel) / यहु (this) / जेहिं (so that) / तात (son) / तुम्हरे (your) / राम (Rama) / सिय (Sita) / सुख (comfort) / पावहीं (may find) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / प्रिय (dear) / परिवार (family) / पुर (city) / सुख (comforts) / सुरति (memory) / बन (forest) / बिसरावहीं (may forget)॥ / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / प्रभुहि (to the lord) / सिख (teaching) / देइ (giving) / आयसु (command) / दीन्ह (gave) / पुनि (then) / आसिष (blessing) / दई (gave)॥ / रति (love/attachment) / होउ (may be) / अबिरल (unbroken) / अमल (pure) / सिय (Sita) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / पद (feet) / नित-नित (day by day) / नई (new)
ramacharitamanas::2325.speaker: Sumitra
ramacharitamanas::2325.essence: True love sends you where service is needed, not where comfort remains.
ramacharitamanas::2325.simple_meaning: Sumitra tells Lakshman to go in a way that brings comfort to Ram and Sita, forgets home comforts, and deepens his pure love for their feet.
ramacharitamanas::2325.simple_insight: Love becomes real when it makes room for service, not comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2325.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sumitra sends Lakshman into exile with Ram and Sita. She does not cling to family comfort; she blesses him to serve them well and keep his love for their feet fresh and pure.
ramacharitamanas::2325.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love leave for a hard season, and you do not ask them to stay safe and small. You bless them to serve well and love without fading.
ramacharitamanas::2325.insight: It shifts loyalty from personal comfort to wholehearted support for dharma and beloved companions.

ramacharitamanas::2326.verse_sanskrit: मातु चरन सिरु नाइ चले तुरत संकित हृदयँ। बागुर बिषम तोराइ मनहुँ भाग मृगु भाग बस ॥
ramacharitamanas::2326.verse_hindi: माता के चरणों में सिर नवाकर, हृदय में डरते हुए (कि अब भी कोई विघ्न न आ जाए) लक्ष्मणजी तुरंत इस तरह चल दिए जैसे सौभाग्यवश कोई हिरन कठिन फंदे को तुड़ाकर भाग निकला हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2326.english_translation: Bowing his head to his mother’s feet, he set out at once, his heart still trembling. Like a deer that has broken a deadly snare and fled, he moved on by good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::2326.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / चरन (feet) / सिरु (head) / नाइ (bowing) / चले (went) / तुरत (immediately) / संकित (fearful, trembling) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बागुर (snare) / बिषम (dangerous, difficult) / तोराइ (breaking) / मनहुँ (as if) / भाग (fortune) / मृगु (deer) / भाग (ran) / बस (by force, quickly)
ramacharitamanas::2326.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2326.essence: Respect first, then move without delay.
ramacharitamanas::2326.simple_meaning: He bows to his mother and leaves at once, still uneasy, like a deer escaping a trap.
ramacharitamanas::2326.simple_insight: Even a difficult departure can be done with respect and urgency.
ramacharitamanas::2326.detailed_meaning: Lakshman has just received his mother’s instruction and the blessing of the family. He bows to her feet and leaves immediately, still anxious, because the real task is to reach Ram and Sita without delay. The verse lingers on that urgent departure.
ramacharitamanas::2326.modern_relevance: You finally hang up after a hard family call, still shaken, but you get up and do the next right thing anyway.
ramacharitamanas::2326.insight: It teaches you to move forward quickly after honoring the relationship that matters.

ramacharitamanas::2327.verse_sanskrit: गए लखनु जहँ जानकिनाथू। भे मन मुदित पाइ प्रिय साथू॥ बंदि राम सिय चरन सुहाए। चले संग नृपमंदिर आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2327.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी वहाँ गए जहाँ श्री जानकीनाथजी थे और प्रिय का साथ पाकर मन में बड़े ही प्रसन्न हुए। श्री रामजी और सीताजी के सुंदर चरणों की वंदना करके वे उनके साथ चले और राजभवन में आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2327.english_translation: Lakshman went to where Janakinath was. Finding the company of the beloved, his mind became joyful. Bowing to the beautiful feet of Ram and Sita, he walked with them and came to the royal palace.
ramacharitamanas::2327.translation_literal: गए (went) / लखनु (Lakshman) / जहँ (where) / जानकिनाथू (Lord of Janaki) / भे (became) / मन (mind) / मुदित (glad) / पाइ (having found) / प्रिय (beloved) / साथू (company) / बंदि (bowing) / राम (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / चरन (feet) / सुहाए (beautiful) / चले (walked) / संग (with) / नृपमंदिर (royal palace) / आए (came)
ramacharitamanas::2327.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2327.essence: True devotion shows itself in humble companionship.
ramacharitamanas::2327.simple_meaning: Lakshman reaches Ram and Sita, feels joy at being with them, bows to their feet, and goes with them to the palace.
ramacharitamanas::2327.simple_insight: Love becomes visible in simple acts of respect, presence, and companionship.
ramacharitamanas::2327.detailed_meaning: Lakshman finally reaches Ram and Sita after the painful decision to leave. Seeing them lifts his heart at once. He bows, then walks beside them back to the palace, showing that service and joy belong together.
ramacharitamanas::2327.modern_relevance: You finally get to the hospital room after the long drive, and the first thing you do is hold the hand of the person you came for. Relief arrives before words.
ramacharitamanas::2327.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic declaration to quiet loyalty: show up, bow down, stay close.

ramacharitamanas::2328.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं परसपर पुर नर नारी। भलि बनाइ बिधि बात बिगारी॥ तन कृस मन दुखु बदन मलीने। बिकल मनहुँ माखी मधु छीने ॥
ramacharitamanas::2328.verse_hindi: नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष आपस में कह रहे हैं कि विधाता ने खूब बनाकर बात बिगाड़ी! उनके शरीर दुबले, मन दुःखी और मुख उदास हो रहे हैं। वे ऐसे व्याकुल हैं, जैसे शहद छीन लिए जाने पर शहद की मक्खियाँ व्याकुल हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::2328.english_translation: People in the city, men and women alike, say to one another, “The Creator has spoiled what was well made.” Their bodies grow thin, their minds are sorrowful, and their faces pale. They are restless like bees whose honey has been taken away.
ramacharitamanas::2328.translation_literal: कहहिं (say) / परसपर (to one another) / पुर (city) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / भलि (well) / बनाइ (having made) / बिधि (the Creator) / बात (matter) / बिगारी (spoiled)॥ / तन (body) / कृस (thin) / मन (mind) / दुखु (sorrow) / बदन (face) / मलीने (sullied/pale) / बिकल (restless) / मनहुँ (as if) / माखी (bee) / मधु (honey) / छीने (taken away)॥
ramacharitamanas::2328.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2328.essence: A broken departure can leave an entire city grieving.
ramacharitamanas::2328.simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya are grieving so deeply that they say fate has ruined what was once good. Their bodies weaken, their minds ache, and they feel restless with loss.
ramacharitamanas::2328.simple_insight: Grief can hollow out an entire community, not just one person.
ramacharitamanas::2328.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Ram’s exile, the city itself feels wounded. Men and women speak together in sorrow, blaming the higher order for ruining what had been beautifully arranged. Their bodies and faces show the pain, and the whole town trembles with loss.
ramacharitamanas::2328.modern_relevance: At a family dinner after a sudden breakup, nobody knows what to say. Everyone feels the absence in the room, and even the strongest voice sounds tired.
ramacharitamanas::2328.insight: It shows how loss spreads through a whole community, turning private pain into shared sorrow.

ramacharitamanas::2329.verse_sanskrit: कर मीजहिं सिरु धुनि पछिताहीं। जनु बिनु पंख बिहग अकुलाहीं॥ भइ बड़ि भीर भूप दरबारा। बरनि न जाइ बिषादु अपारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2329.verse_hindi: सब हाथ मल रहे हैं और सिर धुनकर (पीटकर) पछता रहे हैं। मानो बिना पंख के पक्षी व्याकुल हो रहे हों। राजद्वार पर बड़ी भीड़ हो रही है। अपार विषाद का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2329.english_translation: They wring their hands and beat their heads in regret, like birds fluttering without wings. A great crowd gathers at the palace gate, and the depth of grief cannot be described.
ramacharitamanas::2329.translation_literal: कर (hands) / मीजहिं (rub) / सिरु (head) / धुनि (shaking) / पछिताहीं (repent) / जनु (as if) / बिनु (without) / पंख (wings) / बिहग (birds) / अकुलाहीं (are restless) / भइ (became) / बड़ि (great) / भीर (crowd) / भूप (king) / दरबारा (court) / बरनि (to describe) / न (not) / जाइ (can be) / बिषादु (grief) / अपारा (boundless)
ramacharitamanas::2329.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2329.essence: Grief overwhelms speech and leaves only helpless motion.
ramacharitamanas::2329.simple_meaning: The people are overwhelmed with grief and regret. They gather at the palace, but the sorrow is too deep to describe.
ramacharitamanas::2329.simple_insight: Some grief is so large it leaves people wordless, only moving in shared shock and regret.
ramacharitamanas::2329.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the news of Ram's exile has hit Ayodhya like a wound. Men and women crowd the palace gate, beating their heads and lamenting as the royal city sinks into helpless sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2329.modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after one message changes everything. People keep typing, deleting, and typing again, but no one can find words that fit the shock.
ramacharitamanas::2329.insight: It shows grief as a collective collapse: the body laments when speech can no longer hold the loss.

ramacharitamanas::2330.verse_sanskrit: सचिवँ उठाइ राउ बैठारे। कहि प्रिय बचन रामु पगु धारे॥ सिय समेत दोउ तनय निहारी। ब्याकुल भयउ भूमिपति भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2330.verse_hindi: 'श्री रामजी पधारे हैं', ये प्रिय वचन कहकर मंत्री ने राजा को उठाकर बैठाया। सीता सहित दोनों पुत्रों को (वन के लिए तैयार) देखकर राजा बहुत व्याकुल हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2330.english_translation: The minister helped the king sit up and spoke gentle words: "Ram has arrived." Seeing Sita with both sons, the king was deeply shaken.
ramacharitamanas::2330.translation_literal: सचिवँ (the minister) / उठाइ (lifting up) / राउ (the king) / बैठारे (made sit) / कहि (saying) / प्रिय बचन (pleasant words) / रामु (Ram) / पगु धारे (has placed his feet / has arrived) / सिय समेत (with Sita) / दोउ तनय (both sons) / निहारी (seeing) / ब्याकुल भयउ (became agitated) / भूमिपति (lord of the earth / king) / भारी (greatly)
ramacharitamanas::2330.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2330.essence: Hope briefly lifts the king; love makes the loss hurt again.
ramacharitamanas::2330.simple_meaning: The minister comforts Dasharath with hopeful news, but the sight of Ram, Sita, and the sons makes the king collapse into grief and agitation.
ramacharitamanas::2330.simple_insight: Love can steady the heart and break it in the same instant.
ramacharitamanas::2330.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court is already drowning in sorrow after Ram's exile. The minister tries to lift Dasharath's spirits by saying Ram has arrived, but when the king sees Ram, Sita, and the two sons, his grief surges again and he becomes deeply agitated.
ramacharitamanas::2330.modern_relevance: You finally hear the person you miss is at the door, and your body reacts before your mind can. Relief and heartbreak can arrive together.
ramacharitamanas::2330.insight: It shows how grief can be triggered by the very presence that was hoped for, making emotion stronger than explanation.

ramacharitamanas::2331.verse_sanskrit: सीय सहित सुत सुभग दोउ देखि देखि अकुलाइ। बारहिं बार सनेह बस राउ लेइ उर लाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2331.verse_hindi: सीता सहित दोनों सुंदर पुत्रों को देख-देखकर राजा अकुलाते हैं और स्नेह वश बारंबार उन्हें हृदय से लगा लेते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2331.english_translation: Seeing Sita and his two beautiful sons, the king grows restless and, overcome by love, repeatedly draws them to his chest.
ramacharitamanas::2331.translation_literal: सीय (Sita) / सहित (together with) / सुत (sons) / सुभग (beautiful, fortunate) / दोउ (both) / देखि देखि (seeing again and again) / अकुलाइ (becomes restless) / बारहिं बार (again and again) / सनेह (love) / बस (under the control of) / राउ (the king) / लेइ (taking) / उर (to the chest) / लाइ (embraces)
ramacharitamanas::2331.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2331.essence: Love makes separation unbearable before it even begins.
ramacharitamanas::2331.simple_meaning: Dasharath cannot bear the sight of Sita and his sons. Love overwhelms him, and he keeps pulling them into his arms.
ramacharitamanas::2331.simple_insight: Love can make even a king tremble, because attachment is stronger than rank.
ramacharitamanas::2331.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has just learned that Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are leaving. He sees them together and cannot hold himself steady. Overcome by affection, he keeps embracing them, knowing this moment is slipping away.
ramacharitamanas::2331.modern_relevance: You keep hugging your child before a long trip, even though you already said goodbye twice. Your body knows what your words cannot fix: this is the last moment together.
ramacharitamanas::2331.insight: It shows how grief and love can break composure before a loss has even fully arrived.

ramacharitamanas::2332.verse_sanskrit: सकइ न बोलि बिकल नरनाहू। सोक जनित उर दारुन दाहू॥ नाइ सीसु पद अति अनुरागा। उठि रघुबीर बिदा तब मागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2332.verse_hindi: राजा व्याकुल हैं, बोल नहीं सकते। हृदय में शोक से उत्पन्न हुआ भयानक सन्ताप है। तब रघुकुल के वीर श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने अत्यन्त प्रेम से चरणों में सिर नवाकर उठकर विदा माँगी- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2332.english_translation: The king could not speak. Grief burned fiercely in his heart. Then Ram, the hero of the Raghu line, bowed his head at his father's feet with deep affection and asked to leave.
ramacharitamanas::2332.translation_literal: सकइ न (could not) / बोलि (to speak) / बिकल (overwhelmed) / नरनाहू (king) / सोक (grief) / जनित (born of) / उर (heart) / दारुन (fierce) / दाहू (burning pain) / नाइ (bowing) / सीसु (head) / पद (feet) / अति (great) / अनुरागा (affection) / उठि (rising) / रघुबीर (hero of the Raghu line) / बिदा (leave) / तब (then) / मागा (asked)
ramacharitamanas::2332.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2332.essence: Duty can be carried on a bowed head.
ramacharitamanas::2332.simple_meaning: Dasharath is too overwhelmed to speak. Ram bows to his feet with great love and asks permission to leave.
ramacharitamanas::2332.simple_insight: Love can be quiet and still carry the hardest duty.
ramacharitamanas::2332.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is shattered by the coming separation, and his words fail him. Ram does not force the moment; he bows low, honors his father, and asks for leave. The scene shows duty carried with tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::2332.modern_relevance: Your parent is too upset to talk, but the flight is booked and the taxi is waiting. You lower your voice, touch their feet or hand, and ask for permission before you go.
ramacharitamanas::2332.insight: It teaches you to meet painful duty with humility, not force.

ramacharitamanas::2333.verse_sanskrit: पितु असीस आयसु मोहि दीजै। हरष समय बिसमउ कत कीजै॥ तात किएँ प्रिय प्रेम प्रमादू। जसु जग जाइ होइ अपबादू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2333.verse_hindi: हे पिताजी! मुझे आशीर्वाद और आज्ञा दीजिए। हर्ष के समय आप शोक क्यों कर रहे हैं? हे तात! प्रिय के प्रेमवश प्रमाद (कर्तव्यकर्म में त्रुटि) करने से जगत में यश जाता रहेगा और निंदा होगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2333.english_translation: Father, give me your blessing and your command. Why do you grieve at a time of joy? Dear father, if affection makes us forget our duty, our fame will be lost and the world will blame us.
ramacharitamanas::2333.translation_literal: पितु (father) / असीस (blessing) / आयसु (command) / मोहि (to me) / दीजै (give) / हरष (joy) / समय (time) / बिसमउ (grief) / कत (why) / कीजै (is done) / तात (dear father) / किएँ (because of) / प्रिय (beloved) / प्रेम (love) / प्रमादू (careless lapse) / जसु (fame) / जग (world) / जाइ (goes) / होइ (becomes) / अपबादू (blame, reproach)
ramacharitamanas::2333.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2333.essence: Affection cannot be allowed to erase duty.
ramacharitamanas::2333.simple_meaning: Ram asks Dasharath for blessing and permission to go ahead with what must be done. He says love should not make a person forget duty, because that brings blame and loss of honour.
ramacharitamanas::2333.simple_insight: Love is real, but it cannot cancel responsibility.
ramacharitamanas::2333.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is overwhelmed as Ram prepares to leave. Ram gently asks for his father's blessing and command, then reminds him that affection must not distort duty. The exile has become a test of royal word and righteous conduct.
ramacharitamanas::2333.modern_relevance: Your parent begs you to stay, but you still have to make the hard call that keeps your promise. The ache is real; the responsibility is still yours.
ramacharitamanas::2333.insight: It teaches you to honour affection without letting it override what must be done.

ramacharitamanas::2334.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सनेह बस उठि नरनाहाँ। बैठारे रघुपति गहि बाहाँ॥ सुनहु तात तुम्ह कहुँ मुनि कहहीं। रामु चराचर नायक अहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2334.verse_hindi: यह सुनकर स्नेहवश राजा ने उठकर श्री रघुनाथजी की बाँह पकड़कर उन्हें बैठा लिया और कहा- हे तात! सुनो, तुम्हारे लिए मुनि लोग कहते हैं कि श्री राम चराचर के स्वामी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2334.english_translation: Hearing this, the king rose in affection, took Raghupati by the arm, and seated him. Then he said, “Listen, father. The sages say that Ram is the lord of all moving and unmoving beings.”
ramacharitamanas::2334.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सनेह बस (because of affection) / उठि (rising) / नरनाहाँ (the king) / बैठारे (seated) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / गहि (grasping) / बाहाँ (arm) ॥ / सुनहु (listen) / तात (father) / तुम्ह कहुँ (for you) / मुनि (sages) / कहहीं (say) / रामु (Ram) / चराचर (moving and unmoving) / नायक (lord) / अहहीं (is)
ramacharitamanas::2334.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2334.essence: Love naturally bows before Ram’s greatness.
ramacharitamanas::2334.simple_meaning: Moved by love, the king seats Ram beside him and says that the sages call Ram the lord of all beings and all that exists.
ramacharitamanas::2334.simple_insight: Love makes reverence natural. The heart rises to honor what it already knows is greater.
ramacharitamanas::2334.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath cannot bear the separation and grief around him. Moved by affection, he draws Ram close, seats him beside him, and speaks of Ram’s cosmic lordship. The scene turns personal love into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2334.modern_relevance: A father pulls his son close after a hard conversation and, for a moment, pride disappears. What remains is the simple recognition that love bows before what it cherishes most.
ramacharitamanas::2334.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract praise to embodied reverence, where affection itself becomes worship.

ramacharitamanas::2335.verse_sanskrit: सुभ अरु असुभ करम अनुहारी। ईसु देइ फलु हृदयँ बिचारी॥ करइ जो करम पाव फल सोई। निगम नीति असि कह सबु कोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2335.verse_hindi: शुभ और अशुभ कर्मों के अनुसार ईश्वर हृदय में विचारकर फल देता है, जो कर्म करता है, वही फल पाता है। ऐसी वेद की नीति है, यह सब कोई कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2335.english_translation: The divine gives fruits in accordance with good and bad deeds, considering them in the heart. One who acts receives that very result; this is the rule of the Vedas, as everyone says.
ramacharitamanas::2335.translation_literal: सुभ (good) / अरु (and) / असुभ (bad) / करम (actions) / अनुहारी (according to) / ईसु (the divine) / देइ (gives) / फलु (fruit/result) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारी (having considered) / करइ (does) / जो (who) / करम (action) / पाव (gets/receives) / फल (fruit/result) / सोई (that very) / निगम (Veda) / नीति (rule) / असि (thus) / कह (says) / सबु (all) / कोई (everyone)
ramacharitamanas::2335.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2335.essence: Every deed carries its own result back to the doer.
ramacharitamanas::2335.simple_meaning: Actions bring matching results. Nothing is random or handed out blindly; the moral quality of what you do returns to you.
ramacharitamanas::2335.simple_insight: Your actions matter more than your excuses. What you plant is what comes back.
ramacharitamanas::2335.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the grief around Dasharath and Ram's exile is turning toward moral reflection. The speaker states a law of action: good and bad deeds bear their own fruit, and the result belongs to the one who acted.
ramacharitamanas::2335.modern_relevance: You send the message in anger, then wait for the reply that stings. The delay feels personal, but the pattern was set by your own hand.
ramacharitamanas::2335.insight: It shifts attention from blaming circumstances to owning the causes you create.

ramacharitamanas::2336.verse_sanskrit: औरु करै अपराधु कोउ और पाव फल भोगु। अति बिचित्र भगवंत गति को जग जानै जोगु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2336.verse_hindi: (किन्तु इस अवसर पर तो इसके विपरीत हो रहा है,) अपराध तो कोई और ही करे और उसके फल का भोग कोई और ही पावे। भगवान की लीला बड़ी ही विचित्र है, उसे जानने योग्य जगत में कौन है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2336.english_translation: Another commits the offense, and another bears the suffering. Who in the world can understand the divine order, which is wonderfully strange?
ramacharitamanas::2336.translation_literal: औरु (and another) / करै (does) / अपराधु (offense) / कोउ (someone) / और (another) / पाव (gets) / फल (result) / भोगु (suffering) / अति (very) / बिचित्र (strange, wondrous) / भगवंत (of the divine) / गति (course, way) / को (who) / जग (world) / जानै (knows) / जोगु (fit, able)
ramacharitamanas::2336.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2336.essence: The consequences of wrongdoing often fall on someone else.
ramacharitamanas::2336.simple_meaning: Wrongdoing and suffering do not always fall on the same person. The world’s order is strange and hard to understand.
ramacharitamanas::2336.simple_insight: It softens the urge to demand neat fairness from life and makes room for humility.
ramacharitamanas::2336.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the king is trying to keep Ram from leaving, while the larger drama of exile is already unfolding. The speaker pauses to note a painful mystery: one person may cause the harm, and another may bear its result.
ramacharitamanas::2336.modern_relevance: You watch a family argument start over one sharp sentence, yet the quietest person at the table ends up carrying the hurt for days. Life does not distribute consequences neatly.
ramacharitamanas::2336.insight: It shifts the mind from rigid moral bookkeeping to humility before events that exceed simple cause and effect.

ramacharitamanas::2337.verse_sanskrit: रायँ राम राखन हित लागी। बहुत उपाय किए छलु त्यागी॥ लखी राम रुख रहत न जाने। धरम धुरंधर धीर सयाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::2337.verse_hindi: राजा ने इस प्रकार श्री रामचन्द्रजी को रखने के लिए छल छोड़कर बहुत से उपाय किए, पर जब उन्होंने धर्मधुरंधर, धीर और बुद्धिमान श्री रामजी का रुख देख लिया और वे रहते हुए न जान पड़े, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2337.english_translation: The king tried many ways, abandoning deceit, to keep Ram there. But when he saw Ram's resolve, steady wisdom, and nobility, he knew Ram would not stay.
ramacharitamanas::2337.translation_literal: रायँ (the king) / राम (Ram) / राखन हित लागी (for the sake of keeping) / बहुत उपाय (many means) / किए (did) / छलु (deceit) / त्यागी (abandoning) ॥ लखी (seeing) / राम रुख (Ram's face/resolve) / रहत न जाने (did not know to remain) / धरम धुरंधर (bearer of dharma) / धीर (calm) / सयाने (wise) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2337.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2337.essence: A firm dharmic resolve ends all argument.
ramacharitamanas::2337.simple_meaning: The king tried every honest and dishonest way to keep Ram from leaving, but Ram's firm, wise resolve made it clear he would not stay.
ramacharitamanas::2337.simple_insight: Sometimes a noble decision cannot be negotiated away, no matter how much we plead.
ramacharitamanas::2337.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the king is desperate to keep Ram close and tries many approaches, even dropping deceit. But Ram stands firm in dharma, calm and unshaken. The scene shows the pain of a father facing a son whose duty cannot be softened.
ramacharitamanas::2337.modern_relevance: You keep rewriting the message, hoping they will stay, but their mind is already made up. At some point, dignity means seeing the decision clearly instead of forcing another round of persuasion.
ramacharitamanas::2337.insight: It teaches you to recognise when duty has already settled the matter, and to stop resisting what must be done.

ramacharitamanas::2338.verse_sanskrit: तब नृप सीय लाइ उर लीन्ही। अति हित बहुत भाँति सिख दीन्ही॥ कहि बन के दुख दुसह सुनाए। सासु ससुर पितु सुख समुझाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2338.verse_hindi: तब राजा ने सीताजी को हृदय से लगा लिया और बड़े प्रेम से बहुत प्रकार की शिक्षा दी। वन के दुःसह दुःख कहकर सुनाए। फिर सास, ससुर तथा पिता के (पास रहने के) सुखों को समझाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2338.english_translation: Then the king drew Sita close to his heart and lovingly instructed her in many ways. He described the unbearable hardships of the forest and explained the comfort of living with her mother-in-law, father-in-law, and father.
ramacharitamanas::2338.translation_literal: तब (then) / नृप (king) / सीय (Sita) / लाइ (bringing) / उर (heart) / लीन्ही (took) / अति (very) / हित (for welfare) / बहुत भाँति (many ways) / सिख (instruction) / दीन्ही (gave) / कहि (saying) / बन (forest) / के (of) / दुख (sorrows) / दुसह (hard to bear) / सुनाए (made hear) / सासु (mother-in-law) / ससुर (father-in-law) / पितु (father) / सुख (comforts) / समुझाए (explained)
ramacharitamanas::2338.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2338.essence: Love can plead, but it cannot change a chosen path.
ramacharitamanas::2338.simple_meaning: Dasharath embraces Sita and gently tries to persuade her by describing the forest's hardships and the comforts of staying with her elders.
ramacharitamanas::2338.simple_insight: Love can still sound like persuasion when someone is trying not to lose what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::2338.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is trying to prevent Sita from going into exile with Ram. He holds her close, speaks tenderly, and contrasts the pain of the forest with the safety of palace life. The scene shows a fatherly plea before loss becomes unavoidable.
ramacharitamanas::2338.modern_relevance: A parent stands in a doorway, voice soft but urgent, trying to keep a child from a hard choice. The words are loving, but the fear underneath is unmistakable.
ramacharitamanas::2338.insight: It shows how attachment speaks through care, trying to protect by reminding someone of comfort and danger.

ramacharitamanas::2339.verse_sanskrit: सिय मनु राम चरन अनुरागा। घरुन सुगमु बनु बिषमु न लागा॥ औरउ सबहिं सीय समुझाई। कहि कहि बिपिन बिपति अधिकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2339.verse_hindi: परन्तु सीताजी का मन श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में अनुरक्त था, इसलिए उन्हें घर अच्छा नहीं लगा और न वन भयानक लगा। फिर और सब लोगों ने भी वन में विपत्तियों की अधिकता बता-बताकर सीताजी को समझाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2339.english_translation: But Sita's mind was attached to Ram's feet, so home felt unwelcome and the forest did not seem terrible. Then everyone else also tried to persuade Sita, repeating how full the forest was of hardships.
ramacharitamanas::2339.translation_literal: सिय (Sita) / मनु (mind) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / अनुरागा (attached) / घरुन (home) / सुगमु (easy) / बनु (forest) / बिषमु (terrible) / न लागा (did not seem) / औरउ (also) / सबहिं (everyone) / सीय (Sita) / समुझाई (explained, persuaded) / कहि कहि (again and again saying) / बिपिन (forest) / बिपति (hardships) / अधिकाई (great amount)
ramacharitamanas::2339.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2339.essence: Love for Ram makes comfort and hardship feel the same.
