ramacharitamanas::2339.simple_meaning: Sita's heart is already with Ram, so neither palace life nor forest hardship changes her mind. The others keep warning her about the dangers ahead.
ramacharitamanas::2339.simple_insight: Love can make hardship feel small, even before it begins.
ramacharitamanas::2339.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has tried every way to soften the blow of exile. Sita listens with a heart fixed on Ram, while the household keeps describing the forest's dangers. Her devotion makes the choice feel already made.
ramacharitamanas::2339.modern_relevance: Your family keeps listing every reason not to leave a safe job, move cities, or follow someone you love. You hear them, but your heart has already chosen what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::2339.insight: It shifts attention from fear of discomfort to the pull of devotion.

ramacharitamanas::2340.verse_sanskrit: सचिव नारि गुर नारि सयानी। सहित सनेह कहहिं मृदु बानी॥ तुम्ह कहुँ तौ न दीन्ह बनबासू। करहु जो कहहिं ससुर गुर सासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2340.verse_hindi: मंत्री सुमंत्रजी की पत्नी और गुरु वशिष्ठजी की स्त्री अरुंधतीजी तथा और भी चतुर स्त्रियाँ स्नेह के साथ कोमल वाणी से कहती हैं कि तुमको तो (राजा ने) वनवास दिया नहीं है, इसलिए जो ससुर, गुरु और सास कहें, तुम तो वही करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2340.english_translation: The wives of ministers, the teacher's wife, and other wise women speak gently and with affection: 'You were not given exile. Do what your father-in-law, teacher, and mother-in-law tell you.'
ramacharitamanas::2340.translation_literal: सचिव (minister) / नारि (women) / गुर (teacher) / नारि (women) / सयानी (wise) / सहित (with) / सनेह (affection) / कहहिं (say) / मृदु (soft) / बानी (speech) ॥ तुम्ह (you) / कहुँ (for) / तौ (indeed) / न (not) / दीन्ह (given) / बनबासू (forest exile) / करहु (do) / जो (what) / कहहिं (say) / ससुर (father-in-law) / गुर (teacher) / सासू (mother-in-law) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2340.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2340.essence: Gentle advice can still pull against the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2340.simple_meaning: Wise women gently tell Sita that she has not been sent into exile, so she should do what her elders ask.
ramacharitamanas::2340.simple_insight: Kind words can still carry pressure. Not every gentle voice is asking for what your heart can bear.
ramacharitamanas::2340.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Ram is sent away, Sita is being counseled by older women around the palace. They speak softly and lovingly, but their advice is practical: she has not been exiled, so she should remain obedient to the elders at home. Their tenderness makes the moment more painful, not less.
ramacharitamanas::2340.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with caring advice from relatives after a family crisis. Everyone sounds loving, but the message is the same: stay, comply, adjust. The pressure feels gentle and heavy at once.
ramacharitamanas::2340.insight: It reveals how social duty can arrive wrapped in affection, making refusal emotionally harder.

ramacharitamanas::2341.verse_sanskrit: सिख सीतलि हित मधुर मृदु सुनि सीतहि न सोहानि। सरद चंद चंदिनि लगत जनु चकई अकुलानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2341.verse_hindi: यह शीतल, हितकारी, मधुर और कोमल सीख सुनने पर सीताजी को अच्छी नहीं लगी। (वे इस प्रकार व्याकुल हो गईं) मानो शरद ऋतु के चन्द्रमा की चाँदनी लगते ही चकई व्याकुल हो उठी हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2341.english_translation: Hearing this cool, helpful, sweet, and gentle counsel did not please Sita. She grew restless like a chakor bird at the sight of autumn moonlight.
ramacharitamanas::2341.translation_literal: सिख (counsel) / सीतलि (cool) / हित (beneficial) / मधुर (sweet) / मृदु (gentle) / सुनि (hearing) / सीतहि (to Sita) / न (not) / सोहानि (pleasing) / सरद (autumn) / चंद (moon) / चंदिनि (moonlight) / लगत (on seeing) / जनु (as if) / चकई (chakor bird) / अकुलानि (restless)
ramacharitamanas::2341.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2341.essence: Gentle advice cannot calm a heart already flying toward love.
ramacharitamanas::2341.simple_meaning: Sita does not welcome the gentle advice meant for her comfort. She feels restless and pained, like a bird disturbed by moonlight.
ramacharitamanas::2341.simple_insight: Love can make even kind advice feel unbearable when it pulls you away from what you cherish.
ramacharitamanas::2341.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita has just been urged to accept the exile calmly. The women around her speak softly and wisely, but her heart is already fixed on Ram. Their comforting words only deepen her ache and agitation.
ramacharitamanas::2341.modern_relevance: A friend says, “It’ll be fine, just stay back.” But your chest tightens because the thing you want most is to go with the person you love. Reasonable advice can still feel wrong when the heart has already chosen.
ramacharitamanas::2341.insight: It shows that emotional truth can overpower polite counsel, especially when devotion is already set on one path.

ramacharitamanas::2342.verse_sanskrit: सीय सकुच बस उतरु न देई। सो सुनि तमकि उठी कैकेई॥ मुनि पट भूषन भाजन आनी। आगें धरि बोली मृदु बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2342.verse_hindi: सीताजी संकोचवश उत्तर नहीं देतीं। इन बातों को सुनकर कैकेयी तमककर उठी। उसने मुनियों के वस्त्र, आभूषण (माला, मेखला आदि) और बर्तन (कमण्डलु आदि) लाकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी के आगे रख दिए और कोमल वाणी से कहा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2342.english_translation: Sita, out of modesty, gave no reply. Hearing this, Kaikeyi sprang up in anger. She brought garments of ascetics, ornaments, and utensils, placed them before Ram, and spoke gently.
ramacharitamanas::2342.translation_literal: सीय (Sita) / सकुच बस (because of modesty) / उतरु (reply) / न देई (did not give) / सो सुनि (hearing that) / तमकि (suddenly, in anger) / उठी (rose) / कैकेई (Kaikeyi) / मुनि-पट (ascetic garments) / भूषन (ornaments) / भाजन (utensils) / आनी (bringing) / आगें (in front) / धरि (placing) / बोली (spoke) / मृदु बानी (soft words)
ramacharitamanas::2342.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2342.essence: Gentle words can carry a decisive blow.
ramacharitamanas::2342.simple_meaning: Sita stays silent from modesty. Kaikeyi reacts sharply, then places ascetic items before Ram and speaks politely.
ramacharitamanas::2342.simple_insight: A soft voice can hide a hard intent. Not every gentle act is gentle at heart.
ramacharitamanas::2342.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace women try to soften Sita with careful words. Sita remains silent. Kaikeyi then rises in sudden anger, brings ascetic clothing and simple vessels, and sets them before Ram. The scene turns from persuasion to the first visible sign of exile.
ramacharitamanas::2342.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone avoids answering the question everyone is circling. Then a person smiles, slides a paper across the table, and changes everything without raising their voice.
ramacharitamanas::2342.insight: It teaches you to watch the force behind polite speech, not just its tone.

ramacharitamanas::2343.verse_sanskrit: नृपहि प्रानप्रिय तुम्ह रघुबीरा। सील सनेह न छाड़िहि भीरा॥ सुकृतु सुजसु परलोकु नसाऊ। तुम्हहि जान बन कहिहि न काऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2343.verse_hindi: हे रघुवीर! राजा को तुम प्राणों के समान प्रिय हो। भीरु (प्रेमवश दुर्बल हृदय के) राजा शील और स्नेह नहीं छोड़ेंगे! पुण्य, सुंदर यश और परलोक चाहे नष्ट हे जाए, पर तुम्हें वन जाने को वे कभी न कहेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2343.english_translation: O Raghuvira, you are dearer to the king than his own life. In fear and love, he will not abandon virtue and affection. Even if merit, good name, and the next world are lost, he will never ask you to go to the forest.
ramacharitamanas::2343.translation_literal: नृपहि (to the king) / प्रानप्रिय (dearer than life) / तुम्ह (you) / रघुबीरा (O Raghuvira) / सील (virtue) / सनेह (affection) / न (not) / छाड़िहि (will leave) / भीरा (fearful one) / सुकृतु (merit) / सुजसु (good fame) / परलोकु (the next world) / नसाऊ (destroyed) / तुम्हहि (you) / जान (knowing) / बन (forest) / कहिहि (will say) / न (not) / काऊ (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::2343.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2343.essence: Tender love can make the hardest duty impossible to speak.
ramacharitamanas::2343.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi says King Dasharath loves Ram more than his own life and would never send him to the forest, even if it ruined his virtue, reputation, and future.
ramacharitamanas::2343.simple_insight: Love can be so strong that it resists the very demand that will later break it.
ramacharitamanas::2343.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi stands before Ram and frames Dasharath's heart as too tender to send his beloved son away. She knows the king's love, and she uses that knowledge to press toward exile. The verse deepens the trap closing around the royal family.
ramacharitamanas::2343.modern_relevance: A parent says, “I could never ask you to leave,” while knowing a hard decision is coming. The tenderness is real — and that is what makes the later break unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2343.insight: It shows how affection can delay duty, even when the cost will be enormous.

ramacharitamanas::2344.verse_sanskrit: अस बिचारि सोइ करहु जो भावा। राम जननि सिख सुनि सुखु पावा॥ भूपहि बचन बानसम लागे। करहिं न प्रान पयान अभागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2344.verse_hindi: ऐसा विचारकर जो तुम्हें अच्छा लगे वही करो। माता की सीख सुनकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने (बड़ा) सुख पाया, परन्तु राजा को ये वचन बाण के समान लगे। (वे सोचने लगे) अब भी अभागे प्राण (क्यों) नहीं निकलते! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2344.english_translation: Thinking thus, do whatever you like. Hearing the mother’s counsel, Ram found joy. The king’s words struck like arrows; the unlucky man still did not die.
ramacharitamanas::2344.translation_literal: अस (thus) / बिचारि (having thought) / सोइ (that same) / करहु (do) / जो (what) / भावा (is pleasing) / राम जननि (Ram's mother) / सिख (instruction) / सुनि (hearing) / सुखु (joy) / पावा (found) / भूपहि (to the king) / बचन (words) / बानसम (like arrows) / लागे (struck) / करहिं (do) / न (not) / प्रान (life-breaths) / पयान (departure) / अभागे (unlucky ones)
ramacharitamanas::2344.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2344.essence: Gentle words can carry the sharpest wound.
ramacharitamanas::2344.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi speaks as if she is giving gentle advice, but her words wound Dasharath deeply. The same words that bring Ram joy feel like arrows to the king.
ramacharitamanas::2344.simple_insight: Words can comfort one heart and break another in the same moment.
ramacharitamanas::2344.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi has just pressed her demands. She speaks softly, but her counsel is part of the trap that will send Ram into exile. Ram receives the instruction with calm joy; Dasharath hears it as a fatal blow.
ramacharitamanas::2344.modern_relevance: A message meant to sound reasonable lands like a slap in a family group chat. One person hears calm advice; another hears betrayal. The same sentence can carry two completely different worlds.
ramacharitamanas::2344.insight: It teaches you to notice how tone and intention can hide harm behind polite language.

ramacharitamanas::2345.verse_sanskrit: लोग बिकल मुरुछित नरनाहू। काह करिअ कछु सूझ न काहू॥ रामु तुरत मुनि बेषु बनाई। चले जनक जननिहि सिरु नाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2345.verse_hindi: राजा मूर्छित हो गए, लोग व्याकुल हैं। किसी को कुछ सूझ नहीं पड़ता कि क्या करें। श्री रामचन्द्रजी तुरंत मुनि का वेष बनाकर और माता-पिता को सिर नवाकर चल दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2345.english_translation: The king fell unconscious, and everyone was distraught. No one knew what to do. Ram at once dressed as a sage and left, bowing to his parents.
ramacharitamanas::2345.translation_literal: लोग (people) / बिकल (agitated, distraught) / मुरुछित (fainted, unconscious) / नरनाहू (the king) / काह (what) / करिअ (is to be done) / कछु (anything) / सूझ (is understood) / न (not) / काहू (to anyone)॥ / रामु (Ram) / तुरत (at once) / मुनि (sage) / बेषु (disguise, attire) / बनाई (making) / चले (went) / जनक (to Janaka) / जननिहि (to his mother) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing)॥
ramacharitamanas::2345.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2345.essence: Duty moves first, even when everyone else is overwhelmed.
ramacharitamanas::2345.simple_meaning: The king collapses, everyone panics, and Ram immediately prepares to leave in the garb of a sage after bowing to his parents.
ramacharitamanas::2345.simple_insight: When duty becomes clear, hesitation ends. He moves at once, even in the middle of grief.
ramacharitamanas::2345.detailed_meaning: Dasharath lies unconscious and the palace is in confusion. No one can think straight. In that moment, Ram does not resist the exile or linger in emotion; he quietly takes on the sage's dress and bows before leaving.
ramacharitamanas::2345.modern_relevance: A family crisis has everyone speaking at once, but one person still packs the bag, makes the call, and steps forward. Clear duty cuts through panic.
ramacharitamanas::2345.insight: It shifts attention from emotional chaos to the one necessary action that must be done now.

ramacharitamanas::2346.verse_sanskrit: सजि बन साजु समाजु सबु बनिता बंधु समेत। बंदि बिप्र गुर चरन प्रभु चले करि सबहि अचेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::2346.verse_hindi: वन का सब साज-सामान सजकर (वन के लिए आवश्यक वस्तुओं को साथ लेकर) श्री रामचन्द्रजी स्त्री (श्री सीताजी) और भाई (लक्ष्मणजी) सहित, ब्राह्मण और गुरु के चरणों की वंदना करके सबको अचेत करके चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2346.english_translation: Having prepared all the forest provisions, the Lord departed with Sita and Lakshman. Bowing to the Brahmins and the guru's feet, he left everyone stunned.
ramacharitamanas::2346.translation_literal: सजि (having prepared) / बन साजु (forest equipment) / समाजु सबु (all provisions) / बनिता (with the woman) / बंधु समेत (together with the brother) / बंदि (bowing) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / गुर चरन (the guru's feet) / प्रभु (the Lord) / चले (departed) / करि (making) / सबहि (everyone) / अचेत (unconscious, stunned)
ramacharitamanas::2346.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2346.essence: Prepare fully, bow properly, and step into exile without complaint.
ramacharitamanas::2346.simple_meaning: Ram leaves for the forest fully prepared, with Sita and Lakshman beside him, after bowing to the guru and the Brahmins.
ramacharitamanas::2346.simple_insight: Even a painful departure can be done with dignity, preparation, and respect.
ramacharitamanas::2346.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is reeling after the exile order. Ram, Sita, and Lakshman prepare the needed forest supplies, bow to the Brahmins and guru, and leave the palace. The whole court is stunned as the exile becomes real.
ramacharitamanas::2346.modern_relevance: You close the apartment door after packing the last box, then pause to thank the neighbor who helped. The move hurts, but the leaving can still be graceful.
ramacharitamanas::2346.insight: It teaches you to meet forced change with readiness and reverence, not panic.

ramacharitamanas::2347.verse_sanskrit: निकसि बसिष्ठ द्वार भए ठाढ़े। देखे लोग बिरह दव दाढ़े॥ कहि प्रिय बचन सकल समुझाए। बिप्र बृंद रघुबीर बोलाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2347.verse_hindi: राजमहल से निकलकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी वशिष्ठजी के दरवाजे पर जा खड़े हुए और देखा कि सब लोग विरह की अग्नि में जल रहे हैं। उन्होंने प्रिय वचन कहकर सबको समझाया, फिर श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने ब्राह्मणों की मंडली को बुलाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2347.english_translation: Leaving the palace, Ram stood at Vashishtha's door and saw everyone burning in the fire of separation. He spoke kind words, comforted them all, and then called the assembly of brahmins.
ramacharitamanas::2347.translation_literal: निकसि (having come out) / बसिष्ठ (Vashishtha) / द्वार (door) / भए (became) / ठाढ़े (standing) / देखे (saw) / लोग (people) / बिरह (separation) / दव (fire) / दाढ़े (burning) / कहि (saying) / प्रिय (dear) / बचन (words) / सकल (all) / समुझाए (consoled, explained) / बिप्र (brahmins) / बृंद (group) / रघुबीर (Ram, hero of the Raghu line) / बोलाए (called)
ramacharitamanas::2347.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2347.essence: Calm words can hold a room on fire.
ramacharitamanas::2347.simple_meaning: Ram steps out, sees everyone suffering from separation, comforts them with gentle words, and gathers the brahmins.
ramacharitamanas::2347.simple_insight: Even in grief, he responds with calm care instead of adding more pain.
ramacharitamanas::2347.detailed_meaning: After the palace upheaval, Ram goes to Vashishtha's door and finds the whole city burning with separation. Rather than sink into the sorrow, he speaks gently, steadies everyone, and calls the brahmin assembly to continue the next steps.
ramacharitamanas::2347.modern_relevance: You walk into a house after bad news, and everyone is frozen, crying, or angry. Instead of feeding the panic, you lower your voice, steady the room, and handle what must be handled.
ramacharitamanas::2347.insight: It teaches emotional steadiness in crisis: soothe others first, then move to action.

ramacharitamanas::2348.verse_sanskrit: गुर सन कहि बरषासन दीन्हे। आदर दान बिनय बस कीन्हे॥ जाचक दान मान संतोषे। मीत पुनीत प्रेम परितोषे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2348.verse_hindi: गुरुजी से कहकर उन सबको वर्षाशन (वर्षभर का भोजन) दिए और आदर, दान तथा विनय से उन्हें वश में कर लिया। फिर याचकों को दान और मान देकर संतुष्ट किया तथा मित्रों को पवित्र प्रेम से प्रसन्न किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2348.english_translation: He gave the guru a year’s provisions, and used respect, gifts, and humility to win them over. He satisfied the beggars with charity and honor, and delighted his friends with pure love.
ramacharitamanas::2348.translation_literal: गुरु सन (to the guru) / कहि (having said) / बरषासन (year’s provisions) / दीन्हे (gave) / आदर (respect) / दान (gifts) / बिनय (humility) / बस (under control) / कीन्हे (made) / जाचक (beggars) / दान (charity) / मान (honor) / संतोषे (satisfied) / मीत (friends) / पुनीत (pure) / प्रेम (love) / परितोषे (delighted)
ramacharitamanas::2348.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2348.essence: True duty includes honoring the teacher, the needy, and the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::2348.simple_meaning: Ram honors the guru, supports the needy, and cares for friends with loving generosity.
ramacharitamanas::2348.simple_insight: Warmth and generosity can settle a tense moment better than force.
ramacharitamanas::2348.detailed_meaning: After leaving the palace, Ram pauses at Vashishtha’s door. The exiled prince does not rush ahead blindly; he first provides for the guru, then for beggars and friends. This verse shows how his exile begins with care, not complaint.
ramacharitamanas::2348.modern_relevance: Before a long move, you pack a box for your teacher, send food to the neighbor who helps everyone, and thank the friend who showed up. Small acts of care steady the whole day.
ramacharitamanas::2348.insight: It shifts duty from bare obedience to generous, relationship-centered action.

ramacharitamanas::2349.verse_sanskrit: दासीं दास बोलाइ बहोरी। गुरहि सौंपि बोले कर जोरी॥ सब कै सार सँभार गोसाईं। करबि जनक जननी की नाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2349.verse_hindi: फिर दास-दासियों को बुलाकर उन्हें गुरुजी को सौंपकर, हाथ जोड़कर बोले- हे गुसाईं! इन सबकी माता-पिता के समान सार-संभार (देख-रेख) करते रहिएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2349.english_translation: Then he called the servants and maidservants again, entrusted them to the guru, and said with folded hands: "Lord, care for all of them as a mother and father would."
ramacharitamanas::2349.translation_literal: दासीं (maidservants) / दास (servants) / बोलाइ (calling) / बहोरी (again) / गुरहि (to the guru) / सौंपि (having entrusted) / बोले (spoke) / कर जोरी (with joined hands) / सब कै (of all) / सार सँभार (care and upkeep) / गोसाईं (Lord) / करबि (do) / जनक जननी (father and mother) / की नाईं (like)
ramacharitamanas::2349.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2349.essence: True duty protects even the smallest people around you.
ramacharitamanas::2349.simple_meaning: Ram hands the servants over to the guru and asks him to care for everyone like a parent would.
ramacharitamanas::2349.simple_insight: Real nobility includes looking after the people around you, not just making a grand gesture.
ramacharitamanas::2349.detailed_meaning: Ram has already reached the guru’s place in the grief-filled exile scene. Now he gathers the servants and maidservants, places them under the guru’s care, and asks for their welfare as if they were children. His conduct shows gentle responsibility in the middle of loss.
ramacharitamanas::2349.modern_relevance: You move out of a house and still worry about the cleaner, the driver, the cook — whether they’ll be looked after. That quiet concern is the standard here.
ramacharitamanas::2349.insight: It shifts duty from self-protection to protective care for everyone dependent on you.

ramacharitamanas::2350.verse_sanskrit: बारहिं बार जोरि जुग पानी। कहत रामु सब सन मृदु बानी॥ सोइ सब भाँति मोर हितकारी। जेहि तें रहै भुआल सुखारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2350.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी बार-बार दोनों हाथ जोड़कर सबसे कोमल वाणी कहते हैं कि मेरा सब प्रकार से हितकारी मित्र वही होगा, जिसकी चेष्टा से महाराज सुखी रहें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2350.english_translation: Rama repeatedly folded his hands and spoke gently to everyone: "My true well-wisher is the one whose efforts keep the king happy."
ramacharitamanas::2350.translation_literal: बारहिं बार (again and again) / जोरि (joining) / जुग पानी (both hands) / कहत (speaking) / रामु (Rama) / सब सन (to everyone) / मृदु बानी (gentle speech)॥ / सोइ (that one) / सब भाँति (in every way) / मोर (my) / हितकारी (beneficial friend) / जेहि तें (by whose means) / रहै (remain) / भुआल (the king) / सुखारी (happy) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2350.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2350.essence: Real help is whatever truly steadies the one who must be protected.
ramacharitamanas::2350.simple_meaning: Rama speaks politely to everyone and says that the real helper is the one who keeps the king content and at ease.
ramacharitamanas::2350.simple_insight: True service is measured by whether it protects the one you serve, not by how much attention you receive.
ramacharitamanas::2350.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Rama is preparing for exile and speaking to the people around him with folded hands and soft words. He is not asking for comfort for himself; he is identifying the kind of support that matters most — whatever keeps King Dasharath peaceful.
ramacharitamanas::2350.modern_relevance: You are trying to help a family member through a hard day, and the loudest advice is not the best one. Real support is the choice that actually eases their burden, not the one that makes you feel useful.
ramacharitamanas::2350.insight: It shifts attention from self-expression to practical care for the person at the center of the situation.

ramacharitamanas::2351.verse_sanskrit: मातु सकल मोरे बिरहँ जेहिं न होहिं दुख दीन। सोइ उपाउ तुम्ह करेहु सब पुर जन परम प्रबीन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2351.verse_hindi: हे परम चतुर पुरवासी सज्जनों! आप लोग सब वही उपाए कीजिएगा, जिससे मेरी सब माताएँ मेरे विरह के दुःख से दुःखी न हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::2351.english_translation: O most skilful people of the city, please do whatever ensures that all my mothers do not suffer grief from my separation.
ramacharitamanas::2351.translation_literal: मातु (mothers) / सकल (all) / मोरे (my) / बिरहँ (from separation) / जेहिं (by which) / न होहिं (do not become) / दुख (sorrow) / दीन (afflicted) / सोइ (that) / उपाउ (means) / तुम्ह (you all) / करेहु (do) / सब (all) / पुर (city) / जन (people) / परम (most) / प्रबीन (skilful)
ramacharitamanas::2351.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2351.essence: True care measures separation by the pain it leaves behind.
ramacharitamanas::2351.simple_meaning: Ram asks the city’s wise people to find a way that keeps his mothers from suffering because of his separation.
ramacharitamanas::2351.simple_insight: Love becomes practical when it tries to spare others pain.
ramacharitamanas::2351.detailed_meaning: Ram is preparing to leave Ayodhya, and his heart is already thinking of the women who raised him. He asks the city’s wise people to arrange things so his mothers will not be crushed by his absence. The moment shows his tenderness before exile.
ramacharitamanas::2351.modern_relevance: You are packing for a move and keep thinking about the parent who will sit in the quiet after you leave. Real care means planning for their hurt, not just your departure.
ramacharitamanas::2351.insight: It shifts attention from personal departure to the burden that departure places on others.

ramacharitamanas::2352.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि राम सबहि समुझावा। गुर पद पदुम हरषि सिरु नावा॥ गनपति गौरि गिरीसु मनाई। चले असीस पाइ रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2352.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार श्री रामजी ने सबको समझाया और हर्षित होकर गुरुजी के चरणकमलों में सिर नवाया। फिर गणेशजी, पार्वतीजी और कैलासपति महादेवजी को मनाकर तथा आशीर्वाद पाकर श्री रघुनाथजी चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2352.english_translation: In this way, Ram explained everything to everyone, then joyfully bowed his head to the lotus feet of his teacher. After pleasing Ganesh, Parvati, and Lord Shiva, and receiving their blessings, Raghunath departed.
ramacharitamanas::2352.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / राम (Ram) / सबहि (everyone) / समुझावा (explained) / गुर (teacher) / पद (feet) / पदुम (lotus) / हरषि (joyfully) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) / गनपति (Ganapati) / गौरि (Parvati) / गिरीसु (Lord of the mountain, Shiva) / मनाई (having pleased) / चले (departed) / असीस (blessings) / पाइ (having received) / रघुराई (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::2352.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2352.essence: True dignity bows before it moves on.
ramacharitamanas::2352.simple_meaning: Ram settles everyone’s concerns, bows to his teacher, honors Ganesh, Parvati, and Shiva, and leaves with their blessings.
ramacharitamanas::2352.simple_insight: Even the one who is revered still bows, honors others, and departs with grace.
ramacharitamanas::2352.detailed_meaning: After explaining the situation to everyone, Ram first bows to his teacher with joy. He then honors Ganesh, Parvati, and Shiva before leaving. The verse shows the dignity of his departure and the sacredness of this farewell moment.
ramacharitamanas::2352.modern_relevance: You finish a hard conversation, thank the people who guided you, and leave without ego. The moment stays clean because you did not make it about yourself.
ramacharitamanas::2352.insight: It teaches graceful departure: resolve what must be said, honor your teachers, and move on without self-importance.

ramacharitamanas::2353.verse_sanskrit: राम चलत अति भयउ बिषादू। सुनि न जाइ पुर आरत नादू॥ कुसगुन लंक अवध अति सोकू। हरष बिषाद बिबस सुरलोकू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2353.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के चलते ही बड़ा भारी विषाद हो गया। नगर का आर्तनाद (हाहाकर) सुना नहीं जाता। लंका में बुरे शकुन होने लगे, अयोध्या में अत्यन्त शोक छा गया और देवलोक में सब हर्ष और विषाद दोनों के वश में गए। (हर्ष इस बात का था कि अब राक्षसों का नाश होगा और विषाद अयोध्यावासियों के शोक के कारण था) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2353.english_translation: As Rama departed, deep grief arose. The city's cries could not be borne. Ominous signs appeared in Lanka, great sorrow fell on Ayodhya, and even the heavenly worlds were caught between joy and grief.
ramacharitamanas::2353.translation_literal: राम (Rama) / चलत (departing) / अति (very) / भयउ (became) / बिषादू (grief) / सुनि (hearing) / न जाइ (cannot be endured) / पुर (city) / आरत (anguished) / नादू (cries) / कुसगुन (bad omens) / लंक (Lanka) / अवध (Ayodhya) / अति (great) / सोकू (sorrow) / हरष (joy) / बिषाद (grief) / बिबस (helplessly under) / सुरलोकू (the heavenly worlds)
ramacharitamanas::2353.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2353.essence: Rama's departure sends grief and omens through every realm.
ramacharitamanas::2353.simple_meaning: Rama's departure shakes every world: Ayodhya grieves, Lanka shows bad omens, and even the higher worlds feel mixed joy and sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2353.simple_insight: A single departure can ripple through many lives at once.
ramacharitamanas::2353.detailed_meaning: Rama has left Ayodhya for the forest, and the emotional shock spreads everywhere. The people cry, Lanka sees bad signs, Ayodhya sinks into grief, and even the celestial realms feel divided. This verse paints the atmosphere, not the argument.
ramacharitamanas::2353.modern_relevance: A train pulls away after a goodbye no one wanted. One person leaves, but the whole house feels altered — and everyone reacts differently to the same loss.
ramacharitamanas::2353.insight: It shifts attention from one event to the many layers of grief and consequence it creates.

ramacharitamanas::2354.verse_sanskrit: गइ मुरुछा तब भूपति जागे। बोलि सुमंत्रु कहन अस लागे॥ रामु चले बन प्रान न जाहीं। केहि सुख लागि रहत तन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2354.verse_hindi: मूर्छा दूर हुई, तब राजा जागे और सुमंत्र को बुलाकर ऐसा कहने लगे- श्री राम वन को चले गए, पर मेरे प्राण नहीं जा रहे हैं। न जाने ये किस सुख के लिए शरीर में टिक रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2354.english_translation: When his fainting passed, the king woke and called Sumantra, saying: "Rama has gone to the forest, yet my life does not leave. For what happiness does this body still remain?"
ramacharitamanas::2354.translation_literal: गइ (gone) / मुरुछा (fainting) / तब (then) / भूपति (the king) / जागे (awoke) / बोलि (calling) / सुमंत्रु (Sumantra) / कहन (to say) / अस (thus) / लागे (began)॥ / रामु (Rama) / चले (has gone) / बन (to the forest) / प्रान (life-breath) / न (not) / जाहीं (go)॥ / केहि (for what) / सुख (happiness) / लागि (for) / रहत (remain) / तन (body) / माहीं (in) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2354.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2354.essence: Life can remain in the body after joy has already left.
ramacharitamanas::2354.simple_meaning: Dasharath wakes from fainting and realizes Rama has gone to the forest. He feels his own life should leave too, because the body has no joy left without Rama.
ramacharitamanas::2354.simple_insight: Some losses are so deep that ordinary survival feels strange and empty.
ramacharitamanas::2354.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has just heard the unbearable news of Rama's exile. After fainting, he wakes and calls Sumantra. His words show a father and king whose inner life has already broken, even though his body still remains.
ramacharitamanas::2354.modern_relevance: You open your phone and see the message that changes everything. The room is the same, your body is the same, but the person who made life feel alive is suddenly gone.
ramacharitamanas::2354.insight: It shifts attention from outward survival to the inner fact of grief: the body can remain while the person feels already gone.

ramacharitamanas::2355.verse_sanskrit: एहि तें कवन ब्यथा बलवाना। जो दुखु पाइ तजहिं तनु प्राना॥ पुनि धरि धीर कहइ नरनाहू। लै रथु संग सखा तुम्ह जाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2355.verse_hindi: इससे अधिक बलवती और कौन सी व्यथा होगी, जिस दुःख को पाकर प्राण शरीर को छोड़ेंगे। फिर धीरज धरकर राजा ने कहा- हे सखा! तुम रथ लेकर श्री राम के साथ जाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2355.english_translation: What pain could be greater than this, when grief makes life leave the body? Then, gathering himself, the king said, “Friend, take the chariot and go with Ram.”
ramacharitamanas::2355.translation_literal: एहि तें (than this) / कवन (which) / ब्यथा (pain) / बलवाना (stronger) / जो (which) / दुखु (grief) / पाइ (having received) / तजहिं (leave) / तनु (body) / प्राना (life-breath) ॥ / पुनि (again) / धरि (holding) / धीर (steadiness) / कहइ (says) / नरनाहू (the king) / लै (take) / रथु (chariot) / संग (with) / सखा (friend) / तुम्ह (you) / जाहू (go) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2355.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2355.essence: Grief can break the body and still leave duty intact.
ramacharitamanas::2355.simple_meaning: Dasharath says no pain is greater than this grief, because it is killing him. After steadying himself, he asks Sumantra to take the chariot and go with Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2355.simple_insight: Even heartbreak can still make room for one final act of care.
ramacharitamanas::2355.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has just awakened from collapse after hearing that Ram has gone to the forest. The king feels grief so strong it seems to drain life itself, yet he gathers himself enough to send Sumantra after Ram with the chariot.
ramacharitamanas::2355.modern_relevance: You get the worst news of your life, sit in silence for a long minute, and still manage one careful text to help someone else. Grief does not erase duty.
ramacharitamanas::2355.insight: It shifts the mind from self-consuming pain to one last responsible action.

ramacharitamanas::2356.verse_sanskrit: सुठि सुकुमार कुमार दोउ जनकसुता सुकुमारि। रथ चढ़ाइ देखराइ बनु फिरेहु गएँ दिन चारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2356.verse_hindi: अत्यन्त सुकुमार दोनों कुमारों को और सुकुमारी जानकी को रथ में चढ़ाकर, वन दिखलाकर चार दिन के बाद लौट आना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2356.english_translation: Take the very tender princes and the tender daughter of Janaka in the chariot, show them the forest, and return after four days.
ramacharitamanas::2356.translation_literal: सुठि (very) / सुकुमार (tender, delicate) / कुमार (princes) / दोउ (both) / जनकसुता (daughter of Janaka) / सुकुमारि (tender, delicate woman) / रथ (chariot) / चढ़ाइ (having placed) / देखराइ (showing) / बनु (forest) / फिरेहु (return) / गएँ (after) / दिन (days) / चारि (four)
ramacharitamanas::2356.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2356.essence: Grief turns exile into a brief errand to survive the pain.
ramacharitamanas::2356.simple_meaning: Dasharath asks that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita be taken by chariot to see the forest and brought back after four days.
ramacharitamanas::2356.simple_insight: A father tries to soften unbearable separation by making it sound temporary.
ramacharitamanas::2356.detailed_meaning: Dasharath, crushed by Rama’s exile, is speaking to Sumantra with a heart already breaking. He tries to frame the impossible as a short outing: take the delicate trio to the forest and return in four days. The line reveals how grief bargains with reality.
ramacharitamanas::2356.modern_relevance: You keep saying, “Just a few days,” while helping someone pack for a move that changes everything. The mind reaches for any small promise that makes loss feel manageable.
ramacharitamanas::2356.insight: It shows how grief clings to a temporary story when it cannot bear permanent loss.

ramacharitamanas::2357.verse_sanskrit: जौं नहिं फिरहिं धीर दोउ भाई। सत्यसंध दृढ़ब्रत रघुराई॥ तौ तुम्ह बिनय करेहु कर जोरी। फेरिअ प्रभु मिथिलेसकिसोरी ॥॥
ramacharitamanas::2357.verse_hindi: यदि धैर्यवान दोनों भाई न लौटें- क्योंकि श्री रघुनाथजी प्रण के सच्चे और दृढ़ता से नियम का पालन करने वाले हैं- तो तुम हाथ जोड़कर विनती करना कि हे प्रभो! जनककुमारी सीताजी को तो लौटा दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2357.english_translation: If the two brothers do not return, for Raghunath is steadfast in truth and fixed vows, then you should pray with folded hands: "Lord, please send back the princess of Mithila."
ramacharitamanas::2357.translation_literal: जौं (if) / नहिं (not) / फिरहिं (return) / धीर (steadfast) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / सत्यसंध (bound to truth) / दृढ़ब्रत (firm in vows) / रघुराई (Raghurama) / तौ (then) / तुम्ह (you) / बिनय (request) / करेहु (do) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined) / फेरिअ (send back) / प्रभु (Lord) / मिथिलेसकिसोरी (princess of Mithila)
ramacharitamanas::2357.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2357.essence: Steadfast vows can make one request more important than everything else.
ramacharitamanas::2357.simple_meaning: If the brothers do not come back, ask only for Sita to be returned. Dasharath trusts Ram's vow and focuses on protecting the daughter-in-law.
ramacharitamanas::2357.simple_insight: Love becomes clear when it stops asking for everything and asks for the one thing that matters most.
ramacharitamanas::2357.detailed_meaning: Dasharath, already crushed by the thought of exile, gives one final instruction. If Ram and Lakshman stay away, the king knows Ram will keep his word. So he asks only that Sita, the princess of Mithila, be brought back safely.
ramacharitamanas::2357.modern_relevance: A parent watches a child leave for a hard move across the country and cannot fix everything. In the middle of helplessness, the heart narrows to one urgent prayer: keep the one who is most vulnerable safe.
ramacharitamanas::2357.insight: It shifts attention from broad loss to the one responsibility that cannot be neglected.

ramacharitamanas::2358.verse_sanskrit: जब सिय कानन देखि डेराई। कहेहु मोरि सिख अवसरु पाई॥ सासु ससुर अस कहेउ सँदेसू। पुत्रि फिरिअ बन बहुत कलेसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2358.verse_hindi: जब सीता वन को देखकर डरें, तब मौका पाकर मेरी यह सीख उनसे कहना कि तुम्हारे सास और ससुर ने ऐसा संदेश कहा है कि हे पुत्री! तुम लौट चलो, वन में बहुत क्लेश हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2358.english_translation: When Sita sees the forest and grows afraid, then, at a fitting moment, say this to her: 'Your mother-in-law and father-in-law have sent this message: Daughter, return home. The forest holds much hardship.'
ramacharitamanas::2358.translation_literal: जब (when) / सिय (Sita) / कानन (forest) / देखि (seeing) / डेराई (becomes afraid) / कहेहु (say) / मोरि (my) / सिख (instruction) / अवसरु (opportunity) / पाई (having found)॥ / सासु (mother-in-law) / ससुर (father-in-law) / अस (thus) / कहेउ (said) / सँदेसू (message) / पुत्रि (daughter) / फिरिअ (return) / बन (forest) / बहुत (much) / कलेसू (hardship) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2358.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2358.essence: Borrowed concern can hide a controlling intent.
ramacharitamanas::2358.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi tells the messenger to speak gently to Sita if the forest frightens her, and to urge her to return because forest life is full of hardship.
ramacharitamanas::2358.simple_insight: A fearful moment can be used to push someone toward the choice you want.
ramacharitamanas::2358.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi is still shaping the exile plan through careful words. She instructs the messenger to wait until Sita looks uneasy about the forest, then deliver a message from her elders asking her to return home.
ramacharitamanas::2358.modern_relevance: Someone waits until you look uncertain, then calls it concern and presses you toward the safer choice. The timing is gentle; the intention is not.
ramacharitamanas::2358.insight: It shows how persuasion often works through borrowed authority and emotional vulnerability.

ramacharitamanas::2359.verse_sanskrit: पितुगृह कबहुँ कबहुँ ससुरारी। रहेहु जहाँ रुचि होइ तुम्हारी॥ एहि बिधि करेहु उपाय कदंबा। फिरइ त होइ प्रान अवलंबा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2359.verse_hindi: कभी पिता के घर, कभी ससुराल, जहाँ तुम्हारी इच्छा हो, वहीं रहना। इस प्रकार तुम बहुत से उपाय करना। यदि सीताजी लौट आईं तो मेरे प्राणों को सहारा हो जाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2359.english_translation: Stay sometimes in your father’s house, sometimes in your in-laws’ house, wherever you wish. In this way, use any means. If Sita returns, it will become the support of my life.
ramacharitamanas::2359.translation_literal: पितुगृह (father’s house) / कबहुँ (sometimes) / कबहुँ (sometimes) / ससुरारी (in-laws’ house) / रहेहु (stay) / जहाँ (where) / रुचि (wish) / होइ (is) / तुम्हारी (your) / एहि (this) / बिधि (way) / करेहु (do) / उपाय (means) / कदंबा (many) / फिरइ (returns) / त (then) / होइ (becomes) / प्रान (life-breath) / अवलंबा (support)
ramacharitamanas::2359.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2359.essence: Desperation will offer any bargain to keep love from leaving.
ramacharitamanas::2359.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is still trying to bring Sita back by offering her any arrangement she wants, hoping that Sita’s return will save Dasharath’s life.
ramacharitamanas::2359.simple_insight: Desperation will bargain with anything when love and fear are both at their peak.
ramacharitamanas::2359.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi is speaking in the middle of a desperate appeal after exile has shattered the family. She tries every possible arrangement to persuade Sita to return, because Dasharath’s life now feels tied to her coming back.
ramacharitamanas::2359.modern_relevance: You keep texting, calling, and making promises you never planned to make because someone you love is slipping away. Panic makes the mind negotiate with reality.
ramacharitamanas::2359.insight: It shows how fear can make a person grasp at any compromise to undo loss.

ramacharitamanas::2360.verse_sanskrit: नाहिं त मोर मरनु परिनामा। कछु न बसाइ भएँ बिधि बामा॥ अस कहि मुरुछि परा महि राऊ। रामु लखनु सिय आनि देखाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2360.verse_hindi: (नहीं तो अंत में मेरा मरण ही होगा। विधाता के विपरीत होने पर कुछ वश नहीं चलता। हा! राम, लक्ष्मण और सीता को लाकर दिखाओ। ऐसा कहकर राजा मूर्छित होकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::2360.english_translation: “Otherwise, my death will be the result. Nothing can be done when fate turns hostile.” Saying this, the king fainted and fell to the earth. “Bring Ram, Lakshman, and Sita before me.”
ramacharitamanas::2360.translation_literal: नाहिं (otherwise/not) / त (then) / मोर (my) / मरनु (death) / परिनामा (result/end) / कछु (something) / न (not) / बसाइ (is in control) / भएँ (when becoming) / बिधि (fate/divine ordinance) / बामा (hostile/wrong) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / मुरुछि (fainted) / परा (fell) / महि (on the earth) / राऊ (king) / रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / आनि (bringing) / देखाऊ (show me)
ramacharitamanas::2360.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2360.essence: When helplessness deepens, even a king collapses.
ramacharitamanas::2360.simple_meaning: Dasharath collapses under grief and helplessness. He feels that if Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are not brought back, death is all that remains.
ramacharitamanas::2360.simple_insight: Some grief is so complete that the body gives way before the heart can speak.
ramacharitamanas::2360.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has already lost control of the crisis that sent Ram into exile. Overwhelmed by sorrow and helplessness, he says nothing can be done against hostile fate, then faints and falls, crying for Ram, Lakshman, and Sita to be brought before him.
ramacharitamanas::2360.modern_relevance: You stare at an empty chair after the argument, the phone still silent, and your chest tightens because nothing you can say will undo what has happened.
ramacharitamanas::2360.insight: It shows grief at the edge of surrender, where speech breaks and the body registers loss first.

ramacharitamanas::2361.verse_sanskrit: पाइ रजायसु नाइ सिरु रथु अति बेग बनाइ। गयउ जहाँ बाहेर नगर सीय सहित दोउ भाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2361.verse_hindi: सुमंत्रजी राजा की आज्ञा पाकर, सिर नवाकर और बहुत जल्दी रथ जुड़वाकर वहाँ गए, जहाँ नगर के बाहर सीताजी सहित दोनों भाई थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2361.english_translation: Receiving the king's command, Sumantra bowed his head, quickly prepared the chariot, and went to where the two brothers were outside the city with Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2361.translation_literal: पाइ (receiving) / रजायसु (royal command) / नाइ (bowing) / सिरु (head) / रथु (chariot) / अति बेग (very quickly) / बनाइ (having prepared) / गयउ (went) / जहाँ (where) / बाहेर (outside) / नगर (city) / सीय (Sita) / सहित (along with) / दोउ (both) / भाइ (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::2361.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2361.simple_meaning: Sumantra obeys the king at once, prepares the chariot quickly, and goes to Rama, Lakshman, and Sita outside the city.
ramacharitamanas::2361.simple_insight: Sometimes the right response is simple obedience, carried out without delay.
ramacharitamanas::2361.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, King Dasharath has fallen into helpless grief and orders Sumantra to bring Rama back. Sumantra bows, acts at once, and goes to the city outskirts where Rama, Lakshman, and Sita are waiting, setting up the painful return scene.
ramacharitamanas::2361.modern_relevance: Your manager calls with a last-minute change, and you stop arguing and just move. The moment is not for drama; it is for clean, immediate response.
ramacharitamanas::2361.insight: It shifts attention from hesitation to prompt, respectful action when a rightful command arrives.

ramacharitamanas::2362.verse_sanskrit: तब सुमंत्र नृप बचन सुनाए। करि बिनती रथ रामु चढ़ाए॥ चढ़ि रथ सीय सहित दोउ भाई। चले हृदयँ अवधहि सिरु नाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2362.verse_hindi: तब (वहाँ पहुँचकर) सुमंत्र ने राजा के वचन श्री रामचन्द्रजी को सुनाए और विनती करके उनको रथ पर चढ़ाया। सीताजी सहित दोनों भाई रथ पर चढ़कर हृदय में अयोध्या को सिर नवाकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2362.english_translation: Then Sumantra conveyed the king's command, and with humble request helped Ram onto the chariot. The two brothers rode with Sita and departed, bowing their hearts to Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::2362.translation_literal: तब (then) / सुमंत्र (Sumantra) / नृप (king's) / बचन (words) / सुनाए (made heard, conveyed) / करि (having done) / बिनती (request, entreaty) / रथ (chariot) / रामु (Ram) / चढ़ाए (made ascend) / चढ़ि (having mounted) / रथ (chariot) / सीय (Sita) / सहित (together with) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / चले (went, departed) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / अवधहि (to Ayodhya) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing)
ramacharitamanas::2362.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2362.essence: A painful departure can still be carried with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2362.simple_meaning: Sumantra brings the king's order, places Ram on the chariot, and the three depart after bowing inwardly to Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::2362.simple_insight: Sometimes leaving with honor matters more than staying with comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2362.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has reached Ram with Dasharath's command. After pleading respectfully, he seats Ram, Sita, and Lakshman in the chariot. They leave Ayodhya in silence, carrying the city's blessing in their hearts as exile begins.
ramacharitamanas::2362.modern_relevance: You pack the car after a family argument, everyone quiet, nobody wanting the moment to be real. The departure itself carries the grief.
ramacharitamanas::2362.insight: It shifts attention from the mechanics of departure to the dignity of leaving with inward respect.

ramacharitamanas::2363.verse_sanskrit: चलत रामु लखि अवध अनाथा। बिकल लोग सब लागे साथा॥ कृपासिंधु बहुबिधि समुझावहिं। फिरहिं प्रेम बस पुनि फिरि आवहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2363.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी को जाते हुए और अयोध्या को अनाथ (होते हुए) देखकर सब लोग व्याकुल होकर उनके साथ हो लिए। कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामजी उन्हें बहुत तरह से समझाते हैं, तो वे (अयोध्या की ओर) लौट जाते हैं, परन्तु प्रेमवश फिर लौट आते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2363.english_translation: Seeing Ram depart, Ayodhya felt orphaned. The people became distraught and followed him. The ocean of compassion tried many ways to comfort them, but they returned only to come back again out of love.
ramacharitamanas::2363.translation_literal: चलत (departing) / रामु (Ram) / लखि (seeing) / अवध (Ayodhya) / अनाथा (orphaned) / बिकल (distressed) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / लागे (began) / साथा (with him) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / समुझावहिं (he comforts/explains) / फिरहिं (they return) / प्रेम (love) / बस (under the control of) / पुनि (again) / फिरि (return) / आवहिं (they come)
ramacharitamanas::2363.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2363.essence: Love overrules farewell and keeps calling people back.
ramacharitamanas::2363.simple_meaning: As Ram leaves, Ayodhya feels abandoned and everyone runs after him. Ram gently tries to calm them, but love keeps drawing them back to him.
ramacharitamanas::2363.simple_insight: Love can be so strong that even farewell becomes a form of return.
ramacharitamanas::2363.detailed_meaning: Ram is leaving Ayodhya for exile, and the city feels suddenly parentless. The people trail after him in grief. Ram, the ocean of compassion, keeps soothing them, but their love overpowers their restraint and pulls them back again.
ramacharitamanas::2363.modern_relevance: You watch someone you depend on walk out of the room, and the whole place feels hollow. You try to act normal, then find yourself following them just to stay near a little longer.
ramacharitamanas::2363.insight: It shifts attention from formal departure to the pull of attachment that keeps reversing separation.

ramacharitamanas::2364.verse_sanskrit: लागति अवध भयावनि भारी। मानहुँ कालराति अँधिआरी॥ घोर जंतु सम पुर नर नारी। डरपहिं एकहि एक निहारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2364.verse_hindi: अयोध्यापुरी बड़ी डरावनी लग रही है, मानो अंधकारमयी कालरात्रि ही हो। नगर के नर-नारी भयानक जन्तुओं के समान एक-दूसरे को देखकर डर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2364.english_translation: Ayodhya felt terribly fearsome, as if dark Night herself had come. The city's men and women feared one another like savage creatures.
ramacharitamanas::2364.translation_literal: लागति (seemed) / अवध (Ayodhya) / भयावनि (fearsome) / भारी (very great) / मानहुँ (as if) / कालराति (night of death) / अँधिआरी (dark)॥ / घोर (terrible) / जंतु (creatures) / सम (like) / पुर (city) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / डरपहिं (were afraid) / एकहि एक (of one another) / निहारी (seeing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2364.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2364.essence: Loss can make a familiar city feel like a dark wilderness.
ramacharitamanas::2364.simple_meaning: Ayodhya feels so dark and shaken that everyone fears everyone else.
ramacharitamanas::2364.simple_insight: Grief can make a whole home feel unsafe, even when nothing outside has changed.
ramacharitamanas::2364.detailed_meaning: Ram has just left Ayodhya. The city that once felt secure now seems swallowed by darkness, and its people turn fearful and unstable. This verse deepens the atmosphere of collective grief before the next image of collapse.
ramacharitamanas::2364.modern_relevance: A house goes silent after one devastating argument. Nobody says it, but everyone moves carefully, afraid of the next glance or word.
ramacharitamanas::2364.insight: It turns grief into atmosphere: a broken bond can distort how an entire community sees itself.

ramacharitamanas::2365.verse_sanskrit: घर मसान परिजन जनु भूता। सुत हित मीत मनहुँ जमदूता॥ बागन्ह बिटप बेलि कुम्हिलाहीं। सरित सरोवर देखि न जाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2365.verse_hindi: घर श्मशान, कुटुम्बी भूत-प्रेत और पुत्र, हितैषी और मित्र मानो यमराज के दूत हैं। बगीचों में वृक्ष और बेलें कुम्हला रही हैं। नदी और तालाब ऐसे भयानक लगते हैं कि उनकी ओर देखा भी नहीं जाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2365.english_translation: The house feels like a cremation ground; relatives seem like ghosts; sons, friends, and well-wishers seem like messengers of death. The garden trees and vines wither, and rivers and ponds are too dreadful even to look at.
ramacharitamanas::2365.translation_literal: घर (house) / मसान (cremation ground) / परिजन (relatives) / जनु (as if) / भूता (ghosts) / सुत (sons) / हित (well-wishers) / मीत (friends) / मनहुँ (as if) / जमदूता (messengers of death) / बागन्ह (in gardens) / बिटप (trees) / बेलि (vines) / कुम्हिलाहीं (wither) / सरित (rivers) / सरोवर (ponds) / देखि (seeing) / न (not) / जाहीं (go)
ramacharitamanas::2365.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2365.essence: Grief can turn home itself into a place of fear.
ramacharitamanas::2365.simple_meaning: Ayodhya feels so grief-stricken that home, family, friends, gardens, rivers, and ponds all seem frightening and lifeless.
ramacharitamanas::2365.simple_insight: Grief can make even familiar places feel haunted and empty.
ramacharitamanas::2365.detailed_meaning: Ram has left Ayodhya, and the whole city is collapsing under sorrow. People no longer see home as home; relatives, friends, and even the natural world feel ominous. The verse deepens the picture of a kingdom that has lost its center.
ramacharitamanas::2365.modern_relevance: You walk into a house after bad news and everything feels wrong — the chairs, the plants, even the silence. Loss can change the whole shape of a place.
ramacharitamanas::2365.insight: It shows how sorrow distorts perception, turning ordinary life into something unbearable.

ramacharitamanas::2366.verse_sanskrit: हय गय कोटिन्ह केलिमृग पुरपसु चातक मोर। पिक रथांग सुक सारिका सारस हंस चकोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::2366.verse_hindi: करोड़ों घोड़े, हाथी, खेलने के लिए पाले हुए हिरन, नगर के (गाय, बैल, बकरी आदि) पशु, पपीहे, मोर, कोयल, चकवे, तोते, मैना, सारस, हंस और चकोर- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2366.english_translation: Millions of horses and elephants, tame deer, city animals, and birds like chataka, peacock, cuckoo, chakravaka, parrot, myna, saras, swan, and chakor.
ramacharitamanas::2366.translation_literal: हय (horses) / गय (elephants) / कोटिन्ह (millions) / केलिमृग (tame deer) / पुरपसु (city animals) / चातक (chataka bird) / मोर (peacock) / पिक (cuckoo) / रथांग (chakravaka) / सुक (parrot) / सारिका (myna) / सारस (saras bird) / हंस (swan) / चकोर (chakor)
ramacharitamanas::2366.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2366.essence: The city’s sorrow spreads until even its creatures seem changed.
ramacharitamanas::2366.simple_meaning: Ayodhya is filled with countless animals and birds, all listed as part of the scene. The verse deepens the sense that the whole city is shaken by Ram's absence.
ramacharitamanas::2366.simple_insight: Even the living world around you can feel the weight of separation.
ramacharitamanas::2366.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya has already been shown as terrifying and grief-stricken. Now the narrator widens the scene: horses, elephants, tame deer, city animals, and many birds all seem caught in the same sorrow. This is not a teaching verse on its own, but part of the city's mourning.
ramacharitamanas::2366.modern_relevance: A house goes strangely quiet after someone leaves for good. The pets, the rooms, the familiar sounds — everything still exists, but the whole place feels altered.
ramacharitamanas::2366.insight: It shifts attention from human grief alone to a whole environment marked by absence.

ramacharitamanas::2367.verse_sanskrit: राम बियोग बिकल सब ठाढ़े। जहँ तहँ मनहुँ चित्र लिखि काढ़े॥ नगरु सफल बनु गहबर भारी। खग मृग बिपुल सकल नर नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2367.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के वियोग में सभी व्याकुल हुए जहाँ-तहाँ (ऐसे चुपचाप स्थिर होकर) खड़े हैं, मानो तसवीरों में लिखकर बनाए हुए हैं। नगर मानो फलों से परिपूर्ण बड़ा भारी सघन वन था। नगर निवासी सब स्त्री-पुरुष बहुत से पशु-पक्षी थे। (अर्थात अवधपुरी अर्थ, धर्म, काम, मोक्ष चारों फलों को देने वाली नगरी थी और सब स्त्री-पुरुष सुख से उन फलों को प्राप्त करते थे।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2367.english_translation: All stood stunned in Rama's separation, as if painted and fixed in place. The city was like a great, fruitful forest, full of birds, beasts, men, and women.
ramacharitamanas::2367.translation_literal: राम (Rama) / बियोग (separation) / बिकल (distressed) / सब (all) / ठाढ़े (standing still) / जहाँ तहँ (here and there) / मनहुँ (as if) / चित्र (picture) / लिखि (having written) / काढ़े (drawn out) / नगरु (city) / सफल (fruitful) / बनु (forest) / गहबर (dense) / भारी (great) / खग (birds) / मृग (beasts) / बिपुल (many) / सकल (all) / नर (men) / नारी (women)
ramacharitamanas::2367.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2367.essence: Rama's absence turns a living city into stillness.
ramacharitamanas::2367.simple_meaning: Rama's absence left everyone stunned and motionless. Ayodhya felt like a dense, fruitful forest full of life, yet emptied by grief.
ramacharitamanas::2367.simple_insight: Loss can freeze an entire world, even when everything around it still looks full.
ramacharitamanas::2367.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya has just lost Rama to exile. The people stand frozen in shock, as if someone has painted them into a scene. Tulsidas shows a city that once overflowed with life now feeling like a forest emptied by grief.
ramacharitamanas::2367.modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after the bad news lands. Everyone is still online, still awake, but no one knows what to say. Grief can make a living home feel unmoving.
ramacharitamanas::2367.insight: It shifts attention from outward activity to the paralysis grief creates in an entire community.

ramacharitamanas::2368.verse_sanskrit: बिधि कैकई किरातिनि कीन्ही। जेहिं दव दुसह दसहुँ दिसि दीन्ही॥ सहि न सके रघुबर बिरहागी। चले लोग सब ब्याकुल भागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2368.verse_hindi: विधाता ने कैकेयी को भीलनी बनाया, जिसने दसों दिशाओं में दुःसह दावाग्नि (भयानक आग) लगा दी। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विरह की इस अग्नि को लोग सह न सके। सब लोग व्याकुल होकर भाग चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2368.english_translation: Providence made Kaikeyi a huntress, and she set a terrible fire in all ten directions. People could not bear the burning grief of separation from Raghubar. Everyone, overwhelmed, ran away in distress.
ramacharitamanas::2368.translation_literal: बिधि (fate / providence) / कैकई (Kaikeyi) / किरातिनि (huntress) / कीन्ही (made) / जेहिं (who) / दव (fire) / दुसह (unbearable) / दसहुँ (ten) / दिसि (directions) / दीन्ही (gave) ॥ / सहि (bearing) / न (not) / सके (could) / रघुबर (Raghubar / Ram) / बिरहागी (the fire of separation) / चले (went) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / भागी (running away) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2368.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2368.essence: One cruel turn can set the whole world burning.
ramacharitamanas::2368.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi's action is compared to a fire spreading everywhere, and Ram's separation hurts so deeply that no one can bear it.
ramacharitamanas::2368.simple_insight: Some wounds spread through an entire family or community, and grief makes even strong people flee.
ramacharitamanas::2368.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi's demand has turned the royal city upside down. Tulsidas compares her to a huntress whose act sets the whole world ablaze. The people of Ayodhya cannot endure the grief of Ram's exile, so they scatter in anguish.
ramacharitamanas::2368.modern_relevance: A single decision in a family group chat can scorch every relationship in the room. What starts as one person's demand can leave everyone else stunned, silent, and emotionally burned.
ramacharitamanas::2368.insight: It frames harmful action as a spreading fire and shows how grief can overwhelm an entire community.

ramacharitamanas::2369.verse_sanskrit: सबहिं बिचारु कीन्ह मन माहीं। राम लखन सिय बिनु सुखु नाहीं॥ जहाँ रामु तहँ सबुइ समाजू। बिनु रघुबीर अवध नहिं काजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2369.verse_hindi: सबने मन में विचार कर लिया कि श्री रामजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी के बिना सुख नहीं है। जहाँ श्री रामजी रहेंगे, वहीं सारा समाज रहेगा। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के बिना अयोध्या में हम लोगों का कुछ काम नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2369.english_translation: Everyone thought in their hearts: there is no happiness without Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Wherever Ram stays, that alone is the true assembly. Without Raghubir, Ayodhya has no purpose.
ramacharitamanas::2369.translation_literal: सबहिं (everyone) / बिचारु (thought) / कीन्ह (made) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / बिनु (without) / सुखु (happiness) / नाहीं (not) / जहाँ (where) / रामु (Ram) / तहँ (there) / सबुइ (all) / समाजू (assembly) / बिनु (without) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / अवध (Ayodhya) / नहिं (not) / काजू (purpose/work)
ramacharitamanas::2369.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2369.essence: Without Ram, even Ayodhya has no real purpose.
ramacharitamanas::2369.simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya realize that life without Ram, Lakshman, and Sita feels empty. Their city only feels complete when Ram is present.
ramacharitamanas::2369.simple_insight: Real belonging comes from presence, not from buildings, power, or routine.
ramacharitamanas::2369.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is reeling after Ram’s exile. The people quietly accept a painful truth: without Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, the city has lost its heart. The next verse shows them choosing to go with Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2369.modern_relevance: You enter a house after someone essential has left, and the rooms still look the same. Nothing feels alive until the person who makes the place feel like home returns.
ramacharitamanas::2369.insight: It shifts attention from outer order to the presence that gives a place meaning.

ramacharitamanas::2370.verse_sanskrit: चले साथ अस मंत्रु दृढ़ाई। सुर दुर्लभ सुख सदन बिहाई॥ राम चरन पंकज प्रिय जिन्हही। बिषय भोग बस करहिं कि तिन्हही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2370.verse_hindi: ऐसा विचार दृढ़ करके देवताओं को भी दुर्लभ सुखों से पूर्ण घरों को छोड़कर सब श्री रामचन्द्रजी के साथ चले पड़े। जिनको श्री रामजी के चरणकमल प्यारे हैं, उन्हें क्या कभी विषय भोग वश में कर सकते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2370.english_translation: Having firmly resolved, they left homes filled with pleasures hard even for the gods to obtain, and went with Ram. Those who love Ram's lotus feet can never be ruled by worldly pleasures.
ramacharitamanas::2370.translation_literal: चले (went) / साथ (with) / अस (thus) / मंत्रु (resolve) / दृढ़ाई (made firm) / सुर (gods) / दुर्लभ (hard to obtain) / सुख (pleasures) / सदन (homes) / बिहाई (leaving behind) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / पंकज (lotus) / प्रिय (dear) / जिन्हही (for those who) / बिषय (worldly objects) / भोग (enjoyments) / बस (under control) / करहिं (do) / कि (can?) / तिन्हही (them)
ramacharitamanas::2370.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2370.essence: Love for Ram breaks the spell of comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2370.simple_meaning: The people made a firm decision, left comfortable homes behind, and followed Ram. Anyone who truly loves Ram's feet cannot be ruled by worldly pleasures.
ramacharitamanas::2370.simple_insight: Real love makes comfort lose its grip on you.
ramacharitamanas::2370.detailed_meaning: The people of Ayodhya have already decided that life without Ram, Lakshman, and Sita has no joy. Now they act on that resolve: they leave homes of great comfort and follow Ram into exile, proving that devotion is stronger than pleasure.
ramacharitamanas::2370.modern_relevance: You have a stable life, good food, and a safe home, but your heart says something deeper matters. When that call becomes clear, comfort stops being the master.
ramacharitamanas::2370.insight: It shifts loyalty from comfort to devotion, showing that attachment weakens when love becomes firm.

ramacharitamanas::2371.verse_sanskrit: बालक बृद्ध बिहाइ गृहँ लगे लोग सब साथ। तमसा तीर निवासु किय प्रथम दिवस रघुनाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2371.verse_hindi: बच्चों और बूढ़ों को घरों में छोड़कर सब लोग साथ हो लिए। पहले दिन श्री रघुनाथजी ने तमसा नदी के तीर पर निवास किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2371.english_translation: Leaving children and elders at home, everyone went along together. On the first day, Raghunath stayed on the bank of the Tamasa River.
ramacharitamanas::2371.translation_literal: बालक (children) / बृद्ध (elders) / बिहाइ (leaving behind) / गृहँ (at home) / लगे (went) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / साथ (together) / तमसा (Tamasa) / तीर (bank) / निवासु (dwelling) / किय (made) / प्रथम (first) / दिवस (day) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::2371.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2371.essence: Even exile begins as a collective act of love.
ramacharitamanas::2371.simple_meaning: Everyone left home and followed Ram. On the first day, Ram camped by the Tamasa River.
ramacharitamanas::2371.simple_insight: Big departures begin with one quiet night away from home.
ramacharitamanas::2371.detailed_meaning: The people of Ayodhya have decided to follow Ram into exile. They leave behind children and elders and begin the journey together. On the first day, Ram stays on the bank of the Tamasa River, marking the start of a sorrowful but devoted procession.
ramacharitamanas::2371.modern_relevance: A family leaves the house before dawn for a move nobody wanted, carrying boxes in silence. The first stop feels small, but it marks the moment life has already changed.
ramacharitamanas::2371.insight: It turns a departure into a shared act of loyalty, not just a journey.

ramacharitamanas::2372.verse_sanskrit: रघुपति प्रजा प्रेमबस देखी। सदय हृदयँ दुखु भयउ बिसेषी॥ करुनामय रघुनाथ गोसाँई। बेगि पाइअहिं पीर पराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2372.verse_hindi: प्रजा को प्रेमवश देखकर श्री रघुनाथजी के दयालु हृदय में बड़ा दुःख हुआ। प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी करुणामय हैं। पराई पीड़ा को वे तुरंत पा जाते हैं (अर्थात दूसरे का दुःख देखकर वे तुरंत स्वयं दुःखित हो जाते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2372.english_translation: Seeing the people moved by love, Raghupati's compassionate heart felt deep sorrow. The merciful Lord quickly feels another's pain as his own.
ramacharitamanas::2372.translation_literal: रघुपति (Lord of Raghu; Ram) / प्रजा (the people) / प्रेमबस (moved by love) / देखी (seeing) / सदय (compassionate) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / दुखु (sorrow) / भयउ (became) / बिसेषी (great)॥ / करुनामय (full of compassion) / रघुनाथ (Lord of Raghu; Ram) / गोसाँई (lord) / बेगि (quickly) / पाइअहिं (is found / is felt) / पीर (pain) / पराई (of another)॥
ramacharitamanas::2372.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2372.essence: Compassion means another person's pain lands in you at once.
ramacharitamanas::2372.simple_meaning: Ram sees the people acting from love, and his compassionate heart aches for their suffering. He feels other people's pain immediately as his own.
ramacharitamanas::2372.simple_insight: You are seen in your suffering; compassion is not distant but immediate.
ramacharitamanas::2372.detailed_meaning: As the people follow Ram with love during the exile journey, he looks at them and feels sorrow for their hardship. The verse shows his heart as tender and responsive, unable to ignore anyone else's pain.
ramacharitamanas::2372.modern_relevance: You watch a friend smile through exhaustion after helping everyone else at the wedding. The room is loud, but you notice the strain behind their face. Real compassion catches that hidden hurt immediately.
ramacharitamanas::2372.insight: It trains attention toward another person's suffering, not just their behavior, and turns sympathy into quick, caring response.

ramacharitamanas::2373.verse_sanskrit: कहि सप्रेम मृदु बचन सुहाए। बहुबिधि राम लोग समुझाए॥ किए धरम उपदेस घनेरे। लोग प्रेम बस फिरहिं न फेरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2373.verse_hindi: प्रेमयुक्त कोमल और सुंदर वचन कहकर श्री रामजी ने बहुत प्रकार से लोगों को समझाया और बहुतेरे धर्म संबंधी उपदेश दिए, परन्तु प्रेमवश लोग लौटाए लौटते नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2373.english_translation: Speaking sweet, gentle, loving words, Ram explained many things to the people in many ways and gave them many teachings about dharma, but out of love the people would not turn back.
ramacharitamanas::2373.translation_literal: कहि (speaking) / सप्रेम (with love) / मृदु (gentle) / बचन (words) / सुहाए (pleasant) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / राम (Ram) / लोग (the people) / समुझाए (explained) / किए (gave) / धरम (dharma) / उपदेस (teachings) / घनेरे (many) / लोग (the people) / प्रेम बस (under the control of love) / फिरहिं न फेरे (do not turn back)
ramacharitamanas::2373.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2373.essence: Love can hold people so tightly that even dharma cannot send them back.
ramacharitamanas::2373.simple_meaning: Ram gently and lovingly tried to explain dharma to the people, but their love for him kept them from turning back.
ramacharitamanas::2373.simple_insight: Love can make even a clear instruction hard to follow.
ramacharitamanas::2373.detailed_meaning: As Ram leaves Ayodhya, the townspeople follow him in grief and devotion. He speaks kindly, teaching them to return home and hold to dharma, but their love is so strong that they cannot bring themselves to leave him.
ramacharitamanas::2373.modern_relevance: You tell a friend to go home, rest, and stop worrying about you. They keep standing there, unable to walk away because caring has become stronger than instruction.
ramacharitamanas::2373.insight: It shows that affection can override even the clearest practical advice.

ramacharitamanas::2374.verse_sanskrit: सीलु सनेहु छाड़ि नहिं जाई। असमंजस बस भे रघुराई॥ लोग सोग श्रम बस गए सोई। कछुक देवमायाँ मति मोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2374.verse_hindi: शील और स्नेह छोड़ा नहीं जाता। श्री रघुनाथजी असमंजस के अधीन हो गए (दुविधा में पड़ गए)। शोक और परिश्रम (थकावट) के मारे लोग सो गए और कुछ देवताओं की माया से भी उनकी बुद्धि मोहित हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2374.english_translation: Character and affection cannot be abandoned. Raghunath was overcome by bewilderment. People fell asleep from grief and exhaustion, and some were deluded by the divine illusion.
ramacharitamanas::2374.translation_literal: सीलु (character / virtue) / सनेहु (affection / love) / छाड़ि (leaving) / नहिं (not) / जाई (can be done) / असमंजस (confusion / dilemma) / बस (under the power of) / भे (became) / रघुराई (Raghunath) / लोग (people) / सोग (grief) / श्रम (fatigue) / बस (under the power of) / गए (went) / सोई (to sleep) / कछुक (some) / देवमायाँ (by divine illusion) / मति (mind / understanding) / मोई (became deluded)
ramacharitamanas::2374.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2374.essence: Love and virtue do not vanish, even when confusion clouds action.
ramacharitamanas::2374.simple_meaning: Ram cannot simply cast off his gentleness and love, even when the situation has become confusing. Meanwhile, the people are overwhelmed by grief and exhaustion, and some lose their clarity.
ramacharitamanas::2374.simple_insight: Even a divine heart can feel torn when love and duty collide.
ramacharitamanas::2374.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is trying to hold together a kingdom that is breaking under grief and exile. He remains gentle and loving, yet the situation leaves him momentarily caught in confusion. Around him, the people collapse into sorrow and fatigue.
ramacharitamanas::2374.modern_relevance: You are trying to stay kind in a family crisis, but every conversation seems to pull you in two directions. Even steadiness can wobble when love, duty, and exhaustion collide.
ramacharitamanas::2374.insight: It shows that compassion does not erase human strain; it reveals how hard righteous action can be under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::2375.verse_sanskrit: जबहिं जाम जुग जामिनि बीती। राम सचिव सन कहेउ सप्रीती॥ खोज मारि रथु हाँकहु ताता। आन उपायँ बनिहि नहिं बाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2375.verse_hindi: जब दो पहर बीत गई, तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने प्रेमपूर्वक मंत्री सुमंत्र से कहा- हे तात! रथ के खोज मारकर (अर्थात पहियों के चिह्नों से दिशा का पता न चले इस प्रकार) रथ को हाँकिए। और किसी उपाय से बात नहीं बनेगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2375.english_translation: When two watches of the night had passed, Ram said lovingly to Sumantra, "Drive the chariot so its tracks cannot be traced, father. No other way will work."
ramacharitamanas::2375.translation_literal: जबहिं (when) / जाम जुग (two watches) / जामिनि (night) / बीती (had passed) / राम (Ram) / सचिव सन (to the minister) / कहेउ (said) / सप्रीती (with affection) / खोज मारि (erasing tracks) / रथु (chariot) / हाँकहु (drive) / ताता (father) / आन उपायँ (by any other means) / बनिहि (will work) / नहिं (not) / बाता (matter)
ramacharitamanas::2375.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2375.essence: The right move can be tender and tactical at once.
ramacharitamanas::2375.simple_meaning: Ram gently asks Sumantra to drive the chariot in a way that leaves no tracks, because no other method will do.
ramacharitamanas::2375.simple_insight: Sometimes the next right step is quiet, careful, and irreversible.
ramacharitamanas::2375.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is leaving Ayodhya for exile. The chariot must be hidden from pursuit, and Ram speaks tenderly to Sumantra even in this painful departure. The moment is practical, urgent, and full of restraint.
ramacharitamanas::2375.modern_relevance: You slip out before dawn after a hard goodbye, trying not to wake the whole house. Some exits need care, not drama.
ramacharitamanas::2375.insight: It shifts attention from emotion to precise action: do what the moment requires, cleanly and without delay.

ramacharitamanas::2376.verse_sanskrit: राम लखन सिय जान चढ़ि संभु चरन सिरु नाइ। सचिवँ चलायउ तुरत रथु इत उत खोज दुराइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2376.verse_hindi: शंकरजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर श्री रामजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी रथ पर सवार हुए। मंत्री ने तुरंत ही रथ को इधर-उधर खोज छिपाकर चला दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2376.english_translation: After bowing their heads at Shiva's feet, Ram, Lakshman, and Sita mounted the chariot. The minister quickly drove it away, hiding the tracks in every direction.
ramacharitamanas::2376.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / जान (having mounted) / चढ़ि (climbing) / संभु (Shiva) / चरन (feet) / सिरु (head) / नाइ (bowing) / सचिवँ (by the minister) / चलायउ (was driven) / तुरत (immediately) / रथु (chariot) / इत उत (here and there) / खोज (tracks) / दुराइ (hiding)
ramacharitamanas::2376.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2376.essence: Leave with reverence, then go without looking back.
ramacharitamanas::2376.simple_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita bow to Shiva before leaving in the chariot. Sumantra quickly drives them away and hides the tracks.
ramacharitamanas::2376.simple_insight: Even departure can be done with reverence and care.
ramacharitamanas::2376.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are finally leaving Ayodhya in exile. Before the chariot moves, they bow to Shiva. Sumantra then drives quickly and covers the tracks, helping them leave before the city fully wakes.
ramacharitamanas::2376.modern_relevance: You leave before dawn with one bag, hoping no one sees the exit. A quiet goodbye, a final bow, and then the road takes over.
ramacharitamanas::2376.insight: It shifts attention from drama to disciplined departure: honor what matters, then move without delay.

ramacharitamanas::2377.verse_sanskrit: जागे सकल लोग भएँ भोरू। गे रघुनाथ भयउ अति सोरू॥ रथ कर खोज कतहुँ नहिं पावहिं। राम राम कहि चहुँ दिसि धावहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2377.verse_hindi: सबेरा होते ही सब लोग जागे, तो बड़ा शोर मचा कि रघुनाथजी चले गए। कहीं रथ का खोज नहीं पाते, सब 'हा राम! हा राम!' पुकारते हुए चारों ओर दौड़ रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2377.english_translation: At dawn, everyone woke up and there was a great uproar: Raghunath had gone. They could not find the chariot anywhere, and all ran in every direction crying, “Ram, Ram!”
ramacharitamanas::2377.translation_literal: जागे (woke up) / सकल लोग (all people) / भएँ भोरू (at dawn) / गे (gone) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / भयउ (became) / अति (great) / सोरू (uproar) ॥ / रथ (chariot) / कर (of) / खोज (search) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / नहिं (not) / पावहिं (find) / राम राम (Ram, Ram) / कहि (saying) / चहुँ दिसि (in all four directions) / धावहिं (they ran) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2377.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2377.essence: Absence turns a quiet morning into collective panic.
ramacharitamanas::2377.simple_meaning: At dawn, the whole camp wakes to panic. Ram is gone, the chariot cannot be found, and everyone runs around crying out his name.
ramacharitamanas::2377.simple_insight: Panic spreads fast when the one you depend on is suddenly absent.
ramacharitamanas::2377.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, dawn breaks after Ram, Sita, and Lakshman have left in secret. The camp wakes to confusion and grief. Sumantra and the others search for the chariot, then scatter in distress, crying out Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::2377.modern_relevance: You wake up and the person who was supposed to lead the meeting has vanished, leaving only unanswered messages. The room turns restless in seconds.
ramacharitamanas::2377.insight: It shows how quickly uncertainty spreads when support disappears and no one knows what happened.

ramacharitamanas::2378.verse_sanskrit: मनहुँ बारिनिधि बूड़ जहाजू। भयउ बिकल बड़ बनिक समाजू॥ एकहि एक देहिं उपदेसू। तजे राम हम जानि कलेसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2378.verse_hindi: मानो समुद्र में जहाज डूब गया हो, जिससे व्यापारियों का समुदाय बहुत ही व्याकुल हो उठा हो। वे एक-दूसरे को उपदेश देते हैं कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने, हम लोगों को क्लेश होगा, यह जानकर छोड़ दिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2378.english_translation: It was as if a ship had sunk in the ocean, and the whole merchant crowd was thrown into deep distress. They kept advising one another, saying, "Ram has left us, knowing that we will suffer."
ramacharitamanas::2378.translation_literal: मनहुँ (as if) / बारिनिधि (in the ocean) / बूड़ (sank) / जहाजू (a ship) / भयउ (became) / बिकल (distressed) / बड़ (great) / बनिक (merchant) / समाजू (assembly) / एकहि एक (one another) / देहिं (give) / उपदेसू (advice) / तजे (left) / राम (Ram) / हम (us) / जानि (knowing) / कलेसू (suffering)
ramacharitamanas::2378.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2378.essence: Ram's absence hits like a shipwreck.
ramacharitamanas::2378.simple_meaning: Ram's departure shocks everyone so deeply that they feel like a ship has sunk in the sea. The whole crowd is stunned and keeps telling itself that Ram left to spare them pain.
ramacharitamanas::2378.simple_insight: When someone truly anchors your life, their absence can feel like the ground itself has vanished.
ramacharitamanas::2378.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya has just woken to find Ram gone. The city is in panic, and the people are searching for meaning in the shock. Tulsidas compares their grief to merchants losing a ship at sea, because Ram's departure feels like the loss of everything that held them together.
ramacharitamanas::2378.modern_relevance: You wake up to a message that changes everything, and suddenly the day feels unmoored. The mind keeps circling the same sentence, trying to make sense of the loss.
ramacharitamanas::2378.insight: It turns grief into a shared shock, showing how deeply one beloved presence can hold a whole community together.

ramacharitamanas::2379.verse_sanskrit: निंदहिं आपु सराहहिं मीना। धिग जीवनु रघुबीर बिहीना॥ जौं पै प्रिय बियोगु बिधि कीन्हा। तौ कस मरनु न मागें दीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2379.verse_hindi: वे लोग अपनी निंदा करते हैं और मछलियों की सराहना करते हैं। (कहते हैं-) श्री रामचन्द्रजी के बिना हमारे जीने को धिक्कार है। विधाता ने यदि प्यारे का वियोग ही रचा, तो फिर उसने माँगने पर मृत्यु क्यों नहीं दी! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2379.english_translation: They blame themselves and praise the fish: 'Life without Raghubir is cursed. If fate has already made us lose the beloved, why was death not given when we asked for it?'
ramacharitamanas::2379.translation_literal: निंदहिं (they blame) / आपु (themselves) / सराहहिं (praise) / मीना (fish) / धिग (cursed be) / जीवनु (life) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / बिहीना (without) / जौं (if) / पै (indeed) / प्रिय (beloved) / बियोगु (separation) / बिधि (fate) / कीन्हा (has made) / तौ (then) / कस (why) / मरनु (death) / न (not) / मागें (on asking) / दीन्हा (given)
ramacharitamanas::2379.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2379.essence: Love can make life feel cursed when the beloved is gone.
ramacharitamanas::2379.simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya feel life has no value without Ram. They are so overwhelmed by separation that they even wish death had come instead.
ramacharitamanas::2379.simple_insight: Love can make absence feel heavier than life itself.
ramacharitamanas::2379.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya has awakened to Ram's exile, and the city is in raw grief. People wander in shock, speaking against themselves and longing for death, because Ram's absence has made ordinary life feel unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2379.modern_relevance: You open your phone and see the message that changes everything: they are gone, and the day still expects you to continue. This verse knows that unbearable gap.
ramacharitamanas::2379.insight: It names grief honestly: when someone central is missing, even survival can feel like a burden.

ramacharitamanas::2380.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि करत प्रलाप कलापा। आए अवध भरे परितापा॥ बिषम बियोगु न जाइ बखाना। अवधि आस सब राखहिं प्राना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2380.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार बहुत से प्रलाप करते हुए वे संताप से भरे हुए अयोध्याजी में आए। उन लोगों के विषम वियोग की दशा का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। (चौदह साल की) अवधि की आशा से ही वे प्राणों को रख रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2380.english_translation: In this way, grieving and lamenting, they came to Ayodhya filled with sorrow. Their unbearable separation cannot be described. They kept their lives only by holding on to the hope that fourteen years would pass.
ramacharitamanas::2380.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / करत (doing) / प्रलाप कलापा (lamenting and grieving) / आए (came) / अवध (Ayodhya) / भरे (filled) / परितापा (with sorrow)॥ / बिषम (severe) / बियोगु (separation) / न जाइ (cannot be) / बखाना (described) / अवधि (the term/period) / आस (hope) / सब (all) / राखहिं (are keeping) / प्राना (their lives)
ramacharitamanas::2380.speaker: Narrator
