ramacharitamanas::2380.essence: A fixed hope can keep you alive inside deep separation.
ramacharitamanas::2380.simple_meaning: The people return to Ayodhya in deep sorrow, unable to bear the separation from Ram. They stay alive by clinging to the hope that the exile will end.
ramacharitamanas::2380.simple_insight: Even unbearable grief can be endured when the mind has something to wait for.
ramacharitamanas::2380.detailed_meaning: After Ram leaves, Ayodhya becomes a city of mourning. The people return home crying, unable to describe their pain. What keeps them alive is not comfort, but the thin hope that fourteen years will eventually end.
ramacharitamanas::2380.modern_relevance: You came home after the hospital visit and sat in the car for ten minutes, unable to speak. What kept you from falling apart was the date circled on the calendar.
ramacharitamanas::2380.insight: It shifts attention from total despair to the one time-bound hope that makes endurance possible.

ramacharitamanas::2381.verse_sanskrit: राम दरस हित नेम ब्रत लगे करन नर नारि। मनहुँ कोक कोकी कमल दीन बिहीन तमारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2381.verse_hindi: (सब) स्त्री-पुरुष श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन के लिए नियम और व्रत करने लगे और ऐसे दुःखी हो गए जैसे चकवा, चकवी और कमल सूर्य के बिना दीन हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2381.english_translation: For the sight of Ram, men and women began to observe vows and fasts. They became miserable like a chakwa, chakwi, and lotus without the sun.
ramacharitamanas::2381.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / दरस (darshan, sight) / हित (for the sake of) / नेम (vows) / ब्रत (fasts) / लगे (began) / करन (to do) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / मनहुँ (as if) / कोक (chakwa bird) / कोकी (chakwi bird) / कमल (lotus) / दीन (dejected) / बिहीन (without) / तमारि (sun)
ramacharitamanas::2381.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2381.essence: Separation makes people turn their whole lives toward one glimpse.
ramacharitamanas::2381.simple_meaning: People in Ayodhya began fasting and taking vows just to see Ram. Without him, they felt as helpless as birds and flowers without the sun.
ramacharitamanas::2381.simple_insight: Longing can turn ordinary people into people who wait, pray, and change their habits.
ramacharitamanas::2381.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is already drowning in separation from Ram. Men and women try to endure the pain by taking vows and fasting for his sight, but the verse shows that waiting itself has become their condition.
ramacharitamanas::2381.modern_relevance: You keep checking the train platform, hoping one more delay will still end in the face you miss. The waiting changes your habits, your appetite, even your days.
ramacharitamanas::2381.insight: It shifts longing from private feeling into disciplined waiting and devotion.

ramacharitamanas::2382.verse_sanskrit: सीता सचिव सहित दोउ भाई। सृंगबेरपुर पहुँचे जाई॥ उतरे राम देवसरि देखी। कीन्ह दंडवत हरषु बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2382.verse_hindi: सीताजी और मंत्री सहित दोनों भाई श्रृंगवेरपुर जा पहुँचे। वहाँ गंगाजी को देखकर श्री रामजी रथ से उतर पड़े और बड़े हर्ष के साथ उन्होंने दण्डवत की ॥
ramacharitamanas::2382.english_translation: Sita and the two brothers, along with the minister, reached Sringaverpur. Seeing the Ganga there, Ram got down and bowed with great joy.
ramacharitamanas::2382.translation_literal: सीता (Sita) / सचिव सहित (along with the minister) / दोउ भाई (both brothers) / सृंगबेरपुर (Sringaverpur) / पहुँचे (reached) / जाई (having gone) ॥ / उतरे (got down) / राम (Ram) / देवसरि (the Ganga) / देखी (seeing) / कीन्ह (did) / दंडवत (prostration) / हरषु (joy) / बिसेषी (great) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2382.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2382.essence: Respect can arrive before words do.
ramacharitamanas::2382.simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, Lakshman, and the minister reached Sringaverpur. Seeing the Ganga, Ram got down and bowed with great joy.
ramacharitamanas::2382.simple_insight: Even a king can pause before what is sacred and respond with humility.
ramacharitamanas::2382.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, Lakshman, and Sumantra arrive at Sringaverpur during exile. Spotting the Ganga, Ram dismounts at once and bows with delight. The verse is a scene of reverence, not a teaching statement.
ramacharitamanas::2382.modern_relevance: You step out of the car before entering a temple, a riverbank, or your grandmother’s home, and your body softens before your mind does.
ramacharitamanas::2382.insight: It models instant humility before what deserves reverence, even in motion.

ramacharitamanas::2383.verse_sanskrit: लखन सचिवँ सियँ किए प्रनामा। सबहि सहित सुखु पायउ रामा॥ गंग सकल मुद मंगल मूला। सब सुख करनि हरनि सब सूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::2383.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी, सुमंत्र और सीताजी ने भी प्रणाम किया। सबके साथ श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सुख पाया। गंगाजी समस्त आनंद-मंगलों की मूल हैं। वे सब सुखों को करने वाली और सब पीड़ाओं को हरने वाली हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2383.english_translation: Lakshmana, the minister, and Sita also bowed. Ram found joy together with everyone. The Ganga is the root of all delight and auspiciousness. She gives every happiness and removes every pain.
ramacharitamanas::2383.translation_literal: लखन (Lakshmana) / सचिवँ (with the minister) / सियँ (with Sita) / किए (made) / प्रनामा (bows) / सबहि सहित (with everyone) / सुखु (joy) / पायउ (found) / रामा (Ram) / गंग (Ganga) / सकल (all) / मुद (joy) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मूला (root) / सब (all) / सुख (happiness) / करनि (the doer) / हरनि (remover) / सब (all) / सूला (pains)
ramacharitamanas::2383.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2383.essence: Even a river crossing becomes blessed when you meet it with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2383.simple_meaning: Lakshmana, Sumantra, and Sita bow to the Ganga, and Ram feels joy with them. The river is praised as the source of joy, blessing, happiness, and relief from pain.
ramacharitamanas::2383.simple_insight: Reverence can turn a crossing into a moment of relief and shared joy.
ramacharitamanas::2383.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, Lakshmana, and Sumantra have reached the Ganga at Shringaverpur. After the bows, the scene pauses to honor the river itself as a giver of joy and the remover of suffering, deepening the sacred mood before the journey continues.
ramacharitamanas::2383.modern_relevance: You finally arrive somewhere after a hard drive, and the first thing you do is pause, breathe, and feel grateful. Even the crossing matters when your heart is open.
ramacharitamanas::2383.insight: It shifts attention from mere travel to the sacredness of what carries and comforts you.

ramacharitamanas::2384.verse_sanskrit: कहि कहि कोटिक कथा प्रसंगा। रामु बिलोकहिं गंग तरंगा॥ सचिवहि अनुजहि प्रियहि सुनाई। बिबुध नदी महिमा अधिकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2384.verse_hindi: अनेक कथा प्रसंग कहते हुए श्री रामजी गंगाजी की तरंगों को देख रहे हैं। उन्होंने मंत्री को, छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी को और प्रिया सीताजी को देवनदी गंगाजी की बड़ी महिमा सुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2384.english_translation: While recounting countless stories, Ram kept watching the waves of the Ganga. He then told his minister, his younger brother Lakshman, and Sita about the great glory of the divine river.
ramacharitamanas::2384.translation_literal: कहि कहि (speaking and speaking) / कोटिक (countless) / कथा (stories) / प्रसंगा (occasions, episodes) / रामु (Ram) / बिलोकहिं (was watching) / गंग तरंगा (the Ganga's waves) / सचिवहि (to the minister) / अनुजहि (to the younger brother) / प्रियहि (to the beloved) / सुनाई (told) / बिबुध नदी (the river of the radiant beings, the divine river) / महिमा (glory) / अधिकाई (greatness)
ramacharitamanas::2384.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2384.essence: Sacred attention turns an ordinary stop into a living blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2384.simple_meaning: Ram watches the Ganga while sharing stories with those close to him. He speaks of the river's greatness with affection and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2384.simple_insight: Even a sacred journey becomes richer when you notice, share, and honor what is before you.
ramacharitamanas::2384.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, Sita, and Sumantra are travelling through Shrngverpur. As they pause by the Ganga, Ram keeps speaking of many things while gazing at the river, then lovingly explains its greatness to those with him. The verse deepens the sacred mood before the bath.
ramacharitamanas::2384.modern_relevance: You stop beside a river on a long drive, and the whole group falls quiet for a moment. Someone begins naming what the place means, and the journey feels blessed instead of rushed.
ramacharitamanas::2384.insight: It turns travel into reverence by teaching you to pause, notice, and speak with gratitude.

ramacharitamanas::2385.verse_sanskrit: मज्जनु कीन्ह पंथ श्रम गयऊ। सुचि जलु पिअत मुदित मन भयऊ॥ सुमिरत जाहि मिटइ श्रम भारू। तेहि श्रम यह लौकिक ब्यवहारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2385.verse_hindi: इसके बाद सबने स्नान किया, जिससे मार्ग का सारा श्रम (थकावट) दूर हो गया और पवित्र जल पीते ही मन प्रसन्न हो गया। जिनके स्मरण मात्र से (बार-बार जन्म ने और मरने का) महान श्रम मिट जाता है, उनको 'श्रम' होना- यह केवल लौकिक व्यवहार (नरलीला) है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2385.english_translation: After bathing, the fatigue of the road was gone, and drinking the pure water made the mind joyful. For the one whose remembrance removes the great burden of wandering through birth and death, ordinary fatigue is only a human appearance.
ramacharitamanas::2385.translation_literal: मज्जनु (bathing) / कीन्ह (did) / पंथ (road) / श्रम (fatigue) / गयऊ (went away) / सुचि (pure) / जलु (water) / पिअत (drinking) / मुदित (joyful) / मन (mind) / भयऊ (became) / सुमिरत (remembering) / जाहि (whom) / मिटइ (is removed) / श्रम (fatigue) / भारू (burden) / तेहि (for that one) / श्रम (fatigue) / यह (this) / लौकिक (worldly) / ब्यवहारू (ordinary conduct)
ramacharitamanas::2385.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2385.essence: Remembrance of Ram makes even suffering feel small.
ramacharitamanas::2385.simple_meaning: A simple bath and drink remove travel fatigue, but remembering Ram removes the deeper fatigue of repeated wandering through life. Compared to that, ordinary tiredness is small.
ramacharitamanas::2385.simple_insight: You can rest more deeply than sleep allows when your mind turns toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2385.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, Lakshman, and the others pause on the journey and bathe. The immediate fatigue of the road disappears. Tulsidas then lifts the scene higher: the one remembered here is the one whose name can end the far greater fatigue of worldly wandering.
ramacharitamanas::2385.modern_relevance: You get home after a long train ride, drop your bag, wash your face, and feel human again. But some exhaustion is deeper than the body — and this verse points to a rest that reaches that layer too.
ramacharitamanas::2385.insight: It shifts the mind from treating exhaustion as only physical to seeing remembrance as a deeper form of release.

ramacharitamanas::2386.verse_sanskrit: सुद्ध सच्चिदानंदमय कंद भानुकुल केतु। चरितकरत नर अनुहरत संसृति सागर सेतु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2386.verse_hindi: शुद्ध (प्रकृतिजन्य त्रिगुणों से रहित, मायातीत दिव्य मंगलविग्रह) सच्चिदानंद-कन्द स्वरूप सूर्य कुल के ध्वजा रूप भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी मनुष्यों के सदृश ऐसे चरित्र करते हैं, जो संसार रूपी समुद्र के पार उतरने के लिए पुल के समान हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2386.english_translation: The pure, blissful, consciousness-filled Lord of the Sun dynasty acts like a human, and his deeds become a bridge across the ocean of worldly existence.
ramacharitamanas::2386.translation_literal: सुद्ध (pure) / सच्चिदानंदमय (made of being-consciousness-bliss) / कंद (source) / भानुकुल (Sun dynasty) / केतु (banner) / चरितकरत (doing deeds) / नर (human) / अनुहरत (imitating) / संसृति (worldly cycle) / सागर (ocean) / सेतु (bridge)
ramacharitamanas::2386.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2386.essence: His human life becomes the bridge that carries you beyond the world.
ramacharitamanas::2386.simple_meaning: Ram is pure and beyond change, yet he acts like a human so his life can carry people across suffering and confusion.
ramacharitamanas::2386.simple_insight: You are not asked to admire him from a distance; you are invited to cross over through his example.
ramacharitamanas::2386.detailed_meaning: On the banks of the Ganga, Ram travels in exile with Lakshman, Sita, and companions. Amid the journey, Tulsidas pauses to reveal Ram's true nature: the supreme, blissful source of the Sun dynasty who still chooses human conduct so his life can become a crossing place for others.
ramacharitamanas::2386.modern_relevance: You watch someone stay gentle under pressure, keep their word, and carry others without needing credit. Their steadiness does more than inspire you — it shows you how to get across your own turbulent stretch.
ramacharitamanas::2386.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as distant majesty to seeing his life as a usable path.

ramacharitamanas::2387.verse_sanskrit: यह सुधि गुहँ निषाद जब पाई। मुदित लिए प्रिय बंधु बोलाई॥ लिए फल मूल भेंट भरि भारा। मिलन चलेउ हियँ हरषु अपारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2387.verse_hindi: जब निषादराज गुह ने यह खबर पाई, तब आनंदित होकर उसने अपने प्रियजनों और भाई-बंधुओं को बुला लिया और भेंट देने के लिए फल, मूल (कन्द) लेकर और उन्हें भारों (बहँगियों) में भरकर मिलने के लिए चला। उसके हृदय में हर्ष का पार नहीं था ॥
ramacharitamanas::2387.english_translation: When Guha the Nishada heard this news, he became delighted, called his dear companions and brothers, took fruits and roots as gifts, filled loads with them, and went to meet them with immense joy in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::2387.translation_literal: यह (this) / सुधि (news) / गुहँ (Guha) / निषाद (Nishada chief) / जब (when) / पाई (received) / मुदित (joyful) / लिए (took) / प्रिय (dear) / बंधु (companions, brothers) / बोलाई (called) / लिए (took) / फल (fruits) / मूल (roots) / भेंट (gifts) / भरि (filled) / भारा (loads) / मिलन (to meet) / चलेउ (went) / हियँ (heart) / हरषु (joy) / अपारा (limitless)
ramacharitamanas::2387.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2387.essence: Love that is real moves your hands before your words.
ramacharitamanas::2387.simple_meaning: Guha hears that Ram is coming and is overjoyed. He gathers his people, loads up fruits and roots, and hurries out to welcome them.
ramacharitamanas::2387.simple_insight: Joy becomes action when love gets good news.
ramacharitamanas::2387.detailed_meaning: On the banks of the Ganga in Ayodhyakand, Guha the Nishada chief hears that Ram has arrived nearby. He immediately gathers his companions, prepares humble gifts of fruits and roots, and rushes out with overflowing happiness to meet his beloved guest.
ramacharitamanas::2387.modern_relevance: You hear that someone you love is finally arriving after a long delay. Instantly, you start gathering food, calling people, and making space for them before they even walk in.
ramacharitamanas::2387.insight: It shows how devotion turns greeting into service, not just feeling.

ramacharitamanas::2388.verse_sanskrit: करि दंडवत भेंट धरि आगें। प्रभुहि बिलोकत अति अनुरागें॥ सहज सनेह बिबस रघुराई। पूँछी कुसल निकट बैठाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2388.verse_hindi: दण्डवत करके भेंट सामने रखकर वह अत्यन्त प्रेम से प्रभु को देखने लगा। श्री रघुनाथजी ने स्वाभाविक स्नेह के वश होकर उसे अपने पास बैठाकर कुशल पूछी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2388.english_translation: After bowing down and offering his gift, he looked at the Lord with deep love. Raghunath, moved by natural affection, seated him close and asked after his welfare.
ramacharitamanas::2388.translation_literal: करि (having done) / दंडवत (full prostration) / भेंट (offering) / धरि (placing) / आगें (in front) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / बिलोकत (seeing) / अति (very) / अनुरागें (with love) / सहज (natural) / सनेह (affection) / बिबस (moved by) / रघुराई (Raghunath) / पूँछी (asked) / कुसल (well-being) / निकट (near) / बैठाई (having seated)
ramacharitamanas::2388.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2388.essence: Love makes reverence feel like home.
ramacharitamanas::2388.simple_meaning: Guh bows before Ram with love, and Ram responds by drawing him close and asking after his well-being.
ramacharitamanas::2388.simple_insight: Love lowers the distance between giver and receiver.
ramacharitamanas::2388.detailed_meaning: Guh, the Nishad chief, finally reaches Ram in exile after bringing fruit and roots as an offering. He bows fully before the Lord, and Ram immediately receives him with warmth, seating him nearby and asking how he is doing.
ramacharitamanas::2388.modern_relevance: You meet someone after years apart, and they don’t keep you at a polite distance. They pull you close, ask how you really are, and make you feel seen.
ramacharitamanas::2388.insight: It shows that true respect includes closeness, not formality.

ramacharitamanas::2389.verse_sanskrit: नाथ कुसल पद पंकज देखें। भयउँ भागभाजन जन लेखें॥ देव धरनि धनु धामु तुम्हारा। मैं जनु नीचु सहित परिवारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2389.verse_hindi: निषादराज ने उत्तर दिया- हे नाथ! आपके चरणकमल के दर्शन से ही कुशल है (आपके चरणारविन्दों के दर्शन कर) आज मैं भाग्यवान पुरुषों की गिनती में आ गया। हे देव! यह पृथ्वी, धन और घर सब आपका है। मैं तो परिवार सहित आपका नीच सेवक हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2389.english_translation: Nishadraj said: "O Lord, seeing your lotus feet is enough for my welfare. By that sight alone, I count myself among the fortunate. O divine one, this earth, wealth, and home are all yours. I am only your lowly servant, along with my family."
ramacharitamanas::2389.translation_literal: नाथ (lord) / कुसल (well-being) / पद पंकज (lotus feet) / देखें (having seen) / भयउँ (I became) / भागभाजन (a share-holder of fortune) / जन लेखें (among people counted)॥ / देव (divine one) / धरनि (earth) / धनु (wealth) / धामु (home) / तुम्हारा (yours) / मैं (I) / जनु (as) / नीचु (lowly) / सहित (together with) / परिवारा (family)॥
ramacharitamanas::2389.speaker: Nishadraj Guha
ramacharitamanas::2389.essence: Seeing Ram makes possession feel borrowed and service feel natural.
ramacharitamanas::2389.simple_meaning: Guha says that simply seeing Ram's feet has made him feel blessed. He offers everything he has as belonging to Ram and calls himself a humble servant with his family.
ramacharitamanas::2389.simple_insight: Real belonging begins when admiration turns into humble offering.
ramacharitamanas::2389.detailed_meaning: Guha has just welcomed Ram to the bank of the Ganga with overflowing joy. Standing before him, he says that even a single sight of Ram's feet has made life complete, and that his land, wealth, home, and family all belong to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2389.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence steadies you after months of noise, and suddenly your status games feel small. What you own matters less than what you are willing to offer.
ramacharitamanas::2389.insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to open-handed surrender of everything you call yours.

ramacharitamanas::2390.verse_sanskrit: कृपा करिअ पुर धारिअ पाऊ। थापिय जनु सबु लोगु सिहाऊ॥ कहेहु सत्य सबु सखा सुजाना। मोहि दीन्ह पितु आयसु आना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2390.verse_hindi: अब कृपा करके पुर (श्रृंगवेरपुर) में पधारिए और इस दास की प्रतिष्ठा बढ़ाइए, जिससे सब लोग मेरे भाग्य की बड़ाई करें। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने कहा- हे सुजान सखा! तुमने जो कुछ कहा सब सत्य है, परन्तु पिताजी ने मुझको और ही आज्ञा दी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2390.english_translation: Please be gracious and enter the city, and raise this servant’s honor so that everyone may praise my good fortune. Shri Ram said, “O wise friend, what you have said is true, but my father has given me a different command.”
ramacharitamanas::2390.translation_literal: कृपा (grace) / करिअ (do) / पुर (city) / धारिअ (place your feet, enter) / पाऊ (feet) / थापिय (establish) / जनु (so that) / सबु (all) / लोगु (people) / सिहाऊ (praise, admire)॥ / कहेहु (you said) / सत्य (true) / सबु (all) / सखा (friend) / सुजाना (wise) / मोहि (to me) / दीन्ह (gave) / पितु (father) / आयसु (command) / आना (other, different) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2390.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2390.essence: Applause can wait; a father’s command cannot.
ramacharitamanas::2390.simple_meaning: Ram gently refuses the invitation to enter the city because his father’s command is greater than public praise.
ramacharitamanas::2390.simple_insight: Real dignity comes from keeping faith with your word, not from being admired.
ramacharitamanas::2390.detailed_meaning: In Shrngverpur, Guha welcomes Ram with love and asks him to enter the city so everyone can honour him. Ram responds kindly, but he explains that Dasharath’s command to live in exile must be obeyed first.
ramacharitamanas::2390.modern_relevance: A manager offers you a flattering shortcut that would make everyone applaud, but it would break the promise you already made. The verse reminds you that integrity matters more than approval.
ramacharitamanas::2390.insight: It shifts the mind from seeking recognition to protecting a binding commitment.

ramacharitamanas::2391.verse_sanskrit: बरष चारिदस बासु बन मुनि ब्रत बेषु अहारु। ग्राम बासु नहिं उचित सुनि गुहहि भयउ दुखु भारु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2391.verse_hindi: (उनकी आज्ञानुसार) मुझे चौदह वर्ष तक मुनियों का व्रत और वेष धारण कर और मुनियों के योग्य आहार करते हुए वन में ही बसना है, गाँव के भीतर निवास करना उचित नहीं है। यह सुनकर गुह को बड़ा दुःख हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2391.english_translation: I must live in the forest for fourteen years, wearing the dress and discipline of a sage and eating only what is fit for hermits. Hearing that, Guha was overwhelmed with sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2391.translation_literal: बरष (years) / चारि-दस (fourteen) / बासु (residence) / बन (forest) / मुनि (sage) / ब्रत (vow/discipline) / बेषु (dress/form) / अहारु (food) / ग्राम (village) / बासु (residence) / नहिं (not) / उचित (proper) / सुनि (hearing) / गुहहि (to Guha) / भयउ (became) / दुखु (sorrow) / भारु (heavy)
ramacharitamanas::2391.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2391.essence: Duty stays binding even when it demands painful renunciation.
ramacharitamanas::2391.simple_meaning: Ram says he must spend fourteen years in the forest, living like a sage and following the rules of exile. Guha hears this and feels deep sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2391.simple_insight: A true commitment does not bend for comfort or convenience.
ramacharitamanas::2391.detailed_meaning: At the bank of the Ganga, Guha has just welcomed Ram, Lakshman, and Sita with reverence. Now he hears the full weight of Ram's exile: fourteen years in the forest, with sage-like dress, vows, and food. The news fills Guha with sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2391.modern_relevance: You accept a posting far from home because you made a promise, even though it changes everything. The cost is real, but the promise still stands.
ramacharitamanas::2391.insight: It shifts attention from personal comfort to the duty you have already accepted.

ramacharitamanas::2392.verse_sanskrit: राम लखन सिय रूप निहारी। कहहिं सप्रेम ग्राम नर नारी॥ ते पितु मातु कहहु सखि कैसे। जिन्ह पठए बन बालक ऐसे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2392.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी के रूप को देखकर गाँव के स्त्री-पुरुष प्रेम के साथ चर्चा करते हैं। (कोई कहती है-) हे सखी! कहो तो, वे माता-पिता कैसे हैं, जिन्होंने ऐसे (सुंदर सुकुमार) बालकों को वन में भेज दिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2392.english_translation: Seeing the forms of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, the village men and women speak with love. "Tell me, friend, what must their parents be like, who sent such tender children into the forest?"
ramacharitamanas::2392.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / रूप (form) / निहारी (having seen) / कहहिं (say) / सप्रेम (with love) / ग्राम (village) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / ते (they) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / कहहु (tell) / सखि (friend) / कैसे (how) / जिन्ह (who) / पठए (sent) / बन (forest) / बालक (children) / ऐसे (such)
ramacharitamanas::2392.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2392.essence: Their beauty makes the pain of exile impossible to ignore.
ramacharitamanas::2392.simple_meaning: The villagers see Ram, Lakshman, and Sita and are moved by their beauty and innocence. They wonder what kind of parents could send such gentle children into the forest.
ramacharitamanas::2392.simple_insight: Sometimes compassion begins with simply seeing how much a situation costs others.
ramacharitamanas::2392.detailed_meaning: As Ram, Lakshman, and Sita pass through the village on their way into exile, the local men and women are struck by their beauty and tenderness. Their admiration quickly turns to grief and wonder: what kind of parents could bear to send such children away?
ramacharitamanas::2392.modern_relevance: You watch a young family leave a station with one suitcase and tired faces, and suddenly the whole room feels the ache of separation.
ramacharitamanas::2392.insight: It shifts attention from the spectacle of exile to the human cost felt by ordinary people around it.

ramacharitamanas::2393.verse_sanskrit: एक कहहिं भल भूपति कीन्हा। लोयन लाहु हमहि बिधि दीन्हा॥ तब निषादपति उर अनुमाना। तरु सिंसुपा मनोहर जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2393.verse_hindi: कोई एक कहते हैं- राजा ने अच्छा ही किया, इसी बहाने हमें भी ब्रह्मा ने नेत्रों का लाभ दिया। तब निषाद राज ने हृदय में अनुमान किया, तो अशोक के पेड़ को (उनके ठहरने के लिए) मनोहर समझा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2393.english_translation: Some say, “The king has done well; by this, Brahma has granted us the blessing of seeing them.” Then Nishad-raja thought in his heart that the tamarind tree looked lovely for their stay.
ramacharitamanas::2393.translation_literal: एक (some) / कहहिं (say) / भल (good) / भूपति (king) / कीन्हा (has done) / लोयन (of eyes) / लाहु (gain) / हमहि (to us) / बिधि (Brahma / the divine order) / दीन्हा (has given) ॥ तब (then) / निषादपति (Nishad-raja) / उर (in heart) / अनुमाना (thought, inferred) / तरु (tree) / सिंसुपा (tamarind) / मनोहर (lovely) / जाना (knew, regarded) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2393.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2393.essence: Gratitude for a holy sight becomes care for their comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2393.simple_meaning: The villagers feel grateful to see Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Nishad-raja quietly notices a suitable tree nearby for their stay.
ramacharitamanas::2393.simple_insight: A sacred arrival changes the whole atmosphere; even ordinary people begin to see with gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::2393.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are passing through the village in exile. The people are so moved by their sight that they speak with joy and wonder, while Nishad-raja immediately turns his attention to their comfort and shelter.
ramacharitamanas::2393.modern_relevance: You spot someone you deeply respect at a roadside stop, and the whole place feels different. Gratitude makes even a simple tree seem like a gift.
ramacharitamanas::2393.insight: It shifts attention from spectacle to service: first wonder, then practical care for the guests.

ramacharitamanas::2394.verse_sanskrit: लै रघुनाथहिं ठाउँ देखावा। कहेउ राम सब भाँति सुहावा॥ पुरजन करि जोहारु घर आए। रघुबर संध्या करन सिधाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2394.verse_hindi: उसने श्री रघुनाथजी को ले जाकर वह स्थान दिखाया। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने (देखकर) कहा कि यह सब प्रकार से सुंदर है। पुरवासी लोग जोहार (वंदना) करके अपने-अपने घर लौटे और श्री रामचन्द्रजी संध्या करने पधारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2394.english_translation: He led Raghunath there and showed him the place. Ram said it was beautiful in every way. The townspeople bowed and returned home, and Raghubar went to perform his evening prayers.
ramacharitamanas::2394.translation_literal: लै (taking) / रघुनाथहिं (Raghunath) / ठाउँ (place) / देखावा (showed) / कहेउ (said) / राम (Ram) / सब (all) / भाँति (ways) / सुहावा (beautiful) / पुरजन (townspeople) / करि (doing) / जोहारु (bowing) / घर (home) / आए (came) / रघुबर (Raghuvar) / संध्या (evening prayer) / करन (to do) / सिधाए (went)
ramacharitamanas::2394.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2394.essence: A humble welcome can turn exile into home.
ramacharitamanas::2394.simple_meaning: Guh shows Ram a place to stay. Ram finds it pleasing, the townspeople bow and leave, and Ram goes to do his evening prayer.
ramacharitamanas::2394.simple_insight: Even a simple resting place becomes sacred when offered with respect and accepted with grace.
ramacharitamanas::2394.detailed_meaning: Guh has guided Ram, Lakshman, and Sita to a place by the river. Ram approves it warmly, the villagers bow and go home, and the evening settles into prayer. The verse quietly bridges arrival, welcome, and the first night of exile.
ramacharitamanas::2394.modern_relevance: You arrive tired at a friend's home after a hard day, and they quietly make space for you. No speech is needed; respect, welcome, and routine hold the moment together.
ramacharitamanas::2394.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic events to the dignity of simple hospitality and calm acceptance of the moment.

ramacharitamanas::2395.verse_sanskrit: गुहँ सँवारि साँथरी डसाई। कुस किसलयमय मृदुल सुहाई॥ सुचि फल मूल मधुर मृदु जानी। दोना भरि भरि राखेसि पानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2395.verse_hindi: गुह ने (इसी बीच) कुश और कोमल पत्तों की कोमल और सुंदर साथरी सजाकर बिछा दी और पवित्र, मीठे और कोमल देख-देखकर दोनों में भर-भरकर फल-मूल और पानी रख दिया (अथवा अपने हाथ से फल-मूल दोनों में भर-भरकर रख दिए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2395.english_translation: Guha arranged a soft bed of kusa grass and tender leaves, beautiful and comfortable. Knowing the fruits, roots, and water to be pure, sweet, and gentle, he filled two leaf-bowls with them and placed them there.
ramacharitamanas::2395.translation_literal: गुहँ (Guha) / सँवारि (having arranged) / साँथरी (bed) / डसाई (spread, laid down) / कुस (kusa grass) / किसलयमय (made of tender leaves) / मृदुल (soft) / सुहाई (beautiful, pleasing) / सुचि (pure) / फल (fruits) / मूल (roots) / मधुर (sweet) / मृदु (soft, tender) / जानी (knowing) / दोना (leaf-bowls) / भरि भरि (again and again, full) / राखेसि (he placed) / पानी (water)
ramacharitamanas::2395.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2395.essence: True welcome is shown through simple, careful service.
ramacharitamanas::2395.simple_meaning: Guha prepares a soft resting place and offers clean fruit, roots, and water to Ram and the others.
ramacharitamanas::2395.simple_insight: Care becomes sacred when you offer comfort without making a show of it.
ramacharitamanas::2395.detailed_meaning: After leading Ram to a resting place in the forest, Guha quietly prepares everything for the night. He spreads soft grass and leaves, then sets out fruit, roots, and water for Ram, Sita, and Lakshman. The scene shows his humble hospitality before the family rests.
ramacharitamanas::2395.modern_relevance: You set out extra blankets for a guest who arrived tired and unannounced. No speech, no display — just the quiet dignity of making someone feel safe.
ramacharitamanas::2395.insight: It shifts attention from grand devotion to practical care: comfort, cleanliness, and readiness for others.

ramacharitamanas::2396.verse_sanskrit: सिय सुमंत्र भ्राता सहित कंद मूल फल खाइ। सयन कीन्ह रघुबंसमनि पाय पलोटत भाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2396.verse_hindi: सीताजी, सुमंत्रजी और भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित कन्द-मूल-फल खाकर रघुकुल मणि श्री रामचन्द्रजी लेट गए। भाई लक्ष्मणजी उनके पैर दबाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2396.english_translation: Ram, Sita, Lakshman, and Sumantra ate roots, fruits, and bulbs, then the jewel of Raghu's line lay down while Lakshman massaged his feet.
ramacharitamanas::2396.translation_literal: सिय (Sita) / सुमंत्र (Sumantra) / भ्राता (brother) सहित (together with) / कंद (roots and bulbs) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruits) / खाइ (eating) / सयन (sleeping) / कीन्ह (did) / रघुबंसमनि (jewel of the Raghu line) / पाय (feet) / पलोटत (massaging) / भाइ (brother)
ramacharitamanas::2396.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2396.essence: Service becomes sacred when it asks for nothing back.
ramacharitamanas::2396.simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, Lakshman, and Sumantra ate simple forest food. Then Ram lay down, and Lakshman lovingly massaged his feet.
ramacharitamanas::2396.simple_insight: Love shows itself in small acts of care, not grand speeches.
ramacharitamanas::2396.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram has accepted exile with grace. Sita, Lakshman, and Sumantra share a simple meal of roots and fruit, then Ram rests while Lakshman serves him by massaging his feet. The scene shows quiet devotion, not philosophy.
ramacharitamanas::2396.modern_relevance: After a long day away from home, someone shares the last simple meal with you, then stays awake to make sure you rest. That kind of care says everything.
ramacharitamanas::2396.insight: It shifts attention from status to service, showing that love is proved through practical care.

ramacharitamanas::2397.verse_sanskrit: उठे लखनु प्रभु सोवत जानी। कहि सचिवहि सोवन मृदु बानी॥ कछुक दूरि सजि बान सरासन। जागन लगे बैठि बीरासन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2397.verse_hindi: फिर प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को सोते जानकर लक्ष्मणजी उठे और कोमल वाणी से मंत्री सुमंत्रजी को सोने के लिए कहकर वहाँ से कुछ दूर पर धनुष-बाण से सजकर, वीरासन से बैठकर जागने (पहरा देने) लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2397.english_translation: Then Lakshman, seeing that the Lord was asleep, gently told the minister Sumantra to sleep. He moved a little away, armed himself with bow and arrows, and sat in a warrior's posture to keep watch.
ramacharitamanas::2397.translation_literal: उठे (rose) / लखनु (Lakshman) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सोवत (sleeping) / जानी (having known) / कहि (saying) / सचिवहि (to the minister) / सोवन (to sleep) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (words) / कछुक (a little) / दूरि (away) / सजि (adorned/put on) / बान (arrows) / सरासन (bow and quiver) / जागन (to keep awake) / लगे (began) / बैठि (sitting) / बीरासन (warrior's posture)
ramacharitamanas::2397.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2397.essence: Love stays awake so someone else can rest.
ramacharitamanas::2397.simple_meaning: Lakshman quietly tells Sumantra to rest, then arms himself and stays awake guarding Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2397.simple_insight: Real care often looks like staying alert so someone else can sleep.
ramacharitamanas::2397.detailed_meaning: Ram has just lain down in exile, and the forest camp settles into night. Lakshman refuses rest, gently sending Sumantra to sleep while he takes up arms and keeps vigil nearby. His service becomes protection.
ramacharitamanas::2397.modern_relevance: You finally get your child to sleep after a hard day, but you keep one eye open, listening for every sound. Love sometimes means being the one who does not rest.
ramacharitamanas::2397.insight: It shifts service from words into protective presence: you guard what you love even while others sleep.

ramacharitamanas::2398.verse_sanskrit: गुहँ बोलाइ पाहरू प्रतीती। ठावँ ठावँ राखे अति प्रीती॥ आपु लखन पहिं बैठेउ जाई। कटि भाथी सर चाप चढ़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2398.verse_hindi: गुह ने विश्वासपात्र पहरेदारों को बुलाकर अत्यन्त प्रेम से जगह-जगह नियुक्त कर दिया और आप कमर में तरकस बाँधकर तथा धनुष पर बाण चढ़ाकर लक्ष्मणजी के पास जा बैठा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2398.english_translation: Guha called trusted guards and placed them everywhere with great affection. Then he himself sat near Lakshman, fastening his quiver at his waist and lifting his bow and arrows.
ramacharitamanas::2398.translation_literal: गुहँ (Guha) / बोलाइ (calling) / पाहरू (guards) / प्रतीती (trusted) / ठावँ ठावँ (in every place) / राखे (placed) / अति प्रीती (with great affection) ॥ / आपु (himself) / लखन पहिं (near Lakshman) / बैठेउ (sat) / जाई (going) ॥ / कटि (waist) / भाथी (quiver) / सर (arrows) / चाप (bow) / चढ़ाई (having lifted/strung) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2398.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2398.essence: Love proves itself by standing guard.
ramacharitamanas::2398.simple_meaning: Guha carefully posts trusted guards everywhere, then sits beside Lakshman armed and ready.
ramacharitamanas::2398.simple_insight: Real care is not just words; it shows up as protection, presence, and readiness.
ramacharitamanas::2398.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank during Ram's exile, Guha quietly takes charge of the night watch. He spreads trusted guards around the camp, then sits near Lakshman with bow and arrows in hand, guarding the sleeping Ram with loyal vigilance.
ramacharitamanas::2398.modern_relevance: You stay awake beside a friend in crisis, checking the door, the phone, the room, because love sometimes looks like staying alert.
ramacharitamanas::2398.insight: It shows devotion as practical protection, not sentiment. Love becomes watchfulness when someone vulnerable must be kept safe.

ramacharitamanas::2399.verse_sanskrit: सोवत प्रभुहि निहारि निषादू। भयउ प्रेम बस हृदयँ बिषादू॥ तनु पुलकित जलु लोचन बहई। बचन सप्रेम लखन सन कहई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2399.verse_hindi: प्रभु को जमीन पर सोते देखकर प्रेम वश निषाद राज के हृदय में विषाद हो आया। उसका शरीर पुलकित हो गया और नेत्रों से (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल बहने लगा। वह प्रेम सहित लक्ष्मणजी से वचन कहने लगा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2399.english_translation: Seeing the Lord sleeping on the ground, Nishad's heart filled with sorrow born of love. His body thrilled, tears flowed from his eyes, and he spoke lovingly to Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::2399.translation_literal: सोवत (sleeping) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / निहारि (seeing) / निषादू (Nishad) / भयउ (became) / प्रेम (love) / बस (under the sway of) / हृदयँ (heart) / बिषादू (sorrow) / तनु (body) / पुलकित (thrilled) / जलु (water/tears) / लोचन (eyes) / बहई (flowed) / बचन (words) / सप्रेम (with love) / लखन सन (to Lakshman) / कहई (spoke)
ramacharitamanas::2399.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2399.essence: Love deepens into sorrow when greatness chooses humility.
ramacharitamanas::2399.simple_meaning: Nishad sees Ram sleeping on the ground and feels such loving sorrow that his body trembles and tears flow.
ramacharitamanas::2399.simple_insight: Love can hurt beautifully when you see someone you cherish treated with humility.
ramacharitamanas::2399.detailed_meaning: At night, in the forest, Ram is resting on the ground while Lakshman keeps watch. Nishad sees this and is overwhelmed. His love turns into tears, and he begins speaking gently to Lakshman, moved by Ram's simplicity and dignity.
ramacharitamanas::2399.modern_relevance: You see someone you respect sleeping on a hard floor after helping everyone else, and something in you breaks open. Gratitude and tenderness arrive together.
ramacharitamanas::2399.insight: It shows how devotion can become visible as tears, trembling, and gentle speech.

ramacharitamanas::2400.verse_sanskrit: भूपति भवन सुभायँ सुहावा। सुरपति सदनु न पटतर पावा॥ मनिमय रचित चारु चौबारे। जनु रतिपति निज हाथ सँवारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2400.verse_hindi: महाराज दशरथजी का महल तो स्वभाव से ही सुंदर है, इन्द्रभवन भी जिसकी समानता नहीं पा सकता। उसमें सुंदर मणियों के रचे चौबारे (छत के ऊपर बँगले) हैं, जिन्हें मानो रति के पति कामदेव ने अपने ही हाथों सजाकर बनाया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2400.english_translation: King Dasharath's palace is naturally beautiful. Even Indra's own mansion could not match it. Its lovely upper chambers are built of gems, as if Cupid himself had decorated them with his own hands.
ramacharitamanas::2400.translation_literal: भूपति (of the king) / भवन (palace) / सुभायँ (by nature) / सुहावा (beautiful) / सुरपति (lord of the devas) / सदनु (mansion) / न (not) / पटतर (equal) / पावा (found)॥ / मनिमय (made of gems) / रचित (constructed) / चारु (beautiful) / चौबारे (upper chambers) / जनु (as if) / रतिपति (lord of desire) / निज (own) / हाथ (hands) / सँवारे (decorated)॥
ramacharitamanas::2400.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2400.essence: Splendor can surround a house long before sorrow enters it.
ramacharitamanas::2400.simple_meaning: Dasharath's palace is described as extraordinarily beautiful, richer than even Indra's abode, with gem-built upper chambers.
ramacharitamanas::2400.simple_insight: Some scenes are painted to show the world before loss arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2400.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the story briefly lingers inside Dasharath's splendid palace before grief overtakes the royal house. The narrator describes its beauty in rich detail, setting up the contrast between outward grandeur and the sorrow that will soon enter it.
ramacharitamanas::2400.modern_relevance: You walk through a house that once felt full of life, noticing the polished floor, the lights, the careful order. Beauty can stay in a place even after joy begins to leave it.
ramacharitamanas::2400.insight: It frames the palace as a world of luxury, making the coming emotional collapse feel sharper.

ramacharitamanas::2401.verse_sanskrit: सुचि सुबिचित्र सुभोगमय सुमन सुगंध सुबास। पलँग मंजु मनि दीप जहँ सब बिधि सकल सुपास ॥
ramacharitamanas::2401.verse_hindi: जो पवित्र, बड़े ही विलक्षण, सुंदर भोग पदार्थों से पूर्ण और फूलों की सुगंध से सुवासित हैं, जहाँ सुंदर पलँग और मणियों के दीपक हैं तथा सब प्रकार का पूरा आराम है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2401.english_translation: There are pure, wondrous, delightful offerings; flowers scent the air; a lovely bed, jeweled lamps, and every comfort are there.
ramacharitamanas::2401.translation_literal: सुचि (pure) / सुबिचित्र (wonderfully varied) / सुभोगमय (full of delightful enjoyments) / सुमन (flowers) / सुगंध (fragrance) / सुबास (sweet smell) / पलँग (bed) / मंजु (lovely) / मनि (jewels) / दीप (lamps) / जहँ (where) / सब बिधि (in every way) / सकल (all) / सुपास (comfort, ease)
ramacharitamanas::2401.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2401.essence: Luxury here is not vanity; it is care made visible.
ramacharitamanas::2401.simple_meaning: The place is richly prepared with fragrant flowers, a beautiful bed, jeweled lamps, and every kind of comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2401.simple_insight: Sometimes love shows itself in the care taken to make another person rest well.
ramacharitamanas::2401.detailed_meaning: In Dasharath's palace, the scene lingers on the luxury prepared for Ram and Sita. The poet lists flowers, lamps, bedding, and comforts to show the beauty of the royal setting before the deeper emotional contrast that follows.
ramacharitamanas::2401.modern_relevance: You walk into a guest room someone prepared for you with fresh sheets, soft light, and flowers on the table. The detail itself says: you were expected, and you were cared for.
ramacharitamanas::2401.insight: It shifts attention from mere luxury to the tenderness hidden inside hospitality.

ramacharitamanas::2402.verse_sanskrit: बिबिध बसन उपधान तुराईं। छीर फेन मृदु बिसद सुहाईं॥ तहँ सिय रामु सयन निसि करहीं। निज छबि रति मनोज मदु हरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2402.verse_hindi: जहाँ (ओढ़ने-बिछाने के) अनेकों वस्त्र, तकिए और गद्दे हैं, जो दूध के फेन के समान कोमल, निर्मल (उज्ज्वल) और सुंदर हैं, वहाँ (उन चौबारों में) श्री सीताजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी रात को सोया करते थे और अपनी शोभा से रति और कामदेव के गर्व को हरण करते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2402.english_translation: There, with many garments, pillows, and mattresses soft as milk foam, Sita and Ram used to sleep at night, and their beauty humbled the pride of Rati and Kamadeva.
ramacharitamanas::2402.translation_literal: बिबिध (various) / बसन (garments) / उपधान (pillows) / तुराईं (mattresses) / छीर (milk) / फेन (foam) / मृदु (soft) / बिसद (clear, bright) / सुहाईं (beautiful) / तहँ (there) / सिय (Sita) / रामु (Ram) / सयन (sleep) / निसि (night) / करहीं (would do) / निज (their own) / छबि (beauty) / रति (Rati) / मनोज (Kamadeva) / मदु (pride) / हरहीं (would remove)
ramacharitamanas::2402.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2402.essence: Royal comfort means little beside the radiance of Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2402.simple_meaning: Sita and Ram once slept in royal comfort, surrounded by soft, beautiful bedding. Their radiance was so great it outshone even the pride of desire itself.
ramacharitamanas::2402.simple_insight: Beauty and comfort are fragile; what truly dazzles is the presence of the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::2402.detailed_meaning: The palace of Ayodhya is being described in its full luxury before the exile. Sita and Ram sleep there at night among costly bedding and ornaments, yet even that royal splendor is only a backdrop to their own radiance. The verse prepares the contrast with their coming hardship.
ramacharitamanas::2402.modern_relevance: You remember the house before the breakup: warm sheets, quiet rooms, everything in place. The details matter because they make the loss feel real.
ramacharitamanas::2402.insight: It sets up a sharp contrast between former comfort and the exile that follows.

ramacharitamanas::2403.verse_sanskrit: ते सिय रामु साथरीं सोए। श्रमित बसन बिनु जाहिं न जोए॥ मातु पिता परिजन पुरबासी। सखा सुसील दास अरु दासी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2403.verse_hindi: वही श्री सीता और श्री रामजी आज घास-फूस की साथरी पर थके हुए बिना वस्त्र के ही सोए हैं। ऐसी दशा में वे देखे नहीं जाते। माता, पिता, कुटुम्बी, पुरवासी (प्रजा), मित्र, अच्छे शील-स्वभाव के दास और दासियाँ- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2403.english_translation: There, Sita and Ram slept on a grass bed, exhausted and unclothed, unseen in that state by mother, father, family, city people, friends, noble servants, and maidservants.
ramacharitamanas::2403.translation_literal: ते (they) / सिय (Sita) / रामु (Ram) / साथरीं (on a bed) / सोए (slept) / श्रमित (tired) / बसन (clothes) / बिनु (without) / जाहिं (are) / न (not) / जोए (seen) / मातु (mother) / पिता (father) / परिजन (family) / पुरबासी (city-dwellers) / सखा (friends) / सुसील (well-mannered) / दास (servants) / अरु (and) / दासी (maidservants)
ramacharitamanas::2403.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2403.essence: Comfort can vanish, and still the beloved remains.
ramacharitamanas::2403.simple_meaning: Ram and Sita are sleeping on a simple grass bed, worn out and stripped of royal comfort. The people who once surrounded them with care can no longer even see them there.
ramacharitamanas::2403.simple_insight: Greatness can be hidden in hardship, and love often remains when comfort disappears.
ramacharitamanas::2403.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the royal life has collapsed into exile. Ram and Sita, once cared for by an entire household, now sleep on grass, exhausted and deprived. The verse lingers on the contrast between past abundance and present loss.
ramacharitamanas::2403.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love sleep on a hospital chair after a brutal day, too tired to speak. The room is quiet, and all the status that once surrounded them feels far away.
ramacharitamanas::2403.insight: It shifts attention from royal dignity to the human cost of exile and separation.

ramacharitamanas::2404.verse_sanskrit: जोगवहिं जिन्हहि प्रान की नाईं। महि सोवत तेइ राम गोसाईं॥ पिता जनक जग बिदित प्रभाऊ। ससुर सुरेस सखा रघुराऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2404.verse_hindi: सब जिनकी अपने प्राणों की तरह सार-संभार करते थे, वही प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी आज पृथ्वी पर सो रहे हैं। जिनके पिता जनकजी हैं, जिनका प्रभाव जगत में प्रसिद्ध है, जिनके ससुर इन्द्र के मित्र रघुराज दशरथजी हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2404.english_translation: The one everyone cared for like their own life is now sleeping on the ground, Lord Ram. His father is Janak, whose fame is known throughout the world, and his father-in-law is Dasharath, friend of Indra and lord of Raghu.
ramacharitamanas::2404.translation_literal: जोगवहिं (they cared for) / जिन्हहि (whom) / प्रान की नाईं (like life itself) / महि (on the ground) / सोवत (sleeping) / तेइ (that very) / राम (Ram) / गोसाईं (lord)॥ / पिता (father) / जनक (Janak) / जग (world) / बिदित (known) / प्रभाऊ (whose fame/power is known) / ससुर (father-in-law) / सुरेस (Indra) / सखा (friend) / रघुराऊ (lord of Raghu)
ramacharitamanas::2404.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2404.essence: Honor and hardship can belong to the same person at once.
ramacharitamanas::2404.simple_meaning: Ram, who was once cared for like a precious life, now lies asleep on the bare ground. The verse also reminds us of his noble family and standing.
ramacharitamanas::2404.simple_insight: Greatness can be stripped of comfort in an instant, and dignity still remains.
ramacharitamanas::2404.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the prince who should have rested in royal ease is now in exile, sleeping on the earth. Tulsidas lingers on the contrast: the one cherished like life itself is reduced to hardship, even while his family and status remain glorious.
ramacharitamanas::2404.modern_relevance: You watch someone who once had every advantage sit on a hard floor after everything changes overnight. Status can vanish; character is what stays visible.
ramacharitamanas::2404.insight: It trains the mind to notice how quickly worldly comfort can fall away without touching a person's worth.

ramacharitamanas::2405.verse_sanskrit: रामचंदु पति सो बैदेही। सोवत महि बिधि बाम न केही॥ सिय रघुबीर कि कानन जोगू। करम प्रधान सत्य कह लोगू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2405.verse_hindi: और पति श्री रामचन्द्रजी हैं, वही जानकीजी आज जमीन पर सो रही हैं। विधाता किसको प्रतिकूल नहीं होता! सीताजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी क्या वन के योग्य हैं? लोग सच कहते हैं कि कर्म (भाग्य) ही प्रधान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2405.english_translation: And Janaki's husband, Ramchandra, is lying on the ground. Who has not felt the world turn against them? Are Sita and Ram fit for the forest? People truly say that karma is supreme.
ramacharitamanas::2405.translation_literal: रामचंदु (Ramchandra) / पति (husband) / सो (that) / बैदेही (Vaidehi, Sita) / सोवत (sleeping) / महि (on the ground) / बिधि (fate / the creator) / बाम (adverse) / न (not) / केही (to whom) / सिय (Sita) / रघुबीर (Raghubir, Ram) / कि (whether) / कानन (forest) / जोगू (fit for) / करम (karma) / प्रधान (supreme) / सत्य (true) / कह (say) / लोगू (people)
ramacharitamanas::2405.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2405.essence: Even the noblest lives must sometimes bow to hard reality.
ramacharitamanas::2405.simple_meaning: Even Ram and Sita are sleeping on the ground in exile. The verse accepts that life can turn harsh for anyone, and people call this the rule of karma.
ramacharitamanas::2405.simple_insight: You can stop arguing with reality and see hardship as part of life’s pattern.
ramacharitamanas::2405.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's grief, Ram and Sita are now living in the forest on the ground. The speaker looks at their suffering and names the hard truth: even the most worthy lives are not spared reversal, and people call that the working of karma.
ramacharitamanas::2405.modern_relevance: You did everything right, and still the plan collapsed. The apartment fell through, the parent got sick, the promotion vanished. This verse meets you there and asks you to stop pretending life owes fairness.
ramacharitamanas::2405.insight: It shifts the mind from protest to sober acceptance of what cannot be controlled.

ramacharitamanas::2406.verse_sanskrit: कैकयनंदिनि मंदमति कठिन कुटिलपन कीन्ह। जेहिं रघुनंदन जानकिहि सुख अवसर दुखु दीन्ह ॥
ramacharitamanas::2406.verse_hindi: कैकयराज की लड़की नीच बुद्धि कैकेयी ने बड़ी ही कुटिलता की, जिसने रघुनंदन श्री रामजी और जानकीजी को सुख के समय दुःख दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2406.english_translation: The daughter of Kaikeyi acted with cruel, crooked intent. She brought sorrow to Raghunandan and Janaki at the very moment of their joy.
ramacharitamanas::2406.translation_literal: कैकयनंदिनि (daughter of Kaikeyi) / मंदमति (of dull intelligence) / कठिन (harsh) / कुटिलपन (crookedness) / कीन्ह (did) / जेहिं (by whom) / रघुनंदन (Raghunandan) / जानकिहि (to Janaki) / सुख (joy) / अवसर (time, occasion) / दुखु (sorrow) / दीन्ह (gave)
ramacharitamanas::2406.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2406.essence: Crooked choices turn joy into grief for everyone nearby.
ramacharitamanas::2406.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi acted with cruel deceit and turned Ram and Sita's happiness into sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2406.simple_insight: A selfish choice can poison joy for everyone around it.
ramacharitamanas::2406.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram and Sita are already being forced into hardship. Tulsidas names Kaikeyi's betrayal directly: her crooked choice has broken the family’s happiness and set grief loose across Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::2406.modern_relevance: A parent’s harsh decision at the wrong moment can shatter a home’s peace. One act of manipulation can turn a celebration into a wound that everyone carries.
ramacharitamanas::2406.insight: It exposes how desire and cunning can damage not just one life, but an entire household.

ramacharitamanas::2407.verse_sanskrit: भइ दिनकर कुल बिटप कुठारी। कुमति कीन्ह सब बिस्व दुखारी॥ भयउ बिषादु निषादहि भारी। राम सीय महि सयन निहारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2407.verse_hindi: वह सूर्यकुल रूपी वृक्ष के लिए कुल्हाड़ी हो गई। उस कुबुद्धि ने सम्पूर्ण विश्व को दुःखी कर दिया। श्री राम-सीता को जमीन पर सोते हुए देखकर निषाद को बड़ा दुःख हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2407.english_translation: She became an axe for the solar dynasty's tree. That foolish mind brought sorrow to the whole world. Nishad felt deep grief seeing Ram and Sita sleeping on the ground.
ramacharitamanas::2407.translation_literal: भइ (became) / दिनकर (sun) / कुल (lineage) / बिटप (tree) / कुठारी (axe) / कुमति (foolish mind) / कीन्ह (did) / सब (all) / बिस्व (world) / दुखारी (made sorrowful) / भयउ (became) / बिषादु (grief) / निषादहि (to Nishad) / भारी (great) / राम (Ram) / सीय (Sita) / महि (on the ground) / सयन (sleeping) / निहारी (seeing)
ramacharitamanas::2407.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2407.essence: A crooked choice can wound an entire world.
ramacharitamanas::2407.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi's bad choice cut down the royal family's peace and hurt the whole world. Seeing Ram and Sita sleeping on the ground filled Nishad with grief.
ramacharitamanas::2407.simple_insight: One selfish choice can wound far beyond the people directly involved.
ramacharitamanas::2407.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the exile has already begun. Kaikeyi's demand has torn the royal house apart, and Ram and Sita now sleep on the ground. Nishad, loyal and tender-hearted, sees the cost of that decision and feels the grief of the whole scene.
ramacharitamanas::2407.modern_relevance: You watch one harsh message shatter a family dinner, and everyone goes quiet. The damage is bigger than the argument itself.
ramacharitamanas::2407.insight: It shifts attention from private impulse to public consequence: your choices ripple through everyone around you.

ramacharitamanas::2408.verse_sanskrit: बोले लखन मधुर मृदु बानी। ग्यान बिराग भगति रस सानी॥ काहु न कोउ सुख दुख कर दाता। निज कृत करम भोग सबु भ्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2408.verse_hindi: तब लक्ष्मणजी ज्ञान, वैराग्य और भक्ति के रस से सनी हुई मीठी और कोमल वाणी बोले- हे भाई! कोई किसी को सुख-दुःख का देने वाला नहीं है। सब अपने ही किए हुए कर्मों का फल भोगते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2408.english_translation: Then Lakshman spoke in sweet, gentle words, filled with the flavor of wisdom, non-attachment, and devotion. No one gives anyone else happiness or sorrow, brother. Everyone experiences the fruit of their own actions.
ramacharitamanas::2408.translation_literal: बोले (spoke) / लखन (Lakshman) / मधुर (sweet) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (speech) / ग्यान (wisdom) / बिराग (non-attachment) / भगति (devotion) / रस (essence) / सानी (mixed) / काहु (someone) / न (not) / कोउ (anyone) / सुख (happiness) / दुख (sorrow) / कर (of) / दाता (giver) / निज (own) / कृत (done) / करम (actions) / भोग (experience) / सबु (all) / भ्राता (brother)
ramacharitamanas::2408.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::2408.essence: Your experience comes from your own actions, not from other people.
ramacharitamanas::2408.simple_meaning: Lakshman says that nobody else is the true giver of your happiness or sorrow. What you experience comes from your own actions.
ramacharitamanas::2408.simple_insight: Blame softens when you remember your life is not being handed to you by others.
ramacharitamanas::2408.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Kaikeyi's demand has shattered Ram's life, Lakshman speaks gently to ease the pain. He brings wisdom, non-attachment, and devotion together to say that suffering is not simply given by another person; it unfolds through karma.
ramacharitamanas::2408.modern_relevance: You replay a harsh email for hours, convinced one person ruined your day. Lakshman's words ask you to look deeper: what you feel now is also shaped by your own habits, reactions, and past choices.
ramacharitamanas::2408.insight: It shifts blame into responsibility, so you stop seeing yourself as a victim of other people's hands.

ramacharitamanas::2409.verse_sanskrit: जोग बियोग भोग भल मंदा। हित अनहित मध्यम भ्रम फंदा॥ जनमु मरनु जहँ लगि जग जालू। संपति बिपति करमु अरु कालू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2409.verse_hindi: संयोग (मिलना), वियोग (बिछुड़ना), भले-बुरे भोग, शत्रु, मित्र और उदासीन- ये सभी भ्रम के फंदे हैं। जन्म-मृत्यु, सम्पत्ति-विपत्ति, कर्म और काल- जहाँ तक जगत के जंजाल हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2409.english_translation: Union and separation, pleasure and pain, good and bad, friend and enemy, are all traps of confusion. Birth and death, gain and loss, action and time — all belong to the net of the world.
ramacharitamanas::2409.translation_literal: जोग (union) / बियोग (separation) / भोग (enjoyment) / भल (good) / मंदा (bad) / हित (benefit/friend) / अनहित (harm/enemy) / मध्यम (neutral) / भ्रम (delusion) / फंदा (snare) ॥ / जनमु (birth) / मरनु (death) / जहँ लगि (as far as) / जग (world) / जालू (net) ॥ / संपति (wealth) / बिपति (adversity) / करमु (action) / अरु (and) / कालू (time) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2409.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2409.essence: Opposites are part of the trap, not the final reality.
ramacharitamanas::2409.simple_meaning: Opposites like pleasure and pain, friend and enemy, birth and death all belong to the world’s confusion. They are not the final reality.
ramacharitamanas::2409.simple_insight: You can stop treating every swing of life as ultimate. That brings quiet distance from the pull of events.
ramacharitamanas::2409.detailed_meaning: Lakshman has just spoken after Ram’s exile, trying to steady grief with wisdom. The verse widens the lens: every pair of opposites, every life event, even time itself, belongs to the world’s net. None of it is final.
ramacharitamanas::2409.modern_relevance: You get a promotion and feel lifted, then one email ruins your day. This verse reminds you that both highs and lows are part of the same passing pattern.
ramacharitamanas::2409.insight: It shifts you from chasing and resisting opposites to seeing them as passing conditions, not your identity.

ramacharitamanas::2410.verse_sanskrit: दरनि धामु धनु पुर परिवारू। सरगु नरकु जहँ लगि ब्यवहारू॥ देखिअ सुनिअ गुनिअ मन माहीं। मोह मूल परमारथु नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2410.verse_hindi: धरती, घर, धन, नगर, परिवार, स्वर्ग और नरक आदि जहाँ तक व्यवहार हैं, जो देखने, सुनने और मन के अंदर विचारने में आते हैं, इन सबका मूल मोह (अज्ञान) ही है। परमार्थतः ये नहीं हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2410.english_translation: Earth, home, wealth, city, and family; even heaven and hell belong only to worldly dealings. Whatever is seen, heard, or thought in the mind has ignorance at its root. In ultimate reality, none of this is what it seems.
ramacharitamanas::2410.translation_literal: दरनि (earth) / धामु (home) / धनु (wealth) / पुर (city) / परिवारू (family) / सरगु (heaven) / नरकु (hell) / जहँ लगि (as far as) / ब्यवहारू (worldly dealings) / देखिअ (seen) / सुनिअ (heard) / गुनिअ (thought over) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / मोह (delusion) / मूल (root) / परमारथु (ultimate reality) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::2410.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2410.essence: What the mind clings to is not the final truth.
ramacharitamanas::2410.simple_meaning: What looks real in ordinary life—possessions, places, family, even ideas of reward and punishment—can all be shaped by delusion. Ultimate reality is different from what the mind usually takes in.
ramacharitamanas::2410.simple_insight: You can stop treating appearances as final and feel less trapped by them.
ramacharitamanas::2410.detailed_meaning: Laxman has been explaining how the world of opposites traps the mind. He now points to everything people cling to—land, wealth, home, family, even heaven and hell—and says all of it belongs to the realm of delusion, not final reality.
ramacharitamanas::2410.modern_relevance: You refresh the same bank app, the same family chat, the same status update, hoping it will settle your mind. This verse asks you to notice that the craving itself is what keeps the whole scene spinning.
ramacharitamanas::2410.insight: It shifts you from trusting appearances to questioning the mind that labels them.

ramacharitamanas::2411.verse_sanskrit: सपनें होइ भिखारि नृपु रंकु नाकपति होइ। जागें लाभु न हानि कछु तिमि प्रपंच जियँ जोइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2411.verse_hindi: जैसे स्वप्न में राजा भिखारी हो जाए या कंगाल स्वर्ग का स्वामी इन्द्र हो जाए, तो जागने पर लाभ या हानि कुछ भी नहीं है, वैसे ही इस दृश्य-प्रपंच को हृदय से देखना चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2411.english_translation: As in a dream a king becomes a beggar and a beggar becomes the lord of the heavens, yet on waking there is neither gain nor loss, so you should regard this seen world in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2411.translation_literal: सपनें (in a dream) / होइ (becomes) / भिखारि (beggar) / नृपु (king) / रंकु (pauper) / नाकपति (lord of heaven) / होइ (becomes) / जागें (on waking) / लाभु (gain) / न हानि (nor loss) / कछु (anything) / तिमि (thus) / प्रपंच (world of appearances) / जियँ (in the heart) / जोइ (see)
ramacharitamanas::2411.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2411.essence: What shakes you in appearance may leave no trace in awakening.
ramacharitamanas::2411.simple_meaning: Worldly highs and lows are like dream changes: dramatic while they last, but empty after awakening. See the world with that distance, and it loses its grip.
ramacharitamanas::2411.simple_insight: You can stop being shaken by success and failure once you see how temporary they are.
ramacharitamanas::2411.detailed_meaning: After listing how every worldly thing falls into confusion, Tulsidas gives the key insight in Ayodhyakand: the world of appearances is like a dream. A king can become a beggar in sleep, but waking erases the whole story.
ramacharitamanas::2411.modern_relevance: You wake up to a message that your promotion was cancelled, and by lunch another email says it was restored. The panic felt absolute for an hour, but the event itself was never the whole of you.
ramacharitamanas::2411.insight: It trains you to step back from emotional overreaction by seeing success, loss, and status as temporary appearances.

ramacharitamanas::2412.verse_sanskrit: अस बिचारि नहिं कीजिअ रोसू। काहुहि बादि न देइअ दोसू॥ मोह निसाँ सबु सोवनिहारा। देखिअ सपन अनेक प्रकारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2412.verse_hindi: ऐसा विचारकर क्रोध नहीं करना चाहिए और न किसी को व्यर्थ दोष ही देना चाहिए। सब लोग मोह रूपी रात्रि में सोने वाले हैं और सोते हुए उन्हें अनेकों प्रकार के स्वप्न दिखाई देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2412.english_translation: Thinking this way, you should not get angry, and you should not blame anyone in vain. Everyone sleeps in the night of delusion and sees many kinds of dreams.
ramacharitamanas::2412.translation_literal: अस (thus) / बिचारि (having considered) / नहिं (not) / कीजिअ (should be done) / रोसू (anger) । / काहुहि (to anyone) / बादि (needlessly) / न देइअ (should not give) / दोसू (fault) ॥ / मोह (delusion) / निसाँ (night) / सबु (everyone) / सोवनिहारा (sleeping one) । / देखिअ (are seen) / सपन (dreams) / अनेक (many) / प्रकारा (kinds) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2412.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2412.essence: Anger fades when you see people as dreamers in delusion.
ramacharitamanas::2412.simple_meaning: Do not get angry or assign blame carelessly. People act from confusion, like sleepers having different dreams in the dark.
ramacharitamanas::2412.simple_insight: It softens judgment and makes room for patience with human confusion.
ramacharitamanas::2412.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is widening the lens after showing how worldly life and even heaven and hell belong to the realm of appearance. He now says anger and blame are pointless because people are moving through delusion, like dreamers in the night.
ramacharitamanas::2412.modern_relevance: Someone cuts you off in traffic, then you see the same person later with tears in their eyes after a phone call. The verse asks you to pause before turning one moment into a verdict about their whole character.
ramacharitamanas::2412.insight: It trains you to observe confusion without immediately converting it into blame.

ramacharitamanas::2413.verse_sanskrit: एहिं जग जामिनि जागहिं जोगी। परमारथी प्रपंच बियोगी॥ जानिअ तबहिं जीव जग जागा। जब सब बिषय बिलास बिरागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2413.verse_hindi: इस जगत रूपी रात्रि में योगी लोग जागते हैं, जो परमार्थी हैं और प्रपंच (मायिक जगत) से छूटे हुए हैं। जगत में जीव को जागा हुआ तभी जानना चाहिए, जब सम्पूर्ण भोग-विलासों से वैराग्य हो जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2413.english_translation: In this world-night, yogis stay awake. Those devoted to the highest aim and free from worldly illusion are awake. A living being is truly awake only when all desire for pleasures has fallen away.
ramacharitamanas::2413.translation_literal: एहिं (in this) / जग (world) / जामिनि (night) / जागहिं (stay awake) / जोगी (yogis) । परमारथी (those devoted to the highest aim) / प्रपंच (worldly illusion) / बियोगी (separated from) ॥ जानिअ (know) / तबहिं (then only) / जीव (living being) / जग (in the world) / जागा (awake) । जब (when) / सब (all) / बिषय (sense-pleasures) / बिलास (enjoyments) / बिरागा (dispassion has arisen) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2413.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2413.essence: Wakefulness begins when desire for pleasure no longer controls you.
ramacharitamanas::2413.simple_meaning: True wakefulness is not just being physically alert. A person is truly awake when attachment to pleasures has dropped away.
ramacharitamanas::2413.simple_insight: There is relief in realizing that freedom begins when craving loosens its grip.
ramacharitamanas::2413.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the sorrow over exile and delusion has already been contrasted with a deeper way of seeing. The narrator now says that yogis are awake in this world-night, and that real wakefulness appears only when desire for pleasures has faded.
ramacharitamanas::2413.modern_relevance: You close one tab, open another, and still feel restless. The phone is silent, but your mind keeps reaching for the next hit of distraction. This verse calls that restlessness sleep, not wakefulness.
ramacharitamanas::2413.insight: It shifts attention from external alertness to inner freedom from craving.

ramacharitamanas::2414.verse_sanskrit: होइ बिबेकु मोह भ्रम भागा। तब रघुनाथ चरन अनुरागा॥ सखा परम परमारथु एहू। मन क्रम बचन राम पद नेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2414.verse_hindi: विवेक होने पर मोह रूपी भ्रम भाग जाता है, तब (अज्ञान का नाश होने पर) श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों में प्रेम होता है। हे सखा! मन, वचन और कर्म से श्री रामजी के चरणों में प्रेम होना, यही सर्वश्रेष्ठ परमार्थ (पुरुषार्थ) है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2414.english_translation: When clear seeing arises, confusion and delusion fall away. Then love for Raghunath's feet awakens. Friend, the highest purpose is this: loving Ram's feet with mind, speech, and action.
ramacharitamanas::2414.translation_literal: होइ (happens) / बिबेकु (clear seeing) / मोह (delusion) / भ्रम (confusion) / भागा (runs away) / तब (then) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / चरन (feet) / अनुरागा (love) / सखा (friend) / परम (highest) / परमारथु (supreme purpose) / एहू (this) / मन (mind) / क्रम (action) / बचन (speech) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / नेहू (love)
ramacharitamanas::2414.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2414.essence: Clear seeing ends confusion, and devotion becomes your highest purpose.
ramacharitamanas::2414.simple_meaning: When confusion clears, love for Ram naturally rises. Loving Ram with mind, speech, and action is the highest human purpose.
ramacharitamanas::2414.simple_insight: Real clarity does not make you colder; it makes your love steadier and more complete.
ramacharitamanas::2414.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the teaching turns from grief and illusion toward vision. Tulsidas says that once confusion falls away, devotion to Ram's feet awakens, and that devotion through thought, words, and action is the highest aim.
ramacharitamanas::2414.modern_relevance: After a long night of overthinking, you finally see the situation clearly and feel your heart soften toward what matters most. Clarity does not distance you from love; it deepens it.
ramacharitamanas::2414.insight: It shifts the mind from vague emotion to whole-life devotion: thought, speech, and action aligned toward Ram.

ramacharitamanas::2415.verse_sanskrit: राम ब्रह्म परमारथ रूपा। अबिगत अलख अनादि अनूपा॥ सकल बिकार रहित गतभेदा। कहि नित नेति निरूपहिं बेदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2415.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी परमार्थस्वरूप (परमवस्तु) परब्रह्म हैं। वे अविगत (जानने में न आने वाले) अलख (स्थूल दृष्टि से देखने में न आने वाले), अनादि (आदिरहित), अनुपम (उपमारहित) सब विकारों से रहति और भेद शून्य हैं, वेद जिनका नित्य 'नेति-नेति' कहकर निरूपण करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2415.english_translation: Ram is Brahman, the supreme reality, beyond change, unseen, without beginning, incomparable. Free of all alteration and beyond division, the Vedas describe him only by saying, 'not this, not this.'
ramacharitamanas::2415.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / परमारथ रूपा (in the form of the supreme reality) / अबिगत (unmanifest, beyond change) / अलख (unseen) / अनादि (without beginning) / अनूपा (incomparable)॥ सकल (all) / बिकार (modifications) / रहित (free from) / गतभेदा (beyond division) / कहि (saying) / नित (always) / नेति नेति (not this, not this) / निरूपहिं (describe) / बेदा (the Vedas)
ramacharitamanas::2415.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2415.essence: Ram cannot be captured by form, change, or language.
ramacharitamanas::2415.simple_meaning: Ram is the supreme reality: changeless, beginningless, unseen, and beyond all divisions. The Vedas can only point to him by negating every limited description.
ramacharitamanas::2415.simple_insight: Some truths are too vast to capture directly; you approach them by letting go of every smaller label.
ramacharitamanas::2415.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the teaching rises from ethical devotion into pure metaphysics. Tulsidas now names Ram not just as the beloved lord of exile and grief, but as the supreme reality itself: changeless, beyond form, beyond duality, and beyond ordinary speech.
ramacharitamanas::2415.modern_relevance: You keep trying to define yourself by job title, mood, or role, and it never fully fits. Some part of you knows you are larger than every label you wear.
ramacharitamanas::2415.insight: It shifts the mind from grasping at descriptions to resting in what cannot be boxed in.

ramacharitamanas::2416.verse_sanskrit: भगत भूमि भूसुर सुरभि सुर हित लागि कृपाल। करत चरित धरि मनुज तनु सुनत मिटहिं जग जाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::2416.verse_hindi: वही कृपालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी भक्त, भूमि, ब्राह्मण, गो और देवताओं के हित के लिए मनुष्य शरीर धारण करके लीलाएँ करते हैं, जिनके सुनने से जगत के जंजाल मिट जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2416.english_translation: That compassionate Ram takes a human body and performs his divine play for the good of devotees, the earth, the wise, cows, and the radiant beings; hearing of it loosens the knots of the world.
ramacharitamanas::2416.translation_literal: भगत (devotees) / भूमि (earth) / भूसुर (wise ones) / सुरभि (cow) / सुर (radiant beings) / हित (for the good) / लागि (for) / कृपाल (compassionate one) / करत (doing) / चरित (deeds, play) / धरि (taking) / मनुज तनु (human body) / सुनत (hearing) / मिटहिं (are removed) / जग जाल (worldly knots)
ramacharitamanas::2416.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2416.essence: Ram enters human life to untie the knots that burden you.
ramacharitamanas::2416.simple_meaning: Ram takes a human form and acts for the good of devotees and all who depend on him. Simply hearing about his life helps free the mind from worldly entanglement.
ramacharitamanas::2416.simple_insight: You are not meant to carry every knot alone; remembering the divine can soften what feels stuck.
ramacharitamanas::2416.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram as the compassionate one who enters human life for the welfare of devotees, the earth, the wise, cows, and the radiant beings. In this Ayodhyakand passage, that truth prepares the listener to let go of confusion and turn toward Ram’s feet.
ramacharitamanas::2416.modern_relevance: You are exhausted after weeks of carrying family drama, deadlines, and guilt. Then one story, one prayer, one reminder of grace makes your chest unclench. That is the kind of relief this verse promises.
ramacharitamanas::2416.insight: It shifts attention from tangled self-management to receptive remembrance of Ram’s saving presence.

ramacharitamanas::2417.verse_sanskrit: सखा समुझि अस परिहरि मोहू। सिय रघुबीर चरन रत होहू॥ कहत राम गुन भा भिनुसारा। जागे जग मंगल सुखदारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2417.verse_hindi: हे सखा! ऐसा समझ, मोह को त्यागकर श्री सीतारामजी के चरणों में प्रेम करो। इस प्रकार श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुण कहते-कहते सबेरा हो गया! तब जगत का मंगल करने वाले और उसे सुख देने वाले श्री रामजी जागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2417.english_translation: Friend, understand this and leave delusion behind. Be devoted to the feet of Sita and Raghubir. While speaking of Ram's qualities, dawn arrived; then Ram, who brings auspiciousness and joy to the world, awoke.
ramacharitamanas::2417.translation_literal: सखा (friend) / समुझि (understand) / अस (this) / परिहरि (leaving aside) / मोहू (delusion) / सिय (Sita) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / चरन (feet) / रत (attached/devoted) / होहू (be) ॥ कहत (speaking) / राम (Ram) / गुन (qualities) / भा (became) / भिनुसारा (dawn) / जागे (awoke) / जग (world) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / सुखदारा (giver of joy) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2417.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2417.essence: Devotion can carry the night until dawn arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2417.simple_meaning: Let go of delusion and stay devoted to Ram and Sita. The praise of Ram continued until dawn, and then Ram awoke.
ramacharitamanas::2417.simple_insight: Even praise can become a form of devotion that carries you through the night.
ramacharitamanas::2417.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the grief and devotion around Ram's exile are still unfolding. The speaker urges a companion to drop delusion and hold to Sita and Ram's feet, then shows how their praise carried them into dawn, when Ram finally awoke.
ramacharitamanas::2417.modern_relevance: You sit beside a friend through a long, sleepless night, talking only about what keeps you steady. By sunrise, the conversation itself has become a kind of prayer.
ramacharitamanas::2417.insight: It shifts attention from restless thinking to steady remembrance and devotion.

ramacharitamanas::2418.verse_sanskrit: सकल सौच करि राम नहावा। सुचि सुजान बट छीर मगावा॥ अनुज सहित सिर जटा बनाए। देखि सुमंत्र नयन जल छाए॥
ramacharitamanas::2418.verse_hindi: शौच के सब कार्य करके (नित्य) पवित्र और सुजान श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने स्नान किया। फिर बड़ का दूध मँगाया और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित उस दूध से सिर पर जटाएँ बनाईं। यह देखकर सुमंत्रजी के नेत्रों में जल छा गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2418.english_translation: After completing all cleansing rites, Rama bathed. The wise one then had bark-cloth and milk brought, and with Lakshmana he made matted hair on his head. Seeing this, Sumantra's eyes filled with tears.
ramacharitamanas::2418.translation_literal: सकल (all) / सौच (purification) / करि (doing) / राम (Rama) / नहावा (bathed) / सुचि (pure) / सुजान (wise) / बट (banyan/bark) / छीर (milk) / मगावा (had brought) / अनुज (younger brother) / सहित (together with) / सिर (head) / जटा (matted hair) / बनाए (made) / देखि (seeing) / सुमंत्र (Sumantra) / नयन (eyes) / जल (water/tears) / छाए (filled)
ramacharitamanas::2418.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2418.essence: Duty can be carried with complete calm, even when the heart is breaking.
ramacharitamanas::2418.simple_meaning: Rama prepares for exile with complete calm: he bathes, puts on matted hair, and makes Lakshmana do the same. Sumantra is moved to tears by the sight.
ramacharitamanas::2418.simple_insight: Even sorrow can be met with dignity when you accept what must be done.
ramacharitamanas::2418.detailed_meaning: Rama is leaving Ayodhya for exile, and the household is already breaking apart. Before stepping out, he performs the required cleansing, dresses for forest life, and prepares Lakshmana too. Sumantra watches this quiet resolve and cannot hold back tears.
ramacharitamanas::2418.modern_relevance: You pack your bag for a move you never wanted, then still make the bed and lock the door properly. Some departures ask for dignity, not drama.
ramacharitamanas::2418.insight: It turns a painful departure into an act of composed obedience to dharma.

ramacharitamanas::2419.verse_sanskrit: हृदयँ दाहु अति बदन मलीना। कह कर जोर बचन अति दीना॥ नाथ कहेउ अस कोसलनाथा। लै रथु जाहु राम कें साथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2419.verse_hindi: उनका हृदय अत्यंत जलने लगा, मुँह मलिन (उदास) हो गया। वे हाथ जोड़कर अत्यंत दीन वचन बोले- हे नाथ! मुझे कौसलनाथ दशरथजी ने ऐसी आज्ञा दी थी कि तुम रथ लेकर श्री रामजी के साथ जाओ, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2419.english_translation: His heart burned with grief and his face grew pale. With folded hands he spoke in utter humility: "My lord, King of Kosala gave me this command: take the chariot and go with Ram."
ramacharitamanas::2419.translation_literal: हृदयँ (in the heart) / दाहु (burning pain) / अति (very) / बदन (face) / मलीना (darkened, pale) / कह (saying) / कर (hands) / जोर (joined) / बचन (words) / अति (very) / दीना (humble, pitiable) / नाथ (lord) / कहेउ (I said) / अस (thus) / कोसलनाथा (King of Kosala) / लै (taking) / रथु (chariot) / जाहु (go) / राम (Ram) / कें (with) / साथा (together)
ramacharitamanas::2419.speaker: Sumantra
ramacharitamanas::2419.essence: Grief and obedience can live in the same breath.
ramacharitamanas::2419.simple_meaning: Sumantra is overwhelmed with grief as he repeats Dasharath’s order to take the chariot and go with Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2419.simple_insight: Some duties hurt because they carry love, not just instruction.
ramacharitamanas::2419.detailed_meaning: At dawn in Ayodhya, Sumantra stands before Ram, Lakshman, and Sita after the king’s command. He is torn apart inside, yet he must speak the words that send them toward exile. This verse shows his pain, not a new teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2419.modern_relevance: You have to deliver news that will hurt someone you care about. Your face gives you away before your words are finished.
ramacharitamanas::2419.insight: It shows how duty can be carried with humility even when the heart is breaking.

ramacharitamanas::2420.verse_sanskrit: बनु देखाइ सुरसरि अन्हवाई। आनेहु फेरि बेगि दोउ भाई॥ लखनु रामु सिय आनेहु फेरी। संसय सकल सँकोच निबेरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2420.verse_hindi: वन दिखाकर, गंगा स्नान कराकर दोनों भाइयों को तुरंत लौटा लाना। सब संशय और संकोच को दूर करके लक्ष्मण, राम, सीता को फिरा लाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2420.english_translation: Show them the forest, bathe them in the Ganga, and quickly bring both brothers back. Remove every doubt and hesitation, and bring Lakshman, Ram, and Sita back again.
ramacharitamanas::2420.translation_literal: बनु (forest) / देखाइ (showing) / सुरसरि (the celestial river, Ganga) / अन्हवाई (having bathed) / आनेहु (bring) / फेरि (again) / बेगि (quickly) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) ॥ / लखनु (Lakshman) / रामु (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / आनेहु (bring) / फेरी (back again) / संसय (doubt) / सकल (all) / सँकोच (hesitation) / निबेरी (removing)
ramacharitamanas::2420.speaker: Sumantra
ramacharitamanas::2420.essence: Hesitation cannot stop what duty has already set in motion.
ramacharitamanas::2420.simple_meaning: Sumantra asks that the brothers be shown the forest, bathed in the Ganga, and brought back quickly, with all hesitation removed.
ramacharitamanas::2420.simple_insight: A loyal heart keeps moving until the last doubt is cleared.
ramacharitamanas::2420.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Sumantra is torn between duty to the king and love for Ram. He urges that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita be taken to the forest and returned quickly, trying to smooth away every doubt before the exile begins.
ramacharitamanas::2420.modern_relevance: You know that moment when you’re trying to delay bad news, hoping one more explanation will soften the blow? This verse carries that helpless urgency.
