ramacharitamanas::2420.insight: It shows a mind trying to manage grief by removing uncertainty before the painful step happens.

ramacharitamanas::2421.verse_sanskrit: नृप अस कहेउ गोसाइँ जस कहइ करौं बलि सोइ। करि बिनती पायन्ह परेउ दीन्ह बाल जिमि रोइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2421.verse_hindi: महाराज ने ऐसा कहा था, अब प्रभु जैसा कहें, मैं वही करूँ, मैं आपकी बलिहारी हूँ। इस प्रकार से विनती करके वे श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में गिर पड़े और बालक की तरह रो दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2421.english_translation: The king had said this: now, Lord, whatever you say, I will do. I am yours. After making this plea, he fell at Ram's feet and wept like a child.
ramacharitamanas::2421.translation_literal: नृप (the king) / अस (thus) / कहेउ (said) / गोसाइँ (Lord) / जस (as) / कहइ (says) / करौं (I will do) / बलि (offering) / सोइ (that only) / करि (having done) / बिनती (request) / पायन्ह (at the feet) / परेउ (fell) / दीन्ह (gave) / बाल (child) / जिमि (like) / रोइ (weeping)
ramacharitamanas::2421.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2421.essence: Real surrender stops arguing and places everything at Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::2421.simple_meaning: The minister surrenders his own will and asks Ram to decide everything. His grief is so deep that he falls at Ram's feet and cries like a child.
ramacharitamanas::2421.simple_insight: There is relief in letting a wiser hand carry what you cannot.
ramacharitamanas::2421.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, a royal minister stands before Ram after the exile order has shattered Ayodhya. He no longer argues or resists. He places the whole burden before Ram, then breaks down in helpless grief.
ramacharitamanas::2421.modern_relevance: You finally admit you cannot fix the family crisis alone. After days of trying, you ask the one steady person left to decide what comes next.
ramacharitamanas::2421.insight: It shifts the mind from control to humble dependence on what is right.

ramacharitamanas::2422.verse_sanskrit: तात कृपा करि कीजिअ सोई। जातें अवध अनाथ न होई॥ मंत्रिहि राम उठाइ प्रबोधा। तात धरम मतु तुम्ह सबु सोधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2422.verse_hindi: (और कहा -) हे तात ! कृपा करके वही कीजिए जिससे अयोध्या अनाथ न हो श्री रामजी ने मंत्री को उठाकर धैर्य बँधाते हुए समझाया कि हे तात ! आपने तो धर्म के सभी सिद्धांतों को छान डाला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2422.english_translation: “Dear father, please do only what keeps Ayodhya from becoming orphaned.” Ram lifted the minister up and reassured him, saying, “Father, you have examined the whole matter of dharma.”
ramacharitamanas::2422.translation_literal: तात (father) / कृपा करि (showing kindness) / कीजिअ (please do) / सोई (that only) / जातें (by which) / अवध (Ayodhya) / अनाथ (orphaned) / न होई (does not become) / मंत्रिहि (the minister) / राम (Ram) / उठाइ (lifting up) / प्रबोधा (comforted / reassured) / तात (father) / धरम (dharma) / मतु (principles / opinion) / तुम्ह (you) / सबु (all) / सोधा (examined thoroughly)
ramacharitamanas::2422.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2422.essence: Duty means choosing what prevents others from being left helpless.
ramacharitamanas::2422.simple_meaning: Ram asks that the decision made should keep Ayodhya from feeling leaderless. He then comforts the minister, saying the minister has already understood dharma well.
ramacharitamanas::2422.simple_insight: Real duty is measured by what protects others from collapse.
ramacharitamanas::2422.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the minister stands shaken while Ram prepares for exile. Ram does not argue for himself; he asks for the choice that will keep the kingdom from becoming helpless, then lifts the minister up and steadies him.
ramacharitamanas::2422.modern_relevance: You are about to leave a team, and everyone is silently wondering who will hold things together. The most mature move is not defending yourself — it is protecting the people who remain.
ramacharitamanas::2422.insight: It shifts attention from personal loss to the responsibility of preserving order for others.

ramacharitamanas::2423.verse_sanskrit: सिबि दधीच हरिचंद नरेसा। सहे धरम हित कोटि कलेसा॥ रंतिदेव बलि भूप सुजाना। धरमु धरेउ सहि संकट नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2423.verse_hindi: शिबि, दधीचि और राजा हरिश्चन्द्र ने धर्म के लिए करोड़ों (अनेकों) कष्ट सहे थे। बुद्धिमान राजा रन्तिदेव और बलि बहुत से संकट सहकर भी धर्म को पकड़े रहे (उन्होंने धर्म का परित्याग नहीं किया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2423.english_translation: Shibi, Dadhichi, and King Harishchandra endured countless hardships for dharma. Wise King Rantideva and Bali held to dharma through many dangers and did not abandon it.
ramacharitamanas::2423.translation_literal: सिबि (Shibi) / दधीच (Dadhichi) / हरिचंद (Harishchandra) / नरेसा (kings) / सहे (endured) / धरम हित (for dharma's sake) / कोटि (crores, countless) / कलेसा (hardships) / रंतिदेव (Rantideva) / बलि (Bali) / भूप (king) / सुजाना (wise) / धरमु (dharma) / धरेउ (held) / सहि (bearing) / संकट (dangers) / नाना (many)
ramacharitamanas::2423.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2423.essence: Dharma is proven when hardship arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2423.simple_meaning: Great kings and sages endured huge suffering to stay loyal to dharma. The point is not comfort, but steadfastness.
ramacharitamanas::2423.simple_insight: You can stay true even when it costs you dearly.
ramacharitamanas::2423.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is trying to steady the broken kingdom after his exile. Tulsidas reminds the listener that noble figures like Shibi, Dadhichi, Harishchandra, Rantideva, and Bali accepted suffering rather than abandon dharma.
ramacharitamanas::2423.modern_relevance: You keep a promise that ruins your weekend, your budget, and your mood. No one applauds, but you still do it because backing out would cost more than effort.
ramacharitamanas::2423.insight: It shifts the mind from comfort-seeking to principled endurance.

ramacharitamanas::2424.verse_sanskrit: धरमु न दूसर सत्य समाना। आगम निगम पुरान बखाना॥ मैं सोइ धरमु सुलभ करि पावा। तजें तिहूँ पुर अपजसु छावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2424.verse_hindi: वेद, शास्त्र और पुराणों में कहा गया है कि सत्य के समान दूसरा धर्म नहीं है। मैंने उस धर्म को सहज ही पा लिया है। इस (सत्य रूपी धर्म) का त्याग करने से तीनों लोकों में अपयश छा जाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2424.english_translation: The scriptures say there is no dharma higher than truth. I have attained that dharma easily, and abandoning it would spread disgrace through all three worlds.
ramacharitamanas::2424.translation_literal: धरमु (dharma) / न (not) / दूसर (other) / सत्य (truth) / समाना (equal to) / आगम (scripture) / निगम (Veda) / पुरान (Puranas) / बखाना (declare)॥ / मैं (I) / सोइ (that) / धरमु (dharma) / सुलभ (easy) / करि (having made) / पावा (have attained)॥ / तजें (by abandoning) / तिहूँ (three) / पुर (worlds) / अपजसु (disgrace) / छावा (will spread)॥
ramacharitamanas::2424.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2424.essence: Truth is the one duty you cannot abandon without losing honour.
ramacharitamanas::2424.simple_meaning: Truth is the highest form of right action. Ram says he has already held to it, and giving it up would bring shame everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::2424.simple_insight: Integrity feels costly, but it keeps your name clean inside and out.
ramacharitamanas::2424.detailed_meaning: Ram is speaking in Ayodhyakand while trying to keep Ayodhya from becoming orphaned by bad judgment. He points to the old standard of kings and sages: truth is the highest dharma. To abandon it now would dishonour him before everyone.
ramacharitamanas::2424.modern_relevance: You’re asked to cover up a mistake in a meeting because it would look better for everyone. The easier option protects your image, but the lie would follow you long after the room empties.
ramacharitamanas::2424.insight: It shifts you from protecting appearances to protecting integrity, even when honesty is uncomfortable.

ramacharitamanas::2425.verse_sanskrit: संभावित कहुँ अपजस लाहू। मरन कोटि सम दारुन दाहू॥ तुम्ह सन तात बहुत का कहउँ। दिएँ उतरु फिरि पातकु लहऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2425.verse_hindi: प्रतिष्ठित पुरुष के लिए अपयश की प्राप्ति करोड़ों मृत्यु के समान भीषण संताप देने वाली है। हे तात! मैं आप से अधिक क्या कहूँ! लौटकर उत्तर देने में भी पाप का भागी होता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2425.english_translation: For an honorable person, disgrace is as dreadful as millions of deaths. Father, what more can I say to you? Even answering you again would make me share in wrongdoing.
ramacharitamanas::2425.translation_literal: संभावित (for an honorable person) / कहुँ (for me) / अपजस (disgrace) / लाहू (I may get) / मरन (death) / कोटि सम (equal to millions) / दारुन (terrible) / दाहू (burning pain)॥ / तुम्ह सन (to you) / तात (father/dear one) / बहुत (much) / का (what) / कहउँ (I say)॥ / दिएँ (by giving) / उतरु (answer) / फिरि (again) / पातकु (wrongdoing) / लहऊँ (I incur)॥
ramacharitamanas::2425.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2425.essence: Honor can be wounded so deeply that even replying becomes costly.
ramacharitamanas::2425.simple_meaning: A respected person feels disgrace as a terrible suffering, even worse than death. Bharat says he cannot add more and that even replying again would be wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2425.simple_insight: Some losses wound dignity so deeply that silence feels wiser than defending yourself.
ramacharitamanas::2425.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is speaking to the people around him after Ram has been sent away. The family’s honor has been shattered, and Bharat feels the weight of that public shame. He says even answering further would deepen the wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2425.modern_relevance: You read a message that twists your words in public, and your first urge is to defend yourself. Bharat’s response is the harder one: know when more explanation only deepens the wound.
ramacharitamanas::2425.insight: It teaches restraint in conflict: not every accusation deserves another round of speech.

ramacharitamanas::2426.verse_sanskrit: पितु पद गहि कहि कोटि नति बिनय करब कर जोरि। चिंता कवनिहु बात कै तात करिअ जनि मोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2426.verse_hindi: आप जाकर पिताजी के चरण पकड़कर करोड़ों नमस्कार के साथ ही हाथ जोड़कर बिनती करिएगा कि हे तात! आप मेरी किसी बात की चिन्ता न करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2426.english_translation: Go and hold my father's feet, offer countless bows, and pray with folded hands: “Father, do not worry about me.”
ramacharitamanas::2426.translation_literal: पितु (father) / पद (feet) / गहि (holding) / कहि (saying) / कोटि (crores, countless) / नति (bows) / बिनय (request, plea) / करब (to do) / कर जोरि (with joined hands) / चिंता (worry) / कवनिहु (any) / बात (matter) / कै (of) / तात (fatherly address) / करिअ (do) / जनि (do not) / मोरि (my)
ramacharitamanas::2426.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2426.essence: Humility can carry love farther than argument.
ramacharitamanas::2426.simple_meaning: Bharat asks that his father be reassured through humble respect: bow deeply, plead with folded hands, and tell him not to worry about Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::2426.simple_insight: Real love can sound like humility: you ease another person's pain by putting your pride aside.
ramacharitamanas::2426.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat is trying to soften the blow of Ram's exile and Dasharath's sorrow. He instructs the messenger to bow before the father and speak gently, because the moment calls for reverence, not argument.
ramacharitamanas::2426.modern_relevance: You know a family conversation is breaking when every sentence could wound. In that moment, you lower your voice, bow your pride, and speak only to ease the other person's heart.
ramacharitamanas::2426.insight: It teaches you to use humility as a way to reduce another person's suffering.

ramacharitamanas::2427.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह पुनि पितु सम अति हित मोरें। बिनती करउँ तात कर जोरें॥ सब बिधि सोइ करतब्य तुम्हारें। दुख न पाव पितु सोच हमारें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2427.verse_hindi: आप भी पिता के समान ही मेरे बड़े हितैषी हैं। हे तात! मैं हाथ जोड़कर आप से विनती करता हूँ कि आपका भी सब प्रकार से वही कर्तव्य है, जिसमें पिताजी हम लोगों के सोच में दुःख न पावें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2427.english_translation: You are also as dear to me as a father. I beg you with folded hands: your duty, in every way, is to keep Father from suffering grief over us.
ramacharitamanas::2427.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / पुनि (also) / पितु (father) / सम (like) / अति (very) / हित (beneficial, dear) / मोरें (to me) / बिनती (request, plea) / करउँ (I make) / तात (dear one) / कर जोरें (with joined hands)॥ / सब बिधि (in every way) / सोइ (that same) / करतब्य (duty) / तुम्हारें (for you) / दुख (grief, suffering) / न (not) / पाव (may get) / पितु (father) / सोच (worry, grief) / हमारें (because of us) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2427.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2427.essence: Duty becomes love when it shields others from grief.
ramacharitamanas::2427.simple_meaning: Bharat speaks with deep respect and asks the other person to act in a way that keeps his father from suffering over their situation.
ramacharitamanas::2427.simple_insight: Real care means protecting people from avoidable pain, not just speaking politely.
ramacharitamanas::2427.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is trying to hold a broken family together after Ram’s exile. Speaking with folded hands, he treats the other man like a father and asks him to do whatever is needed so Dasharath will not be wounded by worry.
ramacharitamanas::2427.modern_relevance: You call your older sibling late at night because your parents are already overwhelmed. You are not asking for perfection — only for one choice that spares them another round of pain.
ramacharitamanas::2427.insight: It shifts duty from self-protection to protecting the emotional well-being of those who depend on you.

ramacharitamanas::2428.verse_sanskrit: सुनि रघुनाथ सचिव संबादू। भयउ सपरिजन बिकल निषादू॥ पुनि कछु लखन कही कटु बानी। प्रभु बरजे बड़ अनुचित जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2428.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी और सुमंत्र का यह संवाद सुनकर निषादराज कुटुम्बियों सहित व्याकुल हो गया। फिर लक्ष्मणजी ने कुछ कड़वी बात कही। प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने उसे बहुत ही अनुचित जानकर उनको मना किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2428.english_translation: Hearing the exchange between Raghunath and Sumantra, Nishadraj grew agitated with his family. Then Lakshman spoke some sharp words, and the Lord stopped him, seeing them as very improper.
ramacharitamanas::2428.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / सचिव (minister) / संबादू (conversation) / भयउ (became) / सपरिजन (with family) / बिकल (agitated) / निषादू (Nishadraj)॥ / पुनि (then) / कछु (some) / लखन (Lakshman) / कही (spoke) / कटु (sharp) / बानी (words) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बरजे (restrained) / बड़ (very) / अनुचित (improper) / जानी (knowing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2428.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2428.essence: Care without restraint can still wound; Ram corrects that instantly.
ramacharitamanas::2428.simple_meaning: Nishadraj is shaken by the conversation, and Lakshman says something harsh. Ram immediately stops him because the words are out of place.
ramacharitamanas::2428.simple_insight: Even in tension, restraint matters more than winning the moment.
ramacharitamanas::2428.detailed_meaning: As Ram prepares to leave, Sumantra’s exchange has already stirred Nishadraj and his household. Lakshman, protective and angry, speaks sharply. Ram intervenes at once, showing that even grief and loyalty must stay within maryada.
ramacharitamanas::2428.modern_relevance: In a tense family argument, someone says the cutting thing everyone was thinking. The room goes cold. Then the person who cares most steps in and stops the damage before it spreads.
ramacharitamanas::2428.insight: It teaches you to interrupt harsh speech before it hardens into harm.

ramacharitamanas::2429.verse_sanskrit: सकुचि राम निज सपथ देवाई। लखन सँदेसु कहिअ जनि जाई॥ कह सुमंत्रु पुनि भूप सँदेसू। सहि न सकिहि सिय बिपिन कलेसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2429.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सकुचाकर, अपनी सौगंध दिलाकर सुमंत्रजी से कहा कि आप जाकर लक्ष्मण का यह संदेश न कहिएगा। सुमंत्र ने फिर राजा का संदेश कहा कि सीता वन के क्लेश न सह सकेंगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2429.english_translation: Ram, feeling shy, made Sumantra swear and said, "Do not go and tell Lakshman this message." Then Sumantra repeated the king's message: "Sita cannot bear the hardships of the forest."
ramacharitamanas::2429.translation_literal: सकुचि (feeling shy) / राम (Ram) / निज (his own) / सपथ (oath) / देवाई (made [him] swear) / लखन (Lakshman) / सँदेसु (message) / कहिअ (should be said) / जनि (do not) / जाई (go) / कह (said) / सुमंत्रु (Sumantra) / पुनि (again) / भूप (king) / सँदेसू (message) / सहि (bear) / न (not) / सकिहि (will be able to) / सिय (Sita) / बिपिन (forest) / कलेसू (hardships)
ramacharitamanas::2429.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2429.essence: Mercy sometimes means holding back a message.
ramacharitamanas::2429.simple_meaning: Ram quietly stops Sumantra from repeating a message to Lakshman. The message is that Sita would not be able to bear forest life.
ramacharitamanas::2429.simple_insight: Some truths are too painful to pass along carelessly.
ramacharitamanas::2429.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sumantra is caught between royal orders and the ache of exile. Ram, already burdened by separation, hesitates and blocks the message from reaching Lakshman. The verse sits inside a larger, sorrowful exchange about Sita, forest life, and unbearable loss.
ramacharitamanas::2429.modern_relevance: You draft a message, read it twice, and realize it would only wound someone already struggling. Not every truth needs to be delivered in full force.
ramacharitamanas::2429.insight: It teaches restraint in speech when words would deepen another person's pain.

ramacharitamanas::2430.verse_sanskrit: जेहि बिधि अवध आव फिरि सीया। होइ रघुबरहि तुम्हहि करनीया॥ नतरु निपट अवलंब बिहीना। मैं न जिअब जिमि जल बिनु मीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2430.verse_hindi: अतएव जिस तरह सीता अयोध्या को लौट आवें, तुमको और श्री रामचन्द्र को वही उपाय करना चाहिए। नहीं तो मैं बिल्कुल ही बिना सहारे का होकर वैसे ही नहीं जीऊँगा जैसे बिना जल के मछली नहीं जीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2430.english_translation: So arrange it that Sita returns to Ayodhya. You and Ram must find a way to do this. Otherwise, I will be utterly without support and will not live, just as a fish cannot live without water.
ramacharitamanas::2430.translation_literal: जेहि बिधि (in whatever way) / अवध (Ayodhya) / आव (returns) / फिरि (again) / सीया (Sita) / होइ (may be) / रघुबरहि (for Ram) / तुम्हहि (for you) / करनीया (to be done) / नतरु (otherwise) / निपट (completely) / अवलंब (support) / बिहीना (without) / मैं (I) / न (not) / जिअब (will live) / जिमि (as) / जल (water) / बिनु (without) / मीना (fish)
ramacharitamanas::2430.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2430.essence: Separation from Ram and Sita feels like losing the ground beneath you.
ramacharitamanas::2430.simple_meaning: Bharat says Sita must be brought back to Ayodhya somehow, or he cannot go on living without her and Ram's support.
ramacharitamanas::2430.simple_insight: Love can make separation feel physically unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2430.detailed_meaning: Bharat is grieving in Ayodhya after Ram's exile. Speaking with deep anguish, he says only one thing can restore his life: Sita must return home. Without that support, he feels he cannot survive.
ramacharitamanas::2430.modern_relevance: You wait in an empty house after someone leaves, and every room feels wrong. Bharat names that ache: when the heart loses its center, even breathing feels borrowed.
ramacharitamanas::2430.insight: It reveals how devotion can turn absence into a felt loss of support, not just sadness.

ramacharitamanas::2431.verse_sanskrit: मइकें ससुरें सकल सुख जबहिं जहाँ मनु मान। तहँ तब रहिहि सुखेन सिय जब लगि बिपति बिहान ॥
ramacharitamanas::2431.verse_hindi: सीता के मायके (पिता के घर) और ससुराल में सब सुख हैं। जब तक यह विपत्ति दूर नहीं होती, तब तक वे जब जहाँ जी चाहें, वहीं सुख से रहेंगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2431.english_translation: Sita has happiness in both her parents' home and her in-laws' home. Until this trouble passes, let her stay happily wherever she wishes.
ramacharitamanas::2431.translation_literal: मइकें (in mother's home) / ससुरें (in father-in-law's home) / सकल सुख (all happiness) / जबहिं (when) / जहाँ (where) / मनु (the mind) / मान (accepts) / तहँ (there) / तब (then) / रहिहि (will remain) / सुखेन (happily) / सिय (Sita) / जब लगि (until) / बिपति (trouble) / बिहान (passes away)
ramacharitamanas::2431.speaker: Sumantra
ramacharitamanas::2431.essence: Love sometimes means leaving someone where they can feel safe.
ramacharitamanas::2431.simple_meaning: Sita can stay wherever she feels comfortable, because both homes are places of happiness. Until this crisis ends, there is no need to force her elsewhere.
ramacharitamanas::2431.simple_insight: Sometimes care means stopping the push and letting safety decide.
ramacharitamanas::2431.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sumantra relays Ram's tender response to Dasharath's courtly crisis. The focus is not on command or strategy, but on easing Sita's distress: she may remain wherever she finds comfort until the exile's pain settles.
ramacharitamanas::2431.modern_relevance: A family argument has left someone exhausted, and nobody wants to decide anything tonight. The kindest move is not pressure, but giving them room to breathe until the storm passes.
ramacharitamanas::2431.insight: It shifts you from forcing a solution to protecting emotional safety first.

ramacharitamanas::2432.verse_sanskrit: बिनती भूप कीन्ह जेहि भाँती। आरति प्रीति न सो कहि जाती॥ पितु सँदेसु सुनि कृपानिधाना। सियहि दीन्ह सिख कोटि बिधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2432.verse_hindi: राजा ने जिस तरह (जिस दीनता और प्रेम से) विनती की है, वह दीनता और प्रेम कहा नहीं जा सकता। कृपानिधान श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने पिता का संदेश सुनकर सीताजी को करोड़ों (अनेकों) प्रकार से सीख दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2432.english_translation: In whatever way the king pleaded, his humility and love cannot be fully described. After hearing his father's message, the compassionate Ram gave Sita countless kinds of counsel.
ramacharitamanas::2432.translation_literal: बिनती (plea/request) / भूप (king) / कीन्ह (made) / जेहि भाँती (in whatever manner) / आरति (humility/distress) / प्रीति (love) / न (not) / सो (that) / कहि जाती (can be spoken) ॥ पितु (father's) / सँदेसु (message) / सुनि (hearing) / कृपानिधाना (treasure of compassion) / सियहि (to Sita) / दीन्ह (gave) / सिख (counsel/advice) / कोटि बिधाना (in countless ways) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2432.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2432.essence: True care can sound like firm guidance in a painful moment.
ramacharitamanas::2432.simple_meaning: The king's plea was full of humility and love. After hearing his father's message, Ram gave Sita many kinds of advice.
ramacharitamanas::2432.simple_insight: Love sometimes means giving hard counsel, not only comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2432.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath's message reaches Ram and Sita during the pain of exile. The king's pleading is so humble and loving that words cannot capture it. Ram responds by gently instructing Sita in many ways before she speaks back.
ramacharitamanas::2432.modern_relevance: You call someone you love to explain a painful family decision, and every sentence lands with care. Sometimes the most loving response is clear guidance, not easy reassurance.
ramacharitamanas::2432.insight: It shows that duty can include tenderness: even in separation, Ram answers with patient, protective counsel.

ramacharitamanas::2433.verse_sanskrit: सासु ससुर गुर प्रिय परिवारू। फिरहु त सब कर मिटै खभारू॥ सुनि पति बचन कहति बैदेही। सुनहु प्रानपति परम सनेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2433.verse_hindi: (उन्होंने कहा-) जो तुम घर लौट जाओ, तो सास, ससुर, गुरु, प्रियजन एवं कुटुम्बी सबकी चिन्ता मिट जाए। पति के वचन सुनकर जानकीजी कहती हैं- हे प्राणपति! हे परम स्नेही! सुनिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2433.english_translation: If you return home, your mother-in-law, father-in-law, teacher, beloved ones, and family will all be relieved. Hearing her husband's words, Vaidehi says, "Listen, my lord of life, my most beloved one."
ramacharitamanas::2433.translation_literal: सासु (mother-in-law) / ससुर (father-in-law) / गुर (teacher) / प्रिय (beloved) / परिवारू (family) / फिरहु (return) / त (then) / सब (all) / कर (of) / मिटै (will be removed) / खभारू (worry) ॥ / सुनि (hearing) / पति (husband) / बचन (words) / कहति (says) / बैदेही (Vaidehi) / सुनहु (listen) / प्रानपति (lord of life) / परम (supreme) / सनेही (beloved) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2433.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2433.essence: True love thinks of everyone’s burden before its own comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2433.simple_meaning: Sita gently points out that returning home would ease the worries of everyone who loves them. She then turns to Rama with deep tenderness and asks him to listen.
ramacharitamanas::2433.simple_insight: Love here speaks with care, not demand. Even in pain, she thinks of everyone’s burden.
ramacharitamanas::2433.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the exile has fractured the whole family. Sita answers Rama’s situation with grace, reminding him that his return would relieve his parents, teacher, and loved ones. Her words are not refusal but loving counsel shaped by concern for all.
ramacharitamanas::2433.modern_relevance: You are about to make a choice that affects your whole family, and everyone is quietly carrying it. The most loving voice in the room thinks beyond itself.
ramacharitamanas::2433.insight: It shifts the mind from personal desire to the wider circle of care around a decision.

ramacharitamanas::2434.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु करुनामय परम बिबेकी। तनु तजि रहति छाँह किमि छेंकी॥ प्रभा जाइ कहँ भानु बिहाई। कहँ चंद्रिका चंदु तजि जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2434.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! आप करुणामय और परम ज्ञानी हैं। (कृपा करके विचार तो कीजिए) शरीर को छोड़कर छाया अलग कैसे रोकी रह सकती है? सूर्य की प्रभा सूर्य को छोड़कर कहाँ जा सकती है? और चाँदनी चन्द्रमा को त्यागकर कहाँ जा सकती है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2434.english_translation: O Lord, you are full of compassion and supremely discerning. How can a shadow be kept apart after the body is gone? Where can sunlight go after leaving the sun, and where can moonlight go after leaving the moon?
ramacharitamanas::2434.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / करुनामय (full of compassion) / परम (supremely) / बिबेकी (discerning) / तनु (body) / तजि (leaving) / रहति (remains) / छाँह (shadow) / किमि (how) / छेंकी (separated) / प्रभा (light/radiance) / जाइ (goes) / कहँ (where) / भानु (sun) / बिहाई (leaving) / कहँ (where) / चंद्रिका (moonlight) / चंदु (moon) / तजि (leaving) / जाई (goes)
ramacharitamanas::2434.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2434.essence: True belonging cannot be forced apart.
ramacharitamanas::2434.simple_meaning: Sita says she cannot be kept apart from Ram any more than a shadow can be separated from a body, or sunlight from the sun.
ramacharitamanas::2434.simple_insight: Love can feel more real than distance, duty, or fear.
ramacharitamanas::2434.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita answers the pressure to return to Ayodhya. Speaking with reverence, she tells Ram that separation is unnatural for her. Her bond with him is like shadow, sunlight, and moonlight: inseparable from their source.
ramacharitamanas::2434.modern_relevance: You are asked to leave the person who gives your life meaning, and your chest tightens. Some attachments are not stubbornness; they are identity itself.
ramacharitamanas::2434.insight: It shifts the mind from treating devotion as a choice to seeing it as a natural belonging.

ramacharitamanas::2435.verse_sanskrit: पतिहि प्रेममय बिनय सुनाई। कहति सचिव सन गिरा सुहाई॥ तुम्ह पितु ससुर सरिस हितकारी। उतरु देउँ फिरि अनुचित भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2435.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार पति को प्रेममयी विनती सुनाकर सीताजी मंत्री से सुहावनी वाणी कहने लगीं- आप मेरे पिताजी और ससुरजी के समान मेरा हित करने वाले हैं। आपको मैं बदले में उत्तर देती हूँ, यह बहुत ही अनुचित है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2435.english_translation: Having spoken her loving plea to her husband, Sita then addressed the minister in gentle words: "You are like my father and father-in-law, a benefactor to me. It would be very improper for me to answer you in return."
ramacharitamanas::2435.translation_literal: पतिहि (to the husband) / प्रेममय (full of love) / बिनय (humble plea) / सुनाई (having spoken) / कहति (speaking) / सचिव (minister) / सन (to) / गिरा (speech) / सुहाई (gentle, pleasing) / तुम्ह (you) / पितु (father) / ससुर (father-in-law) / सरिस (like) / हितकारी (benefactor) / उतरु (reply) / देउँ (I give) / फिरि (in return) / अनुचित (improper) / भारी (very much)
ramacharitamanas::2435.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2435.essence: Gentle speech preserves dignity under pressure.
ramacharitamanas::2435.simple_meaning: Sita speaks politely to the minister, saying he is like a father and father-in-law to her, so replying sharply would be wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2435.simple_insight: Respect can stay intact even in disagreement.
ramacharitamanas::2435.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita is caught in the pain of exile and duty. After speaking tenderly to her husband, she turns to the minister with calm dignity, honoring him as an elder and benefactor rather than meeting concern with sharpness.
ramacharitamanas::2435.modern_relevance: A family member raises a difficult issue at dinner, and you feel the urge to snap back. Sita shows another way: keep your dignity, answer gently, and do not let hurt become disrespect.
ramacharitamanas::2435.insight: It teaches you to protect relationships with measured speech, even when you disagree.

ramacharitamanas::2436.verse_sanskrit: आरति बस सनमुख भइउँ बिलगु न मानब तात। आरजसुत पद कमल बिनु बादि जहाँ लगि नात ॥
ramacharitamanas::2436.verse_hindi: किन्तु हे तात! मैं आर्त्त होकर ही आपके सम्मुख हुई हूँ, आप बुरा न मानिएगा। आर्यपुत्र (स्वामी) के चरणकमलों के बिना जगत में जहाँ तक नाते हैं, सभी मेरे लिए व्यर्थ हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2436.english_translation: But, O father, I have come before you only in distress. Do not take offense. Without the lotus feet of the noble prince, all ties in this world are empty to me.
ramacharitamanas::2436.translation_literal: आरति (distress) / बस (only) / सनमुख (before) / भइउँ (I have come) / बिलगु (offense) / न मानब (do not take) / तात (father) / आरजसुत (noble prince's son) / पद कमल (lotus feet) / बिनु (without) / बादि (empty) / जहाँ लगि (as far as) / नात (relations)
ramacharitamanas::2436.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2436.essence: Without Ram, every other bond becomes hollow.
ramacharitamanas::2436.simple_meaning: Sita tells the messenger she has come out of distress and asks him not to be offended. Without Ram, every relationship in the world feels meaningless to her.
ramacharitamanas::2436.simple_insight: Love can become so complete that everything else loses its weight.
ramacharitamanas::2436.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Sita speaks to Ravana's messenger with controlled pain. She explains that she has come only because of distress, and that without Ram's presence, every worldly tie has become hollow. Her words turn suffering into surrender.
ramacharitamanas::2436.modern_relevance: You keep answering calls from people who only want a version of you that can function. But the part of you that matters most is still asking for the one bond that makes everything else bearable.
ramacharitamanas::2436.insight: It shifts attachment away from social ties and toward the one relationship that gives all others meaning.

ramacharitamanas::2437.verse_sanskrit: पितु बैभव बिलास मैं डीठा। नृप मनि मुकुट मिलित पद पीठा॥ सुखनिधान अस पितु गृह मोरें। पिय बिहीन मन भाव न भोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2437.verse_hindi: मैंने पिताजी के ऐश्वर्य की छटा देखी है, जिनके चरण रखने की चौकी से सर्वशिरोमणि राजाओं के मुकुट मिलते हैं (अर्थात बड़े-बड़े राजा जिनके चरणों में प्रणाम करते हैं) ऐसे पिता का घर भी, जो सब प्रकार के सुखों का भंडार है, पति के बिना मेरे मन को भूलकर भी नहीं भाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2437.english_translation: I have seen my father's royal splendor; kings bow where his feet rest. Yet even my father's house, a treasury of delight, does not please my mind without my husband.
ramacharitamanas::2437.translation_literal: पितु (father's) / बैभव (splendor) / बिलास (display, grandeur) / मैं (I) / डीठा (have seen) / नृप (kings) / मनि (jewel) / मुकुट (crowns) / मिलित (meeting, touching) / पद (feet) / पीठा (seat, footstool) ॥ सुखनिधान (treasury of happiness) / अस (such) / पितु (father's) / गृह (house) / मोरें (for me, my) / पिय (husband) / बिहीन (without) / मन (mind) / भाव (pleases) / न (not) / भोरें (even in the morning) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2437.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2437.essence: Wealth means little when the heart is separated from its beloved.
ramacharitamanas::2437.simple_meaning: Sita says she has seen her father's great royal life, but even that rich and honored home cannot satisfy her without her husband.
ramacharitamanas::2437.simple_insight: Even the finest comfort feels empty when the heart is cut off from the one it loves.
ramacharitamanas::2437.detailed_meaning: Sita is speaking to the messenger in Ayodhya after Ram has been sent away. She remembers the grandeur of her father's palace and its honor, but says none of it can replace her husband. The verse deepens her refusal to accept comfort without Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2437.modern_relevance: You can sit in a beautiful family home, surrounded by care and status, and still feel a sharp emptiness after separation. Comfort does not always touch the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2437.insight: It shifts value from luxury and rank to the presence of the beloved.

ramacharitamanas::2438.verse_sanskrit: ससुर चक्कवइ कोसल राऊ। भुवन चारिदस प्रगट प्रभाऊ॥ आगें होइ जेहि सुरपति लेई। अरध सिंघासन आसनु देई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2438.verse_hindi: मेरे ससुर कोसलराज चक्रवर्ती सम्राट हैं, जिनका प्रभाव चौदहों लोकों में प्रकट है, इन्द्र भी आगे होकर जिनका स्वागत करता है और अपने आधे सिंहासन पर बैठने के लिए स्थान देता है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2438.english_translation: My father-in-law is the emperor of Kosala, whose glory is manifest across the fourteen worlds. Even Indra comes forward to receive him and offers him a seat on half his throne.
ramacharitamanas::2438.translation_literal: ससुर (father-in-law) / चक्कवइ (emperor) / कोसल राऊ (king of Kosala) / भुवन (worlds) / चारिदस (fourteen) / प्रगट (manifest) / प्रभाऊ (glory, influence) / आगें (forward, in front) / होइ (becomes) / जेहि (whom) / सुरपति (lord of the gods, Indra) / लेई (takes, receives) / अरध (half) / सिंघासन (throne) / आसनु (seat) / देई (gives)
ramacharitamanas::2438.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2438.essence: Even the greatest honor feels hollow without Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2438.simple_meaning: Sita is praising her father-in-law Dasharath as a mighty emperor whose fame reaches all worlds, so great that even Indra honors him.
ramacharitamanas::2438.simple_insight: Status can be real and still feel empty when the heart is not at home.
ramacharitamanas::2438.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita is speaking about the grandeur she has entered by marrying Ram. She describes Dasharath's royal power in cosmic terms, showing how immense Ayodhya appears from outside, just before revealing that such splendor still cannot comfort her without Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2438.modern_relevance: You walk into a house with polished floors, honored relatives, and every sign of success. It should feel like arrival, but without the person you love, it still feels incomplete.
ramacharitamanas::2438.insight: It shifts attention from outward prestige to the deeper condition of the heart.

ramacharitamanas::2439.verse_sanskrit: ससुरु एतादृस अवध निवासू। प्रिय परिवारु मातु सम सासू॥ बिनु रघुपति पद पदुम परागा। मोहि केउ सपनेहुँ सुखद न लागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2439.verse_hindi: ऐसे (ऐश्वर्य और प्रभावशाली) ससुर, (उनकी राजधानी) अयोध्या का निवास, प्रिय कुटुम्बी और माता के समान सासुएँ- ये कोई भी श्री रघुनाथजी के चरण कमलों की रज के बिना मुझे स्वप्न में भी सुखदायक नहीं लगते ॥
ramacharitamanas::2439.english_translation: Such a father-in-law, such a home in Ayodhya, dear relatives, and mothers-like mothers-in-law — none of these feel pleasant to me, even in a dream, without the dust of Raghunath's feet.
ramacharitamanas::2439.translation_literal: ससुरु (father-in-law) / एतादृस (such) / अवध (Ayodhya) / निवासू (residence) / प्रिय (dear) / परिवारु (family) / मातु सम (like mother) / सासू (mother-in-law) / बिनु (without) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / पद (feet) / पदुम (lotus) / परागा (dust) / मोहि (to me) / केउ (anything) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / सुखद (pleasant) / न (not) / लागा (seem)
ramacharitamanas::2439.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2439.essence: Without Ram, even abundance feels like exile.
ramacharitamanas::2439.simple_meaning: Bharat says that even a blessed family and a royal home mean nothing to him without Ram's presence and grace.
ramacharitamanas::2439.simple_insight: Real belonging comes from love and devotion, not from status or comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2439.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat is describing the very things most people would long for: a powerful father-in-law, a beloved family, and a gracious household. But after Ram's exile, all of it feels hollow to him unless it is touched by Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::2439.modern_relevance: You move into the apartment you worked so hard to get, but the room still feels cold because the one person you miss is not there. Bharat knows that ache.
ramacharitamanas::2439.insight: It shifts the mind from measuring comfort by possessions to measuring it by presence and love.

ramacharitamanas::2440.verse_sanskrit: अगम पंथ बनभूमि पहारा। करि केहरि सर सरित अपारा॥ कोल किरात कुरंग बिहंगा। मोहि सब सुखद प्रानपति संगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2440.verse_hindi: दुर्गम रास्ते, जंगली धरती, पहाड़, हाथी, सिंह, अथाह तालाब एवं नदियाँ, कोल, भील, हिरन और पक्षी- प्राणपति (श्री रघुनाथजी) के साथ रहते ये सभी मुझे सुख देने वाले होंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2440.english_translation: The impassable forest path, wild land, mountains, elephants, lions, endless lakes and rivers, the Kol and Kirat people, deer and birds — all of them will be pleasing to me when I am with my lord of life.
ramacharitamanas::2440.translation_literal: अगम (impassable) / पंथ (path) / बनभूमि (forest-land) / पहारा (mountains) / करि (elephants) / केहरि (lions) / सर (lakes) / सरित (rivers) / अपारा (boundless) / कोल (Kol people) / किरात (Kirat people) / कुरंग (deer) / बिहंगा (birds) / मोहि (to me) / सब (all) / सुखद (pleasing) / प्रानपति (lord of life) / संगा (with)
ramacharitamanas::2440.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2440.essence: Ram's presence turns danger into comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2440.simple_meaning: Sita says that even forests, mountains, animals, and rough people will feel pleasant if she is with Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2440.simple_insight: Love changes the whole world around you; even hardship becomes bearable when the right presence is near.
ramacharitamanas::2440.detailed_meaning: Sita is preparing to leave Ayodhya for the forest with Ram. She lists every danger and discomfort ahead — wild terrain, animals, rivers, unfamiliar people — and says none of it matters if she can stay beside him.
ramacharitamanas::2440.modern_relevance: You move to a new city, sleep on a bare mattress, and miss everything familiar. Then the person you trust most walks in, and the place stops feeling hostile.
ramacharitamanas::2440.insight: It shifts attention from external comfort to the presence that makes any setting livable.

ramacharitamanas::2441.verse_sanskrit: सासु ससुर सन मोरि हुँति बिनय करबि परि पायँ। मोर सोचु जनि करिअ कछु मैं बन सुखी सुभायँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2441.verse_hindi: अतः सास और ससुर के पाँव पड़कर, मेरी ओर से विनती कीजिएगा कि वे मेरा कुछ भी सोच न करें, मैं वन में स्वभाव से ही सुखी हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2441.english_translation: So please fall at my mother-in-law's and father-in-law's feet and tell them not to worry about me. I am naturally happy in the forest.
ramacharitamanas::2441.translation_literal: सासु (mother-in-law) / ससुर (father-in-law) / सन (with) / मोरि हुँति (from my side) / बिनय (request) / करबि (you should do) / परि पायँ (falling at the feet) / मोर सोचु (my worry) / जनि (do not) / करिअ (do) / कछु (any) / मैं (I) / बन (forest) / सुखी (happy) / सुभायँ (by nature)
ramacharitamanas::2441.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2441.essence: Exile loses its sting when your heart is already at rest.
ramacharitamanas::2441.simple_meaning: Sita asks someone to reassure her in-laws that they need not worry. She says the forest life is naturally comfortable for her.
ramacharitamanas::2441.simple_insight: Real peace is not dependent on the setting around you.
ramacharitamanas::2441.detailed_meaning: Sita, now living in the forest with Ram and Lakshman, sends a message back to Ayodhya. She asks that her mother-in-law and father-in-law be reassured. Even exile cannot disturb her settled heart.
ramacharitamanas::2441.modern_relevance: You move into a new city with almost nothing familiar, and everyone keeps asking whether you're managing. Quietly, you are. This verse understands the strange calm of being uprooted but not undone.
ramacharitamanas::2441.insight: It shifts the mind from needing comfort in surroundings to carrying comfort within.

ramacharitamanas::2442.verse_sanskrit: प्राननाथ प्रिय देवर साथा। बीर धुरीन धरें धनु भाथा॥ नहिं मग श्रमु भ्रमु दुख मन मोरें। मोहि लगि सोचु करिअ जनि भोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2442.verse_hindi: वीरों में अग्रगण्य तथा धनुष और (बाणों से भरे) तरकश धारण किए मेरे प्राणनाथ और प्यारे देवर साथ हैं। इससे मुझे न रास्ते की थकावट है, न भ्रम है और न मेरे मन में कोई दुःख ही है। आप मेरे लिए भूलकर भी सोच न करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2442.english_translation: My dear lord and younger brother are with me, warriors skilled with bow and quiver in hand. So I feel no weariness, no confusion, and no sorrow on the road. Do not worry about me, not even by morning.
ramacharitamanas::2442.translation_literal: प्राननाथ (lord of life) / प्रिय (dear) / देवर (younger brother) / साथा (with me) / बीर (warriors) / धुरीन (foremost) / धरें (holding) / धनु (bow) / भाथा (quiver) / नहिं (not) / मग (road) / श्रमु (fatigue) / भ्रमु (confusion) / दुख (pain) / मन (mind) / मोरें (in me) / मोहि (for me) / लगि (for) / सोचु (worry) / करिअ (do) / जनि (do not) / भोरें (by morning)
ramacharitamanas::2442.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2442.essence: Presence transforms hardship into something you can carry.
ramacharitamanas::2442.simple_meaning: Sita tells Sumantra not to worry about her because Ram and Lakshman are with her. Their presence removes her fear, fatigue, and sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2442.simple_insight: Real support changes everything — even a hard road feels bearable when you are not alone.
ramacharitamanas::2442.detailed_meaning: On the road into exile, Sita reassures Sumantra. Ram and Lakshman are beside her, armed and steady, so she feels no fear or exhaustion. Her calm turns the painful departure into a lesson in trust and companionship.
ramacharitamanas::2442.modern_relevance: You are leaving a hospital with someone you love, and the drive home feels impossible. Then a trusted friend sits beside you, takes the bag, and the whole night becomes bearable.
ramacharitamanas::2442.insight: It shifts attention from hardship itself to the stabilising power of loyal presence.

ramacharitamanas::2443.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुमंत्रु सिय सीतलि बानी। भयउ बिकल जनु फनि मनि हानी॥ नयन सूझ नहिं सुनइ न काना। कहि न सकइ कछु अति अकुलाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2443.verse_hindi: सुमंत्र सीताजी की शीतल वाणी सुनकर ऐसे व्याकुल हो गए जैसे साँप मणि खो जाने पर। नेत्रों से कुछ सूझता नहीं, कानों से सुनाई नहीं देता। वे बहुत व्याकुल हो गए, कुछ कह नहीं सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::2443.english_translation: Listening to Sita's calm words, Sumantra became distraught, like a serpent deprived of its jewel. He could neither see nor hear properly, and in his overwhelming anguish he could say nothing.
ramacharitamanas::2443.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुमंत्रु (Sumantra) / सिय (Sita's) / सीतलि (cool, calming) / बानी (speech) / भयउ (became) / बिकल (distraught) / जनु (as if) / फनि (serpent) / मनि (jewel) / हानी (loss)॥ / नयन (eyes) / सूझ (see clearly) / नहिं (not) / सुनइ (hear) / न काना (not ears) / कहि (speak) / न सकइ (cannot) / कछु (anything) / अति (very) / अकुलाना (agitated)॥
ramacharitamanas::2443.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2443.essence: Grief can make the mind go dark in a single moment.
ramacharitamanas::2443.simple_meaning: Sumantra is so overwhelmed by Sita's calm words that he loses his composure, his senses fail him, and he cannot speak.
ramacharitamanas::2443.simple_insight: Deep grief can make even a steady person feel momentarily unmoored.
ramacharitamanas::2443.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita is preparing to leave with Ram and Lakshman, and Sumantra is caught in the unbearable weight of the moment. Her calmness only deepens his distress, leaving him stunned, speechless, and unable to think clearly.
ramacharitamanas::2443.modern_relevance: You hear someone stay calm while their life is breaking apart, and your own chest tightens. Sometimes another person's steadiness makes your grief louder.
ramacharitamanas::2443.insight: It shows how emotional shock can shut down perception, speech, and clear thought all at once.

ramacharitamanas::2444.verse_sanskrit: राम प्रबोधु कीन्ह बहु भाँती। तदपि होति नहिं सीतलि छाती॥ जतन अनेक साथ हित कीन्हे। उचित उतर रघुनंदन दीन्हे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2444.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने उनका बहुत प्रकार से समाधान किया। तो भी उनकी छाती ठंडी न हुई। साथ चलने के लिए मंत्री ने अनेकों यत्न किए (युक्तियाँ पेश कीं), पर रघुनंदन श्री रामजी (उन सब युक्तियों का) यथोचित उत्तर देते गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2444.english_translation: Ram tried to comfort him in many ways, but his chest did not grow calm. The minister made many efforts and appeals, and Raghunandan answered each one fittingly.
ramacharitamanas::2444.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / प्रबोधु (comforting counsel) / कीन्ह (did) / बहु भाँती (in many ways) / तदपि (even then) / होति (becomes) / नहिं (not) / सीतलि (cool) / छाती (chest)॥ / जतन (effort) / अनेक (many) / साथ (with) / हित (welfare) / कीन्हे (were done) / उचित (fitting) / उतर (reply) / रघुनंदन (Raghunandan) / दीन्हे (gave) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2444.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2444.essence: Kind words cannot always reach a heart in shock.
ramacharitamanas::2444.simple_meaning: Ram speaks kindly and tries many ways to calm Sumantra, but Sumantra's grief does not ease. Even well-meant efforts cannot always soften a heart in shock.
ramacharitamanas::2444.simple_insight: Sometimes care is real, and still the pain stays for a while.
ramacharitamanas::2444.detailed_meaning: After Ram, Sita, and Lakshman leave for exile, Sumantra is broken by grief. Ram tries to steady him with gentle words, and Sumantra keeps searching for some way to make the exile bearable. This verse shows the limits of comfort in the middle of loss.
ramacharitamanas::2444.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone after bad news and say everything right, but their face stays frozen. Not every wound opens to explanation; some hearts need time before they can receive comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2444.insight: It teaches you to respect the pace of grief instead of forcing immediate relief.

ramacharitamanas::2445.verse_sanskrit: मेटि जाइ नहिं राम रजाई। कठिन करम गति कछु न बसाई॥ राम लखन सिय पद सिरु नाई। फिरेउ बनिक जिमि मूर गवाँई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2445.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी की आज्ञा मेटी नहीं जा सकती। कर्म की गति कठिन है, उस पर कुछ भी वश नहीं चलता। श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीताजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर सुमंत्र इस तरह लौटे जैसे कोई व्यापारी अपना मूलधन (पूँजी) गँवाकर लौटे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2445.english_translation: Ram's command cannot be undone. The movement of karma is hard to resist; nothing can control it. Bowing his head at the feet of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, Sumantra returned like a merchant who has lost his capital.
ramacharitamanas::2445.translation_literal: मेटि जाइ (can be erased) / नहिं (not) / राम (Ram's) / रजाई (command) / कठिन (hard) / करम (karma) / गति (movement) / कछु (anything) / न (not) / बसाई (under control) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / पद (feet) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing) / फिरेउ (returned) / बनिक (merchant) / जिमि (like) / मूर (capital) / गवाँई (lost)
ramacharitamanas::2445.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2445.essence: Some commands and consequences cannot be reversed.
ramacharitamanas::2445.simple_meaning: Ram's command cannot be undone, and karma moves beyond human control. Sumantra bows to Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, then returns in grief like a merchant who has lost everything.
ramacharitamanas::2445.simple_insight: Some losses are so complete that only humility remains.
ramacharitamanas::2445.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has just failed to keep Ram with him and has watched the exile unfold. After trying everything, he bows at Ram, Lakshman, and Sita's feet and turns back shattered, carrying the ache of a duty no effort could change.
ramacharitamanas::2445.modern_relevance: You leave the hospital after hearing there is nothing more to do. You replay every choice, but the outcome has already moved beyond your hands.
ramacharitamanas::2445.insight: It shifts the mind from control to humility when effort has reached its limit.

ramacharitamanas::2446.verse_sanskrit: रथु हाँकेउ हय राम तन हेरि हेरि हिहिनाहिं। देखि निषाद बिषाद बस धुनहिं सीस पछिताहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2446.verse_hindi: सुमंत्र ने रथ को हाँका, घोड़े श्री रामचन्द्रजी की ओर देख-देखकर हिनहिनाते हैं। यह देखकर निषाद लोग विषाद के वश होकर सिर धुन-धुनकर (पीट-पीटकर) पछताते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2446.english_translation: The chariot moved on. The horses kept looking toward Ram and whinnying. Seeing this, the Nishads were overcome with grief, beating their heads in regret.
ramacharitamanas::2446.translation_literal: रथु (the chariot) / हाँकेउ (was driven) / हय (the horses) / राम तन (toward Ram's body/presence) / हेरि हेरि (looking again and again) / हिहिनाहिं (whinny) / देखि (seeing) / निषाद (the Nishads) / बिषाद बस (overcome by grief) / धुनहिं (beat) / सीस (heads) / पछिताहिं (regret)
ramacharitamanas::2446.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2446.essence: Even the horses cannot bear Ram's departure.
ramacharitamanas::2446.simple_meaning: As Ram leaves, even the horses keep turning toward him, and the Nishads grieve deeply at the sight.
ramacharitamanas::2446.simple_insight: When love is real, even the animals feel the loss.
ramacharitamanas::2446.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has driven the chariot away from Ayodhya. The horses keep looking back at Ram and crying out, while the Nishads watch in helpless grief. This is not a teaching verse by itself; it is part of the emotional fallout of Ram's departure.
ramacharitamanas::2446.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love leave, and even the dog keeps running to the door. The room itself seems to know something precious has gone.
ramacharitamanas::2446.insight: It deepens the scene of separation, showing grief spreading through everyone who witnesses it.

ramacharitamanas::2447.verse_sanskrit: जासु बियोग बिकल पसु ऐसें। प्रजा मातु पितु जिइहहिं कैसें॥ बरबस राम सुमंत्रु पठाए। सुरसरि तीर आपु तब आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2447.verse_hindi: जिनके वियोग में पशु इस प्रकार व्याकुल हैं, उनके वियोग में प्रजा, माता और पिता कैसे जीते रहेंगे? श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने जबर्दस्ती सुमंत्र को लौटाया। तब आप गंगाजी के तीर पर आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2447.english_translation: How will the people, mother, and father live without the one whose separation leaves even animals distressed? Ram sent Sumantra back by force, and then came to the bank of the Ganga.
ramacharitamanas::2447.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / बियोग (separation) / बिकल (distressed) / पसु (animals) / ऐसें (like this) / प्रजा (people) / मातु (mother) / पितु (father) / जिइहहिं (will live) / कैसें (how)॥ / बरबस (by force) / राम (Ram) / सुमंत्रु (Sumantra) / पठाए (sent back) / सुरसरि (Ganga) / तीर (bank) / आपु (himself) / तब (then) / आए (came) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2447.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2447.essence: Ram's absence is so deep that even the world around him feels it.
ramacharitamanas::2447.simple_meaning: Even the animals are grief-stricken at Ram's departure, so how can the people, mother, and father bear it? Ram sends Sumantra back and continues on to the Ganga bank.
ramacharitamanas::2447.simple_insight: Some departures wound everyone around them, not just the one leaving.
ramacharitamanas::2447.detailed_meaning: On the road to exile, even the horses cannot bear Ram's absence. The scene widens from animals to the whole kingdom: parents, subjects, and friends all face the same unbearable loss. Ram sends Sumantra back and moves on to the Ganga bank.
ramacharitamanas::2447.modern_relevance: You leave a hospital room after saying goodbye, and the silence in the car feels heavier than the news itself. Some separations change the air around everyone who loves.
ramacharitamanas::2447.insight: It turns private grief into a shared human fracture, showing how deeply one person's presence can hold a whole community together.

ramacharitamanas::2448.verse_sanskrit: मागी नाव न केवटु आना। कहइ तुम्हार मरमु मैं जाना॥ चरन कमल रज कहुँ सबु कहई। मानुष करनि मूरि कछु अहई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2448.verse_hindi: श्री राम ने केवट से नाव माँगी, पर वह लाता नहीं। वह कहने लगा- मैंने तुम्हारा मर्म (भेद) जान लिया। तुम्हारे चरण कमलों की धूल के लिए सब लोग कहते हैं कि वह मनुष्य बना देने वाली कोई जड़ी है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2448.english_translation: Kevat did not bring the boat. He said, "I know your secret. Everyone says the dust of your lotus feet is a herb that turns humans into something else."
ramacharitamanas::2448.translation_literal: मागी (asked for) / नाव (boat) / न (not) / केवटु (the boatman) / आना (brought) / कहइ (said) / तुम्हार (your) / मरमु (secret) / मैं (I) / जाना (have known) / चरन (feet) / कमल (lotus) / रज (dust) / कहुँ (for) / सबु (everyone) / कहई (says) / मानुष (human) / करनि (making) / मूरि (herb) / कछु (some) / अहई (is)
ramacharitamanas::2448.speaker: Kevat
ramacharitamanas::2448.essence: A heart in awe cannot treat the sacred as ordinary.
ramacharitamanas::2448.simple_meaning: The boatman refuses at first because he believes Ram's feet are so holy that even their dust can transform a person.
ramacharitamanas::2448.simple_insight: Even refusal can hide reverence when the heart is overwhelmed by holiness.
ramacharitamanas::2448.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank after exile begins, Ram asks the boatman for a ride. Kevat delays, not from greed, but from awe. He has heard stories about Ram's feet and fears their dust will change everything.
ramacharitamanas::2448.modern_relevance: You hesitate before letting someone in because their presence feels too important to handle casually. Respect can make even a simple task feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::2448.insight: It shows how devotion can turn ordinary service into a moment of trembling care.

ramacharitamanas::2449.verse_sanskrit: छुअत सिला भइ नारि सुहाई। पाहन तें न काठ कठिनाई॥ तरनिउ मुनि घरिनी होइ जाई। बाट परइ मोरि नाव उड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2449.verse_hindi: जिसके छूते ही पत्थर की शिला सुंदरी स्त्री हो गई (मेरी नाव तो काठ की है)। काठ पत्थर से कठोर तो होता नहीं। मेरी नाव भी मुनि की स्त्री हो जाएगी और इस प्रकार मेरी नाव उड़ जाएगी, मैं लुट जाऊँगा (अथवा रास्ता रुक जाएगा, जिससे आप पार न हो सकेंगे और मेरी रोजी मारी जाएगी) (मेरी कमाने-खाने की राह ही मारी जाएगी) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2449.english_translation: The stone became a beautiful woman at your touch. Wood is not harder than stone. If my boat turns into a sage's wife, it will be ruined on the road.
ramacharitamanas::2449.translation_literal: छुअत (by touching) / सिला (stone) / भइ (became) / नारि (woman) / सुहाई (beautiful) / पाहन (stone) / तें (than) / काठ (wood) / कठिनाई (hardness) / तरनिउ (even the boat) / मुनि (sage) / घरिनी (wife) / होइ जाई (will become) / बाट (on the road) / परइ (fall) / मोरि (my) / नाव (boat) / उड़ाई (ruined / carried off)
ramacharitamanas::2449.speaker: Kevat
ramacharitamanas::2449.essence: Reverence can sound like bargaining when the heart is afraid to lose its livelihood.
ramacharitamanas::2449.simple_meaning: Kevat jokes that if Ram's touch turned stone into a woman, his wooden boat might also be transformed and lost.
ramacharitamanas::2449.simple_insight: Even a plea for livelihood can hide reverence and wit.
ramacharitamanas::2449.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank in Ayodhyakand, Ram asks Kevat for a crossing. Kevat delays with playful excuses, praising Ram's power through a comic fear that even his boat could be changed by Ram's touch. The moment softens the scene before the crossing.
ramacharitamanas::2449.modern_relevance: You stall for time with a joke when someone you admire asks for help and you know the moment matters.
ramacharitamanas::2449.insight: It shows how devotion can wear the mask of practical concern while still keeping the heart turned toward Ram.

ramacharitamanas::2450.verse_sanskrit: एहिं प्रतिपालउँ सबु परिवारू। नहिं जानउँ कछु अउर कबारू॥ जौं प्रभु पार अवसि गा चहहू। मोहि पद पदुम पखारन कहहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2450.verse_hindi: मैं तो इसी नाव से सारे परिवार का पालन-पोषण करता हूँ। दूसरा कोई धंधा नहीं जानता। हे प्रभु! यदि तुम अवश्य ही पार जाना चाहते हो तो मुझे पहले अपने चरणकमल पखारने (धो लेने) के लिए कह दो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2450.english_translation: I support my whole family with this boat alone. I know no other trade. Lord, if you truly want to cross over, tell me to wash your lotus feet first.
ramacharitamanas::2450.translation_literal: एहिं (with this) / प्रतिपालउँ (I support) / सबु (all) / परिवारू (family) / नहिं (not) / जानउँ (I know) / कछु (any) / अउर (other) / कबारू (trade/occupation)॥ / जौं (if) / प्रभु (Lord) / पार (across/to the other side) / अवसि (certainly) / गा (gone) / चहहू (you want) / मोहि (me) / पद (feet) / पदुम (lotus) / पखारन (to wash) / कहहू (say/tell) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2450.speaker: Kevat
ramacharitamanas::2450.essence: True service can be both practical and deeply reverent.
ramacharitamanas::2450.simple_meaning: Kevat says his boat is his family’s only livelihood, and he asks Ram to let him wash the divine feet before crossing.
ramacharitamanas::2450.simple_insight: Respect can become a way of service, even in the middle of ordinary work.
ramacharitamanas::2450.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are at the riverbank, speaking with Kevat, the boatman. After hinting that he knows Ram’s true nature, Kevat explains that ferrying people is his only livelihood and asks for the chance to wash Ram’s feet before taking them across.
ramacharitamanas::2450.modern_relevance: A taxi driver pauses before helping a passenger with muddy shoes. The gesture is small, but the respect behind it changes the whole exchange.
ramacharitamanas::2450.insight: It shows how livelihood and reverence can meet in one humble act of service.

ramacharitamanas::2451.verse_sanskrit: पद कमल धोइ चढ़ाइ नाव न नाथ उतराई चहौं। मोहि राम राउरि आन दसरथसपथ सब साची कहौं॥ बरु तीर मारहुँ लखनु पै जब लगि न पाय पखारिहौं। तब लगि न तुलसीदास नाथ कृपाल पारु उतारिहौं॥
ramacharitamanas::2451.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! मैं चरण कमल धोकर आप लोगों को नाव पर चढ़ा लूँगा, मैं आपसे कुछ उतराई नहीं चाहता। हे राम! मुझे आपकी दुहाई और दशरथजी की सौगंध है, मैं सब सच-सच कहता हूँ। लक्ष्मण भले ही मुझे तीर मारें, पर जब तक मैं पैरों को पखार न लूँगा, तब तक हे तुलसीदास के नाथ! हे कृपालु! मैं पार नहीं उतारूँगा।
ramacharitamanas::2451.english_translation: O Lord, I will wash your lotus feet, place you in the boat, and take no fee. By Ram, by your own word, and by Dasharath's oath, I speak only the truth. Even if Lakshman were to strike me with an arrow, I will not ferry you until I have washed your feet.
ramacharitamanas::2451.translation_literal: पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / धोइ (washing) / चढ़ाइ (having boarded) / नाव (boat) / न (not) / नाथ (lord) / उतराई (fare) / चहौं (I desire) / मोहि (to me) / राम (Ram) / राउरि (your) / आन (oath) / दसरथसपथ (Dasharath's oath) / सब (all) / साची (true) / कहौं (I say) / बरु (rather) / तीर (arrow) / मारहुँ (strike) / लखनु (Lakshman) / पै (even if) / जब लगि (until) / न (not) / पाय (feet) / पखारिहौं (I wash) / तब लगि (until then) / न (not) / तुलसीदास (Tulsidas) / नाथ (lord) / कृपाल (merciful) / पारु (across) / उतारिहौं (I will ferry)
ramacharitamanas::2451.speaker: Kevat
ramacharitamanas::2451.essence: True devotion refuses payment and asks only to serve first.
ramacharitamanas::2451.simple_meaning: The boatman refuses payment and insists on washing Ram's feet before taking Him across. His devotion is so strong that he values that service above even his own safety.
ramacharitamanas::2451.simple_insight: Love makes service feel like an honour, not a transaction.
ramacharitamanas::2451.detailed_meaning: On the bank of the Ganga, Kevat is speaking to Ram, Sita, and Lakshman after the boatman's earlier hesitation. He will not accept payment. Instead, he asks for the chance to wash Ram's feet first, turning a simple crossing into an act of reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2451.modern_relevance: You help someone move apartments, and they offer money, but you smile and refuse. What you really wanted was the chance to serve well, not to be paid for it.
ramacharitamanas::2451.insight: It shifts service from commerce to reverence, showing that the deepest help is given freely.

ramacharitamanas::2452.verse_sanskrit: सुनि केवट के बैन प्रेम लपेटे अटपटे। बिहसे करुनाऐन चितइ जानकी लखन तन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2452.verse_hindi: केवट के प्रेम में लपेटे हुए अटपटे वचन सुनकर करुणाधाम श्री रामचन्द्रजी जानकीजी और लक्ष्मणजी की ओर देखकर हँसे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2452.english_translation: Hearing the boatman’s strange, love-filled words, the compassionate Lord smiled and looked at Janaki and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::2452.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / केवट (boatman) / के बैन (the words) / प्रेम (love) / लपेटे (wrapped) / अटपटे (awkward, unusual) / बिहसे (smiled) / करुनाऐन (compassionate-eyed) / चितइ (looking at) / जानकी (Janaki) / लखन (Lakshman) / तन (toward)
ramacharitamanas::2452.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2452.essence: Sincere love matters more than polished speech.
ramacharitamanas::2452.simple_meaning: Ram smiles at the boatman’s awkward but loving words and looks at Sita and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::2452.simple_insight: Love can make even awkward words feel beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::2452.detailed_meaning: At the riverbank, the boatman has just spoken with clumsy but sincere devotion. Ram, Sita, and Lakshman hear him. Instead of judging the rough language, Ram smiles with compassion, setting up the gentle exchange that follows.
ramacharitamanas::2452.modern_relevance: Someone fumbles through a heartfelt apology, and you can hear the love underneath the awkwardness. You smile instead of correcting every word.
ramacharitamanas::2452.insight: It trains you to notice sincerity before polish, and respond with warmth rather than criticism.

ramacharitamanas::2453.verse_sanskrit: कृपासिंधु बोले मुसुकाई। सोइ करु जेहिं तव नाव न जाई॥ बेगि आनु जलपाय पखारू। होत बिलंबु उतारहि पारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2453.verse_hindi: कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी केवट से मुस्कुराकर बोले भाई! तू वही कर जिससे तेरी नाव न जाए। जल्दी पानी ला और पैर धो ले। देर हो रही है, पार उतार दे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2453.english_translation: The ocean of compassion smiled and said, “Do what keeps your boat from going away. Quickly bring water and wash my feet. There is no time to waste; take us across.”
ramacharitamanas::2453.translation_literal: कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / बोले (spoke) / मुसुकाई (smiling) / सोइ (that) / करु (do) / जेहिं (by which) / तव (your) / नाव (boat) / न (not) / जाई (go away) / बेगि (quickly) / आनु (bring) / जल (water) / पाय (feet) / पखारू (wash) / होत (there is) / बिलंबु (delay) / उतारहि (take across) / पारू (to the far shore)
ramacharitamanas::2453.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2453.essence: Ram receives humble service with delight and removes every obstacle himself.
ramacharitamanas::2453.simple_meaning: Ram responds warmly to the boatman’s humility and asks him to hurry so the crossing can begin.
ramacharitamanas::2453.simple_insight: Small, sincere humility can open the way faster than pride ever could.
ramacharitamanas::2453.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank, Kevat has just spoken with loving boldness. Ram smiles and answers gently, telling him to do whatever keeps his boat safe and to hurry the crossing. The moment turns courtesy into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2453.modern_relevance: You’re trying to help someone you deeply respect, and they meet your awkward sincerity with a smile instead of judgment. That kind response can dissolve your fear in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::2453.insight: It shifts the mind from self-consciousness to simple, loving service.

ramacharitamanas::2454.verse_sanskrit: जासु नाम सुमिरत एक बारा। उतरहिं नर भवसिंधु अपारा॥ सोइ कृपालु केवटहि निहोरा। जेहिं जगु किय तिहु पगहु ते थोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2454.verse_hindi: एक बार जिनका नाम स्मरण करते ही मनुष्य अपार भवसागर के पार उतर जाते हैं और जिन्होंने (वामनावतार में) जगत को तीन पग से भी छोटा कर दिया था (दो ही पग में त्रिलोकी को नाप लिया था), वही कृपालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी (गंगाजी से पार उतारने के लिए) केवट का निहोरा कर रहे हैं! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2454.english_translation: The one whose name, remembered even once, carries people across the endless sea of becoming is now humbly asking the boatman for help. The same gracious Ram who once measured the world in three steps has made himself smaller than the world.
ramacharitamanas::2454.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / नाम (name) / सुमिरत (remembering) / एक बारा (one time) / उतरहिं (cross over) / नर (people) / भवसिंधु (sea of becoming) / अपारा (boundless)॥ / सोइ (that same) / कृपालु (gracious one) / केवटहि (to the boatman) / निहोरा (request) / जेहिं (by whom) / जगु (the world) / किय (made) / तिहु पगहु (of three steps) / ते (than) / थोरा (smaller) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2454.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2454.essence: The greatest one proves greatness by becoming humble.
ramacharitamanas::2454.simple_meaning: Ram's name is so powerful that it can carry people across life's endless struggles, yet Ram himself humbly asks a boatman for help.
ramacharitamanas::2454.simple_insight: Real greatness does not need to prove itself. It can stay humble without losing any power.
ramacharitamanas::2454.detailed_meaning: On the bank of the Ganga, Ram is asking Kevat to ferry him across. Tulsidas pauses to marvel: the same Ram whose name can carry anyone across the endless sea of becoming is now requesting a boatman, showing divine greatness through humility.
ramacharitamanas::2454.modern_relevance: You know the feeling of being the most capable person in the room, yet still asking for help to get through one stubborn problem. Humility does not reduce strength; it reveals it.
ramacharitamanas::2454.insight: It shifts pride into reverence, showing that true power can choose gentleness and dependence.

ramacharitamanas::2455.verse_sanskrit: पद नख निरखि देवसरि हरषी। सुनि प्रभु बचन मोहँ मति करषी॥ केवट राम रजायसु पावा। पानि कठवता भरि लेइ आवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2455.verse_hindi: प्रभु के इन वचनों को सुनकर गंगाजी की बुद्धि मोह से खिंच गई थी (कि ये साक्षात भगवान होकर भी पार उतारने के लिए केवट का निहोरा कैसे कर रहे हैं), परन्तु (समीप आने पर अपनी उत्पत्ति के स्थान) पदनखों को देखते ही (उन्हें पहचानकर) देवनदी गंगाजी हर्षित हो गईं। (वे समझ गईं कि भगवान नरलीला कर रहे हैं, इससे उनका मोह नष्ट हो गया और इन चरणों का स्पर्श प्राप्त करके मैं धन्य होऊँगी, यह विचारकर वे हर्षित हो गईं।) केवट श्री रामचन्द्रजी की आज्ञा पाकर कठौते में भरकर जल ले आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2455.english_translation: Seeing the Lord's feet and toenails, the river goddess was delighted. Hearing the Lord's words, her mind was pulled by wonder. Then Kevat received Ram's command and brought water in a wooden vessel.
ramacharitamanas::2455.translation_literal: पद नख (toenails of the feet) / निरखि (seeing) / देवसरि (the river goddess) / हरषी (was delighted) / सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु बचन (the Lord's words) / मोहँ (by wonder/delusion) / मति (mind) / करषी (was pulled) / केवट (Kevat) / राम (Ram) / रजायसु (command) / पावा (received) / पानि (water) / कठवता (wooden vessel) / भरि (filling) / लेइ (taking) / आवा (came)
ramacharitamanas::2455.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2455.essence: Seeing the sacred removes doubt and invites service.
ramacharitamanas::2455.simple_meaning: Ganga is first puzzled by Ram's humble request, then delighted when she sees his feet. Kevat obeys and brings water in a wooden vessel.
ramacharitamanas::2455.simple_insight: Wonder softens the mind, and devotion turns hesitation into service.
ramacharitamanas::2455.detailed_meaning: At the river crossing in Ayodhyakand, Ram is still speaking gently with Kevat. Ganga, the river goddess, watches from close by. Ram's words first seem strange, but the sight of his feet brings joy; Kevat then moves into service and fetches water.
ramacharitamanas::2455.modern_relevance: You hear someone ask for help in a way that seems almost too humble to be real. Then you see their sincerity, and the resistance in you melts into willingness.
ramacharitamanas::2455.insight: It shows how reverence clears confusion and turns the next action into service.

ramacharitamanas::2456.verse_sanskrit: अति आनंद उमगि अनुरागा। चरन सरोज पखारन लागा॥ बरषि सुमन सुर सकल सिहाहीं। एहि सम पुन्यपुंज कोउ नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2456.verse_hindi: अत्यन्त आनंद और प्रेम में उमंगकर वह भगवान के चरणकमल धोने लगा। सब देवता फूल बरसाकर सिहाने लगे कि इसके समान पुण्य की राशि कोई नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2456.english_translation: Overwhelmed with great joy and love, he began washing the Lord's lotus feet. All the radiant beings showered flowers and said, 'No one has a store of merit equal to this.'
ramacharitamanas::2456.translation_literal: अति (greatly) / आनंद (joy) / उमगि (surging) / अनुरागा (love) / चरन (feet) / सरोज (lotus) / पखारन (to wash) / लागा (began) / बरषि (showering) / सुमन (flowers) / सुर (radiant beings) / सकल (all) / सिहाहीं (marvelled) / एहि (this) / सम (equal) / पुन्यपुंज (store of merit) / कोउ (anyone) / नाहीं (is not)
ramacharitamanas::2456.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2456.essence: Love-filled service becomes greater than any ritual reward.
ramacharitamanas::2456.simple_meaning: He is so filled with love and joy that he washes Ram's feet, and the radiant beings praise this as unmatched merit.
ramacharitamanas::2456.simple_insight: Selfless service becomes sacred when it is done from overflowing love, not obligation.
ramacharitamanas::2456.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the humble boatman Kevat receives Ram on the riverbank. Overcome with delight, he washes Ram's feet, and the celestial beings marvel at his devotion. The moment turns simple service into a sacred act.
ramacharitamanas::2456.modern_relevance: You help someone after a long day, not because it looks impressive, but because your heart is full. That quiet willingness is what makes ordinary care feel luminous.
ramacharitamanas::2456.insight: It shifts service from transaction to offering, where the value lies in the love behind the act.

ramacharitamanas::2457.verse_sanskrit: पद पखारि जलु पान करि आपु सहित परिवार। पितर पारु करि प्रभुहि पुनि मुदित गयउ लेइ पार ॥
ramacharitamanas::2457.verse_hindi: चरणों को धोकर और सारे परिवार सहित स्वयं उस जल (चरणोदक) को पीकर पहले (उस महान पुण्य के द्वारा) अपने पितरों को भवसागर से पार कर फिर आनंदपूर्वक प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को गंगाजी के पार ले गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2457.english_translation: After washing the feet, he drank that water with his whole family, brought his ancestors across, and then joyfully took the Lord across the river.
ramacharitamanas::2457.translation_literal: पद (feet) / पखारि (having washed) / जलु (water) / पान (drinking) / करि (having done) / आपु (himself) / सहित (along with) / परिवार (family) / पितर (ancestors) / पारु (across) / करि (having made) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / पुनि (then) / मुदित (joyful) / गयउ (went) / लेइ (taking) / पार (across)
ramacharitamanas::2457.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2457.essence: Serving Ram becomes a blessing that reaches the whole family.
ramacharitamanas::2457.simple_meaning: The boatman washed Ram's feet, drank the water with his family, felt his ancestors freed, and then joyfully ferried Ram across the river.
ramacharitamanas::2457.simple_insight: Even a humble act of service can become a source of blessing for generations.
ramacharitamanas::2457.detailed_meaning: At the riverbank in Ayodhyakand, Kevat has just washed Ram's feet and drunk the water with his family. The moment becomes more than a crossing: he feels his ancestors released, then takes Ram, Sita, and Lakshman across in joy.
ramacharitamanas::2457.modern_relevance: You help someone move house, and the whole family ends up eating dinner from the same exhausted kitchen. A small act of service quietly blesses everyone involved.
ramacharitamanas::2457.insight: It turns service into reverence and shows how devotion can overflow into family and lineage.

ramacharitamanas::2458.verse_sanskrit: उतरि ठाढ़ भए सुरसरि रेता। सीय रामुगुह लखन समेता॥ केवट उतरि दंडवत कीन्हा। प्रभुहि सकुच एहि नहिं कछु दीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2458.verse_hindi: निषादराज और लक्ष्मणजी सहित श्री सीताजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी (नाव से) उतरकर गंगाजी की रेत (बालू) में खड़े हो गए। तब केवट ने उतरकर दण्डवत की। (उसको दण्डवत करते देखकर) प्रभु को संकोच हुआ कि इसको कुछ दिया नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2458.english_translation: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman stepped ashore and stood on the sand by the Ganga. The boatman came down and bowed fully. Seeing that, the Lord felt embarrassed that he had given him nothing.
ramacharitamanas::2458.translation_literal: उतरि (having descended) / ठाढ़ भए (stood) / सुरसरि (the Ganga, river of the gods) / रेता (sand) / सीय रामुगुह (Sita, Ram, and Guha) / लखन समेता (together with Lakshman) ॥ / केवट (the boatman) / उतरि (having come down) / दंडवत (full prostration) / कीन्हा (did) ॥ / प्रभुहि (to the Lord) / सकुच (embarrassment) / एहि (this) / नहिं (not) / कछु (anything) / दीन्हा (given) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2458.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2458.essence: Pure devotion can leave even the great feeling they owe more.
ramacharitamanas::2458.simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman step onto the riverbank, and the boatman bows down completely. Ram feels shy because he has nothing to offer in return.
ramacharitamanas::2458.simple_insight: True humility can make even the giver feel indebted.
ramacharitamanas::2458.detailed_meaning: After crossing the Ganga, Ram, Sita, and Lakshman stand on the sandy bank with Guha. The boatman bows at their feet in pure devotion. In that simple gesture, Ram feels the sweetness and awkwardness of receiving without being able to repay.
ramacharitamanas::2458.modern_relevance: You accept help from someone who expects nothing back, and their kindness leaves you strangely humbled. The moment reminds you that real devotion can make gratitude feel larger than payment.
ramacharitamanas::2458.insight: It shows how sincere service can reverse the usual power dynamic and awaken deep humility.

ramacharitamanas::2459.verse_sanskrit: पिय हिय की सिय जाननिहारी। मनि मुदरी मन मुदित उतारी॥ कहेउ कृपाल लेहि उतराई। केवट चरन गहे अकुलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2459.verse_hindi: पति के हृदय की जानने वाली सीताजी ने आनंद भरे मन से अपनी रत्न जडि़त अँगूठी (अँगुली से) उतारी। कृपालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने केवट से कहा, नाव की उतराई लो। केवट ने व्याकुल होकर चरण पकड़ लिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2459.english_translation: Sita, who knows what is in her husband's heart, happily removed her jeweled ring. The gracious Ram said, "Take the fare for the boat." The boatman, overwhelmed, fell at his feet.
ramacharitamanas::2459.translation_literal: पिय (husband's) / हिय (heart) / की (of) / सिय (Sita) / जाननिहारी (knower) / मनि मुदरी (jeweled ring) / मन मुदित (with a joyful mind) / उतारी (removed) ॥ / कहेउ (said) / कृपाल (the gracious one) / लेहि (take) / उतराई (fare) / केवट (boatman) / चरन (feet) / गहे (grasped) / अकुलाई (overwhelmed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2459.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2459.essence: Love sees need and answers it without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::2459.simple_meaning: Sita understands Ram without needing words, and Ram pays the boatman fairly. The boatman is so moved that he falls at Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::2459.simple_insight: True devotion notices what love needs before it is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2459.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank after crossing the Ganga, Sita quietly removes her ring for the boatman, while Ram offers payment with kindness. The boatman is overwhelmed by their grace and immediately bows at Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::2459.modern_relevance: You notice a friend is struggling before they ask for help, and you respond without making it a performance. That kind of care changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::2459.insight: It shows how quiet understanding and respectful generosity can melt pride and create instant trust.

ramacharitamanas::2460.verse_sanskrit: नाथ आजु मैं काह न पावा। मिटे दोष दुख दारिद दावा॥ बहुत काल मैं कीन्हि मजूरी। आजु दीन्ह बिधि बनि भलि भूरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2460.verse_hindi: (उसने कहा-) हे नाथ! आज मैंने क्या नहीं पाया! मेरे दोष, दुःख और दरिद्रता की आग आज बुझ गई है। मैंने बहुत समय तक मजदूरी की। विधाता ने आज बहुत अच्छी भरपूर मजदूरी दे दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2460.english_translation: “Lord, what have I not gained today? My faults, sorrow, and poverty’s fire have all been put out. I have laboured for a long time; today fate has given me a rich and fitting reward.”
ramacharitamanas::2460.translation_literal: नाथ (Lord) / आजु (today) / मैं (I) / काह (what) / न (not) / पावा (got, found) / मिटे (were erased) / दोष (faults) / दुख (sorrow) / दारिद (poverty) / दावा (fire) / बहुत (much, many) / काल (time) / मैं (I) / कीन्हि (did) / मजूरी (labour, wage-work) / आजु (today) / दीन्ह (gave) / बिधि (fate, providence) / बनि (fittingly, appropriately) / भलि (good) / भूरी (abundant, plenty)
ramacharitamanas::2460.speaker: Kevat
ramacharitamanas::2460.essence: Serving Ram turns even labour into abundance.
ramacharitamanas::2460.simple_meaning: The boatman feels that serving Ram has given him everything he lacked: relief from guilt, suffering, and poverty. What he receives is not just payment, but grace.
ramacharitamanas::2460.simple_insight: Real fulfillment can arrive as kindness, not as compensation.
ramacharitamanas::2460.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank, Kevat has just ferried Ram, Sita, and Lakshman across the Ganga. Overwhelmed by Ram’s presence, he says he has received far more than a fare: his old burdens, pain, and poverty feel erased. This is his grateful surrender.
ramacharitamanas::2460.modern_relevance: You help someone move house, expecting only a thank-you, and they quietly cover your rent for the month. The deeper gift is not the money — it is the feeling of being seen and lifted.
ramacharitamanas::2460.insight: It shifts you from measuring life by wages to recognising grace as the truest reward.

ramacharitamanas::2461.verse_sanskrit: अब कछु नाथ न चाहिअ मोरें। दीन दयाल अनुग्रह तोरें॥ फिरती बार मोहि जो देबा। सो प्रसादु मैं सिर धरि लेबा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2461.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! हे दीनदयाल! आपकी कृपा से अब मुझे कुछ नहीं चाहिए। लौटती बार आप मुझे जो कुछ देंगे, वह प्रसाद मैं सिर चढ़ाकर लूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2461.english_translation: O Lord, I need nothing more. By your grace, I am content. Whatever you give me on your return, I will receive as sacred blessing on my head.
ramacharitamanas::2461.translation_literal: अब (now) / कछु (anything) / नाथ (Lord) / न चाहिअ (is not needed) / मोरें (for me) / दीन दयाल (compassionate to the poor) / अनुग्रह (grace) / तोरें (your) / फिरती (on returning) / बार (time) / मोहि (to me) / जो (whatever) / देबा (you will give) / सो (that) / प्रसादु (grace/offering) / मैं (I) / सिर धरि (placing on the head) / लेबा (will receive)
ramacharitamanas::2461.speaker: Kevat
ramacharitamanas::2461.essence: Grace ends need; whatever comes next becomes an offering.
