ramacharitamanas::2461.simple_meaning: Kevat says he needs nothing else from Ram. Whatever Ram gives later, he will accept it as a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2461.simple_insight: When the heart is full of grace, desire falls away.
ramacharitamanas::2461.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank, Kevat has just ferried Ram, Sita, and Lakshman across and refused payment. Overwhelmed by their kindness, he says he wants nothing now. If Ram gives anything on the return journey, he will accept it as sacred grace.
ramacharitamanas::2461.modern_relevance: You help someone move house, and they keep thanking you even after the work is done. You realize the real gift was not money or credit, but the feeling of being touched by kindness.
ramacharitamanas::2461.insight: It shifts gratitude from transaction to blessing, and teaches you to receive without grasping.

ramacharitamanas::2462.verse_sanskrit: बहुत कीन्ह प्रभु लखन सियँ नहिं कछु केवटु लेइ। बिदा कीन्ह करुनायतन भगति बिमल बरु देइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2462.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी ने बहुत आग्रह (या यत्न) किया, पर केवट कुछ नहीं लेता। तब करुणा के धाम भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने निर्मल भक्ति का वरदान देकर उसे विदा किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2462.english_translation: The Lord, Lakshman, and Sita offered much, but the boatman took nothing. Then the abode of compassion sent him away, giving him the pure boon of devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2462.translation_literal: बहुत (much) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रभु (the Lord) / लखन (Lakshman) / सियँ (and Sita) / नहिं (not) / कछु (anything) / केवटु (the boatman) / लेइ (takes) / बिदा (farewell) / कीन्ह (gave) / करुनायतन (abode of compassion) / भगति (devotion) / बिमल (pure) / बरु (boon) / देइ (giving)
ramacharitamanas::2462.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2462.essence: Refusing payment becomes the doorway to a greater gift.
ramacharitamanas::2462.simple_meaning: Kevat refuses payment, and Ram blesses him with devotion instead of money. The exchange becomes a lesson that love and grace are worth more than any gift.
ramacharitamanas::2462.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing the deepest exchange cannot be bought.
ramacharitamanas::2462.detailed_meaning: At the riverbank, Kevat has just ferried Ram, Lakshman, and Sita across. They try to reward him, but he refuses. Moved by his humility, Ram sends him off with a blessing: devotion itself, not payment, is the real reward.
ramacharitamanas::2462.modern_relevance: You help a stranger move house, and they keep trying to hand you cash. What stays with you is not the money refused, but the quiet dignity of giving without keeping score.
ramacharitamanas::2462.insight: It shifts the mind from transaction to offering, showing that the highest return is inward.

ramacharitamanas::2463.verse_sanskrit: तब मज्जनु करि रघुकुलनाथा। पूजि पारथिव नायउ माथा॥ सियँ सुरसरिहि कहेउ कर जोरी। मातु मनोरथ पुरउबि मोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2463.verse_hindi: फिर रघुकुल के स्वामी श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने स्नान करके पार्थिव पूजा की और शिवजी को सिर नवाया। सीताजी ने हाथ जोड़कर गंगाजी से कहा- हे माता! मेरा मनोरथ पूरा कीजिएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2463.english_translation: After bathing, the Lord of the Raghu clan worshiped the sacred image and bowed his head to Shiva. Sita joined her palms and said to the Ganga, "Mother, may you fulfill my wish."
ramacharitamanas::2463.translation_literal: तब (then) / मज्जनु (bath) / करि (having done) / रघुकुलनाथा (Lord of the Raghu clan) / पूजि (worshiped) / पारथिव (earth-made image) / नायउ (bowed) / माथा (head) / सियँ (Sita) / सुरसरिहि (to the heavenly river) / कहेउ (said) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined) / मातु (mother) / मनोरथ (wish) / पुरउबि (fulfill) / मोरी (my)
ramacharitamanas::2463.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2463.essence: Reverence begins with the body before it becomes a prayer.
ramacharitamanas::2463.simple_meaning: Ram bathes, worships Shiva, and bows his head. Sita folds her hands before the Ganga and asks the river-mother to fulfil her wish.
ramacharitamanas::2463.simple_insight: Reverence is shown through action first, then through prayer.
ramacharitamanas::2463.detailed_meaning: On the journey through exile, Ram stops after bathing to honor Shiva, while Sita turns to the Ganga with folded hands. The scene is part of their respectful passage, not a finished teaching, and leads into Sita's prayer for safe return.
ramacharitamanas::2463.modern_relevance: Before a long trip, you pause at a roadside shrine, touch your forehead, and ask quietly for safe passage. The gesture matters because it holds your whole hope.
ramacharitamanas::2463.insight: It shows devotion as a lived act: bow, pray, and move forward with humility.

ramacharitamanas::2464.verse_sanskrit: पति देवर सँग कुसल बहोरी। आइ करौं जेहिं पूजा तोरी॥ सुनि सिय बिनय प्रेम रस सानी। भइ तब बिमल बारि बर बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2464.verse_hindi: जिससे मैं पति और देवर के साथ कुशलतापूर्वक लौट आकर तुम्हारी पूजा करूँ। सीताजी की प्रेम रस में सनी हुई विनती सुनकर तब गंगाजी के निर्मल जल में से श्रेष्ठ वाणी हुई- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2464.english_translation: "So that I may return safely with my husband and brother-in-law, and come back to worship you." Hearing Sita's plea, soaked in the nectar of love, the pure waters then spoke in a noble voice.
ramacharitamanas::2464.translation_literal: पति (husband) / देवर (brother-in-law) / सँग (with) / कुसल (safe, well) / बहोरी (back again) / आइ (coming) / करौं (I may do) / जेहिं (so that) / पूजा (worship) / तोरी (your)॥ / सुनि (hearing) / सिय (Sita's) / बिनय (plea, humble request) / प्रेम (love) / रस (essence, nectar) / सानी (soaked, mixed) / भइ (became) / तब (then) / बिमल (pure) / बारि (water) / बर (excellent, noble) / बानी (voice) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2464.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2464.essence: Trust asks for help first and honors it afterward.
ramacharitamanas::2464.simple_meaning: Sita asks the river for safe passage back with Ram and Lakshman, promising to return and worship it afterward. Her request is full of love and trust.
ramacharitamanas::2464.simple_insight: Love can ask for help without losing humility.
ramacharitamanas::2464.detailed_meaning: At the riverbank in Ayodhyakand, Sita stands with Ram and Lakshman before crossing onward. She asks the river for safe return first, then promises worship later. The moment shows her tender trust and the river answering that devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2464.modern_relevance: You ask a friend, teacher, or elder for help before a hard trip, promising to thank them properly when you return. Real gratitude begins with trust.
ramacharitamanas::2464.insight: It teaches you to ask with humility and to treat help as something sacred, not automatic.

ramacharitamanas::2465.verse_sanskrit: सुनु रघुबीर प्रिया बैदेही। तब प्रभाउ जग बिदित न केही॥ लोकप होहिं बिलोकत तोरें। तोहि सेवहिं सब सिधि कर जोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2465.verse_hindi: हे रघुवीर की प्रियतमा जानकी! सुनो, तुम्हारा प्रभाव जगत में किसे नहीं मालूम है? तुम्हारे (कृपा दृष्टि से) देखते ही लोग लोकपाल हो जाते हैं। सब सिद्धियाँ हाथ जोड़े तुम्हारी सेवा करती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2465.english_translation: Listen, beloved Vaidehi of Raghubir: who in the world does not know your power? Merely by seeing you, rulers become guardians of the world. All powers stand with folded hands and serve you.
ramacharitamanas::2465.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / रघुबीर (Lord of Raghu) / प्रिया (beloved) / बैदेही (Vaidehi) / तब (your) / प्रभाउ (power/influence) / जग (world) / बिदित (known) / न (not) / केही (who) / लोकप (world-guardians) / होहिं (become) / बिलोकत (by seeing) / तोरें (you) / तोहि (you) / सेवहिं (serve) / सब (all) / सिधि (powers/perfections) / कर (hands) / जोरें (folded)
ramacharitamanas::2465.speaker: Ganga
ramacharitamanas::2465.essence: True greatness needs no display; everything bows to it naturally.
ramacharitamanas::2465.simple_meaning: Sita's presence is so powerful that even rulers and spiritual powers bow to her and serve her.
ramacharitamanas::2465.simple_insight: You do not need to chase respect when your presence is rooted in grace.
ramacharitamanas::2465.detailed_meaning: Ganga is answering Sita's humble prayer by praising her instead of receiving honor. In this moment, Sita's quiet greatness is revealed: the world already knows her power, and even the highest forces serve her.
ramacharitamanas::2465.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after years of being underestimated, and the mood changes before you speak. Some people don't need to announce their worth; their steadiness does it for them.
ramacharitamanas::2465.insight: It shifts attention from self-promotion to the quiet authority that comes from inner grace.

ramacharitamanas::2466.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह जो हमहि बड़ि बिनय सुनाई। कृपा कीन्हि मोहि दीन्हि बड़ाई॥ तदपि देबि मैं देबि असीसा। सफल होन हित निज बागीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2466.verse_hindi: तुमने जो मुझको बड़ी विनती सुनाई, यह तो मुझ पर कृपा की और मुझे बड़ाई दी है। तो भी हे देवी! मैं अपनी वाणी सफल होने के लिए तुम्हें आशीर्वाद दूँगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2466.english_translation: You have shown me great humility and given me honour. Still, O Devi, I will bless you so that my words bear fruit.
ramacharitamanas::2466.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / जो (which) / हमहि (to me) / बड़ि (great) / बिनय (humility, request) / सुनाई (made heard) / कृपा (grace) / कीन्हि (did) / मोहि (to me) / दीन्हि (gave) / बड़ाई (honour, greatness)॥ / तदपि (still) / देबि (O Devi) / मैं (I) / देबि (will bless) / असीसा (blessing) / सफल (fruitful) / होन (to become) / हित (for the sake of) / निज (my own) / बागीसा (speech, words) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2466.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2466.essence: Humility invites blessing and turns speech into grace.
ramacharitamanas::2466.simple_meaning: Sita says the other woman’s respectful request has honoured her, and she responds by giving a blessing so her words may prove fruitful.
ramacharitamanas::2466.simple_insight: True respect softens the heart and invites a generous response.
ramacharitamanas::2466.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita is speaking to the river Ganga after asking for blessing before leaving. Ganga has praised her devotion and answered kindly. Now Sita returns that honour, showing the graceful exchange between reverence and blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2466.modern_relevance: You thank someone for their kindness, and they answer by blessing your path. A humble request can turn a conversation into mutual grace.
ramacharitamanas::2466.insight: It teaches you to meet respect with generosity, not superiority.

ramacharitamanas::2467.verse_sanskrit: प्राननाथ देवर सहित कुसल कोसला आइ। पूजिहि सब मनकामना सुजसु रहिहि जग छाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2467.verse_hindi: तुम अपने प्राणनाथ और देवर सहित कुशलपूर्वक अयोध्या लौटोगी। तुम्हारी सारी मनःकामनाएँ पूरी होंगी और तुम्हारा सुंदर यश जगतभर में छा जाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2467.english_translation: You will return to Kosala safely with your lord and your brother. All your wishes will be fulfilled, and your beautiful fame will spread through the world.
ramacharitamanas::2467.translation_literal: प्राननाथ (lord of life) / देवर (brother-in-law) / सहित (together with) / कुसल (safe, well) / कोसला (to Kosala) / आइ (coming, returning) / पूजिहि (will be fulfilled, honored) / सब (all) / मनकामना (wishes) / सुजसु (good fame) / रहिहि (will remain) / जग (world) / छाइ (spreading, covering)
ramacharitamanas::2467.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2467.essence: Safe return, fulfilled longing, and lasting honor are all promised together.
ramacharitamanas::2467.simple_meaning: Sita is assured that she will return safely to Kosala with Ram and Lakshman, that her wishes will be fulfilled, and that her good name will spread everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::2467.simple_insight: Promise and reassurance can steady a heart that has been through fear.
ramacharitamanas::2467.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita is being comforted as the exile’s grief begins to turn toward return. The speaker blesses her with safety, fulfilled wishes, and lasting honor, preparing the emotional ground for Ram, Lakshman, and Sita to move back toward Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::2467.modern_relevance: After weeks of uncertainty, someone finally texts: the interview went well, the family is safe, and you can exhale. This verse carries that relief — the fear is not the final word.
ramacharitamanas::2467.insight: It shifts the mind from dread to received assurance.

ramacharitamanas::2468.verse_sanskrit: गंग बचन सुनि मंगल मूला। मुदित सीय सुरसरि अनुकूला॥ तब प्रभु गुहहि कहेउ घर जाहू। सुनत सूख मुखु भा उर दाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2468.verse_hindi: मंगल के मूल गंगाजी के वचन सुनकर और देवनदी को अनुकूल देखकर सीताजी आनंदित हुईं। तब प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने निषादराज गुह से कहा कि भैया! अब तुम घर जाओ! यह सुनते ही उसका मुँह सूख गया और हृदय में दाह उत्पन्न हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2468.english_translation: Hearing Gangaji's words, the source of auspiciousness, and seeing the river goddess favorable, Sita felt joy. Then Lord Ram said to Guha, "Go home now." Hearing this, Guha's mouth went dry and his heart burned.
ramacharitamanas::2468.translation_literal: गंग (Ganga) / बचन (words) / सुनि (having heard) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मूला (root) / मुदित (delighted) / सीय (Sita) / सुरसरि (river goddess) / अनुकूला (favorable) / तब (then) / प्रभु (Lord) / गुहहि (to Guha) / कहेउ (said) / घर (home) / जाहू (go) / सुनत (hearing) / सूख (dried) / मुखु (mouth) / भा (became) / उर (heart) / दाहू (burning)
ramacharitamanas::2468.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2468.essence: A welcome sign can steady you, but parting still burns.
ramacharitamanas::2468.simple_meaning: Sita feels reassured by Gangaji's favorable sign. Ram then tells Guha to return home, and Guha is pained by the sudden separation.
ramacharitamanas::2468.simple_insight: Even a kind farewell can hurt when your heart wants to stay close.
ramacharitamanas::2468.detailed_meaning: On the bank of the Ganga, Sita takes the river's response as an auspicious sign and feels at ease. Ram then gently tells Guha to return home. Guha, who longs to serve longer, is struck with sudden sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2468.modern_relevance: You finally get a warm reply after days of uncertainty, and your chest loosens. Then the other person says they have to leave, and the ache returns at once.
ramacharitamanas::2468.insight: It shows how quickly joy and grief can turn when attachment meets separation.

ramacharitamanas::2469.verse_sanskrit: दीन बचन गुह कह कर जोरी। बिनय सुनहु रघुकुलमनि मोरी॥ नाथ साथ रहि पंथु देखाई। करि दिन चारि चरन सेवकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2469.verse_hindi: गुह हाथ जोड़कर दीन वचन बोला- हे रघुकुल शिरोमणि! मेरी विनती सुनिए। मैं नाथ (आप) के साथ रहकर, रास्ता दिखाकर, चार (कुछ) दिन चरणों की सेवा करके- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2469.english_translation: Guha, with folded hands, spoke humbly: "Listen to my request, jewel of Raghu's line. Let me stay with you, show you the path, and serve your feet for four days."
ramacharitamanas::2469.translation_literal: दीन (humble) / बचन (words) / गुह (Guha) / कह (said) / करि (doing) / जोरी (folded hands) / बिनय (request) / सुनहु (listen) / रघुकुलमनि (jewel of Raghu's line) / मोरी (my)॥ / नाथ (master) / साथ (with) / रहि (staying) / पंथु (path) / देखाई (showing) / करि (doing) / दिन (days) / चारि (four) / चरन (feet) / सेवकाई (service)॥
ramacharitamanas::2469.speaker: Guha
ramacharitamanas::2469.essence: Humility turns into service when love wants to help, not impress.
ramacharitamanas::2469.simple_meaning: Guha asks Ram to let him stay nearby, guide the route, and serve Him humbly for a few days.
ramacharitamanas::2469.simple_insight: Real devotion often looks like practical help, not grand speech.
ramacharitamanas::2469.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are leaving for the forest, and Guha cannot bear to let them go unsupported. With folded hands, he asks for one thing: a chance to guide, accompany, and serve them before they depart.
ramacharitamanas::2469.modern_relevance: Someone is leaving town with a broken heart, and you do not offer speeches. You pack water, print the route, and stay until the last bag is lifted. That is Guha's kind of love.
ramacharitamanas::2469.insight: It shifts service from sentiment to action: be present, make the path easier, and ask for nothing back.

ramacharitamanas::2470.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं बन जाइ रहब रघुराई। परनकुटी मैं करबि सुहाई॥ तब मोहि कहँ जसि देब रजाई। सोइ करिहउँ रघुबीर दोहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2470.verse_hindi: हे रघुराज! जिस वन में आप जाकर रहेंगे, वहाँ मैं सुंदर पर्णकुटी (पत्तों की कुटिया) बना दूँगा। तब मुझे आप जैसी आज्ञा देंगे, मुझे रघुवीर (आप) की दुहाई है, मैं वैसा ही करूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2470.english_translation: O Lord of Raghu, whichever forest you go to live in, I will make a beautiful leaf-hut there. Then, whatever command you give me, I swear by Raghubir I will do it.
ramacharitamanas::2470.translation_literal: जेहिं (whichever) बन (forest) जाइ (go) रहब (will live) रघुराई (Lord of Raghu) / परनकुटी (leaf-hut) मैं (I) करबि (will make) सुहाई (beautiful)॥ तब (then) मोहि (to me) कहँ (to) जसि (whatever) देब (you give) रजाई (command) / सोइ (that only) करिहउँ (I will do) रघुबीर (Raghubir) दोहाई (by oath)॥
ramacharitamanas::2470.speaker: Guh
ramacharitamanas::2470.essence: Service means making your hands available before your pride speaks.
ramacharitamanas::2470.simple_meaning: Guh offers to build Ram a hut wherever He stays in the forest and promises to do exactly as Ram commands.
ramacharitamanas::2470.simple_insight: Love becomes real when it turns into ready service.
ramacharitamanas::2470.detailed_meaning: Guh is standing before Ram as exile begins. He does not ask for reward or closeness; he offers shelter, labor, and obedience. In this brief vow, devotion takes the form of practical service.
ramacharitamanas::2470.modern_relevance: A friend moves into a new place and you show up with tools, boxes, and a plan. You do not ask what you’ll get back. You just make their burden lighter.
ramacharitamanas::2470.insight: It teaches you to turn affection into concrete help, and to obey what truly matters without hesitation.

ramacharitamanas::2471.verse_sanskrit: सहज सनेह राम लखि तासू। संग लीन्ह गुह हृदयँ हुलासू॥ पुनि गुहँ ग्याति बोलि सब लीन्हे। करि परितोषु बिदा तब कीन्हे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2471.verse_hindi: उसके स्वाभाविक प्रेम को देखकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने उसको साथ ले लिया, इससे गुह के हृदय में बड़ा आनंद हुआ। फिर गुह (निषादराज) ने अपनी जाति के लोगों को बुला लिया और उनका संतोष कराके तब उनको विदा किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2471.english_translation: Seeing his natural affection, Ram took Guha along, and Guha’s heart filled with joy. Then Guha called his people, satisfied them, and only after that did he bid them farewell.
ramacharitamanas::2471.translation_literal: सहज (natural) / सनेह (affection) / राम (Ram) / लखि (seeing) / तासू (his) / संग (with) / लीन्ह (took) / गुह (Guha) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / हुलासू (joy)॥ / पुनि (then) / गुहँ (Guha) / ग्याति (people/kinsmen) / बोलि (calling) / सब (all) / लीन्हे (took/assembled) / करि (having done) / परितोषु (satisfaction) / बिदा (farewell) / तब (then) / कीन्हे (did)
ramacharitamanas::2471.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2471.essence: Affection becomes joy when it is recognised and returned.
ramacharitamanas::2471.simple_meaning: Ram notices Guha’s natural affection and lets him stay close, which fills Guha with joy. Guha then gathers his people, settles them, and sends them back with contentment.
ramacharitamanas::2471.simple_insight: Real closeness is received through warmth, not status. When affection is simple, everyone feels included.
ramacharitamanas::2471.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank before exile begins, Guha has offered Ram loyal service. Ram sees the sincerity behind it and welcomes him as a companion, not a servant. Guha then turns to his own people, reassures them, and sends them away with peace.
ramacharitamanas::2471.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a difficult family gathering, and they treat your care as something precious instead of awkward. That simple welcome changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::2471.insight: It shifts the mind from hierarchy to mutual affection, showing that genuine welcome creates belonging.

ramacharitamanas::2472.verse_sanskrit: तब गनपति सिव सुमिरि प्रभु नाइ सुरसरिहि माथ। सखा अनुज सिय सहित बन गवनु कीन्ह रघुनाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2472.verse_hindi: तब प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी गणेशजी और शिवजी का स्मरण करके तथा गंगाजी को मस्तक नवाकर सखा निषादराज, छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सहित वन को चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2472.english_translation: Then Lord Raghunath, remembering Ganapati and Shiva and bowing his head to the Ganga, went to the forest with his friend Guha, his younger brother Lakshman, and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2472.translation_literal: तब (then) / गनपति (Ganapati) / सिव (Shiva) / सुमिरि (remembering) / प्रभु (the Lord) / नाइ (bowing) / सुरसरिहि (to the celestial river Ganga) / माथ (head) / सखा (with friend) / अनुज (younger brother) / सिय (Sita) / सहित (together with) / बन (forest) / गवनु (going) / कीन्ह (did) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::2472.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2472.essence: A hard leaving becomes graceful when you begin with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2472.simple_meaning: Ram begins the journey to the forest with Lakshman, Sita, and Guha after honoring Ganesh, Shiva, and the Ganga.
ramacharitamanas::2472.simple_insight: Even a painful departure can begin with reverence and calm.
ramacharitamanas::2472.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya has lost its prince, and the exile is now real. Ram leaves the city with Sita, Lakshman, and Guha, first honoring Ganesh, Shiva, and the Ganga. The verse marks the solemn crossing from palace life into forest life.
ramacharitamanas::2472.modern_relevance: You pack the car after a life-changing goodbye, stop once to bow your head, and then keep driving. The next chapter starts with respect, not noise.
ramacharitamanas::2472.insight: It turns departure into a sacred transition, not a collapse.

ramacharitamanas::2473.verse_sanskrit: तेहि दिन भयउ बिटप तर बासू। लखन सखाँ सब कीन्ह सुपासू॥ प्रात प्रातकृत करि रघुराई। तीरथराजु दीख प्रभु जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2473.verse_hindi: उस दिन पेड़ के नीचे निवास हुआ। लक्ष्मणजी और सखा गुह ने (विश्राम की) सब सुव्यवस्था कर दी। प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सबेरे प्रातःकाल की सब क्रियाएँ करके जाकर तीर्थों के राजा प्रयाग के दर्शन किए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2473.english_translation: That day they stayed beneath a tree. Lakshman and their friend Guha arranged everything for their rest. At dawn, after completing his morning rites, Lord Ram went to see Prayag, the king of holy places.
ramacharitamanas::2473.translation_literal: तेहि दिन (that day) / भयउ (was) / बिटप तर (under a tree) / बासू (dwelling) । / लखन (Lakshman) / सखाँ (with the friend) / सब (all) / कीन्ह (made) / सुपासू (proper arrangement) ॥ / प्रात (in the morning) / प्रातकृत (morning rites) / करि (doing) / रघुराई (Lord of the Raghu clan) । / तीरथराजु (king of holy places) / दीख (saw) / प्रभु (the Lord) / जाई (going) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2473.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2473.essence: Resting in exile, Ram keeps reverence and routine intact.
ramacharitamanas::2473.simple_meaning: Ram spends the night under a tree, while Lakshman and Guha arrange the rest. In the morning, Ram completes his rituals and goes to see Prayag.
ramacharitamanas::2473.simple_insight: Even exile is lived with care, order, and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2473.detailed_meaning: After leaving Ayodhya, Ram, Lakshman, Sita, and Guha rest outdoors on the riverbank. Lakshman and Guha prepare everything with devotion, and Ram rises at dawn to complete his rites before visiting Prayag. The verse moves the journey forward, not the argument.
ramacharitamanas::2473.modern_relevance: You sleep on a borrowed floor after a hard day of travel, and someone quietly makes the space decent for you. The kindness matters more than the place.
ramacharitamanas::2473.insight: It shows how dignity can remain intact even in hardship, through simple order and respectful care.

ramacharitamanas::2474.verse_sanskrit: सचिव सत्य श्रद्धा प्रिय नारी। माधव सरिस मीतु हितकारी॥ चारि पदारथ भरा भँडारू। पुन्य प्रदेस देस अति चारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2474.verse_hindi: उस राजा का सत्य मंत्री है, श्रद्धा प्यारी स्त्री है और श्री वेणीमाधवजी सरीखे हितकारी मित्र हैं। चार पदार्थों (धर्म, अर्थ, काम और मोक्ष) से भंडार भरा है और वह पुण्यमय प्रांत ही उस राजा का सुंदर देश है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2474.english_translation: A king's minister is truth, his beloved queen is trust, and his helpful friend is like Madhav. His treasury is full of the four aims of life, and his beautiful country is a land of merit.
ramacharitamanas::2474.translation_literal: सचिव (minister) / सत्य (truth) / श्रद्धा (trust) / प्रिय (beloved) / नारी (woman, wife) / माधव (Madhav) / सरिस (like) / मीतु (friend) / हितकारी (beneficial) / चारि (four) / पदारथ (aims/objects) / भरा (filled) / भँडारू (treasury) / पुन्य (merit) / प्रदेस (region) / देस (country) / अति (very) / चारू (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::2474.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2474.essence: A life ruled by truth and trust already contains its own wealth.
ramacharitamanas::2474.simple_meaning: A good life is built on truth, trust, and helpful friendship. When those are present, even your surroundings feel rich, orderly, and blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2474.simple_insight: You feel steadier when your life is supported by honesty, trust, and people who genuinely help you.
ramacharitamanas::2474.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the ideal place and the ideal ruler in one sweep. In this vision, truth serves as the minister, trust becomes the beloved companion, and helpful friendship stands beside the king. Such a realm is already full of life's highest aims.
ramacharitamanas::2474.modern_relevance: A home where people tell the truth, keep faith with each other, and show up when needed feels different the moment you walk in. The air is lighter, the arguments soften, and even ordinary life starts to feel abundant.
ramacharitamanas::2474.insight: It shifts attention from outer wealth to the relationships and values that make a life truly prosperous.

ramacharitamanas::2475.verse_sanskrit: छेत्रु अगम गढ़ु गाढ़ सुहावा। सपनेहुँ नहिं प्रतिपच्छिन्ह पावा॥ सेन सकल तीरथ बर बीरा। कलुष अनीक दलन रनधीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2475.verse_hindi: प्रयाग क्षेत्र ही दुर्गम, मजबूत और सुंदर गढ़ (किला) है, जिसको स्वप्न में भी (पाप रूपी) शत्रु नहीं पा सके हैं। संपूर्ण तीर्थ ही उसके श्रेष्ठ वीर सैनिक हैं, जो पाप की सेना को कुचल डालने वाले और बड़े रणधीर हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2475.english_translation: The sacred field is an inaccessible, fortified, beautiful stronghold that evil cannot reach even in dreams. All the great holy places are its finest warriors, brave in battle and destroyers of impurity.
ramacharitamanas::2475.translation_literal: छेत्रु (field/sacred place) / अगम (hard to reach) / गढ़ु (fortress) / गाढ़ (strong) / सुहावा (beautiful) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / नहिं (not) / प्रतिपच्छिन्ह (opposing forces/enemies) / पावा (can reach) // सेन (army) / सकल (all) / तीरथ (holy places) / बर (best) / बीरा (warriors) / कलुष (impurity) / अनीक (army) / दलन (destroying) / रनधीरा (battle-brave)
ramacharitamanas::2475.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2475.essence: Holiness becomes a fortress that impurity cannot breach.
ramacharitamanas::2475.simple_meaning: Prayag is described as a sacred fortress so protected by holy power that impurity cannot enter it. Its many holy places are like brave warriors destroying inner corruption.
ramacharitamanas::2475.simple_insight: Some places feel protected by goodness itself, as if they guard your mind before you even arrive.
ramacharitamanas::2475.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Guha are moving through the sacred land around Prayag. The poet pauses to praise the place itself: its holiness is so complete that even evil cannot approach it, and its many shrines stand like fearless defenders.
ramacharitamanas::2475.modern_relevance: You walk into a temple courtyard after a chaotic day and your shoulders drop before anyone speaks. Some spaces don't just host devotion — they seem to defend it.
ramacharitamanas::2475.insight: It turns a place into a living force that repels corruption and strengthens the mind.

ramacharitamanas::2476.verse_sanskrit: संगमु सिंहासनु सुठि सोहा। छत्रु अखयबटु मुनि मनु मोहा॥ चवँर जमुन अरु गंग तरंगा। देखि होहिं दुख दारिद भंगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2476.verse_hindi: (गंगा, यमुना और सरस्वती का) संगम ही उसका अत्यन्त सुशोभित सिंहासन है। अक्षयवट छत्र है, जो मुनियों के भी मन को मोहित कर लेता है। यमुनाजी और गंगाजी की तरंगें उसके (श्याम और श्वेत) चँवर हैं, जिनको देखकर ही दुःख और दरिद्रता नष्ट हो जाती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2476.english_translation: The confluence itself is his splendid throne. The Akshayvat tree is his canopy, captivating even the minds of sages. The waves of the Yamuna and Ganga are his two fly-whisks; just seeing them destroys sorrow and poverty.
ramacharitamanas::2476.translation_literal: संगमु (the confluence) / सिंहासनु (throne) / सुठि (very) / सोहा (shone beautifully) / छत्रु (canopy) / अखयबटु (Akshayvat tree) / मुनि (sages) / मनु (mind) / मोहा (delighted/captivated) / चवँर (fly-whisks) / जमुन (Yamuna) / अरु (and) / गंग (Ganga) / तरंगा (waves) / देखि (seeing) / होहिं (become) / दुख (sorrow) / दारिद (poverty) / भंगा (broken/destroyed)
ramacharitamanas::2476.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2476.essence: Sacred presence can turn landscape into a throne of relief.
ramacharitamanas::2476.simple_meaning: The sacred meeting place of rivers is described like a royal seat, with the tree as a canopy and the river waves as ceremonial fans. Just seeing it is said to wash away sorrow and lack.
ramacharitamanas::2476.simple_insight: Some places feel so holy and alive that they seem to lift your burdens before you even speak.
ramacharitamanas::2476.detailed_meaning: The narrator is praising Prayag after describing its greatness. The rivers, tree, and landscape are turned into royal symbols to show that this is not ordinary geography but a living sacred center. The verse builds the beauty that the next lines will complete.
ramacharitamanas::2476.modern_relevance: You step into a riverbank temple at dawn, and the sound of water, bells, and wind seems to untie something tight in your chest before you say a word.
ramacharitamanas::2476.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary scenery to sacred presence, where place itself becomes a support for the mind.

ramacharitamanas::2477.verse_sanskrit: सेवहिं सुकृती साधु सुचि पावहिं सब मनकाम। बंदी बेद पुरान गन कहहिं बिमल गुन ग्राम ॥
ramacharitamanas::2477.verse_hindi: पुण्यात्मा, पवित्र साधु उसकी सेवा करते हैं और सब मनोरथ पाते हैं। वेद और पुराणों के समूह भाट हैं, जो उसके निर्मल गुणगणों का बखान करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2477.english_translation: The virtuous and pure serve him, and all their wishes are fulfilled. The Vedas and Puranas sing the spotless array of his virtues.
ramacharitamanas::2477.translation_literal: सेवहिं (serve) / सुकृती (the virtuous) / साधु (the holy) / सुचि (pure) / पावहिं (obtain) / सब (all) / मनकाम (desired wishes) / बंदी (bards) / बेद (the Vedas) / पुरान (the Puranas) / गन (groups) / कहहिं (sing/say) / बिमल (spotless) / गुन ग्राम (clusters of virtues)
ramacharitamanas::2477.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2477.essence: Serving Ram fulfills the heart more deeply than getting what it wants.
ramacharitamanas::2477.simple_meaning: Good and pure people serve Ram, and their deepest wishes are fulfilled. Even the Vedas and Puranas praise his flawless virtues.
ramacharitamanas::2477.simple_insight: There is relief in serving something worthy: devotion does not diminish you; it gathers your life into meaning.
ramacharitamanas::2477.detailed_meaning: At Prayag, Tulsidas pauses the geography to praise Ram's presence there. The holy serve him, desires are fulfilled, and even the Vedas and Puranas become singers of his virtues. This turns a sacred place into a living devotional truth.
ramacharitamanas::2477.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for the person who never asks for applause, and somehow that loyalty starts changing you. This verse knows that service can become its own reward.
ramacharitamanas::2477.insight: It shifts attention from getting blessings to becoming the kind of person who serves what is truly worthy.

ramacharitamanas::2478.verse_sanskrit: को कहि सकइ प्रयाग प्रभाऊ। कलुष पुंज कुंजर मृगराऊ॥ अस तीरथपति देखि सुहावा। सुख सागर रघुबर सुखु पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2478.verse_hindi: पापों के समूह रूपी हाथी के मारने के लिए सिंह रूप प्रयागराज का प्रभाव (महत्व-माहात्म्य) कौन कह सकता है। ऐसे सुहावने तीर्थराज का दर्शन कर सुख के समुद्र रघुकुल श्रेष्ठ श्री रामजी ने भी सुख पाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2478.english_translation: Who can describe the glory of Prayag? It is a lion that destroys the elephant of heaps of sin. Seeing that lovely king of pilgrimages, Ram, the ocean of joy, also felt joy.
ramacharitamanas::2478.translation_literal: को (who) / कहि (to say) / सकइ (can) / प्रयाग (Prayag) / प्रभाऊ (power, glory) / कलुष (sin, impurity) / पुंज (heap) / कुंजर (elephant) / मृगराऊ (lion) / अस (such) / तीरथपति (lord of holy places) / देखि (seeing) / सुहावा (pleasing, lovely) / सुख (joy) / सागर (ocean) / रघुबर (best of the Raghu line, Ram) / सुखु (joy) / पावा (found, received)
ramacharitamanas::2478.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2478.essence: Some sacred places cleanse you before you even ask.
ramacharitamanas::2478.simple_meaning: Prayag is praised as a powerful sacred place that destroys heavy impurities. Even Ram felt joy at seeing it.
ramacharitamanas::2478.simple_insight: Some places do not just receive you; they change what you carry.
ramacharitamanas::2478.detailed_meaning: Ram has reached Prayag in exile and is seeing the confluence and sacred landscape for himself. Tulsidas pauses the journey to praise the place’s cleansing power, showing that even Ram delights in its presence before the next blessing is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2478.modern_relevance: You step into a riverside town after months of noise, and your chest loosens before anyone speaks. Some places quiet the mind simply by being what they are.
ramacharitamanas::2478.insight: It shifts attention from travel as movement to travel as purification and reverence.

ramacharitamanas::2479.verse_sanskrit: कहि सिय लखनहि सखहि सुनाई। श्री मुख तीरथराज बड़ाई॥ करि प्रनामु देखत बन बागा। कहत महातम अति अनुरागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2479.verse_hindi: उन्होंने अपने श्रीमुख से सीताजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सखा गुह को तीर्थराज की महिमा कहकर सुनाई। तदनन्तर प्रणाम करके, वन और बगीचों को देखते हुए और बड़े प्रेम से माहात्म्य कहते हुए- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2479.english_translation: He spoke to Sita, Lakshman, and his friend, praising the glory of Prayagraj with his own holy lips. Then he bowed, looked at the forests and gardens, and spoke of its greatness with deep love.
ramacharitamanas::2479.translation_literal: कहि (having said) / सिय (to Sita) / लखनहि (to Lakshman) / सखहि (to the friend) / सुनाई (made hear) / श्री मुख (with holy mouth) / तीरथराज (king of holy places) / बड़ाई (praise) ॥ करि (having done) / प्रनामु (bowing) / देखत (seeing) / बन (forest) / बागा (gardens) / कहत (speaking) / महातम (greatness) / अति (very) / अनुरागा (with love) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2479.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2479.essence: Reverence deepens even a simple arrival.
ramacharitamanas::2479.simple_meaning: Ram lovingly explains the greatness of Prayagraj to Sita, Lakshman, and Guha, then bows and keeps praising the place as he looks around.
ramacharitamanas::2479.simple_insight: Love turns even a place of pilgrimage into something intimate and alive.
ramacharitamanas::2479.detailed_meaning: Ram has reached Prayagraj with Sita, Lakshman, and Guha. Before moving on, he bows and lovingly praises the sacred place, showing reverence rather than haste. The verse slows the journey to reveal Ram's humility and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2479.modern_relevance: You arrive somewhere meaningful and do not rush past it. You pause, bow inwardly, and let gratitude shape how you look at the place.
ramacharitamanas::2479.insight: It teaches you to meet sacred or meaningful places with reverence, not speed.

ramacharitamanas::2480.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि आइ बिलोकी बेनी। सुमिरत सकल सुमंगल देनी॥ मुदित नहाइ कीन्हि सिव सेवा। पूजि जथाबिधि तीरथ देवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2480.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार श्री राम ने आकर त्रिवेणी का दर्शन किया, जो स्मरण करने से ही सब सुंदर मंगलों को देने वाली है। फिर आनंदपूर्वक (त्रिवेणी में) स्नान करके शिवजी की सेवा (पूजा) की और विधिपूर्वक तीर्थ देवताओं का पूजन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2480.english_translation: In this way, Ram came and beheld the confluence, which gives all auspiciousness simply by being remembered. Then, rejoicing, he bathed, served Shiva, and worshipped the deities of the sacred place in proper order.
ramacharitamanas::2480.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this manner) / आइ (coming) / बिलोकी (having seen) / बेनी (the confluence) / सुमिरत (remembering) / सकल (all) / सुमंगल (auspicious blessings) / देनी (giving) / मुदित (joyful) / नहाइ (bathing) / कीन्हि (did) / सिव (Shiva) / सेवा (service) / पूजि (worshipping) / जथाबिधि (according to proper method) / तीरथ (sacred place) / देवा (deities)
ramacharitamanas::2480.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2480.essence: Reverence becomes real through careful action.
ramacharitamanas::2480.simple_meaning: Ram reaches the sacred confluence, bathes happily, honors Shiva, and worships the local deities in the proper way.
ramacharitamanas::2480.simple_insight: Even the highest reverence begins with simple, respectful action.
ramacharitamanas::2480.detailed_meaning: Ram arrives at the holy meeting of rivers in Prayag, where the place itself is praised as a giver of auspiciousness. He bathes joyfully, serves Shiva, and performs the proper worship before moving on to meet Bharadwaj.
ramacharitamanas::2480.modern_relevance: You enter a temple or shrine after a long journey, wash your hands, lower your voice, and naturally slow down. Reverence shows up first as careful, respectful action.
ramacharitamanas::2480.insight: It teaches you that devotion is expressed through orderly, humble conduct, not just feeling.

ramacharitamanas::2481.verse_sanskrit: तब प्रभु भारद्वाज पहिं आए। करत दंडवत मुनि उर लाए॥ मुनि मन मोद न कछु कहि जाई। ब्रह्मानंद रासि जनु पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2481.verse_hindi: (स्नान, पूजन आदि सब करके) तब प्रभु श्री रामजी भारद्वाजजी के पास आए। उन्हें दण्डवत करते हुए ही मुनि ने हृदय से लगा लिया। मुनि के मन का आनंद कुछ कहा नहीं जाता। मानो उन्हें ब्रह्मानन्द की राशि मिल गई हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2481.english_translation: Then the Lord came to Bharadwaj. The sage embraced him to his heart as he bowed down. The sage's joy cannot be described. It was as if he had received a treasury of supreme bliss.
ramacharitamanas::2481.translation_literal: तब (then) / प्रभु (the Lord) / भारद्वाज पहिं (to Bharadwaj) / आए (came) / करत (doing) / दंडवत (full prostration) / मुनि (sage) / उर (heart) / लाए (brought/held) / मुनि (the sage's) / मन (mind) / मोद (joy) / न (not) / कछु (anything) / कहि (said) / जाई (can be said) / ब्रह्मानंद (supreme bliss) / रासि (treasury/heap) / जनु (as if) / पाई (received)
ramacharitamanas::2481.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2481.essence: Humility draws down the joy of being fully received.
ramacharitamanas::2481.simple_meaning: Ram arrives before Bharadwaj, bows to him, and the sage hugs him with overwhelming joy. The meeting feels like receiving a treasure of supreme bliss.
ramacharitamanas::2481.simple_insight: There is deep peace in being fully received by someone you revere.
ramacharitamanas::2481.detailed_meaning: After bathing and worship at the river confluence, Ram comes to Bharadwaj's hermitage. He bows low, and the sage pulls him into an embrace. The moment is so charged with devotion that words fail and joy overflows.
ramacharitamanas::2481.modern_relevance: You finally meet the mentor who shaped your life, and they greet you like family. The relief is not in being praised, but in being truly held.
ramacharitamanas::2481.insight: It shifts devotion from distance to intimate meeting: reverence becomes warmth, and humility becomes connection.

ramacharitamanas::2482.verse_sanskrit: दीन्हि असीस मुनीस उर अति अनंदु अस जानि। लोचन गोचर सुकृत फल मनहुँ किए बिधि आनि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2482.verse_hindi: मुनीश्वर भारद्वाजजी ने आशीर्वाद दिया। उनके हृदय में ऐसा जानकर अत्यन्त आनंद हुआ कि आज विधाता ने (श्री सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन राकर) मानो हमारे सम्पूर्ण पुण्यों के फल को लाकर आँखों के सामने कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2482.english_translation: Bharadvaja, the sage-king, gave his blessing and felt immense joy, as if the fruit of all past merit had been brought before his eyes by fate.
ramacharitamanas::2482.translation_literal: दीन्हि (gave) / असीस (blessing) / मुनीस (lord of sages) / उर (in the heart) / अति (very) / अनंदु (joy) / अस (thus) / जानि (knowing) / लोचन (eyes) / गोचर (within sight) / सुकृत (merit) / फल (fruit) / मनहुँ (as if) / किए (made) / बिधि (fate/divine ordering) / आनि (bringing)
ramacharitamanas::2482.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2482.essence: True reward is seeing the beloved before you.
ramacharitamanas::2482.simple_meaning: Bharadvaja blesses Ram and feels overwhelming joy, as though the result of all his good deeds has arrived in visible form.
ramacharitamanas::2482.simple_insight: Deep devotion can make a simple meeting feel like the answer to a lifetime of prayer.
ramacharitamanas::2482.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman have reached Bharadvaja's hermitage after bathing at Prayag. The sage greets them with blessing and wonder, feeling that all his merit has taken visible form in their presence.
ramacharitamanas::2482.modern_relevance: You open the door to someone you have long admired, and the room changes. The relief is not in being noticed — it is in finally being near what you have loved from afar.
ramacharitamanas::2482.insight: It shifts attention from achievement to presence: the highest reward is not possession, but sacred nearness.

ramacharitamanas::2483.verse_sanskrit: कुसल प्रस्न करि आसन दीन्हे। पूजि प्रेम परिपूरन कीन्हे॥ कंद मूल फल अंकुर नीके। दिए आनि मुनि मनहुँ अमी के ॥
ramacharitamanas::2483.verse_hindi: कुशल पूछकर मुनिराज ने उनको आसन दिए और प्रेम सहित पूजन करके उन्हें संतुष्ट कर दिया। फिर मानो अमृत के ही बने हों, ऐसे अच्छे-अच्छे कन्द, मूल, फल और अंकुर लाकर दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2483.english_translation: After asking after their well-being, the sage gave them seats and welcomed them with loving devotion. Then he brought and offered excellent roots, fruits, and sprouts, as if they were nectar itself.
ramacharitamanas::2483.translation_literal: कुसल (well-being) / प्रस्न (inquiry) / करि (having done) / आसन (seats) / दीन्हे (gave) / पूजि (having honored) / प्रेम (love) / परिपूरन (fully filled) / कीन्हे (made) / कंद (roots/tubers) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruits) / अंकुर (sprouts) / नीके (excellent) / दिए (gave) / आनि (bringing) / मुनि (sage) / मनहुँ (as if) / अमी (nectar) / के (of)
ramacharitamanas::2483.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2483.essence: Love proves itself by how it welcomes and nourishes.
ramacharitamanas::2483.simple_meaning: Bharadwaj welcomes Ram warmly, gives him a seat, and offers simple forest food with great love.
ramacharitamanas::2483.simple_insight: Respect becomes real when it feeds and shelters the person in front of you.
ramacharitamanas::2483.detailed_meaning: Ram has reached Bharadwaj's hermitage in Ayodhya's exile journey. The sage does not just greet him; he offers a seat, honors him, and brings forest food with affection. The scene shows hospitality as devotion in action before the deeper conversation begins.
ramacharitamanas::2483.modern_relevance: A guest arrives tired at your door after a long train ride, and you stop everything to sit them down, pour water, and bring what you have. Love becomes visible in the welcome.
ramacharitamanas::2483.insight: It teaches you to turn reverence into practical care: seating, feeding, and honoring the person before you.

ramacharitamanas::2484.verse_sanskrit: सीय लखन जन सहित सुहाए। अति रुचि राम मूल फल खाए॥ भए बिगतश्रम रामु सुखारे। भारद्वाज मृदु बचन उचारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2484.verse_hindi: सीताजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सेवक गुह सहित श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने उन सुंदर मूल-फलों को बड़ी रुचि के साथ खाया। थकावट दूर होने से श्री रामचन्द्रजी सुखी हो गए। तब भारद्वाजजी ने उनसे कोमल वचन कहे- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2484.english_translation: Sita, Lakshman, and the devoted companion Guha gladly ate the roots and fruits. When Ram was free from fatigue and refreshed, Bharadwaj spoke gentle words.
ramacharitamanas::2484.translation_literal: सीय (Sita) / लखन (Lakshman) / जन सहित (along with the companion) / सुहाए (pleasantly) / अति रुचि (with great relish) / राम (Ram) / मूल फल (roots and fruits) / खाए (ate) / भए (became) / बिगतश्रम (free from fatigue) / रामु (Ram) / सुखारे (refreshed) / भारद्वाज (Bharadwaj) / मृदु बचन (gentle words) / उचारे (spoke)
ramacharitamanas::2484.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2484.essence: Simple food and kind company restore the weary traveler.
ramacharitamanas::2484.simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, Lakshman, and Guha eat simple forest food after travel. Once Ram is rested, Bharadwaj speaks kindly to him.
ramacharitamanas::2484.simple_insight: Even the humblest meal can feel sacred when shared with love and ease.
ramacharitamanas::2484.detailed_meaning: At Bharadwaj's hermitage, Ram, Sita, Lakshman, and Guha eat roots and fruits with delight after the strain of travel. Ram's fatigue fades, and only then does Bharadwaj begin his gentle, respectful speech.
ramacharitamanas::2484.modern_relevance: After a long walk in the heat, you finally sit under a tree and share simple food with people who care for you. The relief itself becomes a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2484.insight: It slows the scene and shows that care begins with rest, nourishment, and gentle speech.

ramacharitamanas::2485.verse_sanskrit: आजु सफल तपु तीरथ त्यागू। आजु सुफल जप जोग बिरागू॥ सफल सकल सुभ साधन साजू। राम तुम्हहि अवलोकत आजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2485.verse_hindi: हे राम! आपका दर्शन करते ही आज मेरा तप, तीर्थ सेवन और त्याग सफल हो गया। आज मेरा जप, योग और वैराग्य सफल हो गया और आज मेरे सम्पूर्ण शुभ साधनों का समुदाय भी सफल हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2485.english_translation: O Ram, seeing you today has made my austerity, pilgrimages, and renunciation fruitful. Today my chanting, yoga, and detachment have become fruitful, and all my auspicious practices have succeeded.
ramacharitamanas::2485.translation_literal: आजु (today) / सफल (fruitful) / तपु (austerity) / तीरथ (pilgrimage) / त्यागू (renunciation) / आजु (today) / सुफल (well-fruited) / जप (chanting) / जोग (yoga) / बिरागू (detachment) / सफल (fruitful) / सकल (all) / सुभ (auspicious) / साधन (practices) / साजू (array) / राम (Ram) / तुम्हहि (you) / अवलोकत (seeing) / आजू (today)
ramacharitamanas::2485.speaker: Bharadvaja
ramacharitamanas::2485.essence: Ram's presence is the completion every practice was reaching for.
ramacharitamanas::2485.simple_meaning: Meeting Ram makes every spiritual practice complete. Austerity, pilgrimage, chanting, yoga, and detachment all find their fulfillment in his presence.
ramacharitamanas::2485.simple_insight: The deepest relief is not in perfect practice, but in the presence that makes practice complete.
ramacharitamanas::2485.detailed_meaning: At Bharadvaja's hermitage, Ram, Sita, and Lakshman arrive after the forest journey. The sage is overwhelmed, not by ritual success, but by the living presence before him. He declares that every discipline of his life has now borne fruit.
ramacharitamanas::2485.modern_relevance: You finish the retreat, the long prayers, the disciplined habits — and then one quiet moment with the person you love makes everything feel complete.
ramacharitamanas::2485.insight: It shifts devotion from technique to fulfillment: practice matters, but presence is the real completion.

ramacharitamanas::2486.verse_sanskrit: लाभ अवधि सुख अवधि न दूजी। तुम्हरें दरस आस सब पूजी॥ अब करि कृपा देहु बर एहू। निज पद सरसिज सहज सनेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2486.verse_hindi: लाभ की सीमा और सुख की सीमा (प्रभु के दर्शन को छोड़कर) दूसरी कुछ भी नहीं है। आपके दर्शन से मेरी सब आशाएँ पूर्ण हो गईं। अब कृपा करके यह वरदान दीजिए कि आपके चरण कमलों में मेरा स्वाभाविक प्रेम हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2486.english_translation: There is no greater gain and no greater happiness than your sight. Seeing you has fulfilled all my hopes. Now, please grant this blessing: natural love for your lotus feet.
ramacharitamanas::2486.translation_literal: लाभ (gain) / अवधि (limit) / सुख (happiness) / अवधि (limit) / न (not) / दूजी (other) / तुम्हरें (your) / दरस (sight) / आस (hope) / सब (all) / पूजी (fulfilled) / अब (now) / करि (doing) / कृपा (grace) / देहु (give) / बर (boon) / एहू (this) / निज (own) / पद (feet) / सरसिज (lotus) / सहज (natural) / सनेहू (love)
ramacharitamanas::2486.speaker: Bharadvaja
ramacharitamanas::2486.essence: Ram's sight is the highest gain; everything else becomes secondary.
ramacharitamanas::2486.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram is the highest gain and joy. Bharadvaja says all his hopes are fulfilled, and he asks for one blessing: natural love for Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::2486.simple_insight: Real fulfillment is not getting more things, but loving what is holy with ease and sincerity.
ramacharitamanas::2486.detailed_meaning: Bharadvaja has welcomed Ram, Sita, and Lakshman with reverence and now speaks from the fullness of that encounter. He says no gain or happiness can exceed Ram's sight, and then asks for the one thing that matters most: effortless love at Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::2486.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you have admired for years, and the room goes quiet. No achievement on your list feels as complete as that moment. What you ask for next is not more success, but a heart that can love without strain.
ramacharitamanas::2486.insight: It shifts desire from external reward to steady devotion, and from admiration to intimate love.

ramacharitamanas::2487.verse_sanskrit: करम बचन मन छाड़ि छलु जब लगि जनु न तुम्हार। तब लगि सुखु सपनेहुँ नहीं किएँ कोटि उपचार ॥
ramacharitamanas::2487.verse_hindi: जब तक कर्म, वचन और मन से छल छोड़कर मनुष्य आपका दास नहीं हो जाता, तब तक करोड़ों उपाय करने से भी, स्वप्न में भी वह सुख नहीं पाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2487.english_translation: Until a person lets go of deceit in action, speech, and mind and becomes your servant, even millions of efforts bring no peace, not even in a dream.
ramacharitamanas::2487.translation_literal: करम (action) / बचन (speech) / मन (mind) / छाड़ि (leaving) / छलु (deceit) / जब लगि (until) / जनु (person) / न (not) / तुम्हार (yours) / तब लगि (until then) / सुखु (happiness) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / नहीं (not) / किएँ (doing) / कोटि (crores of) / उपचार (remedies, efforts)
ramacharitamanas::2487.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2487.essence: No remedy works until your whole being turns toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2487.simple_meaning: Real peace comes only when you stop being divided between what you do, say, and think, and fully belong to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2487.simple_insight: It feels relieving to know that inner honesty matters more than endless fixes.
ramacharitamanas::2487.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands before Ram in Ayodhya, overwhelmed by longing and humility. After praising Ram's feet, he admits that no amount of ritual or effort can satisfy the heart unless deceit is gone and complete devotion has begun.
ramacharitamanas::2487.modern_relevance: You keep apologizing, explaining, and trying new fixes after hurting someone you love. But until your actions, words, and intentions line up, the relationship still feels broken.
ramacharitamanas::2487.insight: It shifts attention from external remedies to inner integrity and wholehearted surrender.

ramacharitamanas::2488.verse_sanskrit: सुनि मुनि बचन रामु सकुचाने। भाव भगति आनंद अघाने॥ तब रघुबर मुनि सुजसु सुहावा। कोटि भाँति कहि सबहि सुनावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2488.verse_hindi: मुनि के वचन सुनकर, उनकी भाव-भक्ति के कारण आनंद से तृप्त हुए भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी (लीला की दृष्टि से) सकुचा गए। तब (अपने ऐश्वर्य को छिपाते हुए) श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने भारद्वाज मुनि का सुंदर सुयश करोड़ों (अनेकों) प्रकार से कहकर सबको सुनाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2488.english_translation: Hearing the sage's words, Ram was bashful, yet full of devotion and joy. Then Raghubar lovingly praised the sage's noble fame in countless ways and told everyone.
ramacharitamanas::2488.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (sage) / बचन (words) / रामु (Ram) / सकुचाने (felt bashful) / भाव (devotion, feeling) / भगति (devotion) / आनंद (joy) / अघाने (were filled) / तब (then) / रघुबर (Raghubar, Ram) / मुनि (sage) / सुजसु (noble fame) / सुहावा (lovely) / कोटि भाँति (in countless ways) / कहि (having said) / सबहि (to everyone) / सुनावा (made heard)
ramacharitamanas::2488.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2488.essence: Love bows even when the world tries to lift it up.
ramacharitamanas::2488.simple_meaning: Ram hears the sage with loving joy, then humbly praises the sage's good name before everyone.
ramacharitamanas::2488.simple_insight: Real devotion makes pride soften and praise come naturally.
ramacharitamanas::2488.detailed_meaning: In Bharadvaj's presence, Ram hears the sage's words and feels both joy and gentle bashfulness. Instead of accepting praise, he turns to honoring the sage's noble fame, showing how true greatness bows before devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2488.modern_relevance: Someone compliments you in a room full of people, and you feel the urge to deflect instead of absorb it. Humility isn't shrinking — it's letting love move through you without self-importance.
ramacharitamanas::2488.insight: It shifts attention from receiving praise to honoring the one who offered it.

ramacharitamanas::2489.verse_sanskrit: सो बड़ सो सब गुन गन गेहू। जेहि मुनीस तुम्ह आदर देहू॥ मुनि रघुबीर परसपर नवहीं। बचन अगोचर सुखु अनुभवहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2489.verse_hindi: (उन्होंने कहा-) हे मुनीश्वर! जिसको आप आदर दें, वही बड़ा है और वही सब गुण समूहों का घर है। इस प्रकार श्री रामजी और मुनि भारद्वाजजी दोनों परस्पर विनम्र हो रहे हैं और अनिर्वचनीय सुख का अनुभव कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2489.english_translation: The one you honor is truly great and the home of every virtue. In that way, Rama and the sage Bharadvaja bow to each other and taste wordless joy.
ramacharitamanas::2489.translation_literal: सो (that) / बड़ (great) / सो (that) / सब (all) / गुन गन (clusters of virtues) / गेहू (home) / जेहि (whom) / मुनीस (sage-lord) / तुम्ह (you) / आदर (honour) / देहू (give)॥ / मुनि (sage) / रघुबीर (Rama) / परसपर (mutually) / नवहीं (bow) / बचन (speech) / अगोचर (beyond words) / सुखु (joy) / अनुभवहीं (experience)॥
ramacharitamanas::2489.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2489.essence: True greatness bows, and that humility itself becomes joy.
ramacharitamanas::2489.simple_meaning: True greatness lies in humility. Rama and the sage honor each other, and that mutual respect creates a joy beyond words.
ramacharitamanas::2489.simple_insight: You do not lose dignity by honoring others; you often discover deeper joy there.
ramacharitamanas::2489.detailed_meaning: At Bharadvaja's hermitage, Rama meets the sage with perfect courtesy. Neither claims superiority. Their mutual bowing becomes the real event, and the atmosphere fills with a joy that cannot be spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2489.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is trying to seem important. Then one person quietly gives credit away, and the whole room softens. That is the kind of dignity this verse honors.
ramacharitamanas::2489.insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing that respect can be the source of joy.

ramacharitamanas::2490.verse_sanskrit: यह सुधि पाइ प्रयाग निवासी। बटु तापस मुनि सिद्ध उदासी॥ भारद्वाज आश्रम सब आए। देखन दसरथ सुअन सुहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2490.verse_hindi: यह (श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीताजी के आने की) खबर पाकर प्रयाग निवासी ब्रह्मचारी, तपस्वी, मुनि, सिद्ध और उदासी सब श्री दशरथजी के सुंदर पुत्रों को देखने के लिए भारद्वाजजी के आश्रम पर आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2490.english_translation: Hearing this news, the people of Prayag—celibates, ascetics, sages, perfected ones, and renunciates—came to Bharadvaja's hermitage to see the beautiful sons of Dasharath.
ramacharitamanas::2490.translation_literal: यह (this) / सुधि (news) / पाइ (having received) / प्रयाग (Prayag) / निवासी (residents) / बटु (celibates) / तापस (ascetics) / मुनि (sages) / सिद्ध (perfected ones) / उदासी (renunciates) / भारद्वाज (Bharadvaja) / आश्रम (hermitage) / सब (all) / आए (came) / देखन (to see) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / सुअन (sons) / सुहाए (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::2490.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2490.essence: Their arrival alone is enough to gather saints from everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::2490.simple_meaning: News of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita's arrival spreads quickly, and holy people rush to Bharadvaja's hermitage to see them.
ramacharitamanas::2490.simple_insight: Some presences draw people without effort. Reverence itself becomes movement.
ramacharitamanas::2490.detailed_meaning: In Prayag, word spreads that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita have arrived. Celibates, ascetics, sages, perfected beings, and renunciates all gather at Bharadvaja's hermitage, eager to see Dasharath's beautiful sons. The verse simply sets the scene for their arrival.
ramacharitamanas::2490.modern_relevance: A rumor lands in a group chat before sunrise, and by noon everyone is rearranging plans just to catch a glimpse. Some people create their own gravity.
ramacharitamanas::2490.insight: It shifts attention from the crowd's reaction to the quiet magnetism of Ram's presence.

ramacharitamanas::2491.verse_sanskrit: राम प्रनाम कीन्ह सब काहू। मुदित भए लहि लोयन लाहू॥ देहिं असीस परम सुखु पाई। फिरे सराहत सुंदरताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2491.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सब किसी को प्रणाम किया। नेत्रों का लाभ पाकर सब आनंदित हो गए और परम सुख पाकर आशीर्वाद देने लगे। श्री रामजी के सौंदर्य की सराहना करते हुए वे लौटे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2491.english_translation: Ram bowed to everyone. They were delighted to behold him, received the greatest joy, gave blessings, and returned praising his beauty.
ramacharitamanas::2491.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / प्रनाम (bowed respectfully) / कीन्ह (did) / सब (all) / काहू (to everyone) / मुदित (delighted) / भए (became) / लहि (having received) / लोयन (eyes) / लाहू (profit, gain) / देहिं (give) / असीस (blessings) / परम (supreme) / सुखु (joy) / पाई (having received) / फिरे (returned) / सराहत (praising) / सुंदरताई (beauty)
ramacharitamanas::2491.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2491.essence: Real greatness makes everyone else feel honoured.
ramacharitamanas::2491.simple_meaning: Ram greets everyone humbly, and everyone feels deeply blessed just by seeing him. They leave praising his beauty.
ramacharitamanas::2491.simple_insight: A humble presence can give others more joy than words ever could.
ramacharitamanas::2491.detailed_meaning: At Prayag, Ram, Lakshman, and Sita meet holy people gathered around Bharadwaj's hermitage. Ram bows to everyone first. The sages are so moved by his presence that they bless him, rejoice, and leave still admiring him.
ramacharitamanas::2491.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm humility changes the whole room. Nobody feels smaller around them; everyone leaves lighter, kinder, and strangely grateful.
ramacharitamanas::2491.insight: It shows how true greatness bows first and lifts others by simple presence.

ramacharitamanas::2492.verse_sanskrit: राम कीन्ह बिश्राम निसि प्रात प्रयाग नहाइ। चले सहितसिय लखन जन मुदित मुनिहि सिरु नाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2492.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने रात को वहीं विश्राम किया और प्रातःकाल प्रयागराज का स्नान करके और प्रसन्नता के साथ मुनि को सिर नवाकर श्री सीताजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सेवक गुह के साथ वे चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2492.english_translation: Ram rested there through the night, bathed at Prayag at dawn, and then departed happily with Sita, Lakshman, and the servant Guha after bowing to the sage.
ramacharitamanas::2492.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / कीन्ह (did) / बिश्राम (rest) / निसि (night) / प्रात (morning) / प्रयाग (Prayag) / नहाइ (having bathed) / चले (departed) / सहितसिय (with Sita) / लखन (Lakshman) / जन (servant) / मुदित (joyful) / मुनिहि (to the sage) / सिरु (head) / नाइ (bowing)
ramacharitamanas::2492.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2492.essence: The journey continues with grace, not hurry.
ramacharitamanas::2492.simple_meaning: Ram spends the night at Prayag, bathes in the morning, bows to the sage, and leaves with Sita, Lakshman, and Guha.
ramacharitamanas::2492.simple_insight: Even a journey can be carried with calm respect and quiet joy.
ramacharitamanas::2492.detailed_meaning: After meeting the sages at Prayag, Ram stays the night, takes the morning bath, and leaves with Sita, Lakshman, and Guha. The verse simply moves the story forward, showing gracious travel before the next exchange with the sage.
ramacharitamanas::2492.modern_relevance: You leave a guesthouse at dawn after a long trip, pack quietly, thank the host, and step back into the road without drama.
ramacharitamanas::2492.insight: It keeps attention on the movement of the story, not on a separate teaching.

ramacharitamanas::2493.verse_sanskrit: राम सप्रेम कहेउ मुनि पाहीं। नाथ कहिअ हम केहि मग जाहीं॥ मुनि मन बिहसि राम सन कहहीं। सुगम सकल मग तुम्ह कहुँ अहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2493.verse_hindi: (चलते समय) बड़े प्रेम से श्री रामजी ने मुनि से कहा- हे नाथ! बताइए हम किस मार्ग से जाएँ। मुनि मन में हँसकर श्री रामजी से कहते हैं कि आपके लिए सभी मार्ग सुगम हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2493.english_translation: With deep affection, Ram asked the sage, “Lord, which road should we take?” The sage smiled inwardly and said to Ram, “For you, every road is easy.”
ramacharitamanas::2493.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सप्रेम (with affection) / कहेउ (said) / मुनि (sage) / पाहीं (to) / नाथ (lord) / कहिअ (tell) / हम (we) / केहि (which) / मग (road) / जाहीं (go) / मुनि (sage) / मन (mind) / बिहसि (smiled) / राम (Ram) / सन (to) / कहहीं (said) / सुगम (easy) / सकल (all) / मग (roads) / तुम्ह (you) / कहुँ (for) / अहहीं (are)
ramacharitamanas::2493.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2493.essence: Right guidance makes every path workable.
ramacharitamanas::2493.simple_meaning: Ram asks the sage which path to take, and the sage replies that every path is easy for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2493.simple_insight: You can stop fearing the route when your heart is aligned with the right guide.
ramacharitamanas::2493.detailed_meaning: At Prayag, Ram speaks gently to the sage as he prepares to continue the exile journey with Sita and Lakshman. The sage’s smiling reply shows that for Ram, no path is difficult because his presence makes the journey itself благ.
ramacharitamanas::2493.modern_relevance: You stand at a train platform with three routes on the board, afraid of choosing wrong. This verse says the right presence makes even uncertain roads manageable.
ramacharitamanas::2493.insight: It shifts you from obsessing over the route to trusting the one who walks it with you.

ramacharitamanas::2494.verse_sanskrit: साथ लागि मुनि सिष्य बोलाए। सुनि मन मुदित पचासक आए॥ सबन्हि राम पर प्रेम अपारा। सकल कहहिं मगु दीख हमारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2494.verse_hindi: फिर उनके साथ के लिए मुनि ने शिष्यों को बुलाया। (साथ जाने की बात) सुनते ही चित्त में हर्षित हो कोई पचास शिष्य आ गए। सभी का श्री रामजी पर अपार प्रेम है। सभी कहते हैं कि मार्ग हमारा देखा हुआ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2494.english_translation: Then the sage called his disciples to go along. Hearing this, about fifty disciples came joyfully in their minds. All of them had immense love for Ram. All said, "We know the path well."
ramacharitamanas::2494.translation_literal: साथ (along) / लागि (for) / मुनि (the sage) / सिष्य (disciples) / बोलाए (called) । / सुनि (hearing) / मन (mind) / मुदित (joyful) / पचासक (fifty) / आए (came) ॥ / सबन्हि (all) / राम (Ram) / पर (toward) / प्रेम (love) / अपारा (boundless) । / सकल (all) / कहहिं (say) / मगु (path) / दीख (seen) / हमारा (ours) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2494.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2494.essence: Love for Ram makes even guidance feel like service.
ramacharitamanas::2494.simple_meaning: The sage gathers his disciples, and many come gladly. They all love Ram deeply and say they know the route.
ramacharitamanas::2494.simple_insight: Shared devotion makes service feel natural, even eager.
ramacharitamanas::2494.detailed_meaning: At Prayag, Ram asks the sage which road to take next. The sage calls his disciples, and many rush forward happily. Their love for Ram is so strong that they all claim to know the way.
ramacharitamanas::2494.modern_relevance: A friend says, “I need help moving this weekend,” and suddenly people you barely expected show up without complaint. Love makes guidance and service feel easy.
ramacharitamanas::2494.insight: It shows how devotion turns ordinary help into willing participation.

ramacharitamanas::2495.verse_sanskrit: मुनि बटु चारि संग तब दीन्हे। जिन्ह बहु जनम सुकृत सब कीन्हे॥ करि प्रनामु रिषि आयसु पाई। प्रमुदित हृदयँ चले रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2495.verse_hindi: तब मुनि ने (चुनकर) चार ब्रह्मचारियों को साथ कर दिया, जिन्होंने बहुत जन्मों तक सब सुकृत (पुण्य) किए थे। श्री रघुनाथजी प्रणाम कर और ऋषि की आज्ञा पाकर हृदय में बड़े ही आनंदित होकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2495.english_translation: Then the sage assigned four young brahmacharis to accompany them, men who had earned merit through many births. After bowing and receiving the sage's permission, Raghunath set out with great joy in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::2495.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / बटु (young brahmacharis) / चारि (four) / संग (with) / तब (then) / दीन्हे (gave/assigned) / जिन्ह (who) / बहु (many) / जनम (births) / सुकृत (merit) / सब (all) / कीन्हे (did) / करि (having done) / प्रनामु (bow) / रिषि (sage) / आयसु (permission/command) / पाई (having received) / प्रमुदित (joyful) / हृदयँ (in heart) / चले (went) / रघुराई (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::2495.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2495.essence: Joy deepens when you accept guidance with humility.
ramacharitamanas::2495.simple_meaning: The sage sends four devoted students to accompany Ram. Ram bows, receives the sage's permission, and leaves happily.
ramacharitamanas::2495.simple_insight: True joy can come from humble permission, not from control.
ramacharitamanas::2495.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sage has already welcomed Ram and offered guidance. Now he sends four disciplined students to travel with him. Ram bows first, accepts the sage's order, and moves on in delight. The scene shows reverence, service, and cheerful obedience.
ramacharitamanas::2495.modern_relevance: You finally get the green light from someone you respect, and the whole task feels lighter. The work hasn't changed — but your heart has.
ramacharitamanas::2495.insight: It teaches you to begin with respect, then move forward without resistance.

ramacharitamanas::2496.verse_sanskrit: ग्राम निकट जब निकसहिं जाई। देखहिं दरसु नारि नर धाई॥ होहिं सनाथ जनम फलु पाई। फिरहिं दुखित मनु संग पठाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2496.verse_hindi: जब वे किसी गाँव के पास होकर निकलते हैं, तब स्त्री-पुरुष दौड़कर उनके रूप को देखने लगते हैं। जन्म का फल पाकर वे (सदा के अनाथ) सनाथ हो जाते हैं और मन को नाथ के साथ भेजकर (शरीर से साथ न रहने के कारण) दुःखी होकर लौट आते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2496.english_translation: When they pass near a village, men and women run to behold their sight. Having gained the fruit of human birth, they feel sheltered, and then return sorrowful, sending their minds away with the Lord.
ramacharitamanas::2496.translation_literal: ग्राम (village) / निकट (near) / जब (when) / निकसहिं (they go out) / जाई (having gone) / देखहिं (they see) / दरसु (darshan, sight) / नारि (women) / नर (men) / धाई (running) / होहिं (they become) / सनाथ (with a sheltering lord) / जनम (birth) / फलु (fruit) / पाई (having obtained) / फिरहिं (they return) / दुखित (sorrowful) / मनु (mind) / संग (with) / पठाई (sent)
ramacharitamanas::2496.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2496.essence: Ram's sight gives shelter, and separation turns that blessing into longing.
ramacharitamanas::2496.simple_meaning: Just seeing Ram fills people with a sense of being protected and fulfilled, but because they cannot stay with him, they return with sad hearts.
ramacharitamanas::2496.simple_insight: Real closeness can leave you softer, not smaller.
ramacharitamanas::2496.detailed_meaning: As Ram and the four young seekers pass near villages, men and women rush out just to catch his sight. In that single glimpse, they feel their life has been fulfilled and their loneliness lifted, yet they must leave him and return in longing.
ramacharitamanas::2496.modern_relevance: You leave a room after meeting someone whose presence felt unmistakably safe. The conversation was brief, but the ache of returning to ordinary life tells you it mattered.
ramacharitamanas::2496.insight: It shifts devotion from idea to experience: even a moment of true presence can transform how you carry absence.

ramacharitamanas::2497.verse_sanskrit: बिदा किए बटु बिनय करि फिरे पाइ मन काम। उतरि नहाए जमुन जल जो सरीर सम स्याम ॥
ramacharitamanas::2497.verse_hindi: तदनन्तर श्री रामजी ने विनती करके चारों ब्रह्मचारियों को विदा किया, वे मनचाही वस्तु (अनन्य भक्ति) पाकर लौटे। यमुनाजी के पार उतरकर सबने यमुनाजी के जल में स्नान किया, जो श्री रामचन्द्रजी के शरीर के समान ही श्याम रंग का था ॥
ramacharitamanas::2497.english_translation: Then Ram bade farewell to the four brahmacharis with blessings. Crossing over, they bathed in the Yamuna, whose dark water matched Ram's own dark form.
ramacharitamanas::2497.translation_literal: बिदा किए (sent off) / बटु (brahmacharis) / बिनय करि (with humility) / फिरे (they returned) / पाइ (having obtained) / मन काम (the heart's desired thing) / उतरि (crossing down) / नहाए (bathed) / जमुन जल (Yamuna water) / जो (which) / सरीर सम (like the body) / स्याम (dark, blue-black)
ramacharitamanas::2497.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2497.essence: Meeting Ram leaves the heart already full.
ramacharitamanas::2497.simple_meaning: Ram sends the four students away with kindness, and they feel fulfilled. They then cross the Yamuna and bathe in its dark water, which resembles Ram's dark complexion.
ramacharitamanas::2497.simple_insight: Even a brief meeting with the beloved can leave you feeling fully blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2497.detailed_meaning: Ram and Sita are moving through the forest, and a small group of brahmacharis has just been given the blessing of a close encounter. After receiving Ram's kindness, they leave fulfilled, cross the Yamuna, and bathe in its dark water before the next wave of villagers arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2497.modern_relevance: You leave a brief visit with someone you deeply admire, and the whole day feels changed. The meeting was short, but it gave you exactly what you needed.
ramacharitamanas::2497.insight: It shows how contact with Ram's presence satisfies longing and turns even ordinary places into reminders of him.

ramacharitamanas::2498.verse_sanskrit: सुनत तीरबासी नर नारी। धाए निज निज काज बिसारी॥ लखन राम सिय सुंदरताई। देखि करहिं निज भाग्य बड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2498.verse_hindi: यमुनाजी के किनारे पर रहने वाले स्त्री-पुरुष (यह सुनकर कि निषाद के साथ दो परम सुंदर सुकुमार नवयुवक और एक परम सुंदरी स्त्री आ रही है) सब अपना-अपना काम भूलकर दौड़े और लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामजी और सीताजी का सौंदर्य देखकर अपने भाग्य की बड़ाई करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2498.english_translation: Hearing this, the men and women living by the Yamuna ran, forgetting their own tasks. Seeing the beauty of Lakshman, Ram, and Sita, they praised their own good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::2498.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / तीरबासी (riverbank dwellers) / नर नारी (men and women) / धाए (ran) / निज निज (their own) / काज (tasks) / बिसारी (forgot)॥ / लखन (Lakshman) / राम (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / सुंदरताई (beauty) / देखि (seeing) / करहिं (do) / निज (their own) / भाग्य (fortune) / बड़ाई (praise)
ramacharitamanas::2498.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2498.essence: Their beauty makes people forget everything else.
ramacharitamanas::2498.simple_meaning: People by the river forget their work and rush to see Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Their beauty makes them feel blessed just to have seen them.
ramacharitamanas::2498.simple_insight: Some presence is so moving that ordinary life stops for a moment.
ramacharitamanas::2498.detailed_meaning: As Ram, Lakshman, and Sita travel by the Yamuna, the riverbank villagers hear they are near and rush out, abandoning their chores. Their first response is wonder; their second is gratitude at having seen them.
ramacharitamanas::2498.modern_relevance: You hear a beloved teacher, artist, or elder has arrived nearby, and you leave your half-finished work to catch one glimpse. Some meetings feel like a gift before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2498.insight: It shows how awe can interrupt routine and turn attention toward what feels sacred or rare.

ramacharitamanas::2499.verse_sanskrit: अति लालसा बसहिं मन माहीं। नाउँ गाउँ बूझत सकुचाहीं॥ जे तिन्ह महुँ बयबिरिध सयाने। तिन्ह करि जुगुति रामु पहिचाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::2499.verse_hindi: उनके मन में (परिचय जानने की) बहुत सी लालसाएँ भरी हैं। पर वे नाम-गाँव पूछते सकुचाते हैं। उन लोगों में जो वयोवृद्ध और चतुर थे, उन्होंने युक्ति से श्री रामचन्द्रजी को पहचान लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2499.english_translation: Their minds were full of eager curiosity, yet they felt shy to ask the names and village. Among them, the older and wiser ones recognized Ram through clever discernment.
ramacharitamanas::2499.translation_literal: अति (very much) / लालसा (eager longing) / बसहिं (they dwell) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / नाउँ (name) / गाउँ (village) / बूझत (asking) / सकुचाहीं (they feel shy) / जे (those who) / तिन्ह महुँ (among them) / बयबिरिध (aged) / सयाने (wise) / तिन्ह करि (by them, through) / जुगुति (skillful means) / रामु (Ram) / पहिचाने (recognized)
ramacharitamanas::2499.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2499.essence: The wise recognize what shy curiosity cannot ask aloud.
ramacharitamanas::2499.simple_meaning: People are curious about the strangers, but they hesitate to ask directly. The older and wiser ones figure out that they are Ram and his companions.
ramacharitamanas::2499.simple_insight: Quiet observation can reveal what direct questioning misses.
ramacharitamanas::2499.detailed_meaning: At the Yamuna bank, villagers have gathered around Ram, Sita, and Lakshman. Their hearts are eager, but they are too shy to ask who these radiant visitors are. A few older, shrewder people read the signs and recognize Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2499.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence feels important, but you hesitate to ask the obvious question. Someone older in the room notices the clues first and names what everyone else only senses.
ramacharitamanas::2499.insight: It shifts attention from open curiosity to careful reading of signs and context.

ramacharitamanas::2500.verse_sanskrit: सकल कथा तिन्ह सबहि सुनाई। बनहि चले पितु आयसु पाई॥ सुनि सबिषाद सकल पछिताहीं। रानी रायँ कीन्ह भल नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2500.verse_hindi: उन्होंने सब कथा सब लोगों को सुनाई कि पिता की आज्ञा पाकर ये वन को चले हैं। यह सुनकर सब लोग दुःखित हो पछता रहे हैं कि रानी और राजा ने अच्छा नहीं किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2500.english_translation: They told everyone the whole story: the sons had gone to the forest after receiving their father's command. Hearing this, everyone was distressed and regretted that the queen and king had done wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2500.translation_literal: सकल (all) / कथा (story) / तिन्ह (they) / सबहि (to everyone) / सुनाई (told) / बनहि (to the forest) / चले (went) / पितु (father's) / आयसु (command) / पाई (having received)॥ सुनि (hearing) / सबिषाद (full of sorrow) / सकल (everyone) / पछिताहीं (regretted) / रानी (queen) / रायँ (king) / कीन्ह (did) / भल (good) / नाहीं (not)॥
ramacharitamanas::2500.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2500.simple_meaning: The news spreads that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita have gone to the forest because of their father's command. Everyone feels sorrow and realises the royal decision was wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2500.simple_insight: Some choices echo beyond the household that made them.
ramacharitamanas::2500.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the truth of the exile reaches the people. They hear that the princes left only because Dasharath's word had to be kept, and grief spreads through the city. The verse records public sorrow, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2500.modern_relevance: A family decision made behind closed doors can hit the wider circle later — relatives, neighbours, and friends all feel the cost when the truth finally comes out.
ramacharitamanas::2500.insight: It shows how a hidden decision becomes a shared wound once everyone understands it.

ramacharitamanas::2501.verse_sanskrit: तेहि अवसर एक तापसु आवा। तेजपुंज लघुबयस सुहावा॥ कबि अलखित गति बेषु बिरागी। मन क्रम बचन राम अनुरागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2501.verse_hindi: उसी अवसर पर वहाँ एक तपस्वी आया, जो तेज का पुंज, छोटी अवस्था का और सुंदर था। उसकी गति कवि नहीं जानते (अथवा वह कवि था जो अपना परिचय नहीं देना चाहता)। वह वैरागी के वेष में था और मन, वचन तथा कर्म से श्री रामचन्द्रजी का प्रेमी था ॥
ramacharitamanas::2501.english_translation: At that moment, a renunciate arrived — radiant, youthful, and lovely. His movement was poetically indescribable; he wore the garb of a seeker, and in mind, speech, and action he loved Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2501.translation_literal: तेहि (that) / अवसर (occasion) / एक (one) / तापसु (ascetic) / आवा (came) / तेजपुंज (bundle of radiance) / लघुबयस (young in age) / सुहावा (beautiful) / कबि (poet) / अलखित (unseen / indescribable) / गति (movement) / बेषु (garb) / बिरागी (renunciate) / मन (mind) / क्रम (deed) / बचन (speech) / राम (Ram) / अनुरागी (loving devotee)
ramacharitamanas::2501.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2501.essence: Renunciation means little without love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2501.simple_meaning: A young ascetic arrives, glowing with radiance and beauty. He looks like a renunciate, but his mind, words, and actions are all devoted to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2501.simple_insight: True devotion shows up in how you live, not just in how you look.
ramacharitamanas::2501.detailed_meaning: As the people of Ayodhya grieve Ram's exile, a radiant young renunciate appears. His outer appearance suggests detachment, but the verse reveals his real identity through his inner devotion to Ram. The scene is building toward Bharat's meeting with him.
ramacharitamanas::2501.modern_relevance: A quiet person in simple clothes walks into a room where everyone is hurting. No announcement, no performance — but their calm, steady love changes the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::2501.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to inner alignment: the real measure is whether mind, speech, and action point the same way.

ramacharitamanas::2502.verse_sanskrit: सजल नयन तन पुलकि निज इष्टदेउ पहिचानि। परेउ दंड जिमि धरनितल दसा न जाइ बखानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2502.verse_hindi: अपने इष्टदेव को पहचानकर उसके नेत्रों में जल भर आया और शरीर पुलकित हो गया। वह दण्ड की भाँति पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ा, उसकी (प्रेम विह्वल) दशा का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2502.english_translation: His eyes filled with tears, his body thrilled as he recognised his chosen Lord. He fell to the ground like a staff, beyond words to describe.
ramacharitamanas::2502.translation_literal: सजल (moist) / नयन (eyes) / तन (body) / पुलकि (thrilled) / निज (own) / इष्टदेउ (chosen Lord) / पहिचानि (having recognised) / परेउ (fell) / दंड (staff) / जिमि (like) / धरनितल (on the earth's surface) / दसा (state) / न जाइ (cannot be spoken) / बखानि (described)
ramacharitamanas::2502.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2502.essence: Recognition of Ram makes the body fall silent.
