ramacharitamanas::2502.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram, he is overwhelmed with love: tears come, his body shivers, and he falls flat to the ground.
ramacharitamanas::2502.simple_insight: Real devotion can undo pride at once and leave only reverent surrender.
ramacharitamanas::2502.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the disguised sage arrives just as the exiled brothers are being mourned. He recognises Ram as his chosen Lord, and emotion overtakes him completely. This verse captures the body’s surrender before the heart can speak.
ramacharitamanas::2502.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you have long prayed to see, and your whole body reacts before your mind catches up.
ramacharitamanas::2502.insight: It shows devotion as a full-body response that collapses ego and control.

ramacharitamanas::2503.verse_sanskrit: राम सप्रेम पुलकि उर लावा। परम रंक जनु पारसु पावा॥ मनहुँ प्रेमु परमारथु दोऊ। मिलत धरें तन कह सबु कोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2503.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने प्रेमपूर्वक पुलकित होकर उसको हृदय से लगा लिया। (उसे इतना आनंद हुआ) मानो कोई महादरिद्री मनुष्य पारस पा गया हो। सब कोई (देखने वाले) कहने लगे कि मानो प्रेम और परमार्थ (परम तत्व) दोनों शरीर धारण करके मिल रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2503.english_translation: Ram lovingly and with delight embraced him to his chest. It was as if a poor man had found a touchstone. Everyone watching said it was as though love and the highest reality had taken form and met in one body.
ramacharitamanas::2503.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सप्रेम (with love) / पुलकि (thrilled) / उर (chest) / लावा (embraced) / परम (supreme) / रंक (poor man) / जनु (as if) / पारसु (touchstone) / पावा (found) / मनहुँ (as if) / प्रेमु (love) / परमारथु (highest reality) / दोऊ (both) / मिलत (meeting) / धरें (took form) / तन (body) / कह (said) / सबु (everyone) / कोऊ (someone)
ramacharitamanas::2503.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2503.essence: True devotion makes meeting the divine feel like finding a priceless treasure.
ramacharitamanas::2503.simple_meaning: Ram embraces the devotee with joy, and the moment feels like meeting the greatest treasure. Love and ultimate truth seem to become visible together.
ramacharitamanas::2503.simple_insight: Being met with love can feel like finding everything you were missing.
ramacharitamanas::2503.detailed_meaning: The unknown ascetic has just revealed himself as Ram's devotee, and Ram responds instantly with tenderness. In front of everyone, the meeting becomes more than a reunion: it looks like love itself and the highest reality have taken human form.
ramacharitamanas::2503.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone who has carried you in their heart for years, and the room changes. The relief is not just being recognized — it is being loved without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::2503.insight: It shifts devotion from idea to lived encounter: love becomes something you can receive in the body.

ramacharitamanas::2504.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि लखन पायन्ह सोइ लागा। लीन्ह उठाइ उमगि अनुरागा॥ पुनि सिय चरन धूरि धरि सीसा। जननि जानि सिसु दीन्हि असीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2504.verse_hindi: फिर वह लक्ष्मणजी के चरणों लगा। उन्होंने प्रेम से उमंगकर उसको उठा लिया। फिर उसने सीताजी की चरण धूलि को अपने सिर पर धारण किया। माता सीताजी ने भी उसको अपना बच्चा जानकर आशीर्वाद दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2504.english_translation: Then he fell at Lakshman's feet. Lakshman lifted him up with overflowing affection. Then he placed Sita's dust on his head, and Sita blessed him as a mother blesses her child.
ramacharitamanas::2504.translation_literal: बहुरि (then) / लखन (Lakshman) / पायन्ह (feet) / सोइ (that one) / लागा (fell at) / लीन्ह (took) / उठाइ (lifting up) / उमगि (overflowing) / अनुरागा (with affection) / पुनि (again) / सिय (Sita) / चरन (feet) / धूरि (dust) / धरि (placing) / सीसा (head) / जननि (mother) / जानि (knowing) / सिसु (child) / दीन्हि (gave) / असीसा (blessing)
ramacharitamanas::2504.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2504.essence: Love received in humility becomes blessing, not hierarchy.
ramacharitamanas::2504.simple_meaning: He bows to Lakshman, is lifted up with love, then receives Sita's blessing like a child receiving a mother's care.
ramacharitamanas::2504.simple_insight: Real honour can feel like being welcomed, not being admired.
ramacharitamanas::2504.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the devotee has just reached Ram and collapsed in tears of love. Now Lakshman and Sita respond before any formal words are spoken: one lifts him, the other blesses him. The scene shows how Ram's circle receives sincere devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2504.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a hard week, expecting judgment. Instead, someone helps you up, and someone else treats you like family.
ramacharitamanas::2504.insight: It shifts attention from status to belonging, showing that devotion is answered through human warmth and acceptance.

ramacharitamanas::2505.verse_sanskrit: कीन्ह निषाद दंडवत तेही। मिलेउ मुदित लखि राम सनेही॥ पिअत नयन पुट रूपु पियुषा। मुदित सुअसनु पाइ जिमि भूखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2505.verse_hindi: फिर निषादराज ने उसको दण्डवत की। श्री रामचन्द्रजी का प्रेमी जानकर वह उस (निषाद) से आनंदित होकर मिला। वह तपस्वी अपने नेत्र रूपी दोनों से श्री रामजी की सौंदर्य सुधा का पान करने लगा और ऐसा आनंदित हुआ जैसे कोई भूखा आदमी सुंदर भोजन पाकर आनंदित होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2505.english_translation: Nishad bowed down before him. Seeing Ram's beloved devotee, he met him with delight. He drank in Ram's beauty through the twin cups of his eyes, like a hungry man tasting fine food.
ramacharitamanas::2505.translation_literal: कीन्ह (did) / निषाद (Nishad) / दंडवत (prostration) / तेही (to him) / मिलेउ (met) / मुदित (joyful) / लखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / सनेही (beloved devotee) / पिअत (drinking) / नयन पुट (eye cups) / रूपु (form, beauty) / पियुषा (nectar) / मुदित (delighted) / सुअसनु (good food) / पाइ (having received) / जिमि (like) / भूखा (hungry one)
ramacharitamanas::2505.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2505.essence: Ram's presence nourishes the one who loves him.
ramacharitamanas::2505.simple_meaning: Nishad bows down, and Ram welcomes him warmly. Everyone drinks in Ram's beauty with joy, like a hungry person receiving food.
ramacharitamanas::2505.simple_insight: Love makes even a simple meeting feel like nourishment.
ramacharitamanas::2505.detailed_meaning: On the way to the forest, Ram meets Nishadraj, the loyal boatman-chief who has come in devotion. Nishad bows fully, and Ram receives him with delight. The scene lingers on mutual affection, not action, showing how Ram's presence feeds everyone who loves him.
ramacharitamanas::2505.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you admire after months of distance, and the room changes. Their warmth feels like food after a long fast.
ramacharitamanas::2505.insight: It shifts attention from status to devotion, showing that true welcome is recognition of love.

ramacharitamanas::2506.verse_sanskrit: ते पितु मातु कहहु सखि कैसे। जिन्ह पठए बन बालक ऐसे॥ राम लखन सिय रूपु निहारी। होहिं सनेह बिकल नर नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2506.verse_hindi: (इधर गाँव की स्त्रियाँ कह रही हैं) हे सखी! कहो तो, वे माता-पिता कैसे हैं, जिन्होंने ऐसे (सुंदर सुकुमार) बालकों को वन में भेज दिया है। श्री रामजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी के रूप को देखकर सब स्त्री-पुरुष स्नेह से व्याकुल हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2506.english_translation: O friend, tell me what kind of father and mother sent such tender boys into the forest. Seeing the forms of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, men and women are overcome with affection.
ramacharitamanas::2506.translation_literal: ते (those) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / कहहु (tell) / सखि (friend) / कैसे (how kind) / जिन्ह (who) / पठए (sent) / बन (forest) / बालक (children) / ऐसे (such)॥ / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / रूपु (form) / निहारी (seeing) / होहिं (become) / सनेह (affection) / बिकल (disturbed) / नर (men) / नारी (women) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2506.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2506.essence: Tenderness can make even strangers feel like family.
ramacharitamanas::2506.simple_meaning: The village women are amazed that such tender children were sent into the forest. Just seeing Ram, Lakshman, and Sita makes everyone feel deep affection and distress.
ramacharitamanas::2506.simple_insight: Some forms are so moving that they awaken tenderness before any words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2506.detailed_meaning: In the forest, village women catch sight of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita and cannot stop staring. Their beauty and innocence make them wonder how any parents could send such tender children away. The moment is pure public tenderness, not teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2506.modern_relevance: You see a young family at a train station, one child asleep on a shoulder, and something in you softens. Some sights make the heart ache before the mind can explain why.
ramacharitamanas::2506.insight: It shows how beauty and innocence can disarm judgment and pull the mind into compassion.

ramacharitamanas::2507.verse_sanskrit: तब रघुबीर अनेक बिधि सखहि सिखावनु दीन्ह॥ राम रजायसु सीस धरि भवन गवनु तेइँ कीन्ह ॥
ramacharitamanas::2507.verse_hindi: तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सखा गुह को अनेकों तरह से (घर लौट जाने के लिए) समझाया। श्री रामचन्द्रजी की आज्ञा को सिर चढ़ाकर उसने अपने घर को गमन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2507.english_translation: Then Raghubir counseled his friend in many ways. Keeping Ram's command on his head, he went home.
ramacharitamanas::2507.translation_literal: तब (then) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / अनेक बिधि (in many ways) / सखहि (to the friend) / सिखावनु (instruction / counsel) / दीन्ह (gave)॥ / राम (Ram's) / रजायसु (command) / सीस धरि (placing on the head) / भवन (home) / गवनु (going) / तेइँ (he) / कीन्ह (did) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2507.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2507.essence: Love makes obedience feel natural, not forced.
ramacharitamanas::2507.simple_meaning: Ram gently tells Guha to go back home, and Guha obeys immediately, treating Ram's order as something sacred and final.
ramacharitamanas::2507.simple_insight: There is dignity in obeying what is right without dragging your feet.
ramacharitamanas::2507.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank after the first meeting with Guha, Ram does not let his friend linger in sadness. He explains patiently, and Guha accepts the instruction at once, placing Ram's command above his own wish to stay.
ramacharitamanas::2507.modern_relevance: Your friend keeps trying to stay and help, but the visit is over and the house is already quiet. The loving thing is not to prolong the moment — it is to let them leave in peace.
ramacharitamanas::2507.insight: It shifts obedience from pressure to love, showing that right action can be immediate and wholehearted.

ramacharitamanas::2508.verse_sanskrit: पुनि सियँ राम लखन कर जोरी। जमुनहि कीन्ह प्रनामु बहोरी॥ चले ससीय मुदित दोउ भाई। रबितनुजा कइ करत बड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2508.verse_hindi: फिर सीताजी, श्री रामजी और लक्ष्मणजी ने हाथ जोड़कर यमुनाजी को पुनः प्रणाम किया और सूर्यकन्या यमुनाजी की बड़ाई करते हुए सीताजी सहित दोनों भाई प्रसन्नतापूर्वक आगे चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2508.english_translation: Then Sita, Ram, and Lakshman folded their hands and bowed again to the Yamuna. Praising the daughter of the Sun, they moved on joyfully with Sita, the two brothers continuing ahead.
ramacharitamanas::2508.translation_literal: पुनि (again) / सियँ (with Sita) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined) / जमुनहि (to the Yamuna) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रनामु (bowing) / बहोरी (again)॥ / चले (went) / ससीय (with Sita) / मुदित (joyful) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / रबितनुजा (daughter of the Sun) / कइ (of) / करत (doing) / बड़ाई (praise)॥
ramacharitamanas::2508.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2508.essence: Gratitude and forward motion can move together.
ramacharitamanas::2508.simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman bow to the Yamuna again, praise her, and continue their journey happily.
ramacharitamanas::2508.simple_insight: Even a journey can be full of reverence; gratitude and motion can live together.
ramacharitamanas::2508.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman have crossed into the next stretch of exile. Before moving on, they bow once more to the Yamuna and honor her. The verse simply marks their respectful departure, keeping the journey flowing.
ramacharitamanas::2508.modern_relevance: You leave a place after a hard goodbye, glance back once more, and quietly thank what carried you through. Then you keep walking.
ramacharitamanas::2508.insight: It teaches respectful movement: honor what supports you, then continue without delay.

ramacharitamanas::2509.verse_sanskrit: पथिक अनेक मिलहिं मग जाता। कहहिं सप्रेम देखि दोउ भ्राता॥ राज लखन सब अंग तुम्हारें। देखि सोचु अति हृदय हमारें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2509.verse_hindi: रास्ते में जाते हुए उन्हें अनेकों यात्री मिलते हैं। वे दोनों भाइयों को देखकर उनसे प्रेमपूर्वक कहते हैं कि तुम्हारे सब अंगों में राज चिह्न देखकर हमारे हृदय में बड़ा सोच होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2509.english_translation: Along the road, many travelers meet them. Seeing the two brothers, they speak with love: “The marks of royalty are on all your limbs, and our hearts are filled with deep wonder.”
ramacharitamanas::2509.translation_literal: पथिक (travelers) / अनेक (many) / मिलहिं (meet) / मग (road) / जाता (going) / कहहिं (say) / सप्रेम (with love) / देखि (seeing) / दोउ (both) / भ्राता (brothers) / राज (royal) / लखन (marks) / सब (all) / अंग (limbs) / तुम्हारें (in your) / देखि (seeing) / सोचु (wonder / concern) / अति (very) / हृदय (heart) / हमारें (our)
ramacharitamanas::2509.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2509.essence: Your outer signs can reveal a life out of place.
ramacharitamanas::2509.simple_meaning: Travelers meet Ram and Lakshman on the road and lovingly notice their royal signs. Their hearts fill with wonder at why such noble brothers are walking like this.
ramacharitamanas::2509.simple_insight: Sometimes other people can see the mismatch in your life before you can.
ramacharitamanas::2509.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are moving along the road in exile. Ordinary travelers keep meeting them and, with affection, notice the royal marks on the two brothers. Their surprise deepens the emotional tension before the next verse explains why they are walking on foot.
ramacharitamanas::2509.modern_relevance: You show up in plain clothes to a formal event, and everyone can tell something is off. Their puzzled looks catch the gap between who you are and how you’re being made to live.
ramacharitamanas::2509.insight: It highlights how visible dignity can be, even when circumstances force humility.

ramacharitamanas::2510.verse_sanskrit: मारग चलहु पयादेहि पाएँ। ज्योतिषु झूठ हमारें भाएँ॥ अगमु पंथु गिरि कानन भारी। तेहि महँ साथ नारि सुकुमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2510.verse_hindi: (ऐसे राजचिह्नों के होते हुए भी) तुम लोग रास्ते में पैदल ही चल रहे हो, इससे हमारी समझ में आता है कि ज्योतिष शास्त्र झूठा ही है। भारी जंगल और बड़े-बड़े पहाड़ों का दुर्गम रास्ता है। तिस पर तुम्हारे साथ सुकुमारी स्त्री है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2510.english_translation: “You are walking on foot, so we think astrology must be false. The path is hard, with mountains and forests, and you have a delicate woman with you.”
ramacharitamanas::2510.translation_literal: मारग (path) / चलहु (you are walking) / पयादेहि (on foot) / पाएँ (by the feet) / ज्योतिषु (astrology) / झूठ (false) / हमारें (to us) / भाएँ (seems)॥ अगमु (difficult) / पंथु (path) / गिरि (mountains) / कानन (forest) / भारी (great, heavy) / तेहि महँ (in that) / साथ (with) / नारि (woman) / सुकुमारी (delicate) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2510.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2510.essence: Outer hardship can look like error to shallow eyes.
ramacharitamanas::2510.simple_meaning: The travelers see Ram, Sita, and Lakshman walking through a harsh forest path and wrongly assume the stars have lied.
ramacharitamanas::2510.simple_insight: People often judge spiritual truth by comfort, not by depth.
ramacharitamanas::2510.detailed_meaning: On the road to exile, villagers watch Ram, Sita, and Lakshman walking barefoot through rough country. Seeing a delicate woman on such a path, they mock the idea that destiny or astrology could be true. The verse shows ordinary people misreading sacred suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2510.modern_relevance: You see someone choosing the harder road, and you assume they must be confused. But some lives look impractical precisely because they are being lived with integrity.
ramacharitamanas::2510.insight: It shifts the mind from judging by appearances to respecting choices that serve dharma.

ramacharitamanas::2511.verse_sanskrit: करि केहरि बन जाइ न जोई। हम सँग चलहिं जो आयसु होई॥ जाब जहाँ लगि तहँ पहुँचाई। फिरब बहोरि तुम्हहि सिरु नाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2511.verse_hindi: हाथी और सिंहों से भरा यह भयानक वन देखा तक नहीं जाता। यदि आज्ञा हो तो हम साथ चलें। आप जहाँ तक जाएँगे, वहाँ तक पहुँचाकर, फिर आपको प्रणाम करके हम लौट आवेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2511.english_translation: We have not even seen this terrible forest full of elephants and lions. If you permit, we will travel with you. We will take you as far as you go, then bow and return.
ramacharitamanas::2511.translation_literal: करि (having made) / केहरि (lions) / बन (forest) / जाइ (go) / न (not) / जोई (seen) / हम (we) / सँग (with) / चलहिं (will walk) / जो (if) / आयसु (permission) / होई (is)॥ / जाब (go) / जहाँ (where) / लगि (up to) / तहँ (there) / पहुँचाई (having reached) / फिरब (will return) / बहोरि (again) / तुम्हहि (you) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing)॥
ramacharitamanas::2511.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2511.essence: True help walks beside you, then lets you continue alone.
ramacharitamanas::2511.simple_meaning: The travelers say the forest is dangerous, but they offer to escort the brothers as far as needed and then return respectfully.
ramacharitamanas::2511.simple_insight: Kindness can be practical: help someone safely, then step back without claiming anything.
ramacharitamanas::2511.detailed_meaning: On the road to exile, Ram and Lakshman meet villagers who are moved by their sight. Seeing the brothers walk into a wild forest, the people offer to guide them partway and then return with respect. The scene shows ordinary hearts trying to serve dharma.
ramacharitamanas::2511.modern_relevance: You see someone heading into a rough neighborhood alone after dark, and you offer to walk with them to the next corner. You help without taking over.
ramacharitamanas::2511.insight: It teaches you to offer support with humility, not possession.

ramacharitamanas::2512.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि पूँछहिं प्रेम बस पुलक गात जलु नैन। कृपासिंधु फेरहिं तिन्हहि कहि बिनीत मृदु बैन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2512.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार वे यात्री प्रेमवश पुलकित शरीर हो और नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भरकर पूछते हैं, किन्तु कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी कोमल विनययुक्त वचन कहकर उन्हें लौटा देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2512.english_translation: In this way, the travelers ask with love, their bodies thrilled and their eyes full of tears. The ocean of compassion, Ram, sends them back with gentle, humble words.
ramacharitamanas::2512.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / पूँछहिं (they ask) / प्रेम बस (under the force of love) / पुलक गात (body thrilled) / जलु नैन (water in the eyes) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / फेरहिं (turns back) / तिन्हहि (them) / कहि (speaking) / बिनीत (humble) / मृदु बैन (soft words)
ramacharitamanas::2512.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2512.essence: Kindness can be complete even when it is brief.
ramacharitamanas::2512.simple_meaning: The travelers, moved by love, ask their questions with tears in their eyes, and Ram gently sends them on their way.
ramacharitamanas::2512.simple_insight: Warm kindness can answer without lingering, and still leave everyone feeling seen.
ramacharitamanas::2512.detailed_meaning: On the road through Ayodhya’s exile route, villagers stop to ask the travelers questions with overflowing affection. Ram, already burdened by the journey, responds gently and lets them return. The moment shows his tenderness, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2512.modern_relevance: A stranger asks for directions while you are rushing to catch a train. You still slow down, answer kindly, and move on without making it about yourself.
ramacharitamanas::2512.insight: It highlights Ram’s gentle presence: even brief encounters become acts of grace.

ramacharitamanas::2513.verse_sanskrit: जे पुर गाँव बसहिं मग माहीं। तिन्हहि नाग सुर नगर सिहाहीं॥ केहि सुकृतीं केहि घरीं बसाए। धन्य पुन्यमय परम सुहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2513.verse_hindi: जो गाँव और पुरवे रास्ते में बसे हैं, नागों और देवताओं के नगर उनको देखकर प्रशंसा पूर्वक ईर्षा करते और ललचाते हुए कहते हैं कि किस पुण्यवान् ने किस शुभ घड़ी में इनको बसाया था, जो आज ये इतने धन्य और पुण्यमय तथा परम सुंदर हो रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2513.english_translation: The villages and towns along the road are so blessed that even the cities of the gods envy them, asking, "What righteous person settled them, and in what lucky hour, that they have become so beautiful and full of merit?"
ramacharitamanas::2513.translation_literal: जे (those) / पुर (towns) / गाँव (villages) / बसहिं (reside) / मग (road) / माहीं (in) / तिन्हहि (them) / नाग (serpents) / सुर (devas) / नगर (cities) / सिहाहीं (envy) / केहि (which) / सुकृतीं (righteous one) / केहि (which) / घरीं (auspicious hour) / बसाए (settled) / धन्य (blessed) / पुन्यमय (full of merit) / परम (supremely) / सुहाए (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::2513.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2513.essence: Where Ram passes, ordinary places become enviable.
ramacharitamanas::2513.simple_meaning: Any place where Ram's journey passes becomes so blessed that even heavenly cities envy it.
ramacharitamanas::2513.simple_insight: Sacredness is not about grandeur; it is about contact with what is truly holy.
ramacharitamanas::2513.detailed_meaning: As Ram travels through the countryside in exile, Tulsidas pauses to praise the villages and towns on his path. The point is not the settlements themselves but the sanctifying power of Ram's presence, which makes even celestial cities seem small.
ramacharitamanas::2513.modern_relevance: A train platform where someone you love finally steps off can feel more alive than a palace. Presence changes the meaning of a place more than architecture ever can.
ramacharitamanas::2513.insight: It shifts attention from external beauty to the blessing created by holy presence.

ramacharitamanas::2514.verse_sanskrit: जहँ जहँ राम चरन चलि जाहीं। तिन्ह समान अमरावति नाहीं॥ पुन्यपुंज मग निकट निवासी। तिन्हहि सराहहिं सुरपुरबासी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2514.verse_hindi: जहाँ-जहाँ श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरण चले जाते हैं, उनके समान इन्द्र की पुरी अमरावती भी नहीं है। रास्ते के समीप बसने वाले भी बड़े पुण्यात्मा हैं- स्वर्ग में रहने वाले देवता भी उनकी सराहना करते हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2514.english_translation: Wherever Ram's feet have walked, even Amaravati cannot match that place. Those who live near that road are highly blessed, and the beings of heaven praise them.
ramacharitamanas::2514.translation_literal: जहँ जहँ (wherever) / राम चरन (Ram's feet) / चलि जाहीं (have walked) / तिन्ह समान (equal to that) / अमरावति (Amaravati) / नाहीं (is not)॥ / पुन्यपुंज (a mass of merit) / मग निकट निवासी (residents near the road) / तिन्हहि (them) / सराहहिं (praise) / सुरपुरबासी (inhabitants of heaven) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2514.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2514.essence: Ram's presence makes ordinary ground more precious than heaven.
ramacharitamanas::2514.simple_meaning: Any place touched by Ram's feet becomes greater than heaven. Even people living near that path are considered deeply blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2514.simple_insight: Closeness to the sacred can transform ordinary ground into something precious.
ramacharitamanas::2514.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, people along the road are speaking with wonder about Ram's exile journey. They say that any place his feet touch becomes more glorious than Amaravati, and even the nearby residents are praised by the heavenly beings.
ramacharitamanas::2514.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after someone kind, steady, and deeply loved has passed through it. The air feels different. Some presence doesn't need a throne to change everything around it.
ramacharitamanas::2514.insight: It shifts attention from status to presence: holiness is measured by contact with Ram, not by location.

ramacharitamanas::2515.verse_sanskrit: जे भरि नयन बिलोकहिं रामहि। सीता लखन सहित घनस्यामहि॥ जे सर सरित राम अवगाहहिं। तिन्हहि देव सर सरित सराहहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2515.verse_hindi: जो नेत्र भरकर सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित घनश्याम श्री रामजी के दर्शन करते हैं, जिन तालाबों और नदियों में श्री रामजी स्नान कर लेते हैं, देवसरोवर और देवनदियाँ भी उनकी बड़ाई करती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2515.english_translation: Those who behold Ram with full eyes, along with Sita and Lakshman, and those lakes and rivers in which Ram bathes — even the divine lakes and rivers praise them.
ramacharitamanas::2515.translation_literal: जे (those who) / भरि (filled) / नयन (eyes) / बिलोकहिं (behold) / रामहि (Ram) / सीता (Sita) / लखन (Lakshman) / सहित (along with) / घनस्यामहि (the dark-hued Ram)॥ / जे (those which) / सर (lakes) / सरित (rivers) / राम (Ram) / अवगाहहिं (bathe in) / तिन्हहि (them) / देव (divine) / सर (lakes) / सरित (rivers) / सराहहिं (praise) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2515.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2515.essence: Ram's presence turns ordinary places into places of honor.
ramacharitamanas::2515.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram with Sita and Lakshman makes a place sacred. Even lakes and rivers become worthy of praise when Ram bathes in them.
ramacharitamanas::2515.simple_insight: What you love and attend to can transform the world around you.
ramacharitamanas::2515.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is praising the places blessed by Ram's exile journey. Even ordinary lakes and rivers gain honor through Ram's presence, and people who see him with Sita and Lakshman are considered fortunate.
ramacharitamanas::2515.modern_relevance: You walk into a quiet temple courtyard after a hard week, and the whole place feels different because of one calm presence. Some people don't just enter a space — they change it.
ramacharitamanas::2515.insight: It shifts attention from objects themselves to the sanctifying power of presence and devotion.

ramacharitamanas::2516.verse_sanskrit: जेहि तरु तर प्रभु बैठहिं जाई। करहिं कलपतरु तासु बड़ाई॥ परसि राम पद पदुम परागा। मानति भूमि भूरि निज भागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2516.verse_hindi: जिस वृक्ष के नीचे प्रभु जा बैठते हैं, कल्पवृक्ष भी उसकी बड़ाई करते हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणकमलों की रज का स्पर्श करके पृथ्वी अपना बड़ा सौभाग्य मानती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2516.english_translation: The tree beneath which the Lord sits is praised even by the wish-fulfilling tree. Touching the pollen of Ram's lotus feet, the earth counts itself greatly blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2516.translation_literal: जेहि (which) / तरु (tree) / तर (under) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बैठहिं (sit) / जाई (go) / करहिं (do) / कलपतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / तासु (its) / बड़ाई (praise) / परसि (touching) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / पदुम (lotus) / परागा (pollen) / मानति (counts as) / भूमि (earth) / भूरि (great) / निज (its own) / भागा (fortune)
ramacharitamanas::2516.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2516.essence: Ram's presence makes even nature feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2516.simple_meaning: Even ordinary places become sacred when Ram is there. The tree under him is praised, and the earth feels fortunate just to touch his feet.
ramacharitamanas::2516.simple_insight: What matters is not the place itself, but who blesses it with presence.
ramacharitamanas::2516.detailed_meaning: As Ram, Sita, and Lakshman move through exile, Tulsidas pauses to show how creation responds to Ram's presence. A tree becomes greater than a wish-fulfilling tree, and the earth itself feels honored by his footsteps.
ramacharitamanas::2516.modern_relevance: A room where someone kind and steady enters can feel different at once. The space did not change — but your whole nervous system did.
ramacharitamanas::2516.insight: It shifts attention from objects to presence: holiness comes from contact with the worthy, not from status alone.

ramacharitamanas::2517.verse_sanskrit: छाँह करहिं घन बिबुधगन बरषहिं सुमन सिहाहिं। देखत गिरि बन बिहग मृग रामु चले मग जाहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2517.verse_hindi: रास्ते में बादल छाया करते हैं और देवता फूल बरसाते और सिहाते हैं। पर्वत, वन और पशु-पक्षियों को देखते हुए श्री रामजी रास्ते में चले जा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2517.english_translation: Clouds shade the path, radiant beings shower flowers and rejoice. Seeing the hills, forests, birds, and animals, Ram walks onward.
ramacharitamanas::2517.translation_literal: छाँह (shade) / करहिं (make) / घन (clouds) / बिबुधगन (radiant beings) / बरषहिं (shower) / सुमन (flowers) / सिहाहिं (rejoice) / देखत (seeing) / गिरि (mountains) / बन (forest) / बिहग (birds) / मृग (deer) / रामु (Ram) / चले (walked) / मग (path) / जाहिं (go)
ramacharitamanas::2517.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2517.essence: Ram's presence turns the whole world into welcome.
ramacharitamanas::2517.simple_meaning: As Ram walks, nature itself seems to welcome him: clouds give shade, radiant beings shower flowers, and the hills, forests, birds, and animals are all part of the scene.
ramacharitamanas::2517.simple_insight: When your presence is aligned, even the world around you feels gentler.
ramacharitamanas::2517.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are moving through the landscape on exile. This couplet pauses the story to paint the world responding to Ram's presence: clouds shade him, flowers fall, and every part of nature seems to witness his passing.
ramacharitamanas::2517.modern_relevance: You walk into a place after a hard day, and the room feels different before anyone speaks. Sometimes presence changes the atmosphere more than words ever could.
ramacharitamanas::2517.insight: It shifts attention from action to aura: the verse makes Ram's presence itself the event.

ramacharitamanas::2518.verse_sanskrit: सीता लखन सहित रघुराई। गाँव निकट जब निकसहिं जाई॥ सुनि सब बाल बृद्ध नर नारी। चलहिं तुरत गृह काजु बिसारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2518.verse_hindi: सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित श्री रघुनाथजी जब किसी गाँव के पास जा निकलते हैं, तब उनका आना सुनते ही बालक-बूढ़े, स्त्री-पुरुष सब अपने घर और काम-काज को भूलकर तुरंत उन्हें देखने के लिए चल देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2518.english_translation: When Raghunath, along with Sita and Lakshman, comes near a village, hearing of their arrival all the old and young, men and women, leave their homes and work at once to go see them.
ramacharitamanas::2518.translation_literal: सीता (Sita) / लखन (Lakshman) / सहित (together with) / रघुराई (Raghunath) / गाँव (village) / निकट (near) / जब (when) / निकसहिं (come out) / जाई (going) // सुनि (hearing) / सब (all) / बाल (children) / बृद्ध (old) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / चलहिं (go) / तुरत (immediately) / गृह (home) / काजु (work) / बिसारी (forgetting)
ramacharitamanas::2518.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2518.essence: Ram’s nearness makes ordinary life irrelevant for a moment.
ramacharitamanas::2518.simple_meaning: When Ram, Sita, and Lakshman come near a village, everyone leaves home and work to see them.
ramacharitamanas::2518.simple_insight: Some presences pull people away from routine without effort.
ramacharitamanas::2518.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are passing near a village on the road. The moment people hear they are close, everyone from children to elders rushes out, forgetting home and work. The verse shows how naturally Ram draws every heart.
ramacharitamanas::2518.modern_relevance: You hear a beloved teacher is coming to your neighborhood, and suddenly errands, chores, and schedules lose their grip. Something deeper than routine has already taken hold of you.
ramacharitamanas::2518.insight: It shows how devotion can interrupt ordinary life and make presence matter more than productivity.

ramacharitamanas::2519.verse_sanskrit: राम लखन सिय रूप निहारी। पाइ नयन फलु होहिं सुखारी॥ सजल बिलोचन पुलक सरीरा। सब भए मगन देखि दोउ बीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2519.verse_hindi: श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीताजी का रूप देखकर, नेत्रों का (परम) फल पाकर वे सुखी होते हैं। दोनों भाइयों को देखकर सब प्रेमानन्द में मग्न हो गए। उनके नेत्रों में जल भर आया और शरीर पुलकित हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2519.english_translation: Seeing the forms of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, they became joyful as if their eyes had found their true reward. Seeing the two brothers, everyone was lost in love and delight. Their eyes filled with tears and their bodies thrilled with goosebumps.
ramacharitamanas::2519.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / रूप (form) / निहारी (seeing) / पाइ (having found) / नयन (eyes) / फलु (fruit/reward) / होहिं (become) / सुखारी (happy) / सजल (wet) / बिलोचन (eyes) / पुलक (goosebumps) / सरीरा (body) / सब (all) / भए (became) / मगन (absorbed) / देखि (seeing) / दोउ (both) / बीरा (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::2519.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2519.essence: Their presence alone turns seeing into fulfillment.
ramacharitamanas::2519.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram, Lakshman, and Sita fills everyone with joy, tears, and goosebumps. Their presence alone makes the crowd feel fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::2519.simple_insight: Real devotion can make a simple sight feel like a blessing you had been waiting for.
ramacharitamanas::2519.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are passing near a village on the road to exile. The people rush out, overwhelmed just by seeing them. This verse lingers on the crowd's tears and trembling joy before the next verse compares their state to finding a priceless treasure.
ramacharitamanas::2519.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone you deeply respect across a crowded station, and your whole chest softens. Some presences speak before any words do.
ramacharitamanas::2519.insight: It shows how sacred presence can move people beyond thought into immediate love and reverence.

ramacharitamanas::2520.verse_sanskrit: बरनि न जाइ दसा तिन्ह केरी। लहि जनु रंकन्ह सुरमनि ढेरी॥ एकन्ह एक बोलि सिख देहीं। लोचन लाहु लेहु छन एहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2520.verse_hindi: उनकी दशा वर्णन नहीं की जाती। मानो दरिद्रों ने चिन्तामणि की ढेरी पा ली हो। वे एक-एक को पुकारकर सीख देते हैं कि इसी क्षण नेत्रों का लाभ ले लो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2520.english_translation: Their state cannot be described. It was as if the poor had found heaps of wish-fulfilling jewels. Each one called to another and said, “Take in the sight now, in this very moment.”
ramacharitamanas::2520.translation_literal: बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाइ (can be gone) / दसा (state) / तिन्ह (their) / केरी (of) / लहि (having found) / जनु (as if) / रंकन्ह (by the poor) / सुरमनि (wish-fulfilling jewel) / ढेरी (heap) / एकन्ह (one to another) / एक (one) / बोलि (calling) / सिख (advice) / देहीं (they give) / लोचन (eyes) / लाहु (benefit) / लेहु (take) / छन (moment) / एहीं (this)
ramacharitamanas::2520.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2520.essence: Presence so precious makes every second feel like treasure.
ramacharitamanas::2520.simple_meaning: The people are overwhelmed by Ram, Lakshman, and Sita’s presence. Their joy is beyond description, like the poor suddenly finding priceless treasure.
ramacharitamanas::2520.simple_insight: Some moments are so precious that you feel urgency just to see them fully.
ramacharitamanas::2520.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are passing near a village in Ayodhyakand, and the crowd rushes out to see them. The sight is so overwhelming that people compare it to sudden wealth and urge one another not to waste even a moment.
ramacharitamanas::2520.modern_relevance: You catch a brief glimpse of someone you love across a crowded station platform, and your whole body says, don’t look away.
ramacharitamanas::2520.insight: It turns attention into urgency: when something precious appears, the right response is immediate presence.

ramacharitamanas::2521.verse_sanskrit: रामहि देखि एक अनुरागे। चितवत चले जाहिं सँग लागे॥ एक नयन मग छबि उर आनी। होहिं सिथिल तन मन बर बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2521.verse_hindi: कोई श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर ऐसे अनुराग में भर गए हैं कि वे उन्हें देखते हुए उनके साथ लगे चले जा रहे हैं। कोई नेत्र मार्ग से उनकी छबि को हृदय में लाकर शरीर, मन और श्रेष्ठ वाणी से शिथिल हो जाते हैं (अर्थात् उनके शरीर, मन और वाणी का व्यवहार बंद हो जाता है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2521.english_translation: Some, filled with love just by seeing Ram, keep walking along with him while still gazing at him. Others bring his beauty into their hearts through a glance and then become quiet in body, mind, and speech.
ramacharitamanas::2521.translation_literal: रामहि (Ram) / देखि (seeing) / एक (some) / अनुरागे (filled with love) / चितवत (while gazing) / चले (walked) / जाहिं (go) / सँग (with) / लागे (attached) / एक (some) / नयन (eye) / मग (path) / छबि (beauty) / उर (heart) / आनी (bringing) / होहिं (become) / सिथिल (quiet/limp) / तन (body) / मन (mind) / बर (excellent) / बानी (speech)
ramacharitamanas::2521.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2521.essence: Love for Ram can quiet the whole person at once.
ramacharitamanas::2521.simple_meaning: Just seeing Ram overwhelms people in different ways: some follow him while staring, and some become so absorbed that body, mind, and speech fall quiet.
ramacharitamanas::2521.simple_insight: Real love can make you forget yourself without losing awareness.
ramacharitamanas::2521.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are moving through a crowd already swept up in their presence. People respond in different ways, but all of them are equally overcome by love and wonder.
ramacharitamanas::2521.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone you deeply admire across a crowded station, and for a moment everything else drops away. Attention, speech, and even your posture change before you notice.
ramacharitamanas::2521.insight: It shows how genuine devotion shifts the whole person, not just the thoughts.

ramacharitamanas::2522.verse_sanskrit: एक देखि बट छाँह भलि डासि मृदुल तृन पात। कहहिं गवाँइअ छिनुकु श्रमु गवनब अबहिंकि प्रात ॥
ramacharitamanas::2522.verse_hindi: कोई बड़ की सुंदर छाया देखकर, वहाँ नरम घास और पत्ते बिछाकर कहते हैं कि क्षण भर यहाँ बैठकर थकावट मिटा लीजिए। फिर चाहे अभी चले जाइएगा, चाहे सबेरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2522.english_translation: Seeing a good banyan-tree shade, they spread soft grass and leaves and say, "Rest here a moment and ease your fatigue. You may leave now or in the morning."
ramacharitamanas::2522.translation_literal: एक (one) / देखि (seeing) / बट (banyan-tree) / छाँह (shade) / भलि (good) / डासि (spreading) / मृदुल (soft) / तृन (grass) / पात (leaves) / कहहिं (they say) / गवाँइअ (let be spent / let pass) / छिनुकु (a moment) / श्रमु (fatigue) / गवनब (to depart) / अबहिंकि (now / immediately) / प्रात (morning)
ramacharitamanas::2522.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2522.essence: Devotion becomes real when it makes room for someone to rest.
ramacharitamanas::2522.simple_meaning: People see Ram and lovingly prepare a shady resting place for him, telling him to sit a moment and rest before continuing his journey.
ramacharitamanas::2522.simple_insight: Love notices fatigue before it is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2522.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, people gathered along Ram's path are overwhelmed by devotion. Seeing a cool banyan shade, they spread grass and leaves so he can rest, and gently ask him to pause before moving on. Their care becomes an offering.
ramacharitamanas::2522.modern_relevance: You notice someone dragging after a long day and quietly pull out a chair, a bottle of water, and a place to breathe. Care often begins there.
ramacharitamanas::2522.insight: It shifts attention from admiration to practical care.

ramacharitamanas::2523.verse_sanskrit: एक कलस भरि आनहिं पानी। अँचइअ नाथ कहहिं मृदु बानी॥ सुनि प्रिय बचन प्रीति अति देखी। राम कृपाल सुसील बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2523.verse_hindi: कोई घड़ा भरकर पानी ले आते हैं और कोमल वाणी से कहते हैं- नाथ! आचमन तो कर लीजिए। उनके प्यारे वचन सुनकर और उनका अत्यन्त प्रेम देखकर दयालु और परम सुशील श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2523.english_translation: Some bring a pot full of water and softly say, “Lord, please take a sip.” Hearing their loving words and seeing their deep affection, compassionate and ever-gentle Ram...
ramacharitamanas::2523.translation_literal: एक (one) / कलस (pot) / भरि (filled) / आनहिं (bring) / पानी (water) / अँचइअ (please sip) / नाथ (Lord) / कहहिं (say) / मृदु (soft) / बानी (speech) / सुनि (hearing) / प्रिय (dear) / बचन (words) / प्रीति (love) / अति (very much) / देखी (seeing) / राम (Ram) / कृपाल (compassionate) / सुसील (gentle) / बिसेषी (especially)
ramacharitamanas::2523.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2523.essence: Affection becomes real when it turns into care.
ramacharitamanas::2523.simple_meaning: People lovingly bring water and invite Ram to rest and refresh himself. Their affection moves him, and his gentle nature responds to their care.
ramacharitamanas::2523.simple_insight: Love becomes practical service, and even a simple kindness can soften the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2523.detailed_meaning: On the road to exile, the people of Ayodhya keep following Ram. They do not just admire him; they serve him with water, shade, and tender words. This verse pauses on that mutual tenderness before the journey continues.
ramacharitamanas::2523.modern_relevance: You hand someone a glass of water after a hard day, and the whole room changes. Small care, offered with love, can carry more power than grand speeches.
ramacharitamanas::2523.insight: It shifts attention from admiration to service: love is proven by what you do for someone in front of you.

ramacharitamanas::2524.verse_sanskrit: जानी श्रमित सीय मन माहीं। घरिक बिलंबु कीन्ह बट छाहीं॥ मुदित नारि नर देखहिं सोभा। रूप अनूप नयन मनु लोभा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2524.verse_hindi: मन में सीताजी को थकी हुई जानकर घड़ी भर बड़ की छाया में विश्राम किया। स्त्री-पुरुष आनंदित होकर शोभा देखते हैं। अनुपम रूप ने उनके नेत्र और मनों को लुभा लिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2524.english_translation: Knowing Sita was tired, they paused for a while in the shade of a banyan tree. Men and women looked on with delight; his unmatched beauty captivated their eyes and minds.
ramacharitamanas::2524.translation_literal: जानी (knowing) / श्रमित (tired) / सीय (Sita) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / घरिक (for a while) / बिलंबु (delay) / कीन्ह (made) / बट छाहीं (in banyan shade) / मुदित (delighted) / नारि (women) / नर (men) / देखहिं (see) / सोभा (beauty) / रूप (form) / अनूप (matchless) / नयन (eyes) / मनु (mind) / लोभा (were captivated)
ramacharitamanas::2524.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2524.essence: Care for the tired person first; beauty follows naturally.
ramacharitamanas::2524.simple_meaning: Seeing Sita was tired, they rested briefly in the shade. Everyone around them felt joy, and Ram's unmatched beauty drew the eyes and hearts of all.
ramacharitamanas::2524.simple_insight: Even a small pause can become beautiful when it is made with care.
ramacharitamanas::2524.detailed_meaning: During the journey through the forest, Ram notices Sita's fatigue and stops for a moment beneath a banyan tree. The people around them are filled with joy simply by seeing the scene, and Ram's beauty quietly holds everyone's attention.
ramacharitamanas::2524.modern_relevance: You notice someone beside you is exhausted, so you slow down, find shade, and let the moment breathe. That small kindness changes the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::2524.insight: It teaches you to respond to another person's fatigue with immediate care, not efficiency.

ramacharitamanas::2525.verse_sanskrit: एकटक सब सोहहिं चहुँ ओरा। रामचन्द्र मुख चंद चकोरा॥ तरुन तमाल बरन तनु सोहा। देखत कोटि मदन मनु मोहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2525.verse_hindi: सब लोग टकटकी लगाए श्री रामचन्द्रजी के मुख चन्द्र को चकोर की तरह (तन्मय होकर) देखते हुए चारों ओर सुशोभित हो रहे हैं। श्री रामजी का नवीन तमाल वृक्ष के रंग का (श्याम) शरीर अत्यन्त शोभा दे रहा है, जिसे देखते ही करोड़ों कामदेवों के मन मोहित हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2525.english_translation: Everyone stands all around, gazing without blinking, like chakors around the moon-face of Ramchandra. His body, dark as a young tamal tree, shines so beautifully that it enchants the minds of millions of Cupids.
ramacharitamanas::2525.translation_literal: एकटक (without blinking) / सब (all) / सोहहिं (look beautiful) / चहुँ ओर (on all four sides) / रामचन्द्र (Ramchandra) / मुख चंद (moon-face) / चकोरा (chakor bird)॥ / तरुन (young) / तमाल (tamal tree) / बरन (color) / तनु (body) / सोहा (shone beautifully) / देखत (seeing) / कोटि (millions) / मदन (Cupids) / मनु (mind) / मोहा (was enchanted) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2525.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2525.essence: Ram's presence makes everyone forget everything else.
ramacharitamanas::2525.simple_meaning: Everyone is spellbound by Ram's beauty. His face is like the moon to loving eyes, and his dark, graceful form overwhelms every heart.
ramacharitamanas::2525.simple_insight: Some presence is so beautiful that attention becomes devotion without effort.
ramacharitamanas::2525.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the people gather around Ram before exile and cannot look away. They circle him with reverent delight, seeing his face and dark, radiant form as irresistibly beautiful. The moment deepens the ache of separation that is about to come.
ramacharitamanas::2525.modern_relevance: You enter a room and the whole mood changes before anyone speaks. Some people carry a calm beauty that draws every eye and softens every heart.
ramacharitamanas::2525.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary appearance to the power of presence itself.

ramacharitamanas::2526.verse_sanskrit: दामिनि बरन लखन सुठि नीके। नख सिख सुभग भावते जी के॥ मुनि पट कटिन्ह कसें तूनीरा। सोहहिं कर कमलनि धनु तीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2526.verse_hindi: बिजली के से रंग के लक्ष्मणजी बहुत ही भले मालूम होते हैं। वे नख से शिखा तक सुंदर हैं और मन को बहुत भाते हैं। दोनों मुनियों के (वल्कल आदि) वस्त्र पहने हैं और कमर में तरकस कसे हुए हैं। कमल के समान हाथों में धनुष-बाण शोभित हो रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2526.english_translation: Lakshman, the one with lightning-like color, looks truly splendid. Beautiful from head to toe, he delights the heart. Wearing the bark cloth of a forest ascetic and a quiver at his waist, his lotus-like hands carry bow and arrows.
ramacharitamanas::2526.translation_literal: दामिनि (lightning) / बरन (color) / लखन (Lakshman) / सुठि (truly) / नीके (splendid) / नख सिख (from nail to crest) / सुभग (beautiful) / भावते (delight) / जी के (the heart's) / मुनि (sage) / पट (cloth) / कटिन्ह (at the waist) / कसें (tied) / तूनीरा (quiver) / सोहहिं (shine) / कर कमलनि (lotus hands) / धनु (bow) / तीरा (arrows)
ramacharitamanas::2526.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2526.essence: True beauty is strength placed in loving service.
ramacharitamanas::2526.simple_meaning: Lakshman is described as strikingly beautiful, dressed like a forest ascetic, with a bow and arrows ready at his side.
ramacharitamanas::2526.simple_insight: Strength and beauty can live together when they are placed in service.
ramacharitamanas::2526.detailed_meaning: Ram and Sita rest under a tree in exile, and Lakshman stands beside them like a living guard. Tulsidas lingers on his appearance: ascetic cloth, armed waist, lotus hands, and a face that wins every heart. The verse builds the dignity of his service.
ramacharitamanas::2526.modern_relevance: You show up to protect someone you love, wearing no badge and asking for no credit. Even then, your steadiness changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::2526.insight: It shifts attention from mere appearance to the dignity of devoted protection.

ramacharitamanas::2527.verse_sanskrit: जटा मुकुट सीसनि सुभग उर भुज नयन बिसाल। सरद परब बिधु बदन बर लसत स्वेद कन जाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::2527.verse_hindi: उनके सिरों पर सुंदर जटाओं के मुकुट हैं, वक्षः स्थल, भुजा और नेत्र विशाल हैं और शरद पूर्णिमा के चन्द्रमा के समान सुंदर मुखों पर पसीने की बूँदों का समूह शोभित हो रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2527.english_translation: Their heads wear lovely matted-crown locks, their chests, arms, and eyes are broad, and drops of sweat shine on their moonlike faces.
ramacharitamanas::2527.translation_literal: जटा (matted hair) / मुकुट (crown) / सीसनि (on the heads) / सुभग (beautiful) / उर (chest) / भुज (arms) / नयन (eyes) / बिसाल (broad) / सरद (autumn) / परब (full moon) / बिधु (moon) / बदन (faces) / बर (beautiful) / लसत (shining) / स्वेद (sweat) / कन (drops) / जाल (net, cluster)
ramacharitamanas::2527.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2527.essence: Hardship does not dim their radiance.
ramacharitamanas::2527.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are described as radiant and beautiful, with matted hair, broad bodies, and sweat shining on their faces.
ramacharitamanas::2527.simple_insight: Even in the forest, their presence is so beautiful that strain only makes it more vivid.
ramacharitamanas::2527.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the forest scene is unfolding around Ram and Lakshman. After the earlier lines praise their appearance, this verse adds another detail: their faces shine with sweat, yet nothing diminishes their grace. It is part of the larger description of their divine beauty.
ramacharitamanas::2527.modern_relevance: After a long walk in the heat, your shirt is damp and your face is tired — yet someone still looks at you with admiration. Effort does not cancel dignity.
ramacharitamanas::2527.insight: It shifts attention from polished appearance to the beauty of steadfast presence.

ramacharitamanas::2528.verse_sanskrit: बरनि न जाइ मनोहर जोरी। सोभा बहुत थोरि मति मोरी॥ राम लखन सिय सुंदरताई। सब चितवहिं चित मन मति लाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2528.verse_hindi: उस मनोहर जोड़ी का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता, क्योंकि शोभा बहुत अधिक है और मेरी बुद्धि थोड़ी है। श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीताजी की सुंदरता को सब लोग मन, चित्त और बुद्धि तीनों को लगाकर देख रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2528.english_translation: That lovely pair cannot be described; my understanding is too small for their great beauty. Everyone is looking at the beauty of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita with full attention of mind, heart, and intellect.
ramacharitamanas::2528.translation_literal: बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाइ (can go) / मनोहर (beautiful) / जोरी (pair) / सोभा (beauty, splendor) / बहुत (very much) / थोरि (small) / मति (understanding) / मोरी (my) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / सुंदरताई (beauty) / सब (all) / चितवहिं (are gazing) / चित (mind) / मन (heart) / मति (intellect) / लाई (having applied)
ramacharitamanas::2528.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2528.essence: True beauty leaves words behind and holds the whole mind still.
ramacharitamanas::2528.simple_meaning: Their beauty is beyond description, and everyone is looking at Ram, Lakshman, and Sita with complete attention.
ramacharitamanas::2528.simple_insight: Some moments are so beautiful they quiet the mind before words can begin.
ramacharitamanas::2528.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the three are moving through a scene of public wonder. The narrator pauses to say their beauty cannot be fully described. People are so absorbed that they are staring with all their attention, caught in reverent amazement.
ramacharitamanas::2528.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and everyone falls silent for a second, not from awkwardness but from presence. Some people carry a beauty that makes language feel too small.
ramacharitamanas::2528.insight: It shifts attention from explanation to direct seeing, where beauty is recognized before it is analyzed.

ramacharitamanas::2529.verse_sanskrit: थके नारि नर प्रेम पिआसे। मनहुँ मृगी मृग देखि दिआ से॥ सीय समीप ग्रामतिय जाहीं। पूँछत अति सनेहँ सकुचाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2529.verse_hindi: प्रेम के प्यासे (वे गाँवों के) स्त्री-पुरुष (इनके सौंदर्य-माधुर्य की छटा देखकर) ऐसे थकित रह गए जैसे दीपक को देखकर हिरनी और हिरन (निस्तब्ध रह जाते हैं)! गाँवों की स्त्रियाँ सीताजी के पास जाती हैं, परन्तु अत्यन्त स्नेह के कारण पूछते सकुचाती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2529.english_translation: The men and women, thirsty for love, grew still as if deer had seen a lamp. The village women went near Sita, but their great affection made them shy to ask anything.
ramacharitamanas::2529.translation_literal: थके (were worn/still) / नारि नर (women and men) / प्रेम पिआसे (thirsty for love) / मनहुँ (as if) / मृगी (doe) / मृग (deer) / देखि (seeing) / दिआ से (a lamp) ॥ / सीय समीप (near Sita) / ग्रामतिय (village women) / जाहीं (go) / पूँछत (asking) / अति सनेहँ (with great affection) / सकुचाहीं (feel shy)
ramacharitamanas::2529.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2529.essence: A loving presence can leave people speechless.
ramacharitamanas::2529.simple_meaning: The people are so captivated by Ram, Lakshman, and Sita that they stand still in wonder. The village women approach Sita, but their affection makes them too shy to speak freely.
ramacharitamanas::2529.simple_insight: Deep admiration can make even simple speech feel impossible.
ramacharitamanas::2529.detailed_meaning: The trio’s beauty has frozen the villagers in awe. Men and women gaze in silence, and the village women gather near Sita but cannot easily ask their questions. The scene shows how love and reverence overwhelm ordinary conversation.
ramacharitamanas::2529.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and suddenly forget what you were going to say. The person in front of you feels so graceful, so kind, that your own words come out timid and small.
ramacharitamanas::2529.insight: It captures how reverence can quiet the mind before a beloved presence.

ramacharitamanas::2530.verse_sanskrit: बार बार सब लागहिं पाएँ। कहहिं बचन मृदु सरल सुभाएँ॥ राजकुमारि बिनय हम करहीं। तिय सुभायँ कछु पूँछत डरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2530.verse_hindi: बार-बार सब उनके पाँव लगतीं और सहज ही सीधे-सादे कोमल वचन कहती हैं- हे राजकुमारी! हम विनती करती (कुछ निवेदन करना चाहती) हैं, परन्तु स्त्री स्वभाव के कारण कुछ पूछते हुए डरती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2530.english_translation: Again and again they touched her feet and spoke in gentle, simple words: 'Princess, we wish to make a request, but in a woman's nature there is some fear in asking.'
ramacharitamanas::2530.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / सब (all) / लागहिं (they touch) / पाएँ (feet) / कहहिं (they speak) / बचन (words) / मृदु (gentle) / सरल (simple) / सुभाएँ (by nature) / राजकुमारि (princess) / बिनय (request) / हम (we) / करहीं (do) / तिय (woman) / सुभायँ (by nature) / कछु (some) / पूँछत (asking) / डरहीं (they fear)
ramacharitamanas::2530.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2530.essence: Humility can make even fear speak beautifully.
ramacharitamanas::2530.simple_meaning: The women repeatedly bow to Sita and speak with soft respect, asking permission to speak while admitting they feel shy and hesitant.
ramacharitamanas::2530.simple_insight: Gentleness can carry more courage than force.
ramacharitamanas::2530.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, women approach Sita after seeing Ram, Lakshman, and Sita together. Overwhelmed by reverence, they keep touching her feet and speaking humbly. This verse shows their modesty and the social hesitation that shapes the conversation.
ramacharitamanas::2530.modern_relevance: You rehearse the message three times before knocking on her door, then soften your voice the moment she opens it. Respect can make even fear speak gently.
ramacharitamanas::2530.insight: It shows how reverence turns hesitation into courteous speech.

ramacharitamanas::2531.verse_sanskrit: स्वामिनि अबिनय छमबि हमारी। बिलगु न मानब जानि गवाँरी॥ राजकुअँर दोउ सहज सलोने। इन्ह तें लही दुति मरकत सोने ॥
ramacharitamanas::2531.verse_hindi: हे स्वामिनी! हमारी ढिठाई क्षमा कीजिएगा और हमको गँवारी जानकर बुरा न मानिएगा। ये दोनों राजकुमार स्वभाव से ही लावण्यमय (परम सुंदर) हैं। मरकतमणि (पन्ने) और सुवर्ण ने कांति इन्हीं से पाई है (अर्थात मरकतमणि में और स्वर्ण में जो हरित और स्वर्ण वर्ण की आभा है, वह इनकी हरिताभ नील और स्वर्ण कान्ति के एक कण के बराबर भी नहीं है।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2531.english_translation: O mistress, forgive our rudeness and do not take us for simple village women. These two princes are naturally beautiful; emerald and gold get their glow from them.
ramacharitamanas::2531.translation_literal: स्वामिनि (O mistress) / अबिनय (rudeness) / छमबि (forgive) / हमारी (our) / बिलगु (offense) / न (not) / मानब (take [it]) / जानि (knowing) / गवाँरी (village women) / राजकुअँर (princes) / दोउ (both) / सहज (by nature) / सलोने (beautiful) / इन्ह (from them) / तें (than) / लही (obtained) / दुति (lustre) / मरकत (emerald) / सोने (gold)
ramacharitamanas::2531.speaker: Village women
ramacharitamanas::2531.essence: Natural beauty makes hesitation turn into reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2531.simple_meaning: The village women politely ask Sita to forgive their boldness and say the two princes are naturally radiant and beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::2531.simple_insight: Beauty can soften pride and make strangers speak with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2531.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the village women approach Sita with shy admiration as Ram and Lakshman pass by. They apologize for speaking too freely, then marvel that the princes are so naturally beautiful that even emerald and gold seem dim beside them.
ramacharitamanas::2531.modern_relevance: You meet someone so composed and radiant that your own awkwardness suddenly feels small. Instead of pretending confidence, you speak more gently and honestly.
ramacharitamanas::2531.insight: It shifts attention from social hesitation to spontaneous reverence before genuine beauty.

ramacharitamanas::2532.verse_sanskrit: स्यामल गौर किसोर बर सुंदर सुषमा ऐन। सरद सर्बरीनाथ मुखु सरद सरोरुह नैन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2532.verse_hindi: श्याम और गौर वर्ण है, सुंदर किशोर अवस्था है, दोनों ही परम सुंदर और शोभा के धाम हैं। शरद पूर्णिमा के चन्द्रमा के समान इनके मुख और शरद ऋतु के कमल के समान इनके नेत्र हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2532.english_translation: Dark and fair, both are beautiful youths, full of loveliness. Their faces are like the autumn moon, and their eyes like autumn lotuses.
ramacharitamanas::2532.translation_literal: स्यामल (dark) / गौर (fair) / किसोर (youthful) / बर (excellent) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुषमा (loveliness) / ऐन (full) / सरद (autumn) / सर्बरीनाथ (autumn moon) / मुखु (face) / सरद (autumn) / सरोरुह (lotus) / नैन (eyes)
ramacharitamanas::2532.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2532.essence: Their beauty is so complete it makes even language wait.
ramacharitamanas::2532.simple_meaning: Both princes are strikingly beautiful, with moonlike faces and lotus-like eyes.
ramacharitamanas::2532.simple_insight: Beauty can stop a room before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2532.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the women of the house are beholding Ram and Lakshman for the first time. Their beauty leaves everyone speechless, and this line lingers on their appearance before the question of who they are is asked.
ramacharitamanas::2532.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone across a crowded room and forget your own sentence. Some moments begin with beauty before they begin with words.
ramacharitamanas::2532.insight: It pauses the scene on pure appearance, letting wonder build before identity is revealed.

ramacharitamanas::2533.verse_sanskrit: कोटि मनोज लजावनिहारे। सुमुखि कहहु को आहिं तुम्हारे॥ सुनि सनेहमय मंजुल बानी। सकुची सिय मन महुँ मुसुकानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2533.verse_hindi: हे सुमुखि! कहो तो अपनी सुंदरता से करोड़ों कामदेवों को लजाने वाले ये तुम्हारे कौन हैं? उनकी ऐसी प्रेममयी सुंदर वाणी सुनकर सीताजी सकुचा गईं और मन ही मन मुस्कुराईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2533.english_translation: O beautiful one, tell me who these are that shame millions of Cupids. Hearing that tender, lovely speech, Sita grew shy and smiled inwardly.
ramacharitamanas::2533.translation_literal: कोटि (millions) / मनोज (Cupids) / लजावनिहारे (those who shame) / सुमुखि (O beautiful-faced one) / कहहु (tell) / को (who) / आहिं (are) / तुम्हारे (yours) / सुनि (hearing) / सनेहमय (full of affection) / मंजुल (lovely) / बानी (speech) / सकुची (shy) / सिय (Sita) / मन महुँ (within the mind) / मुसुकानी (smiled)
ramacharitamanas::2533.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2533.essence: Gentle speech can make beauty feel even more overwhelming.
ramacharitamanas::2533.simple_meaning: The two princes are so beautiful that they seem to outshine even countless Cupids. Their gentle words make Sita shy and quietly happy.
ramacharitamanas::2533.simple_insight: Even admiration can arrive as tenderness, making the heart both shy and glad.
ramacharitamanas::2533.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Sita is seeing Ram and Lakshman for the first time. Their beauty has already stunned her, and now their affectionate, respectful speech deepens her shy delight. This moment captures the first ripple of mutual attraction before the bow is lifted.
ramacharitamanas::2533.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose kindness is as striking as their appearance, and suddenly you cannot hide your smile. The heart notices before the mind can speak.
ramacharitamanas::2533.insight: It shows how grace, not display, creates the deepest first impression.

ramacharitamanas::2534.verse_sanskrit: तिन्हहि बिलोकि बिलोकति धरनी। दुहुँ सकोच सकुचति बरबरनी॥ सकुचि सप्रेम बाल मृग नयनी। बोली मधुर बचन पिकबयनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2534.verse_hindi: उत्तम (गौर) वर्णवाली सीताजी उनको देखकर (संकोचवश) पृथ्वी की ओर देखती हैं। वे दोनों ओर के संकोच से सकुचा रही हैं (अर्थात न बताने में ग्राम की स्त्रियों को दुःख होने का संकोच है और बताने में लज्जा रूप संकोच)। हिरन के बच्चे के सदृश नेत्र वाली और कोकिल की सी वाणी वाली सीताजी सकुचाकर प्रेम सहित मधुर वचन बोलीं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2534.english_translation: Seeing them, fair Sita looks down at the ground. Shy from both sides, the fair lady grows bashful. Blushing with love, the doe-eyed one speaks sweetly, like a cuckoo.
ramacharitamanas::2534.translation_literal: तिन्हहि (them) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बिलोकति (looks) / धरनी (the ground) । / दुहुँ (from both) / सकोच (shyness) / सकुचति (grows bashful) / बरबरनी (fair lady) ॥ / सकुचि (blushing) / सप्रेम (with love) / बाल मृग नयनी (doe-eyed one) / बोली (spoke) / मधुर (sweet) / बचन (words) / पिकबयनी (cuckoo-voiced) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2534.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2534.essence: Shy love speaks softly before it speaks clearly.
ramacharitamanas::2534.simple_meaning: Sita feels shy when she sees them and lowers her gaze. Blushing with love and modesty, she finally speaks in a soft, sweet voice.
ramacharitamanas::2534.simple_insight: Tenderness can make even first contact feel sacred and careful.
ramacharitamanas::2534.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Sita has just noticed the two princes. Their beauty and presence overwhelm the moment, and she looks down in shy delight. This verse captures the first stirrings of modest, loving speech before she identifies Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::2534.modern_relevance: You meet someone important and suddenly forget your rehearsed words. The pause, the lowered eyes, the careful first sentence — that is human warmth before confidence.
ramacharitamanas::2534.insight: It shows how reverence and affection can shape the very way you speak.

ramacharitamanas::2535.verse_sanskrit: सहज सुभाय सुभग तन गोरे। नामु लखनु लघु देवर मोरे॥ बहुरि बदनु बिधु अंचल ढाँकी। पिय तन चितइ भौंह करि बाँकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2535.verse_hindi: ये जो सहज स्वभाव, सुंदर और गोरे शरीर के हैं, उनका नाम लक्ष्मण है, ये मेरे छोटे देवर हैं। फिर सीताजी ने (लज्जावश) अपने चन्द्रमुख को आँचल से ढँककर और प्रियतम (श्री रामजी) की ओर निहारकर भौंहें टेढ़ी करके, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2535.english_translation: By natural disposition, handsome and fair-bodied, his name is Lakshman, my younger brother-in-law. Then Sita covered her moonlike face with the edge of her veil and, looking at her beloved's body, arched her brows.
ramacharitamanas::2535.translation_literal: सहज (natural) / सुभाय (disposition) / सुभग (beautiful) / तन (body) / गोरे (fair) / नामु (name) / लखनु (Lakshman) / लघु (younger) / देवर (brother-in-law) / मोरे (my) / बहुरि (then) / बदनु (face) / बिधु (moon) / अंचल (edge of veil) / ढाँकी (covered) / पिय (beloved) / तन (body) / चितइ (looking at) / भौंह (brows) / करि (making) / बाँकी (arched)
ramacharitamanas::2535.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2535.essence: Shyness becomes its own language when love is already understood.
ramacharitamanas::2535.simple_meaning: Sita shyly identifies Lakshman as her younger brother-in-law, then hides her face and glances toward Ram with a playful, loving gesture.
ramacharitamanas::2535.simple_insight: Love can be spoken without boldness; a shy glance can carry everything.
ramacharitamanas::2535.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s court, Sita is answering a teasing question about the two handsome brothers. She points out Lakshman first, then, overcome with affection and shyness, covers her face and signals toward Ram. The verse is a small movement in a larger courtship scene.
ramacharitamanas::2535.modern_relevance: At a family gathering, you introduce the person you love with a smile, then look down because everyone already understands more than your words say.
ramacharitamanas::2535.insight: It shows how affection often reveals itself through gesture, not explanation.

ramacharitamanas::2536.verse_sanskrit: खंजन मंजु तिरीछे नयननि। निज पति कहेउ तिन्हहि सियँ सयननि॥ भईं मुदित सब ग्रामबधूटीं। रंकन्ह राय रासि जनु लूटीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2536.verse_hindi: खंजन पक्षी के से सुंदर नेत्रों को तिरछा करके सीताजी ने इशारे से उन्हें कहा कि ये (श्री रामचन्द्रजी) मेरे पति हैं। यह जानकर गाँव की सब युवती स्त्रियाँ इस प्रकार आनंदित हुईं, मानो कंगालों ने धन की राशियाँ लूट ली हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::2536.english_translation: Sita glanced sideways with her beautiful eyes and signaled, “He is my husband.” Hearing this, all the village women rejoiced, as if beggars had found heaps of treasure.
ramacharitamanas::2536.translation_literal: खंजन (like a khanjan bird) / मंजु (lovely) / तिरीछे (sideways) / नयननि (eyes) / निज (own) / पति (husband) / कहेउ (said) / तिन्हहि (to them) / सियँ (Sita) / सयननि (by a glance) / भईं (became) / मुदित (delighted) / सब (all) / ग्रामबधूटीं (village women) / रंकन्ह (of beggars) / राय (royal) / रासि (heap) / जनु (as if) / लूटीं (had been looted)
ramacharitamanas::2536.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2536.essence: Love needs no loud announcement; the heart understands at once.
ramacharitamanas::2536.simple_meaning: Sita quietly points out Ram as her husband, and the village women feel overjoyed at the sight of such a blessed union.
ramacharitamanas::2536.simple_insight: A small gesture can carry immense joy when love is finally seen and understood.
ramacharitamanas::2536.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, Sita is being introduced to the gathered women beside Ram and Lakshman. Too shy to speak openly, she signals with her eyes that Ram is her husband. The women are thrilled, as though they have stumbled on a fortune.
ramacharitamanas::2536.modern_relevance: You catch the look between two people who finally belong together, and everyone nearby feels it. Some joy is so pure it spreads without explanation.
ramacharitamanas::2536.insight: It shows how recognition can transform a quiet moment into shared celebration.

ramacharitamanas::2537.verse_sanskrit: अति सप्रेम सिय पाँय परि बहुबिधि देहिं असीस। सदा सोहागिनि होहु तुम्ह जब लगि महि अहि सीस॥117
ramacharitamanas::2537.verse_hindi: वे अत्यन्त प्रेम से सीताजी के पैरों पड़कर बहुत प्रकार से आशीष देती हैं (शुभ कामना करती हैं), कि जब तक शेषजी के सिर पर पृथ्वी रहे, तब तक तुम सदा सुहागिनी बनी रहो, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2537.english_translation: With deep love, they bowed at Sita's feet and blessed her in many ways: 'May you always remain a blessed wife as long as the earth rests on Shesha's head.'
ramacharitamanas::2537.translation_literal: अति सप्रेम (with deep love) / सिय (Sita) / पाँय परि (falling at the feet) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / देहिं (give) / असीस (blessings) / सदा (always) / सोहागिनि (blessed wife) / होहु (may you be) / तुम्ह (you) / जब लगि (as long as) / महि (earth) / अहि (serpent) / सीस (head)
ramacharitamanas::2537.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2537.essence: Love becomes blessing when it wishes another person lasting wholeness.
ramacharitamanas::2537.simple_meaning: The women lovingly honor Sita and pray that she always remain happily united with her husband.
ramacharitamanas::2537.simple_insight: There is tenderness in wishing someone lasting joy, not just a passing moment of happiness.
ramacharitamanas::2537.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the village women are overwhelmed by Sita's beauty and fortune. They bow at her feet and bless her with the wish that her married life remain auspicious and protected for as long as the world endures.
ramacharitamanas::2537.modern_relevance: At a wedding, an elder quietly blesses the bride after the ceremony, not with grand words but with a wish that her home stay full of warmth and steadiness. That simple blessing carries real love.
ramacharitamanas::2537.insight: It turns admiration into blessing, showing how love naturally wants another person's life to remain whole.

ramacharitamanas::2538.verse_sanskrit: पारबती सम पतिप्रिय होहू। देबि न हम पर छाड़ब छोहू॥ पुनि पुनि बिनय करिअ कर जोरी। जौं एहि मारग फिरिअ बहोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2538.verse_hindi: और पार्वतीजी के समान अपने पति की प्यारी होओ। हे देवी! हम पर कृपा न छोड़ना (बनाए रखना)। हम बार-बार हाथ जोड़कर विनती करती हैं, जिसमें आप फिर इसी रास्ते लौटें, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2538.english_translation: Be as devoted to your husband as Parvati is. O goddess, do not withdraw your grace from us. Again and again, with folded hands, we beg you to return by this path.
ramacharitamanas::2538.translation_literal: पारबती (Parvati) / सम (like) / पतिप्रिय (loving one's husband) / होहू (be) / देबि (O goddess) / न (not) / हम (to us) / पर (on) / छाड़ब (to leave) / छोहू (grace, kindness)॥ / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / बिनय (request, prayer) / करिअ (do) / कर जोरी (with folded hands) / जौं (if) / एहि (this) / मारग (path) / फिरिअ (return) / बहोरी (again)
ramacharitamanas::2538.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2538.essence: True devotion asks for grace without claiming control.
ramacharitamanas::2538.simple_meaning: The women ask Sita to be as devoted to her husband as Parvati is, and to keep showing them kindness so she will return this way again.
ramacharitamanas::2538.simple_insight: Devotion can be asked for with humility, not demand. Love deepens when reverence and longing speak together.
ramacharitamanas::2538.detailed_meaning: Sita has been found in Lanka, and the women around her are overwhelmed by her grace. They pray that she remain as devoted as Parvati and keep blessing them with her kindness, because they long to see her again.
ramacharitamanas::2538.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose steadiness softens a whole room, and you find yourself wanting to ask, almost shyly, that they stay the same. This is the language of reverence, not possession.
ramacharitamanas::2538.insight: It teaches you to honor devotion in others without trying to own it.

ramacharitamanas::2539.verse_sanskrit: दरसनु देब जानि निज दासी। लखीं सीयँ सब प्रेम पिआसी॥ मधुर बचन कहि कहि परितोषीं। जनु कुमुदिनीं कौमुदीं पोषीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2539.verse_hindi: और हमें अपनी दासी जानकर दर्शन दें। सीताजी ने उन सबको प्रेम की प्यासी देखा और मधुर वचन कह-कहकर उनका भलीभाँति संतोष किया। मानो चाँदनी ने कुमुदिनियों को खिलाकर पुष्ट कर दिया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2539.english_translation: Knowing them as her own servants, Sita gave them darshan. Seeing them all thirsty for love, she soothed them with sweet words, like moonlight nourishing night-blooming lilies.
ramacharitamanas::2539.translation_literal: दरसनु (darshan / sacred sight) / देब (to give) / जानि (knowing) / निज (own) / दासी (servants) / लखीं (she saw) / सीयँ (Sita) / सब (all) / प्रेम (love) / पिआसी (thirsty) / मधुर (sweet) / बचन (words) / कहि कहि (speaking again and again) / परितोषीं (she satisfied) / जनु (as if) / कुमुदिनीं (night-lilies) / कौमुदीं (moonlight) / पोषीं (nourished)
ramacharitamanas::2539.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2539.essence: Tenderness satisfies longing more deeply than status ever could.
ramacharitamanas::2539.simple_meaning: Sita welcomes the women kindly, sees their longing, and comforts them with gentle words.
ramacharitamanas::2539.simple_insight: A warm response can soften fear faster than force ever could.
ramacharitamanas::2539.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the women come to see Sita with devotion and longing. Sita treats them as her own, gives them her sight, and answers with sweet words. The scene deepens the tenderness around her departure.
ramacharitamanas::2539.modern_relevance: A room full of people is waiting for your attention, and you can feel their need before they say a word. A few gentle words can change the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::2539.insight: It teaches you to notice emotional hunger and answer it with kindness, not distance.

ramacharitamanas::2540.verse_sanskrit: तबहिं लखन रघुबर रुख जानी। पूँछेउ मगु लोगन्हि मृदु बानी॥ सुनत नारि नर भए दुखारी। पुलकित गात बिलोचन बारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2540.verse_hindi: उसी समय श्री रामचन्द्रजी का रुख जानकर लक्ष्मणजी ने कोमल वाणी से लोगों से रास्ता पूछा। यह सुनते ही स्त्री-पुरुष दुःखी हो गए। उनके शरीर पुलकित हो गए और नेत्रों में (वियोग की सम्भावना से प्रेम का) जल भर आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2540.english_translation: At that moment, seeing Ram's mood, Lakshman politely asked the people for the way. Hearing this, the men and women became sorrowful; their bodies trembled with emotion and tears filled their eyes.
ramacharitamanas::2540.translation_literal: तबहिं (then) / लखन (Lakshman) / रघुबर (Ram) / रुख (mood, direction) / जानी (having known) / पूँछेउ (asked) / मगु (the way) / लोगन्हि (from the people) / मृदु (soft) / बानी (words) // सुनत (hearing) / नारि (women) / नर (men) / भए (became) / दुखारी (sorrowful) / पुलकित (horripilated, thrilled) / गात (bodies) / बिलोचन (eyes) / बारी (water, tears)
ramacharitamanas::2540.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2540.essence: A gentle question can reveal a whole village's grief.
ramacharitamanas::2540.simple_meaning: Lakshman asks local people for the way in a gentle voice. They feel sudden sorrow at the thought of Ram leaving, and tears come to their eyes.
ramacharitamanas::2540.simple_insight: Even a simple question can carry the pain of separation.
ramacharitamanas::2540.detailed_meaning: Lakshman senses Ram's resolve and politely asks the villagers for directions. The people immediately understand what this means: Ram is about to leave them. Their grief rises at once, before any farewell is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2540.modern_relevance: You ask a stranger for directions, and their face changes because they know you are leaving for good. Sometimes the smallest question carries the weight of goodbye.
ramacharitamanas::2540.insight: It shows how deeply people feel Ram's presence, and how quickly the fear of separation spreads.

ramacharitamanas::2541.verse_sanskrit: मिटा मोदु मन भए मलीने। बिधि निधि दीन्ह लेत जनु छीने॥ समुझि करम गति धीरजु कीन्हा। सोधि सुगम मगु तिन्ह कहि दीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2541.verse_hindi: उनका आनंद मिट गया और मन ऐसे उदास हो गए मानो विधाता दी हुई सम्पत्ति छीने लेता हो। कर्म की गति समझकर उन्होंने धैर्य धारण किया और अच्छी तरह निर्णय करके सुगम मार्ग बतला दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2541.english_translation: Their joy faded and their minds turned gloomy, as if fate were snatching away a gift it had given. Understanding the workings of karma, they held their patience and, after careful thought, showed the easy road.
ramacharitamanas::2541.translation_literal: मिटा (faded) / मोदु (joy) / मन (minds) / भए (became) / मलीने (gloomy) / बिधि (fate) / निधि (gift/treasure) / दीन्ह (given) / लेत (taking) / जनु (as if) / छीने (snatching away) / समुझि (understanding) / करम (karma) / गति (working/course) / धीरजु (patience) / कीन्हा (did) / सोधि (searching carefully) / सुगम (easy) / मगु (road) / तिन्ह (they) / कहि (having said) / दीन्हा (gave)
ramacharitamanas::2541.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2541.essence: Patience lets you stay useful even when your heart is heavy.
ramacharitamanas::2541.simple_meaning: The people feel sad when Ram leaves, but they stay calm, understand the situation, and point out the easiest route.
ramacharitamanas::2541.simple_insight: Even hurt can be met with composure, and composure helps you respond wisely.
ramacharitamanas::2541.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are leaving Ayodhya, and the villagers are heartbroken. Their joy collapses, yet they do not panic. Seeing the situation clearly, they steady themselves and guide the travelers on the safest, easiest road.
ramacharitamanas::2541.modern_relevance: You just got difficult news, but someone still needs directions, a decision, or a calm answer. This verse shows how grief and usefulness can coexist.
ramacharitamanas::2541.insight: It teaches you to pause your reaction, understand the situation, and respond with practical calm.

ramacharitamanas::2542.verse_sanskrit: लखन जानकी सहित तब गवनु कीन्ह रघुनाथ। फेरे सब प्रिय बचन कहि लिए लाइ मन साथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2542.verse_hindi: तब लक्ष्मणजी और जानकीजी सहित श्री रघुनाथजी ने गमन किया और सब लोगों को प्रिय वचन कहकर लौटाया, किन्तु उनके मनों को अपने साथ ही लगा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2542.english_translation: Then Raghunath departed with Lakshman and Janaki. He sent everyone back with kind words, yet carried their hearts away with him.
ramacharitamanas::2542.translation_literal: लखन (Lakshman) / जानकी (Janaki) / सहित (together with) / तब (then) / गवनु (departure) / कीन्ह (made) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / फेरे (sent back) / सब (all) / प्रिय (dear) / बचन (words) / कहि (having spoken) / लिए (took) / लाइ (attaching) / मन (hearts / minds) / साथ (with)
ramacharitamanas::2542.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2542.essence: Kind words can soothe departure, but not erase longing.
ramacharitamanas::2542.simple_meaning: Ram leaves with Lakshman and Sita, speaking kindly to the people, but their hearts remain with him.
ramacharitamanas::2542.simple_insight: Some people leave quietly but still carry everyone’s love with them.
ramacharitamanas::2542.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita finally move on from the crowd gathered around them. Ram speaks gently and sends the people back, but the separation is already painful. This is the moment before grief fully breaks open.
ramacharitamanas::2542.modern_relevance: You say a warm goodbye at the train station, but the room still feels empty after they leave. Their kindness helps, yet the ache stays.
ramacharitamanas::2542.insight: It shows how love can remain even after departure, and how a gentle farewell does not erase loss.

ramacharitamanas::2543.verse_sanskrit: फिरत नारि नर अति पछिताहीं। दैअहि दोषु देहिं मन माहीं॥ सहित बिषाद परसपर कहहीं। बिधि करतब उलटे सब अहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2543.verse_hindi: लौटते हुए वे स्त्री-पुरुष बहुत ही पछताते हैं और मन ही मन दैव को दोष देते हैं। परस्पर (बड़े ही) विषाद के साथ कहते हैं कि विधाता के सभी काम उलटे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2543.english_translation: Men and women returning home feel deep regret. They blame fate in their hearts and, in sorrow, tell one another that the workings of fate are all reversed.
ramacharitamanas::2543.translation_literal: फिरत (returning) / नारि नर (women and men) / अति (very) / पछिताहीं (regret) / दैअहि (fate) / दोषु (fault) / देहिं (give) / मन माहीं (in the mind)॥ / सहित (with) / बिषाद (sorrow) / परसपर (to one another) / कहहीं (say) / बिधि (fate's) / करतब (working) / उलटे (reversed) / सब (all) / अहहीं (are) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2543.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2543.essence: Grief makes the heart call the world upside down.
ramacharitamanas::2543.simple_meaning: The people leaving feel regret and blame fate. In their sorrow, they say everything has gone backward.
ramacharitamanas::2543.simple_insight: When loss hits, the mind looks for someone to blame before it can accept what changed.
