ramacharitamanas::2543.detailed_meaning: As Ram, Sita, and Lakshman move away from Ayodhya, the crowd turns back in grief. Men and women who had come to see them now feel the pain of separation and mutter that fate has turned everything upside down.
ramacharitamanas::2543.modern_relevance: You leave a hospital room after bad news and keep replaying the last ten minutes. The mind wants an explanation before it can bear the hurt.
ramacharitamanas::2543.insight: It shows how grief turns the mind toward blame and backward-looking regret instead of clear seeing.

ramacharitamanas::2544.verse_sanskrit: निपट निरंकुस निठुर निसंकू। जेहिं ससि कीन्ह सरुज सकलंकू॥ रूख कलपतरु सागरु खारा। तेहिं पठए बन राजकुमारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2544.verse_hindi: वह विधाता बिल्कुल निरंकुश (स्वतंत्र), निर्दय और निडर है, जिसने चन्द्रमा को रोगी (घटने-बढ़ने वाला) और कलंकी बनाया, कल्पवृक्ष को पेड़ और समुद्र को खारा बनाया। उसी ने इन राजकुमारों को वन में भेजा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2544.english_translation: That utterly unchecked, cruel, and fearless creator made the moon wan and blemished, made the wish-fulfilling tree a mere tree, and made the sea salty. That same power has sent these princes into the forest.
ramacharitamanas::2544.translation_literal: निपट (utterly) / निरंकुस (unchecked) / निठुर (cruel) / निसंकू (fearless) / जेहिं (by whom) / ससि (moon) / कीन्ह (made) / सरुज (wan/sickly) / सकलंकू (blemished) / रूख (tree) / कलपतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / सागरु (sea) / खारा (salty) / तेहिं (by that one) / पठए (sent) / बन (to the forest) / राजकुमारा (princes)
ramacharitamanas::2544.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2544.essence: Grief sees even the world’s beauty as wounded.
ramacharitamanas::2544.simple_meaning: The speaker blames the creator for making even beautiful things imperfect and for sending the princes into exile.
ramacharitamanas::2544.simple_insight: Pain can make the world feel unfair, even when the speaker cannot see the larger pattern.
ramacharitamanas::2544.detailed_meaning: As Ayodhya reels from Ram’s exile, people walking home are stunned and bitter. They blame the force that governs events for turning beauty into imperfection and for sending the beloved princes into the forest. This verse intensifies the grief before the next lament.
ramacharitamanas::2544.modern_relevance: You watch someone kind lose everything in one afternoon, and your mind reaches for someone to blame. Grief often speaks first in accusation.
ramacharitamanas::2544.insight: It shows how sorrow turns perception harsh and makes suffering look like cruelty.

ramacharitamanas::2545.verse_sanskrit: जौं पै इन्हहिं दीन्ह बनबासू। कीन्ह बादि बिधि भोग बिलासू॥ ए बिचरहिं मग बिनु पदत्राना। रचे बादि बिधि बाहन नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2545.verse_hindi: जब विधाता ने इनको वनवास दिया है, तब उसने भोग-विलास व्यर्थ ही बनाए। जब ये बिना जूते के (नंगे ही पैरों) रास्ते में चल रहे हैं, तब विधाता ने अनेकों वाहन (सवारियाँ) व्यर्थ ही रचे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2545.english_translation: If these princes must live in the forest, then luxury was created in vain. If they must walk barefoot on the road, then countless vehicles were created in vain.
ramacharitamanas::2545.translation_literal: जौं (if) / पै (indeed) / इन्हहिं (for these) / दीन्ह (given) / बनबासू (forest exile) / कीन्ह (made) / बादि (in vain) / बिधि (the creator) / भोग (pleasure) / बिलासू (luxury, enjoyment) ॥ ए (these) / बिचरहिं (wander, move) / मग (road, path) / बिनु (without) / पदत्राना (footwear) / रचे (created) / बादि (in vain) / बिधि (the creator) / बाहन (vehicles, mounts) / नाना (many) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2545.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2545.simple_meaning: The verse laments that luxury and vehicles seem pointless when these princes have been sent into forest exile and must travel on foot.
ramacharitamanas::2545.simple_insight: Loss can strip away everything decorative and show what was never necessary.
ramacharitamanas::2545.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the people watch Ram, Lakshman, and Sita disappear into exile. Grief turns into bitter reflection: if such noble people must live in the forest and walk barefoot, then all the comforts of palace life seem wasted.
ramacharitamanas::2545.modern_relevance: You pack for a trip, then the flight is canceled and you end up walking through rain with one bag and sore feet. Suddenly, all the polished plans feel absurd beside what is actually needed.
ramacharitamanas::2545.insight: It shifts the mind from status and comfort to what remains usable in hardship.

ramacharitamanas::2546.verse_sanskrit: ए महि परहिं डासि कुस पाता। सुभग सेज कत सृजत बिधाता॥ तरुबर बास इन्हहि बिधि दीन्हा। धवल धाम रचि रचि श्रमु कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2546.verse_hindi: जब ये कुश और पत्ते बिछाकर जमीन पर ही पड़े रहते हैं, तब विधाता सुंदर सेज (पलंग और बिछौने) किसलिए बनाता है? विधाता ने जब इनको बड़े-बड़े पेड़ों (के नीचे) का निवास दिया, तब उज्ज्वल महलों को बना-बनाकर उसने व्यर्थ ही परिश्रम किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2546.english_translation: When they lie on the ground on kusa grass and leaves, why would the Creator make a beautiful bed? When they have been given life under great trees, the bright palaces built again and again were wasted effort.
ramacharitamanas::2546.translation_literal: ए (these) / महि (on the ground) / परहिं (lie) / डासि (spread) / कुस (kusa grass) / पाता (leaves) / सुभग (beautiful) / सेज (bed) / कत (why) / सृजत (creating) / बिधाता (the Creator) / तरुबर (great trees) / बास (dwelling) / इन्हहि (for these) / बिधि (by fate/Creator) / दीन्हा (given) / धवल (bright/white) / धाम (palaces) / रचि रचि (again and again, constructing) / श्रमु (effort) / कीन्हा (made)
ramacharitamanas::2546.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2546.essence: When simplicity is enough, luxury becomes unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::2546.simple_meaning: The princes have been sent to live simply in the forest, so grand comforts and palaces no longer matter. Their present life makes luxury feel unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::2546.simple_insight: You can feel lighter when you stop measuring life by comfort and display.
ramacharitamanas::2546.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are already moving into forest exile. The poet looks at their bare life on grass and under trees and asks why anyone would build palaces for people destined for such simplicity.
ramacharitamanas::2546.modern_relevance: You unpack into a tiny rented room after losing the apartment you thought was permanent. The bare floor, the thin mattress, the quiet air — suddenly, the expensive things you chased feel less important.
ramacharitamanas::2546.insight: It shifts desire away from display and toward what can actually sustain you.

ramacharitamanas::2547.verse_sanskrit: जौं ए मुनि पट धर जटिल सुंदर सुठि सुकुमार। बिबिध भाँति भूषन बसन बादि किए करतार ॥
ramacharitamanas::2547.verse_hindi: जो ये सुंदर और अत्यन्त सुकुमार होकर मुनियों के (वल्कल) वस्त्र पहनते और जटा धारण करते हैं, तो फिर करतार (विधाता) ने भाँति-भाँति के गहने और कपड़े वृथा ही बनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2547.english_translation: If these handsome, delicate ones wear the dress of sages and matted hair, then the Creator made ornaments and fine clothes in vain.
ramacharitamanas::2547.translation_literal: जौं (if) / ए (these) / मुनि पट (sage-cloth) / धर (wear) / जटिल (matted-haired) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुठि (very) / सुकुमार (delicate) / बिबिध भाँति (in many kinds) / भूषन (ornaments) / बसन (clothes) / बादि (in vain) / किए (made) / करतार (the Creator)
ramacharitamanas::2547.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2547.essence: Real beauty makes ornament feel unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::2547.simple_meaning: Their natural beauty is so complete that even rough sage-clothes and matted hair suit them; compared with that, ornaments and fine clothes seem unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::2547.simple_insight: There is peace in seeing that some forms of beauty need nothing extra.
ramacharitamanas::2547.detailed_meaning: Bharat’s grief has turned into reverence as he imagines Ram, Lakshman, and Sita living in exile. Looking at their delicacy and beauty, he says even the finest ornaments and clothes seem pointless beside them.
ramacharitamanas::2547.modern_relevance: You watch someone leave for a long, hard season with only a backpack and one plain shirt, yet they somehow look more complete than anyone dressed for display. Some people make excess feel unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::2547.insight: It shifts attention from decoration to intrinsic worth, showing that true beauty does not depend on display.

ramacharitamanas::2548.verse_sanskrit: जौं ए कंदमूल फल खाहीं। बादि सुधादि असन जग माहीं॥ एक कहहिं ए सहज सुहाए। आपु प्रगट भए बिधि न बनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2548.verse_hindi: जो ये कन्द, मूल, फल खाते हैं, तो जगत में अमृत आदि भोजन व्यर्थ ही हैं। कोई एक कहते हैं- ये स्वभाव से ही सुंदर हैं (इनका सौंदर्य-माधुर्य नित्य और स्वाभाविक है)। ये अपने-आप प्रकट हुए हैं, ब्रह्मा के बनाए नहीं हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2548.english_translation: If they eat roots, bulbs, and fruits, then nectar-like foods in the world are pointless. Some say they are naturally lovely: their beauty and sweetness are self-evident, not made by Brahma.
ramacharitamanas::2548.translation_literal: जौं (if) / ए (these) / कंदमूल (roots and bulbs) / फल (fruits) / खाहीं (eat) / बादि (vainly) / सुधादि (nectar and such) / असन (foods) / जग माहीं (in the world)॥ / एक (some) / कहहिं (say) / ए (these) / सहज (natural) / सुहाए (lovely) / आपु (themselves) / प्रगट (manifest) / भए (became) / बिधि (Brahma) / न बनाए (not made)
ramacharitamanas::2548.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2548.essence: Simple living can make the finest things seem unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::2548.simple_meaning: Forest life makes simple food feel enough, and these people seem so naturally lovely that their beauty feels self-made, not manufactured.
ramacharitamanas::2548.simple_insight: What looks plain can become the most precious thing in the world.
ramacharitamanas::2548.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the exiled lives of the brothers are being praised through comparison: if they can live on roots and fruits, then rich foods lose their appeal. The verse also says their beauty seems so natural that it feels beyond ordinary making.
ramacharitamanas::2548.modern_relevance: You open a lunchbox after a long day and a simple banana tastes better than a luxury meal. When life is stripped down, what is natural and enough starts to shine.
ramacharitamanas::2548.insight: It shifts attention from luxury to sufficiency, and from manufactured beauty to what is naturally complete.

ramacharitamanas::2549.verse_sanskrit: जहँ लगिबेद कही बिधि करनी। श्रवन नयन मन गोचर बरनी॥ देखहु खोजि भुअन दस चारी। कहँ अस पुरुष कहाँ असि नारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2549.verse_hindi: हमारे कानों, नेत्रों और मन के द्वारा अनुभव में आने वाली विधाता की करनी को जहाँ तक वेदों ने वर्णन करके कहा है, वहाँ तक चौदहों लोकों में ढूँढ देखो, ऐसे पुरुष और ऐसी स्त्रियाँ कहाँ हैं? (कहीं भी नहीं हैं, इसी से सिद्ध है कि ये विधाता के चौदहों लोकों से अलग हैं और अपनी महिमा से ही आप निर्मित हुए हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2549.english_translation: As far as the Vedas describe the workings of the Creator that can be known by hearing, seeing, and mind, search through all fourteen worlds: where are such a man and such a woman? They are nowhere.
ramacharitamanas::2549.translation_literal: जहँ लगि (as far as) बेद (the Vedas) कही (have said) बिधि (the Creator) करनी (work/doing) / श्रवन (hearing) नयन (eyes) मन (mind) गोचर (within reach) बरनी (described)॥ / देखहु (look) खोजि (search) भुअन (worlds) दस चारी (fourteen) / कहँ (where) अस (such) पुरुष (man) कहाँ (where) असि (such) नारी (woman)॥
ramacharitamanas::2549.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2549.simple_meaning: Even the Vedas can only partly describe them. If you search all fourteen worlds, you will not find a man or woman like them.
ramacharitamanas::2549.simple_insight: Some greatness is so complete that comparison itself fails.
ramacharitamanas::2549.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the poet pauses while describing the extraordinary beauty and grace of the figures being spoken of. He says their nature is beyond ordinary description: even sacred texts can only point toward it, and no one in the fourteen worlds compares to them.
ramacharitamanas::2549.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm, dignity, and goodness make every comparison feel small. You stop trying to rank them and simply recognise: this person stands apart.
ramacharitamanas::2549.insight: It shifts the mind from comparison to reverence, letting excellence be seen without reducing it.

ramacharitamanas::2550.verse_sanskrit: इन्हहि देखि बिधि मनु अनुरागा। पटतर जोग बनावै लागा॥ कीन्ह बहुत श्रम ऐक न आए। तेहिं इरिषा बन आनि दुराए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2550.verse_hindi: इन्हें देखकर विधाता का मन अनुरक्त (मुग्ध) हो गया, तब वह भी इन्हीं की उपमा के योग्य दूसरे स्त्री-पुरुष बनाने लगा। उसने बहुत परिश्रम किया, परन्तु कोई उसकी अटकल में ही नहीं आए (पूरे नहीं उतरे)। इसी ईर्षा के मारे उसने इनको जंगल में लाकर छिपा दिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2550.english_translation: Seeing them, the creator's mind became enchanted. He began making others worthy of comparison, but after much effort, none matched them. Out of envy, he brought them into the forest and hid them there.
ramacharitamanas::2550.translation_literal: इन्हहि (seeing these) / देखि (having seen) / बिधि (the creator) / मनु (mind) / अनुरागा (became attached, enchanted) / पटतर (more fitting, more comparable) / जोग (worthy, suitable) / बनावै (to make) / लागा (began) ॥ / कीन्ह (did, made) / बहुत (much) / श्रम (effort, labor) / ऐक (one) / न (not) / आए (came, matched) / तेहिं (by that) / इरिषा (envy) / बन (forest) / आनि (bringing) / दुराए (hid, concealed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2550.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2550.essence: True beauty defeats imitation and exposes the limits of making.
ramacharitamanas::2550.simple_meaning: Their beauty was so complete that even the creator was captivated. He tried to make others like them, but failed, and then hid them in the forest out of envy.
ramacharitamanas::2550.simple_insight: Some beauty cannot be copied or improved on. It leaves even the maker humbled.
ramacharitamanas::2550.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the forest is being described through praise rather than action. The speaker says these figures are so extraordinary that even the creator tried and failed to match them, then hid them away in envy. It continues the same flowing description, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2550.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence makes every polished imitation feel flat. No filter, no upgrade, no careful branding can reproduce what is naturally whole.
ramacharitamanas::2550.insight: It shifts attention from manufactured perfection to the rare presence that cannot be manufactured.

ramacharitamanas::2551.verse_sanskrit: एक कहहिं हम बहुत न जानहिं। आपुहि परम धन्य करि मानहिं॥ ते पुनि पुन्यपुंज हम लेखे। जे देखहिं देखिहहिं जिन्ह देखे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2551.verse_hindi: कोई एक कहते हैं- हम बहुत नहीं जानते। हाँ, अपने को परम धन्य अवश्य मानते हैं (जो इनके दर्शन कर रहे हैं) और हमारी समझ में वे भी बड़े पुण्यवान हैं, जिन्होंने इनको देखा है, जो देख रहे हैं और जो देखेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2551.english_translation: Some say, “We know very little, but we count ourselves supremely blessed.” They also call blessed those who have seen them, who are seeing them, and who will see them.
ramacharitamanas::2551.translation_literal: एक (some) / कहहिं (say) / हम (we) / बहुत (much) / न (not) / जानहिं (know) / आपुहि (ourselves) / परम (supreme) / धन्य (blessed) / करि (having made) / मानहिं (consider) / ते (those) / पुनि (again) / पुन्यपुंज (heap of merit) / हम (we) / लेखे (counted) / जे (those who) / देखहिं (see) / देखिहहिं (will see) / जिन्ह (whom) / देखे (having seen)
ramacharitamanas::2551.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2551.essence: Seeing what is precious makes even simple presence feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2551.simple_meaning: The people are overwhelmed by the sight of these figures. They say they do not know much, but feel deeply blessed just to be there, and they praise anyone who has seen them.
ramacharitamanas::2551.simple_insight: Sometimes presence matters more than understanding.
ramacharitamanas::2551.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, people are gathering around Ram’s family and speaking with wonder. They do not try to explain what they are seeing; they simply feel fortunate. The verse captures a shared awe so strong that even sight itself becomes a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2551.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and feel words fail because something precious is happening there. You do not need to explain it to know you are fortunate to witness it.
ramacharitamanas::2551.insight: It shifts attention from analysis to reverent presence, letting wonder become the response.

ramacharitamanas::2552.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि कहि कहि बचन प्रिय लेहिं नयन भरि नीर। किमि चलिहहिं मारग अगम सुठि सुकुमार सरीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::2552.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार प्रिय वचन कह-कहकर सब नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर लेते हैं और कहते हैं कि ये अत्यन्त सुकुमार शरीर वाले दुर्गम (कठिन) मार्ग में कैसे चलेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2552.english_translation: Saying such loving words, they all fill their eyes with tears and ask, "How will these very delicate bodies walk the difficult road?"
ramacharitamanas::2552.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / कहि कहि (speaking again and again) / बचन (words) / प्रिय (loving) / लेहिं (take) / नयन (eyes) / भरि (filling) / नीर (water, tears) / किमि (how) / चलिहहिं (will they walk) / मारग (road) / अगम (hard to reach, difficult) / सुठि (very) / सुकुमार (delicate) / सरीर (body)
ramacharitamanas::2552.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2552.essence: Love sees the road, then worries about the body that must walk it.
ramacharitamanas::2552.simple_meaning: Everyone speaks with love and tears, worried that such delicate bodies cannot bear the hard journey ahead.
ramacharitamanas::2552.simple_insight: Love can make even simple goodbyes feel unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2552.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the loved ones are parting from Ram, Sita, and Lakshman. Their eyes fill with tears as they try to bless them, but grief keeps returning to one fear: these tender bodies must now face a harsh road.
ramacharitamanas::2552.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love leave with a small bag and tired eyes. The blessing rises in your throat, but what you really feel is fear for their strength.
ramacharitamanas::2552.insight: It turns parting into tenderness, showing how love notices fragility first.

ramacharitamanas::2553.verse_sanskrit: नारि सनेह बिकल बस होहीं। चकईं साँझ समय जनु सोहीं॥ मृदु पद कमल कठिन मगु जानी। गहबरि हृदयँ कहहिं बर बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2553.verse_hindi: स्त्रियाँ स्नेहवश विकल हो जाती हैं। मानो संध्या के समय चकवी (भावी वियोग की पीड़ा से) सोह रही हो। (दुःखी हो रही हो)। इनके चरणकमलों को कोमल तथा मार्ग को कठोर जानकर वे व्यथित हृदय से उत्तम वाणी कहती हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2553.english_translation: Women, overcome by love, become helpless. Like a chakavi at dusk, they seem to sink into sorrow. Knowing the lotus-soft feet are tender and the road is hard, they speak beautiful words from troubled hearts.
ramacharitamanas::2553.translation_literal: नारि (women) / सनेह (affection, love) / बिकल (distressed, overcome) / बस होहीं (become helpless) / चकईं (chakavi birds) / साँझ समय (at dusk) / जनु (as if) / सोहीं (sleep, sink into stillness) / मृदु (soft, tender) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / कठिन (hard, difficult) / मगु (path, road) / जानी (knowing) / गहबरि (anxious, troubled) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / कहहिं (they speak) / बर (excellent, beautiful) / बानी (words)
ramacharitamanas::2553.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2553.essence: Love makes hardship feel unbearable, so the heart speaks gently.
ramacharitamanas::2553.simple_meaning: Love makes them weak with grief. Seeing the feet as tender and the path as hard, they speak gently from troubled hearts.
ramacharitamanas::2553.simple_insight: Deep care can make even brave people tremble when they must let someone go.
ramacharitamanas::2553.detailed_meaning: As the women of Ayodhya watch Ram, Sita, and Lakshman prepare for exile, their love turns into helpless grief. They see the family’s tender feet and the harsh road ahead, so they speak through tears, trying to protect them with words.
ramacharitamanas::2553.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love zip up a bag for a move you cannot stop. Your throat tightens because you know the road will be harder than they admit.
ramacharitamanas::2553.insight: It shows how love can soften speech, even when the heart is breaking.

ramacharitamanas::2554.verse_sanskrit: परसत मृदुल चरन अरुनारे। सकुचति महि जिमि हृदय हमारे॥ जौं जगदीस इन्हहि बनु दीन्हा। कस न सुमनमय मारगु कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2554.verse_hindi: इनके कोमल और लाल-लाल चरणों (तलवों) को छूते ही पृथ्वी वैसे ही सकुचा जाती है, जैसे हमारे हृदय सकुचा रहे हैं। जगदीश्वर ने यदि इन्हें वनवास ही दिया, तो सारे रास्ते को पुष्पमय क्यों नहीं बना दिया? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2554.english_translation: Touching their soft, red feet, the earth shrinks back just as our hearts are shrinking. If the lord of the world has sent them to the forest, why was the whole road not made of flowers?
ramacharitamanas::2554.translation_literal: परसत (touching) / मृदुल (soft) / चरन (feet) / अरुनारे (reddish) / सकुचति (shrinks) / महि (earth) / जिमि (just as) / हृदय (heart) / हमारे (our) / जौं (if) / जगदीस (lord of the world) / इन्हहि (these) / बनु (forest) / दीन्हा (gave) / कस (why) / न (not) / सुमनमय (made of flowers) / मारगु (road)
ramacharitamanas::2554.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2554.essence: Even the road feels wrong when love is being sent away.
ramacharitamanas::2554.simple_meaning: The people are so heartbroken that even the ground seems to recoil under Rama and Sita's tender feet. They wish the exile road itself had been softened for them.
ramacharitamanas::2554.simple_insight: Love makes even a hard road feel unbearable, and the heart longs to protect what it cannot keep.
ramacharitamanas::2554.detailed_meaning: As Rama and Sita leave Ayodhya, the women watching them are overwhelmed by grief. They imagine the earth itself shrinking under Sita's soft feet and ask why a painful exile from the lord of the world could not have been made gentler.
ramacharitamanas::2554.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love leave with a small bag and no complaint, and the whole street feels too hard, too ordinary, too cruel for that moment.
ramacharitamanas::2554.insight: It turns grief into tenderness, making the reader feel how deeply the heart resists separation.

ramacharitamanas::2555.verse_sanskrit: जौं मागा पाइअ बिधि पाहीं। ए रखिअहिं सखि आँखिन्ह माहीं॥ जे नर नारि न अवसर आए। तिन्ह सिय रामु न देखन पाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2555.verse_hindi: यदि ब्रह्मा से माँगे मिले तो हे सखी! (हम तो उनसे माँगकर) इन्हें अपनी आँखों में ही रखें! जो स्त्री-पुरुष इस अवसर पर नहीं आए, वे श्री सीतारामजी को नहीं देख सके ॥
ramacharitamanas::2555.english_translation: If such a sight could be obtained by asking Brahma, friend, we would keep it in our eyes. Men and women who did not come at this moment did not get to see Siya-Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2555.translation_literal: जौं (if) / मागा (asked for) / पाइअ (is obtained) / बिधि (Brahma, the creator) / पाहीं (from) / ए (these) / रखिअहिं (let them be kept) / सखि (friend) / आँखिन्ह (in the eyes) / माहीं (within) / जे (those who) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / न (not) / अवसर (opportunity, occasion) / आए (came) / तिन्ह (they) / सिय रामु (Sita and Ram) / न (not) / देखन (to see) / पाए (got)
ramacharitamanas::2555.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2555.essence: Some sights are so precious you want to keep them in your eyes forever.
ramacharitamanas::2555.simple_meaning: The speaker says this sight is so precious that, if it could be asked from Brahma, it should be kept in the eyes forever. Anyone who missed this moment missed seeing Sita and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2555.simple_insight: Some moments feel so rare that missing them feels like missing a lifetime.
ramacharitamanas::2555.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the people gather in excitement around Sita and Ram. The speaker marvels at their beauty and says this is a sight worth preserving forever. The verse also gently notes that anyone absent at this moment has missed something unforgettable.
ramacharitamanas::2555.modern_relevance: You scroll past the invitation, assume there will be another chance, and later hear everyone talk about the one evening you skipped. Some moments do not repeat.
ramacharitamanas::2555.insight: It teaches you to recognise rare, life-defining moments before they pass.

ramacharitamanas::2556.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुरूपु बूझहिं अकुलाई। अब लगि गए कहाँ लगि भाई॥ समरथ धाइ बिलोकहिं जाई। प्रमुदित फिरहिं जनमफलु पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2556.verse_hindi: उनके सौंदर्य को सुनकर वे व्याकुल होकर पूछते हैं कि भाई! अब तक वे कहाँ तक गए होंगे? और जो समर्थ हैं, वे दौड़ते हुए जाकर उनके दर्शन कर लेते हैं और जन्म का परम फल पाकर, विशेष आनंदित होकर लौटते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2556.english_translation: Hearing of his beauty, they anxiously ask, “Brother, how far has he gone now?” The capable run to see him and return delighted, having found the fruit of life.
ramacharitamanas::2556.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुरूपु (beautiful form) / बूझहिं (they ask) / अकुलाई (anxiously) / अब लगि (until now) / गए (has gone) / कहाँ लगि (up to where) / भाई (brother) / समरथ (the capable) / धाइ (running) / बिलोकहिं (they behold) / जाई (going) / प्रमुदित (delighted) / फिरहिं (they return) / जनमफलु (fruit of life) / पाई (having obtained)
ramacharitamanas::2556.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2556.essence: Ram’s beauty makes people restless until they reach him.
ramacharitamanas::2556.simple_meaning: People are so moved by Ram’s beauty that they ask where he has gone. The able rush to see him and feel they have gained life’s highest reward.
ramacharitamanas::2556.simple_insight: Even a glimpse of what is truly beautiful can make ordinary life feel suddenly complete.
ramacharitamanas::2556.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram’s presence turns the streets of Ayodhya into a place of longing. People hear of his beauty, grow restless, ask where he has gone, and the fortunate who can run to him return overjoyed. This verse completes that public wave of devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2556.modern_relevance: You hear someone mention a person who changed the whole room, and suddenly you need to see for yourself. The ones who make the effort come back lighter, as if they found something they had been missing.
ramacharitamanas::2556.insight: It shifts attention from passive admiration to active seeking, showing that closeness transforms longing into joy.

ramacharitamanas::2557.verse_sanskrit: अबला बालक बृद्ध जन कर मीजहिं पछिताहिं। होहिं प्रेमबस लोग इमि रामु जहाँ जहँ जाहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2557.verse_hindi: (गर्भवती, प्रसूता आदि) अबला स्त्रियाँ, बच्चे और बूढ़े (दर्शन न पाने से) हाथ मलते और पछताते हैं। इस प्रकार जहाँ-जहाँ श्री रामचन्द्रजी जाते हैं, वहाँ-वहाँ लोग प्रेम के वश में हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2557.english_translation: Women, children, and the elderly rub their hands in regret when they miss seeing Ram. Wherever Ram goes, people are overcome by love.
ramacharitamanas::2557.translation_literal: अबला (helpless women) / बालक (children) / बृद्ध जन (elderly people) / कर मीजहिं (rub their hands) / पछिताहिं (regret) / होहिं (become) / प्रेमबस (under the power of love) / लोग (people) / इमि (thus) / रामु (Ram) / जहाँ जहाँ (wherever) / जाहिं (goes)
ramacharitamanas::2557.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2557.essence: Ram's presence turns regret into love.
ramacharitamanas::2557.simple_meaning: Ram's presence moves everyone, especially the vulnerable. People feel regret if they miss him, because his arrival awakens love in them.
ramacharitamanas::2557.simple_insight: Being near what is truly beautiful makes the heart melt without effort.
ramacharitamanas::2557.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, people are rushing to glimpse Ram as he moves through the city. Women, children, and the elderly feel the sharpest regret if they miss him. The verse shows that Ram's presence naturally draws love from everyone around him.
ramacharitamanas::2557.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone who changes a room, and suddenly everyone leans in. No speech, no performance — just a presence that makes people feel more alive.
ramacharitamanas::2557.insight: It shifts attention from Ram's actions to the magnetic effect of his presence on ordinary people.

ramacharitamanas::2558.verse_sanskrit: गाँव गाँव अस होइ अनंदू। देखि भानुकुल कैरव चंदू॥ जे कछु समाचार सुनि पावहिं। ते नृप रानिहि दोसु लगावहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2558.verse_hindi: सूर्यकुल रूपी कुमुदिनी को प्रफुल्लित करने वाले चन्द्रमा स्वरूप श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन कर गाँव-गाँव में ऐसा ही आनंद हो रहा है, जो लोग (वनवास दिए जाने का) कुछ भी समाचार सुन पाते हैं, वे राजा-रानी (दशरथ-कैकेयी) को दोष लगाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2558.english_translation: In village after village there is such joy at seeing Ram, the moon of the solar dynasty. But when people hear even a little of the exile, they blame the king and queen.
ramacharitamanas::2558.translation_literal: गाँव गाँव (village after village) / अस (such) / होइ (happens) / अनंदू (joy) / देखि (seeing) / भानुकुल (solar dynasty) / कैरव (water lily) / चंदू (moon) ॥ / जे (those who) / कछु (some) / समाचार (news) / सुनि (hearing) / पावहिं (receive) / ते (they) / नृप (king) / रानिहि (queen) / दोसु (blame) / लगावहिं (attach)
ramacharitamanas::2558.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2558.essence: Ram's joy is public; his exile becomes everyone's grief.
ramacharitamanas::2558.simple_meaning: Ram's presence brings joy everywhere. But news of his exile makes people blame Dasharath and Kaikeyi.
ramacharitamanas::2558.simple_insight: A beloved person's suffering spreads pain beyond the family. The heart that loves also feels injustice quickly.
ramacharitamanas::2558.detailed_meaning: As Ram is seen and remembered in village after village, people rejoice at the moon of the Raghu line. Yet the same crowd, hearing of his exile, turns to anger and blames Dasharath and Kaikeyi. The scene shows how deeply the exile has wounded the land.
ramacharitamanas::2558.modern_relevance: You hear one painful detail about a friend's breakup, and suddenly the whole story feels unfair. People don't stay neutral when someone beloved has been hurt.
ramacharitamanas::2558.insight: It shifts attention from celebration to collective grief, showing how public feeling can turn into moral judgment.

ramacharitamanas::2559.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं एक अति भल नरनाहू। दीन्ह हमहि जोइ लोचन लाहू॥ कहहिं परसपर लोग लोगाईं। बातें सरल सनेह सुहाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2559.verse_hindi: कोई एक कहते हैं कि राजा बहुत ही अच्छे हैं, जिन्होंने हमें अपने नेत्रों का लाभ दिया। स्त्री-पुरुष सभी आपस में सीधी, स्नेहभरी सुंदर बातें कह रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2559.english_translation: Some say, “The king is very noble; he has given us the gift of seeing him.” Men and women speak to one another in simple, loving, delightful words.
ramacharitamanas::2559.translation_literal: कहहिं (they say) / एक (some) / अति (very) / भल (good, noble) / नरनाहू (king) / दीन्ह (gave) / हमहि (to us) / जोइ (that which) / लोचन लाहू (profit of the eyes, the gift of seeing) / कहहिं (say) / परसपर (to one another) / लोग (people) / लोगाईं (men and women) / बातें (talks) / सरल (simple) / सनेह (love) / सुहाईं (pleasant, lovely)
ramacharitamanas::2559.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2559.essence: Ram’s presence turns strangers into gentle, grateful people.
ramacharitamanas::2559.simple_meaning: People are so happy to see Ram that they praise the king and speak lovingly to one another.
ramacharitamanas::2559.simple_insight: His presence makes ordinary people kinder, softer, and grateful.
ramacharitamanas::2559.detailed_meaning: As Ram moves through the land in exile, whole villages brighten just from seeing him. People praise Dasharath’s son as a noble king and speak to one another with warmth. This verse shows the social ripple of Ram’s presence, setting up the deeper praise that follows.
ramacharitamanas::2559.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a hard week, and the mood changes before you say a word. People relax, smile, and speak more gently because your presence feels safe.
ramacharitamanas::2559.insight: It shows how a steady, respectful presence can transform the tone of everyone around you.

ramacharitamanas::2560.verse_sanskrit: ते पितु मातु धन्य जिन्ह जाए। धन्य सो नगरु जहाँ तें आए॥ धन्य सो देसु सैलु बन गाऊँ। जहँ-जहँ जाहिं धन्य सोइ ठाऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2560.verse_hindi: (कहते हैं-) वे माता-पिता धन्य हैं, जिन्होंने इन्हें जन्म दिया। वह नगर धन्य है, जहाँ से ये आए हैं। वह देश, पर्वत, वन और गाँव धन्य है और वही स्थान धन्य है, जहाँ-जहाँ ये जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2560.english_translation: Blessed are the parents who gave them birth. Blessed is the city they came from. Blessed is the land, hill, forest, and village. Blessed is every place they visit.
ramacharitamanas::2560.translation_literal: ते (those) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / धन्य (blessed) / जिन्ह (who) / जाए (were born) / धन्य (blessed) / सो (that) / नगरु (city) / जहाँ (where) / तें (from) / आए (came) / धन्य (blessed) / सो (that) / देसु (land) / सैलु (hill) / बन (forest) / गाऊँ (village) / जहँ-जहँ (wherever) / जाहिं (they go) / धन्य (blessed) / सोइ (that very) / ठाऊँ (place)
ramacharitamanas::2560.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2560.essence: Ram makes every place and every family feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2560.simple_meaning: People feel that Ram makes every place and every family blessed just by being there.
ramacharitamanas::2560.simple_insight: Being near what is noble changes how you see everything around it.
ramacharitamanas::2560.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, people are speaking with wonder about Ram and Lakshman as they pass through the land. Their presence feels so pure and auspicious that parents, cities, forests, and villages are all praised as blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2560.modern_relevance: A friend walks into a tense family gathering and the whole room softens. You realize some people don't just enter a place — they change its atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::2560.insight: It shifts attention from physical location to the moral and emotional quality a person brings into it.

ramacharitamanas::2561.verse_sanskrit: सुखु पायउ बिरंचि रचि तेही। ए जेहि के सब भाँति सनेही॥ राम लखन पथि कथा सुहाई। रही सकल मग कानन छाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2561.verse_hindi: ब्रह्मा ने उसी को रचकर सुख पाया है, जिसके ये (श्री रामचन्द्रजी) सब प्रकार से स्नेही हैं। पथिक रूप श्री राम-लक्ष्मण की सुंदर कथा सारे रास्ते और जंगल में छा गई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2561.english_translation: Brahma found fulfillment in creating the one whom Ram loves in every way. The sweet story of Ram and Lakshman as travelers spread through the roads and forests.
ramacharitamanas::2561.translation_literal: सुखु (happiness) / पायउ (found) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / रचि (creating) / तेही (that one) / ए (this) / जेहि (whom) / के (of whom) / सब (all) / भाँति (ways) / सनेही (loving) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / पथि (on the road) / कथा (story) / सुहाई (sweet) / रही (remained) / सकल (all) / मग (paths) / कानन (forests) / छाई (spread)
ramacharitamanas::2561.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2561.essence: Ram’s presence turns even exile into something sweet.
ramacharitamanas::2561.simple_meaning: Brahma feels fulfilled only in creating the one whom Ram loves completely. Then Ram and Lakshman’s journey becomes such a beloved story that it spreads everywhere they pass.
ramacharitamanas::2561.simple_insight: Being loved by the divine makes even an ordinary journey feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2561.detailed_meaning: As Ram and Lakshman walk through exile, people along the road are so moved that their simple presence becomes a sweet story. The verse praises both Ram’s universal affection and the way their journey blesses every place they pass through.
ramacharitamanas::2561.modern_relevance: A quiet walk to a new city, carrying your bag and your worries, can still change the whole mood of the street. Some people leave behind a trail of calm just by being present.
ramacharitamanas::2561.insight: It shifts attention from the travelers themselves to the blessing their presence brings to others.

ramacharitamanas::2562.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि रघुकुल कमल रबि मग लोगन्ह सुख देत। जाहिं चले देखत बिपिन सिय सौमित्रि समेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::2562.verse_hindi: रघुकुल रूपी कमल को खिलाने वाले सूर्य श्री रामचन्द्रजी इस प्रकार मार्ग के लोगों को सुख देते हुए सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित वन को देखते हुए चले जा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2562.english_translation: In this way, Ram, the sun of the Raghu line, gave joy to the people on the road as he walked through the forest with Sita and Saumitra, looking around.
ramacharitamanas::2562.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / रघुकुल (Raghu clan) / कमल (lotus) / रबि (sun) / मग (road) / लोगन्ह (to the people) / सुख (joy) / देत (giving) / जाहिं (going) / चले (walked) / देखत (looking) / बिपिन (forest) / सिय (Sita) / सौमित्रि (Saumitra) / समेत (together with)
ramacharitamanas::2562.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2562.essence: Their presence itself turns hardship into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2562.simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman move through the forest, and everyone who sees them feels blessed and happy.
ramacharitamanas::2562.simple_insight: Even a difficult journey can become a source of comfort when your presence brings ease to others.
ramacharitamanas::2562.detailed_meaning: The exile procession continues through the forest. Ram walks with Sita and Lakshman, and the people along the road feel uplifted just by seeing them. This is a quiet scene of grace, not a teaching moment.
ramacharitamanas::2562.modern_relevance: You pass through a hard season, but your calm presence still changes the room. Even while carrying your own burden, you can leave others feeling lighter.
ramacharitamanas::2562.insight: It shows how steady conduct can bless others without a speech or display.

ramacharitamanas::2563.verse_sanskrit: आगें रामु लखनु बने पाछें। तापस बेष बिराजत काछें॥ उभय बीच सिय सोहति कैसें। ब्रह्म जीव बिच माया जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2563.verse_hindi: आगे श्री रामजी हैं, पीछे लक्ष्मणजी सुशोभित हैं। तपस्वियों के वेष बनाए दोनों बड़ी ही शोभा पा रहे हैं। दोनों के बीच में सीताजी कैसी सुशोभित हो रही हैं, जैसे ब्रह्म और जीव के बीच में माया! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2563.english_translation: Ram and Lakshman stand ahead, dressed as ascetics behind. How beautifully Sita shines between them, like Maya between Brahman and the individual self.
ramacharitamanas::2563.translation_literal: आगें (in front) / रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / बने (having become) / पाछें (behind) / तापस बेष (ascetic guise) / बिराजत (shining, dwelling) / काछें (nearby) ॥ / उभय (both) / बीच (between) / सिय (Sita) / सोहति (shines beautifully) / कैसें (how) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / जीव (individual self) / बिच (between) / माया (Maya) / जैसें (like) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2563.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2563.essence: A forest image turns into a map of reality itself.
ramacharitamanas::2563.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman walk in front and behind in ascetic dress, with Sita shining between them like Maya between the supreme reality and the individual self.
ramacharitamanas::2563.simple_insight: Even a simple image can carry a whole philosophy of how appearance, devotion, and identity relate.
ramacharitamanas::2563.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the three leave behind palace life and move through the forest in plain ascetic dress. Tulsidas pauses on the sight itself: Ram ahead, Lakshman behind, and Sita between them. The image becomes a spiritual comparison, not just a description.
ramacharitamanas::2563.modern_relevance: You see a family walking through an airport after a life-changing move, dressed simply, carrying everything they own. The scene looks ordinary, but it already holds a whole story of loss, role, and hidden meaning.
ramacharitamanas::2563.insight: It trains the mind to read visible scenes as symbols of deeper reality.

ramacharitamanas::2564.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि कहउँ छबि जसि मन बसई। जनु मधु मदन मध्य रति लसई॥ उपमा बहुरि कहउँ जियँ जोही। जनु बुध बिधु बिच रोहिनि सोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2564.verse_hindi: फिर जैसी छबि मेरे मन में बस रही है, उसको कहता हूँ- मानो वसंत ऋतु और कामदेव के बीच में रति (कामेदव की स्त्री) शोभित हो। फिर अपने हृदय में खोजकर उपमा कहता हूँ कि मानो बुध (चंद्रमा के पुत्र) और चन्द्रमा के बीच में रोहिणी (चन्द्रमा की स्त्री) सोह रही हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2564.english_translation: Again I describe the beauty as it lives in my mind: like Rati shining between Madhu and Madan. Again I search my heart for a fitting comparison: like Rohini shining between Budh and the moon.
ramacharitamanas::2564.translation_literal: बहुरि (again) / कहउँ (I say) / छबि (beauty) / जसि (as) / मन (mind) / बसई (dwells) / जनु (as if) / मधु (spring) / मदन (Kama) / मध्य (between) / रति (Rati) / लसई (shines) ॥ उपमा (comparison) / बहुरि (again) / कहउँ (I say) / जियँ (in the heart) / जोही (having searched) / जनु (as if) / बुध (Budh) / बिधु (moon) / बिच (between) / रोहिनि (Rohini) / सोही (adorns herself) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2564.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2564.essence: True beauty makes even poetry feel inadequate.
ramacharitamanas::2564.simple_meaning: The speaker keeps searching for the best comparison to describe Sita's beauty, using celestial and poetic images.
ramacharitamanas::2564.simple_insight: Some beauty feels too full for ordinary speech; the mind reaches for the nearest stars.
ramacharitamanas::2564.detailed_meaning: As Ram, Lakshman, and Sita walk through the forest in exile, the poet pauses to marvel at Sita's radiance. He keeps searching for images strong enough to hold her beauty, but even his comparisons only circle around it.
ramacharitamanas::2564.modern_relevance: You try to explain someone you love, and every sentence feels too small. The feeling is real, but language keeps falling short.
ramacharitamanas::2564.insight: It shifts attention from literal description to the limits of language before beauty.

ramacharitamanas::2565.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु पद रेख बीच बिच सीता। धरति चरन मग चलति सभीता॥ सीय राम पद अंक बराएँ। लखन चलहिं मगु दाहिन लाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2565.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के (जमीन पर अंकित होने वाले दोनों) चरण चिह्नों के बीच-बीच में पैर रखती हुई सीताजी (कहीं भगवान के चरण चिह्नों पर पैर न टिक जाए इस बात से) डरती हुईं मार्ग में चल रही हैं और लक्ष्मणजी (मर्यादा की रक्षा के लिए) सीताजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी दोनों के चरण चिह्नों को बचाते हुए दाहिने रखकर रास्ता चल रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2565.english_translation: Sita walks carefully, placing her feet between Rama's footprints, afraid of stepping on his sacred marks. Lakshman walks on the right, guarding the footprints of both Sita and Rama.
ramacharitamanas::2565.translation_literal: प्रभु (lord) / पद रेख (footprints) / बीच बीच (between, between) / सीता (Sita) / धरति (placing) / चरन (feet) / मग (path) / चलति (walking) / सभीता (with fear)॥ / सीय (Sita) / राम (Rama) / पद (feet) / अंक (marks) / बराएँ (protecting) / लखन (Lakshman) / चलहिं (walk) / मगु (path) / दाहिन (right side) / लाएँ (keeping, bringing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2565.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2565.essence: Reverence and service can shape even the way you walk.
ramacharitamanas::2565.simple_meaning: Sita walks so carefully that she avoids stepping on Rama's footprints, and Lakshman walks beside them to protect both of them.
ramacharitamanas::2565.simple_insight: Love becomes visible in the smallest acts of care and protection.
ramacharitamanas::2565.detailed_meaning: On the road in exile, Rama, Sita, and Lakshman move together like a living picture of devotion. Sita avoids even Rama's footprints out of reverence, while Lakshman stays to the side, guarding their path and their honour.
ramacharitamanas::2565.modern_relevance: You notice someone lowering their voice in a hospital corridor so a sleeping child won't wake. That quiet restraint, that protection of another's peace, is what this scene feels like.
ramacharitamanas::2565.insight: It teaches you that devotion and service are shown through careful conduct, not loud declarations.

ramacharitamanas::2566.verse_sanskrit: राम लखन सिय प्रीति सुहाई। बचन अगोचर किमि कहि जाई॥ खग मृग मगन देखि छबि होहीं। लिए चोरि चित राम बटोहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2566.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी की सुंदर प्रीति वाणी का विषय नहीं है (अर्थात अनिर्वचनीय है), अतः वह कैसे कही जा सकती है? पक्षी और पशु भी उस छबि को देखकर (प्रेमानंद में) मग्न हो जाते हैं। पथिक रूप श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने उनके भी चित्त चुरा लिए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2566.english_translation: The lovely affection of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita cannot be put into words. Birds and animals, too, are captivated by their beauty. Ram, the traveler on the road, has stolen even their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::2566.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / प्रीति (loving affection) / सुहाई (beautiful) / बचन (words) / अगोचर (beyond speech) / किमि (how) / कहि (spoken) / जाई (can be said) / खग (birds) / मृग (animals) / मगन (absorbed) / देखि (seeing) / छबि (beauty) / होहीं (become) / लिए (taken) / चोरि (stolen) / चित (minds) / राम (Ram) / बटोहीं (traveler)
ramacharitamanas::2566.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2566.essence: Their love is so radiant that even the world around them is transformed.
ramacharitamanas::2566.simple_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita share a beauty and affection so deep that words cannot capture it. Even birds and animals are moved by seeing them.
ramacharitamanas::2566.simple_insight: Some presence is so pure that it softens every heart around it.
ramacharitamanas::2566.detailed_meaning: As Ram, Sita, and Lakshman move along the forest path in exile, the poet pauses to describe their beauty and tenderness. Their bond is so radiant that even birds and animals are enchanted, and the whole scene feels touched by grace.
ramacharitamanas::2566.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a hard day, and the tension shifts before anyone speaks. Some people carry a quiet beauty that calms everything around them.
ramacharitamanas::2566.insight: It shifts attention from what is said to the power of lived presence.

ramacharitamanas::2567.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह जिन्ह देखे पथिक प्रिय सिय समेत दोउ भाइ। भव मगु अगमु अनंदु तेइ बिनु श्रम रहे सिराइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2567.verse_hindi: प्यारे पथिक सीताजी सहित दोनों भाइयों को जिन-जिन लोगों ने देखा, उन्होंने भव का अगम मार्ग (जन्म-मृत्यु रूपी संसार में भटकने का भयानक मार्ग) बिना ही परिश्रम आनंद के साथ तय कर लिया (अर्थात वे आवागमन के चक्र से सहज ही छूटकर मुक्त हो गए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2567.english_translation: Whoever sees Sita and both brothers, the hard road of worldly wandering becomes effortless and joyful for them; they are freed without strain.
ramacharitamanas::2567.translation_literal: जिन्ह जिन्ह (whoever) / देखे (saw) / पथिक (travellers) / प्रिय (beloved) / सिय (Sita) / समेत (together with) / दोउ (both) / भाइ (brothers) / भव (worldly becoming) / मगु (path) / अगमु (hard to reach) / अनंदु (joy) / तेइ (they) / बिनु (without) / श्रम (effort) / रहे (remained) / सिराइ (ended)
ramacharitamanas::2567.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2567.essence: Their presence makes even the hardest journey feel effortless.
ramacharitamanas::2567.simple_meaning: Anyone who sees Sita and the two brothers finds the difficult path through worldly life becoming easy and joyful.
ramacharitamanas::2567.simple_insight: Devotion can change the felt weight of life itself.
ramacharitamanas::2567.detailed_meaning: As Ram, Sita, and Lakshman walk the forest road, their beauty and presence transform everyone who sees them. Tulsidas says that simply beholding them eases the painful journey through worldly existence.
ramacharitamanas::2567.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a brutal week, and one calm, loving presence steadies you at once. Some people do not solve your life; they make the road bearable.
ramacharitamanas::2567.insight: It shifts attention from the difficulty of the path to the transforming power of holy company.

ramacharitamanas::2568.verse_sanskrit: अजहुँ जासु उर सपनेहुँ काऊ। बसहुँ लखनु सिय रामु बटाऊ॥ राम धाम पथ पाइहि सोई। जो पथ पाव कबहु मुनि कोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2568.verse_hindi: आज भी जिसके हृदय में स्वप्न में भी कभी लक्ष्मण, सीता, राम तीनों बटोही आ बसें, तो वह भी श्री रामजी के परमधाम के उस मार्ग को पा जाएगा, जिस मार्ग को कभी कोई बिरले ही मुनि पाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2568.english_translation: Even now, the one whose heart holds Lakshman, Sita, and Ram, even in a dream, will find Ram's abode — a path that only rare sages ever reach.
ramacharitamanas::2568.translation_literal: अजहुँ (even now) / जासु (whose) / उर (heart) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / काऊ (someone) / बसहुँ (dwell) / लखनु (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / रामु (Ram) / बटाऊ (travellers) ॥ राम धाम (Ram's abode) / पथ (path) / पाइहि (will obtain) / सोई (that one) / जो (who) / पथ (path) / पाव (finds) / कबहु (ever) / मुनि (sage) / कोई (someone) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2568.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2568.essence: Keeping Ram in your heart makes the impossible path reachable.
ramacharitamanas::2568.simple_meaning: Anyone who keeps Ram, Sita, and Lakshman in the heart, even in dreams, can reach Ram's divine abode. Devotion opens a path that even sages rarely find.
ramacharitamanas::2568.simple_insight: Love and remembrance can take you where effort alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::2568.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the forest journey has become a sacred sight. The poet says that even a dream-level closeness to Ram, Sita, and Lakshman can open the way to Ram's abode. This is not just travel; it is grace made reachable.
ramacharitamanas::2568.modern_relevance: You fall asleep replaying the face of someone you love, or the loss you fear, and wake changed. This verse says the heart you keep through the night shapes the road you walk by day.
ramacharitamanas::2568.insight: It shifts devotion from ritual to remembrance: what lives in the heart becomes the path under your feet.

ramacharitamanas::2569.verse_sanskrit: तब रघुबीर श्रमित सिय जानी। देखि निकट बटु सीतल पानी॥ तहँ बसि कंद मूल फल खाई। प्रात नहाइ चले रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2569.verse_hindi: तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी सीताजी को थकी हुई जानकर और समीप ही एक बड़ का वृक्ष और ठंडा पानी देखकर उस दिन वहीं ठहर गए। कन्द, मूल, फल खाकर (रात भर वहाँ रहकर) प्रातःकाल स्नान करके श्री रघुनाथजी आगे चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2569.english_translation: Then Lord Raghubir, seeing Sita tired and finding a banyan tree and cool water nearby, stayed there. They ate roots, bulbs, and fruit, and at dawn bathed and set out again.
ramacharitamanas::2569.translation_literal: तब (then) / रघुबीर (Raghubir, Ram) / श्रमित (tired) / सिय (Sita) / जानी (knowing) / देखि (seeing) / निकट (nearby) / बटु (banyan tree) / सीतल (cool) / पानी (water) / तहँ (there) / बसि (staying) / कंद (roots/bulbs) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruit) / खाई (eating) / प्रात (morning) / नहाइ (bathed) / चले (set out) / रघुराई (Lord of the Raghu line, Ram)
ramacharitamanas::2569.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2569.essence: Love notices fatigue and turns it into rest.
ramacharitamanas::2569.simple_meaning: Ram notices Sita is tired, so he stops where there is shade and cool water. They rest, eat simple forest food, bathe in the morning, and continue on their way.
ramacharitamanas::2569.simple_insight: Care sometimes looks like stopping, not pushing harder.
ramacharitamanas::2569.detailed_meaning: On the road through the forest, Ram sees that Sita is exhausted. He finds a banyan tree and cool water, so the three travelers rest there, eat what the forest offers, and leave at dawn. The verse shows their tender, practical care during exile.
ramacharitamanas::2569.modern_relevance: You notice your partner is worn out after a long day, so you skip the plan, find water, sit down, and let the evening become gentler.
ramacharitamanas::2569.insight: It teaches you to respond to another person's fatigue with immediate, practical care.

ramacharitamanas::2570.verse_sanskrit: देखत बन सर सैल सुहाए। बालमीकि आश्रम प्रभु आए॥ राम दीख मुनि बासु सुहावन। सुंदर गिरि काननु जलु पावन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2570.verse_hindi: सुंदर वन, तालाब और पर्वत देखते हुए प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी वाल्मीकिजी के आश्रम में आए। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने देखा कि मुनि का निवास स्थान बहुत सुंदर है, जहाँ सुंदर पर्वत, वन और पवित्र जल है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2570.english_translation: Seeing the lovely forests, lakes, and hills, Lord Ram came to Valmiki's hermitage. Ram saw the sage's dwelling as beautiful, with lovely mountains, forests, and pure water.
ramacharitamanas::2570.translation_literal: देखत (seeing) / बन (forest) / सर (lakes) / सैल (hills) / सुहाए (lovely) / बालमीकि (Valmiki's) / आश्रम (hermitage) / प्रभु (Lord) / आए (came) / राम (Ram) / दीख (saw) / मुनि (sage) / बासु (dwelling) / सुहावन (beautiful) / सुंदर (beautiful) / गिरि (mountains) / काननु (forest) / जलु (water) / पावन (pure)
ramacharitamanas::2570.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2570.essence: Beauty itself can prepare the heart for holy company.
ramacharitamanas::2570.simple_meaning: Ram arrives at Valmiki's hermitage and sees its natural beauty — hills, forests, and pure water.
ramacharitamanas::2570.simple_insight: Sacred places feel alive when the mind is calm enough to notice beauty.
ramacharitamanas::2570.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are still moving through the forest in exile. As they reach Valmiki's hermitage, the scene pauses on the beauty of the place itself: hills, trees, lakes, and clean water. The verse simply opens the setting before the next action.
ramacharitamanas::2570.modern_relevance: You step off a noisy road into a quiet garden and your shoulders drop before anyone speaks. Some places steady you just by receiving you.
ramacharitamanas::2570.insight: It shifts attention from plot to atmosphere, letting the setting prepare the heart for what follows.

ramacharitamanas::2571.verse_sanskrit: सरनि सरोज बिटप बन फूले। गुंजत मंजु मधुप रस भूले॥ खग मृग बिपुल कोलाहल करहीं। बिरहित बैर मुदित मन चरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2571.verse_hindi: सरोवरों में कमल और वनों में वृक्ष फूल रहे हैं और मकरन्द रस में मस्त हुए भौंरे सुंदर गुंजार कर रहे हैं। बहुत से पक्षी और पशु कोलाहल कर रहे हैं और वैर से रहित होकर प्रसन्न मन से विचर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2571.english_translation: Lotuses bloom in the lakes and trees bloom in the forest. Bees hum sweetly, drunk on nectar. Birds and animals make a lively sound and roam happily, free from hostility.
ramacharitamanas::2571.translation_literal: सरनि (lakes) / सरोज (lotuses) / बिटप (trees) / बन (forest) / फूले (bloomed) / गुंजत (humming) / मंजु (sweetly) / मधुप (bees) / रस (nectar) / भूले (drunk, lost) / खग (birds) / मृग (animals) / बिपुल (many) / कोलाहल (noise, bustle) / करहीं (make) / बिरहित (without) / बैर (hostility) / मुदित (joyful) / मन (mind) / चरहीं (roam)
ramacharitamanas::2571.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2571.essence: Peace changes even the forest into a gentle home.
ramacharitamanas::2571.simple_meaning: The forest around Valmiki's hermitage is in full bloom, full of bees, birds, and animals living peacefully together.
ramacharitamanas::2571.simple_insight: A place touched by holiness feels safe, alive, and free of fear.
ramacharitamanas::2571.detailed_meaning: Ram and Sita have reached Valmiki's hermitage after wandering through the forest. The landscape itself seems to welcome them: flowers bloom, bees hum, and animals move without fear. This verse paints the peaceful setting before Valmiki comes to receive them.
ramacharitamanas::2571.modern_relevance: You step into a quiet park after a long, tense day and notice how even your breathing softens. Some places seem to lower the temperature of the heart before anyone says a word.
ramacharitamanas::2571.insight: It shifts attention from action to atmosphere, showing how harmony is felt in the world around you.

ramacharitamanas::2572.verse_sanskrit: सुचि सुंदर आश्रमु निरखि हरषे राजिवनेन। सुनि रघुबर आगमनु मुनि आगें आयउ लेन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2572.verse_hindi: पवित्र और सुंदर आश्रम को देखकर कमल नयन श्री रामचन्द्रजी हर्षित हुए। रघु श्रेष्ठ श्री रामजी का आगमन सुनकर मुनि वाल्मीकिजी उन्हें लेने के लिए आगे आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2572.english_translation: Seeing the pure, beautiful hermitage, lotus-eyed Ram felt joy. Hearing of Raghubar's arrival, the sage came forward to receive him.
ramacharitamanas::2572.translation_literal: सुचि (pure) / सुंदर (beautiful) / आश्रमु (hermitage) / निरखि (seeing) / हरषे (felt joy) / राजिवनेन (lotus-eyed one) / सुनि (hearing) / रघुबर (Raghu's श्रेष्ठ / noble one, Ram) / आगमनु (arrival) / मुनि (sage) / आगें (ahead) / आयउ (came) / लेन (to receive)
ramacharitamanas::2572.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2572.essence: A pure place and a welcoming heart meet Ram with joy.
ramacharitamanas::2572.simple_meaning: Ram reaches Valmiki's hermitage, feels pleased by its purity and beauty, and the sage comes forward to welcome him.
ramacharitamanas::2572.simple_insight: A welcoming place softens the heart before any words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2572.detailed_meaning: Ram arrives at Valmiki's hermitage in the forest. The place is pure, beautiful, and peaceful, and Ram feels delight at seeing it. When the sage hears of Ram's arrival, he comes forward to receive him with honor.
ramacharitamanas::2572.modern_relevance: You walk into a home that feels calm before anyone says hello. The room itself tells you: you are welcome here.
ramacharitamanas::2572.insight: It shifts attention from grand events to the sacred power of hospitality and place.

ramacharitamanas::2573.verse_sanskrit: मुनि कहुँ राम दंडवत कीन्हा। आसिरबादु बिप्रबर दीन्हा॥ देखि राम छबि नयन जुड़ाने। करि सनमानु आश्रमहिं आने ॥
ramacharitamanas::2573.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने मुनि को दण्डवत किया। विप्र श्रेष्ठ मुनि ने उन्हें आशीर्वाद दिया। श्री रामचन्द्रजी की छबि देखकर मुनि के नेत्र शीतल हो गए। सम्मानपूर्वक मुनि उन्हें आश्रम में ले आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2573.english_translation: Ram bowed to the sage. The best of the learned gave him blessings. Seeing Ram's beauty, the sage's eyes softened, and he respectfully led him into the hermitage.
ramacharitamanas::2573.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / कहुँ (to) / राम (Ram) / दंडवत (prostration) / कीन्हा (did) / आसिरबादु (blessing) / बिप्रबर (best of the learned) / दीन्हा (gave) / देखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / छबि (beauty) / नयन (eyes) / जुड़ाने (became soothed) / करि (doing) / सनमानु (honour) / आश्रमहिं (to the hermitage) / आने (brought)
ramacharitamanas::2573.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2573.essence: Humility and honour make a holy meeting possible.
ramacharitamanas::2573.simple_meaning: Ram bows to the sage, receives blessings, and is welcomed into the hermitage with honour.
ramacharitamanas::2573.simple_insight: Respect opens the door before words do.
ramacharitamanas::2573.detailed_meaning: Ram arrives at Valmiki's hermitage in exile. He bows first, the sage blesses him, and the sight of Ram's beauty fills the sage with delight. This verse simply marks their sacred meeting.
ramacharitamanas::2573.modern_relevance: You enter a home carrying grief, and the first thing you do is bow with humility. That simple respect changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::2573.insight: It shows how humility and welcome create sacred relationship before any conversation begins.

ramacharitamanas::2574.verse_sanskrit: मुनिबर अतिथि प्रानप्रिय पाए। कंद मूल फल मधुर मँगाए॥ सिय सौमित्रि राम फल खाए। तब मुनि आश्रम दिए सुहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2574.verse_hindi: श्रेष्ठ मुनि वाल्मीकिजी ने प्राणप्रिय अतिथियों को पाकर उनके लिए मधुर कंद, मूल और फल मँगवाए। श्री सीताजी, लक्ष्मणजी और रामचन्द्रजी ने फलों को खाया। तब मुनि ने उनको (विश्राम करने के लिए) सुंदर स्थान बतला दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2574.english_translation: The great sage welcomed his life-dearest guests, had sweet roots, tubers, and fruits brought, and then showed Ram, Sita, and Lakshman a pleasant place to rest.
ramacharitamanas::2574.translation_literal: मुनिबर (great sage) / अतिथि (guests) / प्रानप्रिय (dearest to life) / पाए (having received) / कंद (roots) / मूल (tubers) / फल (fruits) / मधुर (sweet) / मँगाए (had brought) // सिय (Sita) / सौमित्रि (Lakshman) / राम (Ram) / फल (fruits) / खाए (ate) / तब (then) / मुनि (sage) / आश्रम (hermitage) / दिए (gave) / सुहाए (pleasant)
ramacharitamanas::2574.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2574.essence: Kindness first feeds and shelters before it speaks.
ramacharitamanas::2574.simple_meaning: Valmiki welcomes Ram, Sita, and Lakshman with simple forest food and a place to rest.
ramacharitamanas::2574.simple_insight: Real hospitality begins with making room, feeding well, and easing someone’s fatigue.
ramacharitamanas::2574.detailed_meaning: At Valmiki’s hermitage in Ayodhyakand, Ram, Sita, and Lakshman arrive as beloved guests. The sage responds immediately with forest food and a resting place, showing the quiet dignity of welcome before any deeper conversation begins.
ramacharitamanas::2574.modern_relevance: A tired friend shows up at your door after a hard day, and you stop everything to feed them and clear a place to sit. Care often begins with ordinary kindness.
ramacharitamanas::2574.insight: It shifts attention from grand gestures to the first practical act of welcome.

ramacharitamanas::2575.verse_sanskrit: बालमीकि मन आनँदु भारी। मंगल मूरति नयन निहारी॥ तब कर कमल जोरि रघुराई। बोले बचन श्रवन सुखदाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2575.verse_hindi: (मुनि श्री रामजी के पास बैठे हैं और उनकी) मंगल मूर्ति को नेत्रों से देखकर वाल्मीकिजी के मन में बड़ा भारी आनंद हो रहा है। तब श्री रघुनाथजी कमलसदृश हाथों को जोड़कर, कानों को सुख देने वाले मधुर वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2575.english_translation: Valmiki's heart swelled with joy, seeing the auspicious form before his eyes. Then Raghuvir joined his lotus hands and spoke words that delighted the ear.
ramacharitamanas::2575.translation_literal: बालमीकि (Valmiki) / मन (mind) / आनँदु (joy) / भारी (great) / मंगल (auspicious) / मूरति (form) / नयन (eyes) / निहारी (having seen)॥ / तब (then) / कर (hands) / कमल (lotus-like) / जोरि (joining) / रघुराई (Raghuvir) / बोले (spoke) / बचन (words) / श्रवन (ears) / सुखदाई (giving delight)॥
ramacharitamanas::2575.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2575.essence: Real greatness makes room for humility.
ramacharitamanas::2575.simple_meaning: Valmiki feels deep joy seeing Ram's auspicious presence, and Ram responds with respectful, pleasing words.
ramacharitamanas::2575.simple_insight: Reverence flows both ways: true greatness still bows, and true welcome feels tender.
ramacharitamanas::2575.detailed_meaning: In Valmiki's forest hermitage, Ram, Sita, and Lakshman have been welcomed as honored guests. Valmiki is overwhelmed by Ram's presence, and Ram answers with folded hands and gentle speech. The scene shows mutual grace before the teaching begins.
ramacharitamanas::2575.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm presence changes the room, and even the most respected person becomes humble. The exchange feels less like status and more like grace.
ramacharitamanas::2575.insight: It shifts attention from rank to reverence, showing that dignity and humility can meet without conflict.

ramacharitamanas::2576.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह त्रिकाल दरसी मुनिनाथा। बिस्व बदर जिमि तुम्हरें हाथा ॥ अस कहि प्रभु सब कथा बखानी। जेहि जेहि भाँति दीन्ह बनु रानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2576.verse_hindi: हे मुनिनाथ! आप त्रिकालदर्शी हैं। सम्पूर्ण विश्व आपके लिए हथेली पर रखे हुए बेर के समान है। प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने ऐसा कहकर फिर जिस-जिस प्रकार से रानी कैकेयी ने वनवास दिया, वह सब कथा विस्तार से सुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2576.english_translation: O lord of sages, you see all three times. The whole world is like a berry held in your hand. Having said this, the Lord then told the whole story of how Queen Kaikeyi gave the exile, in every detail.
ramacharitamanas::2576.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / त्रिकाल-दरसी (seer of the three times) / मुनि-नाथा (lord of sages) / बिस्व (world) / बदर (berry) / जिमि (like) / तुम्हरें (in your) / हाथा (hand) / अस (thus) / कहि (having said) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सब (all) / कथा (story) / बखानी (told) / जेहि-जेहि (in whatever) / भाँति (manner) / दीन्ह (gave) / बनु (forest exile) / रानी (queen)
ramacharitamanas::2576.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2576.essence: True understanding makes even painful history feel fully held.
ramacharitamanas::2576.simple_meaning: Ram praises Valmiki as one who sees all of time, then explains the whole story of Kaikeyi's role in sending him into exile.
ramacharitamanas::2576.simple_insight: Deep understanding can hold the whole story without losing tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::2576.detailed_meaning: At Valmiki's forest hermitage, Ram and Sita have been welcomed with reverence. Ram speaks to the sage as one who sees all times, then calmly recounts the painful chain of events behind his exile, opening his heart to a listener who can truly understand.
ramacharitamanas::2576.modern_relevance: You finally tell the full story to someone who already sees past the surface. The relief is not in hiding less, but in being understood without explanation.
ramacharitamanas::2576.insight: It shows that truthful speech lands best in the presence of real understanding.

ramacharitamanas::2577.verse_sanskrit: तात बचन पुनि मातु हित भाइ भरत अस राउ। मो कहुँ दरस तुम्हार प्रभु सबु मम पुन्य प्रभाउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2577.verse_hindi: (और कहा-) हे प्रभो! पिता की आज्ञा (का पालन), माता का हित और भरत जैसे (स्नेही एवं धर्मात्मा) भाई का राजा होना और फिर मुझे आपके दर्शन होना, यह सब मेरे पुण्यों का प्रभाव है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2577.english_translation: And he said: O Lord, the keeping of my father's word, my mother's welfare, my brother Bharat's rule, and then my having your darshan — all of this is the result of my past merit.
ramacharitamanas::2577.translation_literal: तात (father's word) / बचन (word) / पुनि (again) / मातु (mother's) / हित (welfare) / भाइ (brother) / भरत (Bharat) / अस (such) / राउ (king) / मो कहुँ (for me) / दरस (darshan) / तुम्हार (your) / प्रभु (Lord) / सबु (all) / मम (my) / पुन्य (merit) / प्रभाउ (effect)
ramacharitamanas::2577.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2577.essence: What seems like burden can reveal itself as blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2577.simple_meaning: Ram says that his father's command, his mother's welfare, Bharat's rule, and this meeting with the sages are all signs of his past merit.
ramacharitamanas::2577.simple_insight: What feels like sacrifice can also be a blessing in disguise.
ramacharitamanas::2577.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram speaks after reaching the sages in the forest. He looks back on the painful chain of events — exile, family duty, Bharat's care, and this holy meeting — and sees not tragedy but grace working through it.
ramacharitamanas::2577.modern_relevance: You miss a promotion, move cities, and end up caring for family in a way you never planned. Later, you realise the detour gave you something cleaner than success: a life that actually fits.
ramacharitamanas::2577.insight: It shifts the mind from resentment about interruption to recognition of hidden grace in obligation.

ramacharitamanas::2578.verse_sanskrit: देखि पाय मुनिराय तुम्हारे। भए सुकृत सब सुफल हमारे॥॥ अब जहँ राउर आयसु होई। मुनि उदबेगु न पावै कोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2578.verse_hindi: हे मुनिराज! आपके चरणों का दर्शन करने से आज हमारे सब पुण्य सफल हो गए (हमें सारे पुण्यों का फल मिल गया)। अब जहाँ आपकी आज्ञा हो और जहाँ कोई भी मुनि उद्वेग को प्राप्त न हो- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2578.english_translation: O sage king, seeing your feet has made all our good deeds fruitful. Now, wherever you command, let no sage feel distress.
ramacharitamanas::2578.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / पाय (feet) / मुनिराय (sage-king) / तुम्हारे (your) / भए (became) / सुकृत (good deeds) / सब (all) / सुफल (fully fruitful) / हमारे (our) ॥ अब (now) / जहँ (wherever) / राउर (your) / आयसु (command) / होई (may be) / मुनि (sage) / उदबेगु (distress) / न (not) / पावै (may get) / कोई (anyone) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2578.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2578.essence: Honor becomes complete when power protects peace.
ramacharitamanas::2578.simple_meaning: Seeing the sage's feet brings full blessing, and Ram asks to be commanded in a way that never troubles any sage.
ramacharitamanas::2578.simple_insight: True fulfilment comes from humble presence and from using power so carefully that no one is harmed.
ramacharitamanas::2578.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is speaking with the sage Bharadvaja after exile has begun. He bows deeply, says that even seeing the sage's feet has fulfilled all his merit, and asks for guidance that will not disturb any holy person.
ramacharitamanas::2578.modern_relevance: You meet someone who has quietly guided you for years, and the first thing you do is listen instead of perform. Real respect is not loud; it protects the other person's peace.
ramacharitamanas::2578.insight: It teaches you to treat authority as responsibility and to measure success by whether others remain untroubled.

ramacharitamanas::2579.verse_sanskrit: मुनि तापस जिन्ह तें दुखु लहहीं। ते नरेस बिनु पावक दहहीं॥ मंगल मूल बिप्र परितोषू। दहइ कोटि कुल भूसुर रोषू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2579.verse_hindi: क्योंकि जिनसे मुनि और तपस्वी दुःख पाते हैं, वे राजा बिना अग्नि के ही (अपने दुष्ट कर्मों से ही) जलकर भस्म हो जाते हैं। ब्राह्मणों का संतोष सब मंगलों की जड़ है और भूदेव ब्राह्मणों का क्रोध करोड़ों कुलों को भस्म कर देता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2579.english_translation: Kings who cause suffering to sages and ascetics burn themselves up without fire. The satisfaction of good Brahmins is the root of all auspiciousness, and the anger of Brahmins can burn millions of families to ash.
ramacharitamanas::2579.translation_literal: मुनि (sages) / तापस (ascetics) / जिन्ह तें (from whom) / दुखु (suffering) / लहहीं (receive) / ते (those) / नरेस (kings) / बिनु (without) / पावक (fire) / दहहीं (burn) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मूल (root) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / परितोषू (satisfaction) / दहइ (burns) / कोटि (crores/millions) / कुल (families) / भूसुर (Brahmins) / रोषू (anger)
ramacharitamanas::2579.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2579.essence: Disrespecting the wise turns your own power against you.
ramacharitamanas::2579.simple_meaning: A ruler who harms sages destroys himself. Peace with wise people brings blessing, while provoking them can ruin whole families.
ramacharitamanas::2579.simple_insight: You do not have to win every conflict. Respect can protect you more than force.
ramacharitamanas::2579.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharadwaj is speaking within a sacred setting where royal conduct is being measured by spiritual conduct. The verse warns that power used against sages backfires, and that a ruler's real safety lies in keeping the wise content.
ramacharitamanas::2579.modern_relevance: You snap at the person who has quietly guided you for years, then wonder why support dries up. This verse says power without reverence burns its own house down.
ramacharitamanas::2579.insight: It shifts you from dominance to reverence, showing that how you treat the wise shapes your own safety.

ramacharitamanas::2580.verse_sanskrit: अस जियँ जानि कहिअ सोइ ठाऊँ। सिय सौमित्रि सहित जहँ जाऊँ॥ तहँ रचि रुचिर परन तृन साला। बासु करौं कछु काल कृपाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::2580.verse_hindi: ऐसा हृदय में समझकर- वह स्थान बतलाइए जहाँ मैं लक्ष्मण और सीता सहित जाऊँ और वहाँ सुंदर पत्तों और घास की कुटी बनाकर, हे दयालु! कुछ समय निवास करूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2580.english_translation: Knowing this in my heart, please tell me the place where I may go with Sita and Lakshman. There I will build a lovely hut of leaves and grass and stay there for some time, O compassionate one.
ramacharitamanas::2580.translation_literal: अस (thus) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानि (knowing) / कहिअ (please tell) / सोइ (that) / ठाऊँ (place) / सिय (Sita) / सौमित्रि (Lakshman) / सहित (together with) / जहँ (where) / जाऊँ (I may go) / तहँ (there) / रचि (building) / रुचिर (beautiful) / परन (leaf) / तृन (grass) / साला (hut) / बासु (stay) / करौं (I may do) / कछु (some) / काल (time) / कृपाला (compassionate one)
ramacharitamanas::2580.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2580.essence: Simplicity can be the highest form of royal dignity.
ramacharitamanas::2580.simple_meaning: Ram asks for a place where he can live with Sita and Lakshman in a simple hut made of leaves and grass.
ramacharitamanas::2580.simple_insight: Greatness does not need comfort. A life of purpose can choose simplicity without losing dignity.
ramacharitamanas::2580.detailed_meaning: In the forest exile, Ram speaks to the sage after accepting life away from the palace. He asks for a quiet place for Sita and Lakshman, and says he will build a simple hut there. The royal life is gone; dharma remains.
ramacharitamanas::2580.modern_relevance: You finally move out of the apartment with the marble lobby and choose the small room near the trees. Less status, less noise, more room to live the life you actually mean.
ramacharitamanas::2580.insight: It shifts you from chasing comfort to choosing the setting that supports your true duties.

ramacharitamanas::2581.verse_sanskrit: सहज सरल सुनि रघुबर बानी। साधु साधु बोले मुनि ग्यानी॥ कस न कहहु अस रघुकुलकेतू। तुम्ह पालक संतत श्रुति सेतू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2581.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी की सहज ही सरल वाणी सुनकर ज्ञानी मुनि वाल्मीकि बोले- धन्य! धन्य! हे रघुकुल के ध्वजास्वरूप! आप ऐसा क्यों न कहेंगे? आप सदैव वेद की मर्यादा का पालन (रक्षण) करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2581.english_translation: Hearing Raghubar's simple, सहज words, the wise sage said, 'Well said! Well said! Why would you not say this, O banner of the Raghu line? You always uphold the boundary of the sacred tradition.'
ramacharitamanas::2581.translation_literal: सहज सरल (naturally simple) / सुनि (having heard) / रघुबर (Raghubar, Ram) / बानी (speech) / साधु साधु (well said, well said) / बोले (spoke) / मुनि (sage) / ग्यानी (wise) / कस (why) / न (not) / कहहु (do you say) / अस (thus) / रघुकुलकेतू (banner of the Raghu line) / तुम्ह (you) / पालक (protector) / संतत (always) / श्रुति सेतू (bridge of the sacred tradition)
ramacharitamanas::2581.speaker: Valmiki
ramacharitamanas::2581.essence: True greatness speaks simply and protects dharma without strain.
ramacharitamanas::2581.simple_meaning: Valmiki praises Ram's humble, straightforward speech and recognizes that Ram always protects the sacred order of conduct.
ramacharitamanas::2581.simple_insight: Gentleness can be a sign of strength, not weakness.
ramacharitamanas::2581.detailed_meaning: Valmiki has just heard Ram speak plainly about where He will live in exile. Instead of grand claims, Ram speaks with ease and humility. The sage immediately recognizes that this is the mark of someone who always protects dharma.
ramacharitamanas::2581.modern_relevance: A leader answers a difficult question without posturing, and everyone in the room feels the difference. Real authority does not need to sound impressive; it protects what matters by speaking simply and acting rightly.
ramacharitamanas::2581.insight: It shifts respect away from display and toward steady conduct that preserves order.

ramacharitamanas::2582.verse_sanskrit: श्रुति सेतु पालक राम तुम्ह जगदीस माया जानकी। जो सृजति जगु पालति हरति रुख पाइ कृपानिधान की॥ जो सहससीसु अहीसु महिधरु लखनु सचराचर धनी। सुर काज धरि नरराज तनु चले दलन खल निसिचर अनी॥
ramacharitamanas::2582.verse_hindi: हे राम! आप वेद की मर्यादा के रक्षक जगदीश्वर हैं और जानकीजी (आपकी स्वरूप भूता) माया हैं, जो कृपा के भंडार आपका रुख पाकर जगत का सृजन, पालन और संहार करती हैं। जो हजार मस्तक वाले सर्पों के स्वामी और पृथ्वी को अपने सिर पर धारण करने वाले हैं, वही चराचर के स्वामी शेषजी लक्ष्मण हैं। देवताओं के कार्य के लिए आप राजा का शरीर धारण करके दुष्ट राक्षसों की सेना का नाश करने के लिए चले हैं।
ramacharitamanas::2582.english_translation: O Ram, protector of the bridge of the Vedas and lord of the world, Janaki is your own power. By your grace, she creates, sustains, and withdraws the world. The thousand-headed serpent lord, bearer of the earth, is Lakshman, lord of all moving and unmoving beings. For the gods' work, you have taken a king's body and gone to destroy the armies of evil beings.
ramacharitamanas::2582.translation_literal: श्रुति (Veda) / सेतु (bridge) / पालक (protector) / राम (Ram) / तुम्ह (you) / जगदीस (lord of the world) / माया (power) / जानकी (Janaki) / जो (who) / सृजति (creates) / जगु (the world) / पालति (sustains) / हरति (withdraws) / रुख (favor) / पाइ (having received) / कृपानिधान (treasure of grace) / की (of) / जो (who) / सहससीसु (thousand-headed) / अहीसु (serpent lord) / महिधरु (earth-bearer) / लखनु (Lakshman) / सचराचर (moving and unmoving) / धनी (lord) / सुर (gods) / काज (work) / धरि (having taken) / नरराज (king) / तनु (body) / चले (went) / दलन (to destroy) / खल (evil) / निसिचर (night-wanderers) / अनी (armies)
ramacharitamanas::2582.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2582.essence: The highest power can move through a human form without losing its sovereignty.
ramacharitamanas::2582.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the lord of the world, with Janaki as his power and Lakshman as the great serpent-bearing supporter. He has taken human form to protect dharma and destroy evil forces.
ramacharitamanas::2582.simple_insight: The divine can enter ordinary life without losing its majesty.
ramacharitamanas::2582.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is welcoming Ram in Ayodhya and begins to praise his cosmic identity. He sees Janaki as Ram's power, Lakshman as the great supporter, and Ram's human journey as a divine mission to protect the world and remove destructive forces.
ramacharitamanas::2582.modern_relevance: You look ordinary to everyone at work, but your quiet role may be carrying a much larger purpose than anyone sees.
ramacharitamanas::2582.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing Ram as only a prince to seeing his human life as divine action in the world.

ramacharitamanas::2583.verse_sanskrit: राम सरूप तुम्हार बचन अगोचर बुद्धिपर। अबिगत अकथ अपार नेति नेति नित निगम कह।126॥
ramacharitamanas::2583.verse_hindi: हे राम! आपका स्वरूप वाणी के अगोचर, बुद्धि से परे, अव्यक्त, अकथनीय और अपार है। वेद निरंतर उसका 'नेति-नेति' कहकर वर्णन करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2583.english_translation: O Ram, your true form is beyond speech and beyond the discerning mind. It is unmanifest, indescribable, boundless; the Vedas continually point to it by saying, 'not this, not this.'
ramacharitamanas::2583.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सरूप (true form) / तुम्हार (your) / बचन (speech) / अगोचर (beyond speech) / बुद्धिपर (beyond the discerning mind) / अबिगत (unmanifest) / अकथ (indescribable) / अपार (boundless) / नेति नेति (not this, not this) / नित (continually) / निगम (the Vedas) / कह (say)
ramacharitamanas::2583.speaker: Valmiki
ramacharitamanas::2583.essence: The deepest reality is known by what words cannot hold.
ramacharitamanas::2583.simple_meaning: Ram's true nature cannot be fully described by words or grasped by the mind. The Vedas approach it only by saying what it is not.
ramacharitamanas::2583.simple_insight: Some realities are too vast to define; reverence begins where language ends.
ramacharitamanas::2583.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Valmiki responds to Ram's gentle speech by lifting the conversation beyond praise. He says Ram's true form cannot be held by language or intellect, and even the Vedas can only gesture toward it by negation.
ramacharitamanas::2583.modern_relevance: You try to explain someone you love to a friend, and every sentence feels too small. Some things are not reduced by being unnamed; they are honoured.
ramacharitamanas::2583.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to define the highest reality to recognising its limits and bowing in humility.
