ramacharitamanas::2584.verse_sanskrit: जगु पेखन तुम्ह देखनिहारे। बिधि हरि संभु नचावनिहारे॥ तेउ न जानहिं मरमु तुम्हारा। औरु तुम्हहि को जाननिहारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2584.verse_hindi: हे राम! जगत दृश्य है, आप उसके देखने वाले हैं। आप ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और शंकर को भी नचाने वाले हैं। जब वे भी आपके मर्म को नहीं जानते, तब और कौन आपको जानने वाला है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2584.english_translation: O Ram, the world is what is seen, and you are the Seer. You make Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva dance. Even they do not know your mystery, so who else could know you?
ramacharitamanas::2584.translation_literal: जगु (the world) / पेखन (to be seen) / तुम्ह (you) / देखनिहारे (the Seer) / बिधि (Brahma) / हरि (Vishnu/Ram) / संभु (Shiva) / नचावनिहारे (the one who makes dance) / तेउ (even they) / न (not) / जानहिं (know) / मरमु (mystery/secret essence) / तुम्हारा (your) / औरु (else) / तुम्हहि (you) / को (who) / जाननिहारा (knower)
ramacharitamanas::2584.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2584.essence: The deepest reality is the Seer, not the seen.
ramacharitamanas::2584.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond the world of appearances. He is the one who sees everything, while even the highest beings cannot fully understand him.
ramacharitamanas::2584.simple_insight: Humility grows when you stop assuming reality is fully knowable by your own mind.
ramacharitamanas::2584.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas turns from the pain of exile to praise Ram's unfathomable nature. Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva themselves are shown as moved by him, yet unable to grasp his full mystery.
ramacharitamanas::2584.modern_relevance: You can spend years trying to explain everything, then watch a crisis expose how little you control. This verse reminds you that the deepest reality is larger than your explanations.
ramacharitamanas::2584.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to master the whole picture to bowing before what exceeds understanding.

ramacharitamanas::2585.verse_sanskrit: सोइ जानइ जेहि देहु जनाई। जानत तुम्हहि तुम्हइ होइ जाई॥ तुम्हरिहि कृपाँ तुम्हहि रघुनंदन। जानहिं भगत भगत उर चंदन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2585.verse_hindi: वही आपको जानता है, जिसे आप जना देते हैं और जानते ही वह आपका ही स्वरूप बन जाता है। हे रघुनंदन! हे भक्तों के हृदय को शीतल करने वाले चंदन! आपकी ही कृपा से भक्त आपको जान पाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2585.english_translation: Only the one whom you reveal can know you; and in knowing you, that one becomes like you. By your grace alone, O Raghu's delight, devotees know you, sandalwood cooling the hearts of devotees.
ramacharitamanas::2585.translation_literal: सोइ (that very one) / जानइ (knows) / जेहि (to whom) / देहु (you give) / जनाई (the making-known) / जानत (knowing) / तुम्हहि (you) / तुम्हइ (you yourself) / होइ (becomes) / जाई (goes) ॥ / तुम्हरिहि (by your) / कृपाँ (grace) / तुम्हहि (you) / रघुनंदन (O delight of the Raghu line) / जानहिं (they know) / भगत (devotees) / भगत (devotees) / उर (heart) / चंदन (sandalwood) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2585.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2585.essence: Knowing Ram is itself a gift from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2585.simple_meaning: No one can know Ram by personal effort alone. Only the grace that reveals him makes real understanding possible, and that understanding changes the devotee from within.
ramacharitamanas::2585.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that closeness is received, not forced.
ramacharitamanas::2585.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is praising Ram’s hidden greatness after saying even Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva cannot fully grasp him. The next turn is devotional: Ram is knowable only when he chooses to make himself known, and that revelation transforms the devotee.
ramacharitamanas::2585.modern_relevance: You can read every book, sit in every retreat, and still feel shut out. Then one quiet moment lands, and something opens that effort never could. That is how grace feels.
ramacharitamanas::2585.insight: It shifts the mind from self-made understanding to received revelation.

ramacharitamanas::2586.verse_sanskrit: चिदानंदमय देह तुम्हारी। बिगत बिकार जान अधिकारी॥ नर तनु धरेहु संत सुर काजा। कहहु करहु जस प्राकृत राजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2586.verse_hindi: आपकी देह चिदानन्दमय है (यह प्रकृतिजन्य पंच महाभूतों की बनी हुई कर्म बंधनयुक्त, त्रिदेह विशिष्ट मायिक नहीं है) और (उत्पत्ति-नाश, वृद्धि-क्षय आदि) सब विकारों से रहित है, इस रहस्य को अधिकारी पुरुष ही जानते हैं। आपने देवता और संतों के कार्य के लिए (दिव्य) नर शरीर धारण किया है और प्राकृत (प्रकृति के तत्वों से निर्मित देह वाले, साधारण) राजाओं की तरह से कहते और करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2586.english_translation: Your body is made of consciousness and bliss, free from all change. Only the qualified know this mystery. You have taken a human form for the work of saints and radiant beings, yet you speak and act like an ordinary king.
ramacharitamanas::2586.translation_literal: चिदानंदमय (made of consciousness-bliss) / देह (body) / तुम्हारी (your) । बिगत (free from) / बिकार (change, distortion) / जान (know) / अधिकारी (qualified one) ॥ नर (human) / तनु (body) / धरेहु (you took) / संत (saints) / सुर (radiant beings) / काजा (for the work) । कहहु (you speak) / करहु (you act) / जस (like) / प्राकृत (ordinary, material) / राजा (king) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2586.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2586.essence: Ram's human form hides a nature untouched by change.
ramacharitamanas::2586.simple_meaning: Ram's true nature is beyond ordinary physical change, and only those fit to understand can see it. He has taken a human form to serve saints and radiant beings, while outwardly living like a king.
ramacharitamanas::2586.simple_insight: What looks ordinary can hold something far greater than appearances suggest.
ramacharitamanas::2586.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the speaker is praising Ram's hidden nature. Ram appears as a human prince, speaking and acting like a king, but his body is described as pure consciousness and bliss. The verse reveals the gap between outer appearance and inner reality.
ramacharitamanas::2586.modern_relevance: You meet someone who seems quiet, even plain, and only later realise their presence has been holding everything together. This verse reminds you that the deepest reality is often hidden behind the most ordinary surface.
ramacharitamanas::2586.insight: It shifts attention from outward form to inward essence, and from surface judgment to deeper recognition.

ramacharitamanas::2587.verse_sanskrit: राम देखि सुनि चरित तुम्हारे। जड़ मोहहिं बुध होहिं सुखारे॥ तुम्ह जो कहहु करहु सबु साँचा। जस काछिअ तस चाहिअ नाचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2587.verse_hindi: हे राम! आपके चरित्रों को देख और सुनकर मूर्ख लोग तो मोह को प्राप्त होते हैं और ज्ञानीजन सुखी होते हैं। आप जो कुछ कहते, करते हैं, वह सब सत्य (उचित) ही है, क्योंकि जैसा स्वाँग भरे वैसा ही नाचना भी तो चाहिए (इस समय आप मनुष्य रूप में हैं, अतः मनुष्योचित व्यवहार करना ठीक ही है।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2587.english_translation: O Ram, seeing and hearing your deeds, the foolish fall into delusion, while the wise become joyful. Whatever you say and do is true and right, because when you have taken a human form, you should behave like a human being.
ramacharitamanas::2587.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / देखि (seeing) / सुनि (hearing) / चरित (deeds, conduct) / तुम्हारे (your) / जड़ (the foolish) / मोहहिं (fall into delusion) / बुध (the wise) / होहिं (become) / सुखारे (joyful) ॥ / तुम्ह (you) / जो (whatever) / कहहु (you say) / करहु (you do) / सबु (all) / साँचा (true) / जस (as) / काछिअ (a costume, role) / तस (so) / चाहिअ (should) / नाचा (dance) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2587.speaker: Hanuman
ramacharitamanas::2587.essence: True greatness can look ordinary when it wears a human form.
ramacharitamanas::2587.simple_meaning: Ram's actions can bewilder shallow minds, but they bring joy to the wise. Whatever he does is right, because he is choosing to live as a human being.
ramacharitamanas::2587.simple_insight: You can stop demanding that the divine look impressive and start trusting what is right in the moment.
ramacharitamanas::2587.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Hanuman is speaking about Ram's conduct as an incarnate king. He says Ram's life will confuse the foolish but satisfy the wise, because Ram is not pretending to be anything other than human while still acting with perfect rightness.
ramacharitamanas::2587.modern_relevance: A parent looks ordinary while making a hard decision that children won't understand yet. A wise friend doesn't need the choice to look dramatic to know it is right.
ramacharitamanas::2587.insight: It shifts you from judging by appearances to trusting conduct that fits the role and the moment.

ramacharitamanas::2588.verse_sanskrit: पूँछेहु मोहि कि रहौं कहँ मैं पूँछत सकुचाउँ। जहँ न होहु तहँ देहु कहि तुम्हहि देखावौं ठाउँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2588.verse_hindi: आपने मुझसे पूछा कि मैं कहाँ रहूँ? परन्तु मैं यह पूछते सकुचाता हूँ कि जहाँ आप न हों, वह स्थान बता दीजिए। तब मैं आपके रहने के लिए स्थान दिखाऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2588.english_translation: You asked me where I should stay. But I hesitate to ask where you are not. Tell me that place, and I will show you where to stay.
ramacharitamanas::2588.translation_literal: पूँछेहु (you asked) / मोहि (me) / कि (that) / रहौं (I should stay) / कहँ (where) / मैं (I) / पूँछत (asking) / सकुचाउँ (hesitate) / जहँ (where) / न (not) / होहु (you are) / तहँ (there) / देहु (give/tell) / कहि (saying) / तुम्हहि (to you) / देखावौं (I will show) / ठाउँ (place)
ramacharitamanas::2588.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2588.essence: Separation from the beloved is the only place that feels unfit.
ramacharitamanas::2588.simple_meaning: Ram answers with humility and devotion: he does not want a place that is separate from the one he loves. Home is wherever that presence is found.
ramacharitamanas::2588.simple_insight: Love stops being a location and becomes a way of belonging.
ramacharitamanas::2588.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the sage asks Ram where he should live. Ram replies with tender reverence: he cannot even ask for a place unless it is away from the sage. The moment turns a practical question into pure devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2588.modern_relevance: You move into a new city, but the room feels empty until someone you love walks in. Suddenly the address matters less than the presence inside it.
ramacharitamanas::2588.insight: It shifts belonging from geography to relationship, teaching you to see presence as the real shelter.

ramacharitamanas::2589.verse_sanskrit: सुनि मुनि बचन प्रेम रस साने। सकुचि राम मन महुँ मुसुकाने॥ बालमीकि हँसि कहहिं बहोरी। बानी मधुर अमिअ रस बोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2589.verse_hindi: मुनि के प्रेमरस से सने हुए वचन सुनकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी रहस्य खुल जाने के डर से सकुचाकर मन में मुस्कुराए। वाल्मीकिजी हँसकर फिर अमृत रस में डुबोई हुई मीठी वाणी बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2589.english_translation: Hearing the sage's words, steeped in the nectar of love, Ram smiled inwardly, shy and amused. Then Valmiki laughed and spoke again in sweet words soaked with nectar.
ramacharitamanas::2589.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (sage) / बचन (words) / प्रेम रस (the nectar of love) / साने (soaked with) / सकुचि (feeling shy) / राम (Ram) / मन महुँ (within the mind) / मुसुकाने (smiled) / बालमीकि (Valmiki) / हँसि (laughing) / कहहिं (spoke) / बहोरी (again) / बानी (speech) / मधुर (sweet) / अमिअ रस (nectar-essence) / बोरी (drenched)
ramacharitamanas::2589.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2589.essence: True affection can make reverence feel shy and sweet.
ramacharitamanas::2589.simple_meaning: Ram hears Valmiki's loving words and smiles shyly. Valmiki then speaks again with even sweeter, nectar-like speech.
ramacharitamanas::2589.simple_insight: Love can make even holy words feel playful, tender, and alive.
ramacharitamanas::2589.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Valmiki is welcoming Ram and preparing to show him a place to stay. Ram's shy smile shows he already senses the affection behind the sage's words. The scene softens before the next instruction is given.
ramacharitamanas::2589.modern_relevance: Someone praises you too warmly after you help them, and you look down with that small embarrassed smile. You know the kindness is real, and it lands deeper than flattery.
ramacharitamanas::2589.insight: It highlights the tenderness that appears when reverence and affection meet.

ramacharitamanas::2590.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु राम अब कहउँ निकेता। जहाँ बसहु सिय लखन समेता॥ जिन्ह के श्रवन समुद्र समाना। कथा तुम्हारि सुभग सरि नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2590.verse_hindi: हे रामजी! सुनिए, अब मैं वे स्थान बताता हूँ, जहाँ आप, सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी समेत निवास कीजिए। जिनके कान समुद्र की भाँति आपकी सुंदर कथा रूपी अनेक सुंदर नदियों से- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2590.english_translation: Listen, Ram, I now tell you the dwelling place where you, Sita, and Lakshman may live. Those whose ears are like the ocean receive many lovely streams of your beautiful story.
ramacharitamanas::2590.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / राम (Ram) / अब (now) / कहउँ (I say) / निकेता (dwelling place) / जहाँ (where) / बसहु (you live) / सिय (Sita) / लखन (Lakshman) / समेता (together with) ॥ / जिन्ह (those who) / के (whose) / श्रवन (ears) / समुद्र (ocean) / समाना (equal to) / कथा (story) / तुम्हारि (your) / सुभग (beautiful) / सरि (river) / नाना (many) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2590.speaker: Valmiki
ramacharitamanas::2590.essence: A heart that loves your story becomes your true home.
ramacharitamanas::2590.simple_meaning: Valmiki says Ram, Sita, and Lakshman should live in hearts that eagerly receive Ram's beautiful story.
ramacharitamanas::2590.simple_insight: A heart that truly listens becomes a place of belonging.
ramacharitamanas::2590.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is answering Ram's search for a place to stay. He says the best dwelling is not a palace, but a heart so vast and receptive that it keeps drinking in Ram's story, with Sita and Lakshman present in that sacred welcome.
ramacharitamanas::2590.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose eyes light up when you speak, and the whole room softens. That kind of welcome is rarer than a guest room — and far more real.
ramacharitamanas::2590.insight: It shifts devotion from external space to inner receptivity.

ramacharitamanas::2591.verse_sanskrit: भरहिं निरंतर होहिं न पूरे। तिन्ह के हिय तुम्ह कहुँ गुह रूरे॥ लोचन चातक जिन्ह करि राखे। रहहिं दरस जलधर अभिलाषे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2591.verse_hindi: निरंतर भरते रहते हैं, परन्तु कभी पूरे (तृप्त) नहीं होते, उनके हृदय आपके लिए सुंदर घर हैं और जिन्होंने अपने नेत्रों को चातक बना रखा है, जो आपके दर्शन रूपी मेघ के लिए सदा लालायित रहते हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2591.english_translation: They are never full; their hearts are the lovely home where you dwell. They have made their eyes like the chatak bird, always longing for the rain-cloud of your sight.
ramacharitamanas::2591.translation_literal: भरहिं (they fill) / निरंतर (continually) / होहिं (become) / न (not) / पूरे (full) / तिन्ह के (their) / हिय (hearts) / तुम्ह कहुँ (for you) / गुह (cave/home) / रूरे (beautiful) / लोचन (eyes) / चातक (chatak bird) / जिन्ह करि (having made) / राखे (kept) / रहहिं (remain) / दरस (sight) / जलधर (rain-cloud) / अभिलाषे (longing)
ramacharitamanas::2591.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2591.essence: A heart that never feels full becomes Ram's true home.
ramacharitamanas::2591.simple_meaning: Real devotion never feels complete without Ram. The heart becomes his home, and the eyes keep waiting for his sight.
ramacharitamanas::2591.simple_insight: Longing itself can become a form of love that keeps you open, tender, and alive.
ramacharitamanas::2591.detailed_meaning: In the conversation with Valmiki, Ram is being shown the kind of hearts worthy to receive him. The saint describes devotees whose hearts stay unsatisfied except by Ram, and whose eyes wait like a chatak bird for the rain-cloud of his presence.
ramacharitamanas::2591.modern_relevance: You scroll past another beautiful thing, but nothing quite lands. That restless ache may be telling you your heart is still made for something deeper than passing satisfaction.
ramacharitamanas::2591.insight: It shifts devotion from possession to longing, showing that desire for the divine can itself purify the heart.

ramacharitamanas::2592.verse_sanskrit: निदरहिं सरित सिंधु सर भारी। रूप बिंदु जल होहिं सुखारी॥ तिन्ह कें हृदय सदन सुखदायक। बसहु बंधु सिय सह रघुनायक ॥
ramacharitamanas::2592.verse_hindi: तथा जो भारी-भारी नदियों, समुद्रों और झीलों का निरादर करते हैं और आपके सौंदर्य (रूपी मेघ) की एक बूँद जल से सुखी हो जाते हैं (अर्थात आपके दिव्य सच्चिदानन्दमय स्वरूप के किसी एक अंग की जरा सी भी झाँकी के सामने स्थूल, सूक्ष्म और कारण तीनों जगत के अर्थात पृथ्वी, स्वर्ग और ब्रह्मलोक तक के सौंदर्य का तिरस्कार करते हैं), हे रघुनाथजी! उन लोगों के हृदय रूपी सुखदायी भवनों में आप भाई लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सहित निवास कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2592.english_translation: Those who turn away from great rivers, oceans, and lakes and are satisfied by a single drop of your beauty—Lord of Raghu, dwell in their heart-homes of joy with Lakshman and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2592.translation_literal: निदरहिं (disregard) / सरित (rivers) / सिंधु (oceans) / सर (lakes) / भारी (great) / रूप (form/beauty) / बिंदु (drop) / जल (water) / होहिं (become) / सुखारी (contented) / तिन्ह कें (in their) / हृदय (heart) / सदन (dwelling) / सुखदायक (joy-giving) / बसहु (dwell) / बंधु (brother) / सिय (Sita) / सह (with) / रघुनायक (Lord of Raghu)
ramacharitamanas::2592.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2592.essence: A single glimpse of Ram makes all lesser beauty fade.
ramacharitamanas::2592.simple_meaning: Worldly beauty loses its power beside even a tiny glimpse of Ram's divine form. Such a heart becomes fit for Ram, Sita, and Lakshman to dwell in.
ramacharitamanas::2592.simple_insight: What you truly love begins to reorder everything else.
ramacharitamanas::2592.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising the kind of heart that has outgrown ordinary pleasures. In Ayodhyakand, as exile and separation press on the family, he says that anyone satisfied by even a drop of Ram's beauty has a heart-home worthy of Ram, Sita, and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::2592.modern_relevance: You scroll past a hundred polished images, then one face, one song, one moment of grace stops you cold. After that, everything else feels thinner. This verse names that reversal of taste.
ramacharitamanas::2592.insight: It shifts desire from collecting more experiences to recognizing what is truly nourishing.

ramacharitamanas::2593.verse_sanskrit: जसु तुम्हार मानस बिमल हंसिनि जीहा जासु। मुकताहल गुन गन चुनइ राम बसहु हियँ तासु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2593.verse_hindi: आपके यश रूपी निर्मल मानसरोवर में जिसकी जीभ हंसिनी बनी हुई आपके गुण समूह रूपी मोतियों को चुगती रहती है, हे रामजी! आप उसके हृदय में बसिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2593.english_translation: In your pure lake of fame, let the tongue become a swan that keeps picking up the pearls of your qualities. O Ram, dwell in that heart.
ramacharitamanas::2593.translation_literal: जसु (fame) / तुम्हार (your) / मानस (lake of the mind) / बिमल (pure) / हंसिनि (swan-like) / जीहा (tongue) / जासु (whose) / मुकताहल (pearls) / गुन (qualities) / गन (group) / चुनइ (picks) / राम (Ram) / बसहु (dwell) / हियँ (in the heart) / तासु (in that one)
ramacharitamanas::2593.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2593.essence: A heart that praises Ram becomes His dwelling place.
ramacharitamanas::2593.simple_meaning: A heart filled with loving praise for Ram becomes a home for Ram himself. The tongue should keep gathering his qualities like a swan picking pearls.
ramacharitamanas::2593.simple_insight: Praise changes what lives in you.
ramacharitamanas::2593.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is describing the kind of heart fit for Ram's presence. Not status, not force, but a tongue that lovingly gathers Ram's qualities and a mind made pure by remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::2593.modern_relevance: You keep replaying someone's flaws in your head after the argument. This verse turns the habit around: what you repeatedly honor and speak of begins to shape the home inside you.
ramacharitamanas::2593.insight: It shifts attention from criticism to devoted remembrance, training the mind to dwell on what it loves.

ramacharitamanas::2594.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु प्रसाद सुचि सुभग सुबासा। सादर जासु लहइ नित नासा॥ तुम्हहि निबेदित भोजन करहीं। प्रभु प्रसाद पट भूषन धरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2594.verse_hindi: जिसकी नासिका प्रभु (आप) के पवित्र और सुगंधित (पुष्पादि) सुंदर प्रसाद को नित्य आदर के साथ ग्रहण करती (सूँघती) है और जो आपको अर्पण करके भोजन करते हैं और आपके प्रसाद रूप ही वस्त्राभूषण धारण करते हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2594.english_translation: Those who respectfully inhale the sacred, fragrant offerings of the Lord, eat only food offered to You, and wear garments and ornaments received as Your grace.
ramacharitamanas::2594.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord's) / प्रसाद (grace-offering) / सुचि (pure) / सुभग (fragrant, beautiful) / सुबासा (sweet scent) / सादर (with respect) / जासु (whose) / लहइ (receives) / नित (daily) / नासा (nose) ॥ / तुम्हहि (to You) / निबेदित (offered) / भोजन (food) / करहीं (they eat) / प्रभु (the Lord's) / प्रसाद (grace-offering) / पट (cloth) / भूषन (ornaments) / धरहीं (they wear) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2594.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2594.essence: Devotion turns ordinary receiving into worship.
ramacharitamanas::2594.simple_meaning: A devoted person treats even food, fragrance, clothes, and ornaments as offerings received with reverence, not as possessions to boast about.
ramacharitamanas::2594.simple_insight: Ordinary life becomes sacred when you receive everything as grace.
ramacharitamanas::2594.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is describing the marks of a heart already turned toward Ram. In this Ayodhyakand prayer, the devotee does not consume or adorn for ego; even scent, food, cloth, and jewelry are lived as offerings to the Lord.
ramacharitamanas::2594.modern_relevance: You sit down to dinner after a long day and pause before the first bite. The meal, the clothes you wear, even the small comforts around you can become reminders that life is received, not owned.
ramacharitamanas::2594.insight: It shifts you from possession to reverence, so daily habits become acts of remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::2595.verse_sanskrit: सीस नवहिं सुर गुरु द्विज देखी। प्रीति सहित करि बिनय बिसेषी॥ कर नित करहिं राम पद पूजा। राम भरोस हृदयँ नहिं दूजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2595.verse_hindi: जिनके मस्तक देवता, गुरु और ब्राह्मणों को देखकर बड़ी नम्रता के साथ प्रेम सहित झुक जाते हैं, जिनके हाथ नित्य श्री रामचन्द्रजी (आप) के चरणों की पूजा करते हैं और जिनके हृदय में श्री रामचन्द्रजी (आप) का ही भरोसा है, दूसरा नहीं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2595.english_translation: Those whose heads bow in loving reverence when they see the radiant beings, the teacher, and the learned; whose hands daily worship Ram's feet; and whose hearts hold no support except Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2595.translation_literal: सीस (heads) / नवहिं (bow) / सुर (radiant beings) / गुरु (teacher) / द्विज (learned ones) / देखी (seeing) / प्रीति सहित (with love) / करि (doing) / बिनय बिसेषी (special reverence) ॥ / कर (hands) / नित (daily) / करहिं (do) / राम पद (Ram's feet) / पूजा (worship) ॥ / राम भरोस (trust in Ram) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / नहिं दूजा (no other) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2595.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2595.essence: Real devotion bows, serves, and trusts without a second refuge.
ramacharitamanas::2595.simple_meaning: True devotion shows itself in humility, daily worship, and a heart that relies on Ram alone.
ramacharitamanas::2595.simple_insight: You do not need many supports when your heart has found one steady refuge.
ramacharitamanas::2595.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is describing the kind of person Ram truly lives in: someone humble before the wise, devoted in daily worship, and inwardly certain that no other support is needed. It is a portrait of settled bhakti.
ramacharitamanas::2595.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is measuring status, and you quietly respect the people who deserve it, do your practice, and stop chasing approval. That steady center is what this verse honors.
ramacharitamanas::2595.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to dependence: respect outwardly, worship consistently, and let Ram become your only inner support.

ramacharitamanas::2596.verse_sanskrit: चरन राम तीरथ चलि जाहीं। राम बसहु तिन्ह के मन माहीं॥ मंत्रराजु नित जपहिं तुम्हारा। पूजहिं तुम्हहि सहित परिवारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2596.verse_hindi: तथा जिनके चरण श्री रामचन्द्रजी (आप) के तीर्थों में चलकर जाते हैं, हे रामजी! आप उनके मन में निवास कीजिए। जो नित्य आपके (राम नाम रूप) मंत्रराज को जपते हैं और परिवार (परिकर) सहित आपकी पूजा करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2596.english_translation: Their feet go on pilgrimage to Ram's holy places. Ram lives in their hearts. They chant your king of mantras daily and worship you with their whole family.
ramacharitamanas::2596.translation_literal: चरन (feet) / राम (Ram) / तीरथ (holy places) / चलि (having gone) / जाहीं (go) / राम (Ram) / बसहु (dwell) / तिन्ह (in those) / के (of) / मन (mind) / माहीं (within) / मंत्रराजु (king of mantras) / नित (daily) / जपहिं (they chant) / तुम्हारा (your) / पूजहिं (they worship) / तुम्हहि (you) / सहित (along with) / परिवारा (family)
ramacharitamanas::2596.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2596.essence: Repeated devotion invites Ram to stay in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2596.simple_meaning: People who go to Ram's holy places, repeat his name, and worship him with their families are asking Ram to live in their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::2596.simple_insight: Devotion is not only ritual; it becomes a living presence that settles inside you.
ramacharitamanas::2596.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas describes the kind of people Ram can dwell with: those who travel to his holy places, repeat his mantra, and worship him together with their families. The verse turns outward devotion into inward presence.
ramacharitamanas::2596.modern_relevance: You light a lamp before leaving for work, then whisper a name under your breath on the train. The ritual is small, but it changes the room inside you.
ramacharitamanas::2596.insight: It shifts worship from outward performance to inward companionship with Ram.

ramacharitamanas::2597.verse_sanskrit: तरपन होम करहिं बिधि नाना। बिप्र जेवाँइ देहिं बहु दाना॥ तुम्ह तें अधिक गुरहि जियँ जानी। सकल भायँ सेवहिं सनमानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2597.verse_hindi: जो अनेक प्रकार से तर्पण और हवन करते हैं तथा ब्राह्मणों को भोजन कराकर बहुत दान देते हैं तथा जो गुरु को हृदय में आपसे भी अधिक (बड़ा) जानकर सर्वभाव से सम्मान करके उनकी सेवा करते हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2597.english_translation: They perform many kinds of offerings and fire rituals, feed learned guests, give much charity, and serve the teacher with full respect, holding the teacher in their heart as greater even than you.
ramacharitamanas::2597.translation_literal: तरपन (offerings for the ancestors) / होम (fire offering) / करहिं (they do) / बिधि (in ways) / नाना (many) / बिप्र (learned priests) / जेवाँइ (feeding) / देहिं (they give) / बहु (much) / दाना (charity) / तुम्ह तें (than you) / अधिक (greater) / गुरहि (the teacher) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानी (knowing) / सकल (with all) / भायँ (mood) / सेवहिं (they serve) / सनमानी (with respect)
ramacharitamanas::2597.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2597.essence: Ritual matters less than the humility that makes service sincere.
ramacharitamanas::2597.simple_meaning: They honor the sacred through ritual, charity, and service, but the deepest devotion is their reverence for the teacher and for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2597.simple_insight: Devotion becomes real when reverence turns into humble service.
ramacharitamanas::2597.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas describes the kind of people Ram blesses: they do rituals, feed priests, give generously, and serve their teacher with complete respect. This is part of a larger prayer for lives shaped by devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2597.modern_relevance: You donate, volunteer, and keep every tradition carefully, but the real test is whether humility shows up in how you treat the person who teaches you.
ramacharitamanas::2597.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to lived reverence, with service as the proof.

ramacharitamanas::2598.verse_sanskrit: सबु करि मागहिं एक फलु राम चरन रति होउ। तिन्ह कें मन मंदिर बसहु सिय रघुनंदन दोउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2598.verse_hindi: और ये सब कर्म करके सबका एक मात्र यही फल माँगते हैं कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में हमारी प्रीति हो, उन लोगों के मन रूपी मंदिरों में सीताजी और रघुकुल को आनंदित करने वाले आप दोनों बसिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2598.english_translation: After doing all this, they ask for only one fruit: love for Ram's feet. May both Sita and Ram live in the temple of their minds.
ramacharitamanas::2598.translation_literal: सबु (all) / करि (having done) / मागहिं (they ask) / एक (one) / फलु (fruit) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / रति (love) / होउ (may it be) / तिन्ह कें (in those people's) / मन (mind) / मंदिर (temple) / बसहु (may you dwell) / सिय (Sita) / रघुनंदन (delighter of the Raghu clan) / दोउ (both)
ramacharitamanas::2598.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2598.essence: All practice is fulfilled by love for Ram alone.
ramacharitamanas::2598.simple_meaning: After every ritual and act of devotion, the only true request is love for Ram. When that love comes, Ram and Sita live in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2598.simple_insight: All practice becomes beautiful when it leads to loving closeness, not to display or reward.
ramacharitamanas::2598.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas lists holy acts, offerings, and service, then strips them down to one request. The point is not ritual success but a heart so devoted that Ram and Sita naturally dwell within it.
ramacharitamanas::2598.modern_relevance: You finish a long prayer, a charity drive, or a family ritual and still feel empty unless love has actually deepened. This verse says the real result is not applause, but closeness.
ramacharitamanas::2598.insight: It shifts devotion from performing acts to asking for inner nearness and lasting love.

ramacharitamanas::2599.verse_sanskrit: काम कोह मद मान न मोहा। लोभ न छोभ न राग न द्रोहा॥ जिन्ह कें कपट दंभ नहिं माया। तिन्ह कें हृदय बसहु रघुराया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2599.verse_hindi: जिनके न तो काम, क्रोध, मद, अभिमान और मोह हैं, न लोभ है, न क्षोभ है, न राग है, न द्वेष है और न कपट, दम्भ और माया ही है- हे रघुराज! आप उनके हृदय में निवास कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2599.english_translation: Free from desire, anger, pride, delusion, greed, agitation, attachment, hatred, deceit, hypocrisy, and illusion—O Lord of Raghu, dwell in such hearts.
ramacharitamanas::2599.translation_literal: काम (desire) / कोह (anger) / मद (intoxication of pride) / मान (self-importance) / न (not) / मोहा (delusion) / लोभ (greed) / न (not) / छोभ (agitation) / न (not) / राग (attachment) / न (not) / द्रोहा (hatred) / जिन्ह कें (in whose) / कपट (deceit) / दंभ (hypocrisy) / नहिं (not) / माया (illusion) / तिन्ह कें (in those) / हृदय (heart) / बसहु (dwell) / रघुराया (Lord of Raghu)
ramacharitamanas::2599.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2599.essence: A heart without ego becomes Ram's home.
ramacharitamanas::2599.simple_meaning: A heart emptied of craving, anger, pride, greed, attachment, hatred, deceit, and illusion becomes fit for Ram to live in.
ramacharitamanas::2599.simple_insight: Inner purity is not emptying for its own sake; it creates space for something sacred to stay.
ramacharitamanas::2599.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the speaker turns from ritual offerings to a deeper offering: the purified heart. After praising those who serve and seek Ram's feet, this verse names the inner conditions that make a person fit for Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::2599.modern_relevance: You can do all the right rituals, post the right words, and still feel crowded inside. The real preparation is simpler and harder: clear out the noise that keeps love from staying.
ramacharitamanas::2599.insight: It shifts devotion from outer performance to inner readiness.

ramacharitamanas::2600.verse_sanskrit: सब के प्रिय सब के हितकारी। दुख सुख सरिस प्रसंसा गारी॥ कहहिं सत्य प्रिय बचन बिचारी। जागत सोवत सरन तुम्हारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2600.verse_hindi: जो सबके प्रिय और सबका हित करने वाले हैं, जिन्हें दुःख और सुख तथा प्रशंसा (बड़ाई) और गाली (निंदा) समान है, जो विचारकर सत्य और प्रिय वचन बोलते हैं तथा जो जागते-सोते आपकी ही शरण हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2600.english_translation: They are dear to everyone and helpful to everyone. Pleasure and pain, praise and blame are the same to them. They speak truth after reflection, with words that are pleasing. Awake or asleep, they remain in your refuge.
ramacharitamanas::2600.translation_literal: सब (all) / के प्रिय (dear to) / सब (all) / के हितकारी (beneficial to) / दुख (pain) / सुख (pleasure) / सरिस (equal) / प्रसंसा (praise) / गारी (abuse) / कहहिं (they speak) / सत्य (truth) / प्रिय (pleasant) / बचन (words) / बिचारी (after reflecting) / जागत (awake) / सोवत (sleeping) / सरन (refuge) / तुम्हारी (your)
ramacharitamanas::2600.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2600.essence: Devotion makes you steady, kind, and free from the crowd's verdict.
ramacharitamanas::2600.simple_meaning: Ram stays with those who are kind to everyone, steady in praise or blame, truthful in speech, and always surrendered to him.
ramacharitamanas::2600.simple_insight: Real devotion changes how you treat people, speak, and respond to criticism.
ramacharitamanas::2600.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the qualities of Ram's true devotees are being described. They are kind to everyone, steady in joy and sorrow, and honest without harshness. Their whole life rests in Ram's refuge, day and night.
ramacharitamanas::2600.modern_relevance: You get praised in the meeting, then mocked in the group chat. The verse asks whether your character changes with either one, or stays steady anyway.
ramacharitamanas::2600.insight: It trains you to become consistent: kind, truthful, and unshaken by public approval or rejection.

ramacharitamanas::2601.verse_sanskrit: तुम्हहि छाड़ि गति दूसरि नाहीं। राम बसहु तिन्ह के मन माहीं॥ जननी सम जानहिं परनारी। धनु पराव बिष तें बिष भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2601.verse_hindi: और आपको छोड़कर जिनके दूसरे कोई गति (आश्रय) नहीं है, हे रामजी! आप उनके मन में बसिए। जो पराई स्त्री को जन्म देने वाली माता के समान जानते हैं और पराया धन जिन्हें विष से भी भारी विष है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2601.english_translation: Besides you, they have no other refuge. O Ram, dwell in the hearts of those who see another man's wife as their mother and another man's wealth as poison heavier than poison.
ramacharitamanas::2601.translation_literal: तुम्हहि (you alone) / छाड़ि (leaving aside) / गति (refuge) / दूसरि (other) / नाहीं (not) / राम (Ram) / बसहु (dwell) / तिन्ह के (their) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / जननी सम (like a mother) / जानहिं (they know) / परनारी (another man's wife) / धनु (wealth) / पराव (other's) / बिष तें (than poison) / बिष भारी (heavier poison)
ramacharitamanas::2601.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2601.essence: Ram enters the heart that has stopped chasing poison.
ramacharitamanas::2601.simple_meaning: People who have no refuge except Ram, and who treat another man's wife like a mother and another man's wealth like poison, become fit for Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::2601.simple_insight: Purity is not repression; it is a heart that no longer reaches for what harms it.
ramacharitamanas::2601.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas turns from Bharat's grief to a moral prayer: Ram should live only in hearts that have surrendered every lesser refuge and turned away from desire, greed, and betrayal. Such inner cleanliness makes a person fit for divine presence.
ramacharitamanas::2601.modern_relevance: You scroll past what you know will stir desire, then close the app before it drags you further. That small refusal is the kind of inner cleanliness this verse honors.
ramacharitamanas::2601.insight: It shifts the focus from spiritual display to inner restraint, showing that Ram dwells where desire and greed have been refused.

ramacharitamanas::2602.verse_sanskrit: जे हरषहिं पर संपति देखी। दुखित होहिं पर बिपति बिसेषी॥ जिन्हहि राम तुम्ह प्रान पिआरे। तिन्ह के मन सुभ सदन तुम्हारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2602.verse_hindi: जो दूसरे की सम्पत्ति देखकर हर्षित होते हैं और दूसरे की विपत्ति देखकर विशेष रूप से दुःखी होते हैं और हे रामजी! जिन्हें आप प्राणों के समान प्यारे हैं, उनके मन आपके रहने योग्य शुभ भवन हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2602.english_translation: Those who rejoice at another's good fortune and feel deep sorrow at another's hardship, and those for whom you are dear as life itself, their hearts are a blessed home for you, O Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2602.translation_literal: जे (those who) / हरषहिं (rejoice) / पर (other's) / संपति (prosperity) / देखी (seeing) / दुखित (grieved) / होहिं (become) / पर (other's) / बिपति (misfortune) / बिसेषी (especially) / जिन्हहि (for whom) / राम (Ram) / तुम्ह (you) / प्रान (life-breath) / पिआरे (dear) / तिन्ह (their) / के (of) / मन (mind/heart) / सुभ (auspicious) / सदन (dwelling) / तुम्हारे (your)
ramacharitamanas::2602.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2602.essence: Empathy makes the heart fit for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2602.simple_meaning: A heart that rejoices in others' happiness and grieves in others' pain becomes fit for Ram to dwell in.
ramacharitamanas::2602.simple_insight: Love grows when your happiness is tied to others, not just yourself.
ramacharitamanas::2602.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is describing the kind of person Ram naturally lives within. It is not wealth or status that makes a heart worthy, but empathy, shared joy, and shared sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2602.modern_relevance: You hear good news about a colleague who got the promotion you wanted, and instead of bitterness, something in you softens. That quiet generosity is the kind of space this verse points to.
ramacharitamanas::2602.insight: It shifts attention from self-centered feeling to shared emotional life, where devotion becomes possible.

ramacharitamanas::2603.verse_sanskrit: स्वामि सखा पितु मातु गुर जिन्ह के सब तुम्ह तात। मन मंदिर तिन्ह कें बसहु सीय सहित दोउ भ्रात ॥
ramacharitamanas::2603.verse_hindi: हे तात! जिनके स्वामी, सखा, पिता, माता और गुरु सब कुछ आप ही हैं, उनके मन रूपी मंदिर में सीता सहित आप दोनों भाई निवास कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2603.english_translation: O dear one, for those whose only lord, friend, father, mother, and teacher are you, dwell in their mind-temple, along with Sita and your two brothers.
ramacharitamanas::2603.translation_literal: स्वामि (lord) / सखा (friend) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / गुर (teacher) / जिन्ह के (for whom) / सब (all) / तुम्ह (you) / तात (dear one) / मन (mind) / मंदिर (temple) / तिन्ह कें (in their) / बसहु (dwell) / सीय सहित (with Sita) / दोउ (both) / भ्रात (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::2603.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2603.essence: Whoever makes Ram their everything is already home.
ramacharitamanas::2603.simple_meaning: People who already hold Ram as their father, mother, teacher, friend, and lord are asked to keep him and Sita in their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::2603.simple_insight: Love deepens when nothing else is asked to take Ram's place.
ramacharitamanas::2603.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the poet turns from grief and exile to prayer. He asks Ram to live in the hearts of those who already depend on him for every role of care and guidance, showing devotion as complete inner belonging.
ramacharitamanas::2603.modern_relevance: After a hard day, you call the one person who steadies you, then realize you want more than comfort — you want your whole life to have that same center.
ramacharitamanas::2603.insight: It shifts devotion from occasional prayer to making the heart a living home for Ram.

ramacharitamanas::2604.verse_sanskrit: अवगुन तजि सब के गुन गहहीं। बिप्र धेनु हित संकट सहहीं॥ नीति निपुन जिन्ह कइ जग लीका। घर तुम्हार तिन्ह कर मनु नीका ॥
ramacharitamanas::2604.verse_hindi: जो अवगुणों को छोड़कर सबके गुणों को ग्रहण करते हैं, ब्राह्मण और गो के लिए संकट सहते हैं, नीति-निपुणता में जिनकी जगत में मर्यादा है, उनका सुंदर मन आपका घर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2604.english_translation: Those who drop faults and gather everyone's good qualities, who endure hardship for the sake of priests and cows, and whose conduct is known everywhere for wise justice—your home is a beautiful mind.
ramacharitamanas::2604.translation_literal: अवगुन (faults) / तजि (leaving) / सब (all) / के (of) / गुन (qualities) / गहहीं (they gather) / बिप्र (priests) / धेनु (cows) / हित (for the good of) / संकट (hardship) / सहहीं (they endure) / नीति (right conduct) / निपुन (skilled) / जिन्ह कइ (whose) / जग (world) / लीका (mark/reputation) / घर (home) / तुम्हार (your) / तिन्ह कर (of those) / मनु (mind) / नीका (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::2604.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2604.essence: A heart that protects others becomes Ram's true home.
ramacharitamanas::2604.simple_meaning: Ram's home belongs to people who notice goodness in others, endure hardship for the vulnerable, and live with wise fairness.
ramacharitamanas::2604.simple_insight: A generous, steady heart becomes a place where the divine naturally belongs.
ramacharitamanas::2604.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is describing the kind of person fit to hold Ram and Sita in the heart. It is not wealth or status, but goodness, courage, and just conduct that make a person inwardly worthy.
ramacharitamanas::2604.modern_relevance: You stay late to defend a coworker who was treated unfairly, even though it costs you. That kind of heart is not just decent — it is spacious enough to hold Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2604.insight: It shifts devotion from ritual to character: become the kind of person whose mind can shelter the divine.

ramacharitamanas::2605.verse_sanskrit: गुन तुम्हार समुझइ निज दोसा। जेहि सब भाँति तुम्हार भरोसा॥ राम भगत प्रिय लागहिं जेही। तेहि उर बसहु सहित बैदेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2605.verse_hindi: जो गुणों को आपका और दोषों को अपना समझता है, जिसे सब प्रकार से आपका ही भरोसा है और राम भक्त जिसे प्यारे लगते हैं, उसके हृदय में आप सीता सहित निवास कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2605.english_translation: Those who see your virtues as yours and their faults as their own, who trust you in every way, and who find Ram's devotees dear—may you dwell in their heart with Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2605.translation_literal: गुन (virtues) / तुम्हार (your) / समुझइ (understands) / निज (own) / दोसा (faults) / जेहि (who) / सब भाँति (in every way) / तुम्हार (your) / भरोसा (trust) / राम भगत (Ram's devotee) / प्रिय (dear) / लागहिं (seem) / जेही (to whom) / तेहि (that person's) / उर (heart) / बसहु (dwell) / सहित (with) / बैदेही (Sita)
ramacharitamanas::2605.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2605.essence: Humility, trust, and love for devotees make the heart fit for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2605.simple_meaning: The heart that stays humble, trusts Ram completely, and loves Ram's devotees becomes a fitting home for Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2605.simple_insight: Real closeness begins when pride drops and trust becomes complete.
ramacharitamanas::2605.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas turns from describing the ideal devotee to offering a prayer. The devotee is humble, trusts Ram in every way, and feels affection for Ram's followers. Such a heart becomes fit for Ram and Sita to dwell in.
ramacharitamanas::2605.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose kindness feels effortless, and you wonder why their presence feels so safe. It is because they do not keep score, trust deeply, and welcome the people you love.
ramacharitamanas::2605.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to receptivity: humility, trust, and love for fellow devotees prepare the heart to receive grace.

ramacharitamanas::2606.verse_sanskrit: जाति पाँति धनु धरमु बड़ाई। प्रिय परिवार सदन सुखदाई॥ सब तजि तुम्हहि रहइ उर लाई। तेहि के हृदयँ रहहु रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2606.verse_hindi: जाति, पाँति, धन, धर्म, बड़ाई, प्यारा परिवार और सुख देने वाला घर, सबको छोड़कर जो केवल आपको ही हृदय में धारण किए रहता है, हे रघुनाथजी! आप उसके हृदय में रहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2606.english_translation: Leaving caste, status, wealth, duty, honor, dear family, and a comfortable home, the one who keeps only you in the heart — O Raghunath, stay in that person's heart.
ramacharitamanas::2606.translation_literal: जाति (caste) / पाँति (rank) / धनु (wealth) / धरमु (duty) / बड़ाई (honor) / प्रिय (dear) / परिवार (family) / सदन (home) / सुखदाई (comfort-giving) / सब (all) / तजि (leaving) / तुम्हहि (you alone) / रहइ (keeps) / उर (heart) / लाई (placing) / तेहि (that person's) / के (of) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / रहहु (remain) / रघुराई (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::2606.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2606.essence: When Ram is all you keep, your heart becomes his home.
ramacharitamanas::2606.simple_meaning: Real devotion means letting go of status, wealth, family comfort, and social pride, and keeping Ram alone in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2606.simple_insight: There is freedom in needing less, and peace in loving one thing completely.
ramacharitamanas::2606.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is describing the kind of heart that can truly receive Ram. The person who drops status, wealth, family pride, and comfort, and holds only Ram inside, becomes Ram's dwelling place.
ramacharitamanas::2606.modern_relevance: You step out of a family dinner where everyone is measuring success, reputation, and who has done better. Somewhere beneath all that noise, you know what you actually want to keep.
ramacharitamanas::2606.insight: It shifts attention from social identity and possessions toward single-pointed devotion.

ramacharitamanas::2607.verse_sanskrit: सरगु नरकु अपबरगु समाना। जहँ तहँ देख धरें धनु बाना॥ करम बचन मन राउर चेरा। राम करहु तेहि कें उर डेरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2607.verse_hindi: स्वर्ग, नरक और मोक्ष जिसकी दृष्टि में समान हैं, क्योंकि वह जहाँ-तहाँ (सब जगह) केवल धनुष-बाण धारण किए आपको ही देखता है और जो कर्म से, वचन से और मन से आपका दास है, हे रामजी! आप उसके हृदय में डेरा कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2607.english_translation: He sees heaven, hell, and liberation as the same, because everywhere he looks he sees you holding bow and arrows. One who serves you in deed, word, and mind — Ram, please make that heart your home.
ramacharitamanas::2607.translation_literal: सरगु (heaven) / नरकु (hell) / अपबरगु (liberation) / समाना (equal) / जहँ तहँ (here and there; everywhere) / देख (sees) / धरें (holding) / धनु (bow) / बाना (arrows)॥ / करम (action) / बचन (word) / मन (mind) / राउर (your) / चेरा (servant) / राम (Ram) / करहु (do) / तेहि कें (to that one) / उर (heart) / डेरा (dwelling) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2607.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2607.essence: A heart fully given to Ram no longer chases reward.
ramacharitamanas::2607.simple_meaning: A devoted heart sees Ram everywhere and no longer treats heaven, hell, and liberation as separate rewards. Such a person serves Ram through action, speech, and thought.
ramacharitamanas::2607.simple_insight: Devotion simplifies everything: once Ram fills the heart, outer rewards lose their power over you.
ramacharitamanas::2607.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas turns from Bharat’s grief toward the ideal devotee. He describes the person whose whole life is aligned with Ram — seeing Ram everywhere, valuing no reward above love, and offering body, speech, and mind completely.
ramacharitamanas::2607.modern_relevance: You’re walking through a crowded station after a hard day, but one call from someone you love changes everything. The world is still noisy, yet your attention has found its true home.
ramacharitamanas::2607.insight: It shifts devotion from ritual to total alignment: your actions, words, and thoughts all become one offering.

ramacharitamanas::2608.verse_sanskrit: जाहि न चाहिअ कबहुँ कछु तुम्ह सन सहज सनेहु। बसहु निरंतर तासु मन सो राउर निज गेहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2608.verse_hindi: जिसको कभी कुछ भी नहीं चाहिए और जिसका आपसे स्वाभाविक प्रेम है, आप उसके मन में निरंतर निवास कीजिए, वह आपका अपना घर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2608.english_translation: Let the one who never wants anything from you and loves you naturally live forever in your mind; that heart is your true home.
ramacharitamanas::2608.translation_literal: जाहि (to whom) / न चाहिअ (is not wanted) / कबहुँ (ever) / कछु (anything) / तुम्ह सन (from you) / सहज सनेहु (natural love) / बसहु (dwell) / निरंतर (continually) / तासु मन (in that mind) / सो (that) / राउर (your) / निज गेहु (own home)
ramacharitamanas::2608.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2608.essence: The heart that asks for nothing becomes the divine's home.
ramacharitamanas::2608.simple_meaning: A person who asks nothing from Ram and loves Him naturally becomes Ram's own home. Pure love, not demand, makes the heart fit for Him.
ramacharitamanas::2608.simple_insight: Love deepens when it stops asking. What remains is a place where presence can stay.
ramacharitamanas::2608.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the sages are describing the kind of heart Ram naturally dwells in. After praising total devotion and non-attachment, this couplet gives the climax: a mind free of demands, held by सहज सनेहु, becomes Ram's own home.
ramacharitamanas::2608.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after helping someone, hoping for a thank-you that never comes. This verse turns that ache around: the deepest bond is the one that needs nothing back.
ramacharitamanas::2608.insight: It shifts devotion from transaction to belonging, showing that asking less makes room for presence.

ramacharitamanas::2609.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि मुनिबर भवन देखाए। बचन सप्रेम राम मन भाए॥ कह मुनि सुनहु भानुकुलनायक। आश्रम कहउँ समय सुखदायक ॥
ramacharitamanas::2609.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार मुनि श्रेष्ठ वाल्मीकिजी ने श्री रामचन्द्रजी को घर दिखाए। उनके प्रेमपूर्ण वचन श्री रामजी के मन को अच्छे लगे। फिर मुनि ने कहा- हे सूर्यकुल के स्वामी! सुनिए, अब मैं इस समय के लिए सुखदायक आश्रम कहता हूँ (निवास स्थान बतलाता हूँ) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2609.english_translation: In this way the sage showed Ram the dwelling. His loving words pleased Ram's mind. Then the sage said, “Listen, O lord of the solar race. I will now tell you of a resting place that is pleasant for this time.”
ramacharitamanas::2609.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / मुनिबर (best of sages) / भवन (dwelling) / देखाए (showed) / बचन (words) / सप्रेम (with love) / राम (Ram) / मन (mind) / भाए (were pleasing) / कह (said) / मुनि (sage) / सुनहु (listen) / भानुकुलनायक (lord of the solar race) / आश्रम (hermitage) / कहउँ (I tell) / समय (time) / सुखदायक (bringing comfort)
ramacharitamanas::2609.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2609.essence: A loving guide turns even a simple shelter into comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2609.simple_meaning: The sage shows Ram a place to stay, and Ram is pleased by the loving way he speaks. Then the sage offers to point out a suitable hermitage nearby.
ramacharitamanas::2609.simple_insight: Kind guidance can feel like shelter before any place is chosen.
ramacharitamanas::2609.detailed_meaning: In Chitrakoot, the sage guides Ram through the forest and points out a dwelling with affection. Ram responds warmly to the kindness itself. This verse sets up the practical search for a place to live during exile.
ramacharitamanas::2609.modern_relevance: A friend walks you through a new neighborhood after a hard move, pointing out where you could settle. Before the address matters, the care in the guidance already eases your heart.
ramacharitamanas::2609.insight: It shifts attention from a destination to the kindness that makes refuge possible.

ramacharitamanas::2610.verse_sanskrit: चित्रकूट गिरि करहु निवासू। तहँ तुम्हार सब भाँति सुपासू॥ सैलु सुहावन कानन चारू। करि केहरि मृग बिहग बिहारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2610.verse_hindi: आप चित्रकूट पर्वत पर निवास कीजिए, वहाँ आपके लिए सब प्रकार की सुविधा है। सुहावना पर्वत है और सुंदर वन है। वह हाथी, सिंह, हिरन और पक्षियों का विहार स्थल है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2610.english_translation: Stay on Mount Chitrakoot. There, everything will be comfortable for you. It is a lovely mountain and a beautiful forest, where elephants, lions, deer, and birds roam.
ramacharitamanas::2610.translation_literal: चित्रकूट (Chitrakoot) / गिरि (mountain) / करहु (do) / निवासू (residence) / तहँ (there) / तुम्हार (your) / सब भाँति (in every way) / सुपासू (comfortable) / सैलु (mountain) / सुहावन (lovely) / कानन (forest) / चारू (beautiful) / करि (with) / केहरि (lions) / मृग (deer) / बिहग (birds) / बिहारू (roaming)
ramacharitamanas::2610.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2610.essence: A place of exile can still become a place of rest.
ramacharitamanas::2610.simple_meaning: The sage is inviting Ram to live in Chitrakoot, describing it as a beautiful, comfortable place filled with wildlife.
ramacharitamanas::2610.simple_insight: Sometimes the right place is simply the one that lets your heart rest.
ramacharitamanas::2610.detailed_meaning: Valmiki is showing Ram the forest home that can shelter him during exile. He praises Chitrakoot as beautiful, peaceful, and fit for life in the wilderness. The verse is part of a larger invitation, not the main teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::2610.modern_relevance: A friend points you toward a quiet hill town after your life has become too loud. They are not offering luxury — only a place where your mind can finally unclench.
ramacharitamanas::2610.insight: It shifts attention from loss to the possibility of dignified living in exile.

ramacharitamanas::2611.verse_sanskrit: नदी पुनीत पुरान बखानी। अत्रिप्रिया निज तप बल आनी॥ सुरसरि धार नाउँ मंदाकिनि। जो सब पातक पोतक डाकिनि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2611.verse_hindi: वहाँ पवित्र नदी है, जिसकी पुराणों ने प्रशंसा की है और जिसको अत्रि ऋषि की पत्नी अनसुयाजी अपने तपोबल से लाई थीं। वह गंगाजी की धारा है, उसका मंदाकिनी नाम है। वह सब पाप रूपी बालकों को खा डालने के लिए डाकिनी (डायन) रूप है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2611.english_translation: There is a pure river praised in the ancient texts, brought here by Anusuya through the power of her austerity. It is the stream of the celestial river, called Mandakini, and it devours all sins like a witch devours children.
ramacharitamanas::2611.translation_literal: नदी (river) / पुनीत (pure) / पुरान (ancient texts) / बखानी (praised) / अत्रिप्रिया (wife of Atri) / निज (her own) / तप (austerity) / बल (power) / आनी (brought) / सुरसरि (celestial river) / धार (stream) / नाउँ (name) / मंदाकिनि (Mandakini) / जो (which) / सब (all) / पातक (sins) / पोतक (children) / डाकिनि (witch)
ramacharitamanas::2611.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2611.essence: A sacred place holds the power of the discipline that sanctified it.
ramacharitamanas::2611.simple_meaning: The place has a holy river called Mandakini, brought by Anusuya's austerity. It is described as so pure that it destroys all sins.
ramacharitamanas::2611.simple_insight: Sacred places are not just beautiful; they are meant to cleanse and transform the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2611.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are being shown the beauty of Chitrakoot. The narrator points out Mandakini, a holy river linked to Anusuya's austerity and ancient praise. The verse deepens the sense that this forest is not ordinary land but a purified refuge.
ramacharitamanas::2611.modern_relevance: You step into a quiet riverside after a long, ugly week, and something in you loosens. Some places feel charged with calm because people have lived their discipline there.
ramacharitamanas::2611.insight: It shifts attention from scenery alone to the spiritual charge a place can carry through devotion and discipline.

ramacharitamanas::2612.verse_sanskrit: अत्रि आदि मुनिबर बहु बसहीं। करहिं जोग जप तप तन कसहीं॥ चलहु सफल श्रम सब कर करहू। राम देहु गौरव गिरिबरहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2612.verse_hindi: अत्रि आदि बहुत से श्रेष्ठ मुनि वहाँ निवास करते हैं, जो योग, जप और तप करते हुए शरीर को कसते हैं। हे रामजी! चलिए, सबके परिश्रम को सफल कीजिए और पर्वत श्रेष्ठ चित्रकूट को भी गौरव दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2612.english_translation: Many great sages, beginning with Atri, live there, practicing yoga, chanting, and austerity, and strengthening their bodies. O Ram, come and make all this effort fruitful; bring honor to the best of mountains, Chitrakoot.
ramacharitamanas::2612.translation_literal: अत्रि आदि (beginning with Atri) / मुनिबर (great sages) / बहु (many) / बसहीं (live) / करहिं (do) / जोग (yoga) / जप (chanting) / तप (austerity) / तन (body) / कसहीं (strengthen) / चलहु (come) / सफल (fruitful) / श्रम (effort) / सब (all) / कर (do) / करहू (do) / राम (Ram) / देहु (give) / गौरव (honor) / गिरिबरहू (best of mountains)
ramacharitamanas::2612.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2612.essence: Effort becomes complete only when Ram arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2612.simple_meaning: Chitrakoot is a sacred place where many sages live in discipline. The verse asks Ram to come there so their efforts become fruitful and the mountain receives honor.
ramacharitamanas::2612.simple_insight: A holy place becomes complete when the one you long for arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2612.detailed_meaning: The sages have already praised Chitrakoot’s beauty, rivers, and forests. Now they describe its living heart: Atri and other great ascetics who practice yoga and austerity there. The verse turns into a prayer that Ram himself should come and bless the place.
ramacharitamanas::2612.modern_relevance: You clean the room, prepare the meal, and wait for someone who matters deeply. Their arrival makes all the effort feel complete.
ramacharitamanas::2612.insight: It shifts attention from scenery and effort to the presence that gives them meaning.

ramacharitamanas::2613.verse_sanskrit: चित्रकूट महिमा अमित कही महामुनि गाइ। आइ नहाए सरित बर सिय समेत दोउ भाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2613.verse_hindi: महामुनि वाल्मीकिजी ने चित्रकूट की अपरिमित महिमा बखान कर कही। तब सीताजी सहित दोनों भाइयों ने आकर श्रेष्ठ नदी मंदाकिनी में स्नान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2613.english_translation: The great sage has sung the limitless glory of Chitrakoot. Then Sita and both brothers came and bathed in the best river, Mandakini.
ramacharitamanas::2613.translation_literal: चित्रकूट (Chitrakoot) / महिमा (glory) / अमित (limitless) / कही (said) / महामुनि (great sage) / गाइ (sang) / आइ (coming) / नहाए (bathed) / सरित (river) / बर (best) / सिय समेत (with Sita) / दोउ भाइ (both brothers)
ramacharitamanas::2613.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2613.essence: A holy place becomes real when Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana enter it.
ramacharitamanas::2613.simple_meaning: Valmiki praises Chitrakoot, and then Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana bathe in the Mandakini river.
ramacharitamanas::2613.simple_insight: Sacred places become alive when the beloved finally arrives there.
ramacharitamanas::2613.detailed_meaning: After Valmiki’s praise of Chitrakoot, Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana reach the Mandakini and bathe there. The verse is a gentle scene-setting moment, preparing the reader for their stay in the forest.
ramacharitamanas::2613.modern_relevance: You finally reach the place everyone described so beautifully — a hill town, a riverside, a quiet retreat — and the first thing you do is wash the journey off you.
ramacharitamanas::2613.insight: It shifts attention from the praise of a place to the lived arrival that makes the praise real.

ramacharitamanas::2614.verse_sanskrit: रघुबर कहेउ लखन भल घाटू। करहु कतहुँ अब ठाहर ठाटू॥ लखन दीख पय उतर करारा। चहुँ दिसि फिरेउ धनुष जिमि नारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2614.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने कहा- लक्ष्मण! बड़ा अच्छा घाट है। अब यहीं कहीं ठहरने की व्यवस्था करो। तब लक्ष्मणजी ने पयस्विनी नदी के उत्तर के ऊँचे किनारे को देखा (और कहा कि-) इसके चारों ओर धनुष के जैसा एक नाला फिरा हुआ है॥।1॥
ramacharitamanas::2614.english_translation: Raghubar said, "Lakshman, this is a good landing place. Arrange our stay here." Lakshman saw the high northern bank of the Payaswini river and said, "A channel has curved around it like a bow."
ramacharitamanas::2614.translation_literal: रघुबर (Ram, lord of Raghu) / कहेउ (said) / लखन (Lakshman) / भल (good) / घाटू (landing place, bank) / करहु (do, arrange) / कतहुँ (somewhere) / अब (now) / ठाहर (stay, halt) / ठाटू (arrangement)॥ / लखन (Lakshman) / दीख (saw) / पय (water, river) / उतर (north) / करारा (high bank) / चहुँ दिसि (on all four sides) / फिरेउ (turned, curved) / धनुष (bow) / जिमि (like) / नारा (string, cord) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2614.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2614.essence: A wise pause begins with noticing where to rest.
ramacharitamanas::2614.simple_meaning: Ram chooses a good place to stop, and Lakshman notices the riverbank curves around it like a bow.
ramacharitamanas::2614.simple_insight: Even a resting place can be seen with alert, discerning eyes.
ramacharitamanas::2614.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have reached Chitrakoot and are looking for a place to stay. Ram points out a suitable bank, and Lakshman notices the shape of the river and land. The verse simply sets the scene for their forest dwelling.
ramacharitamanas::2614.modern_relevance: You arrive tired at a new place and start scanning for the safest corner, the best light, the quietest seat. This is that same practical attention.
ramacharitamanas::2614.insight: It trains attention toward placement and surroundings, not just movement.

ramacharitamanas::2615.verse_sanskrit: नदी पनच सर सम दम दाना। सकल कलुष कलि साउज नाना॥ चित्रकूट जनु अचल अहेरी। चुकइ न घात मार मुठभेरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2615.verse_hindi: नदी (मंदाकिनी) उस धनुष की प्रत्यंचा (डोरी) है और शम, दम, दान बाण हैं। कलियुग के समस्त पाप उसके अनेक हिंसक पशु (रूप निशाने) हैं। चित्रकूट ही मानो अचल शिकारी है, जिसका निशाना कभी चूकता नहीं और जो सामने से मारता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2615.english_translation: The river is the bowstring, self-restraint, control of the senses, and giving are the arrows. All the many sins of Kali are the wild beasts it shoots down. Chitrakoot is like an unmoving hunter whose aim never fails and who strikes straight on.
ramacharitamanas::2615.translation_literal: नदी (river) / पनच (five) / सर (arrows) / सम (like) / दम (self-control) / दाना (giving) / सकल (all) / कलुष (sins) / कलि (of Kali) / साउज (weapons) / नाना (many) / चित्रकूट (Chitrakoot) / जनु (like) / अचल (unmoving) / अहेरी (hunter) / चुकइ (misses) / न (not) / घात (aim/strike) / मार (hitting) / मुठभेरी (directly, in close combat)
ramacharitamanas::2615.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2615.essence: Chitrakoot becomes a force that hunts down corruption.
ramacharitamanas::2615.simple_meaning: The verse compares Chitrakoot and the river there to a hunter and his bow, saying that self-control and giving destroy the many harms of the age.
ramacharitamanas::2615.simple_insight: Sacred places are not just scenery here — they become tools that help you cut through inner corruption.
ramacharitamanas::2615.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman have reached Chitrakoot and are settling by the river. The poet turns the landscape into a living image: the river, restraint, and generosity become weapons, while the harms of Kali become prey. It is a poetic description, not a standalone teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2615.modern_relevance: You sit by a quiet river after a brutal week, and somehow the noise inside you starts to thin. A place, a practice, and a calmer rhythm can feel like they are hunting your worst habits down.
ramacharitamanas::2615.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing holiness as decoration to seeing it as active protection against decay.

ramacharitamanas::2616.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि लखन ठाउँ देखरावा। थलु बिलोकि रघुबर सुखु पावा॥ रमेउ राम मनु देवन्ह जाना। चले सहित सुर थपति प्रधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2616.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर लक्ष्मणजी ने स्थान दिखाया। स्थान को देखकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सुख पाया। जब देवताओं ने जाना कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी का मन यहाँ रम गया, तब वे देवताओं के प्रधान थवई (मकान बनाने वाले) विश्वकर्मा को साथ लेकर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2616.english_translation: Laxman showed the place. Seeing the spot, Ram felt content. When the devas knew that Ram's mind had settled there, they came with Vishwakarma, the chief craftsman.
ramacharitamanas::2616.translation_literal: अस कहि (thus saying) / लखन (Laxman) / ठाउँ (place) / देखरावा (showed) / थलु (spot) / बिलोकि (seeing) / रघुबर (Ram) / सुखु (contentment) / पावा (got) / रमेउ (dwelt/settled) / राम (Ram) / मनु (mind) / देवन्ह (by the devas) / जाना (known) / चले (went) / सहित (with) / सुर (devas) / थपति (craftsman) / प्रधाना (chief)
ramacharitamanas::2616.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2616.essence: Ram’s contentment turns an ordinary place into a sacred home.
ramacharitamanas::2616.simple_meaning: Laxman shows Ram a place to stay, and Ram feels pleased with it. Seeing that Ram likes the spot, the devas arrange for help to build a dwelling.
ramacharitamanas::2616.simple_insight: A place becomes right when it brings ease to the heart, not just comfort to the body.
ramacharitamanas::2616.detailed_meaning: In Chitrakoot, Laxman points out a suitable spot for Ram to rest. Ram feels happy there, and the devas notice his contentment. That quiet approval becomes the signal for divine help to begin preparing a home.
ramacharitamanas::2616.modern_relevance: You step into a friend’s empty room, and something in you says, ‘Yes, this will do.’ Before the furniture arrives, the feeling of belonging is already there.
ramacharitamanas::2616.insight: It shifts attention from building a shelter to recognising the place where the heart naturally settles.

ramacharitamanas::2617.verse_sanskrit: कोल किरात बेष सब आए। रचे परन तृन सदन सुहाए॥ बरनि न जाहिं मंजु दुइ साला। एक ललित लघु एक बिसाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::2617.verse_hindi: सब देवता कोल-भीलों के वेष में आए और उन्होंने (दिव्य) पत्तों और घासों के सुंदर घर बना दिए। दो ऐसी सुंदर कुटिया बनाईं जिनका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता। उनमें एक बड़ी सुंदर छोटी सी थी और दूसरी बड़ी थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2617.english_translation: All the Kol and Kirat people came in disguise and built lovely homes of leaves and grass. Two beautiful huts were made that cannot be described. One was charmingly small, and the other was large.
ramacharitamanas::2617.translation_literal: कोल (forest tribes) / किरात (hill hunters) / बेष (disguise) / सब (all) / आए (came) / रचे (made, built) / परन (leaves) / तृन (grass) / सदन (homes) / सुहाए (beautiful) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाहिं (can be) / मंजु (beautiful) / दुइ (two) / साला (huts) / एक (one) / ललित (lovely) / लघु (small) / एक (one) / बिसाला (large)
ramacharitamanas::2617.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2617.essence: Love becomes shelter when it turns into service.
ramacharitamanas::2617.simple_meaning: The forest people came together and built two lovely leaf-and-grass huts for Ram, Sita, and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::2617.simple_insight: Love shows up in practical help, not grand speeches.
ramacharitamanas::2617.detailed_meaning: At Chitrakoot, the local forest people arrive in humble disguise and build beautiful leaf huts for Ram, Sita, and Lakshman. The verse lingers on the simple, loving care they offer, before the next line describes the holy family settling in.
ramacharitamanas::2617.modern_relevance: A neighbour drops by with groceries after your move, then stays to help assemble the bed. No applause, no ceremony — just care made visible.
ramacharitamanas::2617.insight: It shifts attention from admiration to service, showing that devotion becomes shelter, work, and welcome.

ramacharitamanas::2618.verse_sanskrit: लखन जानकी सहित प्रभु राजत रुचिर निकेत। सोह मदनु मुनि बेष जनु रति रितुराज समेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::2618.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी और जानकीजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी सुंदर घास-पत्तों के घर में शोभायमान हैं। मानो कामदेव मुनि का वेष धारण करके पत्नी रति और वसंत ऋतु के साथ सुशोभित हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2618.english_translation: Lord Ram, with Lakshman and Sita, shines in a lovely hut. It is as if Cupid has taken a sage's form, joined by Rati and spring.
ramacharitamanas::2618.translation_literal: लखन (Lakshman) / जानकी (Sita) / सहित (together with) / प्रभु (Lord) / राजत (shining) / रुचिर (beautiful) / निकेत (dwelling) / सोह (looks splendid) / मदनु (Cupid) / मुनि (sage) / बेष (guise) / जनु (as if) / रति (Rati) / रितुराज (spring) / समेत (together with)
ramacharitamanas::2618.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2618.essence: A humble home becomes radiant when Ram and Sita are there.
ramacharitamanas::2618.simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman shine in a beautiful forest hut. Their simple dwelling looks so lovely that it feels like spring itself has arrived there.
ramacharitamanas::2618.simple_insight: Peace can make the simplest place feel radiant.
ramacharitamanas::2618.detailed_meaning: In Chitrakoot, the exile life has begun to settle into beauty. Lakshman has just shown Ram the spot, and the forest dwellings have been arranged. Ram now sits with Sita and Lakshman in that humble hut, and the scene is so graceful that it reads like a divine painting.
ramacharitamanas::2618.modern_relevance: A bare room, a borrowed mattress, and two people you love can feel richer than any polished home when the heart is settled.
ramacharitamanas::2618.insight: It shifts attention from luxury to the quality of presence that makes a place feel complete.

ramacharitamanas::2619.verse_sanskrit: अमर नाग किंनर दिसिपाला। चित्रकूट आए तेहि काला॥ राम प्रनामु कीन्ह सब काहू। मुदित देव लहि लोचन लाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2619.verse_hindi: उस समय देवता, नाग, किन्नर और दिक्पाल चित्रकूट में आए और श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सब किसी को प्रणाम किया। देवता नेत्रों का लाभ पाकर आनंदित हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2619.english_translation: At that time the immortals, serpents, celestial singers, and guardians of the directions came to Chitrakoot. Ram bowed to them all, and the immortals rejoiced, blessed with the sight of his eyes.
ramacharitamanas::2619.translation_literal: अमर (immortals) / नाग (serpents) / किंनर (celestial singers) / दिसिपाला (guardians of the directions) / चित्रकूट (Chitrakoot) / आए (came) / तेहि काला (at that time)॥ / राम (Ram) / प्रनामु (bowed) / कीन्ह (did) / सब (all) / काहू (to everyone) / मुदित (delighted) / देव (immortals) / लहि (having received) / लोचन (eyes) / लाहू (gain) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2619.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2619.simple_meaning: The divine beings came to see Ram in Chitrakoot, and Ram honored them all. They left joyful after seeing him.
ramacharitamanas::2619.simple_insight: Even the highest beings feel blessed by a humble bow.
ramacharitamanas::2619.detailed_meaning: Ram is living quietly in Chitrakoot with Sita and Lakshman when the celestial beings come to witness him. Instead of receiving worship, Ram bows to all of them. Their joy comes not from power, but from seeing his gracious humility.
ramacharitamanas::2619.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence is calm and generous, and they greet the room with respect instead of pride. That small bow changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::2619.insight: It shows that true greatness includes humility, not distance.

ramacharitamanas::2620.verse_sanskrit: बरषि सुमन कह देव समाजू। नाथ सनाथ भए हम आजू॥ करि बिनती दुख दुसह सुनाए। हरषित निज निज सदन सिधाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2620.verse_hindi: फूलों की वर्षा करके देव समाज ने कहा- हे नाथ! आज (आपका दर्शन पाकर) हम सनाथ हो गए। फिर विनती करके उन्होंने अपने दुःसह दुःख सुनाए और (दुःखों के नाश का आश्वासन पाकर) हर्षित होकर अपने-अपने स्थानों को चले गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2620.english_translation: The divine assembly showered flowers and said, “O Lord, today we are blessed by your presence.” They offered their prayers, told of their unbearable sorrows, and then returned happily to their own abodes.
ramacharitamanas::2620.translation_literal: बरषि (showering) / सुमन (flowers) / कह (said) / देव समाजू (the divine assembly) / नाथ (Lord) / सनाथ (protected, with a lord) / भए (became) / हम (we) / आजू (today) / करि (having done) / बिनती (prayer, request) / दुख (sorrows) / दुसह (unbearable) / सुनाए (told) / हरषित (joyful) / निज निज (each one's own) / सदन (home, abode) / सिधाए (departed)
ramacharitamanas::2620.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2620.essence: True refuge makes even sorrow feel bearable.
ramacharitamanas::2620.simple_meaning: The heavenly beings rejoice at Ram's presence, pray to him about their suffering, and leave comforted.
ramacharitamanas::2620.simple_insight: Being seen by the right presence can turn suffering into relief.
ramacharitamanas::2620.detailed_meaning: In Chitrakoot, Ram is living in the forest with Sita and Lakshman. The divine beings arrive, shower flowers, call themselves blessed by his presence, and lay out their troubles before departing reassured. The scene shows Ram's quiet radiance drawing even higher beings to him.
ramacharitamanas::2620.modern_relevance: A room full of people can feel heavy until the one person who truly listens walks in. Suddenly everyone breathes easier, speaks honestly, and leaves lighter than they arrived.
ramacharitamanas::2620.insight: It shifts attention from solving alone to seeking the presence that steadies suffering.

ramacharitamanas::2621.verse_sanskrit: चित्रकूट रघुनंदनु छाए। समाचार सुनि सुनि मुनि आए॥ आवत देखि मुदित मुनिबृंदा। कीन्ह दंडवत रघुकुल चंदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2621.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी चित्रकूट में आ बसे हैं, यह समाचार सुन-सुनकर बहुत से मुनि आए। रघुकुल के चन्द्रमा श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने मुदित हुई मुनि मंडली को आते देखकर दंडवत प्रणाम किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2621.english_translation: Raghunandan has settled in Chitrakoot. Hearing the news again and again, many sages came. Seeing the joyful assembly of sages arrive, the moon of Raghu bowed down to them.
ramacharitamanas::2621.translation_literal: चित्रकूट (Chitrakoot) / रघुनंदनु (Raghunandan) / छाए (settled) / समाचार (news) / सुनि सुनि (hearing again and again) / मुनि (sages) / आए (came) / आवत (coming) / देखि (seeing) / मुदित (joyful) / मुनिबृंदा (assembly of sages) / कीन्ह (did) / दंडवत (prostration) / रघुकुल चंदा (moon of the Raghu clan)
ramacharitamanas::2621.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2621.essence: Greatness reveals itself by bowing to wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::2621.simple_meaning: The sages hear that Ram is staying in Chitrakoot, so they come to see him. Ram greets them with full respect.
ramacharitamanas::2621.simple_insight: True greatness bows first. Reverence draws wisdom closer than power ever could.
ramacharitamanas::2621.detailed_meaning: Ram is living in Chitrakoot during exile, and the news spreads among the sages. They come happily to see him, and Ram immediately bows to them. The scene shows how holiness and humility meet before any teaching begins.
ramacharitamanas::2621.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after everyone has heard good news about you, and you still choose humility first. That quiet respect changes the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::2621.insight: It shows that real stature expresses itself through respect, not self-display.

ramacharitamanas::2622.verse_sanskrit: मुनि रघुबरहि लाइ उर लेहीं। सुफल होन हित आसिष देहीं॥ सिय सौमित्रि राम छबि देखहिं। साधन सकल सफल करि लेखहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2622.verse_hindi: मुनिगण श्री रामजी को हृदय से लगा लेते हैं और सफल होने के लिए आशीर्वाद देते हैं। वे सीताजी, लक्ष्मणजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी की छबि देखते हैं और अपने सारे साधनों को सफल हुआ समझते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2622.english_translation: The sages embrace Raghubar to their hearts and bless him for his success. Seeing the beauty of Sita, Saumitra, and Ram, they feel all their spiritual practice has borne fruit.
ramacharitamanas::2622.translation_literal: मुनि (sages) / रघुबरहि (Raghubar) / लाइ (bringing) / उर (to the heart) / लेहीं (they take) / सुफल (fruitful) / होन (to become) / हित (for) / आसिष (blessings) / देहीं (they give) // सिय (Sita) / सौमित्रि (Saumitra) / राम (Ram) / छबि (beauty) / देखहिं (they see) / साधन (practices) / सकल (all) / सफल (successful) / करि (making) / लेखहिं (they consider)
ramacharitamanas::2622.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2622.essence: A single glimpse of Ram makes years of practice feel fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::2622.simple_meaning: The sages are overwhelmed by Ram's presence. They embrace him, bless him, and feel that all their discipline has finally borne fruit.
ramacharitamanas::2622.simple_insight: Some moments quietly reward every effort you have made.
ramacharitamanas::2622.detailed_meaning: In Chitrakut, the sages come to see Ram after hearing he has settled there. When they behold Ram with Sita and Lakshman, they are so filled with joy that they bless him like beloved kin and feel their whole spiritual life has succeeded.
ramacharitamanas::2622.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after months of hard work, and one person you deeply respect nods with recognition. Suddenly the long effort feels worth it; that is the feeling here.
ramacharitamanas::2622.insight: It shifts attention from private striving to the grace of being seen by what you revere.

ramacharitamanas::2623.verse_sanskrit: जथाजोग सनमानि प्रभु बिदा किए मुनिबृंद। करहिं जोग जप जाग तप निज आश्रमन्हि सुछंद ॥
ramacharitamanas::2623.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने यथायोग्य सम्मान करके मुनि मंडली को विदा किया। (श्री रामचन्द्रजी के आ जाने से) वे सब अपने-अपने आश्रमों में अब स्वतंत्रता के साथ योग, जप, यज्ञ और तप करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2623.english_translation: The Lord respectfully sent the sages away, and they returned to their own hermitages, free to perform yoga, chanting, sacrifice, and austerity.
ramacharitamanas::2623.translation_literal: जथाजोग (according to what is fitting) / सनमानि (having honored) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बिदा किए (sent off) / मुनिबृंद (the sage assembly) / करहिं (they do) / जोग (yoga) / जप (chanting) / जाग (sacrifice) / तप (austerity) / निज (their own) / आश्रमन्हि (to hermitages) / सुछंद (freely)
ramacharitamanas::2623.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2623.essence: Respect should leave others freer, not more dependent.
ramacharitamanas::2623.simple_meaning: Ram honors the sages and sends them back to their hermitages, where they can resume their spiritual practices freely.
ramacharitamanas::2623.simple_insight: True welcome leaves others freer than before.
ramacharitamanas::2623.detailed_meaning: Ram is staying in Chitrakoot, and the forest sages have come to honor him. After receiving them properly, he sends them back with respect. Their visit ends not in dependence, but in renewed freedom to continue their practices.
ramacharitamanas::2623.modern_relevance: You leave a mentor's home after a long, nourishing visit, and the best gift they gave you is not advice — it's the strength to return to your own work.
ramacharitamanas::2623.insight: It shows that real honor restores other people's independence instead of creating dependence.

ramacharitamanas::2624.verse_sanskrit: यह सुधि कोल किरातन्ह पाई। हरषे जनु नव निधि घर आई॥ कंद मूल फल भरि भरि दोना। चले रंक जनु लूटन सोना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2624.verse_hindi: यह (श्री रामजी के आगमन का) समाचार जब कोल-भीलों ने पाया, तो वे ऐसे हर्षित हुए मानो नवों निधियाँ उनके घर ही पर आ गई हों। वे दोनों में कंद, मूल, फल भर-भरकर चले, मानो दरिद्र सोना लूटने चले हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::2624.english_translation: When the Kol and Kirat people heard this news, they rejoiced as if the nine treasures had come to their home. They filled two bowls with roots, tubers, and fruits and set out like the poor rushing to seize gold.
ramacharitamanas::2624.translation_literal: यह (this) / सुधि (news) / कोल (Kol people) / किरातन्ह (Kirat people) / पाई (having received) / हरषे (they rejoiced) / जनु (as if) / नव (nine) / निधि (treasures) / घर (home) / आई (had come)॥ / कंद (roots) / मूल (tubers) / फल (fruits) / भरि भरि (filling again and again) / दोना (bowls) / चले (they went) / रंक (poor people) / जनु (as if) / लूटन (to loot) / सोना (gold) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2624.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2624.essence: A small offering becomes priceless when it is given with love.
ramacharitamanas::2624.simple_meaning: The forest tribes are so delighted by Ram's arrival that they bring him the best food they have, as if they have received a great fortune.
