ramacharitamanas::2624.simple_insight: Love shows itself in the giving, not in the size of the gift.
ramacharitamanas::2624.detailed_meaning: In the forest, word of Ram's arrival reaches the Kol and Kirat people. They are overjoyed and gather roots, fruits, and tubers to offer him. Their simple gift becomes a sign of pure welcome before Ram even appears among them.
ramacharitamanas::2624.modern_relevance: Your friend shows up after a hard week, and you bring the only warm food in the house. The gift is small; the welcome is everything.
ramacharitamanas::2624.insight: It shifts attention from wealth to wholehearted offering, showing that devotion makes even simple food feel precious.

ramacharitamanas::2625.verse_sanskrit: तिन्ह महँ जिन्ह देखे दोउ भ्राता। अपर तिन्हहि पूँछहिं मगु जाता॥ कहत सुनत रघुबीर निकाई। आइ सबन्हि देखे रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2625.verse_hindi: उनमें से जो दोनों भाइयों को (पहले) देख चुके थे, उनसे दूसरे लोग रास्ते में जाते हुए पूछते हैं। इस प्रकार श्री रामचन्द्रजी की सुंदरता कहते-सुनते सबने आकर श्री रघुनाथजी के दर्शन किए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2625.english_translation: Among them, those who had already seen the two brothers were asked the way by the others. Hearing and speaking of Raghuvir's beauty, everyone came and saw Raghuraj.
ramacharitamanas::2625.translation_literal: तिन्ह (among them) / महँ (among) / जिन्ह (those who) / देखे (had seen) / दोउ (both) / भ्राता (brothers) / अपर (others) / तिन्हहि (to them) / पूँछहिं (ask) / मगु (the way) / जाता (going) / कहत (saying) / सुनत (hearing) / रघुबीर (Raghuvir) / निकाई (beauty) / आइ (coming) / सबन्हि (all) / देखे (saw) / रघुराई (Raghuraj)
ramacharitamanas::2625.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2625.essence: Ram’s beauty makes people come looking for him.
ramacharitamanas::2625.simple_meaning: People who had already seen Ram and Lakshman were asked for directions by others. As word spread about Ram's beauty, everyone came to see him.
ramacharitamanas::2625.simple_insight: A true presence draws people in without effort.
ramacharitamanas::2625.detailed_meaning: In the forest, villagers and tribespeople hear that Ram and Lakshman have arrived. Those who have already seen them are asked for the way, and the rest follow the praise until they too reach Ram. The verse shows devotion spreading through simple human curiosity.
ramacharitamanas::2625.modern_relevance: Someone mentions a friend’s kindness in a crowded train station, and strangers start asking, “Where is she?” Goodness travels faster than explanation.
ramacharitamanas::2625.insight: It shows how beauty and goodness create their own path: hearing about Ram becomes the reason to seek him out.

ramacharitamanas::2626.verse_sanskrit: करहिं जोहारु भेंट धरि आगे। प्रभुहि बिलोकहिं अति अनुरागे॥ चित्र लिखे जनु जहँ तहँ ठाढ़े। पुलक सरीर नयन जल बाढ़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::2626.verse_hindi: भेंट आगे रखकर वे लोग जोहार करते हैं और अत्यन्त अनुराग के साथ प्रभु को देखते हैं। वे मुग्ध हुए जहाँ के तहाँ मानो चित्र लिखे से खड़े हैं। उनके शरीर पुलकित हैं और नेत्रों में प्रेमाश्रुओं के जल की बाढ़ आ रही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2626.english_translation: Holding out offerings in front of them, they bow to the Lord and gaze at him with deep love. They stand there like painted figures, their bodies thrilled with goosebumps and their eyes overflowing with tears of love.
ramacharitamanas::2626.translation_literal: करहिं (they do) / जोहारु (salutation, bow) / भेंट धरि (placing offerings) / आगे (in front) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / बिलोकहिं (they behold) / अति अनुरागे (with deep love) / चित्र लिखे (painted) / जनु (as if) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / ठाढ़े (standing) / पुलक (thrilled goosebumps) / सरीर (body) / नयन (eyes) / जल (water, tears) / बाढ़े (overflowing)
ramacharitamanas::2626.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2626.essence: True love can leave you wordless, still, and overflowing at once.
ramacharitamanas::2626.simple_meaning: The people greet Ram with offerings and look at him with overwhelming love. They stand still, moved to tears and trembling with devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2626.simple_insight: Love can make you freeze in reverence, unable to do anything except behold what you cherish.
ramacharitamanas::2626.detailed_meaning: The forest people have rushed to see Ram after hearing he has come near. Now they stand before him with offerings, unable to contain their joy. Their love is so strong they seem motionless, tears and goosebumps showing what words cannot.
ramacharitamanas::2626.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone whose presence you had only imagined, and your rehearsed words disappear. Your body says what your mouth cannot: you are moved beyond speech.
ramacharitamanas::2626.insight: It shows devotion as a bodily response: bow, behold, tremble, and weep before what you love.

ramacharitamanas::2627.verse_sanskrit: राम सनेह मगन सब जाने। कहि प्रिय बचन सकल सनमाने॥ प्रभुहि जोहारि बहोरि बहोरी। बचन बिनीत कहहिंकर जोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2627.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने उन सबको प्रेम में मग्न जाना और प्रिय वचन कहकर सबका सम्मान किया। वे बार-बार प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को जोहार करते हुए हाथ जोड़कर विनीत वचन कहते हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2627.english_translation: Ram saw that everyone was lost in love, and he honored them all with loving words. Again and again they bowed to the Lord, speaking humbly with folded hands.
ramacharitamanas::2627.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सनेह (love) / मगन (absorbed) / सब (all) / जाने (knew) / कहि (speaking) / प्रिय (dear) / बचन (words) / सकल (all) / सनमाने (honored) / प्रभुहि (to the Lord) / जोहारि (bowing) / बहोरि बहोरी (again and again) / बचन (words) / बिनीत (humble) / कहहिं (they speak) / कर जोरी (with joined hands)
ramacharitamanas::2627.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2627.essence: Love is answered with honor, and humility becomes natural.
ramacharitamanas::2627.simple_meaning: Ram notices the love in the crowd and responds with kind words. Everyone keeps bowing to him with folded hands and humble speech.
ramacharitamanas::2627.simple_insight: True respect moves both ways: love is recognized, and humility deepens it.
ramacharitamanas::2627.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram and Lakshman meet the people who have come to see them. The crowd is overwhelmed with devotion, and Ram answers with warmth and honor. This verse lingers on that mutual tenderness before the people speak their blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2627.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is nervous to meet you, and you lower the tension with a kind sentence. That small warmth changes the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::2627.insight: It shows how gracious recognition can meet devotion without ego or distance.

ramacharitamanas::2628.verse_sanskrit: अब हम नाथ सनाथ सब भए देखि प्रभु पाय। भाग हमारें आगमनु राउर कोसलराय ॥
ramacharitamanas::2628.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! प्रभु (आप) के चरणों का दर्शन पाकर अब हम सब सनाथ हो गए। हे कोसलराज! हमारे ही भाग्य से आपका यहाँ शुभागमन हुआ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2628.english_translation: O Lord, seeing your feet, we are all now blessed. O King of Kosala, your auspicious arrival has come by our own good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::2628.translation_literal: अब (now) / हम (we) / नाथ (Lord) / सनाथ (with a protector) / सब (all) / भए (became) / देखि (seeing) / प्रभु (Lord) / पाय (feet) / भाग (fortune) / हमारें (our) / आगमनु (arrival) / राउर (your) / कोसलराय (King of Kosala)
ramacharitamanas::2628.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2628.essence: Being near Ram turns strangers into the protected.
ramacharitamanas::2628.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram makes everyone feel protected and fortunate. His presence itself is a blessing, and his arrival is treated as the greatest good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::2628.simple_insight: There is deep relief in feeling sheltered by someone worthy of trust.
ramacharitamanas::2628.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the people greet Ram with overflowing love as he arrives in their midst. They do not just admire him; they feel protected by his very presence and call his coming their own good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::2628.modern_relevance: When a weary family member finally walks into the room after a long separation, the tension drops at once. Their presence alone makes everyone breathe easier.
ramacharitamanas::2628.insight: It shifts attention from what Ram can give to what his presence already does: it restores belonging.

ramacharitamanas::2629.verse_sanskrit: धन्य भूमि बन पंथ पहारा। जहँ जहँ नाथ पाउ तुम्ह धारा॥ धन्य बिहग मृग काननचारी। सफल जनम भए तुम्हहि निहारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2629.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! जहाँ-जहाँ आपने अपने चरण रखे हैं, वे पृथ्वी, वन, मार्ग और पहाड़ धन्य हैं, वे वन में विचरने वाले पक्षी और पशु धन्य हैं, जो आपको देखकर सफल जन्म हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2629.english_translation: Blessed are the earth, forest, path, and mountains where you have placed your feet. Blessed are the birds and animals of the forest; seeing you, they have found their lives fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::2629.translation_literal: धन्य (blessed) / भूमि (earth) / बन (forest) / पंथ (path) / पहारा (mountains) / जहँ-जहँ (wherever) / नाथ (lord) / पाउ (feet) / तुम्ह (your) / धारा (placed)॥ / धन्य (blessed) / बिहग (birds) / मृग (animals) / काननचारी (forest-dwellers) / सफल (fulfilled) / जनम (birth) / भए (became) / तुम्हहि (you) / निहारी (seeing)
ramacharitamanas::2629.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2629.essence: Your presence can sanctify everything around you.
ramacharitamanas::2629.simple_meaning: Every place you touch becomes blessed, and every creature that sees you finds its life fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::2629.simple_insight: Presence itself can bless a place and make ordinary life feel complete.
ramacharitamanas::2629.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the forest dwellers greet Ram with overflowing reverence. They see the earth, paths, trees, birds, and animals as blessed simply because he has come among them. Their joy turns the forest into a sacred welcome.
ramacharitamanas::2629.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a hard week, and the mood changes before you say a word. Some people carry that kind of blessing with them.
ramacharitamanas::2629.insight: It shifts attention from what Ram receives to what his presence transforms around him.

ramacharitamanas::2630.verse_sanskrit: हम सब धन्य सहित परिवारा। दीख दरसु भरि नयन तुम्हारा॥ कीन्ह बासु भल ठाउँ बिचारी। इहाँ सकल रितु रहब सुखारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2630.verse_hindi: हम सब भी अपने परिवार सहित धन्य हैं, जिन्होंने नेत्र भरकर आपका दर्शन किया। आपने बड़ी अच्छी जगह विचारकर निवास किया है। यहाँ सभी ऋतुओं में आप सुखी रहिएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2630.english_translation: We and our families are blessed to have seen you with our own eyes. You have chosen a truly good place to stay; may you live here happily in every season.
ramacharitamanas::2630.translation_literal: हम (we) / सब (all) / धन्य (blessed) / सहित (along with) / परिवारा (families) / दीख (saw) / दरसु (darshan, sacred sight) / भरि (filled) / नयन (eyes) / तुम्हारा (your)॥ / कीन्ह (made) / बासु (stay) / भल (good) / ठाउँ (place) / बिचारी (having considered) / इहाँ (here) / सकल (all) / रितु (seasons) / रहब (to remain) / सुखारी (happily) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2630.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2630.essence: Being near the beloved makes ordinary land feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2630.simple_meaning: The villagers feel blessed just to see Ram. They praise the place he has chosen to stay and wish him comfort in every season.
ramacharitamanas::2630.simple_insight: Presence itself becomes a blessing when love is near.
ramacharitamanas::2630.detailed_meaning: In Chitrakoot, local people greet Ram after his arrival in exile. They are overwhelmed by his sight, call themselves blessed with their families, and praise the spot he has chosen to rest. Their welcome turns exile into sacred hospitality.
ramacharitamanas::2630.modern_relevance: A guest arrives after a long drive, and the whole house feels brighter. No speech is needed — everyone knows that being near the right person changes the atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::2630.insight: It shifts attention from what is lacking to the grace of welcomed presence.

ramacharitamanas::2631.verse_sanskrit: हम सब भाँति करब सेवकाई। करि केहरि अहि बाघ बराई॥ बन बेहड़ गिरि कंदर खोहा। सब हमार प्रभु पग पग जोहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2631.verse_hindi: हम लोग सब प्रकार से हाथी, सिंह, सर्प और बाघों से बचाकर आपकी सेवा करेंगे। हे प्रभो! यहाँ के बीहड़ वन, पहाड़, गुफाएँ और खोह (दर्रे) सब पग-पग हमारे देखे हुए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2631.english_translation: We will serve you in every way, protecting you from elephants, lions, snakes, and tigers. Lord, these rough forests, mountains, caves, and ravines are all familiar ground to us step by step.
ramacharitamanas::2631.translation_literal: हम (we) / सब भाँति (in every way) / करब (will do) / सेवकाई (service) / करि (protecting) / केहरि (lion) / अहि (snake) / बाघ (tiger) / बराई (from) / बन (forest) / बेहड़ (rough wilderness) / गिरि (mountain) / कंदर (cave) / खोहा (ravine) / सब (all) / हमार (our) / प्रभु (Lord) / पग पग (step by step) / जोहा (known/seen)
ramacharitamanas::2631.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2631.essence: Service becomes real when your knowledge keeps others safe.
ramacharitamanas::2631.simple_meaning: The forest people promise to serve Ram by guiding and protecting him through dangerous terrain they know well.
ramacharitamanas::2631.simple_insight: True service means making your own strength available for someone else's safety.
ramacharitamanas::2631.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the forest dwellers speak to Ram and Sita with reverence. They offer practical help, saying they know the wild paths, caves, and dangers of the forest and can protect the pair from beasts. It is a humble promise of service, not a standalone teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2631.modern_relevance: A local guide leads you through a mountain trail after dark, pointing out every loose stone and hidden turn. He is not showing off; he is offering himself as shelter.
ramacharitamanas::2631.insight: It shifts service from words to usable protection and lived familiarity.

ramacharitamanas::2632.verse_sanskrit: तहँ तहँ तुम्हहि अहेर खेलाउब। सर निरझर जलठाउँ देखाउब॥ हम सेवक परिवार समेता। नाथ न सकुचब आयसु देता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2632.verse_hindi: हम वहाँ-वहाँ (उन-उन स्थानों में) आपको शिकार खिलाएँगे और तालाब, झरने आदि जलाशयों को दिखाएँगे। हम कुटुम्ब समेत आपके सेवक हैं। हे नाथ! इसलिए हमें आज्ञा देने में संकोच न कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2632.english_translation: We will take you hunting there and there, and show you ponds, springs, and waters. We are your servants, along with our families. O Lord, do not hesitate to give us your commands.
ramacharitamanas::2632.translation_literal: तहँ तहँ (there there) / तुम्हहि (to you) / अहेर (hunting/game) / खेलाउब (we will make you play) / सर (ponds) / निरझर (springs) / जलठाउँ (water places) / देखाउब (we will show) // हम (we) / सेवक (servants) / परिवार समेता (along with family) / नाथ (Lord) / न (not) / सकुचब (hesitate) / आयसु (command) / देता (giving)
ramacharitamanas::2632.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2632.essence: True service makes the other person feel completely at home.
ramacharitamanas::2632.simple_meaning: The forest people offer Ram food, guidance, and service. They want him to feel welcome and ask for anything without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::2632.simple_insight: Real care means making room for someone else to rest, not just speaking kindly.
ramacharitamanas::2632.detailed_meaning: The forest dwellers are welcoming Ram, Sita, and Lakshman into their world. After promising protection and hospitality, they offer to guide them through the forest and serve them with their families, showing humble devotion and trust.
ramacharitamanas::2632.modern_relevance: You have guests in a place they do not know, and you keep pointing out where to eat, rest, and find water. That kind of quiet hospitality is what this verse honors.
ramacharitamanas::2632.insight: It shifts service from words to practical care: guide, provide, and remove hesitation.

ramacharitamanas::2633.verse_sanskrit: बेद बचन मुनि मन अगम ते प्रभु करुना ऐन। बचन किरातन्ह के सुनत जिमि पितु बालक बैन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2633.verse_hindi: जो वेदों के वचन और मुनियों के मन को भी अगम हैं, वे करुणा के धाम प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी भीलों के वचन इस तरह सुन रहे हैं, जैसे पिता बालकों के वचन सुनता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2633.english_translation: The Lord, who is beyond the words of the Vedas and the minds of sages, listens to the forest people’s words like a father listening to his children.
ramacharitamanas::2633.translation_literal: बेद बचन (words of the Vedas) / मुनि मन (the minds of sages) / अगम (unreachable) / ते (those) / प्रभु (the Lord) / करुना (compassion) / ऐन (dwelling place) / बचन (words) / किरातन्ह (of the forest people) / के (of) / सुनत (listening) / जिमि (like) / पितु (a father) / बालक (children) / बैन (words)
ramacharitamanas::2633.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2633.essence: Ram is beyond understanding, yet utterly open to your voice.
ramacharitamanas::2633.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond ordinary understanding, yet he listens to the forest people with the tenderness of a father hearing his children.
ramacharitamanas::2633.simple_insight: You do not need perfect words to be heard; love makes room for you.
ramacharitamanas::2633.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the people offer hospitality to Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. The verse pauses on a deeper wonder: the one beyond the reach of sages is still fully present, listening gently to simple forest folk as a father listens to children.
ramacharitamanas::2633.modern_relevance: You try to explain yourself to someone important and your words come out clumsy, half-formed, embarrassed. This verse says tenderness can understand what polished speech cannot.
ramacharitamanas::2633.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to relationship, showing that humble speech can still meet divine attention.

ramacharitamanas::2634.verse_sanskrit: रामहि केवल प्रेमु पिआरा। जानि लेउ जो जान निहारा॥ राम सकल बनचर तब तोषे। कहि मृदु बचन प्रेम परिपोषे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2634.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी को केवल प्रेम प्यारा है, जो जानने वाला हो (जानना चाहता हो), वह जान ले। तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने प्रेम से परिपुष्ट हुए (प्रेमपूर्ण) कोमल वचन कहकर उन सब वन में विचरण करने वाले लोगों को संतुष्ट किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2634.english_translation: Ram is beloved only by love; let the one who wants to know, know this. Then Ram satisfied all the forest dwellers by speaking soft, loving words.
ramacharitamanas::2634.translation_literal: रामहि (to Ram) / केवल (only) / प्रेमु (love) / पिआरा (dear) / जानि लेउ (let [one] know) / जो (who) / जान निहारा (the knower, the one who seeks to know) / राम (Ram) / सकल (all) / बनचर (forest dwellers) / तब (then) / तोषे (satisfied, pleased) / कहि (speaking) / मृदु (soft) / बचन (words) / प्रेम (love) / परिपोषे (nourished, strengthened)
ramacharitamanas::2634.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2634.essence: Ram is reached through love, and love changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::2634.simple_meaning: Ram responds to love, not display or force. When he speaks gently, even the forest people feel satisfied and cared for.
ramacharitamanas::2634.simple_insight: You do not need to impress what you love; sincerity and tenderness go further than performance.
ramacharitamanas::2634.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram meets the local people with warmth instead of royal distance. The verse pauses the scene to reveal the heart of his presence: he belongs to love, and his gentle speech immediately puts everyone at ease.
ramacharitamanas::2634.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense family gathering and stop trying to win the room. You listen, soften your voice, and the atmosphere changes before anyone notices why.
ramacharitamanas::2634.insight: It shifts the mind from proving yourself to meeting others with genuine warmth.

ramacharitamanas::2635.verse_sanskrit: बिदा किए सिर नाइ सिधाए। प्रभु गुन कहत सुनत घर आए॥ एहि बिधि सिय समेत दोउ भाई। बसहिं बिपिन सुर मुनि सुखदाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2635.verse_hindi: फिर उनको विदा किया। वे सिर नवाकर चले और प्रभु के गुण कहते-सुनते घर आए। इस प्रकार देवता और मुनियों को सुख देने वाले दोनों भाई सीताजी समेत वन में निवास करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2635.english_translation: After bowing their heads, they departed. Speaking and listening to the Lord's virtues, they returned home. In this way, the two brothers, together with Sita, lived in the forest, which became a joy to the gods and sages.
ramacharitamanas::2635.translation_literal: बिदा किए (having bid farewell) / सिर नाइ (bowing the head) / सिधाए (departed) / प्रभु (the Lord) / गुन (virtues) / कहत (speaking) / सुनत (listening) / घर (home) / आए (came) / एहि बिधि (in this way) / सिय समेत (together with Sita) / दोउ भाई (both brothers) / बसहिं (lived) / बिपिन (forest) / सुर मुनि (gods and sages) / सुखदाई (giving joy)
ramacharitamanas::2635.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2635.essence: Even leaving can become devotion when your mind stays on Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2635.simple_meaning: They took leave, went home while speaking of Ram's virtues, and then Rama, Sita, and Lakshman lived in the forest, bringing joy to sages and radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::2635.simple_insight: A holy presence changes even ordinary movement into something peaceful and blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2635.detailed_meaning: After the meeting with the forest dwellers, the brothers bow and depart. Their walk home is filled with Ram's praise. The verse then shifts to the settled life of Ram, Sita, and Lakshman in the forest, setting up the forest as a place transformed by their presence.
ramacharitamanas::2635.modern_relevance: You leave a difficult visit quietly, still talking about what was good and true. By the time you reach home, the heaviness has eased because the conversation itself carried you.
ramacharitamanas::2635.insight: It turns departure into remembrance and shows how sacred company changes the atmosphere around it.

ramacharitamanas::2636.verse_sanskrit: जब तें आइ रहे रघुनायकु। तब तें भयउ बनु मंगलदायकु॥ फूलहिं फलहिं बिटप बिधि नाना। मंजु बलित बर बेलि बिताना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2636.verse_hindi: जब से श्री रघुनाथजी वन में आकर रहे तब से वन मंगलदायक हो गया। अनेक प्रकार के वृक्ष फूलते और फलते हैं और उन पर लिपटी हुई सुंदर बेलों के मंडप तने हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2636.english_translation: Since Raghunath came here, the forest has become auspicious. Many kinds of trees bloom and bear fruit, and lovely vines spread their canopies over them.
ramacharitamanas::2636.translation_literal: जब तें (since) / आइ (came) / रहे (remained) / रघुनायकु (Raghunath) / तब तें (since then) / भयउ (became) / बनु (forest) / मंगलदायकु (auspicious-giving) ॥ / फूलहिं (bloom) / फलहिं (bear fruit) / बिटप (trees) / बिधि नाना (of many kinds) / मंजु (beautiful) / बलित (twining) / बर (excellent) / बेलि (vines) / बिताना (canopies)
ramacharitamanas::2636.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2636.essence: Ram's presence turns even the forest into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2636.simple_meaning: Ram's presence makes the forest feel blessed and alive. Trees bloom, bear fruit, and vines spread beautifully everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::2636.simple_insight: What you carry inside can change the whole atmosphere around you.
ramacharitamanas::2636.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman have settled into forest life. The wild place around them is no longer harsh and empty; it begins to flourish and feel sacred. This verse shows how Ram's presence transforms even the natural world.
ramacharitamanas::2636.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room, and the mood shifts before anyone speaks. Some presences make life feel more alive, more generous, more whole.
ramacharitamanas::2636.insight: It shifts attention from the setting itself to the transformative effect of noble presence.

ramacharitamanas::2637.verse_sanskrit: सुरतरु सरिस सुभायँ सुहाए। मनहुँ बिबुध बन परिहरि आए॥ गुंज मंजुतर मधुकर श्रेनी। त्रिबिध बयारि बहइ सुख देनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2637.verse_hindi: वे कल्पवृक्ष के समान स्वाभाविक ही सुंदर हैं। मानो वे देवताओं के वन (नंदन वन) को छोड़कर आए हों। भौंरों की पंक्तियाँ बहुत ही सुंदर गुंजार करती हैं और सुख देने वाली शीतल, मंद, सुगंधित हवा चलती रहती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2637.english_translation: They were naturally beautiful like wish-fulfilling trees, as if they had left the gods' own grove behind. Beautiful rows of bees hummed, and a gentle, cool, fragrant breeze gave delight.
ramacharitamanas::2637.translation_literal: सुरतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / सरिस (like) / सुभायँ (by nature) / सुहाए (beautiful) / मनहुँ (as if) / बिबुध (of the radiant beings) / बन (grove) / परिहरि (leaving behind) / आए (came) / गुंज (humming) / मंजुतर (very lovely) / मधुकर (bees) / श्रेनी (rows) / त्रिबिध (three kinds) / बयारि (breeze) / बहइ (blows) / सुख देनी (giving delight)
ramacharitamanas::2637.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2637.essence: Ram's presence makes the forest feel like a divine grove.
ramacharitamanas::2637.simple_meaning: The forest around Ram is so lovely that it feels like a divine grove. Bees hum softly, and a cool breeze makes everything pleasant.
ramacharitamanas::2637.simple_insight: When presence is pure, even the air around it feels different.
ramacharitamanas::2637.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are living in the forest during exile. Tulsidas pauses the story to show how their presence transforms the wild into something like a heavenly garden. This verse is part of that scenic praise, not the main teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::2637.modern_relevance: You walk into a home where someone kind has been living alone for weeks. The room feels calmer, the air lighter, even the silence gentler. Some presences change the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::2637.insight: It shifts attention from the scene itself to the sanctifying effect of Ram's presence.

ramacharitamanas::2638.verse_sanskrit: नीलकंठ कलकंठ सुक चातक चक्क चकोर। भाँति भाँति बोलहिं बिहग श्रवन सुखद चित चोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::2638.verse_hindi: नीलकंठ, कोयल, तोते, पपीहे, चकवे और चकोर आदि पक्षी कानों को सुख देने वाली और चित्त को चुराने वाली तरह-तरह की बोलियाँ बोलते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2638.english_translation: Blue-throated birds, cuckoos, parrots, chataks, chakravaks, and chakors all sing in many ways, delighting the ear and stealing the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2638.translation_literal: नीलकंठ (blue-throated bird) / कलकंठ (cuckoo) / सुक (parrot) / चातक (chatak) / चक्क (chakravak) / चकोर (chakor) / भाँति भाँति (in many ways) / बोलहिं (they speak/sing) / बिहग (birds) / श्रवन (the ear) / सुखद (giving delight) / चित (the mind/heart) / चोर (stealing)
ramacharitamanas::2638.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2638.essence: Ram's presence makes even the forest sing.
ramacharitamanas::2638.simple_meaning: The forest is so beautiful that even the birds' songs delight the ear and captivate the mind.
ramacharitamanas::2638.simple_insight: Beauty can soften the heart before you even notice it.
ramacharitamanas::2638.detailed_meaning: Ram has entered the forest, and the whole place is being transformed by his presence. After the trees and vines, Tulsidas turns to the birds: their many songs now make the forest feel alive, tender, and enchanted.
ramacharitamanas::2638.modern_relevance: You walk into a quiet park after a hard week, and the first birdsong loosens something in your chest. Some places feel different because of the presence they hold.
ramacharitamanas::2638.insight: It shifts attention from bare scenery to the way presence changes an entire environment.

ramacharitamanas::2639.verse_sanskrit: करि केहरि कपि कोल कुरंगा। बिगतबैर बिचरहिं सब संगा॥ फिरत अहेर राम छबि देखी। होहिं मुदित मृग बृंद बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2639.verse_hindi: हाथी, सिंह, बंदर, सूअर और हिरन, ये सब वैर छोड़कर साथ-साथ विचरते हैं। शिकार के लिए फिरते हुए श्री रामचन्द्रजी की छबि को देखकर पशुओं के समूह विशेष आनंदित होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2639.english_translation: Elephants, lions, monkeys, boars, and deer all roam together, free of enmity. While roaming for the hunt, they see Ram's radiant form, and the herds of deer become especially joyful.
ramacharitamanas::2639.translation_literal: करि (elephant) / केहरि (lion) / कपि (monkey) / कोल (boar) / कुरंगा (deer) / बिगतबैर (free from enmity) / बिचरहिं (roam) / सब (all) / संगा (together)॥ / फिरत (roaming) / अहेर (for hunt) / राम (Ram) / छबि (radiant form) / देखी (having seen) / होहिं (become) / मुदित (joyful) / मृग बृंद (herds of deer) / बिसेषी (especially) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2639.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2639.essence: Ram's presence turns fear into harmony.
ramacharitamanas::2639.simple_meaning: Even natural enemies live together in peace here, and Ram's presence makes the animals especially happy.
ramacharitamanas::2639.simple_insight: His presence softens what would normally be separate, tense, or afraid.
ramacharitamanas::2639.detailed_meaning: The scene is no longer just a forest; it has become Ram's forest. Tulsidas shows elephants, lions, monkeys, boars, and deer living without fear or hostility. Even the hunted creatures brighten when they glimpse Ram's beauty.
ramacharitamanas::2639.modern_relevance: A room full of people who normally compete starts to relax the moment the person everyone trusts walks in. The atmosphere changes before anyone says a word.
ramacharitamanas::2639.insight: It shifts attention from danger and division to the peace created by a noble presence.

ramacharitamanas::2640.verse_sanskrit: बिबुध बिपिन जहँ लगि जग माहीं। देखि रामबनु सकल सिहाहीं॥ सुरसरि सरसइ दिनकर कन्या। मेकलसुता गोदावरि धन्या ॥
ramacharitamanas::2640.verse_hindi: जगत में जहाँ तक (जितने) देवताओं के वन हैं, सब श्री रामजी के वन को देखकर सिहाते हैं, गंगा, सरस्वती, सूर्यकुमारी यमुना, नर्मदा, गोदावरी आदि धन्य (पुण्यमयी) नदियाँ, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2640.english_translation: Wherever the divine groves exist in the world, they all envy Ram's forest. The sacred rivers — Ganga, Saraswati, Yamuna, Narmada, and Godavari — are blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2640.translation_literal: बिबुध (of the divine beings) / बिपिन (groves, forests) / जहँ लगि (as far as) / जग माहीं (in the world) / देखि (seeing) / रामबनु (Ram's forest) / सकल (all) / सिहाहीं (envy) ॥ / सुरसरि (sacred river) / सरसइ (Saraswati) / दिनकर कन्या (sun-born daughter, Yamuna) / मेकलसुता (daughter of Mekala, Narmada) / गोदावरि (Godavari) / धन्या (blessed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2640.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2640.essence: Ram's presence makes even holy places feel small.
ramacharitamanas::2640.simple_meaning: Ram's forest is so beautiful that even the divine groves seem to envy it. Sacred rivers like Ganga, Saraswati, Yamuna, Narmada, and Godavari are praised as blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2640.simple_insight: Beauty can be so complete that it feels larger than the world around it.
ramacharitamanas::2640.detailed_meaning: The story pauses in Ayodhya's sorrow to praise the places touched by Ram's presence. Tulsidas lists forests and holy rivers, saying they lose their pride before Ram's forest and its sanctity. The verse builds a devotional landscape, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2640.modern_relevance: You walk into a quiet riverside grove at dawn and feel, for a moment, that the whole place has been sanctified by presence alone.
ramacharitamanas::2640.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary scenery to sacred atmosphere created by association.

ramacharitamanas::2641.verse_sanskrit: सब सर सिंधु नदीं नद नाना। मंदाकिनि कर करहिं बखाना॥ उदय अस्त गिरि अरु कैलासू। मंदर मेरु सकल सुरबासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2641.verse_hindi: सारे तालाब, समुद्र, नदी और अनेकों नद सब मंदाकिनी की बड़ाई करते हैं। उदयाचल, अस्ताचल, कैलास, मंदराचल और सुमेरु आदि सब, जो देवताओं के रहने के स्थान हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2641.english_translation: All ponds, oceans, rivers, and countless streams praise the Mandakini. The eastern and western mountains, Kailash, Mandar, and Meru, all the homes of the radiant beings, too.
ramacharitamanas::2641.translation_literal: सब (all) / सर (ponds) / सिंधु (oceans) / नदीं (rivers) / नद (streams) / नाना (many) / मंदाकिनि (Mandakini) / कर (of) / करहिं (they do) / बखाना (praise) ॥ उदय (rising) / अस्त (setting) / गिरि (mountains) / अरु (and) / कैलासू (Kailash) / मंदर (Mandar) / मेरु (Meru) / सकल (all) / सुरबासू (homes of the radiant beings) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2641.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2641.essence: Sacred greatness draws every other greatness into praise.
ramacharitamanas::2641.simple_meaning: Every river, sea, and mountain is described as praising the Mandakini and the holy places around it.
ramacharitamanas::2641.simple_insight: Greatness is shown by the way everything around it naturally bows to it.
ramacharitamanas::2641.detailed_meaning: The narration is praising Chitrakoot through its sacred geography. Rivers, seas, and great mountains are all said to honor Mandakini and the divine landscape there, building the sense that this exile-place has become spiritually supreme.
ramacharitamanas::2641.modern_relevance: You walk into a place and feel its quiet authority before anyone speaks. The room, the people, even the silence seem to recognize what matters there.
ramacharitamanas::2641.insight: It shifts attention from isolated greatness to the way holiness makes its surroundings testify.

ramacharitamanas::2642.verse_sanskrit: सैल हिमाचल आदिक जेते। चित्रकूट जसु गावहिं तेते॥ बिंधि मुदित मन सुखु न समाई। श्रम बिनु बिपुल बड़ाई पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2642.verse_hindi: और हिमालय आदि जितने पर्वत हैं, सभी चित्रकूट का यश गाते हैं। विन्ध्याचल बड़ा आनंदित है, उसके मन में सुख समाता नहीं, क्योंकि उसने बिना परिश्रम ही बहुत बड़ी बड़ाई पा ली है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2642.english_translation: All the mountains, including the Himalayas, sing the glory of Chitrakoot. Vindhyachal is filled with joy; his heart cannot contain the delight, because he received such great praise without any effort.
ramacharitamanas::2642.translation_literal: सैल (mountains) / हिमाचल (Himalaya) / आदिक (and others) / जेते (all that are) / चित्रकूट (Chitrakoot) / जसु (glory) / गावहिं (sing) / तेते (those)॥ / बिंधि (Vindhya) / मुदित (delighted) / मन (mind) / सुखु (happiness) / न (not) / समाई (fits within) / श्रम (effort) / बिनु (without) / बिपुल (great) / बड़ाई (praise) / पाई (received) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2642.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2642.essence: Grace can make even the proud rejoice without effort.
ramacharitamanas::2642.simple_meaning: Even the great mountains praise Chitrakoot. Vindhyachal feels overjoyed because he has received great honor without any effort.
ramacharitamanas::2642.simple_insight: True honor can feel sweeter when it arrives without striving.
ramacharitamanas::2642.detailed_meaning: As the exile journey settles into Chitrakoot, Tulsidas widens the scene into a chorus of mountains praising the holy place. Vindhyachal is especially joyful, not because he achieved something, but because grace has made him worthy of praise.
ramacharitamanas::2642.modern_relevance: You get unexpectedly praised in a room where you said almost nothing. The surprise is not the attention itself, but the feeling that something larger than effort is moving through your life.
ramacharitamanas::2642.insight: It shifts attention from achievement to grace, showing that worth can be received, not only earned.

ramacharitamanas::2643.verse_sanskrit: चित्रकूट के बिहग मृग बेलि बिटप तृन जाति। पुन्य पुंज सब धन्य अस कहहिं देव दिन राति ॥
ramacharitamanas::2643.verse_hindi: चित्रकूट के पक्षी, पशु, बेल, वृक्ष, तृण-अंकुरादि की सभी जातियाँ पुण्य की राशि हैं और धन्य हैं- देवता दिन-रात ऐसा कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2643.english_translation: The birds, animals, vines, trees, and blades of grass of Chitrakoot are all said to be a heap of merit and blessed; the devas say this day and night.
ramacharitamanas::2643.translation_literal: चित्रकूट के (of Chitrakoot) / बिहग (birds) / मृग (deer, animals) / बेलि (vines) / बिटप (trees) / तृन (grass) / जाति (kinds) / पुन्य पुंज (heap of merit) / सब (all) / धन्य (blessed) / अस (thus) / कहहिं (say) / देव (devas) / दिन राति (day and night)
ramacharitamanas::2643.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2643.essence: Ram's presence makes even grass and birds feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::2643.simple_meaning: Even the birds, animals, plants, and grass of Chitrakoot are considered blessed. The verse says this sacredness is so complete that even the devas keep praising it.
ramacharitamanas::2643.simple_insight: Some places feel so alive with holiness that even the smallest things seem transformed.
ramacharitamanas::2643.detailed_meaning: The narrator is praising Chitrakoot after describing its hills, rivers, and forests. Every living thing there—birds, deer, vines, trees, and even grass—is treated as blessed. The point is to prepare for Ram's presence there and the holiness his arrival brings.
ramacharitamanas::2643.modern_relevance: You walk into a place where someone deeply loved has lived, and even the ordinary chair, cup, and doorway feel charged with meaning. Presence changes everything around it.
ramacharitamanas::2643.insight: It shifts attention from scenery alone to the sacred quality a presence can give to an entire place.

ramacharitamanas::2644.verse_sanskrit: नयनवंत रघुबरहि बिलोकी। पाइ जनम फल होहिं बिसोकी॥ परसि चरन रज अचर सुखारी। भए परम पद के अधिकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2644.verse_hindi: आँखों वाले जीव श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर जन्म का फल पाकर शोकरहित हो जाते हैं और अचर (पर्वत, वृक्ष, भूमि, नदी आदि) भगवान की चरण रज का स्पर्श पाकर सुखी होते हैं। यों सभी परम पद (मोक्ष) के अधिकारी हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2644.english_translation: All who have eyes and behold Raghubar become free of sorrow, having found the fruit of birth. Even beings without movement become blessed by touching the dust of his feet, and all become worthy of the highest state.
ramacharitamanas::2644.translation_literal: नयनवंत (those with eyes) / रघुबरहि (Raghubar) / बिलोकी (having seen) / पाइ (having obtained) / जनम (birth) / फल (fruit) / होहिं (become) / बिसोकी (free from sorrow) // परसि (touching) / चरन (feet) / रज (dust) / अचर (motionless beings) / सुखारी (blessed) / भए (became) / परम (highest) / पद (state) / के (of) / अधिकारी (worthy, entitled)
ramacharitamanas::2644.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2644.essence: Ram's presence alone turns sorrow into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2644.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram brings the true reward of life. Even trees, rocks, and rivers are blessed by the dust of his feet.
ramacharitamanas::2644.simple_insight: Closeness to the divine changes everything — even what cannot move is made holy.
ramacharitamanas::2644.detailed_meaning: In Chitrakoot, the forest itself seems transformed by Ram and Lakshman’s presence. Tulsidas says that anyone with eyes becomes free of sorrow by seeing Ram, and even unmoving beings are blessed by the dust of his feet.
ramacharitamanas::2644.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the whole mood changes because one person arrived with real presence. That is the feeling here: being near Ram is not just comforting, it is transforming.
ramacharitamanas::2644.insight: It shifts attention from what Ram gives to what his presence itself does.

ramacharitamanas::2645.verse_sanskrit: सो बनु सैलु सुभायँ सुहावन। मंगलमय अति पावन पावन॥ महिमा कहिअ कवनि बिधि तासू। सुखसागर जहँ कीन्ह निवासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2645.verse_hindi: वह वन और पर्वत स्वाभाविक ही सुंदर, मंगलमय और अत्यन्त पवित्रों को भी पवित्र करने वाला है। उसकी महिमा किस प्रकार कही जाए, जहाँ सुख के समुद्र श्री रामजी ने निवास किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2645.english_translation: That forest and mountain are naturally beautiful, filled with auspiciousness, and purer than the pure. How can their glory be described, where the ocean of joy made his home?
ramacharitamanas::2645.translation_literal: सो (that) / बनु (forest) / सैलु (mountain) / सुभायँ (by nature) / सुहावन (beautiful) / मंगलमय (full of auspiciousness) / अति (very) / पावन (pure) / पावन (purifying the pure)॥ / महिमा (glory) / कहिअ (is spoken) / कवनि (which) / बिधि (way) / तासू (of that) / सुखसागर (ocean of joy) / जहँ (where) / कीन्ह (made) / निवासू (residence)॥
ramacharitamanas::2645.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2645.essence: Ram's presence turns even wild places into sanctuaries.
ramacharitamanas::2645.simple_meaning: The forest and mountain became beautiful and deeply pure because Ram lived there. Their holiness is beyond words.
ramacharitamanas::2645.simple_insight: Love and presence can sanctify even the roughest place.
ramacharitamanas::2645.detailed_meaning: In Chitrakoot, the exile has turned a forest into a holy refuge. Tulsidas pauses to marvel that Ram's stay has transformed the mountains and woods themselves, making them feel more pure than anything else.
ramacharitamanas::2645.modern_relevance: You walk into a plain, cramped room after someone steady and kind has lived there for months. The room still looks ordinary, but it feels different because their presence changed its atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::2645.insight: It shifts attention from scenery to presence: what matters most is not the place, but who dwells there.

ramacharitamanas::2646.verse_sanskrit: पय पयोधि तजि अवध बिहाई। जहँ सिय लखनु रामु रहे आई॥ कहि न सकहिं सुषमा जसि कानन। जौं सत सहस होहिं सहसानन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2646.verse_hindi: क्षीर सागर को त्यागकर और अयोध्या को छोड़कर जहाँ सीताजी, लक्ष्मणजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी आकर रहे, उस वन की जैसी परम शोभा है, उसको हजार मुख वाले जो लाख शेषजी हों तो वे भी नहीं कह सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::2646.english_translation: Leaving the ocean of milk and abandoning Ayodhya, the forest where Sita, Lakshman, and Ram came to live is so beautiful that even a thousand-hooded serpent could not describe it.
ramacharitamanas::2646.translation_literal: पय (milk) / पयोधि (ocean) / तजि (leaving) / अवध (Ayodhya) / बिहाई (abandoning) / जहँ (where) / सिय (Sita) / लखनु (Lakshman) / रामु (Ram) / रहे (stayed) / आई (came) / कहि (say) / न सकहिं (cannot) / सुषमा (beauty) / जसि (as) / कानन (forest) / जौं (even if) / सत (hundred) / सहस (thousand) / होहिं (become) / सहसानन (thousand-mouthed serpent)
ramacharitamanas::2646.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2646.essence: Love makes even exile feel radiant.
ramacharitamanas::2646.simple_meaning: The forest becomes unimaginably beautiful because Ram, Sita, and Lakshman live there. Even the greatest speaker could not fully describe it.
ramacharitamanas::2646.simple_insight: What you love transforms the place you are in.
ramacharitamanas::2646.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya’s exile, the sacred trio has settled in the forest. Tulsidas pauses the story to say that their presence makes the wilderness radiant beyond description. The verse is a praise of place transformed by love, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2646.modern_relevance: A cramped rented room can feel like home the moment the people you love sit on the floor and laugh there. Presence changes the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::2646.insight: It shifts attention from scenery to sanctifying presence.

ramacharitamanas::2647.verse_sanskrit: सो मैं बरनि कहौं बिधि केहीं। डाबर कमठ कि मंदर लेहीं॥ सेवहिं लखनु करम मन बानी। जाइ न सीलु सनेहु बखानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2647.verse_hindi: उसे भला, मैं किस प्रकार से वर्णन करके कह सकता हूँ। कहीं पोखरे का (क्षुद्र) कछुआ भी मंदराचल उठा सकता है? लक्ष्मणजी मन, वचन और कर्म से श्री रामचन्द्रजी की सेवा करते हैं। उनके शील और स्नेह का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2647.english_translation: How can I possibly describe it? Could even a tiny pond turtle lift Mount Mandara? Lakshman serves Ram with mind, speech, and action. His character and affection cannot be described.
ramacharitamanas::2647.translation_literal: सो (that) / मैं (I) / बरनि (describing) / कहौं (can say) / बिधि (in what way) / केहीं (which) / डाबर (pond) / कमठ (turtle) / कि (or) / मंदर (Mandara mountain) / लेहीं (lift) / सेवहिं (serve) / लखनु (Lakshman) / करम (action) / मन (mind) / बानी (speech) / जाइ (can go) / न (not) / सीलु (character) / सनेहु (affection) / बखानी (described)
ramacharitamanas::2647.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2647.essence: True service is so complete that description falls short.
ramacharitamanas::2647.simple_meaning: Lakshman serves Ram with complete devotion in thought, speech, and action, and his character and affection are beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::2647.simple_insight: Some service is so complete that words can only point toward it, never contain it.
ramacharitamanas::2647.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is describing the beauty of the forest life where Ram, Sita, and Lakshman live together. After praising the forest itself, he turns to Lakshman’s total service to Ram, saying even impossible comparisons fail to capture his devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2647.modern_relevance: You try to explain why one friend stayed up all night helping you move, then still refused credit. The explanation always feels smaller than the loyalty itself.
ramacharitamanas::2647.insight: It shifts attention from performance to wholehearted service that is carried through mind, speech, and action.

ramacharitamanas::2648.verse_sanskrit: छिनु छिनु लखि सिय राम पद जानि आपु पर नेहु। करत न सपनेहुँ लखनु चितु बंधु मातु पितु गेहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2648.verse_hindi: क्षण-क्षण पर श्री सीता-रामजी के चरणों को देखकर और अपने ऊपर उनका स्नेह जानकर लक्ष्मणजी स्वप्न में भी भाइयों, माता-पिता और घर की याद नहीं करते ॥
ramacharitamanas::2648.english_translation: Moment by moment, seeing Sita and Ram's feet and knowing their love for him, Lakshman never even dreams of brother, mother, father, or home.
ramacharitamanas::2648.translation_literal: छिनु छिनु (moment by moment) / लखि (seeing) / सिय राम पद (Sita and Ram's feet) / जानि (knowing) / आपु पर नेहु (their love for him) / करत (doing) / न सपनेहुँ (not even in a dream) / लखनु (Lakshman) / चितु (mind) / बंधु (brother) / मातु पितु (mother and father) / गेहु (home)
ramacharitamanas::2648.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2648.essence: True devotion makes every lesser attachment fade.
ramacharitamanas::2648.simple_meaning: Lakshman is so absorbed in Ram and Sita's presence and love that he forgets his own family and home completely.
ramacharitamanas::2648.simple_insight: Deep love can reorder what your mind calls important.
ramacharitamanas::2648.detailed_meaning: In exile, Lakshman lives beside Ram and Sita in the forest. Their presence and affection are so complete for him that he no longer turns back toward his parents, brother, or palace. This verse praises total loving service.
ramacharitamanas::2648.modern_relevance: You keep checking your old group chat, your family thread, your childhood photos, looking for a feeling that has already been replaced by something deeper. Real belonging can make the old ache go quiet.
ramacharitamanas::2648.insight: It shifts attention from what you have left behind to what you are serving now.

ramacharitamanas::2649.verse_sanskrit: राम संग सिय रहति सुखारी। पुर परिजन गृह सुरति बिसारी॥ छिनु छिनु पिय बिधु बदनु निहारी। प्रमुदित मनहुँ चकोर कुमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2649.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के साथ सीताजी अयोध्यापुरी, कुटुम्ब के लोग और घर की याद भूलकर बहुत ही सुखी रहती हैं। क्षण-क्षण पर पति श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चन्द्रमा के समान मुख को देखकर वे वैसे ही परम प्रसन्न रहती हैं, जैसे चकोर कुमारी (चकोरी) चन्द्रमा को देखकर ! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2649.english_translation: Sita lives happily with Ram, forgetting the city, family, and home. Again and again she looks at her beloved Ram's moonlike face, delighted like a chakor bird seeing the moon.
ramacharitamanas::2649.translation_literal: राम संग (with Ram) / सिय (Sita) / रहति (remains) / सुखारी (happy) / पुर (city) / परिजन (family) / गृह (home) / सुरति (remembrance) / बिसारी (forgot) ॥ / छिनु छिनु (moment by moment) / पिय (beloved) / बिधु (moon) / बदनु (face) / निहारी (gazing) / प्रमुदित (delighted) / मनहुँ (as if) / चकोर (chakor bird) / कुमारी (maiden) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2649.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2649.essence: Presence with the beloved makes the whole world recede.
ramacharitamanas::2649.simple_meaning: Sita feels complete with Ram beside her. She forgets palace life and family ties, and finds joy simply in looking at his face.
ramacharitamanas::2649.simple_insight: Love can make even the grandest home feel secondary.
ramacharitamanas::2649.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita lives beside Ram in Ayodhya with such contentment that palace, relatives, and domestic comforts no longer matter to her. Her happiness comes from his presence alone, and she keeps turning to his face like a bird drawn to the moon.
ramacharitamanas::2649.modern_relevance: You come home exhausted, drop your phone, and sit beside the one person who makes the day feel lighter. The noise of work, family demands, and unfinished tasks suddenly loosens its grip.
ramacharitamanas::2649.insight: It shifts attention from external comfort to the steady joy of shared presence.

ramacharitamanas::2650.verse_sanskrit: नाह नेहु नित बढ़त बिलोकी। हरषित रहति दिवस जिमि कोकी॥ सिय मनु राम चरन अनुरागा। अवध सहस सम बनु प्रिय लागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2650.verse_hindi: स्वामी का प्रेम अपने प्रति नित्य बढ़ता हुआ देखकर सीताजी ऐसी हर्षित रहती हैं, जैसे दिन में चकवी! सीताजी का मन श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में अनुरक्त है, इससे उनको वन हजारों अवध के समान प्रिय लगता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2650.english_translation: Seeing her lord's love grow every day, Sita remains delighted like a chakori in daylight. Her mind is attached to Ram's feet, so the forest feels as dear to her as thousands of Ayodhyas.
ramacharitamanas::2650.translation_literal: नाह (lord) / नेहु (love) / नित (always) / बढ़त (growing) / बिलोकी (seeing) / हरषित (delighted) / रहति (remains) / दिवस (day) / जिमि (like) / कोकी (chakori) / सिय (Sita) / मनु (mind) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / अनुरागा (attached in love) / अवध (Ayodhya) / सहस (thousand) / सम (equal to) / बनु (forest) / प्रिय (dear) / लागा (seems)
ramacharitamanas::2650.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2650.essence: Devotion can make exile feel like home.
ramacharitamanas::2650.simple_meaning: Sita is so devoted to Ram that his growing love fills her with joy, and the forest itself feels dear to her.
ramacharitamanas::2650.simple_insight: Love can transform hardship into belonging.
ramacharitamanas::2650.detailed_meaning: Sita is in the forest with Ram, far from Ayodhya, yet her heart is not in exile. She sees Ram's affection growing, and that devotion makes the wilderness feel as precious as the kingdom she left behind.
ramacharitamanas::2650.modern_relevance: You move to a new city and the apartment is bare, the streets unfamiliar, the days long. Then one steady relationship makes the whole place feel livable.
ramacharitamanas::2650.insight: It shifts attachment from place and comfort to presence and love.

ramacharitamanas::2651.verse_sanskrit: परनकुटी प्रिय प्रियतम संगा। प्रिय परिवारु कुरंग बिहंगा॥ सासु ससुर सम मुनितिय मुनिबर। असनु अमिअ सम कंद मूल फर ॥
ramacharitamanas::2651.verse_hindi: प्रियतम (श्री रामचन्द्रजी) के साथ पर्णकुटी प्यारी लगती है। मृग और पक्षी प्यारे कुटुम्बियों के समान लगते हैं। मुनियों की स्त्रियाँ सास के समान, श्रेष्ठ मुनि ससुर के समान और कंद-मूल-फलों का आहार उनको अमृत के समान लगता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2651.english_translation: The forest hut feels dear when you are with your beloved. Deer and birds feel like family. The women of the forest feel like mothers-in-law, the great sages feel like fathers-in-law, and roots, fruits, and tubers taste like nectar.
ramacharitamanas::2651.translation_literal: परनकुटी (forest hut) / प्रिय (dear) / प्रियतम (beloved) / संगा (with) । प्रिय (dear) / परिवारु (family) / कुरंग (deer) / बिहंगा (birds) । सासु (mother-in-law) / ससुर (father-in-law) / सम (like) / मुनितिय (women sages) / मुनिबर (great sages) । असनु (food) / अमिअ (nectar) / सम (like) / कंद (roots) / मूल (tubers) / फर (fruits) ।
ramacharitamanas::2651.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2651.essence: Love can turn exile into belonging.
ramacharitamanas::2651.simple_meaning: When you are with the one you love, even a forest hut feels dear. Everything around you starts to feel like family, and simple forest food feels delicious.
ramacharitamanas::2651.simple_insight: Love changes the world around you; hardship softens when the heart feels held.
ramacharitamanas::2651.detailed_meaning: Sita is living in the forest with Ram. She no longer feels exiled: the hut feels lovely, the animals feel like kin, the forest women feel like relatives, and even plain roots and fruit taste sweet. Love has transformed deprivation into comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2651.modern_relevance: You move to a new city and the room is bare, the streets are strange, and the food is plain. Then one person you love walks in, and the whole place stops feeling foreign.
ramacharitamanas::2651.insight: It shifts attention from outer comfort to the transforming power of loving presence.

ramacharitamanas::2652.verse_sanskrit: नाथ साथ साँथरी सुहाई। मयन सयन सय सम सुखदाई॥ लोकप होहिं बिलोकत जासू। तेहि कि मोहि सक बिषय बिलासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2652.verse_hindi: स्वामी के साथ सुंदर साथरी (कुश और पत्तों की सेज) सैकड़ों कामदेव की सेजों के समान सुख देने वाली है। जिनके (कृपापूर्वक) देखने मात्र से जीव लोकपाल हो जाते हैं, उनको कहीं भोग-विलास मोहित कर सकते हैं! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2652.english_translation: Being with my Lord, this simple bed of grass and leaves feels as सुखदायक as a hundred beds of desire. Those whom even the celestial guardians long to behold—how could worldly pleasures ever tempt me?
ramacharitamanas::2652.translation_literal: नाथ (Lord) / साथ (with) / साँथरी (bed) / सुहाई (beautiful, pleasing) / मयन (of desire) / सयन (bed) / सय (hundred) / सम (like) / सुखदाई (giving joy)॥ / लोकप (world-guardians) / होहिं (become) / बिलोकत (by seeing) / जासू (whom) / तेहि (that one) / कि (how) / मोहि (to me) / सक (can) / बिषय (sense-pleasures) / बिलासू (luxury, indulgence) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2652.speaker: Sita
ramacharitamanas::2652.essence: Ram's presence turns hardship into ease and luxury into irrelevance.
ramacharitamanas::2652.simple_meaning: Sita says that being with Ram makes a simple grass bed feel better than luxurious comfort. When even great beings long to see him, worldly pleasures lose all appeal.
ramacharitamanas::2652.simple_insight: Love can make hardship feel gentle and luxury feel unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::2652.detailed_meaning: In the forest exile, Sita lives in a tiny leaf hut beside Ram. She looks at the simple bed and feels no lack at all, because Ram's presence turns poverty into comfort. The verse shows how devotion changes the value of everything around her.
ramacharitamanas::2652.modern_relevance: You sit on a hard floor in a crowded train station, waiting beside someone you love, and the discomfort barely matters. Presence changes the whole experience.
ramacharitamanas::2652.insight: It shifts attention from external comfort to the quality of companionship.

ramacharitamanas::2653.verse_sanskrit: सुमिरत रामहि तजहिं जन तृन सम बिषय बिलासु। रामप्रिया जग जननि सिय कछु न आचरजु तासु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2653.verse_hindi: जिन श्री रामचन्द्रजी का स्मरण करने से ही भक्तजन तमाम भोग-विलास को तिनके के समान त्याग देते हैं, उन श्री रामचन्द्रजी की प्रिय पत्नी और जगत की माता सीताजी के लिए यह (भोग-विलास का त्याग) कुछ भी आश्चर्य नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2653.english_translation: Those who remember Ram let go of worldly pleasures as if they were blades of grass. For Sita, beloved of Ram and mother of the world, that is no surprise.
ramacharitamanas::2653.translation_literal: सुमिरत (remembering) / रामहि (Ram) / तजहिं (let go) / जन (people) / तृन सम (like grass) / बिषय बिलासु (worldly pleasures) / रामप्रिया (beloved of Ram) / जग जननि (mother of the world) / सिय (Sita) / कछु (some) / न (not) / आचरजु (surprise) / तासु (for her)
ramacharitamanas::2653.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2653.essence: Love for Ram makes pleasure lose its power.
ramacharitamanas::2653.simple_meaning: Remembering Ram makes worldly pleasures lose their grip. For Sita, who belongs to Ram completely, giving them up is natural, not remarkable.
ramacharitamanas::2653.simple_insight: You can become so full of love that old cravings stop feeling important.
ramacharitamanas::2653.detailed_meaning: In exile, Ram and Sita live in a forest hut. Tulsidas pauses the story to say that people who remember Ram can treat pleasure like grass. For Sita, Ram's beloved and the world's mother, such renunciation is simply her nature.
ramacharitamanas::2653.modern_relevance: You finally leave a party early, not from boredom but because your child's fever is rising and your mind is already elsewhere. What used to feel irresistible now feels small beside what you love most.
ramacharitamanas::2653.insight: It shifts desire from chasing pleasure to resting in what truly matters.

ramacharitamanas::2654.verse_sanskrit: सीय लखन जेहि बिधि सुखु लहहीं। सोइ रघुनाथ करहिं सोइ कहहीं॥ कहहिं पुरातन कथा कहानी। सुनहिं लखनु सिय अति सुखु मानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2654.verse_hindi: सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी को जिस प्रकार सुख मिले, श्री रघुनाथजी वही करते और वही कहते हैं। भगवान प्राचीन कथाएँ और कहानियाँ कहते हैं और लक्ष्मणजी तथा सीताजी अत्यन्त सुख मानकर सुनते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2654.english_translation: In whatever way Sita and Lakshman find happiness, Raghunath does and says the same. He tells ancient stories and tales, and Lakshman and Sita listen with great delight.
ramacharitamanas::2654.translation_literal: सीय (Sita) / लखन (Lakshman) / जेहि बिधि (in whatever way) / सुखु (happiness) / लहहीं (find) / सोइ (the same) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / करहिं (does) / सोइ (the same) / कहहीं (says) / कहहिं (say) / पुरातन (ancient) / कथा (stories) / कहानी (tales) / सुनहिं (listen) / लखनु (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / अति (greatly) / सुखु (joy) / मानी (considering)
ramacharitamanas::2654.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2654.essence: True closeness means shaping yourself around another's joy.
ramacharitamanas::2654.simple_meaning: Ram naturally does and says whatever brings Sita and Lakshman happiness. He spends time telling old stories, and they listen with deep joy.
ramacharitamanas::2654.simple_insight: Love is not abstract here; it adapts itself to the happiness of the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::2654.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is living in exile with Sita and Lakshman. Instead of acting like a distant prince, he stays close to their hearts: he speaks, tells old stories, and chooses whatever brings them ease. Their joy becomes his way of being.
ramacharitamanas::2654.modern_relevance: You come home exhausted, and instead of scrolling away in silence, you tell the story they needed to hear. The real intimacy is not grand speech — it is learning what brings the other person peace.
ramacharitamanas::2654.insight: It shifts love from self-expression to responsive companionship.

ramacharitamanas::2655.verse_sanskrit: जब जब रामु अवध सुधि करहीं। तब तब बारि बिलोचन भरहीं॥ सुमिरि मातु पितु परिजन भाई। भरत सनेहु सीलु सेवकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2655.verse_hindi: जब-जब श्री रामचन्द्रजी अयोध्या की याद करते हैं, तब-तब उनके नेत्रों में जल भर आता है। माता-पिता, कुटुम्बियों और भाइयों तथा भरत के प्रेम, शील और सेवाभाव को याद करके- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2655.english_translation: Whenever Ram remembers Ayodhya, tears fill his eyes. He remembers his mother, father, family, brothers, and Bharat's love, character, and service.
ramacharitamanas::2655.translation_literal: जब जब (whenever) / रामु (Ram) / अवध (Ayodhya) / सुधि (remembrance) / करहीं (do) / तब तब (then) / बारि (water) / बिलोचन (eyes) / भरहीं (fill) ॥ / सुमिरि (remembering) / मातु (mother) / पितु (father) / परिजन (family) / भाई (brothers) / भरत (Bharat) / सनेहु (love) / सीलु (character) / सेवकाई (service) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2655.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2655.essence: Remembrance can bring even Ram to tears.
ramacharitamanas::2655.simple_meaning: Ram thinks of Ayodhya and weeps, remembering his family and Bharat's loving service.
ramacharitamanas::2655.simple_insight: Love stays alive through memory, and even the strongest heart can soften with longing.
ramacharitamanas::2655.detailed_meaning: In exile, Ram keeps thinking of Ayodhya. Each remembrance brings tears, not from weakness but from the ache of love. He especially remembers Bharat's devotion, along with the family bonds he has left behind.
ramacharitamanas::2655.modern_relevance: You pass the old neighborhood on the train and suddenly your chest tightens. A name, a street, a face you miss — memory can still bring tears.
ramacharitamanas::2655.insight: It shows that remembrance is not passive; it can reopen love, grief, and gratitude all at once.

ramacharitamanas::2656.verse_sanskrit: कृपासिंधु प्रभु होहिं दुखारी। धीरजु धरहिं कुसमउ बिचारी॥ लखि सिय लखनु बिकल होइ जाहीं। जिमि पुरुषहि अनुसर परिछाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2656.verse_hindi: कृपा के समुद्र प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी दुःखी हो जाते हैं, किन्तु फिर कुसमय समझकर धीरज धारण कर लेते हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी को दुःखी देखकर सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी भी व्याकुल हो जाते हैं, जैसे किसी मनुष्य की परछाहीं उस मनुष्य के समान ही चेष्टा करती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2656.english_translation: The ocean of compassion, the Lord, feels sorrow; then, seeing the wrong time, he steadies himself. Seeing Ram distressed, Sita and Lakshman become restless too, just as a shadow follows the body.
ramacharitamanas::2656.translation_literal: कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / प्रभु (Lord) / होहिं (become) / दुखारी (sorrowful) / धीरजु (patience, steadiness) / धरहिं (they hold) / कुसमउ (wrong time, bad moment) / बिचारी (considering) / लखि (seeing) / सिय (Sita) / लखनु (Lakshman) / बिकल (agitated) / होइ (become) / जाहीं (go) / जिमि (just as) / पुरुषहि (the person) / अनुसर (following) / परिछाहीं (shadow)
ramacharitamanas::2656.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2656.essence: Your inner weather quietly becomes everyone else's.
ramacharitamanas::2656.simple_meaning: Ram feels the pain of the moment, but he holds himself steady. When he is distressed, Sita and Lakshman are disturbed too, just as a shadow follows the body.
ramacharitamanas::2656.simple_insight: Your state affects the people closest to you more than you realize.
ramacharitamanas::2656.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is living in exile and remembering the pain of his situation. Even the compassionate Lord feels sorrow, but he restrains himself. Sita and Lakshman instantly mirror his mood, showing how deeply shared love binds them.
ramacharitamanas::2656.modern_relevance: You walk into the house after a brutal phone call, and everyone feels the shift before you say a word. Your silence, tension, or steadiness spreads faster than explanations.
ramacharitamanas::2656.insight: It shows how emotional states ripple through close relationships and how self-restraint protects others from being swept along.

ramacharitamanas::2657.verse_sanskrit: प्रिया बंधु गति लखि रघुनंदनु। धीर कृपाल भगत उर चंदनु॥ लगे कहन कछु कथा पुनीता। सुनि सुखु लहहिं लखनु अरु सीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2657.verse_hindi: तब धीर, कृपालु और भक्तों के हृदयों को शीतल करने के लिए चंदन रूप रघुकुल को आनंदित करने वाले श्री रामचन्द्रजी प्यारी पत्नी और भाई लक्ष्मण की दशा देखकर कुछ पवित्र कथाएँ कहने लगते हैं, जिन्हें सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सुख प्राप्त करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2657.english_translation: Seeing the condition of his dear wife and brother, the gentle, compassionate Raghunandan, the sandalwood for devotees' hearts, began to speak some holy stories. Hearing them, Lakshman and Sita found peace.
ramacharitamanas::2657.translation_literal: प्रिया (dear) / बंधु (brother) / गति (condition) / लखि (seeing) / रघुनंदनु (Raghunandan) / धीर (calm) / कृपाल (compassionate) / भगत (devotees') / उर (heart) / चंदनु (sandalwood) / लगे (began) / कहन (to speak) / कछु (some) / कथा (stories) / पुनीता (holy) / सुनि (hearing) / सुखु (peace) / लहहिं (they obtain) / लखनु (Lakshman) / अरु (and) / सीता (Sita)
ramacharitamanas::2657.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2657.essence: Ram heals distress by speaking what steadies the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2657.simple_meaning: Seeing Lakshman and Sita distressed, Ram begins speaking holy stories to soothe them. His words bring them peace.
ramacharitamanas::2657.simple_insight: Care sometimes looks like telling the right story at the right time.
ramacharitamanas::2657.detailed_meaning: In the forest exile, Ram lives with Sita and Lakshman in hardship. When he sees their condition, he responds not with grand speeches but with gentle, sacred words. The verse shows Ram's tenderness and the comfort his presence gives.
ramacharitamanas::2657.modern_relevance: Your partner is overwhelmed, your sibling is quiet, and you can feel the tension in the room. Instead of forcing solutions, you speak calmly and give them something steady to hold.
ramacharitamanas::2657.insight: It shifts care from fixing problems to offering calming presence.

ramacharitamanas::2658.verse_sanskrit: रामु लखन सीता सहित सोहत परन निकेत। जिमि बासव बस अमरपुर सची जयंत समेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::2658.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सहित श्री रामचन्द्रजी पर्णकुटी में ऐसे सुशोभित हैं, जैसे अमरावती में इन्द्र अपनी पत्नी शची और पुत्र जयंत सहित बसता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2658.english_translation: Ram, with Lakshman and Sita, looks splendid in the forest hut, like Indra in Amaravati with Shachi and Jayant.
ramacharitamanas::2658.translation_literal: रामु (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / सीता (Sita) / सहित (together with) / सोहत (looks beautiful) / परन निकेत (leaf hut) / जिमि (like) / बासव (Indra) / बस (dwelling) / अमरपुर (Amaravati, city of the radiant beings) / सची (Shachi) / जयंत (Jayant) / समेत (along with)
ramacharitamanas::2658.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2658.essence: True splendor can live inside a simple shelter.
ramacharitamanas::2658.simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman living in a forest hut are described as shining with the dignity of a royal household.
ramacharitamanas::2658.simple_insight: Even in exile, a life lived with love and right conduct can look radiant.
ramacharitamanas::2658.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's loss, Ram has already accepted the forest with Sita and Lakshman beside him. Tulsidas pauses to show that exile has not diminished their dignity; the hut itself has become as splendid as a heavenly palace.
ramacharitamanas::2658.modern_relevance: A family sharing a tiny rented room after a hard move can still feel rich if there is love, steadiness, and mutual care. Circumstance does not decide dignity.
ramacharitamanas::2658.insight: It shifts attention from outward comfort to the grace created by how people live together.

ramacharitamanas::2659.verse_sanskrit: जोगवहिं प्रभुसिय लखनहि कैसें। पलक बिलोचन गोलक जैसें॥ सेवहिं लखनु सीय रघुबीरहि। जिमि अबिबेकी पुरुष सरीरहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2659.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी की कैसी सँभाल रखते हैं, जैसे पलकें नेत्रों के गोलकों की। इधर लक्ष्मणजी श्री सीताजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी की (अथवा लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी की) ऐसी सेवा करते हैं, जैसे अज्ञानी मनुष्य शरीर की करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2659.english_translation: How does Lord Ram care for Sita and Lakshman? Like eyelids guard the eyes. Lakshman serves Sita and Raghuvir just as a careless person serves the body.
ramacharitamanas::2659.translation_literal: जोगवहिं (care for) / प्रभुसिय (Lord Ram and Sita) / लखनहि (Lakshman) / कैसें (how) / पलक (eyelids) / बिलोचन (eyes) / गोलक (eyeballs) / जैसें (like) / सेवहिं (serve) / लखनु (Lakshman) / सीय (Sita) / रघुबीरहि (Raghuvir) / जिमि (like) / अबिबेकी (unwise) / पुरुष (person) / सरीरहि (the body)
ramacharitamanas::2659.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2659.essence: True devotion protects gently and serves completely.
ramacharitamanas::2659.simple_meaning: Ram protects Sita and Lakshman with constant care, and Lakshman serves Ram and Sita with complete devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2659.simple_insight: Love becomes visible in how carefully you protect and serve.
ramacharitamanas::2659.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram, Sita, and Lakshman live close together in exile. The poet shows two kinds of love at once: Ram’s tender protection and Lakshman’s selfless service. Their bond is the heart of this quiet scene.
ramacharitamanas::2659.modern_relevance: You check on a tired sibling before you sleep, then stay up helping them anyway. Real love is both protection and service, given without complaint.
ramacharitamanas::2659.insight: It teaches you to measure love by care given and service offered, not by words alone.

ramacharitamanas::2660.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि प्रभु बन बसहिं सुखारी। खग मृग सुर तापस हितकारी॥ कहेउँ राम बन गवनु सुहावा। सुनहु सुमंत्र अवध जिमि आवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2660.verse_hindi: पक्षी, पशु, देवता और तपस्वियों के हितकारी प्रभु इस प्रकार सुखपूर्वक वन में निवास कर रहे हैं। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- मैंने श्री रामचन्द्रजी का सुंदर वनगमन कहा। अब जिस तरह सुमन्त्र अयोध्या में आए वह (कथा) सुनो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2660.english_translation: In this way, the Lord lived happily in the forest, bringing benefit to birds, animals, devas, and sages. Tulsidas says: I have told the lovely departure of Ram to the forest. Now listen to how Sumantra returned to Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::2660.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बन (forest) / बसहिं (lives) / सुखारी (happily) / खग (birds) / मृग (animals) / सुर (devas) / तापस (sages) / हितकारी (benefit-giving) / कहेउँ (I have told) / राम (Ram) / बन गवनु (forest-going) / सुहावा (lovely) / सुनहु (listen) / सुमंत्र (Sumantra) / अवध (Ayodhya) / जिमि (how) / आवा (came)
ramacharitamanas::2660.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2660.essence: Ram's exile still blesses every being around him.
ramacharitamanas::2660.simple_meaning: Ram lives in the forest in peace, and his presence benefits every kind of being there. The poet then turns the story toward Sumantra's return to Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::2660.simple_insight: A holy presence changes the whole atmosphere around it, even in exile.
ramacharitamanas::2660.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are settled in the forest, and the poet pauses to show that their exile is not barren. Birds, animals, devas, and sages all receive benefit from Ram's presence. This verse then shifts the story toward Sumantra's return to Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::2660.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room and people soften without knowing why. Some presence quiets the whole space, even when nothing outward has improved.
ramacharitamanas::2660.insight: It shifts attention from loss to the quiet blessing a righteous presence brings.

ramacharitamanas::2661.verse_sanskrit: फिरेउ निषादु प्रभुहि पहुँचाई। सचिव सहित रथ देखेसि आई॥ मंत्री बिकल बिलोकि निषादू। कहि न जाइ जस भयउ बिषादू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2661.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को पहुँचाकर जब निषादराज लौटा, तब आकर उसने रथ को मंत्री (सुमंत्र) सहित देखा। मंत्री को व्याकुल देखकर निषाद को जैसा दुःख हुआ, वह कहा नहीं जाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2661.english_translation: After escorting Lord Ram away, Nishad returned and saw the chariot with the minister. Seeing the minister distressed, the grief Nishad felt cannot be told.
ramacharitamanas::2661.translation_literal: फिरेउ (returned) / निषादु (Nishad) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / पहुँचाई (having escorted) / सचिव (minister) / सहित (along with) / रथ (chariot) / देखेसि (he saw) / आई (coming)॥ / मंत्री (minister) / बिकल (agitated) / बिलोकि (seeing) / निषादू (Nishad) / कहि न जाइ (cannot be said) / जस (how much) / भयउ (became) / बिषादू (grief) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2661.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2661.essence: Grief moves from one heart to another without a single word.
ramacharitamanas::2661.simple_meaning: Nishad returns after seeing Ram off and finds Sumantra in deep distress. That sight fills him with grief too, and the verse lingers on shared sorrow rather than teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2661.simple_insight: Someone else’s heartbreak can enter you before any words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2661.detailed_meaning: Nishad has just escorted Ram away and comes back to the camp. There he sees Sumantra with the chariot, visibly shaken. The verse pauses on the spread of grief between them, setting up the collapse that follows.
ramacharitamanas::2661.modern_relevance: You walk back into a room after dropping someone at the airport, and one face tells you everything went wrong. Grief passes silently before anyone explains it.
ramacharitamanas::2661.insight: It shows how sorrow is often recognized first through another person’s body and silence, not through speech.

ramacharitamanas::2662.verse_sanskrit: राम राम सिय लखन पुकारी। परेउ धरनितल ब्याकुल भारी॥ देखि दखिन दिसि हय हिहिनाहीं। जनु बिनु पंख बिहग अकुलाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2662.verse_hindi: (निषाद को अकेले आया देखकर) सुमंत्र हा राम! हा राम! हा सीते! हा लक्ष्मण! पुकारते हुए, बहुत व्याकुल होकर धरती पर गिर पड़े। (रथ के) घोड़े दक्षिण दिशा की ओर (जिधर श्री रामचन्द्रजी गए थे) देख-देखकर हिनहिनाते हैं। मानो बिना पंख के पक्षी व्याकुल हो रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::2662.english_translation: Sumantra cried out, "Ram! Ram! Sita! Lakshman!" and fell to the ground in great distress. Seeing toward the south, the horses neighed again and again, as if birds without wings were in anguish.
ramacharitamanas::2662.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / राम (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / लखन (Lakshman) / पुकारी (crying out) / परेउ (fell) / धरनितल (to the ground) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / भारी (greatly) / देखि (seeing) / दखिन दिसि (toward the south) / हय (horses) / हिहिनाहीं (neighed) / जनु (as if) / बिनु पंख (without wings) / बिहग (birds) / अकुलाहीं (were anguished)
ramacharitamanas::2662.speaker: Sumantra
ramacharitamanas::2662.essence: Absence can make the whole world ache.
ramacharitamanas::2662.simple_meaning: Sumantra breaks down in grief after Ram, Sita, and Lakshman leave. Even the horses seem to mourn their absence.
ramacharitamanas::2662.simple_insight: Separation can shake even the steady. Grief shows up in the body, not just the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2662.detailed_meaning: After helping Ram leave, Sumantra returns alone and is overwhelmed by loss. He cries the names of Ram, Sita, and Lakshman and collapses. The horses also turn toward the south, grieving the direction they departed.
ramacharitamanas::2662.modern_relevance: You come home after dropping someone at the airport, and the silence in the car feels physical. Even the smallest details keep turning toward the one who left.
ramacharitamanas::2662.insight: It turns grief into a shared scene, showing how absence can echo through people and even animals.

ramacharitamanas::2663.verse_sanskrit: नहिं तृन चरहिं न पिअहिं जलु मोचहिं लोचन बारि। ब्याकुल भए निषाद सब रघुबर बाजि निहारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2663.verse_hindi: वे न तो घास चरते हैं, न पानी पीते हैं। केवल आँखों से जल बहा रहे हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के घोड़ों को इस दशा में देखकर सब निषाद व्याकुल हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2663.english_translation: The horses neither graze nor drink water. They only pour tears from their eyes. Seeing Ram's horses in this state, all the Nishads were overcome with grief.
ramacharitamanas::2663.translation_literal: नहिं (not) / तृन (grass) / चरहिं (graze) / न (not) / पिअहिं (drink) / जलु (water) / मोचहिं (release) / लोचन (eyes) / बारि (water/tears) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / भए (became) / निषाद (Nishads) / सब (all) / रघुबर (Ram) / बाजि (horses) / निहारि (seeing)
ramacharitamanas::2663.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2663.essence: Even the horses are grieving Ram's absence.
ramacharitamanas::2663.simple_meaning: Ram's horses are so distressed by separation that they won't eat or drink. Even the Nishads feel that grief deeply when they see them.
ramacharitamanas::2663.simple_insight: Grief can be so real that even the creatures around you seem to share it.
ramacharitamanas::2663.detailed_meaning: After Ram has moved on, Nishadraj returns and sees Sumantra collapsed in sorrow. Now the focus shifts to Ram's horses, who refuse grass and water and seem to weep. Their condition deepens the whole scene of separation.
ramacharitamanas::2663.modern_relevance: You come home and your dog won't touch its food because the house feels wrong without someone it loved. Grief can live in the whole room, not just in you.
ramacharitamanas::2663.insight: It turns separation into a shared atmosphere, showing how loss affects everyone present, not only the most obvious mourner.

ramacharitamanas::2664.verse_sanskrit: धरि धीरजु तब कहइ निषादू। अब सुमंत्र परिहरहु बिषादू॥ तुम्ह पंडित परमारथ ग्याता। धरहु धीर लखि बिमुख बिधाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2664.verse_hindi: तब धीरज धरकर निषादराज कहने लगा- हे सुमंत्रजी! अब विषाद को छोड़िए। आप पंडित और परमार्थ के जानने वाले हैं। विधाता को प्रतिकूल जानकर धैर्य धारण कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2664.english_translation: Then, gathering courage, Nishad said to Sumantra: "Now let go of grief. You are learned and know the higher purpose. Hold steady, seeing that fate has turned against you."
ramacharitamanas::2664.translation_literal: धरि (having held) / धीरजु (courage, patience) / तब (then) / कहइ (said) / निषादू (Nishad) / अब (now) / सुमंत्र (Sumantra) / परिहरहु (give up, छोड़िए) / बिषादू (grief) / तुम्ह (you) / पंडित (learned) / परमारथ (higher purpose) / ग्याता (knower) / धरहु (hold) / धीर (steadiness) / लखि (seeing) / बिमुख (turned against) / बिधाता (fate, the ordainer)
ramacharitamanas::2664.speaker: Nishad
ramacharitamanas::2664.essence: Steadiness begins when you stop arguing with what has already turned.
ramacharitamanas::2664.simple_meaning: Nishad asks Sumantra to stop grieving and remain steady, since he understands higher purpose and can see that events have turned against them.
ramacharitamanas::2664.simple_insight: Sometimes strength is not fixing the loss, but refusing to collapse inside it.
ramacharitamanas::2664.detailed_meaning: At the edge of Ayodhya's pain, Nishad sees Sumantra broken by separation from Ram. He speaks gently, almost like a healer, reminding him that learning means more than knowledge: it means steadiness when life turns harsh.
ramacharitamanas::2664.modern_relevance: Your friend sits in the parked car after a family argument, staring at the steering wheel, unable to speak. You don't solve everything — you help them breathe, name what happened, and keep their footing.
ramacharitamanas::2664.insight: It shifts the mind from panic to composure, teaching you to meet reversal without losing dignity.

ramacharitamanas::2665.verse_sanskrit: बिबिधि कथा कहि कहि मृदु बानी। रथ बैठारेउ बरबस आनी॥ सोक सिथिल रथु सकइ न हाँकी। रघुबर बिरह पीर उर बाँकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2665.verse_hindi: कोमल वाणी से भाँति-भाँति की कथाएँ कहकर निषाद ने जबर्दस्ती लाकर सुमंत्र को रथ पर बैठाया, परन्तु शोक के मारे वे इतने शिथिल हो गए कि रथ को हाँक नहीं सकते। उनके हृदय में श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विरह की बड़ी तीव्र वेदना है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2665.english_translation: Nishad spoke gently and told many kinds of stories, then forced Sumantra onto the chariot. But Sumantra had become so weakened by grief that he could not drive the chariot; in his heart burned the sharp pain of separation from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2665.translation_literal: बिबिधि (various) / कथा (stories) / कहि कहि (speaking again and again) / मृदु (soft) / बानी (speech) / रथ (chariot) / बैठारेउ (made sit) / बरबस (by force) / आनी (bringing) / सोक (grief) / सिथिल (weakened) / रथु (chariot) / सकइ (able) / न (not) / हाँकी (to drive) / रघुबर (Ram) / बिरह (separation) / पीर (pain) / उर (heart) / बाँकी (sharp/bent)
ramacharitamanas::2665.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2665.essence: Grief can leave you unable to move, even when you must.
ramacharitamanas::2665.simple_meaning: Nishad gently speaks to Sumantra and seats him on the chariot, but grief has left him too weak to drive. His heart is pierced by separation from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2665.simple_insight: Love can hurt so deeply that even simple tasks become impossible.
