ramacharitamanas::2665.detailed_meaning: On the road after Ram’s exile, Nishad tries to steady Sumantra with gentle talk and physically seats him back on the chariot. But Sumantra is crushed by Ram’s absence, and that private grief is now stronger than his ability to act.
ramacharitamanas::2665.modern_relevance: You sit in the car after dropping someone at the airport, hands still on the wheel, unable to start the engine. The silence is heavier than the road ahead.
ramacharitamanas::2665.insight: It shows how separation can drain the body, not just the mind.

ramacharitamanas::2666.verse_sanskrit: चरफराहिं मग चलहिं न घोरे। बन मृग मनहुँ आनि रथ जोरे॥ अढ़ुकि परहिं फिरि हेरहिं पीछें। राम बियोगि बिकल दुख तीछें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2666.verse_hindi: घोड़े तड़फड़ाते हैं और (ठीक) रास्ते पर नहीं चलते। मानो जंगली पशु लाकर रथ में जोत दिए गए हों। वे श्री रामचन्द्रजी के वियोगी घोड़े कभी ठोकर खाकर गिर पड़ते हैं, कभी घूमकर पीछे की ओर देखने लगते हैं। वे तीक्ष्ण दुःख से व्याकुल हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2666.english_translation: The horses stumble off the road and do not go straight. It is as if wild animals were yoked to the chariot. They trip, fall, turn back to look behind, and burn with sharp pain at Ram’s separation.
ramacharitamanas::2666.translation_literal: चरफराहिं (stumble about) / मग (road) / चलहिं (they move) / न (not) / घोरे (horses) / बन (forest-wild) / मृग (animals) / मनहुँ (as if) / आनि (bringing) / रथ (chariot) / जोरे (yoked) / अढ़ुकि (stumbling) / परहिं (they fall) / फिरि (again) / हेरहिं (they look) / पीछें (behind) / राम (Ram) / बियोगि (separated from) / बिकल (distressed) / दुख (pain) / तीछें (sharp)
ramacharitamanas::2666.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2666.essence: Separation makes even the steady lose their way.
ramacharitamanas::2666.simple_meaning: The horses are so grief-stricken by Ram’s absence that they cannot even walk properly. They stumble, fall, and keep looking back.
ramacharitamanas::2666.simple_insight: Even the horses feel the ache of separation; grief can unsettle the whole world around you.
ramacharitamanas::2666.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has been forced to carry Ram away from Ayodhya, and even the horses drawing the chariot cannot bear the separation. They lose the road, stumble, and keep looking back, showing how deeply Ram’s absence has shaken the scene.
ramacharitamanas::2666.modern_relevance: You start driving home after a goodbye that has cracked something open inside you. Your hands stay on the wheel, but your mind keeps turning back to the person you left behind.
ramacharitamanas::2666.insight: It turns grief into a physical force, showing how separation can disrupt even ordinary movement.

ramacharitamanas::2667.verse_sanskrit: जो कह रामु लखनु बैदेही। हिंकरि हिंकरि हित हेरहिं तेही॥ बाजि बिरह गति कहि किमि जाती। बिनु मनि फनिक बिकल जेहिं भाँती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2667.verse_hindi: जो कोई राम, लक्ष्मण या जानकी का नाम ले लेता है, घोड़े हिकर-हिकरकर उसकी ओर प्यार से देखने लगते हैं। घोड़ों की विरह दशा कैसे कही जा सकती है? वे ऐसे व्याकुल हैं, जैसे मणि के बिना साँप व्याकुल होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2667.english_translation: Anyone who says Ram, Lakshman, or Sita's name makes the horses whinny and look lovingly that way. How can the horses' longing be described? They are as distressed as a snake without its jewel.
ramacharitamanas::2667.translation_literal: जो (who) / कह (says) / रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / बैदेही (Sita) / हिंकरि हिंकरि (whinnying softly) / हित (with affection) / हेरहिं (look) / तेही (that way)॥ / बाजि (horses) / बिरह (separation) / गति (state) / कहि (speak) / किमि (how) / जाती (can be said) / बिनु (without) / मनि (jewel) / फनिक (snake) / बिकल (distressed) / जेहिं (in which) / भाँती (way) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2667.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2667.essence: Longing can make even the body answer a beloved name.
ramacharitamanas::2667.simple_meaning: The horses are so overcome by separation from Ram, Lakshman, and Sita that even hearing their names makes them turn and whinny with longing.
ramacharitamanas::2667.simple_insight: Love can leave even animals restless when they sense what they miss.
ramacharitamanas::2667.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has been forced back toward Ayodhya, but the chariot horses cannot bear the separation. In the middle of Bharat's grief, even they respond to the names of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita with visible longing. The scene deepens the ache of exile.
ramacharitamanas::2667.modern_relevance: You hear a song tied to someone you lost, and your chest tightens before you can think. Memory can pull the body toward what the heart still misses.
ramacharitamanas::2667.insight: It turns a passing scene into proof that separation is felt physically, not just mentally.

ramacharitamanas::2668.verse_sanskrit: भयउ निषादु बिषादबस देखत सचिव तुरंग। बोलि सुसेवक चारि तब दिए सारथी संग ॥
ramacharitamanas::2668.verse_hindi: मंत्री और घोड़ों की यह दशा देखकर निषादराज विषाद के वश हो गया। तब उसने अपने चार उत्तम सेवक बुलाकर सारथी के साथ कर दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2668.english_translation: Seeing his minister and the horses in such a state, Nishadraj was overcome with sorrow. Then he called four of his best servants and sent them along with the charioteer.
ramacharitamanas::2668.translation_literal: भयउ (became) / निषादु (Nishadraj) / बिषादबस (under the grip of sorrow) / देखत (seeing) / सचिव (minister) / तुरंग (horses) / बोलि (calling) / सुसेवक (good servants) / चारि (four) / तब (then) / दिए (gave/sent) / सारथी (charioteer) / संग (with)
ramacharitamanas::2668.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2668.essence: Compassion becomes real when grief turns into help.
ramacharitamanas::2668.simple_meaning: Seeing the grief around him, Nishadraj is moved to sorrow and sends four trusted servants with the charioteer.
ramacharitamanas::2668.simple_insight: Some moments of care are shown not in words, but in immediate help.
ramacharitamanas::2668.detailed_meaning: Guh watches Sumantra and the horses leave Ayodhya in deep distress after Ram's exile. Their pain moves him at once, and he arranges for four trusted servants to accompany the charioteer. It is a small act of care in a scene of shared heartbreak.
ramacharitamanas::2668.modern_relevance: You see a friend leaving in tears, and without asking for thanks you quietly arrange the ride, the bag, the help they need. Grief often reveals who will act first.
ramacharitamanas::2668.insight: It shifts attention from feeling sympathy to offering practical support immediately.

ramacharitamanas::2669.verse_sanskrit: गुह सारथिहि फिरेउ पहुँचाई। बिरहु बिषादु बरनि नहिं जाई॥ चले अवध लेइ रथहि निषादा। होहिं छनहिं छन मगन बिषादा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2669.verse_hindi: निषादराज गुह सारथी (सुमंत्रजी) को पहुँचाकर (विदा करके) लौटा। उसके विरह और दुःख का वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। वे चारों निषाद रथ लेकर अवध को चले। (सुमंत्र और घोड़ों को देख-देखकर) वे भी क्षण-क्षणभर विषाद में डूबे जाते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2669.english_translation: Guh returned after seeing Sumantra off. His grief and sorrow cannot be described. The four Nishadas took the chariot toward Ayodhya, and every moment they sank again into sadness.
ramacharitamanas::2669.translation_literal: गुह (Guh) / सारथिहि (the charioteer) / फिरेउ (returned) / पहुँचाई (after escorting) / बिरहु (separation) / बिषादु (sorrow) / बरनि (described) / नहिं जाई (cannot be) / चले (went) / अवध (to Ayodhya) / लेइ (taking) / रथहि (the chariot) / निषादा (the Nishadas) / होहिं (become) / छनहिं छन (every moment) / मगन (immersed) / बिषादा (in sorrow)
ramacharitamanas::2669.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2669.essence: Separation changes the ones who help carry it.
ramacharitamanas::2669.simple_meaning: Guh sends Sumantra on his way and returns in grief. The Nishadas take the chariot toward Ayodhya, but their hearts keep sinking into sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2669.simple_insight: When love is real, even a simple goodbye can leave everyone changed.
ramacharitamanas::2669.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's exile aftermath, Guh has just escorted Sumantra away after helping Ram, Lakshman, and Sita's journey continue. The four Nishadas now carry the chariot back, but the separation has filled them with grief that words cannot hold.
ramacharitamanas::2669.modern_relevance: You walk back from the station after dropping off someone you cared for deeply. The road home is the same, but every step feels heavier because the leaving has changed you.
ramacharitamanas::2669.insight: It shows how separation can linger in the body long after the farewell is over.

ramacharitamanas::2670.verse_sanskrit: सोच सुमंत्र बिकल दुख दीना। धिग जीवन रघुबीर बिहीना॥ रहिहि न अंतहुँ अधम सरीरू। जसु न लहेउ बिछुरत रघुबीरू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2670.verse_hindi: व्याकुल और दुःख से दीन हुए सुमंत्रजी सोचते हैं कि श्री रघुवीर के बिना जीना धिक्कार है। आखिर यह अधम शरीर रहेगा तो है ही नहीं। अभी श्री रामचन्द्रजी के बिछुड़ते ही छूटकर इसने यश (क्यों) नहीं ले लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2670.english_translation: Sumantra, overwhelmed by sorrow, thinks life without Raghuvir is unbearable. This worthless body will not even last to the end; why did it not lose its fame the moment it was separated from Ram?
ramacharitamanas::2670.translation_literal: सोच (thinking) / सुमंत्र (Sumantra) / बिकल (agitated) / दुख (sorrow) / दीना (dejected) / धिग (shame on) / जीवन (life) / रघुबीर (Raghuvir) / बिहीना (without)॥ / रहिहि (will remain) / न (not) / अंतहुँ (even to the end) / अधम (wretched) / सरीरू (body) / जसु (fame) / न (not) / लहेउ (obtained) / बिछुरत (separated) / रघुबीरू (from Raghuvir) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2670.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2670.essence: Without Ram, even life feels like a burden.
ramacharitamanas::2670.simple_meaning: Sumantra is crushed by grief after Ram leaves. He feels life without Ram is unbearable and even this body feels worthless without that closeness.
ramacharitamanas::2670.simple_insight: Separation can make even survival feel empty.
ramacharitamanas::2670.detailed_meaning: After carrying Ram away from Ayodhya, Sumantra is left broken on the road back. The grief is no longer private; it has entered his body and thoughts. He mourns not just Ram’s absence, but the collapse of meaning itself.
ramacharitamanas::2670.modern_relevance: You drop someone at the airport and drive home in silence, replaying the last goodbye. The house is still yours, but it feels strangely uninhabited.
ramacharitamanas::2670.insight: It names grief as a total loss of meaning, not just sadness. The mind begins to question whether life itself still has purpose.

ramacharitamanas::2671.verse_sanskrit: भए अजस अघ भाजन प्राना। कवन हेतु नहिं करत पयाना॥ अहह मंद मनु अवसर चूका। अजहुँ न हृदय होत दुइ टूका ॥
ramacharitamanas::2671.verse_hindi: ये प्राण अपयश और पाप के भाँडे हो गए। अब ये किस कारण कूच नहीं करते (निकलते नहीं)? हाय! नीच मन (बड़ा अच्छा) मौका चूक गया। अब भी तो हृदय के दो टुकड़े नहीं हो जाते! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2671.english_translation: These breaths have become vessels of disgrace and wrongdoing. Why do they not depart now? Alas, the foolish mind has missed the moment. Why is the heart not split in two even now?
ramacharitamanas::2671.translation_literal: भए (became) / अजस (disgrace) / अघ (wrongdoing) / भाजन (vessels) / प्राना (breaths) । / कवन (which) / हेतु (reason) / नहिं (not) / करत (doing) / पयाना (departure) ॥ / अहह (alas) / मंद (foolish) / मनु (mind) / अवसर (opportunity) / चूका (missed) ॥ / अजहुँ (still now) / न (not) / हृदय (heart) / होत (becoming) / दुइ (two) / टूका (pieces) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2671.speaker: Sumantra
ramacharitamanas::2671.essence: Missing the right moment can make life feel stained beyond repair.
ramacharitamanas::2671.simple_meaning: Sumantra is overwhelmed with regret. He feels his life has become stained by shame, and he laments that he missed the chance to act at the right moment.
ramacharitamanas::2671.simple_insight: Missed chances can feel unbearable when you realize they mattered most.
ramacharitamanas::2671.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has returned after taking Ram, Sita, and Lakshman toward exile. Left behind in Ayodhya, he is crushed by regret. He feels his life has been ruined by this failure and cannot bear that he missed the decisive moment.
ramacharitamanas::2671.modern_relevance: You replay the moment after the text was sent, the meeting ended, the chance passed. What hurts most is not the loss itself, but knowing you were there and still missed it.
ramacharitamanas::2671.insight: It captures the grief of failed timing and the self-blame that follows a missed duty.

ramacharitamanas::2672.verse_sanskrit: मीजि हाथ सिरु धुनि पछिताई। मनहुँ कृपन धन रासि गवाँई॥ बिरिद बाँधि बर बीरु कहाई। चलेउ समर जनु सुभट पराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2672.verse_hindi: सुमंत्र हाथ मल-मलकर और सिर पीट-पीटकर पछताते हैं। मानो कोई कंजूस धन का खजाना खो बैठा हो। वे इस प्रकार चले मानो कोई बड़ा योद्धा वीर का बाना पहनकर और उत्तम शूरवीर कहलाकर युद्ध से भाग चला हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2672.english_translation: Sumantra wrings his hands and beats his head in regret, as if a miser had lost a treasure of wealth. Bound by duty and called a brave man, he went on like a great warrior who flees the battle.
ramacharitamanas::2672.translation_literal: मीजि (rubbing) / हाथ (hands) / सिरु (head) / धुनि (beating) / पछिताई (regretting) / मनहुँ (as if) / कृपन (miser) / धन (wealth) / रासि (heap, treasure) / गवाँई (lost) / बिरिद (pledge, reputation) / बाँधि (binding) / बर (great) / बीरु (warrior) / कहाई (called) / चलेउ (went) / समर (battle) / जनु (as if) / सुभट (heroic warrior) / पराई (fled)
ramacharitamanas::2672.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2672.essence: Missed duty turns courage into bitter shame.
ramacharitamanas::2672.simple_meaning: Sumantra is overwhelmed with regret. He feels as if he has lost something precious and has failed the honour of a great warrior.
ramacharitamanas::2672.simple_insight: Regret can feel like losing a whole treasure after the moment has already passed.
ramacharitamanas::2672.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has just watched Ram leave for exile and knows he has failed to stop it. He is not teaching anything here; he is collapsing under shame, grief, and helplessness. The verse stays inside that broken moment.
ramacharitamanas::2672.modern_relevance: You replay the conversation on the drive home and realise the chance is gone. The apology, the warning, the brave sentence you should have said — all of it arrives too late.
ramacharitamanas::2672.insight: It captures the pain of recognising missed responsibility after the decisive moment has passed.

ramacharitamanas::2673.verse_sanskrit: बिप्र बिबेकी बेदबिद संमत साधु सुजाति। जिमि धोखें मदपान कर सचिव सोच तेहि भाँति ॥
ramacharitamanas::2673.verse_hindi: जैसे कोई विवेकशील, वेद का ज्ञाता, साधुसम्मत आचरणों वाला और उत्तम जाति का (कुलीन) ब्राह्मण धोखे से मदिरा पी ले और पीछे पछतावे, उसी प्रकार मंत्री सुमंत्र सोच कर रहे (पछता रहे) हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2673.english_translation: Like a discerning Brahmin, learned in the Vedas, praised by the good, and of noble conduct, who is tricked into drinking liquor and then regrets it, so Sumantra is filled with sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2673.translation_literal: बिप्र (Brahmin) / बिबेकी (discerning) / बेदबिद (knower of the Vedas) / संमत (approved) / साधु (by the good) / सुजाति (of noble birth) / जिमि (like) / धोखें (by deception) / मदपान (drinking liquor) / कर (having done) / सचिव (minister) / सोच (sorrow) / तेहि भाँति (in that manner)
ramacharitamanas::2673.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2673.essence: Deep regret can feel like moral contamination after a helpless mistake.
ramacharitamanas::2673.simple_meaning: Sumantra’s grief is compared to the shame of a good, wise man who has been tricked into drinking alcohol and then feels deep regret.
ramacharitamanas::2673.simple_insight: Some sorrow is not just pain — it is the sting of having been made helpless by circumstances.
ramacharitamanas::2673.detailed_meaning: After Ram leaves for exile, Sumantra returns in anguish, ashamed that he could not stop the disaster. Tulsidas compares his regret to a respected, wise Brahmin who is deceived into drinking and then feels unbearable shame.
ramacharitamanas::2673.modern_relevance: You replay the conversation after the damage is done, wondering how you missed the warning signs. The pain is not only loss — it is the humiliation of realizing you were powerless to prevent it.
ramacharitamanas::2673.insight: It frames grief as shame mixed with helplessness, not just sadness.

ramacharitamanas::2674.verse_sanskrit: जिमि कुलीन तिय साधु सयानी। पतिदेवता करम मन बानी॥ रहै करम बस परिहरि नाहू। सचिव हृदयँ तिमि दारुन दाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2674.verse_hindi: जैसे किसी उत्तम कुलवाली, साधु स्वाभाव की, समझदार और मन, वचन, कर्म से पति को ही देवता मानने वाली पतिव्रता स्त्री को भाग्यवश पति को छोड़कर (पति से अलग) रहना पड़े, उस समय उसके हृदय में जैसे भयानक संताप होता है, वैसे ही मंत्री के हृदय में हो रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2674.english_translation: Like a noble, virtuous, wise wife who holds her husband as her only deity, yet must live apart from him by fate, the minister's heart burns with the same terrible pain.
ramacharitamanas::2674.translation_literal: जिमि (like) / कुलीन (noble-born) / तिय (woman, wife) / साधु (virtuous) / सयानी (wise) / पतिदेवता (husband as deity) / करम (by fate, by deed) / मन (mind) / बानी (speech) / रहै (remains) / करम बस (under the control of fate) / परिहरि (leaving aside) / नाहू (husband) / सचिव (minister) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / तिमि (thus, in that way) / दारुन (terrible) / दाहू (burning pain)
ramacharitamanas::2674.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2674.essence: Separation from what you love can burn like fire inside the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2674.simple_meaning: The minister's grief is compared to a devoted wife forced to live away from her husband. It is a pain of separation, not just sadness.
ramacharitamanas::2674.simple_insight: Some losses feel like a wound in the heart, not just a change in circumstance.
ramacharitamanas::2674.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has been forced to return after Ram's exile, and the separation is tearing him apart. Tulsidas compares his pain to a devoted wife who must live away from her husband against her will, showing how deep and helpless his grief is.
ramacharitamanas::2674.modern_relevance: You drop someone at the airport after a life-changing goodbye, then sit in the car unable to start it. The distance is physical, but the ache feels lodged in your chest.
ramacharitamanas::2674.insight: It turns separation into a bodily grief, making emotional loss feel real and unavoidable.

ramacharitamanas::2675.verse_sanskrit: लोचन सजल डीठि भइ थोरी। सुनइ न श्रवन बिकल मति भोरी॥ सूखहिं अधर लागि मुहँ लाटी। जिउ न जाइ उर अवधि कपाटी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2675.verse_hindi: नेत्रों में जल भरा है, दृष्टि मंद हो गई है। कानों से सुनाई नहीं पड़ता, व्याकुल हुई बुद्धि बेठिकाने हो रही है। होठ सूख रहे हैं, मुँह में लाटी लग गई है, किन्तु (ये सब मृत्यु के लक्षण हो जाने पर भी) प्राण नहीं निकलते, क्योंकि हृदय में अवधि रूपी किवाड़ लगे हैं (अर्थात चौदह वर्ष बीत जाने पर भगवान फिर मिलेंगे, यही आशा रुकावट डाल रही है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2675.english_translation: Tears fill the eyes and the gaze grows dim. Hearing fails, the mind grows unsteady and confused. The lips dry up and the mouth goes slack, yet life does not leave the body, because the doors of the heart are held shut by the hope that fourteen years will pass and Ram will return.
ramacharitamanas::2675.translation_literal: लोचन (eyes) / सजल (filled with water) / डीठि (sight) / भइ (became) / थोरी (dim) । / सुनइ (hears) / न (not) / श्रवन (ears) / बिकल (disturbed) / मति (mind) / भोरी (confused) ॥ / सूखहिं (dry up) / अधर (lips) / लागि (having been applied) / मुहँ (mouth) / लाटी (slack, lifeless) । / जिउ (life) / न (not) / जाइ (goes) / उर (heart) / अवधि (the fixed term) / कपाटी (doors, shutters) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2675.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2675.essence: Hope can keep the heart closed against surrender.
ramacharitamanas::2675.simple_meaning: Sumantra is so overwhelmed by grief that his body shows signs of death, yet he cannot die because he still hopes to see Ram after the exile ends.
ramacharitamanas::2675.simple_insight: Grief can be so deep that only hope keeps you alive.
ramacharitamanas::2675.detailed_meaning: After Ram leaves for exile, Sumantra is left shattered. His eyes fill with tears, his hearing and mind fail, and his body weakens as if death has begun. But he cannot let go, because he is still clinging to the hope that Ram will return after fourteen years.
ramacharitamanas::2675.modern_relevance: You sit in a hospital corridor at 3 a.m., staring at a phone that still hasn’t rung. Your body feels spent, but one small hope keeps you from collapsing completely.
ramacharitamanas::2675.insight: It shows how longing can suspend collapse, keeping a person alive through sheer expectation.

ramacharitamanas::2676.verse_sanskrit: बिबरन भयउ न जाइ निहारी। मारेसि मनहुँ पिता महतारी॥ हानि गलानि बिपुल मन ब्यापी। जमपुर पंथ सोच जिमि पापी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2676.verse_hindi: सुमंत्रजी के मुख का रंग बदल गया है, जो देखा नहीं जाता। ऐसा मालूम होता है मानो इन्होंने माता-पिता को मार डाला हो। उनके मन में रामवियोग रूपी हानि की महान ग्लानि (पीड़ा) छा रही है, जैसे कोई पापी मनुष्य नरक को जाता हुआ रास्ते में सोच कर रहा हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2676.english_translation: Sumantra's face changed so much it could not be looked at. It was as if he had killed his own parents. A deep sense of loss and shame filled his mind, like a sinner walking toward the lower realm and thinking of his fate.
ramacharitamanas::2676.translation_literal: बिबरन (face turned pale/changed) / भयउ (became) / न जाइ (cannot be) / निहारी (to look at) / मारेसि (as if killed) / मनहुँ (as if) / पिता (father) / महतारी (mother) / हानि (loss) / गलानि (shame/grief) / बिपुल (great) / मन (mind) / ब्यापी (spread through) / जमपुर (lower realm) / पंथ (path) / सोच (thought) / जिमि (like) / पापी (sinner)
ramacharitamanas::2676.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2676.essence: Loyalty can hurt so deeply it feels like guilt.
ramacharitamanas::2676.simple_meaning: Sumantra is overwhelmed with grief and shame after leaving Ram behind. His face looks unrecognisable, as if he has committed the worst possible act.
ramacharitamanas::2676.simple_insight: Separation can make even a loyal heart feel guilty, as if love itself has failed.
ramacharitamanas::2676.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has returned from leaving Ram in exile, and the pain has broken him. His face has changed so much that people can hardly bear to look at him. The verse dwells on his crushing grief before he even speaks.
ramacharitamanas::2676.modern_relevance: You come home after dropping someone at the airport and sit in the car for ten minutes, unable to start the engine. The silence feels like you failed them, even though you did everything you could.
ramacharitamanas::2676.insight: It shows how love can turn into self-reproach when duty forces separation.

ramacharitamanas::2677.verse_sanskrit: बचनु न आव हृदयँ पछिताई। अवध काह मैं देखब जाई॥ राम रहित रथ देखिहि जोई। सकुचिहि मोहि बिलोकत सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2677.verse_hindi: मुँह से वचन नहीं निकलते। हृदय में पछताते हैं कि मैं अयोध्या में जाकर क्या देखूँगा? श्री रामचन्द्रजी से शून्य रथ को जो भी देखेगा, वही मुझे देखने में संकोच करेगा (अर्थात मेरा मुँह नहीं देखना चाहेगा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2677.english_translation: No words come to his mouth; his heart is full of regret: what will I see if I go to Ayodhya? Whoever sees the chariot without Ram will shrink back from looking at me.
ramacharitamanas::2677.translation_literal: बचनु (word/speech) / न (not) / आव (comes) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / पछिताई (regret) / अवध (Ayodhya) / काह (what) / मैं (I) / देखब (will see) / जाई (going)॥ / राम (Ram) / रहित (without) / रथ (chariot) / देखिहि (will see) / जोई (whoever) / सकुचिहि (will shrink back) / मोहि (me) / बिलोकत (seeing) / सोई (that one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2677.speaker: Sumantra
ramacharitamanas::2677.essence: Grief can make you feel unworthy to face the people you love.
ramacharitamanas::2677.simple_meaning: Sumantra is overwhelmed with shame and grief. He feels he cannot return to Ayodhya or face anyone there after bringing back a chariot without Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2677.simple_insight: Some losses make even speaking feel impossible.
ramacharitamanas::2677.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has returned from the forest with only the chariot, not Ram. As he nears Ayodhya, shame and sorrow crush him. He imagines the citizens' faces and feels he cannot bear their eyes or questions.
ramacharitamanas::2677.modern_relevance: You come home after failing to protect someone who trusted you, and the silence in the car feels heavier than any explanation. That is Sumantra's pain.
ramacharitamanas::2677.insight: It shows how grief can make you fear the very people who care about you most.

ramacharitamanas::2678.verse_sanskrit: धाइ पूँछिहहिं मोहि जब बिकल नगर नर नारि। उतरु देब मैं सबहि तब हृदयँ बज्रु बैठारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2678.verse_hindi: नगर के सब व्याकुल स्त्री-पुरुष जब दौड़कर मुझसे पूछेंगे, तब मैं हृदय पर वज्र रखकर सबको उत्तर दूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2678.english_translation: When the anxious men and women of the city rush to ask me, I will answer them with a heart like steel.
ramacharitamanas::2678.translation_literal: धाइ (rushing) / पूँछिहहिं (will ask) / मोहि (me) / जब (when) / बिकल (distressed) / नगर (city) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / उतरु (answer) / देब (will give) / मैं (I) / सबहि (to everyone) / तब (then) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बज्रु (thunderbolt) / बैठारि (placing)
ramacharitamanas::2678.speaker: Sumantra
ramacharitamanas::2678.essence: A heavy heart still has to speak clearly.
ramacharitamanas::2678.simple_meaning: Sumantra knows the people of Ayodhya will ask him what happened. He steels himself to answer their painful questions.
ramacharitamanas::2678.simple_insight: Some truths hurt to say, but courage means carrying them for others.
ramacharitamanas::2678.detailed_meaning: Sumantra returns toward Ayodhya after taking Ram away. He can already imagine the city grieving and crowding around him for answers. This verse captures the moment before he must speak the unbearable truth.
ramacharitamanas::2678.modern_relevance: You walk into a house after bad news has spread, and everyone turns to you first. You know the questions are coming, and you brace yourself to answer with care.
ramacharitamanas::2678.insight: It teaches you to face painful responsibility directly instead of avoiding the people who need the truth.

ramacharitamanas::2679.verse_sanskrit: पुछिहहिं दीन दुखित सब माता। कहब काह मैं तिन्हहि बिधाता। पूछिहि जबहिं लखन महतारी। कहिहउँ कवन सँदेस सुखारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2679.verse_hindi: जब दीन-दुःखी सब माताएँ पूछेंगी, तब हे विधाता! मैं उन्हें क्या कहूँगा? जब लक्ष्मणजी की माता मुझसे पूछेंगी, तब मैं उन्हें कौन सा सुखदायी सँदेसा कहूँगा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2679.english_translation: When all the grieving mothers ask me, what can I tell them, O Creator? When Lakshman's mother asks me, what comforting message can I give her?
ramacharitamanas::2679.translation_literal: पुछिहहिं (will ask) / दीन (poor, helpless) / दुखित (grieving) / सब (all) / माता (mothers) / कहब (what will I say) / काह (what) / मैं (I) / तिन्हहि (to them) / बिधाता (O Creator) / पूछिहि (will ask) / जबहिं (when) / लखन (Lakshman) / महतारी (mother) / कहिहउँ (what will I say) / कवन (which) / सँदेस (message) / सुखारी (comforting)
ramacharitamanas::2679.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2679.essence: Some news is so painful that silence feels kinder than speech.
ramacharitamanas::2679.simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed by grief. He imagines the mothers in Ayodhya asking about Ram and Lakshman, and he cannot think of any answer that would not break their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::2679.simple_insight: Grief can make even simple questions unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2679.detailed_meaning: Bharat is returning toward Ayodhya after Ram's exile, already crushed by the thought of what he must face. He imagines the city’s mothers asking about their sons, especially Lakshman's mother, and feels unable to offer any words that would soften the pain.
ramacharitamanas::2679.modern_relevance: You rehearse the conversation in the car before walking into the house, knowing a mother is waiting for news you cannot make gentle.
ramacharitamanas::2679.insight: It shows how love makes you measure every word against another person's pain.

ramacharitamanas::2680.verse_sanskrit: राम जननि जब आइहि धाई। सुमिरि बच्छु जिमि धेनु लवाई॥ पूँछत उतरु देब मैं तेही। गे बनु राम लखनु बैदेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2680.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी की माता जब इस प्रकार दौड़ी आवेंगी जैसे नई ब्यायी हुई गौ बछड़े को याद करके दौड़ी आती है, तब उनके पूछने पर मैं उन्हें यह उत्तर दूँगा कि श्री राम, लक्ष्मण, सीता वन को चले गए! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2680.english_translation: When Ram's mother comes running, remembering her calf like a cow that has just given birth, I will answer her: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita have gone to the forest.
ramacharitamanas::2680.translation_literal: राम जननि (Ram's mother) / जब (when) / आइहि (will come) / धाई (running) / सुमिरि (remembering) / बच्छु (calf) / जिमि (like) / धेनु (cow) / लवाई (that has given birth) // पूँछत (asking) / उतरु (answer) / देब (will give) / मैं (I) / तेही (to her) / गे (went) / बनु (to the forest) / राम (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / बैदेही (Sita)
ramacharitamanas::2680.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2680.essence: Honesty can demand the courage to wound someone you love.
ramacharitamanas::2680.simple_meaning: Bharat knows Ram's mother will rush to ask where her sons have gone. He prepares himself to answer honestly, even though the truth will be unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2680.simple_insight: Some truths cannot be softened. Love sometimes means carrying the pain of honesty.
ramacharitamanas::2680.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands in the wreckage of exile, already imagining the questions that will come from the women of Ayodhya. He sees Ram's mother rushing like a cow searching for her calf and steels himself to tell her the unbearable truth.
ramacharitamanas::2680.modern_relevance: You rehearse the phone call before you make it, knowing the other person will ask where they are. The truth is simple, but saying it cleanly takes everything you have.
ramacharitamanas::2680.insight: It trains you to face painful conversation without hiding behind delay, excuses, or half-truths.

ramacharitamanas::2681.verse_sanskrit: जोई पूँछिहि तेहि ऊतरु देबा। जाइ अवध अब यहु सुखु लेबा॥ पूँछिहि जबहिं राउ दुख दीना। जिवनु जासु रघुनाथ अधीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2681.verse_hindi: जो भी पूछेगा उसे यही उत्तर देना पड़ेगा! हाय! अयोध्या जाकर अब मुझे यही सुख लेना है! जब दुःख से दीन महाराज, जिनका जीवन श्री रघुनाथजी के (दर्शन के) ही अधीन है, मुझसे पूछेंगे, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2681.english_translation: Whoever asks, I will have to give the same answer. Alas, after reaching Ayodhya, I must take this sorrow as my only comfort. When grief-stricken King Dasharath asks me, whose life depends on Raghunath, ...
ramacharitamanas::2681.translation_literal: जोई (whoever) / पूँछिहि (will ask) / तेहि (to that one) / ऊतरु (answer) / देबा (to give) / जाइ (going) / अवध (Ayodhya) / अब (now) / यहु (this) / सुखु (comfort) / लेबा (to take) / पूँछिहि (will ask) / जबहिं (when) / राउ (king) / दुख दीना (grief-stricken) / जिवनु (life) / जासु (whose) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / अधीना (dependent)
ramacharitamanas::2681.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2681.essence: Some answers are unavoidable, even when they reopen grief.
ramacharitamanas::2681.simple_meaning: He knows he will have to answer everyone in Ayodhya, especially Dasharath, and that the answer will bring only pain.
ramacharitamanas::2681.simple_insight: Some returns carry no joy, only the weight of what was lost.
ramacharitamanas::2681.detailed_meaning: After leaving Ram, Lakshman, and Sita behind, the messenger is already imagining the questions waiting in Ayodhya. Dasharath, broken with grief and living only for Ram, will ask for news. The verse sits in a chain of dread, not a complete teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2681.modern_relevance: You rehearse the conversation on the drive home, knowing someone will ask the question you cannot soften. The answer is true, but it will hurt the one who hears it.
ramacharitamanas::2681.insight: It frames the return not as relief, but as the burden of reporting unbearable news.

ramacharitamanas::2682.verse_sanskrit: देहउँ उतरु कौनु मुहु लाई। आयउँ कुसल कुअँर पहुँचाई॥ सुनत लखन सिय राम सँदेसू। तृन जिमि तनु परिहरिहि नरेसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2682.verse_hindi: तब मैं कौन सा मुँह लेकर उन्हें उत्तर दूँगा कि मैं राजकुमारों को कुशल पूर्वक पहुँचा आया हूँ! लक्ष्मण, सीता और श्रीराम का समाचार सुनते ही महाराज तिनके की तरह शरीर को त्याग देंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2682.english_translation: Then what face would I have to answer with, saying I have safely brought the princes here? Hearing news of Lakshman, Sita, and Ram, the king will leave his body like a blade of grass.
ramacharitamanas::2682.translation_literal: देहउँ (would give) / उतरु (answer) / कौनु (which) / मुहु (face) / लाई (bringing) / आयउँ (I came) / कुसल (safely, well) / कुअँर (princes) / पहुँचाई (having brought and delivered) / सुनत (on hearing) / लखन (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / सँदेसू (message, news) / तृन (grass blade) / जिमि (like) / तनु (body) / परिहरिहि (will cast off) / नरेसू (king)
ramacharitamanas::2682.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2682.essence: Grief can be so deep that even good news becomes unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2682.simple_meaning: The speaker fears that reporting the safe return of Ram, Sita, and Lakshman will overwhelm the king with grief and make him give up his body.
ramacharitamanas::2682.simple_insight: Sometimes even good news can feel unbearable when love is already wounded.
ramacharitamanas::2682.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the returning messenger stands before a court already trembling with loss. He has brought word that Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are safe, but he knows Dasharath's heart is so broken that even this news may finish him.
ramacharitamanas::2682.modern_relevance: You finally call with the update everyone prayed for, but the person on the other end has already been shattered by waiting. Even relief can land like a blow.
ramacharitamanas::2682.insight: It shows how grief can make even joy feel dangerous, and how love can exhaust the body before the mind can recover.

ramacharitamanas::2683.verse_sanskrit: हृदउ न बिदरेउ पंक जिमि बिछुरत प्रीतमु नीरु। जानत हौं मोहि दीन्ह बिधि यहु जातना सरीरु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2683.verse_hindi: प्रियतम (श्री रामजी) रूपी जल के बिछुड़ते ही मेरा हृदय कीचड़ की तरह फट नहीं गया, इससे मैं जानता हूँ कि विधाता ने मुझे यह 'यातना शरीर' ही दिया है (जो पापी जीवों को नरक भोगने के लिए मिलता है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2683.english_translation: My heart did not split like mud when my beloved was taken away. I know the creator gave me this torment-body.
ramacharitamanas::2683.translation_literal: हृदउ (heart) / न (not) / बिदरेउ (split) / पंक (mud) / जिमि (like) / बिछुरत (separating) / प्रीतमु (beloved) / नीरु (water) / जानत (knowing) / हौं (I) / मोहि (to me) / दीन्ह (gave) / बिधि (the creator) / यहु (this) / जातना (torment) / सरीरु (body)
ramacharitamanas::2683.speaker: Sumantra
ramacharitamanas::2683.essence: Enduring separation reveals how much pain the body can hold.
ramacharitamanas::2683.simple_meaning: Sumantra says his heart did not shatter when Ram left, so he knows he has been given a body made for suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2683.simple_insight: Some grief is so deep that surviving it feels like proof of endurance, not comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2683.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has just carried Ram, Sita, and Lakshman away from Ayodhya and is returning in anguish. He says that even though separation hurts terribly, his heart has not broken apart. That endurance itself makes him feel trapped in a body made for pain.
ramacharitamanas::2683.modern_relevance: You watched a train pull away after saying goodbye to someone who changed your life. Your chest stayed intact, but only just. This verse names that strange survival.
ramacharitamanas::2683.insight: It shifts grief from private failure to a burden the body is simply carrying.

ramacharitamanas::2684.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि करत पंथ पछितावा। तमसा तीर तुरत रथु आवा॥ बिदा किए करि बिनय निषादा। फिरे पायँ परि बिकल बिषादा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2684.verse_hindi: सुमंत्र इस प्रकार मार्ग में पछतावा कर रहे थे, इतने में ही रथ तुरंत तमसा नदी के तट पर आ पहुँचा। मंत्री ने विनय करके चारों निषादों को विदा किया। वे विषाद से व्याकुल होते हुए सुमंत्र के पैरों पड़कर लौटे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2684.english_translation: In this way, Sumantra kept regretting along the road. Soon the chariot reached the bank of the Tamasa river. The minister politely bade farewell to the Nishadas, and they returned, overcome with sorrow, falling at his feet.
ramacharitamanas::2684.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / करत (doing) / पंथ (road) / पछितावा (regret) / तमसा (Tamasa) / तीर (bank) / तुरत (at once) / रथु (chariot) / आवा (came)॥ / बिदा (farewell) / किए (having done) / करि (with) / बिनय (humility) / निषादा (Nishadas) / फिरे (returned) / पायँ (feet) / परि (falling) / बिकल (distressed) / बिषादा (sorrow) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2684.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2684.essence: Departure can be polite and still break the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2684.simple_meaning: Sumantra travels in regret, reaches the Tamasa bank, gently dismisses the Nishadas, and they return in deep sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2684.simple_insight: Some goodbyes leave everyone more wounded than before.
ramacharitamanas::2684.detailed_meaning: Sumantra is carrying Ram, Sita, and Lakshman away from Ayodhya, still shaken by the exile he helped carry out. At the Tamasa riverbank, he respectfully sends the Nishadas back, and their sorrow shows how painful this journey has become.
ramacharitamanas::2684.modern_relevance: You wave goodbye after dropping someone at the station, but the car feels unbearably quiet on the drive home. Everyone has said enough, yet nobody feels finished.
ramacharitamanas::2684.insight: It keeps the focus on the emotional cost of separation, not the logistics of travel.

ramacharitamanas::2685.verse_sanskrit: पैठत नगर सचिव सकुचाई। जनु मारेसि गुर बाँभन गाई॥ बैठि बिटप तर दिवसु गवाँवा। साँझ समय तब अवसरु पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2685.verse_hindi: नगर में प्रवेश करते मंत्री (ग्लानि के कारण) ऐसे सकुचाते हैं, मानो गुरु, ब्राह्मण या गौ को मारकर आए हों। सारा दिन एक पेड़ के नीचे बैठकर बिताया। जब संध्या हुई तब मौका मिला ॥
ramacharitamanas::2685.english_translation: The minister entered the city in shame, as if he had killed his teacher, a Brahmin, or a cow. He spent the whole day under a tree. Only at dusk did he find the chance.
ramacharitamanas::2685.translation_literal: पैठत (entering) / नगर (city) / सचिव (minister) / सकुचाई (in shame) । / जनु (as if) / मारेसि (he had killed) / गुर (teacher) / बाँभन (Brahmin) / गाई (cow) ॥ / बैठि (sitting) / बिटप तर (under a tree) / दिवसु (day) / गवाँवा (spent) । / साँझ समय (at evening time) / तब (then) / अवसरु (opportunity) / पावा (found) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2685.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2685.essence: Shame can make even coming home feel impossible.
ramacharitamanas::2685.simple_meaning: The minister feels deep shame on returning to Ayodhya. He stays hidden under a tree all day and waits until evening to enter the city.
ramacharitamanas::2685.simple_insight: Some moments are so heavy that even arrival feels like concealment.
ramacharitamanas::2685.detailed_meaning: Sumantra has brought Ram, Sita, and Lakshman to the edge of exile and now returns alone to Ayodhya. Ashamed and broken, he cannot enter the city openly. He waits under a tree until dusk, when the darkness gives him cover.
ramacharitamanas::2685.modern_relevance: You come home after delivering news that changed everything, and you sit in your car for an hour before walking inside. Some truths make even ordinary entrances feel unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2685.insight: It shows how guilt can make a person delay even the simplest action.

ramacharitamanas::2686.verse_sanskrit: अवध प्रबेसु कीन्ह अँधिआरें। पैठ भवन रथु राखि दुआरें॥ जिन्ह जिन्ह समाचार सुनि पाए। भूप द्वार रथु देखन आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2686.verse_hindi: अँधेरा होने पर उन्होंने अयोध्या में प्रवेश किया और रथ को दरवाजे पर खड़ा करके वे (चुपके से) महल में घुसे। जिन-जिन लोगों ने यह समाचार सुना पाया, वे सभी रथ देखने को राजद्वार पर आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2686.english_translation: At dusk they entered Ayodhya, left the chariot at the gate, and slipped into the palace. Whoever heard the news came to the royal gate to see the chariot.
ramacharitamanas::2686.translation_literal: अवध (Ayodhya) / प्रबेसु (entry) / कीन्ह (made) / अँधिआरें (in darkness) / पैठ (entered) / भवन (house/palace) / रथु (chariot) / राखि (having left/kept) / दुआरें (at the door) / जिन्ह जिन्ह (whoever) / समाचार (news) / सुनि (having heard) / पाए (got) / भूप (king's) / द्वार (door) / रथु (chariot) / देखन (to see) / आए (came)
ramacharitamanas::2686.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2686.essence: A hidden arrival can announce a wound before any words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2686.simple_meaning: They reached Ayodhya at night, left the chariot at the gate, and went inside quietly. Hearing the news, people came to see the chariot at the royal door.
ramacharitamanas::2686.simple_insight: Some moments are so heavy that even a chariot becomes a message.
ramacharitamanas::2686.detailed_meaning: Sumantra returns to Ayodhya after the painful journey with Ram, Sita, and Lakshman. He enters in darkness, hides the chariot, and slips into the palace. Word spreads fast, and the city gathers at the gate, sensing that something has gone terribly wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2686.modern_relevance: You pull into the driveway after a hard night and switch off the engine before anyone sees you. The silence itself tells the house that something has changed.
ramacharitamanas::2686.insight: It shifts attention from action to atmosphere: even ordinary objects can carry grief, shock, and unspoken news.

ramacharitamanas::2687.verse_sanskrit: रथु पहिचानि बिकल लखि घोरे। गरहिं गात जिमि आतप ओरे॥ नगर नारि नर ब्याकुल कैसें। निघटत नीर मीनगन जैसें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2687.verse_hindi: रथ को पहचानकर और घोड़ों को व्याकुल देखकर उनके शरीर ऐसे गले जा रहे हैं (क्षीण हो रहे हैं) जैसे घाम में ओले! नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष कैसे व्याकुल हैं, जैसे जल के घटने पर मछलियाँ (व्याकुल होती हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2687.english_translation: Recognizing the chariot and seeing the horses agitated, their bodies seemed to melt like hail in the sun. How distraught the men and women of the city were, like fish when the water level drops.
ramacharitamanas::2687.translation_literal: रथु (chariot) / पहिचानि (recognizing) / बिकल (distressed) / लखि (seeing) / घोरे (horses) / गरहिं (melt) / गात (bodies) / जिमि (like) / आतप (sun/heat) / ओरे (melt away)॥ / नगर (city) / नारि (women) / नर (men) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / कैसें (how) / निघटत (decreasing) / नीर (water) / मीनगन (fish-groups) / जैसें (like)
ramacharitamanas::2687.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2687.essence: A whole city can feel grief before it is told.
ramacharitamanas::2687.simple_meaning: The city instantly senses that something terrible has happened. People grow pale with fear and confusion, like fish trapped as water dries up.
ramacharitamanas::2687.simple_insight: Shared fear can spread through a whole community before anyone even speaks.
ramacharitamanas::2687.detailed_meaning: The ministers have entered Ayodhya in shame after Ram's exile. Now the city notices the familiar chariot and the restless horses, and panic spreads through men and women alike. This is the silent moment when the people sense disaster before the news is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2687.modern_relevance: You hear the ambulance outside before anyone explains. The room changes at once, because everyone feels what is coming before the words arrive.
ramacharitamanas::2687.insight: It shows how atmosphere can carry truth faster than speech, turning a city into one trembling body.

ramacharitamanas::2688.verse_sanskrit: सचिव आगमनु सुनत सबु बिकल भयउ रनिवासु। भवनु भयंकरु लाग तेहि मानहुँ प्रेत निवासु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2688.verse_hindi: मंत्री का (अकेले ही) आना सुनकर सारा रनिवास व्याकुल हो गया। राजमहल उनको ऐसा भयानक लगा मानो प्रेतों का निवास स्थान (श्मशान) हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2688.english_translation: Hearing that the minister had come alone, the entire women’s quarters was thrown into distress. The palace seemed so dreadful to them, as if it were a dwelling of ghosts.
ramacharitamanas::2688.translation_literal: सचिव (minister) / आगमनु (arrival) / सुनत (hearing) / सबु (all) / बिकल (distressed) / भयउ (became) / रनिवासु (women’s quarters) / भवनु (palace) / भयंकरु (terrifying) / लाग (seemed) / तेहि (to them) / मानहुँ (as if) / प्रेत (ghosts) / निवासु (dwelling)
ramacharitamanas::2688.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2688.essence: Fear can turn home into a place of haunting.
ramacharitamanas::2688.simple_meaning: When the minister arrived alone, everyone in the women’s quarters panicked. The palace itself felt like a place of death and dread.
ramacharitamanas::2688.simple_insight: Fear can make a familiar home feel unrecognizable in an instant.
ramacharitamanas::2688.detailed_meaning: After the secret return to Ayodhya, Sumantra’s lone arrival reaches the royal women’s quarters. The queenly household instantly senses that something terrible has happened, and the palace, once familiar, now feels like a house of the dead.
ramacharitamanas::2688.modern_relevance: You hear one knock at the door late at night, and your stomach drops before anyone speaks. Sometimes the room changes before the news does.
ramacharitamanas::2688.insight: It shows how dread spreads through a place before any facts are spoken.

ramacharitamanas::2689.verse_sanskrit: अति आरति सब पूँछहिं रानी। उतरु न आव बिकल भइ बानी॥ सुनइ न श्रवन नयन नहिं सूझा। कहहु कहाँ नृपु तेहि तेहि बूझा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2689.verse_hindi: अत्यन्त आर्त होकर सब रानियाँ पूछती हैं, पर सुमंत्र को कुछ उत्तर नहीं आता, उनकी वाणी विकल हो गई (रुक गई) है। न कानों से सुनाई पड़ता है और न आँखों से कुछ सूझता है। वे जो भी सामने आता है उस-उससे पूछते हैं कहो, राजा कहाँ हैं ? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2689.english_translation: In deep anguish, all the queens keep asking, but Sumantra cannot answer; his speech fails him. He cannot hear, cannot see clearly, and asks everyone he meets, 'Where is the king?'
ramacharitamanas::2689.translation_literal: अति (very) / आरति (anguish) / सब (all) / पूँछहिं (ask) / रानी (queens) / उतरु (answer) / न (not) / आव (comes) / बिकल (distressed) / भइ (became) / बानी (speech) / सुनइ (hears) / न (not) / श्रवन (ears) / नयन (eyes) / नहिं (not) / सूझा (see clearly) / कहहु (tell) / कहाँ (where) / नृपु (king) / तेहि तेहि (each one) / बूझा (asked)
ramacharitamanas::2689.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2689.essence: Shock steals speech and leaves only one question.
ramacharitamanas::2689.simple_meaning: The queens are desperate for news, but Sumantra is too shaken to answer. He keeps asking everyone where King Dasharath is.
ramacharitamanas::2689.simple_insight: Grief can make even simple speech disappear.
ramacharitamanas::2689.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, word of the crisis has thrown the palace into panic. The queens press Sumantra for news, but his own shock leaves him unable to speak clearly. He moves through the palace asking where the king is, carrying the weight of disaster.
ramacharitamanas::2689.modern_relevance: You get the call no one wanted to make, and suddenly your words vanish. You know something terrible has happened, but your mind keeps circling the same question.
ramacharitamanas::2689.insight: It shows how shock breaks communication and turns the mind into repeated searching.

ramacharitamanas::2690.verse_sanskrit: दासिन्ह दीख सचिव बिकलाई। कौसल्या गृहँ गईं लवाई॥ जाइ सुमंत्र दीख कस राजा। अमिअ रहित जनु चंदु बिराजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2690.verse_hindi: दासियाँ मंत्री को व्याकुल देखकर उन्हें कौसल्याजी के महल में लिवा गईं। सुमंत्र ने जाकर वहाँ राजा को कैसा (बैठे) देखा मानो बिना अमृत का चन्द्रमा हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2690.english_translation: The servants saw the minister in distress and took him to Kaushalya's chamber. Sumantra went and saw the king there, like the moon shining without nectar.
ramacharitamanas::2690.translation_literal: दासिन्ह (the servants) / दीख (saw) / सचिव (the minister) / बिकलाई (distressed) / कौसल्या (Kaushalya) / गृहँ (to the chamber/home) / गईं (went) / लवाई (led/took along)॥ / जाइ (going) / सुमंत्र (Sumantra) / दीख (saw) / कस (how) / राजा (the king) / अमिअ (nectar) / रहित (without) / जनु (as if) / चंदु (the moon) / बिराजा (shone/sat enthroned) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2690.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2690.essence: Grief can strip even a king of all radiance.
ramacharitamanas::2690.simple_meaning: The servants noticed Sumantra's distress and brought him to Kaushalya. There he saw the king looking drained and sorrowful, like the moon stripped of its nectar.
ramacharitamanas::2690.simple_insight: Some grief is so deep it drains all radiance from a person.
ramacharitamanas::2690.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sumantra has returned with terrible news. The palace is collapsing into grief, and the servants lead him to Kaushalya's chambers. There he finds Dasharath no longer like a king, but like a moon robbed of its life-giving nectar.
ramacharitamanas::2690.insight: It prepares the mind to see grief not as weakness, but as visible depletion.

ramacharitamanas::2691.verse_sanskrit: आसन सयन बिभूषन हीना। परेउ भूमितल निपट मलीना॥ लेइ उसासु सोच एहि भाँती। सुरपुर तें जनु खँसेउ जजाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2691.verse_hindi: राजा आसन, शय्या और आभूषणों से रहित बिलकुल मलिन (उदास) पृथ्वी पर पड़े हुए हैं। वे लंबी साँसें लेकर इस प्रकार सोच करते हैं, मानो राजा ययाति स्वर्ग से गिरकर सोच कर रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::2691.english_translation: Deprived of seat, bed, and ornaments, the king lay on the bare ground, utterly dull. Drawing long breaths, he brooded like Yayati fallen from heaven.
ramacharitamanas::2691.translation_literal: आसन (seat) / सयन (bed) / बिभूषन (ornaments) / हीना (deprived of) / परेउ (fell, lay) / भूमितल (ground surface) / निपट (utterly) / मलीना (dull, soiled) / लेइ (taking) / उसासु (long breath) / सोच (grief, worry) / एहि भाँती (in this way) / सुरपुर (heavenly city) / तें (from) / जनु (as if) / खँसेउ (fell) / जजाती (Yayati)
ramacharitamanas::2691.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2691.essence: Sorrow can bring a king down to the ground.
ramacharitamanas::2691.simple_meaning: The king is lying on the ground in grief, stripped of comfort and dignity. He keeps sighing and sinking into sorrow as if he has fallen from a heavenly height.
ramacharitamanas::2691.simple_insight: Grief can strip away every outer sign of power and leave only raw human pain.
ramacharitamanas::2691.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace is collapsing under Ram's exile. Dasharath has been brought low by sorrow, no longer seated like a king but lying on the ground. The image shows how deeply the loss has broken him before his final death.
ramacharitamanas::2691.modern_relevance: You sit on the bedroom floor after the worst phone call of your life, unable to reach the bed. Even dignity feels too heavy to carry.
ramacharitamanas::2691.insight: It shifts attention from royal status to the physical truth of grief: the body itself can collapse under sorrow.

ramacharitamanas::2692.verse_sanskrit: लेत सोच भरि छिनु छिनु छाती। जनु जरि पंख परेउ संपाती॥ राम राम कह राम सनेही। पुनि कह राम लखन बैदेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2692.verse_hindi: राजा क्षण-क्षण में सोच से छाती भर लेते हैं। ऐसी विकल दशा है मानो (गीध राज जटायु का भाई) सम्पाती पंखों के जल जाने पर गिर पड़ा हो। राजा (बार-बार) 'राम, राम' 'हा स्नेही (प्यारे) राम!' कहते हैं, फिर 'हा राम, हा लक्ष्मण, हा जानकी' ऐसा कहने लगते हैं॥4
ramacharitamanas::2692.english_translation: Moment by moment, grief fills the king's chest. He is like Sampati fallen after his wings were burned. He keeps crying, 'Ram, Ram, my beloved Ram,' and then, 'Ram, Lakshman, Sita.'
ramacharitamanas::2692.translation_literal: लेत (taking) / सोच (grief, thought) / भरि (filled with) / छिनु छिनु (moment by moment) / छाती (chest) / जनु (as if) / जरि (burned) / पंख (wings) / परेउ (fell) / संपाती (Sampati) / राम (Ram) / राम (Ram) / कह (saying) / राम सनेही (beloved Ram) / पुनि (again) / कह (saying) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / बैदेही (Sita)
ramacharitamanas::2692.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2692.essence: Grief keeps calling the names it cannot bear to lose.
ramacharitamanas::2692.simple_meaning: Dasharath is overwhelmed with grief and keeps calling out the names of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2692.simple_insight: Grief can make even a king collapse into helpless longing.
ramacharitamanas::2692.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath lies broken after Ram's exile. His chest fills with sorrow every moment, and he cries out the names of the son, brother, and daughter-in-law he has lost to separation.
ramacharitamanas::2692.modern_relevance: You stare at your phone after a message you can't undo, and your chest keeps tightening. The mind keeps returning to the names it misses.
ramacharitamanas::2692.insight: It shows how loss narrows attention to repeated, aching remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::2693.verse_sanskrit: देखि सचिवँ जय जीव कहि कीन्हेउ दंड प्रनामु। सुनत उठेउ ब्याकुल नृपति कहु सुमंत्र कहँ रामु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2693.verse_hindi: मंत्री ने देखकर 'जयजीव' कहकर दण्डवत् प्रणाम किया। सुनते ही राजा व्याकुल होकर उठे और बोले- सुमंत्र! कहो, राम कहाँ हैं ? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2693.english_translation: The minister saw him, bowed fully, and said, "Victory to the living." Hearing this, the king rose in distress and asked Sumantra, "Where is Ram?"
ramacharitamanas::2693.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / सचिवँ (the minister) / जय जीव (victory, O living one) / कहि (saying) / कीन्हेउ (did) / दंड प्रनामु (prostrating bow) / सुनत (on hearing) / उठेउ (rose) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / नृपति (the king) / कहु (tell) / सुमंत्र कहँ (to Sumantra) / रामु (Ram)
ramacharitamanas::2693.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2693.essence: Separation turns every moment into a search.
ramacharitamanas::2693.simple_meaning: Sumantra bows to Dasharath, and the king immediately rises in anguish, asking where Ram is.
ramacharitamanas::2693.simple_insight: Longing can be so sharp that even a small cue brings it rushing back.
ramacharitamanas::2693.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath lies broken after Ram’s exile. Sumantra enters and bows respectfully. The king is so consumed by separation that the sight of his minister only makes him ask again for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2693.modern_relevance: You hear a name in a crowded room and your chest tightens before you can stop it. Some absences stay so alive that every small reminder opens them again.
ramacharitamanas::2693.insight: It shows how grief makes the mind circle back to the one it has lost.

ramacharitamanas::2694.verse_sanskrit: भूप सुमंत्रु लीन्ह उर लाई। बूड़त कछु अधार जनु पाई॥ सहित सनेह निकट बैठारी। पूँछत राउ नयन भरि बारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2694.verse_hindi: राजा ने सुमंत्र को हृदय से लगा लिया। मानो डूबते हुए आदमी को कुछ सहारा मिल गया हो। मंत्री को स्नेह के साथ पास बैठाकर नेत्रों में जल भरकर राजा पूछने लगे- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2694.english_translation: The king clasped Sumantra to his heart, as if a drowning man had found a little support. Seating the minister nearby with affection, the king asked with tears in his eyes.
ramacharitamanas::2694.translation_literal: भूप (king) / सुमंत्रु (Sumantra) / लीन्ह (took) / उर (heart) / लाई (bringing) / बूड़त (drowning) / कछु (some) / अधार (support) / जनु (as if) / पाई (found) / सहित (with) / सनेह (affection) / निकट (near) / बैठारी (having seated) / पूँछत (asking) / राउ (king) / नयन (eyes) / भरि (filling) / बारी (water/tears)
ramacharitamanas::2694.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2694.essence: Grief reaches for closeness before it can ask for news.
ramacharitamanas::2694.simple_meaning: Dasharath pulls Sumantra close like a drowning man grabbing support. He seats him beside him with love and, through tears, asks about Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2694.simple_insight: Grief makes even a king reach for human closeness before he can speak.
ramacharitamanas::2694.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has been shattered by Ram's exile. When Sumantra returns, the king clings to him like a drowning man to a raft, seats him near with affection, and asks about Ram through tears. The scene is pure anguish, not doctrine.
ramacharitamanas::2694.modern_relevance: You get the call that changes everything, and your first instinct is to hold on to the nearest trusted person. Before answers, you need a witness to your pain.
ramacharitamanas::2694.insight: It shows how sorrow seeks immediate human support before it can even ask its question.

ramacharitamanas::2695.verse_sanskrit: राम कुसल कहु सखा सनेही। कहँ रघुनाथु लखनु बैदेही॥ आने फेरि कि बनहि सिधाए। सुनत सचिव लोचन जल छाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2695.verse_hindi: हे मेरे प्रेमी सखा! श्री राम की कुशल कहो। बताओ, श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और जानकी कहाँ हैं? उन्हें लौटा लाए हो कि वे वन को चले गए? यह सुनते ही मंत्री के नेत्रों में जल भर आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2695.english_translation: Tell me, my dear friend, how is Ram? Where are Raghunath, Lakshman, and Sita? Have you brought them back, or have they gone to the forest again? Hearing this, the minister's eyes filled with tears.
ramacharitamanas::2695.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / कुसल (well-being) / कहु (tell) / सखा (friend) / सनेही (dear, beloved) / कहँ (where) / रघुनाथु (Raghunath) / लखनु (Lakshman) / बैदेही (Sita) / आने (brought) / फेरि (back again) / कि (or) / बनहि (to the forest) / सिधाए (went) / सुनत (hearing) / सचिव (minister) / लोचन (eyes) / जल (water, tears) / छाए (came, filled)
ramacharitamanas::2695.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2695.essence: Love makes a king ask like a frightened child.
ramacharitamanas::2695.simple_meaning: Dasharath anxiously asks Sumantra whether Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are safe and whether they have returned or gone back to the forest. The question overwhelms Sumantra with tears.
ramacharitamanas::2695.simple_insight: Love can make even a king sound helpless when the people he cherishes are away.
ramacharitamanas::2695.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has just heard Sumantra return. He pulls the minister close like a drowning man gripping a support, then asks again and again about Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. His fear and love spill into the room, and Sumantra breaks down.
ramacharitamanas::2695.modern_relevance: You refresh your phone after a long silence, hoping for one name to appear. The question is simple, but your whole chest is already answering it.
ramacharitamanas::2695.insight: It shifts attention from royal authority to raw attachment, showing how grief strips away status.

ramacharitamanas::2696.verse_sanskrit: सोक बिकल पुनि पूँछ नरेसू। कहु सिय राम लखन संदेसू॥ राम रूप गुन सील सुभाऊ। सुमिरि सुमिरि उर सोचत राऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2696.verse_hindi: शोक से व्याकुल होकर राजा फिर पूछने लगे- सीता, राम और लक्ष्मण का संदेशा तो कहो। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के रूप, गुण, शील और स्वभाव को याद कर-करके राजा हृदय में सोच करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2696.english_translation: Overcome with grief, the king asks again, "Tell me the message from Sita, Ram, and Lakshman." Remembering Ram's beauty, virtues, character, and nature again and again, the king keeps grieving in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::2696.translation_literal: सोक (grief) / बिकल (distressed) / पुनि (again) / पूँछ (asks) / नरेसू (the king) / कहु (tell) / सिय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / संदेसू (message) / राम (Ram) / रूप (form/beauty) / गुन (virtues) / सील (gentleness/character) / सुभाऊ (nature) / सुमिरि सुमिरि (remembering again and again) / उर (in the heart) / सोचत (grieving/thinking) / राऊ (the king)
ramacharitamanas::2696.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2696.essence: Love remembered in grief only deepens the wound.
ramacharitamanas::2696.simple_meaning: The king is overwhelmed with grief and keeps asking for news of Ram, Sita, and Lakshman. As he remembers Ram's beauty and virtues, his sorrow deepens.
ramacharitamanas::2696.simple_insight: Grief keeps circling back to the one you love most.
ramacharitamanas::2696.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is already broken by the exile of Ram. He turns again to Sumantra, desperate for any message from Sita, Ram, and Lakshman. Each memory of Ram only sharpens the king's sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2696.modern_relevance: You keep reopening the chat thread, hoping for one more message from someone you miss. The memory itself is both comfort and wound.
ramacharitamanas::2696.insight: It shows how love and loss can keep the mind returning to the same ache.

ramacharitamanas::2697.verse_sanskrit: राउ सुनाइ दीन्ह बनबासू। सुनि मन भयउ न हरषु हराँसू॥ सो सुत बिछुरत गए न प्राना। को पापी बड़ मोहि समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2697.verse_hindi: (और कहते हैं-) मैंने राजा होने की बात सुनाकर वनवास दे दिया, यह सुनकर भी जिस (राम) के मन में हर्ष और विषाद नहीं हुआ, ऐसे पुत्र के बिछुड़ने पर भी मेरे प्राण नहीं गए, तब मेरे समान बड़ा पापी कौन होगा ? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2697.english_translation: I told him he was exiled to the forest. Even then, his mind held neither joy nor sorrow. But when my son was separated from me, my life did not leave me. Who is more sinful than I?
ramacharitamanas::2697.translation_literal: राउ (king) / सुनाइ (having told) / दीन्ह (gave) / बनबासू (forest exile) / सुनि (hearing) / मन (mind) / भयउ (became) / न (not) / हरषु (joy) / हराँसू (sorrow) / सो (that) / सुत (son) / बिछुरत (being separated) / गए (went) / न (not) / प्राना (life-breaths) / ना (no) / को (who) / पापी (sinful) / बड़ (greater) / मोहि (than me) / समाना (equal)
ramacharitamanas::2697.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2697.essence: Ram stayed steady; Dasharath's suffering reveals his own brokenness.
ramacharitamanas::2697.simple_meaning: Dasharath admits that Ram accepted exile without emotional disturbance, while Dasharath himself cannot bear separation from his son and calls himself deeply blameworthy.
ramacharitamanas::2697.simple_insight: Grief can expose how much love and attachment still rule the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2697.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath is crushed by the result of his own promise and Kaikeyi's demand. He remembers that Ram accepted exile without joy or sorrow, yet Dasharath nearly dies from the pain of separation. That contrast turns his sorrow into self-condemnation.
ramacharitamanas::2697.modern_relevance: You sign the transfer letter that sends your child away, then sit in the quiet house and feel the cost in your chest. Sometimes the deepest pain is not punishment — it is seeing what your own choices have done.
ramacharitamanas::2697.insight: It turns grief into moral self-recognition instead of self-pity.

ramacharitamanas::2698.verse_sanskrit: सखा रामु सिय लखनु जहँ तहाँ मोहि पहुँचाउ। नाहिं त चाहत चलन अब प्रान कहउँ सतिभाउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2698.verse_hindi: हे सखा! श्री राम, जानकी और लक्ष्मण जहाँ हैं, मुझे भी वहीं पहुँचा दो। नहीं तो मैं सत्य भाव से कहता हूँ कि मेरे प्राण अब चलना ही चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2698.english_translation: O friend, take me to wherever Rama, Sita, and Lakshman are. Otherwise, I tell you in all sincerity, my life no longer wishes to continue.
ramacharitamanas::2698.translation_literal: सखा (friend) / रामु (Rama) / सिय (Sita) / लखनु (Lakshman) / जहँ तहाँ (wherever) / मोहि (me) / पहुँचाउ (take) / नाहिं त (otherwise) / चाहत (wishes) / चलन (to go on) / अब (now) / प्रान (life-breath) / कहउँ (I say) / सतिभाउ (with sincerity)
ramacharitamanas::2698.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2698.essence: Separation from what you love can make life itself feel unwanted.
ramacharitamanas::2698.simple_meaning: Dasharath says he wants to be taken to Rama, Sita, and Lakshman immediately. If that cannot happen, he feels ready to let his life end.
ramacharitamanas::2698.simple_insight: Love can become so total that separation feels physically unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2698.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has just learned that Rama, Sita, and Lakshman are in the forest. Grief has stripped away royal strength and argument. He speaks like a father whose heart can no longer bear distance, asking to be taken to them or allowed to die.
ramacharitamanas::2698.modern_relevance: You stare at a phone that never lights up with the message you need. After enough silence, even ordinary hours can feel too heavy to carry.
ramacharitamanas::2698.insight: It shows how longing can overtake the will to continue and how attachment reshapes the body’s own energy.

ramacharitamanas::2699.verse_sanskrit: पुनि पुनि पूँछत मंत्रिहि राऊ। प्रियतम सुअन सँदेस सुनाऊ॥ करहि सखा सोइ बेगि उपाऊ। रामु लखनु सिय नयन देखाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2699.verse_hindi: राजा बार-बार मंत्री से पूछते हैं- मेरे प्रियतम पुत्रों का संदेशा सुनाओ। हे सखा! तुम तुरंत वही उपाय करो जिससे श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीता को मुझे आँखों दिखा दो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2699.english_translation: The king kept asking the minister again and again, “Tell me news of my beloved sons. My friend, quickly find some way to let me see Ram, Lakshman, and Sita with my own eyes.”
ramacharitamanas::2699.translation_literal: पुनि पुनि (again and again) / पूँछत (asking) / मंत्रिहि (the minister) / राऊ (the king) / प्रियतम (beloved) / सुअन (sons) / सँदेस (news, message) / सुनाऊ (tell) / करहि (do) / सखा (friend) / सोइ (that) / बेगि (quickly) / उपाऊ (means, way) / रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / नयन (eyes) / देखाऊ (show)
ramacharitamanas::2699.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2699.essence: Separation makes even a king plead like a child.
ramacharitamanas::2699.simple_meaning: Dasharath keeps asking for news of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, and begs for a way to see them with his own eyes.
ramacharitamanas::2699.simple_insight: Love under pressure becomes urgent, tender, and helpless all at once.
ramacharitamanas::2699.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is breaking under the pain of separation after Ram’s exile. He keeps turning to his minister, not for policy, but for any possible way to glimpse the three beloved figures he longs for. The verse shows grief becoming restless repetition.
ramacharitamanas::2699.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing your phone for one message from someone you miss. You don't want advice — you want their face, their voice, their presence.
ramacharitamanas::2699.insight: It shows how grief narrows the mind to one impossible wish: just let me see them again.

ramacharitamanas::2700.verse_sanskrit: सचिव धीर धरि कह मृदु बानी। महाराज तुम्ह पंडित ग्यानी॥ बीर सुधीर धुरंधर देवा। साधु समाजु सदा तुम्ह सेवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2700.verse_hindi: मंत्री धीरज धरकर कोमल वाणी बोले- महाराज! आप पंडित और ज्ञानी हैं। हे देव! आप शूरवीर तथा उत्तम धैर्यवान पुरुषों में श्रेष्ठ हैं। आपने सदा साधुओं के समाज की सेवा की है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2700.english_translation: The minister, steadying himself, spoke gently: "Maharaj, you are learned and wise. O noble one, you are a hero, steadfast and foremost among the brave. You have always served the company of saints."
ramacharitamanas::2700.translation_literal: सचिव (minister) / धीर धरि (gathering steadiness) / कह (said) / मृदु बानी (soft words) / महाराज (Maharaj) / तुम्ह (you) / पंडित (scholar) / ग्यानी (wise) / बीर (heroic) / सुधीर (very steady) / धुरंधर (foremost bearer) / देवा (noble one) / साधु समाजु (company of saints) / सदा (always) / तुम्ह (your) / सेवा (service)
ramacharitamanas::2700.speaker: Minister
ramacharitamanas::2700.essence: Gentle words can steady a heart already breaking.
ramacharitamanas::2700.simple_meaning: The minister speaks gently and praises the king as wise, brave, steady, and devoted to serving holy people.
ramacharitamanas::2700.simple_insight: Even in grief, dignity and kindness can steady a room.
ramacharitamanas::2700.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the king is shattered by separation from Ram and keeps asking for news. The minister answers carefully, trying to calm him by reminding him of his learning, courage, steadiness, and lifelong service to holy company.
ramacharitamanas::2700.modern_relevance: A parent in tears still needs someone to speak with care, not panic. The right words do not erase pain, but they can hold it without making it worse.
ramacharitamanas::2700.insight: It teaches you to meet someone’s suffering with calm respect and affirming speech.

ramacharitamanas::2701.verse_sanskrit: जनम मरन सब दुख सुख भोगा। हानि लाभु प्रिय मिलन बियोगा॥ काल करम बस होहिं गोसाईं। बरबस राति दिवस की नाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2701.verse_hindi: जन्म-मरण, सुख-दुःख के भोग, हानि-लाभ, प्यारों का मिलना-बिछुड़ना, ये सब हे स्वामी! काल और कर्म के अधीन रात और दिन की तरह बरबस होते रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2701.english_translation: Birth and death, the experience of pleasure and pain, loss and gain, meeting and parting from loved ones — all of this, O Lord, happens helplessly under time and action, like night and day.
ramacharitamanas::2701.translation_literal: जनम (birth) / मरन (death) / सब (all) / दुख (pain) / सुख (pleasure) / भोगा (experience) / हानि (loss) / लाभु (gain) / प्रिय (beloved) / मिलन (meeting) / बियोगा (separation) / काल (time) / करम (action) / बस (under the control of) / होहिं (happen) / गोसाईं (O Lord) / बरबस (compelled) / राति (night) / दिवस (day) / की नाईं (like)
ramacharitamanas::2701.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2701.essence: Everything you gain and lose is carried by time, not by your control.
ramacharitamanas::2701.simple_meaning: Life brings birth, death, joy, sorrow, gain, loss, meeting, and separation. All of it happens under the force of time and action, not personal control.
ramacharitamanas::2701.simple_insight: It softens the grip of panic by showing that change is part of the structure of life, not a personal failure.
ramacharitamanas::2701.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court is drowning in grief and helplessness after Ram's exile. The speaker reminds everyone that every human life is ruled by time and action: gain, loss, union, and separation all arrive in their own season.
ramacharitamanas::2701.modern_relevance: You get the call that a job offer vanished, the relationship changed, or a loved one moved away. The mind wants someone to blame, but this verse points to a larger pattern: change is built into life itself.
ramacharitamanas::2701.insight: It shifts the mind from resisting change to seeing it as part of the natural order, which makes steadiness possible.

ramacharitamanas::2702.verse_sanskrit: सुख हरषहिं जड़ दुख बिलखाहीं। दोउ सम धीर धरहिं मन माहीं॥ धीरज धरहु बिबेकु बिचारी। छाड़िअ सोच सकल हितकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2702.verse_hindi: मूर्ख लोग सुख में हर्षित होते और दुःख में रोते हैं, पर धीर पुरुष अपने मन में दोनों को समान समझते हैं। हे सबके हितकारी (रक्षक)! आप विवेक विचारकर धीरज धरिए और शोक का परित्याग कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2702.english_translation: Fools rejoice in pleasure and weep in sorrow. The steadfast keep both equal in their minds. O protector of all, think wisely, hold firm, and abandon all grief.
ramacharitamanas::2702.translation_literal: सुख (pleasure) / हरषहिं (rejoice) / जड़ (fools) / दुख (sorrow) / बिलखाहीं (weep) / दोउ (both) / सम (equal) / धीर (steadfast) / धरहिं (hold) / मन माहीं (in the mind) ॥ / धीरज (steadiness) / धरहु (hold) / बिबेकु (wisely) / बिचारी (thinking) / छाड़िअ (abandon) / सोच (grief) / सकल (all) / हितकारी (for the good of all) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2702.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2702.essence: Steady minds are not shaken by pleasure or pain.
ramacharitamanas::2702.simple_meaning: Most people get carried away by happiness and sadness. A wise person stays steady through both and lets go of grief after thinking clearly.
ramacharitamanas::2702.simple_insight: You don't have to be ruled by every swing of feeling.
ramacharitamanas::2702.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the minister tries to calm the grieving king after the blow of exile. He reminds him that pleasure, loss, meeting, and separation all rise and fall with time. The real strength is to stay balanced and not drown in sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2702.modern_relevance: You get a praise email in the morning and a harsh message by noon. The mind wants to soar, then crash. This verse teaches you to stay even through both.
ramacharitamanas::2702.insight: It shifts attention from emotional reaction to steady discernment.

ramacharitamanas::2703.verse_sanskrit: प्रथम बासु तमसा भयउ दूसर सुरसरि तीर। न्हाइ रहे जलपानु करि सिय समेत दोउ बीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::2703.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी का पहला निवास (मुकाम) तमसा के तट पर हुआ, दूसरा गंगातीर पर। सीताजी सहित दोनों भाई उस दिन स्नान करके जल पीकर ही रहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2703.english_translation: Their first stop was on the bank of the Tamsa River; their second was on the bank of the Ganga. Ram, Sita, and both brothers bathed and drank water before resting there.
ramacharitamanas::2703.translation_literal: प्रथम (first) / बासु (dwelling) / तमसा (Tamsa) / भयउ (became) / दूसर (second) / सुरसरि (Ganga, river of the devas) / तीर (bank) / न्हाइ (bathed) / रहे (remained) / जलपानु (drinking water) / करि (having done) / सिय (Sita) / समेत (together with) / दोउ (both) / बीर (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::2703.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2703.essence: Even exile begins with ordinary stops and a little water.
ramacharitamanas::2703.simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and the two brothers paused at two riverbanks on their journey, bathing and resting there.
ramacharitamanas::2703.simple_insight: Sometimes the holiest journeys still move one quiet stop at a time.
ramacharitamanas::2703.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman have left Ayodhya and are moving through the forest in exile. This verse simply notes their overnight stops by the Tamsa and then the Ganga, preparing for the next meeting with Kevat.
ramacharitamanas::2703.modern_relevance: You leave home with a heavy heart, stop by a roadside river, wash your face, drink water, and keep going. Even sacred journeys still need ordinary pauses.
ramacharitamanas::2703.insight: It reminds you that major transitions unfold through simple, bodily moments of rest and movement.

ramacharitamanas::2704.verse_sanskrit: केवट कीन्हि बहुत सेवकाई। सो जामिनि सिंगरौर गवाँई॥ होत प्रात बट छीरु मगावा। जटा मुकुट निज सीस बनावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2704.verse_hindi: केवट (निषादराज) ने बहुत सेवा की। वह रात सिंगरौर (श्रृंगवेरपुर) में ही बिताई। दूसरे दिन सबेरा होते ही बड़ का दूध मँगवाया और उससे श्री राम-लक्ष्मण ने अपने सिरों पर जटाओं के मुकुट बनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2704.english_translation: Kevat rendered much service. He spent that night in Singraur. At dawn he brought banyan milk, and Ram and Lakshman made crowns of matted hair for their heads.
ramacharitamanas::2704.translation_literal: केवट (the boatman) / कीन्हि (did) / बहुत (much) / सेवकाई (service) / सो (that) / जामिनि (night) / सिंगरौर (Singraur) / गवाँई (spent) ॥ / होत (being) / प्रात (morning) / बट (banyan) / छीरु (milk) / मगावा (got brought) / जटा (matted hair) / मुकुट (crown) / निज (own) / सीस (head) / बनावा (made) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2704.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2704.essence: Service turns an ordinary night into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2704.simple_meaning: Kevat serves Ram and Lakshman with care, stays with them through the night, and helps them prepare simple crowns of matted hair at dawn.
ramacharitamanas::2704.simple_insight: Quiet service can become sacred when it is given with love.
ramacharitamanas::2704.detailed_meaning: At Singraur, the boatman Kevat is no longer just a ferryman; he is a devoted helper to Ram and Lakshman. He spends the night serving them, then brings banyan milk at dawn so they can make their matted-hair crowns before continuing the exile.
ramacharitamanas::2704.modern_relevance: You stay up late helping a guest settle in, then wake early to make breakfast before they leave. No applause, no ceremony — just care offered cleanly.
ramacharitamanas::2704.insight: It shows how humble service supports sacred duty without asking for recognition.

ramacharitamanas::2705.verse_sanskrit: राम सखाँ तब नाव मगाई। प्रिया चढ़ाई चढ़े रघुराई॥ लखन बान धनु धरे बनाई। आपु चढ़े प्रभु आयसु पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2705.verse_hindi: तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी के सखा निषादराज ने नाव मँगवाई। पहले प्रिया सीताजी को उस पर चढ़ाकर फिर श्री रघुनाथजी चढ़े। फिर लक्ष्मणजी ने धनुष-बाण सजाकर रखे और प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी की आज्ञा पाकर स्वयं चढ़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::2705.english_translation: Then Ram's friend had the boat brought. First he helped Sita board it, and then Raghunath climbed aboard. Lakshman, with bow and arrows ready, boarded only after receiving the Lord's command.
ramacharitamanas::2705.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सखाँ (friend) / तब (then) / नाव (boat) / मगाई (had brought) / प्रिया (beloved) / चढ़ाई (made board) / चढ़े (climbed) / रघुराई (Raghunath) / लखन (Lakshman) / बान (arrows) / धनु (bow) / धरे (held) / बनाई (ready) / आपु (self) / चढ़े (boarded) / प्रभु (Lord) / आयसु (command) / पाई (having received)
ramacharitamanas::2705.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2705.essence: True service knows who goes first and who waits.
ramacharitamanas::2705.simple_meaning: Nishadraj brings a boat, Sita boards first, then Ram, and Lakshman follows only after the Lord's command, with weapons ready.
ramacharitamanas::2705.simple_insight: Service here is quiet and exact: each person moves in the right order, without forcing his own way.
ramacharitamanas::2705.detailed_meaning: At the riverbank in Ayodhyakand, Nishadraj serves Ram like an old friend and ferries the exile party across. Sita boards first, Ram follows, and Lakshman stays ready with bow and arrows until Ram gives the word.
ramacharitamanas::2705.modern_relevance: You're helping someone move in the rain, carrying the heavier box, making sure the most vulnerable person goes first. Real care is practical, ordered, and attentive.
ramacharitamanas::2705.insight: It teaches you to serve with precision, protect without drama, and wait for the right command before acting.

ramacharitamanas::2706.verse_sanskrit: बिकल बिलोकि मोहि रघुबीरा। बोले मधुर बचन धरि धीरा॥ तात प्रनामु तात सन कहेहू। बार बार पद पंकज गहेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2706.verse_hindi: मुझे व्याकुल देखकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी धीरज धरकर मधुर वचन बोले- हे तात! पिताजी से मेरा प्रणाम कहना और मेरी ओर से बार-बार उनके चरण कमल पकड़ना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2706.english_translation: Seeing me distraught, Raghuvira spoke gentle words with composure: “Father, offer my salutations to our father, and again and again hold his lotus feet for me.”
ramacharitamanas::2706.translation_literal: बिकल (distraught) / बिलोकि (seeing) / मोहि (me) / रघुबीरा (Raghuvira) / बोले (spoke) / मधुर (sweet) / बचन (words) / धरि (holding) / धीरा (composure) / तात (father) / प्रनामु (salutation) / तात (father) / सन (to) / कहेहू (say) / बार बार (again and again) / पद (feet) / पंकज (lotus) / गहेहू (hold)
ramacharitamanas::2706.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2706.essence: Composure can carry love even through painful departure.
ramacharitamanas::2706.simple_meaning: Ram sees the pain around him and still speaks gently. Even at the edge of exile, he asks Lakshman to carry his reverence to their father.
ramacharitamanas::2706.simple_insight: Grace can stay calm even when everything is breaking.
ramacharitamanas::2706.detailed_meaning: At the riverbank after the painful farewell, Lakshman is shaken and Ram is about to leave for the forest. Ram answers that grief with steadiness, asking that his respect be carried to Dasharath. The moment shows how he keeps duty, tenderness, and composure together.
ramacharitamanas::2706.modern_relevance: You are leaving home after a fight, and your voice could easily turn sharp. Instead, you choose the calm sentence that protects the relationship.
ramacharitamanas::2706.insight: It teaches you to keep respect alive even in separation and distress.
