ramacharitamanas::2707.verse_sanskrit: करबि पायँ परि बिनय बहोरी। तात करिअ जनि चिंता मोरी॥ बन मग मंगल कुसल हमारें। कृपा अनुग्रह पुन्य तुम्हारें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2707.verse_hindi: फिर पाँव पकड़कर विनती करना कि हे पिताजी! आप मेरी चिंता न कीजिए। आपकी कृपा, अनुग्रह और पुण्य से वन में और मार्ग में हमारा कुशल-मंगल होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2707.english_translation: Then bow at his feet again and say, 'Father, do not worry about me. By your grace, favor, and merit, we will be safe in the forest and on the road.'
ramacharitamanas::2707.translation_literal: करबि (having done) / पायँ परि (falling at the feet) / बिनय (request) / बहोरी (again) / तात (father) / करिअ (do) / जनि (do not) / चिंता (worry) / मोरी (about me) / बन (forest) / मग (path) / मंगल (auspiciousness, well-being) / कुसल (welfare) / हमारें (for us) / कृपा (grace) / अनुग्रह (favor) / पुन्य (merit) / तुम्हारें (yours)
ramacharitamanas::2707.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2707.essence: True care sends others forward without burdening them with fear.
ramacharitamanas::2707.simple_meaning: Ram asks Dasharath not to worry. He says the forest journey will be safe through his father's grace and merit.
ramacharitamanas::2707.simple_insight: Love can calm fear without denying danger.
ramacharitamanas::2707.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank, Ram is preparing to leave Ayodhya with Sita and Lakshman. He speaks gently to Dasharath, asking him to bless the journey and release his worry. The exile is painful, but Ram turns it into trust.
ramacharitamanas::2707.modern_relevance: You’re dropping someone at the airport after a hard goodbye, trying not to show how scared you are for them. Their calm voice steadies you more than your own worry ever could.
ramacharitamanas::2707.insight: It shifts concern into blessing: instead of clinging anxiously, you send the person forward with trust.

ramacharitamanas::2708.verse_sanskrit: तुम्हरें अनुग्रह तात कानन जात सब सुखु पाइहौं। प्रतिपालि आयसु कुसल देखन पाय पुनि फिरि आइहौं॥ जननीं सकल परितोषि परि परि पायँ करि बिनती घनी। तुलसी करहु सोइ जतनु जेहिं कुसली रहहिं कोसलधनी॥
ramacharitamanas::2708.verse_hindi: हे पिताजी! आपके अनुग्रह से मैं वन जाते हुए सब प्रकार का सुख पाऊँगा। आज्ञा का भलीभाँति पालन करके चरणों का दर्शन करने कुशल पूर्वक फिर लौट आऊँगा। सब माताओं के पैरों पड़-पड़कर उनका समाधान करके और उनसे बहुत विनती करके तुलसीदास कहते हैं- तुम वही प्रयत्न करना, जिसमें कोसलपति पिताजी कुशल रहें।
ramacharitamanas::2708.english_translation: By your grace, father, I will find all happiness in the forest. By faithfully obeying your command, I will return safely to see you again. After comforting all the mothers and bowing again and again at their feet, Tulsidas says: do whatever ensures that the lord of Kosala remains well.
ramacharitamanas::2708.translation_literal: तुम्हरें (by your) / अनुग्रह (grace) / तात (father) / कानन (forest) / जात (going) / सब (all) / सुखु (happiness) / पाइहौं (I will attain) / प्रतिपालि (having faithfully followed) / आयसु (command) / कुसल (safely) / देखन (to see) / पाय (having obtained) / पुनि (again) / फिरि (returning) / आइहौं (I will come) / जननीं (mothers) / सकल (all) / परितोषि (satisfying) / परि परि (again and again) / पायँ (at the feet) / करि (doing) / बिनती (entreaty) / घनी (many) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / करहु (do) / सोइ (that) / जतनु (effort) / जेहिं (by which) / कुसली (well) / रहहिं (remain) / कोसलधनी (lord of Kosala)
ramacharitamanas::2708.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2708.essence: True obedience protects the one who gave the command.
ramacharitamanas::2708.simple_meaning: Ram tells Dasharath that, by his blessing, exile will still be bearable and he will return safely after obeying his command. He also asks that every effort be made to keep Dasharath well.
ramacharitamanas::2708.simple_insight: Love can hold duty without resentment, and obedience can still be tender.
ramacharitamanas::2708.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram speaks to Dasharath before leaving for the forest. He reassures his father that exile will not break him, because obedience itself becomes his support. He then asks that the mothers be comforted and that everything be done for Dasharath's well-being.
ramacharitamanas::2708.modern_relevance: You leave the hospital after a hard conversation, then text your family that you are okay so they can breathe. Sometimes the kindest obedience is not dramatic — it is steady, reassuring, and focused on the other person's well-being.
ramacharitamanas::2708.insight: It teaches you to carry out a painful duty without adding fear to someone else's heart.

ramacharitamanas::2709.verse_sanskrit: गुर सन कहब सँदेसु बार बार पद पदुम गहि। करब सोइ उपदेसु जेहिं न सोच मोहि अवधपति ॥
ramacharitamanas::2709.verse_hindi: बार-बार चरण कमलों को पकड़कर गुरु वशिष्ठजी से मेरा संदेशा कहना कि वे वही उपदेश दें, जिससे अवधपति पिताजी मेरा सोच न करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2709.english_translation: Again and again, bow at the guru's lotus feet and tell him my message: let him give only such counsel that the king of Ayodhya does not grieve over me.
ramacharitamanas::2709.translation_literal: गुर (teacher) / सन (to) / कहब (say) / सँदेसु (message) / बार बार (again and again) / पद पदुम (lotus feet) / गहि (grasping) / करब (do) / सोइ (that only) / उपदेसु (instruction) / जेहिं (by which) / न सोच (not grieve) / मोहि (for me) / अवधपति (king of Ayodhya)
ramacharitamanas::2709.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2709.essence: Care with your words can protect the heart that receives them.
ramacharitamanas::2709.simple_meaning: Bharat asks that his message be delivered respectfully to Guru Vashistha, and that the advice given should keep Dasharath from worrying about him.
ramacharitamanas::2709.simple_insight: Love is not only feeling — it is choosing words that protect another person's heart.
ramacharitamanas::2709.detailed_meaning: Bharat, standing in the middle of Ayodhya's family crisis, sends word through the guru to his father, Dasharath. He wants his own message shaped so carefully that it eases the king's sorrow rather than adding to it.
ramacharitamanas::2709.modern_relevance: You draft a text to your father after a painful argument, deleting the sharp line before sending it. You want the truth to land softly, because the relationship matters more than winning.
ramacharitamanas::2709.insight: It teaches you to filter speech through compassion, so your message reduces suffering instead of multiplying it.

ramacharitamanas::2710.verse_sanskrit: पुरजन परिजन सकल निहोरी। तात सुनाएहु बिनती मोरी॥ सोइ सब भाँति मोर हितकारी। जातें रह नरनाहु सुखारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2710.verse_hindi: हे तात! सब पुरवासियों और कुटुम्बियों से निहोरा (अनुरोध) करके मेरी विनती सुनाना कि वही मनुष्य मेरा सब प्रकार से हितकारी है, जिसकी चेष्टा से महाराज सुखी रहें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2710.english_translation: Father, request all the townspeople and relatives for me. Tell them my plea: that person is truly helpful to me who keeps King Dasharath content and at ease.
ramacharitamanas::2710.translation_literal: पुरजन (townspeople) / परिजन (relatives) / सकल (all) / निहोरी (with request) / तात (father) / सुनाएहु (tell) / बिनती (plea) / मोरी (my) ॥ / सोइ (that alone) / सब भाँति (in every way) / मोर (my) / हितकारी (beneficial) / जातें (by which) / रह (remain) / नरनाहु (king) / सुखारी (content, at ease) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2710.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2710.essence: Serving Ram begins with easing the burden of his father.
ramacharitamanas::2710.simple_meaning: Ram asks his father to tell everyone that the person who truly helps him is the one who keeps King Dasharath happy and peaceful.
ramacharitamanas::2710.simple_insight: Real loyalty is measured by what protects the people who matter most.
ramacharitamanas::2710.detailed_meaning: Just before leaving for exile, Ram speaks with calm clarity to Dasharath. He asks that every townsman and relative be told his wish: anyone who truly cares for him will keep the king content. His love is already turning outward into duty.
ramacharitamanas::2710.modern_relevance: You are leaving for a new city, and the last thing you ask your family is simple: please look after the parent who is staying behind. Love becomes practical right there.
ramacharitamanas::2710.insight: It shifts care from self-interest to protecting the well-being of those who hold the family together.

ramacharitamanas::2711.verse_sanskrit: कहब सँदेसु भरत के आएँ। नीति न तजिअ राजपदु पाएँ॥ पालेहु प्रजहि करम मन बानी। सेएहु मातु सकल सम जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2711.verse_hindi: भरत के आने पर उनको मेरा संदेशा कहना कि राजा का पद पा जाने पर नीति न छोड़ देना, कर्म, वचन और मन से प्रजा का पालन करना और सब माताओं को समान जानकर उनकी सेवा करना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2711.english_translation: Tell Bharat when he arrives: do not abandon righteous conduct after gaining the throne. Protect the people with your actions, words, and mind, and serve all the mothers as equal.
ramacharitamanas::2711.translation_literal: कहब (say) / सँदेसु (message) / भरत के (to Bharat) / आएँ (when he comes) / नीति (righteous conduct) / न तजिअ (do not abandon) / राजपदु (royal seat) / पाएँ (having obtained) ॥ / पालेहु (protect) / प्रजहि (the people) / करम (with action) / मन (mind) / बानी (speech) / सेएहु (serve) / मातु (mothers) / सकल (all) / सम (equal) / जानी (knowing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2711.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2711.essence: True authority is measured by conduct, not by the throne.
ramacharitamanas::2711.simple_meaning: Power should never make you careless. If you rise to a higher role, keep your conduct pure and serve everyone fairly.
ramacharitamanas::2711.simple_insight: Leadership becomes trustworthy when success does not soften your standards.
ramacharitamanas::2711.detailed_meaning: In exile, Ram sends a message for Bharat through his companions. Even if Bharat becomes king, he must not let conduct slip. He should protect the people carefully and treat all the mothers with equal respect.
ramacharitamanas::2711.modern_relevance: You get promoted, and suddenly people start watching how you speak, decide, and treat the team. This verse reminds you that a higher seat demands cleaner conduct, not a bigger ego.
ramacharitamanas::2711.insight: It shifts leadership from entitlement to responsibility, with equal care in thought, speech, and action.

ramacharitamanas::2712.verse_sanskrit: ओर निबाहेहु भायप भाई। करि पितु मातु सुजन सेवकाई॥ तात भाँति तेहि राखब राऊ। सोच मोर जेहिं करै न काऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2712.verse_hindi: और हे भाई! पिता, माता और स्वजनों की सेवा करके भाईपन को अंत तक निबाहना। हे तात! राजा (पिताजी) को उसी प्रकार से रखना जिससे वे कभी (किसी तरह भी) मेरा सोच न करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2712.english_translation: Brother, keep brotherhood alive to the end by serving your father, mother, and good people. Dear one, keep Father in such a way that he never has any worry because of me.
ramacharitamanas::2712.translation_literal: ओर (and) / निबाहेहु (maintain) / भायप (brotherhood) / भाई (brother) / करि (doing) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / सुजन (good people) / सेवकाई (service) / तात (dear one) / भाँति (way) / तेहि (that) / राखब (keep) / राऊ (king/father) / सोच (worry) / मोर (my) / जेहिं (by which) / करै (does) / न (not) / काऊ (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::2712.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2712.essence: Brotherhood survives through service, not sentiment.
ramacharitamanas::2712.simple_meaning: Ram asks Bharat to keep family duty alive by serving parents and good people, and to care for Dasharath so he feels no worry on Ram's account.
ramacharitamanas::2712.simple_insight: Love becomes real when it shows up as care, steadiness, and protection.
ramacharitamanas::2712.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is still in exile and Bharat is carrying the pain of a broken kingdom. Ram sends a message through him: honour brotherhood by serving parents and elders, and keep Dasharath free from sorrow over Ram's absence.
ramacharitamanas::2712.modern_relevance: You call your parents after a hard day and hear the strain in their voice. Instead of making them carry your burden, you steady them with your presence. That is the kind of love Ram asks for.
ramacharitamanas::2712.insight: It shifts duty from a formal role into a lived act of care that protects others from worry.

ramacharitamanas::2713.verse_sanskrit: लखन कहे कछु बचन कठोरा। बरजि राम पुनि मोहि निहोरा॥ बार बार निज सपथ देवाई। कहबि न तात लखन लारिकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2713.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी ने कुछ कठोर वचन कहे, किन्तु श्री रामजी ने उन्हें डांट कर फिर मुझसे अनुरोध किया और बार-बार अपनी सौगंध दिलाई (और कहा) हे तात! लक्ष्मण का लड़कपन वहाँ न कहना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2713.english_translation: Lakshman spoke some harsh words, but Ram stopped him and again urged me. He made me swear again and again: 'Father, do not call Lakshman childish there.'
ramacharitamanas::2713.translation_literal: लखन (Lakshman) / कहे (said) / कछु (some) / बचन (words) / कठोरा (harsh) / बरजि (restraining) / राम (Ram) / पुनि (again) / मोहि (to me) / निहोरा (request) / बार बार (again and again) / निज (own) / सपथ (oath) / देवाई (made [me] take) / कहबि (say) / न (not) / तात (father) / लखन (Lakshman) / लारिकाई (childishness)
ramacharitamanas::2713.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2713.essence: True care refuses to shame the one you love.
ramacharitamanas::2713.simple_meaning: Ram insists that Lakshman not be dismissed as childish, even while Lakshman has spoken harshly. He protects his brother’s dignity in front of others.
ramacharitamanas::2713.simple_insight: Love does not humiliate. It defends the other person’s dignity, even in tense moments.
ramacharitamanas::2713.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the family is already wounded by exile and separation. Lakshman has spoken sharply, but Ram immediately asks for restraint and makes others swear not to insult him. Even pain does not loosen Ram’s care for his brother.
ramacharitamanas::2713.modern_relevance: A family argument is still ringing in the kitchen, and someone starts mocking the younger brother for being immature. The wisest person in the room stops it immediately. Protecting dignity matters more than winning the moment.
ramacharitamanas::2713.insight: It shifts you from reacting to the offense toward guarding the relationship and the other person’s honor.

ramacharitamanas::2714.verse_sanskrit: कहि प्रनामु कछु कहन लिय सिय भइ सिथिल सनेह। थकित बचन लोचन सजल पुलक पल्लवित देह ॥
ramacharitamanas::2714.verse_hindi: प्रणाम कर सीताजी भी कुछ कहने लगी थीं, परन्तु स्नेहवश वे शिथिल हो गईं। उनकी वाणी रुक गई, नेत्रों में जल भर आया और शरीर रोमांच से व्याप्त हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2714.english_translation: After offering her प्रणाम, Sita tried to say a few words, but love made her weak. Her speech faltered, her eyes filled with tears, and her body trembled with goosebumps.
ramacharitamanas::2714.translation_literal: कहि (having said) / प्रनामु (salutation) / कछु (some) / कहन (to say) / लिय (began) / सिय (Sita) / भइ (became) / सिथिल (weak, slack) / सनेह (love) / थकित (tired) / बचन (words, speech) / लोचन (eyes) / सजल (filled with water) / पुलक (goosebumps) / पल्लवित (sprouted, covered) / देह (body)
ramacharitamanas::2714.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2714.essence: Love can make even a farewell wordless.
ramacharitamanas::2714.simple_meaning: Sita begins to speak after bowing, but emotion overwhelms her. Her voice fails, tears come, and her body shivers with love.
ramacharitamanas::2714.simple_insight: Sometimes the deepest feeling is too full for words.
ramacharitamanas::2714.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita stands in the painful farewell scene as Ram prepares to leave. After bowing, she tries to speak, but affection and sorrow overtake her. The moment is not argument or instruction, but pure emotion breaking speech.
ramacharitamanas::2714.modern_relevance: You start to say goodbye at the train platform, but your throat closes. The words are there, yet love and grief arrive first.
ramacharitamanas::2714.insight: It shows how love can silence speech and reveal itself through tears, trembling, and stillness.

ramacharitamanas::2715.verse_sanskrit: तेहि अवसर रघुबर रुख पाई। केवट पारहि नाव चलाई॥ रघुकुलतिलक चले एहि भाँती। देखउँ ठाढ़ कुलिस धरि छाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2715.verse_hindi: उसी समय श्री रामचन्द्रजी का रुख पाकर केवट ने पार जाने के लिए नाव चला दी। इस प्रकार रघुवंश तिलक श्री रामचन्द्रजी चल दिए और मैं छाती पर वज्र रखकर खड़ा-खड़ा देखता रहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2715.english_translation: At that moment, seeing Ram's readiness, the boatman set the boat across the river. Then the jewel of Raghu's line moved on, and I stood there with a chest like thunder, watching.
ramacharitamanas::2715.translation_literal: तेहि (at that) / अवसर (moment) / रघुबर (Ram, lord of Raghu) / रुख (inclination, readiness) / पाई (having obtained, seeing) / केवट (the boatman) / पारहि (to the far side) / नाव (boat) / चलाई (drove, set moving) / रघुकुलतिलक (ornament of Raghu's line) / चले (went, moved on) / एहि भाँती (in this way) / देखउँ (I watch) / ठाढ़ (standing) / कुलिस (thunderbolt) / धरि (holding) / छाती (chest)
ramacharitamanas::2715.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2715.essence: Love can leave you standing still while the beloved moves on.
ramacharitamanas::2715.simple_meaning: The boatman sends Ram across the river, and the speaker watches Ram depart with a heart as hard as a thunderbolt.
ramacharitamanas::2715.simple_insight: Some departures leave you standing still, unable to do anything but watch.
ramacharitamanas::2715.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank, the boatman finally reads Ram's intention and rows him across. Ram, the jewel of Raghu's line, moves onward while the speaker is left behind, stunned and aching. The verse captures the quiet pain of separation.
ramacharitamanas::2715.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love walk through an airport gate, unable to call them back. The body stays still, but the chest feels sealed shut.
ramacharitamanas::2715.insight: It shows how devotion can deepen into helpless longing without turning bitter.

ramacharitamanas::2716.verse_sanskrit: मैं आपन किमि कहौं कलेसू। जिअत फिरेउँ लेइ राम सँदेसू॥ अस कहि सचिव बचन रहि गयऊ। हानि गलानि सोच बस भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2716.verse_hindi: मैं अपने क्लेश को कैसे कहूँ, जो श्री रामजी का यह संदेशा लेकर जीता ही लौट आया! ऐसा कहकर मंत्री की वाणी रुक गई (वे चुप हो गए) और वे हानि की ग्लानि और सोच के वश हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2716.english_translation: How can I speak of my suffering? I returned alive carrying Ram's message. Saying this, the minister's voice stopped, and he was overcome by grief, shame, and anxious thought.
ramacharitamanas::2716.translation_literal: मैं (I) / आपन (my own) / किमि (how) / कहौं (shall I say) / कलेसू (suffering) / जिअत (alive) / फिरेउँ (I returned) / लेइ (taking) / राम (Ram) / सँदेसू (message) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / सचिव (minister) / बचन (words) / रहि गयऊ (stopped) / हानि (loss) / गलानि (shame/grief) / सोच (anxious thought) / बस (under the control of) / भयऊ (became)
ramacharitamanas::2716.speaker: Sumantra
ramacharitamanas::2716.essence: Some pain returns with you and refuses to become words.
ramacharitamanas::2716.simple_meaning: Sumantra cannot even finish speaking. He has returned alive with Ram's message, but the pain of what happened has left him speechless.
ramacharitamanas::2716.simple_insight: Some grief is too heavy to explain; it shuts the voice before it finds words.
ramacharitamanas::2716.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sumantra returns after taking Ram, Sita, and Lakshman toward exile. He has brought back Ram's message, but the sight and memory of that separation crush him. His words break off because the loss is still living inside him.
ramacharitamanas::2716.modern_relevance: You come home after dropping someone at the airport, and the house feels wrong in a way you can't explain. The words stay stuck because the absence is still fresh.
ramacharitamanas::2716.insight: It shows how deep loss can silence speech before the mind can organize it.

ramacharitamanas::2717.verse_sanskrit: सूत बचन सुनतहिं नरनाहू। परेउ धरनि उर दारुन दाहू॥ तलफत बिषम मोह मन मापा। माजा मनहुँ मीन कहुँ ब्यापा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2717.verse_hindi: सारथी सुमंत्र के वचन सुनते ही राजा पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े, उनके हृदय में भयानक जलन होने लगी। वे तड़पने लगे, उनका मन भीषण मोह से व्याकुल हो गया। मानो मछली को माँजा व्याप गया हो (पहली वर्षा का जल लग गया हो) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2717.english_translation: As soon as the charioteer's words reached King Dasharath, he fell to the ground, and a fierce burning seized his chest. He thrashed in unbearable delusion, his mind overwhelmed—like a fish struck by the first rain.
ramacharitamanas::2717.translation_literal: सूत (charioteer) / बचन (words) / सुनतहिं (as soon as hearing) / नरनाहू (king) / परेउ (fell) / धरनि (to the ground) / उर (chest) / दारुन (fierce) / दाहू (burning) / तलफत (thrashing) / बिषम (unbearable) / मोह (delusion) / मन (mind) / मापा (was measured/overwhelmed) / माजा (first rain) / मनहुँ (as if) / मीन (fish) / कहुँ (for) / ब्यापा (struck/afflicted)
ramacharitamanas::2717.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2717.essence: Grief can strike so hard that the body surrenders first.
ramacharitamanas::2717.simple_meaning: Dasharath collapses when he hears the news. Grief and confusion seize him so completely that he cannot hold himself together.
ramacharitamanas::2717.simple_insight: Some pain hits so hard that the body gives way before the mind can.
ramacharitamanas::2717.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sumantra's words reach Dasharath after Ram has left for exile. The king does not merely feel sad; he physically breaks down under the shock. This verse shows grief turning into collapse before the family’s larger lament begins.
ramacharitamanas::2717.modern_relevance: You read one message and feel your chest drop before you can even think. Some news arrives so suddenly that your body understands it first.
ramacharitamanas::2717.insight: It shows how overwhelming grief can overwhelm reason and pull the body into collapse.

ramacharitamanas::2718.verse_sanskrit: करि बिलाप सब रोवहिं रानी। महा बिपति किमि जाइ बखानी॥ सुनि बिलाप दुखहू दुखु लागा। धीरजहू कर धीरजु भागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2718.verse_hindi: सब रानियाँ विलाप करके रो रही हैं। उस महान विपत्ति का कैसे वर्णन किया जाए? उस समय के विलाप को सुनकर दुःख को भी दुःख लगा और धीरज का भी धीरज भाग गया! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2718.english_translation: All the queens weep in grief. How can such a great calamity be described? Hearing their lament, even sorrow felt sorrow, and even courage fled from courage.
ramacharitamanas::2718.translation_literal: करि (doing) / बिलाप (lamentation) / सब (all) / रोवहिं (wept/are weeping) / रानी (queens) / महा (great) / बिपति (disaster) / किमि (how) / जाइ (can be) / बखानी (described)॥ / सुनि (hearing) / बिलाप (lamentation) / दुखहू (even sorrow) / दुखु (grief) / लागा (felt) / धीरजहू (even patience/courage) / कर (of) / धीरजु (steadiness) / भागा (ran away)॥
ramacharitamanas::2718.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2718.essence: Grief can become so vast that even courage cannot stand upright.
ramacharitamanas::2718.simple_meaning: The queens are crying over a disaster so terrible that words cannot capture it. The grief is so deep it shakes even sorrow and courage itself.
ramacharitamanas::2718.simple_insight: Some losses are so heavy that even strength feels helpless beside them.
ramacharitamanas::2718.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the palace has collapsed into mourning after Dasharath's death and Ram's exile. The queens are weeping together, and the whole scene is swallowed by grief. Tulsidas lingers on the scale of the sorrow before the city itself erupts in lament.
ramacharitamanas::2718.modern_relevance: You walk into a house after bad news has already spread. No one is speaking clearly, only crying. In that kind of room, even the strongest person feels the floor give way.
ramacharitamanas::2718.insight: It shows how communal grief can overwhelm language, steadiness, and self-control all at once.

ramacharitamanas::2719.verse_sanskrit: भयउ कोलाहलु अवध अति सुनि नृप राउर सोरु। बिपुल बिहग बन परेउ निसि मानहुँ कुलिस कठोरु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2719.verse_hindi: राजा के रावले (रनिवास) में (रोने का) शोर सुनकर अयोध्या भर में बड़ा भारी कुहराम मच गया! (ऐसा जान पड़ता था) मानो पक्षियों के विशाल वन में रात के समय कठोर वज्र गिरा हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2719.english_translation: A great uproar spread through Ayodhya when the king's palace heard the lament; it was as if a hard thunderbolt had struck a forest full of birds in the night.
ramacharitamanas::2719.translation_literal: भयउ (became) / कोलाहलु (uproar) / अवध (Ayodhya) / अति (greatly) / सुनि (hearing) / नृप (king's) / राउर (palace) / सोरु (crying) / बिपुल (vast) / बिहग (birds) / बन (forest) / परेउ (fell) / निसि (at night) / मानहुँ (as if) / कुलिस (thunderbolt) / कठोरु (hard)
ramacharitamanas::2719.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2719.essence: Grief can strike a whole city like lightning.
ramacharitamanas::2719.simple_meaning: Ayodhya is thrown into panic and grief after hearing the king's palace filled with lament. The scene is compared to a thunderbolt striking a forest of birds at night.
ramacharitamanas::2719.simple_insight: Some grief is so sudden it feels like the world itself has cracked.
ramacharitamanas::2719.detailed_meaning: After Sumantra's words and the queens' crying, the sorrow inside Dasharath's palace spills into the whole city of Ayodhya. The verse pauses on the shock itself, showing how one family's loss becomes a city's collapse.
ramacharitamanas::2719.modern_relevance: You hear crying from the next room and your whole body tightens before you even know why. Some news lands like a blow before your mind can name it.
ramacharitamanas::2719.insight: It turns grief into a shared shock, not a private feeling. The mind is made to register the weight of loss instantly.

ramacharitamanas::2720.verse_sanskrit: प्रान कंठगत भयउ भुआलू। मनि बिहीन जनु ब्याकुल ब्यालू॥ इंद्रीं सकल बिकल भइँ भारी। जनु सर सरसिज बनु बिनु बारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2720.verse_hindi: राजा के प्राण कंठ में आ गए। मानो मणि के बिना साँप व्याकुल (मरणासन्न) हो गया हो। इन्द्रियाँ सब बहुत ही विकल हो गईं, मानो बिना जल के तालाब में कमलों का वन मुरझा गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2720.english_translation: The king's breath rose to his throat. Like a snake made frantic without its jewel, he was shaken to the core. All his senses grew unsteady, like a lotus grove in a pond left without water.
ramacharitamanas::2720.translation_literal: प्रान (breath/life) / कंठगत (gone to the throat) / भयउ (became) / भुआलू (the king) । मनि (jewel) / बिहीन (without) / जनु (like) / ब्याकुल (agitated) / ब्यालू (snake) । इंद्रीं (the senses) / सकल (all) / बिकल (unsteady) / भइँ (became) / भारी (greatly) । जनु (like) / सर (pond) / सरसिज (lotuses) / बनु (grove) / बिनु (without) / बारी (water) ।
ramacharitamanas::2720.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2720.essence: Grief can unmake the body before the mind finds words.
ramacharitamanas::2720.simple_meaning: Dasharath is so overwhelmed by grief that his breath seems stuck in his throat. His body and senses lose their steadiness, like a pond of lotuses left without water.
ramacharitamanas::2720.simple_insight: Grief can empty the body of steadiness before words can even form.
ramacharitamanas::2720.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the queens are already weeping, and the palace is collapsing under sorrow. Dasharath is now so shaken by the news of Ram's exile that life seems to rise into his throat. The verse lingers on his physical collapse before the next line shows Kaushalya noticing it.
ramacharitamanas::2720.modern_relevance: You get the message that breaks you, and suddenly your chest tightens, your hands go numb, and the room feels far away. Grief can arrive as a bodily event before it becomes a thought.
ramacharitamanas::2720.insight: It shifts attention from explaining pain to noticing how deeply the body carries it.

ramacharitamanas::2721.verse_sanskrit: कौसल्याँ नृपु दीख मलाना। रबिकुल रबि अँथयउ जियँ जाना॥ उर धरि धीर राम महतारी। बोली बचन समय अनुसारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2721.verse_hindi: कौसल्याजी ने राजा को बहुत दुःखी देखकर अपने हृदय में जान लिया कि अब सूर्यकुल का सूर्य अस्त हो चला! तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी की माता कौसल्या हृदय में धीरज धरकर समय के अनुकूल वचन बोलीं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2721.english_translation: Kaushalya saw the king in deep sorrow and knew in her heart that the sun of the सूर्यवंश had set. Then, holding courage in her heart, Ram's mother spoke words suited to the moment.
ramacharitamanas::2721.translation_literal: कौसल्याँ (Kaushalya) / नृपु (the king) / दीख (saw) / मलाना (grief-stricken) / रबिकुल (sun-clan) / रबि (sun) / अँथयउ (has set) / जियँ (in the heart) / जाना (knew) / उर (in the heart) / धरि (placing) / धीर (steadiness) / राम महतारी (Ram's mother) / बोली (spoke) / बचन (words) / समय (the moment) / अनुसारी (appropriate)
ramacharitamanas::2721.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2721.essence: Grief is met first with steadiness, then with the right words.
ramacharitamanas::2721.simple_meaning: Kaushalya sees Dasharath's grief and realizes the line of the सूर्यवंश is ending. She steadies herself and speaks with care.
ramacharitamanas::2721.simple_insight: Even in heartbreak, there is a dignity in speaking with steadiness and timing.
ramacharitamanas::2721.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is dying from the pain of Ram's exile. Kaushalya sees his face collapse with grief and understands that the royal sun has set. She gathers herself and begins the words that will meet this unbearable moment.
ramacharitamanas::2721.modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room and see a parent’s face change before anyone speaks. In that instant, you know the room has crossed into grief, and your next words must be chosen carefully.
ramacharitamanas::2721.insight: It teaches you to notice emotional collapse quickly and answer it with measured speech, not panic.

ramacharitamanas::2722.verse_sanskrit: नाथ समुझि मन करिअ बिचारू। राम बियोग पयोधि अपारू॥ करनधार तुम्ह अवध जहाजू। चढ़ेउ सकल प्रिय पथिक समाजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2722.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! आप मन में समझ कर विचार कीजिए कि श्री रामचन्द्र का वियोग अपार समुद्र है। अयोध्या जहाज है और आप उसके कर्णधार (खेने वाले) हैं। सब प्रियजन (कुटुम्बी और प्रजा) ही यात्रियों का समाज है, जो इस जहाज पर चढ़ा हुआ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2722.english_translation: O lord, think it through in your mind: separation from Ram is an endless ocean. You are the boat’s helmsman, and Ayodhya is the ship. All your loved ones and subjects have boarded it together.
ramacharitamanas::2722.translation_literal: नाथ (lord) / समुझि (having understood) / मन (mind) / करिअ (do) / बिचारू (reflection) / राम (Ram) / बियोग (separation) / पयोधि (ocean) / अपारू (boundless) / करनधार (helmsman) / तुम्ह (you) / अवध (Ayodhya) / जहाजू (ship) / चढ़ेउ (boarded) / सकल (all) / प्रिय (dear) / पथिक (travellers) / समाजू (company)
ramacharitamanas::2722.speaker: Kaushalya
ramacharitamanas::2722.essence: Your sorrow may be vast, but others are still in your care.
ramacharitamanas::2722.simple_meaning: Kaushalya asks Dasharath to think clearly: losing Ram feels like an endless sea, and he must guide the whole family through it safely.
ramacharitamanas::2722.simple_insight: Grief becomes lighter when someone stays steady enough to carry others too.
ramacharitamanas::2722.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath is collapsing under the pain of Ram’s exile. Kaushalya speaks with urgency and love, reminding him that he is still the helmsman of the royal household. If he loses balance now, the whole family will be overwhelmed.
ramacharitamanas::2722.modern_relevance: Your family is in the car after bad news, and everyone is looking at you to stay calm. You may be hurting too, but your steadiness becomes the bridge for everyone else.
ramacharitamanas::2722.insight: It shifts you from private overwhelm to responsible steadiness for others.

ramacharitamanas::2723.verse_sanskrit: धीरजु धरिअ त पाइअ पारू। नाहिं त बूड़िहि सबु परिवारू॥ जौं जियँ धरिअ बिनय पिय मोरी। रामु लखनु सिय मिलहिं बहोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2723.verse_hindi: आप धीरज धरिएगा, तो सब पार पहुँच जाएँगे। नहीं तो सारा परिवार डूब जाएगा। हे प्रिय स्वामी! यदि मेरी विनती हृदय में धारण कीजिएगा तो श्री राम, लक्ष्मण, सीता फिर आ मिलेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2723.english_translation: Keep patience, and you will reach the other shore. Otherwise, the whole family will drown. Dear husband, if you hold my plea in your heart, Ram, Lakshman, and Sita will come back together.
ramacharitamanas::2723.translation_literal: धीरजु (patience) / धरिअ (keep) / त (then) / पाइअ (is reached) / पारू (the other shore) / नाहिं (otherwise) / त (then) / बूड़िहि (will drown) / सबु (the whole) / परिवारू (family) / जौं (if) / जियँ (in the heart) / धरिअ (you keep) / बिनय (the plea) / पिय (dear) / मोरी (my) / रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / मिलहिं (will meet) / बहोरी (again)
ramacharitamanas::2723.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::2723.essence: Patience is the raft that carries love across grief.
ramacharitamanas::2723.simple_meaning: Kausalya asks Dasharath to stay patient and listen. She says his calm will save the family, and her plea is that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita may be reunited.
ramacharitamanas::2723.simple_insight: Calm is not passive here; it is the strength that keeps love from collapsing.
ramacharitamanas::2723.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kausalya sees Dasharath drowning in grief over Ram's exile. She urges him to hold patience like a raft: if he stays steady, the family can survive this loss and the exile can still end in reunion.
ramacharitamanas::2723.modern_relevance: You're in the middle of a family crisis, and every sharp word makes it worse. One person choosing calm can keep the whole house from breaking apart.
ramacharitamanas::2723.insight: It teaches you to treat patience as active support, not weakness, when emotions threaten to overwhelm everyone.

ramacharitamanas::2724.verse_sanskrit: प्रिया बचन मृदु सुनत नृपु चितयउ आँखि उघारि। तलफत मीन मलीन जनु सींचत सीतल बारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2724.verse_hindi: प्रिय पत्नी कौसल्या के कोमल वचन सुनते हुए राजा ने आँखें खोलकर देखा! मानो तड़पती हुई दीन मछली पर कोई शीतल जल छिड़क रहा हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2724.english_translation: Hearing his beloved wife's gentle words, the king opened his eyes. He was like a dying fish revived by cool water.
ramacharitamanas::2724.translation_literal: प्रिया (beloved) / बचन (words) / मृदु (gentle) / सुनत (hearing) / नृपु (king) / चितयउ (looked) / आँखि (eyes) / उघारि (opening) / तलफत (thrashing) / मीन (fish) / मलीन (worn-out) / जनु (as if) / सींचत (sprinkling) / सीतल (cool) / बारि (water)
ramacharitamanas::2724.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2724.essence: Tender words can briefly revive a heart already sinking.
ramacharitamanas::2724.simple_meaning: The king, overwhelmed by grief, stirs slightly when he hears his wife's tender words. Her voice is like cool water reaching someone gasping for relief.
ramacharitamanas::2724.simple_insight: Even in collapse, a gentle voice can bring someone back to themselves.
ramacharitamanas::2724.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is dying from the pain of Ram's exile. Kaushalya speaks softly to him, and he briefly opens his eyes. The image shows how grief has drained him, and how her tenderness gives a moment of relief before the larger tragedy continues.
ramacharitamanas::2724.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone shattered by bad news, and your calm voice is the only thing they can still receive.
ramacharitamanas::2724.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic action to the healing force of tenderness in a moment of collapse.

ramacharitamanas::2725.verse_sanskrit: धरि धीरजु उठि बैठ भुआलू। कहु सुमंत्र कहँ राम कृपालू॥ कहाँ लखनु कहँ रामु सनेही। कहँ प्रिय पुत्रबधू बैदेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2725.verse_hindi: धीरज धरकर राजा उठ बैठे और बोले- सुमंत्र! कहो, कृपालु श्री राम कहाँ हैं? लक्ष्मण कहाँ हैं? स्नेही राम कहाँ हैं? और मेरी प्यारी बहू जानकी कहाँ है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2725.english_translation: Steadying himself, the king sat up and said to Sumantra, “Where is kind Ram? Where is Lakshman? Where is loving Ram? Where is my dear daughter-in-law, Vaidehi?”
ramacharitamanas::2725.translation_literal: धरि (having held) / धीरजु (patience) / उठि (having risen) / बैठ (sat) / भुआलू (the king) / कहु (tell) / सुमंत्र (Sumantra) / कहँ (where) / राम (Ram) / कृपालू (the compassionate one) / कहाँ (where) / लखनु (Lakshman) / कहँ (where) / रामु (Ram) / सनेही (the loving one) / कहाँ (where) / प्रिय (dear) / पुत्रबधू (daughter-in-law) / बैदेही (Vaidehi, Sita)
ramacharitamanas::2725.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2725.essence: Grief still reaches for the ones it cannot bear to lose.
ramacharitamanas::2725.simple_meaning: Dasharath gathers himself enough to ask where Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are. His grief has made him weak, but his love is still searching for them.
ramacharitamanas::2725.simple_insight: Love can make even a broken heart reach outward before it gives way.
ramacharitamanas::2725.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has been shattered by the exile of Ram. After struggling for breath and hearing Kaushalya's gentle words, he sits up and asks Sumantra where Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are. The question shows both his fading strength and his unbearable attachment.
ramacharitamanas::2725.modern_relevance: You wake from a fevered sleep and ask for the person who matters most before you ask anything else. Grief does that: it makes the heart search first.
ramacharitamanas::2725.insight: It shows how love and loss can pull attention away from the body and toward the absent beloved.

ramacharitamanas::2726.verse_sanskrit: बिलपत राउ बिकल बहु भाँती। भइ जुग सरिस सिराति न राती॥ तापस अंध साप सुधि आई। कौसल्यहि सब कथा सुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2726.verse_hindi: राजा व्याकुल होकर बहुत प्रकार से विलाप कर रहे हैं। वह रात युग के समान बड़ी हो गई, बीतती ही नहीं। राजा को अंधे तपस्वी (श्रवणकुमार के पिता) के शाप की याद आ गई। उन्होंने सब कथा कौसल्या को कह सुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2726.english_translation: The king lamented in many ways, beside himself. The night passed like an age and would not end. Then the blind sage's curse came back to mind, and he told the whole story to Kausalya.
ramacharitamanas::2726.translation_literal: बिलपत (lamenting) / राउ (the king) / बिकल (overwhelmed) / बहु भाँती (in many ways) / भइ (became) / जुग सरिस (like an age) / सिराति (passing) / न राती (the night not) / तापस (the ascetic) / अंध (blind) / साप (curse) / सुधि (memory) / आई (came) / कौसल्यहि (to Kausalya) / सब कथा (the whole story) / सुनाई (told)
ramacharitamanas::2726.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2726.essence: Grief turns one night into an age and makes hidden guilt return.
ramacharitamanas::2726.simple_meaning: Dasharath is overwhelmed with grief. Time feels unbearable. In his pain, he remembers the curse linked to his past and tells Kausalya everything.
ramacharitamanas::2726.simple_insight: Grief can make time feel endless, and old memories surface when the heart finally breaks open.
ramacharitamanas::2726.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has already begun to collapse under the pain of Ram's exile. Through the long night, his sorrow deepens until the memory of the blind sage's curse returns. He then confides the whole burden to Kausalya.
ramacharitamanas::2726.modern_relevance: You lie awake after a fight, and one hour feels like five. Then an old mistake you thought was buried comes back with full force, and you finally say the whole truth aloud.
ramacharitamanas::2726.insight: It shows how unresolved pain stretches time and brings buried guilt to the surface.

ramacharitamanas::2727.verse_sanskrit: भयउ बिकल बरनत इतिहासा। राम रहित धिग जीवन आसा॥ सो तनु राखि करब मैं काहा। जेहिं न प्रेम पनु मोर निबाहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2727.verse_hindi: उस इतिहास का वर्णन करते-करते राजा व्याकुल हो गए और कहने लगे कि श्री राम के बिना जीने की आशा को धिक्कार है। मैं उस शरीर को रखकर क्या करूँगा, जिसने मेरा प्रेम का प्रण नहीं निबाहा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2727.english_translation: While recounting the old story, the king became distraught and said, "A life without Ram is cursed. What use is keeping this body, if it has not fulfilled my vow of love?"
ramacharitamanas::2727.translation_literal: भयउ (became) / बिकल (distraught) / बरनत (while recounting) / इतिहासा (the old story) / राम (Ram) / रहित (without) / धिग (cursed) / जीवन (life) / आसा (hope) ॥ / सो (that) / तनु (body) / राखि (keeping) / करब (shall I do) / मैं (I) / काहा (what) ॥ / जेहिं (by which) / न (not) / प्रेम (love) / पनु (vow) / मोर (my) / निबाहा (was fulfilled) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2727.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2727.essence: A body without fulfilled love feels like a burden.
ramacharitamanas::2727.simple_meaning: Dasharath sees that life without Ram has lost its value. He feels his body is useless if he cannot keep the promise of love he made.
ramacharitamanas::2727.simple_insight: Grief can strip away every excuse and reveal what truly mattered all along.
ramacharitamanas::2727.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has been asking for Ram in despair. As he speaks of the old story, his mind breaks open: Ram is gone, and the king feels his own body has no purpose left. The verse captures the moment his longing turns into surrender.
ramacharitamanas::2727.modern_relevance: You keep scrolling old photos after a breakup, realizing the apartment, the routines, even your own body feel strangely hollow. When the bond is gone, the life built around it can feel uninhabited.
ramacharitamanas::2727.insight: It shifts attention from physical survival to the deeper question of whether your life is still aligned with what you love.

ramacharitamanas::2728.verse_sanskrit: हा रघुनंदन प्रान पिरीते। तुम्ह बिनु जिअत बहुत दिन बीते॥ हा जानकी लखन हा रघुबर। हा पितु हित चित चातक जलधर ॥
ramacharitamanas::2728.verse_hindi: हा रघुकुल को आनंद देने वाले मेरे प्राण प्यारे राम! तुम्हारे बिना जीते हुए मुझे बहुत दिन बीत गए। हा जानकी, लक्ष्मण! हा रघुवीर! हा पिता के चित्त रूपी चातक के हित करने वाले मेघ! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2728.english_translation: O delight of Raghu's line, beloved of my life! I have lived many days without you. O Janaki, Lakshman, O Raghubar! O cloud that brings relief to my father's thirsty heart!
ramacharitamanas::2728.translation_literal: हा (alas) / रघुनंदन (delight of Raghu's line) / प्रान पिरीते (beloved of life) / तुम्ह (you) / बिनु (without) / जिअत (living) / बहुत (many) / दिन (days) / बीते (have passed) ॥ / हा (alas) / जानकी (Janaki) / लखन (Lakshman) / हा (alas) / रघुबर (Raghubar) / हा (alas) / पितु (father) / हित (for the well-being) / चित (mind) / चातक (chatak bird) / जलधर (cloud)
ramacharitamanas::2728.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2728.essence: Separation makes even living feel like endurance.
ramacharitamanas::2728.simple_meaning: Dasharath cries out in grief, saying Ram is the beloved of his life and that living without him has gone on too long. He also calls to Sita, Lakshman, and Ram as the one who relieved his father’s heart.
ramacharitamanas::2728.simple_insight: Love can make mere survival feel empty, and separation can turn time into ache.
ramacharitamanas::2728.detailed_meaning: Dasharath is dying in Ayodhya after Ram’s exile. In his grief, he calls out to Ram, Sita, Lakshman, and remembers Ram as the one who brought peace to his own heart. The verse is a cry of separation before death.
ramacharitamanas::2728.modern_relevance: You keep going through the motions after someone leaves, answering emails, making tea, sleeping badly. From the outside it looks normal; inside, you know you are only enduring the days.
ramacharitamanas::2728.insight: It names grief honestly instead of dressing it up, and shows how absence can hollow out ordinary time.

ramacharitamanas::2729.verse_sanskrit: राम राम कहि राम कहि राम राम कहि राम। तनु परिहरि रघुबर बिरहँ राउ गयउ सुरधाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::2729.verse_hindi: राम-राम कहकर, फिर राम कहकर, फिर राम-राम कहकर और फिर राम कहकर राजा श्री राम के विरह में शरीर त्याग कर सुरलोक को सिधार गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2729.english_translation: Saying Ram, Ram, Ram, Ram, the king left his body in separation from Raghubar and went to the higher realm.
ramacharitamanas::2729.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / राम (Ram) / कहि (saying) / राम (Ram) / कहि (saying) / राम (Ram) / राम (Ram) / कहि (saying) / राम (Ram) / तनु (body) / परिहरि (giving up) / रघुबर (Raghubar, Ram) / बिरहँ (in separation) / राउ (king) / गयउ (went) / सुरधाम (higher realm)
ramacharitamanas::2729.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2729.essence: Separation from Ram becomes the king's final passage.
ramacharitamanas::2729.simple_meaning: Dasharath died with Ram's name on his lips, overwhelmed by separation from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2729.simple_insight: Love can become so complete that even death is held inside remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::2729.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath has been shattered by Ram's exile. After crying out again and again for Ram, he gives up his body in that longing. The verse marks the king's final release.
ramacharitamanas::2729.modern_relevance: Someone keeps whispering a loved one's name after a hospital call, unable to stop the ache. This verse understands that grief can become the last prayer.
ramacharitamanas::2729.insight: It shows how longing can shape even the final moment, turning loss into remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::2730.verse_sanskrit: जिअन मरन फलु दसरथ पावा। अंड अनेक अमल जसु छावा॥ जिअत राम बिधु बदनु निहारा। राम बिरह करि मरनु सँवारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2730.verse_hindi: जीने और मरने का फल तो दशरथजी ने ही पाया, जिनका निर्मल यश अनेकों ब्रह्मांडों में छा गया। जीते जी तो श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चन्द्रमा के समान मुख को देखा और श्री राम के विरह को निमित्त बनाकर अपना मरण सुधार लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2730.english_translation: Dasharath received the fruit of both living and dying; his spotless fame spread across countless worlds. While alive, he beheld Ram's moon-like face, and through separation from Ram, he made his death complete.
ramacharitamanas::2730.translation_literal: जिअन (living) / मरन (dying) / फलु (fruit) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / पावा (received) / अंड (worlds) / अनेक (many) / अमल (spotless) / जसु (fame) / छावा (spread) / जिअत (while living) / राम (Ram) / बिधु (moon) / बदनु (face) / निहारा (beheld) / राम (Ram) / बिरह (separation) / करि (having made) / मरनु (death) / सँवारा (made complete)
ramacharitamanas::2730.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2730.essence: A life touched by Ram is complete, even in grief.
ramacharitamanas::2730.simple_meaning: Dasharath found fulfillment in both living and dying. He saw Ram's beautiful face while alive, and even Ram's separation became part of a blessed end.
ramacharitamanas::2730.simple_insight: Love can make even loss feel complete, not wasted.
ramacharitamanas::2730.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has just died of grief after Ram's exile. The narrator reflects that his life was fulfilled by seeing Ram, and his death was purified by the pain of separation. This turns private loss into a sacred completion.
ramacharitamanas::2730.modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed after a long goodbye, knowing nothing can be fixed now. Yet the love was real, and the life shared was not empty.
ramacharitamanas::2730.insight: It shifts the mind from measuring life by comfort to measuring it by love and completion.

ramacharitamanas::2731.verse_sanskrit: सोक बिकल सब रोवहिं रानी। रूपु सीलु बलु तेजु बखानी॥ करहिं बिलाप अनेक प्रकारा। परहिं भूमितल बारहिं बारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2731.verse_hindi: सब रानियाँ शोक के मारे व्याकुल होकर रो रही हैं। वे राजा के रूप, शील, बल और तेज का बखान कर-करके अनेकों प्रकार से विलाप कर रही हैं और बार-बार धरती पर गिर-गिर पड़ती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2731.english_translation: The queens, overcome with grief, weep. They keep praising the king’s beauty, character, strength, and radiance, and lament in many ways, falling to the ground again and again.
ramacharitamanas::2731.translation_literal: सोक (grief) / बिकल (overwhelmed) / सब (all) / रोवहिं (weep) / रानी (queens) / रूपु (beauty) / सीलु (character) / बलु (strength) / तेजु (radiance) / बखानी (praising) / करहिं (they do) / बिलाप (lamentation) / अनेक प्रकारा (many kinds) / परहिं (fall) / भूमितल (on the ground) / बारहिं बारा (again and again)
ramacharitamanas::2731.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2731.essence: Grief makes even praise collapse into tears.
ramacharitamanas::2731.simple_meaning: The queens are shattered by grief. They keep remembering the king’s virtues and collapse in mourning again and again.
ramacharitamanas::2731.simple_insight: Love can make grief physical — praise becomes the only language left when loss is too large.
ramacharitamanas::2731.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has just died in exile, and Ayodhya is breaking open with loss. In the palace, the queens cannot hold themselves together; they cry out his virtues and fall to the ground repeatedly, as grief takes over the whole court.
ramacharitamanas::2731.modern_relevance: You stand beside a hospital bed after the last goodbye, and your mind keeps circling the same memories. Grief turns praise, memory, and collapse into one motion.
ramacharitamanas::2731.insight: It shows how bereavement moves through remembrance, not argument: the heart keeps returning to what it has lost.

ramacharitamanas::2732.verse_sanskrit: बिलपहिं बिकल दास अरु दासी। घर घर रुदनु करहिं पुरबासी॥ अँथयउ आजु भानुकुल भानू। धरम अवधि गुन रूप निधानू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2732.verse_hindi: दास-दासीगण व्याकुल होकर विलाप कर रहे हैं और नगर निवासी घर-घर रो रहे हैं। कहते हैं कि आज धर्म की सीमा, गुण और रूप के भंडार सूर्यकुल के सूर्य अस्त हो गए? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2732.english_translation: The servants and maidservants weep in anguish, and the townspeople cry in every home. They say, "Today the sun of the सूर्यवंश has set—the treasure of duty, virtue, and beauty."
ramacharitamanas::2732.translation_literal: बिलपहिं (weep) / बिकल (distressed) / दास (servants) / अरु (and) / दासी (maidservants) / घर घर (house after house) / रुदनु (weeping) / करहिं (do) / पुरबासी (townspeople) / अँथयउ (has set) / आजु (today) / भानुकुल (solar dynasty) / भानू (sun) / धरम (dharma) / अवधि (limit) / गुन (virtue) / रूप (beauty) / निधानू (treasure)
ramacharitamanas::2732.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2732.essence: A righteous life can become the light a whole city depends on.
ramacharitamanas::2732.simple_meaning: Everyone in Ayodhya is grieving. They feel that the light of their kingdom has gone out with Dasharath's death.
ramacharitamanas::2732.simple_insight: When a good ruler falls, a whole community feels the loss.
ramacharitamanas::2732.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Dasharath's death, grief has spread beyond the palace. Servants and ordinary townspeople are crying in every house, seeing him as the sun of the सूर्यवंश, the living measure of duty, virtue, and grace.
ramacharitamanas::2732.modern_relevance: A neighborhood goes quiet after the respected elder who held everyone together is gone. People don't just miss one person; they miss the moral center that made the place feel whole.
ramacharitamanas::2732.insight: It shows how deeply a just leader shapes the emotional life of an entire community.

ramacharitamanas::2733.verse_sanskrit: गारीं सकल कैकइहि देहीं। नयन बिहीन कीन्ह जग जेहीं॥ एहि बिधि बिलपत रैनि बिहानी। आए सकल महामुनि ग्यानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2733.verse_hindi: सब कैकेयी को गालियाँ देते हैं, जिसने संसार भर को बिना नेत्रों का (अंधा) कर दिया! इस प्रकार विलाप करते रात बीत गई। प्रातःकाल सब बड़े-बड़े ज्ञानी मुनि आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2733.english_translation: Everyone curses Kaikeyi, saying she has made the world blind. In this way they keep lamenting through the night, and at dawn all the great sages and wise men arrive.
ramacharitamanas::2733.translation_literal: गारीं (abuses/curses) / सकल (all) / कैकइहि (to Kaikeyi) / देहीं (give) / नयन (eyes) / बिहीन (without) / कीन्ह (made) / जग (the world) / जेहीं (who)॥ / एहि बिधि (in this way) / बिलपत (lamenting) / रैनि (night) / बिहानी (passed) / आए (came) / सकल (all) / महामुनि (great sages) / ग्यानी (wise ones) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2733.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2733.essence: Blame floods the mind before wisdom can return.
ramacharitamanas::2733.simple_meaning: People blame Kaikeyi for the disaster and say she has blinded the world. Their grief lasts through the night until the sages arrive at dawn.
ramacharitamanas::2733.simple_insight: Grief first looks for someone to blame before it can begin to heal.
ramacharitamanas::2733.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is drowning in Dasharath's death and Ram's exile. The people spend the night in raw blame and mourning, turning on Kaikeyi as the cause of everything. By morning, sages and wise men arrive to steady the city.
ramacharitamanas::2733.modern_relevance: After a family rupture, everyone keeps replaying who ruined everything, and the blame keeps the house awake until morning.
ramacharitamanas::2733.insight: It shows how shock turns into accusation, and how wisdom enters only after the first wave of pain.

ramacharitamanas::2734.verse_sanskrit: तब बसिष्ठ मुनि समय सम कहि अनेक इतिहास। सोक नेवारेउ सबहि कर निज बिग्यान प्रकास ॥
ramacharitamanas::2734.verse_hindi: तब वशिष्ठ मुनि ने समय के अनुकूल अनेक इतिहास कहकर अपने विज्ञान के प्रकाश से सबका शोक दूर किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2734.english_translation: Then sage Vashishtha, speaking in the right time with fitting stories, dispelled everyone's grief with the light of his own wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::2734.translation_literal: तब (then) / बसिष्ठ मुनि (sage Vashishtha) / समय सम (according to the moment) / कहि (speaking) / अनेक इतिहास (many stories) / सोक (grief) / नेवारेउ (removed) / सबहि कर (of everyone) / निज (own) / बिग्यान (wisdom) / प्रकास (light)
ramacharitamanas::2734.speaker: Vashishtha
ramacharitamanas::2734.essence: The right wisdom at the right time can carry people through grief.
ramacharitamanas::2734.simple_meaning: Vashishtha spoke fitting stories at the right moment, and his clear understanding helped everyone move through their grief.
ramacharitamanas::2734.simple_insight: Grief can be eased by presence, timing, and words that meet people where they are.
ramacharitamanas::2734.detailed_meaning: After Dasharath's death and the palace's collapse into mourning, the sage Vashishtha steps in. He does not argue with sorrow; he speaks in a way suited to the moment, and his wisdom begins to steady everyone.
ramacharitamanas::2734.modern_relevance: A family sits in silence after bad news, and no one knows what to say. One calm person tells the right story, at the right pace, and the room slowly breathes again.
ramacharitamanas::2734.insight: It teaches you to meet pain with measured speech instead of forceful correction.

ramacharitamanas::2735.verse_sanskrit: तेल नावँ भरि नृप तनु राखा। दूत बोलाइ बहुरि अस भाषा॥ धावहु बेगि भरत पहिं जाहू। नृप सुधि कतहुँ कहहु जनि काहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2735.verse_hindi: वशिष्ठजी ने नाव में तेल भरवाकर राजा के शरीर को उसमें रखवा दिया। फिर दूतों को बुलवाकर उनसे ऐसा कहा- तुम लोग जल्दी दौड़कर भरत के पास जाओ। राजा की मृत्यु का समाचार कहीं किसी से न कहना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2735.english_translation: Vashishtha had the king's body placed in an oil-filled vessel, then called the messengers and said, "Hurry to Bharat at once. Do not tell anyone of the king's death."
ramacharitamanas::2735.translation_literal: तेल (oil) / नावँ (vessel) / भरि (filling) / नृप (king) / तनु (body) / राखा (placed, kept) / दूत (messengers) / बोलाइ (calling) / बहुरि (then) / अस (thus) / भाषा (spoke) ॥ धावहु (hurry) / बेगि (quickly) / भरत पहिं (to Bharat) / जाहू (go) ॥ नृप (king's) / सुधि (news, mention) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / कहहु (tell) / जनि (do not) / काहू (to anyone) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2735.speaker: Vashishtha
ramacharitamanas::2735.essence: Grief first demands protection, not explanation.
ramacharitamanas::2735.simple_meaning: Vashishtha preserves Dasharath's body and sends messengers to bring Bharat quickly, while hiding the news of the king's death.
ramacharitamanas::2735.simple_insight: In shock, the next duty is simple: protect what must be protected before sorrow spreads.
ramacharitamanas::2735.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has died, and Ayodhya is still reeling. Vashishtha acts at once, placing the king's body in oil and sending messengers to Bharat with urgent instructions. This is a practical pause before the family's grief reaches its next turning point.
ramacharitamanas::2735.modern_relevance: A hospital corridor goes quiet after the doctor gives you the news. Before the relatives arrive, someone has to steady the room, make the calls, and keep panic from spreading.
ramacharitamanas::2735.insight: It shifts attention from emotional collapse to immediate, careful action.

ramacharitamanas::2736.verse_sanskrit: एतनेइ कहेहु भरत सन जाई। गुर बोलाइ पठयउ दोउ भाई॥ सुनि मुनि आयसु धावन धाए। चले बेग बर बाजि लजाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2736.verse_hindi: जाकर भरत से इतना ही कहना कि दोनों भाइयों को गुरुजी ने बुलवा भेजा है। मुनि की आज्ञा सुनकर धावन (दूत) दौड़े। वे अपने वेग से उत्तम घोड़ों को भी लजाते हुए चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2736.english_translation: Tell Bharata only this: the guru has summoned both brothers. Hearing the sage's order, the messengers rushed off, moving so fast they shamed the finest horses.
ramacharitamanas::2736.translation_literal: एतनेइ (only this much) / कहेहु (say) / भरत (to Bharata) / सन (to) / जाई (going) / गुर (the guru) / बोलाइ (having called) / पठयउ (sent) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) ॥ / सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (sage's) / आयसु (order) / धावन (the messengers) / धाए (ran) ॥ / चले (they went) / बेगि (swiftly) / बर (excellent) / बाजि (horses) / लजाए (put to shame) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2736.speaker: Vashishtha
ramacharitamanas::2736.essence: Some messages are so urgent they outrun hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::2736.simple_meaning: Vashishtha tells the messengers to inform Bharata that both brothers have been summoned. They hurry off at once, running so fast they outpace even the best horses.
ramacharitamanas::2736.simple_insight: Urgency can make ordinary effort feel impossible to match.
ramacharitamanas::2736.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Rama's exile has shattered the royal household, Vashishtha sends messengers to Bharata and Shatrughna. This verse simply shows their immediate departure: the crisis is deepening, and every movement now carries fear and haste.
ramacharitamanas::2736.modern_relevance: The phone rings at midnight, and you already know the news is serious. You grab your keys before the message is even finished.
ramacharitamanas::2736.insight: It captures the speed of action under pressure, before thought can catch up.

ramacharitamanas::2737.verse_sanskrit: अनरथु अवध अरंभेउ जब तें। कुसगुन होहिं भरत कहुँ तब तें॥ देखहिं राति भयानक सपना। जागि करहिं कटु कोटि कलपना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2737.verse_hindi: जब से अयोध्या में अनर्थ प्रारंभ हुआ, तभी से भरतजी को अपशकुन होने लगे। वे रात को भयंकर स्वप्न देखते थे और जागने पर (उन स्वप्नों के कारण) करोड़ों (अनेकों) तरह की बुरी-बुरी कल्पनाएँ किया करते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2737.english_translation: Since the moment calamity began in Ayodhya, ominous signs appeared for Bharat. He would see frightening dreams at night and, upon waking, fall into countless dark imaginings.
ramacharitamanas::2737.translation_literal: अनरथु (calamity) / अवध (Ayodhya) / अरंभेउ (began) / जब तें (since then) / कुसगुन (bad omens) / होहिं (happen) / भरत कहुँ (for Bharat) / तब तें (from then on) / देखहिं (he sees) / राति (at night) / भयानक (terrifying) / सपना (dreams) / जागि (waking up) / करहिं (does) / कटु (bitter) / कोटि (crores, countless) / कलपना (imaginations)
ramacharitamanas::2737.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2737.essence: Trouble first appears as fear in the mind.
ramacharitamanas::2737.simple_meaning: From the moment trouble began in Ayodhya, Bharat was surrounded by bad signs, frightening dreams, and anxious thoughts.
ramacharitamanas::2737.simple_insight: When your world feels off, the mind starts inventing fears before facts arrive.
ramacharitamanas::2737.detailed_meaning: As Ayodhya slips into disaster, Bharat is already feeling it before anyone tells him. Night after night, his sleep fills with fear, and waking only multiplies his dread. The verse shows grief arriving as intuition before news.
ramacharitamanas::2737.modern_relevance: You wake at 3 a.m. after a bad dream, then spend the next hour turning it into ten worse stories. Bharat knows that spiraling feeling before the phone even rings.
ramacharitamanas::2737.insight: It shows how inner anxiety can mirror a family crisis before the crisis is spoken aloud.

ramacharitamanas::2738.verse_sanskrit: बिप्र जेवाँइ देहिं दिन दाना। सिव अभिषेक करहिं बिधि नाना॥ मागहिं हृदयँ महेस मनाई। कुसल मातु पितु परिजन भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2738.verse_hindi: (अनिष्टशान्ति के लिए) वे प्रतिदिन ब्राह्मणों को भोजन कराकर दान देते थे। अनेकों विधियों से रुद्राभिषेक करते थे। महादेवजी को हृदय में मनाकर उनसे माता-पिता, कुटुम्बी और भाइयों का कुशल-क्षेम माँगते थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2738.english_translation: They fed Brahmins and gave daily charity, performed Shiva worship in many ways, and in their hearts prayed to Mahesh for the well-being of their mother, father, family, and brothers.
ramacharitamanas::2738.translation_literal: बिप्र (Brahmins) / जेवाँइ (feeding) / देहिं (they give) / दिन (daily) / दाना (charity) / सिव (Shiva) / अभिषेक (ritual bathing) / करहिं (they perform) / बिधि नाना (many ways) / मागहिं (they ask) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / महेस (Mahesh/Shiva) / मनाई (having remembered/pleased) / कुसल (well-being) / मातु (mother) / पितु (father) / परिजन (family) / भाई (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::2738.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2738.essence: Fear makes love reach for rituals and protection.
ramacharitamanas::2738.simple_meaning: Bharat and the people around him keep doing rituals, charity, and prayers for the safety of their loved ones.
ramacharitamanas::2738.simple_insight: Grief often turns into ritual when love has nowhere else to go.
ramacharitamanas::2738.detailed_meaning: Bharat is already shaken by the disaster in Ayodhya. In that anxious household, people try to ward off harm through charity, Shiva worship, and heartfelt prayers for the family’s safety. The verse shows their fear before the messenger arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2738.modern_relevance: You start lighting incense, calling relatives, and checking on everyone after a family crisis. The rituals do not fix the pain, but they show how love reaches for protection.
ramacharitamanas::2738.insight: It shows how anxious love looks for every possible way to protect the people it cannot control.

ramacharitamanas::2739.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि सोचत भरत मन धावन पहुँचे आइ। गुर अनुसासन श्रवन सुनि चले गनेसु मनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2739.verse_hindi: भरतजी इस प्रकार मन में चिंता कर रहे थे कि दूत आ पहुँचे। गुरुजी की आज्ञा कानों से सुनते ही वे गणेशजी को मनाकर चल पड़े।157॥
ramacharitamanas::2739.english_translation: While Bharat was thinking like this in his mind, the messenger arrived. Hearing the guru's instruction, he at once invoked Ganesh and set out.
ramacharitamanas::2739.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / सोचत (thinking) / भरत (Bharat) / मन (mind) / धावन (running) / पहुँचे (arrived) / आइ (coming) / गुर (guru's) / अनुसासन (instruction) / श्रवन (ears/hearing) / सुनि (having heard) / चले (set out) / गनेसु (Ganesh) / मनाई (having invoked/pleased)
ramacharitamanas::2739.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2739.essence: True readiness is moving before anxiety can finish its story.
ramacharitamanas::2739.simple_meaning: Bharat is lost in worry when the messenger arrives. As soon as he hears the guru's order, he invokes Ganesh and leaves at once.
ramacharitamanas::2739.simple_insight: When responsibility calls, hesitation ends. He moves the moment guidance reaches him.
ramacharitamanas::2739.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat has been living with dread since the kingdom's crisis began. While his mind is still racing, a messenger arrives. The guru's instruction is enough to end delay, and Bharat prepares to depart immediately.
ramacharitamanas::2739.modern_relevance: You are spiraling over bad news when your phone rings with the one message that matters. The noise in your head doesn't vanish first; you move first, and clarity follows.
ramacharitamanas::2739.insight: It shifts attention from anxious thinking to immediate response to rightful guidance.

ramacharitamanas::2740.verse_sanskrit: चले समीर बेग हय हाँके। नाघत सरित सैल बन बाँके॥ हृदयँ सोचु बड़ कछु न सोहाई। अस जानहिं जियँ जाउँ उड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2740.verse_hindi: हवा के समान वेग वाले घोड़ों को हाँकते हुए वे विकट नदी, पहाड़ तथा जंगलों को लाँघते हुए चले। उनके हृदय में बड़ा सोच था, कुछ सुहाता न था। मन में ऐसा सोचते थे कि उड़कर पहुँच जाऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2740.english_translation: Driving horses as fast as the wind, they crossed rough rivers, hills, and forests. Their heart was heavy with worry; nothing felt pleasant. In their mind, they wished they could fly there.
ramacharitamanas::2740.translation_literal: चले (they moved) / समीर (wind) / बेग (speed) / हय (horses) / हाँके (driving) / नाघत (crossing) / सरित (rivers) / सैल (hills) / बन (forests) / बाँके (rough) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / सोचु (worry) / बड़ (great) / कछु (anything) / न (not) / सोहाई (felt pleasant) / अस (thus) / जानहिं (they know) / जियँ (in the mind) / जाउँ (I go) / उड़ाई (flying)
ramacharitamanas::2740.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2740.essence: An anxious heart turns every road into a delay.
ramacharitamanas::2740.simple_meaning: The travelers rushed forward as fast as they could, crossing difficult terrain. Their mind was full of worry, and they wanted to reach the city even faster.
ramacharitamanas::2740.simple_insight: Urgency can make every mile feel too slow.
ramacharitamanas::2740.detailed_meaning: Bharat is racing toward Ayodhya after hearing the terrible news. The road, the rivers, and the hills cannot match the speed of his anxious heart. This verse shows only the hurry and distress of the journey, not its teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2740.modern_relevance: You keep checking the map while the taxi crawls through traffic, because your mind is already at the hospital door.
ramacharitamanas::2740.insight: It captures the way grief and urgency make the body move faster than the world allows.

ramacharitamanas::2741.verse_sanskrit: एक निमेष बरष सम जाई। एहि बिधि भरत नगर निअराई॥ असगुन होहिं नगर पैठारा। रटहिं कुभाँति कुखेत करारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2741.verse_hindi: एक-एक निमेष वर्ष के समान बीत रहा था। इस प्रकार भरतजी नगर के निकट पहुँचे। नगर में प्रवेश करते समय अपशकुन होने लगे। कौए बुरी जगह बैठकर बुरी तरह से काँव-काँव कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2741.english_translation: A single moment passed like a year. In this way Bharat drew near the city. Ominous signs appeared as he entered the city. Crows sat in bad places and cawed harshly.
ramacharitamanas::2741.translation_literal: एक (one) / निमेष (moment) / बरष (year) / सम (like) / जाई (goes) / एहि (this) / बिधि (way) / भरत (Bharat) / नगर (city) / निअराई (neared) / असगुन (bad omen) / होहिं (happen) / नगर (city) / पैठारा (entering) / रटहिं (cry) / कुभाँति (in bad manner) / कुखेत (bad places) / करारा (harshly)
ramacharitamanas::2741.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2741.essence: Grief makes a single moment feel like a year.
ramacharitamanas::2741.simple_meaning: Bharat is nearing Ayodhya, but every moment feels painfully long and the city is filled with bad omens.
ramacharitamanas::2741.simple_insight: Anxious waiting can make time feel endless.
ramacharitamanas::2741.detailed_meaning: Bharat rides toward Ayodhya with a heart already burdened by grief. As the city comes into view, the scene itself turns dark: time stretches, omens sour, and even the crows seem to warn him that something is terribly wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2741.modern_relevance: You are ten minutes from home after a hard phone call, and every red light feels cruel. When your mind is braced for loss, even ordinary signs start to feel heavy.
ramacharitamanas::2741.insight: It shows how fear can distort time and make the world feel hostile before anything has even happened.

ramacharitamanas::2742.verse_sanskrit: खर सिआर बोलहिं प्रतिकूला। सुनि सुनि होइ भरत मन सूला॥ श्रीहत सर सरिता बन बागा। नगरु बिसेषि भयावनु लागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2742.verse_hindi: गदहे और सियार विपरीत बोल रहे हैं। यह सुन-सुनकर भरत के मन में बड़ी पीड़ा हो रही है। तालाब, नदी, वन, बगीचे सब शोभाहीन हो रहे हैं। नगर बहुत ही भयानक लग रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2742.english_translation: Donkeys and jackals are speaking in inauspicious ways. Hearing them again and again, Bharat feels deep pain. Lakes, rivers, forests, and gardens all seem stripped of beauty; the city itself feels terrifying.
ramacharitamanas::2742.translation_literal: खर (donkeys) / सिआर (jackals) / बोलहिं (speak) / प्रतिकूला (in hostile or inauspicious ways) / सुनि सुनि (hearing again and again) / होइ (becomes) / भरत (Bharat) / मन (mind) / सूला (pierced with pain)॥ / श्रीहत (deprived of beauty) / सर (lakes) / सरिता (rivers) / बन (forests) / बागा (gardens) / नगरु (city) / बिसेषि (especially) / भयावनु (fearful) / लागा (seemed).
ramacharitamanas::2742.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2742.essence: Pain makes even familiar places feel hostile.
ramacharitamanas::2742.simple_meaning: Bharat reaches the city, but every sign around him feels wrong and frightening. The bad omens deepen his pain and make the whole place seem stripped of joy.
ramacharitamanas::2742.simple_insight: Grief can change the way everything looks, even familiar places.
ramacharitamanas::2742.detailed_meaning: Bharat is nearing Ayodhya after days of urgent travel. The land itself seems to warn him: ugly sounds, bad omens, and a city that no longer feels like home. His heart is already wounded, and this sight makes the wound sharper.
ramacharitamanas::2742.modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital waiting room and every fluorescent light feels harsher than before. When your heart is already braced for loss, even ordinary places can feel ominous.
ramacharitamanas::2742.insight: It shows how inner pain colors outer perception, turning beauty into threat.

ramacharitamanas::2743.verse_sanskrit: खग मृग हय गय जाहिं न जोए। राम बियोग कुरोग बिगोए॥ नगर नारि नर निपट दुखारी। मनहुँ सबन्हि सब संपति हारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2743.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के वियोग रूपी बुरे रोग से सताए हुए पक्षी-पशु, घोड़े-हाथी (ऐसे दुःखी हो रहे हैं कि) देखे नहीं जाते। नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष अत्यन्त दुःखी हो रहे हैं। मानो सब अपनी सारी सम्पत्ति हार बैठे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::2743.english_translation: Birds, animals, horses, and elephants look as if they can no longer bear the pain of Ram's separation. The men and women of the city are utterly sorrowful, as if they have lost all their wealth.
ramacharitamanas::2743.translation_literal: खग (birds) / मृग (animals) / हय (horses) / गय (elephants) / जाहिं (go) / न (not) / जोए (seen) / राम (Ram) / बियोग (separation) / कुरोग (disease) / बिगोए (ruined) / नगर (city) / नारि (women) / नर (men) / निपट (utterly) / दुखारी (sorrowful) / मनहुँ (as if) / सबन्हि (all) / सब (all) / संपति (wealth) / हारी (lost)
ramacharitamanas::2743.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2743.essence: Ram's absence makes even the city seem sick with loss.
ramacharitamanas::2743.simple_meaning: Ram's absence weighs so heavily on the city that even the animals seem afflicted, and everyone feels as if they have lost everything.
ramacharitamanas::2743.simple_insight: Separation can make the whole world feel diminished.
ramacharitamanas::2743.detailed_meaning: As Bharat nears Ayodhya, the city itself seems wounded by Ram's exile. Birds, animals, and the people all appear overcome by grief, turning the whole landscape into a mirror of loss.
ramacharitamanas::2743.modern_relevance: You return to a house after a devastating breakup, and even the quiet feels bruised. The room, the street, the familiar faces — everything seems touched by absence.
ramacharitamanas::2743.insight: It turns private grief into a shared atmosphere, so the reader feels how absence reshapes an entire world.

ramacharitamanas::2744.verse_sanskrit: पुरजन मिलहिं न कहहिं कछु गवँहि जोहारहिं जाहिं। भरत कुसल पूँछि न सकहिं भय बिषाद मन माहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2744.verse_hindi: नगर के लोग मिलते हैं, पर कुछ कहते नहीं, गौं से (चुपके से) जोहार (वंदना) करके चले जाते हैं। भरतजी भी किसी से कुशल नहीं पूछ सकते, क्योंकि उनके मन में भय और विषाद छा रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2744.english_translation: The townspeople meet him but say nothing, bowing in silence as they pass. Bharat cannot ask anyone how they are, because fear and sorrow fill his mind.
ramacharitamanas::2744.translation_literal: पुरजन (townspeople) / मिलहिं (meet) / न (not) / कहहिं (say) / कछु (anything) / गवँहि (silently) / जोहारहिं (bow in greeting) / जाहिं (go) / भरत (Bharat) / कुसल (well-being) / पूँछि (asking) / न सकहिं (cannot) / भय (fear) / बिषाद (sorrow) / मन माहिं (in the mind)
ramacharitamanas::2744.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2744.essence: Grief can make even greeting feel like too much.
ramacharitamanas::2744.simple_meaning: The city is so heavy with grief that people only bow to Bharat in silence. Even Bharat cannot bring himself to ask after anyone's well-being.
ramacharitamanas::2744.simple_insight: Shared sorrow can make even simple greetings feel impossible.
ramacharitamanas::2744.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is still reeling from Ram's exile. The townspeople meet Bharat with silent respect, but no one can speak freely. Bharat himself is so overwhelmed by fear and grief that even asking how others are feels out of reach.
ramacharitamanas::2744.modern_relevance: You walk into a house after bad news has spread. Everyone lowers their eyes, offers a quiet nod, and keeps moving. No one has the energy for small talk.
ramacharitamanas::2744.insight: It shows how grief can freeze ordinary human contact, turning even kindness into silence.

ramacharitamanas::2745.verse_sanskrit: हाट बाट नहिं जाइ निहारी। जनु पुर दहँ दिसि लागि दवारी॥ आवत सुत सुनि कैकयनंदिनि। हरषी रबिकुल जलरुह चंदिनि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2745.verse_hindi: बाजार और रास्ते देखे नहीं जाते। मानो नगर में दसों दिशाओं में दावाग्नि लगी है! पुत्र को आते सुनकर सूर्यकुल रूपी कमल के लिए चाँदनी रूपी कैकेयी (बड़ी) हर्षित हुई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2745.english_translation: The market and roads could not be seen, as if a fire had spread in all ten directions through the city. Hearing that her son was coming, Kaikeyi—moonlight for the lotus of the solar dynasty—was overjoyed.
ramacharitamanas::2745.translation_literal: हाट (market) / बाट (roads) / नहिं (not) / जाइ (gone) / निहारी (seen) / जनु (as if) / पुर (city) / दहँ (ten) / दिसि (directions) / लागि (having caught) / दवारी (fire) / आवत (coming) / सुत (son) / सुनि (hearing) / कैकयनंदिनि (Kaikeyi's daughter-in-law / Kaikeyi) / हरषी (became glad) / रबिकुल (solar clan) / जलरुह (lotus) / चंदिनि (moonlight)
ramacharitamanas::2745.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2745.essence: Personal joy can feel cruel inside a shared wound.
ramacharitamanas::2745.simple_meaning: The city feels scorched with grief, and Kaikeyi feels joy at hearing her son is coming home.
ramacharitamanas::2745.simple_insight: One person’s joy can sit beside a whole city’s sorrow without either cancelling the other.
ramacharitamanas::2745.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is still shaken by Ram’s exile. The streets feel unbearable, as if the city itself is burning. In that wounded atmosphere, Kaikeyi hears that her son is coming and feels sudden delight, sharpening the emotional fracture around her.
ramacharitamanas::2745.modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering after a painful breakup, and one person is smiling too brightly because their own news is good. The room can hold both relief and hurt at once.
ramacharitamanas::2745.insight: It shows how private relief can become morally jarring when everyone around you is grieving.

ramacharitamanas::2746.verse_sanskrit: सजि आरती मुदित उठि धाई। द्वारेहिं भेंटि भवन लेइ आई॥ भरत दुखित परिवारु निहारा॥ मानहुँ तुहिन बनज बनु मारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2746.verse_hindi: वह आरती सजाकर आनंद में भरकर उठ दौड़ी और दरवाजे पर ही मिलकर भरत-शत्रुघ्न को महल में ले आई। भरत ने सारे परिवार को दुःखी देखा। मानो कमलों के वन को पाला मार गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2746.english_translation: She quickly arranged an aarti, rose in delight, met him at the door, and brought him into the house. Bharat saw the whole family in sorrow, as if a frost had struck a forest of lotuses.
ramacharitamanas::2746.translation_literal: सजि (having arranged) / आरती (aarti) / मुदित (joyful) / उठि (rising) / धाई (ran quickly) / द्वारेहिं (at the doorway) / भेंटि (meeting) / भवन (house/palace) / लेइ (taking) / आई (brought) / भरत (Bharat) / दुखित (sorrowful) / परिवारु (family) / निहारा (saw) / मानहुँ (as if) / तुहिन (frost) / बनज (lotus) / बनु (forest) / मारा (struck)
ramacharitamanas::2746.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2746.essence: Joy at the door cannot hide grief inside.
ramacharitamanas::2746.simple_meaning: A joyful welcome turns suddenly into grief when Bharat sees the whole family sunk in sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2746.simple_insight: Some arrivals carry joy for one person and heartbreak for everyone else.
ramacharitamanas::2746.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyā, Bharat and Shatrughna arrive after the exile has already broken the royal household. A woman welcomes them with an aarti and brings them inside, but Bharat immediately sees that the family is devastated. The warmth of arrival meets the coldness of grief.
ramacharitamanas::2746.modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering and feel the room go quiet. Someone has tried to welcome you, but the sadness in everyone’s faces is louder than the greeting.
ramacharitamanas::2746.insight: It shifts attention from the welcoming gesture to the deeper emotional wound already filling the home.

ramacharitamanas::2747.verse_sanskrit: कैकेई हरषित एहि भाँती। मनहुँ मुदित दव लाइ किराती॥ सुतिह ससोच देखि मनु मारें। पूँछति नैहर कुसल हमारें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2747.verse_hindi: एक कैकेयी ही इस तरह हर्षित दिखती है मानो भीलनी जंगल में आग लगाकर आनंद में भर रही हो। पुत्र को सोच वश और मन मारे (बहुत उदास) देखकर वह पूछने लगी- हमारे नैहर में कुशल तो है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2747.english_translation: Kaikeyi alone looked delighted, like a forest woman rejoicing after setting the woods ablaze. Seeing her son sorrowful and downcast, she asked, "Is everyone well at my parental home?"
ramacharitamanas::2747.translation_literal: कैकेई (Kaikeyi) / हरषित (delighted) / एहि भाँती (in this way) / मनहुँ (as if) / मुदित (glad) / दव (forest-fire) / लाइ (having set) / किराती (forest woman) / सुतिह (the son) / ससोच (sorrowful) / देखि (seeing) / मनु मारें (with mind struck down) / पूँछति (she asks) / नैहर (parental home) / कुसल (well-being) / हमारें (our)
ramacharitamanas::2747.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2747.essence: Self-centered joy can bloom right beside someone else's grief.
ramacharitamanas::2747.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is the only one who seems pleased. Seeing her son deeply troubled, she asks whether her parental home is doing well.
ramacharitamanas::2747.simple_insight: Some joy is hollow when it rises from another person's pain.
ramacharitamanas::2747.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharata arrives home to a house soaked in grief. Amid the sorrow, Kaikeyi alone appears pleased, while Bharata sits crushed by what has happened. Her question about her parental home reveals the same self-interest driving the exile.
ramacharitamanas::2747.modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering and feel the tension instantly. One person seems oddly pleased while everyone else is hurting, and their concern sounds more like self-protection than care.
ramacharitamanas::2747.insight: It exposes the blindness of desire: a mind fixed on itself can mistake harm for happiness.

ramacharitamanas::2748.verse_sanskrit: सकल कुसल कहि भरत सुनाई। पूँछी निज कुल कुसल भलाई॥ कहु कहँ तात कहाँ सब माता। कहँ सिय राम लखन प्रिय भ्राता ॥
