ramacharitamanas::2748.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने सब कुशल कह सुनाई। फिर अपने कुल की कुशल-क्षेम पूछी। (भरतजी ने कहा-) कहो, पिताजी कहाँ हैं? मेरी सब माताएँ कहाँ हैं? सीताजी और मेरे प्यारे भाई राम-लक्ष्मण कहाँ हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2748.english_translation: Bharat first asked after everyone's well-being, then asked about his own family: "Where is my father? Where are all my mothers? Where are Sita, Ram, and my dear brother Lakshman?"
ramacharitamanas::2748.translation_literal: सकल (all) / कुसल (well-being) / कहि (having said) / भरत (Bharat) / सुनाई (made heard) / पूँछी (asked) / निज (own) / कुल (family/lineage) / कुसल (well-being) / भलाई (goodness) / कहु (tell) / कहँ (where) / तात (father) / कहाँ (where) / सब (all) / माता (mothers) / कहँ (where) / सिय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / प्रिय (dear) / भ्राता (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::2748.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2748.essence: Love asks after everyone else before it asks for itself.
ramacharitamanas::2748.simple_meaning: Bharat speaks with care and respect, asking first about everyone's welfare and then about his father, mothers, Sita, Ram, and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::2748.simple_insight: True concern begins by remembering everyone, not just yourself.
ramacharitamanas::2748.detailed_meaning: Bharat has just arrived at Ayodhya and sees grief everywhere. Before asking anything about himself, he asks after the well-being of the whole family. His questions reveal love, humility, and the ache of separation from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2748.modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital waiting room and ask about everyone else before mentioning your own pain. That instinct — to care first, to inquire gently — is Bharat's.
ramacharitamanas::2748.insight: It shifts attention from personal urgency to relational care and respectful inquiry.

ramacharitamanas::2749.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुत बचन सनेहमय कपट नीर भरि नैन। भरत श्रवन मन सूल सम पापिनि बोली बैन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2749.verse_hindi: पुत्र के स्नेहमय वचन सुनकर नेत्रों में कपट का जल भरकर पापिनी कैकेयी भरत के कानों में और मन में शूल के समान चुभने वाले वचन बोली- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2749.english_translation: Hearing her son's affectionate words, Kaikeyi filled her eyes with deceptive tears and spoke words to Bharata that pierced his ears and heart like a thorn.
ramacharitamanas::2749.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुत (son's) / बचन (words) / सनेहमय (full of affection) / कपट (deceit) / नीर (water/tears) / भरि (filling) / नैन (eyes) / भरत (Bharata's) / श्रवन (ears) / मन (mind) / सूल (thorn) / सम (like) / पापिनि (sinful woman) / बोली (spoke) / बैन (words)
ramacharitamanas::2749.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2749.essence: Deceptive tenderness can wound more sharply than open anger.
ramacharitamanas::2749.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi hears Bharata's loving words, but answers with false tears and painful words that wound him deeply.
ramacharitamanas::2749.simple_insight: A loving moment can be twisted by deceit, and the wound reaches both the heart and the ears.
ramacharitamanas::2749.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharata returns home speaking with love and concern. Kaikeyi hears him, hides her intent behind tears, and answers with words meant to sting. This is the moment her deception cuts into Bharata's trust.
ramacharitamanas::2749.modern_relevance: You finally speak gently to someone you love, and they answer with polished concern that feels strangely cold. The smile is there, but something in the words lands like a blade.
ramacharitamanas::2749.insight: It reveals how false emotion can disguise harmful intent and hurt trust at the very moment affection is expected.

ramacharitamanas::2750.verse_sanskrit: तात बात मैं सकल सँवारी। भै मंथरा सहाय बिचारी॥ कछुक काज बिधि बीच बिगारेउ। भूपति सुरपति पुर पगु धारेउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2750.verse_hindi: हे तात! मैंने सारी बात बना ली थी। बेचारी मंथरा सहायक हुई। पर विधाता ने बीच में जरा सा काम बिगाड़ दिया। वह यह कि राजा देवलोक को पधार गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2750.english_translation: Father, I had arranged everything. Poor Manthara helped me. But fate spoiled a small part of it in between: the king has gone to the higher realm.
ramacharitamanas::2750.translation_literal: तात (father) / बात (matter) / मैं (I) / सकल (all) / सँवारी (set right, arranged) / भै (became) / मंथरा (Manthara) / सहाय (helper) / बिचारी (poor, unfortunate) / कछुक (some) / काज (task, matter) / बिधि (fate, the ordering power) / बीच (in the middle) / बिगारेउ (spoiled) / भूपति (king) / सुरपति (lord of the radiant beings) / पुर (city) / पगु (feet) / धारेउ (placed, set)
ramacharitamanas::2750.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2750.essence: A single disruption can undo a carefully arranged plan.
ramacharitamanas::2750.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi says she had everything arranged, but fate interrupted and Dasharath has died. The verse is part of her explanation, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::2750.simple_insight: Even careful plans can collapse in one unexpected moment.
ramacharitamanas::2750.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi speaks after the exile bargain has taken effect and Dasharath is gone. She tells Bharat she had things arranged, blames Manthara's help, and then admits that the king has passed into the higher realm. The verse is a link in the chain of grief.
ramacharitamanas::2750.modern_relevance: You think the plan is settled, the messages are sent, and the meeting is confirmed — then one call changes everything. This verse sits inside that sudden collapse.
ramacharitamanas::2750.insight: It shows how quickly control slips away, turning a planned outcome into loss.

ramacharitamanas::2751.verse_sanskrit: सुनत भरतु भए बिबस बिषादा। जनु सहमेउ करि केहरि नादा॥ तात तात हा तात पुकारी। परे भूमितल ब्याकुल भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2751.verse_hindi: भरत यह सुनते ही विषाद के मारे विवश (बेहाल) हो गए। मानो सिंह की गर्जना सुनकर हाथी सहम गया हो। वे 'तात! तात! हा तात!' पुकारते हुए अत्यन्त व्याकुल होकर जमीन पर गिर पड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::2751.english_translation: Hearing this, Bharat was overcome by grief, as if a lion’s roar had startled an elephant. Crying, “Father! Father! Ah, father!” he fell to the ground in deep anguish.
ramacharitamanas::2751.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / भरतु (Bharat) / भए (became) / बिबस (helpless) / बिषादा (with grief) / जनु (as if) / सहमेउ (was startled) / करि (by) / केहरि (lion) / नादा (roar) / तात (father) / तात (father) / हा (alas) / तात (father) / पुकारी (calling) / परे (fell) / भूमितल (to the ground) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / भारी (greatly)
ramacharitamanas::2751.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2751.essence: Grief can strike so hard that the body falls before the mind understands.
ramacharitamanas::2751.simple_meaning: Bharat is shattered by the news and collapses in grief, calling out for his father in helpless anguish.
ramacharitamanas::2751.simple_insight: Some losses hit so hard they leave you unable to stand, think, or speak clearly.
ramacharitamanas::2751.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat hears the truth about Dasharath’s death and the broken promise around Ram’s exile. The shock hits him like a physical blow. He cries for his father and falls to the ground, showing grief before any words of explanation can begin.
ramacharitamanas::2751.modern_relevance: You open a message and your body goes cold before your mind can catch up. Some news doesn't arrive as information — it arrives as collapse.
ramacharitamanas::2751.insight: It shows grief as a full-body reaction, not a polished emotion.

ramacharitamanas::2752.verse_sanskrit: चलत न देखन पायउँ तोही। तात न रामहि सौंपेहु मोही॥ बहुरि धीर धरि उठे सँभारी। कहु पितु मरन हेतु महतारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2752.verse_hindi: (और विलाप करने लगे कि) हे तात! मैं आपको (स्वर्ग के लिए) चलते समय देख भी न सका। (हाय!) आप मुझे श्री रामजी को सौंप भी नहीं गए! फिर धीरज धरकर वे सम्हलकर उठे और बोले- माता! पिता के मरने का कारण तो बताओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2752.english_translation: “I never got to see you leave, dear father. You never handed me over to Ram. Then, gathering himself, he rose and said, ‘Mother, tell me the reason for my father’s death.’”
ramacharitamanas::2752.translation_literal: चलत (while departing) / न (not) / देखन (to see) / पायउँ (I was able) / तोही (you) / तात (dear father) / न (not) / रामहि (to Ram) / सौंपेहु (you handed over) / मोही (me) / बहुरि (again) / धीर (steadiness) / धरि (having held) / उठे (rose) / सँभारी (gathering himself) / कहु (tell) / पितु (father) / मरन (death) / हेतु (reason) / महतारी (mother)
ramacharitamanas::2752.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2752.essence: Loss first breaks the heart; then it demands an explanation.
ramacharitamanas::2752.simple_meaning: Bharat grieves that he could not see his father’s final departure and that Dasharath did not entrust him to Ram. After steadying himself, he asks Kaikeyi why his father died.
ramacharitamanas::2752.simple_insight: Grief can make you ask the hardest question only after you’ve gathered yourself again.
ramacharitamanas::2752.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has died, and Bharat is shattered by the loss. In the middle of his lament, he mourns missing his father’s final moment and the lost chance to be placed under Ram’s care. Then he steadies himself and turns to Kaikeyi for the cause of the king’s death.
ramacharitamanas::2752.modern_relevance: You miss the last call, the last message, the last chance to say goodbye. Later, after the shock settles, you finally ask the question you were avoiding: what happened?
ramacharitamanas::2752.insight: It shows grief moving from raw lament to a search for cause and responsibility.

ramacharitamanas::2753.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुत बचन कहति कैकेई। मरमु पाँछि जनु माहुर देई॥ आदिहु तें सब आपनि करनी। कुटिल कठोर मुदित मन बरनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2753.verse_hindi: पुत्र का वचन सुनकर कैकेयी कहने लगी। मानो मर्म स्थान को पाछकर (चाकू से चीरकर) उसमें जहर भर रही हो। कुटिल और कठोर कैकेयी ने अपनी सब करनी शुरू से (आखिर तक बड़े) प्रसन्न मन से सुना दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2753.english_translation: Hearing her son’s words, Kaikeyi began to speak. It was as if she were stabbing the wound and pouring poison into it. Crooked, harsh Kaikeyi recounted all her deeds from the very beginning with a pleased mind.
ramacharitamanas::2753.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुत (son) / बचन (words) / कहति (speaking) / कैकेई (Kaikeyi) / मरमु (wound, tender spot) / पाँछि (after piercing) / जनु (as if) / माहुर (poison) / देई (giving) / आदिहु तें (from the beginning) / सब (all) / आपनि (her own) / करनी (deeds) / कुटिल (crooked) / कठोर (harsh) / मुदित (pleased) / मन (mind) / बरनी (described, recounted)
ramacharitamanas::2753.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2753.essence: Pride can make you poison your own wound.
ramacharitamanas::2753.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi calmly repeats the very actions that caused the disaster, as if she has no tenderness left in her heart.
ramacharitamanas::2753.simple_insight: A mind caught in its own desire can wound without even flinching.
ramacharitamanas::2753.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is shattered by news of Dasharath’s death and Ram’s exile. Kaikeyi answers his pain not with remorse but with a cold, pleased account of her own actions. The scene exposes how desire can harden a person against their own conscience.
ramacharitamanas::2753.modern_relevance: Someone in a family argument keeps replaying old choices with a strange pride, making the hurt deeper each time. The verse captures that chilling lack of self-awareness.
ramacharitamanas::2753.insight: It shows how the unexamined mind can keep justifying harm instead of seeing it clearly.

ramacharitamanas::2754.verse_sanskrit: भरतहि बिसरेउ पितु मरन सुनत राम बन गौनु। हेतु अपनपउ जानि जियँ थकित रहे धरि मौनु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2754.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का वन जाना सुनकर भरतजी को पिता का मरण भूल गया और हृदय में इस सारे अनर्थ का कारण अपने को ही जानकर वे मौन होकर स्तम्भित रह गए (अर्थात उनकी बोली बंद हो गई और वे सन्न रह गए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2754.english_translation: Hearing that Ram had gone to the forest, Bharat forgot his father's death and stood silent, realizing in his heart that he himself was the cause of this disaster.
ramacharitamanas::2754.translation_literal: भरतहि (to Bharat) / बिसरेउ (was forgotten) / पितु मरन (father's death) / सुनत (hearing) / राम बन गौनु (Ram's going to the forest) / हेतु (cause) / अपनपउ (own self) / जानि (knowing) / जियँ (in heart) / थकित (weary, stunned) / रहे (remained) / धरि मौनु (holding silence)
ramacharitamanas::2754.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2754.essence: Guilt can make even grief disappear.
ramacharitamanas::2754.simple_meaning: Bharat is so shocked by Ram's exile that even his father's death fades from his mind. He blames himself and falls silent.
ramacharitamanas::2754.simple_insight: Guilt can silence you more than grief. Sometimes the heart freezes when it thinks it caused the wound.
ramacharitamanas::2754.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace is collapsing under grief and blame. Bharat hears that Ram has gone to the forest and is struck numb. Even Dasharath's death recedes as he feels himself to be the source of this ruin.
ramacharitamanas::2754.modern_relevance: You read the message that changed everything, and your first thought is, 'This is my fault.' The room goes quiet, and even your own pain feels secondary.
ramacharitamanas::2754.insight: It shifts attention from outward loss to inward responsibility, showing how guilt can eclipse every other feeling.

ramacharitamanas::2755.verse_sanskrit: बिकल बिलोकि सुतहि समुझावति। मनहुँ जरे पर लोनु लगावति॥ तात राउ नहिं सोचै जोगू। बिढ़इ सुकृत जसु कीन्हेउ भोगू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2755.verse_hindi: पुत्र को व्याकुल देखकर कैकेयी समझाने लगी। मानो जले पर नमक लगा रही हो। (वह बोली-) हे तात! राजा सोच करने योग्य नहीं हैं। उन्होंने पुण्य और यश कमाकर उसका पर्याप्त भोग किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2755.english_translation: Seeing her son agitated, Kaikeyi tried to console him, as if rubbing salt into a burn. She said, “Dear child, a king is not meant for sorrow. He has already enjoyed the full fruit of his merit and fame.”
ramacharitamanas::2755.translation_literal: बिकल (agitated) / बिलोकि (seeing) / सुतहि (the son) / समुझावति (she consoles) / मनहुँ (as if) / जरे (burned) / पर (on) / लोनु (salt) / लगावति (she applies) / तात (dear child) / राउ (the king) / नहिं (not) / सोचै (for sorrow) / जोगू (fit) / बिढ़इ (already) / सुकृत (merit) / जसु (fame) / कीन्हेउ (he did) / भोगू (enjoyment)
ramacharitamanas::2755.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2755.essence: Words meant to soothe can cut deeper than silence.
ramacharitamanas::2755.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi comforts her son by saying that a king should not grieve and has already received the reward of his good deeds and fame.
ramacharitamanas::2755.simple_insight: Sometimes comfort can deepen pain when it ignores what the heart is actually carrying.
ramacharitamanas::2755.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kaikeyi sees Bharat shaken by the news of Ram's exile and Dasharath's death. Instead of easing his grief, she speaks in a way that only sharpens it, trying to justify the king's life as already complete.
ramacharitamanas::2755.modern_relevance: Someone tells you to “move on” five minutes after your world has cracked. The words may be neat, but they can land like salt on an open wound.
ramacharitamanas::2755.insight: It shows how misplaced consolation can feel cruel when someone is grieving.

ramacharitamanas::2756.verse_sanskrit: जीवत सकल जनम फल पाए। अंत अमरपति सदन सिधाए॥ अस अनुमानि सोच परिहरहू। सहित समाज राज पुर करहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2756.verse_hindi: जीवनकाल में ही उन्होंने जन्म लेने के सम्पूर्ण फल पा लिए और अंत में वे इन्द्रलोक को चले गए। ऐसा विचारकर सोच छोड़ दो और समाज सहित नगर का राज्य करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2756.english_translation: They had already reaped the full fruit of life, and in the end they went to the abode of Indra. Thinking this way, let go of sorrow and, with the assembly, govern the city and kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::2756.translation_literal: जीवत (while living) / सकल (all) / जनम (births) / फल (fruit) / पाए (obtained) / अंत (at the end) / अमरपति (lord of the immortals) / सदन (abode) / सिधाए (departed) / अस (thus) / अनुमानि (having considered) / सोच (sorrow) / परिहरहू (let go) / सहित (together with) / समाज (assembly) / राज (kingdom) / पुर (city) / करहू (do)
ramacharitamanas::2756.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2756.essence: Loss can be honored without letting it stop your duty.
ramacharitamanas::2756.simple_meaning: The speaker says the dead king and queen had already lived a fulfilled life, so grief should be set aside and the kingdom should be managed with the people.
ramacharitamanas::2756.simple_insight: Grief does not have to erase responsibility. You can honor loss and still keep going.
ramacharitamanas::2756.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi tries to steady Bharat after Dasharath’s death and Ram’s exile have shattered the family. She argues that the departed have completed their lives, so sorrow should be put aside and the city should still be governed.
ramacharitamanas::2756.modern_relevance: After the funeral, someone still has to answer the phone, feed the children, and sign the papers. This verse speaks to the hard dignity of carrying on without pretending the loss did not happen.
ramacharitamanas::2756.insight: It shifts the mind from being swallowed by grief to meeting the next duty with steadiness.

ramacharitamanas::2757.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुठि सहमेउ राजकुमारू। पाकें छत जनु लाग अँगारू॥ धीरज धरि भरि लेहिं उसासा। पापिनि सबहि भाँति कुल नासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2757.verse_hindi: राजकुमार भरतजी यह सुनकर बहुत ही सहम गए। मानो पके घाव पर अँगार छू गया हो। उन्होंने धीरज धरकर बड़ी लम्बी साँस लेते हुए कहा- पापिनी! तूने सभी तरह से कुल का नाश कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2757.english_translation: Hearing this, the prince was deeply shaken, as if a spark had touched a healed wound. Gathering himself, he let out a long breath and said, 'Wicked woman, you have ruined the whole family in every way.'
ramacharitamanas::2757.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुठि (very much) / सहमेउ (was shaken) / राजकुमारू (the prince) । / पाकें (on a healed) / छत (wound) / जनु (as if) / लाग (touched) / अँगारू (a spark of fire) ॥ / धीरज (patience / composure) / धरि (holding) / भरि (filled) / लेहिं (he took) / उसासा (a long breath) । / पापिनि (wicked woman) / सबहि भाँति (in every way) / कुल (the family line) / नासा (destroyed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2757.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2757.essence: A hidden betrayal can strike like fire on old pain.
ramacharitamanas::2757.simple_meaning: Bharat is stunned by Kaikeyi’s words and struggles to steady himself before accusing her of destroying the family.
ramacharitamanas::2757.simple_insight: Some wounds are not physical; betrayal can make even a calm heart gasp.
ramacharitamanas::2757.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi’s demands have just become clear. Bharat hears the truth and is shaken to the core, as if fire touched a healed injury. He gathers himself, breathes deeply, and lashes out at the woman whose actions have shattered his family.
ramacharitamanas::2757.modern_relevance: You open a message and feel your stomach drop. Before you even speak, you know something precious has been broken.
ramacharitamanas::2757.insight: It shows how sudden betrayal can overwhelm composure and force the truth into speech.

ramacharitamanas::2758.verse_sanskrit: जौं पै कुरुचि रही अति तोही। जनमत काहे न मारे मोही॥ पेड़ काटि तैं पालउ सींचा। मीन जिअन निति बारि उलीचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2758.verse_hindi: हाय! यदि तेरी ऐसी ही अत्यन्त बुरी रुचि (दुष्ट इच्छा) थी, तो तूने जन्मते ही मुझे मार क्यों नहीं डाला? तूने पेड़ को काटकर पत्ते को सींचा है और मछली के जीने के लिए पानी को उलीच डाला! (अर्थात मेरा हित करने जाकर उलटा तूने मेरा अहित कर डाला) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2758.english_translation: If your heart was so cruel, why didn't you kill me at birth? You cut the tree and watered the leaves, and you spilled water for a fish to live!
ramacharitamanas::2758.translation_literal: जौं (if) / पै (indeed) / कुरुचि (cruel intention) / रही (remained) / अति (very much) / तोही (in you) / जनमत (at birth) / काहे (why) / न (not) / मारे (killed) / मोही (me) / पेड़ (tree) / काटि (cutting) / तैं (you) / पालउ (leaf) / सींचा (watered) / मीन (fish) / जिअन (to live) / निति (always) / बारि (water) / उलीचा (spilled out)
ramacharitamanas::2758.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2758.essence: Good intentions become cruelty when they destroy what they meant to protect.
ramacharitamanas::2758.simple_meaning: Bharat, overwhelmed by grief, says his mother’s actions were meant to help but only harmed him. He feels her care has brought the opposite of what she intended.
ramacharitamanas::2758.simple_insight: Love can feel unbearable when it arrives through the wrong hands.
ramacharitamanas::2758.detailed_meaning: Bharat has just learned how Kaikeyi's demands drove Ram into exile and broke Dasharath's heart. In shock and pain, he turns on his mother, saying her supposed care has done the opposite of care.
ramacharitamanas::2758.modern_relevance: You hear a parent say, 'I did this for your future,' but the result is wreckage. In that moment, intention means nothing beside the wound left behind.
ramacharitamanas::2758.insight: It exposes how misplaced care can become harm, and how grief speaks in bitter images.

ramacharitamanas::2759.verse_sanskrit: हंसबंसु दसरथु जनकु राम लखन से भाइ। जननी तूँ जननी भई बिधि सन कछु न बसाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2759.verse_hindi: मुझे सूर्यवंश (सा वंश), दशरथजी (सरीखे) पिता और राम-लक्ष्मण से भाई मिले। पर हे जननी! मुझे जन्म देने वाली माता तू हुई! (क्या किया जाए!) विधाता से कुछ भी वश नहीं चलता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2759.english_translation: I was born into the solar lineage, with Dasharath as father and Ram and Lakshman as brothers. But, mother, you were the one who gave me birth. What can be done when fate itself does not obey anyone?
ramacharitamanas::2759.translation_literal: हंसबंसु (solar lineage) / दसरथु (Dasharath) / जनकु (father) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / से (like) / भाइ (brothers) / जननी (mother) / तूँ (you) / जननी (mother) / भई (became) / बिधि (fate) / सन (with) / कछु (anything) / न (not) / बसाइ (stays in control)
ramacharitamanas::2759.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2759.essence: Even a blessed life can be shattered by one painful choice.
ramacharitamanas::2759.simple_meaning: Bharat says he was blessed with the best family, but his real pain is that his mother caused the exile. He ends by saying no one can control what fate allows.
ramacharitamanas::2759.simple_insight: Love and grief can sit in the same sentence, and neither makes the other smaller.
ramacharitamanas::2759.detailed_meaning: Bharat has just learned that Kaikeyi's demand has sent Ram into exile. Shocked and wounded, he turns toward his mother and speaks with bitter clarity: he has Ram and Lakshman as brothers, Dasharath as father, yet the same mother who gave him life has broken his world.
ramacharitamanas::2759.modern_relevance: You find out, after the family argument, that the person you trusted most helped trigger the damage. In that moment, gratitude and betrayal can exist side by side.
ramacharitamanas::2759.insight: It captures the ache of betrayal inside a loving family and the helplessness of watching events move beyond your control.

ramacharitamanas::2760.verse_sanskrit: जब मैं कुमति कुमत जियँ ठयऊ। खंड खंड होइ हृदउ न गयऊ॥ बर मागत मन भइ नहिं पीरा। गरि न जीह मुँह परेउ न कीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2760.verse_hindi: अरी कुमति! जब तूने हृदय में यह बुरा विचार (निश्चय) ठाना, उसी समय तेरे हृदय के टुकड़े-टुकड़े (क्यों) न हो गए? वरदान माँगते समय तेरे मन में कुछ भी पीड़ा नहीं हुई? तेरी जीभ गल नहीं गई? तेरे मुँह में कीड़े नहीं पड़ गए? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2760.english_translation: When I formed such evil intent in my heart, why did my heart not split apart? When I asked for the boon, why did my mind feel no pain? Why did my tongue not rot, and why did worms not fall into my mouth?
ramacharitamanas::2760.translation_literal: जब (when) / मैं (I) / कुमति (evil intent) / कुमत (bad thought) / जियँ (in the heart) / ठयऊ (was set) / खंड खंड (pieces and pieces) / होइ (becoming) / हृदउ (heart) / न (not) / गयऊ (went)॥ / बर (boon) / मागत (asking) / मन (mind) / भइ (became) / नहिं (not) / पीरा (pain) / गरि (rotted) / न (not) / जीह (tongue) / मुँह (mouth) / परेउ (fell) / न (not) / कीरा (worms) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2760.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2760.essence: A wrong intention can feel so vile that the heart itself should reject it.
ramacharitamanas::2760.simple_meaning: The speaker curses a cruel thought and says it should have destroyed the heart, mind, tongue, and mouth the moment it arose.
ramacharitamanas::2760.simple_insight: Some choices feel so wrong that they seem to deserve immediate punishment.
ramacharitamanas::2760.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi’s harsh decision has already broken the royal family. The speaker turns on that inner corruption itself, blaming the moment the bad intention took shape and wishing the body had rejected it at once.
ramacharitamanas::2760.modern_relevance: You send the text, then stare at the screen wishing you could pull it back. The regret hits after the damage is done, not before.
ramacharitamanas::2760.insight: It exposes how a single poisoned intention can feel unbearable once its consequences begin.

ramacharitamanas::2761.verse_sanskrit: भूपँ प्रतीति तोरि किमि कीन्ही। मरन काल बिधि मति हरि लीन्ही॥ बिधिहुँ न नारि हृदय गति जानी। सकल कपट अघ अवगुन खानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2761.verse_hindi: राजा ने तेरा विश्वास कैसे कर लिया? (जान पड़ता है,) विधाता ने मरने के समय उनकी बुद्धि हर ली थी। स्त्रियों के हृदय की गति (चाल) विधाता भी नहीं जान सके। वह सम्पूर्ण कपट, पाप और अवगुणों की खान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2761.english_translation: How did the king come to trust you? At the time of death, fate took away his judgment. Even fate could not understand a woman's heart. It is a mine of deceit, fault, and flaws.
ramacharitamanas::2761.translation_literal: भूपँ (the king) / प्रतीति (trust) / तोरि (your) / किमि (how) / कीन्ही (did [he] make)॥ / मरन काल (at the time of death) / बिधि (fate) / मति (judgment) / हरि (took away) / लीन्ही (took)॥ / बिधिहुँ (even fate) / न (not) / नारि (woman) / हृदय गति (movement of the heart) / जानी (knew) / सकल (all) / कपट (deceit) / अघ (fault) / अवगुन (flaws) / खानी (mine)॥
ramacharitamanas::2761.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2761.essence: Fear and blame can disguise themselves as certainty.
ramacharitamanas::2761.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi blames the king’s trust and questions the nature of women’s hearts, calling them full of deceit and flaws.
ramacharitamanas::2761.simple_insight: It shows how wounded minds turn suspicion into certainty.
ramacharitamanas::2761.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi justifies the damage she has caused by attacking the king’s trust and dismissing the nature of women. The verse is part of her defensive argument, not a calm truth.
ramacharitamanas::2761.modern_relevance: After a family argument, someone starts rewriting the whole story to make themselves look right. Old hurt turns into harsh generalisations, and the real issue gets buried.
ramacharitamanas::2761.insight: It shifts attention from the claim itself to the mind that is trying to protect itself through blame.

ramacharitamanas::2762.verse_sanskrit: सरल सुसील धरम रत राऊ। सो किमि जानै तीय सुभाऊ॥ अस को जीव जंतु जग माहीं। जेहि रघुनाथ प्रानप्रिय नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2762.verse_hindi: फिर राजा तो सीधे, सुशील और धर्मपरायण थे। वे भला, स्त्री स्वभाव को कैसे जानते? अरे, जगत के जीव-जन्तुओं में ऐसा कौन है, जिसे श्री रघुनाथजी प्राणों के समान प्यारे नहीं हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2762.english_translation: The king was simple, virtuous, and devoted to dharma. How could he understand a woman's nature? And who in the world is not dear to Raghunath as life itself?
ramacharitamanas::2762.translation_literal: सरल (simple) / सुसील (virtuous) / धरम रत (devoted to dharma) / राऊ (king) / सो (so) / किमि (how) / जानै (would know) / तीय सुभाऊ (a woman's nature) / अस (such) / को (who) / जीव जंतु (living beings) / जग माहीं (in the world) / जेहि (whom) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / प्रानप्रिय (dear as life) / नाहीं (is not)
ramacharitamanas::2762.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2762.essence: A virtuous heart can still miss deception, while Ram is universally beloved.
ramacharitamanas::2762.simple_meaning: Dasharath was gentle, virtuous, and devoted to dharma, so he could not understand Kaikeyi's mind. At the same time, Ram is dear to every living being.
ramacharitamanas::2762.simple_insight: A good heart can still be blind to manipulation, while Ram remains dear to all.
ramacharitamanas::2762.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the tragedy is now clear: Dasharath was honest and dharma-minded, so he could not read Kaikeyi's hidden intent. The verse also widens the scene by reminding us that Ram is beloved by every living being, making the coming rupture feel even more painful.
ramacharitamanas::2762.modern_relevance: You trusted someone because they always seemed decent, and only later saw how little they understood the person beside them. At the same time, some people are simply loved by everyone who meets them.
ramacharitamanas::2762.insight: It shifts you from judging only character to noticing how innocence can miss what is hiding in plain sight.

ramacharitamanas::2763.verse_sanskrit: भे अति अहित रामु तेउ तोहीं। को तू अहसि सत्य कहु मोही॥ जो हसि सो हसि मुँह मसि लाई। आँखि ओट उठि बैठहि जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2763.verse_hindi: वे श्री रामजी भी तुझे अहित हो गए (वैरी लगे)! तू कौन है? मुझे सच-सच कह! तू जो है, सो है, अब मुँह में स्याही पोतकर (मुँह काला करके) उठकर मेरी आँखों की ओट में जा बैठ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2763.english_translation: Even Ram has become your enemy. Who are you? Tell me the truth. You are what you are—go blacken your face and sit out of sight.
ramacharitamanas::2763.translation_literal: भे (became) / अति (very) / अहित (enemy, harmful) / रामु (Ram) / तेउ (also) / तोहीं (to you) / को (who) / तू (you) / अहसि (are) / सत्य (truth) / कहु (tell) / मोही (to me) / जो (whatever) / हसि (you are) / सो (that) / हसि (you are) / मुँह (face, mouth) / मसि (ink, blackening) / लाई (apply) / आँखि (eye) / ओट (out of sight) / उठि (getting up) / बैठहि (sit) / जाई (go)
ramacharitamanas::2763.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2763.essence: Mockery erupts when truth is too painful to face.
ramacharitamanas::2763.simple_meaning: The speaker is mocking someone as a liar and enemy of Ram, demanding the person admit the truth and disappear from sight.
ramacharitamanas::2763.simple_insight: Pride can turn into humiliation when someone is exposed as false.
ramacharitamanas::2763.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the speaker lashes out in bitter contempt after feeling betrayed and cornered by the truth of Ram’s exile. This is not a teaching verse but a sharp emotional outburst, part of a larger argument about blame, deception, and shame.
ramacharitamanas::2763.modern_relevance: A heated argument spills into insults, and suddenly the real issue is buried under mockery. The verse captures how quickly wounded pride turns truth into attack.
ramacharitamanas::2763.insight: It shows how anger tries to punish dishonesty by shaming the person instead of resolving the wound.

ramacharitamanas::2764.verse_sanskrit: राम बिरोधी हृदय तें प्रगट कीन्ह बिधि मोहि। मो समान को पातकी बादि कहउँ कछु तोहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2764.verse_hindi: विधाता ने मुझे श्री रामजी से विरोध करने वाले (तेरे) हृदय से उत्पन्न किया (अथवा विधाता ने मुझे हृदय से राम का विरोधी जाहिर कर दिया।) मेरे बराबर पापी दूसरा कौन है? मैं व्यर्थ ही तुझे कुछ कहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2764.english_translation: The creator made me from a heart opposed to Ram. Who is as sinful as I am? I speak to you in vain.
ramacharitamanas::2764.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बिरोधी (opposed to) / हृदय (heart) / तें (from) / प्रगट (made manifest) / कीन्ह (made) / बिधि (the creator) / मोहि (me) / मो (my) / समान (equal) / को (who) / पातकी (sinful one) / बादि (in vain) / कहउँ (I speak) / कछु (something) / तोहि (to you)
ramacharitamanas::2764.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2764.essence: Self-condemnation is the first honest response to betraying Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2764.simple_meaning: The speaker says he was brought forth from a heart that opposes Ram, and that no one is as blameworthy as he is.
ramacharitamanas::2764.simple_insight: Shame can make a person see their own fault with painful honesty.
ramacharitamanas::2764.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court’s grief and accusation are rising after Ram’s exile. The speaker turns inward and calls himself the worst offender, saying even speaking further is pointless because his own heart has become the proof of guilt.
ramacharitamanas::2764.modern_relevance: You realize, mid-argument, that your own resistance caused the mess. The urge to defend yourself drops, and all that remains is honest regret.
ramacharitamanas::2764.insight: It shifts blame outward into self-recognition, where remorse becomes more important than argument.

ramacharitamanas::2765.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सत्रुघुन मातु कुटिलाई। जरहिं गात रिस कछु न बसाई॥ तेहि अवसर कुबरी तहँ आई। बसन बिभूषन बिबिध बनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2765.verse_hindi: माता की कुटिलता सुनकर शत्रुघ्नजी के सब अंग क्रोध से जल रहे हैं, पर कुछ वश नहीं चलता। उसी समय भाँति-भाँति के कपड़ों और गहनों से सजकर कुबरी (मंथरा) वहाँ आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2765.english_translation: Hearing of the queen's crookedness, Shatrughna's body burned with anger, but he could not control it. At that moment, Kubri came there dressed in many kinds of clothes and ornaments.
ramacharitamanas::2765.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सत्रुघुन (Shatrughna) / मातु (mother/queen) / कुटिलाई (crookedness) / जरहिं (are burning) / गात (limbs/body) / रिस (anger) / कछु (some) / न (not) / बसाई (under control) ॥ / तेहि (that) / अवसर (moment) / कुबरी (Kubri/Manthara) / तहँ (there) / आई (came) / बसन (clothes) / बिभूषन (ornaments) / बिबिध (various) / बनाई (made/donned) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2765.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2765.essence: Anger rises first; action comes only when the next spark arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2765.simple_meaning: Shatrughna hears of the queen's deceit and burns with anger. Before he can act, Manthara arrives dressed up in ornaments.
ramacharitamanas::2765.simple_insight: Anger can flare instantly, but it still needs a moment before it becomes action.
ramacharitamanas::2765.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the news of Kaikeyi's crookedness reaches Shatrughna. He is furious, but still restrained by the moment. Then Manthara arrives, dressed in ornaments, setting up the next surge of conflict.
ramacharitamanas::2765.modern_relevance: You hear a betrayal in the middle of the day, and your whole body tightens before you even speak. The next person walking in can either calm the room or ignite it further.
ramacharitamanas::2765.insight: It shows the instant when outrage gathers force, but the scene is still waiting to explode.

ramacharitamanas::2766.verse_sanskrit: लखि रिस भरेउ लखन लघु भाई। बरत अनल घृत आहुति पाई॥ हुमगि लात तकि कूबर मारा। परि मुँह भर महि करत पुकारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2766.verse_hindi: उसे (सजी) देखकर लक्ष्मण के छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्नजी क्रोध में भर गए। मानो जलती हुई आग को घी की आहुति मिल गई हो। उन्होंने जोर से तककर कूबड़ पर एक लात जमा दी। वह चिल्लाती हुई मुँह के बल जमीन पर गिर पड़ी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2766.english_translation: Seeing her, Lakshman’s younger brother was filled with rage, like fire meeting a fresh offering of ghee. He sprang up, aimed a kick at her hump, and she fell face-first, crying out.
ramacharitamanas::2766.translation_literal: लखि (seeing) / रिस (rage) / भरेउ (was filled) / लखन (Lakshman's) / लघु भाई (younger brother) / बरत (burning) / अनल (fire) / घृत (ghee) / आहुति (offering) / पाई (having received) / हुमगि (springing up) / लात (kick) / तकि (aiming) / कूबर (hump) / मारा (struck) / परि (fell) / मुँह भर (face-first) / महि (on the ground) / करत (doing) / पुकारा (cried out)
ramacharitamanas::2766.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2766.essence: Rage, once fed, moves faster than thought.
ramacharitamanas::2766.simple_meaning: Shatrughna’s anger flares at the sight of the hunchback woman, and he kicks her down in a burst of rage.
ramacharitamanas::2766.simple_insight: Uncontrolled anger can turn a moment into needless harm.
ramacharitamanas::2766.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Manthara’s crooked scheming has already poisoned the court. When Shatrughna sees her, his anger surges instantly and he strikes her down. The verse is a burst of reaction, not a teaching in itself.
ramacharitamanas::2766.modern_relevance: You read one cruel message and your body is already hot, your fingers already moving. In that split second, damage can happen before thought returns.
ramacharitamanas::2766.insight: It shows how quickly resentment becomes action when anger is left unchecked.

ramacharitamanas::2767.verse_sanskrit: कूबर टूटेउ फूट कपारू। दलित दसन मुख रुधिर प्रचारू॥ आह दइअ मैं काह नसावा। करत नीक फलु अनइस पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2767.verse_hindi: उसका कूबड़ टूट गया, कपाल फूट गया, दाँत टूट गए और मुँह से खून बहने लगा। (वह कराहती हुई बोली-) हाय दैव! मैंने क्या बिगाड़ा? जो भला करते बुरा फल पाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2767.english_translation: Her hump was broken, her skull split, her teeth smashed, and blood streamed from her mouth. Crying out, she said, “Alas, what wrong have I done? I did good and got a cruel result.”
ramacharitamanas::2767.translation_literal: कूबर (hump) / टूटेउ (was broken) / फूट (split) / कपारू (skull) / दलित (crushed) / दसन (teeth) / मुख (mouth) / रुधिर (blood) / प्रचारू (spread) / आह (alas) / दइअ (fate) / मैं (I) / काह (what) / नसावा (did wrong) / करत (doing) / नीक (good) / फलु (result) / अनइस (cruel) / पावा (got)
ramacharitamanas::2767.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2767.essence: Harm done to others can return and wound you first.
ramacharitamanas::2767.simple_meaning: She is badly injured and cries that she did good but received a bad result.
ramacharitamanas::2767.simple_insight: Cruel actions can collapse in a moment, and the mind suddenly sees the cost.
ramacharitamanas::2767.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi's maid Manthara has been struck in the quarrel over Ram's exile. Bloodied and broken, she laments that her mischief has brought her suffering. The scene keeps the palace conflict moving toward Bharat's intervention.
ramacharitamanas::2767.modern_relevance: You spend weeks stirring trouble in a group chat, then the blowback lands on you first. The damage feels sudden, but it was already set in motion.
ramacharitamanas::2767.insight: It shows how harmful schemes can rebound on the one who set them in motion.

ramacharitamanas::2768.verse_sanskrit: सुनि रिपुहन लखि नख सिख खोटी। लगे घसीटन धरि धरि झोंटी॥ भरत दयानिधि दीन्हि छुड़ाई। कौसल्या पहिं गे दोउ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2768.verse_hindi: उसकी यह बात सुनकर और उसे नख से शिखा तक दुष्ट जानकर शत्रुघ्नजी झोंटा पकड़-पकड़कर उसे घसीटने लगे। तब दयानिधि भरतजी ने उसको छुड़ा दिया और दोनों भाई (तुरंत) कौसल्याजी के पास गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2768.english_translation: Hearing her words and seeing her wickedness from head to toe, Shatrughna began dragging her by the hair. Then merciful Bharat freed her, and both brothers went to Kaushalya.
ramacharitamanas::2768.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / रिपु-हन (enemy-slayer, Shatrughna) / लखि (seeing) / नख सिख (from nail to head) / खोटी (wicked) / लगे (began) / घसीटन (dragging) / धरि धरि (grabbing repeatedly) / झोंटी (hair tuft)॥ / भरत (Bharat) / दयानिधि (ocean of mercy) / दीन्हि (gave) / छुड़ाई (release) / कौसल्या (Kaushalya) / पहिं (to) / गे (went) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers)॥
ramacharitamanas::2768.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2768.essence: Mercy can stop anger before it becomes harm.
ramacharitamanas::2768.simple_meaning: Shatrughna sees the woman as evil and drags her by the hair, but Bharat stops him and sends both brothers to Kaushalya.
ramacharitamanas::2768.simple_insight: Even in anger, mercy can step in and stop harm before it goes too far.
ramacharitamanas::2768.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the brothers are still reeling from the insult and cruelty around them. Shatrughna grabs the woman by her hair, but Bharat, known for mercy, restrains him. The scene turns from punishment to restraint as they go to Kaushalya.
ramacharitamanas::2768.modern_relevance: You catch someone in the middle of a cruel outburst and feel your own anger rising. Then one calmer person steps in, breaks the chain, and keeps the moment from becoming worse.
ramacharitamanas::2768.insight: It shifts you from retaliating at once to letting mercy interrupt escalation.

ramacharitamanas::2769.verse_sanskrit: मलिन बसन बिबरन बिकल कृस शरीर दुख भार। कनक कलप बर बेलि बन मानहुँ हनी तुसार ॥
ramacharitamanas::2769.verse_hindi: कौसल्याजी मैले वस्त्र पहने हैं, चेहरे का रंग बदला हुआ है, व्याकुल हो रही हैं, दुःख के बोझ से शरीर सूख गया है। ऐसी दिख रही हैं मानो सोने की सुंदर कल्पलता को वन में पाला मार गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2769.english_translation: Kaushalya wears soiled clothes, her face has lost its color, she is restless, and grief has dried her body. She looks like a golden wish-fulfilling vine struck by frost in the forest.
ramacharitamanas::2769.translation_literal: मलिन (soiled) / बसन (clothes) / बिबरन (pale, colorless) / बिकल (distressed) / कृस (thin, emaciated) / शरीर (body) / दुख (sorrow) / भार (weight) / कनक (golden) / कलप (wish-fulfilling) / बर (excellent) / बेलि (vine) / बन (forest) / मानहुँ (as if) / हनी (struck) / तुसार (frost)
ramacharitamanas::2769.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2769.essence: Grief can make living beauty look frostbitten.
ramacharitamanas::2769.simple_meaning: Kaushalya is so worn down by grief that she looks physically faded and weakened, like a beautiful vine damaged by frost.
ramacharitamanas::2769.simple_insight: Grief can drain the body until even beauty looks wounded.
ramacharitamanas::2769.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court has been torn apart by exile and sorrow. Kaushalya is no longer just a queen waiting in grief; she looks physically diminished by heartbreak, as if the life has been knocked out of her before Bharat even reaches her.
ramacharitamanas::2769.modern_relevance: You spot someone at the hospital waiting room after a sleepless night: wrinkled clothes, hollow eyes, a body that looks older than yesterday. Loss does that before words can.
ramacharitamanas::2769.insight: It turns sorrow into a visible, bodily reality rather than an abstract feeling.

ramacharitamanas::2770.verse_sanskrit: भरतहि देखि मातु उठि धाई। मुरुचित अवनि परी झइँ आई॥ देखत भरतु बिकल भए भारी। परे चरन तन दसा बिसारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2770.verse_hindi: भरत को देखते ही माता कौसल्याजी उठ दौड़ीं। पर चक्कर आ जाने से मूर्च्छित होकर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ीं। यह देखते ही भरतजी बड़े व्याकुल हो गए और शरीर की सुध भुलाकर चरणों में गिर पड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::2770.english_translation: Seeing Bharata, Mother Kausalya rushed to him. She fainted and fell to the ground. Seeing this, Bharata was overwhelmed with grief and, forgetting himself, fell at her feet.
ramacharitamanas::2770.translation_literal: भरतहि (Bharata) / देखि (seeing) / मातु (mother) / उठि (rising) / धाई (ran) / मुरुचित (fainted) / अवनि (on the ground) / परी (fell) / झइँ (down) / आई (came) / देखत (seeing) / भरतु (Bharata) / बिकल (distressed) / भए (became) / भारी (greatly) / परे (fell) / चरन (at feet) / तन (body) / दसा (condition) / बिसारी (forgot)
ramacharitamanas::2770.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2770.essence: Grief can bring both the mother and son to their knees.
ramacharitamanas::2770.simple_meaning: Kausalya runs to Bharata and faints from emotion. Bharata is so shaken by her grief that he falls at her feet, forgetting his own body.
ramacharitamanas::2770.simple_insight: Love can overwhelm pride so completely that only tenderness remains.
ramacharitamanas::2770.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharata returns to a house broken by exile and grief. Kausalya sees him and rushes forward, but sorrow and shock make her faint. Bharata answers her pain not with words, but by collapsing at her feet in shared anguish.
ramacharitamanas::2770.modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room and see your mother break down at the sight of you. In that instant, all your plans disappear; only love and helplessness remain.
ramacharitamanas::2770.insight: It shifts attention from action to emotional presence, showing that grief is sometimes met by silent surrender.

ramacharitamanas::2771.verse_sanskrit: मातु तात कहँ देहि देखाई। कहँ सिय रामु लखनु दोउ भाई॥ कैकइ कत जनमी जग माझा। जौं जनमि त भइ काहे न बाँझा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2771.verse_hindi: (फिर बोले-) माता! पिताजी कहाँ हैं? उन्हें दिखा दें। सीताजी तथा मेरे दोनों भाई श्री राम-लक्ष्मण कहाँ हैं? (उन्हें दिखा दें।) कैकेयी जगत में क्यों जनमी! और यदि जनमी ही तो फिर बाँझ क्यों न हुई?- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2771.english_translation: “Mother, Father, please show me where they are. Where are Sita and my two brothers, Ram and Lakshman? Why was Kaikeyi born into this world at all? If she was born, why was she not born barren?”
ramacharitamanas::2771.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / तात (father) / कहँ (where) / देहि (please give/show) / देखाई (showing) / कहँ (where) / सिय (Sita) / रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / कैकइ (Kaikeyi) / कत (why) / जनमी (was born) / जग (world) / माझा (in) / जौं (if) / जनमि (born) / त (then) / भइ (became) / काहे (why) / न (not) / बाँझा (barren)
ramacharitamanas::2771.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2771.essence: Separation makes even a noble heart cry out in bitterness.
ramacharitamanas::2771.simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed with grief and asks to be shown his parents, Sita, Ram, and Lakshman. In his pain, he blames Kaikeyi for the ruin of the family.
ramacharitamanas::2771.simple_insight: Grief can make love sound like accusation when the heart cannot bear separation.
ramacharitamanas::2771.detailed_meaning: After seeing his mother collapse, Bharat breaks in Ayodhya and searches for the missing figures who made his world whole: Dasharath, Sita, Ram, and Lakshman. His anguish turns into a bitter outcry against Kaikeyi, showing how exile has shattered the family.
ramacharitamanas::2771.modern_relevance: You walk into a house after a funeral and ask for the people who should still be there. The question is simple; the loss behind it is not.
ramacharitamanas::2771.insight: It reveals how sorrow narrows attention to absence and turns pain into blame.

ramacharitamanas::2772.verse_sanskrit: कुल कलंकु जेहिं जनमेउ मोही। अपजस भाजन प्रियजन द्रोही॥ को तिभुवन मोहि सरिस अभागी। गति असि तोरि मातुजेहि लागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2772.verse_hindi: जिसने कुल के कलंक, अपयश के भाँडे और प्रियजनों के द्रोही मुझ जैसे पुत्र को उत्पन्न किया। तीनों लोकों में मेरे समान अभागा कौन है? जिसके कारण हे माता! तेरी यह दशा हुई! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2772.english_translation: The one who gave birth to me is a stain on the family, a source of disgrace, and a traitor to loved ones. Who in the three worlds is as unlucky as I am? Mother, because of me you have come to this state.
ramacharitamanas::2772.translation_literal: कुल कलंकु (stain on the family) / जेहिं (who) / जनमेउ (gave birth) / मोही (to me) / अपजस (disgrace) / भाजन (vessel) / प्रियजन (loved ones) / द्रोही (betrayer) / को (who) / तिभुवन (three worlds) / मोहि (me) / सरिस (like) / अभागी (unfortunate) / गति (state) / असि (such) / तोरि (your) / मातु (mother) / जेहि (because of whom) / लागी (happened)
ramacharitamanas::2772.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2772.essence: Grief makes Bharat see himself as the cause of all suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2772.simple_meaning: Bharat blames himself completely for the suffering around him. He sees himself as the cause of his mother's condition and the family’s disgrace.
ramacharitamanas::2772.simple_insight: Guilt can make you see yourself as the source of every wound, even when the pain is larger than you.
ramacharitamanas::2772.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat has just seen Kaushalya collapse at the sight of him. Overwhelmed by grief and shame, he turns the blame inward, calling himself the family’s disgrace and the cause of his mother’s suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2772.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a family argument and feel everyone’s pain land on you at once. Even the parts you didn’t cause start to feel like your fault.
ramacharitamanas::2772.insight: It reveals how grief and guilt collapse into self-condemnation, making a person take responsibility for everything.

ramacharitamanas::2773.verse_sanskrit: पितु सुरपुर बन रघुबर केतू। मैं केवल सब अनरथ हेतू॥ धिग मोहि भयउँ बेनु बन आगी। दुसह दाह दुख दूषन भागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2773.verse_hindi: पिताजी स्वर्ग में हैं और श्री रामजी वन में हैं। केतु के समान केवल मैं ही इन सब अनर्थों का कारण हूँ। मुझे धिक्कार है! मैं बाँस के वन में आग उत्पन्न हुआ और कठिन दाह, दुःख और दोषों का भागी बना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2773.english_translation: My father is in heaven and Raghubar is in the forest. I alone am the cause of all these calamities. Shame on me! I was born like fire in a bamboo grove, bringing unbearable burning, sorrow, and ruin.
ramacharitamanas::2773.translation_literal: पितु (father) / सुरपुर (heavenly realm) / बन (forest) / रघुबर (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / केतू (banner) / मैं (I) / केवल (only) / सब (all) / अनरथ (misfortune, calamity) / हेतू (cause) / धिग (shame) / मोहि (me) / भयउँ (became) / बेनु (bamboo) / बन (forest) / आगी (fire) / दुसह (unbearable) / दाह (burning) / दुख (sorrow) / दूषन (defilement, ruin) / भागी (bearing, fated)
ramacharitamanas::2773.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2773.essence: Grief can make you mistake yourself for the cause of everything.
ramacharitamanas::2773.simple_meaning: Bharat blames himself completely for the exile and family ruin. He sees himself as the source of all suffering and feels deep shame.
ramacharitamanas::2773.simple_insight: Guilt can become so heavy that you start seeing yourself as the cause of everything.
ramacharitamanas::2773.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat has just learned the full cost of Kaikeyi’s demand. Ram is in the forest, Dasharath is gone, and the kingdom is shattered. Overwhelmed by grief, Bharat turns his pain inward and calls himself the source of all disaster.
ramacharitamanas::2773.modern_relevance: You replay one bad decision at 2 a.m. and suddenly every problem feels like your fault. Bharat’s grief shows how pain can turn into total self-condemnation.
ramacharitamanas::2773.insight: It reveals how grief can distort judgment, turning sorrow into self-blame and collapsing the whole world into one wounded self.

ramacharitamanas::2774.verse_sanskrit: मातु भरत के बचन मृदु सुनि पुनि उठी सँभारि। लिए उठाइ लगाइ उर लोचन मोचति बारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2774.verse_hindi: भरतजी के कोमल वचन सुनकर माता कौसल्याजी फिर सँभलकर उठीं। उन्होंने भरत को उठाकर छाती से लगा लिया और नेत्रों से आँसू बहाने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2774.english_translation: Hearing Bharata's gentle words, Mother Kaushalya gathered herself and rose again. She lifted Bharata into her arms, held him to her chest, and tears flowed from her eyes.
ramacharitamanas::2774.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / भरत के (of Bharata's) / बचन (words) / मृदु (gentle) / सुनि (hearing) / पुनि (again) / उठी (rose) / सँभारि (gathering herself) / लिए (took) / उठाइ (lifting) / लगाइ (embracing) / उर (to the chest) / लोचन (eyes) / मोचति (releasing) / बारि (water, tears)
ramacharitamanas::2774.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2774.essence: Tender words can melt grief into embrace.
ramacharitamanas::2774.simple_meaning: Kaushalya hears Bharata's soft words, regains herself, hugs him close, and cries. Her grief and love overflow together.
ramacharitamanas::2774.simple_insight: Love can steady a broken heart even while the tears keep coming.
ramacharitamanas::2774.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharata is overwhelmed with guilt and grief after Ram's exile. Kaushalya hears his gentle words, rises from her shock, and embraces him like a mother who cannot stop loving even in sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2774.modern_relevance: You hear your child finally say the honest thing they've been carrying. Your anger softens, and the hug comes before the explanation does.
ramacharitamanas::2774.insight: It shifts you from blame to tenderness, showing how grief can open into care.

ramacharitamanas::2775.verse_sanskrit: सरल सुभाय मायँ हियँ लाए। अति हित मनहुँ राम फिरि आए॥ भेंटेउ बहुरि लखन लघु भाई। सोकु सनेहु न हृदयँ समाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2775.verse_hindi: सरल स्वभाव वाली माता ने बड़े प्रेम से भरतजी को छाती से लगा लिया, मानो श्री रामजी ही लौटकर आ गए हों। फिर लक्ष्मणजी के छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न को हृदय से लगाया। शोक और स्नेह हृदय में समाता नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2775.english_translation: With a gentle nature, the mother embraced Bharata to her heart, as if Ram himself had returned. Then she embraced Shatrughna, Lakshmana's younger brother. Grief and affection could not fit together in her heart.
ramacharitamanas::2775.translation_literal: सरल (simple) / सुभाय (nature) / मायँ (mother) / हियँ (heart) / लाए (brought close) / अति (very) / हित (loving, beneficial) / मनहुँ (as if) / राम (Ram) / फिरि (returned) / आए (came) / भेंटेउ (embraced) / बहुरि (again) / लखन (Lakshmana) / लघु (younger) / भाई (brother) / सोकु (grief) / सनेहु (affection) / न (not) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / समाई (fit, remain)
ramacharitamanas::2775.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2775.essence: A grieving heart still reaches for the people it loves.
ramacharitamanas::2775.simple_meaning: Kausalya embraces Bharata like returning Ram, then holds Shatrughna close. Her heart is too full to hold both grief and love at once.
ramacharitamanas::2775.simple_insight: Love after loss can feel almost unbearable — the heart reaches for comfort even while it still aches.
ramacharitamanas::2775.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, grief still hangs over Dasharath's death and Ram's exile. Kausalya sees Bharata and Shatrughna and clings to them as if Ram has come back. The verse captures a mother's heart overflowing with both sorrow and tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::2775.modern_relevance: You see a child after a long absence and hug them too hard, half-relieved and half-breaking inside. Some reunions carry both comfort and grief in the same breath.
ramacharitamanas::2775.insight: It shows how grief can live beside affection without either one disappearing.

ramacharitamanas::2776.verse_sanskrit: देखि सुभाउ कहत सबु कोई। राम मातु अस काहे न होई॥ माताँ भरतु गोद बैठारे। आँसु पोछिं मृदु बचन उचारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2776.verse_hindi: कौसल्याजी का स्वभाव देखकर सब कोई कह रहे हैं- श्री राम की माता का ऐसा स्वभाव क्यों न हो। माता ने भरतजी को गोद में बैठा लिया और उनके आँसू पोंछकर कोमल वचन बोलीं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2776.english_translation: Seeing her nature, everyone said, “Why should Ram’s mother not be like this?” The mother seated Bharat in her lap, wiped away his tears, and spoke gently.
ramacharitamanas::2776.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / सुभाउ (nature) / कहत (saying) / सबु कोई (everyone) / राम (Ram) / मातु (mother) / अस (like this) / काहे (why) / न (not) / होई (be) ॥ माताँ (mother) / भरतु (Bharat) / गोद (lap) / बैठारे (made sit) / आँसु (tears) / पोछिं (wiping) / मृदु (gentle) / बचन (words) / उचारे (spoke)
ramacharitamanas::2776.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2776.essence: A mother's tenderness can turn grief into belonging.
ramacharitamanas::2776.simple_meaning: Kausalya’s tenderness is so complete that everyone sees why Ram came from her. She comforts Bharat like her own child, wiping his tears and speaking softly.
ramacharitamanas::2776.simple_insight: Love becomes most visible when it calms someone else’s grief.
ramacharitamanas::2776.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat returns burdened by grief and misunderstanding. Kausalya does not meet him with blame or distance. She lifts him into her lap, wipes his tears, and answers with a mother’s gentleness, becoming the emotional shelter of the scene.
ramacharitamanas::2776.modern_relevance: Your younger brother shows up after a family fight, eyes red, trying to act fine. You pull him close, hand him water, and let your softness do what arguments cannot.
ramacharitamanas::2776.insight: It shifts the response from judgment to shelter, showing how care can steady a shaken heart.

ramacharitamanas::2777.verse_sanskrit: अजहुँ बच्छ बलि धीरज धरहू। कुसमउ समुझि सोक परिहरहू॥ जनि मानहु हियँ हानि गलानी। काल करम गति अघटित जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2777.verse_hindi: हे वत्स! मैं बलैया लेती हूँ। तुम अब भी धीरज धरो। बुरा समय जानकर शोक त्याग दो। काल और कर्म की गति अमिट जानकर हृदय में हानि और ग्लानि मत मानो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2777.english_translation: O child, I bless you. Still, keep your courage. Seeing the wrong season, let go of grief. Knowing the movement of time and action as unfathomable, do not carry loss or shame in your heart.
ramacharitamanas::2777.translation_literal: अजहुँ (still) / बच्छ (child) / बलि (I bless you) / धीरज (courage / patience) / धरहू (hold) / कुसमउ (bad season / wrong time) / समुझि (understanding) / सोक (grief) / परिहरहू (let go) / जनि (do not) / मानहु (consider) / हियँ (in the heart) / हानि (loss) / गलानी (shame / distress) / काल (time) / करम (action) / गति (movement / course) / अघटित (unfathomable) / जानी (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::2777.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::2777.essence: Not every loss is yours to carry as guilt.
ramacharitamanas::2777.simple_meaning: Kausalya comforts Bharata by telling him to stay brave, release grief, and not blame himself for what time and action have brought.
ramacharitamanas::2777.simple_insight: You can face painful events without turning them into personal failure.
ramacharitamanas::2777.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kausalya holds Bharata like her own child after the fracture in the royal family. She sees his pain, but instead of adding blame, she asks him to bear the season with courage and accept what time has done.
ramacharitamanas::2777.modern_relevance: You sit on the edge of your bed after a family argument, replaying every sentence and wondering what you ruined. This verse says not every wound is proof of your failure.
ramacharitamanas::2777.insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame to calm endurance when life turns harsh.

ramacharitamanas::2778.verse_sanskrit: काहुहि दोसु देहु जनि ताता। भा मोहि सब बिधि बाम बिधाता॥ जो एतेहुँ दुख मोहि जिआवा। अजहुँ को जानइ का तेहि भावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2778.verse_hindi: हे तात! किसी को दोष मत दो। विधाता मेरे िलए सब प्रकार से उलटा हो गया है, जो इतने दुःख पर भी मुझे जिला रहा है। अब भी कौन जानता है, उसे क्या भा रहा है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2778.english_translation: Father, do not blame anyone. Fate has turned against me in every way, yet it still keeps me alive through this suffering. Who can know what it truly intends?
ramacharitamanas::2778.translation_literal: काहुहि (to anyone) / दोसु (blame) / देहु (give) / जनि (do not) / ताता (father) / भा (has become) / मोहि (for me) / सब बिधि (in every way) / बाम (opposite/unfavourable) / बिधाता (the ordainer) / जो (who/which) / एतेहुँ (even this much) / दुख (pain) / मोहि (me) / जिआवा (kept alive) / अजहुँ (still) / को (who) / जानइ (knows) / का (what) / तेहि (to that one) / भावा (is pleasing)
ramacharitamanas::2778.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2778.essence: Blame falls away when you admit life is moving beyond your control.
ramacharitamanas::2778.simple_meaning: She asks Bharat not to blame anyone and says her life feels turned upside down, yet she is still being kept alive. She admits no one can know what the hidden order truly wants.
ramacharitamanas::2778.simple_insight: There is relief in stopping the search for someone to blame when life turns painful and confusing.
ramacharitamanas::2778.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi speaks to Bharat after the palace has been shattered by Ram’s exile and Dasharath’s sorrow. She is no longer defending herself; she is overwhelmed by the consequences and can only admit that the larger order has become unbearable and mysterious.
ramacharitamanas::2778.modern_relevance: You get the call at midnight and everything changes, but no one can explain why it happened. Before the blame starts flying, this verse asks you to pause and face the confusion honestly.
ramacharitamanas::2778.insight: It shifts the mind from blaming people to facing the mystery of what life is doing.

ramacharitamanas::2779.verse_sanskrit: पितु आयस भूषन बसन तात तजे रघुबीर। बिसमउ हरषु न हृदयँ कछु पहिरे बलकल चीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::2779.verse_hindi: हे तात! पिता की आज्ञा से श्री रघुवीर ने भूषण-वस्त्र त्याग दिए और वल्कल वस्त्र पहन लिए। उनके हृदय में न कुछ विषाद था, न हर्ष! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2779.english_translation: O father, by his father's command, Raghubir gave up ornaments and fine clothes and put on bark garments. His heart held neither sorrow nor joy.
ramacharitamanas::2779.translation_literal: पितु (father's) / आयस (command) / भूषन (ornaments) / बसन (clothes) / तात (father) / तजे (gave up) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / बिसमउ (wonder) / हरषु (joy) / न (not) / हृदयँ (in heart) / कछु (anything) / पहिरे (wore) / बलकल (bark-cloth) / चीर (garments)
ramacharitamanas::2779.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2779.essence: Duty stays intact even when all outward honor is stripped away.
ramacharitamanas::2779.simple_meaning: Ram obeys his father's command, gives up royal clothes, and puts on bark garments. He does it without inner excitement or grief.
ramacharitamanas::2779.simple_insight: True dignity does not depend on what you wear or lose.
ramacharitamanas::2779.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram is leaving palace life for exile. At his father's command, he removes ornaments and fine clothes and accepts bark garments. The verse shows his complete steadiness: no pride in luxury, no sadness in loss.
ramacharitamanas::2779.modern_relevance: You pack away the suit, the title, the polished image, and walk into the harder role anyway. What matters is not the outfit, but the steadiness you bring with it.
ramacharitamanas::2779.insight: It shifts attention from outer status to inner steadiness under obligation.

ramacharitamanas::2780.verse_sanskrit: मुख प्रसन्न मन रंग न रोषू। सब कर सब बिधि करि परितोषू॥ चले बिपिन सुनि सिय सँग लागी। रहइ न राम चरन अनुरागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2780.verse_hindi: उनका मुख प्रसन्न था, मन में न आसक्ति थी, न रोष (द्वेष)। सबका सब तरह से संतोष कराकर वे वन को चले। यह सुनकर सीता भी उनके साथ लग गईं। श्रीराम के चरणों की अनुरागिणी वे किसी तरह न रहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2780.english_translation: His face was cheerful, his mind free of attachment and anger. After pleasing everyone in every way, he went to the forest. Hearing this, Sita too followed him, and she could no longer stay apart from Ram’s feet.
ramacharitamanas::2780.translation_literal: मुख (face) / प्रसन्न (cheerful) / मन (mind) / रंग (color) / न (not) / रोषू (anger) / सब (all) / कर (of) / सब बिधि (in every way) / करि (having done) / परितोषू (satisfaction) / चले (went) / बिपिन (forest) / सुनि (hearing) / सिय (Sita) / सँग (with) / लागी (attached/followed) / रहइ (remained) / न (not) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / अनुरागी (loving/attached)
ramacharitamanas::2780.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2780.essence: Calm dignity can carry love through exile.
ramacharitamanas::2780.simple_meaning: Ram leaves for the forest with a calm face and an untroubled mind, having satisfied everyone as much as possible. Sita hears this and follows him, unable to stay away from his feet.
ramacharitamanas::2780.simple_insight: A steady heart can move through loss without bitterness, and love follows naturally behind it.
ramacharitamanas::2780.detailed_meaning: The moment after exile is set in motion, Ram does not flare with resentment or panic. He leaves with composure, having softened everyone’s hearts as much as he can. Sita hears of it and cannot remain behind; her love draws her into the same कठिन path.
ramacharitamanas::2780.modern_relevance: You get the news you dreaded, and your face still has to meet the room. This verse shows how calm dignity can carry you through a painful turn without turning cruel.
ramacharitamanas::2780.insight: It shifts the reader from reactive hurt to composed acceptance, showing that love can move without complaint.

ramacharitamanas::2781.verse_sanskrit: सुनतहिं लखनु चले उठि साथा। रहहिं न जतन किए रघुनाथा॥ तब रघुपति सबही सिरु नाई। चले संग सिय अरु लघु भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2781.verse_hindi: सुनते ही लक्ष्मण भी साथ ही उठ चले। श्री रघुनाथ ने उन्हें रोकने के बहुत यत्न किए, पर वे न रहे। तब श्री रघुनाथजी सबको सिर नवाकर सीता और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण को साथ लेकर चले गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2781.english_translation: As soon as he heard, Lakshman rose and went along. Raghunath tried many ways to stop him, but he would not stay. Then Raghupati bowed to everyone and left with Sita and his younger brother.
ramacharitamanas::2781.translation_literal: सुनतहिं (as soon as hearing) / लखनु (Lakshman) / चले (went) / उठि (rising) / साथा (alongside) । / रहहिं (to remain) / न (not) / जतन (with efforts) / किए (made) / रघुनाथा (Raghunatha) । / तब (then) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / सबही (to everyone) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing) / चले (went) / संग (with) / सिय (Sita) / अरु (and) / लघु भाई (younger brother) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2781.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2781.essence: Loyalty moves Lakshman faster than hesitation can speak.
ramacharitamanas::2781.simple_meaning: Lakshman immediately follows Ram, and Ram, after trying to stop him, leaves with Sita and Lakshman, bowing to everyone first.
ramacharitamanas::2781.simple_insight: Love can make you follow without hesitation, even when staying would be easier.
ramacharitamanas::2781.detailed_meaning: Ram is leaving for the forest, and Lakshman cannot bear to let him go alone. He rises at once, despite Ram’s efforts to stop him. The scene shows brotherly loyalty in motion, not argument.
ramacharitamanas::2781.modern_relevance: Your best friend says, “Don’t come, I can manage.” You still grab your bag and go anyway. Some loyalties move before thought does.
ramacharitamanas::2781.insight: It shows how true loyalty answers before hesitation and chooses presence over convenience.

ramacharitamanas::2782.verse_sanskrit: रामु लखनु सिय बनहि सिधाए। गइउँ न संग न प्रान पठाए॥ यहु सबु भा इन्ह आँखिन्ह आगें। तउ न तजा तनु जीव अभागें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2782.verse_hindi: श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीता वन को चले गए। मैं न तो साथ ही गई और न मैंने अपने प्राण ही उनके साथ भेजे। यह सब इन्हीं आँखों के सामने हुआ, तो भी अभागे जीव ने शरीर नहीं छोड़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2782.english_translation: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita went to the forest. I did not go with them, nor did I send my life with them. All this happened before my eyes, yet this unlucky body did not leave.
ramacharitamanas::2782.translation_literal: रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / बनहि (to the forest) / सिधाए (departed) / गइउँ (I went) / न (not) / संग (with) / न (not) / प्रान (life-breath) / पठाए (sent) / यहु (this) / सबु (all) / भा (happened) / इन्ह (these) / आँखिन्ह (eyes) / आगें (before) / तउ (then) / न (not) / तजा (left) / तनु (body) / जीव (living being) / अभागें (unlucky)
ramacharitamanas::2782.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2782.essence: Some losses are witnessed too late to prevent, and still impossible to bear.
ramacharitamanas::2782.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is overwhelmed by regret. She says Ram, Lakshman, and Sita left for the forest before her eyes, yet she still could not let her body die.
ramacharitamanas::2782.simple_insight: Regret can be so sharp that even life feels unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2782.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi watches the exile she caused become real. Ram, Lakshman, and Sita have already gone, and her guilt is now unbearable. This line is not teaching doctrine; it is the cry of a woman trapped inside the consequences of her own demand.
ramacharitamanas::2782.modern_relevance: You watch the person you pushed away walk out the door, and the silence after feels heavier than the argument. The mind keeps replaying what cannot be undone.
ramacharitamanas::2782.insight: It shows how guilt can outlive the moment of action and harden into bodily grief.

ramacharitamanas::2783.verse_sanskrit: मोहि न लाज निज नेहु निहारी। राम सरिस सुत मैं महतारी॥ जिऐ मरै भल भूपति जाना। मोर हृदय सत कुलिस समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2783.verse_hindi: अपने स्नेह की ओर देखकर मुझे लाज नहीं आती; राम सरीखे पुत्र की मैं माता! जीना और मरना तो राजा ने खूब जाना। मेरा हृदय तो सैकड़ों वज्रों के समान कठोर है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2783.english_translation: Looking at my own love, I feel no shame: I am the mother of a son like Ram. The king knows how to live and die; my heart is as hard as hundreds of thunderbolts.
ramacharitamanas::2783.translation_literal: मोहि (to me) / न (not) / लाज (shame) / निज (my own) / नेहु (love) / निहारी (seeing, looking at) / राम (Ram) / सरिस (like) / सुत (son) / मैं (I) / महतारी (mother) / जिऐ (to live) / मरै (to die) / भल (well) / भूपति (king) / जाना (knows) / मोर (my) / हृदय (heart) / सत (hundreds) / कुलिस (thunderbolts) / समाना (equal to, like)
ramacharitamanas::2783.speaker: Kaushalya
ramacharitamanas::2783.essence: A mother’s pride in Ram survives even the crushing blow of separation.
ramacharitamanas::2783.simple_meaning: Kaushalya says she feels no shame in her love for Ram. She is proud to be the mother of a son like him, while her heart has become unbearably hard from grief.
ramacharitamanas::2783.simple_insight: Love can make grief feel honorable, even when it breaks you open.
ramacharitamanas::2783.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaushalya speaks after Ram, Sita, and Lakshman have gone into exile. She is defending her love for Ram while admitting the pain has turned her heart hard as thunderbolts. Her words carry both pride and heartbreak.
ramacharitamanas::2783.modern_relevance: You watch your child leave for a life you cannot protect, and pride and pain arrive together. You don't apologize for loving deeply, even when that love hurts.
ramacharitamanas::2783.insight: It shows how devotion can coexist with unbearable grief without becoming self-pity.

ramacharitamanas::2784.verse_sanskrit: कौसल्या के बचन सुनि भरत सहित रनिवासु। ब्याकुल बिलपत राजगृह मानहुँ सोक नेवासु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2784.verse_hindi: कौसल्याजी के वचनों को सुनकर भरत सहित सारा रनिवास व्याकुल होकर विलाप करने लगा। राजमहल मानो शोक का निवास बन गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2784.english_translation: Hearing Kausalya's words, Bharata and the whole royal household were overwhelmed and began to lament. The royal palace became like a dwelling of grief.
ramacharitamanas::2784.translation_literal: कौसल्या (Kausalya's) / के (of) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / भरत (Bharata) / सहित (along with) / रनिवासु (the women of the royal household) / ब्याकुल (agitated) / बिलपत (lamenting) / राजगृह (royal palace) / मानहुँ (as if) / सोक (grief) / नेवासु (dwelling-place)
ramacharitamanas::2784.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2784.essence: Grief, once spoken aloud, fills every corner of the home.
ramacharitamanas::2784.simple_meaning: Kausalya's words shake Bharata and everyone in the palace. Their grief fills the whole royal house.
ramacharitamanas::2784.simple_insight: Some words do more than inform — they break open the grief everyone was carrying.
ramacharitamanas::2784.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kausalya has just spoken from the wound of Ram's exile. Bharata and the women of the palace hear her and collapse into lament. The verse is a scene of shared grief, not a new teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2784.modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after one honest message about loss. No one needs to explain it — the whole room has already changed.
ramacharitamanas::2784.insight: It shows how one truthful sorrow can spread through an entire household and make denial impossible.

ramacharitamanas::2785.verse_sanskrit: बिलपहिं बिकल भरत दोउ भाई। कौसल्याँ लिए हृदयँ लगाई॥ भाँति अनेक भरतु समुझाए। कहि बिबेकमय बचन सुनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2785.verse_hindi: भरत, शत्रुघ्न दोनों भाई विकल होकर विलाप करने लगे। तब कौसल्याजी ने उनको हृदय से लगा लिया। अनेकों प्रकार से भरतजी को समझाया और बहुत सी विवेकभरी बातें उन्हें कहकर सुनाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2785.english_translation: Bharat and Shatrughna, both distraught brothers, wept. Kausalya drew them close to her heart and, in many ways, consoled Bharat with wise words.
ramacharitamanas::2785.translation_literal: बिलपहिं (wept) / बिकल (distraught) / भरत (Bharat) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / कौसल्याँ (Kausalya) / लिए (took) / हृदयँ लगाई (embraced to the heart) / भाँति अनेक (in many ways) / भरतु (Bharat) / समुझाए (consoled, explained) / कहि (saying) / बिबेकमय (full of discernment) / बचन (words) / सुनाए (made hear)
ramacharitamanas::2785.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2785.essence: Comfort begins with closeness, not correction.
ramacharitamanas::2785.simple_meaning: Bharat and Shatrughna are overwhelmed with grief. Kausalya holds them close and comforts Bharat with wise, calming words.
ramacharitamanas::2785.simple_insight: Grief softens when someone meets it with warmth and clear words.
ramacharitamanas::2785.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace is drowning in sorrow after Ram's exile. Bharat and Shatrughna break down in tears, and Kausalya gathers them into her arms. This verse shows a mother's first response to unbearable loss: comfort, then understanding.
ramacharitamanas::2785.modern_relevance: Your younger brother is crying in the kitchen after bad news, and you stop everything just to hold him. Before advice, before fixing, presence itself becomes the first mercy.
ramacharitamanas::2785.insight: It shows that pain often needs embrace first, explanation second.

ramacharitamanas::2786.verse_sanskrit: भरतहुँ मातु सकल समुझाईं। कहि पुरान श्रुति कथा सुहाईं॥ छल बिहीन सुचि सरल सुबानी। बोले भरत जोरि जुग पानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2786.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने भी सब माताओं को पुराण और वेदों की सुंदर कथाएँ कहकर समझाया। दोनों हाथ जोड़कर भरतजी छलरहित, पवित्र और सीधी सुंदर वाणी बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2786.english_translation: Bharat also comforted all the mothers by telling them beautiful stories from the Puranas and the Vedas. With both hands joined, Bharat spoke in pure, simple, deceit-free, and beautiful words.
ramacharitamanas::2786.translation_literal: भरतहुँ (Bharat also) / मातु (the mothers) / सकल (all) / समुझाईं (comforted, explained) / कहि (telling) / पुरान (Puranas) / श्रुति (Vedas) / कथा (stories) / सुहाईं (beautiful) / छल बिहीन (without deceit) / सुचि (pure) / सरल (simple) / सुबानी (good speech) / बोले (spoke) / भरत (Bharat) / जोरि (joining) / जुग (both) / पानी (hands)
ramacharitamanas::2786.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2786.essence: Gentle truth can steady even a house in grief.
ramacharitamanas::2786.simple_meaning: Bharat comforts the grieving women with sacred stories and speaks to them with honest, gentle words.
ramacharitamanas::2786.simple_insight: Grief softens when someone meets it with sincerity, not performance.
ramacharitamanas::2786.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace is drowning in grief after Dasharath's death and Ram's exile. Bharat, overwhelmed himself, turns to the mothers and speaks with joined hands, using sacred stories and gentle truth to steady them.
ramacharitamanas::2786.modern_relevance: You sit beside a crying parent after bad news, and you do not try to fix everything. You speak simply, honestly, and let your steadiness do the comforting.
ramacharitamanas::2786.insight: It shows that calm, truthful speech can hold a room that is breaking apart.

ramacharitamanas::2787.verse_sanskrit: जे अघ मातु पिता सुत मारें। गाइ गोठ महिसुर पुर जारें॥ जे अघ तिय बालक बध कीन्हें। मीत महीपति माहुर दीन्हें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2787.verse_hindi: जो पाप माता-पिता और पुत्र के मारने से होते हैं और जो गोशाला और ब्राह्मणों के नगर जलाने से होते हैं, जो पाप स्त्री और बालक की हत्या करने से होते हैं और जो मित्र और राजा को जहर देने से होते हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2787.english_translation: The sins of killing mother, father, or child; burning a cowshed or a city of the learned; killing women and children; and poisoning a friend or king—
ramacharitamanas::2787.translation_literal: जे (the) / अघ (sins) / मातु (mother) / पिता (father) / सुत (son) / मारें (killing) / गाइ गोठ (cow-shed) / महिसुर (learned ones / brahmins) / पुर (city) / जारें (burning) / जे (the) / अघ (sins) / तिय (women) / बालक (children) / बध (killing) / कीन्हें (done) / मीत (friend) / महीपति (king) / माहुर (poison) / दीन्हें (given)
ramacharitamanas::2787.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2787.essence: Some harms are so grave they need no embellishment.
ramacharitamanas::2787.simple_meaning: It lists terrible acts of violence and betrayal: killing family members, burning sacred places, harming women and children, and poisoning trusted people.
ramacharitamanas::2787.simple_insight: Some actions cut so deeply that they stain everything around them.
ramacharitamanas::2787.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is overwhelmed by grief and moral anguish. He is not praising these acts; he is naming the worst kinds of wrongdoing as he prepares to speak with complete honesty and self-condemnation.
ramacharitamanas::2787.modern_relevance: A family feud turns vicious, and someone says the unforgivable out loud: not every wound is accidental. Some betrayals are so grave they leave no room for excuses.
ramacharitamanas::2787.insight: It sharpens moral speech by naming the darkest forms of harm without softening them.

ramacharitamanas::2788.verse_sanskrit: जे पातक उपपातक अहहीं। करम बचन मन भव कबि कहहीं॥ ते पातक मोहि होहुँ बिधाता। जौं यहु होइ मोर मत माता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2788.verse_hindi: कर्म, वचन और मन से होने वाले जितने पातक एवं उपपातक (बड़े-छोटे पाप) हैं, जिनको कवि लोग कहते हैं, हे विधाता! यदि इस काम में मेरा मत हो, तो हे माता! वे सब पाप मुझे लगें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2788.english_translation: Whatever major and minor sins arise through action, speech, and mind, as poets describe, may all of those sins fall on me, O Creator, if this is my mother's wish.
ramacharitamanas::2788.translation_literal: जे (whatever) / पातक (sins) / उपपातक (minor sins) / अहहीं (there are) / करम (action) / बचन (speech) / मन (mind) / भव (existence) / कबि (poets) / कहहीं (say) / ते (those) / पातक (sins) / मोहि (on me) / होहुँ (may fall) / बिधाता (O Creator) / जौं (if) / यहु (this) / होइ (be) / मोर (my) / मत (wish/opinion) / माता (mother)
ramacharitamanas::2788.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2788.essence: Bharat would rather carry blame than let family loyalty break.
ramacharitamanas::2788.simple_meaning: Bharat is so devoted to his mother’s wishes that he is willing to take responsibility for any wrongdoing tied to this decision.
ramacharitamanas::2788.simple_insight: Love can make you absorb blame rather than protect your own image.
ramacharitamanas::2788.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is trying to hold the family together after the exile has shattered the kingdom. He speaks with complete humility, even offering to bear the burden of any wrong if that is what his mother wants, showing how deeply torn duty and family loyalty have become.
ramacharitamanas::2788.modern_relevance: You sit at the dinner table after a family decision has gone badly, and everyone is blaming each other. Instead of defending your pride, you choose to carry the discomfort and keep the bond intact.
ramacharitamanas::2788.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to sacrificial responsibility.

ramacharitamanas::2789.verse_sanskrit: जे परिहरि हरि हर चरन भजहिं भूतगन घोर। तेहि कइ गति मोहि देउ बिधि जौं जननी मत मोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::2789.verse_hindi: जो लोग श्री हरि और श्री शंकरजी के चरणों को छोड़कर भयानक भूत-प्रेतों को भजते हैं, हे माता! यदि इसमें मेरा मत हो तो विधाता मुझे उनकी गति दे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2789.english_translation: Those who abandon Hari and Hara's feet and worship terrifying spirits—if this is my own view, O Mother, may the Creator give me their fate.
