ramacharitamanas::2789.translation_literal: जे (those who) / परिहरि (leaving aside) / हरि (Hari) / हर (Hara) / चरन (feet) / भजहिं (worship) / भूतगन (groups of spirits) / घोर (terrifying) / तेहि (that) / कइ (of) / गति (fate) / मोहि (to me) / देउ (give) / बिधि (Creator) / जौं (if) / जननी (mother) / मत (opinion) / मोर (my)
ramacharitamanas::2789.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2789.essence: Fearful worship cannot replace true refuge.
ramacharitamanas::2789.simple_meaning: People who turn away from Hari and Shiva and instead worship frightening spirits are choosing the wrong refuge. Tulsidas says he would accept their fate if that were his own view.
ramacharitamanas::2789.simple_insight: Your heart settles when it chooses the highest refuge, not fear.
ramacharitamanas::2789.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas pauses the grief of exile and judgment to draw a sharp devotional line. He rejects worship that turns away from Hari and Shiva toward fear-driven powers, and he asks the Creator to judge him by that standard if he is wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2789.modern_relevance: You are anxious at midnight and reach for whatever promises quick relief, even if it deepens the fear. This verse asks whether you are turning toward what truly shelters you, or toward what only feeds panic.
ramacharitamanas::2789.insight: It shifts devotion from fear-based seeking to clear refuge in what is worthy of trust.

ramacharitamanas::2790.verse_sanskrit: बेचहिं बेदु धरमु दुहि लेहीं। पिसुन पराय पाप कहि देहीं॥ कपटी कुटिल कलहप्रिय क्रोधी। बेद बिदूषक बिस्व बिरोधी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2790.verse_hindi: जो लोग वेदों को बेचते हैं, धर्म को दुह लेते हैं, चुगलखोर हैं, दूसरों के पापों को कह देते हैं, जो कपटी, कुटिल, कलहप्रिय और क्रोधी हैं तथा जो वेदों की निंदा करने वाले और विश्वभर के विरोधी हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2790.english_translation: Those who sell the Vedas, milk dharma dry, gossip about others' faults, and are deceitful, crooked, quarrelsome, angry, critics of the Vedas, and enemies of the world...
ramacharitamanas::2790.translation_literal: बेचहिं (sell) / बेदु (the Vedas) / धरमु (dharma) / दुहि (milking) / लेहीं (take away) / पिसुन (slanderous) / पराय (others') / पाप (sins/faults) / कहि (saying) / देहीं (give out) / कपटी (deceitful) / कुटिल (crooked) / कलहप्रिय (fond of quarrels) / क्रोधी (angry) / बेद बिदूषक (mockers of the Vedas) / बिस्व (world) / बिरोधी (opponents)
ramacharitamanas::2790.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2790.essence: Corruption shows itself first in how you speak and what you attack.
ramacharitamanas::2790.simple_meaning: Tulsidas is listing the kinds of people who would fall into terrible ruin: those who misuse sacred learning, exploit righteousness, spread gossip, and live in deceit, conflict, and anger.
ramacharitamanas::2790.simple_insight: A corrupt mind damages everything it touches, including its own understanding.
ramacharitamanas::2790.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is not telling a story event but building a moral warning. He stacks up the traits of people who twist sacred things, harm others with speech, and live in hostility. The next verse continues the list.
ramacharitamanas::2790.modern_relevance: A group chat turns poisonous the moment someone starts trading in gossip, mockery, and outrage. The verse points to the kind of mind that feeds on conflict and slowly poisons every room it enters.
ramacharitamanas::2790.insight: It trains you to recognise moral corruption by its speech, habits, and hostility before it spreads further.

ramacharitamanas::2791.verse_sanskrit: लोभी लंपट लोलुपचारा। जे ताकहिं परधनु परदारा॥ पावौं मैं तिन्ह कै गति घोरा। जौं जननी यहु संमत मोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2791.verse_hindi: जो लोभी, लम्पट और लालचियों का आचरण करने वाले हैं, जो पराए धन और पराई स्त्री की ताक में रहते हैं, हे जननी! यदि इस काम में मेरी सम्मति हो तो मैं उनकी भयानक गति को पाऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2791.english_translation: I would meet the terrible fate of those who are greedy, licentious, and always eyeing other people's wealth and women, if my mother agrees.
ramacharitamanas::2791.translation_literal: लोभी (greedy) / लंपट (licentious) / लोलुपचारा (moving in craving) / जे (those who) / ताकहिं (look toward) / परधनु (other people's wealth) / परदारा (other people's women) / पावौं (may I receive) / मैं (I) / तिन्ह कै (of those) / गति (fate) / घोरा (terrible) / जौं (if) / जननी (mother) / यहु (this) / संमत (approved) / मोरा (my)
ramacharitamanas::2791.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2791.essence: Desire for what is not yours leads straight to ruin.
ramacharitamanas::2791.simple_meaning: Greed and desire for what belongs to others lead to a terrible downfall. Tulsidas says he would accept that fate if his mother approved.
ramacharitamanas::2791.simple_insight: Unchecked wanting doesn't just cloud judgment — it can drag a whole life into ruin.
ramacharitamanas::2791.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas pauses the exile story to warn about moral collapse. After condemning those who chase other people's wealth and women, he says he would accept that same terrible fate if his own mother agreed. The warning is sharp and personal.
ramacharitamanas::2791.modern_relevance: You open a private tab, then another, chasing what someone else has. The verse cuts through that restless hunger before it hardens into character.
ramacharitamanas::2791.insight: It shifts attention from tempting possession to the cost of desire itself.

ramacharitamanas::2792.verse_sanskrit: जे नहिं साधुसंग अनुरागे। परमारथ पथ बिमुख अभागे॥ जे न भजहिं हरि नर तनु पाई। जिन्हहि न हरि हर सुजसु सोहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2792.verse_hindi: जिनका सत्संग में प्रेम नहीं है, जो अभागे परमार्थ के मार्ग से विमुख हैं, जो मनुष्य शरीर पाकर श्री हरि का भजन नहीं करते, जिनको हरि-हर (भगवान विष्णु और शंकरजी) का सुयश नहीं सुहाता, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2792.english_translation: Those who have no love for the company of the good, who are unfortunate and turn away from the path of the highest good; those who do not worship Hari even after receiving a human body, and whom the fame of Hari and Hara does not delight.
ramacharitamanas::2792.translation_literal: जे (those who) / नहिं (not) / साधुसंग (company of the good) / अनुरागे (loving) / परमारथ (highest good) / पथ (path) / बिमुख (turned away) / अभागे (unfortunate) / जे (those who) / न भजहिं (do not worship) / हरि (Hari) / नर तनु (human body) / पाई (having obtained) / जिन्हहि (to whom) / न हरि हर (Hari and Hara) / सुजसु (good fame) / सोहाई (delights)
ramacharitamanas::2792.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2792.essence: Human life is wasted when Ram no longer draws your heart.
ramacharitamanas::2792.simple_meaning: A human life becomes empty when it avoids good company, turns away from what truly matters, and never turns toward Hari.
ramacharitamanas::2792.simple_insight: You are meant for more than drifting; the right company and devotion restore your direction.
ramacharitamanas::2792.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is listing the signs of a life that has lost its way: no love for saintly company, no pull toward the highest good, no worship of Hari despite receiving a human birth. In this Ayodhyakand passage, he is warning that the rare gift of life can be wasted.
ramacharitamanas::2792.modern_relevance: You keep scrolling past the one friend who actually steadies you, then wonder why your mind feels scattered. This verse points straight at that drift: the people you keep close and what you praise shape your whole life.
ramacharitamanas::2792.insight: It shifts attention from random desire to the habits that either nourish or waste a human life.

ramacharitamanas::2793.verse_sanskrit: तजि श्रुतिपंथु बाम पथ चलहीं। बंचक बिरचि बेष जगु छलहीं॥ तिन्ह कै गति मोहि संकर देऊ। जननी जौं यहु जानौं भेऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2793.verse_hindi: जो वेद मार्ग को छोड़कर वाम (वेद प्रतिकूल) मार्ग पर चलते हैं, जो ठग हैं और वेष बनाकर जगत को छलते हैं, हे माता! यदि मैं इस भेद को जानता भी होऊँ तो शंकरजी मुझे उन लोगों की गति दें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2793.english_translation: Those who leave the straight path of the Vedas and walk a crooked road, who are deceitful and disguise themselves to cheat the world—Mother, if I know such people, may Shiva give me their fate.
ramacharitamanas::2793.translation_literal: तजि (leaving) / श्रुतिपंथु (the path of the Vedas) / बाम पथ (crooked path) / चलहीं (they walk) / बंचक (deceitful) / बिरचि (making) / बेष (disguise) / जगु (the world) / छलहीं (they cheat) / तिन्ह (of those) / कै गति (fate) / मोहि (to me) / संकर देऊ (Shiva may give) / जननी (Mother) / जौं (if) / यहु (this) / जानौं (I know) / भेऊ (secret)
ramacharitamanas::2793.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2793.essence: False appearance corrupts the one who chooses it.
ramacharitamanas::2793.simple_meaning: Bharat rejects deceit, hypocrisy, and crooked conduct so strongly that he says he would rather be punished than understand such people.
ramacharitamanas::2793.simple_insight: Integrity can be so complete that even knowing dishonesty feels like contamination.
ramacharitamanas::2793.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is speaking with his mother about right conduct after Ram's exile has shattered the family. He condemns those who abandon the true path, wear false appearances, and trick the world. His refusal is so intense that he calls on Shiva to give him their fate if he ever shares their mindset.
ramacharitamanas::2793.modern_relevance: You sit through a meeting where everyone smiles, but half the room is performing. Bharat's words hit that moment hard: you can refuse the mask, even if it costs you approval.
ramacharitamanas::2793.insight: It trains you to see false appearance as a moral danger, not a clever survival skill.

ramacharitamanas::2794.verse_sanskrit: मातु भरत के बचन सुनि साँचे सरल सुभायँ। कहति राम प्रिय तात तुम्ह सदा बचन मन कायँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2794.verse_hindi: माता कौसल्याजी भरतजी के स्वाभाविक ही सच्चे और सरल वचनों को सुनकर कहने लगीं- हे तात! तुम तो मन, वचन और शरीर से सदा ही श्री रामचन्द्र के प्यारे हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2794.english_translation: Hearing Bharata's sincere, simple words, Mother Kaushalya said, “Dear son, you are always beloved to Ram in mind, speech, and body.”
ramacharitamanas::2794.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / भरत के (of Bharata's) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / साँचे (true) / सरल (simple, straight) / सुभायँ (by nature) / कहति (says) / राम प्रिय (beloved of Ram) / तात (dear son) / तुम्ह (you) / सदा (always) / बचन (speech) / मन (mind) / कायँ (body)
ramacharitamanas::2794.speaker: Kaushalya
ramacharitamanas::2794.essence: True love shows itself when mind, speech, and action all agree.
ramacharitamanas::2794.simple_meaning: Kaushalya tells Bharata that his honest, simple nature makes him always dear to Ram in thought, speech, and action.
ramacharitamanas::2794.simple_insight: Sincerity itself becomes devotion when your whole life matches your heart.
ramacharitamanas::2794.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharata has returned in grief and humility. Kaushalya hears the truth in his plain words and blesses him: his mind, speech, and body are all aligned with Ram. The family sees that his love is not performative but complete.
ramacharitamanas::2794.modern_relevance: You speak plainly to someone you love, with no hidden agenda. They feel it immediately — because your words, intentions, and actions all match.
ramacharitamanas::2794.insight: It shifts devotion from display to alignment: what matters is whether your whole being points the same way.

ramacharitamanas::2795.verse_sanskrit: राम प्रानहु तें प्रान तुम्हारे। तुम्ह रघुपतिहि प्रानहु तें प्यारे॥ बिधु बिष चवै स्रवै हिमु आगी। होइ बारिचर बारि बिरागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2795.verse_hindi: श्री राम तुम्हारे प्राणों से भी बढ़कर प्राण (प्रिय) हैं और तुम भी श्री रघुनाथ को प्राणों से भी अधिक प्यारे हो। चन्द्रमा चाहे विष चुआने लगे और पाला आग बरसाने लगे, जलचर जीव जल से विरक्त हो जाए, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2795.english_translation: Ram is dearer to you than life itself, and you are dearer to Raghupati than life itself. If the moon dripped poison, if frost rained fire, if a water-dwelling creature grew indifferent to water, ...
ramacharitamanas::2795.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / प्रानहु तें (than life/breath itself) / प्रान (life/breath) / तुम्हारे (your) / तुम्ह (you) / रघुपतिहि (to Raghupati) / प्रानहु तें (than life/breath itself) / प्यारे (dear) / बिधु (moon) / बिष (poison) / चवै (drip) / स्रवै (flow) / हिमु (frost) / आगी (fire) / होइ (becomes) / बारिचर (water-dwelling creature) / बारि (water) / बिरागी (indifferent)
ramacharitamanas::2795.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::2795.essence: A true bond survives even when the world turns impossible.
ramacharitamanas::2795.simple_meaning: Kausalya tells Bharat that Ram is more precious to him than life, and Bharat is equally dear to Ram. Even impossible reversals in nature would be easier than changing that bond.
ramacharitamanas::2795.simple_insight: Real love can be mutual, steady, and stronger than any outward circumstance.
ramacharitamanas::2795.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kausalya is speaking to Bharat after seeing his pure loyalty and grief. She blesses the bond between Bharat and Ram as something nature itself cannot undo. The verse prepares the next point: Bharat will never turn against Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2795.modern_relevance: You have a friend who would cross town at midnight just to sit with you after bad news. No one is keeping score, but both of you know the bond is real.
ramacharitamanas::2795.insight: It shifts attention from fragile social ties to a bond rooted in mutual devotion and steadfastness.

ramacharitamanas::2796.verse_sanskrit: भएँ ग्यानु बरु मिटै न मोहू। तुम्ह रामहि प्रतिकूल न होहू॥ मत तुम्हार यहु जो जग कहहीं। सो सपनेहुँ सुख सुगति न लहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2796.verse_hindi: और ज्ञान हो जाने पर भी चाहे मोह न मिटे, पर तुम श्री रामचन्द्र के प्रतिकूल कभी नहीं हो सकते। इसमें तुम्हारी सम्मति है, जगत में जो कोई ऐसा कहते हैं, वे स्वप्न में भी सुख और शुभ गति नहीं पावेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2796.english_translation: Even if knowledge arises and delusion does not fully fade, you can never stand against Ram. What the world says is your approval—those who say such a thing will not find happiness or a good end, even in a dream.
ramacharitamanas::2796.translation_literal: भएँ (having arisen) / ग्यानु (knowledge) / बरु (even if) / मिटै (is erased) / न (not) / मोहू (delusion) / तुम्ह (you) / रामहि (to Ram) / प्रतिकूल (opposed) / न (not) / होहू (become) ॥ / मत (opinion/consent) / तुम्हार (your) / यहु (this) / जो (which) / जग (the world) / कहहीं (they say) ॥ / सो (those) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / सुख (happiness) / सुगति (good destination) / न (not) / लहहीं (obtain) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2796.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::2796.essence: Loyalty to Ram cannot be overturned by confusion or gossip.
ramacharitamanas::2796.simple_meaning: Even if confusion remains, you can still stay loyal to Ram. The world may speak wrongly about you, but that does not make it true.
ramacharitamanas::2796.simple_insight: You can be misunderstood and still remain steady in what you know is right.
ramacharitamanas::2796.detailed_meaning: Kausalya is holding Bharat close after hearing his pure-hearted words. She reassures him that even if some confusion remains, he cannot be against Ram. She also rejects the world’s gossip about his intentions.
ramacharitamanas::2796.modern_relevance: A family group chat starts spinning your choice into something ugly, and suddenly everyone has an opinion about your motives. This verse says their story does not define your heart.
ramacharitamanas::2796.insight: It shifts you from defending your image to trusting the integrity of your own loyalty.

ramacharitamanas::2797.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि मातु भरतु हिएँ लाए। थन पय स्रवहिं नयन जल छाए॥ करत बिलाप बहुत एहि भाँती। बैठेहिं बीति गई सब राती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2797.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर माता कौसल्या ने भरतजी को हृदय से लगा लिया। उनके स्तनों से दूध बहने लगा और नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल छा गया। इस प्रकार बहुत विलाप करते हुए सारी रात बैठे ही बैठे बीत गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2797.english_translation: Saying this, Mother Kaushalya drew Bharat into her heart. Milk flowed from her breasts and tears covered her eyes. In this way, they kept lamenting, and the whole night passed sitting there.
ramacharitamanas::2797.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / मातु (mother) / भरतु (Bharat) / हिएँ (into the heart) / लाए (brought embraced) / थन (breasts) / पय (milk) / स्रवहिं (flow) / नयन (eyes) / जल (water/tears) / छाए (covered) / करत (doing) / बिलाप (lamentation) / बहुत (much) / एहि भाँती (in this manner) / बैठेहिं (sitting) / बीति गई (passed) / सब (all) / राती (night)
ramacharitamanas::2797.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2797.essence: Love can hold grief without fixing it.
ramacharitamanas::2797.simple_meaning: Kaushalya hugs Bharat and weeps with him all night. Their grief is so deep that even her body responds like a mother’s at the sight of her child.
ramacharitamanas::2797.simple_insight: Some losses are too deep for words; love simply holds and weeps.
ramacharitamanas::2797.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat has returned to a kingdom shattered by Ram's exile and Dasharath's death. Kaushalya, Ram's mother, pulls Bharat close as if he were her own child. Their shared grief fills the night, and no one can yet move forward.
ramacharitamanas::2797.modern_relevance: You hold your brother after a funeral and neither of you knows what to say. Grief does not need polished language; sometimes it only needs an embrace that lasts through the night.
ramacharitamanas::2797.insight: It shifts attention from solving grief to witnessing it with tenderness.

ramacharitamanas::2798.verse_sanskrit: बामदेउ बसिष्ठ तब आए। सचिव महाजन सकल बोलाए॥ मुनि बहु भाँति भरत उपदेसे। कहि परमारथ बचन सुदेसे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2798.verse_hindi: तब वामदेवजी और वशिष्ठजी आए। उन्होंने सब मंत्रियों तथा महाजनों को बुलाया। फिर मुनि वशिष्ठजी ने परमार्थ के सुंदर समयानुकूल वचन कहकर बहुत प्रकार से भरतजी को उपदेश दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2798.english_translation: Then Vamadeva and Vashistha came. They called all the ministers and leading elders. The sage gave Bharat many kinds of instruction, speaking timely words of highest truth.
ramacharitamanas::2798.translation_literal: बामदेउ (Vamadeva) / बसिष्ठ (Vashistha) / तब (then) / आए (came) / सचिव (ministers) / महाजन (leading elders) / सकल (all) / बोलाए (called) / मुनि (sage) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / भरत (Bharat) / उपदेसे (instructed) / कहि (speaking) / परमारथ (highest truth) / बचन (words) / सुदेसे (timely/good instruction)
ramacharitamanas::2798.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2798.essence: Steady counsel gathers people when grief has made them unsteady.
ramacharitamanas::2798.simple_meaning: Vashistha and Vamadeva arrive, gather the ministers and elders, and begin guiding Bharat with timely, serious counsel.
ramacharitamanas::2798.simple_insight: Sometimes the right help is calm guidance, not more emotion.
ramacharitamanas::2798.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the night of grief, the elders gather around Bharat. Vamadeva and Vashistha arrive and call the ministers and respected men together. The moment calls for steadiness, so Vashistha begins teaching Bharat what must be done next.
ramacharitamanas::2798.modern_relevance: After a family crisis, everyone is exhausted, and the room is full of tears and unfinished decisions. Then the one steady elder speaks, gathers everyone, and names the next right step.
ramacharitamanas::2798.insight: It shifts attention from emotional collapse to the responsibility of guiding the moment wisely.

ramacharitamanas::2799.verse_sanskrit: तात हृदयँ धीरजु धरहु करहु जो अवसर आजु। उठे भरत गुर बचन सुनि करन कहेउ सबु साजु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2799.verse_hindi: (वशिष्ठजी ने कहा-) हे तात! हृदय में धीरज धरो और आज जिस कार्य के करने का अवसर है, उसे करो। गुरुजी के वचन सुनकर भरतजी उठे और उन्होंने सब तैयारी करने के लिए कहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2799.english_translation: O dear one, keep courage in your heart and do today what must be done. Hearing the guru's words, Bharata rose and said to make all the arrangements.
ramacharitamanas::2799.translation_literal: तात (dear one) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / धीरजु (patience, courage) / धरहु (hold) / करहु (do) / जो (which) / अवसर (occasion, task) / आजु (today) / उठे (rose) / भरत (Bharata) / गुर (guru's) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / करन (to do) / कहेउ (said) / सबु (all) / साजु (arrangements)
ramacharitamanas::2799.speaker: Vasishtha
ramacharitamanas::2799.essence: Courage is holding steady long enough to do what the moment requires.
ramacharitamanas::2799.simple_meaning: Keep your heart steady and do the task in front of you. Bharata hears the guidance, rises at once, and begins the necessary arrangements.
ramacharitamanas::2799.simple_insight: Pressure becomes bearable when you focus only on the next rightful act.
ramacharitamanas::2799.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Dasharath's death, grief has flooded the palace. Vasishtha gives Bharata one clear instruction: steady your heart and do what this moment requires. Bharata rises immediately and begins the preparations.
ramacharitamanas::2799.modern_relevance: Your phone rings with bad news, the house is full of crying, and someone still has to make the next call. This verse gives you one clean instruction: steady yourself and do the needed thing.
ramacharitamanas::2799.insight: It shifts attention from emotional overwhelm to the one action the moment demands.

ramacharitamanas::2800.verse_sanskrit: नृपतनु बेद बिदित अन्हवावा। परम बिचित्र बिमानु बनावा॥ गाहि पदभरत मातु सब राखी। रहीं रानि दरसन अभिलाषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2800.verse_hindi: वेदों में बताई हुई विधि से राजा की देह को स्नान कराया गया और परम विचित्र विमान बनाया गया। भरतजी ने सब माताओं को चरण पकड़कर रखा (अर्थात प्रार्थना करके उनको सती होने से रोक लिया)। वे रानियाँ भी (श्री राम के) दर्शन की अभिलाषा से रह गईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2800.english_translation: The king's body was bathed according to the Vedas, and a wondrous bier was prepared. Bharat held back all the queens by clasping their feet. The queens remained longing for Ram's darshan.
ramacharitamanas::2800.translation_literal: नृपतनु (the king's body) / बेद बिदित (known by the Vedas) / अन्हवावा (was bathed) / परम बिचित्र (most wondrous) / बिमानु (bier/vehicle) / बनावा (was made) / गाहि (grasping) / पद (feet) / भरत (Bharat) / मातु (mothers/queens) / सब (all) / राखी (held back) / रहीं (remained) / रानि (queens) / दरसन (darshan) / अभिलाषी (longing)
ramacharitamanas::2800.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2800.essence: Love sometimes protects by holding others back.
ramacharitamanas::2800.simple_meaning: Dasharath's body is prepared for the last rites, while Bharat stops the queens from joining him in death. Their hearts stay fixed on seeing Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2800.simple_insight: Grief can be held with care, not only acted out.
ramacharitamanas::2800.detailed_meaning: After Dasharath's death in Ayodhya, the rites begin. Bharat, already carrying unbearable sorrow, prevents the queens from following the king in death. Around the body, longing for Ram still hangs over everyone.
ramacharitamanas::2800.modern_relevance: A family gathers after a death, and someone has to stop the room from collapsing into panic. This verse holds that painful moment where love means restraint.
ramacharitamanas::2800.insight: It shifts grief from impulsive action to protective steadiness.

ramacharitamanas::2801.verse_sanskrit: चंदन अगर भार बहु आए। अमित अनेक सुगंध सुहाए॥ सरजु तीर रचि चिता बनाई। जनु सुरपुर सोपान सुहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2801.verse_hindi: चंदन और अगर के तथा और भी अनेकों प्रकार के अपार (कपूर, गुग्गुल, केसर आदि) सुगंध द्रव्यों के बहुत से बोझ आए। सरयूजी के तट पर सुंदर चिता रचकर बनाई गई, (जो ऐसी मालूम होती थी) मानो स्वर्ग की सुंदर सीढ़ी हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2801.english_translation: Loads of sandalwood, agarwood, and many fragrant materials arrived. On the bank of the Sarayu, a beautiful funeral pyre was built, like a lovely stairway to the higher realm.
ramacharitamanas::2801.translation_literal: चंदन (sandalwood) / अगर (agarwood) / भार (loads) / बहु (many) / आए (came) / अमित (countless) / अनेक (many) / सुगंध (fragrances) / सुहाए (pleasant) / सरजु (Sarayu) / तीर (bank) / रचि (having built) / चिता (funeral pyre) / बनाई (was made) / जनु (as if) / सुरपुर (higher realm) / सोपान (stairway) / सुहाई (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::2801.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2801.essence: Even the last farewell can be made beautiful with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2801.simple_meaning: Many fragrant materials are brought, and a beautiful funeral pyre is built by the Sarayu River like a stairway to the higher realm.
ramacharitamanas::2801.simple_insight: Even grief is being met with care, beauty, and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2801.detailed_meaning: After Dasharath’s body is prepared, the people of Ayodhya gather what is needed for the cremation. The verse lingers on the fragrant woods and the carefully built pyre by the Sarayu, turning a moment of loss into one of solemn dignity.
ramacharitamanas::2801.modern_relevance: You watch relatives carry flowers, wood, and cloth to a cremation ground, each detail handled with quiet respect. Even in farewell, love tries to make the last act beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::2801.insight: It shifts attention from raw loss to the dignity with which a final rite is carried out.

ramacharitamanas::2802.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि दाह क्रिया सब कीन्ही। बिधिवत न्हाइ तिलांजुलि दीन्ही॥ सोधि सुमृति सब बेद पुराना। कीन्ह भरत दसगात बिधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2802.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार सब दाह क्रिया की गई और सबने विधिपूर्वक स्नान करके तिलांजलि दी। फिर वेद, स्मृति और पुराण सबका मत निश्चय करके उसके अनुसार भरतजी ने पिता का दशगात्र विधान (दस दिनों के कृत्य) किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2802.english_translation: In this way, all the funeral rites were completed. Everyone bathed properly and offered water mixed with sesame. After consulting the Vedas, Smritis, and Puranas, Bharat carried out the ten-day rites for his father.
ramacharitamanas::2802.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / दाह क्रिया (funeral rites) / सब (all) / कीन्ही (were done) / बिधिवत (according to proper rule) / न्हाइ (bathing) / तिलांजुलि (sesame-water offering) / दीन्ही (was given) / सोधि (having examined) / सुमृति (Smriti texts) / सब (all) / बेद (Vedas) / पुराना (Puranas) / कीन्ह (did) / भरत (Bharat) / दसगात (ten-day rites) / बिधाना (ritual procedure)
ramacharitamanas::2802.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2802.essence: Even in grief, Bharat does what duty requires.
ramacharitamanas::2802.simple_meaning: The funeral was performed exactly as prescribed, and Bharat completed the required rites for his father after consulting sacred tradition.
ramacharitamanas::2802.simple_insight: Grief can still be held with care, order, and respect.
ramacharitamanas::2802.detailed_meaning: Dasharath has died in Ayodhya, and Bharat is carrying the weight of a kingdom and a son's sorrow. After the cremation, he follows every required rite with precision, consulting sacred authorities so nothing is left undone.
ramacharitamanas::2802.modern_relevance: You are arranging every detail after a parent’s death, even while your hands shake. Love can still show up as careful responsibility.
ramacharitamanas::2802.insight: It shifts grief into dutiful action, showing that sorrow does not excuse neglect.

ramacharitamanas::2803.verse_sanskrit: जहँ जस मुनिबर आयसु दीन्हा। तहँ तस सहस भाँति सबु कीन्हा॥ भए बिसुद्ध दिए सब दाना। धेनु बाजि गज बाहन नाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2803.verse_hindi: मुनि श्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी ने जहाँ जैसी आज्ञा दी, वहाँ भरतजी ने सब वैसा ही हजारों प्रकार से किया। शुद्ध हो जाने पर (विधिपूर्वक) सब दान दिए। गायें तथा घोड़े, हाथी आदि अनेक प्रकार की सवारियाँ, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2803.english_translation: Wherever the sage Vashishtha gave an order, Bharat carried it out in a thousand ways. After becoming purified, he gave all the gifts in proper form: cows, horses, elephants, and many other vehicles.
ramacharitamanas::2803.translation_literal: जहँ (wherever) / जस (as) / मुनिबर (best of sages) / आयसु (order) / दीन्हा (gave) / तहँ (there) / तस (so) / सहस भाँति (thousand ways) / सबु (all) / कीन्हा (did) ॥ भए (became) / बिसुद्ध (pure) / दिए (gave) / सब (all) / दाना (gifts) / धेनु (cows) / बाजि (horses) / गज (elephants) / बाहन (vehicles) / नाना (many)
ramacharitamanas::2803.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2803.essence: Obedience becomes grace when it is carried out completely.
ramacharitamanas::2803.simple_meaning: Bharat obeyed Vashishtha’s instructions completely and gave away everything properly, including cows, horses, elephants, and other gifts.
ramacharitamanas::2803.simple_insight: True humility shows up in how completely you follow what is right.
ramacharitamanas::2803.detailed_meaning: After Dasharath’s death, Bharat is carrying out the rites at the riverbank. Vashishtha guides the ceremony, and Bharat responds without resistance, giving gifts in full measure. The verse shows his disciplined obedience and generosity.
ramacharitamanas::2803.modern_relevance: You’re in the middle of a family ritual, tired and grieving, but you still do every step properly because it matters. Bharat’s steadiness is that kind of respect.
ramacharitamanas::2803.insight: It teaches you to act with exactness and generosity when duty is already heavy.

ramacharitamanas::2804.verse_sanskrit: सिंघासन भूषन बसन अन्न धरनि धन धाम। दिए भरत लहि भूमिसुर भे परिपूरन काम ॥
ramacharitamanas::2804.verse_hindi: सिंहासन, गहने, कपड़े, अन्न, पृथ्वी, धन और मकान भरतजी ने दिए, भूदेव ब्राह्मण दान पाकर परिपूर्णकाम हो गए (अर्थात उनकी सारी मनोकामनाएँ अच्छी तरह से पूरी हो गईं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2804.english_translation: Bharat gave away thrones, ornaments, clothes, food, land, wealth, and houses. The Brahmins received full gifts and their wishes were completely fulfilled.
ramacharitamanas::2804.translation_literal: सिंघासन (throne) / भूषन (ornaments) / बसन (clothes) / अन्न (food) / धरनि (land) / धन (wealth) / धाम (house) / दिए (gave) / भरत (Bharat) / लहि (having received) / भूमिसुर (Brahmins) / भे (became) / परिपूरन (fully) / काम (desires)
ramacharitamanas::2804.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2804.essence: Real renunciation gives away even what looks most precious.
ramacharitamanas::2804.simple_meaning: Bharat gave away royal goods, wealth, and property as gifts to the Brahmins, leaving them fully satisfied.
ramacharitamanas::2804.simple_insight: Generosity becomes complete when nothing is held back for yourself.
ramacharitamanas::2804.detailed_meaning: After Dasharath’s funeral rites in Ayodhya, Bharat follows Vashistha’s instructions and gives away royal possessions, land, wealth, and household goods to the Brahmins. The verse shows his grief expressed as self-emptying service.
ramacharitamanas::2804.modern_relevance: After a family loss, someone quietly sorts through the house and gives away what can help others — clothes, furniture, valuables. Grief turns into generosity, and the giving itself becomes a way of honoring love.
ramacharitamanas::2804.insight: It shifts the mind from keeping and controlling to releasing and serving.

ramacharitamanas::2805.verse_sanskrit: पितु हित भरत कीन्हि जसि करनी। सो मुख लाख जाइ नहिं बरनी॥ सुदिनु सोधि मुनिबर तब आए। सचिव महाजन सकल बोलाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2805.verse_hindi: पिताजी के लिए भरतजी ने जैसी करनी की वह लाखों मुखों से भी वर्णन नहीं की जा सकती। तब शुभ दिन शोधकर श्रेष्ठ मुनि वशिष्ठजी आए और उन्होंने मंत्रियों तथा सब महाजनों को बुलवाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2805.english_translation: The way Bharat served his father cannot be described by millions of mouths. Then, after choosing an auspicious day, the great sage Vashishtha came and summoned the ministers and all the elders.
ramacharitamanas::2805.translation_literal: पितु (father's) / हित (for welfare) / भरत (Bharat) / कीन्हि (did) / जसि (as) / करनी (deed) / सो (that) / मुख (mouth) / लाख (a hundred thousand) / जाइ (go) / नहिं (not) / बरनी (described) / सुदिनु (auspicious day) / सोधि (choosing) / मुनिबर (great sage) / तब (then) / आए (came) / सचिव (ministers) / महाजन (elders) / सकल (all) / बोलाए (called)
ramacharitamanas::2805.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2805.essence: Some acts of filial service are too vast for words.
ramacharitamanas::2805.simple_meaning: Bharat's service to his father was beyond description. After that, Vashishtha arrived on an auspicious day and called together the ministers and elders.
ramacharitamanas::2805.simple_insight: True devotion often speaks through action so large that words fail.
ramacharitamanas::2805.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat has already shown extraordinary loyalty and sacrifice for his father. The narrator pauses to praise that service as beyond speech, then shifts the scene: Vashishtha arrives on an auspicious day and gathers the kingdom's leaders for the next step.
ramacharitamanas::2805.modern_relevance: You quietly handled your father's hospital paperwork, calls, and bills for weeks. Nobody posted about it. Nobody needed to. Some acts are too full for praise.
ramacharitamanas::2805.insight: It highlights service so complete that recognition becomes irrelevant, then moves the story toward the next public gathering.

ramacharitamanas::2806.verse_sanskrit: बैठे राजसभाँ सब जाई। पठए बोलि भरत दोउ भाई॥ भरतु बसिष्ठ निकट बैठारे। नीति धरममय बचन उचारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2806.verse_hindi: सब लोग राजसभा में जाकर बैठ गए। तब मुनि ने भरतजी तथा शत्रुघ्नजी दोनों भाइयों को बुलवा भेजा। भरतजी को वशिष्ठजी ने अपने पास बैठा लिया और नीति तथा धर्म से भरे हुए वचन कहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2806.english_translation: Everyone went and sat in the royal assembly. Then the sage sent for both brothers, Bharat and Shatrughna. Vashishtha seated Bharat near him and spoke words full of policy and dharma.
ramacharitamanas::2806.translation_literal: बैठे (sat) / राजसभाँ (in the royal assembly) / सब (all) / जाई (going) / पठए (sent for) / बोलि (calling) / भरत (Bharat) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / भरतु (Bharat) / बसिष्ठ (Vashishtha) / निकट (near) / बैठारे (made sit) / नीति (policy) / धरममय (full of dharma) / बचन (words) / उचारे (spoke)
ramacharitamanas::2806.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2806.essence: Wise counsel begins when the right person is seated close enough to listen.
ramacharitamanas::2806.simple_meaning: The court gathers, Bharat and Shatrughna are called in, and Vashishtha places Bharat close to him to speak wise, righteous words.
ramacharitamanas::2806.simple_insight: Sometimes guidance begins with being brought close enough to hear clearly.
ramacharitamanas::2806.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court has assembled after the great grief in the royal house. Vashishtha calls Bharat and Shatrughna forward, seats Bharat beside him, and begins the counsel that will explain recent events and shape the brothers' response.
ramacharitamanas::2806.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense family meeting and someone who knows the whole story asks you to sit beside them before speaking. That small gesture changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::2806.insight: It shifts the moment from public confusion to intimate instruction, where dharma can be heard without noise.

ramacharitamanas::2807.verse_sanskrit: प्रथम कथा सब मुनिबर बरनी। कैकइ कुटिल कीन्हि जसि करनी॥ भूप धरमुब्रतु सत्य सराहा। जेहिं तनु परिहरि प्रेमु निबाहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2807.verse_hindi: पहले तो कैकेयी ने जैसी कुटिल करनी की थी, श्रेष्ठ मुनि ने वह सारी कथा कही। फिर राजा के धर्मव्रत और सत्य की सराहना की, जिन्होंने शरीर त्याग कर प्रेम को निबाहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2807.english_translation: First, the sage recounted Kaikeyi's crooked deed in full. Then he praised the king's vow of truth and duty, for he gave up his body yet kept faith with love.
ramacharitamanas::2807.translation_literal: प्रथम (first) / कथा (story) / सब (all) / मुनिबर (best of sages) / बरनी (described) / कैकइ (Kaikeyi) / कुटिल (crooked) / कीन्हि (did) / जसि (as) / करनी (deed)॥ / भूप (king) / धरमुब्रतु (vow of dharma) / सत्य (truth) / सराहा (praised) / जेहिं (who) / तनु (body) / परिहरि (having left) / प्रेमु (love) / निबाहा (kept/fulfilled)॥
ramacharitamanas::2807.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2807.essence: True love is proved by truth kept at the cost of everything.
ramacharitamanas::2807.simple_meaning: The sage first tells how Kaikeyi acted wrongly, then praises the king for keeping truth and love even as he gave up his body.
ramacharitamanas::2807.simple_insight: A life can be measured by what it refuses to break, even under loss.
ramacharitamanas::2807.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court is gathering around Bharat's grief. Vashishtha begins by naming Kaikeyi's harmful action, then turns to Dasharath's greatness: he held to truth and love even when it cost him his life. It is part of a larger consolation, not the passage's final teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2807.modern_relevance: At a family meeting after a painful inheritance dispute, someone finally names the betrayal, then remembers the parent who stayed honest even while breaking apart.
ramacharitamanas::2807.insight: It shifts attention from blame alone to the harder praise of integrity under suffering.

ramacharitamanas::2808.verse_sanskrit: कहत राम गुन सील सुभाऊ। सजल नयन पुलकेउ मुनिराऊ॥ बहुरि लखन सिय प्रीति बखानी। सोक सनेह मगन मुनि ग्यानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2808.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुण, शील और स्वभाव का वर्णन करते-करते तो मुनिराज के नेत्रों में जल भर आया और वे शरीर से पुलकित हो गए। फिर लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी के प्रेम की बड़ाई करते हुए ज्ञानी मुनि शोक और स्नेह में मग्न हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2808.english_translation: As he spoke of Ram's virtues, character, and nature, the sage's eyes filled with tears and his body thrilled. Then, praising Lakshman and Sita's love, the wise sage became lost in sorrow and affection.
ramacharitamanas::2808.translation_literal: कहत (speaking) / राम (Ram) / गुन (qualities) / सील (character) / सुभाऊ (nature) / सजल (moist) / नयन (eyes) / पुलकेउ (thrilled) / मुनिराऊ (sage-king) / बहुरि (again) / लखन (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / प्रीति (love) / बखानी (praised) / सोक (sorrow) / सनेह (affection) / मगन (immersed) / मुनि (sage) / ग्यानी (wise)
ramacharitamanas::2808.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2808.essence: Praise of Ram becomes tears, and tears become devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2808.simple_meaning: The sage is overwhelmed with emotion while praising Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Their virtues move him so deeply that tears, joy, sorrow, and love all rise together.
ramacharitamanas::2808.simple_insight: Real devotion is not cold admiration; it can fill you with tears, tenderness, and reverence at once.
ramacharitamanas::2808.detailed_meaning: In Bharadwaj's gathering, the sage finishes recounting Ram's story and then turns to Lakshman's and Sita's love. The words do not stay abstract: the speaker is visibly moved, showing how deeply this family embodies devotion, duty, and sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2808.modern_relevance: You hear someone describe a person who kept every promise, and suddenly your own eyes sting. Some lives are so steady, so loving, they break through your defenses.
ramacharitamanas::2808.insight: It shows that true praise can become a form of surrender, where emotion itself confirms what the mind knows.

ramacharitamanas::2809.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु भरत भावी प्रबल बिलखि कहेउ मुनिनाथ। हानि लाभु जीवनु मरनु जसु अपजसु बिधि हाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2809.verse_hindi: मुनिनाथ ने बिलखकर (दुःखी होकर) कहा- हे भरत! सुनो, भावी (होनहार) बड़ी बलवान है। हानि-लाभ, जीवन-मरण और यश-अपयश, ये सब विधाता के हाथ हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2809.english_translation: Listen, Bharat. Fate is strong, the sage said in grief. Loss and gain, life and death, fame and disgrace are all in the hands of the divine order.
ramacharitamanas::2809.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / भरत (Bharat) / भावी (fate) / प्रबल (strong) / बिलखि (grievingly) / कहेउ (said) / मुनिनाथ (lord of sages) / हानि (loss) / लाभु (gain) / जीवनु (life) / मरनु (death) / जसु (fame) / अपजसु (disgrace) / बिधि (divine order) / हाथ (in the hands)
ramacharitamanas::2809.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2809.essence: What happens to you is not fully yours to command.
ramacharitamanas::2809.simple_meaning: The sage tells Bharat that outcomes are not fully in human control. Gain, loss, life, death, praise, and blame all unfold under a larger order.
ramacharitamanas::2809.simple_insight: It brings relief: you can do your part without carrying the whole universe on your back.
ramacharitamanas::2809.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the sage is speaking to Bharat after the kingdom has been shattered by exile and grief. He is trying to steady Bharat's heart by showing that praise, blame, survival, and loss all move according to a larger order.
ramacharitamanas::2809.modern_relevance: You refresh your inbox and see the decision went the other way. The sting is real, but this verse reminds you that not every outcome was ever yours to hold.
ramacharitamanas::2809.insight: It shifts the mind from personal control to humble acceptance of what unfolds.

ramacharitamanas::2810.verse_sanskrit: अस बिचारि केहि देइअ दोसू। ब्यरथ काहि पर कीजिअ रोसू॥ तात बिचारु करहु मन माहीं। सोच जोगु दसरथु नृपु नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2810.verse_hindi: ऐसा विचार कर किसे दोष दिया जाए? और व्यर्थ किस पर क्रोध किया जाए? हे तात! मन में विचार करो। राजा दशरथ सोच करने के योग्य नहीं हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2810.english_translation: With this in mind, whom should you blame? Why waste anger on anyone? O dear one, think carefully in your heart. King Dasharath is not someone to grieve over.
ramacharitamanas::2810.translation_literal: अस (thus) / बिचारि (having considered) / केहि (whom) / देइअ (should be given) / दोसू (blame) / ब्यरथ (futile) / काहि (on whom) / पर (upon) / कीजिअ (should be done) / रोसू (anger) / तात (dear one) / बिचारु (reflection) / करहु (do) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / सोच (grief) / जोगु (fit for) / दसरथु (Dasharath) / नृपु (king) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::2810.speaker: Muni
ramacharitamanas::2810.essence: Grief becomes clearer when you stop searching for someone to punish.
ramacharitamanas::2810.simple_meaning: There is no useful person to blame here, and anger will not help. The wiser response is to think calmly and accept that Dasharath's sorrow is not something to dwell on.
ramacharitamanas::2810.simple_insight: Not every pain needs a culprit. Sometimes the only clean response is to stop fighting the fact of loss.
ramacharitamanas::2810.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the sage is speaking to Bharat after the blow of exile and royal loss has shaken the whole family. He asks Bharat to look beyond blame and anger, and to see that Dasharath's suffering is not a matter for resentment but for clear, sorrowful understanding.
ramacharitamanas::2810.modern_relevance: You replay the argument after the funeral, looking for who ruined everything. But some losses have no villain you can punish. The first mercy is to stop turning grief into blame.
ramacharitamanas::2810.insight: It shifts the mind from accusation to clear seeing, so sorrow can be held without adding more harm.

ramacharitamanas::2811.verse_sanskrit: सोचिअ बिप्र जो बेद बिहीना। तजि निज धरमु बिषय लयलीना॥ सोचिअ नृपति जो नीति न जाना। जेहि न प्रजा प्रिय प्रान समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2811.verse_hindi: सोच उस ब्राह्मण का करना चाहिए, जो वेद नहीं जानता और जो अपना धर्म छोड़कर विषय भोग में ही लीन रहता है। उस राजा का सोच करना चाहिए, जो नीति नहीं जानता और जिसको प्रजा प्राणों के समान प्यारी नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2811.english_translation: You should worry about a Brahmin who does not know the Vedas and is absorbed in sensual pleasure after abandoning his own duty. You should worry about a king who does not know right conduct and does not love his people as dearly as life itself.
ramacharitamanas::2811.translation_literal: सोचिअ (should be worried about) / बिप्र (Brahmin) / जो (who) / बेद (the Vedas) / बिहीना (without) / तजि (abandoning) / निज (own) / धरमु (duty) / बिषय (sensual objects) / लयलीना (absorbed) ॥ / सोचिअ (should be worried about) / नृपति (king) / जो (who) / नीति (right conduct) / न जाना (does not know) / जेहि (whom) / न (not) / प्रजा (subjects) / प्रिय (dear) / प्रान (life) / समाना (equal to) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2811.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2811.essence: A role becomes shameful when it loses its duty.
ramacharitamanas::2811.simple_meaning: A person in a role should be judged by whether they live that role well. A priest without learning and a ruler without care for the people are both cause for concern.
ramacharitamanas::2811.simple_insight: Titles mean little without conduct; responsibility is proven by how you treat others.
ramacharitamanas::2811.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the grief over Dasharath has turned into reflection on how a life should be measured. Tulsidas widens the lesson: a Brahmin without learning or duty, and a king without justice or love for his people, both fail the trust placed in them.
ramacharitamanas::2811.modern_relevance: A manager with a fancy title ignores the team’s burnout and calls it leadership. A parent says they care, but never notices the child’s fear. This verse asks whether your role is actually being lived.
ramacharitamanas::2811.insight: It shifts attention from status to responsibility, and from public role to real care.

ramacharitamanas::2812.verse_sanskrit: सोचिअ बयसु कृपन धनवानू। जो न अतिथि सिव भगति सुजानू॥ सोचिअ सूद्रु बिप्र अवमानी। मुखर मानप्रिय ग्यान गुमानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2812.verse_hindi: उस वैश्य का सोच करना चाहिए, जो धनवान होकर भी कंजूस है और जो अतिथि सत्कार तथा शिवजी की भक्ति करने में कुशल नहीं है। उस शूद्र का सोच करना चाहिए, जो ब्राह्मणों का अपमान करने वाला, बहुत बोलने वाला, मान-बड़ाई चाहने वाला और ज्ञान का घमंड रखने वाला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2812.english_translation: One should feel concern for a wealthy merchant who is miserly and poor in hospitality, and for a shudra who insults brahmins, talks too much, craves honor, and is proud of his knowledge.
ramacharitamanas::2812.translation_literal: सोचिअ (one should feel concern for) / बयसु (merchant) / कृपन (miserly) / धनवानू (wealthy) / जो (who) / न (not) / अतिथि (guest) / सिव (and) / भगति (devotion) / सुजानू (skilled) / सोचिअ (one should feel concern for) / सूद्रु (shudra) / बिप्र (brahmins) / अवमानी (insulting) / मुखर (talkative) / मानप्रिय (fond of honor) / ग्यान (knowledge) / गुमानी (proud)
ramacharitamanas::2812.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2812.essence: Status without humility is still spiritual poverty.
ramacharitamanas::2812.simple_meaning: Wealth, learning, or social standing are not enough on their own. A person should be judged by humility, hospitality, respect for others, and freedom from pride.
ramacharitamanas::2812.simple_insight: Real worth shows up in how you treat people, not in what you claim to be.
ramacharitamanas::2812.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the grief of Dasharath's court becomes a lesson in moral seeing. The speaker lists people whose outer status hides inner failure: a rich miser, an arrogant talker, someone proud of knowledge. The passage trains judgment away from appearances.
ramacharitamanas::2812.modern_relevance: You meet someone who talks endlessly about expertise but never listens, never gives, and never shows respect. The discomfort you feel is the same warning this verse gives: status can hide poverty of character.
ramacharitamanas::2812.insight: It shifts attention from rank and display to conduct, humility, and how you treat the people around you.

ramacharitamanas::2813.verse_sanskrit: सोचिअ पुनि पति बंचक नारी। कुटिल कलहप्रिय इच्छाचारी॥ सोचिअ बटु निज ब्रतु परिहरई। जो नहिं गुर आयसु अनुसरई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2813.verse_hindi: पुनः उस स्त्री का सोच करना चाहिए जो पति को छलने वाली, कुटिल, कलहप्रिय और स्वेच्छा चारिणी है। उस ब्रह्मचारी का सोच करना चाहिए, जो अपने ब्रह्मचर्य व्रत को छोड़ देता है और गुरु की आज्ञा के अनुसार नहीं चलता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2813.english_translation: Again, you should feel concern for a wife who deceives her husband, is crooked, loves quarrels, and follows only her own wishes. You should feel concern for a student who abandons his vow of celibacy and does not follow the teacher's command.
ramacharitamanas::2813.translation_literal: सोचिअ (should feel concern for) / पुनि (again) / पति (husband) / बंचक (deceiving) / नारी (woman) / कुटिल (crooked) / कलहप्रिय (fond of quarrels) / इच्छाचारी (following own wishes)॥ / सोचिअ (should feel concern for) / बटु (student / celibate student) / निज (own) / ब्रतु (vow) / परिहरई (abandons) / जो (who) / नहिं (does not) / गुर (teacher) / आयसु (command) / अनुसरई (follow)
ramacharitamanas::2813.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2813.essence: Character weakens when trust, restraint, and guidance are abandoned.
ramacharitamanas::2813.simple_meaning: A person loses honour when they betray trust, stir conflict, or abandon the discipline they promised to keep.
ramacharitamanas::2813.simple_insight: Integrity is not abstract; it shows up in loyalty, restraint, and obedience to what you have committed to.
ramacharitamanas::2813.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is listing the kinds of people who deserve concern because they have strayed from their proper conduct. After naming corrupt householders and selfish rulers, he turns to a deceitful wife and a student who breaks vows and ignores the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::2813.modern_relevance: You promised yourself one small rule and broke it by noon. The real loss is not the rule itself — it is the slow erosion of trust in your own word.
ramacharitamanas::2813.insight: It shifts the mind from excuse-making to responsibility for the vows and guidance that shape character.

ramacharitamanas::2814.verse_sanskrit: सोचिअ गृही जो मोह बस करइ करम पथ त्याग। सोचिअ जती प्रपंच रत बिगत बिबेक बिराग ॥
ramacharitamanas::2814.verse_hindi: उस गृहस्थ का सोच करना चाहिए, जो मोहवश कर्म मार्ग का त्याग कर देता है, उस संन्यासी का सोच करना चाहिए, जो दुनिया के प्रपंच में फँसा हुआ और ज्ञान-वैराग्य से हीन है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2814.english_translation: You should grieve for a householder who abandons the path of action out of delusion, and for a renunciant who clings to worldly entanglement, lacking discernment and detachment.
ramacharitamanas::2814.translation_literal: सोचिअ (should be grieved for) / गृही (householder) / जो (who) / मोह बस (under the sway of delusion) / करइ (does) / करम पथ (path of action) / त्याग (abandonment) / सोचिअ (should be grieved for) / जती (renunciant) / प्रपंच रत (attached to worldly entanglement) / बिगत (without) / बिबेक (discernment) / बिराग (detachment)
ramacharitamanas::2814.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2814.essence: Running from duty and clinging to renunciation are both forms of confusion.
ramacharitamanas::2814.simple_meaning: A person can go wrong in two opposite ways: a householder may abandon action out of confusion, and a renunciant may still be trapped in worldly attachment.
ramacharitamanas::2814.simple_insight: The outer role matters less than the clarity and freedom behind it.
ramacharitamanas::2814.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is listing the kinds of lives that deserve pity. He moves from a householder who quits his duties in delusion to a renunciant who still loves worldly display. Both have missed the real point.
ramacharitamanas::2814.modern_relevance: You quit a responsibility because it feels heavy, then later chase approval in a simpler life that still feels noisy. The problem was never the role — it was the mind carrying it.
ramacharitamanas::2814.insight: It shifts attention from labels and roles to the state of mind doing them.

ramacharitamanas::2815.verse_sanskrit: बैखानस सोइ सोचै जोगू। तपु बिहाइ जेहि भावइ भोगू॥ सोचिअ पिसुन अकारन क्रोधी। जननि जनक गुर बंधु बिरोधी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2815.verse_hindi: वानप्रस्थ वही सोच करने योग्य है, जिसको तपस्या छोड़कर भोग अच्छे लगते हैं। सोच उसका करना चाहिए जो चुगलखोर है, बिना ही कारण क्रोध करने वाला है तथा माता, पिता, गुरु एवं भाई-बंधुओं के साथ विरोध रखने वाला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2815.english_translation: The forest-dweller who abandons austerity for pleasure is worth grieving over. Grieve the one who slanders, grows angry for no reason, and opposes mother, father, teacher, and brothers.
ramacharitamanas::2815.translation_literal: बैखानस (forest-dweller / renunciant) / सोइ (that one) / सोचै (should be grieved over) / जोगू (fit, worthy) / तपु (austerity) / बिहाइ (leaving behind) / जेहि (whom) / भावइ (pleases) / भोगू (pleasure, enjoyment) ॥ सोचिअ (should be grieved over) / पिसुन (slandering) / अकारन (without cause) / क्रोधी (angry) / जननि (mother) / जनक (father) / गुर (teacher) / बंधु (brothers, kin) / बिरोधी (opposed to) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2815.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2815.essence: When self-restraint is abandoned, character starts to unravel.
ramacharitamanas::2815.simple_meaning: A person deserves concern when they abandon self-restraint for comfort, gossip, anger, and opposition to the people who raised and guided them.
ramacharitamanas::2815.simple_insight: It reminds you that self-control protects your relationships, not just your habits.
ramacharitamanas::2815.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is listing the kinds of people who have lost their inner discipline. The forest-dweller who prefers pleasure over austerity, and the person who becomes malicious, angry, and hostile to parents, teachers, and kin, all deserve concern because they have drifted from right conduct.
ramacharitamanas::2815.modern_relevance: You watch someone slowly become impossible to live with: quick to snap, eager to gossip, dismissive of the people who care for them. The verse says the real loss is not just bad behaviour — it is the collapse of discipline.
ramacharitamanas::2815.insight: It shifts attention from judging manners to seeing the breakdown of restraint underneath them.

ramacharitamanas::2816.verse_sanskrit: सब बिधि सोचिअ पर अपकारी। निज तनु पोषक निरदय भारी॥ सोचनीय सबहीं बिधि सोई। जो न छाड़ि छलु हरि जन होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2816.verse_hindi: सब प्रकार से उसका सोच करना चाहिए, जो दूसरों का अनिष्ट करता है, अपने ही शरीर का पोषण करता है और बड़ा भारी निर्दयी है और वह तो सभी प्रकार से सोच करने योग्य है, जो छल छोड़कर हरि का भक्त नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2816.english_translation: One should grieve for the person who harms others, feeds only their own body, and is deeply cruel. In every way, the one who is truly blameworthy is the person who, without giving up deceit, does not become a devotee of Hari.
ramacharitamanas::2816.translation_literal: सब बिधि (in every way) / सोचिअ (one should grieve) / पर (others) / अपकारी (harm-doer) / निज (own) / तनु (body) / पोषक (feeder) / निरदय (merciless) / भारी (very great) ॥ / सोचनीय (worthy of grief) / सबहीं (all) / बिधि (ways) / सोई (that one) / जो (who) / न (not) / छाड़ि (giving up) / छलु (deceit) / हरि (Hari) / जन (devotee) / होई (becomes) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2816.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2816.essence: Cruelty and deceit are the real signs of a fallen heart.
ramacharitamanas::2816.simple_meaning: A cruel person who hurts others and lives only for themselves deserves concern. The deepest fault is staying deceitful while refusing sincere devotion to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2816.simple_insight: It turns your attention toward character, not image: real devotion cannot coexist with cruelty and deceit.
ramacharitamanas::2816.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the lesson is widening from bad conduct in household life to the deepest moral failure. Tulsidas says grief belongs to the person who harms others, lives only for bodily comfort, and stays merciless. Even worse is refusing Hari while clinging to deceit.
ramacharitamanas::2816.modern_relevance: You meet someone who smiles in public, undermines people in private, and still wants to be seen as decent. This verse cuts through that split: harm, deceit, and hollow piety cannot be separated.
ramacharitamanas::2816.insight: It shifts judgment from outward respectability to the inner pattern of harm, self-absorption, and dishonesty.

ramacharitamanas::2817.verse_sanskrit: सोचनीय नहिं कोसलराऊ। भुवन चारिदस प्रगट प्रभाऊ॥ भयउ न अहइ न अब होनिहारा। भूप भरत जस पिता तुम्हारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2817.verse_hindi: कोसलराज दशरथजी सोच करने योग्य नहीं हैं, जिनका प्रभाव चौदहों लोकों में प्रकट है। हे भरत! तुम्हारे पिता जैसा राजा तो न हुआ, न है और न अब होने का ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2817.english_translation: King Dasharath of Kosala is not fit for sorrow. His fame is manifest across the fourteen worlds. O Bharat, no king like your father has ever been, is now, or will ever be.
ramacharitamanas::2817.translation_literal: सोचनीय (fit for sorrow) / नहिं (not) / कोसलराऊ (King of Kosala) / भुवन (worlds) / चारिदस (fourteen) / प्रगट (manifest) / प्रभाऊ (fame/power) / भयउ (was) / न (not) / अहइ (is) / न (not) / अब (now) / होनिहारा (to be) / भूप (king) / भरत (Bharat) / जस (like) / पिता (father) / तुम्हारा (your)
ramacharitamanas::2817.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2817.essence: Greatness does not disappear when grief narrows your view.
ramacharitamanas::2817.simple_meaning: Dasharath is being praised as a king whose greatness is known everywhere. Bharat is told that his father is beyond ordinary sorrow and beyond comparison.
ramacharitamanas::2817.simple_insight: Some losses hurt because they were tied to someone truly rare.
ramacharitamanas::2817.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is drowning in grief after Dasharath's death and Ram's exile. The speaker interrupts the sorrow to remind him that Dasharath was no ordinary father-king: his fame filled all directions, and his greatness cannot be measured by loss alone.
ramacharitamanas::2817.modern_relevance: You stand at a funeral and hear stories that make you realize the person was larger than your private grief. Their life touched more people than you ever knew.
ramacharitamanas::2817.insight: It shifts the mind from personal mourning to a wider recognition of a person's public and moral stature.

ramacharitamanas::2818.verse_sanskrit: बिधि हरि हरु सुरपति दिसिनाथा। बरनहिं सब दसरथ गुन गाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2818.verse_hindi: हब्रह्मा, विष्णु, शिव, इन्द्र और दिक्पाल सभी दशरथजी के गुणों की कथाएँ कहा करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2818.english_translation: Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, Indra, and the guardians of the directions all sing the praises of Dasharath's virtues.
ramacharitamanas::2818.translation_literal: बिधि (Brahma) / हरि (Vishnu) / हरु (Shiva) / सुरपति (Indra) / दिसिनाथा (guardians of the directions) / बरनहिं (describe) / सब (all) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / गुन (virtues) / गाथा (praises)
ramacharitamanas::2818.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2818.essence: A truly noble life is praised even beyond human voices.
ramacharitamanas::2818.simple_meaning: Even the highest beings speak of Dasharath's virtues. His greatness is so wide that it reaches beyond ordinary praise.
ramacharitamanas::2818.simple_insight: Some lives are so noble that praise itself feels too small.
ramacharitamanas::2818.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharata is being told that his father Dasharath does not need lament or blame. This line raises the praise further: even Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, Indra, and the guardians of the directions speak of his virtues.
ramacharitamanas::2818.modern_relevance: At a memorial, people keep saying the same thing: he was the kind of person everyone respected. The grief is real, but so is the rare dignity of a life that leaves that kind of echo.
ramacharitamanas::2818.insight: It shifts attention from one person's loss to the scale of the life that was lived.

ramacharitamanas::2819.verse_sanskrit: कहहु तात केहि भाँति कोउ करिहि बड़ाई तासु। राम लखन तुम्ह सत्रुहन सरिस सुअन सुचि जासु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2819.verse_hindi: हे तात! कहो, उनकी बड़ाई कोई किस प्रकार करेगा, जिनके श्री राम, लक्ष्मण, तुम और शत्रुघ्न-सरीखे पवित्र पुत्र हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2819.english_translation: Father, who could possibly praise one whose pure sons are Ram, Lakshman, you, and Shatrughna?
ramacharitamanas::2819.translation_literal: कहहु (tell) / तात (father) / केहि भाँति (in what way) / कोउ (anyone) / करिहि (will do) / बड़ाई (praise) / तासु (of him) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / तुम्ह (you) / सत्रुहन (Shatrughna) / सरिस (like) / सुअन (good sons) / सुचि (pure) / जासु (whose)
ramacharitamanas::2819.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2819.essence: A worthy life is praised by the children it raises.
ramacharitamanas::2819.simple_meaning: A father's greatness is beyond ordinary praise when his sons themselves are noble and pure.
ramacharitamanas::2819.simple_insight: It softens the urge to measure worth by words alone.
ramacharitamanas::2819.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, grief around Dasharath has turned into reflection. The speaker reminds Bharat that no one can properly praise a king whose sons are Ram, Lakshman, Bharat, and Shatrughna. The verse shifts the mind from sorrow to recognition of blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2819.modern_relevance: You’re standing at a memorial, trying to speak about a parent who shaped four good children. The tribute feels too small, because the real proof of their life is already standing beside you.
ramacharitamanas::2819.insight: It redirects attention from eulogy to legacy: a life is measured by the character it leaves behind.

ramacharitamanas::2820.verse_sanskrit: सब प्रकार भूपति बड़भागी। बादि बिषादु करिअ तेहि लागी॥ यह सुनि समुझि सोचु परिहरहू। सिर धरि राज रजायसु करहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2820.verse_hindi: राजा सब प्रकार से बड़भागी थे। उनके लिए विषाद करना व्यर्थ है। यह सुन और समझकर सोच त्याग दो और राजा की आज्ञा सिर चढ़ाकर तदनुसार करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2820.english_translation: The king was blessed in every way. Grieving for him is pointless. Hearing this and understanding it, let go of sorrow and obey the king's command with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2820.translation_literal: सब प्रकार (in every way) / भूपति (king) / बड़भागी (highly fortunate) / बादि (useless) / बिषादु (grief) / करिअ (is done) / तेहि (for him) / लागी (for the sake of)॥ यह (this) / सुनि (hearing) / समुझि (understanding) / सोचु (sorrow) / परिहरहू (give up) / सिर (head) / धरि (placing) / राज (king's) / रजायसु (command) / करहू (do) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2820.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2820.essence: Grief must give way to reverent action.
ramacharitamanas::2820.simple_meaning: There is no need to grieve for the king. He was fortunate in every way, and the proper response is to drop sorrow and follow his command.
ramacharitamanas::2820.simple_insight: Sometimes love looks like releasing grief and honoring what must be done.
ramacharitamanas::2820.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the family and court are reeling after Dasharath's death. The speaker reminds everyone that the king lived a blessed life, so mourning cannot change anything. What matters now is to accept his order and act with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2820.modern_relevance: After a funeral, relatives sit in a quiet room arguing over what the deceased would have wanted. This verse asks you to stop feeding sorrow and honor the responsibility left behind.
ramacharitamanas::2820.insight: It shifts you from emotional collapse to clear obedience to what remains to be done.

ramacharitamanas::2821.verse_sanskrit: रायँ राजपदु तुम्ह कहुँ दीन्हा। पिता बचनु फुर चाहिअ कीन्हा॥ तजे रामु जेहिं बचनहि लागी। तनु परिहरेउ राम बिरहागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2821.verse_hindi: राजा ने राज पद तुमको दिया है। पिता का वचन तुम्हें सत्य करना चाहिए, जिन्होंने वचन के लिए ही श्री रामचन्द्रजी को त्याग दिया और रामविरह की अग्नि में अपने शरीर की आहुति दे दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2821.english_translation: The king gave the throne to you. You should make your father's word come true. He gave up Ram for the sake of his promise and gave his body up in the fire of separation from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2821.translation_literal: रायँ (the king) / राजपदु (the royal seat) / तुम्ह कहुँ (to you) / दीन्हा (gave) / पिता (father) / बचनु (word) / फुर (true) / चाहिअ (should) / कीन्हा (be made) / तजे (gave up) / रामु (Ram) / जेहिं (for whom) / बचनहि (for the word) / लागी (for the sake of) / तनु (body) / परिहरेउ (gave up) / राम बिरहागी (burning in separation from Ram)
ramacharitamanas::2821.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2821.essence: The real inheritance is not power, but the duty to keep a promise alive.
ramacharitamanas::2821.simple_meaning: The throne was given to Bharata, but the real duty is to prove his father's words true. Dasharatha himself gave up Ram and even his body for the sake of truth.
ramacharitamanas::2821.simple_insight: Some inherit power; others inherit a promise. Keeping the promise is the deeper honor.
ramacharitamanas::2821.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the family is grieving Dasharatha after Ram's exile. The speaker reminds Bharata that his father gave him the throne, but more importantly gave him a sacred responsibility: make Dasharatha's words true by acting with the same loyalty to truth that cost the king everything.
ramacharitamanas::2821.modern_relevance: You were handed a family responsibility you never asked for: a hospital bill, a sibling's promise, a parent’s unfinished task. What matters now is not the title you received, but whether you carry the word faithfully.
ramacharitamanas::2821.insight: It shifts the mind from entitlement to responsibility, and from receiving a role to fulfilling the promise inside it.

ramacharitamanas::2822.verse_sanskrit: नृपहि बचन प्रिय नहिं प्रिय प्राना। करहु तात पितु बचन प्रवाना॥ करहु सीस धरि भूप रजाई। हइ तुम्ह कहँ सब भाँति भलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2822.verse_hindi: राजा को वचन प्रिय थे, प्राण प्रिय नहीं थे, इसलिए हे तात! पिता के वचनों को प्रमाण (सत्य) करो! राजा की आज्ञा सिर चढ़ाकर पालन करो, इसमें तुम्हारी सब तरह भलाई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2822.english_translation: The king loved his word more than his life. O dear one, prove your father's command true. Bow your head to the king's order; in every way, that is your good.
ramacharitamanas::2822.translation_literal: नृपहि (to the king) / बचन (word) / प्रिय (dear) / नहिं (not) / प्रिय (dear) / प्राना (life-breaths) / करहु (do) / तात (dear one) / पितु (father's) / बचन (word) / प्रवाना (made true) / करहु (do) / सीस (head) / धरि (placing) / भूप (king) / रजाई (command) / हइ (is) / तुम्ह (for you) / कहँ (for) / सब (all) / भाँति (ways) / भलाई (good)
ramacharitamanas::2822.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2822.essence: A son's greatness begins with making his father's word come true.
ramacharitamanas::2822.simple_meaning: A king values his word more than his own life. So the son should treat the father's command as sacred and obey it fully.
ramacharitamanas::2822.simple_insight: There is dignity in treating a promise as heavier than comfort or fear.
ramacharitamanas::2822.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the exile has already begun and the family is trying to live inside Dasharath's broken promise. This verse urges Bharata to honour his father's command exactly, because keeping a king's word is the only way to preserve righteousness now.
ramacharitamanas::2822.modern_relevance: You promised your mother you'd handle the family matter, even though it means canceling your plans and swallowing your pride. This verse asks you to treat that promise as binding, not optional.
ramacharitamanas::2822.insight: It shifts you from personal preference to responsibility grounded in your word.

ramacharitamanas::2823.verse_sanskrit: परसुराम पितु अग्या राखी। मारी मातु लोक सब साखी॥ तनय जजातिहि जौबनु दयऊ। पितु अग्याँ अघ अजसु न भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2823.verse_hindi: परशुरामजी ने पिता की आज्ञा रखी और माता को मार डाला, सब लोक इस बात के साक्षी हैं। राजा ययाति के पुत्र ने पिता को अपनी जवानी दे दी। पिता की आज्ञा पालन करने से उन्हें पाप और अपयश नहीं हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2823.english_translation: Parashuram kept his father's command and killed his mother; all the world is witness. The son of King Yayati gave his youth to his father. By obeying a father's command, they incurred no sin or disgrace.
ramacharitamanas::2823.translation_literal: परसुराम (Parashuram) / पितु (father's) / अग्या (command) / राखी (kept) / मारी (killed) / मातु (mother) / लोक (world) / सब (all) / साखी (witness)॥ / तनय (son) / जजातिहि (Yayati's son) / जौबनु (youth) / दयऊ (gave) / पितु (father's) / अग्याँ (command) / अघ (sin) / अजसु (disgrace) / न (not) / भयऊ (became) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2823.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2823.essence: Some duties cost dearly and still leave your honor intact.
ramacharitamanas::2823.simple_meaning: The verse praises people who obey a father's command, even at great personal cost, and says such obedience can still be honorable.
ramacharitamanas::2823.simple_insight: You can face hard duty without feeling corrupted by it.
ramacharitamanas::2823.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the argument for keeping a father's word is being built through examples. Parashuram and Yayati's son are held up as proof that obedience to a father's command can demand extreme sacrifice and still leave no disgrace.
ramacharitamanas::2823.modern_relevance: You agree to help a parent move, even though it ruins your weekend and drains you. The cost is real, but so is the dignity of keeping your word.
ramacharitamanas::2823.insight: It shifts you from judging duty by comfort to judging it by fidelity.

ramacharitamanas::2824.verse_sanskrit: अनुचित उचित बिचारु तजि ते पालहिं पितु बैन। ते भाजन सुख सुजस के बसहिं अमरपति ऐन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2824.verse_hindi: जो अनुचित और उचित का विचार छोड़कर पिता के वचनों का पालन करते हैं, वे (यहाँ) सुख और सुयश के पात्र होकर अंत में इन्द्रपुरी (स्वर्ग) में निवास करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2824.english_translation: Those who set aside judgments of right and wrong and keep their father's word become fit for happiness and good fame here, and dwell in Indra's city in the end.
ramacharitamanas::2824.translation_literal: अनुचित (wrong) / उचित (right) / बिचारु (judgment) / तजि (leaving aside) / ते (they) / पालहिं (keep) / पितु (father's) / बैन (word) / ते (they) / भाजन (fit recipients) / सुख (happiness) / सुजस (good fame) / के (of) / बसहिं (dwell) / अमरपति (Indra) / ऐन (in the end)
ramacharitamanas::2824.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2824.essence: Keeping a father's word can matter more than personal comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2824.simple_meaning: A child who follows a father's command without overthinking right and wrong earns honor and lasting good.
ramacharitamanas::2824.simple_insight: Sometimes loyalty matters more than personal comfort or clever judgment.
ramacharitamanas::2824.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the crisis of exile has already begun. The court is torn between grief and obedience, and Tulsidas praises the children who keep a father's word even when it hurts. That loyalty becomes the measure of their worth.
ramacharitamanas::2824.modern_relevance: You know the moment: your parent asks for something awkward, inconvenient, and clearly not to your advantage. The verse says real character shows up when you honor the word anyway.
ramacharitamanas::2824.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to faithful obedience in a binding relationship.

ramacharitamanas::2825.verse_sanskrit: अवसि नरेस बचन फुर करहू। पालहु प्रजा सोकु परिहरहू॥ सुरपुर नृपु पाइहि परितोषू। तुम्ह कहुँ सुकृतु सुजसु नहिं दोषू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2825.verse_hindi: राजा का वचन अवश्य सत्य करो। शोक त्याग दो और प्रजा का पालन करो। ऐसा करने से स्वर्ग में राजा संतोष पावेंगे और तुम को पुण्य और सुंदर यश मिलेगा, दोष नहीं लगेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2825.english_translation: Surely keep the king's word true. Set aside grief and protect the people. Then the king will find contentment in the higher realm, and you will gain merit and good fame, not blame.
ramacharitamanas::2825.translation_literal: अवसि (surely) / नरेस (of the king) / बचन (word) / फुर (true) / करहू (do) / पालहु (protect) / प्रजा (the people) / सोकु (grief) / परिहरहू (set aside) / सुरपुर (higher realm) / नृपु (king) / पाइहि (will attain) / परितोषू (contentment) / तुम्ह कहुँ (for you) / सुकृतु (merit) / सुजसु (good fame) / नहिं (not) / दोषू (blame)
ramacharitamanas::2825.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2825.essence: Keep the promise, even when grief asks you to stop.
ramacharitamanas::2825.simple_meaning: A ruler must keep his father's promise, stop grieving, and continue protecting the people. Doing that brings honor, not blame.
ramacharitamanas::2825.simple_insight: Sometimes love means carrying the burden without letting grief stop your duty.
ramacharitamanas::2825.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the crisis of exile has left the kingdom wounded. The speaker urges the heir to honor the king's word, release grief, and continue ruling for the people's welfare, because true loyalty is measured by steady responsibility.
ramacharitamanas::2825.modern_relevance: You are still expected at the family meeting after the loss, even when your chest feels tight. The work of care does not pause just because your heart is breaking.
ramacharitamanas::2825.insight: It shifts the mind from private sorrow to public responsibility, showing that duty can continue even in grief.

ramacharitamanas::2826.verse_sanskrit: बेद बिदित संमत सबही का। जेहि पितु देइ सो पावइ टीका॥ करहु राजु परिहरहु गलानी। मानहु मोर बचन हित जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2826.verse_hindi: यह वेद में प्रसिद्ध है और (स्मृति-पुराणादि) सभी शास्त्रों के द्वारा सम्मत है कि पिता जिसको दे वही राजतिलक पाता है, इसलिए तुम राज्य करो, ग्लानि का त्याग कर दो। मेरे वचन को हित समझकर मानो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2826.english_translation: It is well known in the Vedas and accepted by all scriptures that the one whom the father gives the coronation belongs on the throne. So take the kingdom, let go of your grief, and accept my words as beneficial.
ramacharitamanas::2826.translation_literal: बेद (Vedas) / बिदित (well known) / संमत (accepted) / सबही का (by everyone) / जेहि (whom) / पितु (father) / देइ (gives) / सो (that one) / पावइ (receives) / टीका (coronation)॥ / करहु (do) / राजु (the kingdom) / परिहरहु (give up) / गलानी (grief) / मानहु (accept) / मोर (my) / बचन (words) / हित (beneficial) / जानी (knowing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2826.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::2826.essence: Duty can arrive wearing grief, and still need your yes.
ramacharitamanas::2826.simple_meaning: The rightful coronation belongs to the son chosen by the father. Dasharath asks Bharat to accept the throne, drop his sorrow, and trust that this is for everyone's good.
ramacharitamanas::2826.simple_insight: Sometimes love means accepting a role you never wanted and trusting the larger good.
ramacharitamanas::2826.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath is trying to steady Bharat after the shock of Ram’s exile. He appeals to sacred custom and family duty, saying the father’s chosen heir should receive the coronation. This verse pushes Bharat toward accepting the kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::2826.modern_relevance: Your family hands you a responsibility you never asked for, and everyone is waiting while you hesitate. The room is heavy with emotion, but the task still belongs to you.
ramacharitamanas::2826.insight: It shifts the mind from personal reluctance to accepting the binding duty in front of you.

ramacharitamanas::2827.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुखु लहब राम बैदेहीं। अनुचित कहब न पंडित केहीं॥ कौसल्यादि सकल महतारीं। तेउ प्रजा सुख होहिं सुखारीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2827.verse_hindi: इस बात को सुनकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी और जानकीजी सुख पावेंगे और कोई पंडित इसे अनुचित नहीं कहेगा। कौसल्याजी आदि तुम्हारी सब माताएँ भी प्रजा के सुख से सुखी होंगी॥
ramacharitamanas::2827.english_translation: Hearing this, Ram and Sita will be happy, and no wise person will call it improper. Kaushalya and all the other mothers will also rejoice in the people's happiness.
ramacharitamanas::2827.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुखु (happiness) / लहब (will receive) / राम (Ram) / बैदेहीं (Sita) / अनुचित (improper) / कहब (to say) / न (not) / पंडित (wise person) / केहीं (any) / कौसल्यादि (Kaushalya and others) / सकल (all) / महतारीं (mothers) / तेउ (they also) / प्रजा (people) / सुख (happiness) / होहिं (become) / सुखारीं (happy)
ramacharitamanas::2827.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2827.essence: A righteous choice pleases the whole household, not just the ruler.
ramacharitamanas::2827.simple_meaning: A right decision will please Ram and Sita, and no wise person will object. It will also make the royal mothers happy because the people will be happy too.
ramacharitamanas::2827.simple_insight: A just choice is never private; when it serves others, it also brings peace to those you love.
ramacharitamanas::2827.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the ministers are arguing over the throne after Dasharath's death. This verse continues the case for giving the kingdom to Ram: it will satisfy Ram and Sita, satisfy the wise, and bring joy to Kaushalya and the other queens because the people will prosper.
ramacharitamanas::2827.modern_relevance: You’re deciding whether to take the promotion that looks good on paper but hurts your team. The verse points you toward the option that leaves everyone steadier, not just you.
ramacharitamanas::2827.insight: It shifts decision-making from personal gain to the wider well-being your choice creates.

ramacharitamanas::2828.verse_sanskrit: परम तुम्हार राम कर जानिहि। सो सब बिधि तुम्ह सन भल मानिहि॥ सौंपेहु राजु राम के आएँ। सेवा करेहु सनेह सुहाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2828.verse_hindi: जो तुम्हारे और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के श्रेष्ठ संबंध को जान लेगा, वह सभी प्रकार से तुमसे भला मानेगा। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के लौट आने पर राज्य उन्हें सौंप देना और सुंदर स्नेह से उनकी सेवा करना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2828.english_translation: Anyone who understands the noble bond between you and Ram will regard you as good in every way. When Ram returns, hand the kingdom over to him and serve him with loving devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2828.translation_literal: परम (supreme) / तुम्हार (your) / राम (Ram) / कर (of) / जानिहि (will know) / सो (that one) / सब बिधि (in every way) / तुम्ह सन (with you) / भल (good) / मानिहि (will regard)॥ / सौंपेहु (hand over) / राजु (kingdom) / राम के आएँ (on Ram's return) / सेवा (service) / करेहु (do) / सनेह (loving affection) / सुहाएँ (beautiful, pleasing)॥
ramacharitamanas::2828.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2828.essence: Power becomes noble when you can return it with love.
ramacharitamanas::2828.simple_meaning: Bharat says everyone will see the bond between him and Ram as noble. He should return the kingdom to Ram and serve him lovingly when Ram comes back.
ramacharitamanas::2828.simple_insight: Real dignity comes from knowing when to hold power and when to hand it back.
ramacharitamanas::2828.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is being urged to rule in Ram's absence, but this verse turns the whole idea around. The kingdom is only a trust, not a possession. Bharat's greatness will be shown by giving it back and serving Ram with affection.
ramacharitamanas::2828.modern_relevance: You’ve been covering for a sibling, colleague, or friend and everyone now treats the role as yours. The harder move is to hand it back cleanly, without resentment, and let love stay intact.
ramacharitamanas::2828.insight: It shifts you from possession to stewardship: hold only what truly belongs to you, and return the rest without bitterness.

ramacharitamanas::2829.verse_sanskrit: कीजिअ गुर आयसु अवसि कहहिं सचिव कर जोरि। रघुपति आएँ उचित जस तस तब करब बहोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2829.verse_hindi: मंत्री हाथ जोड़कर कह रहे हैं- गुरुजी की आज्ञा का अवश्य ही पालन कीजिए। श्री रघुनाथजी के लौट आने पर जैसा उचित हो, तब फिर वैसा ही कीजिएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2829.english_translation: The ministers fold their hands and say, "You must obey the teacher's command. When Raghunath returns, then do what is fitting."
ramacharitamanas::2829.translation_literal: कीजिअ (should be done) / गुर (teacher) / आयसु (command) / अवसि (certainly) / कहहिं (say) / सचिव (ministers) / कर जोरि (with hands joined) / रघुपति (Raghupati) / आएँ (upon arrival) / उचित (proper) / जस तस (as it is fitting) / तब (then) / करब (should do) / बहोरि (again)
