ramacharitamanas::2829.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2829.essence: Honor the present duty; leave the larger decision for later.
ramacharitamanas::2829.simple_meaning: The ministers ask Bharata to obey the teacher's order first and leave the final decision for after Ram returns.
ramacharitamanas::2829.simple_insight: You do not have to solve everything at once; some duties only ask for faithful first steps.
ramacharitamanas::2829.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the ministers speak to Bharata with folded hands after Ram's exile has thrown the kingdom into uncertainty. They urge him to honor the teacher's command now and leave the deeper decision for when Ram comes back.
ramacharitamanas::2829.modern_relevance: Your family is arguing in the kitchen and everyone wants an answer tonight. But the wisest move may be to honor the immediate responsibility first and postpone the final call until tempers cool.
ramacharitamanas::2829.insight: It trains you to separate immediate duty from later judgment, so action stays steady under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::2830.verse_sanskrit: कौसल्या धरि धीरजु कहई। पूत पथ्य गुर आयसु अहई॥ सो आदरिअ करिअ हित मानी। तजिअ बिषादु काल गति जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2830.verse_hindi: कौसल्याजी भी धीरज धरकर कह रही हैं- हे पुत्र! गुरुजी की आज्ञा पथ्य रूप है। उसका आदर करना चाहिए और हित मानकर उसका पालन करना चाहिए। काल की गति को जानकर विषाद का त्याग कर देना चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2830.english_translation: Kaushalya, steadying herself, said: 'Son, the guru's command is like medicine. Honour it and follow it as good for you. Knowing time's course, let go of grief.'
ramacharitamanas::2830.translation_literal: कौसल्या (Kaushalya) / धरि (holding) / धीरजु (steadiness) / कहई (said) / पूत (son) / पथ्य (wholesome, like medicine) / गुर (guru's) / आयसु (command) / अहई (is) ॥ / सो (that) / आदरिअ (honour) / करिअ (do) / हित (beneficial) / मानी (considering) / तजिअ (let go) / बिषादु (grief) / काल (time) / गति (course) / जानी (knowing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2830.speaker: Kaushalya
ramacharitamanas::2830.essence: What is truly good may arrive wearing the face of pain.
ramacharitamanas::2830.simple_meaning: Kaushalya tells her son to treat the guru's instruction as something beneficial, follow it with respect, and drop grief by understanding that time moves on.
ramacharitamanas::2830.simple_insight: You can obey what is right without collapsing into sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2830.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kaushalya steadies herself while the family is breaking apart over Ram's exile. She speaks to Bharata like a mother who knows duty is painful but necessary: respect the guru's word, recognise its value, and do not drown in grief.
ramacharitamanas::2830.modern_relevance: You get a message that changes everything, and your first instinct is to spiral. Then someone steadier reminds you that not every painful instruction is harmful; some are the medicine you needed.
ramacharitamanas::2830.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional resistance to respectful acceptance of guidance.

ramacharitamanas::2831.verse_sanskrit: बन रघुपति सुरपति नरनाहू। तुम्ह एहि भाँति तात कदराहू॥ परिजन प्रजा सचिव सब अंबा। तुम्हहीं सुत सब कहँ अवलंबा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2831.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी वन में हैं, महाराज स्वर्ग का राज्य करने चले गए और हे तात! तुम इस प्रकार कातर हो रहे हो। हे पुत्र! कुटुम्ब, प्रजा, मंत्री और सब माताओं के, सबके एक तुम ही सहारे हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2831.english_translation: Ram has gone to the forest and the king of the gods has gone to his realm, yet you are grieving like this, dear one. Son, for your family, your people, your ministers, and all the mothers, you alone are the support for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::2831.translation_literal: बन (forest) / रघुपति (Ram, lord of the Raghu clan) / सुरपति (lord of the gods) / नरनाहू (king among men) / तुम्ह (you) / एहि भाँति (in this way) / तात (dear one) / कदराहू (are grieving) / परिजन (family) / प्रजा (subjects) / सचिव (ministers) / सब (all) / अंबा (mothers) / तुम्हहीं (you alone) / सुत (son) / सब कहँ (for all) / अवलंबा (support)
ramacharitamanas::2831.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::2831.essence: When everyone else is shaken, you become the support.
ramacharitamanas::2831.simple_meaning: Kausalya reminds Bharat that Ram is in the forest, Dasharath has gone to the higher realm, and the whole family and kingdom now depend on him.
ramacharitamanas::2831.simple_insight: Love can be heavy, but responsibility still remains in your hands.
ramacharitamanas::2831.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace is full of grief after Ram's exile and Dasharath's death. Kausalya speaks to Bharat as the family falls apart around him. She reminds him that his sorrow cannot erase his duty to hold everyone together.
ramacharitamanas::2831.modern_relevance: You are sitting in a hospital corridor while your family keeps calling your phone. You can cry later, but right now everyone is looking to you to decide what happens next.
ramacharitamanas::2831.insight: It shifts the mind from private grief to the responsibility of steadying others.

ramacharitamanas::2832.verse_sanskrit: लखि बिधि बाम कालु कठिनाई। धीरजु धरहु मातु बलि जाई॥ सिर धरि गुर आयसु अनुसरहू। प्रजा पालि परिजन दुखु हरहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2832.verse_hindi: विधाता को प्रतिकूल और काल को कठोर देखकर धीरज धरो, माता तुम्हारी बलिहारी जाती है। गुरु की आज्ञा को सिर चढ़ाकर उसी के अनुसार कार्य करो और प्रजा का पालन कर कुटुम्बियों का दुःख हरो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2832.english_translation: Seeing fate as adverse and time as harsh, keep your courage, mother. Place the teacher's command on your head, rule the people, and remove the grief of your family.
ramacharitamanas::2832.translation_literal: लखि (seeing) / बिधि (fate) / बाम (adverse) / कालु (time) / कठिनाई (harshness) / धीरजु (courage, steadiness) / धरहु (keep) / मातु (mother) / बलि जाई (I am devoted to you)॥ / सिर (head) / धरि (placing) / गुर (teacher's) / आयसु (command) / अनुसरहू (follow) / प्रजा (people) / पालि (protect, rule) / परिजन (family members) / दुखु (grief) / हरहू (remove)॥
ramacharitamanas::2832.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2832.essence: Steadiness lets you carry duty even in harsh times.
ramacharitamanas::2832.simple_meaning: Stay steady even when fate feels harsh. Honor your teacher's instruction, do your duty, care for the people, and ease your family's suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2832.simple_insight: Pressure does not cancel responsibility; it reveals the strength needed to carry it.
ramacharitamanas::2832.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharata is being urged to stay steady after the shock of Ram's exile and Dasharath's collapse. The counsel is simple: do not break under grief; obey the teacher, protect the people, and care for the family left behind.
ramacharitamanas::2832.modern_relevance: Your phone keeps buzzing after bad news, but the team still needs a calm decision and your family still needs you. This verse reminds you that steadiness is part of love.
ramacharitamanas::2832.insight: It shifts you from emotional collapse to responsible action under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::2833.verse_sanskrit: गुरु के बचन सचिव अभिनंदनु। सुने भरत हिय हित जनु चंदनु॥ सुनी बहोरि मातु मृदु बानी। सील सनेह सरल रस सानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2833.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने गुरु के वचनों और मंत्रियों के अभिनंदन (अनुमोदन) को सुना, जो उनके हृदय के लिए मानो चंदन के समान (शीतल) थे। फिर उन्होंने शील, स्नेह और सरलता के रस में सनी हुई माता कौसल्या की कोमल वाणी सुनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2833.english_translation: Bharat heard the ministers' approving words and the guru's blessing, and they felt cool to his heart like sandalwood. Then he heard Mother Kausalya's gentle voice, soaked in virtue, affection, and simplicity.
ramacharitamanas::2833.translation_literal: गुरु के (of the teacher's) / बचन (words) / सचिव (ministers') / अभिनंदनु (approval, blessing) / सुने (heard) / भरत (Bharat) / हिय (heart) / हित (beneficial, soothing) / जनु (as if) / चंदनु (sandalwood)॥ / सुनी (heard) / बहोरि (again) / मातु (mother's) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (voice, words) / सील (virtue) / सनेह (affection) / सरल (simple, sincere) / रस (essence) / सानी (mixed, soaked) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2833.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2833.essence: Kind words can soothe a heart before it breaks.
ramacharitamanas::2833.simple_meaning: Bharat is comforted by the elders’ support and by his mother’s gentle, loving words.
ramacharitamanas::2833.simple_insight: Even grief softens when truth is spoken with care.
ramacharitamanas::2833.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands in the middle of family sorrow and royal duty. The ministers and the teacher try to steady him, and Kausalya speaks with tenderness. This verse shows the emotional atmosphere before Bharat breaks down in grief.
ramacharitamanas::2833.modern_relevance: You are overwhelmed after a family argument, and then one calm voice cuts through the noise. Not because it solves everything, but because it sounds like care instead of pressure.
ramacharitamanas::2833.insight: It shows how gentle, trustworthy words can steady a heart before deeper grief surfaces.

ramacharitamanas::2834.verse_sanskrit: सानी सरल रस मातु बानी सुनि भरतु ब्याकुल भए। लोचन सरोरुह स्रवत सींचत बिरह उर अंकुर नए॥ सो दसा देखत समय तेहि बिसरी सबहि सुधि देह की। तुलसी सराहत सकल सादर सीवँ सहज सनेह की॥
ramacharitamanas::2834.verse_hindi: सरलता के रस में सनी हुई माता की वाणी सुनकर भरतजी व्याकुल हो गए। उनके नेत्र कमल जल (आँसू) बहाकर हृदय के विरह रूपी नवीन अंकुर को सींचने लगे। (नेत्रों के आँसुओं ने उनके वियोग-दुःख को बहुत ही बढ़ाकर उन्हें अत्यन्त व्याकुल कर दिया।) उनकी वह दशा देखकर उस समय सबको अपने शरीर की सुध भूल गई। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- स्वाभाविक प्रेम की सीमा श्री भरतजी की सब लोग आदरपूर्वक सराहना करने लगे।
ramacharitamanas::2834.english_translation: Hearing his mother’s words steeped in simplicity, Bharat became overwhelmed. His lotus eyes poured tears, watering the new sprouts of separation in his heart. Seeing him like that, everyone forgot their own bodies. Tulsidas praises the natural love that makes such devotion worthy of respect.
ramacharitamanas::2834.translation_literal: सानी (soaked) / सरल (simple) / रस (essence) / मातु (mother's) / बानी (speech) / सुनि (hearing) / भरतु (Bharat) / ब्याकुल (overwhelmed) / भए (became) / लोचन (eyes) / सरोरुह (lotus) / स्रवत (flowing) / सींचत (watering) / बिरह (separation) / उर (heart) / अंकुर (sprouts) / नए (new) / सो (that) / दसा (state) / देखत (seeing) / समय (at that time) / तेहि (that) / बिसरी (forgot) / सबहि (all) / सुधि (awareness) / देह की (of the body) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / सराहत (praising) / सकल (all) / सादर (respectfully) / सीवँ (limit) / सहज (natural) / सनेह की (of love)
ramacharitamanas::2834.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2834.essence: Natural love can make grief visible to everyone.
ramacharitamanas::2834.simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed by his mother’s gentle words. His tears deepen his grief, and everyone around him forgets themselves seeing his pain.
ramacharitamanas::2834.simple_insight: Real love can break you open without making you less noble.
ramacharitamanas::2834.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat has just heard the soft, painful words around his exile and Ram’s absence. Kaikeyi’s son is no longer holding himself together; grief pours out of him so fully that even the onlookers lose track of their own bodies.
ramacharitamanas::2834.modern_relevance: You hear a mother’s voice on the phone after a family rupture, and the whole room goes quiet. Some grief is so human that everyone nearby feels it too.
ramacharitamanas::2834.insight: It shifts attention from control to the raw force of love and loss.

ramacharitamanas::2835.verse_sanskrit: भरतु कमल कर जोरि धीर धुरंधर धीर धरि। बचन अमिअँ जनु बोरि देत उचित उत्तर सबहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2835.verse_hindi: धैर्य की धुरी को धारण करने वाले भरतजी धीरज धरकर, कमल के समान हाथों को जोड़कर, वचनों को मानो अमृत में डुबाकर सबको उचित उत्तर देने लगे- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2835.english_translation: Holding onto patience, Bharat joined his lotus-like hands and began giving everyone a fitting reply, as if dipping his words in nectar.
ramacharitamanas::2835.translation_literal: भरतु (Bharat) / कमल कर (lotus-like hands) / जोरि (joining) / धीर धुरंधर (bearer of steadfast patience) / धीर धरि (having steadied himself) / बचन (words) / अमिअँ (in nectar) / जनु (as if) / बोरि देत (dipping and giving) / उचित (fitting) / उत्तर (reply) / सबहि (to everyone)
ramacharitamanas::2835.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2835.essence: Steady hands and gentle words can hold grief without spilling it.
ramacharitamanas::2835.simple_meaning: Bharat steadies himself, joins his hands, and answers everyone gently and appropriately.
ramacharitamanas::2835.simple_insight: Even in grief, you can answer with grace instead of agitation.
ramacharitamanas::2835.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is surrounded by elders, mothers, and ministers after hearing the painful truth about Ram's exile. He gathers himself, joins his hands, and speaks with calm respect. This verse shows his controlled humility before the fuller explanation that follows.
ramacharitamanas::2835.modern_relevance: You are shaken, but the family group chat is waiting for a reply. Instead of firing back, you pause, breathe, and answer with care. That restraint changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::2835.insight: It teaches you to slow the mind before speaking, so your words carry steadiness instead of raw emotion.

ramacharitamanas::2836.verse_sanskrit: मोहि उपदेसु दीन्ह गुरु नीका। प्रजा सचिव संमत सबही का॥ मातु उचित धरि आयसु दीन्हा। अवसि सीस धरि चाहउँ कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2836.verse_hindi: गुरुजी ने मुझे सुंदर उपदेश दिया। (फिर) प्रजा, मंत्री आदि सभी को यही सम्मत है। माता ने भी उचित समझकर ही आज्ञा दी है और मैं भी अवश्य उसको सिर चढ़ाकर वैसा ही करना चाहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2836.english_translation: My guru gave me noble instruction. All the people and ministers agree with it. My mother has given her command as proper, and I too will certainly place it on my head and do it.
ramacharitamanas::2836.translation_literal: मोहि (to me) / उपदेसु (instruction) / दीन्ह (gave) / गुरु (teacher) / नीका (good, noble) / प्रजा (subjects) / सचिव (ministers) / संमत (agreed) / सबही (all) / का (of) / मातु (mother) / उचित (proper) / धरि (having considered) / आयसु (command) / दीन्हा (gave) / अवसि (certainly) / सीस (head) / धरि (placing) / चाहउँ (I want) / कीन्हा (to do)
ramacharitamanas::2836.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2836.essence: Right action becomes easy when every rightful guide points the same way.
ramacharitamanas::2836.simple_meaning: Bharat says he has received good guidance from his teacher, and the approval of his family and leaders. He will accept his mother's command and carry it out fully.
ramacharitamanas::2836.simple_insight: There is calm in obeying what is clearly right, even when many voices have already weighed in.
ramacharitamanas::2836.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat stands before his mother and the court after Ram's exile. He is not acting from impulse; he is measuring every rightful authority — teacher, ministers, mother — and choosing the duty that all of them support.
ramacharitamanas::2836.modern_relevance: You get three texts from family, your mentor, and your team, and they all point the same way. The relief is not in overthinking it — it is in finally doing what you already know is right.
ramacharitamanas::2836.insight: It teaches you to act on clear duty once wise guidance has aligned.

ramacharitamanas::2837.verse_sanskrit: गुर पितु मातु स्वामि हित बानी। सुनि मन मुदित करिअ भलि जानी॥ उचित कि अनुचित किएँ बिचारू। धरमु जाइ सिर पातक भारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2837.verse_hindi: (क्योंकि) गुरु, पिता, माता, स्वामी और सुहृद् (मित्र) की वाणी सुनकर प्रसन्न मन से उसे अच्छी समझकर करना (मानना) चाहिए। उचित-अनुचित का विचार करने से धर्म जाता है और सिर पर पाप का भार चढ़ता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2837.english_translation: Listen to the words of your guru, father, mother, master, and well-wisher with a glad mind, and accept them as good. If you start judging what is proper and improper, dharma slips away and the burden of wrongdoing rises on your head.
ramacharitamanas::2837.translation_literal: गुर (teacher) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / स्वामि (master) / हित (well-wishing) / बानी (words) / सुनि (hearing) / मन (mind) / मुदित (glad) / करिअ (should be done) / भलि (well) / जानी (knowing) / उचित (proper) / कि (or) / अनुचित (improper) / किएँ (by doing) / बिचारू (deliberation) / धरमु (dharma) / जाइ (goes away) / सिर (head) / पातक (wrongdoing) / भारू (load)
ramacharitamanas::2837.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2837.essence: Good counsel works only when you receive it without inner resistance.
ramacharitamanas::2837.simple_meaning: When trusted people guide you, receive it with a willing heart. Endless weighing of right and wrong can make you lose your sense of duty.
ramacharitamanas::2837.simple_insight: Peace comes from trusting good counsel instead of getting trapped in hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::2837.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is trying to respond rightly to the exile crisis. Tulsidas turns that moment into a rule for living: when guru, parents, masters, or well-wishers speak for your good, accept it without ego-driven second-guessing.
ramacharitamanas::2837.modern_relevance: Your mother, mentor, or manager gives you clear advice before a hard decision, and you keep reopening it in your head until the moment passes. This verse says the heart should receive good counsel before the mind turns it into noise.
ramacharitamanas::2837.insight: It shifts you from suspicious self-justification to humble acceptance of guidance.

ramacharitamanas::2838.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह तौ देहु सरल सिख सोई। जो आचरत मोर भल होई॥ जद्यपि यह समुझत हउँ नीकें। तदपि होत परितोष न जी कें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2838.verse_hindi: आप तो मुझे वही सरल शिक्षा दे रहे हैं, जिसके आचरण करने में मेरा भला हो। यद्यपि मैं इस बात को भलीभाँति समझता हूँ, तथापि मेरे हृदय को संतोष नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2838.english_translation: You are giving me the simple teaching that would do me good if I followed it. Even though I understand it well, my heart still finds no peace.
ramacharitamanas::2838.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / तौ (indeed) / देहु (you give) / सरल (simple) / सिख (teaching) / सोई (that same) / जो (which) / आचरत (by practicing) / मोर (my) / भल (good) / होई (happens) ॥ / जद्यपि (although) / यह (this) / समुझत (understanding) / हउँ (I am) / नीकें (well) / तदपि (still) / होत (happens) / परितोष (contentment) / न (not) / जी (heart) / कें (in)
ramacharitamanas::2838.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2838.essence: You can understand the right thing and still not feel at ease.
ramacharitamanas::2838.simple_meaning: A person can understand the right guidance clearly and still not feel settled inside. Knowing what is good is not always enough to bring peace.
ramacharitamanas::2838.simple_insight: It’s possible to agree with truth and still need time for the heart to catch up.
ramacharitamanas::2838.detailed_meaning: Bharat is speaking in Ayodhya after hearing guidance about what is right. He understands the teaching fully, yet admits that his heart still cannot settle. The verse shows the gap between clear understanding and inner peace.
ramacharitamanas::2838.modern_relevance: You nod through the conversation, say the sensible thing, and still feel tight in your chest after everyone leaves. Knowing the answer and living the answer are not the same.
ramacharitamanas::2838.insight: It separates intellectual agreement from emotional resolution, showing that clarity alone may not yet transform the heart.

ramacharitamanas::2839.verse_sanskrit: अब तुम्ह बिनय मोरि सुनि लेहू। मोहि अनुहरत सिखावनु देहू॥ ऊतरु देउँ छमब अपराधू। दुखित दोष गुन गनहिं न साधू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2839.verse_hindi: अब आप लोग मेरी विनती सुन लीजिए और मेरी योग्यता के अनुसार मुझे शिक्षा दीजिए। मैं उत्तर दे रहा हूँ, यह अपराध क्षमा कीजिए। साधु पुरुष दुःखी मनुष्य के दोष-गुणों को नहीं गिनते।
ramacharitamanas::2839.english_translation: Now please hear my request and teach me according to my capacity. Please forgive me for replying. Good people do not keep counting the faults and virtues of someone who is distressed.
ramacharitamanas::2839.translation_literal: अब (now) / तुम (you) / विनय (request) / मोरि (my) / सुनि (hearing) / लेहू (please take) / मोहि (to me) / अनुहरत (according to capacity) / सिखावनु (instruction) / देहू (give) ॥ ऊतरु (reply) / देउँ (I give) / छमब (forgive) / अपराधू (fault) / दुखित (distressed) / दोष (faults) / गुन (virtues) / गनहिं (count) / न (not) / साधू (good people) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2839.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2839.essence: A hurting person needs mercy before correction.
ramacharitamanas::2839.simple_meaning: Bharat asks for guidance suited to him and asks forgiveness for speaking back. He says kind people do not judge someone who is already in pain.
ramacharitamanas::2839.simple_insight: Pain changes the way words should be received. Compassion matters more than scoring who is right.
ramacharitamanas::2839.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is speaking with elders as grief and duty press on him. He lowers himself, asks to be taught gently, and reminds them that a sorrowful person should not be measured harshly.
ramacharitamanas::2839.modern_relevance: A family argument after bad news can turn every sentence into a weapon. This verse reminds you that when someone is hurting, the first response should be mercy, not analysis.
ramacharitamanas::2839.insight: It shifts you from evaluating a wounded person to responding with restraint and care.

ramacharitamanas::2840.verse_sanskrit: पितु सुरपुर सिय रामु बन करन कहहु मोहि राजु। एहि तें जानहु मोर हित कै आपन बड़ काजु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2840.verse_hindi: पिताजी स्वर्ग में हैं, श्री सीतारामजी वन में हैं और मुझे आप राज्य करने के लिए कह रहे हैं। इसमें आप मेरा कल्याण समझते हैं या अपना कोई बड़ा काम (होने की आशा रखते हैं)? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2840.english_translation: My father is in heaven, Sita and Ram are in the forest, and you ask me to rule. Do you mean my welfare, or your own great gain?
ramacharitamanas::2840.translation_literal: पितु (father) / सुरपुर (heavenly city) / सिय रामु (Sita and Ram) / बन (forest) / करन (to do) / कहहु (you say) / मोहि (to me) / राजु (rule) / एहि तें (from this) / जानहु (know) / मोर (my) / हित (welfare) / कै (or) / आपन (your own) / बड़ (great) / काजु (work, gain)
ramacharitamanas::2840.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2840.essence: What looks like power can be a burden disguised as help.
ramacharitamanas::2840.simple_meaning: Bharat rejects the idea that ruling the kingdom could be good for him. With Ram in exile and his father gone, he sees the offer as serving someone else's gain, not his own welfare.
ramacharitamanas::2840.simple_insight: Real care sometimes means refusing what looks impressive but feels wrong.
ramacharitamanas::2840.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before the court after Ram's exile and Dasharath's death. He sees the kingdom as poisoned by betrayal and absence. So when rule is offered to him, he questions whether it is meant for his good or for someone else's advantage.
ramacharitamanas::2840.modern_relevance: A family asks you to take over a business after a painful loss, but the role feels like a trap dressed as responsibility. Bharat's clarity helps you name when an offer is not truly for your good.
ramacharitamanas::2840.insight: It teaches you to test every opportunity by whether it serves your true good, not just others' convenience.

ramacharitamanas::2841.verse_sanskrit: हित हमार सियपति सेवकाईं। सो हरि लीन्ह मातु कुटिलाईं॥ मैं अनुमानि दीख मन माहीं। आन उपायँ मोर हित नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2841.verse_hindi: मेरा कल्याण तो सीतापति श्री रामजी की चाकरी में है, सो उसे माता की कुटिलता ने छीन लिया। मैंने अपने मन में अनुमान करके देख लिया है कि दूसरे किसी उपाय से मेरा कल्याण नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2841.english_translation: My true good is serving Sita's lord, but my mother’s crookedness has taken that away. I have seen it clearly in my own mind: no other remedy will bring me good.
ramacharitamanas::2841.translation_literal: हित (good) / हमार (my) / सियपति (Sita's lord) / सेवकाईं (service) / सो (that) / हरि (Ram) / लीन्ह (took away) / मातु (mother's) / कुटिलाईं (crookedness)॥ / मैं (I) / अनुमानि (having judged) / दीख (saw) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / आन (other) / उपायँ (by means) / मोर (my) / हित (good) / नाहीं (not)॥
ramacharitamanas::2841.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2841.essence: What you truly need is not status but the chance to serve what you love.
ramacharitamanas::2841.simple_meaning: Bharat sees that his true welfare lies in serving Ram, and he accepts that his mother's actions have blocked that path. He concludes that no other option can make him whole.
ramacharitamanas::2841.simple_insight: Peace comes when you stop bargaining with what you already know is true.
ramacharitamanas::2841.detailed_meaning: Bharat is speaking in Ayodhya after Ram has been sent away. He has already refused the throne in his heart. Here he names the wound plainly: his mother’s scheme has cut him off from Ram’s service, and he sees no other life that feels right.
ramacharitamanas::2841.modern_relevance: You get the promotion everyone wanted, but it feels empty because it pulls you away from what you truly care about. Bharat’s clarity is that some gains are losses in disguise.
ramacharitamanas::2841.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing status to recognising where your real fulfilment lies.

ramacharitamanas::2842.verse_sanskrit: सोक समाजु राजु केहि लेखें। लखन राम सिय बिनु पद देखें॥ बादि बसन बिनु भूषन भारू। बादि बिरति बिनु ब्रह्मबिचारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2842.verse_hindi: यह शोक का समुदाय राज्य लक्ष्मण, श्री रामचंद्रजी और सीताजी के चरणों को देखे बिना किस गिनती में है (इसका क्या मूल्य है)? जैसे कपड़ों के बिना गहनों का बोझ व्यर्थ है। वैराग्य के बिना ब्रह्मविचार व्यर्थ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2842.english_translation: What is a kingdom worth when Lakshman, Ram, and Sita cannot be seen? Ornaments are useless without clothes, and thought of Brahman is useless without detachment.
ramacharitamanas::2842.translation_literal: सोक समाजु (the gathering of grief) / राजु (kingdom) / केहि लेखें (for what count) / लखन राम सिय (Lakshman, Ram, and Sita) / बिनु (without) / पद देखें (seeing the feet) ॥ / बादि (vain) / बसन बिनु (without clothes) / भूषन (ornaments) / भारू (a burden) / बादि (vain) / बिरति बिनु (without detachment) / ब्रह्मबिचारू (contemplation of Brahman) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2842.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2842.essence: Without detachment, even wisdom becomes a burden.
ramacharitamanas::2842.simple_meaning: A kingdom has no value to Bharat without seeing Ram, Sita, and Lakshman. Outer possessions and even spiritual thought become empty without detachment.
ramacharitamanas::2842.simple_insight: What looks impressive can feel useless when the heart is elsewhere.
ramacharitamanas::2842.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands in Ayodhya after Ram's exile, refusing the throne his mother won for him. He measures everything against the absence of Ram, Sita, and Lakshman, and concludes that both worldly rule and dry philosophy are hollow without inner renunciation.
ramacharitamanas::2842.modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the title, the bigger office — and still feel sick because the one person you wanted to share it with is gone. Bharat knows that emptiness.
ramacharitamanas::2842.insight: It shifts value from status and display to presence and inner release.

ramacharitamanas::2843.verse_sanskrit: सरुज सरीर बादि बहु भोगा। बिनु हरिभगति जायँ जप जोगा॥ जायँ जीव बिनु देह सुहाई। बादि मोर सबु बिनु रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2843.verse_hindi: रोगी शरीर के लिए नाना प्रकार के भोग व्यर्थ हैं। श्री हरि की भक्ति के बिना जप और योग व्यर्थ हैं। जीव के बिना सुंदर देह व्यर्थ है, वैसे ही श्री रघुनाथजी के बिना मेरा सब कुछ व्यर्थ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2843.english_translation: A diseased body gains nothing from pleasures. Without devotion to Hari, chanting and yoga are useless. A beautiful body is useless without the living being within it, and everything of mine is useless without Raghunath.
ramacharitamanas::2843.translation_literal: सरुज (diseased) / सरीर (body) / बादि (vain, useless) / बहु (many) / भोगा (pleasures) / बिनु (without) / हरिभगति (devotion to Hari) / जायँ (go) / जप (chanting) / जोगा (yoga) / जायँ (go) / जीव (living being) / बिनु (without) / देह (body) / सुहाई (beautiful) / बादि (vain, useless) / मोर (my) / सबु (everything) / बिनु (without) / रघुराई (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::2843.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2843.essence: Everything loses meaning when Ram is missing.
ramacharitamanas::2843.simple_meaning: Pleasure, practice, beauty, and possessions all lose their value when Ram is absent. Real worth comes from devotion, not from outward success.
ramacharitamanas::2843.simple_insight: It brings relief to stop chasing what cannot complete you.
ramacharitamanas::2843.detailed_meaning: Bharat is grieving in Ayodhya after Ram's exile. He looks at body, ritual, pleasure, and possessions and sees them all as empty without Ram. This verse turns his sorrow into a total rejection of life without devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2843.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the new phone, the perfect apartment — and the room still feels strangely bare. Bharat names that ache: without what you love most, everything else can feel hollow.
ramacharitamanas::2843.insight: It shifts value away from outer gain and toward devotion as the measure of a full life.

ramacharitamanas::2844.verse_sanskrit: जाउँ राम पहिं आयसु देहू। एकाहिं आँक मोर हित एहू॥ मोहि नृप करि भल आपन चहहू। सोउ सनेह जड़ता बस कहहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2844.verse_hindi: मुझे आज्ञा दीजिए, मैं श्री रामजी के पास जाऊँ! एक ही आँक (निश्चयपूर्वक) मेरा हित इसी में है। और मुझे राजा बनाकर आप अपना भला चाहते हैं, यह भी आप स्नेह की जड़ता (मोह) के वश होकर ही कह रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2844.english_translation: Please let me go to Ram. My true good lies in that one aim. You want to make me king for my own benefit, but you say it only because love has clouded your mind.
ramacharitamanas::2844.translation_literal: जाउँ (let me go) / राम पहिं (to Ram's presence) / आयसु (permission) / देहू (give) । एकाहिं (only one) / आँक (aim) / मोर (my) / हित (good) / एहू (this) ॥ मोहि (me) / नृप करि (as king making) / भल (good) / आपन (your own) / चहहू (you want) । सोउ (that also) / सनेह (love) / जड़ता (stiffness / dullness) / बस (under the control of) / कहहू (you say) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2844.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2844.essence: True benefit may be refusing the crown and walking toward what you love.
ramacharitamanas::2844.simple_meaning: Bharat asks for permission to go to Ram and says that is his only real good. He rejects the offer of kingship as a confused act of misplaced affection.
ramacharitamanas::2844.simple_insight: Real clarity can look like refusing what everyone else calls success.
ramacharitamanas::2844.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before the elders after Ram's exile. He does not want power or comfort; he wants to go to Ram. Even the offer of the throne feels like love blinded by attachment, not true care.
ramacharitamanas::2844.modern_relevance: Your family insists the promotion is the safe choice, but your chest tightens because it would pull you away from what matters most. Bharat knows that not every good offer is your good.
ramacharitamanas::2844.insight: It shifts you from accepting status to asking what actually serves your deepest duty.

ramacharitamanas::2845.verse_sanskrit: कैकेई सुअ कुटिलमति राम बिमुख गतलाज। तुम्ह चाहत सुखु मोहबस मोहि से अधम कें राज ॥
ramacharitamanas::2845.verse_hindi: कैकेयी के पुत्र, कुटिलबुद्धि, रामविमुख और निर्लज्ज मुझ से अधम के राज्य से आप मोह के वश होकर ही सुख चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2845.english_translation: O son of Kaikeyi, you are crooked-minded, turned away from Ram, and shameless. You desire happiness only because of delusion, and you want the kingdom for me, the most fallen of men.
ramacharitamanas::2845.translation_literal: कैकेई सुअ (Kaikeyi's son) / कुटिलमति (crooked-minded) / राम बिमुख (turned away from Ram) / गतलाज (without shame) / तुम्ह (you) / चाहत (desire) / सुखु (happiness) / मोहबस (under the grip of delusion) / मोहि (me) / से (like) / अधम (fallen) / कें (for) / राज (kingdom)
ramacharitamanas::2845.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2845.essence: Power gained through delusion cannot satisfy a clear heart.
ramacharitamanas::2845.simple_meaning: Bharat rejects the idea that kingdom can bring real happiness when it comes from greed and turning away from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2845.simple_insight: False gain feels attractive, but it leaves the heart poorer than before.
ramacharitamanas::2845.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is refusing the throne and exposing Kaikeyi's desire as delusion. He sees that a kingdom won by turning away from Ram cannot bring real good, and he speaks with bitter honesty before the court.
ramacharitamanas::2845.modern_relevance: You get offered the promotion everyone else envies, but your stomach knots because it would cost your integrity. Bharat names that feeling: some victories are just delusion wearing a crown.
ramacharitamanas::2845.insight: It trains you to question rewards that separate you from what is right.

ramacharitamanas::2846.verse_sanskrit: कहउँ साँचु सब सुनि पतिआहू। चाहिअ धरमसील नरनाहू॥ मोहि राजु हठि देइहहु जबहीं। रसा रसातल जाइहि तबहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2846.verse_hindi: मैं सत्य कहता हूँ, आप सब सुनकर विश्वास करें, धर्मशील को ही राजा होना चाहिए। आप मुझे हठ करके ज्यों ही राज्य देंगे, त्यों ही पृथ्वी पाताल में धँस जाएगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2846.english_translation: I speak the truth; listen and believe me all of you: only a righteous king should rule. The moment you force the kingdom on me, the earth will sink into the underworld.
ramacharitamanas::2846.translation_literal: कहउँ (I speak) / साँचु (truth) / सब (all) / सुनि (having heard) / पतिआहू (believe) / चाहिअ (should be) / धरमसील (righteous) / नरनाहू (king) / मोहि (me) / राजु (kingdom) / हठि (by force) / देइहहु (you will give) / जबहीं (the moment) / रसा (earth) / रसातल (underworld) / जाइहि (will go) / तबहीं (then)
ramacharitamanas::2846.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2846.essence: Power given by force cannot hold a world together.
ramacharitamanas::2846.simple_meaning: Bharat says a kingdom should go only to a righteous ruler, and he warns that forcing him to accept it would be disastrous.
ramacharitamanas::2846.simple_insight: Real leadership cannot be taken by pressure; it must rest on character.
ramacharitamanas::2846.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is refusing the throne that came to him through family crisis. He tells the assembly that a righteous king alone should rule, and that if he is forced into power, the whole order will collapse.
ramacharitamanas::2846.modern_relevance: A family business gets handed to the one person who never wanted it, while the capable one is ignored. Bharat would say: don’t confuse pressure with rightful leadership.
ramacharitamanas::2846.insight: It shifts the mind from grabbing authority to honoring moral fitness for responsibility.

ramacharitamanas::2847.verse_sanskrit: मोहि समान को पाप निवासू। जेहि लगि सीय राम बनबासू॥ रायँ राम कहुँ काननु दीन्हा। बिछुरत गमनु अमरपुर कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2847.verse_hindi: मेरे समान पापों का घर कौन होगा, जिसके कारण सीताजी और श्री रामजी का वनवास हुआ? राजा ने श्री रामजी को वन दिया और उनके बिछुड़ते ही स्वयं स्वर्ग को गमन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2847.english_translation: Who is a storehouse of sin like me, because of whom Sita and Ram were sent to the forest? The king gave Ram the forest, and the moment they parted, he departed for the higher realm.
ramacharitamanas::2847.translation_literal: मोहि (me) / समान (like) / को (who) / पाप (sin) / निवासू (abode) / जेहि (because of whom) / लगि (for) / सीय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / बनबासू (forest exile) ॥ रायँ (the king) / राम कहुँ (to Ram) / काननु (forest) / दीन्हा (gave) / बिछुरत (on parting) / गमनु (departure) / अमरपुर (higher realm) / कीन्हा (made)
ramacharitamanas::2847.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2847.essence: Grief turns inward and names itself as the wound's cause.
ramacharitamanas::2847.simple_meaning: The speaker blames himself for Ram and Sita's exile and says Dasharath died the moment they were separated.
ramacharitamanas::2847.simple_insight: Grief can strip away excuses and leave only raw honesty.
ramacharitamanas::2847.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands inside the wreckage caused by Kaikeyi's demand. He sees Ram sent away to the forest and Dasharath collapse into death from separation. The verse is his anguished self-blame, not a calm doctrine.
ramacharitamanas::2847.modern_relevance: You replay one conversation for days after it breaks a family apart. Even if you didn't mean harm, your heart keeps asking what you set in motion.
ramacharitamanas::2847.insight: It shifts the mind from explanation to accountability, letting grief name the cost without hiding behind excuses.

ramacharitamanas::2848.verse_sanskrit: मैं सठु सब अनरथ कर हेतू। बैठ बात सब सुनउँ सचेतू॥ बिन रघुबीर बिलोकि अबासू। रहे प्रान सहि जग उपहासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2848.verse_hindi: और मैं दुष्ट, जो अनर्थों का कारण हूँ, होश-हवास में बैठा सब बातें सुन रहा हूँ। श्री रघुनाथजी से रहित घर को देखकर और जगत् का उपहास सहकर भी ये प्राण बने हुए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2848.english_translation: I am a fool, the cause of every disaster. I sit here awake, hearing everything. Seeing the home without Raghubir, and bearing the world's ridicule, these breaths still remain.
ramacharitamanas::2848.translation_literal: मैं (I) / सठु (foolish one) / सब (all) / अनरथ (disasters) / कर (of doing) / हेतू (cause) / बैठ (sitting) / बात (talk) / सब (all) / सुनउँ (I hear) / सचेतू (awake, alert) / बिन (without) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / बिलोकि (seeing) / अबासू (home, dwelling) / रहे (remain) / प्रान (breaths, life) / सहि (bearing) / जग (world) / उपहासू (mockery)
ramacharitamanas::2848.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2848.essence: Self-blame keeps breathing when love has been broken.
ramacharitamanas::2848.simple_meaning: Bharat calls himself the cause of disaster. He says he sits awake, sees the house without Ram, and still endures the world's mockery while life remains.
ramacharitamanas::2848.simple_insight: Grief can make you judge yourself harshly, even while you keep breathing and carrying on.
ramacharitamanas::2848.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands inside a home emptied by exile and shame. He blames himself for the rupture that sent Ram and Sita to the forest, and says he still lives only by enduring public ridicule and private pain.
ramacharitamanas::2848.modern_relevance: You replay the family argument at 2 a.m., convinced you caused everything. The room is quiet, but your mind keeps calling you the reason the house broke.
ramacharitamanas::2848.insight: It shifts the reader from self-justifying denial to honest remorse and the weight of consequences.

ramacharitamanas::2849.verse_sanskrit: राम पुनीत बिषय रस रूखे। लोलुप भूमि भोग के भूखे॥ कहँ लगि कहौं हृदय कठिनाई। निदरि कुलिसु जेहिं लही बड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2849.verse_hindi: (इसका यही कारण है कि ये प्राण) श्री राम रूपी पवित्र विषय रस में आसक्त नहीं हैं। ये लालची भूमि और भोगों के ही भूखे हैं। मैं अपने हृदय की कठोरता कहाँ तक कहूँ? जिसने वज्र का भी तिरस्कार करके बड़ाई पाई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2849.english_translation: Ram is pure and untouched by worldly taste, but these people are greedy and hungry for land and pleasure. How far can I speak of my own hard-heartedness? The one who has even surpassed a thunderbolt has won praise.
ramacharitamanas::2849.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / पुनीत (pure) / बिषय रस (worldly taste) / रूखे (dry, untouched) । / लोलुप (greedy) / भूमि भोग (land and enjoyment) / के भूखे (hungry for) ॥ / कहँ (how far) / लगि (up to) / कहौं (shall I say) / हृदय (heart) / कठिनाई (hardness) । / निदरि (disregarding) / कुलिसु (thunderbolt) / जेहिं (by whom) / लही (was obtained) / बड़ाई (praise) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2849.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2849.essence: Greed makes the heart harder than a thunderbolt.
ramacharitamanas::2849.simple_meaning: Ram remains untouched by worldly pleasure, while others crave land and enjoyment. The speaker blames his own hard heart, saying even a thunderbolt could be outdone by such hardness.
ramacharitamanas::2849.simple_insight: When desire hardens the heart, even obvious truth can feel powerless.
ramacharitamanas::2849.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the exile has shattered the royal family. Tulsidas speaks in grief, contrasting Ram's purity with the greed and hardness that caused the suffering. The verse is part of a flowing lament, not a complete teaching on its own.
ramacharitamanas::2849.modern_relevance: You watch someone cling to property, status, or comfort long after it has begun hurting everyone around them. The tragedy is not only what they want, but how wanting has made them unreachable.
ramacharitamanas::2849.insight: It frames greed as a hardening of the heart that blocks repentance and clear seeing.

ramacharitamanas::2850.verse_sanskrit: कारन तें कारजु कठिन होइ दोसु नहिं मोर। कुलिस अस्थि तें उपल तें लोह कराल कठोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::2850.verse_hindi: कारण से कार्य कठिन होता ही है, इसमें मेरा दोष नहीं। हड्डी से वज्र और पत्थर से लोहा भयानक और कठोर होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2850.english_translation: The task becomes hard because of its cause; the fault is not mine. From bone comes the thunderbolt, and from stone comes iron — both are fiercely hard.
ramacharitamanas::2850.translation_literal: कारन तें (because of the cause) / कारजु (the task) / कठिन (hard) / होइ (becomes) / दोसु (fault) / नहिं (not) / मोर (mine) / कुलिस (thunderbolt) / अस्थि (from bone) / तें (from) / उपल (stone) / तें (from) / लोह (iron) / कराल (fierce) / कठोर (hard)
ramacharitamanas::2850.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2850.essence: Hardness often comes from causes, not from your moral failure.
ramacharitamanas::2850.simple_meaning: A difficult outcome can come from the conditions that created it. Not everything hard is a personal failure.
ramacharitamanas::2850.simple_insight: It gives you relief from self-blame and helps you see the real forces behind a painful situation.
ramacharitamanas::2850.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is grieving the exile of Ram and examining his own heart with painful honesty. He says the situation became hard because of its causes, not because of him, using hard materials as an image for how stubborn this suffering has become.
ramacharitamanas::2850.modern_relevance: You walk into a family meeting already tense from weeks of silence, and the first sharp word makes everything worse. Later, you realise the conflict did not begin with that one moment.
ramacharitamanas::2850.insight: It shifts the mind from personal blame to causal understanding, so you can respond more clearly instead of collapsing into guilt.

ramacharitamanas::2851.verse_sanskrit: कैकेई भव तनु अनुरागे। पावँर प्रान अघाइ अभागे॥ जौं प्रिय बिरहँ प्रान प्रिय लागे। देखब सुनब बहुत अब आगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2851.verse_hindi: कैकेयी से उत्पन्न देह में प्रेम करने वाले ये पामर प्राण भरपेट (पूरी तरह से) अभागे हैं। जब प्रिय के वियोग में भी मुझे प्राण प्रिय लग रहे हैं, तब अभी आगे मैं और भी बहुत कुछ देखूँ-सुनूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2851.english_translation: The lowly, unlucky life that loves Kaikeyi's body is already full. If life still feels dear even in separation from the beloved, then much more is still to come.
ramacharitamanas::2851.translation_literal: कैकेई (Kaikeyi) / भव-तनु (body born in the world) / अनुरागे (attached in love) / पावँर (lowly, base) / प्रान (life-breaths) / अघाइ (filled) / अभागे (unfortunate) / जौं (if) / प्रिय (beloved) / बिरहँ (in separation) / प्रान (life-breaths) / प्रिय (dear) / लागे (seem) / देखब (seeing) / सुनब (hearing) / बहुत (many) / अब (now) / आगे (ahead)
ramacharitamanas::2851.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2851.essence: Even life feels heavy when separation has already begun.
ramacharitamanas::2851.simple_meaning: These words describe how the speaker feels trapped by attachment and bad fortune, yet still expects even more suffering ahead.
ramacharitamanas::2851.simple_insight: Some grief is so deep that even breathing feels like a burden.
ramacharitamanas::2851.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the fallout of Kaikeyi's demand is tearing through the royal family. The speaker, overwhelmed by the pain of separation from Ram, speaks bitterly of life itself and senses that even harder sights and sounds still lie ahead.
ramacharitamanas::2851.modern_relevance: You get the call after midnight, and one bad choice has already split the family in two. You can feel the next wave coming before it arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2851.insight: It shifts the reader into bracing awareness: pain is not over, and the heart is already carrying too much.

ramacharitamanas::2852.verse_sanskrit: लखन राम सिय कहुँ बनु दीन्हा। पठइ अमरपुर पति हित कीन्हा॥ लीन्ह बिधवपन अपजसु आपू। दीन्हेउ प्रजहि सोकु संतापू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2852.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मण, श्री रामजी और सीताजी को तो वन दिया, स्वर्ग भेजकर पति का कल्याण किया, स्वयं विधवापन और अपयश लिया, प्रजा को शोक और संताप दिया, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2852.english_translation: Lakshman, Ram, and Sita were sent to the forest; the king was made to serve their good. I took widowhood and disgrace upon myself, and gave the people sorrow and anguish.
ramacharitamanas::2852.translation_literal: लखन (Lakshman) / राम (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / कहुँ (to) / बनु (forest) / दीन्हा (gave) / पठइ (sending) / अमरपुर पति (lord of the higher realm) / हित (welfare) / कीन्हा (did) / लीन्ह (took) / बिधवपन (widowhood) / अपजसु (disgrace) / आपू (myself) / दीन्हेउ (gave) / प्रजहि (to the people) / सोकु (sorrow) / संतापू (anguish)
ramacharitamanas::2852.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2852.essence: A defended wrong can still leave everyone wounded.
ramacharitamanas::2852.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi justifies her demand by claiming it helped the king, but it brought exile, disgrace, and suffering to everyone else.
ramacharitamanas::2852.simple_insight: A mind can defend a harmful choice and still be unable to escape its consequences.
ramacharitamanas::2852.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kaikeyi defends the exile of Ram, Sita, and Lakshman as if it were for Dasharath's good. But the result is the opposite: the household is shattered, she is left with disgrace, and the people are drowned in grief.
ramacharitamanas::2852.modern_relevance: You explain a decision in the meeting as 'necessary,' but your team is silent and hurt. The story you tell yourself can sound noble while the damage spreads anyway.
ramacharitamanas::2852.insight: It exposes how self-justification can hide the real cost of your choices.

ramacharitamanas::2853.verse_sanskrit: मोहि दीन्ह सुखु सुजसु सुराजू। कीन्ह कैकईं सब कर काजू॥ ऐहि तें मोर काह अब नीका। तेहि पर देन कहहु तुम्ह टीका ॥
ramacharitamanas::2853.verse_hindi: और मुझे सुख, सुंदर यश और उत्तम राज्य दिया! कैकेयी ने सभी का काम बना दिया! इससे अच्छा अब मेरे लिए और क्या होगा? उस पर भी आप लोग मुझे राजतिलक देने को कहते हैं! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2853.english_translation: You gave me happiness, fine fame, and a splendid kingdom! Kaikeyi has done everything well! What more could be right for me now? And yet you still speak of giving me the coronation!
ramacharitamanas::2853.translation_literal: मोहि (to me) / दीन्ह (gave) / सुखु (happiness) / सुजसु (good fame) / सुराजू (excellent kingdom) / कीन्ह (did) / कैकईं (Kaikeyi) / सब (all) / कर (of) / काजू (work, task) / ऐहि (of this) / तें (than) / मोर (my) / काह (what) / अब (now) / नीका (good, right) / तेहि (that) / पर (on) / देन (to give) / कहहु (you say) / तुम्ह (you) / टीका (coronation mark, royal consecration)
ramacharitamanas::2853.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2853.essence: Real contentment makes even a crown feel unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::2853.simple_meaning: Bharat says he already has happiness, fame, and a kingdom, so he sees no need for more. He questions why anyone would even offer him coronation.
ramacharitamanas::2853.simple_insight: Contentment can make ambition look strangely unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::2853.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat speaks from the wound of exile and the burden of kingship. Surrounded by grief, he rejects the idea that royal power could improve his life. The verse shows his deep refusal of desire.
ramacharitamanas::2853.modern_relevance: You get the promotion email after a week of chaos, but your chest feels empty instead of excited. Bharat knows that some prizes stop mattering once you see what they cost.
ramacharitamanas::2853.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing status to seeing how little status can satisfy.

ramacharitamanas::2854.verse_sanskrit: कैकइ जठर जनमि जग माहीं। यह मोहि कहँ कछु अनुचित नाहीं॥ मोरि बात सब बिधिहिं बनाई। प्रजा पाँच कत करहु सहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2854.verse_hindi: कैकयी के पेट से जगत् में जन्म लेकर यह मेरे लिए कुछ भी अनुचित नहीं है। मेरी सब बात तो विधाता ने ही बना दी है। (फिर) उसमें प्रजा और पंच (आप लोग) क्यों सहायता कर रहे हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2854.english_translation: Having been born into the world from Kaikeyi's womb, nothing in this is improper for me. My entire situation has been arranged by fate. Then why are you all, the subjects and the council, helping in this matter?
ramacharitamanas::2854.translation_literal: कैकइ (of Kaikeyi) / जठर (womb) / जनमि (having been born) / जग माहीं (in the world) / यह (this) / मोहि कहँ (for me) / कछु (anything) / अनुचित (improper) / नाहीं (is not) / मोरि (my) / बात (matter) / सब (all) / बिधिहिं (by fate / the divine ordering) / बनाई (made) / प्रजा (subjects) / पाँच (council of five) / कत (why) / करहु (are you doing) / सहाई (help)
ramacharitamanas::2854.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2854.essence: What has already unfolded cannot be made wrong by your resistance.
ramacharitamanas::2854.simple_meaning: Bharat says that being born from Kaikeyi does not make his situation improper. He sees the whole event as already arranged, and asks why anyone is still trying to fix it.
ramacharitamanas::2854.simple_insight: There is relief in stopping the fight against what has already unfolded.
ramacharitamanas::2854.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat has just rejected the throne after Ram's exile. He speaks with painful clarity: his birth, his family position, and the whole crisis are already part of a larger order. The verse closes the argument by moving from protest to acceptance.
ramacharitamanas::2854.modern_relevance: You replay a family argument at 1am, trying to rewrite every line. At some point, the harder truth arrives: the event is done, and your peace depends on how you receive it.
ramacharitamanas::2854.insight: It shifts the mind from resisting the past to meeting reality without self-torment.

ramacharitamanas::2855.verse_sanskrit: ग्रह ग्रहीत पुनि बात बस तेहि पुनि बीछी मार। तेहि पिआइअ बारुनी कहहु काह उपचार ॥
ramacharitamanas::2855.verse_hindi: जिसे कुग्रह लगे हों (अथवा जो पिशाचग्रस्त हो), फिर जो वायुरोग से पीड़ित हो और उसी को फिर बिच्छू डंक मार दे, उसको यदि मदिरा पिलाई जाए, तो कहिए यह कैसा इलाज है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2855.english_translation: What kind of cure is it to give liquor to someone already seized by an evil influence, troubled by wind disorder, and then stung by a scorpion?
ramacharitamanas::2855.translation_literal: ग्रह-ग्रहीत (seized by an evil influence) / पुनि (again) / बात-बस (troubled by wind disorder) / तेहि (to that one) / पुनि (again) / बीछी-मार (scorpion sting) / तेहि (to that one) / पिआइअ (is given to drink) / बारुनी (liquor) / कहहु (say) / काह (what) / उपचार (remedy)
ramacharitamanas::2855.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2855.essence: A wrong remedy can intensify the wound it claims to fix.
ramacharitamanas::2855.simple_meaning: A bad remedy can make a bad situation worse. Tulsidas uses a sharp image to say that the wrong response only deepens suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2855.simple_insight: You can recognize when a fix is actually another layer of harm.
ramacharitamanas::2855.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is arguing over the damage Kaikeyi's demand has caused. He compares the situation to a person already afflicted by one illness, then struck again, and then given liquor as treatment. The point is bitter: some responses only worsen what is already broken.
ramacharitamanas::2855.modern_relevance: You are already overwhelmed, and someone tells you to just drink, scroll, or shut down. The verse names that false relief: not every soothing thing is a cure.
ramacharitamanas::2855.insight: It shifts you to question quick fixes that numb rather than heal.

ramacharitamanas::2856.verse_sanskrit: कैकइ सुअन जोगु जग जोई। चतुर बिरंचि दीन्ह मोहि सोई॥ दसरथ तनय राम लघु भाई। दीन्हि मोहि बिधि बादि बड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2856.verse_hindi: कैकेयी के लड़के के लिए संसार में जो कुछ योग्य था, चतुर विधाता ने मुझे वही दिया। पर 'दशरथजी का पुत्र' और 'राम का छोटा भाई' होने की बड़ाई मुझे विधाता ने व्यर्थ ही दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2856.english_translation: Whatever was fit for Kaikeyi's son in this world, the wise creator gave me that alone. The glory of being Dasharath's son and Ram's younger brother was given to me by fate in vain.
ramacharitamanas::2856.translation_literal: कैकइ (Kaikeyi's) / सुअन (son) / जोगु (fit, suitable) / जग (world) / जोई (whatever) / चतुर (wise) / बिरंचि (creator) / दीन्ह (gave) / मोहि (to me) / सोई (that only)॥ / दसरथ (Dasharath's) / तनय (son) / राम (Ram) / लघु (younger) / भाई (brother) / दीन्हि (gave) / मोहि (to me) / बिधि (fate, the arranger) / बादि (in vain) / बड़ाई (glory, honour)॥
ramacharitamanas::2856.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2856.essence: Real dignity comes from accepting the place that truly fits you.
ramacharitamanas::2856.simple_meaning: Bharat says he received only what suited him, and the honour of being Ram's brother was never truly his to claim.
ramacharitamanas::2856.simple_insight: Relief comes when you stop reaching for a role that was never yours.
ramacharitamanas::2856.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat rejects the throne and looks at his own life without envy. He says the creator gave him only what fit him, while the title of Dasharath's son and Ram's younger brother was a borrowed honour, not a possession.
ramacharitamanas::2856.modern_relevance: You watch someone else get the title, the praise, the family approval you wanted. Bharat's clarity says the role that fits you is enough, and borrowed honour cannot feed your heart.
ramacharitamanas::2856.insight: It shifts you from comparison to rightful place, so you stop measuring yourself by someone else's status.

ramacharitamanas::2857.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह सब कहहु कढ़ावन टीका। राय रजायसु सब कहँ नीका॥ उतरु देउँ केहि बिधि केहि केही। कहहु सुखेन जथा रुचि जेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2857.verse_hindi: आप सब लोग भी मुझे राज तिलक कराने को कह रहे हैं! राजा की आज्ञा सभी के लिए अच्छी है। मैं किस-किस को किस-किस प्रकार से उत्तर दूँ? जिसकी जैसी रुचि हो, आप लोग सुखपूर्वक वही कहें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2857.english_translation: You all are telling me to arrange the coronation! The king's command is good for everyone. How am I to answer each person in each way? Speak freely as you like, in whichever way suits you.
ramacharitamanas::2857.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you all) / सब (all) / कहहु (say) / कढ़ावन (for crowning / arranging the coronation) / टीका (coronation) / राय (king's) / रजायसु (command) / सब (all) / कहँ (for) / नीका (good) / उतरु (answer) / देउँ (I give) / केहि (to whom) / बिधि (in what way) / केहि (to whom) / केही (what) / कहहु (say) / सुखेन (comfortably) / जथा (as) / रुचि (preference) / जेही (whose)
ramacharitamanas::2857.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2857.essence: You do not need to satisfy every demand at once.
ramacharitamanas::2857.simple_meaning: Bharat says he cannot answer everyone’s expectations about his coronation. He asks them to speak as they wish and says the king’s order must be respected.
ramacharitamanas::2857.simple_insight: When everyone pulls you in different directions, you can still stay calm and let the rightful order stand.
ramacharitamanas::2857.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat stands before people who are urging him toward the throne. But he has already turned inward toward Ram’s exile and his father’s command. This verse shows his quiet refusal to get trapped in public pressure.
ramacharitamanas::2857.modern_relevance: Your family group chat is full of opinions about what you should do next, and every message wants a different answer. Bharat’s calm shows you can refuse the noise without becoming harsh.
ramacharitamanas::2857.insight: It teaches you to stay composed under competing demands and not let public pressure distort your duty.

ramacharitamanas::2858.verse_sanskrit: मोहि कुमातु समेत बिहाई। कहहु कहिहि के कीन्ह भलाई॥ मो बिनु को सचराचर माहीं। जेहि सिय रामु प्रानप्रिय नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2858.verse_hindi: मेरी कुमाता कैकेयी समेत मुझे छोड़कर, कहिए और कौन कहेगा कि यह काम अच्छा किया गया? जड़-चेतन जगत् में मेरे सिवा और कौन है, जिसको श्री सीता-रामजी प्राणों के समान प्यारे न हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::2858.english_translation: Leaving aside my evil-minded mother, who will say that this was well done? In all the moving and unmoving world, who besides me does not hold Sita and Ram dearer than life?
ramacharitamanas::2858.translation_literal: मोहि (me) / कुमातु (evil-minded mother) / समेत (along with) / बिहाई (leaving aside) / कहहु (say) / कहिहि (will say) / के (who) / कीन्ह (done) / भलाई (goodness)॥ / मो (me) / बिनु (without) / को (who) / सचराचर (moving and unmoving) / माहीं (in the world) / जेहि (to whom) / सिय रामु (Sita and Ram) / प्रानप्रिय (dearer than life) / नाहीं (are not) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2858.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2858.essence: What looks like a gain to others can still be a deep loss to you.
ramacharitamanas::2858.simple_meaning: Bharat says no one can call this choice good, because he has been left behind. For him, nothing in the world is dearer than Sita and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2858.simple_insight: Real devotion can feel like loss to everyone else and still remain true.
ramacharitamanas::2858.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before the court after learning of Ram's exile and his own unwanted position. He rejects praise for the situation, saying that anyone who truly loves Ram and Sita would see the pain in it.
ramacharitamanas::2858.modern_relevance: You smiled through the family dinner after being blamed for a decision you never made. Everyone called it fine. You knew exactly what it cost.
ramacharitamanas::2858.insight: It teaches you to trust your own clear seeing when others mistake sacrifice for success.

ramacharitamanas::2859.verse_sanskrit: परम हानि सब कहँ बड़ लाहू। अदिनु मोर नहिं दूषन काहू॥ संसय सील प्रेम बस अहहू। सबुइ उचित सब जो कछु कहहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2859.verse_hindi: जो परम हानि है, उसी में सबको बड़ा लाभ दिख रहा है। मेरा बुरा दिन है किसी का दोष नहीं। आप सब जो कुछ कहते हैं सो सब उचित ही है, क्योंकि आप लोग संशय, शील और प्रेम के वश हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2859.english_translation: What is my greatest loss looks like the greatest gain to everyone else. My own bad day is no one else's fault. Everything you say is proper, because you are all moved by doubt, virtue, and love.
ramacharitamanas::2859.translation_literal: परम हानि (greatest loss) / सब कहँ (for everyone) / बड़ लाहू (great gain) / अदिनु (bad day) / मोर (my) / नहिं (not) / दूषन (fault) / काहू (of anyone) / संसय (doubt) / सील (virtue) / प्रेम (love) / बस (under the sway) / अहहू (you all are) / सबुइ (all) / उचित (proper) / सब (all) / जो कछु (whatever) / कहहू (you say)
ramacharitamanas::2859.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2859.essence: Loss can be borne without blame when the heart stays clear.
ramacharitamanas::2859.simple_meaning: Bharat says his exile feels like a huge loss to him, but others may see benefit in it. He refuses blame and accepts that everyone is speaking from care, doubt, and love.
ramacharitamanas::2859.simple_insight: You can face loss without turning it into blame. That keeps the heart open.
ramacharitamanas::2859.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before the court after Ram has been sent away. He knows the kingdom has gained nothing real from his suffering, yet he refuses accusation. He sees that the people around him are speaking from concern, uncertainty, and affection.
ramacharitamanas::2859.modern_relevance: You got passed over for a promotion, and the team says it was 'for the best.' It still hurts. This verse teaches you to hold the pain without immediately turning it into resentment.
ramacharitamanas::2859.insight: It shifts you from accusation to mature acceptance, letting you name pain without making enemies of everyone around you.

ramacharitamanas::2860.verse_sanskrit: राम मातु सुठि सरलचित मो पर प्रेमु बिसेषि। कहइ सुभाय सनेह बस मोरि दीनता देखि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2860.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी की माता बहुत ही सरल हृदय हैं और मुझ पर उनका विशेष प्रेम है, इसलिए मेरी दीनता देखकर वे स्वाभाविक स्नेहवश ही ऐसा कह रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2860.english_translation: Ram's mother is very simple-hearted and has special affection for me, so seeing my helplessness, she speaks this way out of natural love.
ramacharitamanas::2860.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / मातु (mother) / सुठि (very) / सरलचित (simple-hearted) / मो पर (for me) / प्रेमु (love) / बिसेषि (special) / कहइ (speaks) / सुभाय (by nature) / सनेह (affection) / बस (driven by) / मोरि (my) / दीनता (helplessness) / देखि (seeing)
ramacharitamanas::2860.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2860.essence: Bharat sees affection beneath Kaikeyi's harshness.
ramacharitamanas::2860.simple_meaning: Bharat says Kaikeyi is naturally tender toward him and speaks out of affection after seeing his helplessness.
ramacharitamanas::2860.simple_insight: Love can be mistaken for approval, especially when grief is speaking.
ramacharitamanas::2860.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat is trying to make sense of the ruin left by Kaikeyi's demand and Dasharath's collapse. He softens her blame by saying she is simple-hearted and loves him, so her words came from affection stirred by his helpless state.
ramacharitamanas::2860.modern_relevance: A parent says something cutting while watching you break down, and later you realize the words came from worry, not cruelty. Hurt can distort even love.
ramacharitamanas::2860.insight: It shifts the mind from judging only the surface words to seeing the emotion underneath them.

ramacharitamanas::2861.verse_sanskrit: गुर बिबेक सागर जगु जाना। जिन्हहि बिस्व कर बदर समाना॥ मो कहँ तिलक साज सज सोऊ। भएँ बिधि बिमुख बिमुख सबु कोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2861.verse_hindi: गुरुजी ज्ञान के समुद्र हैं, इस बात को सारा जगत् जानता है, जिसके लिए विश्व हथेली पर रखे हुए बेर के समान है, वे भी मेरे लिए राजतिलक का साज सज रहे हैं। सत्य है, विधाता के विपरीत होने पर सब कोई विपरीत हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2861.english_translation: The guru is an ocean of discernment, and the whole world knows it. To him, the world is like a berry held in the palm. Yet even he is arranging my coronation. When fate turns against you, everyone turns against you too.
ramacharitamanas::2861.translation_literal: गुर (teacher) / बिबेक (discernment) / सागर (ocean) / जगु (world) / जाना (known) / जिन्हहि (to whom) / बिस्व (world) / कर (hand) / बदर (berry) / समाना (equal)॥ मो (me) / कहँ (for) / तिलक (coronation mark) / साज (ornaments) / सज (arranging) / सोऊ (that one) / भएँ (having become) / बिधि (fate) / बिमुख (turned away) / बिमुख (turned away) / सबु (all) / कोऊ (someone) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2861.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2861.essence: Even wisdom cannot stop the world from turning harsh when fortune turns.
ramacharitamanas::2861.simple_meaning: Bharat says that even the greatest teacher sees the world as small, yet he is preparing a coronation for him. But when fate turns against someone, everyone seems to turn away too.
ramacharitamanas::2861.simple_insight: Grief can make the whole world feel unreliable, even when wisdom is present.
ramacharitamanas::2861.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat speaks from the pain of Ram's exile and his own rejection of power. He praises the guru's vast understanding, yet admits that the forces moving this moment have turned everyone upside down, including himself.
ramacharitamanas::2861.modern_relevance: You watch a promotion vanish, and suddenly even your allies go quiet. This verse names that strange loneliness: when life shifts against you, people often shift with it.
ramacharitamanas::2861.insight: It shifts the mind from expecting fairness in the moment to seeing how quickly support can change under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::2862.verse_sanskrit: परिहरि रामु सीय जग माहीं। कोउ न कहिहि मोर मत नाहीं॥ सो मैं सुनब सहब सुखु मानी। अंतहुँ कीच तहाँ जहँ पानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2862.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी और सीताजी को छोड़कर जगत् में कोई यह नहीं कहेगा कि इस अनर्थ में मेरी सम्मति नहीं है। मैं उसे सुखपूर्वक सुनूँगा और सहूँगा, क्योंकि जहाँ पानी होता है, वहाँ अन्त में कीचड़ होता ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2862.english_translation: No one in the world, except Ram and Sita, will say I had no part in this. I will hear it gladly and bear it, because where there is water, mud will eventually appear.
ramacharitamanas::2862.translation_literal: परिहरि (leaving aside) / रामु (Ram) / सीय (Sita) / जग माहीं (in the world) / कोउ (anyone) / न कहिहि (will not say) / मोर (my) / मत (consent) / नाहीं (not)॥ / सो (that) / मैं (I) / सुनब (will hear) / सहब (will bear) / सुखु मानी (taking it gladly) / अंतहुँ (in the end) / कीच (mud) / तहाँ (there) / जहँ (where) / पानी (water) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2862.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2862.essence: A clean heart can endure blame without needing to defend itself.
ramacharitamanas::2862.simple_meaning: Bharat says he will accept blame without protest. Even if people accuse him, he will endure it calmly, because any situation with good intentions can still end in some stain.
ramacharitamanas::2862.simple_insight: You do not have to defend yourself from every accusation. A steady heart can stay clean even when blame gathers around it.
ramacharitamanas::2862.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat has already refused the throne and placed Ram's sandals on it. Now he faces the suspicion that his own hands are part of the exile's injustice. He says he will accept the criticism calmly, because worldly action always leaves some mud behind.
ramacharitamanas::2862.modern_relevance: You helped organize the plan, and now the group chat is blaming you for the mess. You could scramble to clear your name, or you could stay steady and let the noise pass.
ramacharitamanas::2862.insight: It shifts you from image-protection to inner steadiness, so you can endure blame without losing your centre.

ramacharitamanas::2863.verse_sanskrit: डरु न मोहि जग कहिहि कि पोचू। परलोकहु कर नाहिन सोचू॥ एकइ उर बस दुसह दवारी। मोहि लगि भे सिय रामु दुखारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2863.verse_hindi: मुझे इसका डर नहीं है कि जगत् मुझे बुरा कहेगा और न मुझे परलोक का ही सोच है। मेरे हृदय में तो बस, एक ही दुःसह दावानल धधक रहा है कि मेरे कारण श्री सीता-रामजी दुःखी हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2863.english_translation: I do not fear that the world will call me base, nor do I worry about the next world. Only one unbearable fire burns in my heart: because of me, Sita and Ram are suffering.
ramacharitamanas::2863.translation_literal: डरु न (I do not fear) / मोहि (for me) / जग (the world) / कहिहि (will say) / कि (that) / पोचू (base) / परलोकहु (even the next world) / कर (of) / नाहिन (not) / सोचू (worry) / एकइ (only one) / उर (in the heart) / बस (dwells) / दुसह (unbearable) / दवारी (fire) / मोहि लगि (because of me) / भे (have become) / सिय (Sita) / रामु (Ram) / दुखारी (sorrowful)
ramacharitamanas::2863.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2863.essence: Love hurts most when it sees itself as the cause of another's pain.
ramacharitamanas::2863.simple_meaning: Bharat says he does not care about public shame or even the afterlife. What torments him is that Ram and Sita are suffering because of him.
ramacharitamanas::2863.simple_insight: Real remorse is not about reputation. It hurts because love has been wounded.
ramacharitamanas::2863.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is crushed by the exile that has separated Ram and Sita. He rejects concern for public opinion and the next world alike. His only agony is the pain his actions have brought to the people he loves most.
ramacharitamanas::2863.modern_relevance: You replay a conversation all night, not because people might judge you, but because someone you love is hurting and you helped cause it.
ramacharitamanas::2863.insight: It shifts remorse from self-image to relationship: the measure is not how you look, but whom you have wounded.

ramacharitamanas::2864.verse_sanskrit: जीवन लाहु लखन भल पावा। सबु तजि राम चरन मनु लावा॥ मोर जनम रघुबर बन लागी। झूठ काह पछिताउँ अभागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2864.verse_hindi: जीवन का उत्तम लाभ तो लक्ष्मण ने पाया, जिन्होंने सब कुछ तजकर श्री रामजी के चरणों में मन लगाया। मेरा जन्म तो श्री रामजी के वनवास के लिए ही हुआ था। मैं अभागा झूठ-मूठ क्या पछताता हूँ? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2864.english_translation: Lakshman has gained the best reward of life: leaving everything, he set his mind on Ram's feet. My birth was meant for Raghubar's exile; why should I, the unfortunate one, pretend to regret it?
ramacharitamanas::2864.translation_literal: जीवन (life) / लाहु (profit, gain) / लखन (Lakshman) / भल (good, excellent) / पावा (has found) / सबु (everything) / तजि (leaving) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / मनु (mind) / लावा (attached, applied)॥ / मोर (my) / जनम (birth) / रघुबर (Lord of the Raghu clan) / बन (forest, exile) / लागी (for, meant for) / झूठ (false) / काह (why) / पछिताउँ (should I regret) / अभागी (unfortunate one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2864.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2864.essence: What looks like sacrifice can be the truest gain.
ramacharitamanas::2864.simple_meaning: Lakshman’s life is praised as successful because he gave up everything and fixed his mind on Ram. The speaker also accepts that her own life was meant to support Ram’s exile.
ramacharitamanas::2864.simple_insight: Real worth can come from loyal service, not personal gain.
ramacharitamanas::2864.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaikeyi faces the full weight of what her demand has caused. Looking at Lakshman’s total devotion and at Ram’s exile, she admits the painful irony: one brother has gained life through surrender, while her own life is bound to this sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2864.modern_relevance: You walk past a promotion because taking it would betray someone you love. Later, you realise the real loss would have been becoming the kind of person who could not do that.
ramacharitamanas::2864.insight: It shifts the mind from measuring success by gain to measuring it by fidelity.

ramacharitamanas::2865.verse_sanskrit: आपनि दारुन दीनता कहउँ सबहि सिरु नाइ। देखें बिनु रघुनाथ पद जिय कै जरनि न जाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2865.verse_hindi: सबको सिर झुकाकर मैं अपनी दारुण दीनता कहता हूँ। श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणों के दर्शन किए बिना मेरे जी की जलन न जाएगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2865.english_translation: Bowing to everyone, I speak of my deep helplessness. Without seeing Raghunath's feet, the burning in my heart will not go.
ramacharitamanas::2865.translation_literal: आपनि (my own) / दारुन (severe) / दीनता (helplessness) / कहउँ (I speak) / सबहि (to everyone) / सिरु नाइ (bowing the head) / देखें (seeing) / बिनु (without) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / पद (feet) / जिय (of the heart) / कै (of) / जरनि (burning) / न जाइ (does not go)
ramacharitamanas::2865.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2865.essence: Humble surrender names the wound that only Ram can heal.
ramacharitamanas::2865.simple_meaning: Bharat says he is deeply helpless and humbly admits it to everyone. Only seeing Ram again can ease the burning in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::2865.simple_insight: There is relief in admitting you cannot fix everything yourself.
ramacharitamanas::2865.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before others after Ram has been sent away. He bows his head and confesses his helplessness. The only relief he can imagine is seeing Ram's feet again.
ramacharitamanas::2865.modern_relevance: You’ve replayed the same conversation all night, and nothing in you settles. The apology, the reunion, the answer you’re waiting for — you know exactly where your heart is headed.
ramacharitamanas::2865.insight: It shifts you from self-protective pride to humble longing for what truly restores you.

ramacharitamanas::2866.verse_sanskrit: आन उपाउ मोहि नहिं सूझा। को जिय कै रघुबर बिनु बूझा॥ एकहिं आँक इहइ मन माहीं। प्रातकाल चलिहउँ प्रभु पाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2866.verse_hindi: मुझे दूसरा कोई उपाय नहीं सूझता। श्री राम के बिना मेरे हृदय की बात कौन जान सकता है? मन में एक ही आँक (निश्चयपूर्वक) यही है कि प्रातः काल श्री रामजी के पास चल दूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2866.english_translation: I can see no other way. Who can understand the heart without Ram? My mind has made one firm resolve: at dawn, I will go to my Lord.
ramacharitamanas::2866.translation_literal: आन (other) / उपाउ (means) / मोहि (to me) / नहिं (not) / सूझा (seems) / को (who) / जिय (heart) / कै (of) / रघुबर (Ram) / बिनु (without) / बूझा (understands) / एकहिं (only one) / आँक (firm resolve) / इहइ (this) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / प्रातकाल (at dawn) / चलिहउँ (I will go) / प्रभु (Lord) / पाहीं (to)
ramacharitamanas::2866.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2866.essence: When the heart is clear, only return remains.
ramacharitamanas::2866.simple_meaning: Bharat feels there is no other solution except to go to Ram at dawn. Only Ram can truly understand what is in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::2866.simple_insight: When confusion ends, surrender begins. The heart stops bargaining and moves toward the one place it belongs.
ramacharitamanas::2866.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands in the pain of exile and separation, unable to find any worldly remedy. He knows only Ram can read his heart, and he fixes on one clear action: go to Ram at daybreak.
ramacharitamanas::2866.modern_relevance: You lie awake after a family argument, rehearsing explanations that never feel enough. Then the mind settles on one honest move: go face the person who matters, not the story in your head.
ramacharitamanas::2866.insight: It shifts you from mental circling to direct return. The right response is not more analysis, but movement toward what is sacred and true.

ramacharitamanas::2867.verse_sanskrit: जद्यपि मैं अनभल अपराधी। भै मोहि कारन सकल उपाधी॥ तदपि सरन सनमुख मोहि देखी। छमि सब करिहहिं कृपा बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2867.verse_hindi: यद्यपि मैं बुरा हूँ और अपराधी हूँ और मेरे ही कारण यह सब उपद्रव हुआ है, तथापि श्री रामजी मुझे शरण में सम्मुख आया हुआ देखकर सब अपराध क्षमा करके मुझ पर विशेष कृपा करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2867.english_translation: Though I am unworthy and guilty, and all this trouble came because of me, still, if Ram sees me come before him in surrender, he will forgive every fault and show me special grace.
ramacharitamanas::2867.translation_literal: जद्यपि (although) / मैं (I) / अनभल (unworthy, bad) / अपराधी (guilty) / भै (became) / मोहि (to me) / कारन (cause) / सकल (all) / उपाधी (troubles, afflictions)॥ / तदपि (still) / सरन (surrender, refuge) / सनमुख (face to face, before) / मोहि (me) / देखी (seeing) / छमि (forgiving) / सब (all) / करिहहिं (will do) / कृपा (grace) / बिसेषी (special)॥
ramacharitamanas::2867.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2867.essence: Surrender does what guilt cannot: it makes forgiveness possible.
ramacharitamanas::2867.simple_meaning: Even when you know you caused the pain, surrendering sincerely can meet forgiveness and special grace.
ramacharitamanas::2867.simple_insight: You do not have to hide your fault to be met with mercy.
ramacharitamanas::2867.detailed_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed by guilt in Ayodhya after Ram's exile. He believes he is the cause of all the suffering, yet he still trusts that Ram's heart will turn toward him if he comes in surrender.
ramacharitamanas::2867.modern_relevance: You rehearse an apology in the car before walking into the room where you hurt someone. The fear says hide. This verse says come honestly anyway.
ramacharitamanas::2867.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to humble return, trusting grace to meet honesty.

ramacharitamanas::2868.verse_sanskrit: सील सकुच सुठि सरल सुभाऊ। कृपा सनेह सदन रघुराऊ॥ अरिहुक अनभल कीन्ह न रामा। मैं सिसु सेवक जद्यपि बामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2868.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी शील, संकोच, अत्यन्त सरल स्वभाव, कृपा और स्नेह के घर हैं। श्री रामजी ने कभी शत्रु का भी अनिष्ट नहीं किया। मैं यद्यपि टेढ़ा हूँ, पर हूँ तो उनका बच्चा और सेवक ही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2868.english_translation: Raghunath is the home of virtue, modesty, simplicity, compassion, and love. Ram has never harmed even an enemy. Though I am crooked, I am still his child and servant.
ramacharitamanas::2868.translation_literal: सील (virtue) / सकुच (modesty) / सुठि (very) / सरल (simple) / सुभाऊ (nature) / कृपा (compassion) / सनेह (love) / सदन (abode) / रघुराऊ (Raghunath) ॥ / अरिहुक (even enemy) / अनभल (harm) / कीन्ह (did) / न (not) / रामा (Ram) ॥ / मैं (I) / सिसु (child) / सेवक (servant) / जद्यपि (although) / बामा (crooked) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2868.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2868.essence: Ram's love is large enough to hold your crookedness.
ramacharitamanas::2868.simple_meaning: Ram is naturally kind, gentle, and loving. He never harms even an enemy. The speaker calls himself crooked, yet still claims the place of a child and servant.
ramacharitamanas::2868.simple_insight: You do not have to be perfect to be held with love.
ramacharitamanas::2868.detailed_meaning: Bharat is speaking from exile-time grief, trying to explain why he can still approach Ram. He praises Ram's gentle nature and admits his own crookedness, yet trusts that childlike service still counts in Ram's eyes.
ramacharitamanas::2868.modern_relevance: You rehearse an apology in the car before walking back into a room where you know you messed up. This verse says your mistake is real, but your place in love is not gone.
ramacharitamanas::2868.insight: It shifts you from self-rejection to humble return: speak honestly, serve sincerely, and trust that devotion still reaches home.

ramacharitamanas::2869.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह पै पाँच मोर भल मानी। आयसु आसिष देहु सुबानी॥ जेहिं सुनि बिनय मोहि जनु जानी। आवहिं बहुरि रामु रजधानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2869.verse_hindi: आप पंच (सब) लोग भी इसी में मेरा कल्याण मानकर सुंदर वाणी से आज्ञा और आशीर्वाद दीजिए, जिसमें मेरी विनती सुनकर और मुझे अपना दास जानकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी राजधानी को लौट आवें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2869.english_translation: Please, all of you, see this as my good. Give me your blessing and kind words so that, hearing my plea and knowing me as your servant, Ram may return to the capital.
ramacharitamanas::2869.translation_literal: तुम्ह पै (from you all) / पाँच मोर (my five; all of you) / भल मानी (consider it good) / आयसु (permission, command) / आसिष (blessing) / देहु (give) / सुबानी (kind words)॥ / जेहिं (so that) / सुनि (hearing) / बिनय (humble plea) / मोहि (me) / जनु जानी (knowing as a servant) / आवहिं (may come back) / बहुरि (again) / रामु (Ram) / रजधानी (to the capital)॥
ramacharitamanas::2869.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2869.essence: Humility asks for blessing so the beloved may return.
ramacharitamanas::2869.simple_meaning: Bharat asks everyone to bless him and speak kindly so Ram will return to the capital. He treats this as the highest good, not his own gain.
ramacharitamanas::2869.simple_insight: Love becomes powerful when it asks for nothing for itself.
ramacharitamanas::2869.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat stands before elders and loved ones after Ram's exile. He is not asking for power or praise. He begs for blessings only so his humble devotion may help bring Ram back to the capital.
