ramacharitamanas::2869.modern_relevance: You call three relatives before making a hard family decision, not to defend yourself, but to ask for their blessing. You want the choice to serve what is right, not what flatters you.
ramacharitamanas::2869.insight: It shifts you from self-protection to humble service of a larger good.

ramacharitamanas::2870.verse_sanskrit: जद्यपि जनमु कुमातु तें मैं सठु सदा सदोस। आपन जानि न त्यागिहहिं मोहि रघुबीर भरोस ॥
ramacharitamanas::2870.verse_hindi: यद्यपि मेरा जन्म कुमाता से हुआ है और मैं दुष्ट तथा सदा दोषयुक्त भी हूँ, तो भी मुझे श्री रामजी का भरोसा है कि वे मुझे अपना जानकर त्यागेंगे नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2870.english_translation: Although I was born from a bad mother and am wicked and always full of faults, I still trust Raghubir will not abandon me, knowing me as his own.
ramacharitamanas::2870.translation_literal: जद्यपि (although) / जनमु (birth) / कुमातु तें (from a bad mother) / मैं (I) / सठु (wicked) / सदा (always) / सदोस (full of faults) / आपन (own) / जानि (knowing) / न त्यागिहहिं (will not abandon) / मोहि (me) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / भरोस (trust)
ramacharitamanas::2870.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2870.essence: Your flaws do not end Ram's claim on you.
ramacharitamanas::2870.simple_meaning: Bharat says he is full of flaws, yet he trusts that Ram will not reject him because Ram recognizes him as his own.
ramacharitamanas::2870.simple_insight: There is relief in being known and held even when you feel undeserving.
ramacharitamanas::2870.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is speaking with deep humility after Ram's exile has shattered the family. He calls himself flawed and unworthy, yet he trusts Ram's love will not turn away from him. That trust is the heart of his devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2870.modern_relevance: You replay your mistakes before sleep and assume they have made you unlovable. This verse answers that fear with a quieter truth: being flawed does not erase belonging.
ramacharitamanas::2870.insight: It shifts the mind from self-rejection to trust in being accepted despite imperfection.

ramacharitamanas::2871.verse_sanskrit: भरत बचन सब कहँ प्रिय लागे। राम सनेह सुधाँ जनु पागे॥ लोग बियोग बिषम बिष दागे। मंत्र सबीज सुनत जनु जागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2871.verse_hindi: भरतजी के वचन सबको प्यारे लगे। मानो वे श्री रामजी के प्रेमरूपी अमृत में पगे हुए थे। श्री रामवियोग रूपी भीषण विष से सब लोग जले हुए थे। वे मानो बीज सहित मंत्र को सुनते ही जाग उठे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2871.english_translation: Bharat's words were dear to everyone. They seemed soaked in the nectar of Ram's love. Everyone was scorched by the terrible poison of separation from Ram. Hearing those seed-filled words, they woke as if from sleep.
ramacharitamanas::2871.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / बचन (words) / सब कहँ (to everyone) / प्रिय (dear) / लागे (became) । / राम (Ram) / सनेह (love) / सुधाँ (nectar) / जनु (as if) / पागे (soaked) ॥ / लोग (people) / बियोग (separation) / बिषम (terrible) / बिष (poison) / दागे (scorched) । / मंत्र (mantra/words) / सबीज (with seed) / सुनत (hearing) / जनु (as if) / जागे (woke up) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2871.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2871.essence: Love-filled words can wake people from grief.
ramacharitamanas::2871.simple_meaning: Bharat's words comfort everyone because they are full of love for Ram. His speech reaches people who are already hurting from separation and helps them wake up from grief.
ramacharitamanas::2871.simple_insight: A loving voice can reach people even when grief has made them numb.
ramacharitamanas::2871.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is speaking to a room already burned by Ram's exile. His words carry such tenderness that everyone feels soothed at once. The verse shows how devotion can steady a whole community in shared grief.
ramacharitamanas::2871.modern_relevance: A family meeting after a painful loss can feel locked in silence until one person speaks with real tenderness. That kind of speech doesn't erase grief, but it lets everyone breathe again.
ramacharitamanas::2871.insight: It shows how compassionate speech can interrupt collective despair and restore attention.

ramacharitamanas::2872.verse_sanskrit: मातु सचिव गुर पुर नर नारी। सकल सनेहँ बिकल भए भारी॥ भरतहि कहहिं सराहि सराही। राम प्रेम मूरति तनु आही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2872.verse_hindi: माता, मंत्री, गुरु, नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष सभी स्नेह के कारण बहुत ही व्याकुल हो गए। सब भरतजी को सराह-सराहकर कहते हैं कि आपका शरीर श्री रामप्रेम की साक्षात मूर्ति ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2872.english_translation: The mother, ministers, teacher, and all the men and women of the city were overwhelmed with love. Everyone kept praising Bharata, saying, 'Your body is nothing but a living form of love for Rama.'
ramacharitamanas::2872.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / सचिव (minister) / गुर (teacher) / पुर (city) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / सकल (all) / सनेहँ (with love) / बिकल (disturbed) / भए (became) / भारी (greatly) ॥ / भरतहि (Bharata) / कहहिं (they say) / सराहि सराही (praising again and again) / राम (Rama) / प्रेम (love) / मूरति (form) / तनु (body) / आही (is)
ramacharitamanas::2872.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2872.essence: Love for Ram becomes so complete that it shows on the body itself.
ramacharitamanas::2872.simple_meaning: Everyone in Ayodhya is overwhelmed by love and grief, and they praise Bharata as a living embodiment of love for Rama.
ramacharitamanas::2872.simple_insight: Real devotion changes how people see you: they recognize love before they notice status.
ramacharitamanas::2872.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Ram’s exile, the whole city is shaken. Bharata’s humility has already moved everyone, and now the mother, ministers, teacher, and common people openly praise him. This verse is part of the swelling grief and reverence around his name.
ramacharitamanas::2872.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone refuses an unfair advantage and still speaks gently. People don’t call that weakness — they feel the depth of a heart that loves without bargaining.
ramacharitamanas::2872.insight: It shifts attention from outward role to inward devotion, showing that love can become a person’s visible identity.

ramacharitamanas::2873.verse_sanskrit: तात भरत अस काहे न कहहू। प्रान समान राम प्रिय अहहू॥ जो पावँरु अपनी जड़ताईं। तुम्हहि सुगाइ मातु कुटिलाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2873.verse_hindi: हे तात भरत! आप ऐसा क्यों न कहें। श्री रामजी को आप प्राणों के समान प्यारे हैं। जो नीच अपनी मूर्खता से आपकी माता कैकेयी की कुटिलता को लेकर आप पर सन्देह करेगा, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2873.english_translation: O dear Bharat, why would you not say this? Ram is dear to you as life itself. Anyone who, in their foolishness, doubts you because of your mother Kaikeyi's crookedness is vile.
ramacharitamanas::2873.translation_literal: तात (dear one) / भरत (Bharat) / अस (such) / काहे (why) / न (not) / कहहू (you say) / प्रान (life-breath) / समान (equal to) / राम (Ram) / प्रिय (dear) / अहहू (you are) / जो (who) / पावँरु (fool) / अपनी (own) / जड़ताईं (foolishness) / तुम्हहि (you) / सुगाइ (suspecting) / मातु (mother) / कुटिलाईं (crookedness) /
ramacharitamanas::2873.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2873.essence: True love for Ram cannot be hidden by public suspicion.
ramacharitamanas::2873.simple_meaning: Bharat's love for Ram is so obvious that no wise person should doubt him because of Kaikeyi's actions.
ramacharitamanas::2873.simple_insight: Real devotion does not need to prove itself to everyone.
ramacharitamanas::2873.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the people are defending Bharat from suspicion after Kaikeyi's role in Ram's exile. This verse insists that Bharat's love for Ram is pure and obvious, and that only a fool would blame him for his mother's wrongdoing.
ramacharitamanas::2873.modern_relevance: After a family scandal, people start whispering that you must be complicit too. This verse reminds you that your own love and integrity are not erased by someone else's choice.
ramacharitamanas::2873.insight: It separates your character from the actions of those around you, and asks others to judge you fairly.

ramacharitamanas::2874.verse_sanskrit: सो सठु कोटिक पुरुष समेता। बसिहि कलप सत नरक निकेता॥ अहि अघ अवगुन नहिं मनि गहई। हरइ गरल दुख दारिद दहई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2874.verse_hindi: वह दुष्ट करोड़ों पुरखों सहित सौ कल्पों तक नरक के घर में निवास करेगा। साँप के पाप और अवगुण को मणि नहीं ग्रहण करती, बल्कि वह विष को हर लेती है और दुःख तथा दरिद्रता को भस्म कर देती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2874.english_translation: That wicked one, along with millions of others, will dwell for hundreds of kalpas in the house of hell. A snake's poison and faults are not taken by a jewel; instead, it removes the poison and burns away suffering and poverty.
ramacharitamanas::2874.translation_literal: सो (that) / सठु (wicked one) / कोटिक (millions) / पुरुष (men, people) / समेता (together with) / बसिहि (will dwell) / कलप सत (hundreds of kalpas) / नरक निकेता (in the house of hell)॥ / अहि (snake) / अघ (sin) / अवगुन (faults) / नहिं (not) / मनि (by a jewel) / गहई (is taken) / हरइ (removes) / गरल (poison) / दुख (suffering) / दारिद (poverty) / दहई (burns, destroys)॥
ramacharitamanas::2874.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2874.essence: A pure person removes poison instead of carrying it.
ramacharitamanas::2874.simple_meaning: A truly wicked person falls into deep suffering, while a true jewel does the opposite of poison: it removes harm and destroys misery.
ramacharitamanas::2874.simple_insight: Character matters because it either spreads harm or absorbs it and turns it away.
ramacharitamanas::2874.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court and family are reeling from Bharat's grief and praise. This line uses a harsh contrast: the corrupt sink into suffering, but a jewel-like person does not take on poison — they remove it. The point supports the praise of Bharat's purity.
ramacharitamanas::2874.modern_relevance: A room full of gossip can make one person meaner, but another person calmly changes the whole atmosphere. Some people absorb poison; others quietly clear it.
ramacharitamanas::2874.insight: It shifts attention from outer status to inner effect: does your presence spread harm, or remove it?

ramacharitamanas::2875.verse_sanskrit: अवसि चलिअ बन रामु जहँ भरत मंत्रु भल कीन्ह। सोक सिंधु बूड़त सबहि तुम्ह अवलंबनु दीन्ह ॥
ramacharitamanas::2875.verse_hindi: हे भरतजी! वन को अवश्य चलिए, जहाँ श्री रामजी हैं, आपने बहुत अच्छी सलाह विचारी। शोक समुद्र में डूबते हुए सब लोगों को आपने (बड़ा) सहारा दे दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2875.english_translation: O Bharat, you should surely go to the forest where Ram is. You have made a wise decision, and you have given everyone a great support while they were sinking in an ocean of sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2875.translation_literal: अवसि (surely) / चलिअ (should go) / बन (to the forest) / रामु (Ram) / जहँ (where) / भरत (Bharat) / मंत्रु (counsel) / भल (good) / कीन्ह (made) / सोक (sorrow) / सिंधु (ocean) / बूड़त (sinking) / सबहि (everyone) / तुम्ह (you) / अवलंबनु (support) / दीन्ह (gave)
ramacharitamanas::2875.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2875.essence: Wise support can keep others afloat in grief.
ramacharitamanas::2875.simple_meaning: Bharat is praised for wisely choosing to go to Ram in the forest, and for giving grieving people real support.
ramacharitamanas::2875.simple_insight: A steady heart can hold up everyone else, even in the middle of grief.
ramacharitamanas::2875.detailed_meaning: After Ram’s exile, Bharat’s grief has spread through the whole family. The speaker praises Bharat’s wise decision to go to Ram in the forest, saying his clear counsel has kept everyone from sinking deeper into sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2875.modern_relevance: You are the one everyone texts when a family crisis hits, even though you are barely holding it together. Your calm choice can become the hand that keeps others from going under.
ramacharitamanas::2875.insight: It shifts the mind from private grief to responsible steadiness, showing how your judgment can become shelter for others.

ramacharitamanas::2876.verse_sanskrit: भा सब कें मन मोदु न थोरा। जनु घन धुनि सुनि चातक मोरा॥ चलत प्रात लखि निरनउ नीके। भरतु प्रानप्रिय भे सबही के ॥
ramacharitamanas::2876.verse_hindi: सबके मन में कम आनंद नहीं हुआ (अर्थात बहुत ही आनंद हुआ)! मानो मेघों की गर्जना सुनकर चातक और मोर आनंदित हो रहे हों। (दूसरे दिन) प्रातःकाल चलने का सुंदर निर्णय देखकर भरतजी सभी को प्राणप्रिय हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2876.english_translation: Everyone’s heart filled with joy, like a chatak and a peacock hearing thunder. At dawn, seeing his noble decision to depart, Bharat became dear as life to everyone.
ramacharitamanas::2876.translation_literal: भा (became) / सब कें (for everyone) / मन (mind) / मोदु (joy) / न (not) / थोरा (small) / जनु (as if) / घन (cloud) / धुनि (sound/thunder) / सुनि (having heard) / चातक (chatak bird) / मोरा (peacock) / चलत (going/moving) / प्रात (morning) / लखि (seeing) / निरनउ (decision) / नीके (noble/good) / भरतु (Bharat) / प्रानप्रिय (dear as life) / भे (became) / सबही (of everyone) / के (to)
ramacharitamanas::2876.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2876.essence: Selfless resolve makes you beloved without asking for praise.
ramacharitamanas::2876.simple_meaning: Everyone felt great joy when Bharat decided to leave at dawn. His choice made him beloved to all.
ramacharitamanas::2876.simple_insight: A clear, selfless decision can lift everyone around you.
ramacharitamanas::2876.detailed_meaning: After Bharat’s wise counsel, the household’s grief begins to loosen. At dawn, when he is ready to depart, the people see his resolve and feel relief and affection. His humility and steadiness make him dear to all.
ramacharitamanas::2876.modern_relevance: A tense family meeting ends, and someone finally says, “I’ll handle it.” The room changes at once. Clear, unselfish action can calm everyone faster than long explanations.
ramacharitamanas::2876.insight: It shows how decisive, humble action restores trust and softens collective sorrow.

ramacharitamanas::2877.verse_sanskrit: मुनिहि बंदि भरतहि सिरु नाई। चले सकल घर बिदा कराई॥ धन्य भरत जीवनु जग माहीं। सीलु सनेहु सराहत जाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2877.verse_hindi: मुनि वशिष्ठजी की वंदना करके और भरतजी को सिर नवाकर, सब लोग विदा लेकर अपने-अपने घर को चले। जगत में भरतजी का जीवन धन्य है, इस प्रकार कहते हुए वे उनके शील और स्नेह की सराहना करते जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2877.english_translation: After bowing to the sage and to Bharat, everyone took leave and returned home. In the world, Bharat's life is blessed, they said, praising his character and affection.
ramacharitamanas::2877.translation_literal: मुनिहि (to the sage) / बंदि (bowing) / भरतहि (to Bharat) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowed) / चले (went) / सकल (all) / घर (home) / बिदा (farewell) / कराई (having taken) / धन्य (blessed) / भरत (Bharat) / जीवनु (life) / जग (world) / माहीं (in) / सीलु (character) / सनेहु (affection) / सराहत (praising) / जाहीं (they went)
ramacharitamanas::2877.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2877.essence: Bharat's nobility makes departure feel like a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2877.simple_meaning: Everyone bows to the sage and to Bharat, then leaves. Bharat is praised as blessed in this world for his noble conduct and loving heart.
ramacharitamanas::2877.simple_insight: True greatness leaves people grateful, humble, and softened.
ramacharitamanas::2877.detailed_meaning: At Nandigram, the gathered people have just received Bharat's guidance and are preparing to return home. Before leaving, they bow to Vashishtha and to Bharat, honouring the holiness of the moment and the rare gentleness of Bharat's character.
ramacharitamanas::2877.modern_relevance: After a difficult family meeting, people stand up quietly, touch an elder's feet, and leave with less anger than they arrived. Some people change a room simply by how they carry themselves.
ramacharitamanas::2877.insight: It shows that real authority can inspire reverence without force, and that character can make even a farewell feel sacred.

ramacharitamanas::2878.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं परसपर भा बड़ काजू। सकल चलै कर साजहिं साजू॥ जेहि राखहिं रहु घर रखवारी। सो जानइ जनु गरदनि मारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2878.verse_hindi: आपस में कहते हैं, बड़ा काम हुआ। सभी चलने की तैयारी करने लगे। जिसको भी घर की रखवाली के लिए रहो, ऐसा कहकर रखते हैं, वही समझता है मानो मेरी गर्दन मारी गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2878.english_translation: They said to one another, "A great task has been done." Everyone began making preparations to leave. Whoever is told to stay and guard the house feels as if his throat has been cut.
ramacharitamanas::2878.translation_literal: कहहिं (they say) / परसपर (to one another) / भा (became) / बड़ (great) / काजू (task) / सकल (all) / चलै (to leave) / कर (for) / साजहिं (they prepare) / साजू (arrangements) / जेहि (whomever) / राखहिं (they keep) / रहु (stay) / घर (house) / रखवारी (guarding) / सो (that one) / जानइ (knows) / जनु (as if) / गरदनि (throat) / मारी (struck)
ramacharitamanas::2878.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2878.essence: The unseen duty feels like a wound to the one who must carry it.
ramacharitamanas::2878.simple_meaning: Everyone is eager to go, and nobody wants to be left behind to guard the house. Being assigned the staying role feels like a punishment.
ramacharitamanas::2878.simple_insight: It captures how people resist the role that asks for quiet sacrifice instead of visible reward.
ramacharitamanas::2878.detailed_meaning: After honoring Bharat, the people prepare to return home from the gathering in Ayodhya. The mood is joyful, but one practical problem remains: someone must stay behind to watch the house. The verse shows how even a small duty can feel unbearable when everyone wants the easier path.
ramacharitamanas::2878.modern_relevance: The group chat is full of excitement about the trip, but someone has to stay back and lock up. The volunteer role is invisible, yet the whole plan depends on it.
ramacharitamanas::2878.insight: It shifts attention from the glamorous task to the necessary one that keeps everything safe.

ramacharitamanas::2879.verse_sanskrit: कोउ कह रहन कहिअ नहिं काहू। को न चहइ जग जीवन लाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2879.verse_hindi: कोई-कोई कहते हैं- रहने के लिए किसी को भी मत कहो, जगत में जीवन का लाभ कौन नहीं चाहता? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2879.english_translation: Some say, 'Do not ask anyone to stay.' Who in the world does not want the gain of life?
ramacharitamanas::2879.translation_literal: कोउ (someone) / कह (says) / रहन (to stay) / कहिअ (say) / नहिं (not) / काहू (to anyone) / को (who) / न (not) / चहइ (wants) / जग (world) / जीवनु (life) / लाहू (gain)
ramacharitamanas::2879.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2879.essence: Everyone clings to life’s benefit, even while speaking of letting go.
ramacharitamanas::2879.simple_meaning: People may say no one should be asked to stay, because everyone wants the benefit of life. The line points to a shared human urge to keep living and keep what life offers.
ramacharitamanas::2879.simple_insight: It softens judgment by showing that everyone is driven by the wish to continue and preserve what matters.
ramacharitamanas::2879.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the household is preparing to disperse after a painful turning point. As people speak about who should remain and who should leave, the verse pauses on a plain human fact: every living person wants the benefit of being alive.
ramacharitamanas::2879.modern_relevance: At a family meeting where everyone is quietly trying to protect their own corner, the same motive is everywhere: nobody wants loss, and everyone wants to keep the good of their life intact.
ramacharitamanas::2879.insight: It shifts attention from blame to shared human desire, making the scene feel less personal and more universal.

ramacharitamanas::2880.verse_sanskrit: जरउ सो संपति सदन सुखु सुहृद मातु पितु भाइ। सनमुख होत जो राम पद करै न सहस सहाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2880.verse_hindi: वह सम्पत्ति, घर, सुख, मित्र, माता, पिता, भाई जल जाए जो श्री रामजी के चरणों के सम्मुख होने में हँसते हुए (प्रसन्नतापूर्वक) सहायता न करे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2880.english_translation: May that wealth, home, comfort, friend, mother, father, and brother burn away that does not gladly help when the feet of Ram are in sight.
ramacharitamanas::2880.translation_literal: जरउ (may burn) / सो (that) / संपति (wealth) / सदन (home) / सुखु (comfort) / सुहृद (friend) / मातु (mother) / पितु (father) / भाइ (brother) / सनमुख (face-to-face / in sight) / होत (being) / जो (which) / राम पद (Ram's feet) / करै (does) / न (not) / सहस सहाइ (gladly help)
ramacharitamanas::2880.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2880.essence: Anything that cannot help you face Ram is not worth keeping.
ramacharitamanas::2880.simple_meaning: Wealth, home, comfort, and even family are worthless if they do not joyfully support your movement toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2880.simple_insight: Love for Ram makes every other attachment smaller and clearer.
ramacharitamanas::2880.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the household is preparing for Bharat's return and the pull of duty and devotion is overwhelming everyone. Tulsidas declares that any wealth, home, comfort, or family bond is worthless if it does not gladly support turning toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2880.modern_relevance: You are packing for a move and suddenly see which friendships, habits, and comforts truly support your deepest commitments. Anything that quietly pulls you away may not deserve a place.
ramacharitamanas::2880.insight: It shifts loyalty from possession and comfort to what helps you face the divine.

ramacharitamanas::2881.verse_sanskrit: घर घर साजहिं बाहन नाना। हरषु हृदयँ परभात पयाना॥ भरत जाइ घर कीन्ह बिचारू। नगरु बाजि गज भवन भँडारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2881.verse_hindi: घर-घर लोग अनेकों प्रकार की सवारियाँ सजा रहे हैं। हृदय में (बड़ा) हर्ष है कि सबेरे चलना है। भरतजी ने घर जाकर विचार किया कि नगर घोड़े, हाथी, महल-खजाना आदि- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2881.english_translation: People in every house were preparing many kinds of vehicles. Their hearts were full of joy, because they would leave at dawn. Bharat went home and thought it over: the city, its horses, elephants, palaces, and stores of wealth...
ramacharitamanas::2881.translation_literal: घर घर (in every house) / साजहिं (they prepare) / बाहन (vehicles) / नाना (many kinds) / हरषु (joy) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / परभात (dawn) / पयाना (departure) / भरत (Bharat) / जाइ (going) / घर (home) / कीन्ह (made) / बिचारू (thought) / नगरु (city) / बाजि (horses) / गज (elephants) / भवन (palaces) / भँडारू (stores of wealth)
ramacharitamanas::2881.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2881.essence: Before leaving, Bharat first measures what he must not neglect.
ramacharitamanas::2881.simple_meaning: The city is getting ready to leave at dawn, and Bharat is taking stock of everything the kingdom contains.
ramacharitamanas::2881.simple_insight: Big decisions often begin with a quiet, honest inventory of what you are responsible for.
ramacharitamanas::2881.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, everyone is preparing for the journey at daybreak. Bharat returns home and looks over the city’s horses, elephants, palaces, and wealth. This is the moment before he decides how to protect everything in Ram’s absence.
ramacharitamanas::2881.modern_relevance: You stand in a half-packed house before moving day, checking what must stay safe, what must be carried, and what cannot be abandoned carelessly.
ramacharitamanas::2881.insight: It shifts attention from excitement about departure to responsibility for what remains behind.

ramacharitamanas::2882.verse_sanskrit: संपति सब रघुपति कै आही। जौं बिनु जतन चलौं तजि ताही॥ तौ परिनाम न मोरि भलाई। पाप सिरोमनि साइँ दोहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2882.verse_hindi: सारी सम्पत्ति श्री रघुनाथजी की है। यदि उसकी (रक्षा की) व्यवस्था किए बिना उसे ऐसे ही छोड़कर चल दूँ, तो परिणाम में मेरी भलाई नहीं है, क्योंकि स्वामी का द्रोह सब पापों में शिरोमणि (श्रेष्ठ) है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2882.english_translation: All wealth belongs to Raghupati. If I leave it behind without arranging for its care, there will be no good outcome for me, for betraying a master is the chief of all sins.
ramacharitamanas::2882.translation_literal: संपति (wealth) / सब (all) / रघुपति कै (of Raghupati) / आही (belongs) / जौं (if) / बिनु (without) / जतन (care/arrangement) / चलौं (I go) / तजि (leaving) / ताही (that) ॥ तौ (then) / परिनाम (result) / न (not) / मोरि (my) / भलाई (good) / पाप (wrong) / सिरोमनि (chief) / साइँ (master) / दोहाई (betrayal/call to witness) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2882.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2882.simple_meaning: Bharat sees Ram's property as Ram's alone, and he refuses to leave it unattended. For him, neglecting a master's trust is a serious moral failure.
ramacharitamanas::2882.simple_insight: Real loyalty shows up in what you protect, not just what you say.
ramacharitamanas::2882.detailed_meaning: Bharat is preparing to leave Ayodhya, but he stops to think like a true servant. Ram's wealth is not his to abandon carelessly. Before he moves, he makes sure nothing entrusted to Ram will be neglected.
ramacharitamanas::2882.modern_relevance: You hand over your apartment keys before a long trip and keep wondering whether the plants, bills, and mail were left in good hands. Bharat feels that same weight: trust is something you must actively protect.
ramacharitamanas::2882.insight: It shifts loyalty from sentiment to responsibility: if something has been entrusted to you, you must preserve it carefully.

ramacharitamanas::2883.verse_sanskrit: करइ स्वामि हित सेवकु सोई। दूषन कोटि देइ किन कोई॥ अस बिचारि सुचि सेवक बोले। जे सपनेहुँ निज धरम न डोले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2883.verse_hindi: सेवक वही है, जो स्वामी का हित करे, चाहे कोई करोड़ों दोष क्यों न दे। भरतजी ने ऐसा विचारकर ऐसे विश्वासपात्र सेवकों को बुलाया, जो कभी स्वप्न में भी अपने धर्म से नहीं डिगे थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2883.english_translation: The true servant acts for the master's good, even if millions of faults are laid upon him. Thinking this, Bharat called trustworthy servants who never wavered from their duty, even in a dream.
ramacharitamanas::2883.translation_literal: करइ (does) / स्वामि (master) / हित (good) / सेवकु (servant) / सोई (that only) / दूषन (faults) / कोटि (crores/millions) / देइ (gives) / किन (whether) / कोई (anyone) ॥ अस (thus) / बिचारि (thinking) / सुचि (pure/trustworthy) / सेवक (servants) / बोले (called/spoke) / जे (who) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / निज (own) / धरम (duty) / न (not) / डोले (waver) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2883.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2883.essence: Real service puts another's good above your own reputation.
ramacharitamanas::2883.simple_meaning: A real servant protects the master's good, no matter how much criticism comes. Bharat then chose only those helpers who would never drift from their duty.
ramacharitamanas::2883.simple_insight: You can stay loyal to what is right without needing approval.
ramacharitamanas::2883.detailed_meaning: Bharat is preparing to manage Ayodhya without claiming the throne. He needs servants he can trust, so he defines service clearly: a servant exists to protect the master's good, not personal reputation. This becomes his standard for appointment.
ramacharitamanas::2883.modern_relevance: You take the heat for a family decision, then still do the next right thing. The comments may sting, but the work still needs loyal hands.
ramacharitamanas::2883.insight: It shifts attention from protecting your image to protecting the task and the people depending on you.

ramacharitamanas::2884.verse_sanskrit: कहि सबु मरमु धरमु भल भाषा। जो जेहि लायक सो तेहिं राखा॥ करि सबु जतनु राखि रखवारे। राम मातु पहिं भरतु सिधारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2884.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने उनको सब भेद समझाकर फिर उत्तम धर्म बतलाया और जो जिस योग्य था, उसे उसी काम पर नियुक्त कर दिया। सब व्यवस्था करके, रक्षकों को रखकर भरतजी राम माता कौसल्याजी के पास गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2884.english_translation: Having explained everything clearly and spoken of righteous conduct in gentle words, he assigned each person to the task suited to them. After making all arrangements and posting guards, Bharata went to Queen Kausalya, Ram's mother.
ramacharitamanas::2884.translation_literal: कहि (having said) / सबु (all) / मरमु (the inner matter) / धरमु (righteous conduct) / भल (good) / भाषा (speech) / जो (who) / जेहि (to which) / लायक (fit) / सो (that one) / तेहिं (to that) / राखा (kept) / करि (having done) / सबु (all) / जतनु (careful effort) / राखि (having placed) / रखवारे (guards) / राम (Ram) / मातु (mother) / पहिं (to) / भरतु (Bharata) / सिधारे (went)
ramacharitamanas::2884.speaker: Bharata
ramacharitamanas::2884.essence: Care becomes real when it organizes people and protects what matters.
ramacharitamanas::2884.simple_meaning: Bharata explains the situation, gives everyone the right responsibility, sets guards in place, and then goes to Kausalya.
ramacharitamanas::2884.simple_insight: Real care is not just feeling deeply; it also means organizing, protecting, and placing people where they can help.
ramacharitamanas::2884.detailed_meaning: Bharata has taken charge of Ayodhya after Ram's exile. He speaks gently, assigns duties to the right people, and secures the palace with guards. Only after restoring order does he go to Ram's mother, Kausalya.
ramacharitamanas::2884.modern_relevance: A family crisis hits, and everyone is panicking in different directions. You stop, explain the situation clearly, give each person a role, and only then go to comfort the one who is grieving most.
ramacharitamanas::2884.insight: It teaches you to turn concern into structure: clear communication, proper roles, and steady protection before emotional reassurance.

ramacharitamanas::2885.verse_sanskrit: आरत जननी जानि सब भरत सनेह सुजान। कहेउ बनावन पालकीं सजन सुखासन जान ॥
ramacharitamanas::2885.verse_hindi: स्नेह के सुजान (प्रेम के तत्व को जानने वाले) भरतजी ने सब माताओं को आर्त (दुःखी) जानकर उनके लिए पालकियाँ तैयार करने तथा सुखासन यान (सुखपाल) सजाने के लिए कहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2885.english_translation: Knowing all the mothers were distressed, wise Bharata said, "Prepare palanquins and comfortable seats for them."
ramacharitamanas::2885.translation_literal: आरत (distressed) / जननी (mothers) / जानि (knowing) / सब (all) / भरत सनेह सुजान (Bharata, wise in love) / कहेउ (said) / बनावन (to prepare) / पालकीं (palanquins) / सजन (to arrange) / सुखासन (comfortable seats) / जान (vehicles)
ramacharitamanas::2885.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2885.essence: Love shows itself by making suffering easier to carry.
ramacharitamanas::2885.simple_meaning: Bharat sees that the mothers are in pain and immediately arranges a comfortable way for them to travel.
ramacharitamanas::2885.simple_insight: Real care notices pain quickly and turns into practical help.
ramacharitamanas::2885.detailed_meaning: After organizing the servants and assigning each person his role, Bharat turns to the grieving mothers in Ayodhya. He understands their distress and orders palanquins and comfortable seats to be prepared, so their journey can be managed with care.
ramacharitamanas::2885.modern_relevance: Your mother is exhausted after bad news, and you stop everything to arrange the ride, the chair, the water, the plan. Love becomes logistics.
ramacharitamanas::2885.insight: It shifts care from feeling sympathy to removing someone’s burden in concrete ways.

ramacharitamanas::2886.verse_sanskrit: चक्क चक्कि जिमि पुर नर नारी। चहत प्रात उर आरत भारी॥ जागत सब निसि भयउ बिहाना। भरत बोलाए सचिव सुजाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2886.verse_hindi: नगर के नर-नारी चकवे-चकवी की भाँति हृदय में अत्यन्त आर्त होकर प्रातःकाल का होना चाहते हैं। सारी रात जागते-जागते सबेरा हो गया। तब भरतजी ने चतुर मंत्रियों को बुलवाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2886.english_translation: Like chakwa and chakwi, the people of the city longed for morning with aching hearts. The whole night passed awake, and then Bharat called his wise ministers.
ramacharitamanas::2886.translation_literal: चक्क चक्कि (like chakwa and chakwi) / जिमि (as) / पुर (city) / नर नारी (men and women) / चहत (desire) / प्रात (morning) / उर (in the heart) / आरत भारी (great anguish) ॥ / जागत (staying awake) / सब (all) / निसि (night) / भयउ बिहाना (became morning) / भरत (Bharat) / बोलाए (called) / सचिव (ministers) / सुजाना (wise) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2886.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2886.essence: Restless hearts make even dawn feel like rescue.
ramacharitamanas::2886.simple_meaning: The city is filled with restless longing, and the night feels endless. When dawn finally comes, Bharat gathers his wise ministers.
ramacharitamanas::2886.simple_insight: Some waiting is so heavy that even morning feels like relief.
ramacharitamanas::2886.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyā, the people are sleepless with grief and longing after Ram's exile. Their hearts ache through the night like separated birds. As dawn breaks, Bharat, carrying the burden of the kingdom, calls his trusted ministers to act.
ramacharitamanas::2886.modern_relevance: You keep checking the clock at 4:17 a.m., unable to sleep before a hard conversation. The room is quiet, but your chest isn't. This verse knows that kind of night.
ramacharitamanas::2886.insight: It frames collective grief as a tense pause before the next act of duty.

ramacharitamanas::2887.verse_sanskrit: कहेउ लेहु सबु तिलक समाजू। बनहिं देब मुनि रामहि राजू॥ बेगि चलहु सुनि सचिव जोहारे। तुरत तुरग रथ नाग सँवारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2887.verse_hindi: और कहा- तिलक का सब सामान ले चलो। वन में ही मुनि वशिष्ठजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी को राज्य देंगे, जल्दी चलो। यह सुनकर मंत्रियों ने वंदना की और तुरंत घोड़े, रथ और हाथी सजवा दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2887.english_translation: Take all the tilak arrangements with you. In the forest, the sage Vasishtha will give Ram the kingdom. Hearing this, the ministers bowed, and at once had horses, chariots, and elephants prepared.
ramacharitamanas::2887.translation_literal: कहेउ (said) / लेहु (take) / सबु (all) / तिलक (coronation) / समाजू (arrangements) / बनहिं (in the forest) / देब (will give) / मुनि (sage) / रामहि (to Ram) / राजू (kingdom) / बेगि (quickly) / चलहु (go) / सुनि (hearing) / सचिव (ministers) / जोहारे (bowed) / तुरत (at once) / तुरग (horses) / रथ (chariots) / नाग (elephants) / सँवारे (made ready)
ramacharitamanas::2887.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2887.essence: Real loyalty prepares another person's honor before your own comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2887.simple_meaning: Bharat tells everyone to bring the coronation items and prepare to go quickly, because he believes Ram will be crowned in the forest. The ministers bow and ready the horses, chariots, and elephants.
ramacharitamanas::2887.simple_insight: When your heart is set on serving the right thing, even urgency becomes calm.
ramacharitamanas::2887.detailed_meaning: Bharat has taken charge of Ayodhya in Ram's absence, but he refuses the throne for himself. Here he orders the court to prepare the coronation materials, convinced that Ram alone should receive kingship, even if it must happen in exile.
ramacharitamanas::2887.modern_relevance: You are packing for a ceremony that should have happened in your own home, but you still arrange everything for someone else. That is the strange dignity Bharat lives with.
ramacharitamanas::2887.insight: It shifts attention from personal gain to rightful service, even when the setting is painful.

ramacharitamanas::2888.verse_sanskrit: अरुंधती अरु अगिनि समाऊ। रथ चढ़ि चले प्रथम मुनिराऊ॥ बिप्र बृंद चढ़ि बाहन नाना। चले सकल तप तेज निधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2888.verse_hindi: सबसे पहले मुनिराज वशिष्ठजी अरुंधती और अग्निहोत्र की सब सामग्री सहित रथ पर सवार होकर चले। फिर ब्राह्मणों के समूह, जो सब के सब तपस्या और तेज के भंडार थे, अनेकों सवारियों पर चढ़कर चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2888.english_translation: First, the sage Vashistha rode out in a chariot with Arundhati and the fire offerings. Then the Brahmins, all treasure-houses of austerity and radiance, set out on many mounts.
ramacharitamanas::2888.translation_literal: अरुंधती (Arundhati) / अरु (and) / अगिनि (fire) / समाऊ (with offerings) / रथ (chariot) / चढ़ि (riding) / चले (went) / प्रथम (first) / मुनिराऊ (the great sage) ॥ / बिप्र बृंद (group of Brahmins) / चढ़ि (riding) / बाहन (mounts) / नाना (various) / चले (went) / सकल (all) / तप (austerity) / तेज (radiance) / निधाना (treasure-houses) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2888.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2888.essence: The procession begins with reverence, not haste.
ramacharitamanas::2888.simple_meaning: Vashistha leads the procession, followed by Brahmins riding out in splendour. It is a ceremonial departure, not a teaching verse.
ramacharitamanas::2888.simple_insight: Some moments simply move the story forward, carrying the weight of everyone’s hope.
ramacharitamanas::2888.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the city is rushing toward Ram’s return and coronation in exile. Vashistha goes first, followed by Brahmins on many mounts, as the whole royal procession sets out for Chitrakoot. The verse mainly paints the scene.
ramacharitamanas::2888.modern_relevance: A wedding convoy pulls out before dawn, cars packed with flowers, elders, and ritual items. Everyone is in motion because something sacred is about to happen.
ramacharitamanas::2888.insight: It shifts attention from inner teaching to the communal movement of a sacred occasion.

ramacharitamanas::2889.verse_sanskrit: नगर लोग सब सजि सजि जाना। चित्रकूट कहँ कीन्ह पयाना॥ सिबिका सुभग न जाहिं बखानी। चढ़ि चढ़ि चलत भईं सब रानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2889.verse_hindi: नगर के सब लोग रथों को सजा-सजाकर चित्रकूट को चल पड़े। जिनका वर्णन नहीं हो सकता, ऐसी सुंदर पालकियों पर चढ़-चढ़कर सब रानियाँ चलीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2889.english_translation: All the people of the city, dressed and ready, set out for Chitrakoot. The queens climbed into beautiful palanquins beyond description and went along too.
ramacharitamanas::2889.translation_literal: नगर (city) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / सजि सजि (dressed and prepared) / जाना (went) / चित्रकूट (to Chitrakoot) / कहँ (toward) / कीन्ह (made) / पयाना (departure) ॥ / सिबिका (palanquins) / सुभग (beautiful) / न (not) / जाहिं (can be) / बखानी (described) / चढ़ि चढ़ि (having climbed up) / चलत (moving) / भईं (became) / सब (all) / रानी (queens) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2889.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2889.essence: Ayodhya itself turns toward Chitrakoot in shared grief.
ramacharitamanas::2889.simple_meaning: The whole city sets out for Chitrakoot, with the queens traveling in beautiful palanquins.
ramacharitamanas::2889.simple_insight: Some moments are so important that an entire city moves as one.
ramacharitamanas::2889.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is in motion behind Bharata's resolve. Citizens prepare themselves and leave for Chitrakoot, and the queens follow in splendid palanquins. This is not the point of the teaching; it is the visible gathering of a kingdom around Ram's exile.
ramacharitamanas::2889.modern_relevance: A family loads the car before dawn, not for a holiday but for a goodbye no one wants. Everyone moves together because the moment matters more than comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2889.insight: It shows the scale of the farewell and the public weight of Ram's exile.

ramacharitamanas::2890.verse_sanskrit: सौंपि नगर सुचि सेवकनि सादर सकल चलाइ। सुमिरि राम सिय चरन तब चले भरत दोउ भाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2890.verse_hindi: विश्वासपात्र सेवकों को नगर सौंपकर और सबको आदरपूर्वक रवाना करके, तब श्री सीता-रामजी के चरणों को स्मरण करके भरत-शत्रुघ्न दोनों भाई चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2890.english_translation: Entrusting the city to trustworthy servants and sending everyone off with respect, Bharat and Shatrughna then left, remembering the feet of Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::2890.translation_literal: सौंपि (entrusting) / नगर (the city) / सुचि (trustworthy, pure) / सेवकनि (servants) / सादर (with respect) / सकल (everyone) / चलाइ (sending off) / सुमिरि (remembering) / राम (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / चरन (feet) / तब (then) / चले (left) / भरत (Bharat) / दोउ (both) / भाइ (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::2890.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2890.essence: You serve best when you release ownership.
ramacharitamanas::2890.simple_meaning: Bharat leaves after handing the city over to trusted servants and respectfully sending everyone away, while keeping Ram and Sita in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::2890.simple_insight: True duty can be carried out with humility, not pride.
ramacharitamanas::2890.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat prepares to leave for Chitrakoot after arranging the city’s care. He does not storm out in anger or self-importance. He hands responsibility to trusted servants, bows inwardly to Ram and Sita, and walks away with Shatrughna.
ramacharitamanas::2890.modern_relevance: You lock the office, brief the team, and leave the keys with someone reliable before stepping into the night. Real responsibility is calm, respectful, and complete.
ramacharitamanas::2890.insight: It shifts duty from control to trust, showing how to leave something in good hands.

ramacharitamanas::2891.verse_sanskrit: राम दरस बस सब नर नारी। जनु करि करिनि चले तकि बारी॥ बन सिय रामु समुझि मन माहीं। सानुज भरत पयादेहिं जाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2891.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन के वश में हुए (दर्शन की अनन्य लालसा से) सब नर-नारी ऐसे चले मानो प्यासे हाथी-हथिनी जल को तककर (बड़ी तेजी से बावले से हुए) जा रहे हों। श्री सीताजी-रामजी (सब सुखों को छोड़कर) वन में हैं, मन में ऐसा विचार करके छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्नजी सहित भरतजी पैदल ही चले जा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2891.english_translation: All men and women were seized by the sight of Ram, rushing forward like thirsty elephants and cows toward water. Thinking in their minds, “Sita and Ram are in the forest,” Bharat and Shatrughna walked on foot.
ramacharitamanas::2891.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / दरस (sight) / बस (under the control) / सब (all) / नर नारी (men and women) / जनु (as if) / करि करिनि (male elephant and female elephant) / चले (went) / तकि (seeking) / बारी (water)॥ / बन (forest) / सिय रामु (Sita and Ram) / समुझि (remembering/understanding) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / सानुज (with younger brother) / भरत (Bharat) / पयादेहिं (on foot) / जाहीं (were going) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2891.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2891.essence: Longing for Ram makes comfort feel irrelevant.
ramacharitamanas::2891.simple_meaning: Everyone is drawn toward Ram with intense longing, and Bharat walks on foot, keeping Sita and Ram in mind.
ramacharitamanas::2891.simple_insight: Love can make a whole crowd move as one, and it can make power look unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::2891.detailed_meaning: The people of Ayodhya are following Bharat toward Chitrakूट, overwhelmed by longing for Ram. Even the royal procession feels too slow. Bharat, remembering that Sita and Ram live in the forest, chooses to walk with Shatrughna instead of riding in comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2891.modern_relevance: You see a loved one after months apart, and the whole room starts moving faster without anyone saying why. That pull is what this verse captures.
ramacharitamanas::2891.insight: It shifts attention from status and comfort to the force of sincere longing.

ramacharitamanas::2892.verse_sanskrit: देखि सनेहु लोग अनुरागे। उतरि चले हय गय रथ त्यागे॥ जाइ समीप राखि निज डोली। राम मातु मृदु बानी बोली ॥
ramacharitamanas::2892.verse_hindi: उनका स्नेह देखकर लोग प्रेम में मग्न हो गए और सब घोड़े, हाथी, रथों को छोड़कर उनसे उतरकर पैदल चलने लगे। तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी की माता कौसल्याजी भरत के पास जाकर और अपनी पालकी उनके समीप खड़ी करके कोमल वाणी से बोलीं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2892.english_translation: Seeing their affection, the people were filled with love and got down from horses, elephants, and chariots to walk on foot. Then Kaushalya, Ram's mother, came near Bharat, placed her palanquin beside him, and spoke softly.
ramacharitamanas::2892.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / सनेहु (affection) / लोग (people) / अनुरागे (became loving) / उतरि (getting down) / चले (went) / हय (horses) / गय (elephants) / रथ (chariots) / त्यागे (having left) / जाइ (going) / समीप (near) / राखि (placing) / निज (own) / डोली (palanquin) / राम (Ram) / मातु (mother) / मृदु (soft) / बानी (speech) / बोली (spoke)
ramacharitamanas::2892.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2892.essence: True affection makes even a crowd move gently.
ramacharitamanas::2892.simple_meaning: Bharat's presence moves everyone to tenderness. People abandon their vehicles and walk beside him, and Kaushalya approaches him gently to speak.
ramacharitamanas::2892.simple_insight: Real reverence changes how people move, not just what they say.
ramacharitamanas::2892.detailed_meaning: Bharat and Shatrughna are travelling back toward Ayodhya after the long exile begins. The crowd around them is so moved by Bharat's affection and humility that they leave their vehicles and walk. Kaushalya then comes close to speak with him.
ramacharitamanas::2892.modern_relevance: You enter a room after a painful family decision, and the whole atmosphere changes. People lower their voices, stand up, and move more carefully because your presence has made tenderness necessary.
ramacharitamanas::2892.insight: It shows how sincere love can soften an entire crowd and shift the social mood without force.

ramacharitamanas::2893.verse_sanskrit: तात चढ़हु रथ बलि महतारी। होइहि प्रिय परिवारु दुखारी॥ तुम्हरें चलत चलिहि सबु लोगू। सकल सोक कृस नहिं मग जोगू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2893.verse_hindi: हे बेटा! माता बलैया लेती है, तुम रथ पर चढ़ जाओ। नहीं तो सारा परिवार दुःखी हो जाएगा। तुम्हारे पैदल चलने से सभी लोग पैदल चलेंगे। शोक के मारे सब दुबले हो रहे हैं, पैदल रास्ते के (पैदल चलने के) योग्य नहीं हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2893.english_translation: “My dear, mount the chariot. Your mother blesses you. Otherwise, the whole family will remain sorrowful. If you walk, everyone will walk with you. Everyone is already worn thin with grief and not fit for the road on foot.”
ramacharitamanas::2893.translation_literal: तात (my dear) / चढ़हु (mount) / रथ (chariot) / बलि (blessing) / महतारी (mother) / होइहि (will become) / प्रिय (dear) / परिवारु (family) / दुखारी (sorrowful) ॥ / तुम्हरें (because of you) / चलत (walking) / चलिहि (will walk) / सबु (all) / लोगू (people) / सकल (entire) / सोक (grief) / कृस (thin/emaciated) / नहिं (not) / मग (road) / जोगू (fit) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2893.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::2893.essence: Love sometimes means choosing the easier road for everyone else.
ramacharitamanas::2893.simple_meaning: The speaker asks the brothers to ride in the chariot so the grieving family does not have to follow on foot and suffer more.
ramacharitamanas::2893.simple_insight: Sometimes love means easing the burden others are already carrying.
ramacharitamanas::2893.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the people are following Ram and Lakshman in overwhelming grief. Ram gently asks the brothers to take the chariot so the family will not be forced to walk in their sorrow. The moment shows compassion for others' exhaustion.
ramacharitamanas::2893.modern_relevance: You see a loved one already exhausted, yet you keep asking them to keep pace with you. This verse reminds you to notice when your own choice is making everyone else suffer more.
ramacharitamanas::2893.insight: It shifts attention from personal preference to the strain your choice places on others.

ramacharitamanas::2894.verse_sanskrit: सिर धरि बचन चरन सिरु नाई। रथ चढ़ि चलत भए दोउ भाई॥ तमसा प्रथम दिवस करि बासू। दूसर गोमति तीर निवासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2894.verse_hindi: माता की आज्ञा को सिर चढ़ाकर और उनके चरणों में सिर नवाकर दोनों भाई रथ पर चढ़कर चलने लगे। पहले दिन तमसा पर वास (मुकाम) करके दूसरा मुकाम गोमती के तीर पर किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2894.english_translation: Bowing their heads to their mother's command and touching their heads to her feet, the two brothers set out in a chariot. They spent the first day at the Tamasa River and the second on the bank of the Gomati.
ramacharitamanas::2894.translation_literal: सिर (head) / धरि (placing) / बचन (word/command) / चरन (feet) / सिरु (head) / नाई (bowing) / रथ (chariot) / चढ़ि (mounting) / चलत (moving) / भए (became) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) ॥ तमसा (Tamasa) / प्रथम (first) / दिवस (day) / करि (doing) / बासू (stay) / दूसर (second) / गोमति (Gomati) / तीर (bank) / निवासू (stay) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2894.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2894.essence: Respect is proven by the way you move after you bow.
ramacharitamanas::2894.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana obey their mother, bow to her feet, and begin their journey, stopping first at Tamasa and then at the Gomati bank.
ramacharitamanas::2894.simple_insight: Love becomes visible in obedient action, not just in feeling.
ramacharitamanas::2894.detailed_meaning: After the painful farewell, Rama and Lakshmana leave Ayodhya exactly as their mother’s word requires. They honour her command with reverence, then begin the exile journey, resting first by the Tamasa and then by the Gomati.
ramacharitamanas::2894.modern_relevance: You finally make the hard call your family asked for, even though it costs you. The respect is not in the speech you gave, but in the steps you took.
ramacharitamanas::2894.insight: It shifts attention from emotional talk to embodied obedience and respectful follow-through.

ramacharitamanas::2895.verse_sanskrit: पय अहार फल असन एक निसि भोजन एक लोग। करत राम हित नेम ब्रत परिहरि भूषन भोग ॥
ramacharitamanas::2895.verse_hindi: कोई दूध ही पीते, कोई फलाहार करते और कुछ लोग रात को एक ही बार भोजन करते हैं। भूषण और भोग-विलास को छोड़कर सब लोग श्री रामचन्द्रजी के लिए नियम और व्रत करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2895.english_translation: Some live on milk, some on fruit, some eat only once at night. Giving up ornaments and pleasures, they all keep vows and disciplines for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2895.translation_literal: पय (milk) / अहार (food) / फल (fruit) / असन (eating) / एक (one) / निसि (night) / भोजन (meal) / एक (one) / लोग (people) / करत (doing) / राम हित (for Ram's sake) / नेम (rules) / ब्रत (vows) / परिहरि (giving up) / भूषन (ornaments) / भोग (pleasures, luxuries)
ramacharitamanas::2895.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2895.essence: Love for Ram shows itself as disciplined simplicity.
ramacharitamanas::2895.simple_meaning: People are changing their eating habits, clothes, and comforts to keep vows for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2895.simple_insight: Love can reorganize your habits without making you miserable.
ramacharitamanas::2895.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have set out on exile, and the people of Ayodhya are following behind in grief and love. In that atmosphere, many give up comfort, simplify their lives, and keep vows for Ram as if their own bodies should share his hardship.
ramacharitamanas::2895.modern_relevance: You skip the dessert, turn off the music, and keep your promise anyway because someone you love is counting on you. That quiet discipline is a form of devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2895.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone into concrete habits, restraint, and self-discipline.

ramacharitamanas::2896.verse_sanskrit: सई तीर बसि चले बिहाने। सृंगबेरपुर सब निअराने॥ समाचार सब सुने निषादा। हृदयँ बिचार करइ सबिषादा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2896.verse_hindi: रात भर सई नदी के तीर पर निवास करके सबेरे वहाँ से चल दिए और सब श्रृंगवेरपुर के समीप जा पहुँचे। निषादराज ने सब समाचार सुने, तो वह दुःखी होकर हृदय में विचार करने लगा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2896.english_translation: After staying by the Sayi river through the night, they set out at dawn and came near Shrngverpur. Nishadraj heard all the news and, sorrowful, began to think deeply in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::2896.translation_literal: सई तीर (by the Sayi riverbank) / बसि (having stayed) / चले (they set out) / बिहाने (in the morning) / सृंगबेरपुर (Shrngverpur) / सब (all) / निअराने (came near) / समाचार (news) / सब (all) / सुने (heard) / निषादा (Nishadraj) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचार (thought) / करइ (does) / सबिषादा (with sorrow)
ramacharitamanas::2896.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2896.essence: News arrives first; the heart reacts before the mind knows why.
ramacharitamanas::2896.simple_meaning: After spending the night by the river, the party moved on at dawn and reached near Shrngverpur. Nishadraj heard the news and began worrying in sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2896.simple_insight: A sudden change in events can stir fear before the facts are clear.
ramacharitamanas::2896.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita have already left Ayodhya and are moving through the forest. After resting by the Sayi river, they approach Shrngverpur. Nishadraj hears of their arrival and, uneasy, starts turning the situation over in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::2896.modern_relevance: You hear a rumor before sunrise that someone important is coming to your town, and your stomach tightens before you know why. That is Nishadraj's moment.
ramacharitamanas::2896.insight: It shows how uncertainty can trigger sorrowful speculation before understanding arrives.

ramacharitamanas::2897.verse_sanskrit: कारन कवन भरतु बन जाहीं। है कछु कपट भाउ मन माहीं॥ जौं पै जियँ न होति कुटिलाई। तौ कत लीन्ह संग कटकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2897.verse_hindi: क्या कारण है जो भरत वन को जा रहे हैं, मन में कुछ कपट भाव अवश्य है। यदि मन में कुटिलता न होती, तो साथ में सेना क्यों ले चले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2897.english_translation: What reason could Bharat have for going to the forest? There must be some deceit in his heart. If there were no crookedness in him, why would he have brought an army along?
ramacharitamanas::2897.translation_literal: कारन (reason) / कवन (what) / भरतु (Bharat) / बन (to the forest) / जाहीं (is going) / है (there is) / कछु (some) / कपट (deceit) / भाउ (feeling) / मन (in the mind) / माहीं (within) ॥ / जौं (if) / पै (indeed) / जियँ (in the heart) / न (not) / होति (there were) / कुटिलाई (crookedness) / तौ (then) / कत (why) / लीन्ह (taken) / संग (with) / कटकाई (an army) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2897.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2897.essence: A suspicious mind sees deceit even in ordinary movement.
ramacharitamanas::2897.simple_meaning: The speaker suspects Bharat's intentions because he is traveling to the forest with an army. A pure-hearted person would not need such a display.
ramacharitamanas::2897.simple_insight: Suspicion reveals more about the watcher’s mind than the person being watched.
ramacharitamanas::2897.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, people are trying to understand Bharat's sudden movement toward the forest. Seeing him travel with troops, the narrator voices doubt: if Bharat were innocent, why bring an army? The verse exposes how fear reads hidden motives into outward signs.
ramacharitamanas::2897.modern_relevance: You see someone arrive with two lawyers and a folder of printouts, and your mind fills in the worst. The verse shows how quickly suspicion turns gesture into proof.
ramacharitamanas::2897.insight: It shifts you from reacting to appearances toward examining the assumptions behind your judgment.

ramacharitamanas::2898.verse_sanskrit: जानहिं सानुज रामहि मारी। करउँ अकंटक राजु सुखारी॥ भरत न राजनीति उर आनी। तब कलंकु अब जीवन हानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2898.verse_hindi: समझते हैं कि छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण सहित श्री राम को मारकर सुख से निष्कण्टक राज्य करूँगा। भरत ने हृदय में राजनीति को स्थान नहीं दिया (राजनीति का विचार नहीं किया)। तब (पहले) तो कलंक ही लगा था, अब तो जीवन से ही हाथ धोना पड़ेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2898.english_translation: They think Bharat wants to kill Ram and Lakshman to rule an unchallenged kingdom in comfort. Bharat never let such politics enter his heart; first that was a stain, and now it would cost him his life.
ramacharitamanas::2898.translation_literal: जानहिं (they think/know) / सानुज (with the younger brother) / रामहि (Ram) / मारी (killing) / करउँ (I will do) / अकंटक (without obstacles) / राजु (kingdom/rule) / सुखारी (comfortably) ॥ भरत (Bharat) / न (not) / राजनीति (statecraft/politics) / उर (in the heart) / आनी (brought) । तब (then) / कलंकु (stain) / अब (now) / जीवन (life) / हानी (loss) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2898.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2898.essence: Pure motives can still be crushed by suspicion.
ramacharitamanas::2898.simple_meaning: People suspect Bharat of wanting to kill Ram and Lakshman so he can rule without opposition. But Bharat never had such a thought; even the suspicion itself is a stain, and now it could ruin his life.
ramacharitamanas::2898.simple_insight: Sometimes innocence suffers most from being misunderstood.
ramacharitamanas::2898.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat's return is being judged through suspicion. Some fear he wants power, but his heart holds no such scheme. The verse shows how quickly a pure act can be mistaken for ambition, deepening the crisis around Ram's exile.
ramacharitamanas::2898.modern_relevance: You volunteer to help, and someone still assumes you have an angle. The hurt is not just the accusation — it's that your good motive never even got a hearing.
ramacharitamanas::2898.insight: It shifts the mind from judging by appearances to seeing how easily noble action gets misread.

ramacharitamanas::2899.verse_sanskrit: सकल सुरासुर जुरहिं जुझारा। रामहि समर न जीतनिहारा॥ का आचरजु भरतु अस करहीं। नहिं बिष बेलि अमिअ फल फरहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2899.verse_hindi: सम्पूर्ण देवता और दैत्य वीर जुट जाएँ, तो भी श्री रामजी को रण में जीतने वाला कोई नहीं है। भरत जो ऐसा कर रहे हैं, इसमें आश्चर्य ही क्या है? विष की बेलें अमृतफल कभी नहीं फलतीं! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2899.english_translation: Even if all radiant beings and shadow beings came together as warriors, none could defeat Ram in battle. Why be surprised that Bharat acts this way? A vine of poison never bears the fruit of nectar.
ramacharitamanas::2899.translation_literal: सकल (all) / सुरासुर (radiant beings and shadow beings) / जुरहिं (come together) / जुझारा (warriors) / रामहि (Ram) / समर (battle) / न (not) / जीतनिहारा (one who can defeat) ॥ / का (what) / आचरजु (surprise) / भरतु (Bharat) / अस (thus) / करहीं (does) ॥ / नहिं (not) / बिष (poison) / बेलि (vine) / अमिअ (nectar) / फल (fruit) / फरहीं (bear) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2899.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2899.essence: What you are rooted in will eventually show itself.
ramacharitamanas::2899.simple_meaning: No army can defeat Ram, so Bharat's noble conduct should not surprise anyone. Poisonous roots do not produce sweet fruit.
ramacharitamanas::2899.simple_insight: Character reveals character: what is rooted in darkness cannot suddenly bear purity.
ramacharitamanas::2899.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, suspicion still hangs over Bharat as people try to understand his motives. The narrator cuts through doubt with a sharp truth: Ram is unconquerable, and Bharat's conduct is no accident. A poisoned root cannot produce sweet fruit.
ramacharitamanas::2899.modern_relevance: When a family member keeps doubting your intentions, you can feel the sting of being misread. This verse reminds you that actions grow from character, not performance.
ramacharitamanas::2899.insight: It shifts attention from surface appearances to the moral source underneath them.

ramacharitamanas::2900.verse_sanskrit: अस बिचारि गुहँ ग्याति सन कहेउ सजग सब होहु। हथवाँसहु बोरहु तरनि कीजिअ घाटारोहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2900.verse_hindi: ऐसा विचारकर गुह (निषादराज) ने अपनी जाति वालों से कहा कि सब लोग सावधान हो जाओ। नावों को हाथ में (कब्जे में) कर लो और फिर उन्हें डुबा दो तथा सब घाटों को रोक दो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2900.english_translation: Thinking this, Guha told his companions to stay alert: seize the boats, sink them, and block every crossing place.
ramacharitamanas::2900.translation_literal: अस (thus) / बिचारि (having thought) / गुहँ (Guha) / ग्याति सन (to his companions) / कहेउ (said) / सजग (alert) / सब (all) / होहु (be) / हथवाँसहु (seize) / बोरहु (sink) / तरनि (boats) / कीजिअ (make) / घाटारोहु (block the crossings)
ramacharitamanas::2900.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2900.essence: Care can look like caution before trust is proven.
ramacharitamanas::2900.simple_meaning: Guha orders his people to stay alert, take control of the boats, sink them, and block the river crossings.
ramacharitamanas::2900.simple_insight: When danger feels near, people move fast to protect what they love.
ramacharitamanas::2900.detailed_meaning: At the riverbank, Guha sees the situation clearly: Bharata is approaching, and no one knows his intent yet. He tells his companions to guard the boats and block the crossings, preparing for possible conflict rather than trusting blindly.
ramacharitamanas::2900.modern_relevance: A security guard notices a crowd gathering near a closed gate and quietly locks the side entrances before anyone can rush in.
ramacharitamanas::2900.insight: It shows how vigilance works before certainty arrives: protect the vulnerable first, then sort out intentions.

ramacharitamanas::2901.verse_sanskrit: होहु सँजोइल रोकहु घाटा। ठाटहु सकल मरै के ठाटा॥ सनमुख लोह भरत सन लेऊँ। जिअत न सुरसरि उतरन देऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2901.verse_hindi: सुसज्जित होकर घाटों को रोक लो और सब लोग मरने के साज सजा लो (अर्थात भरत से युद्ध में लड़कर मरने के लिए तैयार हो जाओ)। मैं भरत से सामने (मैदान में) लोहा लूँगा (मुठभेड़ करूँगा) और जीते जी उन्हें गंगा पार न उतरने दूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2901.english_translation: Get ready, block the crossings, and prepare yourselves for death. I will face Bharat head-on and never let him cross the Ganga alive.
ramacharitamanas::2901.translation_literal: होहु (be) / सँजोइल (prepared, arranged) / रोकहु (block) / घाटा (the crossings, fords) / ठाटहु (set up, arrange) / सकल (all) / मरै (for death) / के (of) / ठाटा (array, preparations) / सनमुख (face-to-face) / लोह (fight, clash) / भरत (Bharat) / सन (with) / लेऊँ (I will take, engage) / जिअत (alive) / न (not) / सुरसरि (Ganga, the heavenly river) / उतरन (to cross) / देऊँ (I will allow)
ramacharitamanas::2901.speaker: Guha
ramacharitamanas::2901.essence: Protecting what you love can make you ready for battle before you know the truth.
ramacharitamanas::2901.simple_meaning: Guha orders his people to block the river crossings and be ready to fight Bharat if needed. He is determined not to let Bharat cross alive.
ramacharitamanas::2901.simple_insight: When loyalty feels threatened, even a gentle heart can turn fiercely protective.
ramacharitamanas::2901.detailed_meaning: At the Ganga crossing in Ayodhya's exile, Guha sees Bharat approaching with a large retinue and fears danger for Ram's cause. He rallies his people to defend the riverbank, ready to confront Bharat before letting him cross.
ramacharitamanas::2901.modern_relevance: You see a rival team arrive with cameras and lawyers, and your whole crew stiffens. In one second, caution becomes a wall.
ramacharitamanas::2901.insight: It shows how fear and loyalty can push a person into defensive action before understanding the full situation.

ramacharitamanas::2902.verse_sanskrit: समर मरनु पुनि सुरसरि तीरा। राम काजु छनभंगु सरीरा॥ भरत भाइ नृपु मैं जन नीचू। बड़ें भाग असि पाइअ मीचू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2902.verse_hindi: युद्ध में मरण, फिर गंगाजी का तट, श्री रामजी का काम और क्षणभंगुर शरीर (जो चाहे जब नाश हो जाए), भरत श्री रामजी के भाई और राजा (उनके हाथ से मरना) और मैं नीच सेवक- बड़े भाग्य से ऐसी मृत्यु मिलती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2902.english_translation: Death in battle, then the bank of the Ganga, and Ram's work—this body is gone in a moment. Bharat is the king, and I am only a low servant; how blessed to receive such a death.
ramacharitamanas::2902.translation_literal: समर (battle) / मरनु (death) / पुनि (then) / सुरसरि (the Ganga) / तीरा (bank) / राम (Ram) / काजु (work) / छनभंगु (broken in a moment) / सरीरा (body) / भरत (Bharat) / भाइ (brother) / नृपु (king) / मैं (I) / जन (servant) / नीचू (lowly) / बड़ें (great) / भाग (fortune) / असि (such) / पाइअ (is received) / मीचू (death)
ramacharitamanas::2902.speaker: Guh
ramacharitamanas::2902.essence: A brief life becomes blessed when it is spent for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2902.simple_meaning: Guh says he would gladly die fighting for Ram's work, especially with Bharat nearby. He sees the body as temporary and feels honored to die in such a cause.
ramacharitamanas::2902.simple_insight: Service becomes fearless when you value the work more than your own safety.
ramacharitamanas::2902.detailed_meaning: Guh stands at the riverbank facing Bharat's party. He is ready to fight and die for Ram's cause, and he sees that even a brief life is worthwhile if it ends in loyal service. His humility turns danger into honor.
ramacharitamanas::2902.modern_relevance: You step in to protect a friend at midnight, knowing you may get blamed. Something in you still says yes. That is the spirit here: service matters more than comfort or self-preservation.
ramacharitamanas::2902.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to wholehearted loyalty in action.

ramacharitamanas::2903.verse_sanskrit: स्वामि काज करिहउँ रन रारी। जस धवलिहउँ भुवन दस चारी॥ तजउँ प्रान रघुनाथ निहोरें। दुहूँ हाथ मुद मोदक मोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2903.verse_hindi: मैं स्वामी के काम के लिए रण में लड़ाई करूँगा और चौदहों लोकों को अपने यश से उज्ज्वल कर दूँगा। श्री रघुनाथजी के निमित्त प्राण त्याग दूँगा। मेरे तो दोनों ही हाथों में आनंद के लड्डू हैं (अर्थात जीत गया तो राम सेवक का यश प्राप्त करूँगा और मारा गया तो श्री रामजी की नित्य सेवा प्राप्त करूँगा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2903.english_translation: I will fight in battle for my master’s work and brighten the fourteen worlds with my fame. I will give up my life for Raghunath’s sake. For me, both hands already hold sweet reward.
ramacharitamanas::2903.translation_literal: स्वामि (master's) / काज (work) / करिहउँ (I will do) / रन (battle) / रारी (fighting) / जस (fame) / धवलिहउँ (I will make bright) / भुवन (worlds) / दस चारी (fourteen) / तजउँ (I give up) / प्रान (life-breath) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / निहोरें (for the sake of) / दुहूँ (both) / हाथ (hands) / मुद (joy) / मोदक (sweet reward) / मोरें (mine)
ramacharitamanas::2903.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2903.essence: When your work is for Ram, both victory and death become gain.
ramacharitamanas::2903.simple_meaning: Bharat says he will fight for Ram's work, even if it costs his life. Whether he wins or dies, he sees only gain in serving Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2903.simple_insight: When service is pure, fear of loss drops away.
ramacharitamanas::2903.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before the crisis of exile and divided loyalty. He is ready to fight for Ram's cause, even to die for it, because serving Ram already feels like victory. That is why he can call both outcomes sweet.
ramacharitamanas::2903.modern_relevance: You take the harder shift, fix the mess, and no one may notice. Still, you know the work mattered because it was for something you love.
ramacharitamanas::2903.insight: It shifts effort from self-protection to wholehearted service, so success and sacrifice both feel meaningful.

ramacharitamanas::2904.verse_sanskrit: साधु समाज न जाकर लेखा। राम भगत महुँ जासु न रेखा॥ जायँ जिअत जग सो महि भारू। जननी जौबन बिटप कुठारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2904.verse_hindi: साधुओं के समाज में जिसकी गिनती नहीं और श्री रामजी के भक्तों में जिसका स्थान नहीं, वह जगत में पृथ्वी का भार होकर व्यर्थ ही जीता है। वह माता के यौवन रूपी वृक्ष के काटने के लिए कुल्हाड़ा मात्र है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2904.english_translation: One who has no place among the company of saints and no place among Ram's devotees lives in the world as a burden on the earth. Such a person is only an axe for cutting down the mother's tree of youth.
ramacharitamanas::2904.translation_literal: साधु (saints) / समाज (company) / न (not) / जाकर (going) / लेखा (count, place) / राम (Ram) / भगत (devotees) / महुँ (among) / जासु (whose) / न (not) / रेखा (line, place) / जायँ (going) / जिअत (living) / जग (world) / सो (that) / महि (earth) / भारू (burden) / जननी (mother) / जौबन (youth) / बिटप (tree) / कुठारू (axe)
ramacharitamanas::2904.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2904.essence: A life outside devotion becomes a burden, not a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2904.simple_meaning: A life that never joins the company of saints or Ram's devotees is called wasted. It does not uplift anyone; it only consumes what it was given.
ramacharitamanas::2904.simple_insight: Belonging matters. A life rooted in devotion stops feeling empty and starts becoming useful.
ramacharitamanas::2904.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the mood has turned from grief to fierce loyalty. Bharat measures a life by one standard: whether it stands with the saints and with Ram's devotees. Without that, even living becomes a kind of waste.
ramacharitamanas::2904.modern_relevance: You scroll through another week of being busy, but nothing in you feels aligned. This verse cuts through that drift: if your life never touches what is holy and loving, it starts to feel like mere occupancy.
ramacharitamanas::2904.insight: It shifts the mind from social success to spiritual belonging and service.

ramacharitamanas::2905.verse_sanskrit: बिगत बिषाद निषादपति सबहि बढ़ाइ उछाहु। सुमिरि राम मागेउ तुरत तरकस धनुष सनाहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2905.verse_hindi: (इस प्रकार श्री रामजी के लिए प्राण समर्पण का निश्चय करके) निषादराज विषाद से रहित हो गया और सबका उत्साह बढ़ाकर तथा श्री रामचन्द्रजी का स्मरण करके उसने तुरंत ही तरकस, धनुष और कवच माँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2905.english_translation: Freed from grief, the king of the Nishads lifted everyone's spirits. Remembering Ram, he immediately asked for his quiver, bow, and armor.
ramacharitamanas::2905.translation_literal: बिगत (gone) / बिषाद (grief) / निषादपति (king of the Nishads) / सबहि (everyone) / बढ़ाइ (lifting up) / उछाहु (enthusiasm) / सुमिरि (remembering) / राम (Ram) / मागेउ (asked for) / तुरत (immediately) / तरकस (quiver) / धनुष (bow) / सनाहु (armor)
ramacharitamanas::2905.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2905.essence: Devotion clears grief and turns it into readiness.
ramacharitamanas::2905.simple_meaning: Nishadraj shakes off grief, encourages everyone around him, remembers Ram, and quickly asks for his bow, quiver, and armor.
ramacharitamanas::2905.simple_insight: Grief does not have to freeze you; remembrance can turn you back into action.
ramacharitamanas::2905.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Nishadraj has just resolved to live and die for Ram. The sadness lifts from him, and that inner turn immediately becomes outward action: he rouses his people and asks for weapons and armor. The scene is moving toward departure, not reflection.
ramacharitamanas::2905.modern_relevance: You get the message that changes everything, and suddenly the room stops feeling heavy. Before anyone else moves, you’re already gathering what you need.
ramacharitamanas::2905.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional collapse to prepared action.

ramacharitamanas::2906.verse_sanskrit: बेगहु भाइहु सजहु सँजोऊ। सुनि रजाइ कदराइ न कोऊ॥ भलेहिं नाथ सब कहहिं सहरषा। एकहिं एक बढ़ावइ करषा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2906.verse_hindi: (उसने कहा-) हे भाइयों! जल्दी करो और सब सामान सजाओ। मेरी आज्ञा सुनकर कोई मन में कायरता न लावे। सब हर्ष के साथ बोल उठे- हे नाथ! बहुत अच्छा और आपस में एक-दूसरे का जोश बढ़ाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2906.english_translation: He said, “Brothers, hurry and get everything ready. Hearing my command, no one should feel fear. They all replied joyfully, “Very well, lord!” and kept lifting one another’s spirits.
ramacharitamanas::2906.translation_literal: बेगहु (quickly) / भाइहु (brothers) / सजहु (prepare) / सँजोऊ (equipment, supplies) / सुनि (hearing) / रजाइ (command) / कदराइ (be afraid) / न (not) / कोऊ (anyone) / भलेहिं (well, indeed) / नाथ (lord) / सब (all) / कहहिं (say) / सहरषा (with joy) / एकहिं एक (one another) / बढ़ावइ (increase) / करषा (enthusiasm, energy)
ramacharitamanas::2906.speaker: Nishadraj
ramacharitamanas::2906.essence: Courage spreads fastest when people begin moving together.
ramacharitamanas::2906.simple_meaning: Nishadraj urges his people to prepare quickly and not lose courage. They answer with joy and encourage each other.
ramacharitamanas::2906.simple_insight: Shared courage can turn fear into motion.
ramacharitamanas::2906.detailed_meaning: After deciding to stand with Ram, Nishadraj turns to his people and gives quick, practical orders. The fear that could have stalled them is answered by cheerful loyalty, and the whole group steels itself for the journey ahead.
ramacharitamanas::2906.modern_relevance: A team gets bad news before dawn, but someone starts assigning tasks calmly. The mood changes not because the problem vanished, but because one steady voice gave everyone a way forward.
ramacharitamanas::2906.insight: It shows how clear leadership and mutual encouragement keep a group from collapsing into hesitation.

ramacharitamanas::2907.verse_sanskrit: चले निषाद जोहारि जोहारी। सूर सकल रन रूचइ रारी॥ सुमिरि राम पद पंकज पनहीं। भाथीं बाँधि चढ़ाइन्हि धनहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2907.verse_hindi: निषादराज को जोहार कर-करके सब निषाद चले। सभी बड़े शूरवीर हैं और संग्राम में लड़ना उन्हें बहुत अच्छा लगता है। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणकमलों की जूतियों का स्मरण करके उन्होंने भाथियाँ (छोटे-छोटे तरकस) बाँधकर धनुहियों (छोटे-छोटे धनुषों) पर प्रत्यंचा चढ़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2907.english_translation: The Nishadas bowed to their leader and departed. They were all brave warriors who loved battle. Remembering the lotus feet of Shri Ramchandra, they fastened their quivers and fitted their bows.
ramacharitamanas::2907.translation_literal: चले (went) / निषाद (Nishadas) / जोहारि (bowing in respect) / जोहारी (showing respect again and again) / सूर (heroes) / सकल (all) / रन (battle) / रूचइ (is pleasing) / रारी (fighting) / सुमिरि (remembering) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / पंकज (lotus) / पनहीं (shoes) / भाथीं (quivers) / बाँधि (tying) / चढ़ाइन्हि (they fitted) / धनहीं (bows)
ramacharitamanas::2907.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2907.essence: Bravery becomes noble when it is armed by remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::2907.simple_meaning: The Nishadas set out with respect, full of courage, remembering Ram as they prepared their weapons.
ramacharitamanas::2907.simple_insight: True readiness is not just courage; it is courage held in remembrance of what is sacred.
ramacharitamanas::2907.detailed_meaning: In Nishadraj’s camp, the men respond to the call to prepare quickly. These are not frightened followers but brave fighters, and before they arm themselves, they remember Ram’s feet with reverence. The verse is a scene-setting detail in the larger departure.
ramacharitamanas::2907.modern_relevance: You gear up before a hard conversation, but first you steady yourself with what you respect most.
ramacharitamanas::2907.insight: It links action with remembrance, so courage stays clean instead of turning restless or proud.

ramacharitamanas::2908.verse_sanskrit: अँगरी पहिरि कूँड़ि सिर धरहीं। फरसा बाँस सेल सम करहीं॥ एक कुसल अति ओड़न खाँड़े। कूदहिं गगन मनहुँ छिति छाँड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::2908.verse_hindi: कवच पहनकर सिर पर लोहे का टोप रखते हैं और फरसे, भाले तथा बरछों को सीधा कर रहे हैं (सुधार रहे हैं)। कोई तलवार के वार रोकने में अत्यन्त ही कुशल है। वे ऐसे उमंग में भरे हैं, मानो धरती छोड़कर आकाश में कूद (उछल) रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::2908.english_translation: They put on armor and helmets, and set their axes, spears, and lances in order. Some are so skilled at blocking sword blows that they seem to leap into the sky, as if leaving the earth behind.
ramacharitamanas::2908.translation_literal: अँगरी (armor) / पहिरि (wearing) / कूँड़ि (helmet) / सिर (head) / धरहीं (they place) / फरसा (axe) / बाँस (spear/bamboo-lance) / सेल (lance) / सम (straight; ready) / करहीं (they make) / एक (some) / कुसल (skilled) / अति (very) / ओड़न (in blocking/defending) / खाँड़े (sword blows) / कूदहिं (they leap) / गगन (sky) / मनहुँ (as if) / छिति (earth) / छाँड़े (left behind)
ramacharitamanas::2908.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2908.essence: Readiness itself can feel like flight.
ramacharitamanas::2908.simple_meaning: The warriors arm themselves, ready their weapons, and move with such energy that they seem to leap off the ground.
ramacharitamanas::2908.simple_insight: Preparation can feel like momentum when courage is already alive.
ramacharitamanas::2908.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the men preparing to accompany Ram are getting fully equipped for the road ahead. This verse simply shows their readiness, their weapons, and their excited force before the journey continues.
ramacharitamanas::2908.modern_relevance: You zip up your jacket, check your bag, and head out before dawn for a long day. The real shift has already happened: you’re no longer hesitating.
ramacharitamanas::2908.insight: It shifts attention from inner hesitation to outward readiness and decisive motion.

ramacharitamanas::2909.verse_sanskrit: निज निज साजु समाजु बनाई। गुह राउतहि जोहारे जाई॥ देखि सुभट सब लायक जाने। लै लै नाम सकल सनमाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::2909.verse_hindi: अपना-अपना साज-समाज (लड़ाई का सामान और दल) बनाकर उन्होंने जाकर निषादराज गुह को जोहार की। निषादराज ने सुंदर योद्धाओं को देखकर, सबको सुयोग्य जाना और नाम ले-लेकर सबका सम्मान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2909.english_translation: They formed their own battle ranks and went to salute Guha the boatman. Seeing the noble warriors, Guha judged them worthy and honoured each one by name.
ramacharitamanas::2909.translation_literal: निज (own) / निज (own) / साजु (equipment, gear) / समाजु (company, assembly) / बनाई (having made) / गुह (Guha) / राउतहि (the boatman-chief) / जोहारे (saluted) / जाई (going) ॥ / देखि (seeing) / सुभट (brave warriors) / सब (all) / लायक (worthy) / जाने (considered) / लै लै (taking, taking) / नाम (names) / सकल (all) / सनमाने (honoured) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2909.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2909.essence: True honour begins by seeing each person clearly.
ramacharitamanas::2909.simple_meaning: The warriors prepare themselves, greet Guha respectfully, and Guha welcomes them by recognizing each one’s worth.
ramacharitamanas::2909.simple_insight: Respect opens the way. When you see worth in others, they feel seen and honoured.
ramacharitamanas::2909.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram’s followers are gathering for the journey ahead. They organise their gear, go to Guha with respect, and Guha responds by naming and honouring the warriors one by one. The verse builds the atmosphere before the larger exchange that follows.
ramacharitamanas::2909.modern_relevance: You arrive at a new workplace, and the senior team member remembers everyone’s name before the meeting starts. That small respect changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::2909.insight: It teaches you to meet strength with recognition, not distance.

ramacharitamanas::2910.verse_sanskrit: भाइहु लावहु धोख जनि आजु काज बड़ मोहि। सुनि सरोष बोले सुभट बीर अधीर न होहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2910.verse_hindi: (उसने कहा-) हे भाइयों! धोखा न लाना (अर्थात मरने से न घबड़ाना), आज मेरा बड़ा भारी काम है। यह सुनकर सब योद्धा बड़े जोश के साथ बोल उठे- हे वीर! अधीर मत हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2910.english_translation: He said, “Brothers, do not flinch today; I have a great task ahead.” Hearing this, the warriors replied with fierce enthusiasm, “Brave one, do not be impatient.”
ramacharitamanas::2910.translation_literal: भाइहु (brothers) / लावहु (bring) / धोख (hesitation, fear) / जनि (do not) / आजु (today) / काज (task, work) / बड़ (great) / मोहि (for me) / सुनि (hearing) / सरोष (with fervour) / बोले (spoke) / सुभट (warriors) / बीर (brave one) / अधीर (impatient) / न (not) / होहि (be)
ramacharitamanas::2910.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2910.essence: Clear resolve turns fear into readiness.
ramacharitamanas::2910.simple_meaning: A leader asks his companions not to hesitate or fear, because an important task must be done. The warriors answer with eager courage.
ramacharitamanas::2910.simple_insight: Courage spreads fast when someone speaks with certainty.
ramacharitamanas::2910.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield at Ayodhya's edge, armed men are gathering for action. One side calls out to the brothers with urgency, and the warriors answer back at once. The verse captures the surge of resolve before combat begins.
ramacharitamanas::2910.modern_relevance: Right before the presentation starts, one person says, “Don’t freeze now, we need this done.” The room straightens instantly. Clear urgency can steady everyone.
ramacharitamanas::2910.insight: It shows how confident speech can rally a group before a difficult task.
