ramacharitamanas::2911.verse_sanskrit: राम प्रताप नाथ बल तोरे। करहिं कटकु बिनु भट बिनु घोरे॥ जीवन पाउ न पाछें धरहीं। रुंड मुंडमय मेदिनि करहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2911.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्रताप से और आपके बल से हम लोग भरत की सेना को बिना वीर और बिना घोड़े की कर देंगे (एक-एक वीर और एक-एक घोड़े को मार डालेंगे)। जीते जी पीछे पाँव न रखेंगे। पृथ्वी को रुण्ड-मुण्डमयी कर देंगे (सिरों और धड़ों से छा देंगे) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2911.english_translation: By Ram's power and by your strength, we will destroy Bharata's army without warriors and without horses. We will not turn back while alive. We will turn the earth into a field of severed heads and bodies.
ramacharitamanas::2911.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / प्रताप (power, glory) / नाथ (lord) / बल (strength) / तोरे (your) / करहिं (will make) / कटकु (army) / बिनु (without) / भट (warriors) / बिनु (without) / घोरे (horses) / जीवन (alive) / पाउ (feet) / न (not) / पाछें (back) / धरहीं (will place) / रुंड (heads) / मुंडमय (full of trunks and heads) / मेदिनि (earth) / करहीं (will make)
ramacharitamanas::2911.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2911.essence: Pride can turn devotion into a vow of destruction.
ramacharitamanas::2911.simple_meaning: The warriors boast that they will destroy the enemy army completely and never retreat alive.
ramacharitamanas::2911.simple_insight: Raw courage can surge into violence when pride takes over.
ramacharitamanas::2911.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Guha has gathered his boatmen and fighters to support Ram's cause. This verse is the heat of their war-boast before battle, not a teaching moment. It shows their fierce loyalty and bloodlust as they prepare to face Bharata's forces.
ramacharitamanas::2911.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with chest-thumping bravado before a confrontation, and everyone sounds unstoppable until the real moment arrives.
ramacharitamanas::2911.insight: It captures the psychology of battle fever: loyalty, fear, and aggression fused into one loud promise.

ramacharitamanas::2912.verse_sanskrit: दीख निषादनाथ भल टोलू। कहेउ बजाउ जुझाऊ ढोलू॥ एतना कहत छींक भइ बाँए। कहेउ सगुनिअन्ह खेत सुहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2912.verse_hindi: निषादराज ने वीरों का बढ़िया दल देखकर कहा- जुझारू (लड़ाई का) ढोल बजाओ। इतना कहते ही बाईं ओर छींक हुई। शकुन विचारने वालों ने कहा कि खेत सुंदर हैं (जीत होगी) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2912.english_translation: Nishadraj saw the fine troop and said, "Beat the war drums." As he spoke, a sneeze came from the left. The omen-readers said, "The field is auspicious; victory is near."
ramacharitamanas::2912.translation_literal: दीख (saw) / निषादनाथ (lord of the Nishadas) / भल (fine) / टोलू (troop) / कहेउ (said) / बजाउ (beat) / जुझाऊ (war) / ढोलू (drum) / एतना (so much) / कहत (speaking) / छींक (sneeze) / भइ (occurred) / बाँए (left) / कहेउ (said) / सगुनिअन्ह (omen-readers) / खेत (field) / सुहाए (auspicious)
ramacharitamanas::2912.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2912.essence: People under pressure turn small signs into certainty.
ramacharitamanas::2912.simple_meaning: Nishadraj sees his warriors and orders the war drums to be beaten. An omen appears, and the omen-readers take it as a sign of victory.
ramacharitamanas::2912.simple_insight: Even in battle, people look for signs to steady their hope.
ramacharitamanas::2912.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Nishadraj watches his troops and prepares them for conflict. Just as the war mood rises, a left-side sneeze interrupts the moment, and the omen-readers immediately read it as a favorable sign for the coming field.
ramacharitamanas::2912.modern_relevance: You are about to send a tense group message, and someone suddenly says, "That timing feels lucky." In moments like that, people cling to any sign that makes courage easier.
ramacharitamanas::2912.insight: It shows how fear and hope quickly turn random events into guidance.

ramacharitamanas::2913.verse_sanskrit: बूढ़ु एकु कह सगुन बिचारी। भरतहि मिलिअ न होइहि रारी॥ रामहि भरतु मनावन जाहीं। सगुन कहइ अस बिग्रहु नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2913.verse_hindi: एक बूढ़े ने शकुन विचारकर कहा- भरत से मिल लीजिए, उनसे लड़ाई नहीं होगी। भरत श्री रामचन्द्रजी को मनाने जा रहे हैं। शकुन ऐसा कह रहा है कि विरोध नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2913.english_translation: An old man, reading the signs, said, 'Meet Bharat; there will be no fight. Bharat is going to persuade Ram. The signs show no conflict.'
ramacharitamanas::2913.translation_literal: बूढ़ु (old man) / एकु (one) / कह (said) / सगुन (omens) / बिचारी (having considered) / भरतहि (to Bharat) / मिलिअ (let [him] be met) / न (not) / होइहि (will be) / रारी (quarrel)॥ / रामहि (to Ram) / भरतु (Bharat) / मनावन (to persuade) / जाहीं (is going) / सगुन (omens) / कहइ (say) / अस (thus) / बिग्रहु (conflict) / नाहीं (not) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2913.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2913.essence: Clear signs can reveal peace before fear does.
ramacharitamanas::2913.simple_meaning: An elder reads the signs and says there will be no conflict. Bharat is going to persuade Ram, not fight him.
ramacharitamanas::2913.simple_insight: Not every tense moment is a battle; sometimes the signs already point toward peace.
ramacharitamanas::2913.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the crowd is anxious and ready for trouble as Bharat moves toward Ram. An old man studies the omens and calms everyone: Bharat is coming to persuade, not to clash. The verse softens the tension before the meeting.
ramacharitamanas::2913.modern_relevance: You see a tense family chat starting to spiral, but one calm voice reads the room correctly. What looked like a fight is really an attempt to make peace.
ramacharitamanas::2913.insight: It teaches you to pause before assuming hostility and to read intentions more carefully.

ramacharitamanas::2914.verse_sanskrit: सुनि गुह कहइ नीक कह बूढ़ा। सहसा करि पछिताहिं बिमूढ़ा॥ भरत सुभाउ सीलु बिनु बूझें। बड़ि हित हानि जानि बिनु जूझें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2914.verse_hindi: यह सुनकर निषादराज गुहने कहा- बूढ़ा ठीक कह रहा है। जल्दी में (बिना विचारे) कोई काम करके मूर्ख लोग पछताते हैं। भरतजी का शील स्वभाव बिना समझे और बिना जाने युद्ध करने में हित की बहुत बड़ी हानि है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2914.english_translation: Hearing this, Guha said, “The old man speaks well. Rash actions make fools regret later. Without understanding Bharata’s nature and character, fighting him would bring great loss.”
ramacharitamanas::2914.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / गुह (Guha) / कहइ (said) / नीक (well) / कह (spoken) / बूढ़ा (the old man) / सहसा (suddenly, rashly) / करि (doing) / पछिताहिं (they regret) / बिमूढ़ा (the deluded)॥ / भरत (Bharata) / सुभाउ (nature, disposition) / सीलु (character, gentleness) / बिनु (without) / बूझें (understanding)॥ / बड़ि (great) / हित (benefit) / हानि (loss) / जानि (knowing) / बिनु (without) / जूझें (fighting) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2914.speaker: Guha
ramacharitamanas::2914.essence: Rash action fades into regret when you ignore a person’s true character.
ramacharitamanas::2914.simple_meaning: Guha warns that acting in haste leads to regret. He says Bharata must be understood first, because attacking him without knowing his true nature would be a serious mistake.
ramacharitamanas::2914.simple_insight: Quick judgment can turn a preventable conflict into a costly one.
ramacharitamanas::2914.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank, Guha hears an old man’s warning and agrees. Bharata is approaching with purpose, and tempers could flare. Guha sees that Bharata’s gentle character must be understood before anyone assumes hostility.
ramacharitamanas::2914.modern_relevance: You read one angry message and almost fire back immediately. Then you pause, ask what the other person actually meant, and avoid making a small misunderstanding into a lasting rupture.
ramacharitamanas::2914.insight: It shifts you from reactive suspicion to careful reading of another person’s character before acting.

ramacharitamanas::2915.verse_sanskrit: गहहु घाट भट समिटि सब लेउँ मरम मिलि जाइ। बूझि मित्र अरि मध्य गति तस तब करिहउँ आइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2915.verse_hindi: अतएव हे वीरों! तुम लोग इकट्ठे होकर सब घाटों को रोक लो, मैं जाकर भरतजी से मिलकर उनका भेद लेता हूँ। उनका भाव मित्र का है या शत्रु का या उदासीन का, यह जानकर तब आकर वैसा (उसी के अनुसार) प्रबंध करूँगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2915.english_translation: Therefore, warriors, gather and block all the crossings. I will go meet Bharata and learn his true intent. Whether his heart is that of a friend, an enemy, or someone neutral, I will return and act accordingly.
ramacharitamanas::2915.translation_literal: गहहु (hold) / घाट (crossings, river-fords) / भट (warriors) / समिटि (gathering together) / सब (all) / लेउँ (I will take) / मरम (inner intent, secret) / मिलि (meeting) / जाइ (going) / बूझि (having learned) / मित्र (friend) / अरि (enemy) / मध्य (middle, neutral) / गति (state, position) / तस (thus) / तब (then) / करिहउँ (I will do) / आइ (coming back)
ramacharitamanas::2915.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2915.essence: First understand another person's intent; then decide how to respond.
ramacharitamanas::2915.simple_meaning: The speaker tells his men to guard the crossings while he goes to meet Bharata and understand his true intention before deciding what to do.
ramacharitamanas::2915.simple_insight: Don’t rush into action before you understand someone’s heart.
ramacharitamanas::2915.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharata is approaching with a large following, and suspicion hangs in the air. A watcher tells the warriors to secure the crossings while he personally meets Bharata first, so the situation can be judged before any response is made.
ramacharitamanas::2915.modern_relevance: Before you answer a tense message or walk into a family argument, you pause, read the room, and find out what the other person actually means.
ramacharitamanas::2915.insight: It shifts you from reactive defense to careful assessment before action.

ramacharitamanas::2916.verse_sanskrit: लखब सनेहु सुभायँ सुहाएँ। बैरु प्रीति नहिं दुरइँ दुराएँ॥ अस कहि भेंट सँजोवन लागे। कंद मूल फल खग मृग मागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2916.verse_hindi: उनके सुंदर स्वभाव से मैं उनके स्नेह को पहचान लूँगा। वैर और प्रेम छिपाने से नहीं छिपते। ऐसा कहकर वह भेंट का सामान सजाने लगा। उसने कंद, मूल, फल, पक्षी और हिरन मँगवाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2916.english_translation: I will recognize his affection from his lovely nature. Enmity and love cannot stay hidden. Saying this, he began arranging gifts, asking for roots, fruits, birds, and deer.
ramacharitamanas::2916.translation_literal: लखब (to recognize) / सनेहु (affection) / सुभायँ (through nature) / सुहाएँ (lovely) / बैरु (enmity) / प्रीति (love) / नहिं (not) / दुरइँ (hide) / दुराएँ (by hiding) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / भेंट (gifts) / सँजोवन (to arrange) / लागे (began) / कंद (roots) / मूल (tubers) / फल (fruits) / खग (birds) / मृग (deer) / मागे (asked for)
ramacharitamanas::2916.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2916.essence: Love and hostility reveal themselves; your true nature cannot stay hidden.
ramacharitamanas::2916.simple_meaning: True feelings show themselves. Love and hostility cannot stay concealed for long. So he prepares gifts and gathers simple forest offerings for the meeting.
ramacharitamanas::2916.simple_insight: You can trust what a person's nature reveals, even before they speak.
ramacharitamanas::2916.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, people are trying to understand Bharat's heart before meeting him. One observer decides that character will reveal everything: love and hostility cannot be faked for long. So he prepares humble gifts—roots, fruits, birds, and deer—for the meeting.
ramacharitamanas::2916.modern_relevance: You meet someone after months of tension, and within two minutes you know whether the warmth is real. The face, the tone, the small gestures reveal what words try to hide.
ramacharitamanas::2916.insight: It shifts attention from spoken claims to the deeper pattern a person's nature keeps showing.

ramacharitamanas::2917.verse_sanskrit: मीन पीन पाठीन पुराने। भरि भरि भार कहारन्ह आने॥ मिलन साजु सजि मिलन सिधाए। मंगल मूल सगुन सुभ पाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2917.verse_hindi: कहार लोग पुरानी और मोटी पहिना नामक मछलियों के भार भर-भरकर लाए। भेंट का सामान सजाकर मिलने के लिए चले तो मंगलदायक शुभ-शकुन मिले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2917.english_translation: Porters brought loads of fish and other gifts. When they set out, arranging the meeting gifts, they found auspicious signs everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::2917.translation_literal: मीन (fish) / पीन (fat, plump) / पाठीन (a kind of fish) / पुराने (old) / भरि भरि (again and again, full of) / भार (loads) / कहारन्ह (by the porters) / आने (brought)॥ / मिलन (meeting) / साजु (arrangements) / सजि (having arranged) / मिलन (for meeting) / सिधाए (set out)॥ / मंगल (auspicious) / मूल (root, source) / सगुन (omens) / सुभ (good) / पाए (found)॥
ramacharitamanas::2917.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2917.essence: Goodwill can turn a difficult meeting into an auspicious one.
ramacharitamanas::2917.simple_meaning: People bring gifts and set out to meet, and the journey is marked by good omens.
ramacharitamanas::2917.simple_insight: Even a tense meeting can feel blessed when goodwill is already present.
ramacharitamanas::2917.detailed_meaning: Nishadraj is preparing to meet Bharata with offerings, while the scene is still full of caution and uncertainty. The gifts are gathered, the meeting is arranged, and the natural signs around the journey feel favorable, easing the tension before the encounter.
ramacharitamanas::2917.modern_relevance: You pack a small gift before visiting someone after a long misunderstanding. The awkwardness is still there, but the effort itself begins to soften the air.
ramacharitamanas::2917.insight: It shifts attention from conflict to the goodwill carried into the meeting.

ramacharitamanas::2918.verse_sanskrit: देखि दूरि तें कहि निज नामू। कीन्ह मुनीसहि दंड प्रनामू॥ जानि रामप्रिय दीन्हि असीसा। भरतहि कहेउ बुझाइ मुनीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2918.verse_hindi: निषादराज ने मुनिराज वशिष्ठजी को देखकर अपना नाम बतलाकर दूर ही से दण्डवत प्रणाम किया। मुनीश्वर वशिष्ठजी ने उसको राम का प्यारा जानकर आशीर्वाद दिया और भरतजी को समझाकर कहा (कि यह श्री रामजी का मित्र है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2918.english_translation: Seeing him from afar, he gave his own name and bowed with full prostration to the sage. Knowing him to be dear to Ram, the sage blessed him and explained to Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::2918.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / दूरि तें (from afar) / कहि (saying) / निज नामू (his own name) / कीन्हि (did) / मुनीसहि (to the sage) / दंड प्रनामू (prostration)॥ / जानि (knowing) / रामप्रिय (dear to Ram) / दीन्हि (gave) / असीसा (blessing) / भरतहि (to Bharat) / कहेउ (said) / बुझाइ (explaining) / मुनीसा (the sage)॥
ramacharitamanas::2918.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2918.essence: Respect opens the door before familiarity does.
ramacharitamanas::2918.simple_meaning: Guha respectfully introduces himself to Vashishtha from a distance, bows fully, and receives a blessing once he is recognized as dear to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2918.simple_insight: A sincere heart is recognised quickly, even before words are fully explained.
ramacharitamanas::2918.detailed_meaning: On the road to exile, Bharat meets Guha, the Nishad king. Guha first bows to Vashishtha from afar and names himself. Vashishtha sees his loyalty to Ram, blesses him, and tells Bharat who this humble ally is.
ramacharitamanas::2918.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a family gathering and feel unsure how to approach. A respectful greeting and a little humility can dissolve distance faster than perfect words.
ramacharitamanas::2918.insight: It shows how recognition begins with respect, not status.

ramacharitamanas::2919.verse_sanskrit: राम सखा सुनि संदनु त्यागा। चले उचरि उमगत अनुरागा॥ गाउँ जाति गुहँ नाउँ सुनाई। कीन्ह जोहारु माथ महि लाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2919.verse_hindi: यह श्री राम का मित्र है, इतना सुनते ही भरतजी ने रथ त्याग दिया। वे रथ से उतरकर प्रेम में उमँगते हुए चले। निषादराज गुह ने अपना गाँव, जाति और नाम सुनाकर पृथ्वी पर माथा टेककर जोहार की ॥
ramacharitamanas::2919.english_translation: Hearing that this was Ram's friend, Bharat left the chariot. He climbed down and walked forward, overflowing with love. Guha announced his village, caste, and name, and bowed with his forehead to the ground.
ramacharitamanas::2919.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सखा (friend) / सुनि (hearing) / संदनु (chariot) / त्यागा (left) / चले (walked) / उचरि (descending) / उमगत (overflowing) / अनुरागा (with love)॥ / गाउँ (village) / जाति (caste) / गुहँ (Guha) / नाउँ (name) / सुनाई (announced) / कीन्ह (did) / जोहारु (respectful bow) / माथ (head) / महि (earth) / लाई (placed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2919.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2919.essence: Love erases rank and makes reverence immediate.
ramacharitamanas::2919.simple_meaning: Bharat hears that Guha is Ram's friend and immediately steps out of his chariot. Guha responds with deep humility, naming himself and bowing fully to the ground.
ramacharitamanas::2919.simple_insight: Love makes status fall away. Respect becomes natural when the heart recognises a friend of the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::2919.detailed_meaning: On the road to meet Ram, Bharat hears that the Nishad king Guha is Ram's friend. Bharat abandons royal distance at once. Guha answers with full humility, naming himself and bowing low. The moment is about love dissolving hierarchy.
ramacharitamanas::2919.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a wedding, and the moment they mention your dearest friend's name, your whole posture changes. Formality drops. Warmth arrives first.
ramacharitamanas::2919.insight: It shifts you from social rank to shared devotion, where recognition matters more than status.

ramacharitamanas::2920.verse_sanskrit: करत दंडवत देखि तेहि भरत लीन्ह उर लाइ। मनहुँ लखन सन भेंट भइ प्रेमु न हृदयँ समाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2920.verse_hindi: दण्डवत करते देखकर भरतजी ने उठाकर उसको छाती से लगा लिया। हृदय में प्रेम समाता नहीं है, मानो स्वयं लक्ष्मणजी से भेंट हो गई हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2920.english_translation: Seeing him bow down, Bharat took him into his arms. Love would not fit in his heart, as if he had met Lakshman himself.
ramacharitamanas::2920.translation_literal: करत (doing) / दंडवत (full prostration) / देखि (seeing) / तेहि (that one) / भरत (Bharat) / लीन्ह (took) / उर (chest) / लाइ (placing) / मनहुँ (as if) / लखन (Lakshman) / सन (with) / भेंट (meeting) / भइ (happened) / प्रेमु (love) / न (not) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / समाइ (fits)
ramacharitamanas::2920.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2920.essence: Love recognises kinship before the world assigns roles.
ramacharitamanas::2920.simple_meaning: Bharat embraces Guha with such love that it feels like meeting Lakshman. The verse shows instant kinship, not social distance.
ramacharitamanas::2920.simple_insight: Real affection sees the person, not their status.
ramacharitamanas::2920.detailed_meaning: On the road to meet Ram, Bharat reaches the riverbank where Guha has bowed in reverence. Bharat lifts him into an embrace so warm it feels like meeting Lakshman again. The moment turns greeting into brotherhood.
ramacharitamanas::2920.modern_relevance: You meet someone in a tense family gathering and, instead of keeping distance, you pull them close. In that instant, respect becomes belonging.
ramacharitamanas::2920.insight: It shifts the mind from rank and formality to shared humanity and immediate warmth.

ramacharitamanas::2921.verse_sanskrit: भेंटत भरतु ताहि अति प्रीती। लोग सिहाहिं प्रेम कै रीती॥ धन्य धन्य धुनि मंगल मूला। सुर सराहि तेहि बरिसहिं फूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::2921.verse_hindi: भरतजी गुह को अत्यन्त प्रेम से गले लगा रहे हैं। प्रेम की रीति को सब लोग सिहा रहे हैं (ईर्षापूर्वक प्रशंसा कर रहे हैं)। मंगल की मूल 'धन्य-धन्य' की ध्वनि करके देवता उसकी सराहना करते हुए फूल बरसा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2921.english_translation: Bharat embraced Guha with deep love. Everyone praised the way of love. With cries of "Blessed, blessed," the heavens rejoiced and showered flowers.
ramacharitamanas::2921.translation_literal: भेंटत (embracing) / भरतु (Bharat) / ताहि (him) / अति (very) / प्रीती (loving affection) / लोग (people) / सिहाहिं (praise with delight) / प्रेम (love) / कै (of) / रीती (way) / धन्य धन्य (blessed, blessed) / धुनि (sound/cry) / मंगल (auspicious) / मूला (root) / सुर (radiant beings) / सराहि (praising) / तेहि (that) / बरिसहिं (shower) / फूला (flowers)
ramacharitamanas::2921.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2921.essence: Love becomes visible when you greet without reserve.
ramacharitamanas::2921.simple_meaning: Bharat's embrace of Guha is so full of love that everyone sees it as a beautiful example of how love should look.
ramacharitamanas::2921.simple_insight: Real affection doesn't stay private; it changes the atmosphere around you.
ramacharitamanas::2921.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank in Ayodhya's exile journey, Bharat meets Guha and holds him close without hesitation. The scene is no longer just about greeting an ally; it becomes a public celebration of pure, selfless love.
ramacharitamanas::2921.modern_relevance: You meet someone who once stood outside your circle, and you greet them without coolness or calculation. That warmth changes the whole room before anyone says a word.
ramacharitamanas::2921.insight: It shifts the mind from social distance to wholehearted welcome.

ramacharitamanas::2922.verse_sanskrit: लोक बेद सब भाँतिहिं नीचा। जासु छाँह छुइ लेइअ सींचा॥ तेहि भरि अंक राम लघु भ्राता। मिलत पुलक परिपूरित गाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2922.verse_hindi: (वे कहते हैं-) जो लोक और वेद दोनों में सब प्रकार से नीचा माना जाता है, जिसकी छाया के छू जाने से भी स्नान करना होता है, उसी निषाद से अँकवार भरकर (हृदय से चिपटाकर) श्री रामचन्द्रजी के छोटे भाई भरतजी (आनंद और प्रेमवश) शरीर में पुलकावली से परिपूर्ण हो मिल रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2922.english_translation: They say the Nishad is low in every way, by worldly custom and by the Vedas. Yet Bharat, the younger brother of Ram, fills him in his arms and meets him with his whole body thrilled.
ramacharitamanas::2922.translation_literal: लोक (world) / बेद (Vedas) / सब (all) / भाँतिहिं (in every way) / नीचा (low) / जासु (whose) / छाँह (shade) / छुइ (touching) / लेइअ (one should take) / सींचा (bath) / तेहि (that) / भरि (filled) / अंक (lap/embrace) / राम (Ram) / लघु भ्राता (younger brother) / मिलत (meeting) / पुलक (hairs standing on end) / परिपूरित (filled completely) / गाता (body)
ramacharitamanas::2922.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2922.essence: Real devotion does not see status; it sees whom to embrace.
ramacharitamanas::2922.simple_meaning: Bharat shows deep love by embracing the Nishad, even though society and scripture rank him low.
ramacharitamanas::2922.simple_insight: Love becomes visible when you stop sorting people by status.
ramacharitamanas::2922.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank after Ram’s exile begins, Bharat meets Guha, the Nishad chief. Others would judge him as low-born, but Bharat ignores rank and embraces him with overflowing affection. This moment shows Bharat’s heart before the next truth about Ram’s grace.
ramacharitamanas::2922.modern_relevance: At a family gathering, everyone quietly skips over the cleaner who has been helping all evening. You walk straight up, thank him, and shake his hand like an equal.
ramacharitamanas::2922.insight: It shifts you from social ranking to wholehearted recognition of another person.

ramacharitamanas::2923.verse_sanskrit: राम राम कहि जे जमुहाहीं। तिन्हहि न पाप पुंज समुहाहीं॥ यह तौ राम लाइ उर लीन्हा। कुल समेत जगु पावन कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2923.verse_hindi: जो लोग राम-राम कहकर जँभाई लेते हैं (अर्थात आलस्य से भी जिनके मुँह से राम-नाम का उच्चारण हो जाता है), पापों के समूह (कोई भी पाप) उनके सामने नहीं आते। फिर इस गुह को तो स्वयं श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने हृदय से लगा लिया और कुल समेत इसे जगत्पावन (जगत को पवित्र करने वाला) बना दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2923.english_translation: Those who even say "Ram, Ram" while yawning are not met by a crowd of sins. And when Shri Ramchandra himself took Guha into his heart, he made him pure, along with his whole family and clan.
ramacharitamanas::2923.translation_literal: राम राम (Ram, Ram) / कहि (saying) / जे (those who) / जमुहाहीं (yawn) / तिन्हहि (to them) / न (not) / पाप पुंज (crowd of sins) / समुहाहीं (come near)॥ यह (this) / तौ (indeed) / राम (Ram) / लाइ (having attached) / उर (heart) / लीन्हा (took) / कुल समेत (along with family) / जगु (the world) / पावन (pure) / कीन्हा (made)॥
ramacharitamanas::2923.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2923.essence: Ram's name works even before your devotion feels complete.
ramacharitamanas::2923.simple_meaning: Even a casual utterance of Ram's name has power. Guha is not just welcomed; Ram embraces him and makes his whole family pure.
ramacharitamanas::2923.simple_insight: You do not need perfect devotion for grace to begin working.
ramacharitamanas::2923.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharata meets Guha on the riverbank after Ram's exile has shattered the kingdom. Tulsidas pauses the story to show how powerful Ram's name is: even casual remembrance protects, and Ram's embrace transforms Guha and his lineage.
ramacharitamanas::2923.modern_relevance: You mutter a prayer under your breath while rushing out the door, distracted and half-awake. Even that small turning toward Ram matters more than your self-criticism.
ramacharitamanas::2923.insight: It shifts the mind from measuring devotion by intensity to trusting the power of even a small remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::2924.verse_sanskrit: करमनास जलु सुरसरि परई। तेहि को कहहु सीस नहिं धरेई॥ उलटा नामु जपत जगु जाना। बालमीकि भए ब्रह्म समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2924.verse_hindi: कर्मनाशा नदी का जल गंगाजी में पड़ जाता है (मिल जाता है), तब कहिए, उसे कौन सिर पर धारण नहीं करता? जगत जानता है कि उलटा नाम (मरा-मरा) जपते-जपते वाल्मीकिजी ब्रह्म के समान हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2924.english_translation: When the Karnali River water merges into the Ganga, who would not place it on their head? The world knows that by chanting the reversed name, 'mara-mara,' Valmiki became like Brahma.
ramacharitamanas::2924.translation_literal: करमनास (Karnali/Karmanasa) / जलु (water) / सुरसरि (Ganga, river of the devas) / परई (falls into, merges) / तेहि (that) / को (who) / कहहु (tell) / सीस (head) / नहिं (not) / धरेई (would place) / उलटा (reversed) / नामु (name) / जपत (chanting) / जगु (the world) / जाना (knows) / बालमीकि (Valmiki) / भए (became) / ब्रह्म (Brahma) / समाना (equal, like)
ramacharitamanas::2924.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2924.essence: Even imperfect remembrance can turn you into something greater.
ramacharitamanas::2924.simple_meaning: A sacred name can transform even a reversed, imperfect chant into something holy. Valmiki became महान by repeating the name in reverse.
ramacharitamanas::2924.simple_insight: You do not need perfect conditions to begin. Even awkward, broken devotion can change you.
ramacharitamanas::2924.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is defending Ram-naam’s power. He says that when ordinary water joins the Ganga, it becomes worthy of reverence; likewise, even Valmiki’s reversed chanting became the path to greatness.
ramacharitamanas::2924.modern_relevance: You mumble a prayer while driving, distracted and tired, and wonder if it counts. The verse says the power is not in your perfection; it is in the contact you make.
ramacharitamanas::2924.insight: It shifts attention from flawless practice to the transforming force of repeated remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::2925.verse_sanskrit: स्वपच सबर खस जमन जड़ पावँर कोल किरात। रामु कहत पावन परम होत भुवन बिख्यात ॥
ramacharitamanas::2925.verse_hindi: मूर्ख और पामर चाण्डाल, शबर, खस, यवन, कोल और किरात भी राम-नाम कहते ही परम पवित्र और त्रिभुवन में विख्यात हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2925.english_translation: Even the lowest outcasts, hunters, forest-dwellers, and others become supremely pure and famed throughout the three worlds when they utter Ram’s name.
ramacharitamanas::2925.translation_literal: स्वपच (outcast) / सबर (forest-dwellers) / खस (Khas people) / जमन (Yavanas) / जड़ (foolish) / पावँर (lowly) / कोल (Kol) / किरात (Kirata) / रामु (Ram) / कहत (saying) / पावन (pure) / परम (supremely) / होत (become) / भुवन (worlds) / बिख्यात (famed)
ramacharitamanas::2925.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2925.essence: Ram’s name makes the lowly radiant.
ramacharitamanas::2925.simple_meaning: No one is beyond Ram’s grace. Even people seen as low or impure become pure and honored when they speak his name.
ramacharitamanas::2925.simple_insight: You are never too far gone for a fresh beginning.
ramacharitamanas::2925.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is building the case for Ram-naam in Ayodhyakand. After saying even a yawn can carry Ram’s name and that reversed speech purified Valmiki, he now widens the claim: people society dismisses become radiant through Ram’s name alone.
ramacharitamanas::2925.modern_relevance: You catch yourself feeling ashamed after a mistake, then whisper Ram’s name in the car before walking back inside. The verse says your lowest hour is not your final identity.
ramacharitamanas::2925.insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to the cleansing power of remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::2926.verse_sanskrit: नहिं अचिरिजु जुग जुग चलि आई। केहि न दीन्हि रघुबीर बड़ाई॥ राम नाम महिमा सुर कहहीं। सुनि सुनि अवध लोग सुखु लहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2926.verse_hindi: इसमें कोई आश्चर्य नहीं है, युग-युगान्तर से यही रीति चली आ रही है। श्री रघुनाथजी ने किसको बड़ाई नहीं दी? इस प्रकार देवता राम नाम की महिमा कह रहे हैं और उसे सुन-सुनकर अयोध्या के लोग सुख पा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2926.english_translation: There is nothing surprising in this; this has gone on age after age. Who has not been uplifted by Raghubir? The gods speak of Ram's greatness, and the people of Ayodhya keep finding comfort in hearing it again and again.
ramacharitamanas::2926.translation_literal: नहिं (not) / अचिरिजु (surprising) / जुग जुग (age after age) / चलि आई (has kept going) / केहि (whom) / न (not) / दीन्हि (gave) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / बड़ाई (greatness)॥ राम (Ram) / नाम (name) / महिमा (glory) / सुर (the radiant beings) / कहहीं (say) / सुनि सुनि (hearing again and again) / अवध (Ayodhya) / लोग (people) / सुखु (comfort) / लहहीं (receive)॥
ramacharitamanas::2926.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2926.essence: Ram's name comforts because his greatness never stops being true.
ramacharitamanas::2926.simple_meaning: Ram's greatness is not new or rare; it has always been praised, and hearing his name brings comfort to people.
ramacharitamanas::2926.simple_insight: Some names calm the heart simply by being heard.
ramacharitamanas::2926.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the pain of exile has already begun to fracture the royal family, the narrator turns to Ram's praise. The gods speak of his greatness, and the people of Ayodhya find comfort just by hearing his name.
ramacharitamanas::2926.modern_relevance: You are exhausted after a hard week, and one voice you trust says, "You are not alone." The relief is immediate. Some words restore you before anything else changes.
ramacharitamanas::2926.insight: It shifts attention from what is missing to the steady comfort of remembering Ram's name.

ramacharitamanas::2927.verse_sanskrit: रामसखहि मिलि भरत सप्रेमा। पूँछी कुसल सुमंगल खेमा॥ देखि भरत कर सीलु सनेहू। भा निषाद तेहि समय बिदेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2927.verse_hindi: राम सखा निषादराज से प्रेम के साथ मिलकर भरतजी ने कुशल, मंगल और क्षेम पूछी। भरतजी का शील और प्रेम देखकर निषाद उस समय विदेह हो गया (प्रेममुग्ध होकर देह की सुध भूल गया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2927.english_translation: Bharat met Nishadraj with love and asked after his well-being, welfare, and peace. Seeing Bharat's character and affection, Nishad was carried beyond body-consciousness in that moment.
ramacharitamanas::2927.translation_literal: रामसखहि (with Ram's friend) / मिलि (meeting) / भरत (Bharat) / सप्रेमा (with love) / पूँछी (asked) / कुसल (well-being) / सुमंगल (auspicious welfare) / खेमा (peace, security) / देखि (seeing) / भरत (Bharat) / कर (of) / सीलु (character, gentleness) / सनेहू (affection, love) / भा (became) / निषाद (Nishad) / तेहि समय (at that moment) / बिदेहू (beyond body-consciousness)
ramacharitamanas::2927.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2927.essence: Love without pride makes another person forget themselves.
ramacharitamanas::2927.simple_meaning: Bharat greets Nishadraj with warmth and asks about his welfare. Nishad is so moved by Bharat's gentleness and affection that he forgets himself.
ramacharitamanas::2927.simple_insight: Real humility can move another person more than praise ever could.
ramacharitamanas::2927.detailed_meaning: On the road to Chitrakoot, Bharat meets Nishadraj, the loyal boatman who helped Ram. Bharat does not arrive with royal pride; he comes with love, respect, and concern. Nishad is so struck by Bharat's gentleness that he loses all self-awareness.
ramacharitamanas::2927.modern_relevance: You meet someone who has helped your family, and instead of acting important, you ask about their life first. That simple respect can disarm years of distance in a moment.
ramacharitamanas::2927.insight: It shifts attention from status to sincere regard, showing how respectful presence creates immediate trust.

ramacharitamanas::2928.verse_sanskrit: सकुच सनेहु मोदु मन बाढ़ा। भरतहि चितवत एकटक ठाढ़ा॥ धरि धीरजु पद बंदि बहोरी। बिनय सप्रेम करत कर जोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2928.verse_hindi: उसके मन में संकोच, प्रेम और आनंद इतना बढ़ गया कि वह खड़ा-खड़ा टकटकी लगाए भरतजी को देखता रहा। फिर धीरज धरकर भरतजी के चरणों की वंदना करके प्रेम के साथ हाथ जोड़कर विनती करने लगा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2928.english_translation: Shyness, love, and joy rose so much in his mind that he stood there staring at Bharat without blinking. Then, gathering courage, he bowed at Bharat's feet and, with loving hands joined, began to speak humbly.
ramacharitamanas::2928.translation_literal: सकुच (shyness) / सनेहु (love) / मोदु (joy) / मन (mind) / बाढ़ा (grew) / भरतहि (at Bharat) / चितवत (gazing) / एकटक (unblinkingly) / ठाढ़ा (standing) / धरि (gathering) / धीरजु (courage/steadiness) / पद (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / बहोरी (again) / बिनय (humble request) / सप्रेम (with love) / करत (doing) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined)
ramacharitamanas::2928.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2928.essence: Love and respect can leave you speechless before they make you bow.
ramacharitamanas::2928.simple_meaning: His heart overflows with shy love and joy at seeing Bharat. He steadies himself, bows to Bharat's feet, and speaks with folded hands.
ramacharitamanas::2928.simple_insight: Deep respect can make even simple greetings feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::2928.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, a devotee meets Bharat and is overwhelmed by his purity and grace. The moment is not a teaching in itself, but a tender bridge into the next exchange, where reverence turns into humble speech.
ramacharitamanas::2928.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you deeply admire, and for a second you forget your words. Respect, gratitude, and affection all arrive at once.
ramacharitamanas::2928.insight: It shows how genuine reverence naturally becomes humility in action.

ramacharitamanas::2929.verse_sanskrit: कुसल मूल पद पंकज पेखी। मैं तिहुँ काल कुसल निज लेखी॥ अब प्रभु परम अनुग्रह तोरें। सहित कोटि कुल मंगल मोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2929.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! कुशल के मूल आपके चरण कमलों के दर्शन कर मैंने तीनों कालों में अपना कुशल जान लिया। अब आपके परम अनुग्रह से करोड़ों कुलों (पीढ़ियों) सहित मेरा मंगल (कल्याण) हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2929.english_translation: O Lord, seeing your lotus feet, the root of all good, I know myself blessed in all three times. Now, by your supreme grace, my welfare has spread to millions of generations.
ramacharitamanas::2929.translation_literal: कुसल (welfare) / मूल (root) / पद (feet) / पंकज (lotus) / पेखी (seeing) / मैं (I) / तिहुँ (three) / काल (times) / कुसल (well-being) / निज (my own) / लेखी (accounting as)॥ / अब (now) / प्रभु (Lord) / परम (supreme) / अनुग्रह (grace) / तोरें (by you) / सहित (together with) / कोटि (crores) / कुल (families) / मंगल (auspicious good) / मोरें (my)॥
ramacharitamanas::2929.speaker: Nishadraj
ramacharitamanas::2929.essence: Ram's presence alone turns personal blessing into family-wide grace.
ramacharitamanas::2929.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram's feet, Nishadraj feels that all his past, present, and future are blessed. He believes Ram's grace has turned his life and lineage toward good.
ramacharitamanas::2929.simple_insight: There is deep relief in being seen by the right presence and knowing nothing else is missing.
ramacharitamanas::2929.detailed_meaning: Nishadraj has just welcomed Bharat with reverence and love. Overcome by Ram's presence in Bharat's feet, he says that merely seeing those lotus feet has made him feel blessed across all three times, and that Ram's grace extends welfare to his whole lineage.
ramacharitamanas::2929.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence immediately settles your chest. No speech, no proof — just the quiet certainty that this moment is good and your life is larger now.
ramacharitamanas::2929.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing security to receiving grace as the source of well-being.

ramacharitamanas::2930.verse_sanskrit: समुझि मोरि करतूति कुलु प्रभु महिमा जियँ जोइ। जो न भजइ रघुबीर पद जग बिधि बंचित सोइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2930.verse_hindi: मेरी करतूत और कुल को समझकर और प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी की महिमा को मन में देख (विचार) कर (अर्थात कहाँ तो मैं नीच जाति और नीच कर्म करने वाला जीव, और कहाँ अनन्तकोटि ब्रह्माण्डों के स्वामी भगवान श्री रामचन्द्रजी! पर उन्होंने मुझ जैसे नीच को भी अपनी अहैतुकी कृपा वश अपना लिया- यह समझकर) जो रघुवीर श्री रामजी के चरणों का भजन नहीं करता, वह जगत में विधाता के द्वारा ठगा गया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2930.english_translation: Considering my conduct and my lineage, and reflecting in your heart on the glory of Lord Ram, whoever does not worship Raghubir's feet is cheated in this world by fate.
ramacharitamanas::2930.translation_literal: समुझि (understanding) / मोरि (my) / करतूति (conduct) / कुलु (lineage) / प्रभु (Lord) / महिमा (glory) / जियँ (in the heart) / जोइ (seeing/reflecting) / जो (whoever) / न (not) / भजइ (worships) / रघुबीर (Raghubir, Ram) / पद (feet) / जग (world) / बिधि (by fate/order) / बंचित (cheated) / सोइ (that one)
ramacharitamanas::2930.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2930.essence: Ignoring Ram is the real loss, not your own smallness.
ramacharitamanas::2930.simple_meaning: Bharat says that when he remembers his own lowliness and Ram's greatness, anyone who does not worship Ram is truly cheated in life.
ramacharitamanas::2930.simple_insight: Humility opens the heart to grace, and grace makes devotion feel like the only sane response.
ramacharitamanas::2930.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands before Ram after the exile has shattered Ayodhya. He sees his own conduct and lineage as small beside Ram's greatness, and from that humility he declares that anyone who does not worship Ram has been cheated out of life’s highest gain.
ramacharitamanas::2930.modern_relevance: You compare your messy life to someone else's steadiness and feel small. Then you remember who has carried you, forgiven you, and stayed close anyway — and gratitude becomes the only honest response.
ramacharitamanas::2930.insight: It shifts the mind from self-judgment to grateful devotion.

ramacharitamanas::2931.verse_sanskrit: कपटी कायर कुमति कुजाती। लोक बेद बाहेर सब भाँती॥ राम कीन्ह आपन जबही तें। भयउँ भुवन भूषन तबही तें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2931.verse_hindi: मैं कपटी, कायर, कुबुद्धि और कुजाति हूँ और लोक-वेद दोनों से सब प्रकार से बाहर हूँ। पर जब से श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने मुझे अपनाया है, तभी से मैं विश्व का भूषण हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2931.english_translation: I am deceitful, cowardly, of confused judgment, and of low birth, outside both social order and scripture in every way. But from the moment Lord Ram accepted me as his own, I became an ornament of the world.
ramacharitamanas::2931.translation_literal: कपटी (deceitful) / कायर (cowardly) / कुमति (confused judgment) / कुजाती (low birth) / लोक (worldly order) / बेद (scripture) / बाहेर (outside) / सब भाँती (in every way) // राम (Ram) / कीन्ह (made) / आपन (his own) / जबही तें (from the moment) / भयउँ (became) / भुवन (world) / भूषन (ornament) / तबही तें (from then)
ramacharitamanas::2931.speaker: Nishad
ramacharitamanas::2931.essence: Ram's acceptance turns an outcast into an ornament of the world.
ramacharitamanas::2931.simple_meaning: Nishad calls himself unworthy by every worldly standard, then says Ram's acceptance alone made him honored.
ramacharitamanas::2931.simple_insight: You do not need to become worthy before you are loved; being received can transform how you see yourself.
ramacharitamanas::2931.detailed_meaning: Nishad is speaking after meeting Bharat's camp in Ayodhyakand. He lowers himself completely, naming his flaws and exclusion, then turns to the miracle of grace: Ram accepted him. That acceptance, not status, gives him honor.
ramacharitamanas::2931.modern_relevance: You walk into a room feeling like the least polished person there, already rehearsing your apology. Then someone you respect treats you like you belong, and your whole posture changes.
ramacharitamanas::2931.insight: It shifts identity from self-judgment to received belonging.

ramacharitamanas::2932.verse_sanskrit: देखि प्रीति सुनि बिनय सुहाई। मिलेउ बहोरि भरत लघु भाई॥ कहि निषाद निज नाम सुबानीं। सादर सकल जोहारीं रानीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2932.verse_hindi: निषाद राज की प्रीति को देखकर और सुंदर विनय सुनकर फिर भरतजी के छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्नजी उससे मिले। फिर निषाद ने अपना नाम ले-लेकर सुंदर (नम्र और मधुर) वाणी से सब रानियों को आदरपूर्वक जोहार की ॥
ramacharitamanas::2932.english_translation: Seeing his affection and hearing his lovely humility, Bharat's younger brother met him again. Then Nishad spoke his own name in gentle words and respectfully greeted all the queens.
ramacharitamanas::2932.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / प्रीति (affection) / सुनि (hearing) / बिनय (humility) / सुहाई (lovely) / मिलेउ (met) / बहोरि (again) / भरत (Bharat) / लघु भाई (younger brother) / कहि (speaking) / निषाद (Nishad) / निज (own) / नाम (name) / सुबानीं (in sweet words) / सादर (respectfully) / सकल (all) / जोहारीं (greeted) / रानीं (queens)
ramacharitamanas::2932.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2932.essence: Respect makes strangers feel like family.
ramacharitamanas::2932.simple_meaning: Nishad's warm respect moves Bharat's brother to meet him again, and Nishad greets the queens politely by name.
ramacharitamanas::2932.simple_insight: Gentle respect opens doors that status never could.
ramacharitamanas::2932.detailed_meaning: After Bharat's grief-filled arrival, Nishad's affection and humility soften the whole scene. Shatrughna meets him again, and Nishad responds with careful courtesy, greeting the queens with honor. The moment shows how devotion and good manners turn tension into fellowship.
ramacharitamanas::2932.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a family gathering who could easily ignore you, but they look you in the eye, remember your name, and make you feel included.
ramacharitamanas::2932.insight: It shows how sincere humility creates immediate trust and dissolves social distance.

ramacharitamanas::2933.verse_sanskrit: जानि लखन सम देहिं असीसा। जिअहु सुखी सय लाख बरीसा॥ निरखि निषादु नगर नर नारी। भए सुखी जनु लखनु निहारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2933.verse_hindi: रानियाँ उसे लक्ष्मणजी के समान समझकर आशीर्वाद देती हैं कि तुम सौ लाख वर्षों तक सुख पूर्वक जिओ। नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष निषाद को देखकर ऐसे सुखी हुए, मानो लक्ष्मणजी को देख रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::2933.english_translation: Thinking him to be like Lakshman, the queens bless him: "May you live happily for a hundred million years." Seeing Nishad, the men and women of the city became happy, as if they were seeing Lakshman himself.
ramacharitamanas::2933.translation_literal: जानि (knowing) / लखन (Lakshman) / सम (like) / देहिं (they give) / असीसा (blessings) / जिअहु (may you live) / सुखी (happily) / सय (hundred) / लाख (hundred thousand) / बरीसा (years) / निरखि (seeing) / निषादु (Nishad) / नगर (city) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / भए (became) / सुखी (happy) / जनु (as if) / लखनु (Lakshman) / निहारी (having seen)
ramacharitamanas::2933.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2933.essence: True goodness is recognized as kin before words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2933.simple_meaning: The queens bless Nishad as if he were Lakshman, and the city’s people feel joy on seeing him. His presence is received like a beloved friend’s.
ramacharitamanas::2933.simple_insight: Kindness makes a stranger feel like family.
ramacharitamanas::2933.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Nishad has won the trust of Ram’s people through humility and loyalty. The queens and city residents respond to him with affection, seeing in him the same devoted spirit they associate with Lakshman. This is a scene of recognition, not doctrine.
ramacharitamanas::2933.modern_relevance: You walk into a house where everyone is tense, and one person greets you with such warmth that the whole room softens. That is the kind of welcome this verse holds.
ramacharitamanas::2933.insight: It shows how devotion and goodwill can make social distance disappear instantly.

ramacharitamanas::2934.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं लहेउ एहिं जीवन लाहू। भेंटेउ रामभद्र भरि बाहू॥ सुनि निषादु निज भाग बड़ाई। प्रमुदित मन लइ चलेउ लेवाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2934.verse_hindi: सब कहते हैं कि जीवन का लाभ तो इसी ने पाया है, जिसे कल्याण स्वरूप श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने भुजाओं में बाँधकर गले लगाया है। निषाद अपने भाग्य की बड़ाई सुनकर मन में परम आनंदित हो सबको अपने साथ लिवा ले चला ॥
ramacharitamanas::2934.english_translation: Everyone says he has gained the true benefit of life, the one whom the благest Ramchandra has embraced in his arms. Hearing his own good fortune praised, Nishad became deeply joyful and led everyone along with him.
ramacharitamanas::2934.translation_literal: कहहिं (they say) / लहेउ (has gained) / एहिं (this) / जीवन (life) / लाहू (profit, gain) / भेंटेउ (embraced, met) / रामभद्र (auspicious Ram) / भरि (full) / बाहू (arms) / सुनि (hearing) / निषादु (Nishad) / निज (his own) / भाग (fortune) / बड़ाई (praise, greatness) / प्रमुदित (delighted) / मन (mind) / लइ (taking) / चलेउ (went) / लेवाई (along with him, to fetch others)
ramacharitamanas::2934.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2934.essence: Being embraced by Ram is the greatest gain of all.
ramacharitamanas::2934.simple_meaning: People see Nishad as blessed because Ram has embraced him. Hearing this, Nishad feels joyful and goes to bring the others along.
ramacharitamanas::2934.simple_insight: Real fulfilment is being held dear by what you love most.
ramacharitamanas::2934.detailed_meaning: After Shatrughna and the women of Ayodhya honour Nishad, the crowd turns his meeting with Ram into a sign of supreme blessing. Nishad hears his fortune praised, feels overwhelmed with joy, and goes to gather the others.
ramacharitamanas::2934.modern_relevance: Someone introduces you at a gathering by the one moment that made your year — the person you admire remembered your name. That recognition can feel like a whole life being affirmed.
ramacharitamanas::2934.insight: It shifts value from status or achievement to being received with love.

ramacharitamanas::2935.verse_sanskrit: सनकारे सेवक सकल चले स्वामि रुख पाइ। घर तरु तर सर बाग बन बास बनाएन्हि जाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2935.verse_hindi: उसने अपने सब सेवकों को इशारे से कह दिया। वे स्वामी का रुख पाकर चले और उन्होंने घरों में, वृक्षों के नीचे, तालाबों पर तथा बगीचों और जंगलों में ठहरने के लिए स्थान बना दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2935.english_translation: He signaled all his servants. Understanding their master's intention, they went and arranged places to stay in houses, under trees, by ponds, and in gardens and forests.
ramacharitamanas::2935.translation_literal: सनकारे (signaled) / सेवक (servants) / सकल (all) / चले (went) / स्वामि (master) / रुख (intention) / पाइ (having received) / घर (houses) / तरु (trees) / तर (under) / सर (ponds) / बाग (gardens) / बन (forests) / बास (places to stay) / बनाएन्हि (they made) / जाइ (going)
ramacharitamanas::2935.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2935.essence: Shared purpose turns many hands into one movement.
ramacharitamanas::2935.simple_meaning: The servants understood their leader’s intention and quickly arranged rest places everywhere along the route.
ramacharitamanas::2935.simple_insight: Good leadership makes people move together without confusion.
ramacharitamanas::2935.detailed_meaning: As Bharat travels toward Nandigram, his attendants read his intent without needing long instructions. They prepare shelter wherever they can, turning the path into a place of care. The verse supports the unfolding arrival, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2935.modern_relevance: You’re coordinating a late-night arrival for someone important, and everyone just knows what to do. No speeches, no chaos — only shared purpose and quiet readiness.
ramacharitamanas::2935.insight: It shows how clear intention can organize a whole group into calm, practical action.

ramacharitamanas::2936.verse_sanskrit: सृंगबेरपुर भरत दीख जब। भे सनेहँ सब अंग सिथिल तब॥ सोहत दिएँ निषादहि लागू। जनु तनु धरें बिनय अनुरागू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2936.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने जब श्रृंगवेरपुर को देखा, तब उनके सब अंग प्रेम के कारण शिथिल हो गए। वे निषाद को लाग दिए (अर्थात उसके कंधे पर हाथ रखे चलते हुए) ऐसे शोभा दे रहे हैं, मानो विनय और प्रेम शरीर धारण किए हुए हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::2936.english_translation: When Bharat saw Srngverpur, all his limbs grew soft with love. Leaning on Nishad’s shoulder, he shone like humility and affection taking bodily form.
ramacharitamanas::2936.translation_literal: सृंगबेरपुर (Srngverpur) / भरत (Bharat) / दीख (saw) / जब (when) / भे (became) / सनेहँ (with love) / सब (all) / अंग (limbs) / सिथिल (limp/soft) / तब (then)॥ / सोहत (shining) / दिएँ (given/placed) / निषादहि (to Nishad) / लागू (leaning/attached) / जनु (as if) / तनु (body) / धरें (having taken form) / बिनय (humility) / अनुरागू (affection/love) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2936.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2936.essence: Love can make humility visible in the body.
ramacharitamanas::2936.simple_meaning: Bharat becomes physically softened by love when he sees Srngverpur, and his closeness to Nishad makes him look like humility and affection embodied.
ramacharitamanas::2936.simple_insight: Real devotion changes how you carry yourself. Love can make strength feel tender instead of proud.
ramacharitamanas::2936.detailed_meaning: On the road to meet Ram, Bharat reaches Srngverpur and sees the place tied to Ram’s journey. The sight overwhelms him. He leans on Nishad with such natural humility that he seems like love and modesty made visible.
ramacharitamanas::2936.modern_relevance: You arrive at a place that reminds you of someone you love, and your whole body loosens. The guard drops, your voice softens, and even your posture begins to show what your heart feels.
ramacharitamanas::2936.insight: It shifts devotion from an idea into a bodily change: love becomes visible in posture, touch, and ease.

ramacharitamanas::2937.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि भरत सेनु सबु संगा। दीखि जाइ जग पावनि गंगा॥ रामघाट कहँ कीन्ह प्रनामू। भा मनु मगनु मिले जनु रामू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2937.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार भरतजी ने सब सेना को साथ में लिए हुए जगत को पवित्र करने वाली गंगाजी के दर्शन किए। श्री रामघाट को (जहाँ श्री रामजी ने स्नान संध्या की थी) प्रणाम किया। उनका मन इतना आनंदमग्न हो गया, मानो उन्हें स्वयं श्री रामजी मिल गए हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::2937.english_translation: In this way Bharat, traveling with the whole army, saw the purifying Ganga. He bowed to Ramghat, and his mind became so absorbed in joy that it was as if he had met Ram himself.
ramacharitamanas::2937.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / भरत (Bharat) / सेनु (army) / सबु (all) / संगा (together with) / दीखि (having seen) / जाइ (going) / जग (world) / पावनि (purifying) / गंगा (Ganga) / रामघाट (Ramghat) / कहँ (to) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रनामू (bow) / भा (became) / मनु (mind) / मगनु (absorbed) / मिले (having met) / जनु (as if) / रामू (Ram)
ramacharitamanas::2937.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2937.essence: Love can make a place feel like meeting Ram again.
ramacharitamanas::2937.simple_meaning: Bharat reaches the holy Ganga, bows at Ramghat, and feels such joy that it seems like meeting Ram himself.
ramacharitamanas::2937.simple_insight: Sacred places can awaken love so deeply that the heart feels presence, not distance.
ramacharitamanas::2937.detailed_meaning: Bharat is traveling with his army toward the forest path of exile. When he sees the Ganga and Ramghat, the memory of Ram floods him. His bow is not formal respect; it is love overflowing into reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2937.modern_relevance: You step off a train at a river town after years away, and one familiar ghat, one old prayer place, brings back someone you miss completely. The place feels like meeting them again.
ramacharitamanas::2937.insight: It shifts reverence from ritual gesture to living remembrance.

ramacharitamanas::2938.verse_sanskrit: करहिं प्रनाम नगर नर नारी। मुदित ब्रह्ममय बारि निहारी॥ करि मज्जनु मागहिं कर जोरी। रामचन्द्र पद प्रीति न थोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2938.verse_hindi: नगर के नर-नारी प्रणाम कर रहे हैं और गंगाजी के ब्रह्म रूप जल को देख-देखकर आनंदित हो रहे हैं। गंगाजी में स्नान कर हाथ जोड़कर सब यही वर माँगते हैं कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में हमारा प्रेम कम न हो (अर्थात बहुत अधिक हो) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2938.english_translation: The men and women of the city bowed with joy at the sight of the Brahman-like waters. After bathing, they joined their hands and asked for one boon: that their love for Ramchandra's feet never grow less.
ramacharitamanas::2938.translation_literal: करहिं (they do) / प्रनाम (bowing) / नगर (city) / नर नारी (men and women) / मुदित (joyful) / ब्रह्ममय (filled with Brahman) / बारि (water) / निहारी (seeing) ॥ / करि (having done) / मज्जनु (bathing) / मागहिं (they ask) / कर जोरी (with joined hands) / रामचन्द्र (Ramchandra) / पद (feet) / प्रीति (love) / न थोरी (not little)
ramacharitamanas::2938.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2938.essence: Seeing holiness makes you ask for more love, not more things.
ramacharitamanas::2938.simple_meaning: The people of the city bow with joy at the holy water, bathe, and ask for one thing: more love for Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::2938.simple_insight: Real devotion asks for more love, not more possessions.
ramacharitamanas::2938.detailed_meaning: As Bharat travels toward Ram's path, the city people see the sacred river and respond with reverence. They bathe, fold their hands, and ask only that their love for Ram keep growing. The moment shows how Ram's presence turns ordinary people toward devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2938.modern_relevance: You step into a temple after a long, messy week and suddenly your requests feel smaller. What you want most is not a better deal — just a softer, steadier love for what is sacred.
ramacharitamanas::2938.insight: It shifts desire from worldly gain to deeper devotion.

ramacharitamanas::2939.verse_sanskrit: भरत कहेउ सुरसरि तव रेनू। सकल सुखद सेवक सुरधेनू॥ जोरि पानि बर मागउँ एहू। सीय राम पद सहज सनेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2939.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने कहा- हे गंगे! आपकी रज सबको सुख देने वाली तथा सेवक के लिए तो कामधेनु ही है। मैं हाथ जोड़कर यही वरदान माँगता हूँ कि श्री सीता-रामजी के चरणों में मेरा स्वाभाविक प्रेम हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2939.english_translation: Bharat said, “O sacred river, your dust gives every kind of joy and is like the wish-fulfilling cow for a servant. With folded hands, I ask only this boon: natural love for the feet of Sita and Ram.”
ramacharitamanas::2939.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / कहेउ (said) / सुरसरि (O sacred river) / तव (your) / रेनू (dust) / सकल (all) / सुखद (joy-giving) / सेवक (for a servant) / सुरधेनू (wish-fulfilling cow) / जोरि (joining) / पानि (hands) / बर (boon) / मागउँ (I ask) / एहू (this) / सीय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / सहज (natural) / सनेहू (love)
ramacharitamanas::2939.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2939.essence: The highest boon is effortless love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2939.simple_meaning: Bharat treats the sacred river as a source of blessing and asks for one thing only: a natural, effortless love for Sita and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2939.simple_insight: Real devotion does not ask for gain — it asks for closeness that feels natural.
ramacharitamanas::2939.detailed_meaning: Bharat has reached the Ganga with his retinue during the long return from exile. Standing in reverence, he does not ask for power or comfort. He asks only for an easy, spontaneous love for Sita and Ram, showing the heart of his devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2939.modern_relevance: You stand in a temple, a hospital corridor, or beside a parent you cannot fix. Instead of asking for control, you ask for a heart that can love cleanly and without strain.
ramacharitamanas::2939.insight: It shifts desire away from outcomes and toward a relationship that can be lived with sincerity.

ramacharitamanas::2940.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि मज्जनु भरतु करि गुर अनुसासन पाइ। मातु नहानीं जानि सब डेरा चले लवाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2940.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार भरतजी स्नान कर और गुरुजी की आज्ञा पाकर तथा यह जानकर कि सब माताएँ स्नान कर चुकी हैं, डेरा उठा ले चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2940.english_translation: In this way, Bharata bathed, received the guru's instruction, and knowing that all the mothers had bathed, he had the camp moved on.
ramacharitamanas::2940.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / मज्जनु (bath) / भरतु (Bharata) / करि (having done) / गुर (guru's) / अनुसासन (instruction) / पाइ (having received) / मातु (mothers) / नहानीं (having bathed) / जानि (knowing) / सब (all) / डेरा (camp) / चले (moved) / लवाइ (having had moved)
ramacharitamanas::2940.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2940.essence: True devotion also remembers the people around you.
ramacharitamanas::2940.simple_meaning: Bharata completes his bath, follows his teacher's guidance, checks on the mothers, and then moves the camp forward.
ramacharitamanas::2940.simple_insight: Even in grief and travel, he stays orderly, considerate, and obedient.
ramacharitamanas::2940.detailed_meaning: On the banks of the Ganga in Ayodhyakand, Bharata is moving with the returning party after his vow of devotion to Ram. After bathing and taking guidance from the guru, he makes sure the queens have also finished before the camp is shifted onward.
ramacharitamanas::2940.modern_relevance: You finish your morning duties, check that everyone in the house is ready, and only then leave. Small care, done quietly, keeps a difficult day from fraying.
ramacharitamanas::2940.insight: It shows a leader whose devotion expresses itself as careful, practical attention to others.

ramacharitamanas::2941.verse_sanskrit: जहँ तहँ लोगन्ह डेरा कीन्हा। भरत सोधु सबही कर लीन्हा॥ सुर सेवा करि आयसु पाई। राम मातु पहिं गे दोउ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2941.verse_hindi: लोगों ने जहाँ-तहाँ डेरा डाल दिया। भरतजी ने सभी का पता लगाया (कि सब लोग आकर आराम से टिक गए हैं या नहीं)। फिर देव पूजन करके आज्ञा पाकर दोनों भाई श्री रामचन्द्रजी की माता कौसल्याजी के पास गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2941.english_translation: People pitched their tents here and there. Bharat checked on everyone. After worshiping the radiant beings and receiving permission, the two brothers went to Ram's mother.
ramacharitamanas::2941.translation_literal: जहँ तहँ (here and there) / लोगन्ह (the people) / डेरा (camp) / कीन्हा (made) / भरत (Bharat) / सोधु (inquiry/checking) / सबही (everyone) / कर (did) / लीन्हा (took) / सुर सेवा (service of radiant beings) / करि (having done) / आयसु (permission) / पाई (having received) / राम मातु (Ram's mother) / पहिं (to) / गे (went) / दोउ भाई (both brothers)
ramacharitamanas::2941.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2941.essence: Devotion here looks like careful, humble order.
ramacharitamanas::2941.simple_meaning: The group settles in camp, Bharat makes sure everyone is accounted for, and then he and his brother go to Ram's mother after worship and permission.
ramacharitamanas::2941.simple_insight: True care shows up in the small logistics: checking on people, honoring protocol, and moving together with humility.
ramacharitamanas::2941.detailed_meaning: After the sacred bath at the Ganga, Bharat quietly organizes the camp and checks that everyone has settled safely. Only then, after worship and permission, does he and Shatrughna go to Kaushalya. The verse keeps the movement gentle and orderly.
ramacharitamanas::2941.modern_relevance: After a long family trip, you count heads before leaving the parking lot, make sure no one is left behind, and only then walk inside together. Care looks like that.
ramacharitamanas::2941.insight: It shifts attention from grand emotion to quiet responsibility and respectful sequence.

ramacharitamanas::2942.verse_sanskrit: चरन चाँपि कहि कहि मृदु बानी। जननीं सकल भरत सनमानी॥ भाइहि सौंपि मातु सेवकाई। आपु निषादहि लीन्ह बोलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2942.verse_hindi: चरण दबाकर और कोमल वचन कह-कहकर भरतजी ने सब माताओं का सत्कार किया। फिर भाई शत्रुघ्न को माताओं की सेवा सौंपकर आपने निषाद को बुला लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2942.english_translation: Touching their feet and speaking softly again and again, Bharat honoured all the mothers. Then he entrusted the mothers' service to his brother Shatrughna and called the Nishad chief to him.
ramacharitamanas::2942.translation_literal: चरन (feet) / चाँपि (pressing) / कहि कहि (saying again and again) / मृदु बानी (soft speech) / जननीं (mothers) / सकल (all) / भरत (Bharat) / सनमानी (honoured) / भाइहि (to brother) / सौंपि (entrusting) / मातु (mothers') / सेवकाई (service) / आपु (himself) / निषादहि (to the Nishad) / लीन्ह (took) / बोलाई (calling)
ramacharitamanas::2942.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2942.essence: True respect is shown by quietly taking care of everyone present.
ramacharitamanas::2942.simple_meaning: Bharat shows respect to the mothers, assigns Shatrughna to care for them, and calls the Nishad chief to him.
ramacharitamanas::2942.simple_insight: Real leadership notices everyone, serves quietly, and puts the right people in the right place.
ramacharitamanas::2942.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is traveling with his family and companions after the painful break with Ayodhya. Even in grief, he bows to the mothers, speaks gently, assigns Shatrughna to their care, and calls the Nishad leader forward. The verse shows his humility and orderliness.
ramacharitamanas::2942.modern_relevance: At a family gathering after a funeral, you notice the elders sitting alone and quietly make sure someone stays with them. That small act reveals character more than any speech.
ramacharitamanas::2942.insight: It shifts attention from status to service, showing that dignity is proved by how you care for others.

ramacharitamanas::2943.verse_sanskrit: चले सखा कर सों कर जोरें। सिथिल सरीरु सनेह न थोरें॥ पूँछत सखहि सो ठाउँ देखाऊ। नेकु नयन मन जरनि जुड़ाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2943.verse_hindi: सखा निषाद राज के हाथ से हाथ मिलाए हुए भरतजी चले। प्रेम कुछ थोड़ा नहीं है (अर्थात बहुत अधिक प्रेम है), जिससे उनका शरीर शिथिल हो रहा है। भरतजी सखा से पूछते हैं कि मुझे वह स्थान दिखलाओ और नेत्र और मन की जलन कुछ ठंडी करो- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2943.english_translation: Holding Nishad Raja's hand, Bharat walked on. His body was weak from love, and his love was boundless. He asked his friend to show him that place and cool the burning in his eyes and mind.
ramacharitamanas::2943.translation_literal: चले (walked) / सखा (friend) / कर सों (with hand) / कर जोरें (joined hands) / सिथिल (weak) / सरीरु (body) / सनेह (love) / न थोरें (not little, boundless)॥ / पूँछत (asking) / सखहि (to the friend) / सो ठाउँ (that place) / देखाऊ (show) / नेकु (a little) / नयन (eyes) / मन (mind) / जरनि (burning) / जुड़ाऊ (cool, soothe)॥
ramacharitamanas::2943.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2943.essence: Longing for Ram makes even the body tremble.
ramacharitamanas::2943.simple_meaning: Bharat walks with Nishad Raja, overwhelmed by love. He asks to be shown the place where Ram rested so his burning heart can be soothed.
ramacharitamanas::2943.simple_insight: Love can make the body weak and the heart ache for a place tied to someone you miss.
ramacharitamanas::2943.detailed_meaning: Bharat has reached the forest with Nishad Raja. As they walk together, his love for Ram is so intense that his body feels unsteady. He asks to be shown the very spot where Ram stayed, because longing has become almost painful.
ramacharitamanas::2943.modern_relevance: You finally arrive at the hospital room after the emergency call. The bed is empty now, but you still want to stand where they stood, just to feel close again.
ramacharitamanas::2943.insight: It shows how devotion can become physical longing, turning memory and place into a way of staying connected.

ramacharitamanas::2944.verse_sanskrit: जहँ सिय रामु लखनु निसि सोए। कहत भरे जल लोचन कोए॥ भरत बचन सुनि भयउ बिषादू। तुरत तहाँ लइ गयउ निषादू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2944.verse_hindi: जहाँ सीताजी, श्री रामजी और लक्ष्मण रात को सोए थे। ऐसा कहते ही उनके नेत्रों के कोयों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया। भरतजी के वचन सुनकर निषाद को बड़ा विषाद हुआ। वह तुरंत ही उन्हें वहाँ ले गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2944.english_translation: Where Sita, Ram, and Lakshman had slept through the night, his eyes filled with tears. Hearing Bharat's words, Nishad felt deep sorrow and quickly took him there.
ramacharitamanas::2944.translation_literal: जहँ (where) / सिय रामु लखनु (Sita, Ram, Lakshman) / निसि (at night) / सोए (slept) / कहत (saying) / भरे (filled) / जल (water/tears) / लोचन (eyes) / कोए (corners) / भरत बचन (Bharat's words) / सुनि (hearing) / भयउ (became) / बिषादू (sorrowful) / तुरत (immediately) / तहाँ (there) / लइ (taking) / गयउ (went) / निषादू (Nishad)
ramacharitamanas::2944.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2944.essence: A loved place can still bring tears after everyone has gone.
ramacharitamanas::2944.simple_meaning: Bharat is shown the place where Ram, Sita, and Lakshman slept. The memory moves everyone there into tears and sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2944.simple_insight: Love can make a place feel sacred long after everyone has gone.
ramacharitamanas::2944.detailed_meaning: Bharat has reached the forest with Nishad. When he asks to see the place where Ram, Sita, and Lakshman slept, Nishad is overwhelmed. This verse is a bridge into Bharat's reverent bow at that spot.
ramacharitamanas::2944.modern_relevance: You return to an empty room after someone you love has left it. The bed is made, but the ache remains. Even silence can carry a presence.
ramacharitamanas::2944.insight: It shifts attention from the scene itself to the devotion memory leaves behind.

ramacharitamanas::2945.verse_sanskrit: जहँ सिंसुपा पुनीत तर रघुबर किय बिश्रामु। अति सनेहँ सादर भरत कीन्हेउ दंड प्रनामु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2945.verse_hindi: जहाँ पवित्र अशोक के वृक्ष के नीचे श्री रामजी ने विश्राम किया था। भरतजी ने वहाँ अत्यन्त प्रेम से आदरपूर्वक दण्डवत प्रणाम किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2945.english_translation: At the sacred tree where Raghubar rested, Bharat bowed down in full prostration with deep love and respect.
ramacharitamanas::2945.translation_literal: जहँ (where) / सिंसुपा (the sacred tree) / पुनीत (pure, holy) / तर (tree) / रघुबर (Raghubar, Ram) / किय (did) / बिश्रामु (rest) / अति (very) / सनेहँ (with love) / सादर (respectfully) / भरत (Bharat) / कीन्हेउ (did) / दंड प्रनामु (prostrating bow)
ramacharitamanas::2945.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2945.essence: Love bows even before a place touched by the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::2945.simple_meaning: Bharat bowed fully at the place where Ram had rested, showing deep love and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2945.simple_insight: Love can become reverence so complete that even a place feels sacred.
ramacharitamanas::2945.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Bharat reaches the spot where Ram rested beneath a holy tree. Overcome with devotion and longing, he falls into full prostration there. The scene is part of his search for Ram's presence, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2945.modern_relevance: You stand in an empty room after someone you love has left, and the silence itself feels charged. Even their chair, their cup, their trace on the floor becomes something you want to honor.
ramacharitamanas::2945.insight: It shows how devotion turns ordinary places into reminders of love and absence.

ramacharitamanas::2946.verse_sanskrit: कुस साँथरी निहारि सुहाई। कीन्ह प्रनामु प्रदच्छिन जाई॥ चरन देख रज आँखिन्ह लाई। बनइ न कहत प्रीति अधिकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2946.verse_hindi: कुशों की सुंदर साथरी देखकर उसकी प्रदक्षिणा करके प्रणाम किया। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरण चिह्नों की रज आँखों में लगाई। (उस समय के) प्रेम की अधिकता कहते नहीं बनती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2946.english_translation: Seeing the lovely grass bed, he bowed and circled it in reverence. He placed the dust of Ram's feet on his eyes. The depth of that love could not be spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2946.translation_literal: कुस (grass) / साँथरी (bed) / निहारि (seeing) / सुहाई (lovely) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रनामु (bowed) / प्रदच्छिन (circumambulation) / जाई (going) / चरन (feet) / देख (seeing) / रज (dust) / आँखिन्ह (eyes) / लाई (placed) / बनइ (is able) / न (not) / कहत (saying) / प्रीति (love) / अधिकाई (greatness/excess)
ramacharitamanas::2946.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2946.essence: Deep love turns even a patch of ground into a shrine.
ramacharitamanas::2946.simple_meaning: Bharat bows to the place where Ram rested and honors even the grass there as precious. His love is so deep that words cannot contain it.
ramacharitamanas::2946.simple_insight: Real devotion makes even the smallest trace of what you love feel priceless.
ramacharitamanas::2946.detailed_meaning: Bharat has reached the forest and is standing at the exact place where Ram, Sita, and Lakshman slept. He bows, circles the spot, and presses the dust of Ram's feet to his eyes. The scene shows love so intense that language fails.
ramacharitamanas::2946.modern_relevance: You find a crumpled note, a worn scarf, or an empty chair that still feels alive with someone's presence. Love can make the smallest trace unbearable and holy at once.
ramacharitamanas::2946.insight: It trains the mind to honor signs, places, and reminders as carriers of relationship, not as ordinary objects.

ramacharitamanas::2947.verse_sanskrit: कनक बिंदु दुइ चारिक देखे। राखे सीस सीय सम लेखे॥ सजल बिलोचन हृदयँ गलानी। कहत सखा सन बचन सुबानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2947.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने दो-चार स्वर्णबिन्दु (सोने के कण या तारे आदि जो सीताजी के गहने-कपड़ों से गिर पड़े थे) देखे तो उनको सीताजी के समान समझकर सिर पर रख लिया। उनके नेत्र (प्रेमाश्रु के) जल से भरे हैं और हृदय में ग्लानि भरी है। वे सखा से सुंदर वाणी में ये वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::2947.english_translation: Seeing two or four golden specks, Bharata placed them on his head, taking them as if they were Sita herself. His eyes were wet with tears, his heart full of remorse, and he spoke to his companion with beautiful words.
ramacharitamanas::2947.translation_literal: कनक (golden) / बिंदु (specks) / दुइ चारिक (two or four) / देखे (saw) / राखे (placed) / सीस (on the head) / सीय (Sita) / सम (like) / लेखे (taking as) / सजल (moist) / बिलोचन (eyes) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / गलानी (remorse) / कहत (speaking) / सखा सन (to the companion) / बचन (words) / सुबानी (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::2947.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2947.essence: Even a trace of the beloved can fill you with longing.
ramacharitamanas::2947.simple_meaning: Bharata finds a few golden specks and reveres them as if they were Sita herself. He is weeping, ashamed, and speaking gently to his companion.
ramacharitamanas::2947.simple_insight: Love makes even a tiny trace feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::2947.detailed_meaning: Bharata is moving through the forest where Ram and Sita once stayed. He sees a few golden specks, treats them like Sita’s presence, and is overcome with tears and remorse. The scene deepens his longing before he speaks.
ramacharitamanas::2947.modern_relevance: You find a scarf, a note, or a broken bracelet that belonged to someone you miss. Your hands go still before your heart does.
ramacharitamanas::2947.insight: It trains attention to treat traces of the beloved with reverence, not possession.

ramacharitamanas::2948.verse_sanskrit: श्रीहत सीय बिरहँ दुतिहीना। जथा अवध नर नारि बिलीना॥ पिता जनक देउँ पटतर केही। करतल भोगु जोगु जग जेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::2948.verse_hindi: ये स्वर्ण के कण या तारे भी सीताजी के विरह से ऐसे श्रीहत (शोभाहीन) एवं कान्तिहीन हो रहे हैं, जैसे (राम वियोग में) अयोध्या के नर-नारी विलीन (शोक के कारण क्षीण) हो रहे हैं। जिन सीताजी के पिता राजा जनक हैं, इस जगत में भोग और योग दोनों ही जिनकी मुट्ठी में हैं, उन जनकजी को मैं किसकी उपमा दूँ? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2948.english_translation: These golden specks, dimmed by separation from Sita, look like Ayodhya's men and women, drained by grief for Ram. What comparison can I make for King Janaka, whose hands hold both enjoyment and yoga, and whose worth is beyond measure?
ramacharitamanas::2948.translation_literal: श्रीहत (dimmed / stripped of radiance) / सीय (Sita) / बिरहँ (by separation) / दुतिहीना (without brightness) / जथा (like) / अवध (Ayodhya) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / बिलीना (merged / faded away)॥ पिता (father) / जनक (Janaka) / देउँ (I give / may I give) / पटतर (equal comparison) / केही (to whom) / करतल (in the palm of the hand) / भोगु (enjoyment) / जोगु (yoga) / जग (world) / जेही (whose)
ramacharitamanas::2948.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2948.essence: Separation makes even the brightest things feel dim.
ramacharitamanas::2948.simple_meaning: Bharat says that even these golden specks have lost their shine in Sita's absence, just as Ayodhya has been dimmed by grief for Ram. He then says Janak is beyond comparison.
ramacharitamanas::2948.simple_insight: Grief changes how everything looks; even beauty feels faded when the heart is wounded.
ramacharitamanas::2948.detailed_meaning: Bharat is walking through the traces of Ram and Sita in exile. Seeing tiny golden specks, he turns them into a mirror for Ayodhya itself: both the city and these objects have lost their brightness through separation. The verse then shifts to his reverence for Janak, Sita's incomparable father.
ramacharitamanas::2948.modern_relevance: You open a drawer and find a small thing they once touched. It should feel ordinary, but it suddenly carries the weight of absence and makes the whole room feel different.
ramacharitamanas::2948.insight: It teaches you how love and loss reshape perception, making even neutral objects carry emotional charge.

ramacharitamanas::2949.verse_sanskrit: ससुर भानुकुल भानु भुआलू। जेहि सिहात अमरावतिपालू॥ प्राननाथु रघुनाथ गोसाईं। जो बड़ होत सो राम बड़ाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2949.verse_hindi: सूर्यकुल के सूर्य राजा दशरथजी जिनके ससुर हैं, जिनको अमरावती के स्वामी इन्द्र भी सिहाते थे। (ईर्षापूर्वक उनके जैसा ऐश्वर्य और प्रताप पाना चाहते थे) और प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी जिनके प्राणनाथ हैं, जो इतने बड़े हैं कि जो कोई भी बड़ा होता है, वह श्री रामचन्द्रजी की (दी हुई) बड़ाई से ही होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2949.english_translation: King Dasharath, the sun of the solar dynasty, was so glorious that even Indra envied him. Yet Ram, his lord of life, is the one whose greatness makes all greatness shine.
ramacharitamanas::2949.translation_literal: ससुर (father-in-law) / भानुकुल (solar dynasty) / भानु (sun) / भुआलू (king) / जेहि (whom) / सिहात (envied) / अमरावतिपालू (lord of Amaravati, Indra) / प्राननाथु (lord of life) / रघुनाथ (Ram, lord of Raghu) / गोसाईं (master) / जो (who) / बड़ (great) / होत (becomes) / सो (that) / राम (Ram) / बड़ाईं (greatness, praise)
ramacharitamanas::2949.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2949.essence: Every crown still rests beneath Ram's greater glory.
ramacharitamanas::2949.simple_meaning: Dasharath was so great that even Indra envied him, but Ram is greater still. Any greatness a person has comes through Ram's blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2949.simple_insight: Pride softens when you remember that every real honor is received, not owned.
ramacharitamanas::2949.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat is grieving the loss of Ram and remembering the royal house around him. He names Dasharath's splendor and then turns to the deeper truth: even the highest worldly greatness is small beside Ram, whose grace makes greatness possible.
ramacharitamanas::2949.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the applause, the title — and then one quiet moment reminds you it all came through forces beyond your control. This verse keeps the ego from hardening.
ramacharitamanas::2949.insight: It shifts attention from personal achievement to the source that makes achievement possible.

ramacharitamanas::2950.verse_sanskrit: पति देवता सुतीय मनि सीय साँथरी देखि। बिहरत हृदउ न हहरि हर पबि तें कठिन बिसेषि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2950.verse_hindi: उन श्रेष्ठ पतिव्रता स्त्रियों में शिरोमणि सीताजी की साथरी (कुश शय्या) देखकर मेरा हृदय हहराकर (दहलकर) फट नहीं जाता, हे शंकर! यह वज्र से भी अधिक कठोर है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::2950.english_translation: Seeing Sita's grass bed, the jewel among devoted wives, my heart does not burst. Shiva, this is harder than a thunderbolt.
ramacharitamanas::2950.translation_literal: पति (husband) / देवता (deity) / सुतीय (of devoted wives) / मनि (jewel) / सीय (Sita) / साँथरी (bed of grass) / देखि (seeing) / बिहरत (while moving) / हृदउ (heart) / न हहरि (does not burst) / हर (Shiva) / पबि (thunderbolt) / तें (than) / कठिन (harder) / बिसेषि (especially)
ramacharitamanas::2950.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2950.essence: Tender suffering can feel harder than any blow.
ramacharitamanas::2950.simple_meaning: Seeing Sita lying on a bed of grass, the speaker is overwhelmed by how unbearably harsh her suffering is.
ramacharitamanas::2950.simple_insight: Some pain is so pure and so unfair that it leaves you stunned instead of speaking.
ramacharitamanas::2950.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the exile has begun and Sita is enduring hardship beside Ram. The poet looks at her simple grass bed and feels that his heart should break from the sight. The verse heightens the grief before the next emotional turn.
ramacharitamanas::2950.modern_relevance: You walk past a child sleeping on a thin mat in a crowded station and feel your chest tighten. Some scenes do not ask for explanation; they ask you to feel the weight of them.
ramacharitamanas::2950.insight: It trains the mind to notice suffering directly instead of looking away or numbing it.

ramacharitamanas::2951.verse_sanskrit: लालन जोगु लखन लघु लोने। भे न भाइ अस अहहिं न होने॥ पुरजन प्रिय पितु मातु दुलारे। सिय रघुबीरहि प्रानपिआरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2951.verse_hindi: मेरे छोटे भाई लक्ष्मण बहुत ही सुंदर और प्यार करने योग्य हैं। ऐसे भाई न तो किसी के हुए, न हैं, न होने के ही हैं। जो लक्ष्मण अवध के लोगों को प्यारे, माता-पिता के दुलारे और श्री सीता-रामजी के प्राण प्यारे हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::2951.english_translation: My dear younger brother Lakshman is so lovely and worthy of love. No brother like him has ever been, is now, or will ever be. He is beloved by the people of Ayodhya, cherished by his parents, and dear as life to Sita and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2951.translation_literal: लालन जोगु (worthy of being cherished) / लखन (Lakshman) / लघु (little/younger) / लोने (lovely) / भे (were) / न (not) / भाइ (brother) / अस (like this) / अहहिं (are) / न (not) / होने (to be) / पुरजन (townspeople) / प्रिय (dear) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / दुलारे (beloved) / सिय (Sita) / रघुबीरहि (to Ram) / प्रानपिआरे (dear as life)
ramacharitamanas::2951.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2951.essence: True loveliness is being dear to everyone without needing to announce yourself.
ramacharitamanas::2951.simple_meaning: Lakshman is described as the kind of brother everyone loves — by the people, by his parents, and by Sita and Ram themselves.
ramacharitamanas::2951.simple_insight: There is deep peace in being the kind of person others naturally trust and cherish.
