ramacharitamanas::2951.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the poet pauses to praise Lakshman before the grief of exile deepens. He is not just Ram's younger brother; he is the beloved of the whole household, a rare presence whose goodness is felt by everyone around him.
ramacharitamanas::2951.modern_relevance: At a family gathering, one person quietly helps with the food, checks on the elders, and makes the children laugh. Nobody has to ask. That is the kind of presence this verse honors.
ramacharitamanas::2951.insight: It shifts attention from status to character: being cherished comes from how you live, not from what you claim.

ramacharitamanas::2952.verse_sanskrit: मृदु मूरति सुकुमार सुभाऊ। तात बाउ तन लाग न काउ॥ ते बन सहहिं बिपति सब भाँती। निदरे कोटि कुलिस एहिं छाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2952.verse_hindi: जिनकी कोमल मूर्ति और सुकुमार स्वभाव है, जिनके शरीर में कभी गरम हवा भी नहीं लगी, वे वन में सब प्रकार की विपत्तियाँ सह रहे हैं। (हाय!) इस मेरी छाती ने (कठोरता में) करोड़ों वज्रों का भी निरादर कर दिया (नहीं तो यह कभी की फट गई होती) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2952.english_translation: Those who are tender in form and gentle by nature are enduring every hardship in the forest. My heart has become so hard that it has not shattered even under millions of thunderbolts.
ramacharitamanas::2952.translation_literal: मृदु (soft) / मूरति (form) / सुकुमार (delicate) / सुभाऊ (nature) / तात (dear) / बाउ (hot wind) / तन (body) / लाग (touched) / न (not) / काउ (any) / ते (they) / बन (forest) / सहहिं (endure) / बिपति (hardship) / सब (all) / भाँती (kinds) / निदरे (disregarded) / कोटि (crores) / कुलिस (thunderbolts) / एहिं (this) / छाती (chest)
ramacharitamanas::2952.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2952.essence: Tenderness and hardship should never have met like this.
ramacharitamanas::2952.simple_meaning: Beautiful, delicate people are bearing the forest's pain, while the speaker feels his own heart has turned harder than thunderbolts.
ramacharitamanas::2952.simple_insight: Love can hurt so deeply that even grief begins to feel like endurance.
ramacharitamanas::2952.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the exile has already begun. Ram, Sita, and Lakshman have gone into the forest, and the speaker looks at their gentle bodies and cannot bear the contrast with their suffering. The verse is a cry of pain, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2952.modern_relevance: You watch someone kind and unprotected keep carrying a burden they never deserved. Your chest tightens because their softness makes the hardship feel unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::2952.insight: It captures the ache of witnessing innocent suffering and the numbness grief can create.

ramacharitamanas::2953.verse_sanskrit: राम जनमि जगु कीन्ह उजागर। रूप सील सुख सब गुन सागर॥ पुरजन परिजन गुरु पितु माता। राम सुभाउ सबहि सुखदाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2953.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी ने जन्म (अवतार) लेकर जगत् को प्रकाशित (परम सुशोभित) कर दिया। वे रूप, शील, सुख और समस्त गुणों के समुद्र हैं। पुरवासी, कुटुम्बी, गुरु, पिता-माता सभी को श्री रामजी का स्वभाव सुख देने वाला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2953.english_translation: By being born, Ram made the world radiant. He is an ocean of beauty, character, joy, and every virtue. For the people of the city, his relatives, the teacher, father, and mother, Ram's nature gives delight to all.
ramacharitamanas::2953.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / जनमि (having been born) / जगु (the world) / कीन्ह (made) / उजागर (bright, radiant) / रूप (beauty, form) / सील (character, gentleness) / सुख (joy) / सब (all) / गुन (virtues) / सागर (ocean) / पुरजन (city people) / परिजन (relatives) / गुरु (teacher) / पितु (father) / माता (mother) / राम (Ram) / सुभाउ (nature) / सबहि (to all) / सुखदाता (giver of joy)
ramacharitamanas::2953.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2953.essence: Ram's presence itself is a gift to everyone around him.
ramacharitamanas::2953.simple_meaning: Ram's birth makes the world shine. His beauty, character, joy, and virtues delight everyone around him.
ramacharitamanas::2953.simple_insight: Real greatness doesn't demand attention; it naturally brings warmth to everyone nearby.
ramacharitamanas::2953.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the people closest to Ram are already feeling the effect of his arrival. Tulsidas pauses the exile story to say that Ram's very nature lights up a home, a city, and every relationship around him.
ramacharitamanas::2953.modern_relevance: A quiet person walks into a tense family gathering, and the room softens before anyone speaks. Some people don't need to announce their goodness — their presence itself changes the atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::2953.insight: It shifts attention from achievement to character: the highest presence is the one that quietly blesses others.

ramacharitamanas::2954.verse_sanskrit: बैरिउ राम बड़ाई करहीं। बोलनि मिलनि बिनय मन हरहीं॥ सारद कोटि कोटि सत सेषा। करि न सकहिं प्रभु गुन गन लेखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2954.verse_hindi: शत्रु भी श्री रामजी की बड़ाई करते हैं। बोल-चाल, मिलने के ढंग और विनय से वे मन को हर लेते हैं। करोड़ों सरस्वती और अरबों शेषजी भी प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी के गुण समूहों की गिनती नहीं कर सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::2954.english_translation: Even enemies praise Ram. His speech, meeting, and humility captivate the heart. Crores of Saraswati and Shesh cannot count the host of Lord Ram's virtues.
ramacharitamanas::2954.translation_literal: बैरिउ (even enemies) / राम (Ram) / बड़ाई (praise) / करहीं (do) / बोलनि (speech) / मिलनि (meeting) / बिनय (humility) / मन (mind/heart) / हरहीं (captivate) / सारद (Saraswati) / कोटि कोटि (crores upon crores) / सत (hundreds) / सेषा (Shesha) / करि न सकहिं (cannot do) / प्रभु (Lord) / गुन गन (groups of virtues) / लेखा (counting)
ramacharitamanas::2954.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2954.essence: Ram’s humility is so complete that even enemies are moved by it.
ramacharitamanas::2954.simple_meaning: Ram's character is so graceful that even enemies admire him. His speech, manners, and humility win hearts, and no one can fully count his virtues.
ramacharitamanas::2954.simple_insight: Real greatness does not need self-promotion; it quietly changes how others feel around you.
ramacharitamanas::2954.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the poem pauses to praise Ram before the exile's pain deepens. Even those opposed to him are drawn to his humility, and the poet says his virtues are beyond counting. This is the portrait of a man whose presence itself teaches devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2954.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense family gathering, and the person everyone expected to argue simply listens well, speaks gently, and lowers the temperature in the room. That kind of presence changes people before any explanation does.
ramacharitamanas::2954.insight: It shifts attention from proving yourself to embodying qualities that naturally earn trust and admiration.

ramacharitamanas::2955.verse_sanskrit: सुखस्वरूप रघुबंसमनि मंगल मोद निधान। ते सोवत कुस डासि महि बिधि गति अति बलवान ॥
ramacharitamanas::2955.verse_hindi: जो सुख स्वरूप रघुवंश शिरोमणि श्री रामचंद्रजी मंगल और आनंद के भंडार हैं, वे पृथ्वी पर कुशा बिछाकर सोते हैं। विधाता की गति बड़ी ही बलवान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2955.english_translation: The joy-filled jewel of Raghu's line, the source of auspiciousness and delight, lies on kusa grass on the ground. Such is the mighty course of fate.
ramacharitamanas::2955.translation_literal: सुखस्वरूप (embodiment of happiness) / रघुबंसमनि (jewel of the Raghu line) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मोद (joy) / निधान (treasure) / ते (they) / सोवत (sleeping) / कुस (kusa grass) / डासि (spread) / महि (on the earth) / बिधि (fate) / गति (course) / अति (very) / बलवान (powerful)
ramacharitamanas::2955.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2955.essence: Even the beloved can be made to sleep on the ground.
ramacharitamanas::2955.simple_meaning: Ram, the source of joy and blessing, is sleeping on kusa grass on the ground. The poet points to how powerful fate can be.
ramacharitamanas::2955.simple_insight: Even the most radiant life can be brought low by circumstances beyond control.
ramacharitamanas::2955.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace has turned into a wound. Ram, the delight of the Raghu line, is now lying on kusa grass instead of a royal bed. Tulsidas pauses on this shocking contrast to show how powerfully fate has overturned Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::2955.modern_relevance: You watch someone who should have been protected sleeping on a hard floor after everything has fallen apart. The image lands because it feels unfair, and because life can change that fast.
ramacharitamanas::2955.insight: It trains the mind to see how quickly status, comfort, and security can be stripped away.

ramacharitamanas::2956.verse_sanskrit: राम सुना दुखु कान न काऊ। जीवनतरु जिमि जोगवइ राउ॥ पलक नयन फनि मनि जेहि भाँती। जोगवहिं जननि सकल दिन राती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2956.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी ने कानों से भी कभी दुःख का नाम नहीं सुना। महाराज स्वयं जीवन वृक्ष की तरह उनकी सार-सँभाल किया करते थे। सब माताएँ भी रात-दिन उनकी ऐसी सार-सँभाल करती थीं, जैसे पलक नेत्रों और साँप अपनी मणि की करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2956.english_translation: Ram had never even heard the word sorrow. The king cared for him like a tree of life. All the mothers protected him day and night like an eyelid guards the eye and a snake guards its jewel.
ramacharitamanas::2956.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सुना (heard) / दुखु (sorrow) / कान (ear) / न (not) / काऊ (anyone's) । जीवनतरु (tree of life) / जिमि (like) / जोगवइ (tends, cares for) / राउ (king) ॥ पलक (eyelid) / नयन (eye) / फनि (snake) / मनि (jewel) / जेहि भाँती (in the way that) । जोगवहिं (they guard) / जननि (mothers) / सकल (all) / दिन राती (day and night) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2956.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2956.essence: Leaving home means losing the world that held you without effort.
ramacharitamanas::2956.simple_meaning: Ram grew up so protected and cherished that sorrow had never touched him. Dasharath and the queens guarded him constantly, with the same instinctive care as an eyelid protects an eye.
ramacharitamanas::2956.simple_insight: Love can be so complete that it feels like being held inside safety itself.
ramacharitamanas::2956.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas pauses before the exile to show what Ram is leaving behind. Ram has known only care, not grief: Dasharath tends him like a living treasure, and the queens guard him through every hour. That makes the coming loss feel even sharper.
ramacharitamanas::2956.modern_relevance: You remember the house where every small need was anticipated before you asked. Leaving that kind of care behind is not just travel — it is heartbreak.
ramacharitamanas::2956.insight: It frames exile as a rupture from total protection, not just a change of place.

ramacharitamanas::2957.verse_sanskrit: ते अब फिरत बिपिन पदचारी। कंद मूल फल फूल अहारी॥ धिग कैकई अमंगल मूला। भइसि प्रान प्रियतम प्रतिकूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::2957.verse_hindi: वही श्री रामचंद्रजी अब जंगलों में पैदल फिरते हैं और कंद-मूल तथा फल-फूलों का भोजन करते हैं। अमंगल की मूल कैकेयी धिक्कार है, जो अपने प्राणप्रियतम पति से भी प्रतिकूल हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2957.english_translation: Now Ram wanders on foot through the forest, living on roots, fruits, and flowers. Shame on Kaikeyi, the root of all inauspiciousness, who turned against her own beloved husband.
ramacharitamanas::2957.translation_literal: ते (those) / अब (now) / फिरत (wandering) / बिपिन (forest) / पदचारी (on foot) / कंद (roots/tubers) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruits) / फूल (flowers) / अहारी (eating) / धिग (shame on) / कैकई (Kaikeyi) / अमंगल (inauspiciousness) / मूला (root) / भइसि (became) / प्रान (life) / प्रियतम (beloved) / प्रतिकूला (opposed)
ramacharitamanas::2957.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2957.essence: Exile begins when loyalty turns against love.
ramacharitamanas::2957.simple_meaning: Ram is now walking through the forest and eating simple forest food because Kaikeyi's actions turned him away from home and into exile.
ramacharitamanas::2957.simple_insight: A single broken promise can send an entire life into exile.
ramacharitamanas::2957.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram has already left Ayodhya. The palace has become memory, and the forest is now his path. The verse contrasts his noble life with the harsh result of Kaikeyi's demand, blaming her for the rupture that forced him away from his beloved home and family.
ramacharitamanas::2957.modern_relevance: You pack a small bag and leave the house after one argument that changes everything. The room is still standing, but the life you knew is not. This verse carries that ache of irreversible fracture.
ramacharitamanas::2957.insight: It shifts attention from the journey itself to the human cost of broken loyalty.

ramacharitamanas::2958.verse_sanskrit: मैं धिग धिग अघ उदधि अभागी। सबु उतपातु भयउ जेहि लागी॥ कुल कलंकु करि सृजेउ बिधाताँ। साइँदोह मोहि कीन्ह कुमाताँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2958.verse_hindi: मुझे पापों के समुद्र और अभागे को धिक्कार है, धिक्कार है, जिसके कारण ये सब उत्पात हुए। विधाता ने मुझे कुल का कलंक बनाकर पैदा किया और कुमाता ने मुझे स्वामी द्रोही बना दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2958.english_translation: Wretched am I, a sea of sin—wretched, wretched! All this upheaval has come because of me. The creator made me a stain on my family line, and my wicked mind made me betray my own lord.
ramacharitamanas::2958.translation_literal: मैं (I) / धिग धिग (shame, shame) / अघ (sin) / उदधि (ocean) / अभागी (unfortunate one) / सबु (all) / उतपातु (upheaval) / भयउ (happened) / जेहि (because of whom) / लागी (for) ॥ / कुल (family line) / कलंकु (stain) / करि (having made) / सृजेउ (created) / बिधाताँ (the creator) / साइँदोह (betrayer of the lord) / मोहि (me) / कीन्ह (made) / कुमाताँ (wicked mind / evil intent) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2958.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::2958.essence: Remorse can make one mistake feel like your whole identity.
ramacharitamanas::2958.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is overwhelmed by guilt. She sees herself as the cause of the disaster, a stain on her family, and a traitor to her own lord.
ramacharitamanas::2958.simple_insight: Guilt can become so heavy that you see yourself only as the damage you caused.
ramacharitamanas::2958.detailed_meaning: After Ram is sent into exile, Kaikeyi collapses into remorse. She blames herself for every crisis, calling herself cursed, dishonoured, and disloyal. This is not a teaching verse on its own; it deepens the grief already unfolding in Ayodhyakand.
ramacharitamanas::2958.modern_relevance: You replay one terrible choice at 2 a.m. and start calling yourself the mistake. The mind turns one action into your whole identity.
ramacharitamanas::2958.insight: It shows how remorse can spiral into self-condemnation instead of repair.

ramacharitamanas::2959.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सप्रेम समुझाव निषादू। नाथ करिअ कत बादि बिषादू॥ राम तुम्हहि प्रिय तुम्ह प्रिय रामहि। यह निरजोसु दोसु बिधि बामहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2959.verse_hindi: यह सुनकर निषादराज प्रेमपूर्वक समझाने लगा- हे नाथ! आप व्यर्थ विषाद किसलिए करते हैं? श्री रामचंद्रजी आपको प्यारे हैं और आप श्री रामचंद्रजी को प्यारे हैं। यही निचोड़ (निश्चित सिद्धांत) है, दोष तो प्रतिकूल विधाता को है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2959.english_translation: Hearing this, Nishad spoke with love: “Lord, why grieve needlessly? Ram loves you, and you love Ram. That is the clear truth; the fault lies with adverse fate.”
ramacharitamanas::2959.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सप्रेम (with love) / समुझाव (spoke to console) / निषादू (Nishad) / नाथ (Lord) / करिअ (do) / कत (why) / बादि (needlessly) / बिषादू (grief) ॥ / राम (Ram) / तुम्हहि (you) / प्रिय (dear) / तुम्ह (you) / प्रिय (dear) / रामहि (to Ram) / यह (this) / निरजोसु (clear / decisive) / दोसु (fault) / बिधि (fate / the ordering power) / बामहि (adverse) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2959.speaker: Nishad
ramacharitamanas::2959.essence: Love can survive even when circumstances turn harsh.
ramacharitamanas::2959.simple_meaning: Nishad tells the grieving person not to waste time in sorrow. Ram and this person love each other, so the real problem is the harsh turn of events, not their bond.
ramacharitamanas::2959.simple_insight: When love is already true, grief does not get the last word.
ramacharitamanas::2959.detailed_meaning: At the riverbank during Ram’s exile, Nishad sees grief clouding the moment and gently interrupts it. He reminds the listener that Ram and the listener are bound by mutual love, and that the real pain comes from the cruel turn of events, not from any break in their relationship.
ramacharitamanas::2959.modern_relevance: You are staring at a phone after a fight, replaying the worst part and ignoring what has not changed. Someone who truly knows you would say: the bond is still there; the hurt came from the turn, not the love.
ramacharitamanas::2959.insight: It shifts attention from self-blame and despair to the underlying relationship that still remains intact.

ramacharitamanas::2960.verse_sanskrit: बिधि बाम की करनी कठिन जेहिं मातु कीन्ही बावरी। तेहि राति पुनि पुनि करहिं प्रभु सादर सरहना रावरी॥ तुलसी न तुम्ह सो राम प्रीतमु कहतु हौं सौंहे किएँ। परिनाम मंगल जानि अपने आनिए धीरजु हिएँ॥
ramacharitamanas::2960.verse_hindi: प्रतिकूल विधाता की करनी बड़ी कठोर है, जिसने माता कैकेयी को बावली बना दिया (उसकी मति फेर दी)। उस रात को प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी बार-बार आदरपूर्वक आपकी बड़ी सराहना करते थे। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- (निषादराज कहता है कि-) श्री रामचंद्रजी को आपके समान अतिशय प्रिय और कोई नहीं है, मैं सौगंध खाकर कहता हूँ। परिणाम में मंगल होगा, यह जानकर आप अपने हृदय में धैर्य धारण कीजिए।
ramacharitamanas::2960.english_translation: The harsh working of fate turned Kaikeyi’s mind. That night, Lord Ram again and again praised you with respect. Tulsidas says: I swear there is no one dearer to Ram than you. Knowing the end will be auspicious, keep courage in your heart.
ramacharitamanas::2960.translation_literal: बिधि (fate) / बाम (adverse) / की करनी (the doing) / कठिन (harsh) / जेहिं (by which) / मातु (mother) / कीन्ही (made) / बावरी (mad) / तेहि (that) / राति (night) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / करहिं (did) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सादर (with respect) / सरहना (praise) / रावरी (of you) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / न (not) / तुम्ह (you) / सो (like) / राम (Ram) / प्रीतमु (beloved) / कहतु (I say) / हौं (I am) / सौंहे किएँ (by oath) / परिनाम (end result) / मंगल (auspicious) / जानि (knowing) / अपने (your own) / आनिए (bring) / धीरजु (patience) / हिएँ (in heart)
ramacharitamanas::2960.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2960.essence: What looks cruel now can still end in blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2960.simple_meaning: Even though Kaikeyi’s actions caused great pain, this verse says Ram still spoke of her with respect, and the result of all this will ultimately be good. So Bharat is urged to stay steady.
ramacharitamanas::2960.simple_insight: You can face a painful moment without losing faith that it can still lead somewhere good.
ramacharitamanas::2960.detailed_meaning: Bharat is drowning in grief after hearing of Ram’s exile and Dasharath’s ruin. Nisadraj tries to steady him by reminding him that Kaikeyi’s act, however harsh, does not erase Ram’s affection or the larger good still to come.
ramacharitamanas::2960.modern_relevance: You’re sitting in a hospital corridor after a family decision has gone badly, and everyone is blaming someone. This verse asks you to breathe, remember that love can survive damage, and not collapse before the outcome is known.
ramacharitamanas::2960.insight: It shifts you from reacting to the wound toward holding steady until the larger result becomes clear.

ramacharitamanas::2961.verse_sanskrit: अंतरजामी रामु सकुच सप्रेम कृपायतन। चलिअ करिअ बिश्रामु यह बिचारि दृढ़ आनि मन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2961.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी अंतर्यामी तथा संकोच, प्रेम और कृपा के धाम हैं, यह विचार कर और मन में दृढ़ता लाकर चलिए और विश्राम कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2961.english_translation: Knowing that Ram is all-knowing, gentle, and a home of grace, go on and rest, holding this firmly in your mind.
ramacharitamanas::2961.translation_literal: अंतरजामी (all-knowing within) / रामु (Ram) / सकुच (with modest gentleness) / सप्रेम (with love) / कृपायतन (abode of grace) / चलिअ (let us go) / करिअ (let us do) / बिश्रामु (rest) / यह (this) / बिचारि (thinking) / दृढ़ (firm) / आनि (bringing) / मन (mind)
ramacharitamanas::2961.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2961.essence: Knowing Ram’s gentle awareness lets you finally rest.
ramacharitamanas::2961.simple_meaning: Put your mind at ease and rest, because Ram is inwardly aware, gentle, loving, and full of grace.
ramacharitamanas::2961.simple_insight: You do not have to force clarity when you are already held with care.
ramacharitamanas::2961.detailed_meaning: Bharat is being urged to stop his grief-stricken wandering and rest. The speaker reminds him that Ram is inwardly aware, tender, and gracious, so Bharat can let his mind settle instead of agonizing further.
ramacharitamanas::2961.modern_relevance: After a long night of replaying a conversation, you finally notice your phone is still in your hand and your shoulders are locked. The verse says you can unclench — the one you love is not absent from your heart.
ramacharitamanas::2961.insight: It shifts the mind from anxious striving to settled trust in Ram’s awareness and care.

ramacharitamanas::2962.verse_sanskrit: सखा बचन सुनि उर धरि धीरा। बास चले सुमिरत रघुबीरा॥ यह सुधि पाइ नगर नर नारी। चले बिलोकन आरत भारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2962.verse_hindi: सखा के वचन सुनकर, हृदय में धीरज धरकर श्री रामचंद्रजी का स्मरण करते हुए भरतजी डेरे को चले। नगर के सारे स्त्री-पुरुष यह (श्री रामजी के ठहरने के स्थान का) समाचार पाकर बड़े आतुर होकर उस स्थान को देखने चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::2962.english_translation: Hearing his friend’s words, Bharat steadied his heart and walked to Rama’s resting place, remembering the Lord of Raghu. When the people of the city heard the news, men and women hurried out in great distress to see that place.
ramacharitamanas::2962.translation_literal: सखा (friend) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / उर (heart) / धरि (holding) / धीरा (steadiness) / बास (lodging/resting place) / चले (went) / सुमिरत (remembering) / रघुबीरा (Lord of Raghu) / यह (this) / सुधि (news) / पाइ (having received) / नगर (city) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / चले (went) / बिलोकन (to see) / आरत (distressed) / भारी (greatly)
ramacharitamanas::2962.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2962.essence: Love turns a resting place into a destination for grieving hearts.
ramacharitamanas::2962.simple_meaning: Bharat hears his friend, gathers himself, and goes to Rama’s resting place while remembering Rama. News spreads through the city, and everyone rushes out in deep distress to see the place.
ramacharitamanas::2962.simple_insight: Grief can move a whole city when someone beloved is absent.
ramacharitamanas::2962.detailed_meaning: Bharat has just been steadied by a friend’s words and walks toward Rama’s camp, holding Rama in mind. The news reaches Ayodhya, and men and women alike pour out in sorrow to see the place where Rama is staying.
ramacharitamanas::2962.modern_relevance: You hear the address of the hospital room where someone you love is waiting, and your chest tightens before you even arrive. Grief turns a location into a magnet.
ramacharitamanas::2962.insight: It shows how love makes a place sacred and pulls an entire community toward shared feeling.

ramacharitamanas::2963.verse_sanskrit: परदखिना करि करहिं प्रनामा। देहिं कैकइहि खोरि निकामा। भरि भरि बारि बिलोचन लेंहीं। बाम बिधातहि दूषन देहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2963.verse_hindi: वे उस स्थान की परिक्रमा करके प्रणाम करते हैं और कैकेयी को बहुत दोष देते हैं। नेत्रों में जल भर-भर लेते हैं और प्रतिकूल विधाता को दूषण देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2963.english_translation: They circle the place and bow down, while blaming Kaikeyi bitterly. Tears fill their eyes again and again, and they curse fate itself.
ramacharitamanas::2963.translation_literal: परदखिना (circumambulation) / करि (having done) / करहिं (they do) / प्रनामा (bowing) / देहिं (they give) / कैकइहि (to Kaikeyi) / खोरि (blame) / निकामा (severe) / भरि भरि (again and again, full) / बारि (water) / बिलोचन (eyes) / लेंहीं (they take) / बाम (adverse) / बिधातहि (to fate) / दूषन (blame) / देहीं (they give)
ramacharitamanas::2963.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2963.essence: Grief makes people bow to what they cannot repair.
ramacharitamanas::2963.simple_meaning: People circle the spot where Bharat passed, bow to it, cry over Kaikeyi's role, and blame the cruel hand of fate.
ramacharitamanas::2963.simple_insight: Grief can turn a place into a shrine, and blame into a way of mourning what cannot be undone.
ramacharitamanas::2963.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Bharat leaves, the townspeople gather around the place he walked. They bow there as if honoring his devotion, weep over Kaikeyi's decision, and lash out at fate. The verse is part of the city's shared grief, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::2963.modern_relevance: You stand outside a house after a family split, staring at the steps where everything changed. People keep retelling the same wound, trying to make sense of what no one can reverse.
ramacharitamanas::2963.insight: It shows how collective sorrow fixes on symbols, turning memory into ritual and pain into accusation.

ramacharitamanas::2964.verse_sanskrit: एक सराहहिं भरत सनेहू। कोउ कह नृपति निबाहेउ नेहू॥ निंदहिं आपु सराहि निषादहि। को कहि सकइ बिमोह बिषादहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::2964.verse_hindi: कोई भरतजी के स्नेह की सराहना करते हैं और कोई कहते हैं कि राजा ने अपना प्रेम खूब निबाहा। सब अपनी निंदा करके निषाद की प्रशंसा करते हैं। उस समय के विमोह और विषाद को कौन कह सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::2964.english_translation: Some praised Bharata's love, and some said the king had kept his love well. All blamed themselves and praised Nishada. Who can describe the confusion and grief then?
ramacharitamanas::2964.translation_literal: एक (some) / सराहहिं (praise) / भरत (Bharata) / सनेहू (love) / कोउ (someone) / कह (says) / नृपति (the king) / निबाहेउ (kept/fulfilled) / नेहू (affection) / निंदहिं (blame) / आपु (themselves) / सराहि (praising) / निषादहि (Nishada) / दि (and) / को (who) / कहि (say) / सकइ (can) / बिमोह (confusion) / बिषादहि (grief)
ramacharitamanas::2964.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2964.essence: Grief makes everyone speak from the wound, not from clarity.
ramacharitamanas::2964.simple_meaning: People are overwhelmed by grief and confusion. They praise Bharata, praise the king's love, blame themselves, and praise Nishada, but no one can fully explain the sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2964.simple_insight: When grief is deep, people speak in fragments. Everyone feels responsible, and no one can make the pain neat.
ramacharitamanas::2964.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Bharata's arrival and the spreading sorrow of Ram's exile, the crowd is emotionally unsteady. Some admire Bharata's devotion, some honor the king's love, and some even praise Nishada's role. The verse captures a city too shaken to think clearly.
ramacharitamanas::2964.modern_relevance: A family group chat after a funeral starts filling with apologies, praise, blame, and memories. Everyone means well, but the room is full of grief no one can organize.
ramacharitamanas::2964.insight: It shows how sorrow scatters judgment, turning even praise and blame into signs of the same wound.

ramacharitamanas::2965.verse_sanskrit: ऐहि बिधि राति लोगु सबु जागा। भा भिनुसार गुदारा लागा॥ गुरहि सुनावँ चढ़ाइ सुहाईं। नईं नाव सब मातु चढ़ाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2965.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार रातभर सब लोग जागते रहे। सबेरा होते ही खेवा लगा। सुंदर नाव पर गुरुजी को चढ़ाकर फिर नई नाव पर सब माताओं को चढ़ाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2965.english_translation: In this way, everyone stayed awake through the night. At dawn, the crossing began. The teacher was put onto the fine boat, and all the mothers were placed onto a new boat.
ramacharitamanas::2965.translation_literal: ऐहि बिधि (in this way) / राति (night) / लोगु (people) / सबु (all) / जागा (stayed awake) / भा (became) / भिनुसार (dawn) / गुदारा (crossing) / लागा (began) / गुरहि (the teacher) / सुनावँ (to place aboard) / चढ़ाइ (having lifted) / सुहाईं (beautiful) / नईं (new) / नाव (boat) / सब (all) / मातु (mothers) / चढ़ाईं (were placed aboard)
ramacharitamanas::2965.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2965.essence: Care is shown by how carefully you get everyone across.
ramacharitamanas::2965.simple_meaning: Everyone stayed awake all night, and at dawn the river crossing began. The teacher was placed on one boat, and the mothers were placed on another.
ramacharitamanas::2965.simple_insight: Some moments are only about getting everyone safely across.
ramacharitamanas::2965.detailed_meaning: After the grief and praise at the riverbank, the night passes in wakeful waiting. At dawn, Bharat’s party begins the crossing, carefully placing the teacher on one boat and the mothers on another. The verse moves the story forward, showing preparation rather than reflection.
ramacharitamanas::2965.modern_relevance: You pack the car before sunrise, checking seats, bags, and who needs help getting in. The day is not about meaning yet — just careful movement, one person safely at a time.
ramacharitamanas::2965.insight: It shifts attention from emotion to orderly action, showing how care becomes practical.

ramacharitamanas::2966.verse_sanskrit: दंड चारि महँ भा सबु पारा। उतरि भरत तब सबहि सँभारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2966.verse_hindi: चार घड़ी में सब गंगाजी के पार उतर गए। तब भरतजी ने उतरकर सबको सँभाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::2966.english_translation: In four watches, everyone crossed over. Then Bharat got down and gathered everyone together.
ramacharitamanas::2966.translation_literal: दंड चारि (four watches) / महँ (in) / भा (became) / सबु (all) / पारा (across) / उतरि (having descended) / भरत (Bharat) / तब (then) / सबहि (everyone) / सँभारा (gathered, took care of)
ramacharitamanas::2966.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2966.essence: Crossing is only half the work; Bharat’s care completes the journey.
ramacharitamanas::2966.simple_meaning: Everyone crossed the river in a short time, and Bharat stepped in to gather and support the group.
ramacharitamanas::2966.simple_insight: True leadership shows up after the crossing, when everyone still needs care.
ramacharitamanas::2966.detailed_meaning: After the night crossing of the Ganga, the whole company reaches the far bank. Bharat steps down from the boat and immediately takes charge, making sure everyone is settled and safe. The verse is a small narrative bridge, not a teaching in itself.
ramacharitamanas::2966.modern_relevance: You finally get everyone through the airport at midnight, bags scattered and children half-asleep. The real work begins after arrival, when someone has to steady the group.
ramacharitamanas::2966.insight: It shifts attention from the feat itself to the quiet responsibility that follows it.

ramacharitamanas::2967.verse_sanskrit: प्रातक्रिया करि मातु पद बंदि गुरहि सिरु नाइ। आगें किए निषाद गन दीन्हेउ कटकु चलाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2967.verse_hindi: प्रातःकाल की क्रियाओं को करके माता के चरणों की वंदना कर और गुरुजी को सिर नवाकर भरतजी ने विषाद गणों को (रास्ता दिखलाने के लिए) आगे कर लिया और सेना चला दी ॥141॥
ramacharitamanas::2967.english_translation: After completing his morning duties, Bharata bowed at his mother's feet and to the teacher, then placed the Nishadas in front and set the retinue in motion.
ramacharitamanas::2967.translation_literal: प्रातक्रिया (morning duties) / करि (having done) / मातु (mother's) / पद (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / गुरहि (to the teacher) / सिरु (head) / नाइ (bowing) / आगें (in front) / किए (made) / निषाद गन (Nishada groups) / दीन्हेउ (he placed) / कटकु (retinue/army) / चलाइ (setting in motion)
ramacharitamanas::2967.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2967.essence: Humility leads the march before authority does.
ramacharitamanas::2967.simple_meaning: Bharata finishes his morning rites, honors his mother and teacher, places the Nishadas ahead, and moves the group onward.
ramacharitamanas::2967.simple_insight: True leadership begins with humility, not self-importance.
ramacharitamanas::2967.detailed_meaning: After crossing the river, Bharata does not rush ahead like a conqueror. He first completes his morning duties, bows to his mother and teacher, then organizes the Nishadas to lead the way as the whole group continues forward.
ramacharitamanas::2967.modern_relevance: You step out of a temple after prayer, then quietly make sure everyone in your family gets home safely. Respect comes first; then responsibility.
ramacharitamanas::2967.insight: It shows leadership as ordered humility: honor what is above you, then guide those who follow.

ramacharitamanas::2968.verse_sanskrit: कियउ निषादनाथु अगुआईं। मातु पालकीं सकल चलाईं॥ साथ बोलाइ भाइ लघु दीन्हा। बिप्रन्ह सहित गवनु गुर कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2968.verse_hindi: निषादराज को आगे करके पीछे सब माताओं की पालकियाँ चलाईं। छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्नजी को बुलाकर उनके साथ कर दिया। फिर ब्राह्मणों सहित गुरुजी ने गमन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2968.english_translation: Bharat placed Nishadraj in front, sent the mothers' palanquins onward, called his younger brother Shatrughna to go with him, and set out with the Brahmins and the guru.
ramacharitamanas::2968.translation_literal: कियउ (made) / निषादनाथु (the lord of the Nishadas) / अगुआईं (leadership, in front) / मातु (mothers) / पालकीं (palanquins) / सकल (all) / चलाईं (sent onward) / साथ (together) / बोलाइ (calling) / भाइ (brother) / लघु (younger) / दीन्हा (placed, gave) / बिप्रन्ह (with the Brahmins) / सहित (together) / गवनु (departure, going) / गुर (the guru) / कीन्हा (made, arranged)
ramacharitamanas::2968.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2968.essence: Leadership begins by placing others where they can move safely.
ramacharitamanas::2968.simple_meaning: Bharat organizes the journey carefully: he puts Nishadraj in front, sends the mothers along, brings Shatrughna with him, and leaves with the priests and teacher.
ramacharitamanas::2968.simple_insight: True leadership looks like careful care for everyone, not just moving yourself forward.
ramacharitamanas::2968.detailed_meaning: After crossing the river, Bharat does not rush ahead alone. He arranges the whole company with respect: Nishadraj leads, the mothers travel safely in palanquins, Shatrughna stays close, and the Brahmins and guru are included in the departure. It is a scene of orderly, humble movement.
ramacharitamanas::2968.modern_relevance: You’re coordinating a family trip after a hard morning, making sure the elders are settled, the younger sibling stays close, and no one is left behind. That quiet care is Bharat’s way.
ramacharitamanas::2968.insight: It shifts attention from personal movement to responsible care for the whole group.

ramacharitamanas::2969.verse_sanskrit: आपु सुरसरिहि कीन्ह प्रनामू। सुमिरे लखन सहित सिय रामू॥ गवने भरत पयादेहिं पाए। कोतल संग जाहिं डोरिआए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2969.verse_hindi: तदनन्तर आप (भरतजी) ने गंगाजी को प्रणाम किया और लक्ष्मण सहित श्री सीता-रामजी का स्मरण किया। भरतजी पैदल ही चले। उनके साथ कोतल (बिना सवार के) घोड़े बागडोर से बँधे हुए चले जा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2969.english_translation: Then Bharata bowed to the Ganga and remembered Sita-Rama along with Lakshmana. Bharata walked on foot, while the tethered horses followed behind without riders.
ramacharitamanas::2969.translation_literal: आपु (himself) / सुरसरिहि (to the river of the gods, Ganga) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रनामू (obeisance) / सुमिरे (remembered) / लखन (Lakshmana) / सहित (along with) / सिय (Sita) / रामू (Rama) / गवने (went) / भरत (Bharata) / पयादेहिं (on foot) / पाए (having feet) / कोतल (horses without riders) / संग (with) / जाहिं (go) / डोरिआए (tied by reins)
ramacharitamanas::2969.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2969.essence: Humility walks where power would rather ride.
ramacharitamanas::2969.simple_meaning: Bharata bows to the Ganga, remembers Ram, Sita, and Lakshmana, and continues on foot while the horses follow untended.
ramacharitamanas::2969.simple_insight: True reverence shows up in how you travel, not just what you say.
ramacharitamanas::2969.detailed_meaning: Bharata is leaving Ayodhya with his family and attendants after taking the first steps of his journey. He honors the Ganga, remembers Ram, Sita, and Lakshmana, and refuses royal comfort by walking barefoot while the horses trail behind.
ramacharitamanas::2969.modern_relevance: You step out of a luxury car to walk the last stretch to a funeral, a temple, or a friend’s small apartment. The gesture says more than the ride ever could.
ramacharitamanas::2969.insight: It shifts status into service: the body follows humility, not entitlement.

ramacharitamanas::2970.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं सुसेवक बारहिं बारा। होइअ नाथ अस्व असवारा॥ रामु पयादेहि पायँ सिधाए। हम कहँ रथ गज बाजि बनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::2970.verse_hindi: उत्तम सेवक बार-बार कहते हैं कि हे नाथ! आप घोड़े पर सवार हो लीजिए। (भरतजी जवाब देते हैं कि) श्री रामचंद्रजी तो पैदल ही गए और हमारे लिए रथ, हाथी और घोड़े बनाए गए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2970.english_translation: The devoted servants keep urging him, again and again, to ride a horse. Bharat replies, "Ram walked on foot, and for us he prepared chariots, elephants, and horses."
ramacharitamanas::2970.translation_literal: कहहिं (they keep saying) / सुसेवक (good servants) / बारहिं बार (again and again) / होइअ (please become) / नाथ (lord) / अस्व (horse) / असवारा (rider) ॥ / रामु (Ram) / पयादेहि (on foot) / पायँ (by foot) / सिधाए (went) / हम कहँ (for us) / रथ (chariots) / गज (elephants) / बाजि (horses) / बनाए (made, arranged) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2970.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2970.essence: True service copies the beloved’s hardship, not your own comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2970.simple_meaning: Bharat refuses comfort because Ram accepted hardship first. He sees service as following Ram's example, not choosing ease for himself.
ramacharitamanas::2970.simple_insight: Real service often means taking less for yourself so someone else can move forward.
ramacharitamanas::2970.detailed_meaning: On the road after exile begins, Bharat is surrounded by attendants urging him to travel in comfort. He answers by remembering Ram, who walked barefoot into the forest while others were given royal transport. His choice turns service into self-denial.
ramacharitamanas::2970.modern_relevance: You’re offered the front seat after someone else has already done the hard walking. Bharat’s answer is the quiet sting of true loyalty: take less, because the one you follow took more.
ramacharitamanas::2970.insight: It shifts service from self-protection to imitation of sacrifice.

ramacharitamanas::2971.verse_sanskrit: सिर भर जाउँ उचित अस मोरा। सब तें सेवक धरमु कठोरा॥ देखि भरत गति सुनि मृदु बानी। सब सेवक गन गरहिं गलानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2971.verse_hindi: मुझे उचित तो ऐसा है कि मैं सिर के बल चलकर जाऊँ। सेवक का धर्म सबसे कठिन होता है। भरतजी की दशा देखकर और कोमल वाणी सुनकर सब सेवकगण ग्लानि के मारे गले जा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2971.english_translation: What is proper for me is to go with my head down. The duty of a servant is the hardest of all. Seeing Bharat's state and hearing his gentle words, all the servants hang their heads in shame.
ramacharitamanas::2971.translation_literal: सिर (head) / भर (only) / जाउँ (I should go) / उचित (proper) / अस (such) / मोरा (mine) / सब तें (from all) / सेवक (servant) / धरमु (duty) / कठोरा (hard)॥ / देखि (seeing) / भरत (Bharat) / गति (condition) / सुनि (hearing) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (speech) / सब (all) / सेवक (servants) / गन (group) / गरहिं (feel) / गलानी (shame) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2971.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2971.essence: True service lowers the ego before it lowers the body.
ramacharitamanas::2971.simple_meaning: Bharat feels that a true servant should be deeply humble, even to the point of bowing low. His example makes everyone serving with him feel ashamed of their own pride.
ramacharitamanas::2971.simple_insight: Humility is not weakness; it is the weight of real devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2971.detailed_meaning: On the road to Prayag, Bharat walks barefoot in grief and devotion, refusing comfort or status. His humility is so intense that the servants around him feel ashamed of their own ease. The scene turns service into a moral mirror.
ramacharitamanas::2971.modern_relevance: You show up to help, but the person you came to support is already carrying the burden better than you are. Their quiet dignity makes your own shortcuts feel small.
ramacharitamanas::2971.insight: It shifts service from performance to self-erasure, where the standard is not comfort but humility.

ramacharitamanas::2972.verse_sanskrit: भरत तीसरे पहर कहँ कीन्ह प्रबेसु प्रयाग। कहत राम सिय राम सिय उमगि उमगि अनुराग ॥
ramacharitamanas::2972.verse_hindi: प्रेम में उमँग-उमँगकर सीताराम-सीताराम कहते हुए भरतजी ने तीसरे पहर प्रयाग में प्रवेश किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2972.english_translation: In the third watch, Bharat entered Prayag, overflowing with love, calling out, "Ram, Sita, Ram, Sita."
ramacharitamanas::2972.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / तीसरे पहर (in the third watch) / कहँ (into) / कीन्ह (made) / प्रबेसु (entry) / प्रयाग (Prayag) / कहत (saying) / रामु (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / रामु (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / उमगि उमगि (surging again and again) / अनुराग (love)
ramacharitamanas::2972.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2972.essence: Repeated remembrance reveals where your heart truly lives.
ramacharitamanas::2972.simple_meaning: Bharat reached Prayag in the afternoon, repeating Ram and Sita’s names with overflowing love.
ramacharitamanas::2972.simple_insight: Love can turn even a journey into prayer.
ramacharitamanas::2972.detailed_meaning: Bharat is on the road in exile-era Ayodhya's heartbreak, walking with the weight of Ram's absence and his own refusal of the throne. As he enters Prayag in the third watch, his heart keeps spilling out Ram and Sita's names.
ramacharitamanas::2972.modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital corridor after hearing bad news, and your mind keeps repeating one name. Love does that: it makes even movement become remembrance.
ramacharitamanas::2972.insight: It shifts attention from the destination to the living presence carried in the heart.

ramacharitamanas::2973.verse_sanskrit: झलका झलकत पायन्ह कैसें। पंकज कोस ओस कन जैसें॥ भरत पयादेहिं आए आजू। भयउ दुखित सुनि सकल समाजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2973.verse_hindi: उनके चरणों में छाले कैसे चमकते हैं, जैसे कमल की कली पर ओस की बूँदें चमकती हों। भरतजी आज पैदल ही चलकर आए हैं, यह समाचार सुनकर सारा समाज दुःखी हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2973.english_translation: How beautifully the blisters on his feet shine, like dew drops on a lotus bud. Bharata has come here on foot, and hearing this, the whole assembly grew sorrowful.
ramacharitamanas::2973.translation_literal: झलका (blisters/shining marks) / झलकत (shining) / पायन्ह (on the feet) / कैसें (how) / पंकज (lotus) / कोस (bud) / ओस (dew) / कन (drops) / जैसें (like) / भरत (Bharata) / पयादेहिं (on foot) / आए (came) / आजू (today) / भयउ (became) / दुखित (sorrowful) / सुनि (hearing) / सकल (all) / समाजू (assembly)
ramacharitamanas::2973.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2973.essence: Bharata's devotion is so costly that even his feet tell the story.
ramacharitamanas::2973.simple_meaning: Bharata has walked barefoot, and the sight of his blistered feet moves everyone to sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::2973.simple_insight: True sacrifice leaves a mark that others can feel without a single explanation.
ramacharitamanas::2973.detailed_meaning: At Prayag, the people watching Bharata see the blisters on his feet and are struck by his suffering. He has chosen to walk on foot in grief and devotion, and the entire gathering is shaken by that sight.
ramacharitamanas::2973.modern_relevance: You notice the blisters after a long day of caring for someone who never asked you to stay. The pain on your feet says what your words never needed to.
ramacharitamanas::2973.insight: It turns attention to visible sacrifice and the quiet grief it awakens in others.

ramacharitamanas::2974.verse_sanskrit: खबरि लीन्ह सब लोग नहाए। कीन्ह प्रनामु त्रिबेनिहिं आए॥ सबिधि सितासित नीर नहाने। दिए दान महिसुर सनमाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::2974.verse_hindi: जब भरतजी ने यह पता पा लिया कि सब लोग स्नान कर चुके, तब त्रिवेणी पर आकर उन्हें प्रणाम किया। फिर विधिपूर्वक (गंगा-यमुना के) श्वेत और श्याम जल में स्नान किया और दान देकर ब्राह्मणों का सम्मान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::2974.english_translation: After learning that everyone had finished bathing, Bharat came to the Triveni and bowed there. Then he bathed properly in the mixed white and dark waters, gave gifts, and honoured the learned priests.
ramacharitamanas::2974.translation_literal: खबरि (news) / लीन्ह (received) / सब (all) / लोग (people) / नहाए (bathed) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रनामु (salutation) / त्रिबेनिहिं (to Triveni) / आए (came) / सबिधि (with proper method) / सितासित (white and dark) / नीर (water) / नहाने (bathed) / दिए (gave) / दान (gifts) / महिसुर (learned priests) / सनमाने (honoured)
ramacharitamanas::2974.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2974.essence: Painful journeys still call for disciplined, respectful action.
ramacharitamanas::2974.simple_meaning: Bharat arrives at the sacred confluence, bows first, bathes properly, gives charity, and shows respect to the priests.
ramacharitamanas::2974.simple_insight: Even in grief, he keeps his actions clean, humble, and orderly.
ramacharitamanas::2974.detailed_meaning: Bharat has reached Prayag on his long, painful journey after leaving Ayodhya. At Triveni, he does not rush past the sacred place. He bows, bathes in the confluence, gives gifts, and honours the priests before moving on.
ramacharitamanas::2974.modern_relevance: You arrive at a funeral or family gathering carrying private pain, but you still greet elders properly, sit quietly, and do what respect requires. Bharat shows grief can remain disciplined.
ramacharitamanas::2974.insight: It shifts attention from emotional overwhelm to respectful conduct, showing that inner pain need not disrupt outer order.

ramacharitamanas::2975.verse_sanskrit: देखत स्यामल धवल हलोरे। पुलकि सरीर भरत कर जोरे॥ सकल काम प्रद तीरथराऊ। बेद बिदित जग प्रगट प्रभाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::2975.verse_hindi: श्याम और सफेद (यमुनाजी और गंगाजी की) लहरों को देखकर भरतजी का शरीर पुलकित हो उठा और उन्होंने हाथ जोड़कर कहा- हे तीर्थराज! आप समस्त कामनाओं को पूर्ण करने वाले हैं। आपका प्रभाव वेदों में प्रसिद्ध और संसार में प्रकट है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2975.english_translation: Seeing the dark and bright waves, Bharata's body shivered with joy, and he folded his hands. "O king of sacred places, you grant every wish. Your glory is known in the Vedas and shines openly in the world."
ramacharitamanas::2975.translation_literal: देखत (seeing) / स्यामल (dark) / धवल (white) / हलोरे (waves) / पुलकि (with goosebumps) / सरीर (body) / भरत (Bharata) / कर (hands) / जोरे (joined)॥ / सकल (all) / काम (desires) / प्रद (giver) / तीरथराऊ (king of sacred places) / बेद (Vedas) / बिदित (known) / जग (world) / प्रगट (manifest) / प्रभाऊ (glory, power) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2975.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2975.essence: True reverence rises when the heart meets a source larger than its own wants.
ramacharitamanas::2975.simple_meaning: Bharat sees the sacred river waves, feels joy rise in his body, and joins his hands in reverence. He praises the holy place as a giver of all wishes and widely renowned.
ramacharitamanas::2975.simple_insight: Reverence comes naturally when you meet something that feels larger than your own wanting.
ramacharitamanas::2975.detailed_meaning: At Prayag, Bharat has already arrived with grief, humility, and a pilgrim's heart. Seeing the dark and light waves of the rivers, he is moved into prayer. The moment turns the landscape into a living presence that receives his devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2975.modern_relevance: You stand at the edge of the ocean after a hard year, and the sight makes you quiet. Some places don't just look beautiful — they make you remember how to bow.
ramacharitamanas::2975.insight: It shifts attention from personal desire to reverent recognition of what feels sacred and fulfilling.

ramacharitamanas::2976.verse_sanskrit: मागउँ भीख त्यागि निज धरमू। आरत काह न करइ कुकरमू॥ अस जियँ जानि सुजान सुदानी। सफल करहिं जग जाचक बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2976.verse_hindi: मैं अपना धर्म (न माँगने का क्षत्रिय धर्म) त्यागकर आप से भीख माँगता हूँ। आर्त्त मनुष्य कौन सा कुकर्म नहीं करता? ऐसा हृदय में जानकर सुजान उत्तम दानी जगत् में माँगने वाले की वाणी को सफल किया करते हैं (अर्थात् वह जो माँगता है, सो दे देते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2976.english_translation: I set aside my own duty and beg from you. In distress, what wrong will a person not do? Knowing this in the heart, wise and generous people make a beggar's words come true.
ramacharitamanas::2976.translation_literal: मागउँ (I beg) / भीख (alms) / त्यागि (leaving aside) / निज (own) / धरमू (duty) / आरत (distressed) / काह (what) / न करइ (does not do) / कुकरमू (wrong deed) / अस (thus) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानि (knowing) / सुजान (wise) / सुदानी (very generous) / सफल (successful) / करहिं (make) / जग (in the world) / जाचक (beggar's) / बानी (speech)
ramacharitamanas::2976.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2976.essence: Need can override pride, and wise generosity makes room for it.
ramacharitamanas::2976.simple_meaning: A person in deep distress may set aside pride and ask for help. Good, generous people recognize that suffering can drive anyone to beg, and they respond kindly.
ramacharitamanas::2976.simple_insight: There is no shame in asking when you truly need help.
ramacharitamanas::2976.detailed_meaning: At the Triveni, Bharat is overwhelmed by devotion and grief. He speaks like a humble beggar, setting aside royal pride. He knows that distress can push anyone into desperate action, and he appeals to the generosity of those who can help.
ramacharitamanas::2976.modern_relevance: You finally text the friend you’ve avoided because the rent is due tomorrow. The honest ask feels humiliating for a second, but it opens the door to real help.
ramacharitamanas::2976.insight: It shifts the mind from protecting pride to asking plainly for what is needed.

ramacharitamanas::2977.verse_sanskrit: अरथ न धरम न काम रुचि गति न चहउँ निरबान। जनम-जनम रति राम पद यह बरदानु न आन ॥
ramacharitamanas::2977.verse_hindi: मुझे न अर्थ की रुचि (इच्छा) है, न धर्म की, न काम की और न मैं मोक्ष ही चाहता हूँ। जन्म-जन्म में मेरा श्री रामजी के चरणों में प्रेम हो, बस, यही वरदान माँगता हूँ, दूसरा कुछ नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2977.english_translation: I want no wealth, no righteousness, no desire, and not even liberation. My only boon is love for Ram's feet, birth after birth.
ramacharitamanas::2977.translation_literal: अरथ (wealth) / न (not) / धरम (righteousness) / न (not) / काम (desire) / रुचि (interest) / गति (liberation) / न (not) / चहउँ (I want) / निरबान (liberation) / जनम-जनम (birth after birth) / रति (love/attachment) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / यह (this) / बरदानु (boon) / न (not) / आन (other)
ramacharitamanas::2977.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::2977.essence: Nothing else satisfies when your heart wants Ram alone.
ramacharitamanas::2977.simple_meaning: Bharat says he wants no wealth, pleasure, or even liberation. His only wish is lifelong love for Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::2977.simple_insight: Real devotion asks for the Beloved, not for spiritual rewards.
ramacharitamanas::2977.detailed_meaning: At the Ganga, Bharat stands before sacred waters with folded hands, speaking like a man who has given up every lesser desire. After refusing the throne, he asks for only one thing: unbroken love for Ram, life after life.
ramacharitamanas::2977.modern_relevance: You finally get the thing you thought would fix everything, and it still feels thin. Bharat shows a different hunger: not for status, comfort, or even escape, but for a bond that never wears out.
ramacharitamanas::2977.insight: It shifts desire away from achievement and toward wholehearted belonging.

ramacharitamanas::2978.verse_sanskrit: जानहुँ रामु कुटिल करि मोही। लोग कहउ गुर साहिब द्रोही॥ सीता राम चरन रति मोरें। अनुदिन बढ़उ अनुग्रह तोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2978.verse_hindi: स्वयं श्री रामचंद्रजी भी भले ही मुझे कुटिल समझें और लोग मुझे गुरुद्रोही तथा स्वामी द्रोही भले ही कहें, पर श्री सीता-रामजी के चरणों में मेरा प्रेम आपकी कृपा से दिन-दिन बढ़ता ही रहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2978.english_translation: Even if Ram himself thinks of me as crooked, and people call me disloyal to my teacher and master, may my love for the feet of Sita and Ram grow day by day by your grace.
ramacharitamanas::2978.translation_literal: जानहुँ (even if know) / रामु (Ram) / कुटिल (crooked) / करि (as) / मोही (me) / लोग (people) / कहउ (call) / गुर (teacher) / साहिब (master) / द्रोही (disloyal) / सीता (Sita) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / रति (love) / मोरें (of mine) / अनुदिन (day by day) / बढ़उ (may grow) / अनुग्रह (grace) / तोरें (your)
ramacharitamanas::2978.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2978.essence: Being misunderstood is bearable when love keeps growing.
ramacharitamanas::2978.simple_meaning: Bharat says he does not mind being seen as dishonest or disloyal, as long as his love for Sita and Ram keeps increasing by grace.
ramacharitamanas::2978.simple_insight: Real devotion can survive misunderstanding, criticism, and even unfair judgment.
ramacharitamanas::2978.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is pleading for nothing except deeper love for Ram and Sita. He is willing to be misunderstood by Ram, by the world, even as a traitor to teacher and master, if only devotion keeps growing.
ramacharitamanas::2978.modern_relevance: You do the right thing, and someone still calls you manipulative. The sting is real, but you keep showing up with a cleaner heart than before.
ramacharitamanas::2978.insight: It shifts attention from protecting your image to protecting your devotion.

ramacharitamanas::2979.verse_sanskrit: जलदु जनम भरि सुरति बिसारउ। जाचत जलु पबि पाहन डारउ॥ चातकु रटिन घटें घटि जाई। बढ़ें प्रेमु सब भाँति भलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2979.verse_hindi: मेघ चाहे जन्मभर चातक की सुध भुला दे और जल माँगने पर वह चाहे वज्र और पत्थर (ओले) ही गिरावे, पर चातक की रटन घटने से तो उसकी बात ही घट जाएगी (प्रतिष्ठा ही नष्ट हो जाएगी)। उसकी तो प्रेम बढ़ने में ही सब तरह से भलाई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2979.english_translation: Let the cloud forget the chataka for a whole lifetime; let it even rain thunderbolts and stones when water is begged for. If the chataka's cry weakens, its very standing falls. Its good lies in love growing in every way.
ramacharitamanas::2979.translation_literal: जलदु (cloud) / जनम भरि (for a whole lifetime) / सुरति (remembrance) / बिसारउ (let it forget) / जाचत (while asking) / जलु (water) / पबि (thunderbolt) / पाहन (stones) / डारउ (let it throw) / चातकु (chataka bird) / रटिन (crying) / घटें (if it decreases) / घटि जाई (it falls away) / बढ़ें (in increasing) / प्रेमु (love) / सब भाँति (in every way) / भलाई (goodness)
ramacharitamanas::2979.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2979.essence: Love deepens when you keep calling without guarantee of reply.
ramacharitamanas::2979.simple_meaning: The chataka bird should keep crying for rain no matter what the cloud does. In devotion, longing itself is part of the blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2979.simple_insight: Your love is not wasted just because the response is delayed or harsh.
ramacharitamanas::2979.detailed_meaning: In Bharat's speech at Triveni, the mood is one of fierce devotion and loyal longing. He compares himself to the chataka bird: even if the cloud forgets him or answers with thunder, his cry should not weaken, because love grows through steadfast longing.
ramacharitamanas::2979.modern_relevance: You keep texting someone who barely replies, yet you still care. This verse says your devotion is not measured by the response you get.
ramacharitamanas::2979.insight: It shifts you from judging love by outcomes to valuing the steadiness of your own longing.

ramacharitamanas::2980.verse_sanskrit: कनकहिं बान चढ़इ जिमि दाहें। तिमि प्रियतम पद नेम निबाहें॥ भरत बचन सुनि माझ त्रिबेनी। भइ मृदु बानि सुमंगल देनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2980.verse_hindi: जैसे तपाने से सोने पर आब (चमक) आ जाती है, वैसे ही प्रियतम के चरणों में प्रेम का नियम निबाहने से प्रेमी सेवक का गौरव बढ़ जाता है। भरतजी के वचन सुनकर बीच त्रिवेणी में से सुंदर मंगल देने वाली कोमल वाणी हुई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2980.english_translation: As gold is refined by fire, so a devoted servant's glory is polished by keeping faith with the beloved's feet. Hearing Bharat's words, a gentle, auspicious voice arose from the middle of the Triveni.
ramacharitamanas::2980.translation_literal: कनकहिं (to gold) / बान (arrow; fire) / चढ़इ (rises, is applied) / जिमि (as) / दाहें (by burning) / तिमि (so) / प्रियतम (beloved) / पद (feet) / नेम (vow, rule) / निबाहें (by keeping, fulfilling) || भरत (Bharat) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / माझ (in the middle) / त्रिबेनी (Triveni) / भइ (became, arose) / मृदु (soft, gentle) / बानि (speech, voice) / सुमंगल (highly auspicious) / देनी (giving)
ramacharitamanas::2980.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2980.essence: Faithful service does not diminish you; it makes your devotion shine.
ramacharitamanas::2980.simple_meaning: Keeping faith with the beloved's feet refines your worth, just as fire refines gold. Bharat's words move the sacred river crossing to answer with a gentle blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2980.simple_insight: Loyalty does not shrink you; it makes your love more radiant.
ramacharitamanas::2980.detailed_meaning: At Triveni, Bharat has just spoken with deep humility and devotion for Ram. The verse compares steadfast service to gold purified by fire, then shows the sacred place itself responding with a soft, auspicious voice.
ramacharitamanas::2980.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone who never promised you anything back. The work feels costly, but over time it makes your devotion unmistakable.
ramacharitamanas::2980.insight: It shifts attention from personal gain to the refining power of faithful service.

ramacharitamanas::2981.verse_sanskrit: तात भरत तुम्ह सब बिधि साधू। राम चरन अनुराग अगाधू॥ बादि गलानि करहु मन माहीं। तुम्ह सम रामहि कोउ प्रिय नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2981.verse_hindi: हे तात भरत! तुम सब प्रकार से साधु हो। श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणों में तुम्हारा अथाह प्रेम है। तुम व्यर्थ ही मन में ग्लानि कर रहे हो। श्री रामचंद्रजी को तुम्हारे समान प्रिय कोई नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2981.english_translation: O Bharat, you are noble in every way. Your love for Ram's feet is boundless. Do not keep blaming yourself in your mind. No one is dearer to Ram than you.
ramacharitamanas::2981.translation_literal: तात (dear one) / भरत (Bharat) / तुम्ह (you) / सब बिधि (in every way) / साधू (noble, good) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / अनुराग (love, attachment) / अगाधू (boundless, unfathomable) / बादि (futile, in vain) / गलानि (self-blame, remorse) / करहु (you do) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / तुम्ह सम (equal to you) / रामहि (to Ram) / कोउ (anyone) / प्रिय (dear) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::2981.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2981.essence: Your deepest love can be greater than your loudest guilt.
ramacharitamanas::2981.simple_meaning: Bharat is praised as noble and deeply devoted to Ram. He should stop blaming himself, because Ram loves him more than anyone else.
ramacharitamanas::2981.simple_insight: Love can be real even when your mind keeps accusing you.
ramacharitamanas::2981.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is grieving his role in Ram's exile and silently punishing himself. The speaker reassures him that his character is pure and his devotion is unmatched. This moment turns remorse into recognition of his hidden greatness.
ramacharitamanas::2981.modern_relevance: You replay one conversation for hours, convinced you ruined everything. But the person you disappointed may still value your heart more than your mistake.
ramacharitamanas::2981.insight: It shifts self-judgment into trust in the sincerity of your devotion and character.

ramacharitamanas::2982.verse_sanskrit: तनु पुलकेउ हियँ हरषु सुनि बेनि बचन अनुकूल। भरत धन्य कहि धन्य सुर हरषित बरषहिं फूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::2982.verse_hindi: त्रिवेणीजी के अनुकूल वचन सुनकर भरतजी का शरीर पुलकित हो गया, हृदय में हर्ष छा गया। भरतजी धन्य हैं, कहकर देवता हर्षित होकर फूल बरसाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2982.english_translation: Hearing Triveni's favorable words, Bharat's body thrilled and joy rose in his heart. 'Bharat is blessed,' the radiant beings said, and flowers rained down in joy.
ramacharitamanas::2982.translation_literal: तनु (body) / पुलकेउ (thrilled) / हियँ (in the heart) / हरषु (joy) / सुनि (hearing) / बेनि (Triveni) / बचन (words) / अनुकूल (favorable) / भरत (Bharat) / धन्य (blessed) / कहि (saying) / धन्य (blessed) / सुर (radiant beings) / हरषित (delighted) / बरषहिं (rain) / फूल (flowers)
ramacharitamanas::2982.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2982.essence: True humility is seen, and the world answers with joy.
ramacharitamanas::2982.simple_meaning: Triveni's kind words fill Bharat with joy, and the heavenly beings celebrate him with flowers.
ramacharitamanas::2982.simple_insight: When genuine goodness is recognised, joy spreads beyond the person to everyone around him.
ramacharitamanas::2982.detailed_meaning: At Prayag, Triveni's praise lands on Bharat like a blessing. His humility and love for Ram are being publicly honoured, and even the radiant beings above respond with celebration. This is a brief burst of shared delight before the larger gathering continues.
ramacharitamanas::2982.modern_relevance: You hear someone finally say what they mean about you after months of quiet effort. The relief is instant, and even the room seems lighter.
ramacharitamanas::2982.insight: It shows how sincere virtue can create a ripple of joy, turning private goodness into public blessing.

ramacharitamanas::2983.verse_sanskrit: प्रमुदित तीरथराज निवासी। बैखानस बटु गृही उदासी॥ कहहिं परसपर मिलि दस पाँचा। भरत सनेहु सीलु सुचि साँचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2983.verse_hindi: तीर्थराज प्रयाग में रहने वाले वनप्रस्थ, ब्रह्मचारी, गृहस्थ और उदासीन (संन्यासी) सब बहुत ही आनंदित हैं और दस-पाँच मिलकर आपस में कहते हैं कि भरतजी का प्रेम और शील पवित्र और सच्चा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2983.english_translation: The residents of Prayag, whether forest-dwellers, celibates, householders, or renunciates, are delighted. Gathering in small groups, they say to one another that Bharat's love and character are pure and true.
ramacharitamanas::2983.translation_literal: प्रमुदित (delighted) / तीरथराज (king of sacred places, Prayag) / निवासी (residents) / बैखानस (forest-dwellers) / बटु (celibates, students) / गृही (householders) / उदासी (renunciates) / कहहिं (say) / परसपर (to one another) / मिलि (gathering) / दस पाँचा (in small groups) / भरत सनेहु (Bharat's love) / सीलु (character, virtue) / सुचि (pure) / साँचा (true)
ramacharitamanas::2983.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2983.simple_meaning: Everyone in Prayag is happy and speaking well of Bharat. They see his love and character as pure and genuine.
ramacharitamanas::2983.simple_insight: When your love is clean, even strangers can feel it.
ramacharitamanas::2983.detailed_meaning: At Prayag, people from every way of life are watching Bharat's devotion unfold. Forest-dwellers, students, householders, and renunciates all feel moved by his sincerity, and they speak among themselves with admiration.
ramacharitamanas::2983.modern_relevance: At a train station, a group of strangers notices the person quietly helping everyone without asking for credit. Soon they are all saying the same thing: that person's heart is unmistakably clean.
ramacharitamanas::2983.insight: It shows how sincere conduct earns trust across every social group.

ramacharitamanas::2984.verse_sanskrit: सुनत राम गुन ग्राम सुहाए। भारद्वाज मुनिबर पहिं आए॥ दंड प्रनामु करत मुनि देखे। मूरतिमंत भाग्य निज लेखे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2984.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के सुंदर गुण समूहों को सुनते हुए वे मुनिश्रेष्ठ भारद्वाजजी के पास आए। मुनि ने भरतजी को दण्डवत प्रणाम करते देखा और उन्हें अपना मूर्तिमान सौभाग्य समझा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2984.english_translation: Hearing the lovely stories of Ram's virtues, they came to the great sage Bharadwaj. The sage saw Bharat bowing down in prostration and felt he was looking at his own embodied good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::2984.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / राम (Ram) / गुन (virtues) / ग्राम (collection) / सुहाए (lovely) / भारद्वाज (Bharadwaj) / मुनिबर (great sage) / पहिं (to) / आए (came) ॥ / दंड प्रनामु (prostrating bow) / करत (doing) / मुनि (sage) / देखे (saw) / मूरतिमंत (embodied) / भाग्य (fortune) / निज (own) / लेखे (account)
ramacharitamanas::2984.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2984.essence: Humility can look like living good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::2984.simple_meaning: Hearing praise of Ram, Bharat goes to Bharadwaj and bows deeply. The sage sees his humility and feels blessed just to witness it.
ramacharitamanas::2984.simple_insight: True devotion makes even a simple bow feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::2984.detailed_meaning: Bharat has reached the hermitage after hearing of Ram's virtues. Bharadwaj sees him bowing with complete humility and recognises in that moment the living shape of blessing itself. The scene is about reverence meeting reverence.
ramacharitamanas::2984.modern_relevance: You meet someone who arrives without any ego, only respect. Their humility changes the whole room before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::2984.insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing that humility itself can be the highest richness.

ramacharitamanas::2985.verse_sanskrit: धाइ उठाइ लाइ उर लीन्हे। दीन्हि असीस कृतारथ कीन्हे॥ आसनु दीन्ह नाइ सिरु बैठे। चहत सकुच गृहँ जनु भजि पैठे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2985.verse_hindi: उन्होंने दौड़कर भरतजी को उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया और आशीर्वाद देकर कृतार्थ किया। मुनि ने उन्हें आसन दिया। वे सिर नवाकर इस तरह बैठे मानो भागकर संकोच के घर में घुस जाना चाहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::2985.english_translation: They ran forward, lifted Bharata into their embrace, blessed him, and made him feel fulfilled. The sage offered a seat, and Bharata sat after bowing his head, as if shyly entering the house of modesty itself.
ramacharitamanas::2985.translation_literal: धाइ (running) / उठाइ (lifting) / लाइ (bringing) / उर (to the chest) / लीन्हे (took) / दीन्हि (gave) / असीस (blessing) / कृतारथ (fulfilled) / कीन्हे (made) / आसनु (seat) / दीन्ह (gave) / नाइ (bowing) / सिरु (head) / बैठे (sat) / चहत (wishing) / सकुच (shyness) / गृहँ (house) / जनु (as if) / भजि (fleeing) / पैठे (entered)
ramacharitamanas::2985.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2985.essence: Humility can be so deep it makes honour feel almost embarrassing.
ramacharitamanas::2985.simple_meaning: The sage welcomes Bharata with warmth, blessing, and respect. Bharata responds with deep humility and such modesty that he seems almost to shrink away from attention.
ramacharitamanas::2985.simple_insight: Real greatness can look like humility, not display.
ramacharitamanas::2985.detailed_meaning: In Prayag, the sages meet Bharata after hearing of Ram's virtues. Bharata's reverence is so complete that even the welcome becomes a lesson: the holy man blesses him, offers a seat, and Bharata sits with such shyness that the scene itself feels like devotion in human form.
ramacharitamanas::2985.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone expects you to speak first, but you bow your head and listen. That quiet modesty can change the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::2985.insight: It shifts attention from status and performance to humility as a lived strength.

ramacharitamanas::2986.verse_sanskrit: मुनि पूँछब कछु यह बड़ सोचू। बोले रिषि लखि सीलु सँकोचू॥ सुनहु भरत हम सब सुधि पाई। बिधि करतब पर किछु न बसाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2986.verse_hindi: उनके मन में यह बड़ा सोच है कि मुनि कुछ पूछेंगे (तो मैं क्या उत्तर दूँगा)। भरतजी के शील और संकोच को देखकर ऋषि बोले- भरत! सुनो, हम सब खबर पा चुके हैं। विधाता के कर्तव्य पर कुछ वश नहीं चलता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2986.english_translation: Seeing Bharata's restraint and hesitation, the sage said, "Bharata, listen. We already know everything. No one can control what fate has set in motion."
ramacharitamanas::2986.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / पूँछब (to ask) / कछु (something) / यह (this) / बड़ (great) / सोचू (worry) / बोले (spoke) / रिषि (sage) / लखि (seeing) / सीलु (restraint) / सँकोचू (hesitation) / सुनहु (listen) / भरत (Bharata) / हम (we) / सब (all) / सुधि (news/knowledge) / पाई (having received) / बिधि (fate / the ordering power) / करतब (deeds) / पर (over) / किछु (anything) / न (not) / बसाई (has control)
ramacharitamanas::2986.speaker: Bharadwaj
ramacharitamanas::2986.essence: Some events cannot be stopped, only met with steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::2986.simple_meaning: Bharadwaj sees Bharata's humility and gently tells him that no one can control everything that happens. Some things are already in motion beyond human power.
ramacharitamanas::2986.simple_insight: You can stop blaming yourself for what was never fully yours to control.
ramacharitamanas::2986.detailed_meaning: Bharata has come to Bharadwaj in Ayodhya, bowed with deep restraint, and seems afraid of what to say. Seeing that hesitation, the sage reassures him: the larger forces behind the exile are already known, and human beings cannot command every turn.
ramacharitamanas::2986.modern_relevance: You replay the message you sent, wondering if you could have prevented the fallout. Then you realize the chain had already started before you touched it. Some outcomes were never in your hands.
ramacharitamanas::2986.insight: It shifts the mind from self-blame to clear acceptance of limits.

ramacharitamanas::2987.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह गलानि जियँ जनि करहु समुझि मातु करतूति। तात कैकइहि दोसु नहिं गई गिरा मति धूति ॥
ramacharitamanas::2987.verse_hindi: माता की करतूत को समझकर (याद करके) तुम हृदय में ग्लानि मत करो। हे तात! कैकेयी का कोई दोष नहीं है, उसकी बुद्धि तो सरस्वती बिगाड़ गई थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2987.english_translation: Do not feel remorse in your heart, remembering your mother's actions. O dear one, Kaikeyi is not at fault; the goddess of speech clouded her understanding.
ramacharitamanas::2987.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / गलानि (remorse) / जियँ (in the heart) / जनि (do not) / करहु (do) / समुझि (remembering, understanding) / मातु (mother's) / करतूति (actions) / तात (dear one) / कैकइहि (Kaikeyi) / दोसु (fault) / नहिं (not) / गई (went) / गिरा (speech) / मति (understanding) / धूति (clouded, disturbed)
ramacharitamanas::2987.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2987.essence: Not every painful act deserves your lifelong guilt.
ramacharitamanas::2987.simple_meaning: Bharat is told not to feel guilty about his mother’s actions. Kaikeyi is not being blamed fully, because her judgment was clouded.
ramacharitamanas::2987.simple_insight: You can hold pain without turning it into self-blame.
ramacharitamanas::2987.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before the sage after the exile has shattered his family. He is ashamed of Kaikeyi’s role and may blame himself by association. The sage softens that wound by saying her judgment was clouded.
ramacharitamanas::2987.modern_relevance: You replay your parent’s worst decision for years, as if it lives inside your own name. This verse says not every family wound belongs to you to carry as guilt.
ramacharitamanas::2987.insight: It shifts the mind from inherited shame to compassionate understanding of impaired judgment.

ramacharitamanas::2988.verse_sanskrit: यहउ कहत भल कहिहि न कोऊ। लोकु बेदु बुध संमत दोऊ॥ तात तुम्हार बिमल जसु गाई। पाइहि लोकउ बेदु बड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2988.verse_hindi: यह कहते भी कोई भला न कहेगा, क्योंकि लोक और वेद दोनों ही विद्वानों को मान्य है, किन्तु हे तात! तुम्हारा निर्मल यश गाकर तो लोक और वेद दोनों बड़ाई पावेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::2988.english_translation: No one would call this good either, for both society and the Vedas approve it. Yet, my dear son, singing your spotless fame will win praise from both society and the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::2988.translation_literal: यहउ (this also) / कहत (saying) / भल (good) / कहिहि (will say) / न (not) / कोऊ (anyone) / लोकु (society/world) / बेदु (Veda) / बुध (wise) / संमत (approved) / दोऊ (both)॥ / तात (son/dear one) / तुम्हार (your) / बिमल (spotless) / जसु (fame) / गाई (singing) / पाइहि (will obtain) / लोकउ (society/world also) / बेदु (Veda) / बड़ाई (praise/greatness) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2988.speaker: Rishi
ramacharitamanas::2988.essence: A pure life makes praise feel true, not flattering.
ramacharitamanas::2988.simple_meaning: A wise person says that speaking well of Bharat is not wrong, because both society and sacred tradition respect it. His pure reputation will bring him honor everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::2988.simple_insight: A life lived cleanly needs no defense; its reputation speaks for itself.
ramacharitamanas::2988.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the sage is reassuring Bharat, who feels troubled by the moral complexity around him. He says that praising Bharat is justified, because Bharat's conduct is pure and will be honored by both public opinion and sacred authority.
ramacharitamanas::2988.modern_relevance: You hesitate before recommending someone who never self-promotes, yet everyone who worked with them already knows the truth. Their integrity carries farther than your praise.
ramacharitamanas::2988.insight: It shifts attention from awkward self-justification to the quiet power of a clean reputation.

ramacharitamanas::2989.verse_sanskrit: लोक बेद संमत सबु कहई। जेहि पितु देइ राजु सो लहई॥ राउ सत्यब्रत तुम्हहि बोलाई। देत राजु सुखु धरमु बड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2989.verse_hindi: यह लोक और वेद दोनों को मान्य है और सब यही कहते हैं कि पिता जिसको राज्य दे वही पाता है। राजा सत्यव्रती थे, तुमको बुलाकर राज्य देते, तो सुख मिलता, धर्म रहता और बड़ाई होती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2989.english_translation: It is accepted by both worldly custom and the Vedas that whoever the father gives the kingdom to receives it. King Dasharath was true to his vow; if he had called you and given you the throne, you would have gained happiness, dharma, and honor.
ramacharitamanas::2989.translation_literal: लोक (worldly custom) / बेद (Vedas) / संमत (accepted) / सबु (all) / कहई (say) / जेहि (whom) / पितु (father) / देइ (gives) / राजु (kingdom) / सो (that one) / लहई (receives)॥ / राउ (king) / सत्यब्रत (true to a vow) / तुम्हहि (you) / बोलाई (calling) / देत (giving) / राजु (kingdom) / सुखु (happiness) / धरमु (dharma) / बड़ाई (honor) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2989.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2989.essence: A vow can matter more than power, even when power is within reach.
ramacharitamanas::2989.simple_meaning: The rightful heir should receive the throne, and Dasharath’s vow-bound nature made that possible. If he had given Bharat the kingdom, Bharat would have gained comfort, duty, and respect.
ramacharitamanas::2989.simple_insight: Sometimes the hardest right choice is the one that protects integrity, not comfort.
ramacharitamanas::2989.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the elders are trying to make sense of a kingdom shattered by Kaikeyi’s demand and Dasharath’s promise. This verse explains the normal order of succession and shows how Dasharath’s truthfulness made the exile unavoidable.
ramacharitamanas::2989.modern_relevance: You promised two people different things, and now both cannot be satisfied. The clean answer is not the easiest one — it is the one that keeps your word intact, even when it hurts.
ramacharitamanas::2989.insight: It shifts attention from personal gain to the moral weight of keeping a promise.

ramacharitamanas::2990.verse_sanskrit: राम गवनु बन अनरथ मूला। जो सुनि सकल बिस्व भइ सूला॥ सो भावी बस रानि अयानी। करि कुचालि अंतहुँ पछितानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::2990.verse_hindi: सारे अनर्थ की जड़ तो श्री रामचन्द्रजी का वनगमन है, जिसे सुनकर समस्त संसार को पीड़ा हुई। वह श्री राम का वनगमन भी भावीवश हुआ। बेसमझ रानी तो भावीवश कुचाल करके अंत में पछताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::2990.english_translation: The exile of Ram was the root of all calamity, and hearing of it brought pain to the whole world. That exile happened by the force of fate. The foolish queen acted wrongly and later regretted it.
ramacharitamanas::2990.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / गवनु (going) / बन (forest) / अनरथ (misfortune) / मूला (root) / जो (which) / सुनि (hearing) / सकल (all) / बिस्व (world) / भइ (became) / सूला (pierced with pain) ॥ / सो (that) / भावी (by fate) / बस (under control) / रानि (queen) / अयानी (foolish, unaware) / करि (doing) / कुचालि (wrong deed) / अंतहुँ (finally) / पछितानी (regretted) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2990.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2990.essence: One wrong turn can become the root of lasting pain.
ramacharitamanas::2990.simple_meaning: Ram's exile became the source of all suffering, and the whole world felt that pain. The queen's wrong choice was driven by fate, and she later regretted it.
ramacharitamanas::2990.simple_insight: Some choices feel small in the moment, but their consequences can wound everyone involved.
ramacharitamanas::2990.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court's broken promises have already pushed Ram toward exile. Tulsidas steps back to show the larger tragedy: this one departure becomes the root of suffering for the world, and the queen who helped cause it is left with regret.
ramacharitamanas::2990.modern_relevance: A family argument that seemed manageable at midnight can still echo through years of silence, regret, and distance the next morning.
ramacharitamanas::2990.insight: It shifts attention from immediate blame to the wider consequences of one wrong turn.

ramacharitamanas::2991.verse_sanskrit: तहँउँ तुम्हार अलप अपराधू। कहै सो अधम अयान असाधू॥ करतेहु राजु त तुम्हहि ना दोषू। रामहि होत सुनत संतोषू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2991.verse_hindi: उसमें भी तुम्हारा कोई तनिक सा भी अपराध कहे, तो वह अधम, अज्ञानी और असाधु है। यदि तुम राज्य करते तो भी तुम्हें दोष न होता। सुनकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी को भी संतोष ही होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2991.english_translation: Even there, anyone who calls your conduct a small fault is base, ignorant, and unrighteous. Even if you had ruled the kingdom, you would still not be at fault. Hearing it, Ram would feel only gladness.
ramacharitamanas::2991.translation_literal: तहँउँ (even there) / तुम्हार (your) / अलप (small) / अपराधू (fault) / कहै (says) / सो (that one) / अधम (base) / अयान (ignorant) / असाधू (unrighteous)॥ / करतेहु (even if you had done) / राजु (rule / kingdom) / त (then) / तुम्हहि (you) / ना (no) / दोषू (fault) / रामहि (to Ram) / होत (would be) / सुनत (hearing) / संतोषू (contentment)॥
ramacharitamanas::2991.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2991.essence: Right action can look like wrongdoing to people who cannot see the heart.
ramacharitamanas::2991.simple_meaning: Bharat is told that even the smallest blame placed on him is unfair. He would not have been wrong even if he had taken the throne, and Ram would have accepted it peacefully.
ramacharitamanas::2991.simple_insight: You can be innocent even when others try to blame your choices.
ramacharitamanas::2991.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the grief over Ram's exile has turned into a moral argument about Bharat and the throne. The speaker defends Bharat completely: even if he had ruled, no fault would have touched him, and Ram himself would have been content.
ramacharitamanas::2991.modern_relevance: A family meeting turns tense because someone implies you should have stepped in sooner. You know you acted from loyalty, not ambition, and the accusation does not fit the truth.
ramacharitamanas::2991.insight: It shifts judgment away from appearances and back to intention, duty, and Ram's approval.

ramacharitamanas::2992.verse_sanskrit: अब अति कीन्हेहु भरत भल तुम्हहि उचित मत एहु। सकल सुमंगल मूल जग रघुबर चरन सनेहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2992.verse_hindi: हे भरत! अब तो तुमने बहुत ही अच्छा किया, यही मत तुम्हारे लिए उचित था। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में प्रेम होना ही संसार में समस्त सुंदर मंगलों का मूल है ॥
