ramacharitamanas::2992.english_translation: O Bharat, you have done very well. This is the right way for you. Love for Raghubar's feet is the root of all auspiciousness in the world.
ramacharitamanas::2992.translation_literal: अब (now) / अति (very) / कीन्हेहु (you have done) / भरत (Bharat) / भल (well) / तुम्हहि (for you) / उचित (proper) / मत (opinion/way) / एहु (this) / सकल (all) / सुमंगल (auspiciousness) / मूल (root) / जग (world) / रघुबर (Lord of Raghu) / चरन (feet) / सनेहु (love)
ramacharitamanas::2992.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2992.essence: Loving Ram is the source of every real blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2992.simple_meaning: Bharat has chosen the right path: loving Ram is the source of all true blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2992.simple_insight: Real goodness is not in possession, but in loving surrender.
ramacharitamanas::2992.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is being praised for refusing the throne and holding only Ram in his heart. The speaker says Bharat has chosen rightly, because love for Ram is the source of every true blessing.
ramacharitamanas::2992.modern_relevance: You turn down the promotion because it would cost your integrity, and people call it foolish. This verse says the deeper choice is the one that keeps your heart aligned with what is highest.
ramacharitamanas::2992.insight: It shifts value from status and gain to devotion as the foundation of a rightly ordered life.

ramacharitamanas::2993.verse_sanskrit: सो तुम्हार धनु जीवनु प्राना। भूरिभाग को तुम्हहि समाना॥ यह तुम्हार आचरजु न ताता। दसरथ सुअन राम प्रिय भ्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::2993.verse_hindi: सो वह (श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों का प्रेम) तो तुम्हारा धन, जीवन और प्राण ही है, तुम्हारे समान बड़भागी कौन है? हे तात! तुम्हारे लिए यह आश्चर्य की बात नहीं है, क्योंकि तुम दशरथजी के पुत्र और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्यारे भाई हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2993.english_translation: That love for Ram's feet is your wealth, your life, and your breath. Who is as fortunate as you? Father, this is no surprise, because you are Dasharath's son and Ram's beloved brother.
ramacharitamanas::2993.translation_literal: सो (that) / तुम्हार (your) / धनु (wealth) / जीवनु (life) / प्राना (breath, life-force) / भूरिभाग (very fortunate) / को (who) / तुम्हहि (to you) / समाना (equal) / यह (this) / तुम्हार (your) / आचरजु (surprise) / न (not) / ताता (father, dear one) / दसरथ सुअन (Dasharath's son) / राम प्रिय भ्राता (Ram's beloved brother)
ramacharitamanas::2993.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::2993.essence: Love for Ram makes Bharat richer than kings.
ramacharitamanas::2993.simple_meaning: Bharat's greatest wealth is his love for Ram. That love is what gives his life meaning, and no one is more fortunate than he is.
ramacharitamanas::2993.simple_insight: Real richness is being held by love, not by possession.
ramacharitamanas::2993.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, people are praising Bharat's refusal of the throne and his total devotion to Ram. They say his bond with Ram is his true wealth, and that his good fortune is no accident — he is Dasharath's son and Ram's beloved brother.
ramacharitamanas::2993.modern_relevance: When everyone around you measures success by salary, status, or control, you quietly choose loyalty to what matters most. That choice can look strange from outside and completely natural from within.
ramacharitamanas::2993.insight: It shifts value away from ownership and toward loving relationship.

ramacharitamanas::2994.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु भरत रघुबर मन माहीं। पेम पात्रु तुम्ह सम कोउ नाहीं॥ लखन राम सीतहि अति प्रीती। निसि सब तुम्हहि सराहत बीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2994.verse_hindi: हे भरत! सुनो, श्री रामचन्द्र के मन में तुम्हारे समान प्रेम पात्र दूसरा कोई नहीं है। लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामजी और सीताजी तीनों की सारी रात उस दिन अत्यन्त प्रेम के साथ तुम्हारी सराहना करते ही बीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::2994.english_translation: Bharat, listen: in Raghubar's heart, no one is as dear as you. Lakshman, Ram, and Sita spent the whole night praising you with love.
ramacharitamanas::2994.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / भरत (Bharat) / रघुबर (Raghubar, Ram) / मन माहीं (in the heart) / पेम पात्रु (vessel of love) / तुम्ह सम (like you) / कोउ नाहीं (no one is) / लखन (Lakshman) / राम (Ram) / सीतहि (to Sita) / अति प्रीती (great love) / निसि (night) / सब (all) / तुम्हहि (you) / सराहत (praising) / बीती (passed)
ramacharitamanas::2994.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2994.essence: True devotion makes you dear without asking to be seen.
ramacharitamanas::2994.simple_meaning: Bharat is told that Ram loves him more than anyone else, and Lakshman, Ram, and Sita spent the night praising him with affection.
ramacharitamanas::2994.simple_insight: Being deeply loved can be a quiet strength you didn't have to earn.
ramacharitamanas::2994.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's devotion has already humbled everyone around him. Now the speaker reveals a tender truth: Ram himself treasures Bharat above others, and even Lakshman, Ram, and Sita spent the night speaking well of him.
ramacharitamanas::2994.modern_relevance: You leave a family gathering unsure whether anyone noticed your effort. Later, someone tells you the person you admire most was speaking warmly about you all evening.
ramacharitamanas::2994.insight: It shifts attention from self-doubt to the reality of being held in genuine affection.

ramacharitamanas::2995.verse_sanskrit: जाना मरमु नहात प्रयागा। मगन होहिं तुम्हरें अनुरागा॥ तुम्ह पर अस सनेहु रघुबर कें। सुख जीवन जग जस जड़ नर कें ॥
ramacharitamanas::2995.verse_hindi: प्रयागराज में जब वे स्नान कर रहे थे, उस समय मैंने उनका यह मर्म जाना। वे तुम्हारे प्रेम में मग्न हो रहे थे। तुम पर श्री रामचन्द्रजी का ऐसा ही (अगाध) स्नेह है, जैसा मूर्ख (विषयासक्त) मनुष्य का संसार में सुखमय जीवन पर होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2995.english_translation: I came to know the secret while bathing at Prayag. They became absorbed in your affection. Lord Raghubar's love for you is like a foolish person's attachment to worldly comfort and praise.
ramacharitamanas::2995.translation_literal: जाना (came to know) / मरमु (secret, inner meaning) / नहात (while bathing) / प्रयागा (at Prayag) / मगन (absorbed) / होहिं (they become) / तुम्हरें (in your) / अनुरागा (affection, love) ॥ / तुम्ह (you) / पर (on, toward) / अस (such) / सनेहु (love, affection) / रघुबर (Lord of Raghu, Ram) / कें (of) / सुख (comfort) / जीवन (life) / जग (world) / जस (fame, praise) / जड़ (foolish) / नर (person) / कें (of) ॥
ramacharitamanas::2995.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2995.essence: Ram's love for you can be as consuming as obsession.
ramacharitamanas::2995.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he understood the depth of Ram's affection for Bharat at Prayag. Ram's love for Bharat is so strong that it resembles a person's attachment to comfort and praise.
ramacharitamanas::2995.simple_insight: You are not overlooked; the love held for you can be deeper than you imagine.
ramacharitamanas::2995.detailed_meaning: At Prayag, Tulsidas reflects on what he has just seen: Ram is emotionally absorbed in Bharat's love. The verse deepens the bond already praised around it, showing that Ram's affection for Bharat is not ordinary kindness but a powerful, consuming attachment.
ramacharitamanas::2995.modern_relevance: You notice someone checking their phone again and again, not for work, but for one message from a person they love. That quiet pull is the closest image to this verse's tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::2995.insight: It shifts attention from your own effort to the depth of Ram's affection for the devotee.

ramacharitamanas::2996.verse_sanskrit: यह न अधिक रघुबीर बड़ाई। प्रनत कुटुंब पाल रघुराई॥ तुम्ह तौ भरत मोर मत एहू। धरें देह जनु राम सनेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2996.verse_hindi: यह श्री रघुनाथजी की बहुत बड़ाई नहीं है, क्योंकि श्री रघुनाथजी तो शरणागत के कुटुम्ब भर को पालने वाले हैं। हे भरत! मेरा यह मत है कि तुम तो मानो शरीरधारी श्री रामजी के प्रेम ही हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::2996.english_translation: This is not great praise of Raghubir, for Raghurai sustains the whole family of those who take refuge. Bharata, my view is that you are as if embodied love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2996.translation_literal: यह (this) / न (not) / अधिक (great) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / बड़ाई (praise) / प्रनत (those who have taken refuge) / कुटुंब (family) / पाल (sustainer) / रघुराई (Raghurai) / तुम्ह (you) / तौ (indeed) / भरत (Bharata) / मोर (my) / मत (view) / एहू (this) / धरें (having taken) / देह (body) / जनु (as if) / राम (Ram) / सनेहू (love)
ramacharitamanas::2996.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2996.essence: Ram's refuge includes everyone you love.
ramacharitamanas::2996.simple_meaning: Ram's greatness is that he protects everyone who takes refuge in him. Bharata is so filled with love for Ram that he seems like love itself in human form.
ramacharitamanas::2996.simple_insight: You can be so devoted that love becomes your identity.
ramacharitamanas::2996.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the praise of Bharata deepens. Tulsidas says Ram's glory is not merely personal affection: he protects the entire family of anyone who surrenders to him. Bharata's own life is then held up as living love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2996.modern_relevance: You watch someone stay up all night caring for a sick parent, then still worry about everyone else in the house. This verse sees that kind of love and says: devotion changes who you are.
ramacharitamanas::2996.insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to a whole way of being that protects others too.

ramacharitamanas::2997.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह कहँ भरत कलंक यह हम सब कहँ उपदेसु। राम भगति रस सिद्धि हित भा यह समउ गनेसु ॥
ramacharitamanas::2997.verse_hindi: हे भरत! तुम्हारे लिए (तुम्हारी समझ में) यह कलंक है, पर हम सबके लिए तो उपदेश है। श्री रामभक्ति रूपी रस की सिद्धि के लिए यह समय गणेश (बड़ा शुभ) हुआ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::2997.english_translation: Bharat, what seems like a stain to you is instruction for all of us. This is an auspicious moment for the completion of the nectar of devotion to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::2997.translation_literal: तुम्ह कहँ (for you) / भरत (Bharat) / कलंक (stain) / यह (this) / हम सब कहँ (for all of us) / उपदेसु (instruction) / राम भगति रस (nectar of Ram devotion) / सिद्धि हित (for completion) / भा (has become) / यह (this) / समउ (time) / गनेसु (auspicious, like Ganesh)
ramacharitamanas::2997.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::2997.essence: What feels like shame can become the doorway to devotion.
ramacharitamanas::2997.simple_meaning: What looks like disgrace to Bharat becomes a teaching for everyone else. Tulsidas says this moment is auspicious because it helps devotion to Ram mature fully.
ramacharitamanas::2997.simple_insight: Even painful misunderstanding can become sacred instruction.
ramacharitamanas::2997.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's refusal of the throne and his grief are being reframed by the poet. What Bharat may feel as humiliation becomes, for others, a lesson in devotion and surrender. This moment is being praised as the right time for Ram-bhakti to deepen.
ramacharitamanas::2997.modern_relevance: You were misunderstood in a family meeting, and the memory still stings. Later, someone else learns courage from that same moment. Pain can become instruction when love is larger than pride.
ramacharitamanas::2997.insight: It shifts you from seeing embarrassment as wasted pain to seeing it as material for devotion and learning.

ramacharitamanas::2998.verse_sanskrit: नव बिधु बिमल तात जसु तोरा। रघुबर किंकर कुमुद चकोरा॥ उदित सदा अँथइहि कबहूँ ना। घटिहि न जग नभ दिन दिन दूना ॥
ramacharitamanas::2998.verse_hindi: हे तात! तुम्हारा यश निर्मल नवीन चन्द्रमा है और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दास कुमुद और चकोर हैं (वह चन्द्रमा तो प्रतिदिन अस्त होता और घटता है, जिससे कुमुद और चकोर को दुःख होता है), परन्तु यह तुम्हारा यश रूपी चन्द्रमा सदा उदय रहेगा, कभी अस्त होगा ही नहीं! जगत रूपी आकाश में यह घटेगा नहीं, वरन दिन-दिन दूना होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2998.english_translation: Your spotless fame, dear Bharat, is like a fresh moon. The servants of Raghubar are the kumud and chakor that live by it. It will rise forever, never set, and it will not fade in the world’s sky; day by day it will grow brighter.
ramacharitamanas::2998.translation_literal: नव (new) / बिधु (moon) / बिमल (pure) / तात (dear brother) / जसु (fame) / तोरा (your) / रघुबर (Raghubar) / किंकर (servants) / कुमुद (kumud lily) / चकोरा (chakor bird) / उदित (risen) / सदा (always) / अँथइहि (will set) / कबहूँ ना (never) / घटिहि (will diminish) / न (not) / जग (world) / नभ (sky) / दिन दिन (day by day) / दूना (double)
ramacharitamanas::2998.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2998.essence: Pure devotion turns your name into a light that only grows.
ramacharitamanas::2998.simple_meaning: Bharat's fame is compared to a moon that never sets or wanes. As long as Ram's devotees exist, that glory will keep growing.
ramacharitamanas::2998.simple_insight: True devotion leaves a light that time cannot dim.
ramacharitamanas::2998.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the pain of exile has already split the royal family, but Bharat's purity stands untouched. The speaker blesses his fame as a moon for Ram's servants, saying it will never fade and will only grow brighter in the world.
ramacharitamanas::2998.modern_relevance: You quietly did the right thing when no one was applauding. Months later, people still trust your name because they felt your steadiness. That kind of goodness compounds.
ramacharitamanas::2998.insight: It shifts attention from short-term praise to the lasting radiance of a life rooted in Ram.

ramacharitamanas::2999.verse_sanskrit: कोक तिलोक प्रीति अति करिही। प्रभु प्रताप रबि छबिहि न हरिही॥ निसि दिन सुखद सदा सब काहू। ग्रसिहि न कैकइ करतबु राहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::2999.verse_hindi: त्रैलोक्य रूपी चकवा इस यश रूपी चन्द्रमा पर अत्यन्त प्रेम करेगा और प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी का प्रताप रूपी सूर्य इसकी छबि को हरण नहीं करेगा। यह चन्द्रमा रात-दिन सदा सब किसी को सुख देने वाला होगा। कैकेयी का कुकर्म रूपी राहु इसे ग्रास नहीं करेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::2999.english_translation: The three worlds will love this moon of fame deeply. The sun of the Lord's splendor will never dim its beauty. It will always give joy to everyone, day and night. Rahu's dark deed of Kaikeyi will not swallow it.
ramacharitamanas::2999.translation_literal: कोक (the chakora bird) / तिलोक (the three worlds) / प्रीति (love) / अति (very much) / करिही (will do) / प्रभु (the Lord) / प्रताप (splendor) / रबि (sun) / छबिहि (beauty) / न (not) / हरिही (will take away) / निसि (night) / दिन (day) / सुखद (joy-giving) / सदा (always) / सब (all) / काहू (to everyone) / ग्रसिहि (will swallow) / न (not) / कैकइ (Kaikeyi's) / करतबु (deed) / राहू (Rahu)
ramacharitamanas::2999.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::2999.essence: True brilliance survives even the darkest blow.
ramacharitamanas::2999.simple_meaning: Rama's fame is like a moon loved by all. Its brightness will never fade, and Kaikeyi's wrongdoing cannot swallow it.
ramacharitamanas::2999.simple_insight: Even betrayal cannot erase what is truly luminous.
ramacharitamanas::2999.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the pain of exile is already in motion, but Tulsidas pauses to defend Rama's honor. He says Rama's fame will keep shining through the three worlds, untouched by Kaikeyi's act, and will keep giving comfort to everyone.
ramacharitamanas::2999.modern_relevance: A rumor starts after a family argument, and suddenly everyone is speaking as if one cruel moment defines the whole person. This verse refuses that collapse: what is truly noble can survive public damage.
ramacharitamanas::2999.insight: It shifts attention from temporary disgrace to enduring worth.

ramacharitamanas::3000.verse_sanskrit: पूरन राम सुपेम पियूषा। गुर अवमान दोष नहिं दूषा॥ राम भगत अब अमिअँ अघाहूँ। कीन्हेहु सुलभ सुधा बसुधाहूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3000.verse_hindi: यह चन्द्रमा श्री रामचन्द्रजी के सुंदर प्रेम रूपी अमृत से पूर्ण है। यह गुरु के अपमान रूपी दोष से दूषित नहीं है। तुमने इस यश रूपी चन्द्रमा की सृष्टि करके पृथ्वी पर भी अमृत को सुलभ कर दिया। अब श्री रामजी के भक्त इस अमृत से तृप्त हो लें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3000.english_translation: This moon is full of Ram's beautiful nectar of love. It is not stained by disrespect to the guru. You have made nectar easy to find on earth, and now Ram's devotees may drink their fill.
ramacharitamanas::3000.translation_literal: पूरन (full) / राम (Ram's) / सुपेम (beautiful love) / पियूषा (nectar) / गुर (guru) / अवमान (disrespect) / दोष (fault) / नहिं (not) / दूषा (stained)॥ / राम (Ram's) / भगत (devotees) / अब (now) / अमिअँ (nectar) / अघाहूँ (fully satisfied) / कीन्हेहु (you have made) / सुलभ (easy to obtain) / सुधा (nectar) / बसुधाहूँ (on earth) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3000.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3000.essence: Pure devotion becomes nectar that feeds everyone around it.
ramacharitamanas::3000.simple_meaning: Ram's loving glory is like nectar that remains pure and can satisfy devotees. A life of devotion can become a blessing others freely share.
ramacharitamanas::3000.simple_insight: There is joy in knowing that sincere love can nourish more than just you.
ramacharitamanas::3000.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas praises King Dasharath's fame as a moonlit nectar of Ram's love. The verse says this glory is not tainted by disrespect to the teacher, and that it has made divine sweetness easy for Ram's devotees to taste on earth.
ramacharitamanas::3000.modern_relevance: You do something beautiful, and people around you quietly feel steadier because of it. A home, a team, or a friendship can become easier to breathe in when your care is clean and generous.
ramacharitamanas::3000.insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to shared nourishment that others can actually receive.

ramacharitamanas::3001.verse_sanskrit: भूप भगीरथ सुरसरि आनी। सुमिरत सकल सुमंगल खानी॥ दसरथ गुन गन बरनि न जाहीं। अधिकु कहा जेहि सम जग नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3001.verse_hindi: राजा भगीरथ गंगाजी को लाए, जिन (गंगाजी) का स्मरण ही सम्पूर्ण सुंदर मंगलों की खान है। दशरथजी के गुण समूहों का तो वर्णन ही नहीं किया जा सकता, अधिक क्या, जिनकी बराबरी का जगत में कोई नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3001.english_translation: King Bhagirath brought the Ganga, whose remembrance itself is a treasury of all auspiciousness. King Dasharath's countless virtues cannot be described; there is no one in the world equal to him.
ramacharitamanas::3001.translation_literal: भूप (king) / भगीरथ (Bhagirath) / सुरसरि (the river of the radiant beings) / आनी (brought) / सुमिरत (remembering) / सकल (all) / सुमंगल (great auspiciousness) / खानी (mine, treasury) ॥ / दसरथ (Dasharath) / गुन (virtues) / गन (groups, heaps) / बरनि (described) / न (not) / जाहीं (can be) । / अधिकु (more) / कहा (what to say) / जेहि (whose) / सम (equal) / जग (world) / नाहीं (is not) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3001.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3001.essence: True greatness is remembered through the blessings it leaves behind.
ramacharitamanas::3001.simple_meaning: Bhagirath is remembered for bringing the Ganga, and Dasharath is praised as a king whose virtues are beyond description and unmatched in the world.
ramacharitamanas::3001.simple_insight: Some people are remembered because their actions bless the world, and others because their character does.
ramacharitamanas::3001.detailed_meaning: The narration pauses to praise great kings before moving toward Dasharath's death and grief. Bhagirath is remembered for bringing the Ganga to earth, and Dasharath is lifted beside him as a ruler whose virtues are beyond comparison, setting the emotional weight of the coming loss.
ramacharitamanas::3001.modern_relevance: A funeral conversation turns to the person everyone admired: not their title, but the way their life quietly improved everyone around them. That is the kind of loss this verse prepares you to feel.
ramacharitamanas::3001.insight: It shifts attention from public power to the lasting fragrance of virtue and service.

ramacharitamanas::3002.verse_sanskrit: जासु सनेह सकोच बस राम प्रगट भए आई। जे हर हिय नयननि कबहुँ निरखे नहीं अघाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3002.verse_hindi: जिनके प्रेम और संकोच (शील) के वश में होकर स्वयं (सच्चिदानंदघन) भगवान श्री राम आकर प्रकट हुए, जिन्हें श्री महादेवजी अपने हृदय के नेत्रों से कभी अघाकर नहीं देख पाए (अर्थात जिनका स्वरूप हृदय में देखते-देखते शिवजी कभी तृप्त नहीं हुए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3002.english_translation: Because of their love and modest reserve, Ram himself came and appeared. Mahadev never grew tired of seeing them with his heart and eyes.
ramacharitamanas::3002.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / सनेह (love) / सकोच (modesty, reserve) / बस (under the influence of) / राम (Ram) / प्रगट भए (appeared) / आई (coming) / जे (those who) / हर (Shiva) / हिय (heart) / नयननि (with the eyes) / कबहुँ (ever) / निरखे (saw) / नहीं (not) / अघाइ (sated, satisfied)
ramacharitamanas::3002.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3002.essence: Love and modesty can draw Ram himself into view.
ramacharitamanas::3002.simple_meaning: Deep love and humble restraint can draw Ram himself near. Such a person becomes endlessly beautiful to Shiva's heart.
ramacharitamanas::3002.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that sincere love is never small enough to be ignored.
ramacharitamanas::3002.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is praising the kind of devotion that makes Ram appear of his own accord. The verse turns to Shiva as the highest witness: even he never feels satisfied gazing at such love.
ramacharitamanas::3002.modern_relevance: You meet someone who stays gentle even when praised, and the room changes. People trust that kind of quiet dignity — it feels like something higher has entered the space.
ramacharitamanas::3002.insight: It shifts attention from outward display to the quiet force of love and humility.

ramacharitamanas::3003.verse_sanskrit: कीरति बिधु तुम्ह कीन्ह अनूपा। जहँ बस राम पेम मृगरूपा॥ तात गलानि करहु जियँ जाएँ। डरहु दरिद्रहि पारसु पाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3003.verse_hindi: (परन्तु उनसे भी बढ़कर) तुमने कीर्ति रूपी अनुपम चंद्रमा को उत्पन्न किया, जिसमें श्री राम प्रेम ही हिरन के (चिह्न के) रूप में बसता है। हे तात! तुम व्यर्थ ही हृदय में ग्लानि कर रहे हो। पारस पाकर भी तुम दरिद्रता से डर रहे हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3003.english_translation: You created a unique moon of fame, where Ram's love lives like a deer. Dear one, do not feel remorse in your heart. Why fear poverty after finding a touchstone?
ramacharitamanas::3003.translation_literal: कीरति (fame) / बिधु (moon) / तुम्ह (you) / कीन्ह (made) / अनूपा (matchless) / जहँ (where) / बस (dwells) / राम (Ram) / पेम (love) / मृगरूपा (in deer-form) / तात (dear one) / गलानि (remorse) / करहु (do) / जियँ (in heart) / जाएँ (going) / डरहु (fear) / दरिद्रहि (poverty) / पारसु (touchstone) / पाएँ (having found)
ramacharitamanas::3003.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3003.essence: Ram's love makes even remorse look unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::3003.simple_meaning: Bharat has already earned extraordinary honor because Ram's love rests in his fame. Shiva tells him not to feel ashamed or think himself spiritually poor after receiving such grace.
ramacharitamanas::3003.simple_insight: Real abundance is being held by Ram's love, not by outward success.
ramacharitamanas::3003.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Parvati about Bharat's devotion in Ayodhyakand. Bharat is tormented by remorse, but Shiva says his fame is already a unique moon lit by Ram's love. The moment matters because Bharat cannot see the greatness of his own surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3003.modern_relevance: You keep replaying the one mistake that went wrong, even though your life is already carrying real love, trust, and earned respect. Shiva's words tell you not to call yourself poor just because perfection is missing.
ramacharitamanas::3003.insight: It shifts attention from self-criticism to the grace already present in your life.

ramacharitamanas::3004.verse_sanskrit: सुनहु भरत हम झूठ न कहहीं। उदासीन तापस बन रहहीं॥ सब साधन कर सुफल सुहावा। लखन राम सिय दरसनु पावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3004.verse_hindi: हे भरत! सुनो, हम झूठ नहीं कहते। हम उदासीन हैं (किसी का पक्ष नहीं करते), तपस्वी हैं (किसी की मुँह देखी नहीं कहते) और वन में रहते हैं (किसी से कुछ प्रयोजन नहीं रखते)। सब साधनों का उत्तम फल हमें लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामजी और सीताजी का दर्शन प्राप्त हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3004.english_translation: Listen, Bharat, we do not speak falsely. We are detached, forest-dwelling ascetics who take no side. The best fruit of all spiritual practice is that we have seen Lakshman, Ram, and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3004.translation_literal: सुनहु (listen) / भरत (Bharat) / हम (we) / झूठ (false) / न (not) / कहहीं (speak) / उदासीन (detached, impartial) / तापस (ascetics) / बन (forest) / रहहीं (remain) / सब (all) / साधन (spiritual practices, means) / कर (of) / सुफल (best fruit) / सुहावा (beautiful, pleasing) / लखन (Lakshman) / राम (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / दरसनु (seeing, sight) / पावा (obtained)
ramacharitamanas::3004.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3004.essence: All striving finds its fulfillment in Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::3004.simple_meaning: All spiritual effort reaches its highest fruit in the direct sight of Ram, Sita, and Lakshman. Detachment and austerity are not the goal; loving encounter is.
ramacharitamanas::3004.simple_insight: Relief comes when striving is no longer the point — presence is.
ramacharitamanas::3004.detailed_meaning: Shiva is speaking to Bharat in the forest, defending the truth of his own detached life. He says that all austerity and discipline have one beautiful result: the chance to behold Ram, Sita, and Lakshman. The moment turns practice into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3004.modern_relevance: You finish a long retreat, a year of therapy, or months of discipline and realize the breakthrough wasn't the achievement. It was finally meeting what you had been preparing yourself to receive.
ramacharitamanas::3004.insight: It shifts spiritual effort from self-improvement to loving encounter.

ramacharitamanas::3005.verse_sanskrit: तेहि फल कर फलु दरस तुम्हारा। सहित प्रयाग सुभाग हमारा॥ भरत धन्य तुम्ह जसु जगु जयऊ। कहि अस प्रेम मगन मुनि भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3005.verse_hindi: (सीता-लक्ष्मण सहित श्री रामदर्शन रूप) उस महान फल का परम फल यह तुम्हारा दर्शन है! प्रयागराज समेत हमारा बड़ा भाग्य है। हे भरत! तुम धन्य हो, तुमने अपने यश से जगत को जीत लिया है। ऐसा कहकर मुनि प्रेम में मग्न हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3005.english_translation: The highest fruit of that great result is your sight. Our good fortune, along with Prayag's, is fulfilled. Bharata, you are blessed; your fame has conquered the world. Saying this, the sage became lost in love.
ramacharitamanas::3005.translation_literal: तेहि (of that) / फल (fruit) / कर (of) / फलु (fruit) / दरस (sight) / तुम्हारा (your) / सहित (together with) / प्रयाग (Prayag) / सुभाग (good fortune) / हमारा (our) / भरत (Bharat) / धन्य (blessed) / तुम्ह (you) / जसु (fame) / जगु (world) / जयऊ (has conquered) / कहि (saying) / अस (thus) / प्रेम (love) / मगन (immersed) / मुनि (sage) / भयऊ (became)
ramacharitamanas::3005.speaker: Bharadvaja
ramacharitamanas::3005.essence: True devotion makes your presence itself the reward.
ramacharitamanas::3005.simple_meaning: Seeing Bharata is treated as the highest reward of all. The sage says this meeting completes their good fortune and praises Bharata’s fame as world-winning.
ramacharitamanas::3005.simple_insight: Being truly devoted can make your very presence feel like a gift to others.
ramacharitamanas::3005.detailed_meaning: Bharadvaja has been speaking to Bharata in Prayag after the painful exile has already shattered Ayodhya’s peace. Now, moved by Bharata’s humility and devotion to Ram, the sage says that even the sacred reward of pilgrimage is fulfilled by Bharata’s arrival.
ramacharitamanas::3005.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone who kept showing up for everyone else, never asking for credit. Their quiet loyalty changes the whole room, and you realize presence itself can be a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3005.insight: It shifts attention from achievement to the grace a devoted presence brings into a place.

ramacharitamanas::3006.verse_sanskrit: सुनि मुनि बचन सभासद हरषे। साधु सराहि सुमन सुर बरषे॥ धन्य धन्य धुनि गगन प्रयागा। सुनि सुनि भरतु मगन अनुरागा॥4
ramacharitamanas::3006.verse_hindi: भारद्वाज मुनि के वचन सुनकर सभासद् हर्षित हो गए। 'साधु-साधु' कहकर सराहना करते हुए देवताओं ने फूल बरसाए। आकाश में और प्रयागराज में 'धन्य, धन्य' की ध्वनि सुन-सुनकर भरतजी प्रेम में मग्न हो रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3006.english_translation: Hearing the sage's words, everyone in the assembly rejoiced. Praising him as noble, the devas showered flowers. The sky and Prayagraj rang with cries of "Blessed! Blessed!" and Bharat, hearing and hearing it all, became lost in love.
ramacharitamanas::3006.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (sage) / बचन (words) / सभासद (members of the assembly) / हरषे (rejoiced) / साधु (well done / noble) / सराहि (praising) / सुमन (flowers) / सुर (devas) / बरषे (showered) / धन्य धन्य (blessed blessed) / धुनि (sound) / गगन (sky) / प्रयागा (Prayagraj) / सुनि सुनि (hearing again and again) / भरतु (Bharat) / मगन (absorbed) / अनुरागा (love)
ramacharitamanas::3006.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3006.essence: Praise ripens devotion when the heart is already surrendered.
ramacharitamanas::3006.simple_meaning: The assembly rejoices at the sage's words, the devas shower flowers, and Bharat is swept deeper into loving devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3006.simple_insight: True praise deepens love; it does not pull Bharat back into pride or control.
ramacharitamanas::3006.detailed_meaning: At Prayagraj, Bharadwaj's words about Bharat's devotion land in a gathered assembly. The saints rejoice, the devas shower flowers, and Bharat only sinks further into love. The scene is celebration, not instruction.
ramacharitamanas::3006.modern_relevance: You hear someone describe your quiet sacrifice with more kindness than you expected, and your throat tightens. Being seen rightly can deepen devotion instead of feeding ego.
ramacharitamanas::3006.insight: It shows how sincere recognition can intensify humility and loving absorption rather than self-importance.

ramacharitamanas::3007.verse_sanskrit: पुलक गात हियँ रामु सिय सजल सरोरुह नैन। करि प्रनामु मुनि मंडलिहि बोले गदगद बैन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3007.verse_hindi: भरतजी का शरीर पुलकित है, हृदय में श्री सीता-रामजी हैं और कमल के समान नेत्र (प्रेमाश्रु के) जल से भरे हैं। वे मुनियों की मंडली को प्रणाम करके गद्गद वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3007.english_translation: Bharat's body trembles with emotion; Ram and Sita fill his heart, and his lotus-like eyes are wet with tears. He bows to the assembly of sages and speaks in a choked voice.
ramacharitamanas::3007.translation_literal: पुलक (hairs standing on end) / गात (body) / हियँ (in the heart) / रामु सिय (Ram and Sita) / सजल (moist, filled with water) / सरोरुह (lotus) / नैन (eyes) / करि (doing) / प्रनामु (bowing) / मुनि मंडलिहि (to the sage assembly) / बोले (spoke) / गदगद (choked, faltering) / बैन (words)
ramacharitamanas::3007.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3007.essence: True reverence makes even your voice bow.
ramacharitamanas::3007.simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed with devotion and tears as he bows to the sages and speaks in a choked voice.
ramacharitamanas::3007.simple_insight: Love can be so full that speech itself begins to tremble.
ramacharitamanas::3007.detailed_meaning: At Prayag, Bharat stands before Bharadvaj and the gathered sages after hearing their praise. His body shivers with feeling, his eyes fill with tears, and he can only answer after bowing deeply. The verse shows devotion overflowing before his next words.
ramacharitamanas::3007.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone whose kindness has held you together for years, and your throat closes before you can thank them. Gratitude arrives faster than language.
ramacharitamanas::3007.insight: It teaches you that deep devotion first appears in the body, then in speech.

ramacharitamanas::3008.verse_sanskrit: मुनि समाजु अरु तीरथराजू। साँचिहुँ सपथ अघाइ अकाजू॥ एहिं थल जौं किछु कहिअ बनाई। एहि सम अधिक न अघ अधमाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3008.verse_hindi: मुनियों का समाज है और फिर तीर्थराज है। यहाँ सच्ची सौगंध खाने से भी भरपूर हानि होती है। इस स्थान में यदि कुछ बनाकर कहा जाए, तो इसके समान कोई बड़ा पाप और नीचता न होगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3008.english_translation: This is the gathering of sages and the king of pilgrimages. Even a true oath taken here loses its value. If you speak falsely in this place, no greater evil or baseness exists.
ramacharitamanas::3008.translation_literal: मुनि समाजु (assembly of sages) / अरु (and) / तीरथराजू (king of pilgrimages) / साँचिहुँ (even truly) / सपथ (oath) / अघाइ (becomes full / loses value) / अकाजू (harm / uselessness)॥ / एहिं (in this) / थल (place) / जौं (if) / किछु (something) / कहिअ (is said) / बनाई (by making up) / एहि (this) / सम (equal to) / अधिक (greater) / न (not) / अघ (sin / wrongdoing) / अधमाई (baseness)॥
ramacharitamanas::3008.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3008.essence: Falsehood feels smallest nowhere less than before the holy and the wise.
ramacharitamanas::3008.simple_meaning: This sacred place is so holy that speaking falsely here is especially shameful. Even a true oath would be wasted if it were used to hide the truth.
ramacharitamanas::3008.simple_insight: Sacredness raises the cost of self-deception. Some places make honesty feel unavoidable.
ramacharitamanas::3008.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands before sages at Prayag, the king of pilgrimages, speaking to an assembly that can see through appearances. He knows this is not the place for crafted words. The verse prepares his honest, trembling declaration to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3008.modern_relevance: You’re in a room where everyone can sense you’re hiding something, and the silence is getting heavier by the second. In that moment, polished words only deepen the crack.
ramacharitamanas::3008.insight: It pushes you to drop performance when the setting demands truth, especially before people who can see through it.

ramacharitamanas::3009.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह सर्बग्य कहउँ सतिभाऊ। उर अंतरजामी रघुराऊ॥ मोहि न मातु करतब कर सोचू। नहिं दुखु जियँ जगु जानिहि पोचू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3009.verse_hindi: मैं सच्चे भाव से कहता हूँ। आप सर्वज्ञ हैं और श्री रघुनाथजी हृदय के भीतर की जानने वाले हैं (मैं कुछ भी असत्य कहूँगा तो आपसे और उनसे छिपा नहीं रह सकता)। मुझे माता कैकेयी की करनी का कुछ भी सोच नहीं है और न मेरे मन में इसी बात का दुःख है कि जगत मुझे नीच समझेगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3009.english_translation: I speak with complete sincerity. You are all-knowing, and Raghunath knows the heart within. I do not worry about Kaikeyi's deed, nor do I grieve that the world will call me low.
ramacharitamanas::3009.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you are) / सर्बग्य (all-knowing) / कहउँ (I speak) / सतिभाऊ (with true feeling) / उर (heart) / अंतरजामी (knower within) / रघुराऊ (Raghuraj) / मोहि (to me) / न (not) / मातु (mother) / करतब (deed) / कर (of) / सोचू (worry) / नहिं (not) / दुखु (sorrow) / जियँ (in the heart) / जगु (the world) / जानिहि (will know) / पोचू (lowly)
ramacharitamanas::3009.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3009.essence: When your heart is already seen, public judgment loses its power.
ramacharitamanas::3009.simple_meaning: Bharat speaks honestly to the sages: Ram knows his heart, so he has no need to hide anything. He is not troubled by Kaikeyi's actions or by public shame.
ramacharitamanas::3009.simple_insight: There is relief in no longer defending yourself against misunderstanding.
ramacharitamanas::3009.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat stands before the sages after Ram's exile has shattered the royal family. He speaks with complete openness: Ram can see his heart, so there is no point in pretending. The pain of blame and reputation no longer matters to him.
ramacharitamanas::3009.modern_relevance: You sit in a family meeting where everyone assumes the worst about you, and you stop trying to win the room. The need to be understood loosens its grip.
ramacharitamanas::3009.insight: It shifts attention from managing your image to standing honestly in what you know is true.

ramacharitamanas::3010.verse_sanskrit: नाहिन डरु बिगरिहि परलोकू। पितहु मरन कर मोहि न सोकू॥ सुकृत सुजस भरि भुअन सुहाए। लछिमन राम सरिस सुत पाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3010.verse_hindi: न यही डर है कि मेरा परलोक बिगड़ जाएगा और न पिताजी के मरने का ही मुझे शोक है, क्योंकि उनका सुंदर पुण्य और सुयश विश्व भर में सुशोभित है। उन्होंने श्री राम-लक्ष्मण सरीखे पुत्र पाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3010.english_translation: I do not fear any harm to the next world, nor grieve my father's death. His good deeds and good name shine across the world, and he gained sons like Ram and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::3010.translation_literal: नाहिन (not) / डरु (fear) / बिगरिहि (will be ruined) / परलोकू (the next world) / पितहु (father's) / मरन (death) / कर (of) / मोहि (to me) / न (not) / सोकू (grief) / सुकृत (good deeds) / सुजस (good name) / भरि (filled with) / भुअन (worlds) / सुहाए (adorned) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / राम (Ram) / सरिस (like) / सुत (sons) / पाए (obtained)
ramacharitamanas::3010.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3010.essence: A life filled with virtue leaves grief less room to grow.
ramacharitamanas::3010.simple_meaning: Bharat says Dasharath’s death does not trouble him deeply, because his father’s virtue and fame are secure, and he was blessed with sons like Ram and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::3010.simple_insight: Loss hurts less when a life has already been fulfilled with honor and love.
ramacharitamanas::3010.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat speaks after Dasharath’s death. He is not clinging to fear about the king’s fate after death, because Dasharath’s life was crowned with virtue, fame, and the blessing of sons like Ram and Lakshman. The grief is real, but it is softened by acceptance.
ramacharitamanas::3010.modern_relevance: You stand at a funeral and hear people speak of a parent’s kindness, integrity, and the children who carry their values forward. The ache remains, but something in you knows the life was not wasted.
ramacharitamanas::3010.insight: It shifts attention from loss itself to the wholeness of a life already completed in virtue.

ramacharitamanas::3011.verse_sanskrit: राम बिरहँ तजि तनु छनभंगू। भूप सोच कर कवन प्रसंगू॥ राम लखन सिय बिनु पग पनहीं। करि मुनि बेष फिरहिं बन बनहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3011.verse_hindi: फिर जिन्होंने श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विरह में अपने क्षणभंगुर शरीर को त्याग दिया, ऐसे राजा के लिए सोच करने का कौन प्रसंग है? (सोच इसी बात का है कि) श्री रामजी, लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी पैरों में बिना जूती के मुनियों का वेष बनाए वन-वन में फिरते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3011.english_translation: What grief is there to feel for a king who gave up his fragile body in separation from Ram? The real sorrow is that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita wander from forest to forest in the dress of ascetics, without shoes.
ramacharitamanas::3011.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बिरहँ (in separation) / तजि (leaving) / तनु (body) / छनभंगू (moment-broken, fragile) / भूप (king) / सोच (grief, concern) / कर (of) / कवन (what) / प्रसंगू (occasion, reason) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / बिनु (without) / पग (feet) / पनहीं (shoes) / करि (having made) / मुनि बेष (sage-like guise) / फिरहिं (wander) / बन बनहीं (in forests)
ramacharitamanas::3011.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3011.essence: The deepest grief is not death, but Ram's exile.
ramacharitamanas::3011.simple_meaning: A king's death is not the real cause for grief, because life is fragile. The deeper sorrow is that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are living in exile, barefoot and dressed like sages.
ramacharitamanas::3011.simple_insight: It shifts grief from personal loss to the larger pain of separation from what is most beloved.
ramacharitamanas::3011.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharadvaja's listener is being led through Dasharath's death and its meaning. Tulsidas turns the focus away from the king's fragile body and toward the far greater ache: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are wandering the forest in exile, deprived of comfort and royal life.
ramacharitamanas::3011.modern_relevance: You miss a funeral and everyone speaks about the loss, but your mind keeps going to the child living far from home, alone and barefoot. This verse teaches you where the deepest sorrow actually lives.
ramacharitamanas::3011.insight: It teaches you to measure pain by separation from dharma and love, not by the mere ending of a body.

ramacharitamanas::3012.verse_sanskrit: अजिन बसन फल असन महि सयन डासि कुस पात। बसि तरु तर नित सहत हिम आतप बरषा बात ॥
ramacharitamanas::3012.verse_hindi: वे वल्कल वस्त्र पहनते हैं, फलों का भोजन करते हैं, पृथ्वी पर कुश और पत्ते बिछाकर सोते हैं और वृक्षों के नीचे निवास करके नित्य सर्दी, गर्मी, वर्षा और हवा सहते हैं। 211॥
ramacharitamanas::3012.english_translation: They wear bark garments, eat fruits, sleep on the ground spread with kusa grass and leaves, and live beneath trees, enduring cold, heat, rain, and wind every day.
ramacharitamanas::3012.translation_literal: अजिन (bark clothing) / बसन (garments) / फल (fruits) / असन (food) / महि (on the earth) / सयन (sleeping) / डासि (spread out) / कुस (kusa grass) / पात (leaves) / बसि (dwelling) / तरु तर (under trees) / नित (always) / सहत (enduring) / हिम (cold) / आतप (heat) / बरषा (rain) / बात (wind)
ramacharitamanas::3012.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3012.essence: Love can make hardship feel bearable.
ramacharitamanas::3012.simple_meaning: The exiled ones live like forest ascetics: simple clothes, simple food, rough sleep, and daily endurance of weather.
ramacharitamanas::3012.simple_insight: A hard life can be accepted without complaint when love and duty are bigger than comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3012.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the pain of exile is being measured through the life Ram, Sita, and Lakshman now live in the forest. They wear bark, eat fruit, sleep on grass and leaves, and endure every season. This verse supports Bharat's grief and wonder at their suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3012.modern_relevance: You unpack a thin mattress in a cold cabin after choosing to stay with someone you love through a difficult season. Comfort is gone, but the choice is clear.
ramacharitamanas::3012.insight: It shifts attention from missing comfort to bearing hardship with dignity.

ramacharitamanas::3013.verse_sanskrit: एहि दुख दाहँ दहइ दिन छाती। भूख न बासर नीद न राती॥ एहि कुरोग कर औषधु नाहीं। सोधेउँ सकल बिस्व मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3013.verse_hindi: इसी दुःख की जलन से निरंतर मेरी छाती जलती रहती है। मुझे न दिन में भूख लगती है, न रात को नींद आती है। मैंने मन ही मन समस्त विश्व को खोज डाला, पर इस कुरोग की औषध कहीं नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3013.english_translation: The fire of this sorrow burns my chest day and night. I feel no hunger by day, no sleep by night. I searched the whole world in my mind, but no medicine exists for this illness.
ramacharitamanas::3013.translation_literal: एहि (this) / दुख (sorrow) / दाहँ (burning) / दहइ (burns) / दिन (day) / छाती (chest) / भूख (hunger) / न (not) / बासर (by day) / नीद (sleep) / न (not) / राती (by night) / एहि (this) / कुरोग (disease) / कर (of) / औषधु (medicine) / नाहीं (not exists) / सोधेउँ (I searched) / सकल (entire) / बिस्व (world) / मन (mind) / माहीं (within)
ramacharitamanas::3013.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3013.essence: Some grief cannot be cured; it must be borne.
ramacharitamanas::3013.simple_meaning: This grief is so intense that it destroys appetite and sleep. Even after searching everywhere, no remedy can be found for it.
ramacharitamanas::3013.simple_insight: Some suffering cannot be fixed quickly; it must be endured and understood.
ramacharitamanas::3013.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the pain of separation from Ram has become physical. The speaker says his chest burns, hunger has vanished, sleep has fled, and no remedy can be found anywhere. This is grief that medicine cannot touch.
ramacharitamanas::3013.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after a breakup, hoping for one message that will make the ache stop. But some losses do not respond to solutions; they ask for patience and honesty.
ramacharitamanas::3013.insight: It shifts you from trying to solve every sorrow to meeting some pain with endurance and acceptance.

ramacharitamanas::3014.verse_sanskrit: मातु कुमत बढ़ई अघ मूला। तेहिं हमार हित कीन्ह बँसूला॥ कलि कुकाठ कर कीन्ह कुजंत्रू। गाड़ि अवधि पढ़ि कठिन कुमंत्रू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3014.verse_hindi: माता का कुमत (बुरा विचार) पापों का मूल बढ़ई है। उसने हमारे हित का बसूला बनाया। उससे कलह रूपी कुकाठ का कुयंत्र बनाया और चौदह वर्ष की अवधि रूपी कठिन कुमंत्र पढ़कर उस यंत्र को गाड़ दिया। (यहाँ माता का कुविचार बढ़ई है, भरत को राज्य बसूला है, राम का वनवास कुयंत्र है और चौदह वर्ष की अवधि कुमंत्र है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3014.english_translation: A mother's wrong-mindedness became the root of sin. She made an axe for our welfare. She forged a crooked device of quarrel, and by reading the harsh spell of fourteen years, she buried it in place.
ramacharitamanas::3014.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / कुमत (wrong-mindedness) / बढ़ई (carpenter) / अघ (sin) / मूला (root) । / तेहिं (by that) / हमार (our) / हित (welfare) / कीन्ह (made) / बँसूला (axe) ॥ / कलि (quarrel) / कुकाठ (bad wood) / कर (of) / कीन्ह (made) / कुजंत्रू (crooked device) । / गाड़ि (burying) / अवधि (fourteen-year period) / पढ़ि (reading) / कठिन (harsh) / कुमंत्रू (spell) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3014.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3014.essence: Wrong intention can turn even help into harm.
ramacharitamanas::3014.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi's wrong choice has turned into the source of suffering. What was meant to help has become the tool that cut the family apart and sent Ram into exile.
ramacharitamanas::3014.simple_insight: A single distorted desire can reshape an entire household and make pain look like policy.
ramacharitamanas::3014.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is reeling from the exile of Ram and the collapse of his family. He describes Kaikeyi's misguided thinking as the force that carved the kingdom apart, turning a promise meant for good into the instrument of ruin.
ramacharitamanas::3014.modern_relevance: A family argument starts with one sharp sentence at dinner, and suddenly everyone is choosing sides. Later, you can trace the whole fracture back to that one twisted thought.
ramacharitamanas::3014.insight: It shows how one corrupt intention can turn a protective plan into a weapon.

ramacharitamanas::3015.verse_sanskrit: मोहि लगि यहु कुठाटु तेहिं ठाटा। घालेसि सब जगु बारहबाटा॥ मिटइ कुजोगु राम फिरि आएँ। बसइ अवध नहिं आन उपाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3015.verse_hindi: मेरे लिए उसने यह सारा कुठाट (बुरा साज) रचा और सारे जगत को बारहबाट (छिन्न-भिन्न) करके नष्ट कर डाला। यह कुयोग श्री रामचन्द्रजी के लौट आने पर ही मिट सकता है और तभी अयोध्या बस सकती है, दूसरे किसी उपाय से नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3015.english_translation: He set this whole trap for me and shattered the world into pieces. This bad alignment can end only when Ram returns, and Ayodhya can be settled by no other means.
ramacharitamanas::3015.translation_literal: मोहि (for me) / लगि (for the sake of) / यहु (this) / कुठाटु (bad trap) / तेहिं (by her) / ठाटा (was set) / घालेसि (threw) / सब (all) / जगु (world) / बारहबाटा (into pieces) ॥ / मिटइ (will end) / कुजोगु (bad alignment) / राम (Ram) / फिरि (returning again) / आएँ (when comes) / बसइ (will settle) / अवध (Ayodhya) / नहिं (not) / आन (other) / उपाएँ (by means) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3015.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3015.essence: Only Ram's return can heal what was broken.
ramacharitamanas::3015.simple_meaning: Bharat says the whole disaster came from a bad scheme, and only Ram's return can restore Ayodhya. No other fix will work.
ramacharitamanas::3015.simple_insight: Some losses cannot be managed around; they need the right presence to return.
ramacharitamanas::3015.detailed_meaning: Bharat is grieving the exile that has split Ayodhya apart. He sees the court's injustice as a trap that damaged everyone, not just him. In this moment, he declares that only Ram's return can end the disorder and restore the kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::3015.modern_relevance: You can rearrange the furniture, change the schedule, and call it progress — but the house still feels wrong after the person who held it together is gone.
ramacharitamanas::3015.insight: It shifts you from looking for quick fixes to recognising that some situations need restoration, not adjustment.

ramacharitamanas::3016.verse_sanskrit: भरत बचन सुनि मुनि सुखु पाई। सबहिं कीन्हि बहु भाँति बड़ाई॥ तात करहु जनि सोचु बिसेषी। सब दुखु मिटिहि राम पग देखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3016.verse_hindi: भरतजी के वचन सुनकर मुनि ने सुख पाया और सभी ने उनकी बहुत प्रकार से बड़ाई की। (मुनि ने कहा-) हे तात! अधिक सोच मत करो। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों का दर्शन करते ही सारा दुःख मिट जाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3016.english_translation: Hearing Bharat's words, the sage felt joy, and everyone praised him in many ways. The sage said, "Dear child, do not grieve so much. Seeing Ram's feet will end all sorrow."
ramacharitamanas::3016.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / बचन (words) / सुनि (having heard) / मुनि (sage) / सुखु (joy) / पाई (having obtained) / सबहिं (by everyone) / कीन्हि (did) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / बड़ाई (praise) / तात (dear child) / करहु (do) / जनि (do not) / सोचु (grief/worry) / बिसेषी (excessive) / सब (all) / दुखु (sorrow) / मिटिहि (will be removed) / राम (Ram) / पग (feet) / देखी (by seeing)
ramacharitamanas::3016.speaker: Muni Bharadvaja
ramacharitamanas::3016.essence: Grief ends when you reach Ram, not when you keep thinking.
ramacharitamanas::3016.simple_meaning: Bharat's words comfort the sage, and the sage tells him not to worry so much. Seeing Ram will end all sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::3016.simple_insight: Peace comes not from solving everything, but from turning your heart toward what is worthy.
ramacharitamanas::3016.detailed_meaning: In Bharadwaj's forest hermitage, Bharat's humility moves the sage deeply. After hearing his words, the sage and the others praise him. Then Bharadwaj gently tells Bharat to stop carrying such heavy sorrow, because meeting Ram will dissolve it.
ramacharitamanas::3016.modern_relevance: You have replayed the same painful conversation all night, trying to make peace with what happened. Sometimes the mind cannot untangle grief — but one real meeting, one true presence, can change everything.
ramacharitamanas::3016.insight: It shifts attention from mental rumination to the healing power of direct presence.

ramacharitamanas::3017.verse_sanskrit: करि प्रबोधु मुनिबर कहेउ अतिथि पेमप्रिय होहु। कंद मूल फल फूल हम देहिं लेहु करि छोहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3017.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार मुनिश्रेष्ठ भारद्वाजजी ने उनका समाधान करके कहा- अब आप लोग हमारे प्रेम प्रिय अतिथि बनिए और कृपा करके कंद-मूल, फल-फूल जो कुछ हम दें, स्वीकार कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3017.english_translation: After giving this reassurance, the great sage said, 'Become our dear guests. Please accept whatever roots, fruits, and flowers we offer.'
ramacharitamanas::3017.translation_literal: करि (having done) / प्रबोधु (reassurance) / मुनिबर (great sage) / कहेउ (said) / अतिथि (guest) / पेमप्रिय (dear to love) / होहु (be) / कंद (roots) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruits) / फूल (flowers) / हम (we) / देहिं (give) / लेहु (take) / करि छोहु (with kindness)
ramacharitamanas::3017.speaker: Bharadwaj
ramacharitamanas::3017.essence: Love turns even simple food into a gift.
ramacharitamanas::3017.simple_meaning: Bharadwaj reassures the guests warmly and invites them to accept the simple food offered with affection.
ramacharitamanas::3017.simple_insight: True hospitality makes even simple offerings feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3017.detailed_meaning: In Bharadwaj's hermitage, Bharat and his companions arrive burdened by grief and hesitation. After calming them, the sage speaks like a loving host, asking them to receive the humble forest food he offers with kindness.
ramacharitamanas::3017.modern_relevance: You arrive at a friend’s home exhausted, apologizing for the trouble, and they smile and say, “Just eat what we have.” That ease is Bharadwaj’s grace.
ramacharitamanas::3017.insight: It shifts attention from status and formality to warmth, welcome, and shared human care.

ramacharitamanas::3018.verse_sanskrit: सुनि मुनि बचन भरत हियँ सोचू। भयउ कुअवसर कठिन सँकोचू॥ जानि गुरुइ गुर गिरा बहोरी। चरन बंदि बोले कर जोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3018.verse_hindi: मुनि के वचन सुनकर भरत के हृदय में सोच हुआ कि यह बेमौके बड़ा बेढब संकोच आ पड़ा! फिर गुरुजनों की वाणी को महत्वपूर्ण (आदरणीय) समझकर, चरणों की वंदना करके हाथ जोड़कर बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3018.english_translation: Hearing the sage's words, Bharata felt a stir of worry in his heart: this awkward hesitation had come at the wrong time. Then, remembering the elders' words as weighty and worthy of respect, he bowed at their feet and spoke with joined hands.
ramacharitamanas::3018.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (sage) / बचन (words) / भरत (Bharata) / हियँ (in the heart) / सोचू (worry) / भयउ (became) / कुअवसर (wrong time) / कठिन (hard) / सँकोचू (hesitation) / जानि (knowing) / गुरुइ (the elders / the teacher) / गुर (weighty) / गिरा (words) / बहोरी (again) / चरन (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / बोले (spoke) / कर (hands) / जोरी (joined)
ramacharitamanas::3018.speaker: Bharata
ramacharitamanas::3018.essence: Hesitation yields to humility when you remember what deserves respect.
ramacharitamanas::3018.simple_meaning: Bharata feels awkward and worried, but he still respects the elders' words, bows to them, and speaks humbly with folded hands.
ramacharitamanas::3018.simple_insight: Respect does not disappear when you feel uneasy; it shows up in how you respond.
ramacharitamanas::3018.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharata is standing before sages and elders after the crisis of Ram's exile. Their words move him, but the moment also feels painfully awkward. Even so, he lowers himself, bows, and answers with humility.
ramacharitamanas::3018.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a tense family argument, and every sentence feels too sharp. Bharata shows the way through: notice the discomfort, honor the people in front of you, and speak only after bowing inwardly.
ramacharitamanas::3018.insight: It teaches you to let reverence guide your response even when the moment feels strained.

ramacharitamanas::3019.verse_sanskrit: सिर धरि आयसु करिअ तुम्हारा। परम धरम यहु नाथ हमारा॥ भरत बचन मुनिबर मन भाए। सुचि सेवक सिष निकट बोलाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3019.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! आपकी आज्ञा को सिर चढ़ाकर उसका पालन करना, यह हमारा परम धर्म है। भरतजी के ये वचन मुनिश्रेष्ठ के मन को अच्छे लगे। उन्होंने विश्वासपात्र सेवकों और शिष्यों को पास बुलाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3019.english_translation: Bearing your command on my head and obeying it is our highest duty, O Lord. Bharata's words pleased the sage's mind, and he called his trusted servants and students near.
ramacharitamanas::3019.translation_literal: सिर धरि (placing on the head) / आयसु (command) / करिअ (should be done) / तुम्हारा (your) / परम धरम (highest duty) / यहु (this) / नाथ (Lord) / हमारा (our) / भरत बचन (Bharata's words) / मुनिबर (best of sages) / मन (mind) / भाए (pleased) / सुचि (pure) / सेवक (servants) / सिष (students) / निकट (near) / बोलाए (called)
ramacharitamanas::3019.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3019.essence: When duty is loved, obedience becomes joy.
ramacharitamanas::3019.simple_meaning: Bharat says that obeying his lord's command is his highest duty. The sage is pleased by this humility and calls his helpers closer.
ramacharitamanas::3019.simple_insight: Real strength can look like obedience when the heart is free of ego.
ramacharitamanas::3019.detailed_meaning: In Bharadwaj's hermitage, Bharat answers with complete humility. He says Ram's command is his highest duty, and the sage is moved by that spirit. This becomes a quiet test of loyalty before the forest journey continues.
ramacharitamanas::3019.modern_relevance: You get a message from someone you deeply respect, and you stop making it about your preference. You do what needs doing because the relationship and the promise matter more than your convenience.
ramacharitamanas::3019.insight: It shifts action from self-will to faithful response.

ramacharitamanas::3020.verse_sanskrit: चाहिअ कीन्हि भरत पहुनाई। कंद मूल फल आनहु जाई। भलेहिं नाथ कहि तिन्ह सिर नाए। प्रमुदित निज निज काज सिधाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3020.verse_hindi: (और कहा कि) भरत की पहुनाई करनी चाहिए। जाकर कंद, मूल और फल लाओ। उन्होंने 'हे नाथ! बहुत अच्छा' कहकर सिर नवाया और तब वे बड़े आनंदित होकर अपने-अपने काम को चल दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3020.english_translation: And he said, "Bharat must be welcomed properly. Go and bring roots, bulbs, and fruits." They bowed their heads and said, "Very well, lord," and then joyfully went off to do their own tasks.
ramacharitamanas::3020.translation_literal: चाहिअ (should be done) / कीन्हि (done) / भरत (Bharat) / पहुनाई (guest-welcome) / कंद (roots/bulbs) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruits) / आनहु (bring) / जाई (go) / भलेहिं (well/very good) / नाथ (lord) / कहि (saying) / तिन्ह (they) / सिर (head) / नाए (bowed) / प्रमुदित (delighted) / निज निज (their own) / काज (tasks) / सिधाए (went off)
ramacharitamanas::3020.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3020.essence: True hospitality begins with simple, sincere service.
ramacharitamanas::3020.simple_meaning: Bharat is to be honored as a guest, so the sages send for simple forest food and then return happily to their work.
ramacharitamanas::3020.simple_insight: Respect can be shown through humble, wholehearted care.
ramacharitamanas::3020.detailed_meaning: Bharat has arrived in the forest, and the sages around him immediately shift into hospitality. Instead of ceremony, they offer roots, fruits, and warm reverence. This verse shows their joyful readiness to serve before the deeper conversation begins.
ramacharitamanas::3020.modern_relevance: A guest shows up at your door with no warning, and you quietly start chopping fruit, boiling tea, and clearing a place to sit. Care often begins in the simplest actions.
ramacharitamanas::3020.insight: It teaches you that honoring someone can be practical, not grand.

ramacharitamanas::3021.verse_sanskrit: मुनिहि सोच पाहुन बड़ नेवता। तसि पूजा चाहिअ जस देवता॥ सुनि रिधि सिधि अनिमादिक आईं। आयसु होइ सो करहिं गोसाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3021.verse_hindi: मुनि को चिंता हुई कि हमने बहुत बड़े मेहमान को न्योता है। अब जैसा देवता हो, वैसी ही उसकी पूजा भी होनी चाहिए। यह सुनकर ऋद्धियाँ और अणिमादि सिद्धियाँ आ गईं (और बोलीं-) हे गोसाईं! जो आपकी आज्ञा हो सो हम करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3021.english_translation: The sage felt anxious: we have invited a very great guest. Such worship should match such a deity. Hearing this, the powers of attainment came and said, "O Lord, whatever you command, we will do."
ramacharitamanas::3021.translation_literal: मुनिहि (to the sage) / सोच (anxiety) / पाहुन (guest) / बड़ (great) / नेवता (invitation) / तसि (such) / पूजा (worship) / चाहिअ (should be) / जस (as) / देवता (a radiant being) / सुनि (hearing) / रिधि (attainments) / सिधि (powers of accomplishment) / अनिमादिक (beginning with anima) / आईं (came) / आयसु (command) / होइ (be) / सो (that) / करहिं (do) / गोसाईं (O Lord)
ramacharitamanas::3021.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3021.essence: Great devotion makes even attainments become servants.
ramacharitamanas::3021.simple_meaning: The sage realizes that a great guest deserves a fitting welcome. The powers of attainment then arrive and offer to obey whatever command is given.
ramacharitamanas::3021.simple_insight: Real reverence changes the whole atmosphere: even powers and attainments bow when devotion is sincere.
ramacharitamanas::3021.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharata has arrived with Sita-like humility and Ram-like worthiness, and the sage hosting him feels the weight of the moment. This is no ordinary guest, so ordinary hospitality is not enough. Even the siddhis come forward in service.
ramacharitamanas::3021.modern_relevance: A friend you deeply respect walks into your home after months away, and suddenly every small gesture matters. You want your welcome to match the love you feel.
ramacharitamanas::3021.insight: It shifts attention from casual welcome to reverent service that rises to the dignity of the guest.

ramacharitamanas::3022.verse_sanskrit: राम बिरह ब्याकुल भरतु सानुज सहित समाज। पहुनाई करि हरहु श्रम कहा मुदित मुनिराज ॥
ramacharitamanas::3022.verse_hindi: मुनिराज ने प्रसन्न होकर कहा- छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न और समाज सहित भरतजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विरह में व्याकुल हैं, इनकी पहुनाई (आतिथ्य सत्कार) करके इनके श्रम को दूर करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3022.english_translation: Bharat, along with his younger brother and the whole company, is restless in separation from Ram. O sage-king, honor them as guests and remove their fatigue.
ramacharitamanas::3022.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बिरह (separation) / ब्याकुल (restless) / भरतु (Bharat) / सानुज (with younger brother) / सहित (along with) / समाज (company) / पहुनाई (guest-honoring) / करि (having done) / हरहु (remove) / श्रम (fatigue) / कहा (said) / मुदित (pleased) / मुनिराज (great sage-king)
ramacharitamanas::3022.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3022.simple_meaning: Bharat and his companions are worn out by longing for Ram, so the sage asks that they be welcomed and rested.
ramacharitamanas::3022.simple_insight: Even grief needs care. A loving welcome can ease what words cannot.
ramacharitamanas::3022.detailed_meaning: In Bharadwaj's ashram, Bharat arrives with Shatrughna and his companions, all aching from separation from Ram. The sage-king sees their condition and orders that they be honored as guests and relieved of their exhaustion.
ramacharitamanas::3022.modern_relevance: You come home after a hard day, and the person who loves you most notices before you speak. Sometimes the kindest response is not advice, but welcome.
ramacharitamanas::3022.insight: It shifts attention from solving sorrow to receiving the sorrowful with care.

ramacharitamanas::3023.verse_sanskrit: रिधि सिधि सिर धरि मुनिबर बानी। बड़भागिनि आपुहि अनुमानी॥ कहहिं परसपर सिधि समुदाई। अतुलित अतिथि राम लघु भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3023.verse_hindi: ऋद्धि-सिद्धि ने मुनिराज की आज्ञा को सिर चढ़ाकर अपने को बड़भागिनी समझा। सब सिद्धियाँ आपस में कहने लगीं- श्री रामचन्द्रजी के छोटे भाई भरत ऐसे अतिथि हैं, जिनकी तुलना में कोई नहीं आ सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3023.english_translation: Holding the sage's words on their heads, the Riddhis and Siddhis felt blessed. The whole company said among themselves, 'There is no guest equal to Ram's younger brother Bharat.'
ramacharitamanas::3023.translation_literal: रिधि सिधि (Riddhis and Siddhis) / सिर धरि (placing on the head) / मुनिबर (great sage) / बानी (words) / बड़भागिनि (most fortunate) / आपुहि (themselves) / अनुमानी (considering)॥ / कहहिं (they say) / परसपर (to one another) / सिधि समुदाई (the gathered Siddhis) / अतुलित (matchless) / अतिथि (guest) / राम (Ram) / लघु भाई (younger brother)
ramacharitamanas::3023.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3023.essence: Devotion makes even a guest feel unmatched.
ramacharitamanas::3023.simple_meaning: The divine powers feel honored to serve Bharat and call him an unmatched guest, because he comes in Ram's name and with Ram in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::3023.simple_insight: Real greatness is being eager to honor someone who carries devotion, not status.
ramacharitamanas::3023.detailed_meaning: In Nandigram, the sage has ordered a royal welcome for Bharat, who arrives grieving Ram's exile. Even the Riddhis and Siddhis treat the command as sacred and recognize Bharat as a guest beyond comparison.
ramacharitamanas::3023.modern_relevance: You meet someone at your door who never asks for special treatment, yet everyone in the room feels the quiet weight of their character. Respect follows devotion faster than rank.
ramacharitamanas::3023.insight: It shifts attention from social status to the sacredness of service.

ramacharitamanas::3024.verse_sanskrit: मुनि पद बंदि करिअ सोइ आजू। होइ सुखी सब राज समाजू॥ अस कहि रचेउ रुचिर गृह नाना। जेहि बिलोकि बिलखाहिं बिमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3024.verse_hindi: अतः मुनि के चरणों की वंदना करके आज वही करना चाहिए, जिससे सारा राज-समाज सुखी हो। ऐसा कहकर उन्होंने बहुत से सुंदर घर बनाए, जिन्हें देखकर विमान भी विलखते हैं (लजा जाते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3024.english_translation: Therefore, today one should bow to the sage's feet and do what makes the whole royal assembly happy. Saying this, they built many beautiful houses, so lovely that even celestial vehicles would feel ashamed seeing them.
ramacharitamanas::3024.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / पद (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / करिअ (should do) / सोइ (that same) / आजू (today) / होइ (becomes) / सुखी (happy) / सब (all) / राज (royal) / समाजू (assembly) ॥ अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / रचेउ (made) / रुचिर (beautiful) / गृह (houses) / नाना (many kinds) / जेहि (which) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बिलखाहिं (feel ashamed) / बिमाना (celestial vehicles) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3024.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3024.essence: True welcome begins with humility and careful preparation.
ramacharitamanas::3024.simple_meaning: Honor the sage first, then do what brings peace to everyone around you. The homes they built were so beautiful that even heavenly chariots would feel outdone.
ramacharitamanas::3024.simple_insight: Respect and beauty can create harmony without needing to announce themselves.
ramacharitamanas::3024.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharata's camp prepares to receive Ram's guests with humility rather than pride. The emphasis is on honoring the sage's feet and arranging the royal space so the whole assembly can live in comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3024.modern_relevance: You clean the house before guests arrive, not to impress them, but to make them feel cared for. Small acts of preparation can turn an ordinary welcome into real hospitality.
ramacharitamanas::3024.insight: It shifts attention from status to service: make the setting worthy of the people in it.

ramacharitamanas::3025.verse_sanskrit: भोग बिभूति भूरि भरि राखे। देखत जिन्हहि अमर अभिलाषे॥ दासीं दास साजु सब लीन्हें। जोगवत रहहिं मनहि मनु दीन्हें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3025.verse_hindi: उन घरों में बहुत से भोग (इन्द्रियों के विषय) और ऐश्वर्य (ठाट-बाट) का सामान भरकर रख दिया, जिन्हें देखकर देवता भी ललचा गए। दासी-दास सब प्रकार की सामग्री लिए हुए मन लगाकर उनके मनों को देखते रहते हैं (अर्थात उनके मन की रुचि के अनुसार करते रहते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3025.english_translation: They filled the houses with abundant pleasures and luxuries, so tempting that even the immortals would long for them. Servants stood ready with every arrangement, watching and serving according to each mind's wish.
ramacharitamanas::3025.translation_literal: भोग (pleasures) / बिभूति (splendor, luxury) / भूरि (abundantly) / भरि (filling) / राखे (kept) / देखत (seeing) / जिन्हहि (whom) / अमर (immortals) / अभिलाषे (desired) / दासीं (maids) / दास (servants) / साजु (arrangements, provisions) / सब (all) / लीन्हें (took, arranged) / जोगवत (watching, attending) / रहहिं (kept staying) / मनहि (the mind) / मनु (mind) / दीन्हें (given, devoted)
ramacharitamanas::3025.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3025.essence: True welcome anticipates every need before it is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3025.simple_meaning: The houses were stocked with lavish comforts, and servants were ready to meet every wish. It is a scene of complete, welcoming hospitality.
ramacharitamanas::3025.simple_insight: Care can be shown through attention, not just words.
ramacharitamanas::3025.detailed_meaning: The siddhis are preparing homes for Ram and Lakshman in the city of Ayodhya. They fill every house with delights and keep servants ready for each guest's liking. This verse adds detail to the larger scene of honor and welcome.
ramacharitamanas::3025.modern_relevance: You walk into a home where every detail was handled before you arrived — the food, the room, the timing. Someone cared enough to notice what would make you comfortable.
ramacharitamanas::3025.insight: It shows devotion expressed as practical attentiveness, where service adapts itself to another's mind.

ramacharitamanas::3026.verse_sanskrit: सब समाजु सजि सिधि पल माहीं। जे सुख सुरपुर सपनेहुँ नाहीं॥ प्रथमहिं बास दिए सब केही। सुंदर सुखद जथा रुचि जेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3026.verse_hindi: जो सुख के सामान स्वर्ग में भी स्वप्न में भी नहीं हैं, ऐसे सब सामान सिद्धियों ने पल भर में सजा दिए। पहले तो उन्होंने सब किसी को, जिसकी जैसी रुचि थी, वैसे ही, सुंदर सुखदायक निवास स्थान दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3026.english_translation: In a moment, the whole assembly was arranged with comforts that even heaven cannot match in dreams. First, everyone was given a beautiful, pleasant dwelling suited to each person's liking.
ramacharitamanas::3026.translation_literal: सब (whole) / समाजु (assembly) / सजि (having arranged) / सिधि (through perfection/power) / पल माहीं (in a moment) / जे (which) / सुख (comforts) / सुरपुर (heavenly realm) / सपनेहुँ (even in dreams) / नाहीं (not) / प्रथमहिं (first) / बास (dwelling places) / दिए (were given) / सब (all) / केही (each one) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुखद (pleasant) / जथा (according to) / रुचि (liking) / जेही (whose)
ramacharitamanas::3026.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3026.essence: True welcome makes room for every person exactly as needed.
ramacharitamanas::3026.simple_meaning: A moment later, everyone had been given a beautiful place to stay, each one arranged according to personal taste, with comforts beyond ordinary imagination.
ramacharitamanas::3026.simple_insight: Even a difficult transition can be softened when everyone is thoughtfully cared for.
ramacharitamanas::3026.detailed_meaning: In Bharadwaj’s ashram, the impossible hospitality has begun. By the power of the sage’s tapas, the entire royal company is instantly housed in beautiful quarters, each suited to their taste. The scene shows the scale of his welcome before Bharat’s deeper meeting with the sage.
ramacharitamanas::3026.modern_relevance: You arrive exhausted at a friend’s home after a hard journey, and they have already set out food, blankets, and a quiet room just for you. Care like that changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::3026.insight: It shifts attention from grandeur to thoughtful care for each person.

ramacharitamanas::3027.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि सपरिजन भरत कहुँ रिषि अस आयसु दीन्ह। बिधि बिसमय दायकु बिभव मुनिबर तपबल कीन्ह ॥
ramacharitamanas::3027.verse_hindi: और फिर कुटुम्ब सहित भरतजी को दिए, क्योंकि ऋषि भारद्वाजजी ने ऐसी ही आज्ञा दे रखी थी। (भरतजी चाहते थे कि उनके सब संगियों को आराम मिले, इसलिए उनके मन की बात जानकर मुनि ने पहले उन लोगों को स्थान देकर पीछे सपरिवार भरतजी को स्थान देने के लिए आज्ञा दी थी।) मुनि श्रेष्ठ ने तपोबल से ब्रह्मा को भी चकित कर देने वाला वैभव रच दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3027.english_translation: Then, for Bharat and his companions, the sage gave such an order. By the power of his austerity, the best of sages created a splendor that astonished even Brahma.
ramacharitamanas::3027.translation_literal: बहुरि (then/again) / सपरिजन (with companions/family) / भरत कहुँ (for Bharat) / रिषि (the sage) / अस (such) / आयसु (order) / दीन्ह (gave) / बिधि (Brahma) / बिसमय दायकु (astonishment-giving) / बिभव (splendor/wealth) / मुनिबर (best of sages) / तपबल (power of austerity) / कीन्ह (made/created)
ramacharitamanas::3027.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3027.essence: A trained inner power can arrange comfort that ordinary means cannot.
ramacharitamanas::3027.simple_meaning: Bharat and his companions were given a separate, fitting place. Bharadwaj's austerity created a wonder-filled display of comfort and splendor.
ramacharitamanas::3027.simple_insight: Great generosity can be created by a mind trained in discipline.
ramacharitamanas::3027.detailed_meaning: In Bharadwaj's hermitage, Bharat arrives with his companions after leaving Ayodhya behind. The sage has already arranged different quarters for everyone. His spiritual power makes even impossible comfort appear at once, setting up the moment when Bharat will see how vast the sage's blessing is.
ramacharitamanas::3027.modern_relevance: You arrive at a retreat house after a long drive, and every room is already prepared without fuss. That quiet care feels almost impossible — like someone had seen your needs before you spoke.
ramacharitamanas::3027.insight: It shows how disciplined inner power can create ease for others without effort or display.

ramacharitamanas::3028.verse_sanskrit: मुनि प्रभाउ जब भरत बिलोका। सब लघु लगे लोकपति लोका॥ सुख समाजु नहिं जाइ बखानी। देखत बिरति बिसारहिं ग्यानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3028.verse_hindi: जब भरतजी ने मुनि के प्रभाव को देखा, तो उसके सामने उन्हें (इन्द्र, वरुण, यम, कुबेर आदि) सभी लोकपालों के लोक तुच्छ जान पड़े। सुख की सामग्री का वर्णन नहीं हो सकता, जिसे देखकर ज्ञानी लोग भी वैराग्य भूल जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3028.english_translation: When Bharat saw the power of the sage, even the realms of the world-lords seemed small. The wealth and comforts cannot be described; even the wise forget non-attachment when they see it.
ramacharitamanas::3028.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / प्रभाउ (power, influence) / जब (when) / भरत (Bharat) / बिलोका (saw) / सब (all) / लघु (small, insignificant) / लगे (seemed) / लोकपति (world-lords) / लोका (realms)॥ / सुख (comfort, pleasure) / समाजु (assembly, collection) / नहिं (not) / जाइ (can be) / बखानी (described) / देखत (seeing) / बिरति (non-attachment) / बिसारहिं (forget) / ग्यानी (the wise)॥
ramacharitamanas::3028.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3028.essence: Great comfort can make even clear-minded people forget restraint.
ramacharitamanas::3028.simple_meaning: Bharat sees the sage's power and the splendor around him, and even wise people can lose their detachment in such abundance.
ramacharitamanas::3028.simple_insight: Even strong discipline can wobble when comfort and beauty flood the senses.
ramacharitamanas::3028.detailed_meaning: In Bharadvaj's hermitage, Bharat enters a space shaped by the sage's tapas. The surroundings are so abundant and refined that even heavenly kings seem small by comparison. Tulsidas pauses to show how overwhelming sacred prosperity can be.
ramacharitamanas::3028.modern_relevance: You walk into a beautifully curated retreat, and your resolve melts before the soft lights, food, and quiet luxury. Even your best intentions can blur when comfort is everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::3028.insight: It shows how atmosphere can overpower resolve and make detachment harder to hold.

ramacharitamanas::3029.verse_sanskrit: आसन सयन सुबसन बिताना। बन बाटिका बिहग मृग नाना॥ सुरभि फूल फल अमिअ समाना। बिमल जलासय बिबिध बिधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3029.verse_hindi: आसन, सेज, सुंदर वस्त्र, चँदोवे, वन, बगीचे, भाँति-भाँति के पक्षी और पशु, सुगंधित फूल और अमृत के समान स्वादिष्ट फल, अनेकों प्रकार के (तालाब, कुएँ, बावली आदि) निर्मल जलाशय, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3029.english_translation: There were seats, beds, fine clothes, canopies, groves, many birds and animals, fragrant flowers, fruits sweet as nectar, and many kinds of clear water places.
ramacharitamanas::3029.translation_literal: आसन (seats) / सयन (beds, resting places) / सुबसन (fine clothes) / बिताना (canopies) / बन (groves, forest-gardens) / बाटिका (gardens) / बिहग (birds) / मृग (deer, animals) / नाना (various) / सुरभि (fragrant) / फूल (flowers) / फल (fruits) / अमिअ समाना (like nectar) / बिमल (clear, pure) / जलासय (water places, tanks) / बिबिध (various) / बिधाना (arrangements, kinds)
ramacharitamanas::3029.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3029.essence: True welcome makes even simple things feel abundant.
ramacharitamanas::3029.simple_meaning: The place was beautifully prepared with comforts, gardens, birds, animals, flowers, fruits, and clean water sources.
ramacharitamanas::3029.simple_insight: Some spaces are made so carefully that they quiet the mind before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3029.detailed_meaning: Bharat has entered Bharadvaj's hermitage, and the poet is showing the richness of the place the sage has created. This verse lists the comforts and natural beauty there, setting up the wonder of a sacred space shaped by tapas.
ramacharitamanas::3029.modern_relevance: You walk into a home where the room is already ready for you: clean sheets, fresh fruit, water, and quiet. The care itself makes you soften before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::3029.insight: It shifts attention from luxury as display to hospitality as spiritual power.

ramacharitamanas::3030.verse_sanskrit: असन पान सुचि अमिअ अमी से। देखि लोग सकुचात जमी से॥ सुर सुरभी सुरतरु सबही कें। लखि अभिलाषु सुरेस सची कें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3030.verse_hindi: तथा अमृत के भी अमृत-सरीखे पवित्र खान-पान के पदार्थ थे, जिन्हें देखकर सब लोग संयमी पुरुषों (विरक्त मुनियों) की भाँति सकुचा रहे हैं। सभी के डेरों में (मनोवांछित वस्तु देने वाले) कामधेनु और कल्पवृक्ष हैं, जिन्हें देखकर इन्द्र और इन्द्राणी को भी अभिलाषा होती है (उनका भी मन ललचा जाता है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3030.english_translation: There were pure foods and drinks, nectar-like and even more delightful than nectar. Everyone felt shy, as if they were renunciates. Every home had wish-fulfilling cows and trees, and even Indra and Indrani would long for them.
ramacharitamanas::3030.translation_literal: असन (food) / पान (drink) / सुचि (pure) / अमिअ (nectar) / अमी (nectar-like) / से (like) / देखि (seeing) / लोग (people) / सकुचात (feel shy) / जमी (renunciates) / से (like) / सुर (radiant beings) / सुरभी (wish-fulfilling cow) / सुरतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / सबही (for everyone) / कें (for) / लखि (seeing) / अभिलाषु (desire) / सुरेस (Indra) / सची कें (of Indrani)
ramacharitamanas::3030.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3030.essence: True abundance makes even desire feel out of place.
ramacharitamanas::3030.simple_meaning: The scene describes a place of effortless abundance, where even heavenly luxuries seem ordinary and people feel humbled by the richness around them.
ramacharitamanas::3030.simple_insight: When abundance is truly complete, craving softens on its own.
ramacharitamanas::3030.detailed_meaning: Bharat is being shown the extraordinary order and beauty around the sages. The homes, food, and trees seem so perfect that ordinary desire loses its edge. This verse is part of a descriptive stretch, not a separate teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3030.modern_relevance: You walk into a home where everything is already set, clean, and generous. There is nothing to grab, nothing to prove. Your hunger quiets before you even speak.
ramacharitamanas::3030.insight: It shifts attention from wanting more to recognising fullness already present.

ramacharitamanas::3031.verse_sanskrit: रितु बसंत बह त्रिबिध बयारी। सब कहँ सुलभ पदारथ चारी॥ स्रक चंदन बनितादिक भोगा। देखि हरष बिसमय बस लोगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3031.verse_hindi: वसन्त ऋतु है। शीतल, मंद, सुगंध तीन प्रकार की हवा बह रही है। सभी को (धर्म, अर्थ, काम और मोक्ष) चारों पदार्थ सुलभ हैं। माला, चंदन, स्त्री आदि भोगों को देखकर सब लोग हर्ष और विषाद के वश हो रहे हैं। (हर्ष तो भोग सामग्रियों को और मुनि के तप प्रभाव को देखकर होता है और विषाद इस बात से होता है कि श्री राम के वियोग में नियम-व्रत से रहने वाले हम लोग भोग-विलास में क्यों आ फँसे, कहीं इनमें आसक्त होकर हमारा मन नियम-व्रतों को न त्याग दे) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3031.english_translation: It is springtime. Three kinds of cool, gentle, fragrant breezes are blowing. The four aims of life are easy to find for everyone. Seeing garlands, sandalwood, and pleasures like women, people are filled with both joy and unease.
ramacharitamanas::3031.translation_literal: ऋतु (season) / वसंत (spring) / बह (blows) / त्रिबिध (three kinds of) / बयारी (breezes) / सब कहँ (for everyone) / सुलभ (easily available) / पदारथ (things/aims) / चारी (four) / स्रक (garlands) / चंदन (sandalwood) / बनितादिक (women and such) / भोगा (pleasures) / देखि (seeing) / हरष (joy) / बिसमय (unease/wonder) / बस (under the control of) / लोगा (people)
ramacharitamanas::3031.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3031.essence: Pleasure is not the real test; your response to it is.
