ramacharitamanas::3031.simple_meaning: Spring has arrived, and everything pleasant is within reach. But the sight of pleasure also stirs mixed feelings in people, because comfort can awaken both delight and doubt.
ramacharitamanas::3031.simple_insight: Even abundance can unsettle you when your heart is trying to stay disciplined.
ramacharitamanas::3031.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat and the sages are living in the forest after Ram's exile. Spring brings beauty, fragrance, and ease, but that very abundance tests their restraint. The verse shows how desire and renunciation can rise together in the same heart.
ramacharitamanas::3031.modern_relevance: You walk into a wedding hall full of music, perfume, and laughter, but your mind tightens because you promised yourself not to get carried away. Plenty can feel like pressure when you are trying to stay steady.
ramacharitamanas::3031.insight: It shifts attention from outer comfort to the mind's response to comfort.

ramacharitamanas::3032.verse_sanskrit: संपति चकई भरतु चक मुनि आयस खेलवार। तेहि निसि आश्रम पिंजराँ राखे भा भिनुसार ॥
ramacharitamanas::3032.verse_hindi: सम्पत्ति (भोग-विलास की सामग्री) चकवी है और भरतजी चकवा हैं और मुनि की आज्ञा खेल है, जिसने उस रात को आश्रम रूपी पिंजड़े में दोनों को बंद कर रखा और ऐसे ही सबेरा हो गया। (जैसे किसी बहेलिए के द्वारा एक पिंजड़े में रखे जाने पर भी चकवी-चकवे का रात को संयोग नहीं होता, वैसे ही भारद्वाजजी की आज्ञा से रात भर भोग सामग्रियों के साथ रहने पर भी भरतजी ने मन से भी उनका स्पर्श तक नहीं किया।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3032.english_translation: Wealth was like a female chakwa bird, Bharat like the male chakwa, and the sage's command was the game. That night, the hermitage-cage held them both until dawn.
ramacharitamanas::3032.translation_literal: संपति (wealth) / चकई (female chakwa bird) / भरतु (Bharat) / चक (male chakwa bird) / मुनि (sage) / आयस (command) / खेलवार (game) / तेहि निसि (that night) / आश्रम (hermitage) / पिंजराँ (in a cage) / राखे (kept) / भा (became) / भिनुसार (dawn)
ramacharitamanas::3032.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3032.essence: True non-attachment stays untouched even in the middle of plenty.
ramacharitamanas::3032.simple_meaning: Bharat stayed among comforts, but his mind remained untouched. The verse compares him to a bird that stays near its mate without yielding to desire.
ramacharitamanas::3032.simple_insight: You can be surrounded by temptation and still remain inwardly free.
ramacharitamanas::3032.detailed_meaning: At Bharadvaja's hermitage, Bharat is kept through the night among luxury and comfort. Tulsidas compares wealth to a female chakwa and Bharat to the male, saying the sage's command held them in place until dawn, but desire never touched him.
ramacharitamanas::3032.modern_relevance: You are at a lavish wedding, everyone urging one more indulgence, one more drink, one more purchase. You can smile, stay courteous, and still not let the night own you.
ramacharitamanas::3032.insight: It trains the mind to remain close to pleasure without becoming captive to it.

ramacharitamanas::3033.verse_sanskrit: कीन्ह निमज्जनु तीरथराजा। नाई मुनिहि सिरु सहित समाजा। रिषि आयसु असीस सिर राखी। करि दंडवत बिनय बहु भाषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3033.verse_hindi: (प्रातःकाल) भरतजी ने तीर्थराज में स्नान किया और समाज सहित मुनि को सिर नवाकर और ऋषि की आज्ञा तथा आशीर्वाद को सिर चढ़ाकर दण्डवत् करके बहुत विनती की ॥
ramacharitamanas::3033.english_translation: At dawn, Bharata bathed at the king of pilgrimages, bowed his head with the sages, placed the sage's command and blessings above his own head, prostrated himself, and spoke many humble words.
ramacharitamanas::3033.translation_literal: कीन्ह (did) / निमज्जनु (bath/immersion) / तीरथराजा (king of pilgrimages) / नाई (bowing) / मुनिहि (to the sage) / सिरु (head) / सहित समाजा (with the assembly) / रिषि (sage) / आयसु (command) / असीस (blessings) / सिर राखी (placing on the head) / करि (doing) / दंडवत (prostration) / बिनय (humble request) / बहु (many) / भाषी (spoke)
ramacharitamanas::3033.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3033.essence: True service starts by lowering your head before guidance.
ramacharitamanas::3033.simple_meaning: Bharata bathes, bows to the sage, honors the sage's command and blessings, and humbly asks for guidance.
ramacharitamanas::3033.simple_insight: Real humility begins with putting guidance above your own pride.
ramacharitamanas::3033.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's season of grief and renunciation, Bharata stands before the sages with his companions. Before he takes another step toward Chitrakoot, he purifies himself, bows low, and accepts the sage's instruction as his own burden to carry.
ramacharitamanas::3033.modern_relevance: Before a difficult family conversation, you pause, take a breath, and listen fully instead of defending yourself. That quiet respect can change the whole direction of the day.
ramacharitamanas::3033.insight: It teaches you to begin a hard journey by honoring guidance, not asserting control.

ramacharitamanas::3034.verse_sanskrit: पथ गति कुसल साथ सब लीन्हें। चले चित्रकूटहिं चितु दीन्हें॥ रामसखा कर दीन्हें लागू। चलत देह धरि जनु अनुरागू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3034.verse_hindi: तदनन्तर रास्ते की पहचान रखने वाले लोगों (कुशल पथप्रदर्शकों) के साथ सब लोगों को लिए हुए भरतजी त्रिकूट में चित्त लगाए चले। भरतजी रामसखा गुह के हाथ में हाथ दिए हुए ऐसे जा रहे हैं, मानो साक्षात् प्रेम ही शरीर धारण किए हुए हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3034.english_translation: With skilled guides leading the way, they all set out, hearts fixed on Chitrakoot. Holding Ram's friend Guha by the hand, Bharat walked as if love itself had taken a body.
ramacharitamanas::3034.translation_literal: पथ-गति (path-knowledgeable) / कुसल (skilled) / साथ (with) / सब (all) / लीन्हें (took) / चले (walked) / चित्रकूटहिं (toward Chitrakoot) / चितु (mind) / दीन्हें (given)॥ / राम-सखा (Ram's friend) / करि (hand) / दीन्हें (gave) / लागू (held) / चलत (walking) / देह (body) / धरि (having taken) / जनु (as if) / अनुरागू (love)
ramacharitamanas::3034.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3034.essence: Love becomes visible when it walks beside someone.
ramacharitamanas::3034.simple_meaning: Bharat and the group travel toward Chitrakoot with careful guides. Bharat holds Guha's hand, and his whole journey feels like love in human form.
ramacharitamanas::3034.simple_insight: Real devotion shows up in how you walk, whom you hold, and where your heart is going.
ramacharitamanas::3034.detailed_meaning: Bharat has crossed from grief into action and is moving toward Ram in Chitrakoot. With experienced guides, he leads the group carefully and walks hand in hand with Guha, Ram's friend. The verse lingers on the tenderness of that journey.
ramacharitamanas::3034.modern_relevance: You leave at dawn with a friend whose family is hurting, and you stay close without needing to fix anything. Sometimes loyalty is just walking beside someone all the way there.
ramacharitamanas::3034.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to visible companionship and steady movement toward the beloved.

ramacharitamanas::3035.verse_sanskrit: नहिं पद त्रान सीस नहिं छाया। पेमु नेमु ब्रतु धरमु अमाया॥ लखन राम सिय पंथ कहानी। पूँछत सखहि कहत मृदु बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3035.verse_hindi: न तो उनके पैरों में जूते हैं और न सिर पर छाया है, उनका प्रेम नियम, व्रत और धर्म निष्कपट (सच्चा) है। वे सखा निषादराज से लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामचंद्रजी और सीताजी के रास्ते की बातें पूछते हैं और वह कोमल वाणी से कहता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3035.english_translation: They have no shoes on their feet and no shade over their heads. Their love, vows, and righteousness are utterly sincere. They ask the friendly guide about the path of Lakshman, Ram, and Sita, and he speaks gently.
ramacharitamanas::3035.translation_literal: नहिं (not) / पद (feet) / त्रान (shoes, protection) / सीस (head) / नहिं (not) / छाया (shade) / पेमु (love) / नेमु (vow, rule) / ब्रतु (vow, observance) / धरमु (righteous conduct) / अमाया (without deceit) / लखन (Lakshman) / राम (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / पंथ (path) / कहानी (talk, account) / पूँछत (asking) / सखहि (to the friend, guide) / कहत (speaks) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (speech)
ramacharitamanas::3035.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3035.essence: Love makes hardship feel like the only honest way to travel.
ramacharitamanas::3035.simple_meaning: Bharat and his companions travel humbly, with no comfort or display, and their devotion is genuine. They ask about the path taken by Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, and receive gentle guidance.
ramacharitamanas::3035.simple_insight: True devotion shows up in how you travel, ask, and listen.
ramacharitamanas::3035.detailed_meaning: Bharat is on the road toward Chitrakoot, still carrying the pain of Ram's exile. He and his companions move like renunciants, with no shoes and no shade, asking a local guide about the route Ram, Lakshman, and Sita took. The scene shows devotion becoming visible in ordinary movement.
ramacharitamanas::3035.modern_relevance: You walk into a place bareheaded, tired, and quiet, only wanting directions to someone you love. Even your simplest questions carry your loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::3035.insight: It shifts attention from outward comfort to inward sincerity in service.

ramacharitamanas::3036.verse_sanskrit: राम बास थल बिटप बिलोकें। उर अनुराग रहत नहिं रोकें॥ देखि दसा सुर बरिसहिं फूला। भइ मृदु महि मगु मंगल मूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3036.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी के ठहरने की जगहों और वृक्षों को देखकर उनके हृदय में प्रेम रोके नहीं रुकता। भरतजी की यह दशा देखकर देवता फूल बरसाने लगे। पृथ्वी कोमल हो गई और मार्ग मंगल का मूल बन गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3036.english_translation: Seeing the places where Ram had stayed and the trees along the way, Bharat's love could not be held back. Seeing his condition, the gods showered flowers. The earth became soft, and the road itself turned into a source of blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3036.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बास (dwelling) / थल (place) / बिटप (trees) / बिलोकें (seeing) / उर (heart) / अनुराग (love) / रहत (remaining) / नहिं (not) / रोकें (restrained)॥ / देखि (seeing) / दसा (condition) / सुर (devas) / बरिसहिं (shower) / फूला (flowers) / भइ (became) / मृदु (soft) / महि (earth) / मगु (road) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मूल (root)
ramacharitamanas::3036.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3036.essence: Love makes even a road sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3036.simple_meaning: Bharat sees the places connected with Ram and cannot contain his love. His devotion is so moving that even the world around him seems blessed.
ramacharitamanas::3036.simple_insight: Love that is real changes the atmosphere around you.
ramacharitamanas::3036.detailed_meaning: Bharat is walking toward Chitrakoot, following the trail of Ram's exile. Every tree and resting place reminds him of Ram's absence. His devotion is so intense that the scene itself feels transformed, and even the gods respond.
ramacharitamanas::3036.modern_relevance: You pass the café where someone once sat across from you, and your chest tightens. A place can hold love so strongly that even ordinary streets feel charged with memory.
ramacharitamanas::3036.insight: It shows how devotion can sanctify even a road, turning grief and longing into blessing.

ramacharitamanas::3037.verse_sanskrit: किएँ जाहिं छाया जलद सुखद बहइ बर बात। तस मगु भयउ न राम कहँ जस भा भरतहि जात ॥
ramacharitamanas::3037.verse_hindi: बादल छाया किए जा रहे हैं, सुख देने वाली सुंदर हवा बह रही है। भरतजी के जाते समय मार्ग जैसा सुखदायक हुआ, वैसा श्री रामचंद्रजी को भी नहीं हुआ था ॥
ramacharitamanas::3037.english_translation: The clouds gave shade and a pleasant breeze blew. The road for Bharat became as pleasant as it had never been for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3037.translation_literal: किएँ (making) / जाहिं (go) / छाया (shade) / जलद (clouds) / सुखद (pleasant) / बहइ (blows) / बर (good) / बात (wind) / तस (so) / मगु (road) / भयउ (became) / न (not) / राम (Ram) / कहँ (for) / जस (as) / भा (became) / भरतहि (for Bharat) / जात (while going)
ramacharitamanas::3037.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3037.essence: A devoted heart makes even the road feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::3037.simple_meaning: Nature itself seems to welcome Bharat’s journey. The road becomes gentle and blessed, as if the world is honoring his devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3037.simple_insight: Even the path feels kinder when your heart is pure.
ramacharitamanas::3037.detailed_meaning: Bharat is walking toward Ram in exile, and the forest road turns soft: clouds shade him and a cool breeze rises. Tulsidas pauses on this detail to show how Bharat’s devotion makes the journey itself feel auspicious.
ramacharitamanas::3037.modern_relevance: You leave home before sunrise to make a hard trip for someone you love, and even the cold air feels kind. Your heart changes the road.
ramacharitamanas::3037.insight: It shifts attention from the physical journey to the moral beauty of the one making it.

ramacharitamanas::3038.verse_sanskrit: जड़ चेतन मग जीव घनेरे। जे चितए प्रभु जिन्ह प्रभु हेरे॥ ते सब भए परम पद जोगू। भरत दरस मेटा भव रोगू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3038.verse_hindi: रास्ते में असंख्य जड़-चेतन जीव थे। उनमें से जिनको प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी ने देखा, अथवा जिन्होंने प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी को देखा, वे सब (उसी समय) परमपद के अधिकारी हो गए, परन्तु अब भरतजी के दर्शन ने तो उनका भव (जन्म-मरण) रूपी रोग मिटा ही दिया। (श्री रामदर्शन से तो वे परमपद के अधिकारी ही हुए थे, परन्तु भरत दर्शन से उन्हें वह परमपद प्राप्त हो गया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3038.english_translation: Countless living beings on the road were touched by the sight of Ram. Those who saw him, or whom he saw, reached the highest state. Bharat's sight removed the sickness of rebirth itself.
ramacharitamanas::3038.translation_literal: जड़ (inert) / चेतन (sentient) / मग (road) / जीव (living beings) / घनेरे (countless) / जे (who) / चितए (saw) / प्रभु (the Lord) / जिन्ह (those who) / प्रभु हेरे (the Lord saw) / ते (those) / सब (all) / भए (became) / परम पद (highest state) / जोगू (fit for) / भरत दरस (Bharat's sight) / मेटा (removed) / भव रोगू (the sickness of rebirth)
ramacharitamanas::3038.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3038.essence: Pure presence can free others without a word.
ramacharitamanas::3038.simple_meaning: Ram's sight blesses every being he meets, and Bharat's presence is so pure that it also frees others from the pain of repeated birth.
ramacharitamanas::3038.simple_insight: Being truly seen by purity changes you at the deepest level.
ramacharitamanas::3038.detailed_meaning: As Bharat walks toward Ram in Ayodhya, even the creatures on the road are transformed by that sacred atmosphere. Tulsidas says Ram's gaze and Bharat's gaze both carry liberating power, and Bharat's devotion softens the burden of existence around him.
ramacharitamanas::3038.modern_relevance: You enter a room already carrying stress, and one person’s steady kindness changes the whole atmosphere. Some people do not just notice you — they make life feel less heavy.
ramacharitamanas::3038.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary seeing to the transforming power of a pure presence.

ramacharitamanas::3039.verse_sanskrit: यह बड़ि बात भरत कइ नाहीं। सुमिरत जिनहि रामु मन माहीं॥ बारक राम कहत जग जेऊ। होत तरन तारन नर तेऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3039.verse_hindi: भरतजी के लिए यह कोई बड़ी बात नहीं है, जिन्हें श्री रामजी स्वयं अपने मन में स्मरण करते रहते हैं। जगत् में जो भी मनुष्य एक बार 'राम' कह लेते हैं, वे भी तरने-तारने वाले हो जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3039.english_translation: This is no great matter for Bharat. Anyone whom Ram remembers in his mind is already lifted across. In the world, whoever even once says 'Ram' becomes a boat that carries others across too.
ramacharitamanas::3039.translation_literal: यह (this) / बड़ि (great) / बात (matter) / भरत (Bharat's) / कइ (of) / नाहीं (not) / सुमिरत (remembering) / जिनहि (whom) / रामु (Ram) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / बारक (once) / राम (Ram) / कहत (saying) / जग (world) / जेऊ (living being) / होत (becomes) / तरन (to cross over) / तारन (to carry across) / नर (person) / तेऊ (that one)
ramacharitamanas::3039.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3039.essence: Ram's remembrance makes ordinary people into carriers of rescue.
ramacharitamanas::3039.simple_meaning: Being remembered by Ram is no small thing. Even one sincere utterance of his name can lift a person across life's struggle and help others too.
ramacharitamanas::3039.simple_insight: You don't have to earn divine attention; being held in remembrance is already grace.
ramacharitamanas::3039.detailed_meaning: As Bharat journeys in Ram's absence, Tulsidas pauses the grief and says something astonishing: Bharat's greatness is not self-made. Ram remembers him inwardly, and even the name of Ram has the power to carry a person across suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3039.modern_relevance: You open your phone and see one message from someone you deeply love — and suddenly the whole day feels different. Being held in someone's heart can change everything, and one sacred name can steady you the same way.
ramacharitamanas::3039.insight: It shifts attention from proving yourself to resting in remembrance, and from self-effort to the power of holy naming.

ramacharitamanas::3040.verse_sanskrit: भरतु राम प्रिय पुनि लघु भ्राता। कस न होइ मगु मंगलदाता॥ सिद्ध साधु मुनिबर अस कहहीं। भरतहि निरखि हरषु हियँ लहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3040.verse_hindi: फिर भरतजी तो श्री रामचंद्रजी के प्यारे तथा उनके छोटे भाई ठहरे। तब भला उनके लिए मार्ग मंगल (सुख) दायक कैसे न हो? सिद्ध, साधु और श्रेष्ठ मुनि ऐसा कह रहे हैं और भरतजी को देखकर हृदय में हर्ष लाभ करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3040.english_translation: Bharat is dear to Ram and is his younger brother. How could the road not become auspicious for him? Siddhas, saints, and great sages say this, and they feel joy in their hearts when they see Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::3040.translation_literal: भरतु (Bharat) / राम (Ram) / प्रिय (dear) / पुनि (also) / लघु (younger) / भ्राता (brother) / कस (how) / न (not) / होइ (become) / मगु (road) / मंगलदाता (giver of auspiciousness) / सिद्ध (accomplished beings) / साधु (saints) / मुनिबर (great sages) / अस (thus) / कहहीं (say) / भरतहि (Bharat) / निरखि (seeing) / हरषु (joy) / हियँ (in the heart) / लहहीं (they obtain)
ramacharitamanas::3040.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3040.essence: Belovedness itself makes the road auspicious.
ramacharitamanas::3040.simple_meaning: Bharat is so dear to Ram that even his path becomes blessed. Saints and sages rejoice just by seeing him.
ramacharitamanas::3040.simple_insight: Being held in loving regard can change the whole atmosphere around you.
ramacharitamanas::3040.detailed_meaning: On the road where Bharat is travelling, the sages see more than a prince. They see Ram’s beloved younger brother, and that changes everything. His presence itself feels fortunate, so much so that wise beings feel joy just looking at him.
ramacharitamanas::3040.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after helping someone you love through a hard week. Nothing about the furniture changed, but the whole place feels lighter. Bharat’s presence works like that.
ramacharitamanas::3040.insight: It shifts attention from status to relationship: closeness to Ram makes ordinary movement feel sacred.

ramacharitamanas::3041.verse_sanskrit: देखि प्रभाउ सुरेसहि सोचू। जगु भल भलेहि पोच कहुँ पोचू॥ गुर सन कहेउ करिअ प्रभु सोई। रामहि भरतहि भेंट न होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3041.verse_hindi: भरतजी के (इस प्रेम के) प्रभाव को देखकर देवराज इन्द्र को सोच हो गया (कि कहीं इनके प्रेमवश श्री रामजी लौट न जाएँ और हमारा बना-बनाया काम बिगड़ जाए)। संसार भले के लिए भला और बुरे के लिए बुरा है (मनुष्य जैसा आप होता है जगत् उसे वैसा ही दिखता है)। उसने गुरु बृहस्पतिजी से कहा- हे प्रभो! वही उपाय कीजिए जिससे श्री रामचंद्रजी और भरतजी की भेंट ही न हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3041.english_translation: Seeing the power of Bharat's love, Indra grew anxious. The world seems good to the good and bad to the bad. He told Brihaspati, 'Do whatever is needed so Ram and Bharat do not meet.'
ramacharitamanas::3041.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / प्रभाउ (power, influence) / सुरेसहि (to Indra) / सोचू (anxiety) / जगु (the world) / भल (good) / भलेहि (to the good) / पोच (bad) / कहुँ (to) / पोचू (bad)॥ गुर (teacher Brihaspati) / सन (to) / कहेउ (said) / करिअ (do) / प्रभु (lord) / सोई (that) / रामहि (Ram) / भरतहि (Bharat) / भेंट (meeting) / न (not) / होई (happen) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3041.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3041.essence: Love so pure can make control itself feel unsafe.
ramacharitamanas::3041.simple_meaning: Bharat's love is so powerful that even Indra worries. He fears Ram and Bharat meeting, because their love could overturn the situation.
ramacharitamanas::3041.simple_insight: Real love can unsettle even the powers that think they are in control.
ramacharitamanas::3041.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's devotion has become so intense that even Indra feels threatened. Watching this, he asks Brihaspati to prevent Ram and Bharat from meeting, because their love could change everything.
ramacharitamanas::3041.modern_relevance: You finally see two people about to reconcile after a long silence, and someone panics because the truth might undo their control. Love can be more disruptive than power.
ramacharitamanas::3041.insight: It shows that sincere devotion can disturb worldly arrangements and expose how fragile control really is.

ramacharitamanas::3042.verse_sanskrit: रामु सँकोची प्रेम बस भरत सप्रेम पयोधि। बनी बात बेगरन चहति करिअ जतनु छलु सोधि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3042.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी संकोची और प्रेम के वश हैं और भरतजी प्रेम के समुद्र हैं। बनी-बनाई बात बिगड़ना चाहती है, इसलिए कुछ छल ढूँढकर इसका उपाय कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3042.english_translation: Ram is modest and moved by love, while Bharat is a sea of love. The settled matter seems ready to break, so find some trick and a way to set it right.
ramacharitamanas::3042.translation_literal: रामु (Ram) / सँकोची (modest, reserved) / प्रेम (love) / बस (under the control of) / भरत (Bharat) / सप्रेम (full of love) / पयोधि (ocean) / बनी बात (settled matter) / बेगरन (to break) / चहति (wants) / करिअ (do) / जतनु (effort, care) / छलु (a stratagem) / सोधि (find out, devise)
ramacharitamanas::3042.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3042.essence: Love can create peace, and peace can still be fragile.
ramacharitamanas::3042.simple_meaning: Ram is gentle and moved by love, while Bharat is pure love itself. Because the situation is delicate, careful action is needed to keep things from falling apart.
ramacharitamanas::3042.simple_insight: Love can hold a fragile peace together, but it still needs wise care.
ramacharitamanas::3042.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's devotion has created a delicate peace around Ram's return. Ram is soft-hearted and modest; Bharat is all love. The gods fear that one wrong move could undo everything, so they quietly look for a way to protect the moment.
ramacharitamanas::3042.modern_relevance: You finally got two estranged siblings to sit in the same room after years of silence. Everyone can feel how fragile it is. One careless sentence could undo weeks of healing.
ramacharitamanas::3042.insight: It teaches you to treat a hard-won harmony as something fragile and worth protecting with skill.

ramacharitamanas::3043.verse_sanskrit: बचन सुनत सुरगुरु मुसुकाने। सहसनयन बिनु लोचन जाने॥ मायापति सेवक सन माया। करइ त उलटि परइ सुरराया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3043.verse_hindi: इंद्र के वचन सुनते ही देवगुरु बृहस्पतिजी मुस्कुराए। उन्होंने हजार नेत्रों वाले इंद्र को (ज्ञान रूपी) नेत्रोंरहित (मूर्ख) समझा और कहा- हे देवराज! माया के स्वामी श्री रामचंद्रजी के सेवक के साथ कोई माया करता है तो वह उलटकर अपने ही ऊपर आ पड़ती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3043.english_translation: At Indra's words, the teacher of the gods smiled. He saw the thousand-eyed king as blind without true sight: anyone who tries trickery against the servant of the master of illusion has that trickery turn back on himself.
ramacharitamanas::3043.translation_literal: बचन (words) / सुनत (upon hearing) / सुरगुरु (teacher of the gods) / मुसुकाने (smiled) / सहसनयन (thousand-eyed) / बिनु (without) / लोचन (eyes) / जाने (understood)॥ / मायापति (master of illusion) / सेवक (servant) / सन (with) / माया (trickery / illusion) / करइ (does) / त (then) / उलटि (reversed) / परइ (falls) / सुरराया (king of the gods)॥
ramacharitamanas::3043.speaker: Brihaspati
ramacharitamanas::3043.essence: What you use against Ram's servant turns back on you.
ramacharitamanas::3043.simple_meaning: Brihaspati smiles at Indra's plan and warns him that any trick used against Ram's devotee will rebound on the trickster.
ramacharitamanas::3043.simple_insight: Trying to outsmart devotion only exposes your own confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3043.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Indra worries that Bharat's devotion may upset the plan to keep Ram away. Brihaspati smiles at that fear and corrects him: Ram protects his servant, and any deceit aimed at that servant will boomerang.
ramacharitamanas::3043.modern_relevance: You try to manipulate a loyal friend into changing their mind, and the whole plan collapses in your own hands. Pressure aimed at devotion often reveals your own weakness.
ramacharitamanas::3043.insight: It shifts the mind from strategic control to reverence for what cannot be manipulated.

ramacharitamanas::3044.verse_sanskrit: तब किछु कीन्ह राम रुख जानी। अब कुचालि करि होइहि हानी। सुनु सुरेस रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। निज अपराध रिसाहिं न काऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3044.verse_hindi: उस समय (पिछली बार) तो श्री रामचंद्रजी का रुख जानकर कुछ किया था, परन्तु इस समय कुचाल करने से हानि ही होगी। हे देवराज! श्री रघुनाथजी का स्वभाव सुनो, वे अपने प्रति किए हुए अपराध से कभी रुष्ट नहीं होते ॥
ramacharitamanas::3044.english_translation: At one time, knowing Ram's mood, some action was taken. But now, if you resort to trickery, it will only bring harm. Listen, lord of the gods: hear the nature of Raghunath. He is never angered by an offense done against himself.
ramacharitamanas::3044.translation_literal: तब (then) / किछु (some) / कीन्ह (did) / राम रुख (Ram's mood) / जानी (knowing) / अब (now) / कुचालि (trickery) / करि (doing) / होइहि (will happen) / हानी (loss) । सुनु (listen) / सुरेस (lord of the gods) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / सुभाऊ (nature) / निज (own) / अपराध (offense) / रिसाहिं (become angry) / न (not) / काऊ (ever)
ramacharitamanas::3044.speaker: Brahma
ramacharitamanas::3044.essence: Ram cannot be manipulated by offense; only deceit brings harm back to you.
ramacharitamanas::3044.simple_meaning: Ram does not get angry when someone harms him personally. Trying to deceive him will only backfire and bring loss.
ramacharitamanas::3044.simple_insight: You can stop fearing that honesty will make you vulnerable with the divine.
ramacharitamanas::3044.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the gods are trying to understand Ram's response to events around Bharat and the throne. Brahma explains that Ram may once have responded to a situation in a certain way, but trickery now will only fail. Ram's own hurt never turns into rage.
ramacharitamanas::3044.modern_relevance: You replay a harsh message in your head, ready to defend yourself or strike back. This verse says the deepest strength does not need revenge; it cannot be manipulated by your offense.
ramacharitamanas::3044.insight: It shifts attention from protecting your ego to trusting a presence that cannot be shaken by insult.

ramacharitamanas::3045.verse_sanskrit: जो अपराधु भगत कर करई। राम रोष पावक सो जरई॥ लोकहुँ बेद बिदित इतिहासा। यह महिमा जानहिं दुरबासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3045.verse_hindi: पर जो कोई उनके भक्त का अपराध करता है, वह श्री राम की क्रोधाग्नि में जल जाता है। लोक और वेद दोनों में इतिहास (कथा) प्रसिद्ध है। इस महिमा को दुर्वासाजी जानते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3045.english_translation: Anyone who wrongs Ram's devotee is burned by Ram's fire of anger. This story is known in the world and in the Vedas; Durvasa knows this greatness.
ramacharitamanas::3045.translation_literal: जो (who) / अपराधु (offense) / भगत (devotee) / कर (doing) / करई (does) / राम (Ram) / रोष (anger) / पावक (fire) / सो (that) / जरई (burns) ॥ / लोकहुँ (in the world too) / बेद (Veda) / बिदित (known) / इतिहासा (story) / यह (this) / महिमा (greatness) / जानहिं (know) / दुरबासा (Durvasa) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3045.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3045.essence: Ram's anger rises for anyone who harms his devotee.
ramacharitamanas::3045.simple_meaning: Harming a devoted follower of Ram brings Ram's fierce response. The verse says this is a well-known truth, remembered in tradition and scripture.
ramacharitamanas::3045.simple_insight: Devotion is not fragile here; it is protected by a force bigger than pride.
ramacharitamanas::3045.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the sages are recalling how even powerful beings must respect Ram's devotees. The verse warns that offending a devotee is not a small social mistake; it invites Ram's burning anger, and the story of Durvasa is cited as proof.
ramacharitamanas::3045.modern_relevance: You mock someone because they are gentle, faithful, or deeply devoted, thinking no one will answer for it. This verse says that cruelty toward the devoted does not stay hidden forever.
ramacharitamanas::3045.insight: It shifts the mind from casual contempt to reverence for those who serve with sincerity.

ramacharitamanas::3046.verse_sanskrit: भरत सरिस को राम सनेही। जगु जप राम रामु जप जेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3046.verse_hindi: सारा जगत् श्री राम को जपता है, वे श्री रामजी जिनको जपते हैं, उन भरतजी के समान श्री रामचंद्रजी का प्रेमी कौन होगा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3046.english_translation: Who loves Ram like Bharat? The whole world chants Ram, and Ram chants the name of Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::3046.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / सरिस (like) / को (who) / राम (Ram) / सनेही (beloved, lover) / जगु (world) / जप (chants, repeats) / राम (Ram) / रामु (Ram) / जप (chants, repeats) / जेही (whose, whom)
ramacharitamanas::3046.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3046.essence: Bharat's devotion is so pure that Ram himself returns it.
ramacharitamanas::3046.simple_meaning: Bharat's love for Ram is so complete that it becomes the standard for devotion. The verse also says Ram holds Bharat in equal affection.
ramacharitamanas::3046.simple_insight: Love feels deepest when it is mutual, steady, and free of self-interest.
ramacharitamanas::3046.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's devotion has become famous. The world repeats Ram's name, but this verse lifts Bharat up as the rare one whose love for Ram is matched by Ram's love for him. It is praise for pure, reciprocal devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3046.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone who never forgets your kindness. In a world full of noisy affection, this verse honors the bond where care is returned without calculation.
ramacharitamanas::3046.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to relationship, showing that true love is recognised and answered.

ramacharitamanas::3047.verse_sanskrit: मनहुँ न आनिअ अमरपति रघुबर भगत अकाजु। अजसु लोक परलोक दुख दिन दिन सोक समाजु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3047.verse_hindi: हे देवराज! रघुकुलश्रेष्ठ श्री रामचंद्रजी के भक्त का काम बिगाड़ने की बात मन में भी न लाइए। ऐसा करने से लोक में अपयश और परलोक में दुःख होगा और शोक का सामान दिनोंदिन बढ़ता ही चला जाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3047.english_translation: O lord of the gods, do not even think of harming the work of Ram's devotee. It brings disgrace in this world, sorrow in the next, and a growing burden of grief day by day.
ramacharitamanas::3047.translation_literal: मनहुँ (even in the mind) / न (not) / आनिअ (bring) / अमरपति (lord of the gods) / रघुबर (Ram, best of the Raghu line) / भगत (devotee's) / अकाजु (harmful work) / अजसु (disgrace) / लोक (in this world) / परलोक (in the next world) / दुख (sorrow) / दिन दिन (day by day) / सोक (grief) / समाजु (heap, burden)
ramacharitamanas::3047.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3047.essence: Hurt Ram's devotee, and sorrow follows you home.
ramacharitamanas::3047.simple_meaning: Do not interfere with the work of Ram's devotee. Doing so brings shame now and sorrow later, and grief keeps increasing.
ramacharitamanas::3047.simple_insight: Respect for devotion protects you from needless shame and suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3047.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the gods are being warned not to obstruct Bharat's devotion to Ram. The verse turns a social rule into a spiritual warning: harming a true devotee damages your standing now and your peace later.
ramacharitamanas::3047.modern_relevance: You try to sabotage someone who is quietly doing the right thing, and it backfires. The damage is not just to them — your own name, mind, and sleep start to unravel.
ramacharitamanas::3047.insight: It teaches you to stop opposing sincere devotion, because resistance to it rebounds as inner and outer pain.

ramacharitamanas::3048.verse_sanskrit: सुनु सुरेस उपदेसु हमारा। रामहि सेवकु परम पिआरा॥ मानत सुखु सेवक सेवकाईं। सेवक बैर बैरु अधिकाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3048.verse_hindi: हे देवराज! हमारा उपदेश सुनो। श्री रामजी को अपना सेवक परम प्रिय है। वे अपने सेवक की सेवा से सुख मानते हैं और सेवक के साथ वैर करने से बड़ा भारी वैर मानते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3048.english_translation: Listen, Indra: this is my counsel. Ram is especially dear to a servant. He takes joy in a servant's service, and he counts enmity toward a servant as a great wrong.
ramacharitamanas::3048.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / सुरेस (lord of the gods) / उपदेसु (instruction) / हमारा (our) / रामहि (to Ram) / सेवकु (servant) / परम (supremely) / पिआरा (dear) ॥ / मानत (counting/considering) / सुखु (joy) / सेवक (servant) / सेवकाईं (service of a servant) / और / सेवक (servant) / बैर (enmity) / बैरु (enmity) / अधिकाईं (very great) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3048.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3048.essence: Ram is closest to the one who serves him.
ramacharitamanas::3048.simple_meaning: Ram is deeply pleased by the service of his devotee. Helping a devotee brings him joy, and harming a devotee is a serious wrong.
ramacharitamanas::3048.simple_insight: Your devotion is never ignored; it is received with love and protection.
ramacharitamanas::3048.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Shiva is instructing Indra about the nature of Ram's heart. The context is Bharat's devotion and the danger of blocking it. Shiva says Ram values a servant above all, rejoices in that service, and treats hostility toward a servant as a major offense.
ramacharitamanas::3048.modern_relevance: You quietly help someone who can never repay you, and the work itself feels sacred. This verse says such service is seen, honored, and protected.
ramacharitamanas::3048.insight: It shifts devotion from a private feeling to a relationship that changes how you act toward others.

ramacharitamanas::3049.verse_sanskrit: जद्यपि सम नहिं राग न रोषू। गहहिं न पाप पूनु गुन दोषू॥ करम प्रधान बिस्व करि राखा। जो जस करइ सो तस फलु चाखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3049.verse_hindi: यद्यपि वे सम हैं- उनमें न राग है, न रोष है और न वे किसी का पाप-पुण्य और गुण-दोष ही ग्रहण करते हैं। उन्होंने विश्व में कर्म को ही प्रधान कर रखा है। जो जैसा करता है, वह वैसा ही फल भोगता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3049.english_translation: Although they are even-minded, free from attachment and anger, and do not take up anyone's virtue or fault, they have made the world governed by action. Whoever does as they do, tastes that result.
ramacharitamanas::3049.translation_literal: जद्यपि (although) / सम (equal) / नहिं (not) / राग (attachment) / न (not) / रोषू (anger) / गहहिं (they grasp) / न (not) / पाप (sin) / पूनु (virtue) / गुन (qualities) / दोषू (faults) / करम (action) / प्रधान (chief) / बिस्व (world) / करि (having made) / राखा (kept) / जो (who) / जस (as) / करइ (does) / सो (that) / तस (so) / फलु (fruit/result) / चाखा (tastes)
ramacharitamanas::3049.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3049.essence: Evenness does not cancel consequence; action still bears its own fruit.
ramacharitamanas::3049.simple_meaning: The divine is beyond attachment, anger, praise, and blame, yet the world still runs on action. What you do returns to you in kind.
ramacharitamanas::3049.simple_insight: There is relief in a world that is fair without being emotional.
ramacharitamanas::3049.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the conversation is turning toward how Ram relates to the world. Tulsidas says Ram remains beyond personal likes and dislikes, but the universe still works by action and consequence. That balance sets up the next verse on how Ram treats devotees differently.
ramacharitamanas::3049.modern_relevance: You can sit in a meeting and stay calm when someone criticises you, but your preparation still shows in the result. The world may not mirror your mood, yet it answers your actions.
ramacharitamanas::3049.insight: It shifts attention from emotional fairness to lawful consequence: what you do matters, even when the higher order is unmoved.

ramacharitamanas::3050.verse_sanskrit: तदपि करहिं सम बिषम बिहारा। भगत अभगत हृदय अनुसारा॥ अगनु अलेप अमान एकरस। रामु सगुन भए भगत प्रेम बस ॥
ramacharitamanas::3050.verse_hindi: तथापि वे भक्त और अभक्त के हृदय के अनुसार सम और विषम व्यवहार करते हैं (भक्त को प्रेम से गले लगा लेते हैं और अभक्त को मारकर तार देते हैं)। गुणरहित, निर्लेप, मानरहित और सदा एकरस भगवान् श्री राम भक्त के प्रेमवश ही सगुण हुए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3050.english_translation: Still, they behave differently according to the hearts of devotees and non-devotees. Though without form, untouched, self-respecting, and ever one, Ram took form only because of a devotee's love.
ramacharitamanas::3050.translation_literal: तदपि (still) / करहिं (do) / सम (equal) / बिषम (unequal) / बिहारा (conduct) / भगत (devotee) / अभगत (non-devotee) / हृदय (heart) / अनुसारा (according to)॥ / अगनु (without form) / अलेप (untouched) / अमान (without pride) / एकरस (ever one) / रामु (Ram) / सगुन (with form) / भए (became) / भगत (devotee's) / प्रेम (love) / बस (under the sway)
ramacharitamanas::3050.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3050.essence: Love makes the formless one meet you in form.
ramacharitamanas::3050.simple_meaning: Ram responds differently to devotees and non-devotees, and his own form appears because of a devotee's love.
ramacharitamanas::3050.simple_insight: Love is not just received here — it changes how the divine appears to you.
ramacharitamanas::3050.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas explains Ram's nature after saying Ram is beyond liking and dislike. Even so, Ram meets each heart in its own way. For the devotee, love itself becomes the reason the formless Ram takes form.
ramacharitamanas::3050.modern_relevance: You sit in a quiet room after a hard day, and the same prayer feels distant one night and near the next. This verse says the difference is not in Ram's care, but in the heart that calls.
ramacharitamanas::3050.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract belief to lived relationship: your inner state shapes how presence is experienced.

ramacharitamanas::3051.verse_sanskrit: राम सदा सेवक रुचि राखी। बेद पुरान साधु सुर साखी॥ अस जियँ जानि तजहु कुटिलाई। करहु भरत पद प्रीति सुहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3051.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी सदा अपने सेवकों (भक्तों) की रुचि रखते आए हैं। वेद, पुराण, साधु और देवता इसके साक्षी हैं। ऐसा हृदय में जानकर कुटिलता छोड़ दो और भरतजी के चरणों में सुंदर प्रीति करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3051.english_translation: Ram has always favored those who serve him. The Vedas, Puranas, sages, and radiant beings all bear witness. Knowing this in your heart, let go of crookedness and hold lovely love for Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::3051.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सदा (always) / सेवक (servants) / रुचि (liking, favor) / राखी (kept) / बेद (Vedas) / पुरान (Puranas) / साधु (sages) / सुर (radiant beings) / साखी (witnesses) // अस (thus) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानि (knowing) / तजहु (leave) / कुटिलाई (crookedness) / करहु (do) / भरत (Bharat) / पद (feet) / प्रीति (love) / सुहाई (lovely)
ramacharitamanas::3051.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3051.essence: Love for Ram shows itself as clean loyalty, not cleverness.
ramacharitamanas::3051.simple_meaning: Ram naturally favors those who serve him. Knowing that, drop all duplicity and offer sincere love to Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::3051.simple_insight: Devotion becomes easier when you trust that love is already being met.
ramacharitamanas::3051.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the crisis around Ram’s exile has turned family loyalty into a spiritual test. Tulsidas reminds the listener that Ram has always cherished his servants, and that this truth should soften envy and crookedness toward Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::3051.modern_relevance: You’re tempted to judge someone who stayed loyal while others chased status. Then you remember: real devotion does not compete. It bows, trusts, and loves cleanly.
ramacharitamanas::3051.insight: It shifts attention from rivalry to sincere service, especially where loyalty is being tested.

ramacharitamanas::3052.verse_sanskrit: राम भगत परहित निरत पर दुख दुखी दयाल। भगत सिरोमनि भरत तें जनि डरपहु सुरपाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::3052.verse_hindi: हे देवराज इंद्र! श्री रामचंद्रजी के भक्त सदा दूसरों के हित में लगे रहते हैं, वे दूसरों के दुःख से दुःखी और दयालु होते हैं। फिर भरतजी तो भक्तों के शिरोमणि हैं, उनसे बिलकुल न डरो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3052.english_translation: Ram's devotees are devoted to others' welfare, pained by others' pain, and full of compassion. Bharata, the best among devotees, is even more beyond fear, O king of the gods.
ramacharitamanas::3052.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / भगत (devotee) / परहित (others' welfare) / निरत (engaged) / पर दुख (others' pain) / दुखी (pained) / दयाल (compassionate) / भगत सिरोमनि (crest-jewel of devotees) / भरत (Bharata) / तें (than) / जनि (do not) / डरपहु (be afraid) / सुरपाल (king of the gods)
ramacharitamanas::3052.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3052.essence: Devotion shows itself as compassion for other people's pain.
ramacharitamanas::3052.simple_meaning: True devotees care for other people's good, feel their pain, and act with compassion. Bharata is held up as the finest example, so even Indra need not fear him.
ramacharitamanas::3052.simple_insight: Devotion is proven by how deeply you care when someone else suffers.
ramacharitamanas::3052.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the speaker reassures Indra while praising Bharata. Ram's true devotees are not self-seeking; they are moved by others' welfare and pain. Bharata stands as the highest example of that compassionate devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3052.modern_relevance: Your friend texts at midnight after a breakup, and you stop scrolling to listen. You don't fix everything. You stay present, and their pain matters to you. That's the shape of real devotion here.
ramacharitamanas::3052.insight: It shifts devotion from private feeling to outward care and shared suffering.

ramacharitamanas::3053.verse_sanskrit: सत्यसंध प्रभु सुर हितकारी। भरत राम आयस अनुसारी॥ स्वारथ बिबस बिकल तुम्ह होहू। भरत दोसु नहिं राउर मोहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3053.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी सत्यप्रतिज्ञ और देवताओं का हित करने वाले हैं और भरतजी श्री रामजी की आज्ञा के अनुसार चलने वाले हैं। तुम व्यर्थ ही स्वार्थ के विशेष वश होकर व्याकुल हो रहे हो। इसमें भरतजी का कोई दोष नहीं, तुम्हारा ही मोह है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3053.english_translation: The Lord is true to His vow and works for the good of the radiant beings. Bharat follows Ram's command. You are only agitated by selfish attachment; Bharat has no fault here. Your delusion is the problem.
ramacharitamanas::3053.translation_literal: सत्यसंध (true to vow) / प्रभु (Lord) / सुर (radiant beings) / हितकारी (benefactor) / भरत (Bharat) / राम (Ram) / आयस (command) / अनुसारी (following) / स्वारथ (self-interest) / बिबस (overpowered) / बिकल (disturbed) / तुम्ह (you) / होहू (are) / भरत (Bharat) / दोसु (fault) / नहिं (not) / राउर (your) / मोहू (delusion)
ramacharitamanas::3053.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3053.essence: True duty is clear; blame often comes from your own attachment.
ramacharitamanas::3053.simple_meaning: Ram stays true to his promise, and Bharat simply follows Ram's command. The real problem is not Bharat's conduct but the speaker's selfish confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3053.simple_insight: It softens blame and turns the mind back toward its own attachment.
ramacharitamanas::3053.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the gods are watching Bharat's refusal of power and his loyalty to Ram. A divine voice sets the record straight: Ram keeps faith, Bharat obeys, and the real distortion is self-centered confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3053.modern_relevance: You blame the coworker who followed the plan exactly, while your own attachment to control keeps burning underneath. The verse asks you to see the real source of the upset.
ramacharitamanas::3053.insight: It shifts attention from blaming another person's conduct to noticing your own attachment and confusion.

ramacharitamanas::3054.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुरबर सुरगुर बर बानी। भा प्रमोदु मन मिटी गलानी॥ बरषि प्रसून हरषि सुरराऊ। लगे सराहन भरत सुभाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3054.verse_hindi: देवगुरु बृहस्पतिजी की श्रेष्ठ वाणी सुनकर इंद्र के मन में बड़ा आनंद हुआ और उनकी चिंता मिट गई। तब हर्षित होकर देवराज फूल बरसाकर भरतजी के स्वभाव की सराहना करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3054.english_translation: Hearing the excellent words of the best of the gods and the teacher of the gods, Indra felt great joy and his worry disappeared. Then, delighted, the lord of the gods showered flowers and began praising Bharat's nature.
ramacharitamanas::3054.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुरबर (best of the radiant beings) / सुरगुर (teacher of the radiant beings) / बर (excellent) / बानी (speech) / भा (became) / प्रमोदु (joy) / मन (mind) / मिटी (removed) / गलानी (worry) / बरषि (showering) / प्रसून (flowers) / हरषि (delighted) / सुरराऊ (lord of the radiant beings) / लगे (began) / सराहन (to praise) / भरत (Bharat) / सुभाऊ (nature)
ramacharitamanas::3054.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3054.essence: Bharat's character is so pure it wins praise from heaven itself.
ramacharitamanas::3054.simple_meaning: Indra hears Brihaspati's words, feels relieved, showers flowers, and praises Bharat's noble nature.
ramacharitamanas::3054.simple_insight: True nobility makes even the heavens relax.
ramacharitamanas::3054.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the gods are watching Bharat's extraordinary loyalty and grief. After Brihaspati speaks, Indra's worry lifts. He responds with joy, rain of flowers, and praise, recognizing Bharat's character as something rare and worthy.
ramacharitamanas::3054.modern_relevance: You hear someone defend a person you had misjudged, and your resistance softens. The tension drops, and you finally see the goodness you had overlooked.
ramacharitamanas::3054.insight: It shifts attention from suspicion to recognition of virtue.

ramacharitamanas::3055.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि भरत चले मग जाहीं। दसा देखि मुनि सिद्ध सिहाहीं॥ जबहि रामु कहि लेहिं उसासा। उमगत प्रेमु मनहुँ चहु पासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3055.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार भरतजी मार्ग में चले जा रहे हैं। उनकी (प्रेममयी) दशा देखकर मुनि और सिद्ध लोग भी सिहाते हैं। भरतजी जब भी 'राम' कहकर लंबी साँस लेते हैं, तभी मानो चारों ओर प्रेम उमड़ पड़ता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3055.english_translation: In this way Bharat kept walking along the road. Seeing his condition, sages and perfected beings felt humbled. Whenever Bharat sighs and says 'Ram,' love seems to overflow from every direction.
ramacharitamanas::3055.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / भरत (Bharat) / चले (walked) / मग (road) / जाहीं (going) / दसा (condition) / देखि (seeing) / मुनि (sages) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / सिहाहीं (feel humbled) / जबहि (whenever) / रामु (Ram) / कहि (saying) / लेहिं (take) / उसासा (sigh) / उमगत (overflowing) / प्रेमु (love) / मनहुँ (as if) / चहु पासा (on all four sides)
ramacharitamanas::3055.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3055.essence: Love for Ram makes even longing feel luminous.
ramacharitamanas::3055.simple_meaning: Bharat walks on with such love and longing for Ram that even holy beings are awed. Every breath and mention of Ram seems to spread devotion all around him.
ramacharitamanas::3055.simple_insight: Real devotion changes your whole presence; it becomes visible even to people who have seen everything.
ramacharitamanas::3055.detailed_meaning: Bharat is on the road, carrying the weight of exile, love, and obedience to Ram. His grief-filled devotion is so intense that sages and perfected beings are astonished. Even his sighs carry Ram's name, and the air around him feels saturated with love.
ramacharitamanas::3055.modern_relevance: You sit in the back seat after a long train ride to see someone you love, exhausted but unable to stop thinking their name. That kind of longing changes the whole room before you even speak.
ramacharitamanas::3055.insight: It shifts attention from outward achievement to the radiance created by wholehearted devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3056.verse_sanskrit: द्रवहिं बचन सुनि कुलिस पषाना। पुरजन पेमु न जाइ बखाना॥ बीच बास करि जमुनहिं आए। निरखि नीरु लोचन जल छाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3056.verse_hindi: उनके (प्रेम और दीनता से पूर्ण) वचनों को सुनकर वज्र और पत्थर भी पिघल जाते हैं। अयोध्यावासियों का प्रेम कहते नहीं बनता। बीच में निवास (मुकाम) करके भरतजी यमुनाजी के तट पर आए। यमुनाजी का जल देखकर उनके नेत्रों में जल भर आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3056.english_translation: Hearing those tender words, even thunderbolts and stone would melt. The love of the people of Ayodhya cannot be fully described. After resting along the way, Bharat came to the bank of the Yamuna. Seeing the water, his eyes filled with tears.
ramacharitamanas::3056.translation_literal: द्रवहिं (melt) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / कुलिस (thunderbolt) / पषाना (stones) / पुरजन (townspeople) / पेमु (love) / न जाइ (cannot be) / बखाना (described) / बीच (in between) / बास (stay) / करि (having done) / जमुनहिं (to the Yamuna) / आए (came) / निरखि (seeing) / नीरु (water) / लोचन (eyes) / जल (water/tears) / छाए (filled)
ramacharitamanas::3056.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3056.essence: Humility melts hardness, and grief rises at the sight of home.
ramacharitamanas::3056.simple_meaning: Bharat's humble words move everyone deeply. The people of Ayodhya love him beyond words. When he reaches the Yamuna, the sight of water brings tears to his eyes.
ramacharitamanas::3056.simple_insight: True humility softens even the hardest hearts and makes grief visible without any effort to hide it.
ramacharitamanas::3056.detailed_meaning: Bharat is travelling toward Ram with a heart full of devotion and sorrow. His words are so tender that even hardness seems to melt, and Ayodhya's people cannot contain their love for him. Reaching the Yamuna, he breaks into tears.
ramacharitamanas::3056.modern_relevance: You say something honest and humble in a family conversation, and the room changes. Later, a simple sight — a river, a cup, a place you shared — suddenly opens the grief you were carrying.
ramacharitamanas::3056.insight: It shows how sincerity disarms resistance and how grief can surface through ordinary sensory moments.

ramacharitamanas::3057.verse_sanskrit: रघुबर बरन बिलोकि बर बारि समेत समाज। होत मगन बारिधि बिरह चढ़े बिबेक जहाज ॥
ramacharitamanas::3057.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी के (श्याम) रंग का सुंदर जल देखकर सारे समाज सहित भरतजी (प्रेम विह्वल होकर) श्री रामजी के विरह रूपी समुद्र में डूबते-डूबते विवेक रूपी जहाज पर चढ़ गए (अर्थात् यमुनाजी का श्यामवर्ण जल देखकर सब लोग श्यामवर्ण भगवान के प्रेम में विह्वल हो गए और उन्हें न पाकर विरह व्यथा से पीड़ित हो गए, तब भरतजी को यह ध्यान आया कि जल्दी चलकर उनके साक्षात् दर्शन करेंगे, इस विवेक से वे फिर उत्साहित हो गए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3057.english_translation: Seeing the lovely dark-blue sight of Raghubar, Bharata and the whole company were lost in love, then climbed back onto the boat of discernment in the ocean of separation.
ramacharitamanas::3057.translation_literal: रघुबर (Raghubar, Ram) / बरन (color) / बिलोकि (seeing) / बर (beautiful) / बारि (water) / समेत (along with) / समाज (company) / होत (becoming) / मगन (immersed) / बारिधि (ocean) / बिरह (separation) / चढ़े (climbed) / बिबेक (discernment) / जहाज (boat)
ramacharitamanas::3057.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3057.essence: Love can flood you, and discernment can still carry you forward.
ramacharitamanas::3057.simple_meaning: The sight of Ram's dark beauty overwhelms Bharata and everyone with love, then the pain of separation reminds them to keep moving with clear judgment.
ramacharitamanas::3057.simple_insight: Love can sweep you away, but clear seeing helps you keep going.
ramacharitamanas::3057.detailed_meaning: Bharata is travelling toward Ram with the people around him. At the Yamuna, the dark water reminds everyone of Ram's dark form, and their love surges so strongly that separation hurts more sharply. The verse shows devotion rising, then being steadied by discernment.
ramacharitamanas::3057.modern_relevance: You see a photo, a place, or a message that brings someone back all at once. Your chest tightens, then you remember what needs to be done next.
ramacharitamanas::3057.insight: It shows how devotion and discernment can work together: feeling deeply without losing your direction.

ramacharitamanas::3058.verse_sanskrit: जमुन तीर तेहि दिन करि बासू। भयउ समय सम सबहि सुपासू॥ रातिहिं घाट घाट की तरनी। आईं अगनित जाहिं न बरनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3058.verse_hindi: उस दिन यमुनाजी के किनारे निवास किया। समयानुसार सबके लिए (खान-पान आदि की) सुंदर व्यवस्था हुई (निषादराज का संकेत पाकर) रात ही रात में घाट-घाट की अगणित नावें वहाँ आ गईं, जिनका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3058.english_translation: That day they stayed on the Yamuna bank, and everything was arranged in time for everyone. At night, countless boats came to every landing, beyond counting.
ramacharitamanas::3058.translation_literal: जमुन (Yamuna) / तीर (bank) / तेहि (that) / दिन (day) / करि (having made) / बासू (stay) / भयउ (became) / समय (time) / सम (according to) / सबहि (for everyone) / सुपासू (good arrangement) / रातिहिं (at night) / घाट-घाट (at every landing) / की (of) / तरनी (boats) / आईं (came) / अगनित (countless) / जाहिं (go) / न (not) / बरनी (described)
ramacharitamanas::3058.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3058.essence: Quiet service makes impossible crossings feel effortless.
ramacharitamanas::3058.simple_meaning: They camped by the Yamuna, and the people were comfortably provided for. At night, so many boats arrived that no one could count them.
ramacharitamanas::3058.simple_insight: Help often appears through people willing to move quietly and quickly for others.
ramacharitamanas::3058.detailed_meaning: After the grief at Ayodhya, Bharat and the group reach the Yamuna bank. The verse pauses on practical care: food, rest, and then an astonishing flood of boats at night, arranged through Nishadraj's devotion so everyone can cross.
ramacharitamanas::3058.modern_relevance: You arrive exhausted at a riverside stop after a long family trip, and someone quietly brings food, blankets, and transport before you even ask. That kind of care changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::3058.insight: It highlights how true service anticipates need and removes friction before anyone has to plead.

ramacharitamanas::3059.verse_sanskrit: प्रात पार भए एकहि खेवाँ। तोषे रामसखा की सेवाँ॥ चले नहाइ नदिहि सिर नाई। साथ निषादनाथ दोउ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3059.verse_hindi: सबेरे एक ही खेवे में सब लोग पार हो गए और श्री रामचंद्रजी के सखा निषादराज की इस सेवा से संतुष्ट हुए। फिर स्नान करके और नदी को सिर नवाकर निषादराज के साथ दोनों भाई चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::3059.english_translation: At dawn, everyone crossed in a single boat, and Ram's friend Nishadraj was pleased by this service. Then they bathed, bowed to the river, and the two brothers set out with Nishadraj.
ramacharitamanas::3059.translation_literal: प्रात (at dawn) / पार भए (crossed over) / एकहि (in one only) / खेवाँ (boat-rowing) / तोषे (were pleased) / रामसखा (Ram's friend) / की सेवाँ (by the service) / चले (they went) / नहाइ (bathing) / नदिहि (to the river) / सिर नाई (bowing the head) / साथ (with) / निषादनाथ (Nishadraj) / दोउ भाई (both brothers)
ramacharitamanas::3059.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3059.essence: Service becomes complete when it asks for nothing back.
ramacharitamanas::3059.simple_meaning: Everyone crosses the river in one boat, and Nishadraj is pleased to serve Ram's party. After bathing and honoring the river, the two brothers continue with him.
ramacharitamanas::3059.simple_insight: True friendship shows up in practical help, not grand words.
ramacharitamanas::3059.detailed_meaning: After a night on the Yamuna bank, Nishadraj arranges the crossing for Ram, Lakshman, and the company. The whole group reaches the far side in one boat, and the brothers move on with him, grateful for his devoted service.
ramacharitamanas::3059.modern_relevance: You drop everything to help a friend move across town before sunrise, then walk them to the door yourself. No applause, just care that makes the whole day lighter.
ramacharitamanas::3059.insight: It highlights service that quietly carries others forward without asking for recognition.

ramacharitamanas::3060.verse_sanskrit: आगें मुनिबर बाहन आछें। राजसमाज जाइ सबु पाछें॥ तेहि पाछें दोउ बंधु पयादें। भूषन बसन बेष सुठि सादें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3060.verse_hindi: आगे अच्छी-अच्छी सवारियों पर श्रेष्ठ मुनि हैं, उनके पीछे सारा राजसमाज जा रहा है। उसके पीछे दोनों भाई बहुत सादे भूषण-वस्त्र और वेष से पैदल चल रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3060.english_translation: Ahead, the best sages ride in fine conveyances; behind them goes the whole royal company. Behind that, the two brothers walk on foot in very simple ornaments, clothes, and appearance.
ramacharitamanas::3060.translation_literal: आगें (ahead) / मुनिबर (best sages) / बाहन (vehicles, conveyances) / आछें (are) / राजसमाज (royal assembly, royal company) / जाइ (going) / सबु (all) / पाछें (behind) / तेहि पाछें (behind that) / दोउ (both) / बंधु (brothers) / पयादें (on foot) / भूषन (ornaments) / बसन (clothes) / बेष (appearance, dress) / सुठि (very) / सादें (simple, plain)
ramacharitamanas::3060.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3060.essence: Simplicity can stand behind honor without losing dignity.
ramacharitamanas::3060.simple_meaning: The sages and royal company travel ahead, while Ram and Lakshman walk behind them in simple dress.
ramacharitamanas::3060.simple_insight: True greatness does not need display. Quiet dignity can walk on foot and still lead the way.
ramacharitamanas::3060.detailed_meaning: After crossing the Yamuna, the group continues toward Bharadwaj’s hermitage. The sages ride ahead, the royal entourage follows, and Ram and Lakshman choose to walk simply behind everyone. The scene quietly shows their humility before the next teaching begins.
ramacharitamanas::3060.modern_relevance: You show up to a formal event in plain clothes while everyone else arrives polished and important. You don't need the spotlight to carry your dignity.
ramacharitamanas::3060.insight: It shifts attention from status and display to humility and restraint.

ramacharitamanas::3061.verse_sanskrit: सेवक सुहृद सचिवसुत साथा। सुमिरत लखनु सीय रघुनाथा॥ जहँ जहँ राम बास बिश्रामा। तहँ तहँ करहिं सप्रेम प्रनामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3061.verse_hindi: सेवक, मित्र और मंत्री के पुत्र उनके साथ हैं। लक्ष्मण, सीताजी और श्री रघुनाथजी का स्मरण करते जा रहे हैं। जहाँ-जहाँ श्री रामजी ने निवास और विश्राम किया था, वहाँ-वहाँ वे प्रेमसहित प्रणाम करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3061.english_translation: The servants, friends, and ministers' sons stayed with them. Lakshman, Sita, and Raghunath kept remembering each other. Wherever Ram had lived or rested, they bowed there with love.
ramacharitamanas::3061.translation_literal: सेवक (servants) / सुहृद (friends) / सचिवसुत (ministers' sons) / साथा (with them) / सुमिरत (remembering) / लखनु (Lakshman) / सीय (Sita) / रघुनाथा (Raghunath) / जहँ जहँ (wherever) / राम (Ram) / बास (dwelling) / बिश्रामा (rest) / तहँ तहँ (there there) / करहिं (they do) / सप्रेम (with love) / प्रनामा (bowing)
ramacharitamanas::3061.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3061.essence: Love makes every remembered place worthy of bowing.
ramacharitamanas::3061.simple_meaning: Lakshman, Sita, and the others walk together, remembering Ram and bowing lovingly at every place he stayed.
ramacharitamanas::3061.simple_insight: Love turns even ordinary places into sacred memory.
ramacharitamanas::3061.detailed_meaning: As Ram, Lakshman, and the others travel through exile, the whole group moves with reverence. Lakshman and Sita remember Ram constantly, and every spot where Ram once rested becomes a place of loving bowing.
ramacharitamanas::3061.modern_relevance: You pass the café where someone once sat across from you, and the memory hits before the coffee does. Certain places keep a person's presence alive.
ramacharitamanas::3061.insight: It shifts attention from movement itself to the tenderness of remembering and honoring what mattered.

ramacharitamanas::3062.verse_sanskrit: मगबासी नर नारि सुनि धाम काम तजि धाइ। देखि सरूप सनेह सब मुदित जनम फलु पाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3062.verse_hindi: मार्ग में रहने वाले स्त्री-पुरुष यह सुनकर घर और काम-काज छोड़कर दौड़ पड़ते हैं और उनके रूप (सौंदर्य) और प्रेम को देखकर वे सब जन्म लेने का फल पाकर आनंदित होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3062.english_translation: Hearing this, men and women living along the road ran out, leaving home and work. Seeing their beauty and love, all of them felt they had gained the fruit of being born.
ramacharitamanas::3062.translation_literal: मगबासी (road-dwelling) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / सुनि (hearing) / धाम (home) / काम (work, duties) / तजि (leaving) / धाइ (ran) / देखि (seeing) / सरूप (beautiful form) / सनेह (love) / सब (all) / मुदित (joyful) / जनम (birth) / फलु (fruit) / पाइ (having obtained)
ramacharitamanas::3062.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3062.essence: Their presence makes people feel their lives have meaning.
ramacharitamanas::3062.simple_meaning: People along the road forget their routines and hurry out to see Ram and Lakshman. Their beauty and affection make everyone feel life has become worthwhile.
ramacharitamanas::3062.simple_insight: Some presence is so moving that it makes ordinary life feel suddenly complete.
ramacharitamanas::3062.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and their procession are moving through Ayodhya. Word spreads along the road, and men and women leave their homes and work to catch a glimpse. This verse captures the public joy and wonder their presence awakens.
ramacharitamanas::3062.modern_relevance: A crowd gathers outside a train station because someone beloved has arrived. People stop errands, forget their plans, and just want one glimpse. Some presences make the whole day feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::3062.insight: It shifts attention from tasks and schedules to the transforming effect of a noble presence.

ramacharitamanas::3063.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं सप्रेम एक एक पाहीं। रामु लखनु सखि होहिं कि नाहीं॥ बय बपु बरन रूपु सोइ आली। सीलु सनेहु सरिस सम चाली ॥
ramacharitamanas::3063.verse_hindi: गाँवों की स्त्रियाँ एक-दूसरे से प्रेमपूर्वक कहती हैं- सखी! ये राम-लक्ष्मण हैं कि नहीं? हे सखी! इनकी अवस्था, शरीर और रंग-रूप तो वही है। शील, स्नेह उन्हीं के सदृश है और चाल भी उन्हीं के समान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3063.english_translation: The village women lovingly ask one another, “Are these Ram and Lakshman or not? Dear friend, their age, bodies, color, beauty, character, affection, and manner of walking are just like theirs.”
ramacharitamanas::3063.translation_literal: कहहिं (they say) / सप्रेम (with love) / एक एक पाहीं (to one another, each one) / रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / सखि (friend) / होहिं (are) / कि नाहीं (or not) / बय (age) / बपु (body) / बरन (color) / रूपु (beauty) / सोइ (the same) / आली (friend) / सीलु (character) / सनेहु (affection) / सरिस (like) / सम (equal) / चाली (walk, manner of moving)
ramacharitamanas::3063.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3063.essence: Love sees the beloved before certainty arrives.
ramacharitamanas::3063.simple_meaning: The women are so struck by the brothers that they compare every detail of them to Ram and Lakshman, yet they are still unsure.
ramacharitamanas::3063.simple_insight: Wonder can make even recognition feel like a tender question.
ramacharitamanas::3063.detailed_meaning: As Ram and Lakshman move through the villages, the women watch them with affection and confusion. Their beauty, manners, and gentle character remind everyone of the brothers they long to see, but the sight is still incomplete and uncertain.
ramacharitamanas::3063.modern_relevance: You see someone in a crowd who feels strangely familiar, and you keep asking friends, “Is that really them?” The heart recognizes before the mind does.
ramacharitamanas::3063.insight: It captures a moment of near-recognition, where longing and familiarity rise before certainty.

ramacharitamanas::3064.verse_sanskrit: बेषु न सो सखि सीय न संगा। आगें अनी चली चतुरंगा॥ नहिं प्रसन्न मुख मानस खेदा। सखि संदेहु होइ एहिं भेदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3064.verse_hindi: परन्तु सखी! इनका न तो वह वेष (वल्कल वस्त्रधारी मुनिवेष) है, न सीताजी ही संग हैं और इनके आगे चतुरंगिणी सेना चली जा रही है। फिर इनके मुख प्रसन्न नहीं हैं, इनके मन में खेद है। हे सखी! इसी भेद के कारण संदेह होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3064.english_translation: But, friend, they do not wear that ascetic dress, nor is Sita with them. And an army of four divisions marches ahead of them. Their faces are not cheerful, and their minds are troubled. Friend, because of these differences, doubt arises.
ramacharitamanas::3064.translation_literal: बेषु (dress) / न (not) / सो (that) / सखि (friend) / सीय (Sita) / न (not) / संगा (with) / आगें (ahead) / अनी (army) / चली (moving) / चतुरंगा (fourfold) / नहिं (not) / प्रसन्न (happy) / मुख (face) / मानस (mind) / खेदा (sadness) / सखि (friend) / संदेहु (doubt) / होइ (arises) / एहिं (this) / भेदा (difference)
ramacharitamanas::3064.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3064.essence: Doubt grows when reality does not match expectation.
ramacharitamanas::3064.simple_meaning: The women notice that this is not the ascetic-looking Ram they expected. Sita is absent, an army is marching ahead, and Ram's face looks troubled, so doubt begins to grow.
ramacharitamanas::3064.simple_insight: Sometimes the smallest mismatch is enough to make certainty wobble.
ramacharitamanas::3064.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, villagers crowd around the passing brothers and compare what they see with the story they have heard. One woman notices the mismatch: no forest dress, no Sita, an army in front, and no joy on Ram's face. Her observation keeps the crowd's curiosity alive.
ramacharitamanas::3064.modern_relevance: You see a friend arrive in the same car, but their expression is tight and they are not with the person you expected. The details don't fit the story, and your mind starts searching for what changed.
ramacharitamanas::3064.insight: It trains the mind to notice concrete signs before accepting a conclusion.

ramacharitamanas::3065.verse_sanskrit: तासु तरक तियगन मन मानी। कहहिं सकल तेहि सम न सयानी॥ तेहि सराहि बानी फुरि पूजी। बोली मधुर बचन तिय दूजी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3065.verse_hindi: उसका तर्क (युक्ति) अन्य स्त्रियों के मन भाया। सब कहती हैं कि इसके समान सयानी (चतुर) कोई नहीं है। उसकी सराहना करके और 'तेरी वाणी सत्य है' इस प्रकार उसका सम्मान करके दूसरी स्त्री मीठे वचन बोली ॥
ramacharitamanas::3065.english_translation: Her reasoning pleased the women’s minds. They all said, “No one is as clever as she is.” After praising her and honoring her words as true, another woman spoke sweetly.
ramacharitamanas::3065.translation_literal: तासु (her) / तरक (reasoning) / तियगन (women's) / मन (minds) / मानी (pleased). / कहहिं (they say) / सकल (all) / तेहि (that one) / सम (equal to) / न (not) / सयानी (wise/clever).॥ तेहि (that one) / सराहि (praising) / बानी (speech) / फुरि (true) / पूजी (honored/worshipped) / । / बोली (spoke) / मधुर (sweet) / बचन (words) / तिय (woman) / दूजी (second/another).॥
ramacharitamanas::3065.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3065.essence: A clear voice can settle a room before the full story is known.
ramacharitamanas::3065.simple_meaning: The women are convinced by her argument and praise her as the wisest among them. Another woman responds with respectful, sweet speech.
ramacharitamanas::3065.simple_insight: Sometimes a clear, well-placed argument wins trust before anyone even agrees with the whole story.
ramacharitamanas::3065.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, village women are discussing the strange sight before them and trying to understand it. One woman's reasoning settles the group’s doubt, and the others praise her intelligence before the conversation moves on.
ramacharitamanas::3065.modern_relevance: In a group chat, one person finally names what everyone has been half-thinking. The room relaxes, and the conversation moves forward because someone put the feeling into words.
ramacharitamanas::3065.insight: It shows how shared uncertainty often resolves when one person speaks with clarity and confidence.

ramacharitamanas::3066.verse_sanskrit: कहि सप्रेम बस कथाप्रसंगू। जेहि बिधि राम राज रस भंगू॥ भरतहि बहुरि सराहन लागी। सील सनेह सुभाय सुभागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3066.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के राजतिलक का आनंद जिस प्रकार से भंग हुआ था, वह सब कथाप्रसंग प्रेमपूर्वक कहकर फिर वह भाग्यवती स्त्री श्री भरतजी के शील, स्नेह और स्वभाव की सराहना करने लगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3066.english_translation: After lovingly recounting how Ram's coronation joy was broken, she again began praising Bharat's character, affection, and noble nature.
ramacharitamanas::3066.translation_literal: कहि (having said) / सप्रेम (with love) / बस (thus) / कथा-प्रसंगू (the story topic) / जेहि बिधि (in which manner) / राम (Ram) / राज-रस (the joy of kingship/coronation) / भंगू (break, disruption) // भरतहि (Bharat) / बहुरि (again) / सराहन (to praise) / लागी (began) / सील (character, gentleness) / सनेह (affection) / सुभाय (nature) / सुभागी (fortunate one)
ramacharitamanas::3066.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3066.essence: Loss reveals the depth of Bharat's gentleness and love.
ramacharitamanas::3066.simple_meaning: She lovingly tells the story of how Ram's coronation was disrupted, then turns to praising Bharat's character and loving nature.
ramacharitamanas::3066.simple_insight: Even painful stories can reveal what is noble in a person.
ramacharitamanas::3066.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the women are discussing the broken coronation and the shock that followed. One speaker finishes the story of that loss with affection, then shifts to praising Bharat, whose gentleness and love stand out even in grief.
ramacharitamanas::3066.modern_relevance: At a family gathering, someone retells the moment everything went wrong, then quietly says who stayed kind through it. Pain and character are being measured at the same time.
ramacharitamanas::3066.insight: It keeps attention on character, not just on the event that caused sorrow.

ramacharitamanas::3067.verse_sanskrit: चलत पयादें खात फल पिता दीन्ह तजि राजु। जात मनावन रघुबरहि भरत सरिस को आजु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3067.verse_hindi: (वह बोली-) देखो, ये भरतजी पिता के दिए हुए राज्य को त्यागकर पैदल चलते और फलाहार करते हुए श्री रामजी को मनाने के लिए जा रहे हैं। इनके समान आज कौन है? ॥।
ramacharitamanas::3067.english_translation: See how Bharat has renounced the kingdom his father gave him, walking on foot and living on fruit as he goes to appease Ram. Who is like him today?
ramacharitamanas::3067.translation_literal: चलत (walking) / पयादें (on foot) / खात (eating) / फल (fruit) / पिता (father) / दीन्ह (gave) / तजि (renouncing) / राजु (kingdom) / जात (going) / मनावन (to appease) / रघुबरहि (to Ram) / भरत (Bharat) / सरिस (like) / को (who) / आजु (today)
ramacharitamanas::3067.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3067.essence: Devotion becomes undeniable when it walks away from comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3067.simple_meaning: Bharat has left behind the throne, travels on foot, eats only fruit, and goes to win Ram back. His devotion is being praised as unmatched.
ramacharitamanas::3067.simple_insight: Love becomes unmistakable when it costs you status and comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3067.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat has refused the throne after Ram's exile. A woman describes his barefoot journey, his simple food, and his single aim: to persuade Ram to return. The verse celebrates devotion made visible in action.
ramacharitamanas::3067.modern_relevance: You turn down a promotion because it would pull you away from someone you promised to stand by. That quiet refusal tells the truth about what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::3067.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to visible sacrifice and loyal action.

ramacharitamanas::3068.verse_sanskrit: भायप भगति भरत आचरनू। कहत सुनत दुख दूषन हरनू॥ जो किछु कहब थोर सखि सोई। राम बंधु अस काहे न होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3068.verse_hindi: भरतजी का भाईपना, भक्ति और इनके आचरण कहने और सुनने से दुःख और दोषों के हरने वाले हैं। हे सखी! उनके संबंध में जो कुछ भी कहा जाए, वह थोड़ा है। श्री रामचंद्रजी के भाई ऐसे क्यों न हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::3068.english_translation: Bharat's brotherly love, devotion, and conduct remove sorrow and fault when spoken of or heard. O friend, whatever can be said is still too little. Why would Ram's brother be any less than this?
ramacharitamanas::3068.translation_literal: भायप (brotherhood) / भगति (devotion) / भरत (Bharat) / आचरनू (conduct) / कहत (speaking) / सुनत (hearing) / दुख (sorrow) / दूषन (fault) / हरनू (remover) / जो (whatever) / किछु (some) / कहब (to say) / थोर (little) / सखि (friend) / सोई (that only) / राम (Ram) / बंधु (brother) / अस (like this) / काहे (why) / न (not) / होई (would be)
ramacharitamanas::3068.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3068.essence: Pure devotion makes sorrow lighter just by being seen.
ramacharitamanas::3068.simple_meaning: Bharat's love, devotion, and conduct are so pure that even hearing about them eases sorrow. His greatness feels too vast for words, and Ram's brother could not be otherwise.
ramacharitamanas::3068.simple_insight: Real devotion doesn't just look beautiful; it softens grief in the person who witnesses it.
ramacharitamanas::3068.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the women of Ayodhya are speaking about Bharat's journey to bring Ram back. After hearing of his character, they feel their own sorrow lift. Bharat's devotion has become a living proof of Ram's grace.
ramacharitamanas::3068.modern_relevance: You hear about someone who gave up comfort to keep a promise, and your chest loosens. Their integrity doesn't just impress you — it restores something in you.
ramacharitamanas::3068.insight: It shifts attention from Bharat's sacrifice alone to the healing power of witnessing selfless conduct.

ramacharitamanas::3069.verse_sanskrit: हम सब सानुज भरतहि देखें। भइन्ह धन्य जुबती जन लेखें॥ सुनि गुन देखि दसा पछिताहीं। कैकइ जननि जोगु सुतु नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3069.verse_hindi: छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न सहित भरतजी को देखकर हम सब भी आज धन्य (बड़भागिनी) स्त्रियों की गिनती में आ गईं। इस प्रकार भरतजी के गुण सुनकर और उनकी दशा देखकर स्त्रियाँ पछताती हैं और कहती हैं- यह पुत्र कैकयी जैसी माता के योग्य नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3069.english_translation: Seeing Bharata with his younger brother Shatrughna, we all count ourselves among the blessed women. Hearing of his virtues and seeing his condition, the women regret and say, 'This son is not worthy of Kaikeyi as a mother.'
ramacharitamanas::3069.translation_literal: हम (we) / सब (all) / सानुज (with younger brother) / भरतहि (Bharata) / देखें (saw) । भइन्ह (became) / धन्य (blessed) / जुबती (women) / जन (people) / लेखें (in count) ॥ सुनि (hearing) / गुन (virtues) / देखि (seeing) / दसा (condition) / पछिताहीं (regret) । कैकइ (Kaikeyi) / जननि (mother) / जोगु (worthy) / सुतु (son) / नाहीं (not) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3069.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3069.essence: Bharata's virtue makes even sorrow feel like blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3069.simple_meaning: The women feel blessed just by seeing Bharata and Shatrughna. But when they hear Bharata's virtues and see his hardship, they lament that such a son does not deserve a mother like Kaikeyi.
ramacharitamanas::3069.simple_insight: A noble life can make others grieve for the cost it paid.
ramacharitamanas::3069.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the women see Bharata arrive with Shatrughna after Ram's exile has shattered the royal family. His virtue and suffering move them so deeply that admiration turns into regret over Kaikeyi's role in the disaster.
ramacharitamanas::3069.modern_relevance: You watch someone carry family pain with dignity at a funeral, and the room goes quiet. Their goodness makes everyone feel both grateful and heartbroken.
ramacharitamanas::3069.insight: It shifts attention from appearance to the moral weight of a person's conduct and suffering.

ramacharitamanas::3070.verse_sanskrit: कोउ कह दूषनु रानिहि नाहिन। बिधि सबु कीन्ह हमहि जो दाहिन॥ कहँ हम लोक बेद बिधि हीनी। लघु तिय कुल करतूति मलीनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3070.verse_hindi: कोई कहती है- इसमें रानी का भी दोष नहीं है। यह सब विधाता ने ही किया है, जो हमारे अनुकूल है। कहाँ तो हम लोक और वेद दोनों की विधि (मर्यादा) से हीन, कुल और करतूत दोनों से मलिन तुच्छ स्त्रियाँ, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3070.english_translation: Some say the queen is not at fault. Fate has done all this to us, to our liking. What are we, poor women lacking both social order and scriptural rule, lowly in family and conduct?
ramacharitamanas::3070.translation_literal: कोउ (someone) / कह (says) / दूषनु (fault) / रानिहि (in the queen) / नाहिन (not) / बिधि (fate, the ordering power) / सबु (all) / कीन्ह (did) / हमहि (to us) / जो (which) / दाहिन (favourable, to our liking) / कहँ (where) / हम (we) / लोक (worldly conduct) / बेद (scriptural rule) / बिधि (rule, order) / हीनी (without) / लघु (small, lowly) / तिय (women) / कुल (family line) / करतूति (conduct) / मलीनी (tainted)
ramacharitamanas::3070.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3070.essence: Sorrow can make blame dissolve into self-condemnation.
ramacharitamanas::3070.simple_meaning: The women say the queen may not be to blame; they feel fate has brought this sorrow. They also call themselves lowly, lacking both social and scriptural standing.
ramacharitamanas::3070.simple_insight: Grief can make people turn blame inward and speak with painful humility.
ramacharitamanas::3070.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the women around the palace are trying to make sense of the exile and the chaos it has caused. Some soften the blame on Kaikeyi, but the verse turns into self-abasement, showing how deeply the shock has shaken the whole court.
ramacharitamanas::3070.modern_relevance: After a family blowup, people start saying, 'Maybe it wasn't just her fault' — and then immediately shrink into self-blame, as if the pain proves their own worthlessness.
ramacharitamanas::3070.insight: It reveals how sorrow distorts judgment: blame, pity, and self-condemnation all blur together.

ramacharitamanas::3071.verse_sanskrit: बसहिं कुदेस कुगाँव कुबामा। कहँ यह दरसु पुन्य परिनामा॥ अस अनंदु अचिरिजु प्रति ग्रामा। जनु मरुभूमि कलपतरु जामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3071.verse_hindi: जो बुरे देश (जंगली प्रान्त) और बुरे गाँव में बसती हैं और (स्त्रियों में भी) नीच स्त्रियाँ हैं! और कहाँ यह महान् पुण्यों का परिणामस्वरूप इनका दर्शन! ऐसा ही आनंद और आश्चर्य गाँव-गाँव में हो रहा है। मानो मरुभूमि में कल्पवृक्ष उग गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3071.english_translation: Those living in bad lands, bad villages, and low homes! And yet, where is this sight? It is the fruit of great merit. Such joy and wonder spread through every village, as if a wish-fulfilling tree had grown in a desert.
ramacharitamanas::3071.translation_literal: बसहिं (they live) / कुदेस (bad lands) / कुगाँव (bad villages) / कुबामा (bad homes) / कहँ (where) / यह दरसु (this sight) / पुन्य परिनामा (fruit/result of merit) / अस (such) / अनंदु (joy) / अचिरिजु (wonder) / प्रति ग्रामा (in every village) / जनु (as if) / मरुभूमि (desert) / कलपतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / जामा (has grown)
ramacharitamanas::3071.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3071.essence: Bharat's presence feels like a miracle in a barren world.
