ramacharitamanas::3071.simple_meaning: Bharat's presence is so beautiful that even ordinary people feel amazed and blessed by seeing him, as if a miracle has appeared in a barren place.
ramacharitamanas::3071.simple_insight: A pure presence can make a whole place feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3071.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the people are overwhelmed as Bharat moves among them after Ram's exile. They speak in wonder, saying his sight feels like the reward of great merit. His arrival turns every village into a place of joy.
ramacharitamanas::3071.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after someone kind and steady arrives, and the whole mood changes. People feel lighter without knowing why. Some people do that just by being present.
ramacharitamanas::3071.insight: It shifts attention from status to the blessing of a person whose presence quietly transforms everyone around them.

ramacharitamanas::3072.verse_sanskrit: भरत दरसु देखत खुलेउ मग लोगन्ह कर भागु। जनु सिंघलबासिन्ह भयउ बिधि बस सुलभ प्रयागु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3072.verse_hindi: भरतजी का स्वरूप देखते ही रास्ते में रहने वाले लोगों के भाग्य खुल गए! मानो दैवयोग से सिंहलद्वीप के बसने वालों को तीर्थराज प्रयाग सुलभ हो गया हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3072.english_translation: Just seeing Bharat, the people along the road felt their fortune open. It was as if, by fate, the people of Lanka had found Prayag within reach.
ramacharitamanas::3072.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / दरसु (sight, darshan) / देखत (seeing) / खुलेउ (opened) / मग (road) / लोगन्ह (of the people) / कर (of) / भागु (fortune) / जनु (as if) / सिंघलबासिन्ह (for the people of Lanka) / भयउ (became) / बिधि बस (by fate) / सुलभ (easy to obtain) / प्रयागु (Prayag)
ramacharitamanas::3072.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3072.essence: A pure presence can feel like a sacred meeting place.
ramacharitamanas::3072.simple_meaning: Bharat's presence blesses everyone who sees him. The people along the road feel as if a rare holy blessing has come to them.
ramacharitamanas::3072.simple_insight: Some people make others feel fortunate just by being near them.
ramacharitamanas::3072.detailed_meaning: Bharat is traveling in exile, absorbed in remembering Ram. The people on the road are so moved by his presence that the poet compares their good fortune to reaching Prayag itself. The line praises Bharat's purity, not a new event.
ramacharitamanas::3072.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a funeral, and their quiet steadiness calms everyone in the room. Without saying much, they make grief feel less lonely.
ramacharitamanas::3072.insight: It shifts attention from what Bharat is doing to what his presence awakens in others.

ramacharitamanas::3073.verse_sanskrit: निज गुन सहित राम गुन गाथा। सुनत जाहिं सुमिरत रघुनाथा॥ तीरथ मुनि आश्रम सुरधामा। निरखि निमज्जहिं करहिं प्रनामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3073.verse_hindi: (इस प्रकार) अपने गुणों सहित श्री रामचंद्रजी के गुणों की कथा सुनते और श्री रघुनाथजी को स्मरण करते हुए भरतजी चले जा रहे हैं। वे तीर्थ देखकर स्नान और मुनियों के आश्रम तथा देवताओं के मंदिर देखकर प्रणाम करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3073.english_translation: Bharat keeps walking while hearing the praises of Ram's virtues and remembering Raghunath. Seeing holy places, sages' hermitages, and shrines of radiant beings, he bathes and bows down.
ramacharitamanas::3073.translation_literal: निज (own) / गुन (qualities) / सहित (along with) / राम (Ram) / गुन (qualities) / गाथा (songs, praise) / सुनत (hearing) / जाहिं (goes) / सुमिरत (remembering) / रघुनाथा (Raghunath) / तीरथ (holy places) / मुनि (sages) / आश्रम (hermitages) / सुरधामा (shrines of radiant beings) / निरखि (seeing) / निमज्जहिं (baths) / करहिं (does) / प्रनामा (bows)
ramacharitamanas::3073.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3073.essence: Devotion makes every step an offering.
ramacharitamanas::3073.simple_meaning: Bharat walks on, thinking of Ram and hearing Ram's praise. Whenever he sees a holy place, a sage's hermitage, or a shrine, he bathes and bows.
ramacharitamanas::3073.simple_insight: Love turns the whole journey into worship.
ramacharitamanas::3073.detailed_meaning: Bharat is travelling in grief and devotion toward Ram. Every stretch of road becomes sacred to him: he remembers Ram, hears Ram's praise, and treats holy places, hermitages, and shrines with reverence. The verse shows his mind already living in surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3073.modern_relevance: You pass a temple on the way to work, step in for a minute, and leave quieter than you entered. Bharat carries that same reflex of reverence wherever he goes.
ramacharitamanas::3073.insight: It shifts travel from movement through space into continuous remembrance and respect.

ramacharitamanas::3074.verse_sanskrit: मनहीं मन मागहिं बरु एहू। सीय राम पद पदुम सनेहू॥ मिलहिं किरात कोल बनबासी। बैखानस बटु जती उदासी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3074.verse_hindi: और मन ही मन यह वरदान माँगते हैं कि श्री सीता-रामजी के चरण कमलों में प्रेम हो। मार्ग में भील, कोल आदि वनवासी तथा वानप्रस्थ, ब्रह्मचारी, संन्यासी और विरक्त मिलते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3074.english_translation: And in their hearts they ask for only this blessing: love for the lotus feet of Sita and Ram. Along the way they meet forest-dwellers, ascetics, celibates, renunciants, and wandering seekers.
ramacharitamanas::3074.translation_literal: मनहीं मन (in the mind itself) / मागहिं (they ask) / बरु (a boon) / एहू (this) / सीय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / पदुम (lotus) / सनेहू (love) / मिलहिं (they meet) / किरात (forest-dwellers) / कोल (Kol people) / बनबासी (forest inhabitants) / बैखानस (renunciants) / बटु (celibates/students) / जती (ascetics) / उदासी (wandering renunciants)
ramacharitamanas::3074.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3074.essence: The journey is already sacred when your heart wants only Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3074.simple_meaning: Bharat and his companions keep asking for one thing in their hearts: love for Ram and Sita. As they travel, they meet many forest people and renunciants.
ramacharitamanas::3074.simple_insight: A holy longing can travel quietly through every encounter.
ramacharitamanas::3074.detailed_meaning: Bharat is walking through the forest in deep grief and devotion, thinking only of Ram. He does not ask for power or comfort. He asks for love at Ram and Sita's feet, and the road itself becomes a meeting place with humble seekers and forest people.
ramacharitamanas::3074.modern_relevance: You keep moving through a difficult season, and all you really want is one thing: to feel love again for what truly matters. Even the people you meet along the way can become reminders of that longing.
ramacharitamanas::3074.insight: It shifts attention from outward travel to inward devotion, showing that the real destination is the heart's orientation.

ramacharitamanas::3075.verse_sanskrit: करि प्रनामु पूँछहिं जेहि तेही। केहि बन लखनु रामु बैदेही॥ ते प्रभु समाचार सब कहहीं। भरतहि देखि जनम फलु लहहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3075.verse_hindi: उनमें से जिस-तिस से प्रणाम करके पूछते हैं कि लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामजी और जानकीजी किस वन में हैं? वे प्रभु के सब समाचार कहते हैं और भरतजी को देखकर जन्म का फल पाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3075.english_translation: They bow to each person they meet and ask, "Which forest are Lakshman, Ram, and Sita in?" Those people tell them everything about the Lord, and seeing Bharat, they feel they have gained the fruit of life.
ramacharitamanas::3075.translation_literal: करि (doing) / प्रनामु (salutation) / पूँछहिं (they ask) / जेहि तेही (whoever, each one) / केहि (which) / बन (forest) / लखनु (Lakshman) / रामु (Ram) / बैदेही (Sita) / ते (they) / प्रभु (Lord) / समाचार (news) / सब (all) / कहहीं (tell) / भरतहि (to Bharat) / देखि (seeing) / जनम (birth) / फलु (fruit) / लहहीं (they receive)
ramacharitamanas::3075.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3075.essence: A devoted heart makes everyone it meets feel blessed.
ramacharitamanas::3075.simple_meaning: Bharat keeps asking everyone where Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are. People who answer him feel blessed just by seeing him.
ramacharitamanas::3075.simple_insight: Love can make even a simple question feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3075.detailed_meaning: Bharat is searching through the forest with a heart full of longing for Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. He bows to everyone, asks the same aching question, and the villagers respond with reverence, feeling their lives have been made complete by seeing him.
ramacharitamanas::3075.modern_relevance: You stop strangers on a long road and ask one name again and again because someone you love is missing. Even the answer feels holy when your heart is that devoted.
ramacharitamanas::3075.insight: It shifts attention from the search itself to the purity of the seeker’s love.

ramacharitamanas::3076.verse_sanskrit: जे जन कहहिं कुसल हम देखे। ते प्रिय राम लखन सम लेखे॥ एहि बिधि बूझत सबहि सुबानी। सुनत राम बनबास कहानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3076.verse_hindi: जो लोग कहते हैं कि हमने उनको कुशलपूर्वक देखा है, उनको ये श्री राम-लक्ष्मण के समान ही प्यारे मानते हैं। इस प्रकार सबसे सुंदर वाणी से पूछते और श्री रामजी के वनवास की कहानी सुनते जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3076.english_translation: Those who say, “We have seen him safe and well” are cherished as dearly as Ram and Lakshman. In this way, they ask everyone with sweet words and keep hearing the story of Ram’s exile.
ramacharitamanas::3076.translation_literal: जे (those who) / जन (people) / कहहिं (say) / कुसल (safe, well) / हम (we) / देखे (have seen) / ते (they) / प्रिय (dear) / राम (Ram) / लखन (Lakshman) / सम (like, equal to) / लेखे (counted)॥ एहि (in this) / बिधि (way) / बूझत (asking) / सबहि (everyone) / सुबानी (sweet speech) / सुनत (hearing) / राम (Ram) / बनबास (forest exile) / कहानी (story)॥
ramacharitamanas::3076.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3076.essence: When love is waiting, even news becomes a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3076.simple_meaning: Anyone who can tell Bharata that Ram and Lakshman are safe becomes dear to him. He keeps asking people gently and listening to the story of Ram’s exile.
ramacharitamanas::3076.simple_insight: Love makes every update precious when your heart is waiting for someone you miss.
ramacharitamanas::3076.detailed_meaning: Bharata and his companions are still searching for news of Ram, Lakshman, and Sita in the forest. Anyone who has seen them safely is treated with great affection, because every word about Ram matters to Bharata in exile.
ramacharitamanas::3076.modern_relevance: You refresh your phone again and again, hoping for one reassuring message. When someone you love is away, even a small update feels priceless.
ramacharitamanas::3076.insight: It shows how longing makes ordinary information feel sacred and turns every listener into a devotee of the beloved’s safety.

ramacharitamanas::3077.verse_sanskrit: तेहि बासर बसि प्रातहीं चले सुमिरि रघुनाथ। राम दरस की लालसा भरत सरिस सब साथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3077.verse_hindi: उस दिन वहीं ठहरकर दूसरे दिन प्रातःकाल ही श्री रघुनाथजी का स्मरण करके चले। साथ के सब लोगों को भी भरतजी के समान ही श्री रामजी के दर्शन की लालसा (लगी हुई) है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3077.english_translation: After staying there that day, they set out at dawn the next morning, remembering Raghunath. Everyone in the group longs to see Ram just as Bharata does.
ramacharitamanas::3077.translation_literal: तेहि (there) / बासर (day) / बसि (staying) / प्रातहीं (at dawn) / चले (they went) / सुमिरि (remembering) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / राम (Ram) / दरस (sight) / की (of) / लालसा (longing) / भरत (Bharat) / सरिस (like) / सब (all) / साथ (together)
ramacharitamanas::3077.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3077.essence: Shared longing turns the whole group toward one beloved presence.
ramacharitamanas::3077.simple_meaning: They spend the night there and leave at dawn, all of them longing to see Ram just as Bharata does.
ramacharitamanas::3077.simple_insight: Longing can move an entire group in the same direction.
ramacharitamanas::3077.detailed_meaning: After searching and asking everyone about Ram, Lakshman, and Sita, Bharata and the others rest for the night. At dawn they set out again, each heart pulled forward by the same ache: to see Ram and end the sorrow of separation.
ramacharitamanas::3077.modern_relevance: You leave before sunrise after a sleepless night on the road, replaying one meeting in your mind. Everyone with you feels the same pull: get there, see them, and let the waiting end.
ramacharitamanas::3077.insight: It shows how shared longing can unify action and keep a group moving together.

ramacharitamanas::3078.verse_sanskrit: मंगल सगुन होहिं सब काहू। फरकहिं सुखद बिलोचन बाहू॥ भरतहि सहित समाज उछाहू। मिलिहहिं रामु मिटिहि दुख दाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3078.verse_hindi: सबको मंगलसूचक शकुन हो रहे हैं। सुख देने वाले (पुरुषों के दाहिने और स्त्रियों के बाएँ) नेत्र और भुजाएँ फड़क रही हैं। समाज सहित भरतजी को उत्साह हो रहा है कि श्री रामचंद्रजी मिलेंगे और दुःख का दाह मिट जाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3078.english_translation: All signs are auspicious. Pleasant twitches move the eyes and arms. Bharat and the whole gathering feel joy, knowing Ram will meet them and the fire of sorrow will be quenched.
ramacharitamanas::3078.translation_literal: मंगल (auspicious) / सगुन (signs) / होहिं (are) / सब (all) / काहू (for everyone) / फरकहिं (twitch) / सुखद (bringing joy) / बिलोचन (eyes) / बाहू (arms) / भरतहि (for Bharat) / सहित (along with) / समाज (the gathering) / उछाहू (joy) / मिलिहहिं (will meet) / रामु (Ram) / मिटिहि (will be removed) / दुख (sorrow) / दाहू (burning)
ramacharitamanas::3078.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3078.essence: Hope itself can begin healing before the meeting arrives.
ramacharitamanas::3078.simple_meaning: Everyone sees hopeful signs, and Bharat’s group feels joy because Ram is about to meet them and their suffering will ease.
ramacharitamanas::3078.simple_insight: Hope can spread through a whole group before the reunion even happens.
ramacharitamanas::3078.detailed_meaning: Bharat and his companions are on the road after leaving Nandigram. The air itself seems to bless the journey: omens look favorable, bodies twitch with hope, and everyone feels Ram’s meeting drawing near. This verse is the emotional lift before reunion.
ramacharitamanas::3078.modern_relevance: You’re waiting outside a hospital room, and someone finally texts that the doctor is coming. Your chest loosens before the door even opens.
ramacharitamanas::3078.insight: It shifts attention from grief to anticipation, showing how hope can steady a shaken mind.

ramacharitamanas::3079.verse_sanskrit: करत मनोरथ जस जियँ जाके। जाहिं सनेह सुराँ सब छाके। सिथिल अंग पग मग डगि डोलहिं। बिहबल बचन प्रेम बस बोलहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3079.verse_hindi: जिसके जी में जैसा है, वह वैसा ही मनोरथ करता है। सब स्नेही रूपी मदिरा से छके (प्रेम में मतवाले हुए) चले जा रहे हैं। अंग शिथिल हैं, रास्ते में पैर डगमगा रहे हैं और प्रेमवश विह्वल वचन बोल रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3079.english_translation: Whatever is in a person's heart, that becomes the person's desire. Everyone moves forward, drunk on the wine of affection; their limbs grow weak, their feet stagger on the path, and love makes them speak in a dazed way.
ramacharitamanas::3079.translation_literal: करत (doing) / मनोरथ (desire, wish) / जस (as) / जियँ (in the heart) / जाके (of whom) / जाहिं (go) / सनेह (affection, love) / सुराँ (wine) / सब (all) / छाके (intoxicated) / सिथिल (weak, slack) / अंग (limbs) / पग (feet) / मग (path) / डगि (staggering) / डोलहिं (waver) / बिहबल (overwhelmed, dazed) / बचन (words) / प्रेम (love) / बस (under the power of) / बोलहिं (speak)
ramacharitamanas::3079.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3079.essence: Longing turns the whole body into a sign of the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3079.simple_meaning: Love and longing make people act differently: their bodies weaken, their steps falter, and their words come out overwhelmed.
ramacharitamanas::3079.simple_insight: Strong feeling changes how you walk, speak, and move through the world.
ramacharitamanas::3079.detailed_meaning: Bharat and his companions are on the road, hearts set on Ram's meeting. Tulsidas pauses to show how longing has taken over the whole group: desire shapes their thoughts, weakens their bodies, and makes even their speech tremble.
ramacharitamanas::3079.modern_relevance: You leave a message unread because your heart is racing, then reread it ten times on the walk. When longing takes over, even your body starts to show it.
ramacharitamanas::3079.insight: It captures how emotion can overtake the body and speech before the mind catches up.

ramacharitamanas::3080.verse_sanskrit: रामसखाँ तेहि समय देखावा। सैल सिरोमनि सहज सुहावा॥ जासु समीप सरित पय तीरा। सीय समेत बसहिं दोउ बीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3080.verse_hindi: रामसखा निषादराज ने उसी समय स्वाभाविक ही सुहावना पर्वतशिरोमणि कामदगिरि दिखलाया, जिसके निकट ही पयस्विनी नदी के तट पर सीताजी समेत दोनों भाई निवास करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3080.english_translation: Ram's friend Nishadraj showed them the lovely mountain at that moment. Near it, on the bank of the Payaswini river, the two brothers live with Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3080.translation_literal: रामसखाँ (Ram's friend) / तेहि समय (at that time) / देखावा (showed) / सैल सिरोमनि (mountain among peaks) / सहज (naturally) / सुहावा (beautiful)॥ / जासु (whose) / समीप (near) / सरित (river) / पय तीरा (on the bank of the Payaswini) / सीय समेत (with Sita) / बसहिं (reside) / दोउ बीरा (both brothers)
ramacharitamanas::3080.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3080.essence: A simple place becomes precious because Ram and Sita live there.
ramacharitamanas::3080.simple_meaning: Nishadraj points out the beautiful hill near the river where Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are staying.
ramacharitamanas::3080.simple_insight: Some places feel sacred because love has lived there.
ramacharitamanas::3080.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the royal party is moving through the forest with longing and reverence. Nishadraj points out the lovely hill near the Payaswini where Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are living. The verse simply marks the place before the reunion scene.
ramacharitamanas::3080.modern_relevance: You arrive at a quiet hillside after hearing stories about it for months. The view matters, but what really moves you is knowing someone you love once stood there too.
ramacharitamanas::3080.insight: It shifts attention from scenery alone to the presence that gives a place meaning.

ramacharitamanas::3081.verse_sanskrit: देखि करहिं सब दंड प्रनामा। कहि जय जानकि जीवन रामा॥ प्रेम मगन अस राज समाजू। जनु फिरि अवध चले रघुराजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3081.verse_hindi: सब लोग उस पर्वत को देखकर 'जानकी जीवन श्री रामचंद्रजी की जय हो।' ऐसा कहकर दण्डवत प्रणाम करते हैं। राजसमाज प्रेम में ऐसा मग्न है मानो श्री रघुनाथजी अयोध्या को लौट चले हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::3081.english_translation: Seeing the mountain, everyone bowed down and said, 'Victory to Rama, the life of Janaki.' The royal assembly was so immersed in love that it seemed as if the lord of Raghu had returned to Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::3081.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / करहिं (they do) / सब (all) / दंड प्रनामा (full prostration) / कहि (saying) / जय (victory) / जानकि जीवन (life of Janaki) / रामा (Rama) / प्रेम मगन (immersed in love) / अस (thus) / राज समाजू (royal assembly) / जनु (as if) / फिरि (again/returned) / अवध (Ayodhya) / चले (had come/went) / रघुराजू (lord of Raghu)
ramacharitamanas::3081.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3081.essence: Deep love makes absence feel like return.
ramacharitamanas::3081.simple_meaning: Everyone bows to the sight of the mountain and praises Rama. The whole royal gathering feels so full of love that it seems as if Rama has already returned home.
ramacharitamanas::3081.simple_insight: Love can make absence feel like presence.
ramacharitamanas::3081.detailed_meaning: At the holy mountain near Kamadgiri, the gathered people bow in reverence and cry Rama's name. The royal assembly is so overwhelmed by devotion and memory that the scene feels like Ayodhya itself has come alive again.
ramacharitamanas::3081.modern_relevance: You walk into a place tied to someone you love, and the whole room changes. Their memory is so strong it feels like they are there.
ramacharitamanas::3081.insight: It turns memory into living presence and shows how devotion reshapes perception.

ramacharitamanas::3082.verse_sanskrit: भरत प्रेमु तेहि समय जस तस कहि सकइ न सेषु। कबिहि अगम जिमि ब्रह्मसुखु अह मम मलिन जनेषु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3082.verse_hindi: भरतजी का उस समय जैसा प्रेम था, वैसा शेषजी भी नहीं कह सकते। कवि के लिए तो वह वैसा ही अगम है, जैसा अहंता और ममता से मलिन मनुष्यों के लिए ब्रह्मानंद! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3082.english_translation: At that moment, Bharat's love could not be fully spoken even by Shesha. For a poet, it is as inaccessible as the bliss of Brahman is to a mind stained by ego and possessiveness.
ramacharitamanas::3082.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / प्रेमु (love) / तेहि समय (at that time) / जस तस (however) / कहि (say) / सकइ (can) / न (not) / सेषु (Shesha) / कबिहि (for the poet) / अगम (unreachable) / जिमि (like) / ब्रह्मसुखु (the bliss of Brahman) / अह (ego) / मम (mine-ness) / मलिन (stained) / जनेषु (for people)
ramacharitamanas::3082.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3082.essence: Love can become so pure that words fail completely.
ramacharitamanas::3082.simple_meaning: Bharat's love at that moment was beyond description. Even the greatest speaker could not fully capture it, just as some joys are unreachable to a restless, self-centered mind.
ramacharitamanas::3082.simple_insight: Real devotion can be so deep that language itself feels too small.
ramacharitamanas::3082.detailed_meaning: As Ram leaves, Bharat's grief and love fill the whole scene in Ayodhyakand. Tulsidas pauses the story to say that even Shesha cannot describe Bharat's feeling, because this kind of devotion is beyond ordinary speech.
ramacharitamanas::3082.modern_relevance: You try to explain why you stayed loyal to someone who gave you nothing back, and the explanation sounds thin. Some bonds are felt more deeply than they can ever be argued.
ramacharitamanas::3082.insight: It shifts the mind from trying to justify devotion to simply recognising its depth.

ramacharitamanas::3083.verse_sanskrit: सकल सनेह सिथिल रघुबर कें। गए कोस दुइ दिनकर ढरकें॥ जलु थलु देखि बसे निसि बीतें। कीन्ह गवन रघुनाथ पिरीतें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3083.verse_hindi: सब लोग श्री रामचंद्रजी के प्रेम के मारे शिथिल होने के कारण सूर्यास्त होने तक (दिनभर में) दो ही कोस चल पाए और जल-स्थल का सुपास देखकर रात को वहीं (बिना खाए-पीए ही) रह गए। रात बीतने पर श्री रघुनाथजी के प्रेमी भरतजी ने आगे गमन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3083.english_translation: Because of their love for Raghubar, everyone became weak. They walked only two kos before sunset. Seeing water and land, they stayed there through the night. At dawn, the devoted Bharat went on ahead.
ramacharitamanas::3083.translation_literal: सकल (all) / सनेह (love) / सिथिल (weakened) / रघुबर (Raghubar, Ram) / कें (for) / गए (went) / कोस (kos) / दुइ (two) / दिनकर (sun) / ढरकें (sloping down, setting)॥ / जलु (water) / थलु (land) / देखि (seeing) / बसे (stayed) / निसि (night) / बीतें (having passed) / कीन्ह (did) / गवन (journey) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath, Ram) / पिरीतें (in love)
ramacharitamanas::3083.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3083.essence: Love for Ram changes exhaustion into forward motion.
ramacharitamanas::3083.simple_meaning: Love for Ram made everyone so weak that they could barely travel. They stopped for the night after only a short distance, and Bharat moved on at dawn.
ramacharitamanas::3083.simple_insight: Love can make even hardship feel bearable when the heart is fixed on Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3083.detailed_meaning: Bharat and the returning party are on the road from Chitrakoot. Their devotion is so intense that ordinary travel feels heavy and slow. They rest by water and land through the night, and at sunrise Bharat resumes the journey, driven by love rather than comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3083.modern_relevance: You leave before sunrise for a long drive to see someone you love. The road feels endless, but you keep going because the heart has already decided.
ramacharitamanas::3083.insight: It shifts attention from physical ease to devotion-powered endurance.

ramacharitamanas::3084.verse_sanskrit: उहाँ रामु रजनी अवसेषा। जागे सीयँ सपन अस देखा॥ सहित समाज भरत जनु आए। नाथ बियोग ताप तन ताए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3084.verse_hindi: उधर श्री रामचंद्रजी रात शेष रहते ही जागे। रात को सीताजी ने ऐसा स्वप्न देखा (जिसे वे श्री रामचंद्रजी को सुनाने लगीं) मानो समाज सहित भरतजी यहाँ आए हैं। प्रभु के वियोग की अग्नि से उनका शरीर संतप्त है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3084.english_translation: There, Ram was still awake while night remained. In sleep, Sita saw a dream: Bharat had come here with his whole company, and his body was burning with the heat of separation from his lord.
ramacharitamanas::3084.translation_literal: उहाँ (there) / रामु (Ram) / रजनी (night) / अवसेषा (remaining) / जागे (awake) / सीयँ (Sita) / सपन (dream) / अस (such) / देखा (saw) / सहित (together with) / समाज (company) / भरत (Bharat) / जनु (as if) / आए (came) / नाथ (lord) / बियोग (separation) / ताप (heat) / तन (body) / ताए (burned)
ramacharitamanas::3084.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3084.essence: Separation burns so deeply it enters even dreams.
ramacharitamanas::3084.simple_meaning: Ram stays awake while night still lingers. Sita dreams that Bharat has arrived with his companions, and that he is burning with grief from separation.
ramacharitamanas::3084.simple_insight: Love keeps the heart alert, even in the night.
ramacharitamanas::3084.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the household lives under the strain of Ram's exile. Before dawn, Ram is still awake, and Sita dreams of Bharat arriving with his company, his body scorched by longing for Ram. The verse deepens the shared ache of separation.
ramacharitamanas::3084.modern_relevance: You wake before sunrise and the first thought is the person who is missing. Even sleep cannot fully loosen the bond, and the mind keeps carrying their pain.
ramacharitamanas::3084.insight: It shows how separation enters both waking life and dreams, turning love into a shared burden.

ramacharitamanas::3085.verse_sanskrit: सकल मलिन मन दीन दुखारी। देखीं सासु आन अनुहारी॥ सुनि सिय सपन भरे जल लोचन। भए सोचबस सोच बिमोचन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3085.verse_hindi: सभी लोग मन में उदास, दीन और दुःखी हैं। सासुओं को दूसरी ही सूरत में देखा। सीताजी का स्वप्न सुनकर श्री रामचंद्रजी के नेत्रों में जल भर गया और सबको सोच से छुड़ा देने वाले प्रभु स्वयं (लीला से) सोच के वश हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3085.english_translation: Everyone was sad, humble, and grieving. The mothers-in-law seemed changed in a troubling way. Hearing Sita's dream, Ram's eyes filled with tears, and the one who frees others from sorrow became overcome by sorrow himself.
ramacharitamanas::3085.translation_literal: सकल (all) / मलिन (sad, troubled) / मन (mind) / दीन (humble, poor) / दुखारी (grieving) / देखीं (saw) / सासु (mothers-in-law) / आन (other, changed) / अनुहारी (in form, appearance) / सुनि (hearing) / सिय (Sita's) / सपन (dream) / भरे (filled) / जल (water, tears) / लोचन (eyes) / भए (became) / सोचबस (under the power of grief) / सोच बिमोचन (freeing from sorrow)
ramacharitamanas::3085.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3085.essence: The one who ends sorrow can still weep with those he loves.
ramacharitamanas::3085.simple_meaning: The household is heavy with grief, and Ram is moved to tears after hearing Sita's dream. Even the one who frees others from sorrow is touched by sorrow here.
ramacharitamanas::3085.simple_insight: Even strength can tremble when love brings bad news.
ramacharitamanas::3085.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are already deep in the pain of exile. Sita recounts a troubling dream, the women around them look altered by grief, and Ram himself is shaken. The scene turns the household's hidden fear into tears.
ramacharitamanas::3085.modern_relevance: You notice your family going quiet after a dream or a late-night call. Everyone pretends to stay composed, but one small sign is enough to bring the whole room into grief.
ramacharitamanas::3085.insight: It shows how shared fear spreads through a family and how even the steady can be pierced by sorrow.

ramacharitamanas::3086.verse_sanskrit: लखन सपन यह नीक न होई। कठिन कुचाह सुनाइहि कोई॥ अस कहि बंधु समेत नहाने पूजि पुरारि साधु सनमाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::3086.verse_hindi: (और बोले-) लक्ष्मण! यह स्वप्न अच्छा नहीं है। कोई भीषण कुसमाचार (बहुत ही बुरी खबर) सुनावेगा। ऐसा कहकर उन्होंने भाई सहित स्नान किया और त्रिपुरारी महादेवजी का पूजन करके साधुओं का सम्मान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3086.english_translation: Laxman, this dream is not a good sign. Someone will bring terrible news. Saying this, he bathed with his brother, worshipped Lord Shiva, and honored the sages.
ramacharitamanas::3086.translation_literal: लखन (Laxman) / सपन (dream) / यह (this) / नीक (good) / न (not) / होई (will be) / कठिन (terrible) / कुचाह (bad news) / सुनाइहि (will tell) / कोई (someone) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / बंधु (brother) / समेत (together with) / नहाने (bathed) / पूजि (worshipped) / पुरारि (Shiva, destroyer of the three cities) / साधु (sages) / सनमाने (honored)
ramacharitamanas::3086.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3086.essence: A bad sign does not justify panic; begin with reverence and steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::3086.simple_meaning: Ram reads the dream as a bad omen, then begins the day with ritual bathing, worship of Shiva, and respect for holy men.
ramacharitamanas::3086.simple_insight: Even unease can be met with reverence, steadiness, and care.
ramacharitamanas::3086.detailed_meaning: After Sita's troubling dream, Ram does not dismiss the feeling. He tells Lakshman the dream is inauspicious and likely points to bad news ahead. Then, before the day unfolds, he and Lakshman bathe, worship Shiva, and honor the sages.
ramacharitamanas::3086.modern_relevance: You wake from a bad dream before dawn and feel the day tilting wrong. Instead of spiraling, you wash your face, pray, and treat the morning with dignity.
ramacharitamanas::3086.insight: It shifts the mind from superstition and panic to composed, respectful action.

ramacharitamanas::3087.verse_sanskrit: सनमानि सुर मुनि बंदि बैठे उतर दिसि देखत भए। नभ धूरि खग मृग भूरि भागे बिकल प्रभु आश्रम गए॥ तुलसी उठे अवलोकि कारनु काह चित सचकित रहे। सब समाचार किरात कोलन्हि आइ तेहि अवसर कहे॥
ramacharitamanas::3087.verse_hindi: देवताओं का सम्मान (पूजन) और मुनियों की वंदना करके श्री रामचंद्रजी बैठ गए और उत्तर दिशा की ओर देखने लगे। आकाश में धूल छा रही है, बहुत से पक्षी और पशु व्याकुल होकर भागे हुए प्रभु के आश्रम को आ रहे हैं। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी यह देखकर उठे और सोचने लगे कि क्या कारण है? वे चित्त में आश्चर्ययुक्त हो गए। उसी समय कोल-भीलों ने आकर सब समाचार कहे।
ramacharitamanas::3087.english_translation: After honoring the gods and bowing to the sages, Ram sat down and looked toward the north. Dust filled the sky, and many birds and animals, frightened and restless, rushed toward the Lord's hermitage. Tulsidas says that seeing this, Ram rose and wondered what had happened. His mind became alert and astonished. Then the Kirat and Kol people came and told the whole news at that moment.
ramacharitamanas::3087.translation_literal: सनमानि (having honored) / सुर (gods) / मुनि (sages) / बंदि (bowing) / बैठे (sat) / उतर दिसि (toward the north) / देखत (looking) / भए (became) । नभ (sky) / धूरि (dust) / खग (birds) / मृग (animals) / भूरि (many) / भागे (ran) / बिकल (disturbed) / प्रभु (lord) / आश्रम (hermitage) / गए (came) ॥ तुलसी (Tulsidas) / उठे (rose) / अवलोकि (seeing) / कारनु (cause) / काह (what) / चित (mind) / सचकित (astonished, alert) / रहे (remained) । सब (all) / समाचार (news) / किरात (Kirat people) / कोलन्हि (Kol people) / आइ (coming) / तेहि अवसर (at that moment) / कहे (told) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3087.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3087.simple_meaning: Ram notices unusual signs in nature and waits in alert surprise. Soon, the forest people arrive and explain what has happened.
ramacharitamanas::3087.simple_insight: Not every sudden disturbance needs immediate action; sometimes awareness comes first.
ramacharitamanas::3087.detailed_meaning: Ram has finished honoring sages and sits quietly, facing north, when the forest itself seems unsettled. Birds and animals flee toward his hermitage. He rises, alert and puzzled, just before the Kirat and Kol arrive with the news that explains the disturbance.
ramacharitamanas::3087.modern_relevance: You hear dogs barking before dawn, then see neighbors stepping outside in confusion. Something is wrong, and you stop talking long enough to pay attention before the explanation arrives.
ramacharitamanas::3087.insight: It teaches you to notice the signs before the news becomes clear.

ramacharitamanas::3088.verse_sanskrit: सुनत सुमंगल बैन मन प्रमोद तन पुलक भर। सरद सरोरुह नैन तुलसी भरे सनेह जल ॥
ramacharitamanas::3088.verse_hindi: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि सुंदर मंगल वचन सुनते ही श्री रामचंद्रजी के मन में बड़ा आनंद हुआ। शरीर में पुलकावली छा गई और शरद् ऋतु के कमल के समान नेत्र प्रेमाश्रुओं से भर गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3088.english_translation: Hearing the auspicious words, Ram's mind filled with joy. His body thrilled with goosebumps, and his eyes, like autumn lotuses, overflowed with love.
ramacharitamanas::3088.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / सुमंगल (most auspicious) / बैन (words) / मन (mind) / प्रमोद (joy) / तन (body) / पुलक (hairs standing on end) / भर (full of) / सरद (autumn) / सरोरुह (lotus) / नैन (eyes) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / भरे (filled) / सनेह (love) / जल (water/tears)
ramacharitamanas::3088.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3088.essence: Joy can overflow into tears before the mind explains it.
ramacharitamanas::3088.simple_meaning: Ram hears good news and is instantly filled with joy, love, and tears.
ramacharitamanas::3088.simple_insight: Even divine composure can soften into tears when the heart hears hope.
ramacharitamanas::3088.detailed_meaning: After signs of unease in Ayodhya, a messenger finally brings hopeful words. Ram's body responds before his mind can settle: joy rises, his skin thrills, and his eyes fill with tears. The verse lingers on that tender release before the next concern arrives.
ramacharitamanas::3088.modern_relevance: You get the message you've been waiting for after a long, anxious evening. Before you can even speak, your chest loosens and tears come.
ramacharitamanas::3088.insight: It shows how the heart reveals relief through the body before thought catches up.

ramacharitamanas::3089.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि सोचबस भे सियरवनू। कारन कवन भरत आगवनू॥ एक आइ अस कहा बहोरी। सेन संग चतुरंग न थोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3089.verse_hindi: सीतापति श्री रामचंद्रजी पुनः सोच के वश हो गए कि भरत के आने का क्या कारण है? फिर एक ने आकर ऐसा कहा कि उनके साथ में बड़ी भारी चतुरंगिणी सेना भी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3089.english_translation: Rama became worried again: what was the reason for Bharat's arrival? Then another person came and said that he had brought a very large fourfold army with him.
ramacharitamanas::3089.translation_literal: बहुरि (again) / सोचबस (under the control of worry) / भे (became) / सियरवनू (Rama) / कारन (reason) / कवन (what) / भरत (Bharat) / आगवनू (arrival)॥ / एक (one person) / आइ (coming) / अस (thus) / कहा (said) / बहोरी (again) / सेन (army) / संग (with) / चतुरंग (fourfold) / न थोरी (not small) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3089.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3089.essence: A brother's arrival can carry both love and threat.
ramacharitamanas::3089.simple_meaning: Rama grows uneasy at Bharat's arrival and hears that Bharat has come with a large army.
ramacharitamanas::3089.simple_insight: Even a loving reunion can stir fear when duty and family loyalty seem to collide.
ramacharitamanas::3089.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Rama is waiting in the forest when news arrives that Bharat is coming. The report is unsettling because Bharat is not alone—he brings a large army. That detail deepens Rama's worry before the real conversation begins.
ramacharitamanas::3089.modern_relevance: You hear that a sibling is coming to talk, but they arrive with lawyers, relatives, and a long silence. Before anyone speaks, your stomach tightens.
ramacharitamanas::3089.insight: It sets up the tension between family affection and the fear of political intent.

ramacharitamanas::3090.verse_sanskrit: सो सुनि रामहि भा अति सोचू। इत पितु बच इत बंधु सकोचू॥ भरत सुभाउ समुझि मन माहीं। प्रभु चित हित थिति पावत नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3090.verse_hindi: यह सुनकर श्री रामचंद्रजी को अत्यंत सोच हुआ। इधर तो पिता के वचन और उधर भाई भरतजी का संकोच! भरतजी के स्वभाव को मन में समझकर तो प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी चित्त को ठहराने के लिए कोई स्थान ही नहीं पाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3090.english_translation: Hearing this, Ram was deeply troubled: his father’s word on one side, Bharat’s hesitation on the other. Thinking of Bharat’s nature, he could not settle his mind.
ramacharitamanas::3090.translation_literal: सो (that) / सुनि (hearing) / रामहि (to Ram) / भा (became) / अति (very) / सोचू (concern) / इत (here/on this side) / पितु (father's) / बच (word) / इत (here/on this side) / बंधु (brother) / सकोचू (hesitation) / भरत (Bharat) / सुभाउ (nature) / समुझि (understanding) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / प्रभु (the Lord) / चित (mind) / हित (for settling) / थिति (steadiness) / पावत (getting) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::3090.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3090.essence: Love and obligation can pull the mind apart at once.
ramacharitamanas::3090.simple_meaning: Ram feels torn between keeping his father's promise and understanding Bharat’s loving hesitation. That conflict leaves his mind unsettled.
ramacharitamanas::3090.simple_insight: Even the right path can feel heavy when love pulls in two directions.
ramacharitamanas::3090.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, news of Bharat’s arrival reaches Ram while exile still hangs over the family. Ram is caught between Dasharath’s binding word and Bharat’s character, and that inner conflict makes calm impossible.
ramacharitamanas::3090.modern_relevance: You get a message that your parent expects one thing, but your sibling’s silence says something else. You can feel the tension before anyone even speaks.
ramacharitamanas::3090.insight: It shows how duty can become emotionally complicated when family loyalty and promise collide.

ramacharitamanas::3091.verse_sanskrit: समाधान तब भा यह जाने। भरतु कहे महुँ साधु सयाने॥ लखन लखेउ प्रभु हृदयँ खभारू। कहत समय सम नीति बिचारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3091.verse_hindi: तब यह जानकर समाधान हो गया कि भरत साधु और सयाने हैं तथा मेरे कहने में (आज्ञाकारी) हैं। लक्ष्मणजी ने देखा कि प्रभु श्री रामजी के हृदय में चिंता है तो वे समय के अनुसार अपना नीतियुक्त विचार कहने लगे- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3091.english_translation: Then he understood: Bharat is noble and wise, and he speaks with obedience. Lakshman saw the worry in Ram's heart and, at the right moment, began to speak with measured judgment.
ramacharitamanas::3091.translation_literal: समाधान (resolution) / तब (then) / भा (became) / यह (this) / जाने (knowing) / भरतु (Bharat) / कहे (in speaking) / महुँ (in) / साधु (noble) / सयाने (wise)॥ / लखन (Lakshman) / लखेउ (saw) / प्रभु (Lord) / हृदयँ (in heart) / खभारू (worry) / कहत (speaking) / समय (time / occasion) / सम (according to) / नीति (right conduct / judgment) / बिचारू (thought)॥
ramacharitamanas::3091.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3091.essence: Right speech comes from seeing both character and timing clearly.
ramacharitamanas::3091.simple_meaning: Ram feels relief when he realises Bharat is wise and obedient. Lakshman notices Ram's worry and chooses the right moment to speak carefully.
ramacharitamanas::3091.simple_insight: Careful timing matters; even truth should arrive when the heart can receive it.
ramacharitamanas::3091.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram is torn between Dasharath's command and Bharat's possible intentions. Relief comes when he sees Bharat's character clearly. Lakshman notices Ram's hidden worry and waits for the proper moment before offering a thoughtful reply.
ramacharitamanas::3091.modern_relevance: You can feel tension in a room before anyone says a word. The wise person notices it, reads the moment, and speaks only when the other heart is ready.
ramacharitamanas::3091.insight: It teaches you to read the room and speak with timing, not impulse.

ramacharitamanas::3092.verse_sanskrit: बिनु पूछें कछु कहउँ गोसाईं। सेवकु समयँ न ढीठ ढिठाईं॥ तुम्ह सर्बग्य सिरोमनि स्वामी। आपनि समुझि कहउँ अनुगामी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3092.verse_hindi: हे स्वामी! आपके बिना ही पूछे मैं कुछ कहता हूँ, सेवक समय पर ढिठाई करने से ढीठ नहीं समझा जाता (अर्थात् आप पूछें तब मैं कहूँ, ऐसा अवसर नहीं है, इसलिए यह मेरा कहना ढिठाई नहीं होगा)। हे स्वामी! आप सर्वज्ञों में शिरोमणि हैं (सब जानते ही हैं)। मैं सेवक तो अपनी समझ की बात कहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3092.english_translation: “Without being asked, I say a little, O Lord. A servant is not rude for speaking at the right time. You are the crown jewel of the all-knowing, O master. I speak only according to my understanding, as your follower.”
ramacharitamanas::3092.translation_literal: बिनु (without) / पूछें (being asked) / कछु (some) / कहउँ (I speak) / गोसाईं (O lord) / सेवकु (servant) / समयँ (at the right time) / न (not) / ढीठ (rude) / ढिठाईं (rudeness) / तुम्ह (you) / सर्बग्य (all-knowing) / सिरोमनि (crown jewel) / स्वामी (master) / आपनि (your own) / समुझि (understanding) / कहउँ (I speak) / अनुगामी (follower)
ramacharitamanas::3092.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::3092.essence: Humility lets you speak clearly without claiming importance.
ramacharitamanas::3092.simple_meaning: A true servant speaks humbly and at the right time, trusting the master’s wisdom while offering honest understanding.
ramacharitamanas::3092.simple_insight: You can be direct without being disrespectful when your intention is service, not self-importance.
ramacharitamanas::3092.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Lakshman is speaking to Ram during a tense family moment. He knows Ram already understands everything, yet he still offers his view carefully. The verse shows loyal service expressed through humble, timely speech.
ramacharitamanas::3092.modern_relevance: You’re in a family group chat, typing and deleting a message because the truth matters but tone matters too. This verse gives you that balance: speak honestly, but speak as someone who is serving, not asserting.
ramacharitamanas::3092.insight: It teaches you to pair honesty with humility, so your words help rather than wound.

ramacharitamanas::3093.verse_sanskrit: नाथ सुहृद सुठि सरल चित सील सनेह निधान। सब पर प्रीति प्रतीति जियँ जानिअ आपु समान ॥
ramacharitamanas::3093.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! आप परम सुहृद् (बिना ही कारण परम हित करने वाले), सरल हृदय तथा शील और स्नेह के भंडार हैं, आपका सभी पर प्रेम और विश्वास है, और अपने हृदय में सबको अपने ही समान जानते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3093.english_translation: O Lord, you are a true well-wisher, utterly simple in heart, a storehouse of virtue and affection. You love and trust everyone, and in your heart you see all as your own equal.
ramacharitamanas::3093.translation_literal: नाथ (Lord) / सुहृद (true well-wisher) / सुठि (utterly) / सरल (simple) / चित (heart-mind) / सील (virtue) / सनेह (affection) / निधान (storehouse) / सब पर (toward all) / प्रीति (love) / प्रतीति (trust) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानिअ (know) / आपु (yourself) / समान (equal)
ramacharitamanas::3093.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3093.essence: True greatness treats everyone as equal and beloved.
ramacharitamanas::3093.simple_meaning: Ram is described as a deeply kind, simple-hearted presence who trusts and loves everyone equally, seeing all beings as his own.
ramacharitamanas::3093.simple_insight: It feels safe to meet a love that does not rank people or keep score.
ramacharitamanas::3093.detailed_meaning: Bharat is speaking in Ayodhyakand, trying to name Ram’s character after exile has shattered the family. He praises Ram not as a distant ruler but as the kindest presence imaginable: simple, affectionate, and equal toward all.
ramacharitamanas::3093.modern_relevance: You meet someone who remembers the names of the quiet people, not just the important ones. They make no one feel lesser, and you leave feeling seen.
ramacharitamanas::3093.insight: It shifts your attention from status and suspicion to equal regard and open-hearted trust.

ramacharitamanas::3094.verse_sanskrit: बिषई जीव पाइ प्रभुताई। मूढ़ मोह बस होहिं जनाई॥ भरतु नीति रत साधु सुजाना। प्रभु पद प्रेमु सकल जगु जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3094.verse_hindi: परंतु मूढ़ विषयी जीव प्रभुता पाकर मोहवश अपने असली स्वरूप को प्रकट कर देते हैं। भरत नीतिपरायण, साधु और चतुर हैं तथा प्रभु (आप) के चरणों में उनका प्रेम है, इस बात को सारा जगत् जानता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3094.english_translation: But a foolish, desire-driven person reveals their true nature when given power, overcome by delusion. Bharat, by contrast, is devoted to right conduct, noble, wise, and known throughout the world for his love at the Lord's feet.
ramacharitamanas::3094.translation_literal: बिषई (desire-driven) / जीव (being) / पाइ (having obtained) / प्रभुताई (authority, power) / मूढ़ (foolish) / मोह (delusion) / बस (under the control) / होहिं (become) / जनाई (revealed)॥ भरतु (Bharat) / नीति (right conduct) / रत (devoted to) / साधु (noble, good) / सुजाना (wise) / प्रभु (lord) / पद (feet) / प्रेमु (love) / सकल (entire) / जगु (world) / जाना (knows)॥
ramacharitamanas::3094.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3094.essence: Power does not transform character; it uncovers what was hidden.
ramacharitamanas::3094.simple_meaning: Power exposes a foolish person's hidden desires. Bharat, however, is known everywhere for right conduct, wisdom, and love for Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::3094.simple_insight: Status does not create character; it uncovers it.
ramacharitamanas::3094.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the contrast between Bharat and a deluded, desire-driven person becomes sharp. Power makes the foolish reveal themselves, but Bharat's life already shows steady conduct, wisdom, and love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3094.modern_relevance: You get promoted, and suddenly everyone sees how you treat the assistant, the deadline, and the credit. Authority doesn't invent your character; it exposes it.
ramacharitamanas::3094.insight: It shifts attention from what power gives you to what power reveals about you.

ramacharitamanas::3095.verse_sanskrit: तेऊ आजु राम पदु पाई। चले धरम मरजाद मेटाई॥ कुटिल कुबंधु कुअवसरु ताकी। जानि राम बनबास एकाकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3095.verse_hindi: वे भरतजी आज श्री रामजी (आप) का पद (सिंहासन या अधिकार) पाकर धर्म की मर्यादा को मिटाकर चले हैं। कुटिल खोटे भाई भरत कुसमय देखकर और यह जानकर कि रामजी (आप) वनवास में अकेले (असहाय) हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3095.english_translation: They have come today to take Ram's place, overturning the bounds of dharma. Seeing the right moment, that crooked brother came knowing Ram was alone in the forest.
ramacharitamanas::3095.translation_literal: तेऊ (they too) / आजु (today) / राम पदु (Ram's place) / पाई (having obtained) / चले (went) / धरम (dharma) / मरजाद (bounds of conduct) / मेटाई (erasing)॥ / कुटिल (crooked) / कुबंधु (evil brother) / कुअवसरु (bad moment) / ताकी (seizing) / जानि (knowing) / राम (Ram) / बनबास (forest exile) / एकाकी (alone) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3095.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3095.essence: A badly timed approach can look like virtue while hiding disruption.
ramacharitamanas::3095.simple_meaning: Bharat has come at the wrong time, when Ram is alone in exile. The verse frames him as taking Ram's place and upsetting rightful conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3095.simple_insight: Some actions look like loyalty from a distance, but timing and intent reveal the real motive.
ramacharitamanas::3095.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's tense aftermath, Bharat is being watched through suspicion and grief. This verse is not a conclusion but a charged accusation in the middle of the scene: he has come while Ram is away, and the speaker reads that as a threat to dharma and rightful rule.
ramacharitamanas::3095.modern_relevance: A sibling shows up after everyone is exhausted, and the room instantly changes. Even before words are spoken, you can feel whether the visit is care, control, or calculation.
ramacharitamanas::3095.insight: It trains the mind to read motive, timing, and consequence together instead of trusting appearances.

ramacharitamanas::3096.verse_sanskrit: करि कुमंत्रु मन साजि समाजू। आए करै अकंटक राजू॥ कोटि प्रकार कलपि कुटिलाई। आए दल बटोरि दोउ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3096.verse_hindi: अपने मन में बुरा विचार करके, समाज जोड़कर राज्यों को निष्कण्टक करने के लिए यहाँ आए हैं। करोड़ों (अनेकों) प्रकार की कुटिलताएँ रचकर सेना बटोरकर दोनों भाई आए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3096.english_translation: Having formed a wicked plan in the mind, they came with a gathered assembly to make the kingdom secure. After plotting countless kinds of deceit, the two brothers came with assembled forces.
ramacharitamanas::3096.translation_literal: करि (having done) / कुमंत्रु (evil counsel) / मन (mind) / साजि (having arranged) / समाजू (assembly) / आए (came) / करै (to make) / अकंटक (free from obstacles) / राजू (kingdom)॥ / कोटि (crores, countless) / प्रकार (kinds) / कलपि (having devised) / कुटिलाई (crookedness, deceit) / आए (came) / दल (army) / बटोरि (having gathered) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3096.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3096.essence: Power guided by crooked intent turns every gathering into suspicion.
ramacharitamanas::3096.simple_meaning: The brothers came with a hidden scheme, trying to secure power by gathering support and force.
ramacharitamanas::3096.simple_insight: Hidden motives make even a public act feel crooked.
ramacharitamanas::3096.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's return is being judged through the lens of suspicion. This verse describes the charge against him: that he came with counsel, supporters, and force to make the kingdom uncontested. The accusation deepens the tension before the moral reversal is revealed.
ramacharitamanas::3096.modern_relevance: A family meeting starts polite, but everyone can feel the hidden agenda under the careful words. The room gets colder when people are really negotiating power, not peace.
ramacharitamanas::3096.insight: It frames political action as suspect when desire for control is hiding underneath it.

ramacharitamanas::3097.verse_sanskrit: जौं जियँ होति न कपट कुचाली। केहि सोहाति रथ बाजि गजाली॥ भरतहि दोसु देइ को जाएँ। जग बौराइ राज पदु पाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3097.verse_hindi: यदि इनके हृदय में कपट और कुचाल न होती, तो रथ, घोड़े और हाथियों की कतार (ऐसे समय) किसे सुहाती? परन्तु भरत को ही व्यर्थ कौन दोष दे? राजपद पा जाने पर सारा जगत् ही पागल (मतवाला) हो जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3097.english_translation: If there were no deceit and crookedness in their hearts, who would enjoy chariots, horses, and elephants at such a time? Who can really blame Bharat? When people get royal power, the whole world goes mad.
ramacharitamanas::3097.translation_literal: जौं (if) / जियँ (in the heart) / होति (there is) / न (not) / कपट (deceit) / कुचाली (crooked conduct) / केहि (who) / सोहाति (would suit) / रथ (chariots) / बाजि (horses) / गजाली (lines of elephants) / भरतहि (to Bharat) / दोसु (fault) / देइ (gives) / को (who) / जाएँ (going) / जग (the world) / बौराइ (goes mad) / राज पदु (royal position) / पाएँ (having obtained)
ramacharitamanas::3097.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3097.essence: Power exposes how quickly judgment bends around status.
ramacharitamanas::3097.simple_meaning: If there were no deceit in the heart, no one would be dazzled by royal display. Don’t single out Bharat; power itself can make people lose judgment.
ramacharitamanas::3097.simple_insight: It softens quick blame and shows how status can cloud anyone’s mind.
ramacharitamanas::3097.detailed_meaning: Bharat’s return to Ayodhya is being judged through suspicion and political gossip. Tulsidas steps back from the accusation and points to a wider truth: royal power intoxicates people, so Bharat should not be condemned so easily.
ramacharitamanas::3097.modern_relevance: A family starts treating someone differently the moment a promotion, inheritance, or title enters the picture. This verse asks you to notice how status changes everyone’s behavior, not just the person at the center.
ramacharitamanas::3097.insight: It shifts judgment from one blamed person to the corrupting pull of power itself.

ramacharitamanas::3098.verse_sanskrit: ससि गुर तिय गामी नघुषु चढ़ेउ भूमिसुर जान। लोक बेद तें बिमुख भा अधम न बेन समान ॥
ramacharitamanas::3098.verse_hindi: चंद्रमा गुरुपत्नी गामी हुआ, राजा नहुष ब्राह्मणों की पालकी पर चढ़ा और राजा वेन के समान नीच तो कोई नहीं होगा, जो लोक और वेद दोनों से विमुख हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3098.english_translation: The moon, Nahusha, and Vena all fell when they turned against the moral order and the learned; Vena was the lowest of all.
ramacharitamanas::3098.translation_literal: ससि (the moon) / गुर (the teacher, or the respected) / तिय गामी (one who went to another's wife) / नघुषु (Nahusha) / चढ़ेउ (mounted) / भूमिसुर (the learned, brahmins) / जान (knowing) / लोक (the world) / बेद (the Veda) / तें (from) / बिमुख (turned away) / भा (became) / अधम (lowest) / न (not) / बेन (Vena) / समान (equal)
ramacharitamanas::3098.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3098.essence: Power turns rotten the moment it abandons right conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3098.simple_meaning: Even famous rulers fell when they violated right conduct and ignored the guidance of the learned. Vena is named as the worst example.
ramacharitamanas::3098.simple_insight: Status cannot protect you from the consequences of moral collapse.
ramacharitamanas::3098.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the debate around Bharat's conduct turns to old examples of rulers destroyed by pride. The narrator recalls Nahusha and Vena to show that power, once cut off from right conduct and wise counsel, becomes a fall waiting to happen.
ramacharitamanas::3098.modern_relevance: A celebrated leader ignores every warning, surrounds himself with flatterers, and then acts surprised when everything unravels. This verse names that pattern before it repeats itself.
ramacharitamanas::3098.insight: It shifts attention from public success to the moral direction behind it.

ramacharitamanas::3099.verse_sanskrit: सहसबाहु सुरनाथु त्रिसंकू। केहि न राजमद दीन्ह कलंकू॥ भरत कीन्ह यह उचित उपाऊ। रिपु रिन रंच न राखब काउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3099.verse_hindi: सहस्रबाहु, देवराज इंद्र और त्रिशंकु आदि किसको राजमद ने कलंक नहीं दिया? भरत ने यह उपाय उचित ही किया है, क्योंकि शत्रु और ऋण को कभी जरा भी शेष नहीं रखना चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3099.english_translation: Who has not been stained by the intoxication of kingship—Sahasrabahu, Indra, and Trishanku? Bharat has taken the right course: never leave an enemy or a debt even a little unpaid.
ramacharitamanas::3099.translation_literal: सहसबाहु (Sahasrabahu) / सुरनाथु (lord of the devas) / त्रिसंकू (Trishanku) / केहि (whom) / न (not) / राजमद (pride of kingship) / दीन्ह (gave) / कलंकू (stain)॥ / भरतहि (to Bharat) / दोसु (fault/blame) / देइ (giving) / को (who) / जाएँ (should go) / जग (world) / बौराइ (go mad) / राज पदु (royal position) / पाएँ (having obtained)॥
ramacharitamanas::3099.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3099.essence: Power corrupts; clean duty keeps you from being ruled by it.
ramacharitamanas::3099.simple_meaning: Kingship often corrupts people, so Bharat's choice is praised as the right way to act: do not leave an enemy or a debt unfinished.
ramacharitamanas::3099.simple_insight: You feel the relief of acting cleanly, without the poison of pride or unfinished obligation.
ramacharitamanas::3099.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the pain of Ram's exile has turned into a lesson about power. Tulsidas recalls rulers like Sahasrabahu, Indra, and Trishanku to show how royal pride stains even the great, then praises Bharat for choosing the right response to duty and debt.
ramacharitamanas::3099.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, and suddenly every old rivalry wakes up in your chest. This verse reminds you that status can poison judgment unless you keep your debts, duties, and motives clean.
ramacharitamanas::3099.insight: It shifts attention from status itself to the moral discipline needed to hold it without corruption.

ramacharitamanas::3100.verse_sanskrit: एक कीन्हि नहिं भरत भलाई। निदरे रामु जानि असहाई॥ समुझि परिहि सोउ आजु बिसेषी। समर सरोष राम मुखु पेखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3100.verse_hindi: हाँ, भरत ने एक बात अच्छी नहीं की, जो रामजी (आप) को असहाय जानकर उनका निरादर किया! पर आज संग्राम में श्री रामजी (आप) का क्रोधपूर्ण मुख देखकर यह बात भी उनकी समझ में विशेष रूप से आ जाएगी (अर्थात् इस निरादर का फल भी वे अच्छी तरह पा जाएँगे) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3100.english_translation: Bharat did not do one thing well: he insulted Ram, thinking him helpless. Today, seeing Ram's anger in battle, he will understand that clearly.
ramacharitamanas::3100.translation_literal: एक (one) / कीन्हि (did) / नहिं (not) / भरत (Bharat) / भलाई (goodness) / निदरे (insulted) / रामु (Ram) / जानि (knowing) / असहाई (helpless) / समुझि (understand) / परिहि (will fall upon) / सोउ (that also) / आजु (today) / बिसेषी (especially) / समर (battle) / सरोष (with anger) / राम मुखु (Ram's face) / पेखी (seeing)
ramacharitamanas::3100.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3100.essence: You can mistake gentleness for weakness only until pressure reveals the truth.
ramacharitamanas::3100.simple_meaning: Bharat once treated Ram as helpless, and that disrespect will soon be answered when he sees Ram in battle.
ramacharitamanas::3100.simple_insight: Pride and misjudgment look small when reality finally stands before you.
ramacharitamanas::3100.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the brothers' honor and Ram's exile are being weighed against each other. The narrator says Bharat made one mistake: he underestimated Ram. Now, as war approaches, that mistake will be answered by Ram's fierce face.
ramacharitamanas::3100.modern_relevance: You dismissed someone as powerless because they stayed quiet. Then one day they stood firm, and your old assumption collapsed.
ramacharitamanas::3100.insight: It shifts you from judging by appearance to respecting hidden strength.

ramacharitamanas::3101.verse_sanskrit: एतना कहत नीति रस भूला। रन रस बिटपु पुलक मिस फूला॥ प्रभु पद बंदि सीस रज राखी। बोले सत्य सहज बलु भाषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3101.verse_hindi: इतना कहते ही लक्ष्मणजी नीतिरस भूल गए और युद्धरस रूपी वृक्ष पुलकावली के बहाने से फूल उठा (अर्थात् नीति की बात कहते-कहते उनके शरीर में वीर रस छा गया)। वे प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणों की वंदना करके, चरण रज को सिर पर रखकर सच्चा और स्वाभाविक बल कहते हुए बोले ॥
ramacharitamanas::3101.english_translation: As he said this, Lakshman forgot all talk of policy and blossomed with heroic fervor. Bowing at his Lord's feet and placing the dust of those feet on his head, he spoke the truth with natural strength.
ramacharitamanas::3101.translation_literal: एतना (this much) / कहत (saying) / नीति रस (the flavor of policy) / भूला (forgot) / रन रस (the flavor of battle) / बिटपु (tree) / पुलक मिस (as if by thrilled hairs) / फूला (blossomed)॥ / प्रभु पद (Lord's feet) / बंदि (bowing) / सीस रज (head dust) / राखी (placed) / बोले (spoke) / सत्य (truth) / सहज (natural) / बलु (strength) / भाषी (speaking)॥
ramacharitamanas::3101.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::3101.essence: True strength speaks only after bowing first.
ramacharitamanas::3101.simple_meaning: Lakshman stops speaking like a strategist and shifts into heroic resolve. He bows to Ram, takes the dust of Ram's feet on his head, and speaks from his true strength.
ramacharitamanas::3101.simple_insight: Real courage begins after surrender, not before it.
ramacharitamanas::3101.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Lakshman has been defending Ram's honor in the face of Bharat's actions. As his anger turns into warrior resolve, he first bows to Ram and honors his feet. Only then does he speak with fearless honesty.
ramacharitamanas::3101.modern_relevance: You were arguing in circles until you paused, took a breath, and remembered who you serve. The next words came cleaner, stronger, and without posture.
ramacharitamanas::3101.insight: It shifts you from reactive debate into grounded speech rooted in loyalty and inner strength.

ramacharitamanas::3102.verse_sanskrit: अनुचित नाथ न मानब मोरा। भरत हमहि उपचार न थोरा॥ कहँ लगि सहिअ रहिअ मनु मारें। नाथ साथ धनु हाथ हमारें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3102.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! मेरा कहना अनुचित न मानिएगा। भरत ने हमें कम नहीं प्रचारा है (हमारे साथ कम छेड़छाड़ नहीं की है)। आखिर कहाँ तक सहा जाए और मन मारे रहा जाए, जब स्वामी हमारे साथ हैं और धनुष हमारे हाथ में है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3102.english_translation: O Lord, do not take my words as improper. Bharata has not treated me lightly. How long should I keep bearing it and swallowing my anger, when my lord is beside me and my bow is in my hand?
ramacharitamanas::3102.translation_literal: अनुचित (improper) / न (not) / मानब (consider) / मोरा (my) / भरत (Bharata) / हमहि (us) / उपचार (treatment) / न थोरा (not little) / कहँ लगि (until how long) / सहिअ (should be endured) / रहिअ (should remain) / मनु मारें (with mind killed / suppressing the mind) / नाथ (Lord) / साथ (with) / धनु (bow) / हाथ (hand) / हमारें (our)
ramacharitamanas::3102.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::3102.essence: Restraint has a limit; then action becomes the honest answer.
ramacharitamanas::3102.simple_meaning: Lakshman says he has tolerated enough. With Ram beside him and his bow in hand, he will no longer stay silent or passive.
ramacharitamanas::3102.simple_insight: There is a point where restraint becomes self-betrayal, and right action must begin.
ramacharitamanas::3102.detailed_meaning: On the battlefield before Ram's cause is fully answered, Lakshman bristles at Bharata's treatment. He tells Ram not to judge him harshly: he has endured enough. With his lord beside him and his bow ready, patience has become impossible.
ramacharitamanas::3102.modern_relevance: You keep swallowing your words in a meeting while someone keeps undermining you. Then your manager is right there, your facts are clear, and you know the moment has come to speak.
ramacharitamanas::3102.insight: It shifts you from passive endurance to decisive, responsible action.

ramacharitamanas::3103.verse_sanskrit: छत्रि जाति रघुकुल जनमु राम अनुग जगु जान। लातहुँ मारें चढ़ति सिर नीच को धूरि समान ॥
ramacharitamanas::3103.verse_hindi: क्षत्रिय जाति, रघुकुल में जन्म और फिर मैं श्री रामजी (आप) का अनुगामी (सेवक) हूँ, यह जगत् जानता है। (फिर भला कैसे सहा जाए?) धूल के समान नीच कौन है, परन्तु वह भी लात मारने पर सिर ही चढ़ती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3103.english_translation: I am born in the Raghu clan, a warrior by birth, and the whole world knows I am Ram's follower. How can I endure this? Even the lowest dust rises to the head when kicked.
ramacharitamanas::3103.translation_literal: छत्रि जाति (warrior caste) / रघुकुल (Raghu clan) / जनमु (birth) / राम अनुग (Ram's follower) / जगु (world) / जान (knows) / लातहुँ (even with kicks) / मारें (when struck) / चढ़ति (rises) / सिर (to the head) / नीच (lowly) / को धूरि (dust) / समान (like)
ramacharitamanas::3103.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::3103.simple_meaning: Lakshman says his birth and loyalty to Ram should be respected, and even something lowly reacts when struck. He is warning that humiliation cannot be taken lightly.
ramacharitamanas::3103.simple_insight: Self-respect can be quiet, but it still has limits.
ramacharitamanas::3103.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Lakshman is already bristling at the insult done to Ram and Bharat's courtly treatment of the exile. He reminds everyone that he is a Kshatriya of Raghu's line and Ram's follower, then declares that even dust rises when kicked.
ramacharitamanas::3103.modern_relevance: You keep swallowing disrespect in a meeting, smiling while someone keeps pushing too far. At some point, your dignity asks for a response, not more endurance.
ramacharitamanas::3103.insight: It teaches you that loyalty does not mean accepting humiliation forever.

ramacharitamanas::3104.verse_sanskrit: उठि कर जोरि रजायसु मागा। मनहुँ बीर रस सोवत जागा॥ बाँधि जटा सिर कसि कटि भाथा। साजि सरासनु सायकु हाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3104.verse_hindi: यों कहकर लक्ष्मणजी ने उठकर, हाथ जोड़कर आज्ञा माँगी। मानो वीर रस सोते से जाग उठा हो। सिर पर जटा बाँधकर कमर में तरकस कस लिया और धनुष को सजाकर तथा बाण को हाथ में लेकर कहा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3104.english_translation: Laxman rose, joined his hands, and asked for permission. It was as if warrior spirit woke from sleep. He tied his matted hair, tightened his waistcloth, and took up his bow and arrows.
ramacharitamanas::3104.translation_literal: उठि (rising) / कर (hand) / जोरि (joined) / रजायसु (permission) / मागा (asked) / मनहुँ (as if) / बीर रस (warrior essence) / सोवत (sleeping) / जागा (woke) / बाँधि (tying) / जटा (matted hair) / सिर (head) / कसि (tightening) / कटि (waist) / भाथा (quiver) / साजि (preparing) / सरासनु (bow) / सायकु (arrows) / हाथा (in hand)
ramacharitamanas::3104.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3104.essence: True courage wakes instantly when duty calls.
ramacharitamanas::3104.simple_meaning: Laxman stands up, asks permission, and prepares for battle. His sleeping courage wakes fully as he arms himself.
ramacharitamanas::3104.simple_insight: Readiness is not noise. It is the quiet moment when courage stands up and acts.
ramacharitamanas::3104.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, tension has risen around Ram, Bharat, and the insult to the Raghu line. Laxman answers at once. He rises, seeks permission, and arms himself, showing the fierce service and battle-readiness that define his loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::3104.modern_relevance: Your phone buzzes with bad news, and you stop scrolling. You take a breath, straighten up, and do what needs doing without drama.
ramacharitamanas::3104.insight: It shifts attention from hesitation to immediate readiness, showing how disciplined loyalty becomes action.

ramacharitamanas::3105.verse_sanskrit: आजु राम सेवक जसु लेऊँ। भरतहि समर सिखावन देऊँ॥ राम निरादर कर फलु पाई। सोवहुँ समर सेज दोउ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3105.verse_hindi: आज मैं श्री राम (आप) का सेवक होने का यश लूँ और भरत को संग्राम में शिक्षा दूँ। श्री रामचंद्रजी (आप) के निरादर का फल पाकर दोनों भाई (भरत-शत्रुघ्न) रण शय्या पर सोवें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3105.english_translation: Today I will earn the praise of being Ram's servant and teach Bharat a lesson in battle. Let the two brothers, having suffered the fruit of disrespecting Ram, lie on the battlefield together.
ramacharitamanas::3105.translation_literal: आजु (today) / राम (Ram) / सेवक (servant) / जसु (fame, praise) / लेऊँ (I take, I earn) / भरतहि (to Bharat) / समर (battle) / सिखावन (teaching, lesson) / देऊँ (I give) / राम (Ram) / निरादर (disrespect) / कर (of, having done) / फलु (fruit, result) / पाई (having obtained) / सोवहुँ (let them sleep) / समर (battle) / सेज (bed) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::3105.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::3105.essence: True service can look like battle when loyalty is tested.
ramacharitamanas::3105.simple_meaning: Lakshman is ready to prove his devotion by fighting for Ram and confronting Bharat. He sees battle as the way to answer disrespect toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3105.simple_insight: Love can become fierce when something sacred is threatened.
ramacharitamanas::3105.detailed_meaning: Lakshman has just risen, asked for permission, and armed himself. Standing before the assembled court at Chitrakoot, he speaks in anger and loyalty at once: if Bharat stands against Ram, he will answer as Ram's servant.
ramacharitamanas::3105.modern_relevance: You hear a friend insult the person you love most, and your whole body tightens. Before you speak, you know loyalty is about to test your restraint.
ramacharitamanas::3105.insight: It turns devotion into action, showing that service can include fearless confrontation when dharma is challenged.

ramacharitamanas::3106.verse_sanskrit: आइ बना भल सकल समाजू। प्रगट करउँ रिस पाछिल आजू॥ जिमि करि निकर दलइ मृगराजू। लेइ लपेटि लवा जिमि बाजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3106.verse_hindi: अच्छा हुआ जो सारा समाज आकर एकत्र हो गया। आज मैं पिछला सब क्रोध प्रकट करूँगा। जैसे सिंह हाथियों के झुंड को कुचल डालता है और बाज जैसे लवे को लपेट में ले लेता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3106.english_translation: Good that the whole assembly has gathered. Today I will bring out all my anger. Like a lion crushing a herd of elephants, like a hawk folding up a lark.
ramacharitamanas::3106.translation_literal: आइ (having come) / बना (became) / भल (good) / सकल (whole) / समाजू (assembly) / प्रगट (manifest) / करउँ (I will do) / रिस (anger) / पाछिल (past, all that was held back) / आजू (today) / जिमि (like) / करि (lion) / निकर (a herd) / दलइ (crushes) / मृगराजू (king of beasts) / लेइ (taking) / लपेटि (folding, seizing) / लवा (lark) / जिमि (like) / बाजू (hawk)
ramacharitamanas::3106.speaker: Ravana
ramacharitamanas::3106.essence: Anger fed by pride always looks for a crowd to conquer.
ramacharitamanas::3106.simple_meaning: Ravana sees the gathered crowd as a chance to unleash the anger he has been holding back, boasting that he will overpower them completely.
ramacharitamanas::3106.simple_insight: Pride turns a crowd into a target and anger into a plan.
ramacharitamanas::3106.detailed_meaning: In Lanka, Ravana has heard the challenge and now sees the whole assembly before him. Instead of restraint, he swells with rage and boasts of crushing everyone like a lion and hawk overpowering weaker creatures.
ramacharitamanas::3106.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense meeting already burning inside, ready to prove a point instead of solve the problem.
ramacharitamanas::3106.insight: It shows how ego converts conflict into domination, not understanding.

ramacharitamanas::3107.verse_sanskrit: तैसेहिं भरतहि सेन समेता। सानुज निदरि निपातउँ खेता॥ जौं सहाय कर संकरु आई। तौ मारउँ रन राम दोहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3107.verse_hindi: वैसे ही भरत को सेना समेत और छोटे भाई सहित तिरस्कार करके मैदान में पछाड़ूँगा। यदि शंकरजी भी आकर उनकी सहायता करें, तो भी, मुझे रामजी की सौगंध है, मैं उन्हें युद्ध में (अवश्य) मार डालूँगा (छोड़ूँगा नहीं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3107.english_translation: I will trample Bharat and his army, along with his younger brother, in the field. Even if Shankar himself comes to help them, by Ram's name I will kill them in battle.
ramacharitamanas::3107.translation_literal: तैसेहिं (likewise) / भरतहि (Bharat) / सेन समेता (together with the army) / सानुज (with the younger brother) / निदरि (disregarding) / निपातउँ (I will strike down) / खेता (in the field) / जौं (if) / सहाय (helper) / कर (as) / संकरु (Shankar) / आई (comes) / तौ (then) / मारउँ (I will kill) / रन (in battle) / राम दोहाई (by Ram's oath)
ramacharitamanas::3107.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::3107.essence: Anger makes even devotion sound like a threat.
ramacharitamanas::3107.simple_meaning: Lakshman vows to crush Bharat, his army, and anyone who helps them, even Shiva himself. His anger is total, and he swears by Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::3107.simple_insight: Rage narrows the mind until even sacred restraint disappears.
ramacharitamanas::3107.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Lakshman has heard Bharat's camp and his own humiliation as a challenge. Standing before the assembled crowd, he answers with a furious vow: he will not spare Bharat, his troops, or even Shiva if he intervenes. The scene is escalating toward a clash.
ramacharitamanas::3107.modern_relevance: You hear a cutting insult in front of everyone and feel your chest tighten. In that instant, the mind wants total victory, not understanding.
ramacharitamanas::3107.insight: It shows how anger turns a conflict into a vow of destruction, leaving no room for restraint.

ramacharitamanas::3108.verse_sanskrit: अति सरोष माखे लखनु लखि सुनि सपथ प्रवान। सभय लोक सब लोकपति चाहत भभरि भगान ॥
ramacharitamanas::3108.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी को अत्यंत क्रोध से तमतमाया हुआ देखकर और उनकी प्रामाणिक (सत्य) सौगंध सुनकर सब लोग भयभीत हो जाते हैं और लोकपाल घबड़ाकर भागना चाहते हैं॥230।
ramacharitamanas::3108.english_translation: Seeing Lakshman blazing with fierce anger and hearing his true oath, everyone grows afraid; even the guardians of the world want to flee in panic.
ramacharitamanas::3108.translation_literal: अति (very) / सरोष (angry) / माखे (blazing) / लखनु (Lakshman) / लखि (seeing) / सुनि (hearing) / सपथ (oath) / प्रवान (true, proven) / सभय (fearful) / लोक (people, beings) / सब (all) / लोकपति (guardians of the world) / चाहत (wanting) / भभरि (in panic) / भगान (to flee)
ramacharitamanas::3108.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3108.essence: Fierce anger can make the whole world flinch.
ramacharitamanas::3108.simple_meaning: Lakshman’s fierce anger and solemn vow terrify everyone around him, even the world’s guardians.
ramacharitamanas::3108.simple_insight: Raw force can freeze a room before a single blow lands.
ramacharitamanas::3108.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the scene has turned volatile: Lakshman is seething, and his oath lands like a thunderclap. The crowd and even the guardians of the world recoil, setting up the next outburst of cosmic praise.
ramacharitamanas::3108.modern_relevance: A heated argument in a packed room can change the air instantly. One person’s certainty, when it turns sharp and absolute, makes everyone else step back.
ramacharitamanas::3108.insight: It shows how uncontained anger radiates outward and makes even powerful beings lose composure.

ramacharitamanas::3109.verse_sanskrit: जगु भय मगन गगन भइ बानी। लखन बाहुबलु बिपुल बखानी॥ तात प्रताप प्रभाउ तुम्हारा। को कहि सकइ को जाननिहारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3109.verse_hindi: सारा जगत् भय में डूब गया। तब लक्ष्मणजी के अपार बाहुबल की प्रशंसा करती हुई आकाशवाणी हुई- हे तात! तुम्हारे प्रताप और प्रभाव को कौन कह सकता है और कौन जान सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3109.english_translation: The whole world fell into fear. Then a voice from the sky praised Lakshman's immense strength: 'Father, who can speak of your glory, and who can truly know it?'
ramacharitamanas::3109.translation_literal: जगु (world) / भय (fear) / मगन (immersed) / गगन (sky) / भइ (became) / बानी (voice) / लखन (Lakshman) / बाहुबलु (arm-strength) / बिपुल (great) / बखानी (praised)॥ / तात (father) / प्रताप (glory) / प्रभाउ (power, influence) / तुम्हारा (your) / को (who) / कहि (say) / सकइ (can) / को (who) / जाननिहारा (knower) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3109.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3109.essence: True force is so great that even its measure disappears.
ramacharitamanas::3109.simple_meaning: The world is shaken with fear, and a heavenly voice praises Lakshman's great strength and says his glory cannot be fully known.
ramacharitamanas::3109.simple_insight: Sometimes real strength is recognized only when fear has already spread.
ramacharitamanas::3109.detailed_meaning: As Lakshman stands ready in the tense Ayodhyakand confrontation, fear spreads through everyone present. Then an unseen voice from the sky praises his strength and says his power cannot be measured. The verse heightens the pressure before the next warning about acting wisely.
ramacharitamanas::3109.modern_relevance: A room goes silent after the one person who can stop the chaos finally speaks. Everyone feels the force in the moment before they can even explain it.
ramacharitamanas::3109.insight: It frames Lakshman's power as undeniable, setting up the need for careful judgment in action.

ramacharitamanas::3110.verse_sanskrit: अनुचित उचित काजु किछु होऊ। समुझि करिअ भल कह सबु कोऊ। सहसा करि पाछे पछिताहीं। कहहिं बेद बुध ते बुध नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3110.verse_hindi: परन्तु कोई भी काम हो, उसे अनुचित-उचित खूब समझ-बूझकर किया जाए तो सब कोई अच्छा कहते हैं। वेद और विद्वान कहते हैं कि जो बिना विचारे जल्दी में किसी काम को करके पीछे पछताते हैं, वे बुद्धिमान् नहीं हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3110.english_translation: Whatever task it may be, consider carefully whether it is right or wrong. Everyone praises a deed done with understanding. The Vedas and the wise say that those who act in haste and later regret it are not truly wise.
ramacharitamanas::3110.translation_literal: अनुचित (improper) / उचित (proper) / काजु (task) / किछु (anything) / होऊ (may be) / समुझि (understanding) / करिअ (do) / भल (good) / कह (say) / सबु (all) / कोऊ (anyone) / सहसा (hastily) / करि (doing) / पाछे (later) / पछिताहीं (regret) / कहहिं (say) / बेद (Vedas) / बुध (wise) / ते (those) / बुध (wise person) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::3110.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3110.essence: Wise action begins with a pause, not a rush.
ramacharitamanas::3110.simple_meaning: Before doing anything, judge carefully whether it is right. People praise thoughtful action, while rushed action often ends in regret.
ramacharitamanas::3110.simple_insight: You save yourself pain when you stop and look before acting.
ramacharitamanas::3110.detailed_meaning: Laxman’s anger has shaken the gathering, and a divine voice has just praised his strength. In that charged moment, the poem pulls back from rage and says: whatever you do, first understand it well, because haste leads to regret.
ramacharitamanas::3110.modern_relevance: You are one text away from sending the angry message, and your thumb is already hovering. This verse asks for one breath before the damage is done.
ramacharitamanas::3110.insight: It teaches you to interrupt impulse and check the consequences before acting.

ramacharitamanas::3111.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुर बचन लखन सकुचाने। राम सीयँ सादर सनमाने॥ कही तात तुम्ह नीति सुहाई। सब तें कठिन राजमदु भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3111.verse_hindi: देववाणी सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी सकुचा गए। श्री रामचंद्रजी और सीताजी ने उनका आदर के साथ सम्मान किया (और कहा-) हे तात! तुमने बड़ी सुंदर नीति कही। हे भाई! राज्य का मद सबसे कठिन मद है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3111.english_translation: Hearing the divine words, Lakshman felt shy. Ram and Sita honored him respectfully. Then Ram said, "Brother, your counsel is excellent. Of all intoxications, the intoxication of power is the hardest to bear."
ramacharitamanas::3111.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुर बचन (divine words) / लखन (Lakshman) / सकुचाने (felt shy) / राम (Ram) / सीयँ (Sita) / सादर (respectfully) / सनमाने (honored) / कही (said) / तात (brother) / तुम्ह (your) / नीति (counsel) / सुहाई (excellent) / सब तें (of all) / कठिन (hardest) / राजमदु (power-intoxication) / भाई (brother)
ramacharitamanas::3111.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3111.essence: Power is the most dangerous form of intoxication.
ramacharitamanas::3111.simple_meaning: Lakshman speaks wisely, and Ram agrees that power is the most dangerous kind of pride because it can quietly intoxicate a ruler.
ramacharitamanas::3111.simple_insight: It warns you to watch success closely, because influence can distort judgment faster than failure does.
ramacharitamanas::3111.detailed_meaning: After a divine voice praises Lakshman, he grows modest. Ram and Sita honor him, then Ram praises his counsel: the real danger for a king is not defeat, but the pride that comes with authority.
ramacharitamanas::3111.modern_relevance: You get promoted, people start agreeing with you, and soon every decision feels obviously right. Ram points to the hidden danger: status can make even good judgment wobble.
ramacharitamanas::3111.insight: It shifts attention from external power to the inner discipline needed to hold it cleanly.

ramacharitamanas::3112.verse_sanskrit: जो अचवँत नृप मातहिं तेई। नाहिन साधुसभा जेहिं सेई॥ सुनहू लखन भल भरत सरीसा। बिधि प्रपंच महँ सुना न दीसा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3112.verse_hindi: जिन्होंने साधुओं की सभा का सेवन (सत्संग) नहीं किया, वे ही राजा राजमद रूपी मदिरा का आचमन करते ही (पीते ही) मतवाले हो जाते हैं। हे लक्ष्मण! सुनो, भरत सरीखा उत्तम पुरुष ब्रह्मा की सृष्टि में न तो कहीं सुना गया है, न देखा ही गया है ॥
