ramacharitamanas::3112.english_translation: Those who have not kept company with the good become drunk with royal pride at the first taste of power. Listen, Lakshman: Bharat is so excellent that his like has neither been heard of nor seen in the created world.
ramacharitamanas::3112.translation_literal: जो (those who) / अचवँत (not having kept company) / नृप (kingly) / मातहिं (with the intoxication) / तेई (they only) / नाहिन (not) / साधुसभा (company of the good) / जेहिं (who) / सेई (served) ॥ / सुनहू (listen) / लखन (Lakshman) / भल (good) / भरत (Bharat) / सरीसा (like) / बिधि (created world) / प्रपंच (world) / महँ (in) / सुना (heard) / न (not) / दीसा (seen) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3112.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3112.essence: Power intoxicates the untrained; Bharat proves nobility can stay untouched.
ramacharitamanas::3112.simple_meaning: People who avoid the company of the good become intoxicated by power, but Bharat is held up as unmatched in virtue.
ramacharitamanas::3112.simple_insight: Real strength stays humble. The right company protects you from becoming inflated by success.
ramacharitamanas::3112.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the conversation turns from royal duty to Bharat's character. Tulsidas tells Lakshman that people without satsang get drunk on power, but Bharat is so pure that no one in the world matches him.
ramacharitamanas::3112.modern_relevance: You get promoted, and suddenly everyone laughs a little louder around you. The verse warns that status can distort you unless your circle keeps you honest.
ramacharitamanas::3112.insight: It shifts attention from status to the moral discipline that keeps status from corrupting you.

ramacharitamanas::3113.verse_sanskrit: भरतहि होइ न राजमदु बिधि हरि हर पद पाइ। कबहुँ कि काँजी सीकरनि छीरसिंधु बिनसाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3113.verse_hindi: (अयोध्या के राज्य की तो बात ही क्या है) ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और महादेव का पद पाकर भी भरत को राज्य का मद नहीं होने का! क्या कभी काँजी की बूँदों से क्षीरसमुद्र नष्ट हो सकता (फट सकता) है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3113.english_translation: Bharat would not become proud of kingship even if he attained the positions of Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh. Can a drop of sour whey ever spoil the ocean of milk?
ramacharitamanas::3113.translation_literal: भरतहि (for Bharat) / होइ (would become) / न (not) / राजमदु (pride of kingship) / बिधि (Brahma) / हरि (Vishnu) / हर (Shiva) / पद (position/feet) / पाइ (having attained) / कबहुँ (ever) / कि (whether) / काँजी (sour whey) / सीकरनि (drop) / छीरसिंधु (ocean of milk) / बिनसाइ (destroy/spoil)
ramacharitamanas::3113.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3113.essence: Greatness cannot inflate a heart already filled with devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3113.simple_meaning: Bharat is so humble that even the highest power would not make him arrogant. His character is too vast to be spoiled by status.
ramacharitamanas::3113.simple_insight: Real humility stays steady even when life offers everything.
ramacharitamanas::3113.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the narrator pauses to praise Bharat after the pain of exile and the collapse of royal pride around him. Bharat’s devotion to Ram is so complete that even the greatest status would not inflate his ego.
ramacharitamanas::3113.modern_relevance: You get promoted, praised, and suddenly everyone is calling you important. Bharat’s example says the real test is whether success changes your heart at all.
ramacharitamanas::3113.insight: It shifts attention from status itself to the inner steadiness that status can either expose or fail to disturb.

ramacharitamanas::3114.verse_sanskrit: तिमिरु तरुन तरनिहि मकु गिलई। गगनु मगन मकु मेघहिं मिलई॥ गोपद जल बूड़हिं घटजोनी। सहज छमा बरु छाड़ै छोनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3114.verse_hindi: अन्धकार चाहे तरुण (मध्याह्न के) सूर्य को निगल जाए। आकाश चाहे बादलों में समाकर मिल जाए। गो के खुर इतने जल में अगस्त्यजी डूब जाएँ और पृथ्वी चाहे अपनी स्वाभाविक क्षमा (सहनशीलता) को छोड़ दे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3114.english_translation: Darkness may swallow the midday sun. The sky may merge into the clouds. Water in a cow's hoofprint may drown Agastya, and the earth may abandon its natural patience.
ramacharitamanas::3114.translation_literal: तिमिरु (darkness) / तरुन (young, midday) / तरनिहि (sun) / मकु (may) / गिलई (swallow) । गगनु (sky) / मगनु (merged) / मकु (may) / मेघहिं (in clouds) / मिलई (merge) । गोपद (cow's hoofprint) / जल (water) / बूड़हिं (drown) / घटजोनी (Agastya) । सहज (natural) / छमा (patience, forbearance) / बरु (rather) / छाड़ै (leave) / छोनी (earth)
ramacharitamanas::3114.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3114.essence: Status cannot corrupt a heart already free of craving.
ramacharitamanas::3114.simple_meaning: The poet says impossible things may happen first: darkness may swallow the sun, the sky may vanish into clouds, and even the earth may lose its patience. But Bharat will still not be proud of power.
ramacharitamanas::3114.simple_insight: Real humility is stronger than any position can make you.
ramacharitamanas::3114.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's refusal of the throne is being defended with wild impossibilities. Tulsidas says the cosmos would have to break its own rules before Bharat could become intoxicated by kingship. The point is his complete non-attachment.
ramacharitamanas::3114.modern_relevance: You get handed a promotion that could change how everyone sees you. Even then, the part of you shaped by service can stay untouched by status.
ramacharitamanas::3114.insight: It teaches you to see Bharat's character as proof that power does not have to corrupt the heart.

ramacharitamanas::3115.verse_sanskrit: मसक फूँक मकु मेरु उड़ाई। होइ न नृपमदु भरतहि भाई॥ लखन तुम्हार सपथ पितु आना। सुचि सुबंधु नहिं भरत समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3115.verse_hindi: मच्छर की फूँक से चाहे सुमेरु उड़ जाए, परन्तु हे भाई! भरत को राजमद कभी नहीं हो सकता। हे लक्ष्मण! मैं तुम्हारी शपथ और पिताजी की सौगंध खाकर कहता हूँ, भरत के समान पवित्र और उत्तम भाई संसार में नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3115.english_translation: Even if Mount Meru were blown away by a mosquito's breath, Bharat would never feel royal pride, brother. Lakshman, I swear by you and by my father's vow: there is no brother in the world as pure and noble as Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::3115.translation_literal: मसक (mosquito) / फूँक (breath) / मकु (even if) / मेरु (Mount Meru) / उड़ाई (blown away) / होइ न (does not happen) / नृपमदु (royal pride) / भरतहि (to Bharat) / भाई (brother) / लखन (Lakshman) / तुम्हार (your) / सपथ (oath) / पितु (father) / आना (vow) / सुचि (pure) / सुबंधु (good brother) / नहिं (not) / भरत समाना (equal to Bharat)
ramacharitamanas::3115.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3115.essence: Power cannot corrupt a heart that has no pride.
ramacharitamanas::3115.simple_meaning: Bharat is so pure and humble that even the greatest power would not make him arrogant. Ram also declares him the noblest brother of all.
ramacharitamanas::3115.simple_insight: Real strength does not inflate the ego; it makes humility possible.
ramacharitamanas::3115.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is speaking to Lakshman about Bharat after the pain of exile has torn the family apart. He defends Bharat's character with an oath, saying that even impossible events would not make Bharat proud. The moment deepens Bharat's moral greatness.
ramacharitamanas::3115.modern_relevance: Someone gets promoted and suddenly talks differently, but one person in the circle stays exactly the same — steady, modest, impossible to corrupt. That is the kind of character Ram is praising here.
ramacharitamanas::3115.insight: It shifts admiration away from status and toward character that stays clean under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::3116.verse_sanskrit: सगुनु खीरु अवगुन जलु ताता। मिलइ रचइ परपंचु बिधाता॥ भरतु हंस रबिबंस तड़ागा। जनमि कीन्ह गुन दोष बिभागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3116.verse_hindi: हे तात! गुरु रूपी दूध और अवगुण रूपी जल को मिलाकर विधाता इस दृश्य प्रपंच (जगत् ) को रचता है, परन्तु भरत ने सूर्यवंश रूपी तालाब में हंस रूप जन्म लेकर गुण और दोष का विभाग कर दिया (दोनों को अलग-अलग कर दिया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3116.english_translation: O dear one, the Creator mixes the milk of virtues with the water of faults to make this visible world. Bharat was born like a swan in the lake of the solar dynasty, separating virtue from defect.
ramacharitamanas::3116.translation_literal: सगुनु (virtue-filled / with qualities) / खीरु (milk) / अवगुन (faults / defects) / जलु (water) / ताता (dear one) / मिलइ (mixes) / रचइ (creates) / परपंचु (the visible world / worldly appearance) / बिधाता (the Creator) ॥ भरतु (Bharat) / हंस (swan) / रबिबंस (solar dynasty) / तड़ागा (lake) / जनमि (having been born) / कीन्हि (made) / गुन (virtues) / दोष (faults) / बिभागा (separation / division) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3116.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3116.essence: Real nobility separates what is worth keeping from what is not.
ramacharitamanas::3116.simple_meaning: The world is a mixture of good and bad, but Bharat is like a swan that knows how to separate them. He does not get confused by appearances.
ramacharitamanas::3116.simple_insight: You can stay clear inside even when life is messy outside.
ramacharitamanas::3116.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's character is being praised after Ram's exile has shattered the royal family. Tulsidas compares the Creator's mixed world to a lake and Bharat to a swan who can separate milk from water, showing his rare clarity and moral discernment.
ramacharitamanas::3116.modern_relevance: A group chat is full of half-truths, gossip, and panic, but you don't have to absorb all of it. Like Bharat, you can keep your judgment clean and choose what deserves your trust.
ramacharitamanas::3116.insight: It trains the mind to discern value without being seduced by confusion.

ramacharitamanas::3117.verse_sanskrit: गहि गुन पय तजि अवगुण बारी। निज जस जगत कीन्हि उजिआरी॥ कहत भरत गुन सीलु सुभाऊ। पेम पयोधि मगन रघुराऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3117.verse_hindi: गुणरूपी दूध को ग्रहण कर और अवगुण रूपी जल को त्यागकर भरत ने अपने यश से जगत् में उजियाला कर दिया है। भरतजी के गुण, शील और स्वभाव को कहते-कहते श्री रघुनाथजी प्रेमसमुद्र में मग्न हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3117.english_translation: Accepting the milk of virtue and discarding the water of fault, Bharat has brightened the world with his own fame. As he spoke of Bharat's character, conduct, and nature, Raghunath himself became immersed in the ocean of love.
ramacharitamanas::3117.translation_literal: गहि (grasping) / गुन (virtue) / पय (milk) / तजि (leaving) / अवगुण (fault) / बारी (water) / निज (own) / जस (fame) / जगत (world) / कीन्हि (made) / उजिआरी (bright)॥ / कहत (speaking) / भरत (Bharat) / गुन (qualities) / सीलु (character) / सुभाऊ (nature) / पेम (love) / पयोधि (ocean) / मगन (immersed) / रघुराऊ (Raghunath)॥
ramacharitamanas::3117.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3117.essence: Virtue shines so clearly that even Ram is swept into love.
ramacharitamanas::3117.simple_meaning: Bharat's virtues are being praised as the light that reveals his true greatness. Hearing that praise, Ram becomes lost in love for him.
ramacharitamanas::3117.simple_insight: Real goodness doesn't need self-promotion; it naturally draws love and respect.
ramacharitamanas::3117.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court's grief over exile has turned into a deeper recognition of Bharat's character. The narrator says people should keep his virtues and set aside his flaws, because even Ram is moved into love when Bharat is described.
ramacharitamanas::3117.modern_relevance: A room full of people is talking about someone who never tries to defend himself. The more honestly his character is named, the more respect he earns without asking for it.
ramacharitamanas::3117.insight: It shifts attention from judging a person by flaws to seeing the light their character gives others.

ramacharitamanas::3118.verse_sanskrit: सुनि रघुबर बानी बिबुध देखि भरत पर हेतु। सकल सराहत राम सो प्रभु को कृपानिकेतु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3118.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी की वाणी सुनकर और भरतजी पर उनका प्रेम देखकर समस्त देवता उनकी सराहना करने लगे (और कहने लगे) कि श्री रामचंद्रजी के समान कृपा के धाम प्रभु और कौन है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3118.english_translation: Hearing Ram's words and seeing His love for Bharat, all the radiant beings praised Him, saying: who is a lord more filled with grace than Ram?
ramacharitamanas::3118.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / रघुबर (Ram) / बानी (words) / बिबुध (radiant beings) / देखि (seeing) / भरत (Bharat) / पर (toward) / हेतु (love/care) / सकल (all) / सराहत (praising) / राम (Ram) / सो (such) / प्रभु (lord) / को (who) / कृपानिकेतु (abode of grace)
ramacharitamanas::3118.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3118.essence: True lordship is revealed by compassion, not command.
ramacharitamanas::3118.simple_meaning: Ram's gentle words and his affection for Bharat make the radiant beings praise him as the very home of compassion.
ramacharitamanas::3118.simple_insight: Real greatness is not loud power; it is the tenderness that others can feel.
ramacharitamanas::3118.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's devotion has already moved the scene, and Ram responds with loving words. Seeing this, the radiant beings praise Ram, recognizing that his greatness is not rule or force but compassion itself.
ramacharitamanas::3118.modern_relevance: You defend someone who has been misunderstood, even when it costs you status. People notice less than you expect, but the ones who see clearly know what grace looks like.
ramacharitamanas::3118.insight: It shifts admiration from achievement to the quality of your care for others.

ramacharitamanas::3119.verse_sanskrit: जौं न होत जग जनम भरत को। सकल धरम धुर धरनि धरत को॥ कबि कुल अगम भरत गुन गाथा। को जानइ तुम्ह बिनु रघुनाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3119.verse_hindi: यदि जगत् में भरत का जन्म न होता, तो पृथ्वी पर संपूर्ण धर्मों की धुरी को कौन धारण करता? हे रघुनाथजी! कविकुल के लिए अगम (उनकी कल्पना से अतीत) भरतजी के गुणों की कथा आपके सिवा और कौन जान सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3119.english_translation: If Bharat had not been born in the world, who would have carried the pole of all dharma on earth? O Raghunath, who besides you can truly know the immeasurable story of Bharat's virtues?
ramacharitamanas::3119.translation_literal: जौं (if) / न (not) / होत (had been) / जग (world) / जनम (birth) / भरत को (of Bharat) / सकल (all) / धरम (dharma) / धुर (pole, burden) / धरनि (earth) / धरत को (of carrying)॥ / कबि (poet) / कुल (lineage, group) / अगम (beyond reach) / भरत (Bharat) / गुन (virtues) / गाथा (story, song) / को (who) / जानइ (knows) / तुम्ह (you) / बिनु (without) / रघुनाथा (O Raghunath) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3119.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3119.essence: Bharat's hidden virtue is so deep only Ram can measure it.
ramacharitamanas::3119.simple_meaning: Bharat is praised as the one who upheld all righteous duty on earth, and his virtues are said to be beyond ordinary understanding.
ramacharitamanas::3119.simple_insight: Real greatness can be quiet, hidden, and still hold up the world.
ramacharitamanas::3119.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's refusal of power and his loyalty to Ram have already stunned everyone. Tulsidas now lifts that devotion higher: Bharat is the pillar holding dharma itself, and only Ram fully knows the depth of his virtues.
ramacharitamanas::3119.modern_relevance: When you quietly keep a promise no one else would notice, the work may look small from outside. But the people who truly matter know what it cost you.
ramacharitamanas::3119.insight: It shifts respect from public achievement to the unseen weight of steadfast character.

ramacharitamanas::3120.verse_sanskrit: लखन राम सियँ सुनि सुर बानी। अति सुखु लहेउ न जाइ बखानी॥ इहाँ भरतु सब सहित सहाए। मंदाकिनीं पुनीत नहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3120.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामचंद्रजी और सीताजी ने देवताओं की वाणी सुनकर अत्यंत सुख पाया, जो वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता। यहाँ भरतजी ने सारे समाज के साथ पवित्र मंदाकिनी में स्नान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3120.english_translation: Lakshman, Ram, and Sita heard the words of the radiant beings and felt a joy beyond description. Here Bharat, along with everyone present, bathed in the pure Mandakini.
ramacharitamanas::3120.translation_literal: लखन (Lakshman) / राम (Ram) / सियँ (Sita) / सुनि (hearing) / सुर बानी (the words of the radiant beings) / अति (very) / सुखु (joy) / लहेउ (received) / न जाइ (cannot be) / बखानी (described) / इहाँ (here) / भरतु (Bharat) / सब सहित (with everyone together) / सहाए (accompanied) / मंदाकिनीं (Mandakini river) / पुनीत (pure) / नहाए (bathed)
ramacharitamanas::3120.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3120.essence: Joy and purity arrive together when the heart is ready.
ramacharitamanas::3120.simple_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita felt indescribable joy on hearing the divine message. Bharat and everyone with him bathed in the holy Mandakini.
ramacharitamanas::3120.simple_insight: Some moments are too full for words; joy and reverence are felt first, then spoken about later.
ramacharitamanas::3120.detailed_meaning: At Chitrakoot, the scene softens after the deeper praise of Bharat. The divine message fills Ram, Lakshman, and Sita with joy, while Bharat and his companions purify themselves in the Mandakini. It is a moment of shared blessing before the next meeting unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::3120.modern_relevance: You get a message that changes everything, and for a second you just sit there smiling. Later you can explain it. First, you simply feel it.
ramacharitamanas::3120.insight: It shifts attention from explanation to direct experience, letting joy and reverence arrive before analysis.

ramacharitamanas::3121.verse_sanskrit: सरित समीप राखि सब लोगा। मागि मातु गुर सचिव नियोगा॥ चले भरतु जहँ सिय रघुराई। साथ निषादनाथु लघु भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3121.verse_hindi: फिर सबको नदी के समीप ठहराकर तथा माता, गुरु और मंत्री की आज्ञा माँगकर निषादराज और शत्रुघ्न को साथ लेकर भरतजी वहाँ चले जहाँ श्री सीताजी और श्री रघुनाथजी थे ॥।
ramacharitamanas::3121.english_translation: Then, leaving everyone by the riverbank and asking permission from his mother, his teacher, and his ministers, Bharat went with Nishadraj and Shatrughna to where Sita and Raghurai were.
ramacharitamanas::3121.translation_literal: सरित (river) / समीप (near) / राखि (having kept) / सब (all) / लोगा (people) / मागि (asking for) / मातु (mother) / गुर (teacher) / सचिव (ministers) / नियोगा (permission, command) / चले (went) / भरतु (Bharat) / जहँ (where) / सिय (Sita) / रघुराई (Raghurai, Ram) / साथ (with) / निषादनाथु (Nishadraj) / लघु (younger) / भाई (brother)
ramacharitamanas::3121.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3121.essence: Devotion does not erase duty; it deepens it.
ramacharitamanas::3121.simple_meaning: Bharat leaves the group safely by the river, seeks permission from his mother, teacher, and ministers, and then goes with Nishadraj and Shatrughna to Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3121.simple_insight: True devotion still moves with care, respect, and responsibility.
ramacharitamanas::3121.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is already burdened by grief and loyalty. Before going to meet Ram and Sita, he leaves the people by the riverbank and asks leave from his mother, guru, and ministers. Even in urgency, he does nothing carelessly.
ramacharitamanas::3121.modern_relevance: You want to rush into a hard conversation, but you still check in with the people who depend on you. Bharat shows that urgency can stay respectful.
ramacharitamanas::3121.insight: It teaches you to act with devotion without dropping your responsibilities to others.

ramacharitamanas::3122.verse_sanskrit: समुझि मातु करतब सकुचाहीं। करत कुतरक कोटि मन माहीं॥ रामु लखनु सिय सुनि मम नाऊँ। उठि जनि अनत जाहिं तजि ठाऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3122.verse_hindi: भरतजी अपनी माता कैकेयी की करनी को समझकर (याद करके) सकुचाते हैं और मन में करोड़ों (अनेकों) कुतर्क करते हैं (सोचते हैं) श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीताजी मेरा नाम सुनकर स्थान छोड़कर कहीं दूसरी जगह उठकर न चले जाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3122.english_translation: Thinking of his mother’s deed, Bharata feels shy and keeps turning over countless thoughts in his mind: “If Ram, Lakshman, and Sita hear my name, may they not rise and leave this place, abandoning it.”
ramacharitamanas::3122.translation_literal: समुझि (thinking of) / मातु (mother) / करतब (deed, conduct) / सकुचाहीं (feels shy) / करत (doing) / कुतरक (misgiving, crooked thought) / कोटि (crores, countless) / मन माहीं (in the mind) // रामु (Ram) / लखनु (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / सुनि (hearing) / मम नाऊँ (my name) / उठि (rising up) / जनि (may not) / अनत (elsewhere) / जाहिं (go) / तजि (leaving) / ठाऊँ (place)
ramacharitamanas::3122.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3122.essence: Shame makes even your own name feel like a burden.
ramacharitamanas::3122.simple_meaning: Bharat feels ashamed remembering Kaikeyi’s deed and worries that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita might leave if they hear his name.
ramacharitamanas::3122.simple_insight: Love can make you fear even your own name if it might cause pain.
ramacharitamanas::3122.detailed_meaning: Bharat has reached the riverbank after learning what has happened in Ayodhya. As he thinks of Kaikeyi’s action, shame and anxiety rise together. Even his own name feels dangerous if it might disturb Ram, Lakshman, and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3122.modern_relevance: You send a message after a family fight, then stare at the screen wondering whether your name will reopen the wound. Bharat knows that ache of being associated with pain.
ramacharitamanas::3122.insight: It shows how deep remorse makes a person watch the effect of their very presence on others.

ramacharitamanas::3123.verse_sanskrit: मातु मते महुँ मानि मोहि जो कछु करहिं सो थोर। अघ अवगुन छमि आदरहिं समुझि आपनी ओर ॥
ramacharitamanas::3123.verse_hindi: मुझे माता के मत में मानकर वे जो कुछ भी करें सो थोड़ा है, पर वे अपनी ओर समझकर (अपने विरद और संबंध को देखकर) मेरे पापों और अवगुणों को क्षमा करके मेरा आदर ही करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3123.english_translation: Considering my mother's counsel, whatever they do is little; they will forgive my faults and honor me, seeing me as their own.
ramacharitamanas::3123.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / मते महुँ (in the counsel) / मानि (considering) / मोहि (me) / जो कछु (whatever) / करहिं (they do) / सो (that) / थोर (little) / अघ (faults) / अवगुन (failings) / छमि (forgiving) / आदरहिं (they honor) / समुझि (understanding) / आपनी ओर (their own side / as their own)
ramacharitamanas::3123.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3123.essence: Love can be stronger than the faults it sees.
ramacharitamanas::3123.simple_meaning: Bharat trusts that his family will judge him with compassion, not harshness. Even if they see his faults, they will still honor him as one of their own.
ramacharitamanas::3123.simple_insight: There is relief in being seen by people who know your flaws and still keep you close.
ramacharitamanas::3123.detailed_meaning: Bharat is on the road after learning of Ram’s exile and his mother Kaikeyi’s role in it. He is ashamed, but he still believes his family will understand him through love and kinship, not accusation. That hope steadies him.
ramacharitamanas::3123.modern_relevance: You send the message after the awkward family fight, expecting blame. Instead, the person who knows your worst habits still answers with warmth. That kind of mercy changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::3123.insight: It shifts you from expecting judgment to trusting relationship can hold imperfection.

ramacharitamanas::3124.verse_sanskrit: जौं परिहरहिं मलिन मनु जानी। जौं सनमानहिं सेवकु मानी॥ मोरें सरन रामहि की पनही। राम सुस्वामि दोसु सब जनही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3124.verse_hindi: चाहे मलिन मन जानकर मुझे त्याग दें, चाहे अपना सेवक मानकर मेरा सम्मान करें, (कुछ भी करें), मेरे तो श्री रामचंद्रजी की जूतियाँ ही शरण हैं। श्री रामचंद्रजी तो अच्छे स्वामी हैं, दोष तो सब दास का ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3124.english_translation: Even if they cast me off as impure, even if they honor me as a servant, my refuge is only Ram's sandals. Ram is a good master; the fault is all the servant's.
ramacharitamanas::3124.translation_literal: जौं (if) / परिहरहिं (they cast aside) / मलिन (impure) / मनु (mind) / जानी (knowing) / जौं (if) / सनमानहिं (they honor) / सेवकु (servant) / मानी (considering) / मोरें (for me) / सरन (refuge) / रामहि (of Ram) / की (only) / पनही (sandals) / राम (Ram) / सुस्वामि (good master) / दोसु (fault) / सब (all) / जनही (of the servant)
ramacharitamanas::3124.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3124.essence: Your worth does not depend on praise when your refuge is Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3124.simple_meaning: Bharat says people may judge him any way they want, but he belongs to Ram alone. He places all fault on himself and all refuge in Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3124.simple_insight: Peace comes from stopping your need to defend yourself and resting in a higher shelter.
ramacharitamanas::3124.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands in Ayodhya, torn between his mother’s actions and his love for Ram. He refuses to make his honor depend on anyone’s opinion. Whether others blame or praise him, he bows only to Ram’s feet.
ramacharitamanas::3124.modern_relevance: A family group chat is tearing your name apart, and you can feel the urge to explain yourself. This verse says your center does not have to move with their verdict.
ramacharitamanas::3124.insight: It shifts you from self-defense to surrender, letting Ram be the only court that matters.

ramacharitamanas::3125.verse_sanskrit: जग जग भाजन चातक मीना। नेम पेम निज निपुन नबीना॥ अस मन गुनत चले मग जाता। सकुच सनेहँ सिथिल सब गाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3125.verse_hindi: जगत् में यश के पात्र तो चातक और मछली ही हैं, जो अपने नेम और प्रेम को सदा नया बनाए रखने में निपुण हैं। ऐसा मन में सोचते हुए भरतजी मार्ग में चले जाते हैं। उनके सब अंग संकोच और प्रेम से शिथिल हो रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3125.english_translation: In the world, only the chatak bird and the fish are truly praiseworthy, because they keep their vow and love forever fresh. Thinking this in his heart, Bharat keeps walking along the road. All his limbs are softened by modesty and love.
ramacharitamanas::3125.translation_literal: जग (world) / जग (world) / भाजन (worthy recipient) / चातक (chatak bird) / मीना (fish) / नेम (vow) / पेम (love) / निज (own) / निपुन (skilled) / नबीना (ever-new) / अस (thus) / मन (mind) / गुनत (thinking) / चले (walked) / मग (path) / जाता (going) / सकुच (shyness) / सनेहँ (with love) / सिथिल (loosened) / सब (all) / गाता (limbs/body)
ramacharitamanas::3125.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3125.essence: True devotion stays fresh, even as the body grows tender.
ramacharitamanas::3125.simple_meaning: Bharat thinks of the chatak bird and the fish as examples of pure, steady love, then keeps walking with his body weakened by humility and affection.
ramacharitamanas::3125.simple_insight: Love can make you tender without making you weak.
ramacharitamanas::3125.detailed_meaning: Bharat is walking away from the throne and toward Ram with complete humility. As he moves, he reflects on creatures that stay true to their nature without wavering. That thought deepens his devotion and softens his whole body.
ramacharitamanas::3125.modern_relevance: You keep walking to someone you love after a hard conversation, replaying what they mean to you. The body grows heavy, but the heart stays loyal.
ramacharitamanas::3125.insight: It shifts devotion from a feeling into a steady, embodied way of moving.

ramacharitamanas::3126.verse_sanskrit: फेरति मनहुँ मातु कृत खोरी। चलत भगति बल धीरज धोरी॥ जब समुझत रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। तब पथ परत उताइल पाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3126.verse_hindi: माता की हुई बुराई मानो उन्हें लौटाती है, पर धीरज की धुरी को धारण करने वाले भरतजी भक्ति के बल से चले जाते हैं। जब श्री रघुनाथजी के स्वभाव को समझते (स्मरण करते) हैं तब मार्ग में उनके पैर जल्दी-जल्दी पड़ने लगते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3126.english_translation: The insult to their mother seems to turn them back, but Bharat carries the weight of patience and moves on through devotion. When they remember Shri Raghunath's nature, their feet hurry along the road.
ramacharitamanas::3126.translation_literal: फेरति (turns back) / मनहुँ (as if) / मातु (mother) / कृत (done) / खोरी (wrong) / चलत (while moving) / भगति (devotion) / बल (strength) / धीरज (patience) / धोरी (bearer)॥ / जब (when) / समुझत (remembering / understanding) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / सुभाऊ (nature) / तब (then) / पथ (path) / परत (falling) / उताइल (quickened) / पाऊ (feet) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3126.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3126.essence: Devotion can make even wounded feet hurry forward.
ramacharitamanas::3126.simple_meaning: Even when hurt makes you want to turn back, devotion and patience keep you walking forward. Remembering Ram's nature gives Bharat new strength and speeds his steps.
ramacharitamanas::3126.simple_insight: Love can turn pain into motion instead of paralysis.
ramacharitamanas::3126.detailed_meaning: Bharat is on the road in exile's shadow, carrying grief for his mother's wrong and his love for Ram at the same time. The verse shows a strange reversal: hurt could stop him, but devotion to Ram keeps his feet moving.
ramacharitamanas::3126.modern_relevance: You get a message that reopens an old family wound, and for a moment you want to shut down. Then you remember the person you are trying to remain loyal to, and you keep going anyway.
ramacharitamanas::3126.insight: It shifts the mind from injury-driven withdrawal to devotion-driven perseverance.

ramacharitamanas::3127.verse_sanskrit: भरत दसा तेहि अवसर कैसी। जल प्रबाहँ जल अलि गति जैसी॥ देखि भरत कर सोचु सनेहू। भा निषाद तेहि समयँ बिदेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3127.verse_hindi: उस समय भरत की दशा कैसी है? जैसी जल के प्रवाह में जल के भौंरे की गति होती है। भरतजी का सोच और प्रेम देखकर उस समय निषाद विदेह हो गया (देह की सुध-बुध भूल गया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3127.english_translation: What was Bharat's state at that moment? Like the movement of a water beetle in flowing water. Seeing Bharat's sorrow and love, Nishad became lost to his body.
ramacharitamanas::3127.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / दसा (state) / तेहि (that) / अवसर (moment) / कैसी (how) / जल (water) / प्रबाहँ (in flow) / जल (water) / अलि (water beetle) / गति (movement) / जैसी (like) / देखि (seeing) / भरत (Bharat) / कर (of) / सोचु (sorrow) / सनेहू (love) / भा (became) / निषाद (Nishad) / तेहि (that) / समयँ (at time) / बिदेहू (bodyless, lost in feeling)
ramacharitamanas::3127.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3127.essence: Love so pure can make even a witness forget himself.
ramacharitamanas::3127.simple_meaning: Bharat's grief and love are so intense that even Nishad loses all sense of his body while watching him.
ramacharitamanas::3127.simple_insight: Deep feeling can be so powerful that it pulls everyone nearby into silence and awe.
ramacharitamanas::3127.detailed_meaning: On the road to meet Ram, Bharat's sorrow and devotion are so overwhelming that the scene itself changes. Nishad watches him and is stunned into forgetfulness of his own body. The verse pauses the story to show how Bharat's love affects everyone around him.
ramacharitamanas::3127.modern_relevance: You watch someone arrive at a funeral carrying both grief and love, and the room goes quiet. Their sincerity is so complete that everyone feels it before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::3127.insight: It shifts attention from events to the force of devotion they awaken in others.

ramacharitamanas::3128.verse_sanskrit: लगे होन मंगल सगुन सुनि गुनि कहत निषादु। मिटिहि सोचु होइहि हरषु पुनि परिनाम बिषादु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3128.verse_hindi: मंगल शकुन होने लगे। उन्हें सुनकर और विचारकर निषाद कहने लगा- सोच मिटेगा, हर्ष होगा, पर फिर अन्त में दुःख होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3128.english_translation: Good omens began to appear. Hearing and considering them, Nishad said, 'Sorrow will fade, joy will arise, but in the end grief will return.'
ramacharitamanas::3128.translation_literal: लगे (began) / होन (to happen) / मंगल (auspicious signs) / सगुन (omens) / सुनि (hearing) / गुनि (considering) / कहत (saying) / निषादु (Nishad) / मिटिहि (will fade) / सोचु (sorrow) / होइहि (will arise) / हरषु (joy) / पुनि (again) / परिनाम (at the end) / बिषादु (grief)
ramacharitamanas::3128.speaker: Nishad
ramacharitamanas::3128.essence: Hope can arrive first, while grief still waits behind it.
ramacharitamanas::3128.simple_meaning: Nishad notices good omens, but he can already feel the mixed fate ahead: relief now, joy later, sorrow again at the end.
ramacharitamanas::3128.simple_insight: Even hopeful moments can carry the ache of what may return.
ramacharitamanas::3128.detailed_meaning: As Bharat approaches Nishad's place in Ayodhya's exile journey, the air seems filled with auspicious signs. Nishad reads them carefully, but his heart stays uneasy: this meeting may ease sorrow and bring joy, yet it cannot end the deeper grief hanging over everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3128.modern_relevance: You finally get a hopeful message after days of dread, but you still know the hard part isn't over. Relief arrives first; the deeper wound may still remain.
ramacharitamanas::3128.insight: It teaches you to hold joy without pretending pain has vanished.

ramacharitamanas::3129.verse_sanskrit: सेवक बचन सत्य सब जाने। आश्रम निकट जाइ निअराने॥ भरत दीख बन सैल समाजू। मुदित छुधित जनु पाइ सुनाजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3129.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने सेवक (गुह) के सब वचन सत्य जाने और वे आश्रम के समीप जा पहुँचे। वहाँ के वन और पर्वतों के समूह को देखा तो भरतजी इतने आनंदित हुए मानो कोई भूखा अच्छा अन्न (भोजन) पा गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3129.english_translation: Bharat accepted the servant's words as true and came near the hermitage. Seeing the forest and the hills there, he was delighted like a hungry person who has found fine food.
ramacharitamanas::3129.translation_literal: सेवक (servant) / बचन (words) / सत्य (true) / सब (all) / जाने (accepted) / आश्रम (hermitage) / निकट (near) / जाइ (going) / निअराने (came close) / भरत (Bharat) / दीख (saw) / बन (forest) / सैल (hills) / समाजू (group) / मुदित (delighted) / छुधित (hungry) / जनु (as if) / पाइ (having found) / सुनाजू (fine food)
ramacharitamanas::3129.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3129.essence: Love makes even the approach feel like fulfillment.
ramacharitamanas::3129.simple_meaning: Bharat trusts the servant's words and moves closer to the hermitage. Seeing the forest and hills, he feels deep joy, like a hungry person finding a good meal.
ramacharitamanas::3129.simple_insight: Even the sight of the place where Ram is near fills Bharat with joy.
ramacharitamanas::3129.detailed_meaning: Bharat is approaching the forest hermitage with Guha's guidance. He believes Guha's words and, as the landscape comes into view, his heart lifts at once. The verse shows his eagerness and love before the meeting itself.
ramacharitamanas::3129.modern_relevance: You finally reach the quiet road outside a place you have long wanted to visit. Even the trees and the gate feel like relief, because your heart has already arrived.
ramacharitamanas::3129.insight: It shifts attention from the destination itself to the joy of nearing what you love.

ramacharitamanas::3130.verse_sanskrit: ईति भीति जनु प्रजा दुखारी। त्रिबिध ताप पीड़ित ग्रह मारी॥ जाइ सुराज सुदेस सुखारी। होहिं भरत गति तेहि अनुहारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3130.verse_hindi: जैसे ईति के भय से दुःखी हुई और तीनों (आध्यात्मिक, आधिदैविक और आधिभौतिक) तापों तथा क्रूर ग्रहों और महामारियों से पीड़ित प्रजा किसी उत्तम देश और उत्तम राज्य में जाकर सुखी हो जाए, भरतजी की गति (दशा) ठीक उसी प्रकार हो रही है ॥ (अधिक जल बरसना, न बरसना, चूहों का उत्पात, टिड्डियाँ, तोते और दूसरे राजा की चढ़ाई- खेतों में बाधा देने वाले इन छह उपद्रवों को 'ईति' कहते हैं)।
ramacharitamanas::3130.english_translation: Like a people made miserable by plague, the three kinds of suffering, cruel planets, and disasters becoming happy after reaching a good land and a good kingdom, Bharata is now in exactly that state.
ramacharitamanas::3130.translation_literal: ईति (plague/disaster) / भीति (fear) / जनु (as if) / प्रजा (people) / दुखारी (suffering) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / ताप (afflictions) / पीड़ित (stricken) / ग्रह (malefic planets) / मारी (disease/disaster) / जाइ (going) / सुराज (good rule) / सुदेस (good land) / सुखारी (happy) / होहिं (become) / भरत (Bharata) / गति (state) / तेहि (that) / अनुहारी (matching)
ramacharitamanas::3130.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3130.essence: Bharata's grief is like a people escaping disaster into safety.
ramacharitamanas::3130.simple_meaning: Bharata's condition is compared to a suffering people who finally reach a safe, prosperous kingdom and feel relief.
ramacharitamanas::3130.simple_insight: Grief can be so complete that even relief feels like a distant country.
ramacharitamanas::3130.detailed_meaning: Bharata has reached the forest and sees the life around Ram's exile. Tulsidas compares his condition to a people escaping plague and suffering by reaching a good kingdom: outwardly he is alive, but inwardly he is desperate for relief.
ramacharitamanas::3130.modern_relevance: You finally get home after days of bad news, missed calls, and a stomach that never unclenched. The relief is real, but it arrives after too much strain.
ramacharitamanas::3130.insight: It shifts the reader to feel Bharata's sorrow as a public disaster, not a private mood.

ramacharitamanas::3131.verse_sanskrit: राम बास बन संपति भ्राजा। सुखी प्रजा जनु पाइ सुराजा॥ सचिव बिरागु बिबेकु नरेसू। बिपिन सुहावन पावन देसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3131.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी के निवास से वन की सम्पत्ति ऐसी सुशोभित है मानो अच्छे राजा को पाकर प्रजा सुखी हो। सुहावना वन ही पवित्र देश है। विवेक उसका राजा है और वैराग्य मंत्री है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3131.english_translation: Ram's presence makes the forest shine like a prosperous kingdom. A lovely forest becomes a holy land, with discernment as king and non-attachment as minister.
ramacharitamanas::3131.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / बास (residence) / बन (forest) / संपति (wealth, prosperity) / भ्राजा (shines) / सुखी (happy) / प्रजा (subjects, people) / जनु (as if) / पाइ (having obtained) / सुराजा (good rule, good king)॥ / सचिव (minister) / बिरागु (non-attachment) / बिबेकु (discernment) / नरेसू (king) / बिपिन (forest) / सुहावन (beautiful) / पावन (purifying) / देसू (land, place) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3131.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3131.essence: Ram's presence turns exile into a kingdom of peace.
ramacharitamanas::3131.simple_meaning: Ram's presence transforms the forest into a place of peace and order. The real rulers there are discernment and non-attachment.
ramacharitamanas::3131.simple_insight: What looks barren can become sacred when your mind is governed well.
ramacharitamanas::3131.detailed_meaning: In the forest near Chitrakoot, Bharat sees that Ram's presence has changed everything. The wild place feels prosperous and protected, as if it were a well-governed kingdom. Tulsidas says the true rulers there are discernment and non-attachment.
ramacharitamanas::3131.modern_relevance: You walk into a cramped apartment after a hard week, and somehow it feels calm because one steady person is there. Presence changes a place more than furniture, money, or status ever can.
ramacharitamanas::3131.insight: It shifts attention from outer conditions to the quality of presence that shapes them.

ramacharitamanas::3132.verse_sanskrit: भट जम नियम सैल रजधानी। सांति सुमति सुचि सुंदर रानी॥ सकल अंग संपन्न सुराऊ। राम चरन आश्रित चित चाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3132.verse_hindi: यम (अहिंसा, सत्य, अस्तेय, ब्रह्मचर्य और अपरिग्रह) तथा नियम (शौच, संतोष, तप, स्वाध्याय और ईश्वर प्रणिधान) योद्धा हैं। पर्वत राजधानी है, शांति तथा सुबुद्धि दो सुंदर पवित्र रानियाँ हैं। वह श्रेष्ठ राजा राज्य के सब अंगों से पूर्ण है और श्री रामचंद्रजी के चरणों के आश्रित रहने से उसके चित्त में चाव (आनंद या उत्साह) है ॥ (स्वामी, आमत्य, सुहृद, कोष, राष्ट्र, दुर्ग और सेना- राज्य के सात अंग हैं।)
ramacharitamanas::3132.english_translation: The warriors are Yama and Niyama. The capital is a mountain. Peace and wise understanding are the two beautiful, pure queens. The king is complete in every part of a noble kingdom, and his mind delights in shelter at Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::3132.translation_literal: भट (warriors) / जम (Yama) / नियम (Niyama) / सैल (mountain) / रजधानी (capital) / सांति (peace) / सुमति (wise understanding) / सुचि (pure) / सुंदर (beautiful) / रानी (queen) / सकल (all) / अंग (parts) / संपन्न (complete) / सुराऊ (noble) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / आश्रित (taking refuge) / चित (mind) / चाऊ (delight)
ramacharitamanas::3132.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3132.essence: A disciplined inner kingdom begins when the mind rests in Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3132.simple_meaning: A well-ordered life has discipline, peace, and wise judgment. When the mind rests at Ram's feet, everything in that inner kingdom comes together.
ramacharitamanas::3132.simple_insight: You feel steadier when your habits, calm, and discernment work together instead of fighting each other.
ramacharitamanas::3132.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the poet turns exile into a picture of ideal rule. The real kingdom is not just land and power: it is a disciplined life where peace and wise understanding sit beside each other, and the mind finds joy in Ram's shelter.
ramacharitamanas::3132.modern_relevance: After a week of broken sleep, missed meals, and scattered focus, you finally clean your room, fix your routine, and notice your mind softening. Order outside begins to restore order inside.
ramacharitamanas::3132.insight: It shifts you from chasing control to building an inner structure that can actually hold calm.

ramacharitamanas::3133.verse_sanskrit: जीति मोह महिपालु दल सहित बिबेक भुआलु। करत अकंटक राजु पुरँ सुख संपदा सुकालु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3133.verse_hindi: मोह रूपी राजा को सेना सहित जीतकर विवेक रूपी राजा निष्कण्टक राज्य कर रहा है। उसके नगर में सुख, सम्पत्ति और सुकाल वर्तमान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3133.english_translation: Having conquered delusion, the discerning king now rules with his army. In his city, happiness, wealth, and good times flourish without obstruction.
ramacharitamanas::3133.translation_literal: जीति (having conquered) / मोह (delusion) / महिपालु (king) / दल सहित (together with the army) / बिबेक भुआलु (the king of discernment) / करत (doing) / अकंटक (without obstruction) / राजु (rule) / पुरँ (in the city) / सुख संपदा (happiness and wealth) / सुकालु (good times)
ramacharitamanas::3133.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3133.essence: Clear seeing takes power when delusion is defeated.
ramacharitamanas::3133.simple_meaning: When confusion is conquered, clear understanding governs life freely, and peace, prosperity, and good fortune follow.
ramacharitamanas::3133.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing your life can be led by clarity instead of inner confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3133.detailed_meaning: Bharat’s exile has turned Ayodhya into a moral landscape. Tulsidas says the real kingdom is not a throne but the mind: when delusion is defeated, discernment rules with no resistance, and life becomes orderly, fruitful, and calm.
ramacharitamanas::3133.modern_relevance: You finally stop replaying the same argument in your head at 2 a.m. Once confusion loses its grip, your home, work, and choices all feel less cramped.
ramacharitamanas::3133.insight: It shifts attention from mental fog to the quiet authority of discernment.

ramacharitamanas::3134.verse_sanskrit: बन प्रदेस मुनि बास घनेरे। जनु पुर नगर गाउँ गन खेरे॥ बिपुल बिचित्र बिहग मृग नाना। प्रजा समाजु न जाइ बखाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3134.verse_hindi: वन रूपी प्रांतों में जो मुनियों के बहुत से निवास स्थान हैं, वही मानो शहरों, नगरों, गाँवों और खेड़ों का समूह है। बहुत से विचित्र पक्षी और अनेकों पशु ही मानो प्रजाओं का समाज है, जिसका वर्णन नहीं किया जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3134.english_translation: The forest regions, where many sages live, are like a spread of cities, towns, villages, and hamlets. The many varied birds and countless animals are like a population beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::3134.translation_literal: बन (forest) / प्रदेस (regions) / मुनि (sages) / बास (dwelling) / घनेरे (many, abundant) / जनु (as if) / पुर (cities) / नगर (towns) / गाउँ (villages) / गन (groups) / खेरे (hamlets) / बिपुल (many) / बिचित्र (varied, wondrous) / बिहग (birds) / मृग (animals) / नाना (many kinds) / प्रजा (subjects, people) / समाजु (assembly, community) / न जाइ (cannot be) / बखाना (described)
ramacharitamanas::3134.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3134.essence: The forest becomes a kingdom when you learn to see its life.
ramacharitamanas::3134.simple_meaning: The forest is described like a living kingdom, full of sages, birds, and animals, as if it were a populated land.
ramacharitamanas::3134.simple_insight: Nature is not empty here; it is a whole world with its own order and life.
ramacharitamanas::3134.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the poem turns from exile into a vision of the forest as a thriving realm. Sages live there like citizens, and birds and animals fill it like a population. The verse sets up the harmony of life in Rama's wilderness.
ramacharitamanas::3134.modern_relevance: You step into a quiet park after a brutal week and notice it is not empty at all. Every tree, bird, and animal feels like part of a larger, breathing community.
ramacharitamanas::3134.insight: It shifts your attention from seeing wilderness as vacant to seeing it as a full, ordered world.

ramacharitamanas::3135.verse_sanskrit: खगहा करि हरि बाघ बराहा। देखि महिष बृष साजु सराहा॥ बयरु बिहाइ चरहिं एक संगा। जहँ तहँ मनहुँ सेन चतुरंगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3135.verse_hindi: गैंडा, हाथी, सिंह, बाघ, सूअर, भैंसे और बैलों को देखकर राजा के साज को सराहते ही बनता है। ये सब आपस का वैर छोड़कर जहाँ-तहाँ एक साथ विचरते हैं। यही मानो चतुरंगिणी सेना है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3135.english_translation: Seeing rhinoceroses, elephants, lions, tigers, boars, buffaloes, and bulls, even a king would praise the splendor. They have given up enmity and roam together everywhere, like a four-part army.
ramacharitamanas::3135.translation_literal: खगहा (rhinoceros) / करि (elephant) / हरि (lion) / बाघ (tiger) / बराहा (boar) / देखि (seeing) / महिष (buffalo) / बृष (bull) / साजु (splendor / arrangement) / सराहा (praised)॥ / बयरु (enmity) / बिहाइ (having left) / चरहिं (they roam) / एक संगा (together) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / मनहुँ (as if) / सेन (army) / चतुरंगा (four-part) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3135.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3135.essence: When enmity drops, even wildness looks like order.
ramacharitamanas::3135.simple_meaning: Wild animals are roaming together peacefully, as if they were one army. The scene is being used to describe the forest as orderly and full of life.
ramacharitamanas::3135.simple_insight: Harmony can make even wildness feel organized and alive.
ramacharitamanas::3135.detailed_meaning: The poem is still describing the forest after the kingdom of wisdom has been established in the earlier verse. Tulsidas lingers on the strange beauty of the woods: fierce animals no longer act like enemies but move together, making the forest seem like a disciplined army.
ramacharitamanas::3135.modern_relevance: You walk into a park where stray dogs, pigeons, and children all share the same path without tension. The scene feels almost arranged, as if nature itself had found its order.
ramacharitamanas::3135.insight: It shifts attention from conflict to the hidden order that can appear when hostility falls away.

ramacharitamanas::3136.verse_sanskrit: झरना झरहिं मत्त गज गाजहिं। मनहुँ निसान बिबिधि बिधि बाजहिं॥ चक चकोर चातक सुक पिक गन। कूजत मंजु मराल मुदित मन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3136.verse_hindi: पानी के झरने झर रहे हैं और मतवाले हाथी चिंघाड़ रहे हैं। मानो वहाँ अनेकों प्रकार के नगाड़े बज रहे हैं। चकवा, चकोर, पपीहा, तोता तथा कोयलों के समूह और सुंदर हंस प्रसन्न मन से कूज रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3136.english_translation: Waterfalls tumble down and wild elephants trumpet, as if many kinds of drums are sounding. Chakravaka, chakor, chatak, parrots, cuckoos, and graceful swans all call out joyfully.
ramacharitamanas::3136.translation_literal: झरना (waterfalls) / झरहिं (are flowing) / मत्त गज (intoxicated elephants) / गाजहिं (trumpet) / मनहुँ (as if) / निसान (drums) / बिबिधि बिधि (various kinds) / बाजहिं (are sounding) / चक चकोर चातक (chakravaka, chakor, and chatak birds) / सुक पिक गन (groups of parrots and cuckoos) / कूजत (calling) / मंजु (sweetly) / मराल (swans) / मुदित मन (with joyful minds)
ramacharitamanas::3136.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3136.essence: Nature itself is singing in celebration.
ramacharitamanas::3136.simple_meaning: The forest is so alive and beautiful that its sounds seem like music: waterfalls, elephants, and birds all create a joyful scene.
ramacharitamanas::3136.simple_insight: Beauty can feel so full that even noise becomes celebration.
ramacharitamanas::3136.detailed_meaning: The exile path has become a living forest kingdom. Tulsidas pauses the story to paint its sounds: water, elephants, and birds all seem to join in one natural festival. This is atmosphere, not instruction.
ramacharitamanas::3136.modern_relevance: You step off a crowded train into a rain-soaked park, and every sound feels brighter than usual. The world itself seems to be breathing with you.
ramacharitamanas::3136.insight: It shifts attention from plot to atmosphere, letting the reader feel the forest as a sacred, living place.

ramacharitamanas::3137.verse_sanskrit: अलिगन गावत नाचत मोरा। जनु सुराज मंगल चहु ओरा॥ बेलि बिटप तृन सफल सफूला। सब समाजु मुद मंगल मूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3137.verse_hindi: भौंरों के समूह गुंजार कर रहे हैं और मोर नाच रहे हैं। मानो उस अच्छे राज्य में चारों ओर मंगल हो रहा है। बेल, वृक्ष, तृण सब फल और फूलों से युक्त हैं। सारा समाज आनंद और मंगल का मूल बन रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3137.english_translation: Bees hum and peacocks dance, as if a noble reign has brought auspiciousness everywhere. Vines, trees, and grasses are full of fruit and flowers; the whole society becomes the source of joy and blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3137.translation_literal: अलिगन (bees) / गावत (singing) / नाचत (dancing) / मोरा (peacocks) । जनु (as if) / सुराज (good rule) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / चहु ओर (on all four sides) ॥ बेलि (vines) / बिटप (trees) / तृन (grass) / सफल (fruitful) / सफूला (flowering) । सब (all) / समाजु (society) / मुद (joy) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मूल (source) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3137.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3137.essence: Right order makes even nature look joyful and full.
ramacharitamanas::3137.simple_meaning: The landscape itself seems alive with joy, as if good rule has made everything flourish. Nature and society both look fruitful, harmonious, and blessed.
ramacharitamanas::3137.simple_insight: When order is right, even the world around you seems to breathe easier.
ramacharitamanas::3137.detailed_meaning: On the mountain path in Ayodhyakand, the scene turns lush and celebratory. Bees hum, peacocks dance, and every plant seems to bear fruit and flowers. It is part of the larger description of the beauty Bharat beholds, preparing his heart for the coming devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3137.modern_relevance: You walk into a neighborhood after the rain and notice children playing, shopkeepers smiling, and even the trees looking brighter. Sometimes a place feels cared for before anyone says a word.
ramacharitamanas::3137.insight: It shifts attention from private feeling to the atmosphere created by right order and harmony.

ramacharitamanas::3138.verse_sanskrit: राम सैल सोभा निरखि भरत हृदयँ अति पेमु। तापस तप फलु पाइ जिमि सुखी सिरानें नेमु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3138.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के पर्वत की शोभा देखकर भरतजी के हृदय में अत्यंत प्रेम हुआ। जैसे तपस्वी नियम की समाप्ति होने पर तपस्या का फल पाकर सुखी होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3138.english_translation: Seeing the beauty of Ram's mountain, Bharat felt deep love in his heart, like a ascetic who has gained the fruit of discipline and rests in joy when the vow is complete.
ramacharitamanas::3138.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सैल (mountain) / सोभा (beauty) / निरखि (seeing) / भरत (Bharat) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / अति (very) / पेमु (love) / तापस (ascetic) / तप (discipline) / फलु (fruit) / पाइ (having obtained) / जिमि (like) / सुखी (happy) / सिरानें (when ended) / नेमु (vow)
ramacharitamanas::3138.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3138.essence: Love can feel like the reward for years of waiting.
ramacharitamanas::3138.simple_meaning: Bharat sees the beauty of the mountain where Ram is staying, and his heart overflows with love. It feels like the joy of a seeker who finally receives the reward of long discipline.
ramacharitamanas::3138.simple_insight: Long devotion can feel like a reward in itself when the heart finally meets what it has been longing for.
ramacharitamanas::3138.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat has come near the place where Ram lives in exile. The mountain’s beauty awakens overwhelming love in him. Tulsidas compares that feeling to an ascetic finishing discipline and tasting the fruit of years of effort.
ramacharitamanas::3138.modern_relevance: You finally reach the place you have been aching to see — a childhood home, a pilgrimage site, a hospital room after long waiting — and your chest loosens before words can come.
ramacharitamanas::3138.insight: It turns longing into fulfilled devotion, showing that the heart can find joy even before the journey is complete.

ramacharitamanas::3139.verse_sanskrit: तब केवट ऊँचे चढ़ि धाई। कहेउ भरत सन भुजा उठाई॥ नाथ देखिअहिं बिटप बिसाला। पाकरि जंबु रसाल तमाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3139.verse_hindi: तब केवट दौड़कर ऊँचे चढ़ गया और भुजा उठाकर भरजी से कहने लगा- हे नाथ! ये जो पाकर, जामुन, आम और तमाल के विशाल वृक्ष दिखाई देते हैं, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3139.english_translation: Then the boatman climbed up quickly and, raising his arm, said to Bharat, "My lord, look at these great trees: pakar, jamun, mango, and tamal."
ramacharitamanas::3139.translation_literal: तब (then) / केवट (boatman) / ऊँचे (high) / चढ़ि (climbing) / धाई (ran quickly) / कहेउ (said) / भरत सन (to Bharat) / भुजा (arm) / उठाई (raised) / नाथ (lord) / देखिअहिं (look) / बिटप (trees) / बिसाला (great) / पाकरि (pakar tree) / जंबु (jamun tree) / रसाल (mango tree) / तमाला (tamal tree)
ramacharitamanas::3139.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3139.essence: The scene pauses to let the forest be seen.
ramacharitamanas::3139.simple_meaning: The boatman points out the names of the large trees around them. It is a scenic detail, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3139.simple_insight: Sometimes the story pauses just to let you see the world clearly.
ramacharitamanas::3139.detailed_meaning: Bharat is walking through the forest, and the boatman leans in, pointing excitedly at the tall trees around them. The verse simply paints the landscape before the deeper reflection on the banyan tree that follows.
ramacharitamanas::3139.modern_relevance: You slow down on a road trip and someone in the car starts naming the trees, as if the world itself deserves a second look.
ramacharitamanas::3139.insight: It shifts attention from plot to place, preparing the mind for the fuller image that comes next.

ramacharitamanas::3140.verse_sanskrit: जिन्ह तरुबरन्ह मध्य बटु सोहा। मंजु बिसाल देखि मनु मोहा॥ नील सघन पल्लव फल लाला। अबिरल छाहँ सुखद सब काला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3140.verse_hindi: जिन श्रेष्ठ वृक्षों के बीच में एक सुंदर विशाल बड़ का वृक्ष सुशोभित है, जिसको देखकर मन मोहित हो जाता है, उसके पत्ते नीले और सघन हैं और उसमें लाल फल लगे हैं। उसकी घनी छाया सब ऋतुओं में सुख देने वाली है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3140.english_translation: Among the finest trees stands a beautiful, विशाल banyan tree. Its sight captivates the mind. Its dense blue leaves and red fruit give cool shade in every season.
ramacharitamanas::3140.translation_literal: जिन्ह (among whom) / तरुबरन्ह (among the best trees) / मध्य (in the middle) / बटु (banyan tree) / सोहा (shone beautifully) । / मंजु (beautiful) / बिसाल (vast) / देखि (seeing) / मनु (mind) / मोहा (was enchanted) ॥ / नील (blue) / सघन (dense) / पल्लव (leaves) / फल (fruits) / लाला (red) । / अबिरल (continuous) / छाहँ (shade) / सुखद (pleasant) / सब (all) / काला (seasons) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3140.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3140.essence: The most beautiful thing here is also the most sheltering.
ramacharitamanas::3140.simple_meaning: A huge banyan tree stands out among the other trees, and its beauty draws the eye. Its thick shade stays pleasant through every season.
ramacharitamanas::3140.simple_insight: Beauty can be a shelter, not just something to admire.
ramacharitamanas::3140.detailed_meaning: Bharat is being shown the forest landscape near the river. Among the many trees, one huge banyan stands out with striking beauty and cool shade. The verse lingers on the scene, preparing for the place where Ram’s cottage will be found.
ramacharitamanas::3140.modern_relevance: You turn off a dusty road and spot one tree giving shade to everyone waiting nearby. It feels like relief before you even sit down.
ramacharitamanas::3140.insight: It trains attention to notice what quietly protects and comforts, not only what is impressive.

ramacharitamanas::3141.verse_sanskrit: मानहुँ तिमिर अरुनमय रासी। बिरची बिधि सँकेलि सुषमा सी॥ ए तरु सरित समीप गोसाँई। रघुबर परनकुटी जहँ छाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3141.verse_hindi: मानो ब्रह्माजी ने परम शोभा को एकत्र करके अंधकार और लालिमामयी राशि सी रच दी है। हे गुसाईं! ये वृक्ष नदी के समीप हैं, जहाँ श्री राम की पर्णकुटी छाई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3141.english_translation: It looks as if Brahma gathered all beauty together and shaped it into a mass of darkness and red glow. O master, these trees stand by the river, where Ram's leaf-hut rests.
ramacharitamanas::3141.translation_literal: मानहुँ (as if) / तिमिर (darkness) / अरुनमय (filled with red glow) / रासी (mass) / बिरची (created) / बिधि (Brahma) / सँकेलि (gathering together) / सुषमा (beauty) / सी (like) / ए (these) / तरु (trees) / सरित (river) / समीप (near) / गोसाँई (O master) / रघुबर (Ram) / परनकुटी (leaf-hut) / जहँ (where) / छाई (is spread)
ramacharitamanas::3141.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3141.essence: Beauty becomes unforgettable when it surrounds Ram's resting place.
ramacharitamanas::3141.simple_meaning: The forest is so beautiful that it feels like all beauty itself has been gathered into one place. The trees stand near the river where Ram's hut is built.
ramacharitamanas::3141.simple_insight: Beauty deepens when it surrounds a place of love and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3141.detailed_meaning: Kevat is guiding Bharat through the forest and pointing out the landscape near Ram's exile hut. The scene pauses on the riverbank trees, turning them into a vision of gathered beauty before the story moves on to the next detail.
ramacharitamanas::3141.modern_relevance: You arrive at a quiet riverside camp and suddenly notice how the whole place feels charged because someone you love once lived there.
ramacharitamanas::3141.insight: It trains the eye to see ordinary nature as sacred when it is touched by devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3142.verse_sanskrit: तुलसी तरुबर बिबिध सुहाए। कहुँ कहुँ सियँ कहुँ लखन लगाए॥ बट छायाँ बेदिका बनाई। सियँ निज पानि सरोज सुहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3142.verse_hindi: वहाँ तुलसीजी के बहुत से सुंदर वृक्ष सुशोभित हैं, जो कहीं-कहीं सीताजी ने और कहीं लक्ष्मणजी ने लगाए हैं। इसी बड़ की छाया में सीताजी ने अपने करकमलों से सुंदर वेदी बनाई है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3142.english_translation: There are many beautiful trees there, planted here and there by Sita and Lakshman. Beneath the banyan's shade, Sita herself has made a lovely altar with her own hands.
ramacharitamanas::3142.translation_literal: तुलसी (Tulsidas / there) / तरुबर (best trees) / बिबिध (various) / सुहाए (beautiful) / कहुँ कहुँ (here and there) / सियँ (by Sita) / कहुँ लखन (by Lakshman) / लगाए (planted) / बट (banyan tree) / छायाँ (shade) / बेदिका (altar/platform) / बनाई (made) / सियँ (Sita) / निज (own) / पानि (hands) / सरोज (lotus-like) / सुहाई (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::3142.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3142.essence: Love can turn exile into a home.
ramacharitamanas::3142.simple_meaning: Sita and Lakshman have made the forest dwelling beautiful and sacred. Sita has even built a small altar under the banyan tree with her own hands.
ramacharitamanas::3142.simple_insight: Even exile can become graceful when love and care shape the space around you.
ramacharitamanas::3142.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are living in the forest at Panchavati. The scene pauses to show their dwelling: trees planted by their own hands, and a small altar made by Sita under the banyan tree. It prepares the sacred, peaceful setting before the sages arrive.
ramacharitamanas::3142.modern_relevance: You move into a bare rented room and slowly make it feel like home — a plant by the window, a clean corner, a place to sit quietly. Care turns hardship into shelter.
ramacharitamanas::3142.insight: It shifts attention from loss to the quiet power of making sacred space through simple acts.

ramacharitamanas::3143.verse_sanskrit: जहाँ बैठि मुनिगन सहित नित सिय रामु सुजान। सुनहिं कथा इतिहास सब आगम निगम पुरान ॥
ramacharitamanas::3143.verse_hindi: जहाँ सुजान श्री सीता-रामजी मुनियों के वृन्द समेत बैठकर नित्य शास्त्र, वेद और पुराणों के सब कथा-इतिहास सुनते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3143.english_translation: Where wise Sita and Ram sit each day with the sages, listening to all the stories and histories of the scriptures, Vedas, and Puranas.
ramacharitamanas::3143.translation_literal: जहाँ (where) / बैठि (sitting) / मुनिगन सहित (together with sages) / नित (daily) / सिय रामु सुजान (wise Sita-Ram) / सुनहिं (listen) / कथा इतिहास (stories and histories) / सब (all) / आगम (scriptures) / निगम (Vedas) / पुरान (Puranas)
ramacharitamanas::3143.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3143.essence: Greatness can sit quietly and still receive wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::3143.simple_meaning: Sita and Ram spend their days among sages, listening respectfully to sacred stories and teachings.
ramacharitamanas::3143.simple_insight: Even the highest presence is shown as humble enough to listen.
ramacharitamanas::3143.detailed_meaning: In the forest setting of Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas describes the simple hermitage where Ram and Sita live among sages. The couple is not isolated in grandeur; they sit quietly and hear the sacred tradition with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3143.modern_relevance: You sit in a room full of expertise and still choose to listen instead of perform. That quiet respect can be its own kind of greatness.
ramacharitamanas::3143.insight: It shifts admiration toward humility: real nobility can include listening deeply.

ramacharitamanas::3144.verse_sanskrit: सखा बचन सुनि बिटप निहारी। उमगे भरत बिलोचन बारी॥ करत प्रनाम चले दोउ भाई। कहत प्रीति सारद सकुचाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3144.verse_hindi: सखा के वचन सुनकर और वृक्षों को देखकर भरतजी के नेत्रों में जल उमड़ आया। दोनों भाई प्रणाम करते हुए चले। उनके प्रेम का वर्णन करने में सरस्वतीजी भी सकुचाती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3144.english_translation: Hearing his friend's words and seeing the trees, Bharata's eyes overflowed with tears. The two brothers walked on with bows of reverence, and even Saraswati would feel shy trying to describe their love.
ramacharitamanas::3144.translation_literal: सखा (friend's) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / बिटप (trees) / निहारी (seeing) / उमगे (overflowed) / भरत (Bharata's) / बिलोचन (eyes) / बारी (water/tears) / करत (doing) / प्रनाम (reverence) / चले (walked) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / कहत (speaking) / प्रीति (love) / सारद (Saraswati) / सकुचाई (felt shy)
ramacharitamanas::3144.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3144.essence: True devotion is so deep that even words fall silent.
ramacharitamanas::3144.simple_meaning: Bharata is overwhelmed with emotion as he sees the sacred place and walks onward with Lakshmana in reverence. Their love is so deep that even language feels inadequate.
ramacharitamanas::3144.simple_insight: Some love is so pure it leaves words behind and turns into tears, reverence, and quiet movement.
ramacharitamanas::3144.detailed_meaning: Bharata and Lakshmana are moving through the forest shrine where Ram has lived. A friend's words and the sight of the trees break Bharata's heart open. Their devotion is so intense that the poet says even Saraswati would hesitate to describe it.
ramacharitamanas::3144.modern_relevance: You stand in a place that still holds someone's memory — a park bench, an empty room, a road you once walked together — and your chest tightens before you can explain why.
ramacharitamanas::3144.insight: It shifts attention from explaining love to embodying it through reverence, tears, and humble action.

ramacharitamanas::3145.verse_sanskrit: हरषहिं निरखि राम पद अंका। मानहुँ पारसु पायउ रंका॥ रज सिर धरि हियँ नयनन्हि लावहिं। रघुबर मिलन सरिस सुख पावहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3145.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणचिह्न देखकर दोनों भाई ऐसे हर्षित होते हैं, मानो दरिद्र पारस पा गया हो। वहाँ की रज को मस्तक पर रखकर हृदय में और नेत्रों में लगाते हैं और श्री रघुनाथजी के मिलने के समान सुख पाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3145.english_translation: Seeing Ram's footprints, both brothers rejoice as if a poor man has found a touchstone. They place the dust on their heads, hold it in their hearts and eyes, and feel the joy of meeting Raghubar himself.
ramacharitamanas::3145.translation_literal: हरषहिं (rejoice) / निरखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / पद अंका (footprints) / मानहुँ (as if) / पारसु (touchstone) / पायउ (found) / रंका (a poor man) / रज (dust) / सिर (head) / धरि (placing) / हियँ (in heart) / नयनन्हि (in the eyes) / लावहिं (they apply) / रघुबर (Raghubar) / मिलन (meeting) / सरिस (equal to) / सुख (joy) / पावहिं (they receive)
ramacharitamanas::3145.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3145.essence: A beloved's trace can feel as fulfilling as meeting them.
ramacharitamanas::3145.simple_meaning: Just seeing Ram's footprints fills the brothers with joy. They treat even the dust as sacred and feel as happy as if they had met Ram himself.
ramacharitamanas::3145.simple_insight: Love makes even a trace feel like presence.
ramacharitamanas::3145.detailed_meaning: Bharat and his brother are walking through the forest in search of Ram. When they find Ram's footprints, their devotion rises instantly: the ground itself becomes precious, and the smallest sign of him feels like his arrival.
ramacharitamanas::3145.modern_relevance: You find an old voice note from someone you miss and listen three times. The sound is tiny, but your whole chest changes. Presence can live in a trace.
ramacharitamanas::3145.insight: It shifts attention from needing direct contact to recognising how love animates every sign.

ramacharitamanas::3146.verse_sanskrit: देखि भरत गति अकथ अतीवा। प्रेम मगन मृग खग जड़ जीवा॥ सखहि सनेह बिबस मग भूला। कहि सुपंथ सुर बरषहिं फूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3146.verse_hindi: भरतजी की अत्यन्त अनिर्वचनीय दशा देखकर वन के पशु, पक्षी और जड़ (वृक्षादि) जीव प्रेम में मग्न हो गए। प्रेम के विशेष वश होने से सखा निषादराज को भी रास्ता भूल गया। तब देवता सुंदर रास्ता बतलाकर फूल बरसाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3146.english_translation: Seeing Bharata's utterly indescribable state, the beasts, birds, and even motionless beings were filled with love. Overcome by affection, his companion, the boatman, lost the path. Then the radiant beings showed the right way and showered flowers.
ramacharitamanas::3146.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / भरत (Bharata) / गति (state, movement) / अकथ (unspeakable) / अतीवा (extremely) / प्रेम (love) / मगन (immersed) / मृग (deer, beasts) / खग (birds) / जड़ (motionless) / जीवा (living beings) / सखहि (companion) / सनेह (affection) / बिबस (helpless, overcome) / मग (path) / भूला (forgot) / कहि (saying) / सुपंथ (right path) / सुर (radiant beings) / बरषहिं (shower) / फूला (flowers)
ramacharitamanas::3146.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3146.essence: True devotion is so strong it changes the world around it.
ramacharitamanas::3146.simple_meaning: Bharat's love is so overwhelming that even the forest creatures feel it. His companion loses the way, and the radiant beings help guide them and honor the moment with flowers.
ramacharitamanas::3146.simple_insight: Deep love changes the atmosphere around you, and even the world seems to respond.
ramacharitamanas::3146.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Bharata's grief and devotion are so intense that the whole scene seems to bend around it. Animals, birds, and even still trees are said to feel it; his companion loses the way in that emotional current, and radiant beings guide them onward with flowers.
ramacharitamanas::3146.modern_relevance: You walk into a room carrying real grief, and everyone feels the weight before you speak. Some moods are that powerful.
ramacharitamanas::3146.insight: It shows how devotion can transform a whole environment, not just the person feeling it.

ramacharitamanas::3147.verse_sanskrit: निरखि सिद्ध साधक अनुरागे। सहज सनेहु सराहन लागे॥ होत न भूतल भाउ भरत को। अचर सचर चर अचर करत को ॥
ramacharitamanas::3147.verse_hindi: भरत के प्रेम की इस स्थिति को देखकर सिद्ध और साधक लोग भी अनुराग से भर गए और उनके स्वाभाविक प्रेम की प्रशंसा करने लगे कि यदि इस पृथ्वी तल पर भरत का जन्म (अथवा प्रेम) न होता, तो जड़ को चेतन और चेतन को जड़ कौन करता? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3147.english_translation: Seeing Bharata's love, even perfected sages and seekers were filled with devotion and praised his natural affection: if Bharata's love had not appeared on earth, who could make the lifeless living and the living lifeless?
ramacharitamanas::3147.translation_literal: निरखि (seeing) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / साधक (seekers) / अनुरागे (became filled with love) / सहज (natural) / सनेहु (affection) / सराहन (to praise) / लागे (began) ॥ होत (would be) / न (not) / भूतल (on the earth) / भाउ (love/state) / भरत को (of Bharata) / अचर (lifeless) / सचर (moving/living) / चर (moving/living) / अचर (lifeless) / करत (making) / को (who) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3147.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3147.essence: Selfless love can make the impossible feel natural.
ramacharitamanas::3147.simple_meaning: Bharata's love is so pure that even sages are moved by it. His affection is praised as something that can transform the impossible.
ramacharitamanas::3147.simple_insight: Pure love changes the atmosphere around it; it makes even wise people feel reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3147.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Bharata's grief and devotion have become so intense that even perfected sages and spiritual seekers are overwhelmed. They praise the naturalness of his love, seeing it as a force that can reverse ordinary life.
ramacharitamanas::3147.modern_relevance: You watch someone give up status, comfort, and control just to honor a promise. The room goes quiet, because everyone can feel that this kind of love is rarer than achievement.
ramacharitamanas::3147.insight: It shifts attention from outward success to the transforming power of selfless devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3148.verse_sanskrit: पेम अमिअ मंदरु बिरहु भरतु पयोधि गँभीर। मथि प्रगटेउ सुर साधु हित कृपासिंधु रघुबीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::3148.verse_hindi: प्रेम अमृत है, विरह मंदराचल पर्वत है, भरतजी गहरे समुद्र हैं। कृपा के समुद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने देवता और साधुओं के हित के लिए स्वयं (इस भरत रूपी गहरे समुद्र को अपने विरह रूपी मंदराचल से) मथकर यह प्रेम रूपी अमृत प्रकट किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3148.english_translation: Love is nectar, separation is Mount Mandara, and Bharat is the deep ocean. For the good of the gods and holy ones, the ocean of mercy, Raghubir, churned it and brought forth this nectar of love.
ramacharitamanas::3148.translation_literal: पेम (love) / अमिअ (nectar) / मंदरु (Mount Mandara) / बिरहु (separation) / भरतु (Bharat) / पयोधि (ocean) / गँभीर (deep) / मथि (churning) / प्रगटेउ (brought forth) / सुर (gods) / साधु (holy ones) / हित (for the good) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of mercy) / रघुबीर (Raghubir)
ramacharitamanas::3148.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3148.essence: Separation can become the very force that reveals devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3148.simple_meaning: Love is compared to nectar, separation to the churning rod, and Bharat to a deep ocean. Ram, moved by mercy, brings out devotion's sweetness through Bharat's intense longing.
ramacharitamanas::3148.simple_insight: Your deepest ache can become the place where love becomes real.
ramacharitamanas::3148.detailed_meaning: Bharat's grief has become so vast that even the forest seems moved by it. In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas turns that sorrow into a sacred image: Ram, the ocean of mercy, churns Bharat's separation to reveal devotion's hidden nectar.
ramacharitamanas::3148.modern_relevance: You miss someone so deeply that the ache feels unbearable, yet that very longing keeps your love alive. Sometimes separation doesn't kill devotion — it distills it.
ramacharitamanas::3148.insight: It teaches you to see longing not as failure, but as the pressure that reveals the depth of love.

ramacharitamanas::3149.verse_sanskrit: सखा समेत मनोहर जोटा। लखेउ न लखन सघन बन ओटा॥ भरत दीख प्रभु आश्रमु पावन। सकल सुमंगल सदनु सुहावन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3149.verse_hindi: सखा निषादराज सहित इस मनोहर जोड़ी को सघन वन की आड़ के कारण लक्ष्मणजी नहीं देख पाए। भरतजी ने प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के समस्त सुमंगलों के धाम और सुंदर पवित्र आश्रम को देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3149.english_translation: Lakshman could not see the beautiful pair with his friend Nishadraj because of the dense forest cover. Bharat saw Lord Ram's holy hermitage, lovely and full of all auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::3149.translation_literal: सखा समेत (with his friend) / मनोहर (beautiful) / जोटा (pair) / लखेउ (saw) / न (not) / लखन (Lakshman) / सघन (dense) / बन (forest) / ओटा (covering) ॥ / भरत (Bharat) / दीख (saw) / प्रभु (Lord) / आश्रमु (hermitage) / पावन (pure) / सकल (all) / सुमंगलों (auspiciousnesses) / सदनु (abode) / सुहावन (beautiful) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3149.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3149.essence: Devotion sees the holy place even before reunion happens.
ramacharitamanas::3149.simple_meaning: Lakshman is blocked by the thick forest, but Bharat sees Ram's pure hermitage, a place filled with auspiciousness and beauty.
ramacharitamanas::3149.simple_insight: What love cannot yet see, reverence can already recognize.
ramacharitamanas::3149.detailed_meaning: Bharat has reached the forest hermitage where Ram is staying. Lakshman, hidden by the dense trees, cannot yet see the pair approaching with Nishadraj. Bharat, however, immediately beholds Ram's sacred dwelling as a place of blessing and beauty.
ramacharitamanas::3149.modern_relevance: You arrive at a quiet retreat after a long, aching journey. One person sees only trees and distance; another sees the place where love has been waiting for them.
ramacharitamanas::3149.insight: It shifts attention from obstruction to sacred presence, showing that devotion perceives meaning before the eyes do.

ramacharitamanas::3150.verse_sanskrit: करत प्रबेस मिटे दुख दावा। जनु जोगीं परमारथु पावा॥ देखे भरत लखन प्रभु आगे। पूँछे बचन कहत अनुरागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3150.verse_hindi: आश्रम में प्रवेश करते ही भरतजी का दुःख और दाह (जलन) मिट गया, मानो योगी को परमार्थ (परमतत्व) की प्राप्ति हो गई हो। भरतजी ने देखा कि लक्ष्मणजी प्रभु के आगे खड़े हैं और पूछे हुए वचन प्रेमपूर्वक कह रहे हैं (पूछी हुई बात का प्रेमपूर्वक उत्तर दे रहे हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3150.english_translation: As soon as he entered the hermitage, Bharat's sorrow and burning vanished, as if a yogi had attained the highest truth. He saw Lakshman standing before the Lord, answering questions with love.
ramacharitamanas::3150.translation_literal: करत (doing) / प्रबेस (entry) / मिटे (were removed) / दुख (sorrow) / दावा (burning) / जनु (as if) / जोगीं (yogi) / परमारथु (highest truth) / पावा (attained) ॥ / देखे (saw) / भरत (Bharat) / लखन (Lakshman) / प्रभु (Lord) / आगे (in front) / पूँछे (asked) / बचन (words) / कहत (speaking) / अनुरागे (with love) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3150.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3150.essence: Presence can end sorrow before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3150.simple_meaning: Bharat enters the hermitage and his grief instantly falls away. Seeing Lakshman before Ram, speaking with love, brings him a deep inner settling.
ramacharitamanas::3150.simple_insight: Some pain ends the moment you reach what your heart has been seeking.
ramacharitamanas::3150.detailed_meaning: Bharat has come to the forest after unbearable separation. The moment he steps into Ram's hermitage, his anguish lifts. He sees Lakshman standing protectively before Ram, and the scene itself becomes a relief.
ramacharitamanas::3150.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after days of dread, and the person you feared facing is simply there, calm and kind. Your chest loosens before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::3150.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional turbulence to quiet release in the presence of what is trusted.

ramacharitamanas::3151.verse_sanskrit: सीस जटा कटि मुनि पट बाँधें। तून कसें कर सरु धनु काँधें॥ बेदी पर मुनि साधु समाजू। सीय सहित राजत रघुराजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3151.verse_hindi: सिर पर जटा है, कमर में मुनियों का (वल्कल) वस्त्र बाँधे हैं और उसी में तरकस कसे हैं। हाथ में बाण तथा कंधे पर धनुष है, वेदी पर मुनि तथा साधुओं का समुदाय बैठा है और सीताजी सहित श्री रघुनाथजी विराजमान हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3151.english_translation: With matted hair on his head, a sage's cloth tied at his waist, a quiver fastened there; bow and arrows in hand and on his shoulder. On the sacred platform, among sages and holy people, Raghuraj shines with Sita beside him.
ramacharitamanas::3151.translation_literal: सीस (head) / जटा (matted hair) / कटि (waist) / मुनि पट (sage-cloth) / बाँधें (tied) / तून (quiver) / कसें (fastened) / कर (hand) / सरु (arrows) / धनु (bow) / काँधें (on shoulder) / बेदी (sacred platform) / पर (on) / मुनि (sages) / साधु (holy people) / समाजू (assembly) / सीय सहित (with Sita) / राजत (shines) / रघुराजू (Raghuraj)
ramacharitamanas::3151.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3151.essence: Renunciation and kingship can live in the same person.
ramacharitamanas::3151.simple_meaning: Ram appears as both a forest sage and a royal figure at once, seated with Sita among holy people on the sacred platform.
ramacharitamanas::3151.simple_insight: The highest life can hold both renunciation and dignity without conflict.
ramacharitamanas::3151.detailed_meaning: At Bharadwaj's sacred hermitage, Bharat has just entered and seen Ram before him. Ram is dressed like a forest ascetic, yet he still carries bow and arrows and shines like the rightful king. The scene shows the harmony of exile, holiness, and royal grace.
ramacharitamanas::3151.modern_relevance: You show up at a wedding in plain clothes after a hard year, and somehow your calm carries more dignity than anyone's polished display.
ramacharitamanas::3151.insight: It teaches you that true nobility does not depend on outward luxury.

ramacharitamanas::3152.verse_sanskrit: बलकल बसन जटिल तनु स्यामा। जनु मुनिबेष कीन्ह रति कामा॥ कर कमलनि धनु सायकु फेरत। जिय की जरनि हरत हँसि हेरत ॥
ramacharitamanas::3152.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के वल्कल वस्त्र हैं, जटा धारण किए हैं, श्याम शरीर है। (सीता-रामजी ऐसे लगते हैं) मानो रति और कामदेव ने मुनि का वेष धारण किया हो। श्री रामजी अपने करकमलों से धनुष-बाण फेर रहे हैं और हँसकर देखते ही जी की जलन हर लेते हैं (अर्थात जिसकी ओर भी एक बार हँसकर देख लेते हैं, उसी को परम आनंद और शांति मिल जाती है।) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3152.english_translation: He wears bark-cloth, his body is matted-haired and dark. It is as if Desire and Love themselves have taken a sage's form. With lotus hands he turns his bow and arrows, and his smiling glance removes the burning from the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3152.translation_literal: बलकल (bark-cloth) / बसन (garment) / जटिल (matted-haired) / तनु (body) / स्यामा (dark) / जनु (as if) / मुनिबेष (sage-form) / कीन्ह (made) / रति (Love) / कामा (Desire) / कर कमलनि (lotus hands) / धनु (bow) / सायकु (arrows) / फेरत (turning) / जिय (heart) / की जरनि (burning) / हरत (removing) / हँसि (smiling) / हेरत (looking)
ramacharitamanas::3152.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3152.essence: Ram's gentle presence cools what desire has burned.
