ramacharitamanas::3152.simple_meaning: Ram looks like a sage, yet his beauty is so powerful it feels like Love itself has taken that form. Even his smiling glance cools the heart's burning.
ramacharitamanas::3152.simple_insight: His presence is so complete that even seeing him feels like relief.
ramacharitamanas::3152.detailed_meaning: Bharat has reached the forest hermitage and now sees Ram and Sita among the sages. Ram is dressed like an ascetic, yet his beauty is overwhelming. This is a descriptive bridge before the next couplet praises how the whole scene shines with devotion and wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::3152.modern_relevance: You walk into a quiet room after weeks of tension, and one calm smile from the right person undoes the whole knot in your chest.
ramacharitamanas::3152.insight: It turns attention from outer appearance to the healing force of presence.

ramacharitamanas::3153.verse_sanskrit: लसत मंजु मुनि मंडली मध्य सीय रघुचंदु। ग्यान सभाँ जनु तनु धरें भगति सच्चिदानंदु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3153.verse_hindi: सुंदर मुनि मंडली के बीच में सीताजी और रघुकुलचंद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी ऐसे सुशोभित हो रहे हैं मानो ज्ञान की सभा में साक्षात् भक्ति और सच्चिदानंद शरीर धारण करके विराजमान हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3153.english_translation: Beautifully seated among the sages, Sita and Raghunath shine like devotion itself appearing in the assembly of wisdom, as if the supreme being of consciousness and bliss has taken form.
ramacharitamanas::3153.translation_literal: लसत (shining) / मंजु (beautiful) / मुनि मंडली (assembly of sages) / मध्य (in the middle) / सीय (Sita) / रघुचंदु (moon of the Raghu clan, Ram) / ग्यान सभाँ (in the assembly of wisdom) / जनु (as if) / तनु धरें (having taken body) / भगति (devotion) / सच्चिदानंदु (consciousness-bliss)
ramacharitamanas::3153.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3153.essence: Devotion becomes visible when wisdom becomes a living presence.
ramacharitamanas::3153.simple_meaning: Ram and Sita sit among the sages like devotion itself taking form inside the world of wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::3153.simple_insight: You do not have to choose between understanding and love; the two can live in the same heart.
ramacharitamanas::3153.detailed_meaning: In the royal gathering at Mithila, sages surround Ram and Sita. Tulsidas stops the scene to reveal what it really means: their presence is not just beautiful, it is the meeting of wisdom and devotion in living form.
ramacharitamanas::3153.modern_relevance: You can be in a room full of experts and still feel the deepest truth is simple love. The most complete understanding often looks less like argument and more like reverent presence.
ramacharitamanas::3153.insight: It shifts the mind from treating wisdom and devotion as separate paths to seeing them as one living reality.

ramacharitamanas::3154.verse_sanskrit: सानुज सखा समेत मगन मन। बिसरे हरष सोक सुख दुख गन॥ पाहि नाथ कहि पाहि गोसाईं। भूतल परे लकुट की नाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3154.verse_hindi: छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न और सखा निषादराज समेत भरतजी का मन (प्रेम में) मग्न हो रहा है। हर्ष-शोक, सुख-दुःख आदि सब भूल गए। हे नाथ! रक्षा कीजिए, हे गुसाईं! रक्षा कीजिए' ऐसा कहकर वे पृथ्वी पर दण्ड की तरह गिर पड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::3154.english_translation: Along with his younger brother and his friend, Bharata's mind was absorbed. He forgot all counts of joy and sorrow, pleasure and pain. Crying, "Protect me, Lord! Protect me, Master!" he fell to the earth like a staff.
ramacharitamanas::3154.translation_literal: सानुज (with younger brother) / सखा (with friend) / समेत (together with) / मगन (absorbed) / मन (mind) / बिसरे (forgot) / हरष (joy) / सोक (sorrow) / सुख (pleasure) / दुख (pain) / गन (groups) / पाहि (protect) / नाथ (Lord) / कहि (saying) / पाहि (protect) / गोसाईं (Master) / भूतल (on the earth) / परे (fell) / लकुट (staff) / की (of) / नाईं (like)
ramacharitamanas::3154.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3154.essence: Devotion can be so complete that even joy and sorrow disappear.
ramacharitamanas::3154.simple_meaning: Bharat becomes so overwhelmed with devotion that he forgets every opposite feeling and collapses on the ground, crying out for protection.
ramacharitamanas::3154.simple_insight: Deep love can quiet the whole storm of mixed emotions.
ramacharitamanas::3154.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands with Shatrughna and Nishadraj, but his attention is fixed only on Ram. Overcome by devotion, he forgets joy and sorrow alike, calls out for protection, and falls flat on the ground in surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3154.modern_relevance: You finally see the person you’ve been missing after a long silence. For a moment, every other feeling drops away — relief, fear, pride, and hurt all dissolve into one helpless cry.
ramacharitamanas::3154.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional self-management to wholehearted surrender.

ramacharitamanas::3155.verse_sanskrit: बचन सप्रेम लखन पहिचाने। करत प्रनामु भरत जियँ जाने॥ बंधु सनेह सरस एहि ओरा। उत साहिब सेवा बस जोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3155.verse_hindi: प्रेमभरे वचनों से लक्ष्मणजी ने पहचान लिया और मन में जान लिया कि भरतजी प्रणाम कर रहे हैं। (वे श्री रामजी की ओर मुँह किए खड़े थे, भरतजी पीठ पीछे थे, इससे उन्होंने देखा नहीं।) अब इस ओर तो भाई भरतजी का सरस प्रेम और उधर स्वामी श्री रामचन्द्रजी की सेवा की प्रबल परवशता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3155.english_translation: Lakshman recognised Bharat through his loving words and understood in his heart that Bharat was bowing. One side was the sweetness of brotherly love; the other was the force of service binding the lord.
ramacharitamanas::3155.translation_literal: बचन (words) / सप्रेम (with love) / लखन (Lakshman) / पहिचाने (recognised) / करत (doing) / प्रनामु (bowing) / भरत (Bharat) / जियँ (in the heart) / जाने (knew) / बंधु (brother) / सनेह (love) / सरस (sweet) / एहि (this) / ओरा (side) / उत (there) / साहिब (lord/master) / सेवा (service) / बस (bound by) / जोरा (force)
ramacharitamanas::3155.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3155.essence: Love may pull your heart one way while service pulls your hands another.
ramacharitamanas::3155.simple_meaning: Lakshman sees Bharat's bowed heart clearly: one side is brotherly affection, the other is devoted service to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3155.simple_insight: Real devotion can include tenderness, duty, and restraint at the same time.
ramacharitamanas::3155.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat has come to Ram with overwhelming love, and Lakshman instantly reads his heart. The verse holds two forces together: Bharat's brotherly affection and Ram's pull as the one he serves.
ramacharitamanas::3155.modern_relevance: You’re standing between family loyalty and a promise you made to someone else. Neither side feels wrong, and that tension is exactly what this verse understands.
ramacharitamanas::3155.insight: It teaches you to see devotion as a living tension between affection and obligation, not a simple emotion.

ramacharitamanas::3156.verse_sanskrit: मिलि न जाइ नहिं गुदरत बनई। सुकबि लखन मन की गति भनई॥ रहे राखि सेवा पर भारू। चढ़ी चंग जनु खैंच खेलारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3156.verse_hindi: न तो (क्षणभर के लिए भी सेवा से पृथक होकर) मिलते ही बनता है और न (प्रेमवश) छोड़ते (उपेक्षा करते) ही। कोई श्रेष्ठ कवि ही लक्ष्मणजी के चित्त की इस गति (दुविधा) का वर्णन कर सकता है। वे सेवा पर भार रखकर रह गए (सेवा को ही विशेष महत्वपूर्ण समझकर उसी में लगे रहे) मानो चढ़ी हुई पतंग को खिलाड़ी (पतंग उड़ाने वाला) खींच रहा हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3156.english_translation: It neither feels right to meet nor to turn away. Only a great poet can describe Lakshman's state of mind. He stayed weighed down by service, like a kite being pulled by the string of the one flying it.
ramacharitamanas::3156.translation_literal: मिलि (meeting) / न जाइ (is not possible) / नहिं (not) / गुदरत (turning away) / बनई (fits) / सुकबि (great poet) / लखन (Lakshman) / मन (mind) / की गति (movement/state) / भनई (can describe)॥ / रहे (remained) / राखि (keeping) / सेवा (service) / पर (on) / भारू (weight) / चढ़ी (mounted) / चंग (kite) / जनु (as if) / खैंच (pulling) / खेलारू (the player) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3156.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3156.essence: True service can hold you even when your heart is pulled apart.
ramacharitamanas::3156.simple_meaning: Lakshman is so absorbed in service that he cannot fully meet or turn away. His mind is caught in a devoted tension, like a kite held by its string.
ramacharitamanas::3156.simple_insight: Service can be so total that even inner conflict becomes part of love.
ramacharitamanas::3156.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat has arrived at the edge of Ram's world, and Lakshman is caught between greeting him and guarding Ram's cause. The poet says only a great poet could capture this tension, because Lakshman stays bound to service even while his heart is pulled in two directions.
ramacharitamanas::3156.modern_relevance: You are on a video call, but half your mind is with the child crying in the next room. You want to respond fully to both, yet only one can hold your body at a time.
ramacharitamanas::3156.insight: It shows how service can remain steady even when the mind feels split, and how duty can anchor divided attention.

ramacharitamanas::3157.verse_sanskrit: कहत सप्रेम नाइ महि माथा। भरत प्रनाम करत रघुनाथा॥ उठे रामु सुनि पेम अधीरा। कहुँ पट कहुँ निषंग धनु तीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3157.verse_hindi: लक्ष्मणजी ने प्रेम सहित पृथ्वी पर मस्तक नवाकर कहा- हे रघुनाथजी! भरतजी प्रणाम कर रहे हैं। यह सुनते ही श्री रघुनाथजी प्रेम में अधीर होकर उठे। कहीं वस्त्र गिरा, कहीं तरकस, कहीं धनुष और कहीं बाण ॥
ramacharitamanas::3157.english_translation: Lakshman bowed to the ground with love and said, “Raghunath, Bharata is offering his respects.” Hearing this, Ram rose in love and excitement, dropping his cloth here, his quiver there, his bow and arrows elsewhere.
ramacharitamanas::3157.translation_literal: कहत (saying) / सप्रेम (with love) / नाइ (bowing) / महि (to the ground) / माथा (head) / भरत (Bharata) / प्रनाम (salutation) / करत (doing) / रघुनाथा (Raghunatha) / उठे (rose) / रामु (Ram) / सुनि (hearing) / पेम (love) / अधीरा (restless, eager) / कहुँ (here) / पट (cloth) / कहुँ (here) / निषंग (quiver) / धनु (bow) / तीरा (arrows)
ramacharitamanas::3157.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3157.essence: Love makes Ram rise before anything else can matter.
ramacharitamanas::3157.simple_meaning: Lakshman respectfully tells Ram that Bharata is bowing to him. Ram is so moved by love that he jumps up in eagerness, dropping his clothes and weapons as he rises.
ramacharitamanas::3157.simple_insight: Love makes even a king forget dignity, because the heart recognizes what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::3157.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Lakshman relays Bharata’s respectful greeting. The moment Ram hears Bharata’s name, his love overflows and he rises at once, dropping his cloth, bow, and arrows. The scene shows the depth of brotherly love before their reunion.
ramacharitamanas::3157.modern_relevance: You hear that someone you love has finally arrived, and you stop mid-task without thinking. The body moves before pride can catch up.
ramacharitamanas::3157.insight: It shows how genuine love dissolves formality and pulls attention straight to the beloved.

ramacharitamanas::3158.verse_sanskrit: बरबस लिए उठाइ उर लाए कृपानिधान। भरत राम की मिलनि लखि बिसरे सबहि अपान ॥
ramacharitamanas::3158.verse_hindi: कृपा निधान श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने उनको जबरदस्ती उठाकर हृदय से लगा लिया! भरतजी और श्री रामजी के मिलन की रीति को देखकर सबको अपनी सुध भूल गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3158.english_translation: The treasure of compassion pulled him up and drew him into an embrace. Seeing Bharat and Ram meet, everyone forgot themselves.
ramacharitamanas::3158.translation_literal: बरबस (forcibly / by sheer love) / लिए (took) / उठाइ (lifting up) / उर (to the chest) / लाए (brought) / कृपानिधान (treasure of compassion) / भरत (Bharat) / राम (Ram) / की मिलनि (their meeting) / लखि (seeing) / बिसरे (forgot) / सबहि (everyone) / अपान (themselves)
ramacharitamanas::3158.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3158.essence: Love can be so overwhelming that it makes everyone forget themselves.
ramacharitamanas::3158.simple_meaning: Ram pulled Bharat up and embraced him. Everyone watching was so moved by their reunion that they forgot themselves.
ramacharitamanas::3158.simple_insight: Some reunions are so full of love that the people watching lose track of everything else.
ramacharitamanas::3158.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat finally reaches Ram after unbearable separation. Ram lifts him into an embrace, and the scene overflows with emotion. The moment is not a teaching by itself; it is one vivid step in the larger account of their meeting.
ramacharitamanas::3158.modern_relevance: You finally see a sibling after years apart, and the room goes quiet. The hug says everything before either of you can speak.
ramacharitamanas::3158.insight: It shows love so complete that even bystanders are pulled out of ordinary awareness.

ramacharitamanas::3159.verse_sanskrit: मिलनि प्रीति किमि जाइ बखानी। कबिकुल अगम करम मन बानी॥ परम प्रेम पूरन दोउ भाई। मन बुधि चित अहमिति बिसराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3159.verse_hindi: मिलन की प्रीति कैसे बखानी जाए? वह तो कविकुल के लिए कर्म, मन, वाणी तीनों से अगम है। दोनों भाई (भरतजी और श्री रामजी) मन, बुद्धि, चित्त और अहंकार को भुलाकर परम प्रेम से पूर्ण हो रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3159.english_translation: How can the love of this meeting be described? It is beyond the reach of a poet's action, mind, and speech. Both brothers are overflowing with perfect love, having forgotten mind, intellect, consciousness, and the sense of separate self.
ramacharitamanas::3159.translation_literal: मिलनि (meeting) / प्रीति (love) / किमि (how) / जाइ (goes) / बखानी (described) / कबिकुल (poets' line) / अगम (unreachable) / करम (action) / मन (mind) / बानी (speech) / परम (supreme) / प्रेम (love) / पूरन (full) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / मन (mind) / बुधि (discerning mind) / चित (inner state) / अहमिति (sense of separate self) / बिसराई (forgotten)
ramacharitamanas::3159.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3159.essence: True meeting dissolves ego before it can be named.
ramacharitamanas::3159.simple_meaning: Their reunion is so full of love that words cannot capture it. Both brothers are lost in perfect affection, beyond ego and ordinary thought.
ramacharitamanas::3159.simple_insight: Some moments are too complete to explain; you only enter them with your whole heart.
ramacharitamanas::3159.detailed_meaning: After Bharata bows and Ram rushes to embrace him, the scene turns inward. Tulsidas pauses the action to say that this meeting cannot be measured by poetry, thought, or speech. Ram and Bharata are so full of love that even the sense of separate self disappears.
ramacharitamanas::3159.modern_relevance: You finally see someone after years apart, and the room goes quiet because nothing you say can match what you feel. Some reunions are larger than language.
ramacharitamanas::3159.insight: It shifts attention from explaining closeness to recognising the depth that makes explanation fail.

ramacharitamanas::3160.verse_sanskrit: कहहु सुपेम प्रगट को करई। केहि छाया कबि मति अनुसरई॥ कबिहि अरथ आखर बलु साँचा। अनुहरि ताल गतिहि नटु नाचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3160.verse_hindi: कहिए, उस श्रेष्ठ प्रेम को कौन प्रकट करे? कवि की बुद्धि किसकी छाया का अनुसरण करे? कवि को तो अक्षर और अर्थ का ही सच्चा बल है। नट ताल की गति के अनुसार ही नाचता है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3160.english_translation: Tell me, who can reveal that supreme love? Whose shadow can the poet's mind follow? The poet has only the true force of words and meaning. The dancer moves only to the rhythm of the drum.
ramacharitamanas::3160.translation_literal: कहहु (tell) / सुपेम (supreme love) / प्रगट (manifest) / को (who) / करई (does) / केहि (whose) / छाया (shadow) / कबि (poet) / मति (mind) / अनुसरई (follows) / कबिहि (for the poet) / अरथ (meaning) / आखर (letters/words) / बलु (strength) / साँचा (true) / अनुहरि (following) / ताल (drumbeat/rhythm) / गतिहि (movement) / नटु (dancer) / नाचा (dances)
ramacharitamanas::3160.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3160.essence: The deepest love can be hinted at, never fully captured.
ramacharitamanas::3160.simple_meaning: The poet says this love is too great to fully describe. Words can only follow its outline, like a dancer following rhythm.
ramacharitamanas::3160.simple_insight: Some truths are so large that language can only circle them with humility.
ramacharitamanas::3160.detailed_meaning: After Bharat and Ram embrace, the scene overflows with a love too deep for ordinary speech. Tulsidas steps back and admits that even a poet can only hint at it, using words the way a dancer follows rhythm.
ramacharitamanas::3160.modern_relevance: You try to explain a moment that changed you, and the sentence keeps breaking apart. Some experiences are real before they are speakable.
ramacharitamanas::3160.insight: It teaches you to respect the limits of language and let feeling exceed description.

ramacharitamanas::3161.verse_sanskrit: अगम सनेह भरत रघुबर को। जहँ न जाइ मनु बिधि हरि हर को॥ सो मैं कुमति कहौं केहि भाँति। बाज सुराग कि गाँडर ताँती ॥
ramacharitamanas::3161.verse_hindi: भरतजी और श्री रघुनाथजी का प्रेम अगम्य है, जहाँ ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और महादेव का भी मन नहीं जा सकता। उस प्रेम को मैं कुबुद्धि किस प्रकार कहूँ! भला, गाँडर की ताँत से भी कहीं सुंदर राग बज सकता है? ॥ (तालाबों और झीलों में एक तरह की घास होती है, उसे गाँडर कहते हैं।)
ramacharitamanas::3161.english_translation: The love of Bharat and Raghubar is beyond reach, where even the minds of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva cannot go. How can I, with dull understanding, describe that love? Can a reed-string ever produce a sweeter tune than a proper lute?
ramacharitamanas::3161.translation_literal: अगम (unreachable) / सनेह (love) / भरत (Bharat) / रघुबर (Raghubar) / को (of) / जहँ (where) / न (not) / जाइ (goes) / मनु (mind) / बिधि (Brahma) / हरि (Vishnu) / हर (Shiva) / को (of)॥ / सो (that) / मैं (I) / कुमति (dull understanding) / कहौं (say) / केहि भाँति (in what way) / बाज (music) / सुराग (proper lute) / कि (or) / गाँडर (reed) / ताँती (string)॥
ramacharitamanas::3161.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3161.essence: True devotion is too vast for even the highest minds to contain.
ramacharitamanas::3161.simple_meaning: Bharat’s love for Ram is beyond ordinary understanding, so deep that even the greatest minds cannot fully grasp it.
ramacharitamanas::3161.simple_insight: Real devotion is too vast to explain neatly; it has to be felt.
ramacharitamanas::3161.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas pauses after describing Bharat and Ram’s meeting. He says their love is so pure and immense that even Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva cannot reach its full depth. Language itself fails, and only wonder remains.
ramacharitamanas::3161.modern_relevance: You try to explain why you still care so deeply for someone who changed your life, and every sentence feels too small. Some bonds are larger than explanation.
ramacharitamanas::3161.insight: It shifts the mind from analyzing love to revering its mystery.

ramacharitamanas::3162.verse_sanskrit: मिलनि बिलोकि भरत रघुबर की। सुरगन सभय धकधकी धरकी॥ समुझाए सुरगुरु जड़ जागे। बरषि प्रसून प्रसंसन लागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3162.verse_hindi: भरतजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के मिलने का ढंग देखकर देवता भयभीत हो गए, उनकी धुकधुकी धड़कने लगी। देव गुरु बृहस्पतिजी ने समझाया, तब कहीं वे मूर्ख चेते और फूल बरसाकर प्रशंसा करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3162.english_translation: Seeing the meeting of Bharat and Raghubar, the celestial beings grew fearful and their hearts pounded. When the divine teacher explained, they came to their senses and began showering flowers in praise.
ramacharitamanas::3162.translation_literal: मिलनि (meeting) / बिलोकि (seeing) / भरत (Bharat) / रघुबर की (of Raghubar) / सुरगन (celestial beings) / सभय (fearful) / धकधकी (pounding) / धरकी (began) / समुझाए (being explained) / सुरगुरु (divine teacher) / जड़ (foolish) / जागे (woke up) / बरषि (showering) / प्रसून (flowers) / प्रसंसन (in praise) / लागे (began)
ramacharitamanas::3162.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3162.essence: Pure love can overwhelm even the wise before it becomes clear.
ramacharitamanas::3162.simple_meaning: The gods were stunned by the depth of Bharat and Ram's meeting. After Brahma explained, they understood and praised it with flowers.
ramacharitamanas::3162.simple_insight: Some bonds are so pure they leave even the highest minds speechless.
ramacharitamanas::3162.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat and Ram finally meet after exile, and the love between them is so overwhelming that even the celestial beings are shaken. Brahma has to explain the scene before they can understand its greatness and respond with praise.
ramacharitamanas::3162.modern_relevance: You watch two siblings reconcile after a family rupture, and the room goes silent. Everyone can feel something sacred has happened, even before anyone finds the words.
ramacharitamanas::3162.insight: It shifts attention from surface drama to the hidden greatness of selfless love.

ramacharitamanas::3163.verse_sanskrit: मिलि सपेम रिपुसूदनहि केवटु भेंटेउ राम। भूरि भायँ भेंटे भरत लछिमन करत प्रनाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::3163.verse_hindi: फिर श्री रामजी प्रेम के साथ शत्रुघ्न से मिलकर तब केवट (निषादराज) से मिले। प्रणाम करते हुए लक्ष्मणजी से भरतजी बड़े ही प्रेम से मिले ॥
ramacharitamanas::3163.english_translation: Then, with love, Rama met Shatrughna. Bharata and Lakshmana met with great affection, offering their salutations.
ramacharitamanas::3163.translation_literal: मिलि (meeting) / सपेम (with love) / रिपुसूदनहि (the slayer of enemies) / केवटु (Shatrughna) / भेंटेउ (met) / राम (Rama) / भूरि (greatly) / भायँ (with affection) / भेंटे (met) / भरत (Bharata) / लछिमन (Lakshmana) / करत (doing) / प्रनाम (salutation)
ramacharitamanas::3163.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3163.essence: Love returns first as greeting, not argument.
ramacharitamanas::3163.simple_meaning: The brothers meet after long separation, and each greeting is full of love and respect. It is a scene of reunion, not teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3163.simple_insight: Some reunions heal without words; affection itself becomes the blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3163.detailed_meaning: After the painful exile and the long strain of separation, Rama’s family finally comes together again. Rama meets Shatrughna with love, and Bharata greets Lakshmana with deep affection and reverence. The verse simply shows the tenderness of that reunion.
ramacharitamanas::3163.modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering after years of distance, and the first hug says what everyone has been holding back. Some bonds need no speech to feel restored.
ramacharitamanas::3163.insight: It shifts attention from conflict to the healing power of respectful reunion.

ramacharitamanas::3164.verse_sanskrit: भेंटेउ लखन ललकि लघु भाई। बहुरि निषादु लीन्ह उर लाई॥ पुनि मुनिगन दुहुँ भाइन्ह बंदे। अभिमत आसिष पाइ अनंदे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3164.verse_hindi: तब लक्ष्मणजी ललककर (बड़ी उमंग के साथ) छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न से मिले। फिर उन्होंने निषादराज को हृदय से लगा लिया। फिर भरत-शत्रुघ्न दोनों भाइयों ने (उपस्थित) मुनियों को प्रणाम किया और इच्छित आशीर्वाद पाकर वे आनंदित हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3164.english_translation: Then Lakshman joyfully embraced his younger brother Shatrughna. After that he drew Nishadraj close to his heart. Then both brothers bowed to the sages, and, receiving the blessing they desired, they were filled with joy.
ramacharitamanas::3164.translation_literal: भेंटेउ (embraced/met) / लखन (Lakshman) / ललकि (joyfully, with eagerness) / लघु भाई (younger brother) / बहुरि (again) / निषादु (Nishadraj) / लीन्ह (took) / उर (heart/chest) / लाई (placing) / पुनि (then again) / मुनिगन (sages) / दुहुँ भाइन्ह (both brothers) / बंदे (bowed) / अभिमत (desired) / आसिष (blessing) / पाइ (having received) / अनंदे (delighted)
ramacharitamanas::3164.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3164.essence: True reunion begins with embrace, humility, and blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3164.simple_meaning: Lakshman greets Shatrughna with joy, embraces Nishadraj, and both brothers bow to the sages and receive blessings.
ramacharitamanas::3164.simple_insight: Love shows itself in quick, humble gestures of respect.
ramacharitamanas::3164.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the reunited brothers are meeting allies and elders after the long exile has torn the family apart. Lakshman welcomes Shatrughna, embraces Nishadraj, and both brothers bow to the sages, receiving blessings before the next emotional reunion unfolds.
ramacharitamanas::3164.modern_relevance: You finally see your sibling after months apart, and the first thing you do is pull them into a hug before greeting anyone else.
ramacharitamanas::3164.insight: It shows how reunion naturally moves from affection to respect, especially when old bonds have been tested.

ramacharitamanas::3165.verse_sanskrit: सानुज भरत उमगि अनुरागा। धरि सिर सिय पद पदुम परागा॥ पुनि पुनि करत प्रनाम उठाए। सिर कर कमल परसि बैठाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3165.verse_hindi: छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न सहित भरतजी प्रेम में उमँगकर सीताजी के चरण कमलों की रज सिर पर धारण कर बार-बार प्रणाम करने लगे। सीताजी ने उन्हें उठाकर उनके सिर को अपने करकमल से स्पर्श कर (सिर पर हाथ फेरकर) उन दोनों को बैठाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3165.english_translation: With Lakshman beside him, Bharat rose in love and placed Sita's lotus dust on his head. Again and again he bowed; Sita lifted them, touched their heads with her lotus hand, and seated them.
ramacharitamanas::3165.translation_literal: सानुज (with younger brother) / भरत (Bharat) / उमगि (rising in joy) / अनुरागा (in love) / धरि (placing) / सिर (head) / सिय (Sita) / पद (feet) / पदुम (lotus) / परागा (dust) / पुनि पुनि (again and again) / करत (doing) / प्रनाम (bowing) / उठाए (lifted up) / सिर (head) / कर (hand) / कमल (lotus) / परसि (touching) / बैठाए (seated)
ramacharitamanas::3165.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3165.essence: Love bows low, and tenderness lifts it back up.
ramacharitamanas::3165.simple_meaning: Bharat and Lakshman bow to Sita with deep love. Sita responds gently, lifting them up and seating them with affection.
ramacharitamanas::3165.simple_insight: Real reverence makes room for warmth, not distance.
ramacharitamanas::3165.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat arrives with Lakshman and meets Sita after Ram's exile has torn the family apart. Overwhelmed by love, he bows again and again, and Sita answers with tender grace, lifting them both and easing the ache of separation.
ramacharitamanas::3165.modern_relevance: You see someone after a long family rupture, and no one knows how to speak first. One person bows low in love; the other answers by making the moment safe again.
ramacharitamanas::3165.insight: It shows respect and affection working together, turning a painful reunion into comfort.

ramacharitamanas::3166.verse_sanskrit: सीयँ असीस दीन्हि मन माहीं। मनग सनेहँ देह सुधि नाहीं॥ सब बिधि सानुकूल लखि सीता। भे निसोच उर अपडर बीता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3166.verse_hindi: सीताजी ने मन ही मन आशीर्वाद दिया, क्योंकि वे स्नेह में मग्न हैं, उन्हें देह की सुध-बुध नहीं है। सीताजी को सब प्रकार से अपने अनुकूल देखकर भरतजी सोचरहित हो गए और उनके हृदय का कल्पित भय जाता रहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3166.english_translation: Sita gave her blessing in her heart. Lost in love, she was unaware of her body. Seeing Sita favorable in every way, Bharat became free of worry, and the fear in his heart vanished.
ramacharitamanas::3166.translation_literal: सीयँ (by Sita) / असीस (blessing) / दीन्हि (gave) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / मनग (absorbed) / सनेहँ (in love) / देह (body) / सुधि (awareness) / नाहीं (not) / सब बिधि (in every way) / सानुकूल (favorable) / लखि (seeing) / सीता (Sita) / भे (became) / निसोच (free from worry) / उर (heart) / अपडर (fear) / बीता (gone)
ramacharitamanas::3166.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3166.essence: Clear love dissolves the fear you were carrying.
ramacharitamanas::3166.simple_meaning: Sita blesses Bharat inwardly, and Bharat’s fear disappears when he sees her kindness and favor.
ramacharitamanas::3166.simple_insight: When love is clear and mutual, fear loses its grip almost at once.
ramacharitamanas::3166.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat has come to Sita with reverence and grief already in his heart. Sita, absorbed in affection, blesses him inwardly. Seeing her fully aligned with him, Bharat’s anxiety dissolves.
ramacharitamanas::3166.modern_relevance: You walk into a room expecting judgment, then catch one kind look and your shoulders drop. A single sign of goodwill can undo hours of fear.
ramacharitamanas::3166.insight: It shifts the mind from suspicion to trust when another person’s goodwill becomes unmistakable.

ramacharitamanas::3167.verse_sanskrit: कोउ किछु कहई न कोउ किछु पूँछा। प्रेम भरा मन निज गति छूँछा॥ तेहि अवसर केवटु धीरजु धरि। जोरि पानि बिनवत प्रनामु करि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3167.verse_hindi: उस समय न तो कोई कुछ कहता है, न कोई कुछ पूछता है! मन प्रेम से परिपूर्ण है, वह अपनी गति से खाली है (अर्थात संकल्प-विकल्प और चांचल्य से शून्य है)। उस अवसर पर केवट (निषादराज) धीरज धर और हाथ जोड़कर प्रणाम करके विनती करने लगा- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3167.english_translation: No one says anything; no one asks anything. The mind is full of love and empty of restless thoughts. At that moment, the boatman, steady and composed, folded his hands and bowed, then spoke his prayer.
ramacharitamanas::3167.translation_literal: कोउ (someone) / किछु (anything) / कहई (says) / न (not) / कोउ (someone) / किछु (anything) / पूँछा (asks) / प्रेम (love) / भरा (filled) / मन (mind) / निज (own) / गति (movement) / छूँछा (empty) / तेहि (that) / अवसर (moment) / केवटु (boatman) / धीरजु (patience, steadiness) / धरि (having held) / जोरि (joined) / पानि (hands) / बिनवत (beseeches) / प्रनामु (bow) / करि (having done)
ramacharitamanas::3167.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3167.essence: Love silences the mind before it lets anyone speak.
ramacharitamanas::3167.simple_meaning: In a moment of deep love, everyone falls silent. The boatman then gathers himself, bows, and begins to speak with respect.
ramacharitamanas::3167.simple_insight: Love can make a room so full that even words feel unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::3167.detailed_meaning: After Bharat has bowed to Sita and received her blessing, the whole scene settles into reverent silence. No one asks questions; no one interrupts. In that still, loving atmosphere, the boatman finds the courage to step forward and speak.
ramacharitamanas::3167.modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room where everyone has already cried. Nobody needs explanations. In that quiet, the person who speaks next does so with care, not noise.
ramacharitamanas::3167.insight: It shows how reverence creates silence first, then makes humble speech possible.

ramacharitamanas::3168.verse_sanskrit: नाथ साथ मुनिनाथ के मातु सकल पुर लोग। सेवक सेनप सचिव सब आए बिकल बियोग ॥
ramacharitamanas::3168.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! मुनिनाथ वशिष्ठजी के साथ सब माताएँ, नगरवासी, सेवक, सेनापति, मंत्री- सब आपके वियोग से व्याकुल होकर आए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3168.english_translation: O Lord, with the sage Vashishtha, all the mothers, the people of the city, servants, generals, and ministers have come, distressed by separation from you.
ramacharitamanas::3168.translation_literal: नाथ (Lord) / साथ (with) / मुनिनाथ (lord of sages, Vashishtha) / के (with) / मातु (mothers) / सकल (all) / पुर (city) / लोग (people) / सेवक (servants) / सेनपति (generals) / सचिव (ministers) / सब (all) / आए (came) / बिकल (distressed) / बियोग (separation)
ramacharitamanas::3168.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3168.essence: Ram's absence is felt by everyone who loves him.
ramacharitamanas::3168.simple_meaning: Everyone from the city has come, overwhelmed by your absence: the mothers, the people, the servants, the generals, and the ministers.
ramacharitamanas::3168.simple_insight: Separation can pull an entire community into one shared ache.
ramacharitamanas::3168.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the news and feeling of Ram's exile have spread through every layer of the city. Vashishtha, the mothers, officials, servants, and citizens all arrive in grief, showing how deeply Ram's absence wounds the whole kingdom.
ramacharitamanas::3168.modern_relevance: A family waiting in a hospital corridor, each person pretending to be steady while the same fear sits in everyone’s chest.
ramacharitamanas::3168.insight: It shifts attention from individual grief to the way one absence can unsettle an entire community.

ramacharitamanas::3169.verse_sanskrit: सीलसिंधु सुनि गुर आगवनू। सिय समीप राखे रिपुदवनू॥ चले सबेग रामु तेहि काला। धीर धरम धुर दीनदयाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3169.verse_hindi: गुरु का आगमन सुनकर शील के समुद्र श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सीताजी के पास शत्रुघ्नजी को रख दिया और वे परम धीर, धर्मधुरंधर, दीनदयालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी उसी समय वेग के साथ चल पड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::3169.english_translation: Hearing that the teacher had arrived, the ocean of virtue Ram placed Shatrughna beside Sita and quickly set out. At that moment, the compassionate one who bears the weight of righteousness went swiftly.
ramacharitamanas::3169.translation_literal: सीलसिंधु (ocean of virtue) / सुनि (hearing) / गुर (teacher) / आगवनू (arrival) / सिय (Sita) / समीप (near) / राखे (placed) / रिपुदवनू (Shatrughna, foe-destroyer) / चले (went) / सबेग (with speed) / रामु (Ram) / तेहि काला (at that moment) / धीर (steady) / धरम धुर (bearer of righteousness) / दीनदयाला (compassionate to the humble)
ramacharitamanas::3169.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3169.essence: Right conduct moves first, even in the middle of sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::3169.simple_meaning: Ram hears that his teacher has arrived, places Shatrughna by Sita, and immediately goes to greet the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::3169.simple_insight: Respect moves faster than hesitation when your teacher arrives.
ramacharitamanas::3169.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the household is already strained by separation and grief. When Ram hears that Guru Vashishtha has come, he does not delay or drift in emotion. He arranges protection for Sita and goes at once to greet the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::3169.modern_relevance: Your mentor texts that they’ve arrived early, and you stop what you’re doing. You don’t keep them waiting, because respect is shown in movement, not intention.
ramacharitamanas::3169.insight: It teaches you to respond to a rightful call immediately, while still protecting those in your care.

ramacharitamanas::3170.verse_sanskrit: गुरहि देखि सानुज अनुरागे। दंड प्रनाम करन प्रभु लागे॥ मुनिबर धाइ लिए उर लाई। प्रेम उमगि भेंटे दोउ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3170.verse_hindi: गुरुजी के दर्शन करके लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी प्रेम में भर गए और दण्डवत प्रणाम करने लगे। मुनिश्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी ने दौड़कर उन्हें हृदय से लगा लिया और प्रेम में उमँगकर वे दोनों भाइयों से मिले ॥
ramacharitamanas::3170.english_translation: Seeing their guru, Ram and Lakshman were filled with love and bowed fully. The best of sages rushed forward and embraced them to his heart. Overflowing with love, the two brothers met him.
ramacharitamanas::3170.translation_literal: गुरहि (the guru) / देखि (seeing) / सानुज (with the younger brother) / अनुरागे (were filled with love) / दंड (full-body) / प्रनाम (bowing) / करन (to do) / प्रभु (the Lord) / लागे (began) / मुनिबर (best of sages) / धाइ (running) / लिए (took) / उर (to the chest) / लाई (having placed) / प्रेम (love) / उमगि (overflowing) / भेंटे (met/embraced) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::3170.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3170.essence: Love deepens when humility and affection meet.
ramacharitamanas::3170.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman see their guru, bow deeply, and receive a warm embrace in return. Love moves both sides of the meeting.
ramacharitamanas::3170.simple_insight: Respect and affection are not opposites; true closeness often begins with humility.
ramacharitamanas::3170.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram and Lakshman meet their teacher Vashishtha after the pain of exile begins to unfold. The brothers bow in love, and the sage rushes to embrace them. The scene shows devotion flowing both ways.
ramacharitamanas::3170.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and see the teacher who changed your life. Before any words, your body lowers itself in gratitude, and the distance disappears in one hug.
ramacharitamanas::3170.insight: It teaches you that reverence can be intimate, and intimacy can still be respectful.

ramacharitamanas::3171.verse_sanskrit: प्रेम पुलकि केवट कहि नामू। कीन्ह दूरि तें दंड प्रनामू॥ राम सखा रिषि बरबस भेंटा। जनु महि लुठत सनेह समेटा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3171.verse_hindi: फिर प्रेम से पुलकित होकर केवट (निषादराज) ने अपना नाम लेकर दूर से ही वशिष्ठजी को दण्डवत प्रणाम किया। ऋषि वशिष्ठजी ने रामसखा जानकर उसको जबर्दस्ती हृदय से लगा लिया। मानो जमीन पर लोटते हुए प्रेम को समेट लिया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3171.english_translation: Then, filled with love and thrill, the boatman bowed from a distance, naming himself. Knowing him as Ram's friend, the sage Vasishtha pulled him into an embrace, as if gathering up love that had rolled on the ground.
ramacharitamanas::3171.translation_literal: प्रेम (with love) / पुलकि (thrilled, with goosebumps) / केवट (the boatman) / कहि (saying) / नामू (name) / कीन्ह (made) / दूरि तें (from a distance) / दंड प्रनामू (prostrated bow) / राम सखा (Ram's friend) / रिषि बरबस (the sage forcibly) / भेंटा (embraced) / जनु (as if) / महि (on the ground) / लुठत (rolling) / सनेह (love) / समेटा (gathered up)
ramacharitamanas::3171.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3171.essence: Love for Ram turns distance into belonging.
ramacharitamanas::3171.simple_meaning: The boatman bows to Vasishtha from afar, and Vasishtha embraces him warmly because he belongs to Ram's circle of love.
ramacharitamanas::3171.simple_insight: Devotion collapses distance and rank; sincere love is enough to be welcomed completely.
ramacharitamanas::3171.detailed_meaning: After Vasishtha arrives in Ayodhya, the boatman Kevat comes forward overwhelmed with love. He bows from a distance, and the sage immediately hugs him as Ram's friend. The scene shows how Ram's devotion makes even social distance disappear.
ramacharitamanas::3171.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a temple, a retreat, or a family gathering and feel no need to perform. They already feel familiar because your love for the same center has made you kin.
ramacharitamanas::3171.insight: It shifts attention from status to shared devotion, showing that belonging can be immediate and wholehearted.

ramacharitamanas::3172.verse_sanskrit: रघुपति भगति सुमंगल मूला। नभ सराहि सुर बरिसहिं फूला॥ एहि सम निपट नीच कोउ नाहीं। बड़ बसिष्ठ सम को जग माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3172.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी की भक्ति सुंदर मंगलों का मूल है, इस प्रकार कहकर सराहना करते हुए देवता आकाश से फूल बरसाने लगे। वे कहने लगे- जगत में इसके समान सर्वथा नीच कोई नहीं और वशिष्ठजी के समान बड़ा कौन है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3172.english_translation: Devotion to Raghupati is the root of all auspiciousness. Saying this in praise, the radiant beings showered flowers from the sky. They said, 'In the world there is none more lowly than this one, and none greater than Vashishtha.'
ramacharitamanas::3172.translation_literal: रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan, Ram) / भगति (devotion) / सुमंगल (most auspicious) / मूला (root, source) / नभ (sky) / सराहि (praising) / सुर (radiant beings) / बरिसहिं (rain) / फूला (flowers) / एहि (this) / सम (like, equal to) / निपट (utterly) / नीच (lowly) / कोउ (someone) / नाहीं (not) / बड़ (great) / बसिष्ठ (Vashishtha) / सम (like, equal to) / को (who) / जग (world) / माहीं (in)
ramacharitamanas::3172.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3172.essence: Devotion to Ram makes the overlooked one truly great.
ramacharitamanas::3172.simple_meaning: Devotion to Ram is the source of all good fortune. When that truth is praised, even the heavens respond with flowers.
ramacharitamanas::3172.simple_insight: Real greatness comes from loving Ram, not from status or pride.
ramacharitamanas::3172.detailed_meaning: After Vashishtha welcomes the Nishad king with joy, the scene turns into a blessing. The radiant beings in the sky praise what they see: devotion to Ram makes a person truly blessed, while outer rank means little.
ramacharitamanas::3172.modern_relevance: You watch someone quietly honor what is sacred while everyone else chases applause. The room feels different around them. That is the kind of greatness this verse points to.
ramacharitamanas::3172.insight: It shifts respect away from social rank and toward devotion as the real measure of a person.

ramacharitamanas::3173.verse_sanskrit: जेहि लखि लखनहु तें अधिक मिले मुदित मुनिराउ। सो सीतापति भजन को प्रगट प्रताप प्रभाउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3173.verse_hindi: जिस (निषाद) को देखकर मुनिराज वशिष्ठजी लक्ष्मणजी से भी अधिक उससे आनंदित होकर मिले। यह सब सीतापति श्री रामचन्द्रजी के भजन का प्रत्यक्ष प्रताप और प्रभाव है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3173.english_translation: Seeing him, the sage Vashishtha was even more delighted than he was with Lakshman. All of this is the clear power and influence of worshiping Sita's lord, Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3173.translation_literal: जेहि (whom) / लखि (seeing) / लखनहु तें (than Lakshman) / अधिक (more) / मिले (met) / मुदित (delighted) / मुनिराउ (the sage-king) / सो (that) / सीतापति (lord of Sita) / भजन (worship) / को (of) / प्रगट (manifest) / प्रताप (power) / प्रभाउ (influence)
ramacharitamanas::3173.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3173.essence: Devotion to Ram changes how the world receives you.
ramacharitamanas::3173.simple_meaning: Worship of Ram changes how people respond to you. Even a sage felt greater joy meeting this man than meeting Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::3173.simple_insight: Devotion softens the world around you and makes welcome appear where distance once stood.
ramacharitamanas::3173.detailed_meaning: At the riverbank, Nishadraj has just met the holy company around Ram. Vashishtha, the royal teacher, is unexpectedly overjoyed to greet him. The couplet explains that this welcome is not ordinary courtesy — it is the visible effect of Ram's worship.
ramacharitamanas::3173.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the tension drops before you speak. No performance can explain it — something steadier in you has already done the work.
ramacharitamanas::3173.insight: It shifts attention from social charm to the transforming force of devotion and character.

ramacharitamanas::3174.verse_sanskrit: आरत लोग राम सबु जाना। करुनाकर सुजान भगवाना॥ जो जेहि भायँ रहा अभिलाषी। तेहि तेहि कै तसि तसि रुख राखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3174.verse_hindi: दया की खान, सुजान भगवान श्री रामजी ने सब लोगों को दुःखी (मिलने के लिए व्याकुल) जाना। तब जो जिस भाव से मिलने का अभिलाषी था, उस-उस का उस-उस प्रकार का रुख रखते हुए (उसकी रुचि के अनुसार) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3174.english_translation: Lord Ram knew all the distressed people. The compassionate, wise Lord then met each person according to the desire in their heart.
ramacharitamanas::3174.translation_literal: आरत (distressed) / लोग (people) / राम (Ram) / सबु (all) / जाना (knew) / करुनाकर (compassionate one) / सुजान (wise) / भगवाना (Lord) // जो (who) / जेहि (according to whom) / भायँ (feeling, wish) / रहा (was staying) / अभिलाषी (desiring) / तेहि तेहि (to each one) / कै (of) / तसि तसि (such and such) / रुख (manner, turn) / राखी (kept)
ramacharitamanas::3174.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3174.essence: Compassion becomes real when it takes the shape of each heart.
ramacharitamanas::3174.simple_meaning: Ram sees every distressed person and responds in the way each heart is ready for. His compassion is personal, not one-size-fits-all.
ramacharitamanas::3174.simple_insight: You are not met as a crowd. You are met as you are.
ramacharitamanas::3174.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, people are coming to Ram with grief, longing, and confusion. Ram, the wise and compassionate one, does not answer them all the same way. He meets each person according to the longing already alive in that heart.
ramacharitamanas::3174.modern_relevance: You open up to a friend after a breakup, but what you need is not advice — just presence. Another person needs practical help. This verse says real care listens first, then responds.
ramacharitamanas::3174.insight: It teaches you to meet people by their actual need, not by your preferred style of helping.

ramacharitamanas::3175.verse_sanskrit: सानुज मिलि पल महुँ सब काहू। कीन्ह दूरि दुखु दारुन दाहू॥ यह बड़ि बात राम कै नाहीं। जिमि घट कोटि एक रबि छाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3175.verse_hindi: उन्होंने लक्ष्मणजी सहित पल भर में सब किसी से मिलकर उनके दुःख और कठिन संताप को दूर कर दिया। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के लिए यह कोई बड़ी बात नहीं है। जैसे करोड़ों घड़ों में एक ही सूर्य की (पृथक-पृथक) छाया (प्रतिबिम्ब) एक साथ ही दिखती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3175.english_translation: Together with Lakshman, he met everyone in a moment and removed their sorrow and burning pain. For Ram, this was no great feat, just as one sun is reflected in countless pots at once.
ramacharitamanas::3175.translation_literal: सानुज (with Lakshman) / मिलि (meeting) / पल महुँ (in a moment) / सब काहू (everyone) / कीन्ह (did) / दूरि (removed) / दुखु (sorrow) / दारुन (terrible) / दाहू (burning pain) / यह (this) / बड़ि बात (great matter) / राम कै (of Ram) / नाहीं (not) / जिमि (as) / घट (pots) / कोटि (crores) / एक (one) / रबि (sun) / छाहीं (shadow/reflection)
ramacharitamanas::3175.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3175.essence: True presence multiplies itself without losing anything.
ramacharitamanas::3175.simple_meaning: Ram, with Lakshman, quickly meets everyone and removes their suffering. The verse says this is natural for him, like one sun reflected in many pots.
ramacharitamanas::3175.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing that true care does not run out, even when many people need it at once.
ramacharitamanas::3175.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram has returned to meet the people who love him. With Lakshman beside him, he moves through the crowd and relieves their grief immediately. Tulsidas says this is effortless for Ram, like one sun appearing in many vessels.
ramacharitamanas::3175.modern_relevance: You walk into a family room after bad news, and everyone wants your attention at once. The verse reminds you that a steady presence can reach many people without being divided.
ramacharitamanas::3175.insight: It shifts attention from limited effort to expansive presence: one grounded person can calm many at once.

ramacharitamanas::3176.verse_sanskrit: मिलि केवटहि उमगि अनुरागा। पुरजन सकल सराहहिं भागा॥ देखीं राम दुखित महतारीं। जनु सुबेलि अवलीं हिम मारीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3176.verse_hindi: समस्त पुरवासी प्रेम में उमँगकर केवट से मिलकर (उसके) भाग्य की सराहना करते हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सब माताओं को दुःखी देखा। मानो सुंदर लताओं की पंक्तियों को पाला मार गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3176.english_translation: The townspeople, filled with love, praised Kevat's good fortune. Ram saw the mothers in sorrow, like rows of lovely vines struck by frost.
ramacharitamanas::3176.translation_literal: मिलि (meeting) / केवटहि (the boatman) / उमगि (overflowing) / अनुरागा (love) / पुरजन (townspeople) / सकल (all) / सराहहिं (praise) / भागा (fortune)॥ देखीं (saw) / राम (Ram) / दुखित (grieved) / महतारीं (the mothers) / जनु (as if) / सुबेलि (beautiful vines) / अवलीं (rows) / हिम (frost) / मारीं (struck)
ramacharitamanas::3176.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3176.essence: Joy and grief can share the same room.
ramacharitamanas::3176.simple_meaning: The people rejoice over Kevat's blessing, and Ram notices the sorrow of the mothers around him.
ramacharitamanas::3176.simple_insight: Love and grief can stand side by side in the same moment.
ramacharitamanas::3176.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank in Ayodhya's exile story, the townspeople celebrate Kevat's fortunate meeting with Ram, while Ram simultaneously sees the mothers' sorrow. The scene is moving, but it mainly carries the story forward into the next emotional meeting.
ramacharitamanas::3176.modern_relevance: At a family gathering, one person is being praised in the living room while another quietly wipes away tears in the kitchen. Both truths are real at once.
ramacharitamanas::3176.insight: It keeps attention on the emotional contrast in the scene rather than turning it into a general lesson.

ramacharitamanas::3177.verse_sanskrit: प्रथम राम भेंटी कैकेई। सरल सुभायँ भगति मति भेई॥ पग परि कीन्ह प्रबोधु बहोरी। काल करम बिधि सिर धरि खोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3177.verse_hindi: सबसे पहले रामजी कैकेयी से मिले और अपने सरल स्वभाव तथा भक्ति से उसकी बुद्धि को तर कर दिया। फिर चरणों में गिरकर काल, कर्म और विधाता के सिर दोष मढ़कर, श्री रामजी ने उनको सान्त्वना दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3177.english_translation: First, Ram met Kaikeyi. By his simple nature and loving devotion, he softened her mind. Then, bowing at her feet, he comforted her further, placing blame on time, karma, and fate.
ramacharitamanas::3177.translation_literal: प्रथम (first) / राम (Ram) / भेंटी (met) / कैकेई (Kaikeyi) / सरल (simple) / सुभायँ (by nature) / भगति (devotion) / मति (mind) / भेई (became)॥ / पग (feet) / परि (at) / कीन्ह (did) / प्रबोधु (comforting) / बहोरी (again) / काल (time) / करम (karma) / बिधि (fate) / सिर (head) / धरि (placing) / खोरी (fault)॥
ramacharitamanas::3177.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3177.essence: Gentleness can soften blame before blame hardens into ruin.
ramacharitamanas::3177.simple_meaning: Ram meets Kaikeyi with such gentleness that her mind softens. He even comforts her by shifting blame away from her and onto time, karma, and fate.
ramacharitamanas::3177.simple_insight: You do not always need force; sometimes steady kindness changes the whole mood.
ramacharitamanas::3177.detailed_meaning: After the exile has shattered the palace, Ram goes first to Kaikeyi. Instead of resentment, he brings simplicity and compassion. He bows, comforts her, and protects her from the full weight of guilt in that painful family moment.
ramacharitamanas::3177.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room after a family argument, and everyone is waiting for the next sharp word. Instead, you lower your voice, sit down, and make it safe to breathe again.
ramacharitamanas::3177.insight: It teaches you to respond to hurt with composure, easing conflict instead of feeding it.

ramacharitamanas::3178.verse_sanskrit: भेटीं रघुबर मातु सब करि प्रबोधु परितोषु। अंब ईस आधीन जगु काहु न देइअ दोषु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3178.verse_hindi: फिर श्री रघुनाथजी सब माताओं से मिले। उन्होंने सबको समझा-बुझाकर संतोष कराया कि हे माता! जगत ईश्वर के अधीन है। किसी को भी दोष नहीं देना चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3178.english_translation: Then Raghubar met all the mothers, comforted them, and calmed their grief. "Mother, the world is under the divine's rule; do not blame anyone."
ramacharitamanas::3178.translation_literal: भेटीं (met) / रघुबर (Raghubar, Ram) / मातु (mothers) / सब (all) / करि (having done) / प्रबोधु (comforting, counsel) / परितोषु (satisfaction, calming) / अंब (mother) / ईस (the divine) / आधीन (under control) / जगु (the world) / काहु (to anyone) / न (not) / देइअ (should be given) / दोषु (blame)
ramacharitamanas::3178.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3178.essence: When you see a larger order, blame loses its grip.
ramacharitamanas::3178.simple_meaning: Ram comforts his grieving mothers and tells them not to blame anyone, because the world moves under the divine's control.
ramacharitamanas::3178.simple_insight: Blame softens when you remember that not everything is in human hands.
ramacharitamanas::3178.detailed_meaning: After meeting Kaikeyi and the other mothers in Ayodhya, Ram gently consoles them. He does not argue or accuse; he steadies their hearts by pointing them toward a larger order, where blame has no lasting use.
ramacharitamanas::3178.modern_relevance: You replay a family argument at 1 a.m., searching for who ruined everything. This verse asks you to stop feeding blame and look at the larger forces at work.
ramacharitamanas::3178.insight: It shifts the mind from accusation to acceptance, helping you respond with calm instead of resentment.

ramacharitamanas::3179.verse_sanskrit: गुरतिय पद बंदे दुहु भाईं। सहित बिप्रतिय जे सँग आईं॥ गंग गौरिसम सब सनमानीं। देहिं असीस मुदित मृदु बानीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3179.verse_hindi: फिर दोनों भाइयों ने ब्राह्मणों की स्त्रियों सहित- जो भरतजी के साथ आई थीं, गुरुजी की पत्नी अरुंधतीजी के चरणों की वंदना की और उन सबका गंगाजी तथा गौरीजी के समान सम्मान किया। वे सब आनंदित होकर कोमल वाणी से आशीर्वाद देने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3179.english_translation: Then both brothers bowed to the wives of the gurus and to the women who had come with Bharata. They honored them all like Ganga and Gauri, and the women, delighted, gave them gentle blessings.
ramacharitamanas::3179.translation_literal: गुरतिय (wives of the guru) / पद (feet) / बंदे (bowed) / दुहु (both) / भाईं (brothers) / सहित (along with) / बिप्रतिय (wives of the brahmins) / जे (who) / सँग (with) / आईं (came) / गंग (Ganga) / गौरिसम (like Gauri) / सब (all) / सनमानीं (honored) / देहिं (gave) / असीस (blessings) / मुदित (delighted) / मृदु (gentle) / बानीं (words)
ramacharitamanas::3179.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3179.essence: Humility turns a formal meeting into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3179.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman show deep respect to the women who came with Bharata and to the guru's wife. Those women, pleased by their humility, bless them warmly.
ramacharitamanas::3179.simple_insight: True greatness shows itself in how gently you honor others.
ramacharitamanas::3179.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the brothers meet the family and return with Bharata’s party, Ram and Lakshman bow not only to elders but also to the women present. Their humility wins immediate blessing and affection in a tense family home.
ramacharitamanas::3179.modern_relevance: You enter a room where the people around your partner are waiting, and you choose respect over self-importance. That small bow changes the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::3179.insight: It teaches you to treat every person in the room with equal dignity, not just the ones with status.

ramacharitamanas::3180.verse_sanskrit: गहि पद लगे सुमित्रा अंका। जनु भेंटी संपति अति रंका॥ पुनि जननी चरननि दोउ भ्राता। परे पेम ब्याकुल सब गाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3180.verse_hindi: तब दोनों भाई पैर पकड़कर सुमित्राजी की गोद में जा चिपटे। मानो किसी अत्यन्त दरिद्र की सम्पत्ति से भेंट हो गई हो। फिर दोनों भाई माता कौसल्याजी के चरणों में गिर पड़े। प्रेम के मारे उनके सारे अंग शिथिल हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3180.english_translation: Then both brothers clung to Sumitra's lap, as if a poor man had suddenly found immense wealth. Then the two brothers fell at their mother Kaushalya's feet, their bodies limp with love.
ramacharitamanas::3180.translation_literal: गहि (grasping) / पद (feet) / लगे (clung) / सुमित्रा (Sumitra) / अंका (lap) / जनु (as if) / भेंटी (met) / संपति (wealth) / अति (very) / रंका (poor man) / पुनि (then) / जननी (mother) / चरननि (feet) / दोउ (both) / भ्राता (brothers) / परे (fell) / पेम (love) / ब्याकुल (overwhelmed) / सब (all) / गाता (bodies)
ramacharitamanas::3180.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3180.essence: Deep love makes strength dissolve into tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::3180.simple_meaning: The brothers rush to their mothers with overwhelming love and gratitude. Their reunion is so moving that their bodies seem to go weak.
ramacharitamanas::3180.simple_insight: Love can make even strength soften into surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3180.detailed_meaning: After Ram's return to Ayodhya, the brothers first greet the women and elders who have carried their exile with them. Here, Bharata and Lakshman throw themselves into Sumitra's lap and at Kaushalya's feet, and the whole family scene turns into tears and tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::3180.modern_relevance: You finally see your mother after months away, and all the words disappear. The body knows what the heart cannot explain.
ramacharitamanas::3180.insight: It shifts attention from formal reunion to the physical language of gratitude and love.

ramacharitamanas::3181.verse_sanskrit: अति अनुराग अंब उर लाए। नयन सनेह सलिल अन्हवाए॥ तेहि अवसर कर हरष बिषादू। किमि कबि कहै मूक जिमि स्वादू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3181.verse_hindi: बड़े ही स्नेह से माता ने उन्हें हृदय से लगा लिया और नेत्रों से बहे हुए प्रेमाश्रुओं के जल से उन्हें नहला दिया। उस समय के हर्ष और विषाद को कवि कैसे कहे? जैसे गूँगा स्वाद को कैसे बतावे? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3181.english_translation: With deep affection, Mother held them to her heart and bathed them in the tears of love from her eyes. How can a poet describe the joy and sorrow of that moment? Like a mute person describing taste.
ramacharitamanas::3181.translation_literal: अति (very) / अनुराग (deep affection) / अंब (mother) / उर (heart) / लाए (brought, held close) / नयन (eyes) / सनेह (love) / सलिल (water) / अन्हवाए (bathed) / तेहि (that) / अवसर (moment) / कर (of) / हरष (joy) / बिषादू (sorrow) / किमि (how) / कबि (poet) / कहै (can say) / मूक (mute) / जिमि (like) / स्वादू (taste)
ramacharitamanas::3181.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3181.essence: Love can flood you with joy and sorrow at once.
ramacharitamanas::3181.simple_meaning: Kaushalya holds Ram and Lakshman close, crying tears of love. The moment is so full of mixed joy and sorrow that words cannot capture it.
ramacharitamanas::3181.simple_insight: Some reunions are too full for language; love and grief can arrive together.
ramacharitamanas::3181.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have returned to Ayodhya after exile, and Kaushalya pulls them into her heart. Her tears are both welcome and painful, because joy has come wrapped in years of separation. The poet pauses because the feeling exceeds speech.
ramacharitamanas::3181.modern_relevance: You finally see someone you have missed for years, and you laugh while crying at the same time. No explanation fits that kind of relief.
ramacharitamanas::3181.insight: It teaches you that the deepest moments of love may also carry grief and cannot be neatly explained.

ramacharitamanas::3182.verse_sanskrit: मिलि जननिहि सानुज रघुराऊ। गुर सन कहेउ कि धारिअ पाऊ॥ पुरजन पाइ मुनीस नियोगू। जल थल तकि तकि उतरेउ लोगू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3182.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी ने छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित माता कौसल्या से मिलकर गुरु से कहा कि आश्रम पर पधारिए। तदनन्तर मुनीश्वर वशिष्ठजी की आज्ञा पाकर अयोध्यावासी सब लोग जल और थल का सुभीता देख-देखकर उतर गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3182.english_translation: Raghunath met his mother with Lakshman beside him and asked the guru to come in. Then, after the sage Vashishtha's command, the people of Ayodhya began descending, choosing paths through water and land.
ramacharitamanas::3182.translation_literal: मिलि (meeting) / जननिहि (the mother) / सानुज (with the younger brother) / रघुराऊ (Raghunath) / गुर (the teacher) / सन (to) / कहेउ (said) / कि (that) / धारिअ (please bring) / पाऊ (the feet) ॥ पुरजन (townspeople) / पाइ (having received) / मुनीस (of the sage) / नियोगू (instruction) / जल (water) / थल (land) / तकि तकि (looking again and again) / उतरेउ (descended) / लोगू (the people) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3182.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3182.essence: The homecoming continues, and the whole city follows.
ramacharitamanas::3182.simple_meaning: Ram meets his mother with Lakshman beside him, invites the teacher, and the people of Ayodhya follow the sage's guidance to go down by land and water.
ramacharitamanas::3182.simple_insight: A family reunion and a public movement unfold together, but the verse mainly moves the scene forward.
ramacharitamanas::3182.detailed_meaning: Ram has returned with Lakshman and met Kaushalya. He asks Vashishtha to come forward, and the people of Ayodhya, guided by the sage, begin descending toward the next place. The verse is transitional, carrying the gathering into motion.
ramacharitamanas::3182.modern_relevance: A group finally reaches the destination after a long trip, and everyone is still figuring out where to stand, who to follow, and what comes next.
ramacharitamanas::3182.insight: It shifts attention from reunion to the next step in the journey.

ramacharitamanas::3183.verse_sanskrit: महिसुर मंत्री मातु गुरु गने लोग लिए साथ। पावन आश्रम गवनु किए भरत लखन रघुनाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3183.verse_hindi: ब्राह्मण, मंत्री, माताएँ और गुरु आदि गिने-चुने लोगों को साथ लिए हुए, भरतजी, लक्ष्मणजी और श्री रघुनाथजी पवित्र आश्रम को चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::3183.english_translation: With a few selected people — brahmins, ministers, mothers, and the teacher — Bharat, Lakshman, and Raghunath went to the sacred hermitage.
ramacharitamanas::3183.translation_literal: महिसुर (brahmins) / मंत्री (ministers) / मातु (mothers) / गुरु (teacher) / गने (counted) / लोग (people) / लिए (taking) / साथ (together) / पावन (sacred) / आश्रम (hermitage) / गवनु (going) / किए (did) / भरत (Bharat) / लखन (Lakshman) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::3183.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3183.essence: The party moves together toward the hermitage.
ramacharitamanas::3183.simple_meaning: Bharat, Lakshman, and Ram set out for the hermitage with a small group of elders and family members.
ramacharitamanas::3183.simple_insight: The journey matters, but this line is mainly moving the story forward.
ramacharitamanas::3183.detailed_meaning: Bharat has come to meet Ram in the forest, and the family closes in around the reunion. With brahmins, ministers, mothers, and Guru Vashistha accompanying them, Bharat, Lakshman, and Ram walk toward the sacred hermitage. The verse simply marks the procession.
ramacharitamanas::3183.modern_relevance: A group of relatives and elders quietly walks with you to a place that matters. The moment feels important, but this line is only the movement into it.
ramacharitamanas::3183.insight: It keeps attention on the scene’s transition rather than on a teaching.

ramacharitamanas::3184.verse_sanskrit: सीय आइ मुनिबर पग लागी। उचित असीस लही मन मागी॥ गुरपतिनिहि मुनितियन्ह समेता। मिली पेमु कहि जाइ न जेता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3184.verse_hindi: सीताजी आकर मुनि श्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी के चरणों लगीं और उन्होंने मन माँगी उचित आशीष पाई। फिर मुनियों की स्त्रियों सहित गुरु पत्नी अरुन्धतीजी से मिलीं। उनका जितना प्रेम था, वह कहा नहीं जाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3184.english_translation: Sita came and bowed at the feet of the noble sage, receiving the blessings her heart desired. Then, along with the wives of the sages, she met the guru’s wife Arundhati. Their affection was beyond words.
ramacharitamanas::3184.translation_literal: सीय (Sita) / आइ (came) / मुनिबर (best of sages) / पग (feet) / लागी (bowed) / उचित (proper) / असीस (blessing) / लही (received) / मन (mind/heart) / मागी (desired)॥ / गुरपतिनिहि (guru's wife) / मुनितियन्ह (with the wives of sages) / समेता (together) / मिली (met) / पेमु (love) / कहि (say) / जाइ (can be gone/told) / न (not) / जेता (as much) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3184.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3184.essence: Humility receives blessings, and reverence turns meeting into love.
ramacharitamanas::3184.simple_meaning: Sita greets the sages and their wives with humility, receives the blessings she hopes for, and shares a love so deep it cannot be measured.
ramacharitamanas::3184.simple_insight: True grace often begins with humility, and love grows quietly in simple acts of respect.
ramacharitamanas::3184.detailed_meaning: After Ram, Lakshman, and Bharata arrive at the sage’s hermitage, Sita enters with reverence. She bows to Vashishtha, receives his blessing, and then meets Arundhati and the sages’ wives. The scene shows her gentle dignity and the warmth surrounding Ram’s return.
ramacharitamanas::3184.modern_relevance: You walk into a family gathering after a long separation, greet the elders first, and feel the room soften around you. Respect opens the door to affection.
ramacharitamanas::3184.insight: It shifts attention from status to reverence, showing how respectful conduct creates trust and closeness.

ramacharitamanas::3185.verse_sanskrit: बंदि बंदि पग सिय सबही के। आसिरबचन लहे प्रिय जी के। सासु सकल सब सीयँ निहारीं। मूदे नयन सहमि सुकुमारीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3185.verse_hindi: सीताजी ने सभी के चरणों की अलग-अलग वंदना करके अपने हृदय को प्रिय (अनुकूल) लगने वाले आशीर्वाद पाए। जब सुकुमारी सीताजी ने सब सासुओं को देखा, तब उन्होंने सहमकर अपनी आँखें बंद कर लीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3185.english_translation: Sita bowed to each of them and received the blessings most dear to her heart. When the delicate Sita saw all her mothers-in-law, she closed her eyes in modest fear.
ramacharitamanas::3185.translation_literal: बंदि बंदि (bowing again and again) / पग (feet) / सिय (Sita) / सबही के (of everyone) / आसिरबचन (blessings) / लहे (received) / प्रिय जी के (dear to the heart) / सासु (mothers-in-law) / सकल (all) / सब (all) / सीयँ (Sita) / निहारीं (saw) / मूदे (closed) / नयन (eyes) / सहमि (startled, shy) / सुकुमारीं (delicate one)
ramacharitamanas::3185.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3185.essence: Grace begins with bowing before you belong.
ramacharitamanas::3185.simple_meaning: Sita respectfully greets everyone, receives their blessings, and lowers her eyes in shy modesty when she sees her mothers-in-law.
ramacharitamanas::3185.simple_insight: Humility can be quiet and graceful. Respect softens fear and makes a new place feel safer.
ramacharitamanas::3185.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Sita enters her new home after the journey with Ram and Lakshman. She greets the elders one by one, takes their blessings, and then feels shy before the queens who will become her mothers-in-law. The scene shows her gentle dignity.
ramacharitamanas::3185.modern_relevance: You walk into your partner’s family home for the first time, trying to remember every name and every custom. Sita’s grace is in that careful, humble pause.
ramacharitamanas::3185.insight: It teaches you to meet new relationships with respect first, not self-display.

ramacharitamanas::3186.verse_sanskrit: परीं बधिक बस मनहुँ मरालीं। काह कीन्ह करतार कुचालीं॥ तिन्ह सिय निरखि निपट दुखु पावा। सो सबु सहिअ जो दैउ सहावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3186.verse_hindi: (सासुओं की बुरी दशा देखकर) उन्हें ऐसा प्रतीत हुआ मानो राजहंसिनियाँ बधिक के वश में पड़ गई हों। (मन में सोचने लगीं कि) कुचाली विधाता ने क्या कर डाला? उन्होंने भी सीताजी को देखकर बड़ा दुःख पाया। (सोचा) जो कुछ दैव सहावे, वह सब सहना ही पड़ता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3186.english_translation: Seeing the in-laws in distress, it seemed to them as if swans had fallen into the hands of a hunter. They thought, “What has the creator done in this crooked way?” Seeing Sita, they felt deep sorrow too. “Whatever fate permits must be borne.”
ramacharitamanas::3186.translation_literal: परीं (appeared) / बधिक (hunter) / बस (under the control) / मनहुँ (as if) / मरालीं (swans) / काह (what) / कीन्ह (did) / करतार (creator) / कुचालीं (crooked act) / तिन्ह (they) / सिय (Sita) / निरखि (seeing) / निपट (very) / दुखु (sorrow) / पावा (felt) / सो (that) / सबु (all) / सहिअ (must be borne) / जो (whatever) / दैउ (fate) / सहावा (causes to be borne)
ramacharitamanas::3186.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3186.essence: Some pain cannot be fixed; it can only be carried.
ramacharitamanas::3186.simple_meaning: The elders feel grief on seeing Sita and think that whatever life brings must be endured.
ramacharitamanas::3186.simple_insight: Some sorrows are simply borne, not solved.
ramacharitamanas::3186.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita has returned to her new household after exile begins. Her in-laws look at her and feel as helpless as swans trapped by a hunter. Their sorrow deepens into quiet resignation: whatever the larger order allows must be endured.
ramacharitamanas::3186.modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed and realize there is nothing clever to say. Sometimes love means staying present with what cannot be changed.
ramacharitamanas::3186.insight: It shifts the mind from resistance to dignified endurance.

ramacharitamanas::3187.verse_sanskrit: जनकसुता तब उर धरि धीरा। नील नलिन लोयन भरि नीरा॥ मिली सकल सासुन्ह सिय जाई। तेहि अवसर करुना महि छाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3187.verse_hindi: तब जानकीजी हृदय में धीरज धरकर, नील कमल के समान नेत्रों में जल भरकर, सब सासुओं से जाकर मिलीं। उस समय पृथ्वी पर करुणा (करुण रस) छा गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3187.english_translation: Then Janaki gathered courage in her heart, filled her lotus-like eyes with tears, and went to meet all her mothers-in-law. At that moment, compassion spread over the earth.
ramacharitamanas::3187.translation_literal: जनकसुता (Janak's daughter) / तब (then) / उर (heart) / धरि (holding) / धीरा (courage) / नील (blue) / नलिन (lotus) / लोयन (eyes) / भरि (filling) / नीरा (water/tears) / मिली (met) / सकल (all) / सासुन्ह (mothers-in-law) / सिय (Sita) / जाई (going) / तेहि (that) / अवसर (moment) / करुना (compassion) / महि (earth) / छाई (spread)
ramacharitamanas::3187.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3187.essence: Courage can look like gentle tears and respectful steps.
ramacharitamanas::3187.simple_meaning: Sita steadies herself, wipes her fear into tears, and goes to meet her mothers-in-law with humility and grace.
ramacharitamanas::3187.simple_insight: Even in grief, you can move with dignity and tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::3187.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita has just entered a painful new household after leaving home. She gathers courage, meets her mothers-in-law one by one, and her humility softens the whole scene into compassion.
ramacharitamanas::3187.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone already knows the tension, and your throat tightens. Still, you smile, bow, and meet each person gently anyway.
ramacharitamanas::3187.insight: It teaches you to answer discomfort with grace instead of defensiveness.

ramacharitamanas::3188.verse_sanskrit: लागि लागि पग सबनि सिय भेंटति अति अनुराग। हृदयँ असीसहिं पेम बस रहिअहु भरी सोहाग ॥
ramacharitamanas::3188.verse_hindi: सीताजी सबके पैरों लग-लगकर अत्यन्त प्रेम से मिल रही हैं और सब सासुएँ स्नेहवश हृदय से आशीर्वाद दे रही हैं कि तुम सुहाग से भरी रहो (अर्थात सदा सौभाग्यवती रहो) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3188.english_translation: Sita lovingly touches everyone's feet, and all the queens bless her from their hearts: “May you always remain blessed in marriage.”
ramacharitamanas::3188.translation_literal: लागि लागि (again and again) / पग (feet) / सबनि (of all) / सिय (Sita) / भेंटति (meeting, touching) / अति (very) / अनुराग (loving affection) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / असीसहिं (they bless) / पेम (love) / बस (because of) / रहिअहु (may you remain) / भरी (full) / सोहाग (married good fortune)
ramacharitamanas::3188.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3188.essence: Humility invites blessing faster than rank ever could.
ramacharitamanas::3188.simple_meaning: Sita greets every queen with deep affection, touching their feet, and they bless her warmly in return.
ramacharitamanas::3188.simple_insight: Love moves in both directions when humility meets care.
ramacharitamanas::3188.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita enters the royal household after exile is decided. The queens are overwhelmed by tenderness, and Sita responds with complete humility. This verse captures that exchange of respect and blessing before Vashishtha begins speaking.
ramacharitamanas::3188.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where the people who should have been formal with you suddenly become tender. A respectful gesture opens the door to blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3188.insight: It shows how humility can soften status and turn greeting into grace.

ramacharitamanas::3189.verse_sanskrit: बिकल सनेहँ सीय सब रानीं। बैठन सबहि कहेउ गुर ग्यानीं॥ कहि जग गति मायिक मुनिनाथा॥ कहे कछुक परमारथ गाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3189.verse_hindi: सीताजी और सब रानियाँ स्नेह के मारे व्याकुल हैं। तब ज्ञानी गुरु ने सबको बैठ जाने के लिए कहा। फिर मुनिनाथ वशिष्ठजी ने जगत की गति को मायिक कहकर (अर्थात जगत माया का है, इसमें कुछ भी नित्य नहीं है, ऐसा कहकर) कुछ परमार्थ की कथाएँ (बातें) कहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3189.english_translation: Sita and all the queens were overcome with emotion. Then the wise teacher asked everyone to sit down. Vashishtha, the sage among sages, spoke of the world's changing nature as illusory and then said a few words about ultimate reality.
ramacharitamanas::3189.translation_literal: बिकल (overcome) / सनेहँ (with affection) / सीय (Sita) / सब (all) / रानीं (queens) / बैठन (to sit) / सबहि (everyone) / कहेउ (said) / गुर (teacher) / ग्यानीं (wise one) / कहि (saying) / जग (world) / गति (course/nature) / मायिक (illusory) / मुनिनाथा (lord of sages) / कहे (said) / कछुक (some) / परमारथ (ultimate reality) / गाथा (verses/stories)
ramacharitamanas::3189.speaker: Vashishtha
ramacharitamanas::3189.essence: What feels permanent is only part of a changing world.
ramacharitamanas::3189.simple_meaning: Sita and the queens are overwhelmed with feeling. Vashishtha settles everyone down and speaks about how the world keeps changing, then turns to deeper spiritual truth.
ramacharitamanas::3189.simple_insight: Even in grief, there is a steadier way to see what is happening.
ramacharitamanas::3189.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the palace is heavy with emotion after Sita's farewell. Sita and the queens are shaken by love and sorrow, and Vashishtha, the family teacher, asks everyone to sit and listen. He begins to lift their minds from loss to a larger understanding.
ramacharitamanas::3189.modern_relevance: You are in a room where everyone is crying after bad news, and someone finally says, sit down, breathe, and see this clearly before the panic spreads.
ramacharitamanas::3189.insight: It shifts the mind from raw feeling to a wider view that can hold grief without being swallowed by it.

ramacharitamanas::3190.verse_sanskrit: नृप कर सुरपुर गवनु सुनावा। सुनि रघुनाथ दुसह दुखु पावा॥ मरन हेतु निज नेहु बिचारी। भे अति बिकल धीर धुर धारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3190.verse_hindi: तदनन्तर वशिष्ठजी ने राजा दशरथजी के स्वर्ग गमन की बात सुनाई। जिसे सुनकर रघुनाथजी ने दुःसह दुःख पाया और अपने प्रति उनके स्नेह को उनके मरने का कारण विचारकर धीरधुरन्धर श्री रामचन्द्रजी अत्यन्त व्याकुल हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3190.english_translation: Vashistha announced King Dasharatha's passing to the higher realm. Hearing it, Raghunath felt unbearable grief. Thinking of the love Dasharatha held for him as the cause of his death, the steady one became deeply distressed.
ramacharitamanas::3190.translation_literal: नृप (king) / कर (of) / सुरपुर (higher realm) / गवनु (going) / सुनावा (announced) / सुनि (hearing) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / दुसह (unbearable) / दुखु (grief) / पावा (felt) / मरन (death) / हेतु (cause) / निज (own) / नेहु (love) / बिचारी (thinking) / भे (became) / अति (very) / बिकल (distressed) / धीर धुर धारी (the steady one who bears the heaviest burden)
ramacharitamanas::3190.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3190.essence: Steadiness does not cancel grief when love is real.
ramacharitamanas::3190.simple_meaning: Dasharath's death is announced, and Ram is overwhelmed with grief. He sees his father's love for him as part of what led to that death.
ramacharitamanas::3190.simple_insight: Love makes loss sharper, not smaller. Grief is not weakness; it is the cost of being deeply held.
ramacharitamanas::3190.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Vashistha tells the court that Dasharath has gone to the higher realm. Ram, who has endured exile with composure, is shaken. He thinks of his father's love and immediately feels the weight of that bond as grief.
ramacharitamanas::3190.modern_relevance: You get the call late at night, and the room goes quiet before anyone speaks. What hurts most is not only the loss — it is remembering how much they loved you.
ramacharitamanas::3190.insight: It normalises grief as the natural response to deep attachment, not as a failure of strength.

ramacharitamanas::3191.verse_sanskrit: कुलिस कठोर सुनत कटु बानी। बिलपत लखन सीय सब रानी॥ सोक बिकल अति सकल समाजू। मानहूँ राजु अकाजेउ आजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3191.verse_hindi: वज्र के समान कठोर, कड़वी वाणी सुनकर लक्ष्मणजी, सीताजी और सब रानियाँ विलाप करने लगीं। सारा समाज शोक से अत्यन्त व्याकुल हो गया! मानो राजा आज ही मरे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::3191.english_translation: Hearing the words, hard as thunderbolt and bitter as poison, Lakshman, Sita, and all the queens began to wail. The whole assembly was shaken with grief, as if the king had died that very day.
ramacharitamanas::3191.translation_literal: कुलिस (thunderbolt) / कठोर (hard) / सुनत (hearing) / कटु (bitter) / बानी (words) / बिलपत (wailing) / लखन (Lakshman) / सीय (Sita) / सब (all) / रानीं (queens) / सोक (grief) / बिकल (shaken) / अति (very) / सकल (whole) / समाजू (assembly) / मानहूँ (as if) / राजु (king) / अकाजेउ (had died) / आजू (today)
ramacharitamanas::3191.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3191.essence: Grief can strike a whole gathering at once.
ramacharitamanas::3191.simple_meaning: The news lands like a blow. Lakshman, Sita, the queens, and everyone else break into grief, as if the king has just died.
ramacharitamanas::3191.simple_insight: Some losses hit so hard that the whole room grieves at once.
ramacharitamanas::3191.detailed_meaning: After Vashishtha has spoken of Dasharath's passing, the shock spreads through the palace. Lakshman, Sita, the queens, and the entire gathering collapse into lamentation. The verse is a scene of collective grief, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3191.modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after one message changes everything. Nobody knows what to say first; the shock arrives before the words do.
ramacharitamanas::3191.insight: It captures how grief spreads through a shared space before anyone can think clearly.

ramacharitamanas::3192.verse_sanskrit: मुनिबर बहुरि राम समुझाए। सहित समाज सुसरित नहाए॥ ब्रत निरंबु तेहि दिन प्रभु कीन्हा। मुनिहु कहें जलु काहुँ न लीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3192.verse_hindi: फिर मुनिश्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी ने श्री रामजी को समझाया। तब उन्होंने समाज सहित श्रेष्ठ नदी मंदाकिनीजी में स्नान किया। उस दिन प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने निर्जल व्रत किया। मुनि वशिष्ठजी के कहने पर भी किसी ने जल ग्रहण नहीं किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3192.english_translation: Then the sage Vashistha again explained things to Ram. Together with the group, they bathed in the sacred Mandakini River. That day the Lord kept a waterless fast, and even when the sage said to take water, no one did.
ramacharitamanas::3192.translation_literal: मुनिबर (great sage) / बहुरि (again) / राम (Ram) / समुझाए (explained) / सहित (together with) / समाज (group) / सुसरित (beautiful river) / नहाए (bathed) / ब्रत (vow/fast) / निरंबु (without water) / तेहि दिन (that day) / प्रभु (Lord) / कीन्हा (did) / मुनिहु (even the sage) / कहें (said) / जलु (water) / काहुँ (anyone) / न (not) / लीन्हा (took)
ramacharitamanas::3192.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3192.essence: Discipline means keeping the vow even when relief is available.
ramacharitamanas::3192.simple_meaning: Ram follows Vashistha’s guidance, bathes with the gathered group, and keeps a strict fast without water for the day.
ramacharitamanas::3192.simple_insight: Real discipline shows up in small, concrete refusals, not just in grand intentions.
ramacharitamanas::3192.detailed_meaning: After hearing of Dasharath’s death, Ram is still in the middle of ritual and grief. Vashistha guides him again, the group bathes together in the Mandakini, and Ram keeps a waterless fast. Even the sage’s instruction to drink is set aside.
ramacharitamanas::3192.modern_relevance: You promised yourself one sober day, one honest conversation, one hour without your phone — and then the old pull came back. Discipline is what you keep when comfort asks to be excused.
ramacharitamanas::3192.insight: It shifts attention from intention alone to the bodily practice that proves commitment.

ramacharitamanas::3193.verse_sanskrit: भोरु भएँ रघुनंदनहि जो मुनि आयसु दीन्ह। श्रद्धा भगति समेत प्रभु सो सबु सादरु कीन्ह ॥
ramacharitamanas::3193.verse_hindi: दूसरे दिन सबेरा होने पर मुनि वशिष्ठजी ने श्री रघुनाथजी को जो-जो आज्ञा दी, वह सब कार्य प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने श्रद्धा-भक्ति सहित आदर के साथ किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3193.english_translation: At dawn, Raghunandan did everything the sage instructed, with reverence and devotion.
