ramacharitamanas::3193.translation_literal: भोरु (dawn) / भएँ (having become) / रघुनंदनहि (to Raghunandan) / जो (whatever) / मुनि (sage) / आयसु (command) / दीन्ह (gave) / श्रद्धा (reverence) / भगति (devotion) / समेत (together with) / प्रभु (Lord) / सो (that) / सबु (all) / सादरु (respectfully) / कीन्ह (did)
ramacharitamanas::3193.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3193.essence: Devotion makes even duty feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3193.simple_meaning: At daybreak, Ram carried out every instruction from Vashishtha with reverence and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3193.simple_insight: True greatness still bows to guidance and does the needed work fully.
ramacharitamanas::3193.detailed_meaning: After the night of grief, morning comes in Ayodhya. Vashishtha gives Ram the rites and instructions for his father’s passing, and Ram carries them out with complete reverence. The verse shows his obedience, tenderness, and devotion at a moment of loss.
ramacharitamanas::3193.modern_relevance: You are exhausted, grieving, and still have to do what must be done: call the relatives, sign the papers, make the arrangements. This verse honours the dignity of doing it with care.
ramacharitamanas::3193.insight: It shifts action from reluctant compliance to respectful, wholehearted service.

ramacharitamanas::3194.verse_sanskrit: करि पितु क्रिया बेद जसि बरनी। भे पुनीत पातक तम तरनी॥ जासु नाम पावक अघ तूला। सुमिरत सकल सुमंगल मूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3194.verse_hindi: वेदों में जैसा कहा गया है, उसी के अनुसार पिता की क्रिया करके, पाप रूपी अंधकार के नष्ट करने वाले सूर्यरूप श्री रामचन्द्रजी शुद्ध हुए! जिनका नाम पाप रूपी रूई के (तुरंत जला डालने के) लिए अग्नि है और जिनका स्मरण मात्र समस्त शुभ मंगलों का मूल है, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3194.english_translation: Having performed his father's rites as the Vedas prescribe, Rama became purified, the destroyer of the darkness of sin. His name is fire for the cotton of wrongdoing; remembering him is the root of all auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::3194.translation_literal: करि (having done) / पितु (father's) / क्रिया (rites) / बेद (Vedas) / जसि (as) / बरनी (described) / भे (became) / पुनीत (purified) / पातक (sins) / तम (darkness) / तरनी (sun) / जासु (whose) / नाम (name) / पावक (fire) / अघ (wrongdoing) / तूला (cotton) / सुमिरत (remembering) / सकल (all) / सुमंगल (auspiciousness) / मूला (root)
ramacharitamanas::3194.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3194.essence: Right action in sorrow can itself become purification.
ramacharitamanas::3194.simple_meaning: Ram completed his father's funeral rites exactly as the sacred law requires, and that act purified him. His name burns away wrongdoing and becomes the source of every good beginning.
ramacharitamanas::3194.simple_insight: Doing the hard duty well can leave you clearer, lighter, and more whole.
ramacharitamanas::3194.detailed_meaning: After Dasharath's death, Ram performs the final rites with complete obedience to sacred duty. The moment is not just grief; it is purification. Tulsidas turns the scene into praise of Ram's name, showing how devotion and right action cleanse the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3194.modern_relevance: You stand at a hospital corridor after a parent dies, signing papers, arranging the last rites, holding yourself together. Doing what must be done can become its own cleansing.
ramacharitamanas::3194.insight: It shifts attention from grief alone to the dignity of faithful action under grief.

ramacharitamanas::3195.verse_sanskrit: सुद्ध सो भयउ साधु संमत अस। तीरथ आवाहन सुसरिजस॥ सुद्ध भएँ दुइ बासर बीते। बोले गुर सनराम पिरीते ॥
ramacharitamanas::3195.verse_hindi: वे (नित्य शुद्ध-बुद्ध) भगवान श्री रामजी शुद्ध हुए! साधुओं की ऐसी सम्मति है कि उनका शुद्ध होना वैसे ही है जैसा तीर्थों के आवाहन से गंगाजी शुद्ध होती हैं! (गंगाजी तो स्वभाव से ही शुद्ध हैं, उनमें जिन तीर्थों का आवाहन किया जाता है, उलटे वे ही गंगाजी के सम्पर्क में आने से शुद्ध हो जाते हैं। इसी प्रकार सच्चिदानंद रूप श्रीराम तो नित्य शुद्ध हैं, उनके संसर्ग से कर्म ही शुद्ध हो गए।) जब शुद्ध हुए दो दिन बीत गए तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी प्रीति के साथ गुरुजी से बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3195.english_translation: He became purified, as the saints agree. It is like the purification of the Ganga by the calling of holy places. After two days had passed in this purified state, Lord Ram lovingly spoke to the teacher.
ramacharitamanas::3195.translation_literal: सुद्ध (pure) / सो (that) / भयउ (became) / साधु (saints) / संमत (agreed-upon) / अस (as) / तीरथ (holy places) / आवाहन (calling) / सुसरिजस (of the pure river) / सुद्ध (pure) / भएँ (having become) / दुइ (two) / बासर (days) / बीते (passed) / बोले (spoke) / गुर (to the teacher) / सनराम (Ram) / पिरीते (lovingly)
ramacharitamanas::3195.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3195.essence: Ram does not receive purity; he gives it.
ramacharitamanas::3195.simple_meaning: Ram is already pure, and even the rites around him become pure through contact with him. After two days, he speaks lovingly to his teacher.
ramacharitamanas::3195.simple_insight: Some presences do not need cleansing; they cleanse everything around them.
ramacharitamanas::3195.detailed_meaning: After Dasharath’s rites, Ram has completed the purification period. The saints’ view is invoked: Ram is not made pure by ritual, but ritual and place become pure through him. Only then does he lovingly turn to Vashishtha and speak.
ramacharitamanas::3195.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm changes the whole room. You came carrying tension, but their presence makes everything feel orderly, clean, and strangely settled.
ramacharitamanas::3195.insight: It shifts attention from ritual as a requirement to purity as an overflowing quality of Ram’s presence.

ramacharitamanas::3196.verse_sanskrit: नाथ लोग सब निपट दुखारी। कंद मूल फल अंबु आहारी॥ सानुज भरतु सचिव सब माता। देखि मोहि पल जिमि जुग जाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3196.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! सब लोग यहाँ अत्यन्त दुःखी हो रहे हैं। कंद, मूल, फल और जल का ही आहार करते हैं। भाई शत्रुघ्न सहित भरत को, मंत्रियों को और सब माताओं को देखकर मुझे एक-एक पल युग के समान बीत रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3196.english_translation: O Lord, everyone here is terribly sorrowful. They live on roots, fruits, and water. Seeing Bharata with his younger brother Shatrughna, the ministers, and all the mothers, every moment feels like an age to me.
ramacharitamanas::3196.translation_literal: नाथ (Lord) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / निपट (utterly) / दुखारी (sorrowful) । / कंद (roots) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruits) / अंबु (water) / आहारी (eaters, taking as food) ॥ / सानुज (with younger brother) / भरतु (Bharata) / सचिव (ministers) / सब (all) / माता (mothers) । / देखि (seeing) / मोहि (me) / पल (moment) / जिमि (as) / जुग (an age) / जाता (passes) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3196.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::3196.essence: Separation makes a single moment feel endless.
ramacharitamanas::3196.simple_meaning: Lakshman tells Ram that Ayodhya is full of sorrow. Everyone is living on very simple food, and seeing Bharata, Shatrughna, the ministers, and the mothers makes even a moment feel unbearably long.
ramacharitamanas::3196.simple_insight: Love and separation can make time feel unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::3196.detailed_meaning: Lakshman speaks in Ayodhya after Ram's exile has left the city wounded. He points to the people's hardship and the pain of seeing Bharata, Shatrughna, the ministers, and the mothers. The verse deepens the emotional case for Ram's return.
ramacharitamanas::3196.modern_relevance: You walk into a house after a family fight and feel the silence before anyone speaks. Everyone is functioning, but the air itself feels heavy and stretched.
ramacharitamanas::3196.insight: It shifts the focus from argument to the lived pain of separation and loss.

ramacharitamanas::3197.verse_sanskrit: सब समेत पुर धारिअ पाऊ। आपु इहाँ अमरावति राऊ॥ बहुत कहेउँ सब कियउँ ढिठाई। उचित होइ तस करिअ गोसाँई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3197.verse_hindi: अतः सबके साथ आप अयोध्यापुरी को पधारिए (लौट जाइए)। आप यहाँ हैं और राजा अमरावती (स्वर्ग) में हैं (अयोध्या सूनी है)! मैंने बहुत कह डाला, यह सब बड़ी ढिठाई की है। हे गोसाईं! जैसा उचित हो, वैसा ही कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3197.english_translation: So please return to Ayodhya with everyone. You are here, and yet the king is in Amravati; Ayodhya feels empty. I have spoken too much and acted boldly. O Lord, let what is proper be done.
ramacharitamanas::3197.translation_literal: सब समेत (with everyone) / पुर (to the city) / धारिअ (please take) / पाऊ (your steps) / आपु (you) / इहाँ (here) / अमरावति (in Amravati) / राऊ (king) / बहुत (much) / कहेउँ (I have said) / सब (all) / कियउँ (did) / ढिठाई (boldness) / उचित (proper) / होइ (becomes) / तस (so) / करिअ (do) / गोसाँई (O Lord)
ramacharitamanas::3197.speaker: Vashishtha
ramacharitamanas::3197.essence: What is proper matters more than pride, comfort, or delay.
ramacharitamanas::3197.simple_meaning: Vashishtha urges Ram to return to Ayodhya with everyone, saying the city feels empty without him and asking him to do what is right.
ramacharitamanas::3197.simple_insight: Real duty is not about comfort or delay; it is about answering what the moment demands.
ramacharitamanas::3197.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Vashishtha sees a kingdom hollowed out by Ram's absence. He speaks with humility after urging enough, then asks Ram to choose what is fitting for the city, the people, and the moment.
ramacharitamanas::3197.modern_relevance: Your family is waiting in a hospital corridor, and everyone keeps looking at the empty chair where the person who holds things together should be. Someone has to come back and make the next right move.
ramacharitamanas::3197.insight: It shifts the mind from hesitation to responsibility, reminding you that the proper action may already be clear.

ramacharitamanas::3198.verse_sanskrit: धर्म सेतु करुनायतन कस न कहु अस राम। लोग दुखित दिन दुइ दरस देखि लहहुँ बिश्राम ॥
ramacharitamanas::3198.verse_hindi: (वशिष्ठजी ने कहा-) हे राम! तुम धर्म के सेतु और दया के धाम हो, तुम भला ऐसा क्यों न कहो? लोग दुःखी हैं। दो दिन तुम्हारा दर्शन कर शांति लाभ कर लें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3198.english_translation: O Ram, bridge of dharma and abode of compassion, why would you not say yes? The people are suffering. Let them have your sight for two days and find relief.
ramacharitamanas::3198.translation_literal: धर्म (dharma) / सेतु (bridge) / करुनायतन (abode of compassion) / कस (why) / न (not) / कहु (say) / अस (thus) / राम (Ram) / लोग (people) / दुखित (suffering) / दिन (days) / दुइ (two) / दरस (sight) / देखि (having seen) / लहहुँ (may obtain) / बिश्राम (rest)
ramacharitamanas::3198.speaker: Vashishtha
ramacharitamanas::3198.essence: Compassion sometimes means letting others rest in your presence.
ramacharitamanas::3198.simple_meaning: Ram is asked to return briefly so the suffering people of Ayodhya can see him and feel relief.
ramacharitamanas::3198.simple_insight: Sometimes your presence is the comfort someone needs more than your words.
ramacharitamanas::3198.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after exile has wounded everyone, Vashishtha speaks to Ram with tenderness and urgency. He calls Ram the bridge of dharma and the home of compassion, then asks him to return briefly so the grieving people can see him and breathe again.
ramacharitamanas::3198.modern_relevance: A sick parent asks to hear your voice before sleep, not for advice but for comfort. Sometimes what heals people is simply being near the one they trust.
ramacharitamanas::3198.insight: It shifts attention from fixing problems to offering reassuring presence.

ramacharitamanas::3199.verse_sanskrit: राम बचन सुनि सभय समाजू। जनु जलनिधि महुँ बिकल जहाजू॥ सुनि गुर गिरा सुमंगल मूला। भयउ मनहुँ मारुत अनुकूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3199.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के वचन सुनकर सारा समाज भयभीत हो गया। मानो बीच समुद्र में जहाज डगमगा गया हो, परन्तु जब उन्होंने गुरु वशिष्ठजी की श्रेष्ठ कल्याणमूलक वाणी सुनी, तो उस जहाज के लिए मानो हवा अनुकूल हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3199.english_translation: Hearing Ram's words, the whole assembly grew fearful, like a ship tossed in the middle of the sea. Hearing Guru Vashistha's auspicious words, it was as if the wind turned favorable for that ship.
ramacharitamanas::3199.translation_literal: राम बचन (Ram's words) / सुनि (hearing) / सभय (fearful) / समाजू (assembly) / जनु (like) / जलनिधि (sea) / महुँ (in) / बिकल (tossed) / जहाजू (ship)॥ / सुनि (hearing) / गुर (guru's) / गिरा (words) / सुमंगल (auspicious) / मूला (root) / भयउ (became) / मनहुँ (as if) / मारुत (wind) / अनुकूला (favorable) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3199.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3199.essence: Wise words can steady what fear has thrown off course.
ramacharitamanas::3199.simple_meaning: The assembly first trembles at Ram's words, then steadies when Vashistha speaks. The scene compares their fear and relief to a ship in rough sea finding favorable wind.
ramacharitamanas::3199.simple_insight: A steady voice can calm what fear has shaken.
ramacharitamanas::3199.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court is already strained by exile and grief. Ram's words unsettle everyone, but Vashistha's guidance restores order, like a ship losing and then regaining its wind.
ramacharitamanas::3199.modern_relevance: A tense family meeting goes silent after one sharp sentence, then softens when the elder speaks calmly. The room changes not because facts changed, but because steadiness returned.
ramacharitamanas::3199.insight: It shows how fear can be reversed by wise counsel, shifting a group from panic back to balance.

ramacharitamanas::3200.verse_sanskrit: पावन पयँ तिहुँ काल नहाहीं। जो बिलोकि अघ ओघ नसाहीं॥ मंगलमूरति लोचन भरि भरि। निरखहिं हरषि दंडवत करि करि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3200.verse_hindi: सब लोग पवित्र पयस्विनी नदी में (अथवा पयस्विनी नदी के पवित्र जल में) तीनों समय (सबेरे, दोपहर और सायंकाल) स्नान करते हैं, जिसके दर्शन से ही पापों के समूह नष्ट हो जाते हैं और मंगल मूर्ति श्री रामचन्द्रजी को दण्डवत प्रणाम कर-करके उन्हें नेत्र भर-भरकर देखते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3200.english_translation: People bathe in the holy river at all three times, and just seeing Ram destroys a heap of wrongdoing. They bow again and again, then look at the auspicious form of Ram with eyes full of joy.
ramacharitamanas::3200.translation_literal: पावन (holy) / पयँ (water, river) / तिहुँ काल (in three times) / नहाहीं (they bathe) / जो (who, which) / बिलोकि (seeing) / अघ (wrongdoing) / ओघ (heap, flood) / नसाहीं (are destroyed) / मंगलमूरति (auspicious form) / लोचन (eyes) / भरि भरि (filling again and again) / निरखहिं (they behold) / हरषि (with joy) / दंडवत (prostration) / करि करि (doing again and again)
ramacharitamanas::3200.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3200.essence: Ram's presence cleanses more deeply than ritual alone.
ramacharitamanas::3200.simple_meaning: People bathe in holy water all day, but Ram's sight is even more purifying. They keep bowing to him and look at him again and again with joy.
ramacharitamanas::3200.simple_insight: There is relief in being near what naturally cleanses you.
ramacharitamanas::3200.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the crowd has gathered around Ram during the exile crisis. The verse shifts from grief to reverence: people treat his presence as purifying, bowing repeatedly and drinking in his sight because being near him feels like blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3200.modern_relevance: You step into a temple after a hard week, but what you really want is the calm that settles when you finally stand before someone who restores you. That is the feeling here.
ramacharitamanas::3200.insight: It shifts devotion from ritual alone to direct, repeated seeing of the beloved form.

ramacharitamanas::3201.verse_sanskrit: राम सैल बन देखन जाहीं। जहँ सुख सकल सकल दुख नाहीं॥ झरना झरहिं सुधासम बारी। त्रिबिध तापहर त्रिबिध बयारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3201.verse_hindi: सब श्री रामचन्द्रजी के पर्वत (कामदगिरि) और वन को देखने जाते हैं, जहाँ सभी सुख हैं और सभी दुःखों का अभाव है। झरने अमृत के समान जल झरते हैं और तीन प्रकार की (शीतल, मंद, सुगंध) हवा तीनों प्रकार के (आध्यात्मिक, आधिभौतिक, आधिदैविक) तापों को हर लेती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3201.english_translation: People go to see Ram's mountain and forest, where all joy is found and all sorrow is absent. Streams pour out water like nectar, and the three kinds of breeze remove the three kinds of suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3201.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / सैल (mountain) / बन (forest) / देखन (to see) / जाहीं (they go) / जहँ (where) / सुख (happiness) / सकल (all) / सकल (all) / दुख (sorrow) / नाहीं (not) / झरना (streams) / झरहिं (flow) / सुधासम (like nectar) / बारी (water) / त्रिबिध (three kinds) / तापहर (remover of heat/suffering) / त्रिबिध (three kinds) / बयारी (breezes)
ramacharitamanas::3201.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3201.essence: Ram's presence turns a place into relief itself.
ramacharitamanas::3201.simple_meaning: Ram's mountain and forest are described as a place of pure comfort: no sorrow, sweet water, and cooling breezes that remove every kind of suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3201.simple_insight: Some places feel peaceful because they seem to carry Ram's presence everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::3201.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the scene shifts from grief and fear to the beauty of Chitrakoot, where people go to see Ram's mountain and forest. Tulsidas paints it as a sanctuary so complete that nature itself seems to soothe every burden.
ramacharitamanas::3201.modern_relevance: You step into a quiet hillside after weeks of noise, and your body loosens before your mind can explain why. Some places seem to hold grief differently.
ramacharitamanas::3201.insight: It turns a landscape into a lived experience of relief, showing how environment can calm the whole person.

ramacharitamanas::3202.verse_sanskrit: बिटप बेलि तृन अगनित जाती। फल प्रसून पल्लव बहु भाँती॥ सुंदर सिला सुखद तरु छाहीं। जाइ बरनि बन छबि केहि पाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3202.verse_hindi: असंख्य जात के वृक्ष, लताएँ और तृण हैं तथा बहुत तरह के फल, फूल और पत्ते हैं। सुंदर शिलाएँ हैं। वृक्षों की छाया सुख देने वाली है। वन की शोभा किससे वर्णन की जा सकती है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3202.english_translation: There are countless kinds of trees, vines, grasses, fruits, flowers, and leaves. Beautiful rocks and soothing shade fill the forest. Who could ever describe the forest's splendor?
ramacharitamanas::3202.translation_literal: बिटप (trees) / बेलि (vines) / तृन (grasses) / अगनित (countless) / जाती (kinds) / फल (fruits) / प्रसून (flowers) / पल्लव (leaves) / बहु (many) / भाँती (sorts) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सिला (rocks) / सुखद (pleasant-giving) / तरु (trees) / छाहीं (shade) / जाइ (go) / बरनि (to describe) / बन (forest) / छबि (beauty) / केहि (who) / पाहीं (can)
ramacharitamanas::3202.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3202.essence: The forest's richness exceeds any single description.
ramacharitamanas::3202.simple_meaning: The forest is overflowing with variety, beauty, and shade. It is so rich and lovely that no description can fully capture it.
ramacharitamanas::3202.simple_insight: Some places are too alive to be reduced to words.
ramacharitamanas::3202.detailed_meaning: Ram's path through the forest is being described as a place of abundance, not hardship. Trees, vines, grasses, flowers, rocks, and shade all add to its beauty, setting the scene before the next line widens the picture further.
ramacharitamanas::3202.modern_relevance: You step off a crowded train into a quiet hillside trail, and the air changes at once. The details keep coming, and you stop trying to name them all.
ramacharitamanas::3202.insight: It shifts attention from utility to presence, letting beauty be seen before it is explained.

ramacharitamanas::3203.verse_sanskrit: सरनि सरोरुह जल बिहग कूजत गुंजत भृंग। बैर बिगत बिहरत बिपिन मृग बिहंग बहुरंग ॥
ramacharitamanas::3203.verse_hindi: तालाबों में कमल खिल रहे हैं, जल के पक्षी कूज रहे हैं, भौंरे गुंजार कर रहे हैं और बहुत रंगों के पक्षी और पशु वन में वैररहित होकर विहार कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3203.english_translation: Lotuses bloom in the lakes, waterbirds call, bees hum, and many-colored birds and animals roam the forest without enmity.
ramacharitamanas::3203.translation_literal: सरनि (lakes/ponds) / सरोरुह (lotus) / जल (water) / बिहग (birds) / कूजत (calling) / गुंजत (humming) / भृंग (bees) / बैर (enmity) / बिगत (gone) / बिहरत (roaming) / बिपिन (forest) / मृग (deer) / बिहंग (birds) / बहुरंग (many-colored)
ramacharitamanas::3203.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3203.essence: Peace changes the whole world around you.
ramacharitamanas::3203.simple_meaning: The forest around Ram is so beautiful and peaceful that even the animals and birds seem free of conflict.
ramacharitamanas::3203.simple_insight: Some places quiet the heart so completely that even nature feels reconciled.
ramacharitamanas::3203.detailed_meaning: Ram’s forest exile is being painted as a living paradise. After the mountains, streams, and trees, this line adds lakes, birds, bees, deer, and colorful creatures moving without hostility, showing the calm harmony of the place before the scene turns to its human inhabitants.
ramacharitamanas::3203.modern_relevance: You step into a quiet park after a brutal week, and even the birds seem less frantic. The world can feel different when you finally stop carrying your own tension into it.
ramacharitamanas::3203.insight: It shifts attention from danger and loss to the healing order present in a peaceful environment.

ramacharitamanas::3204.verse_sanskrit: कोल किरात भिल्ल बनबासी। मधु सुचि सुंदर स्वादु सुधा सी॥ भरि भरि परन पुटीं रचि रूरी। कंद मूल फल अंकुर जूरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3204.verse_hindi: कोल, किरात और भील आदि वन के रहने वाले लोग पवित्र, सुंदर एवं अमृत के समान स्वादिष्ट मधु (शहद) को सुंदर दोने बनाकर और उनमें भर-भरकर तथा कंद, मूल, फल और अंकुर आदि की जूड़ियों (अँटियों) को ॥
ramacharitamanas::3204.english_translation: The forest-dwellers of the Kola, Kirata, and Bhilla tribes bring pure, lovely honey as sweet as nectar, filling leaf-bowls with it and gathering roots, tubers, fruits, and tender shoots.
ramacharitamanas::3204.translation_literal: कोल (forest tribes) / किरात (hill-forest people) / भिल्ल (Bhilla people) / बनबासी (forest dwellers) / मधु (honey) / सुचि (pure) / सुंदर (beautiful) / स्वादु (sweet-tasting) / सुधा सी (like nectar) / भरि भरि (filling again and again) / परन पुटीं (leaf-bowls) / रचि (making/arranging) / रूरी (lovely) / कंद (roots/tubers) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruits) / अंकुर (tender shoots) / जूरी (bundles/collections)
ramacharitamanas::3204.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3204.essence: Even the forest offers Ram what it has most lovingly.
ramacharitamanas::3204.simple_meaning: Forest people bring Ram and his companions gifts from the woods: honey, roots, fruits, and tender shoots.
ramacharitamanas::3204.simple_insight: Simple offerings, given with care, can carry deep warmth.
ramacharitamanas::3204.detailed_meaning: In Chitrakoot, Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are living in the forest among its people. The local tribes come forward with gifts from the land itself — honey, roots, fruits, and shoots — showing the forest welcoming Ram with natural abundance.
ramacharitamanas::3204.modern_relevance: A neighbor shows up with mangoes from their tree and a jar of homemade honey after you move into a new place. No formal gift could feel more generous.
ramacharitamanas::3204.insight: It shifts attention from the size of a gift to the love and effort behind it.

ramacharitamanas::3205.verse_sanskrit: सबहि देहिं करि बिनय प्रनामा। कहि कहि स्वाद भेद गुन नामा॥ देहिं लोग बहु मोल न लेहीं। फेरत राम दोहाई देहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3205.verse_hindi: सबको विनय और प्रणाम करके उन चीजों के अलग-अलग स्वाद, भेद (प्रकार), गुण और नाम बता-बताकर देते हैं। लोग उनका बहुत दाम देते हैं, पर वे नहीं लेते और लौटा देने में श्री रामजी की दुहाई देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3205.english_translation: They greet everyone respectfully, explain the taste, variety, qualities, and names of the goods, and give them away. People offer much money, but they refuse it and send them back, invoking Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3205.translation_literal: सबहि (to everyone) / देहिं (they give) / करि (doing) / बिनय (humility) / प्रनामा (salutations) / कहि कहि (telling repeatedly) / स्वाद (taste) / भेद (differences) / गुन (qualities) / नामा (names) / देहिं (they give) / लोग (people) / बहु (much) / मोल (price) / न लेहीं (do not take) / फेरत (returning) / राम (Ram) / दोहाई (calling upon) / देहीं (they give)
ramacharitamanas::3205.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3205.essence: True giving asks for nothing back.
ramacharitamanas::3205.simple_meaning: The forest people politely offer their goods, describe them carefully, and refuse payment, sending others back with Ram's name on their lips.
ramacharitamanas::3205.simple_insight: Generosity can be so complete that even payment feels unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::3205.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the local people meet travellers with folded hands and gentle respect. They explain every item they offer, but they do not bargain or cling to profit. Their giving is so pure that they send others away in Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::3205.modern_relevance: At a roadside stall, someone hands you extra fruit, waves away the change, and smiles as if kindness itself were the price. That quiet dignity changes the whole exchange.
ramacharitamanas::3205.insight: It shifts giving from transaction to offering, where respect matters more than profit.

ramacharitamanas::3206.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं सनेह मगन मृदु बानी। मानत साधु पेम पहिचानी॥ तुम्ह सुकृती हम नीच निषादा। पावा दरसनु राम प्रसादा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3206.verse_hindi: प्रेम में मग्न हुए वे कोमल वाणी से कहते हैं कि साधु लोग प्रेम को पहचानकर उसका सम्मान करते हैं (अर्थात आप साधु हैं, आप हमारे प्रेम को देखिए, दाम देकर या वस्तुएँ लौटाकर हमारे प्रेम का तिरस्कार न कीजिए)। आप तो पुण्यात्मा हैं, हम नीच निषाद हैं। श्री रामजी की कृपा से ही हमने आप लोगों के दर्शन पाए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3206.english_translation: Overjoyed with love, they speak softly: “The good understand and honor love. You are virtuous; we are lowly Nishads. By Ram’s grace, we have received your sight.”
ramacharitamanas::3206.translation_literal: कहहिं (they say) / सनेह (love) / मगन (immersed) / मृदु (soft) / बानी (speech) / मानत (honoring) / साधु (the good) / पेम (love) / पहिचानी (having recognized)॥ / तुम्ह (you) / सुकृती (virtuous) / हम (we) / नीच (lowly) / निषादा (Nishads) / पावा (received) / दरसनु (sight) / राम (Ram) / प्रसादा (by grace)॥
ramacharitamanas::3206.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3206.essence: Love becomes sacred when it is received with humility.
ramacharitamanas::3206.simple_meaning: True goodness recognizes love and responds with respect. The Nishads humbly say they are lowly and that seeing Ram’s people is itself Ram’s grace.
ramacharitamanas::3206.simple_insight: You do not have to prove love when it is sincere; being received is enough.
ramacharitamanas::3206.detailed_meaning: The Nishads have welcomed Ram’s party with forest gifts and humble service. Overwhelmed by devotion, they speak gently, refusing any transactional exchange. They see the visitors as noble and themselves as blessed simply to have this meeting.
ramacharitamanas::3206.modern_relevance: You bring food to someone who is grieving, and they keep trying to pay you back. The deeper gift is not the meal — it is letting love be received without turning it into a transaction.
ramacharitamanas::3206.insight: It shifts you from measuring care by price or status to honoring the love inside the gesture.

ramacharitamanas::3207.verse_sanskrit: हमहि अगम अति दरसु तुम्हारा। जस मरु धरनि देवधुनि धारा॥ राम कृपाल निषाद नेवाजा। परिजन प्रजउ चहिअ जस राजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3207.verse_hindi: हम लोगों को आपके दर्शन बड़े ही दुर्लभ हैं, जैसे मरुभूमि के लिए गंगाजी की धारा दुर्लभ है! (देखिए) कृपालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने निषाद पर कैसी कृपा की है। जैसे राजा हैं वैसा ही उनके परिवार और प्रजा को भी होना चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3207.english_translation: Your sight is as rare to us as a river of Ganga in a desert. See how kindly Ram has blessed Nishad; a king's family and people should be like him.
ramacharitamanas::3207.translation_literal: हमहि (to us) / अगम (hard to reach) / अति (very) / दरसु (sight) / तुम्हारा (your) । जस (as) / मरु (desert) / धरनि (land) / देवधुनि (Ganga, the river of the divine) / धारा (stream) ॥ राम (Ram) / कृपाल (merciful) / निषाद (Nishad) / नेवाजा (blessed) । परिजन (family) / प्रजा (subjects) / उ (also) / चहिअ (should be) / जस (like) / राजा (king) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3207.speaker: Nishad
ramacharitamanas::3207.essence: True grace does not stop with one devotee; it reshapes everyone nearby.
ramacharitamanas::3207.simple_meaning: Nishad says Ram's presence is precious and rare, like water in a desert. He also says a truly good ruler blesses not only himself but his whole people.
ramacharitamanas::3207.simple_insight: You feel the dignity of being seen by grace, and the hope that goodness should spread beyond one person.
ramacharitamanas::3207.detailed_meaning: On the riverbank, Nishad speaks to Ram after welcoming him with love and humility. He says Ram's sight is almost impossible to receive, then points to Ram's mercy toward him as proof that a righteous king lifts up everyone around him.
ramacharitamanas::3207.modern_relevance: You meet someone who treats the cleaner, the driver, and the assistant with the same warmth they give the CEO. That small consistency tells you more than any speech about character.
ramacharitamanas::3207.insight: It shifts attention from private devotion to the way leadership should shape an entire circle of people.

ramacharitamanas::3208.verse_sanskrit: यह जियँ जानि सँकोचु तजि करिअ छोहु लखि नेहु। हमहि कृतारथ करनलगि फल तृन अंकुर लेहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3208.verse_hindi: हृदय में ऐसा जानकर संकोच छोड़कर और हमारा प्रेम देखकर कृपा कीजिए और हमको कृतार्थ करने के लिए ही फल, तृण और अंकुर लीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3208.english_translation: Knowing this in your heart, set aside hesitation and show kindness, seeing our love. To make us fulfilled, please take fruits, grass, and shoots.
ramacharitamanas::3208.translation_literal: यह (this) / जियँ (in the heart) / जानि (knowing) / सँकोचु (hesitation) / तजि (leaving) / करिअ (do) / छोहु (kindness) / लखि (seeing) / नेहु (love) / हमहि (us) / कृतारथ (fulfilled) / करन लगि (in order to make) / फल (fruits) / तृन (grass) / अंकुर (shoots) / लेहु (take)
ramacharitamanas::3208.speaker: Nishad
ramacharitamanas::3208.essence: Kindness completes the gift, not its size.
ramacharitamanas::3208.simple_meaning: Nishad asks Ram to ignore any hesitation, accept the simple forest gifts, and bless him by receiving them with kindness.
ramacharitamanas::3208.simple_insight: Love becomes real when you receive another person's humble offering with grace.
ramacharitamanas::3208.detailed_meaning: Nishad is welcoming Ram in the forest and feels unworthy before him. After praising Ram's rare visit, he asks Ram to drop any hesitation and accept fruits, grass, and shoots so that the host can feel fulfilled by serving him.
ramacharitamanas::3208.modern_relevance: You bring homemade food to someone recovering from illness, and they hesitate to take it because it feels too little. Their acceptance matters more than the meal itself.
ramacharitamanas::3208.insight: It teaches you to receive simple service as an act of honouring the giver.

ramacharitamanas::3209.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह प्रिय पाहुने बन पगु धारे। सेवा जोगु न भाग हमारे॥ देब काह हम तुम्हहि गोसाँई। ईंधनु पात किरात मिताई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3209.verse_hindi: आप प्रिय पाहुने वन में पधारे हैं। आपकी सेवा करने के योग्य हमारे भाग्य नहीं हैं। हे स्वामी! हम आपको क्या देंगे? भीलों की मित्रता तो बस, ईंधन (लकड़ी) और पत्तों ही तक है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3209.english_translation: You have come to the forest as a beloved guest. We are not worthy of serving you. What can we offer you, lord? For forest people, friendship means only firewood and leaves.
ramacharitamanas::3209.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / प्रिय (dear, beloved) / पाहुने (guest) / बन (forest) / पगु धारे (have placed your feet, have arrived) / सेवा जोगु (fit for service) / न (not) / भाग (fortune, worth) / हमारे (our) / देब (to give) / काह (what) / हम (we) / तुम्हहि (to you) / गोसाँई (lord) / ईंधनु (firewood) / पात (leaves) / किरात (forest-dwellers, hunters) / मिताई (friendship)
ramacharitamanas::3209.speaker: Shabari
ramacharitamanas::3209.essence: Love makes the smallest offering feel complete.
ramacharitamanas::3209.simple_meaning: Shabari welcomes Ram as a beloved guest and humbly says she has nothing worthy to offer except the simple gifts of the forest.
ramacharitamanas::3209.simple_insight: Love is measured by devotion, not by the size of the gift.
ramacharitamanas::3209.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Shabari greets Ram after waiting for him with fierce devotion. Seeing him arrive, she feels unworthy to serve him properly, so she offers the only things she has: firewood, leaves, and heartfelt welcome.
ramacharitamanas::3209.modern_relevance: You host a friend in a tiny apartment with mismatched cups and instant tea, worried it feels too little. What matters is that you opened the door with love.
ramacharitamanas::3209.insight: It shifts attention from perfect hospitality to sincere welcome.

ramacharitamanas::3210.verse_sanskrit: यह हमारि अति बड़ि सेवकाई। लेहिं न बासन बसन चोराई॥ हम जड़ जीव जीव गन घाती। कुटिल कुचाली कुमति कुजाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::3210.verse_hindi: हमारी तो यही बड़ी भारी सेवा है कि हम आपके कपड़े और बर्तन नहीं चुरा लेते। हम लोग जड़ जीव हैं, जीवों की हिंसा करने वाले हैं, कुटिल, कुचाली, कुबुद्धि और कुजाति हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3210.english_translation: This is our great service: we do not steal your clothes or vessels. We are dull beings, killers of living creatures, crooked, deceitful, foolish, and low-born.
ramacharitamanas::3210.translation_literal: यह (this) / हमारि (our) / अति बड़ि (very great) / सेवकाई (service) / लेहिं (take) / न (not) / बासन (vessels) / बसन (clothes) / चोराई (steal) / हम (we) / जड़ (dull) / जीव (beings) / जीव गन (groups of living beings) / घाती (killers) / कुटिल (crooked) / कुचाली (deceitful) / कुमति (foolish mind) / कुजाती (low-born)
ramacharitamanas::3210.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3210.essence: True service may be nothing more than not taking what is not yours.
ramacharitamanas::3210.simple_meaning: The speaker humbly says that the best service he can offer is simply not causing harm or taking anything that is not given.
ramacharitamanas::3210.simple_insight: Humility can begin with restraint: the first gift is to stop adding harm.
ramacharitamanas::3210.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the forest dwellers answer Ram and Lakshman with deep humility. They insist they have nothing worthy to offer except harmlessness itself, confessing their flaws and unworthiness while welcoming Ram as a guest.
ramacharitamanas::3210.modern_relevance: You show up at a friend's house after they have already done too much for you. Instead of performing gratitude, you stop taking, stop demanding, and become easy to host.
ramacharitamanas::3210.insight: It shifts service from grand gestures to simple non-harm and gratitude.

ramacharitamanas::3211.verse_sanskrit: पाप करत निसि बासर जाहीं। नहिं पट कटि नहिं पेट अघाहीं॥ सपनेहुँ धरमबुद्धि कस काऊ। यह रघुनंदन दरस प्रभाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3211.verse_hindi: हमारे दिन-रात पाप करते ही बीतते हैं। तो भी न तो हमारी कमर में कपड़ा है और न पेट ही भरते हैं। हममें स्वप्न में भी कभी धर्मबुद्धि कैसी? यह सब तो श्री रघुनाथजी के दर्शन का प्रभाव है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3211.english_translation: We spend our days and nights in wrongdoing, yet our waists still lack cloth and our bellies still go hungry. We have no sense of righteousness, even in dreams. This is the power of seeing Raghunandan.
ramacharitamanas::3211.translation_literal: पाप (wrongdoing) / करत (doing) / निसि (night) / बासर (day) / जाहीं (pass) / नहिं (not) / पट (cloth) / कटि (waist) / नहिं (not) / पेट (belly) / अघाहीं (filled)॥ / सपनेहुँ (even in dreams) / धरमबुद्धि (sense of righteousness) / कस (how) / काऊ (anyone) / यह (this) / रघुनंदन (Raghunandan) / दरस (seeing) / प्रभाऊ (power/effect)॥
ramacharitamanas::3211.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3211.essence: Ram's presence changes even an unworthy heart.
ramacharitamanas::3211.simple_meaning: The forest people admit their lives are full of wrongdoing and poverty, yet Ram's presence has still transformed them. Just seeing him has awakened a new sense of goodness.
ramacharitamanas::3211.simple_insight: You don't have to be already pure for grace to change you.
ramacharitamanas::3211.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the humble people around Ram and Lakshman are speaking with awe. They call themselves unworthy, sinful, and poor, yet they know one thing clearly: Ram's presence has already begun to change them. That is why this verse matters.
ramacharitamanas::3211.modern_relevance: You sit in a room with someone whose calm changes the whole atmosphere. No lecture, no correction — just being near them makes your own habits feel smaller and your better instincts stronger.
ramacharitamanas::3211.insight: It shifts devotion from earning worthiness to receiving transformation through nearness.

ramacharitamanas::3212.verse_sanskrit: जब तें प्रभु पद पदुम निहारे। मिटे दुसह दुख दोष हमारे॥ बचन सुनत पुरजन अनुरागे। तिन्ह के भाग सराहन लागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3212.verse_hindi: जब से प्रभु के चरण कमल देखे, तब से हमारे दुःसह दुःख और दोष मिट गए। वनवासियों के वचन सुनकर अयोध्या के लोग प्रेम में भर गए और उनके भाग्य की सराहना करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3212.english_translation: Since we beheld the lotus feet of the Lord, our unbearable sorrow and faults have vanished. Hearing the forest dwellers’ words, the people of Ayodhya were filled with love and began praising their good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::3212.translation_literal: जब तें (since) / प्रभु (the Lord) / पद (feet) / पदुम (lotus) / निहारे (beheld) / मिटे (were removed) / दुसह (unbearable) / दुख (sorrow) / दोष (faults) / हमारे (our) ॥ बचन (words) / सुनत (hearing) / पुरजन (townspeople) / अनुरागे (filled with love) / तिन्ह (their) / के (of) / भाग (fortune) / सराहन (to praise) / लागे (began)
ramacharitamanas::3212.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3212.essence: Ram’s presence dissolves sorrow and awakens love in everyone around him.
ramacharitamanas::3212.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram’s feet removes deep sorrow and inner faults. Hearing the forest dwellers speak, the people of Ayodhya feel love and praise their good fortune.
ramacharitamanas::3212.simple_insight: Love for Ram softens pain and turns envy into gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::3212.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the people hear the forest dwellers speak after Ram’s exile. Their words are so full of devotion that the listeners are moved to love, and the sight of Ram’s lotus feet is remembered as the end of unbearable sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::3212.modern_relevance: You hear someone speak with such sincerity that your own bitterness loosens. A single moment of real presence can make old pain feel lighter.
ramacharitamanas::3212.insight: It shifts attention from complaint to gratitude and shows how devotion changes the heart’s atmosphere.

ramacharitamanas::3213.verse_sanskrit: लागे सराहन भाग सब अनुराग बचन सुनावहीं बोलनि मिलनि सिय राम चरन सनेहु लखि सुखु पावहीं॥ नर नारि निदरहिं नेहु निज सुनि कोल भिल्लनि की गिरा। तुलसी कृपा रघुबंसमनि की लोह लै लौका तिरा॥
ramacharitamanas::3213.verse_hindi: सब उनके भाग्य की सराहना करने लगे और प्रेम के वचन सुनाने लगे। उन लोगों के बोलने और मिलने का ढंग तथा श्री सीता-रामजी के चरणों में उनका प्रेम देखकर सब सुख पा रहे हैं। उन कोल-भीलों की वाणी सुनकर सभी नर-नारी अपने प्रेम का निरादर करते हैं (उसे धिक्कार देते हैं)। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि यह रघुवंशमणि श्री रामचन्द्रजी की कृपा है कि लोहा नौका को अपने ऊपर लेकर तैर गया॥
ramacharitamanas::3213.english_translation: All began praising their fortune and speaking words of love. Seeing their speech, meeting, and affection for the feet of Sita and Ram, everyone felt joy. Hearing the speech of those Kol and Bhil people, men and women despised their own lovelessness. Tulsidas says: by the grace of the jewel of Raghu's line, even iron floated across the river.
ramacharitamanas::3213.translation_literal: लागे (began) / सराहन (praising) / भाग (fortune) / सब (all) / अनुराग (love) / बचन (words) / सुनावहीं (were speaking) / बोलनि (speech) / मिलनि (meeting) / सिय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / सनेहु (affection) / लखि (seeing) / सुखु (joy) / पावहीं (were gaining)॥ / नर (men) / नारि (women) / निदरहिं (despise) / नेहु (love) / निज (their own) / सुनि (hearing) / कोल (Kol) / भिल्लनि (Bhil women) / की (of) / गिरा (speech)॥ / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / कृपा (grace) / रघुबंसमनि (jewel of Raghu's line) / की (of) / लोह (iron) / लै (taking) / लौका (boat) / तिरा (floated across)॥
ramacharitamanas::3213.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3213.essence: True love for Ram makes even the hard-hearted feel their own dryness.
ramacharitamanas::3213.simple_meaning: The villagers are moved by the love they see in the forest people for Ram and Sita. Even ordinary people feel ashamed of their own coldness. Tulsidas says Ram's grace can make the impossible happen.
ramacharitamanas::3213.simple_insight: Real devotion changes the people around it. It makes love feel possible, and indifference feel small.
ramacharitamanas::3213.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the people of Ayodhya are hearing about the forest dwellers who speak with love for Ram and Sita. Their affection, and the joy it brings, becomes a living lesson. Tulsidas closes by saying Ram's grace can carry even what should sink.
ramacharitamanas::3213.modern_relevance: You hear a friend speak gently about someone they love, and your own guarded heart suddenly feels thin. Their sincerity exposes how much of your life has been performed without warmth.
ramacharitamanas::3213.insight: It shifts attention from social approval to the transforming power of genuine devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3214.verse_sanskrit: बिहरहिं बन चहु ओर प्रतिदिन प्रमुदित लोग सब। जल ज्यों दादुर मोर भए पीन पावस प्रथम ॥
ramacharitamanas::3214.verse_hindi: सब लोग दिनोंदिन परम आनंदित होते हुए वन में चारों ओर विचरते हैं। जैसे पहली वर्षा के जल से मेंढक और मोर मोटे हो जाते हैं (प्रसन्न होकर नाचते-कूदते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3214.english_translation: Everyone roams through the forest in daily delight, like frogs and peacocks swelling with the first rains.
ramacharitamanas::3214.translation_literal: बिहरहिं (roam) / बन (forest) / चहु ओर (all around) / प्रतिदिन (every day) / प्रमुदित (delighted) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / जल (water) / ज्यों (like) / दादुर (frogs) / मोर (peacocks) / भए (became) / पीन (plump) / पावस (rainy season) / प्रथम (first)
ramacharitamanas::3214.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3214.essence: Shared joy can make exile feel like spring.
ramacharitamanas::3214.simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya now move through the forest happily, as if the first rains have made them bloom with life.
ramacharitamanas::3214.simple_insight: Joy can change even hardship into something people live inside together.
ramacharitamanas::3214.detailed_meaning: In exile, Ram's presence has transformed the forest into a place of shared happiness. The people around him move through it daily with delight, and Tulsidas compares their joy to frogs and peacocks revived by the first rains.
ramacharitamanas::3214.modern_relevance: A long family trip turns into laughter once the tension lifts and everyone starts enjoying the same roadside tea and rain. The place has not changed, but the mood has.
ramacharitamanas::3214.insight: It shows how a blessed presence can make even difficult circumstances feel alive and nourishing.

ramacharitamanas::3215.verse_sanskrit: पुर जन नारि मगन अति प्रीती। बासर जाहिं पलक सम बीती॥ सीय सासु प्रति बेष बनाई। सादर करइ सरिस सेवकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3215.verse_hindi: अयोध्यापुरी के पुरुष और स्त्री सभी प्रेम में अत्यन्त मग्न हो रहे हैं। उनके दिन पल के समान बीत जाते हैं। जितनी सासुएँ थीं, उतने ही वेष (रूप) बनाकर सीताजी सब सासुओं की आदरपूर्वक एक सी सेवा करती हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3215.english_translation: The men and women of Ayodhya were utterly absorbed in love. Their days passed like a blink. Sita dressed herself in the form of each mother-in-law and served every one of them with respect.
ramacharitamanas::3215.translation_literal: पुर (city) / जन (people) / नारि (women) / मगन (absorbed) / अति (very) / प्रीती (love) । / बासर (days) / जाहिं (go) / पलक (blink) / सम (like) / बीती (passed) ॥ / सीय (Sita) / सासु (mother-in-law) / प्रति (for each) / बेष (form, guise) / बनाई (having made) । / सादर (with respect) / करइ (does) / सरिस (equal) / सेवकाई (service) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3215.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3215.essence: Love becomes real when it turns into respectful service.
ramacharitamanas::3215.simple_meaning: Everyone in Ayodhya is caught up in loving joy, and time feels like it flies. Sita also takes on each mother-in-law's form and serves them all respectfully.
ramacharitamanas::3215.simple_insight: Love makes service feel natural, and time itself seems to soften.
ramacharitamanas::3215.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, life with Ram and Sita has filled the whole city with tenderness. Men and women are lost in affection, and even the days seem to vanish. In that same atmosphere, Sita quietly serves each mother-in-law in her own form, showing perfect humility.
ramacharitamanas::3215.modern_relevance: A home full of laughter can make the hours disappear. In the middle of that warmth, someone notices the dishes, the tea, the tired elder in the next room, and serves without making a scene.
ramacharitamanas::3215.insight: It shifts attention from enjoying closeness to expressing it through humble care.

ramacharitamanas::3216.verse_sanskrit: लखा न मरमु राम बिनु काहूँ। माया सब सिय माया माहूँ॥ सीयँ सासु सेवा बस कीन्हीं। तिन्ह लहि सुख सिख आसिष दीन्हीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3216.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी के सिवा इस भेद को और किसी ने नहीं जाना। सब मायाएँ (पराशक्ति महामाया) श्री सीताजी की माया में ही हैं। सीताजी ने सासुओं को सेवा से वश में कर लिया। उन्होंने सुख पाकर सीख और आशीर्वाद दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3216.english_translation: No one understood the mystery except Ram. All illusion rests within Sita's own power. Sita won over her mothers-in-law through service, and they, pleased, gave her blessings and teachings.
ramacharitamanas::3216.translation_literal: लखा (understood) / न (not) / मरमु (mystery) / राम (Ram) / बिनु (except) / काहूँ (anyone) / माया (illusion/power of appearance) / सब (all) / सिय (Sita) / माया (power/illusion) / माहूँ (within) / सीयँ (Sita) / सासु (mothers-in-law) / सेवा (service) / बस (under control) / कीन्हीं (made) / तिन्ह (they) / लहि (having received) / सुख (pleasure) / सिख (teaching) / आसिष (blessings) / दीन्हीं (gave)
ramacharitamanas::3216.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3216.essence: True grace changes others without needing force.
ramacharitamanas::3216.simple_meaning: Only Ram fully knows the hidden mystery. Sita's influence is so complete that even other powers of appearance rest within her, and she wins over her mothers-in-law through humble service.
ramacharitamanas::3216.simple_insight: Quiet service can soften even the hardest hearts, and true grace works without force.
ramacharitamanas::3216.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram and Sita have returned, and the household is being reshaped by their presence. Tulsidas pauses to praise Sita: her grace is so subtle that only Ram fully knows it, and her service wins the affection and blessings of the elder women.
ramacharitamanas::3216.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense family gathering and do the dishes without announcement. By the end of the evening, the room feels different. That is the kind of power this verse honors.
ramacharitamanas::3216.insight: It shifts attention from control and display to gentle influence through service.

ramacharitamanas::3217.verse_sanskrit: लखि सिय सहित सरल दोउ भाई। कुटिल रानि पछितानि अघाई॥ अवनि जमहि जाचति कैकेई। महि न बीचु बिधि मीचु न देई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3217.verse_hindi: सीताजी समेत दोनों भाइयों (श्री राम-लक्ष्मण) को सरल स्वभाव देखकर कुटिल रानी कैकेयी भरपेट पछताई। वह पृथ्वी तथा यमराज से याचना करती है, किन्तु धरती बीच (फटकर समा जाने के लिए रास्ता) नहीं देती और विधाता मौत नहीं देता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3217.english_translation: Seeing both brothers with Sita, simple and gentle, the crooked queen Kaikeyi was filled with regret. She begged the earth and Yama for a way out, but the ground would not open and death would not come.
ramacharitamanas::3217.translation_literal: लखि (seeing) / सिय सहित (with Sita) / सरल (simple, gentle) / दोउ भाई (both brothers) / कुटिल (crooked) / रानि (queen) / पछितानि (regret) / अघाई (filled up)॥ / अवनि (earth) / जमहि (to Yama, lord of death) / जाचति (begging) / कैकेई (Kaikeyi) / महि (ground) / न बीचु (no opening) / बिधि (fate, the creator) / मीचु (death) / न देई (does not give)॥
ramacharitamanas::3217.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3217.essence: Regret can become so heavy that even death feels too slow.
ramacharitamanas::3217.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi sees Ram, Lakshman, and Sita's innocence and feels unbearable regret. She wants the earth to swallow her and death to come, but neither happens.
ramacharitamanas::3217.simple_insight: Some regret is so heavy that even escape feels impossible.
ramacharitamanas::3217.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kaikeyi watches Ram and Lakshman with Sita and sees their simple goodness against her own crooked choice. Her guilt turns crushing. This verse shows the first full wave of remorse after the exile has begun.
ramacharitamanas::3217.modern_relevance: You replay one decision at 2 a.m. and feel your chest tighten. You wish the floor would open, but the mind keeps you awake with what you cannot undo.
ramacharitamanas::3217.insight: It shows regret at its most physical: guilt becomes so intense that the body longs for disappearance.

ramacharitamanas::3218.verse_sanskrit: लोकहुँ बेद बिदित कबि कहहीं। राम बिमुख थलु नरक न लहहीं॥ यहु संसउ सब के मन माहीं। राम गवनु बिधि अवध कि नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3218.verse_hindi: लोक और वेद में प्रसिद्ध है और कवि (ज्ञानी) भी कहते हैं कि जो श्री रामजी से विमुख हैं, उन्हें नरक में भी ठौर नहीं मिलती। सबके मन में यह संदेह हो रहा था कि हे विधाता! श्री रामचन्द्रजी का अयोध्या जाना होगा या नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3218.english_translation: It is famous among people and in the Vedas, and wise poets say that those who turn away from Ram find no place even in the lower realm. Everyone’s mind held one doubt: would Ram go to Ayodhya or not?
ramacharitamanas::3218.translation_literal: लोकहुँ (among people) / बेद (the Vedas) / बिदित (well known) / कबि (poets) / कहहीं (say) / राम बिमुख (turned away from Ram) / थलु (place) / नरक (lower realm) / न लहहीं (do not obtain)॥ / यहु (this) / संसउ (doubt) / सब के (of everyone) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / राम गवनु (Ram’s going) / बिधि (O creator) / अवध (to Ayodhya) / कि नाहीं (or not)
ramacharitamanas::3218.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3218.essence: Turning away from Ram leaves you without refuge.
ramacharitamanas::3218.simple_meaning: Turning away from Ram leaves no true refuge, and everyone is still wondering whether Ram will actually go to Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::3218.simple_insight: Separation from what you love can feel like losing your footing entirely.
ramacharitamanas::3218.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the court and the people are caught between grief and uncertainty. The verse first states a hard truth about being turned away from Ram, then shifts to the public doubt over whether Ram will leave for exile, deepening the emotional break.
ramacharitamanas::3218.modern_relevance: You watch someone you trust walk out of the room, and suddenly the whole day feels unstable. That unsettled feeling is what this verse knows.
ramacharitamanas::3218.insight: It links inner exile with outer loss, then shows a city suspended in uncertainty.

ramacharitamanas::3219.verse_sanskrit: निसि न नीद नहिं भूख दिन भरतु बिकल सुचि सोच। नीच कीच बिच मगन जस मीनहि सलिल सँकोच ॥
ramacharitamanas::3219.verse_hindi: भरतजी को न तो रात को नींद आती है, न दिन में भूख ही लगती है। वे पवित्र सोच में ऐसे विकल हैं, जैसे नीचे (तल) के कीचड़ में डूबी हुई मछली को जल की कमी से व्याकुलता होती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3219.english_translation: Bharat has neither sleep at night nor hunger by day. He is shaken by pure sorrowful thought, like a fish trapped in mud and longing for water.
ramacharitamanas::3219.translation_literal: निसि (at night) / न (not) / नीद (sleep) / नहिं (not) / भूख (hunger) / दिन (by day) / भरतु (Bharat) / बिकल (restless, shaken) / सुचि (pure) / सोच (thought) / नीच (low) / कीच (mud) / बिच (in) / मगन (immersed) / जस (like) / मीनहि (to a fish) / सलिल (water) / सँकोच (lack, restraint, shortage)
ramacharitamanas::3219.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3219.essence: True grief makes even the body feel exiled.
ramacharitamanas::3219.simple_meaning: Bharat is so overwhelmed by pure grief and concern that he cannot sleep or eat. His distress is like a fish trapped in mud, craving water.
ramacharitamanas::3219.simple_insight: Some love hurts so much that the body itself forgets its habits.
ramacharitamanas::3219.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat has been crushed by Ram's exile and by the shame of the palace intrigue that caused it. He cannot rest, cannot eat, and cannot settle his mind. The image shows grief as physical thirst.
ramacharitamanas::3219.modern_relevance: You lie awake after a message changes everything, staring at the ceiling while your body forgets hunger. Bharat's pain is what happens when love and regret become one knot.
ramacharitamanas::3219.insight: It shows how grief can become bodily and total, not just emotional.

ramacharitamanas::3220.verse_sanskrit: कीन्हि मातु मिस काल कुचाली। ईति भीति जस पाकत साली॥ केहि बिधि होइ राम अभिषेकू। मोहि अवकलत उपाउ न एकू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3220.verse_hindi: (भरतजी सोचते हैं कि) माता के मिस से काल ने कुचाल की है। जैसे धान के पकते समय ईति का भय आ उपस्थित हो। अब श्री रामचन्द्रजी का राज्याभिषेक किस प्रकार हो, मुझे तो एक भी उपाय नहीं सूझ पड़ता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3220.english_translation: By my mother’s pretext, fate has played a wicked trick, like a blight striking ripening rice. How can Ram's coronation happen now? I can see no way at all.
ramacharitamanas::3220.translation_literal: कीन्हि (did) / मातु (mother) / मिस (as a pretext) / काल (fate/time) / कुचाली (wicked trick) / ईति (blight, calamity) / भीति (fear) / जस (like) / पाकत (ripening) / साली (rice) / केहि बिधि (by what means) / होइ (will happen) / राम (Ram) / अभिषेकू (coronation) / मोहि (to me) / अवकलत (no way, helplessness) / उपाउ (means, solution) / न एकू (not even one)
ramacharitamanas::3220.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3220.essence: Grief can make every solution disappear.
ramacharitamanas::3220.simple_meaning: Bharat sees Kaikeyi’s demand as a cruel trick of fate. He feels helpless and cannot see any way to stop Ram’s coronation from being ruined.
ramacharitamanas::3220.simple_insight: Helplessness can make the mind see only the disaster, not the path forward.
ramacharitamanas::3220.detailed_meaning: Bharat is trapped inside the shock of Kaikeyi’s demand. He sees the planned coronation for Ram collapsing before his eyes and feels that no human effort can fix it. This is his grief turning into helpless thought.
ramacharitamanas::3220.modern_relevance: You open the email and realize one decision has wrecked the plan you spent months building. Your mind goes straight to panic: no fix, no backup, no way through.
ramacharitamanas::3220.insight: It shows how shock narrows attention to loss and blocks clear action.

ramacharitamanas::3221.verse_sanskrit: अवसि फिरहिं गुर आयसु मानी। मुनि पुनि कहब राम रुचि जानी॥ मातु कहेहुँ बहुरहिं रघुराऊ। राम जननि हठ करबि कि काऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3221.verse_hindi: गुरुजी की आज्ञा मानकर तो श्री रामजी अवश्य ही अयोध्या को लौट चलेंगे, परन्तु मुनि वशिष्ठजी तो श्री रामचन्द्रजी की रुचि जानकर ही कुछ कहेंगे। ( अर्थात वे श्री रामजी की रुचि देखे बिना जाने को नहीं कहेंगे)। माता कौसल्याजी के कहने से भी श्री रघुनाथजी लौट सकते हैं, पर भला, श्री रामजी को जन्म देने वाली माता क्या कभी हठ करेगी? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3221.english_translation: By obeying the teacher's command, Ram will surely return. Vashishtha will speak only after seeing Ram's own wish. Even if mother Kaushalya asks, Raghunath may return—but the mother who gave birth to Ram would never be stubborn.
ramacharitamanas::3221.translation_literal: अवसि (certainly) / फिरहिं (will return) / गुर (teacher's) / आयसु (command) / मानी (having obeyed) / मुनि (sage) / पुनि (again) / कहब (will speak) / राम (Ram's) / रुचि (wish) / जानी (having known) / मातु (mother) / कहेहुँ (even if said) / बहुरहिं (will return) / रघुराऊ (Raghunath) / राम (Ram) / जननि (mother) / हठ (insistence) / करबि (would do) / कि (would) / काऊ (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::3221.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3221.essence: Love is deepest when it refuses to coerce.
ramacharitamanas::3221.simple_meaning: Ram will return because he follows his teacher's command, and even his family speaks only after understanding his own wish. No one should force him.
ramacharitamanas::3221.simple_insight: Real love respects the other person's will instead of pushing its own agenda.
ramacharitamanas::3221.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat is weighing how Ram might be brought back from exile. This verse makes the hierarchy clear: the teacher's command matters, Ram's own wish matters, and even a mother's request cannot become pressure. The scene turns on restraint, not force.
ramacharitamanas::3221.modern_relevance: You're drafting the message that could change everything, then you stop and ask: is this what they want, or just what you want? Sometimes the most loving move is to wait for consent.
ramacharitamanas::3221.insight: It teaches you to honor authority and personal will before trying to influence a decision.

ramacharitamanas::3222.verse_sanskrit: मोहि अनुचर कर केतिक बाता। तेहि महँ कुसमउ बाम बिधाता॥ जौं हठ करउँ त निपट कुकरमू। हरगिरि तें गुरु सेवक धरमू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3222.verse_hindi: मुझ सेवक की तो बात ही कितनी है? उसमें भी समय खराब है (मेरे दिन अच्छे नहीं हैं) और विधाता प्रतिकूल है। यदि मैं हठ करता हूँ तो यह घोर कुकर्म (अधर्म) होगा, क्योंकि सेवक का धर्म शिवजी के पर्वत कैलास से भी भारी (निबाहने में कठिन) है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3222.english_translation: What am I, your servant, worth? The timing is already bad, and fate is against me. If I act stubbornly, it would be a grave wrong, because a servant’s duty is heavier to bear than Mount Kailash.
ramacharitamanas::3222.translation_literal: मोहि (to me) / अनुचर (servant, follower) / कर (as) / केतिक (how much) / बाता (matter, worth) / तेहि महँ (in that) / कुसमउ (bad time) / बाम (opposed, unfavourable) / बिधाता (the ordainer) ॥ जौं (if) / हठ (stubborn insistence) / करउँ (I do) / त (then) / निपट (utterly, completely) / कुकरमू (wrong deed, grave wrong) / हरगिरि (Mount Kailash) / तें (than) / गुरु (heavy, greater) / सेवक (servant) / धरमू (duty) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3222.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3222.essence: Stubborn force is wrong when service itself is the duty.
ramacharitamanas::3222.simple_meaning: Bharat sees himself as a servant who must not act out of stubbornness. For him, forcing things would be wrong, because true service is a serious and difficult duty.
ramacharitamanas::3222.simple_insight: Real service asks for humility, not insistence. The more sacred the role, the less room there is for ego.
ramacharitamanas::3222.detailed_meaning: Bharat has spent the night searching for a way to respond to Ram’s exile without betraying dharma. He feels his own limits, the bad timing, and the weight of service. In this moment he rejects stubborn action and measures himself against the hard duty of a servant.
ramacharitamanas::3222.modern_relevance: You are about to send the angry text, make the dramatic call, or force the meeting to go your way. Bharat’s pause reminds you that not every impulse deserves action.
ramacharitamanas::3222.insight: It shifts the mind from self-assertion to humble responsibility, where restraint is part of service.

ramacharitamanas::3223.verse_sanskrit: एकउ जुगुति न मन ठहरानी। सोचत भरतहि रैनि बिहानी॥ प्रात नहाइ प्रभुहि सिर नाई। बैठत पठए रिषयँ बोलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3223.verse_hindi: एक भी युक्ति भरतजी के मन में न ठहरी। सोचते ही सोचते रात बीत गई। भरतजी प्रातःकाल स्नान करके और प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी को सिर नवाकर बैठे ही थे कि ऋषि वशिष्ठजी ने उनको बुलवा भेजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3223.english_translation: No one solution stayed in Bharata's mind. The night passed while he kept thinking. At dawn, after bathing and bowing to Lord Ram, he sat down just as Vashishtha had him called.
ramacharitamanas::3223.translation_literal: एकउ (one) / जुगुति (solution) / न (not) / मन (mind) / ठहरानी (stayed)। / सोचत (thinking) / भरतहि (for Bharata) / रैनि (night) / बिहानी (passed)॥ / प्रात (morning) / नहाइ (bathed) / प्रभुहि (Lord) / सिर (head) / नाई (bowing) / बैठत (sitting) / पठए (sent) / रिषयँ (by the sage) / बोलाई (calling) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3223.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3223.essence: When the mind finds no answer, humility becomes the next right step.
ramacharitamanas::3223.simple_meaning: Bharat spent the night unable to settle on any answer. In the morning he bathed, bowed to Ram, and came when Vashishtha called him.
ramacharitamanas::3223.simple_insight: Some decisions are so heavy that even sleep cannot soften them.
ramacharitamanas::3223.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat is trapped in grief and duty after Ram's exile. He keeps searching for a way to respond, but none satisfies him. By morning he has only humility, devotion, and readiness to follow Vashishtha's call.
ramacharitamanas::3223.modern_relevance: You stare at your phone all night, trying to decide whether to send the message, resign, or stay silent. By dawn, the problem still exists — but your mind is finally tired enough to listen.
ramacharitamanas::3223.insight: It shows the mind exhausted by moral pressure, then returning to reverence before action.

ramacharitamanas::3224.verse_sanskrit: गुर पद कमल प्रनामु करि बैठे आयसु पाइ। बिप्र महाजन सचिव सब जुरे सभासद आइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3224.verse_hindi: भरतजी गुरु के चरणकमलों में प्रणाम करके आज्ञा पाकर बैठ गए। उसी समय ब्राह्मण, महाजन, मंत्री आदि सभी सभासद आकर जुट गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3224.english_translation: Bharat bowed at the guru's lotus feet and sat down after receiving permission. Then Brahmins, nobles, ministers, and all the assembly gathered there.
ramacharitamanas::3224.translation_literal: गुरु के चरण-कमलों को / प्रणामु (bowing) / करि (having done) / बैठे (sat) / आयसु (permission) / पाइ (having received) / बिप्र (Brahmins) / महाजन (nobles) / सचिव (ministers) / सब (all) / जुरे (gathered) / सभासद (assembly members) / आइ (coming)
ramacharitamanas::3224.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3224.essence: Humility opens the door before any hard truth can be spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3224.simple_meaning: Bharat shows respect to the teacher, takes permission, and sits down. The court then gathers around him.
ramacharitamanas::3224.simple_insight: Respect and order create the space for what must be said next.
ramacharitamanas::3224.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat has come burdened with grief and responsibility. After bowing to the guru and taking permission, he sits quietly as Brahmins, nobles, ministers, and other assembly members gather. The verse sets the scene for the counsel that follows.
ramacharitamanas::3224.modern_relevance: You arrive at a tense family meeting, say nothing first, and wait for the elders to settle the room. That pause changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::3224.insight: It shows how humility and proper order prepare the mind for serious counsel.

ramacharitamanas::3225.verse_sanskrit: बोले मुनिबरु समय समाना। सुनहु सभासद भरत सुजाना॥ धरम धुरीन भानुकुल भानू। राजा रामु स्वबस भगवानू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3225.verse_hindi: श्रेष्ठ मुनि वशिष्ठजी समयोचित वचन बोले- हे सभासदों! हे सुजान भरत! सुनो। सूर्यकुल के सूर्य महाराज श्री रामचन्द्र धर्मधुरंधर और स्वतंत्र भगवान हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3225.english_translation: The great sage said at the right moment, “Listen, assembly and wise Bharata. Ram, the sun of the Raghu line, is the upholder of dharma and the Lord who acts by his own will.”
ramacharitamanas::3225.translation_literal: बोले (spoke) / मुनिबरु (great sage) / समय (time) / समाना (appropriate) / सुनहु (listen) / सभासद (assembly members) / भरत (Bharata) / सुजाना (wise one) / धरम (dharma) / धुरीन (pillar-bearer) / भानुकुल (solar lineage) / भानू (sun) / राजा (king) / रामु (Ram) / स्वबस (self-governed) / भगवानू (the divine Lord)
ramacharitamanas::3225.speaker: Vashistha
ramacharitamanas::3225.essence: True authority comes from freedom aligned with dharma.
ramacharitamanas::3225.simple_meaning: Ram is described as the perfect king: devoted to dharma, noble like the sun, and completely self-governed. He acts from inner freedom, not pressure.
ramacharitamanas::3225.simple_insight: Real strength is not impulse or control by others, but freedom that still honors what is right.
ramacharitamanas::3225.detailed_meaning: In Bharata's assembly at Ayodhya, Vashistha steps in to steady the room. He reminds everyone that Ram is not an ordinary ruler: he is the Raghu line's shining heir, fully rooted in dharma and never ruled by anyone else.
ramacharitamanas::3225.modern_relevance: You’re in a meeting where everyone wants quick compliance, but the one person you trust is calm, principled, and impossible to pressure. That’s the kind of authority this verse honors.
ramacharitamanas::3225.insight: It shifts respect away from power and toward inner freedom aligned with duty.

ramacharitamanas::3226.verse_sanskrit: सत्यसंध पालक श्रुति सेतू। राम जनमु जग मंगल हेतु॥ गुर पितु मातु बचन अनुसारी। खल दलु दलन देव हितकारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3226.verse_hindi: वे सत्य प्रतिज्ञ हैं और वेद की मर्यादा के रक्षक हैं। श्री रामजी का अवतार ही जगत के कल्याण के लिए हुआ है। वे गुरु, पिता और माता के वचनों के अनुसार चलने वाले हैं। दुष्टों के दल का नाश करने वाले और देवताओं के हितकारी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3226.english_translation: He is true to his word and upholds the boundary of the sacred law. Ram's birth came for the world's welfare. He follows the words of his teacher, father, and mother, and destroys the host of the wicked while bringing benefit to the radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::3226.translation_literal: सत्यसंध (true to his vow) / पालक (upholder) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / सेतू (bridge, boundary) / राम जनमु (Ram's birth) / जग मंगल हेतु (for the world's welfare) / गुर (teacher) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / बचन (words) / अनुसारी (following) / खल दलु (host of the wicked) / दलन (destroyer) / देव हितकारी (benefactor of the radiant beings)
ramacharitamanas::3226.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3226.essence: Ram's greatness is that his life serves truth, order, and the welfare of all.
ramacharitamanas::3226.simple_meaning: Ram is described as truthful, obedient to his parents and teacher, born for the world's welfare, and a destroyer of harmful forces.
ramacharitamanas::3226.simple_insight: There is strength in a life that stays faithful to duty and still serves everyone around it.
ramacharitamanas::3226.detailed_meaning: In Bharata's assembly at Nandigram, Vashistha is praising Ram before the gathered elders. He says Ram's life is built on truth, reverence for teachers and parents, and protection of order. This sets up why Ram alone deserves the throne.
ramacharitamanas::3226.modern_relevance: You sign a contract, call your parents back, and show up for the team even when no one is watching. This verse measures greatness by whether your life can be trusted.
ramacharitamanas::3226.insight: It shifts attention from charisma to character: truthfulness, obedience to rightful guidance, and service to the larger good.

ramacharitamanas::3227.verse_sanskrit: नीति प्रीति परमारथ स्वारथु। कोउ न राम सम जान जथारथु॥ बिधि हरि हरु ससि रबि दिसिपाला। माया जीव करम कुलि काला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3227.verse_hindi: नीति, प्रेम, परमार्थ और स्वार्थ को श्री रामजी के समान यथार्थ (तत्त्व से) कोई नहीं जानता। ब्रह्मा, विष्णु, महादेव, चन्द्र, सूर्य, दिक्पाल, माया, जीव, सभी कर्म और काल, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3227.english_translation: No one knows policy, love, supreme purpose, and self-interest as Ram truly does. Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, the moon, the sun, the guardians of the directions, Maya, the living being, karma, the clans, and time itself all stand within his knowing.
ramacharitamanas::3227.translation_literal: नीति (right conduct/policy) / प्रीति (love) / परमारथ (highest purpose) / स्वारथु (self-interest) / कोउ (anyone) / न (not) / राम सम (like Ram) / जान (knows) / जथारथु (truly, as it is) ॥ बिधि (Brahma) / हरि (Vishnu/Ram) / हरु (Shiva) / ससि (moon) / रबि (sun) / दिसिपाला (guardians of the directions) / माया (the veil of appearance) / जीव (the living being) / करम (karma) / कुलि (clans) / काला (time) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3227.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3227.essence: Ram alone sees duty, love, and self-interest exactly as they are.
ramacharitamanas::3227.simple_meaning: Ram understands right conduct, love, higher purpose, and self-interest perfectly. Even the great cosmic forces and time itself are within his full awareness.
ramacharitamanas::3227.simple_insight: You do not have to explain yourself to the one who already sees everything clearly.
ramacharitamanas::3227.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Vashishtha is speaking to the assembly about Ram before Bharat. He lifts Ram above every cosmic power, saying that no being understands life, desire, duty, and time as Ram does. The praise prepares Bharat to see Ram as the rightful king.
ramacharitamanas::3227.modern_relevance: You are trying to justify a choice to three different people, then rereading the message for the tenth time. Ram already sees the clean intention beneath all the noise.
ramacharitamanas::3227.insight: It shifts attention from self-justification to trusting the clarity of Ram's vision.

ramacharitamanas::3228.verse_sanskrit: अहिप महिप जहँ लगि प्रभुताई। जोग सिद्धि निगमागम गाई॥ करि बिचार जियँ देखहु नीकें। राम रजाइ सीस सबही कें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3228.verse_hindi: शेषजी और (पृथ्वी एवं पाताल के अन्यान्य) राजा आदि जहाँ तक प्रभुता है और योग की सिद्धियाँ, जो वेद और शास्त्रों में गाई गई हैं, हृदय में अच्छी तरह विचार कर देखो, (तो यह स्पष्ट दिखाई देगा कि) श्री रामजी की आज्ञा इन सभी के सिर पर है (अर्थात श्री रामजी ही सबके एक मात्र महान महेश्वर हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3228.english_translation: Wherever there is rule—among serpents, kings of the earth, or the underworld—wherever yoga powers and perfected attainments are praised in the Vedas and scriptures, reflect carefully and see: Ram's command rests above them all.
ramacharitamanas::3228.translation_literal: अहिप (among serpents) / महिप (among kings of the earth) / जहँ लगि (as far as) / प्रभुताई (lordship, rule) / जोग (yoga) / सिद्धि (perfections) / निगमागम (Vedas and scriptures) / गाई (are sung) / करि (having done) / बिचार (reflection) / जियँ (in the heart) / देखहु (see) / नीकें (well) / राम (Ram) / रजाइ (command, will) / सीस (head) / सबही (of all) / कें (on)
ramacharitamanas::3228.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3228.essence: All power is borrowed; Ram's command is the source.
ramacharitamanas::3228.simple_meaning: All power, mastery, and even spiritual attainments are ultimately under Ram's command. Nothing stands above his will.
ramacharitamanas::3228.simple_insight: It softens pride by showing that every form of control is limited.
ramacharitamanas::3228.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas pauses the exile story to widen the lens. He says that rulers, sages, and even perfected powers all remain under Ram's authority. The point is to humble human pride and show where true sovereignty lies.
ramacharitamanas::3228.modern_relevance: You finally get the promotion, the title, the authority — and then one bad email reminds you how fragile it all is. This verse puts every kind of power back in its place.
ramacharitamanas::3228.insight: It shifts you from chasing control to recognising a higher order already governing it.

ramacharitamanas::3229.verse_sanskrit: राखें राम रजाइ रुख हम सब कर हित होइ। समुझि सयाने करहु अब सब मिलि संमत सोइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3229.verse_hindi: अतएव श्री रामजी की आज्ञा और रुख रखने में ही हम सबका हित होगा। (इस तत्त्व और रहस्य को समझकर) अब तुम सयाने लोग जो सबको सम्मत हो, वही मिलकर करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3229.english_translation: Therefore, keeping Ram's command is what will benefit us all. Understanding this well, you wise ones should now agree together on what is best.
ramacharitamanas::3229.translation_literal: राखें (to keep) / राम (Ram) / रजाइ (command, wish) / रुख (direction, intention) / हम (we) / सब (all) / कर (of) / हित (welfare, benefit) / होइ (will be) / समुझि (having understood) / सयाने (wise ones) / करहु (do) / अब (now) / सब (all) / मिलि (together) / संमत (agreed, approved) / सोइ (that same thing)
ramacharitamanas::3229.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3229.essence: What serves Ram also serves everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3229.simple_meaning: Real welfare comes from following Ram's command. Once you see that clearly, wise people should agree and act together.
ramacharitamanas::3229.simple_insight: There is calm in choosing what is right over what is merely preferred.
ramacharitamanas::3229.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the elders are weighing how to respond after Ram's exile. Tulsidas cuts through the debate: the real good of everyone lies in accepting Ram's command. This verse pushes the assembly toward agreement.
ramacharitamanas::3229.modern_relevance: A family group chat is spiralling over who should make the next decision, and everyone is arguing from ego. This verse points to the relief of choosing the option that serves the whole, not just the loudest voice.
ramacharitamanas::3229.insight: It shifts decision-making from personal preference to shared alignment with dharma.

ramacharitamanas::3230.verse_sanskrit: सब कहुँ सुखद राम अभिषेकू। मंगल मोद मूल मग एकू॥ केहि बिधि अवध चलहिं रघुराऊ। कहहु समुझि सोइ करिअ उपाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3230.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी का राज्याभिषेक सबके लिए सुखदायक है। मंगल और आनंद का मूल यही एक मार्ग है। (अब) श्री रघुनाथजी अयोध्या किस प्रकार चलें? विचारकर कहो, वही उपाय किया जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3230.english_translation: Ram's coronation would bring happiness to everyone. It is the one path from which auspiciousness and joy arise. But how should Lord Raghunath return to Ayodhya? Think carefully and say what plan should be made.
ramacharitamanas::3230.translation_literal: सब कहुँ (for everyone) / सुखद (bringing happiness) / राम अभिषेकू (Ram's coronation) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / मोद (joy) / मूल (source) / मग (path) / एकू (one) ॥ / केहि बिधि (by what way) / अवध (to Ayodhya) / चलहिं (should go) / रघुराऊ (Lord Raghunath) / कहहु (tell) / समुझि (after considering) / सोइ (that) / करिअ (should be done) / उपाऊ (plan) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3230.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3230.essence: The best outcome still needs the right way home.
ramacharitamanas::3230.simple_meaning: Ram's coronation would bless everyone, so the only question is how to bring him safely back to Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::3230.simple_insight: When the good of all is clear, the mind turns to finding the right way, not the easiest way.
ramacharitamanas::3230.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Ram's exile has been reversed in thought, the court sees his coronation as the source of everyone's happiness. The remaining problem is practical: how can Raghunath be brought home in a way that honours that joy?
ramacharitamanas::3230.modern_relevance: You finally know the decision is right, but the hard part is logistics: how do you bring it about without breaking trust, timing, or relationships?
ramacharitamanas::3230.insight: It shifts attention from debating the goal to arranging the most dharmic means.

ramacharitamanas::3231.verse_sanskrit: सब सादर सुनि मुनिबर बानी। नय परमारथ स्वारथ सानी॥ उतरु न आव लोग भए भोरे। तब सिरु नाइ भरत कर जोरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3231.verse_hindi: मुनिश्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी की नीति, परमार्थ और स्वार्थ (लौकिक हित) में सनी हुई वाणी सबने आदरपूर्वक सुनी। पर किसी को कोई उत्तर नहीं आता, सब लोग भोले (विचार शक्ति से रहित) हो गए। तब भरत ने सिर नवाकर हाथ जोड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::3231.english_translation: Everyone respectfully heard the sage's words, mixed with policy, higher purpose, and worldly benefit. No one had an answer; everyone fell silent. Then Bharat bowed his head and joined his hands.
ramacharitamanas::3231.translation_literal: सब (all) / सादर (respectfully) / सुनि (hearing) / मुनिबर (best among sages) / बानी (words) / नय (policy) / परमारथ (higher purpose) / स्वारथ (worldly benefit) / सानी (mixed)॥ / उतरु (answer) / न (not) / आव (came) / लोग (people) / भए (became) / भोरे (dazed/naive)॥ / तब (then) / सिरु (head) / नाइ (bowing) / भरत (Bharat) / कर (hands) / जोरे (joined)॥
ramacharitamanas::3231.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3231.essence: Humility can answer where argument cannot.
ramacharitamanas::3231.simple_meaning: Everyone listens to the sage's wise words but cannot answer. Bharat responds not with debate, but with humility and respect.
ramacharitamanas::3231.simple_insight: There is strength in not rushing to defend yourself. Quiet respect can be wiser than clever speech.
ramacharitamanas::3231.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the court is trying to decide how to respond to Ram's exile and the crisis around the throne. Vashishtha speaks with a mix of policy, duty, and higher purpose. The others fall silent, and Bharat answers with a bow, showing humility before action.
ramacharitamanas::3231.modern_relevance: A tense family meeting goes quiet after the elder finishes speaking. Everyone has opinions, but no one has the heart to force them. Then the person who loves most lowers their head first.
ramacharitamanas::3231.insight: It shifts you from argumentative certainty to respectful receptivity, where humility becomes the first right move.

ramacharitamanas::3232.verse_sanskrit: भानुबंस भए भूप घनेरे। अधिक एक तें एक बड़ेरे॥ जनम हेतु सब कहँ कितु माता। करम सुभासुभ देइ बिधाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3232.verse_hindi: (और कहा-) सूर्यवंश में एक से एक अधिक बड़े बहुत से राजा हो गए हैं। सभी के जन्म के कारण पिता-माता होते हैं और शुभ-अशुभ कर्मों को (कर्मों का फल) विधाता देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3232.english_translation: Many kings have ruled in the Solar dynasty, each greater than the last. Every being has a mother and father for birth, but the supreme being gives the results of good and bad actions.
ramacharitamanas::3232.translation_literal: भानुबंस (Solar dynasty) / भए (were) / भूप (kings) / घनेरे (many) / अधिक (greater) / एक तें एक (one than another) / बड़ेरे (very great)॥ / जनम (birth) / हेतु (cause) / सब कहँ (for all) / कितु (indeed) / माता (mother) / पिता (father) / करम (actions) / सुभासुभ (good and bad) / देइ (gives) / बिधाता (the ordainer)॥
ramacharitamanas::3232.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3232.essence: Birth comes from parents, but consequences come from action.
ramacharitamanas::3232.simple_meaning: Many great kings have ruled before, but birth comes from parents while the results of actions come from the supreme order.
ramacharitamanas::3232.simple_insight: You are not defined only by where you came from; what you do still matters deeply.
ramacharitamanas::3232.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands before the gathered elders in Ayodhya, speaking after the failed attempt to settle Ram's exile. He widens the view from one family crisis to the whole Solar dynasty, reminding everyone that birth has its source, but moral consequence comes from a higher order.
ramacharitamanas::3232.modern_relevance: You can trace your family tree for hours, but it won't explain why one choice wrecked trust and another repaired it. The deeper pattern is in what you do, not just where you came from.
