ramacharitamanas::3232.insight: It shifts attention from ancestry and status to moral causation and responsibility.

ramacharitamanas::3233.verse_sanskrit: दलि दुख सजइ सकल कल्याना। अस असीस राउरि जगु जाना॥ सो गोसाइँ बिधि गति जेहिं छेंकी। सकइ को टारि टेक जो टेकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3233.verse_hindi: आपकी आशीष ही एक ऐसी है, जो दुःखों का दमन करके, समस्त कल्याणों को सज देती है, यह जगत जानता है। हे स्वामी! आप ही हैं, जिन्होंने विधाता की गति (विधान) को भी रोक दिया। आपने जो टेक टेक दी (जो निश्चय कर दिया) उसे कौन टाल सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3233.english_translation: Your blessing alone can crush sorrow and arrange every blessing. The world knows this, my lord. You are the one who can even stop the course of fate. Who can turn aside what you have firmly resolved?
ramacharitamanas::3233.translation_literal: दलि (crushing) / दुख (sorrow) / सजइ (arranges) / सकल (all) / कल्याना (auspiciousness, blessings) / अस (such) / असीस (blessing) / राउरि (your) / जगु (world) / जाना (knows) ॥ सो (that) / गोसाइँ (lord) / बिधि (fate, the creator's ordering) / गति (course) / जेहिं (by whom) / छेंकी (blocked) / सकइ (can) / को (who) / टारि (turn aside) / टेक (firm resolve) / जो (which) / टेकी (you have set) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3233.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3233.essence: Ram's blessing makes sorrow powerless and gives resolve the final word.
ramacharitamanas::3233.simple_meaning: Bharat praises the power of Ram's blessing and steadfast resolve. Ram's grace removes sorrow, brings good fortune, and cannot be resisted once firmly set.
ramacharitamanas::3233.simple_insight: There is relief in trusting a will wiser than your own.
ramacharitamanas::3233.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands before the elders in Ayodhya, speaking with humility and love after Ram's exile. He praises Ram's blessing as stronger than sorrow and even stronger than fate itself, because Ram's resolve cannot be deflected.
ramacharitamanas::3233.modern_relevance: You are spiralling over a decision you cannot control, then someone you trust says, “Leave it to me.” The body relaxes because their steadiness is stronger than your panic.
ramacharitamanas::3233.insight: It shifts you from anxiety about outcomes to trust in a steady, protective presence.

ramacharitamanas::3234.verse_sanskrit: बूझिअ मोहि उपाउ अब सो सब मोर अभागु। सुनि सनेहमय बचनगुर उर उमगा अनुरागु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3234.verse_hindi: अब आप मुझसे उपाय पूछते हैं, यह सब मेरा अभाग्य है। भरतजी के प्रेममय वचनों को सुनकर गुरुजी के हृदय में प्रेम उमड़ आया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3234.english_translation: Now you ask me for a solution, but all of this is my own misfortune. Hearing Bharat's loving words, the teacher's heart overflowed with affection.
ramacharitamanas::3234.translation_literal: बूझिअ (you ask) / मोहि (me) / उपाउ (remedy, solution) / अब (now) / सो (that) / सब (all) / मोर (my) / अभागु (misfortune) / सुनि (hearing) / सनेहमय (full of love) / बचन (words) / गुर (the teacher) / उर (heart) / उमगा (overflowed) / अनुरागु (love, affection)
ramacharitamanas::3234.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3234.essence: Sincere love can turn misfortune into a moment of grace.
ramacharitamanas::3234.simple_meaning: Bharat says the solution is not in his hands; he sees his situation as misfortune. His loving words move the teacher deeply.
ramacharitamanas::3234.simple_insight: Love can soften a hardened heart, even in the middle of grief.
ramacharitamanas::3234.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat speaks with humility and sorrow, asking for guidance while calling his own condition unfortunate. His tender words stir the teacher's heart, showing how sincere love changes the emotional atmosphere of the scene.
ramacharitamanas::3234.modern_relevance: You finally admit you don't know what to do, and someone answers with kindness instead of correction. That tenderness can change everything.
ramacharitamanas::3234.insight: It shows how humility and loving speech can open the way for guidance.

ramacharitamanas::3235.verse_sanskrit: तात बात फुरि राम कृपाहीं। राम बिमुख सिधि सपनेहुँ नाहीं॥ सकुचउँ तात कहत एक बाता। अरध तजहिं बुध सरबस जाता॥1।
ramacharitamanas::3235.verse_hindi: (वे बोले-) हे तात! बात सत्य है, पर है रामजी की कृपा से ही। राम विमुख को तो स्वप्न में भी सिद्धि नहीं मिलती। हे तात! मैं एक बात कहने में सकुचाता हूँ। बुद्धिमान लोग सर्वस्व जाता देखकर (आधे की रक्षा के लिए) आधा छोड़ दिया करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3235.english_translation: “Father, the matter is true, but only through Ram’s grace. The one who turns away from Ram finds no success, even in a dream. Father, I hesitate to say one thing: wise people abandon half when they see the whole lost.”
ramacharitamanas::3235.translation_literal: तात (father) / बात (matter) / फुरि (true) / राम (Ram) / कृपाहीं (by grace) / राम (Ram) / बिमुख (turned away from) / सिधि (success / accomplishment) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / नाहीं (not) / सकुचउँ (I hesitate) / तात (father) / कहत (saying) / एक (one) / बाता (matter) / अरध (half) / तजहिं (they abandon) / बुध (wise people) / सरबस (the whole / everything) / जाता (gone / lost)
ramacharitamanas::3235.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3235.essence: When the whole is lost, wisdom protects the half that remains.
ramacharitamanas::3235.simple_meaning: Success does not come from turning away from Ram, and a wise person saves what can still be saved instead of losing everything.
ramacharitamanas::3235.simple_insight: You do not need to cling to pride; sometimes wisdom is knowing what to keep and what to release.
ramacharitamanas::3235.detailed_meaning: Bharat speaks to his father in Ayodhya, trying to answer grief with truth. He says Ram’s grace alone makes success possible, and that wise people give up even half if the whole is already slipping away.
ramacharitamanas::3235.modern_relevance: You realize a project is collapsing, but your ego still wants to defend every part of it. This verse says: stop clinging to the whole fantasy; save what remains and let the rest go.
ramacharitamanas::3235.insight: It shifts you from stubborn attachment to practical discernment when loss is already unavoidable.

ramacharitamanas::3236.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह कानन गवनहु दोउ भाई। फेरिअहिं लखन सीय रघुराई॥ सुनि सुबचन हरषे दोउ भ्राता। भे प्रमोद परिपूरन गाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3236.verse_hindi: अतः तुम दोनों भाई (भरत-शत्रुघ्न) वन को जाओ और लक्ष्मण, सीता और श्री रामचन्द्र को लौटा दिया जाए। ये सुंदर वचन सुनकर दोनों भाई हर्षित हो गए। उनके सारे अंग परमानंद से परिपूर्ण हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3236.english_translation: So you two brothers should go to the forest, and Lakshman, Sita, and Lord Ram should be brought back. Hearing these gracious words, both brothers rejoiced; their whole bodies were filled with bliss.
ramacharitamanas::3236.translation_literal: तुम्ह (you) / कानन (forest) / गवनहु (go) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / फेरिअहिं (may be brought back) / लखन (Lakshman) / सीय (Sita) / रघुराई (Lord of the Raghu clan) / सुनि (hearing) / सुबचन (gracious words) / हरषे (rejoiced) / दोउ (both) / भ्राता (brothers) / भे (became) / प्रमोद (joy) / परिपूरन (completely filled) / गाता (bodies)
ramacharitamanas::3236.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3236.essence: Love can turn exile into a path home.
ramacharitamanas::3236.simple_meaning: The brothers are told to go to the forest and bring Ram, Sita, and Lakshman back. Hearing this, they become overjoyed.
ramacharitamanas::3236.simple_insight: Relief can arrive in one sentence, and suddenly the whole body knows it.
ramacharitamanas::3236.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat and Shatrughna hear a decisive, loving instruction: go to the forest and bring Ram, Sita, and Lakshman home. The tension of exile softens for a moment, and their joy floods through them.
ramacharitamanas::3236.modern_relevance: You hear the text message you have been praying for: come home, it’s settled. Your shoulders drop before you even finish reading.
ramacharitamanas::3236.insight: It shows how a single clear decision can dissolve grief and restore energy at once.

ramacharitamanas::3237.verse_sanskrit: मन प्रसन्न तन तेजु बिराजा। जनु जिय राउ रामु भए राजा॥ बहुत लाभ लोगन्ह लघु हानी। सम दुख सुख सब रोवहिं रानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3237.verse_hindi: उनके मन प्रसन्न हो गए। शरीर में तेज सुशोभित हो गया। मानो राजा दशरथजी उठे हों और श्री रामचन्द्रजी राजा हो गए हों! अन्य लोगों को तो इसमें लाभ अधिक और हानि कम प्रतीत हुई, परन्तु रानियों को दुःख-सुख समान ही थे (राम-लक्ष्मण वन में रहें या भरत-शत्रुघ्न, दो पुत्रों का वियोग तो रहेगा ही), यह समझकर वे सब रोने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3237.english_translation: Their minds grew joyful, and their bodies shone with radiance, as if King Dasharath had risen and Ram had become king. Others saw little loss and much gain, but the queens saw equal grief and joy, and they all wept.
ramacharitamanas::3237.translation_literal: मन (mind) / प्रसन्न (delighted) / तन (body) / तेजु (radiance) / बिराजा (shone) / जनु (as if) / जिय (alive) / राउ (king) / रामु (Ram) / भए (became) / राजा (king) / बहुत (much) / लाभ (gain) / लोगन्ह (for the people) / लघु (small) / हानी (loss) / रानी (queens) / सम (equal) / दुख (pain) / सुख (joy) / सब (all) / रोवहिं (weep) / रानी (queens)
ramacharitamanas::3237.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3237.essence: A triumph can still leave the deepest love in tears.
ramacharitamanas::3237.simple_meaning: The family’s mood lifts at the thought of Ram returning to rule, but the queens still feel the pain of separation and begin to cry.
ramacharitamanas::3237.simple_insight: Joy and grief can sit in the same heart at once.
ramacharitamanas::3237.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyā, the news of Ram’s return briefly lights up the palace. Dasharath seems alive again in everyone’s imagination. But the queens know the deeper cost: even a happy turn cannot erase the pain of separation from their sons, so their joy breaks into tears.
ramacharitamanas::3237.modern_relevance: You get the promotion you wanted, and everyone celebrates. But at home, the family still feels the strain of what the win cost. Relief and loss can arrive together.
ramacharitamanas::3237.insight: It shows how a single event can be victory for some and sorrow for others.

ramacharitamanas::3238.verse_sanskrit: कहहिं भरतु मुनि कहा सो कीन्हे। फलु जग जीवन्ह अभिमत दीन्हे॥ कानन करउँ जनम भरि बासू। एहि तें अधिक न मोर सुपासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3238.verse_hindi: भरतजी कहने लगे- मुनि ने जो कहा, वह करने से जगतभर के जीवों को उनकी इच्छित वस्तु देने का फल होगा। (चौदह वर्ष की कोई अवधि नहीं) मैं जन्मभर वन में वास करूँगा। मेरे लिए इससे बढ़कर और कोई सुख नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3238.english_translation: Bharat said, "What the sage said, let that be done. The fruit will be to give every being in the world what they long for. I will live in the forest for my whole life. Nothing is more pleasing to me than this."
ramacharitamanas::3238.translation_literal: कहहिं (they say) / भरतु (Bharat) / मुनि (sage) / कहा (what) / सो (that) / कीन्हे (by doing) / फलु (fruit) / जग (world) / जीवन्ह (living beings) / अभिमत (desired) / दीन्हे (given) / कानन (forest) / करउँ (I will do) / जनम (life) / भरि (for the whole) / बासू (residence) / एहि तें (than this) / अधिक (greater) / न (not) / मोर (my) / सुपासू (pleasure)
ramacharitamanas::3238.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3238.essence: True non-attachment can make hardship feel like the sweetest choice.
ramacharitamanas::3238.simple_meaning: Bharat decides to accept the sage's instruction and live in the forest for life. He sees this as the best possible choice, because it serves everyone and removes his own claim to comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3238.simple_insight: Peace comes when you stop treating comfort as the highest good.
ramacharitamanas::3238.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat has been offered the throne, but his heart is fixed on Ram's exile and the sage's counsel. He says he will live in the forest for life, because that choice feels truer than any royal comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3238.modern_relevance: You turn down a promotion because it would pull you away from what you know is right. The room goes quiet, but inside you feel steady. Bharat knows that refusing ease can be the cleanest form of love.
ramacharitamanas::3238.insight: It shifts you from chasing personal ease to choosing the life that best honors dharma.

ramacharitamanas::3239.verse_sanskrit: अंतरजामी रामु सिय तुम्ह सरबग्य सुजान। जौं फुर कहहु त नाथ निज कीजिअ बचनु प्रवान ॥
ramacharitamanas::3239.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी और सीताजी हृदय की जानने वाले हैं और आप सर्वज्ञ तथा सुजान हैं। यदि आप यह सत्य कह रहे हैं तो हे नाथ! अपने वचनों को प्रमाण कीजिए (उनके अनुसार व्यवस्था कीजिए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3239.english_translation: Ram and Sita know the heart, and you are all-knowing and wise. If this is truly spoken, then, my lord, make your word real.
ramacharitamanas::3239.translation_literal: अंतरजामी (knower of the heart) / रामु (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / तुम्ह (you) / सरबग्य (all-knowing) / सुजान (wise) / जौं (if) / फुर (true) / कहहु (you say) / त (then) / नाथ (lord) / निज (your own) / कीजिअ (make) / बचनु (word) / प्रवान (valid, proven)
ramacharitamanas::3239.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3239.essence: A true promise must become visible in action.
ramacharitamanas::3239.simple_meaning: Bharat says Ram and Sita know the heart, so if Ram's promise is true, it should be fulfilled in action.
ramacharitamanas::3239.simple_insight: Trust becomes stronger when words are matched by lived reality.
ramacharitamanas::3239.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is pleading with the sages and the court after Ram has been sent away. He knows Ram sees through every heart. So he asks for one thing only: if this promise is true, let it be made real.
ramacharitamanas::3239.modern_relevance: You’re in a tense family conversation where everyone says the right thing, but nothing changes. Bharat’s standard is simple: if the promise is real, let life show it.
ramacharitamanas::3239.insight: It shifts you from accepting polished speech to asking whether a promise is actually being honoured.

ramacharitamanas::3240.verse_sanskrit: भरत बचन सुनि देखि सनेहू। सभा सहित मुनि भए बिदेहू॥ भरत महा महिमा जलरासी। मुनि मति ठाढ़ि तीर अबला सी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3240.verse_hindi: भरतजी के वचन सुनकर और उनका प्रेम देखकर सारी सभा सहित मुनि वशिष्ठजी विदेह हो गए (किसी को अपने देह की सुधि न रही)। भरतजी की महान महिमा समुद्र है, मुनि की बुद्धि उसके तट पर अबला स्त्री के समान खड़ी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3240.english_translation: Hearing Bharat's words and seeing his love, the sage and the whole assembly were left speechless. Bharat's greatness is an ocean; the sage's mind stood at its shore like a helpless woman.
ramacharitamanas::3240.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / बचन (words) / सुनि (having heard) / देखि (seeing) / सनेहू (affection, love) / सभा (assembly) / सहित (together with) / मुनि (sage) / भए (became) / बिदेहू (without bodily awareness) ॥ / भरत (Bharat) / महा (great) / महिमा (glory, greatness) / जलरासी (ocean) / मुनि (sage's) / मति (mind, understanding) / ठाढ़ि (standing) / तीर (shore) / अबला (helpless woman) / सी (like) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3240.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3240.essence: True greatness can leave even wisdom speechless.
ramacharitamanas::3240.simple_meaning: Bharat's love overwhelms everyone present so completely that they lose track of their bodies. His greatness is so vast that even the sage's understanding can only stand at its edge.
ramacharitamanas::3240.simple_insight: Real devotion can be so vast that words and logic fall silent.
ramacharitamanas::3240.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat comes with such humility and love that Vasistha and the whole assembly are stunned. The scene is not teaching a doctrine so much as showing the force of Bharat's character: his devotion is too deep for ordinary speech.
ramacharitamanas::3240.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose sincerity is so complete that the room changes. Nobody argues, performs, or postures anymore — everyone just feels the weight of what is real.
ramacharitamanas::3240.insight: It shifts attention from clever explanation to the power of lived devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3241.verse_sanskrit: गा चह पार जतनु हियँ हेरा। पावति नाव न बोहितु बेरा॥ औरु करिहि को भरत बड़ाई। सरसी सीपि कि सिंधु समाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3241.verse_hindi: वह (उस समुद्र के) पार जाना चाहती है, इसके लिए उसने हृदय में उपाय भी ढूँढे! पर (उसे पार करने का साधन) नाव, जहाज या बेड़ा कुछ भी नहीं पाती। भरतजी की बड़ाई और कौन करेगा? तलैया की सीपी में भी कहीं समुद्र समा सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3241.english_translation: She wants to cross to the far shore and has searched for a way in her heart, but she finds no boat, ship, or raft. Who else can praise Bharata’s greatness? Can the ocean fit inside a pond’s shell?
ramacharitamanas::3241.translation_literal: गा (wants to go) / चह (wants) / पार (the far shore) / जतनु (means, effort) / हियँ (in the heart) / हेरा (searched) / पावति (finds) / नाव (boat) / न (not) / बोहितु (ship) / बेरा (raft) / औरु (and) / करिहि (will do) / को (who) / भरत (Bharata) / बड़ाई (praise, greatness) / सरसी (pond) / सीपि (shell) / कि (can) / सिंधु (ocean) / समाई (fit, be contained)
ramacharitamanas::3241.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3241.essence: Real greatness cannot be contained by ordinary praise.
ramacharitamanas::3241.simple_meaning: Bharata's virtue is so immense that ordinary praise cannot contain it. The verse says his greatness is as vast as the ocean, while praise is only a tiny shell.
ramacharitamanas::3241.simple_insight: Some people are larger than the language used to describe them.
ramacharitamanas::3241.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the assembly has just been shaken by Bharata’s humility and devotion. The speaker reaches for an image big enough to hold him, but even that fails: Bharata’s character is like an ocean, and praise is only a shell.
ramacharitamanas::3241.modern_relevance: You try to explain someone who quietly carried a family through crisis, and every sentence feels too small. Their goodness doesn’t fit in compliments, because it was never built for display.
ramacharitamanas::3241.insight: It shifts attention from polished praise to the scale of lived character.

ramacharitamanas::3242.verse_sanskrit: भरतु मुनिहि मन भीतर भाए। सहित समाज राम पहिं आए॥ प्रभु प्रनामु करि दीन्ह सुआसनु। बैठे सब सुनि मुनि अनुसासनु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3242.verse_hindi: मुनि वशिष्ठजी की अन्तरात्मा को भरतजी बहुत अच्छे लगे और वे समाज सहित श्री रामजी के पास आए। प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने प्रणाम कर उत्तम आसन दिया। सब लोग मुनि की आज्ञा सुनकर बैठ गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3242.english_translation: Bharat pleased the sage within his heart, and came with his companions to Rama. Lord Rama bowed to him and offered a fine seat. Everyone sat down after hearing the sage's instruction.
ramacharitamanas::3242.translation_literal: भरतु (Bharat) / मुनिहि (to the sage) / मन भीतर (within the mind) / भाए (became pleasing) / सहित समाज (with the gathering) / राम पहिं (to Rama) / आए (came) ॥ / प्रभु (the Lord) / प्रनामु करि (having bowed) / दीन्ह (gave) / सुआसनु (a fine seat) / बैठे (sat) / सब (all) / सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (the sage's) / अनुसासनु (instruction) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3242.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3242.essence: Honor and humility create the space where wisdom can be heard.
ramacharitamanas::3242.simple_meaning: Bharat comes to Rama with the assembly. Rama honors him with respect, and everyone sits down to hear the sage's guidance.
ramacharitamanas::3242.simple_insight: Respect opens the way for wisdom; humility makes room for everyone to listen.
ramacharitamanas::3242.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat arrives with his companions and wins the sage's approval by his sincerity. Rama greets him with honor and offers a seat. The whole assembly settles in, ready for Vashishtha's instruction.
ramacharitamanas::3242.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense family meeting and choose respect first. That single gesture lowers the temperature enough for everyone to actually hear each other.
ramacharitamanas::3242.insight: It shows that humility and courtesy prepare the mind for guidance.

ramacharitamanas::3243.verse_sanskrit: बोले मुनिबरु बचन बिचारी। देस काल अवसर अनुहारी॥ सुनहु राम सरबग्य सुजाना। धरम नीति गुन ग्यान निधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3243.verse_hindi: श्रेष्ठ मुनि देश, काल और अवसर के अनुसार विचार करके वचन बोले- हे सर्वज्ञ! हे सुजान! हे धर्म, नीति, गुण और ज्ञान के भण्डार राम! सुनिए- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3243.english_translation: The great sage spoke, considering the place, time, and occasion. 'Listen, Ram, all-knowing and wise, treasury of dharma, policy, qualities, and wisdom.'
ramacharitamanas::3243.translation_literal: बोले (spoke) / मुनिबरु (great sage) / बचन (words) / बिचारी (having considered) / देस (place) / काल (time) / अवसर (occasion) / अनुहारी (suited to) ॥ सुनहु (listen) / राम (Ram) / सरबग्य (all-knowing) / सुजाना (wise) / धरम (dharma) / नीति (policy / right conduct) / गुन (qualities) / ग्यान (wisdom) / निधाना (treasury) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3243.speaker: Vasishta
ramacharitamanas::3243.essence: Wise speech fits the moment before it seeks to persuade.
ramacharitamanas::3243.simple_meaning: The sage speaks carefully, choosing words suited to the moment, and addresses Ram as the one who knows dharma, right conduct, virtues, and wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::3243.simple_insight: Good guidance begins with reading the moment clearly before speaking.
ramacharitamanas::3243.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Vasishta turns to Ram after Bharat arrives with the assembly. He speaks with care, matching his words to place, time, and need, because the next counsel must guide a painful family crisis without causing more harm.
ramacharitamanas::3243.modern_relevance: You are about to send a message into a tense family group chat. The right words matter as much as the right intention. Wisdom begins by reading the room.
ramacharitamanas::3243.insight: It teaches you to shape speech to context instead of blurting out what is true in general.

ramacharitamanas::3244.verse_sanskrit: सब के उर अंतर बसहु जानहु भाउ कुभाउ। पुरजन जननी भरत हित होइ सो कहिअ उपाउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3244.verse_hindi: आप सबके हृदय के भीतर बसते हैं और सबके भले-बुरे भाव को जानते हैं, जिसमें पुरवासियों का, माताओं का और भरत का हित हो, वही उपाय बतलाइए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3244.english_translation: You dwell in every heart and know every good and bad intention. Tell us the course that will benefit the people of the city, the mothers, and Bharata.
ramacharitamanas::3244.translation_literal: सब (all) / के (of) / उर (heart) / अंतर (within) / बसहु (you dwell) / जानहु (you know) / भाउ (feeling, intention) / कुभाउ (bad feeling, wrong intention) / पुरजन (city-dwellers) / जननी (mothers) / भरत (Bharata) / हित (welfare) / होइ (may be) / सो (that) / कहिअ (please tell) / उपाउ (course, means)
ramacharitamanas::3244.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3244.essence: Real guidance begins when you care about everyone’s welfare, not just your own.
ramacharitamanas::3244.simple_meaning: Ram is asked to choose the course that will help everyone, because he already knows every heart and every intention.
ramacharitamanas::3244.simple_insight: Peace comes when you stop arguing from ego and ask for the most wholesome way forward.
ramacharitamanas::3244.detailed_meaning: Bharat has come with the sages and the people to Ram in the tense aftermath of exile. Everyone is wounded by duty and loss, so the request is simple and profound: Ram already sees every heart, therefore he alone can name the course that will protect the city, the mothers, and Bharata.
ramacharitamanas::3244.modern_relevance: You’re in a family group chat where everyone is hurt and talking past each other. The wisest person is not the loudest one, but the one who can see what helps everyone most.
ramacharitamanas::3244.insight: It shifts you from partial, self-protective thinking to asking for the action that serves the whole circle.

ramacharitamanas::3245.verse_sanskrit: आरत कहहिं बिचारि न काऊ। सूझ जुआरिहि आपन दाऊ॥ सुनि मुनि बचन कहत रघुराऊ॥ नाथ तुम्हारेहि हाथ उपाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3245.verse_hindi: आर्त (दुःखी) लोग कभी विचारकर नहीं कहते। जुआरी को अपना ही दाँव सूझता है। मुनि के वचन सुनकर श्री रघुनाथजी कहने लगे- हे नाथ! उपाय तो आप ही के हाथ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3245.english_translation: The distressed do not think carefully; a gambler sees only his own stake. Hearing the sage's words, Raghunath said, "Lord, the remedy is in your hands."
ramacharitamanas::3245.translation_literal: आरत (distressed) / कहहिं (speak) / बिचारि (after thinking) / न (not) / काऊ (anyone)। / सूझ (appears) / जुआरिहि (to the gambler) / आपन (his own) / दाऊ (stake)॥ / सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (sage) / बचन (words) / कहत (speaking) / रघुराऊ (Raghunath)॥ / नाथ (Lord) / तुम्हारेहि (in your) / हाथ (hand) / उपाऊ (remedy)॥
ramacharitamanas::3245.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3245.essence: Distress distorts judgment; the real remedy comes from surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3245.simple_meaning: When people are overwhelmed, they stop thinking clearly. Ram says the solution is not in his own hands but in the Lord's.
ramacharitamanas::3245.simple_insight: You can stop carrying every problem alone and feel the relief of handing it over.
ramacharitamanas::3245.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the sage has just spoken about what will help everyone involved in Ram's exile. Ram answers with humility: distressed people cannot judge well, and the real remedy belongs to the higher power guiding events.
ramacharitamanas::3245.modern_relevance: You are staring at a family crisis at 1 a.m., rereading the same message thread, knowing your mind is too shaken to decide well. The verse reminds you that panic shrinks judgment and some remedies require surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3245.insight: It shifts you from self-reliant control to humble release when emotions cloud judgment.

ramacharitamanas::3246.verse_sanskrit: सब कर हित रुख राउरि राखें। आयसु किए मुदित फुर भाषें॥ प्रथम जो आयसु मो कहुँ होई। माथें मानि करौं सिख सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3246.verse_hindi: आपका रुख रखने में और आपकी आज्ञा को सत्य कहकर प्रसन्नता पूर्वक पालन करने में ही सबका हित है। पहले तो मुझे जो आज्ञा हो, मैं उसी शिक्षा को माथे पर चढ़ाकर करूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3246.english_translation: Keeping to your wish is best for everyone. I will gladly carry out whatever order comes first, and I will hold that instruction to my head.
ramacharitamanas::3246.translation_literal: सब (all) / कर (of all) / हित (welfare) / रुख (wish, direction) / राउरि (your) / राखें (keeping) / आयसु (command) / किए (having done) / मुदित (joyfully) / फुर (true, fitting) / भाषें (speaking) / प्रथम (first) / जो (whatever) / आयसु (order) / मो (to me) / कहुँ (for) / होई (comes) / माथें (on the head) / मानि (placing, honoring) / करौं (I do) / सिख (instruction) / सोई (that same)
ramacharitamanas::3246.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3246.essence: True service starts when your own wish yields to rightful command.
ramacharitamanas::3246.simple_meaning: Serving the other person's will is the best way to help everyone. The speaker says he will gladly follow the first instruction given and treat it as sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3246.simple_insight: Real service begins when your own preference steps aside.
ramacharitamanas::3246.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is being asked to accept guidance for the good of everyone around him. He answers with complete humility: whatever order comes first, he will place it above himself and obey it gladly.
ramacharitamanas::3246.modern_relevance: You’re in a family meeting where everyone is tense, and the quietest person says, ‘Tell me what helps most, and I’ll do that first.’ That kind of humility can save a room.
ramacharitamanas::3246.insight: It teaches you to treat rightful guidance as more important than personal preference.

ramacharitamanas::3247.verse_sanskrit: पुनि जेहि कहँ जस कहब गोसाईं। सो सब भाँति घटिहि सेवकाईं॥ कह मुनि राम सत्य तुम्ह भाषा। भरत सनेहँ बिचारु न राखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3247.verse_hindi: फिर हे गोसाईं! आप जिसको जैसा कहेंगे वह सब तरह से सेवा में लग जाएगा (आज्ञा पालन करेगा)। मुनि वशिष्ठजी कहने लगे- हे राम! तुमने सच कहा। पर भरत के प्रेम ने विचार को नहीं रहने दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3247.english_translation: Then, whatever you say, O Lord, will fully turn into service in every way. The sage said, "Ram, what you said is true. But Bharat's love left no room for calculation."
ramacharitamanas::3247.translation_literal: पुनि (then again) / जेहि (whomever) / कहँ (for) / जस (as) / कहब (to say) / गोसाईं (Lord) / सो (that) / सब भाँति (in every way) / घटिहि (will diminish/turn into) / सेवकाईं (service)॥ / कह (said) / मुनि (the sage) / राम (Ram) / सत्य (true) / तुम्ह (your) / भाषा (speech) / भरत (Bharat) / सनेहँ (by love) / बिचारु (calculation/thought) / न (not) / राखा (kept) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3247.speaker: Vashistha
ramacharitamanas::3247.essence: Bharat's love is so pure that calculation cannot survive it.
ramacharitamanas::3247.simple_meaning: True love for Ram turns everything into service. Bharat's devotion is so complete that careful calculation disappears.
ramacharitamanas::3247.simple_insight: Love can become so complete that self-interest has nothing left to say.
ramacharitamanas::3247.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Vashistha speaks to Ram after the pain of exile has split the royal family. Ram sees that service follows the command of the beloved, but Vashistha adds that Bharat's love goes beyond logic itself.
ramacharitamanas::3247.modern_relevance: You stop weighing every benefit and cost before helping someone you love. The heart simply moves, and the mind follows later.
ramacharitamanas::3247.insight: It shifts you from measured compliance to wholehearted service shaped by devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3248.verse_sanskrit: तेहि तें कहउँ बहोरि बहोरी। भरत भगति बस भइ मति मोरी॥ मोरें जान भरत रुचि राखी। जो कीजिअ सो सुभ सिव साखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3248.verse_hindi: इसीलिए मैं बार-बार कहता हूँ, मेरी बुद्धि भरत की भक्ति के वश हो गई है। मेरी समझ में तो भरत की रुचि रखकर जो कुछ किया जाएगा, शिवजी साक्षी हैं, वह सब शुभ ही होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3248.english_translation: That is why I keep saying it again and again: my mind has been won over by Bharat's devotion. In my understanding, whatever is done while keeping Bharat's wish in view will surely be auspicious, Shiva is my witness.
ramacharitamanas::3248.translation_literal: तेहि तें (therefore) / कहउँ (I say) / बहोरि बहोरी (again and again) / भरत भगति (Bharat's devotion) / बस (under the control) / भइ (has become) / मति (mind, understanding) / मोरी (my)॥ / मोरें (in my view) / जान (knowing) / भरत रुचि (Bharat's wish) / राखी (kept) / जो (whatever) / कीजिअ (is done) / सो (that) / सुभ (auspicious) / सिव साखी (Shiva as witness)॥
ramacharitamanas::3248.speaker: Vasistha
ramacharitamanas::3248.essence: Devotion can make even judgment bend toward what is right.
ramacharitamanas::3248.simple_meaning: Vasistha says his judgment is now shaped by Bharat's devotion. He believes any decision that respects Bharat's wishes will be auspicious.
ramacharitamanas::3248.simple_insight: True devotion can reorder even a wise mind.
ramacharitamanas::3248.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Vasistha is defending Bharat's position before Ram. After hearing Bharat's selfless refusal of power, he says his own mind has been won over by Bharat's devotion. He trusts that any action aligned with Bharat's wish will be right.
ramacharitamanas::3248.modern_relevance: You watch someone refuse a promotion so a colleague can keep their job, and the room goes quiet. Suddenly, everyone can feel which choice is cleaner.
ramacharitamanas::3248.insight: It shifts judgment from status and strategy to the moral weight of selfless devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3249.verse_sanskrit: भरत बिनय सादर सुनिअ करिअ बिचारु बहोरि। करब साधुमत लोकमत नृपनय निगम निचोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3249.verse_hindi: पहले भरत की विनती आदरपूर्वक सुन लीजिए, फिर उस पर विचार कीजिए। तब साधुमत, लोकमत, राजनीति और वेदों का निचोड़ (सार) निकालकर वैसा ही (उसी के अनुसार) कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3249.english_translation: First listen to Bharat's request with respect, then reflect on it carefully. After that, take the essence of the wise, public opinion, statecraft, and the Vedas, and act accordingly.
ramacharitamanas::3249.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / बिनय (request, humble plea) / सादर (with respect) / सुनिअ (listen) / करिअ (do, act) / बिचारु (reflection, careful thought) / बहोरि (again, then) / करब (to do) / साधुमत (the view of the wise) / लोकमत (public opinion) / नृपनय (statecraft, kingly policy) / निगम (the Vedas) / निचोरि (essence, extract)
ramacharitamanas::3249.speaker: Vasistha
ramacharitamanas::3249.essence: Respectful listening comes before the right decision.
ramacharitamanas::3249.simple_meaning: Bharat's request should be heard respectfully and judged carefully. The right action comes from weighing wisdom, public feeling, leadership, and sacred guidance together.
ramacharitamanas::3249.simple_insight: Good judgment begins with humility, not with rushing to be right.
ramacharitamanas::3249.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Vasistha is advising Ram about Bharat's plea and the kingdom's future. He says Bharat should be heard respectfully first, then the matter should be weighed through wisdom, public opinion, statecraft, and the Vedas before any decision is made.
ramacharitamanas::3249.modern_relevance: A family argument is already heated, and everyone is talking over each other. The person who pauses, listens to the quieter request, and weighs the fuller picture often makes the cleanest decision.
ramacharitamanas::3249.insight: It shifts you from reacting to a single voice toward making a balanced, responsible decision.

ramacharitamanas::3250.verse_sanskrit: गुर अनुरागु भरत पर देखी। राम हृदयँ आनंदु बिसेषी॥ भरतहि धरम धुरंधर जानी। निज सेवक तन मानस बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3250.verse_hindi: भरतजी पर गुरुजी का स्नेह देखकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी के हृदय में विशेष आनंद हुआ। भरतजी को धर्मधुरंधर और तन, मन, वचन से अपना सेवक जानकर- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3250.english_translation: Seeing the teacher's affection for Bharat, Ram felt special joy in his heart. Knowing Bharat as the upholder of righteousness and as his servant in body, mind, and speech—
ramacharitamanas::3250.translation_literal: गुर (teacher) / अनुरागु (affection) / भरत पर (for Bharat) / देखी (seeing) / राम (Ram) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / आनंदु (joy) / बिसेषी (special) ॥ / भरतहि (Bharat) / धरम धुरंधर (upholder of righteousness) / जानी (knowing) / निज (own) / सेवक (servant) / तन (body) / मानस (mind) / बानी (speech) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3250.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3250.essence: A noble heart rejoices when it sees another's devotion and goodness.
ramacharitamanas::3250.simple_meaning: Ram feels deep joy when he sees the teacher's affection for Bharat, because he recognises Bharat as fully devoted to righteousness and service.
ramacharitamanas::3250.simple_insight: Real love notices and rejoices in another person's goodness.
ramacharitamanas::3250.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's devotion is being praised before Ram and the teacher. When Ram sees the teacher's affection for Bharat, his heart fills with joy. He recognises Bharat not as a rival, but as a righteous servant in every way.
ramacharitamanas::3250.modern_relevance: You watch a mentor praise someone you admire, and your first feeling is joy, not envy. That quiet happiness reveals a generous heart.
ramacharitamanas::3250.insight: It shifts the mind from comparison to appreciation of another's dharma.

ramacharitamanas::3251.verse_sanskrit: बोले गुरु आयस अनुकूला। बचन मंजु मृदु मंगलमूला॥ नाथ सपथ पितु चरन दोहाई। भयउ न भुअन भरत सम भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3251.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी गुरु की आज्ञा अनुकूल मनोहर, कोमल और कल्याण के मूल वचन बोले- हे नाथ! आपकी सौगंध और पिताजी के चरणों की दुहाई है (मैं सत्य कहता हूँ कि) विश्वभर में भरत के समान कोई भाई हुआ ही नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3251.english_translation: Ram spoke words that matched the guru’s command: beautiful, gentle, and full of blessing. “My lord, by your oath and by my father’s feet, I tell the truth: there has never been a brother like Bharat in all the world.”
ramacharitamanas::3251.translation_literal: बोले (spoke) / गुरु (guru) / आयस (command) / अनुकूला (fitting, favorable) / बचन (words) / मंजु (beautiful) / मृदु (soft, gentle) / मंगलमूला (rooted in blessing) || नाथ (lord) / सपथ (oath) / पितु (father) / चरन (feet) / दोहाई (appeal, witness) / भयउ (was) / न (not) / भुअन (world) / भरत (Bharat) / सम (like) / भाई (brother)
ramacharitamanas::3251.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3251.essence: Gentle speech can honor devotion better than force ever will.
ramacharitamanas::3251.simple_meaning: Ram answers with soft, respectful words and praises Bharat as unmatched among brothers. His speech shows gratitude, humility, and love for family duty.
ramacharitamanas::3251.simple_insight: Kind words can carry deep respect without losing strength.
ramacharitamanas::3251.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat’s loyalty has moved Ram deeply. After hearing the praise of Bharat and the guru’s approval, Ram responds with gentle, blessing-filled speech, using his father’s memory and the guru’s authority to honour Bharat’s rare brotherly devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3251.modern_relevance: When a family argument finally softens and someone speaks without sharpness, the room changes. A respectful sentence can do what anger never could: restore dignity and make love visible again.
ramacharitamanas::3251.insight: It teaches you to answer admiration and conflict with language that heals, not hardens.

ramacharitamanas::3252.verse_sanskrit: जे गुर पद अंबुज अनुरागी। ते लोकहुँ बेदहुँ बड़भागी॥ राउर जा पर अस अनुरागू। को कहि सकइ भरत कर भागू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3252.verse_hindi: जो लोग गुरु के चरणकमलों के अनुरागी हैं, वे लोक में (लौकिक दृष्टि से) भी और वेद में (परमार्थिक दृष्टि से) भी बड़भागी होतें हैं! (फिर) जिस पर आप (गुरु) का ऐसा स्नेह है, उस भरत के भाग्य को कौन कह सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3252.english_translation: Those who love the guru's lotus feet are fortunate in both the world and the Vedas. What can anyone say of Bharat's fortune, on whom you have such love?
ramacharitamanas::3252.translation_literal: जे (those who) / गुर (guru) / पद अंबुज (lotus feet) / अनुरागी (loving, devoted) / ते (they) / लोकहुँ (in the world) / बेदहुँ (and in the Vedas) / बड़भागी (very fortunate) / राउर (your) / जा पर (on whom) / अस (such) / अनुरागू (love, affection) / को (who) / कहि (speak) / सकइ (can) / भरत कर (of Bharat's) / भागू (fortune, lot)
ramacharitamanas::3252.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3252.essence: Love for the guru makes ordinary and sacred life fruitful.
ramacharitamanas::3252.simple_meaning: People who are devoted to the guru are truly fortunate. Bharat is especially blessed because the guru loves him so deeply.
ramacharitamanas::3252.simple_insight: Real honour comes from sincere devotion, not from status or achievement.
ramacharitamanas::3252.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is speaking about Bharat's greatness after seeing the love between Bharat and the guru. He says devotion to the guru brings blessing in ordinary life and in spiritual understanding, and Bharat's fortune is beyond measure.
ramacharitamanas::3252.modern_relevance: You meet a teacher who sees your effort before anyone else does. That steady respect changes how you carry yourself, because being received well can matter more than being praised widely.
ramacharitamanas::3252.insight: It shifts attention from public success to the transforming power of loyal reverence.

ramacharitamanas::3253.verse_sanskrit: लखि लघु बंधु बुद्धि सकुचाई। करत बदन पर भरत बड़ाई॥ भरतु कहहिं सोइ किएँ भलाई। अस कहि राम रहे अरगाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3253.verse_hindi: छोटा भाई जानकर भरत के मुँह पर उसकी बड़ाई करने में मेरी बुद्धि सकुचाती है। (फिर भी मैं तो यही कहूँगा कि) भरत जो कुछ कहें, वही करने में भलाई है। ऐसा कहकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी चुप हो रहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3253.english_translation: Seeing his younger brother, his mind felt shy to praise Bharat in his face. Yet he said, "Whatever Bharat says, doing that is best." Saying this, Ram fell silent.
ramacharitamanas::3253.translation_literal: लखि (seeing) / लघु (younger) / बंधु (brother) / बुद्धि (mind) / सकुचाई (felt shy) / करत (doing) / बदन (face) / पर (upon) / भरत (Bharat) / बड़ाई (praise) / भरतु (Bharat) / कहहिं (says) / सोइ (that very) / किएँ (doing) / भलाई (good) / अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / राम (Ram) / रहे (remained) / अरगाई (silent)
ramacharitamanas::3253.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3253.essence: True respect is following the good, not merely praising it.
ramacharitamanas::3253.simple_meaning: Ram feels shy to praise Bharat directly, yet says that doing what Bharat says is the right thing.
ramacharitamanas::3253.simple_insight: Real respect is not flattery; it is willingness to follow what is good.
ramacharitamanas::3253.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat’s devotion is so pure that even Ram hesitates to praise him openly. Ram finally says Bharat’s words should be followed, then falls silent. The moment shows how deeply Ram honours Bharat’s character.
ramacharitamanas::3253.modern_relevance: You’re in a meeting and someone younger than you solves the problem before you do. Instead of defending your status, you admit they’re right and let their insight lead.
ramacharitamanas::3253.insight: It shifts respect from verbal praise to obedient recognition of what is truly right.

ramacharitamanas::3254.verse_sanskrit: तब मुनि बोले भरत सन सब सँकोचु तजि तात। कृपासिंधु प्रिय बंधु सन कहहु हृदय कै बात ॥
ramacharitamanas::3254.verse_hindi: तब मुनि भरतजी से बोले- हे तात! सब संकोच त्यागकर कृपा के समुद्र अपने प्यारे भाई से अपने हृदय की बात कहो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3254.english_translation: Then the sage said to Bharat, "Cast off all hesitation, dear one, and tell your heart's truth to your beloved brother, the ocean of mercy."
ramacharitamanas::3254.translation_literal: तब (then) / मुनि (sage) / बोले (spoke) / भरत सन (to Bharat) / सब (all) / सँकोचु (hesitation) / तजि (leaving) / तात (dear one) / कृपासिंधु (ocean of mercy) / प्रिय बंधु सन (to the beloved brother) / कहहु (say) / हृदय कै बात (the heart's matter)
ramacharitamanas::3254.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3254.essence: Hesitation falls away before real love.
ramacharitamanas::3254.simple_meaning: The sage urges Bharat to stop holding back and speak honestly to Ram, who is full of mercy and love.
ramacharitamanas::3254.simple_insight: There is relief in honest speech when the listener is already compassionate.
ramacharitamanas::3254.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram after a painful fracture in the royal family. The sage steps in and tells Bharat to set aside hesitation and speak from the heart, because Ram is gentle, loving, and ready to receive him.
ramacharitamanas::3254.modern_relevance: You rehearse a difficult text message for an hour, then delete it. The moment you finally speak plainly to someone who cares, the weight starts to lift.
ramacharitamanas::3254.insight: It shifts you from guarded silence to honest self-expression in the presence of trust.

ramacharitamanas::3255.verse_sanskrit: सुनि मुनि बचन राम रुख पाई। गुरु साहिब अनुकूल अघाई॥ लखि अपनें सिर सबु छरु भारू। कहि न सकहिं कछु करहिं बिचारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3255.verse_hindi: मुनि के वचन सुनकर और श्री रामचन्द्रजी का रुख पाकर गुरु तथा स्वामी को भरपेट अपने अनुकूल जानकर सारा बोझ अपने ही ऊपर समझकर भरतजी कुछ कह नहीं सकते। वे विचार करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3255.english_translation: Hearing the sage's words and seeing Ram's favorable mood, Bharat felt that his teacher and lord were fully on his side. Seeing the whole burden on his own head, he could say nothing and kept thinking.
ramacharitamanas::3255.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (sage) / बचन (words) / राम (Ram) / रुख (mood/turn) / पाई (having obtained) / गुरु (teacher) / साहिब (lord) / अनुकूल (favourable) / अघाई (fully satisfied)॥ / लखि (seeing) / अपनें (own) / सिर (head) / सबु (all) / छरु (burden) / भारू (heavy) / कहि (to say) / न (not) / सकहिं (able) / कछु (anything) / करहिं (do) / बिचारू (reflection)॥
ramacharitamanas::3255.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3255.essence: Real responsibility can leave you speechless before it lets you speak.
ramacharitamanas::3255.simple_meaning: Bharat feels the sage and Ram are both in his favor, so he takes the whole burden on himself and falls silent, thinking deeply.
ramacharitamanas::3255.simple_insight: When you feel fully seen, even your silence becomes honest.
ramacharitamanas::3255.detailed_meaning: In the Ayodhyakand gathering, the sage's words and Ram's response leave Bharat overwhelmed. He feels that both his teacher and his beloved brother are inclined toward him, yet the weight of the situation still rests on him, so he cannot speak and turns inward.
ramacharitamanas::3255.modern_relevance: You hear a message in a room full of people, and suddenly you know the decision is already resting on you. Your mouth goes dry, not from fear, but from responsibility.
ramacharitamanas::3255.insight: It shifts the mind from speaking quickly to carrying the weight of the moment with care.

ramacharitamanas::3256.verse_sanskrit: पुलकि सरीर सभाँ भए ठाढ़े। नीरज नयन नेह जल बाढ़े॥ कहब मोर मुनिनाथ निबाहा। एहि तें अधिक कहौं मैं काहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3256.verse_hindi: शरीर से पुलकित होकर वे सभा में खड़े हो गए। कमल के समान नेत्रों में प्रेमाश्रुओं की बाढ़ आ गई। (वे बोले-) मेरा कहना तो मुनिनाथ ने ही निबाह दिया (जो कुछ मैं कह सकता था वह उन्होंने ही कह दिया)। इससे अधिक मैं क्या कहूँ? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3256.english_translation: His body thrilled as he stood in the assembly. Tears of love rose in his lotus eyes. He said, "My words have already been fulfilled by the sage. What more can I say now?"
ramacharitamanas::3256.translation_literal: पुलकि (thrilled) / सरीर (body) / सभाँ (in the assembly) / भए (became) / ठाढ़े (standing) / नीरज (lotus) / नयन (eyes) / नेह (love) / जल (water) / बाढ़े (rose/flooded) / कहब (saying) / मोर (my) / मुनिनाथ (lord of sages) / निबाहा (fulfilled) / एहि तें (from this) / अधिक (more) / कहौं (I say) / मैं (I) / काहा (what)
ramacharitamanas::3256.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3256.essence: True devotion leaves you with nothing left to prove.
ramacharitamanas::3256.simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed with devotion and gratitude. Tears rise as he realizes the sage has already spoken the truth he wanted to express.
ramacharitamanas::3256.simple_insight: When your heart is fully seen, gratitude can be stronger than speech.
ramacharitamanas::3256.detailed_meaning: In the assembly at Chitrakoot, Bharat has been urged to speak plainly to Ram. Hearing the sage's words, he rises with trembling joy and tears. The moment is so complete that he feels his own heart has already been spoken for him.
ramacharitamanas::3256.modern_relevance: You finally sit across from someone who understands your pain before you explain it. The relief is so complete that words feel unnecessary.
ramacharitamanas::3256.insight: It shifts you from self-conscious explanation to grateful recognition that your truth has already been held.

ramacharitamanas::3257.verse_sanskrit: मैं जानउँ निज नाथ सुभाऊ। अपराधिहु पर कोह न काऊ॥ मो पर कृपा सनेहु बिसेषी। खेलत खुनिस न कबहूँ देखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3257.verse_hindi: अपने स्वामी का स्वभाव मैं जानता हूँ। वे अपराधी पर भी कभी क्रोध नहीं करते। मुझ पर तो उनकी विशेष कृपा और स्नेह है। मैंने खेल में भी कभी उनकी रीस (अप्रसन्नता) नहीं देखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3257.english_translation: I know my Lord’s nature well: he never grows angry, even with one who has done wrong. He has special grace and affection for me. I have never seen him displeased, even in play.
ramacharitamanas::3257.translation_literal: मैं (I) / जानउँ (know) / निज (own) / नाथ (lord) / सुभाऊ (nature) / अपराधिहु (even with the offender) / पर (toward) / कोह (anger) / न (not) / काऊ (at all) / मो पर (on me) / कृपा (grace) / सनेहु (affection) / बिसेषी (special) / खेलत (while playing) / खुनिस (displeasure) / न (not) / कबहूँ (ever) / देखी (saw)
ramacharitamanas::3257.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3257.essence: Ram’s grace stays steady even when you fail.
ramacharitamanas::3257.simple_meaning: Ram’s nature is gentle and forgiving. Even when people err, he does not become angry. The speaker feels especially held by Ram’s grace and has never seen him displeased.
ramacharitamanas::3257.simple_insight: You can stop bracing for rejection when love is stronger than your mistakes.
ramacharitamanas::3257.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the speaker reflects on Ram’s character while the exile story is already tightening around the family. What matters here is not strategy but trust: Ram’s nature is so gracious that even fault does not push him into anger.
ramacharitamanas::3257.modern_relevance: You replay a mistake before sending the apology text, expecting coldness. But some people meet your weakness with steadiness, not punishment.
ramacharitamanas::3257.insight: It shifts you from fearing divine anger to trusting a mercy that stays steady even when you falter.

ramacharitamanas::3258.verse_sanskrit: सिसुपन तें परिहरेउँ न संगू। कबहुँ न कीन्ह मोर मन भंगू॥ मैं प्रभु कृपा रीति जियँ जोही। हारेहूँ खेल जितावहिं मोही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3258.verse_hindi: बचपन में ही मैंने उनका साथ नहीं छोड़ा और उन्होंने भी मेरे मन को कभी नहीं तोड़ा (मेरे मन के प्रतिकूल कोई काम नहीं किया)। मैंने प्रभु की कृपा की रीति को हृदय में भलीभाँति देखा है (अनुभव किया है)। मेरे हारने पर भी खेल में प्रभु मुझे जिता देते रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3258.english_translation: I have not left his company since childhood, and he has never broken my heart. I have seen the way the Lord's grace works: even when I lose, he still lets me win the game.
ramacharitamanas::3258.translation_literal: सिसुपन (childhood) / तें (from) / परिहरेउँ (I left) / न (not) / संगू (company) / कबहुँ (ever) / न (not) / कीन्ह (did) / मोर (my) / मन (mind/heart) / भंगू (breaking) / मैं (I) / प्रभु (Lord) / कृपा (grace) / रीति (way/manner) / जियँ (in the heart) / जोही (saw) / हारेहूँ (even when defeated) / खेल (game) / जितावहिं (they let win) / मोही (me)
ramacharitamanas::3258.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3258.essence: Grace can turn even defeat into a hidden victory.
ramacharitamanas::3258.simple_meaning: Bharat says he never left Ram's side since childhood, and Ram never hurt him. He has learned that Ram's grace is such that even in defeat, Ram still lets him win.
ramacharitamanas::3258.simple_insight: Love becomes steadier when you recognize that grace has been protecting you all along.
ramacharitamanas::3258.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat speaks with aching devotion about Ram. He remembers lifelong closeness, says Ram never shattered his trust, and reflects on a strange mercy: even when Bharat seems to lose, Ram still makes him the winner.
ramacharitamanas::3258.modern_relevance: You look back at years of loyalty to someone who never used your trust against you. Even the hard moments now feel like they were guided by a kindness you couldn't see then.
ramacharitamanas::3258.insight: It shifts the mind from measuring life by wins and losses to seeing grace inside both.

ramacharitamanas::3259.verse_sanskrit: महूँ सनेह सकोच बस सनमुख कही न बैन। दरसन तृपित न आजु लगि प्रेम पिआसे नैन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3259.verse_hindi: मैंने भी प्रेम और संकोचवश कभी सामने मुँह नहीं खोला। प्रेम के प्यासे मेरे नेत्र आज तक प्रभु के दर्शन से तृप्त नहीं हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3259.english_translation: I too, held back by love and modesty, never spoke face to face. My eyes, thirsty for his sight, have still not been satisfied.
ramacharitamanas::3259.translation_literal: महूँ (I too) / सनेह (love) / सकोच बस (because of modesty) / सनमुख (face to face) / कही न बैन (did not speak a word) / दरसन (sight) / तृपित (satisfied) / न आजु लगि (not until today) / प्रेम पिआसे (thirsty with love) / नैन (eyes)
ramacharitamanas::3259.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3259.essence: Love can be so deep that even speech feels too small.
ramacharitamanas::3259.simple_meaning: Bharat says his love and modesty kept him from speaking openly, and his eyes have never felt full without Ram's sight.
ramacharitamanas::3259.simple_insight: Real devotion can feel like ache, not comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3259.detailed_meaning: Bharat is speaking after Ram has gone into exile. He is not claiming power or innocence; he is confessing how love made him shy and how separation has left him spiritually hungry. This verse deepens his grief into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3259.modern_relevance: You keep the unread message open because you don't know how to say what matters most. The silence isn't indifference — sometimes it is love mixed with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3259.insight: It shifts devotion from performance to longing, showing that love can be quiet, restrained, and still absolute.

ramacharitamanas::3260.verse_sanskrit: बिधि न सकेऊ सहि मोर दुलारा। नीच बीचु जननी मिस पारा॥ यहउ कहत मोहि आजु न सोभा। अपनीं समुझि साधु सुचि को भा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3260.verse_hindi: परन्तु विधाता मेरा दुलार न सह सका। उसने नीच माता के बहाने (मेरे और स्वामी के बीच) अंतर डाल दिया। यह भी कहना आज मुझे शोभा नहीं देता, क्योंकि अपनी समझ से कौन साधु और पवित्र हुआ है? (जिसको दूसरे साधु और पवित्र मानें, वही साधु है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3260.english_translation: But fate could not bear my affection. It placed a barrier between me and my beloved through the excuse of my lowly mother. Even saying this does not suit me today, for who has become holy and pure by their own judgment?
ramacharitamanas::3260.translation_literal: बिधि (fate) / न सकेऊ (could not) / सहि (bear) / मोर (my) / दुलारा (beloved) / नीच (lowly) / बीचु (between) / जननी (mother) / मिस (excuse) / पारा (placed) / यहउ (this also) / कहत (saying) / मोहि (to me) / आजु (today) / न (not) / सोभा (suitability) / अपनीं (own) / समुझि (understanding) / साधु (holy) / सुचि (pure) / को (who) / भा (became)
ramacharitamanas::3260.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3260.essence: Self-praise stains the very humility it tries to prove.
ramacharitamanas::3260.simple_meaning: Bharat says he should not praise himself as pure or holy. He sees that self-approval is empty and unworthy, especially when he is speaking about his own family and conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3260.simple_insight: Real humility begins when you stop needing your own innocence to be confirmed.
ramacharitamanas::3260.detailed_meaning: Bharat, grieving Ram's exile, is speaking with painful restraint. He refuses to claim moral superiority, even while defending his own heart. The verse shows a man who would rather stay humble than protect his image.
ramacharitamanas::3260.modern_relevance: You almost type a long message defending yourself after being blamed at family dinner. Then you stop. You know that explaining your own purity usually makes you look smaller, not cleaner.
ramacharitamanas::3260.insight: It shifts you away from self-justification and toward humble, quiet conduct.

ramacharitamanas::3261.verse_sanskrit: मातु मंदि मैं साधु सुचाली। उर अस आनत कोटि कुचाली॥ फरइ कि कोदव बालि सुसाली। मुकता प्रसव कि संबुक काली ॥
ramacharitamanas::3261.verse_hindi: माता नीच है और मैं सदाचारी और साधु हूँ, ऐसा हृदय में लाना ही करोड़ों दुराचारों के समान है। क्या कोदों की बाली उत्तम धान फल सकती है? क्या काली घोंघी मोती उत्पन्न कर सकती है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3261.english_translation: To think, 'My mother is bad and I am noble,' is like committing millions of wrongs in the heart. Can a stalk of kodu grain bear fine rice? Can a black shellfish produce pearls?
ramacharitamanas::3261.translation_literal: मातु (mother) / मंदि (bad) / मैं (I) / साधु (noble) / सुचाली (well-conducted) / उर (in the heart) / अस (thus) / आनत (bringing) / कोटि (crores of) / कुचाली (bad deeds) / फरइ (bear fruit) / कि (can) / कोदव (kodu grain) / बालि (stalk) / सुसाली (fine rice) / मुकता (pearls) / प्रसव (produce) / कि (can) / संबुक (shellfish) / काली (black)
ramacharitamanas::3261.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3261.essence: Pride that condemns your own mother is already a moral failure.
ramacharitamanas::3261.simple_meaning: Bharat says it is deeply wrong to think he is noble while his mother is blameworthy. He uses simple images to show that a pure result cannot come from a corrupt source.
ramacharitamanas::3261.simple_insight: Real humility stops you from protecting your ego at someone else's expense.
ramacharitamanas::3261.detailed_meaning: Bharat is grieving in Ayodhya after Ram's exile. Trying to speak honestly about Kaikeyi, he refuses to separate himself from her as if he were morally superior. His point is sharp: a son's character is not clean if it grows from contempt for his own mother.
ramacharitamanas::3261.modern_relevance: You catch yourself telling a friend, 'I would never act like my mother.' The sentence feels clever for a second, then ugly. Bharat shows why self-righteous distance can corrupt the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3261.insight: It shifts you from judgment to responsibility, so you stop using comparison to feel pure.

ramacharitamanas::3262.verse_sanskrit: सपनेहूँ दोसक लेसु न काहू। मोर अभाग उदधि अवगाहू॥ बिनु समुझें निज अघ परिपाकू। जारिउँ जायँ जननि कहि काकू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3262.verse_hindi: स्वप्न में भी किसी को दोष का लेश भी नहीं है। मेरा अभाग्य ही अथाह समुद्र है। मैंने अपने पापों का परिणाम समझे बिना ही माता को कटु वचन कहकर व्यर्थ ही जलाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3262.english_translation: Even in a dream, no one deserves blame. My own misfortune is an endless ocean. Without understanding the fruit of my own sins, I burned my mother by speaking harshly in vain.
ramacharitamanas::3262.translation_literal: सपनेहूँ (even in a dream) / दोसक (of fault) / लेसु (trace) / न (not) / काहू (of anyone) / मोर (my) / अभाग (misfortune) / उदधि (ocean) / अवगाहू (depth, immersion) / बिनु (without) / समुझें (understanding) / निज (own) / अघ (sin) / परिपाकू (ripening, result) / जारिउँ (I burned) / जायँ (in vain) / जननि (mother) / कहि (saying) / काकू (harsh words)
ramacharitamanas::3262.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3262.essence: Blame fades when you finally face your own part.
ramacharitamanas::3262.simple_meaning: Bharat says no one else is at fault. His own misfortune and unrecognized wrongdoing led him to speak harshly to his mother and regret it.
ramacharitamanas::3262.simple_insight: Real remorse begins when you stop outsourcing blame and face your own part honestly.
ramacharitamanas::3262.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat looks back on the rupture in his family and sees his own harsh speech as part of the damage. He does not excuse himself or accuse others; he turns inward and judges himself first.
ramacharitamanas::3262.modern_relevance: After a fight, you replay every line and want to blame the other person. But later, in the quiet of your room, you see the moment you crossed the line too.
ramacharitamanas::3262.insight: It shifts attention from blaming others to owning the harm you helped create.

ramacharitamanas::3263.verse_sanskrit: हृदयँ हेरि हारेउँ सब ओरा। एकहि भाँति भलेहिं भल मोरा॥ गुर गोसाइँ साहिब सिय रामू। लागत मोहि नीक परिनामू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3263.verse_hindi: मैं अपने हृदय में सब ओर खोज कर हार गया (मेरी भलाई का कोई साधन नहीं सूझता)। एक ही प्रकार भले ही (निश्चय ही) मेरा भला है। वह यह है कि गुरु महाराज सर्वसमर्थ हैं और श्री सीता-रामजी मेरे स्वामी हैं। इसी से परिणाम मुझे अच्छा जान पड़ता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3263.english_translation: I searched my heart in every direction and found no other way. One thing alone is surely good for me: my teacher is the lord, and Sita-Ram are my masters. Because of this, the outcome feels right to me.
ramacharitamanas::3263.translation_literal: हृदयँ (in the heart) / हेरि (having searched) / हारेउँ (I was defeated) / सब ओरा (in all directions) / एकहि भाँति (in one way alone) / भलेहिं (indeed good) / भल (good) / मोरा (mine) / गुर (teacher) / गोसाइँ (lord/master) / साहिब (master) / सिय रामू (Sita-Ram) / लागत (seems) / मोहि (to me) / नीक (good) / परिनामू (result)
ramacharitamanas::3263.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3263.essence: Peace begins when you stop seeking a better master.
ramacharitamanas::3263.simple_meaning: Bharat says he has searched every possibility in his heart and found only one good path: accepting Guru and Sita-Ram as his masters.
ramacharitamanas::3263.simple_insight: Relief comes when you stop bargaining with life and place yourself where your heart can rest.
ramacharitamanas::3263.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is explaining his inner state after Ram's exile has shattered the kingdom. He has looked in every direction and found no better answer than complete loyalty to Guru and Sita-Ram. That surrender makes even the painful outcome feel right.
ramacharitamanas::3263.modern_relevance: You keep replaying the same decision at 1 a.m., hoping another option will appear. Then you finally choose the one place your heart can truly stand, and the noise drops away.
ramacharitamanas::3263.insight: It shifts the mind from endless comparison to wholehearted surrender.

ramacharitamanas::3264.verse_sanskrit: साधु सभाँ गुर प्रभु निकट कहउँ सुथल सतिभाउ। प्रेम प्रपंचु कि झूठ फुर जानहिं मुनि रघुराउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3264.verse_hindi: साधुओं की सभा में गुरुजी और स्वामी के समीप इस पवित्र तीर्थ स्थान में मैं सत्य भाव से कहता हूँ। यह प्रेम है या प्रपंच (छल-कपट)? झूठ है या सच? इसे (सर्वज्ञ) मुनि वशिष्ठजी और (अन्तर्यामी) श्री रघुनाथजी जानते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3264.english_translation: In the holy gathering, near the guru and my lord, I speak with true feeling. Is this love or deception? Is it false or true? Only the sages and Raghunath know.
ramacharitamanas::3264.translation_literal: साधु सभाँ (in the holy assembly) / गुर (guru) / प्रभु (lord) / निकट (near) / कहउँ (I speak) / सुथल (in a sacred place) / सतिभाउ (with true feeling) / प्रेम (love) / प्रपंचु (deception, worldly show) / कि (or) / झूठ (false) / फुर (true) / जानहिं (they know) / मुनि (the sage) / रघुराउ (Raghunath, Ram)
ramacharitamanas::3264.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3264.essence: Real devotion does not need to defend itself.
ramacharitamanas::3264.simple_meaning: The speaker admits confusion about whether this is genuine love or just an act, and places the answer in the hands of the guru and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3264.simple_insight: You do not have to prove your heart to everyone. What is real will be known where it matters most.
ramacharitamanas::3264.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the speaker stands before the guru and Ram's presence and confesses a painful uncertainty: is this devotion sincere love or mere show? The verse turns private confusion into surrender, trusting that the teacher and Ram can see what the speaker cannot.
ramacharitamanas::3264.modern_relevance: You send a message after midnight and wonder if your care was genuine or just neediness. The mind keeps judging itself, but the deepest truth of love is not always visible from inside the ache.
ramacharitamanas::3264.insight: It shifts you from self-judgment to trust in a wiser witness of your heart.

ramacharitamanas::3265.verse_sanskrit: भूपति मरन प्रेम पनु राखी। जननी कुमति जगतु सबु साखी॥ देखि न जाहिं बिकल महतारीं। जरहिं दुसह जर पुर नर नारीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3265.verse_hindi: प्रेम के प्रण को निबाहकर महाराज (पिताजी) का मरना और माता की कुबुद्धि, दोनों का सारा संसार साक्षी है। माताएँ व्याकुल हैं, वे देखी नहीं जातीं। अवधपुरी के नर-नारी दुःसह ताप से जल रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3265.english_translation: Keeping the vow of love, the king died; the whole world is witness to the queen's wrong-mindedness. The mothers cannot be looked at in their anguish; the men and women of Ayodhya burn in unbearable heat.
ramacharitamanas::3265.translation_literal: भूपति (the king) / मरन (dying) / प्रेम (love) / पनु (vow) / राखी (kept) / जननी (mother) / कुमति (wrong-mindedness) / जगतु (the world) / सबु (all) / साखी (witness)॥ / देखि (seeing) / न (not) / जाहिं (are able) / बिकल (distressed) / महतारीं (mothers) / जरहिं (burn) / दुसह (unbearable) / जर (heat) / पुर (city) / नर (men) / नारीं (women) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3265.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3265.essence: One wrongful choice can make an entire kingdom grieve.
ramacharitamanas::3265.simple_meaning: Dasharath has died after keeping the promise of love, and Kaikeyi's wrong judgment has brought grief to everyone. The women are shattered, and Ayodhya burns with sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::3265.simple_insight: A broken promise can wound an entire city, not just a single family.
ramacharitamanas::3265.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath is gone and the cost of Kaikeyi's demand is now visible everywhere. The queens are distraught, the mothers cannot bear the sight of one another, and the whole city feels the heat of grief before Ram's exile is even fully spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3265.modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after one harsh decision, and suddenly everyone is carrying the weight. One person's choice can leave an entire home stunned and scorched.
ramacharitamanas::3265.insight: It shifts attention from private regret to the wider damage caused by wrong judgment and broken trust.

ramacharitamanas::3266.verse_sanskrit: महीं सकल अनरथ कर मूला। सो सुनि समुझि सहिउँ सब सूला॥ सुनि बन गवनु कीन्ह रघुनाथा। करि मुनि बेष लखन सिय साथा ॥ बिनु पानहिन्ह पयादेहि पाएँ। संकरु साखि रहेउँ एहि घाएँ॥ बहुरि निहारि निषाद सनेहू। कुलिस कठिन उर भयउ न बेहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3266.verse_hindi: मैं ही इन सारे अनर्थों का मूल हूँ, यह सुन और समझकर मैंने सब दुःख सहा है। श्री रघुनाथजी लक्ष्मण और सीताजी के साथ मुनियों का सा वेष धारणकर बिना जूते पहने पाँव-प्यादे (पैदल) ही वन को चले गए, यह सुनकर, शंकरजी साक्षी हैं, इस घाव से भी मैं जीता रह गया (यह सुनते ही मेरे प्राण नहीं निकल गए)! फिर निषादराज का प्रेम देखकर भी इस वज्र से भी कठोर हृदय में छेद नहीं हुआ (यह फटा नहीं)॥2-3॥
ramacharitamanas::3266.english_translation: Seeing and understanding that I am the root of all misfortune, I have endured every pain. Hearing that Raghunath went to the forest with Lakshman and Sita, dressed like a sage and walking barefoot, I held on by Shiva's witness. Then, even after seeing Nishadraj's love, this heart, harder than lightning, did not break.
ramacharitamanas::3266.translation_literal: महीं (earth) / सकल (all) / अनरथ (misfortune) / कर (of) / मूला (root) / सो (that) / सुनि (hearing) / समुझि (understanding) / सहिउँ (I endured) / सब (all) / सूला (pains)॥ / सुनि (hearing) / बन (forest) / गवनु (going) / कीन्ह (made/did) / रघुनाथा (Raghunath) / करि (having made) / मुनि (sage) / बेष (disguise/garb) / लखन (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / साथा (together)॥ / बिनु (without) / पानहिन्ह (sandals) / पयादेहि (on foot) / पाएँ (feet) / संकरु (Shankar/Shiva) / साखि (witness) / रहेउँ (I remained) / एहि (this) / घाएँ (wound)॥ / बहुरि (again) / निहारि (seeing) / निषाद (Nishadraj) / सनेहू (affection/love) / कुलिस (thunderbolt) / कठिन (hard) / उर (heart) / भयउ (became) / न (not) / बेहू (split/break)॥
ramacharitamanas::3266.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3266.essence: Humility lets you survive what pride would shatter you over.
ramacharitamanas::3266.simple_meaning: Bharat says he has survived unbearable pain by understanding that he himself is the root of the disaster. Even hearing of Ram's exile and seeing Nishadraj's love did not break his heart.
ramacharitamanas::3266.simple_insight: Blame loosens when humility enters, and then grief can be carried without collapse.
ramacharitamanas::3266.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat looks back on the chain of sorrow after Ram leaves for the forest. He sees his own role in the disaster, hears of Ram walking barefoot with Sita and Lakshman, and is stunned that his heart has not shattered. This is grief mixed with humility.
ramacharitamanas::3266.modern_relevance: You replay the argument after midnight and finally admit your part in it. The shame still hurts, but it stops poisoning everything once you stop defending yourself.
ramacharitamanas::3266.insight: It shifts the mind from self-justification to humble endurance, so pain becomes bearable instead of corrosive.

ramacharitamanas::3267.verse_sanskrit: अब सबु आँखिन्ह देखेउँ आई। जिअत जीव जड़ सबइ सहाई॥ जिन्हहि निरखि मग साँपिनि बीछी। तजहिं बिषम बिषु तामस तीछी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3267.verse_hindi: अब यहाँ आकर सब आँखों देख लिया। यह जड़ जीव जीता रह कर सभी सहावेगा। जिनको देखकर रास्ते की साँपिनी और बीछी भी अपने भयानक विष और तीव्र क्रोध को त्याग देती हैं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3267.english_translation: Now I have come and seen it all with my own eyes. Living beings endure only because they are helped by the living. Even snakes and scorpions on the road lay aside their terrible poison and fierce heat when they see such a one.
ramacharitamanas::3267.translation_literal: अब (now) / सबु (all) / आँखिन्ह (with eyes) / देखेउँ (I saw) / आई (coming) / जिअत (living) / जीव (beings) / जड़ (inert) / सबइ (all) / सहाई (supporters) / जिन्हहि (whom) / निरखि (seeing) / मग (road) / साँपिनि (snakes) / बीछी (scorpions) / तजहिं (leave) / बिषम (terrible) / बिषु (poison) / तामस (heat/fury) / तीछी (sharp)
ramacharitamanas::3267.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3267.essence: True presence makes even harshness soften.
ramacharitamanas::3267.simple_meaning: Bharat says he has now seen the full reality for himself: life continues only because others support it, and even fierce dangers soften before truly noble presence.
ramacharitamanas::3267.simple_insight: Grief has made him see clearly how fragile life is and how much kindness holds it together.
ramacharitamanas::3267.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands amid the wreckage left by Ram's exile and Dasharath's death. He speaks with the pain of someone who has finally understood what the loss has done to everyone around him, and why the world now feels unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::3267.modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed after days of bad news, and suddenly the small kindnesses matter most: the water cup, the hand squeeze, the quiet presence that keeps you from breaking.
ramacharitamanas::3267.insight: It shifts attention from power and blame to the fragile support that lets life continue.

ramacharitamanas::3268.verse_sanskrit: तेइ रघुनंदनु लखनु सिय अनहित लागे जाहि। तासु तनय तजि दुसह दुख दैउ सहावइ काहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3268.verse_hindi: वे ही श्री रघुनंदन, लक्ष्मण और सीता जिसको शत्रु जान पड़े, उस कैकेयी के पुत्र मुझको छोड़कर दैव दुःसह दुःख और किसे सहावेगा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3268.english_translation: Those very Raghunandan, Lakshman, and Sita whom you saw as enemies—why should the unbearable sorrow fall on anyone else when Kaikeyi's son must bear it?
ramacharitamanas::3268.translation_literal: तेइ (those very) / रघुनंदनु (Raghunandan) / लखनु (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / अनहित (as enemies / harmful) / लागे (seemed) / जाहि (to whom) / तासु (that person's) / तनय (son) / तजि (leaving) / दुसह (unbearable) / दुख (sorrow) / दैउ (fate) / सहावइ (makes endure) / काहि (to whom)
ramacharitamanas::3268.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3268.essence: The sorrow of your choice comes home to you.
ramacharitamanas::3268.simple_meaning: Bharat says that the unbearable grief belongs to Kaikeyi's son, because Kaikeyi treated Ram, Lakshman, and Sita like enemies and sent them away.
ramacharitamanas::3268.simple_insight: Some choices return as suffering, and the heart has to face what it set in motion.
ramacharitamanas::3268.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat speaks after seeing the cost of Kaikeyi's demand. Ram, Lakshman, and Sita have gone to the forest, and Bharat is crushed by the family wound. He points to himself as the one who must endure the sorrow tied to that decision.
ramacharitamanas::3268.modern_relevance: You finally read the message thread where your decision hurt everyone you love. The silence afterward feels heavier than the choice itself.
ramacharitamanas::3268.insight: It shifts blame into responsibility: the one connected to the act must also carry its grief.

ramacharitamanas::3269.verse_sanskrit: सुनि अति बिकल भरत बर बानी। आरति प्रीति बिनय नय सानी॥ सोक मगन सब सभाँ खभारू। मनहुँ कमल बन परेउ तुसारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3269.verse_hindi: अत्यन्त व्याकुल तथा दुःख, प्रेम, विनय और नीति में सनी हुई भरतजी की श्रेष्ठ वाणी सुनकर सब लोग शोक में मग्न हो गए, सारी सभा में विषाद छा गया। मानो कमल के वन पर पाला पड़ गया हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3269.english_translation: Hearing Bharata's noble words, filled with anguish, love, humility, and moral restraint, everyone in the assembly was overcome with grief. It was as if frost had fallen on a field of lotuses.
ramacharitamanas::3269.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / अति (very) / बिकल (distressed) / भरत (Bharata) / बर (noble) / बानी (speech) / आरति (anguish) / प्रीति (love) / बिनय (humility) / नय (moral conduct) / सानी (mixed with)॥ / सोक (grief) / मगन (immersed) / सब (all) / सभाँ (in the assembly) / खभारू (sadness) / मनहुँ (as if) / कमल (lotus) / बन (forest) / परेउ (fell) / तुसारू (frost)॥
ramacharitamanas::3269.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3269.essence: Bharata's wounded nobility makes the whole assembly grieve with him.
ramacharitamanas::3269.simple_meaning: Bharat speaks with deep pain, love, humility, and restraint, and everyone present falls into grief. The whole assembly feels cold and heavy, like lotus flowers struck by frost.
ramacharitamanas::3269.simple_insight: Even noble grief can spread through a room like weather.
ramacharitamanas::3269.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's grieving court, Bharata's words carry pain, love, humility, and right conduct all at once. The assembly listens in silence, and his sorrow becomes everyone's sorrow, freezing the whole scene before Vasistha begins to soothe him.
ramacharitamanas::3269.modern_relevance: You hear a friend speak after a family loss, and the room changes at once. Their honesty is so full of feeling that everyone else goes quiet with them.
ramacharitamanas::3269.insight: It shows how sincere grief and moral dignity can move an entire gathering without argument.

ramacharitamanas::3270.verse_sanskrit: कहि अनेक बिधि कथा पुरानी। भरत प्रबोधु कीन्ह मुनि ग्यानी॥ बोले उचित बचन रघुनंदू। दिनकर कुल कैरव बन चंदू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3270.verse_hindi: तब ज्ञानी मुनि वशिष्ठजी ने अनेक प्रकार की पुरानी (ऐतिहासिक) कथाएँ कहकर भरतजी का समाधान किया। फिर सूर्यकुल रूपी कुमुदवन के प्रफुल्लित करने वाले चन्द्रमा श्री रघुनंदन उचित वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3270.english_translation: Then the wise sage Vashishtha spoke many kinds of ancient stories to comfort Bharat. After that, the Moon of Raghu's line, Ram, spoke fitting words.
ramacharitamanas::3270.translation_literal: कहि (having said) / अनेक (many) / बिधि (kinds) / कथा (stories) / पुरानी (old, ancient) / भरत (Bharat) / प्रबोधु (comfort, counsel) / कीन्ह (did) / मुनि (sage) / ग्यानी (wise) / बोले (spoke) / उचित (fitting) / बचन (words) / रघुनंदू (Ram, delight of Raghu's line) / दिनकर (sun) / कुल (lineage) / कैरव (water-lily) / बन (forest, grove) / चंदू (moon)
ramacharitamanas::3270.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3270.essence: Comfort comes first; fitting truth follows only when the heart is ready.
ramacharitamanas::3270.simple_meaning: Vashishtha first comforts Bharat with old stories, and then Ram speaks in a way that fits the moment.
ramacharitamanas::3270.simple_insight: Sometimes healing begins with memory, and only then can the truest words be heard.
ramacharitamanas::3270.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat is drowning in grief after Ram's exile. Vashishtha tries to steady him with ancient stories and wise counsel, and then Ram himself answers with words suited to Bharat's pain. This verse is a bridge into that consoling dialogue.
ramacharitamanas::3270.modern_relevance: A friend is crying in your kitchen, and you do not rush to fix it. You sit, you listen, you offer what can actually be heard. Then the right words finally land.
ramacharitamanas::3270.insight: It shows that comfort often needs preparation before instruction can help.

ramacharitamanas::3271.verse_sanskrit: तात जायँ जियँ करहु गलानी। ईस अधीन जीव गति जानी॥ तीनि काल तिभुअन मत मोरें। पुन्यसिलोक तात तर तोरें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3271.verse_hindi: हे तात! तुम अपने हृदय में व्यर्थ ही ग्लानि करते हो। जीव की गति को ईश्वर के अधीन जानो। मेरे मत में (भूत, भविष्य, वर्तमान) तीनों कालों और (स्वर्ग, पृथ्वी और पाताल) तीनों लोकों के सब पुण्यात्मा पुरुष तुम से नीचे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3271.english_translation: Father, do not trouble your heart with grief. Know that the fate of a living being rests in the divine. In my view, all the virtuous beings of the three times and three worlds are beneath you.
ramacharitamanas::3271.translation_literal: तात (father) / जायँ (go) / जियँ (in the heart) / करहु (do) / गलानी (grief, self-reproach) / ईस (the divine) / अधीन (under the control of) / जीव (living being) / गति (fate, course) / जानी (knowing) / तीनि (three) / काल (times) / तिभुअन (three worlds) / मत (in my view) / मोरें (my) / पुन्यसिलोक (virtuous, blessed beings) / तात (father) / तर (below) / तोरें (you)
ramacharitamanas::3271.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3271.essence: Grief eases when you stop making yourself the author of everything.
ramacharitamanas::3271.simple_meaning: Ram tells Bharat not to blame himself. Life moves under a higher order, and even the most virtuous people are not above this truth.
ramacharitamanas::3271.simple_insight: You can stop carrying the whole burden of what happened.
ramacharitamanas::3271.detailed_meaning: Bharat is drowning in grief after Ram’s exile and Dasharath’s death. In the royal assembly at Ayodhya, Ram answers his anguish with tenderness: self-blame cannot change the course of a life already held by a higher order.
ramacharitamanas::3271.modern_relevance: You replay one conversation all night, convinced you ruined everything. Ram’s words meet that spiral: not every outcome belongs to your control, and not every pain is your fault.
ramacharitamanas::3271.insight: It shifts you from self-condemnation to surrendering the burden of control.

ramacharitamanas::3272.verse_sanskrit: उर आनत तुम्ह पर कुटिलाई। जाइ लोकु परलोकु नसाई॥ दोसु देहिं जननिहि जड़ तेई। जिन्ह गुर साधु सभा नहिं सेई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3272.verse_hindi: हृदय में भी तुम पर कुटिलता का आरोप करने से यह लोक (यहाँ के सुख, यश आदि) बिगड़ जाता है और परलोक भी नष्ट हो जाता है (मरने के बाद भी अच्छी गति नहीं मिलती)। माता कैकेयी को तो वे ही मूर्ख दोष देते हैं, जिन्होंने गुरु और साधुओं की सभा का सेवन नहीं किया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3272.english_translation: Even thinking crookedly about you ruins this world and the next. Only fools blame Mother Kaikeyi; they are the ones who have never sat in the company of teachers and saints.
ramacharitamanas::3272.translation_literal: उर (in the heart) / आनत (bringing, placing) / तुम्ह पर (upon you) / कुटिलाई (crookedness, ill intent) / जाइ (goes) / लोकु (this world) / परलोकु (the next world) / नसाई (is ruined) / दोसु (fault) / देहिं (they give) / जननिहि (to Mother) / जड़ (fools) / तेई (only those) / जिन्ह (who) / गुर (teacher) / साधु (saints) / सभा (company, assembly) / नहिं (do not) / सेई (serve, attend)
ramacharitamanas::3272.speaker: Vasistha
ramacharitamanas::3272.essence: Private resentment damages both your present life and what follows.
ramacharitamanas::3272.simple_meaning: Even private ill will against someone harms your life now and after death. People who blame Kaikeyi without understanding are ignorant and have not kept company with wise teachers and saints.
ramacharitamanas::3272.simple_insight: Judgment becomes softer when you realize how much ignorance shapes blame.
ramacharitamanas::3272.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Vasistha is calming Bharat after the exile has shattered the royal family. He explains that even inward hostility destroys both worldly wellbeing and future welfare, and that blaming Kaikeyi reveals a mind untouched by wise company.
ramacharitamanas::3272.modern_relevance: You rehearse blame in your head after a family fight, and the bitterness starts shaping everything you see. This verse says that hidden resentment already damages you before you ever speak.
