ramacharitamanas::3272.insight: It shifts you from blame to discernment, and from judgment to the need for wise company.

ramacharitamanas::3273.verse_sanskrit: मिटिहहिं पाप प्रपंच सब अखिल अमंगल भार। लोक सुजसु परलोक सुखु सुमिरत नामु तुम्हार ॥
ramacharitamanas::3273.verse_hindi: हे भरत! तुम्हारा नाम स्मरण करते ही सब पाप, प्रपंच (अज्ञान) और समस्त अमंगलों के समूह मिट जाएँगे तथा इस लोक में सुंदर यश और परलोक में सुख प्राप्त होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3273.english_translation: O Bharat, by remembering your name, all sins, illusion, and every burden of inauspiciousness are removed. In this world there is good fame, and in the next there is happiness.
ramacharitamanas::3273.translation_literal: मिटिहहिं (are erased) / पाप (sins) / प्रपंच (illusion, worldly deception) / सब (all) / अखिल (entire) / अमंगल (inauspiciousness) / भार (burden) / लोक (in this world) / सुजसु (good fame) / परलोक (in the next world) / सुखु (happiness) / सुमिरत (remembering) / नामु (name) / तुम्हार (your)
ramacharitamanas::3273.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3273.essence: Bharat's remembrance is so pure it washes away burden and brings blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3273.simple_meaning: Remembering Bharat's name is said to remove wrongdoing, confusion, and all misfortune, while bringing good reputation here and happiness beyond.
ramacharitamanas::3273.simple_insight: A life held in remembrance feels lighter, cleaner, and more protected.
ramacharitamanas::3273.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's devotion is being praised after his refusal of the throne. The speaker says that even remembering Bharat's name removes confusion and misfortune, bringing honor in this world and happiness beyond.
ramacharitamanas::3273.modern_relevance: You hear a friend's name after a hard day and feel your chest loosen. Some people steady you just by being remembered with love.
ramacharitamanas::3273.insight: It shifts devotion from ceremony to remembrance as a source of cleansing and strength.

ramacharitamanas::3274.verse_sanskrit: कहउँ सुभाउ सत्य सिव साखी। भरत भूमि रह राउरि राखी॥ तात कुतरक करहु जनि जाएँ। बैर पेम नहिं दुरइ दुराएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3274.verse_hindi: हे भरत! मैं स्वभाव से ही सत्य कहता हूँ, शिवजी साक्षी हैं, यह पृथ्वी तुम्हारी ही रखी रह रही है। हे तात! तुम व्यर्थ कुतर्क न करो। वैर और प्रेम छिपाए नहीं छिपते ॥
ramacharitamanas::3274.english_translation: O Bharat, I speak the truth by nature; Shiva himself is my witness. This earth has remained yours alone. Do not go into useless argument, dear one. Enmity and love cannot be hidden.
ramacharitamanas::3274.translation_literal: कहउँ (I speak) / सुभाउ (by nature) / सत्य (truth) / सिव (Shiva) / साखी (witness) / भरत (Bharat) / भूमि (earth/land) / रह (remained) / राउरि (yours) / राखी (kept)॥ / तात (dear one) / कुतरक (useless argument) / करहु (do) / जनि (do not) / जाएँ (go)। / बैर (enmity) / पेम (love) / नहिं (not) / दुरइ (hide) / दुराएँ (can be hidden)॥
ramacharitamanas::3274.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3274.essence: Love and enmity reveal themselves without disguise.
ramacharitamanas::3274.simple_meaning: Bharat should stop doubting and arguing. Tulsidas says he speaks truthfully, with Shiva as witness, and that love or hostility always reveal themselves.
ramacharitamanas::3274.simple_insight: You don't need to force clarity when your real feeling will eventually show itself.
ramacharitamanas::3274.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is wrestling with doubt and grief over Ram's exile. Tulsidas answers him directly, swearing truth before Shiva, insisting that Bharat's claim to the land remains intact, and warning that love and hatred cannot be disguised for long.
ramacharitamanas::3274.modern_relevance: You're trying to explain your intentions in a long text thread, but the tone already gave you away. No amount of clever wording can hide whether you care, resent, or mean well.
ramacharitamanas::3274.insight: It shifts attention from verbal defense to the deeper truth already visible in conduct and feeling.

ramacharitamanas::3275.verse_sanskrit: मुनिगन निकट बिहग मृग जाहीं। बाधक बधिक बिलोकि पराहीं॥ हित अनहित पसु पच्छिउ जाना। मानुष तनु गुन ग्यान निधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3275.verse_hindi: पक्षी और पशु मुनियों के पास (बेधड़क) चले जाते हैं, पर हिंसा करने वाले बधिकों को देखते ही भाग जाते हैं। मित्र और शत्रु को पशु-पक्षी भी पहचानते हैं। फिर मनुष्य शरीर तो गुण और ज्ञान का भंडार ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3275.english_translation: Birds and animals go near sages, but they flee when they see hunters. Even animals know friend from foe. Then the human body is a treasure-house of virtue and understanding.
ramacharitamanas::3275.translation_literal: मुनिगन (sages) / निकट (near) / बिहग (birds) / मृग (deer, animals) / जाहीं (go) / बाधक (harmful) / बधिक (hunter) / बिलोकि (seeing) / पराहीं (flee) / हित (benefit, friend) / अनहित (harm, foe) / पसु (animals) / पच्छिउ (birds) / जाना (know) / मानुष (human) / तनु (body) / गुन (virtues) / ग्यान (knowledge) / निधाना (treasure-house)
ramacharitamanas::3275.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3275.essence: Human life is wasted if it never becomes clear seeing.
ramacharitamanas::3275.simple_meaning: Even birds and animals can sense who is safe and who is dangerous. Human life is far greater, because it can hold virtue and understanding.
ramacharitamanas::3275.simple_insight: You are capable of discernment, not just survival.
ramacharitamanas::3275.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is urging Bharat to see clearly, not get trapped in suspicion or confusion. He points to animals and birds as proof that even they can recognize danger, then reminds Bharat that human life carries the gift of judgment and wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::3275.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and immediately feel who is steady and who is draining. That instinct is basic. Your human gift is going further: seeing with wisdom, not just sensing risk.
ramacharitamanas::3275.insight: It shifts you from reactive fear to thoughtful discernment.

ramacharitamanas::3276.verse_sanskrit: तात तुम्हहि मैं जानउँ नीकें। करौं काह असमंजस जीकें॥ राखेउ रायँ सत्य मोहि त्यागी। तनु परिहरेउ पेम पन लागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3276.verse_hindi: हे तात! मैं तुम्हें अच्छी तरह जानता हूँ। क्या करूँ? जी में बड़ा असमंजस (दुविधा) है। राजा ने मुझे त्याग कर सत्य को रखा और प्रेम-प्रण के लिए शरीर छोड़ दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3276.english_translation: Dear brother, I know you well. What should I do? My heart is deeply torn. The king upheld truth by abandoning me, and gave up his body for the sake of love and his vow.
ramacharitamanas::3276.translation_literal: तात (dear brother) / तुम्हहि (you) / मैं (I) / जानउँ (know) / नीकें (well) / करौं (do) / काह (what) / असमंजस (confusion) / जीकें (in the heart) / राखेउ (kept) / रायँ (the king) / सत्य (truth) / मोहि (me) / त्यागी (having abandoned) / तनु (body) / परिहरेउ (gave up) / पेम (love) / पन (vow) / लागी (for the sake of)
ramacharitamanas::3276.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3276.essence: Truth can be honored only at the price of a broken heart.
ramacharitamanas::3276.simple_meaning: Bharat tells Lakshman that he knows him well, but he is confused and heartbroken. He says Dasharath upheld truth and love even by giving up his life.
ramacharitamanas::3276.simple_insight: Some choices leave you grieving and respectful at the same time.
ramacharitamanas::3276.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is caught between loyalty to his father’s command and the pain of what it cost. Speaking to Lakshman, he says Dasharath held to truth and love even in death, and that leaves Bharat unable to settle his own heart.
ramacharitamanas::3276.modern_relevance: You read a text message from someone who chose what they believed was right, and now everything feels both noble and unbearable. Bharat knows that kind of split heart.
ramacharitamanas::3276.insight: It shifts the mind from judging grief as weakness to seeing it as the cost of honoring truth.

ramacharitamanas::3277.verse_sanskrit: तासु बचन मेटत मन सोचू। तेहि तें अधिक तुम्हार सँकोचू॥ ता पर गुर मोहि आयसु दीन्हा। अवसि जो कहहु चहउँ सोइ कीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3277.verse_hindi: उनके वचन को मेटते मन में सोच होता है। उससे भी बढ़कर तुम्हारा संकोच है। उस पर भी गुरुजी ने मुझे आज्ञा दी है, इसलिए अब तुम जो कुछ कहो, अवश्य ही मैं वही करना चाहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3277.english_translation: Thinking of their words, my mind feels troubled. Even greater than that is your hesitation. On top of that, the guru has given me this command, so whatever you say, I want to do that for sure.
ramacharitamanas::3277.translation_literal: तासु (their) / बचन (words) / मेटत (erasing) / मन (mind) / सोचू (thought, worry) / तेहि तें (than that) / अधिक (greater) / तुम्हार (your) / सँकोचू (hesitation, modest restraint) / ता पर (on top of that) / गुर (guru) / मोहि (to me) / आयसु (command) / दीन्हा (gave) / अवसि (certainly) / जो (whatever) / कहहु (you say) / चहउँ (I want) / सोइ (that very) / कीन्हा (to do)
ramacharitamanas::3277.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3277.essence: True duty begins when your own preference stops leading.
ramacharitamanas::3277.simple_meaning: Ram says he has already received a command and now wants to follow Bharat's wishes without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::3277.simple_insight: There is peace in yielding personal preference to what is right and asked of you.
ramacharitamanas::3277.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat stands before Ram after the exile has shattered the family. Ram does not argue or defend himself; he lowers his own will and says he will do whatever Bharat asks, because duty, respect, and obedience to the guru now guide him.
ramacharitamanas::3277.modern_relevance: You’re in a tense family call, everyone talking over each other, and you finally say, “Tell me what you need, and I’ll do it.” That shift can stop the spiral.
ramacharitamanas::3277.insight: It shifts you from defending your own position to aligning with a binding responsibility.

ramacharitamanas::3278.verse_sanskrit: मनु प्रसन्न करि सकुच तजि कहहु करौं सोइ आजु। सत्यसंध रघुबर बचन सुनि भा सुखी समाजु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3278.verse_hindi: तुम मन को प्रसन्न कर और संकोच को त्याग कर जो कुछ कहो, मैं आज वही करूँ। सत्य प्रतिज्ञ रघुकुल श्रेष्ठ श्री रामजी का यह वचन सुनकर सारा समाज सुखी हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3278.english_translation: “Set your mind at ease, let go of hesitation, and do today whatever you say. Hearing this vow of truth from the best of the Raghu line, the whole assembly became happy.”
ramacharitamanas::3278.translation_literal: मनु (mind) / प्रसन्न (made glad) / करि (having done) / सकुच (hesitation) / तजि (having abandoned) / कहहु (say) / करौं (I shall do) / सोइ (that only) / आजु (today) / सत्यसंध (bound to truth) / रघुबर (best of the Raghu line) / बचन (word) / सुनि (hearing) / भा (became) / सुखी (happy) / समाजु (assembly)
ramacharitamanas::3278.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3278.essence: A truthful word can calm everyone before any action begins.
ramacharitamanas::3278.simple_meaning: Speak without hesitation, then do exactly what you promised. Ram's truthfulness makes everyone around him feel safe and happy.
ramacharitamanas::3278.simple_insight: Integrity creates relief. People relax when your words and actions finally align.
ramacharitamanas::3278.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the exile crisis has left everyone tense and divided. Here, Ram's steady truthfulness cuts through the uncertainty: he asks others to speak freely and promises to act accordingly, and that honesty immediately steadies the whole gathering.
ramacharitamanas::3278.modern_relevance: You tell a friend, “I’ll be there,” and then you actually show up when it matters. That simple alignment can calm a whole room faster than any explanation.
ramacharitamanas::3278.insight: It teaches you to make your promise and your action one thing, so trust can settle in around you.

ramacharitamanas::3279.verse_sanskrit: सुर गन सहित सभय सुरराजू। सोचहिं चाहत होन अकाजू॥ बनत उपाउ करत कछु नाहीं। राम सरन सब गे मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3279.verse_hindi: देवगणों सहित देवराज इन्द्र भयभीत होकर सोचने लगे कि अब बना-बनाया काम बिगड़ना ही चाहता है। कुछ उपाय करते नहीं बनता। तब वे सब मन ही मन श्री रामजी की शरण गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3279.english_translation: The gods, with Indra at their head, grew fearful and thought, “Now the planned work is about to go wrong.” No remedy seemed to work. Then, in their hearts, they all took refuge in Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3279.translation_literal: सुरगन (the hosts of radiant beings) / सहित (together with) / सभय (fearful) / सुरराजू (the king of the radiant beings, Indra) / सोचहिं (they thought) / चाहत (wanting) / होन (to happen) / अकाजू (the wrong thing, the spoiled work)॥ / बनत (being made) / उपाउ (a remedy, a plan) / करत (doing) / कछु (some) / नाहीं (not) / राम (Ram) / सरन (refuge) / सब (all) / गे (went) / मन माहीं (in the mind, inwardly)॥
ramacharitamanas::3279.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3279.essence: Helplessness becomes grace when you turn to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3279.simple_meaning: The gods panic because their efforts are failing, and they inwardly turn to Ram for refuge.
ramacharitamanas::3279.simple_insight: You do not need control before you can seek help.
ramacharitamanas::3279.detailed_meaning: The gods, led by Indra, see their plan slipping away and realize they cannot fix it by force. In that helplessness, they turn inward and place themselves in Ram's protection.
ramacharitamanas::3279.modern_relevance: You have three backup plans, two phone calls, and one more spreadsheet, but the problem still won't move. In that moment, the mind finally softens and asks for help beyond its own control.
ramacharitamanas::3279.insight: It shifts the mind from anxious fixing to inward surrender when effort reaches its limit.

ramacharitamanas::3280.verse_sanskrit: बहुरि बिचारि परस्पर कहहीं। रघुपति भगत भगति बस अहहीं॥ सुधि करि अंबरीष दुरबासा। भे सुर सुरपति निपट निरासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3280.verse_hindi: फिर वे विचार करके आपस में कहने लगे कि श्री रघुनाथजी तो भक्त की भक्ति के वश हैं। अम्बरीष और दुर्वासा की (घटना) याद करके तो देवता और इन्द्र बिल्कुल ही निराश हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3280.english_translation: Then they reflected together and said, "Raghupati is bound by a devotee's devotion." Remembering Ambarish and Durvasa, the gods and Indra fell completely into despair.
ramacharitamanas::3280.translation_literal: बहुरि (again) / बिचारि (having reflected) / परस्पर (among themselves) / कहहीं (they said) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / भगत (devotee) / भगति (devotion) / बस (under the control of) / अहहीं (is) / सुधि (memory) / करि (having made) / अंबरीष (Ambarish) / दुरबासा (Durvasa) / भे (became) / सुर (gods) / सुरपति (lord of the gods) / निपट (utterly) / निरासा (hopeless)
ramacharitamanas::3280.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3280.essence: Ram is reached by devotion, not by pressure.
ramacharitamanas::3280.simple_meaning: The gods realise that Ram responds to devotion, not power. Remembering old stories of a devoted king and a proud sage, they feel helpless.
ramacharitamanas::3280.simple_insight: You don't have to force the divine response; heartfelt devotion opens what effort cannot.
ramacharitamanas::3280.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the gods are panicking because Ram's exile has shaken the balance of the world. They remember Ambarish and Durvasa and conclude that Ram is won through devotion, not force, leaving even Indra helpless.
ramacharitamanas::3280.modern_relevance: You’ve tried arguing, proving, and pushing for days, and nothing changes. Then one quiet act of sincerity cuts through the whole mess — the kind of opening this verse points to.
ramacharitamanas::3280.insight: It shifts attention from control to reverent trust, showing that devotion can accomplish what force cannot.

ramacharitamanas::3281.verse_sanskrit: सहे सुरन्ह बहु काल बिषादा। नरहरि किए प्रगट प्रहलादा॥ लगि लगि कान कहहिं धुनि माथा। अब सुर काज भरत के हाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3281.verse_hindi: पहले देवताओं ने बहुत समय तक दुःख सहे। तब भक्त प्रह्लाद ने ही नृसिंह भगवान को प्रकट किया था। सब देवता परस्पर कानों से लग-लगकर और सिर धुनकर कहते हैं कि अब (इस बार) देवताओं का काम भरतजी के हाथ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3281.english_translation: The gods endured great sorrow for a long time. Then Prahlada made Narahari appear. Pressing close together, speaking into one another's ears and shaking their heads, they say, “Now the gods’ work is in Bharata’s hands.”
ramacharitamanas::3281.translation_literal: सहे (endured) / सुरन्ह (the gods) / बहु काल (a long time) / बिषादा (sorrow) / नरहरि (Narahari) / किए (made) / प्रगट (manifest) / प्रहलादा (Prahlada) / लगि लगि (pressing close) / कान (ears) / कहहिं (they say) / धुनि (shaking) / माथा (heads) / अब (now) / सुर काज (the gods' work) / भरत के हाथा (in Bharata's hands)
ramacharitamanas::3281.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3281.essence: Quiet devotion can become the only force strong enough to move events.
ramacharitamanas::3281.simple_meaning: The gods have suffered for a long time, and now they see Bharata as the one who can help them. Their hope rests on his devotion and purity.
ramacharitamanas::3281.simple_insight: Real help often comes through someone quiet, faithful, and unassuming.
ramacharitamanas::3281.detailed_meaning: The gods have already tried and failed to restore balance. They remember Prahlada's devotion bringing Narahari forth, and now they whisper that Bharata may be the one through whom help arrives. Their hope shifts from force to pure character.
ramacharitamanas::3281.modern_relevance: Everyone in the room has tried to fix the mess, and the loudest voices have failed. Then someone calm, loyal, and unshowy steps in — and suddenly the whole team turns toward them.
ramacharitamanas::3281.insight: It shifts attention from power and planning to the moral force of devotion and character.

ramacharitamanas::3282.verse_sanskrit: आन उपाउ न देखिअ देवा। मानत रामु सुसेवक सेवा॥ हियँ सपेम सुमिरहु सब भरतहि। निज गुन सील राम बस करतहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3282.verse_hindi: हे देवताओं! और कोई उपाय नहीं दिखाई देता। श्री रामजी अपने श्रेष्ठ सेवकों की सेवा को मानते हैं (अर्थात उनके भक्त की कोई सेवा करता है, तो उस पर बहुत प्रसन्न होते हैं)। अतएव अपने गुण और शील से श्री रामजी को वश में करने वाले भरतजी का ही सब लोग अपने-अपने हृदय में प्रेम सहित स्मरण करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3282.english_translation: O gods, no other remedy appears. Ram honors the service of his devoted servants. So remember Bharat with love in your hearts, for his virtues and noble character have won Ram over.
ramacharitamanas::3282.translation_literal: आन (other) / उपाउ (remedy) / न (not) / देखिअ (is seen) / देवा (O gods) / मानत (honors) / रामु (Ram) / सुसेवक (excellent servant) / सेवा (service) / हियँ (in the heart) / सपेम (with love) / सुमिरहु (remember) / सब (all) / भरतहि (Bharat) / निज (own) / गुन (virtues) / सील (noble conduct) / राम (Ram) / बस (under control) / करतहि (making)
ramacharitamanas::3282.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3282.essence: Pure service can win what force never reaches.
ramacharitamanas::3282.simple_meaning: No other solution works here: Ram responds to devoted service. Remember Bharat with love, because his character and virtue have won Ram's heart.
ramacharitamanas::3282.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that humble devotion can open what pressure never can.
ramacharitamanas::3282.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the gods are searching for a way to steady the world after Ram's exile. The answer is not strategy or force, but Bharat's selfless character. His devotion is so pure that it draws Ram's favor.
ramacharitamanas::3282.modern_relevance: You keep trying to persuade someone with arguments, reminders, and pressure, but nothing changes. Then a quiet act of care lands differently, and the relationship softens on its own.
ramacharitamanas::3282.insight: It shifts attention from control to loving service as the real power in relationship.

ramacharitamanas::3283.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुर मत सुरगुर कहेउ भल तुम्हार बड़ भागु। सकल सुमंगल मूल जग भरत चरन अनुरागु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3283.verse_hindi: देवताओं का मत सुनकर देवगुरु बृहस्पतिजी ने कहा- अच्छा विचार किया, तुम्हारे बड़े भाग्य हैं। भरतजी के चरणों का प्रेम जगत में समस्त शुभ मंगलों का मूल है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3283.english_translation: Hearing the gods' counsel, the teacher of the gods, Brihaspati, said, 'Good. You are greatly blessed. Love for Bharat's feet is the root of all good fortune in the world.'
ramacharitamanas::3283.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुर मत (the gods' counsel) / सुरगुर (the teacher of the gods) / कहेउ (said) / भल (good) / तुम्हार (your) / बड़ (great) / भागु (fortune) / सकल (all) / सुमंगल (auspiciousness) / मूल (root) / जग (world) / भरत (Bharat) / चरन (feet) / अनुरागु (love)
ramacharitamanas::3283.speaker: Brihaspati
ramacharitamanas::3283.essence: Reverence for Bharat is the root of all auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::3283.simple_meaning: Brihaspati blesses the gods' idea and says that loving Bharat is itself a source of all auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::3283.simple_insight: True greatness can be hidden in humility; reverence for it changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::3283.detailed_meaning: The gods are searching for help after Ram's exile, and Brihaspati guides them toward Bharat. He praises Bharat's devotion as the deepest auspicious force at work, showing that the path forward is not power but reverent love.
ramacharitamanas::3283.modern_relevance: You meet someone quietly holding a family together while everyone else chases credit. Later, you realise the whole room runs on their steadiness. This verse says that kind of devotion is not small — it is the source.
ramacharitamanas::3283.insight: It shifts attention from visible status to the hidden devotion that sustains a whole world.

ramacharitamanas::3284.verse_sanskrit: सीतापति सेवक सेवकाई। कामधेनु सय सरिस सुहाई॥ भरत भगति तुम्हरें मन आई। तजहु सोचु बिधि बात बनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3284.verse_hindi: सीतानाथ श्री रामजी के सेवक की सेवा सैकड़ों कामधेनुओं के समान सुंदर है। तुम्हारे मन में भरतजी की भक्ति आई है, तो अब सोच छोड़ दो। विधाता ने बात बना दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3284.english_translation: The service of Rama's servant is as beautiful as hundreds of wish-fulfilling cows. If your mind has turned to Bharata's devotion, let go of worry. The creator has already arranged it well.
ramacharitamanas::3284.translation_literal: सीतापति (Lord of Sita, Rama) / सेवक (servant) / सेवकाई (service) / कामधेनु (wish-fulfilling cow) / सय (hundreds) / सरिस (like) / सुहाई (beautiful)॥ / भरत (Bharata) / भगति (devotion) / तुम्हरें (in your) / मन (mind) / आई (has come)॥ / तजहु (leave) / सोचु (worry) / बिधि (the creator) / बात (matter) / बनाई (has arranged)॥
ramacharitamanas::3284.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3284.essence: Devotion to Ram's devotee is itself a blessing that ends worry.
ramacharitamanas::3284.simple_meaning: Serving a true devotee of Ram is wonderfully rewarding. If your heart has turned toward Bharata's devotion, stop worrying — the situation has already been set right.
ramacharitamanas::3284.simple_insight: Real devotion calms the mind because it trusts that goodness is already at work.
ramacharitamanas::3284.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the gods are watching Bharata's love for Ram and wondering how to respond. Shiva says that serving Ram's servant is more precious than any material abundance, and that Bharata's devotion itself is the sign that everything has been arranged rightly.
ramacharitamanas::3284.modern_relevance: You help someone who loves your family, and the atmosphere changes before anyone says thank you. Something honest and generous has entered the room, and the tension starts to loosen.
ramacharitamanas::3284.insight: It shifts you from anxious fixing to trusting the power of sincere devotion and service.

ramacharitamanas::3285.verse_sanskrit: देखु देवपति भरत प्रभाऊ। सजह सुभायँ बिबस रघुराऊ॥ मन थिर करहु देव डरु नाहीं। भरतहि जानि राम परिछाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3285.verse_hindi: हे देवराज! भरतजी का प्रभाव तो देखो। श्री रघुनाथजी सहज स्वभाव से ही उनके पूर्णरूप से वश में हैं। हे देवताओं ! भरतजी को श्री रामचन्द्रजी की परछाईं (परछाईं की भाँति उनका अनुसरण करने वाला) जानकर मन स्थिर करो, डर की बात नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3285.english_translation: O lord of the gods, look at Bharat’s greatness. By his very nature, Raghunath is completely under his influence. O beings of light, steady your minds and fear not; know Bharat as Ram’s own shadow.
ramacharitamanas::3285.translation_literal: देखु (look) / देवपति (lord of the gods) / भरत (Bharat) / प्रभाऊ (greatness, influence) / सजह (naturally) / सुभायँ (by nature) / बिबस (controlled, helpless) / रघुराऊ (Raghunath, Ram) ॥ / मन (mind) / थिर (steady) / करहु (make) / देव (beings of light) / डरु (fear) / नाहीं (not) ॥ / भरतहि (Bharat) / जानि (knowing) / राम (Ram) / परिछाहीं (shadow, close follower) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3285.speaker: Brihaspati
ramacharitamanas::3285.essence: True devotion can make even the highest heart yield naturally.
ramacharitamanas::3285.simple_meaning: Bharat’s devotion is so great that even Ram naturally responds to it. The gods are told to stop fearing and trust Bharat’s role as Ram’s devoted shadow.
ramacharitamanas::3285.simple_insight: Real devotion can quiet fear because it asks for nothing except faithful closeness.
ramacharitamanas::3285.detailed_meaning: Brihaspati is speaking to the gods after hearing their concern about Bharat. He points to Bharat’s unmatched loyalty and says Ram himself is सहजly moved by it. In this Ayodhyakand moment, Bharat’s devotion becomes the guarantee that everything will remain in dharma.
ramacharitamanas::3285.modern_relevance: You’re worried about whether your loyalty will be misunderstood. Then someone quietly shows up, takes responsibility, and proves that devotion can hold a whole situation together without drama.
ramacharitamanas::3285.insight: It shifts attention from anxious control to the stabilising power of faithful presence.

ramacharitamanas::3286.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुरगुर सुर संमत सोचू। अंतरजामी प्रभुहि सकोचू॥ निज सिर भारु भरत जियँ जाना। करत कोटि बिधि उर अनुमाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3286.verse_hindi: देवगुरु बृहस्पतिजी और देवताओं की सम्मति (आपस का विचार) और उनका सोच सुनकर अन्तर्यामी प्रभु श्री रामजी को संकोच हुआ। भरतजी ने अपने मन में सब बोझा अपने ही सिर जाना और वे हृदय में करोड़ों (अनेकों) प्रकार के अनुमान (विचार) करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3286.english_translation: Hearing the gods' and Brihaspati's concern, the all-knowing Lord felt uneasy. Bharat took the whole burden upon his own head and kept turning over countless thoughts in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::3286.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुरगुर (teacher of the gods, Brihaspati) / सुर (gods) / संमत (agreed-upon) / सोचू (concern, worry) / अंतरजामी (inner-knowing) / प्रभुहि (the Lord) / सकोचू (uneasiness, hesitation)॥ / निज (own) / सिर (head) / भारु (burden) / भरत (Bharat) / जियँ (in the heart) / जाना (knew, took as) / करत (doing) / कोटि (crores, countless) / बिधि (ways, kinds) / उर (in the heart) / अनुमाना (inference, reflection)॥
ramacharitamanas::3286.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3286.essence: True devotion makes even burden feel shared.
ramacharitamanas::3286.simple_meaning: Ram feels a gentle unease after hearing the concern around Bharat, while Bharat carries the whole matter in his heart and turns it over in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::3286.simple_insight: A sincere heart can feel another's burden before anyone speaks it aloud.
ramacharitamanas::3286.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the elders and gods are weighing Bharat's devotion, and Ram, who knows every heart, feels a slight hesitation. Bharat, meanwhile, silently takes the entire weight on himself and keeps thinking through every possibility.
ramacharitamanas::3286.modern_relevance: You read a tense family message and immediately start carrying everyone's feelings on your own shoulders. Before anyone asks, you are already trying to hold the whole room together.
ramacharitamanas::3286.insight: It shows how deep care makes both the giver and the beloved feel responsibility at once.

ramacharitamanas::3287.verse_sanskrit: करि बिचारु मन दीन्ही ठीका। राम रजायस आपन नीका॥ निज पन तजि राखेउ पनु मोरा। छोहु सनेहु कीन्ह नहिं थोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3287.verse_hindi: सब तरह से विचार करके अंत में उन्होंने मन में यही निश्चय किया कि श्री रामजी की आज्ञा में ही अपना कल्याण है। उन्होंने अपना प्रण छोड़कर मेरा प्रण रखा। यह कुछ कम कृपा और स्नेह नहीं किया (अर्थात अत्यन्त ही अनुग्रह और स्नेह किया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3287.english_translation: After thinking it through, he decided in his heart that Ram's command was the best path. He set aside his own vow and upheld mine. That was no small grace or affection.
ramacharitamanas::3287.translation_literal: करि (having done) / बिचारु (thought, reflection) / मन (mind) / दीन्ही (gave) / ठीका (firm decision) / राम (Ram) / रजायस (command) / आपन (own) / नीका (good, best)॥ निज (own) / पन (vow) / तजि (leaving) / राखेउ (kept) / पनु (vow) / मोरा (my) / छोहु (affection, grace) / सनेहु (love) / कीन्ह (did) / नहिं (not) / थोरा (small, little)॥
ramacharitamanas::3287.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3287.essence: Your own vow can be surrendered when a truer duty appears.
ramacharitamanas::3287.simple_meaning: Bharat decides that Ram's command is the right guide, even if it means setting aside his own promise. He sees this as a great act of love.
ramacharitamanas::3287.simple_insight: There is relief in letting a truer duty outrank your personal plan.
ramacharitamanas::3287.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is already carrying the pain of Ram's exile and the burden of the throne. After reflecting deeply, he decides that Ram's order matters more than his own vow, and he sees that choice as loving grace.
ramacharitamanas::3287.modern_relevance: You promised yourself one thing, then a parent, partner, or teacher needed something truer from you. The mature move is not stubborn self-protection; it's knowing which commitment deserves to stand.
ramacharitamanas::3287.insight: It shifts you from defending your own plan to honoring the obligation that matters most.

ramacharitamanas::3288.verse_sanskrit: कीन्ह अनुग्रह अमित अति सब बिधि सीतानाथ। करि प्रनामु बोले भरतु जोरि जलज जुग हाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3288.verse_hindi: श्री जानकीनाथजी ने सब प्रकार से मुझ पर अत्यन्त अपार अनुग्रह किया। तदनन्तर भरतजी दोनों करकमलों को जोड़कर प्रणाम करके बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3288.english_translation: Janakinath has shown me boundless grace in every way. Then Bharat joined his hands, bowed, and said:
ramacharitamanas::3288.translation_literal: कीन्ह (did) / अनुग्रह (grace) / अमित (immeasurable) / अति (very) / सब बिधि (in every way) / सीतानाथ (Lord of Sita) / करि (doing) / प्रनामु (bowing) / बोले (spoke) / भरतु (Bharat) / जोरि (joining) / जलज जुग (pair of lotus-like) / हाथ (hands)
ramacharitamanas::3288.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3288.essence: Grace received with humility becomes the doorway to surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3288.simple_meaning: Bharat bows and says that Ram has shown him limitless grace in every way.
ramacharitamanas::3288.simple_insight: Gratitude softens pride and opens the heart to surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3288.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram after carrying the burden of the kingdom and his own grief. Seeing Ram’s compassion, he bows with folded hands and speaks from humility, not entitlement. This line begins his grateful reply.
ramacharitamanas::3288.modern_relevance: You finally get a message from someone you disappointed, and it is kinder than you deserved. The first honest response is not defense — it is gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::3288.insight: It shifts you from self-justification to humble recognition of the grace you have received.

ramacharitamanas::3289.verse_sanskrit: कहौं कहावौं का अब स्वामी। कृपा अंबुनिधि अंतरजामी॥ गुर प्रसन्न साहिब अनुकूला। मिटी मलिन मन कलपित सूला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3289.verse_hindi: हे स्वामी! हे कृपा के समुद्र! हे अन्तर्यामी! अब मैं (अधिक) क्या कहूँ और क्या कहाऊँ? गुरु महाराज को प्रसन्न और स्वामी को अनुकूल जानकर मेरे मलिन मन की कल्पित पीड़ा मिट गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3289.english_translation: O master, what more can I say or make others say? Ocean of grace, inner witness, when the teacher is pleased and the master is favorable, the imagined pain of my impure mind is gone.
ramacharitamanas::3289.translation_literal: कहौं (shall I say) / कहावौं (have others say) / का (what) / अब (now) / स्वामी (master) / कृपा (grace) / अंबुनिधि (ocean) / अंतरजामी (inner witness) / गुर (teacher) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / साहिब (master) / अनुकूला (favorable) / मिटी (was removed) / मलिन (impure) / मन (mind) / कलपित (imagined) / सूला (pain)
ramacharitamanas::3289.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3289.essence: Grace can end pain the mind itself created.
ramacharitamanas::3289.simple_meaning: Bharat says he has nothing more to say. When the teacher is pleased and Ram is favorable, the pain created by his own troubled mind disappears.
ramacharitamanas::3289.simple_insight: Relief comes when you stop fighting reality and feel yourself held by grace.
ramacharitamanas::3289.detailed_meaning: Bharat has just bowed to Ram after choosing Ram's command over his own claim to the throne. In that surrendered state, he sees that his suffering was mostly mental distortion. With the teacher pleased and Ram favorable, his grief loosens.
ramacharitamanas::3289.modern_relevance: You finally get the message from someone you deeply respect, and the knot in your chest unwinds. The problem was never only outside you; half of it was the story your mind kept replaying.
ramacharitamanas::3289.insight: It shifts attention from self-made suffering to the relief that comes from trust and alignment.

ramacharitamanas::3290.verse_sanskrit: अपडर डरेउँ न सोच समूलें। रबिहि न दोसु देव दिसि भूलें॥ मोर अभागु मातु कुटिलाई। बिधि गति बिषम काल कठिनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3290.verse_hindi: मैं मिथ्या डर से ही डर गया था। मेरे सोच की जड़ ही न थी। दिशा भूल जाने पर हे देव! सूर्य का दोष नहीं है। मेरा दुर्भाग्य, माता की कुटिलता, विधाता की टेढ़ी चाल और काल की कठिनता, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3290.english_translation: I was frightened by a false fear; there was no real cause for sorrow. If I lost my way, the sun was not at fault. My misfortune, my mother’s crookedness, fate’s crooked course, and the harshness of time—these are to blame.
ramacharitamanas::3290.translation_literal: अपडर (false fear) / डरेउँ (I was afraid) / न (not) / सोच (sorrow, worry) / समूलें (at the root) / रबिहि (the sun) / न (not) / दोसु (fault) / देव (O divine one) / दिसि (direction) / भूलें (having lost) / मोर (my) / अभागु (misfortune) / मातु (mother) / कुटिलाई (crookedness) / बिधि (fate) / गति (course) / बिषम (crooked, harsh) / काल (time) / कठिनाई (hardness)
ramacharitamanas::3290.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3290.essence: False fear fades when you stop blaming the innocent.
ramacharitamanas::3290.simple_meaning: Bharat says his fear had no real basis. If he went astray, the blame was not on the sun but on his own misfortune, his mother’s wrongdoing, fate, and the harshness of time.
ramacharitamanas::3290.simple_insight: It brings relief by shifting blame away from the world and toward honest acceptance of what happened.
ramacharitamanas::3290.detailed_meaning: Bharat is speaking after bowing to Ram in Ayodhya, trying to explain his pain without accusing the wrong source. He admits that the sun did not mislead him; the real causes were his own fate, Kaikeyi’s crookedness, and the pressure of time.
ramacharitamanas::3290.modern_relevance: You missed the train, then spent the whole ride blaming the app, the traffic, the weather, anything but the real mistake. This verse asks for cleaner seeing: name the cause without turning it into a story of resentment.
ramacharitamanas::3290.insight: It teaches you to separate real cause from emotional blame, so you can face loss without distortion.

ramacharitamanas::3291.verse_sanskrit: पाउ रोपि सब मिलि मोहि घाला। प्रनतपाल पन आपन पाला॥ यह नइ रीति न राउरि होई। लोकहुँ बेद बिदित नहिं गोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3291.verse_hindi: इन सबने मिलकर पैर रोपकर (प्रण करके) मुझे नष्ट कर दिया था, परन्तु शरणागत के रक्षक आपने अपना (शरणागत की रक्षा का) प्रण निबाहा (मुझे बचा लिया)। यह आपकी कोई नई रीति नहीं है। यह लोक और वेदों में प्रकट है, छिपी नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3291.english_translation: Everyone joined together and drove me down, but you, protector of those who take refuge, kept your own vow and saved me. This is not your new way. It is known openly in the world and in the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::3291.translation_literal: पाउ (foot) / रोपि (planting, bracing) / सब (all) / मिलि (together) / मोहि (me) / घाला (drove down, harmed) / प्रनतपाल (protector of the surrendered) / पन (vow, promise) / आपन (your own) / पाला (kept, upheld) / यह (this) / नइ (not) / रीति (way, practice) / न (not) / राउरि (your) / होई (is) / लोकहुँ (in the world also) / बेद (Vedas) / बिदित (known) / नहिं (not) / गोई (hidden)
ramacharitamanas::3291.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3291.essence: The one who surrenders is never abandoned by Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3291.simple_meaning: Bharat says Ram saved him even after others tried to crush him, because Ram always protects anyone who takes refuge in him.
ramacharitamanas::3291.simple_insight: There is deep relief in trusting someone whose promise does not break under pressure.
ramacharitamanas::3291.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat is grieving and praising Ram's return to righteous rule. He remembers how the court's pressure nearly destroyed him, yet Ram still upheld the vow to protect anyone who surrenders. Bharat says this is Ram's timeless nature, not a one-time kindness.
ramacharitamanas::3291.modern_relevance: You were blamed in a group chat, cornered in a meeting, and left with no defence. Then one person stood beside you anyway. Bharat's praise is the feeling of finding a refuge that does not collapse under social pressure.
ramacharitamanas::3291.insight: It shifts trust from human approval to steadfast refuge in the one who keeps a vow.

ramacharitamanas::3292.verse_sanskrit: जगु अनभल भल एकु गोसाईं। कहिअ होइ भल कासु भलाईं॥ देउ देवतरु सरिस सुभाऊ। सनमुख बिमुख न काहुहि काऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3292.verse_hindi: सारा जगत बुरा (करने वाला) हो, किन्तु हे स्वामी! केवल एक आप ही भले (अनुकूल) हों, तो फिर कहिए, किसकी भलाई से भला हो सकता है? हे देव! आपका स्वभाव कल्पवृक्ष के समान है, वह न कभी किसी के सम्मुख (अनुकूल) है, न विमुख (प्रतिकूल) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3292.english_translation: The whole world may be unkind, but if you alone are kind, whose kindness can make things good? O Lord, your nature is like the wish-fulfilling tree: never favorable to some and hostile to others.
ramacharitamanas::3292.translation_literal: जगु (the world) / अनभल (not good) / भल (good) / एकु (only one) / गोसाईं (lord) / कहिअ (it is said) / होइ (becomes) / भल (good) / कासु (whose) / भलाईं (by goodness) ॥ देउ (O divine one) / देवतरु (wish-fulfilling tree) / सरिस (like) / सुभाऊ (nature) / सनमुख (facing toward) / बिमुख (turned away) / न (not) / काहुहि (to anyone) / काऊ (at all) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3292.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3292.essence: Ram's grace does not favor you; it simply remains good.
ramacharitamanas::3292.simple_meaning: The world may feel hostile, but Ram's nature is always good to everyone. His grace does not depend on whether someone stands near him or turns away.
ramacharitamanas::3292.simple_insight: You can stop bargaining with life and rest in a goodness that does not play favorites.
ramacharitamanas::3292.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is defending his innocence and pointing beyond human blame. He says the world may seem crooked, but Ram's nature is steady like a wish-fulfilling tree, never biased toward some and against others. That is why trust can survive grief.
ramacharitamanas::3292.modern_relevance: You watch two friends get the same bad news, and one says life is unfair while the other quietly keeps faith. This verse speaks to that deeper steadiness: not everything around you is kind, but the highest presence is not arbitrary.
ramacharitamanas::3292.insight: It shifts the mind from judging events as personal favor or rejection to trusting a steady, impartial grace.

ramacharitamanas::3293.verse_sanskrit: जाइ निकट पहिचानि तरु छाहँ समनि सब सोच। मागत अभिमत पाव जग राउ रंकु भल पोच ॥
ramacharitamanas::3293.verse_hindi: उस वृक्ष (कल्पवृक्ष) को पहचानकर जो उसके पास जाए, तो उसकी छाया ही सारी चिंताओं का नाश करने वाली है। राजा-रंक, भले-बुरे, जगत में सभी उससे माँगते ही मनचाही वस्तु पाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3293.english_translation: Approaching that tree and recognizing it, all sorrow ends in its shade. King and beggar, good and bad alike, receive whatever they ask from it.
ramacharitamanas::3293.translation_literal: जाइ (going) / निकट (near) / पहिचानि (having recognized) / तरु (tree) / छाहँ (shade) / समनि (ending) / सब (all) / सोच (sorrow, worry) / मागत (asking) / अभिमत (desired) / पाव (receives) / जग (world) / राउ (king) / रंकु (beggar) / भल (good) / पोच (bad) /
ramacharitamanas::3293.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3293.essence: Near true refuge, worry dissolves and needs are met.
ramacharitamanas::3293.simple_meaning: A truly wish-fulfilling presence removes worry and gives what each person seeks, whether they are powerful or poor.
ramacharitamanas::3293.simple_insight: It feels safe to rest near what never withholds from you.
ramacharitamanas::3293.detailed_meaning: Bharat is speaking in Ayodhya, praising Ram through the image of a wish-fulfilling tree. Near such a presence, sorrow ends and every kind of person receives what they need. The verse prepares the turn from grief to confident surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3293.modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed, exhausted and scared, and one calm person in the room somehow steadies everyone. Being near that kind of presence changes what you can bear.
ramacharitamanas::3293.insight: It shifts the mind from scarcity to confidence in a generous refuge.

ramacharitamanas::3294.verse_sanskrit: लखि सब बिधि गुर स्वामि सनेहू। मिटेउ छोभु नहिं मन संदेहू॥ अब करुनाकर कीजिअ सोई। जन हित प्रभु चित छोभु न होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3294.verse_hindi: गुरु और स्वामी का सब प्रकार से स्नेह देखकर मेरा क्षोभ मिट गया, मन में कुछ भी संदेह नहीं रहा। हे दया की खान! अब वही कीजिए जिससे दास के लिए प्रभु के चित्त में क्षोभ (किसी प्रकार का विचार) न हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3294.english_translation: Seeing the love between guru and master, my distress is gone and my mind has no doubt. O source of compassion, now do only what leaves no burden on your servant's heart.
ramacharitamanas::3294.translation_literal: लखि (seeing) / सब बिधि (in every way) / गुर (guru) / स्वामि (master) / सनेहू (love) / मिटेउ (was removed) / छोभु (distress) / नहिं (not) / मन (mind) / संदेहू (doubt)॥ / अब (now) / करुनाकर (source of compassion) / कीजिअ (please do) / सोई (that only) / जन (servant) / हित (for welfare) / प्रभु (master) / चित (mind) / छोभु (distress) / न होई (may not be)
ramacharitamanas::3294.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3294.essence: True devotion asks for the beloved's ease, not personal gain.
ramacharitamanas::3294.simple_meaning: Bharat sees the affection between teacher and ruler and feels relieved. He asks Ram to act in a way that causes no pain or worry for his servant.
ramacharitamanas::3294.simple_insight: Real devotion wants the beloved's ease, not personal advantage.
ramacharitamanas::3294.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands before Ram in Ayodhya, overwhelmed by the love he sees between teacher and master. His confusion dissolves. In that relief, he asks Ram to choose whatever leaves Bharat's heart free of distress.
ramacharitamanas::3294.modern_relevance: You finally hear someone you love speak gently about you after a long misunderstanding. The relief is immediate, and all you want is to respond in a way that doesn't add to their strain.
ramacharitamanas::3294.insight: It shifts devotion from self-protection to selfless concern for the other person's peace.

ramacharitamanas::3295.verse_sanskrit: जो सेवकु साहिबहि सँकोची। निज हित चहइ तासु मति पोची॥ सेवक हित साहिब सेवकाई। करै सकल सुख लोभ बिहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3295.verse_hindi: जो सेवक स्वामी को संकोच में डालकर अपना भला चाहता है, उसकी बुद्धि नीच है। सेवक का हित तो इसी में है कि वह समस्त सुखों और लोभों को छोड़कर स्वामी की सेवा ही करे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3295.english_translation: A servant who makes the master uneasy for personal gain has poor judgment. A servant's good lies in serving the master, leaving all pleasures and greed behind.
ramacharitamanas::3295.translation_literal: जो (who) / सेवकु (servant) / साहिबहि (the master) / सँकोची (causes unease) / निज (own) / हित (benefit) / चहइ (desires) / तासु (that person's) / मति (mind/judgment) / पोची (low)॥ / सेवक (servant) / हित (welfare) / साहिब (master) / सेवकाई (service) / करै (does) / सकल (all) / सुख (pleasures) / लोभ (greed) / बिहाई (abandoning)॥
ramacharitamanas::3295.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3295.essence: Service becomes pure when your own gain stops mattering.
ramacharitamanas::3295.simple_meaning: A true servant does not put personal gain above the master's ease. Real welfare comes from serving wholeheartedly, without chasing pleasure or greed.
ramacharitamanas::3295.simple_insight: There is dignity in serving cleanly, without trying to turn every role into personal advantage.
ramacharitamanas::3295.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is pleading for Ram to return and rule. Tulsidas turns that longing into a rule of service: a servant should not make the master uneasy for private gain, but should serve without greed.
ramacharitamanas::3295.modern_relevance: You ask a teammate to cover your mistake so your bonus survives. The verse cuts through that reflex: if your role depends on someone else, protect their ease before your own gain.
ramacharitamanas::3295.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to faithful service, especially when another person's trust is at stake.

ramacharitamanas::3296.verse_sanskrit: स्वारथु नाथ फिरें सबही का। किएँ रजाइ कोटि बिधि नीका॥ यह स्वारथ परमारथ सारू। सकल सुकृत फल सुगति सिंगारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3296.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! आपके लौटने में सभी का स्वार्थ है और आपकी आज्ञा पालन करने में करोड़ों प्रकार से कल्याण है। यही स्वार्थ और परमार्थ का सार (निचोड़) है, समस्त पुण्यों का फल और सम्पूर्ण शुभ गतियों का श्रृंगार है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3296.english_translation: O Lord, your return is the good of everyone. In obeying your command, countless forms of welfare are fulfilled. This is the essence of self-interest and the highest good: the fruit of all merit and the adornment of every blessed state.
ramacharitamanas::3296.translation_literal: स्वारथु (self-interest) / नाथ (Lord) / फिरें (in returning) / सबही (of everyone) / का (is) / किएँ (in doing) / रजाइ (command) / कोटि बिधि (in countless ways) / नीका (good) ॥ यह (this) / स्वारथ (self-interest) / परमारथ (highest good) / सारू (essence) / सकल (of all) / सुकृत (merit) / फल (fruit) / सुगति (good destination) / सिंगारू (adornment) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3296.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3296.essence: What is good for everyone is also your highest good.
ramacharitamanas::3296.simple_meaning: Real benefit is not selfish gain. It is doing what is right, because that serves everyone and brings the highest good.
ramacharitamanas::3296.simple_insight: You can stop treating duty and benefit as opposites.
ramacharitamanas::3296.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court is trying to stop Ram from leaving and turn him back toward the throne. The speaker says Ram’s return would help everyone, and obeying his command is the truest welfare for all.
ramacharitamanas::3296.modern_relevance: You’re tempted to choose the option that flatters your ego, but the quieter choice would help everyone in the room. Sometimes what is best for you is the same thing that is best for others.
ramacharitamanas::3296.insight: It shifts the mind from private gain to actions that serve the whole field of relationships.

ramacharitamanas::3297.verse_sanskrit: देव एक बिनती सुनि मोरी। उचित होइ तस करब बहोरी॥ तिलक समाजु साजि सबु आना। करिअ सुफल प्रभु जौं मनु माना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3297.verse_hindi: हे देव! आप मेरी एक विनती सुनकर, फिर जैसा उचित हो वैसा ही कीजिए। राजतिलक की सब सामग्री सजाकर लाई गई है, जो प्रभु का मन माने तो उसे सफल कीजिए (उसका उपयोग कीजिए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3297.english_translation: O divine one, hear my one request. Then do what is fitting. The whole royal coronation has been prepared; if it pleases you, let it be made fruitful.
ramacharitamanas::3297.translation_literal: देव (O divine one) / एक (one) / बिनती (request) / सुनि (hearing) / मोरी (my) / उचित (fitting) / होइ (being) / तस (thus) / करब (do) / बहोरी (again) / तिलक (coronation) / समाजु (arrangement) / साजि (having prepared) / सबु (all) / आना (brought) / करिअ (let be done) / सुफल (fruitful) / प्रभु (Lord) / जौं (if) / मनु (mind) / माना (accepts)
ramacharitamanas::3297.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3297.essence: Prepared plans mean nothing unless they serve the right will.
ramacharitamanas::3297.simple_meaning: Bharat asks Ram to ignore the prepared coronation unless Ram himself approves it. What matters is not the ceremony, but what is fitting to Ram's will.
ramacharitamanas::3297.simple_insight: Real loyalty does not cling to appearances. It bends to what is right, even when everything is already set.
ramacharitamanas::3297.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the coronation goods are ready, but Ram is about to be sent away. Bharat speaks with aching humility, asking Ram to decide what should happen next. The verse turns a royal ceremony into a test of obedience and love.
ramacharitamanas::3297.modern_relevance: You have a venue booked, guests invited, and plans printed — then the person at the center says, 'Not like this.' Bharat's response is to stop protecting the plan and honor what is fitting.
ramacharitamanas::3297.insight: It shifts you from defending your arrangement to submitting it to what is truly right.

ramacharitamanas::3298.verse_sanskrit: सानुज पठइअ मोहि बन कीजिअ सबहि सनाथ। नतरु फेरिअहिं बंधु दोउ नाथ चलौं मैं साथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3298.verse_hindi: छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न समेत मुझे वन में भेज दीजिए और (अयोध्या लौटकर) सबको सनाथ कीजिए। नहीं तो किसी तरह भी (यदि आप अयोध्या जाने को तैयार न हों) हे नाथ! लक्ष्मण और शत्रुघ्न दोनों भाइयों को लौटा दीजिए और मैं आपके साथ चलूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3298.english_translation: Send me to the forest with my younger brother, and make everyone safe by returning. Otherwise, if you will not go back to Ayodhya, Lord, send both brothers back, and I will go with you.
ramacharitamanas::3298.translation_literal: सानुज (with younger brother) / पठइअ (send) / मोहि (me) / बन (to the forest) / कीजिअ (do) / सबहि (everyone) / सनाथ (protected, with a lord) / नतरु (otherwise) / फेरिअहिं (send back) / बंधु (brothers) / दोउ (both) / नाथ (Lord) / चलौं (I will go) / मैं (I) / साथ (with)
ramacharitamanas::3298.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3298.essence: Real loyalty asks for the burden, not the reward.
ramacharitamanas::3298.simple_meaning: Bharat asks to go to the forest with his younger brother, or else asks Ram to send the brothers back and let him go with Ram. He wants everyone else to be सुरक्षित first.
ramacharitamanas::3298.simple_insight: Love becomes real when your own comfort matters less than everyone else's safety.
ramacharitamanas::3298.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat stands before Ram with the kingdom at stake. He does not ask for power or ease; he asks that the others be made safe first. If that cannot happen, he chooses exile beside Ram instead.
ramacharitamanas::3298.modern_relevance: You are offered the better seat, the easier role, the cleaner exit — but someone else would be left carrying the burden. Bharat's answer is to move first for everyone else's good.
ramacharitamanas::3298.insight: It shifts the mind from self-advantage to shared responsibility, even when the cost is personal.

ramacharitamanas::3299.verse_sanskrit: नतरु जाहिं बन तीनिउ भाई। बहुरिअ सीय सहित रघुराई॥ जेहि बिधि प्रभु प्रसन्न मन होई। करुना सागर कीजिअ सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3299.verse_hindi: अथवा हम तीनों भाई वन चले जाएँ और हे श्री रघुनाथजी! आप श्री सीताजी सहित (अयोध्या को) लौट जाइए। हे दयासागर! जिस प्रकार से प्रभु का मन प्रसन्न हो, वही कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3299.english_translation: Or let us three brothers go to the forest, and let you, O Raghu lord, return with Sita. O ocean of compassion, do whatever brings your heart peace.
ramacharitamanas::3299.translation_literal: नतरु (or else) / जाहिं (go) / बन (to the forest) / तीनिउ (all three) / भाई (brothers) / बहुरिअ (return) / सीय सहित (with Sita) / रघुराई (Raghu lord) / जेहि बिधि (in whatever way) / प्रभु (the lord) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / मन (mind) / होई (becomes) / करुना सागर (ocean of compassion) / कीजिअ (do) / सोई (that)
ramacharitamanas::3299.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3299.essence: Love gives up its own plan so the beloved can be at peace.
ramacharitamanas::3299.simple_meaning: Bharat offers to go to the forest with both brothers if that is what Ram wants, and asks Ram and Sita to return if that will please him.
ramacharitamanas::3299.simple_insight: Real love stops bargaining and makes room for the other person's peace.
ramacharitamanas::3299.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat stands before Ram after the exile order has shattered the royal family. He offers the impossible: let all three brothers go to the forest, or let Ram return with Sita. What matters most to him is Ram's peace, not his own preference.
ramacharitamanas::3299.modern_relevance: You're in a family argument and realise you no longer care about winning the point. You just want the other person to feel safe enough to soften. That is Bharat's heart.
ramacharitamanas::3299.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to wholehearted yielding for another's good.

ramacharitamanas::3300.verse_sanskrit: देवँ दीन्ह सबु मोहि अभारू। मोरें नीति न धरम बिचारू॥ कहउँ बचन सब स्वारथ हेतू। रहत न आरत के चित चेतू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3300.verse_hindi: हे देव! आपने सारा भार (जिम्मेवारी) मुझ पर रख दिया। पर मुझमें न तो नीति का विचार है, न धर्म का। मैं तो अपने स्वार्थ के लिए सब बातें कह रहा हूँ। आर्त (दुःखी) मनुष्य के चित्त में चेत (विवेक) नहीं रहता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3300.english_translation: The divine has placed the whole burden on me, yet I have no sense of policy or duty. I speak only for my own gain; a distressed heart cannot keep clear awareness.
ramacharitamanas::3300.translation_literal: देवँ (the divine) / दीन्ह (gave) / सबु (all) / मोहि (to me) / अभारू (the burden) / मोरें (in me) / नीति (policy / right conduct) / न (not) / धरम (duty) / बिचारू (consideration) / कहउँ (I speak) / बचन (words) / सब (all) / स्वारथ (self-interest) / हेतू (for the sake of) / रहत (remaining) / न (not) / आरत (distressed) / के (of) / चित (mind) / चेतू (awareness)
ramacharitamanas::3300.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3300.essence: A distressed heart cannot judge cleanly.
ramacharitamanas::3300.simple_meaning: Bharat admits that he has been given a heavy responsibility, but he lacks the judgment to handle it purely. He says his words are driven by self-interest because grief clouds the mind.
ramacharitamanas::3300.simple_insight: Pain can make even honest speech self-protective.
ramacharitamanas::3300.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat is pleading with Ram not to leave him burdened with rule and separation. He confesses that he cannot think straight, cannot weigh right conduct, and is speaking from wounded attachment rather than calm judgment.
ramacharitamanas::3300.modern_relevance: You’re trying to write a careful message after a brutal argument, but every sentence is tinted by hurt. Bharat names that exact moment: distress makes even good intentions wobble.
ramacharitamanas::3300.insight: It teaches you to notice when grief is steering your speech, so you do not mistake emotional pressure for clear judgment.

ramacharitamanas::3301.verse_sanskrit: उतरु देइ सुनि स्वामि रजाई। सो सेवकु लखि लाज लजाई॥ अस मैं अवगुन उदधि अगाधू। स्वामि सनेहँ सराहत साधू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3301.verse_hindi: स्वामी की आज्ञा सुनकर जो उत्तर दे, ऐसे सेवक को देखकर लज्जा भी लजा जाती है। मैं अवगुणों का ऐसा अथाह समुद्र हूँ (कि प्रभु को उत्तर दे रहा हूँ), किन्तु स्वामी (आप) स्नेह वश साधु कहकर मुझे सराहते हैं! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3301.english_translation: Hearing his master's command, the servant who gives a reply makes even shame feel ashamed. I am an unfathomable ocean of faults, yet out of affection my master praises me as noble.
ramacharitamanas::3301.translation_literal: उतरु (reply) / देइ (giving) / सुनि (hearing) / स्वामि (master's) / रजाई (command) / सो (that) / सेवकु (servant) / लखि (seeing) / लाज (shame) / लजाई (is ashamed)॥ / अस (such) / मैं (I) / अवगुन (faults) / उदधि (ocean) / अगाधू (unfathomable)॥ / स्वामि (master) / सनेहँ (with affection) / सराहत (praising) / साधू (noble)॥
ramacharitamanas::3301.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3301.essence: Real service answers without ego and receives praise without claiming it.
ramacharitamanas::3301.simple_meaning: A real servant does not feel proud when answering a master's command. Bharat calls himself full of faults and says Ram praises him only out of affection.
ramacharitamanas::3301.simple_insight: Service feels clean when you stop decorating yourself with self-importance.
ramacharitamanas::3301.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat stands before Ram and speaks with complete humility. He says that a servant who answers a master's command should feel ashamed of any pride. He sees himself as fault-filled, even while Ram praises him lovingly.
ramacharitamanas::3301.modern_relevance: You get a message from someone you deeply respect, and your first urge is to explain, defend, or polish your image. Bharat shows another way: answer simply, stay humble, and let service speak louder than self-protection.
ramacharitamanas::3301.insight: It shifts you from self-display to obedient, humble service.

ramacharitamanas::3302.verse_sanskrit: अब कृपाल मोहि सो मत भावा। सकुच स्वामि मन जाइँ न पावा॥ प्रभु पद सपथ कहउँ सति भाऊ। जग मंगल हित एक उपाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3302.verse_hindi: हे कृपालु! अब तो वही मत मुझे भाता है, जिससे स्वामी का मन संकोच न पावे। प्रभु के चरणों की शपथ है, मैं सत्यभाव से कहता हूँ, जगत के कल्याण के लिए एक यही उपाय है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3302.english_translation: O compassionate one, now only that counsel pleases me by which the master's mind feels no hesitation. By the Lord's feet, I speak truly: this is the only way for the world's welfare.
ramacharitamanas::3302.translation_literal: अब (now) / कृपाल (compassionate one) / मोहि (to me) / सो (that) / मत (counsel) / भावा (is pleasing) / सकुच (hesitation) / स्वामि (master) / मन (mind) / जाइँ (may go) / न (not) / पावा (find) / प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / सपथ (oath) / कहउँ (I speak) / सति (true) / भाऊ (feeling) / जग (world) / मंगल (welfare) / हित (for the good) / एक (one) / उपाऊ (means)
ramacharitamanas::3302.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3302.essence: Real surrender wants the other person's ease, not your own victory.
ramacharitamanas::3302.simple_meaning: Bharat says the best advice is the one that does not make his master uncomfortable. He insists this is the true way to bring good to the world.
ramacharitamanas::3302.simple_insight: Love becomes practical when it protects the other person's peace, not your own pride.
ramacharitamanas::3302.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram with complete humility after the exile has torn the family apart. He says the only counsel worth following is the one that removes hesitation from the master's mind. His devotion has become surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3302.modern_relevance: You're about to send a message that could pressure someone into agreeing just to keep the peace. Bharat's standard is sharper: if your words create hesitation, they are not yet clean.
ramacharitamanas::3302.insight: It shifts you from pushing your preference to serving what truly eases the other person's heart.

ramacharitamanas::3303.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु प्रसन्न मन सकुच तजि जो जेहि आयसु देब। सो सिर धरि धरि करिहि सबु मिटिहि अनट अवरेब ॥
ramacharitamanas::3303.verse_hindi: प्रसन्न मन से संकोच त्यागकर प्रभु जिसे जो आज्ञा देंगे, उसे सब लोग सिर चढ़ा-चढ़ाकर (पालन) करेंगे और सब उपद्रव और उलझनें मिट जाएँगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3303.english_translation: With a pleased heart, set aside hesitation, and whatever order the Lord gives, everyone will carry it on their heads; all obstacles and confusion will dissolve.
ramacharitamanas::3303.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / मन (mind) / सकुच (hesitation) / तजि (leaving) / जो (who/whatever) / जेहि (to whom) / आयसु (command) / देब (will give) / सो (that) / सिर (head) / धरि धरि (again and again placing) / करिहि (will do) / सबु (all) / मिटिहि (will be removed) / अनट (obstacles) / अवरेब (confusion)
ramacharitamanas::3303.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3303.simple_meaning: When you receive a rightful command with a willing heart, people will follow it and the confusion around it will clear away.
ramacharitamanas::3303.simple_insight: Relief comes from dropping self-conscious hesitation and simply doing what is right.
ramacharitamanas::3303.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is speaking with deep humility after the exile has shattered the royal family. He says that if the Lord's order is accepted without hesitation, others will follow it wholeheartedly and the city's disorder will end.
ramacharitamanas::3303.modern_relevance: You’re in a tense family group chat, and everyone is waiting for someone to speak clearly. The moment you stop circling and say the right thing plainly, the whole mess starts settling.
ramacharitamanas::3303.insight: It teaches you to act with wholehearted clarity instead of dragging hesitation into a necessary task.

ramacharitamanas::3304.verse_sanskrit: भरत बचन सुचि सुनि सुर हरषे। साधु सराहि सुमन सुर बरषे॥ असमंजस बस अवध नेवासी। प्रमुदित मन तापस बनबासी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3304.verse_hindi: भरतजी के पवित्र वचन सुनकर देवता हर्षित हुए और 'साधु-साधु' कहकर सराहना करते हुए देवताओं ने फूल बरसाए। अयोध्या निवासी असमंजस के वश हो गए (कि देखें अब श्री रामजी क्या कहते हैं) तपस्वी तथा वनवासी लोग (श्री रामजी के वन में बने रहने की आशा से) मन में परम आनन्दित हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3304.english_translation: Hearing Bharat's pure words, the devas rejoiced. Praising him as noble, they showered flowers. The people of Ayodhya were left in suspense, while ascetics and forest dwellers felt deep joy in their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::3304.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / बचन (words) / सुचि (pure) / सुनि (hearing) / सुर (devas) / हरषे (rejoiced) / साधु (noble) / सराहि (praising) / सुमन (flowers) / सुर (devas) / बरषे (showered) / असमंजस (suspense) / बस (under) / अवध-नेवासी (Ayodhya residents) / प्रमुदित (delighted) / मन (mind) / तापस (ascetics) / बनबासी (forest dwellers)
ramacharitamanas::3304.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3304.essence: Pure words can lift some hearts while leaving the moment unresolved.
ramacharitamanas::3304.simple_meaning: Bharat's sincere words move everyone differently: the devas rejoice, Ayodhya waits in suspense, and holy people feel joy.
ramacharitamanas::3304.simple_insight: When truth is spoken cleanly, it steadies some hearts and unsettles others before the next step arrives.
ramacharitamanas::3304.detailed_meaning: Bharat has just spoken with complete sincerity in the royal gathering at Ayodhya. His words please the devas and delight the renunciates, but the city remains tense, waiting to see how Ram will answer this moment of family duty and public grief.
ramacharitamanas::3304.modern_relevance: You send a message that finally says what you mean. Some people breathe easier, some freeze, and everyone feels the room change.
ramacharitamanas::3304.insight: It shows how sincere speech can transform a whole atmosphere without resolving the larger conflict yet.

ramacharitamanas::3305.verse_sanskrit: चुपहिं रहे रघुनाथ सँकोची। प्रभु गति देखि सभा सब सोची॥ जनक दूत तेहि अवसर आए। मुनि बसिष्ठँ सुनि बेगि बोलाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3305.verse_hindi: किन्तु संकोची श्री रघुनाथजी चुप ही रह गए। प्रभु की यह स्थिति (मौन) देख सारी सभा सोच में पड़ गई। उसी समय जनकजी के दूत आए, यह सुनकर मुनि वशिष्ठजी ने उन्हें तुरंत बुलवा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3305.english_translation: But Raghunath stayed silent, shy and restrained. Seeing the Lord's silence, the whole assembly fell into thought. Just then, Janak's messengers arrived, and hearing this, sage Vashistha quickly called them in.
ramacharitamanas::3305.translation_literal: चुपहिं (remained silent) / रहे (stayed) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / सँकोची (restrained, shy) / प्रभु (the Lord) / गति (state, condition) / देखि (seeing) / सभा (assembly) / सब (all) / सोची (thought, became thoughtful) / जनक (Janak's) / दूत (messengers) / तेहि (that) / अवसर (moment) / आए (came) / मुनि (sage) / बसिष्ठँ (Vashistha) / सुनि (hearing) / बेगि (quickly) / बोलाए (called in)
ramacharitamanas::3305.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3305.essence: Silence can change a whole room before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::3305.simple_meaning: Ram stays silent and the court grows thoughtful. At that moment, Janak's messengers arrive, and Vashistha has them brought in at once.
ramacharitamanas::3305.simple_insight: Sometimes a room changes when the quiet changes first.
ramacharitamanas::3305.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, after Bharat's noble words, Ram remains modest and silent. His silence unsettles the assembly into reflection. Then messengers from Janak arrive, and Vashistha immediately summons them, moving the story forward.
ramacharitamanas::3305.modern_relevance: You say nothing after a tense family conversation, and everyone in the room starts reading your face. Then a message arrives that shifts the whole evening.
ramacharitamanas::3305.insight: It keeps the focus on the unfolding scene, not a moral claim.

ramacharitamanas::3306.verse_sanskrit: करि प्रनाम तिन्ह रामु निहारे। बेषु देखि भए निपट दुखारे॥ दूतन्ह मुनिबर बूझी बाता। कहहु बिदेह भूप कुसलाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3306.verse_hindi: उन्होंने (आकर) प्रणाम करके श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखा। उनका (मुनियों का सा) वेष देखकर वे बहुत ही दुःखी हुए। मुनिश्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी ने दूतों से बात पूछी कि राजा जनक का कुशल समाचार कहो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3306.english_translation: After bowing, they looked at Ram. Seeing his ascetic dress, they were deeply saddened. Then the great sage Vashishtha asked the messengers, “Tell me, how is King Janaka?”
ramacharitamanas::3306.translation_literal: करि (having done) / प्रनाम (bowing) / तिन्ह (they) / रामु (Ram) / निहारे (looked at) / बेषु (dress/appearance) / देखि (seeing) / भए (became) / निपट (utterly) / दुखारे (saddened) / दूतन्ह (to the messengers) / मुनिबर (the great sage) / बूझी (asked) / बाता (news/matter) / कहहु (tell) / बिदेह भूप (King of Videha, Janaka) / कुसलाता (well-being)
ramacharitamanas::3306.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3306.essence: Ram's exile is visible at a glance, and it wounds the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3306.simple_meaning: The messengers bow to Ram, are saddened by his ascetic look, and Vashishtha asks after Janaka's well-being.
ramacharitamanas::3306.simple_insight: No matter how formal the meeting, grief and concern still show through.
ramacharitamanas::3306.detailed_meaning: Janaka's messengers arrive in Ayodhya, bow before Ram, and are struck by his austere appearance in exile. Their sadness is immediate and human. Vashishtha then turns to the practical matter at hand and asks about Janaka's welfare.
ramacharitamanas::3306.modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room and see someone you love looking thinner, quieter, older. The greeting comes first, but the worry lands before any words do.
ramacharitamanas::3306.insight: It captures how appearance can carry emotional truth before anyone speaks.

ramacharitamanas::3307.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सकुचाइ नाइ महि माथा। बोले चरबर जोरें हाथा॥ बूझब राउर सादर साईं। कुसल हेतु सो भयउ गोसाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3307.verse_hindi: यह (मुनि का कुशल प्रश्न) सुनकर सकुचाकर पृथ्वी पर मस्तक नवाकर वे श्रेष्ठ दूत हाथ जोड़कर बोले- हे स्वामी! आपका आदर के साथ पूछना, यही हे गोसाईं! कुशल का कारण हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3307.english_translation: Hearing this, they grew shy, bowed their heads to the ground, and spoke with joined hands. "Your respectful inquiry itself, my lord, has become the reason for our welfare, O gracious one."
ramacharitamanas::3307.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सकुचाइ (growing shy) / नाइ (bowing) / महि (to the ground) / माथा (head) / बोले (spoke) / चरबर (the excellent messengers) / जोरें (joined) / हाथा (hands) / बूझब (inquiring) / राउर (your) / सादर (respectful) / साईं (lord) / कुसल (well-being) / हेतु (cause) / सो (that) / भयउ (became) / गोसाईं (gracious one)
ramacharitamanas::3307.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3307.essence: Respectful concern can itself become comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3307.simple_meaning: The messengers bow respectfully and answer that Ram's own concern for their well-being has already brought them comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3307.simple_insight: A kind question can ease fear before any answer is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3307.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Janak's messengers stand before Ram after seeing his humble, sorrowful state. Shy and reverent, they bow low and answer carefully. Their first comfort is not news, but Ram's own gracious concern for them.
ramacharitamanas::3307.modern_relevance: You walk into a room already tense, and someone asks about your well-being before the agenda begins. That single respectful question softens everything.
ramacharitamanas::3307.insight: It shows how courtesy itself can become a form of care, turning formal speech into relief.

ramacharitamanas::3308.verse_sanskrit: नाहिं त कोसलनाथ कें साथ कुसल गइ नाथ। मिथिला अवध बिसेष तें जगु सब भयउ अनाथ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3308.verse_hindi: नहीं तो हे नाथ! कुशल-क्षेम तो सब कोसलनाथ दशरथजी के साथ ही चली गई। (उनके चले जाने से) यों तो सारा जगत ही अनाथ (स्वामी के बिना असहाय) हो गया, किन्तु मिथिला और अवध तो विशेष रूप से अनाथ हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3308.english_translation: No, with the lord of Kosala gone, all well-being has left with him. With him gone, the world is orphaned, and Mithila and Ayodhya are especially bereft.
ramacharitamanas::3308.translation_literal: नाहिं (no) / त (then) / कोसलनाथ कें साथ (with the lord of Kosala) / कुसल (well-being) / गइ (went) / नाथ (lord) / मिथिला (Mithila) / अवध (Ayodhya) / बिसेष तें (especially) / जगु सब (the whole world) / भयउ (became) / अनाथ (orphaned, without a protector)
ramacharitamanas::3308.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3308.essence: When the protector falls, everyone feels unmoored.
ramacharitamanas::3308.simple_meaning: Dasharath's death is felt not just as one family's loss, but as a loss of protection for the whole world, especially Mithila and Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::3308.simple_insight: Grief can make the whole world feel unprotected, not just your own heart.
ramacharitamanas::3308.detailed_meaning: The news of Dasharath's death has reached Mithila. The speaker says that with the lord of Kosala gone, well-being itself has departed. The shock is so deep that both Mithila and Ayodhya feel abandoned.
ramacharitamanas::3308.modern_relevance: A family loses the person everyone quietly relied on to hold things together. Suddenly the house feels different, the phone calls feel heavier, and even ordinary routines seem unprotected.
ramacharitamanas::3308.insight: It shifts the mind from private loss to the shared emptiness created when a steady presence disappears.

ramacharitamanas::3309.verse_sanskrit: कोसलपति गति सुनि जनकौरा। भे सब लोक सोकबस बौरा॥ जेहिं देखे तेहि समय बिदेहू। नामु सत्य अस लाग न केहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3309.verse_hindi: अयोध्यानाथ की गति (दशरथजी का मरण) सुनकर जनकपुर वासी सभी लोग शोकवश बावले हो गए (सुध-बुध भूल गए)। उस समय जिन्होंने विदेह को (शोकमग्न) देखा, उनमें से किसी को ऐसा न लगा कि उनका विदेह (देहाभिमानरहित) नाम सत्य है! (क्योंकि देहभिमान से शून्य पुरुष को शोक कैसा?) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3309.english_translation: Hearing of the king of Kosala's passing, all the people of Janakpur were overcome by sorrow and went half-mad. At that moment, anyone who saw Videha in grief would not think his name was true, for how could one free of body-identification be touched by sorrow?
ramacharitamanas::3309.translation_literal: कोसलपति (king of Kosala) / गति (passing, fate) / सुनि (hearing) / जनकौरा (people of Janakpur) / भे (became) / सब (all) / लोक (people) / सोकबस (under the sway of grief) / बौरा (mad)॥ / जेहिं (whom) / देखे (seeing) / तेहि समय (at that time) / बिदेहू (Videha, Janaka) / नामु (name) / सत्य (true) / अस (thus) / लाग (seemed) / न (not) / केहू (to anyone) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3309.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3309.essence: Loss can shake a whole city and strip away every mask of composure.
ramacharitamanas::3309.simple_meaning: News of Dasharath's death leaves everyone in Janakpur stunned with grief. Even Janaka, called Videha, seems unable to live up to his name because sorrow has overtaken him.
ramacharitamanas::3309.simple_insight: Grief can make even the most composed person look unrecognisable.
ramacharitamanas::3309.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, word arrives that Dasharath has died. The whole city collapses into shock and sorrow, and even King Janaka, famed as Videha, is seen in visible grief. The verse heightens the emotional fallout before the story turns to Bharat and Ram's exile.
ramacharitamanas::3309.modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after one message: the elder everyone relied on is gone. Even the calmest person in the room looks shaken, because loss changes the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::3309.insight: It shows how one death can spread grief through an entire community and unsettle even the most steady mind.

ramacharitamanas::3310.verse_sanskrit: रानि कुचालि सुनत नरपालहि। सूझ न कछु जस मनि बिनु ब्यालहि॥ भरत राज रघुबर बनबासू। भा मिथिलेसहि हृदयँ हराँसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3310.verse_hindi: रानी की कुचाल सुनकर राजा जनकजी को कुछ सूझ न पड़ा, जैसे मणि के बिना साँप को नहीं सूझता। फिर भरतजी को राज्य और श्री रामचन्द्रजी को वनवास सुनकर मिथिलेश्वर जनकजी के हृदय में बड़ा दुःख हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3310.english_translation: Hearing the queen's crooked scheme, King Janaka could not think straight, like a snake without its jewel. Hearing of Bharat's rule and Raghuvir's exile, great sorrow rose in Janaka's heart.
ramacharitamanas::3310.translation_literal: रानि (queen) / कुचालि (crooked scheme) / सुनत (hearing) / नरपालहि (the king) / सूझ (understand) / न कछु (nothing) / जस (like) / मनि (jewel) / बिनु (without) / ब्यालहि (snake)॥ / भरत (Bharat) / राज (rule) / रघुबर (Raghuvir) / बनबासू (forest exile) / भा (became) / मिथिलेसहि (to Janaka of Mithila) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / हराँसू (sorrow) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3310.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3310.essence: Shock can blur the mind before sorrow breaks the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3310.simple_meaning: Janaka is shocked by the queen's bad plan, and then he feels deep sorrow when he hears that Bharat will rule and Ram will go into exile.
ramacharitamanas::3310.simple_insight: Grief can hit even before the event fully lands.
ramacharitamanas::3310.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Janaka hears Kaikeyi's scheme and cannot make sense of it, just as a snake without its jewel cannot see clearly. Then news reaches him that Bharat will take the throne while Ram goes to the forest, and his heart sinks with sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::3310.modern_relevance: You hear a family decision that feels wrong, and your mind goes blank. Before you can even argue, the weight of what it means for everyone starts to hurt.
ramacharitamanas::3310.insight: It shows how a sudden moral shock can freeze judgment and turn understanding into grief.

ramacharitamanas::3311.verse_sanskrit: नृप बूझे बुध सचिव समाजू। कहहु बिचारि उचित का आजू॥ समुझि अवध असमंजस दोऊ। चलिअ कि रहिअ न कह कछु कोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3311.verse_hindi: राजा ने विद्वानों और मंत्रियों के समाज से पूछा कि विचारकर कहिए, आज (इस समय) क्या करना उचित है? अयोध्या की दशा समझकर और दोनों प्रकार से असमंजस जानकर 'चलिए या रहिए?' किसी ने कुछ नहीं कहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3311.english_translation: The king asked the wise ministers and assembly, 'Think carefully and tell me what is right to do now.' Seeing Ayodhya's confusion, and feeling both choices uncertain, no one said, 'Go' or 'Stay.'
ramacharitamanas::3311.translation_literal: नृप (king) / बूझे (asked) / बुध (wise) / सचिव (ministers) / समाजू (assembly) / कहहु (tell) / बिचारि (after considering) / उचित (right) / का (what) / आजू (today/now) ॥ / समुझि (understanding) / अवध (Ayodhya) / असमंजस (confusion/dilemma) / दोऊ (both) / चलिअ (go) / कि (or) / रहिअ (stay) / न (not) / कह (said) / कछु (anything) / कोऊ (anyone) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3311.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3311.essence: When a situation is torn both ways, wisdom can fall silent.
ramacharitamanas::3311.simple_meaning: The king asks his advisers what should be done, but the situation is so confused that no one can give a clear answer.
ramacharitamanas::3311.simple_insight: Some moments leave even wise people speechless.
ramacharitamanas::3311.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the crisis after Dasharath's death has spread into the court. The king turns to the learned ministers and asks whether the city should move forward or remain as it is, but the grief and uncertainty are so deep that no one can decide.
ramacharitamanas::3311.modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after bad news, and everyone waits for someone wiser to speak first. Sometimes confusion is so complete that even careful people have no ready answer.
ramacharitamanas::3311.insight: It shows that before action can begin, a community may first have to face its own confusion.

ramacharitamanas::3312.verse_sanskrit: नृपहिं धीर धरि हृदयँ बिचारी। पठए अवध चतुर चर चारी॥ बूझि भरत सति भाउ कुभाऊ। आएहु बेगि न होइ लखाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3312.verse_hindi: (जब किसी ने कोई सम्मति नहीं दी) तब राजा ने धीरज धर हृदय में विचारकर चार चतुर गुप्तचर (जासूस) अयोध्या को भेजे (और उनसे कह दिया कि) तुम लोग (श्री रामजी के प्रति) भरतजी के सद्भाव (अच्छे भाव, प्रेम) या दुर्भाव (बुरा भाव, विरोध) का (यथार्थ) पता लगाकर जल्दी लौट आना, किसी को तुम्हारा पता न लगने पावे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3312.english_translation: With steady heart, the king reflected and sent four clever spies to Ayodhya. He told them to find out Bharat's true feelings toward Ram — goodwill or hostility — and return quickly without being noticed.
ramacharitamanas::3312.translation_literal: नृपहिं (to the king) / धीर धरि (holding patience) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिचारी (having considered) / पठए (sent) / अवध (to Ayodhya) / चतुर (clever) / चर (spies) / चारी (four)॥ / बूझि (finding out) / भरत (Bharat's) / सति भाउ (good feeling) / कुभाऊ (bad feeling) / आएहु (come) / बेगि (quickly) / न होइ (without being) / लखाऊ (noticed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3312.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3312.essence: Steady minds look for truth before they decide.
ramacharitamanas::3312.simple_meaning: The king calmly sends four spies to Ayodhya to learn whether Bharat feels loving loyalty or hidden opposition toward Ram, and to return unseen.
ramacharitamanas::3312.simple_insight: Not every question can be asked openly; sometimes care means checking the truth quietly.
ramacharitamanas::3312.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the shock of Ram's exile and the court's confusion, Dasharath's side needs clarity about Bharat's heart. The king waits, thinks carefully, and sends four discreet spies to see whether Bharat stands with Ram or against him.
ramacharitamanas::3312.modern_relevance: You hear a family rumor and stop yourself from reacting too fast. Before the accusation, you quietly check what is actually true.
ramacharitamanas::3312.insight: It shifts judgment from panic to careful observation before acting.
