ramacharitamanas::3313.verse_sanskrit: गए अवध चर भरत गति बूझि देखि करतूति। चले चित्रकूटहि भरतु चार चले तेरहूति ॥
ramacharitamanas::3313.verse_hindi: गुप्तचर अवध को गए और भरतजी का ढंग जानकर और उनकी करनी देखकर, जैसे ही भरतजी चित्रकूट को चले, वे तिरहुत (मिथिला) को चल दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3313.english_translation: The spies of Ayodhya observed Bharata's conduct and actions. When Bharata set out for Chitrakoot, they left for Tirhut.
ramacharitamanas::3313.translation_literal: गए (went) / अवध (Ayodhya) / चर (spies) / भरत (Bharata) / गति (conduct) / बूझि (having understood) / देखि (having seen) / करतूति (actions) / चले (went) / चित्रकूटहि (to Chitrakoot) / भरतु (Bharata) / चार (spies) / चले (went) / तेरहूति (to Tirhut)
ramacharitamanas::3313.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3313.essence: True conduct is revealed by what you do, not what you say.
ramacharitamanas::3313.simple_meaning: Ayodhya's spies watched Bharata closely, understood his true conduct, and reported back. When Bharata headed to Chitrakoot, the spies returned to Tirhut.
ramacharitamanas::3313.simple_insight: A person's real character shows itself in action, not in claims.
ramacharitamanas::3313.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's tense search for Bharata's intentions, King Dasharath has already sent secret spies to read his heart. They watch Bharata's conduct, see his sincerity, and leave for Tirhut just as Bharata goes to Chitrakoot.
ramacharitamanas::3313.modern_relevance: A manager quietly watches how you handle pressure, not just what you promise in the interview. Your real nature becomes visible in the way you move when no one is applauding.
ramacharitamanas::3313.insight: It shifts attention from public words to visible conduct as the true measure of character.

ramacharitamanas::3314.verse_sanskrit: दूतन्ह आइ भरत कइ करनी। जनक समाज जथामति बरनी॥ सुनि गुर परिजन सचिव महीपति। भे सब सोच सनेहँ बिकल अति ॥
ramacharitamanas::3314.verse_hindi: (गुप्त) दूतों ने आकर राजा जनकजी की सभा में भरतजी की करनी का अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार वर्णन किया। उसे सुनकर गुरु, कुटुम्बी, मंत्री और राजा सभी सोच और स्नेह से अत्यन्त व्याकुल हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3314.english_translation: The messengers returned and described Bharat's conduct in Janak's assembly as best they could. Hearing it, the guru, relatives, ministers, and the king were all overwhelmed with thought and affection.
ramacharitamanas::3314.translation_literal: दूतन्ह (by the messengers) / आइ (having come) / भरत (Bharat's) / कइ करनी (conduct, actions) / जनक समाज (in Janak's assembly) / जथामति (according to their understanding) / बरनी (described) / सुनि (having heard) / गुर (the guru) / परिजन (relatives) / सचिव (ministers) / महीपति (the king) / भे (became) / सब (all) / सोच (thoughtful, worried) / सनेहँ (with affection) / बिकल (distressed) / अति (very much)
ramacharitamanas::3314.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3314.essence: Bharat’s conduct moves people before he even arrives.
ramacharitamanas::3314.simple_meaning: The messengers report Bharat's conduct, and everyone in Janak's court is moved into deep concern and affection.
ramacharitamanas::3314.simple_insight: Your sincerity can stir hearts even before you speak for yourself.
ramacharitamanas::3314.detailed_meaning: Bharat's messengers return to Janak's court after seeing how he is living. They describe his conduct, and the whole assembly — guru, family, ministers, and king — is shaken by concern and affection. The verse builds the emotional response before the next decision.
ramacharitamanas::3314.modern_relevance: A friend comes back from visiting someone you admire and quietly says, 'You should see how they’re living.' Suddenly the room goes still, because their character has already spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3314.insight: It shows how true conduct travels farther than words and changes the atmosphere around you.

ramacharitamanas::3315.verse_sanskrit: धरि धीरजु करि भरत बड़ाई। लिए सुभट साहनी बोलाई॥ घर पुर देस राखि रखवारे। हय गय रथ बहु जान सँवारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3315.verse_hindi: फिर जनकजी ने धीरज धरकर और भरतजी की बड़ाई करके अच्छे योद्धाओं और साहनियों को बुलाया। घर, नगर और देश में रक्षकों को रखकर, घोड़े, हाथी, रथ आदि बहुत सी सवारियाँ सजवाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3315.english_translation: Then Janak, steadying himself and praising Bharat, summoned brave warriors and officers. He posted guards in the house, city, and country, and arranged horses, elephants, chariots, and many vehicles.
ramacharitamanas::3315.translation_literal: धरि (having held) / धीरजु (patience, composure) / करि (doing) / भरत (Bharat) / बड़ाई (praise) / लिए (took, summoned) / सुभट (brave warriors) / साहनी (officers, attendants) / बोलाई (calling) ॥ / घर (house) / पुर (city) / देस (country) / राखि (placing) / रखवारे (guards, watchmen) / हय (horses) / गय (elephants) / रथ (chariots) / बहु (many) / जान (vehicles, conveyances) / सँवारे (made ready, arranged) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3315.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3315.essence: Respect becomes real when it is followed by careful action.
ramacharitamanas::3315.simple_meaning: Janak stays composed, praises Bharat, and prepares guards and transport for the journey.
ramacharitamanas::3315.simple_insight: Steady leadership looks calm on the surface and thorough underneath.
ramacharitamanas::3315.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Janak has just heard of Bharat's extraordinary conduct. He responds with composure, honouring Bharat and quietly organizing protection and travel arrangements. The verse supports the larger scene of respectful departure, not a new teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3315.modern_relevance: When a respected guest is leaving after a tense family visit, you stop talking and start arranging the practical details: security, transport, timing, and dignity.
ramacharitamanas::3315.insight: It shows leadership as calm action: praise the worthy person, then handle the logistics without drama.

ramacharitamanas::3316.verse_sanskrit: दुघरी साधि चले ततकाला। किए बिश्रामु न मग महिपाला॥ भोरहिं आजु नहाइ प्रयागा। चले जमुन उतरन सबु लागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3316.verse_hindi: वे दुघड़िया मुहूर्त साधकर उसी समय चल पड़े। राजा ने रास्ते में कहीं विश्राम भी नहीं किया। आज ही सबेरे प्रयागराज में स्नान करके चले हैं। जब सब लोग यमुनाजी उतरने लगे, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3316.english_translation: They set out at the proper hour and left at once. The king did not rest anywhere on the road. He bathed at Prayagraj this morning and then moved on; when everyone began crossing the Yamuna...
ramacharitamanas::3316.translation_literal: दुघरी (proper hour) / साधि (having arranged) / चले (went) / ततकाला (immediately) / किए (did) / बिश्रामु (rest) / न (not) / मग (on the road) / महिपाला (king) / भोरहिं (in the morning) / आजु (today) / नहाइ (bathed) / प्रयागा (at Prayaga) / चले (went) / जमुन (Yamuna) / उतरन (to cross) / सबु (all) / लागा (began)
ramacharitamanas::3316.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3316.simple_meaning: The king set out immediately, without stopping to rest, after bathing at Prayagraj and reaching the Yamuna crossing with everyone else.
ramacharitamanas::3316.simple_insight: It shows steady movement and urgency, not a teaching meant to stand alone.
ramacharitamanas::3316.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharata’s party is on the road after the news of Ram’s exile has shaken the kingdom. The narrator simply tracks their movement: they depart at the right time, do not stop to rest, and reach the Yamuna crossing. It is scene-setting, not the verse’s main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3316.modern_relevance: You can feel the pace of a journey when everyone is too restless to pause, but this line is still only the movement of the scene.
ramacharitamanas::3316.insight: It keeps the narrative moving from one place to the next.

ramacharitamanas::3317.verse_sanskrit: खबरि लेन हम पठए नाथा। तिन्ह कहि अस महि नायउ माथा॥ साथ किरात छ सातक दीन्हे। मुनिबर तुरत बिदा चर कीन्हे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3317.verse_hindi: तब हे नाथ! हमें खबर लेने को भेजा। उन्होंने (दूतों ने) ऐसा कहकर पृथ्वी पर सिर नवाया। मुनिश्रेष्ठ वशिष्ठजी ने कोई छह-सात भीलों को साथ देकर दूतों को तुरंत विदा कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3317.english_translation: Then, O Lord, they sent us to bring news. Hearing this, they bowed their heads to the ground. The best sage Vashishtha immediately sent the messengers off with six or seven forest dwellers.
ramacharitamanas::3317.translation_literal: खबरि (news) / लेन (to take) / हम (we) / पठए (were sent) / नाथा (O Lord) / तिन्ह (they) / कहि (saying) / अस (thus) / महि (earth) / नायउ (bowed) / माथा (head) / साथ (with) / किरात (forest-dwellers) / छ सातक (six-seven) / दीन्हे (given) / मुनिबर (best sage) / तुरत (immediately) / बिदा (farewell) / चर (messengers) / कीन्हे (made)
ramacharitamanas::3317.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3317.essence: Respect and readiness move the journey forward.
ramacharitamanas::3317.simple_meaning: The messengers explain why they came, bow in respect, and are quickly sent onward with a small escort.
ramacharitamanas::3317.simple_insight: Respect opens the way, and the right support helps a task move quickly.
ramacharitamanas::3317.detailed_meaning: At Janak's court, the messengers explain their errand to Vashishtha. They bow low in reverence, and the sage promptly sends them onward with a few forest guides. The scene keeps the journey moving toward Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::3317.modern_relevance: You finally get the answer you came for, and the other person doesn’t waste time. They acknowledge you, give you help, and send you on with exactly what you need.
ramacharitamanas::3317.insight: It shows how humility and prompt support keep an important task from stalling.

ramacharitamanas::3318.verse_sanskrit: सुनत जनक आगवनु सबु हरषेउ अवध समाजु। रघुनंदनहि सकोचु बड़ सोच बिबस सुरराजु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3318.verse_hindi: जनकजी का आगमन सुनकर अयोध्या का सारा समाज हर्षित हो गया। श्री रामजी को बड़ा संकोच हुआ और देवराज इन्द्र तो विशेष रूप से सोच के वश में हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3318.english_translation: Hearing of Janak's arrival, all of Ayodhya rejoiced. Raghunandan felt shy, and even Indra was overcome with thought.
ramacharitamanas::3318.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / जनक (Janak) / आगवनु (arrival) / सबु (all) / हरषेउ (rejoiced) / अवध (Ayodhya) / समाजु (the assembly) / रघुनंदनहि (for Raghunandan) / सकोचु (shyness) / बड़ (great) / सोच (thought) / बिबस (overcome) / सुरराजु (Indra, king of the devas)
ramacharitamanas::3318.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3318.essence: Joy spreads outward, while greatness often turns inward to humility.
ramacharitamanas::3318.simple_meaning: Ayodhya is happy to hear that Janak has arrived. Ram feels shy, and even Indra is left thoughtful.
ramacharitamanas::3318.simple_insight: Joy can fill a whole city, while a great event still stirs quiet inward hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::3318.detailed_meaning: As Janak comes to Ayodhya, the whole city lights up with joy. Ram responds with modesty rather than pride, while even Indra, watching this unfolding reunion, falls into deep thought. The verse sets the emotional tone before the next turn in the story.
ramacharitamanas::3318.modern_relevance: A family group chat explodes with excitement when a respected elder announces a visit. Everyone is thrilled, but you feel that quiet self-consciousness that comes when something important is about to happen.
ramacharitamanas::3318.insight: It frames a public moment through mixed inner reactions, not just outward celebration.

ramacharitamanas::3319.verse_sanskrit: गरइ गलानि कुटिल कैकेई। काहि कहै केहि दूषनु देई॥ अस मन आनि मुदित नर नारी। भयउ बहोरि रहब दिन चारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3319.verse_hindi: कुटिल कैकेयी मन ही मन ग्लानि (पश्चाताप) से गली जाती है। किससे कहे और किसको दोष दे? और सब नर-नारी मन में ऐसा विचार कर प्रसन्न हो रहे हैं कि (अच्छा हुआ, जनकजी के आने से) चार (कुछ) दिन और रहना हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3319.english_translation: Kakeyi is consumed by remorse. Whom can she tell, and whom can she blame? Meanwhile, men and women all felt glad, thinking they would stay four more days.
ramacharitamanas::3319.translation_literal: गरइ (is consumed) / गलानि (remorse) / कुटिल (crooked) / कैकेई (Kaikeyi) / काहि (to whom) / कहै (to say) / केहि (which) / दूषनु (blame) / देई (give) / अस (such) / मन (mind) / आनि (bringing) / मुदित (glad) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / भयउ (became) / बहोरि (again) / रहब (staying) / दिन (days) / चारी (four)
ramacharitamanas::3319.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3319.essence: Remorse isolates you even in the middle of shared joy.
ramacharitamanas::3319.simple_meaning: Kaikeyi is trapped in remorse and has no one left to blame. At the same time, the people of Ayodhya are happy because Janak's visit means four more days together.
ramacharitamanas::3319.simple_insight: Pride turns inward and burns; simple joy can still live around it.
ramacharitamanas::3319.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Janak's arrival has lifted everyone's mood and extended the celebration. But Kaikeyi, whose choices have already set tragedy in motion, is now eaten by regret. This verse contrasts public happiness with private ruin.
ramacharitamanas::3319.modern_relevance: A group chat is buzzing with plans for one more night together, while you sit alone replaying the choice that started the mess. Everyone else is enjoying the extra time; your own mind has turned against you.
ramacharitamanas::3319.insight: It separates outward celebration from inward remorse, showing how one person's regret can exist beside everyone else's relief.

ramacharitamanas::3320.verse_sanskrit: एहि प्रकार गत बासर सोऊ। प्रात नहान लाग सबु कोऊ॥ करि मज्जनु पूजहिं नर नारी। गनप गौरि तिपुरारि तमारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3320.verse_hindi: इस तरह वह दिन भी बीत गया। दूसरे दिन प्रातःकाल सब कोई स्नान करने लगे। स्नान करके सब नर-नारी गणेशजी, गौरीजी, महादेवजी और सूर्य भगवान की पूजा करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3320.english_translation: Thus that day passed. At dawn everyone rose to bathe. After bathing, the men and women worshiped Ganesha, Gauri, Mahadev, and the Sun.
ramacharitamanas::3320.translation_literal: एहि प्रकार (in this way) / गत (passed) / बासर (day) / सोऊ (that) / प्रात (morning) / नहान (bath) / लाग (began) / सबु (all) / कोऊ (everyone) ॥ / करि (having done) / मज्जनु (bathing) / पूजहिं (worship) / नर नारी (men and women) / गनप (Ganesha) / गौरि (Gauri) / तिपुरारि (Mahadev) / तमारी (the Sun)
ramacharitamanas::3320.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3320.essence: Daily devotion steadies life before the next turning arrives.
ramacharitamanas::3320.simple_meaning: The day ends, and the next morning everyone bathes and offers prayers to the divine forms they honor.
ramacharitamanas::3320.simple_insight: Ritual can mark a turning point in a household without needing big words.
ramacharitamanas::3320.detailed_meaning: After the tense waiting in Ayodhya, the day finally passes. At dawn, the city wakes, bathes, and turns to worship before the next stage of events begins. This verse simply resets the scene through daily devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3320.modern_relevance: You wake before the house is fully alive, shower, and light a lamp before the day begins. Small acts of reverence can steady everything that follows.
ramacharitamanas::3320.insight: It shifts attention from emotional suspense to the quiet discipline of daily worship.

ramacharitamanas::3321.verse_sanskrit: रमा रमन पद बंदि बहोरी। बिनवहिं अंजुलि अंचल जोरी॥ राजा रामु जानकी रानी। आनँद अवधि अवध रजधानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3321.verse_hindi: फिर लक्ष्मीपति भगवान विष्णु के चरणों की वंदना करके, दोनों हाथ जोड़कर, आँचल पसारकर विनती करते हैं कि श्री रामजी राजा हों, जानकीजी रानी हों तथा राजधानी अयोध्या आनंद की सीमा होकर- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3321.english_translation: After bowing again to the feet of the Lord of delight, they pray with folded hands and lifted hems: "May King Ram reign, may Queen Janaki reign, and may Ayodhya, the capital, become the limit of joy."
ramacharitamanas::3321.translation_literal: रमा (of Lakshmi's lord) / रमन (delight) / पद (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / बहोरी (again) / बिनवहिं (they pray) / अंजुलि (palms) / अंचल (hem) / जोरी (joined) / राजा (king) / रामु (Ram) / जानकी (Janaki) / रानी (queen) / आनँद (joy) / अवधि (limit) / अवध (Ayodhya) / रजधानी (capital)
ramacharitamanas::3321.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3321.essence: True joy is a city ruled by Ram and Janaki.
ramacharitamanas::3321.simple_meaning: The people bow to Ram and pray for a life where Ram and Janaki rule Ayodhya together in joy.
ramacharitamanas::3321.simple_insight: Real peace begins when you want the right ruler, not just a comfortable life.
ramacharitamanas::3321.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the people have already turned from regret to prayer. After bowing to Ram again, they join their hands and ask for the only future they trust: Ram as king, Janaki as queen, and the city filled with joy.
ramacharitamanas::3321.modern_relevance: You sit with family after a hard decision and realize everyone wants the same thing: not just success, but a home where goodness actually leads. This verse turns longing into prayer.
ramacharitamanas::3321.insight: It shifts desire from personal comfort to a life ordered by Ram’s presence.

ramacharitamanas::3322.verse_sanskrit: सुबस बसउ फिरि सहित समाजा। भरतहि रामु करहुँ जुबराजा॥ एहि सुख सुधाँ सींचि सब काहू। देव देहु जग जीवन लाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3322.verse_hindi: फिर समाज सहित सुखपूर्वक बसे और श्री रामजी भरतजी को युवराज बनावें। हे देव! इस सुख रूपी अमृत से सींचकर सब किसी को जगत में जीने का लाभ दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3322.english_translation: Then let everyone live together in happiness again. Let Ram make Bharat the crown prince. O divine one, bathe everyone in this nectar of joy and grant the world the blessing of living well.
ramacharitamanas::3322.translation_literal: सुबस (happily) / बसउ (let dwell) / फिरि (again) / सहित (together with) / समाजा (the assembly) । भरतहि (Bharat) / रामु (Ram) / करहुँ (may make) / जुबराजा (crown prince) । एहि (this) / सुख (joy) / सुधाँ (nectar) / सींचि (bathe) / सब (everyone) / काहू (each one) । देव (divine one) / देहु (give) / जग (world) / जीवन (living) / लाहू (blessing, benefit) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3322.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3322.essence: Blessing becomes complete only when it includes everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3322.simple_meaning: The people pray that Ram should make Bharat the crown prince and that everyone should live in happiness again.
ramacharitamanas::3322.simple_insight: Real joy is never private; it becomes complete only when everyone shares it.
ramacharitamanas::3322.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the people have gathered after days of grief and uncertainty. They are not asking for personal gain; they want Ram's rule, Bharat's honour, and the whole city restored to peace. This verse turns longing into a collective prayer.
ramacharitamanas::3322.modern_relevance: After a family crisis, everyone sits around the dinner table pretending to be fine, but what they really want is simple: for things to feel whole again. This verse knows that wish.
ramacharitamanas::3322.insight: It shifts desire from personal advantage to shared well-being under Ram's order.

ramacharitamanas::3323.verse_sanskrit: गुर समाज भाइन्ह सहित राम राजु पुर होउ। अछत राम राजा अवध मरिअ माग सबु कोउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3323.verse_hindi: गुरु, समाज और भाइयों समेत श्री रामजी का राज्य अवधपुरी में हो और श्री रामजी के राजा रहते ही हम लोग अयोध्या में मरें। सब कोई यही माँगते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3323.english_translation: May Ram's rule fill Ayodhya with the guru, the community, and the brothers. While Ram remains king, may everyone here die in Ayodhya; that is what everyone asks for.
ramacharitamanas::3323.translation_literal: गुर समाज (with the guru and the community) / भाइन्ह सहित (together with the brothers) / राम राजु (Ram's rule) / पुर होउ (may fill the city) / अछत (while still living, while present) / राम राजा (Ram as king) / अवध (Ayodhya) / मरिअ (may we die) / माग (ask) / सबु कोउ (everyone)
ramacharitamanas::3323.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3323.essence: Ram's presence is the only crown Ayodhya wants.
ramacharitamanas::3323.simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya want Ram's reign to remain with them always. Their deepest wish is to live and die while Ram is king.
ramacharitamanas::3323.simple_insight: Love becomes simple when your highest wish is just to remain near what you cherish.
ramacharitamanas::3323.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the sorrow of exile, the city’s people speak with one heart. They do not ask for wealth, comfort, or power. They ask only that Ram remain their king, with the guru, the brothers, and the whole community together in his presence.
ramacharitamanas::3323.modern_relevance: A family gathers after a painful move, and nobody talks about success or status. What they really want is to stay together, under one roof, with the person who makes home feel like home.
ramacharitamanas::3323.insight: It shifts desire away from achievement and toward loving presence as the real reward.

ramacharitamanas::3324.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सनेहमय पुरजन बानी। निंदहिं जोग बिरति मुनि ग्यानी॥ एहि बिधि नित्यकरम करि पुरजन। रामहि करहिं प्रनाम पुलकि तन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3324.verse_hindi: अयोध्या वासियों की प्रेममयी वाणी सुनकर ज्ञानी मुनि भी अपने योग और वैराग्य की निंदा करते हैं। अवधवासी इस प्रकार नित्यकर्म करके श्री रामजी को पुलकित शरीर हो प्रणाम करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3324.english_translation: Hearing the loving words of the people of Ayodhya, even wise sages and ascetics forget their pride in yoga and renunciation. In this way, after doing their daily duties, the people of Ayodhya bow to Ram with bodies thrilled with devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3324.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सनेहमय (full of affection) / पुरजन (townspeople) / बानी (speech) / निंदहिं (they condemn) / जोग (yoga) / बिरति (renunciation) / मुनि (sages) / ग्यानी (wise ones)॥ एहि (in this) / बिधि (manner) / नित्यकरम (daily duties) / करि (doing) / पुरजन (townspeople) / रामहि (to Ram) / करहिं (do) / प्रनाम (salutation) / पुलकि (thrilled) / तन (body) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3324.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3324.essence: Love for Ram makes even renunciation bow.
ramacharitamanas::3324.simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya love Ram so deeply that even sages seem to set aside pride in yoga and renunciation. Their daily life itself becomes an offering to him.
ramacharitamanas::3324.simple_insight: Real devotion can be so alive that it makes lofty ideals feel secondary.
ramacharitamanas::3324.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the citizens are speaking with such tender love for Ram that even sages and learned renunciates are imagined as humbled by it. The verse shows a city where ordinary daily duties and devotion to Ram blend into one living practice.
ramacharitamanas::3324.modern_relevance: You watch someone care for their aging parent without drama, without speeches, just steady love. In that quiet devotion, grand theories about detachment suddenly feel less important.
ramacharitamanas::3324.insight: It shifts the mind from abstract spirituality to devotion expressed through ordinary duty and affection.

ramacharitamanas::3325.verse_sanskrit: ऊँच नीच मध्यम नर नारी। लहहिं दरसु निज निज अनुहारी॥ सावधान सबही सनमानहिं। सकल सराहत कृपानिधानहिं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3325.verse_hindi: ऊँच, नीच और मध्यम सभी श्रेणियों के स्त्री-पुरुष अपने-अपने भाव के अनुसार श्री रामजी का दर्शन प्राप्त करते हैं। श्री रामचन्द्रजी सावधानी के साथ सबका सम्मान करते हैं और सभी कृपानिधान श्री रामचन्द्रजी की सराहना करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3325.english_translation: People of every rank — high, middle, and low — receive Ram's darshan according to their own disposition. Ram carefully honors everyone, and all praise the treasure of compassion.
ramacharitamanas::3325.translation_literal: ऊँच (high) / नीच (low) / मध्यम (middle) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / लहहिं (receive) / दरसु (darshan, sight) / निज (own) / निज (own) / अनुहारी (according to)॥ / सावधान (carefully) / सबही (everyone) / सनमानहिं (honor) / सकल (all) / सराहत (praising) / कृपानिधानहिं (the treasure of compassion)
ramacharitamanas::3325.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3325.essence: Ram's compassion meets every person without hierarchy.
ramacharitamanas::3325.simple_meaning: People of every social level can receive Ram's presence according to their own inner readiness. He treats everyone with care, and everyone praises his compassion.
ramacharitamanas::3325.simple_insight: You do not need status to be seen. What matters is your openness, and the grace with which you are received.
ramacharitamanas::3325.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the city is overflowing with longing for Ram. As people wait for his return, the poet shows that Ram does not belong to one class alone. He meets each person according to their heart, and his respect reaches everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3325.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where some people are ignored and others are instantly welcomed. This verse reminds you that real greatness does not sort people by rank; it makes room for everyone with equal care.
ramacharitamanas::3325.insight: It shifts attention from social rank to inner receptivity and mutual respect.

ramacharitamanas::3326.verse_sanskrit: लरिकाइहि तें रघुबर बानी। पालत नीति प्रीति पहिचानी॥ सील सकोच सिंधु रघुराऊ। सुमुख सुलोचन सरल सुभाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3326.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी की लड़कपन से ही यह बान है कि वे प्रेम को पहचानकर नीति का पालन करते हैं। श्री रघुनाथजी शील और संकोच के समुद्र हैं। वे सुंदर मुख के (या सबके अनुकूल रहने वाले), सुंदर नेत्र वाले (या सबको कृपा और प्रेम की दृष्टि से देखने वाले) और सरल स्वभाव हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3326.english_translation: From childhood, Raghubar has known how to honor love while keeping to righteous conduct. Lord of Raghu is an ocean of dignity and restraint, with a pleasing face, gentle eyes, and a simple nature.
ramacharitamanas::3326.translation_literal: लरिकाइहि (from childhood) / तें (since) / रघुबर (Raghubar) / बानी (nature, habit) / पालत (keeping, honoring) / नीति (righteous conduct) / प्रीति (love) / पहिचानी (having recognized) / सील (dignity, virtue) / सकोच (restraint, modesty) / सिंधु (ocean) / रघुराऊ (Lord of Raghu) / सुमुख (pleasing-faced) / सुलोचन (gentle-eyed) / सरल (simple, straightforward) / सुभाऊ (nature)
ramacharitamanas::3326.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3326.essence: Ram’s greatness is gentle, disciplined, and naturally loving.
ramacharitamanas::3326.simple_meaning: Ram has always blended love with righteous conduct. He is gracious, modest, and naturally सरल in the way he meets others.
ramacharitamanas::3326.simple_insight: True greatness can be gentle. You do not need hardness to hold your values.
ramacharitamanas::3326.detailed_meaning: Ayodhya is grieving Ram’s exile, and the people remember who he has always been. Tulsidas pauses the sorrow to describe Ram’s lifelong character: loving, disciplined, modest, and easy to approach. This is a supporting portrait, not the passage’s main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3326.modern_relevance: You meet someone who stays calm when others are emotional, never crude, never cold. Their steadiness feels rare because it carries both warmth and self-control.
ramacharitamanas::3326.insight: It shifts admiration away from charisma and toward character: love, restraint, and moral steadiness together.

ramacharitamanas::3327.verse_sanskrit: कहत राम गुन गन अनुरागे। सब निज भाग सराहन लागे॥ हम सम पुन्य पुंज जग थोरे। जिन्हहि रामु जानत करि मोरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3327.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के गुण समूहों को कहते-कहते सब लोग प्रेम में भर गए और अपने भाग्य की सराहना करने लगे कि जगत में हमारे समान पुण्य की बड़ी पूँजी वाले थोड़े ही हैं, जिन्हें श्री रामजी अपना करके जानते हैं (ये मेरे हैं ऐसा जानते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3327.english_translation: As people spoke of Ram's virtues, they became filled with love and began praising their own good fortune: “Few in the world have such great stores of merit as we do, for Ram knows us as his own.”
ramacharitamanas::3327.translation_literal: कहत (speaking) / राम (Ram) / गुन (virtues) / गन (multitude) / अनुरागे (filled with love) / सब (all) / निज (their own) / भाग (fortune) / सराहन (to praise) / लागे (began) / हम (we) / सम (equal to) / पुन्य (merit) / पुंज (heap) / जग (world) / थोरे (few) / जिन्हहि (whom) / रामु (Ram) / जानत (knows) / करि (as) / मोरे (mine/us)
ramacharitamanas::3327.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3327.essence: Being known by Ram is the rarest and richest blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3327.simple_meaning: Hearing Ram's qualities makes everyone feel loving and grateful. They see being recognized by Ram as their greatest blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3327.simple_insight: You stop measuring yourself by status and start feeling the joy of belonging to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3327.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, people keep speaking about Ram's qualities until the whole gathering softens into love. As they praise him, they also praise their own fortune: Ram knows them as his own, and that recognition feels priceless.
ramacharitamanas::3327.modern_relevance: You hear someone speak of a mentor who remembers your name, your effort, your small kindnesses. Suddenly, the room feels warmer. Being seen by someone you love can change your whole sense of worth.
ramacharitamanas::3327.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to grateful belonging.

ramacharitamanas::3328.verse_sanskrit: प्रेम मगन तेहि समय सब सुनि आवत मिथिलेसु। सहित सभा संभ्रम उठेउ रबिकुल कमल दिनेसु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3328.verse_hindi: उस समय सब लोग प्रेम में मग्न हैं। इतने में ही मिथिलापति जनकजी को आते हुए सुनकर सूर्यकुल रूपी कमल के सूर्य श्री रामचन्द्रजी सभा सहित आदरपूर्वक जल्दी से उठ खड़े हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3328.english_translation: At that moment, everyone was lost in love. Then, hearing that King Janaka of Mithila was arriving, Rama, the sun of the Raghu line, rose at once with the assembly in respectful haste.
ramacharitamanas::3328.translation_literal: प्रेम (love) / मगन (immersed) / तेहि समय (at that time) / सब (all) / सुनि (hearing) / आवत (coming) / मिथिलेसु (Janaka of Mithila) / सहित (with) / सभा (assembly) / संभ्रम (haste / reverent urgency) / उठेउ (rose) / रबिकुल (sun-line) / कमल (lotus) / दिनेसु (sun)
ramacharitamanas::3328.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3328.essence: Love becomes real when respect moves your body.
ramacharitamanas::3328.simple_meaning: Everyone was absorbed in love, and when Janaka's arrival was announced, Rama rose quickly with respectful honor.
ramacharitamanas::3328.simple_insight: Real reverence shows itself in how quickly you rise for another person.
ramacharitamanas::3328.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the mood is overflowing with affection. The moment his arrival is heard, Rama does not remain seated as a king; he rises before the whole assembly with honor. The scene shows his natural humility and respect.
ramacharitamanas::3328.modern_relevance: You hear your mentor has arrived, and you stop mid-conversation to stand and greet them properly. That small movement says more than polished words ever could.
ramacharitamanas::3328.insight: It shifts respect from private feeling to visible action.

ramacharitamanas::3329.verse_sanskrit: भाइ सचिव गुर पुरजन साथा। आगें गवनु कीन्ह रघुनाथा॥ गिरिबरु दीख जनकपति जबहीं। करि प्रनामु रथ त्यागेउ तबहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3329.verse_hindi: भाई, मंत्री, गुरु और पुरवासियों को साथ लेकर श्री रघुनाथजी आगे (जनकजी की अगवानी में) चले। जनकजी ने ज्यों ही पर्वत श्रेष्ठ कामदनाथ को देखा, त्यों ही प्रणाम करके उन्होंने रथ छोड़ दिया। (पैदल चलना शुरू कर दिया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3329.english_translation: Ram and Lakshman went ahead with their brothers, ministers, the teacher, and the townspeople. When King Janaka saw the great mountain, he bowed and got down from his chariot at once.
ramacharitamanas::3329.translation_literal: भाइ (brothers) / सचिव (ministers) / गुर (teacher) / पुरजन (townspeople) / साथा (together) / आगें (ahead) / गवनु (went) / कीन्ह (did) / रघुनाथा (Raghunath) ॥ / गिरिबरु (great mountain) / दीख (saw) / जनकपति (King Janaka) / जबहीं (when) / करि (having done) / प्रनामु (bow) / रथ (chariot) / त्यागेउ (gave up) / तबहीं (then) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3329.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3329.essence: Respect becomes real when you leave comfort and bow.
ramacharitamanas::3329.simple_meaning: Ram leads the procession forward with his companions. Janaka sees the sacred mountain, bows, and immediately leaves his chariot to continue on foot.
ramacharitamanas::3329.simple_insight: True reverence shows itself in action, not posture.
ramacharitamanas::3329.detailed_meaning: On the road to the wedding, Ram moves ahead with his family, ministers, teacher, and townspeople. Janaka spots the holy mountain of Kamadnath, bows, and steps down from his chariot. The verse simply marks that respectful moment.
ramacharitamanas::3329.modern_relevance: You reach a temple, a memorial, or a place that matters deeply to your family, and your body changes before your mind does. You lower your voice, slow your pace, and step more carefully.
ramacharitamanas::3329.insight: It shows reverence through a concrete gesture of humility, not through speech.

ramacharitamanas::3330.verse_sanskrit: राम दरस लालसा उछाहू। पथ श्रम लेसु कलेसु न काहू॥ मन तहँ जहँ रघुबर बैदेही। बिनु मन तन दुख सुख सुधि केही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3330.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के दर्शन की लालसा और उत्साह के कारण किसी को रास्ते की थकावट और क्लेश जरा भी नहीं है। मन तो वहाँ है जहाँ श्री राम और जानकीजी हैं। बिना मन के शरीर के सुख-दुःख की सुध किसको हो? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3330.english_translation: The longing to see Ram and the joy of that hope erase all weariness and hardship. The mind is where Ram and Sita are. Without the mind there is no awareness of the body's pain or pleasure.
ramacharitamanas::3330.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / दरस (sight) / लालसा (longing) / उछाहू (joy) / पथ (path) / श्रम (fatigue) / लेसु (takes) / कलेसु (trouble) / न (not) / काहू (any) / मन (mind) / तहँ (there) / जहँ (where) / रघुबर (Ram) / बैदेही (Sita) / बिनु (without) / मन (mind) / तन (body) / दुख (pain) / सुख (pleasure) / सुधि (awareness) / केही (who)
ramacharitamanas::3330.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3330.essence: Love puts the body’s hardship in the background.
ramacharitamanas::3330.simple_meaning: When your heart is fixed on Ram and Sita, travel feels easy and bodily discomfort loses its grip.
ramacharitamanas::3330.simple_insight: Love can be stronger than fatigue; attention follows what you cherish most.
ramacharitamanas::3330.detailed_meaning: As Janak approaches with his people, the whole scene is charged with devotion and anticipation. The travellers are so absorbed in Ram's presence that the road no longer feels heavy. Their minds already rest with Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3330.modern_relevance: You’ve been on a delayed train for six hours, but your friend is waiting at the station after months apart. The discomfort is still there, yet it barely matters.
ramacharitamanas::3330.insight: It shifts attention from physical strain to the object of devotion, showing how meaning can outweigh discomfort.

ramacharitamanas::3331.verse_sanskrit: आवत जनकु चले एहि भाँती। सहित समाज प्रेम मति माती॥ आए निकट देखि अनुरागे। सादर मिलन परसपर लागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3331.verse_hindi: जनकजी इस प्रकार चले आ रहे हैं। समाज सहित उनकी बुद्धि प्रेम में मतवाली हो रही है। निकट आए देखकर सब प्रेम में भर गए और आदरपूर्वक आपस में मिलने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3331.english_translation: Janak was coming this way, with his whole retinue, his mind intoxicated by love. Seeing one another near, everyone was filled with affection, and they met each other with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3331.translation_literal: आवत (coming) / जनकु (Janak) / चले (walked) / एहि भाँती (in this manner) / सहित (with) / समाज (retinue, assembly) / प्रेम (love) / मति (mind, understanding) / माती (intoxicated) / आए (came) / निकट (near) / देखि (seeing) / अनुरागे (became affectionate) / सादर (respectfully) / मिलन (meeting) / परसपर (one another) / लागे (began to)
ramacharitamanas::3331.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3331.essence: Love makes strangers meet as family.
ramacharitamanas::3331.simple_meaning: Janak approaches with his whole group, and love fills everyone’s minds. When they come close, both sides greet each other with respect and affection.
ramacharitamanas::3331.simple_insight: Warmth softens distance before words ever do.
ramacharitamanas::3331.detailed_meaning: Janak is arriving with his retinue to meet Ram’s side. As the two groups draw near in Ayodhya’s charged atmosphere, pride disappears and affection rises first. The moment is about mutual honour, not politics.
ramacharitamanas::3331.modern_relevance: You spot an old friend across a crowded station platform, and the tension melts before either of you speaks. Respect and affection arrive first, and the meeting becomes easy.
ramacharitamanas::3331.insight: It shifts attention from formality to the human warmth that makes a meeting sacred.

ramacharitamanas::3332.verse_sanskrit: लगे जनक मुनिजन पद बंदन। रिषिन्ह प्रनामु कीन्ह रघुनंदन॥ भाइन्ह सहित रामु मिलि राजहि। चले लवाइ समेत समाजहि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3332.verse_hindi: जनकजी (वशिष्ठ आदि अयोध्यावासी) मुनियों के चरणों की वंदना करने लगे और श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने (शतानंद आदि जनकपुरवासी) ऋषियों को प्रणाम किया। फिर भाइयों समेत श्री रामजी राजा जनकजी से मिलकर उन्हें समाज सहित अपने आश्रम को लिवा चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::3332.english_translation: Janak bowed to the sages, and Raghunandan bowed to the sages in return. Then Ram, together with his brothers, met King Janak and led him, with his whole company, toward the hermitage.
ramacharitamanas::3332.translation_literal: लगे (began) / जनक (Janak) / मुनिजन (sage-people) / पद (feet) / बंदन (bowing) / रिषिन्ह (to the sages) / प्रनामु (salutation) / कीन्ह (did) / रघुनंदन (Raghunandan) / भाइन्ह (with brothers) / सहित (together) / रामु (Ram) / मिलि (meeting) / राजहि (to the king) / चले (went) / लवाइ (leading) / समेत (along with) / समाजहि (the company)
ramacharitamanas::3332.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3332.essence: Real honour begins when both sides bow first.
ramacharitamanas::3332.simple_meaning: Janak and Ram exchange respectful bows, then Ram leads Janak and his company toward the hermitage.
ramacharitamanas::3332.simple_insight: Respect softens distance. Even a king and an avatar meet as humble guests.
ramacharitamanas::3332.detailed_meaning: Janak has arrived with his retinue to meet Ram in the forest. The first response is not ceremony but mutual reverence: Janak bows to the sages, Ram bows back, and then Ram leads him and the gathered company toward the hermitage.
ramacharitamanas::3332.modern_relevance: You enter a room carrying status, but the first thing you do is lower your head and greet the elders properly. That simple respect changes the whole atmosphere before any conversation begins.
ramacharitamanas::3332.insight: It shows that true greatness expresses itself through humility, not rank.

ramacharitamanas::3333.verse_sanskrit: आश्रम सागर सांत रस पूरन पावन पाथु। सेन मनहुँ करुना सरित लिएँ जाहिं रघुनाथु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3333.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी का आश्रम शांत रस रूपी पवित्र जल से परिपूर्ण समुद्र है। जनकजी की सेना (समाज) मानो करुणा (करुण रस) की नदी है, जिसे श्री रघुनाथजी (उस आश्रम रूपी शांत रस के समुद्र में मिलाने के लिए) लिए जा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3333.english_translation: Ram's hermitage is a pure, calming ocean; Janak's company is like a river of compassion that Raghunath is carrying into it.
ramacharitamanas::3333.translation_literal: आश्रम (hermitage) / सागर (ocean) / सांत रस (calm essence) / पूरन (full) / पावन (pure) / पाथु (water) / सेन (company/army) / मनहुँ (as if) / करुना (compassion) / सरित (river) / लिएँ (carrying) / जाहिं (are going) / रघुनाथु (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::3333.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3333.essence: Compassion finds its rest in Ram's calm presence.
ramacharitamanas::3333.simple_meaning: Ram's hermitage is described as a calm, pure ocean, and Janak's whole company as a river of compassion being led there.
ramacharitamanas::3333.simple_insight: A sacred meeting can feel like two great currents merging without conflict.
ramacharitamanas::3333.detailed_meaning: Janak has arrived in Ayodhya with his people, and Ram is receiving them with deep honour. Tulsidas turns the scene into an image: Ram's hermitage is like a vast calm ocean, while Janak's retinue is a river of compassion moving toward it.
ramacharitamanas::3333.modern_relevance: You enter a room where two families, two teams, or two wounds are about to meet. The best host does not control the moment; he makes space for goodwill to flow in.
ramacharitamanas::3333.insight: It frames hospitality as a sacred merging of moods, not just a social formality.

ramacharitamanas::3334.verse_sanskrit: बोरति ग्यान बिराग करारे। बचन ससोक मिलत नद नारे॥ सोच उसास समीर तरंगा। धीरज तट तरुबर कर भंगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3334.verse_hindi: यह करुणा की नदी (इतनी बढ़ी हुई है कि) ज्ञान-वैराग्य रूपी किनारों को डुबाती जाती है। शोक भरे वचन नद और नाले हैं, जो इस नदी में मिलते हैं और सोच की लंबी साँसें (आहें) ही वायु के झकोरों से उठने वाली तरंगें हैं, जो धैर्य रूपी किनारे के उत्तम वृक्षों को तोड़ रही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3334.english_translation: The river of compassion floods the banks of wisdom and detachment. Sorrow-filled words are streams joining it, and sighs are wind-driven waves that break the great trees of patience.
ramacharitamanas::3334.translation_literal: बोरति (floods) / ग्यान (wisdom) / बिराग (detachment) / करारे (banks) / बचन (words) / ससोक (filled with sorrow) / मिलत (joining) / नद (river) / नारे (streams) / सोच (sighs) / उसास (long breaths) / समीर (wind) / तरंगा (waves) / धीरज (patience) / तट (bank) / तरुबर (great trees) / कर भंगा (breaking)
ramacharitamanas::3334.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3334.essence: Grief can flood even wisdom and patience.
ramacharitamanas::3334.simple_meaning: Grief here is so strong that it overwhelms wisdom, detachment, patience, and calm. Sorrow spreads like a river that sweeps everything else along with it.
ramacharitamanas::3334.simple_insight: Deep loss can drown even the clearest mind. Grief is not weakness; it is a force.
ramacharitamanas::3334.detailed_meaning: At Janakpur, Ram and the others are moving through a scene thick with emotion. Tulsidas does not describe the people directly; he turns their grief into a river, showing how sorrow, sighs, and confused speech overwhelm wisdom and patience.
ramacharitamanas::3334.modern_relevance: At a funeral, you try to stay composed, but every conversation breaks into tears and unfinished sentences. The mind knows what happened; the heart keeps flooding over it.
ramacharitamanas::3334.insight: It reframes grief as something that can temporarily overpower discernment, instead of a failure of character.

ramacharitamanas::3335.verse_sanskrit: बिषम बिषाद तोरावति धारा। भय भ्रम भवँर अबर्त अपारा॥ केवट बुध बिद्या बड़ि नावा। सकहिं न खेइ ऐक नहिं आवा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3335.verse_hindi: भयानक विषाद (शोक) ही उस नदी की तेज धारा है। भय और भ्रम (मोह) ही उसके असंख्य भँवर और चक्र हैं। विद्वान मल्लाह हैं, विद्या ही बड़ी नाव है, परन्तु वे उसे खे नहीं सकते हैं, (उस विद्या का उपयोग नहीं कर सकते हैं) किसी को उसकी अटकल ही नहीं आती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3335.english_translation: Fear and sorrow are the river’s fierce current. Fear and confusion are its countless whirlpools. Learned boatmen stand there, and knowledge is a great boat, but no one can row it; no one knows the way.
ramacharitamanas::3335.translation_literal: बिषम (fierce) / बिषाद (sorrow) / तोरावति (breaking, surging) / धारा (current) / भय (fear) / भ्रम (confusion) / भवँर (whirlpool) / अबर्त (eddies) / अपारा (countless, boundless) / केवट (boatman) / बुध (wise) / बिद्या (knowledge) / बड़ि (great) / नावा (boat) / सकहिं (are able) / न (not) / खेइ (to row) / ऐक (one) / नहिं (not) / आवा (came)
ramacharitamanas::3335.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3335.essence: Knowledge cannot carry you through a mind flooded by fear.
ramacharitamanas::3335.simple_meaning: Fear, sorrow, and confusion are like a raging river. Even knowledge is not enough to cross it if the mind cannot use that knowledge.
ramacharitamanas::3335.simple_insight: It is a relief to know that intelligence alone is not the whole answer; steadiness matters too.
ramacharitamanas::3335.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the grief around Ram’s exile is being pictured as a dangerous river. Sorrow is the current, fear and confusion are the whirlpools, and even learned people are like boatmen who cannot cross by knowledge alone.
ramacharitamanas::3335.modern_relevance: You have the plan, the notes, and the experience — then panic hits before the presentation and everything goes blank. Knowing is not the same as being able to act.
ramacharitamanas::3335.insight: It shifts the mind from trusting information alone to seeing the need for steadiness under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::3336.verse_sanskrit: बनचर कोल किरात बिचारे। थके बिलोकि पथिक हियँ हारे॥ आश्रम उदधि मिली जब जाई। मनहुँ उठेउ अंबुधि अकुलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3336.verse_hindi: वन में विचरने वाले बेचारे कोल-किरात ही यात्री हैं, जो उस नदी को देखकर हृदय में हारकर थक गए हैं। यह करुणा नदी जब आश्रम-समुद्र में जाकर मिली, तो मानो वह समुद्र अकुला उठा (खौल उठा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3336.english_translation: The forest-dwellers, the Kol and Kirat, are poor travellers who grow weary and lose heart just by seeing it. When this river of grief reaches the hermitage-sea, it seems the sea itself has risen in agitation.
ramacharitamanas::3336.translation_literal: बनचर (forest-dwellers) / कोल (Kol people) / किरात (Kirat people) / बिचारे (poor, helpless) / थके (weary) / बिलोकि (seeing) / पथिक (travellers) / हियँ (in heart) / हारे (defeated)॥ / आश्रम (hermitage) / उदधि (sea) / मिली (having met) / जब (when) / जाई (goes) / मनहुँ (as if) / उठेउ (rose) / अंबुधि (sea) / अकुलाई (in agitation)॥
ramacharitamanas::3336.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3336.essence: Grief can be so vast it unsettles every place it touches.
ramacharitamanas::3336.simple_meaning: The grief is so overwhelming that even rough forest people feel defeated by it. When it reaches the hermitage, it seems to shake the whole place.
ramacharitamanas::3336.simple_insight: Some sorrow is so heavy it seems to disturb everything around it.
ramacharitamanas::3336.detailed_meaning: The narration is still building the image of Dasharath's grief as a vast river. Even forest dwellers feel worn down by it, and when that sorrow reaches the hermitage, it swells like a restless sea. The verse deepens the emotional scale before the court's collapse is shown.
ramacharitamanas::3336.modern_relevance: You walk into a quiet room carrying bad news, and the whole atmosphere changes before you even speak. Grief has that kind of force.
ramacharitamanas::3336.insight: It turns private sorrow into a visible force that changes every space it enters.

ramacharitamanas::3337.verse_sanskrit: सोक बिकल दोउ राज समाजा। रहा न ग्यानु न धीरजु लाजा॥ भूप रूप गुन सील सराही। रोवहिं सोक सिंधु अवगाही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3337.verse_hindi: दोनों राज समाज शोक से व्याकुल हो गए। किसी को न ज्ञान रहा, न धीरज और न लाज ही रही। राजा दशरथजी के रूप, गुण और शील की सराहना करते हुए सब रो रहे हैं और शोक समुद्र में डुबकी लगा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3337.english_translation: The whole royal assembly was shaken by grief. No one had wisdom, patience, or even shame left. Praising King Dasharath's form, virtues, and noble conduct, they all wept and plunged into the ocean of sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::3337.translation_literal: सोक (grief) / बिकल (disturbed) / दोउ (both) / राज समाजा (royal assembly) / रहा (remained) / न (not) / ग्यानु (wisdom) / न (not) / धीरजु (patience) / लाजा (shame)॥ / भूप (king) / रूप (form) / गुन (qualities) / सील (noble conduct) / सराही (praising) / रोवहिं (they weep) / सोक (sorrow) / सिंधु (ocean) / अवगाही (plunging into)
ramacharitamanas::3337.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3337.essence: Grief can overwhelm even wisdom, patience, and dignity.
ramacharitamanas::3337.simple_meaning: The whole court is overwhelmed by grief after Dasharath's death. People forget wisdom, patience, and restraint, and only weep while remembering his virtues.
ramacharitamanas::3337.simple_insight: Loss can leave even the strongest room unable to think straight.
ramacharitamanas::3337.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath's death has struck Ayodhya like a blow. The royal assembly is no longer composed or orderly; everyone is drowning in grief, remembering the king's character and losing all steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::3337.modern_relevance: A family gathers after a funeral, and even the practical people cannot speak clearly. Grief wipes out composure, and all that remains is the ache of what was loved.
ramacharitamanas::3337.insight: It shows how deep loss breaks judgment, restraint, and social decorum at once.

ramacharitamanas::3338.verse_sanskrit: अवगाहि सोक समुद्र सोचहिं नारि नर ब्याकुल महा। दै दोष सकल सरोष बोलहिं बाम बिधि कीन्हो कहा॥ सुर सिद्ध तापस जोगिजन मुनि देखि दसा बिदेह की। तुलसी न समरथु कोउ जो तरि सकै सरित सनेह की॥
ramacharitamanas::3338.verse_hindi: शोक समुद्र में डुबकी लगाते हुए सभी स्त्री-पुरुष महान व्याकुल होकर सोच (चिंता) कर रहे हैं। वे सब विधाता को दोष देते हुए क्रोधयुक्त होकर कह रहे हैं कि प्रतिकूल विधाता ने यह क्या किया? तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि देवता, सिद्ध, तपस्वी, योगी और मुनिगणों में कोई भी समर्थ नहीं है, जो उस समय विदेह (जनकराज) की दशा देखकर प्रेम की नदी को पार कर सके (प्रेम में मग्न हुए बिना रह सके)।
ramacharitamanas::3338.english_translation: Diving into the ocean of grief, men and women alike are overwhelmed with sorrow. They blame fate in anger, asking, “What has this cruel order done?” Tulsidas says that even gods, perfected beings, ascetics, yogis, and sages could not cross the river of love when they saw Janaka’s condition.
ramacharitamanas::3338.translation_literal: अवगाहि (diving into) / सोक समुद्र (ocean of grief) / सोचहिं (they grieve; they worry) / नारि नर (women and men) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / महा (greatly) । दै (giving) / दोष (blame) / सकल (all) / सरोष (angrily) / बोलहिं (they speak) / बाम (adverse; cruel) / बिधि (fate; the cosmic order) / कीन्हो (did) / कहा (what) ॥ सुर (gods) / सिद्ध (perfected beings) / तापस (ascetics) / जोगिजन (yogis) / मुनि (sages) / देखि (seeing) / दसा (condition) / बिदेह की (of Janaka) । तुलसी (Tulsidas) / न (not) / समरथु (able) / कोउ (anyone) / जो (who) / तरि सकै (could cross) / सरित (river) / सनेह की (of love) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3338.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3338.essence: Love can overwhelm even the most disciplined mind.
ramacharitamanas::3338.simple_meaning: Everyone is overwhelmed by grief, and even the greatest sages cannot remain detached when they see Janaka’s suffering. Love itself becomes a river no one can easily cross.
ramacharitamanas::3338.simple_insight: Some sorrow is so human that even the most disciplined mind is moved by it.
ramacharitamanas::3338.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court is shattered by grief after Ram’s exile and the king’s collapse. People blame the order of the world and lose composure. Tulsidas then widens the scene: Janaka’s suffering is so moving that even sages and yogis would be swept into it.
ramacharitamanas::3338.modern_relevance: You sit beside a hospital bed and try to stay composed, but one look at a loved one’s face breaks your control. Some pain does not ask for analysis; it asks for presence.
ramacharitamanas::3338.insight: It shifts you from judging sorrow to recognizing how deeply love can undo restraint.

ramacharitamanas::3339.verse_sanskrit: किए अमित उपदेस जहँ तहँ लोगन्ह मुनिबरन्ह। धीरजु धरिअ नरेस कहेउ बसिष्ठ बिदेह सन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3339.verse_hindi: जहाँ-तहाँ श्रेष्ठ मुनियों ने लोगों को अपरिमित उपदेश दिए और वशिष्ठजी ने विदेह (जनकजी) से कहा- हे राजन् ! आप धैर्य धारण कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3339.english_translation: Wherever they were, the great sages gave countless teachings, and Vashishtha said to Janak: "O king, hold firm to patience."
ramacharitamanas::3339.translation_literal: किए (did/made) / अमित (countless) / उपदेस (teachings) / जहँ तहँ (here and there, everywhere) / लोगन्ह (to the people) / मुनिबरन्ह (to the great sages) / धीरजु (patience, steadiness) / धरिअ (hold/keep) / नरेस (O king) / कहेउ (said) / बसिष्ठ (Vashishtha) / बिदेह सन (to Janak of Videha)
ramacharitamanas::3339.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3339.essence: Patience is what keeps you upright when grief spreads.
ramacharitamanas::3339.simple_meaning: The sages gave many teachings, and Vashishtha told King Janak to stay patient and steady.
ramacharitamanas::3339.simple_insight: You do not have to be swept away by grief or pressure.
ramacharitamanas::3339.detailed_meaning: After Dasharath's death, the court is drowning in grief. Sages speak wherever they can, trying to steady the people. Vashishtha turns to Janak and gives the simplest support possible: hold patience.
ramacharitamanas::3339.modern_relevance: Your phone keeps buzzing while a family member is in the hospital, and everyone expects answers. In that moment, steadiness is its own form of care.
ramacharitamanas::3339.insight: It shifts you from emotional spillover to deliberate steadiness under strain.

ramacharitamanas::3340.verse_sanskrit: जासु ग्यान रबि भव निसि नासा। बचन किरन मुनि कमल बिकासा॥ तेहि कि मोह ममता निअराई। यह सिय राम सनेह बड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3340.verse_hindi: जिन राजा जनक का ज्ञान रूपी सूर्य भव (आवागमन) रूपी रात्रि का नाश कर देता है और जिनकी वचन रूपी किरणें मुनि रूपी कमलों को खिला देती हैं (आनंदित करती हैं), क्या मोह और ममता उनके निकट भी आ सकते हैं? यह तो श्री सीता-रामजी के प्रेम की महिमा है! (अर्थात राजा जनक की यह दशा श्री सीता-रामजी के अलौकिक प्रेम के कारण हुई, लौकिक मोह-ममता के कारण नहीं। जो लौकिक मोह-ममता को पार कर चुके हैं, उन पर भी श्री सीता-रामजी का प्रेम अपना प्रभाव दिखाए बिना नहीं रहता) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3340.english_translation: Janaka's knowledge is like the sun that destroys the night of becoming. His words are like rays that make the sages bloom like lotuses. Can delusion and possessiveness even come near him? This is the greatness of Sita and Ram's love.
ramacharitamanas::3340.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / ग्यान (knowledge) / रबि (sun) / भव (worldly becoming) / निसि (night) / नासा (destroyed) / बचन (words) / किरन (rays) / मुनि (sages) / कमल (lotuses) / बिकासा (bloomed) / तेहि (to him) / कि (can) / मोह (delusion) / ममता (possessiveness) / निअराई (near) / यह (this) / सिय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / सनेह (love) / बड़ाई (greatness)
ramacharitamanas::3340.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3340.essence: Love can make you too clear for clinging.
ramacharitamanas::3340.simple_meaning: True understanding burns away confusion and softens the heart. When love is that deep, ordinary attachment cannot stay close.
ramacharitamanas::3340.simple_insight: You can feel how real clarity makes possessiveness look small and powerless.
ramacharitamanas::3340.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court is grieving and searching for meaning after Ram's exile. Tulsidas turns to Janaka as an example of a mind purified by Sita and Ram's love: his understanding is so bright that delusion and possessiveness cannot touch him.
ramacharitamanas::3340.modern_relevance: You watch someone you love make a calm decision that surprises everyone at the family table. There is no panic in them, no grasping. That steadiness comes from seeing clearly enough to love without clinging.
ramacharitamanas::3340.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional possession to clear, spacious love.

ramacharitamanas::3341.verse_sanskrit: बिषई साधक सिद्ध सयाने। त्रिबिध जीव जग बेद बखाने॥ राम सनेह सरस मन जासू। साधु सभाँ बड़ आदर तासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3341.verse_hindi: विषयी, साधक और ज्ञानवान सिद्ध पुरुष- जगत में तीन प्रकार के जीव वेदों ने बताए हैं। इन तीनों में जिसका चित्त श्री रामजी के स्नेह से सरस (सराबोर) रहता है, साधुओं की सभा में उसी का बड़ा आदर होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3341.english_translation: The Vedas speak of three kinds of beings in the world: the worldly, the seekers, and the perfected wise. Among them, the one whose mind is soaked in love for Ram is honored most in the company of saints.
ramacharitamanas::3341.translation_literal: बिषई (worldly person) / साधक (seeker) / सिद्ध (perfected one) / सयाने (wise) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / जीव (beings) / जग (world) / बेद (the Vedas) / बखाने (describe)॥ / राम (Ram) / सनेह (love) / सरस (moist, filled) / मन (mind) / जासू (whose) / साधु (saints) / सभाँ (in the assembly) / बड़ (great) / आदर (honour) / तासू (to that one) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3341.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3341.essence: Ram-filled hearts outrank every other kind of greatness.
ramacharitamanas::3341.simple_meaning: The Vedas describe three kinds of people, but the one whose mind is filled with love for Ram is most respected among holy people.
ramacharitamanas::3341.simple_insight: Love for Ram quietly outranks status, learning, and achievement.
ramacharitamanas::3341.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the discussion has turned to what truly makes a person great. Tulsidas says the world may divide people into ordinary, striving, and perfected types, but saints honour most the one whose heart is softened and filled with love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3341.modern_relevance: You can have credentials, discipline, and sharp intelligence, yet still feel empty in the room. The person who moves others most is often the one whose heart is warm, not just impressive.
ramacharitamanas::3341.insight: It shifts value from outer attainment to inner devotion, showing that love for Ram is the highest mark of a human being.

ramacharitamanas::3342.verse_sanskrit: सोह न राम पेम बिनु ग्यानू। करनधार बिनु जिमि जलजानू॥ मुनि बहुबिधि बिदेहु समुझाए। राम घाट सब लोग नहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3342.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के प्रेम के बिना ज्ञान शोभा नहीं देता, जैसे कर्णधार के बिना जहाज। वशिष्ठजी ने विदेहराज (जनकजी) को बहुत प्रकार से समझाया। तदनंतर सब लोगों ने श्री रामजी के घाट पर स्नान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3342.english_translation: Knowledge without love for Ram has no beauty, just as a boat has no use without a helmsman. The sages explained this to King Janak in many ways, and then everyone bathed at Ram's ghat.
ramacharitamanas::3342.translation_literal: सोह (is fitting) / न (not) / राम (Ram) / पेम (love) / बिनु (without) / ग्यानू (knowledge) / करनधार (helmsman) / बिनु (without) / जिमि (like) / जलजानू (boat)॥ / मुनि (sages) / बहुबिधि (in many ways) / बिदेहु (to Janak) / समुझाए (explained) / राम (Ram) / घाट (ghat) / सब (all) / लोग (people) / नहाए (bathed) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3342.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3342.essence: Knowledge only becomes graceful when love gives it direction.
ramacharitamanas::3342.simple_meaning: Knowledge loses its beauty without love for Ram. The verse compares it to a boat that cannot move without someone steering it.
ramacharitamanas::3342.simple_insight: Understanding becomes living wisdom only when it is warmed by devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3342.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the sages are explaining why insight alone is not enough. They say even knowledge needs love for Ram, otherwise it is like a boat with no helmsman. After that teaching, everyone goes to bathe at Ram's ghat.
ramacharitamanas::3342.modern_relevance: You can read, analyse, and still feel strangely dry inside after a long day of learning. The mind has facts, but the heart has not been carried anywhere yet.
ramacharitamanas::3342.insight: It shifts you from treating knowledge as enough to seeing devotion as what gives knowledge direction.

ramacharitamanas::3343.verse_sanskrit: सकल सोक संकुल नर नारी। सो बासरु बीतेउ बिनु बारी॥ पसु खग मृगन्ह न कीन्ह अहारू। प्रिय परिजन कर कौन बिचारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3343.verse_hindi: स्त्री-पुरुष सब शोक से पूर्ण थे। वह दिन बिना ही जल के बीत गया (भोजन की बात तो दूर रही, किसी ने जल तक नहीं पिया)। पशु-पक्षी और हिरनों तक ने कुछ आहार नहीं किया। तब प्रियजनों एवं कुटुम्बियों का तो विचार ही क्या किया जाए? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3343.english_translation: All men and women were overwhelmed with grief. That day passed without even water, to say nothing of food. Even the animals, birds, and deer did not eat. What, then, of their dear relatives and family?
ramacharitamanas::3343.translation_literal: सकल (all) / सोक (grief) / संकुल (filled, crowded) / नर (men) / नारी (women) / सो (that) / बासरु (day) / बीतेउ (passed) / बिनु (without) / बारी (water) / पसु (animals) / खग (birds) / मृगन्ह (deer) / न (not) / कीन्ह (did) / अहारू (food) / प्रिय (dear) / परिजन (family members) / कर (of) / कौन (what) / बिचारू (thought, consideration)
ramacharitamanas::3343.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3343.essence: Shared grief can make an entire world forget hunger.
ramacharitamanas::3343.simple_meaning: Everyone is so grief-stricken that they cannot eat or even drink. The sorrow is so deep that even the animals around them stop feeding.
ramacharitamanas::3343.simple_insight: Grief can empty even the most basic human and animal instincts.
ramacharitamanas::3343.detailed_meaning: After the exile has torn through Ayodhya, the people sit in stunned sorrow. Men, women, and even the animals of the city lose their appetite and thirst. Tulsidas shows a whole world inwardly broken before the next morning's gathering.
ramacharitamanas::3343.modern_relevance: You get bad news at midnight and suddenly the kitchen feels useless, your phone stays untouched, and even your body forgets hunger. Grief can silence everything.
ramacharitamanas::3343.insight: It shifts attention from outward events to grief's physical weight in the body and community.

ramacharitamanas::3344.verse_sanskrit: दोउ समाज निमिराजु रघुराजु नहाने प्रात। बैठे सब बट बिटप तर मन मलीन कृस गात ॥
ramacharitamanas::3344.verse_hindi: निमिराज जनकजी और रघुराज रामचन्द्रजी तथा दोनों ओर के समाज ने दूसरे दिन सबेरे स्नान किया और सब बड़ के वृक्ष के नीचे जा बैठे। सबके मन उदास और शरीर दुबले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3344.english_translation: In the morning, both assemblies — King Nimi and Lord Ram — bathed. Then everyone sat beneath the banyan trees, with minds heavy and bodies thin.
ramacharitamanas::3344.translation_literal: दोउ (both) / समाज (assemblies) / निमिराजु (King Nimi) / रघुराजु (Lord Ram) / नहाने (bathed) / प्रात (in the morning) / बैठे (sat) / सब (all) / बट (banyan) / बिटप (trees) / तर (under) / मन (mind) / मलीन (soiled/heavy) / कृस (thin) / गात (bodies)
ramacharitamanas::3344.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3344.essence: Grief can remain even after the body is washed and the day begins.
ramacharitamanas::3344.simple_meaning: After bathing at dawn, everyone sat under the banyan trees, still weighed down by grief and exhaustion.
ramacharitamanas::3344.simple_insight: Even after a pause, sorrow can stay in the body and mind.
ramacharitamanas::3344.detailed_meaning: After the long night of grief in Mithila, both King Janak's side and Ram's side rise at dawn, bathe, and sit under the banyan trees. No one has recovered; the sadness still sits in their minds and bodies.
ramacharitamanas::3344.modern_relevance: After a sleepless night at the hospital, you finally wash your face and sit in the waiting room. Nothing is solved, but your body has not caught up with the loss yet.
ramacharitamanas::3344.insight: It shows grief as physical and communal, not just private feeling.

ramacharitamanas::3345.verse_sanskrit: जे महिसुर दसरथ पुर बासी। जे मिथिलापति नगर निवासी॥ हंस बंस गुर जनक पुरोधा। जिन्ह जग मगु परमारथु सोधा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3345.verse_hindi: जो दशरथजी की नगरी अयोध्या के रहने वाले और जो मिथिलापति जनकजी के नगर जनकपुर के रहने वाले ब्राह्मण थे तथा सूर्यवंश के गुरु वशिष्ठजी तथा जनकजी के पुरोहित शतानंदजी, जिन्होंने सांसारिक अभ्युदय का मार्ग तथा परमार्थ का मार्ग छान डाला था, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3345.english_translation: The brahmins of Dasharath's city and the residents of Janak's city, along with the teachers of the solar dynasty and Janak's family priest, who had thoroughly understood both worldly welfare and the higher path.
ramacharitamanas::3345.translation_literal: जे (the) / महिसुर (brahmins) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / पुर (city) / बासी (residents) / जे (the) / मिथिलापति (lord of Mithila) / नगर (city) / निवासी (residents) / हंस (swan-like) / बंस (lineage) / गुर (teachers) / जनक (Janak) / पुरोधा (family priest) / जिन्ह (who) / जग (worldly) / मगु (path) / परमारथु (higher good) / सोधा (thoroughly examined)
ramacharitamanas::3345.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3345.essence: The crisis calls for people who know both practical life and the higher good.
ramacharitamanas::3345.simple_meaning: The learned people from Ayodhya and Mithila are gathered here, including royal teachers and priests who understand both worldly affairs and the higher good.
ramacharitamanas::3345.simple_insight: Wisdom is not isolated from life; the people who understand both worlds can guide a crisis best.
ramacharitamanas::3345.detailed_meaning: After the grief of exile has settled over both courts, the respected brahmins, teachers, and priests from Ayodhya and Mithila are named as present. This is the learned assembly that will now speak, because the moment needs both practical judgment and moral clarity.
ramacharitamanas::3345.modern_relevance: In a tense family meeting after a major loss, the people everyone trusts most are the ones who can hold both practical reality and deeper values without panic.
ramacharitamanas::3345.insight: It shifts attention from status to discernment: the right voices in a crisis are those who can see both immediate duty and lasting good.

ramacharitamanas::3346.verse_sanskrit: लगे कहन उपदेस अनेका। सहित धरम नय बिरति बिबेका॥ कौसिक कहि कहि कथा पुरानीं। समुझाई सब सभा सुबानीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3346.verse_hindi: वे सब धर्म, नीति वैराग्य तथा विवेकयुक्त अनेकों उपदेश देने लगे। विश्वामित्रजी ने पुरानी कथाएँ (इतिहास) कह-कहकर सारी सभा को सुंदर वाणी से समझाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3346.english_translation: They began giving many teachings on dharma, policy, renunciation, and clear seeing. Kaushik kept telling old stories and, with graceful words, explained everything to the whole assembly.
ramacharitamanas::3346.translation_literal: लगे (began) / कहन (to speak) / उपदेस (teachings) / अनेका (many) / सहित (along with) / धरम (dharma) / नय (policy) / बिरति (renunciation) / बिबेका (clear seeing)॥ / कौसिक (Kaushik) / कहि कहि (speaking again and again) / कथा (stories) / पुरानीं (old) / समुझाई (explained) / सब (all) / सभा (assembly) / सुबानीं (with graceful words)॥
ramacharitamanas::3346.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3346.essence: Guidance becomes easier to receive when it comes through stories and gentle speech.
ramacharitamanas::3346.simple_meaning: The gathered people begin sharing many teachings and old stories, using kind words to help the whole assembly understand.
ramacharitamanas::3346.simple_insight: Wise guidance often arrives through stories, not lectures.
ramacharitamanas::3346.detailed_meaning: At the riverbank gathering after the day’s events, the assembled elders and sages start explaining dharma, restraint, and clear seeing. Kaushik, speaking gently, uses old stories to steady the whole crowd before the next turn in the journey.
ramacharitamanas::3346.modern_relevance: At a family gathering after a funeral, one elder starts telling old stories to calm the room. The wisdom lands because it is spoken with care, not force.
ramacharitamanas::3346.insight: It shifts understanding from argument to patient, story-shaped guidance.

ramacharitamanas::3347.verse_sanskrit: तब रघुनाथ कौसिकहि कहेऊ। नाथ कालि जल बिनु सुब रहेऊ॥ मुनि कह उचित कहत रघुराई। गयउ बीति दिन पहर अढ़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3347.verse_hindi: तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने विश्वामित्रजी से कहा कि हे नाथ! कल सब लोग बिना जल पिए ही रह गए थे। (अब कुछ आहार करना चाहिए)। विश्वामित्रजी ने कहा कि श्री रघुनाथजी उचित ही कह रहे हैं। ढाई पहर दिन (आज भी) बीत गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3347.english_translation: Then Raghunath said to Kaushik, "Lord, yesterday everyone stayed without water." The sage replied, "Raghuraj speaks rightly; two and a half watches of the day have already passed."
ramacharitamanas::3347.translation_literal: तब (then) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / कौसिकहि (to Kaushik) / कहेऊ (said) / नाथ (Lord) / कालि (yesterday) / जल (water) / बिनु (without) / सुब (all) / रहेऊ (remained) ॥ / मुनि (sage) / कह (said) / उचित (properly) / कहत (speaking) / रघुराई (Raghuraj) / गयउ (has gone) / बीति (passed) / दिन (day) / पहर (watch) / अढ़ाई (two and a half) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3347.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3347.essence: Even sacred discipline must respect the body's limits.
ramacharitamanas::3347.simple_meaning: Ram gently reminds the sage that everyone went without water the previous day, and the sage agrees that it is now time to eat.
ramacharitamanas::3347.simple_insight: Even holy discipline must make room for the body's needs.
ramacharitamanas::3347.detailed_meaning: After a long day of teaching and listening, Ram speaks to Vishwamitra with practical care: the group has gone without water since yesterday, and the day is already far along. The verse keeps the scene moving toward hospitality and proper timing.
ramacharitamanas::3347.modern_relevance: You’ve been powering through meetings, fasting on coffee, and calling it focus. At some point, wisdom sounds like noticing the body and saying: eat, drink, continue.
ramacharitamanas::3347.insight: It shifts attention from heroic endurance to wise, humane timing.

ramacharitamanas::3348.verse_sanskrit: रिषि रुख लखि कह तेरहुतिराजू। इहाँ उचित नहिं असन अनाजू॥ कहा भूप भल सबहि सोहाना। पाइ रजायसु चले नहाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3348.verse_hindi: विश्वामित्रजी का रुख देखकर तिरहुत राज जनकजी ने कहा- यहाँ अन्न खाना उचित नहीं है। राजा का सुंदर कथन सबके मन को अच्छा लगा। सब आज्ञा पाकर नहाने चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::3348.english_translation: Seeing the sage's mood, King Janaka of Tirhut said, 'It is not proper to eat grain here.' His gracious words pleased everyone, and all received permission and went to bathe.
ramacharitamanas::3348.translation_literal: रिषि (sage) / रुख (mood, disposition) / लखि (seeing) / कह (said) / तेरहुतिराजू (king of Tirhut) / इहाँ (here) / उचित (proper) / नहिं (not) / असन (food) / अनाजू (grain) ॥ / कहा (said) / भूप (king) / भल (good, gracious) / सबहि (to everyone) / सोहाना (pleasing) / पाइ (having received) / रजायसु (permission) / चले (went) / नहाना (to bathe) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3348.speaker: Janaka
ramacharitamanas::3348.essence: Respect for the moment matters more than insisting on your own comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3348.simple_meaning: Janaka notices the sage's mood and chooses not to eat grain there. His respectful response pleases everyone, and the group goes to bathe instead.
ramacharitamanas::3348.simple_insight: Courtesy means reading the room and choosing what keeps harmony intact.
ramacharitamanas::3348.detailed_meaning: At Vishvamitra's gathering in Ayodhya, Janaka sees that the sage does not want a meal of grain offered there. He responds with tact and humility, and the whole assembly follows his lead by going to bathe first.
ramacharitamanas::3348.modern_relevance: You can feel a dinner invitation turning awkward, then save it with one respectful sentence. Janaka shows how quickly dignity returns when you notice what the moment asks for.
ramacharitamanas::3348.insight: It teaches you to adapt your conduct to the setting without forcing your own preference.

ramacharitamanas::3349.verse_sanskrit: तेहि अवसर फल फूल दल मूल अनेक प्रकार। लइ आए बनचर बिपुल भरि भरि काँवरि भार ॥
ramacharitamanas::3349.verse_hindi: उसी समय अनेकों प्रकार के बहुत से फल, फूल, पत्ते, मूल आदि बहँगियों और बोझों में भर-भरकर वनवासी (कोल-किरात) लोग ले आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3349.english_translation: At that moment, many forest dwellers brought an abundance of fruits, flowers, leaves, roots, and many other kinds of food, filling baskets and loads again and again.
ramacharitamanas::3349.translation_literal: तेहि अवसर (at that moment) / फल (fruits) / फूल (flowers) / दल (leaves) / मूल (roots) / अनेक प्रकार (many kinds) / लइ आए (brought) / बनचर (forest dwellers) / बिपुल (abundant) / भरि भरि (again and again, full) / काँवरि (baskets/shoulder-baskets) / भार (loads)
ramacharitamanas::3349.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3349.essence: Hospitality becomes abundance when people give freely.
ramacharitamanas::3349.simple_meaning: The forest people arrived with a great variety of food gathered from the forest and carried it in heavy loads.
ramacharitamanas::3349.simple_insight: Small offerings, freely given, can become a whole feast of welcome.
ramacharitamanas::3349.detailed_meaning: After Ram and Lakshman reach the forest, the local forest dwellers come forward with gifts. They bring fruits, flowers, leaves, and roots in heavy loads, showing instant hospitality before the scene shifts to Ram's grace filling the land.
ramacharitamanas::3349.modern_relevance: You show up empty-handed to help set up a meal, and someone quietly brings three bags of food before you can ask. The kindness matters more than the quantity.
ramacharitamanas::3349.insight: It shifts attention from possession to offering, showing how welcome is created by generosity.

ramacharitamanas::3350.verse_sanskrit: कामद भे गिरि राम प्रसादा। अवलोकत अपहरत बिषादा॥ सर सरिता बन भूमि बिभागा। जनु उमगत आनँद अनुरागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3350.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की कृपा से सब पर्वत मनचाही वस्तु देने वाले हो गए। वे देखने मात्र से ही दुःखों को सर्वथा हर लेते थे। वहाँ के तालाबों, नदियों, वन और पृथ्वी के सभी भागों में मानो आनंद और प्रेम उमड़ रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3350.english_translation: By Ram's grace, the mountains became wish-fulfilling. Just seeing them removed sorrow. The ponds, rivers, forests, and lands all seemed to overflow with joy and love.
ramacharitamanas::3350.translation_literal: कामद (wish-fulfilling) / भे (became) / गिरि (mountains) / राम (Ram) / प्रसादा (by grace) । अवलोकत (seeing) / अपहरत (removing) / बिषादा (sorrow) ॥ सर (ponds) / सरिता (rivers) / बन (forest) / भूमि (earth) / बिभागा (regions) । जनु (as if) / उमगत (rising) / आनँद (joy) / अनुरागा (love) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3350.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3350.essence: Ram's presence turns even ordinary nature into relief and delight.
ramacharitamanas::3350.simple_meaning: Ram's grace makes even the landscape feel alive and comforting. Just being there lifts sorrow and fills everything with joy.
ramacharitamanas::3350.simple_insight: Grace can change not just your mood, but the whole atmosphere around you.
ramacharitamanas::3350.detailed_meaning: As Janak's people welcome Vishwamitra and the party reaches the forest, the setting itself begins to feel transformed. Tulsidas lingers on Ram's presence: mountains, waters, trees, and earth seem touched by joy, as if the land itself recognizes him.
ramacharitamanas::3350.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a hard week, and someone calm and kind is already there. Nothing has changed on paper, but the tension drops and everyone breathes easier.
ramacharitamanas::3350.insight: It shifts attention from outer scenery to the healing effect of a noble presence.

ramacharitamanas::3351.verse_sanskrit: बेलि बिटप सब सफल सफूला। बोलत खग मृग अलि अनुकूला॥ तेहि अवसर बन अधिक उछाहू। त्रिबिध समीर सुखद सब काहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3351.verse_hindi: बेलें और वृक्ष सभी फल और फूलों से युक्त हो गए। पक्षी, पशु और भौंरें अनुकूल बोलने लगे। उस अवसर पर वन में बहुत उत्साह (आनंद) था, सब किसी को सुख देने वाली शीतल, मंद, सुगंध हवा चल रही थी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3351.english_translation: All the vines and trees were full of fruit and flowers. Birds, animals, and bees spoke in gentle accord. At that time the forest was filled with joy, and a cool, mild breeze that gave comfort to everyone blew there.
ramacharitamanas::3351.translation_literal: बेलि (vines) / बिटप (trees) / सब (all) / सफल (fruitful) / सफूला (flowering) / बोलत (speaking) / खग (birds) / मृग (deer/animals) / अलि (bees) / अनुकूला (in gentle accord) / तेहि अवसर (at that time) / बन (forest) / अधिक (great) / उछाहू (joy/excitement) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / समीर (wind/breeze) / सुखद (pleasant) / सब (to all) / काहू (everyone)
ramacharitamanas::3351.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3351.essence: A noble presence makes even the forest feel joyful.
ramacharitamanas::3351.simple_meaning: The forest itself seems to celebrate Ram's arrival: plants bloom, creatures respond gently, and even the breeze feels soothing.
ramacharitamanas::3351.simple_insight: When your presence is right, the whole atmosphere softens around you.
ramacharitamanas::3351.detailed_meaning: As Ram enters the forest in exile, nature responds as if blessing him. Trees are heavy with fruit, flowers open, birds and animals are calm, and the air itself feels kind. This verse paints the forest's welcome before the next scene of reverent arrival.
ramacharitamanas::3351.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a tense argument, and even the silence feels different. Nothing has been said yet, but the atmosphere already knows whether you bring ease or strain.
ramacharitamanas::3351.insight: It shifts attention from what a place looks like to the feeling your presence creates there.

ramacharitamanas::3352.verse_sanskrit: जाइ न बरनि मनोहरताई। जनु महि करति जनक पहुनाई॥ तब सब लोग नहाइ नहाई। राम जनक मुनि आयसु पाई ॥ देखि देखि तरुबर अनुरागे। जहँ तहँ पुरजन उतरन लागे॥ दल फल मूल कंद बिधि नाना। पावन सुंदर सुधा समाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3352.verse_hindi: वन की मनोहरता वर्णन नहीं की जा सकती, मानो पृथ्वी जनकजी की पहुनाई कर रही है। तब जनकपुर वासी सब लोग नहा-नहाकर श्री रामचन्द्रजी, जनकजी और मुनि की आज्ञा पाकर, सुंदर वृक्षों को देख-देखकर प्रेम में भरकर जहाँ-तहाँ उतरने लगे। पवित्र, सुंदर और अमृत के समान (स्वादिष्ट) अनेकों प्रकार के पत्ते, फल, मूल और कंद-॥3-4॥
ramacharitamanas::3352.english_translation: The forest's beauty cannot be described, as if the earth itself were hosting Janak's people. Then everyone bathed, and after receiving the orders of Ram, Janak, and the sage, the people of Janakpur, moved by love at the sight of the beautiful trees, came down wherever they could. There were many kinds of holy, beautiful leaves, fruits, roots, and tubers, sweet like nectar.
ramacharitamanas::3352.translation_literal: जाइ न (cannot be described) / बरनि (to describe) / मनोहरताई (beauty) / जनु (as if) / महि (the earth) / करति (is doing) / जनक पहुनाई (Janak's hosting) / तब (then) / सब लोग (all people) / नहाइ नहाई (bathed again and again) / राम (Ram) / जनक (Janak) / मुनि (sage) / आयसु (command) / पाई (having received) / देखि देखि (seeing again and again) / तरुबर (beautiful trees) / अनुरागे (became प्रेम-भरे) / जहँ तहँ (here and there) / पुरजन (townspeople) / उतरन (to get down) / लागे (began) / दल (leaves) / फल (fruits) / मूल (roots) / कंद (tubers) / बिधि नाना (many kinds) / पावन (holy) / सुंदर (beautiful) / सुधा समाना (like nectar)
ramacharitamanas::3352.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3352.essence: The world can feel like an offering when you arrive with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3352.simple_meaning: The forest feels so beautiful that it seems like the earth is welcoming Janak's people as guests. Everyone bathes, admires the trees, and comes down to enjoy the holy fruits, roots, and tubers there.
ramacharitamanas::3352.simple_insight: Beauty can soften a crowd into gratitude, making even simple food feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3352.detailed_meaning: On the journey through the forest in Ayodhyakand, Janakpur's people are overwhelmed by the scene before them. The trees, fruits, and roots feel so welcoming that the land itself seems to be hosting them, and they stop to rest, bathe, and eat with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3352.modern_relevance: You step off a long bus ride into a hillside orchard, tired and dusty, and the place feels like it has made room for you. Hunger turns into gratitude before the first bite.
ramacharitamanas::3352.insight: It shifts attention from scarcity to welcome, so ordinary nourishment feels received rather than taken.

ramacharitamanas::3353.verse_sanskrit: सादर सब कहँ रामगुर पठए भरि भरि भार। पूजि पितर सुर अतिथि गुर लगे करन फरहार ॥
