ramacharitamanas::3353.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के गुरु वशिष्ठजी ने सबके पास बोझे भर-भरकर आदरपूर्वक भेजे। तब वे पितर-देवता, अतिथि और गुरु की पूजा करके फलाहार करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3353.english_translation: Vashishtha, Ram's guru, respectfully sent gifts to everyone in loads. Then, after honoring the ancestors, the radiant beings, guests, and the teacher, they began eating fruit.
ramacharitamanas::3353.translation_literal: सादर (respectfully) / सब कहँ (to everyone) / रामगुर (Ram's teacher) / पठए (sent) / भरि भरि (full of, in loads) / भार (loads) / पूजि (having honored) / पितर (ancestors) / सुर (radiant beings) / अतिथि (guests) / गुर (teacher) / लगे (began) / करन (to do) / फरहार (fruit meal)
ramacharitamanas::3353.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3353.essence: Honor what sustains you before you take for yourself.
ramacharitamanas::3353.simple_meaning: Ram's teacher sends gifts for everyone, and the people first honor ancestors, radiant beings, guests, and the teacher before eating fruit.
ramacharitamanas::3353.simple_insight: Respect comes before enjoyment, and gratitude gives even a simple meal its dignity.
ramacharitamanas::3353.detailed_meaning: After the joyful welcome in the forest, Vashishtha, Ram's teacher, sends generous offerings to everyone. The people respond with proper reverence, honoring ancestors, radiant beings, guests, and the teacher before taking fruit as their meal.
ramacharitamanas::3353.modern_relevance: You open a packed lunch after helping set up a family gathering, but first you make sure the elders are served and the guest is welcomed. The meal feels fuller because respect came first.
ramacharitamanas::3353.insight: It teaches you to place gratitude and reverence before personal comfort.

ramacharitamanas::3354.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि बासर बीते चारी। रामु निरखि नर नारि सुखारी॥ दुहु समाज असि रुचि मन माहीं। बिनु सिय राम फिरब भल नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3354.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार चार दिन बीत गए। श्री रामचन्द्रजी को देखकर सभी नर-नारी सुखी हैं। दोनों समाजों के मन में ऐसी इच्छा है कि श्री सीता-रामजी के बिना लौटना अच्छा नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3354.english_translation: In this way, four days passed. Everyone, men and women alike, felt joy just seeing Ram. Both groups shared the same wish in their hearts: returning without Sita and Ram would not be good.
ramacharitamanas::3354.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / बासर (days) / बीते (passed) / चारी (four) / रामु (Ram) / निरखि (seeing) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / सुखारी (made happy) / दुहु (both) / समाज (groups) / असि (such) / रुचि (wish) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / बिनु (without) / सिय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / फिरब (to return) / भल (good) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::3354.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3354.essence: Being near Ram makes separation feel wrong.
ramacharitamanas::3354.simple_meaning: Four days pass in joyful company. Everyone feels happy just seeing Ram, and both groups agree that leaving without Sita and Ram would be wrong.
ramacharitamanas::3354.simple_insight: Some presences make leaving feel impossible.
ramacharitamanas::3354.detailed_meaning: In Janakpur, Ram has spent four days among people who cannot stop looking at him. Men and women alike feel their hearts pulled toward him. The scene builds toward one shared feeling: no one wants this meeting to end with separation.
ramacharitamanas::3354.modern_relevance: You visit someone’s home, and by the fourth evening nobody wants the gathering to end. The warmth in the room makes departure feel like loss.
ramacharitamanas::3354.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the bond it creates.

ramacharitamanas::3355.verse_sanskrit: सीता राम संग बनबासू। कोटि अमरपुर सरिस सुपासू॥ परिहरि लखन रामु बैदेही। जेहि घरु भाव बाम बिधि तेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3355.verse_hindi: श्री सीता-रामजी के साथ वन में रहना करोड़ों देवलोकों के (निवास के) समान सुखदायक है। श्री लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामजी और श्री जानकीजी को छोड़कर जिसको घर अच्छा लगे, विधाता उसके विपरीत हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3355.english_translation: Living in the forest with Sita and Ram is as delightful as millions of heavenly realms. Whoever prefers home after leaving Lakshman, Ram, and Vaidehi, fate has turned against them.
ramacharitamanas::3355.translation_literal: सीता राम संग (with Sita and Ram) / बनबासू (forest dwelling) / कोटि (millions) / अमरपुर (heavenly realms) / सरिस (like) / सुपासू (very pleasant) / परिहरि (leaving aside) / लखन (Lakshman) / रामु (Ram) / बैदेही (Vaidehi, Sita) / जेहि (to whom) / घरु (home) / भाव (feels pleasing) / बाम (crooked, adverse) / बिधि (fate) / तेही (for that one)
ramacharitamanas::3355.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3355.essence: Ram's company makes exile sweeter than comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3355.simple_meaning: Being with Ram, Sita, and Lakshman makes forest exile feel better than the finest heavenly worlds. If someone still prefers ordinary comfort after losing that company, something is deeply wrong.
ramacharitamanas::3355.simple_insight: What you value reveals your inner direction more than your surroundings do.
ramacharitamanas::3355.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the family and citizens are feeling the ache of Ram's exile. Tulsidas turns that pain into a startling claim: being with Ram, Sita, and Lakshman in the forest is richer than any palace. The real loss is not the home left behind.
ramacharitamanas::3355.modern_relevance: You move into a smaller apartment, lose the job title, and suddenly the room feels empty. But if the right people are with you, even a stripped-down life can feel fuller than comfort ever did.
ramacharitamanas::3355.insight: It shifts attention from external comfort to the quality of presence you are living with.

ramacharitamanas::3356.verse_sanskrit: दाहिन दइउ होइ जब सबही। राम समीप बसिअ बन तबही॥ मंदाकिनि मज्जनु तिहु काला। राम दरसु मुद मंगल माला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3356.verse_hindi: जब दैव सबके अनुकूल हो, तभी श्री रामजी के पास वन में निवास हो सकता है। मंदाकिनीजी का तीनों समय स्नान और आनंद तथा मंगलों की माला (समूह) रूप श्री राम का दर्शन, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3356.english_translation: Only when fortune turns favorable can you live in the forest near Ram. Bathing in the Mandakini three times a day and seeing Ram brings a garland of joy and auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::3356.translation_literal: दाहिन (favorable) / दइउ (fortune) / होइ (becomes) / जब (when) / सबही (for everyone) / राम (Ram) / समीप (near) / बसिअ (to live) / बन (forest) / तबही (then only) ॥ मंदाकिनि (Mandakini) / मज्जनु (bathing) / तिहु काला (three times a day) / राम (Ram) / दरसु (darshan, sight) / मुद (joy) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / माला (garland) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3356.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3356.essence: Ram's presence turns even exile into a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3356.simple_meaning: Living near Ram in the forest is a rare blessing. Even bathing in the river and seeing him fill life with joy and auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::3356.simple_insight: Some places change you because of who is there, not because of what they offer.
ramacharitamanas::3356.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the forest exile is being imagined as a blessing rather than a loss. The speaker says that only when circumstances are fully favorable can one live near Ram, bathe in the Mandakini, and feel every sight of him as joy.
ramacharitamanas::3356.modern_relevance: You visit a place only because someone you love is there, and suddenly the long drive, the small room, the simple meal all feel worth it. Presence changes the value of everything around it.
ramacharitamanas::3356.insight: It shifts attention from the forest itself to the transforming power of Ram's presence.

ramacharitamanas::3357.verse_sanskrit: अटनु राम गिरि बन तापस थल। असनु अमिअ सम कंद मूल फल॥ सुख समेत संबत दुइ साता। पल सम होहिं न जनिअहिं जाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3357.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी के पर्वत (कामदनाथ), वन और तपस्वियों के स्थानों में घूमना और अमृत के समान कंद, मूल, फलों का भोजन। चौदह वर्ष सुख के साथ पल के समान हो जाएँगे (बीत जाएँगे), जाते हुए जान ही न पड़ेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3357.english_translation: Roaming through Ram's mountains, forests, and places of tapas is a joy. Roots, bulbs, and fruits taste like nectar. The fourteen years will pass in happiness like a moment, and you will not even notice them going by.
ramacharitamanas::3357.translation_literal: अटनु (roaming) / राम (Ram's) / गिरि (mountains) / बन (forests) / तापस थल (places of tapas) / असनु (food) / अमिअ सम (like nectar) / कंद मूल फल (roots, bulbs, fruits) / सुख समेत (with happiness) / संबत दुइ साता (the fourteen years) / पल सम (like a moment) / होहिं (will become) / न जनिअहिं (will not be noticed) / जाता (going)
ramacharitamanas::3357.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3357.essence: Ram's presence makes even exile feel like a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3357.simple_meaning: Life in the forest with Ram feels so sweet that fourteen years will pass without feeling long.
ramacharitamanas::3357.simple_insight: Presence changes everything; what hurts alone can feel light beside the one you love.
ramacharitamanas::3357.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the exile is no longer just a punishment. The speaker imagines Ram, Sita, and Lakshman living among mountains, forests, and hermitages, eating simple forest food. Even fourteen years would feel like a brief, happy visit.
ramacharitamanas::3357.modern_relevance: You move to a new city for work and expect loneliness, but a single trusted friend turns the whole place bearable. The outer situation stays hard; companionship changes the experience.
ramacharitamanas::3357.insight: It shifts attention from the hardship itself to the company that transforms hardship.

ramacharitamanas::3358.verse_sanskrit: एहि सुख जोग न लोग सब कहहिं कहाँ अस भागु। सहज सुभायँ समाज दुहु राम चरन अनुरागु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3358.verse_hindi: सब लोग कह रहे हैं कि हम इस सुख के योग्य नहीं हैं, हमारे ऐसे भाग्य कहाँ? दोनों समाजों का श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणों में सहज स्वभाव से ही प्रेम है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3358.english_translation: Everyone says, “Who are we to deserve this joy? Where is such fortune?” Both groups naturally feel love for Ram’s feet.
ramacharitamanas::3358.translation_literal: एहि (this) / सुख (joy) / जोग (worthy) / न (not) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / कहहिं (say) / कहाँ (where) / अस (such) / भागु (fortune) / सहज (natural) / सुभायँ (by nature) / समाज (assemblies) / दुहु (both) / राम (Ram) / चरन (feet) / अनुरागु (love)
ramacharitamanas::3358.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3358.essence: True devotion feels natural, not earned.
ramacharitamanas::3358.simple_meaning: The people feel unworthy of such joy, yet love for Ram arises in them naturally. Devotion is not forced here; it flows on its own.
ramacharitamanas::3358.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that real devotion does not have to be manufactured.
ramacharitamanas::3358.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the gathered people and companions are overwhelmed by the grace of being near Ram during exile. They keep saying they are unworthy of this joy, yet their love for Ram’s feet comes effortlessly.
ramacharitamanas::3358.modern_relevance: You stand quietly outside a hospital room after someone you love finally wakes up. You don’t feel deserving of the relief, only grateful that love arrived on its own.
ramacharitamanas::3358.insight: It shifts devotion from effortful performance to a spontaneous response of the heart.

ramacharitamanas::3359.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि सकल मनोरथ करहीं। बचन सप्रेम सुनत मन हरहीं॥ सीय मातु तेहि समय पठाईं। दासीं देखि सुअवसरु आईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3359.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार सब मनोरथ कर रहे हैं। उनके प्रेमयुक्त वचन सुनते ही (सुनने वालों के) मनों को हर लेते हैं। उसी समय सीताजी की माता श्री सुनयनाजी की भेजी हुई दासियाँ (कौसल्याजी आदि के मिलने का) सुंदर अवसर देखकर आईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3359.english_translation: In this way they all kept making their wishes come true. Hearing those loving words, it stole the heart. Then, at that very time, the maidservants sent by Sita's mother came, seeing the right moment.
ramacharitamanas::3359.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / सकल (all) / मनोरथ (wishes, desires) / करहीं (were doing) / बचन (words) / सप्रेम (with love) / सुनत (hearing) / मन (mind) / हरहीं (were stealing) / सीय मातु (Sita's mother) / तेहि समय (at that time) / पठाईं (sent) / दासीं (maidservants) / देखि (seeing) / सुअवसरु (good opportunity) / आईं (came)
ramacharitamanas::3359.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3359.essence: Love prepares the moment before the meeting arrives.
ramacharitamanas::3359.simple_meaning: Everyone is happily making plans and speaking lovingly. Their words are so sweet that they win hearts. At that moment, the maidservants sent by Sita's mother arrive at just the right time.
ramacharitamanas::3359.simple_insight: Kind words can open a door that effort alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::3359.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the royal women are eager to meet after a long separation. The atmosphere is full of affectionate planning and shared longing. Just then, the maidservants sent by Sita's mother arrive, turning a private wish into an actual meeting.
ramacharitamanas::3359.modern_relevance: You are mid-conversation in a family group chat when the exact person everyone wanted to see finally calls. Warm words had already prepared the moment.
ramacharitamanas::3359.insight: It shows how affection creates the right opening and draws people together at the right time.

ramacharitamanas::3360.verse_sanskrit: सावकास सुनि सब सिय सासू। आयउ जनकराज रनिवासू॥ कौसल्याँ सादर सनमानी। आसन दिए समय सम आनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3360.verse_hindi: उनसे यह सुनकर कि सीता की सब सासुएँ इस समय फुरसत में हैं, जनकराज का रनिवास उनसे मिलने आया। कौसल्याजी ने आदरपूर्वक उनका सम्मान किया और समयोचित आसन लाकर दिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3360.english_translation: Hearing that all of Sita's mothers-in-law were free at that time, the royal household of Janaka came to meet them. Kaushalya received them respectfully and brought seats at the proper time.
ramacharitamanas::3360.translation_literal: सावकास (at leisure/free) / सुनि (hearing) / सब (all) / सिय (of Sita) / सासू (mothers-in-law) / आयउ (came) / जनकराज (King Janaka's) / रनिवासू (royal household) / कौसल्याँ (Kaushalya) / सादर (respectfully) / सनमानी (honoured) / आसन (seats) / दिए (gave) / समय सम (according to the occasion) / आनी (bringing)
ramacharitamanas::3360.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3360.essence: Care becomes visible in the way you welcome people.
ramacharitamanas::3360.simple_meaning: Janaka's household comes to visit when the women are free, and Kaushalya welcomes them with honor and proper seating.
ramacharitamanas::3360.simple_insight: Respect is shown in small, timely gestures, not grand speeches.
ramacharitamanas::3360.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the families are drawn together by love and relief, Janaka's household arrives to meet Kaushalya and the others. Kaushalya responds with formal warmth, showing the etiquette and tenderness that hold the gathering together.
ramacharitamanas::3360.modern_relevance: Your in-laws arrive after a long drive, and you notice who offers water, who pulls out a chair, who makes everyone feel expected. That quiet care changes the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::3360.insight: It teaches you that dignity is communicated through timely hospitality and attentive manners.

ramacharitamanas::3361.verse_sanskrit: सीलु सनेहु सकल दुहु ओरा। द्रवहिं देखि सुनि कुलिस कठोरा॥ पुलक सिथिल तन बारि बिलोचन। महि नख लिखन लगीं सब सोचन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3361.verse_hindi: दोनों ओर सबके शील और प्रेम को देखकर और सुनकर कठोर वज्र भी पिघल जाते हैं। शरीर पुलकित और शिथिल हैं और नेत्रों में (शोक और प्रेम के) आँसू हैं। सब अपने (पैरों के) नखों से जमीन कुरेदने और सोचने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3361.english_translation: Seeing and hearing the character and love on both sides, even a hard thunderbolt would melt. Their bodies tremble and soften, tears fill their eyes, and everyone begins to scratch the ground with their nails in thought and grief.
ramacharitamanas::3361.translation_literal: सीलु (character/gentleness) / सनेहु (love) / सकल (all) / दुहु (of both) / ओरा (sides) / द्रवहिं (melt) / देखि (seeing) / सुनि (hearing) / कुलिस (thunderbolt) / कठोरा (hard) / पुलक (horripilation) / सिथिल (loosened) / तन (body) / बारि (water/tears) / बिलोचन (eyes) / महि (earth) / नख (nails) / लिखन (to scratch) / लगीं (began) / सब (all) / सोचन (to think/grieve)
ramacharitamanas::3361.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3361.essence: Love softens even the hardest heart.
ramacharitamanas::3361.simple_meaning: Everyone is overwhelmed by the gentleness and love on both sides. Even the hardest heart would soften. Their bodies tremble, their eyes fill with tears, and they stand there grieving and thinking deeply.
ramacharitamanas::3361.simple_insight: Real love can undo hardness faster than argument ever could.
ramacharitamanas::3361.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the women of Janak's household arrive at Kaushalya's court, and both families are moved by the tenderness they see in each other. The scene is less about speech than shared emotion; the verse lingers on the bodily signs of grief and love.
ramacharitamanas::3361.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where two families are trying to stay composed after a painful wedding conversation. No one needs to say much — the tears, the silence, and the care in the room say everything.
ramacharitamanas::3361.insight: It shifts attention from words to the emotional truth already visible in the body.

ramacharitamanas::3362.verse_sanskrit: सब सिय राम प्रीति की सि मूरति। जनु करुना बहु बेष बिसूरति॥ सीय मातु कह बिधि बुधि बाँकी। जो पय फेनु फोर पबि टाँकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3362.verse_hindi: सभी श्री सीता-रामजी के प्रेम की मूर्ति सी हैं, मानो स्वयं करुणा ही बहुत से वेष (रूप) धारण करके विसूर रही हो (दुःख कर रही हो)। सीताजी की माता सुनयनाजी ने कहा- विधाता की बुद्धि बड़ी टेढ़ी है, जो दूध के फेन जैसी कोमल वस्तु को वज्र की टाँकी से फोड़ रहा है (अर्थात जो अत्यन्त कोमल और निर्दोष हैं उन पर विपत्ति पर विपत्ति ढहा रहा है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3362.english_translation: All are forms of the love of Sita and Ram, as if compassion itself has taken many shapes and is grieving. Sita's mother, Sunayana, says: the Creator's mind is crooked, shattering something as soft as milk foam with a thunderbolt.
ramacharitamanas::3362.translation_literal: सब (all) / सिय राम (Sita and Ram) / प्रीति (love) / की सि मूरति (form itself) / जनु (as if) / करुना (compassion) / बहु बेष (many forms) / बिसूरति (grieving)॥ / सीय मातु (Sita's mother) / कह (said) / बिधि (the Creator) / बुधि (mind) / बाँकी (crooked) / जो (which) / पय (milk) / फेनु (foam) / फोर (to break) / पबि टाँकी (thunderbolt chisel)॥
ramacharitamanas::3362.speaker: Sunayana
ramacharitamanas::3362.essence: Tenderness can feel unbearable when the world turns harsh.
ramacharitamanas::3362.simple_meaning: Sita and Ram are seen as pure love and compassion itself, but their family is grieving because fate is striking the tender and innocent with harsh suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3362.simple_insight: Some pain feels so unfair that even love itself seems to weep.
ramacharitamanas::3362.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Sita's family and Ram's family are meeting in the middle of heartbreak. Sunayana looks at the tenderness between them and then at the suffering closing in, and she cries out against the cruelty of the unseen order.
ramacharitamanas::3362.modern_relevance: You watch a gentle person get hit with one loss after another, and your first reaction is not explanation but protest. This verse gives voice to that grief without pretending it is tidy.
ramacharitamanas::3362.insight: It validates grief before resolution, letting the mind name injustice instead of rushing past it.

ramacharitamanas::3363.verse_sanskrit: सुनिअ सुधा देखिअहिं गरल सब करतूति कराल। जहँ तहँ काक उलूक बक मानस सकृत मराल ॥
ramacharitamanas::3363.verse_hindi: अमृत केवल सुनने में आता है और विष जहाँ-तहाँ प्रत्यक्ष देखे जाते हैं। विधाता की सभी करतूतें भयंकर हैं। जहाँ-तहाँ कौए, उल्लू और बगुले ही (दिखाई देते) हैं, हंस तो एक मानसरोवर में ही हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3363.english_translation: Nectar is heard, but poison is seen everywhere. The deeds of fate are terrible. Everywhere you look, there are crows, owls, and herons; swans appear only on the Manasarovar.
ramacharitamanas::3363.translation_literal: सुनिअ (is heard) / सुधा (nectar) / देखिअहिं (is seen) / गरल (poison) / सब (all) / करतूति (deeds) / कराल (terrible) / जहँ तहँ (everywhere) / काक (crow) / उलूक (owl) / बक (heron) / मानस (Manasa) / सकृत (only once) / मराल (swan)
ramacharitamanas::3363.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3363.essence: Purity is rare; most of what you meet is harsh and mixed.
ramacharitamanas::3363.simple_meaning: Goodness may be praised in words, but the world often shows cruelty and corruption instead. Rare purity is like a swan seen only in a special place.
ramacharitamanas::3363.simple_insight: It helps you stop being fooled by appearances and notice how rare real goodness can be.
ramacharitamanas::3363.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, grief is spreading after Ram's exile. Tulsidas compares the world to a place where poison is visible everywhere, while nectar exists mostly in talk. True purity is rare, like a swan on Manasarovar.
ramacharitamanas::3363.modern_relevance: You scroll through polished promises, then open the app and see another betrayal, another lie, another polished excuse. This verse names that ache: pure things are rare, and you have to look carefully to find them.
ramacharitamanas::3363.insight: It shifts the mind from idealized expectation to clear-eyed discernment about what the world usually shows.

ramacharitamanas::3364.verse_sanskrit: सुनि ससोच कह देबि सुमित्रा। बिधि गति बड़ि बिपरीत बिचित्रा॥ जो सृजि पालइ हरइ बहोरी। बालकेलि सम बिधि मति भोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3364.verse_hindi: यह सुनकर देवी सुमित्राजी शोक के साथ कहने लगीं- विधाता की चाल बड़ी ही विपरीत और विचित्र है, जो सृष्टि को उत्पन्न करके पालता है और फिर नष्ट कर डालता है। विधाता की बुद्धि बालकों के खेल के समान भोली (विवेक शून्य) है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3364.english_translation: Hearing this, Sumitra said with grief, “The course of fate is great, reversed, and strange. It creates, sustains, and then destroys again. Fate’s mind is like a child at play—simple and unaware.”
ramacharitamanas::3364.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / ससोच (with grief) / कह (said) / देबि (lady/goddess) / सुमित्रा (Sumitra) / बिधि (fate) / गति (course) / बड़ि (great) / बिपरीत (reversed) / बिचित्रा (strange) / जो (which) / सृजि (creating) / पालइ (sustains) / हरइ (destroys) / बहोरी (again) / बालकेलि (child's play) / सम (like) / बिधि (fate) / मति (mind) / भोरी (naive)
ramacharitamanas::3364.speaker: Sumitra
ramacharitamanas::3364.essence: Life can overturn itself without warning, and you must still bow to it.
ramacharitamanas::3364.simple_meaning: Sumitra sees that life can feel reversed and strange: what is born is also sustained and then taken away. Some events must be met with acceptance, not blame.
ramacharitamanas::3364.simple_insight: Grief softens when you stop demanding that life make immediate sense.
ramacharitamanas::3364.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the women of the palace are stunned by Ram’s exile and the collapse of the royal family. Hearing the sorrow around her, Sumitra says the order of life is strange and hard to read, and that creation and loss both lie beyond human control.
ramacharitamanas::3364.modern_relevance: You get the call in the hospital corridor and nothing feels fair anymore. In that moment, the mind wants a culprit; this verse asks for a steadier response: accept what you cannot untangle right now.
ramacharitamanas::3364.insight: It shifts you from searching for blame to making peace with what cannot be explained.

ramacharitamanas::3365.verse_sanskrit: कौसल्या कह दोसु न काहू। करम बिबस दुख सुख छति लाहू॥ कठिन करम गति जान बिधाता। जो सुभ असुभ सकल फल दाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3365.verse_hindi: कौसल्याजी ने कहा- किसी का दोष नहीं है, दुःख-सुख, हानि-लाभ सब कर्म के अधीन हैं। कर्म की गति कठिन (दुर्विज्ञेय) है, उसे विधाता ही जानता है, जो शुभ और अशुभ सभी फलों का देने वाला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3365.english_translation: Kausalya said, "No one is at fault. Pleasure and pain, loss and gain, all are ruled by action. The course of action is hard to understand; only the creator knows it, and he gives every good and bad result."
ramacharitamanas::3365.translation_literal: कौसल्या (Kausalya) / कह (said) / दोसु (fault) / न (not) / काहू (of anyone) / करम (action) / बिबस (controlled by) / दुख (pain) / सुख (pleasure) / छति (loss) / लाहू (gain) / कठिन (hard) / करम गति (course of action) / जान (knows) / बिधाता (the creator) / जो (who) / सुभ (good) / असुभ (bad) / सकल (all) / फल (results) / दाता (giver)
ramacharitamanas::3365.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::3365.essence: Suffering feels personal, but its roots run deeper than blame.
ramacharitamanas::3365.simple_meaning: No one is to blame. Pain and pleasure, loss and gain all arise through action, and the deeper pattern is beyond easy understanding.
ramacharitamanas::3365.simple_insight: It softens blame and helps you face hardship without turning it into a personal attack.
ramacharitamanas::3365.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, grief has entered the palace after Ram's exile. Kausalya responds to the sorrow around her by refusing blame and pointing to the hidden working of action and the creator's order. Her words continue the family's effort to make sense of suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3365.modern_relevance: You get a painful email, then spend the whole night replaying who caused it. Kausalya's response stops the spiral of blame and asks you to face what happened without collapsing into accusation.
ramacharitamanas::3365.insight: It shifts the mind from personal blame to a wider view of cause, consequence, and acceptance.

ramacharitamanas::3366.verse_sanskrit: ईस रजाइ सीस सबही कें। उतपति थिति लय बिषहु अमी कें॥ देबि मोह बस सोचिअ बादी। बिधि प्रपंचु अस अचल अनादी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3366.verse_hindi: ईश्वर की आज्ञा सभी के सिर पर है। उत्पत्ति, स्थिति (पालन) और लय (संहार) तथा अमृत और विष के भी सिर पर है (ये सब भी उसी के अधीन हैं)। हे देवि! मोहवश सोच करना व्यर्थ है। विधाता का प्रपंच ऐसा ही अचल और अनादि है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3366.english_translation: The divine command rests on everyone’s head. Creation, preservation, destruction, nectar, and poison all rest within it. O lady, to grieve in delusion is pointless; the pattern of the creator is fixed and beginningless.
ramacharitamanas::3366.translation_literal: ईस (the divine) / रजाइ (command) / सीस (head) / सबही (everyone) / कें (on) / उतपति (creation) / थिति (preservation) / लय (dissolution) / बिषहु (poison also) / अमी कें (nectar also) / देबि (O lady) / मोह बस (under the sway of delusion) / सोचिअ (to grieve) / बादी (vain) / बिधि (creator's) / प्रपंचु (pattern, unfolding) / अस (thus) / अचल (fixed) / अनादी (beginningless)
ramacharitamanas::3366.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::3366.essence: Peace begins when you stop arguing with the order already in motion.
ramacharitamanas::3366.simple_meaning: Everything that happens is under a higher order, including both joy and pain. Grieving in confusion only adds suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3366.simple_insight: There is relief in stopping the fight with reality.
ramacharitamanas::3366.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kausalya and Sumitra are absorbing the blow of Ram’s exile. Kausalya answers grief by naming a larger order: life, death, sweetness, and poison all move under it. Her words try to steady a broken household.
ramacharitamanas::3366.modern_relevance: You get the diagnosis, then spend the night replaying every worst-case ending. This verse asks you to stop feeding panic and see that not everything is yours to control.
ramacharitamanas::3366.insight: It shifts the mind from resisting events to meeting them without delusion.

ramacharitamanas::3367.verse_sanskrit: भूपति जिअब मरब उर आनी। सोचिअ सखि लखि निज हित हानी॥ सीय मातु कह सत्य सुबानी। सुकृती अवधि अवधपति रानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3367.verse_hindi: महाराज के मरने और जीने की बात को हृदय में याद करके जो चिन्ता करती हैं, वह तो हे सखी! हम अपने ही हित की हानि देखकर (स्वार्थवश) करती हैं। सीताजी की माता ने कहा- आपका कथन उत्तम है और सत्य है। आप पुण्यात्माओं के सीमा रूप अवधपति (महाराज दशरथजी) की ही तो रानी हैं। (फिर भला, ऐसा क्यों न कहेंगी) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3367.english_translation: Thinking of the king's death and life in her heart, she grieves only for her own loss, O friend. Sita's mother said, "Your words are noble and true. You are the queen of Ayodhya's righteous king, the king who was the limit of virtue."
ramacharitamanas::3367.translation_literal: भूपति (king) / जिअब (living) / मरब (dying) / उर आनी (bringing into the heart) / सोचिअ (she grieves / she worries) / सखि (friend) / लखि (seeing) / निज (own) / हित (welfare) / हानी (loss) ॥ सीय मातु (Sita's mother) / कह (said) / सत्य (true) / सुबानी (good speech) / सुकृती (virtuous) / अवधि (limit) / अवधपति (lord of Ayodhya) / रानी (queen) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3367.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3367.essence: True grief becomes clearer when you notice your own attachment.
ramacharitamanas::3367.simple_meaning: Sita's mother says grief is often driven by self-interest, and that Sita's words are true and noble because she belongs to Dasharath, the righteous king of Ayodhya.
ramacharitamanas::3367.simple_insight: Not every sorrow is pure; sometimes it shows where attachment still lives.
ramacharitamanas::3367.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the shock of Ram's exile and Dasharath's decline, Sita's mother answers with calm clarity. She says real grief is often mixed with concern for one's own loss, and she honours Sita's speech as truthful and fitting for Dasharath's queen.
ramacharitamanas::3367.modern_relevance: You hear bad news about someone you love, and the first sting is not only concern for them — it is the fear of what their loss will cost you. This verse asks you to notice that layer honestly.
ramacharitamanas::3367.insight: It shifts you from self-protective sorrow to a cleaner, more honest response.

ramacharitamanas::3368.verse_sanskrit: लखनु रामु सिय जाहुँ बन भल परिनाम न पोचु। गहबरि हियँ कह कौसिला मोहि भरत कर सोचु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3368.verse_hindi: कौसल्याजी ने दुःख भरे हृदय से कहा- श्री राम, लक्ष्मण और सीता वन में जाएँ, इसका परिणाम तो अच्छा ही होगा, बुरा नहीं। मुझे तो भरत की चिन्ता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3368.english_translation: Kausalya said with a grief-stricken heart: Let Ram, Lakshman, and Sita go to the forest; the result will be good, not bad. I only worry about Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::3368.translation_literal: लखनु (Lakshman) / रामु (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / जाहुँ (go) / बन (forest) / भल (good) / परिनाम (result) / न (not) / पोचु (bad) / गहबरि (distressed) / हियँ (heart) / कह (said) / कौसिला (Kausalya) / मोहि (to me) / भरत (Bharat) / कर (of) / सोचु (worry)
ramacharitamanas::3368.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::3368.essence: You may accept the outcome and still grieve for the one who bears it.
ramacharitamanas::3368.simple_meaning: Kausalya accepts that Ram, Lakshman, and Sita going to the forest will lead to something good. Her real sorrow is for Bharat, who will suffer most.
ramacharitamanas::3368.simple_insight: Acceptance does not erase love; it simply reveals where the deepest ache still lives.
ramacharitamanas::3368.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kausalya speaks through grief after Ram's exile has begun. She can see that the forest journey will not end badly for Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. Her motherly mind turns instead to Bharat, whose burden she cannot ignore.
ramacharitamanas::3368.modern_relevance: You agree to a hard family decision because you know it is necessary, but your mind keeps going to the brother who will carry the emotional cost. That is Kausalya's pain.
ramacharitamanas::3368.insight: It teaches you to hold a painful truth without denying the person who will hurt most.

ramacharitamanas::3369.verse_sanskrit: ईस प्रसाद असीस तुम्हारी। सुत सुतबधू देवसरि बारी॥ राम सपथ मैं कीन्हि न काऊ। सो करि कहउँ सखी सति भाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3369.verse_hindi: ईश्वर के अनुग्रह और आपके आशीर्वाद से मेरे (चारों) पुत्र और (चारों) बहुएँ गंगाजी के जल के समान पवित्र हैं। हे सखी! मैंने कभी श्री राम की सौगंध नहीं की, सो आज श्री राम की शपथ करके सत्य भाव से कहती हूँ- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3369.english_translation: By the divine grace and by your blessings, my four sons and four daughters-in-law are pure as the waters of the Ganga. O friend, I have never sworn by Ram before; so I speak now with truthful feeling, taking Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::3369.translation_literal: ईस (the divine) / प्रसाद (grace) / असीस (blessings) / तुम्हारी (your) / सुत (sons) / सुतबधू (daughters-in-law) / देवसरि (Ganga, river of the divine) / बारी (waters) / राम (Ram) / सपथ (oath) / मैं (I) / कीन्हि (did) / न (not) / काऊ (ever) / सो (so) / करि (doing that) / कहउँ (I speak) / सखी (friend) / सति (true) / भाऊ (feeling)
ramacharitamanas::3369.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::3369.essence: True feeling needs no ornament; it stands on its own.
ramacharitamanas::3369.simple_meaning: Kausalya says her sons and daughters-in-law are pure by divine grace and the listener's blessings. She then says she is speaking truly, with Ram as her witness.
ramacharitamanas::3369.simple_insight: Truth spoken from the heart carries more weight than any formal oath.
ramacharitamanas::3369.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kausalya is speaking to a close friend while the pain of exile and family fracture hangs over Ayodhya. She reassures the listener, then seals her words by invoking Ram, showing both tenderness and moral seriousness.
ramacharitamanas::3369.modern_relevance: When a mother quietly says, after a long family argument, that she is speaking honestly and needs no performance to prove it, you feel the force of lived truth.
ramacharitamanas::3369.insight: It shifts speech away from display and toward quiet, trustworthy sincerity.

ramacharitamanas::3370.verse_sanskrit: भरत सील गुन बिनय बड़ाई। भायप भगति भरोस भलाई॥ कहत सारदहु कर मति हीचे। सागर सीप कि जाहिं उलीचे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3370.verse_hindi: भरत के शील, गुण, नम्रता, बड़प्पन, भाईपन, भक्ति, भरोसे और अच्छेपन का वर्णन करने में सरस्वतीजी की बुद्धि भी हिचकती है। सीप से कहीं समुद्र उलीचे जा सकते हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3370.english_translation: Bharat's character, virtues, humility, greatness, brotherly love, devotion, trust, and goodness are beyond speech. Even Saraswati's mind falters. Can the ocean be scooped out with a seashell?
ramacharitamanas::3370.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / सील (character) / गुन (virtues) / बिनय (humility) / बड़ाई (greatness) / भायप (brotherhood) / भगति (devotion) / भरोस (trust) / भलाई (goodness) / कहत (speaking) / सारदहु (even Saraswati) / कर (of) / मति (mind) / हीचे (fails) / सागर (ocean) / सीप (seashell) / कि (whether) / जाहिं (can be) / उलीचे (scooped out)
ramacharitamanas::3370.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3370.essence: True greatness is too deep for speech to contain.
ramacharitamanas::3370.simple_meaning: Bharat's virtues are so great that even the goddess of speech cannot fully describe them. His goodness is like an ocean that cannot be measured by a shell.
ramacharitamanas::3370.simple_insight: Real greatness doesn't need to announce itself; it overwhelms language by its own depth.
ramacharitamanas::3370.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaushalya is speaking of Bharat as the family reels from exile and broken promises. She says his character, humility, devotion, and brotherly love are beyond description, and even Saraswati cannot fully praise him.
ramacharitamanas::3370.modern_relevance: You try to explain a friend who quietly held your family together through a crisis, and every sentence feels too small. Some people are so steady and selfless that praise starts to sound childish.
ramacharitamanas::3370.insight: It shifts attention from public greatness to the kind of character that can only be recognized, never fully captured.

ramacharitamanas::3371.verse_sanskrit: जानउँ सदा भरत कुलदीपा। बार बार मोहि कहेउ महीपा॥ कसें कनकु मनि पारिखि पाएँ। पुरुष परिखिअहिं समयँ सुभाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3371.verse_hindi: मैं भरत को सदा कुल का दीपक जानती हूँ। महाराज ने भी बार-बार मुझे यही कहा था। सोना कसौटी पर कसे जाने पर और रत्न पारखी (जौहरी) के मिलने पर ही पहचाना जाता है। वैसे ही पुरुष की परीक्षा समय पड़ने पर उसके स्वभाव से ही (उसका चरित्र देखकर) हो जाती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3371.english_translation: I have always known Bharata as the lamp of the family. The king has told me this again and again. Gold is tested by the touchstone and a gem by the jeweler; a person is tested by character when the time comes.
ramacharitamanas::3371.translation_literal: जानउँ (I know) / सदा (always) / भरत (Bharata) / कुलदीपा (lamp of the family) / बार बार (again and again) / मोहि (to me) / कहेउ (said) / महीपा (the king) / कसें (by testing) / कनकु (gold) / मनि (gem) / पारिखि (by the tester/jeweler) / पाएँ (is obtained/recognized) / पुरुष (a person) / परिखिअहिं (is tested) / समयँ (in time) / सुभाएँ (by nature/character)
ramacharitamanas::3371.speaker: Kaikeyi
ramacharitamanas::3371.essence: Pressure reveals the character already inside you.
ramacharitamanas::3371.simple_meaning: A person's real nature is revealed by how they respond when life puts them under pressure.
ramacharitamanas::3371.simple_insight: You don't need to guess who someone is forever; difficult moments often tell the truth.
ramacharitamanas::3371.detailed_meaning: Kaikeyi is speaking in Ayodhya about Bharata, defending his worth after the court's grief and suspicion. She says Bharata is the family's lamp, and that true character is recognized only when life tests it, just as gold and gems are tested.
ramacharitamanas::3371.modern_relevance: Someone is calm in meetings but cruel in a family argument. Another person looks ordinary until a crisis hits and they quietly hold everyone together. Pressure does not invent character; it exposes it.
ramacharitamanas::3371.insight: It shifts judgment from appearances to behavior under strain.

ramacharitamanas::3372.verse_sanskrit: अनुचित आजु कहब अस मोरा। सोक सनेहँ सयानप थोरा॥ सुनि सुरसरि सम पावनि बानी। भईं सनेह बिकल सब रानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3372.verse_hindi: किन्तु आज मेरा ऐसा कहना भी अनुचित है। शोक और स्नेह में सयानापन (विवेक) कम हो जाता है (लोग कहेंगे कि मैं स्नेहवश भरत की बड़ाई कर रही हूँ)। कौसल्याजी की गंगाजी के समान पवित्र करने वाली वाणी सुनकर सब रानियाँ स्नेह के मारे विकल हो उठीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3372.english_translation: But today it would be improper for me to say such things. Grief and affection leave little room for wisdom. Hearing Kaushalya's speech, pure as the Ganga, all the queens were overwhelmed with love.
ramacharitamanas::3372.translation_literal: अनुचित (improper) / आजु (today) / कहब (to say) / अस (such) / मोरा (mine) / सोक (grief) / सनेहँ (with affection) / सयानप (wisdom) / थोरा (little)॥ / सुनि (hearing) / सुरसरि (the Ganga) / सम (like) / पावनि (purifying) / बानी (speech) / भईं (became) / सनेह (love) / बिकल (overwhelmed) / सब (all) / रानी (queens) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3372.speaker: Kaushalya
ramacharitamanas::3372.essence: Love and grief can make even true praise feel unfit.
ramacharitamanas::3372.simple_meaning: Kaushalya feels awkward praising Bharata too much because grief and love cloud clear judgment. Her pure, gentle words move the other queens deeply.
ramacharitamanas::3372.simple_insight: When love is raw, even praise can feel too small to hold it.
ramacharitamanas::3372.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the queens are speaking through tears about Bharata's greatness and the pain of exile. Kaushalya checks herself, saying grief and affection weaken impartial judgment. Her words still move every queen to tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::3372.modern_relevance: You try to speak at a funeral, but your voice breaks on the first sentence. Even honest praise feels inadequate when love and loss are both in the room.
ramacharitamanas::3372.insight: It shows how grief can humble speech and make even praise feel insufficient.

ramacharitamanas::3373.verse_sanskrit: कौसल्या कह धीर धरि सुनहु देबि मिथिलेसि। को बिबेकनिधि बल्लभहि तुम्हहि सकइ उपदेसि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3373.verse_hindi: कौसल्याजी ने फिर धीरज धरकर कहा- हे देवी मिथिलेश्वरी! सुनिए, ज्ञान के भंडार श्री जनकजी की प्रिया आपको कौन उपदेश दे सकता है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3373.english_translation: Kausalya, regaining her composure, said, “Listen, princess of Mithila. Who can instruct you, the beloved of the king who is a treasure-house of discernment?”
ramacharitamanas::3373.translation_literal: कौसल्या (Kausalya) / कह (said) / धीर धरि (gathering composure) / सुनहु (listen) / देबि (O देवी) / मिथिलेसि (princess of Mithila) / को (who) / बिबेकनिधि (treasure-house of discernment) / बल्लभहि (beloved) / तुम्हहि (you) / सकइ (can) / उपदेसि (instruct)
ramacharitamanas::3373.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::3373.essence: True respect begins where instruction ends.
ramacharitamanas::3373.simple_meaning: Kausalya gently tells Sita that no one can really instruct her, because she already belongs to a wise and discerning husband.
ramacharitamanas::3373.simple_insight: Respect deepens when you stop trying to correct someone who already sees clearly.
ramacharitamanas::3373.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the queens are speaking through grief and loyalty as the exile unfolds. Kausalya addresses Sita with tenderness, acknowledging her as the wife of Janak’s wise daughter and of a husband known for discernment. The verse softens the conversation before the next request.
ramacharitamanas::3373.modern_relevance: You’re trying to advise someone who has already thought it through, and your words start sounding clumsy. Sometimes the wiser move is humility, not instruction.
ramacharitamanas::3373.insight: It shifts you from correcting others to recognising their inner readiness and wisdom.

ramacharitamanas::3374.verse_sanskrit: रानि राय सन अवसरु पाई। अपनी भाँति कहब समुझाई॥ रखिअहिं लखनु भरतु गवनहिं बन। जौं यह मत मानै महीप मन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3374.verse_hindi: हे रानी! मौका पाकर आप राजा को अपनी ओर से जहाँ तक हो सके समझाकर कहिएगा कि लक्ष्मण को घर रख लिया जाए और भरत वन को जाएँ। यदि यह राय राजा के मन में (ठीक) जँच जाए, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3374.english_translation: O queen, when you get the chance, explain it to the king in your own way: let Lakshman stay at home and let Bharat go to the forest. If this proposal seems right to the king's mind, ...
ramacharitamanas::3374.translation_literal: रानि (queen) / राय (king) / सन (with) / अवसरु (opportunity) / पाई (having obtained) / अपनी (own) / भाँति (way) / कहब (to say) / समुझाई (explaining) / रखिअहिं (let be kept) / लखनु (Lakshman) / भरतु (Bharat) / गवनहिं (let go) / बन (to the forest) / जौं (if) / यह (this) / मत (proposal) / मानै (accepts) / महीप (king) / मन (mind)
ramacharitamanas::3374.speaker: Kaushalya
ramacharitamanas::3374.essence: Love makes even practical requests feel unbearably heavy.
ramacharitamanas::3374.simple_meaning: Kaushalya asks the queen to persuade the king to keep Lakshman at home and send Bharat to the forest if the king agrees.
ramacharitamanas::3374.simple_insight: Duty can be so tangled with love that even the right request feels painful.
ramacharitamanas::3374.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kaushalya speaks carefully to the queen, trying to protect Lakshman while easing Bharat toward exile. The family is already torn by Rama's banishment, and this request shows how grief makes every choice feel loaded with love and loss.
ramacharitamanas::3374.modern_relevance: You draft a message three times before sending it, because one sentence could hurt someone you love. Even a practical request can carry the weight of family loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::3374.insight: It shows how people try to manage duty through careful, indirect speech when the stakes are emotionally loaded.

ramacharitamanas::3375.verse_sanskrit: तौ भल जतनु करब सुबिचारी। मोरें सोचु भरत कर भारी॥ गूढ़ सनेह भरत मन माहीं। रहें नीक मोहि लागत नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3375.verse_hindi: तो भलीभाँति खूब विचारकर ऐसा यत्न करें। मुझे भरत का अत्यधिक सोच है। भरत के मन में गूढ़ प्रेम है। उनके घर रहने में मुझे भलाई नहीं जान पड़ती (यह डर लगता है कि उनके प्राणों को कोई भय न हो जाए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3375.english_translation: Then, thinking carefully, do your best. I am deeply worried about Bharat. His heart holds hidden love, and staying in the palace does not seem right to me.
ramacharitamanas::3375.translation_literal: तौ (then) / भल (well) / जतनु (effort) / करब (to do) / सुबिचारी (with careful thought) / मोरें (my) / सोचु (worry) / भरत (Bharat) / कर (of) / भारी (heavy, great) / गूढ़ (hidden, deep) / सनेह (love) / भरत (Bharat) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) / रहें (to remain) / नीक (good) / मोहि (to me) / लागत (seems) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::3375.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::3375.essence: Hidden love can make the safest arrangement feel wrong.
ramacharitamanas::3375.simple_meaning: Kausalya asks for careful effort, but her real concern is Bharat's hidden love and the danger of keeping him in the palace.
ramacharitamanas::3375.simple_insight: Love can make even a safe place feel unsafe.
ramacharitamanas::3375.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Kausalya speaks after hearing the queen's proposal about Bharat and Lakshman. She knows Bharat's heart is full of quiet devotion, and that knowledge makes her uneasy. Her worry is not political; it is protective and deeply loving.
ramacharitamanas::3375.modern_relevance: You see someone smiling too politely after a family argument, and you know the room is not as calm as it looks. The deepest worry is often the one no one says out loud.
ramacharitamanas::3375.insight: It shifts attention from outward arrangements to the hidden emotional reality underneath them.

ramacharitamanas::3376.verse_sanskrit: लखि सुभाउ सुनि सरल सुबानी। सब भइ मगन करुन रस रानी॥ नभ प्रसून झरि धन्य धन्य धुनि। सिथिल सनेहँ सिद्ध जोगी मुनि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3376.verse_hindi: कौसल्याजी का स्वभाव देखकर और उनकी सरल और उत्तम वाणी को सुनकर सब रानियाँ करुण रस में निमग्न हो गईं। आकाश से पुष्प वर्षा की झड़ी लग गई और धन्य-धन्य की ध्वनि होने लगी। सिद्ध, योगी और मुनि स्नेह से शिथिल हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3376.english_translation: Seeing her nature and hearing her simple, noble words, all the queens were drenched in compassion. Flower petals rained from the sky, cries of “Blessed, blessed” rose everywhere, and even perfected sages, yogis, and seers grew limp with love.
ramacharitamanas::3376.translation_literal: लखि (seeing) / सुभाउ (nature) / सुनि (hearing) / सरल (simple) / सुबानी (good speech) / सब (all) / भइ (became) / मगन (absorbed) / करुन रस (the flavor of compassion) / रानी (queens) ॥ नभ (sky) / प्रसून (flowers) / झरि (having rained down) / धन्य धन्य (blessed, blessed) / धुनि (sound) / सिथिल (weakened, softened) / सनेहँ (with love) / सिद्ध (perfected) / जोगी (yogis) / मुनि (sages) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3376.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3376.essence: Gentleness can move even the hardest hearts.
ramacharitamanas::3376.simple_meaning: Kausalya’s gentle nature and humble words move everyone deeply. The queens are overcome with compassion, heaven seems to celebrate, and even great sages are softened by love.
ramacharitamanas::3376.simple_insight: True gentleness can move an entire room without force.
ramacharitamanas::3376.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the queens are witnessing Kausalya’s tender dignity after the exile has shattered the royal household. Her calm, loving speech touches everyone so deeply that grief turns into compassion and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3376.modern_relevance: You watch someone speak with such quiet dignity that the whole room changes. No one argues, no one performs — people simply soften.
ramacharitamanas::3376.insight: It shows how sincere tenderness can dissolve resistance and awaken shared feeling.

ramacharitamanas::3377.verse_sanskrit: सबु रनिवासु बिथकि लखि रहेऊ। तब धरि धीर सुमित्राँ कहेऊ॥ देबि दंड जुग जामिनि बीती। राम मातु सुनि उठी सप्रीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::3377.verse_hindi: सारा रनिवास देखकर थकित रह गया (निस्तब्ध हो गया), तब सुमित्राजी ने धीरज करके कहा कि हे देवी! दो घड़ी रात बीत गई है। यह सुनकर श्री रामजी की माता कौसल्याजी प्रेमपूर्वक उठीं- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3377.english_translation: The whole royal household stood stunned. Then Sुमित्रा gathered her courage and said, “Lady, two watches of the night have passed.” Hearing this, Ram’s mother Kaushalya rose with affection.
ramacharitamanas::3377.translation_literal: सबु (all) / रनिवासु (royal household) / बिथकि (stunned, bewildered) / लखि (seeing) / रहेऊ (remained) / तब (then) / धरि (holding, gathering) / धीर (courage, patience) / सुमित्राँ (Sumitra) / कहेऊ (said) / देबि (lady) / दंड (watch, a measure of time) / जुग (two) / जामिनि (night) / बीती (passed) / राम मातु (Ram's mother) / सुनि (hearing) / उठी (rose) / सप्रीती (with affection)
ramacharitamanas::3377.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3377.essence: Gentle courage helps grief take its next step.
ramacharitamanas::3377.simple_meaning: The women in the palace are overwhelmed with grief and silence. Sumitra gently reminds Kaushalya that time has passed, and Kaushalya rises with loving concern.
ramacharitamanas::3377.simple_insight: Even in grief, a gentle voice can help everyone take the next step.
ramacharitamanas::3377.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the royal women are still reeling from the exile of Ram. The palace sits in stunned silence. Sumitra, steady and kind, gathers herself and speaks to Kaushalya, who then rises with affection. The verse is a small bridge between shock and action.
ramacharitamanas::3377.modern_relevance: A house goes quiet after bad news, and someone finally says, “It’s getting late.” That small sentence helps everyone move from numbness to the next necessary act.
ramacharitamanas::3377.insight: It shows how calm presence can interrupt paralysis and restore movement in a grief-struck room.

ramacharitamanas::3378.verse_sanskrit: दोहाथ बेगि पाउ धारिअ थलहि कह सनेहँ सतिभाय। हमरें तौ अब ईस गति कै मिथिलेस सहाय ॥
ramacharitamanas::3378.verse_hindi: और प्रेम सहित सद्भाव से बोलीं- अब आप शीघ्र डेरे को पधारिए। हमारे तो अब ईश्वर ही गति हैं, अथवा मिथिलेश्वर जनकजी सहायक हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3378.english_translation: And with loving goodwill she said, "Please return to your tent at once. For us now, only the divine is our refuge, or King Janaka is our support."
ramacharitamanas::3378.translation_literal: दोहाथ (with loving affection) / बेगि (quickly) / पाउ (feet) / धारिअ (place, return) / थलहि (to the ground, to the tent) / कह (said) / सनेहँ (with love) / सतिभाय (with true goodwill) / हमरें (for us) / तौ (indeed) / अब (now) / ईस (the divine) / गति (refuge, support) / कै (either) / मिथिलेस (Janaka, lord of Mithila) / सहाय (helper, support)
ramacharitamanas::3378.speaker: Kausalya
ramacharitamanas::3378.essence: Grace grows when you accept limits and let higher help carry what you cannot.
ramacharitamanas::3378.simple_meaning: Kausalya speaks lovingly and asks them to leave. She says her only refuge now is the divine, and Janaka can help too.
ramacharitamanas::3378.simple_insight: Even in loss, you can speak with grace and let support come without grasping.
ramacharitamanas::3378.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's grieving palace, Kausalya has seen the royal women break into sorrow. With gentle dignity, she tells Janaka's household to return. She accepts that human support is limited, and places the moment in the care of the divine.
ramacharitamanas::3378.modern_relevance: After a family funeral, someone quietly starts clearing the plates and says, "Please go rest." They are not cold. They are holding everyone together with calm acceptance.
ramacharitamanas::3378.insight: It teaches you to release panic, speak kindly, and accept help without making it your final support.

ramacharitamanas::3379.verse_sanskrit: लखि सनेह सुनि बचन बिनीता। जनकप्रिया गह पाय पुनीता॥ देबि उचित असि बिनय तुम्हारी। दसरथ घरिनि राम महतारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3379.verse_hindi: कौसल्याजी के प्रेम को देखकर और उनके विनम्र वचनों को सुनकर जनकजी की प्रिय पत्नी ने उनके पवित्र चरण पकड़ लिए और कहा- हे देवी! आप राजा दशरथजी की रानी और श्री रामजी की माता हैं। आपकी ऐसी नम्रता उचित ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3379.english_translation: Seeing Kaushalya's affection and hearing her humble words, Janaka's beloved wife held her sacred feet and said, 'O देवी, your humility is fitting. You are King Dasharath's queen and Ram's mother.'
ramacharitamanas::3379.translation_literal: लखि (seeing) / सनेह (affection) / सुनि (hearing) / बचन (words) / बिनीता (humble) / जनकप्रिया (Janaka's beloved) / गह (grasped) / पाय (feet) / पुनीता (sacred) / देबि (O देवी) / उचित (fitting) / असि (such) / बिनय (humility) / तुम्हारी (your) / दसरथ घरिनि (Dasharath's queen) / राम महतारी (Ram's mother)
ramacharitamanas::3379.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3379.essence: True worth can wear complete humility.
ramacharitamanas::3379.simple_meaning: Kaushalya is treated with reverence because she is Ram's mother and Dasharath's queen. Her humility is seen as natural and worthy of respect.
ramacharitamanas::3379.simple_insight: Respect grows naturally when you recognise someone’s quiet greatness.
ramacharitamanas::3379.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the queens meet amid the pain of exile and separation. Janaka's beloved wife responds to Kaushalya's tenderness by bowing and praising her humility, honouring both her status and her devotion as Ram's mother.
ramacharitamanas::3379.modern_relevance: You meet the mother of someone everyone admires, and she speaks with such softness that your first response is respect. Quiet dignity often carries the deepest authority.
ramacharitamanas::3379.insight: It teaches you to honour humility, not just rank.

ramacharitamanas::3380.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु अपने नीचहु आदरहीं। अगिनि धूम गिरि सिर तिनु धरहीं॥ सेवकु राउ करम मन बानी। सदा सहाय महेसु भवानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3380.verse_hindi: प्रभु अपने निज जनों का भी आदर करते हैं। अग्नि धुएँ को और पर्वत तृण (घास) को अपने सिर पर धारण करते हैं। हमारे राजा तो कर्म, मन और वाणी से आपके सेवक हैं और सदा सहायक तो श्री महादेव-पार्वतीजी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3380.english_translation: The Lord honors even the lowly. Fire bears smoke, and a mountain bears grass upon its head. Our king serves you in action, mind, and speech, and the true helpers are always Mahesh and Bhavani.
ramacharitamanas::3380.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / अपने (own) / नीचहु (even the lowly) / आदरहीं (honor) । / अगिनि (fire) / धूम (smoke) / गिरि (mountain) / सिर (head) / तिनु (grass) / धरहीं (bear) । / सेवकु (servant) / राउ (king) / करम (action) / मन (mind) / बानी (speech) / सदा (always) / सहाय (helper) / महेसु (Mahesh) / भवानी (Bhavani) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3380.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3380.essence: Ram honors the lowly, and devotion itself becomes protection.
ramacharitamanas::3380.simple_meaning: Ram honors even the lowly, and the speaker says the king serves Ram with body, mind, and speech while Shiva and Parvati remain the true helpers.
ramacharitamanas::3380.simple_insight: You do not need status to be held with respect; sincere service is enough.
ramacharitamanas::3380.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Kaushalya and Janaki are speaking in the tense aftermath of exile. The speaker praises Ram's nature: he honors even the humble. Bharat is described as serving Ram with complete devotion, while Shiva and Parvati are named as the ever-present protectors of that devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3380.modern_relevance: You show up for someone who has nothing to offer back, and they still treat you with dignity. That feeling of being seen without earning it is what this verse carries.
ramacharitamanas::3380.insight: It shifts the mind from status and usefulness to humility and devoted service.

ramacharitamanas::3381.verse_sanskrit: रउरे अंग जोगु जग को है। दीप सहाय की दिनकर सोहै॥ रामु जाइ बनु करि सुर काजू। अचल अवधपुर करिहहिं राजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3381.verse_hindi: आपका सहायक होने योग्य जगत में कौन है? दीपक सूर्य की सहायता करने जाकर कहीं शोभा पा सकता है? श्री रामचन्द्रजी वन में जाकर देवताओं का कार्य करके अवधपुरी में अचल राज्य करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3381.english_translation: Who in the world is fit to stand beside you? Can a lamp add glory by serving the sun? Lord Ram will go to the forest to do the work of the radiant beings, and Ayodhya will remain firmly ruled.
ramacharitamanas::3381.translation_literal: रउरे (your) / अंग (side, support) / जोगु (fit, worthy) / जग (world) / को (of whom) / है (is) / दीप (lamp) / सहाय (help, support) / की (of) / दिनकर (sun) / सोहै (looks beautiful, shines)॥ / रामु (Ram) / जाइ (going) / बनु (forest) / करि (doing) / सुर (radiant beings, devas) / काजू (work, task) / अचल (firm, unmoving) / अवधपुर (Ayodhya city) / करिहहिं (will do) / राजू (rule, kingdom)॥
ramacharitamanas::3381.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3381.essence: True greatness can go away and still hold everything together.
ramacharitamanas::3381.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond comparison, like the sun beyond a lamp. He goes to the forest for a higher purpose, yet Ayodhya remains secure under his rule.
ramacharitamanas::3381.simple_insight: You can do what is needed without losing your place or your dignity.
ramacharitamanas::3381.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the farewell is turning into a lesson. The speaker praises Ram as unmatched: he can leave for the forest to complete a greater task, and still his presence keeps the kingdom firm. This is not loss; it is noble purpose.
ramacharitamanas::3381.modern_relevance: You leave your home for a year-long assignment, and everyone worries it will pull your life apart. But the right calling does not weaken you — it reveals how steady you already are.
ramacharitamanas::3381.insight: It teaches you to see service as enlargement, not self-erasure.

ramacharitamanas::3382.verse_sanskrit: अमर नाग नर राम बाहुबल। सुख बसिहहिं अपनें अपनें थल॥ यह सब जागबलिक कहि राखा। देबि न होइ मुधा मुनि भाषा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3382.verse_hindi: देवता, नाग और मनुष्य सब श्री रामचन्द्रजी की भुजाओं के बल पर अपने-अपने स्थानों (लोकों) में सुखपूर्वक बसेंगे। यह सब याज्ञवल्क्य मुनि ने पहले ही से कह रखा है। हे देवि! मुनि का कथन व्यर्थ (झूठा) नहीं हो सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3382.english_translation: By Ram's mighty arms, gods, serpents, and humans will all dwell happily in their own places. Yajnavalkya has already said this, O Devi; a sage's words cannot be false.
ramacharitamanas::3382.translation_literal: अमर (immortal beings) / नाग (serpents) / नर (humans) / राम (Ram) / बाहुबल (arm-strength) / सुख (happily) / बसिहहिं (will dwell) / अपनें (their own) / अपनें (own) / थल (places) ॥ / यह (this) / सब (all) / जागबलिक (Yajnavalkya's) / कहि (having said) / राखा (kept) / देबि (O Devi) / न (not) / होइ (is) / मुधा (false) / मुनि (sage) / भाषा (speech) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3382.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3382.essence: Ram's strength quietly holds every realm in order.
ramacharitamanas::3382.simple_meaning: All beings can live securely in their proper places because Ram's power supports the world. The sage Yajnavalkya's words are being affirmed as true.
ramacharitamanas::3382.simple_insight: You can rest when you trust the force that holds life together.
ramacharitamanas::3382.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Shiva is reassuring Parvati as Ram's exile begins. The fear is that the world will lose its balance without Ram's presence in Ayodhya. Shiva answers that Ram's strength supports every realm, and a sage's word never fails.
ramacharitamanas::3382.modern_relevance: When your family feels unstable and everyone is asking who will hold things together, this verse says the deepest support is already there. Ram's strength is what keeps the world from falling apart.
ramacharitamanas::3382.insight: It shifts attention from visible control to the sustaining power beneath events.

ramacharitamanas::3383.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि पग परि प्रेम अति सिय हित बिनय सुनाइ। सिय समेत सियमातु तब चली सुआयसु पाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3383.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर बड़े प्रेम से पैरों पड़कर सीताजी (को साथ भेजने) के लिए विनती करके और सुंदर आज्ञा पाकर तब सीताजी समेत सीताजी की माता डेरे को चलीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3383.english_translation: Saying this, with great love she bowed at the feet, made a humble request for Sita's company, and, after receiving the gracious permission, then went away with Sita and Sita's mother.
ramacharitamanas::3383.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (having said) / पग (feet) / परि (falling) / प्रेम (love) / अति (very much) / सिय हित (for Sita's good) / बिनय (humble request) / सुनाइ (having made heard) / सिय समेत (together with Sita) / सियमातु (Sita's mother) / तब (then) / चली (went) / सुआयसु (gracious permission) / पाइ (having received)
ramacharitamanas::3383.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3383.essence: Love asks gently and leaves without forcing.
ramacharitamanas::3383.simple_meaning: With loving humility, she asks for Sita's company and leaves after receiving permission.
ramacharitamanas::3383.simple_insight: Gentle respect can carry a request farther than force ever could.
ramacharitamanas::3383.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the women are preparing for Sita's departure. This line shows a tender family moment: someone bows, asks lovingly for Sita's company, and leaves only after receiving permission. It is a small but respectful transition in the larger grief of exile.
ramacharitamanas::3383.modern_relevance: You need to ask a family member for something delicate, and you do it with care instead of pressure. The request lands because your respect is real.
ramacharitamanas::3383.insight: It models how to make a difficult request without violating dignity.

ramacharitamanas::3384.verse_sanskrit: प्रिय परिजनहि मिली बैदेही। जो जेहि जोगु भाँति तेहि तेही॥ तापस बेष जानकी देखी। भा सबु बिकल बिषाद बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3384.verse_hindi: जानकीजी अपने प्यारे कुटुम्बियों से- जो जिस योग्य था, उससे उसी प्रकार मिलीं। जानकीजी को तपस्विनी के वेष में देखकर सभी शोक से अत्यन्त व्याकुल हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3384.english_translation: Sita met her dear relatives, giving each the kind of meeting they were fit for. Seeing Janaki dressed as an ascetic, everyone became deeply shaken with grief.
ramacharitamanas::3384.translation_literal: प्रिय (dear) / परिजनहि (relatives) / मिली (met) / बैदेही (Sita) / जो (who) / जेहि (for whom) / जोगु (fit) / भाँति (manner) / तेहि (that) / तेही (same) / तापस (ascetic) / बेष (dress) / जानकी (Janaki) / देखी (seeing) / भा (became) / सबु (all) / बिकल (distressed) / बिषाद (grief) / बिसेषी (especially great)
ramacharitamanas::3384.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3384.essence: Closeness itself becomes sorrow when separation is already written on the face.
ramacharitamanas::3384.simple_meaning: Sita meets her family one by one, and each meeting fits the relationship. But when they see her dressed like an ascetic, everyone is overwhelmed with sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::3384.simple_insight: Love feels most painful when it meets separation in plain sight.
ramacharitamanas::3384.detailed_meaning: Back in Janak's court, Sita is being prepared to leave. She meets her relatives according to each bond, but her ascetic dress makes the family feel the full weight of what exile has cost them.
ramacharitamanas::3384.modern_relevance: You see someone you love at a farewell in plain clothes, carrying one small bag. No one needs to say it aloud — the whole room feels the leaving.
ramacharitamanas::3384.insight: It turns a family meeting into a moment of shared grief and makes the cost of separation visible.

ramacharitamanas::3385.verse_sanskrit: जनक राम गुर आयसु पाई। चले थलहि सिय देखी आई॥ लीन्हि लाइ उर जनक जानकी। पाहुनि पावन प्रेम प्रान की ॥
ramacharitamanas::3385.verse_hindi: जनकजी श्री रामजी के गुरु वशिष्ठजी की आज्ञा पाकर डेरे को चले और आकर उन्होंने सीताजी को देखा। जनकजी ने अपने पवित्र प्रेम और प्राणों की पाहुनी जानकीजी को हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3385.english_translation: Receiving the order from Ram's guru, Janak went to the camp and came to see Sita. Janak embraced Janaki to his heart as a sacred guest of his pure love and life.
ramacharitamanas::3385.translation_literal: जनक (Janak) / राम (Ram) / गुर (guru) / आयसु (order) / पाई (receiving) / चले (went) / थलहि (to the camp/ground) / सिय (Sita) / देखी (seeing) / आई (came) / लीन्हि (embraced/took) / लाइ (by placing) / उर (to the heart) / जनक (Janak) / जानकी (Janaki) / पाहुनि (guest) / पावन (pure) / प्रेम (love) / प्रान (life) की (of)
ramacharitamanas::3385.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3385.essence: Pure love can hold a farewell without trying to stop it.
ramacharitamanas::3385.simple_meaning: Janak comes to see Sita and embraces her with deep love, treating her as a sacred guest of his life.
ramacharitamanas::3385.simple_insight: Love can be tender, reverent, and physically close all at once.
ramacharitamanas::3385.detailed_meaning: In the camp after Sita is to depart, Janak arrives with Ram's guru's permission and sees his daughter again. Instead of clinging or protesting, he holds her to his heart with a parent's sacred love. The verse deepens the family grief before the farewell.
ramacharitamanas::3385.modern_relevance: You hug someone at the airport and both of you know this goodbye is heavier than words. Love does not always speak; sometimes it simply holds on for one more breath.
ramacharitamanas::3385.insight: It shows how affection can be expressed as reverent embrace, not possessiveness.

ramacharitamanas::3386.verse_sanskrit: उर उमगेउ अंबुधि अनुरागू। भयउ भूप मनु मनहुँ पयागू॥ सिय सनेह बटु बाढ़त जोहा। ता पर राम पेम सिसु सोहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3386.verse_hindi: उनके हृदय में (वात्सल्य) प्रेम का समुद्र उमड़ पड़ा। राजा का मन मानो प्रयाग हो गया। उस समुद्र के अंदर उन्होंने (आदि शक्ति) सीताजी के (अलौकिक) स्नेह रूपी अक्षयवट को बढ़ते हुए देखा। उस (सीताजी के प्रेम रूपी वट) पर श्री रामजी का प्रेम रूपी बालक (बाल रूप धारी भगवान) सुशोभित हो रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3386.english_translation: Love rose like an ocean in Janaka's heart. The king's mind became like Prayag. Within that ocean, he saw Sita's unfading love growing like a banyan tree, and on that love, Ram's childlike love shone beautifully.
ramacharitamanas::3386.translation_literal: उर (heart) / उमगेउ (rose up) / अंबुधि (ocean) / अनुरागू (love) / भयउ (became) / भूप (king) / मनु (mind) / मनहुँ (as if) / पयागू (Prayag) / सिय (Sita's) / सनेह (affection/love) / बटु (banyan tree) / बाढ़त (growing) / जोहा (saw) / ता पर (on that) / राम (Ram's) / पेम (love) / सिसु (child) / सोहा (shone beautifully)
ramacharitamanas::3386.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3386.essence: Love can make the heart feel vast enough to hold the sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3386.simple_meaning: Janaka's heart overflows with love as he sees Sita's deep affection for Ram and Ram's tender love for Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3386.simple_insight: Real love makes the heart feel vast, sacred, and alive.
ramacharitamanas::3386.detailed_meaning: Janaka has just arrived and seen Sita after her time in exile. In that intimate reunion, he is overwhelmed by the depth of Sita's devotion and by Ram's tender love for her. The scene is less about action than about the spiritual force of their bond.
ramacharitamanas::3386.modern_relevance: You watch two people meet after months apart, and the room changes. What you feel isn't drama — it's the quiet shock of seeing love that has survived distance.
ramacharitamanas::3386.insight: It shifts attention from outward reunion to the inner power that makes reunion sacred.

ramacharitamanas::3387.verse_sanskrit: चिरजीवी मुनि ग्यान बिकल जनु। बूड़त लहेउ बाल अवलंबनु॥ मोह मगन मति नहिं बिदेह की। महिमा सिय रघुबर सनेह की ॥
ramacharitamanas::3387.verse_hindi: जनकजी का ज्ञान रूपी चिरंजीवी (मार्कण्डेय) मुनि व्याकुल होकर डूबते-डूबते मानो उस श्री राम प्रेम रूपी बालक का सहारा पाकर बच गया। वस्तुतः (ज्ञानिशिरोमणि) विदेहराज की बुद्धि मोह में मग्न नहीं है। यह तो श्री सीता-रामजी के प्रेम की महिमा है (जिसने उन जैसे महान ज्ञानी के ज्ञान को भी विकल कर दिया) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3387.english_translation: The sage of endless life, though wise, was as if drowning and found a childlike support. Janaka's mind was not lost in delusion; this was the greatness of Sita and Raghubar's love.
ramacharitamanas::3387.translation_literal: चिरजीवी (endlessly living) / मुनि (sage) / ग्यान (wisdom) / बिकल (distressed) / जनु (as if) / बूड़त (drowning) / लहेउ (found) / बाल (childlike) / अवलंबनु (support) / मोह (delusion) / मगन (absorbed) / मति (mind) / नहिं (not) / बिदेह की (of Videha/Janaka) / महिमा (greatness) / सिय (Sita) / रघुबर (Raghubar/Ram) / सनेह (love) की (of)
ramacharitamanas::3387.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3387.essence: Love can move even the wisest mind beyond its usual control.
ramacharitamanas::3387.simple_meaning: Even Janaka, a great sage-king, is overwhelmed by Sita and Ram's love. His confusion is not ignorance; it is the force of devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3387.simple_insight: There is relief in knowing that being moved by love is not weakness.
ramacharitamanas::3387.detailed_meaning: Janaka has just come to see Sita, and the sight of her opens a flood of feeling. Tulsidas says that even a mind as steady as Janaka's seems to drown and then find support again, showing that Sita and Ram's love can overwhelm wisdom itself.
ramacharitamanas::3387.modern_relevance: You thought you had yourself together, then one message from someone you love undid you completely. That collapse may not be failure; it may be the depth of what truly matters.
ramacharitamanas::3387.insight: It shifts the mind from treating emotional overwhelm as weakness to seeing it as devotion's power.

ramacharitamanas::3388.verse_sanskrit: सिय पितु मातु सनेह बस बिकल न सकी सँभारि। धरनिसुताँ धीरजु धरेउ समउ सुधरमु बिचारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3388.verse_hindi: पिता-माता के प्रेम के मारे सीताजी ऐसी विकल हो गईं कि अपने को सँभाल न सकीं। (परन्तु परम धैर्यवती) पृथ्वी की कन्या सीताजी ने समय और सुंदर धर्म का विचार कर धैर्य धारण किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3388.english_translation: Overcome by love for her father and mother, Sita could not steady herself. Yet the daughter of the earth held her patience, considering the time and the demands of right conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3388.translation_literal: सिय (Sita) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / सनेह (love) / बस (under the control of) / बिकल (distressed) / न (not) / सकी (could) / सँभारि (steady herself) / धरनिसुताँ (daughter of the earth) / धीरजु (patience) / धरेउ (held) / समउ (time) / सुधरमु (right conduct) / बिचारि (considering)
ramacharitamanas::3388.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3388.essence: Love can shake you without taking away your steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::3388.simple_meaning: Sita is overwhelmed by love for her parents, but she regains herself by choosing patience and right conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3388.simple_insight: You can be deeply moved without being ruled by the feeling.
ramacharitamanas::3388.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Sita is overwhelmed by affection for her father and mother as the moment of her departure nears. For an instant she nearly loses composure, then she remembers timing and right conduct and steadies herself.
ramacharitamanas::3388.modern_relevance: You are crying in the car after a family goodbye, and your chest feels too full to breathe. Even then, you can gather yourself and do what is right.
ramacharitamanas::3388.insight: It teaches emotional steadiness: feel the wave fully, then choose the response that fits the moment.

ramacharitamanas::3389.verse_sanskrit: तापस बेष जनक सिय देखी। भयउ पेमु परितोषु बिसेषी॥ पुत्रि पबित्र किए कुल दोऊ। सुजस धवल जगु कह सबु कोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3389.verse_hindi: सीताजी को तपस्विनी वेष में देखकर जनकजी को विशेष प्रेम और संतोष हुआ। (उन्होंने कहा-) बेटी! तूने दोनों कुल पवित्र कर दिए। तेरे निर्मल यश से सारा जगत उज्ज्वल हो रहा है, ऐसा सब कोई कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3389.english_translation: Seeing Sita in the dress of an ascetic, Janaka felt special love and deep satisfaction. "Daughter, you have purified both families. Your spotless fame brightens the whole world," everyone says.
ramacharitamanas::3389.translation_literal: तापस बेष (ascetic dress) / जनक (Janaka) / सिय (Sita) / देखी (seeing) / भयउ (became) / पेमु (love) / परितोषु (satisfaction) / बिसेषी (special)॥ / पुत्रि (daughter) / पबित्र (pure) / किए (made) / कुल (families) / दोऊ (both)॥ / सुजस (good fame) / धवल (white/spotless) / जगु (world) / कह (says) / सबु (all) / कोऊ (everyone)॥
ramacharitamanas::3389.speaker: Janaka
ramacharitamanas::3389.essence: True greatness makes both your home and the world brighter.
ramacharitamanas::3389.simple_meaning: Janaka sees Sita in ascetic dress and feels deep joy. He praises her for bringing honor to both families and for making her reputation pure and radiant.
ramacharitamanas::3389.simple_insight: A life lived with dignity can bless far beyond your own home.
ramacharitamanas::3389.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, Sita appears in the dress of an ascetic. Her father does not see loss; he sees greatness. Overcome with love and pride, he praises her for purifying both families and for the spotless fame that now spreads through the world.
ramacharitamanas::3389.modern_relevance: You watch your daughter walk into a room in simple clothes, calm and unshowy, and feel something in you settle. Her character is speaking louder than any display ever could.
ramacharitamanas::3389.insight: It shifts attention from outward appearance to the quiet power of character and family honor.

ramacharitamanas::3390.verse_sanskrit: जिति सुरसरि कीरति सरि तोरी। गवनु कीन्ह बिधि अंड करोरी॥ गंग अवनि थल तीनि बड़ेरे। एहिं किए साधु समाज घनेरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3390.verse_hindi: तेरी कीर्ति रूपी नदी देवनदी गंगाजी को भी जीतकर (जो एक ही ब्रह्माण्ड में बहती है) करोड़ों ब्रह्माण्डों में बह चली है। गंगाजी ने तो पृथ्वी पर तीन ही स्थानों (हरिद्वार, प्रयागराज और गंगासागर) को बड़ा (तीर्थ) बनाया है। पर तेरी इस कीर्ति नदी ने तो अनेकों संत समाज रूपी तीर्थ स्थान बना दिए हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3390.english_translation: Your fame has crossed even the Ganga and spread through countless worlds. The Ganga makes only three great holy places on earth, but your fame has made many communities of saints into holy places.
ramacharitamanas::3390.translation_literal: जिति (having conquered) / सुरसरि (the river of the devas, Ganga) / कीरति सरि (river of fame) / तोरी (crossed) / गवनु (movement, going) / कीन्ह (made) / बिधि (by Brahma's order / destiny) / अंड करोरी (crores of cosmic eggs / countless universes) / गंग (Ganga) / अवनि (earth) / थल (places) / तीनि (three) / बड़ेरे (made great) / एहिं (by this) / किए (made) / साधु समाज (assembly of saints) / घनेरे (many, abundant)
ramacharitamanas::3390.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3390.essence: A pure life makes whole communities feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3390.simple_meaning: Your praise has spread beyond ordinary limits and made many gatherings of holy people sacred. Even the Ganga seems smaller beside the reach of your fame.
ramacharitamanas::3390.simple_insight: A life rooted in virtue can bless far beyond what you can see.
ramacharitamanas::3390.detailed_meaning: Janak is speaking after seeing Sita in a renunciate form and feeling deep pride and tenderness. He praises her fame as something vast enough to surpass the Ganga itself, saying her presence has turned many saintly gatherings into holy places.
ramacharitamanas::3390.modern_relevance: You show up for a grieving friend, and the room feels calmer the moment you enter. No speech, no spotlight — just a steady way of being that changes the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::3390.insight: It shifts attention from personal achievement to the quiet power of a life that elevates everyone around it.

ramacharitamanas::3391.verse_sanskrit: पितु कह सत्य सनेहँ सुबानी। सीय सकुच महुँ मनहुँ समानी॥ पुनि पितु मातु लीन्हि उर लाई। सिख आसिष हित दीन्हि सुहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3391.verse_hindi: पिता जनकजी ने तो स्नेह से सच्ची सुंदर वाणी कही, परन्तु अपनी बड़ाई सुनकर सीताजी मानो संकोच में समा गईं। पिता-माता ने उन्हें फिर हृदय से लगा लिया और हितभरी सुंदर सीख और आशीष दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3391.english_translation: Janak spoke true and lovingly; Sita sank into modest silence. Then her parents drew her close again and gave her loving counsel and blessings.
ramacharitamanas::3391.translation_literal: पितु (father) / कह (spoke) / सत्य (true) / सनेहँ (with love) / सुबानी (sweet words) / सीय (Sita) / सकुच (shyness) / महुँ (within) / मनहुँ (as if) / समानी (merged) / पुनि (again) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / लीन्हि (took) / उर (to the heart) / लाई (having brought) / सिख (counsel) / आसिष (blessings) / हित (for welfare) / दीन्हि (gave) / सुहाई (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::3391.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3391.essence: True affection praises you without making you feel exposed.
ramacharitamanas::3391.simple_meaning: Janak praises Sita with loving words, but she grows shy. Her parents embrace her again and bless her with kind advice.
ramacharitamanas::3391.simple_insight: Love can be gentle enough to make even praise feel humbling.
ramacharitamanas::3391.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Janak has just honored Sita for her purity and grace. The moment is tender rather than triumphant: Sita turns shy under her father's praise, and both parents hold her close, offering affection, guidance, and blessings before the next step in her life.
ramacharitamanas::3391.modern_relevance: Your parent says something proud about you in front of relatives, and you suddenly want the floor to open. That mix of love, embarrassment, and reassurance feels exactly like this moment.
ramacharitamanas::3391.insight: It shows how praise, when rooted in love, can still leave room for humility and care.

ramacharitamanas::3392.verse_sanskrit: कहति न सीय सकुचि मन माहीं। इहाँ बसब रजनीं भल नाहीं॥ लखि रुख रानि जनायउ राऊ। हृदयँ सराहत सीलु सुभाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3392.verse_hindi: सीताजी कुछ कहती नहीं हैं, परन्तु सकुचा रही हैं कि रात में (सासुओं की सेवा छोड़कर) यहाँ रहना अच्छा नहीं है। रानी सुनयनाजी ने जानकीजी का रुख देखकर (उनके मन की बात समझकर) राजा जनकजी को जना दिया। तब दोनों अपने हृदयों में सीताजी के शील और स्वभाव की सराहना करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3392.english_translation: Sita says nothing, but in her heart she feels shy: staying here at night is not right. Seeing her mood, Queen Sunaina told King Janaka. Then both of them praised Sita's modesty and gentle nature in their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::3392.translation_literal: कहति (speaks) / न (not) / सीय (Sita) / सकुचि (with shyness) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / इहाँ (here) / बसब (to stay) / रजनीं (at night) / भल (good) / नाहीं (not) / लखि (seeing) / रुख (mood/attitude) / रानि (queen) / जनायउ (made known) / राऊ (king) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / सराहत (praising) / सीलु (modesty/virtue) / सुभाऊ (nature/disposition)
ramacharitamanas::3392.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3392.essence: True refinement is felt before it is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3392.simple_meaning: Sita stays quiet, but her hesitation is clear. Sunaina understands her feeling and tells Janaka, and both parents admire Sita's modest, gracious nature.
ramacharitamanas::3392.simple_insight: Quiet dignity can speak louder than words.
ramacharitamanas::3392.detailed_meaning: At Janaka's home, Sita has been welcomed with honor, but night is approaching and she feels shy about staying away from the women she serves. Sunaina notices her restraint, tells Janaka, and both parents quietly admire her character.
ramacharitamanas::3392.modern_relevance: You sit at a dinner table where everyone is urging you to stay longer, but your body says it's time to leave. Someone who loves you notices the hesitation without making it awkward.
ramacharitamanas::3392.insight: It trains you to notice unspoken discomfort and honor it with grace.

ramacharitamanas::3393.verse_sanskrit: बार बार मिलि भेंटि सिय बिदा कीन्हि सनमानि। कही समय सिर भरत गति रानि सुबानि सयानि ॥
