ramacharitamanas::3393.verse_hindi: राजा-रानी ने बार-बार मिलकर और हृदय से लगाकर तथा सम्मान करके सीताजी को विदा किया। चतुर रानी ने समय पाकर राजा से सुंदर वाणी में भरतजी की दशा का वर्णन किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3393.english_translation: The king and queen repeatedly met Sita, embraced her, and sent her off with honour. Then the wise queen spoke at the right time, beautifully describing Bharata's condition to the king.
ramacharitamanas::3393.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / मिलि (meeting) / भेंटि (embracing) / सिय (Sita) / बिदा (farewell) / कीन्हि (made) / सनमानि (with honour) / कही (spoke) / समय (at the right time) / सिर भरत गति (Bharata's condition) / रानि (queen) / सुबानि (beautiful speech) / सयानि (wise)
ramacharitamanas::3393.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3393.essence: Kindness and timing can soften even a painful parting.
ramacharitamanas::3393.simple_meaning: Sita is sent away with love and respect, and Queen Sunaina then speaks wisely about Bharata's situation.
ramacharitamanas::3393.simple_insight: Care and timing matter as much as the words themselves.
ramacharitamanas::3393.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the family is parting from Sita with affection and honour. Queen Sunaina then uses the moment to speak wisely to the king about Bharata, preparing the ground for the next emotional turn in the scene.
ramacharitamanas::3393.modern_relevance: You wait until the room is calm, then say the hard thing kindly. The timing of a truth can change everything.
ramacharitamanas::3393.insight: It shows how respect and good timing can carry a difficult message without harshness.

ramacharitamanas::3394.verse_sanskrit: सुनि भूपाल भरत ब्यवहारू। सोन सुगंध सुधा ससि सारू॥ मूदे सजन नयन पुलके तन। सुजसु सराहन लगे मुदित मन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3394.verse_hindi: सोने में सुगंध और (समुद्र से निकली हुई) सुधा में चन्द्रमा के सार अमृत के समान भरतजी का व्यवहार सुनकर राजा ने (प्रेम विह्वल होकर) अपने (प्रेमाश्रुओं के) जल से भरे नेत्रों को मूँद लिया (वे भरतजी के प्रेम में मानो ध्यानस्थ हो गए)। वे शरीर से पुलकित हो गए और मन में आनंदित होकर भरतजी के सुंदर यश की सराहना करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3394.english_translation: Hearing of Bharat's conduct, the king's heart filled with wonder. Like fragrance in gold and nectar in the moon, Bharat's character seemed even more precious. His eyes closed in love, his body thrilled, and his mind delighted as he praised Bharat's good fame.
ramacharitamanas::3394.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / भूपाल (the king) / भरत (Bharat) / ब्यवहारू (conduct, manner of conduct) / सोन (gold) / सुगंध (fragrance) / सुधा (nectar) / ससि (moon) / सारू (essence, finest part) / मूदे (closed) / सजन (moistened, filled) / नयन (eyes) / पुलके (bristled with thrill) / तन (body) / सुजसु (good fame) / सराहन (to praise) / लगे (began) / मुदित (delighted) / मन (mind)
ramacharitamanas::3394.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3394.essence: Bharat's character is so rare it feels like treasure inside treasure.
ramacharitamanas::3394.simple_meaning: The king hears about Bharat's character and is overwhelmed with joy and admiration. Bharat's conduct seems as rare and precious as fragrance in gold or nectar in the moon.
ramacharitamanas::3394.simple_insight: A truly noble life can move even a listener into reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3394.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's renunciation has begun to reveal its moral weight. Hearing of his conduct, the king is overcome with emotion: his eyes close, his body shivers, and he praises Bharat's fame. This verse pauses the story to honor Bharat's character.
ramacharitamanas::3394.modern_relevance: You hear how someone gave up comfort to keep a promise, and suddenly your own complaints feel small. Real character can silence a room without raising its voice.
ramacharitamanas::3394.insight: It shifts attention from what people possess to the quality of how they live.

ramacharitamanas::3395.verse_sanskrit: सावधान सुनु सुमुखि सुलोचनि। भरत कथा भव बंध बिमोचनि॥ धरम राजनय ब्रह्मबिचारू। इहाँ जथामति मोर प्रचारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3395.verse_hindi: (वे बोले-) हे सुमुखि! हे सुनयनी! सावधान होकर सुनो। भरतजी की कथा संसार के बंधन से छुड़ाने वाली है। धर्म, राजनीति और ब्रह्मविचार- इन तीनों विषयों में अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार मेरी (थोड़ी-बहुत) गति है (अर्थात इनके संबंध में मैं कुछ जानता हूँ) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3395.english_translation: (He said:) O graceful and bright-eyed one, listen carefully. The story of Bharat frees you from the bonds of the world. In dharma, politics, and spiritual reflection, I have some understanding according to my own measure.
ramacharitamanas::3395.translation_literal: सावधान (carefully) / सुनु (listen) / सुमुखि (O graceful-faced one) / सुलोचनि (O bright-eyed one) / भरत कथा (the story of Bharat) / भव (of the world) / बंध (bonds) / बिमोचनि (freeing)॥ / धरम (dharma) / राजनय (statecraft) / ब्रह्मबिचारू (reflection on the supreme reality) / इहाँ (here) / जथामति (according to my measure) / मोर (my) / प्रचारू (understanding / reach)॥
ramacharitamanas::3395.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3395.essence: Bharat's story is meant to free you, not just inform you.
ramacharitamanas::3395.simple_meaning: Bharat's story is presented as deeply freeing. The speaker says he understands enough about duty, leadership, and spiritual reflection to begin telling it.
ramacharitamanas::3395.simple_insight: A true story can loosen the grip of attachment and make you see what matters.
ramacharitamanas::3395.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the narrator turns to Parvati and prepares her for Bharat's story. He says it can free the mind from worldly bondage, and he frames his own telling as limited but sincere, touching dharma, rule, and spiritual reflection.
ramacharitamanas::3395.modern_relevance: You hear a friend begin a story by saying, 'This one changed me.' Before the details even start, you feel that something in you may need to shift too.
ramacharitamanas::3395.insight: It frames Bharat's life as a teaching story, not just a family episode, and invites the listener into a freer way of seeing duty and renunciation.

ramacharitamanas::3396.verse_sanskrit: सो मति मोरि भरत महिमाही। कहै काह छलि छुअति न छाँही॥ बिधि गनपति अहिपति सिव सारद। कबि कोबिद बुध बुद्धि बिसारद ॥
ramacharitamanas::3396.verse_hindi: वह (धर्म, राजनीति और ब्रह्मज्ञान में प्रवेश रखने वाली) मेरी बुद्धि भरतजी की महिमा का वर्णन तो क्या करे, छल करके भी उसकी छाया तक को नहीं छू पाती! ब्रह्माजी, गणेशजी, शेषजी, महादेवजी, सरस्वतीजी, कवि, ज्ञानी, पण्डित और बुद्धिमान- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3396.english_translation: My mind can never describe Bharat's greatness. Even in deceit, it cannot touch even his shadow. Brahma, Ganesha, Shesha, Shiva, Saraswati, poets, sages, scholars, and the wise...
ramacharitamanas::3396.translation_literal: सो (that) / मति (mind, understanding) / मोरि (my) / भरत (Bharat) / महिमाही (greatness, glory) / कहै (to speak) / काह (what) / छलि (by deceit) / छुअति (touches) / न (not) / छाँही (shadow) / बिधि (Brahma) / गनपति (Ganesha) / अहिपति (Shesha, lord of serpents) / सिव (Shiva) / सारद (Saraswati) / कबि (poets) / कोबिद (the learned) / बुध (the wise) / बुद्धि (intelligence) / बिसारद (skilled, expert)
ramacharitamanas::3396.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3396.essence: Bharat's greatness is so pure that even thought falls short.
ramacharitamanas::3396.simple_meaning: Bharat's greatness is beyond ordinary understanding. Even the speaker's own mind cannot fully describe it, and only the greatest beings and wisest minds can begin to approach it.
ramacharitamanas::3396.simple_insight: Real devotion makes a person larger than explanation. You feel reverence before you can fully understand why.
ramacharitamanas::3396.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the narrator pauses after praising Bharat's conduct and warns Parvati that even his carefully trained mind cannot capture Bharat's glory. He then invokes Brahma, Ganesha, Shesha, Shiva, Saraswati, poets, sages, and scholars as witnesses to how hard Bharat is to describe.
ramacharitamanas::3396.modern_relevance: You meet someone who quietly keeps a promise no one else would notice. When you try to explain why that loyalty moves you, words feel too small. Bharat's example has that kind of weight.
ramacharitamanas::3396.insight: It shifts you from measuring worth by cleverness to recognising the depth of lived devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3397.verse_sanskrit: भरत चरित कीरति करतूती। धरम सील गुन बिमल बिभूती॥ समुझत सुनत सुखद सब काहू। सुचि सुरसरि रुचि निदर सुधाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3397.verse_hindi: सब किसी को भरतजी के चरित्र, कीर्ति, करनी, धर्म, शील, गुण और निर्मल ऐश्वर्य समझने में और सुनने में सुख देने वाले हैं और पवित्रता में गंगाजी का तथा स्वाद (मधुरता) में अमृत का भी तिरस्कार करने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3397.english_translation: Bharat’s character, fame, deeds, righteousness, restraint, virtues, and spotless excellence are pleasing to understand and hear. In purity, they surpass the Ganges; in sweetness, they outshine even nectar.
ramacharitamanas::3397.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / चरित (character) / कीरति (fame) / करतूती (deeds) / धरम (righteousness) / सील (restraint, virtue) / गुन (qualities) / बिमल (spotless) / बिभूती (splendor, excellence) / समुझत (understanding) / सुनत (hearing) / सुखद (giving joy) / सब काहू (to everyone) / सुचि (pure) / सुरसरि (Ganges) / रुचि (sweetness) / निदर (surpassing, putting aside) / सुधाहू (even nectar)
ramacharitamanas::3397.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3397.essence: Bharat’s virtue is so pure it becomes its own reward.
ramacharitamanas::3397.simple_meaning: Bharat’s character is so noble that hearing about him brings joy. His purity and virtue are described as greater than the Ganges and even sweeter than nectar.
ramacharitamanas::3397.simple_insight: There is peace in meeting a life that needs no exaggeration to shine.
ramacharitamanas::3397.detailed_meaning: After praising Bharat’s story as liberating and beyond ordinary speech, the narrator pauses on Bharat himself. His character, reputation, conduct, and virtues are so refined that simply hearing about them gives delight. The verse crowns him as a model of moral beauty.
ramacharitamanas::3397.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose integrity needs no announcement: they show up, keep faith, and leave a room calmer. Later, people speak of them with the same quiet admiration this verse gives Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::3397.insight: It shifts attention from status to character, showing that true excellence is felt in the way a life affects others.

ramacharitamanas::3398.verse_sanskrit: निरवधि गुन निरुपम पुरुषु भरतु भरत सम जानि। कहिअ सुमेरु कि सेर सम कबिकुल मति सकुचानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3398.verse_hindi: भरतजी असीम गुण सम्पन्न और उपमारहित पुरुष हैं। भरतजी के समान बस, भरतजी ही हैं, ऐसा जानो। सुमेरु पर्वत को क्या सेर के बराबर कह सकते हैं? इसलिए (उन्हें किसी पुरुष के साथ उपमा देने में) कवि समाज की बुद्धि भी सकुचा गई! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3398.english_translation: Bharat is a person of limitless virtues, beyond comparison. Bharat can only be known as Bharat himself. Can Mount Sumeru be measured against a seer? Even the minds of poets shrink back from making such a comparison.
ramacharitamanas::3398.translation_literal: निरवधि (limitless) / गुन (virtues) / निरुपम (without comparison) / पुरुषु (person) / भरतु (Bharat) / भरत सम (equal to Bharat) / जानि (knowing) / कहिअ (can be said) / सुमेरु (Mount Sumeru) / कि (whether) / सेर सम (equal to a seer) / कबिकुल (poets' group) / मति (mind/intelligence) / सकुचानि (shrinks back)
ramacharitamanas::3398.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3398.essence: True greatness cannot be measured by comparison.
ramacharitamanas::3398.simple_meaning: Bharat's virtues are so vast that no comparison fits him. Even poets feel hesitant trying to measure him against anyone else.
ramacharitamanas::3398.simple_insight: Some people are so complete that comparison only makes them smaller.
ramacharitamanas::3398.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the speaker is praising Bharat's character after describing his fame, conduct, and purity. The point is not to rank him above others, but to say his greatness cannot be measured by ordinary standards.
ramacharitamanas::3398.modern_relevance: You meet someone who quietly carries more grace than any title can show. The urge to rank them, label them, or compare them feels clumsy and inadequate.
ramacharitamanas::3398.insight: It shifts the mind away from comparison and toward reverence for character that cannot be reduced to a scale.

ramacharitamanas::3399.verse_sanskrit: अगम सबहि बरनत बरबरनी। जिमि जलहीन मीन गमु धरनी॥ भरत अमित महिमा सुनु रानी। जानहिं रामु न सकहिं बखानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3399.verse_hindi: हे श्रेष्ठ वर्णवाली! भरतजी की महिमा का वर्णन करना सभी के लिए वैसे ही अगम है जैसे जलरहित पृथ्वी पर मछली का चलना। हे रानी! सुनो, भरतजी की अपरिमित महिमा को एक श्री रामचन्द्रजी ही जानते हैं, किन्तु वे भी उसका वर्णन नहीं कर सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::3399.english_translation: O noble lady, the greatness of Bharat is beyond description, like a fish on dry land. O queen, only Ram knows Bharat's limitless glory, yet even Ram cannot fully describe it.
ramacharitamanas::3399.translation_literal: अगम (beyond reach) / सबहि (for all) / बरनत (describing) / बरबरनी (best of the describers) / जिमि (like) / जलहीन (without water) / मीन (fish) / गमु (movement) / धरनी (earth) / भरत (Bharat) / अमित (limitless) / महिमा (glory) / सुनु (listen) / रानी (queen) / जानहिं (knows) / रामु (Ram) / न (not) / सकहिं (can) / बखानी (describe)
ramacharitamanas::3399.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3399.essence: Bharat's greatness is so deep that even praise cannot contain it.
ramacharitamanas::3399.simple_meaning: Bharat's greatness is beyond ordinary description. Even Ram alone fully knows it, yet its full measure cannot be put into words.
ramacharitamanas::3399.simple_insight: Real devotion can make a life so vast that praise itself falls short.
ramacharitamanas::3399.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the narrator pauses the grief and politics to praise Bharat's character. His virtue is so immense that no ordinary speaker can measure it. Even Ram understands him completely, yet still cannot exhaust his greatness in words.
ramacharitamanas::3399.modern_relevance: You try to explain why a certain friend stayed loyal when everything would have rewarded betrayal. The explanation feels too small. Some people are larger than the language you have for them.
ramacharitamanas::3399.insight: It shifts attention from public reputation to the hidden depth of character that only love can truly know.

ramacharitamanas::3400.verse_sanskrit: बरनि सप्रेम भरत अनुभाऊ। तिय जिय की रुचि लखि कह राऊ॥ बहुरहिं लखनु भरतु बन जाहीं। सब कर भल सब के मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3400.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार प्रेमपूर्वक भरतजी के प्रभाव का वर्णन करके, फिर पत्नी के मन की रुचि जानकर राजा ने कहा- लक्ष्मणजी लौट जाएँ और भरतजी वन को जाएँ, इसमें सभी का भला है और यही सबके मन में है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3400.english_translation: After lovingly describing Bharat's greatness, the king saw his wife's wish and said, 'Let Lakshman return and let Bharat go to the forest; that would be best for everyone, and that is what everyone wants in their heart.'
ramacharitamanas::3400.translation_literal: बरनि (describing) / सप्रेम (with love) / भरत (Bharat) / अनुभाऊ (influence, greatness) / तिय (wife) / जिय (heart) / की (of) / रुचि (wish, liking) / लखि (seeing, noticing) / कह (said) / राऊ (the king)॥ / बहुरहिं (let return) / लखनु (Lakshman) / भरतु (Bharat) / बन (forest) / जाहीं (go) / सब (all) / कर (of) / भल (good) / सबे (everyone's) / के (of) / मन (mind) / माहीं (in) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3400.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3400.essence: The king tries to heal a wound by naming the wish already living in the family.
ramacharitamanas::3400.simple_meaning: The king, sensing his wife's feelings, says Lakshman should return and Bharat should go to the forest. He believes this would be best for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3400.simple_insight: Sometimes a family crisis is so tangled that even a king can only speak from the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3400.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the king is trying to ease a painful family conflict after Ram's exile. He speaks with affection about Bharat and then, reading his wife's mind, proposes a reversal that sounds impossible. The verse is a supporting step in the larger emotional argument.
ramacharitamanas::3400.modern_relevance: You are in a tense family group chat, trying to say the one thing that might calm everyone down. The real issue is not logic — it's reading what each person is carrying.
ramacharitamanas::3400.insight: It shows how public decisions are often shaped by hidden feelings in the room.

ramacharitamanas::3401.verse_sanskrit: देबि परन्तु भरत रघुबर की। प्रीति प्रतीति जाइ नहिं तरकी॥ भरतु अवधि सनेह ममता की। जद्यपि रामु सीम समता की ॥
ramacharitamanas::3401.verse_hindi: परन्तु हे देवि! भरतजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी का प्रेम और एक-दूसरे पर विश्वास, बुद्धि और विचार की सीमा में नहीं आ सकता। यद्यपि श्री रामचन्द्रजी समता की सीमा हैं, तथापि भरतजी प्रेम और ममता की सीमा हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3401.english_translation: O goddess, Bharata's love for Raghubara and their mutual trust cannot be measured by reason or thought. Though Ram is the limit of perfect equality, Bharata is the limit of love and affection.
ramacharitamanas::3401.translation_literal: देबि (O goddess) / परन्तु (but) / भरत (Bharata) / रघुबर की (of Raghubara) / प्रीति (love) / प्रतीति (trust) / जाइ (goes) / नहिं (not) / तरकी (by reasoning) / भरतु (Bharata) / अवधि (limit) / सनेह (affection) / ममता (clinging love) की (of) / जद्यपि (although) / रामु (Ram) / सीम (limit) / समता (equality) की (of)
ramacharitamanas::3401.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3401.essence: True devotion cannot be measured, only lived.
ramacharitamanas::3401.simple_meaning: Bharata's love and trust in Ram cannot be measured by logic. Ram remains perfectly even-hearted, while Bharata becomes the limit of loving devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3401.simple_insight: Some bonds are too deep for explanation; they are known by their steadiness, not by arguments.
ramacharitamanas::3401.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court is still living with the wound of exile. The speaker turns to Bharata and Ram as the clearest example of devotion and trust: Ram's evenness never wavers, and Bharata's love cannot be contained by ordinary reasoning.
ramacharitamanas::3401.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone who cannot fully explain why they matter so much. The relationship stops being about logic and becomes a quiet proof of loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::3401.insight: It shifts attention from proving love to embodying it. The bond becomes something lived, not argued.

ramacharitamanas::3402.verse_sanskrit: परमारथ स्वारथ सुख सारे। भरत न सपनेहुँ मनहुँ निहारे॥ साधन सिद्धि राम पग नेहू। मोहि लखि परत भरत मत एहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3402.verse_hindi: (श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्रति अनन्य प्रेम को छोड़कर) भरतजी ने समस्त परमार्थ, स्वार्थ और सुखों की ओर स्वप्न में भी मन से भी नहीं ताका है। श्री रामजी के चरणों का प्रेम ही उनका साधन है और वही सिद्धि है। मुझे तो भरतजी का बस, यही एक मात्र सिद्धांत जान पड़ता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3402.english_translation: Bharat has never even dreamed of seeking worldly gain, selfish gain, or pleasure. Love for Ram's feet is his means and his fulfillment. In my view, that is Bharat's only principle.
ramacharitamanas::3402.translation_literal: परमारथ (highest good) / स्वारथ (selfish gain) / सुख (pleasures) / सारे (all) / भरत (Bharat) / न (not) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / मनहुँ (even in the mind) / निहारे (looked at) ॥ साधन (means) / सिद्धि (fulfillment) / राम (Ram) / पग (feet) / नेहू (love) / मोहि (to me) / लखि (seeing) / परत (appears) / भरत (Bharat) / मत (view / principle) / एहू (this) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3402.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3402.essence: Love for Ram becomes both the path and the reward.
ramacharitamanas::3402.simple_meaning: Bharat has no interest in personal gain or pleasure. Loving Ram is both his path and his fulfillment.
ramacharitamanas::3402.simple_insight: Real contentment comes when love itself becomes enough.
ramacharitamanas::3402.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court is trying to understand Bharat’s heart after Ram’s exile. The king sees that Bharat has no appetite for profit, comfort, or status. His only aim is loving service to Ram, and that love is both the road and the destination.
ramacharitamanas::3402.modern_relevance: You turn down the promotion, the applause, and the shortcut because they would pull you away from what you love. Bharat shows what it looks like when devotion is more satisfying than winning.
ramacharitamanas::3402.insight: It shifts your priorities from acquisition to wholehearted devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3403.verse_sanskrit: भोरेहुँ भरत न पेलिहहिं मनसहुँ राम रजाइ। करिअ न सोचु सनेह बस कहेउ भूप बिलखाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3403.verse_hindi: राजा ने बिलखकर (प्रेम से गद्गद होकर) कहा- भरतजी भूलकर भी श्री रामचन्द्रजी की आज्ञा को मन से भी नहीं टालेंगे। अतः स्नेह के वश होकर चिंता नहीं करनी चाहिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3403.english_translation: The king, overcome with emotion, said, "Bharat will not even in the slightest disobey Ram's command. Do not worry out of love."
ramacharitamanas::3403.translation_literal: भोरेहुँ (even by mistake) / भरत (Bharat) / न (not) / पेलिहहिं (will push aside, will disobey) / मनसहुँ (even in the mind) / राम (Ram's) / रजाइ (command) / करिअ (do) / न (not) / सोचु (worry) / सनेह (love) / बस (because of) / कहेउ (said) / भूप (the king) / बिलखाइ (weeping)
ramacharitamanas::3403.speaker: Dasharath
ramacharitamanas::3403.essence: Love that is true does not need suspicion.
ramacharitamanas::3403.simple_meaning: Dasharath says Bharat will never even mentally go against Ram's command, so no one should worry out of affection.
ramacharitamanas::3403.simple_insight: Real love does not keep testing loyalty. It learns to rest in trust.
ramacharitamanas::3403.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Dasharath is weeping as he speaks about Bharat's devotion and Ram's command. The family is shattered by exile, yet the king wants everyone to know Bharat's heart is completely aligned with Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3403.modern_relevance: You keep replaying the text, wondering whether your friend will stay loyal or your partner will understand. This verse softens that fear: true love does not rush to suspicion.
ramacharitamanas::3403.insight: It shifts the mind from anxious doubt to steady trust in another's devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3404.verse_sanskrit: राम भरत गुन गनत सप्रीती। निसि दंपतिहि पलक सम बीती॥ राज समाज प्रात जुग जागे। न्हाइ न्हाइ सुर पूजन लागे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3404.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी और भरतजी के गुणों की प्रेमपूर्वक गणना करते (कहते-सुनते) पति-पत्नी को रात पलक के समान बीत गई। प्रातःकाल दोनों राजसमाज जागे और नहा-नहाकर देवताओं की पूजा करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3404.english_translation: As Ram and Bharat’s virtues were lovingly counted, the night passed like a blink for the couple. At dawn, the royal assembly awoke, bathed, and began worshipping the radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::3404.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / भरत (Bharat) / गुन (virtues) / गनत (counting) / सप्रीती (with love) / निसि (night) / दंपतिहि (for the couple) / पलक सम (like a blink) / बीती (passed) // राज समाज (royal assembly) / प्रात (morning) / जुग (both) / जागे (awoke) / न्हाइ न्हाइ (bathing again and again) / सुर (radiant beings) / पूजन (worship) / लागे (began)
ramacharitamanas::3404.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3404.essence: Love for Ram and Bharat makes sorrow feel brief.
ramacharitamanas::3404.simple_meaning: Ram and Bharat’s qualities are so dear that talking about them makes the night pass quickly. By morning, everyone is awake, bathed, and ready to worship.
ramacharitamanas::3404.simple_insight: Love makes time disappear, and devotion turns even an ordinary morning into a fresh beginning.
ramacharitamanas::3404.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the grief and tension around Ram’s exile, the royal household settles into a quieter morning. People spend the night lovingly speaking of Ram and Bharat’s virtues, then rise, bathe, and begin worship before the next meeting with the teacher and the court.
ramacharitamanas::3404.modern_relevance: You stay up late with family, remembering the person everyone misses most. Morning comes, and even the silence feels gentler because love was spoken aloud.
ramacharitamanas::3404.insight: It shows how shared remembrance softens grief and prepares the mind for right action.

ramacharitamanas::3405.verse_sanskrit: गे नहाइ गुर पहिं रघुराई। बंदि चरन बोले रुख पाई॥ नाथ भरतु पुरजन महतारी। सोक बिकल बनबास दुखारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3405.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी स्नान करके गुरु वशिष्ठजी के पास गए और चरणों की वंदना करके उनका रुख पाकर बोले- हे नाथ! भरत, अवधपुर वासी तथा माताएँ, सब शोक से व्याकुल और वनवास से दुःखी हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3405.english_translation: After bathing, Rama went to Guru Vashishtha. Bowing at his feet, he spoke after seeing his mood: "Lord, Bharata, the people of Ayodhya, and the mothers are all shaken with grief and pained by exile."
ramacharitamanas::3405.translation_literal: गे (went) / नहाइ (after bathing) / गुर पहिं (to the guru) / रघुराई (Rama) / बंदि (bowing) / चरन (feet) / बोले (spoke) / रुख पाई (having seen the mood)॥ / नाथ (lord) / भरतु (Bharata) / पुरजन (townspeople) / महतारी (mothers) / सोक (grief) / बिकल (distressed) / बनबास (forest exile) / दुखारी (suffering)
ramacharitamanas::3405.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3405.essence: Before asking for help, Rama names everyone’s suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3405.simple_meaning: Rama bows to his teacher and reports that Bharata, the people of Ayodhya, and the mothers are all suffering from grief and exile.
ramacharitamanas::3405.simple_insight: Even the noblest return starts with honest concern for everyone who is hurting.
ramacharitamanas::3405.detailed_meaning: After morning bathing, Rama goes to Guru Vashishtha and bows before him. He first reads the moment correctly, then speaks of Bharata, the citizens of Ayodhya, and the mothers, all overwhelmed by grief and the pain of exile. The scene prepares the next counsel.
ramacharitamanas::3405.modern_relevance: You finally sit down with the person who can help, after a night of family tension. Before asking for anything, you name who is hurting and why.
ramacharitamanas::3405.insight: It shifts you from private emotion to responsible speech, so the real situation can be addressed clearly.

ramacharitamanas::3406.verse_sanskrit: सहित समाज राउ मिथिलेसू। बहुत दिवस भए सहत कलेसू॥ उचित होइ सोइ कीजिअ नाथा। हित सबही कर रौरें हाथा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3406.verse_hindi: मिथिलापति राजा जनकजी को भी समाज सहित क्लेश सहते बहुत दिन हो गए, इसलिए हे नाथ! जो उचित हो वही कीजिए। आप ही के हाथ सभी का हित है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3406.english_translation: Even King Janaka of Mithila, with his whole assembly, has endured sorrow for many days. So, O Lord, do what is right. The welfare of everyone rests in your hands.
ramacharitamanas::3406.translation_literal: सहित (along with) / समाज (assembly, company) / राउ (king) / मिथिलेसू (of Mithila) / बहुत (many) / दिवस (days) / भए (have been) / सहत (enduring) / कलेसू (sorrow, distress)॥ / उचित (right, proper) / होइ (be) / सोइ (that) / कीजिअ (do) / नाथा (O Lord) / हित (welfare) / सबही (of everyone) / कर (of) / रौरें (your) / हाथा (hands) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3406.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3406.essence: What is right becomes larger when many lives depend on it.
ramacharitamanas::3406.simple_meaning: Bharat asks Ram to do what is proper, saying that the suffering of Janaka and the whole gathering has gone on long enough and that everyone's welfare depends on Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3406.simple_insight: Doing the right thing is not private; it can steady an entire home.
ramacharitamanas::3406.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat stands before Ram and the gathered elders after days of grief and waiting. He reminds Ram that Janaka and the assembly have suffered long enough, then asks him to act according to what is proper, because the well-being of everyone depends on him.
ramacharitamanas::3406.modern_relevance: A family has been living in silence after one person's decision shook everyone. At last, someone says the hard thing: stop avoiding it, do what's right, and let the whole house breathe again.
ramacharitamanas::3406.insight: It shifts the mind from personal hesitation to responsibility for the wider good.

ramacharitamanas::3407.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि अति सकुचे रघुराऊ। मुनि पुल के लखि सीलु सुभाऊ॥ तुम्ह बिनु राम सकल सुख साजा। नरक सरिस दुहु राज समाजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3407.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर श्री रघुनाथजी अत्यन्त ही सकुचा गए। उनका शील स्वभाव देखकर (प्रेम और आनंद से) मुनि वशिष्ठजी पुलकित हो गए। (उन्होंने खुलकर कहा-) हे राम! तुम्हारे बिना (घर-बार आदि) सम्पूर्ण सुखों के साज दोनों राजसमाजों को नरक के समान हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3407.english_translation: Saying this, Raghunath grew very shy. Seeing his gentle nature, the sage was filled with delight. He said openly: "Without you, Ram, all the comforts of home are like hell to both royal households."
ramacharitamanas::3407.translation_literal: अस कहि (saying thus) / अति (very) / सकुचे (became shy) / रघुराऊ (Raghunath) / मुनि (the sage) / पुलक (with delight) / लखि (seeing) / सीलु (gentleness) / सुभाऊ (nature) / तुम्ह (you) / बिनु (without) / राम (Ram) / सकल (all) / सुख (comforts) / साजा (arranged) / नरक (hell) / सरिस (like) / दुहु (both) / राज (royal) / समाजा (households/assemblies)
ramacharitamanas::3407.speaker: Vashistha
ramacharitamanas::3407.essence: Without Ram, comfort itself becomes misery.
ramacharitamanas::3407.simple_meaning: Ram feels shy after speaking humbly. Vashistha sees his gentle nature and says that without Ram, even royal comfort feels unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::3407.simple_insight: Real peace comes from presence, not possessions.
ramacharitamanas::3407.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram speaks with humility before Vashistha while the exile crisis still hangs over Ayodhya and Mithila. The sage, moved by Ram's tenderness, says that without Ram, even the finest royal life feels like misery.
ramacharitamanas::3407.modern_relevance: You can have the perfect apartment, the nicest furniture, and a full calendar — and still feel empty if the one person who matters is missing.
ramacharitamanas::3407.insight: It shifts value from outer comfort to the living presence that makes life feel whole.

ramacharitamanas::3408.verse_sanskrit: प्रान-प्रान के जीव के जिव सुख के सुख राम। तुम्ह तजि तात सोहात गृह जिन्हहि तिन्हहि बिधि बाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::3408.verse_hindi: हे राम! तुम प्राणों के भी प्राण, आत्मा के भी आत्मा और सुख के भी सुख हो। हे तात! तुम्हें छोड़कर जिन्हें घर सुहाता है, उन्हे विधाता विपरीत है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3408.english_translation: O Ram, you are the life within life, the joy within joy. Father, those who find comfort in a home without you are set against the right order of things.
ramacharitamanas::3408.translation_literal: प्रान-प्रान (life of life) / के (of) / जीव (living being) / के (of) / जिव (life) / सुख (joy) / के (of) / सुख (joy) / राम (Ram) / तुम्ह (you) / तजि (leaving) / तात (father/dear one) / सोहात (is pleasant) / गृह (home) / जिन्हहि (to whom) / तिन्हहि (to them) / बिधि (fate / the divine order) / बाम (opposite / adverse)
ramacharitamanas::3408.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3408.essence: Without Ram, even a home becomes out of tune.
ramacharitamanas::3408.simple_meaning: Ram is the deepest source of life and joy. A home feels empty and out of order when he is absent.
ramacharitamanas::3408.simple_insight: Real comfort is not in possessions or place, but in the presence that makes everything feel alive.
ramacharitamanas::3408.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the sages are urging Ram to stay and restore order, but Ram's exile is already unfolding. Tulsidas turns the moment into devotion: without Ram, even a home loses its rightness, because he is the heart of all living joy.
ramacharitamanas::3408.modern_relevance: You sit in a beautiful apartment after a breakup and nothing feels settled. The furniture is fine, the room is fine, but the warmth is gone. This verse names that ache exactly.
ramacharitamanas::3408.insight: It shifts attention from outer comfort to the presence that gives life its meaning.

ramacharitamanas::3409.verse_sanskrit: सो सुखु करमु धरमु जरि जाऊ। जहँ न राम पद पंकज भाऊ॥ जोगु कुजोगु ग्यानु अग्यानू। जहँ नहिं राम प्रेम परधानू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3409.verse_hindi: जहाँ श्री राम के चरण कमलों में प्रेम नहीं है, वह सुख, कर्म और धर्म जल जाए, जिसमें श्री राम प्रेम की प्रधानता नहीं है, वह योग कुयोग है और वह ज्ञान अज्ञान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3409.english_translation: Any happiness, action, or duty burns away where love for Ram's lotus feet is absent. Without Ram as the center, yoga becomes misguidance and wisdom becomes ignorance.
ramacharitamanas::3409.translation_literal: सो (that) / सुखु (happiness) / करमु (action) / धरमु (duty) / जरि जाऊ (may burn away) / जहँ (where) / न (not) / राम (Ram) / पद पंकज (lotus feet) / भाऊ (love)॥ / जोगु (yoga) / कुजोगु (misguided yoga) / ग्यानु (wisdom) / अग्यानू (ignorance) / जहँ (where) / नहिं (not) / राम (Ram) / प्रेम (love) / परधानू (chief)
ramacharitamanas::3409.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3409.essence: Without love for Ram, even virtue and wisdom lose their value.
ramacharitamanas::3409.simple_meaning: Love for Ram is what gives value to happiness, action, duty, yoga, and wisdom. Without that love, even good things lose their worth.
ramacharitamanas::3409.simple_insight: What matters most is not achievement, but what your heart is oriented toward.
ramacharitamanas::3409.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the conversation has turned from grief and exile to the deepest measure of a life. Tulsidas says that without love for Ram, even happiness, duty, yoga, and knowledge lose their real worth.
ramacharitamanas::3409.modern_relevance: You can build the perfect career, follow every wellness rule, and still feel empty if your heart has no center. This verse asks what your life is actually arranged around.
ramacharitamanas::3409.insight: It shifts attention from outer success to the devotion that gives all action meaning.

ramacharitamanas::3410.verse_sanskrit: तुम्ह बिनु दुखी सुखी तुम्ह तेहीं। तुम्ह जानहु जिय जो जेहि केहीं॥ राउर आयसु सिर सबही कें। बिदित कृपालहि गति सब नीकें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3410.verse_hindi: तुम्हारे बिना ही सब दुःखी हैं और जो सुखी हैं वे तुम्हीं से सुखी हैं। जिस किसी के जी में जो कुछ है तुम सब जानते हो। आपकी आज्ञा सभी के सिर पर है। कृपालु (आप) को सभी की स्थिति अच्छी तरह मालूम है॥2
ramacharitamanas::3410.english_translation: You alone are the source of sorrow and joy. You know what lives in every heart. Your command rests on every head, and the compassionate one knows every state perfectly.
ramacharitamanas::3410.translation_literal: तुम्ह बिनु (without you) / दुखी (sorrowful) / सुखी (happy) / तुम्ह (you) / तेहीं (by that one) / तुम्ह (you) / जानहु (know) / जिय (heart) / जो (whatever) / जेहि केहीं (of each one) / राउर (your) / आयसु (command) / सिर (head) / सबही कें (on everyone) / बिदित (known) / कृपालहि (to the compassionate one) / गति (condition) / सब (all) / नीकें (well)
ramacharitamanas::3410.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3410.essence: The one who governs your life already knows your heart.
ramacharitamanas::3410.simple_meaning: Ram is the source of both sorrow and joy, and he knows every heart completely. Everyone stands under his authority, and nothing about anyone's condition is hidden from him.
ramacharitamanas::3410.simple_insight: There is comfort in being fully seen by the one who also holds your life.
ramacharitamanas::3410.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, after the pain of exile has fractured the royal family, the verse turns to Ram's all-knowing compassion. It says that every heart is open to him, and every life already lies under his care.
ramacharitamanas::3410.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone who cannot say what hurts, yet you already feel the shape of it. This verse speaks to the relief of being understood before you can explain yourself.
ramacharitamanas::3410.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to trust in being known and guided.

ramacharitamanas::3411.verse_sanskrit: आपु आश्रमहि धारिअ पाऊ। भयउ सनेह सिथिल मुनिराऊ॥ करि प्रनामु तब रामु सिधाए। रिषि धरि धीर जनक पहिं आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3411.verse_hindi: अतः आप आश्रम को पधारिए। इतना कह मुनिराज स्नेह से शिथिल हो गए। तब श्री रामजी प्रणाम करके चले गए और ऋषि वशिष्ठजी धीरज धरकर जनकजी के पास आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3411.english_translation: 'Please return to your hermitage,' he said. The sage-king was then softened by affection. After bowing, Ram departed, and the sage gathered his composure and came to Janak.
ramacharitamanas::3411.translation_literal: आपु (your own) / आश्रमहि (to the hermitage) / धारिअ (please return/hold) / पाऊ (footsteps) / भयउ (became) / सनेह (affection) / सिथिल (softened) / मुनिराऊ (sage-king) / करि (doing) / प्रनामु (bow) / तब (then) / रामु (Ram) / सिधाए (departed) / रिषि (sage) / धरि (gathering) / धीर (composure) / जनक पहिं (to Janak) / आए (came)
ramacharitamanas::3411.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3411.essence: Affection can soften the heart without breaking dignity.
ramacharitamanas::3411.simple_meaning: The sage asks Ram to return to his hermitage. Ram bows and leaves, and the sage regains composure before going to Janak.
ramacharitamanas::3411.simple_insight: Even a brief parting can soften the heart, but dignity returns when duty calls.
ramacharitamanas::3411.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, the conversation with Ram has been so moving that the sage-king is overcome with affection. Ram bows and leaves respectfully, while the sage steadies himself and goes on to speak with Janak. The verse mainly moves the scene forward.
ramacharitamanas::3411.modern_relevance: You finish a hard conversation, bow your head, and walk out before your emotions spill over. The moment is tender, but the next duty still waits.
ramacharitamanas::3411.insight: It shows how reverence and composure can coexist even in emotional transitions.

ramacharitamanas::3412.verse_sanskrit: राम बचन गुरु नृपहि सुनाए। सील सनेह सुभायँ सुहाए॥ महाराज अब कीजिअ सोई। सब कर धरम सहित हित होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3412.verse_hindi: गुरुजी ने श्री रामचन्द्रजी के शील और स्नेह से युक्त स्वभाव से ही सुंदर वचन राजा जनकजी को सुनाए (और कहा-) हे महाराज! अब वही कीजिए, जिसमें सबका धर्म सहित हित हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3412.english_translation: The guru conveyed Ram's words to the king, words shaped by grace and loving nature: "Great king, now do what brings dharma-filled good to everyone."
ramacharitamanas::3412.translation_literal: राम (Ram's) / बचन (words) / गुरु (the teacher) / नृपहि (to the king) / सुनाए (made heard) / सील (gentle character) / सनेह (love) / सुभायँ (by nature) / सुहाए (beautiful) / महाराज (great king) / अब (now) / कीजिअ (do) / सोई (that only) / सब (all) / कर (of all) / धरम (dharma) / सहित (with) / हित (welfare) / होई (may happen)
ramacharitamanas::3412.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3412.essence: The best choice is the one that protects dharma for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3412.simple_meaning: Ram's message is that the king should choose the course of action that is righteous and beneficial for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3412.simple_insight: Real strength is choosing the option that protects everyone, not just your own side.
ramacharitamanas::3412.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, Ram's words are carried through the teacher as the tension over Sita's swayamvar resolves. The king is being urged to act in a way that keeps dharma intact and brings good to all present.
ramacharitamanas::3412.modern_relevance: A family meeting is stuck because every option benefits one person and hurts another. The wisest voice in the room asks for the choice that leaves the whole group better, not just the loudest person.
ramacharitamanas::3412.insight: It shifts decision-making from personal preference to the wider good of everyone involved.

ramacharitamanas::3413.verse_sanskrit: ग्यान निधान सुजान सुचि धरम धीर नरपाल। तुम्ह बिनु असमंजस समन को समरथ एहि काल ॥
ramacharitamanas::3413.verse_hindi: हे राजन् ! तुम ज्ञान के भंडार, सुजान, पवित्र और धर्म में धीर हो। इस समय तुम्हारे बिना इस दुविधा को दूर करने में और कौन समर्थ है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3413.english_translation: O king, you are a storehouse of wisdom, discerning, pure, and steadfast in dharma. Without you, who is capable of ending this confusion at this time?
ramacharitamanas::3413.translation_literal: ग्यान (wisdom) / निधान (storehouse) / सुजान (wise) / सुचि (pure) / धरम (dharma) / धीर (steadfast) / नरपाल (king) / तुम्ह (you) / बिनु (without) / असमंजस (confusion) / समन (ending) / को (who) / समरथ (capable) / एहि (this) / काल (time)
ramacharitamanas::3413.speaker: Vasishta
ramacharitamanas::3413.essence: Steady wisdom becomes the authority that ends confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3413.simple_meaning: Janak is praised as wise, pure, and steady in dharma, the one best able to resolve the present confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3413.simple_insight: Real authority comes from inner steadiness, not status alone.
ramacharitamanas::3413.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Vasishta turns to King Janak as the marriage preparations and Ram's presence create a delicate moment. He is not flattering him; he is naming the one person calm and clear enough to end the uncertainty.
ramacharitamanas::3413.modern_relevance: A room full of people is stuck, everyone talking at once, and the one person who stays calm finally names the next step. That is the kind of steadiness this verse honours.
ramacharitamanas::3413.insight: It shifts attention from noise and hesitation to the person whose clarity can resolve the moment.

ramacharitamanas::3414.verse_sanskrit: सुनि मुनि बचन जनक अनुरागे। लखि गति ग्यानु बिरागु बिरागे॥ सिथिल सनेहँ गुनत मन माहीं। आए इहाँ कीन्ह भल नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3414.verse_hindi: मुनि वशिष्ठजी के वचन सुनकर जनकजी प्रेम में मग्न हो गए। उनकी दशा देखकर ज्ञान और वैराग्य को भी वैराग्य हो गया (अर्थात उनके ज्ञान-वैराग्य छूट से गए)। वे प्रेम से शिथिल हो गए और मन में विचार करने लगे कि हम यहाँ आए, यह अच्छा नहीं किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3414.english_translation: Hearing the sage's words, Janaka was filled with love. Seeing his state, even knowledge and detachment seemed to lose their grip. Softened by affection, he thought in his heart, 'Coming here was not a good choice.'
ramacharitamanas::3414.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (sage) / बचन (words) / जनक (Janaka) / अनुरागे (became प्रेम-filled) । / लखि (seeing) / गति (state) / ग्यानु (knowledge) / बिरागु (detachment) / बिरागे (became detached) । / सिथिल (softened) / सनेहँ (by affection) / गुनत (thinking) / मन (mind) / माहीं (within) । / आए (came) / इहाँ (here) / कीन्ह (did) / भल (good) / नाहीं (not) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3414.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3414.essence: Love can melt the very detachment that once seemed strongest.
ramacharitamanas::3414.simple_meaning: Janaka hears the sage and becomes tender with love. His usual detachment weakens, and he feels that coming there was a mistake.
ramacharitamanas::3414.simple_insight: Even the most composed heart can be undone by love.
ramacharitamanas::3414.detailed_meaning: In Janaka's court, Vashishtha's words have just opened a deeper emotional current. Janaka, usually known for wisdom and detachment, is overcome by feeling as he watches the unfolding situation. This verse shows his inner softening before the next decision is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3414.modern_relevance: You sit in a meeting trying to stay composed, but one sentence from someone you respect changes everything. Your usual distance drops, and the heart speaks first.
ramacharitamanas::3414.insight: It shows how love can dissolve even a carefully held stance of detachment.

ramacharitamanas::3415.verse_sanskrit: रामहि रायँ कहेउ बन जाना। कीन्ह आपु प्रिय प्रेम प्रवाना॥ हम अब बन तें बनहि पठाई। प्रमुदित फिरब बिबेक बड़ाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3415.verse_hindi: राजा दशरथजी ने श्री रामजी को वन जाने के लिए कहा और स्वयं अपने प्रिय के प्रेम को प्रमाणित (सच्चा) कर दिया (प्रिय वियोग में प्राण त्याग दिए), परन्तु हम अब इन्हें वन से (और गहन) वन को भेजकर अपने विवेक की बड़ाई में आनन्दित होते हुए लौटेंगे (कि हमें जरा भी मोह नहीं है, हम श्री रामजी को वन में छोड़कर चले आए, दशरथजी की तरह मरे नहीं!) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3415.english_translation: King Dasharatha told Rama to go to the forest and made his own love for his beloved fully real. We will now send him from the forest into deeper forest and return, proud of our wisdom, as if we feel no attachment at all.
ramacharitamanas::3415.translation_literal: रामहि (to Rama) / रायँ (the king) / कहेउ (said) / बन (forest) / जाना (to go) / कीन्ह (made) / आपु (self) / प्रिय (beloved) / प्रेम (love) / प्रवाना (manifested as true) / हम (we) / अब (now) / बन तें (from the forest) / बनहि (to deeper forest) / पठाई (send) / प्रमुदित (delighted) / फिरब (return) / बिबेक (wisdom) / बड़ाई (greatness)
ramacharitamanas::3415.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3415.essence: Love is tested by how much it can release without becoming false.
ramacharitamanas::3415.simple_meaning: True love is shown when you can release someone you cherish without pretending it does not hurt.
ramacharitamanas::3415.simple_insight: Love becomes honest when it stops clinging and still remains wholehearted.
ramacharitamanas::3415.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Dasharath has already sent Rama away, and that grief is now part of the kingdom's memory. The verse turns that pain into a mirror: some people act proud of detachment, but real love is measured by what it can bear to lose.
ramacharitamanas::3415.modern_relevance: You wave goodbye at the station after helping someone move cities, then force a smile and call it maturity. The verse cuts through that pose and asks whether your detachment is real or just performance.
ramacharitamanas::3415.insight: It shifts the mind from proving control to honoring attachment honestly.

ramacharitamanas::3416.verse_sanskrit: तापस मुनि महिसुर सुनि देखी। भए प्रेम बस बिकल बिसेषी॥ समउ समुझि धरि धीरजु राजा। चले भरत पहिं सहित समाजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3416.verse_hindi: तपस्वी, मुनि और ब्राह्मण यह सब सुन और देखकर प्रेमवश बहुत ही व्याकुल हो गए। समय का विचार करके राजा जनकजी धीरज धरकर समाज सहित भरतजी के पास चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::3416.english_translation: Seeing and hearing this, the ascetics, sages, and priests were overwhelmed by love. Understanding the moment, King Janak steadied himself and went with his whole company to Bharata.
ramacharitamanas::3416.translation_literal: तापस (ascetics) / मुनि (sages) / महिसुर (priests) / सुनि (hearing) / देखी (seeing) / भए (became) / प्रेम बस (under the power of love) / बिकल (distressed) / बिसेषी (especially)॥ / समउ (the moment) / समुझि (understanding) / धरि (holding) / धीरजु (steadiness) / राजा (king) / चले (went) / भरत पहिं (toward Bharata) / सहित समाजा (with the whole company)॥
ramacharitamanas::3416.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3416.essence: Love can shake you; steadiness lets you respond well.
ramacharitamanas::3416.simple_meaning: The holy men are moved to deep emotion, and Janak keeps his composure before going to Bharata with his attendants.
ramacharitamanas::3416.simple_insight: Even strong feeling can be held with dignity when the moment calls for it.
ramacharitamanas::3416.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the news of Ram's exile and the grief around Bharata has spread. The ascetics, sages, and priests are shaken by what they see and hear. Janak, though moved, gathers himself and walks with his company to meet Bharata.
ramacharitamanas::3416.modern_relevance: You hear bad news in a crowded room and feel your chest tighten, but you still stand up, smooth your face, and go meet the person who needs you.
ramacharitamanas::3416.insight: It teaches you to let feeling move you without letting it scatter your conduct.

ramacharitamanas::3417.verse_sanskrit: भरत आइ आगें भइ लीन्हे। अवसर सरिस सुआसन दीन्हे॥ तात भरत कह तेरहुति राऊ। तुम्हहि बिदित रघुबीर सुभाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3417.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने आकर उन्हें आगे होकर लिया (सामने आकर उनका स्वागत किया) और समयानुकूल अच्छे आसन दिए। तिरहुतराज जनकजी कहने लगे- हे तात भरत! तुमको श्री रामजी का स्वभाव मालूम ही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3417.english_translation: Bharat came forward and welcomed them with fitting seats. King Janaka said, “Dear Bharat, you already know the nature of Raghuvir.”
ramacharitamanas::3417.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / आइ (coming) / आगें (forward) / भइ (became) / लीन्हे (took, welcomed) / अवसर (appropriate time) / सरिस (matching) / सुआसन (good seat) / दीन्हे (gave) ॥ तात (dear) / भरत (Bharat) / कह (said) / तेरहुति राऊ (the king of Tirhut, Janaka) / तुम्हहि (to you) / बिदित (known) / रघुबीर (Raghuvir) / सुभाऊ (nature) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3417.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3417.essence: Courtesy opens the way for truth already known.
ramacharitamanas::3417.simple_meaning: Bharat receives the guests respectfully, and Janaka reminds him that Ram’s nature is already well known.
ramacharitamanas::3417.simple_insight: Respectful conduct matters, but the deeper message is already understood: Ram’s character is steady and known.
ramacharitamanas::3417.detailed_meaning: Bharat and the gathered company arrive before Janaka in the tense aftermath of Ram’s exile. Bharat steps forward to receive them properly, and Janaka speaks with care, reminding Bharat that Ram’s nature is already familiar to him.
ramacharitamanas::3417.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone is carrying grief, and you still make space, offer a chair, and speak gently. Small courtesy can hold a heavy moment.
ramacharitamanas::3417.insight: It shows how dignity and tenderness can steady a difficult gathering before deeper words are spoken.

ramacharitamanas::3418.verse_sanskrit: राम सत्यब्रत धरम रत सब कर सीलु स्नेहु। संकट सहत सकोच बस कहिअ जो आयसु देहु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3418.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी सत्यव्रती और धर्मपरायण हैं, सबका शील और स्नेह रखने वाले हैं, इसीलिए वे संकोचवश संकट सह रहे हैं, अब तुम जो आज्ञा दो, वह उनसे कही जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3418.english_translation: Rama is true to his vow and devoted to dharma, full of gentleness and affection for everyone. He is bearing this hardship out of modesty, so please give the command that should be conveyed to him.
ramacharitamanas::3418.translation_literal: राम (Rama) / सत्यब्रत (true to vows) / धरम रत (devoted to dharma) / सब कर (of everyone) / सीलु (gentleness, character) / स्नेहु (affection) / संकट (hardship) / सहत (bearing) / सकोच बस (out of modesty) / कहिअ (should be said) / जो (what) / आयसु (command) / देहु (give)
ramacharitamanas::3418.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3418.essence: True duty stays gentle even under strain.
ramacharitamanas::3418.simple_meaning: Ram stays true to his vows, lives by dharma, and treats everyone with kindness. Even while suffering, he remains humble and waits for the right instruction.
ramacharitamanas::3418.simple_insight: Real strength can look quiet: keeping your word without losing gentleness.
ramacharitamanas::3418.detailed_meaning: At Janak’s court, Bharat is being spoken of with reverence. The speaker reminds everyone that Ram is bound to truth, dharma, and kindness, and that he bears hardship without protest. This prepares Bharat’s response.
ramacharitamanas::3418.modern_relevance: You’re the one who keeps showing up, even when the job is painful and no one sees the strain. The hardest part is still staying kind while you carry it.
ramacharitamanas::3418.insight: It teaches you to see duty and tenderness as companions, not opposites.

ramacharitamanas::3419.verse_sanskrit: सुनि तन पुलकि नयन भरि बारी। बोले भरतु धीर धरि भारी॥ प्रभु प्रिय पूज्य पिता सम आपू। कुलगुरु सम हित माय न बापू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3419.verse_hindi: भरतजी यह सुनकर पुलकित शरीर हो नेत्रों में जल भरकर बड़ा भारी धीरज धरकर बोले- हे प्रभो! आप हमारे पिता के समान प्रिय और पूज्य हैं और कुल गुरु श्री वशिष्ठजी के समान हितैषी तो माता-पिता भी नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3419.english_translation: Hearing this, Bharata’s body thrilled and his eyes filled with tears. Holding firm courage, he said, “My lord is as dear and worthy of worship as my father. My family teacher is my guide; even mother and father are not as helpful.”
ramacharitamanas::3419.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / तन (body) / पुलकि (thrilled) / नयन (eyes) / भरि (filled) / बारी (water, tears) / बोले (spoke) / भरतु (Bharata) / धीर (steady) / धरि (holding) / भारी (firmly, greatly) / प्रभु (lord) / प्रिय (dear) / पूज्य (worthy of worship) / पिता (father) / सम (like) / आपू (self) / कुलगुरु (family teacher) / सम (like) / हित (beneficial, helpful) / माय (mother) / न (not) / बापू (father)
ramacharitamanas::3419.speaker: Bharata
ramacharitamanas::3419.essence: True reverence speaks with a full heart and a steady voice.
ramacharitamanas::3419.simple_meaning: Bharata is overwhelmed with emotion, yet he speaks firmly. He says Ram is as dear and worthy of respect as a father, and the family teacher is even more guiding than parents.
ramacharitamanas::3419.simple_insight: Deep feeling does not have to make you weak; it can make your respect and humility clearer.
ramacharitamanas::3419.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharata stands before respected guests and speaks through tears. He is not claiming power; he is showing reverence. His words place Ram above family pride and place the teacher’s guidance above ordinary attachment.
ramacharitamanas::3419.modern_relevance: You sit across from an elder who changed your life, and your throat tightens before you can speak. Bharata shows that gratitude can be intense without becoming noisy, and respect can be deeply felt without any self-display.
ramacharitamanas::3419.insight: It teaches you to let emotion deepen humility, not disrupt it.

ramacharitamanas::3420.verse_sanskrit: कौसिकादि मुनि सचिव समाजू। ग्यान अंबुनिधि आपुनु आजू॥ सिसु सेवकु आयसु अनुगामी। जानि मोहि सिख देइअ स्वामी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3420.verse_hindi: विश्वामित्रजी आदि मुनियों और मंत्रियों का समाज है और आज के दिन ज्ञान के समुद्र आप भी उपस्थित हैं। हे स्वामी! मुझे अपना बच्चा, सेवक और आज्ञानुसार चलने वाला समझकर शिक्षा दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3420.english_translation: Kausika and the sages are here, along with the ministers. You yourself are here today, ocean of wisdom. O master, regard me as your child, your servant, and one who follows your command, and teach me.
ramacharitamanas::3420.translation_literal: कौसिकादि (Kausika and others) / मुनि (sages) / सचिव (ministers) / समाजू (assembly) / ग्यान (wisdom) / अंबुनिधि (ocean) / आपुनु (yourself) / आजू (today) / सिसु (child) / सेवकु (servant) / आयसु (command) / अनुगामी (follower) / जानि (knowing) / मोहि (me) / सिख (instruction) / देइअ (give) / स्वामी (master)
ramacharitamanas::3420.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3420.essence: Real wisdom begins when you stop trying to look wise.
ramacharitamanas::3420.simple_meaning: Bharat speaks with humility, asking the wise assembly to teach him as if he were a child and servant. Real learning begins with surrendering pride.
ramacharitamanas::3420.simple_insight: There is relief in not pretending to know everything. Humility opens the door to wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::3420.detailed_meaning: In the assembly at Nandigram, Bharat stands before sages, ministers, and Vishwamitra. He does not boast or argue. Instead, he lowers himself completely and asks to be instructed as a child and servant. That humility makes the teaching possible.
ramacharitamanas::3420.modern_relevance: You sit in a room full of experts, your notes half-finished, and your first instinct is to protect your image. Bharat shows another way: ask plainly, listen fully, and let learning begin.
ramacharitamanas::3420.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to teachability, making true understanding possible.

ramacharitamanas::3421.verse_sanskrit: एहिं समाज थल बूझब राउर। मौन मलिन मैं बोलब बाउर॥ छोटे बदन कहउँ बड़ि बाता। छमब तात लखि बाम बिधाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3421.verse_hindi: इस समाज और (पुण्य) स्थल में आप (जैसे ज्ञानी और पूज्य) का पूछना! इस पर यदि मैं मौन रहता हूँ तो मलिन समझा जाऊँगा और बोलना पागलपन होगा तथापि मैं छोटे मुँह बड़ी बात कहता हूँ। हे तात! विधाता को प्रतिकूल जानकर क्षमा कीजिएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3421.english_translation: In this assembly, asking you feels strange. If I stay silent, I look dull; if I speak, I look foolish. Still, I will say a great thing with my small voice. Forgive me, father, if fate seems to oppose it.
ramacharitamanas::3421.translation_literal: एहिं (in this) / समाज (assembly) / थल (place) / बूझब (to ask) / राउर (your) / मौन (silence) / मलिन (stained, dull) / मैं (I) / बोलब (to speak) / बाउर (foolish) / छोटे (small) / बदन (mouth, face) / कहउँ (I say) / बड़ि (great) / बाता (thing, matter) / छमब (forgive) / तात (father) / लखि (seeing) / बाम (opposed, adverse) / बिधाता (fate, the ordainer)
ramacharitamanas::3421.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3421.essence: Humility can still carry a hard truth.
ramacharitamanas::3421.simple_meaning: Bharat says he feels awkward speaking in such a noble assembly, but he must still say something important and asks to be forgiven if his words seem improper.
ramacharitamanas::3421.simple_insight: Sometimes duty means speaking up even when you feel unworthy.
ramacharitamanas::3421.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before sages and ministers after being called back to Ayodhya. Humbled by their presence, he apologizes for speaking as a younger man, yet chooses truth over silence because the moment demands it.
ramacharitamanas::3421.modern_relevance: You’re in a room full of senior people, and your throat tightens before you speak. You know staying quiet would be easier, but the truth in you still needs a voice.
ramacharitamanas::3421.insight: It teaches you to speak from responsibility, not confidence, when the moment requires it.

ramacharitamanas::3422.verse_sanskrit: आगम निगम प्रसिद्ध पुराना। सेवाधरमु कठिन जगु जाना॥ स्वामि धरम स्वारथहि बिरोधू। बैरु अंध प्रेमहि न प्रबोधू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3422.verse_hindi: वेद, शास्त्र और पुराणों में प्रसिद्ध है और जगत जानता है कि सेवा धर्म बड़ा कठिन है। स्वामी धर्म में (स्वामी के प्रति कर्तव्य पालन में) और स्वार्थ में विरोध है (दोनों एक साथ नहीं निभ सकते) वैर अंधा होता है और प्रेम को ज्ञान नहीं रहता (मैं स्वार्थवश कहूँगा या प्रेमवश, दोनों में ही भूल होने का भय है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3422.english_translation: Scripture, the Vedas, the teachings, and the Puranas all say it: service is hard in this world. Duty to a master and self-interest stand opposed; blind attachment and love cannot see clearly.
ramacharitamanas::3422.translation_literal: आगम (scripture) / निगम (Vedas) / प्रसिद्ध (well-known) / पुराना (Puranas) / सेवाधरमु (service-duty) / कठिन (hard) / जगु (the world) / जाना (known) / स्वामि (master) / धरम (duty) / स्वारथहि (self-interest) / बिरोधू (opposed) / बैरु (enmity) / अंध (blind) / प्रेमहि (love) / न (not) / प्रबोधू (clear understanding)
ramacharitamanas::3422.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3422.essence: Service becomes difficult the moment self-interest enters.
ramacharitamanas::3422.simple_meaning: True service is difficult because it often conflicts with personal gain. Loyalty to a master or cause cannot always be mixed with self-interest.
ramacharitamanas::3422.simple_insight: It feels honest: real service asks you to notice where your own gain is getting in the way.
ramacharitamanas::3422.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is speaking with the assembled sages and ministers about what he should do for Ram. He knows service is praised everywhere, but he also knows it becomes hard when personal desire enters the mind.
ramacharitamanas::3422.modern_relevance: You volunteer to help organize a family event, then quietly hope your effort gets noticed. The verse catches that split: service becomes difficult the moment self-interest slips in.
ramacharitamanas::3422.insight: It teaches you to separate genuine service from hidden self-benefit.

ramacharitamanas::3423.verse_sanskrit: राखि राम रुख धरमु ब्रतु पराधीन मोहि जानि। सब कें संमत सर्ब हित करिअ प्रेमु पहिचानि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3423.verse_hindi: अतएव मुझे पराधीन जानकर (मुझसे न पूछकर) श्री रामचन्द्रजी के रुख (रुचि), धर्म और (सत्य के) व्रत को रखते हुए, जो सबके सम्मत और सबके लिए हितकारी हो आप सबका प्रेम पहचानकर वही कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3423.english_translation: Therefore, knowing me to be dependent, keep Ram's will, dharma, and vow in view. Recognize the love that is approved by all and beneficial to all, and act accordingly.
ramacharitamanas::3423.translation_literal: राखि (keeping) / राम रुख (Ram's wish) / धरमु (dharma) / ब्रतु (vow) / पराधीन (dependent) / मोहि (me) / जानि (knowing) / सब कें (for everyone) / संमत (approved) / सर्ब हित (for all welfare) / करिअ (do) / प्रेमु (love) / पहिचानि (recognizing)
ramacharitamanas::3423.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3423.essence: Love becomes clear when it serves everyone, not just your preference.
ramacharitamanas::3423.simple_meaning: Put Ram's will, dharma, and promise first. Then choose the course that everyone can accept and that benefits everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3423.simple_insight: Real love does not push for personal preference; it looks for what is good for all.
ramacharitamanas::3423.detailed_meaning: In Janak's assembly, Bharat speaks with humility after being asked to explain his stance. He says he is not free to choose for himself; he must hold to Ram's wish, dharma, and vow, and then follow the option that is agreeable and beneficial to everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3423.modern_relevance: A family group chat is full of opinions about what you should do next. Instead of forcing your preference, you pause and ask which choice respects the bigger good and the promise already made.
ramacharitamanas::3423.insight: It shifts decision-making from personal insistence to shared welfare and fidelity to what is already right.

ramacharitamanas::3424.verse_sanskrit: भरत बचन सुनि देखि सुभाऊ। सहित समाज सराहत राऊ॥ सुगम अगम मृदु मंजु कठोरे। अरथु अमित अति आखर थोरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3424.verse_hindi: भरतजी के वचन सुनकर और उनका स्वभाव देखकर समाज सहित राजा जनक उनकी सराहना करने लगे। भरतजी के वचन सुगम और अगम, सुंदर, कोमल और कठोर हैं। उनमें अक्षर थोड़े हैं, परन्तु अर्थ अत्यन्त अपार भरा हुआ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3424.english_translation: Hearing Bharata's words and seeing his nature, King Janaka and the gathered assembly praised him. Bharata's speech is easy and difficult, gentle and firm. It uses few words, yet holds immense meaning.
ramacharitamanas::3424.translation_literal: भरत (Bharata) / बचन (words) / सुनि (having heard) / देखि (having seen) / सुभाऊ (nature, disposition) / सहित (along with) / समाज (assembly) / सराहत (praising) / राऊ (king) ॥ / सुगम (easy) / अगम (hard to reach, profound) / मृदु (soft, gentle) / मंजु (beautiful, pleasing) / कठोरे (hard, firm) / अरथु (meaning) / अमित (immeasurable) / अति (very) / आखर (letters, words) / थोरे (few) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3424.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3424.essence: True speech can be brief and still carry immense weight.
ramacharitamanas::3424.simple_meaning: Bharata speaks with a rare balance: his words are gentle yet firm, simple yet profound. The assembly admires how so little speech can carry so much meaning.
ramacharitamanas::3424.simple_insight: You do not need many words to be deeply understood.
ramacharitamanas::3424.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Janaka and the gathered court hear Bharata speak and immediately recognise his character. His speech is brief but layered: soft in tone, firm in truth, and full of meaning. The scene pauses to honour the depth behind his restraint.
ramacharitamanas::3424.modern_relevance: You send a short message that settles a family conflict better than a long explanation ever could. Bharata's kind of speech is brief, exact, and impossible to dismiss.
ramacharitamanas::3424.insight: It teaches you to value speech that is concise, truthful, and rich with intention.

ramacharitamanas::3425.verse_sanskrit: ज्यों मुखु मुकुर मुकुरु निज पानी। गहि न जाइ अस अदभुत बानी॥ भूप भरतू मुनि सहित समाजू। गे जहँ बिबुध कुमुद द्विजराजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3425.verse_hindi: जैसे मुख (का प्रतिबिम्ब) दर्पण में दिखता है और दर्पण अपने हाथ में है, फिर भी वह (मुख का प्रतिबिम्ब) पकड़ा नहीं जाता, इसी प्रकार भरतजी की यह अद्भुत वाणी भी पकड़ में नहीं आती (शब्दों से उसका आशय समझ में नहीं आता)। (किसी से कुछ उत्तर देते नहीं बना) तब राजा जनकजी, भरतजी तथा मुनि वशिष्ठजी समाज के साथ वहाँ गए, जहाँ देवता रूपी कुमुदों को खिलाने वाले (सुख देने वाले) चन्द्रमा श्री रामचन्द्रजी थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3425.english_translation: As a face appears in a mirror held in one’s own hand, yet cannot be grasped, so too this wondrous speech of Bharat cannot be fully caught. Then King Janaka, along with Bharat and the sages, went to where Ram, the moon that delights the celestial lilies, was staying.
ramacharitamanas::3425.translation_literal: ज्यों (just as) / मुखु (face) / मुकुरु (mirror) / मुकुरु (mirror) / निज (one's own) / पानी (hand) / गहि (grasped) / न जाइ (cannot be) / अस (thus) / अदभुत (wondrous) / बानी (speech) / भूप (king) / भरतू (Bharat) / मुनि (sage) / सहित (along with) / समाजू (assembly) / गे (went) / जहँ (where) / बिबुध (celestial beings) / कुमुद (water lilies) / द्विजराजू (moon)
ramacharitamanas::3425.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3425.essence: True feeling can outgrow the words trying to hold it.
ramacharitamanas::3425.simple_meaning: Bharat’s words are so profound that they cannot be easily captured or explained. After that, Janaka, Bharat, and the sages go to meet Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3425.simple_insight: Some words are so sincere that their meaning is larger than language.
ramacharitamanas::3425.detailed_meaning: In Janaka’s assembly, Bharat has just spoken with a depth that leaves everyone stunned. His words are compared to a face seen in a mirror that you can hold but never truly seize. Unable to answer in ordinary speech, the group moves toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3425.modern_relevance: You read a message from someone who loves you deeply, and you sit there unable to reply. The feeling is bigger than any neat sentence. Some truths move people before they can explain them.
ramacharitamanas::3425.insight: It shifts attention from clever wording to the force of sincere feeling and presence.

ramacharitamanas::3426.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सुधि सोच बिकल सब लोगा। मनहुँ मीनगन नव जल जोगा॥ देवँ प्रथम कुलगुर गति देखी। निरखि बिदेह सनेह बिसेषी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3426.verse_hindi: यह समाचार सुनकर सब लोग सोच से व्याकुल हो गए, जैसे नए (पहली वर्षा के) जल के संयोग से मछलियाँ व्याकुल होती हैं। देवताओं ने पहले कुलगुरु वशिष्ठजी की (प्रेमविह्वल) दशा देखी, फिर विदेहजी के विशेष स्नेह को देखा, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3426.english_translation: Hearing the news, everyone was shaken with worry, like fish stirred by the first touch of fresh water. The gods first saw the family teacher Vashishtha in grief, then saw the special tenderness of Videha.
ramacharitamanas::3426.translation_literal: सुनि (hearing) / सुधि (news, remembrance) / सोच (worry) / बिकल (disturbed) / सब (all) / लोगा (people) । मनहुँ (as if) / मीनगन (groups of fish) / नव (new) / जल (water) / जोगा (contact, touch) । देवँ (the gods) / प्रथम (first) / कुलगुरु (family teacher) / गति (state) / देखी (saw) । निरखि (seeing) / बिदेह (Videha, Janaka) / सनेह (affection) / बिसेषी (special, intense) ।
ramacharitamanas::3426.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3426.essence: Shared sorrow can ripple through everyone at once.
ramacharitamanas::3426.simple_meaning: The news leaves everyone shaken. The verse compares their distress to fish stirred by fresh water and notes how the gods saw Vashishtha's grief and Janaka's deep affection.
ramacharitamanas::3426.simple_insight: Some news spreads pain so quickly that even bystanders feel the ache.
ramacharitamanas::3426.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the news has reached the court and the wider assembly. The whole gathering is thrown into grief, while the divine witnesses notice two especially moving sights: Vashishtha's sorrow and Janaka's deep affection. The verse is part of the unfolding reaction, not the main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3426.modern_relevance: A phone call arrives before dawn, and the whole family goes silent. Before anyone knows what to do, the shock has already spread through the room.
ramacharitamanas::3426.insight: It shows how grief moves through a group before anyone can explain it.

ramacharitamanas::3427.verse_sanskrit: राम भगतिमय भरतु निहारे। सुर स्वारथी हहरि हियँ हारे॥ सब कोउ राम प्रेममय पेखा। भए अलेख सोच बस लेखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3427.verse_hindi: और तब श्री रामभक्ति से ओतप्रोत भरतजी को देखा। इन सबको देखकर स्वार्थी देवता घबड़ाकर हृदय में हार मान गए (निराश हो गए)। उन्होंने सब किसी को श्री राम प्रेम में सराबोर देखा। इससे देवता इतने सोच के वश हो गए कि जिसका कोई हिसाब नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3427.english_translation: And then they saw Bharat filled with Ram's devotion. The self-seeking devas lost heart within. They saw everyone drenched in love for Ram, and their minds were thrown into such confusion that it could not be counted.
ramacharitamanas::3427.translation_literal: राम-भक्ति-मय (filled with Ram-devotion) / भरतु (Bharat) / निहारे (saw) / सुर (devas) / स्वारथी (self-seeking) / हहरि (lost heart) / हियँ (in the heart) / हारे (were defeated) / सब कोउ (everyone) / राम-प्रेम-मय (filled with Ram-love) / पेखा (saw) / भए (became) / अलेख (uncountable) / सोच (confusion) / बस (under the control of) / लेखा (count)
ramacharitamanas::3427.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3427.essence: Devotion makes selfishness lose its footing.
ramacharitamanas::3427.simple_meaning: Bharat is seen as full of devotion to Ram, and everyone else appears overwhelmed by that same love. Even the self-interested devas lose confidence before it.
ramacharitamanas::3427.simple_insight: Real devotion changes the whole atmosphere; selfish motives suddenly look small.
ramacharitamanas::3427.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's refusal of power has become visible to everyone. The devas look on and realise this scene is not about politics anymore: Bharat is soaked in Ram-bhakti, and the whole gathering is being transformed by that love.
ramacharitamanas::3427.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where someone has quietly chosen loyalty over advantage. The mood shifts instantly, and all the clever self-interest in the room starts to look thin.
ramacharitamanas::3427.insight: It shifts attention from calculation to the contagious force of sincere love and loyalty.

ramacharitamanas::3428.verse_sanskrit: रामु सनेह सकोच बस कह ससोच सुरराजु। रचहु प्रपंचहि पंच मिलि नाहिं त भयउ अकाजु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3428.verse_hindi: देवराज इन्द्र सोच में भरकर कहने लगे कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी तो स्नेह और संकोच के वश में हैं, इसलिए सब लोग मिलकर कुछ प्रपंच (माया) रचो, नहीं तो काम बिगड़ा (ही समझो) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3428.english_translation: Lord Indra, troubled with worry, said, 'Ram is held back by affection and modesty. All of you together create some scheme; otherwise the plan will surely fail.'
ramacharitamanas::3428.translation_literal: रामु (Ram) / सनेह (affection) / सकोच (modesty, hesitation) / बस (under the control of) / कह (said) / ससोच (with worry) / सुरराजु (king of the gods, Indra) / रचहु (create) / प्रपंचहि (a scheme, illusion) / पंच (five, all of you) / मिलि (together) / नाहिं (otherwise not) / त (then) / भयउ (became) / अकाजु (failure, bad outcome)
ramacharitamanas::3428.speaker: Indra
ramacharitamanas::3428.essence: Fear looks for a scheme when it cannot face gentleness directly.
ramacharitamanas::3428.simple_meaning: Indra sees that Ram's gentle nature may stop him from acting, so he urges the other gods to work together and create a plan.
ramacharitamanas::3428.simple_insight: Not every obstacle is force; sometimes hesitation itself needs to be answered.
ramacharitamanas::3428.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the gods watch Bharat's devotion and fear their own design may collapse. Indra, anxious and calculating, tells the others that Ram's affection and restraint make him vulnerable to a scheme. The verse is a tactical aside, not the teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::3428.modern_relevance: A group chat starts spinning a workaround because the person you need to persuade is too kind to push back. The pressure feels clever, but it is really fear talking.
ramacharitamanas::3428.insight: It reveals how anxious minds try to exploit gentleness when they cannot meet it honestly.

ramacharitamanas::3429.verse_sanskrit: सुरन्ह सुमिरि सारदा सराही। देबि देव सरनागत पाही॥ फेरि भरत मति करि निज माया। पालु बिबुध कुल करि छल छाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3429.verse_hindi: देवताओं ने सरस्वती का स्मरण कर उनकी सराहना (स्तुति) की और कहा- हे देवी! देवता आपके शरणागत हैं, उनकी रक्षा कीजिए। अपनी माया रचकर भरतजी की बुद्धि को फेर दीजिए और छल की छाया कर देवताओं के कुल का पालन (रक्षा) कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3429.english_translation: The devas remembered and praised Saraswati: “O goddess, the devas have taken refuge in you. Protect us. Turn Bharat’s mind with your own power and, through a veil of deception, preserve the lineage of the devas.”
ramacharitamanas::3429.translation_literal: सुरन्ह (the devas) / सुमिरि (remembering) / सारदा (Saraswati) / सराही (praised) / देबि (O goddess) / देव (devas) / सरनागत (those who have taken refuge) / पाही (protect) / फेरि (turn) / भरत (Bharat) / मति (mind) / करि (making) / निज (your own) / माया (power of illusion) / पालु (preserve) / बिबुध (devas) / कुल (lineage) / करि (through) / छल (deception) / छाया (veil/shadow)
ramacharitamanas::3429.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3429.essence: Fear can turn even the powerful toward deception.
ramacharitamanas::3429.simple_meaning: The devas pray to Saraswati to save them by changing Bharat’s mind through her power of illusion.
ramacharitamanas::3429.simple_insight: Not every plea is noble; sometimes fear makes even higher beings ask for manipulation.
ramacharitamanas::3429.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the devas see Bharat’s devotion to Ram and panic that their own plans may fail. They invoke Saraswati and ask her to bend Bharat’s mind through illusion, showing how threatened self-interest can become even in a divine court.
ramacharitamanas::3429.modern_relevance: A room full of people starts quietly steering the conversation because they fear losing influence. The verse shows how quickly anxiety turns into manipulation.
ramacharitamanas::3429.insight: It exposes the mind’s willingness to use cleverness when it cannot win by honesty.

ramacharitamanas::3430.verse_sanskrit: बिबुध बिनय सुनि देबि सयानी। बोली सुर स्वारथ जड़ जानी॥ मो सन कहहु भरत मति फेरू। लोचन सहस न सूझ सुमेरू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3430.verse_hindi: देवताओं की विनती सुनकर और देवताओं को स्वार्थ के वश होने से मूर्ख जानकर बुद्धिमती सरस्वतीजी बोलीं- मुझसे कह रहे हो कि भरतजी की मति पलट दो! हजार नेत्रों से भी तुमको सुमेरू नहीं सूझ पड़ता! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3430.english_translation: After hearing the gods’ plea, the wise goddess said, knowing the gods were driven by self-interest: “You ask me to turn Bharat’s mind? Even with a thousand eyes, you still cannot see Mount Sumeru.”
ramacharitamanas::3430.translation_literal: बिबुध (gods) / बिनय (plea) / सुनि (hearing) / देबि (goddess) / सयानी (wise) / बोली (spoke) / सुर (gods) / स्वारथ (self-interest) / जड़ (foolish) / जानी (knowing)॥ / मो (to me) / सन (from) / कहहु (you say) / भरत (Bharat) / मति (mind) / फेरू (turn) / लोचन (eyes) / सहस (thousand) / न (not) / सूझ (see) / सुमेरू (Mount Sumeru) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3430.speaker: Saraswati
ramacharitamanas::3430.essence: A pure mind cannot be bent by selfish schemes.
ramacharitamanas::3430.simple_meaning: The goddess sees that the gods are acting out of self-interest, and she refuses their request. Bharat's mind is so steady and noble that they cannot even understand it, let alone change it.
ramacharitamanas::3430.simple_insight: Clear seeing protects what is pure from manipulation.
ramacharitamanas::3430.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the gods worry that Bharat's unwavering devotion to Ram will block their plan. They ask Saraswati to twist his mind. She sees through their motive at once and answers that their own selfishness makes them blind to Bharat's greatness.
ramacharitamanas::3430.modern_relevance: A group chat starts plotting how to nudge someone into doing what benefits everyone else. One person quietly refuses the manipulation because they can see the motive behind it. That steadiness is what Saraswati defends here.
ramacharitamanas::3430.insight: It shifts you from trying to control noble people to recognising when your own motives are clouding your judgment.

ramacharitamanas::3431.verse_sanskrit: बिधि हरि हर माया बड़ि भारी। सोउ न भरत मति सकइ निहारी॥ सो मति मोहि कहत करु भोरी। चंदिनि कर कि चंडकर चोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3431.verse_hindi: ब्रह्मा, विष्णु और महेश की माया बड़ी प्रबल है! किन्तु वह भी भरतजी की बुद्धि की ओर ताक नहीं सकती। उस बुद्धि को, तुम मुझसे कह रहे हो कि, भोली कर दो (भुलावे में डाल दो)! अरे! चाँदनी कहीं प्रचंड किरण वाले सूर्य को चुरा सकती है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3431.english_translation: Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva's illusion is immense, yet it cannot even look at Bharat's mind. And you ask me to make that mind foolish? Can moonlight steal the blazing sun?
ramacharitamanas::3431.translation_literal: बिधि (Brahma) / हरि (Vishnu, Ram) / हर (Shiva) / माया (illusion) / बड़ि (great) / भारी (heavy, immense) / सोउ (even that) / न (not) / भरत (Bharat) / मति (mind, understanding) / सकइ (can) / निहारी (look at, observe)॥ / सो (that) / मति (understanding) / मोहि (to me) / कहत (saying) / करु (make) / भोरी (foolish, naive) / चंदिनि (moonlight) / कर (of) / कि (what, can) / चंडकर (blazing sun) / चोरी (steal) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3431.speaker: Saraswati
ramacharitamanas::3431.essence: A mind held by Ram cannot be tricked by illusion.
ramacharitamanas::3431.simple_meaning: Even the strongest illusion cannot touch Bharat's understanding, because his heart is already filled with Ram. Saraswati refuses the request to make him foolish.
ramacharitamanas::3431.simple_insight: Real devotion makes the mind hard to mislead.
ramacharitamanas::3431.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the gods ask Saraswati to confuse Bharat so their plan can continue. She sees the truth clearly: Bharat's mind is already fixed on Ram, and no force of illusion can overpower that steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::3431.modern_relevance: Someone tries to twist your words in a family group chat, but you already know what matters. When your values are anchored, manipulation has less room to enter.
ramacharitamanas::3431.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing devotion as weakness to seeing it as protection against confusion.

ramacharitamanas::3432.verse_sanskrit: भरत हृदयँ सिय राम निवासू। तहँ कि तिमिर जहँ तरनि प्रकासू॥ अस कहि सारद गइ बिधि लोका। बिबुध बिकल निसि मानहुँ कोका ॥
ramacharitamanas::3432.verse_hindi: भरतजी के हृदय में श्री सीता-रामजी का निवास है। जहाँ सूर्य का प्रकाश है, वहाँ कहीं अँधेरा रह सकता है? ऐसा कहकर सरस्वतीजी ब्रह्मलोक को चली गईं। देवता ऐसे व्याकुल हुए जैसे रात्रि में चकवा व्याकुल होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3432.english_translation: Bharat's heart is where Sita and Ram dwell. Where sunlight shines, how can darkness remain? Saying this, Saraswati returned to Brahmaloka. The gods were restless, like chakravaka birds at night.
ramacharitamanas::3432.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat's) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / सिय राम (Sita and Ram) / निवासू (dwelling) / तहँ (there) / कि (how) / तिमिर (darkness) / जहँ (where) / तरनि (sun) / प्रकासू (light) ॥ अस (thus) / कहि (saying) / सारद (Saraswati) / गइ (went) / बिधि (Brahma's) / लोका (realm) / बिबुध (the gods) / बिकल (restless) / निसि (night) / मानहुँ (as if) / कोका (chakravaka birds) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3432.speaker: Saraswati
ramacharitamanas::3432.essence: Where Ram dwells in the heart, darkness has no foothold.
