ramacharitamanas::3432.simple_meaning: Bharat's heart is already filled with Ram and Sita, so there is no place for darkness there. Saraswati says this and leaves, while the gods remain agitated.
ramacharitamanas::3432.simple_insight: A heart held by devotion does not stay confused for long.
ramacharitamanas::3432.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Saraswati has just defended Bharat's purity against the gods' doubts. She declares that Ram and Sita already live in Bharat's heart, so no darkness can enter there. Her answer ends the argument and exposes the gods' restless fear.
ramacharitamanas::3432.modern_relevance: You are exhausted after defending someone decent from unfair gossip, and the room still feels tense. This verse reminds you that a heart anchored in love and loyalty cannot be easily poisoned.
ramacharitamanas::3432.insight: It shifts attention from suspicion to the inner quality that makes devotion unshakeable.

ramacharitamanas::3433.verse_sanskrit: सुर स्वारथी मलीन मन कीन्ह कुमंत्र कुठाटु। रचि प्रपंच माया प्रबल भय भ्रम अरति उचाटु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3433.verse_hindi: मलिन मन वाले स्वार्थी देवताओं ने बुरी सलाह करके बुरा ठाट (षड्यन्त्र) रचा। प्रबल माया-जाल रचकर भय, भ्रम, अप्रीति और उच्चाटन फैला दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3433.english_translation: The selfish, impure-minded devas plotted a bad scheme. They wove a powerful web of illusion, spreading fear, confusion, dislike, and restlessness.
ramacharitamanas::3433.translation_literal: सुर (devas) / स्वारथी (selfish) / मलीन (impure) / मन (mind) / कीन्ह (made) / कुमंत्र (bad counsel) / कुठाटु (evil scheme) / रचि (having woven) / प्रपंच (deceptive display) / माया (illusion) / प्रबल (powerful) / भय (fear) / भ्रम (confusion) / अरति (dislike) / उचाटु (restlessness)
ramacharitamanas::3433.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3433.essence: Selfish minds can manufacture fear, confusion, and unrest.
ramacharitamanas::3433.simple_meaning: Selfish, impure-minded devas created a harmful plot and used illusion to stir fear, confusion, dislike, and restlessness.
ramacharitamanas::3433.simple_insight: A crooked mind can turn even power into disturbance.
ramacharitamanas::3433.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the courtly and cosmic fallout of Bharat’s devotion is being described. Self-serving devas, unable to bear the situation, hatch a deceitful plan. Their plot spreads fear and confusion, setting up the next turn in the story.
ramacharitamanas::3433.modern_relevance: A group chat starts spinning rumors before a family meeting, and suddenly everyone feels tense for no clear reason. This verse names that atmosphere: fear and confusion can be manufactured.
ramacharitamanas::3433.insight: It shows how selfish intent distorts perception and turns collective energy into anxiety.

ramacharitamanas::3434.verse_sanskrit: करि कुचालि सोचत सुरराजू। भरत हाथ सबु काजु अकाजू॥ गए जनकु रघुनाथ समीपा। सनमाने सब रबिकुल दीपा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3434.verse_hindi: कुचाल करके देवराज इन्द्र सोचने लगे कि काम का बनना-बिगड़ना सब भरतजी के हाथ है। इधर राजा जनकजी (मुनि वशिष्ठ आदि के साथ) श्री रघुनाथजी के पास गए। सूर्यकुल के दीपक श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सबका सम्मान किया, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3434.english_translation: By crooked means, Indra kept worrying, thinking that everything depended on Bharata's hands. Meanwhile King Janaka went to Raghunatha, and the lamp of Raghu's line honoured everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3434.translation_literal: करि (doing) / कुचालि (crooked means) / सोचत (thinking) / सुरराजू (king of the devas, Indra) / भरत (Bharata) / हाथ (in the hand) / सबु (all) / काजु (work) / अकाजू (unwork, harm) / गए (went) / जनकु (Janaka) / रघुनाथ (Raghunatha) / समीपा (near) / सनमाने (honoured) / सब (all) / रबिकुल (sun-line) / दीपा (lamp)
ramacharitamanas::3434.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3434.essence: Crooked power worries; Ram answers with honour.
ramacharitamanas::3434.simple_meaning: Indra schemed and worried, thinking Bharata could shape everything. At the same time, Janaka went to Ram, and Ram honoured everyone with dignity.
ramacharitamanas::3434.simple_insight: Power looks busy and anxious here, but Ram's presence quietly restores respect and order.
ramacharitamanas::3434.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's tense aftermath, Indra is still scheming, while Janaka approaches Ram with the sages. The verse shifts from hidden manipulation to a scene of honour, showing Ram receiving everyone with royal grace.
ramacharitamanas::3434.modern_relevance: A group chat fills with suspicion, one person quietly spins the story, and another walks into the room and treats everyone with calm respect.
ramacharitamanas::3434.insight: It contrasts anxious control with dignified conduct, showing that true authority does not need manipulation.

ramacharitamanas::3435.verse_sanskrit: समय समाज धरम अबिरोधा। बोले तब रघुबंस पुरोधा॥ जनक भरत संबादु सुनाई। भरत कहाउति कही सुहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3435.verse_hindi: तब रघुकुल के पुरोहित वशिष्ठजी समय, समाज और धर्म के अविरोधी (अर्थात अनुकूल) वचन बोले। उन्होंने पहले जनकजी और भरतजी का संवाद सुनाया। फिर भरतजी की कही हुई सुंदर बातें कह सुनाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3435.english_translation: Then the family priest of Raghu's line spoke words suited to the time, the gathering, and dharma. He first recounted the dialogue between Janaka and Bharata, and then repeated Bharata's lovely words.
ramacharitamanas::3435.translation_literal: समय (time) / समाज (assembly) / धरम (dharma) / अबिरोधा (unopposed, fitting) / बोले (spoke) / तब (then) / रघुबंस पुरोधा (the priest of Raghu's line)॥ / जनक (Janaka) / भरत (Bharata) / संबादु (dialogue) / सुनाई (told) / भरत कहाउति (Bharata's sayings) / कही (spoken) / सुहाई (pleasant, beautiful)॥
ramacharitamanas::3435.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3435.essence: Wise speech fits the moment without betraying the truth.
ramacharitamanas::3435.simple_meaning: Vashishtha speaks carefully, choosing words that fit the moment. He retells Janaka and Bharata's conversation and repeats Bharata's noble words.
ramacharitamanas::3435.simple_insight: Sometimes the right words are the ones that preserve peace, timing, and dignity all at once.
ramacharitamanas::3435.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the gathering is tense. Vashishtha, the royal priest, steps in and speaks with perfect tact, making sure his words do not clash with the moment, the assembly, or dharma. He then recounts Janaka and Bharata's exchange so the court can hear Bharata's heart clearly.
ramacharitamanas::3435.modern_relevance: In a family meeting where everyone is already upset, one person slows down, chooses careful words, and repeats the exact sentence that keeps the room from breaking apart.
ramacharitamanas::3435.insight: It shows that wise speech is not just true, but well-timed, socially aware, and aligned with dharma.

ramacharitamanas::3436.verse_sanskrit: तात राम जस आयसु देहू। सो सबु करै मोर मत एहू॥ सुनि रघुनाथ जोरि जुग पानी। बोले सत्य सरल मृदु बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3436.verse_hindi: (फिर बोले-) हे तात राम! मेरा मत तो यह है कि तुम जैसी आज्ञा दो, वैसा ही सब करें! यह सुनकर दोनों हाथ जोड़कर श्री रघुनाथजी सत्य, सरल और कोमल वाणी बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3436.english_translation: Then he said, “Father, give me Ram’s command. I think everyone should do only that.” Hearing this, Raghunath joined both palms and spoke with truth, simplicity, and gentleness.
ramacharitamanas::3436.translation_literal: तात (father) / राम (Ram) / जस (as) / आयसु (command) / देहू (give) / सो (that) / सबु (all) / करै (do) / मोर (my) / मत (opinion) / एहू (this) / सुनि (hearing) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / जोरि (joining) / जुग (both) / पानी (palms) / बोले (spoke) / सत्य (true) / सरल (simple) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (speech)
ramacharitamanas::3436.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3436.essence: True greatness bows first and speaks gently.
ramacharitamanas::3436.simple_meaning: Janak says that Ram’s command should guide everyone. Ram responds with folded hands and speaks gently and truthfully.
ramacharitamanas::3436.simple_insight: Humility can be stronger than authority.
ramacharitamanas::3436.detailed_meaning: In Mithila, Janak is arranging the next step of the marriage proceedings. He points away from status and toward Ram’s will. Ram answers not with pride, but with folded hands and gentle speech, showing the ideal of respectful conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3436.modern_relevance: You’re in a family group chat where everyone waits for the most important person to decide. The calmest voice is the one that lowers itself first.
ramacharitamanas::3436.insight: It shifts leadership from control to humility, showing that real dignity does not need to assert itself.

ramacharitamanas::3437.verse_sanskrit: बिद्यमान आपुनि मिथिलेसू। मोर कहब सब भाँति भदेसू॥ राउर राय रजायसु होई। राउरि सपथ सही सिर सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3437.verse_hindi: आपके और मिथिलेश्वर जनकजी के विद्यमान रहते मेरा कुछ कहना सब प्रकार से भद्दा (अनुचित) है। आपकी और महाराज की जो आज्ञा होगी, मैं आपकी शपथ करके कहता हूँ वह सत्य ही सबको शिरोधार्य होगी॥
ramacharitamanas::3437.english_translation: While Mithila's king Janak is still present, anything I say would be improper. Whatever command you and the king give, I swear by your word alone, it will be accepted by all.
ramacharitamanas::3437.translation_literal: बिद्यमान (still present) / आपुनि (yourself) / मिथिलेसू (the king of Mithila) / मोर (my) / कहब (saying) / सब भाँति (in every way) / भदेसू (proper) / राउर (your) / राय (king) / रजायसु (command) / होई (will be) / राउरि (your) / सपथ (oath) / सही (true) / सिर (head) / सोई (that) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3437.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3437.essence: Humility lets truth arrive without self-assertion.
ramacharitamanas::3437.simple_meaning: Ram says it is improper for him to speak while Janak is present. He places both authority and truth in the hands of his elders.
ramacharitamanas::3437.simple_insight: There is peace in knowing you do not need to dominate the room.
ramacharitamanas::3437.detailed_meaning: In Janak's assembly, Ram answers with deep humility. He refuses to speak over the elder king and says he will follow whatever command is given. The moment reveals his perfect courtesy and acceptance of rightful authority.
ramacharitamanas::3437.modern_relevance: You are in a tense family meeting and everyone keeps interrupting. Instead of forcing your point, you wait, respect the elder voice, and let the right order return.
ramacharitamanas::3437.insight: It teaches you to step back from ego and let proper authority or context guide the exchange.

ramacharitamanas::3438.verse_sanskrit: राम सपथ सुनि मुनि जनकु सकुचे सभा समेत। सकल बिलोकत भरत मुखु बनइ न ऊतरु देत ॥
ramacharitamanas::3438.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की शपथ सुनकर सभा समेत मुनि और जनकजी सकुचा गए (स्तम्भित रह गए)। किसी से उत्तर देते नहीं बनता, सब लोग भरतजी का मुँह ताक रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3438.english_translation: Hearing Ram's solemn vow, the sage, Janak, and the whole assembly fell silent. Everyone looked at Bharat, but no one could speak.
ramacharitamanas::3438.translation_literal: राम (Ram's) / सपथ (solemn vow) / सुनि (hearing) / मुनि जनकु (the sage and Janak) / सकुचे (felt awkwardly silent) / सभा समेत (along with the assembly) / सकल (everyone) / बिलोकत (looking) / भरत मुखु (at Bharat's face) / बनइ न (was not able) / ऊतरु (answer) / देत (giving)
ramacharitamanas::3438.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3438.essence: Ram's vow leaves even the wise without words.
ramacharitamanas::3438.simple_meaning: Ram's vow leaves everyone in the hall silent and uneasy. They all look to Bharat, but no one can answer.
ramacharitamanas::3438.simple_insight: Some moments are too serious for easy words. Silence itself can show respect.
ramacharitamanas::3438.detailed_meaning: In Janak's assembly, Ram's solemn vow has just been heard. The sage, Janak, and everyone present are left speechless, turning toward Bharat for a response. This verse captures the pause before Bharat's own restraint and devotion become visible.
ramacharitamanas::3438.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after someone speaks with complete sincerity. Everyone feels the weight of it, and the real response is not noise but restraint.
ramacharitamanas::3438.insight: It shows how a sacred promise can stop argument and force everyone into stillness.

ramacharitamanas::3439.verse_sanskrit: सभा सकुच बस भरत निहारी। राम बंधु धरि धीरजु भारी॥ कुसमउ देखि सनेहु सँभारा। बढ़त बिंधि जिमि घटज निवारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3439.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने सभा को संकोच के वश देखा। रामबंधु (भरतजी) ने बड़ा भारी धीरज धरकर और कुसमय देखकर अपने (उमड़ते हुए) प्रेम को संभाला, जैसे बढ़ते हुए विन्ध्याचल को अगस्त्यजी ने रोका था ॥
ramacharitamanas::3439.english_translation: Bharat looked at the assembly with great restraint. Seeing the wrong moment, Ram's brother held back his rising love, just as Agastya stopped the growing Vindhya.
ramacharitamanas::3439.translation_literal: सभा (assembly) / सकुच (with embarrassment) / बस (under the control of) / भरत (Bharat) / निहारी (having seen) / राम बंधु (Ram's brother) / धरि (holding) / धीरजु (patience) / भारी (great) / कुसमउ (wrong moment) / देखि (seeing) / सनेहु (love) / सँभारा (held back) / बढ़त (growing) / बिंधि (Vindhya) / जिमि (as) / घटज (Agastya) / निवारा (stopped)
ramacharitamanas::3439.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3439.essence: True love can be strongest when it knows when to wait.
ramacharitamanas::3439.simple_meaning: Bharat sees the tense assembly and, though love rises in him, he restrains himself because the moment is not right.
ramacharitamanas::3439.simple_insight: Love is not always loud; sometimes its strength is in holding back at the right time.
ramacharitamanas::3439.detailed_meaning: In Janak's assembly, everyone is tense and embarrassed after the oath to Ram. Bharat, Ram's brother, feels a surge of devotion and emotion, but he does not rush forward. He steadies himself and waits, because this is not the moment to speak.
ramacharitamanas::3439.modern_relevance: You’re about to text back in anger after a family argument, but you pause and reread the room. That restraint can protect what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::3439.insight: It teaches you to regulate emotion by reading context, not by suppressing feeling altogether.

ramacharitamanas::3440.verse_sanskrit: सोक कनकलोचन मति छोनी। हरी बिमल गुन गन जगजोनी॥ भरत बिबेक बराहँ बिसाला। अनायास उधरी तेहि काला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3440.verse_hindi: शोक रूपी हिरण्याक्ष ने (सारी सभा की) बुद्धि रूपी पृथ्वी को हर लिया जो विमल गुण समूह रूपी जगत की योनि (उत्पन्न करने वाली) थी। भरतजी के विवेक रूपी विशाल वराह (वराह रूप धारी भगवान) ने (शोक रूपी हिरण्याक्ष को नष्ट कर) बिना ही परिश्रम उसका उद्धार कर दिया! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3440.english_translation: Grief had swallowed the mind of the whole assembly, which was the source of pure virtues. Bharat's vast discernment, like a mighty boar, lifted it all without effort.
ramacharitamanas::3440.translation_literal: सोक (grief) / कनकलोचन (golden-eyed) / मति (mind) / छोनी (earth) / हरी (swallowed away) / बिमल (pure) / गुन गन (groups of virtues) / जगजोनी (source of the world)॥ / भरत (Bharat) / बिबेक (discernment) / बराहँ (boar) / बिसाला (vast) / अनायास (without effort) / उधरी (was lifted) / तेहि काला (at that time)॥
ramacharitamanas::3440.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3440.essence: Clear discernment can rescue minds buried in grief.
ramacharitamanas::3440.simple_meaning: Grief had overwhelmed everyone, but Bharat's discernment cut through it and restored clarity without any struggle.
ramacharitamanas::3440.simple_insight: You can steady a whole room when you stay clear inside.
ramacharitamanas::3440.detailed_meaning: In the tense assembly at Ayodhya, everyone is shaken by the painful truth of Ram's exile. Bharat stands there, and his wisdom becomes like a rescuing force: it lifts the heaviness of grief from the minds around him without force or drama.
ramacharitamanas::3440.modern_relevance: You walk into a family room after bad news, and everyone is frozen. You don't fix the loss, but your calm, steady clarity keeps the whole moment from collapsing.
ramacharitamanas::3440.insight: It shifts you from being absorbed by collective emotion to becoming the stabilizing presence that helps others think clearly.

ramacharitamanas::3441.verse_sanskrit: करि प्रनामु सब कहँ कर जोरे। रामु राउ गुर साधु निहोरे॥ छमब आजु अति अनुचित मोरा। कहउँ बदन मृदु बचन कठोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3441.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने प्रणाम करके सबके प्रति हाथ जोड़े तथा श्री रामचन्द्रजी, राजा जनकजी, गुरु वशिष्ठजी और साधु-संत सबसे विनती की और कहा- आज मेरे इस अत्यन्त अनुचित बर्ताव को क्षमा कीजिएगा। मैं कोमल (छोटे) मुख से कठोर (धृष्टतापूर्ण) वचन कह रहा हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3441.english_translation: Bharat bowed to everyone with folded hands and humbly begged Ram, King Janak, Guru Vashishtha, and the saints: forgive my utterly improper conduct today. With a gentle face, I am speaking harsh words.
ramacharitamanas::3441.translation_literal: करि (having done) / प्रनामु (bowing) / सब कहँ (to everyone) / कर (hands) / जोरे (joined) / रामु (Ram) / राउ (king) / गुर (teacher) / साधु (saints) / निहोरे (humbly begged) / छमब (forgive) / आजु (today) / अति (very) / अनुचित (improper) / मोरा (my) / कहउँ (I speak) / बदन (face/mouth) / मृदु (gentle) / बचन (words) / कठोरा (harsh)
ramacharitamanas::3441.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3441.essence: Respect can carry even the hardest words.
ramacharitamanas::3441.simple_meaning: Bharat shows deep humility before speaking. He asks everyone to forgive him because he knows his words may sound harsh, even though his intention is respectful.
ramacharitamanas::3441.simple_insight: You can be direct without being arrogant. Humility softens even difficult speech.
ramacharitamanas::3441.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram, Janak, Vashishtha, and the gathered saints after holding back his grief. He bows first, then asks forgiveness before saying anything difficult. The moment shows how reverence can carry even painful truth.
ramacharitamanas::3441.modern_relevance: You’re about to send a message that could sting, so you rewrite it twice and add a softer opening. Bharat’s instinct is the same: respect first, then the hard sentence.
ramacharitamanas::3441.insight: It teaches you to frame difficult speech with humility, so truth does not become aggression.

ramacharitamanas::3442.verse_sanskrit: हियँ सुमिरी सारदा सुहाई। मानस तें मुख पंकज आई॥ बिमल बिबेक धरम नय साली। भरत भारती मंजु मराली ॥
ramacharitamanas::3442.verse_hindi: फिर उन्होंने हृदय में सुहावनी सरस्वती का स्मरण किया। वे मानस से (उनके मन रूपी मानसरोवर से) उनके मुखारविंद पर आ विराजीं। निर्मल विवेक, धर्म और नीति से युक्त भरतजी की वाणी सुंदर हंसिनी (के समान गुण-दोष का विवेचन करने वाली) है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3442.english_translation: Then he remembered lovely Saraswati in his heart, and she came from the lake of his mind to his lotus face. Filled with pure discernment, dharma, and wise conduct, Bharat's speech is like a graceful swan.
ramacharitamanas::3442.translation_literal: हियँ (in the heart) / सुमिरी (remembering) / सारदा (Saraswati) / सुहाई (lovely) / मानस (mind-lake) / तें (from) / मुख पंकज (lotus face) / आई (came) / बिमल (pure) / बिबेक (discernment) / धरम (dharma) / नय (policy/conduct) / साली (endowed with) / भरत (Bharat's) / भारती (speech) / मंजु (graceful) / मराली (swan)
ramacharitamanas::3442.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3442.essence: Clear discernment turns speech into something beautiful and trustworthy.
ramacharitamanas::3442.simple_meaning: Bharat remembers Saraswati, and his speech becomes beautiful because it is guided by clear discernment, dharma, and wise conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3442.simple_insight: When your mind is clear, your words stop being heavy and start carrying grace.
ramacharitamanas::3442.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before the gathered people after Ram's exile has broken the kingdom's heart. Before speaking, he inwardly remembers Saraswati. The verse shows that his words will not come from pride or grief, but from clarity, dharma, and restraint.
ramacharitamanas::3442.modern_relevance: You are about to speak in a family meeting after a painful argument. If you pause long enough to remember what is true, your words can calm the room instead of adding fuel.
ramacharitamanas::3442.insight: It teaches you to let discernment guide speech before emotion takes over.

ramacharitamanas::3443.verse_sanskrit: निरखि बिबेक बिलोचनन्हि सिथिल सनेहँ समाजु। करि प्रनामु बोले भरतु सुमिरि सीय रघुराजु ॥
ramacharitamanas::3443.verse_hindi: विवेक के नेत्रों से सारे समाज को प्रेम से शिथिल देख, सबको प्रणाम कर, श्री सीताजी और श्री रघुनाथजी का स्मरण करके भरतजी बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3443.english_translation: Seeing the gathering with the eye of discernment softened by love, he bowed to all and, remembering Sita and the lord of Raghu, Bharata spoke.
ramacharitamanas::3443.translation_literal: निरखि (seeing) / बिबेक (discernment) / बिलोचनन्हि (with the eyes) / सिथिल (softened) / सनेहँ (with love) / समाजु (the gathering) / करि (having done) / प्रनामु (bowing) / बोले (spoke) / भरतु (Bharata) / सुमिरि (remembering) / सीय (Sita) / रघुराजु (the lord of Raghu)
ramacharitamanas::3443.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3443.essence: Clear seeing lets love replace tension before words begin.
ramacharitamanas::3443.simple_meaning: Bharat looks at everyone with calm discernment and loving respect. He bows to all, remembers Sita and Ram, and begins to speak.
ramacharitamanas::3443.simple_insight: A clear heart can see people without hardness and still honor them all.
ramacharitamanas::3443.detailed_meaning: In the royal assembly at Chitrakoot, Bharat stands before Ram, Sita, the gurus, and the elders. He has already softened the room with humility. This line shows the moment just before his great speech: he sees everyone clearly, bows, and turns inward to Ram and Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3443.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone expects tension, but you pause, breathe, and see people clearly before speaking. That small softness changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::3443.insight: It trains you to meet a charged room with discernment first, reaction second.

ramacharitamanas::3444.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु पितु मातु सुहृद गुर स्वामी। पूज्य परम हित अंतरजामी॥ सरल सुसाहिबु सील निधानू। प्रनतपाल सर्बग्य सुजानू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3444.verse_hindi: हे प्रभु! आप पिता, माता, सुहृद् (मित्र), गुरु, स्वामी, पूज्य, परम हितैषी और अन्तर्यामी हैं। सरल हृदय, श्रेष्ठ मालिक, शील के भंडार, शरणागत की रक्षा करने वाले, सर्वज्ञ, सुजान, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3444.english_translation: O Lord, you are father, mother, friend, teacher, and master. You are worthy of worship, the highest benefactor, and the inner knower. You are simple-hearted, a noble lord, a treasury of character, protector of those who seek refuge, all-knowing, and wise.
ramacharitamanas::3444.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / सुहृद (friend) / गुर (teacher) / स्वामी (master) / पूज्य (worthy of worship) / परम (highest) / हित (benefit) / अंतरजामी (inner knower) / सरल (simple-hearted) / सुसाहिबु (noble lord) / सील (character) / निधानू (treasury) / प्रनतपाल (protector of those who seek refuge) / सर्बग्य (all-knowing) / सुजानू (wise)
ramacharitamanas::3444.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3444.essence: Ram is every true refuge you could ever need.
ramacharitamanas::3444.simple_meaning: Bharat praises Ram as the one who fulfills every loving role at once: parent, friend, teacher, master, protector, and inner knower.
ramacharitamanas::3444.simple_insight: You do not have to earn care from the one you trust most.
ramacharitamanas::3444.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram with total humility. After the grief and rupture of exile, he speaks not as a claimant to power but as a surrendered devotee, naming Ram as father, mother, friend, teacher, master, and inner knower.
ramacharitamanas::3444.modern_relevance: After a family argument, you finally stop defending yourself and say, 'You know what I need better than I do.' That surrender is the mood of this verse.
ramacharitamanas::3444.insight: It shifts devotion from formal praise to complete dependence on Ram's care and understanding.

ramacharitamanas::3445.verse_sanskrit: समरथ सरनागत हितकारी। गुनगाहकु अवगुन अघ हारी॥ स्वामि गोसाँइहि सरिस गोसाईं। मोहि समान मैं साइँ दोहाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3445.verse_hindi: समर्थ, शरणागत का हित करने वाले, गुणों का आदर करने वाले और अवगुणों तथा पापों को हरने वाले हैं। हे गोसाईं! आप सरीखे स्वामी आप ही हैं और स्वामी के साथ द्रोह करने में मेरे समान मैं ही हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3445.english_translation: You are powerful, the refuge of those who surrender, one who values virtue, and one who removes faults and sins. O lord, there is no master like you. I alone am the one who has betrayed my master.
ramacharitamanas::3445.translation_literal: समरथ (powerful) / सरनागत (one who has surrendered) / हितकारी (benefactor) / गुनगाहकु (one who values virtues) / अवगुन (faults) / अघ (sins) / हारी (remover) ॥ / स्वामि (master) / गोसाँइहि (lord) / सरिस (like) / गोसाईं (lord) / मोहि (me) / समान (equal) / मैं (I) / साइँ (master) / दोहाईं (betrayal) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3445.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3445.essence: Refuge is real, but betrayal is never hidden from the one who knows you.
ramacharitamanas::3445.simple_meaning: Bharat praises Ram as the protector of anyone who takes refuge in him, then blames himself for failing his duty and loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::3445.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing refuge is real, and humility in admitting when you have fallen short.
ramacharitamanas::3445.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram after the exile has torn the family apart. He first honours Ram as the protector of those who surrender, then turns inward and confesses that the fault lies with him for violating loyalty and duty.
ramacharitamanas::3445.modern_relevance: You finally call someone after letting them down, and the first thing you say is not an excuse. It is the truth: they were steady; you were not.
ramacharitamanas::3445.insight: It shifts the mind from self-justification to honest surrender and responsibility.

ramacharitamanas::3446.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु पितु बचन मोह बस पेली। आयउँ इहाँ समाजु सकेली॥ जग भल पोच ऊँच अरु नीचू। अमिअ अमरपद माहुरु मीचू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3446.verse_hindi: मैं मोहवश प्रभु (आप) के और पिताजी के वचनों का उल्लंघन कर और समाज बटोरकर यहाँ आया हूँ। जगत में भले-बुरे, ऊँचे और नीचे, अमृत और अमर पद (देवताओं का पद), विष और मृत्यु आदि- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3446.english_translation: Overcome by delusion, I broke my lord's and my father's word and came here with the whole assembly. In this world, there are the good and the bad, the high and the low, nectar and the deathly poison, even the immortal realm and death itself.
ramacharitamanas::3446.translation_literal: प्रभु (lord) / पितु (father) / बचन (word) / मोह बस (under the sway of delusion) / पेली (broke, violated) / आयउँ (came) / इहाँ (here) / समाजु (assembly, company) / सकेली (gathering together) / जग (world) / भल (good) / पोच (bad) / ऊँच (high) / अरु (and) / नीचू (low) / अमिअ (nectar) / अमरपद (immortal realm) / माहुरु (poison) / मीचू (death)
ramacharitamanas::3446.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3446.essence: Delusion makes you violate what you already know is right.
ramacharitamanas::3446.simple_meaning: Bharat admits that confusion led him to break his father and lord's command and come with the gathered court. He also reflects that the world contains opposites: good and bad, high and low, nectar and poison.
ramacharitamanas::3446.simple_insight: Honesty begins when you stop defending the mistake and see how confusion warped your judgment.
ramacharitamanas::3446.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram after the kingdom's crisis and speaks with painful self-accusation. He confesses that he came because of delusion, against the words of his father and lord, and then widens the vision to the mixed nature of the world itself.
ramacharitamanas::3446.modern_relevance: You replay the text thread where you ignored a clear boundary, then tried to justify it afterward. Bharat's honesty cuts through that self-protection and names the confusion before it hardens into pride.
ramacharitamanas::3446.insight: It shifts the mind from excuse-making to clear seeing of how delusion distorts action.

ramacharitamanas::3447.verse_sanskrit: राम रजाइ मेट मन माहीं। देखा सुना कतहुँ कोउ नाहीं॥ सो मैं सब बिधि कीन्हि ढिठाई। प्रभु मानी सनेह सेवकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3447.verse_hindi: किसी को भी कहीं ऐसा नहीं देखा-सुना जो मन में भी श्री रामचन्द्रजी (आप) की आज्ञा को मेट दे। मैंने सब प्रकार से वही ढिठाई की, परन्तु प्रभु ने उस ढिठाई को स्नेह और सेवा मान लिया! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3447.english_translation: I have never seen or heard of anyone who can erase Ram's command even in the mind. I was bold in every way, but the Lord took that boldness as love and service.
ramacharitamanas::3447.translation_literal: राम रजाइ (Ram's command) / मेट (erase) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / देखा सुना (seen or heard) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / कोउ नाहीं (no one) || सो (that) / मैं (I) / सब बिधि (in every way) / कीन्हि (did) / ढिठाई (boldness, insolence) / प्रभु (the Lord) / मानी (accepted) / सनेह (love) / सेवकाई (service)
ramacharitamanas::3447.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3447.essence: Ram can turn even your misstep into loving service.
ramacharitamanas::3447.simple_meaning: No one can erase Ram's command from the heart. Bharat says his own stubborn act was received by Ram as love and service.
ramacharitamanas::3447.simple_insight: Love can transform even a mistake into offering.
ramacharitamanas::3447.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram after the pain of exile and family rupture. He admits that he acted against the expected order, yet Ram did not reject him. Instead, Ram read the act through love.
ramacharitamanas::3447.modern_relevance: You sent the message too sharply, then worried it ruined everything. But the person who loves you may hear the care beneath the clumsiness.
ramacharitamanas::3447.insight: It shifts you from self-condemnation to seeing how sincere intention can redeem imperfect action.

ramacharitamanas::3448.verse_sanskrit: कृपाँ भलाईं आपनी नाथ कीन्ह भल मोर। दूषन भे भूषन सरिस सुजसु चारु चहुँ ओर ॥
ramacharitamanas::3448.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! आपने अपनी कृपा और भलाई से मेरा भला किया, जिससे मेरे दूषण (दोष) भी भूषण (गुण) के समान हो गए और चारों ओर मेरा सुंदर यश छा गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3448.english_translation: O Lord, by your grace and kindness you have done me good. My faults have become ornaments, and my beautiful fame now shines everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::3448.translation_literal: कृपाँ (by grace) / भलाईं (kindness, goodness) / आपनी (your own) / नाथ (Lord) / कीन्ह (did) / भल (good) / मोर (my) / दूषन (faults) / भे (became) / भूषन (ornaments) / सरिस (like) / सुजसु (good fame) / चारु (beautiful) / चहुँ ओर (in all directions)
ramacharitamanas::3448.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3448.essence: Grace can turn your faults into ornaments.
ramacharitamanas::3448.simple_meaning: Ram's kindness has transformed Bharat's shame into honor. What looked like fault has become something beautiful, and his name now shines everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::3448.simple_insight: Being received with love can change how you see your own mistakes.
ramacharitamanas::3448.detailed_meaning: Bharat, standing before Ram after the painful exile has been set in motion, speaks with deep humility. He says Ram's kindness has taken even his faults and made them look like ornaments, filling the world with his good name.
ramacharitamanas::3448.modern_relevance: You sent the apology, expecting distance. Instead, the other person answered with warmth, and your worst moment stopped defining you. Grace can do that.
ramacharitamanas::3448.insight: It shifts self-image from shame to gratitude, showing how loving response can transform guilt into dignity.

ramacharitamanas::3449.verse_sanskrit: राउरि रीति सुबानि बड़ाई। जगत बिदित निगमागम गाई॥ कूर कुटिल खल कुमति कलंकी। नीच निसील निरीस निसंकी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3449.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! आपकी रीति और सुंदर स्वभाव की बड़ाई जगत में प्रसिद्ध है और वेद-शास्त्रों ने गाई है। जो क्रूर, कुटिल, दुष्ट, कुबुद्धि, कलंकी, नीच, शीलरहित, निरीश्वरवादी (नास्तिक) और निःशंक (निडर) है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3449.english_translation: Your noble conduct and beautiful nature are praised throughout the world and sung by the Vedas. Even the cruel, crooked, wicked, ill-minded, stained, low, shameless, irreverent, and fearless...
ramacharitamanas::3449.translation_literal: राउरि (your) / रीति (conduct, way) / सुबानि (beautiful nature) / बड़ाई (praise) / जगत (world) / बिदित (known) / निगमागम (Vedas and scriptures) / गाई (sung) / कूर (cruel) / कुटिल (crooked) / खल (wicked) / कुमति (ill-minded) / कलंकी (stained, tainted) / नीच (low) / निसील (shameless, without conduct) / निरीस (irreverent, without devotion) / निसंकी (fearless, undoubting)
ramacharitamanas::3449.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3449.essence: Ram’s grace is large enough to include even the fallen.
ramacharitamanas::3449.simple_meaning: Your noble conduct is known everywhere, and even the most fallen people are included in your grace.
ramacharitamanas::3449.simple_insight: It softens the heart: no flaw is too deep to be met by grace.
ramacharitamanas::3449.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is praising Ram’s character after surrendering his claim to the throne. He says Ram’s way of being is famous in the world and honored by the scriptures, and that even the worst kinds of people are still within Ram’s reach.
ramacharitamanas::3449.modern_relevance: You’ve written someone off because of their worst behavior, then watched them soften when treated with dignity. This verse remembers that character can transform when grace meets it first.
ramacharitamanas::3449.insight: It shifts judgment into trust, showing that grace can reach even the lowest person.

ramacharitamanas::3450.verse_sanskrit: तेउ सुनि सरन सामुहें आए। सकृत प्रनामु किहें अपनाए॥ देखि दोष कबहुँ न उर आने। सुनि गुन साधु समाज बखाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::3450.verse_hindi: उन्हें भी आपने शरण में सम्मुख आया सुनकर एक बार प्रणाम करने पर ही अपना लिया। उन (शरणागतों) के दोषों को देखकर भी आप कभी हृदय में नहीं लाए और उनके गुणों को सुनकर साधुओं के समाज में उनका बखान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3450.english_translation: Even those who came before you and bowed just once were accepted. You never held their faults in your heart, and when you heard their virtues, you praised them among the noble.
ramacharitamanas::3450.translation_literal: तेउ (even they) / सुनि (hearing) / सरन (to refuge) / सामुहें (before, face-to-face) / आए (came) / सकृत (once) / प्रनामु (bow) / किहें (having done) / अपनाए (accepted) / देखि (seeing) / दोष (faults) / कबहुँ (ever) / न (not) / उर (in the heart) / आने (brought) / सुनि (hearing) / गुन (virtues) / साधु (noble) / समाज (company) / बखाने (praised)
ramacharitamanas::3450.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3450.essence: Surrender meets a heart that remembers your goodness, not your flaws.
ramacharitamanas::3450.simple_meaning: Ram accepts anyone who comes to him in surrender, does not dwell on their faults, and speaks well of their good qualities.
ramacharitamanas::3450.simple_insight: You do not have to arrive perfect to be welcomed. Surrender is met with grace, not a ledger.
ramacharitamanas::3450.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the speaker praises Ram's nature while describing how he treats anyone who comes in surrender. Even a single bow is enough for acceptance. Ram does not keep their faults in mind and lets their good qualities be spoken of openly.
ramacharitamanas::3450.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after making a mess, expecting judgment. Instead, someone meets you without replaying your worst moment. That kind of welcome changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::3450.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to surrender, and from judging others to noticing their goodness.

ramacharitamanas::3451.verse_sanskrit: को साहिब सेवकहि नेवाजी। आपु समाज साज सब साजी॥ निज करतूति न समुझिअ सपनें। सेवक सकुच सोचु उर अपनें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3451.verse_hindi: ऐसा सेवक पर कृपा करने वाला स्वामी कौन है, जो आप ही सेवक का सारा साज-सामान सज दे (उसकी सारी आवश्यकताओं को पूर्ण कर दे) और स्वप्न में भी अपनी कोई करनी न समझकर (अर्थात मैंने सेवक के लिए कुछ किया है, ऐसा न जानकर) उलटा सेवक को संकोच होगा, इसका सोच अपने हृदय में रखे! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3451.english_translation: What master, so gracious to a servant, arranges all the servant’s needs and, without ever thinking, even in a dream, that he has done anything, still worries that the servant may feel shy or troubled?
ramacharitamanas::3451.translation_literal: को (which) / साहिब (master) / सेवकहि (for the servant) / नेवाजी (showing grace) / आपु (yourself) / समाज (arrangement) / साज (equipment, needs) / सब (all) / साजी (arranged) ॥ / निज (own) / करतूति (deed, doing) / न (not) / समुझिअ (understood) / सपनें (even in a dream) / सेवक (servant) / सकुच (shyness, hesitation) / सोचु (worry) / उर (in the heart) / अपनें (own) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3451.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3451.essence: Grace gives fully without making the receiver feel beholden.
ramacharitamanas::3451.simple_meaning: The highest kind of master gives everything a servant needs and never lets the servant feel that a favor was done.
ramacharitamanas::3451.simple_insight: Being cared for can be humble, not humiliating.
ramacharitamanas::3451.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram’s way with devotees in Ayodhyakand. Ram does not just protect or reward; he quietly arranges everything a servant needs and still worries about the servant’s discomfort. This is devotion at its most tender.
ramacharitamanas::3451.modern_relevance: Someone quietly covers your share of the bill, fixes the form you forgot, and never mentions it again. The kindness feels clean because it leaves your dignity intact.
ramacharitamanas::3451.insight: It shifts devotion from transaction to tenderness, showing care that never turns into debt.

ramacharitamanas::3452.verse_sanskrit: सो गोसाइँ नहिं दूसर कोपी। भुजा उठाइ कहउँ पन रोपी॥ पसु नाचत सुक पाठ प्रबीना। गुन गति नट पाठक आधीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3452.verse_hindi: मैं भुजा उठाकर और प्रण रोपकर (बड़े जोर के साथ) कहता हूँ, ऐसा स्वामी आपके सिवा दूसरा कोई नहीं है। (बंदर आदि) पशु नाचते और तोते (सीखे हुए) पाठ में प्रवीण हो जाते हैं, परन्तु तोते का (पाठ प्रवीणता रूप) गुण और पशु के नाचने की गति (क्रमशः) पढ़ाने वाले और नचाने वाले के अधीन है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3452.english_translation: I say with raised arms and a firm vow: there is no lord like you. Animals dance, and parrots become skilled in recitation, but the skill of the parrot and the movement of the animal depend on the teacher and trainer.
ramacharitamanas::3452.translation_literal: सो (that) / गोसाइँ (lord) / नहिं (not) / दूसर (other) / कोपी (angry) / भुजा (arms) / उठाइ (raising) / कहउँ (I say) / पन (vow) / रोपी (fixed)॥ / पसु (animals) / नाचत (dance) / सुक (parrots) / पाठ (recitation) / प्रबीना (skilled) / गुन (skill) / गति (movement) / नट (trainer) / पाठक (teacher) / आधीना (dependent)॥
ramacharitamanas::3452.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3452.essence: Your abilities are not self-made; they still rest in Ram's care.
ramacharitamanas::3452.simple_meaning: No one is as gracious and capable as Ram. Even a creature's skill or movement comes from the one who trains it, so all ability ultimately depends on the divine source.
ramacharitamanas::3452.simple_insight: It softens pride and deepens trust: what looks like your own ability is still being held from beyond you.
ramacharitamanas::3452.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram after describing how he lifts up surrendered devotees and restores their honour. He swears that no other lord matches Ram's grace, because even skill and movement in living beings depend on a guiding power.
ramacharitamanas::3452.modern_relevance: You finally nail the presentation after weeks of practice, and everyone applauds your talent. This verse quietly reminds you that even your steadiness, timing, and nerve were being supported all along.
ramacharitamanas::3452.insight: It shifts credit away from ego and toward the source that makes ability possible.

ramacharitamanas::3453.verse_sanskrit: यों सुधारि सनमानि जन किए साधु सिरमोर। को कृपाल बिनु पालिहै बिरिदावलि बरजोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::3453.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार अपने सेवकों की (बिगड़ी) बात सुधारकर और सम्मान देकर आपने उन्हें साधुओं का शिरोमणि बना दिया। कृपालु (आप) के सिवा अपनी विरदावली का और कौन जबर्दस्ती (हठपूर्वक) पालन करेगा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3453.english_translation: In this way, by correcting their faults and honoring them, you made your servants the foremost among the good. Who, except the compassionate one, would forcefully keep to such a vow?
ramacharitamanas::3453.translation_literal: यों (in this way) / सुधारि (correcting) / सनमानि (honoring) / जन (servants/people) / किए (made) / साधु (good/holy) / सिरमोर (foremost) / को (who) / कृपाल (compassionate one) / बिनु (without) / पालिहै (will keep) / बिरिदावलि (vow of honor) / बरजोर (forcefully)
ramacharitamanas::3453.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3453.essence: Compassion keeps your promises and raises others with them.
ramacharitamanas::3453.simple_meaning: Ram corrects his servants gently and honors them so fully that they become admirable. Only a deeply compassionate master would keep his promise with such loving force.
ramacharitamanas::3453.simple_insight: Real authority makes people better without humiliating them.
ramacharitamanas::3453.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the speaker praises Ram after the exile has begun and Bharat's loyalty is being tested. Ram does not merely command; he restores dignity, corrects mistakes, and turns servants into the best of the good. That compassion is his true greatness.
ramacharitamanas::3453.modern_relevance: A manager notices a mistake in a team member's work and fixes it without embarrassment, then publicly credits them for the improvement. The person leaves stronger, not smaller.
ramacharitamanas::3453.insight: It teaches you to lead by refining and honoring others, not by crushing them into obedience.

ramacharitamanas::3454.verse_sanskrit: सोक सनेहँ कि बाल सुभाएँ। आयउँ लाइ रजायसु बाएँ॥ तबहुँ कृपाल हेरि निज ओरा। सबहि भाँति भल मानेउ मोरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3454.verse_hindi: मैं शोक से या स्नेह से या बालक स्वभाव से आज्ञा को बाएँ लाकर (न मानकर) चला आया, तो भी कृपालु स्वामी (आप) ने अपनी ओर देखकर सभी प्रकार से मेरा भला ही माना (मेरे इस अनुचित कार्य को अच्छा ही समझा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3454.english_translation: I came with my order turned aside, whether from grief, affection, or childish nature. Yet the compassionate Lord looked toward me and accepted my mistake as good in every way.
ramacharitamanas::3454.translation_literal: सोक (grief) / सनेहँ (with affection) / कि (or) / बाल सुभाएँ (by childish nature) / आयउँ (I came) / लाइ (bringing) / रजायसु (the command) / बाएँ (to the left, aside) / तबहुँ (even then) / कृपाल (the compassionate one) / हेरि (looking) / निज ओरा (toward his own side) / सबहि भाँति (in every way) / भल (good) / मानेउ (considered) / मोरा (mine)
ramacharitamanas::3454.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3454.essence: Compassion sees more good in you than your mistake deserves.
ramacharitamanas::3454.simple_meaning: Bharat says he came with his order set aside, but Ram still treated him with kindness and saw the good in him.
ramacharitamanas::3454.simple_insight: You can be forgiven more deeply than you expect.
ramacharitamanas::3454.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is speaking after the wound of exile has split the family. He admits his own failure to obey fully, yet remembers how Ram looked at him without hardness. That mercy becomes the center of his devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3454.modern_relevance: You sent the apology after the damage was already done, expecting coldness back. Instead, the person you hurt chose generosity, and that changed everything.
ramacharitamanas::3454.insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to trust in compassionate seeing.

ramacharitamanas::3455.verse_sanskrit: देखेउँ पाय सुमंगल मूला। जानेउँ स्वामि सहज अनुकूला। बड़ें समाज बिलोकेउँ भागू। बड़ीं चूक साहिब अनुरागू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3455.verse_hindi: मैंने सुंदर मंगलों के मूल आपके चरणों का दर्शन किया और यह जान लिया कि स्वामी मुझ पर स्वभाव से ही अनुकूल हैं। इस बड़े समाज में अपने भाग्य को देखा कि इतनी बड़ी चूक होने पर भी स्वामी का मुझ पर कितना अनुराग है! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3455.english_translation: I saw your feet, the source of all auspiciousness, and knew my master is naturally kind to me. In this great gathering, I saw my own good fortune: even after such a grave mistake, my master still holds love for me.
ramacharitamanas::3455.translation_literal: देखेउँ (I saw) / पाय (feet) / सुमंगल (most auspicious) / मूला (root/source) / जानेउँ (I knew) / स्वामि (master) / सहज (by nature) / अनुकूला (kindly disposed) / बड़ें (great) / समाज (assembly) / बिलोकेउँ (I saw) / भागू (fortune) / बड़ीं (great) / चूक (mistake/fault) / साहिब (master) / अनुरागू (love/affection)
ramacharitamanas::3455.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3455.essence: True love remains steady even after a grave mistake.
ramacharitamanas::3455.simple_meaning: Bharat feels that seeing Ram's feet has shown him both blessing and mercy. Even after his mistake, Ram's affection has not changed.
ramacharitamanas::3455.simple_insight: There is relief in being loved without having to earn perfection.
ramacharitamanas::3455.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands before Ram in Ayodhya after the chaos of exile. He has come burdened by guilt, yet Ram's welcome feels larger than his failure. In this moment, Bharat recognises that Ram's love is greater than his mistake.
ramacharitamanas::3455.modern_relevance: You walk into a family room after saying the wrong thing and expecting distance. Instead, someone meets you with the same warmth. That quiet mercy can undo shame faster than any apology.
ramacharitamanas::3455.insight: It shifts the mind from self-condemnation to receiving grace without resistance.

ramacharitamanas::3456.verse_sanskrit: कृपा अनुग्रहु अंगु अघाई। कीन्हि कृपानिधि सब अधिकाई॥ राखा मोर दुलार गोसाईं। अपनें सील सुभायँ भलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3456.verse_hindi: कृपानिधान ने मुझ पर सांगोपांग भरपेट कृपा और अनुग्रह, सब अधिक ही किए हैं (अर्थात मैं जिसके जरा भी लायक नहीं था, उतनी अधिक सर्वांगपूर्ण कृपा आपने मुझ पर की है)। हे गोसाईं! आपने अपने शील, स्वभाव और भलाई से मेरा दुलार रखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3456.english_translation: The gracious Lord has poured out complete kindness and favor on me, far more than I deserved. O Lord of kindness, you have kept your affection for me alive through your own character, gentleness, and goodness.
ramacharitamanas::3456.translation_literal: कृपा (grace) / अनुग्रहु (favor) / अंगु (entirely) / अघाई (filled full) / कीन्हि (did) / कृपानिधि (treasure of grace) / सब (all) / अधिकाई (excess, more than due) / राखा (kept) / मोर (my) / दुलार (affection) / गोसाईं (Lord) / अपनें (your own) / सील (gentleness, character) / सुभायँ (natural disposition) / भलाई (goodness)
ramacharitamanas::3456.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3456.essence: Grace is greater than merit, and gentleness keeps love alive.
ramacharitamanas::3456.simple_meaning: Bharat says Ram has shown him far more grace than he deserved, and that Ram's gentle nature has kept that affection alive.
ramacharitamanas::3456.simple_insight: Being loved like this softens pride and makes gratitude feel natural.
ramacharitamanas::3456.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands before Ram after the exile has torn the family apart. Trying to explain his own humility, he says Ram has already treated him with more grace than he deserved. This verse is Bharat's praise of Ram's gentle nature.
ramacharitamanas::3456.modern_relevance: You apologized badly, expecting coldness back, and instead the other person answered with patience. That kind of response changes you more than punishment ever could.
ramacharitamanas::3456.insight: It shifts you from measuring what you deserve to noticing how generously you have been received.

ramacharitamanas::3457.verse_sanskrit: नाथ निपट मैं कीन्हि ढिठाई। स्वामि समाज सकोच बिहाई॥ अबिनय बिनय जथारुचि बानी। छमिहि देउ अति आरति जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3457.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! मैंने स्वामी और समाज के संकोच को छोड़कर अविनय या विनय भरी जैसी रुचि हुई वैसी ही वाणी कहकर सर्वथा ढिठाई की है। हे देव! मेरे आर्तभाव (आतुरता) को जानकर आप क्षमा करेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3457.english_translation: Lord, I have been utterly bold. I have set aside all hesitation before my master and this assembly. Whether my words were respectful or not, I spoke as I wished. Please forgive me, knowing my distress.
ramacharitamanas::3457.translation_literal: नाथ (lord) / निपट (utterly) / मैं (I) / कीन्हि (did) / ढिठाई (boldness, brazenness) / स्वामि (master) / समाज (assembly) / सकोच (hesitation, reserve) / बिहाई (having left aside) / अबिनय (lack of decorum) / बिनय (humble speech) / जथारुचि (as desired) / बानी (speech) / छमिहि (will forgive) / देउ (O divine one) / अति (very) / आरति (distress) / जानी (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::3457.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3457.essence: Distress can be more truthful than polished politeness.
ramacharitamanas::3457.simple_meaning: Bharat admits he spoke boldly and without formal restraint. He asks forgiveness, saying his distress made him speak this way.
ramacharitamanas::3457.simple_insight: You can be raw before someone who truly cares and still be received with kindness.
ramacharitamanas::3457.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram and the gathered court, overwhelmed by grief and devotion. He confesses that he has spoken without proper reserve, not to insult but because his heart is in distress. The moment shows surrender through honesty.
ramacharitamanas::3457.modern_relevance: You finally tell a parent, partner, or teacher what you really feel, and your voice shakes. The right listener does not punish the imperfect words; they hear the pain underneath.
ramacharitamanas::3457.insight: It shifts you from polishing your speech to revealing your real condition.

ramacharitamanas::3458.verse_sanskrit: सुहृद सुजान सुसाहिबहि बहुत कहब बड़ि खोरि। आयसु देइअ देव अब सबइ सुधारी मोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3458.verse_hindi: सुहृद् (बिना ही हेतु के हित करने वाले), बुद्धिमान और श्रेष्ठ मालिक से बहुत कहना बड़ा अपराध है, इसलिए हे देव! अब मुझे आज्ञा दीजिए, आपने मेरी सभी बात सुधार दी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3458.english_translation: It is a great fault to say too much to a wise, kind lord. So now, O divine one, give me your command; you have already set my words right.
ramacharitamanas::3458.translation_literal: सुहृद (well-wisher) / सुजान (wise) / सुसाहिबहि (to the good lord) / बहुत (much) / कहब (to speak) / बड़ि (great) / खोरि (fault) / आयसु (command) / देइअ (give) / देव (O divine one) / अब (now) / सबइ (all) / सुधारी (set right) / मोरि (my)
ramacharitamanas::3458.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3458.essence: True guidance begins when your own explaining stops.
ramacharitamanas::3458.simple_meaning: Speaking too much before a wise, kind master is a mistake. The speaker now asks for instruction and trusts that the master's guidance will correct everything.
ramacharitamanas::3458.simple_insight: There is relief in stopping your own talking and letting a wiser presence direct you.
ramacharitamanas::3458.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas has been speaking humbly to Ram after admitting his awkwardness and boldness. Now he says that too much speech before a true well-wisher is itself a fault, and asks Ram to command him instead.
ramacharitamanas::3458.modern_relevance: You keep explaining yourself in a tense conversation, then suddenly realise the other person already understands the heart of it. The next move is not more defending — it is listening.
ramacharitamanas::3458.insight: It shifts you from self-justification to receptive obedience.

ramacharitamanas::3459.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु पद पदुम पराग दोहाई। सत्य सुकृत सुख सीवँ सुहाई॥ सो करि कहउँ हिए अपने की। रुचि जागत सोवत सपने की ॥
ramacharitamanas::3459.verse_hindi: प्रभु (आप) के चरणकमलों की रज, जो सत्य, सुकृत (पुण्य) और सुख की सुहावनी सीमा (अवधि) है, उसकी दुहाई करके मैं अपने हृदय को जागते, सोते और स्वप्न में भी बनी रहने वाली रुचि (इच्छा) कहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3459.english_translation: I invoke the dust of my Lord's lotus feet, the lovely limit of truth, merit, and joy. By that, I speak of the desire that stays in my heart while waking, sleeping, and dreaming.
ramacharitamanas::3459.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / पदुम (lotus) / पराग (dust) / दोहाई (invocation) / सत्य (truth) / सुकृत (good deeds) / सुख (joy) / सीवँ (limit/boundary) / सुहाइ (beautiful) ॥ / सो (that) / करि (doing) / कहउँ (I speak) / हिए (in heart) / अपने (my own) / की (of) / रुचि (desire/taste) / जागत (while waking) / सोवत (while sleeping) / सपने (in dream) / की (of) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3459.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3459.essence: True devotion keeps returning, even in sleep and dream.
ramacharitamanas::3459.simple_meaning: The speaker bows to Ram's feet and says that his heart's real desire stays fixed on Ram at all times, awake, asleep, and dreaming.
ramacharitamanas::3459.simple_insight: Love becomes steady when it is no longer limited to one mood or moment.
ramacharitamanas::3459.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is speaking with deep humility after rejecting worldly power. He calls on Ram's feet as the source of all that is true and good, then confesses that his heart's pull toward Ram never stops, not even in sleep or dream.
ramacharitamanas::3459.modern_relevance: You check your phone before bed and again the moment you wake up, and one person or one longing is still there. This verse names that kind of unbroken attachment, then turns it toward loving service.
ramacharitamanas::3459.insight: It shifts desire from scattered craving to one steady devotion that follows you through every state.

ramacharitamanas::3460.verse_sanskrit: सहज सनेहँ स्वामि सेवकाई। स्वारथ छल फल चारि बिहाई॥ अग्यासम न सुसाहिब सेवा। सो प्रसादु जन पावै देवा।2॥
ramacharitamanas::3460.verse_hindi: वह रुचि है- कपट, स्वार्थ और (अर्थ-धर्म-काम-मोक्ष रूप) चारों फलों को छोड़कर स्वाभाविक प्रेम से स्वामी की सेवा करना। और आज्ञा पालन के समान श्रेष्ठ स्वामी की और कोई सेवा नहीं है। हे देव! अब वही आज्ञा रूप प्रसाद सेवक को मिल जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3460.english_translation: The best service to a master is to obey with natural love, leaving behind selfishness, deceit, and the four aims of life. O divine one, may I receive that blessing of obedience.
ramacharitamanas::3460.translation_literal: सहज (natural) / सनेहँ (with love) / स्वामि (master) / सेवकाई (service) / स्वारथ (self-interest) / छल (deceit) / फल (fruit/result) / चारि (four) / बिहाई (leaving behind) / अग्यासम (like obedience) / न (no) / सुसाहिब (good master) / सेवा (service) / सो (that) / प्रसादु (blessing) / जन (servant) / पावै (may receive) / देवा (O divine one)
ramacharitamanas::3460.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3460.essence: Love serves best when it gives up bargaining.
ramacharitamanas::3460.simple_meaning: The purest service is loving obedience without selfish motives or hidden deals.
ramacharitamanas::3460.simple_insight: Service feels light when you stop bargaining for reward.
ramacharitamanas::3460.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is explaining the spirit of true service. He values serving a rightful master through loving obedience, not through self-interest, manipulation, or even pursuit of the four human aims. This line crystallizes his ideal.
ramacharitamanas::3460.modern_relevance: You help a friend move house, even though nobody will notice how much you carried. You don't keep score. That quiet, unadvertised loyalty is what this verse praises.
ramacharitamanas::3460.insight: It shifts service from transaction to wholehearted obedience.

ramacharitamanas::3461.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि प्रेम बिबस भए भारी। पुलक सरीर बिलोचन बारी॥ प्रभु पद कमल गहे अकुलाई। समउ सनेहु न सो कहि जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3461.verse_hindi: भरतजी ऐसा कहकर प्रेम के बहुत ही विवश हो गए। शरीर पुलकित हो उठा, नेत्रों में (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल भर आया। अकुलाकर (व्याकुल होकर) उन्होंने प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के चरणकमल पकड़ लिए। उस समय को और स्नेह को कहा नहीं जा सकता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3461.english_translation: Saying this, Bharata became overwhelmed with love. His body thrilled with goosebumps, and tears filled his eyes. In distress, he seized Lord Rama's lotus feet. No one can describe that moment or that love.
ramacharitamanas::3461.translation_literal: अस (thus) / कहि (having said) / प्रेम (love) / बिबस (overpowered) / भए (became) / भारी (greatly) / पुलक (horripilation) / सरीर (body) / बिलोचन (eyes) / बारी (water/tears) / प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / गहे (grasped) / अकुलाई (in distress) / समउ (moment) / सनेहु (affection/love) / न (not) / सो (that) / कहि (say) / जाई (can be said)
ramacharitamanas::3461.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3461.essence: True love leaves no room for performance.
ramacharitamanas::3461.simple_meaning: Bharat is overwhelmed by love for Ram. His body trembles, tears come, and he clings to Ram's feet because his feelings are too deep for words.
ramacharitamanas::3461.simple_insight: Deep devotion can dissolve self-consciousness and leave only honest surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3461.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram after years of grief and loyalty. The sight of Ram undoes him completely. He trembles, weeps, and grabs Ram's feet because love has become stronger than speech.
ramacharitamanas::3461.modern_relevance: You finally see someone you have missed for years, and all your rehearsed words disappear. Your chest tightens, your eyes fill, and the first thing you do is reach for their hand.
ramacharitamanas::3461.insight: It shows that devotion is not polished emotion; it is the body moving before the mind can explain itself.

ramacharitamanas::3462.verse_sanskrit: कृपासिंधु सनमानि सुबानी। बैठाए समीप गहि पानी॥ भरत बिनय सुनिदेखि सुभाऊ। सिथिल सनेहँ सभा रघुराऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3462.verse_hindi: कृपासिन्धु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने सुंदर वाणी से भरतजी का सम्मान करके हाथ पकड़कर उनको अपने पास बिठा लिया। भरतजी की विनती सुनकर और उनका स्वभाव देखकर सारी सभा और श्री रघुनाथजी स्नेह से शिथिल हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3462.english_translation: The ocean of compassion honored Bharat with kind words, took his hand, and seated him nearby. Hearing Bharat's plea and seeing his nature, the whole assembly and Raghunath melted with love.
ramacharitamanas::3462.translation_literal: कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / सनमानि (honoring) / सुबानी (with kind words) / बैठाए (seated) / समीप (nearby) / गहि (taking) / पानी (hand) ॥ भरत (Bharat) / बिनय (humble request) / सुनि (hearing) / देखि (seeing) / सुभाऊ (nature) / सिथिल (melted, loosened) / सनेहँ (with love) / सभा (assembly) / रघुराऊ (Raghunath)
ramacharitamanas::3462.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3462.essence: Love deepens when honor is given without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::3462.simple_meaning: Ram receives Bharat with tenderness, seating him close and honoring him. Bharat's humility moves everyone present, and love softens the whole assembly.
ramacharitamanas::3462.simple_insight: Real honor makes room for another person. When humility meets tenderness, even a whole room can soften.
ramacharitamanas::3462.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat has come with grief and devotion, not ambition. Ram welcomes him like a beloved equal, not a rival. Bharat's sincerity and character are so clear that the court itself melts into love.
ramacharitamanas::3462.modern_relevance: You finally meet the sibling who has no wish to outshine you, only to serve. The room changes when you stop defending your place and simply honor theirs.
ramacharitamanas::3462.insight: It shifts attention from status to reverent welcome, showing how humility can transform an entire gathering.

ramacharitamanas::3463.verse_sanskrit: रघुराउ सिथिल सनेहँ साधु समाज मुनि मिथिला धनी। मन महुँ सराहत भरत भायप भगति की महिमा घनी॥ भरतहि प्रसंसत बिबुध बरषत सुमन मानस मलिन से। तुलसी बिकल सब लोग सुनि सकुचे निसागम नलिन से॥
ramacharitamanas::3463.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी, साधुओं का समाज, मुनि वशिष्ठजी और मिथिलापति जनकजी स्नेह से शिथिल हो गए। सब मन ही मन भरतजी के भाईपन और उनकी भक्ति की अतिशय महिमा को सराहने लगे। देवता मलिन से मन से भरतजी की प्रशंसा करते हुए उन पर फूल बरसाने लगे। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- सब लोग भरतजी का भाषण सुनकर व्याकुल हो गए और ऐसे सकुचा गए जैसे रात्रि के आगमन से कमल!
ramacharitamanas::3463.english_translation: Lord Raghunath, the saints, Sage Vashishtha, and King Janaka were softened by affection. In their hearts they praised the greatness of Bharat's brotherhood and devotion. The gods, with hearts made pure, showered flowers in praise of Bharat. Tulsidas says: hearing Bharat's words, everyone was overwhelmed and shy, like lotuses at nightfall.
ramacharitamanas::3463.translation_literal: रघुराउ (Raghunath) / सिथिल (softened) / सनेहँ (by affection) / साधु समाज (saintly assembly) / मुनि (sage) / मिथिला धनी (lord of Mithila) / मन महुँ (in the mind) / सराहत (praising) / भरत भायप (Bharat's brotherhood) / भगति (devotion) / की महिमा (the greatness) / घनी (great)॥ / भरतहि (to Bharat) / प्रसंसत (praising) / बिबुध (gods) / बरषत (showering) / सुमन (flowers) / मानस (mind) / मलिन से (as if stained) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / बिकल (overwhelmed) / सब लोग (all people) / सुनि (hearing) / सकुचे (became shy) / निसागम (nightfall) / नलिन से (like lotuses)
ramacharitamanas::3463.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3463.essence: Sincere devotion can move even the highest hearts.
ramacharitamanas::3463.simple_meaning: Bharat's devotion and brotherly love move everyone present. Even revered elders and the divine beings praise him, while the whole assembly feels overwhelmed by the depth of his heart.
ramacharitamanas::3463.simple_insight: Real devotion changes the atmosphere around you. It makes reverence, humility, and love arise in others too.
ramacharitamanas::3463.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Bharat's grief-filled words and selfless loyalty, Ram, Vashishtha, Janaka, saints, and even the heavenly beings are moved. This verse pauses the story to show how Bharat's bhakti has become visible to everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3463.modern_relevance: You show up for a family crisis with no agenda, no image to protect, and no demand to be praised. People feel it immediately — and their respect changes before you say another word.
ramacharitamanas::3463.insight: It shifts attention from public performance to the quiet force of sincere devotion and brotherly loyalty.

ramacharitamanas::3464.verse_sanskrit: देखि दुखारी दीन दुहु समाज नर नारि सब। मघवा महा मलीन मुए मारि मंगल चहत ॥
ramacharitamanas::3464.verse_hindi: दोनों समाजों के सभी नर-नारियों को दीन और दुःखी देखकर महामलिन मन इन्द्र मरे हुओं को मारकर अपना मंगल चाहता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3464.english_translation: Seeing both communities of men and women grieving and helpless, the utterly impure Indra, even by harming the already fallen, seeks his own gain.
ramacharitamanas::3464.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / दुखारी (grieving) / दीन (helpless) / दुहु (both) / समाज (communities) / नर (men) / नारि (women) / सब (all) / मघवा (Indra) / महा मलीन (utterly impure) / मुए (the dead) / मारि (by killing) / मंगल (welfare) / चहत (seeks)
ramacharitamanas::3464.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3464.essence: Self-interest can remain blind even in the presence of shared suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3464.simple_meaning: Everyone in both groups is sad and powerless, and Indra is so corrupt that he wants his own benefit even if it means hurting those already suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3464.simple_insight: Pity does not always awaken nobility; sometimes another's pain becomes just another chance for selfishness.
ramacharitamanas::3464.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the grief around Bharata's return has softened everyone. Against that atmosphere of shared sorrow, the narrator points to Indra as a moral contrast: even now, he remains selfish and tainted, caring only for his own gain.
ramacharitamanas::3464.modern_relevance: A room goes quiet after bad news, and one person still starts calculating what they can get out of it. That instinct reveals a mind untouched by compassion.
ramacharitamanas::3464.insight: It sharpens the contrast between collective grief and self-serving calculation, exposing selfishness as a failure of character.

ramacharitamanas::3465.verse_sanskrit: कपट कुचालि सीवँ सुरराजू। पर अकाज प्रिय आपन काजू॥ काक समान पाकरिपु रीती। छली मलीन कतहुँ न प्रतीती ॥
ramacharitamanas::3465.verse_hindi: देवराज इन्द्र कपट और कुचाल की सीमा है। उसे पराई हानि और अपना लाभ ही प्रिय है। इन्द्र की रीति कौए के समान है। वह छली और मलिन मन है, उसका कहीं किसी पर विश्वास नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3465.english_translation: Indra, king of the gods, is the height of deceit and crookedness. He loves harm to others and benefit for himself. Indra's way is like a crow's. He is deceitful and impure, and no trust can be placed in him.
ramacharitamanas::3465.translation_literal: कपट (deceit) / कुचालि (crooked conduct) / सीवँ (limit) / सुरराजू (king of the radiant beings) / पर (others') / अकाज (harm) / प्रिय (dear) / आपन (own) / काजू (work, gain) / काक (crow) / समान (like) / पाकरिपु (enemy of the fruit tree) / रीती (way, manner) / छली (deceitful) / मलीन (impure) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / न (not) / प्रतीती (trust, confidence)
ramacharitamanas::3465.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3465.essence: Cleverness without integrity becomes a crow's way.
ramacharitamanas::3465.simple_meaning: Indra is described as selfish, deceitful, and untrustworthy. He wants others harmed if it helps him.
ramacharitamanas::3465.simple_insight: Self-serving cleverness poisons trust and makes even power look small.
ramacharitamanas::3465.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the poet turns from Bharat's grief to Indra's ugly intent. Seeing the heavens' king as a schemer, the verse condemns a mind that values another's loss over its own integrity.
ramacharitamanas::3465.modern_relevance: A colleague smiles in the meeting and then quietly shifts blame onto you in the email thread. The damage is not just the lie — it's the kind of mind that can live with it.
ramacharitamanas::3465.insight: It warns you to see through polished behavior when the motive is selfish gain.

ramacharitamanas::3466.verse_sanskrit: प्रथम कुमत करि कपटु सँकेला। सो उचाटु सब कें सिर मेला॥ सुरमायाँ सब लोग बिमोहे। राम प्रेम अतिसय न बिछोहे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3466.verse_hindi: पहले तो कुमत (बुरा विचार) करके कपट को बटोरा (अनेक प्रकार के कपट का साज सजा)। फिर वह (कपटजनित) उचाट सबके सिर पर डाल दिया। फिर देवमाया से सब लोगों को विशेष रूप से मोहित कर दिया, किन्तु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्रेम से उनका अत्यन्त बिछोह नहीं हुआ (अर्थात उनका श्री रामजी के प्रति प्रेम कुछ तो बना ही रहा) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3466.english_translation: First, they gathered crooked intentions and deceit. Then they spread that restless unease over everyone’s head. By the power of illusion, they bewildered all people, yet their love for Ram Chandr did not break completely.
ramacharitamanas::3466.translation_literal: प्रथम (first) / कुमत (bad intention) / करि (having done) / कपटु (deceit) / सँकेला (collected, gathered) / सो (that) / उचाटु (restless unease) / सब कें (of everyone) / सिर (head) / मेला (placed, put) / सुरमायाँ (by divine illusion) / सब लोग (all people) / बिमोहे (were bewildered) / राम प्रेम (love for Ram) / अतिसय (greatly) / न (not) / बिछोहे (separated, broken apart)
ramacharitamanas::3466.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3466.essence: Illusion can cloud everyone, but love for Ram still survives.
ramacharitamanas::3466.simple_meaning: Deceit and confusion spread across everyone, and people were deeply bewildered. Even so, their love for Ram was not completely destroyed.
ramacharitamanas::3466.simple_insight: Confusion can cloud your mind, but sincere devotion still leaves a thread unbroken.
ramacharitamanas::3466.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the kingdom has been shaken by hidden wrongdoing, Tulsidas describes how confusion spreads through everyone like a fever. People are deluded by illusion, yet even that darkness cannot fully sever their love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3466.modern_relevance: A rumor spreads through a family group chat, and suddenly everyone is upset, suspicious, and half-lost in fear. Even then, the deepest loyalties do not disappear overnight.
ramacharitamanas::3466.insight: It shows how confusion can distort judgment without fully erasing the heart's deepest attachment.

ramacharitamanas::3467.verse_sanskrit: भय उचाट बस मन थिर नाहीं। छन बन रुचि छन सदन सोहाहीं॥ दुबिध मनोगति प्रजा दुखारी। सरित सिंधु संगम जनु बारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3467.verse_hindi: भय और उचाट के वश किसी का मन स्थिर नहीं है। क्षण में उनकी वन में रहने की इच्छा होती है और क्षण में उन्हें घर अच्छे लगने लगते हैं। मन की इस प्रकार की दुविधामयी स्थिति से प्रजा दुःखी हो रही है। मानो नदी और समुद्र के संगम का जल क्षुब्ध हो रहा हो। (जैसे नदी और समुद्र के संगम का जल स्थिर नहीं रहता, कभी इधर आता और कभी उधर जाता है, उसी प्रकार की दशा प्रजा के मन की हो गई) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3467.english_translation: Under fear and agitation, the mind cannot stay steady. One moment it likes the forest, the next it finds the home beautiful. The people suffer from this divided state of mind, like water stirred at the meeting of a river and the sea.
ramacharitamanas::3467.translation_literal: भय (fear) / उचाट (restlessness) / बस (under control of) / मन (mind) / थिर (steady) / नाहीं (not) / छन (moment) / बन (forest) / रुचि (liking) / छन (moment) / सदन (home) / सोहाहीं (seem beautiful) / दुबिध (divided) / मनोगति (movement of mind) / प्रजा (people) / दुखारी (suffering) / सरित (river) / सिंधु (sea) / संगम (meeting) / जनु (like) / बारी (water)
ramacharitamanas::3467.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3467.essence: Fear turns the mind into a place with no rest.
ramacharitamanas::3467.simple_meaning: Fear and agitation make people indecisive. Their minds keep swinging between two choices, and that inner split itself becomes suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3467.simple_insight: You can feel the cost of inner division before any outer decision is made.
ramacharitamanas::3467.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the kingdom is already trembling from rumor and manipulation. People are torn between staying and leaving, home and forest, certainty and fear. Tulsidas shows that public suffering begins when the mind loses steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::3467.modern_relevance: You keep refreshing the message thread, then deleting your reply, then typing again. Fear has split your mind, and even small choices start to hurt.
ramacharitamanas::3467.insight: It shifts attention from the external choice to the inner instability making every choice painful.

ramacharitamanas::3468.verse_sanskrit: दुचित कतहुँ परितोषु न लहहीं। एक एक सन मरमु न कहहीं॥ लखि हियँ हँसि कह कृपानिधानू। सरिस स्वान मघवान जुबानू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3468.verse_hindi: चित्त दो तरफा हो जाने से वे कहीं संतोष नहीं पाते और एक-दूसरे से अपना मर्म भी नहीं कहते। कृपानिधान श्री रामचन्द्रजी यह दशा देखकर हृदय में हँसकर कहने लगे- कुत्ता, इन्द्र और नवयुवक (कामी पुरुष) एक सरीखे (एक ही स्वभाव के) हैं। (पाणिनीय व्याकरण के अनुसार, श्वन, युवन और मघवन शब्दों के रूप भी एक सरीखे होते हैं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3468.english_translation: Because their minds are split in two, they find no satisfaction anywhere, and they do not tell one another their real feelings. Seeing this, the treasure of compassion laughed in his heart and said, "A dog, Indra, and a lustful youth are alike."
ramacharitamanas::3468.translation_literal: दुचित (two-minded / split in two) / कतहुँ (anywhere) / परितोषु (contentment) / न (not) / लहहीं (they obtain) / एक एक सन (with one another) / मरमु (the real feeling / secret) / न (not) / कहहीं (they tell) / लखि (seeing) / हियँ (in the heart) / हँसि (laughing) / कह (said) / कृपानिधानू (the treasure of compassion) / सरिस (like) / स्वान (dog) / मघवान (Indra) / जुबानू (a lustful youth / one with desire)
ramacharitamanas::3468.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3468.essence: A divided mind cannot settle or tell the truth.
ramacharitamanas::3468.simple_meaning: A divided mind cannot feel settled or honest. Ram sees this inner split and points out how restless, secretive, and unsatisfied it makes people.
ramacharitamanas::3468.simple_insight: You feel the cost of inner division: no peace, no clarity, no real connection.
ramacharitamanas::3468.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court and the people are already shaken by fear and confusion. Ram watches how a divided mind makes people restless and unable to speak plainly. His remark turns that social confusion into a lesson about inner fragmentation.
ramacharitamanas::3468.modern_relevance: You draft three versions of the same text message, then delete all of them because none feels safe to send. That hesitation is what a split mind looks like: no rest, no honesty, no ease.
ramacharitamanas::3468.insight: It shifts attention from outer confusion to the inner split that produces it.

ramacharitamanas::3469.verse_sanskrit: भरतु जनकु मुनिजन सचिव साधु सचेत बिहाइ। लागि देवमाया सबहि जथाजोगु जनु पाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3469.verse_hindi: भरतजी, जनकजी, मुनिजन, मंत्री और ज्ञानी साधु-संतों को छोड़कर अन्य सभी पर जिस मनुष्य को जिस योग्य (जिस प्रकृति और जिस स्थिति का) पाया, उस पर वैसे ही देवमाया लग गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3469.english_translation: Except for Bharata, Janaka, the sages, ministers, and wise saints, divine illusion fell on everyone according to each person's nature and capacity.
ramacharitamanas::3469.translation_literal: भरतु (Bharata) / जनकु (Janaka) / मुनिजन (sages) / सचिव (ministers) / साधु (wise saints) / सचेत (aware) / बिहाइ (leaving aside) / लागि (fell upon) / देवमाया (divine illusion) / सबहि (on everyone) / जथाजोगु (according to fitness) / जनु (as if) / पाइ (having found)
ramacharitamanas::3469.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3469.essence: Illusion lands where awareness is weak.
ramacharitamanas::3469.simple_meaning: Divine illusion affects people differently, finding each person according to their nature and vulnerability. Only the truly aware, like Bharata and the wise, remain untouched.
ramacharitamanas::3469.simple_insight: You are not trapped by what everyone else is trapped by. Clear seeing changes what can reach you.
ramacharitamanas::3469.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the people around Rama are split by grief, fear, and confusion after the exile. Tulsidas says divine illusion spread through the crowd according to each person's weakness, but Bharata, Janaka, the sages, ministers, and wise saints stayed awake to what was happening.
ramacharitamanas::3469.modern_relevance: A rumor spreads through a family WhatsApp group and each person reacts differently — panic, anger, denial, blame. The same event does not enter every mind the same way; your inner state decides what takes hold.
ramacharitamanas::3469.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the condition of the mind receiving it.

ramacharitamanas::3470.verse_sanskrit: कृपासिंधु लखि लोग दुखारे। निज सनेहँ सुरपति छल भारे॥ सभा राउ गुर महिसुर मंत्री। भरत भगति सब कै मति जंत्री ॥
ramacharitamanas::3470.verse_hindi: कृपासिंधु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने लोगों को अपने स्नेह और देवराज इन्द्र के भारी छल से दुःखी देखा। सभा, राजा जनक, गुरु, ब्राह्मण और मंत्री आदि सभी की बुद्धि को भरतजी की भक्ति ने कील दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3470.english_translation: The ocean of compassion saw the people suffering, weighed down by their own love and by Indra's deep deceit. In the assembly, the king, the teacher, the learned men, and the ministers all stood fixed by Bharat's devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3470.translation_literal: कृपासिंधु (ocean of compassion) / लखि (seeing) / लोग (people) / दुखारे (made sorrowful, suffering) / निज (own) / सनेहँ (by love) / सुरपति (lord of the radiant beings, Indra) / छल (deceit) / भारे (heavily burdened) ॥ / सभा (assembly) / राउ (king) / गुर (teacher) / महिसुर (learned priests) / मंत्री (ministers) / भरत (Bharat) / भगति (devotion) / सब कै (of all) / मति (mind, understanding) / जंत्री (fixed, held fast) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3470.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3470.essence: Devotion can steady even the most divided minds.
ramacharitamanas::3470.simple_meaning: Ram sees the people's pain and the weight of deceit around them. Bharat's devotion is so strong that it leaves everyone silent and fixed in reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3470.simple_insight: Deep love can quiet confusion and gather scattered minds into one place.
ramacharitamanas::3470.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court is already wounded by exile and divided loyalties. Ram sees the people's suffering, and Bharat's devotion is so powerful that even kings, sages, and ministers are left speechless and focused on him.
ramacharitamanas::3470.modern_relevance: You walk into a family meeting where everyone has an opinion and no one is listening. Then one person's steady loyalty changes the room. That is the force Bharat carries here.
ramacharitamanas::3470.insight: It shifts attention from status and argument to the quiet authority of selfless devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3471.verse_sanskrit: रामहि चितवत चित्र लिखे से। सकुचत बोलत बचन सिखे से॥ भरत प्रीति नति बिनय बड़ाई। सुनत सुखद बरनत कठिनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3471.verse_hindi: सब लोग चित्रलिखे से श्री रामचन्द्रजी की ओर देख रहे हैं। सकुचाते हुए सिखाए हुए से वचन बोलते हैं। भरतजी की प्रीति, नम्रता, विनय और बड़ाई सुनने में सुख देने वाली है, पर उसका वर्णन करने में कठिनता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3471.english_translation: Everyone looks at Ram as if they were painted still; they speak with the hesitation of people who have been taught. Bharat's love, humility, reverence, and greatness are sweet to hear, but hard to describe.
ramacharitamanas::3471.translation_literal: रामहि (at Ram) / चितवत (gazing) / चित्र लिखे से (like painted figures) / सकुचत (hesitating, shrinking) / बोलत (speaking) / बचन (words) / सिखे से (like taught ones) ॥ / भरत (Bharat's) / प्रीति (love) / नति (bowing humility) / बिनय (reverence) / बड़ाई (greatness) / सुनत (in hearing) / सुखद (delight-giving) / बरनत (describing) / कठिनाई (difficulty) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3471.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3471.essence: True devotion makes even praise feel too small.
ramacharitamanas::3471.simple_meaning: Everyone is so moved by Ram that they look almost frozen and speak carefully. Bharat's love, humility, and greatness are beautiful to hear, but beyond full description.
ramacharitamanas::3471.simple_insight: Some devotion is too deep for language; it is felt first, then only partly spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3471.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court is gathered around Ram while Bharat's character is being felt by everyone present. The scene pauses on their awed, restrained response: Ram inspires stillness, and Bharat's devotion leaves even wise people unable to fully explain it.
ramacharitamanas::3471.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose presence changes the room, and suddenly everyone speaks more softly. Some people are so sincere that your usual labels feel too small for them.
ramacharitamanas::3471.insight: It shifts attention from explaining devotion to recognising its quiet force.

ramacharitamanas::3472.verse_sanskrit: जासु बिलोकि भगति लवलेसू। प्रेम मगन मुनिगन मिथिलेसू॥ महिमा तासु कहै किमि तुलसी। भगति सुभायँ सुमति हियँ हुलसी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3472.verse_hindi: जिनकी भक्ति का लवलेश देखकर मुनिगण और मिथिलेश्वर जनकजी प्रेम में मग्न हो गए, उन भरतजी की महिमा तुलसीदास कैसे कहे? उनकी भक्ति और सुंदर भाव से (कवि के) हृदय में सुबुद्धि हुलस रही है (विकसित हो रही है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3472.english_translation: Just a glimpse of his devotion sent sages and even Janak into loving rapture. How can Tulsidas describe Bharat's greatness? His devoted nature itself makes wisdom bloom in the heart.
