ramacharitamanas::3472.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / बिलोकि (seeing) / भगति (devotion) / लवलेसू (a tiny trace) / प्रेम (love) / मगन (immersed) / मुनिगन (groups of sages) / मिथिलेसू (the lord of Mithila, Janak)॥ / महिमा (greatness) / तासु (of that one) / कहै (say) / किमि (how) / तुलसी (Tulsidas)॥ / भगति (devotion) / सुभायँ (by nature) / सुमति (good understanding) / हियँ (in the heart) / हुलसी (blossomed, rejoiced)॥
ramacharitamanas::3472.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3472.essence: A single glimpse of devotion can transform everyone around it.
ramacharitamanas::3472.simple_meaning: Bharat's devotion is so deep that even great sages and Janak are moved by it. Tulsidas says his praise is beyond words, because such devotion naturally awakens wisdom in the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3472.simple_insight: Real devotion changes the atmosphere around you; it quietly stirs love and clarity in others.
ramacharitamanas::3472.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's character is being praised after Ram's exile. Tulsidas says that even a tiny glimpse of Bharat's devotion moves sages and Janak into loving wonder, and that his greatness is too vast to fully describe.
ramacharitamanas::3472.modern_relevance: You watch someone care for an ailing parent without complaint, and the whole room softens. Their love needs no speech; it teaches everyone present what depth looks like.
ramacharitamanas::3472.insight: It shifts attention from performance to the power of lived devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3473.verse_sanskrit: आपु छोटि महिमा बड़ि जानी। कबिकुल कानि मानि सकुचानी॥ कहि न सकति गुन रुचि अधिकाई। मति गति बाल बचन की नाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3473.verse_hindi: परन्तु वह बुद्धि अपने को छोटी और भरतजी की महिमा को बड़ी जानकर कवि परम्परा की मर्यादा को मानकर सकुचा गई (उसका वर्णन करने का साहस नहीं कर सकी)। उसकी गुणों में रुचि तो बहुत है, पर उन्हें कह नहीं सकती। बुद्धि की गति बालक के वचनों की तरह हो गई (वह कुण्ठित हो गई)! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3473.english_translation: Knowing herself small and Bharata's greatness vast, the poet's mind grew shy out of respect for poetic tradition. Her delight in his virtues is so great that she cannot fully speak them; her thinking falters like a child's words.
ramacharitamanas::3473.translation_literal: आपु (self) / छोटि (small) / महिमा (greatness) / बड़ि (great) / जानी (knowing) / कबिकुल (poet-lineage) / कानि (custom/respect) / मानि (having accepted) / सकुचानी (became shy) ॥ / कहि (to say) / न सकति (is not able) / गुन (virtues) / रुचि (interest/delight) / अधिकाई (great amount) / मति (mind/intelligence) / गति (movement/course) / बाल (child) / बचन (words) / की नाई (like) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3473.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3473.essence: True greatness can make even praise fall silent.
ramacharitamanas::3473.simple_meaning: The poet feels too small to fully describe Bharata's greatness, so she falls silent out of respect and awe.
ramacharitamanas::3473.simple_insight: Real reverence can make words feel too small.
ramacharitamanas::3473.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharata's selfless love has already stunned everyone around him. Tulsidas pauses again, saying even the poet's mind shrinks before Bharata's greatness and cannot properly speak his virtues.
ramacharitamanas::3473.modern_relevance: You try to describe the friend who showed up when everyone else vanished, and your words suddenly feel thin. Some goodness is so large that praise itself becomes shy.
ramacharitamanas::3473.insight: It teaches humility before genuine virtue: instead of forcing grand language, the mind bows and lets greatness remain greater than speech.

ramacharitamanas::3474.verse_sanskrit: भरत बिमल जसु बिमल बिधु सुमति चकोरकुमारि। उदित बिमल जन हृदय नभ एकटक रही निहारि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3474.verse_hindi: भरतजी का निर्मल यश निर्मल चन्द्रमा है और कवि की सुबुद्धि चकोरी है, जो भक्तों के हृदय रूपी निर्मल आकाश में उस चन्द्रमा को उदित देखकर उसकी ओर टकटकी लगाए देखती ही रह गई है (तब उसका वर्णन कौन करे?) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3474.english_translation: Bharat’s spotless fame is a spotless moon, and the poet’s good sense is a chakor bird. Seeing that moon rise in the pure sky of devotees’ hearts, it keeps staring without blinking.
ramacharitamanas::3474.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / बिमल (spotless) / जसु (fame) / बिमल (spotless) / बिधु (moon) / सुमति (good sense) / चकोरकुमारि (female chakor bird) / उदित (risen) / बिमल (spotless) / जन (devotees) / हृदय (heart) / नभ (sky) / एकटक (without blinking) / रही (remained) / निहारि (watching)
ramacharitamanas::3474.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3474.essence: True greatness leaves even praise speechless.
ramacharitamanas::3474.simple_meaning: Bharat’s pure fame is compared to a moon, and the poet’s mind is like a bird that can only stare at it in wonder.
ramacharitamanas::3474.simple_insight: Some people’s goodness is so complete that praise itself feels too small.
ramacharitamanas::3474.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas is trying to praise Bharat after describing his selfless greatness. He says Bharat’s spotless fame is like a moon rising in the clear sky of devotees’ hearts, and his own good mind can only gaze at it in silence.
ramacharitamanas::3474.modern_relevance: You meet someone who quietly carried everyone else’s burden and never asked for credit. Words feel clumsy, and admiration turns into silence.
ramacharitamanas::3474.insight: It shifts praise from explanation to reverent witnessing, showing that some virtue can only be admired, not fully captured.

ramacharitamanas::3475.verse_sanskrit: भरत सुभाउ न सुगम निगमहूँ। लघु मति चापलता कबि छमहूँ॥ कहत सुनत सति भाउ भरत को। सीय राम पद होइ न रत को ॥
ramacharitamanas::3475.verse_hindi: भरतजी के स्वभाव का वर्णन वेदों के लिए भी सुगम नहीं है। (अतः) मेरी तुच्छ बुद्धि की चंचलता को कवि लोग क्षमा करें! भरतजी के सद्भाव को कहते-सुनते कौन मनुष्य श्री सीता-रामजी के चरणों में अनुरक्त न हो जाएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3475.english_translation: Bharat's nature is hard to grasp even for the Vedas. Let the poet's small mind be forgiven for its wavering. Who could hear or speak of Bharat's noble heart and not become devoted to the feet of Sita and Ram?
ramacharitamanas::3475.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / सुभाउ (nature) / न (not) / सुगम (easy) / निगमहूँ (even for the Vedas) / लघु (small) / मति (mind) / चापलता (wavering) / कबि (poets) / छमहूँ (forgive)॥ / कहत (saying) / सुनत (hearing) / सति (true) / भाउ (devoted feeling) / भरत (Bharat) / को (of) / सीय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / होइ (becomes) / न (not) / रत (attached) / को (who) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3475.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3475.essence: Bharat's devotion is so pure it makes devotion itself feel natural.
ramacharitamanas::3475.simple_meaning: Bharat's character is so deep that even the Vedas cannot fully describe it. Hearing about his devotion naturally turns the heart toward Sita and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3475.simple_insight: Real devotion is contagious; being near it changes what you love.
ramacharitamanas::3475.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas pauses his praise of Bharat and admits that Bharat's nature is beyond easy description. The poet asks forgiveness for his limited words, then says that anyone who truly hears Bharat's devotion will be drawn to Sita and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3475.modern_relevance: You meet someone who keeps serving quietly while others chase credit. Their steadiness changes the room. Without preaching, they make loyalty feel beautiful and make your own heart want better things.
ramacharitamanas::3475.insight: It shifts attention from clever description to the magnetic power of lived devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3476.verse_sanskrit: सुमिरत भरतहि प्रेमु राम को। जेहि न सुलभु तेहि सरिस बाम को॥ देखि दयाल दसा सबही की। राम सुजान जानि जन जी की ॥
ramacharitamanas::3476.verse_hindi: भरतजी का स्मरण करने से जिसको श्री रामजी का प्रेम सुलभ न हुआ, उसके समान वाम (अभागा) और कौन होगा? दयालु और सुजान श्री रामजी ने सभी की दशा देखकर और भक्त (भरतजी) के हृदय की स्थिति जानकर, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3476.english_translation: Whoever did not easily receive Ram's love by remembering Bharat is the most unfortunate of all. Seeing everyone's condition with compassion, Ram, wise in the hearts of beings, knew the mind of his devotee.
ramacharitamanas::3476.translation_literal: सुमिरत (remembering) / भरतहि (Bharat) / प्रेमु (love) / राम को (of Ram) / जेहि (to whom) / न (not) / सुलभु (easy / available) / तेहि (that one) / सरिस (like) / बाम को (unfortunate / perverse) / देखि (seeing) / दयाल (compassionate) / दसा (condition) / सबही की (of everyone) / राम (Ram) / सुजान (all-knowing) / जानि (knowing) / जन (devotee / person) / जी की (of the heart)
ramacharitamanas::3476.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3476.essence: Bharat's devotion is so pure it should awaken love in you.
ramacharitamanas::3476.simple_meaning: Bharat's devotion is so pure that remembering him should awaken love for Ram. If it does not, something is wrong in the heart. Ram sees everyone's condition and knows the devotee's inner state.
ramacharitamanas::3476.simple_insight: True devotion can wake up devotion in you; if it doesn't, the heart is still guarded.
ramacharitamanas::3476.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's love has become the measure of spiritual sensitivity. Tulsidas says that anyone who cannot feel Ram's love by remembering Bharat is truly unfortunate. Ram, who sees every being's condition and knows the devotee's heart, understands this longing completely.
ramacharitamanas::3476.modern_relevance: You hear a story of someone who gave up power to honor a promise, and it makes your own excuses feel thin. Some people don't just inspire admiration — they reveal whether your heart is still awake.
ramacharitamanas::3476.insight: It teaches you to measure your own openness by what devotion in others awakens in you.

ramacharitamanas::3477.verse_sanskrit: धरम धुरीन धीर नय नागर। सत्य सनेह सील सुख सागर॥ देसु कालु लखि समउ समाजू। नीति प्रीति पालक रघुराजू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3477.verse_hindi: धर्मधुरंधर, धीर, नीति में चतुर, सत्य, स्नेह, शील और सुख के समुद्र, नीति और प्रीति के पालन करने वाले श्री रघुनाथजी देश, काल, अवसर और समाज को देखकर, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3477.english_translation: Raghunath is the pillar of dharma, calm, skilled in conduct, and an ocean of truth, affection, character, and joy. He judges the right action by place, time, occasion, and society.
ramacharitamanas::3477.translation_literal: धरम (dharma) / धुरीन (pillar, foremost) / धीर (calm, steady) / नय (conduct, policy) / नागर (skilled, urbane) / सत्य (truth) / सनेह (affection) / सील (character, virtue) / सुख (joy) / सागर (ocean) / देसु (place, country) / कालु (time) / लखि (seeing, considering) / समउ (occasion, proper moment) / समाजू (society, assembly) / नीति (right conduct, policy) / प्रीति (love, affection) / पालक (upholder, protector) / रघुराजू (Raghunath, lord of Raghu)
ramacharitamanas::3477.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3477.essence: True right action is calm, loving, and perfectly timed.
ramacharitamanas::3477.simple_meaning: Ram is described as the perfect model of steady, wise conduct: truthful, loving, disciplined, and able to judge what fits each situation.
ramacharitamanas::3477.simple_insight: You do not have to choose between kindness and correctness.
ramacharitamanas::3477.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharata's greatness is being praised by first showing the standard he reveres: Ram. Before Bharata speaks, this verse names Ram as the ideal ruler who understands duty, timing, and people with complete steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::3477.modern_relevance: You are about to answer a difficult message and you pause, reread it, and notice the person behind the words. Ram's way is that rare mix of firmness and care that keeps a relationship intact.
ramacharitamanas::3477.insight: It shifts judgment from rigid rules to wise, timely action shaped by truth and affection.

ramacharitamanas::3478.verse_sanskrit: बोले बचन बानि सरबसु से। हित परिनाम सुनत ससि रसु से॥ तात भरत तुम्ह धरम धुरीना। लोक बेद बिद प्रेम प्रबीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3478.verse_hindi: (तदनुसार) ऐसे वचन बोले जो मानो वाणी के सर्वस्व ही थे, परिणाम में हितकारी थे और सुनने में चन्द्रमा के रस (अमृत) सरीखे थे। (उन्होंने कहा-) हे तात भरत! तुम धर्म की धुरी को धारण करने वाले हो, लोक और वेद दोनों के जानने वाले और प्रेम में प्रवीण हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3478.english_translation: He spoke words that were the very essence of speech, beneficial in their outcome and sweet as moonlit nectar to hear. “Dear Bharat, you uphold the weight of dharma. You know both worldly conduct and the Vedas, and you are skilled in love.”
ramacharitamanas::3478.translation_literal: बोले (spoke) / बचन (words) / बानि (speech) / सरबसु (essence, all) / से (like) / हित (beneficial) / परिनाम (result, outcome) / सुनत (hearing) / ससि (moon) / रसु (nectar, sweetness) / से (like) / तात (dear brother) / भरत (Bharat) / तुम्ह (you) / धरम (dharma) / धुरीना (pillar, bearer) / लोक (worldly conduct) / बेद (Veda) / बिद (knower) / प्रेम (love) / प्रबीना (skilled)
ramacharitamanas::3478.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3478.essence: True speech helps, soothes, and still carries moral weight.
ramacharitamanas::3478.simple_meaning: Kind, wise speech can be both helpful and beautiful. Bharat is praised as someone who carries dharma, understands life and scripture, and knows how to love well.
ramacharitamanas::3478.simple_insight: You can be firm without being harsh, and loving without being vague.
ramacharitamanas::3478.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court and family are still shaken by exile and loss. The narrator praises Bharat’s character: his speech is nourishing, his conduct is steady, and he understands both ordinary life and sacred wisdom. This verse elevates him as a model of mature love.
ramacharitamanas::3478.modern_relevance: You’re drafting a message to someone hurting, and every sentence matters. This verse reminds you that the best words are not just correct — they also heal, steady, and reveal your character.
ramacharitamanas::3478.insight: It teaches you to make speech useful, gentle, and rooted in discernment.

ramacharitamanas::3479.verse_sanskrit: करम बचन मानस बिमल तुम्ह समान तुम्ह तात। गुर समाज लघु बंधु गुन कुसमयँ किमि कहि जात ॥
ramacharitamanas::3479.verse_hindi: हे तात! कर्म से, वचन से और मन से निर्मल तुम्हारे समान तुम्हीं हो। गुरुजनों के समाज में और ऐसे कुसमय में छोटे भाई के गुण किस तरह कहे जा सकते हैं? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3479.english_translation: O dear one, only you are pure in deed, word, and mind like this. In the presence of elders and at such an untimely moment, how can a younger brother's virtues be spoken of?
ramacharitamanas::3479.translation_literal: करम (deed) / बचन (word) / मानस (mind) / बिमल (pure) / तुम्ह (you) / समान (like) / तुम्ह (you) / तात (dear one) / गुर (elders) / समाज (assembly) / लघु (younger) / बंधु (brother) / गुन (virtues) / कुसमयँ (untimely moment) / किमि (how) / कहि (said) / जात (can be)
ramacharitamanas::3479.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3479.essence: Purity does not boast; it yields to the rightness of the moment.
ramacharitamanas::3479.simple_meaning: You are pure in action, speech, and mind. In front of elders, and at this bad moment, your younger brother's virtues cannot even be properly spoken of.
ramacharitamanas::3479.simple_insight: Real humility doesn't advertise goodness; it bows before what is greater and keeps quiet.
ramacharitamanas::3479.detailed_meaning: Bharat is speaking to Ram in Ayodhya’s wounded court, just after praising him as the model of truth and love. Overwhelmed, he says that any praise of his own small virtues would be out of place before elders and in this painful moment.
ramacharitamanas::3479.modern_relevance: You’re being praised in a room full of seniors after a crisis, and you know the compliment belongs elsewhere. The honest response is not to inflate yourself, but to step back with grace.
ramacharitamanas::3479.insight: It shifts attention from self-display to rightful modesty and respect for the moment.

ramacharitamanas::3480.verse_sanskrit: जानहु तात तरनि कुल रीती। सत्यसंध पितु कीरति प्रीती॥ समउ समाजु लाज गुरजन की। उदासीन हित अनहित मन की ॥
ramacharitamanas::3480.verse_hindi: हे तात! तुम सूर्यकुल की रीति को, सत्यप्रतिज्ञ पिताजी की कीर्ति और प्रीति को, समय, समाज और गुरुजनों की लज्जा (मर्यादा) को तथा उदासीन, मित्र और शत्रु सबके मन की बात को जानते हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3480.english_translation: You know the customs of the solar line, your father's vow and honor, the needs of the time and company, the respect owed to elders, and the thoughts of friends and foes alike.
ramacharitamanas::3480.translation_literal: जानहु (you know) / तात (dear one) / तरनि कुल (solar lineage) / रीती (customs) / सत्यसंध (truth-bound) / पितु (father's) / कीरति (fame, honor) / प्रीती (affection) / समउ (time, occasion) / समाजु (company, gathering) / लाज (respect, propriety) / गुरजन की (of elders) / उदासीन (neutral ones) / हित (well-being, intention) / अनहित (harm, ill-will) / मन की (of the mind)
ramacharitamanas::3480.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3480.essence: Real duty sees the whole field before it speaks.
ramacharitamanas::3480.simple_meaning: Bharat reminds the listener that he understands family duty, public respect, timing, and the feelings of others.
ramacharitamanas::3480.simple_insight: Clarity comes from seeing the whole situation, not just your own wish.
ramacharitamanas::3480.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat speaks to the brother he trusts most. He is not asking for advice from ignorance; he is showing that he understands royal duty, family honor, and social propriety. That shared understanding makes the coming decision morally weighty.
ramacharitamanas::3480.modern_relevance: You are about to send a message that could change a family relationship forever. Before you hit send, you already know how your words will land, what they owe the moment, and what honor requires.
ramacharitamanas::3480.insight: It shifts the mind from private impulse to a larger sense of duty, timing, and responsibility.

ramacharitamanas::3481.verse_sanskrit: तुम्हहि बिदित सबही कर करमू। आपन मोर परम हित धरमू॥ मोहि सब भाँति भरोस तुम्हारा। तदपि कहउँ अवसर अनुसारा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3481.verse_hindi: तुमको सबके कर्मों (कर्तव्यों) का और अपने तथा मेरे परम हितकारी धर्म का पता है। यद्यपि मुझे तुम्हारा सब प्रकार से भरोसा है, तथापि मैं समय के अनुसार कुछ कहता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3481.english_translation: You know everyone’s duties, and you know what serves our highest good. I trust you completely, yet I still speak according to the moment.
ramacharitamanas::3481.translation_literal: तुम्हहि (to you) / बिदित (known) / सबही (everyone's) / कर (of) / करमू (duties) / आपन (own) / मोर (my) / परम (highest) / हित (good) / धरमू (dharma) / मोहि (to me) / सब (all) / भाँति (ways) / भरोस (trust) / तुम्हारा (your) / तदपि (still) / कहउँ (I speak) / अवसर (occasion) / अनुसारा (according to)
ramacharitamanas::3481.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3481.essence: Complete trust still speaks with restraint.
ramacharitamanas::3481.simple_meaning: Bharat says Ram already knows everyone’s responsibilities and what is best for both of them. Even with complete trust, he speaks carefully according to the situation.
ramacharitamanas::3481.simple_insight: Trust does not erase the need for thoughtful speech.
ramacharitamanas::3481.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands before Ram in Ayodhya, speaking with the humility of a younger brother who knows his place. He trusts Ram completely, yet he still chooses his words carefully because duty, family honour, and timing all matter here.
ramacharitamanas::3481.modern_relevance: You already know your partner understands the issue, but you still choose your words carefully before bringing it up. Trust and timing can live together.
ramacharitamanas::3481.insight: It teaches you to pair deep trust with measured speech, instead of speaking carelessly just because the bond is strong.

ramacharitamanas::3482.verse_sanskrit: तात तात बिनु बात हमारी। केवल गुरकुल कृपाँ सँभारी॥ नतरु प्रजा परिजन परिवारू। हमहि सहित सबु होत खुआरू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3482.verse_hindi: हे तात! पिताजी के बिना (उनकी अनुपस्थिति में) हमारी बात केवल गुरुवंश की कृपा ने ही सम्हाल रखी है, नहीं तो हमारे समेत प्रजा, कुटुम्ब, परिवार सभी बर्बाद हो जाते ॥
ramacharitamanas::3482.english_translation: Father, without Father, our words have only been held together by the grace of the guru's line. Otherwise, with us included, all the people, relatives, and family would have been ruined.
ramacharitamanas::3482.translation_literal: तात (father) / तात (father) / बिनु (without) / बात (matter) / हमारी (our) / केवल (only) / गुरकुल (guru-line) / कृपाँ (by grace) / सँभारी (held together) / नतरु (otherwise) / प्रजा (subjects) / परिजन (kinsfolk) / परिवारू (family) / हमहि (us) / सहित (together with) / सबु (all) / होत (would become) / खुआरू (ruined)
ramacharitamanas::3482.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3482.essence: One steady presence can hold a whole family together.
ramacharitamanas::3482.simple_meaning: Bharat says that without his father, only the guru's grace has kept their affairs from falling apart. Without that support, the whole family and people would have been ruined.
ramacharitamanas::3482.simple_insight: You can feel how much one steady presence protects everyone around it.
ramacharitamanas::3482.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is speaking from the pain of exile and broken order. He tells Ram that Dasharath's absence has shaken the whole kingdom, and only the grace of the guru's line has kept them from total collapse.
ramacharitamanas::3482.modern_relevance: A family group chat goes silent after the one person who always settles arguments is gone. Everyone feels the strain. This verse names how much order can depend on one steady, principled presence.
ramacharitamanas::3482.insight: It shifts attention from personal drama to the stabilising force that quietly holds a community together.

ramacharitamanas::3483.verse_sanskrit: जौं बिनु अवसर अथवँ दिनेसू। जग केहि कहहु न होइ कलेसू॥ तस उतपातु तात बिधि कीन्हा। मुनि मिथिलेस राखि सबु लीन्हा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3483.verse_hindi: यदि बिना समय के (सन्ध्या से पूर्व ही) सूर्य अस्त हो जाए, तो कहो जगत में किस को क्लेश न होगा? हे तात! उसी प्रकार का उत्पात विधाता ने यह (पिता की असामयिक मृत्यु) किया है। पर मुनि महाराज ने तथा मिथिलेश्वर ने सबको बचा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3483.english_translation: If the sun were to set before its proper time, who in the world would not suffer? In the same way, fate has caused this untimely disaster. Yet the sage and the king of Mithila have protected everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3483.translation_literal: जौं (if) / बिनु (without) / अवसर (proper time) / अथवँ (before) / दिनेसू (sun) / जग (world) / केहि (who) / कहहु (tell) / न होइ (would not be) / कलेसू (suffering)॥ / तस (thus) / उतपातु (disaster) / तात (dear one) / बिधि (fate / the cosmic order) / कीन्हा (has done) / मुनि (sage) / मिथिलेस (king of Mithila) / राखि (protecting) / सबु (all) / लीन्हा (took / saved)॥
ramacharitamanas::3483.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3483.essence: Untimely loss feels cosmic, but steady hands can still protect everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3483.simple_meaning: An untimely death is compared to the sun setting too early: it throws the whole world into distress. Yet wise people and the king of Mithila have protected everyone from the full fallout.
ramacharitamanas::3483.simple_insight: Some losses shake everything, but steady people can still hold the world together.
ramacharitamanas::3483.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, grief has entered the royal family after Dasharath's death. The verse compares that death to the sun going down before evening, a cosmic disruption. Even so, the sage and Janak have contained the damage and kept the household from collapsing.
ramacharitamanas::3483.modern_relevance: A family gets the call at 6 a.m. that someone died unexpectedly, and the whole day tilts sideways. One calm person starts making the calls, arranging travel, and keeping everyone from unraveling.
ramacharitamanas::3483.insight: It shifts attention from the shock itself to the stabilising role of those who can hold others through it.

ramacharitamanas::3484.verse_sanskrit: राज काज सब लाज पति धरम धरनि धन धाम। गुर प्रभाउ पालिहि सबहि भल होइहि परिनाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::3484.verse_hindi: राज्य का सब कार्य, लज्जा, प्रतिष्ठा, धर्म, पृथ्वी, धन, घर- इन सभी का पालन (रक्षण) गुरुजी का प्रभाव (सामर्थ्य) करेगा और परिणाम शुभ होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3484.english_translation: The care of the kingdom, honor, duty, the earth, wealth, and home will all be upheld by the guru's grace, and the result will be good.
ramacharitamanas::3484.translation_literal: राज काज (state affairs) / सब (all) / लाज (honor) / पति (status) / धरम (duty) / धरनि (earth) / धन (wealth) / धाम (home) / गुर प्रभाउ (guru's influence) / पालिहि (will uphold) / सबहि (all) / भल (good) / होइहि (will be) / परिनाम (result)
ramacharitamanas::3484.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3484.essence: Grace can uphold what duty alone cannot.
ramacharitamanas::3484.simple_meaning: Guru's grace can protect every part of life — duty, reputation, home, wealth, and order — and lead things to a good result.
ramacharitamanas::3484.simple_insight: You do not have to carry every responsibility alone; guidance can steady what feels too heavy.
ramacharitamanas::3484.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the exile has fractured ordinary life. Bharata's world is being held together by prayer, loyalty, and the guru's influence. This line says that every responsibility — public and private — will remain safe through that higher support.
ramacharitamanas::3484.modern_relevance: You're trying to keep a family crisis from falling apart while answering messages, paying bills, and staying composed in front of everyone. This verse reminds you that steadiness does not come only from force; it can come from guidance and grace.
ramacharitamanas::3484.insight: It shifts responsibility from anxious control to trust in a sustaining influence beyond your own effort.

ramacharitamanas::3485.verse_sanskrit: सहित समाज तुम्हार हमारा। घर बन गुर प्रसाद रखवारा॥ मातु पिता गुर स्वामि निदेसू। सकल धरम धरनीधर सेसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3485.verse_hindi: गुरुजी का प्रसाद (अनुग्रह) ही घर में और वन में समाज सहित तुम्हारा और हमारा रक्षक है। माता, पिता, गुरु और स्वामी की आज्ञा (का पालन) समस्त धर्म रूपी पृथ्वी को धारण करने में शेषजी के समान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3485.english_translation: Your guru's grace protects both your home and your forest life, with all your people around you. Obeying mother, father, guru, and master is like Shesha bearing the earth of all dharma.
ramacharitamanas::3485.translation_literal: सहित (along with) / समाज (community) / तुम्हार (your) / हमारा (our) / घर (home) / बन (forest) / गुर प्रसाद (guru's grace) / रखवारा (protector) ॥ / मातु (mother) / पिता (father) / गुर (guru) / स्वामि (master) / निदेसू (command) / सकल (all) / धरम (dharma) / धरनीधर (earth-bearer) / सेसू (like Shesha) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3485.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3485.essence: Rightful obedience carries the whole burden of dharma.
ramacharitamanas::3485.simple_meaning: A person's safety and right conduct come from following the guidance of guru, parents, and rightful authority. That obedience supports life the way Shesha supports the earth.
ramacharitamanas::3485.simple_insight: There is relief in not having to invent your own standard every moment.
ramacharitamanas::3485.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the crisis around exile has turned family order upside down. Tulsidas reminds the listener that grace and right conduct still protect life in both home and forest, and that obedience to mother, father, guru, and master carries the whole weight of dharma.
ramacharitamanas::3485.modern_relevance: You are torn between your manager's deadline, your parents' expectations, and your own plans for the weekend. This verse asks you to see obligation not as a burden alone, but as the structure that keeps life from collapsing.
ramacharitamanas::3485.insight: It shifts attention from personal preference to responsible alignment with rightful guidance.

ramacharitamanas::3486.verse_sanskrit: सो तुम्ह करहु करावहु मोहू। तात तरनिकुल पालक होहू॥ साधक एक सकल सिधि देनी। कीरति सुगति भूतिमय बेनी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3486.verse_hindi: हे तात! तुम वही करो और मुझसे भी कराओ तथा सूर्यकुल के रक्षक बनो। साधक के लिए यह एक ही (आज्ञा पालन रूपी साधना) सम्पूर्ण सिद्धियों की देने वाली, कीर्तिमयी, सद्गतिमयी और ऐश्वर्यमयी त्रिवेणी है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3486.english_translation: Do that and make me do it too, dear one. Be the protector of the solar dynasty. For the seeker, this one discipline gives every success: fame, a blessed end, and a river of prosperity.
ramacharitamanas::3486.translation_literal: सो (that) / तुम्ह (you) / करहु (do) / करावहु (make do) / मोहू (me too) / तात (dear one) / तरनिकुल (solar dynasty) / पालक (protector) / होहू (be) / साधक (for the seeker) / एक (one) / सकल (all) / सिधि (success) / देनी (giving) / कीरति (fame) / सुगति (blessed end) / भूतिमय (full of prosperity) / बेनी (river confluence)
ramacharitamanas::3486.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3486.essence: Right action carries its own reward and preserves your honour.
ramacharitamanas::3486.simple_meaning: Bharat asks the listener to act in the right way and help him do the same. He says serving one’s duty brings success, good name, and a blessed outcome.
ramacharitamanas::3486.simple_insight: Doing what is right can become its own reward, shaping both character and future.
ramacharitamanas::3486.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat is urging the listener to uphold the royal line and the burden of right conduct. He is not asking for comfort or power, only that duty be carried out fully, because that single discipline brings honour, wellbeing, and a good end.
ramacharitamanas::3486.modern_relevance: Your parent asks you to step up when the family is strained, and you know there will be no applause. You do it anyway, because some responsibilities quietly build the whole life.
ramacharitamanas::3486.insight: It shifts action from reward-seeking to faithful responsibility, treating duty itself as the source of success.

ramacharitamanas::3487.verse_sanskrit: सो बिचारि सहि संकटु भारी। करहु प्रजा परिवारू सुखारी॥ बाँटी बिपति सबहिं मोहि भाई। तुम्हहि अवधि भरि बड़ि कठिनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3487.verse_hindi: इसे विचारकर भारी संकट सहकर भी प्रजा और परिवार को सुखी करो। हे भाई! मेरी विपत्ति सभी ने बाँट ली है, परन्तु तुमको तो अवधि (चौदह वर्ष) तक बड़ी कठिनाई है (सबसे अधिक दुःख है) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3487.english_translation: Thinking this over, endure the heavy hardship and keep the people and family happy. Brother, everyone has shared my suffering, but you must bear the far greater pain for the full fourteen years.
ramacharitamanas::3487.translation_literal: सो (thus) / बिचारि (having considered) / सहि (endure) / संकटु (hardship) / भारी (heavy) / करहु (do) / प्रजा (people) / परिवारू (family) / सुखारी (happy)॥ / बाँटी (shared) / बिपति (misfortune) / सबहिं (by all) / मोहि (to me) / भाई (brother) / तुम्हहि (you) / अवधि (term) / भरि (for the full) / बड़ि (great) / कठिनाई (difficulty)॥
ramacharitamanas::3487.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3487.essence: True duty is carrying the heavier burden so others can live in peace.
ramacharitamanas::3487.simple_meaning: Even in a hard situation, you should keep the people around you safe and steady. Your own burden may be greater, but your role is to hold the family and community together.
ramacharitamanas::3487.simple_insight: Love sometimes means carrying more so others can remain steady.
ramacharitamanas::3487.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram is explaining the exile to Bharat. He asks him to think clearly, accept the heavy hardship, and keep the people and family peaceful. Ram says everyone has shared some suffering, but Bharat must bear the hardest part for the full fourteen years.
ramacharitamanas::3487.modern_relevance: You are the one holding the family together after the bad news, answering calls, calming relatives, and making sure the children still eat. This verse honours the person who carries the hidden weight so others can breathe.
ramacharitamanas::3487.insight: It shifts duty from self-protection to protective responsibility for others.

ramacharitamanas::3488.verse_sanskrit: जानि तुम्हहि मृदु कहउँ कठोरा। कुसमयँ तात न अनुचित मोरा॥ होहिं कुठायँ सुबंधु सहाए। ओड़िअहिं हाथ असनिहु के धाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3488.verse_hindi: तुमको कोमल जानकर भी मैं कठोर (वियोग की बात) कह रहा हूँ। हे तात! बुरे समय में मेरे लिए यह कोई अनुचित बात नहीं है। कुठौर (कुअवसर) में श्रेष्ठ भाई ही सहायक होते हैं। वज्र के आघात भी हाथ से ही रोके जाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3488.english_translation: Knowing you to be gentle, I speak this harsh truth. In a bad time, this is not improper, dear one. In a crisis, only a true brother helps; a hand alone stops a lightning strike.
ramacharitamanas::3488.translation_literal: जानि (knowing) / तुम्हहि (you) / मृदु (gentle) / कहउँ (I speak) / कठोरा (harsh) / कुसमयँ (in a bad time) / तात (dear one) / न (not) / अनुचित (improper) / मोरा (mine) / होहिं (become) / कुठायँ (in a crisis) / सुबंधु (true brother) / सहाए (helpers) / ओड़िअहिं (stop) / हाथ (hand) / असनिहु (lightning) / के (of) / धाए (strikes)
ramacharitamanas::3488.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3488.essence: True care sometimes sounds harsh because crisis needs honesty, not comfort alone.
ramacharitamanas::3488.simple_meaning: Bharat says he is speaking painfully but honestly because difficult times call for clear support, not softness alone. In a crisis, a true brother protects you.
ramacharitamanas::3488.simple_insight: Love is not always gentle; sometimes it tells the hardest truth because care is stronger than comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3488.detailed_meaning: Bharat is speaking to his brother in the middle of a family crisis after Ram has been sent away. He knows his words will hurt, but he says them anyway: real kinship shows up when life turns harsh and unstable.
ramacharitamanas::3488.modern_relevance: You sit beside a friend after a breakup and tell them the part they do not want to hear. They need comfort, yes — but they also need someone brave enough to be honest.
ramacharitamanas::3488.insight: It teaches you to pair tenderness with truth, especially when someone is already under pressure.

ramacharitamanas::3489.verse_sanskrit: सेवक कर पद नयन से मुख सो साहिबु होइ। तुलसी प्रीति कि रीति सुनि सुकबि सराहहिं सोइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3489.verse_hindi: सेवक हाथ, पैर और नेत्रों के समान और स्वामी मुख के समान होना चाहिए। तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं कि सेवक-स्वामी की ऐसी प्रीति की रीति सुनकर सुकवि उसकी सराहना करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3489.english_translation: A servant should be like hands, feet, and eyes, and the master like the face. Tulsidas says that hearing this way of love between servant and master, even wise poets praise it.
ramacharitamanas::3489.translation_literal: सेवक (servant) / कर (hands) / पद (feet) / नयन (eyes) / से (as) / मुख (face) / सो (like that) / साहिबु (master) / होइ (should be) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / प्रीति (love) / कि (of) / रीति (way) / सुनि (hearing) / सुकबि (wise poets) / सराहहिं (praise) / सोइ (that)
ramacharitamanas::3489.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3489.essence: Love is proven by becoming useful to the one you cherish.
ramacharitamanas::3489.simple_meaning: A true servant lives for the master's needs, like hands, feet, and eyes serving the face. Love is shown through useful, selfless service.
ramacharitamanas::3489.simple_insight: Real devotion stops asking what it gets and starts asking what it can do.
ramacharitamanas::3489.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharata is speaking about the bond between loyal servant and rightful master. He describes a love where the servant becomes the master's hands, feet, and eyes, and Tulsidas praises this as the finest form of affection.
ramacharitamanas::3489.modern_relevance: You answer your mother's call before she finishes the sentence. You don't need applause for that. This verse honours the kind of love that moves first and serves quietly.
ramacharitamanas::3489.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone to embodied service in daily life.

ramacharitamanas::3490.verse_sanskrit: सभा सकल सुनि रघुबर बानी। प्रेम पयोधि अमिअँ जनु सानी॥ सिथिल समाज सनेह समाधी। देखि दसा चुप सारद साधी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3490.verse_hindi: रघुनाथजी की वाणी सुनकर, जो मानो प्रेम रूपी समुद्र के (मंथन से निकले हुए) अमृत में सनी हुई थी, सारा समाज शिथिल हो गया, सबको प्रेम समाधि लग गई। यह दशा देखकर सरस्वती ने चुप साध ली ॥
ramacharitamanas::3490.english_translation: Hearing Raghubar's words, the whole gathering was as if stirred into nectar from the sea of love. Seeing their state, even Saraswati fell silent.
ramacharitamanas::3490.translation_literal: सभा (gathering) / सकल (whole) / सुनि (hearing) / रघुबर (Raghubar, Ram) / बानी (words) / प्रेम (love) / पयोधि (ocean) / अमिअँ (nectar) / जनु (as if) / सानी (mixed) / सिथिल (limp, softened) / समाज (assembly) / सनेह (affection) / समाधी (absorbed stillness) / देखि (seeing) / दसा (state) / चुप (silent) / सारद (Saraswati) / साधी (held)
ramacharitamanas::3490.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3490.essence: True affection can silence even the need to speak.
ramacharitamanas::3490.simple_meaning: Ram's words fill the gathering with such love that everyone becomes quiet and absorbed. Even Saraswati, the goddess of speech, falls silent before that scene.
ramacharitamanas::3490.simple_insight: There are moments when love speaks more powerfully than eloquence.
ramacharitamanas::3490.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat and the assembled court are already trembling with emotion. When Ram speaks, his words are so soaked in affection that the entire gathering melts into stillness. Even Saraswati seems unable to add anything.
ramacharitamanas::3490.modern_relevance: You say one honest sentence in a tense family room, and the argument stops mid-breath. Not because you won, but because your care landed before your logic did.
ramacharitamanas::3490.insight: It shifts attention from clever speech to speech that carries genuine feeling.

ramacharitamanas::3491.verse_sanskrit: भरतहि भयउ परम संतोषू। सनमुख स्वामि बिमुख दुख दोषू॥ मुख प्रसन्न मन मिटा बिषादू। भा जनु गूँगेहि गिरा प्रसादू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3491.verse_hindi: भरतजी को परम संतोष हुआ। स्वामी के सम्मुख (अनुकूल) होते ही उनके दुःख और दोषों ने मुँह मोड़ लिया (वे उन्हें छोड़कर भाग गए)। उनका मुख प्रसन्न हो गया और मन का विषाद मिट गया। मानो गूँगे पर सरस्वती की कृपा हो गई हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3491.english_translation: Bharat felt complete contentment. When he stood before his lord, grief and fault turned away. His face brightened and sorrow left his mind, as if speech itself had been granted to the mute.
ramacharitamanas::3491.translation_literal: भरतहि (to Bharat) / भयउ (became) / परम संतोषू (complete contentment) / सनमुख (face to face, before) / स्वामि (lord) / बिमुख (turned away) / दुख (sorrow) / दोषू (fault, pain) / मुख (face) / प्रसन्न (bright, pleased) / मन (mind) / मिटा (vanished) / बिषादू (grief) / भा (became) / जनु (as if) / गूँगेहि (to the mute) / गिरा (speech) / प्रसादू (grace, gift)
ramacharitamanas::3491.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3491.essence: Being before the beloved dissolves grief.
ramacharitamanas::3491.simple_meaning: Bharat finds peace the moment he comes face to face with his lord. His sorrow leaves, his face brightens, and he feels unexpectedly blessed.
ramacharitamanas::3491.simple_insight: Real relief can arrive simply by turning toward the one you trust.
ramacharitamanas::3491.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat has come before Ram after carrying the burden of exile, grief, and duty. The moment Ram stands before him, Bharat's inner pain falls away. The scene shows how devotion can restore a shattered mind.
ramacharitamanas::3491.modern_relevance: You walk into a hospital room after days of dread, and the person you came to see smiles first. Something in you unclenches before any words are spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3491.insight: It shifts attention from internal distress to the healing power of loving presence.

ramacharitamanas::3492.verse_sanskrit: कीन्ह सप्रेम प्रनामु बहोरी। बोले पानि पंकरुह जोरी॥ नाथ भयउ सुखु साथ गए को। लहेउँ लाहु जग जनमु भए को ॥
ramacharitamanas::3492.verse_hindi: उन्होंने फिर प्रेमपूर्वक प्रणाम किया और करकमलों को जोड़कर वे बोले- हे नाथ! मुझे आपके साथ जाने का सुख प्राप्त हो गया और मैंने जगत में जन्म लेने का लाभ भी पा लिया।3॥
ramacharitamanas::3492.english_translation: He bowed again with love and, palms joined, said: “Lord, I have found the joy of going with you, and I have gained the true benefit of being born in this world.”
ramacharitamanas::3492.translation_literal: कीन्ह (did) / सप्रेम (with love) / प्रनामु (bowing) / बहोरी (again) / बोले (spoke) / पानि (hands) / पंकरुह (lotus-like) / जोरी (joined) / नाथ (Lord) / भयउ (became) / सुखु (joy) / साथ (with) / गए (going) / को (of) / लहेउँ (I found) / लाहु (profit, gain) / जग (world) / जनमु (birth) / भए (having been) / को (of)
ramacharitamanas::3492.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3492.essence: Being with Ram is the highest gain life can give.
ramacharitamanas::3492.simple_meaning: Bharat bows again and says that being with Ram is the real joy and the real reward of being born.
ramacharitamanas::3492.simple_insight: Love changes what counts as success: presence matters more than possession, and devotion makes life feel complete.
ramacharitamanas::3492.detailed_meaning: Bharat has just been comforted by Ram's words in the court at Ayodhya. Overwhelmed, he bows again with joined hands and says that the highest gain in life is simply to be with Ram. In exile's shadow, this is devotion speaking at full strength.
ramacharitamanas::3492.modern_relevance: You finally sit beside the friend who showed up when everything fell apart. No grand solution appears, but something in you settles: being with them was the point all along.
ramacharitamanas::3492.insight: It reorders desire around presence, so the mind stops chasing status and starts valuing sacred company.

ramacharitamanas::3493.verse_sanskrit: अब कृपाल जस आयसु होई। करौं सीस धरि सादर सोई॥ सो अवलंब देव मोहि देई। अवधि पारु पावौं जेहि सेई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3493.verse_hindi: हे कृपालु! अब जैसी आज्ञा हो, उसी को मैं सिर पर धर कर आदरपूर्वक करूँ! परन्तु देव! आप मुझे वह अवलम्बन (कोई सहारा) दें, जिसकी सेवा कर मैं अवधि का पार पा जाऊँ (अवधि को बिता दूँ) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3493.english_translation: O gracious one, whatever you command now, I will place on my head and do with reverence. But, O divine one, give me some support to serve, by which I may pass this time.
ramacharitamanas::3493.translation_literal: अब (now) / कृपाल (gracious one) / जस (as) / आयसु (command) / होई (becomes) / करौं (I will do) / सीस (head) / धरि (placing) / सादर (with reverence) / सोई (that very)॥ / सो (that) / अवलंब (support) / देव (O divine one) / मोहि (to me) / देई (give) / अवधि (time-span) / पारु (across) / पावौं (I may reach) / जेहि (by which) / सेई (serving that) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3493.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3493.essence: Surrender can include asking for the strength to keep serving.
ramacharitamanas::3493.simple_meaning: Bharat says he will obey whatever command comes, but he asks for some support so he can keep serving until the waiting period ends.
ramacharitamanas::3493.simple_insight: True devotion can be both obedient and honest about needing support.
ramacharitamanas::3493.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands before Ram after the pain of exile has settled into resolve. He is ready to accept any command and bow his head to it, but he also asks for something to lean on so he can continue serving through the long exile period.
ramacharitamanas::3493.modern_relevance: You’ve agreed to help through a hard season, but you’re exhausted and need a steadying hand. Bharat shows that asking for support does not weaken loyalty; it makes service sustainable.
ramacharitamanas::3493.insight: It teaches you to obey without pride and to ask for what helps you keep serving well.

ramacharitamanas::3494.verse_sanskrit: देव देव अभिषेक हित गुर अनुसासनु पाइ। आनेउँ सब तीरथ सलिलु तेहि कहँ काह रजाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3494.verse_hindi: हे देव! स्वामी (आप) के अभिषेक के लिए गुरुजी की आज्ञा पाकर मैं सब तीर्थों का जल लेता आया हूँ, उसके लिए क्या आज्ञा होती है? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3494.english_translation: O divine one, for your consecration, having received the teacher's command, I have brought water from all the sacred places. What further command is there for me?
ramacharitamanas::3494.translation_literal: देव देव (O divine one) / अभिषेक (consecration) / हित (for the sake of) / गुर (teacher) / अनुसासनु (command) / पाइ (having received) / आनेउँ (I brought) / सब (all) / तीरथ (sacred places) / सलिलु (water) / तेहि कहँ (for that) / काह (what) / रजाइ (command)
ramacharitamanas::3494.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3494.essence: Service asks for the next task, not the reward.
ramacharitamanas::3494.simple_meaning: Bharat says he has brought water from all holy places for Ram's consecration, following his teacher's command, and asks what else he should do.
ramacharitamanas::3494.simple_insight: True service waits for the next instruction, not applause.
ramacharitamanas::3494.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands before Ram in Ayodhya, carrying water gathered from every sacred place for the coronation that will never happen. He has already surrendered the throne to Ram, and now he asks for one more humble task.
ramacharitamanas::3494.modern_relevance: You finish the job no one else wanted, then ask, 'What next?' without needing credit. That is Bharat's way of serving.
ramacharitamanas::3494.insight: It shifts attention from self-display to obedient service: do the needed work, then wait for the next right step.

ramacharitamanas::3495.verse_sanskrit: एकु मनोरथु बड़ मन माहीं। सभयँ सकोच जात कहि नाहीं॥ कहहु तात प्रभु आयसु पाई। बोले बानि सनेह सुहाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3495.verse_hindi: मेरे मन में एक और बड़ा मनोरथ है, जो भय और संकोच के कारण कहा नहीं जाता। (श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने कहा-) हे भाई! कहो। तब प्रभु की आज्ञा पाकर भरतजी स्नेहपूर्ण सुंदर वाणी बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3495.english_translation: I have one more great wish in my heart, but fear and hesitation keep me from saying it. Then, after receiving the Lord's permission, Bharat spoke in sweet, loving words.
ramacharitamanas::3495.translation_literal: एकु (one) / मनोरथु (wish) / बड़ (great) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / सभयँ (with fear) / सकोच (hesitation) / जात (going) / कहि नाहीं (not saying)॥ / कहहु (say) / तात (brother/dear one) / प्रभु (Lord) / आयसु (permission) / पाई (having received) / बोले (spoke) / बानि (words) / सनेह (love) / सुहाई (beautiful) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3495.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3495.essence: Love becomes deeper when it waits for permission.
ramacharitamanas::3495.simple_meaning: Bharat has another deep wish, but he is too humble and afraid to say it until Ram invites him to speak.
ramacharitamanas::3495.simple_insight: Real love can be shy; it waits for permission before asking for more.
ramacharitamanas::3495.detailed_meaning: In Chitrakoot, Bharat has already spoken of surrender and service, but one larger longing still sits in his heart. Standing before Ram, he waits to be invited, then speaks with loving restraint. The moment shows devotion that does not push itself forward.
ramacharitamanas::3495.modern_relevance: You have something important to ask, but you wait until the other person is ready to hear it. That restraint can be its own form of love.
ramacharitamanas::3495.insight: It teaches you to let devotion speak only after humility has opened the door.

ramacharitamanas::3496.verse_sanskrit: चित्रकूट सुचि थल तीरथ बन। खग मृग सर सरि निर्झर गिरिगन॥ प्रभु पद अंकित अवनि बिसेषी। आयसु होइ त आवौं देखी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3496.verse_hindi: आज्ञा हो तो चित्रकूट के पवित्र स्थान, तीर्थ, वन, पक्षी-पशु, तालाब-नदी, झरने और पर्वतों के समूह तथा विशेष कर प्रभु (आप) के चरण चिह्नों से अंकित भूमि को देख आऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3496.english_translation: If you allow it, I would like to go see Chitrakut’s pure holy places, forests, birds and animals, ponds, rivers, streams, and mountains—especially the land marked by your feet.
ramacharitamanas::3496.translation_literal: चित्रकूट (Chitrakut) / सुचि (pure) / थल (places) / तीरथ (holy places) / बन (forest) / खग (birds) / मृग (deer, animals) / सर (lakes) / सरि (rivers) / निर्झर (streams) / गिरिगन (mountain ranges) / प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / अंकित (marked) / अवनि (earth) / बिसेषी (especially) / आयसु (permission, command) / होइ (if it is) / त (then) / आवौं (I would come) / देखी (to see)
ramacharitamanas::3496.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3496.essence: A place becomes sacred when it bears the trace of the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::3496.simple_meaning: Bharat asks for permission to visit Chitrakut and see the sacred land where Ram’s footprints are found.
ramacharitamanas::3496.simple_insight: Love makes even a landscape feel holy when it carries the trace of someone you cherish.
ramacharitamanas::3496.detailed_meaning: Bharat stands before Ram after bringing sacred water for the coronation, but his heart is elsewhere. He wants to see Chitrakut—the forests, rivers, animals, and especially the ground marked by Ram’s feet. The request reveals his longing, not curiosity.
ramacharitamanas::3496.modern_relevance: You visit a place because someone you love once walked there. The street, the park, even the quiet stones feel different because they carry that trace.
ramacharitamanas::3496.insight: It shifts attention from the place itself to what makes the place meaningful: presence, memory, and devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3497.verse_sanskrit: अवसि अत्रि आयसु सिर धरहू। तात बिगतभय कानन चरहू॥ मुनि प्रसाद बनु मंगल दाता। पावन परम सुहावन भ्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3497.verse_hindi: (श्री रघुनाथजी बोले-) अवश्य ही अत्रि ऋषि की आज्ञा को सिर पर धारण करो (उनसे पूछकर वे जैसा कहें वैसा करो) और निर्भय होकर वन में विचरो। हे भाई! अत्रि मुनि के प्रसाद से वन मंगलों का देने वाला, परम पवित्र और अत्यन्त सुंदर है- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3497.english_translation: Certainly honor the command of Atri and go fearlessly into the forest. Brother, by the sage's grace the forest is a giver of blessings, supremely pure, and very beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::3497.translation_literal: अवसि (certainly) / अत्रि (Atri) / आयसु (command) / सिर (head) / धरहू (hold) / तात (brother) / बिगतभय (fearless) / कानन (forest) / चरहू (wander) / मुनि (sage) / प्रसाद (grace) / बनु (forest) / मंगल (blessings) / दाता (giver) / पावन (pure) / परम (supremely) / सुहावन (beautiful) / भ्राता (brother)
ramacharitamanas::3497.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3497.essence: Fearless action begins when you bow to wise guidance.
ramacharitamanas::3497.simple_meaning: Ram tells Bharat to respect Atri's instruction and move through the forest without fear, because the sage's blessing makes the forest pure and auspicious.
ramacharitamanas::3497.simple_insight: Right guidance can turn a hard place into a safe one.
ramacharitamanas::3497.detailed_meaning: Bharat has come to Chitrakoot to meet Ram, and the meeting is shaped by reverence and restraint. Ram tells him to place Atri's command above his own preference and to move through the forest without fear, because blessing changes the meaning of the place.
ramacharitamanas::3497.modern_relevance: You step into a situation that feels uncertain — a new city, a difficult family visit, a decision you don't fully control. The right counsel steadies you, and the place stops feeling hostile.
ramacharitamanas::3497.insight: It shifts the mind from fear of the setting to trust in right instruction.

ramacharitamanas::3498.verse_sanskrit: रिषिनायकु जहँ आयसु देहीं। राखेहु तीरथ जलु थल तेहीं॥ सुनि प्रभु बचन भरत सुखु पावा। मुनि पद कमल मुदित सिरु नावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3498.verse_hindi: और ऋषियों के प्रमुख अत्रिजी जहाँ आज्ञा दें, वहीं (लाया हुआ) तीर्थों का जल स्थापित कर देना। प्रभु के वचन सुनकर भरतजी ने सुख पाया और आनंदित होकर मुनि अत्रिजी के चरणकमलों में सिर नवाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3498.english_translation: And wherever the chief sage Atri gives instruction, place the sacred water and the ritual offerings there. Hearing the Lord's words, Bharata felt joy and bowed his head, delighted, at the sage's lotus feet.
ramacharitamanas::3498.translation_literal: रिषिनायकु (chief of sages) / जहँ (wherever) / आयसु (instruction) / देहीं (gives) / राखेहु (place/keep) / तीरथ जलु (sacred water) / थल तेहीं (there on the ground)॥ / सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु बचन (the Lord's words) / भरत सुखु पावा (Bharata found joy) / मुनि पद कमल (sage's lotus feet) / मुदित (delighted) / सिरु नावा (bowed his head)॥
ramacharitamanas::3498.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3498.essence: Obedience becomes joy when the instruction is righteous.
ramacharitamanas::3498.simple_meaning: Bharata is told to place the sacred water wherever the sage instructs, and he gladly bows in gratitude when he hears Ram's words.
ramacharitamanas::3498.simple_insight: True obedience can feel like relief, not burden.
ramacharitamanas::3498.detailed_meaning: In Chitrakoot, Bharat is arranging the sacred waters brought from holy places. Ram tells him to follow Atri's instructions exactly. The moment shows Bharat's humility: he receives guidance gladly and bows at the sage's feet.
ramacharitamanas::3498.modern_relevance: You're setting up something important and someone wiser than you changes the plan. Instead of resisting, you feel the ease that comes from trusting good direction.
ramacharitamanas::3498.insight: It teaches you to treat right guidance as a gift, not an interruption.

ramacharitamanas::3499.verse_sanskrit: भरत राम संबादु सुनि सकल सुमंगल मूल। सुर स्वारथी सराहि कुल बरषत सुरतरु फूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::3499.verse_hindi: समस्त सुंदर मंगलों का मूल भरतजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी का संवाद सुनकर स्वार्थी देवता रघुकुल की सराहना करके कल्पवृक्ष के फूल बरसाने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3499.english_translation: Hearing the dialogue between Bharat and Ram, the root of all auspiciousness, the self-interested devas praised the Raghu line and showered flowers from the kalpa tree.
ramacharitamanas::3499.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / राम (Ram) / संबादु (dialogue) / सुनि (hearing) / सकल (all) / सुमंगल (auspicious) / मूल (root) / सुर (devas) / स्वारथी (self-interested) / सराहि (praising) / कुल (lineage) / बरषत (showering) / सुरतरु (kalpa tree) / फूल (flowers)
ramacharitamanas::3499.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3499.essence: Pure brotherly love becomes a blessing the whole world can recognize.
ramacharitamanas::3499.simple_meaning: Bharat and Ram speak with such goodness that even the devas celebrate the Raghu family and shower flowers.
ramacharitamanas::3499.simple_insight: Right conduct draws quiet praise, even from those with their own interests.
ramacharitamanas::3499.detailed_meaning: After Bharat meets Ram in exile and speaks from deep loyalty rather than ambition, the scene turns luminous. The devas recognize that this brotherly exchange is itself a source of blessing and honor the Raghu line by showering flowers.
ramacharitamanas::3499.modern_relevance: You watch two siblings choose love over status, and the room changes. Even people with hidden agendas can feel the force of a clean, selfless exchange.
ramacharitamanas::3499.insight: It shifts attention from dramatic events to the moral beauty of how people treat each other.

ramacharitamanas::3500.verse_sanskrit: धन्य भरत जय राम गोसाईं। कहत देव हरषत बरिआईं॥ मुनि मिथिलेस सभाँ सब काहू। भरत बचन सुनि भयउ उछाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3500.verse_hindi: 'भरतजी धन्य हैं, स्वामी श्री रामजी की जय हो!' ऐसा कहते हुए देवता बलपूर्वक (अत्यधिक) हर्षित होने लगे। भरतजी के वचन सुनकर मुनि वशिष्ठजी, मिथिलापति जनकजी और सभा में सब किसी को बड़ा उत्साह (आनंद) हुआ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3500.english_translation: ‘Blessed is Bharat, victory to Ram, the Lord of the world!’ Saying this, the devas became deeply joyful. Hearing Bharat’s words, the sage, King Janak, and everyone in the assembly felt great delight.
ramacharitamanas::3500.translation_literal: धन्य (blessed) / भरत (Bharat) / जय (victory) / राम (Ram) / गोसाईं (lord) / कहत (saying) / देव (devas) / हरषत (rejoicing) / बरिआईं (greatly) / मुनि (sage) / मिथिलेस (king of Mithila) / सभाँ (in the assembly) / सब (all) / काहू (everyone) / भरत (Bharat) / बचन (words) / सुनि (hearing) / भयउ (became) / उछाहू (delight, excitement)
ramacharitamanas::3500.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3500.essence: Bharat’s devotion makes everyone else rejoice too.
ramacharitamanas::3500.simple_meaning: Bharat’s words of devotion to Ram delight everyone, even the devas. The whole assembly feels uplifted by his praise.
ramacharitamanas::3500.simple_insight: Sincere devotion spreads joy beyond the person who speaks it.
ramacharitamanas::3500.detailed_meaning: In Janak’s assembly, Bharat’s humble words about Ram land like a blessing. The sage, King Janak, and everyone present feel lifted, and even the devas rejoice. This is a supporting moment in the larger praise of Bharat’s love for Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3500.modern_relevance: You say one honest sentence about someone you love, and the whole room softens. Real humility has that effect — it gives everyone permission to feel joy.
ramacharitamanas::3500.insight: It shifts attention from status to the joy created by sincere praise and humility.

ramacharitamanas::3501.verse_sanskrit: भरत राम गुन ग्राम सनेहू। पुलकि प्रसंसत राउ बिदेहू॥ सेवक स्वामि सुभाउ सुहावन। नेमु पेमु अति पावन पावन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3501.verse_hindi: भरतजी और श्री रामचन्द्रजी के गुण समूह की तथा प्रेम की विदेहराज जनकजी पुलकित होकर प्रशंसा कर रहे हैं। सेवक और स्वामी दोनों का सुंदर स्वभाव है। इनके नियम और प्रेम पवित्र को भी अत्यन्त पवित्र करने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3501.english_translation: Janaka, the king of Videha, joyfully praises the bond of love between Bharat and Ram, and the many virtues of both. The servant-and-master relationship between them is beautiful; their discipline and love purify even what is already pure.
ramacharitamanas::3501.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / राम (Ram) / गुन (virtues) / ग्राम (group, multitude) / सनेहू (love, affection) / पुलकि (with goosebumps, thrilled) / प्रसंसत (praising) / राउ (king) / बिदेहू (of Videha, Janaka) / सेवक (servant) / स्वामि (master) / सुभाउ (nature, disposition) / सुहावन (beautiful, pleasing) / नेमु (discipline, rule, custom) / पेमु (love) / अति (very) / पावन (pure) / पावन (pure)
ramacharitamanas::3501.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3501.essence: Devotion makes hierarchy beautiful instead of heavy.
ramacharitamanas::3501.simple_meaning: Janaka praises Bharat and Ram’s beautiful bond. Their servant-and-master relationship is so full of love and discipline that it makes holiness feel even holier.
ramacharitamanas::3501.simple_insight: True devotion does not diminish dignity; it deepens it.
ramacharitamanas::3501.detailed_meaning: In Janak's court, after Bharat and Ram's exchange, the king of Videha is visibly moved. He sees that their bond is not politics but sacred affection: a servant's humility and a master's grace joined in a way that makes everyone present reverent.
ramacharitamanas::3501.modern_relevance: You watch two people treat each other with such respect that the whole room changes. No one is performing; one serves, one receives, and the love between them feels cleaner than any rulebook.
ramacharitamanas::3501.insight: It shifts you to see discipline and affection as allies, not opposites.

ramacharitamanas::3502.verse_sanskrit: मति अनुसार सराहन लागे। सचिव सभासद सब अनुरागे॥ सुनि सुनि राम भरत संबादू। दुहु समाज हियँ हरषु विषादू॥3
ramacharitamanas::3502.verse_hindi: मंत्री और सभासद् सभी प्रेममुग्ध होकर अपनी-अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार सराहना करने लगे। श्री रामचन्द्रजी और भरतजी का संवाद सुन-सुनकर दोनों समाजों के हृदयों में हर्ष और विषाद (भरतजी के सेवा धर्म को देखकर हर्ष और रामवियोग की सम्भावना से विषाद) दोनों हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3502.english_translation: The ministers and assembly members, all filled with affection, began praising him according to their own understanding. Hearing the dialogue between Ram and Bharat again and again, both gatherings felt joy and sorrow in their hearts.
ramacharitamanas::3502.translation_literal: मति अनुसार (according to their understanding) / सराहन (to praise) / लागे (began) / सचिव (ministers) / सभासद (assembly members) / सब (all) / अनुरागे (filled with affection) / सुनि सुनि (hearing again and again) / राम (Ram) / भरत (Bharat) / संबादू (dialogue) / दुहु (both) / समाज (gatherings) / हियँ (in the heart) / हरषु (joy) / विषादू (sorrow)
ramacharitamanas::3502.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3502.essence: Love can make everyone glad and heartbroken at once.
ramacharitamanas::3502.simple_meaning: Everyone in both groups is moved by Ram and Bharat's exchange. They praise what they understand, while feeling both joy and sorrow at the same time.
ramacharitamanas::3502.simple_insight: A noble exchange can soften a whole room and stir opposite feelings at once.
ramacharitamanas::3502.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram and Bharat's meeting is being watched by ministers and courtiers on one side, and by the other gathering on the other. Their hearts are moved by the brothers' love, but the possibility of separation keeps sorrow alive.
ramacharitamanas::3502.modern_relevance: You overhear siblings speaking gently after a family rupture, and everyone nearby goes quiet. Their care feels healing, but it also reminds you what has been lost.
ramacharitamanas::3502.insight: It shows how sincere conduct can lift others without erasing grief. The scene carries both admiration and ache.

ramacharitamanas::3503.verse_sanskrit: राम मातु दुखु सुखु सम जानी। कहि गुन राम प्रबोधीं रानी॥ एक कहहिं रघुबीर बड़ाई। एक सराहत भरत भलाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3503.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी की माता कौसल्याजी ने दुःख और सुख को समान जानकर श्री रामजी के गुण कहकर दूसरी रानियों को धैर्य बँधाया। कोई श्री रामजी की बड़ाई (बड़प्पन) की चर्चा कर रहे हैं, तो कोई भरतजी के अच्छेपन की सराहना करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3503.english_translation: Seeing sorrow and joy as equal, Kaushalya comforted the queens by speaking of Ram's virtues. Some praised the greatness of Raghubir, while others praised Bharat's goodness.
ramacharitamanas::3503.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / मातु (mother) / दुखु (sorrow) / सुखु (joy) / सम (equal) / जानी (knowing) / कहि (speaking) / गुन (virtues) / राम (Ram) / प्रबोधीं (comforted) / रानी (queens)॥ / एक (some) / कहहिं (say) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / बड़ाई (greatness) / एक (some) / सराहत (praising) / भरत (Bharat) / भलाई (goodness) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3503.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3503.essence: Sorrow eases when you remember the goodness still standing beside it.
ramacharitamanas::3503.simple_meaning: Kaushalya steadies the grieving queens by speaking of Ram's virtues. In the same gathering, some admire Ram's greatness and others praise Bharat's goodness.
ramacharitamanas::3503.simple_insight: Grief softens when people speak of what is noble in each other.
ramacharitamanas::3503.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after Ram's exile has torn the family apart, the queens gather in sorrow. Kaushalya responds by holding sorrow and joy with the same mind, comforting them through Ram's virtues. Around her, the court divides into praise of Ram and praise of Bharat.
ramacharitamanas::3503.modern_relevance: At a family gathering after bad news, someone quietly changes the room by speaking of what is still good in each person. That doesn't erase the pain, but it keeps the heart from hardening.
ramacharitamanas::3503.insight: It shifts attention from raw hurt to the qualities that can still hold a family together.

ramacharitamanas::3504.verse_sanskrit: अत्रि कहेउ तब भरत सन सैल समीप सुकूप। राखिअ तीरथ तोय तहँ पावन अमिअ अनूप ॥
ramacharitamanas::3504.verse_hindi: तब अत्रिजी ने भरतजी से कहा- इस पर्वत के समीप ही एक सुंदर कुआँ है। इस पवित्र, अनुपम और अमृत जैसे तीर्थजल को उसी में स्थापित कर दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3504.english_translation: Then Atri said to Bharat, 'Near this hill is a lovely well. Place this sacred, unmatched, nectar-like pilgrimage water there.'
ramacharitamanas::3504.translation_literal: अत्रि (Atri) / कहेउ (said) / तब (then) / भरत सन (to Bharat) / सैल (hill/mountain) / समीप (near) / सुकूप (beautiful well) / राखिअ (place) / तीरथ (pilgrimage) / तोय (water) / तहँ (there) / पावन (pure) / अमिअ (nectar-like) / अनूप (matchless)
ramacharitamanas::3504.speaker: Atri
ramacharitamanas::3504.essence: Precious things also need a proper place.
ramacharitamanas::3504.simple_meaning: Atri points Bharat to a nearby well and asks him to place the sacred water there.
ramacharitamanas::3504.simple_insight: Even holy things must be placed with care, so they can keep serving others.
ramacharitamanas::3504.detailed_meaning: During Bharat's journey in exile, Atri guides him near a hill and shows him a well where the sacred water should be kept. The moment is practical and devotional, preparing the next step in the journey rather than delivering a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3504.modern_relevance: You carry a bottle of water after a long hike and look for the safest place to set it down. Small acts of care preserve what is precious.
ramacharitamanas::3504.insight: It shifts attention from reverence alone to the practical care that protects what is sacred.

ramacharitamanas::3505.verse_sanskrit: भरत अत्रि अनुसासन पाई। जल भाजन सब दिए चलाई॥ सानुज आपु अत्रि मुनि साधू। सहित गए जहँ कूप अगाधू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3505.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने अत्रिमुनि की आज्ञा पाकर जल के सब पात्र रवाना कर दिए और छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्न, अत्रि मुनि तथा अन्य साधु-संतों सहित आप वहाँ गए, जहाँ वह अथाह कुआँ था ॥
ramacharitamanas::3505.english_translation: Having received Atri's instruction, Bharata sent all the water vessels away. Then, with his younger brother Shatrughna, Atri Muni, and the other holy men, he went to the deep well.
ramacharitamanas::3505.translation_literal: भरत (Bharata) / अत्रि (Atri) / अनुसासन (instruction) / पाई (having received) / जल (water) / भाजन (vessels) / सब (all) / दिए (gave) / चलाई (sent away)॥ / सानुज (with younger brother) / आपु (himself) / अत्रि मुनि (Atri sage) / साधू (holy men) / सहित (together with) / गए (went) / जहँ (where) / कूप (well) / अगाधू (deep, unfathomable) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3505.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3505.essence: True humility turns instruction into immediate service.
ramacharitamanas::3505.simple_meaning: Bharata follows Atri's guidance, clears the vessels, and goes with Shatrughna and the sages to the deep well.
ramacharitamanas::3505.simple_insight: Quiet obedience can move a sacred task forward without drama.
ramacharitamanas::3505.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya's exile story, Bharata is traveling with saints and his brother Shatrughna. After Atri points out the well, Bharata immediately arranges the water vessels and goes with everyone to the place, showing respectful, practical service rather than hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::3505.modern_relevance: You get a clear instruction from someone wiser, and instead of debating it for an hour, you simply make it happen. That kind of clean response keeps a group moving.
ramacharitamanas::3505.insight: It teaches you to receive guidance quickly and turn it into action without ego or delay.

ramacharitamanas::3506.verse_sanskrit: पावन पाथ पुन्यथल राखा। प्रमुदित प्रेम अत्रि अस भाषा॥ तात अनादि सिद्ध थल एहू। लोपेउ काल बिदित नहिं केहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3506.verse_hindi: और उस पवित्र जल को उस पुण्य स्थल में रख दिया। तब अत्रि ऋषि ने प्रेम से आनंदित होकर ऐसा कहा- हे तात! यह अनादि सिद्धस्थल है। कालक्रम से यह लोप हो गया था, इसलिए किसी को इसका पता नहीं था ॥
ramacharitamanas::3506.english_translation: And the sacred water was placed in that holy site. Then Atri, delighted with love, said, “Dear one, this is an ancient, perfected place. It had been lost over time, so no one knew of it.”
ramacharitamanas::3506.translation_literal: पावन (sacred) / पाथ (water) / पुन्यथल (holy place) / राखा (placed) / प्रमुदित (delighted) / प्रेम (with love) / अत्रि (Atri) / अस (thus) / भाषा (spoke) / तात (dear one) / अनादि (beginningless) / सिद्ध (perfected) / थल (place) / एहू (this also) / लोपेउ (was lost) / काल (over time) / बिदित (known) / नहिं (not) / केहू (anyone)
ramacharitamanas::3506.speaker: Atri
ramacharitamanas::3506.essence: Hidden holiness can survive even when time buries its name.
ramacharitamanas::3506.simple_meaning: Atri rejoices that the sacred water has been restored to an ancient holy place that time had hidden from everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3506.simple_insight: Some places hold a sanctity that survives even when everyone forgets it.
ramacharitamanas::3506.detailed_meaning: After Bharat’s party brings the holy water to the site near Atri’s hermitage, Atri speaks with affection and relief. He recognizes the place as an ancient perfected spot that had disappeared from public memory, and this moment confirms the site’s hidden holiness.
ramacharitamanas::3506.modern_relevance: You return to a childhood home after years away and feel something still sacred in the cracked walls. Time covered it, but it never erased it.
ramacharitamanas::3506.insight: It shifts attention from visible neglect to the deeper sanctity that can remain untouched beneath it.

ramacharitamanas::3507.verse_sanskrit: तब सेवकन्ह सरस थलुदेखा। कीन्ह सुजल हित कूप बिसेषा॥ बिधि बस भयउ बिस्व उपकारू। सुगम अगम अति धरम बिचारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3507.verse_hindi: तब (भरतजी के) सेवकों ने उस जलयुक्त स्थान को देखा और उस सुंदर (तीर्थों के) जल के लिए एक खास कुआँ बना लिया। दैवयोग से विश्वभर का उपकार हो गया। धर्म का विचार जो अत्यन्त अगम था, वह (इस कूप के प्रभाव से) सुगम हो गया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3507.english_translation: Then the servants saw a water-rich spot and made a special well there for the sacred water. By providence, a blessing for the whole world arose. What is extremely hard to understand about dharma became easy to follow.
ramacharitamanas::3507.translation_literal: तब (then) / सेवकन्ह (the servants) / सरस (full of water, pleasant) / थलु (place) / देखा (saw) / कीन्ह (made) / सुजल (good water, sacred water) / हित (for the benefit of) / कूप (well) / बिसेषा (special) / बिधि (providence, fate) / बस (by the power of) / भयउ (became) / बिस्व (world) / उपकारू (benefit, help) / सुगम (easy) / अगम (hard to reach, difficult) / अति (very) / धरम (dharma) / बिचारू (consideration, reflection)
ramacharitamanas::3507.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3507.essence: A single well can turn difficult duty into shared ease.
ramacharitamanas::3507.simple_meaning: Bharat's servants find a water-rich place and create a special well for pilgrims. What was hard to arrange becomes a blessing for everyone, making a difficult dharmic need easy to meet.
ramacharitamanas::3507.simple_insight: Good service can turn a local need into a gift for many.
ramacharitamanas::3507.detailed_meaning: Bharat has come with sages and servants to a holy place near Atri's hermitage. Seeing the need for clean water, they dig a special well. The scene is still practical and local, but its effect becomes larger than anyone planned.
ramacharitamanas::3507.modern_relevance: A neighborhood volunteers to install a water point near a temple fair, and suddenly elderly visitors, children, and pilgrims all benefit. One careful act quietly makes life easier for everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3507.insight: It shifts you from seeing a small practical fix to seeing service that blesses many people.

ramacharitamanas::3508.verse_sanskrit: भरतकूप अब कहिहहिं लोगा। अति पावन तीरथ जल जोगा॥ प्रेम सनेम निमज्जत प्रानी। होइहहिं बिमल करम मन बानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3508.verse_hindi: अब इसको लोग भरतकूप कहेंगे। तीर्थों के जल के संयोग से तो यह अत्यन्त ही पवित्र हो गया। इसमें प्रेमपूर्वक नियम से स्नान करने पर प्राणी मन, वचन और कर्म से निर्मल हो जाएँगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3508.english_translation: People will now call it Bharat's Well. Joined with the waters of holy places, it has become deeply sacred. Anyone who bathes here with love and discipline will become pure in mind, speech, and action.
ramacharitamanas::3508.translation_literal: भरतकूप (Bharat's well) / अब (now) / कहिहहिं (will call) / लोगा (people) / अति (very) / पावन (sacred) / तीरथ (holy place) / जल (water) / जोगा (joined with) ॥ प्रेम (love) / सनेम (with discipline) / निमज्जत (bathing) / प्रानी (a person) / होइहहिं (will become) / बिमल (pure) / करम (action) / मन (mind) / बानी (speech) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3508.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3508.essence: Love and disciplined devotion make purity possible.
ramacharitamanas::3508.simple_meaning: A well becomes sacred through the waters of holy places, and anyone who bathes there with love and discipline becomes pure in thought, speech, and action.
ramacharitamanas::3508.simple_insight: Purity is not just about ritual water; it begins when your intention is sincere.
ramacharitamanas::3508.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the servants create Bharat's Well near a sacred site where holy waters have been gathered. The verse turns that place into a living symbol: love and disciplined devotion can cleanse a person from the inside out.
ramacharitamanas::3508.modern_relevance: You step into a temple after carrying weeks of resentment, and something in you softens. The place matters, but what changes you most is the love and steadiness you bring with you.
ramacharitamanas::3508.insight: It shifts attention from outer cleansing alone to the inner state that makes cleansing real.

ramacharitamanas::3509.verse_sanskrit: कहत कूप महिमा सकल गए जहाँ रघुराउ। अत्रि सुनायउ रघुबरहि तीरथ पुन्य प्रभाउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3509.verse_hindi: कूप की महिमा कहते हुए सब लोग वहाँ गए जहाँ श्री रघुनाथजी थे। श्री रघुनाथजी को अत्रिजी ने उस तीर्थ का पुण्य प्रभाव सुनाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3509.english_translation: While speaking of the well’s greatness, everyone went to the place where Raghunath was. Atri then told Raghubar about the sacred power of that holy spot.
ramacharitamanas::3509.translation_literal: कहत (speaking) / कूप (well) / महिमा (greatness) / सकल (all) / गए (went) / जहाँ (where) / रघुराउ (Raghunath) / अत्रि (Atri) / सुनायउ (told) / रघुबरहि (to Raghubar) / तीरथ (holy place) / पुन्य (meritorious) / प्रभाउ (power, effect)
ramacharitamanas::3509.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3509.essence: Reverence gathers people before the sacred place itself does.
ramacharitamanas::3509.simple_meaning: People gathered around Ram while the greatness of the well and the holiness of the place were being described.
ramacharitamanas::3509.simple_insight: Sacred places become more alive when shared in reverence, not just visited in silence.
ramacharitamanas::3509.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's well has become a place of reverence. As people speak about its greatness, they gather where Ram is staying, and Atri explains the holy power of the site. The verse mainly moves the scene forward.
ramacharitamanas::3509.modern_relevance: A group stands around a new memorial, passing the story from person to person. The place matters, but the shared reverence is what gives it weight.
ramacharitamanas::3509.insight: It shifts attention from the object itself to the meaning a community places around it.

ramacharitamanas::3510.verse_sanskrit: कहत धरम इतिहास सप्रीती। भयउ भोरु निसि सो सुख बीती॥ नित्य निबाहि भरत दोउ भाई। राम अत्रि गुर आयसु पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3510.verse_hindi: प्रेमपूर्वक धर्म के इतिहास कहते वह रात सुख से बीत गई और सबेरा हो गया। भरत-शत्रुघ्न दोनों भाई नित्यक्रिया पूरी करके, श्री रामजी, अत्रिजी और गुरु वशिष्ठजी की आज्ञा पाकर, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3510.english_translation: They spent the night happily, talking lovingly about sacred duty and its stories. At dawn, Bharat and Shatrughna completed their morning rites, then received the blessings of Ram, Atri, and Guru Vashistha.
ramacharitamanas::3510.translation_literal: कहत (speaking) / धरम (duty) / इतिहास (stories) / सप्रीती (with affection) / भयउ (became) / भोरु (dawn) / निसि (night) / सो (that) / सुख (happily) / बीती (passed) / नित्य (daily) / निबाहि (having completed) / भरत (Bharat) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / राम (Ram) / अत्रि (Atri) / गुर (teacher) / आयसु (command) / पाई (having received)
ramacharitamanas::3510.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3510.essence: A night of loving remembrance prepares the heart for the next duty.
ramacharitamanas::3510.simple_meaning: The night passed in loving talk about duty and sacred stories. At dawn, Bharat and Shatrughna finished their morning rites and received blessings before moving on.
ramacharitamanas::3510.simple_insight: Shared reverence can turn even a long night into peace.
ramacharitamanas::3510.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat and Shatrughna are staying in a holy place near Ram. The night passes in affectionate discussion of duty and sacred history. At dawn, after their rites, they receive blessings from Ram, Atri, and their teacher before the journey continues.
ramacharitamanas::3510.modern_relevance: A long night in a quiet guest room, talking with family after a hard decision, can feel strangely light. When the conversation is rooted in what matters, morning arrives without heaviness.
ramacharitamanas::3510.insight: It places spiritual conversation and daily discipline before action, letting the next step begin from clarity.

ramacharitamanas::3511.verse_sanskrit: सहित समाज साज सब सादें। चले राम बन अटन पयादें॥ कोमल चरन चलत बिनु पनहीं। भइ मृदु भूमि सकुचि मन मनहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3511.verse_hindi: समाज सहित सब सादे साज से श्री रामजी के वन में भ्रमण (प्रदक्षिणा) करने के लिए पैदल ही चले। कोमल चरण हैं और बिना जूते के चल रहे हैं, यह देखकर पृथ्वी मन ही मन सकुचाकर कोमल हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3511.english_translation: Ram set out barefoot for the forest with the whole company in simple dress. His soft feet touched the ground without shoes, and the earth, shy at heart, became gentle.
ramacharitamanas::3511.translation_literal: सहित (together with) / समाज (company, assembly) / साज (dress, adornment) / सब (all) / सादें (plain, simple) / चले (went) / राम (Ram) / बन (forest) / अटन (walking, roaming) / पयादें (on foot, barefoot)॥ / कोमल (soft) / चरन (feet) / चलत (walking) / बिनु (without) / पनहीं (shoes) / भइ (became) / मृदु (soft) / भूमि (earth) / सकुचि (shy, modest) / मन (mind) / मनहीं (within the mind) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3511.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3511.essence: Humility can make even exile feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3511.simple_meaning: Ram leaves for the forest on foot, dressed simply. His tender feet make even the earth feel shy and soft.
ramacharitamanas::3511.simple_insight: Even a hard journey can be carried with grace and humility.
ramacharitamanas::3511.detailed_meaning: Ram has accepted exile and now leaves Ayodhya with his companions, dressed plainly and walking barefoot. The scene lingers on his soft feet and the earth's tenderness, turning a departure into a quiet image of dignity and sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::3511.modern_relevance: You leave home before sunrise with a backpack, no fanfare, and a heavy heart. The way you carry yourself can still make the moment feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3511.insight: It shifts attention from the fact of leaving to the grace with which you leave.

ramacharitamanas::3512.verse_sanskrit: कुस कंटक काँकरीं कुराईं। कटुक कठोर कुबस्तु दुराईं॥ महि मंजुल मृदु मारग कीन्हे। बहत समीर त्रिबिध सुख लीन्हे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3512.verse_hindi: कुश, काँटे, कंकड़ी, दरारों आदि कड़वी, कठोर और बुरी वस्तुओं को छिपाकर पृथ्वी ने सुंदर और कोमल मार्ग कर दिए। सुखों को साथ लिए (सुखदायक) शीतल, मंद, सुगंध हवा चलने लगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3512.english_translation: Thorns, sharp gravel, roughness, and harsh things were hidden away. The earth made the path lovely and soft, and the wind blew gently, carrying a threefold comfort.
