ramacharitamanas::3512.translation_literal: कुस (kusa grass) / कंटक (thorns) / काँकरीं (pebbles) / कुराईं (roughnesses) / कटुक (bitter) / कठोर (hard) / कुबस्तु (bad things) / दुराईं (hidden away) / महि (earth) / मंजुल (lovely) / मृदु (soft) / मारग (path) / कीन्हे (made) / बहत (flowing) / समीर (wind) / त्रिबिध (threefold) / सुख (comfort) / लीन्हे (took/received)
ramacharitamanas::3512.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3512.essence: The path softens itself for the one walking in dharma.
ramacharitamanas::3512.simple_meaning: The road becomes soft and pleasant for Ram's walk, as if nature itself removes every rough thing in his way.
ramacharitamanas::3512.simple_insight: When your steps are aligned with what is right, even the world seems to soften around you.
ramacharitamanas::3512.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, Bharat, and the others are walking toward the forest after the exile begins. The earth itself seems to care for Ram's feet, hiding thorns and stones and sending a gentle breeze. The scene shows nature honoring his departure.
ramacharitamanas::3512.modern_relevance: You leave home carrying a heavy goodbye, and the street feels strangely quiet, almost kind. Even grief can seem to soften when you walk with the right purpose.
ramacharitamanas::3512.insight: It shifts attention from hardship to the quiet support that appears around righteous action.

ramacharitamanas::3513.verse_sanskrit: सुमन बरषि सुर घन करि छाहीं। बिटप फूलि फलि तृन मृदुताहीं॥ मृग बिलोकि खग बोलि सुबानी। सेवहिं सकल राम प्रिय जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3513.verse_hindi: रास्ते में देवता फूल बरसाकर, बादल छाया करके, वृक्ष फूल-फलकर, तृण अपनी कोमलता से, मृग (पशु) देखकर और पक्षी सुंदर वाणी बोलकर सभी भरतजी को श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्यारे जानकर उनकी सेवा करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3513.english_translation: The gods showered flowers and made shade with clouds. Trees blossomed and fruited, grass softened, deer looked on, and birds sang sweetly, all serving Bharat as one dear to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3513.translation_literal: सुमन (flowers) / बरषि (showering) / सुर (devas) / घन (clouds) / करि (making) / छाहीं (shade) / बिटप (trees) / फूलि (flowering) / फलि (fruiting) / तृन (grass) / मृदुताहीं (softness) / मृग (deer) / बिलोकि (seeing) / खग (birds) / बोलि (speaking) / सुबानी (sweet words) / सेवहिं (serve) / सकल (all) / राम (Ram) / प्रिय (dear) / जानी (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::3513.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3513.essence: Pure devotion makes even nature feel like a servant.
ramacharitamanas::3513.simple_meaning: Everything around Bharat responds to him kindly. Flowers fall, shade appears, plants bloom, grass softens, and even animals and birds seem to serve him because he is dear to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3513.simple_insight: When your devotion is pure, the world itself seems to soften around you.
ramacharitamanas::3513.detailed_meaning: As Bharat travels in exile-like humility, nature itself seems to honor him. Gods, trees, grass, deer, and birds all appear to serve him because he belongs so completely to Ram. It is a beautiful scene of the world mirroring devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3513.modern_relevance: You walk into a room carrying no agenda, only love for someone else’s good. Even the atmosphere feels different — softer, kinder, almost welcoming you.
ramacharitamanas::3513.insight: It turns Bharat’s presence into a sign that selfless love changes how the world is experienced.

ramacharitamanas::3514.verse_sanskrit: सुलभ सिद्धि सब प्राकृतहु राम कहत जमुहात। राम प्रानप्रिय भरत कहुँ यह न होइ बड़ि बात ॥
ramacharitamanas::3514.verse_hindi: जब एक साधारण मनुष्य को भी (आलस्य से) जँभाई लेते समय 'राम' कह देने से ही सब सिद्धियाँ सुलभ हो जाती हैं, तब श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्राण प्यारे भरतजी के लिए यह कोई बड़ी (आश्चर्य की) बात नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3514.english_translation: When even an ordinary person can gain ease by saying Ram while yawning, then for Ram's dearest Bharat, that is no great wonder.
ramacharitamanas::3514.translation_literal: सुलभ (easy) / सिद्धि (attainment) / सब (all) / प्राकृतहु (even for an ordinary person) / राम (Ram) / कहत (saying) / जमुहात (while yawning) / राम (Ram) / प्रानप्रिय (dearest to life) / भरत (Bharat) / कहुँ (for) / यह (this) / न (not) / होइ (is) / बड़ि (big) / बात (matter)
ramacharitamanas::3514.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3514.essence: True devotion makes Ram's name feel as natural as breathing.
ramacharitamanas::3514.simple_meaning: Even an ordinary person can find ease by saying Ram's name. For Bharat, who loves Ram more than life itself, this is completely natural.
ramacharitamanas::3514.simple_insight: Deep love makes remembrance effortless; what feels miraculous to others feels ordinary to the devoted heart.
ramacharitamanas::3514.detailed_meaning: As Bharat walks through the forest in exile, Tulsidas pauses to praise his devotion. Even a casual utterance of Ram's name can bring spiritual ease to ordinary people; for Bharat, whose whole life is fixed on Ram, that power is unsurprising.
ramacharitamanas::3514.modern_relevance: You catch yourself whispering a loved one's name when you're exhausted, and it steadies you without effort. That is the kind of ease Bharat feels with Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3514.insight: It shifts remembrance from a practice you force into a love that rises by itself.

ramacharitamanas::3515.verse_sanskrit: एहि बिधि भरतु फिरत बन माहीं। नेमु प्रेमु लखि मुनि सकुचाहीं॥ पुन्य जलाश्रय भूमि बिभागा। खग मृग तरु तृन गिरि बन बागा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3515.verse_hindi: इस प्रकार भरतजी वन में फिर रहे हैं। उनके नियम और प्रेम को देखकर मुनि भी सकुचा जाते हैं। पवित्र जल के स्थान (नदी, बावली, कुंड आदि) पृथ्वी के पृथक-पृथक भाग, पक्षी, पशु, वृक्ष, तृण (घास), पर्वत, वन और बगीचे- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3515.english_translation: In this way Bharat wandered through the forest. His discipline and love made even the sages feel shy. The sacred waters, the separate lands, birds, beasts, trees, grasses, hills, forests, and gardens—
ramacharitamanas::3515.translation_literal: एहि बिधि (in this way) / भरतु (Bharat) / फिरत (wandering) / बन माहीं (in the forest) / नेमु (discipline, vow) / प्रेमु (love) / लखि (seeing) / मुनि (sages) / सकुचाहीं (feel shy) / पुन्य (sacred) / जलाश्रय (water-abodes, places of water) / भूमि (land) / बिभागा (distinct parts) / खग (birds) / मृग (beasts) / तरु (trees) / तृन (grasses) / गिरि (hills) / बन (forest) / बागा (gardens)
ramacharitamanas::3515.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3515.essence: Love held with discipline makes even saints feel humble.
ramacharitamanas::3515.simple_meaning: Bharat wanders through the forest with such disciplined love that even sages feel humbled. The verse then begins listing the sacred and beautiful features of the landscape.
ramacharitamanas::3515.simple_insight: True devotion can be so steady and pure that it quietly humbles everyone around it.
ramacharitamanas::3515.detailed_meaning: Bharat is moving through the forest in Ayodhyakand, living with restraint and deep love for Ram. The sages notice his conduct and feel shy before it. The verse then shifts into a catalogue of the holy landscape, setting up the next exchange.
ramacharitamanas::3515.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for someone without asking for credit, and the people around you go quiet. Your consistency speaks louder than praise ever could.
ramacharitamanas::3515.insight: It highlights how disciplined devotion changes the atmosphere around you, even before anyone speaks.

ramacharitamanas::3516.verse_sanskrit: चारु बिचित्र पबित्र बिसेषी। बूझत भरतु दिब्य सब देखी॥ सुनि मन मुदित कहत रिषिराऊ। हेतु नाम गुन पुन्य प्रभाऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3516.verse_hindi: सभी विशेष रूप से सुंदर, विचित्र, पवित्र और दिव्य देखकर भरतजी पूछते हैं और उनका प्रश्न सुनकर ऋषिराज अत्रिजी प्रसन्न मन से सबके कारण, नाम, गुण और पुण्य प्रभाव को कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3516.english_translation: Seeing everything as beautiful, wondrous, pure, and divine, Bharata asks. Hearing him, the sage-king speaks with joy about the cause, the name, the qualities, and the power of merit.
ramacharitamanas::3516.translation_literal: चारु (beautiful) / बिचित्र (wondrous) / पबित्र (pure) / बिसेषी (especially) / बूझत (asking) / भरतु (Bharata) / दिब्य (divine) / सब (all) / देखी (having seen) / सुनि (hearing) / मन (mind) / मुदित (joyful) / कहत (speaks) / रिषिराऊ (sage-king) / हेतु (cause) / नाम (name) / गुन (qualities) / पुन्य (merit) / प्रभाऊ (power/effect)
ramacharitamanas::3516.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3516.essence: Wonder grows when you ask before you assume.
ramacharitamanas::3516.simple_meaning: Bharata looks at the holy places and asks about them. The sage answers happily, explaining their source, names, qualities, and sacred power.
ramacharitamanas::3516.simple_insight: Curiosity opens the door to deeper meaning.
ramacharitamanas::3516.detailed_meaning: Bharata is moving through the forest with reverence, seeing every place as sacred. He asks questions instead of assuming he already knows. The sage-king responds gladly, showing that devotion begins with humble inquiry.
ramacharitamanas::3516.modern_relevance: You stand in a temple courtyard, unsure why each corner matters, and ask the elder beside you. That simple question turns scenery into meaning.
ramacharitamanas::3516.insight: It shifts you from passive seeing to reverent inquiry, where even ordinary places become instructive.

ramacharitamanas::3517.verse_sanskrit: कतहुँ निमज्जन कतहुँ प्रनामा। कतहुँ बिलोकत मन अभिरामा॥ कतहुँ बैठि मुनि आयसु पाई। सुमिरत सीय सहित दोउ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3517.verse_hindi: भरतजी कहीं स्नान करते हैं, कहीं प्रणाम करते हैं, कहीं मनोहर स्थानों के दर्शन करते हैं और कहीं मुनि अत्रिजी की आज्ञा पाकर बैठकर, सीताजी सहित श्री राम-लक्ष्मण दोनों भाइयों का स्मरण करते हैं ॥ तो इसमें लाभ अधिक और हानि कम प्रतीत हुई, परन्तु रानियों को दुःख-सुख समान ही थे (राम-लक्ष्मण वन में रहें या भरत-शत्रुघ्न, दो पुत्रों का वियोग तो रहेगा ही), यह समझकर वे सब रोने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3517.english_translation: Bharat moves through the forest, bathing here, bowing there, beholding lovely places, and sitting where the sage permits, remembering Ram and Lakshman with Sita. Seeing this, the queens weep, realizing that loss remains loss whether the sons stay or go.
ramacharitamanas::3517.translation_literal: कतहुँ (somewhere) / निमज्जन (bathing) / कतहुँ (somewhere) / प्रनामा (bowing) / कतहुँ (somewhere) / बिलोकत (seeing) / मन (mind) / अभिरामा (delightful) / कतहुँ (somewhere) / बैठि (sitting) / मुनि (sage) / आयसु (permission) / पाई (having received) / सुमिरत (remembering) / सीय (Sita) / सहित (together with) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::3517.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3517.essence: Sacred routines cannot cancel the pain of separation.
ramacharitamanas::3517.simple_meaning: Bharat spends his time bathing, bowing, looking at holy places, and remembering Ram and Lakshman with Sita. The queens see that whatever happens, separation still hurts.
ramacharitamanas::3517.simple_insight: Even holy places and sacred routines cannot erase the ache of separation.
ramacharitamanas::3517.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Bharat moves with reverence and restraint under the sage's guidance. He bathes, bows, looks around, and remembers Ram, Lakshman, and Sita. The verse closes by showing the queens' grief: whatever arrangement is made, they still feel the pain of absence.
ramacharitamanas::3517.modern_relevance: You can visit every meaningful place, follow every careful ritual, and still feel the same missing person in your chest when you get home.
ramacharitamanas::3517.insight: It shifts attention from outward movement to the deeper fact that grief follows love, not location.

ramacharitamanas::3518.verse_sanskrit: देखि सुभाउ सनेहु सुसेवा। देहिं असीस मुदित बनदेवा॥ फिरहिं गएँ दिनु पहर अढ़ाई। प्रभु पद कमल बिलोकहिं आई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3518.verse_hindi: भरतजी के स्वभाव, प्रेम और सुंदर सेवाभाव को देखकर वनदेवता आनंदित होकर आशीर्वाद देते हैं। यों घूम-फिरकर ढाई पहर दिन बीतने पर लौट पड़ते हैं और आकर प्रभु श्री रघुनाथजी के चरणकमलों का दर्शन करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3518.english_translation: Seeing Bharata's nature, love, and selfless service, the forest spirits gladly give blessings. After wandering for two and a half watches, he returns and again beholds the lotus feet of Lord Raghunatha.
ramacharitamanas::3518.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / सुभाउ (nature) / सनेहु (love) / सुसेवा (beautiful service) / देहिं (give) / असीस (blessings) / मुदित (joyful) / बनदेवा (forest deities) / फिरहिं (they return) / गएँ (having gone) / दिनु (day) / पहर (watch) / अढ़ाई (two and a half) / प्रभु (lord) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / बिलोकहिं (behold) / आई (coming)
ramacharitamanas::3518.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3518.essence: Selfless love earns blessings and keeps turning back to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3518.simple_meaning: Bharata's loving, selfless conduct wins the blessings of the forest beings, and after wandering for a while he returns to see Ram's feet again.
ramacharitamanas::3518.simple_insight: Quiet service changes the atmosphere around you; even the world seems to bless sincerity.
ramacharitamanas::3518.detailed_meaning: Bharata is moving through the forest in exile, not as a king but as Ram's devoted brother. The forest spirits see his love and humble service, bless him, and watch him return again to Ram's feet after wandering for two and a half watches.
ramacharitamanas::3518.modern_relevance: You show up for someone with no agenda, no performance, no demand for credit. People feel it. The room softens around that kind of sincerity.
ramacharitamanas::3518.insight: It highlights how selfless conduct draws goodwill and keeps attention returning to what truly matters.

ramacharitamanas::3519.verse_sanskrit: देखे थल तीरथ सकल भरत पाँच दिन माझ। कहत सुनत हरि हर सुजसु गयउ दिवसु भइ साँझ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3519.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने पाँच दिन में सब तीर्थ स्थानों के दर्शन कर लिए। भगवान विष्णु और महादेवजी का सुंदर यश कहते-सुनते वह (पाँचवाँ) दिन भी बीत गया, संध्या हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3519.english_translation: In five days, Bharat visited all the holy places. Speaking and listening to the beautiful fame of Hari and Shiva, the fifth day also passed, and evening fell.
ramacharitamanas::3519.translation_literal: देखे (saw) / थल (places) / तीरथ (holy places) / सकल (all) / भरत (Bharat) / पाँच दिन (five days) / माझ (within) / कहत (speaking) / सुनत (listening) / हरि (Hari) / हर (Shiva) / सुजसु (beautiful fame) / गयउ (passed) / दिवसु (day) / भइ (became) / साँझ (evening)
ramacharitamanas::3519.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3519.essence: Devotion makes even time feel like worship.
ramacharitamanas::3519.simple_meaning: Bharat spent five days visiting holy places and listening to praises of Hari and Shiva until evening came.
ramacharitamanas::3519.simple_insight: A devoted heart can turn even a long journey into worship.
ramacharitamanas::3519.detailed_meaning: Bharat is moving through the forest with reverence, not haste. He keeps visiting sacred places, hearing the praise of Ram and Shiva, and the days slip by in his devotion. This couplet simply marks the passage of that holy, unhurried time.
ramacharitamanas::3519.modern_relevance: You spend a whole weekend moving from one sacred place to another, never rushing, never checking the clock. The hours disappear because your attention is fully given.
ramacharitamanas::3519.insight: It shifts attention from schedule and distance to reverent presence.

ramacharitamanas::3520.verse_sanskrit: भोर न्हाइ सबु जुरा समाजू। भरत भूमिसुर तेरहुति राजू॥ भल दिन आजु जानि मन माहीं। रामु कृपाल कहत सकुचाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3520.verse_hindi: (अगले छठे दिन) सबेरे स्नान करके भरतजी, ब्राह्मण, राजा जनक और सारा समाज आ जुटा। आज सबको विदा करने के लिए अच्छा दिन है, यह मन में जानकर भी कृपालु श्री रामजी कहने में सकुचा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3520.english_translation: At dawn, after bathing, Bharata, the Brahmins, King Janaka, and the whole assembly gathered. Knowing in his heart that today was a good day to send them off, compassionate Ram still felt shy to speak.
ramacharitamanas::3520.translation_literal: भोर (dawn) / न्हाइ (having bathed) / सबु (all) / जुरा (gathered) / समाजू (assembly) / भरत (Bharata) / भूमिसुर (Brahmins) / तेरहुति (of Tirhut) / राजू (King) / भल (good) / दिन (day) / आजु (today) / जानि (knowing) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / रामु (Ram) / कृपाल (compassionate) / कहत (speaking) / सकुचाहीं (felt shy)
ramacharitamanas::3520.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3520.essence: Compassion can make the right words hard to say.
ramacharitamanas::3520.simple_meaning: After the morning bath, Bharata, the priests, King Janaka, and everyone gather. Ram knows it is the right day to speak, but he still hesitates out of gentle modesty.
ramacharitamanas::3520.simple_insight: Even the clearest right action can still feel tender and difficult.
ramacharitamanas::3520.detailed_meaning: At dawn in Ayodhya, Bharata, Janaka, the Brahmins, and the whole gathering are ready. Ram knows this is the proper moment to send them back, but his compassionate nature makes him hesitate. The scene shows his softness before he finally speaks.
ramacharitamanas::3520.modern_relevance: You know the meeting should end, the message should be sent, or the goodbye should happen. Even then, your care for people can make the words catch in your throat.
ramacharitamanas::3520.insight: It shows that right action need not be cold; compassion can make even necessary speech feel hesitant.

ramacharitamanas::3521.verse_sanskrit: गुर नृप भरत सभा अवलोकी। सकुचि राम फिरि अवनि बिलोकी॥ सील सराहि सभा सब सोची। कहुँ न राम सम स्वामि सँकोची ॥
ramacharitamanas::3521.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने गुरु वशिष्ठजी, राजा जनकजी, भरतजी और सारी सभा की ओर देखा, किन्तु फिर सकुचाकर दृष्टि फेरकर वे पृथ्वी की ओर ताकने लगे। सभा उनके शील की सराहना करके सोचती है कि श्री रामचन्द्रजी के समान संकोची स्वामी कहीं नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3521.english_translation: Ram looked at Guru Vashishtha, King Janaka, Bharata, and the whole assembly, then, feeling shy, looked down at the ground. The whole assembly praised his humility and thought, "No master is as modest as Ram."
ramacharitamanas::3521.translation_literal: गुर (the teacher) / नृप (king) / भरत (Bharata) / सभा (assembly) / अवलोकी (looked at) / सकुचि (feeling shy) / राम (Ram) / फिरि (again) / अवनि (earth) / बिलोकी (looked) / सील (humility) / सराहि (praising) / सभा (assembly) / सब (all) / सोची (thought) / कहुँ (say) / न (not) / राम (Ram) / सम (like) / स्वामि (master) / सँकोची (modest/shy)
ramacharitamanas::3521.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3521.essence: The highest master is the one who stays modest.
ramacharitamanas::3521.simple_meaning: Ram feels shy before the gathered elders and lowers his gaze. The assembly sees his humility and praises him as the most modest master.
ramacharitamanas::3521.simple_insight: Real greatness does not need to announce itself. It can be soft, respectful, and still fully sovereign.
ramacharitamanas::3521.detailed_meaning: In Bharata’s assembly at Ayodhya, Ram stands before Guru Vashishtha, Janaka, Bharata, and the elders. Instead of claiming attention, he lowers his eyes. The gathering is moved by his natural humility and sees that his greatness is inseparable from modesty.
ramacharitamanas::3521.modern_relevance: You walk into a room where everyone expects you to speak first, defend yourself, or take credit. Instead, you listen, soften, and let your conduct carry the weight. People remember that far longer than a performance.
ramacharitamanas::3521.insight: It shifts respect away from self-display and toward quiet self-command.

ramacharitamanas::3522.verse_sanskrit: भरत सुजान राम रुख देखी। उठि सप्रेम धरि धीर बिसेषी॥ करि दंडवत कहत कर जोरी। राखीं नाथ सकल रुचि मोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3522.verse_hindi: सुजान भरतजी श्री रामचन्द्रजी का रुख देखकर प्रेमपूर्वक उठकर, विशेष रूप से धीरज धारण कर दण्डवत करके हाथ जोड़कर कहने लगे- हे नाथ! आपने मेरी सभी रुचियाँ रखीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3522.english_translation: Wise Bharat saw Ram's face, rose with love, and held himself steady. Bowing low with joined hands, he said, “Lord, you have fulfilled all my wishes.”
ramacharitamanas::3522.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / सुजान (wise) / राम (Ram) / रुख (face, bearing) / देखी (having seen) / उठि (rising) / सप्रेम (with love) / धरि (holding) / धीर (steadiness) / बिसेषी (especially) / करि (doing) / दंडवत (full bow) / कहत (saying) / कर जोरी (with joined hands) / राखीं (kept, fulfilled) / नाथ (Lord) / सकल (all) / रुचि (desires, wishes) / मोरी (my)
ramacharitamanas::3522.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3522.essence: Love kneels and discovers it was already complete.
ramacharitamanas::3522.simple_meaning: Bharat sees Ram and responds with love, humility, and self-control. He tells Ram that all his wishes are already fulfilled in Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::3522.simple_insight: Real fulfillment can arrive before you ask for anything. Reverence itself can be enough.
ramacharitamanas::3522.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram after the pain of exile has fractured the family. Seeing Ram's face, he rises with love, bows fully, and speaks with steady humility. His first feeling is not demand, but gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::3522.modern_relevance: You finally meet the person you have missed for months, and all the rehearsed words disappear. What comes out instead is simple gratitude: just being near them is enough.
ramacharitamanas::3522.insight: It shifts attention from asking for more to recognising fullness already present in devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3523.verse_sanskrit: मोहि लगि सहेउ सबहिं संतापू। बहुत भाँति दुखु पावा आपू॥ अब गोसाइँ मोहि देउ रजाई। सेवौं अवध अवधि भरि जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3523.verse_hindi: मेरे लिए सब लोगों ने संताप सहा और आपने भी बहुत प्रकार से दुःख पाया। अब स्वामी मुझे आज्ञा दें। मैं जाकर अवधि भर (चौदह वर्ष तक) अवध का सेवन करूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3523.english_translation: For my sake, everyone has endured sorrow, and you too have suffered in many ways. Now, my lord, give me your command. I will go and serve Ayodhya for the full term.
ramacharitamanas::3523.translation_literal: मोहि (for me) / लगि (for the sake of) / सहेउ (endured) / सबहिं (everyone) / संतापू (sorrow) / बहुत भाँति (in many ways) / दुखु (pain) / पावा (suffered) / आपू (you yourself) / अब (now) / गोसाइँ (my lord) / मोहि (to me) / देउ (give) / रजाई (command) / सेवौं (I will serve) / अवध (Ayodhya) / अवधि भरि (for the full term) / जाई (going)
ramacharitamanas::3523.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3523.essence: Real love asks for work, not comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3523.simple_meaning: Bharat says everyone has suffered because of him, including Ram. He asks Ram for permission to return and serve Ayodhya for the full exile period.
ramacharitamanas::3523.simple_insight: Love becomes real when it turns into service, not excuses.
ramacharitamanas::3523.detailed_meaning: In the royal assembly at Chitrakoot, Bharat stands before Ram after seeing the cost of the exile. He does not ask for power; he asks for permission to serve Ayodhya in Ram's absence, carrying the burden of love as duty.
ramacharitamanas::3523.modern_relevance: You realize your mistake has cost other people sleep, money, and peace. Instead of defending yourself, you ask how to make things right and keep showing up until the damage is repaired.
ramacharitamanas::3523.insight: It shifts you from self-protection to responsible service after harm has been caused.

ramacharitamanas::3524.verse_sanskrit: जेहिं उपाय पुनि पाय जनु देखै दीनदयाल। सो सिख देइअ अवधि लगि कोसलपाल कृपाल ॥
ramacharitamanas::3524.verse_hindi: हे दीनदयालु! जिस उपाय से यह दास फिर चरणों का दर्शन करे- हे कोसलाधीश! हे कृपालु! अवधिभर के लिए मुझे वही शिक्षा दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3524.english_translation: O compassionate one, by whatever means this servant may again behold your feet, O lord of Kosala and merciful one, teach me that way for the whole period of my stay.
ramacharitamanas::3524.translation_literal: जेहिं (by which) / उपाय (means) / पुनि (again) / पाय (feet) / जनु (this servant) / देखै (may see) / दीनदयाल (compassionate one) / सो (that) / सिख (instruction) / देइअ (give) / अवधि लगि (for the full period) / कोसलपाल (lord of Kosala) / कृपाल (merciful one)
ramacharitamanas::3524.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3524.essence: True devotion asks for the way back, not the reward.
ramacharitamanas::3524.simple_meaning: Bharat asks Ram to teach him the one way that will let him see Ram again and remain devoted for the whole exile period.
ramacharitamanas::3524.simple_insight: Love becomes practical when you ask for the path back, not just the feeling.
ramacharitamanas::3524.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram after rejecting the throne. He does not ask for power or comfort. He begs for one instruction only: how to live these years in a way that keeps him facing Ram again.
ramacharitamanas::3524.modern_relevance: You are moving cities, changing jobs, or living far from someone you love, and you keep asking: what keeps this bond alive? Bharat knows the answer is not possession, but faithful direction.
ramacharitamanas::3524.insight: It shifts devotion from emotion alone into a concrete way of living that keeps return possible.

ramacharitamanas::3525.verse_sanskrit: पुरजन परिजन प्रजा गोसाईं। सब सुचि सरस सनेहँ सगाईं॥ राउर बदि भल भव दुख दाहू। प्रभु बिनु बादि परम पद लाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3525.verse_hindi: हे गोसाईं! आपके प्रेम और संबंध में अवधपुर वासी, कुटुम्बी और प्रजा सभी पवित्र और रस (आनंद) से युक्त हैं। आपके लिए भवदुःख (जन्म-मरण के दुःख) की ज्वाला में जलना भी अच्छा है और प्रभु (आप) के बिना परमपद (मोक्ष) का लाभ भी व्यर्थ है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3525.english_translation: O Lord, the people of Ayodhya, our family, and the subjects are all pure and filled with sweet affection because of your love. For you, even burning in the fire of worldly suffering is good, and without you, even the highest freedom is meaningless.
ramacharitamanas::3525.translation_literal: पुरजन (townspeople) / परिजन (family) / प्रजा (subjects) / गोसाईं (Lord) / सब (all) / सुचि (pure) / सरस (full of relish) / सनेहँ (with affection) / सगाईं (companionship) / राउर (your) / बदि (for) / भल (good) / भव (worldly existence) / दुख (suffering) / दाहू (burning) / प्रभु (Lord) / बिनु (without) / बादि (wasted) / परम (highest) / पद (state) / लाहू (gain)
ramacharitamanas::3525.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3525.essence: Ram’s presence makes suffering bearable and freedom incomplete without him.
ramacharitamanas::3525.simple_meaning: Bharat says Ayodhya’s people, family, and subjects are made pure and joyful by Ram’s presence. Even suffering in the world feels worthwhile for him, while freedom without Ram feels pointless.
ramacharitamanas::3525.simple_insight: Love can make hardship bearable and success feel hollow when the beloved is missing.
ramacharitamanas::3525.detailed_meaning: Bharat is pleading in Ayodhya after Ram’s exile has torn the kingdom apart. He tells Ram that everyone around him has been transformed by his presence, and that life’s highest reward means nothing without him.
ramacharitamanas::3525.modern_relevance: You leave a family gathering and realize one person made the whole room feel alive. The food, the laughter, even the comfort of being there — none of it feels complete without them.
ramacharitamanas::3525.insight: It shifts value from external success to the presence that makes life meaningful.

ramacharitamanas::3526.verse_sanskrit: स्वामि सुजानु जानि सब ही की। रुचि लालसा रहनि जन जी की॥ प्रनतपालु पालिहि सब काहू। देउ दुहू दिसि ओर निबाहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3526.verse_hindi: हे स्वामी! आप सुजान हैं, सभी के हृदय की और मुझ सेवक के मन की रुचि, लालसा (अभिलाषा) और रहनी जानकर, हे प्रणतपाल! आप सब किसी का पालन करेंगे और हे देव! दोनों ओर अन्त तक निबाहेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3526.english_translation: O wise Lord, you know everyone’s heart. You know the desires and longings that live in each person’s mind. Protector of the surrendered, you will care for everyone and keep faith with both sides until the end.
ramacharitamanas::3526.translation_literal: स्वामि (lord) / सुजानु (all-knowing) / जानि (knowing) / सब ही की (of everyone) / रुचि (inclination) / लालसा (longing) / रहनि (way of living) / जन (people) / जी की (of the heart) ॥ / प्रनतपालु (protector of the surrendered) / पालिहि (will protect) / सब काहू (everyone) / देउ (O divine one) / दुहू दिसि (both sides) / ओर (end) / निबाहू (will keep faith) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3526.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3526.essence: Real protection begins when nothing in your heart is hidden.
ramacharitamanas::3526.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as one who knows every heart and will protect everyone, keeping his promise to all sides.
ramacharitamanas::3526.simple_insight: It feels safe to rest with someone who sees your heart and never drops their promise.
ramacharitamanas::3526.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat pleads from a heart split by exile, grief, and loyalty. He addresses Ram as the wise protector who already knows every person’s inner longing and will not fail anyone, even when duty pulls in different directions.
ramacharitamanas::3526.modern_relevance: You’re trying to explain yourself to someone who already understands your patterns better than you do. The deepest relief is being held by someone who knows your heart and still stays faithful.
ramacharitamanas::3526.insight: It shifts trust from self-protection to resting in a presence that sees through you and still protects you.

ramacharitamanas::3527.verse_sanskrit: अस मोहि सब बिधि भूरि भरोसो। किएँ बिचारु न सोचु खरो सो॥ आरति मोर नाथ कर छोहू। दुहुँ मिलि कीन्ह ढीठु हठि मोहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3527.verse_hindi: मुझे सब प्रकार से ऐसा बहुत बड़ा भरोसा है। विचार करने पर तिनके के बराबर (जरा सा) भी सोच नहीं रह जाता! मेरी दीनता और स्वामी का स्नेह दोनों ने मिलकर मुझे जबर्दस्ती ढीठ बना दिया है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3527.english_translation: I have such complete trust in every way. After reflection, not even the slightest worry remains. My helplessness and my lord's affection have together made me stubbornly bold.
ramacharitamanas::3527.translation_literal: अस (such) / मोहि (to me) / सब बिधि (in every way) / भूरि (great) / भरोसो (trust) / किएँ (having made) / बिचारु (reflection) / न (not) / सोचु (worry) / खरो सो (even a little) / आरति (helplessness) / मोर (my) / नाथ (lord) / कर (of hand) / छोहू (affection) / दुहुँ (both) / मिलि (together) / कीन्ह (made) / ढीठु (bold/stubborn) / हठि (insistently) / मोहू (me)
ramacharitamanas::3527.speaker: Bharat
ramacharitamanas::3527.essence: Complete trust ends hesitation and makes humility steady.
ramacharitamanas::3527.simple_meaning: Bharat says he has complete trust, so deep that even careful thought leaves no worry. His helplessness and Ram's affection together have made him boldly stubborn in devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3527.simple_insight: Trust can quiet overthinking and give you the courage to stand firm in love.
ramacharitamanas::3527.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is pleading with humility and devotion, not asking for power but for guidance. He says his heart already trusts Ram completely, and that trust has erased hesitation. His own helplessness and Ram's affection have made him firm.
ramacharitamanas::3527.modern_relevance: You keep rereading the message before sending it, then finally stop because you know the relationship is safe. That steadiness is what Bharat is naming: trust that removes the need to keep checking.
ramacharitamanas::3527.insight: It shifts the mind from second-guessing to settled confidence in the beloved.

ramacharitamanas::3528.verse_sanskrit: यह बड़ दोषु दूरि करि स्वामी। तजि सकोच सिखइअ अनुगामी॥ भरत बिनय सुनि सबहिं प्रसंसी। खीर नीर बिबरन गति हंसी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3528.verse_hindi: हे स्वामी! इस बड़े दोष को दूर करके संकोच त्याग कर मुझ सेवक को शिक्षा दीजिए। दूध और जल को अलग-अलग करने में हंसिनी की सी गति वाली भरतजी की विनती सुनकर उसकी सभी ने प्रशंसा की ॥
ramacharitamanas::3528.english_translation: “My Lord, remove this great fault and, setting aside hesitation, teach me, your servant.” Hearing Bharat's plea, everyone praised him, graceful like a swan separating milk from water.
ramacharitamanas::3528.translation_literal: यह (this) / बड़ (great) / दोषु (fault) / दूरि (removing) / करि (doing) / स्वामी (lord) / तजि (leaving) / सकोच (hesitation) / सिखइअ (teach) / अनुगामी (follower, servant) / भरत (Bharat) / बिनय (humble plea) / सुनि (hearing) / सबहिं (all) / प्रसंसी (praised) / खीर (milk) / नीर (water) / बिबरन (separate) / गति (movement, way) / हंसी (swan)
ramacharitamanas::3528.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3528.essence: Humble honesty makes you fit to receive what pride cannot hear.
ramacharitamanas::3528.simple_meaning: Bharat asks Ram to remove hesitation and teach him openly. Everyone praises the purity and clarity of his humble request.
ramacharitamanas::3528.simple_insight: Real humility is not weakness; it makes room for clear guidance and earns quiet respect.
ramacharitamanas::3528.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram with a plea stripped of pride. He asks Ram to remove his hesitation and teach him plainly. The onlookers praise the rare purity of a heart that can separate what is true from what is mixed.
ramacharitamanas::3528.modern_relevance: You finally admit to a mentor that you are confused and need direct help. The relief comes not from looking capable, but from being honest enough to learn.
ramacharitamanas::3528.insight: It shifts you from self-protection to open receiving, so guidance can actually reach you.

ramacharitamanas::3529.verse_sanskrit: दीनबंधु सुनि बंधु के वचन दीन छलहीन। देस काल अवसर सरिस बोले रामु प्रबीन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3529.verse_hindi: दीनबन्धु और परम चतुर श्री रामजी ने भाई भरतजी के दीन और छलरहित वचन सुनकर देश, काल और अवसर के अनुकूल वचन बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3529.english_translation: Hearing Bharat's humble, deceit-free words, the compassionate and skilled Ram spoke in a way suited to the place, time, and moment.
ramacharitamanas::3529.translation_literal: दीनबंधु (friend of the humble) / सुनि (hearing) / बंधु के वचन (brother's words) / दीन (humble) / छलहीन (without deceit) / देस काल अवसर सरिस (suited to place, time, and occasion) / बोले (spoke) / रामु (Ram) / प्रबीन (skilled, wise)
ramacharitamanas::3529.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3529.essence: True closeness speaks with perfect care.
ramacharitamanas::3529.simple_meaning: Ram hears Bharat's humble, sincere words and answers with perfect tact, matching the moment and the need.
ramacharitamanas::3529.simple_insight: Careful speech can protect love when emotions are raw.
ramacharitamanas::3529.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat kneels before Ram in the forest and speaks with total humility, asking to be corrected. Ram, moved by his brother's sincerity, answers gently and wisely, choosing words that fit the grief, the setting, and the bond between them.
ramacharitamanas::3529.modern_relevance: A tense family conversation after a long silence needs more than honesty. You also need timing, tenderness, and the wisdom to say the right thing without deepening the wound.
ramacharitamanas::3529.insight: It teaches you to answer sincere vulnerability with speech that heals, not speech that wins.

ramacharitamanas::3530.verse_sanskrit: तात तुम्हारि मोरि परिजन की। चिंता गुरहि नृपहि घर बन की॥ माथे पर गुर मुनि मिथिलेसू। हमहि तुम्हहि सपनेहूँ न कलेसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3530.verse_hindi: हे तात! तुम्हारी, मेरी, परिवार की, घर की और वन की सारी चिंता गुरु वशिष्ठजी और महाराज जनकजी को है। हमारे सिर पर जब गुरुजी, मुनि विश्वामित्रजी और मिथिलापति जनकजी हैं, तब हमें और तुम्हें स्वप्न नें भी क्लेश नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3530.english_translation: Father, your worries and mine, the family’s worries, the home’s worries, and the forest’s worries are all on the shoulders of Guru Vashistha and King Janaka. With Guru, sage Vishvamitra, and Janaka above us, neither you nor I have any trouble, even in dreams.
ramacharitamanas::3530.translation_literal: तात (father) / तुम्हारि (your) / मोरि (my) / परिजन (family) / की (of) / चिंता (worry) / गुरहि (to the guru) / नृपहि (to the king) / घर (home) / बन (forest) / की (of) / माथे (on the head) / पर (upon) / गुर (guru) / मुनि (sage) / मिथिलेसू (the lord of Mithila) / हमहि (us) / तुम्हहि (you) / सपनेहूँ (even in a dream) / न (not) / कलेसू (trouble)
ramacharitamanas::3530.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3530.essence: You can release worry when wise hands already hold the burden.
ramacharitamanas::3530.simple_meaning: Ram reassures Bharat that the burden of managing home, forest, and family rests with trusted elders, so neither brother needs to worry.
ramacharitamanas::3530.simple_insight: Peace comes when you stop carrying responsibilities that belong to wiser hands.
ramacharitamanas::3530.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat kneels before Ram with grief and humility. Ram answers by widening the circle of responsibility: Guru Vashistha, Vishvamitra, and King Janaka are guiding everything. That shared trust makes this moment feel safe.
ramacharitamanas::3530.modern_relevance: You are lying awake after a family crisis, trying to solve every detail by morning. This verse reminds you that care can be shared, and not every burden belongs to your hands.
ramacharitamanas::3530.insight: It shifts you from private panic to shared responsibility, trusting competent elders instead of clutching everything yourself.

ramacharitamanas::3531.verse_sanskrit: मोर तुम्हार परम पुरुषारथु। स्वारथु सुजसु धरमु परमारथु॥ पितु आयसु पालिहिं दुहु भाईं। लोक बेद भल भूप भलाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3531.verse_hindi: मेरा और तुम्हारा तो परम पुरुषार्थ, स्वार्थ, सुयश, धर्म और परमार्थ इसी में है कि हम दोनों भाई पिताजी की आज्ञा का पालन करें। राजा की भलाई (उनके व्रत की रक्षा) से ही लोक और वेद दोनों में भला है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3531.english_translation: My and your highest aim, self-interest, good name, duty, and true good all lie in this: that both brothers obey our father's command. The king's welfare is served when both worldly custom and sacred teaching are upheld.
ramacharitamanas::3531.translation_literal: मोर (my) / तुम्हार (your) / परम (highest) / पुरुषारथु (aim) / स्वारथु (self-interest) / सुजसु (good name) / धरमु (duty) / परमारथु (true good) / पितु (father's) / आयसु (command) / पालिहिं (should obey) / दुहु (both) / भाईं (brothers) / लोक (worldly custom) / बेद (sacred teaching) / भल (good) / भूप (king's) / भलाईं (welfare)
ramacharitamanas::3531.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3531.essence: Keeping your father's word is the highest good for both brothers.
ramacharitamanas::3531.simple_meaning: Keeping their father's command is the highest good for both brothers. It is not just obedience; it is their duty, their honor, and what brings real benefit.
ramacharitamanas::3531.simple_insight: Sometimes the noblest choice is not what you want, but what you must uphold.
ramacharitamanas::3531.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram is answering Bharat's plea after exile has torn the family apart. Bharat wants Ram home; Ram insists that their father's command must stand. He turns obedience into the highest form of welfare.
ramacharitamanas::3531.modern_relevance: You are tempted to bend a promise because it would make life easier right now. But the deeper relief comes from keeping what you said, even when it costs you comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3531.insight: It shifts you from chasing convenience to honoring the obligation that preserves your integrity.

ramacharitamanas::3532.verse_sanskrit: गुर पितु मातु स्वामि सिख पालें। चलेहुँ कुमग पग परहिं न खालें॥ अस बिचारि सब सोच बिहाई। पालहु अवध अवधि भरि जाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3532.verse_hindi: गुरु, पिता, माता और स्वामी की शिक्षा (आज्ञा) का पालन करने से कुमार्ग पर भी चलने पर पैर गड्ढे में नहीं पड़ता (पतन नहीं होता)। ऐसा विचार कर सब सोच छोड़कर अवध जाकर अवधिभर उसका पालन करो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3532.english_translation: By following the guidance of your teacher, father, mother, and master, even a wrong road will not make you fall. Thinking this through, let go of sorrow and go to Ayodhya; keep that vow until the end.
ramacharitamanas::3532.translation_literal: गुर (teacher) / पितु (father) / मातु (mother) / स्वामि (master) / सिख (instruction) / पालें (by following) / चलेहुँ (even if you walk) / कुमग (wrong road) / पग (feet) / परहिं (fall) / न (not) / खालें (into pits) // अस (thus) / बिचारि (thinking) / सब (all) / सोच (sorrow) / बिहाई (leaving) / पालहु (keep) / अवध (Ayodhya) / अवधि (the full term) / भरि (for) / जाई (go)
ramacharitamanas::3532.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3532.essence: Right guidance can keep you steady even on a wrong road.
ramacharitamanas::3532.simple_meaning: Following the guidance of your teacher, parents, and master protects you from losing your way. Keep that instruction in mind and carry it through without worry.
ramacharitamanas::3532.simple_insight: There is safety in loyal obedience; you do not have to navigate every road alone.
ramacharitamanas::3532.detailed_meaning: Ram is urging Bharat to honour the guidance of elders and authority figures, even if the path looks difficult. In the exile crisis, this becomes a practical test of character: stay steady, drop grief, and keep the promise through the full term.
ramacharitamanas::3532.modern_relevance: Your phone is buzzing, three people are giving you conflicting advice, and you feel pulled in every direction. This verse says steady yourself by remembering the guidance that deserves your trust.
ramacharitamanas::3532.insight: It shifts action from anxious self-direction to disciplined trust in rightful guidance.

ramacharitamanas::3533.verse_sanskrit: देसु कोसु परिजन परिवारू। गुर पद रजहिं लाग छरुभारू॥ तुम्ह मुनि मातु सचिव सिख मानी। पालेहु पुहुमि प्रजा रजधानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3533.verse_hindi: देश, खजाना, कुटुम्ब, परिवार आदि सबकी जिम्मेदारी तो गुरुजी की चरण रज पर है। तुम तो मुनि वशिष्ठजी, माताओं और मन्त्रियों की शिक्षा मानकर तदनुसार पृथ्वी, प्रजा और राजधानी का पालन (रक्षा) भर करते रहना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3533.english_translation: The burden of land, treasury, kin, family, and kingdom rests on the teacher’s feet. You, having followed the counsel of the sages, mothers, and ministers, should simply protect the earth, the people, and the capital.
ramacharitamanas::3533.translation_literal: देसु (land) / कोसु (treasury) / परिजन (kinsmen) / परिवारू (family) / गुर पद (teacher’s feet) / रजहिं (royal dust) / लाग (attached) / छरुभारू (light burden) / तुम्ह (you) / मुनि (sages) / मातु (mothers) / सचिव (ministers) / सिख (counsel) / मानी (having accepted) / पालेहु (protect) / पुहुमि (earth) / प्रजा (people) / रजधानी (capital)
ramacharitamanas::3533.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3533.essence: True rule is light when it serves guidance, not ego.
ramacharitamanas::3533.simple_meaning: Rule the land, people, and capital, but do it by following wise guidance and staying humble. Real authority is light when it listens.
ramacharitamanas::3533.simple_insight: Leadership becomes cleaner when you stop carrying it alone and let wisdom guide your hands.
ramacharitamanas::3533.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram is preparing for exile while still speaking like the rightful ruler. He tells Bharat that the kingdom, treasury, family, and people are not a personal possession. They must be governed through the guidance of teachers, sages, mothers, and ministers.
ramacharitamanas::3533.modern_relevance: You’re handed a team, a household, or a project, and suddenly every problem feels like it has your name on it. This verse says leadership is not solitary pride; it is stewardship shaped by counsel.
ramacharitamanas::3533.insight: It shifts responsibility from personal control to humble governance guided by trusted wisdom.

ramacharitamanas::3534.verse_sanskrit: मुखिआ मुखु सो चाहिऐ खान पान कहुँ एक। पालइ पोषइ सकल अँग तुलसी सहित बिबेक ॥
ramacharitamanas::3534.verse_hindi: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) मुखिया मुख के समान होना चाहिए, जो खाने-पीने को तो एक (अकेला) है, परन्तु विवेकपूर्वक सब अंगों का पालन-पोषण करता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3534.english_translation: A leader should be like the mouth: taking for itself only food and drink, yet wisely nourishing all the limbs.
ramacharitamanas::3534.translation_literal: मुखिआ (leader) / मुखु (mouth) / सो (that) / चाहिऐ (should be) / खान (eating) / पान (drinking) / कहुँ (for) / एक (one) / पालइ (nourishes) / पोषइ (supports) / सकल (all) / अँग (limbs) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / सहित (with) / बिबेक (discernment)
ramacharitamanas::3534.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3534.essence: A leader stays small in need and large in care.
ramacharitamanas::3534.simple_meaning: A true leader takes only what is needed and uses discernment to support everyone else.
ramacharitamanas::3534.simple_insight: Leadership feels lighter when it becomes service instead of self-advancement.
ramacharitamanas::3534.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram is teaching Bharat how a kingdom should be held together after the exile. The ruler should be like the mouth: modest in its own needs, but constantly sustaining the whole body with wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::3534.modern_relevance: You’re the manager who grabs the last credit while your team carries the load. Or the parent who keeps the house running by quietly giving more than taking. Real authority nourishes others first.
ramacharitamanas::3534.insight: It shifts leadership from self-interest to wise care for the whole.

ramacharitamanas::3535.verse_sanskrit: राजधरम सरबसु एतनोई। जिमि मन माहँ मनोरथ गोई॥ बंधु प्रबोधु कीन्ह बहु भाँती। बिनु अधार मन तोषु न साँती ॥
ramacharitamanas::3535.verse_hindi: राजधर्म का सर्वस्व (सार) भी इतना ही है। जैसे मन के भीतर मनोरथ छिपा रहता है। श्री रघुनाथजी ने भाई भरत को बहुत प्रकार से समझाया, परन्तु कोई अवलम्बन पाए बिना उनके मन में न संतोष हुआ, न शान्ति ॥
ramacharitamanas::3535.english_translation: The whole of righteous rule is this much: like a desire hidden in the mind. Brother Ram explained in many ways, but without a support, Bharat's mind found neither contentment nor peace.
ramacharitamanas::3535.translation_literal: राजधरम (righteous rule) / सरबसु (the whole) / एतनोई (just this much) / जिमि (like) / मन (mind) / माहँ (within) / मनोरथ (desire) / गोई (hidden)॥ / बंधु (brother) / प्रबोधु (instruction) / कीन्ह (did) / बहु भाँती (in many ways) / बिनु (without) / अधार (support) / मन (mind) / तोषु (contentment) / न (not) / साँती (peace)॥
ramacharitamanas::3535.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3535.essence: Peace comes only when the mind finds something firm to stand on.
ramacharitamanas::3535.simple_meaning: Even wise advice cannot bring peace if the mind has nothing solid to hold onto. Bharat is still unsettled because he lacks the support he needs.
ramacharitamanas::3535.simple_insight: Sometimes understanding is not enough; the heart needs an anchor before it can rest.
ramacharitamanas::3535.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram keeps trying to steady Bharat after the shock of exile. He explains duty in many ways, but Bharat's mind still cannot settle. The verse shows that words alone cannot heal a heart that has lost its footing.
ramacharitamanas::3535.modern_relevance: You can read ten messages, get three apologies, and still feel shaky at 1 a.m. What you need is not more explanation, but something steady to hold.
ramacharitamanas::3535.insight: It shifts you from chasing better explanations to finding the support that lets the mind settle.

ramacharitamanas::3536.verse_sanskrit: भरत सील गुर सचिव समाजू। सकुच सनेह बिबस रघुराजू॥ प्रभु करि कृपा पाँवरीं दीन्हीं। सादर भरत सीस धरि लीन्हीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3536.verse_hindi: इधर तो भरतजी का शील (प्रेम) और उधर गुरुजनों, मंत्रियों तथा समाज की उपस्थिति! यह देखकर श्री रघुनाथजी संकोच तथा स्नेह के विशेष वशीभूत हो गए (अर्थात भरतजी के प्रेमवश उन्हें पाँवरी देना चाहते हैं, किन्तु साथ ही गुरु आदि का संकोच भी होता है।) आखिर (भरतजी के प्रेमवश) प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी ने कृपा कर खड़ाऊँ दे दीं और भरतजी ने उन्हें आदरपूर्वक सिर पर धारण कर लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3536.english_translation: Seeing Bharat's noble conduct and the gathered teachers, ministers, and people, Raghunath was overcome by both shyness and love. In compassion, the Lord gave him the sandals, and Bharat placed them respectfully on his head.
ramacharitamanas::3536.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / सील (noble conduct) / गुर (teachers) / सचिव (ministers) / समाजू (assembly) / सकुच (shyness) / सनेह (love) / बिबस (overcome) / रघुराजू (Raghuraj)॥ / प्रभु (Lord) / करि (doing) / कृपा (compassion) / पाँवरीं (sandals) / दीन्हीं (gave) / सादर (respectfully) / भरत (Bharat) / सीस (head) / धरि (placing) / लीन्हीं (took) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3536.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3536.essence: True devotion turns even sandals into something sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3536.simple_meaning: Bharat's love, and the presence of elders and ministers, makes Ram both shy and tender. He gives Bharat his sandals, and Bharat accepts them with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3536.simple_insight: Love can be so pure that even a simple object becomes sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3536.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands before Ram with teachers, ministers, and the whole assembly watching. Ram is moved by Bharat's devotion and gives him his sandals. Bharat lifts them to his head, turning a family moment into an act of surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3536.modern_relevance: You hand back the keys to a home you can no longer keep, and your hands shake a little. What matters most is not possession, but the love with which you release it.
ramacharitamanas::3536.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone into a visible act of reverence and surrender.

ramacharitamanas::3537.verse_sanskrit: चरनपीठ करुनानिधान के। जनु जुग जामिक प्रजा प्रान के॥ संपुट भरत सनेह रतन के। आखर जुग जनु जीव जतन के ॥
ramacharitamanas::3537.verse_hindi: करुणानिधान श्री रामचंद्रजी के दोनों ख़ड़ाऊँ प्रजा के प्राणों की रक्षा के लिए मानो दो पहरेदार हैं। भरतजी के प्रेमरूपी रत्न के लिए मानो डिब्बा है और जीव के साधन के लिए मानो राम-नाम के दो अक्षर हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3537.english_translation: The pair of wooden sandals of the compassionate Lord are like two guardians for the lives of the people, like a casket for Bharat's jewel of love, and like two letters for the soul's practice.
ramacharitamanas::3537.translation_literal: चरनपीठ (pair of sandals) / करुनानिधान (storehouse of compassion) / के (of) / जनु (as if) / जुग (two) / जामिक (guards) / प्रजा (people) / प्रान (life-breath) / के (of)॥ संपुट (casket) / भरत (Bharat) / सनेह (love) / रतन (jewel) / के (of) / आखर (letters) / जुग (two) / जनु (as if) / जीव (living being) / जतन (practice/effort) / के (of)॥
ramacharitamanas::3537.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3537.essence: What is touched by Ram becomes shelter, treasure, and practice.
ramacharitamanas::3537.simple_meaning: Ram's sandals are described as protectors of the people, a container for Bharat's love, and a symbol of the two-letter name that supports spiritual practice.
ramacharitamanas::3537.simple_insight: Even what belongs to Ram becomes a refuge when love is real.
ramacharitamanas::3537.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat is living by Ram's sandals while Ram remains in exile. Tulsidas pauses on those sandals and turns them into a sacred image: they protect the people, preserve Bharat's devotion, and stand for the living power of Ram's name.
ramacharitamanas::3537.modern_relevance: You keep a photo, a voice note, or a worn-out letter from someone you love. It seems small, but it holds your whole devotion. Bharat's sandals carry that same weight.
ramacharitamanas::3537.insight: It shifts attention from the object itself to the love and refuge the object carries.

ramacharitamanas::3538.verse_sanskrit: कुल कपाट कर कुसल करम के। बिमल नयन सेवा सुधरम के॥ भरत मुदित अवलंब लहे तें। अस सुख जस सिय रामु रहे तें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3538.verse_hindi: रघुकुल (की रक्षा) के लिए दो किवाड़ हैं। कुशल (श्रेष्ठ) कर्म करने के लिए दो हाथ की भाँति (सहायक) हैं और सेवा रूपी श्रेष्ठ धर्म के सुझाने के लिए निर्मल नेत्र हैं। भरतजी इस अवलंब के मिल जाने से परम आनंदित हैं। उन्हें ऐसा ही सुख हुआ, जैसा श्री सीता-रामजी के रहने से होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3538.english_translation: The Raghu line has two doors for protection, two hands for good action, and two clear eyes for the noble duty of service. Bharat is overjoyed to have such support, feeling a joy like the presence of Sita and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3538.translation_literal: कुल (family line) / कपाट (doors) / कर (hands) / कुसल (good) / करम (actions) / के (for) / बिमल (clear, pure) / नयन (eyes) / सेवा (service) / सुधरम (noble duty) / के (for) / भरत (Bharat) / मुदित (delighted) / अवलंब (support) / लहे (received) / तें (from) / अस (such) / सुख (joy) / जस (like) / सिय (Sita) / रामु (Ram) / रहे (being) / तें (from)
ramacharitamanas::3538.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3538.essence: True support turns service into joy.
ramacharitamanas::3538.simple_meaning: Service, right action, and clear sight protect the family line. Bharat feels deep joy in having this support, like the joy of being with Sita and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3538.simple_insight: Real support feels like a blessing because it lets you serve well without strain.
ramacharitamanas::3538.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat stands in Ram's presence and receives the sandals that will represent Ram's rule. The poet compares that support to doors, hands, and eyes: protection, action, and service all working together. Bharat's joy rises from seeing duty made visible.
ramacharitamanas::3538.modern_relevance: You finally have a teammate who sees the whole picture, handles the practical work, and protects what matters. That kind of support feels almost sacred because it makes service possible.
ramacharitamanas::3538.insight: It reframes support as the condition that lets duty, service, and right action actually happen.

ramacharitamanas::3539.verse_sanskrit: मागेउ बिदा प्रनामु करि राम लिए उर लाइ। लोग उचाटे अमरपति कुटिल कुअवसरु पाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3539.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने प्रणाम करके विदा माँगी, तब श्री रामचंद्रजी ने उन्हें हृदय से लगा लिया। इधर कुटिल इंद्र ने बुरा मौका पाकर लोगों का उच्चाटन कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3539.english_translation: Bharat bowed and asked to depart; Ram embraced him to his heart. Then, finding a bad opening, the crooked lord of the gods stirred everyone into unease.
ramacharitamanas::3539.translation_literal: मागेउ (asked for) / बिदा (leave, departure) / प्रनामु करि (having bowed) / राम (Ram) / लिए (took) / उर लाइ (embracing to the heart) / लोग (people) / उचाटे (made restless, uneasy) / अमरपति (lord of the immortals) / कुटिल (crooked, sly) / कुअवसरु (bad opportunity) / पाइ (having found)
ramacharitamanas::3539.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3539.essence: Love gives comfort, but unrest can still slip in through a weak moment.
ramacharitamanas::3539.simple_meaning: Bharat asks Ram for permission to leave, and Ram embraces him lovingly. At that moment, a harmful force takes advantage and unsettles the people.
ramacharitamanas::3539.simple_insight: Even a tender farewell can be shadowed by forces that disturb the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3539.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat has come to meet Ram after the exile has torn the family apart. He bows, asks leave, and Ram holds him close. The verse then shifts to the unrest spreading among the people, showing how fragile peace is in this charged moment.
ramacharitamanas::3539.modern_relevance: You finally say goodbye after a painful family visit, and the room feels lighter for a second. Then one sharp comment, one bad mood, and everyone is unsettled again.
ramacharitamanas::3539.insight: It shows how quickly harmony can be disturbed when a vulnerable moment meets outside interference.

ramacharitamanas::3540.verse_sanskrit: सो कुचालि सब कहँ भइ नीकी। अवधि आस सम जीवनि जी की॥ नतरु लखन सिय राम बियोगा। हहरि मरत सब लोग कुरोगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3540.verse_hindi: वह कुचाल भी सबके लिए हितकर हो गई। अवधि की आशा के समान ही वह जीवन के लिए संजीवनी हो गई। नहीं तो (उच्चाटन न होता तो) लक्ष्मणजी, सीताजी और श्री रामचंद्रजी के वियोग रूपी बुरे रोग से सब लोग घबड़ाकर (हाय-हाय करके) मर ही जाते ॥
ramacharitamanas::3540.english_translation: That bad turn became good for everyone. Like the hope of a deadline, it became the medicine that kept life going. Otherwise, the pain of separation from Lakshman, Sita, and Ram would have made everyone cry out and die in grief.
ramacharitamanas::3540.translation_literal: सो (that) / कुचालि (bad turn, ill-planned move) / सब कहँ (for everyone) / भइ (became) / नीकी (good) / अवधि (deadline, limit, appointed time) / आस (hope) / सम (like) / जीवनि (life-giving medicine) / जी की (for the heart/life)॥ / नतरु (otherwise) / लखन (Lakshman) / सिय (Sita) / राम (Ram) / बियोगा (separation) / हहरि (crying out in distress) / मरत (dying) / सब लोग (all people) / कुरोगा (from the bad illness)
ramacharitamanas::3540.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3540.essence: A bad delay can become the medicine that prevents a deeper collapse.
ramacharitamanas::3540.simple_meaning: A seemingly bad event turned out to help everyone. It stopped the pain of separation from Lakshman, Sita, and Ram from overwhelming the people.
ramacharitamanas::3540.simple_insight: Sometimes a painful interruption saves you from a deeper collapse.
ramacharitamanas::3540.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat’s return and Ram’s meeting are so overwhelming that even the divine beings’ interference is described as a troubling move that unexpectedly helps. The verse says that delay became a healing pause; without it, the people would have broken under the grief of separation.
ramacharitamanas::3540.modern_relevance: A meeting gets delayed after a family argument, and the extra hour keeps everyone from saying something unforgivable. What felt like a setback quietly prevents a worse wound.
ramacharitamanas::3540.insight: It shifts you to see delay as possible protection, not always obstruction.

ramacharitamanas::3541.verse_sanskrit: रामकृपाँ अवरेब सुधारी। बिबुध धारि भइ गुनद गोहारी॥ भेंटत भुज भरि भाइ भरत सो। राम प्रेम रसु न कहि न परत सो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3541.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी की कृपा ने सारी उलझन सुधार दी। देवताओं की सेना जो लूटने आई थी, वही गुणदायक (हितकरी) और रक्षक बन गई। श्री रामजी भुजाओं में भरकर भाई भरत से मिल रहे हैं। श्री रामजी के प्रेम का वह रस (आनंद) कहते नहीं बनता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3541.english_translation: By Ram's grace, everything was set right. The host of radiant beings, who had come to seize, became helpful and protective. Ram embraced his brother Bharat in his arms, and the sweetness of Ram's love cannot be spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3541.translation_literal: रामकृपाँ (by Ram's grace) / अवरेब (everything) / सुधारी (was set right) / बिबुध (radiant beings) / धारि (having taken) / भइ (became) / गुनद (beneficial) / गोहारी (protective) / भेंटत (meeting) / भुज भरि (filling the arms) / भाइ (brother) / भरत सो (with Bharat) / राम (Ram) / प्रेम (love) / रसु (essence/sweetness) / न कहि (cannot be spoken) / न परत (cannot be described) / सो (that)
ramacharitamanas::3541.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3541.essence: Ram's grace can turn even threat into shelter.
ramacharitamanas::3541.simple_meaning: Ram's grace turns even trouble into help. He welcomes Bharat with a full embrace, and the joy of that love is beyond words.
ramacharitamanas::3541.simple_insight: Love can dissolve conflict so completely that even danger feels transformed.
ramacharitamanas::3541.detailed_meaning: Bharat has come to meet Ram after a painful family rupture. In that charged reunion, Ram's grace settles everything, even the hostile forces around them. The verse lingers on the embrace and on love so deep that language fails.
ramacharitamanas::3541.modern_relevance: You walk into a room after a family fight, expecting tension, and instead someone opens their arms. In that moment, the whole mood changes before a single explanation is given.
ramacharitamanas::3541.insight: It shifts attention from the conflict itself to the healing power of wholehearted welcome.

ramacharitamanas::3542.verse_sanskrit: तन मन बचन उमग अनुरागा। धीर धुरंधर धीरजु त्यागा॥ बारिज लोचन मोचत बारी। देखि दसा सुर सभा दुखारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3542.verse_hindi: तन, मन और वचन तीनों में प्रेम उमड़ पड़ा। धीरज की धुरी को धारण करने वाले श्री रघुनाथजी ने भी धीरज त्याग दिया। वे कमल सदृश नेत्रों से (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल बहाने लगे। उनकी यह दशा देखकर देवताओं की सभा (समाज) दुःखी हो गई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3542.english_translation: Love surged through body, mind, and speech. Even the steadfast Lord of Raghu let go of composure. He began shedding tears from lotus-like eyes. Seeing this state, the assembly of the devas became sorrowful.
ramacharitamanas::3542.translation_literal: तन (body) / मन (mind) / बचन (speech) / उमग (overflowed) / अनुरागा (love) / धीर (steadfast) / धुरंधर (bearer of steadiness) / धीरजु (composure) / त्यागा (let go) / बारिज (lotus) / लोचन (eyes) / मोचत (releasing) / बारी (water/tears) / देखि (seeing) / दसा (state) / सुर (devas) / सभा (assembly) / दुखारी (sorrowful)
ramacharitamanas::3542.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3542.essence: True steadiness can still dissolve in love.
ramacharitamanas::3542.simple_meaning: Ram's love becomes so intense that even his usual calm breaks, and tears flow from his eyes. The devas are moved to sorrow by seeing it.
ramacharitamanas::3542.simple_insight: Love is not always quiet; sometimes it is so full that it spills over.
ramacharitamanas::3542.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharata and Ram meet after long separation. The reunion is so charged that Ram, usually the model of composure, is overwhelmed. His tears show how deep love can be, and even the heavenly assembly feels the pain of separation and reunion.
ramacharitamanas::3542.modern_relevance: You finally see someone you have missed for years, and the careful mask drops in an instant. The body knows what the mind has tried to hold back.
ramacharitamanas::3542.insight: It reframes tears as an honest sign of love, not a failure of strength.

ramacharitamanas::3543.verse_sanskrit: मुनिगन गुर धुर धीर जनक से। ग्यान अनल मन कसें कनक से॥ जे बिरंचि निरलेप उपाए। पदुम पत्र जिमि जग जल जाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3543.verse_hindi: मुनिगण, गुरु वशिष्ठजी और जनकजी सरीखे धीरधुरन्धर जो अपने मनों को ज्ञान रूपी अग्नि में सोने के समान कस चुके थे, जिनको ब्रह्माजी ने निर्लेप ही रचा और जो जगत् रूपी जल में कमल के पत्ते की तरह ही (जगत् में रहते हुए भी जगत् से अनासक्त) पैदा हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3543.english_translation: The sages, the teacher, and King Janak were steady like that. They had tempered their minds in the fire of wisdom, like gold. Brahma created them untouched, like a lotus leaf in water, living in the world yet unstained.
ramacharitamanas::3543.translation_literal: मुनिगन (sages) / गुर (teacher) / धुर (steady) / धीर (steadfast) / जनक से (like Janak) / ग्यान (wisdom) / अनल (fire) / मन (mind) / कसें (tempered) / कनक से (like gold) / जे (who) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / निरलेप (untouched) / उपाए (created) / पदुम पत्र (lotus leaf) / जिमि (like) / जग (world) / जल जाए (water)
ramacharitamanas::3543.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3543.essence: Real freedom is staying untouched while fully present.
ramacharitamanas::3543.simple_meaning: Great sages and Janak stayed steady, purified by wisdom, and untouched by the world, like a lotus leaf in water.
ramacharitamanas::3543.simple_insight: You can live fully in the world without letting it cling to you.
ramacharitamanas::3543.detailed_meaning: After seeing Ram and Bharat's extraordinary love, the gathering turns inward. Tulsidas points to sages, Guru Vashishtha, and Janak as examples of minds refined by wisdom and untouched by worldly contact, which prepares the mood for the next verse on detachment.
ramacharitamanas::3543.modern_relevance: You leave a tense family dinner, phone buzzing with old arguments, and still choose not to carry the bitterness home. That is the kind of inner freedom this verse praises.
ramacharitamanas::3543.insight: It shifts attention from worldly involvement to inner non-attachment.

ramacharitamanas::3544.verse_sanskrit: तेउ बिलोकि रघुबर भरत प्रीति अनूप अपार। भए मगन मन तन बचन सहित बिराग बिचार ॥
ramacharitamanas::3544.verse_hindi: वे भी श्री रामजी और भरतजी के उपमारहित अपार प्रेम को देखकर वैराग्य और विवेक सहित तन, मन, वचन से उस प्रेम में मग्न हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3544.english_translation: Seeing the incomparable, boundless love between Raghubar and Bharat, they too became absorbed in it with body, mind, and speech, along with detachment and discernment.
ramacharitamanas::3544.translation_literal: तेउ (they too) / बिलोकि (seeing) / रघुबर (Raghubar, Ram) / भरत (Bharat) / प्रीति (love) / अनूप (matchless) / अपार (boundless) / भए (became) / मगन (absorbed) / मन (mind) / तन (body) / बचन (speech) / सहित (along with) / बिराग (detachment) / बिचार (discernment)
ramacharitamanas::3544.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3544.essence: Love at its purest carries both surrender and clear seeing.
ramacharitamanas::3544.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram and Bharat's unmatched love, even the wise were moved into a state of loving absorption, while still keeping detachment and clear judgment.
ramacharitamanas::3544.simple_insight: Real love does not cloud the mind; it can sharpen it.
ramacharitamanas::3544.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the court and sages witness Ram and Bharat's extraordinary bond after the exile crisis. Their love is not ordinary emotion; it is so pure that it draws even the detached into reverent absorption.
ramacharitamanas::3544.modern_relevance: You watch two siblings protect each other through a family crisis, and something in you softens. Their loyalty doesn't make them naive; it makes them clearer about what matters.
ramacharitamanas::3544.insight: It shows that devotion and discernment can coexist, and that genuine love can awaken both feeling and clarity.

ramacharitamanas::3545.verse_sanskrit: जहाँ जनक गुरु गति मति भोरी। प्राकृत प्रीति कहत बड़ि खोरी॥ बरनत रघुबर भरत बियोगू। सुनि कठोर कबि जानिहि लोगू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3545.verse_hindi: जहाँ जनकजी और गुरु वशिष्ठजी की बुद्धि की गति कुण्ठित हो, उस दिव्य प्रेम को प्राकृत (लौकिक) कहने में बड़ा दोष है। श्री रामचंद्रजी और भरतजी के वियोग का वर्णन करते सुनकर लोग कवि को कठोर हृदय समझेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3545.english_translation: Where even Janak and the teacher's wisdom falters, calling that love ordinary is a grave mistake. If I describe the separation of Ram and Bharat, people will think the poet is hard-hearted.
ramacharitamanas::3545.translation_literal: जहाँ (where) / जनक (Janak) / गुरु (teacher) / गति (movement) / मति (mind) / भोरी (faltering) / प्राकृत (ordinary) / प्रीति (love) / कहत (calling) / बड़ि (great) / खोरी (fault)॥ / बरनत (describing) / रघुबर (Ram) / भरत (Bharat) / बियोगू (separation) / सुनि (hearing) / कठोर (hard) / कबि (poet) / जानिहि (will know) / लोगू (people) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3545.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3545.essence: True devotion makes ordinary language feel too small.
ramacharitamanas::3545.simple_meaning: The bond between Ram and Bharat is so extraordinary that calling it ordinary would be wrong. Even describing their separation feels impossible and risks sounding heartless.
ramacharitamanas::3545.simple_insight: Some love is too sacred to reduce. The heart knows more than plain language can hold.
ramacharitamanas::3545.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas pauses while describing the unbearable separation between Ram and Bharat. He says that even Janak and the teacher Vashishtha would find their minds faltering before such love, and that any plain description would fail the depth of it.
ramacharitamanas::3545.modern_relevance: You try to explain why you still care about someone who hurt you, and every sentence sounds too small. Some bonds are real precisely because they resist neat explanation.
ramacharitamanas::3545.insight: It teaches you to respect what cannot be flattened into simple labels and to let deep feeling remain deep.

ramacharitamanas::3546.verse_sanskrit: सो सकोच रसु अकथ सुबानी। समउ सनेहु सुमिरि सकुचानी॥ भेंटि भरतु रघुबर समुझाए। पुनि रिपुदवनु हरषि हियँ लाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3546.verse_hindi: वह संकोच रस अकथनीय है। अतएव कवि की सुंदर वाणी उस समय उसके प्रेम को स्मरण करके सकुचा गई। भरतजी को भेंट कर श्री रघुनाथजी ने उनको समझाया। फिर हर्षित होकर शत्रुघ्नजी को हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3546.english_translation: That shy, indescribable nectar of love made even the poet's beautiful words falter. Ram embraced Bharat and consoled him, then joyfully drew Shatrughna into his heart.
ramacharitamanas::3546.translation_literal: सो (that) / सकोच (shyness, restraint) / रसु (essence, nectar) / अकथ (unspeakable) / सुबानी (beautiful speech) / समउ (time, occasion) / सनेहु (love) / सुमिरि (remembering) / सकुचानी (became shy, faltered) / भेंटि (meeting, embracing) / भरतु (Bharat) / रघुबर (Ram) / समुझाए (consoled, explained) / पुनि (again) / रिपुदवनु (Shatrughna) / हरषि (rejoicing) / हियँ (to the heart) / लाए (brought, embraced)
ramacharitamanas::3546.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3546.essence: True love can be too deep for speech.
ramacharitamanas::3546.simple_meaning: The love between Ram and Bharat is so deep and restrained that words cannot hold it. Ram comforts Bharat, then lovingly embraces Shatrughna.
ramacharitamanas::3546.simple_insight: Some bonds are too tender for speech; they are understood in a look, a touch, and a held heart.
ramacharitamanas::3546.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, after the painful separation, Ram finally meets Bharat. Even the poet feels words fail before their shy, overflowing love. Ram first consoles Bharat, then turns and embraces Shatrughna, carrying the whole family’s grief in one moment of tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::3546.modern_relevance: You finally see a sibling after a long fight, and neither of you knows how to start. One hug says what careful sentences never could.
ramacharitamanas::3546.insight: It shifts attention from explaining love to embodying it through presence, reassurance, and embrace.

ramacharitamanas::3547.verse_sanskrit: सेवक सचिव भरत रुख पाई। निज निज काज लगे सब जाई॥ सुनि दारुन दुखु दुहूँ समाजा। लगे चलन के साजन साजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3547.verse_hindi: सेवक और मंत्री भरतजी का रुख पाकर सब अपने-अपने काम में जा लगे। यह सुनकर दोनों समाजों में दारुण दुःख छा गया। वे चलने की तैयारियाँ करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3547.english_translation: When Bharata's servants and ministers understood Bharata's decision, each returned to their own duties. Hearing this, deep sorrow spread through both groups, and they began preparing to depart.
ramacharitamanas::3547.translation_literal: सेवक (servants) / सचिव (ministers) / भरत (Bharata) / रुख (decision or intention) / पाई (having understood) / निज निज (each one's own) / काज (work, duty) / लगे (became engaged) / सब (all) / जाई (going) / सुनि (hearing) / दारुन (severe) / दुखु (sorrow) / दुहूँ (of both) / समाजा (assemblies, groups) / लगे (began) / चलन (to depart) / के (of) / साजन (companions) / साजा (preparations)
ramacharitamanas::3547.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3547.essence: Love can end a gathering and still leave everyone moving with duty.
ramacharitamanas::3547.simple_meaning: Bharata's people understand his decision and return to their tasks, but everyone feels the pain of separation and starts preparing to leave.
ramacharitamanas::3547.simple_insight: Even necessary departures can hurt deeply when love is real.
ramacharitamanas::3547.detailed_meaning: After Bharata's meeting with Ram, the people around him understand that the moment of reunion is ending. Servants and ministers resume their duties, but both groups are struck by the sorrow of separation and begin making travel preparations.
ramacharitamanas::3547.modern_relevance: The group chat goes quiet after the decision is made. People start packing, booking rides, and pretending they are fine — but the room feels different because everyone knows the visit is ending.
ramacharitamanas::3547.insight: It shows how duty can resume even while grief remains present in the heart.

ramacharitamanas::3548.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु पद पदुम बंदि दोउ भाई। चले सीस धरि राम रजाई॥ मुनि तापस बनदेव निहोरी। सब सनमानि बहोरि बहोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3548.verse_hindi: प्रभु के चरणकमलों की वंदना करके तथा श्री रामजी की आज्ञा को सिर पर रखकर भरत-शत्रुघ्न दोनों भाई चले। मुनि, तपस्वी और वनदेवता सबका बार-बार सम्मान करके उनकी विनती की ॥
ramacharitamanas::3548.english_translation: Both brothers bowed at the Lord's lotus feet and left with Ram's command on their heads. They honored the sages, ascetics, and forest spirits again and again, offering respectful requests.
ramacharitamanas::3548.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / पद (feet) / पदुम (lotus) / बंदि (having bowed) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / चले (left) / सीस (head) / धरि (placing) / राम (Ram's) / रजाई (command)॥ / मुनि (sages) / तापस (ascetics) / बनदेव (forest deities) / निहोरी (with requests, with reverence)॥ / सब (all) / सनमानि (honoring) / बहोरि बहोरी (again and again)॥
ramacharitamanas::3548.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3548.essence: Humility obeys fully and still bows to everyone along the way.
ramacharitamanas::3548.simple_meaning: Bharat and Shatrughna leave after bowing to Ram, carrying his command as their guiding order. Before going, they respectfully honor the sages, ascetics, and forest beings around them.
ramacharitamanas::3548.simple_insight: True humility shows itself in how you leave, not just how you arrive.
ramacharitamanas::3548.detailed_meaning: After meeting Ram, Bharat and Shatrughna do not rush away with pride or possession. They bow, accept Ram's command as supreme, and then respectfully take leave from the sages, ascetics, and forest beings. The scene shows their complete humility and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3548.modern_relevance: You finish the meeting, but before stepping out you thank the people who helped, the assistants, even the quiet ones in the room. Leaving well can be its own form of character.
ramacharitamanas::3548.insight: It teaches you to carry instruction with humility and to honor everyone before moving on.

ramacharitamanas::3549.verse_sanskrit: लखनहि भेंटि प्रनामु करि सिर धरि सिय पद धूरि। चले सप्रेम असीस सुनि सकल सुमंगल मूरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3549.verse_hindi: फिर लक्ष्मणजी को क्रमशः भेंटकर तथा प्रणाम करके और सीताजी के चरणों की धूलि को सिर पर धारण करके और समस्त मंगलों के मूल आशीर्वाद सुनकर वे प्रेमसहित चले ॥
ramacharitamanas::3549.english_translation: Then, greeting Lakshman and bowing, he placed Sita's dust on his head and departed in love after hearing blessings from the source of all auspiciousness.
ramacharitamanas::3549.translation_literal: लखनहि (to Lakshman) / भेंटि (meeting, greeting) / प्रनामु (salutation) / करि (doing) / सिर धरि (placing on the head) / सिय पद धूरि (the dust of Sita's feet) / चले (they went) / सप्रेम (with love) / असीस (blessings) / सुनि (hearing) / सकल सुमंगल मूरि (the root/source of all auspiciousness)
ramacharitamanas::3549.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3549.essence: Respect and love can sanctify even a simple departure.
ramacharitamanas::3549.simple_meaning: They greet Lakshman, bow to Sita, receive blessings, and leave with loving hearts.
ramacharitamanas::3549.simple_insight: Even departure can become sacred when it is full of respect and love.
ramacharitamanas::3549.detailed_meaning: Bharat and Shatrughna are leaving the forest meeting. Before they go, they honor Lakshman, bow to Sita, and receive blessings. The verse lingers on their reverence, not on action, showing how devotion shapes even a farewell.
ramacharitamanas::3549.modern_relevance: You leave a home after a hard conversation, but you still touch the elder's feet, thank the host, and carry the warmth with you.
ramacharitamanas::3549.insight: It turns departure into an act of reverence, not mere movement.

ramacharitamanas::3550.verse_sanskrit: सानुज राम नृपहि सिर नाई। कीन्हि बहुत बिधि बिनय बड़ाई॥ देव दया बस बड़ दुखु पायउ। सहित समाज काननहिं आयउ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3550.verse_hindi: छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी समेत श्री रामजी ने राजा जनकजी को सिर नवाकर उनकी बहुत प्रकार से विनती और बड़ाई की (और कहा-) हे देव! दयावश आपने बहुत दुःख पाया। आप समाज सहित वन में आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3550.english_translation: With Lakshman beside him, Ram bowed to King Janak and praised him in many ways: “By your grace, O noble one, you have suffered much sorrow and come to the forest with your whole assembly.”
ramacharitamanas::3550.translation_literal: सानुज (with younger brother) / राम (Ram) / नृपहि (to the king) / सिर (head) / नाई (bowing) / कीन्हि (did) / बहुत बिधि (many ways) / बिनय (humble request/praise) / बड़ाई (praise) / देव (noble one) / दया बस (by grace) / बड़ दुखु (great sorrow) / पायउ (you suffered) / सहित समाज (with the whole assembly) / काननहिं (to the forest) / आयउ (came)
ramacharitamanas::3550.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3550.essence: True greatness bows first and recognizes another's burden.
ramacharitamanas::3550.simple_meaning: Ram greets King Janak with deep respect and praises his willingness to come into the forest with everyone around him.
ramacharitamanas::3550.simple_insight: Respect can be as moving as power. Even the highest honor bows first.
ramacharitamanas::3550.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram and Lakshman meet King Janak. Ram bows to him, speaks gently, and honors the pain Janak has borne in coming there with his people. The moment shows Ram's humility and Janak's dignity before the next farewell.
ramacharitamanas::3550.modern_relevance: You meet someone at a hospital entrance after they have carried their whole family through a hard night. Before asking anything, you honor what they have already endured.
ramacharitamanas::3550.insight: It teaches you to begin with reverence, especially when another person has already suffered for others.

ramacharitamanas::3551.verse_sanskrit: पुर पगु धारिअ देइ असीसा। कीन्ह धीर धरि गवनु महीसा॥ मुनि महिदेव साधु सनमाने। बिदा किए हरि हर सम जाने ॥
ramacharitamanas::3551.verse_hindi: अब आशीर्वाद देकर नगर को पधारिए। यह सुन राजा जनकजी ने धीरज धरकर गमन किया। फिर श्री रामचंद्रजी ने मुनि, ब्राह्मण और साधुओं को विष्णु और शिव के समान जानकर सम्मान करके उनको विदा किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3551.english_translation: Now, after giving blessings, let the king depart to the city. Hearing this, King Janaka gathered himself and set out with composure. Then Ram honored sages, priests, and holy men, knowing them as equal to Vishnu and Shiva, and bade them farewell.
ramacharitamanas::3551.translation_literal: पुर (to the city) / पगु (footstep; depart) / धारिअ (let be placed; let go) / देइ (giving) / असीसा (blessings) / कीन्हि (did) / धीर धरि (holding composure) / गवनु (departure) / महीसा (king) / मुनि (sages) / महिदेव (priests; revered ones) / साधु (holy men) / सनमाने (honored) / बिदा किए (sent off; bade farewell) / हरि (Ram) / हर (Shiva) / सम (equal) / जाने (knowing)
ramacharitamanas::3551.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3551.essence: True dignity is leaving calmly and honoring the worthy fully.
ramacharitamanas::3551.simple_meaning: Janaka leaves with dignity after receiving blessings, and Ram respectfully sends off the sages and holy men as worthy of the highest honor.
ramacharitamanas::3551.simple_insight: Leave with grace, and treat every worthy person with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3551.detailed_meaning: Janaka has come to bid farewell after the wedding and blessings. He departs with steadiness, not sorrow. Ram then turns to the gathered sages, priests, and holy men, honoring them deeply before sending them away.
ramacharitamanas::3551.modern_relevance: At the end of a wedding, when the elders rise and the room slowly empties, the real beauty is in the way everyone leaves: blessed, composed, and respected.
ramacharitamanas::3551.insight: It teaches graceful departure and humble honor toward the wise.

ramacharitamanas::3552.verse_sanskrit: सासु समीप गए दोउ भाई। फिरे बंदि पग आसिष पाई॥ कौसिक बामदेव जाबाली। पुरजन परिजन सचिव सुचाली ॥
