ramacharitamanas::3552.verse_hindi: तब श्री राम-लक्ष्मण दोनों भाई सास (सुनयनाजी) के पास गए और उनके चरणों की वंदना करके आशीर्वाद पाकर लौट आए। फिर विश्वामित्र, वामदेव, जाबालि और शुभ आचरण वाले कुटुम्बी, नगर निवासी और मंत्री- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3552.english_translation: Then both brothers went to their mother, bowed at her feet, received her blessing, and returned. After that, Kaushik, Vamadeva, Jabali, the townspeople, relatives, and upright ministers...
ramacharitamanas::3552.translation_literal: सासु (mother-in-law / elder mother) / समीप (near) / गए (went) / दोउ (both) / भाई (brothers) / फिरे (returned) / बंदि (bowing) / पग (feet) / आसिष (blessing) / पाई (having received)॥ / कौसिक (Kaushik) / बामदेव (Vamadeva) / जाबाली (Jabali) / पुरजन (townspeople) / परिजन (relatives) / सचिव (ministers) / सुचाली (upright / good-conducted)
ramacharitamanas::3552.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3552.essence: Departure stays noble when it begins with respect.
ramacharitamanas::3552.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman visit their mother, bow to her feet, receive her blessing, and then greet the assembled sages, relatives, citizens, and ministers.
ramacharitamanas::3552.simple_insight: Respect comes before departure. Even in a major life change, they move through blessing, not ego.
ramacharitamanas::3552.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram’s exile is underway, and the farewell continues through the household and court. Ram and Lakshman first honor their mother, then turn to sages, relatives, townspeople, and ministers. The verse is a graceful scene of leave-taking, not a teaching in itself.
ramacharitamanas::3552.modern_relevance: You leave the house for a life-changing move, but first you touch your mother’s feet, thank the elders, and say goodbye properly. Some departures stay clean because they begin with humility.
ramacharitamanas::3552.insight: It shows how to leave without breaking your bonds: honor the people who formed you before you step forward.

ramacharitamanas::3553.verse_sanskrit: जथा जोगु करि बिनय प्रनामा। बिदा किए सब सानुज रामा॥ नारि पुरुष लघु मध्य बड़ेरे। सब सनमानि कृपानिधि फेरे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3553.verse_hindi: सबको छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित श्री रामचंद्रजी ने यथायोग्य विनय एवं प्रणाम करके विदा किया। कृपानिधान श्री रामचंद्रजी ने छोटे, मध्यम (मझले) और बड़े सभी श्रेणी के स्त्री-पुरुषों का सम्मान करके उनको लौटाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3553.english_translation: Rama, along with Lakshmana, respectfully took leave of everyone. The treasure of compassion honored all the women and men, young, middle-aged, and old, and sent them back.
ramacharitamanas::3553.translation_literal: जथा जोगु (as appropriate) / करि (having done) / बिनय (humble request) / प्रनामा (bowing) / बिदा किए (took leave) / सब (all) / सानुज (with younger brother) / रामा (Rama) / नारि (women) / पुरुष (men) / लघु (young/small) / मध्य (middle) / बड़ेरे (elder) / सब (all) / सनमानि (honoring) / कृपानिधि (treasure of compassion) / फेरे (sent back)
ramacharitamanas::3553.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3553.essence: True grace honors everyone, not just the important few.
ramacharitamanas::3553.simple_meaning: Rama and Lakshmana respectfully take leave of everyone, honoring people of every age and rank before sending them back.
ramacharitamanas::3553.simple_insight: Respect is not selective here; everyone is treated with care.
ramacharitamanas::3553.detailed_meaning: After the wedding celebrations in Mithila, Rama and Lakshmana prepare to depart. Before leaving, they bow properly to everyone and honor women and men, young and old alike. The scene shows Rama's grace in ordinary social conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3553.modern_relevance: You leave a family gathering and make sure the quiet aunt, the child, and the elder all feel seen before you go.
ramacharitamanas::3553.insight: It trains you to show equal respect, not just to the people who matter most to you.

ramacharitamanas::3554.verse_sanskrit: भरत मातु पद बंदि प्रभु सुचि सनेहँ मिलि भेंटि। बिदा कीन्ह सजि पालकी सकुच सोच सब मेटि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3554.verse_hindi: भरत की माता कैकेयी के चरणों की वंदना करके प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी ने पवित्र (निश्छल) प्रेम के साथ उनसे मिल-भेंट कर तथा उनके सारे संकोच और सोच को मिटाकर पालकी सजाकर उनको विदा किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3554.english_translation: Lord Ram bowed at Bharata's mother's feet, met her with pure affection, and, removing all her hesitation and worry, had a palanquin prepared and sent her off.
ramacharitamanas::3554.translation_literal: भरत (Bharata) / मातु (mother) / पद (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सुचि (pure) / सनेहँ (with affection) / मिलि (meeting) / भेंटि (having met) / बिदा (farewell) / कीन्ह (did) / सजि (having prepared) / पालकी (palanquin) / सकुच (hesitation) / सोच (worry) / सब (all) / मेटि (removing)
ramacharitamanas::3554.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3554.essence: Respect can soften even a painful family bond.
ramacharitamanas::3554.simple_meaning: Ram shows deep respect to Kaikeyi, meets her with sincere affection, removes her awkwardness and worry, and arranges her farewell kindly.
ramacharitamanas::3554.simple_insight: Even strained relationships can be met with dignity, warmth, and care.
ramacharitamanas::3554.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram is preparing to leave. He meets Kaikeyi, Bharata's mother, not with resentment but with gentle respect. By bowing, speaking kindly, and arranging her departure, he dissolves the tension around her.
ramacharitamanas::3554.modern_relevance: You see someone who hurt your family at a gathering, and everyone stiffens. Ram's response shows another way: meet them with dignity, not poison the room.
ramacharitamanas::3554.insight: It teaches you to lower conflict through respectful action instead of carrying old heat forward.

ramacharitamanas::3555.verse_sanskrit: परिजन मातु पितहि मिलि सीता। फिरी प्रानप्रिय प्रेम पुनीता॥ करि प्रनामु भेंटीं सब सासू। प्रीति कहत कबि हियँ न हुलासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3555.verse_hindi: प्राणप्रिय पति श्री रामचंद्रजी के साथ पवित्र प्रेम करने वाली सीताजी नैहर के कुटुम्बियों से तथा माता-पिता से मिलकर लौट आईं। फिर प्रणाम करके सब सासुओं से गले लगकर मिलीं। उनके प्रेम का वर्णन करने के लिए कवि के हृदय में हुलास (उत्साह) नहीं होता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3555.english_translation: Sita met her parents and relatives, then returned with pure love for her dear husband. She bowed and embraced all her mothers-in-law, and the poet says his heart cannot contain the joy of describing their love.
ramacharitamanas::3555.translation_literal: परिजन (relatives) / मातु पितहि (mother and father) / मिलि (meeting) / सीता (Sita) / फिरी (returned) / प्रानप्रिय (dear as life) / प्रेम (love) / पुनीता (pure) / करि (doing) / प्रनामु (bowing) / भेंटीं (embraced/met) / सब (all) / सासू (mothers-in-law) / प्रीति (love/affection) / कहत (telling) / कबि (poet) / हियँ (in heart) / न (not) / हुलासू (joy/exultation)
ramacharitamanas::3555.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3555.essence: Love becomes complete when respect flows to everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3555.simple_meaning: Sita lovingly meets her family and in-laws before returning. The verse lingers on the warmth and respect flowing between both sides of the family.
ramacharitamanas::3555.simple_insight: Love grows deeper when respect reaches both directions, not just one.
ramacharitamanas::3555.detailed_meaning: After Ram has honored everyone and the departure is being arranged, Sita meets her parents and relatives, then greets all her mothers-in-law with reverence and affection. The scene is not a teaching speech but a tender farewell, and the poet pauses to savor its sweetness.
ramacharitamanas::3555.modern_relevance: You leave a family gathering after hugging both sides of the family, and the room still feels warm behind you. Some goodbyes are made of respect, not distance.
ramacharitamanas::3555.insight: It highlights how affection and proper conduct can coexist without strain.

ramacharitamanas::3556.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सिख अभिमत आसिष पाई। रही सीय दुहु प्रीति समाई॥ रघुपति पटु पालकीं मगाईं। करि प्रबोध सब मातु चढ़ाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3556.verse_hindi: उनकी शिक्षा सुनकर और मनचाहा आशीर्वाद पाकर सीताजी सासुओं तथा माता-पिता दोनों ओर की प्रीति में समाई (बहुत देर तक निमग्न) रहीं! (तब) श्री रघुनाथजी ने सुंदर पालकियाँ मँगवाईं और सब माताओं को आश्वासन देकर उन पर चढ़ाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3556.english_translation: After hearing the advice and receiving the blessing she wanted, Sita remained absorbed in equal affection for both families. Then Lord Raghunath arranged fine palanquins and, reassuring all the mothers, helped them into them.
ramacharitamanas::3556.translation_literal: सुनि (having heard) / सिख (advice) / अभिमत (desired) / आसिष (blessing) / पाई (having received) / रही (remained) / सीय (Sita) / दुहु (both) / प्रीति (affection) / समाई (absorbed) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / पटु (fine) / पालकीं (palanquins) / मगाईं (had brought) / करि (having done) / प्रबोध (reassurance) / सब (all) / मातु (mothers) / चढ़ाईं (placed into)
ramacharitamanas::3556.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3556.essence: True affection makes parting gentle, not painful.
ramacharitamanas::3556.simple_meaning: Sita receives the blessing she wanted and stays equally devoted to both families. Ram then arranges palanquins and gently sends the mothers off with reassurance.
ramacharitamanas::3556.simple_insight: Love can hold two families at once without choosing sides or creating distance.
ramacharitamanas::3556.detailed_meaning: Sita has finished her visit home. After blessings and warm counsel, she remains filled with equal affection for both her birth family and her in-laws. Ram then arranges palanquins and comforts the mothers before sending everyone on their way.
ramacharitamanas::3556.modern_relevance: After a wedding weekend, you stand at the doorway while both families linger, reluctant to part. Someone quietly makes sure everyone is cared for, and the farewell becomes tender instead of awkward.
ramacharitamanas::3556.insight: It shows how care can smooth a transition, honoring both attachment and departure without forcing either.

ramacharitamanas::3557.verse_sanskrit: बार बार हिलि मिलि दुहु भाईं। सम सनेहँ जननीं पहुँचाईं॥ साजि बाजि गज बाहन नाना। भरत भूप दल कीन्ह पयाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3557.verse_hindi: दोनों भाइयों ने माताओं से समान प्रेम से बार-बार मिल-जुलकर उनको पहुँचाया। भरतजी और राजा जनकजी के दलों ने घोड़े, हाथी और अनेकों तरह की सवारियाँ सजाकर प्रस्थान किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3557.english_translation: Again and again, both brothers met and embraced their mothers and escorted them with equal affection. Then Bharat's party set out with horses, elephants, and many kinds of vehicles.
ramacharitamanas::3557.translation_literal: बार बार (again and again) / हिलि मिलि (meeting and embracing) / दुहु भाईं (both brothers) / सम सनेहँ (with equal affection) / जननीं (the mothers) / पहुँचाईं (escorted, brought them to their destination) / साजि (arranged, prepared) / बाजि (horses) / गज (elephants) / बाहन (vehicles, mounts) / नाना (various) / भरत भूप (Bharat, the king) / दल (party, group) / कीन्ह (made, prepared) / पयाना (departure, journey)
ramacharitamanas::3557.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3557.essence: Equal affection is shown in the way you escort, not in grand words.
ramacharitamanas::3557.simple_meaning: The brothers lovingly see their mothers off, and Bharat’s group leaves with a grand procession of horses, elephants, and vehicles.
ramacharitamanas::3557.simple_insight: Love shows itself in how you send people off, not just how you greet them.
ramacharitamanas::3557.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, the farewell is still unfolding after the painful separation. The brothers keep meeting their mothers with equal affection and escort them respectfully. Then Bharat’s camp prepares to depart in royal order, marking the movement of the whole household into grief and duty.
ramacharitamanas::3557.modern_relevance: You walk your parents to the car after a hard family visit, making sure no one feels left behind. Even small gestures can carry the weight of care.
ramacharitamanas::3557.insight: It shifts attention from ceremony to tenderness: the way you part can reveal the depth of your love.

ramacharitamanas::3558.verse_sanskrit: हृदयँ रामु सिय लखन समेता। चले जाहिं सब लोग अचेता॥ बसह बाजि गज पसु हियँ हारें। चले जाहिं परबस मन मारें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3558.verse_hindi: सीताजी एवं लक्ष्मणजी सहित श्री रामचंद्रजी को हृदय में रखकर सब लोग बेसुध हुए चले जा रहे हैं। बैल-घोड़े, हाथी आदि पशु हृदय में हारे (शिथिल) हुए परवश मन मारे चले जा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3558.english_translation: With Ram, Sita, and Lakshman in their hearts, everyone walked on in a daze. Even the cattle, horses, elephants, and other animals, with hearts drooping, moved on helplessly, their minds stricken.
ramacharitamanas::3558.translation_literal: हृदयँ (in the heart) / रामु (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / लखन (Lakshman) / समेता (together with) / चले जाहिं (were going) / सब लोग (all the people) / अचेता (unconscious, dazed)॥ / बसह (cattle) / बाजि (horses) / गज (elephants) / पसु (animals) / हियँ (in the heart) / हारें (defeated, drooping) / चले जाहिं (were going) / परबस (helpless) / मन मारें (with mind struck down)॥
ramacharitamanas::3558.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3558.essence: When Ram leaves, even the city feels grief.
ramacharitamanas::3558.simple_meaning: Everyone is so overwhelmed by Ram’s departure that they walk on in a daze, and even the animals seem subdued and helpless.
ramacharitamanas::3558.simple_insight: Separation can make an entire world feel stunned and empty.
ramacharitamanas::3558.detailed_meaning: As Ram, Sita, and Lakshman leave Ayodhya, the grief is not private anymore. People, animals, and the whole city seem to lose their strength and awareness. This verse lingers on the shared shock of exile.
ramacharitamanas::3558.modern_relevance: You leave the hospital after hearing bad news, and the street looks unreal. People keep moving, but your whole world has gone quiet inside.
ramacharitamanas::3558.insight: It shows how deeply one departure can affect an entire community, not just one family.

ramacharitamanas::3559.verse_sanskrit: गुर गुरतिय पद बंदि प्रभु सीता लखन समेत। फिरे हरष बिसमय सहित आए परन निकेत ॥
ramacharitamanas::3559.verse_hindi: गुरु वशिष्ठजी और गुरु पत्नी अरुन्धतीजी के चरणों की वंदना करके सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी हर्ष और विषाद के साथ लौटकर पर्णकुटी पर आए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3559.english_translation: After bowing to Guru Vashishtha and Arundhati, Lord Ram returned with Sita and Lakshman, filled with joy and wonder, to the forest hut.
ramacharitamanas::3559.translation_literal: गुर (guru) / गुरतिय (guru's wife) / पद (feet) / बंदि (bowing) / प्रभु (Lord) / सीता (Sita) / लखन (Lakshman) / समेत (together with) / फिरे (returned) / हरष (joy) / बिसमय (wonder) / सहित (with) / आए (came) / परन निकेत (forest hut)
ramacharitamanas::3559.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3559.essence: Respect and wonder travel with you even after the moment has passed.
ramacharitamanas::3559.simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman bow to their teachers and return to their forest hut, feeling both joy and wonder.
ramacharitamanas::3559.simple_insight: Even in departure, respect comes first.
ramacharitamanas::3559.detailed_meaning: The farewell at the wedding has ended, and the whole group is moving back from the teachers’ place. Ram, Sita, and Lakshman bow to Vashishtha and Arundhati before returning to the forest hut, carrying both happiness and the strange weight of a life changing direction.
ramacharitamanas::3559.modern_relevance: You leave your mentor’s house after receiving life-changing advice, still smiling and still stunned. The lesson is not just what you heard — it is how you carry yourself after hearing it.
ramacharitamanas::3559.insight: It shifts attention from the event itself to the humility that frames it.

ramacharitamanas::3560.verse_sanskrit: बिदा कीन्ह सनमानि निषादू। चलेउ हृदयँ बड़ बिरह बिषादू॥ कोल किरात भिल्ल बनचारी। फेरे फिरे जोहारि जोहारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3560.verse_hindi: फिर सम्मान करके निषादराज को विदा किया। वह चला तो सही, किन्तु उसके हृदय में विरह का भारी विषाद था। फिर श्री रामजी ने कोल, किरात, भील आदि वनवासी लोगों को लौटाया। वे सब जोहार-जोहार कर (वंदना कर-करके) लौटे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3560.english_translation: After honouring Nishad, Ram sent him away. Ram then moved on, but his heart was heavy with separation. He also sent back the Kol, Kirat, Bhil, and other forest people, and they all returned with repeated salutations.
ramacharitamanas::3560.translation_literal: बिदा (farewell) / कीन्ह (did) / सनमानि (honouring) / निषादू (Nishad) / चलेउ (moved on) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बड़ (great) / बिरह (separation) / बिषादू (sorrow) / कोल (Kol) / किरात (Kirat) / भिल्ल (Bhil) / बनचारी (forest-dwellers) / फेरे (sent back) / फिरे (returned) / जोहारि (saluting) / जोहारी (having saluted)
ramacharitamanas::3560.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3560.essence: Love makes even a proper farewell feel like loss.
ramacharitamanas::3560.simple_meaning: Ram respectfully sends away the forest people who had accompanied him. Everyone parts with deep sadness, because this journey is marked by love and separation.
ramacharitamanas::3560.simple_insight: Even a respectful farewell can hurt when love is real.
ramacharitamanas::3560.detailed_meaning: Ram has left Ayodhya and is moving deeper into exile. Nishadraj Guha, along with the Kol, Kirat, and Bhil forest people, has helped him and now must turn back. The verse lingers on the ache of parting, not on travel.
ramacharitamanas::3560.modern_relevance: You wave goodbye after a long visit, then sit in the car before starting the engine. Everyone was smiling, but the silence after the farewell feels heavier than words.
ramacharitamanas::3560.insight: It shifts attention from the action of leaving to the emotional cost of separation.

ramacharitamanas::3561.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु सिय लखन बैठि बट छाहीं। प्रिय परिजन बियोग बिलखाहीं॥ भरत सनेह सुभाउ सुबानी। प्रिया अनुज सन कहत बखानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3561.verse_hindi: प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी, सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी बड़ की छाया में बैठकर प्रियजन एवं परिवार के वियोग से दुःखी हो रहे हैं। भरतजी के स्नेह, स्वभाव और सुंदर वाणी को बखान-बखान कर वे प्रिय पत्नी सीताजी और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी से कहने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3561.english_translation: Lord Ram, Sita, and Lakshman sat under the shade of a banyan tree, grieving the separation from their loved ones. Ram then spoke to his dear wife Sita and younger brother Lakshman, praising Bharat's affection, nature, and sweet speech.
ramacharitamanas::3561.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord) / सिय (Sita) / लखन (Lakshman) / बैठि (having sat) / बट छाहीं (under the banyan shade) / प्रिय परिजन (dear relatives) / बियोग (separation) / बिलखाहीं (are grieving) / भरत सनेह (Bharat's affection) / सुभाउ (nature) / सुबानी (sweet speech) / प्रिया (dear) / अनुज (younger brother) / सन (with) / कहत (speaking) / बखानी (praising)
ramacharitamanas::3561.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3561.essence: Missing people can deepen, not diminish, the love you feel for them.
ramacharitamanas::3561.simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman sit in sorrow under a tree, missing those they love. Ram begins praising Bharat's loving nature to Sita and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::3561.simple_insight: Love makes separation feel heavier, and praise becomes a way of keeping the absent person near.
ramacharitamanas::3561.detailed_meaning: On the road during exile, Ram, Sita, and Lakshman rest under a banyan tree, still aching from leaving Ayodhya behind. Ram turns to Sita and Lakshman and speaks of Bharat's love, showing how grief and affection move together in this family.
ramacharitamanas::3561.modern_relevance: You sit in a quiet park after leaving home for a hard move, and the people you miss keep rising in your chest. Naming their goodness is one way grief softens.
ramacharitamanas::3561.insight: It teaches you to hold separation without hardening, and to let gratitude keep relationships alive across distance.

ramacharitamanas::3562.verse_sanskrit: प्रीति प्रतीति बचन मन करनी। श्रीमुख राम प्रेम बस बरनी॥ तेहि अवसर खम मृग जल मीना। चित्रकूट चर अचर मलीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3562.verse_hindi: श्री रामचंद्रजी ने प्रेम के वश होकर भरतजी के वचन, मन, कर्म की प्रीति तथा विश्वास का अपने श्रीमुख से वर्णन किया। उस समय पक्षी, पशु और जल की मछलियाँ, चित्रकूट के सभी चेतन और जड़ जीव उदास हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3562.english_translation: Ram, moved by love, spoke from his own mouth about Bharat's love, trust, words, mind, and actions. At that moment, the birds, animals, fish, and all living and still things of Chitrakoot became sorrowful.
ramacharitamanas::3562.translation_literal: प्रीति (love) / प्रतीति (trust) / बचन (words) / मन (mind) / करनी (actions) / श्रीमुख (from the blessed mouth) / राम (Ram) / प्रेम (love) / बस (under the power of) / बरनी (described) / तेहि अवसर (at that moment) / खम (birds) / मृग (animals) / जल (water) / मीना (fish) / चित्रकूट (Chitrakoot) / चर (moving) / अचर (still) / मलीना (sorrowful)
ramacharitamanas::3562.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3562.essence: Love can make an entire place grieve with you.
ramacharitamanas::3562.simple_meaning: Ram speaks lovingly about Bharat's devotion, and even Chitrakoot's living and still world feels the sorrow of separation.
ramacharitamanas::3562.simple_insight: Real love makes even the world around you feel your grief.
ramacharitamanas::3562.detailed_meaning: At Chitrakoot, Ram sits with Sita and Lakshman after the painful separation from Ayodhya. Overcome by love, he speaks of Bharat's faith, words, mind, and conduct. The scene is so charged that birds, beasts, fish, and the hills seem to share the sorrow.
ramacharitamanas::3562.modern_relevance: You hear a friend's voice after months apart, and the whole room seems to change. Some bonds are so deep that even silence feels heavy with them.
ramacharitamanas::3562.insight: It shifts attention from outward events to the emotional force moving through everyone present.

ramacharitamanas::3563.verse_sanskrit: बिबुध बिलोकि दसा रघुबर की। बरषि सुमन कहि गति घर घर की॥ प्रभु प्रनामु करि दीन्ह भरोसो। चले मुदित मन डर न खरो सो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3563.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी की दशा देखकर देवताओं ने उन पर फूल बरसाकर अपनी घर-घर की दशा कही (दुखड़ा सुनाया)। प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी ने उन्हें प्रणाम कर आश्वासन दिया। तब वे प्रसन्न होकर चले, मन में जरा सा भी डर न रहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3563.english_translation: Seeing Raghubar's condition, the gods showered flowers and spoke of their own homes and sorrows. The Lord bowed to them and gave reassurance. Then they left delighted, with no fear left in their minds.
ramacharitamanas::3563.translation_literal: बिबुध (the gods) / बिलोकि (seeing) / दसा (condition) / रघुबर की (of Raghubar) / बरषि (showering) / सुमन (flowers) / कहि (speaking) / गति (condition) / घर घर की (of each home) / प्रभु (the Lord) / प्रनामु (bowing) / करि (having done) / दीन्ह (gave) / भरोसो (reassurance) / चले (they left) / मुदित (delighted) / मन (mind) / डर (fear) / न खरो सो (not at all remaining)
ramacharitamanas::3563.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3563.essence: Humility can steady even the ones who came to steady you.
ramacharitamanas::3563.simple_meaning: The gods see Ram's condition, honor him, and receive comfort. He bows back and reassures them, and they leave relieved.
ramacharitamanas::3563.simple_insight: Even the highest beings find ease when humility and reassurance meet.
ramacharitamanas::3563.detailed_meaning: In Chitrakoot, Ram is living in exile with Sita and Lakshman. Seeing his condition, the gods descend, scatter flowers, and speak of their own household troubles. Ram bows to them and gives reassurance, and they depart with fear gone.
ramacharitamanas::3563.modern_relevance: You visit someone in crisis expecting to comfort them, but their calm steadies you instead. A respectful bow and a few honest words can change the whole room.
ramacharitamanas::3563.insight: It shows that true dignity does not resist care; it receives it and returns courage to others.

ramacharitamanas::3564.verse_sanskrit: सानुज सीय समेत प्रभु राजत परन कुटीर। भगति ग्यानु बैराग्य जनु सोहत धरें सरीर ॥
ramacharitamanas::3564.verse_hindi: छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी समेत प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी पर्णकुटी में ऐसे सुशोभित हो रहे हैं मानो वैराग्य, भक्ति और ज्ञान शरीर धारण कर के शोभित हो रहे हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::3564.english_translation: The Lord, together with Lakshman and Sita, shines in the leaf-hut as if devotion, wisdom, and detachment have taken human form.
ramacharitamanas::3564.translation_literal: सानुज (with younger brother) / सीय समेत (together with Sita) / प्रभु (the Lord) / राजत (shining) / परन कुटीर (leaf-hut) / भगति (devotion) / ग्यानु (wisdom) / बैराग्य (detachment) / जनु (as if) / सोहत (adorned) / धरें सरीर (having taken a body)
ramacharitamanas::3564.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3564.essence: True richness can look like a simple hut.
ramacharitamanas::3564.simple_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita shine in a simple forest hut, and their presence looks like devotion, wisdom, and detachment made visible.
ramacharitamanas::3564.simple_insight: A humble life can still feel complete, radiant, and deeply ordered.
ramacharitamanas::3564.detailed_meaning: Ram is living in exile with Lakshman and Sita in a leaf-hut at Chitrakoot. Even in hardship, their presence looks effortless and luminous. Tulsidas sees not poverty, but devotion, wisdom, and detachment embodied together.
ramacharitamanas::3564.modern_relevance: You sit on a floor mattress in a rented room with almost nothing around you, yet the space feels peaceful because the right people are there. Simplicity stops feeling like lack.
ramacharitamanas::3564.insight: It shifts the mind from measuring life by possessions to recognizing the dignity of inner richness.

ramacharitamanas::3565.verse_sanskrit: मुनि महिसुर गुर भरत भुआलू। राम बिरहँ सबु साजु बिहालू। प्रभु गुन ग्राम गनत मन माहीं। सब चुपचाप चले मग जाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3565.verse_hindi: मुनि, ब्राह्मण, गुरु वशिष्ठजी, भरतजी और राजा जनकजी सारा समाज श्री रामचन्द्रजी के विरह में विह्वल है। प्रभु के गुण समूहों का मन में स्मरण करते हुए सब लोग मार्ग में चुपचाप चले जा रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3565.english_translation: The sages, priests, the teacher, Bharata, and King Janaka were all overwhelmed by separation from Ram. Remembering Ram's countless virtues in their minds, they walked on in silence.
ramacharitamanas::3565.translation_literal: मुनि (sages) / महिसुर (priests) / गुर (teacher) / भरत (Bharata) / भुआलू (king) / राम बिरहँ (in Ram's separation) / सबु साजु (all the company) / बिहालू (overwhelmed) / प्रभु (Lord) / गुन ग्राम (heap of virtues) / गनत (counting) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / सब (all) / चुपचाप (silently) / चले (walked) / मग जाहीं (on the road going)
ramacharitamanas::3565.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3565.essence: Separation from Ram turns even a crowd into a quiet procession.
ramacharitamanas::3565.simple_meaning: Everyone is heartbroken by Ram's absence, and they keep walking while quietly remembering his many virtues.
ramacharitamanas::3565.simple_insight: Love can make even a whole procession move in silence.
ramacharitamanas::3565.detailed_meaning: After Ram's exile, a mixed company of sages, priests, teachers, Bharata, and King Janaka travels together, each carrying the ache of separation. They do not speak much; Ram's qualities fill their minds and soften the whole journey.
ramacharitamanas::3565.modern_relevance: You leave a place after saying goodbye to someone who mattered deeply, and the car stays quiet for miles. Everyone is thinking the same thing, but no one wants to break the spell.
ramacharitamanas::3565.insight: It shifts attention from conversation to shared grief and remembrance, showing how devotion can silence a crowd.

ramacharitamanas::3566.verse_sanskrit: जमुना उतरि पार सबु भयऊ। सो बासरु बिनु भोजन गयऊ॥ उतरि देवसरि दूसर बासू। रामसखाँ सब कीन्ह सुपासू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3566.verse_hindi: (पहले दिन) सब लोग यमुनाजी उतरकर पार हुए। वह दिन बिना भोजन के ही बीत गया। दूसरा मुकाम गंगाजी उतरकर (गंगापार श्रृंगवेरपुर में) हुआ। वहाँ राम सखा निषादराज ने सब सुप्रबंध कर दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3566.english_translation: Everyone crossed the Yamuna and spent that day without food. The next halt was after crossing the Ganga, where Ram's friend Nishadraj arranged everything well.
ramacharitamanas::3566.translation_literal: जमुना (Yamuna) / उतरि (having crossed) / पार (across) / सबु (everyone) / भयऊ (went) । / सो (that) / बासरु (day) / बिनु (without) / भोजन (food) / गयऊ (passed) । / उतरि (crossing) / देवसरि (the Ganga) / दूसर (second) / बासू (halt) / रामसखाँ (Ram's friend) / सब (everything) / कीन्ह (did) / सुपासू (well arranged) ।
ramacharitamanas::3566.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3566.essence: Exile becomes bearable when loyal friendship meets you on the road.
ramacharitamanas::3566.simple_meaning: The travelers crossed two rivers during exile. They went hungry for a day, then rested at a place where Ram's friend arranged their stay.
ramacharitamanas::3566.simple_insight: Hard journeys are made bearable by small acts of care from loyal friends.
ramacharitamanas::3566.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, Lakshman, and their companions are moving through exile toward the forest. They cross the Yamuna, spend the day without food, then cross the Ganga and reach a stop where Nishadraj, Ram's friend, takes care of everything.
ramacharitamanas::3566.modern_relevance: You get off a crowded train after a long day, hungry and tired, and one friend is already there with water, food, and a place to sit. Relief often comes through quiet loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::3566.insight: It shifts attention from grand events to the human kindness that keeps difficult journeys moving.

ramacharitamanas::3567.verse_sanskrit: सई उतरि गोमतीं नहाए। चौथें दिवस अवधपुर आए॥ जनकु रहे पुर बासर चारी। राज काज सब साज सँभारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3567.verse_hindi: फिर सई उतरकर गोमतीजी में स्नान किया और चौथे दिन सब अयोध्याजी जा पहुँचे। जनकजी चार दिन अयोध्याजी में रहे और राजकाज एवं सब साज-सामान को सम्हालकर, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3567.english_translation: Then they crossed the Saryu, bathed in the Gomti, and reached Ayodhya on the fourth day. Janaka stayed in the city for four days, taking care of the kingdom and arranging everything.
ramacharitamanas::3567.translation_literal: सई (Sarayu) / उतरि (crossing) / गोमतीं (in the Gomti) / नहाए (bathed) / चौथें (fourth) / दिवस (day) / अवधपुर (Ayodhya city) / आए (came) / जनकु (Janaka) / रहे (stayed) / पुर (in the city) / बासर (days) / चारी (four) / राज काज (state affairs) / सब (all) / साज (arrangements) / सँभारी (managed)
ramacharitamanas::3567.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3567.essence: Even grief must pause for the duties that keep life in order.
ramacharitamanas::3567.simple_meaning: They crossed the river, bathed, and reached Ayodhya on the fourth day. Janaka stayed four days, managing the kingdom and its arrangements.
ramacharitamanas::3567.simple_insight: Sometimes devotion moves through simple, careful acts of travel, bathing, and settling what must be settled.
ramacharitamanas::3567.detailed_meaning: After the grief-filled journey, the group crosses the Sarayu, bathes in the Gomti, and reaches Ayodhya. Janaka remains in the city for four days, handling royal duties and preparations. The verse quietly marks the transition from mourning to practical order.
ramacharitamanas::3567.modern_relevance: After a funeral, someone still has to book the train, return the keys, and tell the landlord. Grief does not erase the tasks that keep life moving.
ramacharitamanas::3567.insight: It shifts attention from emotion alone to the steady work that follows loss.

ramacharitamanas::3568.verse_sanskrit: सौंपि सचिव गुर भरतहिं राजू। तेरहुति चले साजि सबु साजू॥ नगर नारि नर गुर सिख मानी। बसे सुखेन राम रजधानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3568.verse_hindi: तथा मंत्री, गुरुजी तथा भरतजी को राज्य सौंपकर, सारा साज-सामान ठीक करके तिरहुत को चले। नगर के स्त्री-पुरुष गुरुजी की शिक्षा मानकर श्री रामजी की राजधानी अयोध्याजी में सुखपूर्वक रहने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3568.english_translation: Handing the kingdom to the ministers, the teacher, and Bharat, and arranging everything, they departed for Tirhut. The people of the city, men and women alike, followed the teacher's guidance and lived happily in Ram's capital.
ramacharitamanas::3568.translation_literal: सौंपि (handing over) / सचिव (ministers) / गुर (teacher) / भरतहिं (to Bharat) / राजू (the kingdom) / तेरहुति (to Tirhut) / चले (departed) / साजि (arranging) / सबु (all) / साजू (arrangements) / नगर (city) / नारि (women) / नर (men) / गुर (teacher's) / सिख (instruction) / मानी (accepted) / बसे (lived) / सुखेन (happily) / राम (Ram's) / रजधानी (capital)
ramacharitamanas::3568.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3568.essence: Peace returns when each person accepts the right role.
ramacharitamanas::3568.simple_meaning: The kingdom is placed in Bharat's care, everyone prepares to leave, and the people of Ayodhya settle into peaceful life under the teacher's guidance.
ramacharitamanas::3568.simple_insight: Sometimes peace begins when everyone accepts their place and follows wise guidance.
ramacharitamanas::3568.detailed_meaning: After the long journey back, Janak and his party hand the kingdom over to Bharat, the ministers, and the teacher, then depart for Tirhut. In Ayodhya, the men and women follow the teacher's instruction and live contentedly in Ram's capital.
ramacharitamanas::3568.modern_relevance: A family finally divides responsibilities after weeks of tension: one person handles the accounts, another watches the children, and the house can breathe again. Order returns when everyone accepts their role.
ramacharitamanas::3568.insight: It shows how harmony returns when authority is entrusted properly and people choose discipline over confusion.

ramacharitamanas::3569.verse_sanskrit: राम दरस लगि लोग सब करत नेम उपबास। तजि तजि भूषन भोग सुख जिअत अवधि कीं आस ॥
ramacharitamanas::3569.verse_hindi: सब लोग श्री रामचन्द्रजी के दर्शन के लिए नियम और उपवास करने लगे। वे भूषण और भोग-सुखों को छोड़-छाड़कर अवधि की आशा पर जी रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3569.english_translation: All people fasted and kept vows for Ram's sight. They gave up ornaments and pleasures, living only in hope of the day he would return.
ramacharitamanas::3569.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / दरस (sight) / लगि (for the sake of) / लोग (people) / सब (all) / करत (doing) / नेम (vows) / उपबास (fasts) / तजि तजि (giving up again and again) / भूषन (ornaments) / भोग (pleasures) / सुख (comforts) / जिअत (living) / अवधि (Ayodhya's) / कीं (of) / आस (hope)
ramacharitamanas::3569.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3569.simple_meaning: The people of Ayodhya gave up comfort, beauty, and pleasure. They fasted and kept vows because they longed to see Ram return.
ramacharitamanas::3569.simple_insight: Longing can become a steady strength when what you love matters more than comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3569.detailed_meaning: Back in Ayodhya after Ram's exile, the city has become a place of waiting. People fast, keep vows, and turn away from luxury because their hearts are fixed on Ram's return. This verse shows a whole kingdom living in devotion and hope.
ramacharitamanas::3569.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone after sending the message that matters most. You skip the snack, the party, the distraction, because one return is all you can think about.
ramacharitamanas::3569.insight: It shifts attention from immediate comfort to faithful waiting for what matters most.

ramacharitamanas::3570.verse_sanskrit: सचिव सुसेवक भरत प्रबोधे। निज निज काज पाइ सिख ओधे॥ पुनि सिख दीन्हि बोलि लघु भाई। सौंपी सकल मातु सेवकाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3570.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने मंत्रियों और विश्वासी सेवकों को समझाकर उद्यत किया। वे सब सीख पाकर अपने-अपने काम में लग गए। फिर छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्नजी को बुलाकर शिक्षा दी और सब माताओं की सेवा उनको सौंपी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3570.english_translation: Bharat instructed the ministers and faithful servants, and each took up their own work. Then he called his younger brother Shatrughna, gave him guidance, and entrusted him with the service of all the mothers.
ramacharitamanas::3570.translation_literal: सचिव (ministers) / सुसेवक (faithful servants) / भरत (Bharat) / प्रबोधे (instructed, awakened) / निज निज (each one's own) / काज (work, task) / पाइ (having received) / सिख (instruction) / ओधे (applied, took up) / पुनि (then) / सिख (instruction) / दीन्हि (gave) / बोलि (calling) / लघु भाई (younger brother) / सौंपी (entrusted) / सकल (all) / मातु (mothers) / सेवकाई (service)
ramacharitamanas::3570.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3570.essence: Bharat serves by giving everyone their proper work.
ramacharitamanas::3570.simple_meaning: Bharat gives everyone a clear role: ministers do their work, Shatrughna serves the mothers, and the household keeps moving with order and care.
ramacharitamanas::3570.simple_insight: True leadership is not control; it is placing the right duty in the right hands.
ramacharitamanas::3570.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram is away and Bharat is carrying the burden of the kingdom without claiming it for himself. He organizes the ministers, assigns work, and asks Shatrughna to serve the mothers. This verse shows his quiet, practical stewardship.
ramacharitamanas::3570.modern_relevance: A family emergency hits, and everyone looks to one person for direction. Instead of panicking, you assign tasks, calm the room, and make sure the vulnerable are cared for.
ramacharitamanas::3570.insight: It teaches you to lead by clarifying responsibility, not by centering yourself.

ramacharitamanas::3571.verse_sanskrit: भूसुर बोलि भरत कर जोरे। करि प्रनाम बय बिनय निहोरे॥ ऊँच नीच कारजु भल पोचू। आयसु देब न करब सँकोचू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3571.verse_hindi: ब्राह्मणों को बुलाकर भरतजी ने हाथ जोड़कर प्रणाम कर अवस्था के अनुसार विनय और निहोरा किया कि आप लोग ऊँचा-नीचा (छोटा-बड़ा), अच्छा-मन्दा जो कुछ भी कार्य हो, उसके लिए आज्ञा दीजिएगा। संकोच न कीजिएगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3571.english_translation: Calling the Brahmins, Bharata joined his hands and bowed with humble respect. He said, "For any task, great or small, good or difficult, please give your command without hesitation."
ramacharitamanas::3571.translation_literal: भूसुर (Brahmins) / बोलि (calling) / भरत (Bharata) / कर (hands) / जोरे (joined) / करि (doing) / प्रनाम (bow) / बय (age/status) / बिनय (humble request) / निहोरे (earnest plea) / ऊँच (high) / नीच (low) / कारजु (task) / भल (good) / पोचू (bad/difficult) / आयसु (command) / देब (will give) / न करब (will not do) / सँकोचू (hesitation)
ramacharitamanas::3571.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3571.essence: Humility makes even authority ready to serve.
ramacharitamanas::3571.simple_meaning: Bharata humbly asks the Brahmins to give him any instruction, for any kind of work, without feeling shy or restrained.
ramacharitamanas::3571.simple_insight: True humility stays ready for every task, not just the respectable ones.
ramacharitamanas::3571.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharata has taken charge after Ram's exile. He gathers the Brahmins, bows to them, and asks them to direct him in any duty, large or small. His authority is real, but his humility is greater.
ramacharitamanas::3571.modern_relevance: You’re the team lead, but you still ask the senior colleague, "Tell me what needs doing." That kind of humility keeps power clean and service real.
ramacharitamanas::3571.insight: It teaches you to accept guidance and carry out any duty without ego.

ramacharitamanas::3572.verse_sanskrit: परिजन पुरजन प्रजा बोलाए। समाधानु करि सुबस बसाए॥ सानुज गे गुर गेहँ बहोरी। करि दंडवत कहत कर जोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3572.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने फिर परिवार के लोगों को, नागरिकों को तथा अन्य प्रजा को बुलाकर, उनका समाधान करके उनको सुखपूर्वक बसाया। फिर छोटे भाई शत्रुघ्नजी सहित वे गुरुजी के घर गए और दंडवत करके हाथ जोड़कर बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3572.english_translation: Bharat called together his family, the townspeople, and the rest of the people, calmed them, and settled them comfortably. Then, along with his younger brother Shatrughna, he went again to the guru's house, bowed fully, and spoke with joined hands.
ramacharitamanas::3572.translation_literal: परिजन (family members) / पुरजन (townspeople) / प्रजा (subjects, people) / बोलाए (called together) / समाधानु करि (having calmed and settled) / सुबस (comfortably, well) / बसाए (settled) / सानुज (with younger brother) / गे (went) / गुर गेहँ (to the guru's house) / बहोरी (again) / करि दंडवत (having bowed fully) / कहत (speaking) / कर जोरी (with joined hands)
ramacharitamanas::3572.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3572.essence: Steady everyone first, then bow for guidance.
ramacharitamanas::3572.simple_meaning: Bharat restores order among the people, then returns with Shatrughna to bow before the guru and speak respectfully.
ramacharitamanas::3572.simple_insight: Real leadership calms others first, then returns to humility.
ramacharitamanas::3572.detailed_meaning: After Ram's exile, Bharat is not just grieving — he is holding a kingdom together. He settles his family, citizens, and subjects, then goes with Shatrughna to Vashishtha's home, bowing before seeking guidance.
ramacharitamanas::3572.modern_relevance: A family crisis has shaken everyone, but you still have to answer texts, reassure relatives, and keep the house from falling apart. Bharat shows how to steady others without losing humility.
ramacharitamanas::3572.insight: It teaches you to restore stability around you before seeking counsel, and to approach guidance without pride.

ramacharitamanas::3573.verse_sanskrit: आयसु होइ त रहौं सनेमा। बोले मुनि तन पुलकि सपेमा॥ समुझब कहब करब तुम्ह जोई। धरम सारु जग होइहि सोई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3573.verse_hindi: आज्ञा हो तो मैं नियमपूर्वक रहूँ! मुनि वशिष्ठजी पुलकित शरीर हो प्रेम के साथ बोले- हे भरत! तुम जो कुछ समझोगे, कहोगे और करोगे, वही जगत में धर्म का सार होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3573.english_translation: If you permit me, I will live by your command. Sage Vashishtha, thrilled and full of love, said, “Bharat, whatever you understand, say, and do, that will be the essence of dharma in the world.”
ramacharitamanas::3573.translation_literal: आयसु (command/permission) / होइ (becomes) / त (then) / रहौं (I may remain) / सनेमा (with rules/obedience) / बोले (spoke) / मुनि (sage) / तन (body) / पुलकि (thrilled) / सपेमा (with love) / समुझब (understanding) / कहब (speaking) / करब (doing) / तुम्ह (you) / जोई (whatever) / धरम (dharma) / सारु (essence) / जग (world) / होइहि (will become) / सोई (that)
ramacharitamanas::3573.speaker: Vashishtha
ramacharitamanas::3573.essence: A clear, sincere life becomes the measure of dharma.
ramacharitamanas::3573.simple_meaning: Vashishtha tells Bharat that if he acts with understanding, honesty, and care, his life will become a model of righteous conduct for the world.
ramacharitamanas::3573.simple_insight: It feels steady to know that a clear, sincere life can guide others without force.
ramacharitamanas::3573.detailed_meaning: Bharat has taken charge with humility, asking the sages for guidance instead of power. Vashishtha, moved by Bharat's purity, blesses him with the highest praise: whatever Bharat truly understands, says, and does will show the world what dharma looks like.
ramacharitamanas::3573.modern_relevance: You’re asked to lead a team after a crisis, and everyone is watching how you think before they watch what you decide. The way you understand, speak, and act becomes the standard others follow.
ramacharitamanas::3573.insight: It shifts responsibility from image to integrity: your inner clarity must match your words and actions.

ramacharitamanas::3574.verse_sanskrit: सुनि सिख पाइ असीस बड़ि गनक बोलि दिनु साधि। सिंघासन प्रभु पादुका बैठारे निरुपाधि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3574.verse_hindi: भरतजी ने यह सुनकर और शिक्षा तथा बड़ा आशीर्वाद पाकर ज्योतिषियों को बुलाया और दिन (अच्छा मुहूर्त) साधकर प्रभु की चरणपादुकाओं को निर्विघ्नतापूर्वक सिंहासन पर विराजित कराया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3574.english_translation: Having heard the teaching and received great blessings, Bharat called the astrologers, chose an auspicious time, and reverently seated the Lord's sandals on the throne without obstruction.
ramacharitamanas::3574.translation_literal: सुनि (having heard) / सिख (teaching) / पाइ (having received) / असीस बड़ि (great blessing) / गनक (astrologers) / बोलि (calling) / दिनु (day/time) / साधि (choosing properly) / सिंघासन (throne) / प्रभु (lord) / पादुका (sandals) / बैठारे (seated) / निरुपाधि (without obstruction / without hindrance)
ramacharitamanas::3574.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3574.essence: You can hold power without wanting it for yourself.
ramacharitamanas::3574.simple_meaning: Bharat, after receiving guidance and blessings, arranges the coronation of Ram's sandals on the throne at the right time, with no resistance.
ramacharitamanas::3574.simple_insight: True renunciation can still be careful, orderly, and responsible.
ramacharitamanas::3574.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat has refused power for himself and chosen to serve Ram's absence with discipline. After Vashishtha's guidance, he consults astrologers, fixes the auspicious moment, and places Ram's sandals on the throne as the kingdom's rightful symbol.
ramacharitamanas::3574.modern_relevance: You step into a role you never wanted, but you still do it properly: the meeting is scheduled, the chair is set, and the person who truly belongs there is honored.
ramacharitamanas::3574.insight: It shifts action from self-claiming to faithful stewardship of what belongs to another.

ramacharitamanas::3575.verse_sanskrit: राम मातु गुर पद सिरु नाई। प्रभु पद पीठ रजायसु पाई॥ नंदिगाँव करि परन कुटीरा। कीन्ह निवासु धरम धुर धीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3575.verse_hindi: फिर श्री रामजी की माता कौसल्याजी और गुरुजी के चरणों में सिर नवाकर और प्रभु की चरणपादुकाओं की आज्ञा पाकर धर्म की धुरी धारण करने में धीर भरतजी ने नन्दिग्राम में पर्णकुटी बनाकर उसी में निवास किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3575.english_translation: After bowing to Ram's mother and to his teacher, and receiving the command from Ram's sandals, steadfast Bharata built a leaf hut in Nandigram and lived there.
ramacharitamanas::3575.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / मातु (mother) / गुर (teacher) / पद (feet) / सिरु नाई (bowing the head) / प्रभु (lord) / पद (feet) / पीठ (sandals) / रजायसु (command) / पाई (having received) / नंदिगाँव (Nandigram) / करि (having made) / परन कुटीरा (leaf hut) / कीन्ह (made) / निवासु (residence) / धरम (dharma) / धुर (burden/pillar) / धीरा (steadfast)
ramacharitamanas::3575.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3575.essence: You can renounce comfort and still stand taller than a king.
ramacharitamanas::3575.simple_meaning: Bharata honors his mother, his teacher, and Ram's command, then leaves the palace life behind and lives in a simple hut at Nandigram.
ramacharitamanas::3575.simple_insight: Real strength can look like surrendering comfort without surrendering dignity.
ramacharitamanas::3575.detailed_meaning: Bharata has already refused the throne. After bowing to Kaushalya and Vashistha, he accepts the authority of Ram's sandals and settles in Nandigram. His power now lies in disciplined renunciation, not in royal comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3575.modern_relevance: You turn down the bigger apartment, the title, the corner office, because taking it would betray what you value. Bharata shows that dignity can be stronger than ambition.
ramacharitamanas::3575.insight: It shifts the mind from status-seeking to voluntary simplicity in service of what is right.

ramacharitamanas::3576.verse_sanskrit: जटाजूट सिर मुनिपट धारी। महि खनि कुस साँथरी सँवारी॥ असन बसन बासन ब्रत नेमा। करत कठिन रिषिधरम सप्रेमा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3576.verse_hindi: सिर पर जटाजूट और शरीर में मुनियों के (वल्कल) वस्त्र धारण कर, पृथ्वी को खोदकर उसके अंदर कुश की आसनी बिछाई। भोजन, वस्त्र, बरतन, व्रत, नियम सभी बातों में वे ऋषियों के कठिन धर्म का प्रेम सहित आचरण करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3576.english_translation: With matted hair on his head and ascetic garments on his body, they dug the earth and prepared a bed of kusa grass. They began to practice the hard discipline of a sage, with love, in food, clothing, vessels, vows, and rules.
ramacharitamanas::3576.translation_literal: जटाजूट (matted hair) / सिर (head) / मुनिपट (ascetic garments) / धारी (wearing) / महि (earth) / खनि (dug) / कुस (kusa grass) / साँथरी (bed) / सँवारी (prepared) / असन (food) / बसन (clothing) / बासन (vessels) / ब्रत (vows) / नेमा (rules) / करत (doing) / कठिन (hard) / रिषिधरम (sage-dharma) / सप्रेमा (with love)
ramacharitamanas::3576.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3576.essence: Love can turn hardship into disciplined living.
ramacharitamanas::3576.simple_meaning: They lived like forest sages, with simple clothes, a grass bed, and strict vows. Even the hard discipline of an ascetic life was taken up lovingly.
ramacharitamanas::3576.simple_insight: Real discipline is not cold punishment; it becomes lighter when love is behind it.
ramacharitamanas::3576.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Ram, Sita, and Lakshman have already left palace life behind. In their forest dwelling, they choose the life of sages: matted hair, bark garments, a grass bed, and strict rules. The verse shows how exile is being transformed into sacred discipline.
ramacharitamanas::3576.modern_relevance: You move into a bare rental after a breakup, with a mattress on the floor and one box of dishes. The simplicity feels harsh at first, until it starts to feel clean.
ramacharitamanas::3576.insight: It shifts the mind from seeing hardship as loss to seeing it as chosen training.

ramacharitamanas::3577.verse_sanskrit: भूषन बसन भोग सुख भूरी। मन तन बचन तजे तिन तूरी॥ अवध राजु सुर राजु सिहाई। दसरथ धनु सुनि धनदु लजाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3577.verse_hindi: गहने-कपड़े और अनेकों प्रकार के भोग-सुखों को मन, तन और वचन से तृण तोड़कर (प्रतिज्ञा करके) त्याग दिया। जिस अयोध्या के राज्य को देवराज इन्द्र सिहाते थे और (जहाँ के राजा) दशरथजी की सम्पत्ति सुनकर कुबेर भी लजा जाते थे, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3577.english_translation: They gave up ornaments, clothes, pleasures, and abundant comforts with body, mind, and speech. Ayodhya's kingdom was so splendid that even Indra coveted it, and hearing of Dasharath's wealth made Kubera ashamed.
ramacharitamanas::3577.translation_literal: भूषन (ornaments) / बसन (clothes) / भोग (enjoyments) / सुख (comforts) / भूरी (abundant) / मन (mind) / तन (body) / बचन (speech) / तजे (gave up) / तिन (they) / तूरी (at once)॥ / अवध (Ayodhya) / राजु (kingdom) / सुर (devas) / राजु (royal rule) / सिहाई (coveted) / दसरथ (Dasharath) / धनु (wealth) / सुनि (hearing) / धनदु (Kubera) / लजाई (was ashamed)॥
ramacharitamanas::3577.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3577.essence: True nobility is proven by what you can leave untouched.
ramacharitamanas::3577.simple_meaning: The princes gave up royal luxury completely. Ayodhya was so wealthy and glorious that even heavenly rulers admired it, yet they walked away from all of it.
ramacharitamanas::3577.simple_insight: Real greatness is shown when you can leave comfort behind without hesitation.
ramacharitamanas::3577.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Ram has already turned from palace life toward exile. This verse recalls the luxury he left behind: ornaments, fine clothes, pleasures, and a kingdom envied even by Indra. The contrast makes his renunciation feel immense.
ramacharitamanas::3577.modern_relevance: You sign the promotion letter, then realize the bigger question is what it will cost your peace. This verse remembers the courage to walk away from glitter when your deeper duty asks for less.
ramacharitamanas::3577.insight: It shifts attention from status and comfort to the strength needed to release them.

ramacharitamanas::3578.verse_sanskrit: तेहिं पुर बसत भरत बिनु रागा। चंचरीक जिमि चंपक बागा॥ रमा बिलासु राम अनुरागी। तजत बमन जिमि जन बड़भागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3578.verse_hindi: उसी अयोध्यापुरी में भरतजी अनासक्त होकर इस प्रकार निवास कर रहे हैं, जैसे चम्पा के बाग में भौंरा। श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्रेमी बड़भागी पुरुष लक्ष्मी के विलास (भोगैश्वर्य) को वमन की भाँति त्याग देते हैं (फिर उसकी ओर ताकते भी नहीं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3578.english_translation: In that city, Bharat lived without attachment, like a bee in a champak grove. Those devoted to Ram reject the pleasures of wealth like something vomited and never look back.
ramacharitamanas::3578.translation_literal: तेहिं (in that) / पुर (city) / बसत (living) / भरत (Bharat) / बिनु रागा (without attachment) / चंचरीक (bee) / जिमि (like) / चंपक बागा (champak grove) / रमा (Lakshmi) / बिलासु (pleasures) / राम अनुरागी (Ram-devoted) / तजत (give up) / बमन जिमि (like vomit) / जन बड़भागी (fortunate people)
ramacharitamanas::3578.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3578.essence: Real detachment lives in the middle of abundance.
ramacharitamanas::3578.simple_meaning: Bharat lives in Ayodhya without attachment. A person devoted to Ram can enjoy none of the world’s pleasures and still remain fully alive to duty.
ramacharitamanas::3578.simple_insight: You do not need to chase comfort to be complete.
ramacharitamanas::3578.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, while the kingdom sits under the shadow of exile and grief, Bharat remains there without desire for luxury. Tulsidas compares him to a bee in a champak grove, untouched by the flowers’ pull, because his heart belongs to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3578.modern_relevance: You walk through a house full of gifts after a breakup, and nothing in the room calls to you anymore. Bharat knows that state: being present where you are, without letting comfort own you.
ramacharitamanas::3578.insight: It shifts the mind from craving pleasant experiences to remaining free while surrounded by them.

ramacharitamanas::3579.verse_sanskrit: राम प्रेम भाजन भरतु बड़े न एहिं करतूति। चातक हंस सराहिअत टेंक बिबेक बिभूति ॥
ramacharitamanas::3579.verse_hindi: फिर भरतजी तो (स्वयं) श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्रेम के पात्र हैं। वे इस (भोगैश्वर्य त्याग रूप) करनी से बड़े नहीं हुए (अर्थात उनके लिए यह कोई बड़ी बात नहीं है)। (पृथ्वी पर का जल न पीने की) टेक से चातक की और नीर-क्षीर-विवेक की विभूति (शक्ति) से हंस की भी सराहना होती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3579.english_translation: Bharat is already worthy of Ram's love; this act does not make him great. The chātak is praised for its vow, and the hansa for its discerning power.
ramacharitamanas::3579.translation_literal: राम (Ram) / प्रेम (love) / भाजन (recipient) / भरतु (Bharat) / बड़े (great) / न (not) / एहिं (this) / करतूति (act) / चातक (chātak bird) / हंस (hansa bird) / सराहिअत (are praised) / टेंक (vow, steadfastness) / बिबेक (discernment) / बिभूति (splendor, excellence)
ramacharitamanas::3579.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3579.essence: Sacrifice reveals worth; it does not create it.
ramacharitamanas::3579.simple_meaning: Bharat's refusal of comfort does not make him great; it only reveals the greatness he already had in Ram's eyes. Like the chātak and hansa, he is praised for a natural excellence.
ramacharitamanas::3579.simple_insight: You can stop trying to prove your worth through dramatic sacrifice.
ramacharitamanas::3579.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat has already rejected royal comfort and chosen Ram over the throne. Tulsidas now says that this choice does not make Bharat great; it simply shows the love and discernment he already possessed.
ramacharitamanas::3579.modern_relevance: You decline the promotion, stay late to help, and quietly give up your own comfort — but the deepest value was never in the visible sacrifice. It was in the character that made that choice possible.
ramacharitamanas::3579.insight: It shifts the mind from performing goodness to recognising the inner quality that makes selfless action natural.

ramacharitamanas::3580.verse_sanskrit: देह दिनहुँ दिन दूबरि होई। घटइ तेजु बलु मुखछबि सोई॥ नित नव राम प्रेम पनु पीना। बढ़त धरम दलु मनु न मलीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3580.verse_hindi: भरतजी का शरीर दिनों-दिन दुबला होता जाता है। तेज (अन्न, घृत आदि से उत्पन्न होने वाला मेद) घट रहा है। बल और मुख छबि (मुख की कान्ति अथवा शोभा) वैसी ही बनी हुई है। राम प्रेम का प्रण नित्य नया और पुष्ट होता है, धर्म का दल बढ़ता है और मन उदास नहीं है (अर्थात प्रसन्न है) ॥ संस्कृत कोष में 'तेज' का अर्थ मेद मिलता है और यह अर्थ लेने से 'घटइ' के अर्थ में भी किसी प्रकार की खींच-तान नहीं करनी पड़ती।
ramacharitamanas::3580.english_translation: Day by day Bharat's body grows thinner. His vitality and strength decline, yet his face keeps its radiance. His vow of love for Ram grows ever fresh and strong, dharma's force increases, and his mind remains untroubled.
ramacharitamanas::3580.translation_literal: देह (body) / दिनहुँ दिन (day by day) / दूबरि (thin, emaciated) / होई (becomes) । / घटइ (decreases) / तेजु (vital vitality) / बलु (strength) / मुखछबि (face-radiance, facial beauty) / सोई (same, unchanged) ॥ / नित (daily, always) / नव (new, fresh) / राम (Ram) / प्रेम (love) / पनु (vow, pledge) / पीना (strong, deep) ॥ / बढ़त (increasing) / धरम (dharma) / दलु (force, strength) / मनु (mind) / न मलीना (not dark, not troubled) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3580.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3580.essence: A devoted heart can grow stronger even as the body grows weaker.
ramacharitamanas::3580.simple_meaning: Bharat grows leaner, but his love for Ram grows stronger. His strength and beauty remain, his commitment to dharma increases, and his mind stays cheerful.
ramacharitamanas::3580.simple_insight: Real devotion does not drain you inwardly; it can make you steadier even as the body thins.
ramacharitamanas::3580.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat lives away from the throne he refused. Grief and fasting have made his body lean, but his face still shines. Tulsidas shows that Ram-love can deepen even when the body weakens.
ramacharitamanas::3580.modern_relevance: You skip meals for weeks while caring for someone in crisis, yet something in you feels cleaner, steadier, more alive. Bharat shows that sacrifice can thin the body without dimming the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3580.insight: It shifts attention from physical condition to the steadiness of commitment, showing that inner discipline can outlast bodily decline.

ramacharitamanas::3581.verse_sanskrit: जिमि जलु निघटत सरद प्रकासे। बिलसत बेतस बनज बिकासे॥ सम दम संजम नियम उपासा। नखत भरत हिय बिमल अकासा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3581.verse_hindi: जैसे शरद ऋतु के प्रकाश (विकास) से जल घटता है, किन्तु बेंत शोभा पाते हैं और कमल विकसित होते हैं। शम, दम, संयम, नियम और उपवास आदि भरतजी के हृदयरूपी निर्मल आकाश के नक्षत्र (तारागण) हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3581.english_translation: As the autumn light makes the water recede, bamboo shines and lotus blossoms. Calm, self-control, restraint, discipline, and fasting are the stars in Bharat's pure heart-sky.
ramacharitamanas::3581.translation_literal: जिमि (just as) / जलु (water) / निघटत (recedes) / सरद (autumn) / प्रकासे (in light) / बिलसत (shines) / बेतस (bamboo) / बनज (lotus) / बिकासे (blooming) / सम (calmness) / दम (self-control) / संजम (restraint) / नियम (discipline) / उपासा (fasting) / नखत (stars) / भरत (Bharat's) / हिय (heart) / बिमल (pure) / अकासा (sky)
ramacharitamanas::3581.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3581.essence: Restraint can make the heart more radiant, not less.
ramacharitamanas::3581.simple_meaning: Bharat's inner life is so pure that his discipline shines like stars in a clear autumn sky. His restraint doesn't dim him; it makes his character more radiant.
ramacharitamanas::3581.simple_insight: Self-restraint does not shrink you. It can reveal a quieter, brighter kind of dignity.
ramacharitamanas::3581.detailed_meaning: Bharat is living on little and holding himself in strict discipline while Ram is away in exile. Tulsidas compares his mind to a clear autumn sky, where calmness, restraint, and fasting shine like stars.
ramacharitamanas::3581.modern_relevance: You skip the party, eat simply, and keep your routine while everyone else chases noise. Later, people notice your steadiness. What looked like deprivation was quietly polishing you.
ramacharitamanas::3581.insight: It reframes discipline as something that clarifies character instead of merely denying pleasure.

ramacharitamanas::3582.verse_sanskrit: ध्रुव बिस्वासु अवधि राका सी। स्वामि सुरति सुरबीथि बिकासी॥ राम पेम बिधु अचल अदोषा। सहित समाज सोह नित चोखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3582.verse_hindi: विश्वास ही (उस आकाश में) ध्रुव तारा है, चौदह वर्ष की अवधि (का ध्यान) पूर्णिमा के समान है और स्वामी श्री रामजी की सुरति (स्मृति) आकाशगंगा सरीखी प्रकाशित है। राम प्रेम ही अचल (सदा रहने वाला) और कलंकरहित चन्द्रमा है। वह अपने समाज (नक्षत्रों) सहित नित्य सुंदर सुशोभित है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3582.english_translation: Trust is the fixed star in that sky; remembrance of the Lord is the shining Milky Way. Love for Ram is the steady, spotless moon, always lovely with its companion stars.
ramacharitamanas::3582.translation_literal: ध्रुव (fixed star) / बिस्वासु (trust) / अवधि (limit or span) / राका सी (like the full moon) / स्वामि (lord) / सुरति (remembrance) / सुरबीथि (Milky Way) / बिकासी (shining) / राम (Ram) / पेम (love) / बिधु (moon) / अचल (fixed) / अदोषा (spotless) / सहित (together with) / समाज (company or assembly) / सोह (is beautiful) / नित (always) / चोखा (pure, lovely)
ramacharitamanas::3582.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3582.essence: Trust and love for Ram become the sky that holds everything in place.
ramacharitamanas::3582.simple_meaning: Trust, remembrance of Ram, and love for Ram are compared to stars and the moon in a night sky. They keep a life steady, bright, and beautiful.
ramacharitamanas::3582.simple_insight: Devotion doesn't just comfort you; it gives your life an inner order and glow.
ramacharitamanas::3582.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's life in exile is being measured against the sky itself. His trust is the fixed star, his remembrance of Ram is the glowing river of stars, and his love for Ram is the spotless moon that never wavers.
ramacharitamanas::3582.modern_relevance: You keep checking your phone in the dark, waiting for a message that will settle your heart. This verse says something steadier can hold you: trust, remembrance, and love that do not flicker.
ramacharitamanas::3582.insight: It shifts devotion from emotion alone to a stable inner orientation that can guide your whole life.

ramacharitamanas::3583.verse_sanskrit: भरत रहनि समुझनि करतूती। भगति बिरति गुन बिमल बिभूती॥ बरनत सकल सुकबि सकुचाहीं। सेस गनेस गिरा गमु नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3583.verse_hindi: भरतजी की रहनी, समझ, करनी, भक्ति, वैराग्य, निर्मल, गुण और ऐश्वर्य का वर्णन करने में सभी सुकवि सकुचाते हैं, क्योंकि वहाँ (औरों की तो बात ही क्या) स्वयं शेष, गणेश और सरस्वती की भी पहुँच नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3583.english_translation: All good poets hesitate to describe Bharat's way of life, understanding, conduct, devotion, non-attachment, pure virtues, and splendour. Even Shesha, Ganesha, and Saraswati cannot reach the end of it.
ramacharitamanas::3583.translation_literal: भरत (Bharat) / रहनि (way of living) / समुझनि (understanding) / करतूती (conduct, deeds) / भगति (devotion) / बिरति (non-attachment) / गुन (virtues) / बिमल (pure) / बिभूती (splendour, excellences) / बरनत (describing) / सकल (all) / सुकबि (good poets) / सकुचाहीं (hesitate, feel shy) / सेस (Shesha) / गनेस (Ganesha) / गिरा (speech) / गमु (reach) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::3583.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3583.essence: Bharat's devotion is so complete that language itself gives up.
ramacharitamanas::3583.simple_meaning: Bharat's life is so full of devotion, virtue, and non-attachment that even the greatest poets cannot fully describe it.
ramacharitamanas::3583.simple_insight: True devotion can become so complete that words feel too small to hold it.
ramacharitamanas::3583.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat has refused the throne and lives only to serve Ram's sandals. Tulsidas pauses the story to say that Bharat's character is beyond ordinary description: his conduct, understanding, devotion, and renunciation are so pure that even divine speech falls short.
ramacharitamanas::3583.modern_relevance: You watch someone quietly care for a parent, a partner, or a cause for years without asking for credit. Their goodness is hard to summarize because it lives in action, not performance.
ramacharitamanas::3583.insight: It shifts attention from public achievement to the depth of character revealed in selfless service.

ramacharitamanas::3584.verse_sanskrit: नित पूजत प्रभु पाँवरी प्रीति न हृदयँ समाति। मागि मागि आयसु करत राज काज बहु भाँति ॥
ramacharitamanas::3584.verse_hindi: वे नित्य प्रति प्रभु की पादुकाओं का पूजन करते हैं, हृदय में प्रेम समाता नहीं है। पादुकाओं से आज्ञा माँग-माँगकर वे बहुत प्रकार (सब प्रकार के) राज-काज करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3584.english_translation: They keep worshipping the Lord's sandals every day; their hearts cannot contain their love. Asking the sandals for permission again and again, they carry out all royal duties in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::3584.translation_literal: नित (daily) / पूजत (worshipping) / प्रभु (the Lord) / पाँवरी (sandals/feet) / प्रीति (love) / न (not) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / समाति (fits, is contained) / मागि (asking) / मागि (again and again) / आयसु (permission/command) / करत (doing) / राज काज (kingly affairs) / बहु भाँति (in many ways)
ramacharitamanas::3584.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3584.essence: Love makes power kneel and duty become worship.
ramacharitamanas::3584.simple_meaning: Bharat worships Ram's sandals every day because his love is too deep to hold inside. Even while ruling, he acts only after seeking their permission.
ramacharitamanas::3584.simple_insight: Real devotion changes power into service, not possession.
ramacharitamanas::3584.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat rules Ayodhya only as Ram's representative after exile. He keeps Ram's sandals on the throne, worships them daily, and asks their leave before handling state affairs. His love has turned authority into humility.
ramacharitamanas::3584.modern_relevance: You sit in a meeting chair that should have been someone else's, and every decision still feels borrowed. Bharat shows what it means to lead without claiming the seat as yours.
ramacharitamanas::3584.insight: It shifts leadership from self-importance to reverent service under a higher claim.

ramacharitamanas::3585.verse_sanskrit: पुलक गात हियँ सिय रघुबीरू। जीह नामु जप लोचन नीरू॥ लखन राम सिय कानन बसहीं। भरतु भवन बसि तप तनु कसहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3585.verse_hindi: शरीर पुलकित है, हृदय में श्री सीता-रामजी हैं। जीभ राम नाम जप रही है, नेत्रों में प्रेम का जल भरा है। लक्ष्मणजी, श्री रामजी और सीताजी तो वन में बसते हैं, परन्तु भरतजी घर ही में रहकर तप के द्वारा शरीर को कस रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3585.english_translation: The body trembles with love; Sita and Ram live in the heart. The tongue repeats Ram's name; the eyes overflow with tears. Lakshman, Ram, and Sita live in the forest, but Bharat lives at home and burns his body with austerity.
ramacharitamanas::3585.translation_literal: पुलक (horripilation) / गात (body) / हियँ (in the heart) / सिय (Sita) / रघुबीरू (Ram) / जीह (tongue) / नामु (name) / जप (recites) / लोचन (eyes) / नीरू (water-tears) / लखन (Lakshman) / राम (Ram) / सिय (Sita) / कानन (forest) / बसहीं (live) / भरतु (Bharat) / भवन (house) / बसि (living) / तप (austerity) / तनु (body) / कसहीं (tightens/burns)
ramacharitamanas::3585.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3585.essence: True devotion makes even home feel like exile.
ramacharitamanas::3585.simple_meaning: Bharat's devotion is so intense that his body, speech, and tears all show it. Though he remains in the palace, he lives like an ascetic because his heart is with Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3585.simple_insight: Love can be so complete that even staying still feels like spiritual discipline.
ramacharitamanas::3585.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, the poet pauses over Bharat's condition after Ram's exile. Ram, Sita, and Lakshman live in the forest, but Bharat lives in Ayodhya and still burns with separation, devotion, and restraint. His inner life has become its own austerity.
ramacharitamanas::3585.modern_relevance: You keep your phone on silent at a family wedding because your mind is elsewhere, tied to someone you miss. Bharat knows that kind of divided presence — except his longing has become devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3585.insight: It shifts attention from outward location to inward attachment: where your heart lives matters more than where your body stands.

ramacharitamanas::3586.verse_sanskrit: दोउ दिसि समुझि कहत सबु लोगू। सब बिधि भरत सराहन जोगू॥ सुनि ब्रत नेम साधु सकुचाहीं। देखि दसा मुनिराज लजाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3586.verse_hindi: दोनों ओर की स्थिति समझकर सब लोग कहते हैं कि भरतजी सब प्रकार से सराहने योग्य हैं। उनके व्रत और नियमों को सुनकर साधु-संत भी सकुचा जाते हैं और उनकी स्थिति देखकर मुनिराज भी लज्जित होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3586.english_translation: Everyone, seeing both sides, says that Bharat is worthy of praise in every way. Hearing of his vows and restraints, even holy people grow modest, and seeing his condition, even great sages feel humbled.
ramacharitamanas::3586.translation_literal: दोउ दिसि (both sides) / समुझि (understanding) / कहत (say) / सबु लोगू (all people) / सब बिधि (in every way) / भरत (Bharat) / सराहन जोगू (worthy of praise) ॥ / सुनि (hearing) / ब्रत (vows) / नेम (restraints) / साधु (holy people) / सकुचाहीं (feel modest) / देखि (seeing) / दसा (condition) / मुनिराज (great sages) / लजाहीं (feel humbled) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3586.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3586.essence: Restraint so complete can make even the wise feel small.
ramacharitamanas::3586.simple_meaning: Everyone sees Bharat as worthy of praise. His vows and self-restraint are so deep that even saints and sages feel humbled before him.
ramacharitamanas::3586.simple_insight: Real self-mastery quietly changes the room. It does not demand admiration; it creates it.
ramacharitamanas::3586.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhya, Bharat is living like a renunciant while ruling only through Ram's sandals. People look at his vows, discipline, and humility and feel awed. This verse pauses the story to show how completely he has transformed grief into restraint.
ramacharitamanas::3586.modern_relevance: You keep your promise when no one is watching, and later people sense it without being told. A calm, disciplined life can make others feel their own noise.
ramacharitamanas::3586.insight: It shifts attention from public success to the quiet authority of disciplined conduct.

ramacharitamanas::3587.verse_sanskrit: परम पुनीत भरत आचरनू। मधुर मंजु मुद मंगल कhरनू॥ हरन कठिन कलि कलुष कलेसू। महामोह निसि दलन दिनेसू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3587.verse_hindi: भरतजी का परम पवित्र आचरण (चरित्र) मधुर, सुंदर और आनंद-मंगलों का करने वाला है। कलियुग के कठिन पापों और क्लेशों को हरने वाला है। महामोह रूपी रात्रि को नष्ट करने के लिए सूर्य के समान है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3587.english_translation: Bharat's conduct is supremely pure, sweet, beautiful, and a maker of auspicious joy. It removes the harsh stains and suffering of Kali Yuga and is like the sun that drives away the night of great delusion.
ramacharitamanas::3587.translation_literal: परम पुनीत (supremely pure) / भरत (Bharat) / आचरनू (conduct) / मधुर (sweet) / मंजु (beautiful) / मुद (joy) / मंगल (auspiciousness) / कhरनू (maker) ॥ / हरन (removing) / कठिन (harsh) / कलि (Kali Yuga) / कलुष (stains) / कलेसू (suffering) ॥ / महामोह (great delusion) / निसि (night) / दलन (destroying) / दिनेसू (sun) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3587.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3587.essence: Bharat's purity becomes a light that drives out confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3587.simple_meaning: Bharat's way of living is pure, sweet, and deeply uplifting. It removes suffering and confusion, like sunlight ending night.
ramacharitamanas::3587.simple_insight: A life of integrity can quiet the mind around you and bring relief where confusion once ruled.
ramacharitamanas::3587.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Bharat's renunciation has become a public standard. Tulsidas praises his conduct as gentle, purifying, and powerful enough to drive away the darkness of delusion, showing why the whole gathering sees him as exemplary.
ramacharitamanas::3587.modern_relevance: You watch someone stay honest in a room full of compromise, and the atmosphere changes. Their steadiness doesn't just help them — it makes everyone else breathe easier.
ramacharitamanas::3587.insight: It shifts attention from loud success to the quiet power of lived integrity.

ramacharitamanas::3588.verse_sanskrit: पाप पुंज कुंजर मृगराजू। समन सकल संताप समाजू॥ जन रंजन भंजन भव भारू। राम सनेह सुधाकर सारू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3588.verse_hindi: पाप समूह रूपी हाथी के लिए सिंह है। सारे संतापों के दल का नाश करने वाला है। भक्तों को आनंद देने वाला और भव के भार (संसार के दुःख) का भंजन करने वाला तथा श्री राम प्रेम रूपी चन्द्रमा का सार (अमृत) है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3588.english_translation: The lion that destroys the elephant of accumulated sin, the remover of all suffering, the delight of devotees, the breaker of the burden of worldly existence, is the essence of the moon of Ram's love.
ramacharitamanas::3588.translation_literal: पाप पुंज (heap of sin) / कुंजर (elephant) / मृगराजू (lion-king) / समन (remover) / सकल (all) / संताप (suffering) / समाजू (group) / जन (people/devotees) / रंजन (delight-giver) / भंजन (breaker) / भव (worldly existence) / भारू (burden) / राम (Ram) / सनेह (love) / सुधाकर (moon) / सारू (essence)
ramacharitamanas::3588.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3588.essence: Ram's love is both fierce protection and deep relief.
ramacharitamanas::3588.simple_meaning: Ram's love is compared to a lion that destroys the elephant of sin, removes all suffering, delights devotees, and breaks the burden of worldly life.
ramacharitamanas::3588.simple_insight: You do not have to carry everything alone; devotion can feel like relief, strength, and sweetness at once.
ramacharitamanas::3588.detailed_meaning: In Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas pauses on Bharat's rare greatness and names the force behind it: love for Ram. That love is described as fierce enough to destroy corruption, tender enough to delight the heart, and powerful enough to lift the weight of worldly life.
ramacharitamanas::3588.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone in the hospital waiting room, exhausted by worry and unable to fix anything. The mind softens when love is stronger than panic; that is the kind of relief this verse offers.
ramacharitamanas::3588.insight: It shifts devotion from sentiment to power: love for Ram becomes the force that clears suffering and steadies the heart.

ramacharitamanas::3589.verse_sanskrit: सिय राम प्रेम पियूष पूरन होत जनमु न भरत को। मुनि मन अगम जम नियम सम दम बिषम ब्रत आचरत को॥ दुख दाह दारिद दंभ दूषन सुजस मिस अपहरत को। कलिकाल तुलसी से सठन्हि हठि राम सनमुख करत को॥
ramacharitamanas::3589.verse_hindi: श्री सीतारामजी के प्रेमरूपी अमृत से परिपूर्ण भरतजी का जन्म यदि न होता, तो मुनियों के मन को भी अगम यम, नियम, शम, दम आदि कठिन व्रतों का आचरण कौन करता? दुःख, संताप, दरिद्रता, दम्भ आदि दोषों को अपने सुयश के बहाने कौन हरण करता? तथा कलिकाल में तुलसीदास जैसे शठों को हठपूर्वक कौन श्री रामजी के सम्मुख करता?
ramacharitamanas::3589.english_translation: If Bharat had not been born, full of the nectar of love for Siya and Ram, who would practice the hard vows of yama, niyama, shama, dama, and the rest that even sages find hard to keep? Who would remove sorrow, burning pain, poverty, pride, and other faults under the pretext of his good fame? And in Kali Yuga, who would stubbornly turn stubborn people like Tulsidas toward Ram?
ramacharitamanas::3589.translation_literal: सिय राम (Sita and Ram) / प्रेम (love) / पियूष (nectar) / पूरन (full) / होत (being) / जनमु (birth) / न (not) / भरत को (of Bharat) / मुनि (sages) / मन (mind) / अगम (hard to reach) / जम (restraint) / नियम (discipline) / सम (peace) / दम (self-control) / बिषम (difficult) / ब्रत (vows) / आचरत (practicing) / को (who)॥ / दुख (sorrow) / दाह (burning pain) / दारिद (poverty) / दंभ (pride) / दूषन (faults) / सुजस (good fame) / मिस (as a pretext) / अपहरत (removing) / को (who)॥ / कलिकाल (Kali Yuga) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / से (like) / सठन्हि (stubborn fools) / हठि (stubbornly) / राम (Ram) / सनमुख (facing) / करत (making) / को (who)॥
ramacharitamanas::3589.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3589.essence: Bharat's love turns devotion into discipline for everyone around him.
ramacharitamanas::3589.simple_meaning: Bharat's love for Ram becomes a living example that inspires hard self-discipline, removes faults, and even turns stubborn people toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3589.simple_insight: Love can reshape a person so deeply that even discipline feels natural.
ramacharitamanas::3589.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Bharat at the height of Ayodhyakand's grief. Bharat's devotion is not private sentiment; it becomes a force that models restraint, heals weakness, and pulls even stubborn hearts toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3589.modern_relevance: You watch someone keep a painful promise with quiet dignity, and it changes the room. Their loyalty makes self-control look possible instead of harsh.
ramacharitamanas::3589.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling to transforming force: love becomes the source of conduct, healing, and influence.

ramacharitamanas::3590.verse_sanskrit: भरत चरित करि नेमु तुलसी जो सादर सुनहिं। सीय राम पद पेमु अवसि होइ भव रस बिरति ॥
ramacharitamanas::3590.verse_hindi: तुलसीदासजी कहते हैं- जो कोई भरतजी के चरित्र को नियम से आदरपूर्वक सुनेंगे, उनको अवश्य ही श्रीसीतारामजी के चरणों में प्रेम होगा और सांसारिक विषय रस से वैराग्य होगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3590.english_translation: Tulsidas says: whoever listens to Bharat's character with reverence and discipline will surely develop love for Sita and Ram's feet and grow detached from worldly pleasures.
ramacharitamanas::3590.translation_literal: भरत चरित (Bharat's character) / करि (doing) / नेमु (with discipline, with reverence) / तुलसी (Tulsidas) / जो (who) / सादर (respectfully) / सुनहिं (listen) / सीय राम (Sita and Ram) / पद (feet) / पेमु (love) / अवसि (surely) / होइ (comes to be) / भव रस (worldly flavour, worldly enjoyment) / बिरति (detachment)
ramacharitamanas::3590.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3590.essence: Bharat's example turns respect into love and loosens attachment to pleasure.
ramacharitamanas::3590.simple_meaning: Careful, respectful listening to Bharat's life awakens love for Ram and weakens attachment to worldly pleasures.
ramacharitamanas::3590.simple_insight: What you repeatedly honour shapes what your heart starts to love.
ramacharitamanas::3590.detailed_meaning: At the end of Ayodhyakand, Tulsidas turns Bharat's life into a spiritual mirror. After all the grief, exile, and sacrifice, he says Bharat's character should be heard with reverence because it naturally awakens love for Sita and Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3590.modern_relevance: You hear a story about someone who gave up power for love, and it quietly changes what you admire. That kind of admiration can make ambition feel smaller and devotion feel real.
ramacharitamanas::3590.insight: It shifts attention from consuming stories for entertainment to receiving them as training for the heart.

ramacharitamanas::3591.verse_sanskrit: मूलं धर्मतरोर्विवेकजलधेः पूर्णेन्दुमानन्ददं वैराग्याम्बुजभास्करं ह्यघघनध्वान्तापहं तापहम् । मोहाम्भोधरपूगपाटनविधौ स्वःसम्भवं शंकरं वंदे ब्रह्मकुलं कलंकशमनं श्री रामभूपप्रियम् ॥
ramacharitamanas::3591.verse_hindi: धर्म रूपी वृक्ष के मूल, विवेक रूपी समुद्र को आनंद देने वाले पूर्णचन्द्र, वैराग्य रूपी कमल के (विकसित करने वाले) सूर्य, पाप रूपी घोर अंधकार को निश्चय ही मिटाने वाले, तीनों तापों को हरने वाले, मोह रूपी बादलों के समूह को छिन्न-भिन्न करने की विधि (क्रिया) में आकाश से उत्पन्न पवन स्वरूप, ब्रह्माजी के वंशज (आत्मज) तथा कलंकनाशक, महाराज श्री रामचन्द्रजी के प्रिय श्री शंकरजी की मैं वंदना करता हूँ ॥
