ramacharitamanas::3591.english_translation: I bow to Shankar, born of the sky, destroyer of stain, beloved of Sri Ram, who is the root of the tree of dharma, the moon that delights discernment, the sun that makes non-attachment bloom, the remover of the thick darkness of delusion, and the one who burns away all suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3591.translation_literal: मूलं (root) / धर्मतरोः (of the tree of dharma) / विवेकजलधेः (of the ocean of discernment) / पूर्णेन्दुम् (full moon) / आनन्ददं (giving joy) / वैराग्याम्बुजभास्करं (sun for the lotus of non-attachment) / हि (indeed) / अघघनध्वान्तापहं (remover of the dense darkness of stain) / तापहम् (remover of suffering) / मोहाम्भोधरपूगपाटनविधौ (in the act of splitting the mass of clouds of delusion) / स्वःसम्भवम् (born of the sky) / शंकरम् (Shankar) / वंदे (I bow) / ब्रह्मकुलम् (of Brahma's line) / कलंकशमनम् (pacifier of stain) / श्रीरामभूपप्रियम् (beloved of Sri Ram, king of kings)
ramacharitamanas::3591.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3591.essence: Shiva is praised as the force that clears confusion and awakens release.
ramacharitamanas::3591.simple_meaning: Tulsidas praises Shiva as the source of dharma, clarity, non-attachment, and relief from suffering. He bows to Shiva as Ram's beloved and as the one who destroys delusion.
ramacharitamanas::3591.simple_insight: Reverence can steady the mind, clear confusion, and make detachment feel alive instead of cold.
ramacharitamanas::3591.detailed_meaning: At the start of Aranyakand, Tulsidas pauses the story to praise Shiva before the forest trials begin. He presents Shiva as Ram's beloved, but also as the power that supports dharma, clears confusion, and helps the heart release attachment.
ramacharitamanas::3591.modern_relevance: You are spiraling after bad news, and everything feels foggy. This verse points to the kind of reverence that can cut through mental noise and restore your footing.
ramacharitamanas::3591.insight: It shifts the mind from emotional fog to steadier seeing through devotion and praise.

ramacharitamanas::3592.verse_sanskrit: सान्द्रानन्दपयोदसौभगतनुं पीताम्बरं सुंदरं पाणौ बाणशरासनं कटिलसत्तूणीरभारं वरम् । राजीवायतलोचनं धृतजटाजूटेन संशोभितं सीतालक्ष्मणसंयुतं पथिगतं रामाभिरामं भजे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3592.verse_hindi: जिनका शरीर जलयुक्त मेघों के समान सुंदर (श्यामवर्ण) एवं आनंदघन है, जो सुंदर (वल्कल का) पीत वस्त्र धारण किए हैं, जिनके हाथों में बाण और धनुष हैं, कमर उत्तम तरकस के भार से सुशोभित है, कमल के समान विशाल नेत्र हैं और मस्तक पर जटाजूट धारण किए हैं, उन अत्यन्त शोभायमान श्री सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित मार्ग में चलते हुए आनंद देने वाले श्री रामचन्द्रजी को मैं भजता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3592.english_translation: I worship Ramchandra, radiant and blissful, beautiful in yellow garments, with bow, arrows, and quiver in hand, eyes wide like lotus petals, hair in a matted crown, walking the path with Sita and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::3592.translation_literal: सान्द्रानन्दपयोदसौभगतनुं (whose body is like a dense cloud of bliss and beauty) / पीताम्बरं (yellow-clad) / सुंदरं (beautiful) / पाणौ (in the hand) / बाणशरासनं (arrow and bow) / कटिलसत्तूणीरभारं (with the fine weight of the quiver at the waist) / वरम् (excellent) / राजीवायतलोचनं (lotus-wide-eyed) / धृतजटाजूटेन (with a matted crown held) / संशोभितं (adorned) / सीतालक्ष्मणसंयुतं (joined with Sita and Lakshman) / पथिगतं (walking the path) / रामाभिरामं (delightful Ram) / भजे (I worship)
ramacharitamanas::3592.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3592.essence: Ram is most beautiful when he walks the hard road with his loved ones.
ramacharitamanas::3592.simple_meaning: The speaker offers a devotional praise of Ram: beautiful, armed, radiant, and walking with Sita and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::3592.simple_insight: Devotion can make even a journey feel like being held in grace.
ramacharitamanas::3592.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram is no longer a palace king but a traveler with Sita and Lakshman. Tulsidas pauses the story to worship his beauty, courage, and steady presence on the path.
ramacharitamanas::3592.modern_relevance: You’re walking through a hard season with two people depending on you, and you still choose dignity, steadiness, and tenderness. That is the image this verse holds up.
ramacharitamanas::3592.insight: It turns attention from Ram's royal status to his living presence beside those who love him.

ramacharitamanas::3593.verse_sanskrit: उमा राम गुन गूढ़ पंडित मुनि पावहिं बिरति। पावहिं मोह बिमूढ़ जे हरि बिमुख न धर्म रति॥
ramacharitamanas::3593.verse_hindi: हे पार्वती! श्री रामजी के गुण गूढ़ हैं, पण्डित और मुनि उन्हें समझकर वैराग्य प्राप्त करते हैं, परन्तु जो भगवान से विमुख हैं और जिनका धर्म में प्रेम नहीं है, वे महामूढ़ (उन्हें सुनकर) मोह को प्राप्त होते हैं।
ramacharitamanas::3593.english_translation: O Parvati, Ram's qualities are profound. Learned sages gain detachment by understanding them, but those who turn away from Hari and feel no love for dharma fall into delusion.
ramacharitamanas::3593.translation_literal: उमा (O Parvati) / राम (Ram) / गुन (qualities) / गूढ़ (deep, hidden) / पंडित (learned) / मुनि (sages) / पावहिं (attain) / बिरति (detachment) / पावहिं (attain) / मोह (delusion) / बिमूढ़ (utterly confused) / जे (those who) / हरि (Hari) / बिमुख (turned away) / न (not) / धर्म (dharma) / रति (love, attachment)
ramacharitamanas::3593.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3593.essence: Ram's nature frees the receptive mind and entangles the resistant one.
ramacharitamanas::3593.simple_meaning: Ram's qualities are so deep that wise people become less attached by reflecting on them. But people who turn away from him and dislike dharma become lost in confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3593.simple_insight: What you focus on shapes your mind: devotion clears, while resistance clouds.
ramacharitamanas::3593.detailed_meaning: Shiva speaks to Parvati in the forest teaching. He pauses the story to explain why Ram's nature matters: the wise grow freer by understanding him, but the stubborn become more confused when they reject him.
ramacharitamanas::3593.modern_relevance: You can sit with a wise teacher's words and feel calmer, or scroll past them in irritation and end up more tangled than before. What you lean toward changes what your mind becomes.
ramacharitamanas::3593.insight: It shifts attention from mere hearing to the inner result of how you receive truth.

ramacharitamanas::3594.verse_sanskrit: पुर नर भरत प्रीति मैं गाई। मति अनुरूप अनूप सुहाई॥ अब प्रभु चरित सुनहु अति पावन। करत जे बन सुर नर मुनि भावन ॥
ramacharitamanas::3594.verse_hindi: पुरवासियों के और भरतजी के अनुपम और सुंदर प्रेम का मैंने अपनी बुद्धि के अनुसार गान किया। अब देवता, मनुष्य और मुनियों के मन को भाने वाले प्रभु श्री रामचन्द्रजी के वे अत्यन्त पवित्र चरित्र सुनो, जिन्हें वे वन में कर रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3594.english_translation: I have sung, according to my understanding, the incomparable and lovely love of the people of the city and of Bharat. Now listen to the supremely pure deeds of Lord Ram, which delight gods, humans, and sages, as he lives in the forest.
ramacharitamanas::3594.translation_literal: पुर नर (the people of the city) / भरत (Bharat) / प्रीति (love) / मैं (I) / गाई (sang) / मति (understanding) / अनुरूप (according to) / अनूप (incomparable) / सुहाई (lovely) / अब (now) / प्रभु (Lord) / चरित (deeds, story) / सुनहु (listen) / अति (very) / पावन (pure) / करत (doing) / जे (which) / बन (forest) / सुर (gods) / नर (humans) / मुनि (sages) / भावन (delightful, pleasing)
ramacharitamanas::3594.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3594.essence: Praise gives way to the deeds that make devotion visible.
ramacharitamanas::3594.simple_meaning: The poet closes one part of the story and invites you into Ram's pure forest deeds, which please every kind of being.
ramacharitamanas::3594.simple_insight: Some stories don't just inform you — they clear the heart before the next truth arrives.
ramacharitamanas::3594.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas has just praised the love of Ayodhya's people and Bharat. He now turns the reader toward Ram in the forest, shifting from human devotion to the sacred action that will unfold there. This line opens the next movement of the story.
ramacharitamanas::3594.modern_relevance: You finish speaking about the people who stood by you, then turn to the harder part: what you must do next, quietly and purely, without applause.
ramacharitamanas::3594.insight: It shifts the focus from praise of supporters to the living example of Ram's conduct in exile.

ramacharitamanas::3595.verse_sanskrit: एक बार चुनि कुसुम सुहाए। निज कर भूषन राम बनाए॥ सीतहि पहिराए प्रभु सादर। बैठे फटिक सिला पर सुंदर ॥
ramacharitamanas::3595.verse_hindi: एक बार सुंदर फूल चुनकर श्री रामजी ने अपने हाथों से भाँति-भाँति के गहने बनाए और सुंदर स्फटिक शिला पर बैठे हुए प्रभु ने आदर के साथ वे गहने श्री सीताजी को पहनाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3595.english_translation: Once, choosing lovely flowers, Lord Ram made ornaments with his own hands. Sitting beautifully on a crystal rock, the Lord respectfully put those ornaments on Sita.
ramacharitamanas::3595.translation_literal: एक बार (once) / चुनि (choosing) / कुसुम (flowers) / सुहाए (beautiful) / निज (own) / कर (hands) / भूषन (ornaments) / राम (Ram) / बनाए (made) / सीतहि (to Sita) / पहिराए (put on) / प्रभु (Lord) / सादर (respectfully) / बैठे (sat) / फटिक (crystal) / सिला (rock/slab) / पर (on) / सुंदर (beautiful)
ramacharitamanas::3595.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3595.essence: True love adorns the beloved with its own hands.
ramacharitamanas::3595.simple_meaning: Ram lovingly makes ornaments from flowers and places them on Sita himself, showing care, respect, and tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::3595.simple_insight: Love becomes most beautiful when it serves with its own hands.
ramacharitamanas::3595.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram and Sita are living far from palace comfort. Ram gathers flowers, makes ornaments by hand, and gently adorns Sita while seated on a crystal rock. The scene shows their intimate, graceful love before the story turns toward danger.
ramacharitamanas::3595.modern_relevance: You notice someone you love is tired, so you make tea, fix their collar, and quietly help before they ask. Small care can carry the deepest devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3595.insight: It shifts love from grand words to humble, visible care.

ramacharitamanas::3596.verse_sanskrit: सुरपति सुत धरि बायस बेषा। सठ चाहत रघुपति बल देखा॥ जिमि पिपीलिका सागर थाहा। महा मंदमति पावन चाहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3596.verse_hindi: देवराज इन्द्र का मूर्ख पुत्र जयन्त कौए का रूप धरकर श्री रघुनाथजी का बल देखना चाहता है। जैसे महान मंदबुद्धि चींटी समुद्र का थाह पाना चाहती हो ॥
ramacharitamanas::3596.english_translation: Indra's foolish son took the form of a crow and wanted to test Raghunath's strength. It was like a tiny ant trying to measure the ocean's depth.
ramacharitamanas::3596.translation_literal: सुरपति (of Indra, lord of the radiant beings) / सुत (son) / धरि (taking) / बायस (crow) / बेषा (form) / सठ (foolish one) / चाहत (wants) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / बल (strength) / देखा (to see)॥ / जिमि (like) / पिपीलिका (ant) / सागर (ocean) / थाहा (depth) / महा (great) / मंदमति (slow-minded) / पावन (to measure) / चाहा (wanted)॥
ramacharitamanas::3596.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3596.essence: Ego makes even a tiny challenge look brave.
ramacharitamanas::3596.simple_meaning: A proud fool tries to test Ram's power, but the effort is absurdly out of scale with his own smallness.
ramacharitamanas::3596.simple_insight: Some things are not meant to be tested by ego. Humility sees the size of what it faces.
ramacharitamanas::3596.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a minor divine being disguised as a crow tries to probe Ram's strength. Tulsidas compares that attempt to an ant trying to measure the ocean, setting up the coming act of foolishness and its consequences.
ramacharitamanas::3596.modern_relevance: Someone with almost no context walks into a room and tries to challenge the person who has spent years mastering the field. The mismatch is obvious before anyone speaks.
ramacharitamanas::3596.insight: It warns against testing greatness from a place of arrogance and poor judgment.

ramacharitamanas::3597.verse_sanskrit: सीता चरन चोंच हति भागा। मूढ़ मंदमति कारन कागा॥ चला रुधिर रघुनायक जाना। सींक धनुष सायक संधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3597.verse_hindi: वह मूढ़, मंदबुद्धि कारण से (भगवान के बल की परीक्षा करने के लिए) बना हुआ कौआ सीताजी के चरणों में चोंच मारकर भागा। जब रक्त बह चला, तब श्री रघुनाथजी ने जाना और धनुष पर सींक (सरकंडे) का बाण संधान किया ॥ दोहा :
ramacharitamanas::3597.english_translation: The foolish crow pecked Sita's foot and fled. When blood flowed, Ram noticed and fitted a reed-arrow to his bow.
ramacharitamanas::3597.translation_literal: सीता (Sita's) / चरन (feet) / चोंच (beak) / हति (striking) / भागा (ran away) / मूढ़ (foolish) / मंदमति (slow-witted) / कारन (because of) / कागा (crow) / चला (flowed) / रुधिर (blood) / रघुनायक (Lord of the Raghu clan) / जाना (knew) / सींक (reed) / धनुष (bow) / सायक (arrow) / संधाना (set, fitted)
ramacharitamanas::3597.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3597.essence: Ram turns instantly when suffering touches the one he protects.
ramacharitamanas::3597.simple_meaning: A foolish crow attacks Sita and runs away. The moment blood appears, Ram notices and prepares to shoot.
ramacharitamanas::3597.simple_insight: Even a small wound can awaken swift protection from love.
ramacharitamanas::3597.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Jatayu's son Jayant has taken a crow form to test Ram's strength. He pecks Sita's foot and flees, but the blood gives the moment away. Ram immediately readies his bow, and the scene turns toward divine response.
ramacharitamanas::3597.modern_relevance: Someone you love gets hurt in a careless moment, and your whole body goes alert before you even think. Love notices pain fast.
ramacharitamanas::3597.insight: It shows how quickly Ram responds when innocence is harmed.

ramacharitamanas::3598.verse_sanskrit: अति कृपाल रघुनायक सदा दीन पर नेह। ता सन आइ कीन्ह छलु मूरख अवगुन गेह ॥
ramacharitamanas::3598.verse_hindi: श्री रघुनाथजी, जो अत्यन्त ही कृपालु हैं और जिनका दीनों पर सदा प्रेम रहता है, उनसे भी उस अवगुणों के घर मूर्ख जयन्त ने आकर छल किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3598.english_translation: The gracious Lord of Raghu always loves the humble, yet that fool Jayanta came and tried to deceive him.
ramacharitamanas::3598.translation_literal: अति (very) / कृपाल (gracious) / रघुनायक (Lord of Raghu) / सदा (always) / दीन (humble, needy) / पर (toward) / नेह (love) / ता सन (with him) / आइ (coming) / कीन्ह (did) / छलु (deceit) / मूरख (fool) / अवगुन (faults) / गेह (house)
ramacharitamanas::3598.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3598.essence: Ram’s grace welcomes the humble and unmasks the fool.
ramacharitamanas::3598.simple_meaning: Ram is naturally kind to the humble, but Jayanta still came in disguise and tried to deceive him.
ramacharitamanas::3598.simple_insight: There is safety in humility and foolishness in testing what is already gracious.
ramacharitamanas::3598.detailed_meaning: Jayanta has come as a crow to test Ram’s strength. After pecking Sita and fleeing, he is exposed as a fool who dared to deceive the very Lord who always loves the humble. The verse pauses on Ram’s kindness before the punishment falls.
ramacharitamanas::3598.modern_relevance: You meet someone kind, then still decide to test them with a lie or a game. The verse catches that self-defeating move: grace is not weakness, and deceit only exposes your own fault.
ramacharitamanas::3598.insight: It shifts you from testing goodness to trusting it, and from pride to humility.

ramacharitamanas::3599.verse_sanskrit: प्रेरित मंत्र ब्रह्मसर धावा। चला भाजि बायस भय पावा॥ धरि निज रूप गयउ पितु पाहीं। राम बिमुख राखा तेहि नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3599.verse_hindi: मंत्र से प्रेरित होकर वह ब्रह्मबाण दौड़ा। कौआ भयभीत होकर भाग चला। वह अपना असली रूप धरकर पिता इन्द्र के पास गया, पर श्री रामजी का विरोधी जानकर इन्द्र ने उसको नहीं रखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3599.english_translation: Driven by the mantra, the Brahmastra rushed forward. The crow fled in fear. Taking his true form, he went to his father Indra, but Indra would not shelter one who opposed Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3599.translation_literal: प्रेरित (driven) / मंत्र (mantra) / ब्रह्मसर (Brahmastra) / धावा (rushed) / चला (went) / भाजि (fleeing) / बायस (crow) / भय (fear) / पावा (felt) / धरि (taking) / निज (own) / रूप (form) / गयउ (went) / पितु (father) / पाहीं (to) / राम (Ram) / बिमुख (opposed to) / राखा (kept) / तेहि (that one) / नाहीं (not)
ramacharitamanas::3599.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3599.essence: Opposing Ram leaves even refuge unable to hold you.
ramacharitamanas::3599.simple_meaning: The crow escapes the weapon, returns to his father in his real form, and is rejected for opposing Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3599.simple_insight: Power cannot protect you when your actions place you against what is right.
ramacharitamanas::3599.detailed_meaning: After the crow attacks Sita and Ram sends the Brahmastra, the frightened bird flees and reveals his true form. He turns to Indra for safety, but even his father will not shelter him because he has acted against Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3599.modern_relevance: You try to hide behind status, family, or connections after crossing a line. But when your actions have broken trust, even your strongest support can refuse you.
ramacharitamanas::3599.insight: It shows that wrongdoing strips away protection, no matter how much power or lineage you have.

ramacharitamanas::3600.verse_sanskrit: भा निरास उपजी मन त्रासा। जथा चक्र भय रिषि दुर्बासा॥ ब्रह्मधाम सिवपुर सब लोका। फिरा श्रमित ब्याकुल भय सोका ॥
ramacharitamanas::3600.verse_hindi: तब वह निराश हो गया, उसके मन में भय उत्पन्न हो गया, जैसे दुर्वासा ऋषि को चक्र से भय हुआ था। वह ब्रह्मलोक, शिवलोक आदि समस्त लोकों में थका हुआ और भय-शोक से व्याकुल होकर भागता फिरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3600.english_translation: Then he lost all hope, and fear rose in his mind, just as Durvasa was frightened by the discus. He wandered, exhausted and distressed by fear and sorrow, through Brahmaloka, Shivaloka, and all the worlds.
ramacharitamanas::3600.translation_literal: भा (became) / निरास (hopeless) / उपजी (arose) / मन (mind) / त्रासा (fear) / जथा (like) / चक्र (disc) / भय (fear) / रिषि (sage) / दुर्बासा (Durvasa) / ब्रह्मधाम (Brahmaloka) / सिवपुर (Shivaloka) / सब (all) / लोका (worlds) / फिरा (wandered) / श्रमित (tired) / ब्याकुल (distressed) / भय (fear) / सोका (sorrow)
ramacharitamanas::3600.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3600.essence: Fear keeps running even after the danger has passed.
ramacharitamanas::3600.simple_meaning: The frightened being loses hope and runs through every realm, exhausted and shaken. Fear and sorrow keep driving it onward.
ramacharitamanas::3600.simple_insight: Panic makes even great power feel like nowhere to rest.
ramacharitamanas::3600.detailed_meaning: The scene continues after Jayanta’s failed attack on Ram. Humiliated and terrified, he flees beyond ordinary reach, roaming through higher realms in search of safety. The verse shows how fear strips away pride and leaves only flight.
ramacharitamanas::3600.modern_relevance: You make one mistake, then spend the rest of the day replaying it, checking messages, and imagining worst-case reactions. Fear starts running your whole mind.
ramacharitamanas::3600.insight: It shows how guilt and fear can turn escape into suffering, making the mind restless instead of free.

ramacharitamanas::3601.verse_sanskrit: काहूँ बैठन कहा न ओही। राखि को सकइ राम कर द्रोही ॥ मातु मृत्यु पितु समन समाना। सुधा होइ बिष सुनु हरिजाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3601.verse_hindi: (पर रखना तो दूर रहा) किसी ने उसे बैठने तक के लिए नहीं कहा। श्री रामजी के द्रोही को कौन रख सकता है? (काकभुशुण्डिजी कहते हैं-) है गरुड़ ! सुनिए, उसके लिए माता मृत्यु के समान,
ramacharitamanas::3601.english_translation: No one even offered him a seat. Who can shelter one who is hostile to Ram? Listen, Garuda: for such a person, mother becomes death, father becomes Yama, and nectar turns to poison.
ramacharitamanas::3601.translation_literal: काहूँ (by anyone) / बैठन (for sitting) / कहा (said) / न (not) / ओही (to him) / राखि (to keep) / को (who) / सकइ (can) / राम (Ram) / कर (of) / द्रोही (enemy) ॥ मातु (mother) / मृत्यु (death) / पितु (father) / समन (Yama) / समाना (equal) / सुधा (nectar) / होइ (becomes) / बिष (poison) / सुनु (listen) / हरिजाना (O Garuda, devotee of Hari)
ramacharitamanas::3601.speaker: Kak Bhushundi
ramacharitamanas::3601.essence: Opposition to Ram makes even nourishment feel like harm.
ramacharitamanas::3601.simple_meaning: A person cut off from Ram loses all support and comfort. Even the most loving things in life can feel hostile and painful.
ramacharitamanas::3601.simple_insight: What you resist most can poison even what should nourish you.
ramacharitamanas::3601.detailed_meaning: In the Uttarkand dialogue, Kak Bhushundi warns Garuda about the inner collapse that comes from turning against Ram. Once that break happens, even family, comfort, and sweetness stop feeling safe.
ramacharitamanas::3601.modern_relevance: You can have people around you, food on the table, and a full calendar — yet still feel everything has gone wrong inside. When your heart turns against what is true, even comfort starts to sting.
ramacharitamanas::3601.insight: It shifts attention from outer support to the inner relation that makes support feel alive or dead.

ramacharitamanas::3602.verse_sanskrit: पिता यमराज के समान और अमृत विष के समान हो जाता है ॥ मित्र करइ सत रिपु कै करनी। ता कहँ बिबुधनदी बैतरनी॥ सब जगु ताहि अनलहु ते ताता। जो रघुबीर बिमुख सुनु भ्राता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3602.verse_hindi: मित्र सैकड़ों शत्रुओं की सी करनी करने लगता है। देवनदी गंगाजी उसके लिए वैतरणी (यमपुरी की नदी) हो जाती है। हे भाई! सुनिए, जो श्री रघुनाथजी के विमुख होता है, समस्त जगत उनके लिए अग्नि से भी अधिक गरम (जलाने वाला) हो जाता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3602.english_translation: A father becomes like Yama and nectar turns to poison. A friend acts like a hundred enemies, and the sacred river becomes the river of judgment. O brother, listen: for one who turns away from Raghubir, the whole world burns hotter than fire.
ramacharitamanas::3602.translation_literal: पिता (father) / यमराज (Yama) / के समान (like) / और (and) / अमृत (nectar) / विष (poison) / के समान (like) / हो जाता है (becomes) ॥ / मित्र (friend) / करइ (does) / सत (hundred) / रिपु (enemies) / कै (of) / करनी (action) ॥ / ता कहँ (for that one) / बिबुधनदी (sacred river) / बैतरनी (river of judgment) ॥ / सब (all) / जगु (world) / ताहि (to that one) / अनलहु (fire even) / ते (than) / ताता (hotter) ॥ / जो (who) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / बिमुख (turned away) / सुनु (listen) / भ्राता (brother) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3602.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3602.essence: Turning away from Ram makes even blessings feel hostile.
ramacharitamanas::3602.simple_meaning: Turning away from Ram distorts everything. What should help you can feel harmful, and even the world itself becomes unbearable.
ramacharitamanas::3602.simple_insight: Separation from what is highest makes even blessings feel painful.
ramacharitamanas::3602.detailed_meaning: Kak Bhushundi is warning Garuda in the Uttarkand frame, but the lesson reaches beyond the story. When a being turns away from Ram, the whole order of experience changes: friends feel like enemies, nectar feels poisonous, and even sacred places lose their comfort.
ramacharitamanas::3602.modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the praise, the perfect meal — and still feel strangely hollow. When your center is off, even good things lose their sweetness.
ramacharitamanas::3602.insight: It shifts attention from outer comforts to the direction of your heart.

ramacharitamanas::3603.verse_sanskrit: नारद देखा बिकल जयंता। लगि दया कोमल चित संता॥ पठवा तुरत राम पहिं ताही। कहेसि पुकारि प्रनत हित पाही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3603.verse_hindi: नारदजी ने जयन्त को व्याकुल देखा तो उन्हें दया आ गई, क्योंकि संतों का चित्त बड़ा कोमल होता है। उन्होंने उसे (समझाकर) तुरंत श्री रामजी के पास भेज दिया। उसने (जाकर) पुकारकर कहा- हे शरणागत के हितकारी! मेरी रक्षा कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3603.english_translation: Narada saw Jayaanta in distress and felt compassion, for the hearts of saints are tender. He sent him at once to Ram, and Jayaanta cried out, 'O protector of the surrendered, save me.'
ramacharitamanas::3603.translation_literal: नारद (Narada) / देखा (saw) / बिकल (distressed) / जयंता (Jayaanta) / लगि (arose) / दया (compassion) / कोमल (soft) / चित (heart-mind) / संता (of saints)॥ / पठवा (sent) / तुरत (immediately) / राम पहिं (to Ram) / ताही (him) / कहेसि (said) / पुकारि (calling out) / प्रनत हित पाही (protector of the surrendered, receive/save me)॥
ramacharitamanas::3603.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3603.essence: Compassion sends the frightened straight to refuge.
ramacharitamanas::3603.simple_meaning: Narada sees Jayaanta in distress, feels compassion, and sends him straight to Ram, who protects the surrendered.
ramacharitamanas::3603.simple_insight: A gentle heart does not turn away from fear; it moves toward relief.
ramacharitamanas::3603.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Narada sees Jayaanta shaken and afraid. He does not exploit the moment or punish him further. Instead, his saintly compassion sends the frightened being straight to Ram, the refuge of those who surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3603.modern_relevance: You notice a friend spiraling after a mistake and resist the urge to lecture. You calm them, point them toward help, and let mercy do what shame never could.
ramacharitamanas::3603.insight: It shifts your response from judgment to rescue, making compassion an action rather than a feeling.

ramacharitamanas::3604.verse_sanskrit: आतुर सभय गहेसि पद जाई। त्राहि त्राहि दयाल रघुराई॥ अतुलित बल अतुलित प्रभुताई। मैं मतिमंद जानि नहीं पाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3604.verse_hindi: आतुर और भयभीत जयन्त ने जाकर श्री रामजी के चरण पकड़ लिए (और कहा-) हे दयालु रघुनाथजी! रक्षा कीजिए, रक्षा कीजिए। आपके अतुलित बल और आपकी अतुलित प्रभुता (सामर्थ्य) को मैं मन्दबुद्धि जान नहीं पाया था ॥
ramacharitamanas::3604.english_translation: Distressed and frightened, Jayaanta fell at Ram's feet and cried, 'Save me, save me, merciful Raghurai! I did not understand your immeasurable strength and immeasurable majesty, foolish as I was.'
ramacharitamanas::3604.translation_literal: आतुर (distressed) / सभय (frightened) / गहेसि (he grasped) / पद (feet) / जाई (going) / त्राहि त्राहि (save, save) / दयाल (merciful) / रघुराई (Raghurai) / अतुलित (immeasurable) / बल (strength) / अतुलित (immeasurable) / प्रभुताई (majesty, lordship) / मैं (I) / मतिमंद (foolish, dull-witted) / जानि (knowing) / नहीं (not) / पाई (understood)
ramacharitamanas::3604.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3604.essence: Fear dissolves when pride gives way to Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::3604.simple_meaning: Jayaanta, shaken and afraid, falls at Ram's feet and asks for protection. He admits he failed to understand Ram's power and greatness.
ramacharitamanas::3604.simple_insight: There is relief in admitting you were wrong and asking for help.
ramacharitamanas::3604.detailed_meaning: After Narad sends Jayaanta to Ram, the frightened figure reaches the Lord and drops at his feet. In that moment, fear becomes humility, and the verse turns toward full surrender before Ram's unmatched power.
ramacharitamanas::3604.modern_relevance: After a harsh mistake, you walk into the room with your head down and finally say, 'I was wrong. Please help me fix this.' That honesty changes everything.
ramacharitamanas::3604.insight: It shifts the mind from self-protection to surrender, making room for grace and correction.

ramacharitamanas::3605.verse_sanskrit: निज कृत कर्म जनित फल पायउँ। अब प्रभु पाहि सरन तकि आयउँ॥ सुनि कृपाल अति आरत बानी। एकनयन करि तजा भवानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3605.verse_hindi: अपने कर्म से उत्पन्न हुआ फल मैंने पा लिया। अब हे प्रभु! मेरी रक्षा कीजिए। मैं आपकी शरण तक कर आया हूँ। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे पार्वती! कृपालु श्री रघुनाथजी ने उसकी अत्यंत आर्त्त (दुःख भरी) वाणी सुनकर उसे एक आँख का काना करके छोड़ दिया ॥ सोरठा :
ramacharitamanas::3605.english_translation: I have received the fruit born of my own actions. Now, Lord, protect me; I have come to your refuge. Hearing his deeply distressed plea, the compassionate Raghunath spared him, leaving him one-eyed, O Parvati.
ramacharitamanas::3605.translation_literal: निज (own) / कृत (done) / कर्म (action) / जनित (born) / फल (fruit) / पायउँ (I received) / अब (now) / प्रभु (Lord) / पाहि (protect) / सरन (refuge) / तकि (seeking) / आयउँ (I came) / सुनि (hearing) / कृपाल (compassionate) / अति (very) / आरत (distressed) / बानी (speech) / एकनयन (one-eyed) / करि (making) / तजा (left/spared) / भवानी (Parvati)
ramacharitamanas::3605.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3605.essence: Taking responsibility opens the door to mercy.
ramacharitamanas::3605.simple_meaning: Jayanta admits he has received the result of his own wrongdoing and asks Ram for protection. Ram hears his desperate plea and shows mercy instead of killing him.
ramacharitamanas::3605.simple_insight: Even after a mistake, honest surrender can open the door to mercy.
ramacharitamanas::3605.detailed_meaning: Jayanta, frightened after his offense, falls before Ram and accepts that the pain he faces comes from his own act. In front of Parvati, Shiva describes how Ram responds not with anger but with compassion, sparing the repentant offender.
ramacharitamanas::3605.modern_relevance: You finally admit the mess was partly yours, not just everyone else's. The moment you stop defending yourself and ask for help, the room changes.
ramacharitamanas::3605.insight: It teaches you to stop self-justifying, accept responsibility, and move toward humble surrender instead of pride.

ramacharitamanas::3606.verse_sanskrit: कीन्ह मोह बस द्रोह जद्यपि तेहि कर बध उचित। प्रभु छाड़ेउ करि छोह को कृपाल रघुबीर सम ॥
ramacharitamanas::3606.verse_hindi: उसने मोहवश द्रोह किया था, इसलिए यद्यपि उसका वध ही उचित था, पर प्रभु ने कृपा करके उसे छोड़ दिया। श्री रामजी के समान कृपालु और कौन होगा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3606.english_translation: He acted out of delusion and committed hostility, so his death was deserved; yet the Lord, full of compassion, spared him. Who is as merciful as Raghubir?
ramacharitamanas::3606.translation_literal: कीन्ह (did) / मोह बस (under the sway of delusion) / द्रोह (hostility, betrayal) / जद्यपि (although) / तेहि (for him) / कर बध (death) / उचित (appropriate) / प्रभु (the Lord) / छाड़ेउ (released, spared) / करि (doing) / छोह (compassion) / को (who) / कृपाल (compassionate) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / सम (like)
ramacharitamanas::3606.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3606.essence: Compassion can overrule what punishment demands.
ramacharitamanas::3606.simple_meaning: Even when someone has done wrong and deserves punishment, Ram chooses compassion and lets him go.
ramacharitamanas::3606.simple_insight: You can hold justice without losing tenderness.
ramacharitamanas::3606.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a hostile figure has acted from delusion and earned death by ordinary standards. But Ram, seeing through to mercy, chooses to spare him. The verse pauses to praise that compassion as unmatched.
ramacharitamanas::3606.modern_relevance: Someone lies to you, and every part of you wants to cut them off. You may still choose a response that is firm without becoming cruel.
ramacharitamanas::3606.insight: It shifts the mind from automatic retaliation to measured mercy.

ramacharitamanas::3607.verse_sanskrit: रघुपति चित्रकूट बसि नाना। चरित किए श्रुति सुधा समाना॥ बहुरि राम अस मन अनुमाना। होइहि भीर सबहिं मोहि जाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3607.verse_hindi: चित्रकूट में बसकर श्री रघुनाथजी ने बहुत से चरित्र किए, जो कानों को अमृत के समान (प्रिय) हैं। फिर (कुछ समय पश्चात) श्री रामजी ने मन में ऐसा अनुमान किया कि मुझे सब लोग जान गए हैं, इससे (यहाँ) बड़ी भीड़ हो जाएगी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3607.english_translation: Dwelling in Chitrakoot, Lord Raghupati performed many deeds, sweet as nectar to the ears. Then Ram thought in his mind, "Now everyone knows me; there will be a great crowd here."
ramacharitamanas::3607.translation_literal: रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / चित्रकूट (Chitrakoot) / बसि (dwelling) / नाना (many) / चरित (deeds, pastimes) / किए (did) / श्रुति (the ears / the hearing) / सुधा (nectar) / समाना (equal to) / बहुरि (then, again) / राम (Ram) / अस (thus) / मन (mind) / अनुमाना (thought, inferred) / होइहि (will happen) / भीर (crowd) / सबहिं (to everyone) / मोहि (me) / जाना (known)
ramacharitamanas::3607.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3607.essence: True grace sometimes moves away before it becomes a spectacle.
ramacharitamanas::3607.simple_meaning: Ram lived in Chitrakoot and performed many beautiful deeds there. Then he felt that people had come to know him, so the place would soon become crowded.
ramacharitamanas::3607.simple_insight: Even sacred presence can draw attention; sometimes love must move quietly to protect the moment.
ramacharitamanas::3607.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are living in the forest at Chitrakoot, and the place has become filled with tender, memorable moments. Ram notices that his presence is now widely known, so he decides to leave before a crowd gathers and disturbs the life they are living.
ramacharitamanas::3607.modern_relevance: You finally find a quiet café where you can think, and then the room fills with people who recognize you. Sometimes the right move is to leave before attention destroys the calm you came for.
ramacharitamanas::3607.insight: It teaches you to protect a sacred space before popularity turns it into noise.

ramacharitamanas::3608.verse_sanskrit: सकल मुनिन्ह सन बिदा कराई। सीता सहित चले द्वौ भाई॥ अत्रि के आश्रम जब प्रभु गयऊ। सुनत महामुनि हरषित भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3608.verse_hindi: (इसलिए) सब मुनियों से विदा लेकर सीताजी सहित दोनों भाई चले! जब प्रभु अत्रिजी के आश्रम में गए, तो उनका आगमन सुनते ही महामुनि हर्षित हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3608.english_translation: After taking leave of all the sages, the two brothers set out with Sita. When the Lord reached Atri's hermitage, the great sage was delighted on hearing of his arrival.
ramacharitamanas::3608.translation_literal: सकल (all) / मुनिन्ह (sages) / सन (from) / बिदा (farewell) / कराई (caused to be taken) / सीता सहित (with Sita) / चले (departed) / द्वौ (two) / भाई (brothers) ॥ / अत्रि के (of Atri) / आश्रम (hermitage) / जब (when) / प्रभु (the Lord) / गयऊ (went) / सुनत (hearing) / महामुनि (great sage) / हरषित (joyful) / भयऊ (became) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3608.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3608.essence: Their presence itself awakens joy before they even arrive.
ramacharitamanas::3608.simple_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman leave the sages and continue their forest journey. When they reach Atri's hermitage, the sage feels great joy at hearing they have come.
ramacharitamanas::3608.simple_insight: Some arrivals bring instant joy simply because of who is coming.
ramacharitamanas::3608.detailed_meaning: After visiting the sages in the forest, Ram leaves with Sita and Lakshman. The journey brings them to Atri's hermitage, and the old sage is overjoyed even before he sees them. The verse sets up a warm meeting, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3608.modern_relevance: You hear that someone you deeply respect is on the way, and your whole day changes before they even arrive. That quiet happiness is already part of the meeting.
ramacharitamanas::3608.insight: It frames arrival itself as blessing, preparing the emotional warmth of the next encounter.

ramacharitamanas::3609.verse_sanskrit: पुलकित गात अत्रि उठि धाए। देखि रामु आतुर चलि आए॥ करत दंडवत मुनि उर लाए। प्रेम बारि द्वौ जन अन्हवाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3609.verse_hindi: शरीर पुलकित हो गया, अत्रिजी उठकर दौड़े। उन्हें दौड़े आते देखकर श्री रामजी और भी शीघ्रता से चले आए। दण्डवत करते हुए ही श्री रामजी को (उठाकर) मुनि ने हृदय से लगा लिया और प्रेमाश्रुओं के जल से दोनों जनों को (दोनों भाइयों को) नहला दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3609.english_translation: Atri's body thrilled with joy as he rose and ran forward. Seeing him hurry toward them, Ram and Lakshman came even faster. The sage bowed down and embraced Ram to his heart, bathing both brothers in the waters of his love-filled tears.
ramacharitamanas::3609.translation_literal: पुलकित (thrilled) / गात (body) / अत्रि (Atri) / उठि (rising) / धाए (ran) / देखि (seeing) / रामु (Ram) / आतुर (eagerly) / चलि आए (came walking) / करत (doing) / दंडवत (prostration) / मुनि (sage) / उर (heart/chest) / लाए (brought/embraced) / प्रेम (love) / बारि (water) / द्वौ (both) / जन (persons) / अन्हवाए (bathed)
ramacharitamanas::3609.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3609.essence: Love runs out first, and tears become welcome.
ramacharitamanas::3609.simple_meaning: Atri greets Ram with overwhelming love, bows down, embraces him, and weeps tears of joy over both brothers.
ramacharitamanas::3609.simple_insight: Pure welcome can be so full that even tears become a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3609.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have reached Atri's hermitage in the forest. The old sage, overcome with devotion, rushes out, bows low, and holds Ram to his chest. His tears of love become a sacred welcome for both brothers.
ramacharitamanas::3609.modern_relevance: You see someone you love after months apart, and your whole body moves before your mind does. That rush of recognition is what this scene holds.
ramacharitamanas::3609.insight: It shows love as immediate, bodily, and unashamed — devotion that moves before speech.

ramacharitamanas::3610.verse_sanskrit: देखि राम छबि नयन जुड़ाने। सादर निज आश्रम तब आने॥ करि पूजा कहि बचन सुहाए। दिए मूल फल प्रभु मन भाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3610.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी की छवि देखकर मुनि के नेत्र शीतल हो गए। तब वे उनको आदरपूर्वक अपने आश्रम में ले आए। पूजन करके सुंदर वचन कहकर मुनि ने मूल और फल दिए, जो प्रभु के मन को बहुत रुचे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3610.english_translation: Seeing Ram's beauty, the sage's eyes became filled with delight. He then respectfully brought Him to his hermitage. After worshipping Him and speaking gentle words, the sage offered roots and fruits, which pleased the Lord greatly.
ramacharitamanas::3610.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / छबि (beauty, form) / नयन (eyes) / जुड़ाने (became delighted) / सादर (with respect) / निज (own) / आश्रम (hermitage) / तब (then) / आने (brought) / करि (having done) / पूजा (worship) / कहि (speaking) / बचन (words) / सुहाए (pleasant) / दिए (gave) / मूल (roots) / फल (fruits) / प्रभु (Lord) / मन (mind) / भाए (were pleasing)
ramacharitamanas::3610.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3610.essence: Simple offerings become precious when they come from devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3610.simple_meaning: The sage sees Ram, welcomes Him with honor, worships Him, speaks kindly, and offers simple food that Ram gladly accepts.
ramacharitamanas::3610.simple_insight: Real reverence is shown in welcome, words, and what you offer, not in grandeur.
ramacharitamanas::3610.detailed_meaning: At Atri's hermitage in Aranyakand, the sage is overwhelmed by Ram's presence. He welcomes Ram and Sita with worship, gentle words, and the simplest meal. The scene shows how pure devotion turns ordinary hospitality into something sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3610.modern_relevance: You open the door to someone you deeply respect, and suddenly even tea and fruit feel like an offering. Care changes the ordinary into something memorable.
ramacharitamanas::3610.insight: It shifts attention from lavish display to sincere welcome and heartfelt offering.

ramacharitamanas::3611.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु आसन आसीन भरि लोचन सोभा निरखि। मुनिबर परम प्रबीन जोरि पानि अस्तुति करत ॥
ramacharitamanas::3611.verse_hindi: प्रभु आसन पर विराजमान हैं। नेत्र भरकर उनकी शोभा देखकर परम प्रवीण मुनि श्रेष्ठ हाथ जोड़कर स्तुति करने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3611.english_translation: The Lord sat on the seat. The wise sage filled his eyes with that beauty and, joining his hands, began to praise him.
ramacharitamanas::3611.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / आसन (seat) / आसीन (seated) / भरि (filling) / लोचन (eyes) / सोभा (beauty, splendor) / निरखि (seeing) / मुनिबर (best of sages) / परम (supremely) / प्रबीन (skilled, wise) / जोरि (joining) / पानि (hands) / अस्तुति (praise) / करत (doing)
ramacharitamanas::3611.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3611.essence: Seeing the divine clearly leaves only praise.
ramacharitamanas::3611.simple_meaning: Ram sits before the sage, and the sage is so moved by his beauty that he joins his hands and begins to praise him.
ramacharitamanas::3611.simple_insight: A heart that truly sees beauty naturally turns toward reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3611.detailed_meaning: At Atri's hermitage in the forest, Ram has just arrived with Sita and Lakshman. The great sage sits before him, looks on with overflowing delight, and forgets everything except praise. This verse begins his devotional offering.
ramacharitamanas::3611.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone whose presence feels bigger than words. Before you can even think, gratitude rises and your hands come together in respect.
ramacharitamanas::3611.insight: It shifts attention from analysis to reverent recognition.

ramacharitamanas::3612.verse_sanskrit: नमामि भक्त वत्सलं। कृपालु शील कोमलं॥ भजामि ते पदांबुजं। अकामिनां स्वधामदं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3612.verse_hindi: हे भक्त वत्सल! हे कृपालु! हे कोमल स्वभाव वाले! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ। निष्काम पुरुषों को अपना परमधाम देने वाले आपके चरण कमलों को मैं भजता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3612.english_translation: I bow to the one who loves devotees, who is compassionate and gentle. I worship your lotus feet, which give their own abode to those without desire.
ramacharitamanas::3612.translation_literal: नमामि (I bow) / भक्त वत्सलं (the devotee-loving one) / कृपालु (compassionate) / शील (nature) / कोमलं (gentle) / भजामि (I worship) / ते (your) / पदांबुजं (lotus feet) / अकामिनां (of those without desire) / स्वधामदं (giver of your own abode)
ramacharitamanas::3612.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3612.essence: Ram gives his own home to the one who asks for nothing.
ramacharitamanas::3612.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as gentle, compassionate, and loving toward devotees. Those who let go of desire receive his own supreme abode.
ramacharitamanas::3612.simple_insight: It feels safe to rest in love that does not demand anything from you.
ramacharitamanas::3612.detailed_meaning: The sage has just welcomed Ram into his hermitage and now lifts his hands in praise. In the quiet forest, he names Ram as the one who cherishes devotion and gives his own dwelling to those free of wanting.
ramacharitamanas::3612.modern_relevance: You finally stop chasing approval after a long season of proving yourself. In that quiet, you discover that the deepest welcome comes when you are no longer bargaining for it.
ramacharitamanas::3612.insight: It shifts devotion from transaction to surrender: release desire, and the heart finds its home.

ramacharitamanas::3613.verse_sanskrit: निकाम श्याम सुंदरं। भवांबुनाथ मंदरं॥ प्रफुल्ल कंज लोचनं। मदादि दोष मोचनं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3613.verse_hindi: आप नितान्त सुंदर श्याम, संसार (आवागमन) रूपी समुद्र को मथने के लिए मंदराचल रूप, फूले हुए कमल के समान नेत्रों वाले और मद आदि दोषों से छुड़ाने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3613.english_translation: You are utterly beautiful and dark-hued, like Mount Mandara for churning the ocean of becoming. Your eyes are like blooming lotuses, and you free people from pride and other flaws.
ramacharitamanas::3613.translation_literal: निकाम (utterly) / श्याम (dark-hued) / सुंदरं (beautiful) / भवांबु (the ocean of becoming) / नाथ (lord) / मंदरं (Mount Mandara) / प्रफुल्ल (blooming) / कंज (lotus) / लोचनं (eyes) / मदादि (pride and such) / दोष (faults) / मोचनं (freeing)
ramacharitamanas::3613.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3613.essence: His beauty does what pride cannot survive.
ramacharitamanas::3613.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as dark, beautiful, lotus-eyed, and able to free people from pride and other inner flaws.
ramacharitamanas::3613.simple_insight: True beauty does not flatter ego; it dissolves it.
ramacharitamanas::3613.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sages are not merely seeing Ram — they are praising the divine presence before them. After bowing, they describe his beauty and power in devotional language, ending with the truth that his presence frees the heart from pride.
ramacharitamanas::3613.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose calm makes your own ego feel loud. Instead of trying to impress, you soften. Some presences do not inflate you; they purify you.
ramacharitamanas::3613.insight: It turns admiration into surrender and shows that real greatness clears away self-importance.

ramacharitamanas::3614.verse_sanskrit: प्रलंब बाहु विक्रमं। प्रभोऽप्रमेय वैभवं॥ निषंग चाप सायकं। धरं त्रिलोक नायकं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3614.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! आपकी लंबी भुजाओं का पराक्रम और आपका ऐश्वर्य अप्रमेय (बुद्धि के परे अथवा असीम) है। आप तरकस और धनुष-बाण धारण करने वाले तीनों लोकों के स्वामी, ॥
ramacharitamanas::3614.english_translation: O Lord, your long-armed valor and immeasurable glory are beyond thought. You bear quiver, bow, and arrows, and you are the lord of the three worlds.
ramacharitamanas::3614.translation_literal: प्रलंब (long) / बाहु (arms) / विक्रमं (valor) / प्रभो (O Lord) / अप्रमेय (immeasurable) / वैभवं (glory) / निषंग (quiver) / चाप (bow) / सायकं (arrows) / धरं (bearing) / त्रिलोक (three worlds) / नायकं (lord)
ramacharitamanas::3614.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3614.essence: Power becomes holy when it protects without limit.
ramacharitamanas::3614.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as mighty, limitless, and armed with bow and arrows. He is the ruler of all three worlds.
ramacharitamanas::3614.simple_insight: Greatness here is not abstract; it is the strength that can protect and lead.
ramacharitamanas::3614.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is singing Ram's praise in the forest, building a devotional portrait before the story turns darker. After describing Ram as loving, gentle, and beautiful, he adds this image of power: long-armed, armed for battle, and beyond measure.
ramacharitamanas::3614.modern_relevance: A child feels safe because a parent stands at the door after a hard conversation. Strength is not only force; it is the presence that can hold danger without flinching.
ramacharitamanas::3614.insight: It shifts reverence toward power that is disciplined, protective, and beyond calculation.

ramacharitamanas::3615.verse_sanskrit: दिनेश वंश मंडनं। महेश चाप खंडनं॥ मुनींद्र संत रंजनं। सुरारि वृंद भंजनं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3615.verse_hindi: सूर्यवंश के भूषण, महादेवजी के धनुष को तोड़ने वाले, मुनिराजों और संतों को आनंद देने वाले तथा देवताओं के शत्रु असुरों के समूह का नाश करने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3615.english_translation: The ornament of the solar dynasty, the one who broke Shiva's bow, the delight of sages and saints, and the destroyer of the hosts of hostile beings.
ramacharitamanas::3615.translation_literal: दिनेश-वंश (solar dynasty) / मंडनं (ornament) / महेश-चाप (Shiva's bow) / खंडनं (breaker) / मुनींद्र-संत (sages and saints) / रंजनं (delight-giver) / सुरारि-वृंद (hosts of hostile beings) / भंजनं (destroyer)
ramacharitamanas::3615.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3615.essence: True nobility is known by what it can break and whom it can uplift.
ramacharitamanas::3615.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the glory of the solar dynasty, the one who broke Shiva's bow, the joy of saints, and the destroyer of hostile forces.
ramacharitamanas::3615.simple_insight: Real greatness does not just shine; it protects goodness and cuts through arrogance.
ramacharitamanas::3615.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the praise of Ram rises like a hymn of identity: he is the heir of the solar line, the bow-breaker at Shiva's court, the delight of sages, and the end of hostile powers. The verse gathers his royal grace and divine force into one image.
ramacharitamanas::3615.modern_relevance: At a family gathering, someone keeps retelling your old win like it defines you. This verse reminds you that real stature is not just reputation — it is the power to protect what is good and end what is false.
ramacharitamanas::3615.insight: It shifts admiration from status alone to the ability to defend dharma and remove harm.

ramacharitamanas::3616.verse_sanskrit: मनोज वैरि वंदितं। अजादि देव सेवितं॥ विशुद्ध बोध विग्रहं। समस्त दूषणापहं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3616.verse_hindi: आप कामदेव के शत्रु महादेवजी के द्वारा वंदित, ब्रह्मा आदि देवताओं से सेवित, विशुद्ध ज्ञानमय विग्रह और समस्त दोषों को नष्ट करने वाले हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3616.english_translation: You are worshipped by Shiva, served by Brahma and the other radiant beings, a pure embodiment of knowledge, and the remover of every flaw.
ramacharitamanas::3616.translation_literal: मनोज वैरि (enemy of desire) / वंदितं (worshipped) / अजादि (Brahma and others) / देव (radiant beings) / सेवितं (served) / विशुद्ध (pure) / बोध (awareness) / विग्रहं (embodiment) / समस्त (all) / दूषण (faults) / अपहं (remover)
ramacharitamanas::3616.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3616.essence: Purity itself becomes power when every flaw falls away.
ramacharitamanas::3616.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the one worshipped by Shiva, served by Brahma and other radiant beings, pure in wisdom, and free of all faults.
ramacharitamanas::3616.simple_insight: Greatness here is not power alone, but purity that draws reverence from the highest beings.
ramacharitamanas::3616.detailed_meaning: In this hymn of praise, Tulsidas continues describing Ram’s divine qualities in the forest journey’s opening invocation. The focus is not on action in the story, but on who Ram truly is: revered by Shiva, served by Brahma and other radiant beings, and beyond all blemish.
ramacharitamanas::3616.modern_relevance: When you feel pressured to prove yourself with noise, this verse points to a quieter kind of authority: the kind that needs no self-promotion because its purity speaks for itself.
ramacharitamanas::3616.insight: It shifts attention from status to inner purity, showing that true worth is recognised by character, not display.

ramacharitamanas::3617.verse_sanskrit: नमामि इंदिरा पतिं। सुखाकरं सतां गतिं॥ भजे सशक्ति सानुजं। शची पति प्रियानुजं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3617.verse_hindi: हे लक्ष्मीपते! हे सुखों की खान और सत्पुरुषों की एकमात्र गति! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ! हे शचीपति (इन्द्र) के प्रिय छोटे भाई (वामनजी)! स्वरूपा-शक्ति श्री सीताजी और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित आपको मैं भजता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3617.english_translation: I bow to the Lord of Lakshmi, the source of joy and the refuge of the good. I worship him with his power and his younger brother, the beloved younger brother of Shachi's lord.
ramacharitamanas::3617.translation_literal: नमामि (I bow) / इंदिरा पतिं (the Lord of Lakshmi) / सुखाकरं (the source of joy) / सतां (of the good) / गतिं (refuge, goal) / भजे (I worship) / सशक्ति (with power) / सानुजं (with the younger brother) / शची पति (Shachi's lord) / प्रियानुजं (the beloved younger brother)
ramacharitamanas::3617.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3617.essence: Ram is not only majestic; he is the refuge that gathers love around him.
ramacharitamanas::3617.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the source of joy and the refuge of good people, and the speaker worships him together with his power and his brother Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::3617.simple_insight: Devotion is not lonely here — it rests in the fullness of Ram, his power, and loyal companionship.
ramacharitamanas::3617.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the poem turns from describing Ram's greatness to directly worshipping him. Tulsidas bows to Ram as Lakshmi's lord and the refuge of the virtuous, then includes Sita and Lakshman, showing that divine love is never isolated from loving relationship.
ramacharitamanas::3617.modern_relevance: You reach for something steady after a hard day, and it is not just power you want — it is warmth, loyalty, and a presence that makes life feel held.
ramacharitamanas::3617.insight: It shifts worship from abstract greatness to a living relationship of refuge, power, and companionship.

ramacharitamanas::3618.verse_sanskrit: त्वदंघ्रि मूल ये नराः। भजंति हीन मत्सराः॥ पतंति नो भवार्णवे। वितर्क वीचि संकुले ॥
ramacharitamanas::3618.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य मत्सर (डाह) रहित होकर आपके चरण कमलों का सेवन करते हैं, वे तर्क-वितर्क (अनेक प्रकार के संदेह) रूपी तरंगों से पूर्ण संसार रूपी समुद्र में नहीं गिरते (आवागमन के चक्कर में नहीं पड़ते) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3618.english_translation: Those people who worship at your feet without jealousy do not fall into the ocean of becoming, which is full of waves of doubt and argument.
ramacharitamanas::3618.translation_literal: त्वद् (your) / अंघ्रि-मूल (the root of the feet) / ये (those who) / नराः (people) / भजंति (worship) / हीन (free from) / मत्सराः (jealousy) / पतंति (fall) / नो (not) / भव-अर्णवे (in the ocean of becoming) / वितर्क-वीचि (waves of doubt and argument) / संकुले (crowded, full of)
ramacharitamanas::3618.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3618.essence: Jealousy keeps you in confusion; devotion carries you through it.
ramacharitamanas::3618.simple_meaning: People who worship Ram without jealousy are not thrown into the endless cycle of confusion and rebirth.
ramacharitamanas::3618.simple_insight: When comparison drops, devotion becomes steady and the mind stops being pulled under.
ramacharitamanas::3618.detailed_meaning: In a devotional hymn to Ram, the speaker praises those who come to his feet with no envy in their hearts. In that purity, they are not swept into the ocean of doubt, argument, and repeating confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3618.modern_relevance: You scroll past someone else's success and feel the sting of comparison. The moment you stop measuring yourself, your prayer, work, and attention all become cleaner.
ramacharitamanas::3618.insight: It shifts devotion from mixed motives to a clean, steady trust that can cross confusion.

ramacharitamanas::3619.verse_sanskrit: विविक्त वासिनः सदा। भजंति मुक्तये मुदा॥ निरस्य इंद्रियादिकं। प्रयांतिते गतिं स्वकं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3619.verse_hindi: जो एकान्तवासी पुरुष मुक्ति के लिए, इन्द्रियादि का निग्रह करके (उन्हें विषयों से हटाकर) प्रसन्नतापूर्वक आपको भजते हैं, वे स्वकीय गति को (अपने स्वरूप को) प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3619.english_translation: Those who live in solitude, restrain the senses, and worship with joy for freedom reach their own true state.
ramacharitamanas::3619.translation_literal: विविक्त (secluded/solitary) / वासिनः (dwellers) / सदा (always) / भजंति (worship) / मुक्तये (for freedom) / मुदा (with joy) / निरस्य (having cast out) / इंद्रियादिकं (the senses and the like) / प्रयांतिते (they go) / गतिं (state/goal) / स्वकं (their own)
ramacharitamanas::3619.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3619.essence: Joyful restraint brings you back to your own true nature.
ramacharitamanas::3619.simple_meaning: People who live quietly, control their senses, and worship with joy reach their own true nature and freedom.
ramacharitamanas::3619.simple_insight: Freedom feels less like escape and more like coming back to yourself.
ramacharitamanas::3619.detailed_meaning: The prayer is moving from praise into spiritual method. After describing the divine as the refuge of the pure, the verse says that people who withdraw from distraction, restrain the senses, and worship gladly are led back to their own true state.
ramacharitamanas::3619.modern_relevance: You close the laptop, silence your phone, and sit alone for ten minutes because your mind has been pulled in too many directions. That small withdrawal can become the doorway back to yourself.
ramacharitamanas::3619.insight: It shifts attention from outer stimulation to inner return, showing freedom as a disciplined homecoming.

ramacharitamanas::3620.verse_sanskrit: तमेकमद्भुतं प्रभुं। निरीहमीश्वरं विभुं॥ जगद्गुरुं च शाश्वतं। तुरीयमेव केवलं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3620.verse_hindi: उन (आप) को जो एक (अद्वितीय), अद्भुत (मायिक जगत से विलक्षण), प्रभु (सर्वसमर्थ), इच्छारहित, ईश्वर (सबके स्वामी), व्यापक, जगद्गुरु, सनातन (नित्य), तुरीय (तीनों गुणों से सर्वथा परे) और केवल (अपने स्वरूप में स्थित) हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3620.english_translation: I bow to the one, wondrous Lord: desireless, sovereign, all-pervading, teacher of the world, eternal, beyond the three states, alone in true being.
ramacharitamanas::3620.translation_literal: तम् (that one) / एकम् (one, nondual) / अद्भुतम् (wondrous) / प्रभुम् (the Lord) / निरीहम् (desireless) / ईश्वरम् (sovereign) / विभुम् (all-pervading) / जगद्गुरुम् (teacher of the world) / च (and) / शाश्वतम् (eternal) / तुरीयम् (the fourth, beyond waking-dream-sleep) / एव (indeed) / केवलम् (alone, absolute)
ramacharitamanas::3620.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3620.essence: Ram is beyond all passing states and remains complete in himself.
ramacharitamanas::3620.simple_meaning: Ram is described as the one, wondrous, desireless, all-pervading reality who teaches the world and stands beyond ordinary states of mind.
ramacharitamanas::3620.simple_insight: You are being pointed toward something steadier than thought, mood, or waking life.
ramacharitamanas::3620.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the hymn turns from complaint to vision. The speaker praises Ram not as a local hero but as the one reality beyond change, desire, and the three ordinary states of consciousness. That makes this a peak statement of divine nature.
ramacharitamanas::3620.modern_relevance: You wake from a dream, check your phone, then sink back into restlessness before the day even starts. This verse points to what remains untouched underneath all three states.
ramacharitamanas::3620.insight: It shifts attention from changing experiences to the unchanging ground beneath them.

ramacharitamanas::3621.verse_sanskrit: भजामि भाव वल्लभं। कुयोगिनां सुदुर्लभं॥ स्वभक्त कल्प पादपं। समं सुसेव्यमन्वहं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3621.verse_hindi: (तथा) जो भावप्रिय, कुयोगियों (विषयी पुरुषों) के लिए अत्यन्त दुर्लभ, अपने भक्तों के लिए कल्पवृक्ष (अर्थात् उनकी समस्त कामनाओं को पूर्ण करने वाले), सम (पक्षपातरहित) और सदा सुखपूर्वक सेवन करने योग्य हैं, मैं निरंतर भजता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3621.english_translation: I continually worship the one who loves devotion, is hard to reach for those lost in wrong practice, is like a wish-fulfilling tree for his devotees, impartial, and always easy to serve.
ramacharitamanas::3621.translation_literal: भजामि (I worship) / भाव-वल्लभं (the lover of devotion) / कुयोगिनां (for wrong-practicing seekers) / सुदुर्लभं (very hard to attain) / स्व-भक्त (for his own devotees) / कल्प-पादपं (wish-fulfilling tree) / समं (equal) / सु-सेव्यम् (easy to serve) / अन्वहं (always, daily)
ramacharitamanas::3621.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3621.essence: Sincere devotion reaches Ram; cleverness and pride do not.
ramacharitamanas::3621.simple_meaning: Ram is easy to approach through sincere devotion, but hard to reach through wrong or selfish practice. He treats all devotees equally and fulfills their needs like a wish-fulfilling tree.
ramacharitamanas::3621.simple_insight: You do not need status or perfection to be received; sincerity opens the door.
ramacharitamanas::3621.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the devotional praise continues. Tulsidas turns from abstract description to loving declaration: Ram is not won by clever spiritual pride, but by heartfelt devotion. For his devotees, he becomes instantly generous and accessible.
ramacharitamanas::3621.modern_relevance: You stand in front of someone important, rehearsing the perfect words, but what reaches them is your sincerity. This verse says the same is true with Ram: polished performance fails, honest devotion opens everything.
ramacharitamanas::3621.insight: It shifts the mind from self-display to sincerity, and from earning grace to receiving it through love.

ramacharitamanas::3622.verse_sanskrit: अनूप रूप भूपतिं। नतोऽहमुर्विजा पतिं॥ प्रसीद मे नमामि ते। पदाब्ज भक्ति देहि मे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3622.verse_hindi: हे अनुपम सुंदर! हे पृथ्वीपति! हे जानकीनाथ! मैं आपको प्रणाम करता हूँ। मुझ पर प्रसन्न होइए, मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ। मुझे अपने चरण कमलों की भक्ति दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3622.english_translation: O incomparable beauty, lord of the earth, lord of Janaki, I bow to you. Be pleased with me; I offer my salutations to you. Grant me devotion to your lotus feet.
ramacharitamanas::3622.translation_literal: अनूप (incomparable) / रूप (beauty, form) / भूपतिं (lord of the earth) / नतः (bowed) / अहम् (I) / उर्विजा-पतिं (lord of Janaki) / प्रसीद (be pleased) / मे (with me) / नमामि (I bow) / ते (to you) / पद-अब्ज (lotus feet) / भक्ति (devotion) / देहि (give) / मे (to me)
ramacharitamanas::3622.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3622.essence: Devotion begins when you ask for devotion itself.
ramacharitamanas::3622.simple_meaning: The speaker praises Ram, bows down, and asks for devotion to Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::3622.simple_insight: Real prayer is not just asking for help; it is asking for a heart that can love rightly.
ramacharitamanas::3622.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the poet turns from describing Ram's greatness to direct prayer. He bows to Ram as Janaki's lord and asks for something deeper than help: the ability to love Ram's feet with true devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3622.modern_relevance: You can be standing in a hospital corridor, frightened and helpless, and still know the real request is larger than rescue: give me the strength to love what is worthy.
ramacharitamanas::3622.insight: It shifts prayer from asking for outcomes to asking for a transformed heart.

ramacharitamanas::3623.verse_sanskrit: पठंति ये स्तवं इदं। नरादरेण ते पदं॥ व्रजंति नात्र संशयं। त्वदीय भक्ति संयुताः ॥
ramacharitamanas::3623.verse_hindi: जो मनुष्य इस स्तुति को आदरपूर्वक पढ़ते हैं, वे आपकी भक्ति से युक्त होकर आपके परम पद को प्राप्त होते हैं, इसमें संदेह नहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3623.english_translation: Those who read this praise with reverence, joined to your devotion, surely reach your highest state; there is no doubt.
ramacharitamanas::3623.translation_literal: पठंति (read) / ये (those who) / स्तवं (praise) / इदं (this) / नरादरेण (with reverence) / ते (they) / पदं (state / highest state) / व्रजंति (go / attain) / नात्र (here no) / संशयं (doubt) / त्वदीय (your) / भक्ति (devotion) / संयुताः (joined with)
ramacharitamanas::3623.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3623.essence: Reverent devotion carries you to Ram without doubt.
ramacharitamanas::3623.simple_meaning: Anyone who reads this praise respectfully and with devotion will surely reach Ram's highest state.
ramacharitamanas::3623.simple_insight: Devotion is not wasted effort; it quietly carries you to what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::3623.detailed_meaning: A sage has just offered praise to Ram, asking for grace and devotion. He now declares the power of that praise itself: anyone who reads it with reverence and devotion will reach Ram's highest state without doubt.
ramacharitamanas::3623.modern_relevance: You open a prayer, a poem, or a line of wisdom before bed and read it with real attention, not as a checkbox. That small reverence changes what reaches you.
ramacharitamanas::3623.insight: It shifts practice from casual reading to devotional participation, where reverence itself becomes the vehicle of transformation.

ramacharitamanas::3624.verse_sanskrit: बिनती करि मुनि नाइ सिरु कह कर जोरि बहोरि। चरन सरोरुह नाथ जनि कबहुँ तजै मति मोरि ॥
ramacharitamanas::3624.verse_hindi: मुनि ने (इस प्रकार) विनती करके और फिर सिर नवाकर, हाथ जोड़कर कहा- हे नाथ! मेरी बुद्धि आपके चरण कमलों को कभी न छोड़े ॥
ramacharitamanas::3624.english_translation: After bowing and praying, the sage folded his hands and said, "O Lord, may my mind never leave your lotus feet."
ramacharitamanas::3624.translation_literal: बिनती (prayer) / करि (having done) / मुनि (the sage) / नाइ (bowing) / सिरु (head) / कह (said) / कर (hands) / जोरि (folded together) / बहोरि (again) / चरन (feet) / सरोरुह (lotus) / नाथ (Lord) / जनि (may not) / कबहुँ (ever) / तजै (leave) / मति (mind) / मोरि (my)
ramacharitamanas::3624.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3624.essence: The deepest prayer is to never drift from Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3624.simple_meaning: The sage prays for one thing: that his mind never drift away from Ram's feet.
ramacharitamanas::3624.simple_insight: Devotion can be simple and steady — just keep returning to what you love most.
ramacharitamanas::3624.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sage bows low before Ram and asks for nothing worldly. After his prayer, he only begs that his mind never abandon Ram's feet. The whole moment turns on humble, lasting devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3624.modern_relevance: After a long day of distractions, you finally sit quietly and realize what you keep coming back to. This verse names that returning as the real prayer.
ramacharitamanas::3624.insight: It shifts attention from asking for outcomes to asking for inner steadiness in devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3625.verse_sanskrit: अनुसुइया के पद गहि सीता। मिली बहोरि सुसील बिनीता॥ रिषिपतिनी मन सुख अधिकाई। आसिष देइ निकट बैठाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3625.verse_hindi: फिर परम शीलवती और विनम्र श्री सीताजी अनसूयाजी (आत्रिजी की पत्नी) के चरण पकड़कर उनसे मिलीं। ऋषि पत्नी के मन में बड़ा सुख हुआ। उन्होंने आशीष देकर सीताजी को पास बैठा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3625.english_translation: Then the noble and humble Sita held Anasuya's feet and greeted her. The sage's wife felt great joy, blessed her, and seated her nearby.
ramacharitamanas::3625.translation_literal: अनुसुइया के (of Anasuya) / पद (feet) / गहि (holding) / सीता (Sita) / मिली (met) / बहोरि (again) / सुसील (well-mannered) / बिनीता (humble)॥ / रिषिपतिनी (wife of the sage) / मन (mind) / सुख (joy) / अधिकाई (greatly) / आसिष (blessing) / देइ (giving) / निकट (near) / बैठाई (seated)
ramacharitamanas::3625.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3625.essence: Humility turns a meeting into a blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3625.simple_meaning: Sita humbly greets Anasuya by touching her feet. Anasuya feels delighted, blesses Sita, and invites her to sit close by.
ramacharitamanas::3625.simple_insight: Respect opens the heart, and a blessing often begins with humility.
ramacharitamanas::3625.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita meets Anasuya, the wife of a sage. Sita bows with deep humility, and Anasuya responds with joy and kindness. The scene prepares for a lesson on womanly conduct and inner dignity.
ramacharitamanas::3625.modern_relevance: You meet an elder who has lived through more than you can imagine. Instead of performing confidence, you listen, bow your pride, and receive what they offer.
ramacharitamanas::3625.insight: It shows that reverence creates trust, making guidance and blessing possible.

ramacharitamanas::3626.verse_sanskrit: दिब्य बसन भूषन पहिराए। जे नित नूतन अमल सुहाए॥ कह रिषिबधू सरस मृदु बानी। नारिधर्म कछु ब्याज बखानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3626.verse_hindi: और उन्हें ऐसे दिव्य वस्त्र और आभूषण पहनाए, जो नित्य-नए निर्मल और सुहावने बने रहते हैं। फिर ऋषि पत्नी उनके बहाने मधुर और कोमल वाणी से स्त्रियों के कुछ धर्म बखान कर कहने लगीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3626.english_translation: She dressed her in divine garments and ornaments, ever new, pure, and lovely. Then the sage's wife spoke in soft, sweet words, using this pretext to explain a woman's proper conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3626.translation_literal: दिब्य (divine) / बसन (garments) / भूषन (ornaments) / पहिराए (dressed on) / जे (which) / नित (always) / नूतन (new) / अमल (pure) / सुहाए (beautiful) / कह (said) / रिषिबधू (the sage's wife) / सरस (sweet) / मृदु (gentle) / बानी (speech) / नारिधर्म (woman's conduct) / कछु (some) / ब्याज (pretext) / बखानी (explained)
ramacharitamanas::3626.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3626.essence: Kindness opens the heart before instruction begins.
ramacharitamanas::3626.simple_meaning: Anusuiya clothes Sita in beautiful divine garments and ornaments, then gently begins teaching her about a woman's conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3626.simple_insight: Care can be a doorway to teaching; kindness makes hard truths easier to receive.
ramacharitamanas::3626.detailed_meaning: In the forest hermitage, Sita has just been welcomed by Anusuiya. The sage's wife honors her with radiant clothes and ornaments, then uses that affectionate gesture as a gentle opening to speak about a woman's conduct. The verse is a transition into instruction, not the teaching itself.
ramacharitamanas::3626.modern_relevance: A grandmother fixes your collar before giving you advice you did not ask for. The care softens you first, so the lesson can land without resistance.
ramacharitamanas::3626.insight: It shows how warmth and respect can prepare someone to hear guidance.

ramacharitamanas::3627.verse_sanskrit: मातु पिता भ्राता हितकारी। मितप्रद सब सुनु राजकुमारी॥ अमित दानि भर्ता बयदेही। अधम सो नारि जो सेव न तेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3627.verse_hindi: हे राजकुमारी! सुनिए- माता, पिता, भाई सभी हित करने वाले हैं, परन्तु ये सब एक सीमा तक ही (सुख) देने वाले हैं, परन्तु हे जानकी! पति तो (मोक्ष रूप) असीम (सुख) देने वाला है। वह स्त्री अधम है, जो ऐसे पति की सेवा नहीं करती ॥
ramacharitamanas::3627.english_translation: Parents, brothers, and all family members are helpful, O princess, but only within limits. O Janaki, a husband gives boundless support. A woman is low who does not serve such a husband.
ramacharitamanas::3627.translation_literal: मातु पिता (mother father) / भ्राता (brother) / हितकारी (beneficial) / मितप्रद (limited giver) / सब (all) / सुनु (listen) / राजकुमारी (princess) / अमित (unbounded) / दानि (giver) / भर्ता (husband) / बयदेही (Vaidehi) / अधम (base) / सो (that) / नारि (woman) / जो (who) / सेव न (does not serve) / तेही (that one)
ramacharitamanas::3627.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3627.essence: A committed bond asks for service, not just affection.
ramacharitamanas::3627.simple_meaning: Annsuya teaches Sita that parents and siblings help only in limited ways, while a husband is meant to give boundless support and receive devoted service.
ramacharitamanas::3627.simple_insight: It highlights loyalty as a sacred form of care, not just a social role.
ramacharitamanas::3627.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Anusuya is instructing Sita after honoring her with gifts. She explains household duty through family roles: parents and brothers help, but a husband carries the deepest bond. The verse teaches Sita the ideal of wifely service.
ramacharitamanas::3627.modern_relevance: You are caring for everyone in the house, but one relationship still asks for your most steady presence. This verse speaks to the quiet discipline of showing up for the person who shares your life.
ramacharitamanas::3627.insight: It shifts attention from general affection to the specific obligation of committed partnership.

ramacharitamanas::3628.verse_sanskrit: धीरज धर्म मित्र अरु नारी। आपद काल परिखिअहिं चारी॥ बृद्ध रोगबस जड़ धनहीना। अंध बधिर क्रोधी अति दीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3628.verse_hindi: धैर्य, धर्म, मित्र और स्त्री- इन चारों की विपत्ति के समय ही परीक्षा होती है। वृद्ध, रोगी, मूर्ख, निर्धन, अंधा, बहरा, क्रोधी और अत्यन्त ही दीन- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3628.english_translation: Patience, duty, friend, and wife are tested in times of hardship. The old, the sick, the dull, the poor, the blind, the deaf, the angry, and the deeply distressed...
ramacharitamanas::3628.translation_literal: धीरज (patience) / धर्म (duty) / मित्र (friend) / अरु (and) / नारी (woman/wife) / आपद काल (time of hardship) / परिखिअहिं (are tested) / चारी (four) / बृद्ध (old) / रोगबस (under the power of illness) / जड़ (dull) / धनहीना (without wealth) / अंध (blind) / बधिर (deaf) / क्रोधी (angry) / अति दीना (deeply distressed)
ramacharitamanas::3628.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3628.essence: Pressure reveals whether your bonds are real.
ramacharitamanas::3628.simple_meaning: Patience, duty, friendship, and marriage are truly tested when life gets difficult. The verse also points to people who are especially vulnerable in such times.
ramacharitamanas::3628.simple_insight: Hardship exposes what is real in you and in your relationships.
ramacharitamanas::3628.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a teaching about human bonds unfolds after the sage's wife speaks to Sita. Tulsidas pauses the story to say that patience, duty, friendship, and marriage only prove themselves when life turns hard, and that suffering makes weakness visible.
ramacharitamanas::3628.modern_relevance: A friend disappears the moment your job is lost. A partner stays. A promise survives the pressure. This verse reminds you that difficulty is not just pain — it is the test that reveals what your bonds are made of.
ramacharitamanas::3628.insight: It shifts attention from easy loyalty to loyalty under strain.

ramacharitamanas::3629.verse_sanskrit: ऐसेहु पति कर किएँ अपमाना। नारि पाव जमपुर दुख नाना॥ एकइ धर्म एक ब्रत नेमा। कायँ बचन मन पति पद प्रेमा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3629.verse_hindi: ऐसे भी पति का अपमान करने से स्त्री यमपुर में भाँति-भाँति के दुःख पाती है। शरीर, वचन और मन से पति के चरणों में प्रेम करना स्त्री के लिए, बस यह एक ही धर्म है, एक ही व्रत है और एक ही नियम है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3629.english_translation: Even so, if a wife dishonors her husband, she meets many kinds of suffering in Yama's realm. For body, speech, and mind, loving the husband's feet is her one duty, one vow, and one rule.
ramacharitamanas::3629.translation_literal: ऐसेहु (even so) / पति (husband) / कर (of) / किएँ (having done) / अपमाना (dishonor, insult) / नारि (woman, wife) / पाव (receives) / जमपुर (realm of Yama) / दुख (suffering) / नाना (many, various) ॥ / एकइ (only one) / धर्म (duty, righteous rule) / एक (one) / ब्रत (vow) / नेमा (rule, observance) ॥ / कायँ (with body) / बचन (with speech) / मन (with mind) / पति (husband) / पद (feet) / प्रेमा (love) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3629.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3629.essence: True devotion shows itself in body, speech, and mind together.
ramacharitamanas::3629.simple_meaning: A wife should not dishonor her husband. Her duty is to love him with body, speech, and mind.
ramacharitamanas::3629.simple_insight: Love becomes real when it is lived completely, not only felt privately.
ramacharitamanas::3629.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Rama is teaching Sita about the ideal of a devoted wife. He describes how disrespect toward a husband brings suffering, and he defines her single guiding discipline as loving him fully in body, speech, and mind.
ramacharitamanas::3629.modern_relevance: A marriage starts to crack when respect disappears from small things: the tone of a reply, the eye-roll, the private contempt. This verse asks for wholeness, not performance.
ramacharitamanas::3629.insight: It shifts devotion from a feeling into a total way of relating, where thought, speech, and action must agree.

ramacharitamanas::3630.verse_sanskrit: जग पतिब्रता चारि बिधि अहहीं। बेद पुरान संत सब कहहीं॥ उत्तम के अस बस मन माहीं। सपनेहुँ आन पुरुष जग नाहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3630.verse_hindi: जगत में चार प्रकार की पतिव्रताएँ हैं। वेद, पुराण और संत सब ऐसा कहते हैं कि उत्तम श्रेणी की पतिव्रता के मन में ऐसा भाव बसा रहता है कि जगत में (मेरे पति को छोड़कर) दूसरा पुरुष स्वप्न में भी नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3630.english_translation: There are four kinds of chaste wives in the world. The Vedas, Puranas, and saints all say that the best kind keeps this thought in her heart: there is no other man in the world, even in a dream.
ramacharitamanas::3630.translation_literal: जग (world) / पतिब्रता (devoted to husband) / चारि बिधि (four kinds) / अहहीं (are) / बेद (Vedas) / पुरान (Puranas) / संत (saints) / सब (all) / कहहीं (say)॥ / उत्तम (best) / के (of) / अस (such) / बस (abiding) / मन माहीं (in the mind) / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / आन (other) / पुरुष (man) / जग (world) / नाहीं (is not)॥
ramacharitamanas::3630.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3630.essence: True fidelity leaves no room for a second claim on the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3630.simple_meaning: The highest kind of devoted wife keeps her mind fixed on her husband alone, with no room for anyone else.
ramacharitamanas::3630.simple_insight: Steady love is not scattered; it becomes a quiet inner loyalty.
ramacharitamanas::3630.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the text is defining the ideal of a devoted wife after describing how such devotion is judged in hard times. Tulsidas now names the highest form: a mind so settled in loyalty that even dream-imagined alternatives do not arise.
ramacharitamanas::3630.modern_relevance: You keep checking an old message thread, half-hoping for a different answer. This verse points to a love that is no longer divided by comparison, fantasy, or second choices.
ramacharitamanas::3630.insight: It shifts attention from divided attraction to single-hearted fidelity.

ramacharitamanas::3631.verse_sanskrit: मध्यम परपति देखइ कैसें। भ्राता पिता पुत्र निज जैसें॥ धर्म बिचारि समुझि कुल रहई। सो निकिष्ट त्रिय श्रुति अस कहई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3631.verse_hindi: मध्यम श्रेणी की पतिव्रता पराए पति को कैसे देखती है, जैसे वह अपना सगा भाई, पिता या पुत्र हो (अर्थात समान अवस्था वाले को वह भाई के रूप में देखती है, बड़े को पिता के रूप में और छोटे को पुत्र के रूप में देखती है।) जो धर्म को विचारकर और अपने कुल की मर्यादा समझकर बची रहती है, वह निकृष्ट (निम्न श्रेणी की) स्त्री है, ऐसा वेद कहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3631.english_translation: How does a moderate chaste woman see another man's husband? She sees him like her own brother, father, or son. Considering dharma and understanding her family’s honor, the woman who stays restrained is called the lowest by the scriptures.
ramacharitamanas::3631.translation_literal: मध्यम (moderate) / परपति (another man's husband) / देखइ (sees) / कैसें (how) / भ्राता (brother) / पिता (father) / पुत्र (son) / निज (own) / जैसें (like) ॥ धर्म (dharma) / बिचारि (considering) / समुझि (understanding) / कुल (family line) / रहई (remains) ॥ सो (that) / निकिष्ट (lowest) / त्रिय (woman) / श्रुति (scripture) / अस (thus) / कहई (says) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3631.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3631.essence: What you call someone shapes whether desire can take hold.
ramacharitamanas::3631.simple_meaning: A woman of moderate restraint is told to regard another man's husband as a brother, father, or son, and to remain within family honor and dharma.
ramacharitamanas::3631.simple_insight: Self-control becomes easier when the mind gives a different meaning to what it sees.
ramacharitamanas::3631.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the poem is laying out strict ideals of chaste conduct. After describing the highest form of devotion to a husband, it now defines the middle form: a woman protects her conduct by seeing another man through the lens of kinship and family duty.
ramacharitamanas::3631.modern_relevance: You notice a line is being crossed in a conversation, and you quietly step back before it grows teeth. The mind does not need to chase every attraction; it can choose a cleaner way of seeing.
ramacharitamanas::3631.insight: It trains the mind to redirect desire through disciplined perception, not just through willpower.

ramacharitamanas::3632.verse_sanskrit: बिनु अवसर भय तें रह जोई। जानेहु अधम नारि जग सोई॥ पति बंचक परपति रति करई। रौरव नरक कल्प सत परई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3632.verse_hindi: और जो स्त्री मौका न मिलने से या भयवश पतिव्रता बनी रहती है, जगत में उसे अधम स्त्री जानना। पति को धोखा देने वाली जो स्त्री पराए पति से रति करती है, वह तो सौ कल्प तक रौरव नरक में पड़ी रहती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3632.english_translation: Know the woman who stays faithful only because there was no chance or because fear held her back as low in the world. The woman who betrays her husband and takes desire in another man falls into the Raurava lower realm for a hundred ages.
