ramacharitamanas::3632.translation_literal: बिनु (without) / अवसर (opportunity) / भय तें (because of fear) / रह (stays) / जोई (who) / जानेहु (know) / अधम (lowest) / नारि (woman) / जग (world) / सोई (that) / पति (husband) / बंचक (deceiver) / परपति (another's husband) / रति (desire, attachment) / करई (does) / रौरव (Raurava) / नरक (lower realm) / कल्प सत (hundred ages) / परई (falls)
ramacharitamanas::3632.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3632.essence: Fearful restraint is not true fidelity.
ramacharitamanas::3632.simple_meaning: A woman who is faithful only because she had no chance or was afraid is still judged low. Betraying a husband and seeking another man brings severe suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3632.simple_insight: Outer restraint is not the same as inner purity.
ramacharitamanas::3632.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is defining kinds of marital fidelity in a running argument about women’s conduct. After describing the highest and middle forms, he now marks the lowest: restraint born from fear or lack of opportunity, and betrayal driven by desire. The verse sharpens the moral scale before the next line continues it.
ramacharitamanas::3632.modern_relevance: Someone stays in line only because cameras are on, then acts differently the moment no one is watching. The verse says hidden intention matters more than public appearance.
ramacharitamanas::3632.insight: It shifts attention from outward behavior to the motive underneath it.

ramacharitamanas::3633.verse_sanskrit: छन सुख लागि जनम सत कोटी। दुख न समुझ तेहि सम को खोटी॥ बिनु श्रम नारि परम गति लहई। पतिब्रत धर्म छाड़ि छल गहई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3633.verse_hindi: क्षणभर के सुख के लिए जो सौ करोड़ (असंख्य) जन्मों के दुःख को नहीं समझती, उसके समान दुष्टा कौन होगी। जो स्त्री छल छोड़कर पतिव्रत धर्म को ग्रहण करती है, वह बिना ही परिश्रम परम गति को प्राप्त करती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3633.english_translation: For a moment of pleasure, she does not understand the suffering of countless births; who could be more blameworthy than she? A woman who abandons deceit and takes up the vow of fidelity attains the highest state without effort.
ramacharitamanas::3633.translation_literal: छन (moment) / सुख (pleasure) / लागि (for) / जनम (births) / सत कोटी (hundred million) / दुख (suffering) / न समुझ (does not understand) / तेहि (that one) / सम (equal to) / को (who) / खोटी (blameworthy) / बिनु (without) / श्रम (effort) / नारि (woman) / परम गति (highest state) / लहई (attains) / पतिब्रत धर्म (vow of fidelity) / छाड़ि (abandoning) / छल (deceit) / गहई (takes up)
ramacharitamanas::3633.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3633.essence: Brief pleasure can hide a vast cost; fidelity lifts you effortlessly.
ramacharitamanas::3633.simple_meaning: Short-lived pleasure can lead to great suffering, while a woman who gives up deceit and stays faithful reaches the highest state naturally.
ramacharitamanas::3633.simple_insight: Real dignity comes from refusing the bait of quick pleasure and choosing what is steady.
ramacharitamanas::3633.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the poem is warning against betrayal in marriage and praising fidelity. After describing the lower and middling forms of conduct, it turns to the woman who abandons deceit and holds to her vow: she reaches the highest state without strain.
ramacharitamanas::3633.modern_relevance: You know the text, the flirtation, the secret message you almost sent because it felt harmless for one night. The verse says that tiny thrill can carry a much larger cost, while steady loyalty needs no performance.
ramacharitamanas::3633.insight: It shifts attention from immediate gratification to the long moral weight of a choice.

ramacharitamanas::3634.verse_sanskrit: पति प्रतिकूल जनम जहँ जाई। बिधवा होइ पाइ तरुनाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3634.verse_hindi: किन्तु जो पति के प्रतिकूल चलती है, वह जहाँ भी जाकर जन्म लेती है, वहीं जवानी पाकर (भरी जवानी में) विधवा हो जाती है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3634.english_translation: But the woman who goes against her husband, wherever she is born, becomes a widow in the bloom of youth.
ramacharitamanas::3634.translation_literal: पति (husband) / प्रतिकूल (against) / जनम (birth) / जहँ (wherever) / जाई (goes) / बिधवा (widow) / होइ (becomes) / पाइ (having obtained) / तरुनाई (youth)
ramacharitamanas::3634.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3634.essence: Opposing your bond can turn youth itself into loss.
ramacharitamanas::3634.simple_meaning: Turning against your husband brings ruin instead of security. The verse warns that such a life ends in loss and grief.
ramacharitamanas::3634.simple_insight: Some choices feel rebellious for a moment, but they can leave you with lasting emptiness.
ramacharitamanas::3634.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas continues a harsh warning about marital conduct in the forest-book’s moral instruction. After describing the woman who betrays her husband, he says opposition to a husband leads to widowhood in youth, completing the warning with a grim consequence.
ramacharitamanas::3634.modern_relevance: A relationship starts unraveling when every disagreement becomes defiance. The verse points to the cost of choosing opposition over loyalty until love itself feels gone.
ramacharitamanas::3634.insight: It frames marital disloyalty as self-destructive, not liberating.

ramacharitamanas::3635.verse_sanskrit: सहज अपावनि नारि पति सेवत सुभ गति लहइ। जसु गावत श्रुति चारि अजहुँ तुलसिका हरिहि प्रिय ॥
ramacharitamanas::3635.verse_hindi: स्त्री जन्म से ही अपवित्र है, किन्तु पति की सेवा करके वह अनायास ही शुभ गति प्राप्त कर लेती है। (पतिव्रत धर्म के कारण ही) आज भी 'तुलसीजी' भगवान को प्रिय हैं और चारों वेद उनका यश गाते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3635.english_translation: A woman, by her nature, is impure; by serving her husband, she attains a noble state. Even today, Tulsidas is dear to Ram, and the four Vedas sing his praise.
ramacharitamanas::3635.translation_literal: सहज (by nature) / अपावनि (impure) / नारि (woman) / पति (husband) / सेवत (serving) / सुभ (good) / गति (state, attainment) / लहइ (attains) / जसु (praise, fame) / गावत (singing) / श्रुति (the Vedas) / चारि (four) / अजहुँ (even now) / तुलसिका (Tulsidas) / हरिहि (to Hari/Ram) / प्रिय (dear)
ramacharitamanas::3635.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3635.essence: Faithful service can elevate a life more than birth can.
ramacharitamanas::3635.simple_meaning: Serving one's husband is presented as a path to a better state, and Tulsidas says this kind of devotion is still honoured by Ram and the Vedas.
ramacharitamanas::3635.simple_insight: Dignity grows through faithful service, not through self-display.
ramacharitamanas::3635.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the poem turns from warning to principle: a wife who serves her husband with steadfast devotion reaches a noble state. Tulsidas then links that ideal to Sita, saying even the Vedas praise it and Ram holds such devotion dear.
ramacharitamanas::3635.modern_relevance: You keep showing up for a partner through illness, stress, and long silence. No applause comes, but the relationship deepens because your care is steady.
ramacharitamanas::3635.insight: It shifts attention from status to the transforming power of loyal service.

ramacharitamanas::3636.verse_sanskrit: सुनु सीता तव नाम सुमिरि नारि पतिब्रत करहिं। तोहि प्रानप्रिय राम कहिउँ कथा संसार हित ॥
ramacharitamanas::3636.verse_hindi: हे सीता! सुनो, तुम्हारा तो नाम ही ले-लेकर स्त्रियाँ पतिव्रत धर्म का पालन करेंगी। तुम्हें तो श्री रामजी प्राणों के समान प्रिय हैं, यह (पतिव्रत धर्म की) कथा तो मैंने संसार के हित के लिए कही है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3636.english_translation: Listen, Sita: by remembering your name, women will uphold chastity. You are as dear to Ram as life itself; I have spoken this story for the good of the world.
ramacharitamanas::3636.translation_literal: सुनु (listen) / सीता (Sita) / तव (your) / नाम (name) / सुमिरि (remembering) / नारि (women) / पतिब्रत (chaste devotion to husband) / करहिं (do) / तोहि (to you) / प्रानप्रिय (dear as life) / राम (Ram) / कहिउँ (I spoke) / कथा (story) / संसार (world) / हित (for welfare)
ramacharitamanas::3636.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3636.essence: A beloved example can teach devotion more powerfully than instruction.
ramacharitamanas::3636.simple_meaning: Sita’s name is so pure and powerful that remembering it helps women live with fidelity and devotion. The speaker says this teaching is meant for the good of everyone.
ramacharitamanas::3636.simple_insight: A holy example can shape ordinary lives without force.
ramacharitamanas::3636.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram speaks to Sita with tenderness, praising her as dearest to him and explaining why her story matters beyond their private bond. Her example becomes a guide for others, showing how devotion can lift conduct.
ramacharitamanas::3636.modern_relevance: Someone hears a grandmother speak a name with reverence, and it changes how the whole family behaves. That is how living examples work: they teach without argument and quietly reshape what people think is possible.
ramacharitamanas::3636.insight: It turns virtue into something contagious: one life of devotion can train many others.

ramacharitamanas::3637.verse_sanskrit: सुनि जानकीं परम सुखु पावा। सादर तासु चरन सिरु नावा॥ तब मुनि सन कह कृपानिधाना। आयसु होइ जाउँ बन आना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3637.verse_hindi: जानकीजी ने सुनकर परम सुख पाया और आदरपूर्वक उनके चरणों में सिर नवाया। तब कृपा की खान श्री रामजी ने मुनि से कहा- आज्ञा हो तो अब दूसरे वन में जाऊँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3637.english_translation: Sita felt supreme joy on hearing this and bowed her head respectfully at his feet. Then the treasure of grace, Ram, said to the sage, 'If you permit, I will now go to another forest.'
ramacharitamanas::3637.translation_literal: सुनि (on hearing) / जानकीं (Sita) / परम सुखु (supreme joy) / पावा (received) / सादर (with respect) / तासु (his) / चरन (feet) / सिरु (head) / नावा (bowed) ॥ तब (then) / मुनि (sage) / सन (to) / कह (said) / कृपानिधाना (treasure of grace) / आयसु (permission) / होइ (if there is) / जाउँ (I will go) / बन (forest) / आना (another) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3637.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3637.essence: Joy bows naturally before grace, and duty moves only with permission.
ramacharitamanas::3637.simple_meaning: Sita is overjoyed when she hears Ram's words and bows to him. Ram then asks the sage's permission to move on to another forest.
ramacharitamanas::3637.simple_insight: True devotion softens the heart into gratitude and respect.
ramacharitamanas::3637.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sita hears Ram speak with such grace that she feels deep joy and bows to him. Ram then asks the sage for permission to leave and continue to another forest. The verse shows reverence, humility, and the calm movement of dharma.
ramacharitamanas::3637.modern_relevance: You finally hear the apology you needed, and your chest loosens before you even answer. Respect returns first, then words.
ramacharitamanas::3637.insight: It models a response of gratitude and humility before moving on.

ramacharitamanas::3638.verse_sanskrit: संतत मो पर कृपा करेहू। सेवक जानि तजेहु जनि नेहू॥ धर्म धुरंधर प्रभु कै बानी। सुनि सप्रेम बोले मुनि ग्यानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3638.verse_hindi: मुझ पर निरंतर कृपा करते रहिएगा और अपना सेवक जानकर स्नेह न छोड़िएगा। धर्म धुरंधर प्रभु श्री रामजी के वचन सुनकर ज्ञानी मुनि प्रेमपूर्वक बोले- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3638.english_translation: “Please keep showing me your grace without end. Seeing me as your servant, do not withdraw your affection.” Hearing the words of Dharma's upholder, the wise sage spoke with love.
ramacharitamanas::3638.translation_literal: संतत (continually) / मो (on me) / पर (upon) / कृपा (grace) / करेहू (do keep doing) । / सेवक (servant) / जानि (knowing) / तजेहु (do not abandon) / जनि (do not) / नेहू (affection) ॥ / धर्म (dharma) / धुरंधर (bearer) / प्रभु (Lord) / कै (of) / बानी (words) । / सुनि (hearing) / सप्रेम (with love) / बोले (spoke) / मुनि (sage) / ग्यानी (wise) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3638.speaker: Muni
ramacharitamanas::3638.essence: Devotion asks for nothing except continued grace.
ramacharitamanas::3638.simple_meaning: The sage asks Ram to keep showing kindness and not stop loving him just because he is a servant.
ramacharitamanas::3638.simple_insight: Real devotion does not ask for rewards — only for continued nearness.
ramacharitamanas::3638.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram speaks with the sage after Sita has bowed with relief. Ram's gentle words move the sage deeply, and he answers not with theory but with a humble plea: keep your grace flowing, and do not withdraw your affection from your servant.
ramacharitamanas::3638.modern_relevance: After a hard conversation, you text someone one more time not to ask for anything, just to stay connected. That quiet need to remain held is what this verse understands.
ramacharitamanas::3638.insight: It shifts devotion from getting something to remaining in loving relation.

ramacharitamanas::3639.verse_sanskrit: जासु कृपा अज सिव सनकादी। चहत सकल परमारथ बादी॥ ते तुम्ह राम अकाम पिआरे। दीन बंधु मृदु बचन उचारे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3639.verse_hindi: ब्रह्मा, शिव और सनकादि सभी परमार्थवादी (तत्ववेत्ता) जिनकी कृपा चाहते हैं, हे रामजी! आप वही निष्काम पुरुषों के भी प्रिय और दीनों के बंधु भगवान हैं, जो इस प्रकार कोमल वचन बोल रहे हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3639.english_translation: Brahma, Shiva, and the sages of deep insight all long for your grace. You are the dear one of the desireless and the friend of the humble, yet you speak so gently.
ramacharitamanas::3639.translation_literal: जासु (whose) / कृपा (grace) / अज (Brahma) / सिव (Shiva) / सनकादी (Sanaka and others) / चहत (desire) / सकल (all) / परमारथ बादी (seekers of the supreme aim)॥ / ते (you) / तुम्ह (you) / राम (Ram) / अकाम (desireless) / पिआरे (dear) / दीन बंधु (friend of the humble) / मृदु (gentle) / बचन (words) / उचारे (spoke)॥
ramacharitamanas::3639.speaker: Muni
ramacharitamanas::3639.essence: True greatness stays tender and is loved by the desireless.
ramacharitamanas::3639.simple_meaning: Even the highest seekers long for Ram's grace, yet he remains gentle and loving toward the humble and desireless.
ramacharitamanas::3639.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing greatness can be tender, not distant.
ramacharitamanas::3639.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sage speaks to Ram after hearing his humble request. He praises Ram as the one even Brahma, Shiva, and the sages seek, yet who remains the friend of the humble and the beloved of those without desire.
ramacharitamanas::3639.modern_relevance: You meet someone whose title could make them cold, but they still speak softly to the cleaner, the child, the overlooked person in the room. That kind of greatness feels like relief.
ramacharitamanas::3639.insight: It shifts respect away from status and toward gentleness, humility, and inner freedom.

ramacharitamanas::3640.verse_sanskrit: अब जानी मैं श्री चतुराई। भजी तुम्हहि सब देव बिहाई॥ जेहि समान अतिसय नहिं कोई। ता कर सील कस न अस होई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3640.verse_hindi: अब मैंने लक्ष्मीजी की चतुराई समझी, जिन्होंने सब देवताओं को छोड़कर आप ही को भजा। जिसके समान (सब बातों में) अत्यन्त बड़ा और कोई नहीं है, उसका शील भला, ऐसा क्यों न होगा? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3640.english_translation: Now I understand Lakshmi's wisdom: she abandoned all other radiant beings and worshipped only you. One greater than all others must surely have noble character.
ramacharitamanas::3640.translation_literal: अब (now) / जानी (understood) / मैं (I) / श्री (Lakshmi) / चतुराई (wisdom/craft) / भजी (worshipped) / तुम्हहि (you alone) / सब (all) / देव (radiant beings) / बिहाई (leaving aside)॥ / जेहि (whose) / समान (equal) / अतिसय (greatly) / नहिं (not) / कोई (anyone) / ता कर (of that one) / सील (noble character) / कस (how) / न (not) / अस (like this) / होई (be) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3640.speaker: Muni
ramacharitamanas::3640.essence: The highest being naturally draws the most complete devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3640.simple_meaning: Lakshmi is praised for leaving aside every other radiant being and choosing Ram alone, because the one who is greatest must also have the noblest character.
ramacharitamanas::3640.simple_insight: Devotion becomes clear when you recognize what is truly highest and stop dividing your heart.
ramacharitamanas::3640.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sage speaks to Ram with growing awe. He realises that Lakshmi herself chose Ram over all other radiant beings. That choice reveals Ram's unmatched greatness and the natural nobility of his character.
ramacharitamanas::3640.modern_relevance: You keep checking three different options, hoping one will feel right. Then you meet someone whose presence makes the rest feel small. The mind settles because it has recognized what it was really looking for.
ramacharitamanas::3640.insight: It shifts devotion from blind feeling to clear recognition of what deserves your whole heart.

ramacharitamanas::3641.verse_sanskrit: केहि बिधि कहौं जाहु अब स्वामी। कहहु नाथ तुम्ह अंतरजामी॥ अस कहि प्रभु बिलोकि मुनि धीरा। लोचन जल बह पुलक सरीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3641.verse_hindi: मैं किस प्रकार कहूँ कि हे स्वामी! आप अब जाइए? हे नाथ! आप अन्तर्यामी हैं, आप ही कहिए। ऐसा कहकर धीर मुनि प्रभु को देखने लगे। मुनि के नेत्रों से (प्रेमाश्रुओं का) जल बह रहा है और शरीर पुलकित है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3641.english_translation: How can I say, "Go now, my Lord"? O Master, you are the inner knower; you yourself speak. Saying this, the steadfast sage looked upon the Lord, and tears flowed from his eyes while his body shivered with love.
ramacharitamanas::3641.translation_literal: केहि बिधि (in what way) / कहौं (may I say) / जाहु (go) / अब (now) / स्वामी (master) / कहहु (speak) / नाथ (lord) / तुम्ह (you) / अंतरजामी (inner knower) / अस (thus) / कहि (having said) / प्रभु (the Lord) / बिलोकि (seeing) / मुनि (sage) / धीरा (steadfast) / लोचन (eyes) / जल (water/tears) / बह (flowed) / पुलक (horripilation) / सरीरा (body)
ramacharitamanas::3641.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3641.essence: When love is complete, even farewell becomes surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3641.simple_meaning: The sage cannot bring himself to ask Ram to leave. Since Ram knows every heart, he can only speak with tears and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3641.simple_insight: Love becomes wordless when you feel fully seen.
ramacharitamanas::3641.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sage stands before Ram with tears in his eyes. He cannot bear to say goodbye directly, because Ram already knows the heart. The moment turns farewell into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3641.modern_relevance: You sit across from someone who has helped you through your worst week, and the goodbye sticks in your throat. Some feelings are too full for explanation.
ramacharitamanas::3641.insight: It shifts speech from asking to trusting that the other already understands.

ramacharitamanas::3642.verse_sanskrit: तन पुलक निर्भर प्रेम पूरन नयन मुख पंकज दिए। मन ग्यान गुन गोतीत प्रभु मैं दीख जप तप का किए॥ जप जोग धर्म समूह तें नर भगति अनुपम पावई। रघुबीर चरित पुनीत निसि दिन दास तुलसी गावई॥
ramacharitamanas::3642.verse_hindi: मुनि अत्यन्त प्रेम से पूर्ण हैं, उनका शरीर पुलकित है और नेत्रों को श्री रामजी के मुखकमल में लगाए हुए हैं। (मन में विचार रहे हैं कि) मैंने ऐसे कौन से जप-तप किए थे, जिसके कारण मन, ज्ञान, गुण और इन्द्रियों से परे प्रभु के दर्शन पाए। जप, योग और धर्म समूह से मनुष्य अनुपम भक्ति को पाता है। श्री रघुवीर के पवित्र चरित्र को तुलसीदास रात-दिन गाता है।
ramacharitamanas::3642.english_translation: My body is bristling with love; my eyes stay fixed on Ram's lotus face. I wonder what penance I performed to see the Lord beyond mind, wisdom, qualities, and senses. Through chanting, yoga, and all duties, a person gains incomparable devotion. Tulsidas sings the pure deeds of Raghuvir day and night.
ramacharitamanas::3642.translation_literal: तन (body) / पुलक (bristling) / निर्भर (full) / प्रेम (love) / पूरन (complete) / नयन (eyes) / मुख (face) / पंकज (lotus) / दिए (fixed) / मन (mind) / ग्यान (knowledge) / गुन (qualities) / गोतीत (beyond) / प्रभु (Lord) / मैं (I) / दीख (saw) / जप (chanting) / तप (austerity) / का (what) / किए (did) / जप (chanting) / जोग (yoga) / धर्म (duty) / समूह (group/collection) / तें (from) / नर (person) / भगति (devotion) / अनुपम (matchless) / पावई (obtains) / रघुबीर (Ram) / चरित (deeds) / पुनीत (pure) / निसि दिन (night and day) / दास तुलसी (servant Tulsidas) / गावई (sings)
ramacharitamanas::3642.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3642.essence: Devotion gives you what effort alone cannot reach.
ramacharitamanas::3642.simple_meaning: The poet is overwhelmed by Ram's presence and says that true devotion is greater than chanting, yoga, or ritual duty. He keeps singing Ram's pure story day and night.
ramacharitamanas::3642.simple_insight: You do not have to earn love by force; devotion can arrive as grace and transform everything.
ramacharitamanas::3642.detailed_meaning: The sage has just spoken to Ram in the forest and is struck speechless by the divine presence before him. His body shivers with love, his eyes cannot leave Ram's face, and he realizes that no amount of practice alone explains this blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3642.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone whose presence makes your rehearsed lines disappear. In that moment, trying harder feels smaller than simply opening your heart and letting reverence do the work.
ramacharitamanas::3642.insight: It shifts the mind from spiritual achievement to loving absorption as the real source of fulfillment.

ramacharitamanas::3643.verse_sanskrit: कलिमल समन दमन मन राम सुजस सुखमूल। सादर सुनहिं जे तिन्ह पर राम रहहिं अनुकूल ॥
ramacharitamanas::3643.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का सुंदर यश कलियुग के पापों का नाश करने वाला, मन को दमन करने वाला और सुख का मूल है, जो लोग इसे आदरपूर्वक सुनते हैं, उन पर श्री रामजी प्रसन्न रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3643.english_translation: Ram's beautiful fame destroys the stains of Kali, calms the mind, and is the root of joy. Those who listen to it with reverence receive Ram's favor.
ramacharitamanas::3643.translation_literal: कलिमल (the stains of Kali) / समन (destroying) / दमन (subduing) / मन (mind) / राम सुजस (Ram's good fame) / सुखमूल (root of joy) / सादर (with reverence) / सुनहिं (they listen) / जे (who) / तिन्ह पर (upon them) / राम (Ram) / रहहिं (remain) / अनुकूल (favourable)
ramacharitamanas::3643.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3643.essence: Reverent listening turns Ram's praise into inner medicine.
ramacharitamanas::3643.simple_meaning: Ram's fame clears away the stains of the age, quiets the mind, and brings joy. Anyone who listens respectfully gains Ram's grace.
ramacharitamanas::3643.simple_insight: What you take in shapes you. Reverent listening can steady the mind and make room for grace.
ramacharitamanas::3643.detailed_meaning: After meeting the sage, the verse turns from his devotion to a wider promise for everyone. In this dark age, Ram's praise itself becomes medicine: it cleans the mind, brings joy, and draws Ram's favor toward anyone who listens with respect.
ramacharitamanas::3643.modern_relevance: You put on a podcast while cooking, but half your mind is elsewhere. Then one line lands, and the room feels different. What you receive with attention can change you.
ramacharitamanas::3643.insight: It shifts attention from passive hearing to reverent reception, where the mind is purified by what it truly takes in.

ramacharitamanas::3644.verse_sanskrit: कठिन काल मल कोस धर्म न ग्यान न जोग जप। परिहरि सकल भरोस रामहि भजहिं ते चतुर नर ॥
ramacharitamanas::3644.verse_hindi: यह कठिन कलि काल पापों का खजाना है, इसमें न धर्म है, न ज्ञान है और न योग तथा जप ही है। इसमें तो जो लोग सब भरोसों को छोड़कर श्री रामजी को ही भजते हैं, वे ही चतुर हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3644.english_translation: This is the hard age of Kali, full of corruption. Dharma, knowledge, yoga, and chanting are all scarce here. Wise people abandon every other refuge and worship Ram alone.
ramacharitamanas::3644.translation_literal: कठिन (hard) / काल (age) / मल (corruption) / कोस (storehouse) / धर्म (dharma) / न (not) / ग्यान (knowledge) / न (not) / जोग (yoga) / जप (chanting) / परिहरि (abandoning) / सकल (all) / भरोस (refuges) / रामहि (Ram alone) / भजहिं (worship) / ते (they) / चतुर (wise) / नर (people)
ramacharitamanas::3644.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3644.essence: Real wisdom in a broken age is to lean on Ram alone.
ramacharitamanas::3644.simple_meaning: In this difficult age, ordinary supports are weak. The wise stop leaning on everything else and turn to Ram alone.
ramacharitamanas::3644.simple_insight: You can stop scattering your trust and rest in one steady refuge.
ramacharitamanas::3644.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is speaking in Aranyakand as the forest journey begins and the age of Kali is named for its moral weakness. He says that when dharma, knowledge, yoga, and chanting feel unavailable, the clever response is not despair but single-minded devotion to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3644.modern_relevance: You’ve tried three self-help books, a podcast, and another plan, but the anxiety is still there. This verse says the smartest move may be simpler than your mind wants: stop outsourcing your peace.
ramacharitamanas::3644.insight: It shifts the mind from divided dependence to single-hearted devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3645.verse_sanskrit: मुनि पद कमल नाइ करि सीसा। चले बनहि सुर नर मुनि ईसा॥ आगें राम अनुज पुनि पाछें। मुनि बर बेष बने अति काछें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3645.verse_hindi: मुनि के चरण कमलों में सिर नवाकर देवता, मनुष्य और मुनियों के स्वामी श्री रामजी वन को चले। आगे श्री रामजी हैं और उनके पीछे छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी हैं। दोनों ही मुनियों का सुंदर वेष बनाए अत्यन्त सुशोभित हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3645.english_translation: Bowing their heads to the sages' lotus feet, they walked into the forest. Ram went first, Lakshman behind him, both dressed beautifully like ascetics.
ramacharitamanas::3645.translation_literal: मुनि (sages) / पद (feet) / कमल (lotus) / नाइ (bowing) / करि (having done) / सीसा (head) / चले (walked) / बनहि (to the forest) / सुर (gods) / नर (humans) / मुनि (sages) / ईसा (lords) / आगें (in front) / राम (Ram) / अनुज (younger brother) / पुनि (then) / पाछें (behind) / मुनि (ascetic) / बर (excellent) / बेष (dress) / बने (became) / अति (very) / काछें (handsome, close-fitting)
ramacharitamanas::3645.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3645.essence: Humility opens the road before the journey starts.
ramacharitamanas::3645.simple_meaning: Ram and Lakshman respectfully bow to the sages and then walk into the forest, dressed like holy men, with Ram leading and Lakshman following.
ramacharitamanas::3645.simple_insight: Respect comes first; only then does the journey begin.
ramacharitamanas::3645.detailed_meaning: After honoring the sages, Ram and Lakshman leave for the forest. Ram walks ahead, Lakshman follows, and both wear the simple dress of ascetics. The scene quietly prepares the deeper symbolic vision that comes next.
ramacharitamanas::3645.modern_relevance: You leave a mentor's office after asking for guidance, then step back into a hard decision with humility still intact. The respect you showed changes how you carry the road ahead.
ramacharitamanas::3645.insight: It shows that true departure begins with reverence, not haste.

ramacharitamanas::3646.verse_sanskrit: उभय बीच श्री सोहइ कैसी। ब्रह्म जीव बिच माया जैसी॥ सरिता बन गिरि अवघट घाटा। पति पहिचानि देहिं बर बाटा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3646.verse_hindi: दोनों के बीच में श्री जानकीजी कैसी सुशोभित हैं, जैसे ब्रह्म और जीव के बीच माया हो। नदी, वन, पर्वत और दुर्गम घाटियाँ, सभी अपने स्वामी को पहचानकर सुंदर रास्ता दे देते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3646.english_translation: How beautiful Sita shines between the two, like Maya between Brahman and the individual self. Rivers, forests, mountains, and rough passes all recognise their lord and give him a fine path.
ramacharitamanas::3646.translation_literal: उभय (both) / बीच (between) / श्री (auspicious, radiant) / सोहइ (shines beautifully) / कैसी (how) / ब्रह्म (the supreme reality) / जीव (the individual self) / बिच (between) / माया (the veil of appearance) / जैसी (like)॥ / सरिता (rivers) / बन (forest) / गिरि (mountains) / अवघट (difficult) / घाटा (passes, slopes) / पति (lord, master) / पहिचानि (recognising) / देहिं (give) / बर (fine, excellent) / बाटा (path)॥
ramacharitamanas::3646.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3646.essence: Grace can make even rough ground feel like a path.
ramacharitamanas::3646.simple_meaning: Sita shines beautifully between Ram and Lakshman, like a radiant presence in the middle of a hard journey. Even rivers, forests, mountains, and steep passes seem to recognise their lord and make way.
ramacharitamanas::3646.simple_insight: Love changes the whole landscape; even difficulty feels guided when you walk with the beloved.
ramacharitamanas::3646.detailed_meaning: Ram, Lakshman, and Sita are walking into the forest after the exile begins. Tulsidas lingers on Sita's beauty and the reverence of the natural world around them. This is not just scenery; it shows the forest itself yielding to Ram's presence.
ramacharitamanas::3646.modern_relevance: You walk into a season that should feel harsh — a hospital corridor, a divorce meeting, a job loss — and something steady in you quietly makes the path feel less hostile.
ramacharitamanas::3646.insight: It shifts attention from hardship itself to the presence that makes hardship bearable.

ramacharitamanas::3647.verse_sanskrit: जहँ जहँ जाहिं देव रघुराया। करहिं मेघ तहँ तहँ नभ छाया॥ मिला असुर बिराध मग जाता। आवतहीं रघुबीर निपाता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3647.verse_hindi: जहाँ-जहाँ देव श्री रघुनाथजी जाते हैं, वहाँ-वहाँ बादल आकाश में छाया करते जाते हैं। रास्ते में जाते हुए विराध राक्षस मिला। सामने आते ही श्री रघुनाथजी ने उसे मार डाला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3647.english_translation: Wherever Lord Raghunath goes, clouds spread shade across the sky. On the road, the demon Viradh appeared. As soon as he came near, Raghubir struck him down.
ramacharitamanas::3647.translation_literal: जहँ जहँ (wherever) / जाहिं (go) / देव (divine) / रघुराया (Lord of Raghu) / करहिं (do) / मेघ (clouds) / तहँ तहँ (there and there) / नभ (sky) / छाया (shade) / मिला (met) / असुर (demon) / बिराध (Viradh) / मग (road) / जाता (going) / आवतहीं (coming) / रघुबीर (Raghubir) / निपाता (struck down)
ramacharitamanas::3647.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3647.essence: Ram's presence turns the path itself into protection.
ramacharitamanas::3647.simple_meaning: As Ram walks through the forest, nature responds to him, and Viradh the demon appears. Ram defeats him immediately.
ramacharitamanas::3647.simple_insight: Even in danger, the right presence changes the whole atmosphere.
ramacharitamanas::3647.detailed_meaning: Ram, Sita, and Lakshman are moving deeper into the forest. The path itself seems to honor Ram as clouds cast shade overhead. Then Viradh, a hostile force in the forest, blocks the way, and Ram ends the threat at once.
ramacharitamanas::3647.modern_relevance: You walk into a tense room and the mood shifts before you say a word. Some presence calms the space; some problems disappear the moment they are faced.
ramacharitamanas::3647.insight: It shows Ram's presence as protective and decisive, while also moving the story toward the next encounter.

ramacharitamanas::3648.verse_sanskrit: तुरतहिं रुचिर रूप तेहिं पावा। देखि दुखी निज धाम पठावा॥ पुनि आए जहँ मुनि सरभंगा। सुंदर अनुज जानकी संगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3648.verse_hindi: (श्री रामजी के हाथ से मरते ही) उसने तुरंत सुंदर (दिव्य) रूप प्राप्त कर लिया। दुःखी देखकर प्रभु ने उसे अपने परम धाम को भेज दिया। फिर वे सुंदर छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी के साथ वहाँ आए जहाँ मुनि शरभंगजी थे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3648.english_translation: At once he received a beautiful form. Seeing his sorrow, the Lord sent him to his own supreme abode. Then Ram came there with the lovely younger brother Lakshman and Sita, to where the sage Sarabhanga was.
ramacharitamanas::3648.translation_literal: तुरतहिं (immediately) / रुचिर (beautiful) / रूप (form) / तेहिं (he) / पावा (obtained) / देखि (seeing) / दुखी (sorrowful) / निज (own) / धाम (abode) / पठावा (sent) / पुनि (again) / आए (came) / जहँ (where) / मुनि (sage) / सरभंगा (Sarabhanga) / सुंदर (beautiful) / अनुज (younger brother) / जानकी (Janaki) / संगा (with)
ramacharitamanas::3648.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3648.essence: True compassion ends suffering and then lets the soul move on.
ramacharitamanas::3648.simple_meaning: The sage’s suffering ends immediately, and Ram sends him onward. Then Ram, Lakshman, and Sita arrive at Sarabhanga’s hermitage.
ramacharitamanas::3648.simple_insight: Grace arrives when sorrow is seen clearly and met without delay.
ramacharitamanas::3648.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram meets the sage Sarabhanga after the earlier encounter with Viradha. The sage’s long austerity has reached its fulfilment, and Ram sends him onward in peace. Then Ram, Lakshman, and Sita continue to Sarabhanga’s hermitage.
ramacharitamanas::3648.modern_relevance: A hospital room goes quiet after the doctor gives the final answer, and the family finally exhales. What was waiting in pain can now move on with dignity.
ramacharitamanas::3648.insight: It shows that compassion does not merely comfort suffering; it also knows when to release it.

ramacharitamanas::3649.verse_sanskrit: देखि राम मुख पंकज मुनिबर लोचन भृंग। सादर पान करत अति धन्य जन्म सरभंग ॥
ramacharitamanas::3649.verse_hindi: श्री रामचन्द्रजी का मुखकमल देखकर मुनिश्रेष्ठ के नेत्र रूपी भौंरे अत्यन्त आदरपूर्वक उसका (मकरन्द रस) पान कर रहे हैं। शरभंगजी का जन्म धन्य है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3649.english_translation: Seeing Ram's lotus face, the great sage's eyes, like bees, drink it with reverence. Sarabhanga's birth is truly blessed.
ramacharitamanas::3649.translation_literal: देखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / मुख पंकज (lotus face) / मुनिबर (best of sages) / लोचन (eyes) / भृंग (bees) / सादर (with reverence) / पान करत (drinking) / अति (very) / धन्य (blessed) / जन्म (birth) / सरभंग (Sarabhanga)
ramacharitamanas::3649.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3649.essence: Seeing Ram is itself a blessing that fulfills a life.
ramacharitamanas::3649.simple_meaning: The sage looks at Ram's beautiful face with loving reverence, as bees drink nectar from a lotus. Sarabhanga's life becomes blessed by that sight.
ramacharitamanas::3649.simple_insight: Devotion can turn even seeing into worship, and worship into blessing.
ramacharitamanas::3649.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram arrives before Sarabhanga. The sage has long waited for this meeting, and now even his eyes behave like bees around a lotus. The verse pauses the story to show how blessed a human life becomes when it finally beholds Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3649.modern_relevance: You catch a glimpse of someone you deeply love across a crowded station, and everything else fades. That single sight can make a hard day feel sacred.
ramacharitamanas::3649.insight: It shifts attention from ordinary looking to reverent seeing, where the mind drinks in what it cherishes.

ramacharitamanas::3650.verse_sanskrit: कह मुनि सुनु रघुबीर कृपाला। संकर मानस राजमराला॥ जात रहेउँ बिरंचि के धामा। सुनेउँ श्रवन बन ऐहहिं रामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3650.verse_hindi: मुनि ने कहा- हे कृपालु रघुवीर! हे शंकरजी मन रूपी मानसरोवर के राजहंस! सुनिए, मैं ब्रह्मलोक को जा रहा था। (इतने में) कानों से सुना कि श्री रामजी वन में आवेंगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3650.english_translation: The sage said, “Listen, compassionate Lord Raghuvir, swan of Shiva’s Manasarovar mind. I was on my way to Brahmaloka when I heard through my ears that Ram would come to the forest.”
ramacharitamanas::3650.translation_literal: कह (said) / मुनि (sage) / सुनु (listen) / रघुबीर (Lord Raghuvir) / कृपाला (compassionate) । संकर (Shiva) / मानस (mind-lake) / राजमराला (royal swan) । जात (going) / रहेउँ (I was) / बिरंचि (Brahma) / के (of) / धामा (abode) । सुनेउँ (I heard) / श्रवन (through the ears) / बन (forest) / ऐहहिं (will come) / रामा (Ram) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3650.speaker: Muni
ramacharitamanas::3650.essence: Even Brahmaloka can wait when Ram is near.
ramacharitamanas::3650.simple_meaning: The sage tells Ram that he was on his way to Brahmaloka, but the news that Ram would come to the forest made him stop and wait with devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3650.simple_insight: When your heart is set on Ram, even the highest goal loses its pull.
ramacharitamanas::3650.detailed_meaning: Sarabhanga has just been blessed and sent on. Now the sage speaks to Ram with reverence, calling Him Shiva’s royal swan. He says he was heading toward Brahmaloka, but the moment he heard Ram would enter the forest, he turned his attention fully to that meeting.
ramacharitamanas::3650.modern_relevance: You were about to chase the next milestone, then a message came from someone you love and everything else went quiet. Some arrivals matter more than promotion, plans, or prestige.
ramacharitamanas::3650.insight: It shifts the mind from chasing higher destinations to recognising what is truly worth waiting for.

ramacharitamanas::3651.verse_sanskrit: चितवत पंथ रहेउँ दिन राती। अब प्रभु देखि जुड़ानी छाती॥ नाथ सकल साधन मैं हीना। कीन्ही कृपा जानि जन दीना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3651.verse_hindi: तब से मैं दिन-रात आपकी राह देखता रहा हूँ। अब (आज) प्रभु को देखकर मेरी छाती शीतल हो गई। हे नाथ! मैं सब साधनों से हीन हूँ। आपने अपना दीन सेवक जानकर मुझ पर कृपा की है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3651.english_translation: I kept watching the path day and night. Now that I have seen the Lord, my heart is soothed. O Lord, I am without all means. Seeing me as a humble servant, you have shown me grace.
ramacharitamanas::3651.translation_literal: चितवत (watching) / पंथ (the path) / रहेउँ (I remained) / दिन (day) / राती (night) / अब (now) / प्रभु (Lord) / देखि (having seen) / जुड़ानी (became soothed) / छाती (heart/chest) / नाथ (O Lord) / सकल (all) / साधन (means) / मैं (I) / हीना (without) / कीन्ही (did) / कृपा (grace) / जानि (knowing) / जन (servant) / दीना (humble)
ramacharitamanas::3651.speaker: Sarbhang
ramacharitamanas::3651.essence: Meeting the Lord turns waiting into peace and lack into grace.
ramacharitamanas::3651.simple_meaning: A seeker says he watched for the Lord day and night, and now that he has seen him, his heart is calm. He feels unworthy and sees the meeting as grace.
ramacharitamanas::3651.simple_insight: Longing becomes relief when the one you seek finally appears.
ramacharitamanas::3651.detailed_meaning: Sarbhang has spent his days waiting for Ram's arrival in the forest. At last, Ram stands before him, and the old seeker feels his chest ease. What follows is not pride but humility: he has nothing to offer, only gratitude.
ramacharitamanas::3651.modern_relevance: You kept checking your phone for one message that mattered more than the rest. When it finally came, the anxiety dropped out of your body. Recognition can feel like grace.
ramacharitamanas::3651.insight: It shifts attention from lack to gratitude, and from self-importance to humble reception.

ramacharitamanas::3652.verse_sanskrit: सो कछु देव न मोहि निहोरा। निज पन राखेउ जन मन चोरा॥ तब लगि रहहु दीन हित लागी। जब लगि मिलौं तुम्हहि तनु त्यागी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3652.verse_hindi: हे देव! यह कुछ मुझ पर आपका एहसान नहीं है। हे भक्त-मनचोर! ऐसा करके आपने अपने प्रण की ही रक्षा की है। अब इस दीन के कल्याण के लिए तब तक यहाँ ठहरिए, जब तक मैं शरीर छोड़कर आपसे (आपके धाम में न) मिलूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3652.english_translation: O divine one, this is no favor done to me. You have only kept your own vow, O stealer of hearts. Stay here for this helpless one’s welfare until I leave my body and meet you.
ramacharitamanas::3652.translation_literal: सो (this) / कछु (something) / देव (divine one) / न (not) / मोहि (to me) / निहोरा (favor, obligation) / निज (own) / पन (vow) / राखेउ (kept) / जन (heart) / मन (mind) / चोरा (stealer) / तब (then) / लगि (until) / रहहु (stay) / दीन (helpless) / हित (welfare) / लागी (for) / जब (when) / लगि (until) / मिलौं (I meet) / तुम्हहि (you) / तनु (body) / त्यागी (having left)
ramacharitamanas::3652.speaker: Muni
ramacharitamanas::3652.essence: Devotion receives grace as the keeping of a sacred promise.
ramacharitamanas::3652.simple_meaning: The sage says Ram has not done him a personal favor; Ram has simply upheld his own promise. He asks Ram to remain until his death, for the sage’s welfare.
ramacharitamanas::3652.simple_insight: Real devotion sees grace as promise-keeping, not as debt.
ramacharitamanas::3652.detailed_meaning: Sarabhanga has finally met Ram in the forest. Overwhelmed, he refuses to treat Ram’s presence as a personal favor and instead sees it as Ram keeping his own sacred vow. He then asks Ram to remain for his welfare until he leaves the body.
ramacharitamanas::3652.modern_relevance: You finally hear back from the person you trusted, and they show up exactly when they said they would. The relief is not that they “did you a favor” — it’s that their word held.
ramacharitamanas::3652.insight: It shifts gratitude from feeling indebted to recognising faithful presence.

ramacharitamanas::3653.verse_sanskrit: जोग जग्य जप तप ब्रत कीन्हा। प्रभु कहँ देइ भगति बर लीन्हा॥ एहि बिधि सर रचि मुनि सरभंगा। बैठे हृदयँ छाड़ि सब संगा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3653.verse_hindi: योग, यज्ञ, जप, तप जो कुछ व्रत आदि भी मुनि ने किया था, सब प्रभु को समर्पण करके बदले में भक्ति का वरदान ले लिया। इस प्रकार (दुर्लभ भक्ति प्राप्त करके फिर) चिता रचकर मुनि शरभंगजी हृदय से सब आसक्ति छोड़कर उस पर जा बैठे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3653.english_translation: The sage performed yoga, sacrifice, chanting, austerity, and vows, and offered them all to the Lord, receiving the boon of devotion. In this way, the sage Sharabhanga built a fire, gave up all attachment in his heart, and sat upon it.
ramacharitamanas::3653.translation_literal: जोग (yoga) / जग्य (sacrifice) / जप (chanting) / तप (austerity) / ब्रत (vows) / कीन्हा (did) / प्रभु (Lord) / कहँ (to) / देइ (giving) / भगति (devotion) / बर (boon) / लीन्हा (took) / एहि (this) / बिधि (way) / सर (fire) / रचि (having made) / मुनि (sage) / सरभंगा (Sharabhanga) / बैठे (sat) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / छाड़ि (leaving) / सब (all) / संगा (attachment)
ramacharitamanas::3653.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3653.essence: Everything disciplined can be surrendered into devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3653.simple_meaning: Sharabhanga gave Ram all his spiritual practices and received devotion in return. Then he let go of every attachment and turned fully inward toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3653.simple_insight: Letting go is not loss when it opens the heart to what matters most.
ramacharitamanas::3653.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sharabhanga has waited for Ram with a heart emptied of everything else. He hands over his long practice of yoga, sacrifice, chanting, austerity, and vows, and Ram gives him the rare gift of devotion. Then the sage leaves all attachment behind.
ramacharitamanas::3653.modern_relevance: You can spend years collecting techniques, rituals, and self-improvement habits, then realize none of them matter unless they open your heart. The real turning point is when practice stops being possession and becomes surrender.
ramacharitamanas::3653.insight: It shifts the goal from accumulating spiritual effort to offering it until only devotion remains.

ramacharitamanas::3654.verse_sanskrit: सीता अनुज समेत प्रभु नील जलद तनु स्याम। मम हियँ बसहु निरंतर सगुनरूप श्री राम ॥
ramacharitamanas::3654.verse_hindi: हे नीले मेघ के समान श्याम शरीर वाले सगुण रूप श्री रामजी! सीताजी और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित प्रभु (आप) निरंतर मेरे हृदय में निवास कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3654.english_translation: O Lord Ram, dark as a blue raincloud, with Sita and your younger brother beside you, dwell forever in my heart.
ramacharitamanas::3654.translation_literal: सीता (Sita) / अनुज (younger brother) / समेत (together with) / प्रभु (Lord) / नील (blue) / जलद (raincloud) / तनु (body) / स्याम (dark) / मम (my) / हियँ (heart) / बसहु (dwell) / निरंतर (continuously) / सगुनरूप (with form) / श्री राम (Lord Ram)
ramacharitamanas::3654.speaker: Sarabhanga
ramacharitamanas::3654.essence: Presence, not possessions, is the devotee's highest request.
ramacharitamanas::3654.simple_meaning: Sarabhanga asks Ram to stay in his heart forever, along with Sita and Lakshman, and praises Ram's beautiful dark form.
ramacharitamanas::3654.simple_insight: Love becomes complete when the heart stops asking for anything else.
ramacharitamanas::3654.detailed_meaning: Sarabhanga has met Ram in the forest and is ready to leave his body. Before departing, he does not ask for power or release from suffering. He asks only that Ram, with Sita and Lakshman, remain in his heart forever.
ramacharitamanas::3654.modern_relevance: After a long night of worry, you finally sit quietly and realize you do not need one more answer. What you need is presence — something steady enough to live in your heart.
ramacharitamanas::3654.insight: It shifts devotion from asking for gifts to asking for abiding presence.

ramacharitamanas::3655.verse_sanskrit: अस कहि जोग अगिनि तनु जारा। राम कृपाँ बैकुंठ सिधारा॥ ताते मुनि हरि लीन न भयऊ। प्रथमहिं भेद भगति बर लयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3655.verse_hindi: ऐसा कहकर शरभंगजी ने योगाग्नि से अपने शरीर को जला डाला और श्री रामजी की कृपा से वे वैकुंठ को चले गए। मुनि भगवान में लीन इसलिए नहीं हुए कि उन्होंने पहले ही भेद-भक्ति का वर ले लिया था ॥
ramacharitamanas::3655.english_translation: Having said this, he burned his body in the fire of yoga, and by Ram's grace went to Vaikuntha. The sage did not merge into the divine because he had already received the boon of devoted love with distinction.
ramacharitamanas::3655.translation_literal: अस कहि (having said this) / जोग (yoga) / अगिनि (fire) / तनु (body) / जारा (burned) / राम कृपाँ (by Ram's grace) / बैकुंठ (Vaikuntha) / सिधारा (departed) / ताते (therefore) / मुनि (sage) / हरि (the divine/Ram) / लीन (merged) / न (not) / भयऊ (became) / प्रथमहिं (already, first) / भेद (distinction) / भगति (devoted love) / बर (boon) / लयऊ (received)
ramacharitamanas::3655.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3655.essence: Love can stay personal and still lead beyond the body.
ramacharitamanas::3655.simple_meaning: Sharabhang did not dissolve into the divine in an impersonal way. He had already received a special kind of devotion that kept his loving relationship with Ram intact.
ramacharitamanas::3655.simple_insight: You do not have to erase your individuality to come close to the divine.
ramacharitamanas::3655.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sage Sharabhang has finished his spiritual practice and is ready to leave. He burns his body through yogic power and, by Ram's grace, reaches Vaikuntha. The verse explains that his devotion had a personal relationship, not a merging without distinction.
ramacharitamanas::3655.modern_relevance: You can spend years trying to disappear into a practice, a cause, or a role. This verse says closeness does not require self-erasure; love can remain personal and still be complete.
ramacharitamanas::3655.insight: It shifts devotion from self-erasure to loving relationship, where distinctness is not a flaw but a gift.

ramacharitamanas::3656.verse_sanskrit: रिषि निकाय मुनिबर गति देखी। सुखी भए निज हृदयँ बिसेषी॥ अस्तुति करहिं सकल मुनि बृंदा। जयति प्रनत हित करुना कंदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3656.verse_hindi: ऋषि समूह मुनि श्रेष्ठ शरभंगजी की यह (दुर्लभ) गति देखकर अपने हृदय में विशेष रूप से सुखी हुए। समस्त मुनिवृंद श्री रामजी की स्तुति कर रहे हैं (और कह रहे हैं) शरणागत हितकारी करुणा कन्द (करुणा के मूल) प्रभु की जय हो! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3656.english_translation: The sages saw the rare state of the great ascetic and felt a special joy in their hearts. All the sages praised Ram: victory to the compassionate one who helps those who seek refuge.
ramacharitamanas::3656.translation_literal: रिषि निकाय (group of sages) / मुनिबर (great among sages) / गति (state, destination) / देखी (seeing) / सुखी भए (became joyful) / निज (their own) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / बिसेषी (especially)॥ / अस्तुति (praise) / करहिं (they do) / सकल (all) / मुनि बृंदा (assemblies of sages) / जयति (victory to) / प्रनत (those who bow, the surrendered) / हित (for the good) / करुना कंदा (root of compassion) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3656.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3656.essence: Ram is praised as the compassionate refuge of the surrendered.
ramacharitamanas::3656.simple_meaning: The sages are glad to see Sarabhanga reach a blessed state, and they praise Ram as the compassionate one who helps those who take refuge in him.
ramacharitamanas::3656.simple_insight: It feels reassuring to see sincere effort end in grace.
ramacharitamanas::3656.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sages watch Sarabhanga leave his body and reach a higher realm through Ram's grace. Their joy turns into praise for Ram, whose compassion protects anyone who bows to him. This is a response scene, not the main teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3656.modern_relevance: You watch someone you respected finally find peace after years of struggle, and your first feeling is gratitude. Their ending becomes a reminder that mercy can meet sincere effort.
ramacharitamanas::3656.insight: It turns attention from the ascetic's achievement to Ram's grace as the real source of fulfilment.

ramacharitamanas::3657.verse_sanskrit: पुनि रघुनाथ चले बन आगे। मुनिबर बृंद बिपुल सँग लागे॥ अस्थि समूह देखि रघुराया। पूछी मुनिन्ह लागि अति दाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3657.verse_hindi: फिर श्री रघुनाथजी आगे वन में चले। श्रेष्ठ मुनियों के बहुत से समूह उनके साथ हो लिए। हड्डियों का ढेर देखकर श्री रघुनाथजी को बड़ी दया आई, उन्होंने मुनियों से पूछा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3657.english_translation: Then Raghunath moved deeper into the forest, and a great company of sages followed him. Seeing a heap of bones, Raghuraya felt deep compassion and asked the sages.
ramacharitamanas::3657.translation_literal: पुनि (then again) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / चले (went) / बन (forest) / आगे (ahead) / मुनिबर (best sages) / बृंद (group) / बिपुल (many) / सँग (with) / लागे (followed) / अस्थि (bones) / समूह (heap) / देखि (seeing) / रघुराया (Raghuraya) / पूछी (asked) / मुनिन्ह (the sages) / लागि (with) / अति (very) / दाया (compassion)
ramacharitamanas::3657.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3657.essence: Compassion begins when you truly see what remains after pain.
ramacharitamanas::3657.simple_meaning: Ram walks deeper into the forest with many sages beside him. When he sees a pile of bones, compassion rises immediately, and he asks the sages about it.
ramacharitamanas::3657.simple_insight: A tender heart notices suffering even before it is explained.
ramacharitamanas::3657.detailed_meaning: Ram continues through the forest after Sharbhang's departure, with many sages walking beside him. He notices a heap of bones left behind and feels immediate compassion. That sight leads him to ask what happened there, opening the next revelation.
ramacharitamanas::3657.modern_relevance: You pass a roadside memorial or an empty chair at a family gathering, and something in you goes quiet. Compassion begins the moment you notice what loss has left behind.
ramacharitamanas::3657.insight: It trains attention to move from scenery to suffering, so the heart responds before the mind explains.

ramacharitamanas::3658.verse_sanskrit: जानतहूँ पूछिअ कस स्वामी। सबदरसी तुम्ह अंतरजामी॥ निसिचर निकर सकल मुनि खाए। सुनि रघुबीर नयन जल छाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3658.verse_hindi: (मुनियों ने कहा) हे स्वामी! आप सर्वदर्शी (सर्वज्ञ) और अंतर्यामी (सबके हृदय की जानने वाले) हैं। जानते हुए भी (अनजान की तरह) हमसे कैसे पूछ रहे हैं? राक्षसों के दलों ने सब मुनियों को खा डाला है। (ये सब उन्हीं की हड्डियों के ढेर हैं)। यह सुनते ही श्री रघुवीर के नेत्रों में जल छा गया (उनकी आँखों में करुणा के आँसू भर आए) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3658.english_translation: “You already know everything, Lord. You are the inner knower of all. Yet you ask us anyway? The whole of these sages has been devoured by bands of demons.” Hearing this, Ram’s eyes filled with tears.
ramacharitamanas::3658.translation_literal: जानतहूँ (even while knowing) / पूछिअ (you ask) / कस (how) / स्वामी (Lord) / सबदरसी (all-seeing) / तुम्ह (you) / अंतरजामी (inner knower) / निसिचर निकर (bands of demons) / सकल मुनि (all sages) / खाए (devoured) / सुनि (hearing) / रघुबीर (Ram) / नयन जल (water in the eyes) / छाए (filled)
ramacharitamanas::3658.speaker: Muni
ramacharitamanas::3658.essence: Perfect awareness can still weep for suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3658.simple_meaning: The sages remind Ram that he already knows everything, then tell him how demons destroyed their communities. Ram responds with tears of compassion.
ramacharitamanas::3658.simple_insight: Being able to see everything does not make you cold; it can make you more tender.
ramacharitamanas::3658.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, Ram and the sages walk past a heap of bones left by demons. The sages tell him he is already aware of the whole story, yet they still speak. Ram hears their suffering and his eyes fill with tears.
ramacharitamanas::3658.modern_relevance: You hear a friend describe the same loss for the third time, and you still feel it in your chest. Real care does not get numb from repetition.
ramacharitamanas::3658.insight: It shifts you from detached knowing to felt response, showing that true awareness includes compassion.

ramacharitamanas::3659.verse_sanskrit: निसिचर हीन करउँ महि भुज उठाइ पन कीन्ह। सकल मुनिन्ह के आश्रमन्हि जाइ जाइ सुख दीन्ह ॥
ramacharitamanas::3659.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने भुजा उठाकर प्रण किया कि मैं पृथ्वी को राक्षसों से रहित कर दूँगा। फिर समस्त मुनियों के आश्रमों में जा-जाकर उनको (दर्शन एवं सम्भाषण का) सुख दिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3659.english_translation: Raising his arm, Ram vowed to rid the earth of all forest-dwelling demons. Then he went from one sage's hermitage to another, giving them the joy of his presence and conversation.
ramacharitamanas::3659.translation_literal: निसिचर (demons) / हीन (free of) / करउँ (I will make) / महि (earth) / भुज (arm) / उठाइ (raising) / पन (vow) / कीन्ह (made) / सकल (all) / मुनिन्ह (of the sages) / के (of) / आश्रमन्हि (hermitages) / जाइ जाइ (going to each) / सुख (joy) / दीन्ह (gave)
ramacharitamanas::3659.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3659.essence: Protection becomes real only when your promise reaches people.
ramacharitamanas::3659.simple_meaning: Ram vows to clear the earth of harmful beings, then visits the sages one by one and gives them comfort through his presence.
ramacharitamanas::3659.simple_insight: A true promise protects others first, not your own image.
ramacharitamanas::3659.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sages have just shown Ram the remains of lives ruined by demons. Moved by their suffering, Ram raises his arm and vows to free the earth from that fear. He then visits each hermitage, giving the sages relief and joy.
ramacharitamanas::3659.modern_relevance: You hear the damage in a friend's voice, then do more than sympathize. You show up, make a clear promise, and keep visiting until the fear loosens.
ramacharitamanas::3659.insight: It turns compassion into action: first a vow, then repeated presence where help is needed.

ramacharitamanas::3660.verse_sanskrit: मुनि अगस्ति कर सिष्य सुजाना। नाम सुतीछन रति भगवाना॥ मन क्रम बचन राम पद सेवक। सपनेहुँ आन भरोस न देवक ॥
ramacharitamanas::3660.verse_hindi: मुनि अगस्त्यजी के एक सुतीक्ष्ण नामक सुजान (ज्ञानी) शिष्य थे, उनकी भगवान में प्रीति थी। वे मन, वचन और कर्म से श्री रामजी के चरणों के सेवक थे। उन्हें स्वप्न में भी किसी दूसरे देवता का भरोसा नहीं था ॥
ramacharitamanas::3660.english_translation: Muni Agastya had a wise disciple named Suteekshna, whose heart was devoted to the Lord. With mind, speech, and body, he served Ram's feet; even in a dream, he trusted no other divine power.
ramacharitamanas::3660.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / अगस्ति (Agastya) / कर (of) / सिष्य (disciple) / सुजाना (wise) / नाम (named) / सुतीछन (Suteekshna) / रति (love/devotion) / भगवाना (to the Lord)॥ / मन (mind) / क्रम (speech) / बचन (word) / राम (Ram) / पद (feet) / सेवक (servant)॥ / सपनेहुँ (even in a dream) / आन (other) / भरोस (trust) / न (not) / देवक (of a radiant being)॥
ramacharitamanas::3660.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3660.essence: Wholehearted devotion leaves no room for divided trust.
ramacharitamanas::3660.simple_meaning: Suteekshna was a wise disciple of Agastya who loved Ram deeply. He served Ram with mind, speech, and body, and placed no trust in any other divine power.
ramacharitamanas::3660.simple_insight: Single-hearted devotion makes the mind steady and unconflicted.
ramacharitamanas::3660.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the narrator introduces Suteekshna, Agastya's wise disciple. Before Ram even reaches him, his identity is already clear: he belongs to Ram with thought, speech, and action, and he has no second refuge.
ramacharitamanas::3660.modern_relevance: You keep a backup plan for your backup plan, then wonder why your heart feels split. Suteekshna shows the peace of giving your trust to one center instead of scattering it everywhere.
ramacharitamanas::3660.insight: It shifts you from divided loyalty to undivided trust in Ram.

ramacharitamanas::3661.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु आगवनु श्रवन सुनि पावा। करत मनोरथ आतुर धावा॥ हे बिधि दीनबंधु रघुराया। मो से सठ पर करिहहिं दाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3661.verse_hindi: उन्होंने ज्यों ही प्रभु का आगमन कानों से सुन पाया, त्यों ही अनेक प्रकार के मनोरथ करते हुए वे आतुरता (शीघ्रता) से दौड़ चले। हे विधाता! क्या दीनबन्धु श्री रघुनाथजी मुझ जैसे दुष्ट पर भी दया करेंगे? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3661.english_translation: As soon as he heard of the Lord's arrival, he rushed forward in eagerness, full of hopes. 'O Providence, will the compassionate Raghunath show mercy even to a wretch like me?'
ramacharitamanas::3661.translation_literal: प्रभु (Lord's) / आगवनु (arrival) / श्रवन (by hearing) / सुनि (having heard) / पावा (he obtained) / करत (doing) / मनोरथ (hopes, desires) / आतुर (anxious, eager) / धावा (he ran) / हे (O) / बिधि (Providence) / दीनबंधु (friend of the humble) / रघुराया (Raghunath, king of Raghu's line) / मो से (to one like me) / सठ (wicked one) / पर (upon) / करिहहिं (will do) / दाया (mercy)
ramacharitamanas::3661.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3661.essence: Hope runs toward Ram even while doubt lingers.
ramacharitamanas::3661.simple_meaning: Hearing that Ram has arrived, the devotee rushes forward with hope, yet still wonders whether such mercy can reach someone like him.
ramacharitamanas::3661.simple_insight: Longing can move you before confidence does.
ramacharitamanas::3661.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a seeker hears that Ram has come nearby. That news alone makes him run, even though he still feels unworthy and unsure. The verse holds both eagerness and self-doubt in the same breath.
ramacharitamanas::3661.modern_relevance: You hear a message saying someone important has finally arrived, and you leave the room before finishing your reply. Your body knows hope before your mind can explain it.
ramacharitamanas::3661.insight: It shifts you from waiting passively to moving as soon as grace feels near.

ramacharitamanas::3662.verse_sanskrit: सहित अनुज मोहि राम गोसाईं। मिलिहहिं निज सेवक की नाईं॥ मोरे जियँ भरोस दृढ़ नाहीं। भगति बिरति न ग्यान मन माहीं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3662.verse_hindi: क्या स्वामी श्री रामजी छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित मुझसे अपने सेवक की तरह मिलेंगे? मेरे हृदय में दृढ़ विश्वास नहीं होता, क्योंकि मेरे मन में भक्ति, वैराग्य या ज्ञान कुछ भी नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3662.english_translation: Will Lord Ram come to meet me, along with Lakshman, like a servant? My heart has no firm confidence, and my mind holds no devotion, detachment, or wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::3662.translation_literal: सहित (along with) / अनुज (younger brother) / मोहि (to me) / राम गोसाईं (Lord Ram) / मिलिहहिं (will meet) / निज (his own) / सेवक (servant) / की नाईं (like)॥ / मोरे (my) / जियँ (heart) / भरोस (confidence) / दृढ़ (firm) / नाहीं (not) / भगति (devotion) / बिरति (detachment) / न (not) / ग्यान (wisdom) / मन माहीं (in the mind)॥
ramacharitamanas::3662.speaker: Sutikshna
ramacharitamanas::3662.essence: Ram meets the one who longs for him, even without spiritual credentials.
ramacharitamanas::3662.simple_meaning: Sutikshna longs to be met by Ram as a servant, but he feels unworthy because he lacks firm faith, devotion, detachment, and wisdom.
ramacharitamanas::3662.simple_insight: Even without spiritual strength, sincere longing can open the door to grace.
ramacharitamanas::3662.detailed_meaning: Sutikshna, the disciple of Sage Agastya, has rushed out after hearing that Ram has arrived nearby. In his humility, he wonders whether Ram and Lakshman would meet him at all. He feels spiritually empty, yet his longing itself is already turning him toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3662.modern_relevance: You sit in your parked car before walking into a room where everyone seems more composed, more devoted, more certain than you. You feel unready — but the longing to go in is already its own strength.
ramacharitamanas::3662.insight: It shifts the mind from self-disqualification to receptive trust.

ramacharitamanas::3663.verse_sanskrit: नहिं सतसंग जोग जप जागा। नहिं दृढ़ चरन कमल अनुरागा॥ एक बानि करुनानिधान की। सो प्रिय जाकें गति न आन की ॥
ramacharitamanas::3663.verse_hindi: मैंने न तो सत्संग, योग, जप अथवा यज्ञ ही किए हैं और न प्रभु के चरणकमलों में मेरा दृढ़ अनुराग ही है। हाँ, दया के भंडार प्रभु की एक बान है कि जिसे किसी दूसरे का सहारा नहीं है, वह उन्हें प्रिय होता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3663.english_translation: I have done no holy company, no yoga, no chanting, no sacrifice, and no steady love for the lotus feet. Yet the treasure of compassion has one habit: the one with no other support becomes dear to him.
ramacharitamanas::3663.translation_literal: नहिं (not) / सतसंग (holy company) / जोग (yoga) / जप (chanting) / जागा (sacrifice) / नहिं (not) / दृढ़ (firm) / चरन कमल (lotus feet) / अनुरागा (love) / एक (one) / बानि (habit) / करुनानिधान (treasure of compassion) / की (of) / सो (that) / प्रिय (dear) / जाकें (to whom) / गति (support/refuge) / न आन (no other) / की (of)
ramacharitamanas::3663.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3663.essence: Being helpless can make you most beloved to Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3663.simple_meaning: The speaker admits to having no spiritual practice or steady devotion, yet says Ram is especially kind to those who have nowhere else to turn.
ramacharitamanas::3663.simple_insight: You do not have to be spiritually accomplished to be held. Need itself can open the door.
ramacharitamanas::3663.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the speaker looks toward Ram with humility and self-doubt, feeling unworthy of meeting him. This verse turns that insecurity into hope: Ram's compassion naturally leans toward the person with no other refuge.
ramacharitamanas::3663.modern_relevance: You sit in a hospital waiting room, exhausted and stripped of all control. Nothing polished remains — only need. This verse says that is not a disqualification; it may be the very reason mercy comes close.
ramacharitamanas::3663.insight: It shifts the mind from earning grace to trusting that need can attract grace.

ramacharitamanas::3664.verse_sanskrit: होइहैं सुफल आजु मम लोचन। देखि बदन पंकज भव मोचन॥ निर्भर प्रेम मगन मुनि ग्यानी। कहि न जाइ सो दसा भवानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3664.verse_hindi: (भगवान की इस बान का स्मरण आते ही मुनि आनंदमग्न होकर मन ही मन कहने लगे-) अहा! भव बंधन से छुड़ाने वाले प्रभु के मुखारविंद को देखकर आज मेरे नेत्र सफल होंगे। (शिवजी कहते हैं-) हे भवानी! ज्ञानी मुनि प्रेम में पूर्ण रूप से निमग्न हैं। उनकी वह दशा कही नहीं जाती ॥
ramacharitamanas::3664.english_translation: Today my eyes will bear fruit by seeing the lotus face of the one who frees beings from bondage. O Bhavani, the sage and the wise are so immersed in love that their state cannot be described.
ramacharitamanas::3664.translation_literal: होइहैं (will become) / सुफल (fruitful) / आजु (today) / मम (my) / लोचन (eyes) / देखि (seeing) / बदन (face) / पंकज (lotus) / भव (worldly bondage) / मोचन (liberator) ॥ निर्भर (fully) / प्रेम (love) / मगन (absorbed) / मुनि (sage) / ग्यानी (the wise) / कहि (said) / न जाइ (cannot be said) / सो (that) / दसा (state) / भवानी (O Bhavani) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3664.speaker: Shiva
ramacharitamanas::3664.essence: Ram's sight makes longing feel complete before a word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3664.simple_meaning: Seeing Ram's lotus face will make the sage feel fulfilled. Love has carried the wise so deeply that their condition cannot even be put into words.
ramacharitamanas::3664.simple_insight: Love can be so complete that even a single glimpse feels like fulfillment.
ramacharitamanas::3664.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a sage remembers Ram and becomes overwhelmed before the meeting even happens. Shiva tells Bhavani that the wise lose themselves in love for Ram, and that this inner state is beyond ordinary speech.
ramacharitamanas::3664.modern_relevance: You catch sight of someone you have missed for years, and the whole day changes. Some moments do not just please you — they make your waiting feel worth it.
ramacharitamanas::3664.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract belief to a lived, overwhelming absorption that changes perception itself.

ramacharitamanas::3665.verse_sanskrit: दिसि अरु बिदिसि पंथ नहिं सूझा। को मैं चलेउँ कहाँ नहिं बूझा॥ कबहुँक फिरि पाछें पुनि जाई। कबहुँक नृत्य करइ गुन गाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3665.verse_hindi: उन्हें दिशा-विदिशा (दिशाएँ और उनके कोण आदि) और रास्ता, कुछ भी नहीं सूझ रहा है। मैं कौन हूँ और कहाँ जा रहा हूँ, यह भी नहीं जानते (इसका भी ज्ञान नहीं है)। वे कभी पीछे घूमकर फिर आगे चलने लगते हैं और कभी (प्रभु के) गुण गा-गाकर नाचने लगते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3665.english_translation: They could not tell east from west, or even which path to take. They did not know who they were or where they were going. Sometimes they turned back, and sometimes they danced while singing the divine qualities.
ramacharitamanas::3665.translation_literal: दिसि (direction) / अरु (and) / बिदिसि (intermediate directions) / पंथ (path) / नहिं (not) / सूझा (was seen) ॥ को (who) / मैं (I) / चलेउँ (went) / कहाँ (where) / नहिं (not) / बूझा (understood) ॥ कबहुँक (sometimes) / फिरि (turning) / पाछें (back) / पुनि (again) / जाई (goes) ॥ कबहुँक (sometimes) / नृत्य (dance) / करइ (does) / गुन (qualities) / गाई (singing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3665.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3665.essence: When devotion deepens, even direction and selfhood dissolve.
ramacharitamanas::3665.simple_meaning: Deep devotion makes a person lose track of direction, self-consciousness, and ordinary purpose. They move without planning, sometimes turning back, sometimes singing and dancing in joy.
ramacharitamanas::3665.simple_insight: There is relief in not needing control when the heart is completely carried by love.
ramacharitamanas::3665.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sages are so overwhelmed by Ram's presence that ordinary orientation disappears. They no longer care about direction, self, or destination; devotion itself becomes movement, song, and dance.
ramacharitamanas::3665.modern_relevance: You walk out of a concert or temple with tears in your eyes and no sense of time. For a few minutes, the usual map of self and schedule falls away, and only love remains.
ramacharitamanas::3665.insight: It shifts attention from managing the journey to being carried by devotion itself.

ramacharitamanas::3666.verse_sanskrit: अबिरल प्रेम भगति मुनि पाई। प्रभु देखैं तरु ओट लुकाई॥ अतिसय प्रीति देखि रघुबीरा। प्रगटे हृदयँ हरन भव भीरा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3666.verse_hindi: मुनि ने प्रगाढ़ प्रेमाभक्ति प्राप्त कर ली। प्रभु श्री रामजी वृक्ष की आड़ में छिपकर (भक्त की प्रेमोन्मत्त दशा) देख रहे हैं। मुनि का अत्यन्त प्रेम देखकर भवभय (आवागमन के भय) को हरने वाले श्री रघुनाथजी मुनि के हृदय में प्रकट हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3666.english_translation: The sage gained unbroken loving devotion. The Lord hid behind a tree to watch. Seeing such intense love, Raghubir appeared in the sage's heart and removed the fear of rebirth.
ramacharitamanas::3666.translation_literal: अबिरल (unbroken) / प्रेम (love) / भगति (devotion) / मुनि (sage) / पाई (having obtained) / प्रभु (Lord) / देखैं (to see) / तरु (tree) / ओट (behind the cover) / लुकाई (hiding) / अतिसय (excessive) / प्रीति (love) / देखि (seeing) / रघुबीरा (Raghubir) / प्रगटे (appeared) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / हरन (remover) / भव (worldly becoming) / भीरा (fear)
ramacharitamanas::3666.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3666.essence: Pure love makes Ram appear inside you.
ramacharitamanas::3666.simple_meaning: The sage's love for Ram becomes so intense that Ram reveals himself within the sage's heart and removes fear.
ramacharitamanas::3666.simple_insight: Deep devotion does not just reach outward; it changes what becomes present within you.
ramacharitamanas::3666.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sage's longing has become so pure that Ram hides behind a tree just to witness it. Then, moved by that love, Ram appears inside the sage's heart and frees him from fear of the cycle of rebirth.
ramacharitamanas::3666.modern_relevance: You sit alone after a hard prayer, a tearful chant, or a quiet walk, and suddenly the ache feels answered from inside. Love that sincere changes what your heart can hold.
ramacharitamanas::3666.insight: It shifts devotion from external seeking to inward presence, where fear loses its grip.

ramacharitamanas::3667.verse_sanskrit: मुनि मग माझ अचल होइ बैसा। पुलक सरीर पनस फल जैसा॥ तब रघुनाथ निकट चलि आए। देखि दसा निज जन मन भाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3667.verse_hindi: (हृदय में प्रभु के दर्शन पाकर) मुनि बीच रास्ते में अचल (स्थिर) होकर बैठ गए। उनका शरीर रोमांच से कटहल के फल के समान (कण्टकित) हो गया। तब श्री रघुनाथजी उनके पास चले आए और अपने भक्त की प्रेम दशा देखकर मन में बहुत प्रसन्न हुए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3667.english_translation: The sage sat motionless in the middle of the path, his body bristling like a jackfruit. Then Raghunath came near and was delighted to see the devotion of his own devotee.
ramacharitamanas::3667.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / मग (path) / माझ (middle) / अचल होइ (becoming still) / बैसा (sat) / पुलक (hairs standing on end) / सरीर (body) / पनस फल (jackfruit) / जैसा (like) / तब (then) / रघुनाथ (Raghunath) / निकट (near) / चलि आए (came) / देखि (seeing) / दसा (condition) / निज (own) / जन (devotee) / मन भाए (was pleased in heart)
ramacharitamanas::3667.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3667.essence: Devotion can freeze the body and still draw Ram closer.
ramacharitamanas::3667.simple_meaning: The sage becomes so absorbed in seeing Ram that he sits frozen in the road. Ram comes close and feels joy at the sight of that devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3667.simple_insight: Deep love can stop you in your tracks and still bring you closer to what you love.
ramacharitamanas::3667.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sage has just been overwhelmed by Ram's presence. He stops in the middle of the path, lost in devotional stillness, while his body shivers with emotion. Ram comes near and delights in seeing his devotee's condition.
ramacharitamanas::3667.modern_relevance: You catch yourself standing still after hearing a name that matters to you. Your chest tightens, your mind goes quiet, and the one you love feels suddenly near.
ramacharitamanas::3667.insight: It shows that devotion can make the body still and the heart vivid at once.

ramacharitamanas::3668.verse_sanskrit: मुनिहि राम बहु भाँति जगावा। जाग न ध्यान जनित सुख पावा॥ भूप रूप तब राम दुरावा। हृदयँ चतुर्भुज रूप देखावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3668.verse_hindi: श्री रामजी ने मुनि को बहुत प्रकार से जगाया, पर मुनि नहीं जागे, क्योंकि उन्हें प्रभु के ध्यान का सुख प्राप्त हो रहा था। तब श्री रामजी ने अपने राजरूप को छिपा लिया और उनके हृदय में अपना चतुर्भुज रूप प्रकट किया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3668.english_translation: Ram tried in many ways to wake the sage, but the sage did not wake, because he was tasting the bliss born of meditation. Then Ram hid his royal form and revealed His four-armed form in the sage’s heart.
ramacharitamanas::3668.translation_literal: मुनिहि (the sage) / राम (Ram) / बहु भाँति (in many ways) / जगावा (woke up) / जाग (wake) / न (not) / ध्यान (meditation) / जनित (born from) / सुख (bliss) / पावा (found) / भूप रूप (kingly form) / तब (then) / राम (Ram) / दुरावा (hid) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / चतुर्भुज रूप (four-armed form) / देखावा (showed)
ramacharitamanas::3668.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3668.essence: When the heart is full of Ram, ordinary waking loses its power.
ramacharitamanas::3668.simple_meaning: The sage is so absorbed in the joy of meditation that he cannot be awakened. Ram then hides His outer royal form and reveals a divine form within the sage’s heart.
ramacharitamanas::3668.simple_insight: Deep devotion can make ordinary waking feel too small for the heart.
ramacharitamanas::3668.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram stands before a sage who has become motionless in absorbed remembrance. Even Ram’s attempts to wake him fail. The moment becomes a lesson: true devotion can be so complete that the heart recognizes the divine more deeply than the senses do.
ramacharitamanas::3668.modern_relevance: You finally put your phone down after hours of scrolling, but your mind is still elsewhere. Something deeper has your attention now, and the usual noise can’t quite reach you.
ramacharitamanas::3668.insight: It shifts attention from outer interruption to inner absorption, showing that devotion can transform how you perceive presence.

ramacharitamanas::3669.verse_sanskrit: मुनि अकुलाइ उठा तब कैसें। बिकल हीन मनि फनिबर जैसें॥ आगें देखि राम तन स्यामा। सीता अनुज सहित सुख धामा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3669.verse_hindi: तब (अपने ईष्ट स्वरूप के अंतर्धान होते ही) मुनि ऐसे व्याकुल होकर उठे, जैसे श्रेष्ठ (मणिधर) सर्प मणि के बिना व्याकुल हो जाता है। मुनि ने अपने सामने सीताजी और लक्ष्मणजी सहित श्यामसुंदर विग्रह सुखधाम श्री रामजी को देखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3669.english_translation: Then the sage rose in agitation, like a jewel-less serpent in distress. Before him he saw dark-hued Ram, with Sita and Lakshman, the abode of joy.
ramacharitamanas::3669.translation_literal: मुनि (sage) / अकुलाइ (agitated) / उठा (rose) / तब (then) / कैसें (how) / बिकल (distressed) / हीन (without) / मनि (jewel) / फनिबर (great serpent) / जैसें (like) ॥ / आगें (in front) / देखि (seeing) / राम (Ram) / तन (body/form) / स्यामा (dark-hued) / सीता (Sita) / अनुज (younger brother) / सहित (together with) / सुख धामा (abode of joy) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3669.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3669.essence: Separation itself reveals how precious the beloved is.
ramacharitamanas::3669.simple_meaning: The sage becomes restless when the vision disappears, then sees Ram again with Sita and Lakshman before him.
ramacharitamanas::3669.simple_insight: What you love most can unsettle you when it slips away.
ramacharitamanas::3669.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sage has just been overwhelmed by Ram's presence and then shaken by its withdrawal. Now he rises in agitation, like a serpent without its jewel, and sees Ram again with Sita and Lakshman before him.
ramacharitamanas::3669.modern_relevance: You close your eyes after a moment of deep prayer or grief, and the room feels empty for a second. Then the presence you were reaching for feels suddenly near again.
ramacharitamanas::3669.insight: It shows how intense longing makes absence feel unbearable and return feel like relief.

ramacharitamanas::3670.verse_sanskrit: परेउ लकुट इव चरनन्हि लागी। प्रेम मगन मुनिबर बड़भागी॥ भुज बिसाल गहि लिए उठाई। परम प्रीति राखे उर लाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3670.verse_hindi: प्रेम में मग्न हुए वे बड़भागी श्रेष्ठ मुनि लाठी की तरह गिरकर श्री रामजी के चरणों में लग गए। श्री रामजी ने अपनी विशाल भुजाओं से पकड़कर उन्हें उठा लिया और बड़े प्रेम से हृदय से लगा रखा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3670.english_translation: The blessed sage fell like a staff at Ram's feet, lost in love. Ram lifted him with His broad arms and held him close to His heart.
ramacharitamanas::3670.translation_literal: परेउ (fell) / लकुट इव (like a staff) / चरनन्हि (at the feet) / लागी (touching, falling upon) / प्रेम मगन (immersed in love) / मुनिबर (best of sages) / बड़भागी (greatly fortunate) / भुज बिसाल (broad-armed) / गहि (grasping) / लिए उठाई (lifted up) / परम प्रीति (supreme affection) / राखे (kept) / उर लाई (to the heart, held against the chest)
ramacharitamanas::3670.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3670.essence: The one who falls in devotion is lifted into closeness.
ramacharitamanas::3670.simple_meaning: The sage is so full of love for Ram that he falls at Ram's feet. Ram responds by lifting him up and holding him close.
ramacharitamanas::3670.simple_insight: Devotion does not leave you abandoned; it draws a loving response back toward you.
ramacharitamanas::3670.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sage finally comes face to face with Ram after being overwhelmed by divine sight. He falls at Ram's feet like a staff. Ram immediately lifts him with both arms and presses him to His heart, showing how devotion is met by grace.
ramacharitamanas::3670.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you’ve admired for years, and your voice shakes. Instead of distance, they smile, pull you in, and make your nervousness feel holy.
ramacharitamanas::3670.insight: It turns reverence into intimacy: surrender becomes the doorway to being embraced.

ramacharitamanas::3671.verse_sanskrit: मुनिहि मिलत अस सोह कृपाला। कनक तरुहि जनु भेंट तमाला॥ राम बदनु बिलोक मुनि ठाढ़ा। मानहुँ चित्र माझ लिखि काढ़ा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3671.verse_hindi: कृपालु श्री रामचन्द्रजी मुनि से मिलते हुए ऐसे शोभित हो रहे हैं, मानो सोने के वृक्ष से तमाल का वृक्ष गले लगकर मिल रहा हो। मुनि (निस्तब्ध) खड़े हुए (टकटकी लगाकर) श्री रामजी का मुख देख रहे हैं, मानो चित्र में लिखकर बनाए गए हों ॥
ramacharitamanas::3671.english_translation: The compassionate Ram shone beside the sage like a dark tamala tree embracing a golden tree. The sage stood still, gazing at Ram's face, as if painted in a picture.
ramacharitamanas::3671.translation_literal: मुनिहि (with the sage) / मिलत (meeting) / अस (thus) / सोह (looked beautiful) / कृपाला (the compassionate one) / कनक (gold) / तरुहि (tree) / जनु (as if) / भेंट (embracing) / तमाला (tamala tree) / राम (Ram) / बदनु (face) / बिलोक (seeing) / मुनि (the sage) / ठाढ़ा (standing) / मानहुँ (as if) / चित्र (picture) / माझ (in the middle) / लिखि (written) / काढ़ा (drawn out)
ramacharitamanas::3671.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3671.essence: A true meeting can leave you motionless in wonder.
ramacharitamanas::3671.simple_meaning: Ram's meeting with the sage is described as a beautiful, striking contrast, and the sage stands spellbound, unable to look away.
ramacharitamanas::3671.simple_insight: Some moments are so moving that you stop completely and simply behold them.
ramacharitamanas::3671.detailed_meaning: The sage has just been overwhelmed by Ram's presence and touched His feet. Now Ram stands before him, and the scene turns still: the compassionate Lord beside the sage, the sage frozen in awe. The next verse completes the action by taking Ram into the hermitage for worship.
ramacharitamanas::3671.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you have admired for years, and your mind goes silent. You just stand there, taking in their face, unable to do anything else.
ramacharitamanas::3671.insight: It shifts attention from action to reverent seeing, where presence itself becomes the event.

ramacharitamanas::3672.verse_sanskrit: तब मुनि हृदयँ धीर धरि गहि पद बारहिं बार। निज आश्रम प्रभु आनि करि पूजा बिबिध प्रकार ॥
ramacharitamanas::3672.verse_hindi: तब मुनि ने हृदय में धीरज धरकर बार-बार चरणों को स्पर्श किया। फिर प्रभु को अपने आश्रम में लाकर अनेक प्रकार से उनकी पूजा की ॥
ramacharitamanas::3672.english_translation: Then the sage steadied his heart, touched the Lord's feet again and again, and brought Him to his hermitage, where he worshipped Him in many ways.
ramacharitamanas::3672.translation_literal: तब (then) / मुनि (the sage) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / धीर (steadiness) / धरि (having held) / गहि (grasping) / पद (feet) / बारहिं बार (again and again) / निज (own) / आश्रम (hermitage) / प्रभु (the Lord) / आनि (bringing) / करि (having done) / पूजा (worship) / बिबिध (various) / प्रकार (ways)
ramacharitamanas::3672.speaker: Narrator
