ramacharitamanas::3672.essence: True devotion turns awe into humble service.
ramacharitamanas::3672.simple_meaning: The sage calms himself, bows to Ram's feet again and again, brings Him to his hermitage, and worships Him with many offerings.
ramacharitamanas::3672.simple_insight: When reverence is real, even simple hospitality becomes worship.
ramacharitamanas::3672.detailed_meaning: After meeting Ram in the forest, the sage's joy overflows. He gathers himself, keeps touching Ram's feet, brings the Lord to his hermitage, and serves Him with every form of honour. The scene shows devotion turning into action.
ramacharitamanas::3672.modern_relevance: You finally meet someone you deeply admire, and your first instinct is not to perform — it's to make room, serve well, and show respect without hurry.
ramacharitamanas::3672.insight: It shifts devotion from feeling alone into concrete welcome, bowing, and service.

ramacharitamanas::3673.verse_sanskrit: कह मुनि प्रभु सुनु बिनती मोरी। अस्तुति करौं कवन बिधि तोरी॥ महिमा अमित मोरि मति थोरी। रबि सन्मुख खद्योत अँजोरी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3673.verse_hindi: मुनि कहने लगे- हे प्रभो! मेरी विनती सुनिए। मैं किस प्रकार से आपकी स्तुति करूँ? आपकी महिमा अपार है और मेरी बुद्धि अल्प है। जैसे सूर्य के सामने जुगनू का उजाला! ॥
ramacharitamanas::3673.english_translation: The sage said, “Lord, hear my plea. How can I praise you? Your greatness is boundless, and my mind is small. My light is like a firefly before the sun.”
ramacharitamanas::3673.translation_literal: कह (said) / मुनि (the sage) / प्रभु (Lord) / सुनु (hear) / बिनती (plea) / मोरी (my) / अस्तुति (praise) / करौं (I do) / कवन बिधि (which way) / तोरी (your) / महिमा (greatness) / अमित (boundless) / मोरि (my) / मति (mind) / थोरी (small) / रबि (sun) / सन्मुख (in front of) / खद्योत (firefly) / अँजोरी (light)
ramacharitamanas::3673.speaker: Muni
ramacharitamanas::3673.essence: True devotion knows its own words are too small.
ramacharitamanas::3673.simple_meaning: The sage asks Ram to listen, then admits he cannot properly praise him because Ram's greatness is limitless and his own mind is too small.
ramacharitamanas::3673.simple_insight: Real devotion begins when you stop pretending you can measure the immeasurable.
ramacharitamanas::3673.detailed_meaning: After welcoming Ram into his forest hermitage, the sage stands before him and tries to speak. But reverence overwhelms him. He admits that Ram's greatness cannot be contained by his own limited mind, and that praise itself feels impossible.
ramacharitamanas::3673.modern_relevance: You meet someone who changed your life, and every thank-you sounds too small. That awkward humility is not failure; it is recognition of something larger than language.
ramacharitamanas::3673.insight: It shifts you from performing praise to surrendering into reverence.

ramacharitamanas::3674.verse_sanskrit: श्याम तामरस दाम शरीरं। जटा मुकुट परिधन मुनिचीरं॥ पाणि चाप शर कटि तूणीरं। नौमि निरंतर श्रीरघुवीरं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3674.verse_hindi: हे नीलकमल की माला के समान श्याम शरीर वाले! हे जटाओं का मुकुट और मुनियों के (वल्कल) वस्त्र पहने हुए, हाथों में धनुष-बाण लिए तथा कमर में तरकस कसे हुए श्री रामजी! मैं आपको निरंतर नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3674.english_translation: O dark one, with a body like a garland of blue lotuses; with matted hair as your crown and bark garments; with bow and arrows in your hands and a quiver at your waist, I continually bow to Sri Raghubir.
ramacharitamanas::3674.translation_literal: श्याम (dark) / तामरस (lotus) / दाम (garland) / शरीरं (body) / जटा (matted hair) / मुकुट (crown) / परिधन (garment) / मुनिचीरं (sage-cloth) / पाणि (hand) / चाप (bow) / शर (arrow) / कटि (waist) / तूणीरं (quiver) / नौमि (I bow) / निरंतर (continually) / श्रीरघुवीरं (Sri Raghubir)
ramacharitamanas::3674.speaker: Muni
ramacharitamanas::3674.essence: True devotion sees splendor inside simplicity.
ramacharitamanas::3674.simple_meaning: The sage praises Ram's form and bows to him again and again. He sees the Lord of Raghu as both majestic and forest-dwelling.
ramacharitamanas::3674.simple_insight: Devotion lets you recognize greatness even when it appears humble.
ramacharitamanas::3674.detailed_meaning: In the forest hermitage, the sage has just welcomed Ram and offered worship. Overwhelmed, he begins a hymn: Ram's dark body, matted hair, bark clothes, bow, arrows, and quiver all shine together as divine majesty. The verse is pure praise.
ramacharitamanas::3674.modern_relevance: You meet someone in worn-out clothes after a hard year, but their steadiness changes the room. What looks ordinary may carry a dignity you only notice when your heart is quiet.
ramacharitamanas::3674.insight: It trains the mind to honor the sacred form beneath outward simplicity.

ramacharitamanas::3675.verse_sanskrit: मोह विपिन घन दहन कृशानुः। संत सरोरुह कानन भानुः॥ निसिचर करि वरूथ मृगराजः। त्रास सदा नो भव खग बाजः ॥
ramacharitamanas::3675.verse_hindi: जो मोह रूपी घने वन को जलाने के लिए अग्नि हैं, संत रूपी कमलों के वन को प्रफुल्लित करने के लिए सूर्य हैं, राक्षस रूपी हाथियों के समूह को पछाड़ने के लिए सिंह हैं और भव (आवागमन) रूपी पक्षी को मारने के लिए बाज रूप हैं, वे प्रभु सदा हमारी रक्षा करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3675.english_translation: May the Lord who burns the dense forest of delusion, the sun that makes the lotus-forest of saints bloom, the lion that scatters the herd of demon-elephants, and the hawk that strikes down the bird of worldly becoming protect us forever.
ramacharitamanas::3675.translation_literal: मोह (delusion) / विपिन (forest) / घन (dense) / दहन (burning) / कृशानुः (fire) / संत (saints) / सरोरुह (lotus) / कानन (forest) / भानुः (sun) / निसिचर (night-wanderers, demons) / करि (elephants) / वरूथ (herd) / मृगराजः (lion) / त्रास (fear) / सदा (always) / नो (us) / भव (worldly becoming) / खग (bird) / बाजः (hawk)
ramacharitamanas::3675.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3675.essence: Ram destroys confusion and protects the good from fear.
ramacharitamanas::3675.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the one who destroys confusion, nourishes the good, defeats destructive forces, and frees people from fear and rebirth.
ramacharitamanas::3675.simple_insight: You can rest in a protection stronger than your confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3675.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, after the sages praise Ram, Tulsidas turns to a prayerful vision of who Ram is. He is not only beautiful and noble; he is also the force that burns away delusion, protects the good, and overpowers every threatening power.
ramacharitamanas::3675.modern_relevance: When your mind feels like a dark room full of anxious thoughts, this verse offers a different center: something steady enough to burn through confusion and quiet the fear underneath it.
ramacharitamanas::3675.insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to refuge: Ram is not just praised, he is relied on.

ramacharitamanas::3676.verse_sanskrit: अरुण नयन राजीव सुवेशं। सीता नयन चकोर निशेशं॥ हर हृदि मानस बाल मरालं। नौमि राम उर बाहु विशालं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3676.verse_hindi: हे लाल कमल के समान नेत्र और सुंदर वेश वाले! सीताजी के नेत्र रूपी चकोर के चंद्रमा, शिवजी के हृदय रूपी मानसरोवर के बालहंस, विशाल हृदय और भुजा वाले श्री रामचंद्रजी! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3676.english_translation: With red lotus eyes and a beautiful form, you are the moon for Sita's chakor-like gaze. You are the young swan in Shiva's Manasarovar heart. I bow to Ram, whose chest is vast and whose arms are broad.
ramacharitamanas::3676.translation_literal: अरुण (red) / नयन (eyes) / राजीव (lotus) / सुवेशं (beautifully formed) / सीता (Sita's) / नयन (eyes) / चकोर (chakor bird) / निशेशं (moon) / हर (Shiva's) / हृदि (in the heart) / मानस (Manasarovar) / बाल (young) / मरालं (swan) / नौमि (I bow) / राम (Ram) / उर (chest) / बाहु (arms) / विशालं (vast, broad)
ramacharitamanas::3676.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3676.essence: Ram's beauty is matched by how completely he lives in loving hearts.
ramacharitamanas::3676.simple_meaning: Ram is praised for his beautiful form and for being beloved by Sita and Shiva alike.
ramacharitamanas::3676.simple_insight: Love makes the beloved feel present everywhere, in every heart that remembers him.
ramacharitamanas::3676.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is offering praise to Ram in a devotional string of images. Ram's beauty delights Sita, and his presence rests in Shiva's heart. The verse turns admiration into reverence before moving into deeper praise.
ramacharitamanas::3676.modern_relevance: You see someone you love in a crowded station and your whole attention softens. This verse names that feeling when devotion makes one presence shine through every heart.
ramacharitamanas::3676.insight: It shifts attention from Ram's appearance to his living place in the hearts of devotees.

ramacharitamanas::3677.verse_sanskrit: संशय सर्प ग्रसन उरगादः। शमन सुकर्कश तर्क विषादः॥ भव भंजन रंजन सुर यूथः। त्रातु सदा नो कृपा वरूथः ॥
ramacharitamanas::3677.verse_hindi: जो संशय रूपी सर्प को ग्रसने के लिए गरुड़ हैं, अत्यंत कठोर तर्क से उत्पन्न होने वाले विषाद का नाश करने वाले हैं, आवागमन को मिटाने वाले और देवताओं के समूह को आनंद देने वाले हैं, वे कृपा के समूह श्री रामजी सदा हमारी रक्षा करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3677.english_translation: May Lord Ram, the gracious one, always protect us: he swallows the serpent of doubt, destroys the suffering born of harsh logic, ends the cycle of becoming, and delights the hosts of radiant beings.
ramacharitamanas::3677.translation_literal: संशय (doubt) / सर्प (serpent) / ग्रसन (swallowing) / उरगादः (serpent-eater) / शमन (ending) / सुकर्कश (very harsh) / तर्क (reasoning) / विषादः (despair) / भव (becoming / the cycle of reactivity) / भंजन (breaking) / रंजन (delighting) / सुर (radiant beings) / यूथः (host) / त्रातु (may protect) / सदा (always) / नो (us) / कृपा (grace) / वरूथः (shield)
ramacharitamanas::3677.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3677.essence: Ram destroys doubt before doubt destroys you.
ramacharitamanas::3677.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the one who destroys doubt, ends despair born from harsh reasoning, and frees beings from the cycle of reactivity.
ramacharitamanas::3677.simple_insight: You do not have to be trapped inside your own overthinking.
ramacharitamanas::3677.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Tulsidas pauses the story to praise Ram’s power over the mind itself. Ram is not only the protector in battle; he is the force that swallows doubt, dissolves crippling argument, and gives frightened hearts a refuge.
ramacharitamanas::3677.modern_relevance: You stare at a message for ten minutes, building worst-case stories from one unread reply. This verse names the deeper rescue: a steadier presence that cuts through doubt before it hardens into despair.
ramacharitamanas::3677.insight: It shifts you from compulsive analysis to trust in a presence that can clear confusion.

ramacharitamanas::3678.verse_sanskrit: निर्गुण सगुण विषम सम रूपं। ज्ञान गिरा गोतीतमनूपं॥ अमलमखिलमनवद्यमपारं। नौमि राम भंजन महि भारं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3678.verse_hindi: हे निर्गुण, सगुण, विषम और समरूप! हे ज्ञान, वाणी और इंद्रियों से अतीत! हे अनुपम, निर्मल, संपूर्ण दोषरहित, अनंत एवं पृथ्वी का भार उतारने वाले श्री रामचंद्रजी! मैं आपको नमस्कार करता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3678.english_translation: O Ram, beyond attributes and beyond words, beyond all opposites, pure, flawless, limitless, and incomparable, I bow to you—the one who lifts the burden of the earth.
ramacharitamanas::3678.translation_literal: निर्गुण (without qualities) / सगुण (with qualities) / विषम (uneven, diverse) / सम (equal, balanced) / रूपं (form) / ज्ञान (knowledge) / गिरा (speech) / गोतीतमनूपं (beyond the senses and unmatched) / अमलम् (pure) / अखिलम् (whole) / अनवद्यम् (blameless) / अपारं (boundless) / नौमि (I bow) / राम (Ram) / भंजन (destroyer) / महि (earth) / भारं (burden)
ramacharitamanas::3678.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3678.essence: Ram is beyond every category, yet still carries the world's burden.
ramacharitamanas::3678.simple_meaning: Ram is beyond qualities, beyond speech, beyond the senses, yet also pure, complete, and without flaw. Tulsidas bows to him as the one who removes the world's burden.
ramacharitamanas::3678.simple_insight: There is relief in meeting what cannot be boxed in by labels, yet still cares for the world.
ramacharitamanas::3678.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram in a chain of devotional verses, moving from his beauty and compassion to his deepest nature. Here the praise turns vast: Ram is both beyond description and present in the world, the one who lifts its burden.
ramacharitamanas::3678.modern_relevance: You keep trying to define what matters most in a few neat words, then it shows up as something larger than your categories. This verse lets you rest in reverence instead of control.
ramacharitamanas::3678.insight: It shifts the mind from naming Ram to bowing before what cannot be fully named.

ramacharitamanas::3679.verse_sanskrit: भक्त कल्पपादप आरामः। तर्जन क्रोध लोभ मद कामः॥ अति नागर भव सागर सेतुः। त्रातु सदा दिनकर कुल केतुः ॥
ramacharitamanas::3679.verse_hindi: जो भक्तों के लिए कल्पवृक्ष के बगीचे हैं, क्रोध, लोभ, मद और काम को डराने वाले हैं, अत्यंत ही चतुर और संसार रूपी समुद्र से तरने के लिए सेतु रूप हैं, वे सूर्यकुल की ध्वजा श्री रामजी सदा मेरी रक्षा करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3679.english_translation: May Ram, the banner of the solar line, always protect me: he is the wish-fulfilling grove for devotees, the one who frightens away anger, greed, pride, and desire, and the skilled bridge across the ocean of worldly existence.
ramacharitamanas::3679.translation_literal: भक्त (devotees) / कल्पपादप (wish-fulfilling tree) / आरामः (grove) / तर्जन (frightening) / क्रोध (anger) / लोभ (greed) / मद (pride) / कामः (desire) / अति (very) / नागर (skilled / charming) / भव (worldly existence) / सागर (ocean) / सेतुः (bridge) / त्रातु (may protect) / सदा (always) / दिनकर (sun) / कुल (lineage) / केतुः (banner)
ramacharitamanas::3679.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3679.essence: Ram gives devotees refuge and carries them beyond their own inner enemies.
ramacharitamanas::3679.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as the one who gives devotees everything they truly need, protects them from inner faults, and helps them cross the ocean of worldly struggle.
ramacharitamanas::3679.simple_insight: There is comfort in knowing you are not facing your worst habits alone.
ramacharitamanas::3679.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is offering a prayer to Ram in the forest setting of Aranyakand. After describing Ram as beyond ordinary categories, he now turns to his tender side: the refuge of devotees, the force that drives away inner enemies, and the bridge across suffering.
ramacharitamanas::3679.modern_relevance: You are staring at your phone at 1:30 a.m., angry, restless, and tempted to spiral. This verse reminds you that real refuge does not just comfort you — it also weakens the habits that keep dragging you down.
ramacharitamanas::3679.insight: It shifts devotion from sentiment to protection: Ram is both refuge and the force that dismantles inner disturbance.

ramacharitamanas::3680.verse_sanskrit: अतुलित भुज प्रताप बल धामः। कलि मल विपुल विभंजन नामः॥ धर्म वर्म नर्मद गुण ग्रामः। संतत शं तनोतु मम रामः ॥
ramacharitamanas::3680.verse_hindi: जिनकी भुजाओं का प्रताप अतुलनीय है, जो बल के धाम हैं, जिनका नाम कलियुग के बड़े भारी पापों का नाश करने वाला है, जो धर्म के कवच (रक्षक) हैं और जिनके गुण समूह आनंद देने वाले हैं, वे श्री रामजी निरंतर मेरे कल्याण का विस्तार करें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3680.english_translation: May Lord Ram, whose arms have unmatched splendor and whose strength is immense, whose name destroys the great impurities of Kali Yuga, who protects dharma, and whose qualities bring delight, always expand my welfare.
ramacharitamanas::3680.translation_literal: अतुलित (unmatched) / भुज (arms) / प्रताप (splendor) / बल (strength) / धामः (abode) / कलि (Kali Yuga) / मल (impurities) / विपुल (great) / विभंजन (destroying) / नामः (name) / धर्म (dharma) / वर्म (armor/protection) / नर्मद (delight-giving) / गुण (qualities) / ग्रामः (group/cluster) / संतत (always) / शं (welfare) / तनोतु (may expand) / मम (my) / रामः (Ram)
ramacharitamanas::3680.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3680.essence: Ram’s name protects, purifies, and strengthens you at once.
ramacharitamanas::3680.simple_meaning: Ram is praised as immensely powerful, protective, and purifying. His name destroys the heavy impurities of this age and brings lasting welfare.
ramacharitamanas::3680.simple_insight: You are not left to face inner darkness alone; remembrance of Ram is itself a shelter.
ramacharitamanas::3680.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praising Ram in the forest exile context, after describing him as beyond form and yet full of grace. Here he adds Ram’s strength, his power to destroy the impurities of Kali Yuga, and his role as protector, turning praise into a prayer for personal welfare.
ramacharitamanas::3680.modern_relevance: When your mind feels polluted by doomscrolling, resentment, and self-doubt, you want something stronger than willpower. This verse points to a steadier refuge: repeated remembrance of Ram as protection and cleansing.
ramacharitamanas::3680.insight: It shifts devotion from admiration to reliance: Ram is not only praised, he is taken as shelter.

ramacharitamanas::3681.verse_sanskrit: जदपि बिरज ब्यापक अबिनासी। सब के हृदयँ निरंतर बासी॥ तदपि अनुज श्री सहित खरारी। बसतु मनसि मम काननचारी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3681.verse_hindi: यद्यपि आप निर्मल, व्यापक, अविनाशी और सबके हृदय में निरंतर निवास करने वाले हैं, तथापि हे खरारि श्री रामजी! लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सहित वन में विचरने वाले आप इसी रूप में मेरे हृदय में निवास कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3681.english_translation: Although you are pure, all-pervading, imperishable, and always dwelling in everyone's heart, still, O Ravana-slayer, let you, with Lakshman and Sita, dwell in my mind as the forest-wandering Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3681.translation_literal: जदपि (although) / बिरज (pure, unstained) / ब्यापक (all-pervading) / अबिनासी (imperishable) / सब (all) / के (of) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / निरंतर (continually) / बासी (dwelling)॥ / तदपि (still) / अनुज (with the younger brother) / श्री सहित (together with Sita) / खरारी (O enemy of Khara) / बसतु (may dwell) / मनसि (in the mind) / मम (my) / काननचारी (forest-wandering one)॥
ramacharitamanas::3681.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3681.essence: The all-pervading one is most beloved when he feels near.
ramacharitamanas::3681.simple_meaning: Ram is everywhere and already present in every heart, yet the devotee asks for a personal, loving presence of Ram, Sita, and Lakshman in the mind.
ramacharitamanas::3681.simple_insight: Love does not compete with greatness; it makes the infinite feel intimate.
ramacharitamanas::3681.detailed_meaning: Tulsidas is praying in the forested world of exile, where Ram walks with Lakshman and Sita. He knows Ram is beyond form and present in every heart, yet he still longs for that same Ram to live in his own mind as the beloved forest-wanderer.
ramacharitamanas::3681.modern_relevance: You know someone can be admired by everyone, yet you still want their voice in your own home. This prayer feels like asking for not just respect from afar, but living closeness.
ramacharitamanas::3681.insight: It shifts devotion from abstract reverence to intimate companionship.

ramacharitamanas::3682.verse_sanskrit: जे जानहिं ते जानहुँ स्वामी। सगुन अगुन उर अंतरजामी॥ जो कोसलपति राजिव नयना। करउ सो राम हृदय मम अयना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3682.verse_hindi: हे स्वामी! आपको जो सगुण, निर्गुण और अंतर्यामी जानते हों, वे जाना करें, मेरे हृदय में तो कोसलपति कमलनयन श्री रामजी ही अपना घर बनावें ॥
ramacharitamanas::3682.english_translation: O Lord, those who know You may know You as embodied, formless, and the inner ruler. But for me, may Kosalapati, the lotus-eyed Ram, make His home in my heart.
ramacharitamanas::3682.translation_literal: जे (those who) / जानहिं (know) / ते (they) / जानहुँ (may know) / स्वामी (Lord) / सगुन (with form) / अगुन (without form) / उर (heart) / अंतरजामी (inner ruler) / जो (who) / कोसलपति (Lord of Kosala) / राजिव नयना (lotus-eyed) / करउ (may do) / सो (that) / राम (Ram) / हृदय (heart) / मम (my) / अयना (home)
ramacharitamanas::3682.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3682.essence: Let Ram be your inner home, beyond every argument about form.
ramacharitamanas::3682.simple_meaning: The speaker says that others may understand the divine in many forms, but he wants only Ram to dwell in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::3682.simple_insight: You can stop chasing every spiritual idea and simply let the beloved presence take root in you.
ramacharitamanas::3682.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sage speaks to Ram with complete humility. He does not argue about form or formlessness. Instead, he asks for one thing only: that Ram, the lotus-eyed Lord of Kosala, make His home in his heart.
ramacharitamanas::3682.modern_relevance: You can read a dozen books, compare every path, and still feel empty at night. This verse lands like a quiet decision: stop circling the idea of the divine and let Ram in.
ramacharitamanas::3682.insight: It shifts devotion from debate to intimacy, from understanding Ram to making room for Ram.

ramacharitamanas::3683.verse_sanskrit: अस अभिमान जाइ जनि भोरे। मैं सेवक रघुपति पति मोरे॥ सुनि मुनि बचन राम मन भाए। बहुरि हरषि मुनिबर उर लाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3683.verse_hindi: ऐसा अभिमान भूलकर भी न छूटे कि मैं सेवक हूँ और श्री रघुनाथजी मेरे स्वामी हैं। मुनि के वचन सुनकर श्री रामजी मन में बहुत प्रसन्न हुए। तब उन्होंने हर्षित होकर श्रेष्ठ मुनि को हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3683.english_translation: May this pride never leave you even in a dream: 'I am a servant, and Raghupati is my master.' Hearing the sage's words, Ram was delighted in his heart. Then, pleased, he embraced the great sage.
ramacharitamanas::3683.translation_literal: अस (such) / अभिमान (pride) / जाइ (goes) / जनि (never) / भोरे (in a dream) / मैं (I) / सेवक (servant) / रघुपति (Lord of the Raghu clan) / पति (master) / मोरे (my) / सुनि (hearing) / मुनि (sage) / बचन (words) / राम (Ram) / मन (mind) / भाए (became pleased) / बहुरि (again) / हरषि (joyfully) / मुनिबर (great sage) / उर (chest/heart) / लाए (embraced)
ramacharitamanas::3683.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3683.essence: Pride survives only when it is turned into service.
ramacharitamanas::3683.simple_meaning: The sage says the only pride worth keeping is this: you are a servant of Ram. Ram is pleased by that humility and embraces the sage.
ramacharitamanas::3683.simple_insight: Real dignity comes from surrendering ego, not building it up.
ramacharitamanas::3683.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a sage speaks to Ram with complete humility, calling himself Ram's servant and Ram his master. Ram is delighted by that attitude and embraces him, showing that devotion expressed as service draws divine closeness.
ramacharitamanas::3683.modern_relevance: You help someone without expecting credit, and the quiet thought arises: 'I am only serving.' That inner humility can feel more powerful than applause.
ramacharitamanas::3683.insight: It shifts the mind from self-importance to loving service, showing that humility itself creates closeness.

ramacharitamanas::3684.verse_sanskrit: परम प्रसन्न जानु मुनि मोही। जो बर मागहु देउँ सो तोही॥ मुनि कह मैं बर कबहुँ न जाचा। समुझि न परइ झूठ का साचा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3684.verse_hindi: (और कहा-) हे मुनि! मुझे परम प्रसन्न जानो। जो वर माँगो, वही मैं तुम्हें दूँ! मुनि सुतीक्ष्णजी ने कहा- मैंने तो वर कभी माँगा ही नहीं। मुझे समझ ही नहीं पड़ता कि क्या झूठ है और क्या सत्य है, (क्या माँगू, क्या नहीं) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3684.english_translation: And he said, “O sage, know me to be greatly pleased. Ask for whatever boon you wish, and I will give it to you.” The sage replied, “I have never asked for any boon. I do not even know how to tell what is false and what is true, or what I should ask and what I should not.”
ramacharitamanas::3684.translation_literal: परम (greatly) / प्रसन्न (pleased) / जानु (know) / मुनि (sage) / मोही (me) / जो (whatever) / बर (boon) / मागहु (you ask) / देउँ (I give) / सो (that) / तोही (to you) ॥ / मुनि (sage) / कह (said) / मैं (I) / बर (boon) / कबहुँ (ever) / न (not) / जाचा (asked) / समुझि (understand) / न (not) / परइ (is possible) / झूठ (false) / का (and) / साचा (true) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3684.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3684.essence: True devotion stops asking for random rewards and trusts what comes.
ramacharitamanas::3684.simple_meaning: Ram offers Suṭīkṣṇa any boon, but the sage replies that he has never learned how to ask for one, or even how to separate false from true desire.
ramacharitamanas::3684.simple_insight: There is peace in not chasing what you cannot clearly name.
ramacharitamanas::3684.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram is speaking with the sage Suṭīkṣṇa after being welcomed with deep reverence. Ram offers him any boon at all, but the sage answers with complete simplicity: he has no wish to bargain, and no clear hunger for worldly gain. That humility opens the way for the next teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3684.modern_relevance: Someone finally asks, “What do you want for your birthday?” and you freeze because the honest answer is: you do not know. The verse understands that quiet clarity.
ramacharitamanas::3684.insight: It shifts you from craving and bargaining to honest simplicity about what you truly want.

ramacharitamanas::3685.verse_sanskrit: तुम्हहि नीक लागै रघुराई। सो मोहि देहु दास सुखदाई॥ अबिरल भगति बिरति बिग्याना। होहु सकल गुन ग्यान निधाना ॥
ramacharitamanas::3685.verse_hindi: ((अतः) हे रघुनाथजी! हे दासों को सुख देने वाले! आपको जो अच्छा लगे, मुझे वही दीजिए। (श्री रामचंद्रजी ने कहा- हे मुने!) तुम प्रगाढ़ भक्ति, वैराग्य, विज्ञान और समस्त गुणों तथा ज्ञान के निधान हो जाओ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3685.english_translation: “O Raghunath, giver of ease to your servants, give me whatever is pleasing to you. May I attain unbroken devotion, non-attachment, clear understanding, and become a storehouse of all virtues and wisdom.”
ramacharitamanas::3685.translation_literal: तुम्हहि (to you) / नीक (pleasing) / लागै (seems) / रघुराई (Raghunath) / सो (that) / मोहि (to me) / देहु (give) / दास (servant) / सुखदाई (giver of ease) / अबिरल (unbroken) / भगति (devotion) / बिरति (non-attachment) / बिग्याना (clear understanding) / होहु (become) / सकल (all) / गुन (virtues) / ग्यान (wisdom) / निधाना (storehouse)
ramacharitamanas::3685.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3685.essence: The best boon is becoming fit for devotion, clarity, and non-attachment.
ramacharitamanas::3685.simple_meaning: The seeker asks Ram for whatever Ram thinks is best, and asks to be filled with steady devotion, non-attachment, understanding, and all good qualities.
ramacharitamanas::3685.simple_insight: Real growth begins when you stop bargaining and ask to become worthy instead.
ramacharitamanas::3685.detailed_meaning: In the forest, the sage has already won Ram's favor. Now he makes the highest request: not comfort, but inner transformation. He asks for unbroken devotion, freedom from clinging, clear understanding, and a life full of virtue.
ramacharitamanas::3685.modern_relevance: You finally get the chance to ask for what you want — better pay, a shortcut, a favor. Instead, you ask to become steadier, clearer, and harder to shake.
ramacharitamanas::3685.insight: It shifts desire from getting outcomes to becoming fit for devotion and wisdom.

ramacharitamanas::3686.verse_sanskrit: प्रभु जो दीन्ह सो बरु मैं पावा। अब सो देहु मोहि जो भावा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3686.verse_hindi: (तब मुनि बोले-) प्रभु ने जो वरदान दिया, वह तो मैंने पा लिया। अब मुझे जो अच्छा लगता है, वह दीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3686.english_translation: (Then the sage said-) The blessing the Lord gave, I have already received. Now give me what I truly long for.
ramacharitamanas::3686.translation_literal: प्रभु (the Lord) / जो (which) / दीन्ह (gave) / सो (that) / बरु (boon) / मैं (I) / पावा (have received) / अब (now) / सो (that) / देहु (give) / मोहि (to me) / जो (which) / भावा (is pleasing/desirable)
ramacharitamanas::3686.speaker: Sutiksna
ramacharitamanas::3686.essence: The real boon is the one your heart still needs.
ramacharitamanas::3686.simple_meaning: The sage says he already has the blessing he needed from Ram, and now asks for the deeper gift his heart truly wants.
ramacharitamanas::3686.simple_insight: Real prayer begins after you stop asking for small things and name the deeper longing.
ramacharitamanas::3686.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Sutiksna stands before Ram with humility. He says the Lord has already given him one boon, but that is not the end of his request. What he now wants is the deeper gift of Ram's presence and grace.
ramacharitamanas::3686.modern_relevance: You get the promotion, the apology, the thing you asked for — and still feel the ache underneath. This verse names that second request: not more stuff, but what your heart actually needs.
ramacharitamanas::3686.insight: It shifts you from asking for external rewards to asking for the deeper grace that satisfies longing.

ramacharitamanas::3687.verse_sanskrit: अनुज जानकी सहित प्रभु चाप बान धर राम। मन हिय गगन इंदु इव बसहु सदा निहकाम ॥
ramacharitamanas::3687.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! हे श्री रामजी! छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सहित धनुष-बाणधारी आप निष्काम (स्थिर) होकर मेरे हृदय रूपी आकाश में चंद्रमा की भाँति सदा निवास कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3687.english_translation: O Lord Ram, with your younger brother Lakshman and Sita beside you, bow in hand, may you always dwell in my heart-mind like the moon in the sky, without desire.
ramacharitamanas::3687.translation_literal: अनुज (younger brother) / जानकी सहित (together with Janaki) / प्रभु (Lord) / चाप बान धर (holding bow and arrows) / राम (Ram) / मन हिय (in the heart-mind) / गगन (sky) / इंदु इव (like the moon) / बसहु (dwell) / सदा (always) / निहकाम (without desire)
ramacharitamanas::3687.speaker: Sutīkshna
ramacharitamanas::3687.essence: True devotion asks for Ram's presence, not anything else.
ramacharitamanas::3687.simple_meaning: The speaker asks Ram to stay in the heart forever, along with Lakshman and Sita, like a calm moon in the sky, free from desire.
ramacharitamanas::3687.simple_insight: Peace deepens when the mind becomes a home for loving presence.
ramacharitamanas::3687.detailed_meaning: After receiving Ram's blessing, Sutīkshna asks for the highest gift: not wealth or power, but Ram's constant presence in his heart. He imagines Ram with Lakshman and Sita, serene like the moon, and wants that still companionship to remain forever.
ramacharitamanas::3687.modern_relevance: After a long day, you finally sit alone and realize what you really want is not more control or praise — just a steady presence in your heart that calms everything else.
ramacharitamanas::3687.insight: It shifts devotion from asking for favors to asking for abiding presence.

ramacharitamanas::3688.verse_sanskrit: एवमस्तु करि रमानिवासा। हरषि चले कुंभज रिषि पासा॥ बहुत दिवस गुर दरसनु पाएँ। भए मोहि एहिं आश्रम आएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3688.verse_hindi: 'एवमस्तु' (ऐसा ही हो) ऐसा उच्चारण कर लक्ष्मी निवास श्री रामचंद्रजी हर्षित होकर अगस्त्य ऋषि के पास चले। (तब सुतीक्ष्णजी बोले-) गुरु अगस्त्यजी का दर्शन पाए और इस आश्रम में आए मुझे बहुत दिन हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3688.english_translation: Saying, “So be it,” Ram, the abode of Lakshmi, went joyfully to Sage Agastya. Then Sutikshna said, “It has been many days since I had the teacher’s darshan and came to this hermitage.”
ramacharitamanas::3688.translation_literal: एवमस्तु (so be it) / करि (having said) / रमानिवासा (abode of Lakshmi, Ram) / हरषि (joyfully) / चले (went) / कुंभज (Agastya) / रिषि (sage) / पासा (to the side) ॥ / बहुत (many) / दिवस (days) / गुर (teacher) / दरसनु (darshan) / पाएँ (having obtained) / भए (became) / मोहि (to me) / एहिं (this) / आश्रम (hermitage) / आएँ (having come) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3688.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3688.essence: Joy grows when you move toward the teacher with reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3688.simple_meaning: Ram agrees and goes happily to Agastya’s hermitage. Sutikshna then reflects that it has been a long time since he last saw his teacher and arrived here.
ramacharitamanas::3688.simple_insight: Some meetings are a blessing in themselves, and gratitude makes the journey feel complete.
ramacharitamanas::3688.detailed_meaning: After the exchange with the sages in the forest, Ram accepts the invitation and walks joyfully toward Agastya. The verse then shifts to Sutikshna’s grateful reflection: he has long wanted his teacher’s darshan and feels fulfilled by reaching this hermitage.
ramacharitamanas::3688.modern_relevance: You finally get the call from someone wise enough to guide you, and you leave the room lighter than you entered. The meeting itself feels like a reward.
ramacharitamanas::3688.insight: It shows how reverence turns movement into joy and arrival into gratitude.

ramacharitamanas::3689.verse_sanskrit: अब प्रभु संग जाउँ गुर पाहीं। तुम्ह कहँ नाथ निहोरा नाहीं॥ देखि कृपानिधि मुनि चतुराई। लिए संग बिहसे द्वौ भाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3689.verse_hindi: अब मैं भी प्रभु (आप) के साथ गुरुजी के पास चलता हूँ। इसमें हे नाथ! आप पर मेरा कोई एहसान नहीं है। मुनि की चतुरता देखकर कृपा के भंडार श्री रामजी ने उनको साथ ले लिया और दोनो भाई हँसने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3689.english_translation: "Now I will go with the Lord to the teacher. O Lord, I owe you no favor." Seeing the sage's cleverness, the treasure of compassion took him along, and both brothers laughed.
ramacharitamanas::3689.translation_literal: अब (now) / प्रभु (the Lord) / संग (with) / जाउँ (I will go) / गुर (to the teacher) / पाहीं (near) / तुम्ह (to you) / कहँ (for) / नाथ (Lord) / निहोरा (favor/debt) / नाहीं (not) / देखि (seeing) / कृपानिधि (treasure of compassion) / मुनि (sage) / चतुराई (cleverness) / लिए (took) / संग (along) / बिहसे (laughed) / द्वौ (both) / भाई (brothers)
ramacharitamanas::3689.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3689.simple_meaning: The sage asks to come along, saying he owes no debt for the kindness. Ram sees the sage's cleverness, takes him with him, and the two brothers laugh together.
ramacharitamanas::3689.simple_insight: Warmth can be so complete that even gratitude becomes playful.
ramacharitamanas::3689.detailed_meaning: At Agastya's forest hermitage, the sage cleverly asks to accompany Ram rather than remain behind. Ram sees through the gentle request, accepts him gladly, and the moment turns into shared laughter between the brothers and the sage.
ramacharitamanas::3689.modern_relevance: A friend says, “I’m coming with you,” pretending it’s no big deal, even though the gesture means everything. Some kindnesses are so natural they don’t need repayment.
ramacharitamanas::3689.insight: It shows that true affection can be given without keeping score.

ramacharitamanas::3690.verse_sanskrit: पंथ कहत निज भगति अनूपा। मुनि आश्रम पहुँचे सुरभूपा॥ तुरत सुतीछन गुर पहिं गयऊ। करि दंडवत कहत अस भयऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3690.verse_hindi: रास्ते में अपनी अनुपम भक्ति का वर्णन करते हुए देवताओं के राजराजेश्वर श्री रामजी अगस्त्य मुनि के आश्रम पर पहुँचे। सुतीक्ष्ण तुरंत ही गुरु अगस्त्य के पास गए और दण्डवत् करके ऐसा कहने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3690.english_translation: While speaking of their incomparable devotion on the way, the king of the gods, Ram, reached the sage's hermitage. Suतीkshan quickly went to Guru Agastya, bowed down, and began to speak.
ramacharitamanas::3690.translation_literal: पंथ (on the way) / कहत (speaking) / निज (own) / भगति (devotion) / अनूपा (matchless) / मुनि आश्रम (sage's hermitage) / पहुँचे (reached) / सुरभूपा (king of the gods) / तुरत (quickly) / सुतीछन (Sutikshan) / गुर पहिं (to the teacher's presence) / गयऊ (went) / करि (doing) / दंडवत (full bow) / कहत (speaking) / अस (thus) / भयऊ (became / began)
ramacharitamanas::3690.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3690.essence: Devotion becomes real when it turns into immediate bowing and approach.
ramacharitamanas::3690.simple_meaning: Ram reaches Agastya's hermitage while speaking of devotion, and Sutikshan immediately bows before the guru and begins to speak.
ramacharitamanas::3690.simple_insight: True reverence moves quickly. The heart bows before the mind finishes speaking.
ramacharitamanas::3690.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman are nearing Agastya's hermitage in the forest. The verse shifts from Ram's own praise of devotion to Sutikshan's eager movement toward his guru. It is a transitional moment, not a complete teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3690.modern_relevance: You finally arrive at the mentor's door after a long walk of questions. Before you even sit down, your body already knows to bow, listen, and soften.
ramacharitamanas::3690.insight: It shows devotion as movement toward the teacher, not just feeling or speech.

ramacharitamanas::3691.verse_sanskrit: नाथ कोसलाधीस कुमारा। आए मिलन जगत आधारा॥ राम अनुज समेत बैदेही। निसि दिनु देव जपत हहु जेही ॥
ramacharitamanas::3691.verse_hindi: हे नाथ! अयोध्या के राजा दशरथजी के कुमार जगदाधार श्री रामचंद्रजी छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी और सीताजी सहित आपसे मिलने आए हैं, जिनका हे देव! आप रात-दिन जप करते रहते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3691.english_translation: O Lord, the prince of Ayodhya, the support of the world, has come to meet you. Ram has come with his younger brother and Sita, the one you chant day and night.
ramacharitamanas::3691.translation_literal: नाथ (Lord) / कोसलाधीस (king of Kosala) / कुमारा (prince) / आए (have come) / मिलन (to meet) / जगत (world) / आधारा (support)॥ / राम (Ram) / अनुज (younger brother) / समेत (together with) / बैदेही (Sita) / निसि दिनु (day and night) / देव (O divine one) / जपत (chanting) / हहु (you are) / जेही (whom)
ramacharitamanas::3691.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3691.essence: What you remember with love can one day stand before you.
ramacharitamanas::3691.simple_meaning: The speaker tells Augustya that Ram has arrived with Lakshman and Sita, and reminds him that Augustya has long been remembering Ram day and night.
ramacharitamanas::3691.simple_insight: Meeting what you have long held in your heart can feel like a homecoming.
ramacharitamanas::3691.detailed_meaning: At Augustya's hermitage in the forest, the speaker announces Ram's arrival with Lakshman and Sita. The sage has been devotedly repeating Ram's name, and this moment prepares his joyful meeting with the one he has been longing for.
ramacharitamanas::3691.modern_relevance: You finally meet the person whose name you have been carrying in prayer, memory, and hope. The waiting ends, and recognition arrives before words do.
ramacharitamanas::3691.insight: It shifts longing from private devotion into living encounter.

ramacharitamanas::3692.verse_sanskrit: सुनत अगस्ति तुरत उठि धाए। हरि बिलोकि लोचन जल छाए॥ मुनि पद कमल परे द्वौ भाई। रिषि अति प्रीति लिए उर लाई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3692.verse_hindi: यह सुनते ही अगस्त्यजी तुरंत ही उठ दौड़े। भगवान् को देखते ही उनके नेत्रों में (आनंद और प्रेम के आँसुओं का) जल भर आया। दोनों भाई मुनि के चरण कमलों पर गिर पड़े। ऋषि ने (उठाकर) बड़े प्रेम से उन्हें हृदय से लगा लिया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3692.english_translation: Hearing this, Agastya rose at once and ran forward. Seeing Hari, tears filled his eyes. The two brothers fell at the sage's lotus feet, and the sage, full of love, drew them into his heart.
ramacharitamanas::3692.translation_literal: सुनत (hearing) / अगस्ति (Agastya) / तुरत (at once) / उठि (rising) / धाए (ran) / हरि (Hari) / बिलोकि (seeing) / लोचन (eyes) / जल (water/tears) / छाए (became filled) / मुनि (sage) / पद कमल (lotus feet) / परे (fell) / द्वौ (both) / भाई (brothers) / रिषि (sage) / अति (very) / प्रीति (love) / लिए (taking) / उर (heart) / लाई (brought/embraced)
ramacharitamanas::3692.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3692.essence: Love recognizes the beloved before words begin.
ramacharitamanas::3692.simple_meaning: Agastya rushes to greet Ram and Lakshman with tears of joy. The brothers bow at his feet, and he embraces them with deep affection.
ramacharitamanas::3692.simple_insight: Real reverence shows up as tears, humility, and a warm embrace.
ramacharitamanas::3692.detailed_meaning: Ram and Lakshman have reached Agastya's hermitage in the forest. When the sage hears of their arrival and sees Ram, he rises immediately, overwhelmed with love. The verse pauses on the meeting itself, not a teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3692.modern_relevance: You open the door and see someone you have waited months to meet. Your body moves before your words do, and gratitude shows up as tears.
ramacharitamanas::3692.insight: It highlights devotion as an immediate, embodied response to sacred presence.

ramacharitamanas::3693.verse_sanskrit: सादर कुसल पूछि मुनि ग्यानी। आसन बर बैठारे आनी॥ पुनि करि बहु प्रकार प्रभु पूजा। मोहि सम भाग्यवंत नहिं दूजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3693.verse_hindi: ज्ञानी मुनि ने आदरपूर्वक कुशल पूछकर उनको लाकर श्रेष्ठ आसन पर बैठाया। फिर बहुत प्रकार से प्रभु की पूजा करके कहा- मेरे समान भाग्यवान् आज दूसरा कोई नहीं है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3693.english_translation: The wise sage respectfully asked after their well-being, brought them in and seated them on a fine seat. Then he worshipped the Lord in many ways and said, "No one is as fortunate as I am today."
ramacharitamanas::3693.translation_literal: सादर (respectfully) / कुसल (well-being) / पूछि (asking) / मुनि (sage) / ग्यानी (wise) / आसन (seat) / बर (excellent) / बैठारे (seated) / आनी (bringing) / पुनि (then) / करि (doing) / बहु प्रकार (many kinds) / प्रभु (Lord) / पूजा (worship) / मोहि (me) / सम (like) / भाग्यवंत (fortunate) / नहिं (not) / दूजा (another)
ramacharitamanas::3693.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3693.essence: Honor the divine presence by welcoming it with your whole heart.
ramacharitamanas::3693.simple_meaning: Agastya greets Ram and his companions with honor, seats them well, worships Ram in many ways, and feels blessed by their arrival.
ramacharitamanas::3693.simple_insight: True welcome is reverence in action, not just polite words.
ramacharitamanas::3693.detailed_meaning: In Agastya's hermitage, Ram, Lakshman, and Sita have arrived after the earlier greeting. The sage receives them with honor, seats them properly, worships Ram, and feels that no one in the world is more blessed than he is.
ramacharitamanas::3693.modern_relevance: Someone arrives at your home after a long journey, and you stop everything to make them comfortable, feed them, and give them your best seat. That quiet honor says more than praise ever could.
ramacharitamanas::3693.insight: It shows devotion through hospitality: the sacred guest is welcomed with care, not ceremony alone.

ramacharitamanas::3694.verse_sanskrit: जहँ लगि रहे अपर मुनि बृंदा। हरषे सब बिलोकि सुखकंदा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3694.verse_hindi: वहाँ जहाँ तक (जितने भी) अन्य मुनिगण थे, सभी आनंदकन्द श्री रामजी के दर्शन करके हर्षित हो गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3694.english_translation: All the other sages there became joyful upon seeing the Lord of bliss.
ramacharitamanas::3694.translation_literal: जहँ (where) / लगि (up to) / रहे (were present) / अपर (other) / मुनि (sages) / बृंदा (groups) / हरषे (became joyful) / सब (all) / बिलोकि (seeing) / सुखकंदा (the source of bliss)
ramacharitamanas::3694.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3694.essence: His presence alone turns reverence into joy.
ramacharitamanas::3694.simple_meaning: The other sages present there felt joy just from seeing Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3694.simple_insight: Some presences lift the whole room before a single word is spoken.
ramacharitamanas::3694.detailed_meaning: In Agastya's hermitage, Ram and Lakshman have arrived and been welcomed. As the gathering settles, the other sages simply see Ram and are filled with joy. The verse is a scene detail, showing the atmosphere of reverence around him.
ramacharitamanas::3694.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the tension drops before anyone speaks. Some people bring calm just by being there.
ramacharitamanas::3694.insight: It shows Ram's presence as enough to transform the mood of everyone around him.

ramacharitamanas::3695.verse_sanskrit: मुनि समूह महँ बैठे सन्मुख सब की ओर। सरद इंदु तन चितवन मानहुँ निकर चकोर ॥
ramacharitamanas::3695.verse_hindi: मुनियों के समूह में श्री रामचंद्रजी सबकी ओर सम्मुख होकर बैठे हैं (अर्थात् प्रत्येक मुनि को श्री रामजी अपने ही सामने मुख करके बैठे दिखाई देते हैं और सब मुनि टकटकी लगाए उनके मुख को देख रहे हैं)। ऐसा जान पड़ता है मानो चकोरों का समुदाय शरत्पूर्णिमा के चंद्रमा की ओर देख रहा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3695.english_translation: Ram sits facing everyone in the gathering of sages, and they gaze at his moonlike form like a flock of chakors looking toward the autumn moon.
ramacharitamanas::3695.translation_literal: मुनि समूह (group of sages) / महँ (in) / बैठे (sat) / सन्मुख (facing) / सब (all) / की ओर (toward) / सरद (autumn) / इंदु (moon) / तन (body/form) / चितवन (gaze) / मानहुँ (as if) / निकर (flock) / चकोर (chakors)
ramacharitamanas::3695.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3695.essence: True presence gathers every gaze without asking for it.
ramacharitamanas::3695.simple_meaning: Ram sits facing the gathered sages, and they keep their eyes fixed on his radiant face as if chakors are staring at the autumn moon.
ramacharitamanas::3695.simple_insight: Some presence makes attention effortless. The heart naturally turns toward what it loves.
ramacharitamanas::3695.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a group of wise sages has welcomed Ram with reverence. He sits before them, and every sage feels personally seen. Their loving gaze on his moonlike face creates a still, devotional moment before Ram explains why he has come.
ramacharitamanas::3695.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the noise softens because someone you trust finally arrived. Everyone keeps looking up, not out of politeness, but because presence itself has become the event.
ramacharitamanas::3695.insight: It shifts attention from scattered social chatter to reverent, focused presence.

ramacharitamanas::3696.verse_sanskrit: तब रघुबीर कहा मुनि पाहीं। तुम्ह सन प्रभु दुराव कछु नाहीं॥ तुम्ह जानहु जेहि कारन आयउँ। ताते तात न कहि समुझायउँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3696.verse_hindi: तब श्री रामजी ने मुनि से कहा- हे प्रभो! आप से तो कुछ छिपाव है नहीं। मैं जिस कारण से आया हूँ, वह आप जानते ही हैं। इसी से हे तात! मैंने आपसे समझाकर कुछ नहीं कहा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3696.english_translation: Then Lord Ram said to the sage, “Nothing is hidden from you. You already know why I have come, so, dear one, I did not explain it to you.”
ramacharitamanas::3696.translation_literal: तब (then) / रघुबीर (Ram, hero of the Raghu clan) / कहा (said) / मुनि पाहीं (to the sage) / तुम्ह (you) / सन (with) / प्रभु (Lord) / दुराव (hidden) / कछु (something) / नाहीं (is not) ॥ तुम्ह (you) / जानहु (know) / जेहि (which) / कारन (reason) / आयउँ (I came) / ताते (therefore) / तात (dear one) / न (not) / कहि (saying) / समुझायउँ (explained) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3696.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3696.essence: What is truly understood needs very few words.
ramacharitamanas::3696.simple_meaning: Ram tells the sage that nothing is hidden from him. The sage already knows why Ram has come, so no long explanation is needed.
ramacharitamanas::3696.simple_insight: Real understanding doesn’t need performance; it feels quietly recognized.
ramacharitamanas::3696.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram is speaking with a sage who already understands the situation. Ram does not waste words explaining himself. The moment shows trust, humility, and the ease that comes when the right person already knows your purpose.
ramacharitamanas::3696.modern_relevance: You sit across from a mentor who can read the silence on your face. Before you defend yourself, they already understand. Some conversations become lighter when you stop performing and let the truth stand on its own.
ramacharitamanas::3696.insight: It shifts you from explaining yourself to trusting that the right people can see clearly.

ramacharitamanas::3697.verse_sanskrit: अब सो मंत्र देहु प्रभु मोही। जेहि प्रकार मारौं मुनिद्रोही॥ मुनि मुसुकाने सुनि प्रभु बानी। पूछेहु नाथ मोहि का जानी ॥
ramacharitamanas::3697.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! अब आप मुझे वही मंत्र (सलाह) दीजिए, जिस प्रकार मैं मुनियों के द्रोही राक्षसों को मारूँ। प्रभु की वाणी सुनकर मुनि मुस्कुराए और बोले- हे नाथ! आपने क्या समझकर मुझसे यह प्रश्न किया? ॥
ramacharitamanas::3697.english_translation: "Now give me the counsel, Lord, by which I may kill the forest-dwelling demons who oppose the sages." Hearing the Lord's words, the sage smiled and said, "Lord, why would you ask me that?"
ramacharitamanas::3697.translation_literal: अब (now) / सो (that) / मंत्र (counsel) / देहु (give) / प्रभु (Lord) / मोही (to me) / जेहि प्रकार (in which way) / मारौं (I may kill) / मुनिद्रोही (those hostile to sages) ॥ मुनि (the sage) / मुसुकाने (smiled) / सुनि (hearing) / प्रभु बानी (the Lord's words) / पूछेहु (you asked) / नाथ (Lord) / मोहि (me) / का (why/what) / जानी (knowing) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3697.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3697.essence: A question can hide deeper understanding and invite closer guidance.
ramacharitamanas::3697.simple_meaning: Ram asks the sage for guidance on how to destroy the demons troubling the forest sages. The sage smiles, knowing Ram already understands far more than he is asking aloud.
ramacharitamanas::3697.simple_insight: Sometimes a question is really a way of opening the heart, not seeking information.
ramacharitamanas::3697.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram sits among the sages after hearing their suffering. He asks for a way to defeat the demons who disturb their sacrifices. The sage smiles because Ram is not ignorant; this question is part of a deeper, loving exchange before the true teaching begins.
ramacharitamanas::3697.modern_relevance: You already know the answer, but you still ask someone you trust. The question is not confusion — it is the beginning of a deeper conversation.
ramacharitamanas::3697.insight: It shifts the moment from strategy to relationship, showing that true guidance begins in humility.

ramacharitamanas::3698.verse_sanskrit: तुम्हरेइँ भजन प्रभाव अघारी। जानउँ महिमा कछुक तुम्हारी॥ ऊमरि तरु बिसाल तव माया। फल ब्रह्मांड अनेक निकाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3698.verse_hindi: हे पापों का नाश करने वाले! मैं तो आप ही के भजन के प्रभाव से आपकी कुछ थोड़ी सी महिमा जानता हूँ। आपकी माया गूलर के विशाल वृक्ष के समान है, अनेकों ब्रह्मांडों के समूह ही जिसके फल हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3698.english_translation: O destroyer of sins, I know only a little of your greatness through the power of your own devotion. Your illusion is like a vast fig tree, and countless universes are its fruits.
ramacharitamanas::3698.translation_literal: तुम्हरेइँ (through your own) / भजन (devotion) / प्रभाव (power, influence) / अघारी (destroyer of sins) / जानउँ (I know) / महिमा (greatness) / कछुक (a little) / तुम्हारी (your) / ऊमरि तरु (fig tree) / बिसाल (vast) / तव (your) / माया (illusion) / फल (fruits) / ब्रह्मांड (universes) / अनेक (many) / निकाया (groups, clusters)
ramacharitamanas::3698.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3698.essence: Devotion reveals greatness, but never exhausts it.
ramacharitamanas::3698.simple_meaning: Ram says that even devotion reveals only a small part of his greatness. His cosmic power is so vast that countless universes are only a tiny expression of it.
ramacharitamanas::3698.simple_insight: There is humility in real devotion: the more you love, the more you realise how much remains beyond you.
ramacharitamanas::3698.detailed_meaning: In Aranyakand, Ram speaks to a sage after explaining why he has come to the forest. The conversation turns from a practical request to a glimpse of his cosmic nature: even sincere devotion reveals only a fraction of his greatness, and the worlds themselves rest inside his maya.
ramacharitamanas::3698.modern_relevance: You pray, meditate, or sit in silence and still feel you have only touched the edge. That feeling is not failure; it is a sign that what you seek is larger than your mind can contain.
ramacharitamanas::3698.insight: It shifts the mind from mastery to reverent humility, showing that devotion opens vision without exhausting mystery.

ramacharitamanas::3699.verse_sanskrit: जीव चराचर जंतु समाना। भीतर बसहिं न जानहिं आना॥ ते फल भच्छक कठिन कराला। तव भयँ डरत सदा सोउ काला ॥
ramacharitamanas::3699.verse_hindi: चर और अचर जीव (गूलर के फल के भीतर रहने वाले छोटे-छोटे) जंतुओं के समान उन (ब्रह्माण्ड रूपी फलों) के भीतर बसते हैं और वे (अपने उस छोटे से जगत् के सिवा) दूसरा कुछ नहीं जानते। उन फलों का भक्षण करने वाला कठिन और कराल काल है। वह काल भी सदा आपसे भयभीत रहता है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3699.english_translation: All moving and unmoving beings are like creatures living inside those fruits; they do not know anything beyond that inner world. The fierce, terrible Time that devours those fruits is always afraid of you.
ramacharitamanas::3699.translation_literal: जीव (living beings) / चराचर (moving and unmoving) / जंतु (creatures) / समाना (like) / भीतर (inside) / बसहिं (live) / न (not) / जानहिं (know) / आना (other) ॥ ते (those) / फल (fruits) / भच्छक (devourer) / कठिन (fierce) / कराला (terrible) / तव (your) / भयँ (in fear) / डरत (afraid) / सदा (always) / सोउ (that) / काला (Time) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3699.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3699.essence: You are trapped only when you mistake a small world for the whole.
ramacharitamanas::3699.simple_meaning: All beings live inside a limited world and mistake it for everything. Even Time, the great destroyer, remains afraid of the divine.
ramacharitamanas::3699.simple_insight: It loosens your grip on what seems absolute and restores a sense of vastness.
ramacharitamanas::3699.detailed_meaning: Hanuman is speaking in Lanka, explaining Ram's power through a cosmic image. He says all beings are like tiny creatures inside a fruit, unaware of the larger reality around them, and even Time itself trembles before Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3699.modern_relevance: You spend weeks inside one disappointing email thread and start believing that one room, one boss, one failure is the whole universe. This verse pulls you back into scale.
ramacharitamanas::3699.insight: It shifts you from narrow identification to a wider view of reality and power.

ramacharitamanas::3700.verse_sanskrit: ते तुम्ह सकल लोकपति साईं। पूँछेहु मोहि मनुज की नाईं॥ यह बर मागउँ कृपानिकेता। बसहु हृदयँ श्री अनुज समेता ॥
ramacharitamanas::3700.verse_hindi: उन्हीं आपने समस्त लोकपालों के स्वामी होकर भी मुझसे मनुष्य की तरह प्रश्न किया। हे कृपा के धाम! मैं तो यह वर माँगता हूँ कि आप श्री सीताजी और छोटे भाई लक्ष्मणजी सहित मेरे हृदय में (सदा) निवास कीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3700.english_translation: You are the lord of all worlds, yet you asked me like a human being. O home of grace, I ask for this boon: dwell in my heart with Sita and your younger brother Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::3700.translation_literal: ते (you) / तुम्ह (you) / सकल लोकपति (lord of all worlds) / साईं (lord) / पूँछेहु (you asked) / मोहि (me) / मनुज (human being) / की नाईं (like) / यह (this) / बर (boon) / मागउँ (I ask) / कृपानिकेता (home of grace) / बसहु (dwell) / हृदयँ (in the heart) / श्री (Sita) / अनुज (younger brother) / समेता (together with)
ramacharitamanas::3700.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3700.essence: The highest boon is not gain, but Ram living in your heart.
ramacharitamanas::3700.simple_meaning: The speaker honours Ram as the lord of all worlds, then asks for the highest blessing: that Ram, Sita, and Lakshman live in his heart forever.
ramacharitamanas::3700.simple_insight: Love asks for presence, not possessions.
ramacharitamanas::3700.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a devotee stands before Ram after seeing his vast divine nature. Instead of asking for power or reward, he asks for the one thing that matters most: Ram's living presence in the heart, along with Sita and Lakshman.
ramacharitamanas::3700.modern_relevance: You meet someone who has changed your life, and they ask what they can give you. You don't ask for money or status — you just want them close. That is this verse.
ramacharitamanas::3700.insight: It shifts desire from outer rewards to inward companionship with the divine.

ramacharitamanas::3701.verse_sanskrit: अबिरल भगति बिरति सतसंगा। चरन सरोरुह प्रीति अभंगा॥ जद्यपि ब्रह्म अखंड अनंता। अनुभव गम्य भजहिं जेहि संता।6॥
ramacharitamanas::3701.verse_hindi: मुझे प्रगाढ़ भक्ति, वैराग्य, सत्संग और आपके चरणकमलों में अटूट प्रेम प्राप्त हो। यद्यपि आप अखंड और अनंत ब्रह्म हैं, जो अनुभव से ही जानने में आते हैं और जिनका संतजन भजन करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3701.english_translation: May I have unbroken devotion, detachment, good company, and undying love for your lotus feet. Although you are the boundless, endless supreme reality, the saints know you through direct experience and worship you.
ramacharitamanas::3701.translation_literal: अबिरल (unbroken) / भगति (devotion) / बिरति (detachment) / सतसंगा (good company) / चरन सरोरुह (lotus feet) / प्रीति (love) / अभंगा (unbroken) / जद्यपि (although) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / अखंड (undivided) / अनंता (endless) / अनुभव (direct experience) / गम्य (knowable) / भजहिं (worship) / जेहि (whom) / संता (saints)
ramacharitamanas::3701.speaker: Unknown
ramacharitamanas::3701.essence: Unbroken devotion is the way to know the boundless.
ramacharitamanas::3701.simple_meaning: The speaker asks for steady devotion, non-attachment, holy companionship, and lasting love for Ram's feet. Even the supreme reality is reached through lived devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3701.simple_insight: Real devotion is not a mood; it becomes a way of living that keeps the heart steady.
ramacharitamanas::3701.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a humble seeker speaks to Ram after being asked what blessing he wants. He does not ask for power or comfort. He asks for devotion, detachment, good company, and love that never breaks, because the boundless supreme reality is known through lived devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3701.modern_relevance: You leave a retreat feeling clear, then lose it by Tuesday morning in traffic and noise. What holds is not a high moment, but steady companionship, discipline, and love that keeps returning.
ramacharitamanas::3701.insight: It shifts the aim from getting spiritual experiences to building a life that can sustain devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3702.verse_sanskrit: अस तव रूप बखानउँ जानउँ। फिरि फिरि सगुन ब्रह्म रति मानउँ॥ संतत दासन्ह देहु बड़ाई। तातें मोहि पूँछेहु रघुराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3702.verse_hindi: यद्यपि मैं आपके ऐसे रूप को जानता हूँ और उसका वर्णन भी करता हूँ, तो भी लौट-लौटकर में सगुण ब्रह्म में (आपके इस सुंदर स्वरूप में) ही प्रेम मानता हूँ। आप सेवकों को सदा ही बड़ाई दिया करते हैं, इसी से हे रघुनाथजी! आपने मुझसे पूछा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3702.english_translation: Although I know how to describe your form, I keep returning again and again to loving your manifest, beautiful presence. You always honor your servants, and that is why, O Raghunath, you asked me.
ramacharitamanas::3702.translation_literal: अस (such) / तव (your) / रूप (form) / बखानउँ (I describe) / जानउँ (I know) / फिरि फिरि (again and again) / सगुन (with attributes / manifest) / ब्रह्म (supreme reality) / रति (love) / मानउँ (I hold) ॥ / संतत (always) / दासन्ह (servants) / देहु (you give) / बड़ाई (honour, praise) / तातें (therefore) / मोहि (me) / पूँछेहु (you asked) / रघुराई (O Raghunath) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3702.speaker: Tulsidas
ramacharitamanas::3702.essence: Knowing the divine form is not the same as loving it.
ramacharitamanas::3702.simple_meaning: Tulsidas says he understands Ram's divine form, yet his heart keeps returning to loving that visible, beautiful presence. Ram always honors his servants, so Tulsidas feels invited to speak.
ramacharitamanas::3702.simple_insight: Love does not weaken understanding; it deepens it.
ramacharitamanas::3702.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Tulsidas turns from explanation to devotion. He tells Ram that he knows the divine form in theory, but keeps coming back to love the personal presence he can feel. The verse arises because Ram has already treated a devotee with honor.
ramacharitamanas::3702.modern_relevance: You can read the books, name the principles, and still find your heart softening when someone you love walks into the room. Understanding is not the end of devotion; sometimes it is the doorway.
ramacharitamanas::3702.insight: It shifts you from treating reverence as ignorance to seeing it as a chosen return to what matters most.

ramacharitamanas::3703.verse_sanskrit: है प्रभु परम मनोहर ठाऊँ। पावन पंचबटी तेहि नाऊँ॥ दंडक बन पुनीत प्रभु करहू। उग्र साप मुनिबर कर हरहू ॥
ramacharitamanas::3703.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! एक परम मनोहर और पवित्र स्थान है, उसका नाम पंचवटी है। हे प्रभो! आप दण्डक वन को (जहाँ पंचवटी है) पवित्र कीजिए और श्रेष्ठ मुनि गौतमजी के कठोर शाप को हर लीजिए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3703.english_translation: O Lord, there is a most beautiful and sacred place. Its name is Panchavati. Please sanctify the Dandaka forest there, and remove the severe curse of the great sage.
ramacharitamanas::3703.translation_literal: है (there is) / प्रभु (Lord) / परम (supremely) / मनोहर (beautiful) / ठाऊँ (place) / पावन (sacred) / पंचबटी (Panchavati) / तेहि (that) / नाऊँ (name) / दंडक (Dandaka) / बन (forest) / पुनीत (purify) / प्रभु (Lord) / करहू (do) / उग्र (severe) / साप (curse) / मुनिबर (great sage) / कर (of) / हरहू (remove)
ramacharitamanas::3703.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3703.essence: A sacred presence can transform even a cursed place.
ramacharitamanas::3703.simple_meaning: Panchavati is described as a beautiful, holy place, and Ram is asked to purify the forest and remove the sage’s curse.
ramacharitamanas::3703.simple_insight: A place can become holy when the divine presence touches it.
ramacharitamanas::3703.detailed_meaning: In the forest journey, the sages point Ram toward Panchavati, a place of beauty and purity within the Dandaka forest. They ask him to sanctify that land and relieve the burden of a harsh curse, preparing the ground for the next stage of exile.
ramacharitamanas::3703.modern_relevance: A room can feel heavy after weeks of stress, arguments, and bad news. Then one calm person enters, and the whole atmosphere changes. Some places are healed by the presence they receive.
ramacharitamanas::3703.insight: It shifts attention from scenery to sanctifying presence.

ramacharitamanas::3704.verse_sanskrit: बास करहु तहँ रघुकुल राया। कीजे सकल मुनिन्ह पर दाया॥ चले राम मुनि आयसु पाई। तुरतहिं पंचबटी निअराई ॥
ramacharitamanas::3704.verse_hindi: हे रघुकुल के स्वामी! आप सब मुनियों पर दया करके वहीं निवास कीजिए। मुनि की आज्ञा पाकर श्री रामचंद्रजी वहाँ से चल दिए और शीघ्र ही पंचवटी के निकट पहुँच गए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3704.english_translation: O Lord of Raghu's line, dwell there and show mercy to all the sages. Having received the sage's command, Ram immediately went and soon reached near Panchavati.
ramacharitamanas::3704.translation_literal: बास करहु (dwell) / तहँ (there) / रघुकुल राया (king of Raghu's line) / कीजे (do) / सकल (all) / मुनिन्ह (sages) / पर (upon) / दाया (mercy) / चले (went) / राम (Ram) / मुनि (sage) / आयसु (command) / पाई (having received) / तुरतहिं (immediately) / पंचबटी (Panchavati) / निअराई (near)
ramacharitamanas::3704.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3704.essence: Ram's greatness appears in how quickly he answers a righteous request.
ramacharitamanas::3704.simple_meaning: The sage asks Ram to stay in the holy place and bless the sages with mercy. Ram obeys at once and moves on to Panchavati.
ramacharitamanas::3704.simple_insight: True nobility shows itself in immediate obedience and kindness.
ramacharitamanas::3704.detailed_meaning: In the forest, a sage points Ram toward Panchavati and asks him to live there for the sake of the sages' welfare. Ram accepts the instruction without delay and heads there at once, showing the ease with which he answers righteous request.
ramacharitamanas::3704.modern_relevance: Someone asks you to stay a little longer and help set things right before you leave. You don't make it about your schedule; you simply respond with care.
ramacharitamanas::3704.insight: It trains the mind to treat a worthy request as a call to serve, not an inconvenience.

ramacharitamanas::3705.verse_sanskrit: गीधराज सै भेंट भइ बहु बिधि प्रीति बढ़ाइ। गोदावरी निकट प्रभु रहे परन गृह छाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3705.verse_hindi: वहाँ गृध्रराज जटायु से भेंट हुई। उसके साथ बहुत प्रकार से प्रेम बढ़ाकर प्रभु श्री रामचंद्रजी गोदावरीजी के समीप पर्णकुटी छाकर रहने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3705.english_translation: There, Ram met Jatayu and deepened their affection in many ways. Near the Godavari, the Lord lived in a leaf-hut.
ramacharitamanas::3705.translation_literal: गीधराज (king of the vultures) / सै (with) / भेंट (meeting) / भइ (happened) / बहु बिधि (many ways) / प्रीति (affection) / बढ़ाइ (increasing) / गोदावरी (Godavari) / निकट (near) / प्रभु (the Lord) / रहे (lived) / परन गृह (leaf-hut) / छाइ (setting up)
ramacharitamanas::3705.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3705.essence: Humility and friendship can make a forest home feel complete.
ramacharitamanas::3705.simple_meaning: Ram met Jatayu and grew close to him. Then he stayed in a leaf-hut near the Godavari River.
ramacharitamanas::3705.simple_insight: True greatness can live simply and still create deep friendship.
ramacharitamanas::3705.detailed_meaning: In the forest near the Godavari, Ram and Sita settle into a humble leaf-hut. Before the larger tragedy unfolds, Ram meets Jatayu and forms a warm bond with him. The verse quietly sets the scene for the forest life that follows.
ramacharitamanas::3705.modern_relevance: You move into a small rented room and begin to notice who shows up with warmth, not status. The simplest place can become full of meaning when it holds real friendship.
ramacharitamanas::3705.insight: It shifts attention from grandeur to the quiet dignity of simple living and loyal companionship.

ramacharitamanas::3706.verse_sanskrit: जब ते राम कीन्ह तहँ बासा। सुखी भए मुनि बीती त्रासा॥ गिरि बन नदीं ताल छबि छाए। दिन दिन प्रति अति होहिं सुहाए ॥
ramacharitamanas::3706.verse_hindi: जब से श्री रामजी ने वहाँ निवास किया, तब से मुनि सुखी हो गए, उनका डर जाता रहा। पर्वत, वन, नदी और तालाब शोभा से छा गए। वे दिनोंदिन अधिक सुहावने (मालूम) होने लगे ॥
ramacharitamanas::3706.english_translation: When Ram took up residence there, the sages became happy and their fear disappeared. Mountains, forests, rivers, and lakes all shone with beauty and grew more lovely each day.
ramacharitamanas::3706.translation_literal: जब (when) / ते (then) / राम (Ram) / कीन्ह (made) / तहँ (there) / बासा (residence) / सुखी (happy) / भए (became) / मुनि (sages) / बीती (passed away) / त्रासा (fear) / गिरि (mountains) / बन (forests) / नदीं (rivers) / ताल (lakes) / छबि (beauty) / छाए (were covered) / दिन दिन प्रति (day by day) / अति (very) / होहिं (became) / सुहाए (lovely)
ramacharitamanas::3706.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3706.essence: Ram's presence turns fear into peace and wilderness into beauty.
ramacharitamanas::3706.simple_meaning: Ram's presence brings peace to the sages and beauty to the whole landscape. Fear fades, and everything feels more alive.
ramacharitamanas::3706.simple_insight: Some presences calm fear without saying a word.
ramacharitamanas::3706.detailed_meaning: In the forest near Panchavati, Ram has settled among the sages. His presence changes everything: the ascetics feel safe, and the hills, rivers, and lakes seem brighter. This verse shows the atmosphere around Ram before the story moves onward.
ramacharitamanas::3706.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and the tension drops before anyone speaks. The mood changes because someone steady has arrived.
ramacharitamanas::3706.insight: It shows that a truly steady presence can transform both people and place.

ramacharitamanas::3707.verse_sanskrit: खग मृग बृंद अनंदित रहहीं। मधुप मधुर गुंजत छबि लहहीं॥ सो बन बरनि न सक अहिराजा। जहाँ प्रगट रघुबीर बिराजा ॥
ramacharitamanas::3707.verse_hindi: पक्षी और पशुओं के समूह आनंदित रहते हैं और भौंरे मधुर गुंजार करते हुए शोभा पा रहे हैं। जहाँ प्रत्यक्ष श्री रामजी विराजमान हैं, उस वन का वर्णन सर्पराज शेषजी भी नहीं कर सकते ॥
ramacharitamanas::3707.english_translation: Birds and animals stay delighted there, and bees hum sweetly, adding to the beauty. Even Shesha, the king of serpents, cannot describe that forest where Raghubir is visibly present.
ramacharitamanas::3707.translation_literal: खग (birds) / मृग (deer, animals) / बृंद (groups) / अनंदित (delighted) / रहहीं (remain) / मधुप (bees) / मधुर (sweet) / गुंजत (humming) / छबि (beauty) / लहहीं (receive) / सो (that) / बन (forest) / बरनि (describe) / न (not) / सक (can) / अहिराजा (king of serpents) / जहाँ (where) / प्रगट (manifest) / रघुबीर (Raghubir, Ram) / बिराजा (is seated, abides)
ramacharitamanas::3707.speaker: Narrator
ramacharitamanas::3707.essence: Ram's presence turns even the forest into something beyond description.
ramacharitamanas::3707.simple_meaning: Ram's presence makes the forest feel alive and beautiful. Birds and animals are joyful there, and even the greatest serpent cannot fully describe it.
ramacharitamanas::3707.simple_insight: Some places feel different because of who is present there.
ramacharitamanas::3707.detailed_meaning: Ram is living in the forest near the Godavari, and the whole landscape has changed around him. Birds, deer, and bees seem joyful simply because he is there. The verse pauses on that beauty before Laxman begins his question.
ramacharitamanas::3707.modern_relevance: You walk into a room and feel the tension drop before anyone speaks. Some presence quietly changes the whole atmosphere, and everyone in the space feels it.
ramacharitamanas::3707.insight: It shifts attention from scenery alone to the transforming power of sacred presence.

ramacharitamanas::3708.verse_sanskrit: एक बार प्रभु सुख आसीना। लछिमन बचन कहे छलहीना॥ सुर नर मुनि सचराचर साईं। मैं पूछउँ निज प्रभु की नाईं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3708.verse_hindi: एक बार प्रभु श्री रामजी सुख से बैठे हुए थे। उस समय लक्ष्मणजी ने उनसे छलरहित (सरल) वचन कहे- हे देवता, मनुष्य, मुनि और चराचर के स्वामी! मैं अपने प्रभु की तरह (अपना स्वामी समझकर) आपसे पूछता हूँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3708.english_translation: Once, the Lord was seated in ease. Then Lakshman spoke words free of deceit: “O master of gods, humans, sages, and all moving and unmoving beings, I ask you as I would ask my own lord.”
ramacharitamanas::3708.translation_literal: एक बार (once) / प्रभु (the Lord) / सुख आसीना (seated in ease) / लछिमन (Lakshman) / बचन (words) / कहे (spoke) / छलहीना (free of deceit) / सुर (gods) / नर (humans) / मुनि (sages) / सचराचर (moving and unmoving beings) / साईं (master) / मैं (I) / पूछउँ (ask) / निज (my own) / प्रभु (lord) / की नाईं (like, as)
ramacharitamanas::3708.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::3708.essence: Honest questioning opens the door to real guidance.
ramacharitamanas::3708.simple_meaning: Lakshman speaks honestly and respectfully to Ram, asking a question as if speaking to his own master. The verse sets up a sincere inquiry that leads into deeper teaching.
ramacharitamanas::3708.simple_insight: You do not need polish to be worthy of guidance—only honesty and reverence.
ramacharitamanas::3708.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram is resting and Lakshman approaches without guile. He names Ram as the lord of all beings, then asks permission to speak as a loyal servant would. This opens the teaching that follows on wisdom, detachment, and devotion.
ramacharitamanas::3708.modern_relevance: You sit beside someone you trust after a hard day and finally ask the question you have been carrying. No performance, no cleverness — just honesty. That is the kind of opening that invites real guidance.
ramacharitamanas::3708.insight: It shifts the mind from guarded speech to sincere seeking.

ramacharitamanas::3709.verse_sanskrit: मोहि समुझाइ कहहु सोइ देवा। सब तजि करौं चरन रज सेवा॥ कहहु ग्यान बिराग अरु माया। कहहु सो भगति करहु जेहिं दाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3709.verse_hindi: हे देव! मुझे समझाकर वही कहिए, जिससे सब छोड़कर मैं आपकी चरणरज की ही सेवा करूँ। ज्ञान, वैराग्य और माया का वर्णन कीजिए और उस भक्ति को कहिए, जिसके कारण आप दया करते हैं ॥
ramacharitamanas::3709.english_translation: O divine one, explain it to me so I may leave everything and serve only the dust of your feet. Speak of knowledge, detachment, and illusion, and speak of the devotion through which you show grace.
ramacharitamanas::3709.translation_literal: मोहि (to me) / समुझाइ (explaining) / कहहु (tell) / सोइ (that same) / देवा (divine one) / सब (all) / तजि (leaving) / करौं (I may do) / चरन (feet) / रज (dust) / सेवा (service) ॥ कहहु (tell) / ग्यान (knowledge) / बिराग (detachment) / अरु (and) / माया (illusion) / कहहु (tell) / सो (that) / भगति (devotion) / करहु (you do) / जेहिं (by which) / दाया (grace/mercy) ॥
ramacharitamanas::3709.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::3709.essence: Real understanding ends in service, not pride.
ramacharitamanas::3709.simple_meaning: Lakshman asks Ram to explain the path that leads him to give up everything except loving service at Ram's feet. He also asks for teaching on knowledge, detachment, illusion, and the devotion that draws grace.
ramacharitamanas::3709.simple_insight: The heart is not just asking for answers — it is asking for a life that can let everything else go.
ramacharitamanas::3709.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Lakshman sits before Ram and speaks with complete humility. He wants more than information: he wants the kind of understanding that turns into surrender, clears confusion, and deepens loving service.
ramacharitamanas::3709.modern_relevance: You sit with a teacher after a breakup, a job loss, or a family rupture, and you don't want theory. You want the kind of understanding that actually changes what you cling to.
ramacharitamanas::3709.insight: It shifts inquiry from collecting ideas to seeking the understanding that transforms devotion and conduct.

ramacharitamanas::3710.verse_sanskrit: ईस्वर जीव भेद प्रभु सकल कहौ समुझाइ। जातें होइ चरन रति सोक मोह भ्रम जाइ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3710.verse_hindi: हे प्रभो! ईश्वर और जीव का भेद भी सब समझाकर कहिए, जिससे आपके चरणों में मेरी प्रीति हो और शोक, मोह तथा भ्रम नष्ट हो जाएँ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3710.english_translation: O Lord, explain clearly the difference between the supreme being and the individual being, so that my love for your feet may arise and sorrow, delusion, and confusion may vanish.
ramacharitamanas::3710.translation_literal: ईस्वर (the supreme being) / जीव (individual being) / भेद (difference) / प्रभु (Lord) / सकल (all) / कहौ (tell) / समुझाइ (explaining clearly) / जातें (by which) / होइ (may become) / चरन (feet) / रति (love/attachment) / सोक (sorrow) / मोह (delusion) / भ्रम (confusion) / जाइ (go away)
ramacharitamanas::3710.speaker: Lakshman
ramacharitamanas::3710.essence: Clear understanding can turn confusion into love at the feet of the divine.
ramacharitamanas::3710.simple_meaning: Lakshman asks Ram to explain the difference between the supreme being and the individual self, because true understanding will grow devotion and remove sorrow, delusion, and confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3710.simple_insight: Clarity is not cold here — it becomes love, relief, and inner steadiness.
ramacharitamanas::3710.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Lakshman has already asked Ram for wisdom, detachment, and devotion. Now he goes deeper and asks about the difference between the supreme being and the individual being, hoping that clear understanding will turn his heart fully toward Ram.
ramacharitamanas::3710.modern_relevance: You keep rereading the same message, trying to understand what someone really meant. Beneath the confusion is a deeper hunger: once you see clearly, your heart can settle and love without strain.
ramacharitamanas::3710.insight: It shifts the mind from vague devotion to clear understanding that strengthens devotion.

ramacharitamanas::3711.verse_sanskrit: थोरेहि महँ सब कहउँ बुझाई। सुनहु तात मति मन चित लाई॥ मैं अरु मोर तोर तैं माया। जेहिं बस कीन्हे जीव निकाया ॥
ramacharitamanas::3711.verse_hindi: (श्री रामजी ने कहा-) हे तात! मैं थोड़े ही में सब समझाकर कहे देता हूँ। तुम मन, चित्त और बुद्धि लगाकर सुनो! मैं और मेरा, तू और तेरा- यही माया है, जिसने समस्त जीवों को वश में कर रखा है ॥
ramacharitamanas::3711.english_translation: I will explain everything briefly. Listen carefully, with your mind and attention fixed. "I" and "mine," "you" and "yours"—this is the veil of appearance that has bound all living beings.
ramacharitamanas::3711.translation_literal: थोरेहि (briefly) / महँ (in) / सब (everything) / कहउँ (I will say) / बुझाई (explaining) / सुनहु (listen) / तात (dear one) / मति (mind) / मन (mind) / चित (attention) / लाई (having applied) / मैं (I) / अरु (and) / मोर (mine) / तोर (yours) / तैं (you) / माया (veil of appearance) / जेहिं (by which) / बस (under control) / कीन्हे (made) / जीव (living beings) / निकाया (multitudes)
ramacharitamanas::3711.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3711.essence: Bondage begins the moment life is divided into mine and yours.
ramacharitamanas::3711.simple_meaning: Ram says the whole trap can be understood quickly: the sense of “I,” “mine,” “you,” and “yours” is what binds living beings.
ramacharitamanas::3711.simple_insight: There is relief in seeing that ownership and separateness are the real cage.
ramacharitamanas::3711.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram answers the seeker’s questions about the self, wisdom, and devotion. Instead of a long lecture, he points straight to the root of bondage: the habit of dividing life into “me” and “not me.”
ramacharitamanas::3711.modern_relevance: You feel hurt the moment someone touches your idea, your partner, your status, your plan. The pain is often not the event itself, but the grip of ownership around it.
ramacharitamanas::3711.insight: It shifts attention from external conflict to the mind’s habit of claiming and separating.

ramacharitamanas::3712.verse_sanskrit: गो गोचर जहँ लगि मन जाई। सो सब माया जानेहु भाई॥ तेहि कर भेद सुनहु तुम्ह सोऊ। बिद्या अपर अबिद्या दोऊ ॥
ramacharitamanas::3712.verse_hindi: इंद्रियों के विषयों को और जहाँ तक मन जाता है, हे भाई! उन सबको माया जानना। उसके भी एक विद्या और दूसरी अविद्या, इन दोनों भेदों को तुम सुनो- ॥
ramacharitamanas::3712.english_translation: Whatever the mind can reach through the senses, know all of that as illusion, brother. Hear now the difference between the two: knowledge and ignorance.
ramacharitamanas::3712.translation_literal: गोचर (objects of the senses) / जहँ लगि (as far as) / मन (mind) / जाई (goes) / सो (that) / सब (all) / माया (illusion) / जानेहु (know) / भाई (brother) / तेहि (that) / कर (of) / भेद (difference) / सुनहु (listen) / तुम्ह (you) / सोऊ (that too) / बिद्या (knowledge) / अपर (other) / अबिद्या (ignorance) / दोऊ (both)
ramacharitamanas::3712.speaker: Ram
ramacharitamanas::3712.essence: What the mind can reach is not necessarily what is real.
ramacharitamanas::3712.simple_meaning: Everything the mind can reach through the senses is part of appearance, not ultimate reality. Ram then points to two kinds of understanding: one that frees, and one that keeps you trapped.
ramacharitamanas::3712.simple_insight: You stop trusting every mental grasp as truth and begin asking what is real beneath it.
ramacharitamanas::3712.detailed_meaning: In the forest, Ram is answering a deep question from the seeker in front of him. After speaking of the difference between the supreme reality and the individual self, he now turns to the world of sense experience and says it all belongs to appearance. Then he begins to separate true understanding from confusion.
ramacharitamanas::3712.modern_relevance: You scroll for an hour, feeling like you understand everything because you have seen so much. But seeing more is not the same as seeing clearly. This verse asks you to question what your restless mind keeps collecting.
ramacharitamanas::3712.insight: It trains you to distinguish raw sensory experience from clear understanding, instead of treating every impression as truth.

ramacharitamanas::3713.verse_sanskrit: एक दुष्ट अतिसय दुखरूपा। जा बस जीव परा भवकूपा॥ एक रचइ जग गुन बस जाकें। प्रभु प्रेरित नहिं निज बल ताकें ॥
